review_text: “Prima gelegen - mittendrin in downtown Manhattan” Sicherlich nicht das preiswerteste Hotel New York und sicherlich nicht die größten Zimmer - diese aber stylish gestaltet und komfortable ausgestattet. Das große Plus ist der Washington Square Park direkt nebenan mit seinem pulsierenden Leben - aber auch die Nähe zu Soho und Tribeca. Mehrere U-Bahnstationen sowie den unteren Broadway in der Nähe ist es für Touristen nahezu genial gelegen. Von der näher gelegenen U-Bahn-Station kann direkt zum Flughafen JFK gefahren werden - der A-Express macht's möglich. Ist man - so wie wir - zu Ostern zu Gast, also einer Zeit, in der viele Touristen die Stadt bevölkern, kann es beim Frühstück zu Wartezeiten kommen. Da hilft es doch sehr, dass man vor dem Frühstücksraum - der abends Restaurant ist - sich Kaffee in Becher füllen kann, um sich dann in die Schlange oder wieder ins Bett zu begeben. Wir waren rundherum zufrieden und kommen gerne wieder.

“Great location, but starting to show it's age” This hotel is one block off Michigan ave, midway between the river and the John Hancock. In other words, a great location. Unfortunately though, it's starting to look a little shabby. The rooms are large but a little tatty in the corners if you look closely. Strangely, the bathrooms are really compact. Perhaps they could take some of that room footage and add it in to the bathrooms? Our only real complaint was the elevator noise. They were loud, so we asked for a different room and the desk staff were very happy to oblige. Internet access is $10 a night, which I found hard to swallow. Just go to the pub downstairs and use their service for free. And a good trip for breakfast is to head south 200 feet from the hotel to the Corner Bakery. You can get a good feed there for under $10.

“Depends on your room” I redeemed some points for a room here for 4 nights. It's in a great location, right on the trolley line on union square. Initial nights were in the tower. Tower rooms are small but adequate with nice views. Air conditioning in our room was very noisy, so when we complained, we were switched to the old building, and were given a corner room (reportedly the -06 and -34 rooms are the best) and loved it. Lots of room, lovely view over the square, high ceilings - really great. I had an unusually hard time activating the internet connection ($13/d). If I were to stay here again, I'd ask for the old building overlooking the square. However, I would stay here again.

“抜群の立地” 夫婦なので、ステューディオに宿泊しました。 57丁目と言う最高の立地で、バス、地下鉄も近くにあります。 広さ的には2人であれば、十分だと思います。 バスタブはありませんが、「郷に入れば、郷に従え」だと思います。 夜のセキュリティも、入り口にドアマンがいて、名前、部屋番号の確認をしてからでないと、中に入れません。 部屋は道路に面していなかったせいか、全く以て静かで、ここがNYかと思うほどでした。 朝食は、近くのレストランで済ますか、向かい側のデリで購入するか、近所の大型スーパーで買ってくれば良いと思います。 冷蔵庫は2つあり、片方が空っぽなので、購入してきたものはそちらに入れられます。 備え付けノコーヒメーカーがあるので、味さえ我慢すれば、入れたてのコーヒーが飲めます。(総じて、NYのコーヒーは美味しくないですので、この程度でお金を払わないで済むならばと思います)

“Only place to stay on Upper West Side” My wife and I had an amazing stay at On the Ave. The hotel has great location(77th & Broadway) and is beautifully appointed. Not only that but it is also relatively inexpensive and pet friendly! The staff is incredible and willing to go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable. My only criticism would be the cost of Wi-Fi (over $10 per day) but I will be back to On the Ave the next time I'm in NYC.

“Would return in a heartbeat!” What can I possibly write what has not already been said about this great property? Perhaps this: try to book one of the King Study Rooms. As these seem to be the corner rooms of each floor, they tend to be slightly larger and offer more peace and quiet because they are most remote from elevators and housekeeping rooms and just have one wall towards an adjacent room.

“Lots of potential, but major kinks” I stayed at Hotel Felix for four nights in May at a priceline rate of $150/night. On the first night, after a long night on the town, I was horrified when I pulled back the covers and discovered several (and I'm talking 10-12) strands of someone else's hair stuck to the sheets. I've stayed in tons of hotels around the world and have never seen anything like this. I complained to management and left a very courteous note for the housekeeping staff. To their credit, I never had an issue after that. Still, this is unacceptable. I hope they step up their game, because it's a cute little hotel. Rooms are small, but well appointed and the bath products were great. The lobby/bar area was usually crowded a la W hotels, giving it a trendy vibe. Staff were friendly. Parking was outrageously high, but par for the course in the area.

“Needs Renovation” This hotel needs renovating. It is in a truly wonderful area but to think you are staying in a 4 star place is misleading. Wallpaper in bathroom is peeling. My room is small like a maid's quarters- I booked on Hotwire- and yes they treat you like you booked on it. Too many great hotels to waste your time staying here. The other Intercontinental on Howard Street is leaps and bounds better than this. This hotel should be renamed, "Grannies Bed and Breakfast."

“Disappointed” This used to be my favorite hotel in Seattle, the epitome of old world elegance and service. My visit last month was not up to their usual standard. Upon checking in, around 6 pm, I was told the only rooms they had were smoking, room with a murphy bed or handicapped room. I opted for the handicapped room which was OK but the bathroom was a bit off. But it was OK until I tried to take a shower in the morning and found there was no hot water. No one in the hotel seemed to be overly concerned with this. When I checked out, it took over 20 minutes to get my car, even though I had called down for it. When I asked why it was taking so long, was told they were "very busy". Obviously. It was so jammed that I had to walk to the street and flag my car down as they brought it up because they couldn't put any more cars in the driveway. I think I'll head back to the Monaco next time.

“Nice times square hotel” Stayed here for a couple of days. Hotel is close to Times Square. It is a little to the side, and not in the nicest neighborhood, but the hotel is new and very nice. Close to restaurants and the subway. I would definitely return.

“Above par for Fairfield Inn - very clean and fresh” Arrived quite late, but front desk staff had my room key waiting, making check-in very speedy (quick note for non-Texans - make sure you get off at the right exit for the highway frontage road, otherwise you'll go in circles for a little bit). The room was spacious and very clean, and most furniture looked rather new. Free Internet and free breakfast is always a plus - the Texas shaped waffle iron was a nice touch. My suite also had a microwave and mini-fridge, which would have been helpful if I were staying for more than one night. The only negative in my stay was that housekeeping had forgotten to put soap in the bathroom when cleaning the previous night. Hotel is right near a very upscale mall and several major businesses (including National Instruments) which made it very convenient. For the price, I would definitely stay here again.

“Old and Worn” When traveling to San Diego I would steer clear of this hotel. It is located off the freeway and it hasn't been updated in YEARS. Almost everything about this hotel was depressing, the rooms were small and dark and looked out to the parking lot. The room was clean but in desperate need of an update and overhaul. It was the type of room you sleep in but don't want to spend any other time in. The hotel was fairly near Old Town, just a quick Trolley ride away but it is located in a very inconvenient location when trying to access the downtown or other districts of the city. I felt very isolated and pretty much stuck at the hotel. You can take the nearby trolley but it took us almost an hour with two transfers to reach the downtown. Cab fare to reach downtown was $20 each way. The only upside was that the hotel has a decent pool and hot tub and it was nice to relax there.

“Upgraded Since Wyndham Days” I decided to give this place another try since it changed from Wyndham to Crowne Plaza a couple of years ago. Experiences when it was a Wyndham were not good at all, because they had let it get pretty run down, cut corners on maintenance, and the staff was not very helpful back then. I realize that sometimes the name change is all that really happens, but I figured they couldn't help but improve. So, I booked a room at the now Crowne Plaza because it is so convenient to the Memphis Cook Convention Center where I was attending a trade show. I was pleased to see that the renovations in 2008 made it more pleasing, the bedding was upgraded, and they installed flat screen TVs. The front desk staff was efficient and polite at checkin and gladly answered any questions. The only reason I didn't rate this Crowne Plaza higher is because it isn't as polished as some I've been to, and the bedding isn't as plush and comfortable as others. I didn't notice much noise from the adjacent rooms, but there is little soundproofing between the bathrooms (you can hear haridryers, coughing, and such through the exhaust vents) and you can hear everything that takes place in the hall. And, if you need the elevators during a busy time, the wait can be longer than I liked. I'd also recommend eating all your meals somewhere else (the breakfast is $12.95). Yes, I will probably stay here again next year simply because it is so convenient to the Convention Center and way more affordable than the Marriott across the street.

“Buen hotel en el Distrito Financiero” El hotel es elegante, moderno. Las habitaciones son muy grandes, las camas king size muy cómodas, el baño también es bastante grande y todo muy limpio. Yo pedí una habitación silenciosa, y me la dieron en un piso alto, y no había nada de ruido. La zona, está muerta por la noche, aunque hay algunos sitios para cenar justo enfrente, hamburgueserías y pizzerias, está al lado del Disney Concert Hall, el metro esta a 2 minutos andando, al lado de un parque, si se vuelve por la noche, hay vagabundos durmiendo en el parque, es lo único que da un poquito de cosa. En el hotel siempre hay taxis en la puerta y el personal es muy amable, y correcto. Nosotros no cogimos el desayuno, nos parecía caro, y justo al lado hay Starbucks (también hay uno dentro del hotel, pero suele haber bastante cola y es pequeñito), y algun sitio más para poder desayunar. Creo que si volviera, repetiría en este hotel, ya que además el precio es correcto.

“Cost Cutting in the Extreme” I stayed here frequently when this was a Park Hyatt. Under Starwood, the cost-cutting has reached ridiculous extremes. They've partially redecorated; the furniture that's left over from the Park Hyatt days is old and beaten up, the new stuff is a completely different style (out of the W catalogue?) and doesn't match the space. In my Jr. Suite, for example, where there used to be a sofa and chairs, they now have just two chairs and lots and lots of empty space. They even ration towels now, like a Motel 6 (only TWO bath towels - you've got to be kidding!). If you can get a really good price, this hotel remains a decent financial district option, but just recognize that it is no longer a true four star property.

“Just wonderful” My husband and I just returned from a few days at the Sofitel. I must send out my highest recommendation to anyone looking for a wonderful place to stay. We lived in the Society Hill area of Philly many years ago, and sometimes return to visit, so we know the city...the Sofitel's location is perfect for everything, so we decided to try it. I'd read a couple of reviews describing the rooms as "cramped". I can't speak for the standard rooms, but our Junior Suite was very spacious, and really couldn't have been nicer. I kept walking around the room saying "I LOVE this room". The design was perfect...both living area and bedroom had access ot the bath, which was marble, had a glass shower and separate tub....plus real orchids in a vase! A great bathroom! And, the bed was a tower of fresh linens and 6 inches of puffy feathers, and exquisite. And the service! Wow! From the moment you walk in the door, every single person is programmed to say "Yes Mam, or Yes Sir" to any request. In short, the hotel was just great, and I'll be back there next time. I guess if there was anything not quite perfect, it was the restaurant. While the service and presentation were super, my salmon was overcooked, and the lobster bisque was just ok. But the continental breakfasts delivered to the room were fabulous, as well as the cheesburger I ordered late in the evening. But don't let that stop you from staying here. It's marvelous.

“Standard hotel” I have never stayed in a regular-sized room in NYC, and my room at the Holiday Inn was no exception. I can't fault the hotel for that - the city just lacks space. That being said, the room was adequate and clean. The bed was very comfortable. Very small bathroom, but nice Bath & Body Works toiletries. Friendly staff and automatic check-out. The location is close to many things (Rockefeller Center, Empire State Building, shopping); but the neighborhood directly surrounding the hotel was a bit less upscale - still felt safe; just not such a posh area as a few blocks over. It was a bit difficult finding a taxi in the morning - no taxi line and no one to help you hail one. We walked a few blocks over - but budget a few minutes of extra time if you need to get somewhere. The hotel is fine for a short stay or for business.

“Room 1419 - a dark and cramped furnished closet” Stayed here because it is near our NYC office. Survived one night of dark, dingy room, rattling air conditioner unit and carefully walking the path between bed/closet and bed/bathroom. Glad I am not overweight or would not be able to get through narrow doorway to bathroom and same narrow door way to closet. Poorly designed room has bedside table only on one side - the other side has part of the mini-bar food/snacks on a tray that says "careful - if you touch this we will start charging you" - not helpful, so did a MacGuyver and took trash can liner out and turned trash can upside down to make a bedside spot for water, alarm, etc. Bathroom is claustrophobic even by NY standards...no way two people could be in this bathroom at same time. Not all rooms come with a bathtub, so be sure to check before accepting room key. The concierge wasn't much help at the Whatever Desk. Asked for a recommendation for a good hamburger close by and the best he could do was the outrageouly priced Smith & Wollensky's chop house. After we had the chat "if it was your personal money and the hotel wasn't paying and the restaurant you picked isn't comp'ing you because you send them lots of customers, where would you eat?" - we got sent to a neighborhood pub, the Pig & Whistle on Second Avenue between 50 & 51st - nice atmosphere, very reasonable food and drink -would go back here One positive point -= the Bliss shampoo, cleanser and body lotion. Will stay elsewhere next time....so should you considering the price.

“Best Hampton Inn Ever!” We generally like Hampton Inns, but this one was head and shoulders above the rest. We had a HUGE room (a suite reallyl) with a very comfortable king size bed. There was a separate living room with pullout bed, a small kitchen, dining area, and large bathroom. Everything was spotless. The Wi-Fi access worked just fine. We were there on a Friday night, and it was very quiet. In common with other reviewers, we had a little trouble finding the place, but that doesn't detract from our enthusiasm for this Hampton Inn. Highly recommended.

“July 4th experience” Stayed July 3 - July 6, 2 adults, 1 teenager and 1 preteen. Had read a lot of reviews about this hotel and knew what to expect over the July 4 holiday. Place was full, and it was all families with kids.... like us. At times there were waits for elevators (particularly after the July 3 big fireworks) and the breakfast was unpleasant due to overwhelming amounts of people. That said, the staff handled things well, obviously had dealt with these types of crowds and we felt they did a good job. You had to show your room keys to enter the hotel on July 3rd after the fireworks which kept out the hordes of people streaming off the shoreline. Things quieted down quickly due to the clientel being families. Our room was a 2 double, non-smoking. Very clean and spacious, had a city view. Stayed on Hilton points. Our room not ready at 3pm so they found a compatable room for us so we could check in immediately. Did not use the pool, very small and crowded. Lobby area spacious, very nice, had drinks there one afternoon but left before the crowds arrived for the free drinks and snacks. The location of this hotel was perfect. About 4 blocks to actual Navy Pier enterance, 2 blocks to Mich. Ave. Went to a movie one night in the AMC on lower level of hotel, also bowling there. At ate Grand Lux nearby (very good) also liked Banderas and Dicks Last Resort Dockside (also close by). Would recommend for families, but for adult only trip we liked the Hilton Suites on the upper end of Mich. Ave where we stayed last summer.

“business travelers beware” This is fine hotel unless you need a speedy internet (abysmally slow and their internet provider is atrocious--must have spent 4 hours to no avail), help from the front desk (they can't do anything with their computers to print out anything other than one receipt one way for a trip--tough if you need different receipts for different sources reimbursements), or a polite doorperson (who doesn't yell at you if you don't select the cab he wants even though he is highly enmeshed in a conversation with a friend and doesn't lift a finger to help you with luggage on the way out). On the plus side, the rooms are large and good for families. If I wasn;t travelling on business and I didn't need the internet, I might stay there if I wanted a middle-of-Times Square experience.

“Good hotel, Great location......” A good hotel in a fab location for exploring NYC. On some review sites, this hotel has been classed as 'luxury' which it is not. However, the staff are efficient, the hotel was clean and comfortable, and it was in good condition....but it's very 'touristy', probably by virtue of it's location. There is a shared fitness facility with pool in the hotel - it was full of the 'body beautiful' so could be a little intimidating for the casual user. There is a bar and casual restaurant if needed, and plenty of Starbucks-type outlets nearby if you prefer breakfast outside. The subway and tour buses are close too. I would recommend this hotel for a trip to NYC.

“Good value nice rooms however staff not so great” we booked two rooms in this hotel for us and our two young children (10 and 8) having asked to be close to each other ;however when we arrived the people at the reception were overwhelmed and although we had our reservation confirming our request they put us in 2 rooms on a different floor .Reception and concierge facilities were absolutely below average The rooms however were very nice and clean and noisefree and after all we were ok with the kids . breakfast is very nice and the overall price also was very good. one big minus the guy in the hotel bar was very unfriendly and the bar lacked charm.

“Excellent Stay” I got a great deal on the internet for this hotel. The room was lovely. The restaurant was exceptional. There is a small fitness area. The staff at this hotel are very attentive particularly the hard working bell/valet staff who are happy to arrange tours. The parking is expensive but on par for the DC area. There is not much to do in the neighbourhood after dinner time but hotel staff will make suggestions. I would gladly return!

“Excellent location, would stay again” Picked the Homewood Suites based on Tripadvisor. As some of mentioned, can be a bit confusing finding the entrance. The Homewood Suites shares an entrance with the Hilton Gardens. So the front entrance can be crowded with vehicles of people checking in. The Homewood Suites is in a large complex with a massive gym, movie theater, stores, several restaurants, office space, condos and indoor parking. Check in was quick, my reservations were accurate and the front desk clerk gave me instructions on where the parking lot was. Self parking around the otherside of the building but with an elevator entrance into the lobby of the hotel. My room was very nice with full kitchen, plasma tv and comfortable bed. The sofa looked a bit worn but nothing to complain about. Rooms are laid out as they show on their website. Lots of light and a partial view of the harbor from our room. Wifi worked perfectly and is free so very happy about that. Our floor was quiet, only noise was from the fan in the bathroom which I couldn't turn off. We arrived on a Saturday and immediately walked to the Inner Harbor which was no more than a 15 min walk. Very doable with my 5 year old (although we are from NYC and do walk a lot). Bkfst was on the 2nd floor. It was ok, nothing to complain about. Did not have a problem with it being crowded or no enough seats. Lots of restaurants in walking distance and Whole Foods is one block away so we were able to stock up on a few staples (milk, soda, water, etc) and there is a Starbucks next door. The Maryland Athletic Club which is in the complex and has an entrance on the 2nd floor allows guests of Homewood Suites and Hilton Garden to have free access. Children are allowed in one of the pools (there are a few) and my son had a great time. The gym equipment is quite nice so was able to get some exercise in also. Enjoyed our stay. Only one hiccup, the fire alarm went off early Sunday morning. Guess I'm glad to know that it works and you can hear it very clearly in the room. Walked down several flights of steps to the outside (it was warm since it is August). Luckily Starbucks was open already so went straight there. Fire department came and left but it took the hotel staff (not many around at that hour as you can guess) nearly an hour to reset the elevators, etc so most of us just walked back up. Otherwise, my family enjoyed our stay and would stay there again.

“nice stay, nice rooms” Stayed here in May 2006 over Memorial Day weekend at 119.00 per night for the room. The check in went smoothly and the room was good sized and nicely appointed. I stayed at the Quality Suites in April 2006 and it is next door sharing the parking lot and a few amenities(swimming pool and weight room). The good thing about this hotel is that all the amenities are at the Quality Suites and so all of the noise is at that hotel. I would recommend staying at the Holiday Inn because it is much quieter and the rooms are nicer, even though it is a little more expensive than the Quality Suites. Would stay here again. Only complaint is because they share the parking lot, it can get really crowded and hard to find parking..Other than that, the breakfast is good and the workers are friendly.

“Typical Courtyard but one of few hotels on upper East Side” This is a functional Courtyard but nothing special. The staff at the front desk were friendly and efficient. The rooms are small but typical for Manhattan. There is no breakfast option in the hotel as the adjoining restaurant has gone out of business. It was very difficult to get a cab in the morning in front of the hotel. But the location is ideal if you have business on the upper East Side.

“Wow!” We stayed here for a three day business trip. New hotel in an old building. We loved the modern, contemporary vibe of the hotel. A little on the Ikea side, but nice. Our king room had a sitting room, office space, and kitchen. No tub, but a walk-in shower. The hotel is a green-built hotel and was very clean. Pros - Amazing staff!! Thanks to Eric who was spot-on with all of his recommendations! Location was perfect - very close to the Riverwalk without all the touristy stuff. We walked everywhere the entire trip. Loved ease of being downtown close to everything. Workout facilities were great, machines and weights. Breakfast was included in our price. It's served in the lobby; kind of an extended continental breakfast. Comfortable bed and quiet room. Cons - because this is a green hotel, the vent in the bathroom runs contantly. The air was clean, but it was noisy enough that we had to keep the bathroom door shut. The pool/oversized hot tub could have been hotter. Overall, we loved it and are already making plans to return!

“Nice value hotel!!!” We had a nice, clean, comfortable room for a great price. Lots of convenient places to eat. The desk staff was not overly friendly, but they provided great service! Very happy to have found this place. I wish it were closer to 1-70 but it's worth the drive for the value it provides.

“Overall a very good hotel” I've stayed here many times for business and have only been dissapointed with a few small things such as keys not working, no one answering the guest service hotline, etc. but overall this is a very solid property. I understand that these things will happen and the front desk staff is always quick to help. It also offers a great location, very good restaurants and a good workout facility. Given the age and size of the building the staff does a very good job of running things. Only drawback is that it sells out quick.

“Close to airport - noisy” The hotel itself was fine, clean and the only drawback we could find was that it was noisy with visitors from the airport arriving at all hours of the night. If you are looking for a quick sleep in a clean room - this is good for that but not good for couple weekends out or nice trip out of town.

“Futuristic! Fun! Fabulous!” My daughters and I went DC and New York for spring break 2012! We had a wonderful time!!! Yotel was a great experience for my girls first time to the big Apple. We walked everywhere! Why? because Yotel was that close to everything. Time Square 2-3 blocks away?? The room was clean comfortable and really cool!!!! I love it and will probably stay there only when I return to NYC. The service was great! The 4th floor was out of this world! The Bar, the restaurant, the club, the terrace! Its something for everyone! Well worth the money spent which was not much for everything you got!

“Best location” As other reviewers have noted, the outstanding feature of this hotel is the great location close to many of the top DC tourist sights. The room, while nicely decorated and clean, was small and the bathroom was one of the smallest I've seen. In my opinion, this can never be a 5 star hotel because of the size of the bathroom in the standard rooms. I tried a number of times to upgrade to a larger room, but there seem to be only a few of these and they don't seem to be available frequently. Across the street is the Cafe du Parc which reminds you of being at a side walk cafe in Paris. It's very beautiful and worth the cost. Other restaurants are also nearby. This is a large hotel but it has quite a small pool. Perhaps because we were there right before Memorial Day weekend, and lots of families were traveling, the pool was almost always packed with screaming kids (and I do mean packed). We may be adults, but we like to use the pool, too and it wasn't possible most of the time.

“Great New Years Stay, Excellent Location” We stayed here over the New Year by which time all of the hotel work had finished. As we were staying on Priority Points it was free fro the week but if I had paid the cheapest rate would have cost $4800 in total. The hotel location can not be beaten in the centre of Time Sq with lots in walking distance or only a short tube ride away. The hotel common areas are clean and modern and the rooms are newly refitted including the bathrooms. Our room didn't have a great view but we could see a part of the Hudson but as we not looking out of the window that often it didn't matter. On NYE the hotel was packed and so was all the area around it, don't expect to stay here and see anything of the festivities you have to go out 5 hours before to even have a chance and in the bone chilling sub zero temps it's best avoided. My only complaint is the room service food is so poor and overpriced! I had a club sandwich, bowl of fries and a carrot cake and it was $48. If it was decent I wouldn't have minded but it was cold and tasteless and the carott cake was as long and wide as 2 fingers. If I was paying I would stay at a cheaper hotel as the rooms are nice but not worth the rates they charge, they are for the location not the standard of the hotel.

“What a freefall for what was once a great hotel” The Olympic was rebranded a Fairmount from the Four Seasons a number of years ago. Things made a fairly smooth transition until the "great recession" hit a couple of years ago. I appreciate that the economy fell off a cliff but sadly, one of its casualties was the Olympic. They have greatly reduced staff and it shows. The remaining staff remains upbeat and professional but there are not enough of them. I have stayed here at least annually since 1984. I used to think it was the best hotel in America. No more. The rooms are down at their heels. The fitness center and pool are stunning but filthy. The locker rooms are infrequently tended to so I found it trashed on 2 of the 3 visits I made there. They have some tables at the end of the swimming pool along w/a couple of loveseat sized seats all of which had garbage and food remnants under them. Our breakfast in the Georgian room was an absolute disaster. There were about 10 occupied tables and ONE person tending to all 10 tables. At one point the phone rang, and rang, and rang. Nobody ever picked it up but it rang, loud enough to be heard throughout the whole of that stunning room, for a good 3 or 4 minutes until whomever was calling gave up. Thank goodness. With the economy coming back, perhaps the ownership will spend the money it takes to return the Olympic to its former standing. However, they've lost me and my business. There is a new Four Season in town and the Pan Pacific has recently opened. The Inn at the Market is reliable. All in all, The Olympic has skidded so significantly that I have concluded that it's beyond repair. I shared all of this with the front desk manager when I left who expressed his sympathies. I wrote the general manager who sent me a generic letter that didn't even attempt to address the hotel's failures. After receiving his response, I'm convinced one of the hotel's failings is the general manager. Farewell The Olympic. It was a lovely relationship but it's over for me.

“Perfect for those without cars” My boyfriend and I stayed here for two nights during the holiday season. The staff was very friendly and helpful. They have complimentary coffee/tea and cookies in the lobby. There is also an umbrella in the room for you to use during your stay, which was extremely useful for us. The location is nice if you don't have a car, but if you do, parking costs $20/day self-park (a short walk away) or $28 valet with ins-outs. With that and the hectic driving conditions, I would probably not recommend staying here if you have a car. Otherwise, it's a pleasant stay...a little old for my taste, but that was expected.

“Good Location but Poor Hotel” I thought this hotel was run down and was uncomfortable staying here for the one night that I did. The reservation was by mistake; my boyfriend thought he was reserving The Embassy Suites, so I'd already had a sinking feeling when I read the actual title and saw how cheap of a rate we'd gotten, but our power went out from some pretty torrential winds and lightening in the northeast and with 100 degree weather, I went to the hotel. To make clear how much I didn't care for the property, I was fully prepared to travel on a delayed metro system back to my apartment building which had no electricity. The good points are the location, WiFi, and breakfast. It is well within walking distance of a metro station and steps away from plenty of food options and bars. The front desk staff was friendly enough, and the continental breakfast had a pretty good lineup. The bed was a decent size too. As for the room, they seem pretty stingy with the towels, the gym machines are definitely some of the first to have ever been invented (and something was floating in the gallon of water inside the gym...), and the building has a strange mix of an old carpet and cigarette odor. I sprayed Lysol everywhere and still couldn't get rid of the smell. The bathroom is extremely small but usable for one night. I'm glad I spent one night here because if it was more than that I would have just lost my money and gone back to my powerless apartment. The walls must be extremely thin. I could hear my neighbors clearly and whenever their doors closed I felt the vibration through my bed's headboard. I noticed that someone's review said that they called ahead b/c they needed a refrigerator and one was there when they got in their room for free. I guess it depends on which staff person you speak with, because when I called and asked I was told that they cost $10/night. For those who really don't feel like dealing with the dogs in the elevator, good luck, because this hotel welcomes them.

“Excellent, friendly staff” Booked my stay using Hilton Hhonors Points. Was contacted by email with a brief questionnaire about my preferences and filled that out. I had requested extra pillows and they were there when I arrived. Additionally, the first evening we found a gift basket with a few snacks and a hand-written note from the manager, which was very nice. Location is great and everyone who works there is friendly. Highly recommend. I am always pleased with Hilton properties and this one was no exception.

“Can't wait to return” We just celebrated our 36th anniversary at this hotel..It was a perfect long weekend. The entire staff is friendly, but not overly so..perfect. I had called because I was having roses delivered to our room. When we arrived, they had upgraded us to a suite....perfect Clean...quiet...comfortable..perfect service

“Just a layover” I had a 8 hour lay over in PHX, and did not want to spend it at the airport. The shuttle picked me up quickly and i was able to check in at about 10 am, This was prearranged. The room was clean and quite, I was able to get a nap in and then some homework done on the computer, Good Internet service. The young blonde man working the desk on the Evening of Aug 7, was attentive and polite. The shuttle going back to the airport took a while to arrive but I still had time to get on my flight.

“Enjoyed Our Brief Stay” This a a fairly new hotel in the Columbus area known as Grandview. Its proximity to the Ohio State campus makes it a great place to stay if you have business or pleasure that takes you to campus. It is also close to downtown and because parking is complimentary, you save the added expense that you would pay to park at a downtown hotel. There is no in-hotel restaurant, but the Buckeye Hall of Fame Grille is right next door, which is a great place to have lunch/dinner/drinks. The hotel itself is well-appointed, clean, and comfortable with large rooms. Our room had a big sofa and a large flat screen TV that swiveled so that it could be viewed from all parts of the room. The bathroom was very nice with a separate area for the sink and vanity, which made "getting ready" going more smoothly. All in all, a very nice hotel where we will definitely stay again!

“Mostly hits but some misses” You know the hotel I'm talking about; the significant flat edged screwdriver like structures that grace the San Diego skyline belong to the Manchester Grand Hyatt and well for all its grandeur, my expectations were a bit higher than what had been met. Our family stay at the Hyatt was above all pleasant but surely had some hits and misses. As an architectural landmark it's breathtaking and definitely worthy of the word grand from it's strong wood arches and marbled lobbied floors, the Hyatt on the outside is pleasing to the eye. Its pool is reminiscent of a Las Vegas hotel pool, one of the larger ones in the downtown San Diego hotel district and ample room for everyone to lay out and enjoy the gorgeous weather. The breakfast buffet at Lael's is abundant (omelet station, lox and bagels and delicious coffee) and service is outstanding. The Hyatt also incorporates a lot of complimentary family friendly activities such as a swim-up movie at nightfall, for a small fee you and your fam can enjoy s'mores by the fire pit and an all day activity area for lawn bowling, football and foosball. Am I enticing you yet? Better hold off on the thought because granted its pros there's surely some cons that may be of importance to some of you out there. One of them is the room. The rooms at the Manchester GRAND Hyatt are pretty much your average (insert your 3 star and below hotel here) type rooms. What a disappointment when you've been sold on everything else. And secondly the parking is horrendously expensive and certainly not enough for both hotel structures guests plus those visiting Top of the Hyatt. They also ended up overcharging my account for parking, yikes! Nice try Hyatt, but you still got some work to do.

“Excellent location, clean, and fantastic staff” This hotel is in a wonderful location, very close to Fells Point and the Shot Tower, in a beautiful brick building surrounded by other historic structures and good restaurants. It's true; the parking is expensive, but I didn't need parking, and what would you expect from such a central location? The fitness room was great as well, and the breakfast well run. Would easily recommend.

“Gracious, lovely and wonderful service” I have stayed at the Sofitel three times and it is always a delightful experience. The staff makes every guest feel important and welcome. The rooms are lovely and the location, just off the Magnificent Mile, is terrific. Right now, the rooms are very affordable, though they have been expensive in the past. I paid $139 a night. Since the price was so low, I indulged in room service. I highly recommend the assortment of French cheeses and the Mojitos.

“Great value for money - regal hotel” I'm more of a modern hotel person myself but there is something very nice about an older, well-preserved, regal hotel like the Park Plaza - especially in the winter. PROS - Gorgeous hotel - Amazing public spaces - Comfortable beds - Very clean - Participants in Starwood's Green Housekeeping Program - decline housekeeping and get $5 towards a meal CONS - Small Rooms - Bathrooms are a bit outdated - Not great HVAC, extremely dry air - No Starwood points even though it's a Starwood property

“Bargain price for a great room in NYC” We have stayed at the Carlton several times. It has a very nice lobby and facilities. and the decor is very nice and modern. We were recently booked through my husbands company for one night at a very good rate. The room seemed smaller than we have had in the past and I asked if we could get a larger room. Despite having this low rate they upgraded us to a very large room with a king and a sofa and chair and a very large bath room. Though the hot water faucet did not work very well and the shower head kept turning towards the wall. Also coffee is available 24 hours on the mezzanine. Unfortunately 6am is not the time to get some. It was cold and old.

“Don't be afraid to stay here!” Front desk was warm and very helpful. Rooms are small but well appointed and furnishings and linens were modern and stylish. Yes there was street noise but if you want to be right near the Garden and the bars in that area is this is a great place to stay. If I were staying in Boston and interested in sight seeing I would check to make sure there are no games or concerts that night. Unless you will be one of the ones singing on the street at 2 am!

“Loved it. An oasis in crazy Times Square.” The bell man made the best first impresion when I got out of my cab. He welcomed me by name. It only took seconds but he glanced at my luggage tag and made me feel like The Muse had been doing nothing but waiting for me to get there. I loved my sleek suite on the top floor. The room was polished but also very comfortable. I also liked being able to stay in Times Square, which was central for my work, but being able to leave the crazy energy outside so I could relax and be calm inside. The staff were characteristically helpful (Kimpton employees always are). They pointed me to a nearby vegetarian restaurant, which was great.

“Great Hollywood location” Some negative things... We found a cockroach in the bathroom, but otherwise the rooms were clean. Lots of space in the rooms and our room had a small kitchenette with dining table, fridge and microwave. Breakfast is served in the corridor and there's a patio outside to eat your breakfast. Staff were friendly, though they require you to leave your car keys at the front desk and sometimes (like in our case) move around cars in the very small (but free) parking lot... They put our car in a really tight space and nearly caused my brother to have a meltdown trying to get it out in the morning. This hotel has its charm and feels very 'Hollywood' and the location is great, just next to Hollywood and Vine and the Kodak Theatre. And for any one visiting LA, you should make the effort to take the subway to Downtown LA and visit it. My brother and I did so and saw no fellow tourists, and had a nice experience visiting City Hall were we went to the observation deck (again no tourists) for free to see great views of the city. We even had lunch in the small shop inside City Hall and had some interesting chats with locals, including a city councillor.

“Great stay, perfect for a family” We chose this hotel after a great deal fo research due to having a two bedroom suite. We had never stayed in Soho before but we have a ten month old so we wanted to stay in a little bit more of a neighborhood environment. It was a great find. The rooms were perfect for our needs. We were able to put a crib in one room and hang out in the other after baby bedtime. The location was great. We used a stroller to go everywhere because we have a baby so we did all of our commuting by subway which was extremely simple. The E train is almost right out the front door of the hotel. We used it to go to Flushing Meadows for the US Open, Yankee Stadium, the Financial District and everywhere in between. The staff was excellent. Cullen was a great concierge, Rashawd was an excellent bellman and the rest of the staff was very courteous. They arranged our airport transportation seamlessly. We used the swimming pool in the afternoon on the 7th floor and it was very refreshing. We had a corner room on the 22nd floor that faced NW as one the bedrooms and the view was the best I have ever seen in NYC. We could see the Empire State building, the skyline and Central Park all the way up 6th avenue. The view out the other window was across the Hudson and was gorgeous also. The room has computer controlled curtains, lights and a/c which were great. The television channels had great choices also. The bathrooms were roomy with seperate shower and tub. I cannot imagine that another hotel in NYC is as spacious as the Trump Soho. I didn't use the workout facility but I visited the area and it was a nice room with the cardiovascular equipment facing out for great views. We were not so high that we could not hear street noise but it was not too bad. Within 4 blocks each direction there were restaurants and shopping. A Whole Foods Market was also within walking distance. With a baby, we were close enough to walk to the World Trade Center and Union Square. We made several trios down Spring street to Viva la Crepe which had fantastic crepes and we enjoyed nearby restaurants such as Hundred Acres, Amelias, and Wolfgang puck steakhouse. The hotel rooms and location far exceeded everything we were looking for in our stay. The two bedrooms adjoined through keyed entry way with one room having the living area attached directly. The rooms did have a microwave but only had a mini bar refrigerator that was not exactly designed for storing things and did not have a freezer component for freezing our dry ice packs.

“Great hotel in central Denver location. Minutes away from I-25.” The hotel is 20 minutes away from DIA. There is currently road construction so it may take longer. The hotel staff is great and the facilities good. I found the rooms comparable to other brands like the Hilton. The hotel is not new and is showing its age. The walls between rooms are not fully insulated against noise. I had adjoining rooms, one side was quiet the other not so much due to rowdy neighbors. My son had a room on the 11th floor and he had to put up with noise from a dance floor above. The food service is excellent. Morning brunch for about $14 with made to order omelets and waffles and a variety of side dishes. Staff was excellent. Parking fee applies. Location great for shopping and dining.

“classy hotel must never become part of middle of the road chain.” its used to be classy hotel. its still look classy. however the room decor is dated the service is really not the level of this hotel. the maid service was a speedy one as i went to the street to find out i left my glasses. by that time our room was done. no replacement to my bath wash. I guess they are "eco friendly". hotel. smiling. again one expect more from a palace. i guess but when the palace is own by Sherwood you are doomed ! and i guess the only thing left is the building and the name. ok , some great crown molding. and wide corridors. which clearly they don't make anymore. great courtyard but hey who sleep in the court yard. great Christmas tree. and my favorite bell man Santa. he was funny. the afternoon tea was missing style and service. in whole "we will keep the name and the prices but you will get less and less." they sound like delta/american/united airlines. smiling will i come back? maybe if the price is right~ happy holidays~
“It's a beautiful resort.” The room was very nice. The service was excellent . The location was very convenient. If I go back to Phoenix, I would stay there again.

“così così” ho passato 3 notti nel mese di gennaio 2011. Premesso che LA è una città molto dispersiva che non si può pretendere di "visitare" nel senso canonico del termine, questo albergo direi che tutto sommato è molto buono. Lo staff è indubbiamente gentile e disponibile, ma evitate accuratamente le camere con vista autostrada a meno che non abbiate un sonno profondissimo. L'autostrada è frequentatissima 24 ore su 24 e il rumore è costante. La dependance è un po' lontana dalla reception, ma ha il vantagggio di avere la piscina a portata di mano. Wifi gratuito. Ristorante buono.

“Stuck Staying here” We were booked at another hotel and there was a huge waterline break all around the airport and the marina. Many streets were blocked off. We gave up getting to our original spot and ending up on lost Hotel Circle. Its close to the freeway, in fact we had a lovely view of the freeway, yuk! Our room smelled funny and the bed was too soft. The place was overrun with kids playing in a soccer tournament. Luckily we were exhausted and just happy to have a place to sleep.

“100% Fine” I did two nights here for work. Yes, the executive lounge is underwhelming. I can’t speak for the laundry service mentioned earlier. And yes, it’s near a water reservoir, not a park & pond. None of these are important factors when rating a hotel for me. The service was good, room was clean and quiet, and the beds comfortable. I was very happy with my stay. Note, it’s not in downtown Philly, but that shouldn’t be a mystery with the map displayed on this page. No complaints here, and I would recommend this hotel to most others.

“An Efficient & Tidy Little Hotel” I've stayed here twice on business trips, each of them for 4 days at a time. It's a cute little hotel. The staff is very helpful and the lobby has boba tea, green tea, hot drinks, sandwiches, salad and more. I had a shiatsu massage at the Spa there and it was very good. Just know that Shiatsu massage is not your ordinary deep tissue massage...it's really very different. The room is always clean and I had no complaints about any of it, except maybe that the fridge makes noise all night. The restaurant there is good, but I prefer to walk around the corner to Japanese Village Plaza & eat at Frying Fish. It's amazingly good. And there's the Nijaya Market in Japanese Village too. You can get food there and keep it in your fridge in your room. On Fri & Sat. nights they have outdoor karaoke in the plaza too. Parking your car there is $19.80 a night, with all in & out privileges. I'd stay here again. It's a good value for the price.

“Affinia is Nice Enough” Firstly I loved the room! Roomy nice comfortable bed, very clean nice bath products, good mirrors. Not the suite just the standard room Very nice! Pretty bathroom all very comfortable. The deli around the corner is fantastic! I forget what it's called but begins with an "A". Room service don't bother I paid 28$ for a lobster salad was just awful. The gym was nice and the 2nd floor they had free wine and cheese and coffee. The was something wrong with the phone but maintenance came up almost immediately and fixed the problem. The view sucked and was above some fans but it didn't really bother me. Overall Very good and would definitely go back.

“Grand Hotel, with some maintenance issues” There's nothing like sweeping in the front doors of the Hilton Chicago, a "grand hotel" in the early 20th century tradition. The wide, marble stairways, the high ceilings, the hustle and bustle and delicious smells wafting in from the restaurants -- it's truly like being in a very cool movie, despite the omnipresent conventioneers. Overall our one-night stay was lovely, but marred by some deferred maintenance issues -- and surprising disinterest from the staff. We had a terrific corner room. Although just two double beds, the room itself was quite spacious, with windows on two sides and a partial Lake Michigan view where we were able to watch the fireworks (from Navy Pier?) that began shortly after we arrived. The downside: poor lighting by just two dim bedstand/desk lamps , which could have easily been remedied by adding a floor lamp (certainly plenty of room). The desk was sufficient but with a chair so low as to make it unusable. As others have noted the rooms also lack sufficient electrical outlets, which meant the coffee maker had to be plugged in either at the base of the bedstand lamp or in the bathroom (we couldn't reach the outlet behind the TV/minibar console). The real maintenance issue, though, was the bathroom, with badly peeling paint and some crumbling plaster on the ceiling above the tub, as well as strips of epoxy missing from the tub itself. The drain was also badly clogged -- or simply not up to the task of draining from a high-powered showerhead -- which we didn't discover until in the morning too close to check-out time to call the maintenance staff. (We showered in mid-calf high water; ugh.) When we mentioned this at check-out (the peeling paint , the crumbling plaster, and the nonworking drain), the clerk said simply, "Gosh, I'm sorry to hear that," and proceeded with the check-out transaction. We weren't looking for a discount or a comp, but it's really been on my mind since then that we received such a lackluster response -- perhaps because the staff already knows that the ceilings and the drains need work but can't do anything about it. A gentleman behind on the way said out that this has been a problem in the rooms before when he's stayed there. The bathroom issue really makes it difficult to recommend another stay, although we otherwise loved this grand old hotel.

“Good Business Hotel” The property is good for business travelers not staying too long in DC. I'm not a fan of the atrium design, looks like an indoor motel. But overall the place in clean, despite rooms needing updating. Complimentary breakfast is a nice touch. Hotel was very quiet - slept well.

“Beautiful public spaces, poor rooms, poor service.” This hotel is located conveniently on Market Street within walking distance of the Embarcadero. There is the F line streetcar which will take you to Fisherman's Wharf in one direction and Castro Street in the other. It couldn't be more convenient. It is also in walking distance of Union Square. The main floor of this hotel is beautiful, full of old world charm. The hallways are also very attractive. The guest rooms are very out of date. The windows are not double-glazed and the street noise is very disturbing. I was on the 8th floor and was still awoken by a trumpeter on the sidewalk. The walls of the room are also not sound proof. I could hear the television programs from both neighboring rooms until 2am on my first two nights at the hotel. The bathroom is poorly equipped. There is very little counter space and I ended up knocking my shaving cream and saline solution on the ground several times. The shower stall has not been equipped with a curved shower bar. On top of this there is a huge metal railing affixed to the wall. I found myself alternating between fighting with the shower curtain and then brushing my back against the freezing metal of the hand rail. There is a shortage of electrical outlets in the room. I had to charge my cellphone in the bathroom overnight. The service from the staff is lamentable. My final bill was incorrect. I spent a total of 3 hours waiting for a corrected bill. Housekeeping is also very poor in the rooms.

“Good example of an Embassy with a decent location.” Staff was fantastic at this stay. Though it is one of the smaller Embassy Suites (7 floors and a shared bar with the managers reception). I'd stay here again. The room and cleanliness standards are what would be expected from an Embassy Suites.

“Perfect location for historic hotel” Just got back from a weekend in Charlotte where we stayed at the Dunhill Hotel. This is a historic hotel so the rooms are on the small side, but nicely decorated. The location is great for walking around the downtown area. We enjoyed the hotel except the service was exceptionally bad. We tried to get ice from room service. After 30 minutes we went to the bar. On the weekend we stayed at the hotel the temperature was in the low 80's. The AC could not keep up in the room; I would hate to think about the comfort of the room in the dead of summer. Breakfast was included in our rate. The breakfast was quite good but the servers were surly---I felt like I had to beg for coffee! Front desk was neither helpful nor friendly. If they could upgrade service levels this would be a real gem.

“nice gem in downtown Columbus” OH, I wish I knew about this place when I had to stay in Columbus last November for a conference. Very spacious, well-appointed, immaculately clean hotel room, with a full kitchen. Felt more like an apt. than a hotel room. The complimentary breakfast was a nice touch. The only downside was trying to spot the hotel while driving at night--the sign isn't large or bright enough. No problems, no drama. That's what you want when you are traveling.

“Wonderful hotel experience - stellar view of Manhattan skyline!” We recently spent 3 nights at the Ink48 in NYC and we are so glad we choose this hotel. It had been several years since our last trip to NYC and we were very picky about our current accommodation choice. I did a not of research and comparison shopping as we wanted an upscale modern hotel with decent square footage (including a nice large bathroom), a good location and a stellar view. This combination can be difficult to find in NYC without paying a ridiculous amount of money. Many NYC hotel rooms are very, very small - the last time we were in town our room was so tiny it was down right claustrophobic. We found everything we wanted at Ink48. We booked a City View King room. It was spacious and spotless. Our view of the Manhattan skyline from the 15th floor was amazing day and night. The décor is “Kimpton Cool” and the service was spot-on during our entire stay. The bed was dreamy and the linens and towels were great. We had dinner and drinks at PRINT, the on-site restaurant; we enjoyed the food and service although it is a bit pricy. Our waiter looked like Prince. The rooftop bar is worth having a look as the views are amazing. Again, drinks are pricey at $15+ each. Regarding the location of Ink48; it’s about a 15 minute walk (1/2 mile) straight down 48th or 47th to the heart of Times Square. We never felt unsafe day or night. We stopped in for yummy by-the-slice pizza right around the corner at Hell’s Kitchen Pizza. There are also little grocers, drug and liquor stores within short walks. Cab fare to/from LaGuardia is approximately $40. We had a great experience at Ink48 and would return in a heartbeat.

“La Quinta is Spanish for..."Next to Denny's"” Stayed here for a Friday night trip to the Riverwalk. I was not expecting the hotel to be as nice as it was! Check in was standard. Went up to the room and discovered there were some small black curly hairs lingering in the shower area. Eww. Went back downstairs and explained that housekeeping should probably revisit our room. Was promptly moved to another room and given two free drinks in the hotel bar. YAY! I certainly wasn't about to let those drink coupons go to waste, so we got dressed and returned to the bar. For a Friday night, the bar was empty and that was perfect. I forgot all about the problem with the first room...thank you, drink tickets! We spent the rest of the night on the Riverwalk which culminated in a trip to Denny's on our walk back to the hotel. Yes, Virginia, there is a Denny's right next door. If you are wondering, the hotel is about 1/3 of a mile away from the Riverwalk itself and right off of I-35/I-37. Well within walking distance to major downtown landmarks and across the street from the Rivercenter Mall. The room itself was well-sized, comfortable and clean; full of useful amenities. We didn't make it to the breakfast buffet. Parking is extra, and they do offer valet service but it really wouldn't be worth it as the regular parking lot is right in front of the main entrance. Overall, we were very happy with our stay and would visit this hotel again.

“great location” great location. we got a suite booked. it is technically 1.5 rooms. Housed 3 guests easily. Could have housed 4 or even 5! Service here was great. Everyone was friendly. Would stay here again. The lobby is big enough to hang out for a ride or even wait for people. The only draw back is that you need your room key to get in after 10pm. Its a bit of a hassle but I understand the reasoning.

“good hotel for a stay in Philadelphia” I stayed here for a conference and was not disappointed. My room was small but I was alone so it didn't matter. The bedding was very comfortable and inviting. The room was clean and nicely decorated. No refrigerator but there was a thermostat. The conferance facilities were nice and the service good. The conference food was only so so though. The hotel is just a few blocks from Rittenhouse Square and the good shopping on Walnut Street. It is only 1/2 mile from 30th street Amtrak.

“Maybe it was an off day” I am not sure if it was an off day for the hotel or me. The trip started badly with a flight delay, I arrived at the hotel where a new employee was being instructed on how to check me in. She has to recreate my entire reservation for some reason, which took about 10 minutes, I was already late, and neither seemed concerned with pleas regarding my missing an appointment. One of the two elevators was out of service; I waited 5 minutes for the operational elevator to arrive. I get to the door of my room, the key doesn't work. I call downstairs and request someone bring up a key, I waited 10 minutes, I finally went downstairs to the front desk and got it myself. The room decor is lovely. I was in room 803. I had some complaints regarding the upkeep of the room. The enamel paint on the bathtub was peeling, as the paint on the mirror above the sink. The outlet in the bathroom was not working, and the television was blurry. Other than the above complaints I loved the room. They had a teapot, which was electric and so speedy. They had a great selection of teas. The room was an L shape, with a nice desk area. The only other problem was the noise. The hotel has thin walls; someone down the hall left early and the sound of their door slamming shut almost knocked me out of bed. Speaking of which, the beds are wonderful! I Love the kimpton chair and opt for their hotels any day of the week, but $220 for a Sunday night stay was a bit much. I think next time I am heading for the Helix or the Monaco instead.

“One extremely happy guest!” Booking a hotel in SF for New Year was quite hard and I wasn't massively enthusiastic about booking a (chain) Hilton for such a special trip. But, wow, I was wrong. This place is amazing! 2000 rooms but still felt intimate, friendly and warm. The best Hilton I've ever stayed in, it's made me re-think about them 100% positively! I've stayed at the Waldorf Astoria (also a Hilton family hotel) and this compares to that hands down.

“GOOD HOTEL/GREAT LOCATION” We booked an 8 night stay in Washington through Hotwire requesting a hotel in Dupont circle .I was a little dissapointed when we were allocated the Helix as many previous reviews stated that hotel was in area that had few attractions.I have to say that Logan circle is a fantastic neighbourhood & we were delighted with our stay in the Helix. Okay the hotel is not next door to a metro stop but a pleasent 10 min walk will get you to a choice of 3 different stations & the system is a dream to use with probably the friendliest staff possible.The Helix is only a 15 min walk to the White House & 10 minutes to Dupont Circle.We mostly used Mc Pherson Square station as it is on the main line to the majority of the tourist attractions.A $39 -7 day fast pass is great value for the metro . The staff in the Helix are extremely friendly & we were checked in by an very bubbly Ashley who seemed to be there at every turn during our entire stay-does she ever get home ?.Our room was much larger than I expected with lovely comfortable bedding ,nice seating area & a compact but practical bathroom.The room colours werent as loud as I was expecting & you get used to them very quickly.The bar area was certainly funky & is a great change from the normal bland hotel bar.The Helix also serves complimentary coffee & tea at the bar in the mornings . Two minutes from the hotel there is a 7 eleven for the small goodies & 1 block away there is a Wholefood supermarket which also does a wonderful selection of cooked foods if you want a lazy night in your room.Opposite the wholefoods there is a local bar Stoneys which does a mean burger & next door the more upmarket Logan Tavern .A lot of people seem to head to Dupont Circle for evening food but there is a great selection of restaurants closer to the Helix on 14th street right up to the buzz of U street.Choices of American,Italian,Thai ,Seafood ,Ethiopian,Chinese etc.The area around the Helix has a nice neighbourhood feel to it which comes alive in the evenings rather than some of the downtown areas that can be very quiet.We certainly enjoyed our stay at the Helix especially with the $109 Hotwire price & loved our holiday in Washington -great city -THANKS.

“Unfit for fitness” The room I stayed in was very nicely appointed and clean. Fine location for those traveling for business (LA Mart). HOWEVER, here are a few caveats: There is no minibar. I personally don't use them, except to store water & soda purchased elsewhere but a friend needs one to store medication and you have to pay extra each night for a room with a minibar. The pool looks really nice in the hotel photos, doesn't it? Well, it must have been taken with a special camera lens because the pool is really the size of a large tub. It's about 10 ft long. If you push off the "far" end you will reach the other side in about 2 seconds without the need to actually swim. So, if you want to sunbathe, you're in luck. If you want to swim, look elsewhere. While I was there they even left a letter in guestrooms saying that they were closing the pool for a private function on the terrace, which was fine by me since I couldn't use the pool for exercise. However, when I next saw the "closed" pool, they had put a, I kid you not, rug over it and taped the edges. All I could picture was someone at a company fuction walking over it and falling in - like a cartoon character. And my last comment... the "fitness room." HAHAA! There is one elliptical, 2 treadmills, and an archaic stairmaster and bike. On top of that, there were always about 10 people wanting to work out, so there was a line. And the room wasn't air conditioned properly so that you were working out in about 80 degree heat.

“Très bien” Hotel propre, cosy. Bon accueil. Un peu cher, mais finalement bon rapport qualité prix pour NYC. Bien situé: Upper East side, à 2 minutes (2 blocks) de la station de metro de la ligne 1 qui mène à Downtown (et aussi du bus M104). A 3 blocks du musée d'histoire naturelle et de Central Park. Pas de bruit MAIS climatisation bruyante; et meme s'il fait frais dehors on ne peut ouvrir les fenêtres que sur 10 cm. Déception à la fin du séjour: on nous avait dit pouvoir garder la chambre 2 heures de plus pour se changer avant l'aéroport. Finalement ça n'a pas été possible (60 dollars l'heure sup!!).

“Loved It” I stayed here for two nights. It is a really nice property in a great location. Room was comfortable with a good bed, nice lighting, good tv, and I loved the shower! I had a double which was great for one person. Others in my group had a queen and they thought it was small. Room was very clean. My room overlooked 47th and was naturally noisy. Take earplugs if you are a light sleeper. Service is really friendly. You will enjoy staying here.

“Great Location” I really liked this hotel. I didn't expect it to be as nice when seeing it from the outside, but the room was great, I'm wondering if it was recently remodeled. A good size for a NY hotel room, and I've been in quite a few now. Very good for travelling with children...we had a 16, 13 and 7 year old and they accomodated the 5 of us very well. Central to many NY locations, Times Square, 5th Ave Shops, Central Park, great places to eat.

“Great Hotel” We stayed at the Philadelphia Marriott for a weekend in June after a week at the Jersey Shore. This is a really large hotel, which suits our tastes, located in the heart of Philadelphia. We found the lobby and open spaces to be bright, upbeat and polished. We used the fitness center and really liked it since the equipment was new and the fitness center was just beautiful. Having said that, it could be larger for a hotel of that size. Our room was compact, but again bright, clean and well laid out. The front desk staff indicated that our room had recently been updated, and it showed it. All in all, a great, large, well appointed hotel in the heart of Philly. I already have a reservation for a conference in October and I am looking forward to staying again.

“Top Class Convention Center Hotel” I was with a large group of well traveled industry executives who was able to experience the hotel within its first week of opening. You could tell the hotel ready for us as the staff was a mix of new employees and .experienced managers from other properties. The public areas are full of local artwork which is a refreshing idea. This hotel is very concerned with it's impact on the environment, so you will see many of the LEEDS type of initiatives present. I would have to say, this is one of the better hotels to be connected to a convention center. Now all the city needs to do is completely renovate the Dallas Convention center which is old and tired. AVT audio visual is in house and they did an awesome job with our meeting. They are the premier AV company to have in a hotel environment.

“W Lakeshore is RUDE - bad choice” Stayed here Dec. 18-21 for a getaway with my girlfriend. DO NOT STAY HERE, fellow travellers. BAD experience. A hotel that tries to be hip and cool and instead is loud and obnoxious (there is a reason this place is ranked near bottom at #98). First problem was walking into lobby Friday night - as loud as a nightclub. Sounded like a party going on in the lobby (!). Who wants that after a long flight? Decor/ambience was nice and modern - too bad the people made it seem so awful. In the elevator, got stuck with drunk club kids whooping it up heading up to the rooftop bar (horrible repetitive techno music blaring over elevator speakers, too). Checked into room - decor was nice, larger than average room. Had a nice lake view room (had to pay $50 per night beyond Priceline rate, btw) for a total of $165 night. No complaints. Bit pricey compared to other options - Swisshotel and Hyatt were less. Upon coming back at night, we got denied entry to the rooftop bar (private party). Then upon going back to our room on 27th floor, some drunk people were partying in the hallway (!) and we could hear neighbors talking through paper thin walls. We complained to management - they did nothing, as far as we could tell. Next morning, the room service people banged on our door at 8:30am and woke us up. We told them to go away and they came back again at 9:15am. We complained to management about having our sleep disturbed and they seemed oblivious - as if this is how all hotels operate? Never in my entire hotel life has room service tried to clean a room at 8:30am in the morning. Poor management decisions by W staff here. Ruined our entire stay. End result, $500 in hotel money down the drain. I will never stay at another W (Starwood) hotel ever again. Too many other better options in Chicago - Sofitel, Swisshotel, Hyatt. The kind of person who likes this hotel are 25 year old frat kids, who want to run around screaming drunk till the wee hours of the morning. Poor value. AVOID at all costs.
“シカゴ一” 「シカゴ一」といっても、客室数がですが。。流石に世界屈指のハイアットグループの本拠地のメインホテルだけあって、広さは半端ではないですが、その分特別なホテルにはなりえません。 どうしても最大公約数的なホテルになってしまいますので、ゆっくりホテルでリラックスという訳にはいきません。立地はいいですし、ビジネスユースに最適といいたいのですが、それにしては値段が高すぎるような気がします。

“Nice place, ask for an inside room” Staff is excellent, executive level is amazing, rooms are neat and clean. My room was an outside room (on the street) and it was very noisy. But that's my only complaint. Elevators are quick. My room was a smaller rooms, but was not tiny. Very short block walk to the metro and only a block and a half from the White House. Lots of places to eat near by. Good location.

“Good location, poor nights sleep” The location is great and walkable to downtown Indianapolis. Service upon check in was great. Our first (and only) nights sleep was awful. Our room (220) was above the hotel pool, which is open 6 AM - 11 PM. We were disturbed multiple times through the evening and then starting at 6 AM. Hotel staff was unable, unwilling, or possibly unconcerned to move us to another room. This was a bit surprising given the warm welcome upon arrival. For the first time I checked out of a hotel early due to the sleep quality and unresponsiveness of the hotel. We found the Courtyard near the airport has much quieter rooms.

“Great room, location, and service in midtown Manhattan” I picked this Courtyard hotel for a recent weekend getaway to New York City based on its location, price, and good Tripadvisor reviews. I was not disappointed. I had a king bedroom up on the 25th floor. It was enormous by Manhattan standards, comfortable and clean. The AC controls worked great (not always the case in hotel rooms) -- which I especially appreciated after returning damp and shivering and in need of a quick warm-up. The TV had a decent selection of channels and the bathroom was large enough for my needs. Service was friendly and prompt -- for instance, I requested a mini-fridge and it arrived in only a few minutes, delivered with a smile. I peeked in on the fitness room, and it had several cardio machines as well as free weights and a weight machine. Elevators worked well and were always quick to arrive. Wireless Internet was free (hallelujah!) and worked very well. The location was convenient and the neighborhood had plenty of good restaurants, coffee shops, and stores, including a Duane Reade drugstore next door. My only complaint was that the bed was very hard. Some people might like this, but I woke up a little bit sore each morning. Otherwise, I had a great experience at this Courtyard and would gladly return some day.
“non male, location perfetta” Non eccellente, ho soggiornato in camera superior al 48 piano. Pulizia discreta, camera non enorme ma sufficiente, bagno nella norma. Reception cortese e rapida.

“GREAT EVERYTHINGevereverything prt” I stayed at the hotel only one nite as I was due at a weddig at another hotel. This hotel was PERFECT!. I got the room on Hotwire and thought I may suffer, but I was wrong.. A very nice mand from reservation named Bobbie helped me.(He needs a reward) I told him I may be early and he said it would be no problem if i needed to check in. as it was my plane was late so early check was not needed I had room 232, over looking the street, I heard "0" street noise. The beds were so comfortable , bedroom set up so perect. And on the desk Bobbie from reservations sent to fruit plate, Shows there great servive, I did not eat ot have room service so cannot comment on those, I ahad a charming turn down employeee that was 5 Star, (im sorry didnt get her name). STAY hee for a great hotel vivist.

“The Best” I live in the neighborhood and needed to move to stay in a hotel very last minute late on a Sunday night. W Union Square was available (very lucky). Check in was quick and perfect. Lobby is beautiful. Guestroom was on a high floor in the back of the building with a nice view east over Irving Place. Everything perfect, super comfy bed, good room size, really high ceilings, beautiful bathroom, great Bliss amenities, friendly employees, both wake up call and backup wake up call came on time and did I mention the awesome bed? Hope to never need a hotel under these circumstances again, but either way, the place came through in a pinch. Very grateful.

“Expensive fun” SPG knows how to make a hotel look good. And this hotel has been prefectly art directed. And SPG also knows how to charge for EVERYTHING. A muffin and 1/4 cup of fruit in the lobby was $28 .. the coffee in the lobby was free UNTIL I added the food then it was no longer free. However the LA and NY TIMES were available at no charge. SLS Los Angeles is Hollywood hip and expense account priced. But would some one please suggest that the room designers actually spend a night in their dungeons. The room I had was ample but the bed sat in the middle of the room. There was not a comfortable chair. You could either sit on a backless settee or an uncomfortable 'office' chair. If you wished to sit while applying make up or fixing your hair good luck. If you are not a fan of liquid soap good luck. But more than anything each room should have a warning sign explaining the very cool slate or is it granite and glass shower. In order to keep from being soaked before you are ready you must enter the shower and position yourself behind the shower head and then play with the water temperature until you can actually enter the stream. Oh and make sure you remember to bring your towel from the towel stand some 8 feet from the shower, otherwise it is wet and chilly prance to collect it. Staff is best trained SPG staff I have ever encountered. Usual Hollywod movie star wannbes but unlike all the Ws this time with brains

“Best place to be in Boston! For pleasure or work!” This place has it all: Location, service, cleanliness, spacious bedrooms, cozy ambiance and good price! Perfect option for any kind of trip as it is walking distance from Back Bay as well as North End....

“良いホテルでした” ボストンの中心部から若干離れていますが気になる距離ではないです。 Harvard Universityまで1マイル位の立地です。 まず、スタッフが親切でとても良かったです。 部屋も結構広く清潔感があり、本当に居心地が良かったです。 ボストンのホテルは宿泊料金が結構しますが、ここのホテルは価格と比べても満足度の高いホテルです。 インターネットもワイヤレスで利用出来ました。 設備も必要になる物は揃っています。 また利用したいと感じたホテルです。

“A wonderful hotel in which to end our 3 week holiday in the USA” My husband and I spent three weeks in the USA in July 2012, flying in and out of Houston. I had booked nearly everything in advance, but, although I had researched hotels for our final three nights, in the rush beforehand, I hadn't got round to booking anything and for the first 2.5 weeks we were too busy having a great time to think about the last couple of hotels. So, we booked this hotel only about 36 hours before our arrival there and while I was doing so, my computer crashed which meant that I was unable to request (at a reduced price) a room with a view of the Town Lake and downtown Austin. On our arrival, we were shown to a very nice room on the 8th floor overlooking a nearby hotel and the carpark. I mentioned to the bell boy that I had hoped to be able to upgrade and he immediately encouraged me to call the Front Desk.(I only wish I could recall his name) and he also said that the rooms with patios were really nice. (I had 'rejected' the idea of a 'shared patio', as I feared that I could find we were sharing with smokers). Anyhow, after a bit of discussion, front desk offered us a room with a view and a patio for an extra $25 (plus tax) per night, which we accepted. This was fantastic; the room was on the end of the row, on the 3rd floor, overlooking the lovely landscaped pool, the Town lake and Downtown Austin. We loved it and would return there on a future visit if the price were right! The 'shared' patio was a bit of a misnoma, as there was a low hedge between us and the next patio, but we could have accessed that patio. There was noone in the next room, so we were able to make the most of the extra space on our patio for ourselves. On our last morning a construction workers' conference was beginning and there were men smoking on a nearby patio, but, as we packing up in our room, this didn't trouble us. This hotel had all the advantages of being close to downtown (we walked everywhere), but, at the same time, had the parking advantages of a motel - ie no underground parking and the option to self park with ease. We didn't eat any meals there (breakfast wasn't included in our room rate), but the front desk service was second to none. The pool was fantastic with the water being a lovely temperature - ie not too cold! We stayed for only two nights but wishes we could have stayed longer. The room cost more than any others on our trip, but it was well worth it.

“the difference between good and 'outstanding'” we arrived late with the dreaded news that our room had been inadvertantly double-booked and with an apology and a promise of true compensation, we were chauferred off to the nearby Hilton for the night. The next day upon early check in, the hotel manager himself came to greet and personally escort us to our 'upgrade' - a 3-room luxury suite accompanied by chilled champagne, flowers, a letter of apology , free drinks voucher in their incredible Redwood bar and free breakfasts for the duration of our stay. For the next four days we were treated like royalty in one of the finest hotels I have ever stayed in.
