The Asia de Cuba restaurant is superb, the Redwood Bar an experience and our whole stay perfectly memorable. What a difference a great hotel manager can make. Thank you Steven - we will be back!

“Housekeeping annoying!” Room was fine, what you'd expect from a Hilton. Front desk staff seemed annoyed every time I talked with them. One afternoon we came back to rest up before heading out for the evening, and put do not disturb sign on door. Someone knocked on the door to offer us some free water. We didn't answer. Then they called us on the phone, and I said no thanks, we're sleeping. Then they called AGAIN. waking us a third time. I also found the view of Ground Zero pretty depressing.

“good choice” Omni was a solid choice. Clean relatively spacious room. Upgraded to a "signature" room. Price was right for San Fran over new years. Wlaking distance to Chinatown, North Beach/Little Italy. A cable car runs in front of hotel up to Van Ness where there is a good movie theatre. Highlight of trip was walking tour of San Fran from Chinatown Alleyway Tours. They have a website and you book online. Also, if you like bookstores, City Lights is a must along with the new Cody's bookstore by Market St. Back to the hotel, a good choice/location, but nothing "fancy". Note: Cab from SFO airport should be about $35 to $40. Avoid the SuperShuttle unless you want to visit all the hotels in Union Sq.

“Not a 5 Star Property” I thought the site of the Hotel was not optimum, seeming to be in a sleezier part of SFO. We were bombarded by pan handlers on the street. Hilton calls this property "Hilton on Union Square" It is not. It's four blocks from Union Square. The cafe, Urban Tavern was very hard surface, and uninviting. While the breakfast was exceptional, we spent no other time there. My wife and I stay at 5 star hotels, and I am a Hhonors Diamond. We expected this to be in that category. It wasn't. The room in Tower 1 4272 was nice, but a very ordinary hotel room. No robe available in the room, which is a mistake. Despite the Front Desk accommodations to our needs, I feel this is not a property that we will return to, despite being a HHonors Diamond.

“Laughably Bad!” A friend and I made a hastily planned trip to SF last spring. We were expecting to stay at nearby hotel (I can’t remember which) based on a recommendation from a co-worker, but when we arrived they turned out to have no vacancy (and we didn’t have a reservation). We were referred to the Astoria. We walked in the door and asked if they had any rooms, they did and told us the walk-in rate would be about $85 plus tax. The clerk handed us the room key, which was a physical key, not a keycard. We stepped into what was quite possibly the most rickety elevator every built. I’d never been afraid of an elevator before I used this thing. Our room had two tiny single beds. Overall it just felt dirty. The windows were wide open when we walked in (even though it was quite cold outside) and we either couldn’t figure out how to get the heater working or it just didn’t work. It was about 1am and there was a ton of noise from down on the street. The TV looked like something from the early 80s and barely got reception on any of the channels. The bathroom was just creepy. They did give us two “continental breakfast” cards, but we weren’t about to trust any food from the Astoria. We grabbed out bags the next morning and walked down to Union Square where we checked into the Westin. The difference was night and day. For a little less than twice as much money we stayed in a hotel that was infinitely nicer. Avoid this place unless you’re looking for an experience you can laugh at in the future.

“Dependable offering - close to airport - will stay again” I travel to Phoenix for business about once a quarter for business and have stayed at this property twice now. Both times I have found that: -- The room was clean, and the photos on Travelocity etc are a true representation of what you get -- Rooms are a "suite" that I expect from Doubletree including separate sleeping area and microwave and small fridge -- The front desk staff is above average especially for an airport location -- The breakfast buffet was free and not very crowded (I only stay mid-week when families etc are not around like weekends) -- Parking was available and free The complaints on noise likely come from this location having open common courtyards - not a closed "box" design. I have really not had an issue though with noise. In my view this property is a safe bet for Phoenix airport stays - and I will use it again in the future for my business trips.

“Great place to stay in Downtown- visit the lounge on 35th floor!” The most confusing part of finding this hotel was the hidden underground valet. Although I will excuse it since they have a waiting area complete with printers so you can check in for your flight while you wait for your car! Nice touch. We checked in and were given a room in the yellow tower on the 20th floor. Nice views, the service at the lobby bar was quick and wen I sent back a drink because it didn't taste right they brought me a replacement to my satisfaction. We went to a game at Staples center and this was very closeby- about a $6 taxi ride or about 8-10 blocks. Do NOT miss Bonavista revolving lounge and the souvenir drink glasses, we had such a great time. Our air conditioning decided to heat up to 90 degrees at 1:30am and staff was in our room within 5 minutes of our call to fix it! I was impressed with the friendly and attentive service at every restaurant down to the valets and maintenance staff. While the room leaves a bit to be desired- rather small for $200 the views and the staff make this hotel a charm when visiting Los Angeles. I would definitely consider staying here again if I were in the area.

“my new favorite place” My hubby and I travel to Chicago annually and stayed here at the recommendation of our friends for the first time this past weekend. we took an early flight and were allowed to pre check in (8 a.m.) and our room was ready by noon. they upgraded us to a corner suite which over looked the Chicago river. The bed and linens were wonderful!! I have no complaints about the hotel employees and felt like they really tried to make our stay as enjoyable as possible. I have only two things that I didn't like: *lighting in the room was horrible, especially the bathroom. they do have a make up mirror but the room was soo dark! this could easily be fixed and i'm over it :) *two drinks at the bar in the lobby (bacardi coke and a grey goose gimlet) were 27.00. I understand we are in Chicago but it just seemed excessive. the bartender was very nice and the bar was welcoming. other than that, i have nothing at all to say that isn't 100% positive! it may be worth noting that i've stayed in the Four Seasons, Hotel Palomar, and Hotel Sax while visiting chicago. I would say the Westin is my new favorite along with Palomar. we'll be back !

“Good Value at the Homewood” I had the good fortune to have chosen a very nice hotel in the Homewood for a convention last week. I and two of my colleagues chose a 2-bedroom suite here for 3 nights, and it turned out to be an excellent choice. We paid $224/night, which may seem like it's high, but for the period in which we were staying, that was close to the price for just a plain old double room in many other places that were close to the convention. Instead, we had a very large suite with a combination kitchen/living area, a d/d room and an extremely large king room. There were also 2 bathrooms, which was great. The staff were all exceedingly friendly and courteous. They even went above and beyond in a couple of ways. Most notably, when we were checking out, one of my colleagues had had her suitcase ripped by the baggage handling when we came in, and she asked the front desk if they had any duct tape. She was immediately on the walkie-talkie with maintenance, and in 5 minutes, they had some tape for her to bind her suitcase. That's good service. Everything else was quite nice. The breakfast/reception room has a nice view of this quiet section of the Riverwalk; it's very pleasant in the morning. The breakfast itself was terrific. Bacon, sausage patties, and eggs were provided along with a very nice assortment of the usual continental items. The coffee that was provided (all day, by the way) was exceptionally good for this type of buffet. The evening manager's receptions were, for me, a godsend. My colleagues were quite enamored of Mexican, which I am not particularly fond of, and they also liked to eat later than me. I would go out with them and just have a light snack, but before that, the evening offerings (even on Friday--rare for Homewood!) were more than adequate to count as evening meals. :) Even the frozen margaritas were surprisingly good! The location of the hotel on the Riverwalk was very nice as well. It was a pleasant 10-minute walk to the Convention Center in the morning, without ever having to step out onto the busy streets. Overall, we were very heartily pleased with this establishment. When I have a chance to return to San Antonio for a more leisurely stay, this is where I'll be.

“Great Location” We chose the Omni for its location. It is a comfortable walk to most of the attractions (including the Wharf) we wanted to visit and for those further away the cable car stops almost outside the front door. The front desk staff were informative and helpful. Fresh fruit was also available in the entry (a nice touch). Our room was on the 17th floor and had an attractive city and small harbor view. The room was comfortable, clean and well serviced. We had one in room meal which was very good (creme brulee' was excellent). Breakfast was good with window tables giving an interesting street view. One waiter (male) did not seem to fully understand our requests. However he was the only staff member that was not overly helpful or did not seem very friendly. Although the Omni is not a cheap option it is close to many tourist attractions and shopping. I would not hesitate stay in this hotel again when visiting San Francisco.

“Suitable Hotel, Nothing Special” I spent several weeks at this hotel while traveling for business. I found the hotel staff to be curteous and kind and the hotel itself to be perfectly suitable, but nothing really out of the ordinary. The rooms are all plenty sizeable, clean enough, but a bit dated. The workout facility is small, with few machines, and there is an indoor pool. The surrounding area is pretty good, with several chain restaurants and a movie theater within walking distance, and it's off of the highway - a short drive from the airport. SPG Platinum members get free breakfast as well. My biggest pet peeve was entering the bathroom and having to unplug the bathtub drain upon every visit - I don't want to touch the germy plug, and do they really think that many people are going to take a bath??? Overall, it's a fine hotel for a quick business stay here or there, but not a great spot for a family vacation or a luxurious getaway.

“Beautiful hotel with very nice rooms” We had a very nice stay at the Doubletree in the financial district. We got this reservation through Priceline at a great price, but after my reservation was confirmed, I called to ensure we could get a double bed...that is when they told me I would have to pay $60 more to have a double room since apparently Priceline doesn't guarantee that. That was a bummer, but there was nothing we could do about it. Just keep that in mind if you use Priceline for NYC hotels (this has happened before to us but only in NYC). Upon arriving, we found a parking garage right across the street from the hotel that was about $15 cheaper than valeting so we were happy about that. The lobby is really nice with lots of plush couches. At check-in, they gave each us a warm cookie which was SO good. Such a nice welcoming gift :) We got a room on the 43rd floor which had a great view of the new tower being built near Ground Zero. We were really pleased with that as we got some great photos. The room wasn't very big but it had everything needed plus was very clean. The bathroom was very nice, but small as well (to be expected in NYC). The financial district is very quiet during the weekends which was nice. We felt safe and got a good nights sleep on the comfy beds. One other thing to mention is that the hallways are very very narrows so it's almost impossible to pass someone if you are coming through with luggage. It can be very uncomfortable. Other than that (and the extra price we had to pay), we had a great experience.

“Great location for wandering the city!” This hotel is located in a great area for wandering around the city. Very convenient walk to Penn Station, Flatiron area and Chelsea. Although the rooms and lobby area are quite small, I found mine to be comfortable for two people for one night. The rooms were very very clean as well. It was also remarkably quiet, considering the location, as 29th street was not as busy. We were on a high floor, so that may be one reason it was so quiet.The elevators are slower, especially when you are on a higher floor. What impressed me the most about this hotel was the front office staff. So friendly and they remembered our names.... We did not utilize their restaurant or bar.

“Great Value & Location for Washington DC” Hotel is 10 minutes walk from the Washington DC Conventions Center and ideal for attending events there. If you don't mind walking you can also reach the White House on foot in about 25 minutes. Hotel is in an older building but rooms have been renovated and are comfortable. Breakfast Area is also renovated and nice. Breakfast itself is the typical Comfort Inn stuff, so ok. I don't like the styrofoam plates and think they should switch to something more environmentally friendly such as paper. Front Desk Manager was very friendly and even gave me an early check in. Have booked the same hotel again for a trip in October.

“Great Renovated Suites at Trump International” We stayed at the Trump for Mother's Day weekend in an Executive City View Suite. Elmo and all the front desk staff were really helpful when making our reservations. Our family prefers a suite that has the bedroom separate from the living room and the executive city view does. We asked for a renovated suite and were given one. Didn't love the view, next time I would try a park view. The rooms were spotless and beautifully appointed. The new Kitchens are beautiful with great appliances. Housekeeping even put my toddlers sippy cups into the Miele dishwasher and ran a load for me. Now, I know people don't come to NYC to watch TV but the TV in the bedroom has the best picture on a television that I have ever seen. I don't know what kind of LG it was but It's not a regular hd plasma. We asked the staff to remove some of the more breakable objects in the room because of our 2 year old and they were more than happy to oblige. The room's were a little crowded and felt much bigger without the coffee table. The Columbus circle location is great for going to the park or broadway but not really for major shopping. I usually stay on the upper east side so I can dash into stores and do some quick damage while pushing an uncooperative toddle in a stroller. That didn't happen this trip because by the time we walked all the way down 59th st to 5th ave he was more than uncooperative and in no mood for shoe shopping at bergdorf's. On the whole, I think the renovated rooms are wonderful and a great value for a family looking for a modern suite in NYC.

“Excellent Hotel in the Center of Everything” Stayed here Memorial Day weekend--2nd time in this hotel on a Priceline stay. Service: 4* Room: 3 1/2 * Food Service: 3 1/2* Overall: 4* Overall, an excellent visit. Wonderful early check-in, clean and convenient room, helpful staff. Concierges good but not great, you generally got the feel you were wasting their time. Housekeeping also good but not great, missed adding new TP and Kleenex (though staff quickly replaced). For the location (close to everything), facilities and staff. Overall, well worth the bid--we'd definitely stay again.

“Geat atmosphere, the ducks are cool, the rooms are small” The lobby with its piano player and intricate decor is very impressive. You can hang out eat , drink, watch the ducks and socialize. Yes the rooms are small, but who cares. I found it was part of the charm of this historic building. They have all you need, particularly for solo travellers. Service was great, the brought a fancy bottle of water to the room and chocolates. The bed was comfortable. The duck march is great and visiting their home on the roof is also a must. Be careful on the streets surrounding the hotel at night. One block away from this marvellous hotel lurks the scum of the earth (drug dealers, weirdos). You can find much cheaper hotels a few steps away but this one is unique and worth the extra money if you can afford it.

“Gutes Hotel” Das Holiday Inn liegt in einer Seitenstrasse des berühmten Walk of Fame und dem Chines Theatre, dementsprechend sind diese Sehenswürdigkeiten innerhalb weniger Minuten zu Fuss erreichbar. Ausblick auf die Hollywood Hills sind vom Hotel hervorragend. Das Hotel selbst ist sauber, die Zimmer geräumig und in einem guten Zustand. Empfehlenswert !!!!

“Great Price & New Look!” Ok, now I wish I would have written a re- view for the last 4 times we have stayed here! They were at the beginning of re-doing the hotel last I wrote about it in 2005 I think it was....and yes...it is done and it never was THAT bad to start with. Look you guy's, you can't beat the price, It is a nice hotel, you have a bar & restaurant with GREAT prices and lot's of GOOD restaurants in the area! Great parking (undercover you guy's... for no EXTRA charge) try other hotels get a better price and then see if you don't pay an additional $10-$20 a day folks!!!!!!! For parking!!!! You don't know that when booking on line for an in expensive hotel with all the frills, next to all the attractions and wanting the bang for your buck. Oh what a surprise when you get hit for parking (and it's not covered to boot) no retaurant inside with good prices or a bar. This hotel is great for the business traveler or the leisure traveler having fun. After traveling and staying in hotels all across southeren CA to L.A. for years mainly for business (days on end every week) I think I get a birds eye view of whats hot and whats not. You get first time travelers for leisure (that have this golden picture I guess of what a hotel SHOULD be for the price) they got at bottom dollar and expect a golden castle? Hotels in any large city are not going to be the jack pot, you have hundreds of people in and out of the hotels daily.. This hotel is way under rated for some of the re-views I have read here and I am horrified to read. The hotel is great, the staff is great. It is not a rat hole. I hope and pray everytime I go to priceline I get this hotel for work or pleasure.

“Excellent location, good hotel” Nice little hotel in an excellent location in Georgetown. Nice clean room, with the added bonus of an opening window. Awful breakfast, just coffee, orange juice, sticky buns and cereals in packets, and nowhere to eat it - so you have to go back to your room, or go elsewhere and enjoy a proper breakfast. Check in is at 3pm, and don't bother arriving early; we were made to queue up at the desk like schoolchildren, whilst the lad behind the desk waited for the clock to strike 3 before he would do anything.

“Great stay except for the wi-fi” Loved the location, decor and price. The only real draw back was the wi-fi that went in and out of service. There is a wonderful work desk, good tv reception, nice toiletries, free osmosis water machine in hall, good pub on site, felt very safe/secure, in-room delivery from excellent restaurants nearby, nice staff, and incredibly great pillows! Room decor feels like Japan or a cruise line -- low ceiling, metal doors, shower only (no tub). Loved the fact that I could walk to Tadich Grill, North Beach, Chinatown and the Ferry Building Marketplace. Hotel across the street is Le Meridian and charges four times the price. Embaradero Center cinema complex is also across the street.

“Netter Geheimtipp” Das Blakley Hotel liegt nur je zwei Blocks vom Central Park und der 5th entfernt ganz in der Nähe zum MOMA, hat also die ideale Ausgangslage für Shopping-, Sightseeing und Businesstrips. Das Personal ist SEHR freundlich, die Zimmer sind groß und sauber, es ist etwas laut von der Strasse, aber das Preis-, Leistungsverhältnis ist ausgezeichnet.

“Great for leisure or business” Great place in the heart of downtown, walking distance from pier with nice rooms and bath. Good restaurant. I had a huge beautiful suite with plenty of room. Bathroom was new, rain shower, great bathtub looked in to bedroom but could be darkened. My ONLY gripe is the place can be dark. No light in closet and not a ton of natural light. Staff was very friendly and accommodating.

“Biggest room of all the w hotels i have stayed in” Very comfortable, above the usual w standard. Very large rooms. Oddly, bathroom is open to bedroom and we had to get bellman to add a curtain as we shared our room with our teenagers. great products, all the things you expect from a w

“Not What We Expected” We booked a one night stay at the New York Palace in advance of a 7 night cruise to Florida/Bahamas that was sailing out of New York. We chose the New York Palace as it was offing a "Family Values" special that offered a discounted rate for booking two rooms that touted how parents and children would enjoy the spacious accomodations. We had booked two double-double rooms to meet our family's needs. When we arrived at the hotel, the lobby was like a zoo - very loud and crowded. When we checked in we were told that the hotel had "overbooked" double-double rooms and that there was only one availbale and the other half of our party would need to stay in a King room. The young man at the checkout counter said that as a "special accomodation" they would put a rollaway bed in the King room free of charge (apparenlty there is uaually a $50 charge). When asked if our rooms were close to each other or on the same floor, he just laughed. Our rooms were more than 20 floors away from each other - not exactly lending to the enjoyment of "family values". We checked into the rooms (which were very nice) and went straight out to dinner. Retuned two hours later and found that the rollaway bed had still not been delivered - called down to have it brought up. Once we did get setttled in the rest of the experience was good - room decor is beautiful and the bathrooms luxurious. It would have been a great stay if we had just gotten what we had booked. Since we were in NYC, I couldn't help but think of Seinfeld's joke that anyone can "take" a reservation, but they also need to "hold" the reservation! PS Our rooms were on the cathedral side of the hotel and we did not have any problems with the subway construction noise.

“Stay there!” The going rate on any (reasonable) NYC hotel room is around $250. And that is what we paid for via hotels.com. After staying in the Pennsylvania and the New Yorker for the same price, this was far better! When you enter your room, you have the NYC-appartment feeling: a kitchenette (microwave, coffeemaker, fridge), a spacious living room (huge LCD!), separate bedroom (another LCD) and a bathroom (clean, good hot water). All that for $250 at such a location. As stated in other reviews, the walls could use some paint here and there (so does my appartment at home!), but it is clean. The carpet is clean and not stained, the room is fresh. We contacted the hotel via e-mail, asking for a room in the rear of the hotel. Within 48 hrs frontdesk replied, to state that they will do their best. And they delivered: room 1118 was ours, and it exceeded our expectations. Clean, spacious, comfortable. And the location (with 2 major subwaystations within one block, and Central Park right behind you) is perfect.

“Cool spot in hot desert” Lots of families enjoying the pool scene during a 110 degree summer. There are several swimming pools, which makes it nice for children of any age. I traveled with my 8 and 3 year olds, and they felt safe throughout the property. We hired a Town Car to and from the airport ($30 each way), then rented a nice Toyota for a couple of days from the on-site Beverly Hills Rental Car (competitive rates - no need to wait in line at the airport). Food prices and food were OK - one child eats free with adult entree purchase, and you can expect resort prices. There is a grocery store and pharmacy about half a mile from the resort - stock up on goods there. Free shuttle service to the other Pointe Hilton resort. That one had tremendous views of the city, but the famed Different Point of View restaurant was closed when we went. Downsides? Only a small mini-bar fridge in the room. We didn't see a concierge until the day we left. The building itself was not really all that impressive. Overall - great value.

“Great Hotel - Quiet” We arrived March 9, 2011. This is the second time we stayed at this Courtyard. We arrived early. Our room was not ready. We were offered complimentary refreshments while we waited in the lobby. After a short wait we were given an upgrade. This Courtyard has easy access to the Riverwalk. You can use the city parking for $9.00 around the corner at College & Navarro rather than pay the $25 valet fee. The staff is friendly and helpful. The Bistro is sufficient but no substitute for restaurants on the Riverwalk.

“My new favorite in Chicago” I am quite fussy, and I have only good things to say about my recent stay. The Sofitel has met its match. Clean, quiet, and tasteful. Lovely touches like slippers, robe, free wifi and orchids in the hallway. Good strong coffee in the lounge in the morning. I note that a previous reviewer complained that the decor was boring brown. Sorry that they did not notice the taupe, cream, and silver colors as well, the chocolate leather chairs, and the grey velvet easy chair - to me it was elegant and soothing. The staff was professional, friendly, and accommodating. When I did not like the room I was given on check in because it faced an alley, they changed my room right away. When something broke in my room, they offered to send the maintenance person right away. Great location in the heart of downtown, where the architecture always knocks my socks off - right above Nordstroms, where the shopping is heavenly. Had a great meal with friends at the outdoor restaurant -so nice to be outside but away from traffic on the 5th floor. I was traveling alone to attend a conference over at the Sheraton and I felt very safe. I absolutely recommend this hotel - to me, it was worth every penny.

“muy bueno para familias” Es un muy buen lugar para alojarse en familia, la ubicación es excelente, dormitorios amplios y con buen nivel de limpieza, el personal es amable y servicial. No es un hotel de lujo pero cumple con todos los servicios ofrecidos, el precio es un poco elevado pero en NY todos los alojamientos son caros, especialmente si tiene buena ubicación. Llenó mis expectativas.

“Tired and Worn - just at a super deal or if you must” Hyatt aka bland generic but clean ; typical american congress hotel very worn from lobby that looks like a 80 s mall in some South African Suburb to smelly worn rooms with awful 90s furniture. I had to endure 4 nights before moving to another Chicago Hotel, intially the admittedly fast and courteous staff moved me next to the elevator - I requested a quiet room and got a perfect end of the floor super quiet . thumps up for that !! Rest forget about it the " Stetson " Steakhouse is at best average - Breakfast Buffet a joke and the BIG Bar part of the 80s Lobby - atmosphere like a airport terminal . If you get a deal go for it - if you attend a confertence do yourself a treat move into one of the many many choices with a 1 mile radius . Same price but indefinetely better

“Fun and Interesting” This is a small boutique hotel that has odd attractions such as a recording studio. I like odd. I like the antique feel to the hotel. The hotel is right in the heart of Union Square area and a lot of street noise gets in if you have a room on the street. We overlooked the ACE Hardware store and really, although the room is small, and simple, it is so inexpensive and the quality of stay is good. I recommend staying here. If you are super sensitive to noise probably not the best stay but try a room in back, maybe that is better. They also have shared bathroom rooms that I believe offer a lesser cost to each night's stay.

“Close to the action; exterior rooms nicest” We just got back from SXSW 2009 in Austin. Our original plan was to share a room at the Intercontinental with a friend who was going for work and had a room through the Housing Desk for SXSW. When those accommodations fell through in early January, I suddenly needed to find a room close to the action that wouldn't break our bank. With the AAA discount, we were able to get a King room for $157.50/nt (before taxes & fees). Another person in our group also booked a double room here without the discount for around $170. Though we had hoped for an early check-in, nothing was actually available until the 1p check-in time -- a little rough since we had taken the red-eye and were left wandering around downtown for about 5 hours. The hotel did keep our luggage behind the desk for us, however, which was great. The hotel is in a sort of "L" shape with one outdoor wing facing 11th Street. The other rooms are in a horseshoe around the parking lot and the entrances are off an interior hallway. Our room was in the outdoor part and was MUCH quieter and nicer than our friend's Double on the interior. Someone mentioned hearing rolling suitcases down the cement walks, but I only heard this once the whole time we were there. The room was very clean and the furnishings and linens in very good condition. The bed was also comfortable and the A/C worked perfectly (and helped blocked out any noise from the street). Our friend told us that being on the interior, the hallway echoed voices and all you could hear were slamming doors all night and morning. While the housekeeping staff did an adequate job, it was a bit erratic. One day, our soap was taken from the sink and not replaced. Luckily, I had a bar in my bag from a different trip's lodging. Another day, our coffee condiments were not replaced and I had to use Sweet & Low instead of sugar (yuck!). Our friend's room was not cleaned for 3 days because she had "slept through" the maid service. We also had our DND sign out, not leaving the room until noon, usually, but always had a lovely clean room upon our return. I agree that, especially during a music festival, the breakfast should be served much later than 10 (and 9 on weekdays!). Nearly everyone in the hotel has been out until 2ish the night before and I imagine most of that food just goes to waste. At least leave the coffee out! I also think that the $12.99/day valet fee is a bit steep. And, while not the hotel's fault, the add'l state and local taxes added $25/day to our rate! It would be nice to include these in the total when you book. I would definitely stay here again, but only if I could be guaranteed a room in the "Exterior" wing.

“Big rooms in a good location, great deal via Priceline” Booked this via priceline (downtown, 3 1/2 *, $55) for a recent weekend wedding trip. At $55 this hotel is a screaming deal. It is a great location, 1 1/2 blocks from the 16th St Mall and 1 block from the light rail, very central to downtown. The rooms, like all Residence Inn hotels, were very large (ours was a 1-BR suite, I've had smaller apts). The furnishings were a little tired, but good overall. Like all Residence Inns, decent breakfast and sometimes weeknight dinners, though we didn't partake of either. My only knock is the very expensive parking at $20+ / night. I'm told there are good cheaper options in the area, but we didn't have time to go searching for them. If you can possibly skip the car, this is a good option, since there are great transit connections nearby, including the express bus to the airport.

“fabulous for us (minus sleep, loud conv at 2 am below room).” usually fantastic. we take our two kids and get them own room. one is 18 so they go to movie on sunday evening by pool. did not enjoy their time, other guests were loud and rude. but we did. teenagers!!!!

“Very,Very Good” I was visiting Houston for the first time andf got a great deal on priceline.com for the Westin Galleria for four nights. I hired a car at Hobby airport and drove the 20 or so minutes to the hotel. Complimentary parking is available in the car park adjoining the hotel. A 1 minute walk from the side exit door of the lobby. Check-in was excellent and pleasant. I went straight to my room which was very big, airy and comfortable. If all Westin rooms are like this I will use them again. Wi-fi was about $12.95 a day in-room or complimentary in the lobby. A $5 voucher towards any outlet in the hotel can be earned by not getting your room serviced. This I availed of and used by vouchers towards a meal in hotel's the Grill and Bar restaurant that is situated in the Galleria mall. Shirley at the concierge desk was superb and a great ambassador for the Westin brand. She helped me with any minor query and was extremely professional and patient. As a location the Westin suited my stay perfectly. I could shop, meet friends, free park and had access to loads of restaurants etc. A very, very good experience for the price I paid.

“Not even close to 4 Star” I often joke with friends about people who complain about hotels on Tripadvisor...but now I know how the cranky travelors feel. We booked the Whitehall hotel through Hotwire for Labor Day weekend. It was supposed to be 4 star, and I've never been as disappointed in a hotel. This place is a dump. It's under construction and the staff is rude. (We had to wake up the front desk person to check us in at midnight last night.) We routinely work from hotels. I knew that this hotel charges for internet, but they charge $10 for every laptop you want to use...so we are paying $30 a day for internet access in this hotel which is outrageous. The room isn't even worth $30. From a typically easy going travelor, take my advice and avoid the Whitehall Hotel. It's a dump.

“Finishings starting to wear...housekeeping?” I stay at this hotel every few months. I have noticed that the furniture is in need of some cleaning in some of the rooms. The carpets are getting pretty bad also. When I checked in this time it was obvious that the room had not been vacuumed. This caused me to look around and I noticed how dirty the wallpaper was, could use some basic housekeeping services. I checked in after 5 and there were still dirty glasses sitting in the hallway outside my door from the previous guest. For the rates hotels charge in DC you would think they could do some upkeep and cleaning.

“Off the beaten path from PHX” I stayed here for a horrible trip: going to see a client and get my a** kicked. So my mood was already glum. I arrived with two colleagues from FL at 9:06 am on a weekday. I'd called ahead and was told we'd probably be able to get rooms around 10am even though check-in is usually in the afternoon. My directions from the car rental center were wrong, so I went out of the way. But even without that snafu, this hotel seems a little far from the airport--well, specifically, from the rental car center. It doesn't feel like an airport hotel, as it's situated in a little office park and you drive by some really grim areas filled with stripper shacks to get there. So location merits a D. That said, the front desk clerk very helpfully got us three rooms even though it was only about 10am. (Note the huge, electric blue asparagus stalks in the lobby--weird.) My room was a good five-minute walk from the elevator, which is ridiculously far, so be careful when reserving. The room itself was generic Hilton, albeit with a southwestern flair. I was pleased that the a/c blew very cold, and surprised to find a little balcony off the room that overlooked the pool. I was gone all afternoon and had a 7am flight out the next day, so I didn't check out the gym or the pool or any other amenities. We did have dinner in the hotel restaurant and it was surprisingly good and, as I recall, not overly expensive. Parking, as you'd expect, is free. Another colleague joined us and took the free shuttle, which he said was fine and timely. All in all, it's a perfectly acceptable property, but it doesn't feel all that close to the airport, and I can't imagine why anyone would stay in this part of Phoenix unless s/he had an early morning flight.

“Super Convienent” I was on a business trip to Los Angeles recently and after the conference ended I moved to this hotel to be near the airport for my flight out the next day. It was very convienent when traveling to from LAX. They have a shuttle to the airport that runs all the time. There is a starbucks in the hotel that is great! The rooms were clean and comfortable. There was a nice balcony in my room with a view of a very pretty tropical pool. I did not use the pool on my stay but it looked nice.

“Great location, staff and value” The staff was superb..from the front desk to the valets.. Location was great, walking distance to subway, TD garden, gardens and commons. I was there to do some photography of the city and the location allowed me to do that easily. Parking is expensive, but it normally is anywhere in any bigger city

“Good Value & Location” Hotel grounds and rooms are typical HIE, clean and comfortable. The staff was very friendly. The hotel is within walking distance of downtown atteactions, however, if you return to the hotel late at night, be sure you know exactly how walk back to the hotel (or get a pedicab) as the neighborhood can be a bit "sketchy' at night with lots of lonely, off the beated track stretches that may make one concerned for their safety.

“NYC trip with teenagers” My husband & I brought 7 teenagers, age 13 - 16, to NYC for 2 days. For some it was their first time in the city. We booked the Marriott Marquis because it was in the heart of Times Square. The kids loved it. Huge lobby with glass tube elavators and surprisingly good size rooms. Rooms were very clean and comfortable. They loved sitting in the lounge area that overlooked Times Square. Easy to walk out the door and be in the middle of the action and few steps to subway.

“Not the Greatest Customer Service” When I entered the lobby I thought I was in for a great experience. Not so. The clerk at the front desk rushed me through my check in - when I went back later to ask some questions I was again rushed. My package included breakfast for two - I asked the clerk if since I was just one person could I have room service breakfast instead - she said no and suggested I bring a friend (I'm on vacation in a City where I don't know anyone, but I guess I could have grabbed someone off the street!) I also didn't have a robe in my room - the clerk said not every room has robes, although the hotel's web site doesn't indicate that. They did finally send me a robe but they seemed bothered by my request. One of the shower heads did not work at first - they did finally fix it. The food for the breakfast buffet was boring. The one plus for me was the martinis in the hotel bar - try the cucumber one! Not a 4-star experience for me and I would not likely stay there again unless I got an exceptional deal.

“Tiny bed” We did get a good rate on Hotwire for this hotel, but the bed was TOO small! We had the option to pay 50 dollars more for a queen. We thought this was too much to pay for that size bed. We were disappointed that others here who posted here got free upgrades but we did not. It would seem to make good business sense to allow upgrades for empty rooms. We did think that location was great and the shower was awesome. The front desk was fine although we did get some incorrect information about the TKTS booth. Be sure and confirm all info online if that is possible.

“Great Value For Airport Layover” Great value at this hotel. We stayed on a layover to Hawaii. The shuttle was quick, check in was a breeze. The Hotel is in great shape - clean, comfortable beds, etc. We were surprised at how nice the hotel was for being an "airport" hotel. We will use this hotel again if we have the need to. It was also a great value.

“Intercontinental Very nice” The Intercontinental was very nice for our stay this week. We did get the room off of Priceline for a very good price, but the room was lovely. The bathroom was fairly large as well. Friendly staff. And the old Medinah Athletic Club part of the hotel is absolutely stunning. The renovation was wonderful. We stayed in the newer section. The location is fantastic.

“Newly refurbished: Clean & Comfy” We missed the side road the first time. Pay attention once your are on Santa Monica Blvd going west and crossed Westwood, stay far right and turn immediately into a side road. A few free parking spots in the front but plenty more in the back of the Inn. This is an excellent more economical place to stay if you are visiting UCLA and all the hotels in Westwood are fulled. The reception was friendly, the rooms were newly refurbished, clean and comfy. Complimentary breakfast was good fresh standard fare. We stayed Saturday night, the place was quiet and restful. Good alternative for us when we visit UCLA.

“Nice place to lay your head!” We stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel for two nights this past week. It has a great location. Close to Times Square,Grand Central,lots of shopping etc...The lobby is marble and dark wood and has a nice feel. We had drinks and appetizers at the bar the first night. Big martinis,good food,friendly bartenders! So far so good! Up the elevator,which was quick, to the 12th floor. The hallway seemed dark and dated. The door to our room was a little worn. Once inside,it became clear that we got exactly what we paid for! After all we had chosen the lowest priced room at $245 per night before taxes or parking. The bathroom was miniscule,but clean. The room could barely hold the king (queen?)bed,one end table,desk,and bureau with flatscreen atop!! It was a stretch for two adults to get ready to go out in that bathroom and room! In the morning,while my fiance was getting ready for any appointment,I just stayed in the bed,to stay out his way!!! Almost everywhere I looked,paint was chipped,and things were just worn,in general. The first night,the traffic noise was horrible. The second night I barely noticed,but I would ask for a higher floor next time. Having said that,the bed was very comfortable. Big,nice mattress,pillows and linens. I called housekeeping once for extra towels and the service was fast with a smile. We usually stay at Marriotts and I love them. Safe,reliable and you always know exactly what your getting. But we were intown for a quick getaway and to see a show midweek and the huge price tag at my favorite place was just striking a nerve this time!! After all,what we needed was a place to lay our heads and shower!!! So we went outside of the box for half the price and I would do it again in a second!! It was a very nice stay for the price!!

“Fine if you can get a good rate” The rooms here were very comfortable, quiet and well-appointed (including irons). Bathroom very good too, and very clean. A good view from a high-rise window was pleasant too. In the nearby area there are plenty of interesting restaurants and bars. The big down-side to this hotel is it is a moderate distance (up a hill) to the nearest Subway station, on 3rd Avenue. Some attractions are within walking distance, such as the art museums around Central Park, but there aren't many other things so you'll really need to use the Subway. Unless, of course, you need to be in the Upper East Side, in which case this location is great. You don't really need all the features of this hotel given you're in NYC, so whilst it is comfortable and generally fine, you really need to find a good rate to justify staying at this hotel.

“Family Trip to Chicago for Thanksgiving” We stayed at this hotel from 21-25 November with our children, ages 4 & 6. Since many of the reviews touch on the beauty of the hotel which is as beautiful as everyone says, I'll gear my review towards those traveling with small children and trying to decide if this hotel is a good fit. 1. Location. The Peninsula was perfectly situated for all our excursions to the various museums around town since it's a block from Watertower, the Disney store on Michigan, a couple blocks from Lake Shore Drive and about 2 blocks from the "El" elevated trains/subway. The American Girl store is on the same block around the corner and the Hershey Store and Girardelli were just a few steps more. Plenty of shopping for everyone on Michigan Ave. 2. Staff. Everyone was friendly to us and our children. The staff of Avenues was fantastic. Those on the Lobby Restaurant were hit or miss. 3. Restaurants/Food. The Children's Afternoon Tea in the Lobby was yummy with mini hamburgers, PB & J, & ham and cheese in addition to the sweets and a pot of hot chocolate. Pierre Gourmet, the French Cafe just outside the main entrance, was perfect for breakfast (and probably for lunch). The staff and friendly and attentive to us and our children. Room service did well by us when we ordered dessert for the family one evening. Everything arrived on time and was as ordered. The hotel does have a children's menu at the Lobby and Avenues but the selection is somewhat limited. 4. Pool. There are three swimming lanes and a hot tub on the 19th floor. There were a few swimmers swimming laps while we were there who were politely tolerant of the 10+ children in the area. While not ideal for children or those who are swimming laps for that matter, it might make a good 30 minute diversion. 5. Pen Kids Package. We researched the various packages at the Four Seasons and Ritz Carlton before picking the Peninsula. The most kid friendly package was at the Ritz Carlton and it provided the most value for the $. If you choose the Peninsula, I would go with the standard room rate or the American Girl package and spend the additional $60+/per night from the Pen Kids Package elsewhere. With the package, the kids got a nice welcome snack, Pen Kids multi-color backpacks, a signature bear (who can't keep it's pants on), crayons and some coloring paper. We also received two coupons (one for ice cream at Bloomingdale's and children's admission to the Children's Museum at Navy Pier). A better investment is to buy a family membership at your local ASTC museum which had reciprocity at a number of museums in Chicago (Museum of Science & Industry, Children's Museum and Field Museum, to name only a few). 6. Room. Our bathroom was a nice extension of the main room. Whenever we were there, the kids wanted to take a bath and watch cartoons. This came in handy if one of the kids wanted to nap or as a diversion if one woke up before the other in the morning. 7. We also took advantage of the Thanksgiving buffet offered by the hotel. The food came from all three restaurants and exceeded our expectations. The hotel had also created a separate kids area with movies, playstation, and crafts that our kids enjoyed. The only negative were the $18 mimosas we ordered with the meal but thought were included with the buffet. All in all the Peninsula is a wonderful hotel, in a great location. It is clear that the chain is trying to cater to families - the kids room during the buffet was a good example of this.

“Incredible Staff & Wonderful Boutique Hotel” While I was concerned after reading several reviews, I must admit, the hotel is quite wonderful. Granted, per American standards, the rooms are small. However, the hotel more than makes up for that in other ways. My room was very clean and the housekeeping staff sincerely take pride in their work and ensuring that you have a well kept room. The bed was very comfy. The hotel staff is truly the foundation of Hotel Felix. Every person I encountered was kind, respectful, courteous, helpful, and very personable in the way they deal with guests. They greet you upon entry every time. The bell and valet staff are equally as delightful to deal with. The only exception would be the gentleman who works the Midnight shift. He is curt, somewhat rude, and too busy playing with his cell phone to really be helpful. The hotel offers a nice lobby bar as well. The LM Bistro in the lobby offers wonderful food and the butter lettuce salad is awesome. The staff there is also very accomodating and courteous. Quite frankly, you will sacrifice the size of a typical American hotel room, but the quality of service you receive tips the scale by far. I am in hotels 15-25 nights per month on business and have stayed at more elaborate and pricier hotels in Chicago but did not receive the level of guest service I did at Hotel Felix. I will choose it again when in Chicago. Great service trumps the size of the room for me.

“top notch service, gorgeous property” We stayed in a montevista suite for four nights and got the sunday night complimentary.(439) The room had a queen sofa sleeper and spacious bathroom and king size bed. Pocket doors in the bathroom separated the bedroom and living room. Plasma tv in the living area and large tv in an armoire in the king room. We were treated like royalty. From the moment you walk in you know this is not your average hotel. You feel like you are in your own spanish villa and everyone is happy to take care of all your needs with a smile. My kids loved the pool. The pool guys who I unfortunately cannot remember their names were so very kind and hardworking. I have never seen two people more eager to please their guests. The food at the pool is phenomenal and so were the drinks. We were lucky enough to celebrate an early anniversary at D COOKS and had a lovely meal in a beautiful room with great service. I cannot praise this hotel enough. My only wish is that they would have had a kids pool. If you want romance and service, gorgeous scenery and R and R. GO TO THE ROYAL PALMS...

“Great property! Great location and wonderful experience.” Seamless experience. Staff has done a great job. (Josh at the front desk was very, very helpful.) Perfect location...close to great breakfast spots and a block from the metro. Would stay here again for sure!

“Gute Erfahrung” Hotel liegt 2 Blöcke entfernt von der Metro-Station der Blue Line, die direkt zum Flughafen führt. Die Zimmer mit Standard-Austattung der CQ-Hotelkette, d.h. LCD-TV , kostenloses WLAN, grosses Bett. Zimmer und Bad waren immer sauber. Mitarbeiter sind freundlich, im Untergeschoss gibt es ein Business-Center. Empfehlenswert vor allem wegen der Lage.

“An excellent airport gym” The Hilton O'Hare is very convenient for Terminals 1,2,3 -- it is only a short walk above ground or underground. And as an airport hotel it is relatively standard - the rooms are not remarkable and the restaurant is only ok. After midnight the hotel does not have much -- for example, room service is on pager. Where the hotel really shines though is in its gym -- which many flight crew use between flights as annual membership is very reasonable. The cardio equipment and weights are all good - the machines are more focused on weights though. There is a small pool and a good jacuzzi. The locker rooms are clean and the hours are good too (5 am - 10 pm)

“Noise With View or Quiet Without” This property is in a very convenient location near the airport and the shopping areas along I-10. It is exactly what you would expect from a Residence Inn, but nothing special. The breakfast was up to par, the indoor pool was predictable and the decor was well done. All in all, it is a great place to relax, or stop over in El Paso. Norma, the desk attendant was very helpful when we needed to change rooms. I observed her with other customers and saw that she is very courteous, confident, and knowlegable.

“New and clean” Rooms here are well appointed: good work space, coffee maker, large tv and couch. Not very much sets it apart from other well kept mid-price hotels in the area. It is close to DIA and shuttle service is frequent. I didn't eat here so can't comment on the food/pricing. I did notice restaurants walking distance from the hotel though.

“If you can live with 1 Queen then Fantastic place to Stay” Just in the southern mix of Times Square, you are home. Great Service, Rates and Nice rooms but no space for extra bed, Only 1 Queen bed. We loved the friendly atmosphere with home like amenities. Thank you for a great stay.
“Good Times” A good value for NYC. Nice rooms. We got offered an upgrade. Would stay here again.

“Nice hotel, better staff” This hotel is about 4 miles from SEA and they do have shuttle service every half hour to the hotel. The shuttle leaves a bit to be desired as I was shuttled back and forth on a normal passenger van opposed to a mini-bus, which created issues with the amount of people it carried. Any way, upon arrival to the hotel it appears to not be a newer hotel and when you're inside it is confirmed by the somewhat dreary, or darker appearance. Upon check-in the front desk staff was excellent and the process was speedy. In fact, while my room was not ready upon my arrival, they sought me out in the restaurant personally to hand me my key when the room was ready to be occupied. The room itself was a corner suite and I found it to be acceptable but nothing extraordinary and certainly very dark. The TVs were newer flat screens but they did not offer HD service and the cable options were limited. The room service I ordered was good food, they just didn't get the order right as I received incorrect beverage and condiments. However, in the restaurant itself, all went well and the food was actually surprisingly good. The staff in the restaurant and bar area, specifically Erika and Susan were excellent. Very friendly, well attentive to the needs of the patrons and were extremely courteous. It actually was refreshing to see them interact with the guests and even laugh with them. Greg was an excellent bellman who assisted upon arrival and the waiter Gabriel was also superb, relative to his friendliness and overall service. The stay was ok, but it was made better by the staff. The hotel just seems older and outdated to me but I believe it to be one of the better options if you need to stay near Sea-Tac. My rate was $170 per night and both nights I was there, they were full. Again, this hotel is made by its staff.

“Could use an update” The staff here was great, yet that can't change the fact that this is one of the poorest InterContinentals I have stayed at. Location is great, but the rooms are very small and feeling pretty old, the pool was closed (use the Marriott if you like --- who wants to walk across the street to swim??), shower water pressure weak and the room service food was poor. The intercontinental by the airport is a ton better, san francisco is awesome, toronto and NYC great, but Chicago is hurting.

“Perfect location and no bedbugs!” This month I've visited New York City for the first time. Always wanted to visit this city, but the high prices (compared to holidays in Florida) and scary stories about bedbugs kept me from visiting NYC. After I found cheap flighttickets, it was time to find a nice hotel. On Expedia I found The Edison Hotel for about 105 euro's (136-140 dollars) a night. Good enough for me. I read about it on TripAdvisor first, and I expected an old hotelroom, but I probably got a renovated room on the 11th floor at the end of the hallway with a window also on the side of the building, facing the Hudson river. I wrote down some stuff on my iPod Touch, so I wouldn't forget about it after the trip. Here's what I wrote down; - Clean room, not too big, not too small either. Two nice queensized beds, pillows are a bit too high if you sleep on your stomach. I decided to sleep without a pillow. There is some noise from outside (hey, it's NYC!) so if you are a light sleeper, take some earplugs with you and you will sleep like a baby. Outdated rooms? Not this one. Even the beds looked new. - No bedbugs! I was really scared of this and I check each hotelbed I sleep in, thoroughly, to make sure it's really free from these bugs. I'm not afraid to get bitten, I'm afraid to take them home with me. New York City seems infested with these creatures if you search for it online. I think each hotel might have them, travelers take them with them etc. but if only 1% of the rooms might have them in The Edison, that's only 9 rooms. Sounds much as a number, not as a percentage. Anyway, I didn't find them on my search. - Small bathroom, new sink, bathtub and probably toilet. Because of bad ventilation, there are some moldspots on the ceiling, also between the tiles on some places. Showercurtain is mold-free. It's hard to keep the mold away without proper ventilation, and not that strange for an older building. Yet it's healthier to fix this, but it's a big job. No mold in the room itself, just the bathroom. The showerhead wasn't that nice to me. It had like fast strong short bursts of water, I'd like to see that changed for a more pleasant experience in the shower. - Nice 32 inch flatscreen in the room with adjustable swingarm. Didn't watch much TV, but I always like to watch the local news to know what's going on in the place where I'm staying. - Next to the smoke detector there's also a carbonmonoxide detector in the room. I like that! - Six fast elevators (at least, compared to the ones I'm used to in Holland), security in the lobby which doesn't let you through if you don't show your roomkey(card). Also camera's in the elevators and on all floors. No need to wait long for an elevator is on your floor. - Staff is friendly and always willing to help you. Needed to find a restaurant, but didn't remember the address, no problem in looking that up for me on the net. They even didn't know at that point that I was a guest or not. Got a late checkout free of charge. - ATM in the hotel, but it didn't work with my debit and creditcard for some reason. The ATM in Duane Reade's did (it's almost right outside the hotel on 47th street and 8th ave). This one is even cheaper (additional costs of $ 1,99 instead of $ 3,25 in the hotel). - The hotel is close to a lot of things, probably 50 meters away from Times Square, and on walking distances of a lot of things; Central Park, 5th ave, St. Patricks cathedral, Rockefeller Plaza, USS Intrepid and if you like walking, also the Empire State Building. If you don't like walking, there are some subwaylines near the hotel to take you anywhere you like in the Big Apple. - The Edison Cafe has a lot to offer for breakfast and lunch. Good food and not expensive. Will I be back? Sure, if the price is right. The prices change each month at most hotels I guess, right now it had a perfect price for a perfect location. I had a great time in NYC!

“Not deserving of its #2 spot” My husband and I stayed here with our 9 month old son for one night to meet up with friends in the city. I decided to stay here as it had mostly excellent reviews and the price tag was incredibly reasonable for NYC. Our room was ready when we arrived roughly at 3pm and I had requested an upgrade online for the discounted price and it was honored. The gentleman who checked us in was a perfect blend of professionalism and charm. Was really digging it so far. We opened the door to our suite and I was astonished by its size-sitting area with a couch and two chairs, two flat screen TVs, separate toilet and shower/soaking tub, King bed, CO Bigelow toiletries, and cool control panel allowing you to adjust lights and shades. The pack n play was set up and looked brand new, and I appreciated how snacks and non-alc bevs were included. So far, so good. As an aside, the location sucks if you plan on going further uptown than Chinatown so if you plan on visiting all over I'd say a good base would be closer to midtown. The complimentary wine tasting was surprising in the quality of what was offered, I quite enjoyed my sauvignon blanc. I didn't go to the gym but my husband said it was nice. We ate dinner around the corner at a Japanese restaurant that I wouldn't recommend to fellow TAs. When we got back, I noticed that the hotel was quite noisy not just in the lobby but in the elevators and hallways as well. Glad that I was staying at the end of the corridor with only one room next door. Well, unfortunately that room next door had about six people in it who were super loud and annoying and the wall was not thick enough to filter it. It was only 9:30pm so I wasn't that upset...yet. I ordered dessert from room service and it took 50 minutes for them to deliver it. When it arrived, the ice cream for a dessert was missing. The gentleman who delivered promised to come back with it as soon as possible and let the evening host know about my request for earplugs. 10 minutes later he returns with an itty bitty baby scoop of half melted sorbet and no earplugs. He says that someone else will bring them up shortly. The people next door are still shouting and laughing and making all kinds of noise. It is now 11pm and the baby is sleeping and I'm about ready to sleep myself. I call the host and he says "We don't have any. You can go across the street and get them yourself." Okay, I get it, you don't have any for guests, but did you really have to be so rude about it? Even if I wanted them that badly, I wasn't going to leave my baby alone to get it! My husband returns from drinks with his friends and said the bar downstairs has the worst servers with bad attitudes. So in a nutshell, with cons outweighing the pros: -reasonable rates, complimentary "goodies", pleasant day staff, awesome blackout shades -rude and incompetent evening staff, poor room service (food and execution), thin walls, bad location for tourists, weak internet or even no internet, plenty of wear and tear for a newer hotel that shows in the room furnishings This hotel is a Monet, good from far but far from good...up close. If it weren't for the good customer service I experienced upon check in, I would have given this Andaz property 1 star. I do like Hyatts as they tend to be reliable, but the Andaz Wall Street was a letdown because the customer service we experienced in the couple of situations was deplorable and inexcusable. Will not consider another Andaz in the future for sure. Tip: Brunch is phenomenal, and fortunately you do not need to be a guest to dine there.

“Great Location and Value!” Stayed here for a wedding in Washington over Cherry Blossom weekend. The hotel was very busy but the staff handled it all with ease. The hotel's lobby was great and much nice than the Marriott around the block. The room was small, but well furnished. I loved the walk in shower. I always appreciate it when you can actually get HD content on the HDTV they have in the room (you'd be amazing how little this is the case). Location was great. Close to Foggy Bottom & Dupont Metro stations. The neighborhood is one of the best in DC.

“Great deals in offseason, but quality of room can vary” I've stayed at the Marriott downtown on three occasions. Twice in off season and the prices (for New York) were a great bargain. The hotel is conveniently located in downtown and very close to numerous subways. I didn't hear any noise from the construction going on at Ground Zero, whereas at other hotels in the area it's a constant background noise. Only downside was that for the three times I stayed there I got three very different quality rooms although I paid the same rate each time. Twice I got very spacious rooms, while the last time I stayed there the room was cramped and felt very small. Otherwise, a great stay, clean rooms and friendly staff.

“good hotel good room and good staff” what can i say about this hotel pros: the room, the staff, the pool, the bed, and the overall feel cons: the train noise at night, the eggs on breakfast, the door connecting to the restroom needs to be fixed and the smell of the room was murkey

“The Barclay is a home run Hotel” My wife and I had to attend a conference in New York City in late January 2008. When we started checking out hotel prices we found that there were very few deals unless you lower your standards to a tourist type hotel. In previous trips to New York we stayed in some very nice Hotels, the Waldorf, The Mandarin Oriental, Essex House but never the Barclay InterContinental. A friend recommended it to me so we made a reservation. Wow, what a diamond in the ruff. This property is beautiful. From the moment you enter the lobby you are greeted with pleasant good afternoon and welcome to the Barclay. My wife could not believe the size and beauty of the flower arrangement in the Lobby. Our check in was very swift but our room was not ready which was understandable since the hotel was fully booked. The front desk agent was very informative about the time the room should be ready and even offered to make some dinner reservations for us at a local Italian Restaurant. We went of to our meeting and returned around 6:00PM. We quickly received our key and said our luggage would be sent right up. We had a very nice large room with a sitting area that was very clean, bright and allowed us to spread out. Our luggage arrived with in a few minutes with a very nice and informative bellman who hung up our hang up bag got us some Ice and answered a few questions. The other thing that was a real treat was how comfortable the bed and pillows were. What a great nights rest. The next day our departure was very smooth with a, "Thanks for staying with us" from the Bellman Front Desk Agent and the Doorman. Everyone we came in contact with was nicer than the last person we spoke to who had a Barclay name tag on. The Barclay has hit a home run with us. They have figured out what Hospitality is all about. I give them six stars on a scale of one to five.

“Great place to stay in NYC!” We have just spent Christmas in NYC and stayed at the Courtyard Times Square South. This hotel will not disappoint! The rooms are very clean and very comfortable. The front desk and concierge staff are extremely friendly and very accommodating. The location can't be beat - - - just steps away from the 42nd Street subway to the west and the Bryant Park subway to the east. Breakfast available in the hotel, although we didn't partake given the high prices. Walked everywhere - and this is possible because of the central location. We will DEFINITELY stay here once again - great value, great staff, great price, great hotel!

“A true classic hotel” I stayed here many years ago on my first trip to New York in 2004 and was suitably impressed with the hotel back then. I returned there last year in March and I am delighted to say that the hotel is still as impressive as it seemed to me on my first trip. The room we had, by New York standards, can only be described as huge. No exaggeration. The sleep quality is also second to none in this hotel. The room was clean and tidy and well appointed. The only issue that we had throughout the trip was with the in-room WiFi but as a result of the problem we were not charged upon checkout without any question from staff. Yes the hotel in some ways looks a little dated but this only adds to the charm of it. I would certainly return for a 3rd stay without hesitation. Its also in a fantastic location and within walking distance of most of the main attractions and shops.

“Overpriced, even by Washington standards” This is a very mediocre hotel at full price. The room was small, the amenities few, the view was terrible and there is nothing, absolutely nothing, to do in the area. Seriously, this hotel is blocks from a metro station, blocks from the convention center, and far away from the Mall and areas with classy restaurants. It's not that it's bad, it's just not good, but you pay the same rate as if it had a view of the White House. Oh, and you will eventually get use to the weird smell, but not the strange accents of the staff.

“Very good except for dirty toilet seat” Everything a you'd want in a NYC hotel: good sized and clean room, excellent location, no bedbugs, quiet floor, free Sunday brunch, fast check-in and check-out. But the dirty toilet seat was unacceptable, not to mention a health hazard.

“Welcoming boutique hotel” Upon arrival and departure, the front door was opened for us. At check in we were offered a glass of champagne or water in a wine glass. Very nice. The lobby is refreshing and there is plenty of comfortable seating. Our room was spacious for a boutique hotel and the bathroom was plenty large enough. The bedroom had a desk/counter, bench seating and another comfortable chair. The air-conditioner was functioning well. There is a separate room in the lobby area where you can help yourself to coffee, espresso or teas. A very nice touch. Truly...if you spend too much time in your room in NYC, you are not enjoying the city life. The price was right (approx. $154/night) and it is centrally located to many sights in the city and only a few blocks from Central Park. I would return to The Shoreham and highly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to NYC. My only complaint would be that the elevator button wasn't working well and would often pass our floor.

“Disappointing” We arrived at noon on Saturday the 14th. We didn't expect our room to be ready because we were quite early. Hotel stored our bags and told us to check back at 4pm. Came back at 5pm and our 2 bedroom suite still wasn't available. They gave us another room to stay in until our suite was ready. Went to dinner and came back at 9:30pm. Bellman was just moving our bags into our suite. Yes the suite was awesome. 2 1/2 baths, beautiful view of Central Park on one side and Columbus Circle from the front. All the amenities including a plasma screen tv, robes and slippers in each room. Was a bit noisy as we were only on the 5th floor. We had ordered a cake to be waiting in our suite as it was our daughter's 17th birthday. Had to call about the cake and it finally arrived at 10:15pm. However it was the most awful cake. Couldn't eat it. Told the front desk and they told us to order whatever we wanted from the dessert menu and have it sent to our suite. They also agreed that we should be able to order anything for breakfast and have it sent to our room since our suite was so delayed in being available. Fortunately the weather in NYC was beautiful on Saturday and we were able to spend the entire day enjoying the sights and shopping. However at over $1200 a night there should have been NO PROBLEMS! Would we go back? Hmmm, not so sure. This trip was a very special occassion for our daughter and that it is why we decided to really splurge. We have stayed in many other beautiful hotels in NYC and not had such a delay. I will say that the staff was very friendly and did try to accomodate us as best as possible. But they need to come up with a better plan for getting guests into the type of accomodation they reserved.

“A place to stay at” Stayed overnight for the state fair. Dallas is small so eveyrthing is near hiways and not to far at all. 10-15 min . Front desk had maps and directions they could print out for you if needed. They are prepared to help out visitors. Parking was ample, and noticed a security truck that does rounds in parking lot etc. Overall clean and average hotel. Beds was very nice and soft. Stayed in the normal executive suite i believe. Ample space if needed. TVs are nice with good selection of channels. Bathrooms and bar area was clean and in good condition. Staff very friendly and helpful.

“It's fine if you're not fussy” Went down for an overnight shopping trip. Pro's: 1) Very professional and friendly check in employees 2) Decent hot/cold breakfast as expected. 3) You get a guest pass to 24Hour Fitness located across the street. Nice bonus if you are a work out freak. I unfortunately didn't bring my Nikes :( Con's: 1) Really soft bed that squeeked...barely slept. 2) The carpet felt dingy. Highly recommended that you wear your shoes while in suite. 3) Bathroom faucet and bar faucet have incredibly low water pressure. 4) Sketchy area. We were lucky to find street parking across the street in front of 24Hour Fitness. Felt better that the gym is open 24hours. I would have paid for valet parking otherwise = $28. 5) Beware that this is not a quiet hotel. It's on a major street leading up to I-5. Lots of traffice in front of the hotel. 6) Crappy TV signal. The Residence Inn Lake Union offered HD channels (for comparison). 7) The bath curtain was cut short, I assume because the bottom was moldy and unsightly. It was so short that water from the shower created a mini-lake around the toilet. Not nice....

“Perfectly Fine with a few Gripes” We checked in for one night. Our main beef was with the air conditioning. In our room, it was a wall unit placed behind the beds against the outside wall. We had two queen beds in the bedroom and a pull out sofa in the living room. I haven't seen one of these since I last stayed in a motel like LaQuinta. It definitely did not cool the room with the pull out bed where our grandson was sleeping. We did LOVE the large 42" plasma HDTV in the room. Best picture clarity of a hotel TV I've ever seen! Absolutely loved it. It swiveled around so that the living room and the bedroom could both see the picture. There was a very small bathroom, but we made do. The continental breakfast was very crowded, but we got our breakfast and were able to find a place to sit, and were on our way. Not the best, but not the worst either. I would stay here again.

“Second time staying at the awesome boutique hotel” Staying here for the second time in the past few months. This boutique hotel is awesome. If you're looking for a full-service hotel, with bellman, restaurant, pool, sauna, etc. look elsewhere. This is a boutique (limited-service) hotel in NYC which have become quite standard. Compare the rates with the full-service hotels in the area, and you'll understand why the MAve is priced significantly less. Now stating that, this is not a bad thing. You pay a great price for a great room. They offer a few sizes of rooms, and the square footage is listed on their website, so I'm not sure why other people are complaining that their rooms were "too small". You got exactly what you booked. For a few dollars more, I always book a KING room, which has plenty of space. Also, this is NYC. Rooms are small here, unless you're staying in Times Square at the Hilton. The beds are super comfy. The TV has hi-definition channels. In the KING rooms, there is a real desk and chair to do work at. The staff are incredibly friendly and helpful. The location is great, in my opinion. A 10-minute walk to Penn Station/Madison Square Garden. A 2-minute walk to Park Ave where you can pick up the 4/6 Train. Also, you're in Flatiron/Chelsea where within a 10 minute walk, there are amazing restaurants, shops, etc. And heck, its NYC - get out and walk a bit, and there is amazing things everywhere. Its not close to Times Square. If this is where you're vacationing, might choose a different location. But you can always catch the train or bus north and get there. Cabs in the city are cheap too. $8 to Times Square? Also, regarding the noise from the street. You're in NYC. There's garbage trucks at night; there is construction during the early morning; there are cabs honking. This is NYC. This is what you should expect. Even on the top floors, you hear a ton of street noise. This is to be expected. All the rooms, except the ones ending in 7 face the street. Just be prepared, and know that this isnt unique to The MAve, its everywhere here in midtown. You want quieter? Choose a quieter location...like Key West, Florida. All-in-all, this is a great hotel, at good prices. Give it a try; I dont think you'll be disappointed.

“Fun hotel, great location” The Curtis was certainly as "advertised" on TripAdvisor. The welcome was great as soon as we walked in the door, and the cookies were a nice bonus (however, I would have liked an option without nuts due to allergies). The decor was fun, and the idea of "theme floors" - each with an individual welcome from the elevator and related decor on the walls - was entertaining. We saw multiple people just riding the elevator to "tour" the floors. The fun theme continues in the hotel's info book, which reminds guests that they can borrow games from the front desk - and gives some pretty difficult trivia questions. The location was great - within walking distance of lots of restaurants, the baseball field, the performing arts center, and light rail to the football stadium. I do agree, however, with some of the reviewers. The room was comfortable, but nothing really special, and a fridge would have been nice. Windows didn't open, and there was an odd smell (I'm assuming from the air conditioner, which couldn't have been used much, yet - the smell went away when we turned the AC off). Bed was very comfortable, but AC was a bit loud. I didn't hear any other guest noise, but I don't know if there was anyone on the floor. Parking was $20 for the overnight - you might be able to pay less if you arrive late and are leaving early (as we did). I saw ads for $12 overnight at nearby garages, but I don't know the hours. Might be worth checking. Because of the "funky" feel, the very helpful staff, and the location, I'd highly recommend this hotel, but I agree with other reviewers that it's not worth more than $150 / night.

“Great location and service!” The hotel is located in the center of everything. You can walk to Navy pier (a touristy place but great views along the water), take a fairly quick cab to watch the cubs game or lots of good restaurants. Pros: Centrally located, attentive service, clean and fairly spacious room. The hotel itself is an older building but very well maintained. Comfortable bed and fantastic view of the city from the room. Cons: Breakfast is not included, no matter what your status. Also, late check out is 2pm for platinum members, which is not really up to par with what all the other chains offer. The TV is a small cheap flatscreen. Its an older one and is dated, but it was sufficient for my stay (I wasnt there to watch TV). Also, the front desk was not able to print an invoice - they said it was because it was prepaid (directly through the hotel chain's website). When I called the 800#, they were also not able to and said I had to call the hotel. Finally someone in the accounting department was able to print email it to me. When a friend of mine left his key and ID in the room, security was helpful and escorted him to the room and let him in and check his ID. They were helpful to do so again after an item was left in the room after checkout. I personally prefer Starwood hotels (where I usually get 4pm checkout, breakfast, and internet included) and wanted to stay at the Westin or W Hotel, however, the group decided on the Intercontinental. When I walked into the room, they have a computer screen on the desk offering a welcome message and I believe you can view news, internet, etc. on this screen.
