During the rest of my stay there, the screen displayed an error message "Oops" and didnt work. Not a big deal but I expect things like this to work when I'm paying for a hotel like this. I would stay here again and recommend it to friends!

“Remodel serves this property well...” The newly remodeled Grand Hyatt at GCT is a far cry from its former dull self. The rooms are the hippest, yes I said hippest, European style I have stayed in throghout my domestic travels. The entire room has been reworked from its infrastructure to decor. Case in point is the electrical system. Now what is exiciting about plain old electrical, you flip a switch and there is light. Not in this room. There are no switches to flip just control stations to push and command the lighting scheme in the entire room and bath. One push and all lights are on or maybe just the bath or just your nightlight. It was a very nice feature once I figured out the schematic. The furniture was straight out of a European show room and the bed was very comfortable. Oh and how could I forget to say the room was BIG...huge by NYC standards. Plenty of room and even a nice entry way with full length mirror so all the beautiful people can look at their wonderful outfits before walking out the door. The room was also quiet. I have stayed at this property a number of times and glad to be back after this most recent remodel. Very enjoyable stay all around.

“Nice Stay” Overall, I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The room was clean and quiet, bed was comfortable, good variety of TV channels, and wireless internet was flawless. There are some minor flaws that the hotel can't do anything about like the slow elevator and small bathrooms. Also, the continental breakfast room is too small and has bad traffic flow. The breakfast is the standard HI Express, which I always like.

“Just a "hip" youth hostel” The hotel's roof top bar is terrific. That's why I always wanted to stay in the hotel, hoping that the quality of the rooms would match the great bar experience. I must say that I was more than disappointed. I understand that the hotel wants to be different and hip, but the hotel's hallways and rooms essentially look like a European youth hostel. Especially the bed is super annoying (see the other reviews for more details). So I strongly recommend staying at the Marriott or the Westin and walking a couple of blocks to the Standard, having a drink at the rooftop bar, and then returning to a much more comfortable hotel room. At least that's what I'll do next time I stay in L.A. downtown...

“Perfect place for a honeymoon” My husband and I recently stayed here for our honeymoon and thoroughly enjoyed it. We had made a reservation for a King room, but upon check-in we were informed that they had overbooked. Since we were on our honeymoon, they upgraded us to the Presidential Suite. The staff was extremely friendly, smiling at us each time we left and returned. The decor is very classy, and the location can't be beat. It's near several nice restaurants, lounges/bars, and great shopping. It is right around the corner from a cable car stop and only a few blocks from Union Square. Hop on the cable car, and it takes you right to Fisherman's Wharf. The evening wine tastings are nice, but the breakfasts are miniscule.

“Upper West Side gets you out of Midtown, in style” I love staying on the Upper West Side, even when business takes me to Midtown, For one thing, it's midway between business and family members for me. But additionally, it is near great, relatively moderately priced restaurants and shopping, usually with good bus or subway connections to anywhere I need to go, and feels more like the real New York, where people actually live and hang out. I have returned to On the Ave three times in the past 16 months, once for vacation, once for business, and once for a hybrid of the two. It meets all my needs. Even the smallest rooms are well appointed and comfy and suitable for the business traveler. Very nice staff. Great neighborhood. As a woman of 50 something who often travels alone, I feel safe here and I don't feel like a blowsy midwestern dork the way I sometimes do in impossibly and selfconsciously hip venues.
“enjoyable airport hotel” Stayed here for a three day conference. It was convenient to get in and out of the city as well as the airport, although it is a bit of a walk. Typical conference hotel

“Good Hotel” Great location, freindly staff, good rooms, soft beds and pillows. If you're going to stay down by the Wharf (which I would not recommend - stay downtown instead), then stay here. Even for a Marriott (which has good hotels, for the most part), this Hotel is a real standout.

“Holiday Inn Charlotte Underpromises and Overdelivers” For the price, this hotel is an outstanding deal. The hotel is centrally located, the rooms are reasonably well appointed and the service is great. This hotel competes well with the nearby Omni and Doubletree - and it can generally be booked for a fraction of the price.

“Good +” Three nights at this hotel in the gas lamp. Felt new, bright and friendly. The room was modern and comfortable. I enjoyed being able to have the windows open and get some of that clean fresh air. I had access the concierge which had real good food, much better than the cheese and nuts you often see or unfrozen spring rolls. My only disappointment on this hotel was the gym. You have to walk through a nightcub on the roof to get to it, and its awkward. the equipment was second tier as well in the fitness center, and it was really warm in the room. I decided to go running instead which is great in that part of town. I recall seeing in a prior rating a complaint about the gym some time ago and the hotel responded saying it was going to be moved elsewhere and updated. That wasnt the case yet when I visited.

“History and Location” Stayed in Nov 2009 for a conference. PROS 1. Elegant and impressive common spaces, great for holding large meetings. 2. 10 min walk to White House, 15 or so to the Mall. 3. History (and infamy) of the hotel add to its character! 4. Excellent service, from check in, to concierge, to bag check. CONS 1. Unacceptably SLOW internet access! If you need to work and must depend on hotel internet I would seriously consider staying elsewhere. So slow I could barely perform basic email functions and paid $13.95 a day for the "privilege"! 2. Basic rooms are relatively small and a bit dated. Overall, a good place to stay but not without drawbacks.

“Outstanding in every way!” Very Comfortable! Excellent quality! This hotel is almost like being at home. Very Comfortable Rooms! I almost never sleep well in a hotel the first night. I slept great! Very Quiet even though my room overlooked the street. The staff is very friendly and they know the area! The complimentary breakfast is very high quality.

“What a Great Stay!” My wife made the reservations, b/c she's an InTouch member. She rec'd a "birthday" rate, which included chocolates, a card from the staff, and free champagne and dessert at the hotel's restaurant. Unfortunately, she was sick and couldn't come to Philly - so I took advantage of her perks. The room had been upgraded to a queen queen - so it was spacious and big enough for 6. Everyone at the Palomar treated me with kindness and respect, and I felt very, very comfortable staying there.

“May be a bargain for weekend stays” I've twice spent a long weekend here Fri-Sun, on low rates that I found on Hotwire (under $150/night, all-in.) Positives: A typical Hilton room, good value for the price - modern, comfortable, & clean. Rooms may be a little small, but typical by NYC standards. The views over the WTC site & beyond can be amazing, as many other reviews have mentioned. Negatives: Lobby bar is small and only ever seems to have 1 server, so there may be nowhere to sit and/or a long wait for drinks. Some reviews have mentioned noise from the WTC site - I have stayed twice (2011 and 2009) and the noise was minimal; did not bother or wake me at all - maybe it depends on what day you are there. Also, I like the area myself (there is much more night/weekend life in the area than there used to be), there are plenty of shops/bars etc. within a 5-10 minute walk; but if you are unwilling/unable to walk at least a couple of blocks then you may find the neighborhood boring. Altogether, I think it's a good value for tourists on a discounted weekend rate. At full price ($300+), it may suitable for business travelers, but I think a tourist might be disappointed.

“Could not ask for a better place to stay in Chicago” I love staying in the Gold Coast District / Magnificent Mile in Chicago. I used to stay at the Amabassador East. These hotels were the same price when I booked and with the Ambassador being so outdated I figured I would give the Allerton a chance. I was blown away. I paid extra for a larger king room as I do the Insanity workout DVDs and there was plenty of room. Rooms were clean and nicely decorated. Bed was comfortable and bathroom was big enough. I was on the 21st floor and did not have to wait long for elevators at all. I saw a report that this hotel had a report of bed bugs after I had reserved the room. When I inspected the bed there were not signs of them. If this hotel is in my budget I will always stay there. It is only a few blocks from a CTA Station and plenty of restaurants around. Hotel is centrally located I could walk to most all my appointments.

“Good Value” We stayed at this hotel for 1 night for a quick weekend trip to Chicago. Won the room through priceline at $125. The location is perfect- right off Michigan Ave in the heart of all the action. The beds were comfy. My only complaints were 1- the AC unit was SO loud and I could not get it to stop! It kept waking me up at night. 2- I called housekeeping for extra towels and the lady who answered the phone questioned me on why I needed more bc she stated "don't you already have four?" She then said she'd send somebody up to bring them and that I had to give the person the used towels! Seriously!? lol That was ridiculous! Also, pkg is $50 for 1 night. Although very high, that's how much pkg is anywhere in downtown pretty much. Other than the housekeeping incident, service was wonderful- the bell hops were so kind and the front desk was very kind too.

“Small hotel feel, perfect city location” Great service, friendly check-in process, good rooms, very clean, bar not so crowded you can't get a server's attention, good location to Pru Center, Copley Square, shopping on Boylston St area

“Another gem from the Four Seasons” We stayed here for a weekend stay in early August 2012. This hotel is new, about 9 months since it opened. Typical Four Seasons experience - but a couple things really stood out here. 1. The bathrooms have TV there in. Built into the mirrors. Have seen this at a couple other hotels - nice touch. 2. The rooms have a remote built into the wall on either side of the bed that allows you to kill the lights by reaching over, and - this was big - turn on and off the Do Not Disturb from the bed, in canse you forgot. Do Not Disturb is electronic here, a little red light in the hallway confirms it. 3. The restaurant Wit and Wisdom was specatactular - for dinner one of the best meals I have ever eaten. 4. The inifinty pool outdoors was beautiful, and what a view of Baltimore from there. 5. Hotel is in a quiet area, so easy to walk to the rest of the Inner Harbor. This was a wonderful stay. Our room (City view) still had a view of the marina and was clean and fresh. Hotel seemd to have an odd almost bacon smell when youi first arrived, but after a couple days did not notice it. Faint - but distinctive. Maybe it was a odor trick, but we were not the only guests that mentioned it. However, not strong enough to worry about. The Spa was fully booked so we did not get a chance to use it - next time will do so and review. A beautiful clean gem in Baltimore. We will be back!!!

“Eastside Only” A good hotel overall. Try to get a high floor. I stayed on the 11th floor and heard a lot of street noises; requiring ear plugs in order to sleep through the night. It is also helpful to have a sleeping mask since the window shades are paper thin and do not keep out the exterior lights. Otherwise, the bar/lobby is nice and conducive to a drink before heading out to a restaurant. Please know that the subways are readily available if you are traveling on the eastside. However, in order to switch to the westside you have to take the shuttle from Grand Central, which is about 7 blocks from the hotel and rather time consuming. It is a good buy if you get a good deal as I did through Priceline.com

“Great Lobby but Tiny Loud Room” The hotel has a very cool lobby, and the staff is great- very helpful and responsive. It has the usual Kimpton happy hour, which is always a hit with guests. Our room, however, was TINY and loud. As I have stated in other reviews, I am sensitive to noise issues at hotels- the walls at this hotel were paper thin, to the point where a person could hear drawers closing and hangers being hung. Also, there was no way to escape hall noise. Thank goodness our neighbors in the rooms were not loud guests. I would not go out of my way to stay here again.

“Hilton on the Bay” This hotel is laid out in a park style with a number of buildings making up the hotel. The grounds had lovely landscaping, with birds of paradise surrounded by a low purple flower. The lawns are rolling and well maintained. We were cheerfully greeted as we pulled up to the front of the location. We were greeted a second time by a bellhop as we entered the lobby. The desk hostess continued the warm welcome. We had booked two rooms online using a discount website. The hostess told us the hotel had given us adjoining rooms. One room had a king size bed while the other had two queens. Because we were traveling with another couple we asked if we could have two rooms with king size beds. Even though we used the discounted website, the hostess cheerfully changed our rooms and quickly reassigned us two king size rooms. One room overlooked the freeway while the other one overlooked the bay. The room overlooking the freeway had several minor issues. The paint in the room was chipped just above the desk. The carpet was pulling back and frayed where it met the tile. The cold water did not work at the sink. The room was large and very comfortable overall. The other room had a nice view of the bay with no issues of which to speak. Both rooms were reasonably clean, with some dusting issues. Besides the wear in places, the other drawback was the $32 per night self parking fee. The hotel was about one mile from SeaWorld, two miles from Old Town, seven miles from Petco Park. This is the type of hotel where you bring the family for a family vacation. We didn’t have any time to make use of most of the amenities but everything looked inviting.

“Good Bang For Your Buck” I just returned from staying at the coral sands Motel for 1 week. All in all it was not that bad as the previous review. It is an old motel but very clean and very quiet. Parking is much better than other motels that I have stayed in the same area. The staff all were friendly and helpful. I did see some remodeling going on so it most likely will get even better. Do not go there expecting the Ritz- go expecting a clean room and good location to Hollywood/West Hollywood events. If you want more expect to pay way more otherwise this is a decent choice.

“Not my favorite.” Lets talk about the good things first. Location is not that bad. Great views of the city depending what side of the building you are. Good food at the restaurant downstairs with very friendly waiters and bartender. The only thing I like about the rooms is the flat screen tv. The rooms are not that bad, but need upgrades. Very Holiday Inn. My alarm clock was like from the 80s, and I notice the have different types on other rooms. This was my forth stay here. (not my choice). Not very friendly at the front desk. Not sure if it was because they knew were are there for work or what. The lady at the gift shop was soooooooooo rude to me. (only cash by the way). The workers at the restaurant are the nicest on that hotel. They have parking at the hotel. (check for pricing). The happy hour at 4:30 PM was not that bad, and they have great burgers. The cleaning staff knocked at my door twice with my "do not dirturb" sign on. The hotel is not that bad, but there is no excuse to be rude to a guest. I will not stay here with friends. Sorry. :-(

“Yes, stay here but there are some (very) minor issues.” As business travelers, we picked the Warwick Hotel in NYC because of its location, reputation and TripAdvisor reviews. Good decision based on good tools. The bonus is that the place is very clean and the rooms are very fresh. Some staff that standout include Jamaal at the front desk, Daniel the bellman - who just may have the best attitude for a bellman EVER - and Ray in the package room who is all about doing a good job for his guests. Oh, and the servers and manager in the hotel bar (did not get their names) did a nice job as well. ---- my only minor complaints are with a couple of things that are missing: charging your phone in your room is not easy with the very limited number of outlets, there is no coffee maker and this may be the last hotel on the planet that has not yet installed the curved "heavenly" shower curtain rod. All three seem like very simple fixes and each would elevate this lovely hotel to a preferred status. Thanks Warwick, we enjoyed our stay.

“Don't let the neighborhood spook you...” Yes, its not the best area, but really where is in this area? Its close and convenient to the Hollywood sites, and offers decent nightly rates compared to other hotels in the area. The hotel is clean and quiet for the most part. Nothing fancy, noticeable areas of improvement, but comfortable. They charge almost $20 for parking in their gated lot, which was a bit disappointing, but the complimentary breakfast made up for it. A lot of items to choose from, including an made to order omelet bar. They said they have a bar but it didn't open until 6pm so we weren't able to check it out.

“Amazing four points!!” Staff was cold and disinterested during check-in. Hotel, however, is beautiful, clean, and modern. Loved heavy warm comforters and bedding. Terrific bathroom with modern fixtures, glass shower, and pocket door. Gym was small, but they give access to Balleys across street. Great location with dozens of restaurants nearby, movie theater across street. Bought diet coke at front desk - $3 for an 8 oz bottle?!?! Parking $25 ?!?! Shower drain was clogged up so you finish your shower standing in puddle. Otherwise great hotel, would stay again. Forgive the brevity of this review - typing on iPhone.

“Definitely the best hotel in Detroit” I have moved my review of the Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport to five stars. Over the last few months I have been staying at the Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport while working and visiting Detroit. Coming to Detroit is depressing however staying in the Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport it feels like a five star hotel. Guess that's why it's ranked the number one hotel in Detroit. When staying here it feels like you are not in Detroit. After I have spent many nights at the Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport, here are my top fifteen reasons why I wouldn't stay anywhere else; 1) Easy and fastest access to the terminal. Evening if you have to fly out of the north terminal 2) Exceptional service for the front desk, restaurant staff, to valet parking 3) Best beds in Detroit 4) For an airport hotel the rooms are so quiet, well expect for the buzzing noise near room 826. I avoid rooms near 826. Buzzing noise drives me crazy. I think it's a transformer on the roof. The hotel staff is aware of the issue. 5) Excellent wine list at the bar. I think the prices are great. Recommend the Duckhorn. 6) Pizzas are yummy. You can create your own pizza. I like the cheese, tomato with small cocktail tomatoes. 7) Excellent club lounge. The breakfast, coffee in the morning is very good. Great spread in the evening too. 8) Brand new equipment in the gym 9) Awesome views of planes from your window. If you get a room facing the inside of the hotel it makes a great room watching experience. Amazing what people do in there hotel room without closing the curtains. 10) Great mini bar without the ridiculous instant magnetic charge. 11) Best corporate rate in Detroit. 12) Always get my Platinum upgrade 13) Internet seems to work well. Better from the inner rooms. 14) Best hotel working bar that closes late and has a good crowd. 15) I can always get a last minute reservation here. I guess I cannot say enough good things about the Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport. That is why I keep coming back!! Westin management is doing something right at this location. Its truely what I expect from a Westin hotel.

“Ehhh.... stay elsewhere” A friend and I stayed here MLK weekend. We got the room for $85 on hotwire. We read the reviews on this site and knew the decor would be bad, but the staff good. First the negatives: BEWARE, if you would like to print out your boarding pass you will have to use the business center. This becomes a VERY expensive extra. $5 for 15 minutes of internet time and a $1 minimum printing charge. I believe that if a hotel claims to be a 4 star hotel, then this should be a little extra that the hotel could take care of. Also, they charge you for newspapers, and you don't get one if you are checking out that day. But I refuse to post without mentioning the positives. The location was fantastic. Take the Chicago exit off the red line, go straight two blocks and then up three. When you hit the Louis Vutton store go down half a block. The bellhop and front door staff were absolutely fantastic. The water pressure was great for a hotel. Yes, the decor was ugly and the rooms could be considered "small". I'm not sure if I would stay here again, but the price for the location is something that you should take into consideration. . But I wouldn't not stay here because of the rooms.

“About what you would expect for an airport marriott” Rooms are typical marriott, my guess is refurbished 4 years ago. Good location and they have a free shuttle to the airport. If your in town for business this is a solid choice, if your here for vacation you can do much better.

“Truly a great hidden gem!” Not a chain hotel, but great individual service, care and detail is part of this smaller hotel's charm. Very good pricing for this hotel. It does deserve a 5 star rating, even if small and without an onsite restaurant. Well kept rooms and hotel property. Beautiful landscaping, nice clean pool and areas, clean rooms, nice furniture, good bedding, soft pillows. Very beautiful and charming setting. Area surrounding the hotel is business or light industry. But good location near the I-5 and close to many tourist sites. We stayed in the newer building, so can not speak to the other units, but they appeared to be equally as nice. Liked the rooms floorplan, bath and dressing room space. Nicely arranged mini-refrig. and microwave in wall space. The rooms, carpet, furniture, wall hangings, bedding, lotions, etc. are all nice. Breakfast is provided, it is what one generally is served, which does include hot items of waffles and oatmeal, boiled eggs, cereal, toast, orange juice, coffees, teas, pastries, muffins, fruit, etc. The breakfast room is very nice, but one does notice that the staff goes out of their way to refill items as well as taking pride in keeping it clean and in tip top shape. We greatly appreciated the staff, reception, etc. Location is next to Old Town, so one could walk, as a short walk, 2-4 blocks from the hotel, or drive and park. The Trolly station is within walking distance in Old Town area so if one does not have a car this hotel works if you plan to take the trolley or bus. Many shops and restuarants in Old Town. Within a short drive to other dining options and other areas of the city. The hotel is near the airport, Balboa Park, Gaslamp District, beaches, downtown, La Jolla, etc. I/we visit San Diego often and this is a good choice, especially for budget travel. Parking is free. Excellent experience and we will certainly return to the Old Town Inn.

“One of my favorite hotels anywhere for a small group meeting” I've stayed at the Riverwalk Vista five or six times. I love: the slate shower stalls with rainwater showerheads, the bath amenities in a useful plastic pack, the thick, plentiful towels and the robes, the large rooms and comfortable beds, the windows, the various lounge areas for private conversations, the meeting room with comfortable chairs, the excellent coffee, cookies and healthy breakfast, the staff, the tasteful furniture, art, pictures..... I have always stayed here with small meeting groups. This is the ideal site for 5-12 people to meet. The meeting room is ideal for a group of 10. You have the place pretty much to yourselves for after hours conversations, plus dependable wi-f and, the convenience of a guest room just steps from the meeting room. The location in SA is good: Schilo's German Deli, with superb cheap meals and draft beer, is just across the street (try the pea soup, the sauerbraten in the evening, the deviled eggs and the blackberry cobbler) and will cater your lunch. You can have a Riverwalk dinner or take a cab to La Fogata for the best Mexican. Sights including the Alamo are close at hand. I keep bringing groups here because the combination of the comfort of the hotel and the interesting surroundings are unbeatable. As for the negative comments below: maybe it's because I'm from New York, but the street noise has never bothered me. This week was fiesta, but the double glazed windows kept my Riverwalk-facing room quiet. I do agree that the guest rooms could use a bit more light. We New Yorkers wear only black, and it was hard to tell my various black garments apart in the room.

“Nice BaySide Hotel” This Hilton Hotel is nice. We have stayed a couple times here and all the rooms are nice. Cant really share much cause its been awhile since we been to this hotel. But I do room soom of the villa rooms have a direct access to the bay.

“Very nice Hotel.....” Very nice hotel,Very elegant lobby.Rooms are tasteful and elegant with comfortable beds and pillows.Staff was courteous but NOT extremely friendly.Good deal on Priceline for $110/ nt.

“Pampering in Phoenix” I stayed at the Royal Palms Resort and Spa for three nights while attending a business conference held at the hotel. I had a large room with a patio set in the beatifully landscaped grounds of the hotel. Appointments in the room well all of high quality and the bathroom included a soaking tub as well as a shower. All of the staff from the porters to the front desk and all of the service people were friendly and efficient. Our meals at the conference were catered by the hotel and all were quite good. The spa on the grounds was a delightful interlude that included a professional massage. The hotel is less than a half-hour from the airport but its setting at the base of Camelback mountain is worlds away.

“Neat & Tidy” Stayed here one night for business. After arriving late the reception staff took no time at all to settle me into my room with a King Size Bed which was simply enormous. The decor is dated however the room is clean and everything worked. Whilst I could see a quite busy road from my window the noise did not make it inside. There was even a clock radio in the room with an ipod charging station. The hotel has a pool (outdoors) and a small gym. Breakfast is served in TGI Fridays restuarant located in the hotel lobby. The buffet spread was okay and there was an egg station. Pricing was acceptable. There is also a Starbucks in the lobby if you want an alternative option.

“Older hotel that use a makeover buy was still nice.” I stayed here on May 20th for one night on my way to San Antonio. The hotel was easy to find and had plenty of parking. Check in was quick and the staff very nice. Our room was dated yet very clean. Our bed was awesome and the linens white and crisp. Overall it was a good value for what I paid. I booked on name your own price on priceline and won $59.00 plus fees and taxes We looked at the food menu and it seemed pricy so we opted for one of many places to eat within walking distance. I can't com

“Fantastic Hotel that keeps us coming back” Attentive service, clean and well appointed rooms, fantastic restaurants in the heart of the city. We walked to Millennium Park, the Art Institute, many bars and restaurants, shopping, everywhere! So much more to do than we could possible fit into 3 days. We really could not ask for anything more. Yes, it can be a bit on the pricey side but discounts can be found and the feeling of being in another world is worth every penny.

“Very classy hotel” After looking at Hotwire and being rejected at Priceline, I started looking for reviews of hotels. If I was going to pay full price I wanted the best for my money. To our surprise, Loew's with a AAA rate, was no more expensive than most of the three star hotels in Philadelphia Center City. We had three very nice nights there in a comfortable, quiet room. The lobby is fine, and the staff very accomodating. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. The location is great--close to the Reading terminal market and other center city locals., We joined their loyalty program and recieved a fruit bowl and Fiji water every day.
“Great stay” Nice rooms - fairly large and very comfortable bed. Good and fast food on room service. Gym is excellent - standard W gym but in a relatively large space. Great service.

“Lovely Hotel/Execellent Guest Service” I read the reviews and decided to stay at the Doubletree in Mission Valley. I am sooo glad I did. The ride to the hotel via Super Shuttle from airport is $12.00 per person. Hotel is located in a beautiful part of San Diego; quiet with nice lush green surroundings. The hotel is connect to the Hazard Center which has restaurants such as Joe’s Crab Shack and others. There is also a movie theatre in the Center. The train/trolley is located across the street and can take you to various points around SD. I took the train to the Gaslight District. Along the way there is Fashion Mall for the shoppers/ Cost is $5.00 round trip. Now to the hotel, from the moment I walked in I was greeted warmly by Kirk( who can teach excellent guest service) at the front desk. My room was clean and roomy. Bed was comfortable. The hotel has a Business Center on the first floor. Also there is a computer outside of the room if you only need to print a boarding pass. On the lobby level there is a restaurant(The Fountain) and bar as well. Outside there is a nice pool, pool chairs to sit, relax and read, etc and a hot tub. Doubletree has something called a Care Line. I used it and the service was immediate. Hilton should adopt something like this at all their properties, if they have it I am not aware of it. It really shows you want to take care of the hotel guest. My stay was pleasant and I will return when I am in the san Diego area. Also Doubletree has some of the best chocolate chip cookies :-)

“Perfect” I love this hotel. It is intimate, comfortable, perfectly situated, and a joy to return to. Good bed, furniture, lights, amenities (esp. complimentary high-speed modem). So comfortable, and an intelligent, attentive staff.

“Got a great rate, good location, nice sized rooms, friendly staff” Got a awesome rate here - $99 a night for a Radisson in NYC. Good location - about 4 blocks from Grand Central Station, about 5 blocks from Rockefeller Center. Away from the chaos and noise of Times Square but close enough to walk to sites and subway stops. Room was a good size, especially for NYC, desk, flat screen, 2 drawer dresser, closet with safe and our room had 2 twin beds. Both room and bathroom were clean. Negative is the windows are definitely not soundproof, had asked for a high floor and unfortunately didn't get one - was told it wasn't available but could ask again the next night. We heard all the noise -trash trucks, sounds outside, etc..honking, sirens. Other then not having soundproof windows, I would recommend staying here - nice place and nice location

“I did like all about this hotel” Great location, big rooms, nice staff, The bathroom is very nice, the beds are a little small but in general it's a nice hotel, ask for a Hight floor facing the entrance I mean the side of the entrance of the hotel because the other side is a Hight way but still both sides are very quiet

“Great little hotel in top location: fantastic staff” Stayed in March for a long weekend. Hotel fantastically located: you couldn't want a more central location and across the street from the subway. When we arrived the staff were so warm and welcoming we instantly felt at home. Rooms were upgraded to slightly larger doubles but they were still pretty small. Other reviews had mentioned this but we weren't in New York to stay in our hotel rooms. Happy hour in the hotel bar during weekdays was great and very popular but the downside was we could hear the music on the 2nd floor. Didn't interrupt sleep as the music stopped fairly early but was a minor irritation. Everything worked in the room: large fridge, good TV etc. Nice Aveda products in bathroom. Window looked out onto internal tiny space. Room service was fast and efficient. Breakfast was included with a selection of pastries and tea and coffee. Would definitely stay here again: the price, staff and location were fantastic.

“Good location. Ok property” I had a one night stay at this hotel this week. The location is great - right in the middle of the city and one block from the 16th Street Mall. The check in process was efficient and the room was comfortable. Nothing spectacular but fine. The fitness center is odd. There is a very nice area for cardio equipment but the weights are stuffed in the back of the pool deck. If you are planning to do any strength training while staying at this hotel, be prepared to sweat in the heat and humidity of the pool that is 10 feet from where you are bench pressing. Overall, I would probably stay here again.

“BUSY hotel.” If you can stay at this property for under $100, go for it. My room was VERY clean. Bed was comfortable. Loved the set aside bathroom. Funny how when a hotel provides 2 free bottles of .50 cent water, you feel as though they really care about you! Love the free wifi and free airport shuttle. I arrived at 9:30pm and the place was BUSY. Lots of flight crews stay here. The shuttle at 5:30am was packed! If you need a place to stay near LAX, I recommend this property, but pay under $100.

“Cela reste une vaeur sûre” C'est la deuxième fois que je vais à ce motel. Il est bien placé, on peut se garer, il y a un supermarché à proximité... Bien sûr le personnel est aimable comme une porte de prison mais tenir un motel la nuit à Los Angeles doit rendre méfiant. Le petit déjeuner est plus que symbolique mais en général on y va pas pour cela. Le motel en lui même est sympathique et propre. J'ai eu une chambre différente de la dernière fois et dans les deux cas je n'ai pas eu à me plaindre. La moquette épaisse peut donner une mauvaise impression, ainsi que le coup de peinture aux finitions baclées que l'on peut noter notament dans la salle de bain ; mais il faut garder en tête que c'est bien placé en prix et propre, c'est tout ce que l'on demande quand on va dans cette classe d'établissement.

“Comfortable Stay in Central Location...Just Okay Service” Very comfortable rooms and amenities at the Fairmont. The location is central to restaurants and businesses in the downtown Dallas area. Most restaurants are in walking distance (about .25 to .5 miles away) which can also be reached by cable cars that run on St. Paul. Internet access is also provided for free to club members (which is free). Restaurant and bar food and drinks were okay and we did not find it worth the price. We encountered a couple of issues with service. Our first issue was with the Bar. It took over 15 minutes before anyone came to take our order, then our server disappeared and it took us another 15 minutes to track down someone who was willing to help us. So we didn't have the opportunity to order additional drinks or food. Also, we noticed several inefficiencies with the valet service. Although it didn't impact me directly, I noticed that their disorganization caused significant back-ups in the valet and drive through area for the hotel which is already small to begin with. Be prepared to wait a while if you are looking to pull through during peak times.

“Pela localização - ótimo custo” Estivemos nesse hotel em outubro de 2011 em nossa passagem por San Antonio. O que avaliamos como os pontos mais fortes desse Hotel foram o custo acessível (muito bom) em relação à localização. Além da boa localização, muito próximo do centro e das principais atrações da cidade, como o RiverWalk. Pode-se fazer quase tudo a pé. Para quem está com carro o Hotel dispõe de estacionamento livre. O ponto fraco da Hotel são as instalações desgastadas e o mobiliário bem maltrado. A limpeza também não é grande coisa. O café da manhã é super básico, leite, sucrilhos, pão, manteiga e queijo.

“Like an upscale W” I just got back from a 2 night stay at the new Hotel Palomar Westwood. What a place. A good way to describe it would be an "upscale W". I've never dealt with a friendlier staff than at the Palomar. Every single person I encountered there was great. The rooms, furnishings, bathroom, etc, were all funky-modern-comfortable-perfect. I've never given a hotel an excellent/5 star rating, but they really deserve this. I reserved a spa room, but was upgrated to a 1br spa suite (rm 1801) , which had a seperate living room. The bathroom jacuzzi/spa tub and HUGE glass enclosed shower were incredible. I didnt have a "vista view" room, but being on the 18th floor, I still had a great view of the Hollywood Hills. I didnt want to get out of the bed, it was too comfortable. I would have dragged it out of there into the car if I could have. I did get room service one night and the food was great. Like I said, I really can't find a fault with this place. I would def reccomend staying here if your in LA and want to be treated right.

“Great rooms an Best service I've received in a while.” Hotel is clean and modern with comfortable bedding. Rooms are also very quiet as we didn;t hear a single person in the hallway or outside in the street durring our entire visit. Staff was exceptional at all times from check in to check out. Always greeting you with a warm smile. One staff member (Anwar) went out of his way for my partner who could no locate a pack of his normal cigarette's by driving to a specialty shop and picking them up for him which is far beyond what was expected but truley appreciated. Only downside is hotel is not very close to the main sights and museums. Subway station is about 10-15 minute walk. Highly recommended hotel for the firendly staff and comfortable room.

“Clean and simple, good location” The Sheraton is a good value. It's one of the less expensive hotels in San Francisco. This place is clean with good, friendly service. No frills, nothing fancy. I prefer a hotel in Market Square, where most of the restaurants and attractions in San Francisco are. This hotel is NOT near Market Square (downtown San Fran). This property is however walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf. Quite honestly, the Wharf is ok.....but I would recommend staying in downtown (Market Square) and driving or taking a cab to this area for the day; as opposed to staying at the Wharf. Overall, a positive experience, especially if you are traveling on a bit of a budget.

“Exceeded low expectations” I know it is damning with faint praise, but after reading all of the TA reviews, I was prepared for the worst. Spent 2 nights here, which I booked on Priceline. City was sold out, so the $150 per night supposed discount for an airport hotel with a bad rep did not exactly excite me, but alternatives were worse. Check-in staff was very friendly, though their system seemed momentarily quirky and--arriving tired after 10 p.m., I was greeted by two heads huddled over the computer for 5 minutes. It was an inauspicious start, but the young woman who checked me in was apologetic, very courteous and efficient and had me enroute to my room quickly. Free Tastykake at check-in was a welcome treat, which just about everyone seemed to like. My room was clean, comfortable and well-maintained if not luxurious. Frankly, I was expecting the worst. Unfortunately, the TV reception was poor (brought back childhood memories of "snow" on the screen, the wired internet connection did not work (more below) and the room had virtually no soundproofing, so I "enjoyed" the girls night out conversation well past midnight from the room to my right and the TV or radio until 4 a.m. from the room to my left. Curiously, the windows and exterior wall blocked out the airport noise fairly well. Go figure! The bed was comfortable, though my sleep wasn't the most restful with all of the noise from guests. In fairness, no one was being particularly loud. Standing in the hallway, I could barely hear the guests on either side of me. The problem was not evident until I entered the guest room; the interior walls and the lack of sound insulation really need attention. Leaving the hotel at 7:30 a.m., I reported the TV reception and internet problem to the front desk. They informed me that my room did NOT have internet at all (the connection clearly is there and so is the instruction card for access). The clerk courteously offered to move me, which I declined. She also said that there is free WI-FI in the lobby and that she would have someone fix the TV. Returning to the hotel around 5 p.m., I found a card from the TV repair technician. He claimed to have fixed the reception problem, but it was unchanged when I turned on the TV, so I called again. Went to dinner and he/she had been to the room in my absence. Reception on CNN was good. Unfortunately, it was absymal on all other channels. Breakfast buffet a bit after 7 a.m. Sunday morning was disappointing. Everything had recently been put on the buffet table under lights, but the scrambled eggs, hash browned potatoes and bacon were barely on the cold side of lukewarm. How does that happen with all three items first thing in the morning? I had a schedule to keep and no time to waste, so I ate and left. The restaurant staff was friendly enough, but spent most of their time socializing with each other. I recognize that they had little to do at that hour with just about every guest choosing the buffet, but someone might have thought to check on the food! Check out of the hotel was smooth and, as always, the shuttle drivers were prompt, courteous and friendly. The hotel is convenient if you want to be at the airport. I don't recommend it for tourists who are primarily interested in Philadelphia's attractions. I used the train from the airport to and from Center City and the Hilton's free shuttle to and from the hotel to the airport terminals. It was much less expensive than a taxi (particularly as I was traveling alone), but also is more time-consuming. The hotel shuttle leaves the hotel every 20 minutes and the train schedule is every 30 minutes, so coordinating the two will save time. The "business center" (a closet of a room with 2 computers, no printers) gives you 10 minutes of internet use free, after which exhorbitant charges apply. Come on Hilton, it is 2011, not 1999.

“Loved our stay at the Affina Dumont” We had a great stay at the Affina. The staff was great. Our favorite was Chris Chopin the hospitality professional at the front door. He really kept his eye out for you and seems to enjoy people. Listen to where he tells you to eat...he was great. Our junior suite was very nice. Loved the pillow menu and the exercise kits. Room was nice and clean, roomy and set up nicely. Aveda toiletries was a nice touch. Gym was very good. Loved the location of the hotel. Walked to everyplace from here. Bathroom was small but kitchen was great. Great neighborhood. I would stay again in a minute.

“My New NYC Home” I travel back to NYC several times a year and I have stayed and reviewed in numerous NY hotels. This was my first stay at the Courtyard SOHO. Let me say right off that it was the best experience I've had in a long time. The staff could not be friendlier. Every time I came in or out I was greeted with smiles and courtesy. The room is small but very comfortable. The basement gym is well equipped and underused. The bar/breakfast counter off the lobby serves starbucks coffee and basic breakfast items and the staff there was extraordinarily nice and helpful. Finally the location cannot be beat. Both the 1 and the E or C subway lines are a short walk away. A few blocks to the river and the pathway for running in the morning. A few blocks the other way and your on Prince or Spring Streets in the heart of SOHO. Tribeca is a short walk away as is Little Italy and the Village. Why stay anywhere else- seriously folks this is the place.

“Not worth the price” The Marriott Wardman is a bit outside of what I would consider downtown DC in the Woodley Park area. It is a big convention hotel and that was why we were there. The lobby is huge with a swanky bar / coffee bar, a pub / sports bar, a restaurant but their Starbucks is gone. The property is huge and setup for large conventions. Did not eat in the restaurant as we went to the Palm. The rooms were average and mine was dated in the central tower. Clean and comfortable but some problems with the bathroom. The price was $259 per night plus $37 to park, which both were way out of line. The Omni Shoreham behind the Marriott is a better choice (nicer and usually less expensive). But stay more downtown unless you need to be in the Woodley Park area.

“Spa Rooms are Much Nicer” We stayed in a standard city view room this time- 26th floor. We had a Spa Room last year. What a difference...the Spa bathrooms are much nicer: double sinks, separate water closet, separate glassed in shower from the large soaking tub, and they give you bath salts and sugar scrub. I'm not impressed with the regular room's bathroom- single sink and open toilet. We got a great rate at the multiple night stay of 30% off so it's a good value but Id definitely pay $50 more for the Spa room next time. Also rooms in the lower end numbers: --02 through --24 do not have any great view really regardless of how high you are. The Peninsula's standard room is much nicer.

“Great location for a NYC Stay” We stayed here in November 2008, the good - the location is great, close to Times Square, theatre, Central park , Radio City music hall, basically everything that a tourist wants to see in NYC. The so-so, the staff is OK at best,they spend more time looking busy that working from what I have seen, and would only help you if they had no other choice, The Bad- this hotel is very busy, which maybe is why the staff are the way they are, they might be a little tired and the price is a little high even for NYC, but that all being said the location makes this hotel the place to be. You should try ELLEN's StarDust cafe across the street, its awesome, I would suggest for breakfast.

“Great Service- Nice Hotel- NOt near the Beach” We stayed here just before the 4th of July. They are just finishing up with a room and lobby reservation and the hotel has a very fresh look to it. The rooms have plasma TVs and are well decorated. The staff is very helpful. Both happy hour and breakfast were enjoyable, no problem getting a table. As an example of excellent service, I left some clothing behind and the housekeeping manager Fed-xed them to my home. VERY impressive. The only downside is parking. The 17.00 fee is excessive and the garage is very difficult to drive through ( small and all one way, once at the top you have to drive against incoming cars to get down). Its located in more of a business area, the beach is a 10 min drive. Book with Confidence.
“Excelente ubicación, muy tranquilo.” Muy buen hotel, excelente ubicación, tranquilo, comodo. Personal muy amable.

“Great Location and value” We stayed here 4 nights during our trip to DC. The hotel is 5 blocks from the White House and we walked to all of the sites except for a cab ride to the Capitol. The parking garage was full when we got there so they directed us to the GW Public Parking Garage which was 3 blocks north on 22nd street. I would park there instead of the hotel as it is $12/day less. We had a junior suite which had a separate king bedroom and main room had a pullout couch that slept 2 kids. Kitchen was nice with a full refrigerator and there is a CVS right next door to get groceries. The hotel doesn't have an ice machine and you can buy ice at the liquor store next door but plan in advance as they aren't open on Sundays or in the morning. There is also a Subway a block away and other restaurants north a few blocks. Make sure you ask for a room with a view as we had one that faced East and could see the Capitol and Washington Monument and were on the 8th floor which was nice. Would definately recommend and stay here again!

“Great Hotel, as every hotel should be...” Superb Service Excellent Location close to main attractions... Service is number one! Highly recommend it! Its not the building, its not the location, but yes the attitude of the staff that makes this Four Seasons Hotel one the finest in the World...

“Very good location in DC” Hotel Madera is definitely a very nice choice for staying in DC. Very conveniently located, it has a good restaurant and very nicely decorated large rooms. There is no hall or large shared spaces but this should not influence the overall judgement unless specifically required from the guest. I enjoyed the warm atmosphere and the personal touch of the venue.

“Just an okay Westin” Hotel was okay. I give it 3 stars, for medium. I would not say this is an exceptional Westin because the decor is older style, outdated Place was in pretty good shape overall. Fairly clean...except long hairs on the floor in the bathroom. Internet was very poor, the workspace was poor. See pictures. Chair for desk was poor, needs to be an office style which is adjustable, and swivels. Bed was comfortable. Room service was okay. I left my Mifi hot spot there, and was very thankful that Amanda S., delivered it to me right away at my home address. Thank you Amanda! I got it, and your business card. I am not sure I will stay here again.

“Convenient location, modern decor, high standard - but not huge suites” We had a suite (is it all suite?) but the suite - or at least the one we stayed in - was basically a really large room - like an open plan / studio flat (apartment) with a kitchenette (sink but can't remember if you could cook) but not a true suite with different rooms. Room has coach (sofa) large bed, desk etc. Nicely furnished - good quality. Bar down stairs is really nice plus some of the better restaurants (recommended in the guidebook) are next door / across the road. Also a supermarket quite near by. All the main touristy bits are all within 10-15 minutes walk. No free wifi, except in the lobby, and the gym was tiny - looked like they'd just taken one room and put a few machines in it. Two people and it seem pretty full. But Seattle is easy enough to go running in.

“Good Hotel to Avarage Price” The room was ok and clean, the beds comfortable and the price was right, 300+ for a 2-bed room with breakfast for three. Internet was 12.50 per day, so we used the free internet in the lobby, which everybody else also seemed to do. All seats in the lobby and bar were occupied with people with laptops and iPads. Wouldn't it be an idea to consider to give free internet?

“One of the worst hotels in the W family and better Starwoods in DC” Most rooms are so small the bathroom is actually incorporated into the bedroom. There's a water-closet/shower and the rest of the bathroom setup is in the bedroom. Lame. SPG Platinum upgrade was from an inside small room to an outside small room. Looks like the smallest room on the floor map. Toothpaste remains left on the sink when I checked in. White carpets show many stains. If you're gonna use white carpet, you have to refresh fairly often. Weird kind of brothel-y theme in the lighting and in-room mirrors. Location in downtown near the Treasury so decent location in the daytime and a complete ghost town at night. No wifi. Plus is the DVD player in the room, but I'd rank this as the second worst W only above the W New York.

“Inconsistent” This is another one of those hotels, where if they know you're a first-timer, they will give you the worst possible room and see if you complain. as opposed to giving you the best possible room and want you to return. I don't know why they have this policy, since they are clearly not fully occupied. I decided to stay at this hotel after hearing rave reviews from Tripadvisor. But how frustrating it is when you read about good service from Tripadvisor members only to find it is inconsistent. I guess that's what separates the hotels in the top 20 and those outside the top 50. The ones in the top 20 are mostly consistent in the reviews, whereas the ones outside the top 50 will have one good review, followed by one bad one, and then another good and another bad. I was given a room on the lowest floor with no view. I was also disappointed it had no bathtub. Also, although the hotel says it is smokefree and makes you sign something that says you will be billed $350 if you smoke, the room had a strong smell of someone having smoked there. I was only here for one night so I didn't complain about being on the low floor. I don't think it was because of the rate I paid. I paid $179 plus tax, so it came to about $200 a night. That's a major reason why I don't stay at Best Western very often. If they are charging the same as a Marriott, why would I stay at Best Western? And now I find out that if I want to stay next week at this hotel, I only need to pay $129. Well, I guess I can't complain if I was paying $129, so at $179, I expect a bit more than what I am getting. The only saving aspect of this hotel is that it is located in Chinatown. It's nice to be so close to all the activity in the streets. I found a good Chinese restaurant. But I'm afraid that's it. I would consider staying here again if I got the $129 rate. And now that I know enough about this hotel, I can demand what kind of room I want, instead of letting them give me the worst room possible.

“Great shopping weekend” Just got back from a very busy shopping weekend in New York. This hotel was our haven. Fab location/great staff/comfy beds/great shower/lounge with complimentry hot drinks 24hrs and special eve cheese and wine to help you unwind before a night out. All the staff were so helpful and remembered you when you returned - you would not get this in a large hotel. Thanks to everyone at the hotel for making our weekend complete.

“Has some drawbacks . . .” I would recommend this hotel to any travelers who, like my friend and I, were passing through town without much money to spend on lodging. The hotel is not terribly expensive, it comes with a nice continental breakfast each morning, a 24-hour front desk, nice employees, and indoor entry. However, it is a case of you get what you pay for. The walls seemed paper thin and my friend and I both could hear everything that happened inside and outside of the hotel all night long. Each time a door slammed, the entire wall rattled. The vending machines were abysmal. You have one ice machine, one soda machine, and one of those dinky peanuts-chocolate candies machines on each floor and that is it. And if you have the misfortune of getting in late and needing to eat, you are out of luck. There are not easily accessible fast food places nearby and there is only one entrance to the hotel. If you miss it, you will have to go through a complicated loop-around to get back. If this is the only thing you can afford, you will be better off than if you stayed at the roach motel. But if you are able to put together an extra twenty or thirty dollars, stay elsewhere.

“Crowne Plaza Times Square” Stayed here June 17-21, 2004. Although the room was "average", the price was right and the service was exemplary. Staff easily and quickly accommodated several requests. I especially liked the fact that a security person was stationed at the elevator banks each evening. He checked to see that anyone using the elevators actually was a registered guest (well, that we had room keys which is better than zip!) Location is central to lots of NYC sites. I'd go back in a heartbeat (or as soon as I can find another excellent rate!)

“Great Location next to Times Square!” Upon driving into NYC for the first time I must say I was rather nervous. This hotel was so easy to find and once I dumped my car in a parking garage I could relax. The front desk attendant was very friendly and helpful, the atmosphere in the hotel was very comfortable and upscale. They even allow pets! The hotel was located right by Times Square so we could walk to everything easily! I will definitly return to the Novotel!

“nice hotel in great location.” I was pretty impressed with this place. Very clean, great service all around (especially from the people at the concierge desk), and a great location just a block off the 16th Street Mall, which is the center for all the restaurants and bars and nightlife and all that. they also have a rooftop pool, which is pretty nice. and very convenient for anything going on at the convention center, like the Great American Beer Festival which we went to, or all the foodtrucks on 16th and 17th streets. The beds were also very comfortable. We got a good rate of $130 a night for the festival discount, which for a solid four star hotel was very well worth it.

“Your basic cheap motel, with a noisy neighbor” There are times you just need a relatively inexpensive roof over your head in a convenient location. This fits that bill, but not much else. Feels very much like the old Days Inn it used to be. The lobby has certainly been cleaned up (isn't it always?), but the rest leaves a lot to be desired. Beat-up parking lot and stairs, gross pool area, generally dingy feeling from the moment you exit your car till you enter your room. Room was...a room. I don't say that in a hotel snob way, but I have seen plenty of budget places nowadays that do it much, much better. My room was cleanish and functional, with two key exceptions that you count on most: First, had a case of the classic motel A/C that's mounted under the front window and mainly blows behind the billowing curtain without actually cooling the room. I had to weight down the curtains with some shoes to avoid sweating all night. Second, the shower pulsed between hot and cold most of the time. Not ever scalding or freezing, but just enough to remind you that you wanted out as quickly as possible. I probably could have lived with all that, but the final nail in the coffin was the Buzzbrews 24-hour restaurant about 50 feet from the office. The restaurant itself is good, but be aware that it can draw the post-bar-closing crowd. My first of 3 nights (a MONDAY, not a weekend) was interrupted by a bunch of drunken "woo-hoo!"'s in our shared parking lot from 2:00 to 3:30 AM. If you value your sleep, that alone is reason enough to avoid this place and look elsewhere.

“Noisy with indifferent staff” We stayed at this hotel at the end of our 8 day trip to CA, unfortunately this was a big mistake. There were a catalogue of problems; The first room that we had was facing the main road and was very noisy, far too noisy to sleep in, we were then moved to another room and this was not suitable as all the rooms on one side of the hotel get noise from either the cooling tower or the kitchen. We were finally given a room that was not noisy, but in the process of finding this room we were shown a room with guests already in bed! We were compensated with $100 food voucher, unfortunately the food was deep fried and inedible. This is not what we have come to expect from a Hilton family hotel, if possible stay at a different hotel.

“Wonderful Place for 4th” We stayed at this location for the 4th of July weekend. The location is perfect for visiting Washington. Most downtown attractions are within walking distance. The White House is just 3 blocks, the Mall is about 6 blocks; Ford’s Theater is 6 blocks. There is a Metro station across the street which gives one access to the rest of Washington. The hotel is well maintained. The rooms are large and well furnished with a microwave and small refrigerator. The bathroom is also a good size. Our room was on the 9th floor facing the street. There was some street noise but not enough to disturb. The hotel staff was very accommodating to our needs. There is a nice bar/lounge for late afternoon and evening drinks. There are many restaurants within walking distance.

“Can't beat the location” So, let's just establish as a baseline that the only reason you'd stay at a hotel that is literally attached to O'Hare is if you've flown in late or are leaving early. Definitely don't stay at this place if you're planning a nice weekend in Chicago or anything! [You could stay near the airport if you were doing that to save money, but you should stay at one of the other properties in Rosemont, I think.] I gave this hotel a "very good" because it fulfills its function -- being a decent hotel with a can't-beat-it airport location -- well. If it were a Hilton that was, say, in downtown Chicago, it definitely wouldn't get a "very good;" it'd be more like an "average." I've stayed at this hotel a handful of times (most recently in January 2011), and each time it's been a decent experience. The rooms are small-ish, but they have nice decor, decent beds, a desk, etc.; they meet Hilton standards. The lobby isn't fantastic -- out-of-date decor and basically a big check-in space. The fitness center appears to have a full range of equipment, but I've actually never been able to use it because it closes early and my arrivals have always been late. I have to say that I do think it's a bit weird that an airport property (which is all about late arrivals and early departures) doesn't have a 24-hour fitness option. I've had room service a few times -- it's fine. I've never been able to have breakfast because the restaurant is never option at the time I have to head back to the terminals (again, weird...you'd think an airport hotel would start it's breakfast super-early). Service has always been polite, although once I encountered a VERY long line at check-in (my impression was that a flight had canceled and basically the whole plane had been sent to the Hilton for their airline-provided rooms). The hotel's big plus is its location. Unlike the many other ORD hotels, all of which require going to the bus/shuttle center and waiting for the shuttle bus, this one is on ORD's grounds, connected to the airport. You don't even have to go outside, you just follow the underground tunnels (they can be a bit confusing, but there is signage at every important turn). So, that's hard to beat -- there are times when you are leaving super-early or get in super-late where waiting for that airport hotel shuttle bus is a killer! That said, if you don't mind a shuttle bus, there are NICER hotels all near ORD -- bigger rooms, better decor, better services, etc. Each time I need an ORD hotel, it comes down to price. If the Hilton has a great rate, I book it, because you can't beat the convenience. There are a lot of other times, though, where the Hilton is $100+ more expensive than the other Rosemont hotels, and I don't think that it's location justifies that price premium, so I head to one of the other Rosemont properties and do the shuttle thing.

“Great value, but there are better options!” I stayed at the Hudson Hotel last weekend. I booked it on Tablet Hotels, and it cost $189 on Friday and $209 on Saturday. This is EXCELLENT value for a clean and comfortable hotel with a bit more pizazz than your average chain hotel in New York City. However, I wasn't totally thrilled and likely won't go back unless I need a really cheap hotel quickly. Pros: The hotel is a good location for tourists, especially if you haven't explored NYC much. It's at 58th and 8th, close to many tourist attractions (Times Square, Grand Central Station, Broadway, Central Park, Bloomingdale's). More experienced NYC travelers will appreciate its proximity to Central Park on a nice day, as well as nearby Plaza Hotel, Campbell Apartment, and Per Se. It's a Morgans hotel, so the design is cool and trendy. The room was very clean and it quiet enough to get a good rest. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful in getting taxis. Of course, the price cannot be beat. Cons: The room was just too small. My boyfriend and I felt borderline claustrophobic after an hour (and we had to keep our blind shut due to the view of pipes and dirt). Although I have absolutely no complaints with cleanliness or service, it was hard to move around the room, there was virtually no storage space, and I could barely fit in the bathroom (and I'm a very petite woman). If you've been to NYC many times you likely won't be thrilled with the location. It was a $10-15 taxi ride to our favorite bars and restaurants downtown (and there was a subway issue so we mostly took cabs). It was difficult to find a bagel or deli sandwich nearby and we ended up wandering for a while at lunchtime. Also, we were eager to try the Hudson's famous bar/club on Saturday night. We left the East Village after dinner at Momofuku because we had heard great things about the Hudson's bars. However, we were disappointed that the rooftop closed at 11pm, and the main bar was a little too club-like for our tastes. I think it's had it's day... But, if you're a college student or early 20-something looking for the whole NYC experience, the Hudson is great value. You'll get a clean, stylish room in a good location, with a few bars and a dance club to boot.

“Courtyard a big hit!” This proved to be an excellent choice among the many Washington hotel choices. We arrived late one evening and were pleasantly surprized by the very friendly staff, the excellent condition of the room, and mostly by the outstanding location of the hotel. We walked everywhere, and while the hotel is not located in the heart of the Dupont Circle action, we didn't mind the two blocks walk from the many restaurants and sights that the neighbourhood has to offer. We walked everywhere from this hotel - the White House, the National Mall, Smithsonian, etc. We didn't eat at the hotel restaurant and regretted that there was no continental breakfast included, but this hotel is an outstanding site for the $94.00/night that we paid. We will go back to Washington, and will definately use this hotel once again.

“It depends what you're looking for” It depends what you're looking for. If it's a large, standard room, hotel chain business style, plush carpets, chintz, renaissance or victorian ornaments... stay somewhere else. If on the other hand you want a well priced room, bare modern style, in a central NYC location, you may love the QT. My room was small and the decor so minimalist that it first felt like a cell. After a while, I got used to it though and started to enjoy all the amenities, some gimmicky but most are smart and well-thought in my opinion. Nice comfy bed, flat screen TV, radio with iPod station, free High-Speed Internet, large shower (no tub)... If you are not planning to spend the entire day in your room, everything is there and it's quite clean. The lobby is very small, the pool-bar area a little weird in my opinion, but the free breakfast is a nice plus in NYC and the croissants were really good. If you can get a room for less than $250, this is an excellent choice that it is likely to beat all basic budget NYC hotels easily. If the rates are above $250, think twice, there might be better options, more elegant and with more space.

“Good location - Good price” We had a one night stay in New York and selected this hotel based on the reviews, the price and the location. We arrived on a nice day and decided to walk from Penn Station. It is about a 15 minute walk which was not bad even with wheeled luggage. We arrived very early in the day after an overnight flight and the front desk clerk was able to place us in a room immediately which was very nice. The room was small but comfortaable. We did have a minor problem of ants in our room but they sent someone very quickly to spray the problem area. The bed in the room was a bit odd as it was just a foam mattress on top of a plywood board foundation. It was a bit odd but the bed was fairly comfortable. We found the hotel staff to all be very nice and friendly. An added bonus is that guests of the hotel receive a 10% discount at the Il Punto Restaurnat a block away. The restaurant had great food and great service.

“the only place I stay in Detroit” This Marriott features all you've come to expect from the chain, great bed for sleep, comfortable work desk, good on property restaurants and lounge. Based on their reliability and solid overall performance this is the only place I stay in Detroit. I got great service on my trip last week; bags didn't make my flight and were delivered to the desk in the middle of the night. I'd asked to be called at any time they arrived and the desk called promptly just past midnight. The bellman delivered one of the two bags I needed right away and stored the other at the bellstand. (You're never sure, are you, when you make one of those requests if they'll follow-up? These folks sure did.)

“Great boutique hotel” I was in Houston for a conference and knew I wanted to stay at one of the smaller boutique hotels over the large chain ones that were reserved for the conference. I was happy I ended up at the Alden. The rooms were well designed and very modern. I loved the bathroom and the welcome goodie bag upon arrival was a nice, unexpected surprise (not sure if that was for the conference only but I know my colleagues at other hotels didn't get one). Another great perk: free wi-fi. The only complaint I have is that the lighting in the room was quite dark. I wasn't in my room much since I was out at evening events for the conference but the room could have used more lighting. The lighting in the bathroom was fine. I also ate at the restaurant and I found it quite good. Overall if you are looking for a little something different downtown and like modern hotels, this is the one for you.

“All needs met!” The Quality Inn Cattle Baron in Ft. Worth is a good hotel for the money. Room (king with sofa bed) was perfect for four. Nothing fancy, but clean and orderly. Full breakfast was good, with something for everyone. Sausage, eggs, hash browns, cereal, waffles, cereal etc. Even cinnamon buns that were made on site. Nice dining area with a Texas theme. Never had time to use the pool, but it looked clean. WiFi worked pretty good, a bit slow and got logged off a couple of times. The night manager (Malika?) was very polite and helpful. Only complaints would be that there were pictures (to be hung on the wall) tucked away under the curtain, the light to the bathroom is on the outside of the bathroom door, and it would have been nice to have a shear curtain under the black out curtain for some privacy during the day. But those are minor issues.

“Was okay. The parking is the worst part” Stayes 1 night in a king. We had friends arriving very late at SJC so we opted to stay 1 night as opposed to driving back to the City. Check in great. The hotel is big. Room was big, Comfy bed. Free internet with Presidents Club number (good thing I remembered I had one or they do charge). Nice bathroom but there was some water damage around the base of the outside of the shower stall on both sides that was really obvious. Ate a Gordon Birsch down the street so did not eat in the property. GB was good. The parking is the problem here. you pay a lot for valet and then they park your car somehere off site and it takes a long time to get it. There is alot of congestion so even when you get your car that does not mean you can leave the valet area right away. Make sure you call down more than they say to get your car back or you will wait.

“Huge, made for meetings, but not me” I can't say it was bad, just not what I expect from a Hyatt. It has every possible amenity, but the place is laid out in a weird fashion with multiple floors to accomidate multiple conventions at one time. Finding the workout room was a challenge. The bed was again, not bad, but not great either. And the walls a bit too thin in that I got TMI from the room next door (I could even hear the news stories on their TV).

“A great location” Positives: This is a nice Marriott located in a great area of the city, a great location to start your tours from. Close to the cable car and close to the F Municipal railway. Hotel is very clean and you expect that from a Marriott. Staff were friendly. Good and big rooms. The concierge was taking good care of all visitors and explaining to them patiently about SF. Was very friendly. Newspapers and wireless internet are free in the lobby. By the way, I know this is unusual but my wife liked the shampoo in this hotel. Negatives: This hotel must come into this century by way of internet. They have wired internet in rooms and no self respecting PC has a wired connection these days. I can not remember when I last used it!!!

“Not bad for DC” This is across the street from the Metro which makes it convenient. The rooms are small but this is DC. There is not a lot of work space so it isn't a great business choice but it's comfortable otherwise. It was quiet which is the key issue for me. There is a decent restaurant attached. The staff were helpful the morning breakfast is not a comp - but it's decent.

“Great Hotel - Great Value” This is a very new Courtyard Marriott located just south of Pioneer Square so you are about 6-8 blocks away from the central downtown core (but half a block from Pioneer Square transit station). Pros: modern well equipped rooms, free wifi, great service, decent breakfast in hotel restaurant, great value compared to nearby hotels. Rooms on front of the hotel on high floors have a fabulous unobstructed view of the Seattle harbor. Has an indoor pool in the basement but it is very small. Parking is valet only at $26 but there are much cheaper lots close by. Rooms on front of hotel on low floors may be noisy. Overall a very nice hotel and a great value ... will definitely return.

“One of the nicer DC hotels” I have stayed in a number of DC hotels, and this one probably had about the most helpful staff (to the point of my being a bit uncomfortable, but I am a do it yourself person), and one of the more classy and larger rooms. (I should also note, it is one of the more expensive hotels I have stayed in when in DC as well.) The room was very comfortable, quiet and pleasant, though did lack the coffee maker as noted by another. This is a small inconvenience, though, they provide coffee downstairs: problem is, I drink tea, which is not provided. The bathroom was large as well, and the towels great. The area has a number of reasonable restaurants, but is not flush with them. I did not go to the restaurant on site.

“Close to the Action” Stayed at the Comfort Inn/Zoo/SeaWorld August 18-21st. Hotel is close to the action, right at the intersections of I8 and I10. Rooms were clean, but beds were HARD. Bathrooms a little small, with a really noisy fan. Breakfast was served every morning on the 4th floor, quite the hub bub, lots of kids but there was plenty of food, cereal, milk, pastries. Also had a cappucino machine, nice touch. Hotel is in need of a make over but for the price and location good value.

“Good Central Hotel” Stayed at this hotel for a series of nights after arriving in the USA. It has a great location if you want to be in the centre of the action as you can walk straight out on to Broadway and are on top of Times Square. the downside is in one of the most expensive locations in the city for food, drink and anything else. We tended to eat out, just because of the variety of places available, but have no criticism of the hotel restaurant and bar except we found their modern style decor to be slightly uninviting. The actual room we stayed in was good, with comfortable beds, and on the large size for a central New York location. Absolutely no issues with the staff in generally polite and helpful.

“Character hotel” Great location with character. Very small rooms but that is to be expected in NY. We didn't care. We chose this hotel because of it's character. Concierge was very helpful. Hotel was very busy as it was the weekend of New York marathon! We did not know this until we arrived! Excellent hotel choice.

“It's the location, Not the inside unfortunately.” Ok, I have stayed at a lot of DC hotels and was a former resident for 15 years and just for information I am staying here for 9 days on business. When you stay here you are really staying for the location. For business or tourist - it can not be beat. Near Chinatown and the Verizon Center, close to the mall for tourist activities, plenty of eateries and culture. You are dead center for midtown DC. Aside from that, the Courtyard is in a great looking old bank building - but the looks are mostly from the outside. The inside, well its furnished traditional, and not modern or hip or even updated. The room are very basic. You get tube TV, so-so mattresses and dated decor. The bathroom while clean, was more holiday inn, then Marriott. I stayed here for the advertised free internet, but I can tell you it was very very slow, and good for only basic surfing .. not live video chatting or quick surfing. Too bad. The eatery was ok, but just go out even for breakfast for better fare. You are attached to the Gorden Biersch Brewery which has great happy hour and very convienient for getting a late night bite as well. The staff is friendly, but you never get a greeting coming in and out once you check in. I was tempted to switch hotels for a better bed and better TV and internet, but was too lazy. You won't be disappointed, just dont expect much more.

“Clean but Tired Hotel, Few Ammenities” I stayed at this hotel for a conference. The conference was great -- good sessions, good networking. The hotel, however, was another story. The check in was incredibly poor. The hotel was full the night prior to our conference's checkin, and they had not staffed for a nearly full turnover of rooms. I could not check in to my room until after 8pm. When I checked in they just handed me my key -- no verification of my method of payment, no ensuring my frequent traveler code was in the system, no welcome. I realize they were tired, but that's just poor service. The room was clean (thank goodness -- others at the conference had the previously-mentioned mildew rooms), recently given a quick makover, but was tired. The bathtub was old and the handle to make the tub a shower didn't work well, causing you to pull hard on it. I pulled the faucet so hard I thought I was going to break it.
