The window had been painted blue and was now a neutral beige, but you could see the blue in sections -- poorly painted. The carpet was very old and in need of replacement. There were no minibars in the room, only a nonfunctioning Pepsi machine on the floor. The hotel had no gift/sundry shop, either, just a nonfunctioning vending machine for snacks, drinks, or toothpaste. The woman running the rental car location onsite told me the vending machines never work. I had to go to the bar to buy a bottled water or a soda. While in theory there was high speed wireless internet (for a fee) few at the conference could get it to work. My computer recognized the signal but the login website would not come up. The hotel staff was unable to help troubleshoot the problem. Parking was $10 a day. The conference room was freezing cold and had a very loud blower. It needs an upgrade. The conference food was barely average -- think rubber chicken. One day of the conference they brought out the afternoon's break food (brownies/cookies) at the morning break and the morning's food (yogurt, granola bars) in the afternoon. These details show a lack of attention by the management. There's a pool, but no one was using it. I did not use the workout facilities as I preferred to walk outside. The location is on the river but on the side that is still undergoing revival. The Chart House restaurant next door is very good if you want a nice fish dinner, however. I would not stay here again. The Extended Stay Hotel next door looks much better.

“Great inner harbor location” I was in Baltimore for business and I chose this hotel because my client had a corporate rate there (still pricey, though!). My room had a harbor view which was fantastic. The room itself was spacious and well appointed but just starting to show just a bit of wear. The wireless-only internet offered decent speed and the TV offered a wide variety of channels of which many were in hi-def. The staff was very good, especially the doormen who had to summon my cab every morning. There was a sign at the elevators promising improvements but I did not find them that bad. I ate a couple of meals in the restaurant, which were OK. There are dining options galore, however, ranging from fast food at the directly-attached mall to the many restaurants across the street in the Inner Harbor complex. If you have access to the Concierge Lounge, you will get a basic breakfast but the evening spread is enough to construct a full meal (per-diem business travelers take note).

“A well-priced price in a prime location!” Just came back from a week in NYC. I usually tried to stay away from "touristy" spots like Time Square whenever I visit NYC but the reasonable price and good reviews of this hotel got me curious so I decided to give it a try. All I can say is, what a gem in the middle of Time Square! This hotel is located on W. 44th St. between 8th & 9th St. (close to 9th) and needless to say this is a fantastic location. Tons of eateries on 9th Avenue (as part of the Hells Kitchen area) and numerous shops/stores on 8th Avenue as well. The subway entrance/exit is about half a block away and if you are traveling from JFK Airport, the E train is right there. Speaking of super convenience! Hotel has obviously been refurbished recently so everything looks relatively new. The room is not super huge but of a very decent size with modern decor. Compare to many other hotels I stayed in NYC before, you have a queen size bed, a comfortable couch, a working desk with free internet, a refrigerator and a coffeemaker in room and a fully functional bathroom with a full size tub, plus free breakfast at this hotel. As a AAA member, I got a super deal of $99 w/tax per night! Now where would you go find a quality hotel in the midst of Time Square for less than $100 a night? Sure this is not your fancy and luxurious hotel, but you also don't spend too much time sleeping or hanging at your hotel in NYC, so why would you pay $150, $200 or even more for hotels? I do agree with a couple reviews here that walls are THIN and the elevator can be slow, which may be irritating to some people. Actually I have stayed at other much more expensive NYC hotels before and found many of them having the same problems. Bear in mind many NYC buildings are old so these problems are quite common, especially if your hotels are converted from old buildings. This one is no exception. But if price is what you care most about and you do get a nice comfortable room with a great price at a good spot in town, then these issues really become secondary. Overall, I highly recommend this hotel and will not hesitate to book it again next time when I return to NYC.

“Super !” Lorsqu'on trouve l'hôtel (pas d'enseigne), c'est le bonheur. L'hôtel est très bien situé. Le personnel est charmant et attentionné. La chambre et la salle de douche sont très design et jolies. Un tout petit effort pour le petit déjeuner-buffet (inclus dans le prix) donnerait une note de 10/10. A savoir, tous les extras (eau dans la chambre) sont chers de même que le parking.

“Gutes Hotel in Finanzbezirk von San Francisco” Das Le Meridien befindet sich im Finanzbezirk von San Francisco, dennoch sind die meisten touristischen Sehenswürdigkeiten auch von dort schnell zu Fuss erreichbar. Abends muss man aber ein wenig laufen, um entsprechende Bars oder Restaurants zu finden. China Town liegt in unmittelbarer Nähe des Hotels. Die Zimmer sind ausreichend groß und auch die Ausstattung ist sehr modern. Der Service im Hotel ist sehr gut. Vor allem der Concierge konnte uns viele Tipps zu Sehenswürdigkeiten und Busverbindungen geben. Dies war für uns vor allem deshalb sehr hilfreich, da wir uns vorher nur sehr bedingt über die Stadt informieren konnten.

“Musty smell; friendly but tired and broke down” The staff are friendly and helpful. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. The free breakfast was OK. The indoor pool and hot tub are nice. A LOT of details need attention at this hotel from the loose light switches to the frayed carpet on the stairway to the evidence on the ceiling of obvious roof leaks. The worst thing: a very musty smell throughout the corridors and the room (perhaps related to the leaky roof?) which was made much worse by turning on the air conditioning system - it's like they've never cleaned or changed the filter. I read the other reviews and agree with most of the negative reports here. The only reason we stayed in this hotel was because rooms were so hard to find that week end (The Final Four was happening). You can do worse than this place but you can do a whole lot better. Shop around for better.

“Excellent Times Square location makes up for noisy surroundings” Slightly dated hotel, was rife with noisy tourists and had questionable amenities but the location was outstanding - right near Times Square. Was disappointed in lack of serviceable Internet (wireless unavailable and wired connection was spotty at best) and no room service.

“Location, Location, Location!” If you're looking to be in the heart of the action, this is your home away from home! We spent one week in a third floor, one-bedroom apartment with a living room, full bathroom and full kitchen. Our room had a balcony with a view of the bay. We did not use the kitchen but it was nice to know it was there just in case. We had daily maid service too. You can very easily catch buses and cable cars right outside of the hotel. The staff couldn't have been nicer--all of the staff from the Manager to the maid. We also had a view of Ghiradelli Square from our balcony. If you're looking to stay in the Fisherman's Wharf area, this is your place!

“Love Kimpton properties, but Topaz left us a little disappointed” We love the Kimpton brand because of the uniqueness of the properties and the customer service aspects, so I automatically set out to choose one of the Kimpton properties for our DC mini-vacation. I chose the Topaz, based largely on reviews at Trip Advisor. We arrived a few minutes prior to official check-in. Never have I had a problem at a Kimpton property with early arrivals. This time, we were barely greeted and then the check-in staff member told us that the room was not ready and then looked at us waiting for us to decide what to do...she half-heartedly offered to store our bags, and I had to ask if she knew how long it would be, etc. We never got any orientation on wine hour time, coffee availability, etc. While we waited I watched what appeared to be very overworked staff run in and out of the hotel. This trend continued throughout the stay. Anyway, on to the room. The room was nice and very much in the Kimpton style with fun and crazy color combinations. We had a room overlooking N Street with King bed, sofa and desk over in the corner. The bathroom was small, but the dressing area (table and stool and mirror) outside of the bathroom made up for that fact. The walk path between the end of the bed and the cabinet that contained the honor bar and tv is VERY narrow. Use caution if you get up in the night and have to walk through this space. (I am petite and found this narrow.) As usual, we could not hear fellow guests in their rooms (another major reason that I love Kimpton hotels) but we did encounter more hall noise/doors slamming than ever before. The overall experience was not on-par with what we have encountered in other Kimpton locations. Also, the price seemed high in comparison of what we have spent and experienced in the past. We stayed at another property after our 3 nights here, and it was a worlds-different experience. Then again, maybe we are not supposed to judge a Monaco against a non-Monaco..? That being said, Topaz still out-ranks any chain-type hotel in its class simply because of the uniqueness and the small benefits of being an In-Touch member, like free items from the mini bar, room requests, custom-request of newspapers, etc. The bright spots were the housekeeping staff. They were very friendly and overly apologetic if things were in the hallway, etc. Well, except for our final morning, when housekeeping knocked to see HOW LONG it would be until we checked out! I've never had that happen before. In the future I will look into staying at some of the other DC area Kimptons-if only to see the difference in the style and decor.

“Great stay” You can't beat this location, subway station outside the hotel, rooms are clean and staff is friendly. It's usually very expensive so I'm not sure it's worth the $400+/night that they usually charge but I got an amazing rate on Priceline so I was happy!

“HUGE hotel with tiny rooms. Clean and convenient” I chose this hotel because of the location. It is an enormous hotel with a lobby that is always full of people (maybe free wifi?) The rooms are clean and beds comfortable, but the space is really tiny. Overall a good experience, but I wouldn't stay here again as it was not big enough for me and my children. Also - there were 4 of us in the room, but we were only given 3 towels and 1 small shampoo bottle every day. Had to call the maid service to request more every day. Pool is heated and kids enjoyed that.

“Another great stay at Fairmont - President's Club is Worth it” I often stay at this hotel in DC and this trip was another great experience. Particularly because I stay at this hotel often, having President's Club (something very easy to get for a minimal fee) is a great deal. You get free internet, access to a really amazing fully kitted out gym, and even the delivery of clean gym clothes and shoes. As ever, the staff was incredibly helpful -- whether it was the folks at the front desk, the concierge, the garage attendant, etc. They also gave me a complimentary fridge to store things in and got it to me within 30 minutes of my arrival. I also got an upgraded room so I had a lovely little seating area. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the amenities in the bathroom were lovely. I have had very few bad experiences with this hotel and continue to be incredibly satisfied. The only time the hotel screwed up was in 2008 when I arrived late and they didn't have a room. But the way they dealt with it - a fabulous room in the hotel next door and a $100 gift voucher that I used to buy wine for some friends - was incredibly professional and satisfactory. I encourage you to stay here.

“Contemporary” It is nothing like a hotel. It is very compact, difficult to locate but it is situated in good business center. There is no view, it is merely buildings everywhere and they are so nextby that lifting your curtain up is unpleasant. I don't like it much but for business travelers, it might be ideal. The room itself is rather small and I am a big fan of ice and there is no ice making machine anywhere in this hotel! To get one...need to call and they bring it to your room and of course you got to tip!

“Average Hotel in great location” I chose this hotel based on the many positive reviews in TripAdvisor and am conflicted about how to rate this hotel My prejudice is to stay at 4-5 star hotels when possible. These were so expensive in SF that we tried the Kensington Park. So here are the pros and cons. Pros: Less expensive, very friendly staff, superb location near Union Square, decent rooms, relatively inexpensive valet parking, great coffee and juice bar in morning, cool benches in the elevators Cons: Lobby, hallways, and rooms a bit run down, street side rooms very noisy – especially at night (beware if you are a light sleeper), VERY small closet, inadequate air conditioning, door locks VERY noisy when closing – so whenever any nearly door closes there is a very loud clanking sound (beware if you are a light sleeper - our neighbor came "home" at 2 AM both nights, going in and out twice), Inattentive valets – they were not there most of the time, average wait of 15-20 minutes for your car to be brought by valet. So you decide. Not plush but adequate and noisy.

“Great pool for kids! Nice lake views.” The Lakeway Resort is a large hotel with standard rooms. It is next to the lake with great views, but there is no lake access from the hotel. The pool is fabulous for kids. It has a large slide and a big shallow area as well as a deep pool. There is a separate pool area for adults with hot tubs. The kids cannot go into the hot tubs. The gym is very nice with new equipment and no extra service charge. The hotel is isolated so we ate two meals there. Although the service in the hotel was fine, the service at the restaurant was horrible. We waited over an hour (with hungry kids –painful) to finally receive the worst pizza that I have ever eaten. The breakfast buffet had great food, but I had to clean off a table myself so that we could sit and eat.

“セントラルパークに徒歩でいけます” セントラルパークにも歩いていけますが、MOMAやタイムズスクエアも15分ぐらいで歩いていけます。10時ごろいきましたが、早くチェックインできず、ホテルで荷物を3.75ドルで預かってもらいました。地下鉄の駅のすぐ横にあり、物凄く便利でした。チェックアウト後にラガーディア空港に行くのにホテルに隣接している地下鉄駅から、バスを乗り継いでスムーズにさらに、格安でいけたので驚いたぐらいでした。

“Wonderful Old World Hotel--BY FAR THE BEST IN DC” Stayed here over the Fourth of July with my family. This hotel is like the luxury hotels that I remember when I was very young. Everything is extremely professional. The staff all know the guest names--nothing is overlooked. I travel a lot on business and pleasure and its a rarity to encounter service of this quality in the United States. Other than the Ritz Carlton in San Francisco (my favorite city hotel in the US), nothing else comes to mind. Another attribute that struck me was how good the food was. I know the Obamas love good food and chose this as their hotel while awaiting their White House move. This is some of the best hotel food I have had (again the Ritz Carlton San Francisco comes to mind). All ingredients are fresh and local and expertly prepared by the chef. We stayed for the Fourth of July and the hotel hosted an enormous party with entertainment for children--again really excellent food and so much of it. The location also simply coudn't be better for a visit to DC. Its right across the street from the White House--need one say more? The property is beautiful and historic. The hotel is the product of merging two old DC homes (MR. Hayes house was merged with Mr. Adam's house). It is maintained perfectly and is kept meticulously clean. However, keep in mind that it is old, so the rooms while beautiful are NOT sound proof. Little sounds do travel here (as they do in old historic houses). If you are a very sensitive sleeper, this hotel may not be the best choice. However, by opting to go elsewhere, you will miss a wonderful, historic, oldworld experience. I have traveled to DC a lot in the past few years and stayed at a lot of its hotels (3 of the Ritz Carltons, the Fairmont, The Mandarin Oriental, The Mayfair, The Willard, etc). This is by my favorite hotel in DC. It carries my highest recomendation.

“Great place to stay” I was in town for a wedding and this was the recommended hotel. It was very nice and I have no complaints except it was a bit pricey. It is across the street from the Market. Beware that this hotel has inside rooms with no windows. Those are the cheapest rooms, which is what we reserved but a week or so before our arrival we were offered for an upgrade for $15. If you get that offer, take it.

“Highly recommended! Great location and comfortable accommodations.” The Residence Inn is located in close proximity (easy walking distance) to the Baltimore Convention Center, Camden Yards, Inner Harbor, and much more. The rooms are a nice size, very clean, and comfortably furnished. Ours included a sofa, bed, and desk along with some hassocks that could be used as seats as well. We had our cat with us, and the staff was wonderful about welcoming her and providing us a sign for the door so that the room was not entered without us being there. Breakfast was good, although the breakfast room got very crowded, and when we were leaving breakfast, there was a line to get in! The breakfast room was well attended by the staff, and they kept the guests moving, and kept the space as clean as possible. The front desk staff was friendly and helpful. Overall a great stay, and I would definitely return.

“Great Location and Pet Friendly” Great location, only a few blocks from Union Square and located at the gates to China Town. Close to everything. Great staff. Pet Friendly. Wine tasting from 5-6 each day. Rooms are small, but efficient and comfortable. No restaurant or bar attached to hotel but one on either side. The Irish Bank is around the corner, great food and atmosphere. One of our favorite Irish bars in the US.

“Cute hotel, would stay again” Stayed here for a Sat night with a friend and was pleasantly surprised. Room with two double beds was slightly small but not by SF standards. Was completely fine for two adults, especially if you're planning to spend all day out. Was well priced for the location (right off of Union Square) and having a private bathroom. Came with robes and slippers!

“Mid 30s and I loved it” I was hesitant to try this hotel after reading some of the reviews, but I really enjoyed the hotel. The staff were all very friendly to me and did not ostracize me for being ancient. I did find some of the uniforms the women were wearing to be a bit on the hooker side, but if you can over look the hooker boots the rooms are GREAT! The bed was very comfortable, the shower was perfect, the towels were plush, and the TV was nice... I really enjoyed the hotel. The cafe, Mary Janes, serves some great food for something quick and easy. I was at the hotel on business and the desk workspace was minimal, but it was functional. The gym was nice, had everything one would need while working out at a hotel for a few days. I would stay here more often, but the hotel does not have a loyalty program. I also thought I might hear the train as I was staying in a room that faced the train, I heard nothing. I loved the hotel!

“Awesome Location!” Our room was on the first floor and had a large patio. Although the patio was directly next to a parking lot, seeing the beach & ocean 24 hours a day was so wonderful. If it wasn't for the fact that I wanted to try some different restaurants, we would not have had to drive because you could walk to alot of restaurants and shops. I did think the room was small and the bathroom even smaller. The bathroom only had a shower and did not have a tub to my surprise. Refrigerator and microwave were in the room. Bed were older and were not few comfortable. They could use new linens because the ones in our room were rather thin. The hotel has an underground parking garage with locked gates. To me the $17/day parking was worth this security. Overall, I liked this hotel for the location because there are few hotels directly on the beach in San Diego. I would probably go back for a weekend again.

“Decent but nothing special” Just came back from 5 days at the Serrano Hotel. I chose it for its proximity to the Hilton, as I was attending a conference at the Hilton but prefer to stay at small boutique hotels. I thought the hotel was ok. Service was generally friendly but unexceptional. We arrived in the early afternoon and the first room they gave us was tiny and faced a brick wall. They gave us a much better room (1106) later in the afternoon. The room was small but manageable by SF standards. The bathroom was very small and awkward, easy to bang your elbows on irregular walls. Decor a bit cheesy and uninspiring, although admittedly we prefer modern design. Morning coffee and evening wine reception were good. We got a parking package which was good value. Last time I attended the same conference I stayed at the Adagio which was much nicer. for similar rates Next time I would return to the Adagio, or spend a bit more for the Nikko or Clift. This hotel was fine but just nothing special

“Nice hotel - Although not very accomadating” I recently stayed, and an overall great stay, however , I had a request of the front desk, an to a person, they were unwilling to accommodate, none of them stopped to realize that my request would have been very profitable. As I was willing to pay for a few extra hours, that in the end, I never needed. This is not the first time I had an issue like this, last time it was a room change, which could not be done. This is a first class property, a bit tired in spots, but the front desk staff, needs to try a bit harded to make the guest happy, saying sorry isn't the right solution.

“Good location, good rate, efficient and friendly staff” This hotel is a historic landmark in the Windy City that was originally called the Hotel St. Clair back in the 1920s and was the happening place to be. Famous folk like Dean Martin, Roy Rogers, Judy Garden and Bob Hope all stayed there when visiting Second City. Be sure to check out the 22nd floor Skyline Terrace with views of Chi-town's famous Magnificent Mile. Really good downtown location. The exterior is unassuming. Lobby is bright with natural lighting, free wifi and lots of seating. Rooms are decorated with simple, classic furnishings. Beds are plush. Air conditioning works adequately. Prices are really good. I got a rate around $100 bucks! No breakfast and no coffee at hotel, but a small coffee shop is right next door. Stay again? Absolutely.

“Only 15 floors but nice early check in.” Oh, Philly. Do any of your four star hotels fill any tall buildings? I guess we just can't have it all. On previous trip, we enjoyed the Bellevue Hyatt, which starts at the 10th floor and goes up. On this trip, we stayed on the Westin's tenth but since we foolishly confused the Westin with the very tall building behind it, I guess we were hoping for a lot more height and a lot more view. But let's not fault the Westin for our misunderstanding. And they can't be blamed for this - - why are so many office buildings built with dark or one-way windows? What are they hiding? The other thing with these 2 hotels is the lack of a ground floor spacious lobby. In this case, it wasn't the minor inconvenience of taking an elevator up one floor to get to the lobby but the fact that when you're in the lobby you are starved for natural light. But this may appeal to some. Anyway, no real complaints. Best feature is the single button you push for everything you need and how sweet that woman was every time I called her. OK, I lied. There was one thing even better. My wife likes her filet mignon cooked perfectly her way. So it was with great trepidation that I waited in the room wondering how many times I would have to ask the poor chef to try again. Guess what? They nailed it on the first try. Tips: Getting up a little early will be rewarded by free Starbucks and WSJ. In fact, if all you want is fruit, your breakfast is covered. Details matter in a 4-star. The shower. Everything it could be and should be. Control temperature and flow precisely with solid plumbing fixtures. It gets better. Two heads are better than one but it is easy to turn one off if you favor saving the planet over self indulgence. I won't say which choice I made. I always strive for balance so I have to provide one shortcoming. One morning I wanted any employee (even if the Concierge wasn't on duty until after lunch) to school me on local attractions. It took a while but we finally got most of the info I sought. It was just a bit surprising because the day before we continually were greeted by either the manager or someone who carried himself like the manager. Really not a big deal. Great service, clean, comfortable, yes, they earn that fourth star.

“small rooms” I spend four nights at the Wardham Park Marriott. The rooms were nice but extremely small. You can not walk passed the foot of the bed if the chair is out from under the desk. The bathroom counter was about 18 inches wide, so small that the faucet had to be placed at an angle and not behind the sink. walls are paper thin, can hear everything in room next door, including the bathroom i probably would not stay here again.

“Top Shelf Hotel” Great architecture dating back to 1907, the bed room furniture and materails are high end as you would expect, and the lobby / restaurant / bar areas are beautiful. You need to visit the typically grand Fairmont hotel.

“Upscale hotel with a good location!” I used priceline for a hotel in the Beverly hills/west hollywood area and ended up staying here for a little more than half off the prevailing rate. The hotel is in a good location, not too far from anything. Parking was 36 dollars a night but we were prepared for it. It is also valet only but they were fast in retrieving the car. All the employees we encountered were very helpful and polite. The room was of good size and had two double beds and a small balcony. The bathroom was nice with a seperate tub and shower. Had no complains about the room. The gym is nice and the pool/spa area was a good place to relax. They also have seperate mens and womens locker rooms with a sauna and steam room. I would recommend this hotel since it has a good location and the service was great!

“Better Places are close by” This hotel had been renovated so it has a very nice decor. The beds are good and the rooms are fairly large. However, the service is terrible. The location where ice machines should be are vacant. Their business center consists of one lonely empty desk. They don't have wait staff in the bar area at all times. The continental breakfast is terrible. Just 2 blocks away are a Courtyard by Marriott and a Homewood Suites. Stay there instead.

“Perfect for an overnighter” We stayed one night at the Westin as we had to pick up one of our friends from an early flight into LAX. The area is fine, right by the airport so it was really handy for us. We got a special deal from a website so the rates were quite good for what we got. A king room (which was booked) was unavailable as we were quite late checking in, but they upgraded us to a room on the executive level with two doubles and a voucher for our parking (normally $20) It did take quite a while to check in, I imagine that it's always quite busy being so close to the airport, but check-in itself was pretty quick. The room was clean, comfortable and bathroom was fine. Ours had a pretty decent shower which I would have been happy with if I'd just stepped off a long-haul flight. We had a view of the runway and yes, the sound of planes taking off was a bit noisy, no complaints though, we were right by the airport so you can't really expect silence. That said, it doesn't go on all night. Probably stopped about 12 or 1am and started up again around 6am. Breakfast on the exec. level was complimentary but they do have room service (pretty pricey!) and a restaurant downstairs. Plus there are a few fast food places right nearby.

“Nice business hotel” I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. Spaceous rooms. Convenient location connected to the Galleria. Clean place. The only negative is the dated fitness room. Cheerful staff. Comfortable beds. Could have used a mini bar perhaps. Liked the free water.

“Very Good Stay” Was a little nervous after reading previous reviews, but found the hotel very comfortable. The room was spacious by downtown Chicago standards and had the feel of a recent update. Nice flatscreen TV, air worked well, and minimal noise from the streets below. Very comfortable bed. All in all a very good stay.

“Very Comfortable Stay” Front office was kind as can be upon check-in. Everyone I encountered, which were several different front office associates had a smile and were very courteous. I could tell all of their personalities were genuine and that's something I don't see too frequently when I travel. The blonde girls were really sweet, the girl with the red hair, and an older lady who was working the night shift. A majority of the time when I encounter hotel staff, I am positive that the kindness is all an act. Those people were all a breath of fresh air. Housekeeping was sweet as can be. They work the hardest out of everyone in this industry. Rooms were clean. I gave the location a 5 because my friends and I were traveling two consecutive nights back and forth to a festival 45 minutes east of Austin called Nocturnal Wonderland. It was the closest hotel under my Hilton employee discount. We usually stay downtown when visiting Austin. My one and only complaint is that the hallways don't feel air conditioned at all. Maybe it's broken, I don't know, but I broke a sweat walking to my room.

“Wonderful hotel” We booked this hotel on Priceline for $100/night. When we arrived, we noticed the beautiful grounds and Christmas decorations all around. The check in was quick and the empolyees very friendly. Our room was decent size, with a balcony overlooking the gym area. The bed was very comfortable, probably the best hotel bed we've ever had. A few posters mentioned the thin walls...yes, you can hear the people next to you, but that didn't bother us. We spent very little time in the hotel since we didn't come here to sit in the hotel but to enjoy beautiful San Diego. We were here only to sleep then left for the entire day. The pool area is undergoing construction, but we wouldn't have used the pool anyway in this weather. The area around the hotel is beautiful, with awesome jogging trails nearby. Bring your running shoes. They serve Starbucks coffee in the lobby, but not just coffee as you would normally see. They have almost all the drinks that a regular Starbucks would have. Our only complaint is that they charge for internet and parking. We had our own internet connection, so didn't need to use theirs, but they should offer free wireless. The gym also charges $12/day, but if you sign up for H Honors on their site, you'll get the gym access for free and it costs nothing to sign up. Overall, this is an awesome hotel with friendly staff and a great location. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here.

“A hidden gem” Boutique hotels nowadays try to be edgy and modern but this hotel is a classic hidden gem. I've been staying in so many contemporary style hotels lately I forgot how lovely it can be to stay somewhere with old world charm. Every touch speaks quality, Bulgari amenities, soft fluffy towels embroidered with "L", Wedgewood cutlery... The only flaw I could find in this hotel was the tv in the bathroom. It is mounted above the tub but if you're inside the tub you can't see anything because it doesn't tilt down. Otherwise everything was fabulous.

“Great stay and clean” This hotel has great staff and was very clean. A nice breakfast, even for those on a diet because they have fruit and yogurt. Great location! There is a lot of shopping and dining nearby, and dowtown is only 10 minutes away. Easy access to the highway. I would definitely stay here again.
“Showing it's age” Although room was large and clean, this is a tired hotel in need of some attention and is a good 15 to 20 minute walk away from the city centre.

“Good value, Wicked location!” Stayed for 3 nights with my Dad and brother whilst we were in New York seeing boxing at madison square gardens! The hotel has a wicked location on 3rd avenue. Quite easy to find for taxi drivers too ( especially since most taxi drivers couldn't even locate central park - i kid you not!!!) The entrance is small but functional and of course the service is as good as you expect in New York. The rooms are pretty big by New york standards (although that is small compared to the rest of the USA) If you've stayed in your average premier lodge in the Uk...that kinda sixe. The rooms were clean althougha little dated. Two big double beds and a sofa bed. We requested extra bedding for the sofa which arrived promptly and at no extra charge. Crap view but then I reckon thats always the case unless you're lucky enough to stay at the top of the empire state building! Room was kept cool, not too cold. Large and clean bathroom. brekfast was quite expensive (although search for deals as we had it included on 2/3 of our nights!) Lovely breakfast though. the usual american choices...waffles, fruit, cooked bits, cereals, toast etc etc and good service. the hotel staff were all friendly and did their job well. Even when we arrived back after the boxing (calzaghe win if you're interested) and quite merry, they were helpful! Can store luggage once you've checked out. Always able to hail a bab and the concierge was helpful without wanting to rip us off. All in all a good place to saty. Good value, good size rooms but the localtion wins it!

“Hotel Modesto ma Buon rapporto qualità/prezzo” Il Channel Inn Hotel è un albergo di media categoria situato in centro città a pochi passi dalle principali attrazioni turistiche di Washington e direttamente sul Waterfront. L'abergo è datato e dispone di camere molto spaziose anche se un pò vecchiotte. Tuttavia, il prezzo è molto economico rispetto ai costosissimi hotel della zona centrale e oltretutto dispone di parcheggio coperto gratuito. Nell'hotel è presente un ristorante e nelle vicinanze c'è un ottimo mercato del pesce dove è possibile cenare a prezzi molto buoni. L'hotel dispone di connessione internet wireless e la colazione non è inclusa nel prezzo. Consiglio questo hotel per una breve sosta nella capitale, e per chi è in cerca di una sistemazione centrale ad un costo decisamente abordabile.

“Good choice for $50 on Priceline” The hotel hasn't been updated in 15+ years but it was certainly worth the $50 I paid on Priceline. Good service, a flat screen TV, reasonably priced ROOM SERVICE breakfast (after tax, tip, I had coffee, OJ, and an assortment of pastries for $11... they charged 20% gratuity but no "service fee" like some other hotels), free parking, good business center, etc. When I had indigestion in the middle of the night and needed TUMS, they had them. One thing I didn't like: I stayed for five days and the weather got significantly colder on days 4-5. So I needed to use the heat rather than the AC. Well, the heat was not very precise - it was either off or on and blew out very dry air. For this reason, I would not want to stay here between Oct-Mar. However, for other times of the year, it's a very solid choice.

“Business Travel? Great Location” A very clean and quiet location. The hotel is new and the staff is friendly. Rooms are large, comfortable, have a mini fridge and microwave, and it's a non-smoking hotel. They have a great breakfast (free) and it's located between AMD and the airport. Book your room on their website.

“素晴らしい立地の新しいホテル” 6泊しました。部屋からはロックフェラーセンターと教会が見え素敵な眺めでした。51thストリートに面しているものの静かでアクセスもよく快適! 部屋には必要なものは揃っていて、コーヒーメーカー、冷蔵庫、電子レンジもあり収納も十分で、机も広く快適。無線Wifiも無料でした。また、すべてが大変新しく気持ちよかったです。バスルームは私の泊まった一番安い部屋のタイプにはバスタブがなく、シャワーのみで水圧はあまり強くなかったですが、日本のシャワーのように手で持って使える(固定式ではない)のがよかったです。洗面台も広く使いやすかったです。 各フロアの廊下には空のペットボトルとウォーターサーバーがあり無料でした。ロビーやフロントは極端に狭いものの、2Fには宿泊者のみの広めのラウンジがあり、無料で使えるPCやコーヒーがおいてありました。また、宿泊キーがないとエレベーターが動かないので中心地でありながら安心して過ごせました。 この価格帯でこの立地、清潔さと広さはマンハッタンで何回も泊まっていますが、すばらしいと思います!スタッフもフレンドリーで、次も必ず泊まりたいです。

“Nice place, Nice People, Wonderful Bed” This Hampton Inn is very nice, and a little over year old. The old Hampton Inn is across the parking lot now like a Days Inn or something like that. After 24 hours of flying, I need a place to crash, arriving just past Midnight at SAT, I call the Hotel and the FREE shuttle was there in like 5 min. The driver was very nice and helpful, checked in and went up to my room. The King bed was so nice.. It was a very good night sleep. The room was a good size, and clean. The Breakfast in the AM is what you get at any Hampton, but the staff was so nice, and chipper. Checked out and asked for a ride to the Rental car place, got a free one on the Shuffle, once again a very nice driver. You get a lot for the $109 a night for a reg room, if I was staying longer I would have gone for the Suite for an extra $10.. A very nice Airport Hampton. Less then 5 min from the airport, with NO air noise. A++

“Not the most polished of Garden Inns, great staff, great location” Not the most polished of Garden Inns. The pictures show a much newer and fresher look compared to the state the hotel is really in. Rooms are small, towels are tired BUT bed is very comfortable and toiletteries are nice, hair dryer is proper. Internet is free (good speed), business center offers free printing. Breakfast was just good enough to get you going. Nothing fancy, typical of garden inns and courtyards (in case of marriott). Location is a big plus. If you are on a biz trip, this hotel will meet your basic needs. If you are looking to enjoy a NYC experience/vacation you might want to consider a hotel with some added spice (e.g., Intercont. at W44th and 8th). TO THE HOTEL STAFF( I know you pay attention to the reviews). You have a wonderful team of staff. All friendly and warm. Suggestions: would be nice to have bottles of water in the room/fridge even if they aren't free. At another level, Invest in new towels.

“Fourth Stay at this hotel and loved it again” This hotel is still going great after 3 years. Staff still remember me by name from my first trip and many have been here the whole time. Service is this hotels strength. There are now nicer looking hotels all around this location but still love staying here for the kindness of the staff. Room are well maintained and show few signs of wear and tear. Infact I saw alot of minor maintenance being carried out all over the hotel. Although not grand this is a great little hotel, has microwaves and fridges in every room. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay away from the chaos of Times Square.

“If this is Sheraton, I need to rethink my loyalty to SPG.” I am not that picky, I stay in 30+ hotels a yr but when the bottle of water they charge $5 for is half full, your remote looks like it joined the previous guest in a pizza fight, the water pressure is akin to a drip, the hotel feels dreary and you paid $200+ to be staying on the SPG floor, you surely never stay there again or recommend anyone else does. The only property in the SPG network above $200 per that has dirtier rooms than this property is the Westin Charlotte.

“Hotel muito bem localizado e ao lado da estação do metrô” Fiquei uma semana hospedado e gostei muito do que foi oferecido. Não deixem de experimentar o welcome cookie, muito bom! Um dos problemas existentes e que pode incomodar quem tem o sono leve são a paredes muito finas, pois não há isolamento acústico, então tudo o que os seus vizinhos de quarto fazem você ouve. Não se assustem quando a porta do quarto do vizinho bater e vc achar que tem alguém entrando no seu quarto! Meu quarto ficou em frente à delegacia e o corpo de bombeiros, mas não tive problema com barulhos, pois estava em um andar alto. Por isso recomendo ficar em andar mais alto possível para evitar o barulho da rua. A internet é cobrada no quarto, porém, se vc ficar no lobby o wifi é de graça. Do lado do hotel tem o METRO CAFÉ, excelente lugar para tomar um bom café da manhã. Tirando esses pequenos inconvenientes o hotel é bom e possui uma excelente localização. Minha estadia foi muito agradável. Fui muito bem atendido pelos recepcionistas.

“Reasonable and Clean” I spent a week here. The rooms are narrow and definitely than those in other "suites" hotels. But everything was clean and service was excellent. Location is good for business travelers, maybe less so for tourists. The free breakfast was a step above typical free breakfasts, with milk and a wafflemaker. Sodas and snacks are available for purchase across from the front desk. Parking was free and plentiful. TV channels were limited. Beds and linens were fresh and comfortable.

“Modern & clean but no athmostphere” Clean & nice furniture, everything brand-new. Very modern. Good location, direct access to Grand Station, tube, shops etc... Probably the #2 largest hotel in NY - so little chance to make connection with staff (automatic check in/out machines is encouraged like in the airport). No real athmostphere. Internet not complimentary and rather expensive - outrageous for the room price

“Fantastic Location...But Very Basic Room” Rating this hotel on the Trip Advisor scale is difficult. Here's why: *The location is fantastic. It is one block from the U.S. House of Representatives. If you have any business with Congress or some of the federal agencies located near Captiol Hill, this location can't be beat. Also, the Capitol Hill Metro (subway) stop is literally across the street. *Safe. The Capitol Hill area is protected by their own police force, The Capitol Hill Police. Sitting one block from Congress, this hotel could very possibly be the safest hotel in the entire city -- especially after 9/11. *Room is basic. Just a basic room -- think "Motel 6." It's clean. There's a bed. There's a shower. But that's about it. You won't call home to tell your spouse how wonderful the hotel room is. *No restaurant on site. This is a big deal to some people...but not to me. I used to live in Washington, so I'm fully aware that there are plenty of (good!) restaurants within three blocks of the hotel. But if you were on your first trip to Washington and/or were afraid to venture out alone after dark, this could be a problem. If you have business with the House of Reps, this is the best place to stay. Every morning, I watched (now Majority Leader) John Boehner walk from his townhouse past the hotel front door to his favorite breakfast spot!

“Surprisingly nice” Traveling on business and had not stayed here before. Free breakfast was awesome and convenient. Room was spacious with sitting area and great work space. Layout was ok - kinda choppy - but it worked.

“Update - Disappointing Room Service” All three of us in our party had problems with our room service dinners. My club sandwich and fries was barely warm, not hot, and the wrong soft drink was sent with the dinner. I was unable to get hot water during an early shower. Otherwise the hotel and room were fine.

“Very upsacle and sophisticated” The remodeling is nearly complete and it was well worth the wait. While to old rooms were stylish, the newly redecorated rooms are very sophisticated and modern. The overall concept is great but there were a few things I didn't particularly care for. The bathroom design is spacious but a tad too open with only frosted glass panels separating the sink area from the toilet & shower area. The shower stall does not have a door on it so the water spashed out onto the bathroom floor. Additionally, I was not crazy about the shower gel for bathing. It didn't lather very well. I would have prefered a bar of soap instead. The only other negative was the room thermostat. I don't know if we just didn't know how to set it or whether the air conditioner just wasn't working well. The thermastat's screen was so small and extremely hard to read (even with my reading glasses on). Other than that, A++ on all other amenities and design. Great bedding, lighting, TV, carpet, window treatments, and furniture. The staff is extremely friendly and accomodating. I will definitely stay there again and highly recommend it for DC visitors

“Not much different than other SF 4 star hotels” I live in the Bay Area so stay in SF a lot. I picked the Omni because of its high ratings. It is very nice but I like lots of other places just as well and they aren't as expensive. I prefer to stay in the Union Square area as the financial district doesn't have a lot of restaurants is too isolated on weekends. Although, you can walk anywhere, you have to walk at least 4 blocks to get to anything. That said, you can walk to Chinatown, North Beach, Union Square and the Embarcadero, each in a different direction. The fruit drinks and fruit in the lobby are a nice touch. The rooms are pretty much standard big box hotel style with nice bedding. The real negative about this hotel was that the closet smelled terrible. I like the boutique hotels better that offer things like free wifi and have a lot of charm. I wouldn't stay here again unless is was the least price place. I paid more because of the reviews and was disappointed.

“Loved Everything” When I travel I often choose the mid-high hotel chains (Marriott Resorts, Hyatt, Hilton, Westin) because you often know what you get and receive consistent service and amenities. This hotel may have given the BEST service I have received in a hotel. From amenities, rooms, staff, bars and restaurants, all delivered an amazing level of service. We stayed here for a 6 day, 5 night visit. We requested an early check in with a high floor facing the Rockies ( yeah, I want it all!) We arrived at 1230pm and spent time with Sophia at the front desk. Sophia is one of those people that you feel you know already and she was fantastic. She worked diligently to find a room that fit our requests but none seemed available. She did have a room on the 33rd floor with a city view which I took because I love to be near the top floor. It needed an hour to be completed so we walked to the 16th street mall (just 1 block away) and had lunch. 30 mins later, the hotel called and we could check in. Sophia was not there, but 15 mins after checking in she called our room to apologize for not being at the desk during our check in and wanted to ensure our room was to our likeing ( GREAT SERVICE). The hotel is new and it shows. Everything sparkles and gleems from the lobby to the rooms. The rooms were standard in size and amenities compared to other similiar properties. As mentioned, everything is new which is an upgrade. About 360 sq ft in the room housing a comfy king bed with tons of pillows, flat screen tv, safe, desk and chair, closets, bathrobes, slippers, a standard size bathroom with upgraded counters, sinks and amenities (one suggestion, thicker more plush towels). We stayed in room 3311 on the 33rd floor and had great views of downtown and the Rockies ( thank you Sophia). All rooms have a window that opens which is very nice to have. One thing you do not have to worry about if you receive a high floor is waiting for the elevator. We did not have to wait longer than 10 seconds ever for an elevator to go up or down and from floor 33 to the lobby takes 21 seconds, yes 21 seconds!!!! I have stayed in hotels where floor 1-5 took 30 seconds. We did visit during Labor Day Weekend, but this hotel was hopping all weekend and still no elevator delays. We used the valet for the car for $28 a night. Yes a bit pricy but the ease of dropping it off at the front and calling when you want it back is stress reducing to me. Every valet was great. Always asking if we needed directions, saying hello, opening the door for you, just nice service. Jay was the standout for me. He was quick, friendly, personable and dedicated. Always called me by my name and I would say a real genuine person. They tell you when you call for your car that it will be less that 6 minutes. I would call for my car, walk right out the door, wait 10 secs for the elevator, 21 secs down go to the front and there is my car. We are talking minutes here and not once did I make it to the valet area and my car was not waiting for me (GREAT SERVICE). We utilized most of what the hotel had to offer from concierge to the bars and restaurants. We did not use the pool, fitness center, hot tub area but did walk through the area and it was very spacious, clean and open. A sunning area is off the pool by the hot tub to catch some rays in a seclusive area with great views. We were lucky enough to be able to access the Regency Club during our stay and was very pleased with the assortment and service. We visited for breakfast, the afternoon snack and the desserts from 8pm-9pm and was happy with the layout and the service from the staff. Altitude is their restaurant on the main floor that serves at all times. We went for breakfast one day and was very pleased by the service and the food. There was a small mistake made with my order and it was cleared up very quickly and new food was brought immediately. Now to warn some of you my belgium waffle was $11.50 which is fine by me since you are in a high end hotel, in a very nice restaurant, in a city, etc and not your local Ihop. Strata Bar is a large bar/food area off the lobby. We had a few drinks there and was happy with the service. It is a cool place with 4 story ceilings and windows, tv's tasefully placed with great decor and ambiance. Peaks Lounge is their best views bar on the 27th floor. The bar which had tables, sofas, and a fireplace is the length of the entire hotel so it is a nice size. We partook in some cocktails with family and friends and sampled some of the food and was happy with our choices. This is an amazing place to watch the sun set over the Rockies. Location of the property is great if you like to walk around. The 16th street mall is one block away and has everything from shopping, food, bars, etc. Usually always busy and has a free mall ride that takes you the length of the mall (about a mile or so). You can get on and off at your leisure and one stop is one block from the Hyatt Regency. It felt pretty safe walking at night in the area and there is also another Mall that has 40 stores, movie theatres, bowling, just one block away. We went during the Taste of Colorado and it was only 4 blocks away. Not clammering for parking spaces and battling crowds just to get there, we walked out, walked 4 blocks and we were there. In this area is also the State Capitol so you are very centrally located to many things without the need of a vehicle. Overall we received a fantastic rate ($100 a night) and had an amazing time at the Hyatt Regency. The service the hotel delivered to us is what really makes it stand out to me. I have worked in hotel and retail management for 24 years and know great customer service and received the pampering experince I needed to be able to push my "Reset Button" before going back to the grind. Thank you Hyatt Regency!!!!
“Excellent Stay” The location was excellent, as well as the room. You can't beat the heavenly bed/shower. Tip: self parking is $8.00 cheaper.

“Very nice hotel, bed and TV need an upgrade but price is right” Booked a one night stay via Kayak for $87. Fantastic price for a very nice hotel in a great location. $16 for parking is not out of line with hotels in this area. This hotel far exceeds the Sheraton Suites down the street. The rooms at the Royal Sonesta (formerly Intercontinental) are not huge. Even my corner room which is 30% bigger than a typical room isn't big by any standard. The hotel rooms are updated but the old TV with poor reception and the non-lux bed are the exception. (Bed linen is nice but the bed isn't anything to write home about) The hotel is going to have an update in the spring hopefully they will address these issues. The floor I was on had numerous teenagers but I couldn't hear them at all. For the price paid you cannot get a better deal in Houston.

“You Can Probably Do Better” We’ve been staying at this old and venerable hotel for many years and have been sad to witness its gradual decline. True, the lobby is beautiful. Our room was large, the A/C effective; the bathroom clean and expensive looking. But the TVs are old and small, the décor of the room itself dated, the internet connection slow (at a cost of nearly $15/day including tax), the parking fee exorbitant ($40.50/day + tax vs. $15 for the garage across the street); the bar closed for renovation. Beyond these physical shortcomings is a decline in service (couldn’t cash a check due to a “systems problem”; coffee no longer delivered to the room; no more turndown service; confusion with valet parking). Next time we’ll look for alternatives.

“Very good experience” Hotel's location is very strategic. Service is good. Massive and well maintained fitness facility (i.e. not just a typical small room with limited equipment facility) The room that I am staying at in May 2012 seems to have been renovated recently and so it felt rather new and fresh (e.g. Flat TV). When I stayed here in 2010, the room was old and a bit tired. Hence, the May 2012 stay was a nice surprise compared to what I had. Also, try to have dinner at Juniper. The food is great

“Beautiful hotel in the busiest part of town” My wife and I stayed here for a conference. Excellent hotel. I grew up in NY, thus, never stayed at a hotel there before. This was an amazing first experience. As a New Yorker, I tend to stear clear of Time Square, but for my wife's first time, it was exciting. There is always tons to do. The hotel itself was extremely comfortable. We loved our room, very clean, with views and everything. I don't know how the cost was because our trip was paid for, so it was great to me. If you want to visit New York and stay comfortably in TIme Square this is the way to do it. We were able to retreat to our room to escape all the madness going on outdoors. Check it out if you can.

“The best service we've ever received at any hotel” The W New York is a small gem in the heart of Union Square with the best service I've experienced at any New York hotel, or any Starwood hotel for that matter. The valet staff, front desk, concierge, and service staff are all shining stars that are true ambassadors of the Starwood organization. A special shout out to Chris, Maria, and Doug (bartender) for going "above and beyond" during our most recent visit. Your warm hospitality and graciousness raised the bar for even such well-traveled folks such as ourselves. My kids are still talking about what you all did for them. A million thanks for creating a memorable weekend we will never forget. Now, about the hotel --a perfect mix of old and new -- and the old marble flooring and steps, ornate elevator trim, and antique office trinkets blend perfectly with the espresso furniture and purple satin linens. Rooms are spacious, well-appointed, and stocked with many amenities. Olives is delish, as are all Todd English restaurants. His signature chicken dish is my kid's absolute favorite meal. The only negative about the hotel is that it is so hip and trendy with twentysomethings that it's difficult to get near the bar or a seat in the "living room" on the weekends. This minor glitch, however, will not keep us away from our new favorite hotel in NYC.

“OK for a night but nothing special” As Sheraton Hotels go, the Mission Valley property works well for a business trip but it's nothing special. The room was fine, but if you arrive thinking San Diego, boats, sea breeze, seagulls, and sunsets, you'll be sadly disappointed. This hotel offers nothing of those pleasantries. In fact, none of those things can be found. The north side looks onto the freeway and the south onto a denuded hillside. The dinner menu at the bar was OK and actually the salmon was pretty good when accompanied by a martini. Overall, avoiding the Sheraton San Diego for another property will work for me next time.

“One of the best "boutique" hotels in NYC and great value” I have stayed at the Roger Smith hotel about 17 times over the last 10 years and every time is better than the last. Seems that every time I come to NYC and stay somewhere else I end up saying "I wish I was at the Smith". While some of the rooms are small, the suites are great, like little apartments. The staff in this hotel is top notch and is incredibly helpful in every way. There are fantastic restaurants and good deli all within a short walk. Also Grand Central is just a short 5 block walk which is super convenient. The place is very clean, food is good, staff is always great. If they have rooms available you should stay here, . . . Joe Sloboda

“Luxury at it's best” Suburb service from time of check in to check out. They truly make guests feel special. The concierge service is second to none (special kudos to J Scott Worthington!!). They helped with our daily itineraries and their recommendations were great. They know LA !! As an example they even tell you where the parking deals are ie The Farmers Market (free 2 hour validated parking) and downtown Hollywood ($2. instead of the garage most tourists park at which was $20). The best concierge in my 50 years of traveling. The front desk staff were great as were the Housekeeping staff. Spotless rooms, balconies with great views, turn down service, towel replacement twice daily, free bottled water replaced daily just to mention a few. The spa was very luxurious with multiple treatment options, sauna, steam room etc. Yvette and Hoss provided top notch service at the Lounge and breakfast bar. While the parking is pricey the valets are quick and always helpful (even offering free bottled water for our daily trips). Overall an excellent stay all around. Highly recommended hotel where service is job 1!!

“Impressive!” I have stayed at the Conrad Chicago twice for business. The rooms are immaculate with excellent bath amenities and luxurious bed linens and pillows. Service at the front desk is quick and efficient. For a leisure trip to Chicago, the location can't be beat. For business, the atmosphere is quiet and serene; perfect for unwinding after a day of travel.

“Disappointing Hotel in great location” Sinetime back when boutique hotels came about, you'd be expecting an overwhelming experience from an understated property in a relatively unusual part of whatever town you were in. Some of the usual amenities in regular hotels were spared (Gym, pools in some cases, a business center, etc) but rooms would usually make up for this in style and comfort. This is clearly not the case if the RS, where an average room is just marginally larger than what you can find in the radisson around the corner or at the courtyard a block north. Furniture is old and decaying, which is not the same as vintage and stylish. The AC in our room was loud and the courtains around it could not be brought together to stop light from coming in the room... kind of important if you want to be able to sleep past 7:30 am. Lighting of the whole room was left up to the two lamps atop the night stands, and another lamp on top of the desk. The other two lights were not working but I doubt it would have made a difference with 40w bulbs... The hotel has a lobby but it is not larger than a coffee shop, so getting in and out is easier thru the restaurant than the hotel's main entrance. Having stayed at places ranging from 5 stars to 2 in this city and knowing how to measure each individually, I wonder how this place can rank within the top 200 hotels in NYC in tripadvisor. Poor is a good description for what I see in this hotel, abd there would be nothing the staff could have done to make things better. Next time i'll be saving 20% and staying around the corner.
“チャイナタウンに近いビジネスエリア” DC観光の為に夫婦で宿泊しました。チャイナタウン近辺にあり、歩いていけるほどの距離でした。内部には吹き抜けで噴水などあり雰囲気が良かったです。ただチャイナタウンにはあまり中華のお店がなくちょっとがっかりするかもしれません。

“Westin went Wayward” While room rate was good for location, the stay was just mediocre. Outrageously expensive parking, dated/small lobby. little to no special attention paid to me as a platinum SPG guest upon arrival. Called 3 times for general manager's email and was given three different email addresses. Still have not heard anything from any of those emails. This is in sharp contrast to emails I sent to other managers at Starwood properties. Finally, walked out and no one to get us a cab so we ended up walking to a more main street to help ourselves. So ... nothing horribly wrong, but just not the service level of other Westin and Starwood properties. Good gym, love the double header shower, and the great beds.

“Great Value, Great Location, Great Hotel!” 6 couples stayed at the Novotel Times Square May 13-14 2008. The location alone would be exceptional enough to reccommend this hotel, but the value it offers in a city of high prices hotel rooms makes it a true "find". No it is not the Ritz, or even the Hyatt, but the hotel is well located, the rooms we had were well maintained, the staff is a delight, and did I mention the location. We were in the city for theater, and the Novotel is located in the heart of the theater district. 52nd and Broadway, 2 buildings off Broadway. Rooms were modest, but clean. Bedding was a little soft, and pillows a little small. I have included actual photos of the room and the bathroom. Carpeting was very clean, hallways well lighted, and looked newly wallpapered. No room was more than 1 hallway down from the elevator with straight sight lines. Hair dryer was an older Conair model with a "slow blow" and there was no magnifying mirror in the bathroom...on the other hand, the bathroom was very well lit, and had a ceiling fan to avoid steaming the whole room. Water pressure in the shower (with an adjustable shower head) was high, and the water hot! The front desk staff, and the bell staff were all above and beyond in friendliness and courtesy. The doorman Arthur was a delight! This hotel is an excellent value, and can be booked with Funjet Vacations, Midwest Vacations and I am sure many many more. I cannot tell you how much the actual room rate was, because we purchased a group package, but I know it was rated a 3* and was one of the best priced at that rating.

“A perfect New York hotel...” After several recent bad experiences at New York city hotels, I was starting to think there are no good hotels in the city, but thankfully, the Roosevelt proved I was wrong. This hotel is big, but both the rooms and the public areas are well decorated, comfortable and have great beds. The closet was large and there was plenty of storage space. The room and bathroom were immaculately clean. The breakfast buffet, although pricey, was worth every penny because it included thing like fresh berries, smoked salmon, omelets made to order, etc. The service was excellent and the staff universally friendly. The location is also very convenient since it is right in the middle of midtown, near the subway, shopping, the theater district and many attractions. This hotel is worth the money and many of the hotels I have stayed at in NY charge more and provide less value. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay and will return again.

“Overall, a good deal” We only needed a room for 1 Friday night in Boston and didn't really care about where, so we booked through Hotwire and ended up getting this hotel at a room rate of $89, which was great compared to the going rates at other nearby hotels. When we arrived we were happy to see that there was a parking garage attached to the hotel, where you can pay for public parking (at $32 for 24 hours) or also use a valet option with in-and-out privileges. Very convenient options! The exterior of the hotel was much better than I have seen at other Holiday Inn's. It is also in a good location...lots of options within walking distance, such as Boston Commons and Quincy Market. When we arrived, the desk clerk was very helpful in making sure we knew where we were going and had maps and such to go with us. We were also surprised to find out we were upgraded to a suite! We still have no idea why, but we definitely weren't complaining. Although the suite was bigger, it was not updated any more than the other rooms. The bathroom was tiny and the bathroom door actually hit the toilet when you opened it which was kind of annoying. Although the entrance and lobby seemed to be updated, the rooms weren't so much. They were perfectly fine with the amount we paid, but would have probably be disappointed had we paid much more. Overall, if you can stay there for around $100-120 a night, I would say it's definitely worth it. Although I can speak to many of the amenities because we did not spend much time at the hotel - more outside of it.

“Great location, too expensive” The room was very clean and comfortable - were given a disability room - it was the only kingsize room available. Furtherest from the lift which would have been a problem if we had a mobility problem. There was a very large, noisy function in the lobby when we checked in and pretty much every time we walked through, which we found a bit annoying We were given a key for the room refrigerator - which was non-existent - which seemed a bit strange too. Internet charges were horrendous, as were the parking fees. Parked in another building nearby which was more reasonable. Don't think we have ever stayed in a hotel where it was such a long trek to the room, from the lobby.

“Nice hotel but front desk staff could be more ample” This was my first stay at this property as a colleague selected it. I liked the location as it was convenient to downtown as well as some other spots we needed to visit off Preston Road. There was a nice bar in the lobby. The fitness room was good and had ample machines. My only negative was on the availability of front desk staff. In fairness, there was a large group staying with them during my visit so that did back them up; however, if you know you have a large group, then you bring in extra staff to handle the crowd or you handle their check-in separately.

“Pleasant, conveniently located downtown hotel” We decided to spend the 4th of July weekend in Washington D.C. to take in the fireworks and generally see some of the sights around town. Knowing how crazy things get on the metro after the fireworks, we opted to stay downtown somewhere within walking distance of the mall. This place fit the bill perfectly. Just down from the Verizon Center, a block from the National Archives, across the street from the portrait gallery and spy museum, and three blocks from the mall. One block walk from the Gallery Place metro stop on the yellow line. Very convenient. We used the location to our advantage to get an early start on site seeing and then came back to the room in the middle of the afternoon when it was very hot to relax and then went back out again in the early evening. Great if you are a family with little kids who might need a bit of downtime around lunch/early afternoon for an hour to keep away the "crankies". Room prices were about what you'd expect to pay in a larger city during the height of tourist season. The room was adequately sized, but not spacious and clean. There is a restaurant / bar attached which serves good food, but it is a bit pricey and there are better places to eat in abundance nearby. We did not opt for the breakfast package which costs extra (this should be including in my opinion). The pool is a bit of a joke -- it's very tiny. As long as no one else is using it, it's OK for quick dip to cool off, but not much else. We weren't here to swim in the pool, so that wasn't that big an issue although a better facility would have been appreciated. No onsite parking. There is valet parking service, but like all downtown parking in D.C. it's super expensive. We decided to park at the airport ("B" garage) and ride the metro yellow line to gallery place and walk the one block to the hotel (use 9th an G St exit and walk down hill one block to the hotel). Cost at the airport was $20/night to park. You can park for less using the "economy" lot at the airport, but then you have to ride the shuttle to the terminal. The "B" garage exits right into the metro station on the way to the terminal. Overall a pleasant stay and we're likely to return again in the future to this location solely based on it's excellent location.

“Great Place to Stay in DC” Got the Helix via priceline over memorial day weekend 2008 for $70 a night. That got us two beds overlooking the patio. Room was nice and clean but AC didnt work very well. In any event, the Helix is a cool little place to stay, very different, which in my opinion is good. There is free "bubbly hour" every day from 5-6 where you can have chamagne and rolling rock. The lounge and patio are cool but frequented by a lot of the "yuppie" type which is not my scene. On the last day we were there, Sunday, the suits had cleared out and we had the place to ourselves to hang out. The staff is awesome, very friendly and helpful. The hotel manager, Nabil, is a great guy and really made us feel welcome. Overall the place was great. Popeye's Chicken around the corner is recommended after a night of drinking, haha. Parking is $33 a night, so we parked on a city street bout 10-15 blocks away for free for the weekend. G Man

“never again” The first impression I got was okay, the lobby is nice, but it smelled of natural gas. We checked in and got our room. We went to the room and the halls were narrow, dingy, and dimly lit. The room at first glance was fine. I forgot something in my car so I went to the valet desk and asked for my car so I could retrieve my forgotten item. The valet gave me my keys and directions to the valet lot and my parking spot number. Not sure why I paid extra for valet. We were at an event at the convention center, so the walkway to the convention center was wonderful. The bathroom was filthy. There was mold in the shower and on the door hinges. The phone didn't work, you couldn't answer it. The desk kept calling and we had to call them from our cell phone to tell them the phone was broken. They never offered to send someone to fix it. When we shared our concerns at checkout, the man at the desk was indifferent. We had pictures of the bathroom and he didn't look at them. He told us they would take the room off the market to get it cleaned. I asked to speak to a manager and none was available. It took me 2 days of calling the Westin and their corporate office to get a response.

“Good Property and One of the Better CQs” I stayed here for one night in early May to visit the DC office of my organization. First, the location is fantastic. It is right next to the Farragut West Metro stop. This makes it simple to take the Metro from the airport without having to transfer lines via the blue line. As with all Club Quarters check in and check out is quick via their kiosks. I had a room on the 6th floor. The room was clean and good sized. It also had a microwave - although I didn't use it. The bathroom was small but adequate. The room had free Wi-Fi and a good sized desk area. I've stayed in most of the Club Quarters in NYC and this one was by far the best I have stayed in. It is not super glamorous, but it does the trick.

“Great Find” A beautiful small hotel on West 55th Street across from City Center Theater. Wonderful reception lobby, the room was well furnished and a comfortable bed. The only downside (not the hotel's fault) was a very noisy garbage truck apparently stationed at the Nearby NY Hilton Hotel. My room faced the rear of the building. But if you put the fan on it muffles the noise. The free continental breakfast was a treat and I would return to this gem (maybe with ear plugs) another time.

“Great stay” This hotel has everything one would want in a resort. We stayed with our family,and everyone had a great time. The rooms were very nice, and the amenities were above the norm. The staff was friendly and helpful. The shopping mall across the street had numerous resturants and stores. I could not find anything wrong with this fine edition to the Marriott chain.

“Basically a renovated motel trying *really* hard to be a boutique hotel...” ...and for the most part, they are getting it right. But, unfortunately, there is only so much you can do with a building shell that was obviously a former motel. To provide a bit more background about my travel style, and therefore expectations: I am a TA devotee. When I travel, I always consult TA first and then make my travel plans accordingly. Everyone who knows me knows of my faith in the TA community and our honest, helpful reviews. When my mom and I were planning this short trip to LA, I told her that I would plan the hotel and assured her that she was in good hands. She is more of a hotel brand name follower and I'm sure would have preferred that we booked with Four Seasons or Ritz Carlton, since those brand names give her comfort - and for good reason, since they invariably deliver on their promise of luxury, often at a price. Back to the Elan - when we arrived at the hotel and pulled up alongside where the valet station was located, I could feel my stomach drop. The website, while only providing limited pictures and none of the exterior of the entire building, certainly did not prepare me for what I was seeing. As I mentioned above, the exterior showed a two-story building that was most likely a former motel or travel lodge. The lobby was small, but nicely decorated, as were the rooms themselves. It is obvious that considerable renovations were done to this property, as the furniture in the room had little extra touches, such as wood trim and a flat screen TV. Also, the shower head and water pressure in the bathroom were superb. But unfortunately, the room itself was extremely small, as were the "balcony" and bathroom. I was also disappointed with the quality of the linens. Most distressing was the room's heating mechanism, or more accurately, lack there of - the instructions on the unit were extremely confusing and even when we figured them out and did as instructed, we were still left shivering in a very chilly room! Given the attentiveness of the staff, I feel comfortable that someone would have come to lend a hand if we had called, but we were so tired from being out all day during both days of our short stay, we were simply too tired to hassle with it and just bundled up for bed. Some high points - the breakfast buffet provided a lovely array of baked goods. Also, the location was right down the road from the Beverly Center and close to freeway access. Unfortunately, the road on which the hotel is located (Beverly) is rather busy and the traffic was a bit noisy at night. The free high speed internet really was free and really did work, which was a nice surprise. Overall, this wasn't a bad property - but honestly I was expecting so much more given that it is rated as #1 in all of Los Angeles! This is the first time that I have ever felt let down by TA reviews, and unfortunately I now fear that it has made a skeptic out of my mother. I would not return to this property because I feel that with the great number of hotels within the greater Los Angeles area, there is probably somewhere that I would enjoy more. But I do give kudos to the owners and management of this property for making the most of what they have to work with.

“Great Hotel, Great location, it made all the difference.” We stayed here with our 4 kids ages 16,14, 11, and 8. We got 2 rooms which gave us plenty of room to not be on top of each other. They were great at finding us two rooms next to each other since we didn't reserve the extra room until we got there. It is about a 15 min. metro ride to the main attractions. It is great having the metro right there along with a mall. The free breakfast was great along with everything else.

“Glad to get this on Priceline” Won this 4-star hotel on Priceline at $72 a night for this two-night stay, which included New Year's Eve. The hotel lived up to the lofty ranking on Tripadvisor. The only thing I wasn't happy about was forgetting the camera for some pictures. Hotel Monaco is a Kimpton Hotel located in town but only a couple blocks walk to the Inner Harbor. Rooms had high ceilings, modern decor and a clean, comfortable feel. Our king room only had a walk-in shower in the bathroom if that's a concern. I like the LG HD TV's and they offered about a dozed HD channels. We were on the 12th floor and found it very quiet in the evening, not bad considering the hotel seemed pretty full for New Year's. Valet Parking is the only option at the hotel for $36 a night. There is a parking garage one block up on the left and it was only $21 a night. If we include the tip for valet, I probably saved $40 for the two nights by just walking one block. Be careful when pulling up to the hotel because there is no pull out from Charles Street. Curbside is the only option for unloading. As stated earlier the Harbor is an easy walk and we did it on a snowy, cold morning. The restaurant/bar in the hotel is called B&O American Brasserie and we ate a quality dinner in there. It also has a modern theme, but moderately expensive if one is just looking for a quick bite. However, the smaller brick oven pizzas are excellent for only $9. The Caribou Coffee Cafe across the street was also a nice place to stop for some java. As stated earlier the Harbor is an easy walk and we did it on a snowy, cold morning. I highly recommend this hotel for a great stay in Baltimore.

“Good Deal for the Price” I stayed here for a conference that I was attending at the Peabody Hotel (across the street). Given the feedback from fellow conference attendees, I got a better hotel at a much better price. My room was clean and relatively spacious. The bathroom was very small, but the shower rod was curved, which made it feel bigger than it was. On the down side, the windows were sealed, which meant that I had to rely on A/C at all times. In addition, the Hotel is half a block from Autozone Field (Home of the AAA Memphis Redbirds). After the game they have fireworks an concert, which can be very busy. The room had a very nice chair and ottoman, but since the TV did not move, it was hard to see from anywhere other than the bed. As with many hotels, they tell you that your USA Today is included in your room rate. What they do not tell you is that you can opt out for a savings of $0.75/day. Also, if you are a Priority Club member, a continental breakfast is included (since it is free to join, there is no reason not to join). They are supposed ot inform you of this at check-in, but they seem to be negligent in many cases. Overall, though, this is a good, centrally located hotel and I would stay here again

“Many stays at this property” Our grandkids live a few miles away so this is our place to stay to see them.
