The rooms are clean and spacious, bed was good, check in easy, breakfast is good and varied, pool clean. We also attended a convention in Oak Hill last weekend and spread the news at the meeting that it was only a short drive from this IH express and that people should stay at this property next year. So, I guess we are the new advertising committee! :)

“Disappointed With the Hilton Palacio del Rio” I spent a night at the Hilton Palacio del Rio while I was in San Antonio on business. Overall, I was disappointed with my stay. First the good: the hotel is in a very good location, on the Riverwalk, right next to La Vallita, the centuries-old section of town that is now filled with arts and crafts shops, while the Alamo is only a couple of blocks away. Each room has a refrigerator, a patio and a nice granite sink. Finally, the staff was friendly and competent. Unfortunately, the bad list is much longer: (1) parking is expensive--$15 to self-park at a garage two blocks away, or $29 for valet parking; (2) the entire hotel is in serious need of a major renovation. The hotel was built in 1968, and feels rather dreary due to the low ceilings, dim lighting and cramped lobby; (3) the bed was OK, with lots of pillows and a nice comforter, but not up to "heavenly bed" standards; (4) the TV was a standard 27" tube with a modest 26 channels and limited news selection (no Fox or MSNBC); (5) half the rooms have no view (except of concrete buildings and San Antonio traffic). If you want a view, pay extra; (6) The rooms seemed very tired and the furniture somewhat cheap. Except for the new sink and the new Hilton radio, it does not appear as though much money has been spent on the room. At regular rates of $200+, I consider this hotel a very poor value. If you want a very nice hotel on the Riverwalk, I would stick with the Westin. For a good value, look elsewhere.

“Pleasant Stay, despite a few room issues.” The exterior of the hotel, the lobby, as well as the holiday decorations were all beautiful! The location of the hotel is not the type where everything is at your doorsteps, however the hotel is within walking distance to many of the more popular neighborhoods of DC. The unpleasant experiences I encountered included: the hotel's bathroom containing stains on both the floor and wall, and also the street noise from the bedroom despite being on a high floor of the hotel. Despite these few issues, the hotel's beauty and charm made my first trip to DC one I will never forget!

“Great Location and Nice Hotel for Families” The Palmer House Hilton is such a historic hotel. From the moment you walk through the front doors and walk up to the lobby, the view is amazing! It was really nice to walk into the lobby, see everyone enjoying themselves at the bar or just lounging around, and looking up and seeing the detail in the ceiling. It’s truly a spectacular sight. This is a very large hotel. There are different elevators that go to different floors, so be mindful of which floor you’re going to. Once you’re on the floor, it’s almost like a maze to find your room. There are a lot of signs to tell you where to go, so that helps out. Once in the room, it is very spacious. We had a double room with two queen beds, and the beds felt like all other Hilton beds. The bathroom was a bit cramped, but it was usable. There were a lot of towels in the hotel, which I liked. One strange aspect about our hotel room was the large walk-in closet. It had a safe and ironing board, and it was a good place to store all luggage. Our view from the hotel was just to another hotel room, so be sure your drapes are closed so no one can peek into your room. Overall the hotel was great. The location is nice because the bottom floor opens out to the L at Adams. I didn’t interact much with the hotel staff because there were so many other people in the hotel. This is definitely a family hotel since everywhere we turned, there were kids everywhere.

“Great location, room, service BUT very bad breakfast” The breakfast is included in the hotel room price and this is probably why the breakfast is ... well, I cannot really call it breakfast. Plastic cutlery, very badly tasting juice, tiny canteen-like room, although bagels were ok. The hotel should better provide a choice for guests to have a real BF Otherwise, very central location just minutes to all attractions of Times Sq, clean and well functioning room, friendly staff. If you like good breakfast, either don't stay here or go elsewhere in Times sq for BF.

“Brand new & wonderful” I checked in on January 8, and the clerk said the hotel had only been open 3 days. I've stayed in many, many Hamptons -- and this is the nicest yet. The furnishings befit a four-star. The bed was awesome, the A/C excellent and the shower (a large stall-type in my room) very good. Only occasional airplane noise, but no highway noise. I was able to hear my neighbor quite well, but I decided it was because he was extraordinarily loud. The location is extremely convenient to the airport and many excellent restaurants. Highly recommended!

“A nice place to stay in Seattle” This property is in a great location for downtown Seattle, and within walking distance of several shops, lots of restaurants, and even the Pike Place Market and the Monorail to Seattle Center. The hotel is set back from the street curb, so if it is raining when getting out of a cab, be sure to have an umbrella in hand. Rooms are very nice, and the rates are reasonable but parking (which we did not do) is expensive - $28.00/day for self-parking. We take taxis when downtown! There is no safe in the room, but the front desk has safe deposit boxes available. The concierge was helpful, and all in all it is a very nice place to stay.

“Seems up-to-date” In hotel row with nothing around. Had a large room with two doubles. The sink area is outside the toilet and shower room. Sink could use a lot more counter space especially if there is more than one person. Lobby is spacious and modern looking. Looks like a more recent renovation. Outlets on the bed light/nightstand. Wireless Internet was pretty strong.

“Great location for Broadway/Times Square” Stayed her over the Christmas holidays and again 2nd week in July. Both times, the rooms were clean and the staff warm and friendly. We arrived before our room was ready and our bags were tagged and put away so that we were able to start our sightseeing without a hitch. We used the fold out couch in one of the rooms on the Christmas visit, and it was a bit cramped with the bed out. Other than that, with the bed folded in, the room was a good size. The other room that we had was a corner unit and that seemed to have more space. I think all the beds in the hotel (if I am not mixing hotels) are all king beds.... The kitchen facilities are nice to have, if you need them. Breakfast in the morning was very nice/ample/warm. Nice assortment, something for everyone - I would have liked to make a fresh Belgian waffle instead of having it premade.....they get soggy sitting in the chaffing dishes. But with such a large crowd, I can understand why it is more efficient to serve them pre-made. One thing you have to watch out for is going down too close to closing time...it is extremely busy then, seats are harder to come by and the staff starts to clear things away just about when the breakfast service is over. Because of the crowd, the elevators are also packed and it could take many minutes to get one back up to your room.. We eventually went down so that on the way back up we would have a space! So if possible, try to eat before it gets too crowded. Location is great for seeing/being close to Broadway and Times Square without being in the hustle and bustle. Easy walk.....also an easy walk to the Empire State Building and it is one block from Bryant Park. In the winter, Bryant Park is home to a skating rink - not much wait when we went - and little stores all around, which was nice for wandering and shopping. Valet parking is convenient, but they do need 20 - 30 mins to get your car...... Concierge was very helpful in giving us directions to get to the 911 Memorial via the subway. We said we would return, and we did in July....and we will be back again.

“Classy New York” We recently stayed at Algonquin for 1 night and loved the hotel. The location could not be better and the staff was very attentive, especially as we were travelling with an infant. We were upgraded to a king-size bed room- the room was indeed very small, but impecably clean and functional. The lobby and the bar area are gorgeous- easy to travel back in time and imagine how New York must have been...

“Impeccable attention to detail” I love this hotel & have stayed several times. It is super clean, my number one priority, and I find the staff to be superb. Little things matter - someone was vacuuming the carpet when I approached the elevator with my husband, all the while chatting with another couple. It took me a minute to realize that the cleaning person turned off the vacuum and politely waited until the elevator came, & then turned it back on as we left. It was just so amazingly considerate. When we had a problem with the toilet, I called the front desk & the maintenance man was there to fix it in 5 minutes. Also, I love the outdoor restaurant/bar with the comfy sofas. Not to mention the heavenly croissants they serve. The linens are superb, and the rooms are quiet. This hotel sets the bar.

“Wonderful find on the Upper West Side” Stayed here two nights on business. Room was large, clean, well-appointed, and quiet. Nice bathroom with new fixtures. Wireless internet, flat screen tv, small coffee maker. Front desk staff very helpful. Junior Suite for $100 a night was simply a steal.

“Many good, but some very bad things at this hotel!” Overall, I am very disappointed with my stay at this hotel and I will not stay there again. For the price, i could have stayed at the DC Ritz, but I stayed here instead because it was close to the conference center. No safes in the room and none even available at the front desk is almost a crime! The bad: - The average price of the room was $500/night, for a five night stay, and the room had no view. -Cheap thin towels, not enough left in room, asked for more one time, didn't continue to provide more on future days. - No make-up mirror in room... even a very cheap hotel have these! - Closed concierge room on weekends... for breakfast and snacks. Why is that? - No room safes in any room... come on people, I have valuable to store! Laptops, credit cards, cash, medication, etc! - No safes left at front desk when asked! - Lines WAY WAY too long for coffee at their Starbucks!. Give it free instead of wasting guest time in line! I need my coffee in AM, but I don't have 30 minutes to wait in line for it. And the concierge room is closed on the weekend. And the room coffee is not an option with an outdated and likely dirty machine with hotel water in it and bottled water not available, even for sale, in the room! - Spa slippers cheap -- got a massage and the slippers broke within 5 minutes of wearing them. - Spa robes too short, how sickening! - Online hotel pricing is unfair. If you book for 5 nights, you pay the highest fee of any of the nights. You can save by splitting your visit into two itineraries; saving about $200! - Front desk did not answer phone, repeatedly - No mini bar in room! Whaaaaat? - Cheap toilet paper - Old coffee maker/style in room - Cheap drapes did not close all way - Our room was medium sized, but some friends of ours had a small sized room The good: - VERY close to the DC conference center - Great concierge effort for getting sold out restaurants... even AEX Platinum could not do what these guys were able to do for me. - Bed felt comfortable (very soft) but then hurt my back after 5 days of this because it was TOO soft. - AC is VERY comfortable and has advance settings - There was fridge in room, but I didn't need one? - The brought toothbrush and paste and more hangers, without any hassle - Very clean functioning iron in room - Clean room - Wrapped paper cups for coffee were handy (for water) - Restaurant food reasonably good and simple - Bar area was comfortable

“Average hotel with a good location” We chose this hotel because it was the least expensive hotel remaining in the midtown neighborhood. You get what you pay for. The hotel doesn't have central air conditioning, and our window unit did not get the job done -- can't imagine what if feels like in July and August. Everything else was fine -- the pool was a nice surprise (see picture). People went crazy for the breakfast buffet, which had a nice selection but seemed cramped for the number of people staying the hotel.

“Good experience overall -- really great concierge lounge” I've stayed at this property repeatedly on business over the last 10 years. Since August of this year, I've probably stayed 5-6 times. It's consistent -- but a few ups and downs. Front desk is great. They are friendly and quick. They offer express checkin for Platinum members in peak hours. Rooms are a little small, but functional. Recently redone, with new beds and large flat screen TVs. The Ipod docs in the clock radio are a plus to me --- i don't have to travel with my own any more! Generally, housekeeping does a good job -- attention to detail could be a little better, but no big things. Room service is very hit or miss. Have had a number of issues with delivery time and temperature of food. You're probably better off finding something elsewhere --- even if it's downstairs at Champions -- who does a good burger. Concierge Lounge is what sets this place apart. Staff is wonderful. They remember their guests, are incredibly friendly and always looking for ways to help. Quality / selection of food has gone down a little over the years, but service is still top notch. This is usually my first choice in Charlotte (but I'm very much a Marriott person).

“Clean and Updated Hotel in the Heart of Downtown” Large spacious rooms with extremely comfortable beds. Updated lobby and lounge. Very helpful staff. Walking distance to a lot of great restaurants and attractions. Exceed my expectations. Only thing I could even remotely criticize was the lack of any shampoo in my room, but hardly worth adjusting the rating. I would definitely stay there again.

“Great Stay” We enjoyed our stay. The room was large, quiet and comfortable. The safe box and remote did not work, but both were repaired quickly. The lobby and Library bar are lovely. Valey parking is expensive and valet left our lights on overnight. We will come back and would recommend.

“Cool spot downtown” Cool modern vibe in the middle of downtown. Lots of activity in the hotel. Short walk to resaurants and nightlife. Friendly service at all levels from the staff. Look forward to ext visit.

“Convenient location and very friendly staff” Stayed at this property for 3 nights and being a SPG Gold, we were instantly upgraded to a high floor with a view and automatic late check out at 4 pm without having to ask. The property looks fairly new located just a little west of soho, steps away from Houston or Canal on the 1 train. The area is not bustling during the weekend , away from the madness in the middle of soho. The standard room is equiped with most amenities , a modern bathroom with shower stall. The staff is very friendly in all aspect and helpful. My only comment on this property is there is some level of noise echoing from the bathroom vents coming from housekeeping and also noise from nearby guest rooms. If only they can the doors more soundproof that would be perfect. It could be only that room but I can't say for other rooms. Being an easier sleeper that doesn't bother me..and I will definitely stay there again..

“Not a nice place” I did not enjoy staying here. This was the first hotel I stayed at on a recent teen-tour trip to So. California and Hawaii. My room was on the second floor, and there was no elevator, so lugging by very heavy suitcase up the stairs was a real pain. The rooms are large, but old and smelly. The bathroom was tiny and plain. The shower was kind of gross. I mean, this hotel wasn't terrible, but it was just run down and clearly aimed at budget travellers. The complimentary breakfast was absolutely dreadful. The bagels were soggy and the milk was not even cold, and the coffee had a foul taste to it. If you are travelling on a budget, it satisfies basic needs, but for a vacation, LA has better hotels. I would not recommend this hotel.

“Don't judge this book by it's cover.” As frequent leisure travelers we've stayed in many four star properties. When we first rolled into the porte cochere we were underwhelmed to the point of concern. Once we stepped inside our disappointment turned into excitement. With the exception of the pool this hotel meets all the criteria for a four star property. The staff is well trained and friendly and the rooms are everything you would expect including high quality bedding. The rooms facing north have unbelieveable views of Lady Bird lake, Congress Street bridge and skyline of downtown Austin . The fitness center is large, well equipped and has high end equipment. To walk out the back door and be able to walk or run around the lake is an experience rarely found in a hotel stay. The independenly owned and operated water activities right out the back door give this hotel more of a resort feel than you normally find. We had a fantastic 26th wedding anniversary here and hope to return soon. Maybe by then they will have given the pool area the makeover it desperately needs.

“Absolute Premium Klasse” Waren für 3 Nächte im Trump. Ich kann nur sagen, dass hier alles passt. Sehr schön ausgestattetes großes Zimmer mit einem super Bett. Hier wollen sie nie wieder raus. Das Bad ist extrem groß und wunderschön. Immer ausreichend frische Handtücher sind vorhanden, das Zimmer wird 2x gereinigt. Eine Nespresso Maschine mit gratis Kaffee runden das Ganze noch ab. Fitnesscenter + Pool sind auch vorhanden. Für uns ist eines klar, New York und Trump Hotel passen perfekt zusammen = 100% pures NY feeling. Hier rentiert es sich, ein wenig mehr Geld auszugeben. Die blaue C+E Linie ist 1 min. vom Hotel entfernt. Super.

“Funky and comfy” We enjoyed our stay here. Our room was spacious and had a glamorous bathroom. The bed was super comfy, the owner very friendly and the breakfast yummy. The location in a quiet neighborhood is close to everything. We will be back!

“Scary looking outside but renovated inside” The only reason we stayed at this hotel is because the hotel was three blocks near a church we needed to attend for a funeral. On the outside, it looks like a dump. The folks hanging around the lobby at check-in looked questionable, but we were only there for eight hours to sleep and then check out. The bathroom fixtures and shower curtain were new, the bed was comfortable, the sheets were clean and the carpet was acceptable. The entrance to the room (carpeted) smelled of urine. All in all, this is not a great place to stay, but it's a good place to sleep and move on. We never ate at the restaurant. We paid a $119 a night (AAA rate) during St. Patty's day weekend. Parking was directly in front of our room. I would have never stayed here if my husband were not with me. A paint job on the outside would help the place out a lot. This hotel is not walkable to Michigan Avenue but there is a shuttle service to downtown.

“It's all good....except for the service (Diamond Member Review)” This could be a great hotel but unfortunately the staff bring it down. The Reception staff take actions but don't follow up; the Concierge is completely clueless; the operator takes along time to answer your call, the Executive Lounge never opened; top tier HHonors guests are assigned so-so rooms. The people managing this place need to get back to basics.

“Great location near Magnificent Mile” Stayed at the Holiday Inn Express for 2 nights. The room was beautiful furnished, but a little smallish. We loved the bathroom, it was quite spacious. The first night we had bad luck: There was a problem with the heating and in the morning we were down to 58 degrees F.... It was a general problem and it got solved the next day though. Breakfast was a bit a hassle. There's no proper breakfast room with tables and chairs but a lounge-like area with sofas and coffee tables. The buffet is a little small for so many people. Loved the pancakes-machine! Staff was friendly. Elevators were slow, had to wait quite a lot.

“Good place for our Wedding Party” My wife and I got married one weekend in September in Chicago, and although our wedding was not at the Westin (the reception was across the street), we booked approximately 20+ rooms in the hotel throughout the weekend. Nicole at check-in made the check-in experience worthwhile because she made sure that we had the very best possible rooms in the hotel. At one point, our wedding party and guests had almost all the suites in the hotel. The hotel was perfectly situated for our guests from out of town because of its proximity to the local attractions and shopping. The staff was very accommodating, with whom we were very impressed. The hotel facility shows some wear and tear and could probably use some improvements, but our experience was very satisfactory.

“Perfect location and spacious!” Our family of three stayed in a Junior Suite in June 2006. Large living room with table, desk, Hi-speed internet, fold out sofa(pretty darn comfortable too) & TV, large bedroom with 2 closets & TV. Bath was just updated - fulll size tub with shower, pedistal sink and even an opening window...ahhh. In the entry hall area was a mini kitchen with frig, sink, micro and plates, glasses, silverware, coffee maker & coffee. There are plenty of min-marts around the block and we had breakfast in the room each day before we headed off as tourists. Great location, between Lexington Ave and Park Ave - just 1-1/2 blocks from Grand Central Station (great food court on lower level). Lots of eateries, drug store, bagels shops, you name it on Lexington within a block or two. About a 10-12 min walk to Time Square - a very safe feeling neighborhood for walking in the evenings.The best place we have stayed in NYC yet. The coolest part of our room was a balcony - actually a tiled ledge area with some chairs that only 3 rooms access. We could sit out in the evening and look at the Empire State Building (see my photos) and look down on apts having dinner on their roof tops. Really an added bonus - fresh air and excellent view! Dang I can't remember the room number but be sure and ask for the rooms with the deck. I booked thru the hotel and paid $275/night Friendly staff and pretty little lobby area with a couch and chairs, 2 elevators is a bonus too.

“Excellent stay and value” I was at this hotel for three nights at the end of June through the beginning of July. At the time of my original booking, the price for a larger, two queen room was $200 per night. However, a week before our stay, I checked their website and saw that the price was listed at $110 per night! I called and received the lower rate with absolutely no problems. Our room was large, but basic, and clean. We did not hear any of our neighbors and we all slept well. The staff was very friendly, from the check-in desk, to the person who helped us work the parking garage payment machine. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others who are seeking a great location near the Magnificent Mile.

“Nice Hotel” I can tell you first off that the food here is Excellent. I had a goat cheese pizza at the bar with drinks and for room service I had lobster bisque and Caesar salad-- both meals were wonderful. I don't know if it is a good thing or a bad thing that I am mentioning the food first. The hotel itself was nice. Rooms were comfortable and clean. Location is great. We had a suite and it was spacious with a large bathroom and separate area with couch and TV. The decor is modern.

“Great Stay” Stayed only one night for a cheerleading competition at Reliant Arena. Arrived around 4:30 on Friday afternoon (11/20). The rooms were super clean and comfy. The beds were so comfortable. We all slept great. The breakfast was really good. My only regret was we were there only until early morning. We checked out at 7:30 am, wished we could have returned to the hotel after the competition and relaxed. The hotel is within walking distance from the Galleria. We shopped Friday evening and had dinner at the Cheesecake Factory

“Will Stay Again...” As a Gold Member got a very nice room on the concierge floor for one night. Inside room with a nice view overlooking the pool area. Concierge lounge for breakfast in the morning and heavy snacks in the evening exceeded expectations. Had a drink at the bar and it was a nice place to gather (as many already had) and wind down. Con? Prices in the shop for a tube of toothpaste and a pack of gum were over the top but I knew that before I walked in...

“Shocked at how nice this hotel was.” I'll admit it, I wasn't expecting much from this hotel. I booked at the last minute and found a good rate, so thought I would give it a try. I was extremely pleased with the room. We booked a suite for a great price in NY and had a room overlooking the work at the WTC. Sure, there was some noise but what a wonderful location and everyone understands why they are working so hard to rebuild these towers (or they should). Room was beautiful and all brand new. I stay in NY alot and this is my new favorite!

“Just ok” It's not bad but not as clean as I would have liked. The bath mat was dirty and their were random hairs in the bathroom and on the sheets. There are lots of hotels in this area so I probably would not suggest this one.

“Great for Business” This hotel is perfect for business as its right downtown and connected to the convention center. Also the hotel itself has great decor and is not the typical "convention center" hotel. I had a great stay. There is a shuttle that will take you several locations in the area

“Second Stay better than the first” I-95 is not know for great lodging options but this hotel has been great twice. I stayed at this hotel after leaving home late for a weekend trip to Savannah in 05 and was very impressed. Now once again this time on biz the property was clean and affordable. As an additional bonus the area seams relativly safe and there are several other lodging options just in case. Plus many food and gas options are available.

“Customer Service makes this a great find!” The hotel is in an old bank. It's a cool building. It would have been nice if Marriott decided to embrace the uniqueness of the bank versus using numerous modern colors that frankly clash. But!!! The Front Desk staff and people who serve breakfast are AWESOME! They were so friendly and helpful with any question we asked. They went the extra mile. The studio room is just right for a couple. Families would benefit from getting the two bedroom suite. We did a family weekend so I was able to see both set-ups. Both were very nice. The studio has a stove-top, refrigerator, dishwasher, microwave. The 2 bedroom had a full size oven along with the other items. Valet attendants friendly and $20 not bad, we took the cars in and out and it didn't cost anything extra. The breakfast was very tasty and a large variety of items. Definitely a place I'd stay again.

“Enjoyable stay” My daughter and I were in Chicago for a couple of days during Christmas week, investigating potential neighborhoods for her this summer. We used Hotwire for our room. I emailed the hotel and requested two queen beds which they were kind enough to guarantee. It was an easy train trip from Midway to the Grand stop; then a short walk to the Intercontinental. It's located on Mich. Ave in the heart of the Magnificent Mile. We arrived at 10am and our room was ready for us. They upgraded us to an historic tower room on the 23rd floor. Very nice, big room with two large windows and two queen beds. The beds were quite far apart with a big night table between them that held two large lamps. There were upscale amenities as well as bathrobes. The bathroom was standard fare with a tub/shower combo. and plenty of good quality towels, as well as a 4 cup coffee maker and a hair dryer. Internet was for a fee. It is tricky when signing on --the higher priced option shows first at 17.95. Hit the down arrow next to it and the 14.95 option is visible. We paid because we needed internet access, but felt seriously ripped-off. If all you need is to visit airline websites for seat ressies and/or printing boarding passes there is free access in the lobby for that. There is a Starbucks just off the lobby. We did not try any of the hotel restaurants since there are so many outstanding choices in the area, but we did order room service breakfast our last morning. It arrived within the promised time frame and the table fit very easily in our large room. We ordered simply- fresh fruit, muesli, coffee, etc. Presentation and quality were good. We had a great time in a very nice hotel in a world-class city.

“a little worn, average service, but nice overall” I stayed here with my boyfriend in February of 2006. Overall, the place is a bit worn, and the rooms are small, but not bad at all. The bathroom is nothing fancy, the rooms are not fancy, and you get a basic, clean room with some ornate furnishings. Service was fine, and not rude like you can sometimes risk in New York City, and as for location, it is right by Grand Central Station, which is quite handy for getting around. if you go with a decent expectation of good service and clean, comfy but not fancy rooms, you will not be disappointed. It is a good value for the location.

“excellent hotel” Out family were in the hotel for 5 nights in 4 rooms The rooms are big with a full kitchen The service was very good We do not like the location because it is far from times square and it is not close to metro station so we used taxies for transportttation

“Great spot” My wife and two of three sons stayed here over the weekend and liked it a lot. My wife would be more effusive than I am going to be as she has stayed several times previously for work. The staff is surely the best part of a very good experience. For example, they pulled out the couch and set it up for the boys, standard enough. They also left two little robe and slipper sets, that makes an impression on kids and therefor their parents. The rooms are intimate rather than grand, as is the hotel itself. The area around the hotel is very attractive and great for walking the dog, or restless boys with nice little bakeries and such. We had dinner at LaCroix which we would also recommend highly. It's easy to feel like you are part of the city here rather than just in it.

“Superb Staff!” Just finished a three night stay at the Carlton and it was the best prpperty I have stayed at in the last 10 years of San Francisco visits. The staff, friendly and always ready to help, knew their job and had recommendation for any question. The deluxe room on the 7th floor was large, bright and provided a fine view of the lower Nob Hill area and Financial district. I would agree with other reviewers that the bathroom was a bit plain and does need a shelf to complement the pedistal sink. I would highly recommend this location to anyone who appreciates a limited service boutique hotel and the carlton will be my prperty of choise for future visits.

“Disappointed // We Won't Return I'm Afraid” Let's get the positives in first - this hotel is in a great location, close to attractions and is easy to find. Taxi drivers know it which is always a bonus. The nearest cable car stop isn't too far away and the city sightseeing hop on / hop off buses stop right outside. There are plenty of decent shops and bars close by and there's a Starbucks opposite if that's what you need to start your day. There's also a bistro on the side of the building which served decent food and drinks. The lobby is great - it's well designed and has a warm, friendly and welcoming feel when you first arrive. It was bustling and there was always plenty going on. I'm afraid that's pretty much where the positives end. The staff were friendly but not overly helpful, we had an issue with our booking that wasn't handled well by the hotel team - our booking via Expedia didn't correspond with the booking they had received and as the hotel was full we were stuck with a small twin room on the third floor, rather than a king suite. Not the end of the world but it wasn't our fault and after a long drawn out conversation, we turned down the offer a bottle of wine in the cramped bedroom and accepted their offer of a complimentary breakfast next morning. Not what we had booked, or paid for or expected. Maybe not the hotel staff's fault but certainly not mine either and I expected better handling of the situation by the staff, especially based on Kimptons reputation. I'm not one for complaining - anything for an easy life in fact - but this wasn't on. It wouldn't have been so bad if the third floor we were stuck with didn't smell so bad - kinda like how your grandmothers house might smell, y'know stale overcooked cabbage. We couldn't wait to leave if I'm honest. There were venetian blinds on the window that didn't keep the light out, the air conditioning unit was incredibly noisy and the sink wasn't in the bathroom it was in the bedroom which was both very odd and became an irritant. The beds were uncomfortable and needed changing and I'd have been more comfortable sleeping on a sack of potatoes than using the pillows. Maybe we were spoiled having just stayed at the brand new Aria Hotel in Las Vegas but this room was $60 more per night than we'd paid there and to be totally honest, if we'd only paid $60 p/night at Triton, we'd have felt that too expensive. The free internet access wasn't strictly accurate, you had to register in order to get it. Not the free high speed service we had experienced at other SF hotels. Who wants to register? Just let me get online. So, all in all if your choice of hotel is more about comfy beds than artwork on the walls of the lobby, prefer a pet-free hotel and staff that put the needs of guests first, you might wish to stay elsewhere, but to be balanced, if you want a hotel in a decent location, a nice lobby with a dog to greet you and guest house style rooms with lumpy pillows, book away, i doubt you'll be disappointed. Either way, we certainly won't return as we now know there are many other, better hotels in this great city.

“Nice location, but old rooms” Good location, nice staff, no rollaway charge which was nice, but hotel rooms need upgrading. Toilets were the kind of toilets in public restrooms- no fans or heat lamps in bathrooms either. It just seemed old.
“LAX周辺ではいちばんおすすめ” LAに到着した日に宿泊しました。 中庭に小さいながらもプールがあり、スターバックスで買った朝食を食べている人もいました。 落ち着けるホテルです。 部屋も広く、大きいスーツケースを2個広げても十分なスペースがありました。 LAX周辺ではいろいろなホテルに宿泊しましたが、このホテルがいちばん良かったです。

“Problems with service, signage” The room was fine, but I had all kinds of problems with service. It started with trying to find the hotel. Their street address is one one street, but their actual entry is on the side street. It's all one way streets, and in rush hour traffic, trying to navigate to find their entry, took almost 40 minutes to literally just end up going around the block. And at their street address street, there is an entrance, but not for valet parking. And there is only a tiny sign, maybe two inches long that says something like "ring for service". I only saw the sign when the manager showed it to me. Their entrance for valet is on a very very steep street, and it's quite scary to get in and out, and park there waiting for a valet to show up. There were three separate instances where I was either overcharged, or a promised credit wasn't delivered. When I complained about this, the manager told me, "you've been nothing but trouble since you arrived here". Outside of these problems, the room and hotel were nice.

“Amazing!” Just stayed three nights at The Muse and loved it! The location is perfect to anywhere you want to go in NYC........everyone is friendly from the front desk to the doormen. The complimentary 5:00 pm Wine Hour is very nice in the hotel lobby. Everything I requested for our accomodations was granted. The rooms are great and we had a huge balcony from the 15th floor! My only complaint was that the water was a little slow draining in the sink & shower, but I'm sure when you are in an old building, this is common! Would definitely go back. I have stayed in several other Kimpton hotels and the Muse did not disappoint!

“A Beautiful Restoration” May 2009, a last minute trip to New York City with my daughter before her summer college session. Usually a Ritz Carlton junkie, I found a 20% off deal on the Fairmont website which put us in a Rose Suite at the Plaza for less than the cost of a standard King at the Ritz. Always wanting to try the Plaza since its re-opening, we chose the Fairmont. Upon arrival we were upgraded to a Deluxe Rose Suite due to road construction which would have been an annoyance. These suites are all on the inner courtyard so there is no view. But we don't go to the city to enjoy the view from our room so this was fine with us. Upon entering the suite we were wowed. The renovations are fabulous. I have posted pictures that speak for themselves. I particularly enjoyed the use of the Smart panel they have installed in the wall. From here one can control the lighting, the climate and numerous other features. I used it on check out day to call for the bellman. We did meet our butler but only twice. He came to introduce himself after our arrival and checked back later to ask us about our turndown service. We did not call for him at any time and thus did not utilize his services (whatever they might have been). The room did have a faint hint of cigarette smoking upon entering. But it was not enough to be annoying. However, for the finickiest of traveller it would have been a problem. The staff that we encountered were all courteous and friendly. We found the bath, though wondrously appointed to be a bit on the small side. The shower and water closet were large. Then vanity area was a bit cramped for two people. This was mostly because they hotel provides a lot of amenities and these crowded the countertop. Add your own stuff and it made for some cramped space. Will I stay here again? I am a Ritz person and love the club lounge that they offer. It was fun to experience the Fairmont but will still probably consider the Ritz for starters.

“Pleasantly Surprised” Staying in a hotel connected to a major airport, I had very low expectations. But I was very pleasantly surprised by the quality of the Hilton and have no reservations recommending it to anyone. The hotel is attached to the airport. The quickest way to access the hotel is by walking outside. However, the airport signs direct you through an interior route that makes you think you've walked a mile to get there. NOT the hotel's fault -- try asking someone for the shortest route. Check-in was quick. I asked for a "quiet" room and was given one where I never heard an airplane, despite being next to the airport. The room was of adequate size, with a large desk and comfortable recliner. There is a large TV (not flat screen) and a well-stocked mini-bar. Bed was very comfortable and wake-up call was timely. The bathroom was modern. The only negative was the shower curtain looked dated. Not a huge bathroom, but adequate and well appointed. Room service was prompt and the food was decent (if not exceptional). Many choices on the menu and the server was very pleasant. Empty tray was cleared very quickly. This hotel is obviously geared toward travelers who need to overnight in Chicago. However, having stayed at a number of "airport hotels," this one was much better than most. And, you can't beat the location -- a 3 minute walk to the United terminal. If you find yourself needing to overnight in Chicago and want a nice hotel with great convenience, the Hilton is it. Not having to wait for a shuttle and having a modern, comfortable room are major extras.

“Pros and Cons” The hotel itself is absolutely beautiful, and the location couldn't be better. Service is outstanding as well. The rooms are small, as is the case with most historic hotels. However, the heating system is either on or off, so there is no adjustments to the room temperature, making it either too hot or too cold. According to staff, it is the same in the summer. At the price they charge, I think there are better hotels in the city.

“Perfect location and top notch staff” I have been staying here on business for over 15 years. Thankfully, the rooms have been spiffed up in the past few years: clean,modern design and better lighting in the bathrooms. The front desk staff have been consistently helpful and friendly. The location is perfect for theater going and access to public transportation. The distinctive architecture of the building is helpful when getting lost; look for the zig-zag windows.

“Very impressed” My wife and I stayed at the Sofitel for two nights and were very happy there. The staff was very professional and courteous, accomodating each request we had: a high floor, a late checkout, a specific newspaper each morning, a yellow pages...all handled quickly and with a smile. Our room was larger than the typical New York hotel, even though it was among the least expensive of the 3.5/4 star hotels we looked at. The bathroom was great: very new, very clean. The bed was a queen, but felt bigger somehow. The location was very convenient. We could easily walk to restaurants, theatres, subway stations, and attractions in minutes. You could get to either 5th or 6th in less than a minute. There's a diner-type place called the Red Flame just down 44th toward 6th that does a decent breakfast; for dinner one night we ate at Triomphe (right next door in the Iroquois Hotel) and it was fantastic. All in all, a great hotel in a great spot. Highly recommended.

“Nice location, friendly staff, fine biz hotel” I am normally a Hilton person, so this was a first in a while back at a Hyatt, which was due to the conference I was attending. GOOD - Nice location right off the waterfront (note, not ON the waterfront, as you have to cross a street or use the connected bridge walk). Upper floors have nice view of the harbor. - Staff were all very friendly. - Free USA Today and WSJ available in the lobby (I would have preferred room delivery like my preferred chains) - I suppose the good is just that there was nothing of note, I had no complaints, slept well, and found the facilities acceptable. - Free coffee with coffee maker in room. BAD - On the same line as above, the hotel was very undistinguished and could be any other generic business hotel. - Rooms are pricey. My conference rate was $200 but normal rate was around $350. You can stay about 2 blocks farther away for half the price. - Facility restaurants are also VERY expensive, so I ate every meal over by the waterfront (ex. Cheesecake factory). - No free wireless. - Spotty room service, never cleaned up my ice bucket or provided new bags for ice. The bed was comfortable and there was a nice desk and nice flat panel TV, and a nice alarm that worked perfectly. That said, the room kind of was appropriate for Baltimore in general - it looked pretty nice and shiny when you walked in, but the more you looked at stuff in detail over the stay, you noticed the room was pretty rough around the edges. Carpet warn, old shower. I wouldn't have a problem staying here again as I had no problems, but I won't remember it a week from now and won't be rushing to stay here either.

“Dependable & Comfortable” I usually stay at this location once a month for business. I can always count on great customer sevice during check in and especially at breakfast. The good thing about Embassy Suites is that you get the cocktails in the evening and free breakfast in the morning. The staff at both of these times (and especially breakfast) is so kind and helpful. You would think you were staying at a 5 star! Other great things - location! It is close to Bass Hall, Barnes & Noble, Texas Wesleyan School of Law, a variety of different bars, Circle Theatre, and the comedy club. This is a great hotel with a great location and great staff. I can always count on a happy stay with the Downtown Embassy Suites.

“Great Hotel Just Off I-5” Nice hotel, although you will need a car to get around for sightseeing. If you do have a car, there is convenient, available street parking beside the hotel, so we didn't opt for valet. There is a health club, but strangely, you have to access it from the outside. Since we didn't eat here, I can't rate the food. There are too many other choices nearby to eat at the hotel.

“Gorgeous view, great experience” Well above average hotel bumped up to excellent for the positive experience we had there. Like several other reviewers, we booked through Priceline (doing very well on the price); discount booking notwithstanding, we were treated wonderfully. We were placed on a 20th floor corner room with a gorgeous, expansive view of the river. Room was newly renovated with LCD TV and surprisingly large bathroom. As for the staff, we didn't have much interaction with them, but what little contact we had was pleasant- helpful, proactive explanation of parking (for the few more bucks you pay over city garages, the no-sweat overnight and in-and-out privileges are well worth it), requested extra coffee pods were delivered to room and, as indicated above, wonderful room upgrade. We thought the location was perfect- just the right amount of separation from the Old City District/Independence Hall area. All in all, we were tremendously pleased with our stay and grateful for the wonderful room upgrade. I'm sure hotel managers regularly peruse TripAdvisor; here's another affirmation that encouraging staff to give upgrades to even the humblest (e.g., Priceline) customers is well worth it for the positive word-of-mouth it generates.

“Schönes Hotel in guter Lage” Das Hotel ist sehr günstig am Rand von Tribeca gelegen. Man kann Ground Zero, 21st Century, Soho, Hudson River zu Fuss sehr schnell erreichen. Aber auch eine Metro-Station ist direkt vor der Haustüre. Man kommt sehr gut von Newark oder LaGuardia an. Unser Zimmer war sehr schön designed, mit allem Notwendigen ausgestattet. Auch wenn es keine wirkliche Schwäche gibt, empfanden wir die Hotelatmosphäre als etwas "kalt", was vielleicht am schwarzen Design der Flure liegt. Das Frühstück im Restaurant im Erdgeschoss ist eher mittelmäßig. Es gibt aber sehr viele Alternativen innerhalb weniger Minuten Laufreichweite.

“our favorite hotel in Seattle” My husband and I have spent about 6 weekends in Seattle over the past 2 years. We have stayed at the Red Lion, the Fairmont and the Hilton and this is the one which definitely suits us best. What we appreciate about the Hilton is that the service is always good from the lobby to the top floor. The rooms are small and a bit old fashioned but clean and very comfortable. Above all, we enjoy a lot the top floor beautiful view. The first time we were there, we were no gold members yet and we could only enjoy the view when having our breakfast. Now we are upgraded whenever is possible and we can enjoy it in the evening too, while having a snack and drinking a gin tonic! Last weekend, we forgot our iPhone charger in our room. We called the reception on Monday and they sent it back to us immediately. We received it by Fedex this morning! Just a pity that their croissants and "pains au chocolat" were too dry in the morning.

“Good location, good rate” We do a lot of corporate business with this hotel, which probably had a lot to do with the rate, but the rate I got was significantly lower than other hotels. Something was amiss with my room during checkin, so they upgraded me to a "suite". Now for anyone that has stayed at Club Quarters and knows the size of the rooms the term "suite" is kind of laughable - it's about the same size as a normal room in other hotels. But the CQ continues to be a very clean and convenient hotel for business stays.

“Great view, but.......” Positives: Great view over Navy Pier and Chicago river. The habor and the Wheel, at night they were breathtaking. During summer time, every Wednesday and Saturday night they have the fireworks over at Navy Pier and rooms in this hotel get the front line seats. Negatives: Very plain bathroom. The tub and the shower curtain were somewhat disappointing. In general the room looked a little old if you pay attention to the small details such as the closet space and the armchair, although still within accpetable range from normal expectations. Lack of attention in room service. The restaurants they have in the hotel close at 10pm (which in my opinion is very early), so I ordered room service. They told me 20-25 mins but it took way more than 45 mins, and when food was delivered they forgot the beer that I ordered. I didn't check if they charged me for that beer, my guest and I were just too starving to argue at that point. Btw food came with plastic wrap on the plates, which was a little scary because that reminded me of airline food, but the taste was actually decent. All in all an okay hotel, location is great if you are looking for the view, the service, not so much.

“A Chic Urban Oasis” Aloft is located about 2 blocks from the subway, a block from the famed 125th Street and across from a police station, the Magic Johnson Theater and lots of foot traffic. I am primarily offering this description for those who are not familiar with Harlem as it paints of picture of a lot of activity and energy in the neighborhood. The hotel itself was no different. The lobby had vibrant colors, hip furniture and a cute bar that had a dj that evening. The hallways had interesting colors and the room didn’t disappoint. The furnishings were clean lines and the space was functional. The shower and bathroom were muted and sleek and included bliss products. The bed was comfortable, but not as comfortable as some of the other Starwood properties. I logged onto the internet and was connected right away. The staff was friendly; the hotel was clean, updated and chic. I would definitely return here.

“Not Worth the Money!” I am in the room at the Embassy Suites as I am writing this review. I am attending a conference in Austin and selected this hotel from the conference list. When I first checked in, the hotel lost my reservation and the front desk clerk was alone and was getting very backed up. She had to call the manager, who should have come out to help by the way, but she did get me a room after about 20 minutes. The hotel is rather run down... not what I was expecting. First and most irritating is the heat in the room does not work! The batteries in both TV remotes are also dead. These are things that any quality hotel would catch. Also, what does not look very appealing is the door that opens to the room next door has no door knob or lock, just holes in the door. Also be prepared to pay $10 for Internet! If the housekeeper comes to your door while you are there, you better let them clean your room then because they will not be back. I understand they are doing construction at this time, but my issues are due to hotel operations only. Final word... the hotel staff came across to me as rather lazy and the hotel itself need to be better maintained; this hotel is definitely NOT worth what they charge per room/night.

“Very Good Hotel” My husband, daughter and I stayed at the Embassy Suites for my daughter's Trampoline/Tumbling State meet at Ohio Dominican University. The hotel was only about 2 minutes from ODU which is one of the reasons why I chose it. Check in was easy and I was surprised that for a Friday night the hotel was not that busy. We ate at the cafe onsite which was decent, slightly pricey. I had the chicken panini sandwich that was quite good (although it came with chips) and my husband and daughter had the hamburger which came with fries. You really cannot beat the room set up. Since my daughter had to get up early she was able to go to bed while my husband and I watched TV in the living area. The room temperature was freezing when we got in but the control panel for heating/cooling was easy to work. The bathroom was pretty big and the hair and shampoo were nice (containers were small but I am sure that we could have asked for more). The towels were nice as well. The rooms were very clean. We got to the breakfast buffet at 7:30 am and it is included with your room charge. It was probably one of the best hotel breakfast buffets I have been to. The chef at the omelette station seemed very nice. Also, the coffee in the room was very good and there was even real cream to use which is a big plus for me. I would definitely stay here again even though you can probably find cheaper hotels. We did not use the pool, it did seem a little small.

“Historical Hotel” While I am a big fan of HIlton, and am a Gold VIP, this one was not really my favorite. At $209 a night, it was a little pricey. The staff seemed really extra friendly and accomodating. The Executive Lounge was really really nice and well stocked and I could say it was worth it being able to use that on the top floor. All parking is valet. Downtown Ft Worth is really cool, and there's alot to do.

“wonderful hotel” We were there for four days with our grandchildren and things could not have been better . We had arrival gifts for both rooms. The staff was very helpful every way. I was traveling with a walker and that situation was accomodated

“Go Fish” First of all, online the website says there is 1 hotel at this address. Once you enter the area, it seems there is only 1 property, but there are 2. The second being a standard Holiday Inn. The parking garage is a nightmare, located under each respective building, 1 is locked (holiday inn express), the second is open (holiday inn). They are separated by about 30 foot alley way. If you have the unlucky assignment of entering a garage on accident, due to pushy traffic behind, or no parking spots then you are really hosed. You have to drive backwards (in the HIE) parking garage lot up a huge incline, hoping not to have an auto swing around the sharp wall. The bar "the emerald" seemed okay, except it was happy hour and beers were still 4 bucks a pull. Not exactly a happy price...thanks but no thanks. I'll happily pay an extra buck or two and be where the crowds are more happening. I eventually stayed at the HIE property, the room was dreary, the view was an alley with the possibility of looking into a HI room (how exciting). The bathroom was really cramped. The TV was new flat screen (32 or 37 inch), which alone added a bubble point above. Will I come back, umm.. no. Given I still dropped with taxes over 140 bucks on a weekday, I'd drop an additional 50 to stay somewhere nice, with a view and close to the piers. I did not have the free breakfast, upon review the room looked way cramped for the number served. And after eating multiple HIE breakfasts, I couldn't bare to fight for a free piece of toast. How would I improve? 1. New Carpets 2. New Lobby 3. New Beds 4. Upgrade HVAC 5. Give an option to have a alley view or not. 6. New Elevators (really old looking used here)

“Great budget hotel” When I was in grad school, I attended 2 conferences in San Diego. As a poor student I didn't have much money to spend. Thank God for La Pensione! This is a really lovely but no frills hotel, a step up from a hostel but it does have a sort of college-dorm feel (right down to the laundry room off the reception), and a bit of chic-ness. It's about a mile walk from the convention center, but in a beautiful neighborhood (Little Italy) with many great restaurants and coffee shops at your doorstep. There is a tram stop a block or two away. Stay here if you are on a budget. NB: my last trip here was in 2007.

“1st Class reno of Older Quality Inn and Suites” Great redo, I have stayed at this location 4 or 5 times. It was good, now it's terrific. The rooms are well appointed including big HDTV's. You can't beat the location, short walk to Seattle Center and the Monorail to Downtown. My only complaint is the $12 a day for parking, I know everyone does it now, but it @$%#*^ me off.

“On the Ave, Good Location, Good Price” The rooms are small, but that is typical for NY. Fantastic location by Central Park and good restaurants. trader Joe's just opened nearby, so that is great. The 1,2,3 trains are a couple of blocks away, which is amazing for getting around the city. The rooms could be cleaner, but i never spend much time there. I think the Gym is pretty dismal, but the park is so close, that it is really amazing. The internet is a little slow, which can make it hard for working, but a lot of hotels have that issue too.

“excellent service” We stayed for a week at this hotel my room was on floor 22 my son's on 4th floor. Booking in was uneventful and we were treated very well The Bell boys are amazing and cater for your every need from carrying luggage, storing it, getting a cab etc. My room on the 22nd floor was light and bright, very effective air con and plenty big enough for one or two for that matter. The en suite clean with brilliant shower. My sons room on the 4th floor had different layout, different air con system but still very nice. He felt he perhaps picked up a bit more noise being lower down. The maid service was also very friendly. The room was cleaned thoroughly every day My son paid for Wi-Fi which was good. There is a gift shop attached also accessible from the road as well Here you can book your shuttle, theatre tickets or whatever. The cafe also attached and also accessible from the road is very nice with a typical breakfast menu as well as meals served all day. All of the staff here are pleasant and attentive. We only had breakfast here so cannot comment other than the breakfasts were fine.

“Troppo vicino alla aeroporto di Burbanck” L'albergo è interamente ispirato al volo e ci sono aerei e relativi componenti ovunque. Il tema del volo è molto ben sviluppato in tutti i dettagli. Purtroppo la sua vicinanza all'eroporto è anche un difetto perchè si sentono sempre gli aerei in decollo. Il parcheggio custodito è a pagamento, ma intorno all'albergo si può parcheggiare gratis sulla strada. Internet è gratuito, ma in camera il segnale è un po' debole. La camera era pulita e spaziosa.

“La primera opinion del hotel Marquis en español y mucho mas” Hola primero que nada espero que a las personas que se quieren quedar en este hotel y no hablen ingles solo español les va a servir esta informacion(no se como nadie escribe nada en español). Mi llegada al hotel fue buena exepto por la ubicasion del loby esta en el ocho, me inpresione mucho con los elevadores tiene otro metodo y aparte son el doble o el triple de rapido que otros hoteles. Yo me quede en una habitacion con vista al Times Square en una habitación doble la verdad cuando llege estaba muy limpio ni una mancha y estaba bonito el cuarto tambien el baño, lo malo del cuarto es que no habia minibar y si habia yo no lo encontre. La vista tampoco era para decir Wow pero es linda tenia vista a la calle y a algunos posters(el de coca-cola el de HSBC, tambien el de Samsung y el the una empresa de dinero de EEUU .Lo mejor del hotel es la ubicasion ya que esta alrededor de varios teatros y si train niños es perfecto porque esta el Toys ́rus y la tienda de hershey a menos de 4 cuadras y no escusa de no hacer ejercicio alli ay un icreible gimnasio con vista al Times Square y es gratis. En el piso 8 ha varias cosas aparte del concierge , los botones el check in etc... hay dos tiendas y un Starbucks (tambien uno en el piso 1) y siete restaurantes. De los pisos 1 al 8 no hay cuartos se que en uno hay un teatro y en otros salas de junta pero los otros no. Es mejor traer su computadora inalambrica ya que no le cobran nada y tambien alambrica en los cuartos hay para conectarla, si si hay un Buisness Center pero el precio que me dijeron esta carisimo 1dls por minuto bueno talvez lo cambien pero si nescecita usar el internet hay un cafe internet cerca que cuesta 1dls por hora. Si a usted no le gusto los restaurantes cerca de ahi hay esta el Mc Donalds a menos de una cuadra y junto a el esta un Fridays tambien a una cuadra esta el Planet Holiwood y ha 3 cuadras esta el Hard Rock Cafe. Y si vino por MONUMENTOS el Rockefeller Center y la Iglesia de San Patricio son los mas cercanos, el empire state no esta tan lejos en taxi le cobran 6dls pero en el que le combiene utilisar el metro es para la Estatua de La Libertad porque el ferry esta muy lejos, tambien si lo desea agerre el metro para China Town , Little Italy o el Soho. Para el museo Metropolitano y el de arte natural utilise taxi Ya se que solo querian una opinion del hotel pero como soy la primera persona en escribir en español le conviene esta informacion

“Schickes Hotel in Stadtnähe” Das Hilton San Antonio Downtown ist ein Hotel der Unterkategorie Doubletree. Man kann es nicht gerade mit einem richtigen Hilton Hotel vergleichen . Das Doubletree ist aber auch wirklich in Ordnun. Die Zimmer sind geräumig. das Personal äusserst freundlich und hilfsbereit. Das Hotel befindet sich 15 Gehminuten von San Antonio.

“Beautiful!” The St. Regis is a wonderful hotel. It is very close to the Metro. The rooms are beautifully appointed and the service is wonderful also. The bathroom mirrors are 'electric mirrors' which means that they have a TV in them. The only thing I didn't like about the room is that there isn't much counter space in the bathroom to put all of your stuff. Otherwise everything was great and I would definately stay there again!

“Below Par” Rug dirty HVAC slow to respond, poor control Bathroom floor dirty Used facecloth on shower rod - they blew it on the cleaning Room tight for 2 Queen beds Room tired but stylish Elevator slow $179+ taxes/fees, mid-week Doesn't hold a candle to the Hilton Gardens next door if you see price proximity

“Definitely recommended” My family just returned from a 6 night stay at the Best Western Plus Island Palms and we only have good things to say about this property. Check in was smooth and front desk person was friendly. We received a 2nd floor marina view room in the Casa Marina section of the hotel. Great view and good sized, super clean accomodations. We had 2 queens which were comfortable, everyone slept well. The room was quiet, we never heard our neighbors. Room was serviced every day well except for one time at 4:30 when it hadn't been done and I had to call. When I did someone was promptly sent up without question. The grounds of the hotel were very nice and the location worked great for us. Shelter island is centrally located to all parts of the city while being quiet and relaxed. If you are looking for a lot of activity to walk to this might not be the place for you. Shelter only has hotels, parks and marinas as well as a nice walking path and a fishing pier. We used the rental car quite a bit and I'd say it's a necessity if you are going to explore San Diego. The hotel had 2 pools. We used one and it was nice with a good view of the marina. We had breakfast daily at the Blue Wave hotel restaurant and were happy with it. Service was good and the food was tasty. A nice way to start each day. Overall, everyone we encountered at the hotel was friendly and accomodating. The property was attractive and the rooms were clean and tastefully decorated. I think there is good value here with the location considered and would highly recommend this as your home base to explore San Diego. We really enjoyed this beautiful city and its people.

“Hello Bowery! Bu-bye Staying Anywhere Else!” I selected the Bowery after reading reviews on TripAdvisor on the hotels located in the lower east side. I couldn't have been happier with our choice. It was such a refreshing change from other hotels in New York, which tend to be too modern and contemporary to be practical or comfortable. This hotel is welcoming, cozy, chic and original. The staff was very friendly, and ll of them seemed "in character" (all the doormen had mustaches, like the Bowery's brand logo. Coincidence?) We had drinks and late night snacks in the cool bar area in the lobby, which seemed to be bustling most of the time and is dog-friendly. We stayed in a king room, and were lucky enough to get a corner room, which had large windows with great views. The bed was extremely comfortable and it comes complete with a teddy bear that is dressed like the Bowery's brand logo. We were welcomed to the room with lovely treats on the table in front of the large windows, which I thought was a great overall touch. The bathroom was classic, with white marble, a lovely rain shower and a big, deep tub. This hotel really pays attention to the details and the staff absolutely takes pride in their work. I truly loved it there and will be sure to stay there anytime we return to Manhattan.

“Enjoyable” We were in room 2215, which is in the middle of the floor facing North, It did have a nice view West to Point Loma and the ball park to the East with nice city view in between. Late night drinks on the deck outside was nice, the appetizers were just OK and next time I will most likely skip them. HATE paying $27 per day parking but that is standard now a days.

“First time I walk in to a room and there are no towels” I called the front desk and they said they would send some up. Hour later no towels. I had to go the front desk where there is only one person working during the high check in time and there is a line of people waiting to get rooms Oh it gets better. You can't control the heat in the room only the AC. So it is 43 degrees out side and I am sweating with the AC on. Oh when you walk in to the room don't turn around because you can't. The room is to small for a chair or a desk. I can stand in the middle of the room and almost touch both walls.

“the little things make this place comfortable” we just spent a very nice overnight at hotel clift on our way to napa. i'd reserved a standard king room, noting online that we are celebrating an anniversary. upon check-in, the charming guy behind the desk noted our anniversary, and gave us a nice upgrade along with his good wishes. unexpected and most appreciated. our day's travels had us a bit limp for the evening, so we opted for in-room dining. it was, in a word, terrific. also fast. initially there was sound but now picture on the large screen TV, but a quick call to the desk netted an "house engineer" in less that 5 minutes, who quickly remedied that small issue. every person with whom we came in contact treated us warmly and efficiently, which helped make our stay all the better. very slick design is everywhere. my humble opinion: i think the beds they have are about the best anywhere, covered with what felt like higher thread count fine linens than i've ever experienced. room service breakfast was also great, right down to the room temperature butter (not unspreadably frozen) and delicious and rich hot coffee. with their many fine little things most places overlook making one comfortable, and their cheerful, well-trained staff, i'd say this is one of my new san francisco favorites.

“Sufficient” When I arrived at the airport, I came into Terminal D and had the worst time finding my way to the Marriott. I would not necessarily blame this on the hotel, but more-so the airport itself (which has a terrible layout). I had to walk outside in the cold all the way to Terminal B, re-enter the airport and finally crossed the walkway to the hotel. The hotel itself is nice, everything one would expect from a Marriott. We had a room on the Concierge Level and I have no complaints about the room or its cleanliness. The bed was soft and had a plentiful amount of pillows. The Concierge Lounge was nice, with a full bar and h'ordeurves. The parking situation is a bit of a pain...but being at an airport, you can't ask for much more. As far as the restaurant/bar goes, the staff is great and the atmosphere is nice. The menu could use a few more options and it's definitely pricey. The only good thing about the location of this hotel is if you have an early morning flight. There is absolutely nothing else around except the airport. The closest thing is a Ruby Tuesday. The hotel staff were a bit lacking. The front desk was not overly helpful and did not seem like they cared. We would leave the room mid-day for a bit and request maid service...only to come back to an untouched room. This was very disappointing.

“Nothing superb, but the location is good.” Good location. No complaints at all on the hotel. It is nestled up against the lake. You can either have a room with a city view or one with a lake view. I prefer the Courtyard off of 4th Street because it offers a little more for about the same price. However, like I said I have no real complaints so give it a try.

“I will come back...” Many years ago we had an office holiday party at this location and it was awesome. I was in town to attend the Ravens and Browns game tonight. When I arrived at the hotel the Aliceanna St. was blocked by a police barricade. I was told I would have to wait until the motorcade went by 45 minutes later I noticed 2 coaches being escorted. As it turns out the Cleveland Browns were also staying is this hotel. I immediately made a U-turn and parked and check in with ease. The service was great. The staff was friendly and helpful. I had a great view of the Harbor and Stadium on a high floor as requested. After returning from the game at M & T Stadium soaking wet. I was able to quickly gain access to my room, change freshen up and grab a bite to eat in the bar which was open late and buzzing with guest. It was a great place for us to network and socialize. It was a long night of celebration and good times on Thursday night. The drinks were good and the chicken wings were just ok, but that did not hamper my impression. I really enjoyed my stay...

“Very charming, great value” Terrific location near Union Square, historic charmer, not a cookie-cutter corporate hotel. Rooms not huge, but have all the necessary amenities, attractive nineteenth-century themed decor and extremely comfortable beds. Front-desk and reservations staff very eager to please; when I noticed on line that the rate had dropped (to $79!!), they let me take advantage of the lower rate. This is not 5-star luxury (the bathrooms are older, you can notice peeling paint if you are looking for it), but it is a solid 3.5 stars, with terrific showers and great comfort. I would stay here again in a minute, esp. for this price. The only problems during the stay: the message light would not stop flashing on the phone even though I didn't have a message (covered it with the phone instructions), and the heat system was very strange and I needed maintenance to come turn it off. But they came within 2 minutes. Very pleasant hotel. (Oh - and very nice lobby too, plus free wifi!).
“Good Stay” The rooms were modern and clean. The location was great.

“Clean, new hotel along 465, no hot water” We were visiting Bloomington on homecoming weekend so we decided to stay along 465 so we could get up the next morning and get there before the football traffic. The hotel was a little hard to find, it's in an industrial park and there are no signs or at least none I could see in the dark. If you bring along the hotel's directions or mapquest then you should be able to get to it. The hotel looks to be new, everything is clean and very well maintained. We got a handicapped accessible room although we didn't need it, the room was enormous, 15-20 people could have easily slept in that room. I had hoped to get two separate sleeping areas for the three of us but we got two queen beds in the same room and a sleeper sofa. The partition mentioned on the website didn't separate anything from anything and even if the beds had been on either side of the partition it wouldn't have been large enough to give you privacy. My major complaint is a temporary one, hopefully, we had almost no hot water in the shower, by the time the 3rd person got in there it was ice cold. And the water pressure was so low that it took forever to get the shampoo out of my hair. We mentioned it on the way out and the desk clerk said something to the effect that they knew about it and they were sorry. Breakfast was complimentary which is always nice for families, there was eggs, sausage, make your own waffles, bagels, muffins, fruit, cereal, yogurt, tea, coffee, juice. I'm giving the hotel a higher rating than my personal experience would indicate because the hot water problem seems to be temporary and the hotel actually seemed to be quite nice. It was not good for us because of the privacy issue, most families probably don't care if the beds are in the same room. The location is fine as long as you are using it for the airport (park and fly) or a place to stay when Bloomington is overbooked. Not close to Indy itself.

“Huge Hotel, Great Location” Everything about the Marquis is big; if you are looking for a quiet place to stay, this is not it. But the location in the heart of Times Square cannot be beat. One negative-and it is a big one for business travelers. Internet service is spotty at the Marquis; the lack of reliable service impacted my ability to work. I will stay here again for a fun trip, but I will not do soon business.

“Great location, newly renovated” If you stay here, stay in the Historic Tower. It has recently been redone with new carpet, furniture, wallpaper, etc. It is luxurious and filled with amenities. The views are incredible if you are lucky enough to get a high room on the south or east side of the building. It is an old building located on Michigan Avenue. Consequently, there is outside noise and sometimes if people allow their doors to slam, it can be noisy. Be a good neighbor and don't let the door slam! The pool & fitness center are AMAZING! This is the part I enjoy the most when I stay here. The FC is two levels, with cardio equipment on one level and strength equip on the upper level. The pool is a lap pool, however, so if you have a bunch of kids that want to lounge around in the pool, there may be better choices.

“Vey comfortable stay, let down by lack of restaurants/bars in vicinity” We stayed for 3 nights & were impressed by the comfort & facilities in the room (studio suite) including: 2 ring hob, sink, microwave, full size fridge, coffee maker- all in a spacious room with dining area & large shower. There was free internet access in the room, but via USB (one only)- seemed OK, but not particularly fast. I think there was wifi only in the communal spaces. The queen sized bed was extremely comfortable & standard of cleanliness was good.Staff were always courteous & friendly & willing to assist with any queries. A request for more towels via room service was dealt with quickly & efficiently. There is pool & fitness area but we did not try them. The breakfast was also very reasonable: choice of hot & cold (typically variations of scrambled eggs, sometimes sausages/bacon, along with potatoes/hash browns). Plus toast (white & brown), cereals, juices, selection of teas, coffee, muffins, porridge, yoghurt, fresh grapefruit, tinned fruits & a waffle maker. The free evening meal is only on offer from Monday-Thursday so we missed out on this as we stayed friday- monday. Our issue with this hotel is the location-it is a long way from any restaurants, bars, shops etc. It is very close to the I-5 which makes it convenient for San Diego's big time attractions but not so good if after a hard days sightseeing you just want to pop out to a local haunt for a meal or just to relax as this involved a major drive. There is the sister Hilton Hotel on the same site & we had a meal there one night, which was pleasant, but very quiet. The food was good & the waiter attentive & knowledgeable about the beers & wines available.

“Bobbled Reservation , Super Recovery” We arrived in Boston at 10:30 PM from the west coast to be told that there was no room at the INN. Since we had a reservation number and had paid in advance we were taken aback - After consulting Embassy Suites got us into the Hayatt at LOGAN for the same price plus a complimentary Breakfast. This is the way that Bobbles are supposed to be handled rather than blowing off the customer as a Major Bank would have done. We would consider booking with them in the future.

“Great Suite, Great Location, Great View” I stayed at this hotel for just over 3 weeks. My suite was comfortable, clean, well appointed and had a fantastic view (Empire State Building, Hudson River and the 'Freedom Tower' 1 World Trade Center). My room had a comfortable bed, plenty of closet and drawer space a flat screen tv and DVD player (dvd's are available for overnight rent free at the front desk), and a large writing desk. It also had a kitchenettes with a full sized fridge, a microwave, toaster, coffee maker, dishwasher and all the pots/pans/plates/utensils etc required. The suite was cleaned and restocked once a week, but you could request towel changes, extra dishwashing tablets etc if required at any time. I actually enjoyed not having someone coming into my room every day. I really liked the staff here. The front desk staff greeted me with a smile every time and if I came across housekeeping or other staff in elevators etc, they were all very friendly, which I liked. It made me feel very welcome. I booked here because the hotel I had previously stayed in was not available for my entire stay, I was not disappointed, I would happily stay here again.

“Excellent hotel on Riverwalk” We had an excellent stay at this hotel. We paid the hotel's internet rate of $179 to guarantee a suite with two beds for a Tuesday night through Friday night stay. Even though there wasn't much happening in SA at that time for the leisure traveler (except a convention of 3,000 forensic scientists), the hotels on the Riverwalk were pretty much sold out by the time we arrived; so was this hotel. We found $179 to be a deal for the location; the Westin next door was at least $50 more a night for a room only. Our suite was a real suite, with two separate rooms; one had two queen beds, the other was a living room/kitchen with a pullout bed. I agree with some of the other reviews that the suites can be dark; ours only had a window in the bedroom, but we weren't spending much time during the day in the room anyway. The hotel was built in a historic building, and if you convert a old building, you don't get to change the windows. I for one would rather have a city's historic buildings saved and repurposed and put up with a little dimess rather than have them torn down and replaced. San Antonio has done an impressive job of saving its history. The free breakfast buffet was truly excellent, with scrambled eggs that you could add cheese and salsa to, bacon, fresh fruit, french toast. The hotel warned us that the last hour of the breakfast could be crowded, but we didn't find that during our stay. The breakfast room is beautiful, glassed in and overlooking the Riverwalk. From 530 to 730 there an appetizer and drinks buffet (margarita, wine), which could really serve as a meal.
