The first night we attended it, we never did have dinner because we weren't hungry afterwards. My teenage daughter was with us, and she would have been happy having that as dinner every night. The hotel does charge a lot to park your car ($20), but we didn't find we needed a car in SA. The hotel was in an excellent location, on a quiet part of the Riverwalk but just a short walk to everything, from the action-oriented part of the walk to the Alamo. There's a very tiny but nice hot tub (4 people MAX) on the roof, as well as a pool that was heated enough that we could swim in it at night in February. The rooms also have pay-per-view movies, which we liked. After we arrived on Tuesday, we told the reception staff that we were thinking of cancelling our reservation for Wed. night to spend that night on a ranch in nearby Bandera. They said that wouldn't be a problem. When we made the decision to do that later, the fellow on the next shift at the reception desk said we couldn't do that, because the computer would cancel our entire reservation, and since they were overbooked, he wouldn't be able to override the computer to rebook us for Thursday and Friday nights. But when I talked to the reservation specialist, Monica, the next morning, she straightened the whole thing out very efficiently and we were able to go to Bandera for one night and come back at our internet rate for Thursday and Friday. We thought this hotel was a good deal in a relatively expensive city. We'd definitely stay there again (but this time we would ask in advance for a brighter room, now that I know they exist thanks to this list!).

“Embassy Suites Downtown Chicago” I really enjoyed my stay at thios hotel. It was a great place to relax and and a great place to shop. I t is located in a good area and i would recommend it to anyone. I have stayed at a lot of Embassy Suites all over the country and i must say this is my favorite.

“The Beach Bar -- Sand, cocktails, music and a fire pit!” (The W Hotel's rooftop bar) I went here with my uncle and his date after dinner back in early 2002. We arrived fairly early, and we were able to get prime seating directly in front of their fire pit. The drinks were pricey but strong. The sand was a nice touch, and the background music was decent. As the night progressed, the place became crowded, seemingly beyond capacity. People practically fought for seating near the fire pit as the temperature dropped. I'd recommend this as a great place for after-dinner cocktails, but if crowds aren't your thing, then avoid the Beach Bar for late weekend evenings. Cons: Noisy, crowded, cold if you're not near the fire pit. Overall user rating: Recommended

“My Fav US Hotel!” The Chicago Four Seasons is one my favorite hotels- the service is impeccable from the moment you check in. The rooms are beautiful and perfectly appointed for total relaxation. It is a pleasure to come back to your room and relax after a work day; it's almost better then home (almost!) The best part is turn down service; when yo leave for dinner, housekeeping tidies up, refreshed your towels, lays out your robe, turns on light jazz music, and turns down your bed. I wish everyday could end like that! Room service food is delicious, and the hotel bar has the best collection of Scotches I've ever seen.

“Comfortable Stay” This hotel is great for a business trip or short stay. The staff is excellent, room comfortable and clean, and breakfast delicious. However, the bathroom sink is set too far away (close to the mirror) and it was not easy to lean so far forward to use the sink.

“Trendy and Fun” We recently stayed at The Standard for two nights and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We were with a group of friends (some who live in the city) to celebrate some big birthdays. Hotel is a short cab ride away from Penn Station (we took the train from Boston) We stayed on the 6th floor in a regular room. Yes, the rooms are small but most are in NYC. The bed was king-sized and super comfortable and I loved the pillows. There was a good-sized flat screen TV across from our bed with a ton of channels. The mini-bar was quite extensive with anything you could possibly imagine. You have to be comfortable with who you are staying with if you have a room with the see-through shower. We loved it and thought the water pressure was great. Our room looked over the highline walkway and you can literally look down at people, many waved to us. Be aware of this as it is very easy to see into your room from there and at night, if you want privacy, draw the curtains (which by the way did a great job of blocking out the early morning light) We had friends who stayed on the 12th floor looking over the Hudson. Their room offered more privacy and they had a more private shower with bath. The rooms were relatively quiet. You could not hear any noise from outside, just the occasional door in the hallway. It had a good amount of towels, toiletries (even though I wasn’t a fan of what they provided) and great black robes that my DH loved! My only complaint with the room itself was storage space. Besides the tiny closet, there are no places to put your clothes. I couldn’t imagine what to do if you were there for an extended time. We just kept most of our stuff in our suitcase on the floor. The elevators were awesome with the video constantly playing, sometimes we wanted to keep riding in it just to watch. We went up to the Boom-Boom room late afternoon for cocktails , very stylish with great views! This is closed most weekend nights for private parties. You have to check out the bathrooms, floor to floor glass windows (like the whole hotel) looking out at the city. One of our friends was too uncomfortable to go the bathroom! We also had drinks and snacks in the lobby bar which also had a great outdoor seating area. We were lucky to have a very warm May weekend. Great people watching- we saw a commercial being filmed one day and models another for a magazine spread. Drinks and food are not cheap but we find that nothing is in New York so we were not surprised. We went to the BeerGardern late afternoon with friends which is a great place on a warm day (and they do serve more than beer) and also checkout the Standard Grill late night which had tasty sandwiches (at slightly reasonable prices). This whole area was hopping on Saturday night with a wide range of people. Located in the popular meatpacking district there is a lot to do in this area. We enjoyed walking the Highline which is not completed yet, but definitely a nice walk. Hogs and Heifers is across the street if you like beer and dive bars. Pastis is around the corner for brunch which we did (very busy place) and we also were able to go to Morimoto which is just a few blocks away for some great sushi. Overall, we really enjoyed our time at The Standard and would go back on our next trip to NYC
“Love the Warwick!” Always have a nice time at the Warwick Hotel. A great place. Really fun rooftop pool and the restaurants are really good. Close to the Fillmore and Ogden for a concert stay!

“Ottima posizione, assolutamente consigliato!” Abbiamo soggiornato in questo hotel per 5 notti durante il ponte dell’Immacolata. Essendo la nostra terza visita a New York e non volendola vedere da “turisti” abbiamo scelto un hotel che fosse in una posizione strategica e vicino a Times Square. Dopo una lunga ricerca la scelta è caduta sul 414 Hotel per via dei prezzi competitivi (rispetto ad altri hotel di qualità decisamente inferiore), la posizione e gli ottimi commenti. Premetto che se tornassi a New York, non esiterei a riprenotare in questo piccolo hotel perché l’esperienza è stata davvero positiva. L’hotel si trova sulla Restaurant Row, a un paio di isolati dalla fermata della metro più vicina, nonché dalla stazione degli autobus e vicinissimo a Times Square (neanche 5 minuti a piedi). In meno di un quarto d’ora si raggiunge a piedi anche la Penn Station, dove arriva la maggior parte dei treni diretti a New York. La zona è molto tranquilla e la sera si anima per via dei numerosi ristoranti che si trovano a pochi passi dalla struttura. Ci hanno dato una stanza nella parte interna dell’hotel (a cui si accede attraversando il cortile interno) e nonostante qualche rumore che arrivava dalle scale o dai piani superiori, era davvero silenziosa. L’hotel non dispone di un ascensore e questo può effettivamente essere problematico per gli occupanti delle stanze ai piani alti. Fortunatamente la nostra era al piano terra. L’ingresso è molto carino anche se piuttosto piccolo. Ci sono la reception, un desk con il computer (è possibile usare connessione e stampante gratuitamente), il tavolo per la colazione (se non erro con 6 posti) con un piccolo buffet, un camino e un paio di poltrone... il tutto in pochi metri quadrati. Non ho comunque mai avuto problemi a trovare posto la mattina per fare colazione... Di fianco si trova una piccola cucina dove è possibile servirsi con bevande calde e fredde a ogni ora del giorno. La mattina invece al buffet si possono trovare bagel, briosche, marmellata, succhi, cereali etc. Non variano di giorno in giorno ma è gratis, quindi va bene così!!! Lo staff è molto cordiale inoltre è possibile depositare gratuitamente i bagagli al momento della partenza anche se non c’è un vero e proprio deposito ma vengono lasciati davanti al banco della reception. Consiglio questo hotel a tutti e spero di poterci tornare presto!

“Outstanding location, rest = not bad but not extraordinary” Location: outstanding location – this is the reason to stay here Ambience: the hotel can be a bit too crowded. Service is OK but not outstanding. Value-wise, this is probably not the best in NYC unless you want this truly top location Not sure why it is Westin - it should be more like standard 5-star Sheraton hotel

“Elegant, Large and extremely busy and crowded” Business convention in SF required me to stay at this Beautiful Hotel. Service was great! Rooms in the old building are small but clean and well appointed. Not a bad experience, however it is pricey and too busy for my preference. I seem to like the smaller boutique hotels for my travels. The location is dead center Union Square! So perfect for COnvention Center access, shoppoing like no other! However as SF has enacted free Healthcare for all- the homeless receive this benefit as well- there are homeless 4-8 deep on every corner and they can be aggressive (worse than LA). Be careful.

“Great value, quiet location, shuttle to Johns Hopkins Univ.” Great, low cost alternative if you're visiting Johns Hopkins University. At $89 to $119/night, this is a great value for a hotel. While the rooms are somewhat spartan (and probably needs an update) my double bed room was very spacious, clean and comfortable. It included a flat screen TV (most of the channels were analog though), a refrigerator and a large work space. The shower / bath was also larger than normal. The hotel/conference staff were very friendly. During my one night stay the hotel wasn't that crowded. They also provide a free shuttle to Johns Hopkins Univ, which is about 15 minutes away.

“Hotel has a unique atmosphere, rooms are average.” We stayed here for one night over the Thanksgiving weekend. We were attending a game at Lucas Oil Stadium for the high school football playoffs, it was no more than a 5 minute walk. The hotel is cute with statues featuring people boarding the train and such. There are sleeper cars available for about double the rate ($209 the front desk told us), each with a different theme. We saw the P.T. Barnum and Charlie Chaplin cars, both very unique. I would consider staying in them in the future. Our room was average, nothing special, with a view of an ugly lot despite asking for a nicer room for a special anniversary. The bed was pretty comfortable. The exercise room was fairly nice with a nice variety of equipment. They give you a little "care" package when you get to your room...ear plugs (for the trains that go by that you can hear), an eye mask and some lavender sleep spray to spray the room/linens. We received 2 complimentary drinks at the Pullman Restaurant/Bar. We were disappointed to have last call around midnight. Parking is $27 a night at the hotel which seems a little pricey for Indy, you may want to check out public parking. Overall, this was a nice stay but I'd recommend staying in a sleeper car or looking for something a little more upscale in the same price range.

“Great value -especially if you have a car!” This hotel might seem a bit out of the way but it is an easy walk to Times Square and the theaters. The rooms were modest and very clean. There are no in room coffee makers which is annoying but there is a deli next door and a Dunkin Donuts across the block. Small lobby area but nicely furnished.

“Great location, friendly staff, nice stay” We got this hotel on a hotwire deal for $185/night which considering the other prices around was reasonable. The hotel is really nice inside, rooms are decent size and clean, bathrooms are clean and adequate size. Mini bar prices are excessive but it is the mini bar and you could walk a block and a 1/2 to Safeway or Walgreens to get anything you need. Parking is in line with other major city hotels but considering the garage is under their own building it's ridiculous. If they used a rented city lot or something that I could see having city rates. However, we did read the rate ahead of time and saved about 20/night parking in the garage across the street. Staff is friendly and although we didn't ask for anything after checking in I think they seem pretty accomodating. The managers happy hour lends itself to large groups drinking in excess for an hour and yelling in the lobby but we didn't hear any noise when in our room which was nice. Bed was comfy and they have a great multi outlet port to charge 5 or 6 things at a time. If there is one thing that makes this place worth every penny it's the location. You are a 3min walk to Jefferson by Boudin Bakery, 5ish min walk to Pier 39 packed with stores and restaurants and about a 10min walk the other way to Ghiradelli. It's really easy to drive to other great spots from here to. All in all a good stay and I would definitely reccomend it.

“Love it!!!” This is an amazing small hotel right on the wharf in San Fan. We had a delux ocean room and woke each day to the Bay bridge and the ferries going out to the famous Alcatraz ! The staff were amazing in every way and nothing I can say will explain the service and quality of this hotel.

“Good Standard Hotel” I stayed here for business. This is directly across the road from Hilton Anatole and is sort of tucked away behind the highway. 5 min drive will get you to a lot of good restaurants. Perfect nice quiet place to stay for work travel.
“清潔、立地良し、便利、おすすめできます。” とにかく部屋が清潔です。この点だけでもおすすめできます。ウェストレイクセンターにもコンベンションセンターにも近く、立地も申し分ないでしょう。スタバが1階に入っていて、朝6時から夜遅くまで開いているのも重宝しました。空港行きのバスが停まるのも便利でした。5連泊しましたが、もっと滞在したいと思ったほどです。

“Ace by name - Ace by nature” I stayed at Ace Hotel last May (2011). From the moment you approach the entrance you pick up on the vibe of the place. It's buzzy and exciting. The staff are cool looking (in a London Shoreditch kind of way) but don't give off a judgemental air. I was offered a choice of two rooms - street facing and inner facing. I took one, didn't like the view, then asked to see the other, which I preferred. A guy came up with a new door card and helped me move my stuff. There was no fuss and they seemed to genuinely care that I was happy. I found the rooms to be better in real life than in the pics I've seen. They feel more like being in a nice apartment. The turntable, record selection and Smeg fridge add to this feeling. The style of the hotel is aimed at a specific type of guest. I'm sure my parents would liken it to a hostel. But if you have a sense of design, an appreciation for resalvaged furniture and like faded grandure, then try it out. The room service menu was delicious - a heavy wooden tray laden with wholesome home cooking. A lot has been written about the lobby. Comments of how it's full of Euro-trash rubber-necking. But to me it felt like leaving your cool apartment, stepping into the lift, and getting out in the middle of a trendy bar. Avoid the designated guest area by the bar, and join the regulars on the huge leather sofas or long wooden school-canteen tables. The gym is great too - sexy, red and black with the feeling of a retro boxing gym. And finally, the location. This was my 15th visit and I know NYC pretty well. I found the midtown location much better than I had anticipated. Instead of being either uptown with the boutiques or downtown with the bars, staying at Ace Hotel sort of makes you feel like being at the heart of the city.

“Ok stay at Double Tree will consider other options next time” Stayed here during the second week of February for a 5 day conference. Called the hotel upon arriving at the airport and waited about 15 minutes for the shuttle to arrive. Rooms are average with older furnishings. The water in the bathroom did not get really hot and would water hammer while taking a shower. I am sure the neighboring rooms liked it. The climate control in the room did not work. Luckily it was cool enough outside I could open a window. Relatively close to gas lamp district and little Italy. About a 15 minute walk down to the harbor. Desk staff was not too friendsly. DId not use the fitness center or pool. There are a lot of hotel options in this area and will definitely consider those when staying in San Diego again.

“Superb new suite hotel.....Excellent Service and decor!” My stay here was extremely enjoyable. I am generally a Marriott fan, however the cost of the Westchase hotels is going through the roof. This all suite hotel is extremely clean, well decorated, full sized kitchen and comformable bed. The closet is a walk in and the sofa is comfortable enough to take a nap on. (Clean too) I will absolutely be back.

“Good option in SF” The hotel is old but good. Great location, next to Market Street, Chinatown, Financial District and the Ferry Building. It's an easy walk to the cable car or the BART. Service is helpful and the people at the frontdesk were nice. There's no free wifi, which is a downside.

“Cannot Handle Big Crowds” I was there during the Alamo Bowl in late December. I was forced to wait 4 hours for my room due to it being 100% full. They promised me it would be only 30-45 minutes. I was also talking to some other guys and all of them had been waiting for as long as I had been. I got to my room, and there were no towels. There service was underloaded for this crowd, and that was very bad. I also waited for my car in the valet for almost an hour. They cannot communicate either. The only things good about the trip were the view of the river walk, the nice open atrium hotel, scenic elevators, and nice rooms. Make sure you see what is going on in San Antonio during your planned vacation, or it will be packed when you get there.

“Runtergekommen, unwissendes Personal” Das Hotel ist selbst fuer ein Holiday Inn schon sehr abgenutzt. Die Zimmer sind karg und klein, die Einrichtung angestaubt. Was aber wirklich stoert ist das unwissende Personal. Uns wurde gesagt es gaebe nur Valet Parking fuer $45 pro Tag. Wir haben dann nebenan selbst geparkt wo uns die Mitarbeiter des Parkhauses mitteilten, dass wir eine reduzierte Parkrate von $25 erhalten als Hotelgaeste.

“Excellent Hotel” There are very few hotels where I give my repeat business to. This is one of them. The staff makes you feel welcome the moment that you check in. They are friendly and knowledgeable. If you aren't an Omni Select Guest member, do sign up. You will get free internet during your stay, a free morning beverage of your choice, and free pressing service, all of which are greatly appreciated. If you are coming in for business and need your sleep, be sure to request a room on the interior side of the hotel. The other side of the hotel is close to 6th Street, and you will hear the noise on the street below well past 3am! The room service is there when they say they will be, and the food is also very good. There have been a few occasions where I have needed a late check-out, and the staff is always very accommodating. I also appreciate the fact that the hotel has off-duty Austin Police officers there on the weekends to make sure that guests only are going on the elevators to the guest rooms.

“Great location, great price, but...” This hotel is really well located right downtown Denver within walking distance to everything you could possibly want. I am a stickler for noise from adjoining rooms and water pressure in the shower. Both fared very well for me - shower pressure wasn't super strong but it was "shower-able" and I didn't hear any neighbors. Here are my pros and cons. Pros: - Great location - Reasonable price - Room was well appointed (I got a remodeled room and it was quite nice). - Speed of room service delivery and other delivery (toothpaste) - Fitness center was much bigger than expected and has really great cardio machines and weights. I was pleasantly surprised. Cons: - I was in town for a conference and when I booked my room online in the "notes" section I put that I would like a quiet room away from vending machines and elevators. When I got there I asked about my room location, I was told that it was right across from the door that had access to the elevators and vending machines. Not very quiet! I arrived well past the check-in time but still had to wait a few hours for my alternate "quiet" room to be cleaned. They didn't read my note, clearly. Nor did they have one other room in the entire hotel available to give me right away that was "quiet" although tons of people checked in after me and they could have swapped my original room with one of theirs. - Bed linen issues. The bottom sheet on my bed wasn't fitted and was way too small for the bed, so I had to basically remake my bed when I pulled the top sheet down. The comforter was put on the bed the wrong way up, with the bottom opening up at the head of the bed. Wouldn't have bothered me except there was nothing that closed the comforter so the comforter cover and the comforter itself were both flapping around my face so I had to turn the whole thing around. And finally, the comforter cover had lots of stains on it. Gross. - Tiny bathroom Overall this is a decent hotel and I would stay again for one or two nights (but not more).

“ottimo non solo come transito” Abbiamo pernottato due notti questa estate: la prima come appoggio per cambio volo, la seconda ci siamo ritornati perchè ci siamo trovati veramente bene. Tutto perfetto: posizione, collegamento con l'aeroporto impeccabile, colazione, stanze con una incredibile vista sulla città. Ben collegato anche con Santa Monica (fermata dell'autobus davanti all'hotel). Buon rapporto qualità-prezzo.

“Perfect for First Time NYC Visitors” I booked this room for free with my Marriott rewards points, so I can't really complain about anything. This is a standard Marriott room (spacious and clean) in the heart of Times Square. It is in an ideal location if you have booked a Broadway show, or any of the Hop On Hop Off double decker buses as both are located just steps away. Central Park, Empire State Building, and Rockefeller Center are also within comfortable walking distance. Subway stops are close as well, so we never had to use a taxi. Though I didn't use it, the TKTS booth is also located just across the street. I probably wouldn't choose to stay here again as being in the middle of Times Square there is just too much hustle and bustle for my taste. However, for first time visitors, I would totally recommend the Marriott Marquis as it is the perfect location for most of the main tourist activities.

“Our Fifth Anniversary Celebration” Due to rising costs of flying, not wanting to be too out of range of our little one, and a smaller budget this year, our fifth anniversary turned out to be just a weekend and not a whole vacation. As a result, we looked for something fun and undone by us. We have shopped and explored downtown Chicago, but never stayed at any of the fabulous hotels. Every brand you can think of (and some you don't know), exist in at least one of the two downtowns Chicago offers. Having experience with Marriott and their excellent location on Michigan Avenue, we decided to try this hotel for location and views. Physically the hotel did not dissapoint, but the service could be improved. When reservations are made on Marriott's website, Marriott sends you and email a few days before called the "Virtual Concierge" which is a way for you to alert the hotel of any special needs you may have (allergic to feather pillows, need a roll-in shower, etc.) and you have a space in which to type up a question or request of your own. I wrote that it was our anniversary and I wanted to surprise my wife with something along the lines of chocolate covered strawberries and wine, etc., and I wanted to know their pricing and what they offered. I never heard back and just assumed that my message did not go through, or that they wouldn't read it until the day I arrived. I figured I could let the concierge know later during my stay. We arrived at the hotel early and since they only published they had valet service for 39 bucks a day, I did not plan on using my car to go anywhere, so I just had valet park it and paid for it. However, there was a sign that said that there was self parking for $26 a day. Again, we were on a budget and it would have been nice to know about that in advance. The carport can only fit about four cars at a time, in a single line, under it, so if you valet parked, you may wait a while for your car. If you self park, you may be able to get to the garage and get out quicker. We were not expecting to be able to check in so early (1pm) to the hotel. The had a long line of people waiting to check out, even though they had brand new check-out kiosks waiting. While waiting, it gave me time to check out their newly completed renovations. The lobby is fabulous! There a lot of tables and chairs around the lobby that surround their brand new 360-degree bar. The bar, from talking to other people, used to be against the far wall, but now is smack dab in the middle. It is gorgeous with a granite bar all the way around it and very fanciful decor. Next the the desk is a little convenience shop with very upscale drinks and snacks, and, on the other side, a small Starbucks Coffee shop. The lobby was always full of people hanging out, getting drinks and generally socializing. The Concierge desk, near the entrance, was busy making reservations, handing out directions and giving out information about the hotel and area. They had convenient mapcards that they handed you with turn by turn directions for both walking and driving. The elevators were fast, contrary to what I've read on other reviews, and there were always six elevators available. I think I rode on everyone. The elevators are very clean and shiny and have ads and a LCD info TV in them (no sound.) Much to our surprise, management must have read our info because they gave us a corner room on the second to top floor with a breathtaking view of the northern downtown skyline, incuding the Hancock Building. The hallways and room are small showing that this is an older hotel with a facelift, but the real telling factor is the water closet. I call it that because it hardly qualifies as a room to be called a bathroom. You have to close the door to get in the tub! However, they did decorate the space very nicely. There is adequate counter space on the granite vanity and nice amenities as well. The room came with a mini-fridge (always gets the room extra points from me) and we requested and received a microwave. There was an adequate desk with internet connection, lamp and stationary on the far wall. The TV was in a TV cabinet with drawers underneath for storage. There was a sliding glass door, a railing but no balcony, which meant that you could only crack the door due to the safety feature installed on the door. There was a wonderful sitting bench in front of the sliding doors so you could enjoy the views. (Pics to be attached.) We went out and my wife surprised the chocalate lover in me by taking me to the Hershey's store and the Ghiradelli Café (both across the street from each other). We enjoyed many treats! After getting a few souveniers, we headed back to the room for some rest and to get ready for dinner. Much to both of our surprise, room service had stopped by and dropped off an amenity of chocolate covered strawberries, white wine, and various cheeses and crackers. It worked out for me because I could play it off like I had had it planned, however, since I never knew if I was paying for it or not, or what the price even was, I was a little irked. However, it did make my wife's day, even if it was a day earlier than our actual anniversary! I went to get a safety deposit box and stood in line for a very long time to get it, and subsequently to get in and out of it due to the long lines. After a while though (and especially on Sunday) I started to wonder why they had two or three agents for a sold out hotel, but eight stations available. Deborah at the front desk was fabulous, though. She was attentive, caring and very bright - one of those employees you wish everyone was modeled like. There was another older lady who was clueless. I remember a guest asked her to check into a king room and she had to ask a supervisor (Deborah) which room to check him into. (Huh?) Either she never had any training, or she just wasn't qualified to do this job. Also, many people were taken out of turn at the front desk so it made some people a little upset. Their gift shop patrons also waited a while to pay when the desk was busy. Sometimes they just left their money and left. Others just put their selections back and would opt for the cheaper Walgreens locations along Michigan Avenue. There is an entrance to the hotel on Michigan, but only a walk-up entrance. The drive up entrance is on the opposite street. The Marriott building itself has several stores in it, but no access to them from inside the hotel, only from the outside sidewalks. Across the street is a fabulous restaurant called Bandera, that the concierge was able to get us squeezed into on Saturday. Atmosphere was unbeatable. I scarfed down the BBQ Salmon with Cilantro Rice - Divine!!!! Live music from some old jazz buddies, and attentive service! Just what we were looking for Valet service was super duper slow! We waited about 30 minutes for our car, and even since it was raining and the carport was so small taxi's, and other vehicles that were not allowed in the carport were coming in anyway because of the rain so their customers did not get wet. Before anyone could leave, you were waiting on the car in front to move. And since traffic was backed up on the street, it was gridlock on Sunday midday! In conclusion, I don't think the staff hate their jobs, I think they are a little jaded from all the complaints they received before and during the renovations. I also think that they are frustrated in trying to work three people's worth of work in one shift, so why should they work hard every single day when obviously ownership of this property is only concerned with his bottom line and not the guest's experience. I can see why there are some negative reviews, but some of them I think are grossly exaggerated. I think that if you stay here you shouldn't expect great service, but just know that you are in prime location and can get a great view! Don't let the staff's downfalls ruin your stay.

“Bad Experience” This hotel was a bad experience from the start. My husband and I booked this hotel for 2 nights to go to a show up at the Hollywood Bowl. We booked this hotel because it seemed fairly new and primarily because it was walkable to the Bowl. At check in, the front desk person asked if we were there for the show. When we said yes, our response was met with frowns and groans because they were dreading the amount of people coming in for the show. We got into our room on the 3rd floor. The room itself was fine as far as hotel rooms go – large bed, clean, decent room. However, the one window we had faced a very close wall that went up to the pool area, making it a very dark room. We had checked in but since it was still early, we thought we might ask if there was a front facing room available just for some light and a view outside. We went to ask and there were 3 people at the front desk - 2 of them were chatting to each other and so I went to the one that was free. When I asked, as nicely as I could prefacing my request by telling him I understood if it wasn’t possible but that I thought I’d check just in case it was, the other 2 who were chatting stopped to listen and rolled their eyes and whispered and made faces at each other – very unprofessional. One of them interjected and told me that there were absolutely no front facing rooms and that ‘what did it matter because I would be at the show all night and I wouldn’t remember the room anyway.’ Well, unfortunately I do remember the room and I also remember their attitudes. As far as sleeping in the room, the air conditioner is noisy and even after we turned ours off, I don’t know if it was other people’s ac’s that we could hear or it was because we were next to the pool that we could hear a constant sort of low rumble. Also, the pillowcases are scratchy and rough. FYI, the levels of this hotel are 2nd floor parking, 3rd floor rooms, 4th floor breakfast area. A very bad layout as we found out as by 6-6:30 am, we were woken by chairs scraping and people’s footsteps back and forth across the floor directly above us from the breakfast area. This continued, obviously getting worse as more people went up for breakfast. Using earplugs, we tried to continue to sleep a bit more, but then had housekeeping knocking on our door about 8 – 8:30! (If you like to sleep a little later, I would suggest putting the ‘do not disturb’ sign on your door before bed.) Due to lack of sleep, I decided to try and take a nap a little later after breakfast only to have what I assume was the person cleaning the breakfast room scraping the chairs very, very loudly and constantly back and forth and back and forth for about an hour and a half. It could have been longer, I gave up on trying to nap and got up and left. The next night was more of the same. The topper for me was the price. This hotel is not cheap. You’d think it was from the experience however. I did not appreciate paying the price I paid for the level of service, the room location, etc. I know hotels in this area are not cheap and I would have happily paid a lot more for a courteous staff and a quiet room. Or I could have gone completely the other way and just stayed in a cheap and noisy hostel if I had known what I was in for. The price here just added insult to injury. All in all, a very bad experience. The hotel has a really bad layout and it’s far too expensive for these kinds of rooms and unprofessional staff. I’m giving it 2 stars because the rooms all by themselves are decent and clean (not taking into account looking out at a wall), it’s just unfortunate that they’re in this hotel. I was very sorry I stayed here and will never again! Pros: Walking distance to Hollywood Bowl, good size rooms Cons: Unprofessional staff, bad layout, noisy noisy noisy, far too expensive for what you do and don’t get

“World Class Service” My wife and I stayed for two nights and were absolutely stunned to find world class service. We have travelled extensively throughout the world and have stayed in all classes of hotels. The staff and facilities of the Fairmont are equal to the leading hotels in major international cities (Hong Kong, New York, Seoul, San Francisco, Miami, Las Vegas etc.) We were given a complimentary upgrade to the Gold Floor and the already exquisite stay got even better. The location (four blocks to Georgetown or METRO) was perfect for exploring the city, shopping and night life. Aboslutely recommended.

“Un hotel confortable et calme” Nous avons passé 4 nuits dans l'hotel Hilton Backbay avec deux adultes et deux adolescents. L'hotel est bien placé, proche de Newbury street de du métro. La chambre était confortable et relativement grande. Le service est efficace mais l'acceuil est peu chaleureux. La piscine est convenable et appréciable pour les enfants. Les lits queen sont un peu petits. Eviter à tout prix le petit déjeuner à l'hotel qui est hors de prix. Le parking est aussi très cher.

“Not up to par” I agree with the May 6 reviewer, who wrote "Although the hotel wasn't far from Cherry Creek it felt a world away. The neighboorhood was not dangerous but was borderline. It probably wouldn't be appropriate to walk outside the grounds alone at night. " Indeed. The place looks tired, its Tuscany theme is tired, and it is time to join the 21st century. This is a business hotel, and its competition is way ahead of it. My room was outdated, somewhat worn (though clean), and the TV was ancient compared to the flat-screens I have recently seen in comparable hotels. It is time for a full scale renovation, Loews! Even the woodwork in the elevator (not to mention the faux Tuscan mural in the elevator lobby) look cheesy. I ate in the Tuscan Bar for dinner and the food was OK, but the service, if friendly, was inept (note to Loews: servers should speak SOME English). The woman at the front desk who checked me in was lovely, though, and the VIP lounge on the top floor was a nice touch (I was able to print my boarding pass for my return flight via the internet). All in all, somewhat of a disappointment.

“Great hotel!” Had to come here for a business conference, and the facilities were excellent. We were lucky enough to upgraded to a governors suite room, which was absolutely huge (room 2920). 180 degree views on the 29th floor, bedroom, lounge and bathroom - with a touch of Art Deco. Bed was great and the bathroom very spacious. The Sole Food bar was good for breakfast and on a Thursday night they had a jazz band for happy hour and boy was there a great buzz and lots of people! All of the staff was extremely helpful and friendly. It is also in a great location to walk to all of the tourist sites and it is next door to Macy's which is very handy indeed. Would definitely come back here again!

“Excellent moderately priced hotel” This is the best place we've found near our relatives. We had a very reasonable rate the Friday night after Thanksgiving, probably because of low demand due to the holiday, given all the medical facilities nearby. Although the immediate area looks like a vast wasteland of medical buildings, if you drive north a couple of miles and turn right on Carmel Drive (first light after Max & Erma's), you will find an excellent Meijer's (groceries & more) as well as many places to eat. Our room was clean and attractive, with a king bed, sofa & coffee table, desk & chair, drawers under the TV, and a wardrobe (instead of a closet). The fridge was across from the sink, and the toilet and shower/tub in a comparatively large room of their own. (If there was a microwave, I missed it.) Amenities include nice soap, shampoo, & conditioner. Towels not luxurious but served our needs. I rather appreciated the lack of placards cluttering up the sink area. The carpeting looked extremely clean! The fitness area has weights, a bench, an elliptical, and a treadmill plus towels and drinking water.

“Just like a basic apartment that needs some touch ups. 1 bdrm good for families” This was our 2nd time at the Affinia 50. Came back because having the kitchen and living room really helps us (mom, dad, 6 and 8 year old) spread out and save $ on meals. This time around the kitchen was tiny (yet functional). The furniture was showing some age. The corner bedroom had 2 walls of windows. The TV was placed on a wall to the right of the bed. Making it impossible to watch without a neck ache. The room connected to a very sad balcony with to tattered chairs. The $14 a day WiFi was very slow. The evening pretzels and wine are a nice time to hang out with other guests as there is no restaurant or bar in the hotel. As my kids get older I will probably stay at a nicer hotel with better amenities for the same price.

“Good Value” We've just spent three nights at the Holiday Inn Express & Suites in San Antonio. This is a good value hotel close to the city centre. It's not directly on the Riverwalk but only a ten min walk or alternatively the hotel runs a complimentary shuttle bus to and from the corner of the river centre every hour (be warned that the last bus back to the hotel at night is at 9:45pm so you will have to walk or get a taxi if you want to enjoy San Antonio's nightlife). We were satisfied with our suite - it contained all the basics needed for our stay. Our room was on the front of the hotel and my partner's complaint was the noise!!! The hotel is situated very near to the train station and trains frequently travel through the city and for some reason sound their horns on the approach to the station for what seems like forever. This goes on late into the night and starts again early in the morning. I didn't hear them but then I sleep like a log. My partner was disturbed everytime! Hotel has usual fare for HI Express breakfast - the hours for breakfast could be extended a little and they don't hang about when it comes to clearing everything away. Hotel has a small pool and whirlpool out the back - the water in the pool was freezing and we had to chase the sun round the pool to avoid the mainly shady areas. Hotel has a guest laundry ($1 for both the washer and dryer) which was very handy. Overall I would recommend this hotel for visiting San Antonio but if you prefer to be in the centre of things you will need to chose a hotel located on the Riverwalk and for that you have to pay more!!! Just down the road from the hotel is a Ruth's Chris Steak House - we ate there one evening - excellent meal! Also ate at the Little Rhein Steak House on the Riverwalk - again I would recommend this restaurant for its location and atmosphere. While in San Antonio you have to take a boat ride on the river ... typical tourist activity but worth it to soak in the ambience of the city.

“Decent Stay” The reviews on here are so mixed, I had no idea what to expect. First let me say I got the rooms on Priceline for $100 a night, so I thought it was an incredible bargain. Second, the staff at this hotel is EXTREMELY friendly and accommodating. Everyone spoke to us as we came in the hotel and as we left. Even the cleaning staff was inordinately friendly. They were also extremely accommodating about storing our bags for a late departure. The hotel is very clean -- at least our room was. The room looked a little worn, but certainly nothing unsightly. The beds were comfortable, and altough the room (with two double beds) was not large, it was certainly not tiny by the standards of a crowded big city. It was also quiet -- we could not hear other rooms or outside (we were at the back of the hotel). The lobby is small and the lighting makes it look really weird, but their are computers down there, where we were able to check our light and print our boarding passes. The location of the hotel is also great -- at the "north" tip of Chelsea, so easily walkable to Chelsea but also the Flatiron District and even lower mid-town east. This is not a fancy hotel, but for our purposes, it was really perfect.

“Great out of city hotel” This is a fairly typical Hampton, which is not too far out of Baltimore and has plentiful shopping and dining opportunities immediately around it. The hotel is not the newest of properties but the front desk staff were incredibly helpful, the room was clean and the stay was very comfortable. There is also a small business centre. We'd certainly stay here again.

“One of the best airport hotels in the country!” This hotel connects to DFW airport by the airport train and shuttle, located in D terminal. It is very new, modern, high end, stylish, etc. Very nice, clean, modern rooms. Great lobby bar, restaurant, lounge. Amazing service! One of the few hotels that I actually might consider staying at if I wasn't actually using the airport! Stay here if you are coming/going through DFW airport.

“Spacious suite with bad connecting door” Stayed for one night before making the connecting flight next day. Got upgraded to a queen bed suite. The room was spacious but the connecting door to another room was so thin and poorly fitted that I can hear everything next door. Otherwise the hotel is nice and clean, its personnel was gracious. I will stay there again next time I travel through IAH but will not take that suite unless the connecting door is fixed.

“Not if a non-smoking room is important to you” The Blakely has potential to be an excellent hotel, but in my opinion it has a fatal flaw; a reservation does not guarantee a non-smoking room; this "amenity" is treated as a request, the same as asking for a particular room or view. When my husband and I checked in for a 3-night stay on November 10, we were shown to a room which assaulted our senses with the stench of cigarette smoke. Thinking it was a mere oversight, we called the desk to change rooms, only to be told that the hotel was sold out and the only available rooms were smoking. Furthermore, we were told that although the room could be changed in the morning, we would have to "check-out by noon and could not have the new room until 3 PM." It was late and we were too tired to find another hotel, so we reluctantly stayed in the smoking room with an ionizer provided by housekeeping, which did little but make noise. The next day, a non-smoking room materialized in the morning and the rest of of stay was pleasant. Management confirmed several times however, that "non-smoking" is a "request," not an assured "room-type," so I would not return to The Blakely unless this policy changed, nor recommend it to anyone who desires a non-smoking room.

“Great service” Stayed one night for a wedding so received a discounted rate of $89.00 which was great. Overall hotel was fine. Room was average; showing a little wear. Bathroom fairly small as is typical for city hotels. Bed was comfortable with nice linens. I don't think I would have paid full price as there are probably better values. I have to say Hyatt does have excellent customer service. It really does stand out. Everyone is very friendly and helpful. The food at the reception was very, very good. They did a nice job with this. Also had the breakfast buffet the next morning and it was very good also. Although a little pricey at $20.00 each. They did have cooked to order omelets and a nice assortment of other hot and cold items. Service, again, was excellent. The location is next to Chinatown on one side and downtown crossing (shopping area) on the other. Some may think the area is not all that great. But most of Boston is old and somewhat dirty. It is one of the country's oldest cities and it shows. Not to discourage you because there is a lot to see and a lot of history here. If you can get a good price this is a convenient location to see the sights.

“Many good stays here” I stay here a lot and figured I would give an update to my first review which was basically useless. This hotel is in a great location. It is clean, modern and service is great. Bring earplugs if you are a light sleeper- the sound proofing in this hotel is not the best. You will ample road noise and sirens for the emergency room, you might also hear other guests talking or partying in rooms nearby. I will continue to stay here because it's walking distance of where I need to be. There is also a decent gym, but I could not find any disinfecting wipes for machines. Yuck!

“The good news: no cockroaches” This is a hard hotel to review. There isn't really anything wrong, but I just didn't find anything about it that would make me want to go back, there are much better options right around the corner. The hotel is trying very hard to be hip, but seems to miss the details. The music in the lobby is so overpowering I don't know how the staff can stand to be there all day. Reception was efficient once I got the attention of one of the three people who were standing behind the desk looking self important. The bar is a cave, and hosted by someone who thought reading the newspaper was more important than helping actual customers, and who told me to "hurry" at 11:15 since she was closing at midnight! The room was actually a bit larger than I expected and the free ISDN was welcome. The tiny bathroom seemed to be deliberately laid out to make in impossible to put my things anywhere without them falling on the floor, the towel rack fell off the wall. The most puzzling thing is how they managed to put the shower controls behind the overhead shower. There was no way to turn on the shower and adjust the temperature without standing under the shower head. What were they thinking! I had to call to ask for bathtowels, which were missing from the room, which did arrive quickly. Later, someone came to leave a bathrobe. I pointed out that I didn't need once since I was WEARING IT, but she left another one anyway. Strange. My room was quiet, since I was at the rear of the hotel and I didn't hear any corridor noise at all. No bugs. Not a bad place to stay and I can't give it a bad review, I just think that for the price I'll go back to the Kitano next time.

“Very nice” Great location across from Southpark Mall. Hotel is modern and the staff is very friendly. Had a balcony room on the 7th floor, it's nice being able to have some fresh air in the room. Very comfortable bed. The only down side of the bed were the fitted sheets that keep coming off of the top corners of the mattress. Obviously the sheets are too small for the pillow top mattresses. Wifi was abosolutely horrible. Since we are Marriott Rewards members, Wifi is complimentary. Would have been upset if we paid the $12.95 a day for the sloooowwww connection. Everything is very clean and love the flavored water they offer in the lobby, especially the lime with mint. Yum. In the lobby in the evening they offer complimentary drinks 1 night a glass of red wine the next mango bellini. Concierge club breakfast the same each morning, oatmeal, scrambled eggs, bacon plus pastries, however, the room was extremely too cold! Could not eat fast enough, felt like you were in a freezer. Would stay here again if in this area of Charlotte.

“one complaint-nightly street noise” Stayed here 4 nights with my husband who was here on business. We loved everything about the hotel except for our 11th floor Broadway facing suite was extremely noisy at night. We heard all the street noise even with earplugs. I would not recommend staying below floor 25. Also the fitness center could be more well equipped with workout strength training machines. Other we had a great stay. Very convenient location, but not your quiet part of town. The suite was great with great views of the marquee lights. Concierge staff and bellmen were very helpful.

“Away from the Riverwalk” Stayed at the San Antonio Marriott for staff training. Staff courteous and pleasant, rooms spacious and clean. Unfortunately the meeting room was small and cramped and temperature was difficult to regulate. Internet access is not free (this is truly a minus). The location was also not the greatest for which it would not be my first choice for lodging. The breakfast buffet was a bit expensive (more than the lunch meal).

“Impressed for the time staying at springhill suites” This is first time I have stayed in this type of hotel and I have to say that I was impresses with the cleanliness, size of the room and service. Breakfast is always good when it is complimentary and hot items are served. I actually think it is better than Hampton inn. I felt that I was staying in a small but updated condo building. By the way free wifi and business center, pool and g. I will come back again I I am near the airport

“Acceptable renovated older hotel + great location” We stayed two nights at L'Enfant Plaza for a conference meeting, rooms booked by the organization. Mixed tripadvisor reviews reflect the fact that this is an older property with varied levels of renovation: the lobby is modern and upscale; the floors above left to look much older. My experience was perfectly acceptable with more than adequate levels of cleanliness and comfort. • The room: Room size was Huge, the largest hotel room I have ever encountered, the effect intensified by very little furniture – carpet and furnishings fairly old but good repair. Besides the central space, there was a large dressing room and separate sink area. Bathroom fixtures were perfectly okay and kept clean, hot water constant and decent lighting. Bed comfortable, linens and towels acceptable. Old TV with okay cable package. Climate control was adequate for the mild May weather; not sure how it would stand up to real Washington heat. • Location: because of its age, this hotel must have lower rates available, which makes it a bargain for tourists who want to be walking distance from the major sights and who are nervous about using Washington's excellent subway. The hotel is a short walk from the Mall w/ all major museums and the Capitol. • For travellers who want to make the most of a short visit and walk to major museums and government buildings, this hotel (with a good rate) can be a bargain. But be aware that parking (adjacent underground garage) is $40/24 hours.

“Decent for the Price” Clean place, friendly staff. Very good free breakfast selections with eggs, sausage, biscuits, gravy, etc. Average free manager's reception Monday thru Thursday with heavy snacks, soft drinks and wine (no beer!). Surroundng area is not the greatest but not that bad either. A few restaurants close by and a Thai restaurant right across the street that had great food! Bed was average but the pillows need to go. Lumpy and cheap. On a budget or simply like a few extras for a good price? Stay here no problem. Would stay again for the price.

“Good deal” We booked this hotel to visit the Alamo City for a few days. After the $24 taxi ride from the airport, the front desk was efficient and friendly. Our room was clean, prepared, and fully stocked. The hotel had plenty of pamphlets with things to do and coupons. The location was just right for a young couple like us. There was a restaurant in the hotel (which we did not take advantage of), a convienence store across the street, a bus stop next to the hotel, Market Square (an authentic Mexican Market with a flea market across the way) was two blocks away, and less than a mile to the Riverwalk. Our stay was problem-free. Check-out was efficient as well and the concierge drove us to the airport for half the price as the taxi!

“OK, but nothing fabulous” Stayed here for 10 nights, with high expectations based on the previous reviews. The room was adequate, although nothing special, and it had a "cheap" feel to it(price was not that cheap). The desk chair did not adjust to the correct height, and the internet cable was too short, making it difficult to work. I noticed that despite having a non smoking room, on a non smoking floor, there was a smell of smoke in the kitchen area. It seemed like my vent was connected to that of a smoking room. This suspicion was confirmed when at lunchtime one day there was a smell of frying. Bed was comfortable and other facilities worked OK. The gym was laughable. It contained the following: - 1 Treadmill – working - 1 Treadmill – broken - 1 Cycling machine – working - 1 Cycling machine – broken - 1 Stepping machine – half working - A few free weights I did not go to the pool. Breakfast was un impressive, although this was less important as every room has a kitchen. Staff were generally pleasant and courteous throughout. Would stay here in an emergency but will try somewhere else next time.

“Good Location, but OK Rooms” I have stayed at this hotel twice now, mainly because of its excellent location in the financial district. The rooms are small, but clean. Be sure to ask for a room away from the El trains, otherwise you will be kept awake from the trains rumbling past. I think this this a fine hotel, but the room rate seems inexplicably high.

“Very pleasant” This is my third Fairmont and certainly the best so far. Like all Fairmont hotels (as far as I can tell) the bathroom was surprisingly small; however, the bedroom was huge, especially for the miserly $279/nt that I paid for it. The rooms are as dully conservative as you would expect for a business hotel of this type, but they are at least tasteful and up-to-date, not to mention immaculately maintained. The hotel's restaurants and bars are very pleasant and the staff are efficient and charming. There is nothing extraordinary about this hotel, but it is a pleasant place to spend a night or two.

“Updated public areas, still good” I have stayed many times over the years and the public areas left wome to be desired. They have now been improved, with more striking colors and slightly more places to sit. The restaurant is a hot restaurant, which creates a problem if you want to have a glass of wine in a quiet bar, better find somewhere else. The rooms are good, comfortable bed and crisp white sheets, well done bathrooms, bathrobes, good storage and working space. I strongly urge they improve the bedside lighting however since the lights are difficult to move for good reading. It is also time to begin updating the rooms some. The small kitchens with coffee and refrigerator is always welcome. All in all I usually choose the Benjamin in NY, for location and comfort and I have ALWAYS found the service cheerful and helpful.

“excellent” I usually stay at more budget accomodations, but those options are limited in downtown seattle, so stayed here for $75 after bidding on priceline. Pros - very new very clean hotel staff was very friendly shuttle to downtown locations - Pike place, cruise ships, train station, etc... proximity to stadiums for games (baseball+football) Cons lack of restaraunts/shops close to hotel pricey hotel restaraunt area right around hotel was somewhat industrial (train whistles at night)

“Refreshingly different.” I loved this hotel! I stayed for business and found the trendy decor and large plush rooms a pleasure to come back to after a long day. This is not your cookie cutter hotel . It offers cosy duvet's on the bed and W style decor but rooms that are double the size. High service touches included gourmet cookies provided with turndown and each morning providing an East Coast paper for this East Coast Resident (the New York Times). I was reluctant to stay at the hotel given some negative reviews but had no choice as other hotels were booked out. I'm so glad I stayed and shall definitely return.

“continues to go down hill” Let's start with the good. Great location if you need to be at the convention center. The hotel itself continues to go downhill as does the staff. Check-in is always a challange ( staff turn-over) and the rooms were updated 4-5 years ago when the converted from a hilton but have not aged well. TV's are wall mounted ( they don't move and are too small for room size 32"). The furnishings are circa 1998, the tubs are pitted with rust showing thru. The A/C units are window mounted AKA motel 6 style, which cant keep the rooms cool during 85 degree days and are very loud. As a platinum member they offer access to the concierge lounge which offers free beverages ( beer/wine) for 3 hrs every evening is a nice touch, but doesn't make up for the poor overall condition of the property and below average staff. If you get a great deal, give it a try.

“Great little hotel in good location” Stayed at the Jury's Normandy Hotel in December 2008 with my Mum. As soon as we arrived, we were made to feel very welcome and it seemed very homely. The room had two ultra comfy double beds and had been freshly painted. The lovely, clean bathroom had the most enormous shower cubicle I'd ever seen. Easy walk to Dupont Circle and good city to walk around. Not so easy walk back up to the hotel after a day of walking, but nice to collapse in the comfy bed. No internet facilities on site, but could use business centre at the nearby Courtyard Marriott for free. Unfortunately the hotel was mid-renovation when we stayed and there were no laundry facilities. Housekeeping however, helped us out and did our laundry for us. Very nice of them. For food, try La Tomate near Dupont Circle for good Italian food and Thaiphoon on S Street for good Thai. Would definitely stay at Jury's Normandy again. Fabulous city and great hotel. Highly recommend.

“Good location but thats it, DISAPPOINTING” My wife and i chose this hotel because we have had great experiences in the past with Kimpton Hotels (DC & Vancouver). The location was conveniently located close to Grand Central but other than that, theres not much else in the area. The bad: my wife and i went to breakfast at the Silverleaf Tavern and the hostess was too busy to acknowledge us, so we sat ourselves. When she finally came over to greet us, she asked us if we had the "discount vouchers for breakfast". I assumed it something to do with being an "IN TOUCH" member with that plus I also received an envelope on arrival. So i inquired if i was suppose to receive that from the front desk during check in, she said "yes" and directed me to the front desk. when i inquired about it @ the front desk, the girl was rude and unattentive. instead of explaining to me that the breakfast voucher option was a prepaid choice during booking, she rudely denied me a voucher with no explanation. we were hungry so it stayed for breakfast anyways. service was terrible and the "buffet" was limited with very few options. the server never came to refresh my coffee or offer us a refill on OJ. To my surprise the bill was $64+ a 18% gratuity was added. RIDICULOUS!!!!!!! The rooms were small and lacked lighting. I've stayed in dozens of hotels in Manhattan and i expect the rooms to be smaller but when you chose Kimpton Hotels, you expect a certain standard. This hotel does not meet the expectations of Kimpton name. Wine reception: was served a dirty glass twice. one had lipstick on it still. Checkout was slow and unorganized and door attendants were unhelpful with our bags. I doubt i'll return.

“okay” Overall, we were very satisfied with our stay. The hotel is very nice; not only is it clean and well maintained, but you can tell that they often upgrade amenities and services to stay competitive. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking to stay in Detroit

“Nice Hotel, but poor Managemnet in a Crisis” Bear in mind that there are few cheap NY Hotels and the ones that are cheap are normally substandard. The New Yorker is mid-priced by NY standards. It’s a very nice Art Deco Hotel is an excellent central location – within walking distance of the Empire State Building, the Post office, Penn station and Madison Square Garden. Our room was not enormous but perfectly adequate and clean. The décor and furniture was ‘sound’ and not 'well worn' like many NY Hotels. The Hotels 24 hour ‘Tick Tock’ café was nice but overpriced like most hotels cafes are. I have two gripes: the business centre only has two Internet PC’s (chargeable). I stayed in NY as an ‘Ash refugee’ (flight delays due to the Icelandic volcano) and there were queues to use theses PC’s all hours of the day. I initially booked two nights accommodation. I quickly realised that I would be stuck in NY for nine nights. I tried to book more nights on day one of my stay and was refused. I was told to return to the reception on day two. I was then refused on day two and told to return on the morning of day three (my check-out morning). This was obviously frustrating for me because I wanted to know if I could stay all week or would need to seek alternative accommodation, before I had to pack. Therefore on day two I used the Internet/Expedia UK to book more nights. I presented the confirmation paperwork to the reception desk. The guy said “fine, but if you booked through them I may have got a cheaper rate!” I explained that I had asked twice and not been allowed to. He said “that was odd, they were not fully booked”. So I give the Hotel management one star but the hotel four stars. (If the Manager is reading this, I would love them to explain this strange policy to me)

“Russian Roulette” I booked a lengthy stay and requested a quiet room. Before I arrived I confirmed that I was getting a quiet room (I'd even agreed to downgrade from what I had purchased to get a courtyard room.) On arrival, I should have known something was wrong when I saw a large "white noise" machine next to the bed. Every ten minutes or so, the room would rattle and there would be a grinding sound. This went on all night. After 2 sleepless nights, I complained. The management said I could move but that "check in is at 3pm". They knew the problem right away--the room was next to electrical equipment and the elevator. They knew exactly what they were doing when they put me there. I have to think it was because I purchased through Expedia, because when I confirmed the reservation they said "Oh, I see you used Expedia." Anyway, most of the rooms abut the Embarcadero, which is a six lane highway. This is not a quiet hotel. The room service is limited and expensive. A simple order of a 16 oz. container of coffee is $19--after mandatory tip, service charges and tax. There is almost no storage space--no drawers for clothing, just some hanging space. The neighborhood is the financial district, which is dead on the weekend. I've stayed in SF dozens of times, and thought I'd try something different. Never again--why play Russian Roulette with your vacation.

“Decent Hotel - Good Value” We stayed here Labor Day weekend - couldn't beat the price of $180 per night through their website for a decent NYC hotel. Upon arrival was given a room on the "C" level which involved taking an elevator down one flight from the ground floor lobby. Although this room had a coutyard patio we found it dark and kind of creepy so they moved us to the lobby level which was a little better. Friendly staff, nice lobby and good breakfast. Room was fairly large for NYC standards but very drab color scheme. Very convenient to South Street Seaport and a short walk to the subway. Would not be my first choice in the area but would stay again if the room had the same value.
“Loved this hotel” Great hotel. Breakfast and evening munchies included. Quiet, scenic, great room layout. Very cozy decor. Exceptionally clean. Great value.

“Great value for a convenient location” While there is nothing spectacular about the Sheraton Manhattan, it is a decent hotel that is surprisingly spacious (by NYC standards). It's your run of the mill older hotel that has seen better days but you can't beat the location and especially the value (~$150/night). The lobby is average and there's a restaurant/bar in it that's ok to have a drink. There's a nice bar (Rosie O'Grady's) across the street and there's a convenience store nearby to grab cheaper priced beverages and snacks. I've stayed at hotels in NYC that are comparable to this one at roughly twice the price point though, so overall, this isn't a bad hotel at all.

“You get what you pay for” This is the second time I stayed here, primarily because of it's proximity to my job. It's a Red Roof, not a Hilton, just a Red Roof. The location of the property is great for restaurants and it's not too far for San Antonio's attractions. I got "clean" in the shower and I slept in the bed. That's enough about that. They offer a shuttle service to the attractions and the airport. Basic continental breakfast with a Texas-shaped waffle. Swimming pool looks enticing, but it's not my thing. No complaints, I'd do it again.

“it was just ok, not one of the better quality inns I've stayed at...” I'm into much simpler designed hotels. This one looks like someones grandmother got stoned and went to town with a heavy handed traditional approach. It had a bit of a weird smell in the halls as well. The room wasn't bad once you got in. It just wasn't one of my favorite Quality Inns and I've seen quite a few all over the country.

“Not great, but could have been given a little attention.” I booked this hotel because I had a early morning flight out of Boston and otherwise would have been commuting from New Hampshire. The location was great and very close to public transportation. The hotel is currently under construction and you have to take an elevator to the lobby then an elevator to your room. Check in was quick, easy, friendly, and my request for hypoallergenic room had been honored with no problem. My room was #1609 which had a lovely view of the city. Very large room for Boston's standards. The furnishings look to be on the newer side and are in good condition. The bed was reasonably comfortable but nothing to write home about. The floors were very dirty, both in the room and the bathroom. The shower tile was mildewed. The bathroom lighting was very dim. I retired early, but was awakened by a rowdy bunch of men around 9:30pm. Security responded to my and others complaints several times during the night. So much for getting a good night's rest before my flight. Thankfully, they did have earplugs provided for guests in the night stand.

“Buono” Ho soggiornato in questo hotel dal 24 al 28 settembre 2012. Non mi posso lamentare se penso allo standard americano. Questo hotel di 4 stelle (ma se fosse in Europa sarebbe di 3) si trova vicino a Central Park, ed a 2/3 km da Manhattan. Io ho prenotato tramite il sito 3 giorni prima della partenza una camera al 14o piano con vista su NY, anche se in realta la vista era su di un cantiere aperto allo stesso mio piano dove al mattino alle ore 7:00 la squadra di operai cominciava il lavoro! Prenotando vicino alla partenza ho monitorato il prezzo della camera pagando il 30% in meno, ma comunque rimane sempre un prezzo alto se si considera che la 1a colazione non e' inclusa. La camera comunque era bella ed anche il bagno e soprattutto pulita con cambio asciugamani giornaliero e prodotti da bagno. La colazione pagandola al momento costava circa 10$ + tasse, ma non era quel granche'. Meglio fare colazione nei negozi che si trovano sulle strade (+ economici e con prodotti + freschi). L'hotel si trova a metaà strada fra 2 fermate della metropolitana linea rossa. Inoltre di fronte all'hotel si trovano 2 societa' di noleggio auto. Il ristorante SERAFINA dell'hotel vorrebbe essere stile italiano...pizze e paste non sono malvagie, il prezzo e' nella norma

“Excellent Value and Great Location” I could not find a room in Chicago so I "settled" for the Fairfield Inn on Orchard in downtown, one block off the Magnificent Mile. The staff was super fast and friendly. The suite was large and very clean. The room was quiet and everything worked. I got a great rate (well under $200) and I will now stay there rather than the more expensive hotels around the corner. I had to give up nothing! A great value and location.

“Really comfortable stay, Friendly staff & Excellent service. TRY IT!!!!” Just returned from a 4 night stay at the W. It was really a very comfortable hotel with excellent facilities and very friendly staff. I had been worried after reading the previous reviews but was very glad that my stay was great throughout. The location is excellent, so central and easy to get to anywhere from. The conceirge were so helpful and knowledgeable about everything. the Restaurant, Heartbeat, was truly exceptional. I eat our regularly and enjoy good food and i would have to say that my meal was one of the best i have ever had. The Spa was closed for refurbishment during my stay but the new spa, Bliss, is on its way. They had lovely Bliss toiletries in the rooms as a foretaste of whats to come. Whiskey Blue is a busy bar which tends to attract a trendy crowd, however this shouldnt stop anyone as the drinks are great and the music even better. Yes the rooms are a bit on the small side, but if you want a bigger room upgrade to a suite. It is New York after all and space is at a premium wherever you look. All in all this was a great hotel in a great location. I would definatley stay there again and some of its more quirky touches such as the fresh grass pots etc in the lobby are a novel and fun idea. Give it a try.

“Awesome place!!!” We loved the location of this hotel!! Amazing pool and bar right on the bay. I took a nice walk along the bay and sat on the sand and watched the gorgeous sunset. Very relaxing! The restaurant was quite good. Sat outside and it was very enjoyable. The best was the hot tub with views of the bay and pool drink and food service-thoroughly enjoyed the beers and burger we split!! The room was decent. Unfortunately, we had a view of the freeway, so ask for a room with a better view. Very quiet sleeping, so that was nice. The room was updated.

“Wonderful room and friendly staff!” This was our second time staying at Hyatt Place JAX and it was just as nice as the first. The staff is EXTREMELY friendly and almost encourage you to hang out in the lobby and make yourself at home. I love the fresh smell of the place when you first walk in -- the lobby is very nice with comfortable chairs, business center, and small restaurant. The rooms here are HUGE with a very unique sectional pullout sofabed. Also this hotel offers rooms with 2 queen beds which are so much more desireable to us than rooms with two doubles. The only downside to this hotel, which I think is similar to all Hyatt Place hotels, is that the breakfast selection is very unimpressive. They sell better things from their cafe, but the "free" selection is pretty poor. That's my only suggestion that would make Hyatt Place a nicer place to stay. Other than that, I really like this place...it is surrounded by every kind of dining and shopping you could want! It is one of my two favorite places to stay in Jacksonville, the other being the Hampton Inn & Suites on Southside Blvd. If you're in the northern part of the city or near the airport, look no further than Hyatt Place!!

“The not so upgraded experience” This hotel is beautiful and has lots of history. The rooms are pretty with classic beauty. (not incredibly fancy). In my personal experience the main problem with this hotel is the lack of motivation, dedication and customer focus from all the staff. The Ugly I had to open my own door and drag my luggage from the cab to registration while bellstaff and porter spent their time conversing. I had to drag my luggage to the executive level (The upgraded experience). I arrived into a room of medium size and average amenities only to find a toilet which had been used and not flushed. The fermentation caused for fetid gases to float all around me My room also had a desk with a white crust that I could scratch out with my nail. lots of it (food perhaps). On my closet door I noticed a few stains of what appeared to be dried blood. I notified my "special" concierge in my "special" floor of the problems and requested his help in addresing the issues while I went out for dinner. Upon my return I walked into the same nightmare. When I approached him again he offered an alternate room and gave me a key if I wanted to go take a look prior to relocating. This one had lovely long hairs in the room evidence of a prior guest with a lush mane... When I requested the opportunity to talk to a Manager on Duty I was told by my "special" concierge that they did not have one. Finally he located someone from the front desk who assisted with finding me a clean room. I am now in my clean room enjoying rather comfortable linens, I took a bath in my clean bathroom with a missing shower mat or rug. the water pressure was low but the water was sufficiently hot. To be continued... I still have 5 more days

“Of course I love it. It's a Kimpton!” It's just hard to go wrong with a Kimpton hotel and the Rouge was no different. I think I may have found my new go-to hotel in DC. The Rouge is very trendy and has a fun vibe. And the location is fantastic. You are within a 5-10 minute walk of both Dupont Circle and U Street. I was traveling solo and felt very safe walking in the neighborhood. I will be sure to stay at the Rouge on my next DC trip!

“Very nice room!” I stayed here for business because the conference hotel was sold out. I was glad because I think the rooms here are better than the other location! The room is spacious with a really nice work area and the bed was SO comfortable! I would recommend this hotel and would stay here again if in the area. The only downside was the food and drinks were very, very expensive.

“2PM checkout...attentive service...comfy bed.” We stayed here based on reviews on TripAdvisor and their 2pm checkout..which is something I've never heard of. We were uprgraded to a king loft on check in, but they apparently upgrade alot as we overheard others who were upgraded. Front & bell staff were always friendly and attentive. The room had a musty ordor which didn't give you a good first impression when you came in the door. The room is in a contemporary style...like an upscale IKEA. It was very clean and well-maintained. The bed was very comfortable and we slept well. The media room in the king loft (check it out on their website) is a great idea. It's like big couch with a wall projector T.V. Unfortunately it didn't work and maintenance couldn't fix it and we didn't use it. The hotel also has a "intimacy kit" in the wet bar (for purchase) that had a massager (read vibrator), lubricant, & condoms. This is something I've never seen in a hotel...ever!! That combined with the media room, this places makes for quite the love nest!! Free water in room! Pros: Clean great staff interesting decor turn down, robes, & slippers 2pm checkout close to Starbucks, shopping, & restaurants dimmers on bathroom lights (DW told me to add this) quiet Cons: musty odor in room (hopefully it was only this one) maintenance issues (our clock radio broke as well) sliding style bathroom door was sticky and difficult to close expensive room service Overall, I'd stay here again.

“Horrendous parking” We stayed here for only one night since we didn't want to pay for the Hilton when we flew in so late. We got it for $70/night on Priceline. The parking deck is very poorly designed. You'll see all the scratches on the walls from cars hitting them. If you have a car bigger than a compact, don't bother coming here. You won't be able to maneuver. The room iself is very average. Bathroom is tiny. It's a good place if you plan on sleeping and leaving first thing in the morning. Pool is decent size, but too cold to swim now. And if you're not used to hearing noise, you'll be up all night with the planes overhead. Didn't bother us, since we live in a city. They have breakfast in the morning that consists of fruit, muffins, bread, cereals and other things like that. Nothing special. Overall, stay here if you just need a place to crash for the night. We spent the remainder of our time at the Hilton San Diego resort and loved it.

“Very nice downtown hotel.” Exactly what I expected from a Fairmont Hotel. Helpful, friendly staff. Beautiful, spacious suite (they had no rooms for common folk like me and had to upgrade me!).
