My only nit was some pipes (I guess) that were banging nearby (I was in Room 400). Not enough to keep me from sleeping, but would have been annoying had I stayed more than one night. I'll definitely stay here again.

“Second time at this wonderful hotel- No need to look elsewhere” I had the pleasure of returning to Chicago for business and as my first experience with this Hotel was great- I decided to return again. So glad i did. This is a beutiful boutique hotel in the perfect location near all downtown attractions. State/Rush Street, Business disctrict, Dining, Shopping etc.. The staff at the Indigo are wonderful and helpful. Early check in, great rooms the entire experience is great.
“典型的ヒルトンです” ボストンの中でも便利な立地で、地下鉄の駅にも近いです。 ボストン観光の拠点にはよいと思いました。 駐車場が併設されている数少ないホテルですので、ドライブ旅行には最適です。 ただレートは高いです。

“appreciated the upgrade” have stayed here multiple ties as it's where a regular meeting i attend is held. But that said, the location in downtown is really good and it's very easy to get around the city from here as multiple subway lines are close by. I was upgraded to Gold status which meant i had free internet (brilliant- but i hate paying for internet!) and breakfast in the executive lounge which looks over the river and the statue of liberty. My room was also on a very high floor with the same view, which was much appreciated, given almost my whole stay was in the conference rooms which have zero character and no windows.

“Nice Rooms” Stayed at the Sheraton for 2 nights during Easter. I am a SPG platinum and was upgraded to a suite with a lake view. Beautiful room, nice shower with hot water and nice water pressure. Nice health club with sauna and separate locker rooms. The club room was huge, largest I have seen at a Starwood Property. The only complaint was someone's room service tray was sitting by our door when we got there and was still there when we checked out 2 days later.

“Excellent value” I was delayed in Denver because of a cancelled flight, and ended up at the airport La Quinta. It is a great bargain hotel - immaculately clean with large quiet rooms, comfortable beds, good temperature control, and excellent breakfast. Great choice for airport hotel.

“Great location!” Great Location... Close to subway, Madison Square Garden, Penn Station, Empire State Building.... Small rooms, which is typical for NY. We were there for 4 nights. The first room we had was a top floor, corner room, no much room to put suitcases anywhere....1 night at 1 am, the smoke alarm kept going off, called the front desk 3 times over 40 min before someone finally came and put in a new battery! Lost water for over 8 hours in entire hotel......they did take money off for that night w/o our asking. We had noticed on the side of the bed the rug by the wall was damp, was really damp by 2nd night, figured out that the ceiling in the bathroom was leaking....requested to be moved. We had to pack our bags and leave at the front desk, no rooms were ready at the time. Room was ready when we got back from our outings for part of the day. 2nd room was even smaller! Could not open door to room all the way due to luggage......even worse situation for luggage than 1st room. I will say hotel seemed clean, front desk person we dealt with for most of our stay was very nice and helpful....Food at the restaurant was good. Not sure that I'd stay here again tho...got a great rate at the time.

“Immer wieder gerne- Dupont” War wieder einmal zu Besuch in DC. Ich buchte sehr kurzfristig per E-Mail und wir wurde ein "einfaches Zimmer" zugesprochen. Ich hatte aber das Glück, dass ich ein superior Zimmer ergattern konnte. Eine nette Karte vom Chef lag dann auch auf dem Zimmer bereit. Ich mag, dass das Zimmer keine vorhänge hat sondern die Holzjalousien, so wie bei Hollister. Super gemacht. Das offene Bad und die Regendusche sind traumhaft. Die Lage ist "the best", Es gibt viele clubs und bars in der nähe. Dupont gilt als sicher und Georgetown ist gut zu Fuss erreichbar. Der Sightseeing bus fährt auch in der Nähe ab und die Ubahn ist auch gleich beim Hotel. Aufenthalt November 2011

“New, beautiful, clean hotel” This hotel is new, beautiful and very clean. Rooms smelled clean and fresh. Staff was delightful, very helpful and friendly. Bedding was clean, smelled good, comfortable. Mattress and pillows were nice and comfortable. There was absolutely no road noise at night which is very important to me; however, I'm not sure if the interior walls are extremely thin or if people are just that inconsiderate. It was the weekend of the rodeo and people came & went at all hours. You could here them stomping above you and in the hallways. Our room was 310 and right by elevator. I think a room on the fourth floor and at the end of the hallway would be ideal here. I did call the front desk about all the noise and he did check it out for me. The facility had security at night and the parking lot was well lit. There was an indoor pool but we didn't get to use due to lack of time. Internet was free but again we didn't use. Free continental breakfast was good and typical for this type of hotel. I will definitely stay here again but maybe just ask for a different room location.

“Well run hotel” Considering the size of the place - it's huge - they do a really good job in managing the facility. Check in was smooth and quick, facilities clean and well laid out. However, I had what was the smallest hotel room I've ever had in Chicago. It didn't really matter since I wasn't in the room much - but avoid 1801 in the west tower (or I imagine any of the xx01 rooms in the west tower) unless you don't have claustraphobia. It was certainly a well appointed room, but if I had wanted to swing a cat, it wouldn't have been possible. No offense intended to cats.

“A bit on the small side, but in a great location” Stayed at this hotel when conducting site visits for an upcoming event. I only stayed for one night. The room I had was a corner and very spacious. The bathroom was a bit dated. With the coffee maker, the counterspace was really limited. But overall, the room was clean and quiet. And the bed was really comfortable! The only drawback was that I was a little surprised however at the level of money invested in the "spa" area, when the rest of the hotel looked like it could use some modernization. I did not eat in the dining room, but looked at the menu and it was astronomically priced. The good news is that there were quite a few mid-range dining options available, as well. (Try the Belgium bar two blocks away - they are known for their mussels, which were delicious). The historical aspect of the neighborhood was also a bonus! I walked about a 4-5 block radius around the hotel at night and felt very safe. The staff were very accommodating as well. I was actually very sick while visiting, so they sent up some free hot tea. Also I requested and received 2 wakeup calls which were on time. I also asked for a cab, which was ready and waiting for me when I checked out.

“Great location at a fraction of the price” Location! Location! Location! 0.1 mile from the Empire State Building. Walking distance to shopping, restaurants and to the tour bus route. Continental breakfast served. Rooms though small and basic are clean. Request for a higher floor for better city view. Friendly staff. No concierge, any planning requests like taxi service or tour tickets have a fee. Plan tours on your own or ahead of time.

“I was not impressed...” This is my first negative review - and it is mild. The room was clean, but the shower faucet leaked so bad it woke me up a few times. The elevator placement is odd - there were elevators right next to my room, but we had to walk in a big "U" shape to get to the ones that were operational. I found the staff to be a bit cold - not the "golly we're glad you're here" that this midwesterner expects... The plus side is that the decor is modern - the price is fair, and the location is excellent...

“OK, can see why Euros don't mind it” Fourth or fifth time to Seattle on business, hadn't stayed here before, decided to try it. My title is not meant to be disparaging, it's just that having traveled Europe a decent amount, it's what you'd expect from a mid-level hotel ... older, smaller rooms and bathrooms (the sink was literally the size of a large mixing bowl), radiators and pipe noise as another reviewer mentioned. Good location for tourists, though, and for those looking for a clean place for a decent price, this would be it. Staff was a little discombobulated but I attribute that to the fact that the lobby is undergoing renovation so they have a temporary setup for the front desk right now. Not sure when lobby completion is expected.

“Good Location for Alamo, Riverwalk and Convention Center” This hotel is very clean and has a hot breakfast, which is a very good value. It is right near the River Center Mall, Alamo and the Convention Center. Trolleys and busses run a block away at Alamo Plaza. Since La Quinta began in Texas, the quality of their hotels seems to be better here. It is very clean. Each room has a refrigerator and microwave. Although the staff isn't quite as knowledgeable as they are at a high end hotel, the San Antonio visitor center is a block away. If you are independent and don't care about swanky lobbies, this is a good deal.

“Nice Hotel - great location and helpful staff” Expedia had a terrific rate for this hotel in the heart of Union Square ( $111 per night) so I grabbed it. Impressive lobby, great staff, great location. The rooms are oddly shaped but decent decor and comfortable. My room had 2 small issues- the tv shut itself off every 30 minutes ( no timer issue- I checked) and as I went to iron a shirt as often needs to be done on business trips- I notcied the iron had a nice coat of rust on it and decided to test it on one of their towels-SO glad I did- It would have ruined my shirt! So no harm no foul- Overall the hotel is great - especially for the rate I paid

“GREAT LOCATION” Hotel has been recently been updated.Rooms are very clean but a bit small.Check in was a breeze.Housekeeping was very friendly had prompt service.Room was always ready before 10:00 am.On the other hand the bellman are very rude and slow.Ihad requested a frig to store meds.After waiting several hours i called to check if one would be brought to my room.Iwas told they thought the bellman had already dropped it off.Again i reminded them it was for med storage.After giving up it was finally brought to my room at midnight.Valet is also a big problem service is very slow to bring cars around and to drop car off again.Some very rude lazy group of men who don't want to work but are quick to stick out thier hand for a tip.I was surprised that no one in hotel could have you a good dinning option away from walking distance.Over all hotel is clean with lots of options to dine on.easy to walk to see sights of city.Bed is not comfortable but over all it is a good stay.

“As a platinum and very loyal Marriott guest it was highly disappointing” The bellman was reaching for his tip after he piled 3 of our large heavy duffels on top of each other in the corner of the room-did not get the luggage stand out and did not ask where suitcases s/go. The front desk associates were no more friendly. Worst of all, we left a very specific item of clOthing in the room- it was hanging from the vent and we called as soon as we landed which was still noon EST. they said it was it wasn't there. We know 100% it was! Would NEVER EVER stay/recommend for anyone. I will be writing to Mr Marriott bc of this stay. Otherwise rooms were clean and fine sized. There is a basic concierge lounge which was unattended-never seen that before this stay.

“Wonderful Stay in Chicago” Enjoyed our stay at this hotel and plan to do it again when we return. Plusses: - Wonderful service - Heavenly bed, of course - Nice gym - Within walking distance to the CTA Clarke/Lake Station, Michigan Mile, West Loop (great restaurants), Millenium Park, Chicago River Minuses: - Wi-fi in our room didn't work, and IT wasn't able to fix the problem. Based on our hotel experience, it often appears that rooms furthest away from the router have the weakest signal. You may want to inquire at the front desk if this is important to you. Tips: - Great restaurants (Girl & The Goat, The Publican) - Great tours (Bucktown/Wicker Park Food Tour, Architecture Foundation Boat Cruise)

“Very Average Top to Bottom” My hotel room was GIANT, but the cleanliness was very, very average. Carpets throughout the hotel were worn and often stained. The shower curtain in my room had lots of mildew on the bottom which gives me the creeps. The bed was okay, but not as good as other hotels. I had large windows in my room, but they were not clean, inside or out. The room hadn't been updated to have plugs near the bed. The bathroom was pretty large and there was a microwave and a refrigerator in my room, so that would be good for some people. There wasn't a fitness room. You had to ask for a pass at the front desk and then you could go to the Capital Club which was an adjacent fitness center. That was fine, but on Saturday, I went to it and it was closed....didn't open until 9:00 am. The hotel is downtown, about a 15 minute walk from the Convention center and one block away from High Street which has restaurant choices and about 10 minute walk from the Arena District where there are more food choices. The hotel is across the street from the River and the Christopher Columbus statue and the river has a beautifully done sidewalk/bike path that goes the length of the city. It is really nice and very clean. The elevator system is interesting. From the street you have to take an elevator up 6 floors (which is the parking garage) and then it takes you to the lobby and then you have to get out and cross the lobby to get into the elevators to take you to the rooms. The hotel front desk always seemed shorthanded. I ordered a takeout dinner from the hotel restaurant and took it up to my room. It was extremely average and the dinner portion was crazy small for the amount that they charged. Overall, I was not pleased and it does not do anything to enhance the Doubletree name.

“Nice Hotel, Great Staff, OK location” This is a nice, reasonably priced hotel - it's clean, fairly modern, and has comfortable beds. The staff makes this place as they are very friendly and willing to accomodate. Location is ok, it's near Times Square but next to the Port Authority Bus Station - great for catching cabs as there is a cab line just around the corner, but somewhat sketchy. There is a small bar in the lobby and a fitness center. I'd stay again.

“Poormont not Fairmont” Quite disappointed for a supposedly quality hotel. There was no one on the door to help with cases and no one on reception to greet and this was only late evening. Once the receptionist appeared, she was off hand and just requested a credit card, no real welcome greeting. The room given had major need of repair and had the ceiling coving hanging off. I wrote to the hotel but never received a response. I would not choose to stay here again.

“close to the action...nice rooms...best service in long time...slow elevators” stayed here for business 3 nights...lots of renovated charm (very nice except tub old and need more power in the showerhead) and fantastic service in the included excellent breakfast buffet (smoked salmon and eggs and mueslix etc)...wonderful desk personnel and cozy lobby...good included fitness center...but the elevators were SLOW!!!! i stayed in room near elevators and was surprising quiet.....great shops/waterfront 4 blocks west----climb vertically back up to hotel-- recommend bus---worth$2...esp after stuffing self with crab (see elliotts crab house review)!

“Wish It Had Been Better!” My daughter and I stayed here while she attended the CHA Trade Show at the L.A. Convention Center. The GOOD: the staff was very accommodating and friendly. The room was spacious and the bathroom clean. The BAD: Very few options for dining within walking distance . . . El Pollo Loco, McDonald's, Pollo Campero, Subway. Very hard beds and our room had bugs!! I now know there were bed bugs - I've never experienced that before!!! I have at least 6 bug bites on my arms and wrists. We killed a couple we saw crawling around. In hindsight, we should have asked to be moved to another room!! Also, we were right next to the drive through to the back parking area, so at all hours of the night we were awakened by loud trucks and cars driving through, their antennas scraping against the roof, or vehicles idleing there and people talking loud. Overall, not a good experience and I would not return. Sorry Rodeway Inn!!!

“Eleganza e professionalità” Abbiamo trascorso tre notti in questo splendido albergo. Hall molto elegante e ampia, le stanze sono ampie e molto pulite e ben climatizzate. Il personale è gentile e disponibile con specifico riferimento alla concierge che ha fornito in lingua italiana i più preziosi consigli e la più ampia disponibilità per le prenotazioni dei ristoranti. La posizione è veramente eccezionale, centrale e consente di raggiungere a piedi in pochissimi minuti la quinta strada e la madison. Esso infatti è tra la lexington e park avenue. Volendo trovare il pelo nell'uovo i bagni non sono ampi e non si comprende come mai le stanze non siano dotate di televisori lcd . Consiglio vivamente questa struttura.

“Average to Slightly Above Average” Location is great for CHerry Creek, great shopping and dining. The rooms or at least mine was a bit small. Hotel had limited staff on hand- which were very helpful and were able to get the room ready slightly before that dreaded statement, " Check in is not until 3(insert hour of choice)" This is the most easliy translated hotel excuse for we are understaffed or poorly trained or simply are not concerned for the tired business traveler. Just my pet peeve! However after some push back on my part they were able to expedite the room cleaning.

“Nice hotel” Stayed in this hotel for one night. Booked the Bridal Package - came with free breakfast and champagne - the best package on the Westin internet site. The hotel is modern and interesting looking - and on one of the hotest days of the summer, a cool relief. Check in was quick and efficient - although the "we charge for all calls" lecture seemed harsh - maybe some would fine the admonition helpful. The room was nice - in a modern style, clean, bed was as you would expect in a Westin. Bathroom was small and not particularly luxurious. Ordered a snack at midnight - burger, fries and chicken tenders were barely edible, although delivered within a half hour. Delivered one glass of water for two people. Breakfast in the restaurant - included in the package - was good.

“Boston's best” I couldn't believe a property that didn't charge an arm and a leg would be this fantastic but it is all that and more. The location is elegant. Stroll down Commonwealth for an early walk and soak it all in. Check in is a breeze, with attentive and friendly front desk personnel providing outstanding customer service. Our room was a small suite with tasteful furnishings and a great view. Super comfortable bed with nice linens. The bathroom was clean and functional. One sink but who really cares? Keep in mind $300 per night. The gym is small and barely adequate. No showers. A few nice treadmills and bikes and dumbbells. Breakfast and lunch are first class. When I called to make a reservation Corinne, Director of Revenue, assisted. She steered us to the Island Creek Oyster Bar for dinner and suggested the hotel's bar Hawthorne for a drink. She is a brilliant woman. Both the bar and the restaurant are beyond description. Don't miss either. The hotel, along with the two aforementioned attached establishments, provided an unparalled experience we will never forget.

“Great location but its view was not worthy of the extra cost” Our family stayed at Doubletree Guest Suites in Times Square for 7 nights during April 7 - 14. I picked the hotel for its location and because it is an all-suites hotel. I was not disappointed with its location, right in the middle of Times Square and near the theaters. We watched 3 Broadway shows at night and it was wonderful to walk a couple of blocks to get back to the hotel after the shows. During the day we walked easily to Macy's and Rockefeller Center since taxis were moving very slowly in the traffic. The thing I was disappointed with was the spectacular view I was promised. We paid $459 a night plus tax for a guaranteed high floor with a fantastic view of New York City. What we got was a room on 37th floor where we looked directly at a high rise with offices. We could see some of Times Square below but the high rise office building blocked half of it. So I don't recommend paying extra for high floors or views. The small refridgerator didn't have temp control and was not very cold. The suite also does not have temp control, only a fan that you can turn on to circulate air. The rooms were clean and in good condition. All in all, it was a good hotel to stay at but don't pay extra for the view.

“So nice and quiet” Had heard about this hotel and decided to spend Memorial Day weekend there with my daughter. The service was excellent (room ready by 3pm, no wait) and all the employees were friendly and welcoming. The room looked out onto 6th Avenue and must have been the most soundproof I've ever experienced. Very little siren noise and only rain hitting the window during a big thunderstorm overnight. The Etra amenities were lovely, the shower marble and very modern. Having FoodParc right next door was very convenient. The location of the hotel is also convenient and near all public transportation, but the neighborhood itself, while getting better, is no great thrill. That was the only downside. Our second Kimpton hotel experience and we will be back.

“University Park - The Place” Stayed at the Lumen on a recent business trip to the Big D and found the hotel to be a little jewel across the street from SMU. The hotel is nicely renovated with lots of personal touches. Nice lobby, bar/resturant, good room,gym and great shower. Inaddition to the great decor , is the friendly staff - who go the extra mile to make you feel weclome and comfortable. The location is a little suburban, if your not attending an SMU event - but with a car your 15 minutes to trendy Oak Lawn, Highland Park Village or North Park Mall

“Good value and tourist-friendly location” The hotel was a bit off the beaten track but still within (a 20-minute) walking distance to major landmarks such as the White House and National Mall. The nearest subway stations (Dupont Circle or McPherson Square) were about 10 minutes away. We booked the romance package which came with a junior suite, breakfast for 2 and a bottle of sparkling wine at arrival - pretty good value for a central DC hotel. The room was spacious with a living/dinning area (I suspected all rooms in this hotel were some type of suites). The bathroom was also quite large. Buffet breakfast was adequate. No surprises but all work out nicely.

“Sleep Number Beds!!!!!” The best part of spending a week in Philly? The hotel!!! The beds were so comfortable! The lobby was breathtaking!!! The staff were phenomenal! I will definitely be back again!!! :)

“Excellent service, lovely staff” I arrived at the hotel with my 4 year old son, who proceeded to be sick all night. The staff could not have been lovelier - they moved my room immediately when I called, and even offered to send up tea for him. We had an elaborate check-in system, with the other half of the family arriving the next day, and changes in our stay - all of which were accommodated graciously. The room (a regular suite) was very spacious, one of the largest bathrooms ever, with a nice layout. The only complaint is that -- not sure how this is possible -- rooms on both ends of the hotel appear to face, respectively, a fire station, and an emergency command center? So there were a lot of sirens. I prefer to sleep with the windows open (another plus - windows that open!) despite the noise; the sound might be better if the windows were closed. Also, although we did not use it, the health club is gorgeous.

“Not worth the price” I stayed in this hotel on a business trip. Location is nice near UN and east River, the room was very poor. Totally outdated with a little kitchen and gas range, rusty, wallpaper coming down, tiled dirty. Bathroom subgrade, for a shower you had to let the water run until it was not brown any more. Room was totally dark, windows either boarded up for whatever reason, or very dirty. Maybe there are other rooms that are renovated, however as the hotel management I would not have rented this room at all. A colleague of mine stayed in a room on a different floor and his description of his room was the same. Will definitely not come back here. Lounge on 26th floor though is worthwhile a visit for the view.

“Decent hotel, better than expected for a Four Points” I used to stay here for business and I thought it was a good value for the location. Although it "opened" in February/March 2010, it is not a new hotel so don't kid yourself. Pros: The front desk receptionists are young, but they do provide great customer service. A big perk is they will provide you with a pass to the Bally's Gym across the street. There's a movie theater and lots of restaurants within walking distance. The bar seems to be relatively popular on Thursday nights and the outside bar area is a hit during the summer. Cons: I understand that $20/night is the going rate in downtown San Jose, but it still seems like a rip-off, especially since it's in an open lot. I have noticed that they do not do a great job cleaning the linens as it doesn't have a fresh smell. The rooms are clean, but the smell of the linens give off the impression otherwise. Rooms are also really small. You get horrible cell phone reception using an iPhone, but then again, it could be the iPhone and not the room.

“Buon hotel, colazione così così” Ho soggiornato in questo hotel per due notti nel mese di agosto durante il mio tour degli Stati Uniti. L'hotel è piuttosto centrale e si raggiunge facilmente tutti i punti principali della città sia a piedi (ma è un po'lunga) sia in pochi minuti di metropolitana. L'hotel è un po'piccolo rispetto agli altri Doubletree nei quali ho soggiornato, ma lo standard delle camere è lo stesso. Infatti sono sempre molto grandi e molto pulite. L'unica cosa che non mi ha soddisfatto molto è la colazione che era un po'scarsa. Per il resto è consigliatissimo!!

“Great location!” This hotel was in a fantastic location right in the middle of Greenwich Village... The staff was nice, the bar was cool, and the hotel was walking distance of great nightlife and restaurants. You definitely are paying for location, the room was tiny (but clean) and non-descript...

“Hated it!!!!!” This is by no means a "resort' in my opinion! For the rates they charge, you'd expect 3 stars at the least...the rooms were old and outdated. The door didn't even lock properly therefore allowing my 2 year old to wander out into the parking lot at will. Thankfully, my husband managed to "fix' it for the one hell night we stayed there. Oh and the so called "private" beach???? I don't know what most people call a nice beach, but this isn't it! It was so dirty and filthy that I was afraid to let my toddler play in the sand and surf. Definitely do not waste your time and money!

“Perfect weekend getaway” From the friendly staff to the luck of being placed in one of the larger suites, this was the perfect place for a girls' weekend getaway. My 2 friends and I felt extremely at ease in the neighborhood and walked everywhere! We did not dine on site, so I can't really say anything about the Italian restaurant except that it looked like a nice place and the menu prices seemed reasonable. The buffet was typical for ES, so no surprises there. The pool/jacuzzi area was also typical for ES, but not crowded with kids (possibly because of the time of year). It's a pleasant walk to Foggy Bottom metro station just a few blocks away if needed. Also, the hotel is about 4 or 5 blocks from Georgetown, so we visited there a couple of times for shopping and brunch at Martin's Tavern. No complaints at all about our suite, which was very large, very clean and had comfortable beds. Great exercise facility on site! My only gripe is that the jacuzzi/pool maintenance is performed at a time of morning when I wanted to use those facilities. It would be nice if it could be done during the hours when that area is closed to guests. This was my first time visiting DC, and I look forward to the day I can return. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“So-So, but very convenient for me” I was here for 6 nights. The room was okay, cleanliness was okay, nothing spectacular. The staff was very polite and accommodating. For the price, it was a decent hotel.

“Great location for exploring Boston” We stayed 4 nights in a junior suite. The hotel is very well located to explore Boston. The staff were all very nice and helpful. Our room was spacious and comfortable but the bathroom was very small and pokey, we are not big people and very found it very small. It was disproportionate compared to the size of the junior suite. We had to pay for the wifi connection and were disappointed with it, it was very unstable and kept dropping which I would not expect with a paid connection. It was very frustrating. Having said all that if we were in Boston again we would stay at this hotel again.

“Nice hotel, perfect for concerts” I took my daughter and 5 of her friends to a concert in Charlotte and we stayed 2 nights at the Hyatt House, which is adjacent to the Time Warner Arena. The hotel is quite nice. Very clean and modern and the staff was friendly and extremely tolerant of a hotel full of teenage girls. It was a bit pricey for the type of hotel it is and I'm assuming that was primarily due to high demand during a sold out concert. It was perfect before the concert because the girls could go on their own without even having to cross a street. There are plenty of restaurants and a CVS within easy walking distance, as well as several museums. I highly recommend this hotel for anyone visiting uptown Charlotte.

“Beware of Pricing” For the past several years I've been staying at Hilton Times Square during NY City visits. My most recent stay was in August 2005. I generally visit Manhattan about twice a year and see 3 to 4 shows during one weekend. I've been returning to this hotel because I can usually count on a decent room in a convenient location at a good price (at least by NY standards). A few weeks ago I purchased Broadway tickets for a weekend in March 2006. I intended to book a room at Hilton as usual, but found that the standard room I last paid about $187.00 for was up to $329. I've paid just over $200 there before, but never over $300. My chosen weekend is not on or near a holiday. I've been watching prices for several hotels and see that Hilton's fluctuate quite a bit. Over the past few weeks their standard room price rose to $329 and dropped to $246. I saw it go back up a few dollars to $249, but a nonrefundable price of $212 was then offered (not available before). I later did back-to-back searches and saw that the $212 offer did not come up every time. Now it doesn't come up at all. This leaves me wondering how many times I've overpaid in the past. I also think of the people who have booked at $329 without following up and seeing the price drop. My concerns have been brought to the attention of Hilton Times Square and Hilton Corporate. I've made a reservation elsewhere for March. I will also take some time from that trip to research other hotels for future visits. I have nothing bad to say about the accommodations at Hilton Times Square. I may even return someday, but not before I can be sure that I am not a victim of price gouging.
“Excellent hotel” Excellent hotel, excellent rooms, excellent staff, excellent concierge lounge, excellent everything.

“Very well located and well priced quality Washington hotel” This is a very nice hotel. Easy 20 minute walk to the Mall/Washington Monument/White House etc. Clean and nicely appointed room. Parking around the corner for $10 a day. They have internet access available to guests off the lobby. I would like to recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Washington.

“Very comfy and well located” Stayed here two nights and while the rooms are the smallest I have ever experienced in NY, they were very comfortable, clean and well maintained. The room has a nice flat screen TV, in fact, a lot of TV for a room that size. The staff was excellent including a very cheerful and energetic welcome from Nicholas when we arrived. The pillows were so nice my son (13) wanted to buy one to take home. The hotel is located in SoHo within a block of the MTA and we found that very useful. We didn't use any of the amenities of the hotel or the bar/restaurant. There is a little outside area to sit in to enojor food/drink. We did use a deli and the donut place almost next door to grab a quick bite in the morning before we ventured off. This hotel is adjacent to Little Italy and only a few train stops from the World Trade Center. Normally, I like to stay up near the theater district but this was a nice hotel. If your focus is in the southern end of Manhattan and like to walk, this is a nice choice.

“Good family fun, but overpriced” This resort is similar to a Disney hotel in the mid-price range or a Gaylord hotel, but more expensive. It's less hectic than going to Disney World, if that's what you want. This resort is definitely focused on family, for children up to age 10 or so. There are also some attractions for children up to perhaps 14, but I think the younger age group is happier here. The pool is well suited to younger children, although it gets very crowded as does the lazy river. It's like being at a water park The good: planned daily activities for kids and kid camp. Food served at pool. The pool. The mattresses. Rooms are clean. Antler's restaurant. The mediocre: the food in the "family" cafe restaurant (I don't recommend the buffet). You get a better value for your money dining at their nicer restaurant, but you have to dress business casual to go there. Room decor and size. Service is friendly, but how good can it get with 100 people needing help at the same time? The lines for towels at the pool or for the snack bar or in the store were slow moving. The bad: prices were high for food, drinks and rooms -- I don't think any of it was justified. Worst smoothie I have ever tasted! Stick to water, beer and soda here, but it's best if you buy some at a grocery store and bring it with you to avoid the 100%-200% increase in price. Room sizes are small. People hoard poolside space by placing towels and other items as early as 6 AM and then keep the space all day regardless of where they are or what they are doing. The staff should manage the use of space more effectively so that everyone can enjoy the facilities. The large floats that they get kids to beg their parents to buy for them -- it takes them forever to inflate one and then they are really too big for the pool, plus there are easier to use inner tubes available for free. I saw many of these large floats occupying chairs by the pool. When we arrived, there was a woman crying in the lobby because her reservation had been messed up. I'm not sure what had happened, but apparently they did not have a room big enough for her family available anymore and the hotel was offering to split them into 2 rooms, which obviously is not ideal when you are traveling with young children.

“Over priced and awful!!” I stayed at the Marriott Hotel at the George Bush Airport in Houston, TX after traveling from the Middle East and flying over 24 hrs. I was tired and exhausted and was willing to pay the $300 a night for the convenience and (assumed) luxury that I thought this hotel would provide. When I called the hotel for the shuttle bus to pick me up, I was told that I had to take the underground subway system. I had a ton of luggage and luggage carts are not allowed on the subway. I was not happy about this but dragged my luggage down the elevator and on to the subway. Once at the hotel, I saw a sign that said the subway system would not be working again until 7am the next morning. This created a huge problem because my flight was at 6am and the hotel said they did not have a shuttle service. When I got off the shuttle, I called the phone by the elevator to ask for assistance with my luggage. I waited 20+minutes and no one showed up. I dragged my luggage upstairs to the check-in counter where the customer service was luke warm. I explained my need for shuttle service to the airport the next morning--I was then told that they did have a van to provide transportation to the airport but they do not like people to know about it and prefer people to take the underground subway system. I thought that really stunk that they lied about not having a shuttle service even after I explained that I had just traveled from the Middle East and needed assistance with my luggage. I was then told to make a shuttle reservation with the concierge. I then went up to my room and was surprised at how old, dated and used all the furniture looked. I have stayed at other Marriotts for $100 a night and saw brand new furnishings. This room looked used and abused and was not very clean. I had been in my room 10 minutes when the door swung open--it was the maid service. They did not knock before entering and simply unlocked the door. When I looked startled, the maid told me..."Well, you should put the bar across the door". Wow, talk about rude. Before going to bed, I called the concierge to confirm my reservations--of course they didn't have it. I had to make another reservation. I called the front desk to request a bell hop come to my room to assist me with my luggage for the following morning. I called back 30 minutes later to confirm that service--again, no record of my request. I woke up an hour early to prepare myself for no shuttle or bell hop service and I'm glad I did. The bell hop never showed up and the shuttle service was delayed due to all the people that needed service to the airport. I waited for 3 rounds of people to be taken to the airport before it was finally my turn. I was so disappointed in my stay and the waste of money that I called the Marriott to complain--the customer service rep did not apologize or do anything to rectify the situation. In conversing with other travelers on the shuttle, I found out that their experience was similiar to mine and they were disgusted with the lack of quality service and cleanliness. Marriott Corp. should be ashamed of the service at this hotel and look into making some serious changes.
“Great Location!” Great location. Center of everything. Within walking distance to all the historic sites. Clean hotel but old. Beds are very comfortable and minimal noise level.

“good location, would stay again” We found the people at the front desk to be quite helpful with directions and other questions about the area. It should be noted that we were told (and it seemed true) that paying for hotel valet parking would be valid from check-in until 6pm on day of departure. So, to site-see on the day of departure, they held our bags for the day and our car stayed "free" in their lot. It turned out to be a savings from having to pay more than 24 hours to park our car in a public or private lot. The room was large enough for the rollaway - it fit in with the 2Q beds. We chose the hotel based on the 2 queen (instead of double) beds. It was clean, quiet, and comfortable. We had a good view from the 3rd floor, even. We recommend it and would stay there again. The walk to the historic district was about 10 blocks and was manageable.

“Beautiful hotel on the water - location is great for business travel” Hotel is within walking distance of financial center for meetings. Walking to Chinatown and the Back Bay area is also possible if you have time. Shopping in area is not as good as the Back Bay. Only one meal at the hotel (Sea Grille) for breakfast which was excellent. Sea Grille eggs.

“Great NY trip, Good NY Hotel” We came to NY on business and didn't choose the hotel. When we learned where we had been booked I looked on Trip Advisor. Reading the reviews it seemed like there were two hotels - one a chic, hip boutique hotel in q terrific location, the other a slightly run down, over the hill hotel in a terrific location. I was not sure which one we would find. Well, we found the first one. Everything from the greeting by Miguel, the doorman to the size and decor of our room to the view (we were on 11th floor) pleased us. The room was clean, decorated nicely and had a contemporary vibe. Nice use of space, with some frosted glass panels in the closet and shower that let more light in. The room itself was bright and the wall of mirrors across from the bed, along with stylish reading lamps kept it so eve in the evening. We loved the bar and had drinks there with friends several times. Generous glasses of wine made for good value. Didn't try the restaurant, but one night dined at Chez Josephine on 42nd St., most memorable meal, in fact the highlight of the trip. It is true that there was a line for the elevator several times. So what? Seems that the most common complaint is small rooms. Our room (1108) was not small at all. It was great. Maybe you should specify when booking that you don't want one of their "small" rooms. We would gladly stay here again. Ps. Chris helped us clear our room and get out of town in a hurry after we overslept and thought we might miss our flight. Another example of the great service here. Thanks again Chris, we made it!

“Halfway at the Hyatt” I imagine the room conditions will improve after the current remodel. As with many Hyatt Regencies that were once palaces of modern architecture during the 70's, this one has struggled a bit to keep the ravages of time at bay. Hyatt has always ranked a notch behind Hilton & Marriott in investing in their aging properties & while the public spaces still have a modern George Jetson vibe, the rooms are showing 40 years of wear and tear. My room had peeling wallpaper in a corner, scuffs on the wall, worn, cracked caulking in the shower & dirty tile grout - things you might accept in a motel during Spring Break, but not the standard for a decent business hotel. Again, hopefully these issues will be remedied during their current renovation. The location however, is first rate, smack in the middle of the compact downtown area and easily accessible to all the main venues. There are not a large number of hotel choices in the downtown area, so If you're looking for convenience, a centralized location, full business facilities & reasonable rates, the Hyatt probably has the best location for that - Just don't expect luxury, exceptional service or a 4 star experience.

“Cool Vibe from a Ritz Carlton, who would have thought” I stayed at the Ritz Carlton Georgetown, what a surprise it was, in a good way. I like the Ritz Carlton quality of properties and service but had stopped staying in there properties if I had another luxury choice because they all seemed to be the same. The Georgetown property is not like the other Ritz properties and it is apparent before you even enter the hotel. The hotel has the best location of any hotel in Georgetown. The industry felling carries from the outside of the hotel with a smoke stack rising out of the structure to the inside with the black steel and brick surfaces through out the lobby and hall ways on the inside. The hotel still provided a luxury feeling and service without the sometime stuffy appearance of the "standard" Ritz. The quality of the room and service I received in my short one night stay had me wishing I could stay longer. I would definitely recommend this property to anyone looking for a luxury experience while in Georgetown wanting to be in the center of the action without the noise and the crowds.

“Average room, nice staff.” I stayed here in February 2005 for two nights. Location is convenient, right behind the Kodak Theater. Front desk staff always friendly. The lobby and common areas are very nice and seem to be newly finished. The room, however, was rather dark and dingy. The carpet was dark and industrial-looking with a huge burnt spot in the shape of an iron. Unfinished paint trim in the bathroom and spotty gray wall paint in the room made it look a little seedy. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. The best thing was free parking and internet. I guess for the price it was okay. It seems the owners have a real interest in the property so I feel the place will only get better.

“Lovely location” I've stayed in other locations in San Diego - downtown and on Mission Bay - so was excited about staying in a new neighborhood. The location of the hotel was wonderful! Right across the street from my room was a walking path along the Bay. It was a beautiful way to start - and end - the day. As I was on Eastern Time waking up on the Pacific Coast, I found myself up at about 3:00 each morning, and felt completely safe walking alone along the Bay until the rest of the city awoke. Yes, the walls are thin and I heard every intimate detail of the lives of the people above me. But, I didn't hear any airplanes, which was a surprise being so close to the airport. I was there for a week for a conference and relied on a shuttle to take me to the Convention Center downtown so I didn't rent a car. Having no car - and no desire to spend $20 each way taking a taxi into the heart of the city - made it difficult finding dinner on nights when there were concerts at Humphrey's. Walking to the "mainland", I was able to find Miguel's, a nice Mexican restaurant (nothing to write home about but good food and interesting decor). Be prepared to walk quite a distance to find food when the hotel's restaurant is reserved for concert-goers. Overall, the room was comfortable, the service was great, and the location was beautiful. On my last night at Humphrey's, I attended a concert on the grounds and thoroughly enjoyed the intimate setting on the Bay. Coming from the sweltering MidWest, I was anticipating an outdoor setting to become rather uncomfortable as the sun set, but was delighted to experience a cool musical evening without mosquitos!

“Great stay, even better location!” We booked a hotel due to the power outages from the storm this past weekend. We were going to a wedding in DC anyway, so decided to book a last-minute deal on Hotwire. Got a great rate and that made the experience that much better! The location is AWESOME. Right off the circle, a block away from the north entrance of the metro. They also gave us early check in. The woman at the front desk was so nice and sweet, as was most of the staff we encountered. The room was big by city standards. The decor is lovely. Bed is comfortable. Room was very clean. Nice TV. Heated floors in the bathroom - mind BLOWN. Gym was actually kind of large for a hotel gym and had fresh fruit and flavored ice water (nice touch!). Free coffee from 7 to 11 I believe. Free wi-fi! A couple of weird things: if you are traveling with a friend and not a close significant other, you might find the bathroom setup to be very odd. There is no door separating the toilet and shower, just a pane of glass. There is just a shower like glass door separating the sink and toilet/shower. So hope you are comfortable with each other! The other thing: the fire alarm was going off for HOURS on Sunday morning. Nothing was wrong and the fire alarm in our room was fine, but the incessant "can I have your attention please, this is a fire emergency" is super annoying when you are trying to not be hungover from the wedding the night before. Oh well, got us up and going to the gym at least.

“For families” I chose this hotel because I had a kind of mixed business and family trip. It was the right choice, we had a great stay. The suite had a master bedroom with a king size, comfortable bed and plenty storage space. The second room is the biggest with a living room with a sleeper sofa which became our son's bedroom at night, and a dining room which we used as the working and all purpose area: we had three laptops to work with. The breakfast is self service and simple but at not extra charge. The personal is very attentive and always ready to help. We didn't use the kitchen because in the neighborhood there are plenty of eating options, I recommend La Madeleine; and no grocery stores nearby. The location is great - close to downtown and public transportation.

“Another great experience!” My husband and I have stayed at this hotel three times during weekend excursions to Boston. Each time I have been amazed at the amenities and service they deliver for such a reasonable price. The service, from check-in to housekeeping to the bellmen, is exemplary. Everyone goes above and beyond to make the guests happy. Each room we have stayed in has been spotless. On this trip the hotel gave us free breakfast coupons, even though our rate did not include them. The location, practically on top of the TNEMC station on Boston's Orange Line, makes navigating the city very easy. It is also within steps of all the theater district's venues and a short walk from the best restaurants in Boston's Chinatown.

“Great customer service, good room” Like with most hotels there are pros and cons. I'll start with the pros-- The customer service was fantastic, from the check in, to the people in the restaurant, and even there maids were cheerful. I thought the staff presented themselves in a very friendly manner. Our room was huge, with a king size bed, large flat screen TV, a coffee maker with Lavazza coffee, a safe for laptops etc, big fluffy towels, nice toiletries, and very clean updated bathroom. As far as the cons go--the bathrooms are tiny--I'm short and felt claustrophobic--there wasn't a make-up mirror, nor a mini frig. Also, get a room on the 3rd floor if possible, the rooms are not that soundproof and we heard people walking above us laye into the night and early in the morning. This hotel is up a couple of blocks from the steady flow of traffic and people walking along the wharf, so it's in a perfect location. It isn't a fancy hotel at all, but it doesn't feel cheap either. I would stay again without hesitation. Just don't expect 5 star service and accommodations--it's more of a do it yourself type of place. No doormen or bellmen, however, there is valet parking. Most of the restaurants in this area are pretty bad, so be aware of that. It's a total tourist place. Check some websites before heading out, make sure they get a 4 star rating at least!!!
“触らないサービス” よく利用しています。 スタッフのサービスは抜群です。 日本のホテルかと思う程気の回し方が素晴らしいです。 ディスクに原稿を置いて出てしまっても、触らないでそのままにしてくれていました。 NYCです、不必要な笑顔はありません。 でも、全てに気にならないサービスが行き届いています。 サービスしました。との押し売り的なサービスでない所が気に入っています。

“A cavernous Hilton with some history” First the history - It was at the lower south entrance to this hotel that John Hinckley shot Ronald Reagan. For some reason, it's not the most prominent thing in this hotel's advertising plan.... The rooms are Hilton standard, which means adequate for the business traveler though not plush. Hilton's standards are fairly high, and just about any Hilton I'd rank would get at least a Very Good rating (though I've made exceptions), and this is in that category. But if you're not here for one of the vast number of conferences this hotel hosts, then there are probably better choices. It's not really near the main tourist action in this town (though if you learn how to use the Metro, and you should in this city, getting around is fairly easy; this hotel is a few blocks uphill from the Dupont Circle Metro). The place is big, awkwardly so in my opinion, and it's hard to navigate if you are a business traveler trying to find the room in which your meeting is being held. It's also not particularly quiet, though I've never had too much trouble sleeping here in a number of visits. In short, it has the quality you'd expect of a Hilton, but is really nothing special. You won't at all mind staying there, but the visit may not be memorable.

“Much better this time” We visited this hotel about a year ago and would not have come back based on the last experience, but we got a great rate so decided to give it another try. The good about this hotel: the service was very nice, the location is excellent, the rooms are nice and clean , there is an outdoor pool. The room temperature was more comfortable than many hotels. I think it's still need improvement and here's why: the pool area only had 6 lounge chairs ( we were ok as we were first out there), the sheets are super scratchy and uncomfortable, breakfast is poor (it was included in out price but had it not been would have been $32.00 for both of us. the eggs were runny, the bacon very greasy, no other meat choice, the potatoes were soggy, the grits were watery...just poor. Even for free, next time I will just eat somewhere else (actually the bagel was good) So, all in all, I would still say needs improvement, but better than the last time (I would say 3.5 stars)

“WOW!!” Simply put, a five star experience with very personal service and a great location. The property is small enough to feel very personal, yet large enough where everything you would ever need is located within the hotel. Service was amazing, the room was picture perfect (not in a Ritz or Four Seasons way), and I had the best night sleep and shower you could ask for in a hotel. When I needed a box fan for comfort, I had it. When I needed my shoes shinned at midnight, I got it. When I desired to have some stir fry tofu for room service, I got it......Service, service, service was perfect! Even better, the location to the White House!! Perfect location for to walk to the White House, Dept of Vet Affairs, or just to get a cup of coffee. If I could stay anywhere in D.C., other than the Lincoln bedroom, I would stay at this hotel!

“Great value for the money” We have been going to NYC for years. When we lost our pied-a-terre there after my uncle sold his coop (boo-hoo), we had to stay in hotels like everyone else. Sticker shock!!! We occasionally got a good deal at a boutique hotel off-season, but those became available less and less and have evaporated entirely. I should add we are terrified of BEDBUGS!!! After reading some of the reviews here, we decided to give the Ramada Eastside a chance. Recently, we stayed there for our second time. We have booked a king room both times. The desk staff is friendly enough, although no one has ever offered to take our luggage for us and there is no doorman (that said, the outside doors are automatic, like at the supermarket!). But if someone needed assistance, I imagine they would be able to render it. Both times, the room has been scrupulously clean, and the bed very comfortable. I will mention they use tempurpedic beds, which I find sleep a little too warm, but lots of people like them. I always check the mattress and underneath (see bedbug phobia cited above), and everything is always spotless. The sheets are also good quality. For the price, room size is pretty good. Coffee makers in the room. Shower was fine as far as water pressure and temp. Plenty of clean towels. Free continental breakfast served 6:30-10AM (the usual suspects, --bagels, croissants, various muffiny things, hard-boiled eggs, Yoplait yogurt, bananas, apples, oranges, 3 kinds of cereal (all sugary). Unless you come early, there is no place to sit in the "breakfast" room, since I think there are 101 rooms and maybe seats for 30 people tops, if strangers sit at the same table (which never happened). On the second AM, we grabbed our stuff and juggled it back to our room. NY was having record-breaking heat last weekend, and we did find that the A/C was NOT up to the task. It helped, but set at coolest, the room was still warmer than we would have liked. Checkout was fast (almost never saw any sort of line at the front desk, despite the fact that there only ever seems to be one person there at a time). They happily locked up our bags for safe-keeping after check out so that we could spend the rest of the day in the city. Access to public transport, subway and bus, is nearby. We like this neighborhood, because it's quiet at night. It's easy to get up- or down-town, and you can't beat the price. Also, for those driving in, they have a deal with a lot a block or so away for $20/night. If that sounds like a lot, you haven't parked overnight in NYC lately. Can't speak for how well the free WiFi works, since we usually just use our smart phones. We will definitely stay here again.

“Great family choice at reasonable price” We stayed a week for a family vacation at the Affinia 50 with overall a good experience. The hotel is well located in midtown at 3rd and 50th, close to lots of restaurants and grocery stores. Although more expensive tahn a standard room the one-bedroom suite is definitely worth the money (one bedroom deluxe is worth the extra as well). Adding a rollaway bed to the fold-out sofa kept everyone comfortable. There were some small maintenance issues and the kitchen area is worn, but generally the suite was clean and well equipped. A negative note is the elevators, which are a little small and slow for hotel operation (the hotel was converted from the old Cornell Club and apartments years ago). The 2nd Floor club room is just OK, a little cramped given the hotel size but the paid internet there is first rate. Definitely more oriented for family trips than as a business hotel, but it's OK for both.

“Should be more stars!” We got an amazing value of $69 through Hotwire. We were initially disappointed by how far the hotel is from downtown, but decided it was worth it (we even added a drive by of Graceland as it was convenient even though we didn't want to tour it). The rooms are very comfortable with a large sitting area and huge screen plasma tv. Our kids were so mesmerized they passed on pool time. The beds and amenities are typical high end Hyatt comfort. The only downsides were the location of the bathroom sink (you couldn't turn on the light without it shining right on the beds) and the 75 cent charge that's quietly mentioned on the room card holder for the morning paper unless you call and cancel. We did cancel, but received the paper anyway for no charge. I noticed a lot of other higher end hotels on our trip had this same charge, but was always crossed off. Hopefully this hotel will do the same--it seems very petty. The free breakfast was fine.

“Amazing time, will return” From the moment we checked in, this was a great experience. We spent a weekend here and our room was ready for a late night check-in. It was clean, very roomy and comfortable...that was one of the most comfortable beds I've ever had at a hotel. The only downside is that I wish there was more lighting in the room. The decor was nice and modern and everyone who worked at the hotel was very friendly. The breakfast was also great!! We'd definitely stay here again.

“Great Location, Would Stay Again” A friend and I stayed here for 3 nights. As it was our first time in Chicago, we wanted something with easy access to shopping, lots of things to do and places to eat. The Allerton did not disappoint. We were able to walk to almost everything we wanted to do (parks, navy pier, shopping, restaurants, etc). We did have to take a bus to Bucktown, but the stop was right near the hotel. The staff were friendly, though we didn't interact with them too much. The room was in good condition and clean, but the layout was awkward, not allowing the person on the far side of the bed much room to walk to their side (less than a foot). As two girls, we didn't mind sharing one bed, but it was hard to get around without disturbing one an other. We were very impressed with the fitness center. There are several cardio machines (bikes, elliptical, 4 treadmills) each with their own tv screen and weight machines/ free weights. It was clean and there were always plenty of towels. It is bright and airy and wasn't overly crowded when we were there. The restaurant in the hotel was ok. It had good food, but not really a good place to have a 'night out.' Overall, we would happily stay at the Allerton again; It was the best value for us.

“Pleasant Convention Surprise” Had two conventions back to back and spent 7 nights at the Omni Dallas Hotel. Hotel is new, opened in November 2011. Property is well done with direct connection to the convention center. The room is very nice and features nice amenities for working or pleasure, only hiccups are inconsistent daily room cleaning. Texas Spice restaurant is a wonderful foodie spot and bar, make sure you have Nick at the bar make you one of his signature drinks. Awesome breakfast buffet with farm to table approach and good service.

“Great hotel in downtown Seattle” Traveled to Seattle again for another client. Stayed at the Hyatt with a group of others from my firm. Arrived at the Hyatt early afternoon from the east coast. Fortunately my room was ready (up on the 21st floor with a view over the Roosevelt hotel's red neon sign next door. Guest room looked like the rooms on their website. King bed was very comfortable. Electronic black screen to block out the outside was a nice touch. Although occasionally you could hear a door slam, the room was very quiet and I had a good night sleep. Work desk was fine but there were not enough electric plugs. Was given free wired wifi which was fine. Electronic safe and plenty of closet space. Bathroom included a shower and large deep bathtub. Strangely no cups in the bathroom but there was toothpaste. Location is good. Starbucks in the building with a deli and Japanese restaurant attached. If you wanted to shop, plenty of shopping a few blocks away. The hotel restaurant was a Ruth Chris. Had breakfast and one lunch there. Service and food were fine. The gym was on the 4th floor. No windows but several machines and free weights. No pool but apparently there is a sauna / whirlpool. Was left a bill under my door the night before so check out was quick. Overall, I enjoyed my stay at the Grand Hyatt and would recommend it for work or pleasure. Compared to the FS which I stayed at also, this was a nice alternative and less pricey.

“Great location and nice hotel - Better for business than lesuire” We stayed at the hyatt for a week at the end of April / beginning of may. The rooms were nice and very spacious. It was really nice having a balcony and being able to sit out in the morning (Poolside rooms get sun in the aftenoon road side get sun in the morning). All the staff we came into contact with were very polite and helpful. There was a big conference on whilst we were there but it didnt affect us in any way. The shopping centre is only a 2 minute walk, lots of restaurants and shops and it is really nice having somewhere you can walk to (especially in LA). Only downside is the pool gets shaded in the afternoon (from about 3 onwards so sitting out in the sun is a monring only option. Valet parking was not cheap ($35 per day) but always efficient and not bad for beverly hills!!!!

“Einfallstor nach Chicago” Das Hotel empfiehlt sich insbesondere für eine erste Übernachtung nach einem anstrengenden Transatlantikflug nach Chicago. Das Hotel befindet sich nämlich in fussläufiger Entfernung unmittelbar gegenüber dem Terminal 2 des Flughafens. Trotz der Nähe zu den Terminals und den Landebahnen ist das Hotel überraschend ruhig. Sehr angenehm ist zudem die Tatsache das der sogenannte 'Blue LIne' Train vom Flughafen in die Innenstadt direkt vom Kellergeschoss des Hotels abfährt.

“Friendly staff, Average Hotel” From the time you arrive to the time you exit, the staff are always firendly and attentive which is a real plus. This is one of the hotel's with the huge internal attrium which gives a huge feeling of space. There are lot's of places to sit and have a chat or a drink. I stayed recently for 2 nights whilst attending a workshop at the hotel. The rooms are spacious, clean, with good aircon and a comfortable bed. The bathroom is an adequate size with a small provision of basic amenities. The fitness centre is a modest size with a good selection of weight machines and a reasonable selection of electronic equipment. I did not eat at any of the restuarants nor use room service so I cannot comment on the ,meals. I can however recommend the "Corner Bakery Cafe" which is a short walk out from the front of the hotel. The service here was exceptional and the food amazing. Well worth a walk !

“Average rooms, rude staff” We chose this hotel based on reviews & location to the Philadelphia Convention Center. Front desk & guest services staff are rude. Rooms are average, but bathrooms not as clean as one would expect of a Marriott property. If you can get a good rate for this hotel & need to be close to convention center, then it is convenient. Otherwise, I recommend Alexander Inn, a boutique hotel a few blocks from convention center.

“really a top experience!!! wonderful!” I travelled there with a group and everything was fine! Since the reservation process with Mr. Ryan Cimei until the chek-out everything runs smoothly and perfectly. Extremely polite staff at front desck they did their best for an early check-in even if we arrive 9 a.m. and the ceheck in was scheduled at 3 p.m. Really big and confortable rooms, with big couchbed that fit 4 people confortably and with privacy. Good continental breakfast includded in the rate. Fantastic location walking distance from everywhere and with a matero stop really close. Definitively a wonderful experience!

“Exceptional...” This location is perfect, as well as the service. It's a beautiful hotel and Bob's Steakhouse was excellent. Room service was quick and the food was the right temperature. A must stay while in San Francisco.

“Hope to return” Stayed here for a couple of days whilst on a business trip in Dallas. Very nice hotel, my room was clean, and very comfortable bed. Bathrooms are a bit tired, but bedrooms are well appointed and very comfortable. Breakfast buffet was very good value and great choice. Concierge desk very helpful with good advice of things to do. Overall, a very good hotel with great service. Hope to return.

“Good Hotel, Poor Location” We did not stay here but did a sight inspection for work (I am a travel agent). Holiday Inn Civic Centre is another economy hotel located in downtown San Francisco in their "Civic Cenre". I would recommend this to clients over the Renoir Hotel as the interior of the hotel was of a high standard; it was just the location which lets it down. Rooms are of a good size and family friendly with some rooms interconnecting. Child also eat free of charge when dining with an adult.

“okay but nothing special” I spent three nights at this hotel. I thought the Marilyn Monroe statue in the lobby was tacky. The restaurant had limited menu and the kitchen closed at 10pm. The gym was a joke -- several outdated machines in a small, darkish room. The so-called "business center" is a tiny room with one computer. It costs 40c per minute to go on the web and 25c per page to print documents. In this day and age, who charges people this much to use the computer? The pass card demagnetized easily and I was frequently unable to use the elevator (you need to swipe the card to get the elevator moving). The room itself was nice. Actually, it was a suite, with a bedroom, a sitting room, and a kitchen with a stove, a dishwasher, a full-size fridge, and a set of pots and pans. I think it would have been a great option for a family looking to save some money or for someone staying for an extended period. I used only the coffee maker. There were two TVs in the room -- one in the bedroom and one in the sitting room, with a good selection of channels including two free HBO channels, which I enjoyed. The housekeeping did a good job. The room was cleaned promptly and turn-down service in the afternoon is available upon request. Overall, I don't think this hotel is anywhere near the Marriotts or the Sofitels of the world, but it was adequate (for the most part) for my purposes.

“Excellent Value” Small check in facility but good enough. Staff were very friendly and helpful, one of our rooms even got upgraded to two bedroom suites. The suites are spacious, large fridge and kitchen. Nice dinner table with full table sets ready. Free continental breakfast for every guests, plus free coffee all day. Checkout was swift, will stay there again next time we're in DC area..

“A Tale of Two Hotels” First off, though I only gave the hotel a "3" rating, I would go back, let me explain the rating by pointing out the cons and pros. Cons: Very odd lower level with just a Starbucks and an expensive steakhouse, "Palms," like the one in New York (3 appetizers and 2 glasses of wine for over $100.00) and the main lobby on what is actually the 2nd floor; unfriendly bartenders that couldn't be bothered to come to our table or even carry the drinks out once we ordered; loud noises outside (and I was on the 14th floor! There was a garage across the street and a siren/beeping noise when off each time a car came out of the garage, all day and all night. Could also hear traffic all night, windows must not be sound proof.). Pros: Exceptionally kind and talented valet/bellman; very clean and spacious room with a gorgeous view west to the mountain, nice comfortable bed with nice sheets, very good conference facilities, awesome deck with seating on the 4th floor off the pool with great views of downtown, exceptional location right down on the 16th Street Mall adjacent to great dining and shopping. I c'an forgive the odd lobby arrangement, no big deal, the bartender I can get over (just drink somewhere else), but the noisy room is what caused me to move the rating from a "4" to a "3."

“Quiet, comfortable stay” Located at the crossroad of U.S. 23 and just north of I-270, this hotel does everything well. It's a large, quiet property with generously-sized rooms. all the usual amenities, and a good, solid breakfast. Staff was friendly, efficient and competent...everything to make a visit run smoothly and impressively.

“Very nice hotel” This is a very good hotel. Overall, it's got a great ambiance. The rooms are huge with very nice beds. We saw no bedbugs at all, nor did we have any bedbug bites at all. The bathroom is also quite nice. The central lobby is an atrium with a restaurant downstairs. The gym is small but functional. The pool is indoors. Unfortunately, there is no safe in the room. The location is central phoenix, so it is near most things downtown. Keep in mind, you need a car to get around phoenix, and you really cannot walk around to see stuff.

“Nice Place” I stay at this property do to a, based on their regular rate, very good deal from Priceline. Here's the breakdown: 1. The hotel is well-kept, has a very upscale appearance and in a great location- shopping, restaurants, Philadelphia Convention Center, City Hall,etc. 2. Customer service was excellent. There were enough employees at the front desk that check-in/out lines were kept to a minimum. 3. Rooms were clean and had all of the basic amenities, along with what I believe was a very comfortable bed. My only 2 complaints (and reason I did not give it 5 stars) were 1) Parking -The nights I stayed, the valet parking was full, but we were told we could park in a lot that was across the street and would be cheaper than valet. The lot was very full as it's also used as parking for Reading Terminal Market, and 2 nights cost $70.00. --- Too expensive in my opinion-; I can only imagine the cost of Valet. 2) It's difficult to find food options for late night, but the front desk will provide a delivery menu.

“walk on by” I got this hotel from hotwire. It was rated a 4 star which I completely disagree with. It is described as a boutique hotel so expect very tiny rooms. We had a room with a queen bed and you have a foot basically to walk around the bed. The mattress is not of a 4 star quality. Very hard. The thermostat in the room was not working properly. When set at 72 it felt like 60 and we had to keep changing the temp. We couldn't find the room light switch since it was hidden behind the tv- so you better know where it is before it is nite. Absolutely no where to put your luggage so travel very light. The bathroom is small but very clean -one person at a time. I had a problem with this hotel since I left some articles behind.I have called and left numerous messages to the manager and the housekeeping manager and am still waiting for a call back after a week. So obviously if you have any problem concerning this hotel forget it cause you'll never hear from them!

“Exceptionally nice rooms compared to most Times Square hotels” I attended a convention here and found the room superior to most other hotels in the Times Square/Midtown Manhatten area. The rooms are larger, newer and cleaner than most. The atrium is light, bright and grand. I'm not crazy about the location, which is right in the center of Times Square - I'd rather be 2 blocks awya and away from all of the traffic - but it's nice to have so many theaters right outside the door. This is a good hotel for someone who wants more than a dated, smallish room so commonly found in this part of town. Be warned: you'll pay a few dollars more than in other properties, but you'll appreciate your stay.

“Decor a bit stark” The newest thing in NY is these huber-stark hotels that are so sleek and monotone in decor that there is no warmth about the place. I like the Andaz Fifth Avenue because it is clean and modern and the location can't be beat. The lighting in the rooms is atrocious- you can't even read the newspaper from your bed. Surely Andaz could find an huber-cool floor lamp to lighten the room!? I've stayed here a couple of times and every time I arrive there is no one at the door to help you with your luggage. (You actually have to pull the front doors open.) The staff are friendly, but lack the camraderie and warmth of their Wall Street cousins and just are not as on top of everything. And, similar to comments below, the lobby area is really stark and uninviting. So, relative to other mid-town options I'll stay here, but not at any price.

“Well run property” Spent a two night stay at the Omni San Francisco in January 2008. As a member of their frequent guest program I was sent a coupon for 1/2 off the weekend rate and was able to use it. The staff is excellent. From the on-the-spot front doormen to the absolutely perfect front desk clerk (Bridget? not sure but hope that's correct) I couldn't have been more impressed. Because it was our first stay at this property we were upgraded to a Signature room. The room was beautiful and spotless. Very upscale furnishings and fabrics. The Pecksniff's and Moulton Brown toiletries were much appreciated. Mornings we received complimentary coffee and fresh squeezed OJ delivered to the door along with a newspaper. That perk is yours if you sign up with Omni's frequent guest program online. Overall the hotel was in top notch condition and kept spotless. We enjoyed breakfast both mornings in the dining room. As it usually is with hotel dining rooms the prices were pretty steep for breakfast. However, it was convenient for us and worked out fine. Having lived in San Francisco I would say that the location is definitely geared to the business travelers. It is located in the financial district and is a short walk to the more touristy areas, such as Union Square. The Omni offered us complimentary town car service to Davies Symphony hall which was a very nice surprise! Overall we were treated very well. This was one of the finest properties we've stayed in and it's no surprise it's rated number one in San Francisco. Would return without hesitation.

“Best hotel!” Love this place - my second home. Staff even remembers my name. Stay here! Food is good rooms are clean can't say enough good things. I really really love this hotel. I wish I lived here lol. I seriously have nothing but great things to say about this hotel. Change nothing.

“A Good Four Points, Good Access, Great Rate” Okay, I got in for $99 a night when the rest of the area's comparable hotels were going at twice that rate. For what I got, the value was great and there were no significant complaints. The good: - Renovation is recent, thorough and well-executed. - Highway facing rooms are suprisingly quiet, a colleague said it bothered her but it didn't bother me, didn't even notice it even after requesting a room on the non-available other sides of the hotel. - Decent bar area. - The new room package is well done, the bed is comfortable. - Easy access to Galleria and River Oaks areas. - Decent little bar scene all things considered. The bad: - Some characters lurking about are a little creepy, not as-in drug dealer or thug creepy but more like child molestor creepy. - Front Desk staff is a little disorganized, reminds me of some cheaper motels. When I requested a non-highway facing room, Front Desk Supervisor lied to me and said that there were enough SPG Gold and Diamonds to fill up two thirds of the hotel (all of the non-highway facing rooms). By my count, that's 180 rooms give or take, NO way. They gave rooms away to non-status guests, fine, I arrived late, But I'm a Platinum, they should hold a room for me, especially over Golds which any SPG Elite knows are worthless. Not trying to be a DYKWIA, but just saying, be truthful, don't lie. - Staff leaves stinky steamers in the public restroom, aren't there staff toilets? Just looks (and smells) bad. - Rooms could be cleaner, hairball in bathroom.

“Gem in Austin” We recently spent 4 nights at the Drury while attending the F1 race at COTA. The worst part of our stay was adjusting to the Austin freeway system. Not Drury's fault, in fact the front desk clerk that checked us in said that it was the Land of U-Turns. Everything was top notch with the Drury. We had a 1 bedroom suite on the first floor. The room was large and comfortable. It felt like home away from home with the couch and recliner in the living room. Breakfast was very filling. Full hot breakfast with eggs, sausage, potatoes, etc. The 5:30 kickback was also available in the evening. Although, we only had drinks one night during our trip. There are several restaurants within walking distance. We had dinner at Pappasito's Cantina one night and loved it. Overall, I would highly recommend the Drury to any of my friends and family.

“Good location, best gym ever” Stayed here for four nights while attending a conference at the convention center across the street. The room (1501) was spacious and clean, good view, and no problems. The location is also good, close to the Prudential Center, food on Boylston St., and shopping on Newbury St. The real highlight is the gym and pool area on the seventh floor: huge gym with new-looking machines and weights, with adjoining small pool area. There is also an outdoor patio area if the weather is good. Check this one out if you want to get a good workout while traveling.
