“Great Location. Great Vibe. Very Clean. Still needs some help.” Stayed here four nights recently while attending a conference at the University of Illinois. Had a King bed on the 24th floor. Checkin was smooth at the Preferred guest booth. Customer service was excellent as the young lady was very friendly. Room was typical Westin, but the bed seemed a bit worn as one side constantly pushed down when I sat on the corner. Bathroom was a bit worn and dated as well but I find this at a lot of Westins. My biggest pet peeve is no fans and this one didn't have one in the bathroom. UGh. Still room was very clean and spacious. Since I was situated right near the elevators I was able to hear the 1am drunks stumbling out of the elevator. Oh well. Wifi was terrible in my room. Glad I didn't have to pay for it. The hotel bar was definitely alive after work with people mingling. There was a conference at the hotel (or 2 or 3) so I'm sure a lot of those people frequented the bar. Had a drink or two for a couple of nights but never ate in. One of the elevators also was possessed. Doors would take 4-5 tries to close properly before the elevator would move. Checkout was smooth if not indifferent from the front desk clerk. "Here you go" was the only thing he said as he handed me my bill. You are situated right affront of the Hancock Tower so there is a great buzz around the hotel. Lots of restaurant choices (if not touristy) and lots of overpriced shopping but still a fantastic place to be centered location wise. Would I stay here again? Hmmm maybe. I'm a point lover. But there are lots of hotel options around here. I've stayed at various Westin Properties and this one is probably situated in the middle in terms of typical Westin Experience. Not Bad. Not great either.

“Good location, great service...” Very good hotel for the price. We paid under $150 for our room (granted, a bit small) but left feeling like we got good value for our money. The staff is great--will go out of their way to make sure you are satisfied. While not exactly 5 star, the Vintage Park is a very solid choice for downtown Seattle lodging.

“long term? do not stay here!” This LaQuinta Inn and Suites leaves a lot to be desired. The rooms have an odor, not overpowering, but a musty, dusty scent, and -after being vacuumed it smelled like cat litter for a while. (gross) Also, I question whether they put clean sheets on the bed after a week, or just make the bed. I have also had the maid leave a dirty, used washcloth on the bathroom counter. I requested my weekly room cleaning on Tuesday and they came in on a Monday, my only day off (when I had planned to sleep upon my return to my room). I have privacy issues and I was totally unprepared for maid service, so I found this quite distressing. These units have kitchenettes, but the supply of utensils is strange: 1 room had 4 teaspoons, 1 knife and 1 fork, the next room had 4 knives, 1 spoon and no fork. Some rooms have other cooking utensils and some have none at all. I brought my own pots to cook with and I would not want to see what they may offer in that area. The grouted tile floors in the rooms are disgusting, with the grout really showing the filth in the center of the room and very clean, almost white grout along the corners and under the bathroom counter. The front desk staff --most of them leave a lot to be desired, and only pretend that they care about my concerns. The hotel next door allows a truck driver to park a refrigerator truck where it runs loudly and disturbs guests in the LaQuinta, but no one seems to care about that. This was an awful experience over all and I would never consider staying here again.

“The best staff!” I have stayed at the Burnsley four times. It is a great affordable option for government travelers. It is just a few blocks from the Capitol. The staff is the nicest I have ever encountered at any hotel and I travel a lot and stay in lots of hotels. They have a very convenient shuttle with a very nice driver. Parking is free and the free breakfast is great. My only issues this stay were that the carpet in my room was filthy and the wireless internet never worked. The wired internet worked no problem. My room seemed pretty beat up, scuffed furniture, torn wallpaper...etc. It needed a bit of an update. The rest of the room was very clean. I will continue to stay at the Burnsley when I travel for business.

“Comfortable, good breakfast, helpful staff” This is a typical Embassy Suites layout with rooms around a central atrium. My room was comfortable, but the decor was spartan. There was a nice easy chair and good reading lamp and each room had a large flat screen TV. The front desk staff were very helpful and I enjoyed the cooked to order breakfast.

“Great location, zero complaints great stay!” What a great visit. We arrived early to the hotel (11am) just fully expecting them to hold out luggage while we ventured out. We able to check in immediately. Very clean spacious room walk to everything!

“Great location, huge rooms - but some glaring flaws” After coming from and returning to friendly North Carolina, the curt front desk team was a shock! The only person there who was friendly and welcoming was Lawrence, the Maintenance Engineer who delivered our car as we departed. ($36/day for valet) The rooms, while not shabby, are dark and outdated. The sheets for the pullout bed were worn well past their useful life, and for all the available space in the room, I am left wondering why the bathroom is the size of a postage stamp; it would be easy to move the door over and include the nice little closet area inside the bathroom so there is room to turn around. We got caught in a major downpour during our trip to DC, and had to run for cover back to our room (in a taxi), and once we were locked in there, we discovered that the TVs didn't work; we called the front desk and were told that was due to the rain - WHAT??? I stay 50-60 nights a year in hotels and have never encountered this; we were stuck inside and couldn't even watch TV. Time for a different cable provider. However, the neighborhood is pleasant, and the Metro nearby ... if you can get over the unhelpful staff, this might be the place for a large family, or a lengthy stay.

“Flat screen computer annoying, lounge isnt that great” I have stayed erea couple times. While this property isn't awful, it isn't my favorite hilton property either. I prefer the Palmer House or Wit. Location isn't that great compared to the other two properties. It's a decent walk from the L if you have luggage and are flying and if you are coming from Ohare you need to transfer train lines. In nice weather I don't mind the walk to go shopping, but it is is a hike in bad weather. I usually drive and park my car when I stay here and parking at the hotel is expensive but there is a garage owned by another company directly behind the hotel that is only $25 a day with in/out privledges that is secured. Taxis are easy to get at this property. The exec level on 24 is accessible without an elevator key card which is nice for a fast checkin. The lounge leaves a lot to be desired here. I didn't find the food offerings to be very good at all, I don't typically drink alcohol at Hilton Exec Lounges, but if you do they only have beer and wine which the attendant gets for you and you fill out a drink chit. There is no full service bar like at most lounges. I have never seen them enforce access either, there is a diamond card you are to show the attendant at the front desk and I have never seen them ask anyone to show it for access. I have eaten on site a few times here and the food is good and reasonably priced for hotel food. I really like Kitty O'Sheas.

“Clean hotel, but needs a complete makeover!” The location of the hotel was perfect, in fact I walked everywhere that I wanted to go, I was there for my birthday. The hotel was surrounded by everything that a person could want in terms of dining. I had one problem that really irritated me, when I checked in and I got my keycard, I got to my floor, and the keycard didn't work, so Iand my luggage had to go downstairs to get another card. The lady at the desk informed me that there was a telephone on my floor, I couldn't have called for help. Well it happen again, it sees that every time I left my room and return my keycard didn't work, and neither did the phone, that happen, not one, not two, but three times. I will stay within that location, but never again at the Red Roof Inn in Chicago. Just so you know I went through Hotel.com, in stead of my usually priceline.com. Now I know why they say, go with what you know!

“Very good for NY business travel” I've stayed here twice on business and have another reservation for an upcoming business trip. The hotel is close to Central Park, and perfectly situated in an area with fabulous restaurants and shops. I enjoy the neighborhood feeling of the upper West side. Rooms are clean and well appointed. Staff has been friendly and helpful. My only concern has been that the street can be challenging to find a cab, but a quick walk to Broadway usually remedies that quickly. I've stayed in lots of NY hotels, but this is one that I keep coming back to. Rates are reasonable too.

“Too Noisy for Me” I stayed at this property October 26-28th. I would love to give it a good review since it had a lot going for it. I'll start with the positives. The location provides easy access to restaurants and shops on State Street. The employees were all very friendly and helpful. The room was clean, and the bedding comfortable. The breakfast was fair, with ample bagels, donuts, english muffins, fresh fruit and juice, along with one warm breakfast item each morning. The first morning there was some egg, meat and cheese deal on what looked like a half bagel. It was so-so. The second morning they had waffles, which looked like the frozen kind. I didn't try them. Now for the negatives. As others have mentioned, the fire station is right across the street from the hotel. Even though I made sure our room was on the opposite side, the sirens were loud and plentiful. Additionally, our room was at the end of the hall (room 430), and right below the windows were the air conditioning units for the pool. They ran pretty constantly the whole time the pool was open. Worse than that was the alley below where the neighboring restaurants dumped their trash. All day and into the wee hours of the morning you could hear the trash being dumped, glass breaking and the trash compactors going. With my ear plugs and a pillow over my head, I could muffle the sound enough to get some sleep. So, sadly, I will not stay here again next time I am in Chicago.

“Great Old Hotel” Beautiful, historic old hotel on in the Loop. Lobby is huge, busy--a good place to sit, read, people watch and have a conversation with a friend. Restaurant was good (I only had breakfast and a lunch there.) Decent well-staffed concierge service. Room was well appointed. Terrible view--if you care about that, ask for a room with a view. Plenty of towels and a tub/shower that was comfortable and easy to get in and out of (Im not a kid and that matters these days.) On the second day of a three-day stay, the safe malfunctioned. The initial response was good, but they neglected to get it to work for my last day there which was inconvenient.

“Would Stay Again...” We stayed at the Salisburys over the Easter break for 7 nights, 5 girls in a 1bedroom suite. I had read that the rooms were a little dated,but made up for that in size -- They certainly did! The rooms weren't too dated, all they needed was a lick of paint, and new hostelry on the furniture, and just to go round the skirting boards and re-do the linings (chipped paint etc...) We had two double beds and a sofa bed, the double beds were firm and very comfy -- not what I was expecting at all! Apparently the sofa bed was comfy too. As we were 5 girls, it was a bit annoying having to share 1 bathroom, we managed, I would have preferred two. It was a basic hotel, just a lobby/foyer and 17 floors of rooms. We never tried the $4 breakfast, there was lots of choices for breakfast nearby though (Green Cafe, Europa Cafe, and Metro Cafe). The rooms were clean, comfy and large -- there was only two faults with our stay; 1) The 2nd evaluator was broken for all of our stay which was a pain, especially at the end of the day, when all you wanted to do was get back up to your room , and 2) A Shopping Bag was taken from our room half way during our stay. There was nothing of value in it, it was full of memorabilia of our stay, so it just looked like trash really, after inquiring about the bag frequently we found out that a maid had taken it, assuming it was trash :( Apart from that, we would stay again, maybe not 5 girls, it was comfy and clean!

“Expensive, but nice, friendly and safe” Hotel: The hotel is very nice, the rooms were beautiful, beds were comfortable, and the concierge area was very relaxing with a fireplace and lounges. Service: There is a free hotel car service to downtown areas, which we used to get to Amtrak and to restaurants. The concierge staff were lovely and helpful, and also helped us organise a driving tour (outside of the hotel car service) around 8 Mile and the different neighbourhoods so we could really get a feel for the culture in Greater Detroit. Dining: We went to the Bourbon Steak restaurant in the casion which was REALLY good - I would highly recommend it!!! However, I wouldn't recommend the 24 hour food court - I had a very average chicken burger there and the rest of the dining options looked less than fresh. Overall, I had a pleasant stay at the MGM Grand Detroit and would recommend it to anyone passing through Detroit.

“Free bottled water, free color printing, inviting rooms” I don't usually stay at Hyatt properties but if I do again I will make sure it's a Park Hyatt since it's a far superior experience than your average Hyatt. I appreciate getting more freebies than I'd expect from an upscale hotel: - 2 bottles of water at twice daily room servicing. - Color printing in the business center. - Fitness center offers chilled towels with eucalyptus. - Bath salts next to the tub. The room is far from cookie-cutter and has quality, unique furnishings that make for a masculine yet warm feel. The bed was comfortable and there's a great little nook next to the bed for your phone, etc. There a few things to be aware of: - Wifi is quite fast, but not gratis. - Ironing boards and irons must be requested from the front desk. - Newspaper delivery was spotty; I only received my requested paper the first day of a 3-nt stay. - The fitness center is a bit tough to find.

“Wonderful location” I stayed again at The Dupont Circle Hotel when I found a good weekend rate. This hotel's location is one of my top favorites in Washington DC because of its proximity to restaurants and shops and nightspots and the Metro (Dupont Circle, Red Line). I put this hotel in the "you can't really go wrong" category. This doesn't mean you might not find something to quibble about--the size of some rooms, for instance. But you should feel safe in booking a room here, particularly if you are able to obtain a good discounted rate. Excellent restaurant and bar. I'm not a bar person, but it does seem quite lively. Definitely recommended.

“Vacation in Style” My mother and I celebrated my birthday at Andaz. We stayed 3 nights in Andaz Suite. After booking, I telephoned the hotel reservations and inquired if it was possible to upgrade us to a large Suite and was told that only can be done if initially booked through Andaz directly. To my surprise our regular Suite was larger than any hotel room we ever stayed in. We had corner to adjoining walls of windows with beautiful view of Wall Street and East River. We stayed on the 9th floor, the only thing about this room and I read about it in one of the review that that particular room has faulty heating system and instead of heat it releases cold air, so for the winter I would ask for this room on a different floor. In my case being a survivor of 911 Terrorists attacks I cannot tolerate heat and home live without putting heat on, so it worked for me just fine and air is good as I have difficulty breathing. To sum it all up the entire stuff of the hotel bar none. The property unmarked, love it. Clean, great decor, Wall street style. My dream was to work on Wall street. But to vacation on Wall Street was a unexpected surprise. The restaurant although little bit on a salty side had great food and not overpriced. The hotel price you should expect to pay more, LOCATION. Regarding the bathroom and the mirror. Our corner TV had mirror on the other side, which is one thing I had never seen staying in 5 stars. And that mirror faces window. Plenty of light day or night to put make up and do your hair and for guys to shave. Need magnifying mirror just ask for it. Otherwise, the tub was almost the size of that in mercer and it is for two. Recommended attractions in the area. Battery Park, Liberty and Ellis Island. Enjoy Sea Port and even take a walk on Brooklyn Bridge. If you want to have a view of Manhattan, Brooklyn Staten Island, New Jorsy, and Governor, Liberty Ellis Islands and at the same time to learn everything about you see, take yellow taxi from pier 17 in Sea Port and wallah. One thing that I was impressed with is that I actually felt that I owned apartment in the luxury building. Take advantage of complementary coffees served 24/7, my favorite Late and complementary wine in the evening. Don't forget to tip the guys and girls at the pantry, they will layout their heart for you and if you tip or not they will be there to rifill your glass or make tea or coffee for you. Loved all of the Lobby guys and girl.

“Great Views - Pricey Hotel” We stayed at the Hyatt for a weekend in early August. We did not have a car and found the hotel's downtowns location to be good for walking to all downtown attractions. However, if you needed a vehicle for other San Diego attractions (zoo, Sea World etc) the parking rates at the hotel are high. In general, all of the hotel's amenities (food, drinks, parking, exercise room) are expensive. We stayed in the new tower in one of the smaller suites on the 30th floor. The room was a little larger than an average hotel room but was very clean and had floor-to-ceiling windows with a view of downtown and a slight bay view. The view at night was quite impressive. The overall size of the hotel (two towers that are both 30-plus floors) will make for a busy stay (pool was packed, bar was full etc) but we didn't feel that the crowds actually detracted from our stay. We were able to walk to the San Diego Padres Petco Park and to all of our meals downtown. Cabs were staged right outside for additional transportation needs. The hotel did not have an airport shuttle (a bit of a surprise) and the cab fare is about $10 to the airport.

“Nice place” I stayed here on a road trip. The room was a decent size with floor to ceiling windows. The free drinks and nachos at check in was nice too. Bathroom was a little "old" but other than that, a good place for the money

“Terrific resort.” This charming resort has kept it's amazing Art Decco heritage, immaculate grounds and is truly a destination in and of itself. It is also dog friendly and features som of the best in room dining this traveller has ever experienced. Great value too. Highly recommend.

“Great value” No complaints about the price, cleanliness or location of this property. The staff takes pride in their work and the breakfast is surprisingly good. If you like Hampton Inns, give this place a try. It's a nicer room, a larger room and a better meal the next day.

“Not worth the extra Cheddar!” Up For a Cubs weekend --we usually stay wherever Priceline can put us for $75 or so. That usually means the Hyatt, Drake, Wyndham Chicago, Burnham, Palmer House or Hilton Chicago. Since it was our anniversary and I was able to get a deluxe-view king for about $50 more under Fairmont's Friends and Family promotion (you need an employee id code to get rate--widely available on web)and since Fairmont is generally considered to be a Premium brand a cut above those listed above, we went for it. Pros = Beautiful facility. Our room's view was a knockout, Milennium Park. a slice of the lake, Field Museum and Soldier Field! Bathroom was cool--separate marble shower with huge "rain" showerhead and one of those big round backlit magnifying mirrors that lets you see zits and blackheads at about 10x. Room was also very clean and quiet. Cons = Poor A/C --it was a hot humid weekend. Though the a/c was set on high cool and 64* -- the room never got below 73* I know that is a fine temperature for most--but I cannot sleep unless temp is below 70. I've come to believe that a lot of hotels have some sort of non publicized low end governor and they decide how cool your room will be allowed to get. I want it my way and at a Premium hotel--should be able to get it. I reported it the first morning after the first night and they promised to send an engineer up.--We were out all day so I've no idea if anyone looked at it as they weren't considerate enough to leave me a message. At any rate the second night was the same as the first---hot and humid! First night we went to see "Jersey Boys" (great, highlight of the trip!) and returned to our room at about 10:30 and decided to order up a snack (hotel directory advises 24hr in room dining) after studying extensive menu and making our selections we called to place our order only to be informed "in room dining has closed for the night" !! Here we are in Chicago at a supposed world class upscale hotel and we couldn't get any room service at 10:45 PM !!! I guarantee you I could have scared up a cheeseburger or club sandwich or something at the Holiday Inn in the little Indiana city I live in. Geeez. Location --most reviews call the location good. It is unquestionably in a good, but business oriented neighborhood--other than the CVS across the street, it is about 3 city blocks to any shopping/dining/entertainment venues- (dining choices are severely limited at the Fairmont) so for my purposes, the location is average to poor. Concierge service: I sought the advice of the concierge on two separate minor matters---but each time the concierge desk was overwhelmed and people were waiting 3-4 deep, not how I wanted to spend my time--so I did without their counsel. Was the extra $50 or so per night worth it for the view and the bathroom? IMHO hela no! Won't be back.

“Impressive hotel, yet put off by hairs in bathroom” I stayed at the Westin St Francis for one night on a business trip to San Francisco. The location right at Union Square is fantastic. The hotel is huge, but feels luxurious. The bar serves original cocktails and the elevator has a glass front facing the outside so you can enjoy an amazing view of downtown SF when taking it up to your room. My room was large with a comfortable king bed. The only downside was the cleanliness, specifically of the bathroom. I found various dark hairs all over the bathroom...

“Simply Excellent!” The experience matches the expectation. You expect a great hotel, a great room and a receptive and friendly staff. You get all of this with a central downtown location. Modern decor and amenities in the refurbished room I had on the 14th floor including iPhone and USB ports on the bedside radio and lots of charging outlets. Will definitely be back!

“Not impressed” We stayed here during NeoCon (June 12-15) and had 5 rooms for our group. The A/C sucked to put it bluntly. My room said it was 67 (but it was probably 75) and I had it set on 58 the entire trip. I asked to have it checked and there was no improvement. I got NO additional toiletries in 3 nights. The final morning I had to call down for shampoo because while I travel with my own conditioner, I had more than used up the ONE bottle I was given. I left a note asking the maid to leave the iron out (it was put up each day), to replace a lightbulb (never done) and to leave the shampoo. Maybe she didn't read English but given the notes were left in 3 locations, you would have thought she could have asked someone. The lobby/bar was freezing (which just served to make me more angry regarding the room temperature). The workout facility seemed nice (quite dark) but one didn't work, one other didn't have a good headphone set-up (you had to hold in the plug to get sound) and the 3rd was the only real option if you wanted both headphones and a working treadmill. It was as if maintenance didn't exist at the hotel in my opinion. I will say the bed was very comfortable and I liked the decor. The service was a turn-off tho.

“Overpriced for services offered” The newly renovated Chandler, was disappointing, there is so much competition in NYC. They don't tell you when you book that they have a very limited kitchen and the services they provid are not equal to their stars or pricing. The staff are nice, not very sophisticated, and could use some training

“An Impressive 'Facelift'” Comfort Inn`s renovation of what was formerly The Arlington Hotel is nearly completed. The elevators and breakfast room still need to be refurbished, but the guestrooms, themselves, are beautiful. The hotel is in a terrific location, adjacent to beautiful Madison Square Park and convenient to 3 different subway stops. The compact lobby is certainly pleasant enough and the smiling front desk staff is amiable and efficient. Our room was the biggest surprise. We had reserved a room with 2 double beds and sitting area with a sofa. It was spacious and everything is new and pristine here. All is tastefully decorated, wallpaper and carpeting are unblemished and the original crown molding is still intact and is a nice touch. The bathroom is all new and virtually sparkles. Comfort Inn`s standard amenities are included. We had free local phone calls, iron/ironing board, hairdryer, small refrigerator, free morning newspaper, and continental breakfast included. There is also a small exercise room and business center. Our new beds were firm and extremely comfortable and everything was very quiet, including the new air conditioner which was appreciated in the sultry July heat. For all this we paid $169, which is a great deal for New York. This is a winner and a great value. We`ll definitely be returning.

“A Much Different Hotel in DC” A very different type of boutique hotel..The rooms were very small. The bed was a 5 or 6 inch mattress on a stationary box. The lighting was very dim. The dresser was very organized but made of white plastic. There was not any work space in the room such as a desk. The ceilings were black leather or vinyl. The bathrobes were zebra print and leopard print. The shower was large but unusual. It looked like a spiral cylinder. After returning to the room at 4:00 PM, the room was not yet cleaned. We called to Housekeeping and it took an extra call and an hour later it was finally cleaned. The hotel offered complimentary wine and waters each evening which was very nice. Coffee was also complimentary in the morning. The Lobby opened up to a very nice casual restaurant and bar. Another interesting observation was of a possible "call girl service " that happened as we were returning to our hotel in the evening. Two rather ridiculous girls entered the hotel (obviously not hotel guests) and went quickly up the elevator that was waiting for them upon guidance and direction from a middle aged Asian man...That was very interesting.... Would I ever stay at The Donovan House or recommend this hotel to friends....NO!

“THE BEST NYC has to offer” The Setai Hotel in NYC was one of the best hotels I have eve stayed at. I was upgraded to an apt suite which was 1200 sq feet; it was a piece of heaven in NY where rooms can be the size of a small bathroom. Staff was attentive and friendly- no pretense here just great customer service. I don't usually say this about many hotels but The Setai was perfect. Service at its best without an attitude found at other 5 star hotels.

“Winter Weekend Stay” I'm a Bostonian, who lives in the city, and had the opportunity to stay at this hotel this past weekend. I love being able to wake up right-smack in the middle of the city, especially across from such a lovely place this time of year - Public Gardens. Small but comfortable room with a decent view. Service was great, check-in super easy. I found the lobby and elevators to be a little on the tight side, but such is usually the case with older, more historic hotels. The best part: uber comfortable pillows and bedding!

“Comfortable but completely depressing decoration” Don't stay here if you're looking for a romantic getaway. This hotel is weird. The reception area is decorated in funky red and blue with modern furnishings and lighting. The bedrooms, however, are decorated in various shades of green and beige with matt finishes that make the room drab. Most rooms (except for family suites) face a "courtyard" which is small enough that you can see straight across into the opposite room. But, if you're there just to sleep, the beds are super comfortable and bathroom is well appointed with a nice long bath and plenty of towels. Breakfast is generous but hardly healthy and the eating area can get busy and noisey at peak times. Trays are provided so there is nothing stopping you taking breakfast back to your room. The staff were friendly enough and the area is safe for walking around at night. I would probably shop around before I stayed here again. The room was too average for the price.

“Ready for romance?” The Jane has the feel of 19th Century NYC. The rooms are small, however, they have many retro touches and the decor is very suggestive. If the intention was to create the mood, they are succesful. The decoration is inticing. In addition, the rooms are sound-proof. Even the temperature was perfect. I will return to The Jane for a short stay, it is worth it.

“Location, location, location” This is a fantastic location for seeing shows. There is even a theater right in the hotel. Also, there is no street noise. That can sometime be a problem with other NYC hotels. Beds were comfortable, and rooms were large for NYC. One night there was a large group of teenagers who spent many hours roaming the halls. Hotel security should have been on top of that.

“In need of major renovation” Hyatt just took over this property from Wyndham in June. Renovations have not started yet and will not start until December. The location is great and when Hyatt works its magic the hotel should be wonderful. The decor is very dated and the televisions more so. We were in a suite and the TV'S were two old 19" with NO PREMIUM MOVIE CHANNELS mainly news and sports. We have not been in a property in years with such poor entertainment choices. If you want to watch a football game in HD on a big screen this is not the property for you. The workout room emphasizes aerobics but no weight machines. Hyatt come rescue this hotel. The staff was very nice. There is also a problem with the hot and cold regulation. There are digital thermostats that only go to 60 degrees ( we like it cool) but no matter what is was set the room was 71. THIS PROPERTY IS NOT UP TO HYATT STANDARD AND SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN BRANDED HYATT.

“Nice park and Fly Option” Stayed here for 1 night before leaving from the Midway airport. The location can't be beat if you are flying out of Midway. This hotel is in a complex with other hotels surrounding the Midway airport. There is a Friday's attached to the Courtyard, though we didn't try it. Our room was a bit small but clean and new looking. The staff was very friendly. The shuttle service was very prompt in taking us to and from the airport. We would not hesitate to stay here again for a park and fly.

“Elegant hotel by the Capital” Wonderful hotel. Beautifully appointed rooms with no detail spared. Loved the bath products and amenities in the room. Great location too - close to he white house, top restaurants and shops.

“It's fine - it's a motel” I think I was expecting more than "just a motel" based on the rating that the Lamplighter got on this site so at first I was a little disappointed. But, that's my own fault for having high expectations for what it is - it's a motel!! When you pull up, you realize it's on a street with a few other motels in a part of town that's not really near anything touristy. It's a motel that the parents of the nearby college apparently stay at and I can see why. It's almost within walking distance (but probably driven by most) of the college and two drug stores, but that's about it. My husband and I walked around the block one morning and saw a fraternity/sorority row and a neighborhood. For our purposes, location was just fine. We drove all over the place for the 5 days we were there (La Jolla, Del Mar, Sea World, Zoo, Wild Animal Park) so it was a fine home base location. I felt safe there and the staff at the front desk were nice, although I only talked to them upon check-in. Rooms were fine and the free breakfast was fine as well. It was free so no complaints! Make your own waffles (always fun), 3 cereals to choose from, danish, bagels, OJ, apple juice, hard boiled eggs. My only negative about it was the thinness of the walls. My goodness could we hear anything through them! Our neighbor watched tv at odd hours and so we were listening to it pretty clearly at 2am, 4am etc. That was a little frustrating. It's a very reasonably priced motel in a decent location for driving places. The parking is free so that's a plus!

“Good Value, liked the Battery Park Location” Spent Easter weekend at this Property with a large family group including 5 young children. We all enjoyed the location of the Hotel and found it easy to get around, using cabs and the Subway. We opted for an older-style suite (the Hotel is refurbishing the rooms from the lower floors up) on the 12th floor with magnificent views of the Harbor and city. Some family members stayed in the just-refurbished rooms which are quite modern in style. Marble bathrooms throughout seemed unchanged and are spacious and luxurious. The Hotel is very comfortable and the staff friendly to our children, which we appreciated. I didn't give the highest rating because I thought the Staff, though always willing to assist when sought out, did not offer the very personalized service that I consider a hallmark of a true luxury property. The Guest Reception Team did resolve a room issue at check-in with pleasant efficiency. We chose a Club Suite and the Hotel was in the process of renovating its Club Lounge. The interim Lounge is adequate but I did not see a Club Concierge present, as I have noted at other Ritz Carlton properties. There was no information provided to us regarding the times of the food presentations in the Lounge, which was initially inconvenient. We were not located on the same floor as the Club Lounge, which was fine since we probably received a better view from our room. Offerings in the Lounge were average. I thought the Club Lounge at the property in Washington DC was far superior. We had an excellent dinner at the 2 West Restaurant. Room service was prompt but the food quality just satisfactory. I have to say that I found Housekeeping excellent in this Hotel. Our Suite was always well cleaned and serviced at the most convenient hours. All in all, a good stay and a decent value for NYC. I would definitely return and recommend this Hotel to families.

“nice hotel, friendly, helpful staff” I stayed in Oct and had a nice experience with a clean room, comfortable bed, and pleasant staff. The location was around the corner from Macy's and the subway was steps away. It was a congested area on Broadway, but the hotel was quiet. No problem with getting cabs, they were parked in front of the hotel. I would stay again.

“Always a great stay at the Capital Hilton” This is our 2nd stay at this property. The staff is always pleasant and the location can't be beat. I've always viewed the $42.00/night parking fee a bit absurd, but it's to be expected in DC. The Executive Floor amenities for Diamond Level Honors members is also nice.

“Ein modernes Kimpon-Hotel mit tollem Blick auf Manhattan” Wieder einmal ein sehr stilvolles und modernes Kimpton-Hotel, das auf der 11th Ave Ecke 48 Str liegt. Wir hatten ein wunderschönes City View Premier King Zimmer (mit Badewanne mitten im Zimmer, zusäzlich separate Dusche) in der neunten Etage mit Blick nach Osten auf Manhattan. Da mein Partner während unseres Aufenthaltes im Hotel Geburtstag hatte, gab es zur Begrüßung eine Flasche Sekt. Zusätzlich haben wir eine Behandlung im zum Hotel gehörigen Spa gebucht und dort eine wunderbare Massage bekommen. Das gesamte Personal war sehr zuvorkommend und der Zimmerservice einwandrei. Ein weiteres Plus: Auf dem Dach des Hotels befindet sich eine nette Bar mit genialem Blick auf Manhattan - das sollte man sich nicht entgehen lassen. Leider liegt das Hotel etwas abseits der Subway-Linien.

“Great Hotel in Downtown LA” I am happy to finally have a decent place to stay in downtown LA! The Ritz Carlton is a sleek, spanking-new property well located in the downtown area. I was in a standard King room that was commodious and well appointed. The bed was heavenly and the large bath was a delight. The only drawback is the lack of a Lobby. The entrance from the street is small and resembles an office building. There is a small desk with helpful staff, but there is no central meeting place where one can meet colleagues, or attend to other travel-related businesses.

“The best hotel in NY, discrete heaven yet full of celebrities” We again went to the NY4S which we simply love to go everytime. The rooms, the service and everything about this hotel is just perfect. It lacks a swimming pool if you need one, we do not in NY. But its Ty lounge is fabulous, the staff is just great and its restaurant Joel Robuchon offers an exquisite world class food experience in the utmost relaxed service atmosphere so to us it is simply perfect. Our daughters loved the fact that the hotel had Jennifer Aniston and Justin Bieber in the hotel. Last year the Boston Celtics where hanging out in the lobby, never felt so small! Guests there are all discrete and all enjoy the peaceful atmosphere commanded by its magnificent entrance hall. So that is probably why all celebrities feel good staying there, enjoying themselves and not being disturbed. One of these celebrities is actually my wife which also enjoys the peaceful and distinguished atmosphere. The 4SNY is always a wonderful experience so we keep returning to it everytime.

“Fine hotel” This is a belated review as we stayed last year. I agree with the positive comments made by others. This hotel offers good value and a good location in Greenwich Village. Friendly staff made the stay enjoyable. Clean well equipped bathroom and comfy bed. Room was barely adequate size for two adults and luggage which is the reason I give four stars instead of five.

“Historic hotel” I stayed two nights while attending a conference at the next door Hilton Chigaco hotel. The Blackstone is an historic hotel that has been very tastefully remodeled and well kept. Everything was very clean. The decor of the hotel is great - if you get a chance poke your head into the ballroom on the second floor - very cool. The rooms were very spacious for an older hotel - the bathroom was quite large. I had a room on the 12th floor overlooking Grant Park. Relatively quiet for being on Michigan Avenue. The public rooms of this hotel are smaller, especially compared to the enormous Hilton. The concierge lounge is very small - maybe seating for 12 people. One of the skimpiest breakfast and snack selection I have ever encountered at a Marriott property. It is about 10 blocks south of the Chicago river and the heart of the Magnificant Mile. Walkable, but it is a hike. It is two blocks from the red line that will connect you with the "loop" and also the blue line to O'hare airport. My only issue with the hotel is the staff was just kinda there - nothing extraordinary. Great service when you asked for something but not outgoing at all. During the check-in process they barely greeted me and did not speak at all unless answering a question. Amenities were never explained, etc. Not a huge deal but usually high end properties are looking for ways to make your day. This is the only reason they did not get an excellent rating from me. Everything else was wonderful.
“Perfect” Perfect as always. What else can I say? Service, rooms, location are all what you would expect from the 4 Seasons. Look no further.

“Good Value in Boston” Visited this hotel a couple months ago, but did not get around to writing until today as work has kept me quite busy. This hotel is a hidden gem in Boston. It is housed in the an old YWCA building, but the hotel has been completely renovated transforming it into a cute boutique hotel. The location is fantastic and there are a ton of restaurants within walking distance. The rooms can be a little smaller, but for me it was fine. I believe that they may have larger rooms, but I did not feel the need to upgrade. The price was great compared to other hotels in the same area. I felt very safe and the staff was friendly and helpful. I will be staying here again on my next trip to central Boston!

“My third time there - and as great as the first!” I love the MO DC - for me its location is perfect as I like to visit the Mall. This time I walked to the Jefferson Memorial and around the tidal basin. As a treat for my parents 50th wedding anniversary I brought them along and got them a nice water view room. Kudos to the staff for remember the occasion and surprising them with a special anniversary snack - so much appreciated! MO DC is #1

“Great location, great breakfast” Stayed at this Le Meridien for work and would stay there again if I had business in this part of town. Pros: Clean rooms (a bit worn but nice nonetheless), amazing breakfast with eggs to order and complimentary "eye opener" fruit juice shots designed by super chef Georges Vongerichten. Good room-service. Friendly and helpful staff. It was also a very good value for the price and was close to the location where we had our business meetings. Cons: Not enough lighting in the interior rooms, the parking charges are outrageous considering that there is free parking across the street at the Galleria, the elevators are slow and there are only two (one was broken part of the time), the gym is tiny and inadequate, but there is a 24hr fitness close by.

“Nice hotel but you can do better in Philadelphia” Definitely an upscale hotel but nothing all that dashing. Front desk staff is professional as are the valets and bellhops. The rooms are nicely decorated and spacious. The bathroom was especially nice. We had a room on the 13th floor facing north which was certainly a plus as far as the view. The bed and pillows were extremely comfortable. The downsides: while the hotel is situated in Old City (where the main tourist attractions are located, Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, etc), there is a major highway separating the two. There is a walk way over the highway but it takes away from the total experience of being in such a historic area. There is internet access available in the rooms at a charge of $10 per day. At a hotel of this caliber, you would think it should be free. Not sure if wireless was available. As can be expected, parking is rather expensive, about $20 per night. No free parking is available anywhere nearby. Meters abound but they are patrolled ruthlessly by meter maids from 8am until 10pm everyday of the week including weekends.

“The Hard Rock Hotel: in the thick of things” This is a stylish hotel located right on North Michigan Avenue, a five minute walk from the Orange "Loop" line that will get you to and from Midway Airport. Forget about taking a taxi: the train is a $2 ride and less than 40 minutes away. Our room (1802) was immaculate and spacious (350 sq ft, we were told). Decorated in grays and white, the room was comfortable and soothing, not jarring. On the other hand, we found the lighting to be very poor and had trouble reading, finding keys, etc. No kidding. The bathroom was also quite dark and it didnt have a heating lamp. On the positive side, however, there were Aveda products in the bathroom, the windows were huge, so during the day there was tons of natural light, and no issues with darkness. The king size bed was very firm, but had a plush pillow top which made it very comfortable and inviting. We had a largish TV with a DVD player. There is a safe and munchies. The gym is perfect, equipped with treadmills, ellipticals, bikes and weights. It is open 24/7 and there is video surveillance for safety. There are towels, water, headphones, disposable ear pads, and complimentary green apples. Suggestion: if you are on a floor below the 22nd, take the elevator up to 22nd, then down to L2 to get to the gym. This way you dont have to traverse the lobby. The front desk staff is amiable, and very attentive. I read some other reviews about nasty personnel, but did not have that experience at all. I got a free newspaper with a smile, a free stamp when I needed it, change and all the coffee I could tolerate in the morning. The Hard Rock is located less than a 20 minute walk from the Water Tower, the Drury Theater, John Hancock, and magnificent mile. For those who like a thrifty breakfast, we recommend Gourmet Pantry at 155 N. Michigan Avenue [--]. This deli made a delicious egg on a toasted roll with butter on a Sunday morning, no less: $1.99. The hotel has a breakfast buffet for $15.00 per person, but we did not partake of it. We would stay at the Hard Rock again, and think it is great for people with "tweens." Not sure about the toddler set, though.

“Excellent souvenir” Bel hotel au centre de Houston downtown dans un quartier qui se desertifie a la nuit tombee et les week ends... neanmoins central il permet de rayonner dans la ville et est facilement accessible...belles prestations generales avec un souvenir emu pour la wine & beer party suivie en soiree de la cookies party !! ... Petite piscine au top de l'immeuble avec vue sur la ville et la possibilité de s'y rafraichir les jours d'ete ...

“Perfect location” We stayed here for an opera weekend in late Feb. and got a stellar rate with Marriott eBreaks. The location is perfect, the rooms comfortable and the staff efficient and helpful. Free breakfast was unusually good. The hotel is mere blocks from the Mag Mile and very close to a Dunkin' Donuts with extended hours (not to be underestimated during freezing Feb.). Highly recommend.

“Save your money” Upon arriving check in was quick. When we arrived at our room we noticed an unpleasant odor in the hallway and once again in our room. This odor was confirmed by others in our group that stayed in different rooms on the same floor. The room was not great but nice. Our bathroom had no toilet paper so I called down to the front desk and asked for some and also complained about the odor in our room. The operator said she would send engineering up. Twenty minutes later we received our toilet paper and never heard anything again about the outcome of the smell we dealt with the rest of the trip. We emptied our fragrance bottles during the trip to make the room smell pleasant. Our fault for not complaining again I guess. The view from the room was beautiful but it is not worth it considering the trolley bells and the freight train horn that goes through at 3 am. Unless you’re a heavy heavy sleeper you can’t have your window open. I was even awaken by the aforementioned sounds with the window closed. The common areas of the hotel are very nice and the location to the gas lamp and seaport village is convenient. The prices at the Hyatt for a beer ($8+) and a Mai Tai ($10+) are a bit of gouging in my opinion but I expected that and did most of our leisure activities outside the Hyatt. On a side note we stayed in the older tower so I cannot review the new tower. I have said this more than once, you just don’t get what you pay for these days.

“clean and comfortable” If you want to be near Herald Square, you can hardly do better. The F train is literally right next door. The room is quite large for the location and comes with a microwave and mini-fridge. The lobby is tight and crowded, and if you arrive early there's a good chance that your room won't be ready, but you can leave your luggage with the concierge. We didn't try the breakfast; it was easier just to run out a buy a few groceries instead. I did notice crumbs under the TV set. That attracts vermin!

“コストパフォーマンスは最高レベル” 払った金額に対するパフォーマンスは今までいろいろ泊ったホテルの中で最高レベルと思います。基本的にサンフランシスコ市内は高額なホテルが多いですが、リーズナブルな価格で泊まることができました。朝食はコンチネンタルブレックファストですが、マフィン、食パン、ベーグルからチョイスでき、コーヒー、紅茶、オレンジジュース、ココアなど飲むことができます。オレンジ、リンゴなどその日によって違いますがフルーツも食べれます。セルフサービスで、自室に戻って食べる形式です。またインターネットも無料ですが、泊った部屋の位置が悪いのか、無線LANは入りにくかったですが、有線の接続ポートもあるので、そちらを使うと快適でした。(ということで、短くてもいいので、できれば有線のLANケーブルも持っていたほうがいいです。)部屋には冷蔵庫(ミニバー)がありますので、ちょっとした飲み物なら冷やしておけます。バスルームは湯船ではなく、シャワーですが、共有(安い宿はこの形式が多い)でなく個室についていますので、気兼ねなく使用することができます。ホテルの場所も日航ホテルの前で、パウエルのケーブルカー乗り場まで100mくらいです。周りにはレストラン、スーパーマーケット(コンビニ?)もありますので快適に過ごせるとおもいます。部屋の広さは、価格なりですが、日本のビジネスホテルくらいはあり、ホテルで寝るだけなら十分すぎるほどです。内装はかなりきれいです。(リフォームしたばかりかも?)ネガティブな点は、隣や、上の部屋の歩く音などが聞こえる(フロアは木製?)ことです。私は、慣れてますので熟睡しましたが、音に敏感な方にはお勧めしません。(もっとひどいホテルもありますが・・・。日本のビジネスホテルでも状況は同じと思います。)

“Busy but good” This hotel tends to be on the busy side (although all Regencys and Grands tend to be) but it is a good location and quite nice place to stay. They have remodeled since my last visit and the room and lobby are much more pleasant. In addition, the 24 hour Eistein's is good for early flights out and the Q restaurant is quite good--at least much better than the typical fake British pubs and Mexican places that line the Riverwalk. It is close to the Alamo and right on the Riverwalk for the tourist types as well. I did end up with an interior room (although with a patio) which I hate, but it was crowded and my reservation was very last minute (like 15 minutes before arriving). Still, the atrium lobby made this not so bad. The room was a little on the warm side and the AC didn't seem to want to work, so I couldn't open a window, but all in all the stay was nice. The room was spacious, the desk was one at which one could actually work and there was a reasonable access to plugs in the desk. Good choice for a business traveler or tourist

“Préstations de haute qualité !” J'ai reserve cet hôtel car je suis fidèle aux Intercontinentals lors de mes voyages. Il s'agissait de ma première visite à Boston. L'hôtel est très bien situé juste à coté de la "South Station" et du centre ville. Lors de notre arrivée, nous avons été upgradé dans une suite supérieure de 110 M2. L'accueil qui n'a été offert était très chaleureux avec un bon descriptif des services dans l'hôtel. L'hôtel est divisé en deux sections, une partie avec des chambres et l'autre partie est la résidence "Intercontinental". Il y a deux restaurants, le premier "miel" avec cusine française et l'autre est japonais. Il y a aussi un bar à champagne. La suite était spacieuse, agréable et confortable. Le lit king size était moelleux. Nous avions une belle vue sur les dock à l'arrière de l'hôtel. Le centre remise en forme est bien aménagé avec une belle salle de sport et une belle piscine. Nous avions aussi accès au hammam. Malheureusement, il n'y avait pas de jacuzzi. Si vous en avez les moyens car il faut compter 400 dollars par nuit, n'hésitez pas à vous rendre dans ce magnifique hôtel. Boston est une ville assez chère même pour se restaurer. Mais on peut trouver des chaînes de restaurant pour diminuer l'addition. Par contre si vous voulez vous faire plaisirs, n'hésitez pas à vous rendre à "top of the hubs", dans la tour "Prudentiel", vous aurez une vue imprenable sur le ville.

“Huge rooms, great views, ideal location... but not a true hotel.” OK, so the name says Marriott, but this is not a full service hotel. It's part of their condo, time-share vacation properties. You can't always get a room, but if they're available, grab 'em! The rooms are huge... big living room and separate bedroom, complete w kitchen. The waterfront views are to die for. The staff is very friendly and informed, especially helpful for visitors. The hotel is right at the entrance to the MBTA Blue line (from the airport) and five minutes walk to Faneuil Hall / Qunicy Market. Free wifi too. But there is no restaurant or room service. The breakfast service in a conference room is a token effort and doesn't offer much. Try one of the local diners in the area. All that said, this is property is a much better deal than any other Marriott property in the area.

“I could get used to this” My 'complimentary' one-night stay was arranged by the airline after my international flight had been abruptly rescheduled, resulting in my having to stay an extra night in Houston. Check-in was rapid and efficient, and staff were professional. I was given a spacious room on the executive floor which came with a very comfy bed, a small balcony with a sweeping view of the area, and free Wi-Fi. However, I was a little disappointed in the layout of the bathroom - somehow, the bath and WC had been tucked in a tiny corner next to the closet; the lighting was also somewhat too dim. I was also given free use of the executive lounge/business centre which was also the venue for the daily self-service continental breakfast. I'm glad I had chosen to stay in The Galleria district because the hotel was only 5-10 mins walk from good eating and retail establishments, making it convenient for me to do some last-minute shopping before heading for the airport. I decided to call for room service before checking out - this was fairly fast and friendly, a delight. Overall, I was very pleased with my experience and wouldn't mind returning.
“Great!” Beautiful historic hotel. Great service. Original grand lobby. Close to river walk and downtown attractions. Clean, great price.

“Big Surprise more than expected” We popped into Philadelphia, booked this Hyatt last minute, from the moment we got in the door till the moment we left, it felt like home. the staff at the desk, the waiters in the hotel restaurant and the concierge who knows everything, and he really does. We were pleasantly surprised and we we given a great room overlooking the water, beautiful unexpected views, quiet clean and comfortable.

“A good choice but” A good choice : - room are very clean - staff friedliness is above average - a central location for visiting new york - free wifi in the room - quiet room (at least for our room on 26th floor) - free fitness center but - room are very small - breakfast at the hotel is really standard and not fancy - no swimming pool, sauna or steam bath - price is quite high

“Good location” The location and staff were the highlights of the hotel. I was "placed" at this hotel because of its proximity to UCLA where I was a patient. The hotel is more like a motel with amenities like a microwave and refrigerator. The room was large but when we pulled down the bedding there were a lot of long blonde hairs on the fitted sheet and under it. We called the front desk and they gave the excuse that it was probably from a maid. They offered NOT to change our sheets but we could have the sheets and change it ourselves. I was not impressed with the excuse and I did see most of the housekeeping staff the next morning, none of them were blonde. The one vending machine in the dining area on the first floor only sold sodas, no water. We didn't try the breakfast as we saw the rust of the toasters and general uncleanliness of the area, made me not want to take the chance. I would have rated this hotel as "terrible" but most of the staff was very friendly and helpful and the location to UCLA and restaurants in the area helped.

“This Hotel is..Delicious!” Stayed here for one night with friends. I booked the hotel for the "no frills rate" of $89.00. There was no way we were going to pass up the opportunity to stay at the number 2 most popular hotel in DC for that rate. The hotel is in an excellent location--equisdistant between dupont circle and georgetown (though easier to get to from dupont circle metro). We had a deluxe room with 2 double beds. The room decor is impressive--traditional but elegant and not at all stuffy or drab. The beds were fluffy and everything was clean, most importantly. This is a hotel room that causes you to think twice about leaving it before the start of a long day or after the end of one. If the walls were made of chocolate, this place would truly be heaven on earth! On my next visit to DC I definitely will be back to the St. Gregory if the price is right again. This hotel is number 1 in my book!

“Clean but Hot, Hot, Hot” We checked in only for one night before a flight the next day. The hotel itself was clean and neat. The property was also well kept and quiet. PROS - Internet worked just fine. Night manager was nice and printed out some items for me. Room was clean. Two queen bed suite had fridge, microwave and flat screen. CONS - It was HOT the whole night. Room temp was on 90 when we came in. Only got down to 78 degrees, 5 hours later. We asked about another room and it was equally as hot as the first. Manager did let us try to get that room cool too but we couldnt wait up all night for that to happen. Mr. Patel was nice about letting us turn in both keys the next day. Overall, it is indeed a nice property and I am usually a little leary about staying at Super 8's. This property just needs to tell the cleaning staff not to completely turn the AC's off, or turn them on in the units that are reserved. I'd stay again, but only if Mr. Patel agrees to turn the AC on wayyyyyy before. Husband said breakfast was decent...the usual waffles, cereal, and biscuits with gravy.

“So much space in the heart of Georgetown” The lobby looks like a college dorm room, but the rooms are so huge that makes up for it. We had 1 bedroom with a king bed and a full bathroom, a separate room with a double bed, a full bathroom in the hallway, living room and full kitchen. It is perfect if you are traveling with a family or large group. The rooms are very clean and there are even Bath & Body Works products in the rooms. The people who work at the front desk are pretty incompetent and overcharged us for parking so just double check your bill. There is a continental breakfast that I did not take advantage of. The rooms are not super modern, but immaculately clean and perfect for our needs with all of the space. We could walk to everything in Georgetown so that was very convenient. There is no valet or taxi service, but taxis were were easy to hail just by calling first or walking to the end of the block.
“Parking is expensive” Everything was good except the parking was not cheap!

“Concur: Middle of Nowhere” Now, with that said, the staff is on-task, on-message and bends over backwards to serve its guests (whom, at the time I was there, ranged from the University of North Texas Mean Green to DynCorp, to several overnight conventions). Exercise facility is above average. The one restaurant is marginal. The lounge is a friendly atmosphere. Rooms are above average and the housekeeping staff does a great, considerate job. Adjoining golf course is very nice, and if I get back there, I'll play it. Now, the fact of the matter is that this Marriott property is so far removed, that I doubt I would every stay there of my own volition. While the hotel provided shuttle service to Roanoke and the WalMart, there is ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. ZERO. ZILCH. NADA...within walking distance of this hotel (except the Speedway across the street).

“Outstanding!!!” 1/2 block off Michigan Mag Mile. Clean, modern, quiet, and comfortable. Staff was helpful and friendly. $28 a day to park in adjoining garage (with $7 discount from hotel). $20 extra per day for a room rate that included a terrific bfast buffet for 2 adults and our daughter. This hotel is also within easy walking distance of Navy Pier, Hancock Building, Chicago River, and lots of great places to eat (Gino's East for Pizza!). I would definitely stay here again.

“Well pleased...” Stayed at this hotel overnight for a recent business meeting. Front desk personnel were pleasant and efficient. Concierge was very helpful in trying to find a restaurant for me, but it was raining and late so I opted for room service (french onion soup which was very tasty, and a Cobb salad, which was not as good). My room 541, was at the end of the hall and uniquely shaped. Because it was on a corner it had a long hallway in the room to get to the sleeping area. Bed was very comfortable, shower was large enough for two people comfortably and was an pleasing marble with blue accent tile line. Only bad thing was the handle on the door to the shower was too small to grasp from the inside, and the way the shower is designed you can't turn on the water without being partially IN the shower and so COLD water hits you before you can turn the knob to warm. The room is unique not only is it's shape but in that three of the four walls of the room are all glass floor to ceiling! Since the hotel is nicely located near the water and harbor area the view was engaging and almost surround although there were some office buildings on one side of the view. I totally enjoyed the glass walls, but it did make it so I had to turn up the heat at night, and I did hear street noise in the morning. The elevator was shaped like an arrow and all glass as well. The a/c system was apparently piping out some freshly scented freshner because it was the first thing I noticed getting off the elevator. Wish I could replicate that at home! Their fine dining restaurant was closed oddly enough (it was only 8pm) so I can't comment on it. All in all I would definitely stay here again and recommend it. I have pix on on my cell phone and when I slow down traveling I'll try to post them.

“Good location, but nothing special amenity wise” The location was convenient to everything - we did a whole lot of walking because we could. The room itself was nothing special, although I will say the bed was very comfortable (albeit a double was a bit small for us). The cable channel selection was very limited - we wound up watching a DVD on my laptop. The lack of free internet, the posted charging of $1.50 for local calls and $8 bottled water created what seemed like an "out to get you" brand damaging atmosphere. Granted none of this is horrible, but there's other hotels as nice looking to please you rather than nickel and dimeing you. I highly recommend visiting the Art Institute and Millennium Park. Blue line from the airport was a breeze to use.

“You get what you pay for” The room price is pretty high when compared to other hotels, but you get what you pay for, and in this case it was worth it. The room was large and had a seperate bath with a rain shower. It is also worth paying for a "view" room. I loved my view of the Chicago River. Being pretty centraly located everything is within a short cab ride or walk of the hotel and the staff is very helpful. The little cafe off to the side is not bad either.

“2nd stay as good as the first” We stayed here a couple of years ago, and then again in Sept/Oct 2010. The hotel is very nice. The staff is good. The room was in good shape and despite the vending machines right across the hall, it was very quiet. The continental breakfast is good, with meats, eggs, fruits, cereals, breads, and waffles available. The hotel provides courtesy transportation to locations within 3 (I think) miles. This was very handy. Shop around to all of the online booking sites to find the best rate. I found a rate that was $30 less than the negotiated group rate.

“Food was great, walls were thin” I recently stayed at the Washington Hilton for a conference and the rooms were quite pleasant with sufficient plugs for electronics and room to work. The food served for continental breakfast as part of the conference was fresh and quite pleasant. I really appreciated some healthier alternatives e.g., greek yogurt, fresh fruit, English muffins, oatmeal, etc. There were also danishes and muffins available if you wished. Great location-it's a short walk to the metro My only complaint relates to the thinness of the walls-I could hear the TV from the other room in the background. It wasn't loud enough to hear what program they were listening to, but made for an annoying background sound when I was trying to work.

“I can't recommed it” The location is really good and bad. It's just blocks from the great historic sites, BUT... we paid $180 to stay in a one bedroom suite. We were in awe of how big and beautiful the room was when we walked in. It had a great historic, boutique feel to it. The room was very clean... The bedroom portion of the suite located at the end of the 2nd floor is located less then 25 yards from the I95 off ramp. The noise is worse than I could ever explain. We got NO sleep that night. It sounded as though we were laying on the shoulder of the interstate. There were sirens, speeding cars, buses braking... LOUD! In addition, the staff never denied my belief that the room was directly above the hotels kitchen. I hoped to get to sleep early that night, BUT there were pans banging until @ 11pm. AND if that's not bad there is a parking lot directly outside the room and there were parking lot attendants laughing it up into the late hours. I didn't want to switch hotels as this trip was a special treat for our nephew who slept in the living room on a pull out couch and couldn't hear the noise and I didn't want to ruin the stay for him - we promised him a cool historic inn. In the morning while my husband and nephew enjoyed the nice, complimentary breakfast I stopped by the desk to politely tell the clerk about our night. She was nice - but her comment was basically that if I had read the travel books many of them warn of the street noise. I guess I should have read the books. Later, on the way back to our room we were stopped by Antonio, the owner, who offered us the smoking floor suite. Due to my allergies and we had a busy day planned I declined. If I had more time I would have checked other hotels. It's a real cute place. The staff is nice enough. The rooms are clean. The free breakfast was good. The A/C was quite adequate in 95 degree weather... - but what good is any of that if you can't sleep. I really can't stress just how loud it was. For $180/night I just want to sleep. I will stay somewhere else the next time.

“Good hotel, good facilities” We stayed at the hotel for almost three weeks, as my husband was in Houston on business. We were given a good sized room, with seating area and comfortable bed. The bathroom was also a good size. I used the hotel gym on most days, and during the day time it was empty. It was well air-conditioned and there was water and fresh towels available to use, as well as a TV and a good selection of gym equipment. Also good was the hotel pool, which had a lot of sun loungers (but unfortunately no parasols), although at weekends this seemed to be filled with teenagers and became a no-go zone if you wanted to just chill out poolside, which was disappointing. Also disappointing was the poolside service...which was pretty non-existent. My husband and I had to return inside to the bar to get drinks, even though there were drink menus by the pool. We did enjoy the hotel bar called Black Gold, which has a very Texan feel to it, with an American Shuffleboard available to use, which was a great talking point with other guests. The bar also serves great bar food, and we particularly enjoyed the fajitas, of which one portion was big enough for two to share!

“Rest your head at the med” I stayed here last year and would happily recommend it again. The staff were friendly and helpful without being in-yer-face intrusive. The room was well lit, decorated and equip with everything we needed for our stay and more, the free Starbucks coffee was a lovely Seattle touch and the microwave and refrigeration facilities we requested were very useful, although somewhat unnecessary as Seattle’s fresh flavours shouldn’t be missed for a microwave meal... no matter how tight your travel budget. The location is fantastic, everything we wanted to see was commutable by foot or public transport (very near the monorail). As a side issue I’d also seriously recommend visitors buy the Seattle frommers guide for the walking tours of the city and surrounding neighbourhoods, they’re fantastically informative and fun... and with a landmark like that space needle as a reference point you need not worry about getting lost :) Enjoy this beautiful city and hotel I wish to visit again very soon.

“Best rate on Travelocity for New Years weekend very worth it!” The Flatotel is on a quiet one way street , 52nd, right between 6th and 7th. The front desk staff and concierge were very knowledgeable and friendly. Check in and out were both a breeze. The room was HUGE by NYC standards, you could definitely make the room into a cave with the massive drapes if you wanted to. Bathroom very nice, was hard to get water to come out of just the shower head (not bath faucet). Mojo the restaurant was good, one of my guests had the chicken picatta and said it was the best chicken she ever had! Continental breakfast was okay and love the free apples in the lobby! I will definitely stay again.

“Excellent option for Lower Queen Anne / Seattle Center” I stayed at the Mediterranean Inn for 4 nights in early December. The hotel met all of my needs and was an excellent value. Location is excellent if you want to be in Lower Queen Anne, and just a short walk from Seattle Center (Space Needle, Experience Music Project, etc). Within 1-2 blocks there were excellent coffeeshops, a variety of food options, a great independent record store, a post office and bank/atm. Buses downtown are also easily accessible, and it's even walkable on a nice day. The room was nice enough - not overly large, but fine for me. Flat-screen TV, desk, fairly comfortable bed, large bathroom. Internet access cost $5/day or $15/week (i think) and wireless was weak, but they also provided an ethernet cord. Kitchenette had a mini-fridge, microwave and sink which was useful. Front desk staff was friendly and accommodating - they helped call cabs, stored our bags in a locked room before our late-night flight, etc. Overall no complaints - nothing over the top, but got the job done and was a pleasant stay. If you're looking to stay in Lower Queen Anne I can't imagine a better option that the Mediterranean Inn.

“What a fantastic hotel!” We headed to Baltimore to explore the Inner Harbor, eat crabs, and sing at the infamous Phillips piano bar. This year, since we opted to take the kids, we stayed in walking distance to the Inner Harbor and chose the new Hampton Inn. Not only is the location ideal, the hotel is located in a renovated bank building. It's historic on the exterior yet new and amazingly clean in the interior. The room was beautiful, although it had a view of an abandoned building next door. It didn't matter, as we only were there to sleep and shower. The breakfast buffet had wonderful choices and was VERY busy. Those ladies work there tails off! The staff was very pleasant and we would go back in a heartbeat.
“立地がよかった。” 坂のアップダウンはSFなのでしょうがないとして、それ以外の立地としては便利だと思う。ユニオンスクエアやショッピング街など主要なランドマークは徒歩圏内だし、チャイナタウンはすぐそこなのでお粥が好きな方、もしくはアメリカ料理に飽きた方にはおすすめ。 買い物が目的だったので、サックスフィフスなどのデパートが徒歩で行けたのが便利でした。

“If Ikea furnished a hotel...” ...it would be the Metropolitan. Kinda cool at first but by the end of the week it left me cold. Which sums up my experience at this hotel nicely: It's nice, but there are some things that annoy me, too. The bed is very comfortable. Rooms are on the small side unless you get bumped to an executive level. Great location. Indifferent bell staff, great front desk people. The restaurant is decent but pricey and there are lots of dining choices in the surrounding neighborhood, too. Overall, I've been pleased enough to stay there twice and return again tomorrow, so I can't knock them too hard, but if they'd just kick the service up a notch this would be an outstanding hotel.

“Very good city hotel but could use a better restaurant for dinner; not best choice for families with kids” Of course the views are spectacular from the bridge-to-bridge rooms and the rooms themselves are fine (at least the one i was in 4406). The gym was decent and the spa was very nice. Concierge service was helpful. Location is pretty good if you want to be in the commercial area of town but it will be hard to get a taxi at rush hour. Only thing I didn't like was that I had $100 worth of food credit there but I was so unimpressed with the lobby bistro and its menu that I chose to eat dinner elsewhere and give the credit to an employee. Hotel of this caliber needs a better restaurant with some windows taking advantage of the pretty views you get from this hotel. A guest doesn't just want to enjoy the property from his or her hotel room. This hotel is good for a business trip or a couple visiting the city and expect to mostly eat off property. If I were coming back with the kids, I'd probably go over to the Hyatt Regency 3 blocks away and stay on the club level and you have the more upscale Embarcadero area right across the street. Fisherman's Wharf has a Fairmont and the Argonaut by Kimpton but the area around there is pretty downscale and how many times can you walk around a bunch of souvenir shops; the Ritz Carlton is up on a big hill in the middle of nowhere and I'm told the Four Seasons is a totally corporate feel so I didn't even bother checking it out as I scoped out the area for a future trip with the family.

“Perfect Stay!!” I could not have asked for a more positive experience at a hotel - ever. Everything was great and nothing to complain about at all. They got me checked in early and into an awesome room with a killer view. The staff was incredibly nice and everything was perfect. I've read complaints about the elevator but I had no problems whatsoever. I never waited for more than 2 minutes.

“Nice Hotel; Excellent location” Stayed here for a week-long conference. Situated on the riverwalk, you just can't get more convenient. One block away from the Alamo. Rooms comfortably appointed. Service as you'd expect from a major hotel.

“Great location for shows!” Arrived at the Marriott Marquis for a 1 night stay and was pleaseantly surprised. The room (2804) was large and quiet with a comfy bed. An added plus is that it was next to a stairwell enabling us to walk up two flights to the concierge level rather than wait on the elevators. And DO expect to wait on the elevators! Sometimes it was a 20minute wait even knowing how to use them. This wasn't at 6 pm either -- we are talking any hour of the day -- and we stayed on weekdays. I can't imagine how bad they might be on weekends! We gave up trying to get to The View restuarant after seeing Wicked (which is tremendous) due to the crowds trying to use the elevators. On a positive note, the staff was very friendly, the food was great (particularly the Sushi bar) and the location was great for the theater. Try to visit the diamond district if only for a few hours as it is fascinating.

“Wonderful stay in restored vintage inn.” Ever since enjoying brunch at Smoke this summer, my wife and I have been looking for an opportunity to stay a night at The Belmont. We just returned from a couples overnight trip combining a stay at the Belmont, dinner at Smoke and a concert at the Kessler theater. Check in was easy. Valet parking was very reasonably priced. Enjoyed a few drinks and small plates in the hotel bar with a great view of Dallas. Drinks were well made. Dinner at Smoke was sublime. We took advantage of the free hotel shuttle for our short trip to the Kessler Theater. The room was great. Our suites both had beautiful views, huge romantic tubs in the bedroom, very comfy beds. A full sitting area with huge flat screen. And a nice vintage bathroom with subway tile. We slept in Saturday morning and all was wonderfully quiet. Really a great place to stay and a fun change from the typical Dallas hotel.

“OK hotel” We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights from 25th May. My first impression of the check-in staff was that they were off-hand as previous reviewers have said. The room was clean and comfortable. The location is great being in the heart of the city and we were able to walk everywhere. Because of staff attitude I would hesitate to stay there again

“Just OK” I was booking in a rather spacious corner Junior Suite. While the size of the room was more than adequate, overall it was somewhat rundown and the bathroom was very dated (usually, when I stay in a high end hotel, I think "Gee, I wish my master bathroom at home looked like this." Sutton Place made me appreciate my master bathroom back home!). While there was nothing too wrong with this hotel, overall it didn't have a high end feel to it.

“An average stay at the Sir Francis Drake” I had to go down to SF on business and it was tough finding something within budget this time so I ended up at the Sir Francis Drake. It is located near Union Square. The rooms are pretty average - they did a pretty big renovation it seems. The bathrooms are tiny and mine was a bit dirtier than I would have liked. There was some dirt or something in the bath when I checked in but I was so tired I just left it for the morning. I did my best to clean it up before my shower but it was still a little gross. It did have free wifi if you were an intouch member which was a nice feature. The workout room was sufficient - the machines were generally functional. I think the best part of the hotel was the crazy uniforms worn by the doormen. Kept it interesting!

“Pretty Nice” I stayed at this hotel 4 times between Dec 2006 and July 2007 for business trips. This location was selected because of it’s proximity to the company we were meeting with. It may otherwise be a bit off the beaten path. However, it is within walking distance of Harvard. I consider it within walking distance of the subway, but some people may not consider it walking distance since I’m sure it was a good mile away. There is definitely a Whole Foods grocery store and a drugstore within walking distance. I never had a car when I stayed here. I took a taxi to/from the airport. I took the subway if I wanted to go site seeing or to the North End for dinner. I heard others complain about the cost of parking at the hotel, so I imagine that it is high. The cookies on check-in are absolutely delicious! The restaurant breakfast buffet is okay. The drinks at the bar are way over priced. I recall a pub called something like River God within walking distance that had far better prices. Check with the Concierge as he was extremely helpful whenever we were looking for anything. High speed Internet is not free. I think it was $10 a day. The hotel rooms look like the actual photos. The room is suite style and nice. The wide, flat screen TV in the front room is really nice. Many rooms have good views. A previous reviewer mentioned a conference table in the front room. Usually those are given to business travelers by request. If you didn’t want one, I’d say something about. A typical front room contains a love seat, chair, coffee table, and TV.
