Having been in quite a few rooms, I can tell you that a couple of them are starting to show some wear.

“Very pleasant stay” We thoroughly enjoyed our weekend stay at this small, pretty hotel. Our room was on the small side, but not a bit cramped and the marble bathroom was quite lovely. The bedroom had shiny wood floor, oriental rug, comfy bed, TV, large desk, easy chair, and a gas fireplace. It also had a "balcony" about 18 inches deep--obviously not for sitting on, but cute and nice for checking the weather. The views were interesting--to the left, trees and old steeples; to the right, the bridge and river; straight ahead, demolished building and dumpsters. This is a part of the city undergoing great change as old warehouses become smart shops and condos, so there is a lot of construction. It didn't disturb us at all. The location is excellent for visitors interested in the many historic sites in Philadelphia. Within an easy and pleasant walk are the Liberty Bell, Old Quaker Meeting House, Christ Church, Independence Hall, etc. You can also walk to excellent restaurants and our favorite hangout, Franklin's Fountain (for house-made ice cream). The onsite restaurant, Panorama, is popular so book ahead. It's lively and fun and delicious. The wine bar is amazing. You can order flights of wines (which sounded very tempting, but arrive at table in goofy racks), or single glasses of more than 100 wines. The continental breakfast is pretty good, but not up the standards of the hotel as a whole. The coffee is very good, but there was no cream either day of our stay. The fruit selection and quality were excellent, but the variety of breadstuffs was disappointing. Overall, we enjoyed our stay immensely and will certainly return.

“Good value hotel in San Fransisco” I bought my room on Hotwire for something like $99/night (normally $250/night). Impossible to beat that! The hotel itself was centrally located in the Union Square area. There are a number of grubs walking around the area but that's San Fransisco. The hotel is presently under-going a $7 million upgrade. It should be pretty cool when it's done. They upgraded me into one of their new rooms and it was very nice. Everything was great about the room - no complaints - except i was on the 4th floor. This meant i heard every siren and drunken slur in the wee hours of the night. The front desk folks were excellent and helpful. Parking in San Fran is expensive at $40 overnight so be prepared. Overall, a very good experience. I would recommend this hotel and i will return.

“Gute Lage - Schöner Blick” Das Hilton San Diego ist ziemlich neu und sehr modern gestaltet. Es liegt an der Bay und am Conference Center. Von den oberen Stockwerken hat man einen schönen Blick auf die Stadt und die Bay, bzw. Coronado Insel und Brücke. Die Zimmer sind schön und geräumig. Die Bar verwöhnt mit kleinen Snacks und kreativen Cocktails. Das Frühstücksbuffet läßt keine Wünsche offen und ist nicht nur reichhaltig, sondern auch mit alllerlei ungewöhnlichen Leckereien bestückt.

“Great location downtown Boston” we stayed at the Holiday Inn Beacon Hill for easter holiday. The location is perfectly central to all attractions downtown Boston, 10 min walk to the seashore. Located in fashionable Beacon Hill, convenient for walking through a typical New England high class neiborhood toward the historic district. Very safe location. Hotel was great - got an upgrade to higher floors, very clean hotel, very confortable bed, great breakfast. A very nice afortable place to stay downtown Boston. Will return there for sure.

“Have had two good stays here” Enjoyed the hotel immensely both times. On one trip I got a suite and $50 certificate for food which was a good thing since breakfast for two of us I think ended up around $60. Trendy hotel where I feel a little underdressed and unhip but it doesn't bother me. Staff has been very friendly to me. Very close to Museum District and fantastic pool area for relaxing (though I didn't use it).

“Beautiful & historic, but I would choose another place” This hotel is beautiful and historical, of course...but once you get up to the room it's sort of disappointing. I absolutely adore The Four Seasons on E 57th Street and I think it's comparable to The Waldorf. The rooms are much more comfortable, in my opinion and I were going to spend this kind of money on a hotel room.....I'd definitely choose the Four Seasons!

“Helpful staff, nice GM, beautiful building” I stayed at the Gunter for a conference held at the convention center. It was about a 10 minute walk through a part of town that felt safe, even late at night. The lobby is impressive - beautiful historic touches you won't find anywhere else. The staff at the front desk was extra helpful and extra polite. The staff in the concierge level were very average. After my stay, I received a follow up letter from the hotel's GM, and he seemed very interested in how my stay was and wanted to make sure I left the hotel with a positive feeling. The rooms were nice, but the historical touches were not included within the guest room. The bathrooms are in need of a re-freshing, but the GM assured me they planned to work on them in the short term.

“Worked great for our family” We got a great rate for this Embassy Suites by prepaying on the website. Cheaper than several comparable chain hotels in the area. The room fit us perfectly. We had 6 of us and the two 'boys' crashed on the hide-a-bed which wasn't too bad as hide-a-beds are concerned. The 4 girls all slept in the separate bedroom, the beds were full size at best but nobody complained. The pool was well kept, we went twice. One time it was way too crowded as was the hot tub. The second time (morning) it wasn't used nearly as much. We never did manage to get the sauna to work properly. Location was convenient for our needs. Took in a ballgame, and girls wanted to shop around the renovated Southcenter mall. It was a quick 10 minutes to the ballpark and we miraculously avoided traffic. The location isn't anything special other than convenient. My only gripe was the breakfast. Not the hotel's fault as we were there on a busy weekend but holy cow. A total and complete zoo. The staff worked hard to keep up but it was out of control. If my kids hadn't wanted to eat there so badly I'd have just went and had breakfast elsewhere. Other than the breakfast deal (which is a great bargain, and on regular days I'm sure is great), I'd recommend this property for anyone seeking a functional, convenient and nice/clean property.

“Noisy, tired rooms- Not a quality Marriott” Sub-par Marriott brand hotel- dated rooms, old TV's, bathrooms in need of a serious deep clean. The desk chair in my room was torn and broken- probably more appropriate for a yard sale. The rooms are noisy due to the proximity to a major freeway and elevated ramp. There are much better options for business travelers in the NW San Antonio area.

“if you have to stay in downtown jacksonville this is the place to stay” I've had to come to downtown jacksonville for the last 3 years to go to a convention, I assume that's the only reason anyone would stay in downtown Jacksonville? Downtown Detroit makes Jacksonville look good- I'll never be back. The Hyatt is THE place to stay, ask for a room with a river view. The mexican restaurant at the "landing" next door is excellent, good food, service, drinks

“Very Disappointing” I stayed at the Waldorf for two night on business. I was quite excited because of its history and name, but came away disappointed. I stayed on the 6th floor, the room was small, view of a brick wall, dated furniture and no wireless internet. I ordered room service for room service, 2 eggs/coffee and juice and it was $53. For the price, there are a ton better options and I'll never stay there again.

“Palomar Chicago - hotel delight” This week, I've been enjoying my first Chicago break ensconced in the Palomar, a Kimpton Hotel. Led here by reviews at TripAdvisor, and having stayed in Kimpton properties before, I felt Palomar would be a solid choice and meet my design expectations. I'm happy to report, I was right on both counts. Who can resist a hotel with leopard and zebra bathrobes? The hotel is in a great location, two blocks from Michigan Avenue. Being so new, several taxi drivers were unfamiliar with it, so be sure to keep the address on hand when you visit. The lobby is small but inviting. The reception area features a lovely tufted leather counter with lighted resin countertop, both in a warm gold, very fun and touchable. Gold and black marble floors add drama, along with white patent leather chairs. The color scheme carries into the wine reception room where the over-scale mod floral carpeting keeps the tone whimsical. I really enjoy the mix of materials in the public areas of the hotel. At check-in, which was handled quickly and smoothly, the Kimpton word-of-the-month resulted in a lovely bottle of wine at no charge. The front desk staff also gifted my son with a bag of toys (the beach ball was a huge hit). Membership in the Kimpton InTouch Club also lands you free wi-fi and a $10 voucher for the minibar. We booked into 1127, described as a "luxury one bedroom suite". At 750 square feet, it is certainly a lot of real estate for the price. The living room features seating for six, along with a desk area and plenty of accessible outlets. The bathroom is enormous, with a jetted tub that can easily accommodate four people, if you were so inclined (those same four people could also shower at once)! The king bedroom boasts Frette linens and an assortment of pillows. Palomar gets 5 stars for thinking of everything. Every amenity is available, from a magnifying makeup mirror to toiletries you might have forgotten. The trademark Kimpton bathrobes make me smile! Hmmm, so why am I not singing the praises of the décor? Well, as I've said before, I think hotel designers have an opportunity to take chances with décor, to really create an interesting and original atmosphere. Don't get me wrong, my suite is very nice and quite pretty. But as Elle Décor's Margaret Russell has said: "pretty rooms are rarely memorable". The most exciting aspect of the room is actually the carpeting! The mod floral, downsized from the lobby, is rhythmic and unexpected in the guest room. Subdued in beige and chocolate brown, it leads the color scheme throughout the suite. The textured wallpaper is beige, the furniture mixed dark brown and pale, both with a limed look. The sofa and chairs are light blue and fairly generic. Perfectly nice, but it doesn't have a luxury vibe. The furniture looks like it could live in any average hotel. The bathroom is neutral and very well appointed. I love that the quartz countertop is extra high, and the 12x24 inch marble tiles suit the spacious serenity. Toiletries are L'Occitane - yummy. Overall, I'm a fan of the Palomar, and would definitely recommend to others and stay here again myself. And the restaurant Sable - that story is still playing out - stay tuned for an update. My pictures are posted at: http://exuberanthome.com/palomar-chicago

“A nice place to stay..” Our family stayed at this place based upon reviews. This place suited our needs and we would stay there again. I do agree that the front receptionist (did not get her name) wasn't the friendliest and when I inquired where the "bat" bridge was, she said you could do a google search in our business center. We found the bridge and upon our return to the hotel, the front receptionist was much nicer and informed gave us the information that we should have received earlier. The rooms were nice, beds were comfy, and breakfast was good. We laughed the next morning when we seen on a wall a map of Austin highlighting the "bat bridge." I would stay here and not let one receptionist hinder your experience.

“Great night” We spent one night here on a girls weekend of shopping. I was worried at first when we checked in and there was a large school group there,but no worries. The rooms were large and quiet, staff was friendly and helpful. We checked in ten minutes before the complimentary evening food and drinks were ending so I can't comment on them. The breakfast was a wide variety buffet with everything from waffles to biscuits, gravy, sausage etc. It was very good.The beds were very comfortable and the bathroom a nice size. I look forward to staying again.

“Well located. Some weird rooms. Little service. Lumpy bed.” This hotel's location is great. Short walks to a lot of historic Boston sights. In fact, my room overlooked the site of the original tea party and the recently opened attraction. We were upgraded to a junior suite facing the water. The room was a little weird, however. It was a large oblong space with the bathroom, sleeping area and sitting area in line. The weird part was the connection through a sliding window between the bedroom and the bathroom. When the light was on in the bathroom, it lit the sleeping area. It felt as if there was no privacy. Very unusual. We had a 5-night stay. Requests made during check-in, repeated on day 2 then day 3 were finally fulfilled on day 4. Not the type of service I've received from other I-C hotels internationally. The bed was lumpy without a bottom fitted sheet, so the sheet was gathered under me every morning and I was lying directly on the mattress.

“Great location -- don't count on the free breakfast” The hotel is conveniently located in the Inner Harbor and a short walk to there and the ball park. The hotel room was very roomy and we had a good amount of space to spread out, even if we just stayed overnight. The only negative was the very poor breakfast that was severely picked over when we got there -- and looked like there was not much to start out with. TIP: vallet parking at the hotel is expensive -- you can drive down the block and park for about $10/per night at one of the garages over the weekend ...

“nice area, nice lobby, small rooms” This hotel is nice and clean. The rooms as well are quiet and well maintained, and are in an area near the action, without suffering from a lot of street noise, etc. The lobby is a great place to be seen and the restaurant in the lobby, was very busy every night, though i didnt have a chance myself to go. The only real complaint is that the rooms are quite small. I would compare this hotel to some of the older hotels in chicago size wise, though these rooms have been updated as far as decor, just sized as some older hotels. I would recommend this hotel, I certainly like the location. Close to lots of restaurants, bars, shops etc.

“Nice Choice in Seattle” I spent two nights at the Fairmont Olympic as part of a business event at the hotel in April. Rooms were very nice. King bed had excellent bedding and was very comfortable. Lots of room and included a desk, minibar, big closet and comfortable chair/ottoman. Bathrooms were nice, if a bit small, for this quality of hotel. All events that were a part of the business meeting were top notch, with great service, excellent food and plenty of choice. Facilities were very nice as well, especially the Garden Room, which was really beautiful and a great space for a large group dinner. Location is good for the Seattle business visitor or the tourist as it’s close to everything and only a short taxicab from neighborhoods like Belltown or the sports facilities. I really liked that there was a Brooks Brothers around the corner for a quick tie purchase when I realized I hadn’t packed an extra. I would definitely consider the Fairmont for future stays in Seattle, although I would probably be more likely to stay at the Grand Hyatt Seattle. Both are excellent properties and the choice would really come down to personal preference. The Fairmont is a grand, traditional hotel, while the Grand Hyatt is a sleeker, modern property. Either way, you can’t go wrong at the Fairmont Olympic if you’re in Seattle.

“Location was a real downside” Overall this Omni Suites is an acceptable hotel, but it is showing its age and the location is dreadful. It is not near anything, and cab fare to downtown Austin was about $25.00. The hotel's suttle picks up and delivers to the airport, but nowhere else. Maybe it was just the dates that I was in Austin, but the rental car fee quote that I got (and didn't use) was over $150 for two days, so I declined that. The good: excellent pool and pool-side area; the exercise facility was dated, with machines from ca. early 1990's, but still in workable shape. I have stayed at Omni Suites facilities with far superior exercise facilities, so this is a disappointment. The not-so-good: (1) the phone in my room just didn't work, not even to call down to the front desk to complain about the wi-fi not connecting. (2) I am an Omni Select Guest, but had to speak to the front desk in order to connect to the wi-fi for free. Also, this hotel has the type of wi-fi connection where you have to reconnect every single time you turn off your device. Why? Seems a little outdated. (3) Terrible lighting, particularly in bathroom. (4) windows are sealed and do not open. I am pretty sure I would not stay here again, which I am sad to say because I am generally a big fan of Omni Suites properties.

“Good, Not Great” This hotels location is great and within walking distance to everything. You are right next to Union Square, China Town, and about a 15 min walk to the Embarcadero. The hotel rooms are small but nice. So if you are looking for lots of space, look else where. The room has a desk, bed, flat screen t.v. and an updated bathroom. I did not use the restaurant, or fitness center so I can not comment on those. There was free wireless internet, which was a great perk. I slept well and did not hear any street noise. I would stay here again if I was in the area. Of of course I was here for business and received a rate of $199/night, which was less than half of what they normally charge. But I think $400 is the going rate for 4 stars in the area.

“The Worst managed hotel in Washington” A nightmare of poor customer service. I purchased a prepaid for a room here for two nights on March 14-16 2009, through Priceline. When I arrived, the night manager told me they had overbooked the hotel and had no rooms, and so they said they were putting me at another hotel - but only for one of my two nights, and I would have to move back to the original hotel again the next day. I told them I was absolutely not willing to move a second time and if they didn't have a room for me here for both nights then they would have to leave me at the other hotel for two nights. I'm here on business and have to be in meetings all day, and certainly can't be shuttling from hotel to hotel unpacking and repacking all my things - that is not what I paid for and not what you sold me. The night manager told me he thought that was reasonable but didn't make decisions like that, so I would have to call back the next day. When I did so, the daytime shift manager, as well as the operations manager, Ted Pappagallo, both told me again that they would require me to move twice and that if I insisted on staying in the hotel they moved me to, I would be charged the difference, "unless you can convince the other hotel not to charge you." Here is a guy who can't even run a hotel - he double books his rooms - inconveniencing customers by forcing them to move to a different hotel - and then he wants me to further inconvenience myself by moving a second time - when I need to be in meetings on my business trip - in order to cover up his incompetence. Sparing the lengthy, torrid details, I will merely say that I spent nearly one solid hour on the phone with this incompetent hotel manager, his assistant, and their counterparts at the other hotel, until finally the manager at the other hotel managed to convince the incompetent to do the right thing and leave me where they sent me. The other hotel was the Mayflower, which is a Renaissance Hotel also owned by Marriott. I have to ask: how can a professional hotel chain like Marriott either (1) hire incompetents who can't see how outrageous their customer service is even when it is clearly explained by a customer or (2) have policies that would allow customers to be treated this way? Kudos to the Mayflower, and to Mackey, its manager - Mackey was fantastic, his staff was professional, and his hotel was beautiful and well run. But as for the Residence Inn - don't stay there! You may very well find your room has been sold out from under you and you are up the creek - but only for one night!

“Gorgeous Old School Luxury” If you are looking for top notch old school lux in the perfect location in SF, look no further. The palace is a great hotel and the location can't be beat whether you need to be in the financial district or Union Square or SOMA. The room service food was great and prompt and the staff really tried to please. I have to offer a special thanks to Jenny Lee at the front desk for the incredible upgrade to the ambassador suite. If you've ever wondered what the very best suite in a hotel like this looks like, check out my photos.

“Good location, but very cold.” We stayed 3 nights at the Westin. The location is ideal for tourists. Otherwise, the staff was not friendly. The room was OK. Generally, the place looks very cold and very "industrial".

“Swissotel a business paradise with great service” I have to say after a stay in the Chicago Fairmont, I was a little disappointed in the room at the Swissotel Chicago - it was quite utilitarian, but not necessarily all a bad thing. If I were on a business trip I would have been completely satisfied with the stunning lake and river views. The rooms were clean and well-planned. The bathroom was also clean. But...we were there for a romantic interlude, so the small-ish lobby full of conventioneers, the on-site Palm restaurant full of conventioneers, and the bar full of conventioneers was sort of a drag. The location is on a cul-de-sac, so is actually quiet despite the heavy construction to the North of the hotel - we never heard any noise whatsoever. Downtown is literally a couple of blocks, and Millennium Park and the Art Institute and many restaurants are steps away. Lakeshore Drive is also a couple of blocks away if you want to rent a bike for a few hours along the lakeside. I guess the service is the story here - to then man/woman, everyone went out of their way to say hello, to ask how our stay was, did we need anything, can I help you out...it stood out as exemplary. The breakfast restaurant below the lobby level provided a very nice spread, and, once again, the service was wonderful. I asked if there were any stray newspapers on one occasion and the server went upstairs and got me a brand new one.

“Okay at The James” Date: August 12, 2006 Reviewer: from Lincoln, Nebraska Our stay at The James was quite nice. The rooms were reasonably sized, with contemporary furnishings (think W Hotel chain). The 40" flat-screen TVs were quite nice. They advertise Ipod connections to their in-room stereo, but I had no luck getting it to work. The hotel is very well located, if you want to stay near Michigan Avenue. The workout facilities were as nice as I've seen in a hotel. Great workout equipment and plenty of it. Staff seemed quite good, except our room wasn't cleaned until 2pm or 3pm. Around 4pm, they appear for turndown service! The bellman was very nice and helpful, and front desk staff was competent. Didn't get a chance to try the bar, but it appeared lively. Overall, a nice stay and will likely return.

“Loved the Hotel, but room was small and noisy.” We stayed two nights after Christmas. One night was free with points. Pluses: Clean, comfortable room. Friendly, very helpful staff. Great location, only a block from Riverwalk. Price was better than any other comperable hotels near the Riverwalk. Did not charge us for parking. Minuses: Very small room. Room in front was noisy from street noise. May have gotten a subpar room due to using points. Had to take breakfast back to room to eat. Would stay there again if I could get a room in back with balcony.

“great for downtown sightseeing” This hotel is great. The location was perfect for what we wanted to do (see the city, etc.). It's easy to walk to the Ferry Terminal and Embarcadero and the cable cars pick up right out front. The room was outstanding. The bed/shower/towels/etc. were all good. The TV didn't get many channels, but that wasn't what we were there for, so it didn't bother us. The safe wasn't quite big enough for a medium-size laptop but that wasn't a big issue. Internet wasn't free which was a little annoying, but the connection was good once we logged on. The gym was very good as well and had enough equipment that it wasn't overcrowded. They also don't charge extra for the gym, which was a plus. The bar downstairs is nice but somewhat small and was crowded enough with business people on weekdays that we went elsewhere to grab a quick drink. They kept our luggage for us a few hours after we checked out without any trouble so we were able to go out and have fun for a few hours before our flight. The only really annoying thing was that the elevators, while surprisingly quick when you are finally in one, take forever to show up. We were only on the 5th floor and would have gladly taken the stairs...if we could only find them. Certainly wasn't a huge issue, but it became even more annoying on the weekend when the hotel got more crowded.

“Sleepless in Los Angeles” We stayed at this hotel one night prior to a cruise and one night following the cruise. First, the positive side: the guest rooms and baths are spacious and clean. The windows are large, and offer a good view from some rooms. The TV reception was excellent. The public areas are upscale and nicely decorated. The free shuttle to/from the nearby LAX airport is handy, and runs on a frequent schedule, but it's only fair to tip the driver for moving heavy luggage. Now the negative points: jet takeoff and landing noise from the nearby airport continues all night long, and intrudes into the room. While internet access may be free in the rooms or public areas for your laptop (I don't know), there is a heavy charge for use of the hotel business center computers. The three restaurants, including the Bistro sandwich shop, are very expensive. The elevators, while attractive in appearance, seem to operate with excessive noise and vibration. The guest room alarm clock is wonderously complex and counter-intuitive, confounding any attempt to reset it. Ours went off at 4:13 a.m., courtesy of a previous guest. We finally gave up on the clock and used the automated wake-up system. Bottom line, I will not again pay $239 per night to lie awake while listening to jet noise. We won't be back.

“davvero una buona soluzione per New York” Ecco un buon B&B vicino a Times Square! Si tratta di una tipica casa newyorkese con tanto di scale antincendio esterne molto graziosa. Centrale (10 minuti a piedi per arrivare a Times Square), tranquillo, semplice ma pulito, buona e abbondante prima colazione compresa nel prezzo, personale molto affabile e disponibile e, soprattuttutto, dotata di stanze e bagni ampi, che sono una rarità in questa città. Un indirizzo da provare.

“Cockroach sighted in bath!” I've stayed in quite a number of budget hotels, including Super 8, but this one is the pits - on my third and last night there, I stepped into the bath to find a cockroach there. You can see it in the photos. It ran away somewhere, and while this can happen, it does tend to suggest poor hygiene standards. The bathroom was the worst maintained part of the room, with a large hole in the wall around the shower head (perhaps where the cockroach came from) and several chips in the bath. The room looked the worse for wear and tear also, so I'd advise Super 8 management to thoroughly renovate this property before they lose business. I was in room 144 and neighbours in room 143 caused a lot of noise in the evenings, revving their pick-up truck engine at past midnight, and they also left a pile of rubbish outside their door, strewn all over the place. My experience at this Super 8 was not up to standard.

“Great location, great hotel” I stayed here for two nights and found this to be an ideal base during my trip to San Francisco. Even though it is a big hotel, check-in was done in under 5 minutes thanks to the automated kiosk! My room was big for a city hotel with a great view of downtown (although I had asked for a bay view..I guess the tiny sliver of water out towards Oakland was supposed to count). The bed was super comfortable and the room had a nice size flat screen TV, comfy lounge chair and ample desk space for laptop etc. There was also a mini-fridge which was great for storing drinks and snacks. The bathroom was very clean and everything worked well in there. I am not a huge fan of the sliding doors that seem to be so popular now - I know they save space, but I prefer more privacy... Room service was quick and really tasty. I also appreciated that all staff at the hotel referred to me by name. All of them from the housekeeping staff to the front desk were very friendly and helpful. The location of the hotel is great - smack dab in Union Square where you can find plenty of breakfast spots and of course tons of shopping. BART stations, cable cars, taxis are easy to reach for when you want to explore other parts of the city. Definitely a great spot and would recommend it to anyone staying in San Francisco who wants a classy but not snobby place to stay.

“Perfect location, great friendly staff, clean but needs a refreshment/lick of paint” The most perfect location, next to the convention centre, in the heart of the Gaslamp quarter with plenty of restaurants nearby. The room was spacious, nice comfy bed. Decor was good but we did notice a few stains here and there on the chair and the tables. Could do with looking at the details in each room to gain the extra star from ourselves. Needs the odd stain remover, lick of paint or varnish here or there. But it was clean and great for our stay. The refreshments available in the foyer/reception in the morning were great. Valet is expensive although they were quick and helpful. Would stay again. We were woken by drunken men and women coming back from the bars on both Saturday and Friday, but I dont blame them, great location for a night out. Maybe not great for families?

“Better than the average Garden Inn” This hotel's rooms were larger than the average Garden Inn room. I had a one bedroom. Microwave and Fridge, lots of closet space, free high-speed internet access. Bed was decent. The hotel is arranged a bit awkwardly, so it takes a bit of a walk to get to my room, with a few doors to go through and a walk around the pool, but not a big deal. It's a fine place to stay, not bad but not fantastic. It s good for a business stay, but there are better places for vacationers. Also, it's tucked back off the street so it was a little hard to find.

“Great Stay in our "City"” We decided to play tourists in our own city and spend two nights at the Eliot in August. The hotel is conviently located at the corner of Comm Ave and Mass Ave and very accessible from the MBTA. Check in was quick and easy with a European staff. The hotel did remind me of something I have seen in Paris which was nice for our escape. It had an older elevator (albeit small). Upon check-in we were given two cold bottles of water. On arrival to the room, were some tasty cookies. We had a one bedroom suite which was gorgeous.The king sized bed was extremely comfortable with large and comfy pillows. Each room had its own flat screen tv and the rooms were separated by French doors. We also had a little butler pantry with a wetbar (and expensive mini-bar). The bathroom seemed updated with good water pressure. The room had good black out curtains which blocked out that early morning Eastern sun. My only complaint was the street noise. Massachusetts Ave is very noisy and starts up early in the morning. Unfortunately, our room looked over this road and being a light sleeper, I was awakened by the noise. Besides that, I have no complaints. The room was comfortable, the staff friendly, and the location very convienent to Newbury and Boylston Streets as well as the Common and Public Gardens. Boston is a walkable city and one day that is just what we did. We also went to a concert at nearby Fenway Park which was in walking distance. We did not eat at the restaurants at the hotel. (We liked the menu of the sushi restaurant but it was a little pricey for us and we had some restaurants we wanted to check out)At times, this hotel can be expensive but we received a satisfying rate and I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

“Just Fine” I stayed at this hotel for 1 night on business. The front desk is quite pleasant and there are fresh baked cookies available upon arrival. I had a handicap accessible room, so I can't comment on what the regular rooms are like, although I believe all rooms come with a kitchenette. My room was spacious and the bed was quite comfortable. The fitness center is small but sufficient. Breakfast buffet offers yogurt, cereal, pastries, fruit, juices, coffee and an omlette bar.

“Good value and convenient location” Only stayed here for one night, but service was good and it's a very convenient location to the Theater District, you can even walk down to Prudential Center if the weather is good. Although this isn't a very new hotel as the lobby and the rooms show, everything looked clean and the staff was helpful. The on-site Starbucks offers a good alternative if you don't want a full breakfast. Free internet is available in the lobby, I just had to ask the front desk for a username/password.

“Shabby but Comfortable and Convenient.” We chose BW because it was close to the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Barnes Foundation. The location was outstanding. The decor was outdated and dark, the furnishings shabby, the bed linens thin and worn. Having said that, the service was helpful, the beds comfortable, the room large and clean, and everything worked. We were not disturbed by any noise at night. We liked the neighborhood and it felt very safe. (Police precinct across the street!) The price was reasonable. I do hope this place is thoroughly refurbished because there are not too many places to stay in this locality.

“Decent enough, a little longer to the subway station” I spent four nights at this hotel in mid-December, and basically it was nice. Here are my notes. Location/Price - The hotel is at 900 10th Street NW, which places it very nearly exactly in the center from a trio of Metro stations. Chinatown/Gallery Place seemed the closest. I also walked to Metro Center one time (just a little further, all down hill). Mt Vernon/Convention Center is about the same distance north (uphill). The Chinatown station was 4-5 average blocks, and took about 10 minutes to get there walking with friends. Just fine in nice weather, but a bit much for me if it's cold. I was traveling on government business, and found that I couldn't find any Hilton properties in the District who would let me book at the government rate. They now have the "alternate" government rate, where they charge you more, and you take your chances on getting reimbursed. Since this was the central hotel for my small group of fellow union members, I bit and paid the extra $40 a night. I won't do that again. There are hotels in Crystal City that are even more convenient to the airport and the Metro at the government rate. Hotel - This was a nice hotel, with spacious rooms like you expect at Embassy Suites. Breakfast was wonderful, and the managers reception was what one would expect. I do wish more of these locations would offer just a little bit nicer food selection (some carrots/celery/dip instead of just junk chips). Service was prompt and efficient throughout. The neighborhood gets a little dicey at times, and the hotel security was visible and effective. Every time I returned (bundled up in a hoodie against the chill, I was challenged for my room key as I re-entered (a good thing). My room was spotless, and received excellent, detailed service each day. I did notice that I kept getting two conditioners instead of shampoo, and I wondered if perhaps the maid had a literacy issue (they look identical). I just grabbed a couple of the cart to manage my stay. The misses are few, but worth mentioning. This location has a very limited atrium area compared to the other hotels. The spacious feeling you get at the more modern locations was truly missed. My hallway (8th floor) was a bit dark, and the carpets worn as mentioned by other reviews. The walls are indeed thin. The windows were not effective at keeping the noise out either. I was on the back of the building (just a few feet to an office building for a view), and trucks in the early am were an issue. I head noise in the hallway as well, tho not to the point of being a problem. I have stayed at a lot of ES locations, including one on the final approach to the Atlanta Airport, and this one was much noisier. Enough said, as it will be a while before they can fix that. Meanwhile, about the only other issue was internet kiosks that are very rocky in being useful to print out boarding passes. Combined with $15 a day PER DEVICE for internet, and I was getting quite frustrated. I'm going to begin shopping for a chain that offers free wi-fi at all locations. I would add that an aging glass tube TV in a $200 plus per night hotel is a bit of a stretch. One nights rental pays for a decent flat screen these days. Outlets close to the bed (for phone charger, etc) would also be nice.

“An Old Grand Place...” We just came back from a three-night stay with our two kids. The Waldorf is very different from our "usual," which tends to be more of the boutique, home-style, 4 or 5-star places. The Waldorf is old style. Grand. Old glamour. Traditional. It has some really great features, such as thick walls, heavy real wood doors and furniture, thick gold-colored drapes, real heavy handles for the bathroom door (so it's much easier to open when you have just put lotion on your hands!), door bell and mail slot, etc. The one and only downside is there is no free wi-fi (amazing in this day and age; even at the Hampton Inn there is free wi-fi!). We're glad to have stayed here. Would I do it again? Probably not... but if you haven't stayed here, it's a good experience. We got a really great deal off of their website (pre-paid, no money back, etc.). Comparatively, the price was much cheaper than others we'd looked at. Room service was decent, but super expensive.

“Charming hotel-great location and great service” Our first time to San Fran and we loved the Handlery! When we made the reservation I mentioned that it was our anniversary. The president, John Handlery, greeted us and then sent us a wonderful bottle of wine to enjoy! Our room was a decent size for a big city, nice comfy king bed, fluffy pillows. We wanted a street side room despite the reviews of noise. We wanted to be able to look out and see the city. We had a big bay window with a great view and it was a bit noisy, but it didn't stay noisy throughout the night. There was a great street band outside our window that ended by 10 pm. We heard some garbage trucks but we were so tired after walking up and down the hilly streets there, we slept pretty well. Service was great, everyone was so friendly and efficient. The Daily Grill attached to the hotel was excellent also! Macy's, great restaurants, and tons of shopping were on the same street, so so close (too close,lol) Perfect location! We loved the Handlery and will stay there again on our next visit to San Francisco!

“Perfect Stay in LA” Even though this W hotel is not the newest in the SPG portfolio it is very well maintained on a beautiful street in West LA. It is walking distance to many restaurants, whole foods, trader joes and coffee shops. I was in the property for 9 days on business and honestly did not want to leave. The staff were prompt and courteous, the room was large with plenty of room to stretch out and the hotel is not over crowded with partying LA people. It actually felt very relaxing. I will definitely stay again. As a side note, I used some SPG points to stay one night at the SLS while I was in LA and I feel the staff at the W are far superior when it comes to treating guests with excellent service.

“Stay here about every 4 mos.” Well we booked a room here because Thomas Jefferson (my male friend) had a 2:00am flight out of TJ to head down to Mexico so I opted to send him off and stay... this hotel is a Historical Hotel of America (which I work for one) so I get employee rates. Rooms are small but the decor is very boutique trendy and you really have to take into consideration it is an older hotel. Also room did not have a bath tub and the sink is located in the hallway immediately when you enter the room. I agree with the other reviewers it is obvious they spent money on this property in the tiles in the bathrooms, lobby area, furniture (room and public areas) and Restaurant. Complimentary WI-FI downstairs in the lobby and they also have complimentary internet in the business center so you can print out your plane tickets, directions etc. FYI the only rooms that have bathtubs are the suites. Parking was $35.00 which is what is to be expected of a city hotel. I loved the restaurant "Currant" go during the Happy Hour... which they have twice a day. Food is consistently delicious and drinks are strong. We sit by the window facing the street and just chill interesting artwork on the walls... hmmm Hotel staff is very friendly and helpful especially the bell/valet staff. Centrally located to downtown and the business district I would say it's a nice catch. Respectfully Reviewed

“Just Fine” Stayed with two teenage children. Room for four was fine. Not the biggest but they never are in Manhatten. Free beakfast was excellent and constant free coffee was a refreshing bonus. Staff were friendly and courteous, although the concierge guy could have been a little more helpful. The location is excellent for Times square, Theatres. Central park is a pleaseant stroll 7/8 blocks away. Subway 2 blocks away, Numerous restaurants and delis nearby. Eating out needn't be that expensive. You won't do much more than sleep here, so should provide all you need without breaking trhe bank.

“Good value for the money/Very comfy room and bed” I've stayed at several Hampton Inns and it's always a really good value. This Hampton Inn is fairly new. Stayed in room 525 for three nights. It's a very large room with nice workspace and plenty of space to move around. It's about three miles from the Mayo Clinic. The area is just so-so - strip malls abound and the road out front is a very busy four-lane road with no sidewalks. Getting across the street is a feat of faith and speed. Nowhere to get out for a relaxing walk. There's a Super Target across the street plus several fast-food restaurants. No charm. The free hot breakfast at the Hampton Inn is a nice touch, as is the coffee/tea that's always available. You can use a computer for free in the business center and the wifi is free. The room was very comfy and clean. The bathroom (shower area) could use better lighting. Then only hitch was the free shuttle within five miles. It's a really nice service to offer, but it's not reliable. I took the shuttle four times btwn Mayo Clinic - the trips in the morning were no trouble, as I had scheduled ride the night before. The shuttle back was a bummer - one day I waited an hour and the next day 45 minutes. Not really a viable transport option if you're on a schedule. If you take a taxi from the airport, do NOT go with Duval Taxi. Filthy, cigarette-laden mini van that saw its best days in the 80's. Try Checker Cab instead and ask for Richard.

“Great location, small rooms” So you can read all the other reviews on here about the rooms. The room we had was small... beyond small, it was tiny. I booked through priceline and was very happy with the price. I then called ahead and requested a king size bed. The woman on the phone said she was "pretty sure" that it would be accomadated. When i requested a king at the desk they said they didn't have any. When later in the stay I went to see if any King bed were available i heard a hotel employee tell another guest that if you book through a 3rd party they will only give you a queen. The queen rooms seem to be on the corners of the hotels and are REALLY small. you can only walk around the bed. Things that were great about the hotel... Location - a few blocks to the "L" and a whole foods down the street was nice. You can easily walk to the Hancock tower and Mag. Mile. The shower in the room was terrific. I'm very tall and I loved the high shower head. We flew a red eye from LA which arrived in Chicago at 5am. Went right to the hotel with the expecation of just dropping off our bags and our room was ready. It was very nice to get a few hours of sleep in the morning. Negatives... Room size was even smaller than I imagined. Front desk staff seemed disinterested in general. I banged my leg on the side of the bed twice... partly do to the small room and partly due to the frame. Final Verdict... I wouldn't pay more than the $120 a night I paid from priceline. Its a great location and it looks nice. Be ready for a small room (Smaller than you think even if you are prepared for a small room).

“Very nice hotel, great location and value” We stayed at the Villa Florence for 4 days in February 2010, our first time there. The hotel is very nice and an excellent value, right in Union Square. We had quite a large room with a sitting area, but even without the sitting area, the room would have been more than ample in size. The rooms are older but in good shape and we had no complaints. Service by all staff was extremely friendly and efficient. The lobby has a nice coffee bar that serves drinks and light snacks. Kuleto's restaurant is also in the lobby.

“Brand New Hilton Property” This is a brand new Hilton Property. I understand it was opened early this spring. The hotel is great, the facilities are everything you would expect from an upscale convention hotel. It is located directly accross the street from the San Diego Convention Center. The Gaslight section of San Diego is a long 3 blocks away. This locataion has hundreds of restaurants, bars and shops.

“Scandinavian Style Hotel Has Everything You Want and Eco Friendly to Boot” This hotel is a little out of the way if you have meetings downtown (great if your meetings are with Hewlett Packard) but it's nestled against green trees and a short drive to restaurants and a terrific H.E.B. The design is very Scandinavian, minimal details and light, open spaces. The lobby is modern and inviting. The rooms have everything you need for one night or for a long stay. The kitchen was well appointed with a full size fridge, dishwasher, toaster and microwave convection oven. I was disappointed I only had one night. The complimentary Wi-Fi is always appreciated as is wine and beer social hour and solid breakfast, both included with the room. I love this concept from Westin. It is modern and green but still accessible and comfortable.

“Perfect stay, perfect location!” My husband and I stayed for only one night to catch a Red Sox game, and I only wish we'd been able to stay longer! The hotel is amazing from the moment you walk in. Big Dave grabbed our suitcase and led us to the front desk, giving us a history of the hotel as we walked. He was so polite and friendly...we immediately felt like we'd been to the hotel before. We were checked in early (as requested when I booked the room), and everyone we dealt with had a smile on their faces. The room was larger than I expected, the bathroom was beautiful, and the bed was very comfortable. Yes, there was a bit of traffic noise, but nothing that was bothersome or kept us from sleeping. The only strange thing about the room was that in the bathroom, there were no towel bars by the shower to hang towels or anything in the shower to hang washcloths. Other than that, everything was perfect. The location can't be beat...we were between Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. We walked to both, and it was a nice walk that maybe took 10 minutes. We had a wonderful time, and we're hoping to make this a yearly trip when the Sox come to town!

“Good, but not Great.” The main reason I would not stay here again is the location. I realize most people here LOVE the fact that it is so close to Times Square (which it is). I however am of the opinion that Times Square is the most unappealing part of Manhattan, a tourist trap and for me not what visiting NYC is all about. The crowds of overweight, white-sneakered mid-westerners are simply too much for me. The hotel itself is fine, yes rooms are small (this is NYC after all), and at USD 309 per night for a weekday I'd probably try something else next time,. But the rooms are fine otherwise, big flatscreen TV, nice design (a tad worn but not too bad). staff has been good and responsive (our sink leaked and was fixed pretty rapidly). As a frequent traveller, I appreciated the duvets (i hate dusty blankets), the gym (small but enough for me and in good shape) and the in-room broadband internet ($10/day). A hopping bar on the ground floor. (unfortunately my caipirinha was BAAAD) and pleasant entrance. If you like your hotels modern AND you want to be near times square then The Time is not a bad choice.

“場所が便利でモダンな部屋がGOOD” 11月に。ボストン旅行をした際に、キングサイズ1ベッドルームに2泊しました。 古くからあるホテルなので、内装はどうかなあーっと思っていましたが、いざ部屋に入ってみると、モダンな内装にリニューアルされ、とても気持ちよく過ごすことができました。部屋の窓からは、ヨットハーバーが見え、快適でした。 場所も、クインシーマーケットに程近く、ダウンタウンクロッシングへも、なんとか歩いていける距離です。また、地下鉄の駅はホテルの出口を出てすぐなので、大変便利です。 XXXX Line経由で、1泊$116.5で、大変コストパフォーマンスもよかったと思います。

“Pleasant stay, nothing exceptional but clean and good location” I had a last minute trip to midtown and my usual hotels were full so I tried this hotel. The location is very convenient to midtown locations. Only one block from Madison, two short blocks from Park. The lobby itself is tiny, as are the rooms. I received an upgrade at check in although I am not a Marriott elite, and while the room was clean and functional it is small. However, I was pleased with the room, which was in very good condition. Bathroom looks recently renovated. Furniture and decor all in good shape. The elevators are slow, this may be because there are only two of them, as far as I could tell. Front hotel staff was not super friendly but were not rude. I ordered room service which turns out to be, I think, a local restaurant that contracts with the hotel, although you can charge to your room. I had the chicken vegetable soup and margherita pizza, both of which were fine (about average for room service food). There are a number of casual restaurants directly adjacent to the hotel, and I would probably eat there if I stay here again. In room wi fi worked fine, although it did go in and out a few times, but nothing too inconvenient. There is a lot of construction going on around the entrance - which is covered in scaffolding. Not too unusual for Manhattan to have scaffolding out front, but nevertheless it does detract. If necessary, I would be happy to stay here again, although it is not my first choice because of the rather limited amenities.

“Good value in the $$$ city....” I was worried about staying here because the location is not great, other than being close to Madison Square Garden and Macy's, the neighborhood is safe enough, but has nothing else to recommend it. Having said that, the hotel itself, and especially the rooms are very, very nice. My room had 2 double beds that were very comfortable and each had 3 pillows, (3 firm and 3 soft), to satisfy all sleepers! My room had a flat screen TV, small chest of drawers, desk and an adequate closet. The breakfast is included in the room price and it is actually pretty good, as long as you don't need eggs and bacon everyday. They have fruit, yogurt, cereal, bagels, toast, english muffins, muffins and biscuits. In addition, they have 2 hot selections that they change each day. Newspaper, (USA Today) is also complimentary. The breakfast room is pretty basic, but if you don't need something fancy, it's fine. The only thing I didn't like is that all the cups, plates, bowls and cutlery were plastic, which is pretty environmentally irresponsible! The bathroom in my room was a bit small, but everything was very clean and worked very well. Great water pressure in the shower. The location is convenient for 3 subway lines and there are good cheap internet cafes only 2 blks away, which is important since I don't have a laptop. I would stay here again. I found it much better than some of the 4 and 5 star hotels I have stayed in in Manhattan!

“Excellent location” In town for Rockies games at coors field. Was put on SPG floor with nice city views. Rooms are clean and spacious, although a bit worn/ older compared to other westin hotels I have stayed at. Still, heavenly bed is very comfy. Elevators are a bit slow. There's a steakhouse on first floor but I ate at restaurant in hotel Monaco which is only two blocks away, would highly recommend this Italian joint especially for happy hour (forget the name). Lots of restaurants and nightlife in the area. Almost stayed at hotel Monaco, which seems more fun/hip/contemporary (I'm a Kimpton fan) but for $30 less per night the westin works for me! Not a destination hotel, but certainly worthy of another stay if I am in Denver again.

“Stay somewhere else” Stayed at this hotel for a business conference in October. I would never stay again! Hotel is suppose to be "non smoking" but my room smelled horrible! I asked to be moved, but was told there were no other rooms. I was put in a "connecting" room, which meant I got to listen to the person next door chat on the phone until 2 a.m. I could hear every word he said. The walls were very thin, almost like they were not there. My co-worker was on a different floor, and said there was some problem and the entire floor smelled like sewage. It did not get fixed during our stay. The rooms are just average. The coffee makers were pretty cheesy for a hotel this class and price. Every day I had to get a new room key, as they would stop working. That was also fun. Room service took 90 minutes to arrive. Attempts to reach room service went unanswered, so I didn't know if my food was showing up or not. In a nutshell, I'd stay away from this hotel. It is run down, and service is lacking. There are many other choices in Philly, and I'd take them!

“Perfect Place to Stay in Downtown San Antonio” We stayed at this property with our two teenagers for 5 nights. What a great place. It is a two block walk to the Alamo and Rivercenter Mall. There were plently of families making this walk back and forth at all hours of the day, so we felt very comfortable there. The check in was smooth, and every single person we encountered there was pleasant and helpful to us. We had a 2 bedroom suite, and it was perfect for us. The 3 TV's were actually all runnning at once a lot of the time, so we could watch the news, and the kids could watch MTV or whatever they were interested in at the time and everyone was happy. The bathrooms were spotless. I found the carpering in our suite to be very clean also. The kitchen area was also immaculate. The complimentary breakfast was very good and constantly restocked. It was kept very tidy. In the evenings Mon-Thurs from 5-7pm they have complimentary beer, wine, sodas, and a different light meal. This was a nice way to relax after being out all day, and we took advantage of this. We didn't use the pool, but there were plently of people out there who looked to be enoying themselves. The parking is $12 a day with in and out privileges, but you can park in a lot across the street for $5 a day. SInce the hotel parking was gated and card controlled, we parked it there. The laundry room was also spotless. For people who need incidentals, there is a CVS on the riverwalk, and around the corner from the Crockett Hotel there is a convenience store. This property is close enough to everything, but far enough away from the hustle and bustle. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great Value that's Quiet and near Hollywood Action” I chose this hotel for several reasons and it exceeded my expectations. Most important were: I needed a place close to the action, not noisy, accessible to public transportation that is reasonably priced. This hotel was a 5 - 10 minute walk away from Hollywood Bld which includes Kodak Theater, Grauman's Chinese Theater, Hollywood Walk of Fame, and Jimmy Kimmel Show. The hotel was near the Red Line Metro which allows you to travel via subway to other areas such as Universal Studios which is one stop away. If you don't want to travel by subway there are also buses nearby. There are also local eateries at Hollywood Highland area that include California Pizza Kitchen, Johnny Rockets, Quiznos, etc. The hotel itself was nicely appointed. The lobby is small, but there is always staff available. They have a small pantry for sale of bottled water, potato chips, and frozen meals. I had a 2 queen bed room with a flat screen TV. The room was clean and had soft and firm pillows designated by pillowcases. I also had a place card every night telling me the weather and temperature for the next day. Great perk as a traveler. The FREE Breakfast was great! There was variety, but if you stay for several days you may grow tired of the same selection. Although, you can't beat free! There were eggs, sausage, bacon, biscuits, oatmeal, cereals, yogurt, bananas, muffins, hard boiled eggs, and coffee. The breakfast area was a nice size that comfortably sat about 30 people. I did not have any issues, so I did not have to communicate with staff for problems that required resolutions, which for me means they are doing their job.

“Very Comfortable!!” A great staff, comfortable room, and oh that shower!! The room was extremely quiet, both from street noise and other guests. A nice touch was breakfast included, a NY Sunday Times and bottled water.

“Sehr gutes Hotel in einem fairen Preis-Leistungsverhältnis” Das Hotel liegt ca. 15 Gehminuten außerhalb von Downtown. Das Hotel liegt sehr nahegelegenzur Space-Neadle. Das Hotel macht einen sehr ordentlichen und gepflegten Eindruck. Es trägt schon die neuen Holiday Inn Schriftzüge, ich schätze das Hotel wurde erst vor kurzem renoviert was auch die neuen Zimmer belegen. Die Zimmer entsprechen dem Standart sind aber schon sehr modern eingerichtet. Wir hatten Glück in der 6.Etage untergebracht zu werden, dort erhält man ein Zimmer wenn man im Priority Club Mitglied ist. Man erhält ebenfalls Lounge-Zugang wo morgens Kaffee und ein kleines Frühstück aufgebaut wird. Das Restaurant bietet viele Speisen zu vernünftigen Preisen die auch gut schmecken. Internet ist kostenlos verfügbar. Alles in allem ist das Hotel wirklich sehr empfehlenswert.

“ordinary” I have been a guest at 6 MGM properties and this was the worst easily. It has a great location but it is very dirty the room looked okay. I put on new white socks on my first evening and after walking around in the room the bottom of the socks are brown.Yuk! The towel had a long black hair on it.The food was okay but the service level was only fair. The staff spent more time chatting with each other than the customers. Needs to improve

“great manhattan-style hotel in downtown” I really enjoyed my brief stay at the Hilton Checkers, an early 20th-century building wedged between the skyscrapers in the heart of downtown. The hotel is right next to the public library and Library (USBank) Tower. Even my 2nd floor room had a pretty good view of it and the surrounding buildings, if only while standing at the window. The size of the room was as you would expect for a building of this age, but the space was used well and the marble bathroom and closet were surprisingly large. Most rooms have corner windows for added light. Other nice touches such as back-lit headboards, decorative glass sconces, crown molding, and granite topped furniture make this a much nicer Hilton property than many others. The roof-level pool area is amazing. Trendy restaurants, convenience stores, public transit, and self parking are all less than 2 blocks away. The hotel only offers valet parking for 38.50 but lots nearby charge 12-18 for overnight parking (not secured). Best in-room coffee I've ever had (Lavazza). I would return.

“The Lodge is a Wonderful Place for Business Meetings” Stayed at the Lodge for several nights for a corporate training program. It was a wonderful experience in every way. The staff was polite and attentive, the food was great, and the facilities top-notch. Rooms were clean, large and very comfortable, and the bathrooms were oversized with both shower and jacuzzi tub. The Lodge has many great locations for group gathering and socializing at the end of the day, including a wonderful lounge with fireplace, pool tables, and small meeting rooms. I look forward to returning some day.

“Charming Building, Great Location” Having booked a queen room through Expedia, I was upgraded on arrival to a King bed suite, including large bathroom with separate tub & shower. This was a nice, unexpected touch. There's no question that you can hear the L trains as they rumble along Wabash, but from the seventh floor it was a periodic dull hum that, as an urban apartment dweller, did not bother me. My guess is this would be more significant on the lower floors, especially for light sleepers. The L runs until about 2am, so it won't be a problem for the night owls either way. The mattress was great, and the furniture in general was fine all around. The TVs (there were two) in the room are indeed older tubes & not LCDs, but who'll be wasting their trip watching them anyway? The clock radio was nicer than usual, with two alarms and a CD player built-in. Room overall was quite clean, a couple of notches below 'sparkling'. This didn't bother me, but the guest who wants to see their reflection in the toilet bowl might take issue. For some reason the rubber latch on the shower door appeared to have been broken for some time. Draping a towel over the door kept most of the water from splashing out, but why it was in this condition I can't imagine, as the part couldn't have cost more than $4. I had intended to mention this on departure but forgot. Staying at a hotel on the east side of the Loop, one block from Michigan Av, you're ideally located in a safe area that's an easy walk to many sites of interest, and situated amidst many of the buildings Chicago is known for. Transit access couldn't be much better, and there are plenty of places to eat during the daytime. It's true that the Loop district does somewhat empty out after the close of the business day, but I never felt unsafe walking around in the wee hours. Late night dining options are relatively few in the immediate vicinity though. For the price I paid, I'd stay here again in a second.

“OK- elevators were a pain!” I stayed at this hotel with 3 other colleagues. The prices we got were highly variable despite all booking under AAA discount. The airport shuttle: when I got in and got my luggage I called the hotel to get the shuttle. I was told they came every 1/2 hour so I waited in the designated place. The shuttle wizzed right by without stopping. I called the hotel and she sent the driver back. He said, "There was no one there." Huh? really? There were people standing all over by the curb at the designated hotel curtesey van place. The check in was fine. The lobby is clean, but spartan. The restaurant was good- had outdoor seating that we took advantage of. The room was good. Smaller room with pretty good use of space. Bathroom small with shower only- no tub. Hotel is older- but in good repair. My biggest complaint would have to be the elevators. There are 14 floors and three elevators. One was out of service. the glass elevator can only be called from the ground floor- leaving ONE to service the entire hotel when calling from your floor. Also, there seemed to be some sort of glitch because they stopped at essentially every floor even when no one was there calling for it (not once, not twice, all the time!). I think that the rate descrepency bothers me the most- more than $50/night in variance among our party of 4. I think that is a really high variance. I called the hotel and left a message, but as of yet the call has not been returned. The restaurant across the street was great Anthony's- fish place. Internet was free and was reliable. The "business center" was one computer and there was a charge of 6 or 7 dollars to use it. Pool was warm, exercise room was pretty big and had lots of equipment.

“Excellent stay” My husband & I stayed at the Marriott on Michigan Ave. Friday, January 6th to avoid having to drive back to the suburbs after his work holiday party. We had a wonderful stay. The lobby bar was still going strong at 12:30am when we checked in. It looked like fun. Our room was clean & modern, as was the bathroom. The king sized bed was very comfortable. We had a view to the west, which was also very pretty at night. Guessing rates are lower at most downtown hotels this time of year, but did get a great rate for a Michigan Ave. hotel. Would recommend the Marriott to anyone.

“Snobby staff” Okay hotel standard Holiday Inn Express with the usual breakfast, yet some extras that some don't have, nice rooms, yet at this hotel a very snobby staff. We arrived at the hotel around 7:30 pm the Thursday before Memorial day. We stay in ICH hotels roughly 150 nights a year and as event planners sell roughly close to a thousand room nights a year for ICH hotels. We are platinum priority club members and as such have an abundance of points. We checked on the hotel online at 6:30 pm and they had every room category to purchase but only double bed rooms available for points. We used our points instead of paying for the room as we were traveling to another destination and only staying overnight in Jacksonville. On arrival at the hotel, looking around, we saw roughly 20 cars. As a platinum member, ICH gives us perks and upgrades "when available". When we reserved online we had requested to be upgraded to a king suite or at least king room. On arrival Jean as well as a manager, Darren (sp?) stated they did not have an availability for an upgrade (note this hotel has 13 suites and 38 single bed rooms, which means King rooms). We asked to be upgraded to at least a king room, but again told no upgrades available. We had already stayed in this hotel soon after it opened and the clerk at that previous stay had told us that "no upgrades when you use points" was the policy of the hotel management. After writing a letter after the last time we had stayed about that statement, we were later called by a manager/owner? of the hotel & told that since they were new, the clerk was unaware about upgrades to priority platinum members and that would not happen again. We understand that if a hotel is heavily booked, we would not get an upgrade, but this simply was not the case of this hotel at this time. We believe they still must have the policy of no upgrades. We're sure that had the hotel been almost sold out at 6:30 there would have been no "points" rooms available at all. Also understand that we are not as upset at not getting an upgrade as we are about being lied to about the circumstances. We are determined to spread the word to other Priority members.

“Great Stay” Older 70's building with all remodeled rooms. Convenient location to the convention center, capitol mall and 16th street shopping. Nice amenities including one of the best gyms I've seen in any hotel. Rooms are quiet, comforatable and outfitted with flat screen tv, internet and those comfy Sheraton beds. The lobby has lots of seating areas and a Peets coffee located on the property. I have stayed here before and always come back. Found the rate on Hotwire which was over $100.00 off the AAA rate due to a large medical convention in town.

“Great stay at a great price and comfy beds!” This is the first time I've stayed at a hotel in Houston since I moved out, and I really enjoyed it. The room was really comfy, with good decor, I really liked the shower, the beds were very comfortable, and it's easy to get into the hotel. I never tried the restaurant for anything other than dessert, but judging from my good cheesecake I had, and how good the food smelled, I'd say it's good. But best of all, it's cheap! My dad and I stayed here for 2 nights at $100 a night, which is a great deal for the amenities we got. Just keep in mind that the Crowne Plaza is still converting from a Holiday Inn Select, so there is a little remodeling going on on the second and top floors and at the pool as far as I know, but not bad enough to detract from my stay. Here's a bonus: You can barely hear anything from the freeway! With all that said, I highly recommend staying here if you're coming to Houston!

“Not bad for a boutique hotel” This hotel was pretty good for what it was. My husband and I found the hotel on Expedia and booked two nights over the weekend at about $210 a night. We thought the price was pretty good for the location of the hotel, and for a Friday and Saturday night. It's in a decent neighborhood within walking distance to the Beverly Center and other restaurants. There is no self-parking which is not uncommon for a small boutique hotel, so you can either park in a metered spot or valet. Valet was about $26 a day after taxes, and we thought it was worth it. The valet staff was always on top of it. We got our car in and out of valet several times and each time we would just call ahead of time to have our car ready and our car was always right outside within 15 min. Our room at the hotel was not bad. It was on the first floor and opened into a small courtyard facing other rooms. That said, it was not very private if you opened the curtains so we kept the curtains closed most of the time which made the room dark. And the fact that all the lights in the room were fluorescent lighting didn't help, but overall, that didn't bother us. The room was really tiny and the bathroom was pretty small too with virtually no counter space so I had to put all of our toiletries and my makeup on the desk outside of the bathroom. But again, this is not uncommon for a small boutique hotel and it wasn't that big of a deal to us. The light in our bathroom made an annoying buzzing sound and the bed was a little firm and stiff for my tastes though my husband thought the bed was comfortable. The walls were not sound proof as we could hear noises all around us including doors shutting and people talking constantly. When we first checked in, we smelled pot in the hallway and the smell seeped into our room because there isn't a great seal around the door which I'm sure is also what contributed to how easily we could hear outside noises. I called the front desk about the pot smell and they took care of it right away. Overall though, the room was clean and updated pretty well for, what I could tell was, a really old building. It was also nice that they provided complimentary wifi even though it was kind of slow, breakfast in the mornings, and wine and cheese receptions in the evenings. The staff was also really friendly and courteous. All in all, the hotel and the location were pretty good for the money.

“Great staff, convenient location” I spent two nights at the Westin Riverwalk, for a work conference. Our conference was held in the hotel. What stood out to me the most about this property was the staff. From check in to check out the hotel staff went out of the way to ask me how my stay was when I passed someone in the hall, and they always held doors or elevators for me, and asked if there was anything they could do to make my stay better. This includes the receptionist, the bell hops, the service aids, everyone! The few times I called the front desk for assistance (needing more towels once, and a broken tv remote once), the staff that responded were prompt and almost overly friendly. Problems were fixed in an efficient manner. The room itself was standard; I had two doubles overlooking the city. The bathroom was above average, in size and amenities. The shower had two shower heads, which was awesome! The location of the hotel is as good as it can be. I didn't have much need to get around since the conference was in the hotel, but you could get anywhere on the riverwalk really easily. Even though the hotel is kind of at the end of the tourist section of the loop, if you walk above ground across the street just one or two blocks, then go back down to the river level, you are in the center of the busiest section of the riverwalk. Being at the edge of the busy section was great, because I went running twice, heading away from the tourist section, and was given miles and miles of mostly empty and really nice trails along the outer section of the riverwalk. The gym in the hotel is good. It's kind of small, but has high quality, new equipment. I didn't use the pool, but it looked nice. I drank at the bar downstairs one night, and service was exemplary. I ate conference food for lunches, which was provided by the hotel, and was average at best. I did not use the coffee shop or other restaurants, but did frequent the gift shop, which had a good selection of snacks and drinks. My biggest complaint about the hotel is that the first night, I called and asked for a wake up call. The receptionist took my name, room, time, etc., and said it was all set. Well, the next day I NEVER got a wake up call! I had set the call to get up and workout, so luckily when I woke up on my own I was able to hurry and get ready and not be late for my conference. That afternoon I stopped by the front desk to discuss it, and I received an apology, but no explanation and nothing to make up for the mistake. I think that's kind of a big deal, it is a mistake that shouldn't have been made. Also the first night I had trouble sleeping because there was a persistent buzzing noise that I couldn't identify, but it kept reoccuring. It sounded like an alarm going off in a distant room. The next day I checked for the source and it turns out it was coming from the TV. I unplugged the TV and the noise stopped. Overall I'd reccommend this hotel!

“Best location” This hotel has normal amenities that you would expect of a Marriott - not really much more of less. The big draw is the location. You are in the heart of the tourist attractions and can walk to almost everything. If you need transportation, the "T" subway system stops right outside the hotel. Perfect location for tourists. The hotel has some construction going on right now, but the hotel did a good job minimizing the disruption.

“Perfekte Lage, stylische Zimmer” Das Hotel liegt super zentral in Chicago in einem gemeinsamen Gebaeude mit dem Residence Inn, nicht zu weit von der Magnificient Mile entfernt. Die Zimmer wirken modern und stlisch. Aussicht sollte man keine zu tolle erwarten. Die Lobby ist gross und hell. Abends gibt's eine Happy Hour mit kostenlosem Bier und Wein beim Residence Inn zu der man auch dazu kann. Absolut zu empfehlen, hier kann man nix falsch machen.

“Good Base for visiting Austin and Hill Country” This hotel is just off I-35 exit 229 (Stasney Ln) so only a few miles south of downtown Austin. Reception and check out were friendly, quick and efficient. We had a room on the 5th floor next to the elevator, but fortunately did not notice noise from the elevator despite the fact that the hotel was full due to people attending the UT graduation. The room layout was comfortable - a small sitting area next to a kitchenette/office space separated from the bedroom area. The bed was quite comfortable, but the AC unit went on and off all night and could not seem to keep the room a constant temperature for more than about 20 minutes. In addition, the hotel is perpendicular to I-35 - our room faced oncoming traffic and was quite loud on Friday night, but not as bad on Saturday night so try to ask for the rooms that do not face oncoming traffic. A limited buffet breakfast was included in the room price and was good.

“Overall Very Good Experience” Living in LA I have been to San Diego many times. I have never stayed in The Gas Lamp District before as I thought it appeared to be too touristy. It probably is touristy but was alot of fun. The location of the hotel is right near a lively night life center catering to younger folks of college age but also has several very good restaurants that cater to middle aged folks. The restaurants in the area are pricey for what they are but not outrageous. If you have a car and want to eat at good more moderate restaurants where you are not paying so much for location drive up 5th avenue away from the hotel and the water until you come a few blocks to the end of 5th Avenue which would be University Avenue. There are many very good moderate restaurants over there. We stayed in the 5th Avenue Lofts part of the hotel which was different and fun. It had a modern feel and was not a typical hotel. The hotel is small and had the feel of a boutique hotel rather than a large Hilton which was great. Pool was very tasteful as were the seating areas and the gym was adequate. Room service was prompt and pretty good for a chain hotel. Staff was very polite and considerate. Our climate control was not working properly. They offered to move us which we declined as it was not a big deal but they did comp our breakfasts during our entire stay which was great of them. Also the room was not made up when we returned one day at 5pm. In response to our phone call they made it up immediately, apologized that the housekeepers were behind and sent us a complimentary cheese plate. Yes there is noise from the nearby trains. It did not bother us and did not seem to be a problem at night but one could request a quiet room. Hotel parking is very pricey and we parked at a garage a block away for half the price. Also from 6pm Sat through Mon morning you can park on the street without feeding the meter which we also did. The arm chair in the room was alittle worn but nothing major. The rest of the room was in very good shape. Coffee maker, free waters (not sure if this was because we are Hilton Club Members) and chocolates at night were a nice touch. The staff really went out of their way to make sure everything was in order. I highly recommend this hotel for anyone visting San Diego and will certainly return.

“Nice Hotel” This property is very nice. It is right on the 16th Street Mall within walking distance to many attractions. The hotel has been recently renovated and the rooms are very nice, but a little on the small side. The lobby is large and inviting. The staff was awesome and helped us with a couple of minor requests. We were worried about street noise but there was no sound from outside. There were only a couple of drawbacks to this hotel. The first was the parking, you either have to pay for valet at $36.00 a night or park in a parking garage about a block away for $10.00 a night. Second is that there is no pool and they don't have anywhere nearby that you can go to swim. Needless to say our kids were throughly disappointed.
