And third, if you forget anything at home they don't have complimentary anything. We had forgotten toothpaste and a comb, and were charged $3.00 each for them, and that is for a travel size.

“Room ok; Grounds icey” I was in the area for a two-day conference. The first thing that struck me when I arrived at the hotel was the physical state of the property. It is February and we do get snow in Ohio. However, this is a business in a competitive service industry. Accordingly, one would expect that they would shovel the snow away from the public access areas. Right in front the entrance was clear. Just feet away from the entrance and the parking lot were a mess. Also, since the snow was left un-ploughed, it had compacted and was basically an ice rink. Not cool. Don’t these guys know that they are liable for injury resulting from the ice? The room itself was ok. The free wireless was also a plus. It seems like the hotel is being renovated, which is always a good thing. I had a king room, which had a microwave and small fridge that were really handy. The sheets were not of the best quality – quite rough in fact. However, this is a mid-range hotel. Other nice touches were the apples and cookies by the front desk. I never had their free breakfast and so I cannot comment on this aspect of their service. I did have a problem with my room and I was moved to another on a floor being renovated. The new room looked no different that the old one – I am not sure if both were renovated or un-renovated. If they were renovated I cannot help wondering what they looked like before!

“Would Stay Again” We arrived at the Contessa on the 5th of March and stayed three nights. Our room was a king riverview on the 5th floor. I believe it was #521. The room was very spacious and I really liked the fact that it was a suite so that there was a seperate sitting area from the bedroom. The staff was great for the most part. One of the door men was especially helpful, I just wish I could remember his name. There were two concierge's there - the woman was very helpful and made our diner reservations on night. They obviously knew her because when we got to our restaurant we were asked if we were from the Contessa. The other concierge wasn't quite as helpful - didn;t seem to want to putout much effort. My only issue with the room was the furniture in the sitting room - and this is often the case - made to look nice - but not particularly comfortable. I enjoyed the fact that the contessa was not on the busiest part of the riverwalk - it was nice and quiet there at night and wonderful to sit outside by the river and have a drink. The bartender makes a teriffic mojito! We would definately go back.

“Lovely hotel, but some poorly trained staff” The new Intercontinental is lovely, a few minutes by foot from South Station, right on the water at the south end of downtown. You can walk along the water, past many piers and ferry landings, all the way to the North End. The heart of downtown is 10 minutes away on foot. The room I was given (via Priceline) was outstanding -- huge, with a view of a small portion of the waterfront, a stall shower *and* a very deep tub. The main downside for everyone who will stay there is, they have duvets (warm quilts covered by sheets) instead of blankets. This made it hard for me to sleep --- too hot. The one bad thing that happened was, the maids made up the room the last day, before I checked out. My bags were right there, too! They took my newspapers, which I was not done with. I put this down to very poor training by the housekeeping manager -- and can only hope they redid the room after I checked out, or the next occupant would have been angry, too. Then the front desk made me argue with them for 10 minutes before paying me for the missing paper (a Sunday New York Times). What happened to "the customer is always right"? I can tell you, they would benefit from a "we'll fix it or the stay is free" policy. Also, parking was very expensive. The parking service was excellent (as was room service and bell service) but you have to ask to find how to get to the parking garage -- not signed at all.

“The Best Service I Have Ever Experienced At Any Ritz!” I had the great pleasure of visiting the Ritz-Carlton Georgetown several times for both business and pleasure. My job (I ran two public policy organizations) gave me the opportunity to host a small conference at the hotel. Other visits were for pure pleasure, where I enjoyed the lovely rooms...the great restaurant...and the fun bar. Let me first say that this Ritz looks like no other Ritz you've probably ever seen! The R-C Georgetown was the first Ritz to be built as a small, boutique hotel. Think "steel" and "glass"...not dark wood and antiques. Very modern. I, personally, love it. The staff is amazing. Everyone I have encountered at the hotel -- from the doormen, to the valets, to the front desk staff, to the housekeepers, to the spa personnel, to the sales department, to the waiters and bartenders, right up to the general manager -- have impressed the heck out of me. Top notch service. "The customer is always right." "What can I do for you, Mr. Berry?" I feel like royalty every time I visit the property. The general manager of the hotel is Jenni Brown, an extremely professional young woman who has been with the Ritz-Carlton chain for many years in various countries. She actually lives on-site (reminds me of the old days when hotel general managers always lived on-site), which assures that the hotel is always run to her specificiations. Jenni runs a tight ship, and she never ceases to impress me. The rooms are gorgeous -- large and modern. The beds and beddings are amazing. Bathrooms are stunning. There is a fun bar on the first level called "Degrees." Great atmosphere -- fun and safe. Doesn't feel like a hotel bar at all. The bartenders have great personalities. I just love visiting there. The only restaurant is located on the 2nd floor of the hotel, and I have eaten there many times. I love their food: breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The food is great (not 5-star but definitely 4-star), and the service is outstanding. For female travelers who might be traveling alone: The hotel is very safe. 24 hours per day, a valid room cardkey is required to go up any elevator. This keeps strangers from roaming the halls. A small safety feature...but thoughtful. There is a conference room located at the back of the hotel on level one. My conference attendees loved the space, the food, the rooms, the spa, and the service. The Ritz-Carlton Georgetown was a big hit! (Annabelle in the sales office handled the arrangements - she was terrific.) In terms of location, the Ritz Georgetown is located one block off of "M Street," which is the most fashionable shopping street/district in all of Washington, DC. The location cannot be beat in terms of strolling, shopping, visiting Georgetown University, etc. The Ritz-Carlton Georgetown always charges more for rooms than its sister properties in downtown Washington, at Pentagon City, and at Tyson's Corner. Trust me: Georgetown is the best of all of them. Just a quick word about the other three properties (I have stayed at all of them): Ritz Downtown Washington: The only reason to stay here is if you want access to a fancy gym. The Sports Club/LA is located in the same complex as the hotel, and hotels guests at this property are allowed to use The Sports Club during their stay. Ritz Pentagon City: Great if you have business at the Pentagon or want to stay literally above a Metro (subway) station. Otherwise, why? Ritz Tyson's Corner: Maestro, the top restaurant in this hotel, is truly 5-stars. I had one of the most amazing dinners of my life at Maestro, and even the Washington Post food critic (who doesn't gush about hardly any place) "gushed" about Maestro. Of course, you could always stay at the Ritz-Carlton Georgetown and arrange to have a Ritz car ferry you to Tyson's Corner hotel for dinner! I really can't say enough about this hotel. It's my favorite hotel in America.

“Excellent value for money” This is a very good hotel and excellent value for money. It has one of the best locations in Philadelphia with almost every attraction being within walking distance. The rooms are a good size and the service is exceptional. The best thing was was food which was great and not too expensive.

“DC GETAWAY” Stayed here for 3 days in August with a family of five. The hotel is in a nice safe area of Washington DC, just north of the George Washington University campus. There were 2 other hotels on the same block, a Marriott and Ritz Carlton. The suite was a standard room for Embassy Suites hotels, with a good size living room area that had the pull out sofa bed and 2 double beds in the bedroom. The room was very clean, but had a bit of old and new in it. The living room had a flat screen TV with HD, while the bedroom had a standard one. Sinks had granite tops, but the tub/shower and toilet were dated and a bit beat up. The decorating was a late 80's, early 90's vibe, but overall for the price, compared to other DC properties it was well worth it. The breakfast buffet had a nice spread, but I agree with other reviewers that it was crowded and not easy to find a seat. I saw many people taking their trays up to their rooms. The restaurant in the hotel Nicolas was a solid choice if you don't feel like going back out for dinner after a day of sightseeing. Please note that the hotel is quite a ways from the major attractions. Walking to them is possible, but we mixed in cabs with the walking. There are 2 Metro stations nearby, but we figured with a 12, 9, and 4 year old with a stroller, cabs would be easier than lugging everybody to a train. Overall a pleasant stay and a solid hotel. The atrium interior was also fun for the kids, as they got a kick out of the fish. It probably shouldn't be rated #2 overall in DC, but definetely #1 for families looking to visit Washington.

“Overwhelmed by Gator Bowl Fans” Was management not expecting the hords of guests who came into town for the bowl game? Towels were not replaced. The bathroom amenities were limited to small bottles of shampoo and lotion and small bars of soap. I sorely missed hair conditioner. On Sunday, January 1 the line at the manager's reception snaked through the eating area. Initially, only one person was pouring beverages. Later the on-duty manager did appear to help. Unfortunately, the line was again present on January 2. The snacks were disappointing; potato and corn chips and salsa. Perhaps in consolation, the drinks were generous. Breakfast on January 2, 2006 was a zoo! Obviously, many of the guests had large number of bodies crammed into their suites. The crowd was overwhelming and the floor was a sticky mess. The food was depleted. Half frozen doughnuts were put out at 9:00 a.m. Speaking of breakfast - only eggs are available at the "cook to order station". I would rate the breakfast poorly compared to other Embassy Suites. The morning of January 1 only one fruit (melon) was presented. The hot dishes never vary. In fact they are listed so you can be certain that the choice will be scrambled eggs, pancakes, grits, hash browns, sausage & bacon. Pass on the hash browns as they are "reconstitued potatoes" and have that "instant potato" flavor. The property is a bit "worn". I had the distinct impression that there are financial issues. This is not a top notch Embassy Suites. I do not understand its high rating.

“Great hotel - Well managed, beautifully decorated, and nice staff” Our initial inclination was to stay at the Omni for our trip to San Diego after a great experience at the Omni in San Francisco last summer. But my traveling companion, who is a light sleeper saw the postings about the Omni being noisy and we choose instead to stay at a Marriott property. After one night at the Marriott (the accommodations were depressing) we packed our bags and moved to the Omni where we stayed for about 5 days. It is a great hotel with a wonderful staff (the housekeeping staff is unbelievable) nicely decorated, and has wonderful views. It is a beautiful building with a great gym and business center. On the subject of noise: the hotel overlooks the water and train tracks. Occasionally during the day one could hear the occasional train horn but the noise stopped at night so it was never a problem - even for a light sleeper. Because the hotel is adjacent to the baseball stadium I would presume that once the season kicks off it will increase noise and traffic problems, but since we were there off season I cannot comment on this. This is a well managed hotel - I hope you enjoy your stay in San Diego!

“Very nice hotel. I like it.” I have been here twice, and each time, I have had a fabulous stay. Overall, it's not a super huge hotel, but it is very nice. The hotel is centrally located downtown. The rooms are a reasonable size, and they are extremely clean. They have electronic safes. The rooms are quiet. The bathrooms are very nice, not super-luxurious, but nice. There is nowhere to park around the hotel, and there is a Starbucks across the street. overall, it's a very good place. The gym is very small, but good enough for cardio.

“Nice boutique hotel with great buffet breakfast, but rooms are small” Located smack in the middle of downtown Denver within easy walking distance to most business and leisure attractions, this hotel is in a renovated 100-year old former bank building. It is worth checking out if you like the ambience of boutique hotels. Staff is attentive and friendly, and the hotel has several very nice features: free wireless internet, a full complimentary hot breakfast buffet, a happy hour with free wine and beer, and a milk and cookie bar from 8-10PM. We had several days of meetings there, and it was quite comfortable for that purpose. On the downside, the rooms are small and I found myself constantly bumping into things. Decor is heavy and dark and a bit dreary. Televisions are old but ok. I found the bed linens to be somewhat worn rather than white and crisp as they should be, and the bathroom attempted to be trendy but using the sink was a pain in the neck. Great amenities, but if you're not a fan of the trendiness (and honestly creakiness) of boutique hotels, then consider one of the big chain hotels within the area.

“Good hotel - would stay again” My husband and I visited San Fran for the Comic Con in April. We got a $109 per night rate via Comic Con website. I was very happy with the hotel. Excellent location. Good size rooms. Great bed. Nice room service. Downside. We requested a non smoking room and got a smoking. It didn't reek but there was a faint smell when you entered the room. Housekeeping came late in the afternoon. Took them a long time to clear the room service plates in the corridor.
“Fun place” Room was a little small, but very nice. Free water was a nice touch. Ask for a room that faces the river. Wireless worked OK. Everything is in walking distance. Staff was FIRST CLASS!!!!

“In need of attention.” I love the Menger for it's historic value, clean public spaces, great bar, and nice shops, but it all stops there... What obviously needs attention are the individual rooms. There is always something wrong, as with my last visit, this past weekend along with another party...and, it's not just one thing, but several. It's time for an update... I've read quite a few recent comments, and it's always the same..."thank you for your comments...we're working to resolve......" This hotel will never be what it should be if nothing is done, just words. I doubt that I will be back. It's just sad that something this grand cannot be what it once was...I only give it an "average", and that's for the historic value, service and location. I'm being generous, very generous.

“Needs updating” I was a bit disappointed in this hotel. It was listed as a 3 star, but did not feel like a 3 star at all. The hotel staff were really nice, which is why I'm rating the property a 3 instead of a 2. The hotel was very outdated and smelled - the carpet was old, basically everything was just old and not in a charming way. Our room was small and lacked the sophistication most 3 stars have. There was dirt behind the bathroom door, and the whole bathroom was outdated and grimy. The toilet was installed at an angle and sat very low - a strange configuration. We had a room that had a glass door that led out to the pool area, which was a neat idea, but didn't feel very safe. There was just a small lock from the inside, and the outside had no key lock, so wasn't practical to use unless someone stayed behind in the room to lock it back up. The pool area was decent and had a Tiki bar to grab beverages - very convenient. They over chlorinated the pool and it turned my son's black t-shirt a light brown color, and wasn't very pleasant on the eyes and skin. There is a really nice fitness center - clean and has lots of equipment. There was self or valet parking - I did the self parking at $18/night, it was outside - no covered parking. The hotel is located at the end of the Riverwalk, so is close to downtown and the Rivewalk shopping and restaurants. There is also a trolley nearby that picks up and drops off for a small fare. All in all - not terrible, but I way overpaid for what I got.

“Good stay at the San Carlos Hotel” My husband and I usually stay at the Elysee Hotel but the rates were well over $400 per room for this week. Hubby was in NYC for business and I tagged along. Friends on Trip Advisor recommended the San Carlos over the Affinia 50 for a "suites hotel". We got a nonrefundable rate of $310 per night for an "Executive Suite". The San Carlos is located in a great neighborhood. It is very quiet and very clean. Our room was very nice and large. King sized bed with a living area and small kitchen. The staff was great. The continental breakfast was minimal. They offer muffins and breads. Not quite sure why they do not offer bagels. We would definitely stay here again.

“New, centrally located” Great hotel for business. Rooms reminiscent of W hotels in its modern decor. I liked all the business conveniences like the desk actually works, lots of plugs for gadgets, and in room safe that holds a laptop. The restaurant and bar is excellent for early breakfast with good food options and late night drinks. Pool looked great tho I didn't get use it. They have a hosted wine hour which we missed each night because of long meeting days but the folks hosted our wine at the bar, which was very nice. I had a standard room which was very pleasant for a business stay. The funky bathroom barn-style roller door and half glass shower wall enclosure is form over function, as was the hair dryer that shorted out the GFI circuit. There is no in room coffee, which I don't like anyway but some do. I enjoyed the stay and would definitely go back. The driver service available was also much preferred over the usual taxi rides, at probably the same price. Very pleased overall.

“Very decent hotel near SoHo” Very decent hotel for the price and location very good if you need to be near SoHo. One of my cab drivers had a difficult time finding it as it was fairly new at the time but easy to find for everyone else. Rooms not that big but it is NY. Breakfast good and facility clean. My room had a view of another building very close in proximity but it is NY so that's what you often get.

“Great hotel, great location!” I just returned from a trip to San Fran and a stay at the Fairmont. The Fairmont brings what you would expect from the Fairmont collection. High standards. The hotel lobby was decorated nicely for holidays with a nice Christmas Tree, gingerbread house and a hang out area for kids with TV and table for drawing with crayons. The hotel it atop of Nob Hill, a great location within walking distance from Union Square and restaurants. The trolley stops around the corner so easy to take a ride to/from Union Square and Fishermans Wharf. We plan on returning.

“Not a great experience” There is a historical charm to the hotel, and it is near main museums, etc. We had to transfer to a room on the first day because the original room had many ants in the bathroom and a strong sense of smoke. Guest services never brought up the pillows and spray requested, and the staff is less than friendly.

“Nice stay, great staff, needs a face lift” I stay at this hotel for business. It's a nice place, wine happy hour is a good touch, and the staff is wonderful. For a business stay it works well. The furnishings seem a bit dated, could use a face lift and update. But overall this is a decent hotel choice. But there are many great choices in this area of Chicago.
“良いホテルです” NYCにしては部屋が広いです。 スタッフも親切で安心して宿泊出来ます。 場所も買い物でも観光にでも便利な所です。 ベルサービスも丁寧で安心して任せられます。

“Comfy and nicer than I expected!” I would best describe this hotel and a cross between a Sheraton and an Aloft hotel mixed together. The decor and comfort of a Sheraton but the modern style of an Aloft! Issac at the front desk was extremely helpful and even gave us a complimentary upgrade to a suite for our 2nd night of a 2 night stay! Will def stay here again! The only negative was when we got back from a day at the zoo and Aquarium we changed into our bathing suits and were excited to go jump in the pool and then relax in the hot tub. The pool was not heated and the water was ice cold. There was not a hot tub at all! We had to turn right back and go back to our room. I'm sure the pool will be fine once it starts getting hotter though.

“Crisp modern room, perfect location, gorgeous view, awesome service. A great New York hotel.” I took my husband to this hotel for his birthday, and we had a great experience. The location is amazing. It is very close to 5th Avenue shopping, and also walking distance to Broadway shows and Times Square. The subway is right down the street so it's also easy to get downtown. Across the street is the beautiful Bryant Park, which was filled with cute little gifty shops for Christmas and a skating rink, with Christmas music playing and a Christmas tree. Staying at the hotel made it easy to cross the street in the morning and go skating with almost no line-up. The room itself was a very clean, all white room with blond hardwood. We didn't get one of those magical free instant upgrades that I hear about sometimes, as they said they were sold out for the night, but they did manage to upgrade us to a park-view room for a nominal fee, which I appreciated. The view of the park was beautiful and very festive. I told them it was my husband's birthday and when we got back to our room we discovered a bottle of prosecco and two champagne flutes along with a bag of chocolates. Perhaps this is their standard practice and everyone gets it (which if that is the case, how awesome), but we took it as a nice birthday treat and really enjoyed and appreciated it. They included a funny little ambient noise machine which we thought was an amusing gimmick but ended up actually using. The bathroom was quite huge compared to the size of the bedroom, which was nice too. They also had an all-night room service menu that actually had food I would have ordered, although we didn't use it. The service in the hotel was great. There were so polite in all our interactions. When they held our bags after we checked out and wanted to go shopping, they asked where we were headed afterwards so they could immediately arrange for a taxi to take us to the airport. There were two bars/restaurants in the hotel, Koi, and the Cellar Bar, neither of which we went to, but both looked cool. There was a lineup outside Koi on Saturday night, so it looked pretty busy. Overall, we had a wonderful weekend in New York and a great stay at this hotel. We would totally stay here again.

“comfortable stay” The hotel's title includes downtown. It is about 30 minutes walk to Pier 66, from where boats go to Canada, about 10 minutes to Space Needle and about 20 minutes to Pike Market. So, very good location in that sence. However, the surrounding area is a business type location, so it does not look very attractive at night. I did not walk outside past 7pm, day time and mornings were fine though. The hotel has shuttle that takes you to Space Needel, West Lake shopping mall (4 block from there to Pike Market) and to conference center. All driving times are 5 minutes, if not less. Comfortable rooms, very very spacious. Small bathrooms though, but the sink and mirror were outside of the bathroom, so it was ok. Big screen TV. excellent AC unit, easy to use (unlike in many hotels) and really really QUITE! I have never stayed in a hotel with such a quite AC unit. My room did face the freeway, you do hear the noise but it is somewhat muffled so it did not bother me at all. I am not sure if anyone stayed in adjecent rooms, but i heard nothing at all during the entire stay (4 nights) good breakfast included in room rate, the variety stays the same, but I would not complain since there was not additional charge. There is also coffee/tea service in the lobby all day. The hotel has a bar that serves food, it was good and the pricing was nice. Bathroom amenities are of good quality. The indoor pool is really small, i would compare it with the pool for kids accompanied by adult. The water seemed somewhat chilly to me during the stay, although it was heated to 81 degrees according to thermometer. Complimentary business center, did not use internet in room, so cant write about connection speed etc... front desk is friendly, knowledgebale, very helpful; so are shuttle drivers. The hotel has umbrellas, so you can get one from bell stand if you forgot yours. parking is expensive, right next door is an open parking for a free less then hotel; however based on the non-attractiveness of the surronding area I would park with the hotel, just to be safe, even if its going to be just a few more extra $$

“Great if you get a renovated room” This is a large, atrium-style hotel that caters to the convention crowd. Hotels this big run the risk of being impersonal but I found the front desk and concierge at this Hyatt to be excellent. There was no line to check in and the receptionist gave clear descriptions of my room rate, the type of package I had, where the fitness room was, and told me I had a renovated room, all of which I appreciated. The room has been beautifully redone in sleek, subdued colors and furnishings. This was a gut job, not a cosmetic touch up, and the effort really showed. I especially liked the bathroom with its lit wall mirror and nicely tiled shower. The room has the usual coffee maker and room safe, and also a small empty fridge. I didn't eat in the restaurants but the room service breakfast (included as part of the package) was well prepared and presented, substantial and delicious. The fitness room had a good selection of cardio equipment but little in the way of weights--stations or free weights. I have seen photos of the unrenovated rooms and some of them look downright depressing. If you get a renovated room, it's great value for the money especially if you get a breakfast package.

“Disappointing hotel and asbolutely not worth the money” Title says it all really. Friendly staff at check in although there was a bit of a problem with the booking (although don't think this was the hotel's fault). The room, on the 21st floor, had city views: not even a hint of the park sadly. Room decor was simple but a bit tired and the room was a decent size for New Yor. Room furniture looked pretty cheap though. Reminded of all the fake wood stuff from the 70s. It was a very simply furnished room, no luxury here for sure. The TV (old) was in some giant rotating metal thing. Completely pointless and ugly. Would have been better off mounted on the wall. Closet space was poor: an area in the room with a curtain over it. The bathroom was better and worked well. The bed was okay: they had put in an additional down mattress on top of the traditional one which I'm sure made it more comfortable if a bit lumpy in places. No free wifi in the room which was a bit disappointing but free in the bar. Bar was shockingly expensive and by day became an espresso bar which served very nice coffee. Shame it didn't open until 0730 am. Morning noise was bad due to renovations on the roof. Drilling for hours.....apparently you couldn't escape it no matter where you were due to sound travelling through the building or something. Very irritating. So at $400 a night it was NOT good. Really not worth it. Very mediocre room which may be passble at half that amount but unless you get a really good deal, I wouldn't stay here again. Ever!

“less than 4 star quality” Although the location was good, the hotel itself fell short in several ways. I was initially given a room that had styrofoam packing bits all over the floor. No apologies, just had to go down and get another key for a similar room on a lower floor. The second room was reasonably sized, clean, with an excellent bed and flat screen TV, somewhat cramped bathroom with loose shower door handle, and a rug and a few towels that were beginning to look worn. Service was good, but not special. The hotel was always bustling, with elevators slow and crowded. For the price, I would have expected more, even in Manhattan.

“Very Nice Hotel - Relax and Enjoy” Very nice hotel, rooms were clean and spacious and the price wasn't all that bad - granted I got it at a copr price. It is right next to the Disney Hall of Music and some other attractions and is smak dap in downtown. Internet access sucked though and they put me in a business room. One would think that the internet access would have worked in that room. that pissed me off a bit

“"More than expected"” My wife and I recently stayed at this property for two nights. Check-in was very quick and clerks were friendly. Evening manager reception was less than what I had expected as compared to Embassy Suites in the DFW Metroplex. Breakfast was very good. My only criticism would be the musty smell of the room. Made me think they used to allow smoking in the room. What I was impressed with was the service we got after check-out. My wife left a pair of prescription glasses in the room. Upon returning home, I called the hotel and spoke to Oscar and Corina. The glasses had been found by housekeeping and turned in. I asked that they be mailed COD, however I was told that the hotel would FedEx them to me at no cost. Glasses were returned in good condition. I was impressed.

“Old World Charm” Pretty much everything about this Four Seasons property is a touch of the Old World. As you step out of the first set of elevators, the fountain, small chandeliers, and open, marble foyer greet you. My room was large, bright and airy, with pale floral wallpaper, big heavy drapes, round mirrors and marble-topped bedstands. The pillows are embroidered, crisp and sharp white. Strangley, the bedhead is made of cloth which is a bit icky. I really liked the layout of my room. The bathroom and mini-bar are closest to the door, which allows the bed and desk to be a good distance away from the door and outside hallway. That means it was very quiet and you could hardly notice people moving up and down the hall. Throughout the hotel, the staff are friendly and tend to the little things. The turn-down service refreshes your ice-bucket, cleans down the sink, oh-so-gently tidies things in your room, tilts the TV so you can see it from the bed, and puts some of the decorative pillows away in the closet. The concierge not only calls restaurants that don't take reservations to see how the long the wait is, but also mentions popular dishes you might (or might not) consider. The front-desk staff problem solve very quickly and politely. Excellent service takes a special somebody, and this hotel hires some of the best. The only problem, and it is a minor one, is that while it is called a Ritz-Carlton it really isn't. They don't recognize status in the Ritz-Carlton Rewards program, nor credit stays to that program.

“Not Great” Nice if you are bringing a dog -- they'll go out of their way to make the pet feel at home. However in general it's a disappointment. I stayed here when it first opened and was very impressed. Now in 2004 -- staff let a large bag of trash sit outside my room for days. Vending machines always empty. Minibars empty. They once forgot to bring my room service (which by the way tended to be horrible anyway). I wouldn't waste the money.

“Great Hilton” Stayed in this hotel for 2 nights and was very pleased with it. We were upgraded to a very nice suite and the staff were friendly and very helpful. Breakfast was good and of the usual Hilton standard. The hotel was within easy access of the major points of interest in the city. As we were there at a weekend, it was reasonably quiet and we got it for a very good prepaid rate. Would definitely stay here again.

“Enjoyable Stay” I go to Houston for work about 4 times a year. This is my first stay at the Westin Galleria. Pros: - great beds, as with all Westins. - direct access to Galleria Mall, which offers a lot of eating options. you can eat on a budget at the food court or step up and dine at one of the better restaurants located inside the mall. - spacious fitness center with up to date machinery and also has some free weights. - Starbucks is located a few steps away inside the mall. - free parking at the mall garage lot. but kind of a hard to find the nearest entrance at first. - Galleria area is the best and only place to stay in Houston. Cons: - front desk staff and concierge weren't the friendliest. service in general was pedestrian. - the hotel is supposed to be non-smoking, but my floor had distinct cigarette odor in its hallway. - business center charges an arm and a leg to print documents. better off to go to the kinko's across the street on Westheimer and get them printed there, if you have the time. I would stay here again, if the price was right.

“Good Location for the Price - Neighborhood Coming Up it Appears” I always try to find a location near the Riverwalk for my stays while in San Antonio on business, but with corporate cost cutting I need to keep my stays at $105 or less before taxes. Well, that is nearly impossible these days. I thought I would give this location a try as it came in at $98 before taxes. The hotel is about a half mile walk to Rivercenter mall, so it is a bit of a stretch calling it Rivercenter, but the reason I stay on the river is because I like to jog so that is not an issue. They also offer shuttle service every half hour. The area is a bit deserted, but the streets have been recently remodeled and it appears they are building a big hotel or residential tower nearby. I expect that within a year or so that this area will be booming. I did feel safe walking around and there was a police presence in the neighborhood just like the rest of the tourist areas. On first entering the lobby, I though there would be a breakfast room that is too small, but alas there were always tables in the morning. My room was a nice King room with microwave and fridge and wetbar. The room also had a living room. I believe all rooms at this hotel have a two room suite format, but am not 100% sure on that. Very comfortable bed. I was a bit concerned about the fact that my room faced the train tracks about 2/10 of a mile away. Combine that with the fact they leave ear plugs in the room, well, like I say I was concerned. I left the AC blower on all night and never heard a thing. I worked very late and slept in a bit and the curtains blocked light well and I never heard a train. The breakfast was typical Holiday Inn Express hot premade cheese omlettes, biscuts, gravy, bacon, as wellas cold hard boiled eggs, pastries, toaster french toast, muffins, cereals, juice, milk. Guest laundry is available on 3rd floor. They have small sized business center downstairs with one computers, a printer fax. High Speed Internet connection was nice. The inside of the hotel clean and nice looking with a nice enough lobby. They had a typical small but clean exercise room as well as a pool and hot tub. I will continue to stay here when the need arises in the area.

“É realmente um "achado". Muito bom.” Encontrei este hotel em NY e após uma pesquisa lendo as avaliações positivas resolví reservar através do site do próprio hotel para um curto período no início de setembro. Encontrei uma tarifa interessante e pouco abaixo da média dos valores cobrados pelos hotéis nas proximidades (5 avenida - St. Patrick e Central Park). Atendimento rápido e eficiente na entrada e na saída, quarto super confortável e grande incluindo o banheiro com banheira e tudo impecável desde a roupa de cama até os metais, cofre, tv nova c/ mesa de trabalho num apartamento standard...incrível ! Tudo brilhando com cara de novo...piso, lustres, espelhos etc. Elevadores amplos, novos e modernos (rapidos), restaurante no térreo e uma vista bem gostosa de se curtir nas espreguiçadeiras do terraço lá do alto em frente a academia. Vale a pena conhecer.

“Gorgeous Hotel - Larger Room!” Hotels in NY usually have gross, small rooms. This hotel is boutique and small, but has great dining options and a cool bar scene. Best part, is the room is spacious and the bathroom was really nice and clean! Great location, right in Soho, walking distance to TriBeCa and the village.

“Awesome location!” Enjoyed two nights in this wonderfully located hotel! Very nice lobby area and the staff were all very helpful and friendly. The room was comfortable, though a little older and worn. We did a lot of walking and shopping in this area. Staff was very accommodating when we asked for a later check out since our flight left later in the day, and they stored our luggage while we did last day shopping. A great experience at this hotel and I would return again!

“Not the Best W and not the Worst” Stayed here for New Years 2012. No major complaints. Was upgraded to a suite. The room was spacious with modern decore. Only downside was that I had to have housekeeping re-clean the room upon arrival.There were M&M mashed on the carpet.

“Superb on all levels (including parking)” I just returned from a three night stay (April 5-8). On previous visits I stayed at the Springhill Suites and Residence Inn, but this is my place from now on. As a road warrior (30 weeks on the road a year), I appreciated all this hotel had to offer. However, my first comment has to be on the post immediately prior to mine (one star), as to the $30 a day parking and no where to park. I, too, hate to pay hotel prices for parking. However, directly across the street as well as the surrounding streets is FREE parking from 6 p.m. to 8 a.m. and other times are $2.00 an hour. We paid a total of $9.00 for three days parking at this hotel. As previously mentioned the breakfast and dinner options are top notch and plentiful. Wine and beer is included at night. The staff is very friendly and the rooms are top notch. We were on the 9th floor which is the Hilton Executive floor. The rooms included kitchen, fireplace and balcony. The hotel is near the freeway, but my room faced an inside courtyard and was very quiet. As a gym rat, I seldom find hotel gyms satisfactory. This gym had the standard precors, treadmills, one bike and some free weights. However, there is an excellent 24 Hour Fitness (Sport) approximately five minutes away by foot (1827 Yale) with all the machines and equipment anyone could want. Cheers. Marius

“Professionally Run Hotel” I visited Baltimore in 2009 and stayed in the Hyatt, which is the next hotel to the Sheraton and unlike the Sheraton has views of the waterfront. The views of the waterfront are the Hyatt's only bonus - the Sheraton is a far better hotel. I stayed in the Sheraton for a conference. The conference and the hotel arrangements were professionally organised. The rooms were standard US style with a comfortable king size bed, excellent bathroom, widescreen TV. I got a good night's sleep every night I stayed at the Sheraton. The staff were very friendly and keen to assist wherever they could. The food in the Oriels restaurant could do with improving. The breakfast buffet was not good with lots of fat and sugary fare and little in the way of fresh items. The al carte breakfasts were better. The lunches were typical US with large colourful portions with salt and sugar being the primary flavours. I found the food disappointing but I am not fond of US style food which for me is strong on portion size, presentation, fats and sugars but lacking in quality and taste.

“Is lacking in friendly, acccommodating, hospitable, service” All of you non-smokers may not appreciate this review, but you should forget about the bad habit issue and read this to get an idea about the lack of courtesy and hospitality. Unfortunately, there are still travellers around who are smokers and go through some extra time and effort to find hotels willing to take our money (in this case a lot of money !). What happened to the slogan : 'Your home away from home' ? I had stayed at the Shelburne Murray Hill before, it was more than a bit worn down at the time (see other people's reviews from 2007 and before). I was delighted to hear that they did a major renovation and was looking forward to staying there, as it is convenient to all of the locations I had to go to during my one week stay. Double and triple-checked their website and did not find any reference ‘we are a non-smoking facility’. I had stayed in a smoking room during my earlier trip. Made the reservation well in advance and asked in capital letters for a smoking room. Received the confirmation, without any additional comments from the hotel. So, I’m thinking: I’m home free and all is in good order. The confirmation looked ‘personalized’ to me. Re-confirmed my arrival two days before and pointed out again, that I had asked for a smoking room when I made the reservation. Again, no reaction from the hotel. When we arrived, after 12 hours of travelling, they realized that I had asked for a smoking room and told me ‘there are no smoking rooms in this hotel’. When I mentioned my 2 email requests, the answer was ‘and you did not call to confirm this ?' Ok, so now it was my fault, I should have known that the hotel does not read their emails (seeing from some other reviews that seems to be a regular habit ). I always believed that hotel managers have to go to charm school and are being taught in their first class: ‘ the customer is always right’. After some discussions, that I am not willing to spend 298 US$ (incl. Tax) per day i.e. 1,970 $ (!!) for a week in a non-smoking room, the receptionist came-up with the splendid idea to give us a room with a balcony (it was raining outside and bad weather was expected all week) . I was also advised, that if I closed the door no smoke would get into the room, thus saving me the 250 $ a night (!!!) surcharge for extra cleaning (what would they be doing for that kind of money every day ? Bring in a crew of ten to fumigate the place ??) They were expecting me to sit outside in the rain with my laptop to get my work done ? The receptionist finally had the bright idea to call the manager over (who did not bother to show-up for another 15 minutes). No ‘we’re sorry for your inconvenience’ – no! it was back to this being all my fault, as I had obviously not seen the notice on their website, that they are a non-smoking facility. When I told him I checked it several times, he admitted that he had not looked at it in a while and would have to call the IT-people to change this, if it was indeed not mentioned. Aha, what happened to ‘the customer is always right’ ? Again more discussions and although the receptionist had confirmed that all of their affiliate hotels are non-smoking hotels, the manager finally offered to call around and see if any had rooms available ( again, it appeared to be my problem more than his, to find an alternative hotel.), but only ‘if I wanted him to do so’. Their affiliate ‘around the corner’ (separate and favourable (!!) review to follow under ‘Eastgate Tower Hotel’) accepted us. The manager with the ‘it-is-all-your-fault-and-I-saved-your-day-attitude’ did not bother to call us a cab (maybe because the rain had let off) and it is not ‘around the corner’ to get there ( from 37th over to 39th and from Lexington to 2nd is a hike with two heavy suitcases on a steamy NY afternoon, after 12 hours of travelling). While I understand that it is a nuisance for non-smokers to stay in a room where someone has been smoking (out most of the day, in only in the am and late at night – how many ziggies can that be !) you would think the economy is bad enough for them to accommodate someone willing to pay almost 2,000 US$, even if it meant to spend some extra time to clean the room. Again, it was NOT mentioned on their website, I did NOT get any response from them and I was ‘stranded’ at their place at 5 pm after 12 hours of travelling. Aha, all my fault, I should have called them and asked them if they did read my emails ? Sorry, but the rooms may be all nice and clean and renovated, but even when I turn into a non-smoker, this is not a place I would visit again, because of their attitude and the way they are treating their customers.

“Disappointing- Nice Room, Indifferent Service” Just returned from a 2 night stay. The Valencia is in a great location in the dead center of the Santana Row area, with shops and restaurants all around it. It is modern and has a cool atmosphere. The room was very comfortable. Valet parking in front is quick and convenient. Sounds great so far right ? This would easily have been a 4 star rating from me except for 2 things. First, the service at the front desk was cool and indifferent. In order to get in and out of the hotel you pass the desk , never a greeting , never a smile. The staff look more interested in each other than in the guests. I checked a couple of bags and the guy stood and watched me as I tagged them, put them in the area and then again when I retrieved them. Never even offered to help. One time my wife cheerily said good night to the staff on our way up and none of them even responded. I rarely criticize hotels to this degree but the management here needs to do some guest sensitivity training. The only exception were the valet guys who were uniformly nice. The second point is the buffet breakfast. Very limited choices and even worse hardly any place to sit. So poor that even though it was included on our second morning we passed and went out for breakfast. This place is cool but that quality wears off fast if you don't take care of the basics.

“An airport hotel with no airport transportation available?” I chose this hotel because it had van service to the airport an I needed a place to stay the night before an early morning flight. The rate seemed reasonable for a mid-quality hotel and TripAdvisor's reviews made it sound acceptable . . . there were some complaints but more than one had a "Great!" experience. My GPS took me to where I could see the hotel on my left and then told me to turn right. I should have listened. The building looks run down, possibly even deserted, from a block or so away. I was relieved to find it crowded with guests. Then I began to sense problems. While checking in, I confronted a sign informing me that van service to the airport began at 4:30 a.m. I needed a van at 4 a.m. Discouraged, I asked the front desk to reserve a cab to take me to the airport the next morning. Upstairs, the hallways were worn and dog-eared. The room itself was o.k., but the bathroom was so small there was no way two people could have fit in it at the same time. Luckily, I was traveling alone. In order to avoid having to return my rental car so early the next morning, before the rental agency opened, I returned it that evening, took the rental car van to a terminal and called the hotel to come pick me up, as they had instructed me to do. Over half an hour later, I called again. They told me to take a cab and they would reimburse me. I may be asking too much, but the least I expect from an airport-area hotel is a ride to and from the airport. Live and learn.

“An awesome, preserved gem!” Wow! Everywhere you look there is incredible detail. It really is a privilege to wander the hotel and take it all in - time travel! A sable throw on the bed! It's located in the thick of 6th street so there are plenty of opportunities to have fun.

“Very comfortable and great location for the city” Stayed at this hotel this month on a quick business trip. We arrived late on the Saturday night and check in was as simple as ever, the only issue was they (the hotel staff) put both rooms in my travel companions name which confused the billing quite a lot. The room was fine, not extremely large but as a city goes it was good, plenty of space really for one person. It was very clean and I have to say was well decorated and kept very well. The bathroom was a great size and like other reviewers I did not like the shutter separating the bathroom from the bedroom. Overall the room was very comfortable and well furnished, the TV had plenty of choice. We did dine in the bar the 1st night and had a single appetizer with two beers which cost us over $55 bucks which was expensive. The hotel is a large city hotel and lacks charter really, the staff could do better to make you feel more at home but location and comfort was great.

“Nice stay at the Doubletree” We stayed at the Doubletree from Sept. 10th-11th. I have to admit everyone was absolutely right about the delicious chocolate chip cookies. They were very tasty and a wonderful welcoming treat! The reason we selected this hotel was the price ($118, plus parking-$9/day) and the location. We wanted to be near downtown Boston, but didn't want to pay the hefty price. The Doubletree was perfect because it is two blocks from the T (red/green line). We walked over in the morning, bought a day pass, and spent the rest of our day in the heart of Boston. We really didn't spend any other time at the hotel or in our room except to sleep. Overall, the hotel was nice and I can't complain about the warm cookies! P.S. If you want two GREAT restaurants in Boston, try Vida Dolce (Italian) and Stephanie's on Newbury (try the meatloaf)! Both are EXCELLENT!!!

“Comfort and convenience in the theater district” My room was large and very comfortable, especially for NYC hotels in this price range (under $300 per night). The linens and toiletries were exceptional and housekeeping was very attentive. There was a coffeemaker, 'fridge and microwave oven in a small kitchen area. The location is great for theater venues as well as any other NYC locales as it is just a couple of blocks from the subway system (50th St. stations). I must add that the staff were very helpful with particular kudos to David, the doorman, who seemed to know every good restaurant in the neighborhood, and there are several. I can highly recommend the Belvedere.

“Like a magnificent wine in its slow but inexorable decline....” I wish there were a way to award The Towers 4.5 stars but there isn't. Having said that, many things about the hotel are charming and very beautiful. We traveled on Amex Platinum and were upgraded to a GIGANTIC suite, complete with a hallway, pantry, huge living room, a ladies' boudoir and very large bedroom. Antiques everywhere in the suite, although here is where the problems began. The marble bathroom was clearly outdated in terms of lighting and fixtures. Water pressure was OK, but the water never got really hot. Lights around mirror were not great, impossible to put on makeup and know that it wasn't going to look clownish when stepping outside. The HVAC unit was broken in the bedroom - had to call maintenance who appeared after 5 minutes (good) and proclaimed that someone - a guest or who knows - had inserted "a screw" into the unit somehow, thereby preventing the temperature from going over 69 in the room. Nevermind, it was May and we turned off the A/C altogether. But the bedroom unit needed replacement or renovation for sure. Bedding was very nice - great, starched sheets, many pillows, great comforter. Bose radio and flatscreen TV in the room, totally OK. But NO SIZEABLE BLACKOUT drapes, meaning at 6am, the bedroom was quite light - not great if you're coming from a different time zone and just want to sleep in. Some of the antiques in the suite were lovely, but also in need of reparation. The little chair in front of the ladies' desk had very stained upholstery - not appealing. Toiletries were so-so - I would have expected Hermes or at least L'Occitane in this class of hotel. Internet wireless was OK - $15.95 for every 24 hours, although we are HH Gold members and got ours for free. The minibar was simply OUTRAGEOUS. A 6oz. still water bottle was $8. And that was Waldorf's own water - not Evian or Pellegrino. The rest of the snacks were strange - glass containers of jelly candy, nuts at $16 and some cookies - I've seen better minibars at Hyatt or Marriott. Didn't have occasion to use the spa or the fitness room, although we made an attempt to have the included Continental breakfast in the Tower Lounge on the 26th floor. It was absolutely mobbed when we got there, so the manager graciously offered us free American breakfast at Oscar's downstairs in the Astoria portion of the hotel. Perfectly serviceable buffet, in fact the oatmeal was cooked from scratch, whereas the Lounge only provides oatmeal in packets. Granted, a trifle, but for oatmeal lovers it does mean something. The fresh fruit could have been more varied - have had so much better buffets at other 5 star hotels, but that's a different matter. Oscar's is most likely not 5-star, as it belongs to the Astoria and not the Towers. So was there anything positive? Yes of course. The service is impeccable. The staff is flawless. The sheer grandeur of the suite was breathtaking - where are you going to get 1,200 sq feet in NYC for less than $600/night? But the entire Tower needs a serious renovation, from carpeting that is so worn down that we kept slipping and sliding in the room, to the faded beige walls. I am all for antiques - I truly despise chains like W and the like - but bathroom fixtures, lighting, HVAC systems, and dirty upholstery need to be replaced with some frequency. After all is said and done, I will save any future stay for the post-renovation party.

“Seemed better than the rating suggested” I stayed 3 nights at the Hyatt for a conference at the Washington Convention Center. I found the room to be spacious, the bed comfortable, and the shower really quite good. The room was perfectly clean. I had a room on the 11th floor that overlooked the atrium. I can see what others mean about the sound of the air conditioning and the atrium noise at night, but neither of them were loud enough to bother me at all. I was disappointed with the internet service, which was important for the work that I was doing while there. I paid the exorbitant $15/day for "faster" service, and it still wasn't terribly fast. WiFi costs hotels very little - that's why less pricey hotels can offer it for free. So it's just crazy that pricier hotels rip off their customers like this. I liked the fact that the hotel was just a couple of blocks walk to Chinatown and the Gallery Place/Verizon Center area, where there are lots of places to eat.

“Clean, plush and comfortable” Rooms are spacious, clean and the beds are VERY comfortable. Starbucks coffee in the room. Fitness room is very nice. Good location, walking distance to just about everything. Highly recommend this hotel.

“Nice hotel, good location, good price” This is a well located, nice hotel with friendly staff. The room we stayed in was large and modern. The location is central and the price is very reasonable. We were able to walk to and from the mall which has a movie theatre and some nice shopping. I would stay here again.

“good cheap motel” easy friendly check in, paid about $90.00 + tax for the room which was very small but clean and updated. My big mistake was not waiting for a room away from the street, the noise was terrible. These rooms should be sold at a discounted rate. Free internet was nice as I was on a brief business trip and needed to spend time doing email before my meeting.

“A nice stay at a nice hotel in an excellent area” We spent 3 mights at the hotel, beginning July 22 and had a very nice stay. We arrived at the location to be informed we needed to go to a different area for parking / check-in. What made this initial annoying experience a good one was the fact they had personnel at the curb to direct you and a pre printed map with driving directions to the correct entrance. It was a nice touch. Check-in was fine and quick. Bell service was prompt and friendly. We parked at the hotel and while it outrageously expensive ($49.02 a night), it is very convenient. We proceeded to our room which was on the 14th floor in the mid-rise tower. The room was well appointed, spacious and clean. There was a nice bathroom and a great flat screen tv. Another excellent feature was the "wired room" concept. A centralized station where you can connect your laptop, Ipod etc. Listened to our Ipod on the flat screen much of the stay. We visited the Starbucks in the lobby but didin't use any other food outlet. The gym is currently in transition and located in a banquet room. Although the location isn't ideal, the equipment is brand new and top notch. This is a temporary gripe. Our only problem at all during the stay was when we first arrived at the room, the sheets on the bed were dirty and ripped. While I would not have expected to see such, a single phone call was all that was needed for prompt action. The service manager apologized to excess, and within 2 or 3 minutes (I swear, and this place has 1,500 rooms), the housekeeping manager was in our room. He too apologized and offered something to make up for the very modest inconvenience (we didn't take him up on any offer as none was truly needed). He promised a housekeeper would be up momentarily to change the sheets and again within a couple moments she appeared as well. All in all it was a very pleasant stay. At $140 a night plus tax, I think it was a fair price for a very nice, centrally located property with employees who care about your experience.

“Noisy but fun hotel” I stayed here on business for two nights in April 2011. The suite was clean and functioned well but seemed a bit small compared to the description. The only issue was noise. My room faced the pool/nightclub area that comes alive on Friday night. This made it hard to rest until 2am. I guess that it is to be expected when "Rock" is in the name of the hotel! Great location and we loved having NOBU for sushi right in the lobby!

“Solid 4.5 but thin walls” My wife and I stayed at the Palace for three nights, having driven up in our rental car from Santa Cruz. I booked the room on Hotwire and got a great deal--a huge room with king bed for 150 dollars a night plus tax. The lobby and first floor of the hotel are remarkably beautiful, and our room was very nicely appointed in terms of linens, towels, furniture, etc. Beautiful vintage solid brass hardware on the door of the room, monogrammed, etc. Very nice. We did not demand much of the staff but our experience was with them was just fine, nor did we use the beautiful pool, much to our regret. Others have commented on the very thin walls and it is true--and weird for a hotel of this caliber. Bring your earplugs or sleep with a pillow over your head if the guy in the next room has a cough. A couple of things you should know: they charge for internet in the room (still!) but there is free wi-fi in the lobby. A small biz computer in the lobby is for printing out boarding passes and not for e-mail. Otherwise checking your e-mail in the business center will cost you 5. 25 min. charge (please). The hotel is in the middle of the biz district so night time there is dead, but three blocks aways is Union Square, and a few more in the opposite direction is the Embarcadero. Better location imho than Nob Hill etc. Re. coffee in the a.m. they supply it in the lobby and it is fine. We did not check out the bar or restaurant because there are so many within walking distance. Less than a block to to the right as you exit the hotel is a Starbucks if you need latte (which we do). Parking by the hotel is 50 bucks per night (highway robbery) but they will tell you that right around the corner on the same block are two garages where you can park for 20 dollars a night--fine for a big city and plenty convenient. Very easy walking distance (2 blocks) to SFMoMa (and other museums such as the Jewish Contemporary) and the Yerba Buena Arts Center. Be sure to grab dinner at The Slanted Door at the Ferry Bldg. on the Embarcadero. You can walk there (and make your rez online, early). Would I stay there again? Sure, but keep in mind the thin wall problem. Everything else was 4.5 in my book.

“Another Great Hotel Monaco” I am a big fan of the Monaco hotels (have stayed at them in San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver), and would happily stay at any one of them again if I had the choice. I love the boutique-y details (pet-friendly, that you can have a goldfish delivered to your room to keep you company, the jazz music playing when I arrived in my room, the wine in the evenings). The location of the hotel is also great for both downtown business and proximity to restaurants and other things to do.

“Unexpected gem five steps from Fanuiel Hall” In all the times I have been to Fanuiel Hall, I never knew the Harborside Inn was just steps away on State Street. It was a pleasant surprise! The hotel is modern and offers free wi-fi. The bed was very comfortable and there were no issues with the room. There are several parking options and Fanuiel Hall/Quincy Market and the North End are right at your front door.

“Great stay at Embassy Suites” Excellent location, great room, great breakfast -- we were pleasantly surprised by how nice the rooms were, and enjoyed use of the internet towers in the lobby. It was quite crowded since we were there over spring break, but the hotel dealt cheerfully and efficiently with huge crowds at breakfast -- food was quite decent and the coffee was really good, which is such a rarity at these places. I would recommend it whole heartedly to families.

“Impressive older hotel” My wife and I stayed 3 nights at the Park Hyatt Bellevue in late July for a business conference. The overall experience was above average but I question whether the hotel rates a "5 star" as indicated. I disagree with one reviewer who said it was easy to find - the entrance for the hotel is not well-marked and is actually on a side street. The hotel is unique in that the lobby is on an upper floor with only a small entry area on floor level. The lobby is also small but I found this appealing. The real strength of the hotel is its excellent customer service. The staff is friendly and does an impressive job such as actually remembering your names. The check-in clerk walked us to the elevator and highlighted aspects of the hotel- a nice touch. Later we asked about seeing a suite and were personally shown two suites with no pressure. The room service was very timely and the housekeeping was excellent. The concierge always provided helpful advice. The other positive about the hotel is the older architecture which is most noteworthy in the rooms. Some will like this, others won't. Travelers who like modern hotels should stay at another place. I thought the room had character and our room had been well maintained. I liked that the business center provided free internet access. The hotel obviously has a great downtown location and we felt the price was reasonable for the low 200's per night. The negatives were a fairly slow elevator and I did not like having to share the exercise facility with half of downtown Philly as the facility is actually open to the public.

“Overrated” We took the CTA Blue Line from O'Hare to Clark & Lake. The hotel is between two CTA stations. The other one at Chicago and Milwaukee does not have an elevator. With luggage, you want the Lake and Clark CTA station, which has an elevator. From Clark & Lake, it's a short $5 cab ride to the Waldorf. The day before we arrived, I noticed online that we had been pre-assigned to an Astoria suite, but at check-in we got downgraded to a Waldorf suite. Upon asking, we ended up in an Astoria suite on the 7th floor with a huge terrace. Despite the lower floor, the room was quiet. Our room had Asprey toiletries, which are being phased out and replaced by Ferragamo products. As Diamond members, we got the free drink coupons that can be used in the 2nd floor bar or in the 3rd floor restaurant Balsan. We had our free drinks with dinner at Balsan and also used the 15% off food coupon. The waiter was friendly and cheerful and returned the food coupon to us in case we wanted to re-use it for breakfast the following morning. Food portions were on the small side (probably average-sized, but not the gargantuan ones that Americans expect.) We each ordered a large plate and then ordered a third large plate and a dessert to share. Aside for Balsan, we found the service to be so-so. The Balsan staff was wonderful and there is an obligatory 18% tip accessed. Since there is no tipping elsewhere in the hotel, the service seemed perfunctory. The staff went through the motions, but without any enthusiasm or sincerity. While the room was nice (4-stars), I place a higher value on customer service and thus downgraded the rating to 3-stars.

“Great hotel, Great location” The hotel was at a great location, quite area, esay access to Space neddle. the staff was excellent and very friendly and helpful. Very clean rooms with comfortable beds. Would stay again

“Long elevator waits at busy times” The hotel is a good value for Georgetown, but a tiny lobby and an inadequate number of elevators make it feel somewhat claustrophobic and overcrowded. Entrance is in a courtyard off the street, so it is easy to off load the car or taxi. Our suite was large, but only had a single bath for such a large unit. It was clean and fairly comfortable. Good breakfast, and the usual tight, over-priced DC parking garage (self-park). That said, if you want to be in Georgetown, this is a good location. Lots of restaurants and stores nearby (and lots of tourists) and the staff (there weren't many) were friendly.

“Clean and Comfortable.....but temporarily noisy with off site construction” I was warmly greeted by staff....Room is clean and comfortable.... Unfortunately the property is surrounded by construction on both freeway and backside building. The property entrance was difficult to locate as it is in the middle of construction zone. The first night, a good sleep, normal traffic sounds.....However, 2 nd night was noisy with off site construction.....i know management cannot control off site public works ....once construction ends the hotel will be a nice place to relax.... Parking is well lit and plentiful. Internet works well. Love the Starbucks coffee in the room.....Thanks again for the good humor at check in!

“More On The Greatness” I agree with everything that's been said so far. The location is great. Beautiful rooms. The food and service at the restaurant were outstanding. But I also wanted to add that the fitness room was in excellent condition.

“A tale of two parts” There are a lot of great things about this place and a few bad things. I have stayed here a few times. It is the only half decent hotel in the Dundalk area of Baltimore. They offer free shuttles to the Inner Harbour but not to the airport. There is a dinner theatre in the hotel which shares its Kitchen with the hotel restaurant, so the food is very good. The bar is ok, but it is kind of stuck at the entrance to the restaurant. The hotel used to also serve as the Grayhound terminus, and had a few fast food places in the terminus, but that has now closed. The rooms are adequet, and very resonably priced. I had a problem on this visit with the restaurant closing 15 minutes early and refusiing to serve me, but the manager came out and talked to me, and dealt with the situation camly, prefessionaly and pleasantly, turning the whole situation into a positive.

“Pre Holiday Getaway” Spent 2 nights at the hotel Monaco as a pre-holiday get away w/ my 2 twenty-something nieces and my sister. The hotel is a relatively quick $35 cab ride from BWI and just a few blocks from the inner harbor. Front desk staff were very welcoming and expedient upon our arrival. Our double queen room on the 12th floor was extremely spacious and perfect for the 4 of us. The beds were clean and comfortable and the bathroom was nice and spacious. However, the sliding door was a bit off ~ I would prefer a real door vs. the slider. We had a drink at the B&O Friday night which had a few customers at the bar and a few diners throughout the restaurant. Service was slow and they were not able to offer the wine presented on their bar menu. The hotel recommended Maisy's restaurant which is a bistro just a few blocks away. The restaurant and service was wonderful and we really enjoyed our home made crabcakes! We found it a bit odd that there seemed to be a lot of people lingering/sleeping in the lower part of the hotel lobby during the next day (Saturday) ~ It was not clear if these folks were just very tired hotel guests taking a break or non-hotel guests coming off the street and relaxing on the comfortable chairs/couches. We enjoyed walking around the inner harbor and took advantage of the good sales in the harbor shop mall. On Saturday night we went to Howl at the Moon dueling piano bar. This place is great and tons of fun! I highly recommend to anyone. The bar does not serve any food so you would want to eat prior if you planned on staying a while. Cover charge is $5 before 8:00pm and then increases to $10. The hotel completely missed the mark on our room service order. We called in for 4 sandwiches around 1:00am and waited close to an hour for extremely sub-par pulled pork sandwiches that were cold and somewhat tasteless. The gym is on the 3rd floor and is equipped with numerous cardio machines and free weights. The treadmills did not allow for headphones and the remotes some of the remotes were not in working order. The water taxi is a nice way to travel to Fells Point or other areas within the harbor. The fee is $10per person for an all day pass. Lots of the bars/pubs in Fells point have great bunch and drink specials on the weekends (ie, $10 for all you can drink bloody mary’s or mimosa). Overall a good trip but if I went to Baltimore again I would stay right on the harbor or in Fells Point ~ we did not always feel 100% safe walking back to the hotel in the late evening hours. . The hotel was very helpful with holding our luggage until departure and the bellhop was attentive in securing a town car for our ride back to the airport.

“First time in an Aloft - great stay” Stayed two nights. The area is OK but not as good as Midtown or Upper East/West Side. The subway station is about 2 blocks away. Aloft adopts W’s hip style but offers everything in a budget. Differences are in details - no 100% cotton sheets, no pillow top on mattress, no ipod dock, and such. This Aloft is brand new - just opened for a couple of months and I think they are doing a great job in pulling this off since a lot of times you will encounter many issues in a newly opened hotel but we had no issues at all during our stay. The bed is good and the room is good size in NYC standard. The sink top is small but looks nice and you can put your stuffs on the shelf next to it. The Bliss toiletries are nice. The bathroom has no tub but a big shower - just like in W. A daily bottle of water and internet are free (the speed is slow though). The staff were all nice and friendly. I think our experience exceeded our expectation and I will definitely consider this hotel for future visits to NYC.

“Very good downtown LA” Very good downtown LA hotel - Above average luxury rooms. We had great service and an excellent bfast. Nice small pool and hot tub on the roof. You will be happy with this hotel - we spent $86 via priceline. Only negative is the potential view (anoth building) if you are on the woring side of the hotel.

“Small-scale luxury” I have stayed at the Hotel Lumen numerous times for short and longer stays. The staff is top-notch. It's small overall size reminds me of a European property, but the rooms are large, comfortable and clean. And it's pretty easy to get a good deal on rooms and I have often gotten an upgrade. The location is awesome, it's in the middle of Dallas, in University Park, directly across the street from SMU with easy access to highways and the DART train. It's 10 minutes to the heart of downtown and 10 minutes north to Northpark for shopping. I recommend the Hotel Lumen to European travelers looking for a good "home base" in Dallas.

“Good Location & Service” Four nights at end of May into early June for roughly $350/night through travel agent for an upgraded, nice "spectacular room" (Starwood labeling). Very good value, have stayed here before, will again but not for more than ~ $450/night. Bellman - helpful, efficient. Lobby - slightly cramped. Check in - computer down and given someone else's room, problem quickly rectified. Three elevators - cramped and older, but never too long of a wait. Room - good size, no obvious signs of wear. Service - extra towels brought within minutes of call. Location - close to shopping and metro.

“Comfortable, clean, and convenient” This is a great hotel to stay at in San Antonio. Check-in was very smooth, and the front desk staff are warm and welcoming. The room was very nice. We got a suite with two queen beds. The room was big, clean, and the beds were terrific. The coffee maker did not work well, however. It was also very cute. I appreciated the Manager's Reception at night. The snacks at the reception are simple snacks like pretzels, chips, and gummi bears. The big draw for me was free drinks. That is always a plus. The cooked-to-order breakfast went like this; What they cook to order are egg dishes and omelets. The omelets were actually very yummy, and were cooked well. The other thing is the hot breakfast buffet, and that was mediocre at best. The big thing is that this hotel is within reasonable walking distance to the Riverwalk, as well as the Majestic and Empire theaters, the former of which we went to for the symphony that played the night we stayed here. The location is exceptionally convenient to all of that. This, as I said, is a great new hotel, and a great place to stay in Downtown San Antonio

“Great Hotel/Modern Ammenities” You can't go wrong at this hotel. Great location, service, etc. I had a room problem at check-in. The front desk person was giving me the boilerplate on not being able to accommodate what had already been promised and noted. Five minutes after going to the less desirable room, management called and rectified the matter. This is an excellent, NYC hotel with professional, experienced staff, from the doormen to the restaurant staff.

“Marriott Metro Center is one of Washington's better hotels” Conveniently located near the Metro Center metro station, the Marriott Metro Center is nicely situated near Ford's Theater, the White House and the National Mall. The hotel itself is well-appointed and maintained, with large, comfortable guest rooms. There is a Starbucks in the lobby, as well as a restaurant. The hotel has a pool, which is not stadard fare in DC. We found the service and housekeeping to be excellent and the overall hotel quality is among the very best that we've encountered in Washington. Internet service is excellent, but it is an extra charge through a third party vendor.

“Too Many Problems” We love the location of this hotel, but when we stayed there recently we had no hot water one morning and the A/C was not working during our stay. The lovely lady who manages the front desk apologized profusely and made an adjustment on our bill, but the physical plant of this aging facility needs to be overhauled.

“truly great hotel” I do quite a bit of travelling and love boutique hotels. There is something about the Sofitel chain that I feel makes them really wonderful places to stay around the world. I usually stay at Sutton Place Hotel or here and this hotel is better. It's just something they do that makes it better than a lot of other 4 star hotels. Rooms are oh so clean - no dust that you might find in other places. Bathrooms are PRISTINE. Size of room is large but the design still makes the room cozy - just a different feel than your standard avg. hotel room. The hallways and elevators are beautifully decorated and the view from the 17th fl is amazing! The beds have featherbeds so their uber comfy and rooms offer plenty desk space if you are working. The hotel charges for wi-fi in rooms but Tmobile is cheaper per day you can get too. There's a level of quality that makes this hotel my fave in Chicago. There are other cuter more boutique hotels that actually fit my style but Sofitel has for me always been clean, service friendly and consistent most importantly. I like that the staff is courteous, helpful and friendly - professional - w/o trying to be your friend which some hotels do. I'm from Chicago just visiting on this trip but if in Chicago for the 1st time, location in Gold Coast is ideal for restaurants and shopping.

“The biggest hotel room in the world” But oddly laid out. It was (literally) 13 steps from the door to the window, so there was plenty of space, but the bathroom area was beyond tiny -- really small toilet/shower closet and a such a low ceiling in the sink area that the mirror gave me a lovely view of my neck and upper torso. That said, it was a great experience. We were upgraded to a "tranquility" room, which meant that we had a reclining massage chair that was hard to leave. Very comfortable bed, huge room, great view. Very friendly and helpful staff (as seems to be the case in all Kimpton hotels). My one caveat (and this relates to the area more than to the hotel) is that if you're looking for a late-night meal, you're out of luck. I wandered all over Dupont Circle trying to find someplace to eat before finding a (fortunately very, very good) gyro place more or less around the corner (and across the street from the Hotel Palomar (where we'd stayed the week before and which offers 24-hour room service; I was almost tempted to go in, say I'd been there, was staying around the corner, and could I pretend I was still checked in so I could order room service ...). Regardless, a great, great experience, and I'd happily stay there again.

“Great hotel!” We were very impressed with the quality of this hotel. Upon being picked up from the airport (in the complimentary airport shuttle), we were offered bottles of water (it was a hot day). We also took advantage of the airport shuttle for our return trip, and we were once again pleased. All of the staff that we encountered were friendly and helpful. The hotel was always clean, as was our room. The complimentary breakfast was great; it included cereals, oatmeal, fruits, a waffle maker, juice, milk, hard-boiled eggs, bagels, toast, breakfast sandwiches, yogurt, muffins, coffee, and tea, and we could eat as much as we wanted to!
