The coffee and tea are also available 24 hours a day. The business center features 2 computers, a printer (maybe 2), and an ATM. The outdoor pool and whirlpool are very nice, clean, and well-kept. The "exercise room" could use some serious updating, but it's better than nothing. It features an old weight machine, stair-climber, and a broken treadmill. Additionally, there was a broken scale, towels, water, and a TV. The location of the hotel is convenient, however, it is not really near any nightlife or excitement. The light rail runs right by the hotel, and we were concerned that it would be loud, however, it was not. Our room was very quiet and the a/c unit worked perfectly. If your purpose for staying in this hotel is nightlife and fun, it is not recommended. However, if you are looking for a nice hotel in a central location, this is the place!

“Charming, antique ... ok, old.” A historic building on the edge of Balboa Park and walking distance to Hillcrest. Beautiful architecture, exterior facade and charming, traditional public spaces. But my room was just plain old. The floors creaked, paper thin walls, the wall finishes were a bit worn, no forced air heat/AC, ceiling fans and radiators, doors that didn't fit quite well, and a bathroom in need of a renovation. A parking lot for 40 cars and 72 rooms, do the math. That aside, the staff at the hotel are great! The type of service you'd expect at a much more expensive hotel. They are attentive, friendly, and sincere. Would I stay here again? Probably not, since I much prefer a modern and contemporary space. But some would definitely appreciate the charm.

“Best choice in SOHO” This is a great property. I'm usually a bit skeptical of "trendy" boutique properties as the style usually comes at the expense of good service. This property does a good job of playing it cool while still providing good service. The rooms are small but reasonable by NY standards. The complementary mini-bar is a great amenity. The location could not be better for SOHO.

“Historic Hotel” Stayed two nights at the Hilton Towers on Michigan Avenue attending a conference. If you like hotels steeped in history this might be just right for your stay. It is a massive property with 3000 rooms, and lots of meeting space. We liked the mini TV’s in the elevators that showed trivia presentations about the history of the hotel. We learned that the last 20 minutes of “The Fugitive” with Harrison Ford was filmed in and around the hotel, and that every president of the America has visited at some point. Our room (with two double beds) was comfortable. The hotel is showing a little wear and tear along the room corridors but everything worked. The concierge desk was very knowledgeable with regards to restaurant recommendations, bookings, and directions. In fact all the hotel staff was very professional. Recommendation: Visit Buddy Guy’s Legends Bar behind the hotel for a great Cajun meal and some fantastic Blues.

“Great location, some cleanliness issues” This hotel is locate very close to Millennial Park (where the silver bean - cloudgate is), The Navy Pier, the river, the lake, the Miracle Mile. It is a great location. Overall the property is probably a 4 star but this stay rated a 2 star because of the unsanitary conditions in my room. Things to know: -Wifi is $13.95 a night but free in the lobby - Parking is $51 a night - The refrigerators in the rooms are only for mini bar. If you take something out you are AUTOMATICALLY charged for the item plus 11% tax, and 20% restocking fee (that makes for some expensive chips). - A fridge is $25.00 if you need one -This is a pretty quiet hotel for it's size - There are starbucks pouches of coffee, early grey and wild orange TZAO tea in the room - There is a coffee shop called Link in the bottom of the hotel, coffee prices are a little inflated soda cans are $3.50 - In general the pricing in the hotel is high -This is a really big hotel. If you stay here make sure you build in time for things like check-in check out - I waited for 5 minutes for an elevator during a conference break. - It took me two hours to get to the Sheraton from O'Hare on a shuttle and it wasn't rush hour. Check in was easy, I got upgraded to a river-view and they comped the very expensive (13.95 a night wifi).It went down hill from there. My room was nasty. I travel a lot and only once have I ever encountered a room as disgusting as this upon arrival. It had clearly not been cleaned. There were personal items from the previous guest, the towels had clearly been refolded (they smelled very funky) and when I got them replaced the new ones smelled fine. There was thick dust on the tables and tv stand. The glass glasses had lots of smudges on them, the paper coffee cups had been used and turned back over. There were long strands of hair that were not mine all over the bathroom and desk. The duvee cover (which normally isn't changed between guests) was stained and the bed ruffles were just downright disgusting. To me this indicates that the room is not routinely cleaned well. I let the front desk know and they responded very well but there continued to be cleanliness issues throughout my 4 night stay. Every time I complained they responded - but - I should not have to ask for CLEAN towels on my first night in the room. It sounded like my issue may have been isolated to the floor I was staying on - so maybe there is a training issue with new housekeeping staff? Regardless, it was gross. The front desk staff was VERY kind and responsive. I stayed at this hotel about 7 years ago for a different conference and had a nice stay.

“Excellent - Pure Excellent!” Visit NYC often - always stay more in upscale hotels, I was a little concerned about the "Red Roof" name...but when I arrived I was pleasantly surprised by the beautiful intimate lobby. Then off to my room...WOW - better than most upscale hotels! Contemporary, stylish, immaculate, unbelievable! Flat screen televisions - the works...and FREE Hi-Speed Internet in NYC - unheard of! This place is the best! I still cannot believe it and the price! WONDERFUL!!!!!!!!!!!!!

“Excellent quality and great value” Room and bathroom were very clean, very comfortable bed, and friendly service. My rating is based on the value I received which was excellent. I've rated "fancier" hotels lower because they did not live up to their promise or standards. This hotel lives up to it's standard by providing a very nice room at a great price. Breakfast is free and adequate. Coffee is served all day long. Internet is free.

“A good place to sleep, not much more” Hotel had crowded feel. Location was attached to mall and business offices. Found room with used soap in bathroom and toiletries not refreshed. When brought to hotel's attention at checkout, did apologize. Could not get my phone to work to call front desk. Room comfortable and slept well. In conference room, had trouble with internet going in and out.

“Great location and service” Stayed 2 nights. Hotel with superb location, close to everything. It was very nice to jog along the harbor. Didn't have time to use the pool and gym, but they looked nice and clean. Food was tasty and at the reasonable price. My room had awesome view of the San Diego Bay (see photo). Loved watching the sun set from my big balcony. Staff was the best - extremelly friendly, empathetic, and helpful in a genuine way.

“Comfortable, great location, attentive and friendly staff!” I always like staying at the Orchard! It's close to Union Square without being in the middle of the throng of tourists, and within easy walking distance to BART, Muni and pretty much everything else you would need. We had an issue with our reservation that was booked through Booking.com (who wouldn't help us at all), and the reservation manager and the front desk manager did everything they could to make sure things were taken care of. The bar had a super friendly bartender named Jen that chatted with us, recommended nice wines and made the experience that much better. The beds are very comfortable, the rooms are quiet and wifi is free (as it should be!) I highly recommend :)

“Average hotel” Honestly, I'm not sure that I would stay here again. I did win this hotel through a Priceline bid and so there really isn't too much that I can complain about. However, if I had paid full price for this hotel you can bet the tone of this review would be different. For the 4 nights that we were at the hotel we don't remember a single time when the hotel felt quiet or peaceful. We somewhat anticipated the bustle of the hotel simply because it is downtown in Union Square but we did not anticipate on several occasions there being a 5 minute wait just to use the elevators to get up to our room. It was crowded... and then some. We were on the 16th floor and actually had little issue with noise apart from the occasional loud voice in the hall. We had little encounters with anyone who worked at the hotel (apart from check in and check out). The rooms are tiny and the bathroom is microscopic. The bed was so so... but the curtains would black out the room in case you wanted to sleep in (which we did). Tip: When you arrive at the front with your baggage you can walk to the left and curve around to the elevators to avoid having to carry all your baggage up the very large set of stairs when you first walk in. We did not know this and carried our heavy bags up all those stairs... which was not fun. Don't expect much help with your bags unless you ask for it. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel for a normal visit, but would recommend it for a good Priceline bid.

“Best Customer Service Ever” I'm quite suprised reading the previous reviews compared with my experience. I was blown away by the staff of this hotel--their customer service was the best I've encountered. I stayed at this hotel for two weeks, attending a conference. I brought along my infant son and my husband. Upon check-in, the person at the front desk upgraded us from a studio to a 1-bedroom so that we could stay up while our baby slept. Anyone who has ever had a baby who doesn't sleep very well can imagine how great this was, especially when facing a 2-week hotel stay. A couple of days into our stay, we asked for a fan to provide white noise (we were waking the baby, the hotel was quiet) and they gave us the fan from behind the front desk. One day it was raining really hard and the girl at the front desk lent me her personal umbrella for the walk to the convention center. We also needed a ride to the aquarium, which they provided free of charge (though they prioritize those going to John Hopkins, as they should). My son dropped his pacifier in the lobby and the bellhop brought it back up to our room. The people in the deli knew us by name and were just wonderful to us. They arranged corporate passes for us to go to the aquarium, saving us a lot of money (these aren't always available). I was truly impressed by the customer service at the hotel, it went above and beyond expected courtesy. The rooms were good--nice sheets, large size. The tv froze a couple of times, causing us to miss the end of House and all of the Office :(. Other than that, I was really happy and highly recommend the Tremont Plaza.

“Great hotel - ok location” I stayed here with a friend for 2 nights in early December. We came down to Seattle to shop and we usually Hotwire a hotel. That's how we ended up at the Silver Cloud Stadium. The hotel itself was very nice. Clean rooms, friendly staff, good water pressure in the shower. We had a 2 queen room and it had a bar area with a mini fridge and microwave. If we had been staying longer I'm sure we would have found those handy. As it was December we didn't have a chance to try the outdoor, rooftop pool or hot tub. We did have breakfast downstairs the first day. I had an omelet and it was good, my friend had pancakes and felt they were salty. We normally try to stay right downtown in the shopping district so we can drop off packages and rest up before dinner. The Silver Cloud does have a shuttle to drop you off and pick you up. We did use it to drop us off at the Harry Potter exhibit near the Space Needle. We ended up taking a cab back to the hotel after we had dinner downtown ($10 including tip). There were no games going on while we stayed at the hotel, and I don't know if noise would be an issue during a game or concert. but we found the hotel to be very quiet. Overall it's not my first choice of hotel for staying in Seattle. But if I got it for the right price on Hotwire again I wouldn't be too disappointed. Really the location was the only drawback for me.

“Not Recommended” Not the best of hotels in NY, the hotel staff were not the friendliest bunch of people and the girl who checked us in had stains all down her uniform, the corridor had a musty old smell. The room was resonably clean, however there was many hairs on the bathroom floor!! The bar was a pleasant place to sit at night and the gift shop was decent enough, however this year we've decided to choose a different hotel. Sorry!

“Lovely hotel - despite some problems” The Fairfax is a small European style hotel that competes with the Jefferson and the Hay Adams. It is enjoyable to stay at despite some draw backs. As the name implies, it is just off DuPont circle and surrounded by embassies. This makes it a fun neighborhood to walk around in. The hotel's lobby is quite small but there is a nice bar a few steps off the lobby that serves as a meeting place. The front desk staff is insanely good. They went above and beyond on every issue. Not the phony Ritz Carlton concern. I really felt they took ownership of my problems (both of which were of my own making). The same is true of the bellman, and this is the kind of hotel where you feel awkward if you don't use a bellman, plus there are a couple of staIrs to get to the elevator. I would recommend you try to avoid a queen sized bed, even if you are a single. The queen rooms are tiny and the bathroom is silly small. It is so small that there is no place to put a waste basket and, I suspect, anyone over six feet tall would be unable to comfortably sit on the toilet. There are three things that drive me nuts about hotels as a frequent business traveler, and all three are present at the Fairfax. First is the lack of electric sockets. The only socket is in the lamp on the tiny little desk. So if you use that for your laptop, you have no place else to plug in your phone (and in my case, a CPAP). To access another socket requires moving the bed and unplugging a lamp. Would it kill hotels to supply a power strip? The second is the tiny little print on identical looking bottles of shampoo, conditioner, lotion and body wash. Most people dont wear glasses into the shower. The third is paying for wifi (although the Fairfax's charge is cheap at $9.95 and the wifi is pretty fast). I had occasion to eat breakfast in the 2100 Prime restaurant (used to be The Jockey Club), lunch in the bar and dinner at 2100. All were excellent and not too expensive by Washington standards. But, all in, the quality of the people who work at the Fairfax exceeds any of the other problem, and I look forward to staying again

“I would go back to LA just to stay at the Magic Castle!” There is nothing I can add that has not been said in earlier reviews - we loved the Magic Castle - the staff are wonderful and could not be more helpful, the children loved the free mini-bar, we felt very safe there, the pool was excellent, rooms incredibly spacious for the area and price - it's a wonderful, wonderful place - a real gem!

“Hotel Monaco Has Flair” I am a frequent travler to Chicago. I was part of a larger group conference and probably had the smallest room the hotel offered. With that said, it was very comfortable. The furnishings were very nice but the bathroom was small and spartan with lmiited toiletries. I have stayed at Hotel Monacos in DC, Denver and Portland, and Chicago suffers by comparison. The building is quite old and there was only so much improvements that could be made. With that said, it is still a nice hotel and worth considering for the location and price.

“Best Value, Minus Location” I recently stayed here to try out the Doubletree brand in Austin, and I was very pleased. The top three things that stuck out to me in a good way were, 1) modern accommodations and decorations, 2) value in dining-in, and 3) sleeping/working quality of the rooms. For the first, the decor is nicely done. The rooms remind me of the Westin at the Arboretum. The walk-in shower and marble finish counter made me feel like I was staying at a nice place. Second, the room service was a great value. Is that an ocymoron? No, I order an appetizer and main course for under $20 before room service fees. I barely get a drink and appetizer at the Sheraton or HGI for that price. Lastly, since the hotel is not off 6th Street and the desk/work areas were actually near available outlets, my quality of 'living' in the room was very positive. I was able to get a good night sleep, and during the morning, I was able to get out emails, while ironing my cloths. With that said, your only dining options are hotel, the next door Denny's, or Domino's delivery. If you want to enjoy 6th Street, you better hop in a cab. You basically trade off nightlife/dining for sleep/work quality (surprisingly, my room didn't have a single HD channel working). Since the hotel is on or near campus, there's tendency for the staff and clientele to not be very up on the manners. What I mean is that, you may see more business and family folks at Hampton Inn or Sheraton and that aura may be very high in politeness or friendliness, but when college recruiting or events happen, the environment changes. This may be one thing for high school seniors checking out the campus, but different for traveling sales people. In all, I recommend this Doubletree to anyone that wants a quality stay that off the highway. There's no nightlife, but a relaxing bed,a warm shower, and a warm cookie awaits you.

“Not great, not bad” I stayed for 4 nights at the downtown San Diego Bristol during the last week of October 2008. Some bad points about the hotel are its location, which can be a little sketchy after dark. There are many homeless bums on the surrounding streets (even the daytime). Although most of them are harmless, you still need to be alert. Another bad point is that the rooms are slightly older, as is the entire hotel. One other bad point is that I could hear the traffic (train and airplane) noise constantly, but that's probably true for all downtown hotels in San Diego, since the airport is so close by. I did use earplugs to sleep every night, as my neighbors were sometimes noisy. The TV was ok, but there were no movie channels (HBO, etc.). Good points are that the hotel staff are great. The front desk staff are very helpful and nice. The cleaning staff are also very polite. They never came before 10AM to start cleaning my room, so the mornings were quiet. There were free apples at the front desk, which were nice. The rooms were very clean and I was satisfied with that aspect of it. The lobby of the hotel is also very cute and comfortable. So, there were good and bad aspects of this hotel, but I think that there is more good than bad.

“Probably the best hotel in Indianapolis” Great staff, smaller but clean rooms. I have stayed here a few times and have never had an issue. One of my children had a cold and when I looked for the hotel store, the staff asked what I needed, ran to the store and came back with it. Simply wonderful. The Capital Grill for breakfast in the lobby was great as well.

“Für Anspruchslose genau das richtige...” Ich habe mit einem Freund in diesem Hotel übernachtet und unsere Anforderungen an die zwei Nächte lauteten: zentrale Lage und annehmbare Sauberkeit. Und genau das und nichts anderes hat dieses Hotel erfüllt, Das von uns gebuchte Zimmer hatte kein eigenes Bad und so musste man hierfür das Gemeinschaftsbad (das sich nicht einmal auf dem gleichen Stockwerk befand) benutzen. Dieses war nicht dreckig aber durch den regen Duschverkehr war der Boden ganz nass und daher sind Badeschuhe sicherlich zu empfehlen. Das Zimmer war sehr einfach aber sauber und völlig in Ordnung. Die Lautstärke war etwas störend, da das Fenster zur Straße hin die ganze Nacht die NY-typische Kulisse aus Sirenen und hupenden Autos zu uns durchdringen lies. Sicherlich ist das Hotel aber für einen kurzen Aufenthalt OK. Da ich nun aber auch schon in deutlich besseren Hotels übernachtet habe, weiß ich, was dies wert ist und würde nicht nochmal hier übernachten. Für die meiner Meinung nach potentiellen Bewohner dieses Hotels würde vielleicht auch ein Hostel in Frage kommen (o.A Pod-Hotel etc.)

“An average experience” I am a fan of the Hyatt Regency brand but this property is not among my favorites. Pros include price, great staff, and a very comfortable bed. Cons include location (the area is pretty desolate at night and it was difficult to find both taxis and good, nearby restaurants on the weekend - it is in the financial district so everything shuts down on weekends), rooms that showed wear and tear (particularly in the bathroom), and noise. Truly, this hotel was one of the noisiest I have ever been in - slamming doors and the conversation of people in the hallways was easily heard in both rooms we were in - we ultimately had to change rooms from the 17th floor to the 20th floor due to noise but the change in volume was somewhat minimal. Be sure to ask for a higher floor if noise is an issue for you - frankly, I am not overly sensitive to hotel noise so the need to change rooms was an unfortunate development. In the event I am again in Boston, I would stay again at the Marriot Copely Place (see prior review for this property). It was much more conveniently located with great shopping nearby and despite the number of guests it attracts, was far quieter.

“No Room for Improvement” The location, service, room were all 100% incredible. There simply was no flaw to be found at this hotel. The views of Lake Michigan were breathtaking, and the rooms are adequate size.

“Not a single bad thing to say” I travel for a living and in the end I am gone far more than I am home. However, your hotel can make the week seem shorter and make home feel a little less far away. The Marriott City Center was an excellent hotel with excellent staff. I cannot think of a single bad thing to say about my stay there. The staff was extremely polite and offered great dining recommendations for the area. It is greatly appreciated when a hotel can make the week seem a little less like work, and a little more like vacation. If you are traveling to Dallas for business near the Art District or Uptown Dallas, I highly recommend this hotel. If you are traveling for pleasure and sightseeing, this hotel is a little north of West End and Old downtown. It is a bit of a walk to get to the sights of downtown and uptown, but if this hotel is one of your options I would definitely consider it regardless of location.

“Great Location next to Grand Central - Fancy Boutique Style Accomodations” We just got back from our stay at the 70 Park Avenue Hotel. The style, location, and service were great. The hotel is boutique style and quaint, offering comfortable settings and cozy couches to relax in the intimate lobby. There was also a nightly hosted wine hour from 5-6pm, this was nice to come 'home' to each night. The location is on Park Avenue - 3 blocks from Grand Central Station. We had easy access to all sub lines from this location and could be anywhere in the city quicker than a cab ride. I would suggest buying a 1-day unlimited metro card rather than $10 bucks metro card for 2 people at $2 per ride. Great restaurants, delis, and groceries were 1-2 blocks in all directions. Everything you need was right there. The hotel room we had was a king, with modern decor and lots of lighting. The bed was nice and comfy, with extra pillows. Large flat screen TV, working desk w/ WIFI access, and iHome alarm clock w/ docking station for iPhone/iPod. Hotel rooms are never enormous in NYC, but arrangment of the bed, desk, and chair worked with the size constraints. The bath products were L'Occitane and the hotel offered a laundry list of bath items for free in case you forgot your toothbrush, toothpaste, hairdryer, flatiron, to name a few. However, ice is a room service request, but they were always speedy to send it up. We did eat one night, appetizers, at the Silverleaf Lounge in the hotel. We liked the atmosphere of the window seats to watch the people outside and enjoy a martini and frites. We would definitely recommend the hospitality of the 70 Park Ave to anyone visiting NYC, who is wanting a Midtown location with a classy style.

“How Absolutely Insulting” I had business in New York City on the Friday leading into the Memorial day weekend. I thought it would be an excellent opportunity for a quick family excursion. I spent a couple of days researching the Manhattan area for the best 'luxury value' and ran across the Peninsula. Relative to other similar status properties in the area, the Peninsula seemed to offer us the best price for accommodations for three (husband, wife, young adult daughter). I learned the hard way to follow the wisdom of the trip advisor crowd. Here's my story. Typically, I would have booked this hotel through my Amex Platinum Card Fine Resorts and Hotel program, but I found a much better value by calling the Peninsula's reservation desk. The reservationist arranged our accommodations, king with roll-away-bed at 'x' cost per night for a 2 night stay. Ultimately, they tried to run a scam on us and up sell us unknowingly. Because I planned to meet my family later in the evening after my business meeting, I arranged with the receptionist for my husband and daughter to check in prior to my arrival. I was assured that everything would be handled seamlessly. On check-in day, my husband and daughter checked in as planned and I arrived later to join them. I thought the room was lovely, facing 5th avenue, with windows that actually opened. While the decor was a little dated, we were comfortable, in a great location, and the room was fresh. Mind you, this is not the Peninsula Beverly Hill's which is one of the most perfect hotel experiences that we have ever had. As some of the reviews have suggested and I should have paid attention to, this is like the budget version of a true Peninsula. I digress, let me cut to the chase. On check out, there were problems with our billing that I took issue with. The bill was corrected, but a month later, Peninsula NY recharged the expenses to my credit card. I called them to challenge the charges and honestly, they put what sounded like a trainee on the phone who spoke to me in the most condescending manner. When I told him that I would hand the matter over to Amex and tried to end the contact (because honestly I was concerned that I was dealing with someone unstable), he tried to call me again a couple of times. I immediately phoned Amex and the situation was handled. I have never had such an insulting experience in all of my days and this was the Peninsula, or so I thought! I should have paid closer attention to all those trip advisor reports that were implicit of something shady going on at that place cause folks, it's true! I was holding on to a fond memory of the Peninsula Beverly Hills and the two are not the same! Bright spots: food was delicious, room adequate value (until they tried to rip me off). Mediocre: rooftop bar drink was pretty bad. I actually saw a couple of drinks returned.

“Very Good” Stayed here last night while passing through the area. Holiday Inns have come a long way recently. If not for the plastic cups you'd think you were in a Doubletree. Clean, fresh rooms at a resonable rate. Right off I-95 at the foot of the Dela Memorial Bridge.

“Location can't be beat” I have stayed at this location a number of times - I love the location (close to 5th Ave shopping, the 6 line etc). Also there is a Bliss spa in the building which makes going for a massage or facial a real pleasure - just get in the elevator and you're there. I do have a few complaints from this last stay - Mario who checked me in neglected to ask what benefit I wanted based on my Gold membership - he assumed I wanted points (no!) and I wanted the free internet. And seriously - 19.95 per day for WiFi? This was changed on check out. And oh yes, on my second last day I find an invoice under the door - I had to go down and persuade them that I was not checking out that day but rather the day after. This is a busy hotel - but the front desk staff could be more gracious and less peeved with any request (see above). And then there are the elevators - you have to insert your key card to gain access to the floors with rooms and this is a challenge as the key reader doesn't want to "take' your card and you have to stand there and jam it in and out and sometimes the elevator takes off to a floor that you don't want to go to. And the gym is small with some machines less than well maintained; they seem to be doing some work on that floor so maybe an upgrade is coming.... Will I stay there again? Yes - because of the location but I hope that management see this review and think about what a loyal Starwood (and W) guest has to say.

“small, clean, comfy beds” We needed a place to stay in the Soho/ Tribeca area for under $300 and this hotel did the trick. Rooms seem to have been recently updated, ours was a 2 double beds for 3 adults. Room is small, (door opens to bed) but there is desk for storage as well a pullout under the bed. (large suitcases would be tough for room). Also, there is not a "closet" but a mirror unit that has about 10 hangers w/in unit to hang clothes. THe beds are very comfy w/ big pillows. Room clean as well as bathroom which had shampoo, creame, mouthwash. Hotel staff friendly. Ray's pizza down the street for yummy slice. Area is convenient to area's stores for shopping & dining. The word "clarion" is not on the building, it states "the gem hotel" on the outside. Also, there are steps to go up to the small reception area, but there is a 1 person ADA elavator if needed. This is perfect for a short stay and you want a clean, inexpensive (nyc prices), well located hotel. I would stay again.

“Surpassed my recommendation” I had stayed in 2 Drury Inns in different cities over the past year, and booked my extended family into the Indianapolis hotel based on my good impressions. It was a very important trip, as my mother is newly handicapped and assuming she can't do anything anymore - including travel. We needed to have things go as smoothly as possible for her to get her confidence back. Thus the extra care in choosing SWA, probably the last airline to consider passenger care a priority, and the Drury Inn, both for location and my experience with them. I just can't thank the Indy Drury Inn enough for their graciousness. Everything I knew of them as a chain, plus the extra of great staff training. Family members were all arriving at different times, but the desk was aware of the group. Everyone working there treated my mother like royalty without fawning over her handicap. In fact, the family voted to cancel the next night's lodging in a different city and drive back to this Drury instead. Like a restaurant with a gorgeous view, hotels that offer a good bang for the buck don't really have to be more than that to get business. This Drury Inn offered the freebies AND the quality: bedrooms were clean, beds were luxurious, lobby was inviting and the staff was exceptional!

“Nice Hotel” I just returned from a one night stay at the Courtyard in downtown Philadelphia. I booked a culture package which included a standard room and two VIP tickets to the Renoir exhibit at the Philadelphia Art Museum. These tickets allowed me to enter at any time instead of a set time if I'd booked through the museum. According to the museum website other hotels had similar packages but the Courtyard had the lowest price of the better reviewed hotels on Trip Advisor. My room was ready when I arrived at 11:30 a.m. and the museum tickets were handed to me when I registered without having to ask for them. I had requested a high floor with a city view and my room was on the 14th (of 15) floors with a view of the city, the river and one of the bridges. The room was large and very quiet. Not as well furnished as a regular Marriott but certainly comfortable. The public rooms were very well maintained and the historic nature of the building added to the elegant feeling of the hotel - not your usual Courtyard. The rains came as I was leaving the art museum several hours later and between the 33 degree temperature and the pouring rain I decided to eat dinner in the hotel's Annex Restaurant. Even with a Christmas tree and a fire in the fireplace it was pretty basic ambiance (and a crying baby who the parents did not take for a much needed walk for far too long didn't help) but the food surprised me by being quite good. The same restaurant is used for breakfast which I didn't have but I did go in to get complimentary coffee. They were also serving hot chocolate in the lobby with a large selection of toppings which was nice. The valet parking was prompt and pleasant. All the staff were pleasant and helpful. I would stay here again.

“Charming, romantic, quaint” No complaints. Very, very pleasant accomodating staff. Room was lovely and quite large with a king bed and ultra comfortable mattress. Neither my husband or I felt unsafe in the area even after dark, but I can see if you're somewhat skittish you might be nervous since it isn't a high traffic area like it is right on Union Square. Great shower and vanity and loved the complimentary sodas in the fridge everyday. Will stay there again on our next visit.....

“5 Minuten Fußweg zum Riverwalk” Das Hotel liegt günstig zum Riverwalk (incl. FoodCourt & Restaurants) und Alamodome. Auch "The Alamo" und "The Tower of the America" ($8.50) ist per Fuß erreichbar. Parken ist kostenlos, aber Parkplätze sind abends knapp. WIFI hat gepaßt, "Business-Center" liegt separiert mit 1 PC, der hatte sehr schnelle Verbindung. Zimmer sind groß, sauber aber etwas dunkel (im Erdgeschoß). Frühstück ist Standard besteht aus Toast, diversen Müsli und Waffeln. Es war immer ein Mitarbeiter anwesend, der auffüllte und Tische abwischte. Laundry kostet $2,50 und ist sauber. Rezeption ist 24 h besetzt und Mitarbeiter sind freundlich und engagiert. Als Rewards Diamond Mitglied lag 1 Fl. Wasser und salziger Snack gratis im Zimmer. Hier gab es auch Kühlschrank, Mikrowelle aber kein Safe. Empfehlen kann ich noch die Bootstour (Riverwalk, $ 8.50)

“Nice location, nice hotel...” Dream is a nice hotel in the midtown area of NYC. It has a cool ambiance, and a very cool bar called AVA. The rooms are small, but for a few dollars more you can get a "Medium" or "Large" room, and I would recommend that route. It is a cool option for not a ton of money.

“Old World” Lovely hotel reminiscent of another era. Service was good for the most part - we were leaving on a cruise the following day and we asked to borrow a stapler so we could attach our luggage tags to our luggage and were required to exchange our drivers license in exchange for the stapler. Not good PR for a top hotel! We were told they had lost too many staplers! Our suite was very nice with a partial waterfront view, comfortable king bed and nice sitting area with french doors separating the bedroom and sitting area. Nice bathrooms with quality anemities Food was very good.
“Ok, but need renovation” An older Red Roof that need freshening. A lot of semi drivers stay here on corp rates. But very quiet and solid with a great view of the lights of Juarez at night.

“Fantastic location!” After reading the great reviews on here, I booked a room here for 3 nights at the beginning of November (marathon time.) I could not have been happier with this hotel. At check in, I found the staff to be professional and they happily accomodated all of my room requests. The hotel was quiet with spacious rooms and big beds with several types of pillows to choose from. They have a great breakfast with 'hot' and 'cold' selections. If you miss breakfast as we did one time, they have breakfast 'to go' snack bags at the front desk. There is also a great little 24 hour diner right across the street. Hot coffee, tea and hot chocolate are available in the lobby all day as well as fresh fruit, and cookies in the afternoon. The staff was pleasant, friendly and always willing to assist. (The day we left, one of the staff even hooked us up with a limo out front for our ride back to the airport for basically the same price as a cab.) Finally, the location cannot be beat - right smack in the Theater District but about a half block away from Broadway so you're sleeping away from the hubbub and noise. Easy walk to Central Park, Rockefeller Center/Top of the Rock, MoMA, Broadway/Times Square. Perfect.

“Comfortable, very clean, great staff” Spent two nights here. Staff was wonderful, very helpful, very accomodating. The room was absolutely, perfectly clean, especially the bathroom. Comfortable beds. Breakfast in the morning was very good, plenty of selection and plenty of seating. Valet parking was efficient. Walking distance to everything downtown. Great stay, no complaints at all.

“GRACIOUS HOSPITALITY AND UNDERSTATED LUXURY” The friendliness begins at the front door and continues into the welcoming lobby reached by elevator and into every area and each staff member in this outstanding deluxe property. Perfect Mag Mile location mere steps from great shopping and restaurants. Many Asian refinements attest to the lineage of the small but luxurious chain. Considerate service and fairly priced meal in main dining room with high ceiling and big windows. Gazeworthy artwork throughout. Guest rooms about 725 sq. ft, among the largest anywhere, with city views regardless of location. The curtains and liner operated by remote control. Very comfortable beds with turndown service but surprisingly no nightly bed favor. Approx 48 inch flat screen TV has, also surprisingly, no HD. Full size desk and chair. Muted gold accents very effective. Separate full dressing room with setee and ample drawer space. Big bright marble bath has a tub to remember with its own TV, telephone, and separate controls. Separate glass enclosed toilet with telephone, and separate enclosed shower. For all the elegance, however, the bath ventilation exhaust, which is hotel controlled for all rooms, is inadequate for the space and quickly produces steam on glass and mirrors. Also not expected in a property of such quality are the toiletries, which are adequate but should be superior. The top or 20th floor has a well equipped exercise room, separate spa services, and a large and welcoming indoor pool with outdoor sun area. Don't expect dramatic skyline or Lake Michigan views and consider that paying extra for superior or deluxe rooms only affect floor and view, not room size. These comments aside, staying at the Peninsula is an experience to be remembered.

“Feels like home” I stay at this Westin a lot and the staff really do treat you like family. I enjoy staying here and I always feel rested and relaxed. The Heavenly bed and showers are the best. The food at the bar is great and the bartenders take good care of you. Lynne the Concierge is very helpful and makes sure you are in good hands. It may not be the most modern hotel in DC but everything else makes up for it.

“excellent location” Everything about this hotel was perfect really. Firstly the price was very competitive. The location perfect. The end of the road one way was all the buzz otf Times Square and in the other the exclusive shopping on Fifth Avenue. The room clean and good with lots of storage, the bathroom clean and new with a shower over the bath. I was very comfortable here. The staff were pleasant and helpful

“Very Good Hotel - Perfect Location” Stayed at this hotel for one night to see a concert at Staples Center. Efficient check-in with nice lobby. Valet parking is the only option at $40.00/day. Location is perfect for access to Staples Center, Nokia Theatre, and LA Live. Breakfast buffet was good, although $24.00/person. Room was nice, bathroom was very nice. Pool on the 4th floor is really pretty with a cool bar. Lobby has coffee shop, nice bars, and LA Market restaurant. Room service of a personal pizza & chocolate cake was good. I enjoyed the stay at this hotel. I would give it 4 dots, but it sneaks into the Excellent range because of the perfect location.

“Beautiful Public Spaces” Loved this hotel. Very beautiful and comfortable lobby. Cool and soothing. Mainly a business hotel with a downtown location and thoroughly enjoyed my stay given that my activities were focused in the downtown area. Rooms were larger than typical rooms you find at the large chains. Very well-appointed and clean. Nice pool and patio area. Didn't have extensive interaction with the staff, but overall very polite and accommodating staff. Valet parking with in and out privileges. Easy access the Santa Monica and Harbor freeway, and Interstate 5. Finally, the bar in the lobby was fantastic...relaxing place to have a drink and watch a game or chat. Would stay there again in a minute, for business or pleasure. Highly recommended.

“Great Experience” We stayed here for 3 nights and were pleased with everything. There was a good breakfast (only drawback was that it never changed). The location was good - short walk to buses and trains. We got a good rate from travelzoo - would definitely stay here again!

“Wonderful Weekend Getaway” My wife, adult daughter, and I just returned home from a weekend at the Omni Severin in Indianapolis. Great hotel, great staff, and plenty to do in downtown Indianapolis. We weren't there for the Colts football game, but you couldn't help feel the excitement of the fans and the hotel staff.

“We cannot stay anywhere else...” This is our third stay on this property but our first since the change from the elysian. Gorgeous, so relaxing,outstanding service and a tremendous value for all the amenities you receive. Splurge and you won't regret that you did....

“This Sofitel doesn't live up to the brand” I'm a big fan of Sofitel hotels (particularly in Europe) and liked this one's central location (used to live nearby so know the neighborhood). It was an okay stay. Service was competent (a previous reviewer noted that there were a surprising lot of bell staff and I have to agree) and the food in the restaurant was just outstanding, everything, from breakfast (where you served a delicious, complimentary mini-smoothie) to lunch (fantastic pizza) to cocktails on the ingenuously designed outdoor patio that almost makes you forget you're at the crossroads of two massive L.A. boulevards. The nightclub/bar, which is adjacent, frankly looked like something from the early 1980s, and was rather creepy, anything but enticing. Our room was just so-so. First room I was given was tiny, with a shower-only bathroom (I'm a regular Sofitel customer and I don't understand why I was given a crappy room to begin with when clearly there were other, better rooms in my price category). To its credit Sofitel moved quickly when I asked for a bathroom with tub, and the second room, along the same corridor, was much larger. Pleasant but unexceptional with one particularly oddity: There was no headboard and a framed print was placed where your head would rest if you were reading in bed. Literally the framed hit the middle of the back of my head. Bizarre and uncomfortable. The bathroom was adequate but nothing special, even with the aforementioned bath, which was one of those 1970s models that's shallow. The view was terrible -- we looked out on the Beverly Center parking lot. Depressing. I don't think I'll go back to this hotel again -- there are too many better options for the same money in L.A. It reminds of the Miami airport Sofitel, which also could use a cash infusion. But the big difference is that at the airport the pickings are slim. Here, not so much.

“Good layover spot” Laid over here for 12 hours on the return portion of a business trip. The van to and from the airport runs every half hour and is efficient if a little crowded at the hours I used. The rooms are clean and very well furnished, if a bit dimly lit. Some aircraft noise is unavoidable in this location, but it was well muffled. The free internet service worked well. The selection of restaurants within walking distance is quite limited (I try to avoid hotel restaurants when possible): Taco Bell, pizza, Subway, chinese. Overall, a quiet, clean, well-furnished place for a layover, and a pretty good value. I would use it again if necessary.

“The Langham Boston Continues To Impress” I recently stayed at the Langham Boston while attending a conference held at the hotel. This was probably my sixth stay at the Langham over the past six years and the hotel fits me like a glove. Check in and check out were efficient and pleasant. Front desk, concierge and housekeeping staff were pleasant and accommodating as always. My room and bathroom were impeccably clean throughout my stay. Although the hotel was at capacity, I heard no noise from adjacent rooms and virtually no noise from the hallway outside my door. My room was on the seventh floor and I heard no street noise. I slept soundly on the comfortable bed and there were plenty of great pillows. I always request a room on a high floor and away from the elevator and the Langham is always happy to oblige. I am a member of Langham's 1865 loyalty program. As a result, fresh fruit and a newspaper were delivered to my room daily and I was afforded a late 2:00 p.m. checkout on my final day allowing me to change into comfortable clothing for my travel home. Much appreciated. I did not have occasion to use the pool or fitness center during my stay. I did not use room service during my visit however, all meals served as part of my conference were nothing short of excellent, far exceeding any expectations I would have for large group meals. A festive adult beverage with colleagues in the trendy bar was most enjoyable as well. Private meeting rooms were excellent and spacious and were serviced regularly by hotel staff throughout each meeting day. This was a fine choice indeed for a conference venue. When my travels take me to Boston, the Langham is my first choice in hotels. I look forward to my next visit.

“Great balcony room” This is the second time I've stayed here it keeps getting better. My room was great because of the balcony with a clear view of coit tower and the bay. Front desk was very pleasant and efficient . My Hilton Honors loyalty was recognized and appreciated. My only annoying experience was that security mistakenly accused me of putting my feet on the furniture in the lobby. I don't do that in my own home and certainly don't do it in a hotel lobby. But, since it was an effort to keep the place nice, I let it slide.

“Solo una noche ... lástima!” Siempre me gusta el Residence y su calidad incomparable y aquí no fue la excepción. Un trato muy amable, habitaciones con todo, limpias y en excelente estado. Lo único que no me gustó fue estar en el tercer piso, por que iba con mucho equipaje y fue algo incómodo. Pero eso no fue obstáculo para disfrutar de mi corta estancia en el hotel. La ubicación está buena para trasladarse en servicio público a las atracciones del centro de San Antonio por que no está exactamente en el centro.

“On the low end of decent for Courtyards. Obnoxious club adjacent to lobby.” The building is attractive from the outside, and in pretty decent shape on the inside. The room was pretty standard CY fare, although a bit dated, particularly when compared to the renovated CYs that are popping up around the country. My main complaint was the obnoxious dance club which is adjacent to the lobby which is overflowing with early twenty-somethings and has overwhelming bass reverberating everywhere. Oh, and don't fall for the $35 valet parking, there's much cheaper garage or street parking nearby.

“Good hotel good price no complaints” Stayed for 3 nights whilst attending a conference in the nearby 'full service' Marriott. Selected the hotel because the rate was the best out of the 'full service' Marriott and the Marriott Courtyard. All these 3 hotels are in basically adjacent to each other. Its a standard Residence Inn so rooms have kitchenettes, etc. My room was large (especially for a town center), clean and comfortable. Broadband worked perfectly and was free. The basement has a good gym/pool area. The gym is sufficiently large and spacious and has a glass wall to the pool. It has two cross/elliptical trainers, two bikes and two joggers and some basic free weights. All in good working order. In fact the whole gym pool area seemed light and spacious. The work on the lobby area (which they pre-advertised) seemed to be more-or-less over and, yes, it is a pain to have to insert your room key to use the elevator but this is a downtown location so that is entirely sensible and expected. I'd have no problem staying there again and would even potentially chose it over the Courtyard.

“Stylish, fairly comfortable, fun.” This is a stylish, comfortable, well-located hotel. It has a funky, hip, yet accessible feel. Terrific location, steps away from great shopping, a few streets over from great restaurants, easy to take a walk downtown, and my room had a view of the river. It was easy to get to the museums, to the Shedd, and to the couple of business meetings I had on Michigan Ave. I got in late at night via taxi (so I can't comment on parking), and I was initially worried because there's a lively, crowded (good people-watching!) club downstairs. No worries, I didn't hear a thing when I wanted to get to sleep. The hotel really is geared, some might say, "young," but I just think it's hip and in step with the times and a nice break from big chains. You can tell they're trying to accommodate how people live and what they want when they travel. For example, there's a cool media room you can book for free where you can play xbox and wii and hang out. So I'll say it's definitely a new 'hotel experience' for me, but a good one! The room was comfortable and reasonably sized and tidy. I was in a non-smoking room but strangely there was what looked like a cigarette burn in one of the end tables. The hallways maybe are a little more dark and slightly dank than I'd like andI think the ventilation in the room wasn't as good as I would have liked, either, but overall ok there. It does seem like I have to note how hip and chic the style of the hotel and room is, and I really liked it, but really it has to be comfortable and serviceable or else it just fails as a hotel, and Hotel Sax was comfortable and had good check-in service (even if they had to shout over the music downstairs late at night... it was totally quiet during the day). The concierge helped me get connected with an architecture tour and recommended a couple of good places to eat and shop. Before arriving, I requested a non-feather hypo-allergenic room, and they made it up accordingly, which was great. There are plenty of soft towels and a bathrobe to use, and the toiletries are good quality. The building seems to be a remodeled older building, and they did a nice job of updating the bathroom but retaining some elements that let you know the building was built awhile ago. I never had breakfast at the hotel, so I can't comment on it, but I did have lunch at the downstairs restaurant, Bin 36, and it was very good, had a salad and a gourmet sandwich. Pricey, but you really are getting something special.

“Deluxe King room w/Club access” We are a family of four and had 2 "deluxe" king rooms on the 18th floor. The rooms are small but well done. I doubt the rooms can handle more than 2 people each. We took the club level option and that made this hotel stay amazing --- the 21st floor terrace has great skyline views of the Empire State Building. Breakfast is included in club access and my 4 thought it was perfect --- scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, hash browns, fruit salads, local bagels, pastries, whole wheat croissants, etc. The evening hors d'oeuvres are very simple but soda, water, tea & coffee are free and the views on the outdoor terrace cannot be beat! if you don't have club access, Tribeca Bagels is right out the front door and open 24/7 - you can get drinks, fruits, smoothies, bagels, sandwiches, etc. Location was great for us. We didn't want midtown this time. Access to the A C E subway lines is just around the corner, but it was well located to walk to SOHO, Lower East Side (Tenement Museum), Little Italy & Chinatown. We shopped at Pylones, Kate's Paperie, Sur la Table, Paul Frank, Vans --- all on foot! Only real complaint --- even on the 18th story (1810 & 1812 are facing 6th -- Ave of the Americas) the traffic beeps and sirens in the evening are fairly constant until quite late. It did not affect our ability to fall asleep or stay asleep but might have if we were on a lower floor. Parking is $55 per 24 hours - no in and out. Call ahead 30 - 45 minutes for your car to be brought around. You must use the key in the elevator to go UP. I saw many people confused with how to do this. Look at arrow on your key, insert it and take it out. You will hear a little beep. Press your floor # and you're good to go! (You do not need to use the key to go down to the lobby.) Priceline "named hotel" option was $229 Saturday then $159 Sunday + 14.75% taxes + $3.5 room fees but included breakfast and club level terrace access. Great deal!

“OK but housekeeping is hit and miss” The hotel is in a good location, close to very good bars and restaurants in Chelsea. Several subway stops within a couple of blocks. As it's new , everything is new and clean. Good HDTV, free wifi and printers available in the business centre. We didn't have to wait too much for the lifts, however they did break down one day (when we were inside!). We also found the room quiet with no street noise (we were on 23rd floor), and had a great view of the Empire State Building. Rooms are small, but I gather they're about normal for New York! My main issue with this hotel is the housekeeping. One day the towels were not replaced, and it took several calls to get them. Another day coffee cups weren't replaced. Another day bins were emptied but no replacement bin liners put in. Maybe if the staff spent less time joking about in the lifts together then these things would not be forgotten?? Reception staff were very friendly and helpful though. Overall we were happy, but the room was free (reward points), at $400 a night I may not have been so impressed?

“My favorite hotel in Philly” I love this grand old hotel. The staff is very friendly, the lobby area beautiful, and the rooms extremely large and comfortable. The decadence of the large marble bathrooms, with separate tub and shower and television, along with separate vanity area is fun! Huge closets, robes, turn down service with bottled water, radio on, lights dimmed, bed turned down and slippers by the bed all a very nice touch. Check in was fine. She asked if we were return guests (wouldn't that be in their system?) and then gave us a complementary upgrade to a something room. Not sure about the upgrade as it looked like all the rooms we have stayed in here. Disappointed it was not overlooking the park, I should have asked for that. Tip: ask for even numbered rooms for a view. We received a nice fruit basket and note for being return customers. This was very nice. Love having cocktails at the bar in Lacroix. Bartenders are always so friendly, and love the happy hour complementary snacks... yum. Did not, however, like hearing the bartender chastised by wait staff (or management?) for not cooling down a vodka correctly. If necessary, this should have been done behind the scenes, not in front of guests. I thought she was fantastic and a prime example of friendly and accommodating staff that make me want to return to this hotel again and again. For example, she made us a special favorite cocktail that was no longer on the menu. In fact she keeps some frozen grapes for it because she knows people still want this drink.. The only suggestion I would have for improvement: get different bed pillows! They are so thick, hard and unyielding they are very uncomfortable! Wish we were staying here for son's college graduation next spring, but due to the "holiday rate" and non refundable policy for that weekend, we have to go to our number 2 favorite Philly hotel, the Four Seasons.
“Loved everything about this place.” Great location, lovely room, fantastic staff, especially the lovely lady concierge. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend or return. Great rates over Xmas & New Year.

“Wonderful views, but not perfect service” We stayed here one night with an upgrade to a corner room like on the tripadvisor room pics. In the evening, the views were fantastic but the windows very dirty. It's a plus that you can open them, but the building is a bit old - very loud noise from the street despite being on one of the highest floors. Also, a doorman lost our bag from the way to the room from our car using valet parking.

“Would definitely stay here again” I spent one night at the Hilton Garden Inn by the Intercontinental Airport. I had originally tried to get the StayBridge Suites but they were sold out. The hotel has an airport shuttle and they were quick picking us up. The check in was very ease, lobby was nice with an area to hang out and watch TV if needed. The business center was very easy to access on the first floor to print boarding passes. Our room had 2 queens, refrigerator, microwave, and coffee set up. The room was very clean and comfortable. The AC/Heater was not noisy an I never heard any noises of slamming doors or loud guests the entire time. They have a shuttle that will take you to nearby places for free and they are very friendly. I bought the online breakfast package for 2 for an extra 8 dollars which means in the morning you have access to the buffet and made to order pancakes, eggs, french toast, which was very good. The shuttle back to the airport was quick and very easy. I have nothing negative to report on our stay,we would stay here again.

“Gutes Hotel, aber nur der Preis ist Luxusklasse” Wir waren eine Woche im Mandarin. Die Lage ist gut und die die Zimmer genügend gross und gut eingerichtet. Eher durchschnittlich war der Service. Die Wartezeiten im Restaurant war zu lange und brachten uns regelmässig zur Verzweiflung. Dass das Zimmer zum Teil um 2 Uhr Nachmittag immer noch nicht gemacht war, ist wirklich mühsam. Von Weihnachtsstimmung war wenig zu spüren; es gibt in diesem Hotel wenig geschenkt; bei einem so hohen Zimmerpreis erwarten wir beispielsweise beim Aufdecken eine kleine Aufmerksamkeit vorzufinden. Die Heizung war leider auch nicht 5* wert. Das Badezimmer war schlich und einfach kalt, da keine Bodenheizung vorhanden war; eher unverständlich bei einem Marmorboden. Unterdurchschnittlich war auch die Lärmdämpfung der Fenster. Der Ausblick ist natürlich sehr toll, aber ss ist sehr laut am Columbus-Circle und wir konnten die Sirenen und die regelmässigen Hupkonzerte so gut hören, dass wir mit dem Einschlafen grosse Mühe hatten. Mehrfachverglasung ist hier scheinbar kein Thema. Einziger wirklicher Lichtblick war der Concierge-Service. Die Damen und Herren waren sehr effizient und haben uns immer sehr gut und kompetent beraten.

“Super location!” I stayed at the Bulfinch Hotel for 4 nights. There were 3 adults, so we booked a room with 2 double beds. Our room was on the 7th floor. The beds were extremely comfortable! The room was clean and well taken care of. There is very limited closet space. Unfortunately, we were there during the very rainy weekend, so only got one chance to walk from the hotel to Fanueil Hall. It was a very quick walk! The rain put a damper to our weekend in Boston, but the comfy beds made it very relaxing. One negative thing that happened was that the only elevator in the hotel was not working for one whole day. This made it difficult having to climb up and down 7 flights of stairs, especially one member of our group having a heart condition. The elevator was back in service the next day. We ate at the hotel restaurant twice while there (b/c the rain prevented a lot of exploring) but the food was very good, although a little pricey. The staff were nice and friendly. Peet's Coffee and Tea were served in the lobby. We were able to book the government rate, which was a good price. I would come back to the Bulfinch again.

“Great Customer Service” I've stayed here several times, but not in about a year. The staff is what makes this downtown hotel great. Devon at the restaurant and bar is a gem. The rooms are always clean and wonderfully decorated for relaxation. Ask for an upgrade to a suite, they are huge.

“Good hotel, but staff unhelpful and don't care” The front desk staff not helpful didin't care. Public phones broken didn't care, the in room staff excellent, room was spotless. I would not stay here unless a fairly expereinced traveller, because hotel a bit away from everything including food, and the staff were not interested in helping with directions or hints as to what to do.

“Great location, good value” We traveled with family here for 3 nights and occupied two rooms. Both rooms were clean, spacious and comfortable. Location is fantastic, within walking distance to Beale street around the corner, Rock& Soul museum, Gibson Guitar factory and plenty of great restaurants. One room faced Beale street and the music at night was definitely noticeable. Ironically, it was the noise from the next room that carried through the thin walls and adjoining door that kept us awake. While the hotel was also a good value, I would consider staying at the Doubletree one block away just to be a little further from all the noise. Take the time to visit the museums, Stax,Civil Rights, Sun Studios, Rock & Soul. If taking the Gibson tour, don't take the last tour of the day - as the factory workers have already left. And by all means, go to Gus's chicken. It's a quick walk and you won't regret it.
“Exceeded Expectations” This "new LQ" is recently refurbished - with modern decor. Very comfortable room, pleasant staff and much better than the standard LQ breakfast. A very nice experience.

“Will Be Back” This is a very comfortable and very reasonably priced hotel. Great value. We stayed in a king suite. The layout is very nice, the decor is up to date, and the room is clean. The service is also accommodating and professional. I look forward to returning during my next visit to San Antonio. The only sub-par item I would mention is the use of those little square pillows so many hotels today are using. They are awful! You can't turn around on them without your head falling off. I certainly hope they will consider reinstituting standard sized pillows again. I did find one tucked away in the room, but it seemed to be rendered unusable (from overuse by people avoiding the little square pillows?). Anyhow, if this is an issue for you, and you are able, bring your own.

“Great value in River North” I am in the city often for business and leisure travel. Chose to stay here as we were needing an inexpensive place to crash following a concert. The Springhills have been upgrading their design concept - kind of modern funky - I like it - the rooms were very clean - breakfast is okay - but its the value and location that are primary here. No, its not the sofitel, but its very centrally located, excellant service and a great rate for the class of hotel it is. The breakfast is just okay to me- but it is complimentary. I am a loyal Marriott rewards member and try to stay in Marriotts when I can - this place is great for people bringing kids to the city - with its internet in the lobby, pool and fabulous location. For a romantic weekend - try the Sofitel!

“Good location, nice breakfast, small, noisy room” I and a colleague shared a room here on a business visit. Located in the heart of downtown Indianapolis, the hotel is bustling and has a lovely lobby. But our room was a disappointment that just got worse. It was very oddly shaped; we entered through a hallway so narrow that the side of the TV cabinet almost blocked it off. Another odd, narrow hallway led to the tiniest bathroom I've ever seen in an American hotel. The toiled was stuck onto a strange raised platform just inside the door; when sitting on it, even a small person's knees were up against the wall, and the paper was on a rickety holder that threatened to fall over constantly. We also kept stubbing our toes on that strange platform. The pedestal sink was so small we could barely fit our toothbrushes on the edge. The desk was the only place in the room to set the coffee maker, but when we did so, there was inadequate space to work. The beds were comfortable, but our room was on a low floor and directly above a street with quite a few bars. A giant dumpster-emptier arrived each morning at 2AM, and spent an extremely noisy 30-40 minutes emptying the dumptsters. The breakfast buffet was very tasty. Valet parking was slow and expensive.

“An ideal airport hotel” This is an ideal airport hotel for those using LAX airport and nothing else. It is miles away from the Hollywood glitz and not ideal for the beaches surrounding Los Angeles. We arrived in L A from London at 2.50 pm picked up our rental car and had booked into the hotel at 4 p.m. it is that close. The room was spacious and it was nice to have a comfy clean queen bed to flop into for a couple of hours before finding something to eat. The decor of the room was o k and the carpet had a dye stain on it but that did not bother us. The hotel has a restaurant that offers a limited dinner menu and a bar. It does offer a complementary buffet breakfast to guests. Guest can also have use of the hotel car park at a fee of $12 per day. The staff were not the happiest bunch of people that I have come across but they did their jobs efficiently and the service within the hotel was good. This area of Central Blvd. is limited for restaurants for those not wishing to use actual hotel facilities. There are a couple of fast food chain drive throughs and a number of larger hotel chains close by offering food. We elected for the internet cafe across the road from the hotel which offered cheap hot food which sufficed our needs but nothing special. To summerise, this is a hotel that is convenient for the airport and is recommended for that purpose only just for one night and no more.

“when was that photo taken!!!” Looked lovely on the website, not quite like that in real life, hence the title. Fabulous location, but my room was a bit worn. Had previously been in the lobby, thought that next time I visited New York, I would like to stay in the hotel. Stayed 2 nights, had a good stay, toilet dripped all night, absolutely no view, well of the wall of the next part of the hotel, which made the room dark all the time. I suppose not every room can have a view. Took an eternity to book in, staff were friendly enough though

“Average” This hotel is perfect for a couple, that is looking for a place to sleep. It is not a place for families or people wanting to stay in the room for a long time. We stayed for one night and only had one problem. We were in our room getting ready to go out and our door opened. It was two girls, who the front desk person gave us our room as well. So they fixed that, but when we got back at 2am our keys didn't work. So we had to go back downstairs to get it fixed. Pros Clean Cheap Comfy beds Cons Front desk screw up Small rooms

“Staff went above and beyond!” We decided to take an in-town vacation and celebrated a special occasion at the Ritz-Carlton Dallas. The service was impeccable. Every staff member greeted us and went out of their way to make our short stay special. The spa was fantastic - even if you don't get a service, I highly recommend buying a day pass to use the whirlpool, steam room, pool, and sauna - don't forget the relaxation room! The staff must have realized we were celebrating, because they sent up a special treat for us to enjoy during our stay - it was these small gestures that really showed the dedication that the hotel has to it's guests. There is construction going on but we heard absolutely NO noise whatsoever. Our room was large and had a fabulous bathroom with a great amenity kit. We didn't want to leave! The hotel is quite close to several wonderful restaurants and museums. We will be back soon!

“good and bad” What this hotel does well, they do very well, and what isn't done well isn't. There's no in between. Pros of staying here: Free wine tasting some nights during happy hour, the toiletries are awesome, the bathroom is huge & the room's a great size, hotel restaurant is good, and the staff is very, very polite. Cons: There's no view to speak of, you can't get any type of breakfast here or near here unless you want to spend $20 for it, and there's nothing to do around the hotel unless you want to hit clubs and then there's nothing to do during the day. Also a train passes by the hotel each night around 4 am (I was on 12th floor & it still woke me up) but they do provide earplugs as a toiletry. Unique circumstance: There is free wi-fi in the rooms, but American broke my laptop so I couldn't access it. Still needed to check email, though, for work, and explained the circumstances to staff hoping they'd let me use the business center for free and they wouldn't. The young lady was very polite and explained the business center is run by a third-party so it wasn't up to her, but I still think there should have been some sort of pass code or something as inevitably this reflects poorly on the hotel, not the nameless third-party. This was the only blip, though, in an otherwise pleasant stay.

“Warm cookie, Warm Welcome and good stay.” Upon arrival was welcomed warmly by hotel and reception staff. Our request for a high floor was honoured. Room is spacious with nice big comfy beds. Good bathroom with Neutrogena toiletries. Good facilities in hotel. Downside was business centre was expensive to use. Internet $6 for 15 minutes. Location good, near the Magnificent Mile and facilities nearby such as a 7-11 shop and pubs and restaurants. A good stay, nice hotel.

“Nice hotel but maybe not my style” We stayed here over Veteran's Day weekend and were in town on a college visit tour with my daughter. This is a big hotel with fairly ornate decor. We have mixed feelings about our visit. The staff was very pleasant but seemed either new or a little confused. As a Kimpton member we received an upgrade to a suite but we requested to have our original room as we preferred two beds to sharing one large king. The room was comfortable and there was not too much street noise. We were across from the elevator and this was quite noisy as we could clearly hear the elevator arriving and people talking on the way to their rooms and while they waited for the elevator. They could use a bit of soundproofing. There was also a woman on our floor that had a small dog that walked around several times for several laps in the short time we were there. The dog peed in the elevator when we got on with her but was overall quiet and luckily it was on our way out. The bathroom was ok - a little on the small side and the sink was odd as the water pooled on the edge and ended up getting your mid section wet. We preordered breakfast and this was delivered right on time and cheerfully. The breakfast was very tasty. We received a large a carafe of coffee which we did not order and there was a lot of confusion at the front desk when we checked out and tried to have this charge removed. This was eventually resolved. We did go to the wine reception, which was ok. There was one red and one white wine available and some endive with a spread but that was it. The sitting area was lovely and very comfortable. I felt like the hotel furnishings were a little tired and could use some refreshing. This was our first trip to Baltimore so I am not sure what the other hotels are like but I am surprised at the other glowing reviews. We only walked around the neighborhood at night to go to dinner. Most of the businesses were closed and it felt pretty desolate. I am a city person but there were definitely some sketchy characters in the immediate six block area of the hotel that gave me some concerns of safety. I would potentially give this hotel another try based on the other reviews but I would also consider trying something else.

“For the money.... not bad.” I was traveling to New York for the first time and was with a friend so we didn't need anything fancy. I just wanted a place that was clean and safe. I'll break this down into different areas because somethings may be of more importance than other things to each traveler. Outside appearance: 3 There is nothing fancy about this building. If you feel the need for the big marque... look elsewhere. Lobby: 3 Again.... if you like the big grand lobby with all the fancy are and waterfalls... not going to find it here. Check-In: 5 Having never been to New York but read tons about how the staff at hotels were not friendly and often rude...I was ready for that. At the desk was a girl named Chris and a manager named Jason. They both were smiling and welcomed us to New York. Unfortunately our room wasn't ready but it was before 3:00 and they offered to keep our bags while we went to lunch. They were always friendly and helpful. Room: 4 It was small but I think all hotel rooms are small in New York. However...the hallways smelled clean, the rooms were clean...the beds were fine. Again...if you plan on spending a lot of time in your room sitting around watching TV...may want to go somewhere else but if you just need a place to shower and sleep...this place is fine. Location: 4 Anywhere you stay is going to be great for some things and a hike for others. China town is just a few blocks away.... the BEST food in New York is 3 blocks away down Mulberry in Little Italy. There's a subway nearby also. (See my New York review for restaurants and subway travel though) Price: 4 We payed $189 a night which is pretty cheap for New York. I have 1 issue with the hotel however..... not that big of a deal but I must mention it. The free WiFi does not work...at all...ever... at least on the 11th floor it doesn't. They do offer a business center in the lobby for a nominal fee where you can go check your email and surf the net. My feeling is that if the provided free WiFi sucks ... they should give you free access to the business center. It wasn't that big of a deal because both of us have iPhones and can get the net anywhere anyways but if you needed/wanted to google for some good places to eat...you would have to pay $3. By the way...I recommend taking your iPhone or a GPS when you take off walking.... much easier than a map.

“A Great Marriott Idea” The person at Marriott who came up with the concept of turning wonderful old downtown bank buildings into hotels should be promoted, with a nice raise. This is the second time in a month I've stayed at one of these converted hotels. Both experiences were excellent (the other one was the SpringHill Suites in downtown Baltimore). The lobby here is charming. The old vault has been cleverly turned into the eating area (the breakfast food, by the way, was fresh, varied and tasty). The rooms are just great, with everything you expect in a Residence Inn suite along with some decorating touches and the nice, high-floor views you DON'T get at a boilerplate RI hotel off of an interstate highway. This particular hotel has some cool restaurants near it. And the Cafe Brioso coffee shop a few doors down is a can't miss morning stop.

“Une adresse au rapport qualité-prix parfait !” Nous venons de découvrir cette très belle ville de Chicago que nous avons beaucoup aimé, le fait d'avoir choisi un hotel central,avec une situation parfaite, a aussi contribué à notre satisfaction. C'est bien le cas de cet hotel situé à coté de Grand Avenue et son arrêt de métro, mais avec également des lignes de bus si l'on veut se rendre dans les différents quartiers. Chambres très spacieuses, genre studio, avec un petit salon et une tv, un four micro ondes, nécessaire à café, une chambre parfaitement insonorisée, confortable, avec très bonne litterie. salle de bain très bien aussi. le petit déjeuner est inclus, ce qui est appréciable, un buffet très correct est proposé avec un assez vaste choix. Il y a une piscine intérieure située au 2ème étage. Cet hotel était en outre d'un prix très correct, imbattable me semble-t-il pour ce confort et cette situation. A recommander !

“Location + free parking” Its all you have to know. There are not many budget friendly places to stay in san francisco that are in a good location. I'd say for its price it can't be beat just because the rooms were decent, the rooms were quiet and clean, and lastly free parking. I'd say stay here as well because there is a bus stop that can take you pretty much anywhere in the city a couple of blocks away and you are next to a lot of good nightlife.

“great hotel- very convenient” Great spot in Easton- every bit as convenient as the Hilton. Pretty new- rooms were big, clean and comfortable. We parked the car and walked or shopping and dining. We stayed on a Sunday nite- great rate and less crowded.

“Not a place to stay if you want to rest” As many others have written I was the victim of a cancelled Delta flight (broken cargo door) and was booked into this hotel. When I arrived at 1005 pm there was one desk clerk and fifteen people in front of me. It took 35 minutes before I could get a room. Isn't there anyone else on duty that could have opened up and checked in others? There were people still checking in at 11 pm! They did clear the line when the lady who was supposed to come in at 11 pm showed up but at times there were over 20 people and one slow desk clerk. The hotel is a place I would never return to. My room had a tube TV but the batteries in the remote were dead (I had extras and replaced them). I woke frequently during the night as the water pipes banged and squeaked and squealed. They may be renovating the rooms, I suspect the one I was in had been renovated but the did nothing to fix ancient plumbing. The only redeeming factor was that they kept their restaurant open. Fried chicken, black eyed peas and collard greens were very good on the buffet and they accepted the Delta vouchers. As a Delta Diamond and Two Million Miler I am going to bring the issue of this particular hotel up with their management. They should not be sending weary travelers here.

“Old, not as good as it used to be...” I used to visit this hotel 10 years ago, when it first opened, and it was incredibly nice back then, so I thought I might revisit. Of course, and to be expected, a lot has deteriorated over the past 10 years. Other than the hotel being old, the room was dingy. The carpet was dingy. The kitchen looked old and dirty. It smelled of mildew or something. I only stayed for one night - less than 8 hours, so I didn't use the kitchen, but I was scared to even use a cup for water. The towels were old, very rough on the skin.
