The floor was old and dingy, there was a old black tarry dirty spot on the floor - not even sure what it was - wore shoes the entire time, was afraid to go barefoot. Everything was functional - only old and dingy. There was a mysterious knocking that occurred the entire night. At first I thought someone was knocking on the door, but after looking through the peephole many times and being fooled, realized it was just the room. It sounds like someone lightly tapping on the door - all through the night. Was scared - thought room was haunted. This is NOT an extravagant hotel, so if that is what you are looking for, this is not for you. Everything is old. I wouldn't say it is dirty - so much as - it has the stench of being old and overused. Everything works, just don't expect luxury. If you want something bare-bones and minimal, this is ok. Personally, I thought it was quite expensive for what they were offering...which isn't much. I would rate this hotel as a 1-2 star, not much more. I don't discourage it, but I certainly don't recommend it. Only good point is that there are a lot of things around hotel - grocery stores, department stores, restaurants, so you can do other things - and not have to STAY in the room. :P

“The very definition of average” The Omni is a stunning building from the outside, and the blandest thing ever once inside. There's nothing wrong with it, but it lacks personality, style, and sense of place. A banal business property, with poorly designed rooms, very disappointing given the stark contrast with the shiny architecture. Service is competent though, which is good thing in such a busy property. Definitely not my cup of tea, although reasonably priced. Would only recommend it to undemanding business customers looking for a safe place to crash with a swift laundry service, or for attendees at a conference on the other side of the street, you won't get any closer than this to the Convention Center.

“Great hotel, great location” Excellent hotel and a very convenient location within walking distance to Times Square. Though the rooms are much smaller than the typical Hilton Garden Inn, they are more spacious than many places in NYC. Breakfast is very good and there's a small bar. There's a subway station right outside the door. A great deal for NYC! We'll be back!

“Had a Great Experience” Just spent two nights at this hotel for business. The hotel is centrally located and everything I wanted to see or do was within walking distance. The room and bathroom were very clean. The bed was very comfortable with nice linens. The rooms also have high speed internet access. I didn't eat at the restaurants, but there seemed to be a pretty decent variety of places in the hotel (steakhouse, sushi, sports bar/pub, diner type restaurant). There is also a Starbucks in the hotel lobby area. There are lots of good and interesting places to eat within an easy walk though, so go explore. The only downside was parking. The hotel has valet parking for $32/day. There is a garage across the street from the hotel that was a bit cheaper (I think) and an outdoor lot on the side street next to the hotel. I would definitely stay here again.

“Not a Bad Place to Be Marooned” I was stuck in Charlotte for the evening and the airline put me up in this hotel. The rooms are really spacious and well appointed, the lobby is nice and the service was really friendly. There is also an Omaha Steakhouse in the building, not a bad option for an airport hotel. If you are stuck in the city due to travel changes or need to stay somewhere for an early flight the next day, I would highly recomment this hotel.
“5 star hotel!!!!!” This hotel was amazing!! It was spotless, clean, spacious, and modern!!! If I'm ever in Boston again, I will deff be back here!!! :)

“Fantastic!” This hotel has a fantastic location, right on Central Park on West 59th Street at 6th Avenue (Avenue of the Americas). Every major designer store is within walking distance as is Bloomingdale's, Barney's, Bergdorf's and Saks. There is a complimentary Bentley Flying Spur with chaffeur at your free disposal to take you anywhere on the island of Manhattan you desire. The Front Desk team was fantastic upon arrival and checkout. The Concierge were extremely helpful in terms of transportation, theatre and dining. The room was very spacious and the bathroom was gorgeous as was the view of the park. The La Prarie Spa was fantastic for a massage and facial. The Club Lounge was a great place to relax after a fast paced day and night. The Star lounge was a beautiful bar . I am not too crazy about BLT Market as I think it is far too casual for the Upper West Side and the Ritz Carlton! It is also very pricey for breakfast! But I would go back in a heartbeat!

“Not for Us” Is not bad pretty good? I feel strange about this review. If you are looking for a "Mid scale limited service hotel", then you will like this place. I can't believe I paid $14 to self park my car. We are used to valet parking at hotels, where you give them the keys and they park your car and take your bags up to your room. Don't expect that here. We had to carry all our stuff around a crowded parking garage. We had a room on the seventh floor that was so tiny and I think it was a two step upgrade. It had a small patio that overlooked the river. It was clean, but even though we left the card on our bed, the linens weren't changed. I have never stayed in hotel that only changes the linens every three days unless you signal them to do so. The bed was like a trampoline, bouncy and soft. Not good for us at all. The hotel did have extra pillows and towels waiting like I had asked for, most you still have to ask for them after you arrive. The breakfast was ok, but there were lots of children acting like brats, including a group of surly high school cheerleaders and their families from a local suburb. Just once, I'd like to see a high school math club on an outing. As far as the happy hour, people bring me drinks, I don't stand in long lines for them. Hot dogs? The senior crowd was all over them. I have to be nice, here are the good things. This hotel is in a great building in a great location if you want to park your car (yourself) and explore San Antonio. A young family would love this place. The staff was really nice. Everytime I saw anyone, they said hello and asked how I was doing, just like in the best hotels. I loved the gentleman telling the guests that he was attending the Asian Festival and what it was at Breakfast. I wonder if he got his eggrolls? The hotel should be proud of all its staff. Except house keeping that didn't change our bed.

“Upmarket without the price tag” Three of us stayed for 4 days here. Staff courteous friendly and attentive, the concierge remembers you by name! Modern entrance with clean lines, the rooms very comfortable and clean, bathroom products nice too. A balcony adds a little open air feel to the room. A tad expensive but that's Boston so money well spent here. Positioned good right In The theatre district and not far from the Boston commons, downtown or the convention centre.( the slight walk will invigorate you) even the trolley tour is right out front. A few small negatives, noisy air conditioner, needed coffee set up for 4 not 2 and the lifts were a wee bit tardy at times. All in all a place very worth staying at.

“Can I Bring the Bed Home?” Positives: The beds were large and absolutely fantastic to sleep in. Along with the big pillows, I was tempted not to go home.....The staff was courteious and extremely helpful....Nice decor with the lights set at a intimate setting....Great location to walk around downtown and close to Pike St Market Negatives: I don't mind when the rooms are chilly, but I did notice the AC was on full blast...The biggest pain was probably the parking. Not a big area to pull up the car for valet, so found myself waiting in the street for the person in front of me plus a few cars coming out Overall a good hotel and would recommend staying there

“Great location need some updating” We stayed on a weekend (Friday and Saturday). As others have commented, the rooms were somewhat dated but clean. We got a good rate, so it was okay. Location was excellent for visiting the West End and it's attractions. Complimentary breakfast was good with lots of choices. One major issue was the rooftop concert at a local club on Saturday night. Not the hotel's fault, but it was sure hard to sleep. I might stay here again if we were visiting Dallas, but I also would shop for a good rate elsewhere.

“Im Herzen vom Union Square District” Das Hotel liegt sehr gut im Herzen vom Union Square District. Alles ist bequem zu Fuss erreichbar. Eine Cable Car Haltestelle liegt quasi direkt vor der Tür, zur Market Street gelangt man zu Fuss in weniger als 10 Minuten. In der näheren Umgebung liegen die meisten grossen Geschäfte, direkt gegenüber ein Starbucks. Die Zimmer sind für ein Stadthotel sehr gross und geräumig. Es ist zu empfehlen, ein "Bayview" Zimmer zu verlangen. Man kann von hier zwar nicht wirklich die Bay sehen, sondern blickt eher auf die Hinterhöfe, hat aber keine Strassenlärm der doch sehr störend und laut sein kann, wenn alle 5 Minuten die Cable Car vorbei rattert. Die Zimmer sind sehr gut eingerichtet und es wird sehr auf Sauberkeit geachtet. Ein kleiner Negativpunkt ist, dass die Zimmer ueber keinen eigenen Safe verfuegen. Es wird aber kostenlos ein Safe bei der Rezeption zur Verfuegung gestellt. Das Personal an der Rezeption koennte etwas freundlicher sein. Da das Hotel immer sehr gut gebucht ist (auch viele Airlines lassen ihre Crews hier uebernachten), hat man es wohl nicht noetig, die Gaeste freundlich zu begruessen. Aber das ist nur eine Kleinigkeit. Das Hotel verfuegt ueber ein Restaurant (nicht ausprobiert, da relativ teuer und genuegend Restaurants in unmittelbarer Umgebung) und eine Bar. Die Bar ist leider nur bis 23:00 Uhr geoeffnet, verfuegt aber dennoch ueber ein breites Getraenke- und Snackangebot. Insgesamt ist das Hotel fuer SF Toristen sehr empfehlenswert, aufgrund der sehr zentralen Lage.

“Good, but not great” This is my tenth FS property and my least favorite. I could not understand how any FS hotel could rate so low on TA, but one stay here and you may know why it is middle-ranked. For the price the service should be flawless and for the most part the staff held true to this. The spa staff, concierge desk and housekeeping department were top notch. The front desk also did a fantastic job. However, the doormen and bellmen failed miserably on nearly every arrival/departure from the hotel. I think living in NYC requires grit, attitude and a gimic; and the FS staff can give you plenty of that. Maybe I am a naive, over-friendly, optimistic country mouse, but it sure would be nice to at least get a greeting from the staff when you're paying $1000 a night. The one shocker is that the spa is located seven floors underground. A sinking thought to be in the bowels of NYC. Ask for the fire escape plan on arrival and try to settle into a relaxing massage with this on your pragmatic mind. Not worth the asking price. Get half the price and twice the service at The New York Palace.

“Aging Property, OK for a Night, Noisy” Aging property, needs a Hampton upgrade, no flat screen TVs, leaky air units allow outside air in and noise, beaten hallway walls with obvious patching, for a night its clean but not up to usual HI standards.
“場所が最高” まず場所がとっても便利。ホテルのフロントはフロントといえないほど狭いけど、みなさん親切でした。他の方も書いていましたが、トランクが開けられないほどの広さです。。あと私の部屋は車椅子でも対応している部屋で、シャワーの所に区切りがないので、シャワーをするたびに、シンクのあたりがびしょびしょになってしまいました。ちなみにここのホテルとブルックリンのNUホテルは姉妹ホテルです。

“Gute Wahl” Das La Quinta Inn war eine gute Wahl für San Antonio. Die meisten Attraktionen sind per Fuss zu erreichen. Zimmer sind neu, sauber und man hat den üblichen 3 Stene Standart. Plus war das ein 'Full Breakfast" inclusive war, jedoch wie fast allen Hotels kostet das Parken 20 Dollar pro Tag. Alamo und Tower of the Americas sind 5 Minuten weg und Abends laed eine Bar auf einen Drink in der Lobby ein. Fuer den kleinen Hunger gibt es in der Bar auch Snacks. Pool und Hot Tub sind vorhanden.

“Decent Hotel” I stayed here for one night after my flight out of NYC was cancelled. The lobby and room were both average: nothing to write home about, but both were tastefully decorated and clean. The bed was comfortable. The bathroom showed its age a bit, but the fixtures worked well. The room and bathroom were both above average in terms of size. The hotel is in a nice location for many attractions. The price was also very reasonable for Manhattan. This is a good choice for those looking for a decent hotel at a reasonable price.

“The best hotel by far on the West Side of Town in El Paso” Okay, so I have stayed in a few hotels throughout my visits to El Paso. In fact, I originally booked a different hotel and stayed there one night and...it was terrible so I stopped at the Holiday Inn and asked if they had rooms. I moved my stuff over there asap the following day and spent the last three days I was in town there! I travel there once or twice a year to visit family. I have to say that if you're looking to stay near the West side of town in El Paso..that this is your best bet. The room was clean and big. The staff was very nice and friendly and very helpful. I had to get an early check in..by early meaning 8am (I hated the hotel I was in so I had to get out!) and they let me have a room. No problem. The gym is brand new at the hotel. There is no other hotel that I have stayed at in El Paso that has a workout facility like this one. Most of them offer one treadmill that barely works and a bike and they call it a gym. This one had several cardio machines..all new and weights as well as flat screen tvs. I went into shock when I walked in! The pool..is small but clean and above average from what I've seen at other places. The location of the hotel is great! It's right near the mall, the racetrack and several great areas. Overall, the hotel isn't brand new and luxurious...perhaps stay near the airport if you are looking for more of that (although they are old as well..) but it is nice. I had pleasant stay and I will tell you that I will stay there from now on every time I visit El Paso. Having grown up in that city....I know the city well and this place was worth the money and pleasant. It's not the fanciest of places..that's not what you'll get. But it's comfortable. nice bar in the lobby too and free internet access.

“Not bad, but very expensive for what you get.” My wife and I spent a night in the Flatotel during a recent visit to New York. We got a good rate through an internet booking website, but it is still a pretty expensive accommodation (260 USD per night). It is conveniently located in 52nd Street, next to the Sheraton, close to a lot of theaters, many attractions and tons of upscale restaurants. The lobby is dark, what is not very welcoming, and the front desk staff is efficient but not very nice. When we arrived our room was not ready, so we had to use the restrooms in the lobby to refresh before hitting the city. I am not very picky, but those restrooms were very dirty, what was very annoying. Our room was on the 17th floor, it was spacious, but the furniture was quite outdated. The TV was old, but the bed was comfortable. The bathroom was big and clean. Soundproofing was good, what is a must in Midtown and we could enjoy a good night's sleep. We did not try the restaurant as we preferred to have breakfast in a dinner nearby. In the last 2 years I have spent 10 weekends in New York, always in different hotels. It is hard to believe how much prices tend to fluctuate and how you will only have an average or lower than average room if you spend a small fortune.

“Train-station type of hotel, 4star service” Good room – spacious, clean. Good view from 50th floor. Healthy breakfast in club lounge – limited but healthy choice - they have eggs, juices, porridge, some fruits (banana, apples), cereal, tea and coffee Service - suffers... I left an item for overnight laundry, and at 7am it was not in my room as promised the night before. At 7.10, I just wanted to find out what’s happening, and during the next 20 minutes I tried to speak to reception, concierge, operator, laundry...everyone was happy to transfer me to someone else. No one knew where the shirt was, and no one wanted to deal with this ‘search’. It exposed a total chaos in this hotel. When I told the next day not to charge $18 for this service, the receptionist deleted it at once even without understanding what happened... such things probably occur there on a daily basis. Overall feel in this hotel is that it’s so large that it’s difficult to provide a truly good service. One certainly does not feel any luxury here.

“Great Georgetown location, super value for a huge suite” The Georgetown Suites actually has two separate buildings a couple of blocks apart. I stayed at the 30th Street location, which is just off M Street. This was a great location from which to explore the shops and restaurants to Georgetown. The suites were huge - a large living room, a full kitchen and a large bedroom. I paid about $220 a night which, given the size of the room and the location, seemed like an excellent value for Washington DC. A simple continental breakfast was served in the lobby. Room service was available by ordering form local restaurants which delivered.

“Location, location, location but...” My husband had a conference that was based out of this hotel. The location in Union Square was great - walking distance to great shopping and convenient to public transportation. The hotel, though, appears to be a converted motel with outdoor corridors. We had the "premier" section which meant walking up stairs, then across the pool area before catching an elevator to the next floor, crossing the area outside area again to get to our room. This was not expected and it was not easy with luggage. (The bellman uses a service elevator that guests cannot use) Also not expected was the noise level, with door slamming all evening long and large groups of people by the pool even at 2:00am. Other guests in our group had the same issue. Where is security?? I would rate the room as average, but the bed was very, very comfortable. Only advantage to premier level was free internet and 2 free bottles of water (which were never replaced). The overall service though at the hotel was very good. Service at the restaurant though was very poor. I probably would not stay at this hotel again unless I had a very, very low rate.

“Superb hotel for a superb stay in SF” You will not be disappointed with this hotel. The Rooms are spacious, cosy, bright and airy. A nice little touch was of an evening:- dressing gown and chocolates were laid on the bed of an evening. Complimentary hot drinks arrived at the room each morning too. The hotel staff are very friendly and helpful. The location is also fab!

“Comfort with a price” My daughter and I stayed at The Benjamin from April 15-21 in a one bedroom suite on the fourth floor. The accomodations were very spacious for NYC, very clean and well appointed especially for business travelers with fax, large desk for working, internet access and good lighting. The closets are big with lots of storage space. The kitchen is great for snacks/breakfast. The bathrooms are all white and updated. There are lots of windows that open for fresh air and natural light. The gym was adequate. The staff is excellent and the lobby has the soothing fragrance of a spa. The drawbacks were noise from the street even with the windows closed. The living room was in need of renovation. The walls were too muted in color, and the furniture was very heavy and dark which made the room depressing and unwelcoming, but I would stay again. The noisy street views are preferrable to no views in some hotels or those awful views of another room or the air conditioning equipment. Considering the rates of NYC hotels, I think it was a good value and a great midtown location.

“Would not recommend hotel for leisure stay” I have been visiting San Diego for 20 years and this was my first visit to this hotel. There are far too many choices that are significantly better than this hotel. I got a good rate on the internet but parking was over $20 per day. Breakfast buffet which is not outstanding was $20 per person. The internet site said they had a shuttle which they did not offer. The restaurant closes early and late room service not available. The lobby is on the 12th floor, you park on the 11th floor so must drive up to the 11 floor snaking though each floor to get to the 11th floor, this is tedious if you take your auto out much. The room was nice, a suite, very clean, and quiet. I would not stay here again because I felt too enclosed and away from what I love about San Diego....the sun and the sea.

“A must!” Modern, metropolitan and minimalist. Impeccable as few are able to consistently be, effortlessly luxurious with a genuinely attentive service. If you learned to appreciate this recipe at the James Chicago you will be pleased to find it in New York too. It's all those little unexpected touches that get you to L O V E the James New York. I won't list them because the discovery journey is part of what make you smile. Whether you have been to NYC many many times and you want to breath Soho in or this is your first visit, the James is a MUST.

“Disappointed.” For $250/night, I'd hope to have Internet access and room service that takes less than 90 minutes to arrive. We are in town for Marine Corps Marathon, but are swamped by people here for the Colbert/Stewart rally. Too many people. Staff is friendly enough (except for very grumpy waiter in Squares restaurant), but everything is way too packed to even enjoy the beautiful lobby. The bar was at least 4 people deep on Saturday at 3pm, restaurant packed, room service takes forever. If you sell out the hotel, you should staff accordingly. We regularly choose Renaissance properties, but this does not meet the same standards that we are accustomed to with a Renaissance name on the building. One highlight was the fitness center - very nice.

“Perfect location, walk inside from airport” Walk inside from airport. Easy checkin, friendly staff. Large comfortable rooms, well appointed. Bed side outlets, good coffee. Perfect for the traveler that needs to stay before their flight.

“Rooms could use an update, but overall we were pleased with this hotel.” We thought this hotel was close to seaworld. It was 12 miles away, but took us about an hour to get there. We had to get on 4 interstates to get there. Once we finally got there everything was great. Staff was wonderful. The rooms could use an update but were very clean. The breakfast was over at 9:00 am. Since we were on vacation, we missed that. We did eat dinner there at resturant, and it was very good. We would stay there again.

“Another wonderful stay at the Inn” Inn at the Market has become our go to place when visiting in Seattle. Because of conference housing requirements we've had to stay at other hotels on other visits and have always missed being at the Inn. The major pluses are the 1) incredible courtesy and helpfulness of the staff 2) the location so close to the Public Market and 3) the general ambiance of relaxed elegance. Typically Pacific Northwest in its decor, the best feature is the rooftop deck that overlooks Elliot Bay. From there, you can sip wine, watch the sunset and the ferries coming in. We stayed at the Inn as "bookends" on our trip to the San Juan Islands and were lucky enough to be upgraded in room type on both ends of our journey. The free wireless worked well and the self-serve business center had a computer to use to print out boarding passes for our flight.

“Historic hotel in great location” Lovely, historic hotel conveniently located on Boston's Freedom Trail. Rooms are small ( single occupancy rooms are reminiscent of Pullman accommodations) but well appointed. On the plus side the food in the main dining room was outstanding in terms of sourcing and quality. The concierge suggested creative inexpensive nearby activities.

“Good value” Needing another one night stay near LAX, we gave the Radisson a try, having previously stayed at the nearby Sheraton and Four Points and both much more expensive on this occasion. Like the Sheraton next door it's not very modern but it has everything you need for a stopover. The bathroom was quite small but everything was clean and worked. The staff were friendly and helpful and one nice feature is that you can check the progress of the shuttles on a screen which tracks them using GPS. You also get free WiFi throughout, something the Sheraton doesn't offer. I would normally rate this place as 3 stars but we got a very cheap rate for one night so I've raised it to 4 stars. Out of the three LAX hotels we've tried, the Sheraton is probably slightly nicer than the other two, but there's very little in it. The cost would probably decide it the next time we transit through LA.

“Fine Stay” Stayed at the Fairfield because hotels in downtown San Jose were extremely pricey. Overall, I was satisfied, but would probably spend more to stay downtown next time because there is more to do. Upon check-in, I was disappointed that as an elite Marriott member my request for a 2nd floor room was not granted; however, I did receive a first floor room that opened to the pool area. Strange setup for a Fairfield, its rooms surround a central pool area. Breakfast was fine, but seating space was somewhat limited. Complimentary goodie back for elite members upon check-in is a nice touch.

“Bates Motel” We stopped in off the interstate on our way to New Orleans we just needed a place to stop and sleep, but this place violated some major health code violations i am sure, When I walked in there was a girl at the front desk with a Tattoo across her neck, and shady characters hanging around. and i thought to myself this is just one night and we wil be out in the morning. when we got to the room and pulled back to covers, there was "body hair" under the sheets and dried blood on the back of the comforter. Needless to say i was out the door and back to the front office, where it took and act ofcongress to get my money back. DO NOT stay here. so we drove down into Mississippi and found a nice days inn in Hernando Mississippi

“Just what we wanted” Off the beaten path, clean suite, free parking, complimentary breakfast. The suite was perfect for this family of 2 parents and a teenager. Board games need to be replaced, but front desk loaned us a deck of cards. Front desk and housekeeping very professional and helpful. After very busy days, it was nice to return to our quiet "home". This is the first hotel (ever!) that we did not hear slamming doors and loud guests in the hallways.

“Like trains?” The Fairfield Inn NW on the Mo-Pac is well located for this author's purposes; convenient to 183 via Braker Street and restaurants. Do not miss Sushi Sake if you like sushi, see that review. The staff is friendly and well-trained, and they recognize Marriott Elite members on return visits. The morning breakfast staff is quite good, although breakfast is really not adequate and not up to Marriott's standards. Trains. The rooms are nicer than most FairField Inn rooms, well-appointed and maintained. This author has never had any issues with facilities or rooms at this Fairfield Inn. Trains. Breakfast eggs. The eggs are powdered, the sausage and bacon are unrecognizable. Forget it and go out to eat. There are plenty of good places close, though, so no worries. Trains. This hotel would be much better without the train set in the backyard. The train set is very realistic and runs all night long on the east side so try and get a room on the west side - though the author has never been successful.

“Odd European-style 2-star hotel in questionable area” The first thing you'll notice are the ancient elevators. Or, elevator singular -- the second was closed for the first part of my trip. Apparently the fastest elevators in the USA when they were installed in 1920-1930 (can't remember when). They're the kind of elevator cage doors you have to manually open. Kind of cool, but impossible to deal with while carrying luggage. There really needs to be a porter on the main floor to help people who are checking in open the cage elevator door. And also a bottle of Purell on each floor. The cage and outer door were sticky with oils and whatnot from other guests hands. The rooms are incredibly tiny, and beds even tinier. I was traveling alone, so this was fine, but had I been sharing the bed it would've been incredibly uncomfortable. It could've been a queen bed, but looked more like a double. The bathroom isn't actually separated from the room. The sink is in the bedroom area, next to the bed and make-shift closet. There is a sliding door that covers the entrance to the toilet and shower, but it isn't any different than having a curtain. If you are traveling alone, as I was, no big deal. But if you are traveling with another person, you will hear every sound as if it were in the same room. Because it is essentially in the same room. Sheets were clean, and the A/C which was a haphazard window unit, worked fine. The service at the front desk, complimentary airport shuttle, housekeeping... all were totally fine. The Gaslamp area is a questionable location. It could be perfect for you if you are a college student looking to party until the wee hours of the morning (as there are endless night clubs and bars and large crowds of other drunk or stoned people every 20 feet for about an eight-block radius) when you'll be able to drunkenly stagger into the hotel's lobby cafe for food at 4 AM (it's open 24 hrs and was PACKED at 4 AM with both late-night party-types; and also people who worked in nearby clubs and bars who had just gotten off work). One night I was standing outside of the hotel having a cigarette and was asked by a person just walking by at random, if I "wanted any heroin?" I simply said, No, thanks, and they asked, "Crack?" No, I said, I'm fine. "Coke? Weed?" Really, I said, I'm fine, thank you. They finally left me alone and walked on. Another night walking back from a restaurant, I was at the corner of the hotel outside the 24 hr cafe, and a young college kid, obviously drunk, asked me if I had any cocaine. In all my travels in a variety of places of the world I've never been asked to buy drugs or if I had them to share. This is why I'd consider the Gaslamp area questionable. I mean, if you like that kind of thing, great! Good for you. You'd have a ball staying at this hotel, as it's right in the center of it all. But if you are looking for something safer, or if you are traveling with kids, my advice is to stay anywhere but the Gaslamp area. I visited the restaurants in the Hillcrest area, which seemed much safer and calmer. Nicer. I didn't get to see any of the hotels by the beach, or in any other area. If I ever return to San Diego, I'll be staying in one of those.

“Great Place - Garage Sux” The ONLY thing I have to gripe about this place is the Garage. It is small and not really set up for the two-way traffic down one-way lanes. There is no elevator service, despite being three levels tall. The stairs to levels 2 and 3 are uneven and actually tilt you forward for a bit. There is no attendant at this lot (at $19 per day), so you must enter your credit card at a machine that sometimes doesn't work. Great hotel otherwise. Super friendly service - excellent PF Chang's right across the driveway.
“great place” very nice, updated hotel. Very comfy, but only negative was that the parking was $38 per night. I believe you may be able to park next door for $28, but probably not worth the hassle.

“Excellent Hotel At Central Location That Is Welcoming” Location: Within one minute on foot to Union Square Park, very close to Macy's and lots of shops. From the airport, take BART to Powell St and walk about 5 minutes slightly uphill. Cable car is just outside which can take you to Fisherman's Wharf. Reception: Small reception as the hotel was originally an older building. Still, the staff was friendly throughout, giving out tips and recommendations. Room: Although my room was next to the elevator, there was not much noise. Once inside, the bedroom was to the left and the living area was to the right, and the bathroom is right down the middle. The bedroom had a door and both rooms have flat screen TV's with plenty of channels. The living room had a view of Post St. Both rooms were of decent size. The living room is especially comfortable. Even though some of the paint was chipped in certain corners, the furniture itself was in very good condition. The room did not feel old at all. The hallways were also bright (definitely not dark and dim as another review suggested). Comfortable beds if a bit soft, and good toiletries included. Free WiFi. Happy Hour: Between 5 to 7pm daily, there is a free wine and cheese tasting in the hotel. There is a very pleasant staff member present to help serve and you can ask him for tips or just chat. It's also a great time to meet some of your fellow travelers. Breakfast: Self-service free continental breakfast on each floor and it was fine. You can take the food back to your room or eat at the table. Overall/Value: I generally enjoy staying at modern properties instead of places with "charm." However, Inn at Union Square has managed to combine the feel of warmth and uniqueness along with modern comforts. Service was impeccable throughout. The room costs about $200. While certainly not cheap, at central San Francisco, this is very reasonable vs many other hotels that offer less.

“An institutional monster. Not bad for a conference.” This hotel is HUGE. If you're at a conference beware if meetings are being held on both the tower and Atrium side as there is a good 100yds between each building. The large auditorium is closest to the atrium side. Media bar has good food and a decent atmosphere when the hotel is full. The hotel is not really near anything so plan on taking a taxi everywhere. The gym is impressive but is a full 5 min walk from the atrium side of the hotel. I would unlikely choose to stay here if I was on a vacation in Dallas because of the location.

“Wonderful Wild Weekend” We stayed at the Ink48 for 3 nights. We had a wonderful King room with a city view that was breathtaking at night. Our room was modern, comfortable and perfectly clean. The shower was the best i have experienced in any hotel ever. We walked to several nice restaurants nearby, the Landmark Tavern an Irish bar and restaurant just down the street on 11th Ave, had good food and friendly service. Nizza on 9th for Italian was awesome, Mercury Bar on 9th at 46th for great drinks and food. We stopped in at Grace wine and liquor on 44th and 10th for a nice bottle wine for our room. Easy walk to Times Square which was only a 10 minute walk through a nice neighborhood area on 9th with many restaurants and bars to check out. We walked from Central Park all the way back to our hotel down 5th avenue to the beautiful St. Patricks Cathedral then down 53rd to broadway then over to Times Square and on to our hotel at 48th and 11th, it was a great walking adventure. The rooftop bar at Ink48 was a great place to end our walk with a fantastic martini, the rooftop bar has a fabulous view of the city, you must check it out. We had a fantastic stay with no complaints, no excessive noise, no problems at all. We will definately stay here on our next visit to New York City!

“A Delight” Check in: friendly & helpful. Acknowledged my advanced request for a quiet room. Even better, they delivered one. Room: Clean and comfortable. Great room décor, as expected from a W. Window seat is a nice touch, but you can’t sit in it with the shutters open. Shutters on the windows seem a strange choice to me. They did fine blocking most of the light. There is also a sheer curtain, so you could have the shutters open for light and still have some privacy. The desk was groovy and well appointed with Ethernet and six outlets. It’s not the most ergonomic workspace, so probably not the best choice for someone working in the room for long hours. The room was big enough for two, but would be cramped if you tried to fit a family of four into a double. Lighting was a bit skimpy. If I was in the room during the day, I opened the shutters for more light. Noise: Hallway noise was fairly typical for a hotel: you hear door slams and people in the hall. I heard almost no street noise—quite impressive for a downtown hotel in a major city—from my room facing towards the Bay Bridge. However, you should note that the south side of the hotel is next to a firehouse. I’m guessing rooms on that side will hear the sirens. I could hear toilet flushing/showers, and muffled TV from the room above, but did not notice any footfall or conversation noise. Bed: Quite comfortable. They provide a generous 4 pillows per double bed. Location: ideal for conventions at the Moscone Center. This was one of my primary considerations. It’s also an easy walk to BART and the shopping district at Market St. Restaurants and a movie theater are also quite close. Sustainability: I took the no-maid-service option at checking. I don’t need my sheets and towels changed every day and I didn’t figure I’d generate much trash either. I have found that at hotels that say they don’t change and wash your towels everyday upon request, they actually do. Security: elevators require a key card to ascend above the 5th floor. Food: Pricey, but in line with this class of downtown hotel. Breakfast was better than I expected. Dinner was just OK. Technology: In-room internet was $16/day. Not cheap. If you want internet access included with your room, go to a hotel that offers it. I’m certainly not going to complain about a charge that I knew to expect. Nice HDTV with actual HD content. The clock radio is a stylish Tivoli and had an ipod dock connected. It struck me as impractical to go with the high style radio then cobble on a dock that either has to sit on top of the radio’s speaker or take up more of the limited bedside space. Parking: I didn’t park at the hotel. It’s an easy walk from BART. Service: Employees were eager to help. Late on the second day, water started to gurgle up through the shower drain. I called it in and was told engineering would be up to fix it. However, they quickly called back and offered to move me to another room (on a higher floor) and comp me a breakfast. Unfortunately that floor had a group that was up all night moving from room to room. The next morning, I asked to be moved again and was given another room. It was inconvenient to have to move, but they were clearly concerned about my comfort and safety. Spa: I did indulge in a massage my last night there. Facilities were quite good, especially for a downtown hotel (as opposed to a rural, desert location). My therepist, Angeles, was great. One of the best massages I’ve had. Overall I was very pleased. I was worried based on some of the complaints I had read. Sound isolation could have been better, but certainly was not significantly worse than most hotels.

“Fine LA hotel” We have stayed at the Carlyle Inn numerous times in the past five years. It is reasonably priced and is in a good location for us to visit our family in Los Angeles. The rooms and bathrooms are clean and comfortable. Breakfast is included and is quite adequate. Free internet is available in the lobby, and free but sometime slow wi-fi is available in the rooms as well. We are quite pleased with the Carlyle, and anticipate that we will stay there on future visits

“Fantastic Large Hotel, Exceptional Location, Metro, VG Buffet Breakfast” This is a very large conference / convention hotel with three accomodation towers. Checkin & checkout was fast & efficient. It could be different at busy times with many new arrivals. I had a good clean modern very comfortable room on 8th floor. It was about 10 rooms for elevators (4). Yes you will get lots of exercise just walking around within hotel complex. Please wear comfortable footwear. I would recommend that everybody spends 10+ minutes exploring hotel as soon as possible after checkin. It will help you become familiar with layout and location of coffee shops / convenience store / pub and restaurants / fitness centre / swimming pools / various conference rooms. All the public areas were in very good condition and clean. It is located in a quiet residential area with very nice landscaped grounds. It is a nice area to take a walk around the block. It is an easy walk down Connecticut Ave to the White House area etc etc. It is easy to get to the Zoo and or the National Cathedral. The Red Line Metro stop is next to one of the hotel exits. A large convenience store is minutes away. Many dining choices available locally. You have a choice of entrances, one is a gentle slope, another is a little hill climb. No problem with reasonable fitness. My reaction to many of the negative posts was "Are we talking about the same hotel ?" I will stay again and would recommend to family and business colleagues. Please compare the special hotel price offered via email/phone for specific dates with various internet sites. The price variations offered can be unbelievable.

“Very Trendy, Fun, but a little pricey” My wife and I stayed here for our anniversary and really liked the hotel. I stayed here for two nights for free because of my Hilton honors points but otherwise it would have been a very expensive weekend. I realize that this is downtown Chicago but our room was priced at over $300 a night, our drinks on the rooftop were between $12-$15 (for nothing special) and breakfast was also very pricey. I don't mind paying extra for being in the city, but all of the food and drinks were cheaper everywhere else we went in the city. Having said all of that this is a very nice hotel. The staff was good, the rooms were really fun and well decorated, and the beds were comfortable. Great weekend get away overall!

“Beautiful hotel at a great rate” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Capitol Hill with my adult children in late December, 2007. I was a bit concerned when I booked the rooms because of some of the reviews. The rate was excellent, just over $100 per night, including a full buffet breakfast. We were not disappointed. The hotel staff were very welcoming. We were allowed to check in around 9:00 a.m. after arriving from a red eye flight out of San Francisco. The room was quiet at all hours, well-appointed, and very clean. The location is excellent, just two blocks from Union Station and the Capitol. We often walked to various points of interest. Great transportation and tours are available at Union Station. The full breakfast buffet was appreciated. It was typical buffet fare and served us quite well. We did not eat other meals at the hotel. There are not a lot of restaurants in the area, but great dining is a short cab ride or walk away. We always felt safe walking the streets. We were in a room facing the firehouse and only heard the fire trucks twice in three days. We were on the sixth floor and did not hear any street noise. My advice would be to get breakfast early. The restaurant got crowded after 8:00 a.m. We always went to breakfast at 7:30 and it was fine. The public areas are very nice in the hotel and we enjoyed drinks in the bar on a couple of occasions. Drinks are expensive like in most hotel bars. The staff gladly stored our luggage on checkout. All in all, it was a great stay and I would recommend the hotel, expecially if you can get a good rate with breakfast included.

“Nice Place!” My husband and I spent 2 nights and 1 cold stormy day in Oct. 2007 at the Edgewater. We found the hotel's decor unique and impressive. We liked the in-room Starbucks coffee, the world's best showerhead, the wonderful pillows and comfortable beds, the waterfront lobby, and the free hourly shuttle service to downtown attractions. Our room faced the parking lot, not the water. A train goes by this side of the hotel several times a day (and night), but we found that the closed windows provided good soundproofing. However, if the windows are open to cool the room, the noise level would be very disturbing. Fortunately, we were aware of this problem and brought good earplugs. We understand that the waterview rooms can also be noisy due to cruise ship and barge traffic. We enjoyed our stay at the Edgewater and would return.

“Great location - loved the suite for our family” We stayed at Hotel Erwin recently and although it was not our first choice in Venice Beach, we were really impressed with the facilities of the property. As we were a family of 5, we stayed in a 1 bedroom suite, there was more than enough room for all of us, we had 1 separate bedroom with lovely comfortable king size bed, and really good linen and pillows on the bed... Our children (3 teenage girls), shared 1 queen sized sofa bed, and we also had a roll away bed. Only down side with this was the rollaway mattress was really thin and so bed a bit uncomfortable, but hey, she's 12 and didn't care all that much!! There's 1 bathroom, but good size with nice amenities. We could see Venice Beach from our room, plus we had a small deck which was nice. All in all the room was super comfortable (oh, and it had a kitchen too!), and the price was right - much cheaper than taking 2 rooms (which we had done everywhere else..). The rooftop bar was a perfect spot to finish off a great day in LA, and do a bit of people spotting, and the restaurant downstairs - served a fantastic breakfast with great service.. The area the hotel is in is slightly dingy, but it is Venice Beach, and there are a lot of shady people around, so I guess that's to be expected.

“Friendly hotel in good location” We recently stayed 3 nights at the Courtyard Marriott Times Square South. We arrived slightly ahead of check-in but it was no problem for the staff. They were always helpful with a smile on their faces. We even received a late checkout (2pm!) when we asked. The bed was super comfortable and the room and bathroom were very clean. The street itself was quiet for being so close to Times Square. The subway was just on the corner and Bryant Park was also nearby as a welcome patch of green in the city. Ate breakfast at the cafe nearby - Harrie's Bakery. All in all, good standard and friendly staff. However, not unique or exciting. Value not great, but about average price for New York weekends!

“Nice, clean hotel in great location” This was our first experience with a JW Marriott. We got a good rate with a Marriott Rewards special that they were running over the summer. So we booked it for November. The hotel was very conveniently located to all of the tourist attractions; White House, Smithsonian Museums, Memorials, and Monuments as well as numerous restaurants and stores. Also near many government office buildings and a couple of Metro stations. The hotel was large but staff was very friendly. The room was a standard city hotel size and the bathroom was on the small size. There were just two of us so the size was fine. The beds were comfortable and everything was very clean. We had a room on the 10th floor overlooking a courtyard and it was very quiet. I had requested a quiet room and this room was. The only annoyance were some inconsiderate hotel guests that let their doors bang shut. (Why can't people take an extra second and guide the door shut quietly?) We ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant the first morning. It was very good but way overpriced. The next couple of mornings we walked up the street to the Corner Bakery cafe. A much better value and good food. We did eat one dinner in the hotel restaurant and it was very good. Prices comparable to any of the nicer restaurants around. We also had drinks and apps in the bar. They had Happy Hour prices during the week which was a good value. Try the flatbread..it was delicious. If the price were right we would stay here again as the location is perfect for exploring all the DC has to offer.

“Pretty Great” Had an incredible stay this week.The hotel is almost complete with construction and Is absolutely beautiful.Upon check in we had requested and booked adjoining rooms.We were shown to the room and It wasnt adjoining.We had even asked them at the desk to confirm this and It still wasnt correct.However the bellman was so professional and offered us to sit in the room and offered to make us coffee while we waited for the desk to find our correct rooms. The rooms were located and simply perfect.The rooms are very modern and HUGE.They each have mini sub zero and miele dishwasher(not sure why anyone needs this,but Its great)The room also had a super easy espresso machines for a quick cup in the mornings.The bathrooms are awesome and my favorite part.The typical TV in mirror that you see at most upscale hotels these days(finally put one in at home)The shower and bathtub is side by side behind a glass wall.The lighting and drapes are all controlled electonically and easy to operate.The flat screen TV didnt work and the maintenence dept. came directly up with a new TV and were efficient and and quick with the installation.The staff is well trained and always greet you with a "Welcome back"each time you return. I booked a massage a was a bit disappointed.A female should always have another female show her around the spa.With that in mind,I checked in for the massage and had a very nice man show me to the door of the ladies locker room and went away.I was alone in the locker and didnt have a robe in my locker and had to get completely dressed to go back to the desk to ask where to get the robe.It was a little eerie in the locker because I was completely alone with NOBODY around. Ater a mediocre massage I was shown back to the door of the locker room.When walking back to the showers I had to weave around a group of people being given a tour of the spa,with the group of business people in suits.Those of you people who get massages understand how you look after the treatment.I felt very uncomfortable. I dont know maybe thats just me. The hotel is amazing and you wont be disappointed.Go soon before It stays booked year round as It surely will.

“Another great stay!!” We stayed for one night while attending a concert in Camden. We had a corner waterfront room and it was very nice. Size was fine and very clean. Check in and out were quick and efficient. We always stay here when we are in Philly and have yet to have any problem with the Hyatt.

“Enjoyed my stay” The Conrad is in a great location, with entrances on Rush Street and Michigan Avenue. It required two elevator rides to exit from my room to the street level, which was a little odd, but no big deal. Being on ninth floor was not high enough to avoid being awakened multiple times by sirens on Saturday night, but Sunday and Monday night were much quieter. The room was spacious and clean. A minor detail was the safe was not fastened down, but I really wasn't worried about anyone walking off with it. The room had a Keurig coffee maker (nice!) and aromatherapy products for soaps and shampoos (also nice!). There was a breakfast buffet on Sunday only--the food was good but its selections were somewhat limited compared to other hotels. The exercise room was heavy on treadmills, with only one bike. The sky-way to the mall was convenient. The highlight of the hotel was the friendly service--folks seem to genuinely like working there, which is hard to fake. I'd definitely stay there again.

“Very Nice Hotel” My husband and I stayed at the Hyatt Downtown on August 5th, our wedding. My mother and I checked in promptly at 2pm, did valet parking ($21+tip) with in-out privildges. If asked, they will park your car under their canopy, where loading and unloading of guests is, which is wonderful, at least for us, we didn't have to wait to have our car brought round. Before we checked in, I went straight to the conceirge desk and asked them for a ride to the beauty shop and they obliged. Jim was super nice as they even found the phone number and address (I left it at home). He picked us up within minutes of our call for the return to the hotel. When Mom and I checked in, they took our luggage and the gentleman at the desk upgraded me, simply because it was our wedding night, which was nice. It was a large King room. The decor was beautiful, it was very clean and nicely appointed. The bathroom was big and had wonderful ammenties Portico (I believe) was the name of the toiletries and smelled delicious! Can't go wrong with lavender. The towels were soft, the tub was large and had enough room for two comfortably ;-). The bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in, the high speed internet worked perfectly, a starbucks in the lobby. The lobby is enormous, the hotel itself is 30 stories high with the Spindletop restaurant on top (gotten to by separate elevators), so when you stand in the lobby and look up itt goes on forever! We were on the 30th floor looking out over downtown and could see Reliant Stadium from our room. I would stay there again in a heartbeat. The cons: 1.The ice maker didn't work and there was only 1 per floor that I saw. 2. We cranked the A/C down to 60 and it still never cooled properly. I'm very hot natured so that wasn't a good thing for me at all. Don't get me wrong it was ok, just not cold like at home. I think hotels should install ceiling fans in all their rooms, don't you?

“A great location and perfect spot for a Michigan Avenue stay” I've stayed here twice - once was when it was operated by Le Meridien and once as the Conrad. This hotel is perfect if you want a Michigan Avenue location, but don't want to deal with staying in a huge hotel. It has an almost residential feel, and the location is great (albiet you do have to walk through the Shops at Northbridge from Mich Ave to get to the hotel). The staff were all very friendly - front desk, housekeeping, and foodservice were all great! The rooms are very nice - but the best part HAS to be the bathrooms. They are very large, with big walk-in showers, seperate tub, etc. It's really nice to have that "master bathroom" feel when traveling. Overall, I would reccomend this hotel - it's quiet, manageable, and well-run.

“Three nights was too long” Room was noisy and had seats outside so we had to listen to some drunken argument at 2am. Expensive and the room I booked was not available upon arrival, so we had to switch after the first night.

“Gutes Hostel in SF!” Wer eine Alternative zu günstigen Hotels in San Francisco sucht, ist bei dem Vantaggio Cosmo gut aufgehoben. Die Lage in der Nähe zum Union Square ist sehr interessant und ein optimaler Ausgangspunkt um die Stadt zu erkunden. Natürlich muss man sich von der Vorstellung eines richtigen Hotels lösen, schließlich ist es mehr ein Hostel für Sprachschüler etc. Aber die Zimmer sind wirklich vollkommen ausreichend ausgestattet und die Sauberkeit ist auch in Ordnung. Wer ein bißchen auf sein Budget achten möchte ist hier definitiv richtig aufgehoben. Die Mitarbeiter wirken zwar manchmal etwas "schläfrig" sind aber sehr hilfsbereit und geben auch gute Tips.

“Hotel by the border, OK in a tight” Located in an industrial area across the border. Smelled of body odor as we entered. The room was ok. Bed was ok , bathroom had real granite. Had a refrigerator and micro in office. Good laundry room. It is one of the older HI Expresses. Has some wear. Will not stat here again unless just necessary. Old TV--no flat screen. Furniture is dated.

“Another great TA find” Based on the reviews of TA, my daughter and I stayed at the Distrikt hotel during a recent college touring visit. We chose the hotel based on the location as well as the ease of access to public transport. We were pleasantly surprised to find it comfortable, clean, well staffed, and pleasant all the way around. My daughter in particular found it much more personable and welcoming than the larger brand name hotels that we've stayed in around Times Sq in the past. Appreciated small details like the morning coffee, afternoon iced tea, access to breakfast or snacks in the hotel bar, and the proximity to the subway and Port Authority. Staff will put you to ease at once, and are helpful in almost every way a traveler can hope for. Will definitely stay again.

“disappointed with the W” If you like dark hallways and ever present techno rock,this place is for you. The computers were supposedly down the weekend that I stayed at this hotel and checking in and out was a nightmare. There do not appear to be any grown ups in charge and the staff has way too much attitude. Rooms are ridiculously small,sound proofing is nil and my teenage son did not appreciate the see-through bathroom doors. The location is good but don't expect to get any rest at this hotel.

“Looks Great, Nothing Works, Inexperienced Staff with Young Person's Disease” The Hotel is a Kimpton with some cool amenities - like a FedEx envelope hanging with the laundry bag, an umbrella in the closet, and the Book of the Buddah in the drawer with the Bible. However, it took five requests over two days to get the staff to fix the outlet in the bathroom, housekeeping didn't clean our room on our second day, and our voice mail didn't work. Further, the breakfast sternos went out and the food was ice cold - instead of replacing it with properly heated food, the staff answer was to add another sterno - which is a big no-no in food safety once the food has cooled. Bacteria city. But the staffer was watching TV and eating her OWN breakfast in front of guests, so we assumed she didn't realize she could be poisoning us. The response from staff to all complaints was to assume that we were doing something wrong (eg: did you press the reset button? did you push your message button? did you leave your do not disturb sign on?) The staff answer to the housekeeping problem was that we vacate the room instead of dressing for dinner because the housekeeping staff leaves at 5:00. It took three phone calls for the front desk to finally get that we, as guests, viewed the housekeeping issue as their responsibility and that they should address it after we left for dinner. Overall, the staff seemed friendly but poorly trained, and not old or experienced enough to address any difference in what they expected to happen. This created a sort of sassy, glib attitude that was not appropriate when nothing worked.

“OK hotel, but you can see it's age” I was hear for bussiness for two nights. The staff was very friendly and professional and very helpful with any questions that we had. The rooms have aged, the furniture and bed was OK, nothing special, but not gross by any means. The bathroom is old, paint peeling off the walls, the shower fixture was really wobbly, and the toilet had this very high pitched scream when flushed. The restaurant was OK, two sodas and a candy bar is $8 in the gift shop. If the rate is cheap I would stay here again, but I wouldn't use this hotel for bussiness.

“great location, great price” I just returned from a trip to NYC and a stay at both the Ramada Eastside and the W hotel-Union Square. For the record, I have stayed at this Ramada two times before (in the span of the last two years) and did not have any of the negative experiences as mentioned in other travelers' posts. I was very pleased with the new memory foam mattress in my room at the Ramada, it was actually more comfortable than the mattress at the W! I do also want to mention, that the rooms at the Ramada are small, and the decor is a little worn, but for the price, you can't beat it! The location is central to everything and in my opinion, it is a extra added bonus that it is located in a mainly -residential area. I will also echo the sentiments of earlier posts about the Brasil Coffee shop and the Trattoria Belvedere next door. Both were outstanding! Especially the Trattoria!! The owner was very gracious considering the fact that we were a party of 8 (including two children) with no reservation - we were seated immediately!! The food was spectacular - this coming from a family of italians! Be sure to visit if you can, and leave room for the homemade Tiramisu - it's on the house!

“OUTSTANDING Stay. Lives up to the Omni name!” Okay, first a few things out of the way.... I am not a hotel employee. I am a real business and pleasure traveler just like you who has had the opportunity to stay at many hotels over the course of a year. Check my other reviews on TripAdvisor. I do a rather good job of telling things as they are. When I stay at a hotel, I usually pick one that falls in the mid-price range. You know, the hotels that give you the best bang for the buck. For years my favorite hotel brand was Marriott. Can't beat their hotels. However, since doing more business conventions, I have found myself staying at Omni hotels. First, the one in Atlanta and now Indianapolis. Quite frankly, if you are not here on business, I can't for the life of me think why anyone would come to Indianapolis. It's a nice city. Very clean. Nothing to see or do except perhaps the zoo or a football game. On my free day, I walked around the entire day and found nothing overly exciting here. There are, however, very good restaurants close to the hotel. Oh, back to the hotel.... They say the first impression is a lasting one. From the moment I arrived, I felt I was being treated like a VIP. I stepped out of the town car (Carey Indiana - EXCELLENT) and there were several bellboys at the door entrance eager to assist and open the door for me. I walk in, and there is a very lovely woman bidding me "Good Morning." I get to the desk, and though I am several hours early, I am quickly checked in and handed a room key. Since I was here on business, I booked three rooms for myself and my partners. They were all under my name, yet the hotel desk was very good about assigning the rooms to my partners and making certain that we were located together. My room was on the 11th floor, 1110. It was practically next to the elevator. Complaints have run amok here that the rooms in this Omni are small. I suspect so, due to the fact that this a hotel that was converted from something else. However, if you book a room with double beds (instead of a King) you are getting a larger room, essentially going from 180 to 244 square feet. So, the double bed room that I had didn't especially seem tiny at all. Perhaps the bathroom is smaller than I have seen elsewhere, but I made perfectly do with the space I had available. The room was very clean. Lots of closet space, an iron and electronic safe in the room. The television was a Panasonic flat screen HD. I don't know what signal the hotel is getting, but the picture pixelated often even though the weather was fine. They really need to do something about their TV signal. One thing everyone must do is join their rewards program. It is free by going to the Omni website. It allows you free WiFi and complimentary beverage in the morning delivered to your room. I am guessing I am at the second-tier GOLD status. I love the fact that before I go to sleep I fill out a little form requesting a carafe of coffee, juice or water to be sent to my room and when I wake up, there is a little tray outside my door along with a newspaper. All that is totally complimentary just because I am a rewards member. I think, even at the bottom rung of the program, you get all those amenities. Certainly something more than I get from something like the Marriott. Bed was very comfortable. Lots of pillows. A plug next to it to charge my iPhone. A desk with plug outlets. Very, very nice indeed. If I have ONE complaint it's the loud air-conditioning in the room. It turns on and off according to the thermostat settings. Of course, many of us like a cold room to snuggle beneath the covers with. The thermostat goes to 60 degrees. However, every time the air conditioning comes on, it makes a loud, grinding noise that makes sleeping impossible. So, I pretty much had to turn the air conditioner off at night. If hotel management is reading this (and I am certain they are), I am hoping you can fix the air conditioner noise in that room by the time I return next year. Another problem (not the fault of the hotel) is the noise from the street below. My window was facing the Claddagh Irish Pub. On the weekends, it is a noisy hotspot. Now, on the 11th floor it really didn't bother me. However, I feel sorry for those on the lower floors. There is no escaping that noise. And really, there is no escaping street noise as the hotel is surrounded by nightlife activity practically on all sides. If I can sneak one more problem in the mix it would be the elevators. There are only two that I know of off of the lobby. They are small. They are rather slow. During conventions (and remember, there are conventions here almost weekly) those elevators turn into local cars that stop at every floor and get crowded rather quickly. We were fortunate enough to snag the breakfast package for our stay. Usually breakfast costs $17 for the buffet, we got it at an extra room rate of $10 per night. Totally worth it. Nice selection of fruits, yogurts, breads, cereals, eggs, sausage and bacon, french toast or pancakes (alternates by day) and an omelet station where a cook makes them fresh for you. My favorite was the biscuits and gravy that were available every morning. If you don't get the breakfast package and want to eat cheaper, you don't have to walk far to find an eatery. Back to the hotel.... On my final morning, I had shared car service waiting with Carey Indiana. I am standing outside of the hotel with my luggage at 5:40am. The bellboy was extremely helpful in making certain that I got to my town care as generally, they can drive up to any one of two locations at the hotel. He went out of his way to look for the car and alert the driver of my presence. It was another one of those special moments where I felt like, "Wow, they really are attentive to people's needs here." So, as you probably have gathered by now, I highly recommend this hotel. Yeah, I have read a few of the negative reviews posted on TripAdvisor -- and I am certain they are legitimate complaints -- but I would have to side with many more that are giving the highest accolades to this hotel and their service. From the moment you arrive, the staff goes out of their way to open doors for you and make you feel welcome. I look forward to returning next September. For dinner we thoroughly enjoyed Harry & Izzy's, a few feet from the hotel, which has an excellent variety of food at reasonable prices and casual attire. We also ate at the Brazilian Steakhouse, Fogo de Chao, which is a 5-minute walk. If you have never tried a Brazilian Steakhouse, this is the world's most renowned chain. We even enjoyed milkshakes at Steak & Shake across the street. Damn good -- eat with a spoon -- you get a very large glass topped with whip cream and a cherry for $3.95. Tremendous bargain, and really, I was surprised how good they were. The Circle Center Mall is connected by a skyway. To be honest, nothing really special about this mall. Not even an Apple store inside. The mall was mostly dead, and nothing really caught my eye about it. Of course, all the hotels in the area connect to the Indianapolis Convention Center by a sky walkway. However, taking that walkway from the Omni to the Convention Center will waste 12 minutes of your life. A horribly, long haul that takes you through the mall and beside a parking garage. However, you can get to the convention center in 4 minutes if you simply walk outside and across South Illinois and South Capitol streets.

“Boutique hotel lover says "great!"” I admit, I'm a stickler when it comes to hotels, particularly when they are chain hotels. I have to say, however, the Marriott Long Wharf has got it down. Clean, cheerful rooms, great location right in town, on the water, and not at all noisy. Cheerful, informed staff. Well-planned bathrooms, empty refrigerators to store your doggie-bags and water in, wonderful restaurant, well-decorated and planned public spaces, easy to get a cab or the T, a short walk to the North End and Italian section of town and literally across the street from Fanueil Hall, the aquarium, the harbor.....now if they could just get the "Big Dig" completed.......

“Nice hotel - will consider coming back” Overall, this is a nice hotel. Our stay was comfortable. The bedroom is not that big, but is decent. The suite takes bigger area and is nice to have. Balcony is decent size. Its location is close to many local shops. Bed could be firmer. There is a safe in the room too. Internet is only free in the lobby. The hotel has daily afternoon snack time at which time many guests gather at their bar to enjoy chips, snacks free. It is more of a golfer hotel as many golfers stay there for their golf course. I will consider it and stay there again if I don't have anything better when it is time.

“Nice room/good location” Super efficient staff starting w/valet-luggage; reception and an exceptionally efficient/knowledgeable concierge (3 of them alternate shifts!). Rooms clean & nice size. Location convenient. Hotel restaurant excellent w/noted chef. Bay Trans (617 872 0496) dependable (posh vans) & reasonable if you need shuttle service to/from airport or cruise terminal

“Another good stay.” Hotel was comfortable and experience was as good as the last time. I was able to secure a late check out (2pm) and was given a nice high room. The only negative aspects to the hotel was the air con in the room did not work well. Although it was March, the room was surprisingly warm and I could not get cool air to come through the vent. However this may have been a local fault and I should have really phoned reception to sort it (It really wasn't that bad). The second negative aspect was no free internet access in the business lounge. This is not good. Budget hotels including Holiday Inn Express offer this service, so not sure why the Crowne Plaza cannot. Otherwise the experience was excellent. The room had 2 double beds an immaculate bathroom with a bath and the room was a decent size on the 39th Floor. There was a large LCD TV with lots of channels that I was able to hook my portable DVD player to. Room service was reasonably priced with a wide selection of food. Location is great just to the North of the Centre of Times Square. There are 2 subway stations within 2 minutes of the hotel (49th St on the N-R Line and 50th St on the 1 Local train line). There is a large pool and gym (which I did not use). I have lost my Platinum status of Priority club (owing to not getting enough points in 2010) which meant loss of access to the top floor lounge where complimentary drinks and snacks are served. The staff were very friendly and helpful and the bar area lively and well used. I would definetly recommend this hotel to any one who wishes to visit NYC. Location wise, you will struggle to beat this. I will definetly stay here again, and hope to get a room with a view of Times Square next time.

“Very nice Holiday Inn - Great staff” Checked in at 8am - No Problem Great Business Center Great Breakfast Hotel was excellent for the price paid, room was very clean, staff was friendly & helpful. Will stay here again.

“Dangerous Security at the Sheraton Gateway LAX” I have visited the Sheraton Gateway LAX over two dozen nights a year for the past several years. The rooms are generally average and the location, on Century Boulevard, is very convenient to anyone requiring access to the LAX airport. This present trip, however, has demonstrated to me how far the standards at this hotel have dropped. I was given a room with a broken tv which could not be fixed which meant that I had to pack my belongings again and move to another room (with no help offered by the hotel). I was then given a room which was subsequently assigned to another guest. While I was sitting, partially unclothed, at the workdesk another customer opened the door with a magnetic key and entered the room! It seems they had given the same room to two people. When I contacted the front desk the manager on duty told me how embarassed he had been when he realized that two people had been assigned to the same room. Why he did not call the room when he realized this mistake remains a mystery. I waited in the lobby with all of my luggage over 30 minutes to be given a new room. I have asked to discuss this security breach with the General Manager of this property but he has been unresponsive. I am attaching a few photos of the room I was given to help demonstrate the failing standards of this property.

“Excelent Location” This is an old style hotel that still keeps its old arquitecture and decorationut. The rooms and bathrom are small but clean. Although the Restaurant was closed for renovation they offer some options for Breakfast. The staff is great with good customer focus Just two blocks from Union Square.

“not too impressed with the breakfast” Average is all i can say for this property. Staff was great though and room was always clean when i got back to it. i went down for breakfast once and it was not very good, so i never went back down. if you have stayed in a homewood suites before then you know what you get and it is the same here. as some mentioned it is difficult to get to but it is doable. i would also avoid the outback that is nearby. seperate review to follow. there is a much better Texas Roadhouse across the highway. again, seperate review to follow. i will stay here again because i am a hilton fan and it is close to where i work when i travel to Phoenix.

“Nice Place for One Night” I stayed here one night. It was very convenient to the Airport. The shuttle was quick and the service was friendly. There are restaurants nearby. The hotel was very clean. Breakfast was somewhat limited in selection. Only negative was that the walls were thin - I could hear the person in the next room coughing.
“The Kimpton Way” very frequently travel - awesome hotel, clean and very comfortable bed. Perfect location, short walk to market and in the middle of downtown.

“Nice room with a view” We stayed one night in this busy but clean hotel in the heart of Soho and just blocks from Little Italy and Chinatown. The friendly desk staff urged us to delay check-in so they could finish preparing a room on the corner of the 15th floor with a really nice view of the Empire State and Chrysler buildings and other Midtown landmarks. A great scene to clock out and wake up to. Rates are reasonable for Manhattan and the trappings are about what you'd expect if you've stayed at other Hampton Inns. Minor quibble: the heater/air conditioner was a little loud. Uptown subway is three blocks away and cabs are easy to flag down on 6th Avenue or Broadway. Build in 20-30 mins. if you're heading to Rockefeller Center, Lincoln Center, Central Park or other such addresses.

“Fun had by all!” Two of my college girlfriends and I stayed here August 5-7. The hotel has king, two doubles or two twin rooms. I will say the rooms are your standard NYC room, meaning on the smaller size and definitely not your big chain hotel size room. We had a King room and a room with tow doubles. The king had much more room than the queen, even room for a pack and play if you needed to place one in the room. The king room als had a "makeup" table with a lit mirror in front of it. The double room had something similar. Our double had two closets one for hanging clothes and the other had the safe and shelves. I will say that the shower in our double was too powerful. It was good for washing my thick hair, but not for sensitive skin areas. There was always plenty of hot water and the room was clean. The A/C was a little different in that you had window units in each room. Luckily, we had a new unit and it cooled well, but it felt humid in the room. However, my friend's room had an older unit and it did not cool very well or remove the humidity. My only complaint would be that these were supposed to be non-smoking rooms, but as soon as we went in you could smell the lingering smell of smoke. The hotel also has free continental breakfast, but we wanted something a little more substantial so I can not speak to the quality of the breakfast. As far as the location goes , it was excellent. It is located on the northwest corner of Washington Park. You walk across the street and you can hang out in the park. The fountain is fun for kids to splash and play in. It is only a half block or less to the Metro. You have so many good restaurants and sweet shops in the village. Fish was a good restaurant for dinner, as was Union Square Cafe, the Bagel shop had wonderful breakfast bagels. The western omelet bagel was delicious. You can walk from the hotel to chinatown, Soho, Noho. Overall good location for visiting NYC. Plus you are not in the hubbub of Midtown. The staff was very helpful with taxis, food ideas and shopping ideas.
“Great location” Not one of the most upscale Hilton's but certainly not near the bottom of the dated Hilton brand. Great location and great night's rest. Very convenient to airport. Recommended.

“Quick Business Trip” I stayed here on a quick business trip, and was very happy with my stay. It's in a quite part of the city, and the rooms were larger than some of the rooms I have stayed in at other New York hotels. The rooms were clean and the beds were comfortable. We did have a little trouble getting a cab in the morning, so I would recommend calling a car service if you need to get to the Airport in the morning. I would definitely recommend staying here again.

“Above Avg Hotel, Great location” I switched to this hotel on a recent business trip as it was closer and better suited to the business I was doing while in LA than the other hotel I had stayed at. I found some great things here: 1) The location was not only close to the business that I was there to attend to, but there was also ample things to do in the area within 1 square mile - movies, restaurants, shopping, etc. Was very close to a lot. 2) My parking was comped at the end of my stay as a courtesy - which I certainly appreciated :) Self parking is in a parking garage close to the hotel and requires an outside walk, which for the most part isn't that bad since you're in LA...but when raining was a little hassle. 3) You could tell that the facilities and rooms had recently been redone - carpets were new, furniture looked newer (not brand new), and furnishings in the lobby looked new. 4) There was a Starbucks in the lobby...always a plus. 5) The fitness center was located within the same area as the pool, and to get to it was very odd. Overall, this was a pretty decent hotel and I would stay there on my next trip to the area.

“We felt like Royalty” I would first like to thank all of the front desk staff at the hotel for their utmost professional attitudes upon checking in. It is to be expected of a hotel of this calibur to receive the best hospitality in the nation and they did not fail. I was always under the impression that the hotel rooms in NYNY were "the size of shoe boxes" however we were given a room that had 2 queen beds fit for Royalty. We received an early checkin on a Sunday mid morning and when arriving in the hotel lobby we got to look at the wonderful Sunday Bruch that the hotel provided (at a cost).
