This was an enchanting sight! Crab Legs, Oysters on the half shell, and on and on. What a wonderful stay we had and I would stay here again whenever visiting NYNY again. Thank you!

“Excellent for the price.” I just returned from a three-night stay for business and will most likely stay there again on my next trip. I chose the hotel for the excellent rates and the positive reviews, which I found to be accurate. They've recently done a renovation, so the room I had was extremely fresh and clean. It felt warm and inviting and more like a room in a home than in a hotel. After check-in, I did have a glitch, initially, in that i discovered my first room hadn't been fully cleaned (everything was done but they forgot the bathroom!) The gaffe was handled quickly and considerately and they were even kind enough to provide me with a mini-bar credit as a consolation for the inconvenience. I thought this was more than enough but the next evening I found a hand-written note of apology, bottle of wine and chocolates in my room, as well! The staff are very polite, thoughtful, friendly and seem to genuinely enjoy their jobs. The decor is tasteful and fun. While the room service menu seems somewhat limited, if you ask, they will happily bring you the full menu from the restaurant below. On another note, just a heads-up if you're on a tight schedule: my first wake-up call was delivered by a live person and was a bit late so I switched to requesting an automated wake-up call for the duration of my stay and those were quite punctual. The location is great for pleasure but a little bit out of the way for business. Still, it wasn't too far and I found the area lovely. Again, I am almost certain I will stay here again -- it was a very nice experience overall.

“Excellent views, great neighborhood, relatively small room . . .” My husband and I stayed here in December 2011. The hotel was at that point just transitioning to becoming a member of the "Standard" family. (It had previously been something else.) From what I could tell, most of the rooms were going to stay the same, but there would be some upgrading of the lobby. Our room was very compact (although it was a normal size for many New York hotels). There was room for a king-size bed, room to walk around the bed, and room for a small desk and wardrobe. However, it had floor-to-ceiling windows, and amazing views of the city (we had a corner room on around the 16th floor), which made the room seem less small. Unfortunately, there was a TV on a stand right in front of the window, which blocked a lot of the view, but we moved the TV on the floor for our stay. The bed was fine. There was a bathtub, but it was small and not a particularly enjoyable bathing option. The big draw here for me is the neighborhood. But be careful if you gravitate toward the upper East Side -- the East Village is definitely not everyone's cup of tea. Some might find it a little too transitional. Staff was friendly, and the lobby area was nice to sit in for a while. I preferred working there to working in the room (where desk faced the wall and was small). Wifi worked well in the hotel.

“ボストン美術館鑑賞の拠点に” プルデンシャルセンターに隣接し、ボストンのショッピングやグルメを目一杯楽しめます。 ボストンは175ドル以下の衣類や靴には税金がかからないので、東海岸の隠れたショッピングシティでも あるのですが、シェラトン隣接のプルデンシャルモールには有名ショップや地元のレストランも多数入りここでも十分楽しめます。またボストン美術館も徒歩圏なので、ここを拠点に数日に分けて美術館を堪能するのをお勧めします。 お部屋は至ってシンプル、28平米と若干狭く感じますが、清潔感はありますがやや古くも感じました。

“Grand really just says it all!” I love the Grand Hyatt. It is in the center of downtown and is big enough that it's easy to come and go anonymously, which I consider refreshing. My room had floor to ceiling windows facing West and featured a parlor area with a love seat chair and ottoman, an expansive restroom with plush towels and a bedroom alcove in the back. There was a phone in each room (including the restroom) and a large TV in both the bedroom and parlor areas. The bathtubs are luxuriously deep, the fitness center is huge and they'll loan you workout clothes if you forget yours. They also feature an ah inducing spa tub, sauna and a steam room (a rarity in Seattle). At 3:30pm the front desk called to see when/ if I intended to check out, allowing me ample time to gather my wits about me and depart in an orderly manner. My favorite thing about the Hyatt is the size of it and easy access around the clock.

“Great view!” Stayed at the Hilton Times Square with my mother during the New York City portion of our vacation. (We spent a few days in NYC and then went to California to finish out the remainder of the trip.) We stayed 3/4 through 3/6. Check-in started out a bit rough. When I made my reservations I requested an early check in and I called the day before to verify and I was told that it would be no problem. We show up at the hotel and we were very rudely informed that we could NOT check in early. I nicely explained that we had been promised an early check in because we had a business meeting we had to get ready for but the female desk clerk refused to help us. We ended up just taking over the ladies room in the lobby and with the help of a VERY patient bellman (Caesar) we found all the clothes and makeup we needed to get ready for the meeting. Without the help bellman Caesar I don't know what we would have done! Anyway, when we were finally able to check into the room we were on the 37th floor. We had an AMAZING view of the city looking downtown. The view made us forget about the trouble we had checking in. The room was nice, slightly larger than the room we normally have at the Sofitel (the hotel where we usually stay.) The beds were pretty comfortable and the hotel was quiet. With the exception of the desk clerk we encountered the staff was very friendly. There needed to be more vanity space in the bathroom and the only mirror in the room was in the bathroom. There needed to be one in the "main room". All in all it was a nice stay and the hotel was nice. I'm sure I'll stay there again.

“Wow! What a room. What a view!” This is a really great hotel. First the view was spectacular--Coit Tower in the foreground, Alcatrez to the left and the slopes of Russian Hill and Nob Hill to the left. To the right is the bay and the Ferries. In the distance rise the mountains. Simply fantastic! (These were "bay view" rooms. Obviously not all rooms had this view.) The location was also wonderful. Chinatown is in front of the hotel. North Beach starts just to the right and Market Street and the Financial District are just to the left. Behind you is the Embarcaderro. The room and hotel decor is very stylish and modern, giving this rather large hotel the feel of a smaller upscale boutique hotel. The rooms are not large, but are thoughtfully laid out so that they feel quite comfortable and have very nice work space and bathrooms. Loved the flat screen TV's and the sliding door to the bathroom. The staff was fine, but I didn't have any food or room service. I really enjoyed my stay there--too bad it was for one night only.

“nice hotel with a few problems” Stayed here for a conference in Chicago. Pros: Great breakfast buffet. Managers reception is very nice too. Beds were comfortable. Elevators are fast. Cons: Housekeeping needs improvement. Asked the lady if she would clean our room next. She said yes. So I left for a short while. When I came back our room was not done. So I found the lady once again just one room down from ours. I asked her if she would clean ours next which she replied yes she would. I left again for a few hours. When I came back our room was not cleaned. So I waited a few hours thinking she just got busy and forgot. At about 3pm I went down to the front desk. I told them about housekeeping. They sent someone up to clean it. 45 minutes later the room was cleaned. Make sure to check your receipt before you leave. We received someone elses receipt. Along with a bill for internet charged to our CC. Internet was included in our stay. Had we not checked that they would have charged our cc. I wonder how many people do not check their receipts and get billed for things they thought were included in their stay. Heard sirens all day long.

“Pretty good...but be sure to get a room on the east side of the hotel” I can't complain, really, as I got a last-minute deal here via Priceline. The hotel is everything you'd think a hotel in its price range would be: super clean, super efficient, friendly. The complimentary breakfast alone would cost you $25 if you had to pay for it; a real feast! Very roomy. If you do stay, book a room on the east side of the hotel. Why? On the west side, the lights are a-blazing 24/7 (curtains effectively blocked the light), and there is a view of the highway next door, ie, you'll hear it. There IS free parking immediately on the west side of the hotel, but there are only about 20 spots; I was quite lucky to get one. Otherwise, you'll have to pay $32 overnight valet, which is exorbitant, I think, by any standard.

“Convenient but not worth the money” The lobby, pool and bar are a very pleasant setting with lots of greenery and comfortable seating. However, internet access is not included in the room rate and there is no breakfast. In addition, the water restrictors they have put in the sink faucets cut the water flow so drastically, you have to chase the water drops around to wet your toothbrush. Shower was adequate. Rooms are small and dark. Shuttle to airport was fast and efficient.

“Very Nice and Clean Hotel” The hotel is well-situated on the northern strip of Michigan avenue just next to the Hancock building. You are a block away from access to the beach area and waterfront if you walk further north, and all of the shopping is within walking distance. Guest service is knowledgeable of the area and staff is friendly and helpful. My eighth floor room was very comfortable. I have stayed in more luxurious hotels in Chicago (ie-Meridian), but the Westin is a solid, value-based bet.

“Surprisingly good stay” I had the chance to bring my teenage daughter to the city to see FENCES with Denzel Washington and needed a place to stay one night. Room rates were high in the city and Hotel Pennyslvania had the lowest rates - $125 for 2 beds. I was wary since I was familar with its reputation but booked it. We were pleasantly surprised with the stay. We checked in at 6 pm and the check in line moved quickly, but a young lady named Raquel came and got us out of line and brought us to another area to check us in even quicker. She was very friendly and gave us some background about the hotel and how much she liked working there. (Really? How often does that happen?) Our room was what I had expected - but cleaner. It was simply furnished -2 beds a desk, dresser and nightstand with mismatched but functional furniture. Old style tv, but if you are coming to NYC to watch tv, you should stay home. The beds were twin beds but comfortable. The bathroom was clean but the paint was peeling and there was a bit of an odd stain on the ceiling. However, there was great water pressure and hot water right away. I was surprised at how quiet it was at night since the lobby is a loud, crowded town square sort of place. No coffee maker in the room but the coffee shop in the lobby had great coffee and a very friendly group of workers. We stored our bags for the day for $4 and that worked perfectly. We had a great breakfast at a small convience store/deli for $3 each just a few blocks away.

“Confortable” L’hôtel est un bâtiment de 10 étages, d’architecture plutôt européenne, situé au carrefour de Berverly Bld et La Cienaga, dans un environnement sans intérêt, Beverly Hills est à 2 ou 3 km.. En face de l’hotel, l’immense bloc de béton de Bloomingdales, il faut donc prendre une chambre située à l’arrière de l’hôtel qui donne sur les collines d’Hollywood. Le hall d’entrée est superbe avec une sculpture contemporaine. J’avais réservé une suite, organisée autour de trois espaces qui communiquent deux à deux via des portes coulissantes. Cela donne une circulation fluide et très agréable. L’ameublement et la décoration sont très soignées, harmonie de couleurs, tout le confort, machine expresso, 2 TV, une chaine Hi Fi, de grands fauteuils et un grand canapé, un bureau pour travailler avec la WI FI rapide et stable. La salle de bains avec deux douches est très grande, seul défaut, les toilettes et le dressing sont dans cet espace ce qui n’est pas toujours très pratique. Quelques défauts : à propos du lit : Généralement les lits dans les Sofitel sont très confortables, ce n’était pas le cas, le lit m’a semblé très usagé. L’insonorisation vis-à-vis de l’extérieure est parfaite mais ce n’est pas le cas entre les chambres, j’entendais la musique de mon voisin (qui devait être très forte) et la douche d’un autre voisin. Le bar et les salons sont superbes, avec des livres sur Hollywood. Le fitness est bien équipé, et la piscine est plutôt là pour patauger pas pour nager. Le Valet Parking est très cher (33 $) mais la solution proposée par un avis Trip Advisor est parfaite (le parking gardé de Cedar Sinai Hospital de nuit (10 $) et de CVS de jour(gratuit)

“Not your average Hampton Inn” Travelled to NYC for one night, solo, for a theater performance in Soho, and chose the Hampton Inn for its location near the theater. Getting to the hotel in a cab was a bit of a problem due to the traffic jammed up on Watts St waiting to get to the Holland Tunnel. When I left the following day, the lack of a doorman to help me get a cab was a bit of a problem. The cost of my room was the same that I would have paid at a more full service hotel, so I was a bit disappointed with this lack of service. That complaint aside, the front desk staff was very nice, and my room was comfortable and had an excellent view out to the Empire State Bldg. As others have mentioned, the location was great for walking around Soho. The complimentary breakfast bar was fine, pretty standard Hampton Inn fare. I suspect that there are better hotel choices in the neighborhood, and will shop around a bit more next time.

“Yuck. Avoid unless homeless.” Old, run-down, not clean, overpriced. We are travelers who don't mind small, budget or older lodging, but this was really unpleasant all the way around. Had the 2-bedroom apartment (reminded me of some of the cheap apartments I had to rent as a poor college student) updated in the 70's, perhaps. Air conditioner didn't work, so it was extremely stuffy all night, noises from neighbors on balcony precluded opening windows for ventilation, and paper-thin walls which let us hear the snorer next door made it not a good sleep. There was very old furniture and the unit was not maintained. The office smelled heavily of smoke, though the surly clerk insisted it was a non-smoking hotel. Cramped little breakfast room with packets of oatmeal, cereal, and the smell of smoke. Bottom line, only if you can get an extremely low price ($50-60?) and have nowhere else to go, might it be worth it.

“Good Option for Century City/BH area” I've come to love the Courtyard properties. They are all pretty consistent and it's nice to have the Courtyard Bistro on site. I was in the Century City/Beverly Hills area for a conference. All the hotels are completely overpriced, this Courtyard included. But, it seemed the best value. The lobby and Bistro areas were clean, modern and comfortable as always. My room was a fairly good size and bed was comfortable. They have a small outdoor (enclosed) fitness room with a few pieces of equipment - adequate for me. As always, the staff was friendly and accomodating. The hotel is within walking distance of the Westfield Mall.

“Lovely hotel” We spent four nights here and had a great time. Location was perfect: we could either walk everywhere or use the buses which are regular and incredibly cheap at two dollars for 24 hours. The suite was very spacious and lacked for nothing. Very comfortable seats in the living area and the bed was also comfortable. Air con was easy to control and quiet. Structure of the building which had an internal atrium also provided great views. Three lifts were very fast: the hotel was full and we never had to wait long for a lift to arrive or get us to our suite on the seventh floor. There is an efficient coin operated laundry which is very useful if you are on a long vacation. Breakfast was cooked to order by very efficient, pleasant staff, and the happy hour/ managers reception early evening was a good prelude to going out to our evening meal. We noticed that a lot of people seemed to enjoy the food which accompanied the free beer and wine,but we did not need this. The iced water flavoured with fruits available in the lobby was a lovely touch. Housekeeping was excellent and on the one day we got back and our rooms hadn't been done(which was probably due to us being in them in the middle of the day), a phone call to the front desk produced the maid within two minutes. The standard of the in room tea and coffee supplies were excellent. My husband used the pool and tub each day and enjoyed them. We had a great time in Austin and would strongly recommend this hotel.

“Very NIce” I like Hilton Garden Inns in general, the services available for the price you pay are quite a bargain. The staff at this HGI was very nice, attentive and accomodating. I would stay there again.

“Great hotel near Waldorf” I have stayed here and at the Waldorf and this hotel is so much nicer. The rooms are fairly big for New York wtih ample room in the bathroom. The beds are comfortable and the rooms are clean. All the amenities are up-to-date.

“Great stay at the Wit” My husband and I stayed over July 16-18. I should note that we were using his Hilton points and I don't know if we would have paid the full price otherwise. The lobby, hallways, and rooms were beautiful. We were given a corner room and there was a window in our bathroom with an absolutely spectacular view of downtown Chicago, overlooking south over the Chicago Theatre. The bed was comfortable although I will say that it was hard to sleep during an afternoon nap because were across from the laundry room. The location of the Wit cannot be beat - the El is ride outside the front door. Getting to and from Midway was a snap. Lots of restaurants and bars within a short walk away. Since we were using Hilton points, upon check-in we were given the option of free breakfast, internet, or Hilton points and we chose the free breakfast. We were given vouchers to use at the hotel restaurant, State & Lake. We only had breakfast one of the mornings but it was great! We also had lunch at the restaurant on one of the days, and it was very good and reasonably priced. Unfortunately, we did not make it up to the Roof (even though literally everyone we told we were staying at the Wit told us how beautiful it was). We were in town for a music festival and hadn't brought clothes nice enough to pass the dresscode. We're not fancy people but I really would have liked to see the view from up there. Oh well. Maybe next time. All in all, we were thrilled with our stay, but the best part was that it was free! We'd definitely go back if the price was right....but more likely, we'll wait for another Hilton promotion!

“good value but nothing special” got a room with time square view times square is very far and my room wasnt exactly in the corner of the hotel so my view was there but very unimpressive ,doesnt worth the extra money lobby in upper floor ,small rooms with low ceiling very nice terrace for drinks only stay here if its your less expensive option

“Loved this hotel” I stayed one night (October 2008) and just adored it. The company who flew me to Houston had already booked me into another hotel for the following night and because of a change of plans I had to come in a day earlier, but couldn't get a room at the original hotel for that first night. So I found this online and even though it was pricey, it was near where I needed to be in the morning, so I went for it (however, I spoke with a couple at the bar who were paying nearly half of what I did and they said they booked it through the hotel's website as well, so not sure what the problem for me was!) What I found refreshing here was that it had all the charm that the "big box" hotels lack. It is located in an old bank building and the architecture details inside all around are lovely, including the large vault door behind the reception desk. I found everyone on the staff that I came in contact with from the desk to the breakfast waiter to be courteous. The room (915) was spacious and cozy at the same time. It lacked nothing and the bathtub was incredible - one of those that you can sink into the water up to your neck. I know they feature "spa" bath services, but I did not take advantage of this. The shower was huge and I had to actually dial back the water pressure - it was too much! And the shampoo/cream rinse/body wash in the shower was a nice touch. My only complaint is that the lighting in the bathroom was rather dim, but at least there was a lighted magnifying mirror to help make up for that. Everything was very clean and the bed comfortable. I had dinner at the bar downstairs (which is very nice and I loved the decor, although on a Friday night, it is populated with an interesting crowd) and the food was very good. The bartender had no problem giving me a small pitcher of half & half to take back to my room (which I stored in the mini bar) to have with my coffee in the morning. The coffee service in the room was actually good (I don't usually even bother with them as most are terrible). In the morning the hotel provided a free shuttle to the convention center - I felt rather special pulling up in a chauffeur driven Mercedes SUV all by my lonesome. I was sad to have to change hotels. I would absolutely stay there again, but try for a lower rate like the folks I met at the bar!

“Great Stay” My wife and I stayed there one night right before Thanksgiving. We got a deal for $79, and they even let us check in the morning when we came by to drop off our bags, which made things much easier. The room was spacious, had a couch, and was very quiet. We liked that the bed was off to the side separated by a partial wall from the door. The breakfast in the morning was very good by the standards of these sort of hotels. The location was excellent. We'd stay there again, especially if we got such a good rate.

“Minutes from the Main Mall” We purposely wanted a hotel very close to the monuments and the Smithsonian and the L'Enfant was a good choice. It's just a short walk to the that and the grassy mall that connects the Capitol to the Washington Monument. The hotel sits atop an office building and occupies the upper three floors. The lobby has many comfy chairs and couches, which were taken early each morning by the various officials that obviously stay there when visiting. Lots of people in business attire. We were there for sightseeing and dressed as such for a May day. The room was large and clean. It had a pool atop and the lobby contained a nice gift shop. We ate every dinner at the Foggy Bottom restaurant off the lobby, which offered reasonable and tasty sandwiches, salads and hot entrees. There's a Starbucks kiosk which was jammed each morning so we just got a muffin and used the in-room coffeemaker instead. The view of the Potomac from the room was terrific (see photo). Under the hotel is a mini-mall with delis ahd shops, open during business hours only. So plan accordingly, if you want to buy anything, like a bagel for breakfast the following day. We stayed for four days and walked our legs off, but there are shuttle buses available. Check in with your state Senator for Captol tour passes when booking your vacation. We got to sit in on a senate hearing. Very interesting. But the main advantage is the good location. We will recommend it to our friends and anyone else, in the future.

“Decent for a short stay, but hard beds!” The hotel is in a decent location, close to downtown Austin and easy to get to from the Austin airport. It is located on an access road off the highway, not exactly the best scenery around! Staff was friendly and helpful. Our toilet handle broke during our stay and they repaired it while we were out and left a voucher for a free drink and some chocolates with a note apologizing for the inconvenience. Too bad they couldn't make up for the rock hard beds though. The beds are not comfortable, but you get used to it after the first night. Our room was pretty large, but the bathroom area with the toilet and shower was very small and hard to move around in. The room had a desk and reading chair and plenty of storage and room to hang clothes. The hotel was clean, but seemed old and not what i was used to at other Courtyards. Due to freezing weather during our stay, we did not use the pool facilities. We also did not want to pay for the expensive breakfast at the hotel. There was plenty of parking and a computer in the lobby to check flight information and find out information about things to do while in Austin which was convenient. Overall, it was an OK stay, good enough for a brief weekend visit, if only they would upgrade the beds!
“Very good hotel; moderately priced” Very good hotel; remodeled recently with very modern, Euro-centric look and feel. Starbucks adjacent to the lobby is a nice convenience.

“シアトルのベストホテル” とにかくおすすめです。最近改装したようで、清潔感があり、とても綺麗なホテルでした。全体的にクラシックな感じで落ち着いています。また、インターネットは無料ですし、コヒーはスターバックスのものがおいてあったりと、細かい点のサービスも満足です。スタッフも親切でしたよ。私はシングル用の部屋に泊まったため(アメリカのホテルでは珍しいですよね)、値段も安く抑えることができました。ちなみにシングルの部屋はバスタブないのでご注意を。立地も良く、地下にあるバス停も近く、移動にも便利だと思います。
“One of the best Marriotts I have ever stayed” Great place for families Highly recommend for water activities

“2nd stay at this hotel” We stayed at this hotel in December 2006, and we came back for another stay over Thanksgiving weekend 2007. If anything, it has improved. The quality of the staff is excellent. The people at the front desk, the bell stand and the valet parking seemed truly interested in our being happy, not just in doing their job. We would stay here again.

“Good but not great.” My husband and I stayed here recently for my 40th birthday. This was our third trip to New York in as many years. I did extensive research online before booking at the Michelangelo. Overall I was somewhat disappointed. We were told we would have an upgrade upon check-in but when we got to our room it was the same room I had booked. Not a big deal but the front desk clerk was very rude and actually laughed when we asked for an upgrade! We only asked because we had heard that the Michelangelo was known for their upgrades. The location is nice. Times Square is obviously a very loud and crazy place to stay but we were on the 7th floor so the noise wasn't so bad. We loved the twice daily maid service and the rooms were pretty clean...not perfect but okay. I honestly don't understand why they hassle with breakfast. It is so not worth it and the hours and are very limited with very limited food. The coffee is extremely strong and you can't even bring a cup up to your room. I would probably find breakfast elsewhere, which we did every morning except for two. We have stayed at the Library Hotel and Hotel Giraffe in the past which we've found more to our liking. We even went in the lobby of the Casablanca Hotel just to look around and they couldn't have been more welcoming. They invited us to go up to the lobby and have a drink of iced tea! Quite a stark contrast for the Michelangelo where I don't think the staff cared one way or another about your stay. I think there are better options out there. I don't consider myself a very picky person but most of our nights were $325.00 and I think for that one should deserve more than what was given. I know hotel prices are expensive in New York and I know we came at the one of the busiest times of the year. That still doesn't excuse apathetic service in a supposedly four star hotel. We had drinks two nights in the lobby lounge and both nights the female bartender spent almost the entire time we were there on personal calls. Not exactly professional behavior. Felt bad for interrupting her phone call to wait for a drink. Just my opinion for whatever it's worth.

“HUGE room, super friendly and nice staff, clean, free breakfast, wifi” My room--5D--was enormous! It was a 1 bedroom apartment with a sleeper sofa, a big bathroom, and nice size kitchen. It was very clean, very quiet, air conditioners worked great, it was a lovely place to stay for 4 nights. Breakfast was standard and good, good coffee, lots of families staying there. I stay in A LOT of different hotels, and I would definitely seek this one out again. And the price was ridiculously good for what you got. If you're staying in the city for a while, stay here. Only negative: the wireless was kind of weak, so, you need to use the plug in to connect to the Internet for a strong signal.

“This is a good place to stay in Chelsea” Located on a relatively quiet side street, this relatively small hotel has reasonably nice rooms (medium-size by NY standards) and is clean. The elevators are slow because there are only 2 and 22 stories (each floor does not have many rooms). There is an outdoor cafe/restaurant which is nicely situated as it is in a recess from the street. The front desk service can be slow as the area is small.

“Old building but great location!” A friend and I stayed here for a night for a concert at Key Arena and I will share the good and bad. Good: Location - The location is probably the best feature of this place, it is right across the street from the arena and Seattle Center complex with the Space Needle and monorail nearby. With the monorail and the new light rail, you can get all the way from here to the airport and never have to take a bus. Also there are a lot of bars and restaurants within a couple of blocks. Cost - very affordable, the room for my friend and I was only $60 for two twin beds. Bad: Got woken up by a garbage truck right outside the room very early in the morning. Also could hear other building noise. The building definitely looks old but at least it had a fridge and microwave and very small kitchen setup. Didn't have time to check out the wifi or TV as we were on a tight schedule. I would probably stay here again if there was a concert in the area and because I am cheap.

“Nice Hotel, Great Location, Friendly Staff” I stayed 3 nights at the Palomar last week and was very satisfied. I have stayed at many Kimpton Hotels including their Palomar brand in SF and Dallas. The staff were very friendly, my room was well laid out and I loved the location on Wilshire (as I stayed for business). My coworkers complained about the A/C being loud but I had no issues. The valet had a few missteps but were very apologetic. I would definitely stay at the Palomar again... I also ate at the bar for dinner twice and the bartenders were extremely friendly and fun.

“Nothing spectacular...decent business stay” I stayed here overnight for a business trip. Its a decent hotel with nice rooms. There was nothing spectacular but good for business or a couple of nights to tour DC. In terms of location, its a bit far from the train station (you need to take a cab) and if you are walking to the Capitol Building, be aware that there's a homeless shelter/food bank that you may walk near. I wasn't expecting that and definitely felt uncomfortable walking there alone dressed the way I was (in a business dress).

“Great hotel for the price” We stayed overnight during Spring Break (April, 2011). I got a very cheap rate on Hotwire. The hotel is not really within walking distance of anything but I'd rather take taxis than pay Inner Harbor prices. I had read here about the parking situation in advance so we parked in the public lot across Franklin St. It was very easy to get in and out of and the price was reasonable. The building and lobby of the hotel are nothing special. We had no problems checking in and the man at the front desk was efficient and polite. Our room had no view at all but was very spacious and clean. The temperature control in the room worked fine and we were very comfortable. The beds were firm and comfy and the bathroom was clean. The free wi-fi worked fine. We didn't eat the free breakfast as it ended at 9:00 am. My only issue with the hotel is that there are benches in front of the outside stairs and there always seemed to be random individuals hanging around (maybe there is a bus stop close by or something. Overall, it was a nice stay and I'd recommend the hotel for someone who doesn't mind being a little further away to save some money.

“Ok for a short stay, but check other options first” HOTEL REVIEW # 161 New York MY TRAVEL STYLE: If possible, I try to stay away from business hotels and strongly prefer resorts that resemble the Four Seasons, Aman, and Oberoi but try to find similar properties at lower cost. I seek out the “wow” experiences and I encourage you to view hotels I have stayed at and their respective reviews (by clicking on my name). LOCATION: Not in the heart of the action, but a short taxi ride there. Off in a more quiet neighborhood but still on a busy street. Many restaurants, shops, and bars are steps outside of the restaurant BEST WAY TO GET THERE: Taxi from the airport took about 30 minutes and around $25 TYPE OF ROOM: Standard BED/SHEETS/PILLOW: The highlight of the room is the comfortable bed, very high quality linens, and a perfect down pillow. LIGHTING: Tons of lighting in bedroom and good lighting in bathroom. BATHROOM/SHOWER: Too small. In major need of a remodel. Shower curtain touches leg while in the shower. Shower water pressure is medium to strong with consistently hot water if desired. Shower nozzle is on a wall that aims water across the short end of the tub providing less than adequate space. TOILETRIES: Gilcrest & Soames. Good enough. CLEANLINESS: Common areas are clean but the room and bathroom could have been better. I noticed dust that had collected on window sills and the heating unit (in bathroom). Even if this hotel was spotless, the fact that it’s old would still make it look a bit unclean. A/C: Didn’t use. CLOSET SPACE: More than average and enough space for 2 to unpack most if not all items. STYLE OF ROOM: Old style with just a tad of charm. Carpet is in definite need of updating. Adequate for a few nights stay and comfortable. COMMON AREA: The lobby is small and definitely not a place for hanging out. It has a tiny bit of a hip style to it and with just a bit of work, could be really nice. QUIET: My room faced an inner courtyard and was very quiet. FOOD: Breakfast is complementary but not good. Bananas, oranges, apples, stale muffins and stale bagels. Coffee and orange juice mix is also provided. TV/INTERNET: Internet in the room is wireless only and $12.00 per day. Didn’t use. SERVICE: Staff were very professional and helpful with our trip planning. Surprised when bellboy didn’t offer to take my bags from the front desk to the taxi at checkout. SUMMARY: This room was booked on my behalf. It’s a decent place in a decent area. I would suspect that for $195/night (weekday) that there are much better options nearby. I half-heartedly recommend this hotel, but for my next stay I would try hard to find a better option.

“Nice Visit. Would stay again” My family stayed here from June 9-12, 2012. I got the hotel through Hotwire and was very concerned after i read the reviews on this site. Before we left there was 1 positive review recently which gave me hope. We had nothing to worry about as it turned out. the visit was wonderful from start to finish. The front desk staff were extremely friendly and helpful (even looked up a store and got directions from google for my husband). The area is surrounded by lots of shops and restaurants and is very close to UNC Charlotte. The only negative I can think of the whole visit was the water pressure and temperature in the shower. But that was very minor. We would definately stay there again.

“Good Enough for a Quick Stay” This was a serviceable hotel - the rooms, while slightly dated, were spacious and clean. It was well-located, within walking distance to all the attractions at Union Square and close to the cable car. Housekeeping was inconsistent with replenishing amenities. On one day, they didn't replenish at all and for two girls with long hair, that was a big no! I also, unfortunately, got my wallet and cell phone pick-pocketed at a busy part of town and the hotel staff were not extremely helpful. I probably wouldn't stay here again, unless that rate was rock-bottom and only if I was passing through San Francisco.

“The best boutique hotel in Boston” This is my third time staying at XV Beacon. It's a great small hotel with personalized service in a great location downtown. The prices are pretty steep though so I would say that unless you want to stay at a unique full service small boutique hotel, you might be better off looking elsewhere. If you stay here be sure to try the neighboring Scollay Square restaurant if you like bloody mary's. They have a make your own bloody mary bar! The good: the hotel has a warm cozy feel, staff is very polite and courteous; rooms are unlike any others that I've been in, for example: stereo system with built in speakers throughout the room, working gas fireplace, tastefully decorated as if you are in someone's home, electronic do not disturb/clean my room signal so you don't have to fiddle with door hangars, good size flat screen TV, jacuzzi bathtub; real flowers in the bathroom; nice towels; towel heater in bathroom; TV in bathroom; very nice headboard or four poster bed (depending on what type of room you get); free parking if you have a Lexus and free use of the hotel Lexus with driver who can take you around town as needed; they provide complimentary business cards with your hotel address on them; nightly turn down service; very good restaurant downstairs (Mooo); free wireless internet that's pretty fast; complimentary fruit in the hallways. The OK: the bath products are just so-so, bathtub drained slowly, television in bathroom is a nice touch however it doesn't work (said "no signal"); shower partition leaked a fair amount of water on the floor after taking a shower, elevators could use some freshening up (carpet, walls, and buttons are worn). The Bad: nothing

“A nice place for the most part.....” we stayed here over Christmas and got an amazing rate. I would say its above average for Scottsdale hotels unless you go the resort route and I don't count this place as a resort. The hotel was very nice... the staff very helpful and courteous. Breakfast was typical embassy suites fare, but for the rate we paid, a nice asset. Our room was fine, not dirty (and I am a dirt freak) in the least. The bed was rather soft and yes the sheets did not fit and the door does slam rather loudly, but none were dealbreakers for us. I should mention that the hotel was only about 50% full so perhaps that made things more tolerable in terms of the noise, breakfast, etc. Not sure what it would be like during spring training which is the busiest time of year. The only real bummer was trying to get my cell phone charger back that fell out of my bag in the room. Lost and found there was kind of lame... They had to charge me with a cc# for packing it up and shipping it even though I offered to give them a fedex # and ups #.... Charging for putting it in a fedex envelope? While in Scottsdale, be sure to try Don and Charlies. YUM! A great place for steak lovers and baseball fans.

“Average motel, great value for downtown San Jose” This is an old, decently remodeled property in the "motor-court" style as another reviewer pointed out. It's a couple blocks from the convention center, and several blocks from the university. Plenty of restaurants nearby. We really liked Original Joe's Italian restaurant which is just a short walk. The check-in people are very friendly and helpful. Parking was ample while I was there. This is a 3-story, outside-corridor motel with an elevator. I found it to be very quiet. Just to be sure, you might request a room near the center, since there are a lot of clubs along 1st street. I did not feel unsafe walking in a 3-block radius of the motel, from the convention center to the university. The room was nice in appearance, and very clean. The bedding was nice, but the bed itself was of indifferent quality. It'll seem a little flat and hard if you're used to the pillow-top mattresses in a lot of even mid-range hotels these days.The bath is well appointed but the fixtures are fairly archaic, as is the plumbing - the shower went warm/cool/warm/cool repeatedly every morning during a 3 night stay. Not scalding/freezing, but still annoying. The shower smelt somewhat mildewy. The wall unit A/C looks cheap but worked well and was quiet. Wireless internet was good but you have to hunt/crawl to plug in your laptop. The TV had few channels. Housekeeping was excellent. Overall, the Ramada was a decent place to stay, especially when you consider the price is half or less compared to the convention center hotels a couple blocks away -- and unlike those places, the Ramada has free in-room Internet and free parking. It's definitely not the Ritz but it's a clean, decent place and a good value.

“Beautiful hotel and rooms” Stayed for a few nights in March, 2006 for business. Also stayed in December, 2005 for a few nights. Beautiful, modern property with easy walking distance to the Capitol and Union Station. Is a little pricey if you're on a budget. If you stay on the lower floors, it can be a little noisy with outside traffic due to busy street but if you're on an upper floor it's very quiet. Has internet in rooms. Rooms are very modern and up to date.

“a view would be nice!” Only stayed here two nights. Wish it could have been longer as we love San Francisco. Have stayed at both the Holiday Inns in the past, but decided to treat ourselves to the Argonaut after all its great reviews.After a bit of a mix up when the receptionist thought we'd only reserved one room instead of two, we were pleasantly surprised to find we were entitled to breakfast on the two mornings.It was only juice, tea or coffee, a bowl of fruit and a choice of pastry or toast but it was all right for nothing. The complementary wine in the evening was a nice touch even though we didn't like the wine. The rooms were very smart and actually looked like the photos on the hotel web site. Internet was free in the room , something other hotels should consider in this day and age.My only gripe was that our view was over a courtyard to rooms with shutters at the windows which ,sort of, made me think of Alcatraz!I think you have to pay extra for any decent view.The cost of the valet carparking is rather extortionate, but so was that at both Holiday Inns. Can certainly recommend this hotel for its good points and excellent locality and would definitely go back, but would try to get a better room ( with a view )next time.

“Vastly improved” I have stayed at the Days Broadway previously and was compelled to write reviews describing an awful hotel. A client booked me into a New York hotel for 3 nights and I was horrified to discover they had chosen the Days Hotel Broadway. Anyway, circumstances conspired such that I could not change the reservation and I checked in with trepidation. I have to say the improvement is vast. The room was on the 14th floor and it was clean, the sheets were pristine, the bed was comfortable and the air conditioning/heating worked. My only problems were a lack of hot water and the truely awful elevators. It is hard to conceive how they can be so slow. I will have no hesitation about staying there in future.

“Just OK for an overnight at SeaTac” Stayed here for an overnight, flying in at night - early plane the next day. It's an OK place to stay briefly, but is not really comparable to some of the other three-star hotels near SeaTac. The staff was courteous, but not too helpful and the bed was reasonably comfortable, though the room was not really well-appointed. They transport from the airport in a parking shuttle (Park & Ride A), so we missed the first one, not knowing how to recognize that it was the van for the hotel. Suggestion: Ask hotel staff how to recognize the van before you travel.

“Just back from another great stay at the HGI Chicao” Have got back after staying with them for another 4 days (and an additonal 1 day the week before). Rooms clean and early check-in was available. As always GREAT (free for HH Gold)breakfast in the Webber Grill - cooked to order. Also had a meal in the Webber Grill one evening - good value and recommend the pork chops. Excellent location, just off Michigan Ave for all the shops, and does have Starbucks opposite which is useful. The internet access in the room is free (HH Gold) and is pretty fast; also coffee maker, fridge and microwave which is useful. Good gym and adequate swimming pool. Business centre available for printing any documents you need. Staff always welcome you with a smile. My only comment is the TV volume does not turn down lower than "7" for some reason on any of the TV's in various rooms.

“nice reasonable priced jotel in the medical center” i attended a confefrence at this hoitel - i did not stay at the hotel because i live in san antonio - some of my friends did, i had a chance to look at the rooms - they were nice the conference facilitie were adequate and the service was good did not eat at the hotel so can't rate the food the room rates for our conference were $65 (us) per night plus tax - not bad if someone were coming to visit me in san antonio, i might consider recommending this hotel to them i am from san antonio, texas

“Outstanding, Convenient Hotel with Comfortable Rooms” This is my first time staying in a Marriot Renaissance Hotel; and, this will not be the last time. This hotel is outstanding - great location only minutes east of O'Hare airport from the main airport exit, directly off the Kennedy Expressway. The hotel is located next to the Chicago L Cumberland station (about a 1 minute walk). This is extremely convenient to take the L Train into the city instead of fighting the Chicago traffice. I was a Gold member so they offered a lot of convenient perks for Marriott Gold and Platinum Rewards members. The conceirge lounge is wonderful. although the lounge is only open on weekdays. Despite the lounge being closed on weekends, the hotel allows Conceirge floor guests to have free breakfast in the restaurant and free evening appetizers in the lobby bar when the lounge is closed. I have never seen this benefit before when the lounge is closed. The Conceirge lounge is also located on a key-only access floor - providing utmost privacy and security. During the one day we could use the lounge, they had a very savory dinner along with chocolate chip cookies and desserts. It was nice the lounge had complementary bottles of Evian water I could take to my room. My only complaints are the following: 1) Payying $20 for daily parking :( and 2) There is only wired internet access in the rooms - no WiFi. I thought all hotels had inroom WiFi these days. This hotel only seems to have WiFi set up in their restaurant and lobby areas. The rooms are two room suites with two TVs and sofa-bed which is convenient when traveling with a family. I requested a room overlooking the airport which was nice to see planes landing and taking off. Staff is also very friendly - prompt attention to extra pillow and blanket requests. This is by far one of my favorite Marriotts.

“Another nice stay at a Hampton Inn” We were in town for a baseball game at Redbird Stadium. Easy walk to all the downtown attractions. Covered parking. Pool and Hot Tub. Rooms are large. Ours overlooked a music square off of Beale Street.

“Terrific service, great view, but stuffy, dated decor” Stayed here in a suite while in town. The long and short of it is that the hotel itself feels traditionally conservative (typical for Boston), but in execution it just comes off as a bit dated and stuffy. The rooms (and especially the bathrooms) feel small and cramped with dated marble and the tiniest bathtubs (forget about taking a bubble bath to relax!). The views were incredible though, so peaceful to look over the harbor. The service was also excellent. They originally put me in a room right next to a service door, which kept me up for a good part of the night until I called and complained. Not sure why they would ever put anyone in that room (I forget the number), but stay away! They immediately (at 11pm) moved me into another room (a suite) on another floor. The room was not much different, except for a big sitting room with a couch and a vanity area. Disappointingly the bathroom and tub/shower was the same measly size as the former room. I much preferred my stay at the intercontinental next door.

“Pleasant Room, loud neighbors” We arranged for an double king room, which was nice, but the bathroom was too small and the water pressure low. The music from the room above us played their music loud. Had to call the front desk three times and they finally shut it down at 10:30pm PST. We had an early morning flight and had to get to sleep early. Shuttle van was nice and helpful. Great location.

“Small hotel, good location” I booked one night at Hotel Mela based on a Travelzoo weekly Top 20 promotion. It was a great price for NY - $241 including taxes for a Friday night in April. I usually stick to Hilton properties, but figured I’d give Mela a shot for the great rate. I was looking forward to celebrating my birthday with Broadway shows and a brand new hotel. We checked in on my birthday, which was not acknowledged by the staff. We booked a superior queen room, and it was very small and poorly designed. There was less than 6 inches between the end of the bed and the dresser – barely enough room for person to get by. The bathroom sink had a glass shelf that was not flush against the wall and wasn’t level. I was afraid to put anything on it, as it dropped right off the back of the shelf! I know it is a minor nuisance, but still – how difficult is it to level a bathroom shelf? The location was OK, but I prefer to be closer to 7th or 8th Street. The room was clean, and the hotel was quiet enough. Overall, our stay was worth the discounted price. At regular prices, I would certainly not book Hotel Mela again.

“Boring Choice” This hotel has zero charm and ambiance. The location is very good if you want to be near Union Square but that's about it. You can get a room for under $100 here on Hotwire but it is tiny. You'll need to pay at least another $20 a night to get a room big enough to move around in. Forget paying $45 to park at the hotel; right across the street there is public parking for $28 a day.

“Scratchy sheets, hard bed, sleepless night” For a new hotel this is shameful--at one time the Westin's were known for their 'heavenly beds' but this new property seems to have opted for the lowest possible quality. I stay in a lot of hotels (so far this year, 84 in Starwood Properties alone) and recognize there is a range of quality. What i don't understand is why they opted for the lowest quality in a new property. Other signs of lower quality: I called the front desk upon my arrival in the room as there was no internet (it said i the room had not yet been checked into). it took three calls and 15 minutes with me finally pressing the Operator to locate someone to help, (is there lack of adequate staffing even with the hotel being new?), the creamer in the room is powdered--not even mini moos, there is no option for very high speed internet, and no phone on the desk. The phone by the bed is remote, but no speaker ability on the handset, so to participate in web conferencing with two-way audio one needs to hold the handset. Further, they do not appear to have upgraded the sound proofing, i stay in NYC a lot and know street noise can be muffled.

“A tremendous value” As previosuly said, The Salisbury is perfectly located and very clean. Yes, the furnishings are dated and yes, the elevators are slow. But the room was HUGE (1712 and 1718 on the 17th floor) by New York standards. And the $209 rate was excellent. The $3 breakfast is just what one should expect for $3. It's an easy, quick way to grab something before heading out to see the sights. Our location was quiet and the beds were comfortable. My request for more hangers was never filled, but it didn't matter after we found another closet!

“Great stay, great location in Downtown San Antonio” I had to make a flash trip to San Antonio for business purposes and now chose the Springhill Suites for my stay. I previously stayed at the Fairfield Inn and Suites and had a great experience on a Studio Room there. These two hotels, the Springhill and Fairfield Inn named Downtown/Alamo Plaza are very well located, just two blocks from the Rivercenter and very well connected by the 281 highway to move around San Antonio. They both offer clean rooms and great service. Valet is 21 dollars for the whole day, probably a little bit expensive if you only use it for overnight parking but I thinks it compensates with the rate. The springhill has better breakfast and would definitely stay here again.

“pleasant stay on a holiday weekend” We've stayed at plenty of motels and know they can run the gamut from trashy to passable. The Best Western Seven Seas stands out as a motel that gets it right -- clean, comfortable rooms; attractive grounds; friendly staff; easily accessible parking; excellent freeway access and proximity to local attractions; 24-hour hot tub. We'd stayed at the Seven Seas many, many years ago when we were in college, and we opted to stay there over Memorial Day weekend for a trip down memory lane. We were not disappointed and had a most pleasant stay! Check-in was smooth, and the front desk receptionist was very friendly and helpful. Our room, although on the small side, was well-lit and tastefully decorated. We appreciated the in-room coffee (the best I've had at a motel) and the well-stocked basket of soaps and Pantene shampoo, and the shower head was nice and high -- a plus for tall people who don't like to stoop to wet their hair. The bed was a mixed bag. The mattress was decently comfortable, but the pillows were hard and a bit too large, forcing my head to rest at a funky angle. I woke up with a sore neck after the first night; the second and third nights, I used the plush beluga whale I'd gotten at Sea World for a pillow and had better nights' sleep. The pillow was the only problem though. Everything else about the room was quite satisfactory. We also liked the 24-hour hot tub, and the grounds are beautifully landscaped with tropical plants. Even though the motel abuts two freeways, we did not hear any road noise. Generally, the motel was quiet aside from the typical people-passing-the-window sounds you expect at places like this. The Seven Seas is central to Mission Valley, Mission Bay and Sea World, Old Town, and downtown attractions. There are several restaurants within walking distance of the motel, and more restaurants are a quick car ride away in Old Town and at the Fashion Valley Mall. We enjoyed our stay at the Seven Seas and will happily stay there again in the future.
“Surprisingly nice!” This is a better than average Embassy Suites. Rooms are very nice. Great value and great location in relation to the airport.

“A great place to stay if you are visiting Boston” Stayed at the Holiday Inn for a few nights in June whilst visiting Boston. Loved Boston and enjoyed the stay at the hotel. The room was large (had one of the end rooms), the bathroom was compact but had a large proper shower (not bathtub), it was close to the city and amenities (and in a nice area), nicely decorated (had 5 lamps), outdoor swimming pool, internet access, oh and of course a comfy bed!!!! There is a supermarket (upmarket) around the corner. On the downside, there was a lot of door slamming (hard to close door quietly), and old TV, doors to adjoining rooms, and a lot of overzealous ambulance drivers who use their sirens (despite no traffic and all times of the day and night) to go to the large hospital adjacent. Overall, I would definitely stay here again

“Fading Beauty” This was our third, nonconsecutive Thanksgiving at the Wladorf Astoria (2001, 2010 and 2012). Always pre-pay since I have found the Hotel extends a small discount. I booked a suite plus two additional rooms. Suite 860 has not been updated since our stay in 2001. The first room I occuppied 890, I was greeted with a broken bathroom door (As if someone punched the door. The door was cracked with two small holes and two different color paints on the door) The wall oin the bathroom, over the door was covered in black mold 6 inches by 1 foot. If the door was in good repair I may not have noticed the mold issue. The Housekeeping supervisor was summoned to my room and had no explination but offered to clean the bathroom. I was changed to room 867. Peacock alley: We had Thanksgiving reservations for the 3pm seating. We were finially seated at 3:30pm (not too bad). The table had no silverware, napkins nor glassware. The hostess stated she just wanted to seat us and someone will be over shortly to complete the setup of the table. Oh no Turkey. The buffet kept running out of Turkey (I am not a fan of Turkey but come on, its Thanksgiving) Oscars: When I made the room reservations, my the written e-mail confirmed a $50 breakfast credit at Oscars included with the suite reservation. I reveiwed my parents incidental charges prior to checkout on Friday (they stayed in the Suite) and NO credit not was applied. The front desk agent stated,"that was NOT part of your room rate". I asked to speak with the front desk manager, he checked my reservation on line and stated the same. I stated,"this is an easy fix, we can solve this now or I can dispute the charges with my credit card company" I was credited and later that day when I reviewed my reservation on line, it clearly stated on the second page of the confirmation, a $50 credit will be applied to breakfast at Oscars" No evening houskeeping service. During previous stays, houskeeping would freshed up the rooms, replace towels etc while we were out. The houskeeper for the 8th floor could be seen sitting in her office in the main hall of the 8th floor yet she never seemed to make it to ours rooms. Both in 2001 and 2010 the rooms were straightened while we were out. Upon checkout I called the 1-800 number to complain. Saturday evening at 6:55 pm I recieved a call, on my cell phone, from a manager. I was at the country club with friends and family just sitting down to drinks in the lounge (Yes, some of us still do that) and asked him to call back on Monday or Tuesday. No call was ever recieved. 12/9/12 I was in NYC for the weekend and decided to give the Walforf a second chance (Fool that I can be) and had breakfast at Oscars. I was seated at a table with dirty linen. Specifically a dirty napkin. I asked the hostess for a replacement, she said,"Maybe if you arrived earlier this would not be a problem (it was 9:30 am) and then she took a napkin from a dirty table that was just vacated and handed it to me.... Classy. Steady yourself, This is the worst part. My parents recieved at letter from Ana Tijan, Director of Rooms, Waldorf Astroia, outlining my complaints and offering them a free upgrade on their next stay. I was protecting my elderly parents from the multitude of issues at the Hotel and much to my embarrassment, Ms Ana Tijan was nice to outline all the issues in the letter. I spoke with Ms Tijan on 12/14/12 to tell her how embarressed I was with the letter and her response was,"I sign a lot of letters that other people write" I was transferred to the GM, Mr Eric Long, spoke with his assistant, and I am waiting for a response. I suggest a visit to the lobby, it is fine exapmle of art deco. Yet, there are many other fine Hotels in NYC to stay.

“Classic Hotel in a Great Downtown Location” Classic but average hotel lives up to Marriott Standards. The Blackstone is right in the middle of all the Fort Worth action and within walking distance to the bars/clubs of downtown and only a short drive over to the stockyards or cultural district. I had a corner room with lots of windows and an amazing view of downtown. The hotel was built in 1929 and being the corner room you can see where the windows use to open up but have now been closed off for safety, Classic touches like that are nice. As with all Marriott properties the room was very clean and the bed was very comfy. Being a older hotel the bathroom is very small and the rooms could use a little updating with the electronics, it had a older 25 inch tv on top of a old mini fridge. A hotel like this charging $100-$275 a night should invest in some Flat Panels and HD programming. No restaurant on site but the do connect with the Corner Bakery through the lobby, its good for coffee and pastry. Overall it's a nice location but overpriced in my opinion.

“a great hotel in nyc” I stayed here for one night with my husband. Got a good deal on this hotel from priceline bidding. The wonderful lady at the check-in desk upgraded us to a one bedroom suite. The room was fabulous, roomy and very clean. It is the size of a regular nyc one bedroom apartment. I would definitely stay here again with the kids next time. This hotel would be great for a families with children. It is a bit away from the touristy time square/theater area but if you willing to walk a bit - this is a great location.

“Chillin on the River” Sometimes I think people complain for nothing.We stayed here over the weekend with another couple and had no trouble at all.Sure there is construction on the walkway put it will not last long and if you know how to get around the Riverwalk it is easy getting around the construction. We will return to this place.

“Muy buena ubicacion, tranquilo, comodo” Hotel muy comodo con buena ubicacion muy cerca del Freedom trail, y de centros nocturnos, Faneuil Hill, etc, limpio muy tranquilo, Internet free en habitacion, cafe gratis en el looby Tv con cable con amplia programacion Falencias: no tener cafetera en la habitacion ni heladera

“Nice Place” Great hotel. Very very clean. Great bathroom, bed, nice nice place. A bit noisy at night, but what hotel isn't? Stunning views from upper floor North Tower rooms (Floor 40 and up). Lounge was a very "happening" place at night. Also, location is great, about 5 blocks at most from Pike's Market.. about 3 blocks from the Convention Center. Literally around all shops and so on. Did not eat at hotel, but looked very nice. Hotel is very, very busy, but also well-staffed with nice people. There were numerous times I called the front desk for various things.. and no one answered. So I called later and was finally answered. To be expected. This hotel appears packed at all times. $183 nightly.

“Small and Drafty” My husband and I stayed here for three extremely cold nights in December. Insulation proved to be poor and much cold air entered the room through the window, causing discomfort. The standard room was so small that the queen bed took up most of the space. The tiny closet could only hold two coats and nothing else in its hanging area. There were no hooks in the bathroom, so nothing could be hung there. The TV did not work on our arrival and no one was available to fix it until the next day. No safe was in the room. On the plus side, we got an excellent price on the hotel's web site for New York -- $139 per night, excluding taxes. The location, though not central, was good -- a few blocks from Central Park and two blocks from a subway station. The room was clean and quiet and the bed extremely comfortable. The staff was generally friendly and helpful. The hotel's restaurant, which is almost impossible to get into without a reservation, is outstanding. We both had excellent pasta dishes, which rivaled meals we've eaten in Italy. The chef's special dessert the night we ate there was gingerbread pudding with eggnog sauce ... truly delicious. Getting to JFK Airport has become easy and inexpensive with the Air Train. From Penn Station, we took the Long Island Railroad to the Jamaica station and the Air Train from there to the airport, where it stops at every terminal. It took about half an hour from Penn Station to the airport at a cost of $8.50 per person, which included a senior discount on the LIRR.

“Lukewarm Hotel” Located in the heart of downtown Phoenix, this hotel makes an ideal place to stay for concerts, sporting events and concerts. It is a historic hotel which can be neat and funky at times. However this is also where San Carlos' troubles lie. First off, the walls are paper thin (conversations nose blowing, etc. Were easily heard by me). The rooms are tiny, as well. The hotel seems clean however the dated-appearing carpet, furniture etc. makes you wonder when the last time this place was updated. Given it's location, this hotel could be even better if the owners updated it while keeping some of the place's historic charm (the old school bathroom in the room is awesome). Overall, not a bad place to stay in downtown Phoenix. But if you can find someplace newer, bigger, and cheaper in the neighborhood, I'd go for that option, instead.

“Great views, wonderful room, solid location” We stayed at several in Chicago during a Thanksgiving "Meet the Parents" trip, and this was by far the best one. In fact, this was one of the favorite hotels we have stayed at (and we travel a lot). The upsides were, the amazing view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. We felt like we were sleeping in the John Hancock building. The room was also very elegant and comfortable, which is a tricky combination to achieve. We also enjoy walking, so the location was absolutely perfect as it was just a pinch of a distance to the central shops etc (but I can imagine it would be tricky if you have young children). The only downsides that we experienced was that we did not think the restaurant was that fabulous. The hours were very limited if you wanted to eat at odd times (i.e. because of jet lag), and if there is a vegetarian in your group, you will find their options are quite limited. You're better off eating outside the hotel. Overall, however, a thoroughly enjoyable trip.

“A great location near Fenway Park, but awful room.” We were going to a baseball game at Fenway Park, and selected Howard Johnson's for its convenient location. Our expectations were high after staying in a trip advisor-recommended Howard Johnson's in Buenos Aires earlier in the year, which was great. The room smelled of animal odors, and bugs were crawling across the carpet. The beds themselves and the bathroom were fine. We decided to live with it, since we were out most of the day and at the ballgame until late. We mentioned these items at checkout, which didn't get much of a response from the desk staff. The manager later called us, and apologized since a family with a pet had stayed in the room before us. The restaurant was inexplicably closed for breakfast one morning that we were there, and the pool had a lifeguard...but no swimmers at sixty-five degrees!

“Great Location Except” Valet parking terrible customer service. Location and service were first class. Took advice from other reviews and requested high floor facing 10th street to avoid construciton noise. GREAT ADVICE. Valet parking service was SLOOOOOW! Took an average of 20 mins to get car brought back up. Way too long for $29 per day fee. Overall, this hotel is up to usual Embassy Suites high standards except for parking. If you dont need that particular service, then I highly recommend this hotel.

“Wonderful Getaway” My sister and I went for a weekend to relax. We had a great time. We had the all-inclusive package which was a great savings. We loved the spa - had massage and facial. Food and service was good at restaurant. Grounds are beautiful.

“Great Location!” This hotel is a great location for the Fishermans wharf area. I made my reservations online and used my points, my request always includes extra towels, high floor and extra pillows. I'm never not satifisted with the Marriott Brand. The room was clean and smelled very fresh. The staff at this hotel is so friendly, I think its some of the guests who need a lesson. We were able to check in early and started our day with a walk down to the pier. The location is great, we walked over to Ghiradelli square, down to the pier at Alcatraz to pick up our tickets for the next day, walked to Lombard Street (that was a tough one) took the trolley around the city. All in all, i've stayed at this hotel a number of times and I'm always happy with my stay.

“Not your typical Kimpton...” As another reviewer lamented, I also could not get into the Hotel Monaco or the Hotel Burnham while staying in Chicago, so I stayed at the Allegro. Please don't get this reviewer wrong, the hotel is okay, but it is not your typical first class Kimpton Boutique Hotel. I agree with the other reviewer's: the bathroom is extremely tiny, the lighting is terrible and the room is a little too pink and a little too tired. The pluses: room service was prompt and the food was delicious with great portions. The bed was also very comfortable. My beef with Kimpton is why don't you just upgrade this hotel so it is comparable with your other first-class establishments? Overall, this hotel is not bad for the average traveler, but it should not be associated with the Kimpton Hotel chain.

“Mixed reviews for an average stay” The staff was very friendly and went out of their way to accommodate our requests. The rooms are standard suites which are nice to be able to have the small sitting area separate from the bedrooms. The property is a bit older and not as clean as some other places we've stayed. The surrounding area was a bit suspect for me. The breakfast was not as good as some of the other properties in the area. Close to SeaWorld and plenty of restaurants. Overall, an average stay for price but I'd probably not stay here again with all of the other choices close by.

“Superb service” I've stayed at this hotel 4 times in the past few months and will definitely stay here in future months on business trips. It's an excellent value when compared to the other hotels in the area. The staff is always fun to deal with and eager to help. The rooms are spacious and comfortable and the halls have always been quiet. It's an excellent facility in almost every way. The restaurant food is good and reasonably priced, although if you are looking for an elegant dining experience you probably want to eat elsewhere. I don't think everybody gets free internet access in the rooms, although it is available to Hilton Honors gold members.

“Smallest Rooms Ever!!!” This is the worst W I've ever stayed at!!! I'm not joking when I say our room was no larger than 10" x 11"!!! The queen size bed took up the entire room w/ a tiny little desk in the corner. The tv looked like it was going to fall off the stand. Luckily we weren't in the room a lot but this hotel is NOT worth the money! The maids were terrible- they barely made the rooms up and on the last day they didn't even come after we requested they make the room up when we went out for the day! The bar/lobby scene was the best part as it was nice to come back for drinks after dinner before going to bed. I heard the W in times Square is much better- think i will try that next time...

“Very Nice San Diego Hotel” This is a very large hotel near the Convention Center and San Diego Airport. It rises around 30 stories tall and has great views north and south and across the bay to Coronado Island. The views really sell the rooms, especially those looking out across to the Island and the Pacific Ocean beyond. The rooms are nice, typical Hilton, the bathrooms a bit disappointing because those with King Beds lack tubs. Service was great. Maintenance came up and fixed a problem with my air conditioning system (it was making a strange noise) and check-in was easy. Restaurants are mainly down on the bottom floor and it is a hike to the Starbuck's on the property. The hotel has a good gym and business center.

“Good deal in the heart of Philly” I found a great rate at this hotel for a last-minute trip and decided to overlook some of the negative reviews on this site based on my past experiences with Radisson and the sometimes skewed expectations of travelers who post here. I was not at all disappointed! The hotel is a block from Rittenhouse Square, one of the most picturesque parks in Philly and is a very short walk to both the Suburban Station (where the R1 train from the airport stops) and the main Broad St subway line (takes you directly to the sports stadiums). You really can't get a much better location than this and the price was far below what I would pay for similar accomodations and location in other cities like Boston, NYC, etc. The hotel is itself is pretty nice. My room was spacious, had very powerful AC (which was great as it was about 97+ degrees in the city!) and was quiet at night. It was a smoking room, but did not smell at all like cigarettes. The bathroom wallpaper could have used some retouching, but overall I was very satisfied with cleanliness and upkeep of the room. I did not eat at the hotel restaurant - directly across the street is a great 24-hr diner with cheap breakfasts and there are plenty of other places within walking distance for dinners and lunch, so why eat at the hotel? My only complaint was that the bill they left under my door did not reflect my pre-payment of the room and also quoted a higher rate than I paid. However, with the confirmation printout from my online reservation, this was all resolved quickly at the front desk later that morning. Overall, this is a nice place with an excellent location and friendly staff - include the low special rates and you have a winner!

“Philly Favorite Due To It's Location” What's not to love. This is from a former local's point of view. It's located in the best neighborhood of center city- "Rittenhouse Square". You can walk to everything. The theater district is a few blocks away. Shopping is literally around the corner. Many joints to eat nearby and all around. Di Bruno Brother's italian market, philly's oldest and best, is a 1 minute walk -around the corner- and for the ladies there is a Sephora and Kiehl's as well. We have stayed here for the New Year's Eve weekends of 2011 and 2010. The hotel itself is a true 4 star. Service, from valet parking to front desk and housekeeping, all were wonderful. Philly is the city of "Brotherly Love" and the personnel make sure you feel that Philly warmth down to your soul. The room was standard fare for a 4 star hotel. It was large and had everything you could want. Nice views of Philly all around, from the hallway windows to those of the room. Parking hurts. The hotel was pleasantly decorated for the season. Can't wait to stay here again New Year's Eve 2012 or any other time of the year.

“Once again great stay” Stayed once again due to to the great location, large hotel rooms for the price and the wonderful front desk and other staff folks - was not disappointed. This time found what they call the spa - what I found was an awesome fitness center - last time around the weather was fine so the run was outside - this time there was a blizzard and the staff let me know they had a few treadmills on the lower level - it was more than a few treadmills! Cannot wait to go back in a few months. This place is great

“Great Location in Downtown Philly” This is a great place to stay to visit all the historical sites. It is small, quiet and very friendly. Our room with two double beds was somewhat small but its an old hotel. Free breakfast was very good.

“typical Sofitel” Stayed here on very short notice. Plane delayed because of severe weather and all hotels around airport were sold out. Called the Sofitel, got the room. Sofitel made the best of a lousy situation. Staff friendly and accommodating. Rooms spotless and tastefully decorated. Lounge and restaurant very good. Would definitely stay there again.

“Not what it used to be” I stayed here for one night with my teenage daughter at the end of trip through New England to tour schools. I have stayed at this hotel numerous times in the past when it was the Ritz. It was a lovely hotel in a great location with impeccable service. The Taj chain has completely ruined one of the gems of Boston. Let's start with what was good. The hotel commands a great location right on the Public Garden - within easy walking distance of shopping in the Back Bay and all of the wonderful restaurants and small shops in Beacon Hill. Some of the lobby staff and room service personnel who pre-date the Taj takeover, are still as wonderful, helpful and gracious as always. I should also mention the bed was super comfy. What was wrong: We arrived at 4pm on a Saturday afternoon after a long day of driving. Check-in is at 3pm. We were told that our room was not ready and probably would not be ready for at least another hour, possibly longer. There were a number of people (many with small children) milling around the lobby (which is on the smallish size) who were in the same predicament. Apparently, the hotel had allowed a number of guests from the previous evening to utilize a late check out option - which is fine if you have the capacity to accommodate those folks as well as your new arrivals. Obviously, this was not the case. This was a huge inconvenience for us as we had dinner reservations with friends at 6pm and hoped to shower and freshen before going out. The hotel offered us NOTHING for this inconvenience. Not even a "go have a drink in the bar, while we ready your room". Nothing, zero! When we finally were allowed access to our room, it was clear that the room and bathroom had not been updated in 15 years or longer. The blackout coating on the curtains was peeling and completely gone in places so that with the drapes closed there were huge areas where the bright sunlight penetrated the curtains. The windows have not been re-glazed in 30-40 years and if you have a room facing the common it will be very noisy. The telephone system is very old and several times during the night our phone emitted a loud dial tone through the speaker - 1am, 3am and again at 5:30. It was horrible. They also charge $10.75 per day for internet access. There are many nice hotels in this area, which are much nicer and better value. I will not stay here again. Shame on Taj for ruining what was a Boston institution!

“Nice... in a somewhat overly dramatic sort of way” Nice hotel, in a good location, with a hip vibe and great service. The dramatic dark color schemes and quirky decor (e.g. picture of screaming spider monkey hanging behind toilet) are a bit much - esp. for a business trip with colleagues, but overall the hotel was nice and I'd consider staying there again

“Great Place with the Right Room!” Me and My husband stayed here for a relaxing vacation fairly close to home. When I booked a room here I requested a room with a view. When we arrived the line at the front desk was extremely long! We waited patiently, got our room key and were off to our room. After finding our room (lower down the hill fairly close to the large pool and also had a smaller pool right outside our door) we were Extremely disappointed!
