The elevator to the second floor was disgusting, the room had very little light coming in and the only view we had was of the parking lot on one side and the smaller overcrowded pool on the other side! Also the amount of noise coming from the pool was insane, there wasn't going to be much relaxing going on here. This room had the feel of a cheap apartment not a resort, so, I went back to the front desk and asked for another room! There was no room available but I was told that if we waited about 1-2 hrs there would be one available farther up the hill so we waited. In 1-2 hrs I received a call that a room was available and returned and picked up our room key. This room was as far up the hill as you could get, right below the different point of view restaurant. The parking for our room was at a steep angle and the feel was much better of this location. It seemed cleaner, newer and much more peaceful! No overcrowded swimming pools nearby and a great view! Our room was full of light, a peaceful hallway with interesting plants out front and a beautiful view from a large patio in the back. Our Suite had a flat screen tv, fridge, bar, desk, and comfy couch in the living room and a Comfy King bed & standard tv in the fairly large bedroom. The Bathroom was a bit weird, the vanity was located on one side of the hall, plenty of space on the granite countertop but a noisy air conditioner vent overhead... the shower/tub combo and toilet were on the other side in a pretty cramped space, when you open the door it nearly touches the toilet. It was really clean but could use some new fixtures in the shower/tub, they were really covered in hard water. The view from 'Different Point of View' is great, you can see downtown Phoenix from here. We didn't eat at the restaurant, just took a drive up to look around. We didn't do room service either so I can't comment on that. We ate out while staying here and it was quite a drive to find something. Make sure to plan ahead if you are going to eat out as options in this area are pretty slim. Overall we really liked our stay here and it was very relaxing, I would return to this resort as long as we got a room in the same location... the rooms lower down the hill are a big disappointment!

“Not great; it will do.” I've always avoided the Four Points brand because of a bad experience many years ago. My company booked my room here for one night so it gave me a chance to see if it's improved. Overall the hotel is very average. The public areas were fine. The bar was pretty good but there was only 1 waitress taking care of the whole place- she was too busy. The room was okay. The bathroom was extra small- the door hit the toilet when you open the door! There was no soap in my room and the iron seemed to work intermittently. It was good enough for one night but I'd never book it myself!

“Rooms are fine; avoid the restaurant at breakfast” This is a classic Kimpton hotel - a little eclectic, but with all the amenities and no attitude. The room was quite comfortable and clean, and the staff is friendly and helpful. But, avoid the restaurant at breakfast. It's small, and service is slow. I was staying at this hotel for a convention, and it was as if they hotel never planned for so many people. They didn't have enough staff, and the orders came out so staggered that one person was almost finished before the other person was served. Even on the last day, when most of the convention attendees had left, the restaurant had a waiting line for breakfast.

“Hip, amazing views, roomy rooms” Stayed here for a weekend getaway in an amazing suite with a breathtaking view of the Hudson and great river traffic. Fun to watch the bustle, which you could see from the bed. Pros: The bed is comfortable with great linens. Shower with multiple heads. Big tub. Plenty of towels. Nice desk and chair. Two large flat screen tvs. Big closet. Sexy vibe. Location just a few blocks off the beaten path -- so close enough to be convenient without too much noise or craziness. Nice sitting areas and a pleasant lobby bar -- a good escape from the scene at the roof club. Cons: From the 11th floor, we could hear the thud of rooftop night club until the wee hours. The window shades are hard to maneuver -- electronic controls would be cool. Would prefer a w/c with a door that closes for some privacy and there is not much soundproofing between room and bath. Loud loud A/C unit in room -- it cycles with enough noise and force to wake the sleeping. Hate Kimpton bathrobes with their animal prints. Most people just look ridiculous in them. White terry please Kimpton! The rooftop club is worth a visit for the views alone, but bring lots of money and expect a big scene, beginning with the red velvet ropes leading to the dedicated elevator and the dudes in dark suits with attitudes giving everyone a studied once-over.

“decent place to stay” we got a decent deal via priceline. The hotel is great for what we paid for. The service is great and the room is clean. The hotel needs a facelift compares to other 4 start hotel.

“Great Hotel in Baltimore” We stayed here for an Orioles game and selected this hotel for the convenience. We have stayed at many Inner Harbor hotels over the years, and this was one of the best. I booked a ballpark view room and was not disappointed - just like sitting in the stadium. The price for the room - considering what other hotels charge - was what I would expect. A few negatives, however, but these did not really impact my rating. First, check in was slow because there was only one person working at the desk at 2:00 p.m. on a Sunday. Second, the restaurant was in a part of the hotel which is across the street. Yes, you can get there through an enclosed walkway, but it didn't feel like part of the hotel. We ate there for breakfast - be prepared for the prices. The breakfast buffet was $19, which I feel is high even for the area. One surprising thing was how quiet this hotel is. At other hotels, you could hear the sirens all night. That didn't happen here. If you want a great hotel convenient to the stadium, this is the place to stay. If you're worried about convenience to the harbor, this one is an easy several block walk, but there are comparables closer to the harbor that I would look at.

“Wonderful Stay” My BF and I stayed at the Clift for 4 nights. We were in town to catch the Red Sox play the Giants and we could not have asked for a friendlier, more accomodating staff. We had a red-eye departure and the bellmen took great care of us with our luggage and getting us a car service (not even a cab) to the airport for the same price as a cab! Chic lobby, very moder. Super comfortably to lounge in. Weekends it seems the Clift is the place to be so we encountered more foot traffic upon returning from sight-seeing but nothing that was troublesome. Located a couple blocks (3 min walk) from Union Square Park and tons of shopping. Great, great time. Definitely recommend.

“Why stay elsewhere?” Stayed over at the Eventi last Saturday after a night out in the city. We loved the hotel, very new, modern, and sleek. Located on 6th Avenue and 30th Street, it is a bit removed from mid-town, but this is a benefit, not being in the crowd and traffic 20 blocks further up. A fairly quick trip up 6th, or cross-town in either direction, gets you where you need to be anyway, and parking Saturday night and all day Sunday on the adjacent streets is free. Our room was good-sized, HD flat panel tv, and the MOST comfortable bed. We were on the seventh floor, not a great view overlooking the back and other rooftops, however, very quiet, no traffic noise. Other great features: free wine tasting at 5 p.m. in the lobby, $15 free mini-bar credit and free wi-fi for Kimpton In Touch members (sign up for free in advance), sliding wood panel door to close off the bathroom, a quiet central a/c, mini lamps over the bed for reading, a do-not-disturb light on the outside of the door instead of a flimsy card, and a window that opened slightly to let in fresh air. There are currently very reasonable introductory rates into September. Our only complaint is that the well equipped fitness center needs an exit sign for the separate exit door, as the entrance door evidently can only be opened with a card from the outside and we needed help to figure out how to get out; also no apparent express check out, with the usual receipt left under the door; line on checkout at 11:00 a.m. was a bit long. Otherwise, the Eventi is definitely a place to stay.

“Excellent Location but few amenities” The Marriott has a fabulous location and an interesting lobby. We had a room with a King bed and we thought the room was smaller than most. The bathroom was small, too. I stayed here another time and had a room with two queen beds and the room was considerably larger so next time, I would request a two-Queen room for the additional space. There is NO mini-fridge, NO microwave and NO free in-room internet. Nearby comparable hotels DO offer these things, though. You can access the internet from the hotel lobby. There is a small coffee maker with two paper cups. The coffee pouch makes two small cups of coffee. There is a Jewel grocery store (which is open until midnight) located about three blocks from the Marriott. The complimentary bath products are from Bath and Body Works (Citrus Ginger scent) and are AWESOME. We were on the 30th floor and had a great view of the city at night. All in all, I would stay here again simply for the view (if you are lucky enough to get a room with a view) and for the location and I would get a two Queen room.
“A True Sanctuary” Enjoyed the cool room, the friendly staff and the great location. The bed was comfortable and the room had everything you would need ...

“I Want to Come Back in the Spring!!” This is a really good place to do business and relax at the same time. The staff is awesome and the property has a great location. Pros: location next to PetCo Park The 22nd floor lounge area!!! I want to come back when there is a game! Meeting rooms are very professionally managed Cons: NONE This hotel has a great dining room, but there are numerous choices of establishments witin a block!!

“Not a bad place” I booked two nights here on a business trip since it was at the time I booked the cheapest 4* hotel with available rooms in the Lower Manhattan area. Hotel lobby is very nice, Art Deco style with restaurant/bar on balcony overhead. staff generally pretty friendly and helpful, and check-in was pretty quick. Rooms, as is sadly typicaly of lower Manhattan, were pretty small but there were plenty of hangers in the (large-ish) closet, and everything worked. Bed was pretty comfortable, no noise issues or anything like that (and I was only on 3rd floor so road noise could've been an issue). Location is OK - at 29th St so a few blocks to the 6 line if you want to take subway, or easy to get cabs to both mid-town and down-town. Area didn't seem at all hostile at night. Didn't try the food.

“Loved the Aloft!” I decided to stay here the night before flying out of PHL airport and I was glad I did. Not only was the room amazing, I had such a great night's sleep, courtesy of a wonderful bed. Between the Bliss toiletries and ultra-mod amenitites, I was very pleased indeed. I kept my car at the hotel while I was away - the $7 per-day fee was less than any of the nearby off-site airport parking. If I hadn't been so intimidated by the fact that the pool was in almost full view of the lobby, I'd have gone swimming too!!

“Great stay” We booked the Fairmont Battery Wharf for New Year's Eve. The location is great. Very close to the North End and with a pretty good Boston Harbor view. The staff was very professional with a very speedy check-in. The room was clean, spacious and well appointed. The bed was reasonably comfortable and everything was in working order. Would definitely stay again.

“Best place to stay in Chicage” My wife and I stayed here for her b-day weekend and they made the stay exceptional. It's right down town near everything and the hotel staff made sure that every little detail was taken care of. We were treated like royalty.
“Great hotel, great location” Stayed at the Drake for two nights on business. Classic hotel. Great architecture. Small room but very comfortable and well appointed. Needs wi-fi.

“A beautiful historic building that has to be seen” My husband and I have just returned from the Custom House in Boston and our opinion is as follows: 1. Beautifully decorated and comfortable rooms with loads of wardrobe space. 2. Extremely helpful front desk, porters and concierge. 3. Location simply marvellous with wonderful restaurants at your doorstep. 4. Shopping to die for ! if you have a car try to visit Wrentham outlet mall - terrific and no state tax in Boston ! 5. This is a simply wonderful Historic Building right in the heart of the city that Marriott must be very proud to have. 6. This is our second time here and we will, definitely, return. 7. Your towels are changed and your bins emptied every day at no extra charge. I have read a review where the person wasn't happy you have to push a button to open the main door ? firstly, it can be freezing in Boston and this is an automatic closing door that can't be left open accidentally and, secondly, this is for security as if you are out after 9pm you have a pass card to use, if not you shouldn't be entering without first speaking to the valet. On the 1st floor Continental breakfast is served between 7-10am weekdays and 7-11 weekends. This breakfast is more than adequate and has just about everything you could possibly want with free tea/coffee/hot chocolate. There is also a cocktail lounge open from 6pm onwards. Nearby, you have a variety of wonderful restaurants as well as Quincy Market. We walked the whole of the city and thoroughly enjoyed ourselved in Boston. Finally, you can if you have a car take a trip out to Cape Cod or Rhode Island which aren't too far away. Cape Cod is about 1hr and its best to have lunch at one of the restaurants down by the marina as they are lovely and have a view of the sea. Hope this helps, when I have loaded my photos onto the computer I will post one of the inside of the Custom House which will show the beauty of it.

“Reflection of the signs of the times....” I had stayed at the Hotel Palomar in 2000 when it was somewhere newly opened. From my several trips to and from the US and to San Francisco, my return this year to this hotel would have been a homecoming... NOT! What used to be the Hotel Palomar noted for being a boutique luxury hotel was terribly terribly all wrong. Perhaps it had something to do with a travel agent in the Philippines using another travel agent in the US, booking this hotel for me. I was charged $380 per night for a King Deluxe and breakfast was $35 per head. I eventually found out that continental breakfast was only $14.50 and that if I had booked through the internet, it would have just been $1 breakfast for two. For the last 5 years I had never booked my trips through the travel agency but corporate policies which are still living in the dinosaur ages dictate that we need to go through a travel agent for auditing purposes. Nevertheless, let me say that the King Deluxe was a letdown. There was no water available in the room (you had to buy it at the nearest Walgreens) and the place looked very desolate. The ambience overlooking the awkward looking Zen garden looked sad and pathetic. There was no view. While the room was kept clean by the cleaning lady, there needs to be a makeover and the carpets need to get changed as it smelled musky and moldy. The bathroom was small and the shower curtains (who still uses shower curtains?!?!) were smelly. This was another place in the room that needed a major makeover. Finally was the food. For $14.50 for a continental breakfast, one could get a more decent meal in the next door Westfield Mall for the same price! Talk about having a muffin, some fruits, a croissant, a cup of coffee or fruit juice for this price? There wasn't even yoghurt to go. Geez!! The fitness center was really tiny and you probably are better off jogging in your room than in the tiny place they called Fitness Center. Of course, coming from Sofitel Los Angeles last July and comparing what Sofitel offered and the price I paid for Hotel Palomar was a no brainer. I expect to get what I paid for and if this is what this hotel offers at this price, this must be really the signs of the times in the US...that they are in recession and will stay this way for a decade more with no more cash to upgrade their hotels and provide people with rooms worth their money. Disappointment is a kind word to describe this hotel. I don't think the Kimpton hotels will make it through the next decade.

“Nice Hotel, Way too many homeless surrounding the hotel!” I stayed here for 4 night as part of the annual AGU conference and the hotel was pretty decent. Here are some pros and cons. Pros: 1.) Centralized location to San Francisco. 2.) Clean rooms and comfortable beds 4.) Free movies nightly in make-shift old-time movie theater 5.) Basket of Altoid-Minis at front desk (free) 6.) Free-WiFi 7.) Front desk staff was nice and polite Cons: 1.) The corner the hotel sits on runs rampant with loud and dirty homeless people that hound you for money non-stop. 2.) The room can get very cold without the heat on. Large windows with poor insulation. 3.) Cost was a bit high for this hotel. I know all hotels in San Francisco are overpriced, but this hotel does not have many perks. 4.) Some of the decor was a bit old and rough. 5.) Windows were really dirty due to city grime and pigeon feces. 6.) Not a place you want to roam around late at night. Adjacent neighborhood is questionable. 7.) It is bad when they have a basket of earplugs at the front desk for your use at night while trying to sleep. I know that some people cannot get used to the city noise, but ear plugs do not give you that warm, fuzzy feeling. I enjoyed my stay here, but can only really give it a 3 out of 5 based on my pros and cons listed above.

“Nice rooms.” We booked through Hotwire and got a good deal for the hotel. The hotel is in a good location right down by Fishermans Wharf, we found the area too touristy for us and did not spend much time down there but we did like the location of the hotel. It was right by a Trader Joe's, great for getting breakfast and dinner supplies if you are on a budget as we were. The only draw back was no fridge in the room, these could be supplied for $10 dollars day - we declined. We walked from the hotel to Union Square numerous times which was about 2 miles and it was hilly but we didn't mind at all. The rooms were nicely decorated and you got Starbucks coffee for the machine in your room, always a bonus.

“coolness can be overrated” I have not stayed downtown NYC for some time. This is right by the WTC - so the area is perhaps over run with tourists. The rooms are not generous in size and this particular W needs aoverhaul. The checkin staff was pleasent but the room lacked towles and supplies - quickly brought but housekeeping needs to be aware. Over a 4 night stay this was a repeated failure. My reservation was in 2 blocks and although they managed to keep me in the same room I did have to return to the front deak and get the key revalidated. WHY.

“Paper Thin Walls - Noisy!” Room was fairly clean, staff was Ok. The biggest issue, though, was the sound levels in the room coming from the neighbors. There was a group of at least 4-5 people in the room next to me partying up until almost 3:00am. If I spoke Spanish I could have made out every word they said all night long - but the only word I understood was the "F"-Bomb, which they kept saying about every 30 seconds. It was also a very cold winter night, so I couldn't turn on the fan to try and drown out the noise. I can't believe that a hotel would allow such large groups to carry on that late into the night. Made for a rough night and a crummy 11 hour drive the next day. I have noticed that a lot of the "old Fairfield Inn" hotels (which this is just by looking at the architecture/design) that have been re-franchised have these super thin and uninsulated walls. The hotel does offer free wifi, and a continental breakfast. Granted, the food was more than likely bought from the Costco right across the street, and the orange juice was sitting in a warm pitcher all morning long (yuk), but it was still a free processed pastry to fill my stomach until I made it out of town for lunch. Lots of other hotels in the area flashing similar rates on their signs - might be worth the time to look around first. (I travel all over the country with my job, and I contribute on EVERY hotel I stay in. Trip Advisor has been a great tool for me, and I contribute fairly, for both good and bad facilities.)

“Great hotel for business travel” Stayed at this Sheraton for a couple months and found it to be consistently good on all levels. Front desk was always friendly and called you by name after you've stayed there a couple times and they start recognizing you. Rooms were what you would expect from a Sheraton Suites... good sized, comfortable bed, separate couch and desk for doing work. Lots of space to do morning exercises in the morning if you don't have time to go down to the gym. Speaking of which the gym was very good, but can be quite crowded in the mornings during the week. Internet always worked when I was there (very important for business travelers). Bathrooms were average, but overall the rooms where clean every time I stayed there. Had breakfast a few times and the staff was helpful and friendly. Again, they always called you by name if you're a regular.

“Still great value for Manhattan” Stayed here for one night. I have stayed before and was impressed with the good service, comfortable rooms and location just off the madness of central Manhattan. Arrived early and they were kind to accommodate my early arrival. The room was very comfortable with a view of the Chrysler building- the view is truly iconic! As always the staff are the key to this hotel, friendly and efficient. Looking forward to my next stay.

“Nice Relaxing Stay” Had a very relaxing stay at the Four Seasons Philadelphia. Check in was pleasant and quick, they could not have been nicer or more professional. The swimming pool is wonderful, very soothing and the whirlpool is relaxing and enjoyable. The rooms are nice and quiet, but very traditional-not for everyone's taste, but the beds are comfortable. Bathrooms need to be updated with the new Four Seasons standards (separate showers and bathtubs are not in the regular rooms). Rooms service was quick and accurate, a little pricey.

“Huge room, yummy free breakfast” The Hyatt Place Seattle has a lot going for it. I was impressed with my first stay at this property. I won the property on Priceline.com with a 3-star, Seattle Center location bid. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. I was offered a tour of the hotel upon arrival after I checked in. :) The hotel is located near the Seattle Center and Belltown. There are a number of restaurants and bars within walking distance. There is a Walgreen's across the street from the hotel as well. I was in town for a Taj Mahal show at Jazz Alley, the room was well equipped for what I needed, as well as an easy walk to Jazz Alley. I was entertaining three of my friends before and after the show, and there was plenty of room for the four of us to relax, have a few drinks and watch a slide show of photos I took on my most recent excursion to Europe. :) The room was very large with a separate seating area separated by a partition from the bed. A sectional sofa with a large ottoman allowed all of us to sit comfortably and visit. The room has a small refrigerator to store beverages and snacks. Their is a large flat screen TV with a data input panel in the stand so I could attach a RGB or HDMI cable from my laptop to watch the slide slow. The king size bed was comfortable and the curtains did a nice job of blocking out the light in the morning. :) The breakfast was very good...I had a ham, egg and cheese muffin which I took with me on my walk to the Space Needle in the morning. There were two free coffee stations in the lobby that were open until 10 AM. The hotel has a small coffee stand/snack shop for items to purchase, which I did not use. Underground, secured parking was $20 + tax. Very reasonable for downtown Seattle. The only downside to the hotel was the room to room noise. While not annoying, I could hear the maid cleaning in the adjacent room. Overall, the hotel is a great value...I would definitely stay here again.

“A Unique Experience!” When I first learned that the Liberty Hotel in Boston used to be a jailhouse and still maintains a bit of that history, I just felt as if I had to stay here. On a four night trip to Boston on business, I decided to stay the last night at the Liberty Hotel, one of the very few Luxury Collection hotels in the U.S. Upon arriving at the hotel, you'll notice the small entrance and the historic building that once used to be a jailhouse. Once entering in and going up to the lobby (which is located one level up), you can't help but look around you at how amazing this property really is. The lobby exudes of luxury and class, and is easily one of the best hotel lobbies I have ever been to. The lobby alone might just be worth the money spending here, it's one of those places which will just force your camera out and take pictures at all angles. Checking-in took longer than expected, but the hotel was sold out and there were only a couple front desk agents that were working as hard as they could to get all guests checked-in. Some guests might have looked frustrated, but the agents never showed any signs of this and always greeted everyone professionally and with a smile on their face. Once my turn came up, I was informed that I was upgraded to a Superior Suite on the 8th floor as a part of my Platinum member benefits. A pleasant surprise indeed! I was also offered a glass of fine champagne which was being offered to all guests checking in, and I gladly accepted. I have not seen this at any other Luxury Collection hotel! The room itself was very comfortable and filled with opulence. The living room area is spacious and has a small dining room area which then leads you down a small corridor to the half bath. The views from this room are amazing, you have the river right there and you can see the Boston skyline as well looking towards Copley. The bedroom was very comfortable and up to LC hotel standards, and the main bathroom was in one word - luxurious. Spotless and elegant, this was definitely one of the classier rooms I have stayed at. Well done Liberty Hotel for having well-appointed rooms! In the evening I spent a bit of time with my colleagues at the Liberty Bar which was quite packed, but had a great social scene and an energetic environment. Even better was walking downstairs to Alibi, the lounge/bar that makes it feel as if you are walking through an actual jailhouse except with all the fancy furniture. The drinks were priced at about what you'd really expect to pay at a Luxury Collection hotel, but the cocktails were very much worth it. They've really done a fantastic job of preserving the history of this location, you would never think you were in a hotel but you'd also never think you were in a jailhouse either! A good mix of old and new. The next day I had a chance to grab a quick bite at CLINK. which is located on the lobby level. This is a great dining spot and well worth it for the experience if you get a chance, and the food itself is very good. The kitchen area is open so you can catch all the action, and the dining area looks as if it is several jail cells joined together. Just like everything else at this hotel, it was very unique and this is something any history buff would enjoy. I really enjoyed my stay at the Liberty Hotel, it is one of those properties that you just have to try if you get the chance. There are other Starwood hotels in Boston, and they are all good but this is one of the few Luxury Collection hotels in the Northeast and I believe it lives up to the standards of LC hotels in other cities. I read about this hotel prior to choosing to stay here and was intrigued before I even arrived, and when I left I was left in awe and raving about the incredible and memorable experience at the luxurious Liberty Hotel! I will be back here the next time up in Boston!

“Fun & Trendy in Tribeca” Stayed here for 2 nights over Labor Day weekend. It is as small boutique hotel and I can only vouch for the room I was in but it was a very small room. What helped in our case was we had a nice terrace so we did not feel too closed in. I like fun and trendy small hotels so I definately enjoyed my stay and when in NYC I am mostly running about so I did not mind so much the room was small. It is in a great downtown neighborhood in Tribeca. So if you want to be in the downtown area this is in a good location. We paid only 158.00 per night so what I got for what I paid was of good value. The staff was very friendly and we had to leave before our 3rd night because of a family emergency and they were nice enough not to charge us!

“Perfect Hotel in Downtown Baltimore” This hotel was a welcome respite from the hustle and bustle of downtown Baltimore. Conveniently located near the convention center and Orioles Park, the hotel is new and the rooms are very comfortable and cozy. The bed was amazing. I had one of the best nights sleep in a long time. The service is friendly and efficient. Highly recommend it.

“Perfect location & Typical Marriott Rooms,” Disclaimer: Paid using Marriott Reward Points. Good: - Typical Marriott room with the nice, cushioned bedding and white sheets, typical room amenities, etc. Really enjoyed the many different scented toiletries that were refreshed every day and the chocolates left every night. - Prompt and quick check-in - Staff were very helpful when approached and assisted with recommending restaurants away from the hotel. - Wonderful, perfect location right on the water, next to the Acquarium, right next to the subway, less than 5 minute walk to most tourist attractions, etc.... - I know my wife was thrilled there was a Starbucks in the downstairs........ Bad: - The hotel was nicely designed to look like the other pier type designs, but this resulted in obstructions over half of the hotel windows, really harming the potentially gorgeous views of the city and waterfront. - My room was on the side of the hotel closest to the city (away from the water) and had a moderately loud air conditioning sound when it was running. - Atypical for Marriotts, we noticed that room service trays and items tended to stay in the hall for a long time. - Parking is RIDICULOUS - around $40 a day if I recall. For the love of goodness, if you are flying - DON'T bother with a car if you are only here for Boston. You can take the subway from the airport (about 10 minutes) and then take subway/ walk everywhere else in the city. No reason for a car. SIDE TIP: a) They have 2 half price ticket booths for "day-of" broadway shows. We got seats to Blue Man Group for $25!! [--] b) Get a tourist card. Just remember they are only worth it if you want to, and have time to, see enough of the attractions. There are MANY to choose from - here are some in my order of preference. 1) [--] 2) [--] 3) [--] c) Buy the 7 day unlimited transit travel pass for $15.00 before leaving the airport: [--]

“I love this place...” I stayed here last 4th of July weekend and really took a liking to this hotel. Rooms are clean and modern, not what I would consider luxurious, but nice. Bathrooms are huge with both a walk-in shower and a separate tub. Floor to ceiling windows. The absolute best thing about this hotel is it's location. Great bars and restaurants right outside the front door. In the summer time this whole area is just crawling with party people. If you're into nightlife, stay at this place.

“Huge hotel” You walk in to a very impressive lobby with a great bar to the left that a good place to meet for drinks and bar food, its open and perfect size. The rooms are very nice just like any other Hilton. We were hoping for a brunch on a Sunday but not one. Just the regular menu but the drivers will take you to area restaraunts plus they gave us a free dessert, just for asking. Very nice and restful stay. (If you are on the arena side there is a amphitheater that may have something going on that you may hear in your room)

“Clean, quiet, and the best hotel we stayed at by the airport.” We visit Colorado about once a year, and are always looking for a nice hotel to stay at on our last night. Well, we found it with this one. Very nice, clean, quiet, and a great breakfast. Don't quote me, but it gets set up earlier than said, so it was nice for us with an early departure. There are a couple casual restaurants nearby, and gas stations for the renatl car. The staff was very helpful, and we just had a nice room (chairs), and a good night's sleep. My one improvement would be to have a bigger buisiness center, as it is tight quarters. Otherwise, we will definitely be back. The price is really good for the area, too.

“Very Kind Staff” I stayed here for one night following a long International flight. The staff could not have been kinder to an exhausted guest. The hotel is completing a major renovation. It feels like a brand new Hampton Inn. The bathrooms are completely redone, even the pool is new. Only problem I had is that the shutte bus does not pick up at the airport where all the other hotels do, so it was hard to find them. Otherwise a great stay.
“This is a nice small hotel” For value for money I think it is a great hotel. Service was good. Staff well mannered. The room was nice, huge flat screen television. Great location.

“Absolutely wonderful” I stayed here for a business conference. My husband and I agreed that this hotel is one of the nicest we have stayed in. We booked a standard room, which was beautifully appointed and spacious, with a nice city view. The facility was lovely, but what sets the Fairmont Olympic apart from others in its class is the service. It was perfect-- extremely helpful and attentive, but not cloying. Every person that we dealt with-- from the bell staff, to the reception desk, to random employees we just passed in the hallway-- was courteous, professional and greeted us with a smile and an offer to assist us. It's hard to describe perfect service in words, but when you experience it, it's much appreciated. I would not stay anywhere else in Seattle, as it would be a let-down after the Fairmont.

“Not bad for a short stay” We stayed here for one night passing through Seattle on the way from Vancouver to Olympic NP. To be honest we actually found this place better than we were expecting - especially for the price. The rooms all opened to inside hallways - the hotel was several floors and had elevators. The rooms were pretty dated and had a bit of a musty smell, but the rooms were spacious and the beds comfortable with the A/C working fine. You actually had kind of a view of downtown Seattle out your window. The breakfast was the full typical La Quinta breakfast with lots of choices. The hotel does charge for parking (I think something like $10/night). However, we had to rent a car the next morning, and the host let us park for free for a couple of hours while we loaded it up. There's lots of parking meters nearby anyway. One of the elevators was constantly out of service, so you had to wait and wait and wait for the elevator. The area - its not great, but I wouldn't call it seedy - its mostly just remote compared to the rest of downtown, with just a couple of more run-down motels nearby. There were some great restaurants just a few blocks away - and we walked to them. There was also a Whole Foods like 2 blocks away. The price was excellent for downtown Seattle - really could not be beat at like $100/night. And there's really nothing flat out wrong with the place except the elevator. However, I'd only recommend a one or two night stay here at most. The area is a bit depressing, and the hotel a bit dated, dark, and dingy - so if you're just visiting Seattle for the first time or don't make it back much - you might want a nicer place for better memories.

“Not as good as past trips” Have been here at least 4 times now (once yearly since 2008) and this was by far the worst experience we've had. The positive: Check-in staff is friendly, rooms were clean. However, no information book in room (re: breakfast, fitness center etc) which I think I remember being there in past. Instead, there was a laminated piece of paper with phone/internet information, which had been drawn on by a kid. Breakfast was awful- no hot items, trays not refilled with baked goods, etc. Breakfast was much better in past times I have stayed here. I'm not sure if it was just the room we were in (not club level) but shower didn't work that well. Also not that soundproof- we could hear people fighting in the next room. This has always been our go-to hotel for the Bay Area and we generally love JDV hotels. Most likely will not be going back to this one.

“Nice boutique, great location” Very nice boutique hotel in a great location. The room was very comfortable with a great bathroom. Good shower water pressure and lots of counter space. Plus a magnifying mirror and even a little stool that was a nice touch. Much more space than I expected for an urban boutique. Bed was comfortable and the linens were good quality. I like that they desk was a little lower so you could actually put your computer on it comfortably, and it rolled around so it was nice to position it where you wanted it. I could have used a few more outlets near the bed so I could plug my phone in, but overall, the room was very well put together. The checkin was efficient and the staff very helpful. The doormen were really friendly and didn't make me feel like their hand was constantly out for a tip. They do a breakfast buffet on every floor and it was MUCH better than I expected. It was great to just walk out and grab something. They have a cocktail hour that I never made it to - but will next time. I ordered room service from Harry Carreys across the street. This is a great idea since they don't mark up the food, and it's great. They do add an 18% gratuity and a $2.50 service charge, but that's totally reasonable. And it was very fast. I think more hotels should do this, everyone does what they are good at!

“Ottimo” Al solito ottimo hotel della catena Hilton, posizione molto buona,camere molto belle anche se non enormi,pulizia assoluta. Forse l'unico difetto e' la dimensione di questo hotel che lo rende un po'caotico nella hall ma a parte questo aspetto e'assolutamente consigliato. Assolutamente ingiustificato il costo del parcheggio per l'auto. Pro: posizione,camere ed in generale il servizio Hilton Contro: hall caotica e prezzo del parcheggio auto elevato

“Would stay again, nice place, close to all” This was my first time at this hotel, 10th time in Baltimore, so I have stayed at others in the area. It doesnt have all the bells and whistles as some of the nicer places but it was great. Nice room, (ran out of toilet paper-no spare within), nice service at front desk, good breakfast (included with stay) and helpful service. Secure as well at night with key entry into the lobby area and elevators after a certain time, so that was nice. Parking garag across the street. Had to bring bags uo ourselves, a little surprised, but overall a good stay and would stay again. Thanks

“Exceeded my expectations! Will go back there.” After reading many negative reviews of this hotel, I did not expect much. Well- I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel was clean, the staff efficient and very helpful with directions and tickets, etc. There was a small stain in the carpet, but nothing major. The caution about the water temperature in the showers is warranted. They are very hard to adjust. We arrived at 10:00 a.m. and a room was available for us. The room had a queen bed and locking refrigerator stocked with liquors and beverages available for purchase. We chose to buy our own bottled water and refrigerate it. The location is the BEST. I traveled with my college age daughter and went out during the day and evening feeling completely safe in the neighborhood. There is a market set up outside of the hotel to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables daily. There is also a Dunkin Donuts next door for coffee fans like myself. We did not have our meals in the hotel since there are so many fine establishments to try in the area. I will stay at this hotel again.

“Small but great location” When they say the room is small and views will be of the brick building next door, they aren't joking. But the room was clean and nice, the staff really helpful, and the location great. Read the websites FAQ so you know what you are getting, we skipped the tiny breakfast and went down the street instead. Would stay here again if we come back without the family.

“Hipster Hotel full of not quite hipster guests” As much as I was prepared to be put off by the hipsters populating this place, I really liked it. The hotel and bar staff is very friendly, tho the restaurant staff a bit too NY trendy/languid. Loved the design and decor, loved their straightforward attitude about the price of their rooms. Rooms were comfy, but I opted to upgrade from the tiny "cheap" to a more practical King. Lobby is a scene, full of apple laptops during the day, partiers at night. Kinda fun, if you're up for it.

“Very Good Experience” We (my husband and I, with our two teenagers) stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn West 35th for four days over Easter. We had a very good experience. The hotel is very conveniently located, and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. The hotel was very busy the entire time we were there, yet service never lagged. My only complaint--the room was small, but that is just typical New York. However, it was kept very clean, which means much more! We were happy with our choice of hotel.

“This is a Warwick??” I stayed here with a couple friends and we were not particularly impressed. The service was fine, but the building just didn't feel like it was up to the luxury standards you would expect from the Warwick chain. There was a tacky red sticker on the inside of the elevator that said "watch your step". The light fixtures in the hallways were like cheap 15.99 units out of a cookie-cutter entry level home. The wallpaper, carpet, and overall look of the place was just very "homey", for lack of a better word. I know it's a historic hotel but I have stayed in many and it's not hard to decorate in a way that is modern while recognizing the history of the building. The sheets were VERY rough and scratchy--more motel 6 than Warwick. It's a great looking building on the outside, and the location in the Oak Lawn/Turtle Creek area is good, but that doesn't save it for me. If I hadn't stayed at a discounted rate through the Historic Hotels of America employee trade program, I would have really been upset. This luxury wannabe is not worth the full price.

“Still a reliable Union Square Hotel” I had not stayed here in a while because the prices have been crazy - but recently, the rates dropped to a more reasonable range. I stayed for a couple of days for work meetings. The rooms still look up to date and fresh even though the hotel has been around for a while now. The shower, toilet and bath area could stand a more modern version (especially the shower and toilet). Towels were a bit scratchy and not so fluffy you woudl expect with a higher end boutique hotel. There is a small safe in the closet. The lighting and decor are cool and very trendy, as always. service was good as well at the front desk and at the door. The doormen hailed hard to get cabs when needed on the busy mornings. The Asia de Cuba restaurant is gone - it has been replaced by another restaurant that is new. The front desk gave out discount cards to get guests to try it - i didnt get a chance to. All in all, this still seems to be a good option if the price is good.

“Fine for a short stay” I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights for $80 a night booked on priceline. I didn't eat at the hotel's restaurant which was closed for refurbishment, but the room was fine with all usual amenities. The free wifi & in-room tea & coffee supplies were welcome and the staff was helpful & friendly. I left my luggage here for 3 nights while I went on a trip out of DC & they were only too happy to look after it for me. The hotel is fine, if a bit bland, but for $80 a night in DC it was good value, although it is a little away from many points of interest in DC. I'd probably stay here again at this price.

“Great for wedding guests” I blocked about a dozen rooms at this wonderful little hotel for our daughter's wedding guests to stay at during her March 2012 wedding. Hotel Highland is just a few minutes away from the ceremony and reception site so the location was convenient. They also had free shuttle service and also free breakfast included. Our guests were very happy. Some of them arrived a few days before and stayed a couple days after the wedding. The hotel reception staff and sales dept were so helpful. They're close to many restaurants, a large mall and it has easy access to the interstate but they're in a quiet location on a side street so you don't get a lot of noise. This is really quite a gem of a hotel and I highly recommend it.

“Very Cool” We stayed in a Master Suite for two nights during the week. The check in was smooth, valet service prompt ($30 per day). When we got into our room, it was rather warm, so we turned the AC down to 68 degrees, unpacked and headed out to the streets to find a place for lunch. The Gaslamp Quarter is very cool. There are lots of shops and restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. We got back to our room and it really had not cooled down much (after 2 hours!). It was really warm outside for San Diego - 85 degrees, so we left it set mid 60's and went down to the hotel restaurant where we were seated in a wonderful private booth and the service and food was fantastic! The pool is really cool, we had a glass of wine in the evening on the patio and also took advantage of the nightly wine reception in the lobby sitting room - very nice touch! All in all, we thought the hotel was great. The deep fuji soaking/jetted tub in the bathroom with the window looking out to the downtown buildings was a treat each night before bed!!! It's alitte pricey, but well worth it for the room size, service and location.

“Okay stay for this Downtown Location” This hotel is located centrally downtown and two blocks from Nationwide Arena and directly across the street from the Convention Center. However, the only staff member that impressed me was the bellman. He saw me outside and asked if i needed help, and was nice to get a taxi for me. The rest of the staff were kind of lame, didn't welcome me asked for my credit card and that was it. Trying to get transportation the next morning was hard even though they had set up transportation for me. The closets are extermely small beware if you have nice clothes.

“I'm Loving it!!” Wowsers, This is a really nice property. The staff were very friendly. I loved the rooms. This is literally a home away from home with all of the amenities of a one bedroom apartment. The floor plan was nicely done and the rooms very spacious. I would highly recommend this property not only for business travelers but also families traveling on vacation to the Dallas area.

“excellent stay” I highly recommend this hotel. I got a great deal, booking through United and using a combination of miles and some money down. The hotel is immaculate. It looks and feels crisp and clean, partly due to the Asian aesthetic and partly due to incredible upkeep. The room was large for San Francisco, and the beds were very comfortable. Views through the large picture windows on the upper floors are stunning. The bathroom was a delight with a large vanity, pleasant lighting, and a fantastic shower with superb water pressure. The gym is great, but prepare to pay an extra $10 to use it (very reasonable). The location is ideal, just a couple blocks from Union Square and near great restaurants and bars. The neighborhood feels quite safe, but within about five blocks south and west, it can deteriorate rapidly, but this is San Francisco, so it's a good idea to watch your belongings wherever you go. Service was first-rate - friendly and helpful.

“Better than expected” we had wonderful service, clean rooms, REALLY comfortable beds, right beside the rendezvouse, best ribs on the planet i may add, staff was wonderful and courtious, nice facilities, but they only had one working elevator at that time but i am sure the problem was only temporary

“Very good hotel -- I recommend it” I liked everything about this hotel. Nice open space for gathering with colleagues, excellent meeting room and facilities, good location near the airport, comfortable beds and rooms, and a nice restaurant and lounge (and Starbucks) on site. Service was very good too. There are train tracks nearby so some of my colleagues heard that during the night, but I didn't or it just lulled me to sleep. I would recommend this hotel.

“Would stay here again!” I stayed here for two nights with my husband. Outstanding hotel, great features and customer service. Plenty of spaces to park, free internet in rooms, business center in lobby offers free internet and printing. This is a slightly older hotel compared to the Hilton up the street, but the staff is much friendlier and helpful. Beds were very comfortable. Housekeeping promptly cleans rooms in the morning. Close to everything in the Mission Valley area. We would return here again.

“A wonderful city hotel in downtown Boston.” My wife and I just returned from weekend getaway at the Nine Zero in Boston. Hotel and Location: The Nine Zero is a deluxe boutique hotel located near the northeast corner of Boston Common adjacent to the Freedom Trail. The Nine Zero is within walking distance of the Public Garden, the Government Center, the Theater District, Faneuil Hall, the North End (Little Italy) and downtown restaurants, shopping and nightlife. There's also a nearby "T" (subway) station about a block away. We found the hotel to be so conveniently located that once we handed our car keys to the valet at check-in, we didn't need them again until we checked out. The hotel's somewhat minimalist decor can best be described as "urban chic". The hotel offers complementary wine tastings nightly in the hotel lobby, which is a fantastic amenity. The Nine Zero's well-trained staff is very professional, gracious and accommodating. Room: As a "Kimpton in Touch" member I got a very reasonable "One Day Sale" rate of $209 for a King Premier Room (compared to the $279 weekend rack rate). I must admit that due to the "territory-marking behavior" of dogs I was skeptical of staying at a "pet-friendly" property, but my concerns were unfounded. The room was very clean and stylishly decorated. The extremely comfortable king-sized bed had plush linens, a warm down comforter and the softest down pillows we’ve ever slept on. The marble bathroom was very nice and my wife loved the hotel’s deluxe toiletries. The room and bathroom were more spacious than most standard city hotel rooms. Among the many appreciated in-room amenities were chocolate truffles and raspberries at nightly turndown. For those travelling on business, there's free high speed Internet and wireless connectivity in each room. Dining: We had dinner at "KO Prime", an innovative steakhouse located on the hotel's second floor. KO Prime is an extraordinary restaurant named after renowned Executive Chef Ken Oringer (formally of the Boston Eliot Hotel's Mobil 4-Star restaurant "Clio"). The appetizers, sides, entrees and desserts were all delicious, portions were generous, the service and presentation were superb and the wine list was impressive. The restaurant's "hip" atmosphere was trendy but refined. Like most fine restaurants, KO Prime is somewhat pricey - plan on spending $100 per person for a four-course dinner not including wine (if you order the Kobe Beef, plan on spending at least twice that per person). Most of the reds on the wine list were priced between $100 to $150 per bottle (there were few offerings below that). In fact, my only complaint about the restaurant is that the wine list markup seemed excessive to me. (I have a small wine cellar at home consisting mainly of Barolo, Barbaresco and red Bordeaux, so I consider myself to be pretty good at "cherry picking" limited-production/good value reds off of restaurant wine lists). These days, I can usually find a very good/delicious 1996-2001 Barolo or Barbaresco or "Cru Classe" Bordeaux from a better producer for around $80, which I consider to be a relatively good value at finer restaurants. Unfortunately, I was unable to find a good value at that price point on KO Prime's wine list. Despite this, KO Prime is definitely worth visiting for a special occasion. Overall, the Nine Zero is a wonderful city hotel in a great location... The "One Day Sale" rate of $209 was also a great value... We'd definitely stay here again!

“Good location” Good location within walking distance to the Grove/Farmer's Market. Hotel is a renovated low-rise motel-like building. Rooms are clean and fairly basic in its own quirky farm theme. Given its price, would highly recommend this hotel.

“It's an ok property” Nothing much to complain about, nothing much to shout about. I choose the location due to the proximity to my clients plant. It is right on the gulf (I45) freeway. Due to the near freeway, to room noise was quite loud. Plus its Houston, so the AC has to run all the time. I would suggest a room on the southeast side away from the freeway. Otherwise bring some comfortable ear plugs if road noise bothers you. The property is in good condition. Room furnishings is several years old, but in good shape. The TV’s have been upgraded to flat screens. My king suite had microwave and a refrigerator. They host a reception in the lobby from 5:00 to 6:30pm. They offer soda, wine and beer along with chips and a hot snack (think pizza rolls). That is a nice touch. They always seem to run a bit late, yesterday the drinks were put out after 5:30pm. And breakfast is routinely late all week, except for the morning the cook didn’t show up at all. I was impressed they had to go bags for those looking for breakfast on the day the cook was missing. There are some restaurant nearby but its reported that the neighborhood is not the best. A car is required for this location.

“Elegant - Carming -” I stayed at the Fairfax for only one night. But it was enough for me to decide that this hotel is odd. This hotel is different from other in the Starwood System. I am a Gold SPG member and travel often. This hotel used to be a Westin. Now its part of the Luxury Collection brand. My impression is its neither. The hotel is in a class by itself. It lacks identity with any of the Starwood Brands. Its supposed to be part of the Luxury Collection. But sure does not act or feel like one of those other property's. When you arrive at the hotel it seems luxurious and cozy from the outside. The Bellmen and valet greeted us almost immediately on the royal red carpet. All that was missing was the white gloves. They where elegantly uniformed and the entrance, while small, was elegant and reminiscent of another era. The hotel sits in a rather posh part of town close to Dupont Circle and across the street from the Indian Embassy and others. Check in was a quick, friendly, and efficient. The again elegantly dressed agents where very polite and made you feel welcome. The lobby however was small, cramped, and disappointing. It has great potential. You can tell they have tried to make it work. But it does not. The area for check in is small and uncomfortable. There are steps and no ramps for the luggage. Its a very old building. But the hotel lobby is more 1960 Howard Johnson then 2009 Luxury Collection. Elegant wood adorns the walls and paintings abound. But its not luxury. The restaurant and lounge areas are nice and cozy. But they look tired and worn. Elevators to rooms where ok. They are old and vintage. But they could use a little more up keep. My room (702) was small but lovely. Be sure to get one of the rooms 700 - 720 with the nice views. The rooms in the back face a generators, machines, and a dirty roof. Not very luxurious at all. They have made no effort to make that area even re motley nice. Its awfully. This are could be canvassed and landscaped to make more pleasant. I was fortunate to have an amazing view of Mass Ave and the Embassy across the street. But my friends in (726) had that awful view. The rooms in the back with the bad view have full bathtubs and are larger. The rooms upfromt with the nice view only have showers. Room was very elegant and clean. Super clean. The room smelled good and looked luxury. New flat screen Tv, elegant British toiletry's. Frette Towels. A lot of the basics of a luxury hotel. But it was still lacking. My room did not have robes. I had to call. According to them the housekeper simpl forgot. to place them there. But I think they just don't put them in the rooms unless you ask. In a true luxury hotel. The robes are always there. They did send them right away which was nice. The room has a nice closet and ample bath. I-Pod compatible deluxe stereo for music which was very nice. A beautiful old style alarm clock was a nice touch. Hotel has free shoe service 1 pair per room daily. The Internet charge is 10 per day. Bathroom amenity's where nice. But very basic. Glycerin soap by sink, bath soap in shower, bath gel, shampoo, conditioner, and lotion. They do not provide mouthwash and other toiletry items youd expect at a luxury hotel. If you are en Elite SPG member. This hotel does not have SPG Gold/Platinum dedicated check in lines. There is no SPG floor, no concierge lounge, no recognition except for the key card holder. No welcome amenity noting to make you feel special. They do not even provide a free bottle of water in the room or anything. But they did honor the 4PM check out for me and that's a huge benefit. But it still would of ben nice for the hotel to recognize a frequent guest in some way. But they did not see to really care if you are a preferred guest or not. The 7th floor is unique in that it has a seating area just outside the elevators. Its a cozy seating area and we sat there a few times just to chat or wait for each other to get ready in the mornings or at night on way to dinner. Its a great meeting place and a wonderful concept. We enjoyed this area very much. The gym was small but well equipped and very clean. They had magazines, tv, and bathrooms. But there was no fruit, no bottled water, and no sauna, spa, whirlpool, swimming pool or any of the amenity's one has come to expect of a luxury hotel. The Concierge was not always at his desk. So I had to call 3x before I got through. He was very informative and well versed on the area and where to go. But he was also somewhat obnoxious. Other hotel staff members lack the Grace and training of a St. Regis or a Ritz hotel. But you can tell they are trying. The hotel is an a great location and a very safe neighborhood. Its 2 blocks from the Metro (Dupont Circle) station and within walking distance to many sights, a 24 Hr CVS, and restaurants. Stay here for the neighborhood, the plush rooms, and easy in and out check out. But if you are looking for a true 4 star experience. I suggest going somewhere else. If you do stay here - take the train (Red) one station over to "Woodley Park" and eat at "Gotham City" its open 24 hours a day and its a landmark in DC.There breakfast is served all day and its divine!
“Cheeky hotel with all the basics, good location and service” Love the front desk staff here- they will go the extra mile for you. Great location, nice big if somewhat cheesy rooms.

“Great View in Downtown Austin” Very well run property, situated on Lady Bird Lake in downtown Austin. Getting a high floor with a downtown view is a must. The view at night is spectacular! Our room was very spacious and nicely appointed. The bathroom fixtures were a bit dated. Overall a very good property and we would definitely return.

“Me gustó mucho.Lo recomiendo.” Nos tuvimos q quedar una noche en este hotel por que nuestro vuelo a Lima se canceló por causa de las cenizas del volcán Peyehue en Chile. Tiene un bus gratis aeropuerto/ hotel ,hotel/aerop pasa cada 20 ́ aprox. Me ofrecieron una tarjeta para llamadas internacionales ilimitadas por 7 U$ diarios, me vino muy bien ya q tenía q hacer llamadas a Argentina. Pero las llamadas locales te cobran 2 U$ cada una y también tuve q hacer varias. Las habit son cómodas,no muy grandes. Tiene piscina,gym,un bar donde comer comidas rápidas y buffet variado y barato. Tiene un restaurante donde se pueden comer comidas mas elaboradas. El personal muy simpático y servicial.Por esa zona solo hay hoteles. Me hubiera gustado disfrutar mas del hotel pero estuve de paso y bastante nerviosa por la cancelación del vuelo y la incertidumbre de no saber cuando se iba a normalizar la situación.Pero bueno, las vacaciones en EEUU fueron espectaculares, solo tuve este inconveniente,insignificante, diría, teniendo en cuenta los momentos felices vividos en el gran país del Norte!!

“Just a Perfect Stay...” I'm continually impressed by the Kimpton employees and hotels. I booked a reservation last Friday, showed up on Sunday to a lovely upgraded room, and a stellar Martini 'Bar' in my room as an amenity. The ceiling heights had to be at least 15 feet tall. The building incredibly, and lovingly restored. From the email I received asking if I need a car service before I arrived; to the front desk being sweet, friendly and professional when I arrived; to the delicious room service from Poste - the first evening was perfect. The bathroom had the biggest and deepest jacuzzi tub I've ever seen. The rooms furnishings were stylish and clean. I HIGHLY recommend the hotel to everyone!

“Renovated-review” One of my favorite spots in Chicago is the recently renovated Marriott Chicago on Michigan Avenue. However, I hadn't stayed since the renovation began and was eagerly anticipating this trip to see how it all turned out. The location is still in the heart of it all and the exterior is unchanged, but upon entering the lobby, it was apparent that this was not the same, outdated lobby of old, but a "futuristic" interpretation of what a lobby should look like. Gone are the 2nd floor shops, replaced by a grand staircase leading to "The Restaurant." The bar area is draped in neon and the seating is now more than ample. I will say that it all seems a bit much for me. Not as "hotel-like" as before, with a certain air of pretention. However, I'm still at ease in this hotel and I am glad that I can still fell like this after such a big change. The rooms are unchanged. Small and cosy, with upscale bedding. The bathrooms are also small, but clean. I found the public areas overly air conditioned, but my room was nice and toasty. I love the Marriott's total nonsmoking policy. My room and everywhere else in the hotel was pleasantly without that stale smoky smell. "The Restaurant" was better than average. They only lacked in the bread department, with rolls that were obviously packaged. The lake trout was wonderful, as was the homemade mango sorbet. The staff at this hotel makes you feel welcome and I can honestly say that, even with the neon, I'm still at home in the Marriott Chicago.

“Nice business hotel” This is a nice business or convention hotel, good location, nice property. Stayed here 2 nites in March 2007, pleasant service, good food, drinks in bar a bit small but fairly priced.

“Perfection.” This was our first stay at a Park Hyatt and we are in love. My husband and I stayed here when we were in DC for a wedding on August 17-19, 2012. The best way I can describe the superb experience of staying here is that it was like the hotel was thoughtfully designed to be as efficient and unannoying as possible, and that the staff was trained to be as unobtrusively helpful, competent and friendly as possible. It's rare for a hotel stay to be completely free of any annoyances whatsoever but this place killed it. It's like a sleek, unstuffy-fied version of a certain old school 5 star hotel, in terms of service, yet at a completely reasonable price point. I got the feeling that if I called the front desk and asked for a "single plum floating in perfume in a man's hat" (yes, that's a Simpsons reference), it would not faze anyone, and someone would make that happen post haste. What Makes This Place Awesome in Every Way: Incredibly FAST and efficient checkin and checkout process. The staff member at the front desk who checked us in even offered to add me to the rewards program so I could get extra miles on my United card. Valet service is fast and friendly and you can call the front desk to have the car waiting for you if you're in a hurry. Altogether (with taxes and fees and whatnot), parking comes to a hair under 50 bucks a day. Staff members say "welcome back" with a smile every time you enter the hotel (I should add that they actually seem to mean it)! Every single staff member we encountered (and we encountered many) seemed genuinely friendly, without being chatty. We stayed in a Park Deluxe King on the 6th floor, which looked exactly like the room photos on the website (no surprises). We booked through Jetsetter.com for $175/night, which in my mind, was a total steal. Bed was insanely comfortable. Sheets were super smooth and crisp, down comforter was airy and the perfect weight, and pillows were wonderful. And no superfluous pillows or other stuff to have to move when you actually want to get down to the business of going to sleep! It was like a zen cocoon that I did not wish to leave. Ever. Bathroom was spotless, clad in lots of neutral marble, deep soaking tub, and the cleaning staff provided additional toiletries each day (Le Labo in the bergamot scent). Shaker boxes on the counter contained the hair dryer and shower cap, sewing kit, cotton swabs, toothpaste, etc. The built in closet/wardrobe had a mix of wooden and padded hangers and a shoe shine kit. I think they have a complimentary shoe shine as well where you can give them your shoes, if I recall correctly (we did not try it). The room had great lighting and responsive temperature controls and easy to use, free wi-fi (having to pay for wi-fi is one of my pet peeves). No need for log in information or weird passwords, you just fire up your computer or ipad and a window pops up asking you for your room number and that's it. Wi-fi speed was not the fastest but there was an ethernet cord artfully hidden in one of the boxes on top of the desk (and they have what looked like a well-equipped business center if you really needed it). Minibar and minifridge was in the room which was useful for storing some leftover dessert we brought back from Founding Farmers..The housekeeping staff leave two complimentary bottles of water on each nightstand every day. No irons or ironing boards in the room but we asked the front desk and minutes later, one was brought up to our room. Ipod dock/speaker on one of the nightstands- This place is extremely quiet - I saw other people out and about so I know we weren't the only ones staying at the hotel but it sure felt that way in our room and the hallways outside our room. The pool area was beautiful, sun-lit and airy, and not crowded, and the gym was clean and full of newer equipment. Complimentary coffee and tea in the lobby starting at 6 am (no coffee machines in the rooms). Sadly we didn't get to try the celebrated Blue Duck Tavern or Tea Room (or room service) but they both looked fantastic and we hope to try them when we return to DC in the future. What Makes This Place Not So Great: Nothing! Haven't you read the foregoing?! STAY HERE!

“Great value. Super great location.” This hotel was a little gem. Great location, affordable, clean, super nice staff. Breakfast provided well done. Will stay here again. Only issue, not the hotels fault was the Just Tires store blasts their music at the crack of dawn. Could here that with closed windows. Try to get a room not facing that store.

“Well Located, Undergoing Renovations” Stayed recently for a 2 night business trip. The Hyatt is on the edge of downtown within reasonable waking distance to most of the sights and destinations in Boston. I was able to easily walk to the Quincy Market and North End area for restaurants and Chinatown is a stone's throw from the hotel. The hotel is also very near the downtown crossing T station for other destinations. Overall the service from staff was nice. My room was large and comfortable. Downside at the moment is the lobby is undergoing renovations and feels somehow off. It is on the 3rd floor from street level so 2 elevators are required to access rooms. The fitness center was just OK and quite a hike from the elevators on the 6th floor. Not a bad stay but I'm not sure I'd stay here again.

“Great hote, inconvenient to Metro” This is an excellent DC hotel with great weekend rates. The only drawback, and a minor one, is that it is a seven block walk to the nearest Orange Line Metro station (Farragut West) and four blocks to the nearest Red Line Station (Dupont Circle). We stayed here the night of the 4th of July. Our room had a really nice layout. You enter into a sitting area with a couch, chair, desk, dresser, and a flat-screen TV. You then pass through an area with a kitchen on one side and the bathroom on the other. The kitchen has a full size refrigerator, full stove and oven, dishwasher and a sink. At the window end of the room you have the bed with two very large closets flanking another TV. The bed was very comfortable. The air conditioner was a bit noisy, but maintained the temperature well. I'm fussy about my showers, and this was a great one with a high nozzle (I'm 6 ft tall) and plenty of pressure. This hotel would be great for a long term stay. Due to our limited stay, we didn't explore the hotel's ammenities, bar or restaurant. We did have breakfast at Cosi, just down the block on M Street. For a tasty, inexpensive breakfast, this is a winner. Parking is typically expensive for DC, it was $27 plus tax through the valet, which was the only method available on a holiday. We found the staff to be extremely helpful throughout our stay. Bottom line, we would stay here again, especially long term since the kitchen is so nice.

“Four star rooms in a three star hotel.” What you will like: --Great new renovated rooms. The rooms at the Warwick are four star, and right now, the best part of the Warwick experience. Bed and linens updated, brand new wall coverings and carpet. Most King rooms have a couch. All rooms have Juliet balconies, and those facing north from about the 8th floor and above have classic Space Needle views (and a sliver or two of water in the distance). Please note that, at current, not all rooms are renovated. As well, one room per floor has a funky floor plan owing to the elevator bank--this is a wheelchair accessible room facing south. Avoid this unless you require an accessible room as it is smaller than others. --Location. All you came to downtown Seattle to see is walking distance from the hotel, with Westlake Square (Macy's and Nordstrom shopping) a few blocks away, Pike Place Market a few blocks in the other direction, and monorail to Seattle Center just down the street. Light rail to the airport is about five blocks away. --Staff was helpful and friendly. What you may not care for: --Small mediocre public areas. If the rooms are four star, the rest of the hotel is not. If you require a grand lobby, select another Seattle hotel, not here. --Dismal fitness center and indoor pool. If you intend to work out while you are in Seattle, plan to join a nearby gym temporarily. The facility at the hotel is woefully inadequate. And the pool, even with a recent renovation, looks like an installation at a physical therapy facility. --No frequent flyer or hotel points affiliation. Summary: A pleasant hotel that is a fine stay if you are not picky. My $209 rate came during a large convention, so the value was OK.

“Great room and location” The hotel is located close by the theater district and Times Square. The staff is very nice and the rooms were large with a comfortable bed. We were on an upper level floor so there was no street noise. Decent breakfast which helps to save money as you can skip lunch and have a snack later. I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Very large rooms & great breakfast!!” Stayed at the Embassy suites during the Chicago marathon. The hotel & staff were VERY accomodating to the runners, offering a early morning breakfast of waters, bananas, granola bars, etc. The rooms were very large, the bed was comfortable, the showers nice. And the breakfast in the morning (complimentary) was absolutely wonderful - fresh made omelettes, eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, french toast, etc. Only shortfall was having to pay for internet access ($9.95 per day). The rooms are pretty noisy too. Other than that, no complaints at all and would definitely stay again.

“Big, beautiful rooms!” We stayed at the Omni Shoreham for three nights on a business/pleasure trip. It is located in the Woodley Park area of Washington DC. It is a 25-30 minute walk from Dupont Circle, a 10 minute walk from the heart of Adams Morgan and a 20 minute walk to the zoo. The Woodley Park/ Adams Morgan Metro stop is a 1/2 block away. The king-size rooms are very large and the beds are comfortable. The new decor is very pretty. The linens and towels are of good quality. The bathrooms are new and clean. The bathroom amenities are the typical Omni brand and well stocked. The walk-in closet is enormous and has a safe that easily accommodates a laptop. The wireless in the room is free if you are an "Omni Select" member. It was a weak signal, but did work. If the signal is too weak, call the front desk and they will send up a wireless piece to help. The grounds, lobby and lounge areas are as pretty as everyone has described. The self-parking area is easily accessible to the hotel. On Thursday night we parked in self-parking. On Friday and Saturday night there was plenty of legal parking on the street in front of the hotel. The hotel has been renovated, but it is still an older hotel. (Everything had been completed except the pillows and the mini-bar in our room.) The floors squeak a bit and you can hear everything outside the door. Ask for a room at the end of the hall. My boyfriend realized that most of the noise was coming from under the door and put a towel along the bottom of the door--- it was a great idea and immediately took care of the sound. We didn't hear or see any construction. This hotel is a very traditional hotel in a very quiet section of Washington DC. The hotel is well-maintained the staff are very friendly. It is a good hotel for people that are driving to DC and want to park a car. The large and spacious rooms would also be good for families.

“ナイス コストパフォーマンス” 部屋は広くはないけれど、最近改装されたようできれいです。 角部屋だったのでバスルーームに大きな窓がついていて、開放感 がありました。朝食はシリアル・デニッシュ・ヨーグルト・ゆで卵・ 飲み物など充分でした(早い時間に行く事をお勧めします)。 どうせ一泊だしGとか Mとか現れたらフロントで殺虫剤を借りよう、 と思って行きましたが杞憂でした。次回マンハッタンに泊まる時も 候補に入れたいホテルです。公式サイトのレートをチェックしましょう。

“Excellent value for what we paid” I got a great deal on Twitter for an 8 day stay that really was unbeatable. I wasn't expecting a huge room for the price we paid but surprisingly got a king on the 9th floor which was very dated and worn but clean. The bathroom was old, but again, clean. I understand that the refurbishment hasn't reached this floor yet. On checking in I enquired about the free wifi that had been included in my rate and they knew nothing about it. Thankfully I had print out confirmation of the offer but they still apparently had to bill me the $14.95 daily charge ( sometimes twice in one day..) and then at the end of my stay I had to present the printout to the front desk to have the charge removed. Thank goodness I wasn't paying for the wifi--it was shocking reception up in our room. More than once I just gave up and disconnected. The public areas of the hotel are lovely, the vast majority of the staff extremely helpful. Overall we had a pleasant stay.

“Pit stop for busy manhattan travellers” If you need a spacious room, an impressive lobby with a cozy fireplace and upscale dining, consider the Waldorf=Astoria. It will cost you, though. For those of you who prefer to spend as much time as possible in the city instead of in their hotel room, but want an centrally located hotel with a comfy bed, their own bathroom (by far not standard for NYC) and free internet access, this could just be the ticket. The rooms are small, no question. But the bathrooms are regular sized and stacked with a good selection of toiletries. The room I was in had a king bed, a small desk and a closet. That was it. It was clean and the furniture seemed really new. The bed was very comfortable. Sometimes I would hear housekeeping staff outside of my door in the mornings, but otherwise the hotel was pretty quiet. The location, 24th and 7th Ave, is right in the middle of manhattan - you can get anywhere pretty quickly from here. There are two subway stations rigtht one block down the road and a couple over on 23rd street. There is also a fitness center in the hotel, which I haven't used, though.

“Stop! Stop! Overrated!” I am a regular reader of Tripadvisor and even if it is always your personal view which will count in the end, Tripadvisor do help out when selecting a hotel. However this time I was astonished about the great reviews this hotel had received and the overall rating among the hotels in New York (at time of writing #41). We like to try out different hotels when visiting NYC, on previous occasions we’ve stayed, for instance, at 60 Thompson, Gansevoort and Mercer. Why not Tribeca Grand? Well, we discovered Why not! When we arrived there was no valet service to help us with our luggage. The staff at the reception was not at all as friendly as described by previous visitors. Perhaps they had a bad day, but we are getting used to this nonchalant attitude in NYC. We had booked through American express platinum service and an upgrade was included. We were told no upgrade available. Anyhow we had booked a studio which supposedly should be 333 square ft with 20-foot-wide windows, so we believed this should be fine. On our way to the room we got a general impression of the hotel being pretty run down. Our room was a major let-down! Old, run down, small (definitely not 333 sq ft!), stains on the carpet, ugly furniture, marks on the walls, bathroom terrible with poorly patched up visible damages in bathtub and on the walls. Floor dirty. And absolutely no space for your clothes! Asking the reception for a change to a more refurbished room was useless and when reminding them our booking came with an upgrade (if available though) we were informed the hotel had no agreements with American Express and the duty manager told us American Express was lying!
