If we wanted to change room we would be charged extra! We told the hotel we would check out the following day. The hotel has no atmosphere; just look at the carpeting in the hallways – they should have been changed long time ago. The elevators did not work properly, they stopped all the time on certain floors, despite no one wanted to get off or get in. The lounge, dinner and bar area is dreary. The service is poor, really poor. If you order a drink at the bar, you will not be allowed to sit down. When we asked for a table, we were told it was only for bottle service. Even though it was empty! At midnight there were no people there! On a Saturday! They even turned the music down. We had some friends coming over for a cocktail. We were 14 persons and if it would not have been for us, the place would have been empty! Next morning when we checked out we were charged the double rate for the transportation from the airport. I explained the rate we had been given by the concierge but we were told they could not rectify it until Monday because the accounting department was closed. We waited almost half hour to get it sorted out and it was not until we insisted to speak to the manager when things started to move. He immediately changed our invoice and apologized. Off we went to 60 Thompson where we stayed for the rest of the week – and boy! – what we enjoyed our time in this splendid establishment! Again!

“Mixed Feelings” We stayed for three nights and had a very mixed experience. My first contact with the hotel was extremely negative. I made hotel reservations in late November. I then kept track of the web site to see if there was a New Year's Eve party we could attend since we were staying at the hotel. They did not have reservations for the party available on Open Table. Finally, I noticed that there was a New Year's Eve party advertised on the web site, so I called the hotel and was told that I couldn't reserve over the phone (even with a credit card) but that they would have to either fax or mail (no e-mail) a form for me to fill out and fax or mail back. Are you kidding me???? I gave the employee my address to mail me the form, and then she put me on hold for 8 minutes -- why? Finally, I hung up and they never mailed me the form so we didn't get to go to the New Year's Eve party, even though we were staying at the hotel. When we got to the hotel we asked the receptionist if there were any reservations for the party available as a staff member had told us there were, and she was quite abrupt and curt and told us we had been misinformed and that there were no reservations available. No apology, no attempt to help us find something else, just a very snotty no. That's okay, we went across the street to Bali Hai, which happily accepted our Open Table reservations and we probably had a better time there anyway. Apart from those two staff people, the other staff members were fine and did a good job. The hotel grounds and room were quite lovely and the bar and restaurant were great-the Happy Hour prices are not to be believed. It is also a nice touch that they let you use bicycles for free two hours per day. Throughout the stay, my husband and I were debating whether or not we would stay again and I think we've come down on the side of yes, but more customer service training by certain of the staff would not go amiss.

“My favorite NYC hotel” Hyatt 48 Lex has managed to crack the code in terms of offering an end to end superior New York hotel experience. The concept here is a bit unique - a big brand name but a "boutique" format with just 6-ish rooms per floor with incredibly attentive and friendly staff. Rooms are new and nicely furnished and on the larger size by New York standards. Great TVs, coffee maker, fridge. HIgh speed wireless. Outside noise is minimal (but the higher up you are the better) and interior noise is non-existant. The hotel resaurant (Lexington Brass) is solid. The lounge on the 2nd (3rd?) floor is very nicely done - small but workable fitness room. The lobby is small - very "clean" lines/minimalist decor. Great mid-town location with easy access to Grand Central, shopping on 5th Ave, Roc Center - and if you don't mind a 15 or so min wall Theatre District/Times Square. The most impressive aspect of the hotel however is the staff - personable, friendly, go out of their way to help and make a connection (if you need something just find Carlos - most friendly, competent, helpful guy). Such a far cry from so many hotels (in and outside of NYC) who just run on the script/auto-pilot. And the rest of the team are as on the ball as this exceptional front desk team. Whenever I am in NYC this is my first port of call!

“Decent with great views” I stayed here for 2 nights with a colleague. We both were given king sized rooms on the 5th floor with balconys. The views were spectacular. She had a view of the homes on the hillsides and I had a view of downtown San Diego in the distance. It was an average room with a small desk and a refrigerator under the TV. We didn't realize there was a fridge until the morning we were leaving, otherwise I would have brought some water to keep chilled. The room comes with a coffee maker, sub-standard coffee, hair dryer and an iron & ironing board in the small closet. There wasn't anything spectacular about the room, but nothing terrible either. I only have two minor complaints. 1: the air vent was constantly rattling and I couldn't sleep the first night. I didn't even have the fan or air on so I don't know what that was about. 2: the TV never had a clear picture regardless of the channel. My colleague's TV was fuzzy also (like reception with the old rabbit ears), so it must have just been the way the whole hotel gets their TV. There was a shuttle to the nearby airport, but I never took it as we drove from LA. Parking at the Holiday Inn is free, so that was nice compared to other hotels in the city. Even though the hotel is near the airport, I never heard any planes, so I don't believe they fly over the hotel. The convention center is 4.5 miles away and costs $10 to park there. Beware, you can't exit and return to the convention center without paying again. You pay every time you enter, so you can't eave for the day and return without paying another $10. Overall, this was an average hotel that is clean and comfortable.

“Decent hotel” I recently stayed for 4 nights here. Located about 15 minutes north of downtown, 5 minutes north of Hotel Circle, this Courtyard faces the freeway. Cheaper than sometimes-expensive downtown hotels and not too far out of the city, it was close to major freeways, restaurants and shopping. Check-in service was very good - they were sold out but accomodated my early check-in and even gave me two choices of room. The hotel generally looks recently renovated with new carpets. There are laundry facilities which are well kept. There is a restaurant with a large breakfast buffet for $10. The rooms could use some improvement. The shower heads and matresses could stand replacing but weren't awful. Room was large with good sized furniture. If you want a decent-sized balcony that doesn't face the freeway, ask for rooms facing the pool.

“Lovely accommodations in a really nice hotel” We found the Waldorf Astoria to be a very nice hotel - our room was large and well appointed, the bathroom too was quite large and nicely appointed. The lobby was elegant, the concierge helpful and the location is terrific. The only bad thing about our visit was that the television in the room was broken.

“Solid Value” Can't beat it for the money. It's pretty well located near Thomas Circle, a bit of a walk to the metro. I was pleased with the quality and the size of my room. The Internet was bit slow and the breakfast room was chaotic. Lots of overweight parents and their feral, poorly socialized children packing in for the day but that's an overall social problem. Still, it could be better organized. Nevertheless, the hotel delivers better value than many other higher priced nearby ones and I will definitely stay there again.

“Nice room, busy hotel” Being near the airport, this is the place that many airlines send their "distressed" customers to. I know, there was a shuttle bus full of them! Of course, at the front desk, flight crews get precedence, and if you're arriving later in the evening, there can be a lot of waiting around to check-in. The two clerks on duty seemed harried. It explains why my check-in was a less than stellar experience. It doesn't explain why the concierge was short and too busy talking to the other hotel staff to answer a simple question. The rooms are comfortable and quiet. Plenty of room and clean. Everything worked perfectly and I got much needed couple of nights away!

“We enjoyed the hotel and the location was great!” The hotel was very nice and the location was awesome. It was walking distance to all the major attractions. It was located right across from the Boston Commons. They even brought in a mini fridge for our daughter and a microwave to warm up her food. They provided a nice crib for her too. We would love to go back.

“Give Sole Food a try....” I used to live in Philadelphia, so I already knew of this Loews Hotel, but I never had the opportunity to stay there until now. It is a former office building, otherwise known as the PSFS building, and I think it is pretty cool that Loews decided to keep the neon PSFS sign on top of the roof. The check-in process went quickly, and they placed us in a spacious corner room overlooking Market Street. The other reviews are correct; the beds are very comfortable. The only odd thing was that our room did not have an alarm clock. I don't know if that is the case for every room, and since we did not need an alarm clock, we never bothered to call the front desk to ask for one. We tried the hotel restaurant, Sole Food, for breakfast one morning. The food took a little long to be served, but it was quite good. If guests prefer to eat outside the hotel, the Reading Terminal Market is only a block away and always a great place to visit. Also, the restaurants on Broad Street are also within a couple blocks of the hotel. The SEPTA Frankford line also stops right below the hotel, and there is a PFLASH trolley stop nearby if you prefer to tour all of Center City.

“Great place to stay at San Antonio - location, price, value” I had a pretty darn good stay last weekend at this property. They let me check in early, breakfast was above average for an Embassy. Of course these are great places to bring the family with the 2 room suite setup and vast breakfast array. About the only 2 glitches were housekeeping (came back at 4PM and room not made yet - they showed at 4:30) and some external renovation that cut off the play area. The latter was probably a one time thing and its notable that they have a playground at all. All this and I got a rate under $100 a night - great deal!

“Surprising Style and Comfort on a Budget” I'm a bit of a hotel snob. I travel a lot and as I get older I get much more demanding. I like to be comfortable. I like fast elevators. I don't want to stand in any sort of line for anything. Honestly, places like the Hilton Garden Inn don't generally merit even a glance through their website when I'm choosing a hotel in New York. I just don't expect to find a place that is up to my standards. However, I found myself unexpectedly on a train to New York with a changed flight schedule and no place to spend the night. It was the end of a long trip and while my back was crying out for comfort my wallet was wearing thin from overuse and the cost of this unexpected stay weighed heavily on my conscious. I did not want to explain $300 for an eight hour stay to my bookkeeper. So I booked this hotel. It was the cheapest option. I know the neighborhood. I figured it was only one night and barely a whole night at that so if it was horrible it would at least be short. To my great surprise, I thoroughly enjoyed my stay here. Maybe it was the quick check-in and the warm cookie handed to me upon arrival. Maybe also the super fast elevators. It definitely had something to do with the extravagantly colorful but also cheerful decor in the hallways. But what got me was the large, perfectly comfortable bed. Okay, the room was a little tight but nicely done. The bathroom was very basic but completely functional and while the bath products weren't anything fancy they smelled nice. I watched a little TV a big, flat screen and then I slept very comfortably through the night. Everyone on the staff greeted me with a smile in the morning and I left feeling refreshed and lucky.

“Directly connected to the convention center” The San Jose Hilton is definitely a recommendation when you're attending a conference at the adjacent convention center as it has direct access to the venue. The rooms are what you expect from a Hilton and are clean and in good shape. However, one should be aware of the fact that the hotel is in the direct landing direction of San Jose's airport and it gets really noisy between 06:30am and 10:00pm. The hotel has one restaurant that offers a reasonable food selection a relative high prices (as usual at hotel restaurants) a second restaurant - and actually one that is a bit more like a restaurant not like a bar in the lobby would improve the experience. The staff is friendly but not very proactive. At arrival there was no doorman to assist with my luggage. Also at check-in no assistance was offered. I passed through the lobby several times each day - staff was only sparely present and I was never greeted. This could get some improvement... The executive lounge offers pretty good breakfast and reasonable evening snacks, but is a bit too small.

“Don't Stay Here Unless You Can't Afford Something Else” A number of us are currently staying here for business. I would NOT recommend it unless you can't afford anything else in this area. It is old, small, some are complaining about the "frat house" smell on the 4th floor, and the service isn't great. Positives: - Room service was fast, caesar salad was good. Chicken wasn't chopped; a whole skin-on chicken piece was on the salad - that was odd, but maybe normal to some. Good salad, good chicken, good dressing. - Cheaper than other nearby places - Minibar and room service somewhat cheaper than nearby (I have stayed at the Omni on California and Montgomery MANY times - the room is twice the size and overall hotel MUCH nicer) - Great location near Union Square (which really isn't all that unless you want to shop stores that are everywhere else), Chinatown and Financial District - My room has cabled internet that was extremely slow at first but seems to be fine now (after two days plugged in). Others said they don't have a cable and it took them 2 hours to get wifi working. - Free coffee in the morning and free happy hour something like 5:30-6:30. I haven't been able to go to that yet as that's still a tough time for businesspeople. Negatives: - Minibar not refilled. I drank the half-bottle (2 glasses) of cold chardonnay from the minibar last night and it was not refilled tonight. I called guest services and they said the minibar is normally refilled, and they'd send a new half-bottle. When it arrived (quickly), it was completely warm with absolutely no apology or even an acknowledgement. ?Completely unacceptable and very disappointing. - Room is seriously tiny. SERIOUSLY tiny. If I wasn't here for business and NEVER in the room, I'd hate it more. There isn't room for two people to even shower and get ready to go out in here. - One room my colleague first got put into had no closet. Seriously, there wasn't a closet in existence and he had to change his room. - Rooms AGAIN are seriously tiny. Don't underestimate your need for a little space. - Double bed, not even a queen. They didn't even ask my preference. - Bathroom has pedestal sink and two tiny shelves. Very little space to put toiletries. - One robe in closet. What if my husband had been here too? - Closet has maybe 6 hangers. - Very noisy for my colleagues on street side. - Very inexplicably noisy for me on internal "building-facing" side. Noises that sound like housekeeping is ramming their carts into the walls outside the room. What IS that? - Housekeeping yacks all day right outside your room, so if you're working in here druing the day at all or just want to sleep in, good luck. - They advertise a "modern, well-equipped gym". It has ONE elliptical, one treadmill, and one bike. That's it. Luckily when I was in there at 5:30 PM, there wasn't a soul there. They're probably all out getting exercise seeing the city, but I wouldn't count on that always happening. Overally, I am extremely disappointed with this hotel. Yes, it seems like it's been renovated from an old place to a somewhat better place. It's still not great.

“A real find” I really enjoyed the Sky Hotel. It is brand new, and the staff is outstanding, really friendly and helpful. The room I had was great, no complaints about it's size, it had a small fridge and large bathroom. It was quiet, rarely heard another guest. The location is a little off the beaten path, but it's a short drive to Culver City, which apparently now has a restaurant scene! There were some slight issues with the air conditioning, but I'm sure they'll get sorted out. In a sea of sameness, the Sky Hotel really stands out.

“Perfect haven for business or pleasure” I have stayed at the Hotel Teatro twice and would return on my next trip to Denver. Rooms are stylish, comfortable, and well-maintained. (They even provide free water bottles and bathroom scale, not typical.) Staff is super courteous and helpful. Dining options within the hotel are excellent. Location is perfect for its proximity to the convention center, performing arts center, and the nearby 16th Street Mall. My only suggestion would be to enlarge the tiny workout room.

“Great Hotel outside of the city” I usually stay in downtown Charlotte when in the area, but had a meeting near UNC so chose this property. You never know with Hilton exactly what you will get for your money, but this property over performed. Looks new throughout, flat panels, good internet service. The restaurant was very good and a break from the chains that are in abundance in this area. My room even had a view of the small lake on property. Very nice, and best of all not priced at typical Hilton levels - only about $20 over the local limited service properties.

“una pensioncina di basso livello al prezzo di un 4 stelle” Volevamo un hotel sulla spiaggia di LA per riposarci dopo il nostro tour de force tra monti e deserti dell'Ovest, e unabuona base per girare agevolmente per la città.Le recensioni ci hannno condotto senza esitazioni verso questo piccolo hotel, chiaramente non frills. Il tempo orribile e la temperatura invernale con cui ci ha accolto la spiaggia di LA (a Luglio!) non influenzano minimamente il giudizio su questo posto, su cui non avevamo grosse aspettative, ma....il confronto con la realtà è stato duro. a)Prenotate da oltre due mesi due "DeLuxe Ocean View" al modico prezzo di 170$ a notte, abbiamo trovato due microscopiche stanze al piano terra (una aveva il bagno IN camera, nel senso letterale!!) Vista: ingresso del patio. Oceano??Impossibile avere la "view", perché l'unica finestra Ocean Front è bloccata da una scrivania ikea... b)Greg il "GeneralManager", un tipo molto zen e mooooooolto smart (che vive in una camera/deposito di fronte alla "reception") ci ha fatto pesare di essere arrivati alle 21.30, consegnandoci le chiavi del "paradiso! c)abbiamo il vago sospetto che le lenzuola non fossero proprio di bucato e in due giorni e mezzo NESSUN servizio, nemmeno la minima basic pulizia della stanza (tenete presente che siete SULLA spiaggia e c'è sabbia ovunque......) in giorni di sole il posto in sé acquisterà senz'altro più fascino, ma......con un piccolo sforzo economico, meglio Santa Monica!

“The Drake is Great!” I have read through the reviews of this hotel before writing mine and want to clarify a few things based on my stay. First, this is a boutique historic hotel. When we arrived we heard another guest complaining about the size of her room, and I want to say "what did you expect?" If you want a big boxy standard room, go to the Sheraton. This is why you stay at a place like the Drake, because the quirlky small rooms are charming! We had a king bed (luxurious) in a smaller sized room right near the elevator on the 12th floor. Because this is an old building we couldn't hear a thing outside our door. Not a problem at all with noise. The bedding was very high quality, definitely Kimpton standard. The decor in the room was also great - mismatching striped wallpaper and headboard - also a great quirky feature of a boutique hotel. And yes, the bath was small. Over three days I think we probably spent a total of 30 minutes in the bathroom - does the size really matter? The best part of this hotel is its location in Union Square on the cable car line. You really feel like you in the middle of it all, and it is a great starting point for getting all over the CIty (right near the Bart, Muni, Cable Car, etc.) Also, the dining in this neighborhood is fabulous. Our best restaurant experience was at a Mexican place (Colibri) recommended by the Concierge! We booked on Expedia and got a great three day mid-week rate of $100 a night. The ONLY complaint I have about the Drake is the heating/cooling system (apparently new) in the room. Our thermostat was inoperable and the room hovered between 75 and 80 degrees the whole time we were there. We called to complain twice and either had no response or the fix didn't work (we were out when they came). Because we are from Seattle, I think we were pretty ok with a warm room in spring, but it was mildly annoying. I would definitely recommend this hotel for the value. Definitely above average.

“Sexy but small” I stayed here during the holiday season. By joining the preferred group of hotels I was able to get a decent deal on the room, which was what they call a "medium" size room. The room was about as big as my closet. I actually changed rooms after the first night, which had its pros and cons. The first room was extra tiny and overlooked some kind of generator or something. No view and no daylight at all. But it was pretty quiet. The second room, on the 10th floor, was slightly bigger and faced Broadway but really didn't have a view, unless you consider looking into other people's apartments a view. And the noise level from the street was unbelievable. I had to sleep with earplugs and I could still hear all the street noise, especially the taxis honking their horns! That being said, the room was very very clean and very sexy. The blue lights added a little something extra to those moments with my guy and the bed was super comfortable. Not sure if I would stay here again though. I dont think it was worth the price.

“Extremely Poor Marriott Property” - hallways were dirty and had a bad odor. - room had a strong deodorizer smell (had to air out the room); closet had strong urine smell (sprayed with lysol, kept door closed, didn't use closet) - kitchen and bath floors were filthy. - carpet not vacuumed (found hair pins on carpet). - housekeeping ignored "do not disturb" sign and knocked on the door at 8:20 a.m. to find out when I was going to checkout (checkout is noon). - limited breakfast items with no dining area. - no one inquired about my stay at checkout. - hotel charges $7 for high speed internet (even for Marriott Platinum Members).

“Nice and relaxing at an affordable price” Stayed one night on the first floor of the hotel. Staff was very friendly and allowed us to check-in early. Enjoyed the free hotel movie channel and breakfast. Coffee was very good and waffles turned out perfect. Our room was clean and the bed very comfortable. Only problem we had was trying to use the side entrance which would not open/scan the room key.

“Perfect, except for the theft of my specialty chocolate!” Our organization began our 3 day event with a small private dinner, held in the Pisces Room. I had been given the gift of specialty chocolate during the meeting from one of my friends in attendance. It was packaged in a large shopping bag containing 4 individualized bags of chocolate, all beautifully wrapped with colorful stufffing. I left the meeting early and fogot the chocolate by my seat! Since the room closed after our dinner, the very next day I sought the assistance of the banquet mgr who kindly retrieved the chocolates for me. To my absolute shock, the bag had been rummaged, with half of the candy gone, and the stuffing thrown away from the invididual bags. Clearly someone from the staff had helped themselves since our dinner meeting was a small group who all knew the candies were mine. Very stupid theft since this was a private meeting, with a high likelihood that the attendees were still onsight and hence, the forgotten item would be retrieved. This event was reported to the banquet mgr who indicated she would inform the general mgr. I did not hear more back from the hotel. Aside from that sad theft of the fabulous candy, the hotel was in a perfect location, with very nice ammenities. Rooms were appropriately sized and meeting rooms were well located. Rooms also were very quiet, with no noise issues despite being a very busy weekend. Check in was surprisingly done online, as was checkout. Our foods throughout the weekend were very nicely done. Our group found the event mgr very pleasant to work with and responsive to our needs. The event proceeded smoothly, minus my chocolates.

“Would not stay here again and is not worth the money!” My husband and I got a great deal through hotwire for a 4 star hotel and just ended up at the Brown Palace unfortunately. We read some reviews that were negative and some positive, and after staying here I completely agree with the negative ones. Everything people are saying is true. We are not rich and we don't normally stay at hotels like this, so staying at this hotel should have been a luxury to us but honestly we expected A LOT more from this place. We knew we were proably going to have to valet but tried to find parking at a garage. There are barely any garages or parking and if you do find one it's either monthly, no overnights or the ticket printer won't work. All of that happened to us so we had to just suck up the 26 dollar valet parking. The staff was very nice. Check in was fast and pleasant. It was a little to stuffy feeling for us. We arrived during afternoon tea which was neat to see but not our style. To really sum up how stuffy this hotel is, in the hotel directory book in the room they have a part that talks about suggested attire. It basically said to dress appropriately to match the ambiance of the hotel and the environment that guests expect when staying there. Thought that was pretty snobby. Anyway, we were on the 4th floor and I dont know if we just got screwed or what but the room was literally the smallest room i've ever been in. It was like sleeping in a closet. There was no room to get between the bed and the dresser so basically i racked my knee on the bed posts about 4 times. Came home with a lovely blue knee souvenier. The bed was really unfomfortable. The down comforter was the nicest thing but doesn't make up for a stiff back. Room had a ceiling fan and flat screen tv. The bathroom was the pits. You have to literally step up to get into the bathroom. It wasn't just a one or two inch step. It was so high up that when you step down from it you dont just step down, you fall down into the floor. It gets really annoying after a while. When opening the bathroom door, it pretty much slams into the toilet everytime because the toilet is right behind the door. You can't even see it if the door is completely open. It had an old time sink in there which didn't bother me until i noticed it wouldnt drain. We had to break the plug to get it to work. There's NO counter space. I read a review about this and didn't think it would bother me until i actually needed to lay out a bunch of things and had no room. The tub was disgusting. I hate to admit we didn't even shower for two days because it was so nasty. Brown stains around the drain and all on the wallpaper. It just didn't feel clean. I know this is an older hotel and it's supposed to be so charming and boutique feeling but for the money and star rating, i think they could afford to clean the place up and at least update the tubs so they're not rusting!! Room service was of course very expensive but that's typical. The only thing that bothered us was the 3 dollar 10 oz sodas from room service we had to order b/c the floors don't have vending machines. I had a cold and my husband was too tired to go try and find a walgreens so you pretty much have no choice but to pay the money. This place pretty much ruined our trip. I rather of stayed at the hampton inn down the street. At least if you're staying at a hotel like that and if it's not up to par it's because you're at a [----] hampton. This is supposed to be such an excellent high rated hotel and it wasn't! There are plenty of hotels downtown in great locations. I wouldn't hesitate to book a 3 star hotel next time because it's probably a lot more spacious and cleaner then this hotel. Sometimes you really don't get what you pay for!

“Nice hotel for the price” Booked this hotel via Priceline for $60/night March 20-22nd weekend. Parked at the parking garage right next door to hotel garage for $11 cheaper ($30/night). Check-in was smooth and received 2 warm cookies. Room was better than I was expecting. Nice view of Sheraton hotel. In room Wolfgang Puck coffee was very good. Room was spacious enough with 2 double beds and nice size bathroom. Neutrogena products. Good shower pressure. Hotel is about 2 block walking distance to Michigan Ave, movie theaters, grocery store, all kinds of shopping. etc etc. Elevators were working well. Free wireless internet in lobby only.

“Quaint and cozy hotel; great service” This is the 3rd of the 3 hotels I stayed at during my week in San francisco for memorial day weekend and a medical confence. Tripadvisor reviews always influence my choice of hotels (only failed me once, now I know to look at most recent reviews AND ratio of good and bad reviews). I cannot say anything bad about the very friendly service at this hotel and the staff made me feel very welcome during the whole stay. Rooms are smaller than most of the hotel rooms that I have stayed in, but is very clean. Shower may not be too comfortable for taller guests. Rooms are similar to what you would see in Europe, in terms of the size. Centrally located in union square, within walking distance to the convention center, BART, F train (classic streetcar that takes you from the Fisherman's wharf to the Castro). A lot of places to eat nearby. Enjoyed our stay.

“Great value for the basics.” I stayed at this hotel for four nights, choosing it primarily because of the location - very close to the house of friends I wanted to see. It is well maintained with a good staff, attractive plantings outside, and a well stocked deli/convenience store on site. The free breakfast is ample. I asked for a quiet room and was very glad that I did. On one side of the hotel, the rooms are literally a few yards away from the freeway and the traffic roaring by. My room was fine, but there are still soundproofing issues - I could hear the people in the room above walking around. I would stay here again - it is a great value for the price, centrally located in San Diego, and close to Old Town and the airport. Nothing fancy, but nothing bad, either.

“Très Bon Hotel on s'y sent bien personnel très avenant” Cet hotel est très bien. Chambres de taille correcte, propres, personnel très aimable, concierge un peu moins. Très bon Hotel, bon rapport qualité prix. L'hotel est à 5 minutes à pied d'un centre commercial ou vous pouvez diner ou faire du shopping. Le soir ils organisent de apéritifs avec de la musique dans le hall, l'ambiance est très sympa dans cet hotel.

“Holiday Getaway of sorts” We have stayed at Barton Creek Resort before, so we know that the facility and staff are wonderful. We normally visit during warmer months, but decided to spend Christmas there this year. There were quite a few others that had the same idea - hotel was full! After driving 4 hours to get to Austin, we tried to check in at 5pm and our room was not ready (hadn't been cleaned yet) - extrememly odd. Had to sit in the bar for 45 min. and wait. Once checked-in, the room was nice, clean and overlooked the golf course thank goodness. All else went well as we golfed, visited the spa and ice skated up to Christmas day. The food at the restaurant was good every day except for the Christmas Eve buffet - it was overpriced, had weird food selections that the kiddos couldn't eat and worst of all it had a dried up dessert station so we couldn't even have a nice dessert before turning in. The (entertainment) drunk lady with a wig playing the piano was extrememly odd and a bit scary to both us and our kids. Should have eaten off-site that night! Christmas breakfast was redeeming however with a jolly Santa Clause roaming around greeting guests. The spa services are nice, however; this is not a 5 star facility by any means. The spa area is broken up and feels like a gym locker room - not a upscale hotel spa. They have all of the amenities other spas have but the layout is horrible with treatment rooms on 2 different levels; a waiting area that is not relaxing or quiet at all; and non-private to boot. You have to pass through the common gym/spa reception area to get to the massage rooms - not cool when you're only wearing a bath robe and crazy hair! Overall a good trip. I just think we'll stay away from key timeframes where this place is too crowded, rethink eating on-site on buffet nights, and maybe hit up an off-site spa instead. The views, accomodations and golf help boost this rating. We'll probably give it another shot in the summer and see if things have improved but we may need to find another place to stay if improvements aren't made to upgrade the property soon.

“Good not Great” We spent 4 nights here in an upgraded partial water view room on the 40th floor. Positives first - location is great- easy walk to everywhere, nicely decorated rooms, wonderful service especially the concierge(++), clean safe rooms and very fast elevators. Down side - poor sound proofing to hall - can hear people talking and the "ding" of the elevator, maybe the heavenly bed does not suit us as none of us slept particularly well because the beds were quite soft (also as there were 3 of us we needed 2 beds and they do not have 2 queens only doubles or 1 king and a cot), long & slow line to check in at front desk and competent but not friendly staff, add on extra costs for everything including internet. This was our third stay and like all of the others it was good. Nothing memorable. The gym looked good - too bad we were too tired from all of our adventures to try it out.

“"There's a jungle out there..."” One reviewer in October was horrified at the furnishing of the Greystoke Room. She should have seen Jungle Nook (#28) with its bronze gorilla perched over the jacuzzi, a jaguar by the breakfast nook, and a huge elephant head with tusks suspended over the bed. The assessment for this hotel/inn/motel (it defies description but the sign on the building says "unique bed and breakfast") is based primarily on Jungle Nook and a few observations on the management team. But first of all, the location right near Balboa Park is excellent. You do not even need a car. Bus #7 can take you either to the zoo or to the Museum Place (one direction) or to Central Station (the other). Bus tickets are $2.25 general and $1.00 seniors. I have never found such friendly and helpful people as on the bus. Well done! If you elect to eat in the park, the Cohn Brothers' Prado restaurant is one of the best in town. The bar menu is served all day and will save you half the dinner fare. The restaurant itself, Mediterannean fare, will run $100 for two, with drinks and a full meal. Excellent variety from duck quesadillas to mushroom risotto. So much has already been said about the quirkiness of the rooms but I need to mention specifically the lack of seating in Jungle Nook. There are no chairs in the bedroom. If you wish to sit, there is a table with two chairs in--get ready--the huge bathroom. This is a room with double shower and enormous jacuzzi tub. (Remember the lines "water, water, everywhere"?) To the side of this room is the breakfast table. You will be able to nibble at pastries and cereal while watching the two bath options outfitted with jaguar and gorilla. There is a separate bathroom with dual sinks and toilet (no chairs here but there is a hat rack, if you wish). Yes, you can have your breakfast outside and I would encourage you to do so if the weather is nice. You call to have breakfast brought to you, and you call when you wish your room to be serviced. There is NO window in the Jungle Nook, unless you count the tiny windows over the jacuzzi which can be opened only by scaling the tiles behind the tub. I do need to mention that Paris in the 30's, at a far lower rate, is delightful and airy. Claustrophobes need not worry. But Sunday night there might be some major concern with the management team. We needed to phone the front desk Sunday night at 7:30 PM. There was no one. At 8:30 PM, still there was no one. Also, there is another major glitch. We were told that upon check-in, our credit card would be charged the full balance on the spot. We accepted this. But when we checked in, the charges had already been made and using the original card. Since I intended to use my credit card for the balance (my wife paid the first night's deposit), the management had to void the subsequent charge and credit her the balance and then charge on my card. Fortunately, the desk was charming and helpful despite all this. Our taxi was waiting for us promptly to take us back to the airport. Figure under $20 including tip each way from and to the airport. We managed to see quite a bit of the immediate area by taking local transport. Yes, I recommend Balboa Park Inn. There is so much charm and the location is superb. At least we know what to expect and what to avoid next time.

“Good. No surprises.” In every way, this is a typical Courtyard by Marriott. Good staff. Recently redone with the Courtyard decor and lobby arrangement. Beware of the freeway construction it can make for a challenging drive to some parts of the west loop area.

“Good location, very comfortable” I stayed here for the Pack Expo trade show from Oct. 29-Nov. 1 and had a very comfortable and enjoyable experience. The "Heavenly Bed" was excellent with soft linens and comfy pillows and the room was clean and stylish. The lake views were excellent. The location was perfect for me--the hotel is right on Michigan Ave, right next to the John Hancock Center. We were right in the heart of the Magnificent Mile and therefore close to shopping and restaurants. The staff was courteous and friendly, although I didn't have much interaction with them. The restaurant was ok (ate there for breakfast) but the service was somewhat slow, which was surprising given that it wasn't full. Overall, it was a good stay and I wouldn't hesitate to stay at another Westin (or this one) again. I just wish I'd had more non-working time to enjoy my time on Michigan Ave a little more!

“Location, comfort, and value in Manhattan” We decided to treat ourselves to a night in the city after the Metropolitan Opera (just a 7-block walk), and chose the Beacon based on reviews. It's in an older Upper West Side building that has been nicely renovated. We requested a high floor and were treated to a fabulous view of the city skyline, with glimpses of the distant Hudson River and the New Jersey shoreline. Everyone at the desk and front door was friendly and pleasant. The room was spotless and amazingly quiet considering its location on busy Broadway. We had no complaints about the beds or the amenities, though if more than two people stayed in the room (double double) they'd need to ask for more dinnerware, since there were only settings for two. It's not the cheapest hotel in Manhattan, but the kitchenette ends up saving money since you can enjoy takeout meals from the many local food shops. I would recommend this hotel to anyone, especially if they're looking for a great UWS location near cultural venues, shopping, restaurants, and transportation.

“Would it kill you to open the door?” Kimpton hotels can be a little quirky so I usually have an open mind when I stay at one. The Muse is nice, the room I had (executive king) was spacious and well lit and was bug free. The TV had HBO and Showtime. I will say the AC unit was fairly loud and there was construction next door that started pretty early so if you need silence in order to get your beauty rest you can either use the ear plugs the hotel provides or stay elsewhere. The only issue I had and it's minor was with the staff. They're not very engaging and seem like theyre doing you a favor to answer a question or open the door. If you're paying 500+ a night I would expect a little more hospitality. Oh and if you like Times Square you're in luck, it's half a block away - but if you hate trying to make your way through the general Cluster-F of the area, it will take away from the hotel experience.

“Fabulous ,,, but beware noise problems” If you want value, location and have few demands on hotel facilities then the Mosser is just perfect. The rooms my be minute but they are high quality and contain everything you need, the service is great, the position perfect and the price is unbeatable (if you book online - the rack rate can sometimes be silly). There is however a significant "but". In a recent visit I treated myself to one of the deluxe rooms with bathroom. Unfortuately that meant is was next to another room with a bathroom and you swiftly discover that the bathroom fans are not on a timer. The noise of the neighbourhood fan is much noiser than your own fan. On one night the fan was on all night and on another it went on at 6am and the occupant left the building with it still on. I was woken by the noise even though I had earplugs. Oh this was exacerbated by the fan at the other end of the room which served the public bathroom for those souls without one en suite. With both of them going, it was quite a noise. Until the management sort this out, I'd strongly recommend sticking to the cheaper non-en suite rooms.

“Good for overnight stay before the flight” The hotel has a very interesting design, rooms are rather good. Looks like they they do not have enough staff. No fancy restaurant at the facility - they serve a kind of fast food even at the bar - serving it in the paper box with plastic folk!

“Nice enough for the price you pay” We spent one night at the Golden Triangle Inn. We drove from L.A. to San Diego (which took us 5 hours due to heavy traffic!!) just to see the San Diego Zoo and after that to be on our way to our next stop. The room wasn't that big, but it was clean. The bed was really nice. Requested a room on 2nd or 3rd floor and got a room on the 3rd, as requested. It's right next to the 805, but you don't hear any traffic at all. Breakfast is till 9.30AM. We got in the lobby at 9AM, but most food was already gone and even after 15 minutes was not restocked, except for the juices. So I took the last sweet thing and a glass of orange juice and that was my breakfast. The breakfast was the only downside on this stay. Oh yeah, and the lack of a swimmingpool. But that's something you know when making a reservation. For a short trip to San Diego this is a nice place, when I would stay longer, I would have looked for a hotel/motel with a pool.

“Classy Historic Hotel” I was here for 2 nights during Fiesta and its the classiest place I've stayed on my own dime (rather than at may employer's expense). Front desk staff was nice and efficient -- had no problems with my Expedia reservation. The room itself was a bit small, but I'd expect that for a historic property. It was nicely appointed, with consideration given to the space constraints. My room looked out onto Alamo Plaza, which was great. The room was clean and quiet and very pleasantly furnished. The courtyard area was lovely and a nice place to enjoy their complimentary coffee (act fast, as it's only there until 9am I believe). Location is only a block from the Alamo and the Rivercenter mall and the streetcar stops. I very much enjoyed my stay and would highly recommend the Menger.

“Not your usual Hampton Inn” Located in the heart of Chicago's Loop, this beautifully restored hotel is not your typical Hampton Inn. The rooms, with 12-foot ceilings, top-of-the-line furnishings and big flat-screen HDTV's, would not be out of place in any 5 star hotel. As with any Hampton Inn, there is no "nickel and diming". In-room internet, breakfast and local calls are all free. Be warned though that, if you are staying during a busy period, the breakfast lounge/reception area feels more like a crowded cruise ship restaurant (this is not a good thing). Finding a seat will be all but impossible. The fitness center is painfully small, with a few (albeit new) cardio machines and 1 all-in-one workout contraption. All of the staff are exceedingly friendly. As to whether they are efficient I couldn't say as I had no problems or complaints for the entire 5 days I was there.

“and the best part is...” Ok, nobody loves to stay by the airport, but sometimes you have to. This is a fine choice if you're stuck in one of those late-nite arrival, or early morning departure situations. But the best part is YOU SAVE A BUNDLE ON CAR RENTAL WHEN YOU STAY HERE. It's a two minute walk from Avis, and a 7 minute walk to Hertz from this hotel, so if you fly in, take the shuttle to the hotel, wake up, walk to your car, and save a day's rental. OR, after an LA trip, drop your car off the night before you leave, walk to the hotel, hit the bar, go to bed, and take the shuttle to your earlier than god flight. Oh, and the hotel itself is exactly what you'd expect from a halfway decent chain. Dull, clean, quiet, dull, nice bed, nice staff, mediocre food, and dull. But hey, you're at an airport hotel.

“Newly renovated” Stayed couple nights on business trip in July. I am Platinum SPG member. Breakfast was included in rate so not sure if that was a perk. Hotel is very clean and updated. Lobby very attractive as was restaurant. Rooms were nice with comfortable beds and central air so nice and quite. Parking is a bit of a pain as you have to use room key each day to get in and out but location is right off of frontage road so easy to get on and off expressway. All the staff I talked with were very friendly. Did have flat screen TV with HD channels. Wifi was strong and fast. Will be staying here again if price is right. Did stay down the road at the Westin and not so nice! Would recommend this one over the westin if location works for you.

“An OK Hotel” We booked a hotel on Priceline and this is what we got. It is a nice hotel for the price we paid (less than $100.00) but nothing great. The lobby is outstanding but the rooms are average. The carpet could be replaced. The front desk clerk we interacted with seemed robotic and indifferent. I will say the food from room service was outstanding, although a bit pricey. I would stay here again at the rate we received from Priceline but would not pay full rate for this hotel.

“Nice place; Great location” This is a nice, quiet place that is very well located @ CA and Powell. Their breakfast Lemon Souffle pancakes with Raspberry Sauce and fresh raspberries are a world class "meal" for two.

“Quick weekend in Chicago” What a great place to stay. The hotel is directly on Michigan Ave. Walk out the door and start shopping or just people watch. The hotel has some great views of the city. The Starbucks in the lobby helps get your day underway! Great service for the doormen all the way to the frontdesk staff. So many dining choices provide you with almost too many options. Our room 4629 could use some maintenance. The closet door was not working correctly and the vanity in the batroom could stand to be refinished. Regarding the bathrooms, they are made for one person at a time to get ready. It would be a challenge for two women trying to get ready in that room.

“Perfect Anniversary” My husband and I stayed here for our 5th anniversary. I couldn't have asked for more luxury! The hotel offers the whatever/whenever service and I highly recommend it!! You will not be disappointed. This was an excellent location and had many dining options. Also loved the bliss bath products. I can't say enough positive things about this hotel. I would stay here again in a heartbeat!

“Brand New and Everything is...well, new!” How can you rate a new hotel poorly? The bottom line is that every base board, door, towel hook and patio is perfect. Why? Because it is new. We spent the evening on the pool deck and the pool is small but the deck is wonderful as it overlooks downtown Ft. Worth. Also, it's a bit odd if you are headed to the pool and you have to walk through a huge convention since it is right off all the conference rooms. I can't imagine how it might feel to have wet people walking by your big conference or to be the girl in the suit having to walk by a bunch of business guys. The spa was closed while we were there but it looks like a nice facility and I'd like to know more about it. The greatest restaurant in Dallas is here--Bob's Steakhouse. I've been a huge fan of Bob's original location in the Downtown area and they do not disappoint! If you want a steak, skip any other "tips" and head directly here. Simply the best steaks. They also have a nice bar called the Wiskey and Rye, which has a nice feel with 2 pool tables and tons of people. The beer tap was warm, but it's brand spanking new so it could have been some quirk rather than standard service. Here, skip the fish tacos--you will be disappointed. Other food seemed ok. The lobby was nice with a fireplace and warm feeling. Overall, great place to stay--mostly because everything is brand new!

“Dark Elegance” Why This Hotel? I selected the Sofitel in downtown Chicago after comparing prices amongst all of the upscale hotels. The Elysian was very expensive, as well as the Trump. I probably would have picked the Palomar, based on positive past experience with that property in Philadelphia and #3 ranking, but they were completely booked. I wanted a hotel that was (1) Upscale (2) Ranked high on Trip Advisor and (3) Close to the Water Tower. The Sofitel is a 4 1⁄2 star hotel, and ranked 8 on trip advisor, with an acceptable / competitve price point. It was a 5-8 minute walk to the Magnificent Mile, close to the Water Tower and John Handcock building, making it the winner. Booking: I personally have had good experience booking on hotels.com, and use that site. However, in this case, after I had booked, I realized that you get a better deal on this property booking directly on the hotel website, rather than a 3rd party. I did read from another reviewer this same experience, and that reviewer regretted not booking directly from Sofitel, because you do get a better deal. Bottom line? If you are going to book this hotel, book on Sofitel.com. Check In: When we arrived, we were greeted with a prompt bellman, friendly and professional. Our check-in was seamless, zero wait and accurate information on their records. The female that handled our check in was very kind. I asked whether she had any rooms with double beds, and she said that they did, and for the exact same room, and features, it would be $40 more per night X 3 nights. It seemed unfair to charge more money for the same room, and square footage for double beds, so we declined. Parking: Parking is at cost, which we used. I did ask if there was a way to get parking waived with a coupon, or an online deal to join their newsletter, but she said that there was no way. Although disappointing, it is understandable, and we proceeded to our room. Hotel Vibe: This hotel has a dark and sexy feel to it. The lobby is dimly lit, and has a sensual feel. There are candles burning throughout the property, with tall, glass containers and vases. The hotel is trendy, modern, sophisticated, and has sort of a “dark and mysterious” kind of a feel about it. Room: The rooms here are a lot nicer than the pictures, which did the property no justice. Everything is chrome, and all fixtures are buffed to a high polish shine. It has all clean lines of modern décor, a white bathroom, and a bed to die for. It is a featherbed that is literally one of the nicest beds I have ever slept in; it was incredible. You do have a nice flat screen TV, although I felt like the channels took a long time to load. There is plenty of space for all of your things, and closet space. It has 2 bathrobes, a hairdryer, 2 pairs of slippers, and huge makeup mirror. We were pleased. I will say, I was also glad that I didn’t pay more for a better view. Once we saw the view from the room, we were happy we didn’t upgrade. Extras: As described by a different reviewer, I also liked the Evian water delivered to the room at night. They do nightly turndown service, like most hotels of this star rating. What I LOVED and appreciated were the umbrellas provided at this hotel. It did rain on the Friday night that we were here and it was amazing to have 2 free umbrellas to use on our night out. My hair didn’t get wrecked, so thank you! Drawbacks: The rooms, although lovely, are not spacious. The hotel is not super warm and inviting, but rather, chic, sleek, upscale and sophisticated...bordering on cold? I am not sure. It was my style, personally, but I can see how this wouldn’t be for everyone. Also, don’t touch anything in the fridge because it is sensor monitored. If something moves, you will be charged. It did appear on my bill from just touching an item, but checkout went smoothly and they happily took it off the bill without issue. Value: I think the value is great, for a nice Chicago hotel. It is less expensive than its competitors and does deliver. I wouldn’t say you are going to find a ton of extras and perks here, nor special touches that you would find at the Palomar property, but it does the job, and you can bet on a good experience. Points of Interest: They have the nicest, little library that is very chic and cool. If I had been traveling alone, I probably would have gone down and enjoyed it. This hotel is perfect for: Young couples, romance, trendsetters, jetsetters, business, and solos. This hotel is not great for: Families, those looking for giant rooms / kitchens / amenities and extras.

“It was good.” We got this hotel through priceline and it worked out fine for us. The only issue was that it took a good 5-10mins to get to Grand Central and the subway. We arrived at 8am and couldn't get a room of course, they told us to check back at 12noon. By about 10am we we so exhausted from our red-eye flight we went back and gave our "sad faces" and got a room in the old tower on the 34th floor. It had a great view and was a large room based on NYC standards. I would say the service here was excellent all the way from Frank the bellboy to the rest of the staff. We did not eat here or use the pool, but everything else was fine. Our room was definitely showing some signs of wear and tear, but it was 100 times better than our previous hotels in NY (Best Western and Howard Johnson).
“Elegant historic hotel” Elegant, historic hotel conveniently located. Large well appointed rooms. Don't miss the Round Robin Bar. A good value for DC

“Great hotel at a great location.” The Westin is in the middle of the action it's within walking distance to the various Broadway theatres and restaurants. The staff was friendly and received great information from the concierge regarding Broadway shows. They ordered our show tickets which were great seats! There is also shopping closeby. And if you love to walk Central Park is nearby. Just don't forget good walking shoes!

“Great Views of Macy's Thanksgiving Parade” Wow - what a great location. We booked back in March for parade view rooms for Thanksgiving Week. We couldn't have been more pleased. As everyone notes, the location is right in the middle of Times Square. Taking subways and taxis is a breeze to and from the hotel - just head for Times Square - 57th Street and you're there. From our room overlooking 7th Avenue, we had a great view of the Macy's parade. If you're in town to see a Broadway show, it is just across the street or around the corner. The room was ultra modern decor with a very comfortable bed. Nice flat screen television, too. We liked the Macy's Parade theme stuffed teddy bear that was a gift from the hotel. (Of course, for the holiday, we paid for it in the room price.) That was a nice touch. While the parade view from our room was great, it is almost impossible to go out on the street because of the crowds. I made a quick trip to a corner bakery for some snacks and nearly was killed trying to squeeze back through the throngs of people to get back to the hotel entry. Only negative we can identify is the lack of free wifi access in the rooms.

“a grand old dame” Long line at check in, but most of the staff was very nice and helpful. Our suite was pretty tiny but clean. The beds were comfortable, but the towels were small and thin. Nice view. Didnt appreciate the duct tape holding up the wall paper in our hall.

“Checkers Los Angeles...HATED IT” coming from a great experience at Hilton San Gabriel I looked forward to checkers. BIG mistake. As a Hilton Honnor elite level, in preferences, the basic ones, "Away from elevator" Was goven a room next to ice machine and elevator. Now , regardless of my stored pref and my written request you see a high level frequent traveler and brand loyal WHO WANTS TO BE NEXT TO THE ICE MACHINE??? VERY small room, nice tv and a/v hookup. Vie wof roof and office building. Room services expensive and food cold, burger burned (amazes me how many cannot cook a burger...now I understand gordon ramseys going off) ALL other properties give me a late checkout of 2 hours or more. they grundgingly provided one hour. At check in "Kathy" did not provide the breakfast coupons. The manager is named Kathy I hope someone else because after seeing a decent greeting I was met with indifference. Elevator lights do not all work leaidng to peple chronically pressing buttons. When I mentioned this, the bad food, at check out I was met with im sorry; then after 5 mins she agreed to remove the "pet fee" I wish she didnt, I explained I have a service animal. She said, well I guess it doesnt have a jacket and banner so they thought a pet. Well ASK ME?!? I notified her and provided a copy of CA and Federal ADA laws and to charge me would result in approx 4k in fines... met with "oh im sorry' filled out review form as well. I did not receive an email or call from management which is UNACCEPTABLE. HAd to have internet access fee removed due to poor quality, regardless its a freebie on my hhonors account, why do they charge you and make you stop at the desk...though good thing i did bc the erroneous pet fee was NOT on my bill provided in my room!!! I paid a very low (in comparison to regular rates) rate and feel ripped off. I would not recommend this property to anyone for any reason. The Biltmore is across the street and a much better choice. Next nite was the bonaventure and while a different type of property VASTLY superior Parking 38.00, save 10.00 and park 100 feet next to hotel, especially on weekends where it costs 10.00 per calendar day..o/n 20.00

“Fantastic waterfront location in Embarcadero.” Great small hotel with all the right touches. My 3 must haves in a hotel are location - check, great bed - check and great shower - check. All 3 were AAA+ The location can't be beat. Directly across from the Ferry Building with great views of the Bay Bridge. 2 roof top decks give you all the views you can imagine in Embarcadero. All the best restaurants are blocks away. In fact you can pretty much walk to anything from Chinatown to AT&T Park. Great rooms and great service. Of course you do have to pay for all this but to me it's worth it. Get a high floor room for best views and lower street noise.

“Nice hotel and fabulous staff” Our family travels frequently for pleasure and also for business. Our recent long weekend in Washington DC was thoroughly enjoyable - in large part due to the staff of the Embassy Suites. In particular, the woman who shepherded guests through the always-crowded morning breakfast experience was friendly and unflappable. When she welcomed you, she really meant it. Even though breakfast was always crowded and chaotic, she made it a pleasant experience. The evening manager's reception was fine, but even better was the staff person who cleared dishware and passed out fish food so the children could feel the koi. She was amazing! In spite of the crowds, she remembered my child and made sure that she got a bit of fish food and could enjoy the experience. (She did. Believe me, her favorite part of DC was feeding the fish at the hotel.) Keep it up, Embassy Suites, and we'll be back.

“Wanted to Love It, Could Only Like It” I have stayed at another Affinia property (Affinia 50, Third Ave at 50th) numerous times, but for this trip, I wanted to be in close proximity to MSG, as we were attending a concert there. I really, really wanted to love the Affinia Manhattan as much as I love the 50, but I just couldn't. First of all, be forewarned that if you book a regular guest room at this hotel, it will be not much bigger than a closet. I am very familiar with small NYC hotel rooms, but this was the smallest I ever saw. The bed was literally pushed up against the wall on one side, and on the other, there was just room to squeeze in a night table. There was a small bureau, upon which sat a pretty old looking TV. The only chair in the room was one of those banquet room numbers -- looked like it was about 50 years old and it was filthy. The bathroom was microscopic. There was no desk and my husband needed to work in the room. I immediately called down and offered to pay for an upgraded room. Luckily they were able to accomodate us - and they were exceedingly gracious about it. The second room was nice, not super, studio suite. It was very large and had a desk with excellent lighting and a good chair. The bathroom was still itsy bitsy, but it was clean and functional. The Aveda amenities are one of the things I like about the Affinia group of hotels. We had 2 double beds, which was also just ok. (By contrast, my colleague, who was also there for the same time period, had 2 queens.) There was a kitchenette which came in handy for storing drinks, etc... If we had been there longer, it would have been very appreciated. The biggest issue I had with this room was the lack of control over the temperature. When we walked in, it was at least 80 degrees in the room. We tried to turn off the heat but it would not go off entirely. Luckily, the windows open, but it was about 20 degrees outside, so it was quickly freezing in the room. At no time in our 2 days there were we comfortable with the temp in the room. It was very frustrating. The second issue I had at the hotel was the restaurant. When we arrived for breakfast one morning, we were told there was a 15 minute wait and they asked us to stay in the bar area, where it was freezing cold. I had not brought my coat, so I sat there shivering. When we were finally seated, the pace of service was glacial. It was clear that the wait staff pushed people to the buffet and they seemed to be put out when we ordered off the menu. Our eggs took nearly 30 minutes to emerge from the kitchen, so from start to finish, breakfast took over an hour which would have been great if I had been on vacation, but I was trying to get to work. The best thing about the hotel is the staff. Other than one foorman who blew us off when we asked for help getting a cab, everyone else was terrific, especially a very nice woman at the front desk whose name, I believe, is Lucy. All in all, this was not a bad stay, and the price - about $200 per night, prepaid, non-refundable thru the hotel - was amazing for NYC. But the temperature issue is enough to keep me from staying there again.

“A Terrific hotel in a not so terrific location” All things considered, we had a very positive experience at the JW Marriott, which on many counts exceeded most of my recent hotel stays. The hotel is new, with a large, energetic lobby, large, new, comfortable rooms and excellent staff. We had a pleasant an enjoyable stay. Room: The bed was top notch, the room well designed and always clean. The best part was an awesome shower, large space and great rain shower head. I took two showers a day, just because it was so much fun. Staff: The staff that greeted me at the hotel was some of the friendliest and most courteous hotel staff I have experienced lately. I would like to specifically mention the parking valet, which were over the top each time. Room service were also gracious, as was the breakfast, the best hotel breakfast I had in the US for a good few years. Tasty and served in a bright and appealing way. The concierge was extremely nice and friendly, but less knowledgable than I would hope. Extras: The gym is great and the pool is one of the hotels highlights, the best hotel pool I have seen a hotel for a while. I really enjoyed my morning swims in the pool. The water was perfect temperature, the pool was great for laps and the view + deck made for a great atmosphere. The jacuzzi was also great fun, too bad it is not open at late hours. It was gorgeous. As a final benefit, instead of the low grade Starbucks, they service Illy coffee in the lobby, with baristas who know what they are doing. Cons: The location, unless you are going to a convention or event at the Staples center, there is not much to do there and one is 30 minutes to an hour away from anything good (Beaches, Hollywood etc...), even the food in the area is all chain based. I was there on a business trip, extended for a weekend of pleasure with my daughter. The place was selected for me by my hosts, but if I were visiting LA, I would choose a hotel at another location, even though this hotel is a delight.

“Outstanding” Outstanding! This was our second time staying at the Baltimore Harbourplace Renaissance. The room was a very large king. We were allowed to check in early (11 am) and were even asked if we would prefer a high or low floor. The housekeepers clean the checked out rooms first in the morning and leave the rooms of guests that are staying for later in the afternoon (our room was made up late in the afternoon every day), but this was great for us because we didn't feel we needed to rush out. Also, that is probably why we could check in so very early (five hours early). CLEAN is very important to us, probably our single biggest concern when traveling. On this the hotel gats an A+. The room was clean with very nice white linens. The housekeeping staff actually CLEAN he rooms - we even saw carpets routinely being shampooed, not just swept. Amenities included an indoor pool, hot tub, and sauna. A nice workout area. Nice bath products, too. The lobby is nice (but the restaurant is under renovation). They provide ice cold lemon/lime water in the lobby which is great when you return from the heat and humidity that is Baltimore in the summertime. Fresh lilies make the lobby smell great. The staff was also very friendly. We were always greeted with smiles, doors opened, and a polite "hello" in the hallways. The location is perfect for families and people who want to "see" Baltimore. The hotel is directly on the water, just across from all the tourist hotspots. From here, the water taxi can take you to other neat areas, including Fort McHenry and Fells Point. I wouldn't say this is a five star star hotel only because it lacks a spa, and the restaurant and bar are under renovation. Other than that, the hotel is outstanding!

“Service great; nickel&dime on amenities” Service was exceptional and as business woman traveling solo: neighborhood felt safe if precautions taken (doorman usually around). Signage inside was poor (elevators going up/down? --a mystery). Slighted hotel on rating more b/c Hyatt policy than staff there: pay for WiFi, pay for music via TV, can't move anything in (sensor) mini-bar if wanted to bring in own beverage. Staying 2 nights for almost $800? Throw the Internet in as complimentary. I'd stay elsewhere next time at that rate; there's plenty of choices nearby. (Hyatt, review your policies if you want the business traveler.) Cleaning staff didn't refill toiletries, towel had someone else's makeup on it. Otherwise, superior service from staff!

“Accueil déplorable et propreté doutable” Accueil déplorable au desk. Pas un sourire ni un regard, des pb avec les empreintes carte de credit qui pourtant fonctionnaient partout ailleurs, aucun arrangement; ils ont refusé de donner la seconde chambre, il a fallu sortir 400 USD en cash !!! Après 30 minutes désagréables passées à attendre, nous avons eu 2 chambres à 12 étages d'écart et ils ont refusé de nous mettre au même étage ! Enfin, le pompom... j'arrive à ma chambre et là, je découvre les vestiges du précédent client, savon, déchets.. bref une chambre pas faite !! J'appelle le desk, on me demande de redescendre (avec tous mes bagages, sans proposer aucune aide). On me change de chambre, on s'excuse à peine, et on me dit "finalement si vous voulez, on peut deplacer votre collègues pour vous mettre au même étage" (vraiment donc de la mauvaise volonté). Me voilà enfin dans ma chambre propre, avec une vue vue splendide sur le Chrysler bldg !! Excellent confort. Excellent emplacement. Dernière remarque : un plateau repas a trainé dans le couloir durant les 3 jours de notre séjour...

“Good Location, Nice Hotel” This hotel is right on the Riverwalk with easy access to all the restaurants and shops. Check in/out can get crowded and the valet area is kind of tight for all the cars going in and out, but it's a great location to get on and off the highway since you don't have to go but one block off of 37. We didn't dine at the restaurant, but there is a convenient coffee shop that even has wine by the bottle. The rooms were well maintained and clean, everything looked brand new. I would recommend to anyone staying on the Riverwalk.

“Very comfortable hotel.” Hotel was great location. Very effective air con (it was hot and humid in NYC at the time). Slept really well (didn't want to leave the room at times!). LCD TV with hundreds of channels, good size room. Clean bathroom. Very friendly staff. Pleasant and tasty free breakfast in morning. 5 mins walk to Times Square, seconds from 5th Avenue. What more could you want? Well recommend this hotel to anyone. Tom Griffiths United Kingdom
“Nice hotel, great location” Nice clean new property in the heart of downtown Memphis.

“How not to treat problems” Let me start with the good stuff: this is a delightful neighborhood in which to explore Baltimore. The Walters Art Museum is across the street, there is a great free circulator bus that will take you down to the waterfront, the neighborhood is full of good non-cookie cutter restaurants and bistros, and the little pocket parks and squares are charming and make for great people watching. The hotel staff was pleasant, the rooms clean and while not sparkling new, adequate particularly if you get a decent price on line through one of the discounters. The hotel restaurant is fine for breakfast or a before-dinner drink: with so many good restaurants in the neighborhood I wouldn't recommend it for dinner unless you are too tired to head out and explore (we loved City Cafe down New Hampshire street about 4 blocks and Marie louise Bistro on North Charles). Here's the negative side: I had an unpleasant accident in the restaurant that could have been serious - it wasn't, I'm grateful, and I don't blow things out of proportion. I have severe arthritis and leaned on the restaurant's handrail to help me up a few steps. It wasn't braced and came right out of the wall, tumbling me down the few steps. Staff and customers came right over to help. I was shaken but fine. The manager came over a bit later to check on me and I appreciated that. However, the hotel didn't follow up, didn't offer any help, didn't offer to even comp my breakfast. When you are not litigious, it seems to me the correct response for a place with good customer service, is to say "we're sorry you had an unpleasant experience, let us make it up to you by saying thank you with (fill in the blank)." I don't want to make the hotel out to be a villain nor do I think it's a bad place to stay, but I do feel you should be aware that you're on your own if anything goes wrong. Oh, and the valet parking is seriously overpriced.

“Great location for the price” Our room although small was clean & comfortable. For the price & location, it was great value indeed. A minor gripe - we had booked a King Evolution Room but after we got to the room & unpacked our stuff, realised it was a Queen room. After a very long 18 hour flight, we were way too tired to shift rooms & decided not to complain either as we just wanted to crash for the night. As earlier reviewers have noted, it is a short 5-10 min walk to Times Square, Rockerfeller Centre & even shorter to the theatres. A supermarket is round the corner. There are many restaurants nearby & a great Chinese takeaway (Fung Hin?) with cheap & delicious food across the road. Also a pharmacy opposite. The hotel provides a shuttle service to & from Newark airport at $25 per person (I think) or $46 for two (small discount). Not sure abt the fare for other airports though. We booked the New York City Party Shuttle tour & found it conveniently located about 2 blocks away. Highly recommended tour if you have a very short stay like we did. You cover the major sights in 5.5 hours in a warm, comfortable bus with big windows & a terrific native tour guide who knew all his stuff!

“Good business find but not for families” I chose this hotel because of the positive reviews on this sight, but it didn't fulfill my expectations. The front desk personnel were amazing, so that was a giant plus and we came in early enough to grab the fantastic cookies BUT the facility was showing some signs of difficulty. (front doors would not shut, and the the elevator carpet was severely stained...not good first impression!) I wanted to "treat" my mother, but she complained all the way up to the room. The room itself was nice. Nothing to complain about here. And Holiday Inn does have some good beds. If you want to primarily get sleep, this is an excellent facility. However, if you want to "hang out" with your family or friends, there really is not good place to do that. The pool area was stark and very small. The breakfast was actually exceptional. small touches made it great. That is why I say for business this is perfect...good sleep, good breakfast and quiet because it is in a business park. But for my picky mother---not good enough!

“Bad rooms, incorrect charges” First things first -- I do not usually give a negative review unless necessary. I am a very tolerant and open-minded person. 70 Park Avenue Hotel was booked for me by my company. They paid $398/day for a double double room. When I got my confirmation, I cannot believe it. There are cheaper rooms in NY than this. I immediately called up the hotel and asked for a transfer to a queen or king room since I was the only one in the room and didn't need an extra bed. They said they cannot honor my request because they were fully booked that day. The moment I stepped in the hotel, I was immediately impressed -- nice interiors, friendly doorman, and iMacs at the lobby! Whooot! Front desk was friendly as well, although she couldn't move me to another room as requested earlier. Even gave me a drink voucher for being an InTouch member. Really nice. On my way to my room, I noticed that the elevators are very tiny (a norm in NYC?). I had a good sized room, I wouldn't say huge because it isn't, not even for NYC standards. The worst part is the bathroom. It is soooo tiny, the toilet bowl is right against the wall that my leg wouldn't even fit when I sit. So I had to sit sideways -- uncomfortable and embarrassing. There was no space for my toiletries. I promise, this is the first time this happened to me. They put the shampoo, conditioner, and lotion (they're L'Occitance!) on top of a small wooden box that was placed on top of the toilet. Whhhaaaa .. literally NO space at all for any of my toothbrush, toothpaste, shaver, creme, etc. I immediately called the attention of the front desk and the best thing they can do is move me to another room the next day. Darn! I'd have to live with this then. In the evening, it turned from bad to worse. Airconditioning wasn't working properly. Even if I put the heater on, it's still cold. Th next day, I was moved to a lower floor with one double bed. The room was so tiny, it was difficult for me to move around. My only consolation was that the bathroom was as big as the room. And I had all the toilet shelving I needed, and even more. But there was another problem, this time, the room was so warm, even if the A/C was off. I called up front desk and they said they will look into it. Nobody came nor called. I didn't bother. Since this is one hell of a hotel, the warm room temperature will suite it well. I checked out after 3 nights ... but wait! You think that's the end of my nightmarish experience? Nope. When I got home, I checked my credit card online and I was charged by this hotel. I immediately phoned them and they said that I was charged for something I got from the room bar. Hmmm ... I don't drink soda nor do I drink liquor (I'm allergic). When I arrived I bought 6 bottles of Evian from Duane Reade. So to cut the story short, I didn't get anything from the mini-bar, but still they insisted that I call the hotel's accounting office to investigate. My gosh!!! Are we going to argue over a few bucks???? And I didn't even get anything. Can't you trust me???? I guess not! Bleh! Tasteless. Anyway, I still called and voice mail picked up. "We are currently closed, please call back during office hours ...." So tell me, is my review fair or what? I don't expect a reply from management because as you've noticed, the hotel only replies to those who give a THUMBS UP. Otherwise, they ignore you. So what? I am sure I'm not coming back to your hotel next time I'm in NY. I prefer that boutique hotel in Madison and 37th. I hope this will help you with your decision to stay or avoid this hotel.

“Very nice stay” We went to The Four Seasons with another couple for a weekend get away. The hotel was great and the service was excellent. When I called for a bigger hair dryer and then for a lint brush, we received the request in a few minutes. There was a wide screen TV in the room that was very cool.They also have a very good service that shines your shoes overnight- for free. The concierge was very attentive.
