She went out of her way to help us find the correct restaurants.She even called me on my cel phone several times during our touring to make lunch reservations. The hotel gym was quite good for a hotel. There were some free weights, lots of traedmills and steppers, a pool and steam room.They offered the usual expensive spa stuff (massages and facials.. )but we did not indulge). My only complaint- they are renovating the dining room and the Sunday breakfast buffet was chaotic and confused. They could not find our reservations and the service was very slow and the waiter admitted there were problems. All in all, a great place to go if you are in Boston. It is centrally located and right near the Freedom Trail. it was also nice we had a weekend package so we definitely got our money's worth. Recommended.

“A very practical choice” Stayed here for nights of May 24 and 25,2004 on the strength of previous published reviews.We found it to be a very practical choice at a fair rate which suited our purposes admirably and if travelling to Memphis again we would not hesitate to choose this hotel again.The room was clean,fresh and well presented.Parking was on site and we were able to rely on the streetcar which stops at the backdoor of the hotel to take us to Beale Street and other tourist attractions altough during the day most are within easy walking distance if one is prepared to deal with being approached by beggers on the streets.The free continental breakfast was OK although at peak times available tables to eat it were in short supply.Overall a good practical choice at a reasonable price for a downtown Memphis hotel.

“Excellent Customer Service Makes Up for the Tiny Room!” Attempted to find a cheaper hotel for a recent conference in Boston & booked the Chandler Inn, primarily based on TripAdvisor reviews. Well, the customer service both on the phone & in person was splendid, but OMG, the room was shockingly small--especially if you're a high maintenance lady! Here's the scoop: The positives: All front desk & housekeeping staff were marvelous, especially Von at the front desk. Everyone was cordial--willing to give directions, sight seeing advice, and restaurant suggestions. Other goodies: free coffee/tea/hot chocolate machine down in the lobby; free Internet; adequate toiletries; close enough to the conference hotel; contemporary room decor. The negatives: OMG, the room was TINY! Honestly, my husband (who joined me) said--"Oh, it was fine, especially for a guy!" Ha! It was so friggin' small, that we could barely move! Even though it was super warm/humid for April when we were there, the air conditioner was OFF--and the front desk had no way of turning it on for us. Although the bed was comfy--a person could get claustrophobic in that room...and don't get me started about the bathroom! Good luck, if you need to spend a lot of time grooming!! If you're low maintenance, I'd highly recommend the Chandler Inn, especially because of their extraordinary customer service & affordable rates. However, if you really crave creature comforts (such as a nice-sized bathroom, a swanky robe, and coffee in the room, etc.)--you may want to consider other lodging. But--if you listen to the husband, "Stay there; it's contemporary, it's a good deal & people are nice!"

“Great Location, Stunning Views” Hard to find any faults with The Sheraton Towers when you compare the price of rooms against other hotels in this location and with the same classification. Firstly the location is perfect and within walking distance to Chicago's 'must go' area’s such as The Loop and the Magnificent Mile. The hotel staff are friendly and helpful, I personally found the beds very comfortable and the view of the River/Lake/City are simply stunning. If you are tired on the evening and don't want to venture far there is a steak house and burger located in the hotel that are pricey but quality and there is a good Irish Bar right next door to the hotel.

“Rooms are mediocre; service and food Ritz quality” I don't need to say anything about the service and food quality. It is totally up to Ritz 5 star quality. I have to say I was a bit disappointed with the rooms. They are smallish and showing their age a bit and the bathrooms are small. The rooms are nothing special at all -- the Hyatt rooms are better.

“Best Hampton Inn & Suites Value to Date” This hotel is a great value. The price was right and it is a new hotel. My room was very clean and that includes the bathroom. Bedding was new and very clean. The hotel staff was very nice and I didn't have to wait 20 minutes for the hotel shuttle to pick me up at the airport. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Perfectly acceptable, very clean, but nothing exceptional” I stayed here on the recommendation of my husband who was here for business ten years ago. This was my first trip to Chicago, so having a recommendation was nice and saved me time researching places. Saw it was well-rated, in a convenient location, and no incidents on the bedbug registry, so gave it a shot. Had a one bedroom suite for my daughter and me - in town for a college visit. Very nice to have a separate bedroom and living area. We did not use the kitchen, but it was well-equipped. The bathroom was quite roomy, but had very limited vanity surface - just small sides around the sink. Would have been nice to have shelving or some extra surface area. The suite and hotel overall were very clean and well-kept. The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially Starr at the front desk. Didn't like that all the light bulbs were fluorescent and the bedroom had only one small lamp on one side of the bed, so that room was very dark when getting ready for bed. The $20.12 parking special was no great deal since you couldn't combine it with any other discounts like AAA rate. I think it was less than $5 cheaper than taking the AAA room rate and paying regular parking. The breakfast was OK - only noteworthy thing was the waffles you could make fresh. Avoid the "scrambled eggs" - truly disgusting! The location was fine, although it was very confusing that E. Grand St intersects Michigan Ave BELOW ground and you have to walk up steps to get to Michigan. I'd probably look at other options as we saw lots of nice places while walking around the area.

“charge to use the pool? really?” Our recent stay at the hotel was disappointing. The room was small and there was no view and the temperature was quite warm and could not be adjusted. Most unpleasant was the new, unadvertised charge for the use of the roof-top pool. While the aquatic director was lovely and accomodating, the charge for a brief swim was not. We will not return to this hotel.

“Terrible Bellboys, Terrible beds, Unresponsive re Suggestions” When we arrived, five bellboys surrounded us at the trunk. We said we would handle our own bags, thank you. They grabbed 2, I stopped them. They grabbed the 3rd. I told them to stop. I suggested to the hotel security that that was a very bad practice. Our bed had posts lower than the mattress - yes, we bumped our legs into them several times. Ouch. The sheets were not fitted so came loose all the time - very unsanitary. We had to call to get maid service every day. The hotel was very full but....that is no excuse. The other groups held their meetings between the elevators and escalators - high traffic areas - and the hotel did nothing about this. I let the front desk know and she didn't care. As we were leaving, 10 bell boys tried to grab our bags. We told them to not touch a thing. Each in succession asked us if we wanted a taxi. We said no we had a car waiting. Did they have a car waiting for us - and gave them our name. The answer was no. And no, those cars belonged to the hotel. After a half hour, we called the car service. He had been there for 45 minutes in the hotel car line. We spoke to the head guy who had all sorts of excuses. We just barely made our airplane. We called the manager to make suggestions. He heard us, and said he'd call back after he spoke to the people. We're still waiting.....Not holding our breath. The event we attended is using a different hotel next year. Thank goodness.

“Elegant but with Problems” We stayed at the Hay Adams for 2 nights recently on a weekend visit to DC. It was a nice experience, but not quite up to what I expect from a hotel of this reputation and at this price. Our room was nice, but not substantially nicer than many other hotels I have stayed in. The hotel could use some sprucing up. The hallways were dingy and the carpet needs replacing. The bathroom was spacious, immaculately clean, and very nice, though the shower situation was not great. As one reviewer noted, the water pressure isn't very good, and there is an awkward shower mechanism which we could not adjust to keep it from shooting water in such a way that it drenched the bathroom floor. The room itself had scuffed and chipped floor mouldings and standard-issue furniture. There was no proper closet, only a very small wardrobe that scarcely held our clothes for the weekend. However, the bed was lovely and very comfortable with crisp linens and plentiful pillows. One thing I particularly liked was that, in contrast to many hotels that are now providing only a duvet on the bed (which in most cases is WAY too warm for the room), this bed had a sheet and a light blanket, with a duvet folded at the end of the bed. The sheet and blanket were plenty of cover, and I appreciated not having to swelter under a duvet. In the end the bed is what matters most to me in a hotel, as I'm mostly there to sleep, so this was a positive. Another positive is that housekeeping is very attentive--the bed was beautifully turned down in the evening and after we showered in the afternoon the towels were all always replaced when we came back after dinner. My gripe is that there were several special events in the hotel that weekend and these caused some inconveniences which were not acknowledged by the hotel. There was a roof party on Saturday night and the guests was constant, noisy traffic in the hall from the time we got home from dinner until after 11pm (we were on the 8th floor where the stair to the roof is located). A few of the drunk partygoers were also staying in rooms near ours, and we could hear quite a bit through the walls. As other reviewers have noted, you hear EVERYTHING in this hotel--your neighbors, the housekeeping staff in the hall, etc. Additionally, another special event took over the restaurant, which is a lovely space for breakfast, and instead breakfast was pushed to a small, noisy, windowless room where the staff are clearly not accustomed to serving. No compensation is made for being pushed out of the main dining room. I think a true luxury hotel that wants people to come back should make some kind of concession when the expected amenities are not available because of special events. So in the end, If you are going to Washington to see the monuments, the Smithsonian museums, the National Mall, the White House, this is a great location, and the rooms are nice and service is good. But don't expect a really memorable and special experience. As for me, next time I want to stay in a luxury hotel in Washington I will probably try the Willard.

“Eh” I had been looking forward to staying at this hotel for some time, however, I wish I wouldn't have had such high expectations. Upon arrival, our hotel room was not clean, and there was odd food in the fridge. They offered to "remove the food" since no other rooms were available. Um, I'd prefer for you to CHANGE THE SHEETS instead. Besides getting the initial heebeejeebies about a potentially unclean room, the set up was nice. Really nice bathroom, and large spacious room. However, the view was into a "court yard", also known as the side of a building. The walls are paper thin, and the wedding party or whomever, kept us up all night. Breakfast was a huge disappointment as was the expensive valet parking. Will definitely not stay again. For the same price, you can find another great hotel in the same location.

“Disappointed” It really takes a lot for me to complain, and I know this is an airport hotel, but although it is a Hilton ... it is NO Hilton. First of all, I will give credit where it is due. The staff at the front desk and concierge were polite and helpful. The breakfast was good. We didn't experience the noise issue (i.e., hearing others through the walls) as other people have mentioned. The rooms were clean. But, like others have stated, the hotel is mediocre at best. First of all, the rooms, while updated in some areas, were also lacking in others. We found the lighting to be poor, there was no fan in the bathroom, the sofa was old and dirty, the fridge smelt like "feet" when we opened it, and the air conditioner was incredibly loud and went on and off every minute all night long. Exercise room and pool were nothing special. I think the worst part was the valet service though. I couldn't believe how unprofessional the service was. I SO agree with setter1vb who stated that the staff have NO sense of urgency and stand around talking - that is, when they aren't taking "breaks" and can't be found. The complimentary shuttle will get you to the airport once the driver can be located - you just may miss your flight in the meantime, though. There was also no attention to detail, as we found out when we retrieved our luggage from the storage room and were given the wrong bag because the tag wasn't even checked. And then there was the taxi ride from hell. We had them call us a cab as we were going out for dinner, and we don't know where this driver came from (suspect connection to valet staff), but he arrived in a beat-up black vehicle, told us we "didn't need" to put on our seatbelts, drove like a maniac and ran several red lights, took about 5 personal phone calls during all this, and then ... brought us to the wrong restaurant! And then did it for a second time! He had no idea where he was going, and we ended up being 30 minutes late for our reservation. This Embassy Suites hotel cannot compare with the Embassy Suites that we stayed in last year in Chicago. It was like staying at a completely different hotel. What a disappointment.

“Doable for one night” Stayed there for one night due to having to extend my trip and no availability in my current hotel. Cookie was nasty (must have been in that warmer a while). They overbooked and had to put me in two-bed room instead of king room. Very frustrating to me as I am a Diamond and at the least they should have given me a suite (which they did have available), she just didn't feel like giving me. Room was clean and quiet, though. I did not venture outside, but the area didn't look the best.
“Wonderful Stay!” Staff was extremely friendly, room was clean and had a beautiful river view!

“Rundown and really grubby” What a sad place. Everything is grubby and tatty. The room lighting is abysmal, but then I suppose it makes it harder to see the dirt. The staff are friendly enough, but the place is just so depressing. Yuck.

“Spring Break Family Fun” I travel frequently for work and this time it was actually during Spring Break but it wasn't completely work because I had some family with me. After some office time, phone calls, emails and handling some concerns. We got a balcony view hotel with a beautiful view of the pool and the Riverwalk area. The rooms are spacious and bigger than the Alamo Indigo where I normally stay. Marie at the front desk and Holly the new manager were so helpful and cordial for their assistance and accommodations. The kids went for the pool but it was little cold. I didn't bother to check to see if it was heated or anything like that because we took off to taste the local cuisine. I took some nap time and the beds are so clean and heavenly comfortable. For the most part I would stay here again... for a more quite family retreat. I do hope that management improves parking situation but I never had a inconvenience.

“Standard airport hotel” I had a very short layover in Houston - check-in after midnight for an early morning flight out of IAH. So, I didn't get to try out any of the amenities of this hotel. But I can say that it's a solid airport hotel. Beds were comfortable. Air conditioner was a bit loud, but not terrible. Bathroom was small, but adequate. Getting on the shuttle in the morning was, in my mind, the biggest issue with this hotel. There wasn't enough room and 1 person waiting was not able to get on. I would hope that the hotel has a back-up plan if this happens, but I would plan to be waiting outside some time before the shuttle arrives just in case. Overall, a standard airport hotel. I would stay here again, but would just be cautious about the shuttle situation.

“Room with a view” Went here for a weekend event and have nothing but great things to say about the hotel. The location is fabulous and has sweeping views of Central Park and Columbus Circle. The staff was courteous and friendly and the hotel was immaculate. From the street entrance to the lobby in the sky to the rooms everything was luxurious and classy. Will definitely return to this hot spot.

“Nice hotel, with a few smelly issues and bad lobby music” This is a beautiful hotel in a terrific location. The lobby, on a side street, is gorgeous. When I was there, they were playing some really horrible music. At least for me. My general thought is that if I notice the music, it's probably not good. My room was elegant, with tall ceilings and good light. But once again, I encountered the "Hyatt Smell'. It's sweet and gross, like a Glade plug-in. I realized later what they were hiding because by night the room smelled like smoke, with a touch of vomit. I really liked this hotel, but I think they need to invest in some good steam cleaning or replace the carpets. And come up with a new corporate smell.

“Great location in downtown Jville” I couldn't have been happier with the Omni Jacksonville Hotel. It is right in the heart of downtown in the northbank riverfront district. I've stayed in many downtown hotels in many different cities.. Jacksonville has a great downtown.. well lit and has a very safe feel. This Omni has just been completely renovated and it is amazing! Take some time to check out the rooftop pool.. even if it's winter, just to see the views. Also take a stroll along the riverwalk and take the water taxi for a ride. The rooms are nice and the staff is world-class.

“Great stay, blah location” Typical Kimpton loveliness in a somewhat off the path location. Nice rooms, friendly staff, no views at all from any room. They have the annoying shampoo dispensers in the showers. Nine Zero across town is much nicer, better located and worth the extra cash (youll spend it on cabs anyhow). As much as this was a nice stay, the location kills it for me.

“Great location, front desk is challenging, rooms showing their age” This hotel (and it's neighbor, the Residence Inn) opened as a brand new, newly-built hotel about 4 years ago in 2008. First, the rooms are good, but they're showing their age with constant, tourist use. The light colors of the in-room interiors and carpeting and hallways are starting to look dingy. The powers that be did an unfortunate thing a few months ago and got rid of the larger king suites (end rooms) and switched them to doubles only. Who's bright idea was that? So, on this visit, I was in the smaller king suite. it was OK. The bed linens were clean; the desk seems cramped; the sitting area was acceptable if not tight; the refrigerator worked; the bathroom was small, cramped, but clean; and I didn't bother with the coffee maker. On my first night, I had thread-bare towels. When the room was serviced the following day, I got a few better, thicker, towels. Housekeeping was fine on this visit. I never eat the breakfast with so many other options in the area. The front desk attendants must have gone to the College of I Can't Help You. Every question I have for them, they can't seem to answer. So, I stopped asking a long time ago. Head next door to the Residence Inn if you need information. (The check-in counters for both hotels are on the same floor.) Check-in at this hotel makes my blood pressure rise. The way the curved desk is designed doesn't help define a clear line for "who's next?". As I'm waiting to be served, someone comes out of no where and approaches the desk. Does the desk attendant ever say: "I'm sorry, but I'm helping another guest and there is a line." No. He or she stops what she's doing to help this person who clearly has no consideration for anyone else. The desk attendants perpetuate this problem by not correcting the offending guest. This problem is constant and endemic at this Springhill Suites and I try (but never succeed) in keeping my mouth shut about it. It has happened EVERY time I've checked in as the front desk is usually undermanned. When there are 2 or 3 people waiting, there's one attendant. When the line swells to 5 or 6 people (or more) all of sudden, two or three attendants come chatting and laughing out of the back. I find this consistent and repeated behavior completely offensive. Whoever supervises the front desk (along with the General Manager) should be replaced or returned to Hotel Management School (assuming they've ever attended it or know what it is). Internet was complimentary (and I don't know if that's because I'm a Marriott elite member), but you'll pay extra if you want faster Internet. The basic speed was fine for me. The location of the hotel is excellent: within walking distance of several restaurants and shopping along Michigan Ave. Parking as with any downtown hotel is pricey, but I can live with that. I can't abide with poor management, however.

“Loved the location” The Westin Seattle is a very good choice given it's location downtown - stone's throw from the main shopping area and restaurants, on the monorail line and near a central transit station, nice walk to Pike's Place and all. It's also right around the corner to Dmitriou's, where you can catch really great jazz performances. Bed was super comfortable as in most Westin hotels in North America. My room was a little oddly shaped due to the cylindrical shape of the building, but nonetheless spacious and offered a nice view of the city. Everything was good here. The service was fine, but because the Westin Seattle's also a huge hotel with a large number of guests, the staff were sometimes too busy to attend to you quickly, but no complaints about that. There's free wireless internet in the hotel lobby for hotel guests. Love the location and the quality of the rooms, will be sure to return to this hotel on my next trip.

“Good value & friendly staff” Stayed while I was on business for two nights. We got the penthouse suite. It has two bedroom and two bathrooms with a full kitchen and living room. Room was in good condition minus a wierd sewer smell in the upstairs bathroom. It went away after the first day and we did not report it. Hotel staff was very friendly and the free shuttle was a bonus. The breakfast and social were great. Basically dinner (hot dogs and hamburgers) and breakfast (scrambled eggs, sausage, waffles, oatmeal, fruit...etc) are included in your rate.

“Great Location and Value” An excellent hotel experience. I stay here whenever I'm attending anything at the Convention Center, Staples or the Nokia. It's directly across the street. Saves driving time and parking hassles at the venues. You can get there in the afternoon, relax, attend your event and walk back for the night and avoid parking lot jams. On-site lounge/bar and restaurant for convienence. Sure Staples has these features but it's a madhouse of people. I was here for Van Halen, as much of the hotel guests were too. Will be back four more times at least, into May 2008.

“Argonaut A+” Just returned from a 5 day stay at the Argonaut Hotel. We had two rooms purchased for $123 a night through Hotwire. We found this hotel to be an excellent choice for anyone wishing to be in the Fisherman's Wharf vicinity. It is on the edge of Jefferson Street, adjacent to the Cannery & Maritime Museum and although walking distance to Pier 39 and all other attractions between (about 15 blocks) it is on a more quiet end of the street, away from the bars & tourist stores. The streetcars are a block away and the historic trolleys are kitty corner behind the hotel. It's truly a very restful and scenic stretch of the Wharf. The hotel itself is very attractive in it's "ship" themeing, with lovely plank wood floors, rich red, blue, and golds in the fabrics & carpets, and rich wood fixtures elsewhere. Our queen/queen rooms were typical in their layout (beds, nightstands, desk, tv stand) but very appealing with the exposed brick wall of the original structure on one end, weathered tables, excellent linens, decorative pillows, and the ever present nautical theming. The bath was typically sized and had a generous countertop, shower massager, plenty of nice towels, and luxury bath products. Housekeeping took impeccable care of the room each day. The staff was friendly and efficient, with some members of the front door and bell staff going well out of their way to provide advice, guidance, special services, and friendly conversation when we waited out front for our group or the valet. The only hitch in an otherwise top-notch stay was the front desk failing to relay our request to have our cars brought around on the day of our departure (at least that's what the valet claimed). Because this delayed us nearly 1/2 hour, we had a rather frantic drive to the airport and sprint to the ticket counter to make our flight. I'm not sure where the communication breakdown actually occurred and I only mention it as a word to the wise since it did cause some stress, but it really was a small blemish on an otherwise terrific experience. I highly recommend this hotel, their staff, the service, and the location.

“A Solid Choice by Union Square” I have stayed at the Downtown San Francisco many times over many years. I have found the hotel to be very predictable. The service is always friendly, effecient, and thoughtful. The rooms are adequate and well maintained. The location is ideal for the business traveler or vactioneer. You can walk to Union Square, cable cars, shopping and the BART. Chinatown and the Embarcadero are also in medium walking range. This is a large convention hotel ideally located. Bottom line this is a solid choice.

“Expectation was of Hilton Houston .. not what I got” Right after this hotel was built, I heard great things about it and expected it to be at least as great if not more than the Hilton in Houston - the one attached to the convention center. That hotel 'sparkles' - it's efficient, well-kept, has great staff and places to eat. The Hilton Austin isn't awful - and I rated it "average" - it's just not anything special. What surprised me most was how worn it was. (Has it been renovated since it opened? I didn't think it was 10 years old but I was told it was a front desk staff person who also wasn't sure.) Is it so worn because SXSW is there every year and it gets so much use? I am sure the proximity to the convention center has something to do with how worn it is. So .. backing up and trying to find some good things to say: - convenient to many activities in Austin. - large enough to accommodate meetings. - good coffee outlet (Java Jive) that serves Starbucks. - nice staff esp. in the hotel restaurant. - free internet access if one is an HHonors member. My room was ordinary - and what I found interesting was how the armoire/TV cabinet was uneven! You could plainly see that the doors didn't align. I DID appreciate that there were lots of electrical outlets in the room and that the bedside lamps had them as well. The Liberty Tavern was pleasant with truly great staff. I had a late breakfast there and had the fritatta about which my expectations were great: it came in a skillet and was nice and brown around the edges. Alas, it was also dry and tasteless. Sad. I ate from room service; the portions were far too big and that wasn't explained. I ordered (you shouldn't) the hummus which was listed as an appetizer and got something else with it. There was enough hummus for 4 people! And another night, I got the Mexican chicken soup which was .. awful and huge. (The cheese and chips were put in before delivery, making for a soggy,icky mess in the bowl.) The quesadillas were listed as an appetizer and were far too much food and there were mushrooms in it giving it a strange taste. (I love mushrooms; not in quesadillas!) (For a great treat, leave the hotel and take a cab or drive to the East Side Cafe. IT is truly fabulous and comfortable.) I was there to present education at a meeting and the meeting space was convenient to the guest rooms via elevator or, off the lobby, escalator. The meeting space foyer areas have lots of interesting framed pieces about Texas history. That was the most interesting part of the space! You must see the huge overhead lighting display outside the Grand Ballroom. Fortunately someone identified for me what these lights represented; I had no clue. The banquet service staff worked hard and were pleasant. If you ship boxes in or out, they go through the UPS store in the lobby (next to the front desk.) The charge to do so is less than FedEx charges in comparable hotels. But if you want something you've received delivered to your room, you have to make arrangements w/ the bell staff to do so. And if you arrive after hours, there appears to be no way to retrieve a package. I did Except for proximity to the Convention Center, I'd not stay here again unless I knew the hotel had been renovated and updated and there was more care on the part of senior management and ownership. Disappointing.

“Love the Talbott!” Location, location, location. What a great find! Excellent, well-run, small boutique-type hotel on a tree-lined street near all the action without being in the oppressive crunch of it. Rooms are good-sized and clean; good bed and shower with tub. The air conditioner, as mentioned in other reviews, is noisy, but it's a minor complaint. The staff is simply wonderful and attentive from housecleaning to concierge. The on site restaurant is great. The red-line El is about 3-4 blocks away which makes getting around the city a breeze. You are footsteps away from Rush Street and North Michigan Avenue and Lake Michigan. I would not have a moment's hesitation booking at this hotel again in the future; in fact, I wouldn't book anywhere else.

“Interesting Stay” The hotel is nice in a lot of ways but lacks some necessary things. There is no service elevator so the staff is forced to tie up at least one of the only two elevators to do their work. We waited 15 minutes on one occasion for the opportunity to get down to the street level. It has only five rooms per floor and 26 floors. The staff is nice but unable to help with things like luggage as I had to (gulp!) double park and unload the luggage myself. They do have an arrangement with an obscure parking garage on Cedar Street to park for $30 per night-a steal in lower Manhattan for sure. When I called about these things the person at the desk was always very polite, helpful, and informative, and I appreciate this. The room was small at best but, for the low price, was all that was needed. The only downside to it was that the AC is set to hurricane strength so you are literally blown away by the force. It took a matter of minutes to drop the temp five degrees. I guess I would say that it is overkill to have this much force. We froze ourselves at bedtimes, turned it off, and let the temp creep up as the night progressed. The bathroom is also very small, but has what you need. I thought I saw on their site that they had room safes, but they did not, nor did they have the bellman that are listed. The breakfast area is very nice and all the typical Holiday Inn express items are there. The attendants are very friendly and helpful and make it a good experience.

“Beautiful Property in the middle of it all” I stayed at this property in a Suite looking directly at City Hall in Sept. The hotel is a beautifully restored building with rich woods in the main areas balanced by the modern and stylistic approach expected by the Le Meridien. The bar and Restaurant were centrally located and although I could see how they could be loud at times, were quite nice. The staff was very warm and helpful, going above an beyond to assist. As with many downtown hotels, the main entrances are not at street level, so you must have assistance getting bags up. Doormen were always present for this need. The room I stayed in was a Suite and was very spacious, quiet and comfortable. The seating was comfortable and bed very nice. I would rate the room as one of my favorite suites of SPG hotels. Having stayed in several downtown hotels, this outranks most.

“Well located hotel that is a good value” Excellent location near subway lines and easy walk to shopping makes this a good choice; room itself was a good value but food options in the hotel are pricey. There are plenty of food options nearby. Room was comfortable but showing some wear. Comfortable with great storage. Bath was well appointed but the vessel sink and small vanity is not very useful. Staff was 50/50....some friendly and helpful others seemed anoyed with having guests. The club lounge is ok for breakfast but a big disappointment at night.

“May be my new favorite hotel” What an amazing stay. We checked in and asked for a view of the airport - it was amazing with pics included. So much fun to watch the planes in terminal A. The hotel has its own security and TSA agent so you can go into the terminal at the airport without a boarding pass which is so much fun. We spent hours in the airport watching people at the gates and eating in the airport restaurants. So much fun. We then went back to the hotel and relaxed with an amazing view, great bed and shower. Very clean hotel with beautiful atrium as well. Price was great as well for the weekend. Will definitely stay here again just for fun!!

“Wonderful stay here! Highly recommend!” We just returned from a 2 night stay at the Palomar and I will definitely go back. Everything was perfect. The room was beautiful, comfortable and spotless. We had a King Suite. The tub in our room was a "soaking tub" (meaning super deep) and had two seats across from each other (meaning plenty of room for two). The bed was heavenly and my husband and I both got a great night sleep. The service was first class all the way. Guest services could not have been nicer. The valets out front always got the door for us and got us a cab in a minutes. Even though there was a big wedding there the weekend we were there, we never felt neglected by the busy staff. The location is great. It is on N. State Street, and backs up to Nordstroms! In addition, we were walking distance to almost everything we wanted to do (including Lou Malnati's Pizza, which is only 4 blocks away, and has incredible Chicago deep dish pizza). My only suggestion would be to add a dresser to the room. Although our room was spacious, there were only 4 small drawers (in the TV cabinet). There was a ton of closet space, but we definitely needed more drawers.

“Wonderful staff, comfortable room, great location!” Stayed at this hotel for seven nights over the holidays. This was by far the best hotel stay I've experienced in New York City. The staff, from the front desk, to the doormen, to room service and the housekeeping staff were all excellent. Being from the West Coast, we were on a bit later schedule leaving our room almost every day but our housekeeper never missed a day cleaning our room! She was friendly and professional. Really a lovely lady! The turndown service staff were also great. We ordered room service dinner one evening and it arrived at exactly the time stated! The room service food wasn't spectacular but acceptable. If you're looking for a quick snack, I would recommend 71 Irving. They had excellent chai and their pumpkin lattes were made with real pumpkin--no sugary syrup! Their sandwiches were yummy as well. Really a nice neighborhood place. This hotel will be our first choice for future trips to NYC provided we can get an affordable rate.

“A dump. Avoid” One of those hotels that should be ripped down and started again, rather than undergoing a (noisy) refurbishment. The location is superb right next to Grand Central, but the grandeur of the station only underscores the draft, down-at-heel and plain scruffiness of the hotel. I had one of the so-called "upgraded" rooms - trendy with a bewildering array of lighting options, but it felt smaller than it was, and the corridors look drab even in their new garb. Also it is not good customer service to poke a note under the door at 2am telling me that my water was going to be cut off from 10am to 4pm the next day and hoping (ha!) that it would not disrupt my plans.

“Great Location - Great Rooms” Stayed here the weekend of March 24-26, 2006. Friend and I flew up to NYC to see "The Color Purple". This hotel is in the heart of everything you want to see and if you need a taxi, you can get one very easily. Our room was on the 45th floor and had 2 double beds, was a good size room, was very very clean, and had beds that rival the beds found at the Westin. Security here is excellent as no one gets on the elevators or escalators without showing room keys. Our room was beautiful and we had a beautiful view. Also the hotel personnel was very very nice and accommodating. Now for the negatives....the food at the hotel is way too expensive, even by NYC standards. The concierge is even more ridiculous. We were looking for some last minute Lion King Tickets and they told us they would start at $185 each. We called the theater directly and the price was $111 each. We also wanted to get a towncar to LaGuardia and the womon at the Concierge desk told me it would be $85 saying the service she uses has better insurance. I told her I would call someone else and asked for the number of another service with which I was familiar. She gave me the wrong number (not even close to the right number). Not saying she did it on purpose, but who knows. I did find the right number and the cost was $34.50, but I gave him $40. By the way, the name of the Limo service was CARMEL. They will pick you up at LGA and will also take appointments. They were very prompt and courteous. Other than those 2 points, everything else was great. Oh yeah, if you are looking for a great place for dinner, check out Blue Water Grill at Union Station. Will run you about $125 for dinner for 2, but very much well worth it. It's only about 10 mins from Crowne Plaza by taxi or town car. I will definitely stay at the Crowne Plaza in NYC again. I liked it so much I have booked the Crowne Plaza in San Francisco's Union Station. Enjoy your stay. By the way...The Color Purple was AWESOME!

“Kimpton Palomar - Keeping the Chic in Chicago” Stayed at the Palomar Chicago for 2 nights on return from a week in Vegas. Wanted to stay somewhere handy for all the attractions the city has to offer and the hotel met that expectation. We took the train from the airport and the hotel is a short walk from the station. Next day we walked a few blocks down and were at the bus stop for the City tour. Check in was a breeze and as Kimpton in touch members, we got free wi-fi and were able to 'raid the minibar'. Rooms are not huge, but enough space to get around. Bathrooms on the small side but very clean & modern. As we were celebrating an anniversary, we were given champagne & strawberries on arriving in the room - nice touch. The corridors of the hotel have some rather quirky artwork. Be warned though as some of them stick out in places and you might just catch your arm on them! The pool area and outside deck are gorgeous. In fact, I think they make the Palomar a real winner as many city boutique hotels don't have pools or outside sun decks. We went for a late night swim and it was fab! The hosted wine reception in the evening is a great place to chill for an hour and chat / relax. Great wine & great pizza! The lobby and lounge area are really nice with a gorgeous fireplace. We ate an evening meal at the restaurant and the quality was very good although this is reflected in the prices. All in all, this was a good stay for our short time in Chicago. Would recommend to others and would happily choose this hotel, and the Kimpton brand in the future.

“Cozy, Comfortable, and Clean” The hotel is located conveniently near the freeway system. The Hampton Inn South has rooms that are immaculate! The bed linens were our absolute favorite, as the chain has taken pride in clean, white linen with overstuffed duvets, lumbar pillows, and custom made sheets. Hotel staff is outstanding - friendly and will do whatever it takes to make your stay enjoyable. Free breakfast is from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m. which includes hot eggs and canadian bacon, biscuits, fruit, and pastries. There is a nice workout room as well. A complimentary copy of the USA today is given to guests as part of their service. Each room comes with a hair dryer, ironing board, and small, one cup coffee maker. We did not hear noise from other guests, as the walls appear to have some level of sound proofing material. I believe the hotel is above average and is a good price - worth paying a little more rather than going to cheap. Would definitely stay at the Hampton Inn South again.

“The city-view side is also nice” You can't get much closer to downtown San Diego. But as a business traveler, there were just a few things I wish this hotel had. I stayed in tower #1 (there are actually three towers) and my room faced the new, expanding San Diego cityscape. Rooms in the first tower are on the smallish side, and the closet / wardrobe is actually in the bathroom--the first time I've seen that--anywhere. The beds were comfortable, and I got great sleep. But just don't leave the balcony door open at night. Aircraft taking off from nearby San Diego Airport can clearly be heard. Also, there is some traffic noise and some train noise from the nearby Amtrak Station, which is a block away. However, with the balcony door *closed,* all was quiet. If I had my wish, there would have been a real desk in my room at which I could have done my paper work . A reading chair would also have been nice too, though my room was so small, I don't know where it could have been put. I took a few photos which should be attached.

“We loved it!” I recently traveled to Chicago on business (4 nights) - a friend and two children also traveled with me. The Embassy Suites Chicago Lakefront fit everyone’s needs, from the great location to many sightseeing attractions, to the pool, great free breakfast, big roomy suites, and wonderful friendly service. It is a two-room suite set-up and that just what we needed. We requested early check-in since our train was arriving in the morning and even though the hotel was sold-out; we were able to get in our room before lunch. The maids were super friendly and let us trade out as many towels as we wanted on a daily basis since we declined other service. With four females, we went through a lot of towels. Ron in Engineering fixed our sofa bed and then gave us two free in-room movies for the slight inconvenience. Ken O. and Elena S. were simply delightful to work with! We’ll see you again soon. I have traveled to Chicago numerous times and usually stay at the Omni, but the Embassy Suites Lakefront offers more value for the money. Yes, you have to pay for Internet, but we certainly re-cooped than money with the daily breakfasts, snacks, and drinks. If you want to avoid the lines for omelets, go early to breakfast, otherwise the other foods are available with virtually no wait. Attended the evening reception only once and there was no line. There is just so much to see and do in Chicago, it could easily make a week-long family vacation destination. The hotel was walking distance to Navy Pier, Michigan Avenue, Hancock Building, Water Tower Mall, and the Hershey Store. Also during the trip, had the opportunity to go to Shaw’s Crab House for the Sunday Brunch. All I can say to the seafood lover is “unbelievable”... I never knew king crab could taste so fresh!...and homemade lollipops too.... It’s almost worth flying from PA just to go there! There were also filming Transformers 3 in the city so that added to the excitement. We love Chicago and the Embassy Suites Lakefront and hope to return soon!

“Nice stay.” 2 night stay based on reviews and price. Room a little small and needed some maintenance, especially the bathroom but met our needs. Beds and pillows were fine. Internet worked fine and was fast enough to get my daily pics uploaded in a timely manner. The location isn't downtown but worked fine for us and San Francisco's public transit seems pretty user friendly to me. Breakfast could be a little more extensive but it worked. The biggest issue here, as others have mentioned, is lack of parking. If you get a spot don't move the car, there aren't enough to go around. There is a day care next door and we did hear some noise from it but that wasn't a problem. Price was good for San Francisco and we would stay here again in the future.

“Emplacement excellent. Très bon rapport qualité/prix.” Hôtel très sympa avec un parfait emplacement à l'angle de la 3ème et de la 24ème, tout près de Madison Square et à 5mn à pied du Subway. Les taxis ne sont pas chers vers les principales attractions de New York. L'accueil est très chaleureux; Le personnel est très sympathique et professionnel donnant de précieux conseils pour les attractions, les restos... Les chambres sont très propres avec une excellente literie et une jolie déco. Elles sont spacieuses pour NYC. Très belle terrasse au 10ème avec vue imprenable sur l'Empire State Building.

“Absolutely wonderful--would return and recommend” The Omni hotel is centrally located to absolutely all the main attractions, shopping, parks, and restaurants. The hotel is lovely, well-maintained, and offers a variety of amenities: restaurant, fitness center, pool, spa, etc. The rooms are quite large for a city hotel--we had a standard room that included a king-sized bed, sitting area, two flat-screen TVs, and a granite bathroom. Our room was impeccably clean and surprisingly quiet (we were near the elevator and ice machine and were not disturbed). The hotel staff were extremely polite and helpful. The concierge recommended wonderful restaurants. The only quirk about the hotel were the elevators--you cannot go directly from the lobby to guest rooms, you are required to switch on the third floor. We'll worth the price. We will definitely stay there again and recommend the Omni to friends.

“Good Fairfield Inn” I was looking for a clean, reasonably priced room near my company's offices on Central Avenue. I was a little reluctant to book this hotel because I didn't know much about it. It was a good experience: the staff was friendly and helpful in recommending a place to do some shopping (I had forgotten to pack any ties!) and some not-too-far-away recommendations for dinner. The room was clean and everything worked just fine. I even received an email from the manager a couple of days later asking if everything was OK. I'd certainly stay here again.

“Could Use Some Improvements” Stayed here for one night and here are my observations on the plusses and minuses: Plusses: 1) Great location 2) Terrific water pressure in shower 3) Comfortable bed The minuses: 1) Lots of street noise (I was on 12th floor). Having stayed in many other midtown hotels, this was by far the noisiest. Windows must be original construction 2) Flat screen TV's, but no HD! It's 2012 folks. Watching a standard def picture on a flat screen tv is ridiculous for an upscale midtown property 3) Others have observed that you cannot adjust the room temperature by yourself. You must call the front desk to have someone come up. Not very practical. I returned from an evening engagement at 11 o'clock to find the room chilly. Was I really supposed to call the front desk at that time and wait for someone to show up to make the room warmer? I do hope that the hotel will consider improving on these points.

“Austin stay for Thanksgiving” We stayed here the night before Thanksgiving prior to the TCU-Texas Game. We had a great Thanksgiving meal that was provided for us through the restaurant. In the morning they had a wonderful breakfast that was compliments of the hotel. We had a very nice suite as you normally get with Embassy suites!

“Excellent hotel, very close to Times Square” Stayed at the Paramount as part of a six day trip to NYC. Check-in was very swift - despite reception staff not initially being able to find my reservation. That small matter was cleared up, and no further problems. The room was excellent - I was already aware that it was not the biggest room in the world, so the size of the 18th floor room was not a surprise. It was fine for me, but maybe for a couple or more would have been too small. THe room was extremely clean and modern. The housekeeping staff were excellent, always clean when I returned after a day in NYC. The hotel was close to subway - very convinent for sightseeing. One of the main supports of my visit was to see hockey, and an easy 15 minute walk to MSG. I would fully recommend hotel, and would definately stay there on a return visit to NYC.

“Gute Lage zu den Universal Studios” wir waren im juni 2009 3 nächte in diesem hotel. es its gut zu finden , es liegt in burbank direkt am freeway den mann nachts aber kaum hört. es hat einen schönen pool und das ganze gebäude ist ringsrum mit bäumen bepflanzt. die gegend ist auch sehr gut. die zimmer haben uns nicht ganz so gut gefallen, etwas altmodisch , da wir aber eh den ganzen tag unterwegs waren störrte uns dies nicht. es fährt mehrmals am tag ein shuttle direkt zu den universal studios. die parkgebühren waren auch ok. wir würden das hotel auf unserem nächsten la besuch wieder mit einplanen

“A Birds Eye View of 1600 Pennslyvania Ave.” Visited the city of my youth to stay in a hotel that always looked great from the street, turns out it is great thru and thru or is that through and through, how some ever it is spelled it is that. Historic as much of DC is, you couldn't be more centrally located to all the attractions that Washingtom has to offer. Lovely lobby, a great bar one flight down, Off The Record, rooms very comfortable and many of them afford a stunning view of the President's residence. I can't wait to return.

“Huge hotel, decent value, slow service” I stayed at this hotel on a weekend for two days. The checkin here is EXTREMELY slow. Its a big hotel and to only have 2-3 people working checkin is absolutely unacceptable. As you can imagine checkout is slow too. Why don't they just give you a folio under your door like most hotels and call it good? I needed one because I was here on business and wasted a good 15-20 minutes waiting. Nearly an hour of my life I can't get back. The rooms are extremely average and smell musty. They could also use a makeover, especially the standard def tvs, although you are in San Diego with plenty to do. Ask for a room as far away from the elevators as possible. They are really loud compared to most hotels and run all night because of the enormity of the property. The internet is pay for play and does not live up to its cost. The wifi is spotty and you can forget about the direct ethernet service. This hotel also gets low marks from me because I requested a king size room and ended up with a double.

“upscale overall, just seems like they skimped on oom cleaning a bitr...” We got a last minute Priceline deal and I had scoped out this hotel and knew it was much more upscale a place than we might normally stay. Our total with taxes was $180. So we can't complain much. Great feel and modern decor just 1 block southwest of Union Station. Only complaint is that it seems like housekeeping may have decided our room was clean enough. Random hair on the bed, under covers, by headboard--not ours. Also we found a bobby pin on the carpet and a bandaid wrapper on the bathroom floor. A thorough sweeping would have prevented that. Rack rate on the back of the door is $1,200. If I had paid that I would be irritated. Fancy animal print robes and marble bathroom. Very nice-sized room with desk and chair/ottoman. Great design. Quiet. Starbucks 2+ blocks west. No food in lobby except for their restaurant which did look very nice. One weird thing: we turned down a/c then left so it would be cool when we returned. Room was hot when we got back. Note by a/c says that to save energy they only cool to temp when you are in the room. We spent the rest of the night wondering how they knew we are in our room. I guess you could go off keycard door opening and closing, but that could easily get out-of-sync if you opened and closed the door and stayed IN the room.....right? Room did cool off well. If you are looking for the best place to stay, I would recommend going a bit further west. After walking DC (just one night), I think it would have been better to be closer to 7th street and just have to go north or south. That's were all the restaurants are--up and down 7th. Immediately around this hotel, except for Starbucks to the west--is all office buildings, no restaurants or attractions.

“Classic Hilton in desperate need of renovation!” This hotel is in a GREAT location. The lobby is nice and modern, but furniture shows bad signs of wear. The check in was efficient and friendly. Was upgraded to an Exec Floor rooom. Opened door to room and couldn't believe how old the room was... Stained carpet, 80s desk chair and furniture, tile in shower was moldy and original to building (70s). Mattress was VERY soft and felt old. I can honestly say nothing positive about the room other than it was of reasonable size... I tried to make coffee three times, each time Getting less than an ounce of coffee before cutting off. The bar was being remodeled, so a makeshift bar was set up in a meeting room. It felt like a bad 80s wedding... For $200 per night u can do MUCH better. Not sure how they got a 4 diamond rating. Maybe 2 at best.

“Very nice” Enjoyed our stay here very much. Good location, great view of the city, lake and river from our 17th floor room. Room was good sized and clean. Easy walk to Michigan Ave. stores. Lots of taxis available and the trolly comes right out front. Parking is expensive, but anywhere downtown is. Pool is on the smaller side. Lobby and bar nice. Shula's restaurant is located in the lobby.

“Great location and value” Location is excellent if you're looking for River North area. Hotel is very quiet, clean, and well appointed rooms. The value for the price is very good but this is a basic business hotel without the large groups.

“Seamless and pleasant” We picked the Courtyard when we wanted a comfortable place in the Ballantyne area of Charlotte. It turned out to be very satisfactory, despite the fact that work going on in the public areas made the entrance a cramped hallway. They managed to provide coffee and cookies neatly organized on one side, and they had junk food of various kinds for sale beside the reception counter. The service was great: All the staff weren't just polite, they were really pleasant and helpful. Here's what I liked: - The room was spacious and clean. It had a nice desk with a second pullout desk below it so you could make a comfortable office set-up. - The free wifi internet worked well. - The location was really convenient. Not scenic by any means, but close to restaurants, shops, the gas station, and the freeway. - The website warned of the lobby renovation IN ADVANCE so I was prepared to find it closed off. - The indoor swimming pool looked nice, though I didn't actually go in. Here's what I didn't like so much: - The bathroom was small, and split into a washbasin outside, loo and shower inside. (But it was well-maintained and worked fine.) - The room had only one chair, which I would not have noticed if I'd been alone. But not so nice for couples. - The place could do with some beautification inside and out -- plants, flowers, pictures etc. It's forgettably bland. Maybe the lobby renovation will fix that.

“Fine for a quick stay” We found the Doubletree to be good for what we needed- a place to stay when our plane arrived late and we didn't want to start driving anywhere until the next day. The airport shuttle was very good- better than other hotels I have stayed in. It seemed to ALWAYS be running, and was very convenient. We took the shuttle from the airport, and then back again to pick up our rental car (save the parking fee). The hotel was fine- a big hotel by the airport. I didn't expect much, but some things were better than average. The view we had was of some large trees and some people's backyards- better than the parking lot for us (but I wouldn't want to live there!). The cookies are, of course, one of our favorite things about the Doubletree chain. If I had been wanting to stay for more than one night, be close to anything interesting (other than the artificially created world of SEATAC), or wanted to get some business done, this would not have been the best hotel. But it is fine for what it is- a quick, convenient, comfortable stay by the airport. One thing to think about- this hotel is used by a lot of conventions. When we were there, there were a bunch of real estate agents who were getting a bit rowdy. We couldn't hear them in our room (thankfully), but they were pretty loud throughout the hotel. The hotel is big and busy, so it always feels like there is some commotion going on in the common areas. We did book directly on the Hilton chain website and got a rate of about $89. It looks from other reviews here like you may be able to do better on Priceline if you don't want your Hilton points.

“We enjoyed our stay here due to the great balcony and view!” We stayed at the Fairmont last summer for three nights. We booked online and got a great deal on the Karachi Suite. This is a two room suite which offers an very large private balcony with a great view of the SF Financial District including the TransAmerica Building. Although we were technically only on the 4th floor, due to The Fairmont being atop Nob Hill, we were equivalent to being twenty or thirty stories above the city. We probably would not have enjoyed the stay as much if it were not for this great wrought iron balcony. The hotel itself is full service and offers all amenaties you would expect.

“Horrible Experience at this Sheraton Philly City Center” I called this hotel for a night in July, 06 at the govt. rate. Upon arrival, they had no record of my reservation, even though I had the number, and the name of the person who I spoke with. They were able to secure a room, but it took arguing to be given the govt rate. The room was dirty, there were hairs on the bathroom floor (the kind you don't want to see), and the desk agents were rude. The real fun began when I checked my credit card statement a week later. I saw that I had been billed for the same room twice. I called the hotel immediatley, and was told it would be taken care of and credited in a few days. That did not happen. I called again, asking for a manager- was given voice mail, but never received a call back. I also clicked on the Contact Us link on the homepage, and emailed, explaining the situation. I got a reply, saying the hotel would contact me within 3 days. They never did. It is now 50 days since I stayed, and I still have no credit for the double billing. I am also a SPG Gold card member, which didn't seem to matter to them.

“Elegant and homey” I recently stayed 4 nights at the Hotel Drisco in the beautiful Pacific Heights area. I travel to San Francisco about 4-5 times a year and work in SOMA. The complimentary car service and gourmet continental breakfast buffet were great extras. The hotel has a classic and elegant style, but it is very homey and comfortable like an inn. The staff are very friendly and make you feel very much at home. This was also a great plus when traveling alone for business. They have delicious hot panini sandwiches available, a complimentary DVD collection and a 24 hour tea/coffee area in the sitting rooms. The area is very upscale residential and the views are gorgeous. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone traveling for business or leisure.

“Comfortable Bed, Ultra Clean, Nice Staff” I've walked by this hotel many times over the past three decades and never thought about staying here. in late August, I had a reception and dinner that would end late, so instead of heading home on a very late train, I stayed at the Iroquois. I'm glad I did. The desk clerk was polite and friendly. I was upgraded to a "deluxe" room. This hotel must have been recently renovated because everything looked fresh and immaculately clean. The room was small, but larger than where I usually stay -- The Chemist's Club/Club Quarters a block away. The bed was very comfortable, turned down at night with Belgian chocolates on the pillows, with soothing music on the radio. The bathroom was spotless and featured Moulton Brown toiletries. Even the way they folded the soft, plush bath and hand towels and wash cloths was artistic. There was a one-liter bottle of Poland Spring sparkling water in the room, and unlike many hotels that charge you $5, at the Iroquois, it was with their compliments. What kept me from giving a fifth star? As a previous reviewer noted, I couldn't get the sound to work on the LG flat screen TV's digital channels. The volume on the analog channels was fine. There was a CD player in the room. In the morning, there was a copy of the New York Times placed in a nice cloth bag (not an oversized plastic baggie or thrown on the floor) hanging on the doorknob. There was also no bill slid under the door, which I actually liked. Whenever I see that in the morning, it's almost like saying, "Reminder -- don't forget to pay and try to leave early." Check-out took less than a minute. I did not eat at Triomphe. As expected, breakfast is expensive. I just grabbed a cup of excellent coffee in the lobby and walked three blocks to Grand Central to catch an early train. That close proximity to the station makes this a conveniently located hotel. Broadway is a block away for those who want to catch a show. The Iroquois is a member of the Small Luxury Hotels chain and deservedly so. I will definitely stay here again.

“Close to airport” I enjoy Aloft properties as an affordable, fun and free Internet option. This one is not the nicest I've visited, but close to airport with free shuttle. It offers a nice happy hour and some limited but acceptable food options. There is a small pool, although I did not use. The rooms are small and a bit worn given the age of this hotel, but have everything needed including a fridge. The staff is friendly and helpful. This is a good one night airport option, but not in a good location for longer stays to Phx.

“Muy buen hotel” Es un muy buen hotel con excelentes instalaciones ubicado cerca de Market Place y a 10 minutos caminando de Union Square.El personal es muy amable siempre hay alguien que habla espanol. Te recomiendo que si tenes que ir al aeropuerto desde aca pidas un taxi que es mas barato que un shuttle

“Excellent business hotel / great workout room” I was in Boston for a on overnight business trip so I did not get a chance to fully explore the hotel but I an say the rooms were very clean and large and the workout room was top notch. Valet parking was a bit expensive; there was self parking that I did not investigate.

“This has been upgraded...nice rooms, great location” This is a massive conference hotel with a caverous lobby. Not your place if you want intimate. But its a fine hotel. I stayed here a few years ago and was disappointed. It was mediocre. Guess I had a renovated room this time as it was quite nice. 15th floor, no noise. You have to ask to be away from the elevators as some rooms do back up to them. There is no little fridge. The fitness room is too small for the size of the hotel, but if you manage to get a spot at 6am, the machines are in good shape. The inside two lane lap pool is very clean. The beds in May still had big down" much too hot for the weather" comforters. Even with the room at 65 degrees they were too heavy. The location is terrific for business, dining, tourists.

“Not impressed” I agree with the prior assessment regarding the towels. How two adults are supposed to bath, wash faces, etc. with two bath towels is beyond me. The concierge was terrible. I am convinced they have a very lucrative deal going with the cab drivers as everything we asked about was, according to more than one concierge, too hard to get to by metro. We took our chances and did not find the 2-4 block walk to be prohibitive. Further, though I thought I made it clear that I was not playing along, one of the concierges would not stop flirting with me openly. It made me uncomfortable to walk into the hotel. Beware the "petite" queen room. It is VERY petite (think European). Also, all interior rooms face a parking lot or a wall about 3 feet away. Garbage was constantly overflowing in the public trash cans. On the plus side, great location convenient to the metro. I reserved the hotel at a deep discount on the internet, so no complaints on the price. Front desk staff was very helpful, including printing an attraction ticket for me at no charge so that I did not have to sign into the business center at $5 a pop. Front desk gets no complaints and high marks; they are what save the service rating above from being very poor.

“Very good business oriented hotel” This Westin was nice in that the rooms were very clean (even for Westin standards), modern looking, and quite large. It really felt like the hotel had been built or renovated recently. It was also nice that the hotel's business center and gym were open 24 hours. Room service was great too. Several things to note about this hotel. The hotel looks to be a part of a business building (I think the first 10 or so floors are business offices?). Also, not sure but this building may have been a complete office building before the top floors were converted to hotel rooms--each floor has a name that looks as if you are walking into a doctor's office. Also, one of the other downsides while I was visiting was that the pool had been rented out to a private party. Understandable that the hotel needs to make money, but it seems pretty presumptuous to close the pool on the weekend when that is one of the top amenities at the hotel. It wasn't a deal breaker for me, but I could see that a visiting family might be annoyed. Last but not least, the AC unit in the room does not seem to be adjustable. You can control the temperature range to a degree, but the unit appears to be permanently on. This was annoying if you didn't want the fan blowing on you all night.

“Tolle Zimmer, guter Standard für ein US Hotel” Direkt am Hancock Tower gelegenes Hotel, in Laufweite zum Lake Michigan und der Magnificent Einkaufsmeile. Kleine aber feine Lobby mit kostenlosem Internetzugang (wenn man anschliessend als angemeldeter User ins Zimmer geht kann man kostenlos im Zimmer weitersurfen!). Die Zimmer sind kleine Suites mit getrenntem Wohn- und Schlafraum, Kochnische mit Spüle und Microwellenherd, 2 Flachbildfernseher und schönem Bad. Die Zimmere variieren etwas in Schnitt und grösse, man kann also durchaus mit Glück eine richtig grosse Suite erwischen.

“OUTSTANDING” Everything was oustanding. The room was beautiful. The Service was extraordinary. The bar in the lobby was fantastic and attracted a great non hotel crowd. I travel quite a bit on business and pleasure and very much rank this place highly. Only negative is the price but you do indeed get what you pay for.

“Nice hotel, excellent location” My wife and I stayed here on 24 and 25 September 2012 as part of a Cosmos bus tour to Los Angeles. We loved the location facing the park ; if it's good enough for the grand Hilton Chicago just across a side street, it's good enough for us! Our room was very comfortable with two beds and tea and coffee making facilities, and the hot water and air conditioning were good. The hotel lobby is a nice place to look out to the park across Michigan Avenue. There is no free breakfast, but we stocked up at Trader Joe's on Roosevelt Street, a few blocks south of the hotel. We would stay here again when we come back to Chicago.

“Great home base in Chicago” This was our second visit to Hotel Indigo. What a pleasure to be at this well-kept secret. The location is central - walking distance to Water Tower, a few blocks from the lake, several good restaurants on the same block, large drugstore on the corner for those pesky things you forgot.... It's also convenient to the red line train for an inexpensive way to get around the city. We ate several times at the Third Coast Cafe down the street and had good food and wine at reasonable costs. The decor is fresh and cheery - doesn't feel "big city" but more coastal as it's on the Gold Coast I suppose. There is Aveda product in the bathroom (don't have to bring my own!), a coffee service on the side, and they will bring up a fridge if you need one. The rooms are large with a separate table/sitting area and enclosed shower/toilet area. A few negatives or personal dislikes: there was no ability to crack the windows and at times the hotel had funky odors in the hallways and room. The air conditioner is a bit noisy and cycles on and off repeatedly. My son was unhappy at the few available channels in the room, but the basics are there. The pillows are hard and lumpy - next time I'll bring my own. Service is great and the bar and small cafe in the lobby were handy. Free wifi throughout the hotel. Staff is as attentive as ones you'd find in a luxury hotel. Price point is good for what you get. Look forward to staying here on our next trip!

“Will stay here for every conference in Columbus!” Four of us stayed at this hotel for a conference in Columbus area, booked a 2 QUEEN BEDS STUDIO SUITE W/ SOFABED NONSMOKING room & had PLENTY of room for all of us, our wardrobes, belongings, & shopping items. Great staff, SUPER clean rooms, hotel, delicious breakfast & even a bagged breakfast if you can't/don't have time for the hot breakfast. Had an issue with our first room having a very strong smell (like smoke and a chemical "smoke smell remover" had been used--one of us have a high sensitivity to sensory allergy triggers and the staff at the Hampton Inn moved us without question and verified there were no present odors in the new room. Another reason we'll always choose Hampton Inn! Great value!!

“Slept Soundly @ The City That Never Sleeps” Fashion 26 must be one of the nicest medium size hotels in NYC. The service was impeccable. Lourdes at the front desk exemplified the fine service you'd expect at a much more expensive hotel. Carlos, the porter continued the perfect welcome. In addition, a wonderful building engineer (I can't remember his name, my apologies, assisted me twice). In addition, the head housekeeper (again my memory faults me) went out of her way to help me locate my cell phone recharger. Not once, did any employee "have their hand out" for a tip! The room was gorgeous, with a view of the Empire State building. The bed was more comfy than my one at home. Everything "worked" at this hotel. My hat's off to the employees and the management team of this fine hotel. I will definitely return and recommend Fashion 26 to friends visiting the city.

“Average Business Hotel” I stayed here for one night on a business trip. Great location if you have business that the PA Convention Center. Close to Reading Terminal. I stayed in a suite - bathroom was a bit outdated. Ovearll, room was fine. Nothing extremely special, just a nice average business hotel.

“Hello? 1985 called and wants their hotel back.” After I won a "3.5 star hotel" on Priceline and read the reviews I realized I was in a classic trap... Priceline rated this hotel much higher than is realistic and I couldn't cancel. So, I took it like a man and stayed there. This property is a Crowne Plaza in name only. I got the hotel for $40 ($55 with taxes and fees), and I guess you get what you pay for. But never again. Location: terrible. Tucked back in an industrial/office complex that's as outdated as the hotel. In an older part of town that's a little scary. Staff: friendly. The night crew reminded me of the Ghostbusters but it was clear they were doing the best they could. Rooms: Not good. Wall-to-wall worn and outdated. Not "dirty" per se, but cracked, peeling wallpaper, nasty doors, old furniture and drapery, damaged countertops, worn bathtubs, etc.

“Higher floors are much quieter” I stayed here a few weeks back and was in a room on the 9th floor. There was a lot of street noise that was audible throughout the day and night. This week, I stayed here again and asked for a higher floor. I was put on the 17th floor and it was much quieter, plus the view was considerably better. The rooms were the same. The showers are quite small and it is not possible to get put the spray while you are lathering up. Also, the tv in my room had signal issues on several high def channels.

“A major disappointment” I stayed this past weekend and found the “resort” very lacking. For the quality it was overpriced. The resort was poorly run and based on what the employees said, the management doesn’t care or is incompetent. It’s really too bad as all of the employees I interacted with were friendly, polite, and apologetic for the condition of the hotel. I have never heard “I’m sorry” so much in a hotel. First, when getting out of the shower, I noticed a dirty towel handing on the back of the door. There were hairs on the shower curtain. There was no Do Not Disturb sign in my room. My room was not cleaned until after 4:30pm. In a resort you expect relaxation but if you spend the day waiting for your room to be cleaned it’s not relaxing. There is a $30.00 resort fee which basically is for a small water park that was overcrowded. The wave pool had no waves, just wall to wall people floating on rafts. The pool bar had no fans or misters. Come on, it was 109 degrees. I’ve been to resorts in Las Vegas and Hawaii and guess what; they have fans and often misters. There was a $14.95 per day fee for the internet. I felt this was inappropriate due to the $30.00 resort fee. So in addition to an overpriced room rate, the daily fees were an additional $49.95. What a rip-off! At a resort, I would expect multiple restaurants and bars including some upscale dining. They advertise 3 restaurants but two of them are not run by the hotel or within walking distance. We ate at the steak restaurant and were told it is their best restaurant. The restaurant is about 2 steps below an Outback. It was not part of the hotel, as you needed to drive to it and you could not charge to your room. Breakfast in the Grill was lacking. They had a breakfast buffet for $16.00 that would not make it at Bob’s Big Boy. The bacon was burnt, the eggs dried out as well where the croissants. There was one omelet station with a 10 minute wait. The buffet was set-up in the server area of the kitchen. The floor was greasy. I don’t mean to disparage Outback or Bob’s Big Boy as they deliver value, something this resort fails to do. As for the mini-bar; what a joke, it had a very small selection. It had 2 Snickers bars, 2 bags of M&Ms, and 2 small cans of Pringles. For alcohol it had some beer and 2 mini bottles of vodka along with a few sodas and waters. Not much of a choice. Unless your rate is very low, spend your money at a quality hotel. For what I paid, I should have chosen a Westin, Hyatt or Marriott, it would probably been a much better experience and based on the internet, less expensive.

“Good value but some issues” This is a brand new hotel and very attractive on the inside and outside. Service was great for this level of hotel. The staff was friendly and helpful. The floor plan of the tower was very tight though. The hallways were narrow and there was a housekeeping cart right outside the elevator on our floor nearly every time we returned to the room. The rooms were tiny as well, but that's someone expected in NYC. I did however find myself feeling like the room wasn't big enough for our basic needs, which is not something that I've ever really noticed in a hotel. There were 4 of us and there really was nowhere to unfold our bags and spread out. The beds also were acceptable but nowhere NEAR the comfortability of Hyatt Place beds, and had strange lumps in the comforters. But the location was spectacular right off the busy but not obnoxiously so--I'm talkin' to you Times Square!--Herald Square. The subway station is literally just steps away, so the location is convenient to the whole city. Also we came by train from EWR and it's an easy walk here from Penn Station, even with luggage.

“An absolute gem” Let me start by saying, I spend about 100 nights a year at hotels around the country and the world. And I have to say with all honesty, Hotel Commonwealth is one of the best I've stayed at in several years. It is almost perfect. We'll get the thing that makes it a slight notch less than perfect out of the way first. The location is not perfect (unless you are going to a Red Sox game, in which case, it is perfect). It is near Boston University and Fenway Park, but not much else is around. Still, the neighborhood is safe and active and it is literally right next to the "T" station, which makes getting around town easy. The hotel itself is perfect, in my opinion. The staff is absolutely the best, the rooms are beyond comfortable (with a great, soft bed, huge room, huge bathroom and a great layout). The layout is the best. My king room had a large bathroom (spotless) and a semi-private sitting room and desk. The desk is large and well laid out and the sitting room makes you feel like you are in a suite. As a business traveler, I appreciated that the hotel didn't nick you for $20 for wireless internet (like may of the "luxury" chain hotels do). What can I say? It exceeded all my expectations. When I return to Boston, I will certainly stay at the Commonwealth. I sincerely wish all hotels were just like this.

“Improvement shown” I find myself back here about 6 months after my first visit and it seems the management paid attention to the comments. Issues with shower pressure and room temperature have been solved. Internet is more reliable. Lobby and bar staff are more attentive. It's still not my first choice, but it's greatly improved over December's stay.

“Very nice hotel - good location” This is a very nice hotel, the rooms are spacious and very well equipped as you would expect from the four seasons - nice big bathrooms, comfortable beds, nice window seating area overlooking Market St. Very convenient for the Union Square area directly across the street. Very clean and well maintained - big health club free to guests, open to other members but I will take a well equipped healthclub that is open to a limited one that isn't any day. My small nit-pick is that the lobby and common areas are somewhat soul-less and there is an almost anonymous feel to it. Overall though you can't go wrong here -
