“Great--If You Don't Need a Hot Shower” First, the pros. Great location very near La Cantera. New hotel, very clean, comfortable beds, nice staff (with the notable exception of a housekeeper who nearly ran us down with her laundry cart and didn't even apologize). Now the cons: Thin walls; the 2 bedroom/2 bath suite we stayed in (the most expensive accomodation in the hotel) is situated right next to the housekeeping room; there was a LOT of noise in the morning. Finally, the dealbreaker for me: we could not get truly hot water in the shower, only warm water. This might be OK if you visit during a hot S.A. summer, but it was most aggravating on a cold January morning.

“Bad News” Pros: -Location -Price ($50 on Priceline) Cons: -Dirty rooms -Poor customer service You be the judge. I'd stay here only if you get a good deal on Priceline; otherwise, don't waste your money. Rooms were filthy and staff couldn't care less.

“clean newer hotel next to the convention center” going to Minute Maid Park, flying into Hobby this time. Third time visiting, wanted to stay closer to the ballpark and looked at the three hotels, ES, Hilton and Inn at the Park. Chose ES because of the newness of the place. Checkin was fine on a muggy, humid afternoon. The clerk mention there was parking in my rate, which I knew she was incorrect. Asked if there was comp. water in the room and she replied, Yes. Up to the room, 17th floor, newer hotel and room was fine. The AC could have been set colder (72 degrees is the lowest it went). Fridge, can't remember if there was a microwave. The bathroom was bigger than my closest at home. One window facing north towards some parking lots. All the utility stuff is energy saver type, which doesn't really make things dimmer. The evening reception was on the second floor, chips went quick but refilled. One bartender, at least five people waiting for drinks. The guy was more worried about melting the ice than pouring free drinks. Leaving for the baseball game, I mention to the clerk, no water. "Oh, I'll have housekeeping send it up." When I return, the clerk realizes she forgot to tell housekeeping, no biggie, must have gotten busy. Breakfast was fine with buffet and made to order eggs and omelets. My biggest concern was cost of parking. The parking lots surrounding the hotel can charge $15 for special events (there is the House of Blues for concerts a block away). Paid it because I got there at 3pm and parked overnight. The next day (Saturday), I parked at the meters, $6 from 7am to 6pm. If you do this on a weekday, you have to move and change you space every four hours, Saturday keep your same space. I asked a parking ticketer guy in a city truck. Overall, quiet, peaceful stay.

“Have always found this HGI to be a great choice !” I've stayed at this property at least 3 times in the last year or so. I have found them to be consistent in a good way with cleanliness, service, etc. The rooms are your typical HGI rooms with the little fridge and microwave. The bathroom is a nice size with quite a bit of counter space. The location is convenient to Cypress Fairbanks Hospital, Willow Brook Mall and another nice shopping area. A number of restaurants are close by and there is a PF Chang's less than a block away. On my most recent visit there was some type of high school tournament in town (rugby or soccer) and the hotel was full of high school boys and parents. Frankly, lots of the parents were in the bar more than they were watching their kids -- but -- the hotel staff did a great job of stopping all of the elevator and hallway "running and jumping" that was going on while the parents were in the bar. The weekends are usually pretty quiet though. Would stay here again -

“Austin's Best Kept Secret” This hotel is great for families. You can get a two bedroom suite with a full kitchen and two bathrooms for an excellent price. The location is superb with several great restaurants in the area and it's just minutes from downtown. The hospitality is great and the hot breakfasts and evening meals during the week are an added treat.

“Great location but too many problems” I travel to Houston several times a month for work and stay at this Westin due to its location only. Every time I stay here I tell myself it will be the last time due to all the unnecessary frustration it adds to my trip. Being a SPG frequent traveler I usually enjoy my stays at Westin's. First, I agree with some of the other comments regarding the hotel needing an update. It is not on par with other Westin's. I felt like I need to write a review for the following reasons: It took me almost 15 minutes to check in due to the hotel not having enough front desk agents. This has happened several times and it seems like an easy fix. I called to see if the hotel had a refrigerator and mini bar and was told "YES" several times by multiple people. THEY DO NOT HAVE EITHER! I don’t understand why they continue to give out misleading information. The TV in the room did not work and maintenance had to come to the room each day I was there to reset the cable box. Most hotels have a phone by the bed for calls and so you don’t have to get up and go across the room to answer the wake up call. One phone and not close to the bed. They have installed a new elevator system which is very user unfriendly and very loud. My one suggestion if you stay here is get a room as far from the elevator as possible. I was all the way down the hall and could still here the 4 ear piercing rings every time the elevator opened. It is hit and miss on the hotel staff. Some are very helpful and courteous and some are very rude and unfriendly. I am not looking forward to finding a new place to stay in Houston but I can no longer accept all the problems with this Westin. Also, they share parking with the Galleria mall which is a challenge of its own. Good luck!

“decent hotel experience” I stayed at the Doubletree hotel for a week in february. In general it is a decent place to stay, the room was pretty big ( bedroom + living room), clean, the bathroom also quite big. We booked a room on the 39th floor so the view was also pretty ok. The location was perfect. The only weak point was the service, we have booked a room with the internet, which didn't work at all during the entire week, we were always told to go down to the lobby to use the free wireless. It was pretty disappointing because we payed for the internet already...After many discussions we were offered breakfast instead which was a nice but pretty late gesture though. Also the concierge was a bit weird, we wanted to make reservations in a restaurant and were told to call the restaurant ourselves, after some discussions the concierge allegedly called the restaurant and booked a table but when we showed up at the restaurant they did not have any reservation under our name...(this being a concierge guy...the lady however was really helpful and adorable) Overall it was a good stay, which could have been even better with some minor adjustments. I would recommend the hotel for a NYC trip because the location is just outstanding!

“Cute and Cozy” This is a cute, neighborhood hotel. Nothing fancy, but very shabby/chic. I really needed to stay in midtown, but due to hotels being sold out or asking an ungodly amount of money, I opted to stay at the Franklin. It is way up on the upper east side, in a cute neighborhood...Starbucks is across the street, as well as several delis, restaurants and drugstores. The lobby is really small and they have a cool, old fashioned elevator. My room was very small, but cozy..reminded me of home. I had a tiny little bathroom, but a really large queen bed that was really comfortable. The fixtures in the room are cute and make you feel very much at home. They have a small flatscreen TV on the wall..which makes watching TV in bed very comfortable. The shower was small but worked just great. The only thing that I would say that makes this hotel hard, is that the AC is really loud and I was on a long business trip and had a large suitcase..and there was no where to put it except on the floor next to my bed, and there is no closet. Everyone that works here is really, really nice..and I definately would return to this hotel again.

“Good alternative to the chains....” Sometimes hotels that try and be trendy end up being too focused on being funky and trendy, and forget that at the end of the day people are looking for quiet, comfortable rooms, and great service. Having stayed at some, I feared that Sixty Thompson in Soho New York would be one of the former - as they make much of their style, attitude and locations in trendy parts of town. I had also read mixed reviews, including those talking about the place being a bit shabby. Overall, I was impressed with the hotel. I found the location was great (right within easy access of all that Soho has to offer) but in a quiet spot. I found the decor stylish, without being overly done. The staff almost without exception were friendly, genuine and chatty. The hotel is not cheap, but not many are in New York. I had asked for a room higher up as heard that the lower rooms can suffer from noise from the trendy bar on the lobby floor. And it was quiet and peaceful. The room was a decent size, with decent sized bed (though not as comfy as some of the chain hotels), sofa, big TV. But no desk to be able to sit and work at. This was a miss as sure these days even people not on work also like to sit on a laptop and so on. The wireless access is expensive at $14.75, and it costs per device and so if you attaching a work laptop and maybe a personal iPad you pay twice. The bathroom was great, and had shower and no bath. Something more common these days. Room service was very fast and very friendly. The restaurant downstairs, which is a Thai fusion, was not that good in my view. It is very popular and although I was so-so on the food, they did amazing cocktails (especially the Classic Moijto) There is a very small fitness room in the basement that was average. But enough stuff to have a decent workout. The hotel was good at checking and watching activity on twitter @60_thompson and noted comments and so on through my stay. This was a nice touch too. Overall a pleasant place to stay. Good alternative to chains...

“Great Loctaion, Nice Hotel” Stayed three nights in connecting rooms on the 17th floor. We faced the bay and did not have any problems with noise. The construction is on the other side of the hotel so avoid that side if possible. Rooms were nice and clean with large windows, plenty of desk space and modern decor. We had requested a mini fridge since we were traveling with small children and they had one in the room upon our arrival . Hilton Honors program provided us with free continental breakfast and appetizers each day – both had plentiful choices and quality of food was good. You could upgrade to the “hot” breakfast buffet for $10 per person. Location is great. Short walk to the Embarcadero and Ferry Building. Right next to China Town and North Beach. The Financial District is not crowded on weekends so getting around was easy. Valet Parking is convenient but expensive (as it is at all downtown hotels) with all the taxes and fee’s it comes to about $55/day. You have unlimited in/out privileges and they always had our car ready within 5 minutes max. Overall the staff was very friendly and accommodating. The only thing that was not great was getting a cab. Instead of hailing a cab for you, the Bellman told you to stand out at the curb and get your own. This happened several times during our stay. This was the only disappointment in an otherwise very nice experience.

“Ok , but not worth the money” We stayed here for one night, and found it a hotel that concentrates on conferences rather than your normal guest. We found it hard to get a room in the city for that particular night and so we paid above the odds for this - @ $200 for the night. We felt when we checked in that if you weren't with the conference, then why were we staying in the hotel. The guy at the main door didn't even hold it open when you are trying to lug your bags into the lobby, we then had to que for 15-20 minutes just to check in. We were not given any information about the hotel and when I rang down to reception at one stage to find out if there was a business centre in the hotel that I could access the Internet through, I was just short of being asked why didn't I bring my lap-top with me so I could use the Internet access in the room.... !! I found the staff very rude and not helpful at all and would not recommend this hotel for a tourist.

“The rating would be WAY higher if it weren't for the early AM construction” This is a nice hotel. There's a very cool lobby, with all sorts of interesting chairs. It's literally right next tot he WTC viewing entrance, so if you've come to NY for that, it's very good in that way. It's all what's really terrible about it. The hotel directly overlooks both the WTC memorial-in-progress and the HUGE construction site/pit next to it. Every morning, at about 7:30, the work starts, and it is really really loud. It is pretty amazing to see this view-- moving, upsetting, etc-- and it's a historical opportunity to view-- but at the price of a NYC hotel, you're not going to get much peace and quiet in the morning, and if you're not an early riser, forget it. The rooms are almost all glass, so if you're at all height-phobic, I'd go elsewhere. Otherwise, the experience of being high up in the air surrounded with glass is cool. The bed is not very comfortable in the deluxe hotel sort of way. Kind of middle of the road. the design of the room for suites is nice-- small for sure, but has a European feel. I liked the design of the room and some of the touches-- like the tour books that they leave for you. So: if the construction site will be upsetting for visual or noise reason, go somewhere else. If you love the height and get up at 5 AM, I'd say it's good. Also note, while you can get to the Rector Street subway easily, this is an IMPOSSIBLE neighborhood to navigate around in terms of street driving-- with so many streets being shut off or rerouted, since both 9-11 and now with Zucotti Park.

“Denied offering of packages listed on Trump Website, no alternatives, absent response” Yowzer. My wife and I have been scouting a 'babymoon' for a few weeks. After examining our options we decided on the Trump Central Park babymoon package. However, when I called to book the reservation, after being placed on hold, I was informed the package is no longer offered. When I inquired as to 'why is this package still prominently advertised on your website' no answer could be given. Further, when I inquired about comparable alternatives nothing was offered other than.....big.....empty......awkward....silence.... I politely hung up. To the manager: -Please keep your website updated with current offerings. Your customers deserve better. -Please train, or allow, your representatives to offer SOME alternative upon inquiry. Silence is not good customer service.

“You'll enjoy it” Have now stayed at the Hotel Monaco twice for a total of 5 nights. Overally, I've been very pleased. Checkin and checkout are easy and I've never had to wait in line. I've stayed in both a suite and the basic king room. The suite is essentially a very large room separated by a curtain. The sitting room has a couch and additional flat screen TV. Unless you're traveling with more than 2 people or want to spend a lot of time in your room, the standard room is more than adequate. Suite bath is pretty much the same as a regular room (they do have suites with jacuzzis that might be more elaborate). Hotel is only 11 floors so don't expect panoramic views. Furnishings are "funky" but tasteful. Rooms appear to be in good repair. Robes (with animal print) are standard. Large flat screen TVs with many, many channels are standard. Bathroom amenities (Aveda) are replenished daily. Bathrooms are modern with tile floors and granite counters. I've had mixed room service experiences. Twice, it was fast and food (pizza) was excellent. One morning breakfast was late and cold. The soft-boiled eggs were hard, which is good because they didn't provide a spoon. The attached restaurant is okay, but the one time we tried it service was very slow. Have heard that it's good for lunch/dinner but the menu wasn't that appealing to me so didn't try it. The concierge was helpful but was rarely seen before 9 or after 5. However, the front desk personnel were great. Wake up calls came promptly. There is free wireless and wired interet access as well as a computer in the lobby for those who didn't bring their own. There are some additional nice touches. First, they host a "wine hour" from 5-6 each evening. Wine is decent (and free) and they do refill your glass. It's a nice way to unwind and mingle with colleagues or even strangers. They are also very pet friendly -- actually seem to enjoy pets rather than merely "accepting" them. For example, this huge dog joined the wine hour and started to wander off into the restaurant. The staff didn't panic -- merely quietly alerted the owner who rectified the situation. The location is good -- walking distance to a lot of things. However, the hotel is on a San-Francisco type hill, so if you walk down to Pike Market, it's a VERY steep walk back up. The one nice thing about this hotel is that it caters to a variety of traveler types. We saw Packers' fans (in town for the NFL game), business people, tourists, etc. A nice mix with nice staff. It is a pleasant change from the traditional loud, impersonal hotels you find in so many large cities. Would definitely recommend it and stay there again.

“Secluded Comfort” Stayed 3 nights at the Ritz-Carlton Georgetown in November, 2007. A boutique hotel. In a quiet location just a couple of short blocks from the center of bustling M Street. Room overlooking 31st Street was quiet with muffled street noise and Reagan Airport fly-over noise. No voices or sounds from adjoining rooms. Recent conversion of an old brick "incinerator building". Conversion nicely done--appealing architecture inside and out that fits character of Georgetown. Had a premier room that was relatively small by luxury standards. Dim lights, none adequate for reading. Requested 3-way floor lamp that allowed me to read. Inadequate drawers, only 3 astonishingly small drawers. Very comfortable king bed. Very nice, spacious bath with separate shower. One, not-too-comfortable chair. Very pleasant restaurant. I only had breakfast there which was fine. Had outstanding dinner at Seasons restaurant in nearby Four Seasons hotel. Also very good Italian dinner at Cafe Milano on Prospect Street, just off of Wisconsin. Circulator bus on M Street runs frequently and connects to all sights for $1 per trip. Took to Union Station at end of stay. For arrival from Dulles, took 5A Metro bus from airport to Rosslyn Metro station, then taxi from across from station to hotel. I liked staying in Georgetown. I got used to the room size as my stay went on and ended up being satisfied with my room and the hotel overall.

“Central downtown location, massive hotel” There are 4 towers in the hotel all are connected, but it is a massive hotel. I was on a SPG preferred floor. I believe I was in a newly remodeled room. It was a decent size, large bed. I was only there for a night, but it had it been more the bathroom and closet size would have been in a factor as they were quite small. They have a nice outdoor pool. The gym is large with several treadmills, elliptical, and machine weights as well as free weights. There are many dining options in the hotel. The bona vista lounge actually rotates which is cool and weird all at once. I didn't dine at the steak house.

“Great facility and amazingly convenient to catch early flight” I'm always leery of a Hilton when I travel cause I never know if I'm going to get the elegance of the Santo Domingo Hilton in the Dominican Republic or the run-down, 60's hippish joint like that in Grand Rapids, MI. I was pleasantly surprised by the Hilton O'Hare and blown away by the convenience. I was scheduled to have my rental car till day of departure; 6am Friday morning. I was able to return the car Thursday evening, take the shuttle to terminal 2, drop downstairs to the underground passage, and arrive at the front desk of the Hilton. The room was great. My view overlooked the airport and runways. The fitness center was awesome! It took me 5 minutes to walk from my room on the 10th floor to get security line at the airport. 15 minutes later, i was at my gate. Will definitely stay here again!!!!!

“First class value for money” We stayed two nights at the Coventry Motor Inn and couldn't have been more pleased. I asked for a quiet room and got just that! The price per night was so good that it must be one of the best deals in San Francisco, particularly when one considers free covered parking and free wifi. The room was spacious with a safe, plenty of storage and coffee making facilities. A fridge would have been useful but I understand you can request these. The room was very clean the bed comfortable and the heating very efficient. There is a great restaurant diagonally across the side road on Buchanan Street called the Brazen Head. It is not glaring at you but in a discrete position with atmospheric lighting, a real buzz and excellent food at reasonable prices. The location of the Coventry Motor Inn is very good and even from Union Square, a taxi back is only about 12 dollars. The staff were really friendly and helpful. All in all, an excellent find and if I had a car in San Francisco. this is the obvious place to stay if you are looking for good value for money in a very comfortable hotel.

“Nice hotel, great location, a bit noisy” Overall, I liked the property and had a comfortable stay. The room was moderately spacious, and the wall to wall window overlooking the bay offered a great view (19th floor). Comfortable beds, clean, in-room coffee. Soundproofing should have been a greater emphasis when the property was built. The train, trolley, boats in the bay are heard almost constantly, and I could hear the TV next door. Also, there is only one expensive restaurant on site and a very small convenience store, so plan on leaving the hotel for better dining options. The location is outstanding. Right on the bay, right across the street from the convention center, and the Gaslamp District is next door (lots of dining options, stores, etc). I 'd consider staying here again.

“Well above the average for the Candlewood brand, and the best value near the medical center complex.” Situated between the medical center and some socioeconimcally depressed urbanity to the west, this property is appreciated for its spacious, recently updated rooms, and its proximity to the medical center and fast-food choices including Panda Express, where a RoadWearier can get an inexpensive and relatively healthy meal including ample fresh vegetables. Hotel also offers free, scheduled shuttle service to hospitals. Would definitely stay here again.

“Great Hotel - highly recommended” Stayed for 2 nights having secured a great Kimpton Intouch opening offer of $89 per night. Reserved a 2 bed room as traveling with grown up daughter but on check in was told 2 beds not available - bummer. But to make good we were upgraded to a suite on the 16th floor with a huge lounge and separate bedroom. Bathroom also huge with walk in shower and jacuzzi bath. Kimpton Intouch gift of $10 off minibar item very welcome - hic. Rooftop outside area and indoor pool a big bonus for this hotel and one which would attract me back. Food is available there but at room service rates which is expensive. Wine reception was busy but again something I love about Kimptons. We didn't eat in the restaurant but did have a drink at the bar which was buzzing. Hotel is in a brilliant location - walked to beach in one direction and Willis Tower in the other. Loads of bars and restaurants close by - really liked the Purple Pig for lunch. Finally - the staff - very welcoming and helpful. Can't fault the Palomar - hope to return sometime soon.

“Good location decent rates” Easy location, remodled lobby, and good rate. Rooms were quite and comfortable and offered a nice view. Furtinure in rooms could be updated. Workout space needs to be updated as well and they could not find (they did find after an hour or so) a Fed Ex that I had sent to the hotel which makes me a little suspect.

“Once bitten” Before you decide which hotel to stay at in Venice, think twice about whether you want to stay in Venice at all. If you don't have at least five body piercings, four tattoos and a crystal meth habit you will feel out of place here. It's a very grubby resort. The suites here are quite well appointed and the first impression of the rooms is that they are much nicer than the common parts of the hotel would suggest. However, there are a number of drawbacks that become evident! 1. The standard of the housekeeping is very poor. Don't be surprised if a few of your predecessors hairs remain in the basin and shower to greet you on your arrival. I recommend re-washing up any cup or utensile before you use it. 2. The bedding is old and grubby, don't look under the sheets at the matress if you want to sleep soundly. I was bitten by bedbugs on my first night and retreived two large blood swollen creatures from the bed the next morning. Manangement were very apologetic and offered to refund my remaining stay. It was President's Day weekend and I was very jet-lagged so I took up their offer to clean de-louse the room and I stayed. I was bitten again on my third and last night so the proceedure was clearly ineffective. 3. The walls are paper thin and the amourous activities of your neighbours across the corridor are clearly audible as are the fights down below between the homeless drug addicts who live on the streets of Venice. Although the hotel has a no smoking policy don't be surprised if the coridoors are perfumed with smell of residents enjoying the prescriptions of the many 'Medical Marajuana Doctors' who have set up shop along the broadwalk. I don't know if there is better to be had in Venice, but I would recommend moving up to Marina del Rey and finding something slightly cleaner and more conventional unless you have a strong need to be here, especially as this hotel is not that cheap given the drawbacks listed above.

“Courtyard Gets an Upgrade: Updated Rooms and Lobby In Progress” The Courtyard Austin Northwest is minutes from the Arboretum. Courtyard enthusiasts will be pleased that this hotel has the latest generation rooms with the red and gold background colors. The next step is a lobby upgrade and was in progress during my visit. The construction generated noise, and the crew occupied a corner of the parking lot. The hotel made up for this inconvenience with several commendable gestures. First, I received a welcome bag with water, fruit, and cookies. Second, a complimentary breakfast was served in the meeting room. Finally, I was upgraded to an executive suite, and the extra space was welcome. In summary, the hotel anticipated the construction issues and added several amenities. This hotel will soon represent the latest in Courtyard design. I will definitely return on my next visit to Austin and look forward to the new lobby. Pros: Minutes from Arboretum, updated rooms, commendable hospitality Cons: Lobby construction (nearly complete)

“Very nice hotel in a great location” I've had the opportunity to stay at the Talbott Hotel twice in the past 2 weeks and would recommend it as a well priced option in the Magnificent Mile area. The Talbott is located on a reasonably, quiet block, two blocks west of Michigan Avenue and the hordes of shoppers at the Water Tower Mall. It's a relatively small hotel, at least compared to nearby options like the Sofitel and Four Seasons. Check-in was easy and pleasant both times. I have seen both the standard and the parlor rooms. We like to watch TV in bed, so the smaller standard room was the better choice for us. We paid $145, including a $30 breakfast voucher for one of the best equipped rooms I've encountered. First of all, there's an overhead light, an almost unheard of convenience, as well as plenty of desk/table/floor lamps. The desk lamp has an outlet to plug in a portable power strip that is my must-have travel accessory. There's a refrigerator with minibar stuff in it but it's okay to put your own things in as well (there's a lovely little supermarket around the corner where you can buy pretty much anything you might need). There's a safe and an armchair (unusual for a small room). The flat screen TV is large and Mac Mini computer-based, so the guide lists channels in alphabetical order and you can use it as a dvr as well. The lineup includes several HBO channels. There is also a wireless keyboard that allows you to use the Mac and TV as a computer with high speed Internet. This is a terrific feature. If you prefer a laptop, wifi is free and works fine. The only downside is that the tiny remote control forces you to do everything through a menu-based interface, which can be inconvenient. I couldn't find a mute button either. The bathroom is fine and has huge bath towels. The two queen bed room has 2 sinks. There's a Keurig coffee maker with those convenient little K-cups that makes very decent coffee. The climate control is responsive and kept us cool on a record breaking hot day. I did not try the nearby health club. The restaurant is kind of odd. We only had breakfast there, and if you do so I'd highly recommend avoiding the continental breakfast, which includes a "bakery basket" consisting of a piece of white toast, and a mini muffin and Danish like you get packaged at the supermarket, plus a tiny ramekin filled with maybe a third of a serving of cereal. There's a Starbucks across the street, one of a half dozen within 4 blocks. The location is fantastic, convenient to almost anything. Valet parking is available for what the hotel refers to as the "nominal" charge of $51 a day. This is similar to the other hotels but at more than 1/3 of the room rate I'd say the word nominal should not appear anywhere on their web site. Overall, I'd rate the Talbott a very good hotel and a terrific value for the neighborhood.

“Best of the Best,” I have been an SPG Platinum member for awhile now. We are traveling across country by car and staying wherever we decide to spend the night. We have had no advance reservations. After leaving New Orleans, we decided to stop in Houston went on the Internet and used a few points and some cash. made a reservation at the St Regis. From the moment we arrived until the moment we left it was FIRST CLASS all the way. the hotel staff greeted us showed us to our room and would have waited on us hand and foot if we were so inclined, ( Which we are not ) The room was large, clean, and the bed and linens were crisp and clean and comfortable. The location safe and quiet. So nice we almost decided to stay an extra night. Well worth choosing.

“Wonderful Hotel in Downtown Indianapolis” I booked this hotel through Priceline and got a 99.00 rate. This is a very lovely hotel, with upscale touches and atmosphere. Smack in the middle of downtown near the state capitol, it was a busy weekend when I stayed there, as a major convention was in town. I had trouble finding the entrance (by car) and with all the commotion, it was noisy outside. Inside, though, it was quiet and pleasant. The Westin is noted for their comfortable beds, and the Indianapolis location is no exception. I rested very well my two nights here. This hotel is convenient to the downtown restaurants and shops, and is across the street from the RCA Dome. One thing I wish it had was someplace other than a Starbucks concession to grab a quick snack. $3.00 for a drip coffee is a bit much but oh well...This hotel is also convenient to major interstates and attractions. All in all, a great value.

“Great location, very very poor service. Avoid this hotel!” I have just returned home from one night at the W Union Square. My room was clean and the check-in agent was polite. When I arrived in my room I did not find the free bottle of water which should be provided to Platinum members. When I called the "Whatever" desk I was told that Platinum guests do not receive a free bottle of water. After I insisted the agent put me on hold and checked. she advised me (without an apology) that a bottle would be sent up. I then went to get a bucket of ice. The ice machine was not working. I notified a member of the housekeeping staff. She advised me that she would take care of it and have a bucket of ice brought to my room. After one hour I had still not received the ice. When the bottle of water finally arrived I informed the staff member who brought the water that I was still waiting for the ice. He took my bucket and went to collect ice from another floor. The tv was not properly functioning. HBO and Fox were not available. When I called the "Whatever" line I was advised that they have been having a technical problem for weeks. The following morning I called the "Whatever" line to ask the opening hours of a particular store which I wanted to visit. I was told "I think it opens at 10:00." When I asked if they couldn't call the store to confirm this they told me that they would have to call me back. I was called back and told that the store opened at 11.00. After breakfast I took a taxi to this store only to find that it was closed for Rosh Hashanah. I called directory assistance, found the store number and called the store. The phone message made it very clear that the store was closed all weekend. I checked their website when I arrived at my office later and found that it also clearly states this information. When I checked out from the hotel there was one agent at the check-out desk and a line of 8 people (five rooms) waiting to check out. I asked a passing staff member if someone from the back office could be called to help. He requested help on the radio without receiving any response. No help ever came. I waited 20 minutes, and I was the third person in line.

“Great Location, New Hotel, Restful Stay” My wife and I had a very relaxing stay for three nights at the Downtown Spring Hill Suites in San Antonio during our first time visit to San Antonio. The rate was very reasonable. Although there is a $21 a day valet parking charge, which is fairly typical for a downtown hotel. This is newer hotel that has been open only a little more than one year. It looks and smells new. It has a very modern and appealing décor, and spacious rooms. We liked the study desk, the sectional sofa, and the reading lights on each sides of the bed. The king bed was very comfortable. The room we had was very quiet and clean. The hotel is in an excellent location, with about a two-block walk to the River Walk and Alamo. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The free breakfast buffet of both hot and cold items was very good. The pool, which we did not use, is small and shared with the nearby Fairfield Inn.

“Great Hotel” We stayed at this hotel this past weekend. We arrived Saturday around noon and our room was not ready. We did not expect it to be ready so we stored our luggage and explore the city. When we came back around 3 we received our room keys and made our way up the 25th floor. We had 2 double bed rooms; it was very clean, modern and big for New York standards. We enjoyed the free Kerug coffee machine with free coffee. I wish that the drinks and snacks they put in the mini bar were more reasonably priced, if they were we actually would have bought snacks and drinks out of it but I’m sorry seven dollars for M and M's are way overpriced. The staff was friendly but I thought they were going to be a little bit more welcoming. For example when we returned to the hotel they never said "How Are You" nor "Do you need help finding anything". However the apple cider and the apple computers in the lobby were great.The location is great, a quick 10 minute walk and your in Time Square. Last year we stayed at the Stay Bridge next door and thought that hotel was better, they had free breakfast, kitchenette in the room and the staff was a little bit friendlier. Overall for the price we paid (480 total for Saturday and Sunday nigh with taxes) we thought it was great hotel and would return again if the price is right!

“Small rooms, strange layout” I spent the night (Sept 1, Labor Day) at the Hotel Monaco in Denver. Arrival and check-in were very nice. The pleasant Front Desk agent was friendly, recognized me as a Kimpton in Touch guest, and upgraded me to a King room on the 7th floor. I was stunned when I opened the door to my room to see how small it was. I have added pictures to this review to illustrate. In two of the pictures, I am standing with my back to the door. Because of the small room size, the furniture within is very cramped - note that the living room chair is wedged underneath the desk. I had to pull the desk several feet to the right in order to extract the chair and use it. In a room this small, they probably should have just skipped this chair altogether. Because it was Labor Day, the hotel's restaurant was closed. That turned out to be a good thing, because it forced me to make the 2 block walk to the 16th St. outdoor mall area. There was a lot of activity there and plenty of restaurants to choose from. The exercise room in the Monaco is OK. A treadmill, a pair of elliptical machines, and a stationary bike. Two racks of hand weights are wedged between the treadmill and the door. The room does, however, afford a nice view of the street outside. All in all, the Hotel Monaco is a nice enough place and conveniently located - though I suspect that the rooms in the Residence Inn next door are much, much larger.

“Excellent Location” We got an excellent promotion deal otherwise we probably would have stayed at another hotel where we have status. I think if we had paid the regular rates, we would have been disappointed. The location is excellent. Right in the middle of Times Square. We travel to NYC annually and have never stayed right in the middle of the action before. We took the subway from JFK to Times Square and a short walk to the hotel. No need to spend money on a cab and get stuck in traffic. Upon arrival there was a mix up with our reservation. Took a little while to sort it out, but in they let us check in at 2pm instead of 4pm and made us feel like they were doing us a big favor. They did give us an upgraded room on an upper floor. Our windows had a perfect view of the NYE ball that drops every year. The higher floors had nice views, but the trade off would be the wait for the elevators. The room itself is decent, but not completely 4 star worthy. The bathroom counter was extremely narrow and could use some updating. I can understand this is prime real estate and the bathrooms need to be minimal, but we've stayed at other hotels in the area in the same class and have seen better. The bed was comfy, but the pillows were terribly low. The most recent thing I've been looking for in hotel rooms are outlets to charge my gadgets. None beside the bed for my phone/alarm. That meant plugging in by the desk and not having easy access to my phone. Not the end of the world, but a little annoying. Also lack of outlets caused issues with 2 of us trying to charge our cameras, phones, laptops, etc. Took some juggling to make it happen. We did check out the gym and were impressed with the equipment, but for the number of guest rooms, the size of the gym is tiny. This means you may be waiting for cardio equipment if there are more than 4-5 people in there.

“TERRIBILE!” Dovrebbe essere, nel concetto americano, un hotel antico, invece era solo VECCHIO, reception minuscola, due ascensori lentissimi con uno dei due fuori servizio e questo in un hotel di 20 piani è un problema. stanze in cui mancavano solamente i fori delle pallottole della notte di San Valentino, o in cui ti aspettavi di trovare il cadavere di John Gotti nell'armadio. una pelliccia degli anni 40 gettata sul letto a mo di copriletto. per chi cerca il fascino della vecchia Chicago può andare bene, per chi cerca confort meglio stare alla larga. in tutto ciò, non te lo aspetteresti, internet wireless nelle camere, ma a pagamento!

“Great place, location and service” Great service and setting right opposite Fenway park on coom. Avenue. The rooms are large and comfortable. Definately will be back. The famous Oyster island restaurant is right next door so it was very convenient for a late dinner. Next time in Boston will definately visit again.

“Second stay, staff much friendlier, still room to improve” The location is great, next to Penn and Drexel. Train station right out the door. Upgraded to club floor ($20 with elite status), both breakfast and pre dinner snacks a bit sparse for a club lounge. Housekeeping needs some improvement, left dirty dishes, did not make up the rollaway. Room service pretty much limited to oriental. Speaking of rollaways, still at $30, too much in my opinion for a pricey hotel. On the good side, clean, comfortable room and lobby. The hotel just lacks a "personality", hard to explain, but hopefully makes sense.

“Solid 3 star but not a 4 star property” Just back from a stay at the Affinia 50. Overall was satisfied. On the plus side, the rooms (at least ours) are relatively spacious. Bed is comfy. Good isolation from noise, which I was not sure would be the case because we were down on the 3rd floor and close to the elevator (though not right adjacent to it). On the flip side, the room was showing some minor signs of wear. In two places the molding of the headboard was noticeably peeling away from the frame. The lone dresser was cheaply made, something you might put in a kid's room, not suspension drawers, and one of them was stuck partially opened, enough so that we just didn't use it. The bottom of the inside of the bathroom door was very badly scratched. One bulb in the bathroom light fixture burned out and remained out during our stay (3 nights). And when in the bathroom, the sound of music clearly echoed into it from some other room, could not tell if was from below (the lounge is on the 2nd floor so probably) or above. But while audible in the bathroom it was not loud enough to disturb us in the main room. I stay in Midtown East a lot, and this location is close to the Divine Wine Bar (flights of wine and tapas-like food) which I heartily recommend, Amma (great Indian food) and Dos Caminos (Mexican) which is also good. My complaints/observations are relatively minor, but they are the type of things separating 3 star and 4 star hotels. There are other hotels in the area (which I won't name, as TripAdvisor has rejected a restaurant review of mine in which I named other restaurants), some of which are a clear step up in quality and can be had for similar prices or even less when they run specials. All in all, if you book at Affinia 50 it seems a pretty safe bet you won't be disappointed, but you won't be wowed either.

“Location was great, but the hotel was just "okay"!” I chose this hotel, because I had enough HHonors points for a free night. We usually stay at one of the Embassy Suites in downtown Chicago, but didn't have enough points for a free night there. Getting off the elevator from the parking garage, you are greeted by a pink lobby. My husband gave me the look that said he was doubting my decision. At check-in, they asked us if we wanted to stay in one room one night and then a different room the next night, since one of them was free for using my HHonors points. We said that we'd rather not have to change rooms and he said, "okay"! He gave us our cookies and our keys and sent us on our way. We were given a room on the 3rd floor, that look out at a wall. No view! My guess, is this is what is given to people who stay at enough Hilton Hotels to earn a free room. We weren't going to be in the room very much and it was a free night's stay, worth approx. $206, so we just went with it. The room was mostly clean, except for hair on the bathroom floor and on the first night, a panel fell off the cabinet on bathroom vanity. We tried to put it back on, but it wouldn't go, so we left it for the cleaning person to deal with. They didn't deal with it, so we had a cabinet door on the floor in the bathroom for our stay. The location of this hotel is great. There is a Dominick's grocery store just a block away and Emilio's Tapas restaurant is just down Ohio about a half a block. It's a wonderful place to eat! Only 2 blocks from Michigan Ave, where all the shopping is. We got a bill after the first night, that said we had been charged $206 for our night's stay. Fine. The following morning, I received a bill stating that they were going to charge us $20 for the guest room. We also had a charge for a video game, but my daughter did play a game, so that was fine. I talked to the person at the desk and I got no explanation for it, but she took it off my bill. So check you bill very closely!!!! This wasn't a bad place to stay, but there were just many things about it, that just made it not a great place to stay either. We had just come from staying at a very nice Embassy Suites in another city and this seemed like a very big step down. In large cities, I usually pick 4 star hotels, because we think they would be considered 3 star anywhere else. This hotel was definitely a 2 1/2 - 3 star. The cost of parking for the weekend, was around $80, I believe. I guess I learned, getting a free room, is never free. My husband said he'd rather pay more and stay at an Embassy Suites with breakfast included and the manager's special in the evening. Also, pink with lime green made it look like a cheesy hotel from the 60's or 70's. If they just renovated, they should of changed that. Free internet connection in the lobby only, so the lobby was always crowded.

“Location location location!” I have stayed at this hotel countless times!The major attraction is the convenient location.The hotel is mere steps away from Times Square,opposite Bryant Park and sandwiched between 2 major subway lines.All the rooms newly refurbished,the staff are helpful and since it's a small hotel it doesn't take a long time to get to your room.The lobby is bit dated though and the restaurant doesn't open for dinner,but there are plenty of dining options nearby.

“Best Bed of all Philadelphia Hotels!” I have to say, when I first opened the door I was a little disappointed with the size of the room. Typical RI with a kitchen, living room, etc.. however the best part was when I laid down in bed. It was the most comfortable bed and bedding that I have experienced in quite awhile, even better than a WESTIN!

“Out of the way, but worth the savings” i have stayed at the gem hotel in chelsea a few times and since my meeting this time was close to penn station i decided to try the gem in midtown. the rates were around 20% less than chelsea. the location, on west 36th was convenient for my meeting, but certainly does not have the charm that the chelsea location has. however, that being said, the staff was courteous and knowledgeable, the rooms were "gem" clean and it was a very pleasant stay.

“Nun ja” Für den Preis 250$ erwartet man als Hilton Goldmember etwas besseres. Das Personal beim Check in war sehr freundlich, ohne Zweifel . Auch die Herren für die Koffer sehr sehr nett, aber früh morgn um 08:00 Uhr geht es los. Housekeeping macht ich sehr lautstark bemerkbar, ob bei einem selbst, oder den Nachbar. Das Coninentel breakfast war ok, hatte ein Voucher( da Goldmember), für dn Unterschied von 5 $ gibt es dann ein Full Buffett. Auch hier war der Service des Personals sehr gut. Allerdings war die Zimmergröße wirklich ungenügend um nicht zu sagen Mangelhaft. Kleine Zimmer, der Weg dahin völlig verwinkelt und de Ausstattung ... Na ja, wem es gefällt.

“Very nice NYC hotel” After staying at >20 hotels in NYC over the years - The Hilton Millenium rates very high. Great location for Chinatown - Lil Italy - Battery Park - Chelsea - Soho - lower Manhattan. We had a standard room - very nice- ave sized. You typically cannot go wrong with Hilton - always nice and comfortable. The location basically overlooks the construction at Ground Zero. One might complain about the construction noise - very little for us. Did not have time for fitness / pool / or restaurant. Pool looked nice on their photo page. The staff was very nice and cabs were easy to come by. There is a train station across the street (Ground Zero - path). Cab - $15 to Midtown.

“was ok for a couple nights...but small” My wife and me stayed here for two nights. We just crossed the whole country in four weeks and stayed in NYC for another week. We arrived early, so we needed a hotel for two extra nights and found the Newton. The price was ok, of course it's NYC, so expect higher rates than anywhere else. The Lobby looked very nice and we checked in quite early, around 10am. That was great, so we could enjoy the whole day after that. The room we got was small. Of course, NYC has small rooms, because everybody goes out anyway, nobody stays in the room, except for sleeping. But this room was really small!! Nothing to complain about cleaningness. Very clean room and bathroom, which looked renovated, like the room. It also came with fridge, microwave and flatscreen-TV. Very nice. Bed was alright. The Hotel is on Broadway, but quite North, but very close to a subway. But at night it's getting very quiet, a little too quiet for us. It didn't look dangerous, but somehow we like it when there's more people on the streets. Some front desk clerks have been a little weird. Nothing serious, but they could have been better. Althogether a good hotel. Three stars because of location and because of rooms sized below average. Wanna know more about my trip? route66traveler.jimdo.com

“Super!” We booked our two-night stay through the San Francisco hotel reservation service that the Donatello staff referred us to. We got a rate of around $110 a night, which was so much lower than other nearby hotels that I was a bit concerned about what we'd find. No need to worry -- the hotel was great! (I've certainly paid a lot more for worse rooms.) Staff were very friendly and helpful, and the room/bathroom were spacious and clean. The room also had a mini-kitchen area with sink, mini-fridge and coffee pot. The bed was comfy and there was ample room to stretch out. The club room (where the complimentary continental breakfast was served) was nice, and the spa, jacuzzi and gym were amenities not offered by most of the other hotels I considered. The location was great for playing tourist -- a block away from Union Square and the cable-car line -- but be aware that it's in the middle of a bustling city and there's going to be street noise, particularly from a local nightclub. You may want to ask for a room away from that part of the hotel.

“Great Location, friendly staff, clean rooms.” Location cannot be beat. Staff was very nice at check-in and parking valet's were most helpful with walking directions and suggestions. Older hotel, but completely updated, modern and clean. Rooms were very large, clean and comfortable. Bathroom was very small, but nicely renovated, very clean and nicely appointed. I would have to agree with other reviewers that rooms were a bit loud from neighboring room's noise, neighborhood traffic and hallway noise...I sleep with earplugs so it didn't bother me to any great degree. Parking is VERY expensive, I am so glad I booked room with parking included! Site lists parking fee, however they don't include additional tax on parking, so expect to pay +$50/night! In a nut shell, its a great location, nice staff and beautiful reno.

“Perfect Little Stay!” Stayed here one night on a drive North. Excellent new hotel with clean rooms. Front desk staff called to check all was ok after I checked in. Hotel is right off I-95 and very close to the airport. The hotel airport shuttle picked our friend up who flew in really late. Our room was extremely clean and the beds were super comfortable. Breakfast was the usual hotel continental fare but tasty and did the trick before we got on the road. There is a Longhorn Steakhouse, Zaxby's and other restaurants in the immediate area. On the other side of I-95 is a huge shopping plaza with a Walmart, fast food restaurants, Starbucks, and plenty of sit down restaurants. Less than a 5 minute drive. All in all a perfect one night stay.

“Good Overall Stay” As a platinum member, we had a high floor with a "corner" room with decent views of the city. All in all it was a very good stay that we've come to expect from full service Marriotts.

“Fun, funky, probably overpriced” When I visited, the hotel had been open just over a year, but was still experiencing some teething problems. There was no working A/C in our room, which was hot and stifling most of the time, and the staff advice was to 'crack a window' ... in March. Hot water usually took over 5 minutes to come through, morning or evening. Sound carries in this hotel - people talking and laughing in the corridor at stupid o'clock (and there were a number of them) disturbed us a few times, and while using one of the public computers in a corridor, I could hear every word of a conversation that was taking place in the adjacent room. On the plus side, it has fun, hip decor - many of the rooms have guitars in them (the theme throughout is rock'n'roll), and the minibar/fridge was housed in a black and silver gear case. The dark windowless lobby is full of trendy people hiding out with their laptops and lattes. Our room was very spacious by city standards, though my friend had a single room which was far smaller. The bed was the most comfortable I've ever encountered in a hotel. The staff were courteous and helpful. The location was great - a short walk from Macy's, and close to 2 subway stations. There were some great delis and cafes nearby which we used instead of the hotel's restaurant and coffee shop. I was lucky enough to get a special rate for my stay, which was good as I certainly don't think it was worth the full price!

“Great Place"” Took my hubby there for his birthday, nice chic modern hotel. The room was medium size and it had a great gym in the basement. The folks were very professional but not as friendly as I would have liked. The concierge didn't have a lot of suggestions so we found a lot of stuff on our own. There is a Trader Joe right across the street to get supplies which worked out amazing. The bar area was nice, some vibe but not a lot. Gret location, close to a lot of places to eat and things to do. You can walk anywhere in Chicago, it's easy to get around. Hotel was safe walking back late at night and I loved the quiet of the room. Good choice for couples, friend getaway but think not a family place.

“Close to Georgetown” Stay at all the Hilton properties in DC area for business and this one is in quiet nice neighborhood within 2 blocks of Foggy Bottom Metro and a nice walk into Georgetown (about 1/2 mile to edge). Rooms are huge but feel old and a bit worn but do have kitchens for guests looking for that sort of thing. Great for walk to Kennedy Center but not where you'd stay if you wanted lots of dining options in the immediate area. Will stay again when weather improves and the walks to restaurants won't bother me as much. Staff was friendly.

“Check your calendar before you book” The hotel itself was fine. Given it is NYC, this is considered a spacious hotel. However, I said to check your calendar before you book is because there are alot of international dignitaries that book that hotel because of the brand, history, and status. When I was there, the Iranian President decided to stay there for the UN summit, which means there are extra securities from privately contracted security, NYPD, Secret Service, extra Secret Service, the Iranian police, their security, and not to mention protestors. That aside, the hotel room is nice, the bathroom was small, my room's window faces an airshaft. The shower water pressure was slow when you switch from tub to shower head. That was ok, what's not ok was that the hot water comes and go. I did mention it to the front desk but also understands because of the VIP in house that I was not the priority. I did eat at the bar, and the service was great, food was not bad, just skip the fried brussles sprout, because that was soggy. Otherwise, drink was well done.

“Good Location/No Big Complaints” I stayed at this Westin from 10/28 - 11/1 after having a horrible and God-awful experience at the Hyatt across the street (see related post). I showed up at the Westin's front desk with no reservations, seeking a three nights' stay. John, a front desk manager in the evenings, was most helpful. He was able to provide accommodations for two nights but told me that he could not promise anything beyond that. He asked me to keep checking back. I did, and he was able to accommodate me for a third night. Thank you, John. The hotel has a spacious lobby. There are six elevators, so there is not usually a long wait for one. My room (1337) was clean, and the bed was very comfortable. There were plenty of clean towels. Many reviewers have noted the small bathrooms. This is true. They are small, but I managed. It was not a problem for me. The tub drained a bit slow, so as you shower, you might be standing in a few inches of water. Internet service is reliable but not free (10.00 a day). There are snacks and bottled water provided on those motion sensitive machines, so if you touch the snacks or the water, even if you don't eat or drink, you will probably be charged for it. It is better to take the Indy Go Green Line Shuttle from the airport for $7.00 one way as opposed to a $20.00 or more cab ride. The shuttle boards at the Zone 6 ground transportation area and stops near most major hotels in the downtown area. The Westin is centrally located. Lucas Oil Stadium, the Indiana Convention Center, and the Circle Centre Mall are all accessible by the sky bridge from the hotel, so you do not have to walk on the city streets if you don't want to. Walking the streets is not bad, however. I never felt unsafe, but it is still good to use common sense to avoid poorly lighted areas, and do not jaywalk. There seems to be a beggar/panhandler on almost every corner, but none seemed aggressive in any way. If you do not wish to be bothered, simply ignore them, and keep walking. My stay was a nice one. Either I am too easy to please, or some travelers are very critical. Probably the slow tub drain and the $10.00 a day Internet charges caused the most concern for me, but I do not think that it would stop me from staying at this Westin again. One final note of caution: Stay away from the Hyatt Regency next door!!

“Fantastic Renovation! Amazing Staff!” The renovation is complete and is excellent. Hilton Honors members will love the new Lounge. I stay here frequently and this is THE place to stay in Houston. The staff is simply amazing! Location is excellent and the new decor is wonderful.

“Convienent for business & meets all standards” Three night stay, junior suite. Located adjacent to the interstate, a short drive from Bush Airport. Staff was well trained in all functional areas; service was customer focused, attentive and extremely professional. Free parking. Room well appointed and clean. Common areas immaculate. Meals above average in presentation, ingredients and taste. Robust menu. Price point reasonable Room service superb. Ambiance of bar and lobby conducive to business. Bottom line: a superb business location.

“Westin is in general upscale, and we feel that this is the best of Westin” Westin Oaks is located in Houston Galleria together its sister, - Westin Galleria. These are not only decent hotels, but exhibits excellence. Everything is clean, and there is a "trained hotel staff", not just someone “employed for his or her keep". Parking is free, but so is it for everyone else. Valet parking has designated areas, not so for a hotel guests, which is the only aspect that annoyed me. When the hotel offers "complimentary parking", - it should be for you as a guest! Wireless is not free, a nuisance in such a pricy hotel. There are several Starbucks in the Galleria with free Wi-Fi, and SIMON Wi-Fi that is excellent. The safe wasn't working, but that was quickly fixed. Breakfast is not included, which “in short” means that you may choose food with less sugar that is usually the menu in US hotels. From this perspective, it is no surprise that obesity is a serious handicap in US welfare. If you are on business, - your spouse may appreciate the diversity in "in-house shopping". People from all over the Houston area come to the Galleria to shop, upscale. The Galleria is more than 30 years old as a shopping center and still holds its position as a major attraction. It is our third stay over more than 10 years, and this is our favorite hotel. It is, as a Brit would put it; "top notch!"

“Great Location” Stayed over New Year's Eve with other friends. VERY convenient location. Just blocks from the water. Would be a great spot for tourists to stay. Clean rooms, but a little on the small size. Bathrooms are bit small as well. It's one of those where the vanity is in the little closet sized space between the entry door and the shower/toilet bathroom. It's a little on the tight side. I would've expected a little more for a Sheraton - but they can be hit-or-miss sometimes. Lobby is nice. Staff is friendly. Convenient to not only all the SF tourist areas in the Wharf, but there is also a Safeway conveniently located across the street, which is always nice for extended stays. Not a big fan of Valet only parking, and the parking prices are pretty steep, even as a guest - but I guess it's like that everywhere in San Francsico anyway.

“Almost perfect....” My wife and I stayed at the Harborside in mid-August for 2 nights. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. We were able to park our car when we arrived at 11AM, even though our room wasn't ready until later in the afternoon. The parking is in the structure right next to the aquarium, about 2-3 blocks from the hotel, and the structure is well lit and in a busy place. We had no fears about leaving the car for the time we were there. The hotel is, literally, steps from Quincy Market... go across the street and down a short block and you are there. The North End is a short 10 minute walk away, and most of the Boston sights are within a 10-15 minute walk. Additionally, there is a T stop right outside the hotel where you can get on the subway to go anywhere in the Boston Metro area. In short, The location of this hotel is hard to beat... it is in a PERFECT place for a visit to Boston. We reserved an interior room based on some of the other reviews on this site. The interior rooms have a window that looks out on an atrium and the elevator lobby on each floor. The room was very clean and quiet, our one complaint is that it was not lit well enough. We tried to keep the blinds on the window open, but due to being so close to the elevator, if we had them open other people could see into our room. My wife called down to the desk to ask for an exterior room, but they didn't have any so we stayed the two nights in the interior room. When she called she asked the staff member at the desk about noise in an outside room and they said really one only should worry about noise if they are there on the weekend, during the week it generally is not very noisy outside the hotel at night. We would definitely stay at the Harborside again... probably we'll try an outside room next time. :-)

“Great Customer Service but noisy” I stayed here for 4 nights, and ended up in 3 different rooms as a result of being moved due to being able to hear every thing the persons in the next room were saying. There seemed to be a wedding going on and/or some other groups that made the hotel their party destination (strange, considering that its located in a corporate business park environment) so it was more due to my neighbors having five-ten people in their room at a time and socializing versus normal use. The Marriott staff was awesome and did everything they could to accommodate me. They had the fastest room service I've ever seen and the food was delicious. Aside from the check-in staff, the employees were top notch all the way. The beds were very comfortable and the room furnishings were up-to-date and clean. Internet worked flawlessly and was quite fast. The valet was terrible and didn't even leave his little podium to greet me or the gentlemen that pulled up behind me. After a while we both got out, unloaded our own luggage and traipsed over to the valet. He might have wanted us to park our own cars? The parking fee (self-park or valet) at this property is totally unjustified, they have more than enough land and its not as though its any where near downtown or the ocean. Another sad Marriott add-on just like charging for their internet service daily. Check-in was unreasonably slow considering there were 4 staff members and only 2 other people checking in. The first set of keys that I got didn't work and after lugging 500 lbs of luggage back down to get a set that did work, no one even offered to assist me going back up. I would definitely stay here again although next time I think I'll try the Marriott in LaJolla instead.

“Cher et nul , je déconseille ...” Impossible de dormir a cause des travaux , vue sur les grues . Chambre petite . Ne mérite pas 4 étoiles malgré le coté historique de la batisse . Personnel hautain , surtout le barbu au cheveux blancs il gagne le premier prix du snobisme !!!!

“Great service” The Concierge was amazing!! They were friendly, helpful and went out of their way to make our stay comfy. We had a 2 bedroom suite which was spacious for the 6 in our group. The pillow menu is to die for. I fell in love with the buckwheat pillow! Wonderful hotel and wonderful service. Highly recommended for families especially with younger children since there is a kitchen with a stove, oven and refrigerator/freezer.

“Good Hotel for Convention Center” I recently stayed at Hyatt Regency Denver at Colorado Convention Center while attending a conference. The hotel, which I believe was built very recently, is located just across the street from the convention center. This was very convenient. Also, the hotel was easy walking distance to 16th Street, with its free busses. The check-in was OK, but I noticed that there were only two people at the check-in counter despite the fact that this was a very busy day. There were maybe six or so self-check-in kiosks there, but I'm not sure that's a great idea for a relatively high end hotel such as this one. I really think the hotel is really having a hard time maintaining a sufficient number of full time employees on their roster, since convention business is really going down the drain this year. The whole place is very well maintained. I thought my room was well appointed. However, I noticed a few things I expect in a hotel of this price range were missing: This includes robes, slippers, etc. I think this is also secondary to bad economy. If I had to find one problem with this hotel, its the design of the doors. They seem to slam shut with a very loud noise. More quiet doors should be installed in an establishment such as this one. A few other odd things...I expected their restaurant, called "Altitude" to be located higher up, perhaps on the top floor with a panomamic view of the city and the mountains. However, the restaurant was located on the ground floor. it is a nice restaurant, but calling it "Altitude" is a bit odd for the location. The bar/lounge on the 27th floor called "Peaks" was nice, but also the design of that space was not done correctly, in my humble opinion. Instead of the windows facing the mountains, most of the seating was facing the highrise condos. I expect a lounge called "Peaks" to have a nice view of the Rockies. Anyways, this hotel is a pretty good option, especially for a convention attendee. I'm not sure how much this place usually costs (I stayed there on a government rate reservation), but if you can afford it, this is a great choice.

“Amazing, impeccable service in a beautiful hotel” We stayed here after the New York Marathon. The hotel appeared to be at 100% capacity, but you would never have known that from the service. Every single person we encountered treated us like royalty. Gloria at the front desk was especially helpful and gracious. The housekeeping staff was friendly and helped us find a great Mexican restaurant in the area. The breakfast staff was busy, but kind and deferential. I can't properly convey how overwhelmed we were with the staff's care. It felt much more like a 5-star hotel than a HIE. Breakfast was great and ample. We went during the thick of it. There are 48 chairs arranged around 16 tables in groups of 2, 3, or 4. I counted because it was a concern after reading some of the previous comments. It was the expanded HIE menu including biscuits and gravy, sausage, and pre-made omelets. These were quickly refilled as necessary. Coffee is available 24 hours. Priority Club members can have their breakfast delivered, if they like. The hotel is located a block from the #1 line, or 2.5 blocks from Madison Square Garden/Penn Station. It's a block the other way from the Fashion Institute of Technology. The neighborhood is okay and felt safe walking alone at night; there was a crazy on the street, but it's New York and there are crazies on most blocks. There is a parking lot next door, $28/day, I think. Taxis frequently come by, and can be arranged at the front desk. The business center consists of 3 computers in the lobby. They are at standing level with couches near them. I brought a chair over, which didn't seem to be a problem. There is a nice and fairly large fitness center in the basement, where the ice machine and vending machines are also located. The rooms are compact, as you'd expect in NYC. They were very plush, immaculate, and had upscale furnishings and bedding. Two doubles fit, and still allowed room for a desk, table, and tv area. There is no view to speak of, except for from the top floor (ask for it, if you're a PC member). The price was great; about half as much as most of the other hotels in NYC. I don't know why, and I'm certainly not complaining! Though we have family a short train ride away, we've decided that this hotel is so reasonable and wonderful that we'll always stay here instead.

“Stunning - Absolutely Stunning!” We have travelled around the States quite a bit and have stayed at some very good hotels but I have to say that the Grand del Mar is the best so far. It is not cheap but then again you expect to pay for quality and this hotel has that in abundance. The staff, without exception are polite, attentive and very professional and you feel that nothing is too much trouble. The room was exceptional, we were on the ground floor and had a siiting area outside by the Reflection Pool which was great as the sun was there all morning. We ate at the Amaya, the Lounge Bar and the Clubhouse Grill. The food was of a high quality and reasonably priced. We also took the courtesy limo to eat at a Chinese restaurant in Del Mar. The Concierge arranged everything and even sent us confirmation. I only have two negative comments. On the first night we ate in the Lounge Bar and placed our order with the waiter, after half an hour our food hadn't turned up and we raised it with the waitress. It turned out that the waiter had forgotten to place the order with the kitchen. This was quickly rectified and we weren't charged for the food. My second issue was that at check-out we were charged for some mini-bar items that we did not have, again this was quickly rectified. Overall this place was amazing and I would recommend it anybody.

“Don't judge the book by the cover” I stayed here because of a reccomendation backed up by positive Tripadvisor reviews. I usually stick to the big hotel chains but decided to try something new in Seattle because it is still cruise boat season. During cruise boat season, staying near downtown will cost closer to $200 a night. The hotel rooms are very clean and the room furniture is on the newer side. The room amenities are sparse but the hotel has no problem providing room extras. Albeit small, the bathroom was still clean. It was definitely better than a Super 8, Red Roof, or any of the discount chains. The hotel is located by cool Seattle restaurants and near the new hip area of West Seattle. Would I stay here again? Yes, I would if I was traveling for business. My family would want the full hotel experience (pool, more amenities, and etc) and probably would not enjoy it as much.
“It is Ritz. It has to be good.” Great Place. Rooms, Service, gym, Swimming Pool, Conference Rooms . Everything is good. Real Class. Also available, Spa and Bar.

“Great hotel in a great location” Stayed here 3 nights for a conference. The service was excellent and very friendly from the moment we checked in. The housekeeping service was done every day and left the room spotless. I bumped into a couple of housekeepers and they were extremely friendly as well. The decor of the hotel is very elegant but not stuffy and I liked it very much. I had a deluxe Queen room which was incredibly spacious. The bathroom was also quite roomy and had a glass shower as well as a full tub. I also enjoyed the large LCD TV. The bedding is very comfortable and the room had a view of O'Farrell street. Another plus is that it was literally 2 min. to get from the room to the conference center. The elevators were the quietest I have ever been in and were very fast. The hotel is also in a great location right in downtown San Francisco with plenty of great restaurants, bars, and shops within walking distance. I recommend checking out the Irish House Pub/Restaurant across the street. It has great food/drinks and a great ambiance. Not hotel related but the taxi situation in San Francisco is terrible. If possible, rent a car or use a service such as Uber. It might be more expensive but you'll save a lot of time and headache. Highly recommend this hotel and would love to return.

“Great Hotel , Great staff for the most part” We checked in the hotel for one night on March 10th. Arrived at Logan and shuttle was at the airport to pick us up 20 minutes after we called. We arrived at the hotel and there was one front desk agent. She never greeted us , never said anything really. I finally said we wanted to check in . She said name, never looking at me. Then she asked for my credit card, again never looking at me, never recognizing me as a silver elite, nothing. She gave me my credit card back , handed me my key , and never said a word. She didnt tell me the room number, she didnt say anything , I asked for the room number and she pointed at the key pack. We were hoping the whole experience would not be as cold and unfriendly as this one woman was. We got in the room. It was very nice, clean and spacious. Throughtout the rest of the stay , the other front desk staff and other staff members of the hotel were very friendly and attentive, which is why I will not let this one person spoil my review for the hotel. Thats why i ranked it excellent. Everyone else went above and beyond the call of duty to make sure we were satisfied. Thanks Courtyard South Boston.

“good downtown location” There for several days on business. The staff was excellant, the rooms were comfortable. They serve breakfast each morning and dinner Mon-Thursday. It is all free and nice when you are looking to save money. Although you will want to get out for dinner at one of the many good places nearby. It is near the bay and easy walk. You dont want to go to far off the beaten path though. The inner city of Baltimore is really, really, bad. I could not get over the terrible living conditions with abandoned buildings and people lotering. Again, though you will be fine in the area of the hotel. If you get a chance, DC is only 40 minutes away. You can drive up there for early dinner and walk the main parts and be back in no time. Beds were comfortable and all rooms are suites with kicthens, sofa, desk etc. (free wi-fi). There is a awesome gym that guests can use in the building. Parking is valet $32/night or self park $22/night. the self park though is per in/out. I highly recommend spending the extra $10 per night. It is a lot safer and much more convieint.

“Wow!” I usually stay at the Fairmont in San Jose. No more. The Montgomery is now my favorite hotel in San Jose. This reasonably priced, upscale hotel is in an elegant rehabbed 4 story building in the heart of downtown San Jose. The rooms are large and well furnished. My spacious bathroom had a tub and a stand alone shower. It was stocked with Aveda toiletries. There is a well stocked mini-bar. The bed and pillows were very comfortable. Highspeed Internet access is at no charge The Paragon restaurant has great food and our server was very helpful. The entire staff at the hotel was friendly. On the First Street side, you can hear the ringing of the streetcar bell right outside your window. Romantic or annoying, depending on your mood (and the time of day), I suppose. This is truly the best place to stay in San Jose.
“Wonderful City Hotel” Recently stayed at the sofitel for a wedding. Was upgraded to a suite which was spacious and beautiful.Could have lived there!

“Excellent location, great service” My mom and I stayed at the Fairfax for three nights. We got the room on Priceline for $150 and I think we had the same room as the other priceline reviewer below (king with pull out sofa). They got a better price than us though :) Anyway, we did not feel any less welcome due to our Priceline status! The pullout sofa was comfortable, and the bed was so comfy. Service was excellent, the door people are so friendly. We asked a couple of times for extra coffee and it was delivered immediately and with a smile. The bathroom was very spacious, tons of counter space, free standing hairdrying (vs the hose attached to the wall!), excellent water pressure and hot water through two showers. The location just could not be any better, Dupont Circle metro is right there, and it is right near tons of excellent restaurants, bars/clubs if you want nightlife, bookstores, shopping, (excellent consignment shop at Secondi!), Embassy Row. We didn't eat at the Jockey Cllub, but did have some drinks in the Farifax Lounge. For the Priceline price this was an outstanding value and we really enjoyed it.
“Good for a one night stay” Stayed here while visiting Carowinds for the day. Everything was clean and customer service was great. Location is out there, but no real complaints for a one night stay.

“I loved it” You usually don't stay in hotels in the city you live in, but I needed an extended stay hotel while renovations were being done to my house. I first stayed at the Marriot Town Place suites and moved after 4 days to this property. it was like day and night. This is a brand new hotel with some of the nicest, cleanest rooms I have ever stayed in. I was upgraded to a suite with a separate bedroom at no extra charge and it was beautiful and spacious.
