Beautiful new kitchen, dining table and chairs, living room with HD TV and a separate bedroom with another HD TV. The mattress and pillows are so comfortable that I want to buy them for my own home, which you can. There is little noise of any sort from the adjoining or upstairs rooms and the free breakfast and dinner are great, if a little on the bready, fried, potato-y side. I would have liked to have seen fresh salad dressings instead of those packets that are full of chemicals and calories, and maybe some dinner salads like chicken ceasar, but that's pretty minor. There is free wireless Internet which works great. The a/c is quiet. The machines in the business center are new and include a printer/scanner/fax and computers. The staff, however is an enigma. They seem pleasant enough, but there's never anyone at the front desk, they are always in the back room, and you always have to call for them, which I find strange. I wish they had an outdoor pool, but again, that is very minor. You do have to have a car, as the hotel is located outside of the city center, but if you're here on business for a while, you would have one anyway. To sum up, if I needed an extended stay hotel in Ft. Worth it would be this one hands down.

“great bargain” the rate was great- $33 a night with the aarp discount, cheaper than the motel 6 next door. the room was comparable to a motel 6 room but it had a better tub/shower. there was in-room coffee and 60 channels of cable tv. the breakfast was ok- cereal, toast, juices, rolls, coffee. it was quiet but you can hear some of the nearby interstate traffic- i used the fan to drown out the noise. the only negative was a filthy carpet- it needed to be shampooed.

“Would not stay there again” The hotel looked good from the outside. however, the parking was unsecured and right out in front of the hotel in downtown El Paso. I did not feel safe in the parking lot as there were people wandering around. The rooms had a lot to be desired. The hotel appeared to be older although from the outside it looks newer. I was not comfortable at all in the room and did not get a good night's sleep any of the four nights I was there. The breakfast was what was expected. A nice spread of hot and cold foods. The staff was more than friendly. But, overall the hotel felt like a 2-star.

“Great Hotel, Great Location” Stayed here in June for business. This is a nice hotel in a great location. The rooms are nicely decorated and good sized. The gym is great. There is a sports bar in the lobby and several restaurants/bars nearby on Newbury and the mall.

“Great value!” This is an excellent choice for an extended stay, but the hotel also makes sense for a shorter stay such as my recent five-night visit. This type of hotel is really a hybrid of apartment/hotel. There is a fully-equipped kitchen in each of the studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom suites. The kitchen will enable one to enjoy breakfast in the privacy of one's own room, without having to "scrub up" before entering the usual hotel breakfast room. Of course, it's always a delight to save the $20 hotel restaurant breakfast charge. There are other obvious benefits to having the kitchen amenity. There is limited housekeeping service, but the usual towel, soap, etc., replenishment is done on a daily basis, and I suspect that if I had any further requirements the friendly staff would have gladly supplied them. The location is excellent with many restaurants and stores very close by. It is a healthy one-mile walk to the center of Denver's bustling downtown heart. A final remark: it was a pleasure to be able to open the room window at night when summer temperatures are a delight in Denver. Decor is certainly not "posh", but certainly is most adequate. This can be your "home away from home" in Denver.

“The hotel is a little away from theMain street” The location is not far from the center but is not close aider. I did like that the HD TV is very big and have very nice channels. This hotel is right besides the embassy suites.

“Not like the other Kimptons” We got this hotel on Priceline and only after "winning" it were we made aware of the fact that this hotel only has rooms with 1 bed so if you are traveling with 2 people that are not related, you will have to share a bed. Never had that experience before and really you shouldn't offer yourself on PL unless you can sleep 2 guests. That said, on to the actual hotel. The rooms are tiny, it feels like you're in a closet. I don't think I've ever been in a room this small. It makes all the hotel rooms in Europe seem large! The location was ok and we were able to find free parking on the street since it was a Saturday night. I guess if you're traveling with your pet, this is the place to be. We love Kimptons because they are dog friendly, though we did not have ours with us when we traveled. Would I stay here again? Only if I was traveling with my husband, don't really want to share a bed with other people ever again!

“Would not stay here again” We'll preface this by saying we go into NYC about 3/times a year. We decided, based on the reviews here, to try this hotel. Although the staff is fine, our "double" room had 1 double bed, pushed against a wall. Thus my husband on that side had to crawl down to the foot to exit if I was still in bed, and whacked into the wall when he turned over during the night, disturbing us both. We had asked for a non-smoking room and specifically added that I am allergic to cigarette smoke. Still, we found cigarette burns on the night table and an ashtray in its drawer. The bathroom is so tiny, the shower door opens IN!!! We timed it on 3 occasions, at various times of day, and found it took a full 12 minutes of running the shower to get hot water, and then the water pressure would suddenly cut off for a minute or two mid-shower. When asked, the clerk at the front desk said it takes a long time for the hot water to reach the 7th floor from the basement boiler. Since the sink gets hot water much more quickly, I'm not sure if that's the problem. Noise from the street or other rooms was not a problem, since in the unseasonably hot weather we had to run the A/C, a window unit that was so noisy it was difficult to carry on a conversation or hear the TV, let alone anything outside the room. It is set for one speed, one temperature, and you can't change it, despite controls that would indicate you can. Finally, there is only one tiny elevator in the entire building, --not even a service elevator. This meant waiting for the elevator often took 10-15 minutes. Considering, with taxes, we paid over $210/night, we think we can do better.

“Great downtown location” Starting with the good things. I was pleased to be on the a top floor on the north tower. This is a great view of the water - can't be beat. Great downtown location !!!Also as always, the Westin has the best beds !!!. What this hotel does not have it great bathrooms - theirs are interchangeable with a blah Marriott - your basic bath/shower combo - nothing special. Also, the elevator noise is bad news. Avoid the hotel food.

“This Hotel Excellent” Everthing from the Front Desk Check In to the rooms is excellent. The hotel is in a very busy part of town near the WH on K Street, but it is so quite in the rooms, one would never know it. The rooms are spotless and well taken care of. As a Hilton Diamond member, I was very impressed.

“Beautiful hotel, excellent service” The Dallas Ritz Carlton had only been open a few weeks when we stayed, but you would never have known it except for the groups of hotel trainees going through training in the meeting rooms next to ours. Rooms were beautiful and spacious, dining options all excellent. Common areas such as the lobby, bar and area between the meeting rooms were beautifully furnished and the flowers were spectacular. This is a beautiful venue for a meeting, wedding...

“Great value and convenience” I like this hotel a lot for the price. It is a great value with rooms around $135 or so. It is very convenient, a half block from the 6 train and lots of restaurants around. The room is small and basic, but there is good free wifi and a really nice breakfast in the morning. This is the hotel I choose over and over when I have business at NYU dental school.

“Hipster Haven” If you want to live among the NYC hipsters, this is your place. The boutique hotel is unique and charming in its own way. Funky interior decor will make it seem like you're staying in your cool cousin's dorm room rather than a hotel. Ask to borrow a turntable and record albums when you check in for the full quirky experience. Pretty spendy, but worth it if this is what you're looking for.

“Great location, lots of room.” We travelled to chicago with our two teenaged boys. This hotel was great because of the space. We had a suite with a bedroom and living room. The space was nice and clean. The beds were comfortable although it would have been nice if they had been queen size rather than full/double. Of course in Chicago you have to pay for everything, including parking ($50/night) and wireless internet. Free wifi was available in the lobby, but you had to pay for it if you wanted it in your room. We got a decent price for our room ($135/night on Expedia). The hotel was within walking distance of the Navy Pier, river cruise and the red line (train/El). All in all I would say this was a good place to stay, especially if you're travelling with kids.

“You can't go wrong staying here” I've stayed at this hotel twice, and both times were wonderful. it has an ideal location right across from the PATH station. although it overlooks Ground Zero, there was no noise that I heard, day or night. the views are absoutely sensational and the rooms are also very well appointed. the first time we stayed was for Valentine's Day, and they upgraded us to a junior suite. it was so large it had a hallway, and the views were unreal! the front desk is also very helpful, and everything you could need is just steps away.... and if you dont feel like going out, then stay in and enjoy the bar area. And for what you get, the prices are a steal. I recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay in the downtown area. Also perfect for accessing the statue of liberty- which is just a few blocks away.

“Lots of LONG lines and below average customer service” I recently stayed at the Embassy Suites Lakefront in Chicago. The location is good, but overall, I wasn’t impressed, starting with check in. I had to go through 3 different rooms before I had one that was satisfactory. 4th time is a charm I guess. The first smelled bad, second was an accessible room and the third was stuffed in the corner and about 3⁄4 the size of the other rooms. Finally I ended up in a room with 2 beds (even though I wanted a king). The bed gave me a backache and sank in the middle. The lines...I just couldn’t believe it. I’ve never seen lines like this at any hotel (well okay...maybe Disney during prime season but nowhere else). The made to order line took 1 hour to get through (not exaggerating...there is a clock right next to the line). Unfortunately, I was dumb enough to stand in it, not realizing how slow it would be. Makes sense it’s so slow with only one person cooking. The drink line at the evening reception took about 15 to 20 minutes to get through and they are VERY strict about getting one drink at a time. Makes for a less than enjoyable time waiting so long for one drink. They are free, but I think I’d rather pay to avoid the long lines (not an option). They never did deliver the waters they promised. Also, the walls are VERY thin. The lady next door wouldn’t stop coughing and the kids on the other side were very loud too. The maid service was barely passable...she didn’t even put the cover back on the bed. It was on the floor when I got back. Breakfast trays next door were not picked up until 8pm that evening...they sat outside the neighbor’s room all day. Even though I’m a Diamond member, this clearly didn’t have any impact. When I called to talk to the manager the morning of checkout, the operator couldn’t even put me through because there was only 1 front desk person, a long line in the lobby and someone else on hold (that’s what she told me). This is probably a decent choice for families who are okay with an adequate hotel, but definitely wouldn't recommend for couples or business travelers. The Wit on State and Lake and Hilton Garden Inn at Grand are both way better choices. Great customer service at those hotels with nice rooms.
“Nice” Check in was easy, room was great, in room beverage arrived on time with USA today the next morning. Buffet breakfast was great too.

“Wish I could say it was worth it” My daughter and I stayed at the Sherry Netherland in Nov 2004. It was a mother/daughter shopping weekend and I wanted to treat her to some place nice. The Sherry Netherland was a big disappointment, especially for the price. The front desk people were not very nice. I do have to say that the elevator operators & bellman were very nice though. But we arrived a little early for our room, and we were told the room wasn't ready and to come back at 3, as that it when check in was. We came back at 3:30, only to hear that our room still was not ready. After waiting another 15 minutes, they told us we could go up, but that they were still cleaning, so we got to watch them vacuum & finish cleaning our room. Not what you would expect for a "luxury" hotel! For the money you spend, I would highly recommend looking into another hotel. There are plenty to choose from.

“excellent hotel” L' hotel est bien situé, les chambres sont décorés avec gout dans un style cosi mais rien ne parait vieillot, c est juste tres jolie et chaleureux. Le personnel est trés sympa, professionnel. Le petit bemol, un seul ascenseur en service, pour quatorze étage, à partager avec les femmes de chambre, c est VRAIMENT pas assez. Trés trés bon hotel.

“A Nice property in a colorful neighborhood” I was not looking forward to staying here, I usually like a little more high end properties and like to stay downtown. But the prices that week in the city were absurd and I basically had no choice. I was also a little worried about the reviews I had read. To start- the front desk staff was outstanding. Very curteous, friendly, super nice, I can't say enough. Check in was no problem and whenever I needed anything, they were helpful. Bell staff the same, super friendly and helpful. Great job. The room- it was on the small side, but totally fine and functional. I had no view, but honestly, I left for work early and was back late, never had a chance to care. The bed was fine, a little hard, pillows were good. Starbucks coffee in the room, flat screen TV, free internet access. The shower was great! Also, being off the street was good, no street noise and I slept very well. I didn't eat the free breakfast, just grabbed some coffee, so can't comment on that, but it looked like plenty of folks were taking advantage of it. Never made it up to the sky bar, wish I did. The area is a little sketchy, even for me. I used to live in the city and know it well. But there are peep show places, adult video stores on the block as you walk towards 8th ave as well as a parole office. The bus station brings all sorts in the area anyway. With that said, no problems, no one hassled and I didn't see anything worrisome. It's the real NY, gritty and kind of cool. Once you cross over 8th ave, it's Timesquare area. There are loads and loads of restaurants on 9th ave, so you'll never be short on that. The subway is up the block on 8th ave, very convenient. All in all it was much better than I expected. I would choose it again and be just fine with it. I'm just not a big fan of midtown. Thanks for a really nice stay!

“Good Business Hotel” Stayed here 2 nights on business. It is well located, the rooms are clean, and I like they have Kurig machines. The staff is friendly. They need new mattresses, The hotel is right on the inner harbor, so it's nice to go for a jog in the morning.

“Fairly new Fairfield/Courtyard - 20 mins from PHX airport” This is a fairly new (< 2 years) combo property- Fairfield and Courtyard, adjoined and built in an “L” shape. It’s on the outskirts of Chandler (off Route 101, 20 mins from airport)) and appears to cater to the nearby businesses as opposed to the leisure traveler. There is a hallway that joins the two hotels, either side can check you in. The CY has their new modern look (bistro, etc), the Fairfield is of the Inn and Suites variety. I stayed there3 nights and noticed that the Fairfield desk clerk is not there late at night & early morning, and a sign directs you to the CY desk. Free breakfast at Fairfield, you pay at the CY. Free USA Today but no Wall Street Journal. Fast internet, limited TV channels (40). There are no restaurants within walking distance but dozens within 10-15 minutes, lots of upscale shopping as well. Rooms (as well as both hotels in general) were in excellent shape, very clean and comfortable. Nice exercise room and decently sized pool. In back of the hotel is hundreds of acres of flat land, apparently ready for development some day. Not really much else around the hotel. If you’re a jogger, there is a dirt trail behind the property. I stay in the Phoenix area a lot and have found that these hotels are amongst the most inexpensive Marriott properties, when there is seasonal high hotel demand (like Jan-March). This is likely because they’ve built these properties in advance and in expectation of higher business demand, which is not at the moment. During the summer months, most of the Marriott properties drop their rates and its feasible to even get an upscale resort type property for under $100. I’m sure the 100+ degree heat has something to do with that!

“Nice hotel in a good location.” Overall, we had an enjoyable time at this hotel. While it is not the nicest place we've ever stayed, it is certainly not the worst. Front desk staff was pleasant and helpful. The $5 parking garage across the street was very convenient and a much better deal than the $22 valet at the hotel. Restaurants were close by and the location was very convenient to DART and the 6th Floor Museum. We would stay at this location again.

“A beautiful hotel, ultra-clean but bordering on comically aloof.” We've stayed at about every 'on the map' hotel in NYC over the years, both up and down the scale from this one, but I can't recall such a contrast as the one we experienced during our stay at the Surrey. The Surrey is absolutely beautiful, upscale, ultra-clean and wonderfully quiet, with a great, high upper-eastside location practically in Central Park. So far, fairytale stuff for Manhattan, right? In odd contrast to this visual and auditory delight, and although service was crisply attended, the lobby staff seemed to have all graduated from 'L 'Academie Snooty-Hooty,' with high marks in unnecessary stand-offishness. Don't get me wrong, we don't like to be pawed or overly-familarized by hotel staff, but the extremely aloof posturing we experienced there was like a comedy scene from a 40's movie in which the desk attendants are trying to get rid of the 'riff-raff.' (of note, there is a lovely housekeeping attendant named Kashmira and an elderly doorman who are the perfect balance of professional and friendly) We would stay at the Surrey again, because the quality of accommodations far outweigh the behavioral quirkiness, but as a suggestion to the staff... "Lighten up," and like most NYC hotels... add $20 a day to the room rate instead of insultingly charging separately for hi-speed internet. (even the chain inns get how irritating this is) PS: After re-reading this review, I would mention we aren't Ogres, Mutants or Whiners... just a generic middle-aged couple who wear clean clothes, have clean nails and comb their hair.

“Very nice stay at Westin Tabor Center for conference” My overall stay at this hotel was very nice. I arrived very early to check-in (9 AM), and while a room was not available due to the hotel being sold out the night before, my bags were collected and I was advised to return around noon. I returned around 1 and found I had been assigned a nice room with a king bed. The room and bathroom were incredibly spacious with nice fixtures. Furnishings included a desk, a few chairs, a large dresser, and a flat-screen TV. Hangers, an iron, and a safe were available in the clost. In a "green" effort, and assuming you are staying more than one night, a card can be hung on your door the night before to decline housekeeping for the next day and recieve a $5 credit at the hotel restaurants (I used mine at the lobby's Starbucks). Check-out was at noon and painless as the TV account system actually worked and allowed check-out. Internet is available in-room for a charge. It was a little over $10 a day for regular internet or $20 for highspeed. Free wifi is available in the lobby, so it was not uncommon to see people sitting downstairs with their laptops. This hotel is located on the 16th street mall, which is an area full of shops and restaurants and is serviced by free busses traveling up and down the mall. There is a Walgreens and Rite Aid a few blocks from the hotel if you need medicine or to stock up on snacks. The hotel is about a 5 block walk to the Colorado Convention Center and its surrounding hotels. It took me about 15 minutes or so to walk to the convention center, and with good timing, you might be able to jump a free bus and get to California Street in a few minutes. This is a very busy area, even at night, so I was not too worried about walking around after dark, though 2 AM may be a different story. There are quite a few panhandlers on the street and around the hotel, but they did not seem as aggressive as I've seen in other cities. Downtown Denver is quite a ways from the Denver airport. If you are in a small group (1-2), your best bet is a shared ride shuttle from the airport (SuperShuttle, etc, for about $20/pp). If you have a larger group, a taxi or a towncar would work out to be a better option (faster, about $55 car).

“Great Location but a few minor issues” Stayed last weekend, needed a hotel near Union Station and the Capitol, &the Hotel George was in a perfect location, less than 5 minute walk to the station and a bit more than five to the Capitol; also close to the Mall, Supreme Court and Library of Congress. Balancing the other pros and cons, the hotel is worth a visit. Other pros: Most comfortable beds. Friendly hotel staff. Complimentary wi-fi and $10 free mini-bar with Kimpton In Touch free membership. Free afternoon hot chocolate, and wine reception afterward. Quiet rooms. Uncrowded fitness center. Taxi always waiting outside front door. Fair room rate. Cons: Satellite tv that went out often due to wind, most frustrating. Bathroom shower tiles/grout could use some clean-up, though bathroom was otherwise spotless. Sofa showing a bit of wear, room not as cutting edge as the usual Kimpton vibe. There is also a good restaurant located right at the hotel, Bistro Bis, very convenient after a long day on the town.

“Great Staff, Location, & Experience” We booked for a family vacation to Philly about a month in advance on the chain's website. Our room (double Queen room on the 6th floor) at 200/night cost more than the AAA rate but we selected a room to include breakfast, which saved us both in time and money- and we were very happy we made this decision. I planned in advance to park at the Wannamaker parking lot under Macy's instead of using the valet- at $40/day + 28%, it was worth the trouble to move my own car. The hotel was recently renovated; it was originally the City Hall Annex and the rooms are decent sized. What sets apart this hotel in the world of Marriot is the staff. From the valet to the deskstaff, the maids and the restaurant service, we were impressed at how well and NICELY everyone treated us- at the level of a European deluxe hotel, with constant smiles and pleasantries. What a welcome change! My kids loved that our room has a view of City Hall and the statue of William Penn; the breakfast buffet was wonderful, and while the pool is both small and shallow at only 3' deep, they were thrilled to swim each day between tourist activities. For the room, I wished the mattresses were stiffer (simply my personal choice) , but they were very nice and plush beds and bedding. I also thought that the rooms would include personal safes which I have come to expect in my travels, but this hotel room did not include them. I would not hesitate to stay here again. I have stayed in Philly for business over a dozen times, usually in the business district or in the convention center Marriott, which is HUGE. I like this smaller hotel, its convenience to Old Town, Center City, and its courteous staff.
“Good Stay” Good stay, great value but small rooms and please update the showers! You won't go wrong here great location too!

“Great location” We took our daughter here to celebrate her 10th birthday. For the purposes of our trip, this hotel was perfect. It is a family-friendly hotel with an indoor pool, fitness center, and a small arcade for the children. The hot tub adjacent to the pool was under repair while we were there. There is also a starbucks in the lobby. The rooms were comfortable as they were - plenty of room, clean, good beds - but the upper floors were closed for renovation, so I guess they are upgrading the rooms, including flat-screen tvs. The service was excellent - the best I have had at a Marriott and I have stayed at many of them. I called the day before to have some milk and cookies sent up to the room upon checkin for my daughter's birthday, and they did this complimentary. They also included a pint of Haagen Daz ice cream and a birthday card. Perfect. Room service for breakfast was good and punctual. The view (room 310) was wonderful of the harbor, the park, and the North End beyond. I would recommend this for families who are visiting the Aquarium, Quincy Market, or going whale watching (easy walk to all of these and very safe). It's not a particularly romantic hotel and seems to be used for large functions often(there were several group events and receptions booked the weekend we stayed). This was not a problem because the event rooms are well away from the guest rooms. We were very pleased with our stay.

“Great Choice of a Hotel for reunion with a good friend” I have stayed at one Kimpton hotel previously, the Solarmar in San Diego two years ago and was impressed. I wanted to stay in a nice place to meet up with an old friend and co-worker, so researching the website and reviews here, we ended up at the Palomar. I was not disappointed. The location is great, although the building from the outside is not distinctive at all. Inside, all was pleasant. We were greeted efficiently and were well pleased with our room. ( My friend, in our goofy brand of humor, kept exclaiming, " Man, what a dump! " jokingly of course. ) I have been living out of hotels for the past seven months most of the time and this was one of the finest rooms I have stayed in. The morning we were leaving my friend noticed that the carpet was soaking wet oustside the bathrrom door, perhaps from leakage in the pipe under the sink. I reported this as we were leaving, but it did not detrtact from our stay. We had breakfast in the restaurant this morning, which was fine, although on the pricy side. My intent had been to eat in the italian restaurant the first night, but when I stuck my head in the place was crowded and overly noisy, which turned me off, so we had dinner elsewhere.

“Like it Better than Penninsula” So enjoyed hotel. Love the serrene modern, Asian decor. Have also spent much time at Peninsula-obviously both outstantding-just like modernity of Park Haytt more-beds and linens superior at Park Hyatt-wonderful deep tub and bath-could link my ipod into stereo tv system-Had dinner at hotel restaraunt and found excellent food, decor and service. Prompt morning breakfast room service. Amex Platinum services of lunch and included breakfast very worthwhile.

“Great hotel despite the lobby” This hotel is part of the luxury collection.... the lobby is lacking the element of luxury. The carpet in the lobby is nasty and dirty. If you are here for one night you might not want to stay again based on the lobby, but I was at this hotel for 9 nights and found the hotel to be very nice. I did have a few problems during my long stay and the manager did respond to my problems. My room was large, SPG Plat. member and thus I was able to get an upgrade, and the room was comfortable. As for the hotel restaurant, it is fantastic... they opened up for my group, on an evening they were closed, with short notice and provided excellent service. They are indeed examples of a luxury hotel. The food/service was excellent and I continue to receive positive feedback about the evening. The front desk was not too friendly upon check in... they were a bit cold.... the gym is average, but ok. I would consider staying here again as I do love the location and the large rooms.

“Un bellissimo soggiorno” Situato al centro di San Francisco, vicinissimo a Union Square, dove troverete moltissimi negozi, ristoranti, ecc., e vicino a Chinatown, l'hotel sembra avere molti anni ma i vari dettagli sono ben curati che non fanno notare l'età. Noi siamo arrivati in auto e dovevamo consegnarla proprio ad una filiale di National che si trovava a 300m dall'hotel. Inoltre, il giorno del nostro check out dovevamo recuparare un'altra auto che dovevamo ritirare da una filiale di Alamo che anchessa era a 300m. All'arrivo siamo stati molto ben accolti, i facchini ci han portato le valige in camera alla reception ci hanno aiutato con le varie informazioni e formalità di chek in ed inoltre ci hanno portato una buonissima bottiglia di Champagne della Sonoma County accompagnata da 2 buonissimi cioccolatini. La camera era molto bella, spaziosissima fornita di divanetto, schermo piatto, wi-fi gratuito, stereo, microonde, frigo bar, lavandino, ... all'ingresso c'era un armadio e molto posto dove poter lasciare le valigie cosicché non intralciavano nella zona letto. Il letto comodissimo. Nel bagno si notava sullo specchio solo un po' di vecchiaia dello stesso, ma non sono i difetti che possono rovinare un soggiorno in questo hotel. L'hotel è fornito anche di un bar dove la sera si esibisce un pianista e di un ristorante lo Zingari. All'ultimo piano si trova il il fitness center, il concierge e a nche una terrazza dove e possibile rilassarsi un po'. Inoltre è presente una sala relax molto elegante al coperto. Noi non avevamo la colazione inclusa nel nostro soggiorno ma non era un problema visto che a 300m, ancora una volta, cera uno Starbuks. L'unica cosa che forse ci ha un po' disturbati è stato il club che era di fronte all'hotel ma solo perchè sentivamo molta gente fuori per la strada, altrimenti il nostro soggiorno al Donatello è stato veramente piacevole.

“Enjoyed my stay” I stayed at the Hampton Inn for 4 nights on business. The rooms were very nice - large for NY standards. Comfy beds, small but functional bathroom. Duvet covers & pillows were lovely. The 'breakfast on the go' bags were perfect for my needs. This hotel compares to any full service hotel in terms of comfort, so don't be fooled by the word 'Inn' in the title. I've stayed at the Marriott Marquis just a few streets down and this Hampton was very comparable in terms of room comfort. I would certainly consider staying there again on another trip to NYC.

“Good stay in a good hotel, just some staff issues” So, we was at this hotel for 2 nights, the hotel is really big and the location is good! The front guest woman was sooo welcome and the checkin was fast and "smooth". The room was big, with still this amazing hot cookie! and we got free wifi. Just somes issues with the girls at the inside starbucks, very unfriendly. If I have to go back to Denver, I will definitely stay at this hotel, Quebec street is a "easy access" street, and we have the walmart at 30 sec of the hotel!

“What planet are the reviewers from?” All the reviews that appeared on your site about the Monaco Baltimore were so glowing that I decided to book the hotel on trip earlier this week. I have to say that I thought I was at a different hotel than the one your reviewers wrote about. In my view, the Monaco Baltimore is about 2 1/2 stars (I think I'm being kind). The entrance is on N. Charles St and the interior of the entrance is very tired, dated, "dead". Although the reception staff on the 2nd floor said the hotel was nearly full, it felt deserted - no "buzz". My room first appeared attractive enough - nice colors but the lighting was horrible, including the bathroom. The bedside lighting was particularly egregious, i.e. basically a bulb with frosted 1/2 shade against a mirrored column. I felt like I was in a Chinese restaurant. Moreover, the switch was 3 feet above the bed so one had to sit up to turn the light on or off. The mattress was soft, very overdue to be thrown out, the bed frame very squeaky. The linens were perhaps 300 thread count (when they were new)... I've gotten better at a Bed Bath & Beyond sale. And the bathroom: I had booked a "King Premier" which was supposed to have "special spa amenities" but the only amenities were a VERY small bottle each of shampoo, conditioner and body lotion (so small a bottle that one had to choose to use it on arms OR legs, not both). What I found most offensive was that there were plenty of amenities available in a drawer at the mini-bar... a toothbrush for $5, toothpaste for $5 and lip balm at the bargain price of $12. More on the bathroom: again, horrific lighting but the saving grace in the bathroom was the jacuzzi... while I had no intention of using it, I was forced to when the water in the shower was lukewarm at best. I called the management and reported it but no acknowledgement, apology, NADA. Although they say there are complimentary newspapers, they had run out of the NY Times by 7 am... the only other newspaper I spotted on both days was the Wall St Journal (maybe Rupert Murdoch is now having to discount!). I travel all over the world for my business and so have stayed at hundreds of hotels but the Monaco is without a doubt the worst "luxury" hotel I've stayed out. I should also note that the neighborhood is less than interesting - no restaurants close by, a lot of random people hanging out on the street and the only business or service open after 8 PM is the FedEx office. I opted not to eat in the hotel's restaurant on the ground floor since it is basically a bar turned into a depressing daylight space to serve food. One of the great pities is that the hotel is in the former HQ's of the B&O railroad - lots of original details in some of the common areas. There was the opportunity to reference the former use of the building with old photos of the building, their railroad, etc. but the design team chose to completely ignore this and create a hodgepodge of styles - tired "traditional" entrance but the lounge next to the reception area on the 2nd flopr was very modern and very garish. All in all, it was a depressing experience and an uncomfortable stay. I've never written a review before but this hotel was so bad that I felt compelled to dispel the pretty picture painted by your reviewers. CH, November 9, 2011
“Good Hotel” Basic Hotel but all you need for a base In a good location for access to all parts of the city Small but clean pool

“Solid, consistent business hotel with access to great retail/restaurants” Hilton - Polaris is a solid, consitent "business" hotel located in a major retail hub in north Columbus. Rooms are large, clean and well turned out. The staff is friendly and helpful. The hotel has all of the 'usual" amenities - pool, lounge, gym, business center, meeting facilites and I think that there is a spa there as well. There is great access to any number of retail and restaurant options - to include a very good steak house right in-front of the hotel. The only real distinguishing feature are the "fire features" out back - kinda neat burning torch type things. So take it for what it is - a nice, comfortable, consistent albiet generic business hotel with access to a ton of retail and restaurant options.

“Hidden Treasure” I've stayed here a couple of times. And when it comes to Residence Inns in DC, which theres several this one is the best by far. The lobby and rooms are the most updated and rooms are generous in size. The pool is nice although I never seen to make it there but its indoor and a plus to any downtown hotel. The location is probably the thing I like most. It's off a little street just south of the National Mall a quite one with Nasa offices close by. Metro and train are walking distance and the mall about a 15 min walk. I feel like this hotel is my little secret. Quite, familiar, and comfortable. Long term stay? Defenitly take a look at this hotel. Some constructive critisim: This hotel not sure if it has gotten any better since I've been last but they have the most aggressive Housekeeping staff I've ever encountered in all my travels. Everytime I stay they start to knock way too early for my liking and are VERY persistant. The front desk was kind enough to give me a late check out once but come 12pm they still came knocking were a little rude and told me to call the front desk to get approval? I travel alot and inbetween time zones so felt a little pressured to wrap my stay up. Not the most pleasant and it was very clear they were determined to flip the room. A little lesson in Housekeeper Ettiquette would go a long way.

“Best Location, Best Hotel, Best No Worries” Perfect hotel located within reach of everything. The Hilton employees were very professional, from the front desk to the cleaning staff. Our room, on the 23rd floor, faced North towards the MET Life Bldg. We had a DBL Bed room (larger than the rooms facing the Empire State Bldg), good sized and CLEAN! The bathroom was modern with no issues. Beds were firm and the bed spreads and sheets were very comfortable and CLEAN! The Hilton is right down the street from Macy's. Around the corner is Broadway with a short walk to Times Square. Grand Central, Rockerfeller Center and Empire St Bldg are minutes away. The subway is 30 seconds out the door. The stay was perfect and the Hilton people did a great job with impressing us on our first visit to the Big Apple!

“Excellent hotel - prime location” Recently reserved 2 suites using Hilton Honors points. Called in advance to make sure son's name on one suite so he & family could check in prior to our arrival. Check-in was smooth for both suites which were next to each other. Typical arrangement for Embassy Suites.... 2 rooms... one with sofa, chairs, desk, chairs and small wet bar with refrigerator and the other room with bed(s)... with bathroom being in shortl hallway dividing both rooms. Rooms arranged around center atrium. Overall hotel atmosphere - very bright, clean, modern decor. There are 4 glass enclosed elevators to access suites from the main lobby. Of note, is that the lobby entrance is NOT on the street level. Street Elevator lobby, & valet parking attendants are on 1st floor (Self-parking - $41.00 daily but with NO in&out; Valet parking $49 daily... with in& out privileges). Valet service may take up to 20 minutes to get car... so call from the room & plan accordingly. Breakfast buffet is very good, although lines are long if one goes down in the last hour. Suggestion... go early like at 7:30 or 8 a.m. Omelet station is run well, with one person taking orders and putting out the various ingredients for the chef to add to the omelets. Chef is amazing at the speed in which he makes omelets... fun to watch. Can also get pancakes, biscuits with gravey, hash browns and pancakes in this line.There is also a buffet line for eggs, bacon, etc on steam table. Assorted pastries, yogurt, cereals, and fruit... although fruit could have been expanded. During the week days, the fruit was sliced melons and pineapple. On weekend, fruit was limited to whole oranges and bananas but no pre-sliced melons. On the weekend the hotel was filled with families instead of business people... perhaps that made a difference in what was put out. There is a very large seating area and the tables were quickly cleaned with hotel staff. Suites had 2 flat screen TVs plus sofa, & 3 chairs in living room, one of which was a very comfortable ergonomic chair. Our son's suite did not have an ergonomic chair. There was also a very large ottoman suitable for seating. Directly across the street from the hotel is a large market - Dominick's that also has a Starbucks. Domick's is open until at least midnight and some nights until 1 a.m. In addition to the normal food supplies, one can purchase bus passes at Dominicks... we highly recommend... it's so easy to jump on and off a bus to Navy Pier... the buses are air conditioned, the free trolley is NOT! It's also an easy walk to Michigan Avenue where many buses can be picked up going to and from the Museum Campus and up and down the Magnificent Mile shopping district. Many of the Chicago taxi's are NOT air conditioned. Be careful in flagging down a cab that has windows rolled down! Some cabs are hybrids and drivers actually USE their AC. When we asked valet attendant about getting us a cab to the airport, he suggested we consider a town car as it would be more comfortable with only a slightly higher cost. We opted for this and he immediately called a town car and we paid a flat rate of $45. plus the tip. This is our 2nd stay at this hotel and we'll definitely return here again.

“Oh, the beds!” The hotel is located next to the Chinatown gates, which is convenient for orientation purposes especially for first-timers in the city. Rooms are spacious and nicely appointed but the best part by far is their beds. So, so comfortable!!! Undoubtedly one of the best. They have plasma TVs and iPod docking stations. The hotel is very "green" and environmentally friendly from the lights to the bath products. Wi-fi works great and is free. Staff is very nice and helpful. They even had a wine reception on a Wednesday night at the bar and it was fantastic. I cannot think of any negatives and I would definitely stay there again next time I go to San Francisco.

“A Mixed Bag” This is simultaneously one of the best and one of the worst hotels I've visited in a major American city. The rooms are large and comfortable, with lovely bedding and handsome, well equipped baths. The location, a block from the Walnut Street shopping and restaurant strip and only a little farther from Rittenhouse Square, is terrific. But the lobby and other public spaces are cold, harsh, and deafeningly noisy; the reception desk staff are aggressively incompetent; the food is mediocre, at best; and the entrance is so cramped that it takes only a few cars to bring everything to a halt. The reception staff so badly bungled my registration that they "accidentally" attempted to triple bill me. Throughout my stay, computers were allegedly down, so staff could not show me my actual charges for meals or drinks. When I checked my bags upon departure, the concierge and bell staff took almost 15 minutes to find them again. Though many of the local, Philadelphia staff are kind and competent, the French staff (Sofitel is a French chain) vary from cloyingly cute ("We have been up all night baking croissants just for YOU!") to coldly arrogant. And you pay a lot for the privilege. Though I liked my room, I'll never return.

“Dünne Wände in guter Lage” Nicht weit vom schönen Viertel Georgetown mit vielen Restaurants und Cafés und guter Anbindung an die Innenstadt (Circulator nach Union Square alle 10 Minuten) liegt das etwas in die Jahre gekommene Holiday Inn an einer vielbefahrenen Ausfallstraße. Das Zimmer ist komfortabel eingerichtet, doch sind die Wände so dünn, dass, wenn jemand im Flur die Türe zuknallt, das Kopfteil des Bettes ausschlägt. Die Türen sind ramponiert und verkratzt, die Badewanne mit Email-Farbe überstrichen - nicht wirklich schön! Die Klimaanlage war enorm laut, die Fenster sind schlecht isoliert. Ganz gut fand ich die Regelung, einen Frühstücksvoucher über US $ 20.00 zu erhalten, mit dem ich à la carte mir etwas bestellen konnte. Das Business Center war wegen Renovierung geschlossen. Es gibt einen kostenlosen Shuttle zum Georgetown University Hospital oder zu einer Metro Station (bis 18:30 Uhr).

“Fantastic Weekend!” We spent 3 nights and fortunately, Seattle had beautiful sunny weather the entire time we were there. We splurged on a waterview room and what a view it is! This quaint boutique hotel is tucked in amongst the hustle and bustle of Pike Place Market and the location couldn't be better for walking about downtown Seattle - we did not rent a car; just to took the train from Seatac to Westlake Centre which is 4 blocks away. The staff was fantastic; very knowledgable. The roof top deck for guests offers a spectacular view of the Puget Sound.

“BED BUGS--DON'T STAY HERE!!” I highly suggest looking up the bed bug registry and seeing how many problems The Jane has with bed bugs. The fourth floor seems especially infested. I stayed at The Jane one night although I had reservations for 3 nights. I was in a single room with shared bathroom and thought 99 dollars a night for NYC was a steal . My room was the size of a closet and I had a very uncomfortable sleep because the bed was much smaller than a twin, it was more like a cot. It was a futon type small cot but I am not a huge person so I thought it would be fine. First of all, if you are claustrophobic, DO NOT stay at the Jane. Secondly if you are tall or bigger this bed will never be big enough for you. It was a very hot July night and I turned on the air conditioner, it was unbelievably loud, so much so that I had to turn it off. The bathroom was right down the hall from my room and when people used the hand dryer it was also extremely loud and woke me every time it was used. Actually I can deal with all of this....it was only 99 dollars after all. I woke up the next morning scratching my legs and noticed what looked like mosquito bites. I immediately looked on line to see what bed bug bites looked like and sure enough, they look like mosquito bites. I found the bed bug registry and when I put in The Jane I noticed pages of reports, especially on the fourth floor, which I happened to be on. I jumped out of bed and turned over the sheets and there they were, one right under my pillow actually. I took my pillow down to the lobby and they were not one bit surprised, just told me they would take all my belongings and have them heated to kill any bugs and eggs while they put me in another room with a robe. I couldn't believe they book these rooms knowing they have bed bugs. When I told them I read on line that the 4th floor was infested they told me it isn't always a specific floor, they are on and can be on every floor. They put me in a captains room while they treated my belongings. This room was filthy, the carpet is not clean, the walls are not clean and the furniture has dirty upholstery. It was gross! It was also hot so I turned on the air conditioner which did not work. I told them that the rooms are so small that they can't fit a luggage rack in them and a suitcase should always be off the bed and floor and on a luggage rack in case of bed bugs. They had no comment. The only thing I did not let the bell boy take to get sanitized were an expensive pair of wedding shoes made out of satin, my leather wallet, and my computer. I didn't want them out of my sight so the bell boy had me shower on the 4th floor while he brought my extreme valuables up to the captains room. I rushed to my room only to find the door open and my valuables thrown on the floor. There was a table in this room and a large dresser, but it was thrown on the floor for possibly another bed bug infestation. I panicked but everything was there, he just didn't close the door all the way and make sure it was locked. I was furious at that point. My clothes and belongings were brought back up to me and the suitcase was left on the dirty carpet and not lifted up onto a table or dresser. When I was in my original room I pulled my sheets on the bed back I noticed that there was no mattress protector, just a thin little sheet between you and this little futon. Just a thin little sheet between you and the bed bugs and all the people who stayed there before you, I was really disgusted at this. I have stayed at many places where I have shared a bathroom, but this hotel was the worst. Every other place I stayed at had a shower, toilet and sink in private area where you can close the door and the room is all yours. At the Jane the restrooms, showers and sink are in one room that everyone shares and I found it a bit disgusting to watch half naked people spitting toothpaste in the sink and shaving in front of me. For some reason it just seemed so gross. It was not private in any way and felt dirty, not to mention when I used the shower there was no hot water and you can hear people going to the bathroom. I checked into another hotel and woke up with a bed bug crawling on my chest. I told the hotel manager and he said they have not had one incident in over a year with bed bugs and he was really surprised I had one. I feel terrible because my guess is that I brought it from the Jane. Their little cleaning method did not work, or possible when my things were thrown on the floor in the captains room I got more. I don't know for sure. The only thing I will say about the Jane is that everyone was nice and they did comp my room but how nice are they really when they book a room and put you in one knowing full well that they have bed bugs? This hotel needs to be shut down and treated, each and every floor in my opinion. Lastly I will say that I know bed bugs do not come from dirty people but never in my life have I seen more filthy, dirty, homeless looking people than those staying at this hotel. I WOULD NEVER STAY HERE AGAIN. Don't stay here, even if you are desperate!

“Busy Hotel” We stayed here for a family wedding. The rooms were clean. We requested a quiet room through the gold passport program, which I would highly recommend since the train tracks are right outside. We did indeed get a very quiet room. This is a very busy convention/business hotel. Self parking is across the street in a gated city lot. I would stay here again.

“My New Favorite at SeaTac” Don't get me wrong -- I still love Cedarbrook Lodge near SeaTac. But this trip I went for the Hilton because my flight got in at 1am after a trip lasting 27 hrs. All I wanted was the nearest hotel with a great bed, and boy, did I get it!! Fantastic!! My timing was superb for the free shuttle & I was whisked to the hotel in 2 minutes or so. Check in was courteous & fast (I'm really not sure how coherent I was, so I appreciate that checking in travel-weary patrons can be difficult, I'm sure). After a hot shower, I collapsed into the bliss of a wonderfully comfortable bed made with very nice linens & possessing plenty of perfect feather/down pillows. I detest bouncy pillows. The room was typical sedate, comfortable Hilton. The towels adequate, not great. The hotel has a very nice central garden which my room faced. I had the breakfast buffet which was a bit pricey at $20, but really very excellent. For an airport hotel, I find it odd that they charge for parking. The restaurant & bar are off the lobby, very comfortable, very relaxing, very nice. I've slept in many of the hotels near SeaTac and this one, so far, would be pretty darn hard to beat. I will certainly be back.

“Great location for price” I found this hotel on-line last minute & got it for $79+ tax, so did our friend who's stayed here numerous times & recommended it. However, it is in the middle of renovations inside & out. We had no hot water on 12th floor 1st night or next morning. It was lukewarm at best. The constant hammering in the morning was unbearable. Our friend was on the 28th floor & didn't have a problem. He also had hot water. We were switched to the 28th floor after going to desk & complaining. I tried calling front desk/concierge & leaving msg. twice, but no one called back. After switching to new room, we did not have any problems, & we had a corner room with great view of Hudson river on one side, & the entire city on other. The rooms are typical size for NYC, perhaps a tad bigger than some. Seems all rooms have been up-graded with new beds, linens, big flat-screens, new sinks, tubs & showers. We really liked the bathrm mirrors lighted from behind! They're called "magic mirrors". One thing missing which is usually on the desk in any room; a pen & pad of paper! I was on-line booking something & needed to write a # down, & could find no pen or paper, so I saved it to cell phone... I am sure we'll return when the construction is finished, if we can afford it then. I have the feeling this will be a much desired hotel afterwards. We literally got the last room on-line. They also gave us a gift bag w/souveniers & a discount card for numerous places for our troubles.

“If you just need the basics, this motel is for you.” My friend, her other friend, & I stayed here for one night. It was pretty ok. Like the title says- if you just need the basics(bed, bath, sleep), then this motel will do the job. It's in a quite area- so no worries of loudness outside. I did notice a sheet on the table that stated 'Room Service' but my friend's friend stated that it was pricey(she had gotten there the night before). She said she walked on over to the Sonic- it's a couple of blocks from the motel. They do have a couple of places that deliver to the motel. The motel is located next to some woods and from the looks of it could be considered isolated. So if you are traveling by foot, then be careful when going out. If you want a no frills place to cover your basic needs as well as saving money, then I suggest this place.

“Second stay here, still like this place!.” Second stay as the title says, 2 nights while in town on biz. I like this place a lot, the staff here is fantastic, the place is modern and I think it is the most recent hotel built in the area. I like the style, amenities and location. Good stay overall even though I had to change rooms because I found a few bugs that made me uncomfortable. They looked like tiny bed bugs but couldn't tell and gave a few to the night manager for him to have them looked at the follow day. Didn't hear back from anyone about them, that worries me.

“Wow!” I had never stayed at a St. Regis before. When looking for a hotel in Houston, I wanted something near the Galleria. I used priceline to bid on 5 star hotels in that area and got this hotel for $120/night. I was initially a bit worried about it since the reviews implied a nice but older hotel. After having stayed there, however, I would say yes it is older, but it has been updated and well maintained. The staff is truely exceptional. What I expect from 5 star hotels in Asia rather than the US. Yes, valet parking is pricey ($27/night) and there are lots of people to tip. But they were so nice and the service so great I didn't mind. The room was great and huge. The bed was luxurious. Internet is not free. The bathroom was great. The gym was surprisingly small, but had an attendant who brought me a free headphone, towel, and cold water bottle! This is not the boutiquey/hip hotel I usually stay at. But I would say this is classic elegance. If I need a hotel in Houston again, I would not hesitate to stay here. Loved it!

“Excellent service in a great location!” The MileNorth is in an excellent location for anyone wanting to visit the downtown sights of Chicago. We found all of the staff to be exceptional in their friendliness and helpfulness. Special praise goes to the housekeeping staff for noticing small details about our habits and accomodating them without being asked. Our room was not fancy, but clean and comfortable with a fun, quirky decor and extra amenities, such as free Internet. We were very happy here. One friendly suggestion: Our room had a split level floor, with 3 steps from the entry and bathroom down to the bed area. We found it appealing, but it is hard to see the steps if one gets up in the night. It might be a good safety idea to install a small night light.

“Over the Hill” An overall okay stay with some problems. Pros are nice size rooms and great bathrooms, fabulous in-room dining, Top of the Mark Restaurant is very nice with a view and live entertainment. Cons, rooms are not soundproof, no spa, no pool, some rooms with a limited view, a very loud "fire alarm" was tested three times on a very early SATURDAY MORNING.. internet available for a fee, no wireless service...needs renovation.

“Nice, solid place.” Got a deal on hotels.com. Good location, not great. We had a long wait to check in and they had waters and champagne available. Room was small but nice. Pet friendly. They had a dj in the lobby after 9 pm. Not the quietest, but you are in NYC. I was awakened at 130 am by a vocal young lady that let's just say wasn't sleeping,

“Great Stop Over” We stayed at the Holiday Inn Apr 14, for an early morning flight the next day. I found the place to be quite nice. The rooms were large and everything was fresh and clean. The resturant was great and they even have snacks at happy hour. I would stay here again if I were flying out of LAX, but you wouldn't pick this location for anything else, of coarse.We needed the shuttle bus for 3:30 am and he was right there ready to take us.
“ロケーションは良いです” union squareから2ブロック程度、ケーブルカー乗り場迄も2ブロック程度と立地は良いです。 但し、周囲が高いビルが多いこともあり、景色は全く駄目でした。(隣のビルしか見えません) ベッドは丁度良い硬さで熟睡出来ましたし、バスタブが大きくリラックス出来る点も良いです。

“Big (though worn) rooms, bigger breakfast buffet” The thing I remember most is the massive, generous breakfast buffet. Omelet station, Belgian waffles, hot, cold, pastry, fruit it's all here. Only knocks are the juices weren't so good, the hot buffet items were nearly all the same over 3 mornings, and the muffins/bagels/etc were pretty gross. Well, maybe not gross, just poor quality. They also do a free cocktail reception, and sometimes cookies are at the bell desk. (Cookies weren't great, but how can you complain about such a nice touch, really.) Rooms are oddly appointed and look well-worn in places. Bathrooms have unfortunate college-dorm decor. It seems to attract a lot of families and kids tend to wear out hotels rather quickly. Despite all the young kids bopping around the lobby, I didn't hear much noise in the room and slept well. The beds are in the back of the large rooms, away from the lobby noise. Not terribly close to the Metro, which is deeply unfortunate in DC's famously steamy summers. But it's in a pretty, somewhat residential part of DC, which was a nice alternative to places on busier, commercial areas.

“Very nice” Very nice hotel, rooms were good. Parking is an issue, maybe not as much b/c of the cost (see previous reviews) but b/c it is a bit of a hike from the garage to the hotel. It's not bad, but not simple either. The lobby is sort of strangely laid out if you come in from the self-parking area (hard to get to). The wireless internet is good, but you have to sign up for a day pass with T-mobile or somebody like that, with passwords, credit cards, etc., sort of a pain. But it did work fine, so in the end okay. Got room service breakfast, it was good, but delivered 10 minutes after the time it was supposed to. Small irritation but noted. I would go back, especially if I could get a good rate, which I did.

“Nice boutique hotel” I stayed at the Sorrento for two nights. A colleague and I selected this hotel because it was within walking distance of a business meeting and we found a great rate on the Internet. The hotel was very comfortable and luxurious for the price. The standard rooms are on the small side, but that's to be expected given its location in downtown Seattle. I was given a free upgrade to a room with a more "suite"-like setup and enjoyed two TVs -- one in the bedroom and one in the sitting area. There is free wi-fi in the hotel, but parking is very expensive and valet-only (think carefully before you commit to parking there). If you don't mind walking several blocks, you can get to Pike's Market in perhaps 10-15 min. Convenient location in downtown Seattle; for the price we paid, would definitely recommend.

“A Surprising Value” On our recent trip to D.C., we were getting in very late and thought we would save a few dollars by staying the first two days at the Holiday Inn. We typically stay at more upscale hotels. We feared the worst but were very pleasantly surprised. When we got to the hotel, we were very pleasantly surprised. Lobby decor was very hip and the lobby very spacious. The front desk person was very kind and helpful too. On the way to our room, the decor was good, although we did smell a faint musty "old hotel smell." The room was nicely decorated for the money. Although this is clearly a standard chain hotel, we found the room to our liking and my wife even suggested that we might want to continue our stay there. My biggest complaint was that the shower water pressure was pretty weak. It was the middle of a cold snap in mid-March, so the pool wasn't open. There is a nice courtyard in the hotel that was not open either as it was far too cold. For seeing the Nataional Mall and Smithsonian, the location is excellent. The hotel is about a block from the L'Enfant Plaza metro station. It is also about a block from the Air & Space Museum. Our first day, we saw the museum and then took a walk up to look at the Capitol building. The downside is that there are not very many dining options and no nightlife in the area around the hotel. We booked on the internet. Our Friday - Saturday stay was only $128 per night. This included breakfast in the hotel restaurant. We were travling with our kids (8 & 10 yrs old) who eat free under the hotel's policy. We had breakfast both days in the hotel. We had the buffet, which was not bad. The service was friendly, but both days we didn't make it down to the buffet until about 20 minutes before it was to end (jet lag!) That made the pickings pretty slim. The hotel's restaurant has the typical economy hotel ambiance, but the price was right. Service was mixed. We found several staff people to be extraordinarily helpful. On the other hand, we got the run around and some "feel like a number" service from other staff. I would reccomend this hotel if you are looking for a good deal and would like to be near the national mall. It was clean, centrally located, well decorated, and a very good value overall.

“OK but not great for a Westin” I was here apparently at a sold out time..... rooms were not ready, and they said they would call when one was ready (I asked as a Platinum Starwood member, if they can help provide priority); they took down my phone number and 3 hours later, still nothing. I checked back and said MY room was not ready, after pushing, they had rooms clean and ready but NOT MINE --- after awhile I got her to agree that all I needed was a room and now; not sure what the difference of what MY room meant. The Luggage concierge was not at their desk; so needed to wait for the Front Desk to help me with. They had a package for me - which was a FedEx envelope which they had the gall to charge me $8 for "receipt & storage" of!!! This package wasnt available when I checked it and of course too forever to get to me. The rooms were nice, of the usual Westin quality; which is good; but the service really left a bad taste for me. Hotel is next tot he Convention Center but a few blocks from the city downtown shopping square. Think next time in the area, I might give the Aloft a try which seemed right in the middle of things.

“I've stayed in better” If it is raining when you check in you better hope you have a room in the main building. If not you will get very wet. This LaQuinta has what seems like 3 different sections. All the rooms are outside rooms. There is a football stadium on one side and a fire station on another!! So don't go here for a quiet night. The beds were not very comfortable (like a foam mattress). The rooms were grungy and in need of a fresh coat of paint and some mold removal. It seemed they may have been repainting some of the rooms, already. The breakfast was VERY lacking. Of course they quit serving it at 9:30 and I didn't go down until 9:00. Small yogurts, waffles you can make yourself, apples, boiled eggs and donuts. There may have been bagels too. They would not provide ice for drinks so if you need ice bring your own. There was a machine with apple juice and orange juice and a coffee machine. Seating was very limited!! However there were 4 waffle makers so that did help some. This is a VERY basic motel. The desk staff was all very young (college age/20's) but sweet. On a positive note, our room was ready and it was the type of room we requested. Easy check in and check out. There was free WiFi. The a/c worked great. I would not stay here again, however and I usually love La Quinta!

“Hidden Gem!” I just returned from a 2 night weekend getaway with my husband in NY. We chose The Alex on a friend's recommendation and totally enjoyed it. The hotel is on 45th and 3rd and is therefore slightly off the beaten path... but close enough that most important NY hangouts are a walk or taxi ride away. Like other reviewers we booked a studio suite but were upgraded to a 1 bdrm suite on the 15th floor. The lobby is very small with the concierge and front desk sharing the same space. The service is excellent, from the bellman right on up. The room looked just like the pictures on the website - very 'swanky' is the word I'd use! We ate breakfast and brunch in the restaurant and totally enjoyed both. The french toast is probably the best french toast I've ever had, and my husband was very pleased with his burger. My one complaint was the shower. It was easy enough to operate if you followed the instructions, however it shut off a couple times during my shower(s). That wasn't fun... We were sad to leave after only 2 nights and would very likely return to The Alex for our next trip to NYC.

“Super cute, met my high expectations, right near airport” Although I was slightly nervous approaching the property from outside, once I hit the doors, was immediately taken aback by the cuteness of the hotel from inside. Kind of reminds me of an old embassy suites, with the mexican tile and decor inside, and the big atrium in the center. Rooms were clean, updated, what more to ask for? Only thing I will say, don't ask the hotel for food recommendations. Make sure to find your own. So much local food, and they give you a canned sheet with franchises that you can get anywhere in the country. Experience San Antonio, from the dive to the fancy, tons of GREAT alternatives, really, who wants TGIFridays after a long travel? Close to airport, great location, parking was ample. Although it was on the highway, I never was bothered by any noise.

“Excellent Value” We stayed at The Magic Castle Hotel for 3 nights and we enjoyed it very much. I've booked this hotel based on recommendations on Trip Advisor, and as usual I was not disappointed. As soon as we arrived, we received a refreshing lemonade, and explanation how to get to the Chinese theater, which is within 3 minutes walk. The room we got (for four guests, two queen beds) was large and spacious, and included a full kitchen, well equipped and accessorized. (we bought products in a nearby supermarket and prepared light meals). The room also contained a large dining corner that allowed us to sit comfortably and eat (or work, if necessary). The room had a free wireless internet connection. The bathroom was small but nice, including good quality cosmetics. The television set was little disappointing (not a flat screen) and too small for the size of the room. But anyway, we did not come to Los Angeles to watch TV. Heated pool was great. The children swam in it every night and were very happy. After swimming, they wrapped themselves in robes of the hotel, and felt themselves like in Hollywood... Continental breakfast was pleasant and had a reasonable variety of products. You can sit at the table by the pool or take the food on trays in the room. There is also a free mini-bar, which we almost did not use, although it is nice and generous service. One downside: There was some low noise (not from the street) of some appliances or equipment, sometimes sounding like a buzzing during the night. Summary: highly recommended hotel, I am sure that I'll be back there.

“Still Ritzy” All of our previous NYC vacays have been further north: Mandarin Oriental, Essex House, Plaza, Ritz Carlton Central Park. I was a bit concerned that the Battery Park location woulld be a problem and it was--slightly. There is very little within easy walking distance, especially at night. We still loved the Staue of Liberty views and the people watching in Battery Park. Also, there are several subway lines within 1/4 mile walk, so if you are willing to deal with 4-5 extra stops on that, or fight traffic in a taxi I recommend you stronly consider R-C BP. We stayed in a Statue View Club Suite booked via AmEx Fine Hotels and Resorts. The price was very reasonable. Service is on par with the other places we have stayed. There were a couple of minor mixups on check in and checkout that were quickly remedied with typical R-C aplomb. The propery is beautiful and well-maintained. The club level here was terrific, as good as any I have seen anywhere. Lots of great small bites, snacks, drinls, and very relaxing. We had breakfast there each morning.It's a good thing, because we found the restaurant to be utterly lacking in selection, flavor, and efficiency. The bar is cozy and friendly though. Concierge knowledgeable abd helpful. Our suite was roomy and very well appointed. Typical R-C bed and bathroom appointments. Very comfortable and luxurious. Separate bathtub and shower areas not quite on par with other R-C as far as size but still very nice. You will know without doubt that you are staying at the Ritz. The staff is well trained and helpful. Somehow it does seem a bit...muted? comapred to their sister property on Centrl Park. Didn't bother us one bit. We told them we are celebrating our wedding aniversary and they went over thee top to help us celebrate. Rose petals on the bed and in the bathroom, flowers, and a different little gift each nigt definitely scored points with my wife and me. Very thoughtful and appreciated. SO would we stay again? I think so!

“Fairly priced” We stayed in one of the rooms without bathroom. The room was very, very small, almost two small for two people (but perfect for one guest). The decor I found to be very nice for the price we paid and I must say I was impressed. The rate was something like 119 per night which is very reasonable for a hotel in this neighborhood. The location is great! The room was well equipped with even an iron and an ironing board and a wash basin. No view though. We were also close to the ice machine on the second floor of hotel and it was somewhat noisy. The shared bathroom was OK. I was initially a little grossed out just by showering in the same place that somebody else was, but it seemed nevertheless sufficiently clean. It was not clear to me how many rooms shared this bathroom and shower. We only stayed in the room for three nights. I would probably prefer my own bathroom in the futuree, but if you can bear showering where somebody else did and you want to save on accomodations so you can spend on other things, this is a top choice. Felt that staff were friendly and efficient.

“Pretty Good” This hotel is in a great location in east midtown, so close to many things. We had a suite with one bedroom and a living area with a kitchenette. The bedroom was not large but adequate. The living area was also adequate. It was nice to have the small kitchen. The bathroom however was tiny! Crazy small. We had a balcony which I have to say in Manhattan is super nice. I can recommend this hotel, just don't expect super luxury. It's comfortable.

“Great Start!!! Would go again.....” Great start to our honeymoon, were a little worried reading some reviews going on about the area. We had no problems, Yes you might see the odd weirdo but lets face it you can see them anywhere. The hotel was more than expected, the room was very clean and comfortable, and as it was our honeymoon we had asked for a high room and the hotel obliged by giving us a room on the top floor 17th or something like that. The location is handy for everything (Dollar rent a car is right round the corner) and if travelling to San Fran again I would stay in this hotel again. Overall an excelent start to our trip round the USA. Next stop Santa Barbara. 5*

“It was okay” The hotel is well-located (not far from the airport, near shopping, etc), has nice facilities, and the staff is moderately helpful. The food was not very good, and I tried almost every dining venue. In fact, I was surprised by just how poor the food really was. Even the best restaurant managed to serve a fair-to-bad meal to each of us. I had a lovely suite and beautiful view, although the room was just short of being completely fresh and really well-kept. Paint chips, scratches and dings, some stains and bad grout. It seemed like there was a bit of the deferred maintenance the economy has caused at so many hotels. It was fine for this trip, but not the world class resort it bills itself to be. I don't golf, but heard that the course was great. So a mixed bag, but certainly a good but not great stay.

“Excellent choice in Denver” This newer mega-property had the best and most professional service of any hotel I have ever stayed in. The room was new and clear. Bed was comfortable. A noise maker air cleaner machine kept the outside street noise from the RTD light rail to a minimum (the line runs in front of the hotel). Great full service health club-the best I have ever seen in a hote. Had a high floor with great view of the Rockies. Close to 16th Street Mall. Use a B-Bike rental to get around--there's a station by the convention center. Highly recommended although a bit pricey.

“Location, Location, Location...” My family, which includes 2 boys aged 12 and 10, spent 5 days touring New York City. Having lived in NYC for many years, and taking my family for their first visit to the city, I selected to stay here because of the location. This is a beautiful hotel in an ideal location. So many of the major tourist spots - 5th Ave, Rockefeller Ctr, United Nations, Central Park, Times Square, Broadway etc. are a reasonable walk from the hotel. The Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island, 9/11 site, China town, Yankee Stadium are a short train ride on the # 4,5,6 line which stops right out side the hotel. The hotel lobby is still elegant after all these years and the rooms while a bit dated were very comfortable and clean. The on-site restaurant is a bit expensive for breakfast for 4. An excellent alternative is the out-door cafe (I think it is part of the Double Tree Hotel) located on 50th street between Lexington and 3rd Ave (a half block away when you go out the Lexington Ave exit). While there are more luxurious hotels in NYC than the Waldorf there is still something magical about this place. If you are coming to NYC as a tourist I recommend staying at the Waldorf.

“Why is this a Westin?!?” The Good: The location is nice and is directly across the street from the Hancock building and is on Michigan Ave. --- hummm ... let’s see.... Oh! They have a copy of the Wall Street Journal for you if you get up early! But you have to go to the lobby to get it. The Bad: The rooms are warn, dated and loud. The sheets are not fitted so you end up “kicking” them off and sleeping against the mattress, never washed blanket and comforter. The room – 546 – had mold, rust and water spots all over the ceiling and walls. The onsite dinning is very over priced and subpar. Over all I have no idea why this has the name Westin on it. I have stayed at many Westins in the US and Europe and I have never seen one like this. The quality reminded of a average Red Roof Inn – except the rooms open up to a hallway. Only stay here if you need good location and it is cheep!

“Location as it's best” I did lots of research and finally decided to stay at Monaco. Upon the check in, Sean didn't give me any option for the update and he didn't look pleasure to meet us. I noticed that Sean wasn't a good guy to talk to when you have requests or questions. (For example:My husband asked Sean what time Starbucks nearby closed and he said 11:30pm. So my husband went at 9:30pm and it was closed. Sean confirmed my husband will qualify for State Employee rate and later reservation agent told us he's not eligible.) Kimpton hotel promises to give us some gift for kids upon check in but there was nothing offered for my kids at Monaco. Bell/Valet service was here and there. It's really up to the person. Sometime it's good sometime is really bad. They didn't even come to open the door when we stopped the car at the front. There was nobody to help us with valet parking. Room was clean and Bed was very comfortable. One complaint was that entrance door has small gap and cold wind coming through the bathroom which makes bathroom super cold at night. We just use this hotel to just "sleep" and location was great. Wallgreens across the street, Starbucks near by. There was water and doggie bone by the front door. Dog lover will love this. I stayed at the 7th floor facing the street but noise wasn't too bad. I heard ambulance and firetruck all the time though.

“Can get decent deals on a nice hotel” I booked this room on hotwire for about $130. The hotel was very nice, rooms were big, the pool/hot tub area was very nice, and the location was great and easy to get to. The only negative is the parking situation, which costs $40 for valet without many options. We parked in a public parking site nearby on Wacker and it only cost $14 for the night. I would recommend staying at this hotel if you get a chance.

“A Great Spot By The Airport!” Located on Harbor Island just by the airport, it is hard to beat this hotel if you are flying out the next morning. It offers great views of the harbor, marina and downtown. Each room had a pleasant terrace you could sit out on and enjoy the view. Staff was pleasant and parking was available at a cost of $13 per day. There are a couple of restaurants within walking distance but you will need a ride to the Gaslamp Quarter.

“A functional stay” I stayed at the Club Quarters hotel for 2 nights and it was a comfortable stay. It's a curious mix in terms of amenities, it offers some nice touches such as some phone chargers in the Club Room, but then lacks some features which you might otherwise expect (e.g. in room safes). It is situated in the centre of Boston, but is quiet, with most of the surrounding buildings being office blocks. It is very easily reached from the airport using the Blue line to State St Station. The reception area is compact, and check in can be done via the desk, but check in using the automated machines is encouraged. The staff were courteous, but there wasn't a description of the facilities on check in, however, all of these were made clear in the room itself.
