It is possible to store your bag after check out, but as they are stored on another floor, make sure you allow them 5-10 minutes to retrieve it. I booked a standard room and this was decently sized. The decor is dark and a bit dated, but was not visibly showing wear and tear. It is possible to control the temperature in the room with a thermostat. The room is good if you want to work as it has a well kitted out desk with a desk lamp, and cables to attach a laptop to the TV screen, alongside a comfortable chair. Additionally free wireless internet is provided, and they have a nifty service which allows you to send documents to the printer located in the lounge room on the ground floor. There is a coffee making machine (with a solitary tea bag too), but no fridge. Additionally, there isn't a safe in the room or ironing facilitates. The bed was fine, and whilst not uncomfortable, it is some way off the beds you get at some of the big chains. The bathroom had a decent shower unit with good pressure, although as others have mentioned, the walls are a bit thin, and it was possible to hear the plumbing in the adjacent rooms. The bathroom amenities included a full size hair dryer, soap, body lotion, shampoo and dental rinse. Breakfast and other dining is available in the adjacent pub/restaurant, and there is a Club lounge on the ground floor to relax with some complimentary services such as newspapers, complimentary coffee & tea from a Keurig K-Cup machine and water (in addition to the water machines on each floor - which I liked). There are also 2 PC terminals with a printer. There is no room service, but they do provide a call-in service with local restaurants for a modest fee.

“Nice Hotel” I was pleased when checking in to find the front desk person Jennifer welcome me to the hotel for the 1st time. I was surprised when she gave me a room on the 22nd floor. When I made the reservation, it said I would get a room on the 4th to 7th floors. From the 22nd floor (which is not the highest, 36 is), you can still get some stunning views of San Francisco from one huge floor-to-ceiling window. The room was connected to another room, which is something I don't like, but at least the connecting door was close to the main door, and not in the center of the room. The Internet was way too expensive, $14.95 for a day. Didn't touch the minibar after a notice said the hotel would start charging after 10 seconds if the minibar was touched. Was happy to see there is a safe in the room, I can leave my laptop there. And the bathroom had plenty of towels. It's a nice hotel. I wonder if some employees at this hotel were ever affected by the recession. When I asked what was the cheapest way to get from the hotel to the airport, the concierge told me after discount, I can take the town car for $45. After the financial crisis and recession, the economy may be improving but that does not mean people have money to throw away. If I can take Bart to SFO for $8 and arrive exactly where I want, without any more walking, why would I be interested in paying $45? What I expected them to say is, "we can get a cab for you" for $23. Seems like some were not affected by the recession or else they would know even staying at a fancy hotel, people are looking for the best rates and not splurging like before the crisis.

“Not what I would have expected from a Grand Hyatt” I stayed here for a couple of nights attending a conference. While the location on the waterfront and close to downtown area is excellent, the hotel itself was a bit of a disappointment for me. I changed rooms during my stay because my first room on the 29th floor in the Harbor Tower was directly above the set of elevators that serve floors 1 to 28 and therefore was quite noisy. My request was handled professionally, no questions asked. I found the rooms and bathrooms to be quite dated and the service (aside from the front desk) quite sloppy. A couple of examples: in one room the “wired” internet connection wasn’t physically connected to anything, while it the other room it was. The “free” wired/wireless internet service is pretty much useless. When I arrived in the first room one of the water bottles available for purchase for $4.50 was open and half-empty (I wasn’t charged for it though). There were used dishes from a previous guest outside the door of my second room, and were not cleared away until late evening. This is not what I expect of a Grand Hyatt hotel. My recent stay at the Bayfront Hilton "next door" was a much better experience and I would not stay at this Grand Hyatt again.

“Very Enjoyable hotel” Stayed at the Embassy Suites- Park Central for 1 night recently. This hotel appears to have had a very nice makeover. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The room was very comfortable and clean. Had a very good night sleep, probally the best sleep I have had in a long time in a hotel. Manager's Reception was very nice. Breakfast the next morming was great and had many wonderful choices. Would not hesitate to stay here again when back in Dallas.

“Ok hotel.” Hotel is fine. Not bad but not good either. Front desk staff is very friendly and helpful. Rooms fine but a bit dated. Needs renovation. Everything such as towels, carpet, etc are dated and not particularly nice.

“good value, more apartment than hotel...” I was in Seattle for work and wanted to find a good value compared to the expensive conference hotels downtown. The Marqueen provides good value and is more of a European style hotel, except the rooms are actually more like large studio apartments including a kitchenette, large bath and walk-in closet. The bed and linens were comfortable and the hotel is located in lower Queen Anne in close proximity to some great bars and restaurants, but it is not walking distance to downtown and public transportation options are limited. There is a great coffee shop attached to the hotel and but no restaurant -- no need in this area of the city. This hotel is for a particular type of client. If you are looking for a Sheraton or Holiday Inn, this is not your type of place. If you want a friendly and home-like atmosphere with lots of room to rest your weary body -- then this is your place. PS Noticed no particular musty smells in the lobby or the room and I am usually VERY sensitive to these things.

“A little gem” Booked hotel on hotwire....was pleasantly surprised by its charm...helpful staff...computer in lobby...parking at 11dollars per night...lovely room just off outdoor breakfast terrace...hotel had hot tub and sun loungers on terrace.. hotel was 40mins walk to farmers market and 30 min walk to Beverly Mall and 35 min walk to rodeo drive... A great base but you do need a car..... Breakfast is served on the first floor restaurant with the option of eating indoors or outdoors, and included waffles, eggs, coffee, tea, breads, bagels, cereals..... Internet access was free also....

“Excellent hotel, good value for money” Stayed here for three nights, 16 to 18 October. Great location,easy walking distance to main attractions, Beale Street etc, but quiet. Staff were very helpful and pleasant. We ate breakfast in the bistro each day, didn't seem too expensive and staff were obliging in fixing suitable food to meet our vegetarian needs. The room was a good size, lots of storage space so we could properly unpack. Great shower. Free wifi though not the most powerful, fridge didn't work as others have complained,but this didn't affect our stay. Free guest laundry was an unexpected bonus. Enjoyed our stay here!

“Loved it” We stayed here for 4 nights on a long weekend break in NYC. We have been to the city on several occasions and this is the best hotel we've stayed in in terms of location, value for money and most of all service. The location is fantastic - so many great bars, restaurants and shopping in the area with a subway station right at the end of the street to take you pretty much anywhere you want to go in the city. We had a one bed suite on the 3rd floor which we really liked. Great air con which we needed - it was so hot in the city while we were there, a really comfortable bed and a compact but perfectly adequate bathroom. We enjoyed the breakfast and the note of things to do each day that arrived under our door. The free wifi was also great - we had our own laptop so didn't need to use the business centre. The thing that really made this place stand out though was the staff. From the moment we arrived we were welcomed like long lost relatives - everyone was charming and friendly and nothing was too much trouble. Overall we had a great time and I'm sure we'll be back when we next return to NYC

“bello ma stile particolare” Lo stile W è molto particolare. Personalmente preferisco un stile più classico per un albergo. Cosa non mi è piaciuto al W Boston ? Tanti piccoli dettagli (vedete rece precedente di Giovanni R nella quale mi ritrovo) : nel bagno, davanti al lavandino, una sola luce sulla destra (con problema per farsi la barba sul lato sinistra), separazione trasparente tra il bagno e la camera, sistema di ascensione delle luci complicato, sistema di aria condizionata che non funzionava (ho dovuto lamentarmi diverse volte perché era impossibile spegnerlo), poca dotazione di sapone liquido,.... Rimane comunque un bellissimo albergo, con stanze accoglienti. Ben situato in pieno centro di Boston.

“Top Notch Hotel--Recommended” I just completed a stay here for business. This hotel has much to recommend it--convenient location (a block and a half from the Metro), courteous, professional staff, comfortable rooms. I usually don't stay in places quite this elegant when in DC on business, so this was a nice treat. Special touches include luxurious sheets on the bed, fine toiletries, and wide flat screen TV. All in all, a pleasant stay.

“Tiny Rooms, Great Location” Stayed here as part of a package we booked on Travelocity - I can see now why we got such a great deal. Hotel Union Square is blessed with great location, a very friendly staff and nice amenities. That was pretty much it. The room was beyond tiny - the bathroom sink was right next to the bed, which took up the entire room. It was unseasonably warm that weekend in San Francisco, a fact made even more apparent by the lack of air conditioning in our hotel! Sorry, but for 200 a night in the United States, one should at least get AC. Overall, the central location made it easier to overlook these flaws, but this hotel definitely slides in just over the average threshold.

“Faded and tired” We travelled across the USA on a tour organised by Great Rail Journeys of York between the 7th and 27th October 2009. We had 3 nights in New York at the Holiday Inn Midtown. We thought this was a hotel in big need of refurbishment – the decor was dark (greens, deep reds and browns) and faded and tired looking. While we were there a large number of new mattresses were being delivered! Our room was clean and was adequately serviced. The bathroom was ‘old fashioned’ with extensive use of plastics in the bathroom and with an erratic shower but both queen sized beds were comfortable and gave us a good nights sleep. TV reception was poor and we could clearly hear the family next door. There was no in-room safe. We didn’t eat in the hotel and the Pool was closed for the season. The concierge was helpful but on arrival it took the staff over an hour to deliver our luggage to the room.

“Best bed I've ever slept in. Ever.” I only stayed here for one night on my way somewhere else. So I was jetlagged and basically went straight to bed. And WHAT a bed. It's like sleeping on a cloud of happiness. This is the reason I'd go back. But the reasons I wouldn't. The room was smallish, (not as big as The Standard but bigger than the Soho Grand - and by the way when is someone going to make a website telling us the exact sizes of manhattan hotel rooms? it's needed...) The staff seemed nice enough. The bar downstairs is pretty hot right now - I was too shattered to even consider it. The reception area is extremely charming, with books everywhere. Jetlag sent me to bed at 8pm, then the noise from the bar woke me at 9pm. (The room was on the 3rd floor.) I rang reception and after some umming and awwing they transferred me to the 5th floor. Is that too princessy? Hey ho.

“Comfortable accommodations” I stayed at the Park South Hotel for two nights during the Memorial Day weekend and had a pleasant experience. As others have noted, my room on the eight floor was small but comfortably furnished, with bed linens, towels, bathrobe all of good quality. The bed was also quite comfortable, and the free Wi-Fi and morning newspaper a plus. (The only negative was a non-functioning mini-fridge, which would have been handy if I could have figured out how to plug it in or turn it on; I'd have tried to do so if I had stayed more than a couple of nights.) Continental breakfast was basic but well-stocked with essentials such as dry cereals, fresh bagels and muffins, some fruits, yogurt, sliced ham and chesse, cereal bars and juices (coffee was a bit weak, however.) I didn't dine at the hotel's Black Duck restaurant, but did have a nightcap while listening to a jazz trio after the theater on Friday night. The hotel is well situated in the Murray Hill/Flatiron district, which I enjoyed exploring; a highlight was Madison Square Park, a total gem with a dog run, sculpture lawn, cafe tables and benches, etc. about 5-6 blocks from the hotel. I also enjoyed a tapas dinner at nearby Pamplona restaurant, which was surprisingly empty on a Saturday (perhaps due to the holiday weekend). The #6 subway is a mere half-block away, but I chose to walk for most of my excursions as the hotel is in such a convenient location. Overall, I think the Park South is good value for the money and I'd certainly consider staying there again.

“Good budget option for downtown” OK, I'm tired of some of the finicky reviews of this place. It's a Quality Inn, for Pete's sake. Don't expect the Ritz. It's a perfectly fine 2* hotel. I was there for UW commencement and the city was busy, so this was the best I could do. I got a rate of $95 on Quikbook, and that was the best I could find ANYWHERE for this or any other decent property in downtown. When I arrived, I asked for two beds. The clerk was knowledgeable and efficient, and said she had only one left, but the rate would be $99. No problem. Still a deal for these dates. The lobby had a kind of Northwest lodge feel, with stone walls and floor. There was free coffee available and limited free newspapers. The elevator was kind of creaky and battered, and the guest room hallways were pretty shabby, but the room itself was spotless. Event the edges of the carpet seemed vacuumed, something I often don't see in 4* hotels. It had a beamed ceiling, again with the lodge feeling, and a microwave and mini-fridge. Plenty of room. Free wireless internet (although sometimes a weak signal). No problems with noise. The free breakfast was pretty abundant, although the breakfast room was crowded. There were signs about not taking away food, but my sister brought me stuff anyhow. No big deal. So I was perfectly satisfied. There's FREE parking! Some is in a lot alongside the street (Aurora), but there's also a hard-to-find garage. Go behind the hotel and completely around the block to the other side. You'll see a small Quality Inn sign over the entrance. You enter with your room key, so access is completely controlled. The elevator will take you all the way to the guest floors. I'd say the elevator was the biggest problem here: it was slow, old, creaky, and ugly. Otherwise, everything was fine. They even have a nice indoor pool off the lobby. The location was good. It's not in the thick of downtown, but DT is very accessible in a few minutes walk. If you exit the hotel and go right down Denny Way, there's an area with cafes and restaurants, and further down is the Space Needle food court. There's also a McDonalds near the Space Needle. If you go a few blocks north on Denny Way, there's a Whole Foods Market. And if you're in a hurry, there's a convenience store/gas station on the corner of Denny and Aurora, about 2 minutes walk. So I would not be afraid to stay here. I hope this hotel will move up in the rankings.

“Great Regency Club lounge, access to the Sporting Club, close to Torrey Pines” Located next to Hwy 5, the hotel is convenient to access La Jolla, Torrey Pines Reserve, beaches and is close to the Whole Foods, Peets Coffee, etc. Guests also have access to the Sporting Club for about 10$ a visit (the prices on Hyatt concierge website are outdated) which is an independent high-end gym as well as free pool. Since we had access to the 16th floor club lounge, we found that to be one of the best features of our stay, Recently re-modelled the lounge offered an impressive aray of food, snacks, and their coffee was excellent. The staff are very personable and helpful. The lounge also has two computers with huge monitors, if you do not have T-mobile hotspot access on your laptop.

“Immaculate, lovely, strong customer service, best patio bar in the District” In June, I stayed at the Sofitel for a multi-day Board meeting. My stay lasted three nights. Location: Excellent - right on the corner of 15th and H Streets NW. The McPherson Square Metro stop is right around the corner, and cabs are abundant. In addition, a walk to Metro Center is only 5-10 minutes (depending upon your pace) where there's shopping and another metro stop. Service: Excellent. As expected, bell staff were at the main door available to help with cabs and luggage. The concierge desk is directly inside the front doors, which is very handy. The staff speak (at minimum) both English and French, plus I heard staff speaking Spanish to guests. Front desk staff, servers, housekeeping. . .everyone was well-trained and attentive. Ambiance of the lobby, bar, & restaurant: Excellent. The hotel is a classic and the Sofitel chain has kept it updated. The bar has many comfortable seats and done in dark browns and reds. The restaurant is bright, cheerful and sophisticated. Patio Bar: The best in the district. It sits on the southwest corner of the block so there's no afternoon sun to blind you. They have large umbrellas set up, high tables & stools, as well as cushioned rattan sofas and chairs. You can eat outside, have a drink - it's a wonderful setting. Rooms: Immaculate, well-appointed, comfortable, and quiet. Exactly what you need in a sleeping room. Overall, this is my favorite hotel to stay in when in DC. I highly recommend it.

“Unfortunate stay” Reservaion made on booking.com for 5 nights for a one bedroom suite for e nordhausen. Initially was a problem because my passport says nordhausen. Couldn't believe that. Room was on 43rd floor. Black ac and heating vents, carpet sticky, sofa bed not sleepable and had dirty sheets, had to put a towel underneath door because too noisy from air whipping through halls. Thank goodness i brought two comforters for the couch to make a bed for my daughter. We also booked a towncar for the airport via the concierge and it didn't show up. Beds uncomfortable. Housekeeping kept putting my toothbrushes back in bathroom even though i keep them out. Why? Guess it bothered her. Room service was fine and waiters nice even though they were busy. A bit pricey though. Internet doesn't work unless you order premium at $18 and for each device. All this experience for 529/night. If i hadn't have booked a nonrefundable rate i would have been outta there.

“Good location for exploring the sites” Just returned from a 2 night (thurs/Fri.) stay at the willard intercontinental... I went with my wife and 4 year old son, and it was a great place to explore Washington DC from. It's only 1 block from the White House, and 2-3 blocks from the start of the massive National Mall and all of its attractions. With my wife pregnant, it was close as we could possibly stay to the sites. We got a "cherry blossom" package, which made the rooms about $320 each, including our choice of breakfast or parking each day. Since parking is only $28 a day, we picked the breakfast. Each breakfast bill was about $50 total, so this worked out in our favor. Our room, #1114, was a king size bed with plenty of extra room for our son's roll-away bed, which was also complimentary. Along with the package, they provided my son a little briefcase that had enough crayons, paints,etc. to keep him busy at meal times. Some chocolate covered cherries are provided as well... The lobby is fantastic, and the hotel appears to be well run. The food was more than adequate as well. When we return to Washington, we will stay there again.

“High Expectations Met” Stayed over the weekend and found the location and hotel met all my expectations. Breakfast at the Jockey Club was expensive but worth it with excellent food and service in a great elegant setting. Had drinks in the bar both evenings and found the fire, snacks and service to be first rate. While the Jockey Club breakfast was around $50 drinks in the bar were less than those we had at any other location in the city. The location is great with the subway a block and a half away and dinning spots and two interesting museums within a block of the hotel. The hotel Gym was also quite nice and made me feel better about the large breakfast I consumed every morning. Our room was a decent size with a fairly large bathroom. The bed was very comfortable and while we had a connecting room we did not have any of the noise problems some others have mentioned. I can see how a room without connecting doors would be less prone to noise but only once heard anything from our neighbors and that just enough to let us know that they were there. I found the staff very helpful and plan to make this hotel my destination the next time I am in the nations capital.

“Beautiful hotel almost in the shadow of the airport!” This is a great hotel with comfortable, quiet rooms and (most amazing!) free parking right by the airport! They offer a free airport shuttle for travelers but it's also a convenient hotel for local business travel between Wilmington, King of Prussia and Philadelphia. Convenient to the new ballparks and with all the amenities, including a great concierge lounge.

“Nice, but not my first choice for DC hotels” I stayed at the Washington Hilton for a meeting held across the street; we had a steeply discounted rate. I generally dislike large conference-oriented hotels, and this was no exception, although it is a step above other similar hotels. The room was comfortable if bland. They charge an arm and a leg for internet access (as is typical for conference hotels-- one reason for my disdain). You are likely to have to walk a 1/4 mile from the elevator to your room. The restaurant has decent, if expensive, American food; presentation was nice, but I did not feel it was good value. Room service breakfast was good, abundant (2 types of meat with eggs and toast) and in line with what other hotels charge (which is to say expensive), but not a bad value. There are several bars in the hotel, which is nice for meeting up with colleagues after work. The fitness center was outstanding-- it is actually a club you can join even if not staying at the hotel. Overall, the experience is comfortable yet bland, sterile, and impersonal. The neighborhood is nice, but there are more appealing boutique hotels nearby.

“Not bad, a little banged up, could be cleaner” I used Marriott points for a last minute stay here as I decided to go to a Phillies game. We arrived about 2PM or so and were promptly and pleasantly checked in. I was recognized with my Marriott status, which for this year, I think is only the 2nd time. Got an accessible room with 2 beds as requested. The room was fine and served it's purpose. It wasn't filthy-just little detail things such as a shoe print on the wall, finger prints on the glass over the pictures, and make-up finger prints on the bathroom door. Not gross, but still not nice. I wiped everything with Lysol wipes as usual. Didn't eat in the htotel this time-instead drove about 1-2 miles to a Subway for sandwiches. The A/C actually worked and wasn't overly noisy. TV reception was good, but the game wasn't on so mom couldn't look for me! TVs are NOT HD-not even the newer, big flat screens. Internet (wired only in rooms) is free, but NOT super fast. I had been granted a late checkout by the Operations manager shortly after check in...but no one told the AM crew (and the gal was rather rude until she noticed my status), no one told housekeeping so they knocked on the door, and I specifically asked to get my key extended but it stopped working. That entire situation was very annoying..... The hotel has a 24 hour shuttle and is close to a Ruby Tuesday, as well as offering nightly dinner service (or room service). I asked for a fridge, had to call again, but it did show up. The hotel was quiet-only heard some plane noise and virtually nothing from the hall or the connecting room. (For some reason, most accessible rooms in Marriotts are connecting..) There is security at night, free parking and overall seems to be fairly safe. I would consider staying again, provided they clean up and the few staffers who were NOT nice get their acts together. Fairly easy access to I-95 and there are several other hotels nearby. All in all, if you just want to lay your head someplace, the CY is fine.....

“Huge rooms, location isn't the greatest” Stayed here for one night after a long trip through colorado, before I left for the airport. Extremely friendly staff... the rooms are HUGE, my room was literally bigger than my first apartment, had never fridge and dishwasher, plus a 2 burner stove and microwave. Also had utensils, glasses, bowls, pots and pans, etc. Bathroom has a shower, not a tub, but most of us don't use the tub in a hotel anyway. Bed was comfy. The TV was an older model tube TV with built in DVD/VHS players. The remote was hard to work, but you got lots of stations. The room came with a free drink at night, and free breakfast in the morning, which was nice! The airport shuttle was on time, and the driver was friendly. One note, the shuttle also stops at their sister property, the Microtel, before it gets to the airport. Shuttles leave hourly, it's a 10 person van. You have to sign up ahead of time for it, don't forget. The location of the hotel was good if you're looking for something literally right off the highway, and you have a car. Not much else within walking distance, there's a mcdonalds next door, and gas stations/7-elevens within walking distance. We also ate at Ajuua's mexican restaurant across the street, and it was good. But other than that, it's mostly hispanic-themed strip malls with pawn shops, western unions, burrito places, etc. I never felt unsafe, but if you're not Latino, you might not feel at home going for a jog around the neighborhood. I felt totally safe, but also totally out of my element. Again, if you're looking for a HUGE room at a great price and convenient highway access, I would recommend this place.

“classy retreat” we stayed with our toddler in a harbor view room at the ritz carlton last weekend and felt very well looked after. the welcome - a speedy check-in and chilled champagne for us and an adorable teddy bear for our son - set the tone. we had a standard room which was spacious, well-appointed and in a good state of upkeep - no cracks, chips or 80s furniture hangovers. the bathroom was spacious and so nice to see bulgari white tea toiletries - appropriate brand for an urban luxury hotel. housekeeping were fantastic - a crib was in the room when we arrived made up as requested, and when our son was sick late at night, they silently appeared without fuss, cleared up kiddy vomit from the carpet and crib, moved in a fresh crib and sheets, and left him in peace. we booked a really terrific babysitter upon a recommendation from the hotel - the service was not cheap at $27 per hour plus additions, but for peace of mind, well worth it. my only quibbles, and these were very irritating, were a) that the concierge CONSTANTLY put us on hold whenever we called for help - this is so rude - and b) the bellman who took our luggage down to the lobby hung around for a tip and told us that he probably would not be around when we returned to collect the luggage mid afternoon - yet when we returned at our appointed time, to our surprise there he was. it's disappointing to see service transgressions at such a terrific hotel.

“It Doesn't Get Any Better” I travel extensively and am known as having very exacting standards... so with that as backdrop, I can't say enough good things about my experience at the Four Seasons in D.C. From the moment I drove up, the visit was wonderful. It was a busy time but the staff all knew my name in about 2 minutes and all went out of their way to make my visit pleasant. My room was amaziing.. beautifully appointed, great linens, bathroom, amenities. I was traveling for a client and got their corporate rate but I arrived here after staying for the same client at two Hyatt Regency"s: Houston and Baltimore - absolutely no contest! The one negative - I dont' think their bar/ounge is all that atttractive - just not of the elegance I would expect at this level of hotel.

“Another great Sofitel in a great location....” All I can say is that this stay was better than expected. Nothing at all to fault and the location was fantastic. If going to Washington DC, you must really consider this hotel as your base. One thing just came to mind - my A-Club level (GOLD) really wasn't acknowledged nor was I given any of my normal benefits. Loyalty should be rewarded or at least mentioned. That's all. I must have been too tired from travelling to remember :)

“Great location, good amenities” Stayed at Mariott Copley Place on business. The room was comfortable and clean - the lobby and bar areas well appointed. Connected to both Copley Place and the Prudential - so able to walk around and shop. There are also restaurants that you can get to by walking through the maze of the mall areas, which isnt the most unique way to go - but is a great choice for a female business traveler like me who always has personal safety in mind. Nice lounge area - sports bar with big screens for watching sports. Starbucks on site. Wireless internet is a charge here - even in the lobby. This location is excellent - close to Newbury Street - the T and other back bay locations. Concierge lounge well stocked for both evening drinks and dessert, as well as breakfast in the morning. Although the rooms and decor are really nothing special in terms of luxury, I would stay here again, especially if traveling for business and needed this location as a base.

“Wonderful Stay in Austin” Weekend stay (Aug. 17-19, 2007) with wife, and 3 year-old daughter. Greeted very warmly by Jennifer at check-in, great pool area, and delicious breakfast buffet (incl. w/ stay). Room was very large w/ king bed, seperate living area (sleeper sofa), and reclining chair, refrigetor, two-burner stove, dishwasher, plates, glasses, utensils, etc. Large vanity area and bathroom. Hotel very close to Arboretum shopping and dining within 1/2 mile. Downtown Austin is only 10 min. via MOPAC expressway. Round Rock Premium Outlets / IKEA store 15 min. away. Really enjoyed the comfort and joy of have a large room (suite). Lovely grounds and beautifully landscaped. Executive room a little small, but adequate. No problems with this stay. Noticed that hotel is replacing carpeting in some of rooms, so possibly refurbishing the hotel.

“Basic is an understatment” Yeah, so... This hotel... I'm not sure how Holiday Inn can really put its name to it (even as an "Express"). Poorly furnished rooms, a breakfast that's frankly a joke (if I found a bagel that wasn't solid and dry I was doing well), and it felt like being in a prison camp. On the plus point, it's quiet, but that's about it. The location is near nothing useful at all, a little over 5 minutes' walk to the VTA stop. The WiFi barely worked. It's acceptable, but there must be something better in a good location in San Jose.

“Nice stay in a great location” Stayed three nights in a junior suite. Prior to arrival, Margaret at the front desk was wonderful with reinstating my accommodations when Starwood's customer service messed up my reservation. Check in was a breeze. You do have to walk through Knave, the hotel bar, if you enter from 57th street, but if you take the 56th street entrance you go right to the front desk. The lobby area was always bustling during our stay, but it was quiet up on our floor. My ten year old loved the cartoons in the elevator and the roof top pool. The views from both the pool and attached outdoor sun deck are beautiful. Our junior suite was very spacious and both the bedroom bed and the sofa bed were comfortable. I'm a light sleeper, but was not disturbed by outdoor or hotel sounds during my stay. We had drinks and coffee at Knave. The room is beautiful and the service was good. We ate at the Burger Joint twice and it was delicious and reasonable. The location is close to multiple subway stops and just two blocks from Central Park. It was easy walking to Rockfeller Center, MoMA, Times Square, Empire State Building, and the musuems at Central Park, but I am quite a walker. If you don't walk as much, it is good to know the subway is close by. We had great meals nearby at Rue 57, just about half a block from the hotel at 57th and 6th and also at Bouchon Bakery in the Time Warner Center. I would stay here again because I really liked the location.

“Cheapest prices are on the hotels website.” Loved the hotel, but my wife thought the decor was a little loud. Very "trendy". Room was immaculate, large (double queen). Free internet if you join their club (also free to join). Staff was courteous and helpful. Nice neighborhood for shopping, and within walking distance of museums. We booked the room on priceline. Within a few hours, i discovered that the rooms quoted on the website were actually cheaper. Priceline refused to refund our money, and did not honor their lowest price guarantee. They claimed that the room we booked was for two queen beds, and the room on the Hotels website was for one queen bed. When I asked for a refund, stating that I only booked the room 2 hours ago, they refused, saying they would still charge me over $200, even though their website claims no fees for cancellation. Staff at the hotel informed me that the hotel website has the cheapest prices that can be found online. Go their first, and dont be fooled by misleading priceline marketing. Hotel also has a nintendo Wii in the lobby.

“Location ideal, family friendly” You can't beat the location with the Metra stop outside the front door. Use public transportation. It's easy and locals are friendly. If you are comfortable walking, Michigan Avenue is close and it's a nice walk up the ave. We hopped on the bus to the Adler Planetarium, the Shedd Aquarium and Field Museum from Michigan Avenue, on another day took the Metra to a few blocks near The Sears (Willis) tower went to see the Sky Deck and picked up the bus across the street from it back to Michigan avenue. Another bonus: a lot of restaurant options within walking distance too many to mention but we enjoyed Maggianos they have a kids menu and our daughter who is picky loves it. Final location plus: a grocery across the street. This was fantastic for us, since we don't mind picking up a few items/ snacks to eat in the room including fresh fruit. The rooms have a mini fridge and a microwave. I cranked the temp to max and I filled the ice bucket and put it in there thinking the fridge wouldnt keep anything cold. After 36 hours the ice hadn't melted, in fact our soda had ice crystals in it. A great first for me!!! Service was great, always accommodated our needs. One thing: I will say I'm picky about hotel bathrooms, and this one could have been cleaner, most folks would have been ok with it. And I find more hotels these days must not vaccum every time. We found some pharmaceutical on the floor. Ick. Pool was small and crowded with kids. Over-chlorinated for me. But our daughter enjoyed it fir the most part. Stay here for the location and the room features. For $135 AAA rate we thought it was slightly above average. Remember you are paying for location.

“Great location; very young vibe” The hotel is in a wonderful location. Easy walking distance to bars, shopping, and great restaurants (try La Condesa next door--you won't regret it). However, the hotel is crawing with 20-somethings and is a bit worsened by the fact that a non-hotel guest can purchase a $20 pool pass to Wet (the hotel's pool). While the amenities are fantastic at the hotel, the pool was littered with side way hat wearing, graphic tee sporting, and loud talking 20 year olds. For some this may be great, but was a bit much to handle for me. Overall, the staff was very accomodating; however, the pool staff is short and you will wait a while for a drink or food. Pros: -Great Location -Clean, spacious, night life spot -Wonderful amenities -Staff is willing and able to help. Very friendly Cons: -Young is an understatement (if you have a family or are a couple: head down to Four Seasons) -On weekend nights, this hotel lobby becomes a bit of a hot spot for a very young crowd - Pool gets crowded. Get there early and just be prepared for large, young groups

“Another stay, this one not quite perfect but still very good” I stayed at the Doubletree again this week. Was able to park right near the door, which was nice. The desk was crowded and uncharacteristically disorganized. It got sorted out and I was given a nice warm cookie and a room overlooking the river. This room seemed a bit more tired than some of the ones in which I have stayed, so maybe they are redoing some and have not gotten to others. For example, the phone in the living room was old looking, had a frayed line and kept disconnecting. This did not prompt an offer to swap out a new phone, and since I just used the other one, did not push it. Before, though, it always has seemed to me that the staff was more proactive. My room service came as promised and was good. Like all room service it was expensive. Aside from the hotel retaurants, you are fairly well isolated unless you want to take a shuttle or drive somewhere, and it was late, dark and cold. The Honors continental breakfast was good. The servers were busy conversing, so I got my own mug, and then had to take a spoon off another table, too. This is not the norm. The food was good and I am always grateful for the free wifi and included breakfast. While some of the little details were lacking, this is still a fine hotel, well-located off the Mass Pike and close to Cambridge and Boston.

“OK for a business trip” I have stayed here a number of times for work. They are making updates. The first one is the workout room. It is really above par for a hotel. The rooms are still a bit worn. However, I am a Hilton Honors Gold member so I get the best rooms. Before I was Gold the rooms were hit or miss. The front desk staff is really nice. They try. The buffet in the morning is also above par for a hotel buffet. There too the staff tries to make it good. My only big complaint in the wireless network. If you are in a room at the end of the halls it can be slower than if you are in a room by the elevator. The beds are clean and of high quality. It can be difficult to get to if you don't know exactly where to go. The road in front of the hotel is one way. If you can get a good rate and need to do business in the area this is a good place.

“Nice, but don't face the parking lot” Hotel is elegant and with the right discount, a pretty good value. I stayed one night for business. Had drinks in the lobby and room service. All were very good. The lobby is beautiful. The room was adequate, but it was all I need for one night. Two double beds--not queens which seemed lame. I had a room facing the entry where cars pull in and out. It wasn't terrible, but pretty loud both in the evening and early in the am. Just ask for a room facing the quiet courtyard.

“Very Good Value, Good Location for Weekend Vacationers” Very good hotel for a weekend in Chicago especially if arriving by train. Within walking distance of Union Station. Rooms are clean and comfortable with all amenities. Some may have a view-ours didn't but that was ok. Nice to have unlimited free bottled water, Internet and access to public computers in Business Center. Within walking distance to theater district and many sightseeing attractions and a variety (both price and type) of restaurants. River North area and Mag. Mile may require a cab ride or public transporation for many people. Book a couple weeks in advance if possible for special rates.

“Excellent in every way!” Looked here before booking, and decided based on the rate and the good reviews. I wated to stay within walking distance to Bank of America staduim, and the Nascar hall of fame and this was close to both and had the best rates that weekend. I was not disappointed! I arrived and was welcomed warmly by staff. I was given my room key, told about the market and directed to my room. I walked into a very clean room which was nicely appointed. I was at first a little worried about the room window which faced the pool and thought it might be noisy. The room was in fact, extremely quiet. When the curtains were closed, the room was also very dark, which is nice for light sleepers. The room featured free internet, and had a decent tv channel selection. The bathroom and sink areas were spotless, and I couldn't find one missed spot. (as a bit of a joke, I even ran my finger over the top of the picture frame to find dust. there wasn't any!) My first night I ordered Ruth's Chris which can be billed to the room which is convienent for tired travellers. It only took 20 minutes too! The bed was extremely comfortable, and very clean. Extra pillows could be found inside the drawers if needed. The work desk had multiple outlets for power, which is handy for phones, laptops, ect and the chair was excellent and looked new. Housekeeping was great as well, friendly, and did a great job cleaning each day. I also did like the coffee maker, although heavy coffee drinkers might need more than one cup! I did also dine at the Bistro after the game. After being rained on, a nice hot bowl of soup and a salad hit the spot. Food was good, and service was excellent. The Market also had anything and everything you could need while away from home as well, from food and drink, to travel needs and medicine/bath needs. A bit pricey, but extremely convienent and in line with any other hotel. Since I like to give a complete picture, here are a few minor beefs. When reserving online I asked for foam pillows but did not get them. My advice would be if you are picky or have a special request make it at the front desk, not online. Also, the bathroom is much smaller than it appears online, but the room was so nice and roomy I can understand why. It was still very nice. Also, parking is charged to the room every night, and if you are parking on a weekend be wary as the lot was full on saturday. I had a compact and luckily found one last spot, but the suv behind me wasn't so lucky. Just something to be aware of. Also, the Tv channels were temperamental. The local channels seemed to be iffy, and FOX never worked once in 3 days. Also, other channels seemed to just disappear at times. I am guessing that it was satellite and the weather was causing issues. As a reviewer I felt like I had to have some negatives but this hotel was outstanding. I got a great clean room, great service, and a great location for a price that was lower than the nearby competitors. I would have no problem staying here again.

“Not a "vacation" hotel, but otherwise satisfied” We stayed here for 4 nights. The hotel is at 51st Street directly off of I-10. About a 5 minute drive to Maryvale for Spring Training...15-20 minutes for downtown, golf & other stadiums. Pretty easy to get to/from the airport from here. Keep in mind, this is not a hotel to stay at if you like to hang out at the hotel. The rooms were nicely remodeled and were fine for sleeping. Just come with the realization that there is nothing else to do at the hotel or even within walking distance. While the service at the front desk was excellent, the service at the hotel lounge/bar was abysmal. It took 30-45 minutes to get a drink, the bartenders did not even know how to make basic drinks and they were out of several common things (including Grey Goose, amaretto, etc!) If you wanted anything other than a basic bottle of beer, good luck. This was really too bad as the lounge looks quite nice with TVs, a pool table and a dartboard. Most hotel guests will want to hang out in the bar/lounge...so I hope the Holiday Inn will seek improvements here.

“Nice hotel in Chinatown. Minus the food...” I checked into the hotel and got a pretty nice room with a view. The parking was a bit much, I think $50 a night, but hey this is SF. The rooms were quite and a nice size. The hotel is located in Chinatown so if you do not want Chinese food you need to walk a little ways to find something good. The second night I was there I decided to have a glass of wine and some pizza downstairs in the hotels restaurant. Nice area and all and they had a nice selection of wine. The pizza was good at first until I found a long hair in it! This is my biggest pet peeve and grossed me out like nothing else can. So in the end, if you want a nice room, this place isn't bad. Just do not eat the food. Stick to the wine.

“Tolles Hotel mit Spitzenservice im Financial District” Das Club Quarters San Francisco findet sich im Financial District in der Nähe der Transamerica Pyramid. Habe dort mit einem Freund zwei Nächte verbracht und kann das Hotel nur weiterempfehlen! Beim Check-In wusste man direkt Bescheid, dass ich per Mail ein Zimmer mit zwei Twin-Beds angefragt hatte, was trotz Buchung über Priceline kein Problem darstellte. Das Zimmer selbst ist zwar relativ klein, aber modern eingerichtet und absolut sauber. Auch die Betten waren klasse! Toll am Club Quarters ist insbesondere der Service: Es gibt kostenloses WLAN in allen Zimmern, zusätzlich stehen in der Lobby auch PCs mit Drucker, die jederzeit kostenlos genutzt werden können. Auf allen Fluren gibt es unbegrenzt kostenloses Wasser (Plastikflaschen zum selbst auffüllen) und in der Lobby zusätzlich jederzeit kostenlosen Kaffee und Zeitungen. Da wir uns auf einer Rundreise befunden haben, haben wir außerdem auch von der Laundy im Keller Gebrauch gemacht, in der man kostenlos waschen konnte. Alles in allem nur zu empfehlen!

“A great family hotel” We have a 3-year-old and 1-year-old, and we always like to stay at Hyatt Place because the rooms have a divider that helps the 1-year-old not realize we are sleeping in the same room! (If he saw us, he would never go to sleep!) This hotel is very pleasant and clean. The only thing I didn't like was that the "special hot breakfast item" on the buffet was oatmeal. That is pretty dull when there could be pancakes or biscuits, like I've had at other Hyatt Places. But the staff at this Hyatt Place is SO FRIENDLY and helpful, especially when I was dealing with a rambunctious toddler. Highly recommend.
“Best staff” Stayed here a night before flying out and the staff was great! Everyone was friendly and helpful. I would recommend this hotel to anyone coming to Columbus.

“Good location if you arrive/leave by train to/from Seattle... nothing else.” We stayed at the Courtyard Seattle Downtown for two nights from the 31st December to the 2nd January. It is located very close to the Amtrak station and easy to find. However, it’s far from the city centre and the main tourist attractions. The front desk staff was very friendly during the check-in and gave us helpful hints about Seattle. The room had a nice view of the Puget Sound and Bainbridge Island (despite the elevated motorway just in front) and was decently decorated. We were concerned about the noise since it was New Year’s Eve but did not notice any disturbances. The breakfast was somehow strange: we had a fixed amount of money we could spend in two ways - bread or pastry or cereals + yoghurt + drink (1) or eggs or oat meal + drink (2). If we spent more than the fixed amount, we would have to pay the remainder. We didn't enjoy the system and the food was also not very tasteful. When we checked out and asked for a taxi to take us to the airport, while waiting for the taxi outside the valet guy tried to convince us to go with in his "uncle’s" car (who would charge us the same as the taxi – $40). We obviously refused and were shocked because we did not expect this to happen in a Marriott. Above all, we had a great rate since we booked well in advance and thus the hotel showed a good ratio quality/price.

“Terrific non-chain-like Kimpton in the heart of Chicago” Traveling two or three times a month on business, I love hotels that don't look like hotels - and the Burnham is a typical Kimpton property in that regard. Conveniently located (although not in the heart of Michigan Ave hotel/shopping - closer to Grant Park) and decorated like the turn of the century building it clearly once was. Real doorknobs and keys, doors with frosted glass and early 20th century decor make this a wonderful change of pace hotel. Had a terrific meal in the hip downstairs restaurant and the staff was terrific - had me upgraded to a suite after a very late arrival from ORD. Would stay here as a leisure traveler - and that is the highest praise I can give a hotel!

“Very Good Hotel” had two rooms for two days with 4 kids. nice hotel, old hotel, really big, impressive and busy lobby/bar. made me want to hang out and i did. the service is top notch and the people working are all pros. the steak house was nice though they didnt seem to like a family of six walking in. but they were professional. had a filet, really good, and strip, not good at all. no fridge in room, bathrooms small, mostly clean, 10 layers of paint on everything. good beds, sheets pillows. very high quality furnishings. nice hotel.

“An okay small hotel” The La Quinta in Old Town is an okay hotel for budget travelers, but it wasn't my type of place. I wanted to try something different and stay in a historic area of town (but Old Town was too touristy for me.) It is clean, it provides free parking, a limited continental breakfast, and it is easily accessible to the highway. Other than that do not expect any thrills or frills with this hotel. It only provides your basic neccesities and nothing more. Pros: Free Breakfast Close proximity to the beach, highway, airport, downtown, zoo, and other attractions. It took me less than 15 minutes to get everywhere from this hotel. Free Parking Clean: the housekeeping was great! Nice Staff willing to please Rooms come with microwave & a small refrigerator Close proximity to Sports Arena Drive (there are plenty of restaurants, grocery stores, a Target, and other places Close proximity to Fashion Valley & Mission Valley Malls Close proximity to the Old Town trolley stop Cons: Rooms are way too small: I traveled with my husband and toddler and we felt castrophobic. So, if your traveling with a large family you may want to choose a suite type of hotel. Not enough storage space: the oversized dresser only had 2 drawers and the closet was very tiny Underground Parking Garage: you better have a compact car or know how to park a car in a tight space because coming in and out of that garage was a interesting Rooms facing the courtyard can be a little noisy because of people hanging out at the pool at night (Some nights it was very quiet while other nights it was quite noisy). However, your other choice is to get a room facing the highway. Breakfast could have been a little better Old Town is very congested, too touristy, and the sidewalks are very narrow. If your not into the touristy thing, eating at not so great restaurants, or shopping at nick nack stores, then downtown is a better location. I spent most of my time downtown and realized that I could have stayed down there without a car. It had more of a local feel to it and lots of great restaurants. Other than, that I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. It is just that it was not what I am accustomed to, but I will highly reccommend it if you are looking to save money, a clean place to lay your head. and a place that will allow you to save on travel time to and from places in San Diego.
“工事の音が我慢できれば・・・” WTCの跡地のすぐそばにたつホテル。地下鉄の駅も近く、ディルカウントモールのセンチュリー21もお隣でとても便利です。ただ、WTC跡地の工事が昼夜問わず続けられているので、少しうるさいです。それが我慢できれば価格も系列の中では安いほうですし、お得だと思います。

“A good quality Hilton” It is an older but very well maintained property with recently renovated rooms. The staff is friendly, and the location is good for access to the airport and downtown San Diego. Parking at $17 seems pretty high for the location, but overall this is a quality Hilton hotel.

“Just Like Home -- Because It Is!” I am a San Franciscan who has to live elsewhere because of my job. I come back as often as I can to visit family and friends, and have been staying at the Metro for many years now, instead of with family, because I like to have my privacy. This hotel is perfect for people like me who want to experience ordinary San Francisco living while being in The City. For me this means: airflow comes through windows not vents, no parking (who in their right mind wants to spend their time in San Francisco fighting with traffic? -- take the buses for heaven's sake), cosy rooms, friendly people, firm beds, The rooms are clean. The new ceiling fans are great! And it's lovely to be within walking distance of the Castro, the Duboce Triangle, the Haight, and Cole Valley, and on direct bus and streetcar lines to downtown, the Mission, the Sunset and Richmond districts, the Ocean, the Filmore, and Noe Valley. But the best thing about the hotel for me is what isn't there and seems to be at many of the hotels in the same price range: shouting hookers and drunks. As a woman traveling alone, I always feel safe at the Metro. I wish there were coffee makers in the rooms, but that is minor. You can get coffee three doors down or go to The Grind, a block and a half away, for terrific coffee and one of the best breakfasts in town.

“Best location” Stayed here just one night since our flight was cancelled due to Hurricane Irene. Chose this hotel because of it's location above the metro center metro stop. We had to return our rental car to Union Station and realized we could avoid the harsh elements outside by taking the Redline directly from there to the hotel. Totally convenient - totally dry! We also used the metro to get to the airport the next day. Typical Hyatt room - well appointed, nice, generic. Walking distance to Chinatown and the National Mall. We usually prefer smaller, boutique type hotels with free wi-fi and kitchenettes, but for sightseeing around the mall and convenience to the metro, you can't beat this location. Also walking distance to Megabus/Boltbus stop (for intercity travel). No need to rent a car if you stay here.

“Nothing special” My wife and I stayed 3 days on business/leisure. Pro's: Great Location! 3 blocks from 5th ave, across from Waldorf Very Friendly staff Free hershey kisses Nice bath products Cons: Small Small Small rooms Expensive Not enough outlets in room Crazy busy check in

“Terrific Hotel and Location” The Sofitel Water Tower Place is one of my favorite hotels in America. I probably spend an average of 15 nights per year there and have never been disappointed. The location is great - just one block from Michigan Avenue, Water Tower Place, and Two blocks from the high end fashion on Oak Street. Also easy walking distance to Gibson's, The Whiskey Bar, Level night club, Le Coloniale restaurant, and the really rowdy party district up at the end of Rush Street. You will not hear a sound once inside your room. The staff is very attentive without being pushy (I can cary my own bag, thank you). I am often surprised when the parking valet or one of the desk staff remember my name even when I haven't been to the hotel in several weeks. The lobby is spacious and modern and has a great vibe. A very international clientelle stay here. The rooms are well appointed, I believe they all now have flat screen HDTV. The feel is luxurious contemporary and the bed is perhaps the best anywhere. Just crawl under that big Frette comforter, pile up the pillows, and you'll never want to leave. Bathrooms are fantastic. Cream marble and blonde maple finishes. The best designed vanity mirror/light anywhere. Good shower pressure (some bathrooms on outside walls can take a long time to get hot water in winter months) and very nice bath product. All rooms are of a nice size. The upgrade to "executive" (or whatever they call it) gets you a larger work desk and small seating area. Most of these rooms also have a separate tub and shower. If you splurge on a suite, ask for a room ending in 01 or 08. The 01 rooms are on the triangular point of the hotel and have a nice living area separated from the bedroom. Each of these rooms is somewhat unique, as the corner of the building expands the higher up you go. The 08 rooms are even larger still and have an even larger bathroom with separate toilet room, shower, bath tub (no Jacuzzi) and lots of room to spread out. Unforttunately, over the years, many highrise buildings have been built around the hotel, and lake views are very limited. There are still some great views of the city. Le Bar downstairs is a very good spot for cocktails and often has great scenery no matter what your gender or orientation. You can also get dinner served here from Les Architects, the hotel restaurant. Les Architects has always been a good restaurant. However, they brought in a new chef aboout a year ago and the quality has improved significantly. Some VERY good food here. If you want to camp in the room without using room service, there is a Potash Bros. market just behind the hotel and a very nice wine and gourmet food store as well. If you have stayed at the Sofitel in Rosemont near O'Hare and were unimpressed - so was I. The Water Tower Place location is 100 times nicer. I also recommend The James hotel in this same general part of the city.

“Great New York institution ” This is a wonderful old institution. If you want to experience the real New York and feel like you are in New York, stay here. It may be overpriced, it may be a little old and clunky (and not as renovated as some hotels), but it has that old world charm that you just can't manufacture. And what a location (Park and 50th) and what a history (monarchs and presidents). All in all you can expect a comfortable, clean hotel with good service and good food. But that is not what the Waldorf is about--it is about a sense of history and its about the experience. Walking through the grand lobby or having a drink in one of the bars, or talking a stroll around Park and 5th Avenues in the early morning, or coming back at night and seeing a sea of gowns and tuxedos. Its a part of the world that is fast disapearing. If you want the utmost in luxory stay in the Towers (but you better have the utmost in pocket-book). Othewise don't expect the biggest, most beautiful room, or a private butler/conceriege at your door, or free champagne and cavier. If your room feels a little outdated (a little rust in the bathroom or curtains and wallper that need replacing) just remind yourself that you are the presence of greatness--that you are experiencing history. If you want the newest most renovated room on the block and the extra ameneties you can stay at the Palace or the Benjamin for the same price (I have stayed at both), but you won' get that same sense of presence and history. You wont get that I AM IN NEW YORK feeling that only a few hotels like the Waldorf (or the Plaza--which is now gone) or the St. Regis can provide.

“Not great, but not too bad!!” Just return from the Hotel Nikko this afternoon and can't wait to write this review. The hotel is not a bad hotel,but it's not that great at all, room was small (170 sqf?), so I upgraded to the deluxe King and it still small (250 sqf?). But it is clean and quite. My family and I visit San Francisco many times we stay in many of hotels, this hotel rooms are small (the other small hotel we stayed before it was Palace Hotel, but Palace are Old, Classic and Luxury same price I pay for Hotel Nikko)!! Other than that, we have a great time. The staff are nice, doorman always open door for every guest, and the hotel staff are always smile and greeted. The location is not bad at all, two blocks away from the MUNI and Bart, plus Cable Car. In the center of shopping area, if you love shopping, and don't want to carry your bags, this hotel is the one for you since you are not too far away from the shopping center. Many hotel around SF area, you really need to know what you will like to do when you planning your visit. Lots of hotel offer the good package, check them all out before you book them.

“Very nice hotel but slightly overpriced” The Four Seasons is a beautiful hotel with outsanding service, great rooms and arguably the best location in Washington. However, the public areas are small and it can be fiercely expensive, both for food and the rooms.

“Traditional hotel with pleasant staff” LA Athletic Club is conveniently located with an incredible fitness center, warm and welcoming staff with well appointed rooms. While the building is older, the rooms are big, comfortable and allow for a quiet night's sleep. Love the iHome to charge my phone!

“Outstanding Value - Awful Water Savers in Bathroom” This hotel is exceptionally clean. The entire hotel is VERY family and pet friendly. The food at breakfast is okay but not exceptional in fact it is always cool to cold but free is allowed to be cool to cold. The two worst attributes are the too-soft beds and the terribile water pressure in the shower. If I had traveled with a pair of pliars and a small flat blade screw driver I would have popped that water saver out of the shower head. Is it possible that Embassy Suites fails to understand that guests will use what ever volume of water is necessary to wash themselves? If there is no water saver in the shower head I am rinsed and done in 3 minutes. If there is a water saver I am rinsed and done in 15 minutes. I think that the math speaks for itself. Other than that, the room is terrific and the hotel is very close to everything I need to visit. I'll stay here again but with a pair of pliars the next time.

“Another Kimpton, another great stay . . .” When in NYC, I usually stay a little further north, however, for work purposes, it made it much more convenient for me to stay closer to Times Square. As I've said before, you know what you're getting with Kimpton Hotels. Clean rooms (that is a good size for NYC), as well as the freebies -- morning coffee & tea, happy hour 5-6 pm and Internet. The location is also VERY convenient if you're looking to be in the heart of Times Square and the staff was very helpful and friendly. There were a couple drawbacks: The noise from the street was a little loud. Maybe the windows could have been made a little more soundproof. The front desk/concierge never called to inform me that a package I was expecting arrived. I had to call to see if it had arrived and when I asked to have it brought to my room, I was informed that there was a $5 delivery charge. And as a side note, a colleague of mine who was in NYC the same time as me decided to stay at the Sanctuary hotel, which also has stellar reviews. She ended up moving to the Muse.

“Great hotel, not ideal for business” Staying at The Stoneleigh was a great experience from start to finish, and I have only very minor complaints. The hotel is in a great location and my room was clean and spacious (though I was upgraded from a standard to a deluxe king room when I arrived). My only complaints: there's no coffee maker in the room (is this a new trend? why?), so if you're a business traveler, that means ordering it via room service or going without coffee before your morning meeting. It's annoying, but not fatal. Also, I ended up ordering breakfast in my room both days (it was pretty good) because I was afraid that the sit-down breakfast service would take too long. My only other complaint is that the equipment in the fitness center was pretty inadequate and outdated. It certainly wasn't up to the standards of the rest of the hotel. Overall, this hotel was a great value (I think I paid a $199/night rack rate) for its price class.

“Perfect for a family visiting D.C.” We stayed four nights here in late June, and it was perfect for us (two adults, three kids ages 5, 9, 12). We had a 2-room corner Exec Suite with 2 Queens. There is a large bedroom with a closing door (not a divider or half-wall, but a real door!). There is a bathroom with tub/shower, toilet, and 2 sinks, plus another counter with a sink in the bedroom. The living area is huge, with a sofa/armchair area, a desk area, and a dining area. Plenty of room for the five of us to spread ourselves and our luggage out. There is a small bar-type sink in the dining room, plus a skinny closet with a small fridge and microwave. The room furnishings were decent, clean, and seemed recently updated. All the plumbing worked fine. I did check the mattresses for bedbugs, and all was well :) The two little ones stayed in one queen, my husband in the other, and our 12 yr old on the sofa bed in the living room. We used the dining table for our laptop (something like $12 daily for Wi-Fi), and the kids used it during some indoor "down" time coloring books, doing activity books, etc. Breakfast is complimentary daily, just down in the lobby. A couple of times we ate downstairs, a couple of times my husband and I went down and filled trays with cereals and fruit and milk, and brought it up to eat on the dining table in our room. Having the breakfast option is great--we eat and go! One downside to it is there is pretty much zero variety with the breakfast situation. It's the same thing every single morning. By the 4th morning we were pretty bored with it, but ate it anyway and got going on our day. The other bummer is the lack of fresh fruit! One day there was one mixing bowl of cut-up melon, hiding at the end of a food counter. Another day there was a bowl of oranges, or bananas. I was hoping for a Residence Inn-style variety of fruits daily--fruit salads, berry bowls, tropical fruit, etc. Oh well. There is an indoor pool, not too big. My husband took the kids down one day but they only stayed an hour--it was packed beyond belief with kids! Even my kids, who are never discouraged by a crowded pool, didn't want to stay because there was no room to swim or play whatsoever, and the noise was insane. Hotel itself is clean, with very friendly and quick service and help, and feels safe and pleasant. The neighborhood is safe and interesting, and just a quick walk to everything Dupont Circle has to offer. We never lacked for restaurants, coffee shops, shops, etc., and the Metro stop is right there as well (and wow, what an amazing ride down a 200' escalator!). Would highly recommend this to families.

“Great if you want to be on Capital Hill” I stayed here 2 nights for meetings on Capital Hill. The hotel is an easy walk to the House, Senate and Supreme Court. There are a few places around but this is not prime tourist real estate so if you aren't planning to visit the House and Senate I'd stay elsewhere to avoid getting in and out of cabs. The hotel itself is large. It is used for groups visiting D.C. to lobby Congress. When you enter you see lots of signs - insurance folks meeting this way, disease folks meeting that way. Be prepared for busy mornings as large groups head out for the Hill. The staff are very professional. The rooms were large enough and comfortable. My only complaint was that the walls are a bit thin. I could hear the folks in the next room and they weren't being loud. The area around the hotel varies. It was a sketchy area until recently. It is now in transition but I wouldn't want to walk the streets too much after sundown. Overall it met my purposes and I was pleased.

“Fantastic!” I've stayed at several spots near Copley Place and this is my new favorite. The staff was fantastic. There is a Starbucks in the lobby. They have some very nice suites available for upgrades. The beds and rooms were very comfortable and the hotel is connected to Copley Place...very convenient. I have no complaints about this hotel and will be staying here again on my next trip into Boston.

“B++” Very Nice hotel in Times Square. Huge, clean room. Convenient to theatres and shopping, and the parking garage is just around the corner. The lobby area isn't very comfy or inviting, but who has time to sit and relax in NYC? I am returning for another weekend this summer.

“Nice Property in a Nice Location” This is a nice hotel in a nice location. Fairmont properties are pretty universal in terms of their service and amenities which is a GOOD thing. Their beds and rooms are great! There is a Grill on the Alley attached to it which is a very nice perk of one wants to grab a nice meal. Love Fairmonts and always have.

“Simply the best” Just returned from a combined business trip and pleasure. This was my second stay and it was even better than I remembered. The buildings and rooms are to die for, but what is even better (besides the food) is the service. And it extends from the first moment you check in to the folks who are cleaning your room. I've been to many other 5 star hotels, but this one is truly special.

“Awesome Value, Doesn't Get Better than this!” The Drury is one of the best hotel chains hands down. What you would usually pay for in the big chain hotels like Marriott and Hilton you all get for free here! Free wireless, evening snacks and beverages, and a wonderful breakfast that is much more than the usual continental. Check in was efficient and friendly as were the housekeepers who always said a nice "hello." The room was quite spacious with a nice desk area, large closet and vanity area and large LCD flat planel TV. My bathroom also had a hot tub and a free standing shower. My only two complaints were that the room was quite cold and I couldn't get the temp back up and that the duvet on the bed was very thin, not like usual hotel covers (I had to fold them over to get warm). This hotel is right on the riverwalk, conveienent to many restaurants and shops. We went to a great steak place called the Salthouse, I highly recommend it!

“go to the Omni or the Hilton instead.....tired and "so so"” this place is a very tired marriott. as one of the older hotels in this area you can surely do better at the Omni (fab and great service) or the Hilton (nice, newer and right across the street from the convention center). We had breakfast one morning that was simply abyssmal... both in service and the food. I asked for toast, the server said she had to check to see if they had any (huh?) never came back, 45 minutes (i am not kidding) another server showed up with wheat toast (i guess there are no toast choices here) that was ice cold and not toasted on one side and burnt on the other. (go figure) When we tried to voice our dissatisfaction to manager, he simply shrugged his shoulders (huh X2?) The rooms reminded of a circus tent, though we had a nice view of the downtown. Our air con did not work even after repeated requests to fix it..... It was like staying in a swamp, all our clothes were wet and slimy as well as the sheets. ugh. The pool is nice, but very very small for the number of people staying there.,.... there is even a sign that says no reserving lounge chairs, so there must be a problem..... For the price, there are nicer places to stay. We were there for a convention and it was fine, sans soggy clothes, but next year we will stay elsewhere.
“great place” very nice clean rooms nice pool comfy beds enjoyed my stay.

“Expected way more--” We had never stayed at an Intercontinental before and had thought it was a better chain. We stayed one night. Good location in the Inner Harbor, but we hope this is not the best that Baltimore has to offer. We were first given a smoking room (we were not asked and forgot to specify) that smelled awful. In addition the furniture was in pretty bad condition. Upholstery, ripped and hanging off the bottom of a bench and the table veneer severely damaged. We were then moved to a smoke-free room, but it also had a damaged table, as can be seen in this picture. Overall we found the room kind of depressing. Maybe it was the color, maybe the bare walls or the arrangement of the furniture--not sure. Also, don't order a cappuccino in the restaurant-it is steamed milk with regular coffee. One of our pet peeves is thermostats that do not work. We could not get the room above 68 degrees( it was chilly and damp out) and finally called the maintenance and he said the heat was turned off because people at a party complained it was too hot. It never reached our desired temperature. The positives were the staff was very nice, and it was a very comfortable bed. Not sure I would stay here again. Needs some remodeling, first.

“Very nice and huge hotel” This is a massive hotel right downtown - it has a famous steakhouse in the lobby, nice bar, and remodeled gym. It's a bit pricy but its really big. You'll be fine o stay here or hold a huge conference.

“Great service!” Had a killer AAA deal directly through the hotel website which included breakfast and overnight parking. We had a double deluxe room and because the hotel was not full, we were able to check in at 8:00am (we took a red-eye from SLC) and we even got a late check-out. Breakfast was great at Ringo ( $25.00 per person to spend with the rate) specifically the attentive service and the yummy eggs benedict with chipotle hollandaise and prosciutto! Actually every employee that we encountered at the Alex always had a smile on their face and went out of their way to make each encounter a positive experience! Our room was adequately furnished, beds were super comfy, but the bathroom small with a TV embedded in the wall! The rainshower was also alittle tricky. But I did love the Frederic Fekkai products and the housekeeping staff was very generous with extras! The location was also great - just steps away from Grand Central Station, Times Square, the UN, 5th ave, etc. The lobby is very small and the hotel is very much a boutique sized hotel that is very understated. I would definitely stay at The Alex again, however they should provide free WI-FI!

“Higher floors give an awesome view, ask for a corner room or an odd number” I stayed here for a week, great welcoming staff. great food. Nice areas in walking distance. nice hotel and rooms are well equipped. hotel has valet parking that is a little costly, you can self park 100+ for 5 days. make sure you try the pulled pork quesadillas and the cheese carrot cake.

“Quiet, comfortable” I have stayed at this hotel a few times. Both times, i had a very nice comfortable quiet room. Everything was immaculate, the hotel also has a beautiful lobby and nice seating area to have drinks. The hotel also has a nice bar as well that overlooks Central Park with full wall glass which is nice as you sit and enjoy your drink. Of course, like any high end hotel, the prices are very high. During one of my stays, i did have an issue with what i was charged for vs. what i was offered. I was told i would have a voucher for food and free parking, but they tried to charge me for parking, i had to dispute it with american express and it was a bit of a pain. Eventually it was resolved in my favor, so i do not think about it anymore and I do stay there when i am in the city. if i had to pay that parking, i would have been pretty angry and would not have stayed anymore, but since it all worked out well, its not a factor in my decision to book here. I love the location, its close to midtown in that you can easily walk here from times square, but its also situated in a nicer more residential area, where you have easy access to central park ( across the street). The Essex House is a very nice hotel where all of the times i stayed, i had a restful sleep, clean and comfortable accomodations.

“Decent, business-oriented” I stay here frequently on business in the area. Serviceable, clean, good gym, always polite and receptive staff. Atrium can be noisy at times and most rooms are exposed to it. Best though not least expensive choice in the Arboretum area. Not close to downtown.

“Odd but convenient location, nicely appointed rooms, very comfortable” Location is central to china town, financial district, and the ferry terminal buildings with a short walk to each. Rooms were very nice, but watch out in the tub, the shower curtains were far too long (or the curtain rod is mounted too low) and i slipped and almost fell when I stepped on the 6" of wet curtain laying in the bottom of the tub and it slid. They added someone else's drink tab to ours in the hotel restaurant and didn't fix it, which was disappointing-but likely just a tired server close to the end of her shift.

“Easy access to LAX!” This location was a little hard to enter the property at night there was a lot of driving around to find entrance. (the main location I saw was chained up) The lobby area was beautiful, the pool was way worth the stay, and the room service was very well portion ed meals! Overall it was just ok, I think what took me by surprise was the $25 parking fee, plus the added internet fee... I would have chosen differently if I knew of all the OTHER charges, but again the pool does make up for it!

“I agree - one of Washington's best kept secrets - GREAT hotel” Excellent, excellent two night stay in February. This hotel is nearly perfect - great location, staff & rooms. Front desk staff and restaurant staff were very professional and responsive. The room is pretty large, great big bathroom, too. And everything is SPOTLESS. This is a great hotel in DC. Highly recommended. The only flaw I could see was that the carpet in my room was somewhat worn near the bathroom, but hardly noticeable. This is a fine hotel.

“Not Awful, Not Great!” I just returned from a 4-night stay at the Murray Hill East Suites, booked as a package deal through Priceline. We arrived early and were told that a room wasn't ready, but after sitting in the lobby for about 10 minutes, the lady at the check-in desk called me over to tell me they had one available. She was very sweet and helpful; there was another one that was not so friendly. The room itself was OK - it was straight out of the 80's in decor and the furniture was a bit worn around the edges, but it seemed clean. The door to the bathroom wouldn't close all the way, and the kitchenette oddly had a gas stove, but no microwave. Neither of the bedside lights worked, and I was told that they would send someone up to check them out, but it was never fixed during the entire stay. Free wifi was only available in the lobby, there was no business center, and I was told that they would not print boarding passes, which seemed strange since they had no computer there to print them ourselves!
