All in all, the stay was fine, but nothing special. The nearest subway is about 3 blocks away at Grand Central, and there are several shops nearby to pick up any food items you might need. The neighborhood is fairly quiet, but there is scaffolding over the front entrance right now, and there was some construction noise during the day, but only on the weekdays. I would consider staying again if the price was right, but there are several other budget-type hotels that I prefer over the Murray Hill East Suites.

“Nicely Updated” Location looks like it has recently been updated. Has a slightly contemporary ambiance both in the lobby and the rooms. Plenty of parking, easy access to the highway and the staff was very friendly. I would certainly stay at this location again.

“Lovely hotel, pet friendly, great location” Decided to take the cat away for the holiday weekend and Loews has a great pet policy and a very low fee ($25). I'd reserved on Cyber Monday for their special holiday rate. The hotel is in the old PSFS building right in Center City. We arrived around 10:30 AM on Christmas eve and were able to get right into our 7th floor, pet friendly King bed room. When you arrive with a pet, you're given a little bag with a 'placemat', some bowls and treats and a list of local groomers and vets (this would prove very handy!) There is also a pet Do Not Disturb sign for guests to use if they're in or out of the room-so that housekeeping knows when you're around so they can clean! Our room was a corner king-I'd have preferred to be up higher but since I was traveling with my little cat, we were on the pet floor, near the elevator which was fine! I didn't see other rooms but I believe that they may be somewhat different sizes and shapes. The PSFS building is an older, Art-Deco style so I'm not sure what they did when they converted the offices into rooms. The room also had 3 phones, a nice large, flat screen TV, small fridge, a couple robes, really nice LATHER toiletries and a view of neighboring buildings.You can also see into adjacent windows, so you should probably close the sheer curtains! The room was pretty quiet-I really couldn't hear much street noise, and only minimal hall noise, (and well, the dog barking in an adjacent room!) If you join the Loews YouFirst frequent guest program (which is free), you get free internet. Otherwise, it's $10.95 plus tax per day. The internet is WiFi in the hotel and it was pretty good speed. Also, there's a Keurig single cup coffee maker in the cabinet next to the TV-or a Starbucks across the street. This property is right across from the Reading Terminal Market and PA Convention Center. It's only a couple blocks from City Hall and there's easy access to all the sites in town! I ran over to the Market to get some stuff for lunches and snacks and came back to settle in to do nothing. I wasn't really hungry so I just ordered some good chicken soup from room service. All food and drinks are priced as should be expected in a big city hotel-not cheap, but not ridiculous. Actually my cocktail (the "With Love" Philadelphia drink-pretty good) was $8 which was about 2 bucks less than expected. On Christmas day, the cat needed to go to the vet....she's fine, but I was sure glad that the hotel-in the pet welcome packet-had listed the University of Penn Vet hospital in the info. Smudge the cat was taken care of, and we returned to our room. The bellman was very nice about running out and hailing a cab for me. I was concerned for the cat but all was well. I even wound up with the same cabbie on the way back! There is only valet parking available-but the service getting my car was fast. The hotel was slow all weekend, but there was sufficient staff to handle the guests without long waits. All of the staff were very friendly. I needed engineering a couple times and they came quickly. Once, the bathroom was really hot. I wasn't sure why, turns out there's some sort of heater built into the ceiling (looks like just a panel) and he shut it off. I just wanted to make sure that it was normal, as when you're in a high rise building, and you feel heat, but can't SEE anything, you worry about whether something bad may happen! All in all, we had a nice stay. The room was very clean, as were the public areas. I didn't eat in the restaurant, Sole Food, as I went across to the Marriott for dinner (they owed me one so it was free) but again, the soup I got was very tasty and the cat even ate a little bit of the chicken! The bed was also very comfy. I should have called for a couple extra pillows, but I slept like a baby right through until the cat decided to wake up! This was my first stay in a Loews hotel and if they're all as nice as the one in Philadelphia, then I surely will try another property in the future.

“Andaz discovery” It’s not that I’m not familiar with Hyatt hospitality. It’s mostly that fact that I didn’t expect New York is really able to offer accommodation of exceptional quality for less than $600 per night. Andaz was amazing, from the welcoming start with complimentary ice tea to the absolutely automatic touch screen ctrl in the room. We were located in the tower – very quite. Comfortable bad, amazing stylish bathroom, very attentive stuff, tastefully done décor. We’ve stayed for 2 nights in July 2011, made reservation though the hotel website and paid $500 in total. This was our last stop in the long US holiday vacation, and we couldn’t be more happy with it. I will certainly stay again when visiting on business - 5th avenue is right in the middle of all you need. Nothing but best to Andaz 5th avenue!

“Nice boutique hotel in a great location - old but nice” The Marqueen is, as other reviews have noted, not the Hilton - but it's not the Motel 6 either. Yes, the hotel is old, but that hasn't caused us any problems. Rooms are quite large by hotel standards, and prices are lower than most hotels in Seattle. This is an independant hotel where they have done a nice job in restoration of a very old building. No, it's not "restored to 1900s grandeur" (nor do they claim that) but it's completely comfortable and definitely not visually sterile like most hotels today. Our room had a very comfortable bed and a much less comfortable sofabed ( but all sofabeds are). Decor was older style but fully maintained - in other words older furniture but in great shape. They've done alot with crown molding but the modern walls in the rooms (ie. textured wallboard) look a bit out of place in parts. The bathrooms are perfectly OK. Ours has a long tub (much longer than most hotel tubs). I normally shower but took the opportunity for two nice soaks in the tub - becuase I can. Hotel service has been friendly and good. They serve a continental breakfast that could be a little more variety. There is free wifi, which works well but was not super-fast. Biggest negative - the floors squeak. And I mean WOW do they squeak. Our floor is hardwood with area rugs, and each step could wake the dead, or at least your sleeping companions. Important - many earlier reviewers complained about the street noise. The hotel claimed they were installing noise-abatement windows in street-facing rooms. Verdict: the hotel did as claimed, and the windows work great. We face the street and see the traffic but hear almost nothing. Other reviewers have pointed out that there is no elevator. One reviewer even complained that "the last thing you want to do after a day of walking is climb 5 flights of stairs". That complaint is a little unfair as this hotel has only 3 floors, hence 2 flights of stairs. It's really a non-issue. The location is awesome - with lots of great restaurants just steps away. Don't underestimate the value of this in a city where parking is difficult and expesnive. The hotel does charge $25 a day for valet parking with unlimited in/out but in 3 nights we always found free street parking nearby (but I think we lucked out a bit on that). I would stay here again - read the other reviews, but remember that old doesn't mean shabby,

“Location, friendly and helpful staff, value.” This place has plenty of good reasons for making it a top choice in Austin hotels. The location is perfect for anything downtown. The staff was eager to please and help with any request. Parking at $27 a day is annoying, but the room value was good. Spacious, clean and updated rooms were reasonably priced and had great skyline views. The leisure or business traveler will appreciate the comfortable rooms and the attached Starbucks was a nice bonus for late nighters. In room coffee was bad, so Marriott may want to rethink that choice. It was my only disappointment here, so that is pretty high recommendation. Most downtown things were easy walking. Shopping, restaurants, nightlife all were convenient. Our late night cab was only $5. Overall this was a perfect location and will be a top Austin choice for future trips.

“Excellent Stay” I also checked in on April 14, as a previous poster did. I actually was in line behind her and heard her yelling about not getting the two double beds and the non-smoking room. I felt bad for her, but my experience was the exact opposite. Check in was smooth and we got exactly what we had requested. We were also granted access to the Club Room, just by asking (my husband is a silver points member and the acess is usually only for gold and above). So, with that, we enjoyed desserts in the evening and breakfast in the morning. I didn't visit the pool, but it looked pretty small and crowded from what I could see. We had a great view, and found the room to be very comfortable. The bed was good, and the bathroom was well stocked and worked fine. We got great service and directions from the conceirge and also no problems with the bell hop and valet parking. I loved that the hotel had direct access to a nice mall, and could go shopping easily. In addition, there were many places to eat within walking distance. We also walked to Fells Point for the nightlife. It is about a one mile walk, but very easy and along the waterfront. In all, an excellent stay for us.

“Very Functional, Good Location, but Average Hotel” When we arrived the staff was very friendly, but it took a few minutes of waiting for a staff member to come and check us in. Our room was upgraded from a suite to a one bedroom. However the room is quite dated, the bathroom is functional but certainly nothing special and a bit dark, and the furniture except for the bed was uncomfortable. Everything looked a bit warn, however it was clean. If you put the air conditioner below 70 degree it was quite noisy. There was parking with a fee, but the underground lot took a little bit of maneuvering since there were SUVs parked in spaces for compact cars. There was a very nice variety for breakfast which was nice. All in all if you are looking for function with a bit of a kitchen (the fridge was convenient!) it is fine. If you are looking for more luxurious there are other options (some even cheaper!).

“Central Location, Pretty Funky especially with TravelZoo Rate...” Stayed in NYC Weds - Sun over the UK May Day bank hol wknd 2010 with my friend (her first visit to NYC, my 10th). We had to be careful about how much we spent on a hotel room due to financial constraints and the fact that at the time the exchange rate from £ to $ wasn't great. However I did not want to compromise on quality/surroundings as I'm a boutique/trendy hotel fan, having stayed at Thompson, most of the Ws and Ian Schrager hotels in the past. I checked on TravelZoo and found a $99 per night rate at the Ace Hotel, which seemed too good to be true and I did some research. There was a huge selection of rooms, the cheapest of which was a bunk bed room which was described as small and basic. I booked this as we were 2 girls travelling alone and knew that we'd really only be sleeping and getting ready in the room as most of our time was going to be spent shopping and in bars & restaurants. I was expecting the worst when we arrived but was NOT disappointed. The room was excellently decorated (industrial/monochrome style), the bunk beds were comfy, there was a smeg fridge in the room (!) packed with exotic goodies (which we didn't sample due to $$$). The lobby has been described by many and I can confirm that it is dark, tastefully decorated (apart from the cabinet with dead animals in it) and does indeed boast a plethora of young folk with their imacs. There is a coffee shop attached to the hotel (which is street facing, so open to the public) where the uniform seems to be tattoos and a jaunty hat (fine by me but they were all up themselves and it took them about 4 mins to serve each coffee, making for a very grumpy me in the mornings - picture a 40min queue one morning with only 7 people ahead of me!!). Concierge was very helpful and advised us on where to eat on the evening we decided to spend the evening in Brooklyn. Location is right next to the Empire State Building and Macy's so incredibly central for us as we spent our time equally between Soho/Greenwich and the Central Park area. I won't mention recommended things to do in NYC as there is plenty of useful info on TA on that. Would STRONGLY recommend this hotel but probably only at the rate I paid (ok, maybe a little bit more as it was ridiculously low for this calibre of hotel). I did see some documentation stating that rooms normally start at $400 a night but I'm not quite sure how true that is. Also we never got a chance to eat in the restaurant which is apparently great (and was ridoculous busy every night) but I believe it is run by the same folks as The Spotted Pig. ENJOY! Would not recommend to families or more traditional types but definitely to groups of friends and couples.

“Gut gelegenes Motel in der Nähe Downtown San Antonio” Das Motel ist ideal gelegen am Highway Interstate 10 - von da aus ist man in 20 min. in der Innenstadt von San Antonio, wo man neben Alamo auch den Riverwalk zeitnah erreichbar genießen kann. Die Lage ist sicherlich das große Plus im Verhältnis zu den "Innenstadt-Motels" - wo man gerne mal den doppelten Preis zahlt, ohne dass das Motel tatsäch auch eine bessere Ausstattung bietet. Das Motel bietet das übliche "continental breakfast" an und ist als ordentliches Motel zu bezeichnen - die Zimmerausstattung war mit Microwelle, Klimaanlage, Kaffeemaschine und Kühlschrank "üblicher Standard". Sauber und mit einer fairen Preisgestaltung - d.h. Jan. 2011 USD 38.

“Couldn't get much better.” We had a corner suite on 23rd floor with views of bay and space needle. With the floor to ceiling windows it was like being in a postcard, especially at night. Staff was outstanding. Hotel is within walking distance of all downtown. If you only have a carryon, take the light rail to and from the airport. It's $2.50 a person and you get off at Westlake, 2 blocks from hotel. Best deal is happy hour at Ruth's Chris Steakhouse in the lobby. In the lounge you can get prime rib sliders for $5.95, outstanding!! The reviewer who mentioned no carafe, the coffee maker in the room is designed to just have the cup put below the spout so it's brewed into your coffe cup. The only problem we had was solved without our even asking. I ordered room service breakfast for myself and a carafe of coffee for my wife, they we're a little late and my wife decided to go shopping instead of wait for her coffee. I asked them to take the coffee back when my breakfast arrived, then when I called to have them remove the room service table, they told me they'd comped the whole breakfast since it was a little late. Great service.

“Nice location, friendly staff, needs some upgrades” I stayed here for work, and chose it for a couple reasons. It was on our list of hotels to try in Chicago, since it had a "classic" look to it. It was in the area I like to stay in, and it was in the price range acceptable for business (and comparable to a couple others I was looking at). The staff is very friendly and accomodating, and gave me a very nice corner room. This was even more appreciated, since I arrived about 10:00 am, and appreciated have a room to drop my bags off in before I had to head out. The room was decent size, but there were a couple draw backs. The rooms are old looking, with some overdue wallpaper and fixture updates. The furniture is OK, but could be improved, and there were other needed updates, like outdated switches in the bathroom, some that didn't seem to work on anything. I know taking a shower at 8:00 am can mean less hot water in a hotel, but I had a lukewarm shower my second day. It was a pleasant stay, but I have to say for the price, I could have found nicer. Keep in mind there is one elevator, so it could be a wait. I was two floors up, so I took one stairway up. It is entertaining, as you see in part of the kitchen for Ditka's restaurant. I took the other stairway down, and was further entertained to end up in the back of Ditka's dining room, by the wait staff. Neither one of these affected my stay, but did make it unique.

“Perfekte Lage, gutes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis” Für New Yorker Verhältnisse gute Zimmergröße, modern und interessant eingerichtet, mit Safe und Sitzgelegenheit. Sehr schönes geräumiges Bad. Schöner Barbereich, surrealistisch angehaucht, mit Kamin als Raumtrenner zur Lobby. Direkt beim Times Square, dennoch verhältnismäßig ruhig. Schöne Lobby mit freier Weinprobe am Abend, wo man schnell neue Leute kennenlernen kann. Guter Conciergeservice, der bei Abreise für ein Taxi sorgt.

“Location, room size, breakfast buffet” I stayed for several nights through a major national meeting which was at McCormick Place. The location on the Magnificent Mile, the suites and the buffet breakfast, which caters for different national food preferences, were great. If there is a downside to the hotel, its the logistics of getting in and out. The hotel has a relatively small street frontage and the entrance is a little clumsy with people milling around inside and outside the door. There is limited space for taxis act at the front. The lobby itself has a coffee place that sells sandwiches and drinks to go and some seating. The in/out issues were evident when on the first morning, I needed to get to McCormick Place early. Allowing an hour, I rounded the corner to the conference bus in front of the Westin, to find the queue extending well up Michigan. I returned to the Hotel and asked for a taxi - they have a lot of trouble getting taxis to come in busy times. I eventually got picked up by someone in taxi headed to McCormick. Message: if you need a taxi - reserve one ahead.
“Closet-sized rooms but an excellent value/amazing location” Amazing location (across from 30 Rock) at a cheap price. But don't expect a room larger than your bed. Nice staff, zero amenities.

“A Solid, Well-Run Hotel” I just returned from a six night stay--my third stay this past year. The hotel gets high marks from me in terms of room size, cleanliness, service by all staff, and quality of food. Others have commented on the variety for the free breakfast and I agree. If you cannot find several items for your plate you are truly a picky eater. I have not taken advantage of the evening reception so I don't know if the featured food Monday through Thursday is good but there are always overflow crowds so it must be okay. The few quibbles I have are no newspapers over the weekend, the bathroom lighting was so low the bath/shower was almost completely dark when the curtain was pulled, and the TV remote in both rooms never seemed to work properly. Check-in and check-out went smoothly, free high speed Internet service is much appreciated, and the fairly convenient location made walking to most areas of NW Washington an enjoyable way to see Dupont Circle, Downtown, the Smithsonian, and the gigantic government buildings that dominate the town. I will continue to stay at the Homewood Suites on future visits.

“Donnez du cachet à votre séjour !” Quitte à visiter San Francisco, autant se faire plaisir si possible en logeant dans un Hôtel typique de l'architecture du lieu. L'hôtel est situé dans le centre, non loin de Japantown et à 2 blocs de cafés branchés pour une sortie nocturne. Cet hôtel est magnifique et très bien tenu, les photos du site parlent d'elles-même. Bien sûr c'est plus cher qu'un motel mais quel cachet ! De vraies chambres, un style anglais prononcé, jusque dans l'accueil (exemplaire) et l'ambiance feutrée des parties communes... Rien à reprocher, les chambres sont très propres, des petis cadeaux dans la salle de bain, un réfrigérateur dans la chambre, les chaînes cablées, et un radio réveil pouvant recevoir un Ipod, où l'art de conjuguer tradition et modernité. Le quartier est calme et on dort très bien, sauf si les voisins font du bruit : les murs ont l'âge de la maison... Enfin, il est difficile de se garer dans le quartier si l'on ne veut pas payer un parking. Mais avec un peu de patience, on y arrive... Bref à recommander sans réserves si le budget le permet !

“Nice rooms, ok-ish service” As old Hyatt customers, we have been eager to check out the Andaz in NYC having had the pleasure of staying at the London one. Overall, the property is very modern and slick. Check-in was quick, unpersonal and no further information about the hotel and its services was given. The front-facing staff are a mixed bag ranging from polite and friendly people to aloof and unfriendly ones. Rooms, as everyone else notes on tripadvisor, are extremely spacious for NYC standards with nice bathrooms and big bed rooms. Room cleanliness is ok, but certainly not spectacular. The free soft-drink minibar and wifi is fantastic. The gym is in the basement and equipped modestly, yet offers cold towels and water. The bed linen and toiletries were of a high standard. The breakfast offering is good, but the made to order dishes could be improved (i.e. less butter/fat/sugar). For NYC standards (i.e. smaller rooms, more arrogant concierges than in other cities), the Andaz is certainly above average, but I think definitely not as good as Conde Naste and others believe...

“Second Stay Better Than First” I previously wrote a review of this hotel. I liked this hotel and was willing to stay here again, but found out one additional piece of information which could may your stay better. First, the basics: This is a very nice hotel with clean rooms, comfortable beds, full service, a nice bar, a great staff and, as is the Renaissance standard, Aveda bath products. On my first stay, I had a room with the bathroom to the side, which meant the door to the hallway was a few feet from the bed, without a sound buffer. Hallway noises were a problem. This time, I was given Room 635, which had a better layout. When you walked into the room, there was a long, narrow bathroom which ran the full length of the room, creating a buffer between the bed area and the hallway. The noise problem was non-existent in this room. Make sure you get this room type, rather than the other. The view from this room was quite nice. You could see all the way to the bay. As I walked down the hall, I could tell which people were in the other room type. Their conversations could be heard in the hallway. One odd thing which isn't really a problem, but was humorously odd... Upon exiting the elevator, there is a sign instructing which way to go for which room. Rooms 601-633 had an arrow pointing one direction, while the other instructed to rooms 636-659. At first I figured 635 must be right there, but it wasn't. I finally realized that because 635 was equidistant in both directions, there was not directional information. (There was no Room 634.) So while I recommend the X35 rooms, just know you'll be on your own to find it after exiting the elevator.

“A good hotel -- especially if you get it on Priceline” We stayed at the Hyatt Regency on Sept. 21, after getting it for $64 on Priceline. The location was great for us -- at the interchange of I-30 and I-35E -- because we just needed a place to stay while we were en route to Austin. Parking was kind of a mess. We pulled in front of the hotel to check in, only to encounter a minor traffic jam that blocked us in for about 15 minutes. The front desk said the hotel was valet only, but there's a parking lot less than a half-block away that's half the price and very convenient. We checked in around 11:30 p.m., and the hotel was busy, loud and full of teenagers. Check-in was easy and we got a room on the 19th floor. Maybe it was because we used priceline, but the entire floor had a sort-of septic tank smell to it. The rooms didn't stink, but the hallway sure did. The room itself is fine -- big, cushy bed. I loved the double french doors on the bathroom. We had a single king room, and were somewhat perplexed by the placement of the TV. ... you can't see it well from the bed (it faces the desk and two chairs.) We left early the next morning to continue on the Austin. Check-out was easy, as was retrieving the car from the lot down the straight. The overall: I was pleased with it, flaws on all, because we paid 64 bucks a night for it. Paying twice or three times that may not be worth it.

“Good Value in NW San Antonio” Definitely a good place for the budget minded person or family. The building is a bit tired but the rooms are in fairly good shape although there is too much furniture for the size of the room. Bed and shower was adequate. The front desk people were friendly and helpful and gave good directions to anywhere we needed to go. The breakfast was okay. Plenty of food for the family on the go. Pool was fine except for the noise from the interstate. My only complaint was the ice machine. The only one that worked was on the third floor. Overall, pretty descent place if you are not the critical type.

“Nothing out of the ordinary..” Recently stayed on a Sunday night using a reward night so the room cost was complimentary for me. Upon checking in, i was immediately recognized as being an elite member a few times and my room requests were confirmed and was placed in a 9th floor room. Service at the front desk was very friendly and cordial. As others have alluded in previous reviews, the location of the hotel may not be the greatest. Its right off the freeway and pretty close to a residential area, and I'll agree that it doesn't appear to be in the best of neighborhoods.. But then again, usually neighborhoods near airports aren't the best. It's maybe 5 minutes from the airport, so that was a plus. In hindsight, maybe I should have booked something in downtown as I did enjoy wandering around downtown and Beale street more. Downtown and Beale St does have it's share of panhandlers though.. I had no problems with the room I was in and it was clean. The bed was comfortable and I had requested extra pillows. As reviewers have noted, you can tell its an aging property and it's probably time for a refresh of the rooms and hallways. The tube tv has got to go! I didn't dine at the property or order room service however I had a few drinks at the hotel bar and service was fine. It appeared the bar closed around midnight on a Sun night. All in all, the overall hotel experience was average, although everything was perfectly fine with the service.

“Old hotel that shows lack of attention” Located across the street from Union Square, the lobby of the hotel is really quite striking. There are a lot of very high end shops with the front desk staff and consignee are very good. It is easy to get a cab and walk to Chinatown and North Beach. Unfortunately you don't sleep in the lobby. We stayed in the old (they call it the Landmark) building, but others gave similar description of the rooms in the new "Tower" building. The room is almost square, which is sort of strange. There are two doors on one side - open up one door and it is a closet and another door is the bathroom (I was afraid to walk into the wrong one during the night!). The bathroom is small, almost European small, perhaps 5' x 8', so it really is a little bigger then the closet. The (almost square) room is a nice size but, instead of keeping with the 100+ year old theme of the hotel it seems like they compromised making it sort of modern, making it just another hotel room, nothing special. In addition you hear everything going on either next door or in the hallway, and this was with me requesting and being ensured that this is a quiet room! So forget about a good nights sleep.

“Great location” I love the location of this hotel. Easy on and off the expressway. Right by 6th street and across the street from one of the best restaurants in Austin. Rooms are nice, bed is a dream, had a nice room facing 6th street. Inhouse restaurant is out of this world, little expensive but worth the splurge.
“not bad.. not good...” its okay.. rooms are boring.. sort of stale... But not bad... Lobby is okay... everything is okay... Only real nice part is location....

“Good Value” Stayed here last week and would definitely do so again. Booked via the website, called to confirm twice before arrival -fearing the botched reservation stories on tripadvisor- but no issues with my reservation at all so the calls were likely not needed. Convenient, safe eastside neighbourhood. My room 109 was in good shape...very clean & new sink, wall fixtures and TV. I booked a "non-smoking" room but there was an ashtray in there nonetheless. I also noticed the ashcan in the hallway. Luckily, neither the room nor the hallway smelled of smoke (perhaps I was just lucky to be on a floor without smokers, judging from the previous review). Noise was not an issue...again, I might have just been on a quiet floor. Two things I mentioned to them: no hooks to hang wet towels in the room, and would be nice to have robe/slippers to get to the shared bathroom (given the size of the towels you get, better not be too modest!). Other than that I was very satisfied. Highly recommended.

“Decent, but small room, but curiously poor maintenance and lousy TV” Can't beat the location, as this venerable hotel is immediately adjacent to Grand Central Terminal at 42nd and Lex. The Good: Clean. No visible sign of bedbugs. Fairly recently refurbished rooms. Lots of electric outlets. Pretty good lighting. In-room ironing room and iron. HTML and RGB inputs for TV. Fairly rapid check-in and checkout (although the terminals for self-service don't work properly.) Fairly responsive elevators. Checkout time was extended without trouble. The Bad: Rooms small--many with view only into the adjacent rooms 20 feet away. Low def analog signals for digital TVs resulting in squished, low quality pictures. Some channels like the NBC outlet very snowy. TV Guide hidden in back of book with menus. No in-room coffee brewers. No rack for suitcases. The Strange: Lousy routine maintenance. The sign guiding guests to their room had fallen to the floor, where it remained for at least 24 hours. The fire alarm was not present in the room, leaving only a bracket with cables hanging out. The switch for one of the bedside lamps was shattered. The floor indicator in an elevator was defective.

“You get what you pay for...” We stayed here last weekend for one night. We had stayed at this hotel one other time, last year & the property has gone downhill since then. We booked the Texas Resident rate of $67.50 plus tax. The gal at the front desk was nice. I asked for a high floor not facing the freeway (as this type room can be noisy). She said she could put us on the 2nd floor. I told her again, I'd like a high floor. She said there was a room on the 9th floor, but it would be hot up on that floor. I asked her to check again to see if there wasn't something else.... she found a room on the 8th floor, but it was facing the freeway. So, I took the 2nd floor room. Room 219. We arrived at the very end of the hall (which was fine - more quiet there). The door handle was loose & we had to mess with it to get it to open. Once inside the room looked fine. There was an odor. Not a terrible odor, but a "not so clean" odor. The bed was made as usual, however, there were several marks of things having been placed on the comforter. I had a feeling as if someone else had been in there & decided not to stay in that room. ??? So... I immediately pulled back the covers all the way to the foot of the bed & searched for bed bugs or anything else. Everything was clean. So, I was ok with the room. The A/C temp was set at 72 degrees, so I turned it down to 69...(we like our room COLD) and checked out the rest of the room.... the bathroom was spacious & clean...no mold. Towels were in short supply, but we made it without running out. I looked up at the A/C filter & it was filthy. I told the hubs, that is probably why the room smelled. We went downstairs to the hotel bar & ordered drinks & light snacks. The french fries were really good, but my Bloody Mary was terrible. I didn't even drink half of it. We stopped by the pool, nice & clean, but full of people, mostly kids. So, we passed on swimming. We went back up to our room to wait for our friends to join us for dinner, the room was no cooler than when we had arrived an hour or so earlier. Our friends came & we left for the evening. When we arrived back at our room around 3:00 AM... we couldn't find a parking palce, so we went around back & had to park FAR from the door, in a space that was not a parking space. There's a fence all around the parking lot & signs EVERYWHERE stating the hotel is NOT responsible for break-ins. Also, there are two entrances to the lots & the side one was blocked by a van with out of state tags. Totally parked sideways in the driveway. ????? We had to turn around & get back on the access road & went in the main driveway.... anyway, back to the rear parking lot issue.... we parked, got out, walked up to the back door (which SHOULD HAVE BEEN LOCKED).... it opened right up.... so anyone could have just come in the door without a keycard. Not safe folks! We go up to our room, expecting it to be nice & cool (it was a typical Houston summer night - hot & humid ).... well, the room was still the same temp as when we arrived. So, we pulled off all the covers, except the sheet & crawled into bed. The bed was ok... but the sheets & pillows stank. That same old dirty smell as in the room. But, I know they were clean.... at least they LOOKED clean. Anyway, we had to kick off the sheet to feel comfortable in the room. The fan NEVER turned off (it was on auto), so the A/C was working as hard as it could to cool the room.... which it never did. I HATE to sweat when I sleep... don't you? Anyway, we never complained, but vowed we will never stay here again. There are too many other options in the area (which we come to a few times a year). They offered the best rate, for sure...but to us, it wasn't worth it. We'll pay more next time & get a clean smelling room with an A/C that works.

“Good airport hotel” The shuttle was quick once we had called for it, and the staff on reception were polite and helpful. The room was good and beds comfortable. The hotel is quiet and we didn't hear planes or people all night. Excellent breakfast, better than most, nice eggs , choice of cereal in individual boxes ( not all sweet sugary ones too ) and fresh pastries. Definitely will use this hotel again when flying to Denver.

“Great hotel” The Pan Pacific got 10 out of 10 for us. They have a great desk staff, spacious rooms (we booked a Space Needle corner room) and a great location. Our room was always clean, the staff was friendly and attentive and the bar was a great place to wind down. Nest time in Seattle this is our stay of choice.

“good as an airport hotel, less good for long stays1” I guess the key thing that I need to remember when reviewing this Renaissance Hotel is that it is an airport hotel, and I have been staying at the hotel for extended periods of sometimes up to 10 days. The hotel is really designed to give people in transit staying, I suspect, for an average of one or maybe two nights. That is why I tend to rate the hotel as fine and may other people on tripadvisor.com would rave about the hotel. The hotel has been going through a process of staggered renovation and there has been a real improvement in the quality and state of the bedrooms. One improvement, in my view, being the beds! These are definitely soft, comfortable and have piles of pillows to snuggle down into at night. The rooms are a good size, both the normal rooms and the suites although the latter tend to be fairly dark. There is usually good space to do work, good internet access and fairly good bathrooms with great water pressure. The one thing that is a pity they have not addressed is the air conditioning which is very boisterous and noisy, and I have found that I need to leave it off when going to bed at night and so in summer the rooms get hot and bit uncomfortable over night. The other area that is not great is the bar and dining facilities. The bar is small and not that exciting and the food is pretty average and limited. So while this is fine when there for a night or maybe two, if you stay any longer then you tire of the food. The problem being that as this is a hotel airport there is nowhere to pop out and walk to for an alterative meal. There is a small outdoor pool that is very popular, with small hot tub. The gym is pretty good with a range of cardio equipment to keep most people happy with TVs above each. The weights area is very limited but fine again for a work out. The hotel has a large parking garage with self parking or valet parking. The view from rooms in the front of the hotel are over the airport and worth asking for when you check in - or you get the view of the multi story car park (which you will see I always have had!) So this is a good hotel for an airport hotel, probably good for a conference as is so handy for the airport but not a hotel to spend longer in. One thing as an aside is although planes come really close to the hotel the hotel is very sound proof and even between rooms is very well insulated! A tips is that you can get amazing rates for club room access at the weekend (from a Thursday to a Monday check-out) off their website. You can see videos I made of 2 of the rooms at this link: http://blog.myspace.com/index.cfm?fuseaction=blog.view&friendID=89511767&blogID=159775462

“Loved it! best hotel downtown” This is a brand new hotel all suites and its amazing. The lobby is spacious and luxurious. The room are big and very modern and equipped with espresso machines . The views and location are great. My husband and I went for a romantic weekend spent Friday night at the Mandarin and they were booked for Saturday so we moved to The Conrad and I am so glad we did it was incredible. The staff was so friendly and welcoming. Well done we would definitely book again. The have a roof top bar which was not open yet but I can't wait to check it out when it does open.

“Denver business trip” The Denver Airport (IAH) is 45 minutes from downtown, so you must decide if you want convenience in being near the airport, or staying downtown where the action is. The Hyatt House is minutes from the airport. It's inexpensive ($119 p/n), clean, and full of ameneties. We stayed in a studio suite that has a full kitchen, living room, bedroom, and bathroom with huge shower. This has everything you need if you don't mind being away from downtown. It even includes a full breakfast and wine tasting in the early evening.

“Perfect Union Square location” We stayed for 2 nights and had a wonderful experience. The greeting upon arrival was remarkable , as was the gorgeous corner suite with the heavenly bed! The location was perfect for seeing San Francisco our first time.

“Dated and Tired - needs an Update” This hotel, although well located near Union Square, is in dire need of a facelift in the common areas as well as the rooms. Tired decor. Amenities are weak, especially for a diamond member.

“Hotel Blake is on the decline and not a boutique hotel” Outside the Hotel Blake is a sign saying that this is a historic building. That means it has a historic ventilation system. It was one of the first Hyatt hotels, and it shows. It also may be up for sale or condo conversion, and as a result, things are not being fixed or attended to. Their website proclaims to be a boutique hotel, but really this hotel is a little below a Crowne Plaza. It has free wireless, but the desk in my room did not have a phone on it. The mattress was good, but the towels were thread bare. If you wanted a bathrobe, you had to call and ask for it. The sink didn't have a stopper. The shower has no bathtub and no door. The room smelled of smoke even though the hotel is supposedly non-smoking. in our 3 night stay, the towels and wastebaskets in the fitness center were not replaced/emptied. The doors are very lightweight, so people in the hallway can hear conversations in the room. Bathroom noise carries through the bathroom walls. The first room they gave me was claustrophobic, maybe 200 sq ft with just enough room for a queen bed and a desk. When I complained, they gave me a room (513) at double the size but had smoke smell in the walls. Both rooms I tried had very small windows, so there was very little natural light. No frig, and ice is only on the 12th floor. Windows were single pane, so street noise came through loud and clear, early every morning. The fitness center equipment was broken or very old. But back to the ventilation system... Heat and cold air comes from a central system. The room thermostat only turns on the fan to bring that air into the room. If the central system is running air conditioning, that's all your room will get. And the day I got there, they said the hotel restaurant was no longer serving breakfast, just lunch and dinner. So have I just described a boutique hotel? I think not...

“Ghastly -- Couldn't Wait to Escape” We just spent an agonizing night at the Hotel Americano. We'd planned to stay for two nights, but couldn't wait to escape this morning. Now comfortably ensconced elsewhere. Where do I begin to describe the horrible experience we had -- four of us, in two adjacent rooms? Our experience was similar to that described earlier by MaureenColorado. She wrote, "The hotel's designer seemed to mistake cheap, sparse decor for good design." Please don't let the photos of the rooms on the hotel's website -- or elsewhere -- fool you. A bare concrete floor looks quite nice in a photo, but actually living in a room with a concrete floor is a bit like sleeping in Costco. There are (essentially) no chairs in the room. The stool beneath the teeny, tiny desk is impractical -- nobody could actually sit on it. And the beanbag chair isn't soft, and doesn't envelop you. You sort of sit against it, rather than in it. Totally useless. So your choice is to sit on the bed -- on the floor. There was a peculiar lamp hanging over one side of the bed, with probably a 20 watt bulb. But the switch for the lamp was on the other side of the bed. The other choice was the florescent light bulbs behind the bed -- but they were incredibly bright, and could not be dimmed. The bed -- essentially on the floor -- was surprisingly comfortable, but the sheets were too small and instantly became untucked. The bathroom was awful. It reminded me of a concrete version of a bathroom on an Amtrak train. Tiny shower cubicle, tiny sink, tiny shelf -- and very weak lighting. The towels were on a shelf at least (and I mean this) seven feet above the ground. I'm 6'2" and almost couldn't reach the towels. Her Ladyship is 5'6" and couldn't reach them at all. With so little light in the bathroom there's no way to put on make-up. Although we booked two double rooms, each only had one robe, and one pair of slippers. (Remember the floors are cold, bare concrete.) We had an iPad in our room -- chained to the wall -- but someone had apparently left with the device that charges it, so the battery was all but dead. There was no battery in the clock in my sister's room. We could not control the air conditioning or heating. The rooms had one temperature -- hot. In his reply to MaureeenColorado, Will Jordan wrote, "should you come back this way again at some point in the future, we will have the stool in your room replaced with a chair from our office." That's exactly what they finally did for us -- they brought us two desk chairs, vintage Staples. They were comfortable, but hardly gemütlichkeit. The hotel does not have parking. You need to go two blocks downtown -- yourself -- and park your car in a parking lot. This was explained to me ahead of time. Dinner was actually very good, and our waitress was very friendly and efficient. It was the only nice part of our short stay. But we then found we didn't have any hot water in either of the rooms, and at breakfast the next morning we encountered the snooty waitress from hell. Burnt croissants, no cream cheese (I had to send them out to buy some -- which they did, without much grace). The lack of hot water, hotel-wide, put us way, way over the tipping point -- and we checked out a day early. The hotel did not charge us for our stay -- which was gracious of them. Too bad they couldn't give me back a day of my life. Her Ladyship and I have stayed at the Adam & Eve Hotel in Turkey. It, too, has concrete floors and low-down beds -- but somehow it seems to (generally) work at the Adam & Eve, and doesn't work at all here. This hotel is definitely, absolutely NOT for people like us -- in our early 60's. It's not for families. This is a hotel for young couples -- it looks like it's the perfect place for an out-of-the-way assignation. (Who will know you on West 27th Street? I've lived in Manhattan for years, and have never set foot on this block of West 27th Street until yesterday.) But if you're planning an assignation here -- you'd better hope that the lady likes showers rather than baths, likes sleeping on the floor, and doesn't need light in the bathroom to put on her make-up. When we were checking out, the bellman said he was from a Third World Country and the problems we experienced were "nothing in my country." Hey, guy -- I've been to many Third World Countries, too -- but I made a reservation for a hotel in Manhattan, not Guatemala.

“Low speed internet at High Speed prices” I paid for high speed internet and got low speed internet. I called the provided to see what the issue was and the issue was twofold. The first issue is that you do not really offer high speed internet, the Hotel limits access to a maximum of.5 Mbps of speed, which means at some times when , as the hotel operator said “too many guests are using the internet” the speed will drop to as low as .2 Mbps. I stay at a lot of hotels and when I pay for high speed internet I normally get 2.0 Mbps. Hotels that offer free internet often limit access to .75 Mbps. I can get by with .75 Mbps, but I cannot conduct my business on such a connection that ranges from .2 to .5 Mbps, so I had to go into our office during the day or limit my activities until I could go somewhere else. For $14.95 plus taxes I should get fast internet. There were also some issues with the room temperature being too warm for my tastes. There was no AC and the window would not open. Twice I left the hotel for my office sweating, so I had to change cloths when I got there. I would have checked out, but we were having a company meeting in the hotel and all my co-workers were staying at this hotel. I also had an issues with the hot water being as brown as coffee, but the cleared up and I understand there had been a maintenance issue.

“Nice property, convenient to airport” Clean full service hotel minutes from airport. Helpful, friendly staff. Only complaint is the charge for wifi in room when the business area offers it for free. Still highly recommended hotel.

“Nice Suburban Hotel” This hotel is pretty convenient if you're attending a football game or doing business nearby: it's close to 163, the 5 and the 8, is a very short drive to UCSD and is next-door to a shopping mall and some national chain restaurants, and right down the street from Qualcomm Stadium. The DoubleTree is only 15 minutes from the airport rental car site, so it's an easy option for those needing to work in downtown as well. Our room was large enough for two, it had adequate closet space and dresser/storage space for two, and the king sized bed was comfortable. The only small qualm is that there isn't much counter space around the bathroom sink to accommodate two people. Instead, I used one of the two shelves that held the clean towels and shampoo/conditioner (consolidated them into one shelf) and my wife took the entire space around the sink for her stuff, so it worked out OK. Rooms have a medium sized flat screen LG HD TV, a couple of HBO channels and the usual variety of HD local/national stations as well. The hotel area was always clean, the indoor and outdoor pools were spotless and the exercise facility seemed adequate. There is ample parking, but it's not free--the good news is that your room key gets you into/out of the garage so it's easy to come and go at will. We found the staff in the lobby/desk were all very helpful and pleasant to deal with in terms of directions and suggestions. The three elevators worked fairly quickly so there wasn't a lot of waiting around. Our room was booked to include the buffet breakfast, which was OK. There were scrambled eggs, breakfast potatoes, bacon/sausage, various pastries, yogurt, breads, cereals, etc., but nothing really outstanding or bad. They would also prepare eggs to order or prepare an omelet as part of the buffet offering. There is a fairly large bar/TV area that seemed to get a fair amount of traffic each night, and there was another restaurant that we did not try during our stay. The best overall food item IMHO is the wonderful DoubleTree chocolate-chip cookies that are generously available! Tons of calories AND flavor....and they are simply wonderful.

“Comfortable stay; convenient location” My husband and I spent a grueling day moving our son to his new home in Franklin (south of indy and Greenwood) on a day when temps were above 100. We wanted a comfortable bed and a good night's sleep. We had tried a couple of the hotels and a B&B in Franklin during his college years; we knew the hotels were not up to par and the B&B, while pleasant and close, required more interaction with the hosts than we were up for. We had stayed in one of the whirlpool tub rooms at the HGI a couple of years ago and the stay was pretty good, so we decided to stay again. Decor is an upscale modern blend of clean lines and natural woods; art is better than most hotels. Located at the County Line Rd exit off of I-65, the hotel is only a couple years old (it was brand new when we'd last stayed). I had booked online and selected an offer that included breakfast for us and 8 meals provided through a charity to needy families. There were no king rooms available, but I noted in requests that such was our preference. When we arrived about 7pm Thursday evening, the clerk reviewed our reservation and, before i could ask, stated a king was available. The only glitch in our stay came when the desk clerk said, "Breakfast is offered buffet style with cooked to order eggs or omelets for $9.95 per person." When I told her it was supposed to be included in our offer, she and the manager conferred and gave us vouchers for breakfast, stating that there were so many different offer codes that they are not always familiar with what each one entails. Something to keep in mind. Cookies are complimentary at the front desk; not so great for this gluten free traveler, but others sure were enjoying them. [I only bought the offer I did--$129 versus the best available price of $119--because of the charitable contribution. I didn't know how much of a breakfast was offered or if the timing would meet our needs. With breakfast a substantial offering of fresh fruits (about 8), hot and cold cereals, biscuits and gravy, sausage and bacon, and cooked to order eggs, it was well worth it. The dining room is a lovely cloth napkin and tablecloth place, and flowers decorate the plates from the kitchen. They were very careful regarding my gluten free issues (from the buffet I heard the waitress speaking to the chef and could also observe him using different utensils, etc.) and the food was very good.] In the evening we relaxed in the indoor pool and spa, a blessing on sore muscles. The pool area was very clean and for over an hour we were the only ones in there. (a herd of kids came in as we were leaving) The spa is very hot! The pool was a perfect temp, we did not use the adjacent workout area but the equipment (about 8 varied electronic machines, medicine balls, free weights, etc.) looked state of the art. Our room midway down one hall of the second floor was quiet despite the heavily trafficked area. The room had a refrigerator with tiny freezer and a microwave, so perfect for a gluten free traveler! Right across the street from the hotel is a fabulous Kroger store, and a quick trip through their deli, natural foods, and wine aisle set us up for the evening. We watched HBO movies before having a wonderful night's sleep. Mucho comfortable mattress and despite the ugly heat outside, the room temp was consistently cool all night. By the way, if you happen to be 7 feet tall, the showers in this hotel are built for you! I'm 5'5" and could just reach the shower head to adjust it. Bath & Body Works products. Bathroom fan not so great, but huge towels and ample counter space. We will definitely stay here again.

“Clean, modern, funkyish hotel close to Union Station” I have stayed at this hotel a few times when in business in DC, particularly for meetings near Union Square. The hotel is close to Judiciary Square as well. There isn't that much exciting right in the neighborhood, except that it is very close to the Mall and to Union Station. It is an elegant hotel.
“Worst Hilton Ever !!!” Avoid this Hotel if you can ! It is very old, very dirty and the staff is very unhelpful.

“Not bad, but great location” I stayed here 3 nights in September while attending a conference at the Convention Center. Supposedly the taxi fare is $32 from the airport (as adverstised on the cab window), but none of my colleagues or I got that rate. Something about extra taxes due to the airport. Our fares all ranged from $38-45. The bellman at the Hilton were all very welcoming and friendly and the front desk was nice enough. I checked in at noon, well ahead of the 3pm check in time. The room was clean and fairly up-to-date. The downside was that the bathroom was very tiny. It was quite awkward getting in and out of the bathroom to close the door. Also, the hangers for the closet had the tiny hooks so they couldn't be used on a normal clothes rod in order to help combat theft. As a result of this, you couldn't hang your clothes just anywhere. The only place besides the closet was a tiny hook on the back of the bathroom door. This became quite annoying very quickly when getting ready. On my last night there, it was after 10 pm at night and I heard the sink make a funny gurgling noise. When I looked in there, it was full of brownish black water. I called the front desk and someone came up and had it fixed within half an hour. I don't know if this was an ongoing problem as my neighbor had the same problem that night, but the response was quick and was taken care of quickly. The location of this hotel can't be beat. We were two blocks away from the convention center, and about 5-6 blocks from Pike's Street Market. I walked down there 3 times during my stay. The walk down is all downhill, and the walk back can be quite a challenge depending on which way you come back. If you walk down University street (which the Hilton sits on), it will take you straight to Pier 57 where you'll find many restaurants. We ate at the Crab Pot one night where they have a crab boil and dump all the goods on the table for you to break open with a mallet. Coming back up the stairs and hill after a full dinner was a real challenge! But fun nonetheless! Overall, this was a decent stay at a decent hotel. Not the best...but not the worst. The location of the Hilton and walking around the city made this a memorable visit!

“Cannot say enough good things about this hotel!” This was my second stay at this fabulous property. I'd arrived on an overseas flight from he** the morning I checked in. Despite the fact that check-in is 3pm, they promptly accommodated my arrival at 11:30 am, and were gracious enough to give me the specific room I had requested that I'd enjoyed the year before. The people who work there are unobtrusive but extremely accommodating. I called to schedule a spa appointment, and was given an in-room appointment for the following morning. I called to inquire about using a microwave, and was asked did I want room service to heat my item up for me or should they bring a microwave to the room--no charge. They promptly brought a tub mat and foam pillow to the room when requested. The airline broke a piece of my luggage and the concierge recommended a wonderful luggage store (I ended up buying 2 pieces!!). Truly, no request is too great. The Restaurant is wonderful. . .I had a fabulous steak dinner the night before Ieft. Service and setting are both superb. The gardens and ponds are legendary, as they should be. I was stopped on my walk one morning as I watched a hummingbird go from one flower to another. And I spent much time enjoying breakfast each morning on "my" patio with its own little fountain...what a life. But my absolute favorite part of this property is the swimming pool. There is no other pool like it. . .so beautiful and serene, incredibly relaxing--it's a wonderful place to while away an hour, have lunch, or actually swim! They maintain the water at a steady 82 degrees. . . Ahhhhh. . . I believe myself to be a hotel junkie--I love to try different hotels every time I travel to a city. . .but from now on in LA, there's no reason to "hotel shop" anymore. I will gladly consider the Hotel Bel Air my home away from home as often as I can.

“Review your room charges carefully” Zero stars for the hotel's bookkeeping abilities, and three stars for the accommodations. The hotel's downtown location is a very short walk away from the ferry building and close to a BART station. The room was basic but clean, though it would have been nice had the bathroom had electrical outlets. We might have stayed in this hotel again but for billing errors that we experienced. We booked the hotel through Hotwire (pre-paying in full). When checking out and reviewing our incidental charges, we noticed an erroneous restaurant charge of $95 on our bill. We hadn't visited the restaurant at all during our stay. We notified the front desk that the charge was incorrect, and they assured us twice that the charge would be removed. The charge wasn't removed. A few days later, the $95 charge appeared on my credit card, along with over $400 of additional charges that hadn't appeared on our check-out statement at all. After a number of phone calls to determine what these charges were, the hotel explained that it hadn't realized that we had pre-paid for our stay through Hotwire, and had essentially charged us twice for our stay. I'm still waiting for the charges to be reversed on my credit card.

“Sofitel is a great hotel” My husband and I stayed at the Sofitel on 17th and Sansom while visiting my family in Philadelphia. The hotel was in a convenient location, close to Rittenhouse Square and a lot of restaurants. The room was clean and comfortable. The bar was a great place to get a drink and had a lively atmosphere. We had breakfast at the hotel, and while it was very good, if you head one block down, you could get a great breakfast at Marathon Grill. The staff was courteous, and we had no problems. Valet is around ~34/night, which is typical for a Philadelphia hotel.

“Great location on Lexington by the 6 subway” I did a Saturday to Monday stay here and enjoyed the convenience of walking out the door and hopping on the subway. I had the cozy queen room which was cozy but not abnorably small. Pros: Location! Comfortable bed Extremely large flat screen with large selection of channels. Typical W bathroom products. Use of the gym and locker room: I liked the sauna and steam rooms. Can't miss out on a brownie in the lounge. Cons: Room right by the elevator and with thin doors I could hear every conversation outside. I'm sure they could hear whatever I wa watching on TV. Music in the lobby is a little loud. Otherwise, no other complaints. Booked on Priceline name your own price (mid town east 4*) for a significant discount

“Bulfinch Hotel Boston” Gutes Hotel in der Nähe des TD Garden (5 Gehminuten). Netter Service, gutes WLAN, gutes Restaurant. Und wie gesagt, die Nähe zum TD Garden ist super ich habe dort ein Spiel der Boston Celtics besucht). Das Zimmer wa nicht zu groß, aber für eine Übernachtung absolut ausreichend. Insgesamt ein lohnenswerter Besuch.

“Best deal in NYC!” This hotel doesn't appear to be amazing from the lobby, which is rather small. However, don't let first impressions deter you from staying here! We loved staying at the Residence Inn! We had reserved two rooms for six of us and they asked us if we'd prefer to be in a two-bedrooms suite, which was wonderful. There were two very large bedrooms (each with own bath) with a completely separate living room between them with a sofabed. Also a nice kitchen and full-size refrigerator! The touches to make it more like home are so nice (huge lounge area, wonderful breakfast,afternoon snacks). Plus free wireless high speed internet was nice to have. I'm not sure why this is considered "Times Square" because it is actually a ten-minute walk from the center of Times Square. We loved the area -- lots of bead/jewelry shops (6th Ave.) and other great shopping as well (Macys, Herald Square, etc.). It is very close to Madison Square Garden and Penn Station, too. We actually preferred this location, being closer to midtown, over Times Square. Our room was extremely clean and very spacious. The Residence Inn will be our place to stay for future trips to the city!

“The quality is slipping away somewhat” I hate to post a negative review for the Emabssy Row Hotel. I have stayed there many times in the past (even when it was part of the Hilton string) and have always had very satisfactory comments to post to tripadvisor. This last stay, however, wasn't as great as previous ones. The heat in our room did not work and we spent most of our time in the room under the covers just to stay comfortable. I reported this to the front desk and they did have someone check it out. They did get it working, but it only worked for a short while before quitting again. We actually ended up just turning it off because it was warmer in the room without it on. Other than that, our stay was decent. The hotel is still in nice shape and the staff is friendly. I'm just concerned that there are some issues with this property that need some attention before it declines any further. I hope this will not the case because I actually like the location and the on-line specials that this hotel offers. I still intend to book further stays with the Embassy Row Hotel, as least for now. I just hope they continue to maintain the property in good repair.

“Amazing hotel, great service, loved the room.” Ask for room 4812. It's a corner room, overlooking Times Square. The room was spacious and the bathroom was roomy. Unlike the W on Lexington, I prefer this location. Concierge Michael was extremely efficient and gets and A+. The hotel is walking distance to all Broadway theaters and some pretty good restaurants. Blue Fin in the hotel is also superb.

“I love the Omni!” Great location (everything you want to see in San Fran is walkable), spotlessly clean and modern rooms as well. What truly sets the Omni San Francisco apart, however, is the service. They have a very dedicated staff that tries incredibly hard to make sure your needs are taken care of. There may be bigger and more expensive hotels in San Fran, but I'll be sure to pick the Omni every time (great rates, too!).

“Good enough, but a little strange decor” The Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf was quiet and nice but I had to give it an "average" rating because I thought the decor was very "bright and sunny" and "loud" for such an area. To me, it didn't match the feeling of San Francisco, rather a more beach town like Florida or something. It was mostly like this in the rooms. Otherwise, the parking is convenient (but pricey) and the staff is friendly enough. I was pleased because it felt very clean and that is very important for me.

“Almost too good to be true.” I’ve stayed at just about every decent hotel in Manhattan, and have to say the Intercontinental is among the nicest and most pleasant of them. Modern without being silly (are you listening, Hudson?), noisy (can you hear me, Sheraton?) or laughably dinky (hello, Paramount?), this is a real gem, especially considering its proximity to Times Square. I would consider this THE place to stay for the visiting theatregoer, with major shows just a block or two away. The location, between 8th and 9th Avenues, is just perfect...on one side, you’re within striking distance of Tourist Hell, but not close enough to be engulfed in it...on the other, you’re half a block from the world of quality, fun restaurants and bars (on 9th Ave) that working New Yorkers enjoy and tourists rarely pollute. Rooms are clean and modern, decorated in soothing brown and beige earthtones. The flatscreen TV is spectacular, the work area well-designed, the bath clean and pleasant. All rooms are non-smoking, and feature you-can-open-them floor-to-ceiling windows that make the space bright and cheery (and, amazingly block out all street noise when closed). I don’t know what it’s like on the upper floors, but the views where I stayed were nothing to write home about (I had a primo view of a parking lot); I can’t imagine it’s any better higher up...in this part of town, all you see are the roofs of other buildings. There are two Ça Va dining spaces on ground level...one is a warm, comfy, full-service brasserie, and the other a place to grab something simple and quick. There’s an intimate little guest lounge, and a spiffy fitness center. Service - from the front desk throughout - is professional and friendly. I had wanted to try the Intercontinental for months after it opened, but the rates were always just too dear ($400+ a night) for business travel. Finally, some reservations became available in the $200 range, which is more reasonable, and suggests you should shop for the best rates before you book. If it sounds like I was impressed, I was; I’ll stay here whenever I can, and hope they can continue to meet the high standards of comfort and service they’ve set for themselves. P.S. : Shake Shack is right around the corner. You simply must!

“Newer Hotel . . . Well Worth It!” I arrived late in the evening after traveling from the East Coast. The staff was very welcoming and made my arrival a breeze. I was hungry and was thankful their restaurant "Luke" was open. I was mostly here for meetings. It was nice having space in my room to work. The bath had a wonderful, large shower (no tub, which is fine with me). The bed was confortable and everything was excellent. I am a breakfast eater so between the made-to-order breakfast and the manager's reception each night, we barely even needed much beyond buying lunch. I would recommend this property to anyone.

“Good place to stay” Stayed here this past weekend for a brief stop over in SF. I'm a SPG member and have stayed here before. Rooms nice, staff is great and location is good if you need to be downtown. The one problem I had is that they gave me a free drink ticket for being a gold member (and they couldn't accommodate by bed request). I went to the bar and clearly stated I had the free drink coupon when I ordered but the free drink still ended up costing me $15. I was too tired to argue. Next time I'll skip that free amenity that ended up being costly!

“Disappointing Marriott” The rooms were disappointing for a Marriott brand. There were stains on the curtains, on the walls, and on the carpet. The light switches and hairdryer were dirty, and the rooms need a complete reno. They are tired. The beds and bedding were very comfortable though, and we slept very well. There was a persistent leak from either the shower or the toilet that kept the bathroom tile wet (yuck!). The staff were earnest and eager, but we suspect systemic processes in the hotel kept them from delivering in their good intentions. The room rates are in keeping with what you should expect, and don't let the Marriott name make you think that you are getting "deal". We paid $89 per night, which was about all I would pay. The breakfast buffet at the cafe downstairs is good value, and very reasonable. If you are looking just for place to put your head down, this is it - don't expect to "enjoy" your room otherwise.

“Perfect stay, every time” We have stayed at Sofitel Lafayette Square in D.C. several times, and each time it has been a perfect experience. We always choose a luxury room or a junior or prestige suite if the price is right. The rooms we have inhabited are very well appointed, clean and very comfortable (the only exception was a "Superior" room where friends stayed, which I can confirm had a very hard bed for some reason, quite the opposite of what we have experienced in the other rooms). Service at this hotel is top notch. The restaurant is excellent, and there is a very nice bar across the lobby hall from the restaurant. The location is incredible, just a block from the White House, an easy walk to major attractions in D.C. and very central if you are there on business. Be sure to eat lunch or dinner at least once at the Old Ebbit Grill a couple of blocks down the street - a classic, historic and delicious place to dine - but make a reservation! On our most recent visit Oct 3-4, they upgraded us from a Prestige Suite to the Presidential Suite (where President Sarkozy of France was the last guest before us). Wow! Of course, this was an unusual event, but it was an unsolicited generosity on their part. Also, we brought friends for whom I accidentally booked the wrong date, and the hotel figured out how to get them a room in spite of my error and the fact that they were booked. They really went the extra mile.

“Connected to a great mall” This hotel was recently renovated and the new decor is quite contemporary. I had a king bedroom. It was very spacious. In fact, I think they could have used a bit more furniture. I like the decor, and the bathroom/shower was very nice. Desk was very spacious. Coffemaker was good too. They have gotten rid of the minibar and instead offer some sort of room service. I didn't use it; I wish there was just a minibar like in most hotels. Being connected to the mall is a great plus. It's a very nice mall, with a lot of dining options. The Oceanaire is a chain, but a nice one. I was here on business, and from that standpoint the hotel is OK, but quite honestly I would be just as happy being in the Hyatt DFW and not having to travel back and forth. But if you are planning to visit Dallas for fun, this is a nice hotel.

“Great Hotel, Unusual Location” This hotel was quite comfortable and in a convenient location - particularly for those who want to travel without renting a car. Prepare yourself that it's immediate surroundings are industrial buildings - not other hotels and restaurants. However, Old Town's restaurants and tourist attractions are an easy walk away (you might not feel as comfortable walking after dark). The Old Town Transit Center connects you to trolleys, buses and commuter rail. A cab to the airport was $14 (w/out tip). The front desk staff were extremely helpful in giving us directions to sites we wanted to visit. Plenty of options for breakfast at the hotel's buffet. Pool was pleasant. Would definitely consider a stay there again.

“New Years on 16th Street Mall” We went to the New Years celebration on the 16th Street Mall for 2008/2009. We decided to stay at the Sheraton due to the price and availability. It was a decent hotel, not spectacular but nice. The rooms were clean. The sheets and bed left some comfort to be desired. The bathroom was very small as was the bath tub. Be prepared for a parking experience. If you valet park up front you can park in front of the hotel and check-in. If you are not using valet, you drive around the corner, park in the garage and then go all the way up the elevator to the lobby before checking in. We were quite displeased to see the real glasses insetad of the plastic wrapped cups for sanitary reasons. The cups were not clean and had what looked like food or something else on them. Most hotels have gone to the sealed cups due to health reasons. We had some drinks at Players (Sheraton's sports bar) for the new years celebration and it was a nice place. The staff were quite pleasant.

“Best Courtyard Yet” I am Platinum Marriott Member. Stayed one night on business trip to catch early flight. Hotel is very close to airport. Shuttle is only for Marriott and Courtyard so wasnt to crowded in the morning but I'm sure that varies. Lobby looks to be newly renovated as do the rooms. Nice large rooms very clean and updated. HD TVs with typical selection of channels. Nice workspace. Bath rooms are a bit small as the sink is outside in the living area. Beds were VERY comfortable with quality linens. Eat dinner in the deli downstairs. Food was actually much better than I expected. Limited slection but pretty much something for everyone and prices not to bad. Not sure what I recieved as a Platinum member if anything but I would definetly stay here again as long as price is right! All the staff I spoke with were friendly and helpful. Dont remember if AC was central or wall unit as I never turned it on but slept great.

“Gemütliches Hotel in Flughafennähe” Ich war auf der Durchreise und übernachtete hier eine Nacht. Die Verkehrsanbindung ist wirklich optimal. Subway läuft direkt am Hotel vorbei und nur 2 Stationen vom Airport O'Hare entfernt (Station Cumberland). Über die Fussgängerbrücke rüber und schon ist man im Hotel. Von hier kann auch die Weiterreise auf den Flughafen Midway angetreten werden. Vom Hotel mit der blauen Linie bis nach Clark/Lake und dort umsteigen in die Orange Linie nach Midway. Reisedauer ca. eine Stunde von O'Hare bis Midway. Das Hotel war beim CI sehr schnell und ich wurde nach Stockwerk und Bettenwunsch gefragt. Bekommen habe ich ein Zimmer mit riesen Wohnraum ein Schlafzimmer und ein großes Bad mit Dusche und WC. Bei Reklamationen reagierte man prompt ( das WC war verstopft - und innerhalb von 10 Minuten war der Klemptner vor Ort). Zimmer sehr sauber. Kühlschrank und Safe stehen kostenlos zur Verfügung. Die einzige Beeinträchtigung die ich finde ist der Fluglärm, da das Hotel direkt unter der Einflugschneise steht. Darum auch Nachts etwas laut. Aber das sollte man bei einem Flughafenhotel immer im Hinterkopf haben. Abreise um 04:00 früh funktionierte freundlich und schnell. Hierbei wurde ich noch gefragt, ob ich den kostenlosen Shuttle nach O'Hare benützen möchte. Ich habe über Priceline das Hotel für unter $ 70,- erhalten, und habe somit beim Umrechnungskurs von 1,5 ein super Schnäppchen gemacht. Alles in allem ein angenehmes Hotel. zur Umgebung: Auf der anderen Ubahn- Straßenseite befindet sich Dominick's Shopping Center. Dort kann man auch Tageskarten für die Bahn kaufen, die es leider in O'Hare am Flughafen NICHT gibt. O'Hare verkauft nur ab 3 Tagen aufwärts. Die Karten gelten für 24 Stunden und nicht so wie in NYC von Mitternacht bis Mitternacht. Dadurch besteht auch die Möglichkeit beim Abflug am nächsten Morgen das Ticket wieder zu verwenden. (Preis $5,75 1-Day Fun Pass) Jederzeit gerne wieder!!

“Great city, great hotel” It's unusual, but I really have nothing bad to say. Ok, I'm not keen on the single serve coffee makers, I kind of like having the whole 4 cups available, nor was I impressed by two sugars but only ONE creamer in the coffee condiment package -- but really.... I picked the hotel based on reviews, location, and the fact that they offered luggage storage. I arrived in Chicago at 10:00 am, with a check in of 3:00pm, While there was a possibility the hotel could get me in early, why take a chance on having to wander the cite WITH my luggage. I simply parked it at the hotel and started my sight-seeing. By the time I came back, the room was ready, my luggage was safe, and I was a happy camper. At the end of my trip, my train didn't leave until 6pm, I was able to leave my luggage with the porter and do more sight-seeing, again, WITHOUT the luggage. The room was spacious, as was the bathroom (I loath the tiny bathrooms!). A king bed, large chair, desk, wireless internet (FREE!), flat screen TV w/DVD. and so on. Ok, I had no real view, but I wasn't paying for one, either. Breakfast was pretty darn good. Ok, so I'm a "make your own waffle" fanatic -- and that's what I did, love it. There were also scrambled eggs available (unfortunately well OVER-cooked and rubbery balls both mornings), and bacon on Saturday, sausage gravy on Sunday (w/biscuits, of course). The food was hot and plentiful. There was also a selection of fruits, as well as the obligatory pastry/toasts selection. Coffee, tea, cocoa, and juices at the ready. Three blocks from Millennium Park, a couple of blocks from the Chicago River -- ideally situated. I'm a walker, I walked to Lake Michigan, Shedd Aquarium, Magnificent Mile, Museum of Contemporary Art (Northside), and so on. My feet were dying at the end of each day, but the distances were not the problem. I fell in love with Chicago over these 2.5 days (of course, it was MAY -- February might find my opinion slightly less positive), and intend to return. This hotel will be first on my list.

“Ideal Midtown location - good value” The Wolcott hotel is one of New Yorks hidden secrets despite its Midtown location. I first stayed at The Wolcott in 1998 when it was one of the cheapest hotels in the area, 2012 was my third stay at the Hotel and decor wise it doesn't seem to have changed a great deal during the intervening years, the hotel as the air of having seen better days but its still good value for money. The Wolcott is located on West 31st St between Broadway and 5th Avenue and is in easy walking distance of The Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden, Times Sq and the theater district. The hotel lobby gives the hotel a slight hint of grandeur, the rooms are adequately furnished and clean, the bathroom had a toilet, bath and shower. My overnight weekday stay cost $140 for a double room. New York hotel staff don't seem to be the friendliest so don't expect service with a smile when checking in. Ideally located, good value for money.

“A nice little hotel that grew on me” We booked this hotel for the convenient location to a business venue, which was stellar. The lobby and entrance are beautiful, a blend of historic architecture and clean modern decor. We reserved a superior room which is really a mini suite with a little kitchenette area, a sitting area and adjacent queen bed. We arrived late at night and at first glance, the room was a little disappointing.
