The furnishings are a tad shabby and in need of an update, but two days into a four day stay everything else about the property trumped any negatives we felt about our room. The big walk in shower was great. The kitchenette was great. The free wifi was great. The beautiful second floor lounge with Keurig coffee/tea maker/newspapers/workstations/fireplace/comfortable sitting areas was great. The refillable water bottle stations on every floor were great. The guest supply closets on every floor were pretty good if you needed extra coffee packets/cream/sugar for your room...otherwise they were empty. Guest services was great when we requested a second blanket and extra towels. The location, situated on the river on Wacker just off Michigan Avenue, can't be beat for wherever you want to go in the city. Oh, and one last thing....we slept great every night. The place is solid and the rooms super quiet. Very little outside noise and almost no hallway or adjacent room noise.

“Stuck in the middle.” I think I'll break this review into pros and cons, because we had a nice stay overall but I can see why some people would hate this place. So here are the facts and you can see if it is a place that would fit into your expectations/lifestyle. For informational purposes, we had a painted one-bedroom suite. PROS: Location, location, location. Easy walk to metro lines and BART, close to Market and union square. Funky decor: it was great having a painted room, and living within the art. The room was large, as we had the 1-bedroom suite. Two TVs (not that we used them). Free breakfast. Beautiful clawfoot tub in bathroom. CONS: Taxi drivers have never heard of it, so have the address on hand. Very narrow stairway, and an ancient elevator where you have to pull back the metal grate. Fine for us, but definitely will be difficult for anyone with a disability. One morning the garbage truck came and made an incredible racket around 6am. Not cool. Bathroom is teeny-tiny with old-fashioned fixtures (as it separate faucets for hot and cold), and the water pressure was bad and the temperature in the shower inconsistent. Be careful if you have kids. The door to the room did not have any additional safety locks, it just locks the door behind you... it needs a chain lock or something at least. The lighting in the room was terrible, very dim, the entryway was completely unlit and that was where the only mirror that was functionable was. Okay, so I know I have a lot more cons than pros listed, but honestly the place wasn't so bad. I would recommend it to a friend, but I don't think I would stay there again unless the deal was incredible. And a lot of the rooms have shared bathrooms, which is definitely not for me, but if you are looking for a budget hotel I think this is a good choice. For the price we paid per night for the one-bedroom, we probably could have gotten a generic room at a nicer hotel, but overall I am glad we stayed here for the novelty of it all. Oh, and when we were waiting for our ride to the airport outside the hotel after checking out, the secret service pulled up and Nancy Pelosi went into the salon/cafe next door. So that was pretty cool.

“Standard chain room, good location, poor exercise room” I stay at this chain while in NYC - first time at this site (4in NYC). Affordable, 3 blocks from Times Square. Bed was great. You can bypass the counter for checkin & checkout by using the automated kiosks. I travel 3-4 nights per week, so exercise is important. This ite has the worst exercise room in NYC. One treadmill and weighted balls. Their other NYC sites have an elliptical as well. However - I have seen many low cost NYC hotels with no exercise facilities, but this chain targets business travelers. Had breakfast acros the street at the Cafe Manhattan. Good food but awful coffee.

“Very Nice Hotel” My family of 5 stayed at Double Tree for the National Karate Tourament. Rest of our group stayed at Hyatt. Comparing notes, my family got the better deal. We received great rate through AAA (average $100 per night plus tax and parking) The cookies were a nice treat. Our kids received cookies many times (Suggest that they give cookies without nuts).Our shuttle service was great, we didnt use our car for anything downtown. The only drawback is that Houston itself is like a ghost town...no activity.most of the small restaurants are closed...only open during business hours. SO if traveling with kids...this hotel doesnt have microwave or refridgerator...so eating here can be expensive. The underground walk tunnel is only open m-f from 6 to 6...so you cant go down during weekend to get cheaper breakfast. Although, we shared the breakfast and the food was good and much less expensive then Hyatts. Our hotel was much more updated and quiet compared to Hyatt. And members from our group said Hyatt did not have shuttle that was readily available. SO it was a nicer hotel, less expensive for food, better services. The staff was very friendly in a businesslike manner. Very happy with our stay.

“Conveniently Located” My wife and I stayed here for a few days while on vacation. We found the hotel's location on the freeway to provide convenient access to many area attractions. The area in which the hotel is situated is a little sterile and is centered around the freeway, but there are plenty of restaurants and shops within a minute or two of driving, and Old Town is nearby as well; I would highly recommend an evening in Old Town. The hotel appeared clean inside and the room was satisfactory. The only complaint I have is that the housekeeping staff left us with no wash cloths on one particular day, which was annoying.

“It was a fine residential hotel but now a major rip off aimed at tourists” I used to live in North Beach, SF in the mid 2000's. The city is made up of many residential hotels or SRO's (Single Room Occupancy) hotels because of the insanely high price of rent for a "normal apartment". I stayed at this hotel for several weeks after being driven out of another nearby SRO due to massive bed bug infestation. At this time the "Hotel North Beach" was called "Saint Paul Hotel" and was just another resident hotel but one of those that were kept up better and a haven for many that had been driven out of the various nearby Residential Hotels because the bedbug problem was massive and not being addressed. The Saint Paul Hotel cost less then $200 a week to stay at even with the hotel tax added. A room could be had for one night for $29. A company called Mosserco owns this building along with some others - a mix of tourist hotels, resident hotels and regular apartment buildings. Apparently along with the name change Mosserco has decided to hike the price of this property and sell it as a tourist hotel. Now they are asking upwards of 60-70 dollars a night for rooms that used to be $29 only a few years back? I finally moved out of SF because living in this city comfortable requires either a minimum of a 6 figure income or the ability to live with half a dozen roommates. No choice was acceptable when I was getting into my mid-40's age wise. San Francisco is just getting far too uppity to gain much respectability from me anymore and to anyone who considers staying here this used to be someone's HOME. Now why do you think there are so many HOMELESS in San Francisco. I could be one of them but I just left for a cheaper location and my dignity intact.

“Toplage in San Diego” Das Hotel liegt direkt an der Marina von San Diego und hat somit eine sehr gute Lage. Auch in die Innenstadt und in das Gas Lamp Quarter kann man innerhalb weniger Minuten gelangen. Das Hotel ist von aussen komplett verspiegelt und hat insgesamt eine sehr beeindruckende Architektur. Die Zimmer sind zwar großzügig, aber dafür ist die Einrichtung bereits ein wenig veraltet und könnte erneuert werden. Ich hatte ein Hotelzimmer zur Stadt hinaus, aber auch diese Aussicht war sehr beeindruckend. Das Hotel verfügt über mehrere Restaurants die für jeden Geldbeutel das passende Gericht anbieten. Die Poollandschaft im Hotel ist sehr weitläufig und interessant angelegt.

“Great hotel” Stayed at the Palomar overnight for a business trip. Rooms are elegantly appointed. Bed was comfortable and bathroom was spotless. Members of Kimpton's loyalty program - free - get free and fast Wifi. The hotel's bar on the first floor has great service and fine cocktails. Waitstaff and bartenders are friendly and helpful. They will hook you up with a great drink. Just ask. In all, the Palomar is a great hotel close to the business area of downtown Chicago. It is close to the subway, too. While the Sax hotel nearby is good and has an even better bar, I'd stay at the Palomar over it.

“Just in the right spot....” I recently stayed at the Crowne Plaza for a convention at the Denver Convention Center. It is in a fantastic spot. It literally took me 4 minutes to walk from the lobby of the hotel to the lobby of the convention center. Sure the entrance of the hotel is unappealling, but the gracious staff and comfortable rooms made up for it. I had seen previous complaints about the rooms, but my room on the 16th floor seemed updated. There were nice touches like a bedside kit to make you sleep better, although it was not needed. My room was also closest to the elevator so I was concerned it might be noisy, but it wasn't. The other nice thing is the location, it is in walking distance to all the LoDo restaurants/shops and to the Latimer Square shops and restaurants.

“Location and atmosphere were excellent” We loved the modern look of the property and the room. The location was close to everything we wanted to see in that par of Boston. I had planned on trying to use the water taxi from the airport to the hotel, but after waiting 15 minutes, no bus came by our terminal, so we took a taxi instead. The taxi turned out to be less expensive anyway. The room was clean and comfortable. My only complaint, and it's minor, is the sliding window between the bedroom and the bathroom. Nice concept, but if someone got up in the middle of the night to use the restroom, it pretty much lit up the whole place. Would have preferred solid panels. We didn't eat there but did have a few drinks at the bar. Nice atmosphere there as well. Overall, if I could get the same rate I got on this trip, I'd make it my first choice in Boston.

“Nice choice for Chicago” We have stayed at a number of Chicago hotels, and the Renaissance was a wonderful choice. It is centrally located (especially if you want to see Wicked), has the most comfortable beds, and a nice gym free to guests. We had a river view which was lovely. I would highly recommend this hotel.

“kind of weird” loved the bed--super comfortable (we actually over-slept for father's day brunch....ooops!) the room was clearly newly furnished, but furniture is this bizarre looking traditional style but with asian hardware to make it look contemporary. i am in the design business so am super attentive to that, but my husband agreed....odd. also, in room refrigerator has a large scrolling digital screen that glows bright green at night. i like a dark room and that drove me crazy as i was trying to fall asleep. bathroom was in need of some re-caulking, counter was acrylic (vs. granite or marble) overall the room wasn't as nice as another 3 star we stayed in the previous night. and the parking situation....they have a teensy tiny drop off/pick up area that is a total disaster. the attendants do not speak english well and are very difficult to interpret. also, the area is so small with only one exit/entrance area that cars are constantly getting blocked in by other cars. disastrous and frustrating!

“Unfriendly reception” Stay in this hotel has left inconsistent memoirs. Rooms are beautifully decorated, but in the winter in them is very cold. Heaters work badly. The hotel personnel as a whole is friendly, but some workers talk to visitors very roughly. In particular receptionist Mr Randy alan Ogoff it is very rough, unfriendly, dares to offend visitors, often pretends that doesn't hear, when to him address. The main advantage of this hotel is its location. From here it is possible to reach many sights of New York by foot.

“Lovely people, lovely hotel” Was not sure what to expect, as we were not familiar with this part of downtown LA. We were very pleasantly surprised from the moment we arrived: extremely gracious front desk staff, attractive lobby (with people actually sitting and relaxing in the lobby, always a good sign), nice roomy room with a great view of garden and downtown LA. The bed was a bit firmer than we are used to, but maybe that's what we need because we both slept very well. Also had a fun couple of hours spent wandering around Little Tokyo. No complaints at all -- we will be back!

“Can't Beat the Price” Chose this hotel because it was close to where we were going. Not the best place if you are coming for the Denver sites, but if the location fits your plans, you cannot beat this Doubletree for the price. We paid $89. Spacious and pleasant. Extremely helpful staff. We needed a 2nd room due to a miscommunication and they handled it with terrific customer service and a great compromise. Look forward to returning again soon.

“Nice stay at the Sheraton Boston” I will have to admit that I was not thrilled when I discovered my company had booked our business group at a Sheraton. My past experiences with Sheraton were less than stellar; and I am admittedly biased towards Marriott! However, I was very pleased with the Sheraton Boston. It is a large property; with both North and South Tower accommodations. Our room was in the South tower. The room was large; the bathroom a nice size with a large vanity. The decor was a little dated but it was clean. The hotel itself is very conveniently located as it is attached to the Hynes Convention Center and the Prudential Center. The Prudential Center offers access to the green subway line as well as numerous upscale shops and good restaurants. Be advised that the Sheraton charges for internet; apparently per computer rather than per room. I asked about the double charges for internet on my bill and was asked if there was more than one computer in the room. My husband had his laptop as well; and I have never stayed in a hotel where they charged anything other than a flat daily rate for internet. They did remove the duplicate charges, but I find those charges to be a little ridiculous. There is a business area available in the lobby with computers and printing capabilities; but be aware that if you print your boarding passes there, your room will be charged for those copies as well. It always puzzles me that the more upscale hotels, which charge higher rates, include less complimentary amenities (internet, copies, breakfast, etc). We did not use the hotel's restaurant facilities and so cannot comment on those. There are breakfast options in the Prudential Center which I would imagine are more economical than those at the Sheraton. Bottom line is that this is a nice hotel; conveniently located; good business hotel.

“Lovely hotel in a good location” This is a really nice hotel and very reasonably priced. It's location is not bad at all as there is a really frequent bus service to go downtown and an airport bus, both of which cost $2 for a 24 hour ticket. It's also literally across the road from a the greyhound station which is so convinient if you take the bus to Austin. Beware of the staff as I suspect they are being paid to recommend using taxis, the girl on the check-in desk tried to convince us that we needed a taxi to get downtown, which we did not. The rooms are beautiful, the staff generally friendly and there's an ihop next door! Can't fault it really..

“Great Hotel Stay in Pacific Heights” My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Drisco for three nights in July 2011. The hotel is in a prime Pacific Heights location, the rooms are well appointed, the staff is very professional and friendly, and the breakfast was excellent. The reason for our stay is that we were moving from the neighborhood, and we needed to stay in a hotel near our home during our move. Regardless if you are moving, in town for business, or on vacation in the city, I would highly recommend this hotel -- you will enjoy your stay in this prime location of the city!

“Nice - recently upgraded?” Got a very good deal on this, and it was very nice for the price for NYC. When we checked in everyone was very courteous and friendly, and we were upgraded to a bigger room. Looks as if it has been renovated to a boutique style recently, and the furniture, bed, and so-on were new and attractive. In a nice area of the Upper West Side, close to subway and Museum of Natural History. There are parking garages directly across 77th street.

“Great hotel in Dallas” I travelled to Dallas with my wife back in May 2003. We really wanted to stay in Downtown Dallas. We choose Hotel Lawrence. The hotel was very nice nad with a cozy atmosphere. Staff was really nice to us. Breakfast was included. And it was ok! Hotel Lawrence also has a free shuttle service to downtown sights and restaurants that we used. It was perfect. Visitor center was just 2 or 3 blocks up the street from our hotel. We really recommend the McKinney Ave Trolley that took us through all of downtown Dallas. It was exciting and fun! We also loved the Rodeo show of course. Try Mesquite Rodeo, about a 15-20 minute cabride or drive with your own car.

“comfortable but needs a little polish” Don't get me wrong, the Iroquios is a great hotel in an excellent location on 44th st. It's just that the little things weren't quite nailed and it's often those little things that make the difference between a good hotel and an excellent one. My business colleagues stayed at the Morgans group's Royalton across the street at the same price which although much hipper and up to date than the Iroquios was more of a scene (and a potentially noisier one at that). On the con side: - I arrived an hour earlier than check-in time so they may have rushed my room cleaning, particularly the vacuuming. When I checked into my room after 3pm, I nearly stepped on a safety pin embedded in the carpet and at a closer look found other small plastic objects in the carpet, so clearly vacuuming wasn't adequate. -I booked a wake up call which didn't happen -The bathrooms are a little tired -There was a wall safe in the room (which is a pro!) attached to an exterior wall. The door was wide open and I couldn't figure out how to close it. As it was at shin height blocking the walkway to the bathroom I had to wedge a lamp up against it to prevent injury. Pro's: -The beds are heavenly! Soooo comfortable and topped with plush feather duvets. -Staff are friendly -the Gilly espresso at the Triomphe restaurant (which is part of the hotel ) is so good it's up to European standards! -My room was very quiet - not a sound heard. -wireless internet is free

“Great Hotel” I would recommend this hotel, it is in a good location, the complimentary breakfast is very good and the staff are nice. The beds are very comfortable but the adjoining room can be noisy as the sounds rise up from the reception area. We had a few problems though, our online booking and payment got duplicated in an obvoius error and it was a nightmare getting a refund from this hotel, also when we arrived we were told that our room type was not available even though we had paid for 7 months prior! We did manage to sort our problems out but I got the impression we weren't the only guests to be messed about.

“Can't wait to go back!!” What a great weekend! The hotel is awesome. The staff is outstanding. The location is great. We pulled into the Valet, the doorman asked if we had plans. We said no and he handed us tickets to the Rockies game that started in 10 minutes. We dropped our luggage off and then walked through the lobby and out the front door to walk to the game (it's only 7 blocks away) and the doorman stopped us again and offered us a ride to the game in the Hotels Rolls Royce. The driver was friendly and treated us like royalty. People were taking our picture was we pulled up to the game in the Rolls Royce. The staff and rooms were outstanding. Looking forward to my next trip to Denver - it will definitely be another stay at the Ritz!

“Great Stay in New York” Having stayed in Sofitel hotels in Europe we booked this on personal knowledge along with the reviews on TripAdvisor. We weren't disappointed and spent 4 great nights in New York. The hotel is ideally situated and the rooms are very spacious. The staff were very friendly and extremely professional and we even made use of the room service which I normally avoid. We would certainly stay here again and would recommend it to our friends.

“High Quality Hotel, Convenient to Airport” We made a last minute reservation here for a 7 day park and fly (one-night) stay, and then paid for a couple extra nights of parking at a very reasonable rate. It is a beautiful, high-quality hotel with a nice interior and very clean rooms. There was a bit of confusion on our arrival... when asked, we were told by a bellman standing outside that we should immediately pull into the garage for our stay, park and fly package rather than temporarily park outside the lobby to register and unload our bags. Well, that wasn't quite correct, and we were faced with having to try and carry all our bags through the garage and take an elevator four floors up to the lobby from the parking garage. We decided to leave our bags in the car and check in first... and the front desk was very apologetic when we asked for a bell cart. They sent a bellman all the way down into the parking garage with us to help with the rest of our bags we'd left in the car. They recovered very well from this oversight. We felt completely safe and very taken care of here. A few things to note: the garage ceilings are VERY low.... our Ford Explorer barely made it to the regular parking spaces. There is a sign that states if you have a high profile car, you will have to use the valet parking. Food in the restaurant and cafe is a bit pricey, but there are plenty of choices to be had. They offer complimentary printing of boarding passes in the lobby, which was great! We had no problems catching their free shuttle to the airport at 8AM, but when we returned to the hotel, it seemed the outbound airport shuttle had at least a 30-40 minute wait. Plan appropriately to get to the airport on time during busy shuttle hours. There is an outdoor pool on one of the upper levels, but it's quite small and of course there's lots of airliner noise to contend with. Still, it's a great place for kids to burn off a little steam... and they have four hot tubs surrounding the pool, which is great for parents. You can keep an eye on your kids in the pool while getting a little relaxation yourself. All in all, I'd highly-recommended this hotel if you need to stay near the airport for a flight in or out.

“wonderful hotel and great location” I have never stayed at a Homewood Suites hotel before and now I am sold! This property is located along the bay and is centrally located. The hotel is 1 mile from the airport, 2 miles from an In-N-Out, 2 miles from Ralph's grocery store, 10 minute drive from Balboa Park, 10 minute drive to Seaport Village and 2 miles from C-Level Restaurant, one of our favorite restaurants. Parking is free as well as internet in the room. Breakfast is free which consists of eggs, sausage, oatmeal, bagels, fruit, waffles, juices, coffee. The property is very well maintained and the rooms are large. We stayed in Room 303 which overlooked the bay. It was a king size suite with a double pull out sofa. The kitchen is complete with a coffee maker, full size refrigerator, dishwasher, and a cooktop. The staff is wonderful and I would highly recommend this hotel. We would definitely come back. There is a great exercise room as well as an outdoor pool.

“Nice stay at the Alexander Inn” The Alexander Inn was a pleasant surprise. I had actually booked it as a last resort because my first choice hotel was booked solid. The room was adorable and clean. The art deco decor and original artwork (all by original Philadelphia artists) made for a charming ambiance. The attention paid to service was above average. A continental breakfast buffet hit the spot with fresh pastries, bagels, fruit, yogurt, etc. All in all a lovely place to stay.

“GREAT Location!” Great stay at Westin. The location is excellent: 1) Safe neighborhood (I was at ease walking our kids at night), 2) 5 blocks from Pike Place Market, 3) 15 minute walk to the Seattle Center and Space Needle (you could also take the monorail across the street that will take you directly there), 4) Across the street from Seattle's shopping district (and great restaurants like the infamous Top Pot doughnuts), 5) Across the street is the Light Rail station which takes you to and from the airport so you won't need a car and pay the high parking prices ($22/night), if you rely on these great (and clean) Seattle transportation. We also took in a Mariners game which was easy to get to from the Light Rail. The concierge was also fantastic in getting us around town. The indoor swimming pool was also great for the kids. Perhaps the only negative was the room was small compared to other Westin's we've been to, but we definitely will be returning the next time we find ourselves in the beautiful city of Seattle.

“Loved the view and the location.” Very nice hotel in a nice area. Many choices in rooms, and the fireplace outside with comfortable chairs was very enjoyable. The staff was friendly and helpful. We would recommend this hotel to friends visiting San Diego.

“Not a Lot of Options in Downtown Houston: Service is Always A Plus at The Four Seasons” Well, I'll admit I struggled as to whether I should rate this property as a 3 or 4. One thing you can always count on at the Four Seasons, anywhere, is excellent service. Service was pretty great, but the property itself seems a little neglected. With that said, this is a rather tired Four Seasons. The room where I stayed--especially bathroom-- could stand to be updated to match other properties. Soundproofing between rooms as well as hallway also seemed to be lacking. There were several weddings the weekend I arrived, so it was a bit chaotic, and staff seemed less attentive to us non wedding party people than usual. Understandable, I suppose. A nice amenity is the large outdoor pool w/jacuzzi and bar area. Some rooms lead directly to the pool with poolside patios. If you want some sun and fun, I recommend those rooms, which also provide 24 hr access to the area while others are restricted between late evening and early morning. The fitness room is also quite nice and was in the process of being refurbished at the end of my stay. A real negative for the hotel, that I have not experienced at other Four Seasons, was poor quality food. I ate in the somewhat touted restaurant and it was really mediocre, especially for the money. The menu items sounded good but the execution was less than pleasing: too creamy, too saucy, too salty, etc. I also ordered room service one morning and I was equally disappointed with the poor food quality. And, on a side note, I was charged $7 for an 8 ounce cup of coffee at the pool, when unknowingly, just steps away in the fitness room, there was free coffee and tea. I never signed for the coffee, so could not dispute it at the time. The staff did remedy this charge upon check out as they were in equal disbelief that this was the charge. BUT, with these factors aside, if you have to stay in downtown Houston, not sure you will find a better place.

“Very pleased, great service” Stayed here for work and was amazed by the fantastic service. Free shuttle from the hotel (must be arranged in advance), a bottle of water & NutriGrain bar at check-in (note I am a preferred member), polite & outgoing staff, and every room is a suite. The suite was ideal for business travel--lots of plugs, a desk in the main room plus a work area in the little living room in the front. They also have a cute little Holiday Inn museum on the 2nd floor outside the elevators that's worth taking a quick walk-through. Negatives worth noting: Tub needed to be reglazed around the drain, there's not much natural light in the room, and the curtains don't come flush with the wall on the sides so they let in light at night, which affects sleep quality. Overall, though, a nice place.

“Solid Pick” I stayed here for a couple nights in December 2008 right before Christmas. The hotel is a great represenation of the Westin chain. It is several steps ahead of everyone else, but is still affordable and luxurious for the comman man/woman. This isn't the best Westin, but its a solid pick for comfort and treating yourself. Best Things about this hotel: 1. Location. Its located on the riverwalk, but not next to the restaurants and bars in order to have some peace and quiet. You can easily walk to all of the riverwalk items by going out the front entrance and walking two blocks. 2. Conciege. By far the best knowledgable and friendliest concierge staff I've experienced. They were able to give us recommendations for each day we were there based upon our interests. Not only were we told about things to do in San Antonio, but also instructed on what things were available in Austin since we were open to anything. Hotel parking is high (like any downtown hotel), but there is a parking garage across the street if you want to save some money. If you head to San Antonio, I recommend you stay here.

“Wonderful stay.” The Warwick is a wonderful hotel with a lot of history. The lobby is wonderful and from the moment you step in front of its doors the bellman is ready to help you with your luggage and anything else you may need. We checked in early, and even though I had mention during my reservation that I needed a city view room, I got a room with no views at all. However, I went to the lobby again and spoke with the gentleman there and he kindly advised that since we had checked in early there weren't any more available rooms, but that if we could wait until 3pm he would get us what we wanted. We agreed and they stored our bags for no charge, and so we went to explore the city. At 3 pm sharp we were there and we got an amazing room on the 11th floor facing Avenue of the Americas. The hotel is conveniently located on 52nd st and Ave of the Americas. It's really close to everything, subways, starbucks, MOMA..but it's in the perfect location because you don't get all the hectic noise from times square. I've been in New York a few times and the quality of these rooms were very good. They were very spacious compared to other hotels in the area. The beds were amazingly comfortable and the bathrooms were perfectly clean. You don't get free wi-fi in the bedrooms, if I don't remember wrong it's about $10 dollars per day, but they do have a business center where you cant print your tickets etc..for free and you also get a limited time of free internet per day. There's a little fridge in the rooms that has some snacks, but beware, they're really expensive. Just go get some bottles of water at a supermarket that's down the street and you should be good. Walking distance from Radio city, Rockefeller, MOMA, restaurants, Duane Reed, Times Square, Subways, Central Park etc. The last day of our stay our flight was late at night but check out was around 12pm, so they stored our bags for no extra charge and with no time limit. The last day the receptionist looked a bit grumpy, but I would definitely go back to the Warwick!

“Nice Property but Terrible Service” The hotel property itself is very nice. It is situated in beautifully landscaped business park and is in a quiet location. The lobby is lovely as well. The rooms are about average for a hotel of this caliber. We used the self parking, which is located behind the hotel and is a short walk from the property. It is not inconvenient and gives you an opportunity to walk past the pond with the black swans in residence. It is also free. We signed up as members of the hotel's Select Guest program and as a benefit, the hotel staff delivered complimentary beverages to our room each morning. They were always very prompt and our orders were always correct. We were also given bottled water on our first night's stay, which is also a benefit of the Select Guest program. The deplorable service, however, overshadowed the nice things about our stay. When we arrived there was no one to help with bringing our luggage into the hotel. The front desk staff was quite efficient, but they were not particularly friendly and did not give us any information about the hotel, parking, etc. The first evening of our stay, as we were getting ready for dinner, we noticed there was no shampoo in the room. It took three calls to housekeeping to get it delivered and they were quite surly about our request. The following morning, the toilet would not flush and we had to wait for a technician to come and repair it. The pool area was always littered with towels and trash from prior guests and no one ever came to clean it up. There was also a security guard "patrolling" the pool area. His presence did not make anyone feel welcome, as he followed several guests around. On check out, our bill was incorrect, so that necessitated another trip to the front desk to fix the problem. I was looking forward to a relaxing stay at a hotel brand that is supposedly known for pampering its guests and making them feel welcome. I was very disappointed and would not stay at this property again.

“Loved the Omni!” I stayed at the Omni for 2 nights while on a business trip. Prices were obviously high, as expected for this hotel, but service was definitely up to par. Very friendly and helpful hotel staff. No complaints about anything at all. Food was great at both restaurants -- Noe (creme brulee is awesome!) and the Grand Cafe (french toast is wonderful!). Didn't use the gym facility, but it looked good. My room overlooked the pool and it was situated on a rooftop and looked nice (just too cold out to swim). The room was excellent. Very clean and beautiful bed. Nice bathrobes available to use as well. I did request a single king bed (my preference), but they only had 2 queens when I checked in. Not a major issue, but I did check in at 8am (regular check-in is 3pm I believe), so they were pretty accomodating. I highly recommend signing up for the Select Guest program that the Omni has (free to sign up on website). You get free internet access in your room (otherwise there is a charge) as well as your choice of newspaper in the mornings as well as 2 complimentary beverages each morning. A really great program for no charge, in my opinion. In addition, make sure to provide your mileage program number upon check-in so you earn mileage points for your stay. The location is okay for downtown access. It's connected to the California Plaza, so if you need to get to the Deloitte & Touche or KPMG bldgs, etc....this is the place to stay. Definitely easy access.

“My new NYC favourite” Usual preamble - over 150 nights a year in hotels across the globe from five star palaces to infested motels! So, know a good hotel when I stay in one, and boy is this place something special. I usually stay in either the Ritz Carlton in Central Park or the London, but this is now my second home in NYC. I stayed for two weekends, either side of a week of travel, and both visits were fantastic. The first room was a regular room on the 23rd floor facing east with a slight view uptown to the Empire State Building. The room was huge for NYC standards, the bed delightful and the kit in the room spectacular from the HD TV to a full kitchen sink in the room. The bathroom was very well appointed and the floor to ceiling windows (with electronic curtains) literally throw you into the heart of Soho. The décor is superb, and the position of the hotel excellent for shopping, eating and the subway right across the road. The second weekend I was upgraded to a amazing suite, with an attached lounge. The view was out to the Hudson and was just breathtaking up on the 27th floor. Essentially, you can not fault the hotel physically. There were a few minor (very minor) hiccups. The corridor noise when your in your room is quite annoying, and I think the doormen could do with a few weeks learning how they do it the Ritz Carlton. I know its a busy and narrow entrance to the hotel, but there isn't that 'welcome back' or personal feel yet among the door team. I am sure it will come in time. I also had to wait an hour for a breakfast, but without asking they offered it to me at no charge - that's a good recovery! So, overall - world class, and the minor snags will go over time. If, like me the painfully trendy Soho/Tirbeca hotels don't float your boat - but you still want contemporary excellence - then head here and you cant go wrong.

“2nd visit to Columbus Inn” We stayed at the Columbus Motor Inn a couple of years ago, so when we passed through San Fran on Sept 30 & Oct 1, we booked here again. Can't beat the price, especially with parking included. We had a king room that was equiped for the disabled, so that was a little different. We were on the lower floor, so the room had a bit of a musty smell. Tried to move to a higher floor, and were told they were totally booked, but might be able to get moved the next day. It wasn't bad enough to bother moving, so we just sprayed some cologne.Would stay here again, just request an upper floor. Great location in the city, we walked to everything.

“Showing its age” I've stayed here twice on business. I love Candlewoods because the rooms are comfortable - the desk in the room is perfect to work at - and the $0.25 sodas in the pantry are a nice perk. This one was looking a little worn on the inside. All of the usual Candlewood stuff is here - it's the same layout as all the other Candlewood Suites I've come across, but it is a bigger property than most. The pool is nice. In one room, there was a hole in the wall from someone opening the door too hard. In both rooms there was a fabric shower curtain that wasn't quite long enough and no vinyl liner behind it. The rooms at the front get a lot of freeway noise, so ask for a room at the back. If you need to be near downtown/market center and don't want to fight the traffic, go for this one, but if you don't mind the drive from Los Colinas, the Candlewood there is newer and nicer for about the same rate.

“Trendy to the last drop” The Ace is more about hobnobbing with your hipster brethren than a hotel stay experience. Tiny rooms are still pleasant and functional. Bathroom is minuscule with huge showerhead requiring you stand an inch away from the soap dispenser. Still, the lobby, the corridors, the bar, the restaurant - all fun. Location is cool as well. Staff is attentive and committed to the overall experience. Aim for rooms on as high a floor as possible. 3AM garbage collection outside felt intimately close from the 7th floor.

“Amazing view, a little pricey” I stayed here for a night in September and really did enjoy it. I was a little surprised about how the taxes and the parking charge added up, but I'm glad I stayed here. I particularly enjoyed many of the small touches that make Kimpton hotels unique. Number 1 was definitely the wine happy hour from 5-6 in the lobby., Just a nice, civilized thing that the hotel does. I enjoyed the selections of red and white wine. My room was spacious and the bathroom big. I particularly liked the expansive views my room had looking south over the city. I ordered room service in the morning and the food came quickly.l All the options on the menu were standard, but with a twist. i had the fruit and granola bowl, but it came with Acai berry juice drizzled over it. Very unique. Really enjoyed it. Valet service for my car was quick and expedient. Overall, I stayed here because it was a Kimpton and I do like the chain. While I liked it, I would reconsider staying here in the future if my business in LA wasnt right in the immediate Westwood or perhaps Beverly Hills area as transit can take awhile. Still, I liked it and would recommend it for those staying in the area.

“Basic & reliable” This is my hotel of choice in the Denver area with our office in the busy Tech Center. Lots of restaurant options and convenience to the highway make it a good location. This is standard Garden Inn fare. Unlike some other commentaries, I've found the staff to be friendly. Last time I was here the computers were down and they checked us in by hand and walked us to our rooms (couldn't print key cards). Agree on the comment about the views. Decent gym.

“Wouldn't recommend” I was disappointed. I arrived at midnight after fleeing Hurricane Rita, anxious to get some sleep. Instead, I listened to the hotel's plumbing. Very, very noisy plumbing. Some parts of the room looked recently updated, but other parts looked well worn. The location is awkward to access. Look elsewhere.

“Perfect for short stay” Great location in financial district, close to everything(public transportation and historical sites). Rooms are micro sized, very clean, modern and comfortable. Free wifi, filtered bottle water and use of iPads are nice. Nice bar restaurant is connected to lobby called Elephant & Castle serving British themed pub grub.

“Great place to stay in Chelsea” We have stayed at the Maritime several times over the past few years and we still love the place. Great location, especially if you need to be near the Chelsea art galleries which are walking distance, as is the HighLine. The rooms and bathrooms are small but well-designed. Good amenities. Great honor bar with everything one might want. The on-site bar and the restaurants are terrific and should not be missed. Matsuri is first-rate, and gorgeous. Service at the hotel is quite good; staffers are really responsive and efficient. The rooms could use a bit of rehabbing, but overall, it's still an excellent hotel and we will definitely return. Upper floor rooms are a bit quieter and have excellent views.

“Just Ok.” My group of 6 was in town for 4 nights, and because of a huge convention making finding rooms downtown difficult, we ended up at the Prescott. It's a boutique hotel with average sized rooms, and small bathrooms. There were no sleeper sofas, and no roll-aways available, so beware if you have an extra member of your group that might need one of the above. The thermostat in my room never worked and as a result the room was much too warm. Management said they would fix it - they never did. For $350+ a night we expected better. The window wouldn't open, so we just endured the heat. You receive vouchers for breakfast, which is the usual cereal/fruit/rolls/coffee/juice. For extra money you can get hot eggs, which we didn't do. There is a reception on the Club level from 4:30-6:30 that includes free drinks, cheese, and pizza - very nice. Also in the Club level is a computer and printer. We were going to use it to print out our boarding passes for the flight home...until we saw that it cost $7.95 for 15 minutes use. Not cool at all - we got our boarding passes at a kiosk at the airport instead. The two best things about the Prescott are the location - right downtown, close to the BART, buses, and cable cars...and the friendly help at the front desk and concierge. There was a revolving set of staff during our visit, but all were exceptionally helpful and friendly.

“Very clean and nice rooms but TERRIBLE beds” I'm usually extremely impressed by Hyatt properties and the level of service. Pretty much everything was perfect but the one thing that really matters at the end of the day was not - my ability to get a good night's sleep. The room was extremely clean and spacious and the staff was very friendly. They have free internet and the location is not too bad - everything in Houston is "far away" so it's not their fault. That being said, the bed was too soft and made it almost impossible to get a proper night's sleep. If they fix the beds, this would be a great place to stay.

“This Place Rocks” Spend one night at The Hard Rock. Love the location right on Michigan Ave with walking distance to almost everything. The room was clean, quiet and cool. The carpet and furniture showed very little signs of wear. The themes on each floor are make this more like a museum than a hotel. I was pleasantly suprise with quality of the hotel. Rock on.

“Average hotel.” This hotel is great for a quick stay - home base purpose. It is clean and have the basic amenities you can ask for such as fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. It also have a hair dryer. They have a little play area outside. Pet can say for $25 per stay. Pros: other than mentioned above- 1. Internet is fast 2. Free breakfast. 3. Location- location- location. Close to tons of restaurants and shops.Seawolrd is only 6 mins away and Fiesta Texas is probably about 10 mins. It's a great base if you are going to both theme parks. 4. Clean. Cons: 1. Standard room is small - you might want to opt to a suite instead if you are not on a budget. If you are, and this is just a place to sleep- its ok I guess. Again, this is a very basic - average hotel. A place to simply sleep. I got a great rate since I'm a choice hotel member ( its free by the way). You can register online at http://www.choicehotels.com I got this room for less than $60.00 per night! It's worth it. I do recommend it if you are going to both Seaworld and Fiesta Texas due to its proximity to both places. It is located along highway 1604 - next to La Quinta and Super 8 motel.

“Solid property for a city stay” Excellent location, walking distance to the capitol, bar area, city centre mall. Expect to pay for parking. Nice front desk staff and well appointed guest rooms, updated and clean. Flat screen TVs in both rooms of the suite.

“Big room, great bed, no exec club breakfast” Enjoying a large, clean room near Union Square without paying a fortune is a rarity in San Francisco. The new bedding and the "sleep kit" amenity really did help me sleep better in this lively city. The staff were very courteous and helpful. Usually I have access to the executive club breakfast room in Intercontinental Hotels, but they didn't have one here.... instead I went across the street to an authentic European cafe. The lobby of the hotel is small and busy; perhaps the elevators are not monitored as closely as they should be for people wandering in off the street. Overall, I was pleased and would return.

“Good value with Priceline” This is the second time a Priceline bid landed me a the Westin. The location is good in that its central to downtown and best of all close to Palace Kitchen a great eatery a block north. Parking is expensive but there is street parking free after 8 pm. They do charge for wifi in rooms, but lobby is free

“Great art-deco hotel” We stayed at the Beekman Tower in March 2005 and were impressed with the professionalism and friendliness of the staff; the size and cleanliness of the rooms; and the lovely view of the city from the 26th floor restaurant/bar. Architecturally speaking, this hotel is an art-deco gem. I'd highly recommend it, though other reviews did comment that it's not close to subway stops. (We took cabs and walked.)
“Very good” Great location. Great views across Missisippi River. Spacious room. Friendly staff. Perhaps only criticism is lack of guest laundry.

“Beautiful building, great staff, funky interesting hotel in a good location” Decided to meet someone on a quick side trip to Chicago. Booked an unknown hotel by a third party travel agent and it turned out to be the Hard Rock. Not being a huge fan of the restaurant chain I was skeptical but looked at online reviews and got excited to check it out. The building that the Hard Rock is in (Carbide & Carbon Building) is amazing. If you're a fan of architecture and design take a minute to look around. Tiny busy lobby. The staff was nice and always helpful. The room was tiny, colorful and funky. Simple but creative design in the room. Everything looked new and clean. Had a view of DT and in the distance the silver bean and the museum. Bed was big, clean and very comfy. Decent sized flat screen TV. Very limited channels. Room was quiet. Ordered room service twice and both times it was very good and quick. Bathroom was clean and big. Good toiletries. The concierge is awesome and will help you find great deals on local attractions. Gave great restaurant recommendations. Hard Rock in Chicago really is a nice hotel.

“Classy get-away” My husband and I spent the weekend here as a mini-vacation. Great location, very clean and comfortable room, fabulous restaurant (Eighty-One) on the premises. Enjoyed the old-world charm of the place.

“A family-friendly Hilton resort” Although I was going there as a follow traveller, I was primarily impressed as to how "family-friendly" the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak Resort is - with activities and services for everyone. The hotel itself is divided into two main buildings (South Pointe and North Pointe) and a separate "casita" section featuring townhome style accomodation. The back of the resort features all the water actitivities (lazy river, water slide, pools), as well as a "Western" village. Camp Coyote features activities for the younger kids and sending the kids to camp (registration recommended as space is limited) means that the adults can enjoy some free time on their own. There are a couple of reasonably priced, relatively casual restaurants scattered throughout the resort. Hotel also has a spa/massage/gym complex. There is a small shopping mall nearby with a few additional dining and fast-food options. This hotel is located North of the downtown area (NorthWest of the airport). Driving to/from the property is recommended but a taxi to/from the airport is also an affordable option if you only intend to stay at the resort and not venture out! Location is also good if you intend to do a day tour north of the city (such as Grand Canyon or Sedona desert with a tour company) as you are most likely to be amongst the last ones to be picked-up and first ones to return. As I was there during the extremely low season, I had the pleasure to be upgraded to one of the casitas - an oasis of peace! Bedroom upstairs, with a full kitchen and living room area downstair. Definitely enough space for a family. Bed was extremely comfortable and everything was in working order. Staff is extremely friendly. There are a couple of walking trails nearby (Squaw Peak/Dreamy Trail, ask map at frontdesk). For Gold and Diamond HHonors member, the complementary breakfast consist of 3 items of your choice at Starbucks. I highly recommend to "upgrade" to the full breakfast ($7) at Rico's American Grill

“very nice” Had a 2bedroom suit in the towers and it was beautiful .Our bathroom was a bedroom itself. The room service was excellent and the food was great... very expensive but that was to be expected. The hotel was staff was wonderful and we loved our stay. Location was very good we will return

“Nice Hotel” Nice Hotel in the Financial Area. My room looked at the Willis Tour so that was an added bonus. It is very close to the L and a Garrets Popcorn. The bathroom has the shower and tub separate and it was nice to have turn down service and chocolates every night when I arrived after dinner. All the food that I had there was great as well.

“Good for clean and convenient--totally lacking in NYC style” Clean and convenient. If that's what you're looking for this property fits the bill completely. Rooms are small but not out of line for this part of town. If you want bigger look at Westin or Times Square Hilton, both nearby. Rooms are very comparable to Comfort Inn on 39th, although more rooms per floor. Similar to Hampton Inn and Four Points, both within 4 blocks from here. You will notice on website that there are not many pictures. Really not much to take pictures of. Internet present and free, but slow. Block has parking lot, parking garage, building under construction, Birdland jazz club, Dykes lumber supply and an Italian restaurant. Not much to look at, but convenient. 9th Ave a plethora of food choices. Totally improved recently, that's the direction you should go to get fed. Still, while a little deserted it doesn't have the grungy feel of a few blocks south. Lobby more sterile feeling than anything. Standard Comfort Inn breakfast except no bananas. Good coffee all day long. Asked questions of the folks at the desk a few times. They were not the most informed--probably not native Manhattanites--but always gave a good effort. Busy street during the night. If convenient, competent and sterile is what you seek, this fits the bill. The only real drawback is that there are so many interesting properties in NYC that this seems boring by comparison. Westin and Hilton are much nicer, and just as convenient, although usually more expensive. Dream hotel has similar small rooms, but funky vibe. Lots of choices just east of Times Square. If the price is right it offers basic conveniences in a stellar location. Broadway theaters nearby, food galore, really no downside to worry about. Also, the folks that wrote that Macy's was 2 minutes away were staying at a different Comfort Inn at 35th and Broadway. Here you are about a mile. If expectations are managed they should be easily met. Enjoy your visit.

“Cozy hotel in the middle of a fantastic shopping area” We stayed at the Drake for 3 nights, as a start of our trip this summer. I liked the hotel and would return. First of all, I am not a fan of big chains hotels, that have lots of space and no personality. That said, this hotel is a charming place right in the middle of town. Don't expect big rooms, it is after all a remodeled old hotel. Bathrooms are tiny but extremely clean. Forget the big closets but the beds are soft and the decor really nice. Our room was pretty and well maintained. We had no noise issues. Location: great. I loved the fact that we could walk back to drop packages or change clothes without having to cross town. Last year we stayed at the Adagio on Geary st, nice rooms but a long walk from everywhere. We used also buses to move around town, there's a line next to Sacks that takes you practically anywhere. If you are tired and do not want to walk, there's also Sears restaurant in front of the hotel, offers good meals from breakfast to dinner. The staff was extremely helpful, the concierge great and we got all of the info we were looking for and some smiles too. Kids thought the bellman was awesome.

“Needs to be much better” I checked in to my room which was really small. I'm an Honors gold card holder and this room was on a dedicated Honors floor so thhis can't be the worst they have. There was just a bed and a desk in the room - no comfortable chair, no table for room service to be placed upon. When they deliver your room service breakfast they put it on the bed. The size of the bathroom was worse still. The room was only clean on the surface. Jutting out from underneath the bed was a blood stained towel and a large a amount of trash. These remained for the first two of the four nights I stayed there - as did the hairclips on the carpet. Room service breakfast took 50 minutes to arrive one morning. I called Guest Relations to tell them this and to let them know that there was no hot water in my bathroom. They just said they'd fix the water (which they did) but no word of an apology on either count. On other occasions when I called Guest Relations the phone remained unanswered. One evening I tried to use the pool. The Guest services Directory in the room was empty, the advert for the spa in the elevator told you this was on the 5th floor but it turns out its actually on the 8th floor. I went to the Spa reception on the 8th floor and the receptionist there directed me to the 7th for the pool. On the 7th there is a door to the pool and one toilet cubicle- no changing facility or showers. I retunred to the 8th floor and they told me I could access the pool form there (where there were proper locker rooms) but that 'I wouldn't be able to get back'. I said this was crazy - they agreed, but again did nothing further to help - so don't plan to use the pool because, although it is newly renovated and looking good, this is impossible apparently. On checking out I joined the Honors line. It didn't move and no effort was made to clear it. After 15 minutes I joined the main line which, although slow, moved eventually. The automatic doors to enter and leave the property also move way too slowly - really irritating after a number of days staying there. The newly renovated public areas of this hotel look great - the bar etc., but I really cant think of anything else that I enjoyed about my stay. This is the first time I've ever rated a Hilton property as 'terrible'. Why spend millions renovating a great building like this and then neglect service so badly? There are way better places to stay in Chicago and, after my four nighs at the Palmer House this week, I'll be using them in future.

“Great Hotel” Great hotel, Check-in went quickly. Staff was very friendly, offered good suggestions on nearby restaurants. Room was fabulous, larger then I expected and the bathroom was great. Beds were comfy. Tip to other travelers, you can signup at checkin for the Omni Select Rewards program (Free) you'll get free internet, you also get a complimentary beverage in the morning.

“Classy, elegant and chic!” This is the second hotel in I have stayed in that's a part of Marriott's new Autograph Collection. This one is nice as very nice as well. Beautifully appointed and very nice staff. Downtown location.

“Consistently Good” We have stayed at this hotel seven times. From time to time we try other hotels just to make our visits to Philly a little different, but it is always nice to return to an old favorite. What is so appealing about this hotel is that everything from the rooms to the friendly staff is excellent, so the overall experience is always very nice. The rooms are spacious with modern décor and the large marble bathrooms have a shower and separate tub. The rooms have a brown and beige color scheme which is a little boring, but the overall look is still very nice. Our room was in pretty good shape, but the furniture is starting to show its age with some wear, but it would not discourage us from staying again. We had breakfast in the hotel restaurant which has a charming and whimsical French bistro look. The food was good, and the service friendly and attentive. During our stay the lobby lounge was being renovated which was unfortunate for us, but it is always nice to see a hotel make improvements. In the past, the lobby lounge was usually a popular spot for drinks, and after the upgrade it will probably be even nicer. The hotel location is very good if you want to be in a fun part of the city with good restaurants, shops, museums, and Rittenhouse Square all nearby. The historic sites of the city are about a 15-20 minute walk away. There is a new Palomar hotel across the street that may give the Sofitel some competition, but the overall good experience at this hotel will help it remain one of the best hotels in the city.

“Great Stay” We stayed for two nights over Labor Day weekend. We had a corner room with a Riverwalk view from our balcony. The bed was very comfortable and the dimmers on all of the lights were great if one of us wanted to sleep and the other read in bed. The hotel staff, from check-in, to valet and bellmen, to room service personnel were very professional and provided excellent and efficient service. I can't vouch for the food at the restaurant, but highly recommend at least splurging on room service dessert, as we did. They were delicious and exquisite! My only very minor gripes would be that the shower in the bathroom was a bit tiny considering how large the bathroom itself was. Also, the choices of TV channels were a bit sparse. There was noise from the Riverwalk on Saturday night but it didn't prevent me from sleeping and it quieted down by shortly after midnight. We would definitely stay here again without hesitation.

“Good hotel on Fisherman's wharf” How good your experience of this hotel is may depend, in part, on the room you get allocated. About 6 years ago we had a great stay in a one bedroom corner suite when travelling with our children. This time (our children now a few years older) we were originally allocated a suite at the front of the hotel (251?) which had just one small window in each of the bedroom and the bathroom and no natural light in the sitting area (which had a sofa bed for the children) making the room dark and gloomy - it also suffered from some intrusive street noise. However, after one night we asked to be moved and were allocated the same room we had had 6 years before (301) which was huge with bags of light and was much quieter. Aside from the room (which was great after we were moved), the service is reasonable and there is a decent restaurant for breakfast and other meals. Minor downsides are, first, the public areas are quite small and can become a little crowded and, second, having only two lifts often means something of a wait to get around. Aside from that, this is a decent hotel. If you want to stay in Fisherman's wharf then it also has a good location. Complimentary drinks in the afternoon are a nice touch.

“A Nice Aloft Property” After my disaster of a stay at the Rancho Caucamonga Aloft, I was a little reluctant to stay here....but figured it had to be uphill from there. It was a good stay! and I've returned a couple of times since the summer. No partying or noise issues here....hip but subtle delivery of service. Very nice and helpful front desk clerks (although the gay guy should not look at me with a lingering gaze) ..he is cute, but its a little off putting. Just look quickly please, dont make your guest feel uncomfortable in that way. Im sure that might be a bonus for some guests ;-) The rooms and amenities are as expected from Aloft properties. Nice lay out, and this location has added a nice leather chair to the room which helps. Good views of the airport and south mountain range. Internet speed was acceptable, and shower pressure ok. Lots of free parking. 2 minutes from Airport terminal. 5 minutes to downtown and tempe area. There is NOTHING in this area, so you really have to drive out for pretty much everything. Its a great hotel, good rates...but all the airport hotels in this area have good pricing, so it comes down to personal taste.

“great” We stayed here for christmas 2007 in a suite overlooking the river and the trump building side. The room was wonderfull, the service was great and personal, the lounge was good and the staff were always very friendly and hgelpfull, we really enjoyed this stay and will return when we go to chicago again.

“Imperfect but Unique and Secured My Affection” This review is written from the perspective of a conference attendee/ business traveler with one leisure day. This hotel is FANTASTIC for a conference. The location - three blocks from the zoo, right over a metro stop, and surrounded by cool restaurants - is also great. The operational aspect of my room was imperfect in many ways and I still ended up liking it a lot, and the front desk clerk's resolution of my issues sealed the deal. Pro's: -Tons of great little and big nooks to gather informally to talk and network, with no overbearing loud music or ambiance. In the new section, even the elevator spaces on each floor have gathering space. -The meeting space is set up as a mezzanine with lots of transparency and views across the area so you can see who you want to talk to and network with. -Lots of natural light in common spaces. -Concessions right in the hotel to take care of your needs, including sale of fresh fruit and other noshes as well as Starbucks with a terrace. Campaign buttons for all three Presidential candidates for sale in the gift shop, with Obama's buttons priced 30% higher than the other two - a portent of the future? -Location a half block from the metro and three blocks from the zoo, within a two minute walk of zagat rated restaurants of every cuisine and price. Location was superb. -Front desk took 30% off my bill for the issues I encountered (below) without batting an eye. Any irritation I had developed evaporated like magic. -Charming, unique and stunning historic section with parquet floors, original plaster and large rooms. -Operable windows in the guest room! Hooray! -Because I had a disabled room, there was a mini fridge that was convenient. -Standard Marriott beds, linens, flat screen TV - all the usual stuff. Con's: -The Wardman Tower (historic section) has its share of operational challenges - most of which I experienced - including antique, erratic plumbing, cracked plaster, and an ancient heating and cooling system. Somehow it didn't bug me as much as it would have in a less charming room. -I had a disabled access room, which made the same mistakes most disabled access rooms do - jacking up the desk without providing an adjustable height chair (so you have to type like you're a 5 year old playing a large piano), not enough counter space in the bathroom even though it could have been added without compromising disabled access, because I guess most hoteliers don't think disabled people have lotions, potions and hair dryers. I HATE having to put my cosmetics on the toilet seat. -Not nearly enough outlets for gizmos and you had to crawl around on the floor to plug stuff in. -No safe! Very strange for a property at this level. Really, though, the pro's far outweighed the con's and I would stay at this hotel again in a heartbeat. It charmed me more than its rival neighbor the Omni Shoreham, it supported networking and community creation in a way that is rare in hotels, and the historic section is charming, partially renovated, partially dilapitated, and completely endearing like a darling auntie.

“Lack of Attention to Detail, to the Point it was SCARY!” Ok, so this is hard, as the location of this hotel is perfect for you if you want to go to a ball game or the Convention Center or like me, attend a charity event at a brewery just up the street. I was on business and came with a co-worker so we shared a room. We loved walking the marina and there were tons of great restaurants to enjoy. That's pretty much all the positive I have to say which isn't really about the hotel at all but the location. There are a lot of homeless camping out at night right outside the hotel. There was some San Diego police biking the area, so it was relatively safe, just didn't make for great ambiance. For a Hilton, I expected better. The rooms were nice with exception to two things that became annoying. The lack of electrical outlets in convenient locations in the room (next to a bed for your phone charger, or next to a mirror for your hair appliances for instance). The full length mirror was on a wall next to the bed. So technically it was not full length at all and therefore useless. My co-worker and I laughed that there were two perfectly suited locations for the mirror but they chose the wall next to the bed. To their credit, there is free cable internet in each room. But the cable is visibly strung in the hallways at the ceiling. It looks so haphazard and cheezy I forgot I was in a Hilton. It looks like some guy came in and drilled a hole in the hallway ceilings and ran cable, well, actually that's exactly what happened. My scary moment came when I arrived at my room before my co-worker and got ready for bed. I was asleep for about an hour when she came in. I sat up to greet her, and to my horror there was a stranger standing in my room. Once I sat up and got a handle on the situation, I was shocked to learn that our room key was given out in error for a bachelorette party. I had the girl call the front desk immediately to stop any more keys being given out to our room and to get the right information for the party. An apology was made but the damage was already done with my mistrust of the front desk staff being able to manage important security details of guests. When my REAL roommate arrive we bolted the door. Would I stay here again? NO. I'd rather have my old favorite Best Western around the bay with a spectacular view and take a cab downtown for an event than deal with too many "little" things out of place that add up in the end.
“90ドル以下でこんなに素敵!” このHOTELグループの中でこんなに安く泊まったことはなく、最初は不安でしたが、かなりValue For Moneyです。観光には便利な立地ですし、買い物に行くにも便利です。空港まで30分ぐらいですが、駐車場も無料で本当にまた来たいと思いました。ここから20分のところにあるレストラン(リチャードソン)SAKESUSHIは絶品でしたのでここに行くにも便利ですよ!

“Great hotel for easy access to the airport.” This hotel is really close to the airport and offers agree shuttle bus to the airport, car rental and the T stop. The view across the bay is spectacular and for plane spotters, the rooms at the rear provide unparalleled views of the runways. Parking is outrageously priced at $34 per day! There are better value hotels in Boston but for easy access to the airport this is hard to beat.

“Good location, nice hotel” I stayed at the Wyndham by the Galleria on a business trip in October 2007. The hotel itself is pretty nice (it used to be a Hilton, apparently) and the location is an easy walk to the Galleria and is a quick cab ride from Love airport. The pros: -big, clean rooms with Bath & Body Works bath products. -an easily accessible business center where it was no problem for me to print out my Southwest boarding pass (at no charge) -Very friendly, very helpful staff -A good hotel, though it does permit smoking so be warned if that bothers you -Nice and close to the wonderful Galleria Cons: -No free wireless. I still don't get why ALL hotels don't offer this for free. -I had a busted wake-up call button on my phone (it rang busy.) Those are pretty minor complaints, though. The hotel was great for business travel, and a very comfortable place to stay overall.

“Would of, Could of, should of...” Think it was a Marriott it WOULD OF been a good hotel. Being right on the Metro and almost across the street from the Zoo it COULD OF been a great stay for our Family. And if the service did what it was supposed to of done it SHOULD OFF been a great experience. Here is the back story. Basically this 1980's constructed conference hotel is tired and worn. The rooms are small even for Marriott standards. The furniture in the room is dated and miss-matched. The bathroom is cramped and the finish on the mirror frame is flaking off. This place needs a redo bad! Service was ok except for the housemen. On three occasions our service was terrible. 1st time we waited 2.5 hrs for a roll away to be delivered. The houseman to the front desk staff he delivered. Oddly it wasn't in our room. The bed arrived at midnight. 2nd we called down for extra pillows and towels. This took two hour to come up. 3rd time was for more towels and this time they never arrived. I probably won't of wrote this review at all if it wasn't for the poor performance of the housemen.

“Acceptable for a layover” Used this hotel as I had a quick overnight this week as I had a short layover at LAX. I'm PC Plat and was upgraded I was told but really didn't make use of it as I was at the hotel for less than 6 hours total. The room was acceptable, the bed was acceptable and the staff were acceptable. That is about as good as it got. I might stay here again if a short layover but probably wouldn't recommend it for a vacation hotel.

“What a stay!!” Absolutely gorgeous stay at the Willard. The hotel itself is a jewel in the crown. Baroque-styled lobby and rooms with a heavy touch of elegance and richness. Prices too high but it is definitely worth it when you want to treat yourself.. Breakfast was out of this world. Absolutely delicious.

“Great location but marginal rooms” My wife and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for a romantic weekend. I picked the Grand Hyatt since it was the highest level Hyatt available in the DC area where I could use my Hyatt hotel points for a free night. Here's the pro/con list from our stay: Pro: Great location with museums and restaurants (e.g., Ruth's Chris, McCormick & Schmick) within a short walking distance. The Spy Museum (worth the visit) was also within walking distance. Lobby was very cool and impressive with the water feature Hotel front desk staff was exceptional Starbucks in the hotel lobby Metro station in the building Parking $20/day below the hotel Onsite restaurant & bar which we did not use Cons: Walls are not sound proof so you could hear people in the hallway and adjacent rooms The beds have a pillowtop with some sort of "comfort top" that was not comfortable and my wife complained that it was "hot" and she did not sleep very well Rooms were not big for the full service, high priced hotel that this one is. Overall, it is an average hotel if you are paying $100 or less and not a choice if you are paying $200-300 per night. We got it for free using Hyatt points but I saw via the internet you could get weekend rooms for $99/night. I still would not stay here again because of the bed and lack of solid walls to mitigate outside noise.

“Best hotel in Baltimore” Brand new, beautiful, luxurious and the usual Four Seasons attentive service levels. Harbor East has really become a vibrant, modern locale with great restaurants, shopping etc. Much of downtown is a reasonable walk, though this is all a bit far from the football and baseball stadiums if that's what's bringing you to Baltimore. Minor complaints would be that the room TV system in my harborview suite was virtually incomprehensible, and 3 elevators is not enough for this hotel when it's busy - had a number of waits and slow "local" rides up and down. This is a dramatic step above other Baltimore hotels in luxury and service.

“Gorgeous” I didn't get to the hotel until midnight so it was quiet. However the staff were welcoming and friendly. The room was absolutely lovely, a standard room it had soaf and chairs, workdesk and two beds, so was pretty spacious and looked great. There were nioce little touches such as the TV guide open to that days TV and chocolates on the pillows which one sees so rarely now. I slept well with the room being very quiet and no distrubances from elsewhere in the hotel. In the morning I went to explore Denver and found that the main areas such as the 16th Street Mall were only a couple of blocks away, so it is an indeal location for visiting the city. The hotel delayed my check out by an hour with no problem at all and everyone was friendly and charming throughout. This is a lovely hotel in a great location and if I'm in Denver again I'll defintely stay here.

“Great for families traveling w/ teenagers.” We stayed here for two nights. The hotel is located in a residential area near George Washington University Hospital and the Metro. We took a taxi from Union Station rather than tote luggage on the metro, since it would involve changing trains. However, we did take the metro back to union Station when we departed and it was a lot easier than we thought it would be. The room was a 2 room suite with a large bedroom and a fold out couch in the living room. It did have a small kitchen. Perfect for my wife and I plus two teenagers. The room was clean but showing signs of wear and tear. The curtains were a bit dirty and the wall mounted headboard was loose. The lobby is very small and understaffed. The staff was very polite and helpful. There are really no amenities other than the Doubletree cookie. The nearest food store was a lengthy walk to the Watergate complex. When you start your day, you can get a good breakfast at the George Washington Hospital Cafeteria which is located right above the Metro entrance. The location was the key for us. It is a good location. Close to Metro. We were able to access all the museums via the Metro. Metro to Arlington. Metro and a local bus(long ride but worth it) to Mount Vernon. You can walk to the mall and the Lincoln Memorial from here. It is walking distance to DuPont Circle - we love the small shops and the restaurant behind the bookstore. Short walk to the GW campus with many college restaurants and entertainment venues. Not the best available, but for an active family that just needs a place to sleep it is comfortable and priced right.

“Average Hotel,Great Location” Average large American city centre hotel.Though lobby area being updated at time of visit.Nice room great view though lots of street noise.Great but simple Thai cafe on 1st floor.Great location for the city.

“Missed the mark on cleanliness” I wanted to like this Hilton hotel, but I was put off by the cleanliness of the room so I could not give it a very high rating. There were pieces of hair around the bathtub and sink. If it hadn't been midnight when I checked in (and only for a one night stay), I would have asked to change rooms. Also, the room furnishings were misleading in that they looked nicer than the actual quality. I almost broke the lamp when moving it aside because the pieces were screwed together poorly. Also, the shower did not have very good water pressure. The shuttle from the airport terminal was convenient, but next time I'm going to try another airport hotel.

“Best value ever.” When I booked directly with hotel in march 2011 they were offering basic room at $139 per nt. Not sure they will keep pricing at that level but certainly at that price I would say it was the best deal ever as room was terrific and I thought it warranted it's 4 star rating. Location has to be one of best in manhattan.

“I Would Stay Here Again” Booked through Hotwire for 4 days. Purpose was to attend the Alamo Bowl. Since it is downtown, parking is tight. Right next door to the hotel is a parking lot which charges $10.00 a day. Location wise, it doesn't get much better other than having a room over the Riverwalk. Across the street is the Alamo, a block away is a Riverwalk entrance. Within easy walking distance is the Alamodome. Check in was fast, informative and friendly. We were assigned a king size bed but when the attendant noticed there was a 13 year old girl with us, he changed us to a room with a sofa bed. The Hotwire check-in sheet showed there were 2 adults and 1 child so one would assume we would be assigned a room with two beds and at the least, a bed and a sleeper sofa. To the credit of the attendant at the hotel, he changed the room without us even asking. The sleeper sofa mattress was to be blunt, terrible. We put 6 pillows over the mattress and that made it better. The king size bed was comfortable. The room isn't large but it is big enough. I've stayed in much smaller rooms. The floors in the room are hardwood, the front door is wood. There is a 32 inch flat screen LG that hangs on the wall. The default screen setting was 4:3 and I had to use the remote to change it to 16:9 every time I turned on the TV. Our room had a view of the Alamo as it was on the corner of the hotel. It was a little noisy since this is a busy location but it isn't bad. There wasn't a bathtub in the bathroom, just a shower. Not a big deal with me. The vanity area is good size. Just one bowl sink but plenty of room to move around. Closet is small but there is plenty of drawer space in the room. The only real complaint is the sofa bed, everything else was more than acceptable. All of the soaps and lotions are Aveda so first class there. There is a bar and bistro in the hotel.
