It is open for breakfast and dinner only. It closes at 10:00 AM and we arrived at 10:30. The manager of the 1909 Bar & Bistro, Cruze, volunteered to get us some Orange Juice and muffins. He could have said breakfast is over but didn't. That is service. Dinner is served from 4:00, if I remember correctly, to 10:30. The food portions are large and we all liked the food. Wi-Fi is free and fast. We all said we liked the hotel and would stay here again.

“great location” Stayed here for a few days for business...rooms are very large and spacious however the bedding was a little worn.We were in the Tower across the street, and I have NO idea why the staff tells you to go downstairs to go across street, when you are steps away if you just walk out the front door...geesh! From other reviews, I gather that the Tower is older than the main building.Once inside my room, I got that feeling. Even with being renovated to have newer headboards, a snazzy 55" LCD t.v., it just felt OLD and USED! My room faced the pool...great if you never want to open the curtains.I had floor to ceiling windows that ran the entire length of the pool.OK since not many ppl sat outside since it was chilly...ask to NOT have a pool facing room! Room service was a joke! I ordered a sandwich/fries...It was hard and overcooked, tray had a glass of water and that was it! NO silverware, guess they figured I had finger foods. Server seemed to care less b/c I didn't notice until after she had left, you would think SHE would have added a fork or salt/pepper! Great location for 16th St Mall shopping though, use free bus shuttle or you can walk. Lobby gets VERY busy Thu/Fri nites...like a huge party! If you are checking in, the taxi, pedestrian traffic, bike taxis, and cars can make for a nightmare if you just want to pull up to drop off. Overall, I would stay again, but I might seek out other hotels for the same amount of money.
“Average hotel - good location” I love the location of this hotel - the hotel thoug could use a facelift. There is not anything specifically bad about it, it's just an average OK hotel.

“good location and helpful staff” across the street from the airport so it's a bit noisy and hectic, but the front desk staff are very good at providing excellent service. Good rooms and very good breakfast. Parking is tough but you can find spaces around back.

“Hot and stuffy but has potential” The hotel was nicely appointed with a great bar that is perfect for sporting events. The pool is nice for a business hotel and the gym was clean and had all the essentials. However, the service was a bit weak. The air conditioning in our room did not work well. I asked the hotel to fix it and they said engineering would be up in 5 minutes. 20 minutes late no engineering so I called and cancelled since my children needed to sleep. I asked them to come the next day and fix the problem. Well this time they came and said it was fixed but it was not. The AC does on and off during the night. I had it turned all the way down to 60 and it felt like it never got below 70. Needless to say, two nights of poor sleep did not make for a good weekend. The front desk seemed to be constantly understaffed and the phone was only answered 50% of the time. The hotel had been sold out for weeks so I'm sure they knew they would be busy. I would go back to this hotel if the AC problem was resolved.

“Highly Recommended” I believe that the hotel rooms and parts of the lobby have been updated since my last stay 6 years ago. I cannot recall a time I experienced such excellent customer service. The staff was warm, helpful and kind. Even as a priceline guest they were able to accomodate my needs with a room near the elevator. I loved the rooms...the lighting, the beds were the most comfortable that I've ever experienced at a hotel and the bath products have the best scent ever (Hawaian ginger, I believe). Gorgeous skyline views on the upper floors, easy access to restaurants and stores in the Illinois Center through an indoor walkway. While the food at the hotel is fresh, creative, abundant, my only complaint is the cost.

“Perfect location for conference hotel” I have not stayed at a Sheraton property before, but this was the headquarter hotel for a conference I attended. You really can't beat this location for its proximity to the conference center. I received an email just before the conference with the opportunity to upgrade to the club floor. This was a huge advantage as it provided my collegue and me a continental breakfast each morning and appetizers in the evening and free WiFi. Also cold water and soft drinks throughout the day. I think it's worth the price. The subway is located in the Prudential center which is attached to the convention center. This is a large shopping center. A very easy walk. There were a number of lunch options in and around the Prudential Center. We were there for a week of classes, so tried a lot of them. Not all were your typical fast food choices. We ate at Legal Seafoods a few times . Very good food, maybe a little pricey. There is also a wine shop and a Trader Jo's within walking distance, although this Trader Jo's does not sell wine. We hopped on the subway after our classes were out in the evening and went everywhere. We felt like it was very safe to walk around the area at night. Would definitely stay here again.

“No Complaints” We stayed at the Dana in early August. Nervous due to mixed reviews. We were there for our 34th year of marriage. We had booked a package through Alaska Airlines. Check in was very smooth. They told us we would overlook the tropical pool. We were fine with that. The room was clean. Not fancy, but we did not spend much time sitting there as San Diego is filled with too many great activities. We like a shower, so no tub was fine with us. We received a call to be sure our room was fine. Let it be known that the pool closes at 11 pm. First night the noise continued to 11:15. A call to the desk and the pool promptly was closed. The second night, someone came and closed the pool. We did have partiers, but we have been there ourselves and just closed the window and turned on the air!! We liked the fact it was near water and nice paths for walking. Concierge was very helpful. It has easy access to highways. The newspaper was delivered each day to our door. For us that is a treat! Most of all....Enjoy San Diego.

“Older, renovated property with SUPERB staff.” We had a five day/four night stay here in conjunction with professional meetings. Mrs. Gardiner and I had Kiddo with us, so we were understandably nervous, having read the reviews posted here. Net, we were very, very pleased. First thing we did, since we’d read concerns about the size of the rooms was to pay an upgrade fee to get into a suite. We had a delightful suite on the 20th floor, with windows on three sides (room number 2001) of the suite. WOW. Really, really nice. The room was very clean; linens were Crowne Plaza style (left over from the change of flags, I guess). A rollaway bed was brought for Kiddo, and fit nicely. They had Gilchrist & Soames toiletries, which was very nice. We needed a fridge for milk and apple juice for Kiddo, and one was brought up and plugged in at no charge. The Tap on Two was closed for renovations, and the bar and restaurant had been shoe-horned into the Lobby area. They’re forgiven for this... but I’ll peek back in once this is done. Yes, the elevators are tiny, but they do go all the way to the street level now. Look, the hotel is a Grande Dame. It’s old. Think Palmer House in Chicago, Tutwiler in Birmingham, Marriott East Side in NYC. If you want large rooms in Chicago, book a newer hotel or upgrade the room. Location, though, is just incredible. You know you’re on prime real estate when the street level part of the building houses Brooks Brothers. Apple’s Mich Ave store is just across the street. Service, in every interaction, was crisp and friendly. Concierge gave great direction to terrific restaurants, and even got us a “line cutter” invite that slipped us directly past the long line at Gino’s East! We were part of a set of three day meetings, and the banquet staff was equally crisp, responding to everything from minor A/V issues to extra bottles of water. The meetings went very smoothly, and I’d be happy to book here again. I think I have, though, solved all of my future hotel and travel issues... by hiring one of their people. Not sure how I do this or pay for it, but I want to hire Bennis, who works at the front desk, as my personal hotel handler. I want to have this lady travel a day ahead of me, and be working the front desk at every hotel I visit anywhere in the world. (This will require some travel on her part, I suppose.) She’s that good. Heck, she could even teach the folks at the JWMarriott Hong Kong a few things! She was absolutely superb from the moment we walked into the lobby until we left. She chatted up Kiddo, helped us with directions, had leftover pizza frozen for the trip home, patiently answered questions... wow. Bennis, if you get bored at the Allerton, let me know! Good hotel, will be better when renovations are done. Absolutely superb staff. Excellent stay.

“Quiet Stay at the Seattle Westin” The Westin Seattle is a unique hotel, with its two distinctive, circular towers that can be picked out in any downtown Seattle photo. The hotel is a bustle of activity with a nice mix of business and personal travelers. The hotel does a great job of customer service and getting people where they need to be. Even though I was a Priceline customer, I was offered a higher floor room when I requested one. The hotel common areas, while busy, were not loud or boisterous. I found the service at the lobby level lounge to be quick and efficient. My room was on the 26th floor of North Tower (which I recommend if you have a choice). It was extremely quiet and relaxing. The room was comfortable and nicely appointed. The bathroom was not large, but did not feel cramped. I enjoyed my one night stay at the Seattle Westin. A couple words of caution. The hotel is starting to show a little wear and tear; small things like scuff marks on the walls, dings on the wood trim around the doors, tears in the carpeting, etc. These may be small deals or big ones depending on your expectations. Also, the elevators are quite slow, especially if you are waiting for one or on one during peak usage. The Westin is located on the northern edge of downtown Seattle proper. A couple of the surrounding areas can get a little sketchy the later into the night it gets; mainly the area north of the hotel.

“Great Location - "Decent" hotel for the price, but call hotel directly and speak to someone on-site!!” Just returned from a four night stay at The Whitehall Hotel in Chicago for our anniversary. The location was great for walking to all the sights. When I called the hotel directly to book our stay I was asked what our room preference was regarding smoking. I indicated that it must be a non-smoking room. I was told that a non-smoking room would be no problem and that a king was also available. Upon receiving my email confirmation it listed a smoking-king. I immediately called back and got Annie who is located on-site at the hotel. She was a pleasure to talk to, but told me that there were no non-smoking kings or queens available. She explained that when she is busy the phones ring over to a call bank and they book rooms for the hotel and just book whatever is available, but tell you what you want to hear. After a few minutes of going back and forth Annie did apologize profusely and was finally able to book us in a non-smoking queen room. If you are calling the hotel directly to book your reservation definitely speak to someone who is actually located on the premises in Chicago. The rooms are a bit dark and the bed was extremely hard. You have the normal sounds of a busy city. We travel with a sound machine to help with the city noise. Other than the booking issue and the few other minor issues we found the hotel to be decent enough to consider staying there again. The staff was pleasant and helpful.

“Best Service! Pet Friendly! Great Stay!!” My husband and I booked the Junior Suite with patio at the Affinia Gardens for our 4 night stay in early Oct. We took the red-eye flight to JFK and arrived around 9 am to check in. Of course we knew our room wouldn't be ready, so we made ourselves comfortable in the lobby/lounge/tea room area. The lounge was super comfy--leather deep furniture, floor pillows stacked around, a huge flat screen T.V. on the wall, tea and coffee. Very nice place to just hang out for awhile. The bellman Chris, was so friendly and helpful! He recommended a few places to have breakfast while we waited, and was just a great person to talk to! We travelled with our little pomeranian, and Chris was there to make sure we were ALL comfortable! We only waited a couple of hours when our room became ready. Chris took our things to our suite and explained everything in the room. And what a lovely room it was! The best part of it was the huge patio out back! We spent so much time out there! The room was huge! Nice little kitchen with everything you would need, beds and pillows so comfortable, the bathroom had a tub/shower and was very roomy! And everything was so so clean!!! I'm a clean freak, so when I say clean--it was clean! Chris brought a dog bed and food and water bowls for Sid (our Pom) and I have to say everything was perfect for us during our stay! Kudos to Affinia Gardens! We WILL be back!!! Can I move in?

“Best choice at DTW” I was stranded at DTW and Delta put me up at the Westin. You step out of the terminal and into a tranquil, stylish lobby that puts you at ease. The rooms are standard Westin - plush linens, huge flat panel TV, quiet interior. The gym is on par with any facility you would pay to join outside of a hotel. I am a HHonors diamond and will be hard pressed to stay off DTW if the Westin is available...it's quite comfortable.

“once every ten years....” I got a great rate on Priceline at the same time as the UN General Assembly when it is almost impossible to negotiate NY hotels. AND, the secretary of state and prez were there and holding meetings in the American Suite. Streets were closed; NYPD thick everywhere, but the staff were gracious and acted as if I was just as special as the VIPs. Lines were long at check in, and a concierge took me to her office to assign my room, etc. A little annoying to go thru security and be scrutinized by Secret Service everywhere, but that was not the WA's fault. I was upgraded to the Towers, had a club continental breakfast, and cannot complain. It IS a grand hotel and not to be missed somewhere along the way.

“Good Location” The hotel is very close to Navy Pier. Nice Lobby. The room was clean, but small. My only complaint is the bed was very uncomfortable. I would recommend the hotel because of the location but hopefully they will get some new beds!

“Very Nice, Would Stay Here Again” A very nice hotel with a reasonable downtown LA price. In the safe part of downtown and within easy walking distance of many places to eat. Not a lot of shopping nearby, but the Jewelry District is about 2 blocks away if you are into that. The room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. Staff was curteous and helpful. The breakfast was quite expensive but wonderful. I didn't like the entry to the room. The closet and bath doors bumped against each other and it felt like you were squeezing your way in. Also the TV was dated and small - it's time for a flat screen upgrade Omni. Both minor issues. I liked the property and would stay here again.

“Nice hotel if you can take the view” Very nice hotel, clean, large rooms for New York, great beds, if you can stand the depressing view of the World Trade Center site. Mysterious construction goes on at all times making for some noise, but really not too bad. Good location for financial district or Tribeca, would stay in again if I needed to (just wouldn't look out the window!).

“Affordable for families” We had 3 adults and a teen, so we booked the two double beds and sofa bed suite. It was an affordable way to spend the 4th of July weekend in Boston. We were disappointed that it look a long time to get the bedding for the sofa bed, and never received the two blankets for it that we requested. Their shampoo and conditioner bottles were almost impossible to squeeze and get anything out of. Our in-room safe was not working the first day so we had to wait a day for them to fix it. And the hotel is not really located within walking distance of Boston's T. However, they have free parking next door which is extremely convenient. If you're not out too late, you can use their shuttle bus to drop you or pick you up at a T station, again for free. With the hotel on Mass. Ave. near its junction with I93, it's fairly easy to reach when driving. There is some traffic noise, but not too bad. We used the free wireless connection in the room with our laptop, and tried to use the free printing service in the business office for airline boarding passes. It wasn't working at the time but the clerk let us use the computer and printer at the front desk. All in all, we felt pretty good about our experience with this hotel. We'd recommend insisting repeatedly on all the bedding you need right away, checking that the hotel safe is working early before you need it, and having your own shampoo and conditioner as a backup.

“Interesting...” This hotel was best described by a woman who rode up the elevator with me on day two of my 7-day stay at the W; "...I am as hip as the next person, but I need some LIGHT..." This re-done hotel - tucked behind the historic Fairmont Olympic Hotel Seattle on 4th St - is hip. But if you have trouble seeing, bring a flashlight! Elevators have dark carpet and two tiny pendant lights - and those elevators are FAST, so be ready to jump on and jump off! Lobby is two-level and lighted by tea-lights. Great sleeping room (choose the upgrade, if you can - it is worth it!) with wide screen, flat-panel TVs. Great shiny bathrooms, good office space and comfy couch. Prompt room service, which is good because the "honor bar" is really expensive. Not much of a RS selection, but that's okay, because there are plenty of wonderful places to eat in walking distance (like Schuckers - next door!). Coffee lovers dream (Starbucks, SEattle's Best and Tully's all very close!) Short walk downhill to shopping... Long walk uphill with purchases! One big downer - no pool!

“Comfortable and convenient airport hotel, almost everything works” I stayed here for one night after a late-night LAX arrival. It's got just about everything an airport hotel needs: clean and spacious rooms, good food, a nice executive lounge. And I got a reasonable room rate. My only complaint was that the hotel shuttle took an awfully long time to get to the airport pick-up area. I was waiting for over 30 minutes, possibly because one Hilton shuttle drove by without stopping at my location. Meanwhile several shuttles for less highly regarded hotel chains stopped two or three times to pick up their customers. The main reason to stay at an airport hotel is to be in your room significantly sooner than you would be if you were staying downtown. In this case that objective was not fulfilled. Any more than fifteen minutes' wait for an airport hotel shuttle is too long.

“Old World Charm” We have stayed at this hotel twice. The hotel is historical, and has a very charming lobby. The first time we got a very large nice room. The second time we arrived, we got a small crammed room overlooking the dumpster. Asked to look at two other rooms, and finallly settled on one with a view of the Empire State Building. This room was much smaller and plainer than the room we had had during our first stay at Wolcott Hotel. The hotel is at very convenient location, near the Empire State Building and Fifth Avenue.

“Just OK” Nothing special to report. I would prefer to stay at the Fairmont, but it was booked, so I stayed here. Not a bad location, but not the best. Not the best room, but OK. What can I say, just an average hotel, but in downtown Chicago for under $200 it was, like I said, OK.

“Great if you love barking dogs” This hotel doesn't even come close to what one might expect from a Westin property. They have a shuttle from LAX which is apparently shared with a Holiday Inn and some other hotel. The shuttle made me wish I walked. Not a good start. The room itself was fine - until around 7:00 Sunday morning, when the adjacent dog kennel (?) apparently opens. This would be fine if you needed a 7 a.m. wakeup call - but that wasn't what I was looking for after a 1:00 a.m. check-in. The staff could not have cared less. This is allegedly a 4 star hotel - I've had better experiences at Motel 6. Never again.

“Good location” I booked this hotel to try something different. I have mainly been a Hilton guy and was curious to see what Kimpton had to offer. Finding the hotel (I came straight from SEA-TAC airport) was extremely easy, it was a 1 minute drive off the expressway, and has a nice vertical sign spanning several floors of the facade. They have a full valet service $35 for in and out rights. Across the street is a parking garage for self park, but I think it is close if not the same price. I took an earlier than expected flight and was several hours before check-in time. The front desk was able to accommodate me and placed me on floor 3. The room was smaller than I was used to, but very nice quality. My view was an alley with a parking garage. Cars were parked on the same level as the hotel window, so I had to pull my blinds to ensure privacy. Free wireless access in the room with a Kimpton account. I went down to the lobby to work by the fireplace. They have a few couches and places to sit. This is meant to be a lounge more than a work environment, but it worked out fine. Between 5-6pm they have free wine tasting in the lobby. This is quite popular, as there wasn't a spot to sit down it was so crowded. I wandered out for dinner with some colleagues and almost any direction you walk, you can find restaurants. The location for this hotel was the best part. After dinner I crashed out and woke up around 1am to a dog barking. The hotel must be pet friendly. The barking went on for quite some time. After that, every noise seemed amplified...ice makers, doors slamming (they have no mechanism to stop the door from slamming...it seemed like everytime a door slammed the entire walls shook). I would take advantage of the free wine, so you can hopefully be smashed enough to sleep right through the night. The morning came and I walked by the restaurant inside the hotel. It was not overly crowded, but busy. It smelled good, but I didn't have time to stop. I would say this hotel is average, but does boast a great location for walking distance to many attractions.

“Character and a touch of Luxury” The XV Beacon is a great pace to stay in Boston. The hotel is located on Beacon street, with about a 5 minute walk to Downtown Crossing, 10 Minutes to Quincey Market, 2 minutes to Boston Common and 15 minutes to Charles Street. So for us, we could forget the car and walk everywhere quite comfortably. Even a walk down to Copely Place only took about 30 minutes. In addition to the hotel restaurant, which offers high quality food and service, there is also a cheaper but good dining option right next door and a Dunkin Doughnuts over the road. We stayed in a Corner Studio which was a good size offerred plenty of light and decorated pretty much like the hotel website pictures. Some aspects of the furniture were starting to show a few scratches and bumps, but overall the quality of furnishings and decoration were definately 5 star. The only thing that bugged me was the restaurant adding 20% tip for a table of two. While the service is definately of the highest order, I think it should still be up to me to add a tip which I think is justified. But overall this is a great, albeit expensive, hotel. Its in a great location for exploring Boston and while a little removed from a variety of dining options. many are available with a modest walk. This hotel comes highly recommended.

“Nice hotel in the heart of Union Square” I stayed at the VIlla Florence for 2 nights in a room with 2 double beds on the 4th floor, overlooking Powell Street. We did hear quite a bit of street noise, but it usually tapered off around 11pm. The beds were fairly comfy, and the linens were nice. (NOTE: if you are allergic to feathers or down, do not stay at this hotel!) Each bed had a down feather mattress topper on it, as well as down pillows and a light down comforter. It was a little bit of feather overkill. The bathroom was pretty compact, with a pedestal sink and combo tub/shower. There's not much room to set your toiletries or hair styling tools anywhere! The room does have an actual closet area with a safe, ironing board and iron, which was nice to stow our bags in. We really appreciated the hotel having 2 computers for guest use so that we could check out some of the tour companies and also check in for our flight. There's also free WiFi in the hotel. We arrived in San Fran around 7am, and were able to check into our room at 9:30am. The hotel is really close to the Powell and Hyde cable car turnaround, and also close to the Muni/BART station. The concierge (Albert) was great to provide information on the area and especially to point out the areas to avoid. There are a lot of good restaurants in the area, and we really enjoyed Lefty O'Douls for breakfast. You can definitely tell that this is an old hotel that has been remodeled....but at least it isn't creepy!

“Immer eine Reise wert, bei diesem Hotel.” Das Grand Hyatt New York ist ein guter Griff. Die Lage ist top, der Service sehr gut, der Concierge-Service weiß, wovon er spricht, habe ich all zu oft schon anders erlebt und auch das restliche Personal kennt das Geschäft. Die Anreise mit dem eigenen Pkw ist beschwerlich (Verkehrsstau gibt es in Manhatten ohne Aufpreis), liegt aber nicht am Hyatt, liegt an der Leichtsinnigkeit auf eigene Faust mit dem Pkw den Time Square zu erkunden. :-) Ich war dort allerdings mit dem Dienstwagen unterwegs und bin auch öfters in New York,mit der Zeit geht es. Wenn sie also selbst anreisen, das Hotel ist gut mit dem Auto zu erreichen / zu finden, bereiten Sie sich allerdings auf ordentliche Parkgebühren vor, zwei Nächte für einen Q7 (SUV-Sondergebühr!) 220$, aber eben normal in Manhatten. Die Suiten sind modern und sehr ansprechend eingerichtet, klare Linien bestimmen das Bild. Bequeme Betten, großes sauberes Bad und begehbare Dusche, niedriges Geräuschlevel der Außenwelt im Zimmer selbst. Auch die Sitzgelegenheiten im Zimmer (Couchgarnitur) lädt zum verweilen ein, neu, gepflegt, Leder. Ich buche i.d.R. nur Übernachtung, da es in New York unzählige, tolle und absolut erlebenswerte Cafe's, Restaurants, Deli's, Bagel Baker, usw. gibt, also raus auf die Straße, in Manahtten finden Sie immer was.

“We're in the business to make money” That's what the guy working in the business center told us. We had 2 packages to ship via FedEx and have an account with them. Whenever a pickup is scheduled, an additional $4 per package is added by FedEx, which is understandable. The guy at the business center proceeds to tell us that in addition to that fee, we have to pay him $5 per package, since they are in the business of making money. Those were his exact words. I called FedEx and they said that they already tack on a fee ($8 total for our 2 packages) and under no circumstance to pay an additional $10 to the hotel. If you have stuff to ship, you're better off just walking down the street to the FedEx location yourself. It would have been $18 extra to ship our package through the hotel, which to me is outrageous. Other than that, the hotel is in a great location, but that's about it. We needed a taxi for the airport on our last day and the concierge harassed us every single time we passed by his desk about booking a town car instead. It got so annoying that we would intentionally avoid walking by him since we had no interest in booking a town car when the taxi suited us perfectly and was $20 cheaper. Oh, and the wifi? $14.95 per day, which is ridiculous, give it's 2010 and free wifi is readily available at many hotspots around the city. We passed many hotels while walking through the city that offered free wi fi. This isn't one of them. But, they're in the business of making money so it's ok. Keep that in mind when you book your room, everything is extra here! Overall, the hotel is in a great area, with nice rooms. The staff, however, is very pushy and not at all friendly. Funny thing is, they don't see any of that money they claim the hotel is in the business of making and probably make minimum wage themselves. There were several other hotels on this block. I saw a Fairmont across the street and another really nice one next door, but I'm blanking on the name. Unless you get a deal on Priceline, stay elsewhere!

“Vista su Alcatraz” Ci viene assegnata una stanza al 37°piano. Dopo 28ore di volo, arriviamo esausti, apriamo la porta e vedere una stanza così ci ha fatto dimenticare il volo faticoso. Un letto grande, un tv al plasma e una vista su tutta la città con Alcatraz proprio davanti a noi. Non vi dico che bello vedere il tramonto da qua. Immancabile la macchinetta scaldavivande e le varie buste di the, caffè etc. FrigoBar rifornitissimo La camera era molto pulita e il personale molto cordiale e sempre pronto a soddisfare qualsiasi esigenza.

“Great hotel” Another winner from Priceline. This hotel was very classy, the room was spacious, the king bed extremely comfortable, and the decor modern-attractive. The bath and shower products were especially pleasant. Ipod alarm clock/docking station was appreciated. The (free) umbrellas were great. The hotel is extremely convenient to subway, Port Authority, and Times Square. The hotel seemed like it would have been a great place to relax the day away had it not been for that business meeting. Acceptable pizza can be had after midnight 1 block away. Highly recommend.

“Not so great” Stayed at the Marriott two nights as part of travel to a convention. The location of the hotel is great but the hotel is sorely in need of a makeover. Wallpaper in the room was peeling and while the room seemed clean, the towels were stained. Staff was cordial but when room was cleaned an empty tissue box was not replenished. Similarly a water bottle that had been opened the day before was not replaced. Air conditioner was very noisy. All in all not a place I'm likely to return.

“Sleek and fun” I just returned from a two night stay at the Palomar. The rooms are wonderfully decorated with contemporary furnishings , animal prints, and faux fur throws. The bed was extremely comfortable, and the linens soft. Although the rooms are not huge, they are well designed and have ample rooms. The shower was great, and L'Occident En Provence products wer very nice, espcially the wonderful soap. We had a great view facing south to the Pacific in the distance with the impressive Mormon Temple in the foreground . Hotel Staff were very friendly and accomodating. The wine service in the evening was a great way to wind down in the afternoon, and morning coffee and tea was a nice touch. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was delicious and innovative. An added bonus to staying here is the close proximity to UCLA, Century City, The Getty and the Hammer. Also, ithe Westwood location allows you the luxury of actually walking to dining and attractions. It's nice to experience Ls Angeles as something other than a long Freeway.

“Great Staff, super clean” I read the other reviews before staying here and was expecting some problems but on the contrary it was awesome! At check in the guys were very friendly, I asked for a king bed which they said no problem. I had booked this on priceline and sometimes you get 2 queens in the worst spot and can't change, but not today. Next parking, I was expecting it to be very confusing but the check in staff explained so clearly what to do it was eAsy... Don't get me wrong, it's slightly complicated and if you don't listen you will be driving around saying 'where do I go? What do I do with these 3 tickets...' it also costs $20 a day, not the best since other airport hotels are free but Philly parking, especially center city, expensive. The decor in the hallways and rooms could be updated for sure, it's like alot of hotels, nothing special, but the rooms ARE spotless, I checked, bathrooms, dated but exceptionally clean. We stayed 2 nights and the other person I was traveling with had a 6.30pm flight and asked for a late checkout... They gave her 4pm at no charge, this, was awesome. It's not a real Starbucks in the lobby store, they just brew Starbucks coffee but, it tasted great and the service from the staff excellent. I was prepared not to like this hotel, it was actually very comfortable. It's right AT the airport - attached by a walkway. I didn't hear one plane by the way! My flight departed at 6.15am and it was so good to be right there and have that little extra time that early in the morning. Recommended.

“Quiet and convenient with wonderful staff” I stay in a many hotels in Denver during the year. This was by far the best stay I have had in the past 15 stays at least. The room was spotless. Everything was so clean it seemed brand new. The staff was absolutely the best. The concierge lounge was great. This is the quietest downtown hotel I have ever stayed at. The bed was fantastic. The hotel is close to everything. There is a starbucks in the lobby and a convenience store in the same building. The 16th Street mall is just a block away and the convention center is about 4 or 5 blocks away.

“Great Resort to Relax and Rejuvenate” I spent five days at the JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort in late April. Based on what I had read on TripAdvisor.com and based on information from a person in my office who had briefly visited the resort, I had some hesitation about staying here. I knew that it was in the middle of nowhere, and I also knew that it catered to large groups. Plus, I had the pleasure of staying twice at the JW Marriott Camelback Inn, both times for a business conference. I really enjoyed the Camelback and knew the experience at Desert Ridge would be quite different. However I got offered a package deal at Desert Ridge for a price that I couldn’t turn down and just wanted to relax in the desert for a few days My first reaction was mixed. I checked in on a Saturday, and the place was busy, no doubt about it. It was hot and I was looking forward to a long swim, but the pools were crowded with kids. Plus, the one pool that seemed somewhat suitable for lap swimmers was closed for a special event. I asked the front desk if I could be comped to use the Spa pool, and they said fine. That was a nice bonus (and service proved to be excellent at the resort, during the course of my entire stay), since use of the spa facilities cost $25 at a minimum. The pool was beautiful, but I still felt it in no way compared to the spa pool at the Camelback. Despite my initial mixed reaction, the place grew on me day by day. The Desert Ridge is the largest hotel in Arizona, but to me, it didn’t feel that way. The architect did a great job of making the resort seem like a manageable size. There is still quite a bit of walking to do, but not nearly as much as some of the big Vegas hotels. The hotel was pretty full over the weekend (and less so as the week went on), but for the most part, the restaurants, pool, and area by the pool never seemed congested. There were a couple of big groups there, but they never bothered me. Rooms were quite large size and were very cheerful. The bathroom were large too, with a separate marble tub and shower. There were some quirks with the rooms: there seemed to be a waste paper basket only in the bathroom and not by the desk as well ; the shower leaked, unless you positioned the showerhead in a certain way, and there was no way to turn the light on the balcony off, meaning you had to completely close the curtains to get to sleep. But these complaints are relatively minor and in no way subtract from the great overall experience at the hotel. I only ate at the Blue Sage, the casual restaurant. Great burgers at lunch and dinner; breakfasts was good, but not great. Prices were on the high side, but I’ve seen them higher elsewhere. However, unlike a lot of other resorts, you are not locked into eating only at the overpriced restaurants on the property. A short way from the hotel is an outdoor mall with a good food court, an Albertsons supermarket, Einstein Bagels and a bunch of casual restaurants including On the Border Café and California Pizza Kitchen. This really gives a guest a lot more options, in term of food. For those without a car, I think the hotel runs shuttles to this mall, and if it’s not scorching hot, it’s probably not a bad walk. The best feature of this hotel for me was the beautiful two-level lobby and outdoor patio area, as well as the beautiful pool area. The resort was extremely conducive to relaxation. While it is true, that Desert Ridge is somewhat isolated and away from the heart of the action in Phoenix, I found it fairly easy and quick to get around by car, and since I’ve been to Phoenix many times, I preferred staying close by the hotel. By the end of my stay, I was dreading having to leave and return to the real world. In summary, I highly recommend this hotel!

“Old upper east side history; overpriced” Had one unexpected overnight in NYC and wanted a 5-star, so I took a chance with priceline and ended up with the Carlyle. I should confess that if I'm spending bucks, I like newer updated places, like the Mandarin chain, some of the Four Seasons properties, and funky places like the Hotel on Rivington. The Carlyle is an old upper east side throw-back. Apparently it's Sarkozy's digs when he's in the city. The bar is historic and charming. On arrival, my room wasn't ready, so the staff put me in the bar and comped me a martini. The room was spacious by NYC standards, but really old and dated. It had obviously been set up with twin beds! Lucy and Desi style! They pushed them together with an overlay to make a king bed for me, though. Exposed heating duct pipes and painted over wires along the floor and under the window. The chrome and old marble bathrooms were straight out of a "high class" 60's movie. My impression is that it's a hang-out for moneyed folks looking for exclusivity and subtlety. Interesting experience, but not remotely worth the expense ($750/night).

“VERY average” 100% overpriced for what it is. Pretentious. This hotel pretends to be more than it is. Check in was ordinary and not terribly friendly despite being a Starwood preferred guest. Romm service was disgusting. We arrived 10.00pm. Ordered room service. It all arrived COLD. I called the manager. We got 50% discount on the disgusting food. make a decision NOT to eat dinner here again based on this. Tried the seriously overpriced buffet the next morning. Definitely second class. Virtually no choice at all on the buffet. Forget it. The room was OK but cleaning is not great. If you are going on business and need to use the Internet,forget their $10 per day braodband. It does not have enough bandwidth and is horribly slow. My suggestion - find somewhere else to stay. I will the next time I'm in Philly

“Good hotel” This hotel has a great location. within walking distance to a lot of bars and restaurants. rooms were nice, modern and very clean. Valet parking was expensive but probably the norm in the area! Concierge never at their desk! We always had to wait a while, looked like they were a bit short of staff!

“Cutting Edge, First Rate Service, Excellent Concierge Lounge” This property is undergoing a renovation and the lobby looks fantastic. Trendy furnishings abound and there is cozy seating everywhere. Staff are warm and welcoming and everyone I encountered was helpful. I stayed in the Club Tower, in one of the recently renovated rooms and it was gorgeous. I would compare it to the JW Marriott in Indy, which is one of my all time favorite hotels, anywhere. Trendy but comfortable furnishings, which isn't always easy to accomplish. Wonderful shower and bathroom. The concierge lounge is what a concierge lounge should be. There are little desk areas, each with a large flat panel TV/monitor and multiple chairs to work at, or gather around in a small group for a quiet mini huddle. There are larger areas with TVs to gather and relax as well as dining tables. Food and beverage selection was good and the staff was very friendly and helpful. On property gym was nice, a better selection than most, but an odd location, you have to walk outside to get to it. It's a good option though. They have a spa at the gym location, but I did not have time to try it out. Lobby bar bartender was very friendly and efficient despite dealing with a large convention crowd. Valet staff was very quick, a rarity in DC. I would stay in this hotel again in a heartbeat.

“Pack light” We visit NYC several times a year and usually book our hotel based on rate and location. So I've stayed in a wide variety of hotels over the years. The Mela would certainly not be the worst but also not near the top either. We booked a deluxe king which is not their smallest room and it was really tiny! There was virtually no place to put luggage so we ended up having to keep one suitcase in the bathroom. The room was also very dark and on one side you could barely see even with every light on. The bed was very comfortable and the bed linens were of good quality. The bath towels were a little small and thin. The staff was pleasant but not overly knowledgeable. I asked one of the concierges for a restaurant recommendation one evenng and he was not able to come up with anything (I asked about something casual in the 50's around Carnegie Hall) so I just resorted to my Zagat Guide. The location is very good if you're planning on seeing Broadway shows. The little restaurant next door was good for a drink and we had a pretty good dinner there one night as well. The breakfast prices are way too high so we just went up to the Red Frame a block away for breakfast. If I got an extremely good rate, I'd stay here again but otherwise I've found quite a few other places I prefer.

“Good Location for San Diego Chargers Game-All San Diego Just a Trolley Away” Stayed one night when attending a Chargers game. Good price ($100) and close to stadium. You can walk (about 20 minutes) or take trolley which has a station down the street 5 minutes walk away. Probably faster to walk as we had to wait for 3 trolleys until one had room. Anyways, the hotel check in was nice and easy even with early check in. Self parking was $14? a day but close to room. Nice pool and bar area (limited but OK beers on tap) but did not eat at restaurants. Room was small but had a comfortable bed. Old tube style TV in armoire you have to pull and tilt towards bed but fine for the night. Alarm clock, desk/chair. sofa, decent bathroom and a small balcony not big enough to sit on but maybe if you smoke it's OK. Good for fresh air. Called front desk to let them know alarm clock from next door was going off for the last hour. They sent someone up with 5 minutes and called back to make sure it took care of the issue. Very good job. Used free internet and printer in lobby by check-in. Good gift shop. Friendly and helpful staff all over the property. I would say this is a very well managed hotel (as with most Mariott's) but does need upgrades to room and facilities (some small details didn't work like elevator buttons, lights, creaky bar stools etc) soon to be a real 4 star. Overall, for under $125 w/parking and tax I would say this is a good value.

“Good for business” I was at this hotel for a few nights for business. The lobby and the restaurant was pretty low key, almost subdued. But for my business purpose, it was a convenient location to go between Battery Park and Water Street. I checked in very in the morning and they had my room ready. In addition, it was exciting to get the usual Doubletree welcome cookie for breakfast.

“Really nice but no longer the Grande Dame” Stayed here w/ my wife on a business incentive trip and while we really had a great time in NYC the Waldorf is very good but certainly off it's greatness. Public areas are still beautiful and they carry the luxury brand very well. Restaurants (and we ate at all of them w/ vouchers) were OK at best and incredibly pricey even for NYC. Peacock Alley had a shockingly slim lunch menu and when they charged us $8 for a cup of coffee and$8 tea and a water surcharge of $3, it was too much. Go elsewhere. Bull and Bear was good but way overpriced. Bar included lots of older men wearing black tie and it was a very boring crowd. We thought the staff including the front desk people were great, well-trained and helpful at all times.We relaxed in various lounges @ the main public areas and it was as comfortable a hangout as I have seen in many years of hotels. The room was not large but very well appointed w/ great luxury touches on the sundries. TV was a big flat screen and was terrific. Room heat was amazingly dry but we turned off the heat and on a very cold weekend in NYC, we were warm the whole time. A really good time at the Waldorf.

“Pretty Impressive” This is a grand old property. The location is perfect. The service excels. Matt Damon was rumored to be on the property while I was there. The Peninsula is a unique brand of luxury. It's an experience worth having at least once. Enjoy your stay.

“LOCATION IS OUTSTANDING” My family and I went for the Texas-OU game. It's a great place to stay for anybody going to the game. The downside is that it was very loud with lots of partying all night long. We anticipated this so we brought our own fan to drown out the noise and we slept fine. The staff was very nice. The bar was very nice but the drinks are way overpriced.

“Bien situado con buen precio” Es tipo motel sin grandes pretensiones, pero limpio, cómodo y muy bien situado. Habitación espaciosa, con 2 camas queen, baño, TV, frigo y microondas. Todo limpio y muy funcional. Parking gratuito, autobús y metro muy cerca y a menos de 30 minutos andando del Kodak Theatre.

“Great stay for early flight from OHare” Luckily had advanced booked at very cheap rate about 10 days prior to stay (Jan 20) as due to the sudden snowfall in Chicago the hotel was starting to get full of people from stranded flights when I arrived at about 6pm. Checkin was easy at the HH desk very friendly staff, two bottles of water, breakfast voucher for continental - of which there was a good selection - or you could upgrade to a full cooked breakfast for only a few dollars - great value but I didn't take advantage of this. Room well away from elevator (as requested in my HH profile) comfortable bed and good wifi connection. This is the 2nd time I have stayed at this hotel, and will do again if I have an early flight as located within the airport - so only 5 minute walk to Terminal 3.

“I remembered why I always come back” I travel to DC for work regularly and, every once in a while, I try out a new hotel, looking for something to improve upon the overall experience of my mainstay, the Willard. You can find hotels that exceed the Wllard in any particular category. The Mandarin Oriental is more beautiful. The Ritz Carlton in Georgetown sophisticated and, well, in Georgetown. The Four Seasons is more glamourous and has a more personal staff. Ultimately, I always go back to the Willard and on a recent stay I remembered why. First,the rooms are understated but incredibly comfortable. Beds and bedding are exactly what you'd expect for a superior hotel. There is a snuggly reading chair with ottoman, good lighting, luscious towels. And the location is terrific -- easy access to capitol hill, and most of the adminsitrative offices, and also near the tourist centers on the mall. So one reason I come back is that I know that everything I need is there, and of high quality. But it's the lobby that tells the real story. It is gorgeous in an old fashioned way, not too large and not very modern at all. Look at the mosaic floor and marble and you immediately think of Gore Vidal's great novels of Washington (read them if you haven't.) At any moment security guards for mideast dignitaries could be attempting to clear a path around tourists with strollers, t-shirts and umbrellas. The front desk staff moves from one clientele to the other seamlessly. I also love the fact that for all the Willard's size, you still feel like you are in a smaller hotel. Restaurants are intimate, and the staff is prompt. But for the walk down long halls to your room, you would not comrprehend the size of the place. What's wrong with the Willard -- dumb things, like paying for WIFI, not enough electrical outlets, even in the recently remodeled rooms. Ancient shower heads. And like every top tier hotel, almost everything is over priced, particularly breakfast which is ridiculously expensive and not fabulous. But if you want to have a truly comfortable, pleasant stay, feel very well taken care of, and feel that you have been to the Nation;s capital and not just another nice hotel room, do have a turn at the Willard.

“Really a great hotel!!!” The rooms were very large and clean. Rooms quite and free internet for HH members. Also, they have an employee named Mike. I've stayed at two hotels a month for the past year and I can tell you, Mike is the most helpful staff person I've seen. He noticed that I seemed lost and confused (I had to go to a pharmacy, but thought it was closed). He knew where it was and exactly what time it closed. I had several run in's with him and he was so helpful each time. The Capital Club was amazing (exercise room). In spite of being down town, it was very quiet.

“The Complete Package” Have stayed here previously and this was for a short stay on our way home from Europe. The Marriott is well located and is connected to two very nice malls (Copley and Prudential) with restaurants (Legal Sea Foods among others). We had a nice clean, quiet room with a great view (15th floor). They had already sent up the roll away bed for our daughter (nice, because we were tired from a long flight). Check in was friendly and fast. The hotel has many nice amenities to include an indoor pool and jacuzzi, a Starbucks in the lobby, a sushi bar, and a nice restaraunt. A full breakfast buffet for our daughter was $4.95- a great deal. Hotel is in a nice part of town. You can easily walk to Newbury St. (great shops and restaurants), The Boston Public Garden (swan boats), and to other interesting sites. The subway is also very close by. I would recommend this hotel as a very good overall value and good location for Boston. I would definitely stay here again. Only (very) minor negative comment would be that the hallway carpet was overdue for vaccuuming.

“Great View & Location but can be noisy” This Holida Inn is in a great location right in downtown San Diego right on the bay. It is right across the street from the San Diego Cruise Terminal so cruise ships are coming and going daily. Get a room with a bay view on a high floor and you won't be disappointed. All rooms have balcanies so you can sit outside and watch the boats in the bay as well as seeing the planes coming and going from the airport. The rooms are very nice and completely updated. Everything was comfy and clean. The only thing that was kind of weird was that the bathroom had a frosted glass sliding door which doesn't give much privacy. My only concern was that you could hear noises from other rooms as well as the balcanies from other people talking and partying on their balcanies. Since this is an older hotel, the noise insulation is very poor. But, all in all, this was a great location and easy to get around without the feeling of a busy crammed in downtown hotel. Lots of parking but about $22 per day. Good British Pub style restaurant in the hotel with a Ruth's Chris Steakhouse right on the property also. I would definately stay here again. But again, make sure you get a bay view room on a high floor and you will just love the view.

“Excellent option near Camden Yards” I recently stayed at this Hilton for two nights while at a convention. The check-in was smooth and I was even able to check-in a few hours early - very nice. My room was on the 6th floor and was just a standard king-bed room. One thing I really liked about the TV was that it had music available, including a really nice station that played jazz selections. Very nice to have playing in the background while I was doing work on the computer. There wasn't anything particularly special about this room category. There were some funky new lamps in bright colors which were different and cool. The bathroom was rather small. The shower head was at least 6 1/2 feet in the air. I assume this is because many of the visiting sports teams stay hear and they need the shower head to be that high to keep those customers happy. At 5'5", I could barely reach the head to adjust it. I just thought this was interesting to note, not really a complaint. The room itself was very clean and the maid service was excellent. There were plenty of towels in my room, by the way. There were six elevators, and I never had to wait more than 15 seconds for an elevator. This is a major accomplishment in a high-rose hotel. Kudos to the Hilton! The convention was in the Hilton, and the convention services were excellent. The public bathrooms were spotlessly clean and the food service was fantastic. The fitness center was one of the nicest I've seen in a long time at a hotel. Located on the 4th floor, there were 10 treadmills, at least 6 ellipticals, and 3 bikes, plus free weights and weight machines. The fitness center opens at 5:00 a.m., which is fantastic since my days start early. There were plenty of towels, cups, water and sanitizing wipes. The BEST part of the fitness center was the view of Camden Yards. Absolutely breathtaking. There is a small verandah with chairs next to the fitness area that I'm sure gets a lot of use when the O's are playing. There are numerous restaurants nearyby. We ate lunch at Oliver's, a brew pub about 2 blocks away across the street on Pratt. Excellent sandwiches and craft brews. We also had a few drinks in the lobby bar. I thought the service was excellent and the prices were reasonable. I had breakfast both days in the Executive Lounge, which is a nice perk for Gold Hilton Honors members. There was a good supply of pastries, fruits, breads, and juices. We did walk to the Inner Harbor one evening - less than 15 minutes away and a very enjoyable walk. I am already planning to return for an O's game with my husband.

“More Positives Then Negatives” I can see where people would pick up on the age. There were a couple of crimescene-like stains on my carpet that I tried not to contaminate with trace evidence by stepping in. The WiFi shuts down if too many people are in the hotel. And the hotel was PACKED so it was pretty spotty. And I was on business, so THAT really didn't help. The guys from engineering did something like re-boot the transmitter and it popped on for about 24 hours. They were the ones who acknowledged that the system is deficient. You don't want to be on the northside. You get train AND highway noise. Upside? Beautiful atrium. Very very nice employees. Great buffet and...wait for it...and GREAT non-chain steakhouse on the property.

“I just love the layout Of my room!” Felt secure in this hotel. I feel in love with the layout of my room. Wish all hotels where like this. They have Starbucks coffee in each room! Didn't venture out so this is all I have to say. I will be back.

“Expensive for what it delivers” This hotel does not live up to some of the rave reviews I read on this site and it is expensive for what it delivers. The rooms are adeqaute but old-fashioned, bordering on the shabby. Nobody at the front desk advised me on arrival that there was a free breakfast, and I therefore did not avail of it - indeed these staff, though not discourteous, are not exactly pro-active. The exception is the excellent hall-porter, who is cheerful and efficient and who was coping splendidly with the conditions of Great Blizzard of February 2006. Free Broadband access is only through two terminals in the "business centre" and users are limited to 30 minutes per session - very inconvenient for anybody needing longer access for business communication purposes. I will not be coming back to this hotel, despite its central location.

“Great Stay ” Just got back from New York - stayed at the Affinia Dumont in a king suite. There were three of us - my sister, myself and my adult son. We arrived for check-in early, around 1:00 p.m. and our room was ready. The guy checking us in told us "You are going to love your room." He was right! We were in room 3305, a corner unit. We had views of the Chrysler Building and the East River, it was totally awesome. We were treated like royalty the entire time. The staff is so nice and helpful. We booked through Expedia, and never requested anything special - I was hoping for a room on a high floor - but never asked for it - Normally when I book through a discount booking service, the rooms are not always the best - but you compromise because you get a good price. We were really surprised that we got such a great room at a discounted price. The bed was great, we took advantage of the "pillow" menu and ordered some down feather pillows, which were delivered immediately. My son used the sofa bed and he slept really good on it. The kitchen was great, the bathroom was big too - the bathtub was enormous, great for soaking in the tub. I cannot think of one negative - it was all positive. We loved the Murray Hill section, used the subways and buses mostly to get around - sometimes got a cab - but tried to rely on public transportation. The doorman was great, always helped us and always welcomed us back after a long day of sightseeing. If you go to New York - treat yourself to the Affinia Dumont, it really is a great place.

“Third visit. Can't beat the price, location and size of rooms.” This was our third visit to this Affinia property. Our rate for a Junior Suite was $279/night, which was good at the time. I have reserved this property for less during February and with more advance notice other times of the year. The suite was plenty big for two of us. Make sure to buy water and snacks outside of the hotel, as the prices were very steep for the honor bar - $7 for a bottle of water. The 2nd floor club lounge is nice, with free coffee, tea, wifi, televison and Wii in the back room. This was a valuable place to catch up on business, as internet in the room was at least $15/day. We did not have breakfast at the hotel; they offer a continental room service for $9pp or $15 buffet in the lounge. Instead, we opted to visit Morning Star Cafe on 2nd btw 50th and 51st. I may return to this hotel again, but am thinking of the Affinia Manhattan or Shelbourne next time to compare.

“Fantastic Location!” You just can't go wrong with this location if you want to be in the middle of the best San Fran shopping, it's all right there. I stayed in the old section and enjoyed my room which was updated and so unlike the typical cookie cutter hotel room. The hallways were wide and grand matching the total feel of this old hotel. The in room coffee maker made pretty good coffee as well.

“You Get What You Pay For” This hotel has many pluses and minuses. On the plus side the staff is very friendly. There is free parking, however the garage entrance is extremely narrow and only small cars can get in and maneuver inside. The beds are average quality. They also give you tiny soap bars, so I went out and purchased my own. However, they have good shower heads. The TV remote control is old and does not work very well, and I did not get HBO as advertised. There is a small fridge and microwave in the room. They provide free pastries and coffee for breakfast. The locations is good. The price is low by San Francisco standards, but remember you get what you pay for.

“Very Good......Dated......they mean well” This was the second time we stayed and we had the same Fireplace Suite each time. This time the carpets had been replaced and the furniture re-uppolstered. That made a difference to the feel of the room. This is a very good hotel and staff is nice and well-meaning. Obviously, this is an old property and Taj will have to deal with that until it invests in a full "makeover" which might never happen. There is no comparison between this hotel and the Four Seasons.

“Fantastic hotel.” I was actually on business but had to select "Leisure" for this review because I had my family with me and needed to make the point that this is a great hotel for families. Do not be put off by thinking "maybe it's too much of a party/hipster hotel." It was great. Beginning with the reservationist who help us get an amazing deal (double upgrade to a phat suite) and advised us on the best room type for a family, to the front desk staff, the concierge, the doormen and especially the staff at the Terrace restaurant, everyone made our family feel at home. Our kids are 6 and 18 months and they were naturally all over the place. Not only did we never get the look that says: "this place is far too cool for kids" but just the opposite. The hotel staff went out of their way to be helpful. The hotel is a real feast of design. The lobby and all the public rooms are real knockouts. And there is a rotating contemporary art collection of museum quality pieces that will blow you away - we're talking Mapplethorp, Warhol, Wool, Hirst, - big time stuff. We were in room 404, which is a park view suite (check the website for excellent photos and floor plans). We had plenty of room, a huge walk in closet and a shower that was big enough for all 4 of us at once! The bed was extremely comfortable and we had a view from the bedroom and the living room over Gramercy Park (which as a guest of the hotel you'll have access to, much to the envy of your NYC friends). The living room was nice and large and came with a pull out sofa and a dining table/desk. There were also two closets, one a walk in, which was great to have. The only complaint of the entire stay was that the pull out mattress was a bit flimsy and while fine for a 6 year old weighing 50 lbs, anyone much larger would definitely not be happy with it. Finally, while the room and the furnishing are on the darker side (think a fashionable, modern version of Old New York), unlike some NYC hotels going for mood, every light and switch in the room was on a dimmer so if needed, you could blast the place with light. This sounds minor but after a weeklong stay at the Tribeca Grand last year, we were going nuts because the room was so dark (no dimmers), we were literally losing our belongings in the corners. The hotel is not located near Times Square, Empire State Building, etc. so if you want that, look elsewhere. However, in our opinion the location of the hotel is really a plus if you want a real NYC experience. Gramercy is a great neighborhood filled with cool bars and places to eat, and is also close to great shopping in Union Square, LES, Bowery, Nolita and even Soho. Of course the park itself is an incredible treat and our kids loved running around in it - and how often do you get a beautiful 1.5-acre park in the middle of Manhattan entirely to yourself? Unless you've got $4-5M for a townhouse lining the park, never. Straight across town via a 20 min walk is Chelsea and the whole gallery scene. You're also close to the incredible Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art that is definitely one of New York's hidden gems. And if you want to go uptown, you can catch the 4,5 or 6 trains a block away that will take you to the upper East Side (and to Grand Central as well). Lastly, the food at the hotel was great as well. Breakfasts on the Terrace were really nice and room service was terrific and fast. We had a great experience and would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

“Perfect location.” Perfectly located in the heart of Back Bay, right on Copley square and within a minutes walk to the subway and dozens of restaurants. Stayed here by choice too many times so have got to know the place. Excellent views are to be had from the higher floors, with rooms **01 to **12 facing the river being the most spectacular with the corner room suites taking top spot. The hotel is at the end of the 1/2 mile long walkway connected malls so no need to venture outside when a Nor-Easter hits the city in the depth of winter. Decor varies between rooms, some having been recently redocorated, but from my observations the bathroom fittings were left unchanged so are getting a little faded. Room rates vary considerably due to the various conventions taking place. The Starwood guest complimentary daily Panna water ration can be very illusive. 6 days into this trip and I am still waiting and now gasping for my first bottle. Gym was renovated and extended a few years back and is now quite bright and roomy, although the pool is a little small, but you can take a 8 minute walk through the mall to the sheraton if you need a big pool. For joggers the Charles river is a 1/4 mile away where you can join the hoards of walkers, runners and cyclists, but to enjoy the best views of Boston cross over the river on Mass Ave and return over the Salt + Pepper pot bridge, which is best enjoyed at sun-set. (don't forget the camera). Starbucks just off the lobby helps get the day off to a fine start. Advisable not to send 'cold wash only' items in the laundry. If you get a good room at a reasonable rate this is a very nice hotel.

“Convenient locale, noisy” We love the hotel for being in Financial/ lower Manhattan which, although not busy on the weekends, is very handy for Newark arrivals, next door to discount shopping Mecca Century 21. It's also right by the 5/6 subway and walking distance to the 4. On a nice day, it's an easy walk to Chinatown, Little Italy, Bowery and Tribeca On the downside, it's dead at night and the construction at the twin towers means a lot of noise unless you pay extra for a city view.

“Can we say amazing?!” Really, really nice! I paid the AAA rate and was upgraded to a suite before I got there. There was a nice plate of fruit in the room that was perfectly ripened. Bed was extremely comfortable, great bathroom-lighting was terrific!. Breakfast downstairs was surprisingly good. It's two steps up from standard continental breakfast. Only one issue and it's not something that they could have done anything about--guy above me was so loud!! I could hear his phone conversations and his snoring all night long.

“Tired and too big” Largest hotel in DC, very impersonal. The room was small and pretty standard. The gym has many defect machines and old weight equipment. Very expensive room service, and I travel all over. Not convincing.

“Would love to go back” I stayed here with a couple friends from out of town, and they said it was the first good night's sleep they had in NYC. We may have lucked out with the room: three big windows looking over Broadway instead of a brick wall (my more typical scenario in NY hotels) Beds were super comfortable, room was elegant and quiet, and cookies and Belgian chocolates were a nice touch. I loved the big marble shower, and got a laugh out of the small flat screen television in the bathroom. Great neighborhood, super convenient to subway. Had a good lunch at the cafe at Fairway Market a couple blocks away. Room wasn't cheap, but it was a splurge, and besides, have you checked out the NYC hotel rates this fall?

“traditionelles Hotel in die Jahre gekommen” Wir waren im Oktober 2010 dort und hatten ein Eckzimmer in der 24 Etage . Es ist ein sehr lautes Hotel , die Isolierung der Fenster war schlecht. Es ist empfehlenswert Wachs-Ohrstöpsel zu benutzen. Da das Hotel an einer Kreuzung liegt mitten in NY wird die ganze Nacht gehupt ! Das Zimmer war groß und der Ausblick über NY war interessant. Wir hatten 3 Fenster ( 2 im Schlafzimmer u. 1 im Badezimmer ) Unsere Freunde hatten in der 17 Etage ein Zimmer bekommen, was sie sofort reklamiert haben, als sie unser Zimmer gesehen haben. Es ist wichtig zu wissen, daß ab der 23 Etage die Zimmer heller und freundlicher sind und auch größer ! Danach bekamen sie auch ein Zimmer in unserer Etage, der Preis war bei beiden Zimmern identisch ! Auch die Etagen sehen schon viel freundlicher aus wenn man aus dem Fahrstuhl aussteigt! Außerdem hat dieses Hotel kein Schwimmbad. Man sagte uns, es wäre zu alt um nachzurüsten.. Wie uns an der Rezeption mitgeteilt wurde, gibt es keine leiseren Zimmer. Nur um so höher, desto leiser. Was noch wichtig ist zu sagen!, unbedingt die Hotelrechnung aufheben!!!! Als wir wieder zu Hause waren, meldete das Hotel nochmals die Abbuchung auf der Kreditkarte an, obwohl dieses Hotel beim Reiseveranstalter in Deutschland schon bezahlt wurde ( mit Voucher von "Der Tours " eingecheckt!) unsere Kreditkartenfirma hat uns keine Hilfe angeboten, als wir dies stornieren wollten, obwohl wir beim auschecken eine " Null-Rechnung" erhalten haben. Auch das Hotel reagierte nicht!! Nur unser Reiseveranstalter konnte es nach 6 Wochen erreichen, daß wir das Geld wieder gutgeschrieben bekamen !! Dies empfanden wir auf jeden Fall nicht seriös vom Hotel ! Es ist ein traditionelles Hotel, in dem ich unbedingt einmal wohnen wollte,, aber 1 x reicht auch. Es gibt mittlerweile viel moderner Hotels in NY die viel mehr für Ihre Gäste anbieten. Wir waren 5 Tage dort !

“Customer Service is NOT a priority” Let me be blunt: 1. I had to call the hotel twice to get a shuttle to pick me up from terminal E of the airport. While the operator apologized for “forgetting” to tell the driver after the 1st call, waiting at night for 48 minutes to get a 5 minute ride to the hotel is just plain bad service. 2. The outside of building is ugly. Think 1960’s, concrete block building. 3. No one at the front door to help with bags or the door. Maybe the shuttle driver could have pitched in and helped out? 4. Watch out, if you have a late flight that lands after midnight, there is no room service and no open restaurant. You have to settle for a day-old muffins and a bottle of water in the 24-hr. coffee bar. 5. The 3 year old “renovated” rooms tried look trendy but failed in my opinion. This failure is partly due to being small and dark. The trendy furniture seemed shabby or worn. Only 2 good things to report here: 1. The room was quite, I did not hear outside noise in the hallway or from other rooms. 2. Mr. G’s restaurant. The food is above average (but so is the price) and it has a good drink selection.

“Might be the worst Marriott property to stay if you are a elite member” I am currently staying for 6 nights due to a dermatology convention in town. I could not get rooms closer to the convention center below $350 at the Marriott Marquis or at the gaslamp so I decided to stay here at $160 a night. The room needs renovation and very small by Marriott standards. There is no concierge at this property and although there is a concierge lounge, the variety and quality of food/snacks that are available is poor. The concierge lounge is closed on weekends and usually at other Marriott properties, the hotel will give you a breakfast voucher if you are a platinum member. Well, not at this property. I ordered a simple burger for room service and the food did arrive on time but was cold and not cooked as I ordered. I am usually happy with the Marriott properties due to the consistent level of the properties and the amenities, however unless you have no other options in San Diego, stay away from this one.

“Outclassed by other options” The Taj clearly wants to compete with properties like the Four Seasons or the Mandarin Oriental, but it has a monstrously long way to go to compete with those giants. It's only real asset is location, on a posh corner near the Boston Common. The room decor is more dowdy grandma than chic, and we even noticed some unappealing stains on the carpet. The bathroom was cramped and small, and the inside of the closet looked like it hadn't been modernized in years. When we initially pulled up to the hotel, rather than being greeted by a welcoming valet, we would curtly told we had to enter via a different route. Not a gracious welcome for a hotel aspiring to four or more stars. We ordered room service (coffee and two muffins; a meal that didn't even require turning on a stove), and it was an hour wait; by the time it arrived, we had to leave it behind on the tiny room desk because we had a plane to catch. The housekeeping staff was chatty and loud in the morning; we could hear them outside our door at a regrettably early hour. At almost $500 for a single night's stay in an undistinguished room, this place is egregiously overpriced. At those rates, it should offer something at least distinctive and special. Instead, it felt like a shell of the old Ritz Carlton that time and TLC had long since left in the dust....

“Great location- Nice rooms” We stayed here 7 years ago and liked it and after looking at hotwire options we chose to stay here again because of location and the good breakfast. This place is close to most everything you would want to do. It's a quick walk to the harbor area and the depot. You're a quick drive from just about everything else, including La Jolla. The staff is very accommadating, rooms are nice, breakfast is very good. Parking is not too expensive and you get your own car so its not a big deal any time you want to leave.

“An average W” Nice hotel, centrally situated, with spacious and comfortable rooms. I frankly don't understand why W hotels have to be so poorly lighted in the inside, but perhaps it's only a matter of taste. As other guest mentioned, noise from the fire station can be annoying.

“Great location next to arena and downtown, we'll be back!” We stayed five (yes, 5 adults!) in one double bed room for a major convention at the nearby Nationwide Arena. We had no problem getting a cot bed for odd person. This can sometimes be a challenge nowadays in hotels. As said in the title, the hotel is very close to the arena (the closest we could find). We really enjoyed being able to take the short 2 minute walk there, instead of the usual cab or shuttle. The hotel itself is very nice. I don't care for the brutalist styling on the outside, but that's a minor detail (I enjoy architecture). The lobby is very large and can accommodate alot of people at once... thankfully since the hotel was fully booked and most arrived at the same time at the end of the convention. Too bad the elevators couldn't keep up with the demand! The room seemed to be recently renovated; great modern class. The beds were very comfortable, although a tiny bit soft. I slept like a sheep after exciting days at conference. The ice machine on our floor could barely produce enough ice (I guess we weren't the only ones hoping to use it). Service for extras was very quick, so no problems in that department. One minor quibble : Does water in Columbus ever turn cold? No matter how long we had the tap turned on for cold water, it was, at best, tepid. This may or may not be an issue with the hotel. Another positive is the fact that the hotel is connected directly to a food court where you can get a variety of quick and decent meals. Cheaper than hotel food. Overall, considering the great location downtown, overall amenities at the hotel and quality rooms, I have no problem rating the Hyatt Regency Columbus a top-notch 3.5 star to a very decent 4 star hotel.

“Renovations were a real inconvenience.” The hotel was decent but trying to figure out which walkways were open or closed was a hassle. Perhaps the guests should have received hardhats at check-in. The other thing that was noticeable was the ambivalence of the staff; there appeared to be no motivation to make the guests feel welcomed at the hotel.

“Love it more every time!” I recently revistied the Crescent and I love it twice as much! Upon arrival 9am the front desk staff checked us in immediately and asked us if we would like any room service sent up to the room since we had just arrived from the airport. The notes from the manager of the hotel were such a nice personal touch. We were given a tour of the hotel and we were escorted to our room with the bellman. We stayed in a loft suite which is very spacious and tastefully decorated. The bed is comfortable and you could throw a party in the shower! The opening french doors are a nice touch along with the lady primrose toiletries. The food at Beaunash was fabulous and had a very romantic setting. The Crescent Club for drinks was had a great view and they made the best kir royal we have ever tasted. There are many of Dallas' finest restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. The spa facilities are fabulous with a whirlpool room, steam sauna and private showers. Every amenity you could think of is available to use after your treatments. The eucalytptus towels right next to the steam sauna were refreshing. My only complaint was the spa reception staff: we were never given a tour of the facilities and they were somewhat rude upon checkout when they asked if our tabs would be on one check or two. Spa reception staff needs improvement! Room service was efficient and the breakfast pastries are wonderful. Service is brought out on a wheeled tray with silver which is handy so you can set it up where you like. Check out was smooth and the bill was correct. The valet staff is professional and courteous. One of my favorite hotels to stay in!

“Wonderful hotel, service, but beware of "incidental charges."” My husband and I visited this hotel/city as a late Valentine's Day celebration. The hotel just opened a few months ago. Rooms are very nice-large and comfortable with large windows. Comfortable chairs, desk area, flat screen TV, large closet. Bathroom was large with nice amenities. We had an upper room with views of White River State Park and the White River. Service was wonderful-from the clerk at the front desk through everyone we ran into until check out. All were very helpful, asking how we liked our stay, smiles...very much appreciated. Location was near several attractions-Indiana State Museum was across the street and within walking distance. Indy Zoo, White River Gardens, & Victory Field are all very close. We didn't use Internet or any other services. Valet/parking is available on site, but is $28 for regular parking/$32 for valet. There is a parking garage across the street connected to the hotel by a skywalk that is available for less than half the price that we utilized. We had breakfast in the Osteria Pronto restaurant-also very nice. Lots of the regular breakfast fare plus a made to order omelet bar. Lots of fresh fruit, danish...great assortment all around. And again, service was great. Very attentive without being overbearing. My only complaint about this hotel was the bill....a $50 "incidental fee" was tacked on to the bill when we checked in to cover damages or extras. No mention of this on the confirmation or at check in. Was assured it would be removed and credited to my card within a week.
