Suggested that they might want to mention this somewhere along the way so it's not a surprise when you check out. I would definitely recommend this hotel for a downtown Indy visit.

“Ottima la posizione e la struttura.” Hotel collocato in un antico palazzo proprio in mezzo al centro storico di Philadelphia costituito dall' Indiependence Park. Accoglienza alla reception gradevolissima, resa tale anche dalla raffinatezza della hall. Camera veramente carina con letto a baldacchino (per la verità non proprio comodo). Ambienti curati e puliti, colazione superba. Il mercoledi pomeriggio degustazione di formaggi frutta e vino compresi nel prezzo. Soggiorno piacevolissimo

“Good location near the airport - Great staff!” Spent one night there for a business trip. All of the staff was extremely friendly. As it has been said this hotel is 2 years old but still seems new inside. I like the rooms as they are very comfortable and clean. The breakfast buffet was very good. The layout is a bit awkward (they didn't design that space very well. Too narrow. But all in all a great hotel.

“部屋は広かった” Civic Center駅の前にあるのですぐわかりました。 中心地からはひと駅離れていますが、徒歩でも十分。 値段が安いので全然期待していませんでしたが、部屋は意外と広く、バスルームもゆったりしてきれいでした。 ただ、周囲の環境はあまりよろしくないので夜遅くは出歩かない方がいいと思います。 また、夜遅くまで外では人の話し声(たまに奇声)がして気になって眠れませんでした。 私は気づきませんでしたが、のちにこのホテルに泊まった友人によると、部屋に耳栓が置いてあるとか。

“Bien situé et bon rapport qualité prix.” Hôtel agréable, situé vers la 6 e avenue, avec bus et métro à côté. Chambres propres et de taille suffisante. Clim un peu bruyante mais efficace. Aucun bruit de rue (ns étions au 17eme) et literie excellente. Petit déjeuner complet et toujours bien achalandé: gaufres, fruits frais, céréales, muffins, bagels... Personnel agréable. À recommander!

“One of the Best Large Hotels on the Harbor” Great rooms and public spaces. Courteous staff and walkable jaunts to Fells Point and Inner Harbor. Free Internet for Marriotts Frequent Guest program members. Recommend you self park to save some cash. Great restaurants nearby. Near a water taxi stop.

“Not horrible, but not that great.” For the price, you'd expect more. The rooms are small but nice. The major problem lies in the fact that they do not air condition the common areas. It was blazing hot all the time. Fortunately the air in our room worked great. The hotel seems seriously understaffed. There was never a bell cap or concierge. The front desk staff knew nothing about places to go in the area, where to get the Charm City Circulator, etc. When I tried to get a luggage cart to take our luggage downstairs, they would not allow us to take one without a staff person. ($$$$$$$) We were there for a convention, and the elevators were seriously overtaxed. The wait was ridiculous. The ice machine on our floor was broken most of the week, and the only one that worked was about six floors down. Parking was ridiculous. The area is definitely dicey. I would not stay here again if I have the misfortune to go back to Baltimore.

“Nur zur Not” Wir wählten dieses Hotel, da alle anderen Hotels zu der Zeit entweder ausgebucht oder deutlich zu teuer für unseren Geldbeutel waren. Es handelt sich hier um ein eingeschossiges Motel, welches am Stadtrand von Boston liegt. Ein kostenloser Shuttle fährt zum Bahnhof bzw. zu einer U-Bahn-Station, sodass von daher die Lage für nicht motorisierte Gäste in Ordnung geht. Allerdings liegt das Hotel zwischen Highways und neben einer Bahnstrecke in einem Gewerbegebiet. Unser Zimmer war im Erdgeschoss und dunkel. Der Teppich hat schon bessere Zeiten erlebt, wie das ganze Hotel mal renoviert werden könnte. Das Personal ist zwar freundlich und auch hilfsbereit, wir kamen uns allerdings öfters als lästige Bittsteller vor. Alle zuvor schriftlich bestätigten Wünsche unsererseits wurden nicht berücksichtigt. Das ganze Hotel war dunkel, muffig, staubig und könnte mehr als eine Grundreinigung gut gebrauchen. Richtig gewöhnungsbedürftig war der Frühstücksraum: wie sooft in Motels, gab es "Plastik"-frühstück: Geschirr, Besteck und viele Verpackungen werden von den Gästen weggeschmissen. Das Personal ließ sich in diesem kleinen Raum kaum blicken, es wurden die überquellenden Abfalleimer selten geleert, die Tische nicht gereinigt oder fehlende Lebensmittel nachgelegt. Das ganze Gegenteil war das Restaurant mit Bar in direkter Nachbarschaft: gemütlich, angemessene Preise, leckere Steaks, freundliche Bedienung - dies rettete unseren Aufenthalt! Auf der anderen Seite gab es ein großes Bowlingcenter mit auch anderen Sportmöglichkeiten im Angebot.

“Good hotel, location so-so” My family and I stayed here for 1 night in June 2006. The hotel is right near Houston's Hobby Airport on the south side of town. In fact, we could watch the jets take off from our hotel window. However, I believe Hobby has severe restrictions on nighttime flying. So do not worry about airport activity keeping you up at night. We never heard a single jet during the night. The staff was extremely friendly (check in, check out, restaurant). Our room was very spacious (we were upgraded to a suite) and clean. The breakfast was excellent (hot and cold buffet). It has a very nice outdoor pool. We used it a couple times during our short stay. There was wireless internet access in the room, but it was not free. There was not much in the way of restaurants nearby (other than a Jack-in-the-Box). So plan on a short (15-20 min) drive to find something decent. In the title, I said the location was so-so. The area around Hobby is not the greatest neighborhood. However, we always felt safe at the hotel and the parking lot. So do not let that be a concern. But you have to drive to get to anything. That said, it is a great location if you want to be midway between downtown Houston and NASA and close to (but not next to) the Gulf Freeway.

“Dirty, odor and outdated!” Had to stay due to a cancelled flight. The room is a hike outside from the main lobby. The spread had a huge ugly stain, toothpaste smears still on the counter, hair on bathroom floor, dust on the coffee maker, unpleasant odor and very noisy ac. Couldn't wait to check out of this one!

“Nice But..............” I stayed at this hotel for one night. It is in lower Queen Anne area which is the far north end of downtown. It is within walking distance to the Seattle Center area (Space Needle) but not much else. You will want a car if you are going to sightsee. Check in is a bit difficult as there is no off street place to park the car while you check in. There are three 3 minute loading spaces in front that can be used but once they are filled you have to circle the block and try to find a place to park. Parking is an additional $15 per night which is about normal for the area. The building itself is quite nice and is a solid three star facility EXCEPT there is no air conditioning in the rooms. Even in Seattle you need air conditioning in the summer as the days can easily be in the 80's and sometimes in the 90's. Wi-fi works well EXCEPT it is an additional $5 a day which is not the norm in this class of hotel. Also they strangely make you walk back to the front desk after check in to retrieve a password and charge your account. It would be better if they would just ask you if you wanted wi-fi when you checked in. The room is comfortable and clean although on the small side. It does have an in room coffee maker and refridgerator and also has free popcorn and bottled water. It does not offer a breakfast, although, there is a Starbucks directly attached to the hotel. All in all this would not be my first choice as the lack of air conditioning and the charge for internet is less than the norm for a three star property. Don't get me wrong there is nothing wrong with the property, just not what I have come to expect from hotels of this class.

“Good, not great” We spent one night here on the King Tut package, traveling with another couple. The vip exhibit passes allowed us to bypass horrendous lines and made booking through the convention and visitors bureau website totally worth it but the hotel was not as great as some of the reviews say. We stayed in a renovated room--the flat screen tv was really nice and I liked the overall decor but the furniture had already started to look beat up and not all parts of the room had been upgraded. The carpet in our room and our friends' room was stained and old, the stucco ceiling was cracking and part of our closet frame was falling off. Plus there was trash from previous guests wedged into a gap between the bathroom wall and the vanity. The sleep number bed was fun to try, but sorry Lindsay Wagner, I did wake up in the middle of the night and turn over many times. The fluffy duvet and pillows were really nice though. The main problem was noise--there seemed to be nothing in the way of soundproofing. You could clearly hear everything in the hall and even in other rooms and we could hear the elevator chimes even though we weren't that close. Unless other people were really careful closing their doors the slams when they shut were just awful. If it weren't for the really loud ac, which thankfully provided some white noise, we would not have gotten any sleep. And don't let the lure of included breakfast factor into your decision to stay here. Included in our package were 2 $12 coupons for breakfast but service in the restaurant was just awful and the food was mediocre. It's really unfortunate too as the menu is really interesting and the space is really attractive. Our friends who ate at another time also experienced horrific service. If you can get a good rate, say below $150, this is not a bad place to stay, but for more I'd look around.

“Not So Inspired” The Muse is a stylish boutique hotel near Times Square – an area that is central for tourists and convenient to the theater district – otherwise it is not a very nice area. The hotel lobby is sleek and modern as is the bar. The bathrooms just off the lobby are funky and worth a visit. The room décor was chic and new, but the room itself was not so special, rather small, dark and narrow. The bathroom was also small and dark; the Etro toiletries were a nice touch. Our room faced 46th street, and the street noise was horrible; we were awakened by trucks every morning around 3am. Next time I am in the city, I’ll try another hotel.

“Average Comfort Inn - clean and comfy” Stayed for 1 night while in NYC to see Oprah. Checked in at 11:30 am as we had arrived early form Boston. Had a room right off the Lobby, which was a little noisy, but not horrible. Probably would ask for a room not in the lobby if I stayed again. The breakfast was free and good with eggs, bacon, toast and bread, waffles, juice, coffee and all the other basics. Not bad for free. Overall the rooms are small, as are most NYC rooms, but efficient with everything you need. They are clean and comfy for a couple nights sleep. Great location, convenient to Times Square and Midtowmn, if that is your thing.

“Very Good Experience” We stayed here for two nights with our teenage daughters. The room was clean and modern - two large flat-screen TVs. Every single staff member we encountered was polite and gracious to a fault.

“Excellent Hotel!” After traveling with 3 kids ages 9, 10 & 12 through Europe for 2 1/2 weeks, our last stop was New York for 6 nights. It could not have been a better place for us to end our trip!! The hotel was fantastic and the staff was excellent. The doorman and concierge were very helpful during our whole trip. We obviously needed a laundromat after being in Europe for so long and the concierge recommended his, it was fantastic, my husband and I got to truly experience being New Yorkers! The location is unbeatable, we walked everywhere and the view of St. Patrick's cathedral topped off our stay. We went during 4th of July weekend so we got an excellent deal which included breakfast. Breakfast is super pricey so this was definitely an added bonus. We will definitely stay here again! My boys loved it!!

“Above the high standard for a Marriott” I selected this property based on Trip Advisor advice. I was Not disappointed. The room was commodious and clean. The fitness center was adequate but everything was operational. Breakfast was hot and well-prepared. The staff are typical Marriott-trained and very courteous. I will definitely stay here again.

“Great hotel for business travelers” I've stayed at this hotel a few times now, and I've always had a great experience. The staff knows what they're doing, the rooms seem to be recently refurbished, and the District restaurant was really pretty good. The lobby in particular is stunning and it's fun to have a few drinks at the lobby bar. The hotel is fairly centrally located in downtown Phoenix, within walking distance of just about everything. Just a side note that has nothing to do with the hotel....downtown Phoenix is pretty dead on Sundays, except for the many homeless people that can be pretty aggressive about asking for money!

“A Sanctuary with updated touches” Located on West 47th St., just a half block from the TKTS booth (which you can practically see from the hotel's steps), lies the minimally marked, but dramatically lit, Sanctuary hotel. At night with its uplit facade, carved wooden doors and red carpeted stairs, it looks more like a nightclub than a hotel. The exterior must have been a deliberate choice, because the public spaces inside share this modernized baroque style. I affectionately dubbed it "Cher Meets the Jetsons." The front-to-back lounge has dim lights, dark, vibrant saturated color palette, ornate crystal chandeliers, seating nooks, multiple glass-fronted fireplaces and a tufted leather reception desk staffed by very friendly, enthusiastic workers. Though I didn't have extensive dealings with the folks there, they seemed super helpful, as I heard them working closely with other guests regarding airport transportation and local activities while I was checking in and out. I opted for a $30/night king room upgrade to Room 301. The design motifs carried through to the room with the floor to ceiling tufted leather headboard and crystal chandelier. The room was quite spacious, for this property if not NY in general, with every nook used wisely to maximize storage. I had two windows overlooking 47th, which did make for some noise, but nothing that anyone used to a city would find excessive. The sort of free-floating glass cube rainforest shower was lovely, but may not be for everyone. If you were a couple this could be quite inspirational. I don't know if the double bedded rooms have this feature, but despite the presence of a curtain to draw around the exterior of the cube for privacy, this would be a weird setup for people traveling with children. Each night of my two night stay, I had drinks with local friends at the bar. Cool setup, but it need some polishing. Night one, the bartender opted to yell over to us for our drink orders instead of coming over to get them. Night two the bartender lacked any ice for drinks. Really? A bar without ice probably needs a little more organization in the back. Though both people were pleasant, this was a weak link in the chain of experiences. In short, the design choices were bold, but well done. The staff and location were superlative. The breakfast is a good deal for the price point, though the bar needs a little more polishing in some of its practices. I could easily recommend this hotel to most people for that, but with the slight warning it might not be the best place for families.

“Believe the reviews” Okay, so I read the reviews here and didn't want to believe them so I called the hotel and talked to one of the managers (Bill). He said they were aware of the bad reviews and didn't really understand where they came from. i took him at his word and our family gave it a shot this weekend. Well Bill, here are some reasons your hotel isn't so great. We got to the hotel at 4:20 to find out our room wasn't ready. We left, did some shopping and got some dinner and came back. We went to find our room and couldn't locate it. It turns out it was in the dreaded "Executive tower" mentioned by an earlier poster so we had to cart the family and luggage back down the elevator and trek needlessly to the other building. The room smelt musty (so did the elevator for some reason) and seemed kind of dirty. We went down to the pool and it seemed nasty as well as being overcrowded with poorly behaved kids and adults breaking the posted rules. No enforcement, but then again there were no pool towels either. We called down for a couple of extra bath towels and after waiting more than 30 minutes I went to the front desk to get them and an extra pillow. The problem was they only had one attendant around and his list was so long we would have all been asleep by the time he got to us. It was pretty incredible that on an evening with close to 100% occupancy they only had one attendant around. The management followed suit the next day with only one cook there for your "free cooked to order breakfast". At times the line was 20-25 deep and totally preventable if the management had simply scheduled staff in a way that showed they cared at all about guests. There were nowhere near enough places to sit. Additionally, the beds were very uncomfortable and there were little things like running out of toilet paper without any extra in the room that just indicated they weren't paying attention to the details. While the staff was generally nice, I wouldn't call them terribly competent. the breakfast lines were better the second day we were there, but the food was really not up to Embassy Suites standards. Running out of things, no skim milk either day we were there, undercooked bacon, overly salty corned beef hash, etc. I called to see about checking out early before asking my wife and were told we could without penalty. I spoke with my wife who said as bad as it was moving could be worse and more annoying so I called the front desk again. This time one of the managers answered and to his credit he at least asked why we were displeased. He just didn't do anything about it except offer to move us to another room which I'd already said we weren't interested in. Other Embassy Suites I've been at would have offered something of value to keep my happy - these guys either didn't care or aren't empowered to do anything. Lastly, paying $15/day for 11mbps internet is outright silly given Motel 6 and every other cheap chain gives it away free. This hotel does not have the panache to be charging for internet access. You could say that the many issues we experienced with rude guests and their children is not the hotel's fault but I would say that in my many years of traveling that hotels mostly get the guests they want to get. I realize this is purely subjective on my part but be warned. I definately agree with the earlier poster that this is fo far from a typical Embassy Suites that you should not pay any attention to the brand in the hotel's name. There were some things that were good. The shower worked. They had FoxBusiness on cable. It's close to a nice mall (The Avenues) that has the best pet store we've ever been to if you like puppies (Puppies and Things).

“Still Great” The Peninsula is a fabulous hotel. I have stayed here many times in the past but it has been several years since my last stay (for convenience only). I had read some reviews stating that rooms were tired and in need of a redo. My room was not this way. It was perfect and did not feel dated at all. The rooms are large and well appointed. The bathroom is spacious with separate tub and shower as well as a separate dressing area. The staff and service are excellent. The location is great for shopping and restaurants. I was travelling alone and went to The Bar for a drink and dinner. It was very good. It’s old school with dark wood paneling and a fireplace. When I was there it was not crowded. I ate at the bar and felt totally comfortable alone. The bartender was helpful in a meal selection. Overall I can not recommend the Peninsula more highly.

“Not bad at all! I'd stay here again.” We chose to stay at the Hilton Checkers for our trip to Los Angeles for the Pac 10 tourney at Staples Center and we were very happy with our choice in the end. It is located in the financial district, so it is a little further from Staples Center and LA Live than many of the other hotel options, but overall the walk wasn't bad at all. It was good exercise. And we did the walk in the dark and we never felt uncomfortable. So no worries there. The service was pretty good. We were able to check in pretty early in the day (10am) with no problem. The room was very clean with a pretty nice bathroom and a nice flatscreen tv. The room was kinda small, but that didn't bother me in the least bit. Both nights I slept well when finally going to bed as the bed was very comfortable and there were no noise factors of any kind. Very peaceful which is kinda rare in downtown hotels it seems. The only complaint I had was the high cost of parking your car there, but I already knew about that before I booked it, so it wasn't like it was a big surprise. And pretty much all hotels are doing it now. So overall, I highly recommend this hotel to anyone going to downtown Los Angeles.

“**A Diamond In The Rough**” Just spent the weekend at the Mandarin Oriental, and I must say that by most standards, this was the most superb hotel I have ever had the pleasure of visiting. We found the hotel public spaces and room to be an architectural and interior design masterpiece. The designers did a wonderful job of melding the understated, elegant, peaceful asian atmosphere of MO with the vibrant exuberance of NYC. It seemed as if wherever we stood within the hotel, we were treated to the most spectacular views of NYC I have ever seen. Its location within the brand new Time Warner Center is sublime. It gives a whole new dimension to Columbus Circle and the scale and exterior design of the place is awe-inspiring. Upon arrival, we were upgraded to a Premier Hudson View Room, and what a room it was. Beautiful and plush with every amenity imaginable. It was a corner room with sweeping views of the river and city from every vantage point. We could lie in bed and have a perfect view of the Empire State Building directly in front of us. Amenities included plasma TV, DVD CD comprehensive entertainment system with surround sound, deep soaking tub with another great view, separate marble shower with huge rain shower head, minibar with great selection of beverages and Dean & DeLuca goodies, luxe bedding and feather pillows, robes, slippers, Fiji water and fresh flowers at turn down etc. We also had the pleasure of visiting the hotel spa. This was by far the best spa experience I have ever had. Again, the place is beautiful and refined. We were advised to arrive 45 mins early to use the "heat and water experience" which consists of beautiful, separate whirlpool, sauna/steam bath areas for men and women. Then a rest in the co-ed tea lounge and you're off to your treatment. By the time I got to my massage, I was already so relaxed that the transition was seamless. Afterwards, I was escorted to the relaxation room which is yet another exquisite area with daybeds, fountain, refreshments and more spectacular views of NYC. While the young staff was very friendly and tried very hard, I give the hotel less than five stars right now because of some of the gliches they are still having with service. Examples are, waited 40 mins. for our bags to be brought to our room upon check in (called several times and my husband finally had to go down and find them), room service a little slow (however the food was delicious), difficulty getting room service trays removed, turn down service on second night was very late (we were already in bed), minor difficulties with entertainment center that had to be reset on the second day. This and the fact that everything is EXHORBITANTLY expensive keep me from giving this hotel the highest mark. However, given the fact that it is still relatively new and working out the bugs, I am willing to give MO a little more time to become 5 star. Overall, a wonderful (albeit not cheap) hotel experience for any hotel snob.

“Good location” This hotel has a great location and nice rooms. I only stayed two nights and didn't need a kitchenette however the one in the room had everything you would need to cook a meal and was a descent size. The bed was confortable and the room also had a table for eating, a coffee table, love seat and wing back chair. The bathroom was cramped but adequate with a shower/tub combination and equipped with a hairdryer and drawers for toiletries. The location of this hotel is excellent, within walking distance to Times Square and many attractions. I would definately stay here again.

“Easy Park and Fly” We stayed here the night before an 8AM from O'Hare. The highway access is super easy and the shuttle got us to O'Hare quickly. Our room was on the tenth floor facing the highway so we had a little noise but nothing too bad. We got in late so we didn't visit the restaurant or bar but they looked decent enough. You're just steps from the Cumberland stop on the Blue Line so there are lots more options easily available. The room was a full suite, which I hadn't expected, so there was plenty of room to move around. I would consider this as a base for a long term visit to the city, at least when the Blue Line weekend work is done. Not a luxury hotel but very comfortable. We booked a ridiculously cheap rate through Park Sleep Fly, which included up to 2 weeks of covered parking and the total was less than if we'd used the O'Hare remote lot. We'd definitely stay here again.

“Delightful hotel with great meeting facilities” I love working with this hotel and have spoken at several events here. The location is terrific and it's easy to find. There's a gas station right on the corner so one can fill the gas tank on the way back to the airport rental car return. In fact, several times, I've taken advantage of the chance to save my company money and turned the rental car in early, then had the hotel shuttle pick me up.

“Very comfortable here” I've now stayed here on two separate trips and after this second stay, I'd definitely recommend this hotel. It is very clean, inside and out. Check-in is quick, there is plenty of free parking and an entrance in the front and in the back (with your room key), making it easy to get to your room. Again, clean rooms, comfortable bed and huge tv. There is complimentary breakfast, which I tried this time, and they had a great variety of hot and cold food. There is a wonderful, large fish tank in the lobby as well, which I love. I visited Christmas weekend, and there was a beautiful Christmas tree in the lobby, and I was wished a Merry Christmas that morning by a staff member passing in the hall-very nice! The only negatives I can mention are that it is a little farther away from the main hotel area, but it's right off the freeway so it makes it easy to get anywhere, and that the windows don't open. Not a big deal, but it's a minor annoyance if you're someone like me and would prefer a little fresh air over using the a/c sometimes. I will be considering this hotel again the next time I stay in San Diego.

“nice rooms but but nothing outstanding” great location / very nice rooms / clean / modern / my only complaint was at check-in .... if I'd been a full paying guest it would have been totally unacceptable. We sat in the lobby for at least an hour waiting for our room from about 2:30 to 3:30 ... maybe even longer, I forget now. We did great on Price Line at about 144 for the room .... so I over looked the wait !

“Very good and worth option in Midtown Manhattan” I had a very good stay at this property for two months. The room was spacious, with a very helpful small kitchen and a small bathroom, besides a comfortable bed. Sleep quality was very good, with little noise coming from the street. Sutton Court has a good location, almost on the corner of 57th and 1st. The neighborhood is fine and less crowded than a more central Midtown Manhattan address. There are two supermarkets and some pharmacies nearby, and a wine store right next door. You're gonna find coffee houses and restaurants all around the region. My biggest complaint refers to the distance from the subway. Although being very well located, it was a 10-minute walk to the nearest station. This is not a really bad problem, but keep it in mind if you need to take the train daily and you don't like, don't want or simply can't walk this distance. Obviously you can also take a bus (there's a stop close to the hotel) or a taxi. I would definitely recommend this property.

“Nice room. But average lounge and facilities” For the price the doubletree didnt live up to billing. It does have a downtown location. but the backbay and financial district are better locations to stay at. Pros large good room. Not very common in Boston Cons Small lobby. No safe in room $40 parking

“Good Location but the room had a 1 star almost hostel feel.” The location is fine- great for business and fine for tourism (there's so much going on down there now, and it's nearly almost every subway line). The lobby was tiny but the staff was quick, friendly, and professional (except for the dope who was throwing out profanities while telling his co-workers about his taxi fare). The room was tiny and ugly- tiny bed, super-cheap linens, a total of two crap pillows, super small bathroom, no safe, no chain lock, crappy furniture. I was so embarrassed when my significant other walked in. Plus the bathroom had hairs all over it- gross! I appreciate the hotel trying to offer a value, but in fact it wasn't a value (paid much less for a beautiful Doubletree around the corner). I would not stay here again and feel that Hotwire should be ashamed of themselves by saying this is a 3.5 star hotel.

“Calidad a buen precio” Motel de calidad situado en el downtown de Indianapolis. Aunque no está en el mismo centro en 10 minutos andando estás en el Monument Circle, hay que atravesar una zona un poco oscura de noche pero no hay sensación de inseguridad. En cuanto al motel, aunque por fuera parece un poco antiguo, por dentro está muy bien. Las habitaciones son amplias, con baño completo y TV de plasma. La única pega es que la conexión wi-fi (gratuita) no funciona muy bien. Parking gratuito. El desayuno, también gratuito y completo, se sirve en la planta baja. El personal de recepción es muy amable. Te dan planos, te comentan acerca de la zona, etc. Ideal para estancias cortas en las que no necesites un hotel de lujo.

“Great price and very nice!” My Aunt and I were in Memphis to see Graceland, as we frequently do. We usually stay at the Heartbreak Hotel, but decided to save some money and try the Comfort Inn. Beware, that the area of town is not the best, but don't let that spoil the Hotel. Also the hotel is near the Airport, and sometimes it is very loud. Also, the area has a lot of truck places and a lot of truckers stay at the hotel. The hotel lobby was very nice and open. We really liked the nice lobby and the entry way. We arrived at the Hotel around 10AM to make our reservation, and surprising we could already check in. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. Our room was clean and everything was in it's place. The room had a small microwave and a small fridge, two double beds, a comfy chair, a 22 inch TV. The bathroom was very clean, and the shower water pressure was awesome! We only had two complaints about the room. The first one was that there was small cob webs hanging from the ceiling trim. The second compliant was that the heater really smelt bad when turned on. The hotel offered a free breakfast, and it looked okay and there was a good variety, but we didn't have time to eat. Over all, this is a clean hotel and the room was very cozy. I will stay here again in the future.

“Very Good 4 Star” First time I have stayed at the Sofitel in New York having stayed at many other hotels in the city before. Other than the fact that one of our 3 rooms was not ready for check in at 4.30pm I was very impressed and it is one the best 4 star hotels in New York and can give some of the older 5 stars a run for their money. Positives:- Very comfortable beds Clean and modern Free use of computers in the lobby with a printer Complimentary evian in the rooms Nice size rooms Bathrooms with large bath and shower stall (not just a hip bath as in some hotels in NY) Nice gym with free evian sprays, towels etc Allowed to keep one room until 4pm with no extra charge Negatives:- 44th Street is good location for Times Square but otherwise not the most happening of locations Restaurant is expensive for breakfast (as others have said - use Red Flame a couple of doors away) No room in fridge for own drinks and they charge if you remove anything

“Convenient for flights” I have stayed at this hotel twice. It is very convenient, shuttle to the airport streamlines early morning flight drudgery, and the train is nearby so you can walk to it and be transported to various locations if you have time to get out and see a little bit of Boston. This hotel stands out as far as airport hotels go. The property is maintained in a professional manner and the staff represent the property well.

“Good except for front desk” Good value for this area. Excellent maid service, clean room with clean carpet. King size bed was well worn with some sagging. Breakfast of toast, donuts, cold ceral (instant oatmeal if you heat water in Microwave); watered down orange juice, (with other juice choices I didn't try) apples, oranges, and small muffins. Coffee medicore. Everything in well equiped room worked. Wireless internet access works, but you are left to discover how to get on with password. Front desk man never smiled and volunteered no information beyond where the room was. He must hate his job. Too bad.

“Did not meet expectations” I have to say that overall, the Hotel Indigo Chelsea is average at best. I booked the hotel with high expectations due to the great reviews on Trip Advisor and a great experience at a Hotel Indigo in Asheville, NC. However, we were sadly disappointed. First of all, the lobby is unattractive the white/cream colored carpets have stains. The front desk area is cluttered and appears messy. For someone just entering the hotel for the first time, this gives an impression that the hotel is dingy and unkept. Upon checkin, I asked the front desk clerk to break a $10 bill so that I could tip the bellman for watching my luggage prior to check-in; however, she was unable to do so. This was very inconventient and unaccomodating -especially for a front desk which should be able to provide such a service to its guests. The rooms are neat and have modern decor, but extremely small and the hallway to the rooms is dark and unwelcoming. Our bathroom had a dark colored mold growing in the grout and was not well maintenanced. (see picture). The location is not convenient to local attractions (14 blocks to Times Square) and hailing a taxi is near impossible at this hotel. If you have dinner plans, I highly suggest booking a private car, or mapping out the nearest subway station (Penn Station is 1/2 block up to 7th and 3 blocks to 31st). Walking back to the hotel after dark is a bit scary and the neighborhood is a bit dodgy. After shopping on the first day we returned to rest prior to dinner (approximately 4 pm) to be startled by a man entering our room. He stated he was doing a "room check" which we found extremely odd since we had just checked into the room that afternoon. When I complained to the front desk they stated "yes we do conduct room checks but not usually this late in the day". I was not happy about this as I am not accustomed to strangers entering my room any time they wish, for no apparent reason. Our TV would not work and a maintainence person was called on two different occasions. Finally, the maintenance man determined that in order to turn the channels, we had to stand within a foot of the tv. Since early a.m. and late nights were the only time we utilized the TV we didn't make much of a fuss. The worst part of the stay was the construction. We were awakened very early each morning by loud jack hammers and drills. This was extremely loud and annoying. There is a restaurant and the breakfast was good but pricy. Overall, this hotel is not a good value as the price is similar to the Marriott and Hilton, but does not hold near the same quality of service and accomodations.

“Nice Room, Bleak Location” Relatively new Renaissance, everything fresh, clean and modern. Room was quiet and comfortable, staff was efficient and friendly. The biggest negative is there is literally nothing in the immediate area within walking distance for restaurants, shops, etc. Need to either take a cab or the Silver Line T which stops a half block from the hotel and runs up to South Station. I was only there one night so it wasn't a huge problem but I certainly wouldn't want to be in this location for a longer stay. As a result of the isolation, I did have dinner in the hotel restaurant, which I found surprisingly good.

“Charming Hotel in central Denver” We enjoyed our stay at the Magnolia Hotel in Denver, and it is in a very good location. The 16th street Mall is one block away and you can take the shuttle to Lodo and the Coors Field area. The rooms are old but charming. The lobby of the hotel is surprisingly small and the front of the hotel seems to be in some kind of alley way, but the staff is very friendly. I agree with everyone else on here who commented that the parking is expensive at $26 dollars per night, and the front of the hotel is set up in such a way that even with the valet you will wait behind anyone who may be stopped in front of the main entrance. It took us 10 minutes to get past a big group of people who were loading up their car. it just seemed odd, especially given the price for parking. I would definitely recommend finding a parking garage nearby and walking across the street. You will probably get in and out faster. Overall we really liked our stay and the hotel is unique. The breakfast in the morning has a lot to offer, and we thought Harry's Bar (on the first floor) was a good place for a drink or two.

“Beautiful, comfortable hotel” This hotel was a welcome oasis after a day of travelling. The lobby/bar area is tasteful, dramatic and very welcoming, it really made me feel like I was entering a beautiful hotel. I was not disappointed with the room either. It was a spacious and well appointed, with a modern clean design, and the view was amazing. I liked that there was a deep window ledge at the window to allow you to sit and enjoy the view. The bed was big, soft and comfy. The bathroom was also big with the toilet and the shower each in their own minirooms off the main bathroom. The wall on the side of the tub was actually doors that could open into the main bedroom, allowing you to lounge in the bed and see the view or the TV, and essentially still be in the main room. Everything in the room is controlled by a touch screen device next to the bed, including the lights, and the drapes, which open and close at the touch of the screen. The location of the hotel was great, literally next door to the SF Museum of Modern Art, and right around the corner from all the great shopping in Union Square. I would definitely stay here again.

“Awesome Little Hotel” Ya Gotta stay here. We absolutely loved it. AND WE ARE VERY PICKY CUSTOMERS. The location is great and the area is safe PLUS iTS between a wonderful French Wine Bar and Another wonderful French Restaurant. The double bed rooms are small, but it's an amazing use of space. We found it kind of cozy. The staff was helpful as well. STAY HERE !!!

“地下鉄の真上!” 地下鉄の真上にあり、博物館にも歩いていける便利なホテルです。地下鉄からの入り口は、少し分かりづらいですが、エレベータで行けます。プールもたくさん子供たちが遊んでいて、泳ぎやすいプールでした。皆さんのおっしゃるとおり、レセプションの人は感じが悪く、時刻表を聞いても分からないと言って、調べようともしてくれません。他のポーターの人、ルーム係りの人達はフレンドリーで感じが良いのですが、、、便利さから言うとすごーくお勧めです。

“Extremely nice hotel” My wife and I stayed here for two nights Nov. 12-14 and just loved it. We stayed in a 26th floor Concierge suite which was immaculate and had a beautiful view of Downtown Dallas. The concierge lounge was closed for the weekend so I don't know what it was like. The restaurant was clean and efficient. The food was very good but somewhat pricey as is the case with all hotels. Wireless internet is free for all gold and platinum members. Downtown Dallas is less than a 5 minute drive and DFW airport is about a 15-20 minute drive with no traffic. While in town we dined at the Dakota Steakhouse located at 600 North Akard Street. I had one of the best bone in filets I have ever had. Definitely go there if you're looking for a great steak.

“Heaven in a building” Yes, it was a little intimidating to pull my rental car into the driveway and see 7 Rolls Royces, but the Elysian is amazing and if I had a Rolls I would want to park it there. But there is nothing pretentious about the hotel staff. They are incredibly friendly and attentive and truly seem to like working there. My local friend who came up to meet me in my room suggested we find out where the staff got their happy pills so we could indulge. They engage you in friendly conversation when you're in the lobby and it feels very genuine. There is attention to detail in everything they do - - from the turn-down service to check in and check out. The rooms are decorated the way I would like to decorate my parlor, if I had one - gray walls, a fireplace and a lovely seating area. The bed is incredibly comfortable. Big white fluffy towels and a huge bathroom complete my vision of the perfect hotel. Unfortunately I was only there for a night and didn't have time to check out the restaurants but it's on my list for my next trip.

“Great location” This place is very convenient , located in the heart of all the attractions. It is within a walking distance to time square so it is very easy to get sound especially to the night shows. It is well decorated. The room service is average. This is a kind of place if you stay and want to travel around during the day. I didn't use any facilities inside the hotel though I was there for 5 days. There're lots to see in new York!

“Beware - Construction!” The hotel lets you know when you ARRIVE of the construction they have going on (would have been nice to know this BEFORE booking). It actually wasn't bad HOWEVER, there is a planned hotel going up fairly soon right outside the NON-Empire State Building side so call the hotel and ask. There's good and bad about the hotel. On the bright side, the service was great, everyone (surprisingly) friendly and when I had problems with the phone and bathtub, Omar was there within two minutes and, no kidding, fixed both in under 5 minutes. Convenient to FIT and an easy walk to Greenwich Village or Times Square and the 28th St IRT a block away. I had no problems with the elevators (we were on the 25th floor). Small but nice fitness center. The cookies are a nice touch. On the down side, this is NOT a place for families. Okay, so it was fashion week AND The U.S. Open so nice room prices were jacked up. We pre-paid 239 a night for the 2 twin bed room but it was NOT, I repeat NOT good for 2 adults and two kids (2 and 5). No room to move, or put your bags and we didn't have a problem overtipping the chambermaid for the cyclone that hit that room every morning (the kids). No fridge was a bummer. My wife wants me to let you know the bathroom had a "weird smell" I wouldn't exactly call this a 4 Star hotel as Orbitz, TripAdvisor and others seem to think it is. At best, it's a 3.5

“a clear reminder of why I never stay at ramada” Stayed here only because a business associate I was meeting was already booked here. The one bright spot of my stay was the very friendly & helpful Russian man who ran the gift shop. Now for the rest. Hotel internet down, so the utterly uninterested front desk staff sent me across the street to an "internet cafe": a dank hovel with squalid-looking men huddled over internet terminals available for rent by the hour. This is what the hotel staff considered an appropriate place for one of their guests? Would they have advised me to go there had I been a woman traveling alone? Probably so. In the morning, the breakfast buffet was above-average, but no to-go cups were available for coffee. Instead, there was a stack of cheap chinese ceramic mugs bearing the hotel's name - and a professionally-printed, posted sign warning guests not to remove the mugs from the breakfast area. Apparently, there was such a problem with the $300/night guests "stealing" their precious 50-cent mugs (because no to-go cups were available) that they had to erect a sign. If only there were a solution to this problem! Then the janitor set about to mop the entire tile floor along the only path leading into or out of the breakfast area - during breakfast! Apparently, none of the other twenty hours of the day was quite right for this job. I have seldom been confronted with such inertial stupidity during a hotel stay as during my 14 hours at this ramada (capitalization intentionally omitted). It has been over 15 years since my last ramada stay; hopefully it will be another 15 before my next.

“Wonderful room” The room was wonderful! The king bed was so comfortable that I wish I could have stayed all theday in the room. - The shower was separated from the bathtub and there was complimentary bath salt with a good smell. The towels were so soft... - The TV had lots of channels. - The wifi connection was not the fastest in the world but it was ok. - They offered complimentary bottled water. - The hotel had a lot of rooms but it seemed empty because it was so quiet and there was no noise at all. There were no guests in line to check in (in a week day). - I had breakfast at the Assembly line buffet (located in the dining area, same floor as the lobby). I really recommend it. Unfortunately it's open for breakfast only during the weekends. - Self parking and valet are free and easy to get to (different from those huge parkings in Las Vegas)

“better than average for DC” I stayed here for business and found the hotel to be adequate and average in service and style. The nice part is having a pool and hottub in the hotel, a rarity for DC hotels. The room was standard and the bed quite comfortable. Service was good, but room service was poor. They estimated a 45 minute wait to deliver a salad. I went to the bar and had the same salad in less than 15 minutes. The most annoying aspect of the hotel design was the entrance which is geared 99% for automoible drop-offs and pick-ups. If you are walking out of the hotel you need to wind your way around the many SUVs and taxis driving in and out. Overall, nice location and nice accomodations.

“Very nice business hotel” I am a loyal Hyatt fan, so that preidisposes me to their properties. It has been several years since I have stayed at the flagship because I have chosen the new Andaz properties on 5th Ave and Wall Street. I can't say that I like the remodeled look of the hotel all that much, especially the lobby area which seemed a bit cold to me. I do like the room remodel however. I especially like the high tech lighting system which was convenient and easy to use. The Grand Club was nice and well designed, but the lavish food was significantly cut back from a few years ago. It was still as nice as any Hyatt except for the hotel in Singapore which is very special. So my advice is to try for the Andaz which is very special. But you won't be disappointed here either and the location is very nice.

“top notch service, less then top notch rooms” We booked an executive suite for the weekend Friday- Sunday. I could tell the hotel was dated by the entry. The lighting is very 1980's & early 90's. The check in staff was very friendly and helpful. Our rooom was less then impressive. They had old CRT TV's, not LCD's as advertised. They alaso advertisted DVD players in the executive suite, there wasn't one. The bathroom was small. The furniture was old and worn. But the plave was very clean. Another good point was the car service that will take you to your downtown destinations and pick up back up. I'd love to go back, if they updated the rooms. We are big on plush rooms. For those that don't care about that, then this hotel and room would be great. If you book it, make sure they don't give you room 1616.

“Practically perfect” The Distrikt Hotel blew my expectations out our 32nd floor window (which actually opened to let fresh air in). Our Grandview King room felt palatial by New York City hotel standards, but was actually only 250 sq ft. The amazing view of the Hudson River, Hell’s Kitchen & Times Square made me want to spend as much time as possible in the room. The linens were crisp & soft, the dresser & wardrobe space ample, & the little touches like the cupcakes they left us along with a “Happy Anniversary” note made the stay feel special. It’s definitely worth it to pay a little extra for a “Grandview” room – especially if you’re not a regular NYC visitor. Even on our third day there, I still could not get over how spectacular the view was. The other thing that sets the Distrikt Hotel apart is the customer service. After a bit of a glitch & a rocky start at check-in, our concerns were immediately addressed by the front desk manager & more than made up for. The majority of the staff was welcoming & even remembered little details like the fact that we had our anniversary dinner at Le Bernardin (& allowing us to gush about it the next day). I was nervous about the fact that the hotel was located across from the Port Authority Bus Terminal, but never felt unsafe, even at 1am. The breakfast in bistro downstairs was a bit limited & a bit pricey. It probably fits the needs for the European travelers who seemed to fill the hotel, but if you’re looking for a big, American-style breakfast, you’re better off to hit one of NYC’s many diners. You won’t be able to get a cab to save your life. This isn’t the hotel’s fault; it’s just how the City is. So be prepared to walk, or take the subway – it’s very conveniently located to the hotel just down W. 40th.

“All Around Pleasant” I stayed at The Ashton Hotel for business. It was interesting and quirky, and the building is historic with a cool story. Each room is unique. Mine had a claw tub between the bathroom and the bedroom. I didn't have a view, since there was a building almost right next to my window. But the bed was very comfortable, the room was quiet, and there was a surprise cookie by my bedside after a long day. The rooms have real keys...very nostalgic! I would recommend it for a nice romantic weekend stay.

“Perfect Place ..great Holidays” J 'ai passé un excellent séjour ; personnel de la reception extremement souriant ; toujours à votre écoute ; très sympathique ;(Merci Alban!) ; chambre vaste ; très agreable tout confort ; avec un petit coin pour les repas , un petit coin salon et un autre pour le dressing et coiffeuse . On a l'impression d'être dans un veritable appartement . Un hotel pour des artistes .. Très propre aussi , internet haut debit compris ainsi que petit Dej , tv ecran plat . Le point culminant est bien sur l'emplacement privilégié juste derriere le centre commercial dans une petite avenue calme et très mignonne..simple passage d' un petit corridor avant de rejoindre l'ambiance joyeuse du Highland Center (shopping, restaurants, Lounge, et de toutes les attractions d'Hollywood) . Egalement sauna et petite salle de fitness ainsi qu'un ordinateur à disposition . Tout est parfait .. Je vous le recommande .. hotel toujours complet ..donc reservation à l'avance est recommandée ;)

“Nice hotel, great location” Nice Hilton... it has everything you could possibly want in a NYC hotel. Location, nice rooms, helpful concierge for newbies, and did I mention location? It's only a few blocks from Central Park and Times Square, but not in the super-noisy-hustle-bustle section of the area.

“A nice motel near SDSU” I stayed in this hotel in March 2009 as well as July 2009. My daughter will be attending SDSU as a freshman this fall so we chose this motel for it's proximity to the campus. Both stays were pleasant and the staff was very cordial. It's not a luxury property by any stretch, but a very CLEAN, comfortable option. As an aside, they are doing some remodel work and sprucing up the property. Rooms that we stayed in had new carpet, upgraded bathrooms and 4 or 5 huge comfy pillows on the bed. A good place to stay if you don't mind being at least a 15 to 20 minute drive (in no traffic) from the S.D. metro area.

“Grand stay at the Grand Hyatt” I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for five nights in late June 2005. After reading the reviews on here I was a little worried about my stay, but my fears were alleviated quickly. I was very satisfied with my entire stay at the Hyatt. First off, the location is second to none. You are adjacent to the Grand Central Terminal. So what, you say? Well, the 4, 5, 6, 7, and S subway lines are about a 5 minute walk from the hotel lobby through completely indoor corridors, bypassing a couple of coffee shops, bakeries, and newstands on the way for added convenience. Very nice to have, especially in the morning, and especially when its raining outside. From the hotel lobby, you can be in Times Square in 10 minutes, and in lower Manhattan in about 20 minutes. If you'd rather take a cab, there was always an employee ready to hail a cab for you right in front. I never waited more than 5 minutes for one. Another positive - the rooms had been recently renovated as the Hyatt website mentions. My room had a king size bed, large TV, trendy furnishings, and plenty of space considering it was a Manhattan hotel room. Unlike other reviewers have mentioned, housekeeping did a great job on my room - left it in great shape every afternoon when I returned from sight-seeing. Even though I booked the room through Priceline, I felt like I was treated like a Hyatt club member through my entire stay, right down to getting a copy of the New York Times every morning. The only negative I can think of is the lobby was always mobbed with people. This is a HUGE hotel and there were lots of conventions going on the weekend I was staying. However, on my floor (17th), it was very quiet and I never encountered a noise problem from the street, from the lobby, or from other patrons. Another negative is the hotel charges for internet use: 50 cents a minute. I guess I didn't get the most "one-on-one" service I've ever gotten in a hotel but in all honesty I never needed it because my stay was so great. This hotel deserves to be ranked MUCH higher than the #165 rating it has commanded on Tripadvisor. Top 100 for sure - possibly even the Top 50 when you consider some of the other hotels that are ranked there. Granted, I wouldn't pay Hyatt's normal room rate of $400/night to stay here. But $210/night rate through Priceline was a very reasonable for a stay in this type of hotel in NYC in peak season. I've read that off-season bids on Priceline for 4-star hotel can get you at the Grand Hyatt for even less than that. I would stay here again in a heartbeat for the same rate.

“Would definitely stay here again, especially at the price.” Like a number of people, we reserved the Palmer House via Priceline. I cannot believe a place this nice can be had in a town the size of Chicago for that price. The room was clean and comfortable and reasonably large, which is a basic need of all hotels, and it fulfilled them wonderfully. The location close to the park is excellent, and the red line subway to Wrigley is right out your door. It could be a little closer to the Magnificent Mile area, but that would be nit-picking. Great for a quick weekend in Chicago.

“Fantastic staff and nice place to stay” Greeted and helped by the fantastic staff as soon as I arrived for my 1st trip to NYC. Gave me directions and stored my luggage. Close to everything,. Just go there! Small room but i went to see NYC not the 4 walls. The staff got me to Yankee stadium with a direct subway to Yankee stadium(Thank you to trip advisor forums for telling me to stay in Manhatten)

“Great Hotel, Great Location” I have stayed at dozens of hotels in the city in almost every area of Manhattan. This one makes the top 5 list for me. The hotel is conveniently located in Times Square - great for business or tourist travel. I had a room on the executive floor with free access to the club lounge for breakfast and reception. I was treated great from the time I walked in until checkout. The rooms are very nice with great beds and a flat screen television. The health club is very nice, but it is close enough to the park to do your exercise there (highly recommended). I will choose this hotel again if the price is right.

“Loved it, but Noisy” I recently stayed at The Nolitan on a whim when I found a super low rate of $143.20 on their website for a Neighborhood Room. I had been wanting to stay here since they opened, so I thought I'd take advantage of the great rate & glad I did- I really loved my room! Ben checked me in & he was a great first impression- he was relaxed, cool, super friendly & upgraded me to a Cityscape room on the top floor of the hotel, which was the 9th floor- thanks Ben! I was in room 901- my room was quite small, with cool hardwood floors, a concrete ceiling, a slim wooden desk with an awesome chair, Rose scented Red Flower Bath products that were lovely, super comfy bed with soft linens & great pillows, amazing shower, & an awesome view of the Williamsburg bridge! I loved the feel of the room & was very comfortable! When I called down I was able to extend until 2pm (check out is at 1pm, which is very nice to begin with!) & the hotel provided a delectable little chocolate treat on my bed at turndown service- really nice touch, including the weather card for the next day. However, there are a few things that you should keep in my mind when staying at The Nolitan- even though I was on the highest floor in the building, my room was noisy; not terribly loud, but I could hear traffic & people outside if my window was cracked open for fresh air- I live in the city, so this doesn't really bother me, just something to keep in mind- I can only imagine the lower floors are incredibly noisy. For a brand new building, the Elevators are noisy, I could hear a cell phone conversation two rooms away as I was sitting on my bed, the a/c & heating unit was freakishly loud, so I just turned it OFF completely, as it was a cool night in NYC & the windows & building have really bad soundproofing. Housekeeping was very loud around 9am outside of my room. None of this ruined my stay, but the hotel has really poor insulation to block the noise, which is really unfortunate for a new building. Also, the restaurant is closed, so the hotel is offering a light Continental breakfast in the lobby- the selection when I arrived around 9:45a was really low- a few pastries, yogurt, & a few pieces of whole fruit with half filled carafes of juice. The Danish I had was quite good! The hotel has no room service right now, but providing menus from local neighborhood restaurants for delivery service. The mini bar was decent, with all items reasonably priced. Overall, I'm glad I stayed at The Nolitan- I really adored my room & loved the hardwood floors, the incredible bed & the lovely rain shower! It was a room that I really didn't want to leave, as I love clean, modern lines that were used in the hotel. The only negative towards the hotel in my opinion was the lack of soundproofing- otherwise, a cool, cute hotel in an amazing part of NYC!

“not bad for Austin” Austin is a hard place to book a hotel. The location of the W would have been perfect for us, but not the price. We like boutique hotels, but were unsure of the Hotel San Jose recommended to us by friends, as it had mixed reviews here - the location would have been MUCH better and it did look like a nice place when we walked by. The Casulo is a nice hotel, but in a bad location - you need a car to stay here and it is right off the freeway, which was CLOSED when we stayed here (major pain getting to and from the hotel ALL weekend. Not the hotel's fault, but be ware they are doing highway work). Our view sucked - we were on the Southern side; yay, Sun finally!!!! not so fast...There is an apartment complex next door. We wanted to open our windows, but if you do there is no privacy curtain, only the heavy black out curtain - so it is all or nothing which is a drag. We hung up a towel on the window so we could see the sun and have privacy, really classy ~ why can't the hotel fix this? This hotel is weird. It kind of has a hip vibe, and rejects from the San Jose like us seem to stay here, but there really is nothing hip about it. It is not a boutique hotel, it is more of an upscale cheaper hotel ~ way too expensive for what it really is and it can be a bit deceiving on the internet. The neighborhood isn't great. It seems to be family run which is nice. Breakfast included tator tots - huh? People came down to breakfast in their pajamas! I don't think I have ever stayed anywhere where that is the norm... There is a pool, but it is small if you think you are going to sit out by it and hang out, I doubt you will feel that way when you get there. Despite the younger folks carting drinks up to their rooms, there were no raucous noisy parties when we stayed here - we slept well without ear plugs. I did hear someone in the room next to us with their tv on Sunday night when we were here. Overall our stay was nice, the room was clean, I slept well, but we didn't really like it. But it is Austin and you don't have much of a choice if this is what you are comfortable paying. Stay on the North side, at least you can leave your windows open.

“Great location is a trade-off” Overview: My wife and I visit Washington. on a somewhat regular basis since my daughter is attending college in DC. As such, we’ve had the opportunity to stay at a number of hotels in and around the city. Our basis for deciding which hotel that we will stay in (usually a Friday and Saturday night) is availability and, of course, price. This is the second time that we’ve stayed at this particular Residence Inn. Other hotels we’ve stayed in recently include the Marriott Wardman Park, the Omni Shoreham, the Residence Inn (Bethesda), and the Embassy Suites (Freedom Heights). We stayed at the Residence Inn Dupont Circle in November 2006 and again in mid-March 2007. Three reasons why you’d want to stay here: 1) The suite was roomy, with a nicely equipped kitchenette – good-sized fridge, microwave, dishwasher, coffeemaker, etc. The adjoining bedroom area was adequate in size (the bed was quite comfortable) but the bath was somewhat smallish. The room was nicely decorated in red and tan tones with stylish furniture. There is in-room high speed internet that was easy to connect and to utilize. 2) There is a daily breakfast buffet included in the price, with the usual menu items: eggs, waffles, sausage, donuts, muffins, cereal, fruit, etc. The dining room was very a little small, however. 3) Location: this is a plus AND a minus. The hotel is on P Street in the busy and diverse Dupont Circle area of the city. (We love this area of DC – it is vibrant and alive with activity.)Also, the hotel is very close the Metro (the red line), which goes directly to Union Station, Smithsonian, the Mall, etc., The Metro is about two blocks up the street so you can easily get into the main part of the city in minutes. Also, a wide variety of interesting restaurants are nearby (in fact, one was directly beneath our room – it played loud music until midnight.) The eateries range from Italian to Mexican to Greek to you-name-it: very many choices and many price ranges. Three reasons why you wouldn’t: 1) Location: this is a plus AND a minus. As I said, the hotel is on P Street in the lively Dupont Circle area of the city. On our first visit, we had a room on the ninth floor, so the noise and city-sounds didn’t seem too much of a problem. On the most recent visit, our room was on the second floor. We tried to get it changed to a higher floor, but unfortunately couldn’t. There is a restaurant (with singing wait-staff) on the first floor – do NOT stay on the first four floors of this hotel if you what to get to sleep before 2 a.m. We had to listen to numerous loud conversations held in the restaurant’s outside patio as if the people were in our room. I was not happy. 2) Parking: The parking is expensive, but this is true of any DC hotel. And, the parking garage is really small (does not accommodate all the hotel’s guest cars, as I found out) and it is really narrow and tight. I had to squeeze my minivan in between two cars and then crawl out through the rear door. At least my vehicle was in a space – other cars were parked in the driving lanes. Not good. 3) Noise: Did I mention that the area has noise issues (sirens, honking car horns, etc.)? Stay on the top floors if you want a little peace and quiet. Conclusion: All in all, we recommend the Residence Inn Dupont Circle but only if you can handle the noise and parking issues. Otherwise, there other very good hotel options in the city.

“Great Location - Ok for a short trip” Hotel as a whole was good. Hotel rooms a little small - but was all we needed for a short break. Great location, about 5 mins walking distance from Times Square. Staff were lovely and very helpful. Maintenance men were quick on the scene when we had an overflowing toilet. Very quiet up in hotel room - so had a good nights sleep.

“Not the best location for fun!” Stayed at the Ritz Carlton for 4 nights while attending a conference. My room was on the 4th floor and the room was very spacious and well appointed with a huge bathroom and, great bathroom ammenities! The Ritz provided turndown service with chocolates and tons of free bottled water! Service was excellent - the staff was always smiling and always willing to help out and were not pretentious at all! As a single woman traveling - I felt very safe too! The downside? You had to pay to use the gym, for one night the fire drill would not stop (the building is a tad old) and the location was pretty sterile! Tip: Park your car yourself on Sunday's ONLY in the garage and you won't be charged the daily rate!

“Nice Hotel” Stayed during SXSW Festival. Pros: * Located across from convention center and within walking distance to all parts of SXSW. * Comfortable beds and pillows. * Working A/C (although I had a hard time finding how to turn it off - light switch behind the drapes did the trick) * Good shower * Full restaurant and Starbucks on site * Parking garage underground * Computer with internet in lounge area * Friendly valet guys Cons: * Charge for parking * Unable to park trailer due to underground lot, but we knew this beforehand (it is stated on their website); We found a lot near the capitol and he gave us a discounted rate (charged for only two spaces, although we took up more) and he allowed us to leave it overnight, although the lot was only open until 3 AM. * Inflated rates during SXSW

“great escape” While I live in San Francisco, I decided to spend the weekend at the hotel as an escape. It was a great experience-a quite luxurious oasis--with great service and a modern but not austere design. Would highly recommend for a stress reducing experience.

“Not in best neighborhood but hotel itself is okay” Got this hotel on priceline in Dec 2008 for $59 a nite plus tax. This was significantly cheaper then the hotels located in the Riverwalk area. This hotel was about a 10 minute walk from those. Let me be honest, the neighborhood isnt the greatest. I dont scare easily but my friend was at least somewhat concerned. There is a weird looking abandon building across the way. Wendy's McDonalds is within walk distance but you have to go down a dark street. I wouldnt advice women and children to be out alone. In fact, during out first nite someone's van in the parking lot was broken into and a TV was stolen. The hotel itself was nice. They keep the pool clean and open even though it was too chilly to dip in. They have a computer you can use in the lobby, a fitness room was a treadmill and bike and a free breakfast that is average. The room was clean and i generally wasnt fearful of the area but i kept my eye out. Like i said its about a 10 -15 minute walk to anywhere you want to be on the Riverwalk and for the saving of $$ it was worth it. G Rizzle

“Nice Location-Odd Freeway Acess” This location is kind of hidden from the main highway in a business/residential area. They are doing construction on the highway, my GPS had us go in a circle to get to the location. The staff here is super friendly and helpful. The rooms have recently been remolded, and are comfortable. There is a refrigerator in the room which is nice, along with a mini coffee maker. They have Starbucks coffee in the lobby which is nice, they also have a bistro with limited food items. The internet is FREE as well. On the Negative side the A/C-Heater in the room is a little loud (I am a heavy sleeper) but I can see where it would be distracting if you were not, also the television placement makes it a little difficult to view while in bed. I would return to this location again

“A hotel for shoppers.....” The location of this hotel can't be beat if you want to spend your time shopping in NYC. Macy's is a block away and there is tons of other shopping near and in Times Square (about 7 blocks away). It looks like this is a newer hotel and actually shares a wall with the Hampton Inn next door. Staff was pleasant at check-in and I was given my welcome amenity as an HHonors member (I think the asst. manager checked me in). However, I never received a copy of the USA Today newspaper outside my door while almost everyone else on my floor did. (???) A small item I know but it makes me wonder what benefits do you really get as a hotel club member (I never received the high floor, foam pillows request that I had put in so I didn't get to experience the view of the Empire State Building that others have talked about). Rooms are NY sized-----tiny, but clean, new and comfortable. There is a decent sized refrigerator and microwave in the room as well as an in-room safe. Hallways are tiny and there are only about 7 or 8 rooms on a floor so if you ask for a room away from the elevator, that's nearly impossible (only the bigger sized corner rooms might qualify but you may have to pay more). I didn't dine at the restaurant downstairs but it looked decent (there are tons of places around the corner, if it's too busy). Like others have said the ESB is almost right next door and so is Koreatown (which is basically the next couple of streets down) if you want something different. The Subway is basically right outside the hotel so it's convenient if you don't have a car (which I never do). All in all, a good choice for a clean comfortable hotel.

“Deserve top ratings!” Spent 3 nights in May 2012 in an Executive Suite. We were there to relax and enjoy some of the city's delights. Overall, have to say that this hotel deserves top ratings. There is very little that can be described as deficient. The public areas of this property is fantastic - grand double story lobby area, with discreet front desk and almost private-like elevator entrance to the rooms. The furnishings in the lobby area and general public areas are of good quality and maintained well (most of the furnishings is now quite a few years old), while the cleanliness is consistent and held to a very high standard. Our suite was fantastic - not the biggest rooms in the suite but definitely among the most well thought out and designed. Living room, bathroom and bedroom all had large windows with delicious views. The space almost immediately makes you feel at home. Comfortable yet elegant! The bathroom was beautiful and stunning - lots of room and lots of amenities. Just ask if you need anything else (we did - needed extra shoe horn and a pair of scissors) and they'd get it for you. no questions asked and no changes on our bill. The bed is great - feels luxurious and easy to fall asleep in. But the best part of this hotel is the spa, gym and pool - well thought out and well maintained. Not as good as the Peninsula Bangkok spa and gym, but definitely great. And the staff - professional, courteous, friendly, willing to help and always greet you, regardless of where you are. This high standard of customer service and care makes this property ideal. Finally, this property is much better maintained, much better organized, and much better facilities than the sister property in NYC. The only complaint (a small one) is that you have to take one set of elevators to get to the lobby and then walk quite a distance to get the the next set of elevators to get to your room.

“Great Place to Stay for a While” My wife and I stayed for a week at the Canyon Villas and were sad to leave. Everything about the place made it a great place to stay for an extended period of time. The facilities were top notch (pool, fitness center) there were plenty of scheduled activities for guests, the staff was very friendly and accommodating. You do get full use of the facilities at the adjacent J.W. Marriott, but we never felt the need to go there, all our needs were met at the Canyon Villas. It is located in northern Phoenix, about 30 minutes drive from the airport, you definitely need a car if you want to go explore the Phoenix area. There is a great shopping/entertainment center right across the street with multiple restaurants, a movie theater with IMAX and plenty of stores including an Albertsons. We had a one bedroom King suite overlooking the main pool. Very roomy with a complete kitchen so we were able to save some money by eating in a couple of nights and having breakfast every day. There was a nice patio where we would have coffee in the morning and soak up the sun. The bathroom was nice with a big walk-in shower and a separate soaker tub. Bedroom had a comfortable king sized bed and a flat screen TV and DVD player (same in the living room), one plus is that they also had HD channels available... Overall we would strongly recommend this place and we liked it so much that we are thinking of purchasing a membership in the Marriott Vacation Club.

“Still love the Edison Hotel!” Once again, we stayed at the Hotel Edison for our Memorial Day visit to New York. As always, we love this hotel. While the rooms are not fancy, the location is fantastic and the rate is outstanding, very reasonable by New York standards. While some of these reviews talked about rude staff, we have always found them helpful, and we stay here two to three times a year. And while people talk about rooms, seriously, if you're in New York, how much time are you going to spend in our hotel room? Between theater, restaurants, walking the city and the park, and visiting with friends, we see it to sleep. Give me a clean room in a good location, and I'm happy. Only complaint, which others have noted, is the lack of electric outlets. It's an old building. Still our New York choice!

“Above Avg. as LAX Airports Go” Having stayed at a number of LAX-area hotels over the years (Westin, Renaissance, Marriott, Courtyard, Residence Inn, Hilton, etc.), I have to say that I was positively impressed by this place. The suite was spacious and the self-parking was very convenient (there's an additional charge, but you can go in and out). It's very clean and looks pretty new, whether it is or not. They also do the Manager's cocktail hour with chips, beer, and wine every afternoon if you're into that. And there's a breakfast, too, which I couldn't take advantage of due to a 7 a.m. flight (it didn't open 'til 6 a.m. if I remember correctly).

“落ち着いた部屋” NYにひとりで行く時は、ここが一番良いと思います。 女性の一人旅でも、快適に過ごせるし、なんといってもコリアタウンのすぐ近くなので食事に困ることはありません。 買い物もしやすいですし、Macy's がすぐ近くにあるので、何か買い忘れても朝でも行けるし、デリも近くにあるので、食事にも困らないです。 お部屋はせまいと言えば狭いけど、清潔ですし、シャワーもしっかりと出ます。 businesscenterも使えるのでそれも良いですね。トータルに考えて満足できるホテルです。 ビジネスや時間のない人には本当にお薦めのホテル。 ゴージャスな雰囲気を求める人にはちょっと違うかもしれませんが...私は一押しです。

“Questionable service and no blackout curtains make for a bad stay” We stayed two nights. We got a great deal on a bidding site and i've been to the hotel's bar many times, so I was looking forward to the stay. The hotel is ideally located. Right on Dupont Circle and in the middle of everything in DC. Location aside, the hotel suffers from a number of major design flaws, which would warrant me to tell everyone to stay elsewhere. First, the bathroom has no door. This is a problem if you are staying with someone else and they need to use the bathroom at night. This requires all of the bathroom lights to be turned on, which lights up the room. This is bad. Secondly, the hotel breaks the cardinal rule of "Thou shall be able to sleep late." The hotel has no blackout curtains. And it has a frosted glass window in the shower. Thus, when the sun rises, so do you. This is a terrible terrible flaw. The service also left some to be desired. Our room was not cleaned the one night and we requested a cleaning which was never completed. I've stayed at dozens of hotels in DC and with lots of competition at this price range, I would recommend looking elsewhere. On a positive note, the towels are large and the toiletries are high quality.

“Excellent hotel” I stayed here for business and was very happy with the quality of the hotel. Check in was easy and the staff very welcoming. There is a Starbucks in the lobby of the hotel which was great to pick up a coffee for the walk to the office in the morning. The rooms aren't large but the furnishings very modern and comfortable. I was supposed to stay 2 nights but my meetings were cancelled and therefore only stayed 1. There was no problem at all checking out early, and I was not charged a cancellation fee or the second night's rate, despite giving the hotel less than 24 hours notice, as their policy states. I was very impressed that the hotel did not try to 'double dip'.

“Outstanding Service” I recently stayed at the Crowne Plaza Metro for a business conference and my stay was wonderful! The hotel rooms, while not very large, are very modern, clean, and comfy. What really made my stay great though was the service. The front desk was friendly and helpful, room service was fast and friendly, and the valet was great. - when I was ready to retrieve my car, the valet had my car to me in literally 2 minutes. I would certainly stay here again. The room was nice but nothing unique, however the price was well worth the outstanding service you receive!

“Great Hotel, Great Location” All right, I am a bit prejudiced here. First time I have been here for a while, but it has always been one of my favorite hotels and certainly my preferred hotel and location in New York. Intimate and cosy it is not - this is a big international hotel set up to deal with the masses and the hustle and bustle of Times Square is either to your liking or not. I have always liked the atrium which goes up 30 floors or so from reception. The lifts only take a few seconds for the trip and the glass bubble ones are better than most fairground rides but not, I suspect, if you suffer from vertigo. When I used to come you could wait half an hour for a lift, but they seem to have sorted that out with a new computerised routing system.
