The attached Bob's restaurant is also meant to be decent, as are the giant to-order breakfasts. The retro charm of the detail and grand lobby also carries plenty of appeal. I'd happily stay again, but it's just a "normal" hotel well located for business, not an must-go-to social hub.

“Fairly decent” Stayed here for four nights on business - overall pretty decent but some of the similar problems noted, namely: - room keys do not always work in lifts or rooms - can be a bit temperamental (the red ones work better than the blue ones in my experience) - a mysterious "munchie bar" appeared on my bill but was immediately removed when challenged - rooms aren't the biggest (but not really an issue for business travellers) However, the hotel has many positives, namely: - comfortable beds - quiet by NY standards (my room overlooked Lex and traffic noise wasn't a problem) - good toileteries - very courteous staff (none of the rudeness noted by others observed) - no busloads of schoolkids or tourists - just well-to-do singles and couples on the whole - close to subway - easy to get taxis - doormen actively help you - they also managed to find me one that actually wanted to go to EWR just before shift change - a rarity in NY - decent (corporate) rate (for NY) - OK fitness room - won't win awards but wasn't overcrowded - fairly hip vibe (if that's what you like) - free, easy to set up wifi (in my tariff, but i understand some tariffs make you pay for this) - iPod dock in room - DVD in rom - decent flat screen LCD tv I recommend the Europa deli (east 53rd) for breakfast - a fraction of the hotel cost. Would come back.

“Great El Paso hotel” Great hotel if in town for business; great lounge, excellent menu, outstanding service all around from entire staff. Super workout facilities. My first choice for accomandations when in El Paso for business. Clean, recently remodeled -- an overall great hotel for the professional travel. Quiet, distinctive, no kids running around lobby n bar!

“Trendy hotel with well-designed small rooms in a great Columbus Circle location” Like most travelers, I scour the web and the guidebooks for great advice when it comes to my hotel stay. This is expecially crucial if I have booked a room on Priceline (as in this case). I want to correctly set my expectations prior to arrival. For instance, I really had to get myself in the SMALL ROOM mindset before checking in at The Hudson. Arrival: The hotel doesn't have a sign. Be sure to look at the pics on the website so you know where you're going if you are coming in via subway train. There was a small line at check-in but the front desk staff did a great job keeping everyone moving. There was one very important woman (a trendy I-think-I'm-20-but-I-am-really-45) who felt compelled to jump to the front "Just to ask a question" which of course was her attempt to jump the line. No go! Yay front desk. I made a joke and they took pity on us and got us into a higher level room facing the atrium. :-) Score! The room: Ok. We know. It's small. It's not the end of the world. Unpack your stuff. Be organized and you have plenty of room. Don't throw you stuff all over the room. Now you'll need to sit on the toilet sideways and take turns in the bathroom but....the good parts? Incredible water pressure and a roomy shower plus a VERY comfortable bed. You didn't come to New York to hang out in your hotel room did you? Well then, the shower and the bed are top notch. Done. My husband and I slept like logs in a Queen size which is usually a challenge. I think its really all about the pillows. Noise: Try to get a room above the 6th floor. There will be street noise. It's NY. Buy some freaking Tylenol PM if it's that big of deal. The bigger issue is the nightclub. It's loud. Very loud and very popular. Therefore if you are below Floor 6, you will probably hear it. Join the fun or get something to knock yourself out. Location: As they say in real estate....This is a superb location. The subway is very close and can get you where you need to go quickly. We walked down Columbus Ave after visiting the Natural History Museum and really enjoyed it. Great shops, bars and restaurants al the way down. Lots of dogs and locals give it a nice neighborhood feel. There's a great 24 hour diner and pizza place right on the corner of 58th and 9th. Both are open late. We enjoyed our stay very much. Appreciated the thought and design work that went into the place. Staff was very friendly except for one woman carrying a clipboard in the AM who looked at me like a deer in the headlights when I asked her a question about check out.. Overall a good bet. An even better one if you can score it on Priceline.

“Nice Place, Nice Location” This was my third visit in the last couple of years to Crowne Plaza Market Center. It has most definitely improved over the years. I found the room to be excellent and also found that the employees have been retrained and are really great. They all are helpful and want to make your stay great. The ultimate test probably is I ordered room service at 10:50 P.M. when they close at 11:00 P.M. and it was no problem and they were happy to take care of me. The parking is free and well lighted and the property is located on the Stemmons Freeway making it easy to get downtown, to Market Center, Love Field,or the American Airlines Arena. I would definitely stay here again. They do have a nice bar and small restaurant, indoor pool, and the best fitness equipment around.
“Great location for the capitol” This is a great location to visit the capitol and the mall. Otherwise, it is a relatively normal Hyatt, nothing special.

“Lots for the price!” Wonderful place for me to stay alone. Loved the size and location. Front desk staff and breakfast room staff very helpful and accommodating. I would call this "high end no-frills" and just right for this trip. Felt very safe and liked proximity to theatres, restaurants, public transportation. Rooms small, very clean and HOT! Tiny but accessible business center. Only cardio in fitness room.

“Bargain in Midtown” If anyone complains about the size of the rooms at this hotel, make sure you ask them if they've ever stayed in NYC before. It's very rare to find hotels with rooms as large as these in Manhattan, let alone rooms at DoubleTree prices. Everything was clean and comfortable and the front desk was very accomodating any time we needed something. The location is excellent, very close to subways, taxi's, and Grand Central Station. I would not hesitate to stay here again. ===== ===== ===== RATING SCALE: My ratings are generally based on value vs money. Thus, sometimes a simple hotel will receive a 4 or 5, while a fancy hotel can rank a 1 or 2 if I don't feel it was worth the cost. Also, a hotel can do everything right and still only rank as a 4, unless there's something really exceptional about it. 5 = Hotel gets everything right, and goes above and beyond. 4 = Hotel gets everything right. 3 = Hotel is acceptable value for money spent. 2 = Hotel isn't worth the money spent. 1 = Hotel should pay ME to stay there.

“Barely Recommend--refuse rooms with shared inner door!” Older hotel in great downtown location. Rooms are updated including the bathrooms and shower area. Beds, bedding, towels are all great. Room had flat screen TV and a window you could open. Hotel staff were very helpful and friendly. Lobby and lobby bar are partially updated and as a result not the newest but not really old. Had salmon salad in the bar one evening for dinner and it was better than expected. Also a convenient location for printing boarding passes in the lobby. So with all this why an Average rating: The hotel is just a little dark and dated and common areas seem dingy. The conference hall for my meeting had really poor lighting and was also--well just dingy. Fitnees area has windows and was just okay. I was unfortunate enough to be stuck in an room with a common adjoining door with another room. I could hear every word spoken in the adjacent room. So MAKE SURE you do not get a room with a shared inner door. Unless you enjoy having someone else dictate when you are going to sleep. This happened late in my third night at hotel--too late to want to make a change as I had a 4:30am alarm.

“Sleek for Cheap” This is a great hotel for business travelers. It's not full-service, but it's a definite step up from the Inn & Suites-type places. Decor is very modern & sleek. Highlights/Pros: Great outdoor sitting area with firepit & separate glass fireplace between outdoor & lobby bar, lobby bar attracts a good group of professionals most evenings, you can get breakfast delivered or pick it up in the lobby (not complimentary), very comfy platform-style beds, good gym, glass showers with rain heads, large flatscreen TV mounted on wall, location right on 410 (the main loop), room service available from neighboring pub, pool table in lobby bar area, lots of nearby restaurants & shopping. Cons: No decaf coffee in room (although there is hot tea), the only shampoo is a shampoo/conditioner combo that KILLED my hair (not conditioning at all that I could tell), no bath tub (showers only) only healthy food available from pub/room service is salad, pool is outdoor only, no hot tub. Overall, would recommend it, but not rave about it.

“Just right” We booked the HGI TS for a girls shopping weekend and it was just right for our needs. Easy check in and allowed late check out on last day (2 pm). decent breakfast (complimentary due to HH Gold card) but could have had a bit more variety (same menu on 3 days we were there although I believe there was pancakes on rather than waffles the day before we arrived). Room were large enough to fit the two queen beds and enough room for luggage and shopping bags and to walk around. All the areas were well maintained and clean. We overlooked 48th Street and a courtyard. It was pretty quiet as we were on the 11th floor but you could hear some noises in the distance. Business center allows free internet access although there was problems with the pc and printer which were unresolved during my stay. In room Wi-fi is free if you have your laptop. Good choice of tv channels and microwave, fridge and safe were good too. Nice area to sit and wait in the lobby (free coffee in the morning till around 10.30). Staff were friendly and helpful (Terry at check in and Charles always greeted you on your way in). We booked quite some time in advance and received an excellent rate. I would definitely recommend this hotel. Thanks to the tripadvisors who rated this. Otherwise we would not have booked this hotel.

“Mid town and in the middle of it all - a place to rest” Great Westin Style...in the middle of the hubbub..just opposite the Port Authority Bus station, a block from Times Sq. perfect oasis of corporate comfort in the city's heart. Upper floor rooms with a city view are perfect - quiet with a view! heavenly beds and simple showers...can't go wrong.

“Close for conventions” I traveled here for a work conference at the convention center. For me, Westin's are comfortably predictable. I even enjoy their signature scent. This was a great location because I was able to valet my car and not need it again for 3days. I only had one mishap with room service but they took care of the issue very quickly. The pool is very intimate but I wasn't there to swim. There's too much to explore outside of the hotel. We dined one night at the hotel restaurant, Zocca which was very good. The gym was a perfect size with around 8 pieces of equipment. The coffee nook is a little hidden but they replicated a good Starbucks pumpkin spice latte. If you stay here, be sure to request a riverview room not far from the elevators. If they put you at the end of the hall, it's a long walk, especially if you've been on your feet all day sightseeing or working a conference.

“Front desk staff could do better ...” After a horrendous drive from New York City to Philadelphia, we were looking forward to a relaxing evening meal and a comfy bed. On arrival, I enquired of the front desk about parking facilities, to be brusquely told "Next door. Up the ramp!" On check-in "Miss Charisma" was busy with another client, but did not even acknowledge us for over 5 mins. When she did get around to checking us in she was extremely brusque and half way through the procedure stopped to answer the phone and again to give someone directions! Finally checked in and bags in the room, we headed to the restaurant at 21:10 to be told the restaurant closed at 21:00 and there was no room service! We braved "Miss Charisma" again who reluctantly directed us to a loud bar, come club, that served burgers and such - not what we had in mind. We eventually came across a nice Italian, Maggiano's Little Italy and had a nice meal there. Had we known, this hotel is right near Chinatown, with plenty of choice. The room was spacious, but the bed had definately seen better days (quite a lot of days and nights, judging from the dip in the centre). We also had an issue with the toilet backing up on the first night, which was put right the following day. *Be aware there is no safe in the room and I was very nervous about leaving my laptop, tickets and passports in the room.

“Lacks apology, cleaning, and attached parking” After our stay March 12-16 I have started referring to this place as the Dirty Double Tree, rather that the Doubletree Club San Diego. I can not wait to read the management response to this. Let me guess... “We are sorry you were inconvenienced.” I can’t expect anything else, more about that later. After checking in, driving up the steep hill and navigating the tight $16/night parking garage we hauled our luggage through the garage, down the sidewalk, down the ramp, past the pool and pulled the doors open to actually get inside. Please tell me why the doors to & from the walkway to the parking garage are not automatic at all? I'd even go for the push button for handicap accessibility on one of the doors or something. It would also help if there were luggage carts in the garage, or bell staff that could help with bags or get the door. So we get up to our room and my husband instantly clicks the TV on to catch some March Madness basketball. I look around and start to notice that the room is not clean. It was strange because the bed was made, dirty towels were gone, BUT towels weren't replaced, trash cans were full, there was gunk on the sheets..... What the?! My husband picked up the phone to call the front desk and is asked to hold. No big deal, I just want a new room. 10 minutes later the front desk person picks up and asks if he'll hold again, he said NO! He tells the girl what the problem is and she says that we can come down to get a new room. What's confusing me at this point is why the dirty towels were removed & the bed made, but trash wasn't taken out and towels weren't replaced. I know most hotels don't change the sheets daily, but I've never had the trash not emptied when housekeeping comes in to make the bed & tidy up. We wait at the front desk again. Finally get to the front of the line, pass the keys over while my husband says "I'm the one that called about the dirty room." The response? "Oh, OK," that's it. No “I'm sorry about that.” No “Sorry we weren't aware that housekeeping hadn't serviced that room.” Nothing, just new room # & recoded keys. Our new room was better. Still not super clean but it had been cleaned. The bathroom was your average sized hotel bathroom, nothing thrilling but fine. The beds were the typical DT beds, nice sheets, comfy mattress. Large flat screen TV. In the cabinet under the TV is a mini fridge which was really nice for leftovers, a big plus. The desk area was fine. The couch was comfy. The sliding door lock didn’t work, but on the 3rd floor I wasn’t too concerned since the slide in L shaped metal “lock” was there. Our little rounded balcony looked out over the pool area. Rather The thing was that every night we’d hear all of the kids & families outside in the pool until it closed. Then for some reason after the pool was closed the area around the pool became some sort of hook-up central. There were adults with clothing coming off at least two nights during our stay. Personally, I don’t care if someone was just taking off a jacket, if the pool is closed no one needs to be in that area sharing one lounge chair even cuddling. Go inside and get (into) a (your) room! The drain in our tub was so slow the tub would fill up during one shower. I’m not fond of sitting around in the room in the morning for my husband or I to wait for the tub to drain after the other has showered. It was very par for the course when housekeeping left the hair & soap gunk in the bottom of the tub after they “cleaned” after our first night. I’m sure the housekeeping person just didn’t care that the tub wasn’t draining; it has to be the guests’ job to keep track of those things. So we stopped by the front desk the second morning to let them know that someone had to resolve the tub issue and that the light right inside of our door (the one that is controlled by the switch when you enter the room) had burnt out. I can’t say that I was surprised that a bellman was manning the front desk. It of course took him a while to find something to write our request on. I was actually amazed that they did fix the tub issue and eventually the light too! I know it’s not totally within the hotel’s control, but the people across the hall from us were super loud and obnoxious. The walls in this place are way too thin. From what I saw there were 3 adults and at least 4 kids in that room. Every morning after about 7am they would flip the security latch out so that they could go in & out continuously. That bouncing sound is super when you’re trying to sleep. I’ll also mention the ridiculous rent a cops that just sit & watch TV in the lobby. Glad I can help pay for that too. I would say based on my issues and other reviews those guys probably help get rid of unhappy guests or something. Well, in the past when I’ve had less than stellar hotel stays I have tried not to air all of the details online, I attempt to deal with the hotel first. Since the staff that was on duty through our stay was apathetic at best, that didn’t go anywhere. Only the last day when we were checking out did we see a name for the manager on duty or any sign of the manager. But she was too busy frustrating another guest for us to bother talking to her. I did contact the hotel by submitting a complaint through Hilton’s website. I was contacted by the Front Office Manager (I’m not sure I can post names on here). I went as far as to send this woman photos and point out that my biggest issue with the whole situation is the lack of an apology from the hotel staff when the problems occurred. I have the past been assigned a room that wasn’t cleaned, and the staff has kindly relocated me and apologized. To me, that’s a job well done. Mistakes happen, the front desk might be told by the cleaning staff that a room has been cleaned; they can only go by what they’re told. Unfortunately, the response from the manager was that she was going to have half of my stay refunded, and then said “Once again I am terribly sorry for the trouble this has caused you.” That’s it. I proceeded to respond, and copy the person from Hilton that forwarded my inquiry to the Doubletree Club. Without actually telling her what to say, I went through a whole email explaining that hotels that can apologize when a problem pops up make me as a guest happy. Sure I’m not ecstatic because the problem still happened, but a simple “I am sorry, your room was not acceptable, we will discuss it with our staff” is very sufficient for me. Well, once again, no actual apology, just this: “When I said I was sorry for the trouble, I meant that I was sorry for the inconvenience that we caused you. This situation was discussed with management as well as our team members and it was in no way ignored. Corrective feedback was given to the team members who did not do their job properly.” Look, I don’t want to know what was done to whom. I don’t care what was discussed with whom. I want the hotel management to acknowledge a problem and give an apology. I didn’t want a refund. Why should the company I booked through have to go through the hassle of a refund. Never did I say I was “troubled” or inconvenienced, as I said the indifferent staff was my problem and it should be a problem for this hotel. After my email the manager called my home but I was at work. My husband did give her my cell phone number but I couldn’t pick up. After two calls in a row from the hotel I had one long silence voicemail and one that said “Hello Ms ‘my last name’ this is”. That’s it. No way will I call you back if you can’t actually leave me a message or try back later if you can’t figure out how Sprint’s voicemail works. Ultimately, I gave up on the series of emails. I wasn’t getting anywhere by emailing the hotel directly. Apparently “I’m sorry” was not in the manager’s vocabulary. This place really has potential. The parking situation is bad. The driveway down onto Hotel Circle is steep and you can scrape your car. BUT, had this hotel lived up to the standards one would expect with the Doubletree name those things would have been minor details. The location in hotel circle is great. Easy access of course to the 8 & the 5, but not too bad to head up toward North County either, and really convenient to Old Town. Now they are just problems on a long list of things, most of which could be fixed by this joke of a hotel. Too bad there's a 10 photo limit!

“Nice hotel, when you have a car.” Dallas is one of those "forget it without a car" cities and the location of this Doubletree underscores that. Well located for Market events, it is also fairly convenient as a base to many other areas...if you have a car. Bear in mind, Dallas traffic is awful, the drivers fast and aggressive and most of the highways are in some stage of repair. All that said, the staff work hard to make you feel at home and comfortable from all the driving stress. First impressions: The building itself looks architecturally dated and though I didn't ask, it must have been something else in a previous life. Lobby was bright and you could see the pool. Check in: The staff was consistently delightful. From check-in to driving directions they did all to please. A room was ready for my afternoon arrival and it all took about 5 minutes. The room: It is pretty much standard though a touch dated. Having experienced other properties with hardwood floors (or the laminate version), the wall to wall carpeting seemed old. The bed was comfortable, as was the desk chair. Wireless worked very well. It is worth noting that the air conditioning worked wonders. It hovered around 109oF each day I was there (reaching 117o one day!) but the room cooled quickly when I turned on the AC. Note, keep your drawn during the day to diminish the heat. The lighting needs to be addressed as it is fairly dark at night. The side lamps are on dimmers, a very nice touch, but don't go bright enough to read in bed. This is not peculiar to this hotel, many suffer the same design flaws. The bathroom: Average, starting to feel cramped as newer properties increase the bathroom sizes. Full complement of extras and a nice touch of a card offering "what you forgot" available at the lobby. Lighting good, too. Extras: Nice to have a fridge in the room Decent channel range on TV Of note: •Parking is free and plentiful. You will need a car in Dallas but it is fairly simple to get around and much is a relatively short drive. ("relative" being dependent on traffic) •The area is desolate at night. There is a Denny's across the street and the hotel has a restaurant, but if you want more, you're taking a drive. •The Dallas Design area is nearby, if you're interested, there are many shops, dealers and ideas waiting for you.

“No coffee, no desk, no water, no flowers, no fruit, but...” The wife and I stayed over for three nights on the 20% discount plan. The offered rate of $508 for the 77th Street deluxe room turned out to be more than fair. Pleasing features of this hotel include a perfect location for museums and the UES, Jean Georges restaurant and bar on ground floor, pleasing and spacious spa and workout areas, nice crisp lobby, generally friendly staff, relatively new rooms, towels, linens, and pillows (mattresses ready for replacement), generous room size, apparently new marble bathrooms, and dependable, nice maids. The Mark may be best described as a botique 5 star. It's without the 5 star amenities at the top, the room technology is a bit dated (quite small flat screen, undependable older Crestron system), and the hallway doors close very, very loudly. But failings tend to be nits when run up against the benefits of The Mark We would happily come back to The Mark again, especially if the 20% was on.

“a great hotel” this was a great hotel for me and my wife...excellent location, views of broadway, great staff, and the bonus was the lobby and the lounge, with the outdoor 2nd floor patio where we had dessert one night. Very good sized rooms, good a/c, comfortable beds, tv and lighting good, nice bathrooms (hardwood floors? that's a first). I cannot imagine a negative review. Obviously a favorite with the Euro tourists. I would book it again. Never felt as big as it was - which is a postive.

“Convenient Airport Hotel” I liked this hotel as I stayed here on 2 separate occasions during the past week and it was clean, comfortable and convenient. I got both of my rooms on Priceline at below $100 rates during the week and was quite pleased with the location, where it is actually connected to the airport (via covered walkways). On my first stay, I was given a room with a view towards the Boston cityscape, while not as pretty as the view from the Hyatt, it was still pretty. The only restaurant open was Connelly's Pub (Berkshire's is for Breakfast only) and while it was nice inside, it was definitely overpriced ($17 for a hamburger?) and the service wasn't that friendly. If I had my druthers, I would have taken the shuttle to the T-station and gone to the North End for some better food but it's convenient at the hotel if you're too tired to leave. Nice fitness center which was bigger than most places (they called it a Health Club), with quite a few cardio machines, a nice pool and whirlpool (which I couldn't use because of too many kids) and locker rooms that have dry/steam saunas in them. Rooms were comfortable and clean and I never heard one plane and rarely any of my neighbors. Checked in late (12:30am) on my second stay and I actually walked there from Terminal B (about 5-10 mins). It's easier from A or E but still walkable from the other terminals if you're brave enough and can figure it out. Since it was rainy the next morning, I spent most of it inside and ventured to one of the Terminals for breakfast (cheaper than the hotel). Quite happy with the location and comfort of the hotel and never had a bad interaction with the staff. Wi-Fi is not free but sometimes if you go to the computers behind the lobby, you might find a hotel computer where someone paid for time and then left.....

“Excellent value if you can get it on priceline” I spent 3 nights here with my family over Easter weekend. We were lucky enough to get a great deal on priceline. All the rooms are suites, which comes in handy if you have a couple of people in a room. There are a few pools scattered around the property. The main one is pretty busy with lots of kids and music, but we preferred the one closer to our room. It was smaller, but had a hot tub and there weren't many other people there. I would definitely recommend a trip up to the restaurant at the top of the hill for at least a drink, it really is a gorgeous setting. Unfortunately we went on a Saturday night when a pretty cheesy cover band was playing, maybe it would be quieter during the week. The rooms were well maintained for the age of the hotel. Service was fine, the staff was very friendly. Since this is on the northern edge of Phoenix, we ended up driving quite a bit to go out to eat and explore the city. But it would be a great spot to plop down if you just want to lounge poolside for a couple of days. One annoying thing was the per day charge of $12 for internet, and it wasn't even wireless.

“乾燥対策が必須です” 年末年始にツアーで行きました。 場所はタイムズスクエアの近くです。 また、私は42Street沿いのバスターミナルを利用するので、徒歩圏だったのもよかったです。 ホテルと併設されている劇場は美女と野獣が演目だったようでカードキーがそれでした。かわいかったです。 室内ですが狭めなのはニューヨークだから仕方がないとして、乾燥が半端じゃないくらいすごかったです。声がでなくなるくらいの乾燥で現地で湿気対策グッズをいろいろ購入して大変でした。他のホテルでここまですごい乾燥状態だったことはなかったので、このホテルは特に気をつけたほうがよいと思います。

“A Lovely Hotel to stay at” We stayed at Hotel Tomo because it was close to my son's apartment for the last few days of our trip. Hotel Tomo was a pleasant surprise. It used to be a Best Western and now is not and hence we did not get reward points. The rooms had wonderful view on higher floors, being naturally higher. The staff were nice and warm, typical of San Francisco. The area itself, Japantown, is very peaceful. There a fair amount of eating places in Fillmore. Do not miss out on buffet at Indian Palace. The place does not have looks but the food is great. Clean rooms, airy and comfortable an spacious. Good value for money in a big city.

“Nice upgrades, but bathroom in need of remodel.” The lobby of the hotel was very pleasant and the room's furniture has been updated with a modern flair and a flat screen tv. However, the bathroom really needs work. The grout was dirty and the caulk around the tub was reapplied pretty sloppily. The shower curtain also had a couple of tears in it.

“We were the only guests in the entire hotel!” We were the only guests at this poorly maintained motor inn marketed as a hotel on various travel sites. I should have known the second I saw what appeared to be a lagoon shaped pool of toxic waste in front of the place. "Is that a pool?" I asked my boyfriend. "It must have been," he replied. The checkin process was rather strange and the coffee in the lobby was empty, apparently until further notice. The internet was not currently functional on the circa 1998 computer made available to users in the lobby. Under strict supervision and with frequent reprimands. Wireless internet was not available. We were pleasantly surprised by the size of our room which featured two Queen size beds and a roomy (but semi functional) bathroom. We were exhausted the first night of our two night stay and fell asleep without noticing the substandard air quality and freezing temperatures. It was literally close to freezing in our room and despite numerous calls to the front desk we were not even given extra blankets to ease the chill. We woke the next morning to the front desk pounding on our door telling us it was time to go, although we were planning to stay two nights and had prepaid on line. We went downstairs to consult the woman's computer but unfortunately the whole system was down. Since we were the only guests they elected not to offer the usual continental breakfast. With no where within easy walking distance to get food we looked at one another and said, "let's bounce". We then snuck out the side door at the far end of the pool to avoid having to explain this to the front desk lady. The stay was, without a doubt, the creepiest I have experienced. I would never stay here again, I can't even look at the place without cringing!

“Gem on the westside of Manhattan” The Ink48 was a great hotel. It was clean, well decorated rooms. It was very hotel and reminded me of a toned down version of a W hotel. The staff was very friendly. The rooftop bar offered great views of Manhattan and was very cozy. My only complaint was the extremely limited offering of late night room service options.

“Minutes to Airport and Aurora” I enjoyed this hotel. It is off Pena Blvd. and in a cluster of traveler hotels and restaurants. I enjoyed walking around the area and checking out the prairie dogs and rabbits. The hotel is fairly new and in proximity to excellent restaurants. The suites are nicely appointed and the staff was great. We had an incident where the lock in the bathroom failed and we had to have a maintenance man drill the lock out. It took 20 minutes but my wife stayed calm. This has never happened before and I am sure it was a fluke. It makes one think though, if you were alone you may not be found till until the housekeeper comes in, whenever. We took trips to downtown Denver, the hotel is a few miles from I-70 and to great authentic Mexican restaurants downtown.

“Pricey But Perfect” If you want to stay in a fabulous hotel in the city and you're willing to pay a little extra, I'd recommend this place.Also, pay the extra for a corner room - the views of the city are spectacular.A short walk to Michigan Avenue. Excellent service from the valets, concierge, lobby agents, and waitstaff in the restaurants. The food in the restaurants was great and room service wasn't too shabby either.Well worth the money!

“Great except for the noise” I stayed on business and the hotel was very clean and quite comfortable. The staff was also very accommodating and helpful, and the restaurant was actually quite good. My only complaint would be the noise during the day from the renovations going on, so if you plan on being in the room during the day I would give this place a pass until the renovations are complete.

“Repeat Great Trip Near the Heart of the City” Along the ocean of Chicago, Lake Michigan, sits a wonderful and accomodating hotel in the Hyatt family. I first stayed here 15 years ago for a convention, and this hotel is ideally suited for that purpose. Meeting rooms and internet access abound, as do small places for private breakout sessions. As this latest was a repeat stay with my hubby, I was more interested in the room, appealing culinary options, and current cultural offerings within the city. The room was spacious, but the bathroom was truly Zen. The walls were tiled with stone panels in muted shades, the bathtub was clean, deep and waiting for long soaks, the mirrors were surrounded by wonderful light for makeup purposes, and the towels were thick and comforting. All I missed was a generous terry bathrobe and this experience would have been on par with a stay I had at the Ritz in Boston. Of course there are drawbacks, the most noted being the lack of a pool or workout room for guests. Still, walking along the lakefront ensured exercise remained on my agenda. It was a treat to visit the Museum of Broadcast Communication, which only recently reopened in its new location. By dinner time, my plans to visit Cafe Iberico were thwarted when my love realized that he yearned for a short jaunt to an attached restaurant, which held no appeal to me whatsoever. Experience told me to run from "hotel food" but the food, wine, service and atmosphere of Stetson's was spot-on. There are many great hotels from which to chose on a visit to Chicago, and for this property I will classify it as quite modern in design and execution and at an utterly convenient location just south of the Michigan Avenue bridge on the "ocean" side. Be certain to book a sightseeing cruise via the Chicago Architectural Foundation. Educated and excited docents meld the creativity of the architects over the century with the history that inspired world class competition for designing bragging rights. I extended the stay to hear Michael Franti and Spearhead, who played a free gig at the Taste of Chicago. That was the topping on the ice cream.

“Noisy and Dirty” It's funny. .. .I am a Kimpton Hotel member, and I saw an article regarding the Palomar Phoenix opening in June. The Kimpton Properties are FIRST CLASS all the way. I was thrilled to know there is a property opening in Phoenix in June. There were several comments after the article from Phoenix residents (or Clarendon employees?) sharing their loyalty for the Clarendon Hotel. I actually found that to be odd. I mean, why put down a competitive hotel (before it even opens!), unless you have something to be afraid of. . . .and then I remembered! I stayed at the Clarendon Hotel via Hotwire serveral months ago. My partner and I were so disappointed with our stay, we actually had Hotwire take this hotel out of our hotel options when looking for a place to stay in Phoenix. And I called Hotwire complaining about the property and it's star rating. First, while the rooms are unique with an artistic design, the walls are paper thin. And the environment of the hotel welcomes a "party" atmosphere. The nights we were there there was loud music playing well after midnight, and people walking/running down the halls drunk. I actually felt as if I was in a college dorm, as did my boyfriend. The pool area was FILTHY. Clearly no-one was on sight to clean up during the day. There were used towels everyone, and cups/glasses had not been thrown out (taken away). My boyfriend loves to swim but did not go anywhere near the pool after seeing the lack of care taken for keeping the area clean. The restaurant was good! And as a vegetarian, I appreciated the option provided. If you are looking for a quiet, intimate and relaxing get away, do your self a favor and check out the Palomar. If you are looking to party. . .. the Clarendon is the place for you.

“Beware of and Clearly understand reservation restrictions at Cedarbrook” Even though the Cedarbrook Lodge is a highly regarded Trip Advisor property, I cannot recommend it. As part of a business meeting, I had reserved a room at the Cedarbrook for February 24, 2011 via their website; the room rate was advertised as “non-refundable”. As our firm’s meeting approached a bad winter storm was forecast to hit the Seattle area on the day of our meeting. Because people were coming in from out of town (some by car over the Cascade Mountains), our company elected to postpone our meeting rather than risk weather related problems trying to host it on 2/24/11. I tried to reschedule my room reservation to another day on two occasions with different people. I was not asking to have the room costs refunded. The Lodge personnel were completely uncooperative in my request for relief on the room reservation cost even as facility after facility shut down around the Seattle area due to weather. I was charged $152.86 for a room I never used. Caveat emptor.

“Flawless service and very comfortable accommodations.” Just returned from a long weekend stay at the CSH with my wife and daughter for a college visits. We reserved a "Family Suite" which consisted of two separate king bedrooms of good size and a very small bathroom. The bedrooms were very nicely furnished, very comfortable beds, large flat screen televisions, individual climate controls and free wifi. For the price, this room is an extremely good value if traveling with children. Unfortunately, as stated, the bathroom is out of sync with regard to size with the two bedroom suite where more people will be using the bathroom than in a single hotel room. The service was perfect! The front desk found a room for us to check in to at 11 A.M. without giving the usual brush off and explanation about rooms not being guaranteed before 3 P.M. We parked our car on a side street having missed the proper entrance and the valet retrieved the car without complaint and parked it. Every attempt was made to remember our names, our activities and welcome us back to the hotel at the end of the day. Room service food was generally very good to excellent with prompt service...never taking more than 20 to 30 minutes at any time of day. The location was prime...with shopping and excellent restaurants within steps of the hotel. It is in a somewhat touristy area of Boston but the hotel is not overrun by tourists and always feels homey rather than institutional. I would highly recommend this hotel as a great value without sacrificing comfort, amenities or service.

“Excellent Choice in Manhatten” I stayed here two nights in a corner king. PROS: Very large room, especially for NYC Good location for my needs Room was clean and updated Fantastic view in corner room Quiet room due to only 1 neighbor (corner room) Efficient staff CONS: The HVAC worked a little too hard to keep a constant temperature Old style tube TVs could use an update

“Stay was really just OK” Located toward the south end of the Gaslamp Quarter at 6th and J, the Hotel Solamar is well-situated for roaming the downtown streets of San Diego. Parking is steep at $35 per night. The lobby and public areas have a rather dark, sequestered feeling. The room was very comfortable and well maintained. Windows can be opened for fresh air. The problems I had with the room were minimal lighting in the bathroom, the lack of a coffeemaker. and the fact that I could get virtually nothing into the room safe for storage. By joining the Kimpton frequent guest program, I received an invitation to upgrade my room upon availabililty. When I checked in, the upgraded room was available, but the desk clerk refused to give it to me. I know I would have enjoyed a jacuzzi tub in my room, since the rooftop pool deck doesn't have one. The rooftop bar was pleasant, with personable waitstaff. Since people are mentioning dogs here, there were many dogs. I was not bothered by this whatsoever, nor did I ever hear any barking or any noise from my neighbors whatsoever. For all the hype this hotel receives, overall I felt that the Hotel Solamar did not live up to its reputation.

“Nice Place” I found a special on Travelzoo and booked this place for New Year's Eve. Very nice hotel. The staff was friendly and helpful but not overbearing. The design is great. We went to the hotel's wine reception and enjoyed the champagne. The lobby was modern in design but still very warm and cozy with low lighting and a lit fireplace. The soft music added a nice touch. I was a bit disappointed when we first opened the door to our room because the first thing I noticed was the view. It was very industrial, and we could see a Public Storage building. However, once I closed the drapes, the room looked great. Very smart design with lots of browns, yellows, and blues. We had the standard room, which was fine. The 32-inch flat-screen TV was certainly big enough for the room. The brown striped bathrobes were pretty cool. We had dinner at the hotel's restaurant, Central 214, and we were pleasantly surprised at how good the food was and how large the portions were. The service was wonderful. The hotel is across the street from Mockingbird Station, which includes a Starbucks, an Angelika movie theater and several other restaurants and shops. The clientele seemed pretty upscale, but people were very friendly at the wine reception. Even on New Year's Eve, it was pretty quiet. We hardly heard anything from our rooms. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and loved the design and atmosphere.

“Great Hotel! Clean, modern, and convenient.” This is a very solid hotel. I was pleased with how modern and clean it was. Great workout room, good breakfast, and close to all major freeways and the beachs are about 15 minutes by car. The beds were so comfortable and the large flat screen tv was totally unexpected. It seems like it would be a noisy area, but the hotel was very quiet and the back area was well lighted and very safe feeling. I lived in SD for 2 years and I know the area pretty well - I would not stay anywhere else.

“Loved our Getaway” Just returned for a three night stay at the Park Hyatt. My husband and I went away for a weekend sans kids and loved our stay. This was our first trip to Chicago and I did much research on hotels. I chose this one because of TripAdvisor recommendations and I'm a Hyatt Gold Passport member. Our request for a high floor was honored by the hotel and we had a water view of Lake Michigan. I was disappointed that our room did not have the opening between the bathroom and bedroom that was advertised on the website but it did not spoil our trip. The concierge was extremely helpful and provided some nice dinner suggestions. You must try Cafe Spiaggia. Absolutely the best meal we've ever had. Wonderful! I would recommend this hotel and it is a great location. Convenient to all the shopping. I would also recommend the Chicago Architecture Boat Tour. It was a great 1 1/2 hour boat ride on the Chicago River that really showed the great architecture of the city. The only negative I would have was the carpet was in need of cleaning. For the cost of the rooms I felt the carpet could have been newer or at least clean. It showed wear and tear and many spots. Overall the rest of the room was great.

“Customer service brings this excellent hotel to the top” The staff would butter your fresh croissants or feed you the finest blueberries and raspberries while you reclined on one of their poolside chaises if you asked. Otherwise ask for an extra face cloth or fix the sound for the TCM channel and they are there before you put the phone back on the hook. Going to an out of the way restaurant? Then someone at the front desk will get exact directions for you. Mira checks you in like a first cousin welcoming you to her house. Oh, and besides that the rooms have every amenity that a four or five star hotel would offer except a towel warmer(can you manage without it?). Decor is West Elm or Bo Concepts, all easy on the eye and very functional.

“Stay here for the location and don't expect much else” My wife and I stayed here this past Friday and Saturday night. I've wanted to stay at this hotel ever since I was a little kid and while it is a nice historical landmark, it leaves a lot to be desired in terms of service and hospitality. Granted there was a lot going on as it was New Year's Eve and the hotel was playing host to both UCLA and the University of Illinois for the Kraft Fight Hunger Bowl, but it's not like that was news to them. We arrived on BART from SFO and took the Powell Street exit and walked about 3 or 4 blocks to the hotel. It was around 9 o'clock on Friday night when we got there and we might have been given the worst room in the hotel, which was on the 3rd floor of the main building. I got the room on Priceline and I wasn't expecting much, but when we got in the room it felt like it wasn't thoroughly cleaned and the bathroom was filthy with multiple hairs from a previous guest (or guests) in the shower and on the floor. My wife was disgusted and any points I might have scored from getting this hotel were immediately lost. The room and bathroom were both very small. They gave us a queen bed that was very comfortable and we liked the 42 inch TV. The view was straight into another room across the way so we kept the shade closed which made the room feel even smaller. One saving grace was the high ceiling and the nice chandelier in the room. The bathroom was cramped to say the least. I guess it would've been acceptable for my wife if they took reasonable care in cleaning it but as I already mentioned, that was too much to ask. The shower had barely any water pressure so a Westin heavenly shower it was not. We love the location of the Westin St. Francis and there was plenty of shopping nearby for my wife and a ton of restaurants nearby and lots to do. If you want a hotel with a great location and aren't concerned about much else, this hotel is for you. But the next time we visit San Francisco, we're staying somewhere else.

“Unique and convenient!” Super convenient to the airport and unique building. Very tranquil inside lobby and atrium area. Super large King room with tons of space, large desk, couch and chair. We had an interior view of the lobby. Nice bathroom with two outlets - one on each side of the sink - great hairdryer and water pressure! Loved that there was a full length mirror and a half mirror with plug under it...bed was super comfortable. Room service was very good and fast! Room was very clean - love the large plush towels - never heard much hall noise. Breakfast buffet was awesome for the money - great oatmeal and made to order omelet! Only complaint was that the tv was smaller than preferred and it was very hard to change channels from the bed which is right in front of the bed. Other than that we loved it!

“Nice hotel; spa room not all it's cracked up to be” In town for a concert at the Nokia theater around the corner, we recently stayed the weekend in one of this hotel's spa inspired rooms. In general this is a nice hotel, typical of Westin standards. The location is very good if you wish to be near Times Square and the surrounding areas, as well as to major subway lines. We didn't find the spa room to necessarily be worth the price of the upgrade. The massage chair (our main impetus for reserving the room) was not terribly comfortable, providing no benefit to the legs or feet while being a bit too harsh on the back (even on the lowest settings). The spa bath products were nice but only provided in the typical small hotel packaging, which was not really enough to thoroughly enjoy. The 23rd floor corner room itself was very nice with windows surrounding the outside walls and a view of the river. The bathroom was large by NYC standards and had a spacious tub/shower we loved. The 'heavenly bed' left my husband and I disappointed as we really did not sleep well on it (perhaps it's an acquired comfort as we're used to a more firm mattress as opposed to the memory foam type overlay the mattress has). The pillows were divine and the bed clothes were very nice. Everything was very clean and well kept throughout our stay. The street noise however was a bit loud in the morning. The few staff we encountered throughout our stay were friendly and helpful and we had no problem arranging airport transportation through the concierge or late checkout through the customer service staff. All in all, this was a good stay and perhaps we would return if we needed a hotel in this particular vicinity once again.

“Trendy, but Friendly” Stayed with friends in two rooms for a fun weekend. Trendy hotel with the standard "W" look. Rooms are a little bit on the small side - particularly considering the prices you are paying - but that's pretty standard for all the W hotels I have stayed at. Most everything is a bit on the pricey side. Hotel help was very friendly and helpful all the way around (front desk, bellhops, bar/restaurant). Terrific location in Downtown Seattle. A very reasonable walk up to the shopping areas, down to the stadiums, or over to Pike's Market - very centrally location. Beds are very comfortable, and room were very clean and has all the standard "W" upscale comforts (LCD TV, Stereo, well stock mini bar.) Nice modern decor. In short, nice hotel with good hotel amenities - but you aren't going to be spending a lot of time in the room and taking advantage of them - there are more reasonably priced options for hotels in the area.

“Very Convenient” You can't beat staying at this hotel for its price, convenience and location. Unless you have to, don't get double beds, they seem kind of small. There's easy access to the city. The hotel decor is outdated and could use a huge 21st century make-over. The shower was nice. When I didn't want to leave the hotel, I ordered Chinese and it was delivered to my "room" so I didn't have to deal with meeting anyone in the lobby. There was also the option of eating at their sports bar or buffet. At the time, the buffet was closed so I ate at the sport's bar. It was nothing spectacular (buffalo chicken breast sandwich and fries) and a bit pricey. The staff is extremely helpful and resourceful. My particular housekeeper was a bother however. I didn't want my room cleaned at the time and she wouldn't leave my door until I got out of bed, went to the door and told her to go away. Then when I saw her hours later at the elevator, she pressed me again about going to my dump the trash or give me towels. I kept telling her no and all I wanted was a bottle of water off her cart. There's always free snacks (cookies/cakes) and USA today for guess. Check-in/out was a breeze. I would stay at this hotel again and hope to not deal with the same housekeeper.

“Great location, cool hotel, perfect base for NY exploration” We stayed here for three nights in November 2012. It was out first time here, and I'd highly recommend it. The hotel is "boutique" - meaning small in size (for NY/USA), cool/eclectic in design, with quirky touches. Those touches include free bikes or skateboards, cosy wine'n'cheese each evening, and a generally friendly in-the-know vibe about it. Rooms are not large, but they are classy and well designed, with just enough space for luggage and everything else. We found it perfect, but then, we're Europeans :-) Our American cousins tend to demand larger room sizes! Our room had a working balcony (small, fun) with a view uptown or East to the bridge, and out over Kenmare Street. Neighbourhood (neighborhood) is brilliant; near to Little Italy, to ChinaTown, SoHo, to the subway and lots of bus stops. We did a lot of walking and some running, and it was a brilliant for wherever we wanted to go. It also has a roof terrace (was not is use in November, but I imagine its pretty special in Summer :-) Staff were also very helpful and made some good recommendations wrt eating/drinking in the area. Anyway - I'd use it again.In fact, can't wait!

“Great room - great location - great price” If you want a terrific place to stay at a good price - check this out. Roomy suites are clean, staff is friendly, and location is 1 block from the Alamo and less than 2 from the Riverwalk. (at the end with the mall - lots of shopping, restaurants, etc!) Cost is much less than its' water facing cousins - and a HOT buffet breakfast, as well as an afternoon repast with food and drinks is included in your room rate! One downside - the pool. It is TINY - but why would you be coming to San Antonio for a pool? We were traveling with another couple - stayed in a 2 bedroom 2 bath suite for less than ONE room at the Marriott less than a block away - and a had a full kitchen in which to store water and snacks! (the hotel will actually do your grocery shopping for FREE and add the price of the groceries to your bill!) Perfect location- friendly staff -super clean rooms - great price - who needs a big pool?

“Good Location - Good Value” This hotel is for the person looking for a decent room at a decent price in a good location. The small lobby and sitting areas are fine and I was treated well by every employee I encountered, especially the waiters at breakfast in their restaurant. The room was above average for this type of hotel, with plenty of room to work and a couch and coffee table. The bathroom is a little small, if that kind of thing matters to you. There's also a fridge and microwave and they left a bag of popcorn, a bottle of water and granola bar every morning. The room was well cleaned four out of the five nights of my stay. I attributed the less than steller job the other night to a change in housekeeper. It's a safe easy walk to the Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. There's a couple of little bars down the block and, of course, all the downtown restaurants. For the adventurus, take a walk to the World Famous Lexington Market on a Saturday morning. The area and crowd make look a little dicey to those not used to big city urban living, but it's perfectly safe. Treat yourself to some of the local food at great prices. There's nothing like standing at a counter and enjoying a crab cake and beer amongst the hustle and bustle at 10:30am. And don't forget the warm,fresh roasted peanuts at Konstant's outdoor stand. As a Baltimore native, who lived there most of my life,I've never seen so many policemen in the tourist area. There were almost two a block at night. So you should feel safe. Also, don't forget to head to the bar districts of Fells Point and my old neighborhood of Canton. So, save money on the pricier hotels and spread it around town a little.

“perfection....” Great location, views, rooms.....what really sets this hotel apart is the staff, however! From start to finish, they truly go the extra mile to be sure your stay is top notch. If I could give this property (and most importantly staff) 6 stars I would! If you are looking for the best hotel in Seattle, look no further.....

“Excellent Option with central location” We stayed here for a business trip when our usual corporate hotels were sold out and we could not have been happier. The hotel either has been newly renovated or the upkeep has been fantastic. Every inch of the hotel was extremely clean and the service was friendly, fast and very pleasant. The rooms truly are suites with full kitchens and plenty of space to lounge and relax. The complimentary internet was super fast (didn't lose the connection once in 3 days) and the complimentary buffet breakfast was just the thing to help us kick off a couple of busy days. The breakfast is the usual selection of hot and cold items. There is also a complimentary Happy Hour Monday-Thursday with free beer and wine and light snacks (they had fajitas the night we were there). The location is very central to the 16th St. Pedestrian Mall and the rest of downtown Denver. Excellent value for the money. We would absolutely stay here again.

“Wouldn't recommend staying here” I am in complete agreement with the review from SEH7 about this hotel. They really need to decide if they are a hotel or a night club. The staff was very friendly and helpful. But my one additional complaint would be how bad our bathroom was. The bathtub was peeling and dirty and the mold on the shower curtain was horrible.

“Not bad - as airport hotels go” Typical Hampton Inn in most regards. Pleasant staff, standard architecture. I arrived in Phoenix, needing a room at the last minute - they offered me a good rate, and I was thrilled to get it. However, they said their shuttle service ended at 11:00 PM, and it was about 11:05. Therefore, I should take a cab - and get this - they would pay for it! 2 points for them. (I wish the Phoenix cabbies were as pleasant as the hotel staff). So, when I got to the hotel, it was about 11:30. The room was lovely, and divided quite distinctly into a sitting and sleeping area. Just a room (not a suite), but well laid out. Comfy bed, and nice, large bathroom. So far so good. I finally unwound and fell asleep about 1:00, secure in the knowledge that I had made my return shuttle reservation for 7:00 AM (This particular property requests that you book your shuttle the night before). So, it was unfortunate that I received a call from the desk at 4:30 - wanting to know if I had planned on being on that 4:30 AM shuttle. So, that part was a bummer - but I understood the need. If I had booked a shuttle and overslept, I would want them to call. I was just annoyed that my already reduced sleep had been interrupted. There was a mixup in room numbers. Anyway, it did not detract from my overall opinion of the hotel. If I were in the area again and needed a quick sleep - the Hampton Inn Phoenix North would be on my short list.

“Lovely hotel in a terrific location” This is a great hotel in New York City and only a few blocks from Grand Central Terminal. The staff was very friendly and the rooms are great. The banquet staff is very energetic and makes sure a meeting room is set up right.

“Step Back Into Another Era” An excellent, old fashioned hotel. Super valets. We arrived on motorcycles and they walked us to and from the garage each time we needed the bikes and had the hotel's car available for us when we need that. Hats off to these guys. The rest of the staff certainly was not far behind. We enjoyed the dark calm of the bar with its adjoining sitting room. It truly felt like we were in a fine hotel from decades past. The rooms and bathrooms are immaculate with all modern amenities. The entire hotel is just calm and quiet. The property deserves its ratings and I highly recommend it.

“Closest to LAX, refined” A huge lobby and many conference rooms set the stage for this hotel. Rooms are well appointed with Sleep Number matresses, nice furniture and toiletries. But a smaller CRT TV with weak signal?! Fitness room does NOT match the rest of the hotel with a poorly maintained look which also carries over to the machines. You have to pay it use Internet- $7 for 15 minutes.

“Fun, friendly, funky cool - love it!” I've passed the Argonaut many times and always wondered if it was as inviting inside as it seemed. Finally stayed there, and loved it. I'm not much for a nautical theme, but they've made it work, really well. It's a cool hotel, and the staff are just as cool. "Mandatory" wine hour in the lobby was packed, and everyone seemed to be having a good time. Room was great, nice and big, though my windows had no view. But clean, modern, and again, nicely decorated. Fun animal print robes in the closet a great touch! Plus, you can't beat the location. Maybe a bit pricey, but that's San Francisco.

“Great hotel” Can't beat this hotel. The room was very clean, bed was firm but comfortable. Internet in the room was good. Breakfast was standard fare, with scrambled eggs and sausage. Did not use the fitness center but it is very well equipped. Garage in the lower level had enough spots for us, but not sure if the hotel is full. Good location on the light rail and near the airport. And the best part is the price, especially for silicon valley.

“Looks can be deceiving...” My husband and I chose this hotel for one reason--it was the least expensive hotel within ten miles of Lowe's Motor Speedway that still had rooms available over Memorial Day Weekend. We were going to Charlotte for the NASCAR race and only staying one night, which I am more than thankful for now, as this hotel was overpriced and awful. When we checked in, the front desk staff was friendly and the lobby and bathroom were clean. The outside of the hotel also looked very nice. We had to check in early (11:15 AM) and get over to the track, so they were nice enough to give us our keys even though our room wasn't ready. We were okay with that, but now I wish we had gotten a look at the room before leaving for the day! By the time we got back to the hotel that night, we were tired and sweaty from a long day at the racetrack. It was warm out, but the room was so freezing we had to turn the heat on. It took us forever to figure out that for some reason, the bathroom light was wired to a switch by the door to the hallway, not to the switch in the bathroom itself, which was frustrating. Also, we were given a handicapped room. In my experience, if you are not handicapped, hotels will clarify that it is okay that they are giving you a handicapped room, but this was not the case at this hotel. We were too tired to deal with it, so we went right to bed, and the bed itself was awful. The floor would have been more comfortable, there were only two flat pillows in the entire room, and the "comforter" felt disgusting and grimy. Memorial Day weekend or not, kitchenette or not, there is no way this hotel is worth $108/night. If I had booked a stay of more than one night or spent more than nine hours in the room, I would have complained.

“very lucky to be here” At a time when hotel rates in Manhattan were heading for the stratosphere ($400-plus for a Crowne Plaza? Hunh??), I got this hotel for less than $200. It is worth much, much more. The location is extremely convenient. The lack of a restaurant in the hotel proper is OK since there are all types of places within yards, including excellent NY-style pizza right next door, Starbucks across the street, and a nice cafe at the corner of Seventh Avenue. The bed was extremely firm, and I was in a double-double room despite booking a king. No problem. The bathroom was unusually nice for this sort of older hotel. Overall strong recommendation at this price point.

“Service leaves much desired” Pluses are the historic building, high ceilings and great Penn Quarter neighborhood which has really blossomed in the last few years. Front desk staff need some training in the hospitality industry. No warm welcome (return Kimpton guest) at check in; no explanation of what my package rate included; no interest in helping me upgrade from my basement room (I was relocated after not accepting the basement room-AWFUL!!). Front desk staff were generally surly and aloof. Was this all because I had a dog?? I chose the Monaco in part because I could bring my well behaved Spaniel as they are a "pet-friendly" hotel. Several staff (maid, doorman) were TERRIFIED of my friendly dog. I wondered if I get poor service because I had a dog-but now I have read the other service reviews.

“ottimo il brunch ma attenti ai prezzi” Siamo stati solo per il Brunch e devo dire ECCELSO!!! costa anche 95 dollaria testa e con i costi americani devo dire che è carissssiiimmo, però volevamo consederci qualche cosa di speciale. Ma è arrivata la sorpresina... non le solite tasse o il solito esagerato e spesso ingiustificato "TIP" ma... Dunque abbiamo chiesto alla cameriera se tutto ma veramente tutto era incluso ci ha assicuratodi si.. si.. si. Noi ci accomodiamo e ordiniamo 2 bicchieri di vino bianco da accompagnare alo splendido buffet. POI ci chiedono se vogliamo altro vino e accettiamo. Alla fine ordiniamo 2 bicchierini di vino dolce da dessert (buono).. Ecco il conto 347 DOLLARI il beveraggio è ESCLUSO!!!! naturalmente niente TIP!!!!

“Nice and clean” Clean room but crappy little pillows. Good internet signal in room. Quiet at night. Restaurant was ok but not 5 star. Staff attentive. I like the free shuttle to airport, medical center and other local attractions.

“Tolles Hotel” Das Hilton Times Square in New York bietet seinen Gästen eine tolle Unterkunft mitten im Herzen von New York City - am Times Square. Die Zimmer sind recht groß für New Yorker Verhältnisse und das Preis- / Leistungsverhältnis hierfür sehr gut. Alles ist sauber und die Aussicht aus den Zimmern ist wirklich beeindruckend. Immer wieder zu empfehlen!

“Loved it, great experience” We spent three nights here recently - a great choice, reasonable rates. Arrived late and tired, were nicely welcomed and our room was lovely, comfy, everything clean and fresh and with two bathrobes in the closet, a nice surprise. The windows opened, there was no hallway noise even though we were close to the elevators, big flatscreen TV worked well, doormen and staff were friendly and obliging. We had one room service dinner that was good value and tasty. The little kitchen area has fridge, m/c and a Keurig coffee maker. Makeup area separate from bathroom with good lighting. Great location, easy walk to Hancock building, art museum, shopping, Water Tower. The hotel's parking lot is a block away but it worked out well. I would certainly stay again. (We had a confusion with a booking, having made it online with a booking company, but the hotel management was very gracious in handling it and it all turned out well.)

“great hotel!” We had a great visit to DC at the Phoenix Park Hotel! The rooms were a bit small but comfortable, the staff was extremely friendly, and the location was excellent. The hotel is walking distance to the Smithsonian museums, and across the street from Union Station where the metro will take you to most places you'd want to visit in DC. The rates were very reasonable for DC prices as well. Breakfast at the Dubliner was delicious. I would highly recommend this hotel--as long as you don't need a lot of space in the room itself!

“Cheap and rough, as expected for the price.” Stayed at this property for one night. The lobby was a mix of some older and worn fixtures with a surprising set of new furniture at the very front. Reception was a fortress, like an all night gas station booth. The staff were pleasant. The hallways smelled funny and hallway carpets were stained on my floor. The room furniture seemed like middle school quality, clean but oddly downmarket. Other guests' sounds were audible in the hallway, but the room itself was quiet. The bed was enormous, and I wasn't sure that the sheets were clean. The bathroom was a mix of old and new fixtures, again basically clean, but there were two nickel-size holes worn in the bottom of the tub where you stand for a shower. The room was hot and stuffy and I couldn't get enough air from the cooler outside to bring it down. even though the air outside was cool, so I had to run the AC. The room stayed stuffy. I woke up with a sinus headache and it didn't clear until I had been out of the property for an hour. The Wi-Fi didn't work right. Weak signals on all floors, even in lobby. A lot of guests congregated at night and next morning in the lobby trying to get enough signal and the two I talked to were frustrated. So was I, because I wanted to work in my room. The room had a large TV but the signal was weak and only one channel was easy to view. The wall outlets at the desk were unreliable so my laptop drained and shut off during the night. Oh yeah, and the parking lot takes all comers and fills up so I had to park two blocks away in a city lot. One advantage was that it's just a half block walk to Hollywood Blvd.

“Nice hotel but a few problems” I booked this hotel on Priceline. While I didn't get a huge savings over the regular room price I did save enought to cover the $31 a day parking fee and that was certainly nice. The hotel lobby was very nicely done - large but withouth that convention-like feel that some large hotel lobbies project. Check-in went smoothly and the clerk was very accomodating. Priceline does not guarantee two beds and the clerk went out of his way to find us a double bedded room with a connecting king (I booked two rooms). The rooms themselves were a nice size. They were long but I do wish they were a bit wider from bed to dresser. However, they were very clean and the bathroom was a nice size. The beds were comfy and for there were plenty of pillows on it which I like. There was a flat screen tv and internet service was available for $12.95 a night. Most hotels do not charge for internet access anymore and most even offer wireless access. The bathroom was large and clean. The main problem I had with this hotel was its location. Of course, I knew before I arrived that it was not what I would consider centrally located. It is located near public transportation but it is a good 20 minute walk into Boston proper minimum depending on where you want to go. We were six people and it didn't even pay for us to take public transportation. We drove into Boston and paid for parking. This is supposed to be a 4 star hotel and I hate to sound spoiled but there were just lots of little glitches that I don't usually encounter in hotels of lesser quality. First, the hotel clerk didn't properly activate our room key to give us egress out of the garage so that we got stuck by the exit and had to call upstairs for help. Took a bit of time and then we had to stand in line and have the card activated for a second time. Then our toilet stopped working. Luckily, it was just before we left the room and so we called the front desk and the toilet was fixed when we got back hours later. I have no idea how long it took for a worker to come in and fix the toilet but it could have been a problem if the toilet had broken down late afternoon or during evening hours. When I got my bill, I was charged for a purchase from the honor bar despite the fact that I didn't even have the key for it. I was also charged for the second room -several hundred dollars- even though Priceline makes you pay in full when the room is booked. Hopefully, the problem was rectified at the front desk when I checked out but I won't know for sure until I get my bill. Also, each room is supposed to have a robe but one of my rooms didn't. No big deal but I have a sneaking suspicion that I may end up charged for it even though I informed the hotel clerk that I didn't take it home with me but that it was never in the room to begin with. I just think a four star hotel shouldn't make these kind of mistakes. To sum it all up, the rooms are nice, the price of the hotel is good for Boston but the hotel is a bit isolated and there there are small problems with customer service that one wouldn't expect from a Westin.

“Business Trip, very satisfied, lots of free extras!” I was pleasantly pleased with this hotel for my trip to NY. The breakfast buffet was free, nice selection not just pastries. The wireless Internet was free, and the cheese and wine buffet in the evening was free and excellent! I have stayed at many chain hotels in Manhattan, and this one was very clean, nice decor, great value, and great location. Even though it's a few steps from Times Square, my room was very quiet.

“Quiet and elegance in the heart of Houston” Had an excellent overnight experience at the Magnolia as I was in H-town for a work conference. The hotel has been refurbished but still has the elegant and sturdy feel of a building constructed in the 1920s. Staff was helpful at every time and was most accommodating with the nightly happy hours and breakfast buffet. The rooms were large and clean and my bed was very comfortable. Another pleasant surprise was the peace and quiet in the room. Despite being located in the heart of downtown Houston, you could barely hear a thing outside your window and certainly from the hallways. The bathroom size was ridiculously large and quite comfortable. Oh, the Internet connection – lightning fast. The only two negatives was a bath/shower faucet level not working well and a TV remote which didn’t work at all. Two minor blips really in what was an outstanding experience.

“it's good, but it had better be for the price!” Stayed here for a conference. If you're a first time stayer- there is coupon for free internet in the lobby, but the code also worked on the "wired" internet in the room. It's a big place, be prepared to do some walking to get anywhere! Rooms were nice, but not really fabulous. Lobby was very nice. Starbucks in the lobby as well as a restuarant on site. Lots of rooms for conferences and they were great too. The work out room was very, very nice. Normally there is a charge to use the workout room, but free to Hilton Honors members (hint: if you're not a Hilton Honors member, sign up for free order to save $15 to use the work out room). There is an outdoor pool and hottub on the top of one of hte upper floors. Pool was kind of small for an outdoor pool, but hot tub looked nice. Outside of the hotel you'll likely to run into lots of homeless people sleeping in the streets or asking for hand outs. There are lots of restaurants to choose from in good walking distance. If you just want to pick up some snacks or beer, turn left as you leave the hotel. The liquer store to the left charges about 50% of the price of the liquer store to the right. Nice place to stay, and interesting, but I thought pricey even with the "discounted" conference rate.

“Bring your earplugs” I got a Priceline deal on this hotel -- $60 for a weekend night, which isn't bad for downtown Seattle. It was worth that much, I would say, but if I'd paid full price I wouldn't have been as happy with the value for money. At any rate, I certainly would have asked for a different room on the back of the hotel. The positives: * Location. It's great for downtown Seattle and Capitol Hill, as well as the convention centre. * Decor. The hotel has recently been converted into a Homewood Suites, and the decor is brand spanking new and modern. The room was quite spacious -- bed, couch, large bathroom, decent kitchen. * The bed. The bed was great -- felt just as good as the Westin 'heavenly' beds. * Free breakfast. They even had a buffet with warm food and a waffle maker, which was more than I expected. * Free wi-fi. This is huge -- I hate it when they charge you for this. * Staff. They were friendly when I arrived, offering directions and a map, had I needed it. The negatives: * Noise. This was the one main negative. The hotel sits almost exactly over I-5, the main freeway through town. Rooms on the front aren't well soundproofed, and the traffic doesn't stop at night, so you will hear the sound of cars rushing past all night. It's great that the bed was comfortable, but without earplugs I wouldn't have been able to sleep. * Parking. $25 if you want to park in the hotel's garage. I found free on-street parking (Capitol Hill is generally pretty safe), but it's hard to find at night because residents or people out at the clubs have taken most spaces.

“Location saves it” Got this hotel through priceline for $120 a night so was pleasantly surprised when we checked in to find out we'd been given a corner room on the 26th floor. The room was huge! Massive bed (could have slept 4 very comfortably) and room was very well furnished. Bathroom was tiny (as expected in NY) but I would have loved some counter space for my stuff. No magnifying mirror either, which is unusual and made putting on makeup difficult without my glasses. I would have thought the 26th floor was high enough not to suffer from traffic noise from 42nd st outside the window but I was wrong. The traffic noise was almost as loud as if we were standing outside in it. The window wasn't double-glazed so as well as noise it let in the cold, some mornings there was solid frost on the inside of the window. The room had a/c to heat it up but it was so noisy we could only use it when we were out to heat up the room. 2 electrical sockets in the room were faulty and we didn't report them as we soon learned housekeeping took hours. We requested a sewing kit, and gave up waiting after an hour. One morning we called at 9am to mention that there were room service trays from the night before in the corridoor, they were still there when we returned at 2pm (we called again) and 5pm! These weren't our trays but the smell in the corridoor wasn't pleasant. Housekeeping was very inconsistent, the number and quality of the towels varied every day. Hubby spilt tea on the sheets one morning but they weren't changed that day. The bathroom floor wasn't mopped once during our week, we watched the bootprints add up. The other negative is that the escalator from the lobby to street level broke on Sunday night and they didn't have it fixed until very late on Wednesday night (it was still broken at 7.30pm but working at 1am when we returned). The desk staff were very helpful and the concierge made great dinner recommendations. Complimentary newspapers were delivered to your door weekdays. Having mentioned a lot of negatives, none of these are enough to stop us returning, the location beats them all hands down. All of New York was at our doorstep in Grand Central Station. We'll be back.

“Very nice hotel in good location” The One UN offers a lot compared to similarly priced hotels in Midtown East. The rooms and public space are new, pleasant and clean, if a bit coolly sterile (though not W-like). Most if not all rooms have amazing views, since the hotel occupies floors above 25 and there are no surrounding high buildings (the UN and East River are across First Avenue). There is quiet at night, both indoor and outside, which is a rare thing. The beds are comfortable. Like many NY hotels, the TV is big, new and high def, but the cable service is not hi def; however, there are numerous channels and (since the hotel is across from the UN) a few are in languages other than English. The front desk staff is professional, which is quite welcome compared to several similar NY hotels.
