The lounge has a small coffee shop and bakery with extended hours, as well as bar and restaurant open late and offering room service. Coffeemakers can be requested for the room, although sadly there are no robes (except undoubtedly in the separate pricier West Tower). The hotel has a pool with lovely view, but limited hours. There are the usual NY amenities within a block or two: coffee shops, small food stores, ATMs, etc. The drawbacks include one common to many NY hotels: expensive wifi, charged daily and per device. And one not so common: hand-held (European) shower heads only, at least in our room. It would be nice to see chemical-free soaps/toiletries and (rare to see in any hotel) recycling bins for paper and bottles (though there is the "green" option on linen changes). We two adults were given a room that was allegedly an upgrade from the basic king-bed room, and it was very spacious for NY, with a small sofa and a desk, good-size bathroom, large closet and dressing area, and plenty of space for two people to walk around in. It had a nice River view.

“No Problems” We stayed here 1 night after arriving late to LAX. We had no problem finding a parking spot on the street behind the hotel (free), as I was feeling to cheap to pay for valet. Check-in was a breeze. I requested a room facing south, which was accommodated. The room had plenty of space and was clean, and quiet. The bed was very comfortable. The coffee shop downstairs left a little to be desired with very minimal options for "grab and go" breakfast. I got a great deal on Priceline and would definitely stay here again.

“not that great” This hotel is just OK - It may rate high based on easy access to I-77, and the cheap rate (around $80). The rooms are big- and dirty and the staff is not very friendly. The breakfast amounts to toast and cereal with drinks. It makes a decent stop for a night- but not much more.

“great renovated room!” I stayed at the Doubletree last week and I was in a renovated room on the 32nd floor. It is a great hotel--one of the best business stays I have ever had in NY. (I am comparing to Westins and Sheratons, though.) The cookies on arrival were delicious and they leave yummy chocolates on your pillow at night. The room is spacious enough for a family--with two entrances to the bathroom with two sinks and all new, modern fixtures--with microwave, fridge, and sink in living room area and a large TV too--better than other suite type hotels I have stayed in. Check in was a breeze, breakfast was free (and plentiful and great for families) to Hilton Gold members (with the charge on the statement reading $18 per person waived...), and pleasantly quiet if you are on a high floor. The bed is very comfortable. The only complaint I had was the shower head--it was really weak and sort of irritating. But the maid service was excellent and the elevators come so quickly--even up to high floors--I can't figure out how they do that.

“Nice place, great location” It is an older hotel. The elevated train turns right close by and runs often - so, you do hear it. It is really kind of a neat place, though. If you want luxury, might want to check someplace else. If you want something nice that has an old Chicago feel to it. You might like this place. I will stay here again.

“Great hotel, location is superb” Overall a great hotel, rooms are as expected for a boutique hotel. Check in and check out staff were fast, offering a water or juice is a nice touch. Staff are very friendly. Valet service was fast also. Saturday is very busy at night with two nightclubs in the hotel but the security staff manage the crowds really well

“Brilliant to look at, Brilliant to stay at!” beautifully designed hotel, right from the start you are whisked up an 'Oz like' green lit elevator to a very relaxing lobby maintained by very efficient front desk staff. i stayed for one night in a delux king room that had lots of space to go along with a striking decor. the bed was very comfortable and the powerful AC allowed for a pleasant sleep. the fitness center, located in the sub basement, is open 24 hrs and is bigger than what most city hotels offer. the service from the bellmen and staff is exceptional, i highly recommend this hotel for a columbus circle / central park stay, and the morgans hotel group in general.

“Avoid at all cost!” We chose this hotel only because it was the closest one to Comerica Park which is THE only positive comment about this hotel. It is about a five minute walk between the hotel & Comerica Park but you will probably find yourself running instead of walking. There was not a single building that wasn't abandoned, boarded up, or in need of demoltion and I would include this hotel to be in dire need of all three. The website displays a nice guest room w/ jacuzzi but I believe it is only a model room and not available for rental, except perhaps by the hour. Our room was small, had a 19" TV, and was a couple of doors down from an ice machine that would make a rock concert seem like a library. Here are some of the reasons to avoid this hotel: 1. Our room had a window air conditioner located on the floor that was plugged into an outlet box with exposed conduit. 2. The lamp plugged into this outlet didn't work, nor did one of the lamps next to the bed. 3. The shower pipe was taped to the wall w/ masking tape to prevent any drywall from falling. 4. The stairwell was full of garbage bags, used appliances (a stove & window air conditioners), and gang graffiti. 5. Large sections of the wall (4 ft. x 6 ft.) in the stairwell had broken off. 6. Gated parking because you would be stupid to park your car anywhere else. 7. It is located half a block from the Salvation Army's Transitional Housing building. Avoid this hotel and anything in downtown Detroit. I believe this hotel is a wannabe crack house and you would find better lodging in Baghdad.

“Great 1 night stay” My wife and I, along with another couple had planned a trip to Chicago for a day of bike riding and then a concert at Ravinia. I booked at Orbitz.com and had read many reviews. I paid $150 (Tax included) for a Saturday night stay and I was pleased with the rate. The hotel is right in the loop and only about 4 blocks from union Station. Upon arrival the front desk staff was nice and they stored our bicycles in a secure room at the hotel for free (We did not want to risk leaving them locked onto the bike rack in the parking garage). The room was small, but not bad for a downtown hotel and we basically only were there to sleep. The room was recently remodeled and the bed very comfortable. The windows have a thick pane and we could hear very little street noise. There is no tub in the bathroom, but since we don't use a tub the shower was more than adequate and was a good size. There is free bottled water on every floor, which is nice. The area around the hotel is ok. We walked back to the hotel at about 2am from quite a distance away and never felt unsafe. Overall this hotel is a great value for the money and we would definately stay here again. They do validate parking for a garage about 2 1/2 blcoks away and I paid $19 for the 24 hour stay - not bad for downtown Chicago!.

“It's All About Service” Any hotel can boast a boutique feel, waterfront location, cozy beds and charming furnishings, but a truly spectacular property is once at which the hotel staff is always wondering what they can do to make a guest's stay more special. Harbor Court Hotel's General Manager Jason Stone sets the tone at this waterfront, boutique hotel with his outstanding commitment to customer service. Mr. Stone is truly invested in the well-being of his guests, and he has trained his staff to those same high standards of service. The wine reception and milk and cookies before bed are terrific, but it's the standard of service behind them that makes Harbor Court stand out as a wonderful property. Thanks to the entire staff for an amazing 40th birthday weekend.

“Get ready to Party...” I stayed here with young children and we had a great stay, but this place is meant for people who want a hip, trendy place to stay and want to be close to the action. The location cannot be beat. It is directly across the street from the Convention Center and directly at the entrance of the Gaslamp District; an easy walk to Petco Park and next to the Hard Rock Hotel. This area is party central. First tip: skip the valet parking that is offered for $30+ per night. We parked in a garage at G Street that charges $3 per night on weeknights; $9 per night on weekend nights, plus $1 per hour after 3:00am. Total tab each day was usually $10 for us. Second tip: Weekday happy hour is a great warm up for the night. Excellent complimentary buffet and happy hour drink specials. Children were welcomed in the bar area, but there is also plenty of adjacent lounge space where you can take your food and beverage. This is important because there is often a long wait for dinner at any number of the area restaurants. Third tip: Understand that you are staying in a downtown, urban location with people who want to be in a downtown, urban location. You will hear noise from the railroad tracks and you will know if the people in the room next to you are having an argument. In our case, the people next door were incredibly intoxicated, loud and unruly. They were quickly ejected by the hotel staff (who also comped us for the night because our room was next door). The next morning, I saw housekeeping cleared two empty 32 oz. bottles of Jack Daniels from their room (to give you an indicator). I don't complain about much, but this complaint justified and was ably handled. Next - there is a laundromat about 5 blocks up the street. There were two college basketball team managers doing their laundry there in the morning, so I felt it was a safe, comfortable choice - although obviously there were many "lower caste" users in the area. Many would disagree with me here, but with airlines charging $50 RT to bring anything more than carryon, I thought $6 for doing my laundry was a better value on a two-week trip. Finally, the staff are hit or miss. The hotel has excellent, 5-star quality staff and apathetic, 1-star quality staff. They are pretty easy to tell by their smile (or lack of). Hint: Guests do not exist to provide staff with tips; staff is there to provide guests with excellent service - at which point those who are 5-star will receive generous tips... I have a couple of quick notes after reading previous reviews. First, everything in the downtown area is relatively close and is easily walkable. There is a Hilton Bayfront that is right around the corner for those looking for a more quiet experience and want to stay in the Hilton family and also a Doubletree nearby. That said, all the hotels in this district are within 8 blocks of each other, so there's no reason to pay much more for any one hotel compared to another. Also, be prepared to see homeless people on every block in this area. They are part of the scenery, but not often in your face.

“great way to finish our 2010 vacation” Can only go by our 2 night stay in Dec 2010. The hotel was in a very conveniant location to getting around Houston. The rooms were clean and kept clean. The facilties on offer were very good. The staff we met during the 2 days were indeed a credit to the Marriott group. Would be very happy to stay at this hotel again

“comfortable; quiet; high ceilings; very Kimpton” This was my second stay at the Monaco in Baltimore. I'm a big Kimpton fan and this hotel lived up to the standards I expect from the chain, yet again. Check-in was easy and friendly. My room had very tall ceilings and windows with great views of downtown Baltimore. Comfortable bed. The room was very quiet -- great sleep quality. Huge walk-in shower open to the rest of the bathroom. Valet parking at $36/night was a bit steep for Baltimore, but they were very efficient. As with all Kimpton's, the mini-bar was also stocked with useful items, in addition to food and drink. I forgot to bring toothpaste, and there was Tom's toothpaste in the mini-bar drawer. The bath amenities were aveda (also standard Kimpton), but were in separate bottles and wrapped soaps -- I know that some Kimpton fans prefer the dispensers as green-friendly, but I really like having the individual bottles. Free wi-fi -- one of the reasons I frequent Kimpton hotels.

“Good value hotel” We have stayed at the Warwick several times over the past few years, and I spent the night there on March 25, 2005. The room was fine, with King bed, TV with pay per view movies, and a mini-fridge. Only thing missing was a coffee maker. Nice marble bathroom with hand held shower. The view on the east side of the hotel is the Space Needle, while this time I viewed the 2 Westin hotel towers. The price was right, and I got 10 miles per $ with my AAdvantage card! Only fly in the ointment was the $21 overnight parking charge. I would definately come back, as the location is great.
“Great location, very nice non-smoking hotel” It's tought to find a nice non-smoking hotel in Ft. Worth, but this is a really good one. it's classy and the air is clear. The breakfasts are fantastic!

“Very pleasant. Will be back” Booked Sheraton for one night through hotwire as I extended my stay in Seattle and the Westin was booked out where i had been staying for 5 nights. Really nice hotel. For the price I paid I wasn't expecting a nice room, but the one I was allocated on the 12th floor I was very pleased with. Very comfortable bed, lovely furnishings, really large wardrobe, nice ammenties. Location is great...there is a cheesecake factory right near the hotel, and although I didn't get time to drink there - the lobby bar looked really inviting. I'd definitely stay here again.

“Graceful and elegant but also comfortable.” I've been staying at The Jefferson every year or two for decades. This was the first time I've been there since it's reopened after its renovation. Everything about the renovation is a complete success -- the hotel is simply beautiful. That said, my premium room had a small design problem -- it seemed smaller than the old rooms, and a tad crowded. There was no comfortable place to put a room service table, except to put in directly in front of the side of the bed (it made eating awkward). Also, the tv can only be watched if the cabinet doors are open, but the doors don't "disappear" back into the cabinet.. There is very little room between the bed and the tv cabinet, and it's impossible to walk to the closet, or the door if the cabinet's doors are open (you'd get hit). Also, the desk chair is too low for the desk. I am 5 ft. 6, but still had to prop myself up on a pillow in order to use my computer at the desk. (the free internet is also a plus!). Still, the room was quite lovely, and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was spacious and well equipped. There was a huge and well regulated shower (but no bathtub). The sitting room downstairs is cozy and pretty, and the bar is well staffed, handsome and comfortable. I didn't eat in the restaurant, but I did have room service. The food was good quality, and pricey (as expected), and it was delivered promptly. There was one small mixup with one of my orders, but they fixed it quickly. I did have to call room service nearly two hours after I put my table outside the door because they hadn't picked it up yet (it's a small hotel so I'm guessing this is not usual for them). The staff are efficient and warm enough (the concierge, however, was extremely pleasant and seemed genuine about it). They have a lot of doormen, and yet they were not as attentive as they should have been; I opened my own door on several occasions while the staff chatted with each other. All in all these are minor quibbles, but worth noting because the hotel is nearly perfect. I did stay in other hotels while The Jefferson was being renovated, but I will be back at The Jefferson from now on.

“Good ole Dependable Embassy Suites” We have stayed at the Embassy Suites Philadelphia airport aboiut 10 times nowso you can see we like it. It really is Good ole Dependable! Service is very good. Cooked to order free breakfast, managers free cocktail party with fresh popcorn, an exercise room, pool, free shuttle to and from the airport just 2 miles away and fly and park on site parking make this just Good ole Dependable. We recommend it to your for all of the above reasons.

“Fabulous! Bring your wallet!” We stayed here in 2007, loved it so much, came back for more! We had another excellent stay. Room was beautiful, and gotta love the Ritz cleanliness. Pros: +Excellent location in SF--close to Chinatown and Union Sq. shopping, cable cars, and just a 10 minute taxi ride to Wharf or AT&T Park. +The rooms are amazing--I would book a larger room if you can. Their standard room is a bit small, but it is a city hotel. +Love their lobby lounge +Also loved their breakfast options. +Plenty of bottled waters--in the room, in the a.m. in the lobby. Some Cons: +If you rent a car, the valet parking is steep ($71/day). +Some areas of the Ritz are very good (concierge, gift shop, room service). The Spa continues to disappoint me--surly desk clerk (she practically scolded me for being 20 minutes early for my appt.--god forbid, I just want to relax and read a magazine), so-so service, big price tag. +Valet service is also a disappointment--they only seem to be available when you are checking in or leaving (they must smell the guaranteed tips). We always hailed our own cab or grabbed one right in front of the hotel without their help. When you want to treat yourself, come here!!

“Too grimy for me!” Hotel location is terrific! We were in town to see Young Frankenstein with our teenage boys. Walking distance to Grand Central station, Times Square, Rockefeller Center. Lobby is spectacular. But I'm afraid that's all I can say was pleasant about our stay. We had trouble with check-in (they gave us a king when we clearly stated 2-doubles); however the front desk fixed that pretty quick. We were charged "going rate" despite the fact our reservation through Expedia was at least $100 less when we booked. Still working on getting that hashed out. The biggest problem is, the hotel is just plain dirty. I travel alot and am used to some level of the hotel "scroungies" but this one really was bad. Granted the hotel is in the heart of the city, but there's really no excuse for unswept/unwashed bathroom floors, peeling/stained wallpaper, or other people's left-behind hair clips (in the middle of the floor -- not even squirreled away under a bed). Rarely do I require my kids to wear their shoes 24-7 when walking on a hotel floor, but this was one hotel that we did. It was a rainy night on our visit, so we opted to head to the hotel lounge for a nightcap. The couches in there were dirtier and more stained than those in my son's baseball clubhouse! Seriously! The tables were not wiped between visits so we got to "enjoy" the person before us leftover french fries and salt mess -- both on the table and on the floor under our feet (lots there!). Next time we're in the City, I'll definitely look elsewhere!

“Wouldn't stay there again” Good: Great lobby. Good spot for conferences. Good location near touristy area - alamo, river walk. Wireless internet had good strong signal in room. LCD TV was good. Staff was helpful and friendly. Hotel bar was comfortable, had live music nightly. Bad: Still under construction (April 2008). Woken up before 7 am daily by jackhammers. Kept up late at night by terrible looped smooth techno music coming from pool area (had to call down to ask them to turn it off). Asked for feather free room and sloppy removal job was done. Bad room layout, including strange closet door. Bathroom was pretty rough looking and not very clean. (Staff -spend less time making toilet paper triangles and more time actually sweeping the floor.) Conference catering did not provide easy access to ingredients of meals and my Spanish was not good enough so I accidentally ate something I was allergic to and spent an afternoon on benadryl.

“Can I move in? Please” I did not want to leave. I Love the plaza. The service is amazing. We had a suite and it was one of those experiences where you walk in the room and you feel like a little kid again. Giant chandelier, heated bathroom floors, big fluffy bed. Hooray! The hotel itself is beautiful and the location is unbeatable. At the time there was not much of a gym as it is currently being built but with central park across the street and 5th avenue a few steps away there are better ways to exercise. Check out the food hall. It was very good and the options were endless. If you have a chance to stay at the plaza take it, you will not regret it. - we booked through New York luxury hotels (Magellan) which every time we book through we have a great experience. -wifi was fast and good cell service (AT&T)

“Good value” The Ramada was clean and comfortable, and very reasonably priced. The included breakfast was much better than the standard continental breakfast at similar hotels. Service was courteous and helpful. I would certainly return to this hotel if the occasion arose.

“Lucerne was okay” Just got back from a weeks stay at the Lucerne. Everyone from the doorman to the front desk was very nice. I had booked a double queen suite and asked for a quiet room on arrival. Was given a room on the 3rd floor in the back- no view but very quiet- until Monday when we found that several of the rooms next to ours were being renovated- as in gutted. Electric saws and hammering and the smell of paint. Now the front desk did offer to move us but since it meant repacking everything( I had unpacked everything since it was so quiet on Sun.) we decided to stay put. . We were usually out of the room during the day and the work stopped at 5pm. Just wish we had been informed before hand that there was construction. The beds were very comfortable, we all slept great. Air conditioner worked very well. Had no problems w the internet service. The sitting room was quite small and only had 2 chairs. The bathroom was small but not tiny. Maid service was spotty,the floor was not vacuumed the entire week, toiletries such as soap were not always replaced. The location can't be beat- close to subway, lots of restaurants and I felt very safe. I would stay again but would make sure that my room was not near any renovations

“An Interesting Approach to Relatively Inexpensive Comfort” Aloft Harlem is modern, convenient, has an absolutely delightful staff, and is comfortable. Apparently the Aloft concept (there are some 50 hotels in the group) is Starwood's alternative to Comfort, Days, and other 'Inns' -- and as such, is a superior approach. The hotel fits a lot into a small space. Our room was small, but efficiently designed, and thus perfectly comfortable. Nice touches like free bottles of water (unlike other hotels that charge outrageous amounts). The bar is modern and welcoming with a very upscale diverse clientele. My own personal minor frustration was the lack of skin lotion among the bathroom amenities. But the free wi-fi in a good Manhattan hotel certainly was a worthwhile trade-off. The staff is truly outstanding. Definitely worth more visits.

“Great hotel & location ! Will stay there again!” We stayed at the Hampton in on Dec. 19th and Dec.20th. We used our Hilton Honors points and stayed for free. We chose this hotel based upon location, parking, and the morning breakfast. This hotel is a great location for people with children. The room we stayed in was larger than one we stayed in at a Holiday Inn downtown. It easily accommodated 2 adults and 2 elementary school children. The room is slightly smaller than an average hampton inn but larger than other NY hotels. The room was very clean and the area of town was nice ( not dumpy looking). It was fairly quiet at night. We were on the 5th floor and the 8th street side. We didn't hear any street noise. We did hear the occasional emergency vehicle; however it was very quiet. Next door to the Hampton Inn is a parking garage. We were able to park our car there and leave it without a problem. Hampton Inn will validate your parking card and give you a discount. The location was great for us. There is a subway stop across the street; however, we never took the subway. There is a CVS next door to the hotel. We were one block away from Mars 2112 ( 51st and 7th). This was a fun place to eat with the children. We walked to Times Square and to Rockefeller center. It was several blocks but we were able to do it with our children. We just made stops along the way... the m&m's store, the hershey store, the FDNY store etc. There is also a Food Emporium across the street with sandwiches etc. We also walked to the musical we saw. We saw In the Heights. I chose a Hampton Inn not only because we used our Hilton Honor points and got it for free but because they offer breakfast. It is a real expense and pain to have to search for breakfast when you are with kids. It was great that we were able to wake up and go downstairs and eat. They had hot/cold cereals, coffee, hot chocolate, toast, pastries, english muffins, juice, fruit, waffles, yogurt, meat, and eggs. We did take a cab to the Empire State building and that cost $8 and that included a $2 tip. I highly recommend this hotel and plan to stay there again when we go to New York.

“Great Property and Service” We stayed here before flying out on a trip along with leaving a car for 10 days. They had a very nice clean room, good check in service and a great price from their website. We left our car for the entire trip. Shuttle service was good both going to the airport and returning. Nice little bar with food in the hotel along with a decent breakfast area. Overall - I would stay here anytime before flying out of the Indy airport for a trip!

“Decent Hotel” I have been trying all different hotels in the Seattle area. The next hotel in my lineup was the Silver Cloud Hotel. The location was a bit outside of the city. Technically, it is in Seattle, but definitely not walking distance to the city center. The lobby was busy, I checked in just after 5pm and there was a seminar still going on in a large conference room. Connected to the lobby is a restaurant with full bar. There is an onsite parking garage for $20 per night. My room was spacious, complete with a microwave and refrigerator. Out my window was a great view of Seattle University across the street. The hotel was quiet at night. I didn't hear a peep all night. Comfortable, clean beds with several different pillow types. The bathroom was typical with upscale toiletries. This hotel was decent, if it was located in the heart of the city, I would stay here all the time.

“Great stay” Great overall trip to Sheraton Mission Valley. Booked with SPG points for 1 night and points and cash a second, so had 2 different reservations. Easy check in and no need to check out and back in. Arrived early to the hotel (9AM), and was able to be checked into the room. PROS: Location and easy access to all areas of San Diego Great updated room with huge LCD Staff was great, not one complaint. everyone was nice, pleasant and helpful CONS; Pool is basic, could use some jazzing up. They have towels on the chairs and extras there Parking. $14 a day to park? Really? In that area? What they don't tell you is there is free parking along the side of the hotel and in the back. Used that the 2nd night. No worries, no charge for parking at all at check out. All in all a great stay and would recommend if you konw the area.

“Gerade neu, noch nicht ganz auf dem Hyatt Standard” Richtigerweise muss man sagen, es handelt sich um ein Franchise Hotel, nicht um ein eignes Hyatt. Dennoch ist man auf dem Weg den H Standard zu erreichen und zu halten. Die Lage ist perfekt. An der Lexington Av. und der 48. Strasse gelegen und direkt neben dem Marriott EastSide und gegenüber dem Waldorf Astoria. Von der Einrichtung und Ausstattung eher einem modernen Boutique Hotel entsprechend, allerdings sind die Standardzimmer wohl sehr klein. Mein Corner Room, welcher mit zwei getrennten Räumen zum Wohnen und schlafen ausgestattet war, war dieses nicht. Daher kann ich das nicht beurteilen. Dieser hatte sogar eine kleine Küche, einen Geschirrspüler und eine Mikrowelle. Dazu eine Nespressomaschine im Zimmer.

“Simply a Great Hotel for the Location” We stayed here at the end of an 8 day trip along the Front Range of the Rockies, and all in all, it was the best property. I think Marriott has finally turned itself around and developed a series of mid-range priced options, including Springhill Suites. This property is simply immaculate and very, very nicely appointed, from the lobby to the hallways to the rooms. The breakfast was excellent - the OJ tasted like fresh-sequeezed (not the watered down swill at Hampton Inns), the oatmeal already prepared (not cheesy little packets and some hot water like at most Comfort Inns and Hampton Inns), with several hot items. They even had Dannon Activa yogurt! The complimentary shuttle to DIA leaves every 30 minutes, with a sign-up sheet the night before. It also stops at the nearby Fairfield Inn (funny that there is also a Courtyrad by Marriott also right nearby). You get to the terminal in about 10 minutes. The shuttle driver was very kind and courteous. My only real complaint was that the window AC unit was quite loud, but the window opens just enough to get some fresh air. Also the non-fitted mattress cover kept sliding on the plastic surface of the mattress cover underneath it. Odd when moving around in bed to be sliding around! This is an aiport property and as such it is not at all convenient to the downtown or other tourist sites in Denver, let alone Golden or Boulder, even with a car. There are a handful of chain restaurants within walking distance pf the hotel but nothing fancy or unique. There is a cozy little bar in the hotel for a nightcap -- the bartender was a real conversationalist. One last thing - the property is at the intersection of Tower and 68th Avenue - the Google Map and GPS directions are WRONG! Take the Tower road exit off Pena Expressway and turn right or drive straight north on Tower from I-70. You also cannot get back on Pena heading south to I-70.

“Good location” My husband and I stayed at this hotel for three nights. Pros: location, location, location Cons: - poor quality of service (we couldn't even find a person to asssit us to find a cab. finally after 10 minutes of looking for assistance, a door boy suggested us to take an "unautorized cab".) - Heating system in the room was not functioning well. It was very cold at night and woke up several times at night. I would recommend this hotel if you would like to stay in Times Square area and do not care much about the quality of services.

“Excellent Hotel - Exceeds expectations” I have stayed here twice in the last few months for over 10 nights in total. This is now my preferred hotel in the Galleria area and I pick it over and above the more expensive hotels. The rooms are comfortable and clean, the staff helpful. The location is much quieter than you would expect, being so near the loop. The laundry service is efficient and of good value. The only thing that is really missing is an in room safe. I tend to go for HHonors hotels. I have stayed in many other HHonors hotels in the area and the combination of price, convenience and service make this particular Hampton the best hotel for me in the area.

“Lovely hotel but expensive!” I stayed here for 3 nights in July 2012 with my boyfriend. Our flight into Philadelphia was early so we were there too early to check in. However they held our bags for us and said the room would be ready in 3 or 4 hours. (we were there at 10am). We asked if they would call our cell phone when the room was ready but we were told that wasnt possible and to check back in a few hours. We didnt mind too much but it would've been nice if they called us when the room was ready. We found the concierge very helpful with any questions we had. He gave us some great recommendations for visiting the Amish country in Lancaster county. The hotel itself is very clean and fresh. Our room was lovely and comfortable with excellent comfortable beds. The hotel is located in the heart of the city. Very central to the 'hop on hop off' bus route. We didnt eat in the restaurant as the menu was extremely expensive and we had a drink in the bar one night, again very expensive.

“Great Staff, Cozy Rooms, Actually Spacious for NYC” The guy staffing the front desk was very helpful in getting me situated and recommend a few nice options for dinner. He was very informed about the neighborhood. The rooms are modern but not in an overly trendy way, more in a clean practical way. Unlike most mid priced hotels in New York, I did not feel cramped at all. Good high speed internet. Great area. In the morning the staff was so helpful in directing me to places where I could do my errands. I really have a problem with front desk staff in NYC sometimes being rude or uninformed, not the case here. Good job Guys!

“New Austin gem...” As soon as I valet parked here I knew it would be one of the hotels that I now prefer in Austin. The room was cozy, clean and comfortable. Our meetings took course over a couple of days so I had the opportunity to sample some of the 'in house' menu at all three restaurant options that they have. The breakfast and lunch buffet downstairs at The Carillon was a bit pricey but I must admit so delicious. Grilled pineapple, pasta, and sandwiches had me coming back for more. The 125 coffee shop had me drinking coffee everyday even though I dont really like coffee. Tried a muffin there it was huge but also tasty. Gabriels Cafe was the highlight of my whole trip...the sweet chili wings were so good..I skipped dinner the last day and had them again. They are to die for! One day, we had fire alarms going off at 4:30 in the morning. That wasn't great seeing all of my coworkers coming out in their skippies. Besides that it was an enjoyable stay and I already recommend the hotel to other travelers who havent really heard about it. It's also conveniently located close to food, bars, and UT!

“Very nice hotel!” We stayed here May 13 for a quick getaway! We did our research and heard some really good, and some really bad things about this hotel. Well....having stayed, I'm glad we did! Upon pulling up in our car, we were immediately greeted by both the valet and security. They were prompt and courteous (not sure what happened to those other reviewers who said they were not there). We then walked through a very chic lobby (modern and dark...very urbane and tastefully done). Check-in was prompt (and our schnauzer, Rudy loved the treats given by the receptionist!). The room was also very tastefully decorated! The bed was quite comfortable (I'm usually a fan of Westin's Heavenly bed) but this was close in level of comfort. Lots of nice touches like the large mirror on the side wall, subtle but nice wallpaper, DVD player in room, etc. The bathroom was also quite nice. The sink was really cool to look at. In terms of practicality, I felt sorry for the maid, as the water splashs around the sides and back of it. Great Aveda bath products! We did not dine at the hotel, so we cannot comment on that. The pool area was actually very nicely done as well! Pool is smallish, but the deck area has a bar, fire pits for the evening, etc. Again, very chic...very nice! I'd give this an excellent rating, except that there was one flaw with this hotel. The walls...they're paper-thin! There is nothing worse than being awakened at 2AM by your neighbors doing...well...adult things! To the hotel's credit, apparently these people in the room next to us were SO loud that they were asked to leave, according to the front desk. So at least they addressed the issue (and I don't think that a hotel should bare the blame for irresponsible adults who stay there). So all in all...we would definately return!!

“Amazing location!!” This has to be one of the best locations in NYC. Beautiful hotel overlooking Central Park. Convenient walking distance to everything in midtown. Nice rooms and friendly staff. We booked using a winter promo code offered on their website, so it was even reasonably priced for a hotel of this caliber.

“Not My Idea of Cool” This was a one-night impromtu stay, my flight back to Paris having been cancelled at the last minute, I felt lucky to find a decent place to stay in busy NYC. Reservation over the phone went well, for a King room (whatever stupid name they may call it) on the top floor. When I actually turned up 10 minutes later, the top floor had changed into a 4 th floor. I traded it for a double room on the 14th (1407), upgraded or sa I was told. However, all-in-all check-in was efficient and prompt, despite a blaring music, that also blared in the elvators. Very quiet despite being right across the elevators, and right over Union Square. Tha main noise was actually the wind whistling through both window frames. This was my second stay in a W, previous being San Francisco. It is less cool than San Francisco. Rooms are ok, slightly worn : he heavenly bed is there, but it should be changed. Carpets look old. , and the bathrooms have clearly been re-used from the previous hotel in the buiding. Not even close to trendy. But they work, which is the least thet can do, with poor water pressure in the shower. I remembered great Aveda toiletries, and they are now Bliss, totally unattractive in style. Bar area was dark, music blaring again. Overnight laundry was good, and right on time, eventhough I had cheked in past the time. I tried to have breakfast downstairs at 9.30 am, but no seating was available, and I was requested to ask for 15 minutes, which I did not care of. I ordered from room service. I am not one to discuss prices, but they were extortionate : large orange juice, coffee, one single bagel and a side of smoked salmon set me back $50, which I found steep, evethough they were truly delicious. After checking the menu, I realised that the cream cheese had not made it to the room, and the salmon had been charged three times. I stated this at c/out, and they removed more than they should have at once. The bellman looked like he could not be bothered when I requested my 3 small pieces of luggage to be stroed for the day. Also the guys hopping taxis seemed to prefer discussing tips and enjoying themselves rather than opening the doors and actually hopping taxis. As often in NYC, the attitude issue stays with the lowest employees, and I am easy goiongand rather friendly.

“Great room, great service, great location” Everyone at this hotel did an absolutely outstanding job. Pulled up in a cab and greeted immediately by Danny with valet. Not only did he quickly take care of our bags but he also gave a quick tour of the large lobby and advice on local events going on in the city during our stay. Room was large and clean, very comfortable bed. Room service was quick and polite. Hotel is in a great location, easy walk to the market and restaurants. Fitness was adequate, did not use indoor pool but it looked nice. The staff in the fitness center also did a great job making sure we had plenty water, clean towels etc. Check out was fast and easy. Only one complaint, it would have been nice if the desk in the room had more outlets on top so you don't have to crawl under it to plug in your devices and chargers. Ended up using outlet in bathroom for cell charger. Other than that, there's really nothing else to criticize. Will definitely return.

“Not the "Presidential" Suite but Enough Room to Maintain your "Independence” We stayed in room 485 at the Washington Jefferson Hotel November 19-22, 2007 while in NYC for the 81st Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. We paid $177 a night through Priceline. The hotel is located on 51st St between 8th & 9th Aves which is a great location, there are many delis, Duane Reeds (NYC drug store) & restaurants with in walking distance; Times Square is about a block or 2 away. There is also a subway stop one block from the hotel. The front desk staff were professional & friendly; they offered us a map of the area & a complimentary copy of the New York Times upon check-in. I’ve stayed in many NYC hotels & I must say this was probably the smallest room I’ve stayed in yet. However, it was clean with modern décor & fine for me & my husband. The room had a nice flat screen TV on the wall, a desk, & a mini armoire/closet which also contained a safe, an iron & board, & 2 shoe mitts. The queen size bed was comfortable; however the outside noise level was very high. Our room was facing 51st street which provided a nice view of the quaint street below, however, due to the window mounted air conditioner, it sounded like a window was open but they were all closed. This wasn’t a big issue to us because we’re used to city noise but for those who are not, it will probably be a big issue. A few of the nice room features were an iPod dock on the nightstand and copies of New York IN magazine & Time Out New York magazines which list all of the goings on for the week in NYC. Complementary in-room internet service was also provided. Wireless was supposed to be available but every time we tried to connect to the wireless we had problems logging on, we even asked the front desk who referred us to the service providers customer service line which was unable to help us. We were however, able to connect using the wall connection cable in the room (cables are in the desk drawer in the room). The bathroom was VERY small, but again, it was clean with modern décor. The stand up shower had good water temperature & pressure. Complementary bath products included Gilchrist & Soames Forest Essentials shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, body wash, facial soap, oatmeal bath soap, shower cap, & a little kit containing cotton balls, q-tips & a nail file. I found the sink to be a bit awkward; the faucet was rather large & right in the middle of the sink so it got in the way when washing ones face. The Washington Jefferson hotel is a nice hotel in a great location however, due to the small room size I most likely would not stay there again or recommend it to others (unless the price is right). While in NYC I would recommend having lunch at S’mac in the East Village (345 E. 12th St between 1st & 2nd Aves) it’s a terrific neighborhood restaurant that serves different versions of mac & cheese. After lunch make your way to Little Italy & have one of Caffé Palermo’s “best cannolis on planet earth”. Enjoy your stay in NYC!

“The worst Westin I've stayed in...” The appearance from the outside is striking, with 4 tall circle towers and one lower center one. Once you enter, the place is a maze! The towers are assigned by color, so you got to pay attention to the signs, otherwise, you will be going in circles trying to find your way around. And there is no elevator access from certain floors (weird! How about handicapped people?) The lobby/bar area is nice, with fountains and water ponds all around. There are plenty of restaurants and stores in the mezzanine level. Now, as for the rooms, this is where the level of a "Westin" hotel goes down the toilet... The staff is great, specially the concierges.. I needed to rent a car and he was very helpful calling every single car rental agency downtown to get a car for us. Very nice indeed! The rooms are totally outdated, caught up in the 70's time warp... I hope they do have some plans to remodeled because the rooms are just disgusting! The bathrooms were disgusting, the furniture had broken drawers and multiple scratches accumulated throughout all the decades they have been there... and the carpet? YUK! I had white sports socks on for a couple of hours and they were black by the time I took them off. The bedding... would not even dare to touch the bed spread... The carpet had a iron burn mark, the colors are like the 70/80's and the window curtains are just dusty and ugly. Lets just say, I hope the management of this hotel has room upgrade plans soon... the only reason why they stay in such good business? The name "Westin" and the big groups that have convention and meetings after meetings in the hotel. The only problem with check-out? They charge parking day rate to the room when it was paid in cash at the parking garage... however, the front desk staff took it off the bill right away and gave us a credit. Nicely done! The Final Verdict: Lobby/Reception Area: 4.0 / 5.0 Hotel Amenities/Facilities: 4.0 / 5.0 Staff friendliness/responsiveness: 5.0 / 5.0 Room Decor/Ambiance: 0.0 / 5.0 Room cleanliness: 1.0 / 5.0 Room Amenities: 2.0 / 5.0 Bed Comfort: 1.5 / 5.0 Hotel Bar: (not used) Hotel Restaurant: (not used) Check-in/out Speed: 4.5 / 5.0 Total Score: 22 / 40 ( 55 out of 100% or F Grade) Final Comment: The hotel lobby area is very nice with a bar serving food, Starbucks coffee and well-drinks. Many water fountains and ponds all around. However, the rooms are the worst I've stayed at any Westin Hotel. I've had better decorated, cleaned and more comfortable rooms in cheaper hotels. They must renovate the rooms soon.

“Great Location, Great Service, Very Nice Rooms” My title says it all. My wife and I stayed here a 3 days 2 nights, the weekend before her birthday trip, before heading out on a cruise departing Manhattan Terminal. They allowed us to check in early and upgraded our room to a corner suite (after mistakenly giving us a room that was still being serviced by the house keeping). It was really no inconvenience at all, but they upgraded us for making that small mistake. The bell hops were very helpful and handled all our luggage and even filled our ice bucket after showing us to our room. Room was clean and VERY VERY ROOMY, in comparison to other NY hotels. Front desk staff is very friendly and efficient. SERVICE A++ Location is perfect, close enough to walk to almost everything, Radio City, Rockafeller, Central Park, Time Square ... But far enough away from the noise and madness. Or if you prefer hop on the 6 train (same block) down to Flatiron, NoHo, SoHo, Union Square, East Village, or Chinatown. Will definitely stay here next time.

“Great for families with children, not so much for business stay” Very good location for getting to many sights of DC, room was clean, recently renovated. Did not like having to pay so much for in room internet service, have stayed at DC hotels in the past where it is free. Our bedroom area was quiet, but hallway and living room noisy with constant running & yelling of children. Impossible to get a table at breakfast time, lots and lots of families with young children. Staff was friendly,& helpful.

“One of the better Four Points if you're keeping track” I requested an early check in and was able to book a "Starpicks" rate online that I thought was an excellent value. They were accom at the front desk even though it was very early and I didn't really care about the Starwood VIP floor unavailability. The room was clean and I had no issues with street noise or getting to and from LAX. And as a final note, how refreshing not to see "Fixed" (Fox) news on the channel selection. GOOD CHOICE!

“Huge hotel, great location” The thing that struck me first about the Westin Seattle is how massive it is. The twin towers stand out in the city's skyline and take up pretty much a whole city block. The lobby is also expansive and possibly confusing, but once you find your way around, this is a really great place to stay. The round towers mean the rooms are pie-shaped, so they seem cramped when you first enter, but open up in the bedroom area. Our room on the North Tower's 40th floor had a fantastic view of the Space Needle, the Puget Sound and the snow-capped mountains beyond. Of course it had the awesome Heavenly Bed and dual showerheads, a big flatscreen TV and a nice desk positioned right in front of the window. I give the place only four stars for cleanliness, however, since it appeared that a previous guest had pressed his or her butt cheeks against the glass of the window; the marks remained there throughout our two-day stay. We found it humorous but another guest might find it disgusting. Location couldn't be better: five blocks to the waterfront and Pike Place Market, two blocks to shopping and the monorail that leads to the Space Needle. Service was great and the concierge desk was well-prepared to answer several questions. Just a couple of complaints: Valet parking is (predictably) insanely expensive, and the small Internet lounge charges $7 for 15 minutes of Internet usage (though you can print out boarding passes for free). Also, at least on the 40th floor, the wind whips and the building creaks and moves perceptibly, so be prepared. Otherwise, great place to stay.

“Nothing short of AMAZING!” I stayed at the Omni Dallas Downtown on July 4th & 5th and it was wonderful. Check in was a breeze and the gentleman at the front desk was incredibly helpful. My room was on the 21st floor and I could see for miles and miles from the solid wall of windows in my room. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've slept in. The shower was a huge walk in shower with adequate water pressure. And the electric mirror in the bathroom with the tv in it was really cool. I didn't visit the restaurants other than the sports bar. Ordered a burger to go and it was very tasty. Drinks were a little pricey in the bar, but I expected that. I will stay at this Omni every time I go to Dallas in the future.

“Poor/Average is about right .. Isolated and Dated” Other reviews sum it up nicely, and I'm struggling with 2 or 3 stars for my rating. However: 1. Hotel is dated. The room design is straight out of the 1980s and many cosmetic/maintenance issues. i.e. rusty shower vent, loose shower head, air con hard to control, walls thin. etc. 2. It's far from everything of value. All the sights/any food are a $15-30 cab ride and 15-30min cab ride ... plus this Hyatt is an area you do not want to around in alone. 3. Construction noise. They are building a new tower next door but any rooms that face said tower hear really loud noise starting as early as 7am! That's just not right in a hotel. 4. Food is average at best, with some items awful. Due to its isolation, any quick meals are eaten there, and the Italian takeaway place was never open during my stay, the coffee takeaway was eh and the sit-down coffee shop was just not good. 5. Service is one good thing. Most staff are very friendly. However, I tried to call the conceirge one night for advice and they never picked up multiple times. 6. The last good thing is cleanliness. The rooms are clean from dust, but again multiple maintenance issues. Also A+ for beds. There are much, much better options in Chicago and I'd take any of those places next time. Maybe the renovation will help, but the noise will only get worse in the interim and the location just is not good for Chicago sightseeing. I won't be back anytime soon. The weak points far outweigh the positive,

“Serviceable and Affordable in DC” Got this place over Priceline. The rooms are not huge, but they get the job done. Bathroom is kind of small. Location is good; near Dupont Circle and lots of cool shops. About a 5-10 minute walk to the Dupont Circle Metro stop.

“Great views and beds!” We stayed for 2 nights and had a twin room on the corner of floor 39 with great views although we were overlooking ground zero which was noisy but fine with ear plugs. Beds v comfy, great shower and tea and coffee making. No fan in the bathroom which was very steamy, but overall, great especially with star bucks just downstairs!

“High marks but some IF's” All in all I think this hotel rates some high marks. It’s convenient to many attractions and transportation. Has a large garage for on-site parking (they charge but most hotels in SF do). The lobby is well kept and upscale. They have a restaurant and with a lounge which is pretty good. Room service till 10pm. They have a business center that allows you to print a boarding pass however you pay if you want to print anything else or surf. In the room you have the option of the slower, free internet but if you'd want faster service they have a paid option. Even though the property is older (as are most buildings in SF) it is kept up well. Carpeting is good as are the bathroom fixtures. Bed and bedding are above average. Not a great channel lineup. Soda machines on every other floor but no snack machines. Another if: If you get a regular room you won’t be disappointed. I've stayed twice and came back again. But if you check in later when they are full, you will get....an elevator room! Each floor has 4 rooms which bookmark the elevators. The room is actually L-shaped built around the elevator shafts. It’s not over-powering, but you do hear it. The quirk: They don't tell you this on check-in. If they were straight forward and say we have a room with a negative they could offer a drink ticket or a meal discount to make up for it a bit. But they say nothing and just hope you don't say anything. If you mention it, they just say "That’s all we have available". Mentioning it ahead could also allow you to choose another location. A side note: When I did mention it the desk clerk said the hotel is aware of this negative and turns the corner elevators off at 10pm. She was in fact correct BUT I noticed only the elevator on my corner was off. I actually rode 2 of the others after 10pm. So perhaps they will cut them off only if someone complains? Otherwise, if you’re happy, they are happy? Going forward I will ask the occupancy status if I know I will be checking in late and if they say they are full that night I will probably cancel the reservation instead of taking a chance.

“Perfect Location for LA” Wanting to stay a night in LA, I looked for a Hilton where I can use my points. If you are a member of Hilton Honors, you know that your points don't buy too much so you want to use points and cash if you can. The Hilton Checkers popped up as the perfect hotel both in location and points needed. They only have valet, so you have to pull up to the front door of the hotel and have the attendant park your car. This sets you back $35 a day. My wife noticed afterwards that the next entrance past the front door they had all night parking for $25. Oh well. Maybe if we were going to stay longer. We were put on the 10th floor. First of all, they keep this hotel in top notch condition. The lobby and hallways were spotless. Our room was also spotless and very well appointed. The bathroom was larger than expected. The valet told us to be sure to visit the top floor where they have the pool and jacuzzi. Unfortunately we didn't have a chance to see it until the next morning, but it was also very nice. The pool is small, but perfect for a few. It also has great views, which you can see many of the large downtown buildings, including the Bonaventure. I would definitely recommend this place for nights stay.

“Very welcoming!” Third, (or fourth?) stay at Muse, March 5-11, 2009. A welcoming and comfortable stay, as in the past. Liked the new decor of the rooms which are large and CLEAN! Beds are wonderful! Yes, the lobby was under construction, but didn't impact my stay, (wish I could have stayed a day later to see the new one unveiled!). staff was very helpful and accommodating, especially the door staff! Continental Breakfast was a nice bonus - my only suggestion would be to have coffee makers in the rooms. Location could not be more perfect.

“Nice boutique hotel, but service could be better” Location: A short walk to Fifth Avenu and two blocks to the closest subway stop makes this a good place to stay to get around. For my next visit to NY however, I would prefer a hotel close to Central Park or East/West Village or Soho where I find the dining options better. Rooms: Spotless and very clean. The size was okay judging by New York standards, but the cupboard made the room feel a bit cramped. The street view was nice, especially at night. Service: Staff were courteous and very helpful, but on several occasions there were no staff available for assistance. This happened at the reception, the bellman, doorman and concierge. On the other side I was very happy about the way they got me a fixed price taxi to the airport when leaving. I spent bonus points on my 5 night stay at Renaissance Hotel 57, but I think the rate was around $340 at that time. At this price level I do believe there are better options in New York, though I stress that I was not unhappy about the stay.

“Great hotel less than a mile from CLT airport” I stayed here prior to a flight out of CLT because of the high reviews here on Tripadvisor. I was not disappointed! I was greeted with a professional staff and the room was very nice, and appeared to be fresh and new. When asking about places to eat, the staff said that Carraba's delivered directly to the room. WOW! There was also pizza delivery as well. I enjoyed ordering Carraba's and it arrived within the hour. The neighborhood overall was rather dicey looking, and I did not see any restaurants on the way from the highway, so I was quite happy with the in-room delivery. I did not take advantage of the shuttle service or the breakfast, but both were available. I will definitely stay here again if I have an early flight out of Charlotte. Overall VERY impressive Hampton Inn and stay.

“Another great stay at the Chancellor” This is my fourth stay at the Chancellor over the past 5 years. Still doesn't disappoint. No problems with a late, after midnight, check-in. Room not huge, but more that adequate. Same with bathroom. Maid service excellent, with room and bathroom always kept clean. This is not a modern chain hotel with all mod cons. More of a boutique style hotel - a bit old fashioned, but clean, comfy with a homely feel. Some welcome bonuses included the Macy's discount card, hotel bar 2for1 drinks voucher and the free wi-fi available throughout the hotel. In addition are the free coffee and cookies available around the clock in the lobby area. Considering this hotel is in the middle of down town, right on Union Square, room rates are more that reasonable. Note that this hotel does not have in room AC. This did not turn out to be a problem. There is a multi speed fan hanging from the ceiling, and the windows can be opened. My only suggestion for improvement would be the addition of an in-room fridge and tea/coffee making facilities. Would definitely recommend this hotel and this would still be my first choice on any future visit to San Francisco.

“Good hotel, good service, and location” Pleasantly surprised with this location. While it is located less than a block from Times Square, I was expecting to have a closet of a room but actually ended up being pleasantly surprised with the size of the room, the quietness of the hotel, and decent service. Don't get me wrong - this is no Plaza Hotel.

“Barely average” Rooms are very small even though they call them suites. Wireless internet was so weak that they might as well not have it. The wall are thin so you can hear everything in the rooms next door. Road noise is also an issue.

“Nice hotel good location” Very comfortable room. No coffee maker in room. This hotel (like many) has gone to beds with duvet covers but no top sheet (why???). Good service, large workout facility, nice view of lake.

“Awesome Hotel and Awesome Location” Stayed here for 1 night (wish it could have been more) in August while on vacation in Baltimore. Our goals were to see the Inner Harbor, Fort McHenry, the Babe Ruth Birthplace museum, and of course and Orioles game. The location was perfect - you can't find a better location to Camden Yards - it's right across the street. The Babe Ruth museum was only about 4 short blocks from the hotel as well. The Inner Harbor was about 8 blocks away, not a bad walk though, it was well traveled and felt safe. We drove to Ft. McHenry the next morning on the way out of town. Net - the location is fantastic, especially if you are going to a game. The hotel itself was great - in very nice condition, very clean, and the rooms for a Hampton were nice sized. Ours was large enough to have the queen bed and a sofa bed pulled out, and still plenty of room to walk around. The decor was nice - the retro photos and baseball theme were a nice touch. The staff were very, very friendly and helpful - from the front desk to the breakfast staff to the valet. They were good at giving us directions to all the places we wanted to go, and even printed out Mapquest directions for us to Fort McHenry. The breakfast spread was plentiful and varied, and good quality. Mostly standard Hampton fare, but a lot of selection. The seating area was large and had plenty of tables and seats. They even had an outside area which would have been nice if it had been cooler. They have a pool and exercise area in the basement level, it was also very nice. The neatness and cleanliness of the hotel may be due in part to it being relatively new, but it was neat and clean everywhere, so that was good. It's easy to get to from the airport also - take 295 until it ends in downtown and turn left at the first light - it's right there. No complaints about the hotel at all (except maybe the $26 per day parking, but it's that way at all the hotels down there). Wished we could have stayed longer, it was that nice. I'd definitely stay here again any time I'm back in Baltimore.

“Great Place” I really enjoyed this hotel. I loved it's old-fashioned luxory vibe. It is absolutely beautiful inside and the staff were extremely nice and professional. Check in on a Friday night was easy. I asked for and received a quiet room on the top floor. I let them know I was celebrating my birthday when I made the reservation and there were chocolate covered strawberries waiting in the room which was a nice touch. The room size was fine and considering the hotel is over 100 years I thought it was maintained perfectly. Even though the bathroom is a little small compared to modern high-end hotels, I liked it because it seemed original to the era the hotel was built. The toiletries were very nice, the towels large and fluffy, and everything you could possibly want was provided in the room including a refrigerator. There was a large window and even though it looked over the interior courtyard, it let in lots of light. The best part was the bed, it was very, very, comfortable. The Garden Court, as everyone has mentioned before, was stunning. They day we left they were offering an "Opera Brunch" and although we didn't eat inside, we lingered outside to listen and it was amazing. The location was excellent and the BART station right outside is very convenient. The F-Line also stops out front and the cable cars are a 5 minute walk away. I am so glad I picked this hotel to spend my birthday weekend at. I felt pampered by the excellent service and warmed by the hotel's beauty and elegance. I will definately return.

“Pleasant hotel in a great location” A clean and comfortable property. My room was large (a corner room) and had a great view. The location is perfect. Everything I needed and wanted to do was walkable including the PA Convention Center, great restaurants, coffee shops, theaters and relaxed night life. I've always trusted the Hilton Brand and this Doubletree met my expectations.

“Could be better for the price” I stayed in Room 153 for 2 nights, Nov 10-12, 2005. I paid $199/night. I was not that impressed with the Omni Shoreham. Pros * Both the bedroom and the bathroom were good-sized, and very were very clean and tastefully furnished. * Bed was very comfortable. * Coffee provided with the coffee maker in the room was pretty good (Wolfgang Puck). * Front desk staff were nice and helpful. * Lobby was very nice, with plenty of places to sit. * Bar was nice, but it closed at 1am on a Friday night. * 2 blocks from a Metro stop. Cons (of Room 153) * Room 153 is a terrible location. It is on the first floor, which is one level above the lobby floor (main entrance). It is at the level of the lobby roof, so the view is of an expansive roof with air conditioning and heating equipment on it. It also feels like someone could walk out on the roof and then step through the window into your room. I would at least request a room on a higher floor. * Wireless Internet was too low a signal strength to work in the room. I tried multiple times, and I barely received a sufficient signal for about 3 minutes once. I wasted a good deal of time trying to get on the Internet. I finally had to use my dial-up ISP. I travel a great deal, and I have never simply been unable to use the wireless Internet in a hotel simply because the signal strength was too darn low. This was very disappointing. * Ineffective heating system. A digital thermostat was mounted on the wall. I set it to 74 degrees Fahrenheit, as I like to keep my room warm. The room never heated up past 71 degrees Fahrenheit. * Poor curtains. The room has sheer curtains, with light-blocking curtains behind it. However, the heating and air unit is mounted at the level of the window sill in the middle of the window. The curtains over the heating and air unit did not meet up well with the curtains on each side, so there were persistent gaps in the curtains. This was especially pronounced with the light-blocking curtains. I felt as though people could see through the sizeable gaps between the curtains into my room. This was especially uncomfortable since, as mentioned above, my room was at the level of the lobby roof. * Self-parking was $22/night, and it could not be billed to the hotel room! I had to pay when I was leaving the lot to go to dinner. The parking is not run by the Omni Shoreham! but by a separate company! And the parking is literally adjacent to the Omni Shoreham! That really didn’t make sense. * Concierge was not that helpful with restaurant recommendations. A list of restaurants in the area was provided, but few recommendations were made. The restaurants to which one can walk are okay but not great. When I asked for a medium-priced restaurant for dinner (in Georgetown), the concierges kept referring me to Sea Catch, even though I indicated that I wanted something slightly less expensive. (At the recommendation of a friend, I ate at Sequoia, which is a restaurant on the water in Georgetown, and it was fabulous and not too unreasonable. ) * Very minor annoyance: The cleaning staff made the bed but did not put away the iron and the ironing board that I had left in the middle of the room. In most other hotels the cleaning staff put them away.

“Is #1 in NYC and deserves to be #1+++” I stayed one night in a suite. This hotel deserves its number one rating. The greeting at the hotel door was prompt and friendly, taking my suitcase directly to reception for me. While at reception, the nice concierge walked up and introduced herself to me. Check in was efficient. The bellman escorted me to my suite and showed me how things worked in the suite; the complimentary soft drinks, water and beer in the fridge, the beautiful espresso maker and crystal glasses. Then to my surprise he offered to press five items for me at no cost! When I returned to my room in the early evening, the complimentary hotel pressing of my business suit took only one hour and the shoeshine less than 30 minutes. My clothes were fresh and ready for the next morning. The layout of the suite was magnificent. There were floor to ceiling windows the entire length of this long suite with windows on the side. All the windows open. I immediately enjoyed the cross ventilation. The bathroom is large and also has two large windows with privacy letting in natural light and air. The commode is behind a frosted door in the bathroom. The closet has a large amount of space for hanging clothes and has drawers. There were large areas upon which I could lay out my clothes making it very easy to get dressed in the morning. The telephone is a touch screen and is answered promptly. The televisions are excellent visual and sound quality. I ordered room service dinner and enjoyed surfing the channels. Room service: The quality of the food is superb. The quality of the service was wonderful. They were on time and just a few minutes early both times which took that worry out of whether my evening or morning would be fussed with if room service were late. No late service at this hotel. When I forgot to ask that no mayo be on my crab, the room service server did not get angry or defensive. Instead, the hotel has him equipped with a microphone attached to his collar into which he immediately spoke and asked if the kitchen could prepare the crab without mayonnaise. The answer was yes. I had the plain crab back in my room in less than five minutes! I have to tell you that is the very best service I have ever had. When I went to use the elevator to go outside the hotel meet my driver, the maid saw me coming and pushed the down button for me and waited for the car to start towards my floor before going about her business on the floor. Unbelievable attention to detail. Whoever picked this staff and then trained them should be given a raise. Location: At the side street on 36th there was a great place for my driver to wait with the car. Finding a spot for a car & driver to wait to pick you up can be daunting task in certain parts of Manhatten. The 36th street “cubbyhole” is a good feature for this hotel. When I exited the hotel that fronts on Fifth Avenue, the doorman walked me to my car on 36th. Without naming hotels specifically that are in the vicinity between 55th and Fifth and the Time Warner building, the Hotel Setai puts them to shame in both quality of rooms and service. An insider’s tip about going uptown from the Hotel: If you want to go uptown using Madison Ave. in the morning get to Madison before 10 AM to be able to make a left turn. (North) Madison Square Garden and New York Penn Station is around an 8-14 minute walk depending on your gate. Sleep quality: This area of Fifth is quieter at night and early morning than the 55th to Time Warner area. I slept with one window open and it was delightful to have the cool area coming in. Room service breakfast was really delightful and freshly cooked. I had a pleasant discussion with the room service attendant about the different temperatures needed for brewing black tea versus green tea. I noted that the green tea I ordered was perfect for a room service order because the water was not supposed to be boiling for brewing green tea. He immediately offered to have the black tea start brewing in the kitchen while the water was still boiling if I wanted to order black tea the next time. His demeanor at all times was pleasant and helpful without getting the least bit fussy. That’s the way to start off my day with a happy thought. My checkout was quick and efficient. The receptionist even asked me if I had used the room safe to remind me if I had possibly left something behind. I will be returning soon with plans for next time to allow time for a session at their spa and a workout in their fitness room.

“What a Great Place” This hotel was absolutely fantastic! We were traveling with our married daughter and son-in-law who stayed in the loft of our 2-bedroom suite. Everything about this place was positive. First with the room. The beds and linens were top quality. The entire room was very clean. The living area was comfortable. We did not use the kitchen very much, but it was well-equipped if one chose to fix something in. The lobby area was very pleasant and the morning breakfast was top-notch. The evening supper was just alright, but nonetheless appreciated. Complimentary wine/beer was great. Everyone at the front desk was pleasant and attentive and went out of their way to help. The only negative aspect I can think of is that the hotel is located adjacent to a dump truck terminal. In the morning, the sound of the trucks might wake up a light sleeper.

“Stay away” The newest brand in SPG chain and a mini W. If you are under 35 like staying in a noisey environment and are willing to sacrifice comfort for trendy design and don't mind having to hunt for the hotel then perhaps this property is for you. In a city loaded with numerous fine and reasonibly priced hotels this is not a good choice. It is NOT a good value. And don't be fooled there are less expensive and more comfortable hotels closer to the airport.

“Klasse Hotel – kostenloses Parken” Das Hotel ist ein echter Fund in San Francisco. Leider hatten wir für unseren Aufenthalt eine sehr teure Zeit erwischt und haben auch für dieses Motel sehr viel gezahlt, aber zu „normalen“ Zeiten ist es ein echter Tipp für San Francisco. Die Lage ist genial. Direkt zwischen Chinatown und North Beach. zur einen Seite ist man schnell am Union Square, zur andern Seite sind es nur wenige Minuten bis zu Fishermens Wharf. Und der absolute Hit ist, dass das Parken im Preis inbegriffen ist. Als wir dort waren, war der eigentliche Parkplatz belegt und wir durften sogar in der angrenzenden Tiefgarage kostenlos (Valet)parken. Unser Zimmer lag in den Innenhof raus und es war schön ruhig. Der Blick geht geradeaus zum Mark Hopkins (in dem wir Dank Captn Kirk schon für viel weniger Geld übernachtet hatten ) und nach links sieht man das Financial District und die Pyramide. Das Zimmer war sehr groß und sehr sauber. Das Motel ist etwas älter, was aber einen besonderen Charme ausmacht. Die Fenster sehen von außen aus, wie beim Standart Hotel in New York . Die Möbel im Zimmer waren völlig ok, die Betten bequem und auch das Badezimmer war gut. Lassen Sie sich nicht von den schlechten Kritiken abschrecken. Das Hotel ist von der Lage und der Ausstattung eine gute Alternative zu den teuren Innenstadt-Hotels und gefiel mir besser als z. B. das Columbus Motor Inn.
“Good business hotel” I have been at this hotel many times. I like it because it's close to my meeting location. Nice people, and easy to get to

“Great historical hotel” There are a lot of little touches at this hotel that make it specail. The bed is probably the best I have ever slept in. Way better then the Westin Dream Bed. It seemed like there was always someone cleaning my room whenever I came back to it. Nice, but almost too much. The lights are controlled by touch screen on the phone, which can be confusing. They are also motion sensored. One morning, all the lights went out in the bathroom while I was in the shower. Overall, the experience was great though. I was feeling ill when I arrived and was told that no rooms were available yet (it was about 11:30 AM). When I indicated that I did not feel well, they had a room for me within the hour. Bikes are availbe to use in Central Park. Also, there is a car service that you may use in a limited area.

“So close to being amazing” The property is grand, and what a great seafood restaurant downstairs! Service staff if attentive and hushed. The only thing that would push this one up to the level of the Grand Hyatt or Four Seasons would be to modernize the rooms. It feels like you're staying at grannie's.

“Rather hip, small hotel” We used Hilton points to stay at this hotel. It's surprisingly hip and funky, for a Hilton, with somewhat contemporary furnishings. We had a great flat screen, high-def TV in the room and nice art. The bathroom was just standard, but the room size was large for NYC. We had one snafu with the room safe--when we returned one afternoon, the safe blinked and we were unable to open it. It took security 45 min to arrive and we were sweating it--our Broadway tickets were in the safe and the show started in 1 hour. We had turndown service nightly, and the front desk staff were nice. We were on the 25th floor, which is low for NY, and we only heard light buses, etc. Downside for us was the location on a major street in Times Square--the sidewalks were mobbed at night and we could hardly get to the small entrance. I would prefer to stay off on a side street during peak visitor times. But we were there for the US Open and the 7 line is just a block from the hotel (convenient).

“Location and That's That” We use TripAdvisor religiously to find the best place to stay. Taking our children on a little spring break trip, we decided that being close to Fisherman's Wharf is where we wanted to be. I wanted to stay at The Argonaut Hotel, but it didn't have a pool and our boys were sure it would be nice enough to use a pool. I told them the pool wasn't going to make a difference and to please listen to me and let's stay at The Argonaut. Well, my husband got us a good rate on two rooms through Hotwire and so we went for it. My intution was correct. The Sheraton is a couple of blocks away from all of the action of Fisherman's Wharf, but it has undergone some crazy looking, cheapo renovations and it's really not that nice. It's like the famous line,"You can put lipstick on a pig..." The walls are paper thin (You could hear every little sound from all sides and above.), the average room is super small and those comments about the bathroom being tiny are correct. I am a fairly small person and you could barely sit on the toilet without the door hitting you in the knees if you tried to close it. The beds were not nice at all...mattress just slapped on a platform...I thought they were very uncomfortable. Outside there are these cool little sitting areas around gas fireplaces and we did enjoy sitting there after walking around all day in the mobs of people. It was nice to relax, order a drink and warm by the fire. But since there's only like 5 areas, they were hard to come by. But nonetheless, a nice touch. The conceirge was really nice and helped us find specific restuarants and the few bellmen we had contact with were also super nice. But I would not stay here again for all the fortune cookies in San Francisco! Please listen to me and stay some place away from the noise, crowds and average rooms of this hotel. I travel frequently, probably once a month, and these rooms were among the most uncomfortable I have encountered. It was like staying at the old Super 8's of my youth. If you still want the Fisherman's Wharf location, trust me, stay at The Argonaut! It's at the end of the mess, near Ghiredelli Square and the park with the cable car turn around. Hope this helps!
“Fullfills Hyatt Reputation” Huge hotel (maybe not good?). Great location. Rooms as you'd expect. Lots of things to see in hotel.

“Biggest rooms in NYC ever!” Stayed here with a group of high school/college aged kids to see the lights and holiday displays in Manhattan. Couldn't have been happier with the location! Easy walk to the Rock, Times Square and 5th Avenue shops. The room was HUGE for city standards with lots of room for people to stretch out. Having a full-service mini-mart downstairs was nice - and so was the in-room fridge. My only wish was that there was a little bit bigger lobby area. Don't miss Ess-e-Bagel across the street for your breakfast treat (but do know what you want before you step to the counter. This is the "Soup Nazi" of bagel shops, no doubt!)

“Large, convention-oriented -- but excellent in this category” Washington Hilton is large and convention-oriented -- but excellent in its category. First, everything is clean and well-maintained. Second, rooms are well-furnished and equipped - except for limited counter space in the bathroom. Third, the service is helpful, responsive, and generally, friendly, especially for such a large hotel.
