This includes efficient handling of packages sent ahead, location of a quiet room (as sought), storage of luggage prior to departure, and for departure to airport, successfully finding a taxi that takes credit cards (issue here: only about 10% of DC taxis take credit cards). This property is well-managed and well-maintained. Recommended for business travelers, convention-stayers, and others, including families.

“VERY close to Camden Yards and M&T Bank Stadium” We were in town for the NCAA Mens Lacrosse Championships at M&T Bank Stadium. Great location for the stadium and Camden Yard. Directly across the street from Orioles Park. Good room with fridge. Nice bathroom. We had a great view of the park (room 640) and even though were the first room off the elevator, we had very little noise. Quiet room. Hotel was packed with lax fans but the elevators were pretty quick. Really wish they had queen size beds instead of full. Nice bedding. Flat screen tv with many plugs for chargers. Didn't use internet. Room service Saturday night was not good. Ordered burgers and crab cake sandwich at 9:45pm. At 11:15pm, we canceled the order and they didn't give us a hard time which tells me the order wasn't ready yet. There isn't much within a quick walking distance from the hotel for a late night dinner. Subway was closed! Jimmy John's sandwiches was open as was a nice seafood place and Pratt Street pub but an hour wait for a table that late. Large game crowd. There's a gentleman's club at the other corner so don't go toward Lombard Street when leaving the hotel. Sketchy crowd. Sports pub in the hotel did not have proper staffing Saturday night, especially for a holiday weekend with major sports event in town. But the breakfast buffet (not free) was very good. Our breakfast was comped because of the prior night's room service debacle AND the cold shower I enjoyed Sunday morning. Was the hotel nice? Yes. Was it worth $400/night? No way. I would return for maybe $150/night.

“Functional, dependable 4-star, but not much more” This is a hotel that, for the most part, provides the standard 4-star experience. Rooms, in the more modern tower where I stayed, are presentable and dependable, but unremarkable in most respects. There's little sense of luxury about the place, although that might not be the case for rooms in the historic tower. Some might find them a little on the small side, but that's the price you pay for such a central location, right on North Michigan Avenue. The one major downside, as other reviewers have commented, is the absurd range of additional charges the hotel levies. While these kinds of add-on are not uncommon in other hotels, it's irritating to be charged $12.95 per day for internet access (which really should be free nowadays) or $12 for the gym (a pretty dowdy affair), led alone the predictably ludicrous array of charges for the in-room extras ($5.95 for a bottle of water). All of that said, there's no reason to avoid this hotel, if you can secure it at a decent rate. Equally, though, there's certainly no reason to pay top-dollar to stay here.

“Booked Into A Classic Grande Dame” We stayed at the Warwick about ten years ago when we published a book. The publisher made the reservation and we had very fond memories of this hotel. Well, now we have just published another book, with a different New York publishing house and they, too, put us into the Warwick. A pattern seems to be emerging. Initially we were taken to a suite, large, comfortable and dark. When I pulled back the drapes we were deep into an air shaft. I told the bellman that I couldn't stay in such a dark place (claustrophobia) and that even a small room would be preferable, as long as it had light. He made a quick phone call to the front desk and took us up to the 28th floor and opened the door to The Warwick Suite. Light streamed into the suite from 3 sides. We had a fabulous view, even better at night, down 6th Ave. Large living room, bar and refrigerator, dining table, huge bedroom looking at 6th Ave. going the other way. We had a great stay, a nice comfortable living room to come back to after hours of interviews. Breakfast in the room each day was prompt, eggs and coffee hot just like they should be. I never understand people who can't get over a slow elevator or the other small irritations of hotel living. It is the whole experience that makes up your stay and our experience at The Warwick was stellar. Just hope we don't have to write another book to return.

“Not up to snuff, but great location” We stayed there pre-cruise for an excellent Priceline rate. You can't get a better location if you are going on an NCL cruise, we walked one block to the cruise terminal. The staff was friendly, and upgraded us for free to a larger room when they saw we had a family. BUT: (1) The carpet in the hallways and elevator was dirty. (2) The staff was incompetent. For example, our key card stopped working. The person at the front desk insisted on sending an engineer to check the door lock instead of letting us try a new key in case the old one got demagnetized. Waited 20 minutes for the engineer. Verdict: The key card was demagnetized, a new one solved the issue. (3) Many of the rooms have beautiful water views, but others face the rail tracks and are subject to freight cars 24/7. The windows were pretty good, but you still get some noise. (4) The staff didn't seem to have basic information about Seattle. More generally, the hotel looked like it had seen better days. For pre-cruise and <$100, it's a decent deal. But I would have been sorely disappointed if I had paid the normal $200 plus rate.

“Good, but not great....” My wife and I stayed in a king room on the HHonors floor for two nights, and were not disappointed, but also not impressed.....typical Hilton room, typical Hilton location, typical Hilton service. Clean room, good access to restaurants, subway stop a block away, but nothing special. We stayed for rewards points, but I think I would have been somewhat disappointed if I had paid full price....Boston hotel rooms are very expensive, and for he price, this hotel offers only location. Parking is $41 a night, the rooms are kind of "boring", the bathroom is small, the lobby is lackluster, carpets are old, furniture is '80's modern....just nothing special. Really good: the bed, the continental breakfast (free for HHonors members), and, as I said, the location. Really, really BAD: the television (a primitive satellite system that takes 30 seconds to re-tune eachtime you push channel up/down, pixellating, poor resolution, poor channel reception).....probably the thing I remember most. All in all, an adequate hotel, but not worth more than others in the area (made over 15 trips to the area in the last few years, as my daughter is a BC senior).

“Traditional elegance” This is an excellent hotel, well located in the downtown area. The interior design of the lobby and rooms is traditional and elegant. My room was well-maintained and comfortable. Service was impeccable. I asked the front desk for theater recommendations, and within a few minutes an envelope was delivered to my room with numerous suggestions, printouts and directions. Highly recommended.

“Top Marks from this moving-Mark” I spend a great deal of my time at 35,000 feet or in hotel rooms world-wide...and I can spot a winner on most occasions, before I even leave the curb-side to check-in. This hotel set the stage for a wonderful stay, right from the start for me, and it kept pace with my expectations throughout my stay. I love real pillows, and real people, and I think the owners of this property spend a good bit of time and talent paying attention to both the brick and blankets as well as finding the best help. I had a fistfull of meetings, tight schedules and 'must do' activities while I was in this city...made possible in large part by helping hands at the hotel... The people for me, make any place & this hotel quietly boasts some of the best in Beantown. Please, Don't take my word for it, sample the sheets for yourself... Mark Sheehan, author of "The Scent of a Dollar" by New Holland Books * This property will make my list of top-tens for the next time-around.

“My parents in law loved it” My parents in law stayed in this hotel for a couple of days and I visited them there several times. And Jorge, my dearest father in law, asked me to write this review instead of him and give it ***** stars. It has a very convenient location. You can walk everywhere. It's close enough from the cultural attractions and it's near from supermarket (Whole Foods, CVS, 7 Eleven), bares and restaurants. The room was spacious and it was recently renovated. It had a nice TV and free wi fi. My parents in law loved the breakfast. It has many choices: waffles, toasts, yogurts, eggs, sausages, cereals... The only issue is the elevatores. They are slow and they stop to work very often. The staff is very helpful and nice.

“Going to Universal? Stay here! Tip: the lavish Sunday and Thanksgiving lunch and dinner buffet is excellent” Hilton Universal City is the next door neighbor to the Universal City theme park. You walk across the road from the hotel to the park. Also, it's not far (driving distance) from the Warner Bros. studios at Burbank if you want to do their excellent studio tour. It's a pleasant place to stay, The rooms are spacious and comfortable, and the service is the usual Hilton professional standard. I've stayed here several times, and I have no hesitation in returning. For travelers who frequently stay with Hilton, you should note that there is no Executive Lounge. Also, the Executive Floor rate does not include a complimentary breakfast. A highlight is the Sunday buffet lunch and dinner, which is lavish and offers excellent value- they offer the same buffet for Thanksgiving. The restaurant is excellent, and there's a hospitable cocktail lounge as well. For devotees, there's an In-and-Out burger restaurant just down the road as well. Highly recommended

“Great value” What a great value for anyone traveling with a child. The room was very large with two flat screen televisions -- one in the bedroom and one in the living room. Not the cleanest room I've been in and maybe a bit worn around the edges, but the price was looooowww and we got a lot of room for the money. We were visiting family, so the location was excellent for us. I think for a tourist this may not be the best spot unless you don't mind a lot of driving.

“OMG.. this was actually the most awful experience!” I have never been to a hotel where when you call the operator, guest services or housekeeping you either get NO ANSWER... or the actually disconnect the line when they answer. AWFUL AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE ! ! ! ! Being a Crowne Plaza you would expect better.... AWFUL. Also very VERY LOUD HALLWAYS>.. VERY NOISEY...SLAMMING DOORS...

“Thanks for the advice!” My girlfriend and I stayed two nights because of the amazing deal we got through priceline. Per fellow tripadvisor correspondants, we stayed away from the hotel restaurants/bars and instead spent most of our time by the harbour and in the downtown area. The room was clean and well made both before and during our stay. The box-shaped TV was outdated, but we weren't there to watch TV anyway. As expected, internet was around ten dollars for 24 hours. However, the hotel did charge the wrong credit card despite the lobby person walking me through the self-check out. On top of that, an additional 70+ dollars was charged to my credit card for no reason (when you book through priceline, you do not pay the hotel). I called to inquire about both charges and the customer service representative moved the internet usage charge to the correct card and reversed the "phantom charge". It all turned out just fine and at a reasonable price. Great location, clean hotel. Just be careful about those phantom charges! -Dan

“Rocky Mountain High” 1st time to Denver since the early 70's. I was in town for a wedding and chose the Oxford hotel based on it's proximity to Coor's field for an afternoon baseball game. The Oxford didn't disappoint. The hotel was as I expected: a step back in time, where service is discreet,unobtrusive, and yet still refined. As soon as I entered the lobby I knew this hotel was an excellent choice. The music playing in the background was from the 40's/swing music. Delightful. The lobby oozed of history. After checking in, I actually received a room key (how rare is that) and was told how to use the key (turning it towards the right allowed entry into the room). Never had that experience before from hotel staff. Entering the room there was a king side bed, a separate table and lamps throughout the room that you had to turn on the old fashion way instead of one switch controlling the lights. Stepping into the bathroom was amazing. The old tile floor- straight out of the 30's. And size, one of the larger bathrooms I have ever been in travel wise. A separate tub and shower instead of an all in one package. In fact the bathroom had a clock in it. The bed, to die for. Excellent quality. The room also had a Bose sound system. I'm going out this week to purchase one for my home. At first since I love coffee in the morning in my room I was a bit disappointed that there wasn't a coffee maker in the room. Not to worry though. On each floor there is a coffe urn with coffee. Delicious. I used the limo service available to all guests. Friendly & curteous driver. Waking up early and having my coffee I headed down to the lobby to people watch. Couldn't have had a better time before checking out. Bantered with the entire staff. Such an enjoyable time. Thanks, Gabriel, Heather & Jennifer. Since I am still a post card sender I asked the hotel staff if they had any postcards of the hotel. I was able to secure two postcards circa 1958. Talking to one of the bell captains (sorry I forgot your name but heres a shoutout) he was able to go to down to the basement and brought up a bundle of postcards. Elated to say the least. I generally mail anywhere from 25 to 50 postcards while on a trip. Such a pleasant suprise. Thanks again. Would I come back again? You bet. I can't say enough about the hotel and the entire staff there. It harkens back to a time long since past. Keep up the good work and don't ever become like the rest of the cookie cutter hotels. P.S. This may sound quirky/odd but check out the hotel's mens public restroom Wow. you'll know what I mean.

“Simply Great!” Decided to stay at this hotel after an impressive stay at another great Kimpton Hotel, the Alexis Hotel in Seattle, and I could not have been luckier. This must be one of the nicest hotels I have stayed at in recent years. I received excellent treatment from the staff, $10 voucher for the minibar and free internet for being a Kimpton InTouch member. The location is definitely the best I could have possibly asked for with many great restaurants all around the Fisherman's Wharf. The cable cart and the tourist buses start and end a few meters away. The room was very clean, had a good size, great bed, excellent TV and a nice bathroom. I could not fault this hotel and would definitely recommend it.

“Cheap and Clean!” Now, a lot of you may be shocked when you first step foot in this hotel. But let me tell you it's cheap, clean and pretty much central to everything! I was shocked at the prices of most hotels in DC and this hotel was recommended to me by a work collegue. I stayed 3 nights and it only cost me around US400$. Other hotels wanted over US1k$. If you select a small double room, be warned, it's small, just enough room to put a suitcase. It's within walking distance to the white house, hop-on off bus place and across the road(well maybe 2 roads) from the FBI building and Ford's Theatre where Lincoln was assasinated. The food at the restaurant downstairs is ok. I forgot I was in USA when I ordered a burger with "chips" I expected the deep fried stuff and I acutally got Potato chips like the packet supermarket stuff. So remember when you want Chips it's called FRIES! I'd stay here again and recommend this hotel to anyone who's on a budget.

“Nice accomodations near Ground Zero” I stayed here for a business meeting, and was very worried about its proximity to Ground Zero (the 9/11 World Trade Center site). It was no problem at all, save for the emotions ellicited whenever seeing that great gaping hole and thinking about all the lives that were destroyed. In fact, the location is excellent: very near to the subway, to lots or tourist attractions, and to the PATH train station (in case you need to go to NJ: its only $1.50 each way to Newark). The hotel itself has a small feel, the rooms are in good shape (not new, but not worn out either), and all of the staff were great. I highly recommend this place if you want a great NYC experience without paying the high prices they charge for similar rooms in Midtown.

“Rude/Loud catering staff” This review relates exclusively to the catering staff at a black tie event...not the service, food or servers...all were well above average. During the keynote presentation, the kitchen staff and dining room bussers' access to the event ballroom were immediately behind the stage. This was a speaker all were anxious to hear prognosticate on the upcoming election. The kitchen help was actually yelling behind a swinging door and the staff waiting to bus the tables, actually standing on the event floor, were talking in normal conversational tones not 30 feet from the stage where the speaker was addressing 800+ attendees. Because of the yelling and the multiple conversations we actually could not clearly hear the speaker even though she was using a microphone. This kind of sheer stupidity by the catering staff, especially the management is incomprehensible. The organization paid $$$$ for this event and multiple thousands of dollars to engage the speaker. We finally got up and went through the door to tell them to shut up. The response was total shock that they were being disruptive. They did quiet down, but our table, where the guest of honor was seated, was livid. If you're considering any event engaging the hotel catering service, be forewarned.

“Eh” As Hampton Inns go, I'd say this one is below average. The LOCATION is the best thing going for it, but the look and feel leaves something to be desired. The staff was friendly, the breakfast is the same you get at any other Hampton Inn. Probably the biggest drawback was the train going by loudly once in a while (at any time, day or night). The TV channel selection sucked, no fridge or microwave (should have asked, apparently), and shower pressure was weak. Ok for the price and suitable for business travel, but if you are here on vacation, splurge and upgrade.

“Bird's-Eye View on Philly at the Hyatt” My girlfriend and I recently spent one night at the Hyatt Regency Penn's Landing, and were very pleased by both the accomodations and the service. When in Philadelphia, we usually stay at the Marriott located on 12th and Market, but through Priceline we ended up at this hotel instead. We were slightly wary because the location wasn't really that convenient to the area where we planned to hang out and Philly's sorely lacking in taxicabs, so we wondered how easily we'd get around. As it happens, the bell captain hailed us a taxi almost as soon as we'd asked him to, and a ride to the Rittenhouse Square area was brief and inexpensive. The room at the Hyatt exceeded our expectations, too--we ended up in room 1412, which provided a remarkable view of the cityscape (all the rooms ending in -12 probably have the same lovely view, too--ask when you check in if any are available!) and was spacious, clean, and nicely appointed. Room service was fast and exceedingly friendly, and the front desk staff was likewise polite and accomodating. Our reservations about staying so far away from the center of the city were overcome by the helpful staff and well-kept grounds, and we'd stay here again without hesitation.

“Live like a New Yorker - we're addicted to AKA Sutton Place” When I’m in New York I want an apartment, in an upmarket neighbourhood, with an excellent deli and wine shop across the street. As a result we have become addicted to the AKA Sutton Place. We try and take the same spacious apartment each time we go and we settle in. The staff sorts everything with maximum efficiency, minimum fuss and genuine warmth and good humour. We love this place. It is extremely comfortable and spacious. It feels like coming home, its understated, its private and the you get the sense that everyone staying their feels as lucky as we do to have found it. The added bonus is the swimming pool, a rarity in New York. Our problem is that can’t think of staying anywhere else, and well, yes, it’s not inexpensive but it’s a great deal. If you want to be a New Yorker and not a tourist this the place.

“Fantastic service and spacious rooms” I've stayed at the Hampton Times Square North two times now and was very impressed both times. In fact, I booked a third stay for July 4th holiday. The service at the hotel is outstanding! The employees really seem to enjoy their jobs and are happy to see you. The free breakfast gets a bit crowded at certain hours, but the wait time wasn't terrible. They have a lady walking around with to-go snacks while you eat breakfast...very nice little extra touch. The rooms are clean and spacious. The location is near Times Square, but doesn't have all the noise of Times Square. About a 10 minute walk to Times Square, depending on where you go. We liked the House of Brews around the corner...good ambiance and good beer. Overall, wonderful experiences and highly recommended!

“I would happily stay here again.” Since I don't feel that a fitness center makes a hotel worthy of 4-stars, I would only rate the Warwick as 3-stars. The room did not feel cramped and the bathroom was clean. I am a light sleeper, and the quiet of the room was very welcome. The location was excellent for my purposes, though as somebody who loves to take the subway, I'm happy as long as I am just a couple of stops away from midtown. For the visitor not familiar with NYC, it is close enough to major attractions like Radio City, Central Park and Times Square so that walking is easy. I feel that it is silly for hotels to charge for internet access in guest rooms, and I am not about to pay it. I feel that so-called 4-star hotels might even make up enough by offering free wireless to guests to offset anything tht providing it costs. If Starbuck's can do it, so can they. The view of the air shaft is what I have come to expect, but I wasn't there for the view, so it made no difference to me. If I have the opportunity I will happily stay at the Warwick again.

“Outstanding Stay” This is a really excellent, client-service oriented hotel. I only stayed one night for business, but it was great. As the previous reviewer noted, the adjacent restaurant was undergoing a renovation and thus there was a very limited room-service menu. However, this was clearly disclosed and I had no problem with it. They gave me great suggestions for a close dinner that needed to be fast (Cafe Rialto) as well as a good breakfast (Sam's #3). The free wine "happy hour" is a nice touch. I enjoyed my stay and will definitely syat again.

“My New Favorite Hotel” I am a very particular traveler. The Sofitel did not disappoint. The room was beautiful and the service was excellent. I experienced room service on two occasions (dinner and breakfast) and was equally pleased with both meals. The real appeal of this hotel is the attention to detail-everything just works together including service, decor and amenities. I would highly recommend this hotel and will plan to stay here on any trip to Washington, DC.

“Lobby like Versailles” The lobby area, which runs the length of the hotel is undeniably impressive, with its mirrors and chandeliers and reminds you this is a hotel with a history. The reception area is being revamped and much improved since our last visit; there is more to come - I hope it includes a bit more of a seating area, as the few armchairs there are tend to be colonized by wi-fi users. This time we enjoyed a suite in the former apartment wing of the hotel. It was very well appointed with desk and escritoire, a separate powder-room too and a wet bar. The ceilings are a bit low, but then this is an historic hotel. The air-conditioners though are under-window and noisy. Avoid breakfast charges and walk right through the lobby and out the other side; you find the Sunshine Cafe, Caribou Coffee and Panera bread. The location is ideal. You can walk down to the White House and you are adjacent to a Metro station. A slight general gripe about housekeeping in hotels generally. We use the decaf coffee, leave the wrapper out clearly as a hint that we would like some more the next day; often just not noticed. Or ignored. Shirts would cost you $9 to be laundered.

“eek, look around for better options” I purchased this hotel on priceline and frankly, I got FAR better rooms in MUCH nicer and more convenient neighborhoods for the same price. The room wasn't terribly bad. The hallways though are rough and worn and look really bad. In the lobby there was this lady sitting in a wheelchair all night with a reddened and swollen knee who looks like she needs her leg amputated, I have no idea if shes a friend or long term resident or what, but it was nasty. From the looks of some other reviews, they must be rennovating it one bit at a time. Unfortunately I didn't get a renovated room.

“Great rooms” nice spacious room. Hotel seemed to be quite new. Friendly service. Breakfast nothing out of the ordinary but ok. Stayed here for 4 nights in a business trip. Nothing wrong with the room at all, would stay again for sure.Only thing that bothered me was that the noice from the freeway. So bring earplugs or ask for a room on the backside.

“Second visit--keeps getting better” After a stay a few months back, we returned to the Omni with our five year old son in tow for a family visit. We used a Select Guest upgrade voucher and were able to get the Executive Suite. Nice to have the dining table and a little extra elbow room (note--the bathroom in this suite is actually considerably smaller than the one in the corner suite, but still fine). Once again, the staff and ameneties made this a very enjoyable stay. * Kid extras. Cookies and milk on our first night was a great bonus. This may also have been available on other nights, but we weren't around on other evenings. Also a super bag of books, games and activities. Wasn't available when we checked in (limited number, first come first served), but a tremendously helpful front desk manager-- who also was helpful in a past visit-- made it magically appear when we asked him about it. The pool, while small, is a great bonus when traveling with a child. *Select Guest extras. Definitely sign up for this program. Local paper, coffee, fresh OJ, small smoothie--all delivered to your door each morning. Heavenly. *Small requests not a problem. Early check in, airport car service arrangements through the concierge. *Room service and housekeeping. Very good food delivered quickly; the housekeeping staff did lovely little extras like tuck my son's stuffed animals in his bed so they were waiting for him when we got back to our room in the evening. Sweet.

“Conventional Overnight Hotel that You Might Find Along A Freeway” Two storey motel between the 101 and 118 on Desoto in the SF Valley. Note that at busy hours it can take some time to access either freeway. This motel is located a few minutes drive to two large shopping centers, but this particular street corner offers no real amenities. However, I had a large room with both a microwave and small fridge. I found several supermarkets nearby where I could buy groceries so I wouldn't have to drive miles trying to find an adequate restaurant. My room was sufficiently cleaned each day and had a large flat screen TV. I asked about a complimentary newspaper in the morning and the desk clerk told me that they stopped getting them because nobody bothered to read them. In my room, the message light on my phone wouldn't go off, until a higher ranking reservations clerk came in the next day to fix it. I also couldn't figure out how to re-set the room clock, so I used the one on the microwave. There's a bus stop on the corner from where you can actually get to Hollywood or downtown LA (or anywhere you can transfer to), but it will take quite some time. But if your reason for being here is to stay up here in the valley, then this would be a reasonably inexpensive lodging to use for a few days. Just don't expect too much in the way of extra comfort. And you might want to bypass this place if you're driving a trailer because there's really not suffcient space for parking large vehicles. However, I found the staff to be personable and helpful if you are cordial to them. They returned my driver's license to me the next morning after I inadvertently left it at the front desk the evening of my check-in.

“Good Location, with a few drawbacks” I stayed at this hotel for two nights while visiting Chicago on business in September 2007. The location is excellent being between the financial district and the Magnificent Mile. However, the elevators simply do not work properly, and it is not the place to stay should you need to get to and from your room quickly or frequently. I saw several customers have trouble getting to their rooms, and the front desk staff were nonchalant, and would not even allow customers to take the stairs. (This is obviously a persistent problem.) Nevertheless, it is probably good value for your money, and in a good location.

“Nice, clean and upscale.” We had plans to stay at the Hyatt Regency for a romantic night away but after viewing 3 disgusting dirty rooms there including there nicest room we got our money back and started looking around. We stopped by the Omni by chance and fell in love the minute we walked in. The lobby is very nice and it smells excellent and clean. We wanted to see a room before we booked the the staff was very nice and helpful. After a quick look we booked our stay. The room was a bit tiny but it was excellent in everyway. But you can't expect much for a last minute stop. Overall we were very happy with our stay and would love to stay there again.

“Super Location for Excellent City Experience” We left the car with the valet parking and quickly checked in with out a problem. The room was immaculate, fresh and up to date. The Christmas throng was in good chjeer and the Gingerbread houses were a main hiliday feature. This is a Great Sheraton property. But the main attraction is the bustle of the Seattle stores that are in the immediate area. Further there are a number of excellenet resturants ready to meet your every need. We were most impressed by the reasonable price for this city get-away. We will return without a doubt.

“Large Room - Couch is Not a Sofabed” I booked an Emerald Suite thinking I would have a sofabed in the sitting room and then I would order a roll-away bed for my other teen. No. The rooms in this hotel are very large, the bathroom is large - but we needed 2 roll-away beds. Overall the value of this hotel was excellent. Linens and Rooms were very nice. The Location of the hotel is an easy walk to the water, there is a Starbucks in the base of the hotel and a Ruth's Chris. Easy walk to a lot of other restaurants. There is even a Hertz within a block that will probably same you money if you book your car there instead of at the airport - if that works for you.

“Couldn't Fault - It's Perfect!” If your looking for a hassle free stay with some luxurys then this is the place for you. We had absolutely no problems whatsoever with this hotel. Right from the moment you arrive, your taken back by the grandness of this hotel and just how beautiful it is, but it's not just that. The staff are amazing, they will literally do anything they can for you, receptionists, conceirge, room service, absolutely everyone. Hotel itself is stunning. Rooms are adequate, we got a great rate on a two double bed room for two people and there was more than enough room for us - and we're both girls who like to shop! The shower - I have to say the best shower I've ever had! It's well placed too, you can easily get to whichever attraction you want to visit from here, and being Park Avenue is never short of a taxi if you need one either! All in all would definately stay here again, and would reccommend it to anyone.
“Great hotel” Just completed two night stay at Casablanca. Lived up to expectations and previous reviews.Would certainly recommend and will return next time we're in New York.

“had a great time here” We stayed in a suite that was absolutely perfect. Location on the riverwalk is super, and walking distance to Alamo and the market. The main hotel is an old bank building that retains its atmosphere, and our suite was in the newer tower. It is a bit of a way to get from the lobby to the tower though. As with most Drury's, they have the standard breakfast and happy hour. Just be aware a lot of people stay here, and both are crowded. There were many families here, so it must be a great value. However, if you are traveling alone or with someone else, be aware - there were a lot of kids there. One thing to be aware - the address of the hotel is on St Mary's St - but the guest registration driveway is on Commerce St. When coming in on Commerce - dont turn left at St Marys, and look for the guest registration sign half block up on Commerce.

“Great Hotel, We will go back!!!” If you are going to NYC to see a show on Broadway than this is the Hotel for you. Before our trip, I looked on several different boards regarding the reviews of this hotel. Clearly there were some good and some not so good so going into our trip I didn't know what to expect. Upon arrival we were greeted in a very efficient manor and were quickly checked into our very comfortable and very clean room. All the rooms were redone a year ago so they are very modern with a flat screen 24 inch TV with all the normal channels and in room movie entertainment. Some of the concerns of the people who wrote previous reviews were that the room were to small. Not true! They are just fine for one or two nights. Bathrooms are small but just fine for one person at a time. What also makes this hotel great is that you are located two blocks from Times Square ABC Good Morning America Studios, four blocks from 30 Rockefeller Center and NBC Today Show Studios and all of the Broadway Theaters with in walking distance. All in all this is a great find for the price and location. Remember, when you are in New York as a tourist the only time you are supposed to spend in your room is to sleep and rest up for your next adventure. The Club Quarters Hotel does that just fine!!!

“Ideal for early morning flights” Great location, rooms are a little dated but perfectly comfortable. I arrived late and ordered room service which was delivered fast and tasted great after my transatlantic flight. I had a 7.30am flight so was in the restaurant early for breakfast. Good buffet selection and service was friendly and efficient. Excellent wifi speed in the restaurant. I wouldn't hesitate to stay again if I had an early flight.

“Soemwhat disappointing” The hotel has charm, but unfortunately it seems somewhat dated. Some, but not all rooms are renovated; some rooms are quite small. The halls and rooms are somewhat dark. Restaurant choices are uninspired. All in all, it was less than I hoped for.

“Took good care of us; great location” A week after staying at the Four Seasons in Chicago, my son and I were looking at colleges in the Philadelphia area chose the Four Seasons largely because I had never been to Philadelphia before and wanted the extra service. Also because they were giving a $150 credit. They fulfilled my expectations in every way. We were starving when we arrived and asked for an outdoor cafe recommendation. Got a great one from the desk clerk (The Parc, which was excellent), left our bags and went off for lunch. When we returned, our bags were in our room and we had been bumped up a grade, which was nice. The room was similar to one we had in Chicago, very comfortable with most everything in a low-key beige, though a bit smaller, as was the bathroom. We had lots of questions about getting around, restaurants, the Phillies' game, etc and the staff was very helpful each time. It was a good feeling when you're in a strange place. Our $150 credit went to parking (valet at $42/day, a bit more than the weekday rates at nearby garages and $14 more than the weekend rates) and one breakfast. My son had a $14 bowl of oatmeal and blueberries and two $6 glasses of OJ, which would have been a bit ridiculous if it wasn't included. Liked the fitness center. Very clean and not crowded. Location could not have been better. It's about in the middle of Ben Franklin Parkway, which may be the prettiest urban boulevard in America. It was fun walk to City Hall, the Art Museum, Franklin Institute, and Rittenhouse Square.

“A Diamond in A Rough (Place)” At some point on Van Buren in Phoenix, things get a little dodgy. Right on the border is the Super 8. I stayed here for 2 nights and had two of the best nights sleep in a long time. The room was super clean, everything worked, it was just great. The price was right, too. I booked it on line and went by the reviews, but mostly the Mgr's responses to the bad reviews. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat!!!

“Great Location” I spent almost a week at the hotel while in New York on business. The location is fantastic as it's so close to the financial centre and the subway is across the road. My room (I had to change once as there wasn't a safe in the first room) had a great view out over the world trade centre building site (and memorial). The breakfast as the hotel is a little pricy, but very good. The hotel also helped us in booking tickets for shows and for the WTC memorial. Nice little bar downstairs in the lobby which was well positioned before heading out for dinner. My only gripe would be the cost of daily WiFi, which really adds up and there is no option for a cheaper time period (you have to pay for 24 hour access, regardless of whether you are in the room or not) so a full day in the office and dinner meant paying for 24 hours and using 1 at the most. Great location for business, bit of a long way to get up to Midtown and Central Park.

“Great Hotel, Great Location” We stayed at the Capital Hilton for two nights last week. The location is excellent - two blocks from the White House, two Metro stations within a few blocks, and several restaurants within walking distance. The hotel in general was very clean, and the staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was nice with a very comfortable bed. The only minor complaint is that the thermostat is a little unpredictable, but we had no major issues. Hilton Honors members get free access to the full service gym which is a nice benefit. Yes, Internet access costs 9.95, but this is very common in full service hotels. The area is safe to walk in, and we are a little confused by some of the other posts. We would have to agree about Georgia Browns. We had a great meal there and would recommend it! Our rate included breakfast and parking which we felf was a great deal. Breakfast was very good quality and selection.

“What a disappointment!” When you enter this landmarked hotel lobby, you're overwhelmed with its grand scale, ornate design flourishes, historic charm. Unfortunately, you've also seen the nicest part of the hotel. This place is a joke if this is a "flagship" hotel. I was expecting a small room, so that wasn't surprising, but the tube TV (!!) certainly was. Seriously? In 2011? At these prices? Not only that, the interior decor was *old*, the carpet was frayed all along the edges, and there was visible dirt in the corners. Give me a break, Hilton! On top of all that, they charged $10 to use the fitness center!!! Outrageous!!! To boot, the nearby W is actually less expensive, as I imagine a number of other, better hotels are. The Hilton I stayed at not two weeks earlier in suburban New Jersey was a hundred times better. It's a shame that such a beautiful, historic hotel is being so mismanaged.\ In short: don't stay here. Ever. There are so many better options.

“I really want to love this hotel” We were in town for college hunting for our son and some sight seeing on the side. We got a good- to-great rate ($309 per room for lovely, large connecting rooms) for five nights. I really want to love this hotel and make this my home away from home as my son is probably going to school in D.C. Positives: I love old hotels, the ambiance, the high ceilings, the crown mouldings, the history... this is my favorite kind of place. The beds are super comfy, great linnens. Large, clean bathrooms with nice amenities. Loved the soft robe! The employees were friendly, informative and the housekeeping staff was very efficient... loved the nightly turn down with chocolates and a point of interest flyer. The breakfast waiters who talked soccer with my younger son were a great hit. The downstairs bar is great. It has a phenomenal wine by the glass list and good bar type food. Breakfast in their main dining room is a lovely experience with delicious food (that is priced accordingly) Negatives: Two early a.m. (6:45ish) fire alarms on consecutive days. I think there was some work going on in the hotel and the workers set off the alarms, we don't really know as no explanation or even apology was ever given to guests, at least not to us. It's not a fun way to wake up, grab some clothes, grab the kids and run down 7 flights of stairs... 2x. We were tempted to ignore the second one, but you just can't. I am afraid if there was a real fire after this, many guests would have been in big trouble as they would not have responded a third time! There was something spilled on our room wall across from the bathroom.( looked like coffee or soda?) I did not alert the hotel to it, so I can't say they didn't respond, but it was very noticeable and was there when we checked in, and when we left. I felt I was treated slightly differently when I was dressed nicely (skirt, dress, etc) than when I was in tourist mode (shorts and sports shirt) I'm still the same person spending lots of money at your hotel! It is an old, creaky hotel. You hear the people walking above you, and hear people in the hall. This is nothing to be fixed, and I expect it in this kind of beautiful, historic place. Just a note to light sleepers. So, would I stay here again? Yes, most likely if I could get this rate again. If I had to pay rack rate, I would consider many other hotels in this general price range, including the Ritz, Four Seasons or Willard. I guess I really just wanted some sort of acknowlegement that two mornings out of five, with two fire alarms is an inconvenience, and an explanation and apology would have smoothed everything over. Then they would definitely be my hotel of choice. I really want to love it!
“Quite, convienent and worth the $$” Very nice rooms. Did not hear air traffic at all!!

“Not as Grand as I had hoped...” For brevity, I'll just list the pros and cons, and briefly comment on each as needed.... Pros: -Fairly new hotel -Large (many rooms) -Very nice common areas, banquet, and meeting rooms -Exercise room - huge, and well-equipped - it was basically a full-blown gym like you might find at Bally's, President's, World, or Gold's Gym. -Services was accomodating with special needs, requests, and circumstances -Comfortable (but small) beds, pillows -Large tub/shower -Large bathtowels -Clean (with caveat below) Cons: -Rooms are small - two full sized beds are not comfortable for two adults sharing one bed, and even with the smaller beds, the rooms are fairly cramped. -Rooms did not cool well - my home A/C set at 78F was cooler than the room set at 66F with the fan on high. Do not bother opening your shade, as it will heat your room to the point of being unable to cool it. Because of this, I was unable to sleep well. -Room hallways and elevators are either have the A/C off, or are unairconditioned. Being in South Texas in August, I would work up a sweat from leaving my room to arriving at the lobby or meeting areas. -Better signs indicating room direction: some areas came to a "t" hallway, and you have to look around a corner to read the directional sign. -Pool area - cramped and crowded, disgarded cups and limes were found strewn about the area, and beer bottles, cups, and a warning pylon (cone) was tossed off the balcony across an alley to the roof of a Municipal Performing-Arts Theater. -Parking is woefully inadequate. Five levels are available, but parking spaces are limited and tight - some areas were closed for construction. Self-parking is $15/day, valet parking is $45/day. Our parking (self) was paid by the conference, but none was available. As such, I did not budget for valet parking for the whole weekend. Thankfully, enough complaints were made that the hotel provided the valet parking at no additional charge. -Couch/bed and business chair in the room were stained. -Bathroom needs an exhaust vent. -Room decor can best be described as retro '60's or retro '70's, or modern and spartan - taste is subjective, but I just don't care for that decor. I was expecting something more...opulent -Formica veneer on the center nightstand was chipped, and my two young children were scratched horribly on it trying to access the bed from there. -No free high-speed internet. Come on! Even the mom-and-pop hotels provide free internet these days! I would not recommend this hotel, but only marginally so.

“Nettes Hotel, sehr zentral” Wir haben hier während eines Wochenendtrips übernachtet und waren alles in allem sehr zufrieden. Hervorragend an diesem Hotel ist v.a. allem die sehr zentrale Lage unweit des Union Squares. Die Zimmer (wir hatten ein Standard-Zimmer) waren o.k. Einrichtung ist modern, aber nichts besonderes. Uns wurde angeboten für ein Upsell von 50 USD / Nacht in einen höheren Stock mit besserer Aussicht zu wechseln, das stand allerdings unserer Meinung nach nicht dafür. Service war ansonsten sehr freundlich und zuvorkommend. Kommen hier gerne wieder her.

“Deceptive Website” Since we have been pleased with the one bedroom suites at the Beekman, we booked a studio queen suite on the website for a one night stay. We were dismayed to find a very small double bed in a room that was too small to hold a queen sized bed. The room would have been adequate for one person, but was too small for two -- small enough so that it was difficult to get into the bed. When we complained, we were told that queen suites may have either a double or queen bed, but this is not clear from the website. The room was significantly overpriced for what it was.

“Great hotel at Christmas” I stayed here for two weeks for business in late November/ early December. The hotel is truly beautiful during Christmas. The Mark is exactly what one should expect from a 4-5 star hotel. The service was great the rooms were clean with very comfy bedding and the bathroom was big enough for for two girls to be staying for two weeks. I have not one bad thing to say about this place after spending the longest stretch I have ever spent in one hotel - this fact alone I think speaks volumes.

“Good inexpensive choice in Central San Diego” This is a good choice if you are looking for an inexpensive hotel option in the downtown area of San Diego that is easy to walk to. You are only 8 min walk to the trolley, and the bus stops one block from the hotel going downtown and three block on fifth ave if you are going to the Hillcrest area. The hotel is built around an open courtyard with external outside entrances to the rooms. You can hear and see the airlines landing on Rwy 27 at San Diego international just over this hotel, so putting your room fan on at night will create white noise so you can sleep. The rooms are on the small size, but well laid out. The breakfast is from 7-10 and is basic with pastries, fruit, cereals, tea, coffee, juice and milk. Internet is available via wi fi, and there is a machine in the lobby for those with out a computer. However there is a better option of using Kinkos downtown on C street for access and much cheaper. Good value for sure,and an easy walking hotel.

“More livable than most "hip" hotels” If you have been frustrated by stylish, hip hotels that put style over substance, you will be pleasantly surprised by the W Westwood. Having stayed at several such hotels (mainly Ws) in the recent past where you have to contend with poorly lit hallways, loud elevator music, strange room layout and lobby area crowded with the "young happening crowd" in evenings, I was dreading more of the same. I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is on a residential area, and doesn't seem to attract the nightclub crowd. The front desk was efficient and helpful at check in, and the concierge was helpful with local walking directions. The hotel isn't too big, so you feel you get personal and efficient service. I stayed in a "Spectacular" room, which as others have described, has two parts - one small bedroom with a king bed, a 42" LCD and night lamps; and a living area with a L shaped sofa, a work desk, a refrigerator, and an entertainment center with another 42" LCD+DVD player+music system with iPod deck. Overall, it was pretty spacious and bigger than most rooms that I am used to in business trips. The room service was the usual over priced stuff, so I chose to walk down to the nearby shopping area about 10 minutes away. You can take a map from the concierge that will give you locations of various chain restaurants and shops within walking distance. For more distant trips, there is a taxi stand right outside the hotel. Finally, there were some "triump of style over substance" things in a hotel that does bill itself to be part of the hippest chain of hotels. The sink in the bath room looks great, but has barely enough space for one person's toiletries. The room has quite a few fancy lamps whose on-off switches will be difficult to find (I gave up on some). And the elevator takes your pictures and "broadcasts" it real time in a corner - cute for some but scary for others.

“Incredibly poor fitness center” A good fitness center is important to me when I stay at a hotel and the one in this HGI is the worst I've ever seen for the size and type of property. I googled fitness centers in the area and the Concourse Athletic Club turned out to be right next door. It has 6000 sf of workout area and is complementary to guests and $5 for a day pass. The hotel itself is full service with a bar & grill. To add insult to injury it has a $79 rate and I paid $129 for a joke. Diamond member or not, I will be staying at the Concourse Airport Hotel from now on.

“Quite an average hotel” I spent an extended weekend at the Omni to take a break from the Icon where i usually stay. i thought it looked great being a five star hotel and all, but it was generally quite a basic hotel. The staff were okay as was the service. The decor was rather dulll and nothing was exceptional including their food.

“Disappointing Stay.” We chose Le Parker Meridien, because it was recommended by Fodor's as "family friendly". The only thing family friendly was a coloring book handed out at check-in and a television showing cartoons in the elevator, which didn't impress my son. We wanted a luxury hotel close to Central Park, and this hotel was very convenient for walking to the park. We were told we were being upgraded to a very special room. We stayed in room 2921. I don't know what the standard rooms were like, but this room did not seem like an upgraded room. The room was very quiet, and the bed was comfortable, but the room was dusty. We heard great things about the Burger Joint, but never got to try it. While waiting in line to place our order, guests from the back of the line came in and took all the empty tables prior to ordering their food. When we mentioned this to the man behind the counter, his response was he just worked there and couldn't get involved. We had our 19 month old son with us, so we left. We went to Angelo's Coal Oven Pizzeria across the street and had delicious pizza and fried calamari. Norma's breakfast was very good and expensive. They provide high chairs and booster seats, but we didn't feel the restaurant was a good choice for small children. The staff was accommodating, but not very friendly. The front desk staff however, were exceptionally friendly. We visited FAO Schwartz, which was a few blocks away. They have men dressed as toy soldiers roll out a red carpet and play a bugle to announce the store is open. The employees line up inside and clap as you enter the store. That was special for the kids. Le Parker Meridien was an average hotel. For the price we paid, there are better options for our next visit to New York.

“Fine... Does the job.” This hotel is fine to lay your head down before or after a flight. However, it is most definitely a 3 star. The service was decent, the staff was very accommodating, and the communal areas were presentable and acceptable. The elevator itself was dingy, the hallways a bit musty, and the rooms were starting to show its wear. Though the bed and bedding was acceptable and comfortable, the carpets were stained, the bathroom a bit worn out with slight mildew, but I was still okay with showering without shower shoes... I just made sure to walk around the bathroom and room with flip flops or socks on. Again, the hotel is fine. Its nothing spectacular, but with my Priceline rate of $45/night, who am I to complain? It did its job, and I would mind sleeping here again.

“Mediocre” This is an adequate hotel. Its advantages are its friendly, can-do staff and its convenient location. Although the building is in good repair for the most part, the public spaces on the main floor are big, empty, and anonymous: all the charm of an empty barn. The rooms are middle-of-the-pack functional. The good news is that mine was comfortable, well-equipped, and recently redecorated. On the other hand, water pressure was a problem, and hot water was in short supply some of the time. Along with several other people on my floor, I could never get a swipe card that reliably opened my door. Tried several different cards, but ended up unable to enter my own room on more than one occasion. Unless you want to use room service, the only on-site restaurant for dinner is a pretentious steak house where the waiters have airs, the food is only middling good, and the prices are steep. Do not waste money on the club floor. The amenities in the club lounge are very, very modest -- nothing like the generous food and stylish furniture available in the club lounge at the nearby Renaissance. This is on balance an OK hotel. The hot water and room-key problems I encountered were serious, but probably fixable. But nothing about this hotel rises above the ordinary, and to me it has no warmth whatsoever. The nearby Renaissance is far better.

“very comfortable hotel” I was there for a business conference. superb room and service... and you pay for it. Very much enjoyed my stay. They have valet parking which is very convenient. Health club on the third floor, wireless internet access costs extra.... that should really be included if a room costs $400.

“Hub of downtown with some down-sides” We enjoy staying at Hyatt Hotels usually. My husband had a conference here all week, so I was a solo tourist, diner, & guest for the most part. This Hyatt is very large, & the rooms are of typical Hyatt design/spaciousness. Not very much room to store clothing, though; only 4 clothes hangers in the closet - so bring your own. No counter space in bathrooms either. Our air unit was broken,so the temp was really hot upon arrival, but housekeeping was prompt to fix it. Our door keys were disengaged twice but also promptly fixed once we showed our I.D.s to guest services. For our troubles, they gave us a fruit bowl. The fitness center is small, but the equipment is new/clean. The spa staff were very pushy w/ services. All i wanted was a haircut, but the facial lady literally booked me for a facial w/o my request and insisted it would be the best facial ever. I ended up walking out. (She even followed me down the hall, still trying to make "the sell.") The food in the Bistro is not comparable with the price - dinner or breakfast. You'd do better finding someplace down the street. Every time I ate there, the waiter would bring the check to me immediately after taking my order, which I thought was rude. And they do take away your food before you're finished - a lot of language barriers with wait staff here. But the "Big Bar" is nice if you're into a happy hour scene. Good conference center for business too. I would say if you're here for a conference or enjoy being in the hub of downtown, this will work for you. $13/day for internet is surprising for a semi-luxury hotel, though. Even Motel 6 has free wi-fii!

“Very Nice Hotel in Canoga Park” Best Western, Canoga Park. Adjacent to a Convention Center,Bowling Alley and terrific Coffee Shop, this place has alot to offer. Rooms and public spaces are clean. Staff is quite pleasant. Morning Breakfast is well above average. Cereal, fruit, granola, nuts, raisins, biscuits & gravy, danish, cakes, pastries, three kinds of juices, hard boiled eggs, yogurt. We were pleasatly surprised. Obtain discount bowling coupons from desk, as well as discounted drink coupons for bar in bowling alley. Karaoke most evenings next door. Pool and jacuzzi is cloistered between buildings and is sparkling clean and well maintained. Rooms come equipped with refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker. Terrif budget-minded hotel with many extras. Oh, and the food at the adjacent "Greek Owned" coffee Shop is wonderful.

“The most comfortable bed ever!” Kimpton usually does it right and this is no exception. From the moment you walk in the door you know you are "home". This hotel has the chic factor down pat, but more importantly, it is super comfortable. Many other hotels are overly chic to the point of non-functional. Eventi has it all. The lobby is very inviting and I could have hung out there all night long. They will cater to your every need and make you feel like one of the family. And to top it off, it was absolutely the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever experienced.

“Mostly Good but Some Problems” The hotel is very nice. I stayed in a suite. It was clean and spacious. They had a very nice breakfast. However, there were problems with the wireless service, and I was unable to use it one evening. No one at the hotel could solve this problem. They gave me a number to call. Also, there was work being done one late afternoon. There was quite a bit of noise being made.

“The Four Seasons Excellence” First visit to Seattle and to this Four Seasons Hotel. Arrived late at night with my family, guided directly to our rooms. Rooms as ussual, inmaculate, clean and very very comfortable. Had breakfast at restaurant in the lobby, excellent quality of food and attaentive service. Everyone at this hotel was always witha smile and eager to help. The hotel is very cosy, very well located near to all downtown restaurants, shops and markets. Lovely view of the bay and a tranquill enviroment makes this the perfect destination for couples, business or families. Highly recomended.

“Nice rooms, very clean and good location” Stayed in a 1 bedroom suite. Room had a kitchen with full size frig, stove, microwave, dishwasher & dishes. We were only there for one night for a cheerleading competition for my daughters. The hotel is on the Riverwalk a bit off the beaten path, but still a decent location. Hotel was very clean and the staff was very courteous & helpful. Hotel has a rooftop pool. The rooftop setting is really cool, but the pool is super small. Probably not great for kids and swimming. Hotel offers a free breakfast, but the pickings were very slim, just OK. Overall liked the hotel and would stay there again.

“Solo Traveler in a Sketchy Neighborhood” I had a bit of a debacle booking my hotel room in Philadelphia for a conference I attended this past week. I landed up changing hotels to the Four Points, despite the negative reviews I read on TripAdvisor. I should've listened to what others had to say since the lower price of this hotel was not worth it! I felt completely unsafe walking to and from the Convention Center from my hotel, especially at night. In fact, I had my colleagues, who were staying at the Marriott, which is much nicer and adjacent to the Convention Center, walk me home each night since the area near the Four Points was mostly deserted with the exception of a few people who were just hanging out outside. The hotel is technically across the street from the Convention Center, but you have to walk in an "underground tunnel" for one block to get to the Convention Center's entrance. Once you exit the tunnel, you're in a more decent area with Reading Terminal Market right there. My hotel room was overloaded with furniture, which left me barely any room to move. The bedroom part of it looked clean, but the shower, as I found out on Friday morning when I went to take a shower and was pressed for time, was not cleaned well. Let's just say it had other people's hair all over the place. I told this to the Front Desk, upon checkout, and they offered me a free bottle of water or a free piece of candy. Ugh, no thank you! That doesn't make up for an unclean shower! Since the hotel didn't have any king-size bed rooms available on a high floor when I checked in, I had to take a king-size bed room on the fourth floor. That was just loud. (And I lived in Manhattan for years and I'm telling you this was loud!) The bed was a bit too soft and therefore I didn't sleep very well for the two nights of my stay. If you're a solo traveler, especially a woman, think twice before staying here. I know I felt unsafe!

“A quiet Ritz in a very loud and busy city” In my opinion this hotel is the perfect location for traveler(s) to New York city, that do not want to walk right out of their hotel and face the hustle and bustle of the city. While some indicated it is far from the city, my response is “that is relative”. We had plans on seeing the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island, so this hotel couldn't be more perfectly located (literately right across the street). Also, getting to uptown Manhattan was only a 20 minute subway ride away, which others had mentioned in their reviews that I read on this site. The room was nice, clean, and sizable by New York standards. If you can, get the room with the telescope our kids loved it.

“Perfectly good hotel, but not as amazing as the reviews suggest” I really doubt that this is the 3rd best hotel in NYC as the reviews suggest. It is right next to Port Authority, which is a useful location if you are in town to go to Broadway shows, and it's just a 15 minute walk from Penn Station. It's also very close to the metro. The staff are extremely pleasant and helpful, and the small lobby with free internet access via Macs and free coffee/cider is nice enough, though hardly glamorous. Our room was very standard - neat and very clean, and perfectly comfortable. Free internet, little chocolates left on our pillow nightly, and free NY Times delivered daily were nice touches. A continental breakfast buffet costs $10/person at their little restaurant/bar, and it was very nice. One random issue: the switches for the bedside lights didn't work and we had to unplug to turn them off. Not a drama, obviously. For less than $200/night it wasn't a bad deal - we had a nice time. If you're looking for glamour, this won't work for you. If you're hoping for the third best hotel in NYC you will be disappointed. And if you pay more than $200, you're probably paying too much.

“A Sure Bet” As usual, the Embassy Suites is a sure bet--I'm always confident that I will get a nice room and a good deal. The room was clean and well-appointed, the beds were comfortable, and the location was convenient to all the places we wanted to go on this particular trip. That said, we were given a room on the second floor above the pool and could hear noise all night long. Would have liked to sleep longer, but the breakfast setup was very noisy. If I go back, I'll certainly request a room on the third floor or above.

“agréablement surpris” tout d'abord, ne pas se fier à bcp de sites de réservation qui montre encore de vieilles photos avant rénovation effectuées en 2011. Personnellement j'ai payé 65 euros la nuit, et c'est vraiment pas cher pour L.A. Chambres rénovées, 3 lignes de WIFI (internet) gratuites, distributeur de boissons et glaçons, parking gratuit (vous pouvez vous garer devant la porte de votre chambre presque si vous le voulez. De plus, il y a qqs restaurants; fast food et superettes à qqs mètres. Si vraiment je devais trouver des points négatifs, c'est qu'il manque une lampe de chevet, très peu de chaînes TV, les murs sont un peu fins et on peut entendre un peu de bruit de la route (donc si vous êtres très sensibles au bruit, à éviter ou ramener les boules Quiès). En 10-15 minutes en voiture vous êtes partout et encore une fois vous ne perdez pas de temps avec des voituriers à attendre. bcp d'hôtels à L.A. facturent 30 USD par nuit pour le parking, c est énorme mais cette ville est devenue hors de prix. Il y a un restaurant collé à l'hôtel qui servent des petits déjeuners.j'ai regardé les prix et c'est assez cher. Vous recevez 10% de réduction si vous montrez la carte de l'hôtel. Encore une fois, rapport qualité-prix IMBATTABLE et hôtel surtout fréquenté par une jeune clientèle. Définitivement un 3 étoiles, et plus un 2 étoiles comme avant la rénovation.

“Outstanding” I spent three nights at Hotel Palomar while in Chicago for a conference. I couldn't have been more pleased. This is what you would expect of a Kimpton Hotel. Stylish, minimalist, a bit whimsical, and excellent service. For a small additional fee I was upgraded to a corner king room on the 14th floor, with a great view of the city. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the service was outstanding, with nightly turn-down and chocolates on the pillow. The location is prime: An easy walk to the Magnificent Mile, Art Institute, Museum of Contemporary Art, and so forth. The staff was universally friendly and accomodating. Free coffee and tea in the morning and a complimentary hosted wine bar from 5:00 to 6:00. The restaurant, Sable, is also excellent.

“No food on site at night!” Stayed here three nights for a conference. Good room, updated nicely. Small new York bathroom. Room service very limited. No food onsite at night, which you need if you just want to collaps in your room. Went to a deli close by.

“Fair Value, Good Location, Decent Older Midrange Motor Hotel” This is an older motel / motor hotel (2 stories, exterior entrances) which is fairly clean and well-maintained. They seem to be in the middle of a modest renovation of the rooms: beds, furniture and carpets are close to new; drapes, bedding and fixtures are tired, but clean and serviceable. Wall-mounted A/C under window was a little noisy. The "green room" amenities (wall-mounted air filters, R.O. / cartridge water filters on sink and shower) functioned well. The rooms are relatively large and clean. The dresser / media cabinet included a large tube-type TV set with lots of cable channels and auxiliary hookups on the front. There was a mini-fridge and microwave inside the cabinet as well. A continental breakfast was included (pastries, fruit, juices, make-your-own waffles, boiled eggs); the combined breakfast area / lobby was spacious and kept clean and well-serviced, and seems to have been updated recently. Front desk service was friendly and efficient. There was a single internet PC/printer setup in the lobby near the front desk. The hotel is located in a mixed-use commercial park just west of the 10 / 410 corridor. The road construction in this area is (finally) about complete, but traffic is heavy around rush hours. There are car dealerships in the immediate area and many chain and fast-food restaurants within short (5 min.) driving distance. San Antonio Int'l. Airport is a 15-minute drive east. At around $75, this hotel is a fair value in a good location.

“Ok, clean hotel near Market Square” The hotel is easily accessible off the highway and parking is free. They do have an outdoor pool which is good for families with children. Our rate included the buffet breakfast and we found it to be substantial and good. There is also a full service bar that is open during the evenings.This hotel is NOT on the riverwalk and across the highway from Market Square(restaurants, shops, and street vendors). The rooms were basic but updated. They had flat screen tvs, a sleep number bed, and free wifi. I would recommend this hotel to families for a short stop over in San Antonio.

“A very family friendly hotel with great location” This hotel is located among the Shops at the North Bridge in the Chicago downtown. This means it is near various/countless dining/shopping options. If you buy the Chicago Trolley bus ticket, at least 3 stops are within 5 blocks of this hotel and most downtown attractions are within 10 dolloars taxi. The room was also good with beds in the bedroom and a sofabed in the living room plus a full kitchen. The only thing is that the laundry room, which located on the 7 floor, had only two washing machines and two dryers. Given so many families in this hotel, I really think it's not enough. Every time I went to the laundry room, there was always somebody washing their clothes. I eventually had to wait by the machine until my turn. Other then this, breakfast was free and full American breakfast. It was always packed with families and stopped service at around 9:30am, so be fast and wake up early!! The front desk only had around two people who needed to serve a full-house of guests and they always attended to my needs. I was amazed at their hard-work and would like to pay my respect to all of them at the front desk. They all deserve a good holiday after this peak summer season. I would also suggest a makeover of the carpeting which could be a really worn out.

“Average, reasonably priced hotel but great downtown location” The Hyatt Place is well located within walking distance of the HP Pavillion, SJ Convention Center, SJ Events Center, Performing Arts Center and the Tech Museum. Shops and restaurants are nearby too. Rooms size is average, well appointed (for this caliber of hotel) and very clean. The lobby is spacious and modern. The front desk was friendly enough but did to know the area. Recommendations were inaccurate. Breakfast offerings were extremely disappointing. There were discrepancies on our bill so keep your eye out. This is the first time I have stayed in A Hyatt Place concept and it's OK for this level compared to the competition but nothing to write home about. It served our purpose and we would consider staying here again.

“Beware of blonde night manager” I booked a room at the Radisson after my suburban home lost power in a storm. The hotel was lightly booked, and the weekend manager permitted me and my wife to stay at the hotel for $99 on a Sunday night, $179 on Monday. When I learned that power might not be restored until Wednesday or Thursday, I went down to the Front Desk to inquire about extending my stay, should the power outage continue. The man attending the Front Desk informed me that the hotel had "plenty of availability" and he said he didn't think it would be a problem. Then he asked the night manager, an unattractive, large woman at the desk, and she said the rate for the room woujld be $279. That effectively threw us out in the cold. We booked a less expensive room at the Cosmopolitan downtown. A lovely place. That night manager ruined what could have been a pleasant stay. She should go into a different line of work.

“Not as good as all the hype” Poor 1st impression. Minibar contained former guest sonic rt 44's (disgusting) plus dirty room srvc tray in front of my room upon arrival. My issue was that guest services didn't seem to care. It's ashame b'cuz I prob won't stay again.

“WHat a great Easter weekend” I want to start this review with the staff. I would say that the staff at this Crowne were by far some of the best that I have ever dealt with. A special thanks to Jenna and Sara. Every member of this hotels staff were more than helpful and friendly throughout our entire stay. This is a perfect location if you plan to shop on Michigan Avenue. It is also close enough to Rush Street if you are here to party. A great base station if you plan to hit the Pier or the museums. We were put on the 36th floor which is their quiet floor. I will request this floor from now on. They do not allow people with small children or large groups of people to be on this floor. We loved it. The room was very spacious with a great view. We could see Lake Michigan and Michigan Avenue. The beds were extremly comfortable including the pillows. I would have liked to have had a fridge rather then the mini bar, but you can't have it all. This was a great trip at a great hotel. We will be staying here in the future.

“A solid hotel, nothing more” There are many hotels in Washington that are nicer than this hotel for roughly the same amount of $$. That being said, if you want a solid hotel in a good location and can get this at a good price, then this is a reasonable choice. The hotel is relatively clean, the room service is ok, the conference rooms are ok. It just isn't a hotel that will blow you away. It is simply solid.

“Got it for cheap and it was pretty ghetto” Got it for $35 a nite plus tax on priceline for the day after XMas 2008. First of all the place was some what difficult to find off the highway and access. The highway has exits and then little mini highways on the side so it was hard to get to. When we got there they didnt have my reservation. Luckily i had my priceline print out so i showed it to the guy at the desk and he gave us a room. We went to the room and the beds werent made - the linens and spreads were balled up in a corner. We went back to the front desk and he set us up with another room and replied "here try this one." Haha. This was funny because it made it sound like there was a chance it wouldnt be clean either. Luckily it was. The kitchen didnt look to appealing so we went out to eat instead. There are a few places near by. Its a bummy little motel so for the price i cant gripe but i have stayed in much better for the same amount.

“Good value compared with other hotels in area” I stayed here my first trip to NYC in december. Once I got over the sticker shock of how much hotels are there I finally settled on this one because it was among the cheaper without being a dump. I still can't believe though at $300 a night it was just as good as a Hampton Inn somewhere else. I could stay at the Ritz in New Orleans (pre katrtina) for that much. The hotel staff were not very friendly or helpful. The room was actually a good size and had a closet. Smelled kinda funny though. Bathroom was very bare and only had a teeny tiny vanity for placing tolietries. It could use some updating. I found it to be a very good location. If you are just looking for a place to crash and this hotel comes up as one of the cheaper ones I would reccomend it. The rooftop terrace is neat and there is a nice lounge by the lobby.

“Large Clean Rooms” I've traveled to Houston, quite a bit, but don't normally stay in this part of town. This location was convenient for me this time. Hotel was very clean and comfortable. Rooms were large. Do to company connections, I had access to Executive lounge, which was also nice for breakfast, or to grab a tea or bottle of water. Only ridiculous thing was internet access for $11 per day, but fortunately, that was waived with access to Executive lounge. Hotel parking was also very convenient although there were no good walkways from the parking lot. I would stay at this location again.
“Muy bueno” Excelente la suite, muy buena atención; quizás un poco distante del centro convenciones, pero se puede ir caminando tranquilo. Muy apacible la zona.

“Remede spa” be careful when signing the receipt at the St Regis spa Remede.... they slam an automatic 20% tip onto any fees... they don't suggest... they just add it....WHAM!! This option should be open on the receipt for the customer to add at will.... kind of a crass bit on their part at the end of the experience.

“Great stay - other than Roast” We hotwired our room during the Detroit auto show on a Friday night for $109. We had a double room that was very large. The bathroom is also very nice. The hotel has a cool feel to it, although it is surrounded by a very depressing downtown Detroit. We did not see or use the pool or fitness area. We did try Roast, which I cannot recommend. The service was bad and slow. The food was bland. We felt like we were irritating the waiter even though we made no special requests or complaints. Otherwise the staff at the hotel were very nice.

“Excellent choice” The first impression was great. The young receptionist welcomed us like we haven't been welcomed so far on our trip. Very nice. We could park our rental car in front of The Charlesmark Hotel for 15mins to get our luggage to the room. I must say the bed itself was rather small and not the most comfortable. The bathroom was classy&clean. Then he gave us a map and told us directions to several points of interest. The hotel is well located, just a few steps from the T (Copley Square), which you don't really need as in Boston centre everything's within walking distance. Boylston Street is safe, we could walk at any hour of the day to different areas. Then the Bruins won the Stanley Cup, we saw the parade from the hotel! It was one big party throughout the day and night. Newbury street and it's fancy shops/restaurants is just around the corner. The Charlesmark also has a cocktail bar/lounge where we would have a last drink before going to sleep. They would tidy up the place for breakfast the morning after (bagels / cereals,...) excellent. As we had a late flight from Logan, we could leave our luggage there after having checked-out. Next time in Boston I will consider returning to the Charlesmark Hotel, because of the better price compared to other hotels. Thanks Charlesmark crew!

“Happy with stay - about what was expected - not great/not terrible” Stayed here on a short overnight to avoid a pre-crack 'o' dawn drive to the Indy airport and to utilize their airport shuttle and "park & fly" room rate (or whatever the heck they call it). Front desk service was quick & efficient - both check-in & check-out - and shuttle (which stops at the other nearby La Quinta) also worked well; ~15 - 20 minutes to get to the airport. Given the length of my trip, the rate on the room (w/parking privileges) was just a few bucks more than I would have paid for the cheapest long-term parking. Toss in the extra hour or more of sleep I got by staying nearer to the airport and it was pretty much a no-brainer. Unfortunately, I left too early to take advantage of the "free" breakfast, but was able to at least get a coffee to go.
