That's about all there is too report as about all I did was check in late, sleep and get up early to catch the shuttle.

“Excellent Airport Hotel” I stayed at the Hampton Hotel when flying out of Philadelphia Airport. It is a great location and there is a Ruby Tuesday restaurant directly in front of the hotel. The hotel has free WiFi and breakfast. Overall, I would recommend this hotel if traveling out of Philadelphia Airport.

“A Real Dump” This hotel bills itself as a timelessly elegant boutique hotel. In reality, it is a poorly-cared for badly maintained property. NEGATIVES: - The hotel has a very "cheap" feel to it. - Ridiculously small rooms, even by New York standards. - Dirty, stained carpeting. - Lumpy bed which felt 20 years old. - "Cork" walls and flooring, which are actually rubber stick-on "tiles" -- same as you buy at hime depot for $1.99. I saw these tiles peeling off in my room and elsewhere in the hotel. - View from room was basically an alley/brick wall. - No central a/c. Lousey, noisey window unit hanging out over dirty alley. - Halls dark and unfinished areas covered by black hanging cloth...Tries to evoke a tendy look, but actually looks more like what you would see in a high school gym for a Halloween carnival. - Price- $450+ per night. Just outrageous for this crappy little hotel, with small dank rooms. - Had to stand on bed to get into "closet". POSITIVES: (Not many) - Decent bathroom with good Hermes toiletries. - Location - Free internet access. - Good on-site restaurant.

“Modern Masterpiece Maintains Maximum Moxie” Well, I am writing this while drinking red wine so that may color my review, but this hotel is freakin' awesome. On this second visit, we booked the Emerald Suite after my return from a year in Iraq. We were checked into room 3015, the highest and prettiest suite in the hotel. What can I say? It was the largest and most comfortable suite we have stayed in at any hotel. The view of the Olympic peninsula and the city were flawless and the bed was outstanding. The towels could use some refreshing, but that is the only nit to pick. What a great hotel.

“Great location on Seattle waterfront” The hotel is across a 4-lane road from Elliot Bay but there's a traffic stop switch right outside the hotel so you can stop traffic quickly. Going the other way (up) there's an elevator (and stairs) to get you up the hill to the downtown stores and Pikes Place Market (10 minutes away). Be prepared for steep hills. Good seafood restaurant with great views of bay across the street. More restaurants within 5-10 minute walk. Cruise ships dock diagnally across from hotel and a Japanese training vessel was berthed directly across during our visit. Walking distance to statue park to the right and bay and harbor cruises, etc. to the left. So hotel is in a great location. Our room (upgrade but not the most costly) faced directly to the bay so we could see the Japanese ship and the tail end of the cruise ships. Super view. Some other rooms with small balconies were at right angles to the bay so you would need to be on the balcony to really see the water very much. Staff was friendly enough. Room was clean, but housekeeping cleaned the rooms later than normal (early afternoon). We really never saw the housekeeping carts clogging the hallways as you do in most hotels. System seemed to work well. Ate one meal (breakfast) in the hotel restaurant - a buffet with somewhat limited offerings but was there (including omelet station & very fresh, ripe fruit) was very good eating. Wired Internet in rooms for $12.95/day. When will Marriott get it?! Free wireless in public areas, although our room (#658) was able to access the free Wi-Fi. Refrigerator in room - no honor bar. All in all, a very good stay. We'd definitely go back to the hotel.

“Great hotel with lots of amenities” I recently stayed here for 5 nights. A very nice hotel. It's only 4 blocks from the convention center. I nice easy walk and very safe. Close to the river walk - there is an entrance from the hotel to one part of the river walk. Just outside the main entrance - you can also walk about 1/2 block to another entrance to the riverwalk - close to the restaurants. The room was a nice size. I was on the 18th floor. I had a king sized bed, a nice desk, lazy-boy type chair which was comfortable to watch the LCD flat screen tv. The room had a refrigerator, microwave and drawer space. Very quiet -didn't hear anything in the hallway Staff was very friendly. It was a little hard to find at first where the front desk was. The hotel is in an old bank building. The business center off the lobby has free internet and free printing. The 2nd floor had free hot breakfast, lots of choices. In the evening during happy hour - included free snacks, like nachos, popcorn, etc.. The pool, hot tub and deck are all on the roof - nice view of the city. I would definitely recommend this hotel - lots of amenities, decent price and great location. There is also a great japanese restaurant across the street.

“Great stay, would go back” I stayed at this Sheraton with my family (wife, 7 yr old, 6 yr old) on a Tuesday night just as a stay-over in between seeing other family during the holidays. I had requested via my SPG points a Club Room for a total of 5,000 points. It was hard to find the main entrance due to construction with no signs pointing you toward the main doors. I went in the conference center doors and walked my way to the lobby desk. They informed me right away that the Club lounge would not be open, but instead I could redeem vouchers in the restaurant for the nightly appetizers and morning breakfast that I would have gotten in the lounge. The room was decent sized, and the bathroom was oversized with a standing shower with no tub. I also loved that they recycled. The view from the room looked down onto the connected mall, but that was OK. I redeemed our vouchers that night and the next morning for the meals that we wanted, and while the service was definitely slow, the people were nice - they were just understaffed. All in all, a good stay, and I would go back.

“Hotel Was Nice, Price was a Different Issue” Okay, upon arriving at this hotel, i was nicely greeted by the doorman who took my luggage to the bell stand and then was handed off to another bellman who took me up to the 19th floor to the Lobby. Upon getting to the lobby, i was greeted by the front desk manager and was able to check in about 3 hours early. I was given a corner room on the 39th floor that faced Times Square itself. Very nice views of downtown and of the area. However here is where the concern comes in. The next morning, i went downstairs to the restaurant to get breakfast. I waited at the stand for a few minutes, and since no one was at the desk to sit anyone i just got a seat for myself. Since, i was only really thristy and wanted some fruit, i was asked if i had the breakfast voucher. I handed the guy the voucher and then was on my way. Upon drinking my juice and banana i recieved a bill by the guy. I looked in it, that so called juice and banana i had would of ordinarily cost me $20.50. Then there was a hand stamp on here saying (Gratuity not included) What gratuity, all i had was some juice and a banana. I'd feel sorry for some other person with no voucher who wanted a bowl of cereal and some juice and had to pay $20.50. Then, upon getting my bill, i noticed that the supposed $13.99 for the internet had actually turned into $15.70 with taxes included. So you get the my sense of where i'm going with this. I was just concerned with the price for a juice/banana and internet for one day would of ordinarily cost me over $35.00. So just beware when staying at the hotel about the breakfast price and internet. The fitness center is actually in a make-shift meeting room. There are a couple of pieces of equipment to use but it would be a little embrassing in your workout clothes and have 100 people for a meeting outside the door talking and watching you workout.

“great stay” Just returned from New York and the Affinia Dumont was one of the highlights. We stayed for 2 nights and everything was top notch. The location is great although it should be noted that the hotel is in a more residential area. Nevertheless, it was very easy to walk everywhere and the subway is 2 blocks away. The rooms are very spacious, nicely furnished and equiped with a kitchenette There's a market/deli on the corner which is a nice alternative to eating every meal out. The Murry Hill Diner around the block also offers great breakfasts. The only disappointment was that we requested a room on an upper floor, were told that our request was granted but were given a room on the 11th floor. So, we really didn't have a great view and it was a bit noisy due to street traffic. Overall, I highly recommend this hotel.

“Beautiful rooms” As a former Hilton Diamond member, we have stayed in many Embassy Suites and this is by far the nicest one we have stayed in. The rooms were as fancy as we have seen yet very comfortable. Really nice common areas and outdoor pool. The free breakfast was sheer mayhem and the food which is out for the masses to pick through looked gross. I do not recommend in July as it seems as though every family in America with kids is staying at this hotel. However, I highly recommend this hotel based on the rooms and common areas.

“Fabulous location in a beautifully designed hotel” I would give the James Chicago a 5 rating except for the cooling system. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The modern design is absolutely gorgeous. I was upgraded to a loft which had enough room for a family of 5! The amenities are top notch and I love the attention to 'green' details. You are one and 1/2 block off of the Magnificent Mile so the location is wonderful. I was able to get from my meeting to shopping in no time flat! The ONLY drawback is the air conditioning system. In my loft, it was incredibly noisy and it woke me each and every time it went on during the night. I was attending a meeting at the hotel and we had the same issues with the noise of the air conditioning. Not sure what they can do about this as I believe this may be a function of the older building.

“Avoid this hotel” I travel every week for business and stay at Holiday Inns almost exclusively. While checking in at this hotel, the two clerks on duty decided to have an arguement over room assignments while also trying to activate my room keys. Unfortunately for me, the keys were not properly activated and after arriving at my 7th floor room, via two seperate elevators, I had to go all the way back down again for them to activate the keys properly. Our room temp was set at 76 degress so we immediately turned on the A/C and set it to 70. When we retruned 3 hours later the room was still 74 degrees. The room never di cool off properly using the A/C. We tried to open a window but thye had been locked shut. We also then discovered our remote control was missing eyd when we had a new one brought up the person informed us that housekepign had been looking for a remote for this room but apparently never placed one in the room. After getting the TV situation squared away I went to the business center to check in for my flight. No printer was present in the business center so down to the front desk I went yet again. It's never a good sign at a hotel when you need to interact with the front desk on multiple occasions. I was able to use the front desk computer and was told that management was "working" on getting a new printer. Apparently $150 and a quick visit to Officemax is beyond their capability here. I asked for a manager on duty but there was none and the owner of the hotel doesn't come in until 9am when I'll be long gone. I've stayed at hotels like this in the past and most of the time the poor service can be directly traced back to poor management/ownership. You can't pick who owns and manages a hotel, Holiday Inn is supposed to do that for us and they have obviously failed with this location. While it is very close to Hollywood blvd, it's not worth the aggrevation. Did I mention the hotel pool has been closed for deck painting since January 28th. It's been over two weeks. Avoid this hotel at all costs.

“Very Happy!” We stayed at this hotel in June of 2004 and only paid $39 a night through Priceline. The free breakfasts were wonderful, our room was big and comfortable. We had absolutely no complaints and would stay there again . . . and again . . . and again.

“Solid Business Hotel” Very solid service and nice rooms. Ask for an upgraded room as they usually will accomodate requests if possible. Beautiful 1920's archecture that is well worth exploring the hotel. The roof top pool is not to be missed.

“Spacious rooms, great location” Three of us shared a room with 2 queen beds. The room and bathroom was very spacious, it was clean and quiet. Breakfast was pretty simple, being a Holiday Inn Express it was all about paper plates etc. The breakfast room would fill up quickly at peak time, so it was hard to get a table some mornings. There is a small supermarket/liqour store across the road, but not much else close by - great location though as it is a short walk to the walk of fame, restuarants, tourist information, train station. If you go to disneyland, either book the daytour through starlines (located at walk of fame) the day or two before, or actually stay at the hotels next to disneyland - we got public transport and it took 2-3hrs - absolute nightmare! We went with starlines to universal studios which was so easy - dropped us off and picked us up from hollywood walk of fame.

“Terrific for young kids!” I've never driven in SF and was a little nervous about it. It was super easy to get to the Hotel, and to park. We used muni for most of our stay which was fine, good busses nearby, plus my 7 and 5 yr old walked to Fisherman's Wharf once (not back!). My kids LOVED the hotel. They spent a lot of time in the pool, and loved the breakfast and cookies and lemonade. I liked that when the knob broke on our shower it was fixed immediately, and the room was very clean. Staff were very pleasant and accommodating. This place is a lot brighter and more family- oriented than other Joie De Vivre hotels we have stayed at- maybe not the place for a romantic getaway- but otherwise terrific!

“High marks for location” I only stayed one night and my room faced in, ie no view. It was comfortable and I was happy with my stay but I wouldn't call it either luxury or a boutique hotel as their website does. The main thing about the hotel is the location which is really excellent. Staff were friendly and helpful. Wi-fi in the room was free for me and fast. Some rather odd bathrobes provided, one was leopard skin patterned. The TV was the old type, ie CRT rather than LCD. The noise of the next room's door was sometimes as if it was my door which I found distracting on several occasions. Overall it was fine and I would stay again if in the area.

“Best kept New Years Eve secret!” We stayed for two nights, the first being New Years Eve, with our 5 yr old daughter. We had a Regency Club level room which is the way to go! New Years Eve they served hot/cold appetizers (plenty to make a meal) with an honor bar set up from 4pm. They brought out a wonderful dessert spread around 8 or 9. That was out with drinks (including champagne) until 12:30am. The club passed out streamers, noise makers, hats, champagne, etc just before midnight, and we had a beautiful view of the fireworks. In the club you almost feel like you're in a big living room. It was such a good crowd. Families and couples just hanging out playing games, talking, etc. The staff was excellent and so friendly. On New Years morning they had an upgrade to the usual continental breakfast with scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage. This was in addition to the regular items, oatmeal, dry cereal, fruits, yogurt, muffins, lox, etc. Juice, coffee, sodas and water are available all the time. They have free wireless internet on the club level (not in your room, just in the club, my one complaint) as well as computers with printers available for use, massage chairs and games they loan out. Parking is $57 per night at the hotel, for we opted for the self parking next door (valets will direct you). We paid $79 for 3 days there. Bart, cable cars and the trolley to take you to Fisherman's Wharf are just outside. Also have to try Crepe & Curry for excellent crepes which reminded me of France. I've already made our reservations for next New Years, that's how great it was for us.

“Seen worse” The hotel is conveniently located near the airport. Check-in process was quick and efficient, nice customer service. The room doesn't live up to expectations when compared to main hall. My first room didn't have a functioning LAN cable, and wireless wasn't stable enough. Asked to move, which they agreed to without questions. Second room didn't have any internet problems. The corridors had a nice perfume, not the usual musty smell of huge hotels. The bathroom is the most disappointing part of the room. A/C wasn't noisy, which is always nice in a hotel room. I couldn't get to any TV free channel. It seems like modern trend is to charge for anything and everything.. Newspaper service is USA Today, but you can get a real newspaper (Financial Times) in the Hilton Club on the 16th floor, or in one of the restaurants. I tried their restaurant ("The Cafe"): the salmon was just barely ok, but the veggies it came with were great. Again, good customer service. What I don't like is this modern trend for dimly illuminated restaurants.. They should invest a few $$ and call a lighting PRO. Breakfast buffet mediocre, I'd rather go with the free continental breakfast at the Hilton lounge if you have access to it. Bar is expensive like any hotel bars..

“Enjoyable stay” Stayed here for 3 nights with a friend. Overall I enjoyed this hotel and would stay here again although I had a few issues all pretty minor. Our room was a bit on the small side but very nicely appointed and clean. It looked like it had been recently renovated and housekeeping was always prompt and courteous. The bathroom was average. If I were staying here with my husband and two kids the room really might be a bit too small. But for two people it's fine. The fitness center was OK - decent equiptment and a good size. It's a close jog over to the mall so if you like to run that would be the place to go. Also decent indoor pool. The concierge was helpful in finding a particular movie for me in a nearby theater but I didn't get the impression they knew that much about local restaurants. They couldn't give me any information about the few restaurants that I inquired about (all pretty well known). The location is great if you are sightseeing. Just a couple of blocks (easy walk) to the mall, monuments, white house. And there is decent shopping nearby but better to just take a cab to Georgetown if you want to shop. Very slow elevators which I remember from my last stay at this property. Other guests also commented on this - it can get a bit annoying. Had room service twice - the first day I requested some coffee for 7AM and it came exactly at 7AM. Similar experience the second day. I had a to call a couple of times for more hangers and then another day for a corkscrew but both things showed up in a reasonable amount of time. For $199 I think this place is a good deal - FYI, for not much more you can stay at the Fairmont near Georgetown if you want to be in that area and the rooms are a lot bigger and just as nice.

“Holy Moly! What a Hotel” Wow! This is probably the best overall hotel I've stayed in. Here's the good and the bad: Good: -Location in downtown Houston and Minute Made park is fantastic -Lobby Scene is great -Beatiful hotel -Very nicely appointed rooms and amenities -Friendly staff that did everything perfect (wake up call, valets, checkin/out, etc...) Bad: -None, there is nothing bad about this hotel. I tried to find something but it performed flawlessly

“Customer service lacking” Upon checkin for a conference, which my company pre-paid my rooms for, i was informed I needed to present the pre-pay credit card or use my own personal card. I did not have the card, as our office manager made the reservation, and the card was in his possession. They would not let me check in, unless I put one night on my card. I then contacted our office manager who after explaining situation to at least 4 people, faxed over signed charge forms to keep the billing on office card, as originally arragned and he informed me all was taken care of. Upon checkout, the one night stay was still on my personal card. Desk person told me there was nothing she could do, and to call back on Monday. I called on Monday to also be sure me and company were not double billed for same room. Was informed I needed office manager with original card to call. he did and after 3 days, we have still heard nothing back about the resolution. First time in my extensive business travel I have encountered this situation. The desk staff were not helpful at all, and made me feel I was inconveniencing them. I know this is a minor complaint but when you travel constantly for business and try to follow your company protocol, it was disappointing to face the situation, but even worse to have no help in resolving. On the positive, the rooms were typical Marriott, very clean, comfortable beds, nice amenities. Conference venue was nice. Location was great.

“Deserves to be No. 1” This is a wonderful hotel for a business trip. The rooms were roomy and quiet. They had the desks and bathrooms one would expect. The bar was scrumptious and generous with the alcohol; a very nice place to see and be seen. Great service all around -- I mean it -- from the front desk to the bellman to the server to the concierge -- especially the concierge, who worked for a full 10-15 minutes to find us a good restaurant and worked it until she found it. This was a VERY pleasant place to stay and I would definitely stay there again.

“Great Downtown Location for Tourist” Got an amazing Hotwire rate of $69.00 for our stay in the Sheraton which made our stay all the more sweeter.This is a huge impersonal hotel but we were really happy with our stay and the location is ideal for tourists who like to be within walking distance of most of the downtown attractions of Denver. Our King room was very comfortable & clean & was situated in the tower with lovely views towards Civic Center park and the Denver Art Museum.The tower where most of the rooms are situated is actually across the road from the main reception building which makes it a little confusing for the first day .There is a covered over street walkway which allows access to the tower from the reception area .There is also an elevator directly from street level in the tower itself which is the easiest option to use and for security it requires your room card to operate .There are also separate elevators from the underground car park to either the tower rooms or the reception building. The Sheraton is situated directly on 16 St Mall which is an outdoor mostly pedestrian shopping district. Free buses run the length of 16 St and are great for cutting down on the foot slog when touring downtown.16 St is not a particularly good shopping area but has plenty of restaurants of all grades and can be great for people watching & enjoying the street entertainment.The free buses are also great for anyone staying in the Sheraton and going to a game in the Coors field. The Sheraton is within easy walking distance to the main art museums ,the State Capitol and the convention center.Katie Mullens is a great Irish bar with good food directly across the road from the Sheraton and was really buzzing the weekend we stayed .We also found Earls restaurant & Gumbos on 16th to be really good and within walking distance.

“Not bad for the price.” We spent one night at the Fairfax, after celebrating a friend's special event. The building and common areas are adequate, if not exceptional, and the bar was quite large and empty on a Friday night, so we had it to ourselves. The room itself was nice enough, but again, nothing exceptional. The hotel feels like a bit of a cross between a boutique hotel and larger chain. As with many boutique hotels, the front desk/check-in area is small, so when there are lots of people, it gets crowded and takes too long. Unlike many boutique hotels, I didn't find anything particularly charming about the place. The staff, however, were friendly and competent. My greatest disappointment was the sound-proofing, or lack thereof, in the rooms. We had hoped to sleep late the next morning, after being up late the night before, but the walls were so thin that we awoke early the next morning to the sound of conversation from the room next door, as if we were all in the same room. We could hardly complain to the gabby neighbors - they weren't being loud - they were just talking in normal voices, but we could hear everything loud and clear. The fault was not with the talkers, but with the walls. If not for the fact that we got a good price on Hotwire, I would have been very disappointed with the whole experience.

“Not good. Don't be fooled by the Camino Real name, this is a mess” I have stayed at MANY Camino Real properties in my life, including many of those that preserve and showcase the best of what Mexico has to offer. I really hope that Mr. Olegario Vazquez pays close attention to this property, which is doing great things to damage the Camino Real brand reputation. I confess that I was lured by such promise of impeccable service, high-quality food and high-end hotel amenities that I was used to with Camino Real. However, staying at the Camino Real El Paso was a big dissapointment. While I write this, I am also filling out a customer complaint form in my room, as I see that the manager does not bother answering (or even reading?) the Tripadvisor reviews. My arrival was at around 8 PM with 2 pieces of luggage. Despite the hotel's nice driveway, there is no doorman or bellboy to assist. I was greeted by an empty front desk, where I had to (literally) yell to be checked-in. My appointed room was decent sized but old, not landmark-style old but rather, simply old. The televisions are easily dated late 80 ́s or early 90's and so is the bedside clock. The bathrooms (and amenities) reminded me more of the love motels that I have visited, rather and a -luxury- hotel in Texas. I tried to order dinner but, to my surprise (or not?), the phone kept ringing in room service and nobody every picked up after 8 or 10 attempts. I then tried calling the front desk another 8 times, and same story. I had to go down to the front desk, yell again for attention (at least 3 people were in the office behind the front desk, not minding a bit about guests. I ordered dinner at the front desk and 45 minutes later, dinner arrived. I tasted only lightly what was brought. The quality was just horrendous. I had not had such a badly prepared dinner in many years, except from youth hostels...yes, that bad. After verifying that the room service or front desk phones would not pick up again, I went down to the lobby front desk to complain about the quality of dinner and to order breakfast. The server's answer to my complaint about dinner was that it was my fault as I had asked them to change the recipe (by simply ordering without onions). I guess, she has not traveled much, been trained properly and neither being served much. I have politely asked the front desk lady for a discount on my room fare (not that I really needed it), but honestly thought that no phone service, having to get dressed again twice to go down to the front desk, yell for service, complain about dinner and then getting a disrespectful answer from the server, were reasons enough for a -decently trained- manager to recognize the hotel's faults and need to compensate a guest. Well, I have still one more night to stay here and I really can't say that I look forward to it. I am just glad that I have much work to do and will just be back to sleep. Mr. Olegario Vazquez, please pay attention to your properties. This one is a shame --- bordering scam.

“Great hotel that needs just a few tweeks.” As far as this type of New York hotel goes this is up there with the best. We upgraded our room for more space and were given a very spacious room by New York standards. (Unfortunately, not the Empire State view). A good sized bathroom with an excellent shower once the hot water supply kicked in. I don't sleep very well in hotels but the bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept in and a good nights sleep was had most nights. It was only interupted by the late night crowd returning to their rooms and a nerd of a business man talking to his office on the phone at 6.40 in the morning from the corridor. Why don't they do these calls from the lobby or their room? The staff were helpful and the lobby was always vibrant with plenty going on. If you like a nice quiet hotel this is not for you as there is always some event going on most evenings and that quiet armchair in the corner with a night cap is not going to happen. The location is great, a subway stop around the corner that gets around the 5 boroughs very quickly, short walk to Macy's and Time Square. The fact that it is just south of 34th street means that the outside noise level is kept to minimum. Sounds great so why not give it 5 stars. Well, it takes at least 5 minutes to extract any hot water. The hotel was opened early 2009 and they still have not sorted the air conditioning properly, our room along with all the others was at a constant 72 degrees and no matter how much we tried it could not be altered. Even a guest from California found it too warm. The television reception was either good or downright bad. When any of these problems were queried we were told that they still had some teething problems, even after 15 months, come on guys. It was said in a nice way though. The other thing that I would query is the price on some of the room service. 5 star prices yes but not quite a 5 star hotel but real fun to stay in though.

“Nice hotel” My wife, 14 year old son, and I stayed two nights (4/6 and 4/7/07) in the "older" tower on the 21st floor. Nice clean room and bathroom, great beds, and a window that opens a few inches..enough to let in the nice sea air. The staff was extremely friendly and didn't mention the deep discounted internet P-line price. Our room overlooked the large, and busy pool and jacuzzi area. There were quite a few families with small children using the pool, which was warm. The exercise room is above average and you can avoid the $5.00 use fee by flashing your Hyatt card. The internet charge is a gouge and it's impossible to find out how much it costs unless you ask the front desk. There is no free internet in the lobby either. The parking of $20.00 per night in a covered building also seems extravagant in light of the amount people normally pay just to stay in the hotel. I thought the location was very convenient. Petco Park (home of the Padres) is an easy 13 minute walk. The Gaslamp District is only three or so blocks away. There is a great place to jog in the nearby park and cement trail along the edge of the marina. We didn't use the restaurant, but had a drink in the downstairs bar. I think we paid about $7.75 for an old fashioned and $7.50 for a glass (not a pint) of draft Pilsner Urquel. Considering a whole six pack is usually less than that, it's steep. One downside is the train tracks that are across the street. On Friday night two trains rambled very slowly through town and blew their horn at each and every intersection. With the window open, I thought the train was coming into the room. It woke me, my wife and probably half of downtown. My son, however, slept through it. The trains came by at 12:30 am and 2:30 am. Overall, I was glad we got this hotel and if I bid again for a 4* in the downtown area, I'd be happy to get it.

“Wonderful Hotel in NYC Times Square” We checked in a little early, so our room was not ready. The front desk clerk was super nice, inviting and warm. She politely offered us a seat in the bar area across from her, and had a bellman collect our bags. She informed us that she would text us both, once the room was ready. My biz partner went off into the city, and I asked for a key card to the gym, which was given without question. An hour later, we both received a text and was informed that we were upgraded to a higher floor/bigger room....something I was about to ask for ;) Nice touch indeed. The room was very large for NYC and Times Square...even the smaller rooms I saw, were easily 20% larger than the main competition, directly across the street! Stayed for 2 nights...did not have even one complaint! The room felt more like an Intercontinental hotel, than Hilton...so that was a nice surprise... view was great (bathroom a little old fashioned 90s elegance basic) but typical Hilton and nice enough. Shower was amazing! The housekeeping staff, were some of the friendliest Ive come across in North America...actually ALL of the staff exceeded my expectations in niceness! amazing! Even the bellman from the day before remembered my name, when I returned one night...nice! Great amenities, had a lovely meeting in the bar/lobby area. The location is great for Times Square and the Fashion district (just duck out the back door on 41st St) 42nd St is a zoo! but for tourists, they will LOVE IT!! Slept soundly each night. Great Gym several floors up, with nice views looking south (and free - unlike the hotel competition across the street) For being on 42nd Street (near 8th Ave) you'd never know it once inside the hotel. Plus the hotel rooms do not start until around the 15th floor I believe, so very very quiet! I use to live in Midtown, years ago..so I know the area very well. IF you want to be in the Times Sq area, I cannot recommend this hotel enough, and even for those on business, using the 41st Street entrance is the hidden gem, and the subway is not even a minute away. Port Authority bus station is also 2 mins walk, so handy for anyone who needs to get out of Manhattan for the day. Penn Station is a short cab ride or walk, 7 blocks south on 7th Ave! Enjoy!

“Great Hotel, including the Spa and Restaurant” My wife and I stayed at the Denver Ritz for one night on our way to Denver Airport from our Aspen vacation. We enjoyed a massage before dinner. Jade was a wonderful masseuse who really worked hard during the 50 minute rubdown. Prior to the massage, I enjoyed the whirlpool and steam room in the men's locker room, and admired the incredible work-out facility including the lap pool, basketball court, and multiple cardio and weight machines. These were free to use by Ritz guests at the neighboring fitness facility. Unfortunately, I didn't utilize these, but considering so many hotels charge extra these days for such facilities, I felt it worthwhile mentioning. We enjoyed dinner at Elways. The Tuna appetizer and soup were fantastic, the Steaks were some of the best I have ever had, and our servers were fantastic. We enjoyed a two block walk to the "16th Street Mall", and watched Happy Hour at the various restaurants extend past 10PM. The town was rockin'. Got a great package rate for the spa and restaurant with the room on the Ritz' website. Only downside was that my morning shower was lacking Hot-Water. Not sure if a lot of people were showering or there was a problem, but I will overlook it as the shower was great the night before, and when I told the front desk, they were very apologetic. I would gladly stay at this hotel again.

“Comfortable, great atmosphere...” I was looking for a good pool area, and Renaissance Austin delivered. I've stayed there before, but it was for business, not pleasure. I received an email with Marriott e-Breaks and decided to check it out. We were able to stay for $111 a night. Not bad for a full service hotel. There were very few guests. Our room was quiet. (I made a note to tell the reception staff that we didn't want any noise issues since I had seen a previous review). Our room was larger than I remembered in previous stays. We had two queen beds, a pull out sofa, and a lot of room to move around in. We also got a rollaway. The pull-out sofa didn't have linens, but it looked like it wouldn't be comfortable, so I had the twins share a bed. There was a nice indoor & outdoor pool, hot tub. The bartender was nice and made up a special drink for me that I could take to the pool. Nice tables everywhere. Didn't feel crowded at all. We spent almost $100 on breakfast for a family of 5. I thought that was a bit ridiculous. The food was pretty good, but extremely expensive. They did not offer a buffet the day we went. We did get complimentary mango smoothie shots, strawberry mini-muffins and herbed hash browns, all of which were very good. The staff was very friendly everywhere we went. We'll be back, but we won't eat breakfast there!

“Everything and more....” When reading these reviews there's always a doubt whether it's as good (or as bad) as previous travellers have said but let me assure you theWit is 100% as good as you've read. We stayed here for 6 nights beginning of January and were absolutely delighted. The staff couldn't have been nicer or more helpful - and cookies were gratefully received as we checked in. Our room was very large (and clean which is most important to me) and as we found out very quiet. When you alight from the lifts there is birdsong softly playing in the hallways which we thought very sweet... and then I think in the evening crickets can be heard! Each morning we had breakfast in State and Lake (the restaurant on ground floor), excellent food and great staff. If we wanted something that wasn't on the menu they were more than happy to get it fixed for us. Each evening they did turn-down service and left a little Wit gift in the room - nice touch. Location is excellent - we came into O'Hare so all we had to do was get the Blue Line all the way to Clarke & Lake station - out the station and two blocks to your left and you're at the hotel. All in all a fantastic stay.

“Wonderful beds and rooms” I had a great stay at the W City Center this July. There wasn't much of a view from the room but it's right downtown so I knew what to expect. The room was quite large and comfortable all the way from the bed (as usual for a W) to the chaise lounge by the 27 inch TV. The bathroom seemed quite large to me and the toilet had it's own little room. There was really good water pressure too. I was there over a weekend so the bar wasn't quite as crowded as it would be on a week night. As other's have noted the lobby area is great and well appointed. Then again so are the rooms. Housekeeping does a good job of keeping everything neat and clean. I enjoyed the food from room service, it arrived hot and fresh. All the staff I encountered were very friendly. I had some friends arrive a day later than me, I spoke to the Welcome Desk and they did their best to have their room ready early as my friend's flight got changed and they got to Chicago at 10:00am. They even gave them an upgrade! Eventhough it was very hot (Temps near 100) the A/C didn't give out at all. It's walking distance to shopping and Grant Park. The inroom coffee was nice but there's a Starbucks 1/2 a block away along with a couple of convience stores. The next time I need to be downtown Chicago this is the place I'll pick.

“Content with the Hilton San Francisco Union Square” First, let me start by writing about the location, which has been brought up in many of these reviews. The location of the hotel is in the “Tenderloin Neighborhood.” If you look up this area, it does state that the area is a high crime area. I would not however let this information alter your decision to want to stay here. Believe it or not, I loved the location. It was close to everything, including transportation. We stayed in Tower 3 and enjoyed our room immensely. In many other reviews, you will read about the different towers and how some more updated than others just as I did. When I approached the front desk I politely told them that I read on Trip Advisor that some rooms are more updated than other and if there was a more updated room available, I would appreciate it if we could stay there. The employee was very nice and explained how the rooms in Tower 3 were updated and he did have them available and just like that we were in a renovated room. If you are concerned, it won’t hurt to ask. The furnishings in the room were very dark in my opinion, but very updated. We were on a higher floor and the view of the city was a nice touch. There was a grey couch in the corner near the window as well. Internet was not free, however it was free in the lobby. My husband commented one night how the lobby felt like a train station, meaning it felt very crowded and people are sitting and waiting around. I agree with him. I think the lobby could really benefit from an added touch, either another room away from the check in. The line at the Starbucks at the hotel has to be one of the longest lines I’ve seen in awhile. We just opted to head down the street for coffee. The concierge was very helpful when we needed to set out on an adventure. The gym was very up to date and well equipped. It’s a little tricky to find, but just ask someone, they will guide you. Overall, we had a great stay. We wouldn’t be hesitant to book this hotel again. If you are concerned with the area, just ask someone at the hotel about it. Please don’t let this piece of information misguide your next reservation here. Enjoy your trip!

“Nice hotel but...” - Very good location. - Very nice room, good size, no noise. - Friendly staff. - We were not impressed with the restaurant however. Breakfast was ok except for the huge cockroach that walk under our table and manage to escape into the wall before the staff could get it. We also had dinner at the restaurant and were very disappointed. Go to 'Hook' instead.
“Right in airport” Flight canceled at 10 pm, called hotel from red carpet club and had room waiting for me - asleep by 10:15!

“Staff Friendly, But, rooms not pleasing” Let me start off by saying that I usually stay in 5-10 different hotels a year, and am a Silver VIP member with the Hilton HHonors program. I stayed in the Ritz Boston Common for New Years Eve 2005, on the Club Floor, with a Partial Boston Common view. My room rate was $499 plus tax. Rooms: The room was average, on the smaller side, however the bathroom was beautiful, with a shower, seperate tub, and marble galore. The room was clean, however there was a long hair in the tub, which I didn't bother calling about, since I didn't plan on using the tub anyways. The beds were comfortable, however I have stayed in Ramadas that had better pillows. Staff: Almost every staff member that I encountered was friendly and helpful, and did almost anything to get my requests, and also remembered me, and welcomed be back, whenever I would reenter. Dining: I can only comment on room service, which was beyond execptional, when my I returned to my room at 3am, and was hungry. They were able to make up a fresh fruit plate, and a cesar salad (Which was excellent) in less than 30 minutes. Also, the Private club lounge had some excellent food options throughout my stay, and the staff there was very friendly. Overall Opinion: I would definately NOT stay here again based on the rooms, however I would recommend coming back for the staff.

“Nice hotel” Although the location of this hotel leaves a little to be desired, it turned out to be fine. The set up is strange, you go into a small lobby, and then are instructed to take an elevator up one floor to the “real” lobby. It is small, not very charming, and the concierge desk was not often manned. If you are staying in the Times Square area, be warned, it’s very noisy. I would recommend that you stay closer to Rockefeller Center. It’s much quieter. That being said, our room itself wasn’t bad. The bed was wonderful, the bathroom was good sized and there was a coffee maker, and mini bar in the room. My only complaint about the room was that it didn’t feel real clean, it felt dusty and a little worn, but after our bad experience at the Grand Hyatt—it seemed pretty good. Don’t expect any extras though, unless you ask, they weren’t real big on customer service. I think it’s a NYC thing.

“Great airport hotel stopover” Hotel is located directly across the street from the SeaTac Airport. Lobby is huge and spacious, check-in was friendly and quick. Room was very nice, two double beds, flat screen TV, in room safe which is a big plus, nice bathroom, very clean, with huge fluffy towels. Also offers complimetary shampoo, body lotion, and conditioner. The one big minus is no free wifi, at $12.95 for 24 hours or $4.99 for one hour is in my opinion a rip off. But find that most American chains charge so guess they are in line with others. There is a restaurant, did not eat there, but prices seemed quite high. Free shuttle from/to the airport is included in the rate and runs every 20 minutes. There are a couple of restaurants in the area, 13 Coins about one block away, and some fast food restaurants about 3/4 blocks south. If you arrive by the Sond Transit Link train from downtown Seattle you are but steps away from the hotel. You can walk from the hotel to the airport in less than 10 minutes.

“Big, comfortable, clean, & central” Just as my title states. Stayed here 17-23 Aug in room 2301. Big corner room overlooking the Charles River. Arrived via Logan. Easy shuttle/subway ride to Copley station. Exited the station and walked down 1 block (other side of the library) to the hotel. At check in, standard room was upgraded to junior suite. Front Desk staff were friendly and helpful. Asked for a second refridgerator and it arrived minutes after I got into the room. Junior suite is a standard room and a half. Entered suite into a small hall with closet. Closet had sufficient number of wood hangers, iron, board, and mini safe with key. Hall opened up into a large area with work desk. including lamp, phone, and internet connection. Wireless internet also available and free access with suite. Bathroom was small but nice. Granite counter top, soap, shampoo, conditioner, lotion, body wash, hair dryer. Heavenly bath/double shower head had good pressure but I felt it too low for massage action. King pillowtop bed was supportive. Linens crisp, clean, good supportive pillows. Night stands with lamps on both sides. Pullout sofa bed, side chair, side tables, side chair with foot support, floor lamp, TV armoire, game control, remote, Sony clock radio, phone. Mini bar with key and basket of snacks. Looked well stocked BUT very over priced. $5 for king size candy, $7 for mini liquors. Housekeeping was terrific. Did an excellent job. Didn't use room service but from what I saw on the menu and on service carts in the hall, it looked good. I found the items overpriced. $18 for continental breakfast. Hotel is close to everything. Recommend getting the Transit Link Pass if you're in town for a week. $15 for 7 days. easy subway trains to everywhere you'd want to go in Boston/Cambridge.

“Be mindful of "turndown" service” I have stayed in hundreds of hotels. I have never heard of a hotel coming in your room at night to fix the bed (that you are about to sleep in) while you are gone. Yes I know the rule about putting the do not distrub sign on the door if u don't want/need housekeeping but never knew I had to put it out before we head out to a party at night. Be mindful of that "for select guest" when headed out. Other than that surprise when we returned at 2 in the morning, everything was great

“Great Hotel in a Great Location” The Ritz on Central Park is in a great location. The rooms are very nice, large and comfortable. Being across from Central Park and all the great shops of New York is convenient. We have also stayed there several times with our Yellow Lab and the hotel goes out of their way to accomodate our dog. They always bring her a dog bed, a bowl for food and water. The Club Lounge is also excellent. They have a great selection of food and the service is excellent. If you want to enjoy a great location, very nice hotel near all the shops and restaurants the Ritz is an excellent choice.

“Better than most of the reviews” Stayed now over 70 nights at this property this year. Much better than reviews indicate. Hotel staff is very accomodating to frequent guests. Karen, lead concierge, does a great job getting to know each guest by name and often has "surprises" in store such as gifts to take back for young children at home. Rooms are not huge but well appointed. King beds are very comfortable and often get upgraded to suite. Bathrooms are quite tiny however and most rooms only have showers. Concierge lounge is better than most. Good breakfasts and nice happy hours. Kevin, PM concierge, is very friendly and you can pretty much eat dinner in lounge if you wish. Bar downstairs has good atmosphere albeit at times a bit "cold NY style." Restuarant is much above standard Marriott property. A bit pricey but excellent food and one of the waiters is top-notch. Hotel parking is $23 a noted ... another option is too park under the Capitol. Would very much recommend to business travelers and seems better than other options in downtown Columbus area.

“Top Airporthotel” Wer eine Nacht direkt am Flughafen übernachten will oder vielleicht ja auch muss, der braucht ein zweckmäßiges und günstiges Hotel und das ist genau das was dieses Holiday Inn ist. Zu dem ist es auch noch sehr gepflegt und sehr sauber und das Personal sowie der Zimmerservice sind auch sehr freundlich. Das Frühstück war auch sehr reichhaltig und die Zimmer sind recht modern eingerichtet. Ich kan dieses Hotel sehr empfehlen.

“Depends on why you are staying here.” I had an excellent stay at this hotel. That being said, had circumstances been different, I might not have been as happy. To get the negatives out of the way, the location (while perfect for my trip) could be very inconvenient to a lot of people. It is very awkward to get here and parking is really inconvenient. Those are about the only negatives. I was in town for a wedding. The reception was taking place in the Union Station Ballroom. Naturally, this was a perfect location for me since there is an underground walkway/tunnel connecting the hotel to the reception venue! You can also access Reunion Tower (the skyline's Big Ball) directly off the hotel lobby as well. Our room had an amazing view of downtown. I booked my parents a room in the same hotel and they were not as lucky with the view. They got a stark view of the dried up Trinity River bed and the freeway. But both rooms were very comfortable and the open Atrium area is quite impressive. Like I said, the hotel was perfect for our needs but I would be hesitant to recommend it to a traveler simply looking to explore Dallas.

“Classic Stay” Staying at the Hay-Adams Hotel is an event in itself because of the historical aspects. I would have liked to have had a view (my room had a view of the alley), and a bigger bathroom (small, even for one travelor). But the touches were nice, i.e., bed turn down service in the evening, slippers by your bed on top of a little towel, and chocolates on your pillow). If I had the extra $, I would probably stay here again and get a room with a view. The service was fantastic. The only recommendation I would have is that the bed blanket had a square pattern to it, and I could feel the square pattern through the bed sheet, so it didn't make for a comfortable night sleep.

“Nice size room” We just returned from a night in NYC. My husband had business in the city and I played tag-a-long wife to shop and see a show. Park Central offered convenience and proximity to everywhere I wanted to walk. Our room was clean and larger than average by NYC standards. I got a deal on eliesureline.com for 165 including tax which again by NYC standards was pretty good. The gym was well equiped. Only problem was the check in line (long) and elevators (crowded and slow).

“Needs Improvement” I had the opportunity to take another business trip to Houston, Texas. If you read my previous review for the Courtyard Marriott at Brookhollow, located a few miles outside Houston, from a few weeks ago you will have found that I gave the hotel a fair review. However, I decided not to stay at the same hotel again because the ending of my stay wasn't so great plus the location is fairly far outside the area of Houston that I was working in. So this time around I decided to stay in a totally opposite area of Houston on the other side of the city near the Houston Medical Campus. This is brand new hotel and has only been open for just about a year, so its perfect timing for a fresh review on it. My thinking about booking this hotel was that it had to be better then the Brookhollow experience from a few weeks ago. Location: 7 of 10 The Courtyard Marriott is located just a few miles (2.3 miles) from the massive Texas Medical Campus in Houston. The hotel is located right off Main Street and is a straight shot right into the downtown of Houston. The location of this hotel is much better then the Brookhollow hotel by a long shot and has a lot more restaurants, shopping and general stores around the location. Right across from the Courtyard is a Marriott Residence Inn, and from the looks of it, the way the Courtyard is wedged into the property would make one assume that this location was probably the former parking lot for the Residence Inn. The Courtyard has an underground parking garage and extra parking in the back and I saw quite a few people walking from the parking garage to the Residence Inn. Overall, the location is adequate and easy to get to downtown Houston along with Texas Children's Hospital and surrounding medical facilities. However, one word of caution, I do not recommend trying to make a left hand turn out of the parking lot in the morning hours, its nearly impossible. Make a right turn and proceed down Kirby Avenue and go around the circle to get to the stop light on the other side if you have to go down main street. I knocked a full point off the rating because entering/exiting the hotel facilities for BOTH the Residence Inn and the Courtyard is brutal and horribly designed. In the architects/engineers favor, it doesn't seem they had many options to design it any differently. Service: 4 of 10 Most Marriott Hotels have fairly good service, even the previous stay at Brookhollow had a good service front desk. However, I am not sure what is going on with this Marriott. The front desk staff were a bunch of impolite, moody, unfriendly (insert any other remark!) people that I have dealt with at a Marriott in recent memory. I understand that you may not like your job, but please don't take it out on the guests at the hotel, its unacceptable and extremely unprofessional. The check-in process was acceptable, although as I mentioned above the the lady checking me in didn't even say good afternoon. When I asked if if I was going to be near the elevators or ice machine I got an attitude back and a response of "Well I put you a door or two down I think, I don't remember, if you are unhappy just call the front desk" and she proceeded to walk away like my question was unacceptable to her. The check-out process was even worse. First, every hotel should know by know that business people usually check out of their room early, and usually all at the same time. If you only have a single person working the front desk, PLEASE tell them to BE AT THE FRONT DESK! Its very frustrating to have to wait in line for a simple check out and even worse, have to walk around the corner of the front desk and walk into the back room and interrupt a casual conversation between two employees (that had NOTHING to do with work) and ask if you can be checked out!! Unacceptable! This Marriott failed on the "checkout scale" for me for this stay. Facilities: 7 of 10 for quality - 2 of 10 for Noise Suppression! This Courtyard had all of the typical Marriott specials and guest services including a gym, computer/office area, available printers, internet cafe (free) and cafe/breakfast bar/dinner bar. The lobby area was very spacious and open along with being inviting. There was a very large meeting area setup and casual area for sitting around and meeting with friends and family and holding small meetings. The hotel itself is designed with the new Marriott style "hip" or "contemporary" themed areas, I am not a huge fan of it but it is inviting and open. The BIG issue I have with this hotel is the lack of noise suppression in-between the rooms. I have NEVER been in a hotel where you can hear the person in the room next door crystal clear. At first I thought it was because of the pass through connecting doors between the rooms letting sound escape, but I was wrong. I could hear everything the person was saying in the room on my other side too, including his credit card number when he was on the phone ordering/confirming something. Not cool at all!! I don't know if they simply skipped on the sound suppression material between rooms or they used something cheap, but I was absolutely shocked how much I could hear. Final Rating: 6 of 10 Ok, final rating time, if you can deal with the noise between rooms then this hotel is nice and very acceptable. The rooms are beautiful inside with very comfortable beds and clean new bathrooms with a lot of room and functional layout. I have included some pictures of the room below and as you can see everything is new and designed well. However, I always am able to find something, in my room the carpeting was starting buckle and roll in locations. Basically it happens when the carpet wasn't pulled tight enough during installation, also using a cheap carpet can cause this. Eventually this will become a safety hazard to the elderly and even younger children as the carpet becomes even more uneven and can cause a trip or fall. Overall, I would stay here again. However I would ask for an end room or a room with no one next to me. Obviously I am sure I will get some "attitude" when asking for this, but the noise was just unacceptable for me, especially considering you can hear every single conversation that occurs between rooms and in the hallway.

“Good but stayed in better” Stayed on my own for 5 nights while visiting my daughter in NYC over Thanksgiving. Usually select smaller hotels but decided to try the W as it gave me Starrwood points. Checkin was slick and staff were helpful; the lobby is always busy but in this location you have to expect that. My room was as booked on a high floor (19th), large and comfortable overlooking Union Sq., but I experienced a lot of traffic and wind noise, because the windows did not fit together. This came to a head on my 3rd night which was very windy; I was kept awake by the 'screaming' nioise; someone came to the room to 'fix' it after I complained the following morning. This consisted of opening and closing it hard a couple of times, then jamming 2 towels in the gap between top and bottom window. It was effective but the promised proper repair never materialised and had not happened before I left, with the towels still hanging over the bottom window. Not what I expect from a hotel of this quality!

“Nice Hotel” As stated in previous posts; good central location, free parking, great deli downstairs, inviting outdoor pool, large rooms, got a great winter rate for less than $100 a nite...only negative would be the cleaning sanitizer spray used in the elevators - hotel needs to switch to a cleaning product that is not so strong...

“Location & rooms great, staff horrible” The surly and unhelpful front desk staff don't fit with what I've come to expect from a W hotel. Room was fine, location is great on Union Square. Bellboys were horrible, despite calling twice for help with luggage on checkout, no one came for half an hour. When I went down to bring a luggage cart up to just bring everything out myself, I was rudely yelled at that we couldn't bring one up despite there being 4 empty ones, and a group of bellboys huddled together having a conversation.

“What's in a name?” This hotel was built in 1927 and named after the summer residence of Winston Churchill. It is a quite sanctuary in downtown LA with a rooftop pool with breathtaking view of the downtown area skyscrapers. The only drawback is that its guest relations/ services department is understaffed and hence long lines are expected in the remarkably tiny reception area

“Noisy and a bit shabby” Hotel in an easy location if you are driving, just north of downtown Memphis close to the I-40. However, the room was a bit dirty and the paint in the bathroom was peeling. House keeping are quite noisy if you want to stay in bed late. As with most of Memphis though, the people are really friendly.

“Great location, but the quality lets it down” I too stayed at the Palaccio del Rio recently. Having read some of the negative comments,I wrote to the hotel voicing my concerns. As a diamond member of the Hilton group, normally the issues you raise are taken very seriously and I received a personalised letter from the Manager saying that the room would be checked personally. It wasn't. Although we had an executive Riverwalk room, it was supposed to be non-smoking, but the pillows were satuated with the smell of stale tobacco. The decor was tired and the balcony grubby and small. The woman on the reception wasn't exactly helpful, and when we went to the restaurant, having pre-booked a Riverwalk table, they had forgotten to reserve a place for us, so we went elsewhere, and checked out early the next day. Three weeks ago, I returned to the city, and because I had booked late, there was little choice, especially as I had my partner, our daughter and son-in-law, plus the three grandchildren in tow. We ended up at the Riverwalk Hampton Inn. We only had two rooms - both with two queen beds - but we couldn't get interconnecting rooms, despite requesting the facility, so one of the children had to come in with us. Unlike some reviewers, I didn't didn't use the Riverwalk access, so it was not an issue. The hotel was very well placed for all the main attractions, and just a short walk from the Rivercenter Mall and the Alamo. The price was $119 a night which included a movie night, where you got a free movie, popcorn and soft drinks, and that went down a treat seeing that they had an extensive choice of children's films like Lemony Snickett and the Polar Express. The reception staff were very helpful, and the buffet breakfast was a cut about the norm, so we wee all very pleasantly surprised.

“Great service - perfect location!” I recently stayed at the W San Francisco for a conference. My meetings were literally across the street at Moscone North and it couldn't have been more convenient. Even though the hotel is undergoing some renovation to the common areas and restaurant, the staff didn't miss a beat. The room was lovely and spacious with great views. I used the Acura car service to go to dinner across town and it was wonderful and such a nice perk. The W is a great location, whether you're in SF for business or leisure. I'll definitely stay again.

“Pleasant” Had a pleasant stay at the Indy Conrad. There was a slight glitch with the room, but the staff and manager were on top of it and made sure that we were happy. Food at the lounge was good, and the attached Capitol Grille was fabulous. I would definitely stay here again on my next trip to Indianapolis.

“OK for business” I stayed for two nights in mid-August at the Hilton Post Oak for a business trip. The overall hotel experience was average--acceptable for a business trip but nothing great or exceptional to make it stand out. A mid-day check-in was slow. Only one person was checking people in and when I tried to use the computer check-in, it was not working. During the check-in process, after complaining, I was upgraded to a suite for only $10/night. The lobby is rather unique--looks like it is going for the modern look but only 20 years ago so it appears dated. It just had a look I didn't find appealing. The suite was ok, but it is rapidly approaching the point of needing remodeled. Things just generally look dated. Positives of the hotel: 1) The pool is extremely nice, although there were no towels that I could find, thus requiring me to bring a room towel. 2) The elevators are prompt. I never waited more than five seconds for an elevator (helped by I was on the third floor). 3) The restaurant for breakfast is nice and the staff are very good here. 4) Great location near Galleria. Negatives: The business center charges for their internet usage at 50cents/minute. I find this CHEAP of Hilton and was very annoyed to actually have to pay to print off boarding passes, etc. My other negative experience concerned the pay snacks. When I first entered the room I noticed that my refrigerator containing the snacks was totally empty - I never opened it again and just thought the hotel did not provide pay snacks. When I got my hotel bill - I had been charged over $300 extra for every snack that they stock! I had the manager come to my room and complained to him in person. He said the system was automated and he immediately corrected the bill. Overall, if I was going back, I would probably try the nearby Marriott.

“Good stay - a little off the beaten path” I just stayed here for a conference. It's a little out of the way for downtown Chicago, but there are always cabs available. The room was perfectly acceptable with a large flat screen TV that had HD service. I found the bed to be ridiculously comfortable. President's Club members get the basic bandwidth at no cost, but it's not very fast so you really need to upgrade for $10/day. If you're not a member, it's like $25/day. The gym is pretty large and they give you a towel and bottle of water when you get there, again, if you're a member of the loyalty program. There are like 9 treadmills, 4 ellipticals, a bunch of bikes, a stepper and plenty of weights. It also looks like a very nice spa (but didn't use). All the staff members, from the front desk to the bellhops to the doormen were very professional and pleasant. They are very good ambassadors for the company. The food at the conference was average, and from what I understand ridiculously expensive. It's a union hotel, so that's got to factor into the cost structure. Overall, I don't stay at Fairmonts much, so I wouldn't choose it over the other brands that I typically stay at, but if you do like Fairmonts (or don't care about points), then you'll enjoy your stay.

“OK but....” Nice hotel, good location for union square. As a platinum member, wasn't treated that way. average room, comfortable as always westin bed. check in - 2 people, check in wasn't too bad. check out - i needed a revised receipt, one person - 730 AM - and the person in front of me had issues that required lengthy assistance. come on - only one agent at 730 AM? as for the bar, nice bar, good drinks but no desserts, just bar bites. lastly, for a beautiful hotel, no nice area with sofas and reduced lighting in the lobby. Overall - average. elevator system is interesting and actually works pretty well.

“Step directly into or away from the cocophany of Times Square” This Crowne Plaza hotel is really a part of Times Square. Note that the lobby is on the 2nd floor, and that one enters through the parking garage from either 48th or 49th Street, or through a small doorway on Broadway between those streets. It's a big, somewhat impersonal place with good employees who make you feel welcome (we experienced a friendly valet, desk clerk, concierge, and housekeeper all in quick succession). Views of the Hudson River from our 44th-floor room were remarkable (the "other" side of the hotel overlooks the bright lights of Times Square). The bed was quite comfortable, bathroom was well-appointed; both were very clean and in good shape. Elevator service was able to keep up with a busy summer weekend crowd. In-room wifi seemed pretty expensive ($14.95), as did in-house breakfast buffet ($30). "Restaurant Row" (46th street between 8th & 9th Avenues) is only a block away.

“Charm plus cardio--how can you miss?” If you arrive in downtown Seattle via public transportation, the first thing you'll notice about Virginia Mason is the hike up First Hill. (I'd told the kids to pack light.) Though the Inn seemed a bit too out of the way initially, I was grateful for the location when evening arrived and the huge SeaFair parade began weaving through downtown. We were able to walk to most of the attractions in Seattle from the hotel: downhill to the waterfront, over to the Space Needle, back to Pioneer Square. Though the kids complained about the lack of a pool, the room itself was spacious and clean, with a bathroom big enough for a small party and enough beds to accommodate our family of six. The staff was pleasant and accommodating, plus the place felt cozy--a pleasant contrast to the chains where we spent most of our vacation.

“It's okay” Double Tree, as I understand it, are meant to be Hilton-standard hotels, but in buildings that are not purpose-built. This Double Tree needs, and is getting, a revamp (by Gensler, of Apple store design fame) and I would say it's about time. Although the hotel is not shabby, it has been left behind by new Garden Inns and alike that are probably a few dollars less to stay in. The rooms, naturally, are a bit pokey; my loo got blocked and I had to call three times (at the weekend mind); they didn't notice my HH Gold status at check-in; they also charge bag check if you check out but want to leave your bags (although apparently not on the way in). Erm, that's it I think. Location-wise it's fine (opposite the Waldorf actually) and you can easily walk three or four blocks to the upmarket shops, of across to the theatres. By the way, there was a bed-bug workers union sort of protest outside the hotel, but I had no problem whatsoever in this respect of bugs...the hotel was clean.

“Perfect.” Typically, I stay in boutique hotels when I travel to Seattle. However, my wife and I decided to stay at the Four Seasons for a long weekend and it was perfect. We had a bay view room and it was just magnificent. The price was comparable to other hotels and the location was unbeatable. We never got around to the onsite restaurant but room service was very good. Ate breakfast while overlooking the bay.

“great value for money in great location” Just returned from nine nights at the Hampton Inn and what an excellent Manhattan hotel this is. It's not a luxury hotel but who wants to sit arround their hotel in New York? It's clean, comfortable and has very good facilites. My room at the back on the 14th floor was very comfortable and quiet. Beds are very comfortable and room facilites good. There is a good breakfast available, included in the room price providing a good range of foods to get the day started, even allowing for the paper plates and plastic cutlery. The staff are friendly and helpful and the hotel is in a great location for getting around New York. Overall, excellent value for money and highly recommended.
“Very good hotel” This hotel is a good place to stay in LA. Everything was good except for breakfast, which was very poor.

“For a Kimpton, I was a bit disappointed.” Kimpton has become my favorite chain. So I was a bit disappointed in the lackluster service at this one. As others have noted, the building is a grand old thing, with typical stylish Kimpton furnishings. But I shouldn't have had to ask 3 times for a yoga bag to be delivered (the one I requested in my on-line reservation) or the non-feather pillows. (Curiously, the bag lacked even a strap -- though if you turned on the available Yoga routines on the Kimpton channels, straps were "required" for many of the exercises.) The staff was exceedingly polite, the room was comfortable, and parking -- mandatory valet -- was $36 a night. Make sure you join their frequent guest club to take advantage of the free internet and raid-the-mini-bar. All guests enjoy the complimentary drink-and-snack reception in the evening. Note that at night the neighborhood does get a bit deserted; not necessarily to the point of feeling unsafe, but walking around I was certainly on my guard, so I would probably choose a slightly different area. Otherwise, not much to say. Other than the a-typical service issues, it's your standard upscale Kimpton.

“Great Service, always.” I stay at this property at least once a month on business. While it's not the closest hotel to my work location, I like it because travelling on business is no fun, but this property always makes me feel at home. From the bellman at the front door, to the folks who deliver room service, to the waiters at Craft and the masseuse at Bliss, each is professional, accomodating and pleasant to be around. And I love that ~2 days prior to my arrival, I always receive an email asking me if there's anything I need or anything hey should prep for my visit. They take this very seriously. The rooms are appointed with everything you would find in your own home, from down comforters to ipod docking stations as well as your own munchie station should you require a late night snack. My favorite though are the Bliss bath products. It's like having a spa in your room, should you choose not to make an appointment at their fabulous spa, Bliss. The only area of the hotel that seems to need a bit of brushing up is the coordination of the staff at the front desk. No matter what time of day I check in/out, there only appears to be one person on duty. Sometimes the wait can be more than I like, but I overlook it for the rest of the property is suberb. Note, while this hotel is directly across from American Arena, there are only a few great restaurants in walking distance, so most likely you'll get into your auto to eat. Overall a great pick for work or vacation.

“Huge, Comfortable Rooms but shabby, tired looking” My friend and I stayed at the Fairmont San Francisco for 3 nights in January. We absolutely loved the hotel's stunning architectural features and the spacious, oversized rooms. We booked at a very low rate on Expedia so we expected a less than spectacular room. We were given a room with a view directly into the Mark Hopkins across the street. The room was quiet, with a large flat screen TV and the beds were absolutely fantastic. The decor was nice, but the carpets stained, furniture chipped and scratched, walls showing luggage marks, paint chipping, and the bathroom really needed a make over. The wall paper was peeling, there was rust on the vents, and the sink area was way too small for such a large space. The hotel gym was nice and spacious, but the $15 daily surcharge was absurd. We also skipped the overpriced breakfast. Overall, a wonderful stay but would probably not stay here again. The hotel has seen better days and has a shabby feel to it. It really does not feel like a luxury property and more like a very good, 3 star hotel.

“Nice suites, working (free) wifi, i liked it” I got updraded to a suite, though it was kinda wasted on me! I was just staying one night, and I got in at 10pm or so. Wifi worked, and was free (after registering in the kimpton rewards program). plenty of hot water, and towels, and the bed was comfortable. The desk had enough power outlets for my computer and chargers (the small things in life...). the flatscreen TV looked great on the wall (no time to turn it on!). Room was completely quiet. I didn't hear another soul. Location was great. I stayed here on business, so I can't comment on whether it is a good hotel for family or not.

“Great rooms but was quite noisy” The hotel itself is really great. By itself I would have rated it a 4 (at least). But my room was xx048 which is on a side where there is a tall building across the street and lots of traffic on the road below so the sirens and busses generated a lot of noise all night. Was at a conference. The food was fabulous, the location is great, and the people are too. It is just hard to give it a great rating with the night noise

“solid service, quiet room, great location” we have stayed here numerous times over the past 5 years. suggest getting a suite for a little more space and a room with mountain views. check in is always a pleasure. decent buffet breakfast with an excellent staff. minimal exercise room but ok if not crowded. i stayed here recently even though we had reservations at the jw marriott in cherry creek- 1/3 the price and i got the same nice sleep.

“Great hotel--a nice surprise” I stayed at the Serrano Hotel for one night only for business and the company I worked for arranged the hotel reservation. It was a lovely hotel, my room was cozy and nicely decorated, and the food was excellent. All for a very decent price. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

“Wrong side of highway - need car - free parking” This hotel is a little isolated - averaged Doubletree, no complaints. But minimal restaurant on site, so you need to go elsewhere for lunch or dinner. Nothing in walking distance. Be very careful with cab from airport - although I mentioned Doubletree University, they took me to the downtime hotel. That concierge was very helpful, and their shuttle took me to the correct hotel. {there is also a 3rd Doubletree both of the University. If you are walking choose the other Doubletree on 15th - nearing everything, but expensive parking. If you are driving, this is the better choice. Plenty of free parking.

“Great spot in Downtown Seattle” Recently travelled here with my fiance as we were visiting Seattle on vacation. One of the best check in experiences I have ever had. Since I am a member of the President's club, we did not even have to go to the reception, the doorman simply provided us with our room keys and we were off. Amazing! The hotel itself is older and charming. It has that kind of old elegance that you would expect from a Fairmont. The rooms are large and well appointed with flat screen TV's. The pool, gym and hot tub areas are great. Staff was helpful and accommodating. I really can't say anything bad about this place. Will definitely return next time I'm in Seattle. PS if you are looking for a good spot for dinner make sure to try out Purple next door. Amazing ambience, food and wine!

“Good location for Bush Airport. Huge hotel - very modern” I had 1 evening here in October on a trip back from Central America to the UK. Nice room, huge lobby, decent lounge for Hilton Honours members. Did not get to use any other facilities. Standard US Hilton fare.

“Genuinely warm reception in an excellent location” We have stayed here twice recently and each time have received genuinely warm treatment and really excellent service. The rooms are a good size, many or most with a balcony facing the sunrise or the sunset, nice for coffee in the morning or glass of wine at sunset. Rooms are contemporary and the beds very comfortable. Bathrooms are big, although the light can be a little dim, and modern but in need soon of some renovation. Large closets and plenty of storage. Ample desk space. The facilities and location of the hotel are excellent.
