Very large and inviting pool and surrounding bar area and a large related work-out facility (with extra charge however) The lobby and bar areas are attractive and nice places to sit and read, people watch or eat or drink. The hotel is close to Rodeo drive (a long walk or quick cab ride) and the Century City shopping mall is across the road with high end and fun shops to while away some time or go to eat or a movie. Each time we were there the personnel did something genuinely nice for us and we felt like welcomed guests, which is greatly appreciated as much as we travel.
“Pas mal” Chambres classiques taco Bell et Mac fo a proximité petit dej gratuit 12$ le parking par jour. Bref un bon hotel rapport qualité prix. Et en plus assez calme .

“It's standard fayre” Well, this hotel is okay, I think I chose it becuase it was relatively inexpensive (I am also HH Gold (room upgrade, internet, breakfast etc) and I was just putting my head down for the night. DOn't expect anything too special, and, again, I feel like I'd have been better off in a new Garden Inn than a not too exciting Double Tree. The rooms here are, of course, a bit pokey (I got a room with a little sitting room, so was actually okay) but this place feels a bit uninspired. The breakfast was also not that great. On the plus it was clean, very nice staff (which is always important to me) and I have no overall complaints.

“Clean Decent Hotel in Great Location” We tried to book a hotel way in advance and I had trouble finding anywhere. I was a little worried about staying in a Courtyard in the middle of a big city, although I have stayed at them other times and thought they were fine. This one was in the best area! Just a great location where you could walk and get good restaurants, walk to the Navy Pier, walk to 2 movie theaters, shops, etc., no problem. Our room was very nice and a good size. We had a nice view of the city. We asked the concierge for restaurant reservations and that worked out well. We were very happy with the location and the hotel was clean and decent. We had breakfast across the street at the Dunkin Donuts which worked out fine.

“Great for a Business or Pleasure Trip” I thought this hotel was actually perfect in lots of little ways. Bar and restaurant downstairs was very nice and cozy on a rainy evening. Servers were all very gracious and attentive. Door/valet team was GREAT. The room was quite nice, great rainfall shower, beds were VERY comfy. Room service for breakfast in the morning was EXCELLENT. Good location, etc. Generally just a great hotel. Not going to blow you away but if you can get a decent price or are traveling for business, you can't go wrong here. Oh and I LOVED that they had a nice coffee cafe right in the lobby - very convenient to grab an iced coffee and hop in a cab for a meeting.

“Great location, good staff, nice but small rooms, REVIEW your bill” I normally stay at either a Hilton family hotel in Times Square/Hells Kitchen or the HGI on 28th when I am in NYC and after reading some flyer talk reviews decided to give this property a shot when I found a rate similar to the HGI on 28th for a weekend trip this past weekend. Great staff, especially Lenny at the front desk and Raggo the bartender. I did an Online check in for room 811 and got there to find out I was not assigned that room (was an end room) and was told my room was 1810. Lenny was the clerk that checked me and told me that someone was in 811 and they didn't have any end rooms available but could try moving me Saturday and I just said I would stay in the same room both nights. The elevators require a keycard and will only work for your floor which I liked. The card got me up to 18 but didn't work for my room. I went back to the lobby and Lenny remembered my room number and my keycard got recoded and worked fine. I was also thanked for my loyality as a diamond member upon checkin and he remembered my name the next night when I entered the hotel which I always appreciate from a hotel employee. There was no exec lounge, but K-cup coffee brewers in the room and the free breakfast is the best I have had at a hilton in a while. If you wanted a hot breakfast instead of continental you could chose from a variety of hot entrees from a special menu along with a side and juice or coffee with the voucher with no upcharge. The rooms were very small but modern and the toiletries in the bathroom were great. The room I had was way too noisy. Even with the TV on I could hear people entering and leaving their rooms and people talking in the hallway. The Wifi worked great and there were two computers downstairs you could use for free which I utilized after checkout to print my boarding pass. Location is great. Only a couple blocks from the 28th street 1-line and I don't mind walking and it is a easy walk to the theater district. I ate at the restaurant on Friday night and the hamburger was very good but expensive. Total bill with tip was over $40 for just a cheesburger, fries and a drink. The bartender Raggo was very good and really friendly. I didn't go to the roof bar but it sounded fun. Couple problems with my stay: They only have three elevators and on Saturday they took the one out of service with a sign that said "reserved for a special event". They have an elevator dedicted to the roof bar and only 3 elevators for guests so I felt they shouldn't have taken an elevator out of service on a saturday for their guests. When reviewing my bill Sunday morning I noticed the total was very high. My room rate was to have been only $239 a night and I was charged $315 for one night and $350 for the other night. I went to the front desk to have them correct the problem and there was a long wait to talk to someone. On a sunday morning at 11 they only had 3 employees working at the front desk. After finally getting to speak with someone I showed them my email confirm on my IPAD, they said they would correct the bill. I was given a 2 p.m. check out and returned to the property around 1:15 after being out in the city to go to my room to pack and the keycard wouldn't work again and meant waiting in line again for the card to recoded again.

“What a nice little boutique hotel” The Grand Hyatt was oversold so they gave me the option of transfering to the Monaco, at their cost. I have to say it was a good choice to move. The rooms, while on the small side, are well appointed and charming. There was both a new TV and stereo system as well as free internet service (wireless and wired) througout the hotel. The only negative I saw was the lack of a pool. The hotel was also quirky in that they provide (for a fee) bath packages you can buy and they have a cocktail hour with neck massage machines.

“No complaints here!” My friend and I spent two nights here recently, in a room with two queen beds. We loved the amenities in the room, the coffee maker, fridge and microwave, and the very comfortable beds. We were impressed by the 20 foot ceilings too, and liked the hardwood floors much better than the usual hotel carpet that collects odors. There is a smart phone which controls lights, TV etc and local and long distance calls are free! The location is very central, and we walked to the Old City, to Rittenhouse Square and to the SEPTA train station very easily. As two women traveling alone we saw nothing in the area that made us feel unsafe. While it is true that the room has only one chair, so sitting on the bed is the best option, that did not bother us at all. The free breakfast delivered to us was very simple, and reminded me of what airlines used to serve. If you want a hot meal with all the fixins then you should opt for a full service restaraunt! We were on the second floor, and the nightclub noise was not an issue in the corner room, We could see the courtyard dining area of the club from our room, and we had a great brunch there on Sunday. We could hear diners seated outside from our room Saturday evening, but as the night got cooler, most people went inside, so we were able to sleep just fine. I would return here for sure, next time I stay in Philly, and would ask for a room a couple of floors up in the summer to minimize courtyard noise. A big plus is that it is just a few blocks to my favorite Philly eatery - the Midtown Continental at Chestnut and 18th St. We also had a REALLY good steak at the Plough and Stars on 2nd St.

“Great hotel in a great location” My wife and I spent 3 days in NYC at the end of September and had reserved a room at the Holiday Inn Express based on the reviews seen here on TA. The reviews are right on. The rooms were indeed small, but we weren't in NYC to hang out in our room. Even though the room was small, it was very clean. The breakfast was good and the breakfast area was somewhat small, but we were always able to get a table. The entire staff was helpful and friendly from those at the front desk to the cleaning staff (when we asked about where to go for cheesecake a place called Juniors was recommended and it was very good). They even hailed a yellow cab for us when we needed to get back to the airport. The best thing about the hotel, though, was its location. 2 blocks from Times Square, an easy 10-15 minute walk to Central Park, minutes from Grand Central Terminal and 10 minutes or so from Rockefeller Center. One thing to be aware of if you stay.....the elevators can be very slow at times especially when the rooms are being cleaned.

“Nice good quality Sheraton, not outstanding, but nothing wrong with it either.” Stayed here for one short night recently (late in and early out) but everything was very good. Dinner through room service was delicious but very overpriced ($11 for a small cup of berries!). The breakfast buffet in the restaurant was excellent as well with a very large selection of items. Valet parking also seemed overpriced compared to other hotels nearby. The staff was fabulous! Very friendly and helpful staff (wanted a room overlooking the airport and was accommodated by a very helpful front desk agent). In the end was given the view I wanted and also upgrade to a very large corner suite (I'm SPG Platinum). However, the room furnishings are a little dated - the carpets need replacing and the desk chair was very uncomfortable and old (vinyl). Most hotels have ergonomic desk chairs these days but this one was far from it.

“Not too bad” Spend three nights at the Marriott that is connected to the Convention Center in San Jose. Check-in and check-out was quick and easy. It's your typical Marriott - high-mid-level hotel. There is a Starbucks style shop in the lobby - they aren't Starbucks owned, but do serve Starbucks coffee. You can also get your sundries here. They have a display case for bakery items, but every time I went down in the morning, it was pretty much empty. They said that the deliveries are made at 7am. So if you don't need to be up before then, you'd probably be alright. There is no free parking at the hotel - there is only paid parking in the convention center lot ($20/night) or valet (unknown cost). The elevators are very frustrating - four of them and you can expect to wait a while for any of them. The room - decent sized room, but the bed was WAY too soft. Wireless is NOT free (WHY is it that hotels still charge $10-15/night for wireless? It's obnoxious with how much the room already costs). The bathroom is up-to-date, but the shower does not have a lot of water pressure. If you find yourself with the munchies after 9pm, you're hard pressed to find anything outside of a full-serve restaurant. San Diego State University is about 4 blocks away and there is a large number of restaurants within walking distance. That being said, if you walk the wrong four blocks, it seems to be sketchy.

“The Fairmont Dallas” Il Fairmont è in una posizione molto buona per il centro di Dallas, 1 isolato dalla linea McKinney Ave carrello; 4 blocchi da West End Area e 4 isolati da Main Street con numerosi bar e ristoranti e Neiman Marcus. L'area si sentiva molto sicuro e la passeggiata (se non fosse stato di 100 gradi), molto piacevole. L'hotel stesso era ordinato e pulito e il personale molto cortese. Una cosa che ci è piaciuto è stata la camera di albergo ha avuto 2 piacevole, comode sedie con un tavolo e un sacco di luce - più, di solito si ottiene solo un letto e una scrivania, ma la stanza era molto confortevole per prendere un paio di minuti per rilassarsi e rilassarsi. Il portiere è stato eccellente. Un tesoro "sconosciuto" è solo un paio di isolati di distanza nel Palazzo Chase, che ha una torre di osservazione (ingresso libero), che non è solo bello in sé e per sé, ma belle vedute di Dallas.

“Charming Historic Property with Personal Service” I’m a DC native who no longer lives in the area, but I had the luxury of visiting and staying in this friendly, low-key hotel for one night while conducting business and visiting the National Gallery of Art. The location is perfect for downtown sights and accessible to so many neighborhoods by foot. The hotel itself is charming, inviting and simple with an emphasis on retaining its historic features. The rooms are lovely in a non-slick-boutique-hotel way, and the staff was super friendly. We were upgraded to a suite, which was really wonderful. We wished we could have stayed longer. Personalized service is definitely a priority. Exceptional value.

“Good Budget Stay With Excellent Public Transport Links” I don't drive. You'd think that might be a problem in L.A. Fortunately public transport & cabs are better than most tourists from Europe envisage. I landed in Burbank - if you are arriving domestic it's great - under $50 in a cab from Burbank this hotel is a good solid budget hotel. No frills but clean, quiet apart from the helicopters landing at the hospital (all adds to the atmosphere) pleasant staff and safe. Big sell is the metro station 1 minutes walk which gets you to main tourist strip in about 10 minutes for $1.50 . I was there to meet friends in other parts of town but still found location useful. I'm going back to L.A. soon and will be staying here again. Only down point. I ordered a shuttle pick up for 8am from reception - it didn't arrive by 8.10 so I shared a cab with a fellow guest, $5 deposit down, no big deal but worth a mention for the nervy flier.

“Hotel charge credit card for stay, even cancel 16 days before arrival date” Well, more problem with this hotel again. Our office asked and received assurance from both Quikbook and directly from the Best Western Seaport Inn response to us that we can cancel our advance reservation free of charge if my cancellation is 10 days before arrival. I made advance hotel reservation in August 2009 at QuikBook for 5 nights stay in Oct 26, 2009. I send several email to Best Western Seaport Inn customer service request that we will arrive very late after international flight and want to make sure we get no-smoking room we need. We never received any reply from the hotel. So, we canceled the advance reservation on Oct 10, 2009 and stayed at different hotel. Well, today, my credit card statement arrived and Best Western Seaport Inn charged me one day of stay. We have called our credit card and refuse this charge. But, I assume hassle persist. I assume this hotel will charge your credit card even if you cancel your reservation 16 days ahead of arrival date. This is absolutely unacceptable.

“Great home base for a one day Seattle tour!” We (my wife, two children, and I) had 24 hours in Seattle last week. This was planned on short notice so I tried to find a deal for a room, but didn't have much time to do my homework. I ended up booking a room for about $100 on Hotwire after bidding unsuccessfully for a 3 star on Priceline. Our flight into Seattle arrived very early (8am) on a Tuesday morning, and we were in our rental car in downtown Seattle by 10am; I didn't want to cruise blindly through town, so I thought I would just park the car at the hotel and check in later in the afternoon and we could walk around downtown. As I pulled up to the valet parking attendant at the front door, I had the bellman grab our bags and I headed to the front desk to get registered. The desk clerk was very courteous, and said that she had a room ready if we would like to have our bags brought up to the room now...I was very pleasantly surprised, as all three employees to this point were very friendly and courteous, and treated me as a valued guest. We went up to our room, which was on the 22nd floor and facing south; great view of the other downtown skyscrapers, but facing away from the Puget Sound and Space Needle. Oh well, we weren't planning on spending much time in the room. I flopped on the bed for a few minutes while the others were getting ready and I noticed that the bed was extremely comfortable, one of the best I have encountered in many hotel stays over the past 10 years. The room was very clean, the furnishings were a little dated but in nice shape, and there was plenty of room for the four of us to spread out. Although the room was directly above Interstate 5, and the hotel provided a kit including ear plugs and other (non-drug) aids to sleep, the noise was not very audible from our room. The location of this hotel is perfect if you plan on just "doing" downtown Seattle; we walked down to the Public Market (Pike Street), to the Westlake Monorail station, then down to Pioneer Square. The hotel was pretty much central to all of these attractions (a little further south, but still walkable, are the baseball and football stadiums). The only time I felt like we were being taken was the valet parking fee of $25, but that is pretty much standard in the larger downtown hotels now. I feel like the 24 hours we spent in Seattle at the Crowne Plaza was truly a bargain, and I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to friends, especially if you can work a deal on Hotwire or equivalent.

“Best hotel I've ever stayed in.” Absolutely loved this hotel. The room was very spacious, the pool is lovely, the cookies are great, and the staff was wonderful. We hosted a work function there and the events people were excellent, too.

“What a Nice Hampton Inn!” We chose this hotel for 3 reasons: 1) We're Hilton Honors members and were looking to stay in a Hilton property; 2) We liked the location--an easy walk from the MARC train station and 3) The reviews on this site have been very positive. When making our reservation, we noticed that a room with one king-sized bed cost the same as a room with a king-sized bed and a sofa bed. Given that, we chose the latter. We were given a corner room on the 4th floor. The view wasn't the greatest on one side--across the street was an electrical substation. However, the view from the other window was nice--next to the hotel is an old brick building that had a great mural of the Inner Harbor on the wall. The bed was comfortable--no complaints there. The bathroom had a granite countertop. The only problem was that the sink was too high. I'm short and my husband is average height and we both agreed the sink could have been lower. The hotel provides some toiletries--shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash and lotion. Also provided are shower caps, a makeup remover cloth and a shoeshine cloth. We were pleasantly surprised to find a refrigerator in the room. This especially nice to have in hot weather for storing cold drinks. The free breakfast was decent. In addition to pastries, cereal, milk, yogurt, juices, fruit and coffee, there are some hot items. Both days there were eggs. In addition, one day there was biscuits and gravy and another day there were sausage patties. At night, there are free cookies at the check-in desk. Also, by the desk, there is an area where you can purchase cold drinks, ice cream and snacks. Each floor had a soda vending machine and an ice machine. Housekeeping was excellent. All the staff was friendly and helpful. Thinking back on the experience, I have to say that the hotel offered many amenities that made the stay very pleasant. We would certainly stay here again next time we're in town!

“Great Location, boutique decor, comfortable environment” Stayed at the Clift for 5 days/nights. The foyer/reception is stunning and a great place to chill/chat. The open fire is great for a warm, Our room was small anf ull of mirrors, too many mirrors for my liking however it was very stylish and curtains are provided to hide the large mirrors which can be a little off putting first thing when you wake up in a morning. The room was clean, stylish, our housekeeper came everyday without fail. The bed was comfortable and cosy providing a great nights sleep. Starbucks and a Walmart across the road which was fabulous. Cons= We were woken every morning at 7.30am by a young boy knocking on one of our neighbours door saying 'Grandpa let me in, are you awake? Moms asked me to wake you up!'. Loud knocking would continue for at least 10 minutes every morning at the same time. The walls seems fairly thick however the doors are not. We found this highly annoying and I wish that I had had the guts to have a word with 'grandpa' about this, I just couldnt bear going out in my pjs. Maybe I am just too polite. We did find the doormen at the hotel a little intimidating too (several nights a week the bar would light up, heaps of people would queue up on some sort of red carpet to come into our hotel for a cocktail), was always off putting coming back to the hotel early evening to be asked for our room key, standing next to lots of people dressed beautifully whilst we were in our casual daywear. Having said that we wished we had been able to try out the restaurant. Great place to stay when in San Fran.

“Lucky I found this place” I happened to find this place after my flight was diverted to Charlotte and I was so pleasantly surprised at how nice it was. The price was right. The check in staff was gracious and fantastic and my room was 100% fine. it was clean, and comfortable and spacious and the bed was very nice. I was in a bit of a tough position that night and I'm lucky to have stumbled upon a place nearby that turned out to be more than "just fine." Very friendly staff. :)

“excellent hotel” A fine hotel, 2 1/2 years old but looks brand new, excellent service, kind of a boutique hotel, small lobby, one restaurant, but we like all that. Just across the street from the Grand Hyatt if you want the business type hotel. Pretty close to major shopping areas, Pike's market, etc. We walked everywhere. Rooms very nice, average size. Parking is expensive, valet $41 / day but they did direct us to a public garage at Grand Hyatt for $30/ day. You dont need a car in Seattle. A great fitness center, much better then the average upscale hotel. Two nearby excellent moderately priced restaurants are Purple Wine Bar and Wild Ginger, both very popular so make a reservation or eat in the lounge which we did which was fine. Price quite reasonable for Seattle at $165/night - some kind of Hyatt special

“Beautiful but old” This hotel was lovely. Everything from the rooms to the lobby. I was there during a snowstorm so it was freezing. Since the hotel is on the older side, the heat didn't stay in the room very well, even with the heavy curtains. I found myself sleeping in pants, a sweater, and wrapped up in the bathrobe from the room (which was heavenly btw). Happy hour was fantastic. The bartenders were awesome. Breakfast was delicious if not a bit crowded. The area where you eat is beautiful and allows for sitting in all sorts of books and crannies. The bathroom was awesome with a huge tub and great light. The workout room was OK. I kept shocking myself from the dry air and static electric buildup. I would stay again, but request a lower level floor so the heat doesn't escape!!!

“No pretension, No complaints” We had two rooms for four nights this past week. The rooms were very clean, even if you looked in the corners. Mattresses and pillows very comfortable. Nice size rooms with two large walk-in closets, small refrigerator and microwave in each room. Everything worked. They aren't trying to be fancy or gimmicky, but the rooms had everything we needed. Staff was efficient. (Some more friendly than others, but efficient.) Very convenient location, a few blocks from Columbus Circle, Central Park, subway stops, etc. If I can get a rate as good as I got this time ($132 prepaid on hotels.com), I'd gladly return when I need to be in Upper Midtown, but I admit that I'm surprised this hotel is rated so much higher on this site than others -- like, for example, the 70 Park Ave. Hotel which I find more cozy, posh, upbeat, and service-oriented than the Salisbury. The Salisbury may be better for families; the 70 Park Ave. better for business travelers.

“Sehr schönes Hotel am Fisherman's Wharf” Das Hotel liegt sehr schön am Fisherman's Wharf. Mit Aufpreis kann manein Zimmer mit Blick auf die Golden Gate Bridge bekommen. Das ganze Hotel ist sehr schön maritim eingerichtet. Parken ist wie fast überall in San Francisco teuer. Die Zimmer sind sehr sauber. Einziges Ärgernis war, dass ich für ein Paket eine Aufnahegebühr zahlen musste.

“I've enjoyed staying here for more than 20 years.” Columbus Motor Inn is great on so many levels. The location is great, the staff has very low turnover - I've been talking to the same housekeeper for over 20 years! The rooms are clean and neat, and free parking is worth a LOT in SF. Great place. I've stayed here with my family, and by myself, it's a great value.

“Excellent hotel has all you need - location, comfort, & great service!” I stayed here for a few nights on business and could not have been happier. The location is excellent, right in Union Square, close to Cable Cars, BART, Market St. StreetCar, and good food/shopping. Room size was average, it was very clean, my king bed was very comfortable, and the service at the hotel was top notch. I ordered Chinese take out the day I arrived which was delivered by a local eatery nearby, but they forgot silverware in my bag. I called down to room service with my odd request for a fork and a spoon, and in within what seemed like 2 mins, they sent me up a plate, glass, full set of silverware, and linens to my room. The front desk staff was nice, and I like that I was able to check out using the kiosk to expedite my departure. Computer was available in the lobby to print boarding passes. It seemed really slow, but so be it - I got the convenience I needed. I ate breakfast at the hotel restaurant, GrandViews, which lived up to its name, offering amazing morning views of San Fran, Golden Gate Bridge, and Coit Tower. The food was good, but pricey, and no complaints about the service. When I booked this hotel it was mainly because of location for business, but I'm glad I did, because the location is just one of many reasons why this place was great. I would stay again on my next trip to SFO, and recommend you try it out.

“Comfortable Hotel in a Great Location” My husband and I spent one evening at Magnolia Hotel while visiting Denver. The location was perfect for taking in the sites of downtown Denver. In addition, it was close to many wonderful places to eat and drink. For example, it was a short walk for drinks at Corridor 44 and a delicious dinner Osteria Marco. The hotel had a many perks....free drinks for happy hour, a coffee and cookie bar and a nice breakfast buffet. I would stay again!

“Solid Older "Boutique" Hotel - Great Location” This hotel is in a great location across from the Smithsonian Postal Museum, one block from Union Station (Metro, Amtrak and dining / shopping), an easy walk to Capitol Hill destinations. The room was smallish, clean, well maintained, and included a large flat screen TV. The king size bed was very comfortable and featured upscale linens and pillows. The huge desk / bureau unit made moving around the room somewhat difficult, even for a single traveler. The desk chair was old and substandard. Air conditioning / heat was adequate but controls were antiquated and difficult to regulate. The bathroom was small with very little storage / counter area, but well appointed and usable. Shower water pressure and temperature were fine. Ample linens, a hair dryer and plenty of soaps and shampoos were provided. The adjacent Dubliner pub (reached via a lobby entrance) was convenient. Decent pub food and atmosphere. At government official travel rate, this hotel compares favorably with almost any midrange chain property in the District, especially in the Capitol Hill area.

“nicht zu empfehlen, unsauber und unfreundlich” Immer wenn möglich buchen wir Hilton Hotels, egal wo auf der Welt. Fast immer haben wir gute Erfahrungen gemacht, im Service, bei den Zimmern wusste man was man bekommt, der Desk war freundlich. Ganz das Gegenteil das Hilton am Airport LAX. DIe Lobby sowie das Äußere ist das einzige was ich gut zu diesem Hotel berichten kann. Der Frontdesk war schon beim einchecken nicht so wie ich es bisher bei HIlton gewohnt war. Das erste Zimmer was ich bekam war leider nicht ordentlich sauber. Nachdem ich dieses monierte und ein neues Zimmer bekam, war dieses auch nicht 100% ok. Bei einem Übernachtungspreis von fast 200 USD muß man wenigstens ein TOP-sauberes Zimmer erwarten dürfen. Die Zimmer sind alt und renovierungsbedürftig. (..das hat man wohl schon erkannt, verschiedene Etagen wie die 8.Etage sind wohl schon renoviert...) Leider hatte ich für einen 3 Tages Aufenthalt drei einzelne Buchungen. (wegen Lufthansa Streik mussten wir 2x einen Tag dazu buchen) Beim einchecken habe ich diesen Umstand dann nochmals erläutert. Das wäre kein Problem sagte man mir..... anscheinend aber dann doch. Nach einem langen ersten Tag (mit den Auswirkungen eines Jetlag) kamen wir dann Abends gegen 21 Uhr zurück ins Hotel. Da war dann leider unsere Zimmerkarte gesperrt und das Zimmer nicht gereinigt, keine Handtücher da und die Mülleimer nicht geleert. Ein Anruf am Desk mit der Bitte jemanden mit Handtüchern zu schicken..... nach 45 min war immer noch niemand da. Als wir uns dann an der Rezeption beschwert haben, folgte dort nur ein einfaches "I am sorry"... und das noch nicht einmal glaubwürdig freundlich. DIese Hotel ist absolut nicht empfehlenswert. Wenn wir von unserem Hawaii Trip zurückkommen, wollten wir eigentlich vor der Rückreise nach Frankfurt nochmal hier eine Nacht bleiben. Ich werde in jedem Fall auf ein anderes Hotel umbuchen..... Hilton - so kann das nicht sein. Ohne weitere Worte.....

“Extremely Small, but pretty clean; good location” We booked through the hotel's web site for $109 double room. The staff was friendly, a bit stand-offish, but helpful enough. The room was very tiny, but the beds were clean and so was the bathroom. The hotel is partly condos on some floors, so it was interesting to mingle with the locals on the way in/out. The hotel room has and old feel to it. We didn't see any of the creepy-crawlies that some travelers have complained about. We only used our hotel as a base to facilitate scheduled auditions for our kids in NYC. It was well worth the $109, as we were hardly ever in the room; but, I was happy with the general cleanliness of the room for bathing and sleeping. I would give the hotel another chance if I could get the same nightly rate. Hotel is within great walking distance of Broadway other major streets/aves. Great pizza/shopping just blocks away.

“Great location and friendly staff” My wife and I stayed one night here. Very friendly staff and we were checked in very quickly. The room was ok, needs some renovation, but it is clean. Location is the best, just 5-minute walk to Liberty Bell and the Constituion Museum. The only problem I had was they put another room's breakfast to my credit card, but it was fixed immediately after I called and was transferred to talk to the accounting dept.

“Outstanding Hotel in a Perfect Spot” My sister and My daughter live in and around the San Francisco Bay area so i have little opportunity in the past to experience the true tourist perspective. My wife, four year old daughter and local 21 year old daughter decided on this hotel. I decided to booked a suite. It was a bit more than i usually like to spend, but thought we would be more comfortable and it was cheaper than trying to book to adjoining rooms. The moment we drove up to the front door of the hotel we were pleasantly surprised at the level of service and attention to detail. The door man and valet were extremely kind and helpful. They quickly unloaded our car and assisted us to the front desk. All the while, the door man was playful with my 4 year old. He walked her over to the toy chest and she selected to items. check in was extremely brief as i had booked the room on-line. We were escorted to our suite, give a brief tour of the room and offered to assist us with any local restaurants or activities. The suite was gorgeous. Large (i think the website said it was 900 sq ft), and comfortable. the living room area had a large dining room table, sofa bed and two chairs. Very nicely decorated in a nautical theme. The bedroom was large with its own TV and two chairs. In the closet was two animal print bath robes for adults and one for a child. The bathroom was large with a huge sunken Jacuzzi bathtub and separate shower. the toilet was in a separate water closet. We were extremely happy with the room. The hotel is located in fisherman’s Warf, right next to the trolley turnaround and Ghirardelli square. As well as walking distance to Pier 39 and north beach. Just a perfect spot for visiting San Francisco. We walked, trollied or muni'ed everywhere except for when we went the academy of science in Golden gate Park. a $20 taxi ride was well worth it because we were running late. I really like this property. I consider it one of my best hotel experiences yet.

“JW Marriott SA competes with Grand Hyatt (close, but no cigar)” We stayed here for a couple days over New Years eve. JW Marriott appears to be the brand competing with Grand Hyatt. First, it's a brand new hotel. Very nice and posh. Nice architecture--rooms are well appointed and fairly priced ($199). The service from the staff goes above and beyond other Marriotts--better trained here. The lazy river and pools outside were very fun: heated water, very well designed, nice water slides, etc. We really enjoyed it. The Lantana Spa was nice but the steam room in the men's room was broke (bummer). The only "problems" we encountered were with the food selections (very limited) and lack of nightlife (none). For a resort this "huge" there were only two (2) fine dining restaraunts (Cibilo Moon, 18 Oaks) and one (1) casual dining/sports bar (Velocity). There were no options for quick sandwiches or easy breakfast/lunch, which we thought was strange. Cibilo Moon was priced high end--our dinner ended up costing $100 with tip for two. Was it worth it? Yeah, I guess so--food we good, but not "amazing" and the service kinda lacked (unlike rest of resort) -- waiters seems distracted. We ate at Velocity for lunch--sports bar for lunch (only option). It was moderate priced and the food was "good" but not "great." Then we ate at 18 Oaks for New Years dinner--priced very high end, we paid $200 with tip for their prix fixed New Years menu. I was anticipating an "amazing" knock my socks off experience for that kind of money. We stayed at Grand Hyatt SA last year and their New Years prix fixed dinner was "out of this world" delicious. And at Hyatt we also got complimentary New Years morning breakfast, too. 18 Oaks simply did NOT deliver for the money. The menu selection was limited to only two (2) choices per course and the options were kinda strange: oysters or bison carpaccio for appetizer? And the oysters were served without Tabasco and horseradish. No options for dessert--there were three (3) tiny dessert puffs/mini slice of cheesecake--that's it? This is what you can buy at Costco. I was expecting like a giant piece of Cheescake Factory cheesecake. The chef here seemed to have attitude. Ego run amock. The dinner entree (lobster) for me was "good" -- only bright spot -- but at $75 dollars a head. Thumbs down for the price. Overall, JW Marriott SA was a good experience. They need more dining options here and more work on the food experiences. Every time (no fail) I stay at a Grand Hyatt hotel anywhere in the world, the service and food options are exceptional--Hyatt is run by experienced hotel Gods who know how to blow your mind and "nothing" is ever broke and everything is always perfect. Close, but no cigar, compared to Grand Hyatt.

“In the heart of DC” The JW Marriott Hotel Pennsylvania Avenue located just steps away from the White House, the Washington Monument, and the Smithsonian Museums. This luxurious newly renovated 15 story, 738 room hotel located on the District of Columbia`s famous Pennsylvania Avenue puts you in the center of all the action. Rooms are smaller and higher priced than average but most of them offer great views of the city. One block from Washington`s Metro system and 15 minutes from Reagan National Airport. The excellent location and amenities at this Pennsylvania Avenue Marriott make it the ideal choice for business and leisure traveler.

“A very nice property, very helpful staff.” Not my first time at this hotel, approaching home away from home status. Staff is very helpful. The gym is above average for a hotel property. They do charge $10.00, but in includes a pool, and is far better equiped than most hotels, although not up to a private club level. Worth it. They still charge for internet, which is really inexcuseable, as cheapo places don't. Food in the restaurants is a good bit above average for this kind of property.

“Found my new business hotel in NYC!” After a few not so great experiences at the hotel I normally stay at while in NYC, I took advantage of Jetsetter's sale to obtain a room at the Surrey for an unbeatable rate to see if I should make the Surrey my new business hotel. The first thing that raised my eyebrows about the Surrey was that it doesn't have the same buzz as some of the other hotels in its category such as the Park Plaza, St. Regis or Athenee. However, as I came to find, the Surrey was every bit as luxurious as some of the other boutique hotels but without the crowds and traffic. I will say that I probably won't be booking the Surrey when using Jetsetter again because it was a total logistical nightmare. Normally, with my busy schedule it is very hard to follow up on a hotel booking but it seemed that the Surrey was having some major issues with the Jetsetter site because it took at least 7 emails back and forth with the very helpful GM, Spencer to lock down the day I needed as Jetsetter kept saying it was unavailable and would not show the reservation. I was told there were some issues with the hotel's reservation computer system which might have accounted for the glitch. However, once I actually got to the Surrey, all the hassle I went through making the reservation was worth it. I was upgraded to a fantastic room with a small sitting area and plenty of space. The hotel staff couldn't have been any nicer or friendlier. One of the ways I always judge a hotel is by how the staff treats the guests. From the desk clerks to the doormen to the GM himself, you will be treated as a valued guest here and the staff will go out of the way for you if you make a request. The thing that stood out the most to me was the bed. It was amazing ... without a doubt the best bed I've had at any hotel in NYC. It had extremely nice bedding, including one of the nicest down comforters I've seen ... I forgot to ask where I could buy one when I was checking out of the hotel. I was only there for one night during a worldwind schedule, so its too bad I did not get to use it more. There are plenty of pillows as well, which are not too firm or soft. The room is very tastefully decorated. Normally, I do not love grey, white and black color schemes because I feel they are not very warm and semi-depressing however, the Surrey did it right. The room felt classy and comfortable without feeling too blah. The bathroom was also one of the biggest I've had in NYC with a nice shower that had a great double head and awesome water pressure. The marble and mosaic made it feel very classy. The toiletries were nice and plentiful. One thing I did not use that I thought was cool was instead of the nip-sized bottles in the typical mini-bar ... the Surrey offers bottle service in the room. For $45 - $55 you can buy a 350 ml bottle of liquor (enough for 3-4 drinks) and a bartender will come to your room with the mixers, etc. and mix your first round and leave you the accoutramonts for the other drinks you will make. There are about 15 different drinks you can choose to go with depending on the bottle you choose. The location is great. Those who want to be closer to Broadway/Times Square would not want to walk there and back as it took 30 minutes at a fairly brisk pace to make it to Broadway. It is a short cab-ride to that area and they are pretty good about calling you a cab because this hotel is fairly removed from the action, so cabs aren't plentiful. The location is in a residential part of Central Park. 5th Avenue and Madison Avenue are only a 10 minute walk and because it is so close to Central Park, the walk is not bad. I prefer staying here as opposed to staying more in the 'action' because it is very quiet and laid back ... not at all hustle and bustle. It almost feels like being in a residential neighborhood, which is probably why the price is a bit higher than some comparable hotels. I found the rates to be reasonable ... mid-April seemed to be in the $400 - $500 range for a standard room. You could stay at the W for much less, but I wouldn't say the two are comparable in terms of the luxury bedding/service, however the vibe is similar. One thing I didn't like as much is that if you are traveling with a business partner, they do not have many rooms available at the entry level price range with two beds. I was told upon checking in, the only room they had available with two beds was a junior suite, which would cost $795 per night. The regular rate for an entry level room was $495 at the time. I did not use the restaurant or bar at the hotel. The lobby isn't as spacious as it looks on the website, however it isn't as busy as a lot of other hotels, so that isn't really a problem. I did notice that the staff at this hotel do not beg for tips as they do at a lot of the other full service hotels in the area. At many hotels I stay at for business, it seems like one person takes your bags out of the car, one person wheels them into the hotel, one person parks the car and another person takes the bags to the room. I didn't really find that at the Surrey. I was at the Barclay during this trip as well and was literally chased down into the street by a bellman who moved my bags from my room a few hours earlier who wanted to let me know that it was him that moved my bags earlier that morning. If you have some money to spend and enjoy being outside of the action in a more laid back area, the Surrey is for you. I will say that after several years of staying at their nearby rival hotel, I am making the Surrey my new home for business travel in NYC. I would describe my stay here as luxurious and relaxing and thank the staff and GM for making my business/personal trip so enjoyable.

“Average Hotel” I recently stayed here for one night while in NYC for a business trip. I arrived to the hotel around 11am and they didn't have a room ready for me yet. Not a big deal since check-in time wasn't until later that day anyway, but I thought I would try. They did offer to take my bags and store them until I came back later that day. When I did check-in, the front staff was friendly and even gave me a cupcake. I was slightly disappointed that the lady who handled Preferred members didn't help me since there was nobody in line for her and I had to wait a bit. The room itself was disappointing. It looked like an older room with dings in the furniture, scrapped paint, etc. The HVAC in the room was on the louder side. The room was small, but that is typical for a NYC room. It was clean, so no complaints there. The hotel did offer free wi-fi and continental breakfast. The wi-fi worked well but the breakfast left a bit to be desired. The bananas were a bit brown and the overall selection was limited. I've had better continental breakfasts at cheaper hotels. For what I paid though, I can't really complain.

“We Loved Mansion Del Rio” The Mansion Del Rio is an elegant but not fussy hotel. It's serene and has just the right about of spanish architecture...meaning, that it's not fussy or overdone. Rooms are a delight. Our had one brick wall. Everything was so comfortable. We didn't have need to use many services but each staff member we encountered was so helpful and pleasant. The highlight of our stay was our meal at Las Canerias - I'm sure I spelled that incorrectly, but it's the hotels dining room that overlooks the riverwalk. We had table on patio overlooking river one evening and it was just delightful. The ambiance and food can't be beat. My only regret is that I didn't take more photos of this special hotel.

“Oasis downtown--hits that work/relax blend” Chic yet practical. Food outstanding. Walk to just about anywhere. Light rail nearby. Nice views. Only change I'd make is to improve the lighting, especially in bathroom vanity area. What is it with these energy saving lights that are insufficient? So tired of dimly lit hotel rooms.

“Good location, rooms are small!” I booked a room online and the room was quoted as being 395.00, which I got for a reduced rate. Upon seeing the room it was the size of a broom closet (i expected a bigger room because of the price)I called and request a room that did not face courtyard and was given a larger room. The staff is really helpful and the location is close to everything. I always love a hotel with heavenly beds and free wifi in the room

“This hotel closed in mid-July” This Holiday Inn was purchased by new owners and closed down in mid-July. The Holiday Inn signs have been removed. News reports indicate that new owner plans to renovate the property and rebrand it.

“Perfect Location” The Holiday Inn was decorated for the Christmas season in a spectactular way. Really got one into the spirit. This hotel is convenientally located to everything. The staff was great with where to go and things to do for the out of towners. Food was solid and the rooms were cpmfortable.

“Excellent Service. Huge Rooms. Location Decent.” I stayed at the Marriott Suites this week for a work trip. I was pleasantly surprised by the hotel service. The front desk crew went above and beyond to make sure I had a nice stay. My room (suite) was HUGE with two large flat screen TVs and a nice bathroom. The hotel is right across the street from the Children's Hospital. If you need to be in North Dallas, this hotel is about 15 minutes out of the way. My ONLY complaint is that the coffee maker in my room was wonky and produced a moldy water.

“Great location & rooms!” Perfect location to explore Times Square. The room was really large and had a great view. We sat on the sofa and watched all the activity down below, The beds are soooo comfortable. The elevator system takes a bit of getting used to but it is really effecient. This isn't the newest hotel (the room did show some wear but it was well maintained). It also isn't the fanciest place but it has a great location and a helpful staff. I also liked having the in room safe. I would definately stay again.

“Pretty noisy stay.” 2 night stay based on reviews, price and location. The Western is pretty worn out but its location within walking distance to most everything in Old Town including the Transportation Center which gives access to all of San Diego is the redeeming factor. Basically no real amenities here, but the price is around half of the Marriott next door. Our biggest complaint was the slamming doors. You hear everyone of them and at all hours. Room was passably clean and large enough. Internet slow but stayed connected. We loved the location & price and could put up with the dated worn decor (including the beds) but would look harder for an alternative in the future.

“Nothing but OK” Usually HGI's are a step above a Hampton Inn. At Port of Coumbus both properties are adjacent. I chose the HGI but I'd be interested in the condition of the Hampton. This HGI is showing some wear. The carpets in the hall way look filthy. Rooms were clean but showed wear. Staff is very courteous Only two dining options, McDonald's or HGI restaurant which is busy. Location of the property is right next to the runway on one side which can be load but flight traffic ends early and it shouldn't pose a problem with your sleep. No real problems, just not up to the usual HGI standards.

“Great feeling above ground” This hotel has an ample lobby which is full of natural light during the day. It is build around a 12 floor atrium and does not seem as big as it really is. The staff at the front desk is very corteous when checking in. The only drawback is that the larger convention space is three levels below the street level and there are no visible hotel elevators to take you down to the basement. It is within walking distance of Chinatown, the Verizon Center and very good restaurants. One drawback is the construction project accross the street. When you are above the ground you really like this hotel. Below ground it is not as nice. Rooms are big and well appointed. As far as lodging venues go it is a good one.

“Lovely time at the Fairmont!” After reading the reviews here I almost canceled my reservations. Boy am I glad I didn't! Last week I booked a room as an anniversary surprise for my Husband. We had planned to have dinner at McCormack & Schmicks, a new Seafood restaurant attached to the hotel. I booked a Standard Room on the internet at the Fairmont's website for $99.00. I emailed the concierge and asked them to make our dinner reservations. On Saturday afternoon we arrived at the Fairmont and on check-in found that they had upgraded us to a Suite (the Stanford) on the 19th floor at no extra charge! And no I didn't ask for this upgrade they just gave it to us. While we were exploring the wonderful room there was a knock on the door and it was room service with a bottle of chilled champagne and fruit basket accompanied by a note from the Manager wishing us a Happy Anniversary. The suite was quite nice, not too fancy but very nice. The reception staff were not at all Snooty as has been reported in previous posts, in fact the employee working the "presidents club" desk waved us over and checked us in so we didn't have to wait for the other clerks to finish with their guests. I found the concierge helpful and everyone was very friendly. This is an upscale hotel in a downtown area so the $22 to park overnight was not a shock. The restaurant was fabulous and not at all overpriced for what we had, the $12 corkage fee was inexpensive compared to other places we've been. McCormack & Schmicks has a wonderful reputation and were not disappointed. All the people complaining about overpriced food in the restaurants should remember where they are staying, the Fairmont is a Lxury hotel and as such their prices reflect this. It is not the Holiday Inn. Also, in downtown San Jose there are many places within walking distance to go for dinner if the hotel is a bit too pricey for your taste. All in all it was a wonderful experience one I would highly recommend. If you are looking for a weekend getaway you can certainly find a bargain.

“Beautiful, Sheek and Modern All Wrapped Up in One” I got a nice price through priceline which you could'nt beat. I read the reviews and saw pictures of the hotel on tripadvisor and had my doubts. Upon arrival I was greeted by the doorman and bellman and I must say that they were the most courteous people I have ever met during a hotel stay in Chicago. I wanna say Charles and Benjamin were the stuff!!!!!! They ask you do you have your cell phone and your wallet upon exiting the cabs, which made you double check before the cab left the scene, which I truely appreciate. Checking in was simple and fast no King bed was available, but I expected that due to me being a late check in. Beautiful Lobby and clean hallways tells you alot about the hotel. I entered my room and yes it was a bit on the small side, but as you get aquainted the size grows on you( Have to keep in mind this is a boutique hotel). The bed was to die for sooo comfortable and the showers lets just say I didnt mind taking 2 or 3 a day.... OMG and the curtains(which completely darkens the room incase you doint want the sun shining into your room on an early day) and the computer chair to the desk I just wanted to take home. Great theme colors for the room! Housekeeping was very prompt upon calling for additional wash clothes and towels! My bestfriend and I really do appreciate Benjamin he was of great help he helped us with finding the latest spots to party during New Years Eve and very approachable. He has a good spirit. :) My friend forgot a few of her toiletries and the concierge desk carry complimentary toothbrushes and toothpaste and that was a great help even though there is a Walgreens around the corner.The Fitness Center was a bit on the small side, but carried the latest and modern equipment and also a spa around the corner from the fitness area. I am use to staying at the Hyatt Regency on East Wacker Drive, but I believe Hotel Felix has won me over as a consumer. I cant wait to return..........GREAT SERVICE!!!!!!!!!!!!

“Terrific hotel” I booked a 2 night stay at the Omni through Hotwire for an incredible deal of $68 per night. Low price or not, the Omni is a fantastic hotel. The room was clean and very nice. The ONLY bad mark I would give is I found a dirty sock in the bed tucked in between the turned down bed cover. I have no idea how that could have happened. The check in was quick and I got a room on the 10th floor. The view wasn't all that great, but nothing worth complaining about. I didn't try the restaurant so I can't comment on the food. Bottom line: if you want to stay at a beautiful hotel located downtown, this is the place. I've stayed at the downtown Hyatt before and this place blows it away.

“Affordable hotel that is worth consideration, but prepare for short walks” The Holiday Inn Washington, DC - Central / White House is a very good choice if you're looking for a more affordable stay in the Capitol City, and don't mind walking a little. I say that you shouldn't mind walking, becuase this hotel isn't right near a Metro station like many other hotels in DC. The closest metro is McPherson Square and it is about 4 or 5 blocks away, but not a bad walk at all. The hotel is an older property but is undergoing some moderate upgrades. I had the pleasure of being upgraded to a delux room and it was quite nice with a separate sitting area with 2 bathrooms and some wonderful views of the city. The bed linens were a bit tired, as were the carpet and drapes, but overal the room was clean and tidy, and the bathroom was spottless. The hotel has good FREE wireless internet service, which is DC is a major plus. The hotel has a small reastaurant, and the breakfast buffett was more than acceptable. Overhall I was happy with this stay, and will probably stay again during my next trip to DC.

“Decent Choice” Stayed here for 5 nights in August and found the hotel to be an "ok" choice in the Mission Valley area. Parking was free and the location of the hotel made travel to all the usual tourist attractions very easy and fast. It seemed it took no more than 10 minutes to get anywhere. The Fashion Valley Mall (high end stores) is five minutes away and numerous restaurants are nearby. Also, the trolley is across the highway (we used it to get to Petco Park). Checkin was fast but when I suggested an upgrade for free or pay, I was met with a blank stare. The first room I got was on the hillside as suggested by other reviewers, it reeked of smoke (on a no smoking floor). I changed rooms and the only thing available was on the highway side. Noise did not bother me at all. Rooms were good, but no minibar or refridgerator and the TV lacked Nick and Cartoon network for the kids. Constantly had to ask for more towels, the maid did not seem to get we were a family of four. Food and seervice in the hotel dining room was very good but a little over priced. I guess your paying for the convienece. If you have a car you will not be eating here very often. There is a Denny's one block away for breakfast. Pool area was good. Nice size pool and hot tub. Towels were available at the pool. Its the type of pool where you dont want to hang around all day but nice enough to come back to after a long day of touring. Summary I got the room for free using Starwood points and it was fine. If I was paying $150 - $200 I would look elsewhere.

“A great deal” This hotel is a great deal for staying in LA: good price and good amenities, even if the surrounding area is not the greatest. The hotel doesn't look like anything spectacular from the outside, but it is clean and the rooms are spacious and comfortable, complete with a flat-screen TV and cable channels, a microwave and a small fridge which are very handy. My only complaint is the A/C, it's a bit close too close to one of the beds (we were sleeping in 4 people in the room, so we needed both beds). Included in the room rate are a very good breakfast (they had 3 or 4 different kinds of fruit, pastries, waffle machine, scrambled eggs and bacon, yougurt, etc), free parking and free wi-fi. Breakfast room is a bit small, but we never had problems finding a table (they only have 4 or 5 tables, but you can take the breakfast to your room). The surrounding area is not the best, but we didn't feel unsafe or anything like that, and since we had a rented car it wasn't a problem for us. Overall I recommend this hotel because you get quite a lot for the price (which is not expensive)!

“I liked this hotel but didn't love it...” We chose this hotel due to its excellent reviews and proximity to our daughter's apartment. It was fine. The room was small but not tiny. The bed was comfortable but nothing special. The furnishings trendy but not too over the top (chairs and upholstery don't look like they will hold up long). Shower head very trendy with rainshower and multiple horizontal shower heads but I would have just liked one shower head that had plenty of water pressure as the rainshower and multiple shower heads were a little weak. On check out, we asked the front desk person if he could call a cab for us.. he said that we wouldn't be able to get a cab at that time of the morning but so in so who happens to be reading the paper in our lounge would be happy to take us to the airport and it would only be a few dollars more than the cab. We agreed for the driver to take us as we didn't want to go out on the street with our luggage and hail a cab but we felt a little like he was trying to take advantage of our naivety. Overall, I would pick it again due to the location but it wasn't one of my favorite New York hotel experiences.

“2 stars would be a stretch” We encountered one sullen front desk staff named Ana during check in, though the rest of the staff seem friendly. Extremely cramped, small room with seriously outdated furniture. When I booked the room, Expedia clearly indicated that it would be a renovated queen room, but there was nothing remotely resembling renovation anywhere in the room. I just don't see how anyone can, in reasonable conscience, assign a 4 star rating to this miserable, mediocre place. The Tick Tock Diner was every bit as miserable - the hostess directed us to a table in the corner where the waiting staff were banging away in the very next table replenishing ketchup, salt, sugar containers. Of course we moved to another table, over the objection of our surly waiter, very quickly. This is truly a miserable establishment - avoid at all cost.

“Relaxing stay” I had a one night stay back in Feburary here, and enjoyed it throughly. The hotel is large, although it only comprises the top 3 floors of the building. The lobby is spacious, well lit, and a nice place to sit or meet. There are 2 restaurants, the selection is mediocore, but the food is good. I enjoyed a complimentary hot breakfast buffet in the morning, including everything you could want to eat. The room was a standard king bedded room with a sitting area. It was spacious and clean, and the furnishing were nice, but nothing fantastic. The bathroom was large and well stocked. I used the gym facility, and was pleased, it is in a small space, i think it was undergoing a renovation, so there was a lot of equipment in a small space. Overall I was pleased with the space and the service and no problems.

“Second Stay - Just as good” This was a our second time staying here in the last year - this time was again for a single night. Spent more time at the bar area. The wings were great - sauce was on the side - very spicy and excellent. Drinks were perfect. Ate at Bistro 555 - it was good. Empty the night we were there - but good. Room is very clean. Pretty quiet - though some sirens came up. Had a great view of the capital at night. Stayed in a single room this time, instead of the suite. One complaint was the shower. Very nice design with dual shower heads on opposite sides. very spacious. However the water temperature was all but impossible to control. Could not get hot water, just wamr at best - and that was with a lot of playing around. Still - this is a great hotel. Staff is very attentive. Stay here and enjoy!
“Smelly room” Location is perfect, however; parking and smelly rooms make this one not worth the price.

“Historisch und recht ungepflegt” Das große alte Hilton Chicago ist sicher ein eindrucksvolles Hotel. Die Zimmer können sehr groß sein, inclusive zweier kompletter Bäder. Aber die Einrichtung und insbesondere die sanitären Anlagen sind recht betagt. (Das zweite Bad kommt sehr gelegen, wenn eine Toilette plötzlich verstopft ist....) Die Zimmer werden offenbar nur sehr oberflächlich gereinigt. Ein gebrauchter Kaffeebecher eines Vorgängers hinter der Kommode ist nur ein Zeichen dafür. Service versucht das durch freundlichkeit und ein gelegentliches Frühstück auf Kosten des Hauses auszugleichen. Frühstück ist gut. Zimmer zum Innenhof sind ruhig.

“Dependable, Upscale, Secluded” We have stayed at the Hilton Dallas Park Cities on numerous weekend jaunts to Dallas. The location (Preston Center near the NW Highway and Dallas Tollway intersection), is a major plus. It is well centered to access all parts of Dallas. The staff is friendly, the hotel is pet friendly, and the rooms are comfortable and quiet. Since the hotel is located on a small, secluded street, there is NO street noise. Over the last couple of years, the hotel has been completely renovated. Recently, I was upgraded to an executive floor room that had high ceilings, a comfortable bed, plentiful workspace, and all the amenities one would expect. I had the opportunity to dine in the newly renovated restaurant - bar. The bartenders were terrific and the southwestern flavored small dishes were actually better than I expected. Since we travel to Dallas frequently, the Hilton Park Cities is always one of the two or three "top of the list" lodgings for us. We highly recommend it!

“Very enjoyable stay” The Hilton Americas is a very nice hotel that I will choose to stay in again. The room was very clean, fresh, new, stylish, and very quiet. The bed was very comfortable. The towels were fluffy, fresh, and large. The staff are all very friendly and helpful. The executive lounge is very large and has great views of the downtown skyline. The fitness center is great, very large, well appointed, and also has great views. The hotel is within easy walking distance of the convention center, the Toyota Center, shopping, Discovery Green, and groceries at Phoenicia Specialty Foods.

“Great Price for the Location!” My visit to this property was for business hosting an event at a local restaurant on Sunset. It was a great location as I could either walk or take a car and it felt safe given the amount of foot traffic at all hours of the day. The valet staff were exceptional, helping us manage a cargo van with supplies for the event. I appreciated that they were very flexible. My room was very nice, and for the price, very, very nice! I don't think there is a bad view from this hotel to be honest. Other staff members were situated on different floors and each view was nothing short of spectacular. We ordered room service several times for convenience of our schedule. It took less than 20 minutes so it seemed very accommodating. The food was great! Tried to use the business service office on a Saturday night. Ended up going to a printing store as the machine wasn't full of paper and only one ream was sitting out. There wasn't an attendant there and I'm sure it was because of the weekend but still, if you're going to be open 24 hours (and I like that idea) you should have someone available for assistance. Would I stay here again? Yes, it was a great location and the price was just right.

“Great Place for a Hurricane” I stayed here from 10/28-11/2, during hurricane storm Sandy. My room was on the 10th floor and had a protected window so you wouldn't know that there was a storm out unless you saw it on tv. The room was very quiet and very nice. I love that this hotel provides robes, for when you decide to go to the hottub or swimming. The hottub water is slightly warmer than luke warm, rather disappointing. There is a very nice dry sauna in the locker room which will warm you up quickly. The fitness center was never busy when I went at 9:00 am, 5:00 pm, or 10:00 pm. There are apples in the fitness center, which is a nice snack. The staff was very accommodating during the storm. The bathroom was very small. When you close the bathroom door it almost touches the toilet. The drawer safe in the desk was very convenient. The staff at Starbucks in the lobby is very unfriendly so just around the corner is the Corner Bakery, which I highly recommend. The staff at the restaurant is very helpful. The elevators are the newest technology where you press in your floor number and enter the assigned elevator car. There are so many dining options closeby and a CVS two blocks away in case you forgot anything or want snacks. The Metro is a short two block walk. I will definitely stay here on my next trip to Washington DC!

“Very convenient!” Although my husband and I go to Chicago at least once a year, we’d never before stayed at the Airport Hilton. We arrived on Friday night with tickets to the Cubs game on Saturday. The greatest thing about this hotel is the convenience. 15 minutes after you get off the plane, you can be there by following the signs downstairs from baggage claim. Not to mention getting to town is a breeze since the train is right there, too. The hotel is nice enough. Our room was nice, the bed was comfortable, and it was clean. Another plus is the bar is open late, so you can get a bite to eat if you get in late. The line for check-in was quite long, so we used the automated system, which worked out just fine for us and was much quicker than waiting in line. We got a good rate through Expedia, so overall I thought it was a good choice for us for this quick trip. Usually, it’s a bit pricey for a hotel so far from downtown, but I would recommend it for quick trips and definitely for anyone making an overnight connection through O’Hare.

“Excellent value for money” The Barclay has a vey good location, close to Times Square, 5th Av. or Central Park but not right in the middle of the crowd. If you don't like to walk, cabs are waiting for you in front of the entrance door and there is a metro entrance (Grand Central station) a few meters away. The hotel doesn't meet the standards of other Intercontinental hotels we've been in around the world but New York has its own standards, is'nt it? The lobby has everything you would expect from it. Our room (standard with king bed) was big enough for two people with tons of luggage. However, do not expect to have plenty of extra space... once again, we are in NYC! We have nothing to say regarding cleanliness. Style was oldfashioned and furniture old but well maintained. People at the front desk and the concierge were helpful and quick. The breakfast buffet had not a big choice for this kind of hotel but food was of very good quality. We were very happy to stay at The Barclay and had no doubt: excellent value for money !

“Great, inexpensive, fast airport shuttle.” Formerly the Adam's Mark, Wyndham is rebranding it as one of their products. Most of the elements remain the same, though they have updated the bedding. It is a bit outdated, but most of the staff remained, and they made the Adam's Mark a special place. The beds are comfortable, and the linens/bedding are new. The internet is fast, and free. The climate control was a bit finicky, and I'm not sure it ever adjusted to the temperature I wanted, though it wasn't inherently uncomfortable. (I like cooler rooms for sleeping) Pros: --Fast, frequent airport shuttle. --Fast Internet access (free too!) --Friendly Service --Quiet Cons: --Small-ish rooms --Limited Parking --Lots of construction in the area due to the I-70 reroute. A bargain!

“Adequate lodging” We stayed here for one night on a short side trip we took to San Franciso while we were staying at Lake Tahoe. (Good Points) The hotel is located right near the wharf area which would be a plus for most people. It is only a short walk to the cable cars and trolley. The hotel is new and shows no wear and tear yet. The breakfast is the typical Holiday Inn Select breakfast which I believe to be one of the best around. The hotel staff is friendly and helpful. They put out fruit on the counter in the afternoon. (Needing improvement or that which you may want to be forewarned of) We needed two rooms. The one my son and his friend stayed in was a typical two bed room of adequate size. The one my wife and I stayed in was really small (477 I think). It reminded me of some of the smallish european rooms we have stayed in. It was adequate, but should not have been priced as high as the others. Parking your car here is 32 dollars a pop for one night. I consider that too high even for a large city. I believe you can park it cheaper at some of the local lots. Neither room had a fridge or a micro. As this is a new hotel I would have expected this to have been included. I do not think there is a pool for the kiddies, but I believe you can use the Holiday Inn pool a few doors down. Would I stay here again? Yes

“Great boutique style hotel in a perfect locations” This hotel was great. Huge rooms, like the size of a small apartment, and excellent service. The rooms really are big, not just for Manhattan but for any hotel I have ever stayed in. Standard room is like a large suite.The washroom is seperated into two rooms, shower and sink is sperate from toilet with sink, so its great if you have visitors. Huge windows that open (in bedroom and shower-room), great and comfortable King bed, desk, sitting area and flat-screen TV. Nicely decorated and very chic. Perfect midtown location.... Great lobby bar and 24-hour desk attendant. Very freindly, helpful and professional staff. I would definitely recommend this hotel and stay here again!

“Nice place for exploring Austin area” The hotel delivers as most Springhill Suites - roomy suite-like space. Television is super clear HD, beds very comfortable, and rest of room clean. Breakfast area a little cramped, but food offerings decent. Computer/business area in the breakfast zone, so don't try to work there in the morning hours. Staff was very courteous and friendly, and area was quiet. 5 minute drive to the Domain shopping area and restaurants, although there's a Sam's Boat directly adjacent. One drawback is very difficult to find by map and get there by car when coming from the south; coming from the north, it's easy; so pay careful attention to directions when driving there for the first time.

“Great deal, great staff” We booked this hotel with a deal on priceline the day before we arrived. Prior to our arrival I called with our preferences- upper floor, nonsmoking room, king bed. Even though we were priceline customers and some hotels treat you worse we got everything we asked for. The rooms were lovely- see attached photos- big, soft bed and large television, sitting area, marble sinks in the bathroom, and those nice amenities they offer at Hyatt that smell like lemon verbena or something. The hotel was very quiet . I happened to go to the fitness center the next morning. It's really great. Tons of excellent, new equipment. I didn't try the pool, it looked nice though, and there is a hot tub by it. The staff at this friend really goes out of their way to help you. Kyle at the restaurant downstairs, which was not bad, was very nice. Also when we showed up the valet informed us that we could just park for free around the corner. Check in and check out staff were also very friendly and efficient. Two thumbs up.

“Large business hotel, without much personality” We arrived at the Westin Seattle at 11 PM after coming in from the East Coast. Since it was 2 AM East Coast time, all we wanted to do was sleep when we got to our hotel. Unfortunately, there was only one person working at the front desk, and sadly, the check in process wasn't very efficient. We had requested a room on a high floor for the view, and were happy to see that this request had been noted, even though the room was directly across from the elevator. However, the next morning, we were awakened early by noises that were coming from the room next to us. When we finally got up and moving, we realized that our room was next to a hotel room which had apparently been rented out for use as a focus group room--so there were people coming and going all day long. Since the walls seemed like they were paper thin, it felt like we could hear everything that was going on--it was as if our hotel room were in an office building. Because we were only staying 2 nights and didn't feel like moving, we didn't complain, but I was surprised at the lack of oversight that it would be a bad idea to place hotel guests next to rooms rented out for a business focus group. We are Starwoods Preferred members, so I would hope that it would think about this before it placed its most loyal customers in such a room. The room itself was clean, but nothing special. I just wish that we didn't have such an unpleasant wake up call.

“Nice time at the Doubletree” Had a nice time at this hotel for 2 nights. I was able to check in early and that was great. I ate at their restaurant 2 times, and both times service and food were great. The hotel is a short distance to a nice shopping mall where there's a Cheesecake Factory.

“Clean, competent Hilton property beginning to show its age; very close to the White House” Up until a few weeks ago (see my review of the nearby Madison Hotel, which is my new favorite hotel in the district), the Capitol Hilton was my go-to hotel whenever I was in Washington D.C. The property is gigantic - I never have a problem getting a room, and the produce is very consistent. It is an easy five minute walk from the metro, and about the same distance from the White House, so it is close to everything. The rooms are decently spacious, and pretty quiet - you can hear a bit of traffic from the corridor and doors opening/closing, but overall pretty good, with attractive appointments that are just beginning to show their age. Marble floors in the bathrooms and nice linens on the bed. Overall a good Hilton property. A few notes: some of the rooms have issues (e.g. I've had a tub that flat out wasn't working), be sure to ask for a quick change before you unpack. Despite having something like six elevators, I found myself waiting in the lobby or on my floor for as much as five minutes during high traffic periods (lots of business travelers like myself). The gym requires an extra payment to use, something I found rather annoying. Still, this is a consistently good property, and is the property that I immediately call when none of my particular favorites have availability in the district. I give it four stars because that consistency of service can be somewhat difficult to find in D.C. Don't shop in the hotel shop; if you do, expect prices 3x above the CVS that is just 1.5 blocks away, and with stale (and sometimes expired - check your Sourpatch Kids, as of 6/12 there were two packages that expired in April on the shelf!) food and candy.

“Excellent hotel, but pay attention to the bill!” We had an excellent stay at the Boston Hilton Back Bay while attending a professional conference recently, but make sure you check your bill before checking out. On the positive stay, the staff were very friendly, professional, and accomodating. The room was good and well-equipped but a bit dated. In particular, the small refrigerator was a bit dirty and the racks were broken. The bathroom was clean, but small and seemed like it could use some updating. The temperature control worked excellently and the room was very quiet. The bed was comfortable, and overall we had good nights sleep. But the challenges concerned the cost of the extras and the final bill. The breakfast buffet with a discount coupon was $20 per person, and in-room wi-fi was $14 per day. Thankfully there are computers in the lobby with free internet access. The Starbucks in the lobby was handy as well. But at check-out we disovered that we had been charged for someone else's room with all that person's additional charges. Had we not checked the bill carefully, we would have paid much more! The staff did correct the mistake, but it makes me wonder about how Hilton processes room bills. In the summer I had another bill mix-up at a Hilton in Chicago. Overall, this is a good choice if you are attending a conference at the Hynes Convention center.

“Comfortable well equipped hotel in good location for tourists to Boston” We stayed 1 night for excellent price in large single room; comfortable quiet hotel, well appointed, very traditional - maybe a little staid . Don't expect a young or noisy crowd. In room dining and entertainment good. Perfectly pleasant and a very good location for old Boston. Suit adults travelling alone or in groups, or families with small children.

“Perfect Anniversary Night” We were celebrating our 9th wedding anniversary and from the minute we arrived we were treated like royalty! We stayed in the suite on the 12th floor and it was gorgeous. We were treated to a complimentary glass of champagne on arrival and then the bellman arrived with a complimentary bottle 10 minutes after check-in. We went to Alibi for an appetizer and the order was overlooked, we hadn't even realized it when the bartender said it was on them. We had dinner at Clink and the chef prepared a Gluten free entree for my husband. Both meals were perfect. Breakfast at Clink was also excellent. The music is a bit different but we enjoyed the atmosphere of the entire hotel and highly recommend a stay here. They have done a fabulous job! The Johnson's, Whitman, MA
