“Just OK for a one night stay- nothing special on offer here” I was allocated a room on the top(6th floor) which is labelled the honors floor but not sure there was anything special about this floor-maybe the free bottles of water? The furniture in my room was old and mismatched, old style TV that hummed mysteriously-room not large and fairly basic.The location is right by the New England T but the service on the orange line seems patchy with some long waits encountered. My room faced the hospital on Washington St, however I did not hear any noise from sirens etc mentioned by other reviewers. There is free wireless in the lobby and computers available for guest use.I did not see any evidence of the fung shui they make such a big deal about on their website , other than a few odd chinese style decorative items.Breakfast was standard Doubletree- very acceptable.Each Doubletree hotel has a "careline" for assistance- I suspect it is just the understaffed front desk as the one time I called it was'nt answered - I just gave up. On checkout I was overcharged but this was corrected once pointed out.In summary -not bad not good- only recommended if you can obtain a cheap rate that matches the mediocre offering.

“Chic Dupont Circle Hotel” The Hotel Palomar is my favourite place to stay in DC. I have stayed there many times for work and have always been very satisfied with the service, design and comfort of the rooms. The Palomar is chic in an imitation W Hotel-style way, but pulls it off better than most of the Kimpton hotels manage to do. The last time I stayed there I had a group booking for 13, and all of my guests were very impressed by the hotel. Additionally, I was upgraded to a suite which was a nice surprise, although I had far too much space in the suite all by myself and didn't know what to do with it all! The hotel is very well located, close to the Dupont Circle metro station, and with lots of cafes and restaurants nearby. The evening wine hour is a nice touch, although most nights I miss it as I don't get back to the hotel until after 6.00pm. I wish it ran to 7.00pm!

“Nice hotel with excellent service” I stayed at the Omni recently for a business conference. The hotel shows some age but is nice looking, and the lobby level is very pretty. While I didn't have time to enjoy them, the exercise room and the pool looked very nice. The rooms were a tad small, but not at all uncomfortable. I slept like a baby on a very comfortable bed. I recommend frequent travelers participate in the free Omni Select program, as it affords a few extra niceties like complimentary (two) beverage drinks in the morning and free in-room WIFi. The wireless connection kept kicking me offline, which was frustrating, but I can't rule out that it was equipment problems on my end. When connected it worked very well. What impressed me the most was the customer service. I love being treated with kindness and respect by hotel employees, and obviously this hotel values that and makes it a priority for its employees. Keep up that great work! I bet that is how you get repeat customers and recommendations.

“Classy, sophisticated, and hip” This was my first time staying at a Kimpton Hotel, very impressed. The room was very spacious, modern, comfortable, and clean. I liked the fun touches like the animal print robes, carpet, and fur throw on the bed. Service was great, every time I returned I was always greeted by the front desk. The hotel restaurant was very good. However I don't like pets and didn't like seeing dogs just walking around inside the lobby, what about people who are allergic to pets? The room view was of a back alley and rather seedy. The gym was smallish but decent. The internet was free if you signed up for the loyalty program which was quick and painless.

“It's a bit of a dated Embassy Suites” Just completed a stay at this Embassy Suites in the heart of Denver's best warehouses. Hotel staff members were wonderful - very friendly and helpful (and I mean everybody - the folks clearing tables to the front desk - all helpful and nice). Hotel itself is a bit dated. I love Embassy Suites lobbies, but the atrium is a bit outdated and in need of freshening up. The rooms appear to have been updated sometime in the past 10 years or so, but the sofa was rather old and lumpy. The desk in the bedroom did not have any kind of electrical outlet for my laptop, and the nightstands did not have convenient outlets for my cell phone (I had to move the nightstand away from the wall to plug in my phone - which also doubles as my alarm cock). New flatscreen TV in living room was nice, but old CRT in bedroom was less nice. The desk in the living room did have convenient outlets on it. My HUGE gripe is the horrendous lighting in the rooms. Yes, I know all hotels are switching to fluorescent bulbs...but most have found soft, warm lighting. EVERY lamp in the Embassy Suites rooms was bright blue-white, like a tacky auto shop or something. This really was rough on the eyes and it looks terrible from the lobby to see this terrible lighting from the atrium. Yuck. I know it's probably a minor gripe to a lot of people, but it's enough to turn me away. It feels very low budget for a place that charges $150+ / night. Back to the pluses... the happy hour was very well done. The bartender was friendly and efficient. The snack spread was more than most Embassy Suites hotels put out - chips/salsa, that spicy chex mix (which is very good), fresh popcorn, crudites with dip, and kettle chips. Yum! This would make me come back. All in all, a decent hotel that just needs a little sprucing up. It just seemed to be a bit pricey, since I pay less for Embassy Suites hotels in better locations with nicer finishes.

“Warwick quite disappointing” The Warwick or the "Radisson Plaza Warwick" as the staff are now calling it was adequate but disappointing. We had stayed there a few years ago and thought it elegant and historic, now it is blandly corporate in decor and fixtures. We've no real complaints with the room, except that the tub was badly stained, apparently by a bathmat (it didn't seem to be coming off). My wife felt that the bathroom wasn't adequately cleaned, that dirt remained on the wall throughout our two day stay. Service was fine--we were able to check in early, got a rollaway bed and hypoallergenic pillows promptly upon request. The location is of course great. On the name--I heard a staff member telling another guest that he wasn't using the "historic name"--the Warwick. It was a sad and telling statement.

“Very nice place. Very nice location. Little expensive but close to the bar from the TV show "Cheers."” I tried to show off to my wife by staying at a nice hotel but I may have messed up. The Taj is very nice but it is too nice for me. It is very classic and sophisticated and I am not. You could probably find a cool trendy hotel in the area for cheaper. This place is amazingly similar to The Pierre in NY. I just googled the two hotels and they are actually owned by the same group.

“Great views and location; a very pleasant stay” Check in was a breeze, and I was given the exact room I requested along with my Marriott profile preferences (high room, away from elevator). The view was great, and the room was clean and in perfect condition. High def TV and Internet worked great, and the desk and bed were very comfortable. Maybe the only complaint was that some rooms, like mine, were smaller than others - I don't know why the hotel was built that way. The Starbuck's in the lobby was very convenient. The fitness center was also large and in good condition, and the attendant offered me some fruit on the way out.

“Consistently good” Back for another visit with daughter in college. Love this Holiday Inn. Saw a previous post complaining about no fridge but our room (Room 440) had a fridge. Elevators were quick; restaurant downstairs had decent choices. The gym was very nice. Great equipment, free earbuds, fresh towels, TVs on the equipment. Nice, comfortable room. Fan in bathroom (seems hard to find these days). Coffee maker with Starbucks coffee in room. Lots of electrical outlets that you didn't have to get on hands and knees to find - they were in the base of the lamp stand. Room 440 was quiet - didn't hear a plane or train the whole time.

“great location” Bit late in coming sorry about that, we stayed here in jan 11 and what a great place it was. We stayed in a room with 2 queens with an interconnecting parlour room and it was fantastic for our family of 5,2 of those teenagers and 2 of those adults and the space was incrdible value. Whats more we were about a 5 to 10 min walk from Union station so we got off the train from New York to Washington suitcases in hand and walked to the hotel. The rooms were get beautifully and they were decorated very tastefully, across the road was a Starbucks for our coffee fill and we had a ridiculously cheap breakfst at the cafe across the road to save on a hotel bksfst, great value. Each day we walked up to Union station and jumped on our hop on hop off bus tour to see the sights and didnt miss a thing and the one day we stayed at the Pentagon shopping centre and ate dinner it was less than $20.00 to get back to the Washington by taxi. We ate a couple of dinners at the Union station, cheap and basic but a great way to recoup some spending money, Victoria Secret shopping there is incredible too. So all in all the Court is a great place to stay, lovely staff, quiet, safe location and heaps of space for a budget price because Washington can be pricey, loved it and would stay again..

“What are you talking about?!?!” I honestly do not know what these people are complaining about. I have stayed at this hotel three times now and have always gotten good service and a clean comfortable room and I use Priceline! Check in was a super speedy breeze maybe all of 5 minutes since there was no one in line and I was checking in about 230-3pm. This is a huge convention hotel so there will be lots of people and yes like a typical hotel the bar and resteraunt will be over priced but you know what forget those plays! Go to the neighborhoods and chow down with the locals :) Now after checking in I boogied up to my room. Like my two other rooms it was spacious with slightly more then a sliver view of the river facing east and a view of the fire dept. down on the street and various buildings. I found the room generally clean and well kept. There were no scuff marks, burn holes and what not. My only gripe is the bath soaps they use. They are too perfumey and gave me a very bad headache. I had to run to the grocery store to grab some of my regular bath soap. But other then that I found this another great stay just like the rest. So those bad reviews, take with a small grain of salt cause they are most likely ocd anal folk who nit pick everything.

“Excellent Services and Location” The hotel's staff is definitely the best part of this hotel. Esp the Front desk agent Ronda. She is really helpful agent despite the hotel is really lacking on manpowers. She is very personal yet professional. The room itself is new and fresh. Very typical 4 points decoration but the location adjacent to Philadelphia convention center can not be beat. Some people complained about the neighborhood which I did not find any problem at all. Lots eating options nearby including China town with lots Asian eateries. As for a higher floor room if you are a light sleeper.

“Still the one” The Ritz has been our go-to hotel in Chicago for a number of years. Despite some minor slips for this visit, it's still the one we consider first when planning a trip to the Windy City. We come to Chicago almost annually, but somehow missed last year. As it turns out, we also missed the Ritz's entire remodeling phase where first the rooms and then the public areas were redone. The lobby apparently reopened less than a month before our visit. The rooms, previously a pleasant but busy cacophony of floral prints, are now a more subdued and contemporary palette of blue-gray. The bathrooms were redone previously and are unchanged. The rooms now boast a large desk with ergonomic chair and a console with drawers, and shelves that house the electronic safe and DVD player (the old safes that needed a key to open are still situated in the closet). The new large flat screen, high def TV sits on top. The windows now have a sunscreen as well as block-out drapes. There are interesting architectural photos in both the rooms and public areas. Minor changes that perhaps reflect the current economy: the bar of soap for the shower is the same size as the one for the sink (it used to be larger), there are fewer complimentary newspaper choices offered (Chicago Tribune and Wall Street Journal only, before there also was USA Today and New York Times), the room service menu has an all-day section rather than separate lunch and dinner menus. At first glance, the lobby appears unchanged, but upon closer inspection we realize the marble around the fountain has been replaced, as has the carpeting, now also marble. The former Cafe restaurant is now called Deca, with a private dining room in the Cafe's former entryway. The Greenhouse Lounge under the skylight is now the Deca Bar. There is new furniture throughout. Deca has a French bistro menu--we dined there one evening and it was quite good. Like the Cafe before it, it never seems too crowded. The Greenhouse served a fabulous weekend brunch that for now is no longer offered at Deca, but the hostess said it may soon return. The hotel's strongest attribute has always been its service. Four Seasons standards and Midwestern friendliness combine to great effect here. The concierges are particularly helpful; we recognized many familiar faces. When we checked in around 8am after a red-eye flight, a room was not immediately available, so we went to the spa to shower and freshen up. I ran into the same outgoing local resident (a spa member) from my last visit, who loves to greet new guests and give impromptu tours of the facilities. At least this time he was a bit further along in his routine--he was wearing briefs, whereas last time he was nude. We were contacted by phone around 10:30 saying our room was ready, but we then discovered it didn't have the southern view we prefer. We were immediately moved to another room on the same floor with the desired view, but were not informed, as we should have been, that this room was smaller-- a Moderate vs. a Deluxe. We opted to stay in this room and it was fine--it had all the same furnishings and we actually preferred the bathroom, which was one large room with a single sink, rather than the split bath in the Deluxe rooms with a large double sink area, but a cramped toilet/shower/tub area. As always, we chose to take the CTA subway from O'Hare, a cheap ($2.25) 45 minute ride that ends about 3 blocks from the hotel. There are four stairways and a transfer involved, however. The American Girl store that used to be below the nearby Peninsula Hotel is now in an even larger space in Water Tower Place just below the Ritz, only an elevator ride away. We love the hotel's location just off the Magnificent Mile, and as always, we visited the Museum of Contemporary Art across the street and gawked at the landmark Mies van der Rohe apartments on Lake Shore Drive a few blocks away. We discovered Mies' own apartment was in a building across the street from the Ritz. I'll admit we actually split our hotels for this visit and tried the James as well as the Ritz. We had also heard nice things about the new Elysian. Plus there are the well regarded Peninsula, Park Hyatt, Trump Tower and Four Seasons hotels. But I don't think we'll ever completely shun the Ritz.

“Convenient Location, but Not the Best Doubletree” Booking was done on-line, but not through the Hilton site, since their site was not working for several days straight. Arrived and the Valet Parking was efficient. $37/day with minimal wait to get your car. Check-in was slightly less than stellar. We had three in our party, as I specified on my reservation, but we were given breakfast vouchers for two (I had paid for three when I booked). We were given two cookies (not that I NEEDED a cookie, it simply represented the LACK of attention to detail.) The room was comfortable enough. I didn't find it to be all that small. It lacked the common find in most hotels, highlighting room service offerings, neighborhood restaurants, etc. The bathroom is small and while the tub and tile were clean, the walls were stained. Breakfast was fine. It was a basic hotel hot breakfast buffet, but is handy. It offered fresh omelets and fresh fruit in addition to scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, etc. Our server was delightfully attentive. At first glance, the dining room looks nice, but I did notice that even in the dining room, the walls were quite grimy. This hotel is located in a great neighborhood, with plenty of restaurants within a short walk. If you stay in Doubletree hotels, this hotel may not match up to your experiences elsewhere, but it is a safe, convenient location. My hope is that they start to pay attention to the details. It shows when they don't.

“I guess it depends where your expectations are - we loved it” I can see why some folks wouldnt like this place. The name does make you think fancy and it says its on the riverwalk. The truth is, its a nice, but not fancy hotel and it is on the riverwalk, but its an end without much traffic, not the bustling section you associate with riverwalk view. So, if you expect a nice, fancy hotel in the action, you will be disappointed. However, if you expect a functional hotel with an enojoyable five minute stroll to all the bars and restaurants for a cheaper price than the bigger hotels, you will be happy. I got the hotel off priceline for a decent rate, 80 a night, for NYE and NYD. We had a room looking over the pool but they were nice enough to move us to a balcony over the riverwalk for the second night. Was much nicer and had a king bed instead of two doubles. The staff was friendly and the place was clean. Dont really have any complaints other than the $12 a day they get to park but i guess that is to be expected for the area. Anyways, id be ok with staying here again since you can save a little and still be on the riverwalk.
“A comfortable stay” This hotel has everything you would need, but a little pricey. Definitely great service and accommodating.
“Excellent, leave kids at home, avoid the dragonfly restaurant” Avon garde and total fun. Will do again, but the restaurant must be run by another team.

“Tired and small” This hotel has the smallest rooms I have ever seen. 220 a night got me a 7 by 14 cell. The bed was great, but the shower had almost no hot water and the toilet would not flush properly and eventually overflowed onto the floor causing a big mess. If nothing else is available this place will work, but with so many choices and many with much better locations, why would you stay here? BTW hotel name changed to King and Grove Hotel. Third name change in the last few years....

“Good Stay” I stayed here for a week on business. It was walking distance to my downtown work location. As a gold member I got some free water, free breakfast, and free internet. The hotel is walking distance to the arena district were there are various restaurants. The room was clean and comfortable. There was a living area with a fridge and wet bar. The bedroom was separate and comfortable.

“Excellent service” Apart from the obvious (cleanliness, location, etc.), I would like to compliment the staff on how they handled a little problem we had with our neighbours. They were partying pretty hard all night, and when we complained in the morning we were moved to another room - not a regular room though, but an executive suite! Which obviously was a very nice surprise and helped us get over that one sleepless night pretty quickly. I think the way situations like this are handled goes a long way to show how much management really cares about their customers - kudos!

“Great Value - book through the 'go boston' website!” We stayed at this hotel 31 March - 3 April 2006 and found it fantastic value for money. The location is great if you don't mind a walk - it took us about 15 minutes to get to Quincy Market - which I think is quite reasonable. We stayed as a family of 4 in the one room - spacious enough and very comfortable. There was no view - and I don't think you would get a good view from any of the rooms as it is only 5 levels high and not in a particularly scenic location. The staff were courteous and efficient. We were given late check out on asking. We booked the hotel through the 'go boston' website for one night, and then paid a discounted rate for the subsequent nights. On check in we had 2 adult and 2 children's 'go boston' cards for one day and two nights trolley bus tour - these would cost almost £150 if we were buying them and so worked out to be a fantastic deal. The only disappointment was the car booked to return us to the airport via the concierge (Thomas)- we paid over the odds for the convenience - yet got a surly and unfriendly driver who virtually threw us out of the van when we got there - a distinct difference from our wonderfully friendly welcome by the Bostonions.

“very happy!” A 4 day visit to Indianapolis turned into a 2+ week stay and I am very glad that we chose this hotel to stay at. (It helped that we had work in this part of town) Conveniently located close to I-65, this is a nice and comfortable hotel. Has all the amenities expected of a Marriott Courtyard (free internet, gym, swimming pool, bistro, guest laundry etc.) Rooms are very reasonably priced and I highly recommend getting the breakfast deal with the room rate. The bistro has many nice and healthy breakfast options plus they also brew Starbucks coffee. There are many restaurants within walking distance with a pub right across the parking lot. Starbucks coffee shop is also right around the corner and so is a wine shop :-) In addition, practically all major shops (target, home depot etc.) are within 2 mile radius from this hotel. Location wise this is simply great if you are traveling for business. The hotel staff wasgreat!! They were very friendly, courteous and helped us many a time. My compliments to the staff for doing a good job. I will definitely stay at this hotel again if I visit the area.

“Drury continues to please me” I continue to be very pleased with Drury Inns. They are a great value and the accommodations have been nicer than higher priced hotels. We were in town visiting my son / OSU. The hotel is a short 2.5 miles on High from his place near Lane. We checked in around 5:00 and the free adult beverages were being served - we didn't have time to sample them though. The room was very similar to the Middletown OH Drury that was our first positive experience with this chain. This one had the same very nice lobby, the very functional and clean room, and as good or better of a free hotel breakfast you'll find anywhere. Our schedule was such that we really were just looking for a place to sleep and a breakfast in the AM so I can't comment on any of the other extras (e.g. pool, free internet, etc). For just a tinch over a c-note , tax and parking included (with their e-saver rate) in the downtown location I couldn't be more pleased. A few reviews I read prior to booking had people complaining about being charged for parking - but come on people they only charged $12 and they are right next door to the convention center and near the arena - that's very reasonable, especially when you consider the relatively low room rate. Our beds were comfortable and the staff at the reception desk and breakfast were friendly and helpful. Based on this experience and my other experience in Middletown I'll continue to look for a Drury as one of my first choice hotel selections.

“fabulous four seasons” I guess all Four Seasons hotels are fabulous. This one is, for sure. When we are here I only go to one restaurant in town other than the one in the lobby. I get lazy. They make it easy to get lazy. Great location too.

“Convenient & comfortable!” Landed at Logan and walked across the bridge to the hotel. Incredibly convenient (although the walk from Terminal E to the bridge is a decent hike with luggage) - but within 10 minutes, I was checked in and up in my room. Great room, good pub in the lobby, and service staff were incredibly friendly. Would definitely stay there again!

“Disappointed” We stayed here for just one night on arrival in Boston, and have to say that water taxi is definitely the way to arrive! The hotel is very smart, and appears to have been recently refurbished: however, our room (1018) was quite small, and the harbour view for which we had paid extra was slightly limited by a large empty roof area in front of the room. Also we had requested a room away from the lifts and were given one opposite them! The bed was very comfortable, and the room was spotlessly clean. We had dinner in the bar, which was very good, although service was efficient rather than friendly (we were virtually the only guests in the bar), and breakfast outside on the terrace, which was very nice, and service was excellent. Overall, we felt that our room was overpriced for what we got.

“Great rooms, and great staff” This trip was with 2 of my girl friends. Shopping and sites, with fun at night. The hotel is a very good location, the room was spacious enough that we did not feel cramped at all. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Would stay there again, and reccomend it highly.

“gut geeignet für Mayo Clinic Besucher” wer in die Mayo Clinic muss ist dort gut untergebracht. Hotel ist sauber, der üblicher Hampton Inn Standard. Leider kein Shuttle zum Flughafen, der liegt allerdings auch gute 15 Meilen im Norden. Nur wenige Meilen zu den Jacksonville Beaches. Zimmer sind leise dank der nicht zu öffnenden Fenster. Ganz in der Nähe AVIS Rentel Car, Parken ist kostenfrei. Nach Downtown könnte man auch mit dem Bus fahren. Hotelpool wer es mag.

“Not Impressed” I felt the Soho Grand was pretty overpriced, and not nearly as good a value as other hotels in the area. The room was very small, which is typical in a New York Hotel, but I don't feel the small space was well utilized. I stayed in the Hilton Millennium on the same trip and felt that while the rooms' physical dimensions were smaller, the Hilton actually felt larger because the space was put to better use. The TV was roughly a 32" flat panel LCD, unfortunately there was no HD programming, and many big name cable channels were missing from the lineup. The bar was very overpriced with terrible service (average wait time for a drink was in excess of 10 minutes). The outlets in the room were inconveniently hidden behind dressers, beds and mini-bars. All in all, I probably would not stay here again.

“Whoa. Basic but charming like a huge steamship on land...” This hotel is what I could get on a weekend that was slammed in San Francisco in October. The price was right but I was a bit worried when I saw that you cannot even check in before a certain hour. Now I know many hotels have this policy but the front desk will not even talk to you. This hotel is a big group hotel and that also means it is less than ideal for wither business or romance? Forget about romance here unless you get tickled by the feeling on the floors that you are on an antique steamship that is grounded. The rooms had the cheapest mattresses possible and the bathroom was basic , basic. I think this would be a two star or less. Now, it is affordable and within a Streetcar to the Castro. The room was clean however and that is no small feat in a hotel that seems gigantic. If you just need a place to crash- then fine. If you are coming in from the BART, it is across the street from the Civic Center Station. There is a Starbucks on the groundfloor and a library also across the street. There is a gem of a Middle Eastern food place in front of the library. IT looks a little dicey but the soup and the food is good. You will see locals there.

“Good Location” Stayed here many times.Staff always pleasant and willing to help.Rooms decent size and have all mod cons..Good buffet or ala carte breakfast.Pool and gym ok.The hotel public areas are being revamped at the moment so there is a little disturbance but no noise heard from guest floors.The sushi bar was always worth a visit.The hotel is joined on to a mall so is handy for shopping and has all usual big American name shops.Mall also contains good food court and a Wagamamas which is a relatively new British owned noodle bar!Never had cause to complain at The Copley.

“Snooty Front Desk- Nice ammenities” Stayed here this past weekend as part of a girls weekend with my sister-in-law. We used her Hilton points to stay. Front desk check-in clerk was very snooty about apparently not having the right paperwork, although my sister-in-law never received the right paperwork from Hilton to begin with. Also, snooty upon departure. We also had to ask about breakfast vouchers as part of their diamond program, this was not offered up front. Room was very nice. Big shower, big TV, Bose system with CD player, well stocked min-bar, two nice bathrobes etc. There is a DRAWBACK if you are staying with someone other than your spouse/partner, the shower is a completely glassed in shower. If you have to go to the bathroom or want to wash your face/use sink and the person in the shower is not comfortable with you walking in, you have to wait. Nice location to things. It was about a $5 cab ride at best to a couple things we wanted and didn't feel like walking too. The bellhop outside was very curteous and knowledable. Oh, french toast in the resturaunt was below average and overpriced.

“Sehr zentral gelegenes Hotel in Manhattan” Die Lage des Hotels ist sehr gut, direkt an der U-Bahn gelegen (Linien 6, E, M) und in Gehdistanz zu vielen Geschaeften und Museen in Midtown. Der Eingangsbereich selbst ist recht wenig aufregend, der Checkin etwas lustlos, der Gang zu den Liften gleicht einem Zickzackkurs zwischen einer Bar und einem Informationsstand fuer Hilton Vacations. Als Hilton Honors Gold Member bekam ich ein Upgrade in die Executive Floors und Zugang zur Executive Lounge im 17. Stock. Die Zimmer sind zwar nicht klein, aber auch nicht sonderlich gross. Die Fenster sind etwas niedrig und die ganze Atmosphaere etwas bedrueckend. Dennoch sind die Zimmer im Vergleich zu anderen Hotels in Manhattan groesser und geraeumiger. Das Continental Breakfast in der Executive Lounge ist nett, die Auswahl ist gut, aber nicht ueberwaeltigend. Es gibt einen Obstsalat, Saefte, Tees, Milch, Kaffee, verschiedene Cornflakes, aber weder Wurst noch Eierspeise, also eher eine Sparvariante.

“Spacious room, super comfy bed!” Having stayed at the Sofitel in NYC the weekend before, I couldn’t help but compare the two. I liked the NYC Sofitel just fine, but I liked this one better. Somehow seemed to have a bit more character and warmth, and the staff was a little more personable and helpful. The room (432) was nice and big, though there wasn't a view of anything if that’s important to you. We were, however, offered an upgrade to an exterior room (with a view) for an add’l $30/night, apparently due to occupancy rates. Perhaps something they’ll continue to offer so long as the credit crunch persists... Getting out of bed each morning was incredibly difficult because the bed was oh-so comfortable. There was no top sheet, though, and I wish there had been. I’m sure if I’d asked, they would’ve accommodated. Lots of nice touches, though - flat screen TV, turn-down service with complimentary Evian, plush robe, etc. Like the room, the bathroom was also very spacious and had a separate shower and bathtub, and lots of counter space. Though I didn’t care for the toiletries provided (not the most pleasant smell and they seemed low-end), I appreciated the regular hair dryer versus the weak travel-size ones offered at most hotels. Loved the hotel bar, Le Bar. The dark, cozy red and black décor was really warm and inviting. It had a lounge feel, with plenty of cushy sofas smartly nestled, offering a little privacy. It was the perfect venue to meet up with a group of friends after dinner. Beware that drinks are slightly on the pricey side, though (my champagne flight was $25 for three glasses). Complimentary tea and coffee are offered in the bar in the mornings (though there’s also a Starbucks just across the street). The location is great, just a few blocks from the White House. Though we didn’t do much within the vicinity of the hotel, cab rides to places we were going were quick and cabs were always available out front, we never had to wait for one. Hotel staff was very pleasant and helpful. I’d definitely stay here again.

“Comfy enough” For the everyday business traveler, this location will suffice your needs. Located in the northwest corner of Houston, it has immediate access the highway system and a wide selection of eateries. The room, bedding, tv selections, and service were good. I would stay here again.

“Great Location” Stayed at this hotel for a conference in the area and found it reasonably priced for a downtown hotel. Cheaper than any of the conference hotels, plus the free breakfast and evening reception/drinks were a bonus. As with all Embassy Suites, you get a great room with a bedroom separate from a living area. One thing that I particularly liked about this hotel was the location. It was right next door to an entertainment complex with a big cinema and bowling alley/bar, plus right across the street from a grocery store for picking up fruits and snacks that can be difficult to find when staying in a downtown area. The hotel was a 3-4 block walk from Navy Pier, and close to the popular Dick's Last Resort restaurant on the water where the waiters insult you purposely. It was also only 2-3 blocks from Michigan Avenue shopping and dining--very easy walk. I also walked to the Art Museum and Millenium Park, although these locations weren't terribly close--I'd say 10 blocks south. Overall, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel. The location was excellent, the neighborhood was safe with a booming condo population of professionals moving in all around it, and plenty of entertainment and food options were within walking distance. One other thing, if you want to hop on the train, there is a nearby station about 1-2 blocks away. Easy to take the train south or north to Wrigley Field to catch a Cubs game. I must say I was not expecting much of Chicago, but I left pleasantly surprised with everything there was to do downtown.

“Good Midtown Hotel, But Small Small” The Moderne is a decent hotel in midtown Manhattan, near Columbus Circle. It's convenient to everything in the city, you can walk to the theatres, museums, and Central Park, and it's close to key subway lines. Rooms are modern but very very small. That's to be expected in a midtown hotel, but be prepared. The rooms are recently refurbished, and the designers did a nice job with the small spaces, so the furniture is convenient and works well, but you will find yourself tripping over your bags a bit. The hotel does not offer breakfast, but the staff is courteous, helpful, and very professional. And of course there are many restaurants and diners nearby, so it's not a problem to find food. My room did not have any sort of view, just a tiny window that looked out on a brick wall, I had to go down to the lobby to find out the weather. Also, for newcomers to New York, be aware that the various hotel taxes add up to an astounding $50 per night, so when the hotel advertises $300 rooms, you'll be paying quite a bit more. New York hotels can bust your budget, but this is a good compromise: a nice affordable hotel in a good location.

“Nice little hotel in a fantastic location” Hotel is located right near union square, great for shopping, sightseeing and the hop-on-hop-off bus services. Also cable car rides. Hotel itself has charm and character. It was clean, room average size, although bathroom was a little small, but shower was always hot. TV was tiny though, but your not there to watch TV. At night it was often very noisy but you got used to it. Staff were very friendly. Breakfast is served on each floor and you take it back to your room, great idea! Although there is no cereal and orange juice often ran out. Overall very happy with my stay and would return again.

“Comfortable hotel with great service & walking distance to Barnes and Philadelphia museums” I didn't expect much because of so many negative reviews but the conference I was attending was being held in this hotel. The management must have been reading the same reviews because by the time I arrived they had clean up the hotel rooms and freshened them with designer linens. There was free bottled water in the rooms. The hotel staff at the front desk, the people who cleaned the rooms, and the restaurant service people all made a point of being of service. Internet is available to hotel guests in the lobby. The hotel is a 10-minute walk to the Barnes Museum and a 20-minute walk to the Philadelphia Museum. Downtown shopping is 10-minute walk in the other direction. There are several convenient restaurants close by.

“Excellent Find” This hotel was just wonderful. Quaint old world charm, spacious rooms and excellent service. Breakfast was delicious and more than adequate. Right in the heart of the historic district it is perfectly situated to take advantage of Philedelphia's attractions. It is also close to a range of eateries offering the famous Phillie cheese sliders. This hotel offers great value.

“Great location but very disappointing customer service” I stayed at the Crowne Plaza Time Square for 12 nights. Firstly, the good - great location right on Broadway at Time Square. My room, a corner room, was large and reasonably clean though had maintenance issues (see below). I had a view of the Hudson River, which was nice, but nothing spectacular (and this was from the 20 something floor). I had a number of issues with my room and service however, which while individually were small issues, together I felt really let the hotel down, especially considering this is supposed to be '4 star' property. After waiting until after 3pm and then being checked by some staff that weren't particularly friendly or welcoming, I headed to my room for a shower but found that the shower in my room was clogged and started filling with water when I tried to use it. Hotel maintenance had to come and dismantle the drain and pulled out whatever was stuck in it, which took around an hour or so. Then, I discovered the toilet was clogged. Maintenance again had to come and attend to the issue; and took three visits over as many days to fix the problem permanently. All in all, this was quite inconvenient and annoying and I never really received a proper apology for the inconvenience. A few days after this, I came to to my room and found the card wouldn't open the door. Back downstairs to the front desk, I was given new room keys, apparently it seemed that on check in they had programmed the keys to stop on working a week earlier than I was checking out. A minor inconvenience but still a bit of an annoyance. Room service at the hotel ends at midnight. One night I called just before 11pm, my order was taken and I was told it would be 45 minutes; however it never arrived. By the time I realised it was getting a bit late and called back, it was just after midnight. No answer. I called the front desk and was told they were very sorry but it appeared the kitchen was closed and everyone had left and they didn't know what had happened to my order. Having been on a 7 week visit to the US, staying at 9 different hotel across the country ranging from 2 star to 4 1/2 star; this "4 star" hotel had the worst service of the lot. I should also mention, internet is quite expensive - over the 12 nights I was there, it cost almost $100. Finally, a few days after my stay I received a generic email that hotels send out asking for feedback, which I provided explaining all the issues. I still never heard back from Crowne Plaza. I assume they just don't care. With thousands of hotels in Manhattan, and hundreds around Time Square, there are plenty of other choices before staying at the Crowne Plaza Time Square and I suggest looking elsewhere.

“Absoluter Klassiker” Wer einmal nach San Francisco kommt, sollte auf jeden Fall probieren ein paar Nächte im Westin St. Francis verbringen. Dieses Hotel ist einfach ein Klassiker und das spürt man auch, sobald man das Hotel betritt. Das Personal war stets sehr hilfsbereit und freundlich und hat sogar teilweise den Tip zurückgewiesen. Wenn man Glück hat, bekommt man ein Zimmer in den neueren Türmen und hat eine Aussicht über die halbe Stadt, von der Golden Gate Bridge bis zum Coit Tower! Kracher! Auch die Lage direkt am einfach unbeschreiblichen Union Square machen das Hotel einzigartig in San Francisco. Leider sind die Zimmer teilweise recht kostspielig, aber das ist doch so ziemlich alles in San Francisco, daher sollte man sich den Luxus doch einmal gönnen und ein Teil Geschichte genießen.

“Seattle/Marriott's best secret hotel” The Residence Inn at Seattle/Lake Union was a great find. I booked this hotel since I wanted a suite with 2 bedrooms and a living room. Our Unit had 2 bedrooms with king size beds which were so comfortable. Each bedroom had a bathroom in which the sink was in the bedroom and a separate room with a tub/shower and toilet. The living room was very spacious and decorated lovely. The unit had a full kitchen with granite counters and updated appliances. The view was incredible. We had a view of Lake Union. The hotel had a full breakfast in the morning. The breakfast was huge...Lots of choices. Parking was in a covered garage. There were many restaurants around the lake within walking distance. This was a spectacular place to stay in Seattle. The hotel was approximately 10 minutes from downtown. There is a street car that stops right in front of the hotel that goes downtown. There was a lot of road construction/road closures around the Lake Union district. The hotel has several types of rooms available. One bedroom suites or just single rooms. I was very pleased with this hotel.

“This property needs a MAJOR renovation” I've stayed at this property a few times over the last couple of years, but this time I definitely noticed it is showing its age. The furnishings in the rooms are definitely dated, including the furniture, the carpet, the kitchen appliances and the bathroom area. The plug in the bathroom didn't even work when I went to plug in my electric razor so I was forced to shave in the kitchen with no mirror. The hotel doesn't deliver a copy of your bill under the door of your room at the end of your stay so you're forced to go the front desk in order to get one which is inconvenient since none of the buildings are connected to the lobby. There are plenty of other Hilton properties within the area which are much nicer and I'd definitely suggest seeking one of them out if you are looking for a Hilton property.

“"Mad Men"-Era Historical Property: You Give Up Some Contemporary Amenities” When you walk in, you see old photos of the place, in its hey-day, I would imagine. It's got a couple of shiny brass plaques attesting to the property's official "historical building" status. So I am sure this review will not sit right with the kinds of travelers who love older properties and historical places, like old-timey inns and "charming" B and Bs, and so on. So let me say the nice things: You couldn't be in a better location in downtown Seattle. Perfect for going anywhere on foot. Pikes Place is nearby, and you pass excellent retail places, like Columbia, where we often buy travel clothing. Public transportation is everywhere. The concierge office is great. They lent us two day-passes to the Seattle Art Center. Wow, what a nice perk. We were also upgraded, at no expense, into a large queen "deluxe" room, and it was nice to have the extra square footage for a few nights, to say nothing of the one of the three windows that looked out over the beautiful tree-filled park that has the Occupy Movement and a convenient Starbucks. The upper lobby was very plush, and a nice place for us to cool our heels after we checked out but before we went to the airport later that night. We were offered food and drink service while we sat up there--very nice. The property has an adjoining restaurant and lounge. We hit the lounge for lunch and evening drinks: good service, nice draft selection, good reds. All right, that said, the hotel's weak Wifi is not up to the task. It was down three times in three days, mostly an hour or so each morning. Of course, they blamed Comcast, but it doesn't take an IT specialist to know that their arcane password-protected system is at fault. They deliver a paper newspaper to your door??? Just a waste of money, like the old peoples' television, which we never watch. The bathroom has shampoo, conditioner, and body lotion in pint-sized vats with squirters that are mounted to the wall like its a YMCA gym. Guess it saves them money so they can deliver a newspaper I throw away. The hard bed was a queen-sized bed!!! Hello!!! All this square footage and a little bed-for-one-person. The room was crowded with dated furniture like a hoarder lived there. I had to move everything back against the walls so it resembled a flea market with some room for foot traffic. Housekeeping, I am sad to say (and I tipped every morning), didn't do that great of a job. The stupid hotel landline rang THREE times when we were there. I had to unplug it. The room is filled with really dated stuff: lots of old brass fixtures, a two-prong (i.e., 1980s) electrical strip along the floor that is inadequate for powering cell phones and devices, and old curtains and light shades. There must have been 15 pieces of ad copy paperwork and laminated trifolds on the flat surfaces, when we checked in. Clutter! We piled them up so they were not in the way on one of the several pieces of furniture we never were going to use anyway. Like visiting an elderly aunt who was falling behind on the renovation she did thirty years ago. While we were there, the staff ran some sort of training crew around our floor noisily, and a room across the hall was being worked on equally noisily for one entire day. The workout room has old equipment. The elliptical didn't work, the two treadmills needed replacement, and they had no bathroom. Two yoga mats--always a nice sign in any hotel--were on the floor being walked on by the few of us who were using the equipment: UNSANITARY; no one is going to use them, people! (There is a good yoga place across the street, BTW.) To their credit, they did provide Purell and cleaning wipes. Room service was expensive and not all that good. It wasn't cheap. We paid over two hundred bucks a night. For that money, I would either expect a bit more or be willing to pay a little more to get what I need. I like to visit charming places, not stay in them. So I wouldn't recommend the Mayflower Park to other travelers, unless you were like the friendly dude in the museum who said he and his wife would come into Seattle, from where they lived in the 'burbs, and stay at the Mayflower Park to enjoy its historical ambience for a Saturday night to enjoy the city. There are three or four good modern hotels within a block or so for travelers who carry iPads and devices/phones and so on. Look near the convention center, around the corner for them. Please, if you are hotel management, don't reply to this.

“Hilton Garden Inn Comes Through” On August 22nd, 2012, after a three week stay, I gave this hotel only an average review because I was disappointed with various aspects of our stay. Ms. Gayle DiLorenzo of the Hilton Garden Inn Tribeca responded to the review and suggested I contact her. I did, and she "made things right", so to speak. As a result, we would like to try the Hilton Garden Inn again in the future. Thank you, Ms. DiLorenzo, for your courtesy and consideration.

“...And I started with low expectations...” We were not expecting much from this hotel based on the price (compared to other NYC hotels during the same period), but they failed to meet even my very low expectations. The place is best described as a "Monet" ("From far away, it's OK, but up close, it's a big old mess.") From outside, the lobby (and by implication the hotel) resembles an average well-appointed hotel. However, as you walk through you realize that despite its hipster pop and circumstance, the Park Central is sorely run down dump. Area rugs are worn threadbare, which was all the more unacceptable since they could be replaced for less than they hotel was charging me for what was to be a 5 night stay. In another sleight of hand, they have made a significant investment in fancy, high tech elevators (and other unnecessary accoutrement), which lead to guestrooms in even worse condition than the lobby. Our first room, which had a view of a wall, proved unacceptable once we noticed the amount of mold growing in the bathroom. How does that happen in a hotel which is cleaning the room daily? The room to which we were moved was significantly better but, ultimately, we determined it wasn’t worth the price tag for several reasons: Moldy/musty smell Itchy uncomfortable bedding that gave us bed bug paranoia Generally unclean/stained furnishings Expensive wifi rates (hotels of this low quality almost always include this service free) Awful “cable” (not even 1 commercial-free movie channel, eg. HBO) Overpriced in-hotel amenities (eg. soda machines offering $3 water) Expensive Times Square-ish area meant any hotel savings was lost on paying double and triple at area eateries etc. Even using the 40% discount coupon we can’t recommend this hotel to anyone. For a few (well-spent) bucks more you can get accommodations that match the pomp and circumstance of the hotel. We left after 2 days.

“Very Comfortable and Convenient” I stayed two nights in the Grand Hyatt Seattle in January, 2011 in an Emerald Suite. My room was on a corner on the 30th (top) floor. The views were great out onto Elliott Bay and at the Space Needle. The room was more than spacious. The bath had a separate shower. I thought the rate was reasonable for the size and quality of the room. I heard no noise from the hall or from adjacent rooms. Things less than perfect included the lighting which was relatively dim. There was no good reading lamp by a chair or sofa. The HVAC was drafty and cool. I finally got it to an acceptable warmth by setting the two thermostats to 75 degrees. Wi-Fi internet access cost $10 per night. It should have been free. The hotel is two blocks from the Westlake station on the light rail line. I was able to use light rail to get to the airport at a cost of $2.50. Trains run at least every 15 minutes and the travel time from Westlake to SeaTac was 38 minutes. The Westlake station is part of the bus tunnel system and I used buses to get around downtown for free. The hotel has three eating options: 1) Ruth's Chris Steakhouse, 2) Starbucks and 3) a so-called deli with an assortment of cafeteria-style foods. I found the deli unappealing. I had a decent sandwich at Starbucks. I had two excellent and reasonably price breakfasts at Ruth's plus a light early dinner there. I was pleased with Ruth's on all counts. Downtown Seattle has a lot of interesting things to see and do, including an abundance of restaurants. I visited the impressive Central Library and the Art Museum. A disappointment was the Sculpture Garden north of downtown which had very few sculptures.

“Potentially a very good choice” Bottom line: At the average TripAdvisor price of over $300 this is probably not a good deal, but is a decent value at $160 per night rate I paid. I am sometimes able to find a good hotel at $100 in DC, so you might do better especially at a hotel that includes breakfast or has other free services you need. The hotel is upscale enough to raise expectations, but may fall short. Overall, I felt it was somewhat better than most hotels I have stayed at, but I do not usually stay in top hotels. Pros: -Near metro -Lots of restaurants nearby, including many ethnic restaurants. Personally, I like the Sake Club a lot. -Clean, spacious and elegant room (it was a corner room). -Window in bedroom--very bright. Marble added upscale feeling. -Comfortable bed. -Very nice lobby. -Quiet for D.C. -Some free extras, eg. free daily paper (USA today), mouthwash, etc. Cons: -Indifferent service. Tea was never replenished, and coffee was only replaced some days. They forgot to replace the bathmat one day. -As with most upscale hotels, all additional services are insanely expensive, from the mini bar to internet access from the business center. ($5.50 for the bottle of water in the room!) -Some rust in bathroom, slight stains on carpets. -Tiny elevators (due to age of the hotel). -Only two chairs in room including desk chair. Other thoughts: -Based on other reviews, it appears room quality might very a lot. -Maid service was low-key. I prefer this, but others may not. They simply made the beds, replenished soap and shampoo and replaced towels, but didn't change sheets, take away partial used items, put away ironing board, etc.

“great place for business travelers” excellent stay at Staybridge Suites near Columbus Airport in Oct 2006. inexpensive 1 bedroom suite, nice gym, 50 cents for a draft beer at their evening snack !, clean, friendly staff, and nice morning buffet. only 5 minutes from the airport. This is NOT a vacation get-away hotel, but it is a great deal for families and business travelers.

“Great Location, Mediocre Property” I’ve been to Seattle dozens of times, but had never stayed at the W. I’m usually in the Sheraton that is only a few blocks away, but I thought this time around I would try something different. We were checked into our room by an agent with minimal friendliness. Not very welcoming. The rooms are classic W in décor and classic W by charging for everything! The bathroom had some mild mildew in the shower and the return air vents were pretty dusty, which turned me off a bit. Upon checkout I notified the agent (same guy) of the issue and he responded with – “Oh... Sorry”. Now for the good points. This property is in a great location; heart of downtown. Located only a few blocks from a light rail station and well within walking distance to restaurants and shopping. The bed is amazing – super comfortable with excellent pillows. This alone was worth the other inconveniences. Overall, I would not recommend this property, rather, I would recommend their sister property, the Sheraton.

“Centrally located to tourist areas” We stayed at the Doubletree Metropolitan over Thanksgiving weekend. We were able to walk a few blocks to the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. Many other tourist sites are within walking distance, for example, MOMA. There are also many large department stores and restaurants in the area. We were able to easily get to other parts of the city using the subway, which has a stop right outside the hotel. We felt that this hotel was not as nice as other Hiltons where we have stayed. The outside of the hotel looks very dated but the room was okay and large by New York standards. The lobby of the hotel has lots of room to wait if your room isn’t ready. The housekeeping staff was excellent. There is no coffeemaker in the room. They charge to store luggage, which is the first time I have run into this. My husband used the gym, and he said it was a good gym. The Business Center does not charge to use the computers, which was a nice touch. The bed was really comfortable and we appreciated the blackout curtains. We both slept very well here. If the price was right, we would stay here again.

“Good Location” Our problems started at the reception. Firstly there was a permanent queue there and even to ask aquestion you had to stand in line behind people checking in. I had booked 2 rooms , one with 2 beds for my 2 sons. The reception told me they could only provide one bed and a rollaway bed for an extra $20. I refused to take it. They kept me waiting while they consulted computers and managers. In the end I settled for a smoking room for the boys with 2 beds and they did'nt charge the extra money. But it is a pity they have not heard about air freshners as the room and even the corriodor stunk of stale tobacco. My advice to travellers is to stand your ground at the reception and demand what you have booked.

“Very good business travel hotel” Being a Marriott rewards member I scoured Priceline to see if i could get better value on a 4 or 5 start hotel and couldn't so I booked the Algonquin. Very convenient location. Service at front desk and in lobby was very good. Room was small but really well designed in the renovation. Very clean. Business center was as to be expected. Lobby was well appointed and quaint. Overall would stay here again for sure.
“IMPRESSIVE!!!” Wow!!! This hotel was VERY clean, spacious, and modern!! I have nothing but great stuff to say about it to my friends. I will most certainly be back!! :)

“Great location, great stay!” My husband and I took the Chinatown bus from NYC to Washington DC to see all the sites. The Metro is not too far from the JW Marriott. Upon arrival, we were greeted with smiles and the baggage attendant took our luggage up to our room. The staff was friendly and helpful (i.e., suggesting places to eat or helping us with directions). The facility was under construction (remodeling), but it was not distracting or intrusive. Our room was very comfortable, clean, quiet, and had a great view of the Washington Monument! I would recommend asking for a room with a view...you will not regret it! One thing that was lacking was a bathroom fan/vent. It made the room very humid after taking a shower. We were able to walk to wherever we wanted or took the Metro with ease. The hotel is in a great location to all the various sites (we walked everywhere and saw everything)! Since this is a higher end hotel, there was an internet charge of approximately $9.99/24 hours. Also, since we did not have a car we didn't worry about a parking charge, but I think it's pretty pricey. We did not eat at the restaurants on site, but did have drinks to end the night at the lounge. It was very comfortable and relaxing. The pool/jacuzzi area was convenient and fun to ease our muscles from walking so much during the day. I would definitely stay at this hotel again! It made our trip to Washington DC fun, relaxing, and comfortable.

“Very disappointing for a Staybridge Suites” This hotel is new, just opened in May. It is clean and quiet but the plumbing in my room did not work properly and despite repeated requests and a 15 minute visit with a manager nothing was done. Also, the evening reception with food is near the pool. It is very unappetizing to be getting some food and have some guy walk in from the pool with trunks and NO SHIRT. Oh uck. Appetite gone.

“Another Great Stay” This is our second trip to NYC where we used this hotel. Once again, we come away strongly recommending the Comfort Inn. We arrived for a two night stay in late July. We had booked the room at least six months in advance for $166 per night using the Choice Hotels website, under the "internet users" special rate. We were placed in one of the newly refurbished rooms on the 9th floor. The good: LOCATION(!), clean, new furnishings, great size (for a NYC hotel room), quiet (with regard to other hotel guests.) The bad: since we were on the front of the hotel, the noise from the garbage trucks seemed to go on all night long, the window air conditioner was quite loud (although, it does help drown out the garbage trucks!), the elevator is (still) quite slow, which was not a real big problem because the hotel was not anywhere near 100% occupied for our two nights. The staff, as before, was fabulous. What amazed me is that I remembered most of the staff from my visit here two years earlier. I did not expect that the same people would be working the front desk, the bellman positions, etc. This is the kind of stability that says something about a little hotel such as this. As before, is it the Marriot Marquis? No, that's one block to the West! It's also $400 bucks a night. I would much rather use the extra $200 per night and go out and DO something in NYC with that money. Please feel free to contact me with any questions you have about this property.

“Another nice stay at my favorite hotel chain.” I was entitled to one freebie night being a Kimpton In Touch member, so I decided to use it for a one night stay at this new hotel so I could attend the Phoenix Symphony, a short two block stroll away. I am a huge fan of Kimpton hotels, and I was generally pleased with the Palomar - the room is beautiful ,( although i would supply a second chair around the desk table ) the staff is friendly, the pool area quite attractive, and the food in the restaurant very good, although rather pricy. I had dinner and a late night snack seated at the bar and the bartenders were great and made me feel welcome. Service at breakfast was also excellent. I did mention this one point of negativity, which I mentioned to several of the staff. I appreciate symphonic music, church music, and good jazz. I could do without the raucous music which only makes the restaurant scene louder than it already is ( I know, this is what the bar crowd likes ) and while I enjoyed reading by the side of the pool, and taking a pleasant dip, I could do without the also raucous music playing right above my head. For heaven's sake, turn this stuff off and leave me with some peace and quiet. I seem to be in the minority on this issue, but that is my opinion!

“Very nice hotel with great atmosphere” This hotel was nicely decorated and the staff was great. The 5pm-6pm free wine in the lobby every day was particularly nice. I had a room facing Wilshire Blvd which could be quite noisy with the traffic. There are several restaurants, a movie theatre and stores within walking distance. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

“The Getto” The hotel is located in a deserted part of downtown. There were homeless people hanging out very near the hotel and you had to pass several blocks of abandoned bulding before getting to "civilzation". I booked 2 room, one for my wife and I and the other for my brother-in-law. We did walk to the riverwalk the 1st day (daylight) and my wfie was feeling very uncomfortable so we got a taxi on the way back. The rest of the time, I drove and paid for parking....I felt it was safer than walking. And the hotel itself needed a lot of improvement. Room carpets was nasty. They had safes in the room, but when I tried to get a key, they said that they didn't have keys and I can leave my valuable at the front desk...OK thanks but no thanks. There were trash in the stairway the 2 days we were there....they never cleaned it up. One day there were a huge trash bag outside our door that smells aweful. We finally moved it, when it wasn't picked up after several hours. Both our room's remote didn't work and when I called the front desk, he said that he was alone and I need to come down to get a replacement (this was at 6:30 pm and it was daylight). I did get a replacement but the new remote battery cover was missing and the batteries kept falling out.Please don't stay here if you want to have a good time in San Antonio. It was the worse part of our vacation.

“Close to the convention centre and Pike's Market” Great location, rooms are alright...nothing fancy...average in fact..nice lobby and nice lobby bar..staff reaonable well trained...nothing stands out about this property. They have a nice low cal menu in the restaurant..that was novel and the lobby bar had a few cool drinks..but service was slow...

“Terrific hotel- Can't wait to go back!” The Grand Hyatt was wonderful! Perfect location. They allowed me to check in early and had a gentlemen greeting everyone as they waited to check in/check out. Every staff member I saw greeted me throughout the stay. The room was spacious and spotless. The towels were nice, the bed was comfy, and the toiletries were ok. I had the breakfast buffet one morning since the rate package provided a 1/2 price coupon. It was $10. The buffet was really, really good. All kinds of fresh fruit, eggs, biscuits, fritattas, meats, cheese, breakfast breads, etc. The maids were not intrusive. The room overlooked the atrium and provided a change of pace. If you go, remember to go towards the 11th street Metro exit. The hotel has a corridor from Metro. I didn't know which way to go the first time. The only drawbacks were the extra charges. There was a fee to use the internet in the business center ($10 for about 8 minutes). Local calls were not free either. I have no idea how much my soda from the mini-bar will cost.

“5 Star Hotel in Every Way” The Tower side of the Waldorf Astoria is a big step above the other side. I stayed in a normal room back in December and submitted a mixed review. We had several issues that last time. Due to the fact that I had meetings in one of the Waldorf Towers Suites, I stayed in one as well. WOW! This room was in fact more comparable to an apartment. The room was pristine in all aspects. I really enjoyed the lounge access on this side as well. The price starts at least double the rate of the other side, but worth it if you desire the best of the best. Truly a landmark hotel. I can't wait to see the end results of the nearly billion dollar makeover!

“Unique and funky hotel in the heart of Dupont Circle” The Hotel Palomar is located on 2121 P St NW in the suburb of Dupont Circle. If you are getting here by taxi from Union Station, the fare is approximately $12, or if you are arriving by the metro, it's a 5 minute walk. There are a few restaruants and late night eateries along 2121 P St and plenty more to choose from on the streets that lead off Dupont Circle itself. I was met by a cheery young fellow from concierge and an equally pleasant and knowledgeable front office staff member by the name of Suzanne (I think). After arriving by train from New York, in the mid afternoon, I was expecting my room not to be ready but to my surprise my room was available. The lady at the front desk was very personalable and ensured she covered everything from hotel amenities to things to do in Washington, it was a genuine and friendly welcome to which I was thankful for. I was given a map of the city and also a guide to the city by Suzanne which made for some interesting reading as I could then venture out with at least an updated idea as to what to do whilst I was visiting. Whilst the view was not the greatest (I think other apartments), this was not a major concern for me, however having said that, the room was very spacious and comfortable. The room had a plush animal print bed runner and also 2 robes in the large wardrobe, 1 was zebra print, the other being leopard print - definitely unique and quirky. I did not take up the option of continental breakfast but was offered a tea/coffee when I was checking out really early (5am). The other front office staff member was Bernadette, she was very pleasant and handled the checking out transaction with efficiency and professionalism, she also offered to see if I needed any transportation to my desired location. The hotel also has free wi-fi in the room which is always a bonus and as far as hotels go, seemed like it was always busy which is always a good sign to me. On the downside, the only thing I could pick out was that some of the rooms are quite close together, my room was in a sort of cul-de-sac to coin a phrase, so the rooms opposite mine were very close. This is not a huge issue but guests situated here should be mindful of the close proximity when they are exiting or entering their rooms as their voices travel, particularly when having discussions outside the room. The hotel staff that I encountered were genuinely pleased to be of service and for my stay, the hotel was exactly what I was looking for in terms of location and class.

“Cheap, good value, no frills” We stayed in a 2 roomed suite here for 60 dollars. It is simple and quite old even though we had a refurbished suite but it was clean and excellent value. Breakfast was good, better than we expected. Great for a one night stopover. And free wifi & parking.

“Nice hotel” If you are a gold/platinum member your free breakfast would be a regular coffee and a muffin (or an equivalent combination) from a Starbucks in the lobby. Room service is quite slow. Otherwise, it is a nice hotel in a good location.

“Convenient, Friendly, Quiet” In Washington DC for business and got a great deal at the Homewood Suites. It is in decent area and off the main road as you use a side road to access the hotel main entrance. It is a 10 minute walk from McPherson Sq metro center and lots of restaurants around its location. The hotel does not have a bar or restaurant inside, so consider that if crucial to your decision. They have free breakfast every morning and a light meal at night with beverages (alcholic included) on Mon-Thursday. Room (suite of 2 rooms) were clean and well maintained.

“Sleek, modern, eco-friendly hotel in good location” We recently stayed here for a brief vacation before a work-related conference. Overall, this is an excellent hotel. The room was well appointed and very clean. (One thing we did notice off the bat is that the rooms seem a tad bit narrow - but they're pretty long, so that makes up for it.) The bathroom is nice, but there was only a stand-up shower. Still, plenty of room. The bed was comfortable and the housekeeping service was great. And, the hotel gym is the BEST I've ever seen at a hotel. One downside is that they charge for internet access. The concierge was helpful but there is not really a business center. The location is good - walkable to Pike Place Market and shopping, and not too far from other attractions.

“If you're a tourist, stay here” The hotel is located in the heart of Times Square. While the Marriott Marquis and Doubletree may be fully immersed in the crush of people, the Renaissance is in the thick of it. By the thick of it, you should be prepared to bump (physically) a lot of people. You should be prepared to walk to 8th Avenue (about 5 minutes away) to get a taxi. Once you have made it to the hotel, if you're visiting New York for leisure, this is a fantastic hotel. Though in Times Square, I heard no street noise in my 25th floor room. The floors have fewer than 12 rooms each so you can generally expect quiet. Currently, though, the hotel is undergoing exterior construction from 10 AM to 7 PM Monday to Saturday so expect to hear some drilling regardless of the room. The rooms are nicely appointed and large by New York standards. There is a comfortable chaise by the windows and the desk is large enough with enough plugs if you need to work. The beds are not remarkable; while they are pillow top I would not describe them as soft. Aveda products are stocked in the bathrooms. My King room did not have a tub; instead it had a shower with a seat. Housekeeping does a good job, providing both turn down service and organizing toiletries if you happen to be someone that leaves items all over the counter. The common areas of the hotel are well maintained, though it can seem a little odd taking an elevator from the 7th Avenue entrance up to the main lobby. A staircase would be nice since the wait to get up/down that one floor is usually longer than the wait to get up to the 25th floor. Room and valet service is standard for New York - expect 30 minutes whenever you need staff to come to your room. The staff is, though, very attentive and responsive to concerns. If you're a Broadway fan or just looking for some fun, the TKTS (discounted same-day ticket booth) is about 30 seconds walking from the hotel. Rockefeller Center and 5th Avenue are within 5 minutes and Central Park is 10 minutes.

“Land of the Zombies” I always like to read the other reviews before posting my own to make sure we are writing about the same place because some of the reports are so glowing that I would liike to meet the other reviewers to make sure they are real. We stayed at the studio 6 with advance reservations for 4 nights. The price was high for this sort of place and we paid $20 a night extra because we had 2 dogs and the charge is $10 per might per dog. This brought the total cost up high for this kind of place. Upon arrival in the afternoon, had we been able to do so, we would have kept driving and found a better place closer in to Burbank. This area is crummy and walking the dogs around showed more barbed wire and spiked fences including the motel itself than might be found at Folsom Prison.There are lots of hoody type people hanging around on the corners and night time has a lot of wild traffic activity. Points to consider: the room was okay, a bit worn out, the kitchen was okay but lacking in items. The bathroom was spotless but no counter for toiletries, only the limited part of the sink. The towels and bath mat-- I use better stuff to wash my car. The cheapest linens available were used, maybe Chinese rejects? The t.v. was good, plenty of cable stations but no instructions for the more complicated procedures which caused a problem. the wi fi internet is among the best, fast, swift, easy on line. we even watched a netflix movie through the laptop which proves it was high quality connection. The managers were okay, there is not too much to ask of them. The pool is in the center and unusued due to the cool weather. Its generally a small place with 2 wings, a laundry room. The parking lot is the nightmare area. Spaces are tight and many guests had big trucks and suv's probably because they had pets or children and it was tight terrible parking. We parked a pickup truck with great difficulty and wanted to avoid leaving it on the street due to the area. The first two nights there was a man lurking in the parking lot, smoking. I found out later he was a long term guest. While parking one night, trying to get into a tight spot, we bumped his front bumper. There was no damage to either vehicle. He got argumentative and would not let up saying that his junker 95 nissan pathfinder was damaged. He kept it up and I called the police who arrived in 10 minutes and defused the situation. We checked out the next morning and got a refund for the 4th night. Judge for yourself if you want to stay here. Sad to say, we find Motel 6 generally patronized by crummy people. Many motel 6's are in uncrowded locations which makes them a good place to stay especially on highways. In cities though, they are more like hot sheet places with guests coming in and out for a quickie. They allow pets which is the primary reason we stay there. I know that the company is at the mercy of the guests that are greatly varied. But think carefully before you stay here. The place was clean and the maid service was fine but the value and safety were questionable.

“Average, needs a refresh” This is a convenient location if you need a hotel near the airport. My room was in need of a refresh. Wallpaper was peeling, there were dust marks and holes in the wall from a painting that had been removed. At best, this gets an average score.

“conference hotel good for business not for the holiday maker” Apart that I had to change rooms three times and harbour view is bay view or vice versa I was told by the rather unfriendly staff .The rooms are nowhere 4 or I think that might even 5 Star , 3 at its best . Gym is great pool as well and the conference facilities are state of the art. If you have to go on business go moaning - nothing for a vacation.

“Shower was great, the rest is just 'not bad'” I stayed here rather than a midtown hotel because a friend was having a special event just a couple of subway stops away. On the plus side, this hotel is on the less expensive side for NYC, has large new bathrooms and awesome showers, nice bath toiletries, ample nice towels, and everything was very clean. The desk staff also were friendly and smiling. Location is fairly decent, as it's close to little shops and restaurants and a subway is 2 blocks away, although I would prefer to stay closer to the subway since 2 fairly unpopulated blocks are pretty long and dark at night. On the minus side, the room and its furnishings were kind of old and dingy. I didn't mind the room being small - I don't need a lot of space to shower and relax in my comfy bed for a couple of nights when I spend my days elsewhere. But the walls were a slightly grimy-looking beige, the door was institutional gray, the desk and wardrobe looked about 25 years old and the air conditioning unit even older than that. I wished the room looked a little more spruce since the old rooms didn't seem to fit very well with the shiny modern lobby. The AC did work as far as cooling the room and I guess I should be grateful for that, but the control for the AC was slightly wonky and I could not get the fan to reliably turn off resulting in the room getting very freezing during the night (and no extra blanket in the room). Also slightly wonky were the in-room safe, which worked but you sometimes had to enter the code 4-5 times to get it to lock, and the flush mechanism on the toilet, which had to be held down to flush and which occasionally made a very loud dying cow noise. I was glad I was traveling alone because the noise would have woken up anyone trying to sleep in the next room had I flushed in the night. My room had a window...that looked out on a ginormous piece of building equipment, so no points for a view. They did provide a bathrobe to use in the room but its belt was missing, so it was a bit hard to use it. Finally, I have to echo the person who said the staff didn't really check to see if the people coming in and out had a key. The outside door is not locked, there is no doorman and the staff including the night staff seem pretty young and not like they could stop anyone from going upstairs anyway. You are also not required to use a key to make the elevator stop at your floor, meaning that anybody can pretty much come in and wander around, which given that it's NYC makes me a little nervous. For the price it wasn't a bad deal considering I spent most of my time out of the room, but I'd probably scout around for more options next time, unless the rooms are overhauled and modernized.

“large improvement” I stayed her 9 months ago, but they have renovated the rooms since then.. This is not the W, but for what this hotel is, and for staying here it's great. great breakfast. great staff nice new bedding and very accessible to my meeting and the airport. I would absolutely stay here again and recommend it. they are planning on renovating the front desk and this is probably one of the only things that needs improvement at this time It's really nice to have a frig and microwave in the room and the people are really nice.

“Great hotel - friendly service” Just returned from a great 5-day stay at the Hyatt. This is a very family friendly hotel - they showed a kids movie on a big screen the night we arrived, there was a watermelon eating contest poolside, and a bonfire each night (s'mores fixin's for sale).
