Our boys (age 6 and 11) loved the pools and the waterslides. The pool with the 2 big slides is nice and warm, as is the larger saline pool. The pool with the little slide is not heated - brr! Hot tub is great. There is poolside drink and food service from Swim on the property. Our AAA rate also came with complimentary breakfast and free parking. The breakfast was at the Red Marlin which is the property's nice restaurant, and the buffet was quite good. Read the fine print because we didn't understand that the free parking was for self-parking only... not free valet parking. But their valet staff was very helpful and even put air in our rental car tire when a warning light came on. There was a problem with our queen suite but after quite a wait, they were able to give us a king suite and comped us an adjoining king room which were great. Good water pressure in showers, all staff were very friendly and professional, good spa experience, clean and roomy. Loved the bagel/espresso place on property too. Of course, very close to SeaWorld (cab fare is less than parking, btw). All in all, a great stay - thank you!

“Not Quite There” The title of my review basically sums up our recent stay at the Andra. Overall, we were satisfied with our stay, as we got a deep discount, but I'm left wondering how or why they are listed with Small Luxury Hotels of the World. We had a Lux King corner suite, and the suite itself is quite spacious, and very quiet, we did have a restful sleep. Beds/linens were soft and comfortable, and they brought up extra pillows as requested. There was plenty of storage in our suite -- 2 closets and a set of drawers, plus the generously-sized night tables were a plus. However, the sofa was disappointing -- of cheap construction, and sagging in the middle; fairly uncomfortable to sit on to watch tv. The armchair seriously needed recovering, as the edges were worn, dirty and frayed. The suite is due for an overhaul soon; we noticed chipped paint throughout, plus chipped and scratched furniture. The carpets felt a bit grimy -- there was an overall feeling that the room could have been cleaner. The bathroom is small (I knew this going in, having read past reviews). This did not bother me much, as there were adequate shelves and storage. However, if you like soaking in the tub, forget it. The tub has a very low overflow drain, obviously designed by someone who hates baths. I'm 5'2" and not very big -- the maximum water level came up to my lower abdomen. As I reclined trying to soak, the water kept draining off, and I gave up after about 5 minutes. Shower pressure is good and tons of hot water any time of the day. The Face Stockholm amenities are a delicious subtle white tea fragrance; however the bottles are the size of postage stamps, which seems cheap for a "luxury" hotel. The staff are happy to send up more, but it was tiring to request this on a daily basis. The staff were mostly 20-30 somethings and very pleasant and eager to please. However, I still feel they have not achieved a "luxury" level of service. We had a simple request that we be sent a Seattle Times, v. a New York times as we like to read local news. On a daily basis we received a New York times, which to give them credit, was swiftly replaced with a Seattle Times on request, but we shouldn't have had to keep asking for 4 days in a row. Another time we asked a desk person to reconfirm a reservation (the concierge had left) and he looked at us like we handed him a dead fish. It may seem that I'm nitpicking, but I would expect this from maybe a Motel 6 v. a "luxury" hotel. I would actually place the Andra slightly above a 3 star hotel, not at a "luxury" level. The staff for the most part, are accomodating and pleasant, and the room was ok. We would stay again if we got the same low rate; however, we would not stay if we had to pay the high season rate of approx $480.00 -- we felt the service and room would not be worth it.

“A Murray Hill Must, Comfort and Location” Stayed here for two nights in June with my two teenage daughters in a one bedroom suite. We were extremely surprised at how spacious both rooms were - very comfortable with plenty of lighting and seating. This hotel has been renovated recently and is contemporary - I loved the color scheme. The beds were extremely comfortable - not too hard but just the right support. A very pleasant surprise to find that the suite had two full bathrooms. As you can tell we were very happy with the room. I would highly recommend this for families. There was a limited view of the street and building across - not much to see but actually was fine. There was very little external noise also a nice plus especially for New York city. There was a bit of interior noise. We could hear hallway conversations quite clearly and at night with all the lights out you could see light shining through a thin opening between the side of the door and the door frame (explains the clarity of the noise). This did not bother us that much as we were at the end of the hallway and the other guests around us were pretty quiet. We did have some thumping noise from above either a dog or small child. After some time we called the front desk. When we returned from dinner, the noise had stopped. We heard it one more time the next morning but just briefly. We got a great package which included parking and breakfast - a great deal!! The hotel staff was really friendly and very prompt to respond. I would give high marks to the service. The fitness room was pretty basic - a couple of aerobic machines - elliptical, bike and treadmill and some free weights. It is in a funny location with no access to a bathroom or water. The roof deck was much smaller than it appears in the photo and when we were here there was a sign on the door that led to the deck that said it was just for use by guest on the penthouse (16th) floor. The one big minus here is the elevators are extremely slow and only carry a few people at a time. If you want to stay in the Murray Hill area I would highly recommend this hotel. It will definitely be my first choice to return to.

“ok at best.....good if compared to 3 star resorts...glaringly bad if compared to five star resorts...” I stayed here over New Years with my spouse, three children, and mother-in-law. The purpose of the trip was to pamper my wife and mother in-law at the spa. There was a nice new years eve children's program that allowed us to go out and have dinner. This was a very good program and I recommend it. However, everything else about the stay was mediocre at best. 1) We had two connecting rooms. It was obviously that the previous occupant was smoking cigarettes or cigars. The smell was terrible. We were moved to another room after several hours. They moved us to a higher floor. This time the room was okay but the hallway smelled very badly. This was simply unacceptable. 2) The spa which is supposedly very good was surprisingly average. The service was poor and facilities were not up to par. Therefore, I must give a mixed review. I dont think that I would return unless I was trying out the golf course which looked nice.

“Charming and cool” For a while this was my defacto hotel in Los Angeles. It was kitchy and clean and neer where I wanted to be. As one could guess the place has a farm theme which could be tired but to me it's a winner. My favorite room was the "Don't tell" suite which comes with a wet bar and mirrored ceilings! The televisions in the hotel are small, the bathrooms are small and the pool is small. I guess it's all about the decor and the location right across from the farmers market and the Grovve that make this place worth it. On the F & B side I can say that the restaurant, "Tart" was nice for breakfast.

“Great hotel - excellent location” We only stayed one night and we had got a great deal through expedia. We had booked one of the inward facing rooms as we wanted to be sure of a quiet room but on reaching the room we found we had been put into a "disabled" room which actually overlooked the Apple store. We returned to reception and we were moved without any issues to a room on floor 8 which overlooked the zen garden. The room was lovely - we did have robes hanging in the wardrobe as well as some underwear that you could buy (which I thought was a bit odd). We appreciated the free glass of wine in reception and although the check out time was 12noon, we asked for a later 1pm check-out and this was no problem at all. I was very impressed with this hotel - the location, price and comfort of the room certainly made it the best we have stayed at during any of our trips to San Francisco.

“It's only okay, but definitely not for light sleepers or people with bad backs.” Yes, it's relatively cheap. Yes, the staff is friendly. Yes, the place is clean. Yes, parking is free. Yes, you can walk to the Riverwalk--the quiet part. To get there, you have to walk under a freeway overpass. HOWEVER, the front of the hotel faces an expressway exit ramp which is noisey all night and the back of the hotel faces a major construction site--workers get there at 7:00 AM and stay as late as 9:00 PM. We had oil from a crane drip on our car one night, had to leave the partking lot early one morning (or park overnight in another lot) so that said crane wouldn't splatter the car with liquid stucko being hallued in a large bucket to the roof and it's a small lot. If you arrive much after 7:00, you may have to park on the street. AND there's a very well used freight train track a block away. Trains go through all night sounding their whistles--sometimes only 1/2 hour apart. The beds are very soft. I ended up sleeping on a recliner with my feet on the coffee table, while my husband slept cross-ways on the kingsized bed. The breakfast is okay, but not much more than you'd get for free elsewhere. In short, if your main objective is to find an inexpensive, clean room not too far from the convention center and end of the Riverwalk, you'll probably like this motel. However, if you want a restful vacation hotel with amenities, spend the extra money and stay somewhere else.

“I don't know why Hyatt keeps their name on this hotel” This hotel is fine if your idea of service is a particularly nice Holiday Inn in the late 1970's. The only trouble is, they think they deserve 2008 rates. The place is a huge mess architecturally, With a dated, ugly lobby that is either too hot or too cold, depending on Chicago's weather. The staff is friendly, but poorly managed: Apparently no one has ever instructed the housekeepers not to shout down the hall to each other, and a used room service tray sat in the hall across from my room, unattended and unlovely, for a day and a half, until I finally called Room Service and asked them to take it away The "Big Bar" is an expensive, incredibly mediocre establishment where you can expect to wait 15 minutes with a dirty glass from a previous customer in front of you before you are approached by a bartender. The one bright spot is Stetsons: The resident steakhouse, which has a nice staff, and at least a bit of an idea of service. Seriously, Hyatt is not doing themselves any favors by keeping their name on this thing. I'm sure it's a cash cow, as they have plenty of convention space here, and something like 2000 rooms, but you'd think Hyatt - with their corporate headquarters around the corner - would think twice about this blight on their brand. Tear it down, rebuild it, and start over with a well-trained and well-managed staff.

“Nice hotel in Downtown Detroit” This was a fairly typical current-day full service Marriott hotel. The room size and setup were ok--ample size but not especially large. It is located in Downtown Detroit, and from what I was able to determine was one of the better options there. I was able to book at a discounted convention rate. If I had paid the regular rates, I would have felt the hotel was overpriced. Front desk and staff were helpful. Service for the room was ok, but slightly below other hotels of this type. I was surprised by the plastic cups rather than real water glasses. Bedding was nice. The room decor appeared to have been renovated somewhat recently. We were unable to get anything to eat when we checked in late in the evening on the first night. The bar was not very inviting and service there was spotty. I am rating this hotel "above average" because it has a bar and restaurant available (in comparison to the limited service hotels that don't have them at all), because the room was nice, and because the rate was very good. Some will rate this property as "average", and I would not disagree with that, either. I arrived by taxi. Be aware that if you drive in, you will need pretty good directions--and the motor entrance may be separated from the "front" entrance or the street address (watch out, MapQuest users!). It appeared to me that the hotel entrance is not very visible from the streets, and there are some challenging one-way streets in the immediate vicinity.
“I really like this hotal” Great location, right on the Mile. Practically inside of Nordstrom. Nice lobby, great rooms, great service.

“cheap hotel with a not too bad location and a free parking” We spent one night in this hotel and I am happy we did not stay longer: the bed was not comfortable, the staff was not particularly friendly. We won't come back even if the hotel has its own charm.
“New York 2011” Very nice hotel and nice staff hotel. Although a little bit far away from Times Square, is next to a subway station. Very good option in New York. I tottaly recommend it!

“Loved It - Warm, Friendly Staff” This is a charming hotel with some of the friendliest staff I've ever met. The location of the property was centrally located and convenient, and the amenities offered within the hotel were very nice. The fitness center is modern and up to date with a decent supply of equipment and cardio machines. Had breakfast in the Bistro and it was delicious- and reasonably priced. The bathroom was bit out of date, but they had done a nice job of trying to add updated touches to keep it in line with the rest of the hotel facilities. Loved the lobby and check in area. I even left my phone in the back of one of the town cars that works at the hotel, and the concierge was able to track him down and get my phone back to me - so impressive. Great all around!

“The Best!” WOW! I’m not sure that there are enough superlatives in my vocabulary to completely describe my experience at The Peninsula. The only downside is that this hotel will possibly ruin you for all lesser offerings. My wife and I moved here for one night after spending two nights across the street at the Ritz-Carlton. The desk staff at the Peninsula was accommodating was able to get us assigned a room at the early time of 10:00 AM even though we were visiting on a very busy weekend. This was a nice surprise to begin our stay. The friendly clerk then walked us to our room, introduced us to the many features of the room, and verified that everything was to our satisfaction. I found the level of service throughout the hotel to be exceptional. Every employee that I came into contact with was polite and helpful. The room was very nice. We had reserved basic room, and found it to be quite comfortable and spacious. The earth toned décor is elegant without being overwhelming. The bed and linens are just wonderful, and it can be hard to coax yourself out of bed in the morning. The fact that you can control all of the electrical for your room from a bedside panel was a feature that I had never before experienced, and I just loved it. The bathroom was also large and well appointed. A two person soaking tub with a television perched above was on the far wall. Another control panel for the lights, radio, television, and phone are within easy reach. The tub’s speakerphone even neutralizes the sound of the water so that a caller does not hear that you are calling from the tub! The bathroom which is all finished in marble and frosted glass also includes a large shower and other necessary facilities. The room also contains a fair sized closet, electronic safe, personal fax machine, DVD Player, and well stocked mini-bar. The 19th and 20 floors are where the pool and spa are located. We found these areas to also be very nice. Most of the common areas were stocked with chilled bottled water, and the lobby had a coffee bar set up in the AM hours. The hotel bar is a warm, inviting place to have a drink. However, it can get quite crowded. If there are any negatives to mention, I would say that the selection of soaps in the room could have been better. Also, parking $$$ will break you if you bring an auto, but I guess that is pretty standard for downtown Chicago. In conclusion, this place is just the best! At least the best I have ever stayed in. the Peninsula has a great location right on North Michigan, a warm, friendly staff, and very comfortable rooms. What else can you ask for?

“love-hate relationship” I have a love-hate relationship with the Aloft brand in general, this was my second stay at this particular property. I always want to love the Aloft's trendy Baby W feel, but it always falls way short. For newbies, in the shower at Alfot they do not provide small bottles of shampoo, they have a dispenser mounted in the shower with a top that locks into place so only the staff can refill it. While showering i noticed the top to mine was broken and unlocked, kind of creepy and unhygienic. The light that illuminates the bathroom vanity was disabled and a Post it style note was stuck to the mirror stating the light was not working. The small lamp from the desk was placed on the bathroom counter (odd). Aloft's pillows are the worst, luckily I called and was promptly delivered 2 feather pillows. The window shades are thin and flimsy, they never are able to darken any rooms at Aloft properties. Front desk staff tries to throw around some tragically hip attitude but don't let it get to you. They get the job done and it is obviously part of the staff imaging at this property, like they went to a American Apparel and hired away their workers. The location is unparalleled for food and nightlife, but I think I am going back to The Westin proper.

“The room size is the only drawback” I travel into NYC many times a year for business and am always on the hunt for a great room at a great price. Prices were a little higher this year so I chose this hotel based on the reviews, location to what I needed and price. The hotel is close to everything. Bars, restaurants, shopping are all outside your door. The front desk staff were wonderful and they actually had a room ready for me to check into at 915am. It appears to be a new property and found everything shiny and in good condition. They have a free breakfast in the morning which is a nice way to begin your day. Elevators seemed fast (it is a 20 story hotel) and only had one time I waited more than 3 minutes. I was on the 20th floor and had a great view and NO NOISE. In many hotels in the city, you hear everything out your window no matter how high your floor is. You could tell they installed sound proofed windows since there was a huge difference from window open to closed. I slept like a baby. What little noise you may hear is drowned out by the in wall AC unit and you can have the fan run all night to give you the buffer sound to muffle out all others sounds. The room is small, I mean small even for NY standards. 2 people could stay in a queen room, but it would be tight. They have some nice amenities in the room which helps you look past the size. Nice desk and comfy desk chair (chairs is almost up against the bed), great lighting, granite floors and counter in the bathroom, flat panel TV, safe, coffee maker, windows that open, dual phones, hair dryer, small wardrobe with hangers, iron and board and there are only 3-4 rooms per floor so noise is kept to a real minimum. You have limited space on either side and end of the bed which makes walking a little challenging. No other chair and no other place to really sit but the bed. Would recommend this room for 1 person. Wake up call was on time, everyone I came into contact with was very nice and overall I would stay again for a 1 night stay. If you are looking for a place to sleep and get ready, this is your place. If you are looking for a place to spread out and relax, this may not be the right choice. my rate was $189 plus tax.

“Excellent Service, Great Location” For business travel, my favorite Chicago hotel. I've stayed many times the past several years, and always the service is excellent, easy check-in, providing whatever is needed when needed, anticipating needs, and easy check-out. Probably the best service of any Four Seasons Hotel in the U.S.

“Very Good Overall” The Grand Hyatt is a good option for business travelers. The location is fine, and the staff has a wonderful attitude. The restaurant is very good for breakfast, and the health club is good. The facilities are a bit dated, there were not enough easily accessible outlets in my room, and my tv did not work. On balance, though, this is still a good choice, if only because of the staff.

“First rate hotel in the heart of Chi-town” We held a customer conference at the Elysian in March 2011. The hotel and its staff are first rate and our client event was a huge success thanks to their efforts. Highly recommend this hotel for any purpose when in Chicago.

“Will return to the Michelangelo” We just stayed at the Michelangelo for a total of 3 nights. The hotel upgraded our room to what has to be a very large room for NYC with a great "urban" view - from 3 windows across 2 walls - of NYC. Once might think this would be loud, but they must have sound-proof windows...not to mention double blackout blinds - this and the very comfortable beds/pillows made for a great sleep. The bathroom was lovely - with plush towels - and large. I expected the typical once a day cleaning and was pleasantly surprised that in addition to the standard daily cleaning, the room was "tidied" and towels replaced each evening in connection with the evening turn-down service. The only negative - and a minor one - is that the included "Italian-style breakfast" - is one that I would re-title "coffee with a muffin" - very, very basic. That being said, there's plenty of other places to eat around the hotel so it wasn't a big deal. Generally speaking, the location can't be beat if you want to be centrally located.

“An OK stay” I am currently staying in the Courtyard Cherry Creak in Denver and I am a bit disappointed by it. To set the stage, I have been staying at Marriot brand hotels for business for the past 4 years and have enough perspective for comparision. The Good: I was very impressed with the front desk staff. This has come to be my expectation but they were well above average. After checking me in, they made sure that I had a sense of options for dinner and helped me figure out where I was. When I came back down to the lobby later in the evening, they remembered enough about our initial conversation to continue it without missing a beat. Further, when I came back from dinner a few hours later, they were able to ask me about it in surprising detail. Bravo--very personal touch. I liked the flat screen TV in the room and was pleased to see that the furnishings were reasonably up to date. The Bad: I didn't like the fact that there was no closet in the room. There was a wardrobe, but it took me a while to figure this out. (Please understand that I am not an idiot, but the configuration was not intuitive.) The Ugly: The proximity of the hotel to major streets is a bit of a problem. There was a fair amount of noise (I stayed in the "front" of the hotel facing the main drag) which could have been a problem if I were not a very heavy sleeper. The "view" is also icky--a Hooters, etc. There was obvious construction going on inside the hotel to update it and I am hopeful that the management team decides to try to spruce up the outside a bit.

“brag-worthy” The boyfriend and I pulled up to the Andaz Hotel dressed in cargo shorts and hiking boots (we'd gone hiking & climbing) and even though, we were treated like royalty the instant we pulled up. The hotel is sexy and it smells so damn good. You have no idea how amazing it was to walk in to the Andaz after a long, tiresome day. The atmosphere was soothing and as we checked in we were offered a complimentary beverage (wine, iced tea, water.) Instantly, we knew we were not leaving this property until the moment we had to check-out. We stayed in a Large King Suite, this room is definitely created for a couple. The room was clean, cute, and cozy. There was music playing in the room to set the *mood*. The exposed shower encouraged foreplay. The bed was comfy. Although we did not take full advantage of the amenities the hotel had to offer, we did check out the restaurant on-site as well as the rooftop pool. Both were fancy and brag-worthy. If I had it my way, we would have stayed at the Andaz the entire time we were visiting San Diego, however we were forced to stay at a different place the majority of the week (work!) I will definitely return to the Andaz the next time I am in San Diego.

“Nice addition to Denver!” My husband and I live in Denver, and had the opportunity for 24 hours on our own while family members watched our kids, so we decided to try out the Ritz. Generally speaking, we try to stay at Four Seasons when looking for a luxury experience, but of course that's not an option in Denver. This Ritz actually surprised us - it's much more Four Seasons-like than the other Ritzes I have been to. Very contemporary and more understated than the typical Ritz. Valet was friendly and prompt, no problems there. Valet was $25 overnight, but it's a Ritz and it's downtown, what do you expect? (As a side note, if you go there to use the spa, valet parking is free.) We were offered bell services but didn't need any assistance since we had one tiny suitcase between the two of us. Front desk staff were very professional and friendly, very easy check-in process. The rooms are huge with unique and beautiful hardwood entry. Beds were comfortable with very nice linens. Flat screen HDTV I think was 32". There was an espresso maker in the room - we didn't use it but what a nice touch! The view was of another building - the location of the hotel isn't great for mountain views and I was told that the only rooms with mountain views are the suites. I see the mountains every day so I didn't care much, but it's too bad that out of town visitors won't get a nice Colorado view. Bathroom was very nice, separate shower and large tub, double sinks and separate water closet. Shaving mirror in the shower was nice for my husband, and water pressure was fine. Frette towels were terrific and the toiletries smelled great. I loved that they had a full sized Ionic hairdryer in the room. I have to admit I am a bit perplexed by the location. The hotel used to be an Embassy Suites so I can see the appeal of renovating an existing building, but I can't say I'd expect to see a Ritz directly across the street from the Greyhound station. While the location is pretty good in terms of being a short walk to many attractions, restaurants, etc., you're still stepping over a lot of homeless people and the bus station and immediate area is a bit sketchy, particularly at night. We ate both dinner and breakfast at Elway's - the only restaurant on site. (Though there are many others close by.) We weren't terribly impressed with the dinner. The food all seemed to be overseasoned and the tuna appetizer we ordered was just OK - lacking in imagination. Our steaks were both overcooked. The manager came over (we didn't really complain, just asked that our steaks be redone) to apologize and comped our entire meal other than drinks. It wasn't awful - I'd give it another try if Denver didn't have so many other choices for a steak dinner - Morton's, Sullivan's and Capital Grille are all superior choices and all reasonably close. We had dessert via room service - a warm brownie with ice cream, and it was delicious. The breakfast, though expensive, was quite good. We both booked appointments at the spa. I have been waiting for a luxury hotel with spa to open in Denver because the day spas, though plentiful and many upscale, don't give the same relaxation, in my opinion. The Ritz spa has a beautiful locker room and two relaxation rooms - one where the therapist comes to get you for the appointment, and the other where you won't be bothered at all. (Different rooms for men and women.) The locker room has several showers with dual shower heads, a steam room, whirlpool, and plenty of space and products to get showered and dressed. Towels and bathrobes were soft and fluffy as you'd expect. Relaxation room had cozy chaise lounge chairs, magazines of course, fruit water, tea, nuts and fruit. I discovered a few minor problems and all were taken care of immediately by the attentive staff. My massage was wonderful, and I'd highly recommend the lime blossom scalp treatment - smells amazing. We did not use the gym, though it is a gym that my husband used to belong to before it was renovated and linked to the Ritz. We did take a walk through it. It's a full-service gym, you won't be waiting in line for anything or find that it's lacking in equipment. Overall, I loved it and would recommend the Ritz Denver to anyone. We were also astonished at the price - $199 a night! The hotel was booked solid when we were there, so I'd be surprised if that price sticks around long. If we have the chance to stay again we definitely will, even if the price does go up.

“Great location, nice hotel” This hotel's location is really the reason you'll want to stay here. It's only a block from the Air and Space Museum, which leads out to the Mall, about midway between the Washington Monument and the Capitol. While both are walkable, you'll definitely want some comfy shoes and some cash for an ice cream break for the kids! The hotel itself is nice enough. It has a pleasant little courtyard with tables for gatherings. The lobby is attractive and usually pretty busy. We had a few meals at the restaurant, choosing the buffet both times, once for breakfast and once for dinner. We were happy with the food both times, but the prices were a little high. The room was okay. We had a double room that overlooked C street-great view of the Department of Education! :) It was a quiet room though, didn't hear any trains or traffic. The bathrooms need some updating. The tile is old and dingy and the wallpaper is coming off the walls. We weren't in the room too often so we weren't too concerned with the lack of size of the room. The roof top pool was fun and did have a nice view of the Capitol, especially at night. The water is very cold though, so if the air is even a little cool, you'll freeze! Overall we would definitely stay here again if visiting the mall area.

“Blah... Basic Budget Hotel” I don't know the official star rating of this hotel but it is a solid 2 and nothing more or less. The staff is super friendly, but the rooms are drab and really put the Hilton name at stake. Homewood suites is definitely the lower end line of Hilton but this proves that and that's not really a good thing.

“Outstanding Value, Excellent Service, Great Location, Comfortable, Quiet” We stayed at the Beacon for 2 nights in August and were very impressed. We used to stay at the Hilton Garden Inn at Times Square, but their prices kept going up and the traffic at Times Square was unbearable. The Beacon was a much better choice. The location is convenient to a many great sites, and theater at Times Square and Lincoln Center are still a very short subway ride away. The Beacon Theater offers some outstanding shows. There are a fantastic array of excellent restaurants within walking distance and prices overall seemed more reasonable than Times Square or the East Side. The hotel staff were wonderful and accommodated a last minute change in our room request. The room, though small, was very comfortable and the kitchenette with a fridge and microwave (as well as cooktop) was a real plus. The only negative was the lack of valet parking. But there were several garages within a block or two of the hotel and parking was far cheaper than in Times Square as well. We parked the car and relied on cabs and subway to get around with no regrets. The best part is that the hotel is walking distance to Zabars. We didn't have to pay again to park at 80th St when we went to stock up before our trip home. We will definitely stay at the Beacon again on return visits to the city.

“Great value and super local!” I stayed at this property back in mid July for a couple nights. This trip to Chicago was a bday present to myself but I was on a super tight budget when it came to hotels. I had seen this hotel back in Feb on a previous trip and decided to check it out. Man am I glad I did cause the rates for the rooms are more then worth it. I will admit that the weekend noise from the club across the street can be much and the rooms are in need of some new furnishings but over all the room was clean bed not too bad and those were the two things that I was looking for. Public transport is only a couple blocks away as is Portillos. Next time I am in Chicago and want to stay downtown I will give the hotel another shot just for the price alone.

“Great hotel if you want to be in Times Square” Went to NY for a few nights to attend a conference on the west side. I was not looking forward to staying in Times Square, but many hotels were full, so my office booked me here. This was a great hotel. I'd call it a 4-star business hotel. Comfortable, amazingly it was quiet in the rooms (and I was not on an upper floor), the curtains kept the bright lights out (my room overlooked the M&M building with the massive LED display sign right in my window) and beds were comfortable. Modern bathrooms with big showers with seat - no tubs. Didn't try the restaurant so no comments about that. Wifi was great - $17/night but included in my rate. CONS: Hot water was a little cooler than my liking. A little noise from the elevator and lobby - the layout has no rooms really too far from an elevator. Really good hotel.

“Sehr gutes Hotel am Fusse von Beverly Hills” Dieses Hotel befindet sich in der Region West Hollywood, also südlich von Beverly Hills und etwa 10 Minten Autofahrt davon entfernt. Es ist eine der besseren Gegenden vom Grossraum Los Angeles, da sich hier in der Umgebung vorwiegend reichere Leute aufhalten. Die Nähe zu Hollywood und den Hills wertet dies natürlich noch auf. Gegenüber vom Hotel befindet sich das "Bevery Center" – eines der grösseren und exklusiveren Einkaufszentren der Stadt. Dort kann man auch immer wieder mal auf Stars aus Film und TV treffen, da diese auch dort einkaufen gehen. Das Sofitel ist ein sehr modernes und luxuriöses Hotel, die Zimmer äuusserst komfortabel und sauber, Personal und Service sehr zuvorkommend – allerdiings einfach auch das, was man für dieses Niveau und den entsprechenden Preis erwarten kann. Das Resaurant und die Bar im Erdgschoss scheinen auch für Leute, welche nicht im Hotel nächtigen, ein beliebter Treffpunkt zu sein. Für mich stimmt hier das Gesamtpaket: super Hotel in relativ zentraler Lage (wenn es dies in L.A. überhaupt gibt), gute Zimmer, nettes Personal. Immer wieder!

“You can do better” This property is connected to the airport. You can walk from the plane to the hotel - and from the hotel to check in - without ever stepping outside. That is the good news. It is across from the shuttle area and train station so you can easily catch the train into the city. That is also good news. After that the good ends. The rooms themselves are fine - a bit small and cramped - but not terrible. The front desk is a mess. They tend to have one person working and a long line always. I was there for 3 days and went by the desk a few times. There is a HHonors line - but nobody was ever working it when I was there. The restaurant is OK - the food is pricey - even for an airport. It isn't bad though. The breakfast is decent. There is no Hilton HHonors lounge - surprising for an airport location. Overall it wasn't bad - but my experience with the desk was enough to leave me with a bad overall impression.

“Simply Fantastic” My family recently went to Chicago to see all the sights and stores. We found Holiday Inn Chicago - Mart Plaza to be a fantastic place to stay. The room and entire hotel area were perfectly clean. The view from our room on the 16th floor was fantastic. My wife and daughter liked that the shampoo and lotion were from Bath and Body Works. As previously noted by other reviews, the hotel was very difficult to locate. The riverfront location limits access, but also limits noise. The hotel is quite as a church. I slept like a log. We are Platinum Members and paid for our room with points. Platinum Members get a goody bag at check in. We got an upgrade to a mini-suite. The extra space was handy. We were in a nice corner room with very comfortable beds. There is free wi-fi. We could see both the Willis Tower and the Hancock Building from our room. The room we had overlooked the river and downtown. The hotel is on top of the Chicago Sun Times building and is connected to the Merchandise Mart by a pedway. The pedway closes at 7 PM. There is a food court and subway stop in the Merchandise Mart. Buses are equally handy. We got 3 day metro passes ($14) and never moved our car after parking ($36 per day). We walked to dinner most nights. Carson’s Steak House is only 5 blocks away. To enter the hotel, you go in the Sun Times building and take one elevator to 15th floor, which is the hotel lobby. You take another set of elevators to go to your room. We enjoyed the fitness center and swimming pool. A sauna is also at the pool. There is a flat screen TV in the room and a coffee maker. Our room had a college size refrigerator. There is a deli type store in the lobby of the Sun Times. But even better is the CVS just down the street which sells groceries and Metro passes. We got terrific information from the concierge and bellmen. When we return to Chicago, we will definitely stay here again. Kudos to GM Tony Miu for running such a fine operation. I hope you found this information to be helpful.

“great convention hotel; probably too big if not part of a meeting” stayed 4 nights in mid november. terrific service; excellent food during small meetings we held all day; staff was courteous and attentive; clean, quiet , well appointed room, facing golf course and pool; solid workout room; had a terrific massge on friday afternoon.

“Stay somewhere else! Hotel Carlton is #16 in popularity, really? Really??” I stayed at the Hotel Carlton for a business trip in January 2007. It was part business, part pleasure, as my boyfriend and I decided to spend our weekend there before my business the following week. Here are some important things to keep in mind if you choose this hotel. I would NOT stay here again. I chose it for the price, but I've stayed at a number of inexpensive places in SF, and this dropped to the bottom of my list quickly. 1. This is not a business hotel. Most of the rooms do not have internet access. You have to use the wireless in the lobby. Many of my mornings were spent walking around the lobby with my laptop searching for a good connection, as I had work to do in the morning. If you don't bring a computer with you, you have to pay to use their lobby computers. Most smaller hotels I've stayed at have had a free lobby computer, so this was a little annoying. 2. Request a "Quiet Room." The first room we stayed in was attached to a second room with a door between the two. We were still on East Coast time and went to bed at around 8pm PST, the first night. We were later awoken by the guests in the next room speaking in lowered voices. We could hear them talking as if they were in the room with us! It was totally ridiculous! However, we were able to switch into a quiet room the next day, with no issues, and no bump in price or anything. 3. There are 2 elevators. When we stayed, only one was functioning. So every time we had to go up to our floor, we generally had to wait a good 5-10 minutes standing in the lobby. If there were one or two people with luggage ahead of us in the elevator line, then we had to wait for the next trip, because the elevators are excruciatingly tiny. 4. The soda machine never had any water in it. Seems silly to be annoyed with this but water in SF is fairly undrinkable, so we had to remember to buy water at the drugstore all the time. 5. Nothing in the city is really walking distance from this location. However, if you choose to stay here, walk to the bus to get anywhere decent in the city. It was a bit scary walking around this area alone at night, though! I will NOT stay here again (it boggles the mind that the hotel is at #16 in the tripadvisor SF popularity index). However, the hotel will always hold a special place in my history as my boyfriend popped the question during this trip San Francisco. Anyway, I'm glad he chose to do the popping on our way to In & Out Burger and not in our hotel room!

“Rough Start but Solid Finish at Magnolia Hotel” My wife and I spent 2 nights at the Magnolia this weekend. Building is beautiful. Lobby nice. Hotel is right in the heart of downtown. Our corner suite was great. Large room. Clean. Elegant. Comfy bed. Contemporary room but very comfortable. Great views. We were on the 20th floor and fell asleep to the reflection of the roof top Pegasus off the building across the street. Valet parking was stellar. Fast, and always fully staffed. Room service cheese plate and chocolate cake were very very good. Unfortunately could not get room service to answer the phone so had to leave the room and go downstairs for help. This was part of a bit of a ridiculously bad first hour at check in. The lobby and hotel (elevators, hallways, public and private spaces) were over run by about 200 preteen girls who apparently thought some boy band were staying at the hotel. There was no security at all to manage the mess. The staff just laughed it off. It was very inappropriate. Second we were given a room number and key cards to a room already occupied. After lugging our stuff up and down again (there was no bellman) we were given a nice room upgrade. But then could not get room service. The rest of the weekend was uneventful. We would stay again. It was just a bad start.

“Not the best in the W chain but adequate.” This property needs a little updating. Iin my room, the pull cords on the shades were broken and the shades were frayed. The decor was "ok" and room was small. However, the view was good and I liked the fact that the hotel had an Acura to take us around. I would probably stay here again but it is not high on my list.

“Surface sheen; issues with basics” I've stayed in this hotel several times over the past 20 years. The current incarnation falls prey to the LA/Hollywood preoccupation with surface appeal, which may explain a couple of issues with basics that I had on a recent stay (more on those below). The positive factors: If you want a nice view of the Hollywood Hills in a quiet, plush, eye-pleasing room, in a hotel in west L.A., and cost is not a major concern, this place is for you. The treatment of guests by the front desk, valet parkers and the hotel restaurant staff is very courteous, and the food in the restaurant is very well prepared. But as seems to be the case with a number of faux-luxury chains that try to wow you with a cool lobby, the Sofitel LA seems to be shorting the basics. When I got to my room on a recent stay, and turned down the sheets of the bed, I noticed a couple of hairs. I smelled the sheets and they didn't smell fresh. The bottom sheet only loosely covered a soft feather-filled mattress pad, which looked discolored, and was covered on its surface with dark feathers. I immediately called the front desk and when the attendant arrived, had him remove the mattress pad and all the sheets, bringing a thin cotton pad and fresh sheets, with which he and I remade the bed. The feather pad should have been withdrawn from service a long time ago -- and the hotel's seeming inattention to what is outside the line of sight also showed up in the bathroom, which hadn't been supplied with any kind of mat for the floor. The latter is a small issue, but issues with bedding and a bathroom are the kind of thing you shouldn't encounter in a $300+ room in west L.A.

“Marriott Gaslamp...great location, lots of walking!” the Marriott is nice and rooms are large, ask for ocean and "Petco" view, on the even side. Front desk good, bellboys great! even give you water when when you go out...concierge is a boy and keeps reffering to you as "his mother", but other than that the staff are very friendly. Bathrooms in the rooms are very spacious, nicely supplied and complimentary loofas..hallway carpets could use replacing. If you want transportation to harbourside, take the orange line by the Convention Centre- Harbourside take the "Hornblower" around the bay tour of catch the Coronado ferry. Conceirege boy will make your res and save you $4.00 pper. Lastly- check out the lounge upstairs rooftop- good views of the bay and Petco and a great outdoor fireplace, Conde Naste says it is one of the "top rooftop bars"...it has a very nice feel about it but ..many single business guys and girls just looking to get lucky but some other casual folks as well just enjoying a nice west coast bar. Overall great location and pretty good, young staff...

“Diamond Didn't Seem To Matter” As with other reviews my stay at the Doubletree Metropolitan in August left me unimpressed. The property is nice inside but right from the get go I was not made to feel particularly valued. My son and I got off the train about 130pm and made our way to the hotel by subway (a stop is convenientlt 1 block from the hotel and I recommend that you get a subway pass and use the subways to get around - they are cheap and quick and easy to navigate). Getting in around 2pm I figured there was a good chance that the room would be ready - nope. So we checked our bags - for a fee. It was only a buck and that is what I would have tipped anyway but it just seemed a bit cheap. There was no upgrade in the room provided. The breakfasts were free but only the cold buffet (warm available for $8 each - again seems a bit cheap). The lack of coffee maker in the room meant I simply when to the adjoining deli each evening on the way up to the room. There was a coolness to the attitude of virutally all the staff that lead me to believe that they are so busy they figure folks will always book there (the location is actually excellent and the rooms are clean and comfortable) so they needn't bother. I did take this us with Hilton Honours and they are attempting to make up for the shortcomings of this experience. So far their response has been very positive.

“Good but not great” The hotel is in an amazing location, easy to walk to some of the best parts of the city. Really comfortable bed and very nice bathroom. Views from the room are wonderful. I had a few issues though: *Getting to and from rooms requires two elevator trips. The lobby of the hotel is on the 7th floor of the building. Other hotels with similar set ups (Mandarin in NY) have elevators all the way to the street level. This hotel doesn't. *Cell phone reception is limited in the rooms. I have Verizon and had 1 bar in my room, my friend had AT&T and she also had one bar in her room. When I stayed at the Elysian (two blocks away), I didn't have this problem. *The CD player alarm went off in the middle of the night I hadn't set the alarm. On checkout, I told the receptionist who didn't seem to care too much. Also, it's 2011, not 1999, why do you have a CD player and not an ipod dock?

“Nice hotel in a very good location” We stayed for 3 nights and found the hotel within walking distance of quite a few sights! It's in a good location. The room was very clean and the staff helpful. The concierge recommended a nice place for dinner that was close to the hotel. They also gave us a $5 off coupon, not much, but it was nice.

“Great stay... made even better by the staff” We surprised our father with a trip to Denver as part of our MLB ballpark tour that we arrange every year... and the Downtown Sheraton did not dissapoint. I contacted the hotel prior to our visit to make them aware of our stay... and we were blown away at their hospitality. We were upgraded to a corner suite with panaramic views of the DT area and the distant mountains with lots of room for our party, bags, etc... there were 2 flatscreens with HD, how much more could dudes on a baseball trip want? The room AC was great, bedding was comfortable, and noise was almost non-existing, and the location has already been discussed... perfectly placed among bars, restaurants, and within easy distance to Coors Field. I can't thank Marc and his staff enough for a job well done... the hats and snacks brought to the room simply made it that much better. The best trip we've taken yet on our annual tour so far, by a long shot. Cab to the hotel is probably your best bet, keeping in mind with tip it'll run apporx $65, about a 35 minute trip.

“Nice hotel, good location.” I stayed here recently and was impressed by the lobby/common areas. Very modern. The room was your typical Hilton room with a comfy bed and modern bathroom, nice amenities, etc. The only two things I would point out are 1-the bathroom ceiling needs to be wiped down. When it gets damp from showering there are spots, hair, etc. 2-the housekeeping staff needs to take an attachment and vacuum the edges of the floor by the bed. You could see they stopped where the vacuum hit the ridge on the bed and there is still about three inches left--you can see the dust, etc. These are minor details but important. The breakfast was standard--I thought they'd have more pastries, etc but they didn't. I would stay here again. All in all it's a decent Hilton property. The ppl were are super nice!!

“Nice hotel, rooms are "cozy"” Good midtown location. A little pricey at an average of $270USD per night. Rooms were a little tight - okay for a single traveller but a bit much for 2. No restaurant onsite. Complimentary internet access. Bathroom was decent size. Other than a bit small, room was clean and neat.

“not up to marriott standards” Many of staff suprisingly rude! As a platinum Marriott member, I have stayed at many Marriotts. This one is definitely below standards for staff hospitality, room sizes smaller, fees higher, wallpaper is peeling in bathroom, service is rude even in concierges lounge. Location is good as it is over the riverwalk.

“Not bad, not great” I've never stayed in a Holiday Inn before, and I think this is probably a cut above the average Holiday Inn. The rooms are clean, though outdated. A good 25% of the channels didn't work on our TV. The internet is free, but it's wired-only (the front desk has ethernet cables if you forget yours). It is far from Georgetown proper and the Metro, but the 30-line buses roll up and down Wisconsin Ave often so it's not that bad. It's also nice being a 3 minute walk from a CVS and a Whole Foods Market. When I checked in late at night they gave me a small room with just one queen sized bed. It had a great view, but I needed a double as my assistant was going to be joining me in a few days. When I went down to change rooms the next day, the clerk mentioned that that's their "Priceline" room and she would have to get approval from her manager to give me a better room. The manager gave me a better room without hesitation, but that's a first for me--I've never had a front desk clerk explicitly state that I was given a smaller/inferior room because I got my room thru priceline. I saw the same agent several times during my stay and she was always helpful, so I think this must be a hotel policy.

“A restorative visit” They invested a ton of money a few years ago on a high-end renovation/restoration of this beautiful Victorian mansion located in the Banker's Hill area of San Diego, just off of Balboa Park and within a short walk of several good restaurants (one is literally across the street, on the top floor of a 12 story building). We spent two nights in the Library Room, on the first floor, with no other rooms sharing a wall making it very quiet. The room had a 10 foot ceiling, like the rest of the first floor, and a huge bay window looking west that flooded the room with light. A wardrobe furniture piece was used for a closet, certainly adequate for a short stay. The TV was a small LCD unit connected to the usual litany of cable channels. There was a DVD player if you want to bring your favorite movies. Two upholstered chairs and a round table were in the bay window area. Window coverings, bed covers and decorative pillows were all very tasteful and top quality. An individual room thermostat for the quiet, forced-air heating/cooling system allowed us to keep the room delightfully cool while we slept in the very comfortable bed. The bathroom was large and had a very large, etched glass window bringing in lots of light. The claw foot tub was charming but negotiating the wrap-around shower curtain for taking a shower was a minor challenge. The towel warmer was a thoughtful touch and the terry robes were high quality, as were the towels and bed linens. The late afternoon wine and cheese offering was nicely done. Morning breakfast, served from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. every morning, was excellent. Orange juice and very good coffee were available in advance of a freshly baked pastry (muffin one day, scone the next) that was artfully served with fresh berries and creme fraiche. Three additional items were offered for choice: an omelet (or scramble); eggs any style with chicken sausage; and home-made granola with yogurt and fruit. The dining room was beautifully set with Wedgewood china and quality linens. Tables were also available outside on the porch or in the garden. Parking is available in their driveway for three cars in a row (which can be somewhat inconvenient) or in a small lot diagonally across the street for no extra charge. For a pleasant few days of vacation in the San Diego area, the Britt Scripps Inn would certainly be an excellent choice of a place to stay.

“Großes Hotel mitten in der Stadt, aber nicht 1A” Das Marriot Marquis, ist wahrscheinlich mit Abstand eines der größten Hotels in der Stadtmitte von San Francisco. Jedoch kommt die Größe mit allen Vor- und Nachteilen die man sich denken kann. Ich beschränke mich hier nur auf die Sachen die mich persönlich beeindruckt oder gestört haben. Gut finde ich natürlich die Lage, sowie die professionelle Organisation für aller Art von Events die man als Firma durchführen kann. Das Marriott Management ist hier sehr professionell und erfahren. Schlecht finde ich die Zimmer, die Einrichtung erscheint lieblos zusammen gestellt. Hier nur zwei Beispiele: Der Schrank im Zimmer hat keine Regale, wo will ich dann Sachen ablegen die nicht auf den Hänger kommen? Oder, wenn ich am Schreibtisch sitze und mit dem (in die Jahre gekommen) Bürostuhl selbst bei über 1.80 Meter Körpergröße gerade mal mit der Brust an der Tischkante anstoße macht das Arbeiten am Laptop einfach keinen Spaß macht. Das Personal ist freundlich, zuvorkommend und schnell. Der Preis ist natürlich auf Grund der Lokation eher weiter oben in der Skala angesiedelt.

“Divine Hotel” Divine Hotel at the Stockyards Fort Worth. Beautiful interior, lovely rooms, big enough for three of us. Staff were wonderful, couldn't do enough for us. Breakfast was included and was delicious. Hope to return in the near future.
“Great experience” Newish hotel. Nice SpringHill suites with new furniture. Good breakfast. Simple place and a great value.

“Great New York” L'hotel posto in una posizione ideale per visitare N.y, a 100mt da Times Square e 10 min a piedi per Central Park, la 5th Avenue, ha una vista da mozzafiato tra grattacieli e le luci newyorchesi, le camere sono abbastanza spaziose e il bagno grande e nuovissimo. Se si ama la confusione new yorkese lo consiglio vivamente così come una capatina da Shake Shake per un ottimo hamburger ...

“Pretty guy with ugly teeth . . .” The structure the Courtyard is located in is magnificent. It was the City Hall Annex. So, imagine a majestic structure constructed n 1926 restored to its former glory. There is no question this hotel is gorgeous, it is absolutely centrally located to everything fun ther is in Philly and it is very reasonably priced. Hence, the "pretty guy . . ." metaphor. But, this place has problems. Before launching on the negative, let's stick to the good: the rooms are new and nicely decorated. The lobby is pretty and there is a very tidy little gym and pool area with everything an exercise fanatic might like to see: three ellipticals, 5 treadmills, free weights, weight machines and even some weighted medicine balls. The problems: I am really concerned about security. The back door near the Johnson library leads directly to the elevator. Although the elevator requires a key to access each floor the door into that side of the building is unstaffed and desolate. The only staff I saw was at the front desk, otherwise the buiilding had that unmanned feel. For example, trash sat near the soda vending machine on the 11th floor for a full 24 hours. The gym was not properly cleaned up: towels and empty bottles were about. The room itself was somewhat petite, but even worse, really stuffy. It was either freezing in the room or airless. The bathroom did not have an exhaust which made things worse. Now the towels: rough and thin. The pillows: hands down the worst pillows I have ever encountered. Sleeping on a folding towel would have had more loft. The bed was comfortable, however, and it was certainly clean. There was not much natural light in the room because the black out shade was too wide for the opening and it obstructed half the window. One thing which was really puzzling was why the door beween the bathroom and vanity area swings inwards. The way it is now is not only stupid but dangerous. On the one side is the toilet; on the other the hairdryer. So, if someone has finished showering and wants to walk into the vanity area there is a good chance someone drying their hair is going to get whacked on the head. Now, the breakfast buffet: $16.95. I mean, really, this is just a Courtyard in Philly- way over priced. Had it been priced at $10.95 the place would have been packed. Do away with the omelette guy or charge an additional fee for an omelette. Would I recommend this place? Oddly, yes. It's just that this place can be so much better than it is.

“Stay here if you get a good rate” I am surprised at the number of glowing reviews of this property. I stayed for 1 night last weekend and found the hotel to be of average quality. Nothing was awful but nothing was really great. We had a corner room on the 10th floor. Check in was good - took only a minute or so. The elevator carpets were dirty and the public areas were not decorated in any special way. Our room had great light and good views. The bed was comfortable but a little soft. Sofitel's bed is touted but i don't really care for the duvet only. The management puts out a note saying they are changed daily. The bathroom had a seperate shower tub combo but there were uneven paint marks on the ceiling and a little wear on the trim. You could see some mildew in the shower. The velvet curtains felt a little dusty as did the carpet. We had room service. It arrived promptly but the quality of the food was average. I am not sure how this hotel scores above the Four Seasons in Georgetown. If you want true luxury stay there (in a renovated room).I will stay at the Sofitel again but only if i get a sub $180 a night rate.

“It makes you appreciate staying home” If you are lucky, you'll be assigned to a room in the Wardman Tower. There (after a hike from the reception desk), at least you'll find some threadbare old world elegance. The rooms are large with high ceilings and many have great views and balconies. The suites are from another era (an era when it was the Sheraton Park Hotel with large beautiful grounds, which regrettably have been replaced by sprawling Marriott convention cookie ickiness). In fact, all the rooms in the Wardman Tower evoke that old era, because they have not had updated furnishings or wall paper since JFK was in the White House. Nonetheless, this IS THE GOOD PART of this enormous and otherwise enormously bland hotel. While you stand waiting an excruciatingly long time waiting for one of the two elevators that service the Wardman Tower, you are at least surrounded by some old DC (frayed) elegance. The rest of the hotel unfortunately is eerily familiar - it is the same bad Marriott convention hotel experience you have had in so many other cities, with rooms so bland you cannot remember them. While it would seem that Marriott could get top dollar for the rooms in the old Sheraton Park (now Wardman Tower) with a bit of paint, new wall paper and better linens, they plan to tear it down. It seems to me they plan to tear down the wrong part of this hotel. This was my fourth convention at this hotel in the past eight years, so my expectations were accordingly low. The service is mixed at best and often just bad, the convention room rate might be attractive, but you will overpay for everything (particularly any onsite business services), your food options are not good, and by the end of a five day convention you will be very, very happy that you are leaving (no matter how much you like DC, and, especially, if you like good hotels).

“Very nice, but a few warnings” We liked the Westin Riverwalk very much. I just want to add a few things that might help people who are planning to stay there. First, we had a room overlooking the river, which was very nice. However, we were on the 15th floor, so our view of the river came with a dose of vertigo. If it's important to you to enjoy the river from your balcony, then you should request a room on a lower floor, and also ask them if you'll be directly over the river or over the pool. Also, we tried to leave our French doors open all night for the fresh air, but we kept being awakened by train whistles and were forced to keep our doors closed. When we asked about it at the front desk, the woman looked at us as if we were nuts and said, "There are no trains around here." We decided that we must have heard the trains because we were on the top floor, with no taller buildings around to absorb the sound. (Honestly, we are not nuts--there were train whistles!) Second, the hotel is very large, so our walk from the elevator to our room was pretty long, taking us down several hallways. We didn't mind at all, but if you are disabled or simply don't want to walk that far, you should ask for a room that is closer to the elevators. Finally, if you want good information from the concierge, we found the night-shift concierge much more helpful and knowledgeable than the man on the day shift. The Westin is a lovely place with good service. I think you'll enjoy it.

“Wish You Were Cool? - the Alexis Can Help” My Seattle contacts tell me that the Alexis, with its artful decorations and “with-it” staff, is the place to stay in the city for the young, well-off and hip. Possessing none of these qualities most of the frou-frou charm of what seemed to be a hotel that was working too hard to be cool was lost on me. I will concede that I may have caught Alexis on a bad night – one of the elevators was being redone and the health club was closed. Further, I was “upgraded” to its version of the honeymoon suite which was awkward given that I was traveling on business by myself. More oddly, the suite was laid out in such a way that about a 20 foot hallway was formed leading to the actual room once you cleared the doorway. In the middle of this hallway was leading to a dark staircase – I never ventured down it so no idea where it lead.

“Great for sporting events” After a last minute decision to see the Tigers try to clinch a divsion title (they failed, in case your not a baseball fan), I tried to find a hotel in a safe area of Detroit. I was able to book cheapee tickets (Southwest and Airtran were offering $49/night each way), find baseball tickets online, and just needed the hotel. I knew NOTHING about Detroit, but had some rewards points to use at Hilton, so I searched their site. The site promised the hotel was in a safe area near the stadium. I ooked a room with 2 double beds online. When I called the day before to make sure i could get a roll-away bed (Kids are boy and girl, all 3 of us needed our own beds), I was told the room was too small for it. Since I am a diamond level member of Hilton Honors, i asked for an upgrade to a suite. I was told there were none avail. and the suites at this hotel only had a king bed anyway. However, they did offer me a handicap room which was suppose to be big enough for the cot. We flew in and cabbed into the city ($50 with tax, btw) and pulled up to the hotel. From the outside I thought I would not be thrilled, but it was just one night. However, the inside was very nice. You walk into a small lobby that has a dual sided gas fireplace. You pass their restaurant and the desk is in front of you. As promised we did get the handicap room. It was VERY large - much nicer than expected. We could have put 3 cots in the room with no problem. The only thing that made this a handicap room was bars around the shower and a detachable showerhead. No low walls, no stall. Very nice. I would recommend this location. Actually, most of the ''renewed' area of the city was fine. There is a monorail (they call it a people mover) steps from the hotel, but in reality you don't need it. We walked around both of the stadiums (the lions play across the street), down to greektown (really just one block long, but we found a terrific restaurant at the end of the block - and do NOT miss the pastry shoppe - did I mention our room had a fridge in it), down to the ren. center, and a bit more of the town. Warning - even thought the cab was expensive, I don;t recommend renting a car. Their isn't alot of parking in the area, and the hotel parking was $20 overnight. I would recommend this hotel.

“Huge place with lots to do” Stayed here for business. Rooms were comfortableand staff was very helpful. Not a lot fo choices for food, but there are a lot od restaurants near by. This is a good place to use as a "home base" when visiting Dallas.

“just ok” just a satisfactory hotel, rooms old, not plesantly decorated. A long walk from anywhere including restaurants. Staff very courteous. I have stayed in a lot nicer for the same money. Very clean.

“Great airport hotel that doesn't feel like it's at the airport!” We stayed here for one night after arriving from the UK before hiring a car and driving down to Rhode Island. The hotel was very easy to get to from Terminal E (the international terminal) via a foot bridge. We had paid for a harbour view and we saw some water, but more airport. To be honest, I think there are only 2 rooms per floor that have a full harbour view but our view was nice enough none the less! (plus I don't recall any airport noise waking me up, even though it was very close) And it was good to be able to use my mum's age to get a senior rate for our room!! In the evening we got the Water Taxi over to Boston (in a thunderstorm!!) The hotel shuttle dropped us off at the dock and then on the way back we got the airport shuttle bus. In the morning the hotel shuttle took us to Avis to collect our car. Very convenient! (this will be even more convenient when the central Car Rental place opens next year and all the car rentals are in the same place) And there was a nice coffee shop in the hotel reception where we had breakfast before we left in the morning, free wifi in reception as well. All in all, a great first stop in Boston!

“Will stay here again” My wife and I stayed at the Excelsior for three days in late April. I chose the hotel because of its location. It’s across the street from the Natural History Museum. The Metropolitan Museum of Art is a very pleasant 10 minute walk across Central Park. Lincoln Center is a 20 minute walk. There’s a subway stop at the corner which we used to get to Times Square and lower Manhattan. We had a “Park View” room that had a great view of the park across the street and the Natural History Museum just beyond. The room was tiny but it and the bathroom were spotless. I thought the room was a very good value. This is a residential neighborhood. There are plenty of nearby restaurants in a variety of price ranges. There’s a Starbucks just around the corner. The Excelsior is a low-service hotel, best if you know what you’re doing and where you’re going in New York. The “concierge” is the guy behind the news stand counter who was stumped when I asked if there was a store around where I could by a belly-pack. The staff is there when you want them and not underfoot when you don’t. Some minor complaints: The clerk at check-in was curt to the point of grumpiness. No smile, “please” or “thank you.” The TV channel line-up is missing Fox News, but this is the Upper West Side; maybe it’s illegal!

“A Greatly Appreciated Oasis after a long week of work” After working all week in Northern AZ I drove to Phoenix to spend the night before flying out the next day. I was exhausted and really wanted some quiet time and a good nights sleep. I got that at this hotel. There was a mistake on my booking but the front desk staff took care of it right away. My room was clean, cool and quiet. Starving, I was happy to find a Waffle House on the property so a quick meal and a a nice evening and night in the room.

“Granite and glass monolyth” I had a 3 night mid-week stay. The bathroom was nice sized, but a few of the white towels had yellow stains. I wonder if they were yellowed from too much chlorine bleach something else? The bath in the first room wreaked like someone had dropped a bottle of cheap cologne. I had to leave. The next room was large with a good view of Dallas from the 28th floor. The AC worked great. (August in Dallas is blast furnace hot, and this year Amazon river basin humidity too) So the cool quiet AC was a blessing. I can't stand to watch the TV in these hotel rooms anymore with 5.1 HD at home. Antiquated grandmother's house best describes the decor in this sleek granite and glass monolith. So the inside does not match the exterior. Speaking of housekeeping : 1 day turn-down service, 2 days no turn-down service. 1 day newspaper, 2 days no paper. 2 days coffee for the coffee maker, one day no coffee, 2 days no cream. One day mouthwash, 2 days no mouthwash. Consistency would be nice. I wonder if I need to learn Spanish to tell them. Room service was slow. Seems like too many workers just standing around. I'm not sure that gets you 4 star quality. Maintenance man with a quizzical look was surfing the elevators one day. He said everything was OK. Super-sized security guards waddled the halls each evening, not sure what they could secure beyond another BigMac. It was strange to climb a couple of flights of stairs to get to the roof-top pool 32 floors up. I guess it keeps the fatties out . Scrambled eggs made with what tasted like old cooking oil and tasted terrible. Some of the staff had trouble with English. Who is doing the cooking? Yikes. All the many 3 and 4 star hotels I've been to in the Market Center area need a face-lift. The Westin downtown had a flat panel TV and updated interior and the Ren at MKT CTR is not as nice as the 3 star Hilton Anatole across the freeway either.

“Horribly Overpriced” This is a prime location next to Times Square, but the hotel is nothing special. The rooms and beds are small. I got a twin bed which was shorter than I am. The view from the window was a brick wall. There was no time of day in which sunshine reaches the 3rd floor room I was in. The hotel tries to imitate the W with the same music and style points in the lobby and other areas, but I've stayed at the W Times Square and the Hotel Mela is not in the same league.

“Very nice staff and property” I stayed here for three nights and was not disappointed. The rooms were nice, well appointed and all of the things I expect at a Hilton Garden Inn. There are many restaurants nearby and they offer a very good breakfast.

“Nice Hotel Good Value” Across from Sea Tac Airport. Very big, spread out hotel with very reasonable rates and nice rooms, although some are a bit of a convoluted walk from reception. Lots of air crews use this hotel which has a frequent free shuttle to airport. We stay here and go to Seattle for Mariners games. The shuttle will drop you at the airport train station if you are going to Seattle, but on your way back you must walk from the station to the shuttle bus pick up area at the airport(about a 5 to 10 minute walk). Parking and some extras relatively expensive. We have stayed here a few times and keep coming back because it is good value for money.

“Great place to stay near Market Center & Hospitals” Had a few rooms here this week for me and my employees. Nice clean room, good bedding, nice pool, front desk very helpful. I would stay here for sure in the future.

“Great value” The Churchill is nothing fancy but it's clean and in a fantastic location. If you get it on hotwire or price line for under a hundred bucks you'll be happy, it's not nice enough for retail price around 200 though unless something's in town and there's nothing else.

“Love this hotel! Wish someone would open a restaurant next door!” I couldn't have been more pleased with this hotel; it's a terrific value, especially if you will be spending most of your time at Upper West Side or Upper East Side locations (it's very convenient if you are visiting Columbia University). The rooms are a tad small but very well designed and comfortable; the desk clerk gave us a choice of street view or non-street view when we checked in, and we chose street view on a high floor. It was great to watch the street life in Harlem through our wall of windows (but you might want to ask for a room without a view if noise bothers you). The free wi-fi is also a great feature, as are the high-def TVs with a full menu of satellite channels. And the hotel's lobby is very cozy and homey as well--a great place to have coffee and visit with friends in the morning, or lounge in the bar at night. The worst thing about the hotel is the immediate neighborhood. It wasn't that I felt unsafe (in fact, the incredible overabundance of policemen along 125th St. is actually kind of creepy--felt like I was in a police state!) but rather, there are just very few goods and services available in the surrounding couple of blocks. The hotel's breakfast cafe is reasonably priced and convenient, and there are several good delicatessens nearby for takeout, but if you want a sit-down meal, Chuck E. Cheese's is the only establishment in sight of the hotel's front door. The closest restaurant we found that I would recommend is Harlem BBQ a couple of blocks away on Frederick Douglass Blvd.; otherwise you are going to be walking 5-10 minutes down police-officer row to get to Sylvia's or Red Rooster. It would be great if the hotel would provide some kind of local map or guide in each room, as it can be hard to know which way to walk when mealtime sneaks up on you, or even if you just need to find a drugstore. For travelers looking for a great hotel value in NYC who don't mind spending a few extra minutes on trains or in cabs, Aloft is a great choice. As every other review has mentioned, the staff here is fantastic and go out of their way to help guests.

“Meh.” My husband and I stayed here for three nighs over the Thanksgiving holiday. I booked the room on priceline for $120, which is not a particularly great deal, as the going rate at the time was $139. But whatever. $60 saved. When we arrived, I was surprised at how nice the lobby area was. I've never stayed in an Omni before, so I wasn't quite sure what to expect. I was, however, rather disappointed that when we arrived, there was no bellman to take our luggage from our car inside. When we arrived, it was very windy and cold and no one appeared to be interested in coming outside in the weather to help. A bellman did bring up our luggage and fill our ice bucket. The room was quite nice and rather large. Our room had a sitting area with a full size couch, coffee table and chair. The bed was very comfortable. The room also had a separate sink with vanity that was outside of the shower/toilet area, which was helpful so that I could get ready while my husband showered without dealing with the humidity. However, the shower was absolutely AWFUL. Tiny, tiny, tiny, dirty shower curtain. The curtain rings were rusty. On the wall in stick on letters it said "Please make sure curtain is inside tub during shower," which was helpful because otherwise, the entire bathroom would be full of water. You honestly couldn't shower without having to touch the shower walls with your body as you moved around, which is not a pleasant idea in a hotel bathroom. I am pretty skinny and I felt totally cramped. I can only imagine how unpleasant it must have been for my 6'3" husband. Honestly, the rest of the room's niceness seemed like an apology for the shower. It was that bad. And the towels were threadbare. There was also a lot of noise coming from the halls. There were drunk people making tons of noise. I called the front desk and they immediately attended to the problem, but still..... We came back to the hotel after being out for the day and the cleaning people hadn't cleaned our room, which is pretty ridiculous. We had to call someone at 11:00 to bring fresh towels because i had left ours on the floor so we could get new ones. The workout area is very nice- big screen tv, new treadmills, large weight selection. Also has an indoor heated pool, though the area appeared to be quite dirty. We ordered room service and it was cold and kind of gross. Overall, a decent experience, but I would not stay here again for the shower/bathroom alone.

“only for big spenders” I only stay at Westin properties when I'm attending conferences. The hotel is old but renovated very well. The rooms were great with all of the modern ammenities and the bathroom was better than the one in my house. There's not much around the hotel but there are several night time destinations within 1 mile. Charging for internet service and the outrageous nightly rate is a waste of money. If you have money to waste and want to be pampered, this hotel will do. I value my hard earned money to much for thsi place.

“Good hotel in downtown Detroit” The Marriott is a large hotel in an office complex in downtown Detroit. It is a fairly large complex and driving to the Renaissance Center, I had to make several turns to find the hotel's entrance. Valet parking was efficient, no wait. Took a quick elevator to the lobby. Several employees working on check-in so no wait. Got a room on the 27th floor. Walk to elevator is short and there are several elevator banks. The hotel is circular so had to walk in a semi-circle to get to my room. Decent sized room with king bed. Work desk with lots of outlets and sufficient lighting.
