Had a view of the office building next to us and a partial view of Canada. Room was quiet and bed was comfortable. No slamming doors which was a problem for me a few years ago when I stayed here last. Tried to grab a bite at the hotel restaurant but it was strangely empty so went into the Ren Center as there are several choices there. Ended up at the Italian restaurant, Andiamo, which was good. In the morning, headed downstairs to the Starbucks kiosk in the Center to get my coffee and muffin fix. Bill was under the door. All charges were correct and check-out was quick. Stayed here for a business event so group rate was good. Overall if you need to be downtown, this was a good choice.

“Gorgeous hotel!” It doesn't look like much from the outside, and the street is a bit of a dump, but once you enter the hotel, you are greeted by a huge and beautiful lobby with a very trendy and modern feel to it. The service is great and felt very professional. My room was also very nice. Great décor and it felt very 'fresh' and new. Indeed, the hotel hasn't been around for that long, so everything still has that new car feel to it. The bathroom in particular was gorgeous and spacious. While I could see the Space Needle from my room, there wasn't much of a view outside of that. You have a huge parking structure right across the street. The hotel is located close to the Seattle Center which is pretty convenient. There's also a large 24hr supermarket and 7-11 close by, as well as several restaurants and a few shops. The room had a huge bed and large LCD TV with many channels, including HBO. The Wi-Fi was also fairly good. Nothing to complain about! The Maxwell is a great, modern, hotel in Seattle and feels very luxurious for the rate.

“excellent hotel in a so-so location” This bustling Midtown East hotel is clean and modern, with sleek decor and comfortable furniture. If you have business in the specific area, this hotel would be a great choice. But tourists should understand that, although the hotel is near some great shopping, there is not much else to do in this largely commercial area, particularly at night.

“nice neighborhood, but rooms very small, not worth the price” We first arrived before our room was ready, but we checked our bags, and they told us what room we'd be in, before we headed out to explore the neighborhood. We returned, and they put us in our room (not the same number as they had mentioned at check in), and I was NOT impressed. Really, no room for anything but the bed, with a gorgeous view of...the brick parking garage next door. Needless to say, I was very disappointed given the price that we were paying, and I called down to the front desk to ask what had happened to our original room. We didn't get a full answer, but we did get moved to a room with a view of New York. Not much larger, but at least a view. The lobby is chic and the neighborhood is young and fresh, but I think I'll stay elsewhere when I'm in New York next time.

“Perfect stay” Clean, comfy and accomodating...Although I hate times square (because its so busy and touristy) This hotel has a great location! The bar is lots of fun, rooms and staff are great and way better than the Mariott Marquee down the street.

“Super Small Room With Horrible Customer Service” We checked into this hotel after booking it on Hotwire. Check In was slow and the clerk was not friendly at all. No welcome or thank you. The room was super small the the bathroom is so small you can hardly turn around in it. A view of a fire escape is what we had. The next morning housekeeping knocked on the door at 8:15am and asked if we were ready to leave. Now mind you check out is at noon. At 9:42am they came back and knocked again. And at 10:10am they came back for a third time. Check out took 42 minutes as they only had one clerk working. No thank you and they did not ask how our stay was. A group of hispanic maids were picketing in front of the hotel upon departure. I will never stay here again.

“Hated It” I asked for a queen bed, received a twin. The room size was INCREDIBLY small and suffocating. I had two windows smashed up against brick walls. I kind of knew all this going in but I didn't think it'd be this depressing! I stayed here for two days. During this time I did not shower because there wasn't any hot water up on floor 6, or at least none in my room. The sink also became clogged if you ran the water more than a dribble. The place was clean but felt dirty. The tv was the size of a pebble. Bottom line, for close to 300.00, this place sucked and I will never be back. Hopefully I will not have to do business in the Times Square area ever again.

“We liked this hotel” I stayed at this hotel with my wife back in May 2000. We really enjoyed this hotel. Check in went smoothly and the staff was warm and welcoming, I sure hope all the staff are still working at this hotel. They have changed name from Vance Hotel to Hotel Max. Our room was fantastic with nice view of downtown Seattle and we could see the monorail passing by. We had a corner room. When you are staying at Stewart street, you can walk to almost everything in downtown Seattle. We really recommend Pike Place Market in Seattle with all the fresh seafood. Just a 10 -15 minute walk from the hotel. We are looking forward at staying at this hotel once again on our next visit to Seattle.

“Average hotel very convenient to UPenn and Drexel” Has convenience to Universities as main advantage. 1.5 miles to downtown, but is walkable down Chestnut of Walnut. Bed very comfortable, room clean and pleasant views on high floors. BUT: 1. Stay away from elevator - bell excessively loud (particularly for those in elevator) 2. Restaurant pretty awful except for breakfast, which is passable except for the coffee (awful with no option for cappucino or expresso). Chain chinese, with inattentive staff. 3. Conference facilities antiquated, noisy whistle in air-conditioning, old low resolution projectors. Daisy-chain many extension cords - unsafe practice, which failed mid-way through one talk. Lunch food comes from Chinese restaurant - not the quality one would expect from a Sheraton. 4. Internet is free, but is slow-slow in rooms (much better in restaurant and conference area). Hassle to get code; must log into computer in room, and get from there

“Excellent base for San Francisco” My husband and I stayed here for three nights as part of as a wider trip around California in March/April. We paid an average of $75 plus tax per night for a standard double room. For San Francisco we felt this was excellent value. The room although not large or particularly stylish was of an adequate size, and clean and comfortable. The bathroom was a good size and included a tub as well as a shower (ie the shower was in the tub). The location was excellent – just a few steps from China Town. It was really easy to get around and we felt safe in the area. After reading other comments on this site, we specifically requested a room away from the lift shaft and didn’t have any problems with noise. Wi-fi is available but there is a daily charge for this so we found it better value to go to a local cafe with free wi-fi instead. No breakfast was provided but coffee was available in the lobby throughout the day. There are lots of cafes etc nearby so finding somewhere for breakfast wasn’t a problem. I’d definitely recommend this as a clean, comfortable and good value base for exploring San Francisco.

“Favourite Boutique Hotel in the Loop” Following a mix up on my booking at another Loop hotel, I ended up here - it was no hardship in the end ! Fascinating history - one of the first skyscrapers in the US - the building Burnham built before the Flat Iron in NYC. Beautifully and sensitively restored - the stairway is a particular gem. The rooms are lovely and well equipped (including a goldfish in a bowl !) and bathrooms are excellent. The lounge areas are very comfortable for the nightly free drinks hour. I'd also recommend the Atwood Cafe - excellent restaurant in its own right. Noise from the new shopping mall/CTA station was unobtrusive - when it's complete, the location will be even more convenient. Currently very handy for the Loop business area, State St, Millenium Park and a short walk from Michigan.

“Good Value, free parking” Stayed here 2 nights in late January 2008. No compaints + Price $75 Night for 2 Queen Bed Room with fridge/micro Free parking (don't know if there's enough room if hotel is fully booked) Clean but old TV had so many channels Elevator - No coffee in lobby (room only..I don't use those machines in any hotel) No shampoo 25c for a 1800 call Deposit for TV remote. We didn't think much of the place we were recommended to for breakfast. The second day we drove west along Lombard and had a really good breakfast at Baywatch Restaurant.

“Location + Space, but very Noisy and Old” PROS: the bed was GREAT - even had a pillow menu very large room, especially for NYC great location room had a mini-kitchen! well stocked gym CONS: bathroom was VERY small, shower so small you can't avoid touching the walls older rooms (beds seemed new) WiFi cost $14.95/day NOISY - could hear everything going on on the floor My last "con" here leads me to a story... There was a group of girls staying in the room across the hall from me. But, I thought "how much trouble could a bunch of girls be on a Thursday night?" I went to bed at about 10pm - and was woken up at 10:30 by the noise of catcalls and thumping music. Yes, they had a stripper. On a Thursday night. Now, I do credit the hotel, someone must have called security - because by 10:45 a security guard knocked on their door and escorted out their "guest." The girls quieted down. But, all in all, not a great stay. Would not recommend for business travel. Would be okay for a family, or tourist looking for a hotel with a good location.

“Dirty and Disappointing” We booked under the AmEx Platinum Fine Hotel and Resorts Program and were treated like second rate guests being thrown scraps. We were shown to two different rooms that were dirty. The first was strewn with dirty towels and empty bottles and the second smelled like a stale cigar and old beer. At the second room, the bell boy tried to explain that a wedding party had stayed over the weekend. No excuse for an alleged 5 star hotel. It really calls into question the quality of the housekeeping. The room smelled like a "dive bar" and they didn't notice...IT'S A NON SMOKING HOTEL!!! After being traipsed around the hotel from room to room, you would think they would have given us a fabulous upgrade...WRONG. The staff seems to be under the mistaken belief that treating their guests ungraciously somehow passes as being exclusive. We checked out and went to the Ritz where we were treated like valued guests.

“Parking headache.” Very nice property with comfortable beds, clean rooms, great city views(if on higher floor). The only problem I had was parking related. First I had difficulty finding the proper garage to park in, so I used valet. I was there attending a meeting the next morning. At the meeting I was given a coupon of sorts to use for valet to be taken off of my room charge. But when I checked out, the coupon was refused because it said for "day parking" and I was an overnight guest. And no, the hotel would not deduct the $16 day fee from the $27 charge to my bill. Sigh. No biggie, but I think that a first class hotel should have some leeway for guests in things like this. What was a good stay ended with me in a bad mood as I left the property. If I have a choice, I will stay elsewhere simply to avoid the parking hassle.

“I Love the Carlton” I stay at the Carlton twice a year, every year, on business and I LOVE it. It is my home away from home in New York. The rooms are beautiful and the bathroom is large and gorgeous. The staff can be slightly disinterested, but that's New York for you. Location-wise, it probably isn't the BEST place for tourists, although it is close to a subway stop. If I were in the city for pleasure, though, I'd want to be closer to the park. As a business traveller, it's great. Free WiFi! Also, the bar is nice.

“Luxurious Pampering in Elegant Surroundings” Having stayed at the Plaza ten years ago before its renovations and being disappointed at the small room and dingy hallways, I was eager to change my view of the hotel this time around. The new Plaza did not disappoint. From the airy lobby and the elegant red roses everywhere to the friendly service and the fabulously decorated, spacious room, everything was near perfection. The central location of the hotel could not be beat, and the staff treated us like royalty. I felt quite pampered throughout our eight-day stay. The food at the hotel's various restaurants costed an arm and a leg, and the room rates were certainly on the expensive side. Other than that, what a wonderful experience the Plaza offered.

“Large conference hotel” I'm glad my expectation weren't high because I would have been disappointed. I had to wait about 30 minutes, mid-day, just to check-in. I got a room on the renovated floor and thank goodness as i would hate to see what the unrenovated rooms looked like. Typically, when you open the door, you pass the bathroom and closet. Not here. You open the door right onto the bed! I was very concerned I would be woken up all night so I asked for earplugs which they promptly provided. The beds were very comfortable with fluffy duvets. The bathroom vanity was so small, i had to put my toiletries bag on the floor. There was still a bathtub. Curious as to why they didn't rip out and put a shower in instead? Oh well. Large TV in the room. They had an Irish Pub which I ate at 3 times and each time was very good. The service, however, was dismal at best. The coffee shop had such long lines I only had the patience to wait one morning. Go to Starbucks next door for coffee fix instead. If you're going to Chicago to shop, you may want to pick a location closer to that action. I would not stay here again.

“Wow and only 900m away from the President of the USA.....” This is what I would call an immense surprise! A hotel with a Caracter?! never saw something alike! Red is the color, so if youare a red sox fan (or liverpool or manchester united or bayern munich or hapoel) you think that you are at home cause it is soooooo red. Having emphasized that lets be brief: Big rooms, great beds and linen, great service, great amenities, walking distance to the white house (make sure the president is at home because we missed him, he went on a vacation without our permission) but (nobody is perfect) the breakfast is "so so" (rather poor) and the parking fee (if you come by car) is not the cheapest. If you want to park in the street, get first your degree in nuclear science in order to figure out the parking rules). Great stay, would certainly come back... Mr. President, please next time wait for us...

“Not worth the money” We went to Austin on a busy weekend and none of our favorite hotels were available, so we stayed here as a last resort. It was old and cheap, with stained furniture and carpet. The electric plug was coming out of the wall at the sink, as was the faucet in the shower. I have to stay in a lot of cheaper hotels with my work, because I go to a lot of small towns, and this wasn't the worse hotel I have stayed at, but it is the worse Days Inn I have stayed at. I paid $90 plus tax. Not worth the money at all.

“Great Location & great hotel” I stay in the downtown Columbus area over 30 days per year and always enjoy the Hyatt arena district. It by far is the most consistant of hotels in the area for service, clenlieness and food & drink The rooms have been recently updated with nice ammenities, it is always clean, and the staff are extrememly friendly from valet, restaurant & bar, to front desk. Besides that, for a hotel, the food is extremely good for a hotel. They definatly pay attention to detail when preparing the food from appatizers on up.

“Great property in a great location!” At first I was not sure I was going to like this property at first glance, because of its untraditional building, but I was very wrong. Because of the building, the rooms are huge!!! There was plenty of space for our family of 5. The rooms were clean and appointed as Embassy Suites generally are. It is in a perfect location, in walking distance to all the museums and anything else you would want to do downtown. The managers reception was excellent with friendly staff, but get there early if you want a table. Breakfast was regular Embassy Suites fare served in the restaurant next door. The only thing you may miss at this location is use of a pool and being very busy there can be longer waits for the elevators.

“Good location for downtown work” Room was comfortable. Internet is wired only, a disadvantage for me. Restaurant was marginal and bar expensive and sparse. But the location is great for eating elsewhere. Value stay.
“Perfect value” This hotel is great for overnight stays. Good location, clean and functional as expected in Courtyards.

“Really lovely hotel, but not the best pick for young kids” We stayed at theWit for two nights with two young children (ages 5 & 6). Pros: phenomenal staff -- everyone from the restaurant staff to the bellhops was very friendly and went out of their way to help. Great location -- quick walk to Millennium Park and Michigan Avenue. Very nice rooms, with great views of the park and State Street. Good on-site restaurants. Cons: the hotel had let the folks who were staying in our reserved suite extend their reservation into our time, thus kicking us out of the suite. They did offer us adjoining rooms on our 1st night and a suite upgrade on our 2nd. Very nice accommodations, but they did involve a room change, which was a bit of a hassle. The other con is not at all the hotel's fault, just a statement on who they are. This is a hip spot ideal for couples' getaways, mancations, and girls' getaways -- that definitely seemed like the population that was there at the same time as us. The downside of this, for us, was that our hallway was loud at night. There was a fair amount of traffic throughout our 1st night, and then the folks in the 2 rooms across from us returned from partying at 3:30 a.m. and camped out in the hallway, waking all of us up. I probably wouldn't have minded as much if I were off on a carefree weekend as well, but it was tough to have kids up in the middle of the night. In summary, very nice property with exceptional staff. If you're on an adults-only break, great pick.

“Surprisingly nice hotel!” I booked this hotel through Priceline for a rate of $150 a night. I was very hesitant because it didn't look very nice on the website. I was surprised though. While the hotel is very eclectic and old, it is nice and clean and a very good deal. Our room was a queen room that was surprisingly big. It had a window unit AC that worked well. My only complaint was the claw foot tub in the bathroom - the shower curtain stuck to me on both sides the whole time and it was very unpleasant. The rooms had a nice TV and a wardrobe as well. Other rooms in San Fran for this weekend we went were $400 and up. This hotel is well located (not great but within walking distance of some things) and was clean and the staff was very friendly. I would recommend for budget travelers looking for a nice hotel.

“Hyatt downtown a good choice” good location in the financial district. The area is much safer than it was a few years ago. Nice rooms, great staff. pool but no spa/whirlpool ( that was the only disappointment), and there is a lot of walking in the hotel getting from point A to point B. Parking, expensive 32/day. lose your ticket and it's a TWO day fee MAX.

“overall pretty nice - minor negatives” The Biltmore Hotel was beautiful. Colors were a bit faded compared to the pictures tha you can find about it but to be expected. Room were clean and painted recently. Can be a bit noisy (from the outside) but it is located downtown so expect city noise. Bathroom was a bit cramped although the water pressure was great. TV was not very well situated, off in a corner a bit high so watching a little bit wasn't the most comfortable thing in the world. Elevators were small but plentiful and fast. The fitness center was pretty nice for a hotel once you find it. Parking was valet only at $24/day when I went so don't forget to add that to the cost of the hotel. It looked like valet could get pretty crowded and it did when there was an event at the hotel - a bit of an inconvenience. A few good places to eat within walking distance though so that helped.

“Good location in Fort Worth” Location, Location, Location. If you need to stay downtown Fort Worth, This place is a good location. Most things are walking dist from the hotel. The hotel is like most any Courtyard. It was no different. The room was clean and the staff was nice. I am a fan of Marriott and was not disappointed. For breakfast I suggest the bakery right down stairs. For dinner, head out for a steak. I have done several reviews of the different places I visited during my visit. Try to get a high floor. Have fun. Lots to do in Fort Worth.

“ok if you get a deal” We got a deal by previewing the timeshare. The resort is very spread out. We had just a rm rather than a 1BR. It was very small, handle on drawer broken already. The rm is set up poorly so that the bathrm door opens up to the rm and blocks any passage. The maid svc was spotty. The pool water was even too cold for kids at 76 degrees--heat it! The workout rm is also very small and actually house in 2 rms. It appears to cater to owners or the overflow there on business at the JW.

“Nice stay and a good south Houston Location” I was booked by a client here for a speaking event I had at Ellington Air Force base. It was the first time I ever stayed at a Drury Inn. The check in staff was friendly, the process was easy and quick, just in time for some free drinks and snacks. A nice touch after being on the road, I just made a quick trip to the free happy hour so I'm not sure about the food quality but the rum and coke was pretty darn good, starts at 5:30 not sure when they close it down. They also had free soda (Pepsi products) and pop corn until about 10 or that's a nice touch. I was impressed, working late in my room it was nice to go down for a free refill soda. The hotel does look a bit out of date with fixtures, carpet and wall color but to the credit of this hotel they had a big flat screen TV. The only thing that I noticed that may have been an issue for some was the Tv kept going blank with an error message which read "lost signal". Not too much of an issue for since it was mostly background noise. All the basics are in order, clean towels/sheets and your standard mid range soaps and shampoo's. The pool and hot tube looked nice and was packed out with kids as I passed them on the way to my room. I left too early to check out the free breakfast which is 7-9. I did read the previous review on the earwig bugs in the bathroom area and did an inspection upon getting into my room, Good news no sign of bugs at all, I think the management team responded to this issue. Overall a very Nice Stay! I've stayed at several hotels near by and I'd stay here again for sure.

“Great choice for first Boston Trip” I'm a Hilton Gold VIP and as such have stayed in many Hilton properties. My daughter took a semester off from college and we decided to check out Boston. This hotel was in walking distance from the major stuff, The Common, the Metro (T), waterfront, Fanueil Hall, it was awesome. Had a great room (upgrade because of the Hilton VIP) and everyone was really nice. Comfy beds and friendly staff. What more could you want?

“Good hotel - Good location” I think i have stayed here before (when it was a Raddison) as location and layout very familiar - although did not realise this at time of booking. PC platinum member so had free wifi access and upgraded to a corner suite from a standard King room. The only compliant was the matress seemed to say in the middle so not a great nights sleep - but managed to sleep length ways to avoid the sag. Room very clean - ok as some reviewers say the decor is dated but not "dirty" or unwelcoming. Excellent location - look of shops and attractions within walking distance. Would reccomend for a Chicago trip to anyone - business and leisure.

“Convenient” To be honest, I was expecting more from this brand, but it did the job. The hotel is conveniently located at the airport. I stayed there for an overnight layover and the staff was great in getting me a room at such short notice. The rooms were very old and in need of revamping. There wings were oddly shaped and it was a long walk to reception. Internet kept dropping.

“Unprofessional staff” I checked in just before midnight and was upsold from a fairmont king to a harbour king. Upon checking into my harbour king I realized that it was actually not possible to see the harbour from the room unless i was standing at a particular angle. At this point, I called the front desk and informed them that I was not happy with the room and didn't want to pay for the upsell because I really couldnt see the harbour. I offered to move back to my original deluxe king room. The agent told me to stay because my room had already been given to someone else and further said I would not be charged for the upsell. Ten minutes later, in the shower, I received a phonecall from the manager on duty where he insisted I pay the upsell. I told him no and he moved me to a fairmont king room directly located above the main entrance of building 3. I have to say I did not get any sleep that night because everytime the front entrance door was opened, my entire room would shake. The next day I called the manager on duty and explained what happened and was moved to a nice coast guard room. Third time lucky the room was comfortable. The gentlemen who was the manager on duty was rude and not accommodating. Another point is the valet parking is terrible. $42 a day and on numerous occasions they were unable to find my car in the parking lot after 30 mins. On one occasion I waited up to an hour.

“The Best Hotel in San Francisco” We stayed here for the final 2 days of our honeymoon and were aware that The Huntington had a lot to live up to, as we'd enjoyed some amazing hotel rooms during our honeymoon. There was champagne waiting for us in our room and we had been upgraded to a wonderful room on arrival. Our room was massive. Great bathroom and comfortable bed with some lovely lounge space too. The staff are very helpful and nothing was too much. The decor is so very tasteful and the clientele were friendly. The spa is amazing and they offer a wide range of wonderful treatments. There is a great terrace to eat lunch on and we were able to check out and still use the facilities of the spa to shower before our overnight flight back to the UK. There is a handy business centre with a printer, so we could print off our boarding passes. There is no free Wi-Fi ($10 a day charge) so it was a good facility to have on-site when all you want to do is check in online. We went over to the Fairmont for a quick drink and a look whilst waiting for our room and I have to say - The Huntingdon was heads and shoulders above it in every way. Its distinguished, its classy, its a wonderful place to stay. I can't recommend it enough and although its a steep walk up the hill from Union Sq, its so well worth the effort!!!

“Clean, friendly, convenient” I am travelling several times a year to Round Rock, TX on business and have settled on the south La Quinta. The staff is very friendly and helpful, the rate is reasonable, and the place is kept clean.

“Excellent business hotel” Unfortunately, my two-day stay started late (thanks, United Airlines), at 3:45 am. The staff were quite cheerful for such an hour. Room and bed were excellent. The bed was huge; the room was not. I found surprisingly few moderate-priced restaurants in the area, and much of the neighborhood was nearly empty after business hours.

“Great experience” Went to bro in law's wedding here, had a great time. The hotel did a fantastic job with the wedding, really beautiful. Our room was really nice and quiet, comfortable. They accommodated me with a feather free room. My mother in law was overcharged on her bill for some room service she didn't get, but the staff removed the charges no problem.

“Cosmo Scores Again” This is the fourth or fifth time I've stayed at the Cosmo, and it was once again a pleasure. Immaculately clean as always. Great friendly staff (though not too informed about the free wifi -- and now that they have the wifi, the place is even better than before). Great location. Only caveats: the elevator has gotten slower than ever -- one night it took more than two minutes to get to the sixth floor, and some street noise. Everything I want in a hotel when I go to NY.

“Comfortable and convenient” Stayed here for a convention and the location was ideal. Within easy walking distance to the convention center and the Reading Market. The room was clean, the staff was friendly and the service was excellent. They even had a guard located on each floor where large groups of young students were staying to prevent loud noise and the inevitable student room swapping that usually occurs. We actually didn't need earplugs that night. The bed was comfortable and the breakfast was very good. The air conditioner was very noisy and the place is not located near all the better restaurants but cabs seem to be plentiful in the area. The free internet service worked well and when we had a problem with the toilet it was repaired quickly. This is not a deluxe hotel but it is comfortable and well worth the price.

“Fabulous hotel - close to the action” We found a great bargain here on one of the travel sites, and decided to book it for a night out on the town. This hotel was more than we could ask for - especially for the price. It was close to all the action. In addition, the lobby and bar were modern looking and attractive. The rooms were updated and had flat screens. If we can find this hotel at a similar rate again, we will be back!

“Disappointing facility for weekend in Boston” Checked in Sep 17 early afternoon and left on Sep 19 early morning. After check-in, we dropped our luggage and were out in the City most of the day. Got back to the facility in late evening. Tried to use bathroom and then the real issue encountered. First the bathroom has an enclosed shower; however, the enclosure requires a ceiling height glass door (probably about 5/8” thick) to pull in the ledge to prevent the water from running into the rest of the bathroom floor. The door was too heavy that it must have bent the hinges and the door cannot be closed at all. Thus when you take a shower, it spilled water all over the floor – causing the entire floor to get wet. You literally have layer of water on the floor. You can’t even use the toilet without getting your feet wet. Raised this concern to the front office staff. Literally brought the staff to the room and showed the issue. Their response – sorry about it and we can’t do anything at this hour. Tell us in the morning (Sunday) before we leave the facility and see if we can fix it. On Sep 18 morning, we left the facility a daylong outing in the city and prior to leaving, we reminded their staff to fix the issue. We returned back early evening hours. Upon entering the facility, we asked the front desk if they had fixed the issue. The staff acted with a strange face – as if they are not aware of any issue to be fixed. Total shock. Went to the room and noticed that the issue was not resolved. It was too late to change the room as it was getting late and we had to be out early morning. Other issues observed: mold in shower, the room door lock – makes too much noise that it wakes up the guests. This issue seems to be prevalent to all locks in the facility. The flat screen TV – it would not work. We had to bring their staff to the room to investigate and eventually make it work. The mini refrigerator – it gives an impression that it is working; however, it was not unless you crank up the thermostat inside (we found this out 24 hours later). One would think that the housekeeping staff would check some of these basic stuff. It does not seem to be case. The facility looks pleasant from outside. They do provide a shuttle service to the airport - for $5 per person; we did not use this. We did not use other services such as bar, breakfast services and gyms that it offers. I would have given higher rating – if we did not have encountered the above issues. If you are to stay at this facility, please check out your room and make sure that things are in order before too late. Hopefully the management team will address these items in future.

“Loved the Marcel at Gramercy!” I travel to NYC fairly often (for business and for fun), but this time I wanted to stay a little farther from the overly touristy areas. The neighborhood the Marcel at Gramercy is in is EXACTLY what I was looking for... I loved it. Not too touristy, but of course plenty of great neighborhood restaurants, etc. Closest subway stop (the 6) is just a short walk from the hotel. I absolutely loved my room. I see some other reviewers have complained that the rooms here were small -- yes, it's a little small, but it's an average NYC-size room. I've actually stayed in several much smaller (yet more expensive) hotel rooms. If you're traveling to NYC, you have to skew your idea of ideal room size. And I'm not sure if all rooms/floors in the Marcel are like mine, but I had an awesome high ceiling. I think I was on the 5th floor? Anyway, I loved the design of the room too. It was beautiful and it was CLEAN. No complaints there. I didn't have any communication with the staff beyond checking in, checking out, and checking my bag for a few hours after checkout. Everyone I talked to was very nice, very polite. Again, no complaints. I got a great deal on this room for a January weekend. I'm interested to see what the rates will be during the spring and summer. The Marcel at Gramercy is definitely a new addition to my Go-To NYC hotels list. Can't wait to stay here again!

“Not Bad Overall” We just completed a 4 night stay at this hotel. We wanted to stay in Downtown Denver but most hotels were sold out for the weekend and this hotel was the closest we could find, about 4-5 miles away and 1 mile from the Cherry Creek Mall. It is located on a heavily travelled commercial road across from a strip club. Our room rate for the weekend nights was $114, which was ok, but $186.00 for Sunday and Monday which was not a good value. This is not a new property and appears tired and worn. The public areas like the lobby, restaurant and hallways need freshening. The room we had was small for two persons and the sink was awkwardly situated outside of the bathroom in front of the closet. Negative featuers were the lack of an in-room safe and old fashioned tv. Positive features were a comfortable big leather chair with ottoman and good reading light, comfortable bed, and lightning-quick housekeeping service. Our room rate included a full buffet breakfast each morning that had an omelet station , good variety and fresh fruit, although one morning the grapefruit sections had turned rancid. There was also free underground parking though the parking spaces were for the most part quite narrow. Staff were friendly and helpful.

“Wonderful stay w/ top notch customer service” My sister and I just returned from a 3 night stay w/ her 2 children 11 and 13. The place is great for kids this age . They absolutely loved the pools especially the lazy river. We picked this as our starting point of a 1 week trip which included a trip to Grand Canyon and Las Vegas. Was perfect for kicking back and being pampered. Wonderful breakfast buffet although a bit pricey. Dinner at Roy's on property was top notch all around. Also took advantage of the Cloud Club lounge (extra fee but well worth it) which was staffed by very friendly and accomodating personnel. Stay at alot of Marriotts and have to say I was most impressed by this one. The place just exudes class. Will definitely return when in Phoenix.

“Blah.” That pretty much sums it up. Blah. I stayed here for two nights on a work trip, and while my room was quiet and pretty clean, and I can really say about this property is blah. I was in an unrenovated room, which was a little worn around the edges and tired. It wasn't hideous, it was just blah. The room was rather small and the windows didn't let much light in. The lobby had this weird feel of trying to be trendy on the cheap. I dunno, I feel like only a gut renovation could redeem the place. Maybe I'm too critical, but the little things that are covered at the majority of Hiltons, Marriotts, and Sheratons I stay at are just a notch below here. Cheapo styrofoam coffee cups in the room? Yup. Random bath products each day of the stay? Yup. A closet without closet doors? Yup. This seemed like a good enough Holiday Inn, but not much more. Staff was fine, not insanely outgoing, but not unfriendly. I think this may be a problem with Crowne Plaza in general, that they don't have consistent standards and that these aren't on part with other upper middle chains. Who knows. Anyhow, when I'm back in Dallas, I have no desire to return to the CP.

“An outstanding property with a staff second to none” I had the pleasure of a three night stay at the Park Hyatt in November of 2010. Having read the reviews on TripAdvisor I was a bit concerned as a negative one appeared near the top of the list. I hope my fellow travelers will disregard that review as it is most inaccurate and hardly reflects the true nature of the hotel. Let me begin with the location. How about absolutely perfect? The Park Hyatt is near the corner of 24th and M in Georgetown. A classy and quiet neighborhood with tremendous architecture and retail. Moreover, it is only a few miles from all of the important cultural and historic attractions which make DC such an exciting destination. The check in process is a breeze. Every staff member was professional and eager to please. The lobby area is sterile and designed to get travelers processed quickly and efficiently. The elevators are close by with a lounge and restaurant on the same floor. My room was a gem. A 600 square foot suite with a tastefully designed sitting area complete with a desk and chair for reading. An ethernet connection was provided. The bedroom was close to perfect . The bed and linens were of the highest quality. One nit- no Ipod or dvd player. A glaring omission in an otherwise beautiful room. The bathroom was a treat. A beautiful walk in shower with two heads along with an inviting tub. Nice closet space and all the lotions and potions one would expect. The bathroom alone was worth the price of admission. The gym was fine with four treadmills facing windows with a view to the street. Adequate weights and other aerobic equipment. Not nearly as nice as the gym at the Park Hyatt Chicago but still everything one requires minus a steam and nice locker room. The pool and hot tub were very clean and well maintained. The lounge was very nice. The tables are a mess design wise but the service and food are excellent. The breakfast menu is outstanding. Egg white omletts were cooked to perfection. Tea is served loose and the choices are plentiful. The coffee was quite good as well. Dinner is in a seperate area and was quite good. Local ingredients and an eclectic menu made for a rewarding dining experience. One final word regarding the staff. This hotel is committed to customer service. At the risk of sounding as a hotel snob, I have stayed at many of the five star venues in the states and Europe, and can state unequivocally that this group is as good as it gets. Period.

“Great hotel for first visit to San Diego” The Omni Hotel in San Diego was the perfect place for our first visit to San Diego. I booked the room through the hotel's website and since I am a preferred guest (it's free), I even received a phone call prior to our visit asking if I had any special requests. I did request a high floor, away from the train tracks, since I had read about the noise in previous Trip Advisor reviews. That request was granted. When we arrived at 3 p.m., our room was ready and check-in was efficient. We received a welcome card from the manager and a certificate for breakfast in the hotel's restaurant, McCormick and Schmick's. After we returned from dinner at Seaport Village (a beautiful 20 min. walk from hotel), turn-down service was complete, with mints, a rose and the next day's weather forecast. Our room (2033) had a great view of Petco Stadium and that evening, the Padres were playing the Dodgers, so it was exciting to see some of the game. With the window cracked, we could hear quite well and feel as if we were in the grandstands. The window that looked down at the stadium even had a window seat. The room was spacious and the bed was heavenly. Amenities were nice, even supplying coffee "to go" (paper) mugs and a nicely appointed honors bar. Bathroom amenities included shampoo, conditioner, lotion, mouthwash, a sewing kit, and of couse, soap. We did eat breakfast at the hotel since we had the certificate, but it was pricey. We each ordered a cup of coffee at $4+ a cup. My waffle was around $11 and my husband's french toast was about the same. It was good (came with cute, individual bottles of syrup), but if you are on a budget, might be best to opt for Morsel's, a coffee shop on the other end of the hotel's lobby. Speaking of the lobby, it was beautiful. The 6th floor heated pool had comfy lounge chairs with cushions and a nice supply of white, plush towels. Very nice. We only stayed at the Omni one night as we rented a car (from Enterprise -- great service) and headed north up the coast. If you're visiting San Diego, and particularly going to a baseball game, I recommend the Omni.

“Nice place near beach, but nothing special” I spent 2 nights here as I had meetings in the area. The staff was courteous, the room was clean and modern and the location was reasonably convenient to north San Diego, La Jolla and Del Mar. Unlike most of the Marriott's I've stayed in recently, I found the bed and bed linens a bit uncomfortable - the linens were very stiff. The room A/C-Heat just blew cool air even when set to Heat, I wound up turning it off so the room would warm up. I had drinks in the bar, which was quite lively in the evening. There were multiple events being held during both the day and evening both days I was there, and the noise carried up to my room on the 2nd floor. Parking was on the pricey side, though the room rate was OK with my corporate discount. Overall, it was middle of the road for a Marriott property. I wouldn't go out of my way to stay here, but it was OK for a couple of nights.

“Great value” Stayed here for a 4 night stay. I selected this hotel because the rates were at least $50 less than any other property in the area (except those with "shared baths"). Paying sub-$100 for midweek in midtown, I was unsure what to expect. But everything was fine. The room was clean and well-serviced. The room size was not huge but not bad, especially for Manhattan: I had a King bed and plenty of room to walk around the room, even with my bags out. There were 2 elevators, but one was under maintenance. That made the waits a bit long but not too terrible. I cannot comment on the service here, since I had no problems that required attention. Typical (free) continental breakfast spread: bagels, cereal, etc. Note that the free wireless is extremely weak, to be expected, I guess, in a 100 year old stone building. I could not get any signal at all, either in my corner room or in the lobby. I was able to get a weak signal from the stairs on my floor, but who wants to work there. However, the phones have data ports and local calls are free. Summary - not the best hotel I've ever stayed at, but a great deal for the price. I would return here anytime cost is a consideration.

“Great Location, Amazing Views, Some Issues” I stayed here for 5 nights in November while attending a conference, and overall, I enjoyed my experience. I was in one of the rooms in the tower that has yet to be upgraded, so I believe there were some cleanliness issues. For instance, my bare feet got dirty walking on the carpet (ewwww!) and I saw trash under the cabinet containing the fridge (double ewww). However, the bed and bathroom were clean, and the view of the bay was AMAZING from my 12th floor room. Moreover, the staff were all very friendly, the common areas of the hotel were tasteful and relaxing, and the parking--while waaaayyyyy overpriced--was very convenient. The room service had its high and low points--some dishes were excellent (such as omelets and the cheeseburger), while others were not very good (and the quesadillas were horrible.) I also believe the internet should be free in this day & age, esp. when paying close to $200/night for a room. Despite the issues this giant hotel has, I would definitely stay here again, esp. in an upgraded room, because the locale and views are wonderful.

“Exotic gem” First, the basics: comfy bed, great shower, immaculately clean, fine location (near Times Sq but not too noisy), small room but perfect for solo traveler Next, the extras: nice free continental breakfast, fun flashing of Times Sq neon in my window at night (there was a shade if needed), privacy curtain for shower (Shower is actually in the room, toilet is only additional room) Last: the sensational: the staff, friendliest I have ever encountered and this says a lot as all boutique staffers seem to be trained in the same wonderful hospitality school; the decor, with Indian references and homey gas fireplaces scattered throughout, making for a happy relief coming in from the rain. I booked via Sniqueaway and had gotten a reasonable rate of $174 not including taxes etc Just a lovely all around experience.

“Great location & Fantastic Staff!” Just got back from a fun time in Austin. What a cool city with so much to do! This hotel is within walking distance to 6th Street and the Capitol. Easy access to everything around town. The staff was super nice as well. Gregory Minor at the front desk was so helpful with my stay and had an extremely friendly personality. I look forward to heading back here soon and enjoying more of Austin next time. Enjoy your time in this superb city.

“Excellent base to explore the city” We had a wonderful, wonderful time at the Amalfi. It is so near to everything! We were happy to walk quite a bit, but it truly was close to things like the theater district, the Art Institute, and many of the must do pizza places. The "front desk" is SUPER trendy and modern, but they were always very helpful. There was also a free happy hour with really nice, light appetizers around 4? I believe. We got to the hotel after a trip from Boston just in time for this, so it was a wonderful surprise. We took the subway from the airport into the hotel area, and it was a LONG trip. However, we were happy that we did as the traffic outside our window seemed ridiculous and the trip would have likely been even longer. The room was well kept and clean, with a very contemporary feel to it. Seriously. It was a WONDERFUL base to explore the city as a first-timer to Chicago. Would love to stay there again if I return.

“Good Hotel” This is a good hotel. The staff was friendly, and the rooms are big and clean. There is a nice lounge, and the free wireless interenet access is very nice for business travel. If you are into shopping, you will not be bored. There are also several nice restaurants nearby.

“Excellent stay” After reading mixed reviews I was skeptical. Just completed a two night stay and was very pleased. Took the blue line directly from the airport to the State and Lake stop and paid 5 dollars plus tip to get to the hotel. Normally the cab fare is 40-45 so we were happy to save. I purchased a 2 day pass from the CTA on their website for 9 dollars. Pass arrived within a few days of purchase and makes using the subways and buses easy. Front desk staff was quick to check us in and gave us exactly the room that we requested. We were able to check in very early and were treated very professionally by Megan at the desk. Room was on a higher floor corner facing the Chicago Tribune. Room was extremely clean and I didn't see any food trays etc. as noted on other reviews. Room appeared updated with an extremely clean bathroom. The bed was extremely comfortable with lots of pillows and extra towels and blanket in closet. Not a great deal of drawer space. Didn't wait more than a few minutes for the concierge which were extremely helpful. The location is okay, steps from Michigan Avenue right near transportation. We walked the 10-15 minute walk to the Chicago Art Museum which is free until Feb. 21. The hotel is huge with two towers and holds more than 1800 rooms. It has a convention type setting but we knew this and for what we paid were extremely happy. We took the Gray Line tour which picked us up on time right in front of the hotel. Didn't eat the food but lines in the morning appeared long. There is a Houlihans right next door. Had drinks at the Martini bar and loved the setting. If I was planning a family trip with kids in tow I might look for another hotel considering that there is no pool. Dined at Maggiano's for great Italian family style food with huge portions at inexpensive prices, had a huge portion of meatballs and rigatoni for 11.95. Went to the Chicago Chop House and had a great steak for a fair price. Both places need a reservation and I would make them online on their websites. I would go back in a heart beat for the right price. Bell staff and everyone else truly demonstrated the Hyatt attitude and willingness to do whatever it takes to please the customer.

“great, "no negatives" stay” very polite doorman wheeled luggage in for us; super quick and friendly service at check-in; front desk and concierge very helpful giving us directions; room was very clean & beds extremely comfortable; common areas clean and well-decorated; hotel very accommodating in holding our luggage for better part of a day, between the time we checked-out and before we caught our train; did not use pool or eat at hotel restaurant

“Nice stay in San Jose” We stayed for one night at the Homewood Suites in San Jose (close to San Jose Airport) for one night in late January. The room was quiet, located on the first floor. We had a one bed room with a sofa bed for our son. The bathroom and vanity area was huge. There were two televisions as well as a small dining table, microwave, refrigerator, and small cook top . There are several restaurants adjacent to the parking lot - some ethnic choices as well as a Subway. The breakfast was quite good. We were pleased with our one night stay.

“Excellent rooms & meeting facilities.” Was just there for a conference. Excellent conference facilities and location to restaurants. Temperature of the rooms and acoustics were just right. I really do object to paying for Wifi, but I have my own wireless Wifi, so I don't pay the fees. Always astounds me that any Holiday Inn Express will provide free Wifi, but a Hyatt, Westin, etc, at twice the nightly rate, won't provide it. In today's world that is just unacceptable. I even have a Hyatt Gold Card and still would have had to pay. Ok, enough for that rant. Room was excellent, bed comfortable. Great workout facility.

“What a Gorgeous Hotel in an Incredible Soho Location....” This is one of the loveliest hotels I've had the pleasure of staying in. The decor is so inviting, warm, and cool all at once. Bravo on that. Location laughably good. Turn left and you're at Balthazar, turn right and you're dining at Savoy. All the shopping and excitement of Soho at your feet. The hotel had some minor snafus on the room service front - not just once but twice - and there was confusion about the Sunday screening room procedure and pricing, but overall I had no major quibbles. Hard to imagine doing better in New York unless you really don't enjoy being in the "scene." I found it a nice follow-up to my quiet, wonderful Plaza Athenee stay on the UESide. Great to experience both. I'll definitely return to Crosby and try their London properties as well.

“Nice, Roomy, Great Location for Some” Stayed here one night for an early business meeting. As said on previous reviews, it is withing a couple of blocks from several subway lines and a reasonable walk from the Staten Island Ferry. It is located on West Street, the lower result of the West Side Highway. As said, there are not a ton of restaurant choices in the area, but there enough you won't go hungry! Internet service would be $12.95, but waived for Priority Ckub memebers depending on level. It is a pleasant walk to Batery Park, with the views and boats to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. Some of the Hotel rooms have the views of them also... The room I was in had 2 double beds, very comfortable and roomy by Manhattan standards. Didn't have much interaction with the staff, but checkin was fast and friendly. Because the UN was in session and a late reservation , I paid over $500 for the night.... so I can't say anything about a value.. Depending on price, would stay again.
“Great Hotel and Location for Sea World” Staff was very accommodating and friendly at this hotel. I have a disabled daughter in a wheel chair and they were very helpful to us.

“Unusually Bad W Hotel” I usually enjoy my stays at the W brand; but not this one. As a top-tier frequent guest at Starwood properties I go all the way back to the first W properties in NYC. The W San Diego is easily the worst of the many in which I have stayed. Things started off badly when I arrived and no one was at the valet station (there is no self parking.) I hate paying 35 a night to be inconvenienced. It got worse at the front desk where I had to fight for an upgrade; I had to take a low floor/handicapped room to get a larger room. I booked the room last minute myself but my platinum reservation agent let me know that the hotel had plenty of rooms in all categories for my stay that night so an upgrade should be no problem. The desk clerk falsely claimed that nothing else was available. Warning to SPG members this hotel will not treat you well. I unpacked and started to take a shower. I quickly noticed that the handicapped shower floor was not angled properly causing the water to start to flood into the bathroom. What a pain. I knew this was not good and called the front desk for a room change. I found out that the hotel had been aware of the problem for years and usually asked to guests to make a 'towel dam" on the floor to control the water. This place is a mess. In order to get a non-flooding room I had to take a downgrade to a standard no water view room. Gee thanks. The decor is odd for a W property. The rooms are white laminate (chipped and painted over) with a chalkboard with no chalk or erasers. Probably too many guests were writing This Place Sucks on the blackboard. I have a feeling W rightly abandoned this decor as I have not seen it elsewhere. The pool, pool area, and the fitness room are microscopic. As if that were not bad enough the entire pool area was taken over for a business meeting. It was really bizarre to be sweating on a machine while a business conference is in session inches away. I cant imagine trying to swim with the tablecloths nearly dipping in the water of the tiny pool. It is so wrong for any hotel to usurp the fitness area and pool area for private parties. The location is off putting as welI. It is next to the high-rise jail and is surrounded by the usual bail bond places and their customers. It seems most of the rooms have crappy views. My first room was of a parking lot and bus transit area. The second room view was not much better. The hotel seemed deserted and had none of the usual W vibe. The restaurants were both empty at breakfast and dinner. I did not try them. This hotel is the worst in the W chain and by far the worst of all the Starwood options in San Diego area. Avoid it, as you can find much better nearby.

“Wyndham Garden not up to Wyndham standards” The beds were terrible - uncomfortable, poor quality, hard square pillows and no blanket, just a sheet and very thin cotton cover. Not even a bedspread to pull up for warmth (just a narrow cover over the end of the bed.) We stayed 2 nights, the first morning my husband realized not only was the bed uncomfortable, it was broken! In general the quality and maintenance is poor - remotes that don't work, sliding door handle dropped off, one room had a one-cup coffee pot with one-cup pods, the other room had a large coffee pot but still only one one-cup pod, so we had to call for more coffee. These are minor things, no big deal, but not what you would expect of a 3-star Wyndham, more like a cheap motel. In fairness, I would like to say that management and staff were just fine. The front desk kindly upgraded us to a small suite when I asked if they might have a fridge and microwave to prepare food for our 2 year old son. The manager responded immediately to the broken bed issue, told us we would be moved to a different room and we could do so in the afternoon when we returned from brunch. (We did that and although the front desk called for someone to help us move, no one showed up so we did it ourselves.) The $60 Hotwire rate was reasonable, I would not want to pay more for this property.

“OK for 1 Night Only, Maybe!” Stayed here for 6 nights, never again!! Noisy rooms, On the days I could sleep people were slamming their doors because they are all warped and you need to close them hard, on the one day it was quite the front desk called and woke me they called the wrong room thought I was someone else(thanks) My desk was in the corner so it was hard to eat or just relax and watch TV. Speaking of which NO premium channels (HBO, Showtime etc) Don't remember the last time I stayed in a hotel without at least 1 premium channel?(1980 maybe!!lol) That would not have mattered if the internet wasn't slower then dial up, I could barely get emails, let alone actually work on the computer so that left me to watching re-runs. They do offer a nice buffet style hot breakfast complete with servers to get your drinks and help you (don't forget to tip) This hotel is outdated, overpriced and over rated!!!If you need more then 1 night, Go elsewhere you will be glad you did.

“Ich komme wieder: 100 pro” Das Beach Haven Inn am Pacific Beach "gönnte" mir Anfang Februar 3 Nächte zum Preis von 2en und das zu einer Rate, die fast nicht zu unterbieten war. Mein Appartement (inkl. Küche, Flat-TV) hat mich voll überzeugt, da es unglaublich gut gepflegt und sehr schön ausgestattet war. Von der Sonne, die letzten Monate nicht gerade verwöhnt, verbrachte ich tagsüber immer mal wieder ein paar Stunden am/im geheizten Pool (ca. 24 Grad), so dass ich mich - gut ausgeruht - ins Surfer-Nachtleben stürzen konnte. Durch die sehr zentrale Lage kann man abends getrost auf's Auto verzichten, da alles in wenigen Minuten zu Fuß zu erreichen ist. + Sehr gut supported wurde ich von den freundlichen Leuten an der Rezeption, die mit ihren sehr guten Empfehlungen stets ins Schwarze trafen. Speziell die Tipps für einen Ausflug nach Tihuana (Mexico) erwies sich als sehr hilfreich. + Ich hab mich im Beach Haven Inn super wohl gefühlt, was nicht zuletzt an der lockeren Klientel der Gäste lag (viele Surfer). Ich komme wieder: 100 pro!

“A Gem” Great location, plush and contemporary designed rooms (if small), with quality touches like a hand written card with tomorrow's weather, cookies & milk delivered for our 2 year old, a great bed & pillows, quiet atmosphere, a wonderful restaurant and great front desk service. Oh, I wish more Hoteliers would follow this code. And we got it all for 225 a night.

“Hang out in Austin at the Embassy Suites” Stayed here for a week in November. Nice hotel, clean and spacious rooms. Free breakfast and happy hour. Free internet in the business center, but $10/day in the room. Short walk to 6th street, nice trails around Town Lake. Good location on South Congress with "public" transportation to UT. Austin is not that big so walking is popular, as are bikes. ES is near a Hyatt, a Raddison, and a Hampton Inn, all on Town Lake. At least 3 places to eat near the hotel and more within walking distance. Lots of clubs close by if that's your thing. I got free parking in the garage, but its a walk and an elevator ride away.

“I love Aloft hotels” Since I stayed at the Aloft Denver Airport whenever I can try to sleep in this hotel chain ... The rooms are the same in all hotels and I love ... spacious, modern, amazing shower, toiletries formidable, the excellent treatment. I stayed one night to be near the airport and I had to take a flight to MEX. The recommended hotel bar and fast food they have. Certainly, provided you have the opportunity, stay at Aloft Hotel

“Stayed Here Many Times” I travel about 40 weeks a year, and try to stay at Hilton Family Hotels, mainly Hamptons, as much as possible, being a diamond member with them. I have stayed at this particular Hampton Inn many times over the past several years, and I will say it is up to par with most Hamptons I frequent. The recent remodel in the lobby and the new carpet thru out was needed, but is a nice and inviting. The new Hampton Bed linens are as good as a more expensive hotel, and the staff at this particular Hampton are extremely pleasant. They have a nice happy hour in the afternoons with free hot snakcs, beer, wine, and sodas which a lot of Hamptons do not do. The price here is very reasonable, and if your AAA you get 10% off when booking on their site. My only complaint would be the surrounding area, called "restaurant row" but it is a little seedy. Still some good restaurants for every taste very close to the hotel. I always book this hotel when in Dallas area.
“beautiful hotel” This is a gorgeous hotel with great service. The location could not be better. I love staying at the MUSE.

“Enjoyed our stay” We booked this hotel based on Tripadvisor reviews. It is a beautiful property with direct access to the Riverwalk and only 5 minutes from the heart of the action. The street level location may look a little rough, but it is safe and friendly and only minutes from the Alamo, El Mercado and the big mall. Our room was nice and big, ask for the Alamo Tower, better access to everything. The roof top pool and two hot tubs are great and were not overly busy while we were there. The breakfast is basic, but very convenient and filling. The afternoon happy hour is a bit odd, 3 free drinks, but with no atmosphere, better to take them back to your room or to the pool. The food is what it is, hotdogs and mac and cheese. Good if you have kids. There is a bank in the lobby and security excellent. The staff are wonderful. Ask them anything about San Antonio.

“Check your bill” Stayed here on business two nights. First night was fine. Room is small but cushy, nice view, hyper-priced internet connection. Hotel bar upstairs also has beautiful view, high prices, lousy service. Second night checked out at 4am to catch plane back to Chicago. Printer wasn't working, so they promised to e-mail me a bill. 3 weeks later, still no bill. I had to fax a request! Got my bill: they had added over $200 to the second night's price. After 6 more weeks of calling, I finally got it reversed. If you are rich and don't know any better, this hotel is fine. If you care about service try someplace else.

“Fantanstic, Fun and Trendy Hotel” I stay in a lot of Starwoods Hotels because I think they have one of the best rewards programs. I had to travel to Dallas so I decided to try the W Dallas-Victory. This hotel was fantastic, fun, energetic and very cool. POSITIVES: 1. The bed: This is a given in all Ws which all, I believe, use the "Hevenly Bed." I love this bed, it is pillowed topped and has nice linens and a huge (and heavy) down comforter. It is so comfortable. I was so impressed with this bed the first time I stayed at a W in 2002 that I actually bought one. Its nice to have the same bed in the hotel that I enjoy every night at home. 2. The bar/lobby. Its large and very inviting. Its also very fun, lots of cozy couch and seats to sit in and enjoy the music. Very fun and enegetic area. See pictures. I also heard that the rooftop bar called the Ghost Bar is AMAZING but I was there on business and had to be up early to catch a flight so I did not check it out. 3. The pool: Its outside on the 16th floor with amazing views of the city. It has cool chairs to lounge in and is decorated in a very fashionable way. See pictures. Also has a small bar that is lots of fun with a friendly bar staff and a really nice place to hang and enjoy a drink. 4. Concierge: The staff at the W's conciege desk (which I believbe is call Whereever/Whenever) was wonderful. They helped me find a nearby restaurant for great BBQ, they recommended that I go see the Sixth Floor Museum at the TExas Book Depository (a museum about the JFK assassination, which was FANTANSTIC) and printed movie listing and directioons to the theather so I could see a movie that evening. I rarely comment on staff in my reviews but the two ladies who sat at the concierge desk really went out of there way. 5. Room: Very large and nice furniture, but oddly laid out, see below comment and pictures. NEUTRALS: 1. Price. I paid $299/night booked through spg.com. While this is a little on the high side I felt it was worth it. 2. Room: The color scheme and layout of the room was a tad bizarre. The walls of the room were painted black (or extremely dark blue) which made the room feel dark. Also (besides the tolliet) the bathroom is not seperated from the bedroom. Its hard to explain but you can sit on the bed and see the shower and sink. See pictures. Also the shower has no shower door to close, you simply walk behind a large piece of glass and shower which doesn't keep the steam in. NEGATIVES: 1. The elevators were often slow. 2. The parking at the hotel was $24, which seems high. 3. The hallways leading to your room are extremely dark and although done so purposefully (to add to the club-like feel of the hotel), I would prefer a well-lit, bright, airry and open hallway outside the rooms.

“OK but slow unreliable internet and elevators will make me think twice...” I've stayed here three times int he past 60 days and each trip was 4 nights. Room was decent size. Comfortable bed and nice bathroom. The killer for me is the internet. I know it's free but it's so slow that you can;t even use it. I'd rather pay for it and have it work... I stay here on business and need to work in the evenings and when I can't get on line or get on line and have to wait forever for pages to load then I am not productive and it's a deal breaker. Also, the elevators are slow and there's only three of them which causes long lines. One last gripe is the fitness facility is tiny and underequipped. If u don't care about work outs and the internet and don;t midn waiting up to 15 minutes for an elevator at times then the place is great for the money.

“What One Would Expect From Hilton, Not Bad - Not Terrific” Nice-ishly remodeled hotel. Comfy bed, oddly configured room that was quite small. Valet parking is a total rip off 18$ !!:>0 As was room service. Pricey, as room service always is, but a $2 dine in fee, 18% service charge (NOT an automatic gratuity, service fee!). So your 20$ burger and soda is 20$ + 2$ + 3.96$ (service fee) + 20% tip (5.20$ ). 31 buck for a cold greasy burger with a flat diet coke. But in fairness, it IS in the room service menu fine print. Better to walk over to Denny's or Wendy's ;>) So I would say pass on the room service. Breakfast in the hotel was not bad, but then, not terrific either. Very attentive wait staff, especially the college kid from Ireland. Staff was friendly. Check in and out was quick and pleasant. Valets were very nice. Excellent location. Average chain hotel with very nice college kids working there. Would I stay there again??? Ehhhh mebee....

“Wouldn't Return” This hotel was obviously nice at one point. However, a lack of good housekeeping and maintenance has degraded this building significantly. I made a reservation for a non-smoking room. As I checked in, I had to return to the front desk four times to properly fulfill that request. I effectively got to see four rooms as the first three rooms they gave me were not up to par. Room #1 - Smoking Room Room #2 - The room was not cleaned. Bed was untidy. Towels Used. Room #3 - Although it was a non-smoking room, the room smelt like smoke. Room #4 - Non-Smoking Room that was fine. They gave me a discount and several other free things to accomodate my hassles. The hotel is obviously used and worn and there are visible signs of untidyness in the common areas. The bathrooms are old and need updating. Staff is extremely friendly and obviously embarrassed by the above problems with my room. They are the #1 positive for this hotel. Shuttle service to downtown is convenient and much appreciated. Hotel restaurant has nice views but food is just about average. Overall, I felt like the hotel was dirty and I would definitely not return. I've never really said this about a hotel but I feel this deserved it.

“This is the place to stay in Chicago (especially with young children)” I think it has all been said -- great value, great location, great staff, great amenities. We stayed here for 3 nights in late December and early January (over New Year's Eve). Enjoyed the indoor pool & hot tub and the spacious 1-bedroom suite (living room with kitchen, separate bedroom with adjacent bath). Modern design, everything in good working condition, room was quiet, etc. Two (minor?) things did detract from our stay: the elevator requires a room key to operate but the card readers in the elevator consistently had problems with our room keys and the keys of other guests. It actually forced me to think twice about using the (slow) elevators. The other issue is that the free high-speed internet terminals went out for about 24 hours; this was apparently the result of the bad weather but it really creates a problem in this modern era when we all need internet to check travel plans, do airline check-ins, etc. The staff was made aware of the problems but were apparently helpless to offer remedies. These two issues were minor in our overall stay -- we'd happily stay here again and highly recommend the hotel. I just wanted to be fair/objective in pointing out 'room for improvement' .

“Posh elegance in Keller suburbia” Well I shouldn’t say “surprising” I suppose, since Hilton has a good reputation, but I was blown away by how chic this hotel was! Our stay was fantastic! We needed a hotel close to our old neighborhood in Keller, as we were visiting our rental house so my husband and I selected the Hilton Garden Inn and were pleasantly surprised with its elegance, amazingly nice staff and SUPER comfortable beds. Seriously, the beds were some of the best I have ever stayed in, and we stay in a decent number of hotels. The lobby is very welcoming with dark décor, great lights, and wide open vaulted ceilings. The front desk checked us into our room in about 30 seconds and was very nice. The rooms are very well furnished (I LOVED the paint on the wall, very modern and fancily textured). Everything was very clean, the linens are all washable, including the duvet. I love that they have Neutrogena products as their standard toiletries. My only complaint about the room is that housekeeping didn’t do the most thorough job, as we did not get clean/new drinking glasses in our kitchenette area, but if that is our complaint, hey, it can’t be that terrible. My only other complaint about the hotel is the noise level, not of the staff or road, but of the guests, the hall noise pours easily into the bedrooms and we had some very unconscientious neighbors. But luckily that was only while they were checking out, the rest of the time it was fine. I would totally stay there again in a heartbeat and wish that all hotels were this classy and reasonably priced. Everyone we talked to was very nice, welcoming and competent. The place was not overly crowded. The breakfast had a great selection, the service staff at the restaurant was great! They even have a decent happy hour. The hotel is very close to the airport, Grapevine, and the Ft. Worth suburbs. I was impressed, nice work Hilton Garden Inn, we will surely see you again!

“Very Chic” I've stayed at this W three separate times and have had 3 good experiences. The rooms are larger than a typical room at the W, and I especially appreciate how quiet this hotel is. The location is excellent ($18 taxi from DCA, and 3 blocks from the Metro station) and walking distance to the White House and Washington Monument. Coffee is avaliable in the lobby in the morning (there are no coffee pots in the room), and hot cider is available in the afternoon. The restaurants in the hotel are excellent, and the view from the terrace is superb. Acura was doing a promotion with the W, so I took advantage of the free car service (twice) while I was there. It was raining during my visit, but I was able to borrow an umbrella with a $40 deposit. W Hotels are trendy, and my only criticism is that there are few perks - free wifi in the lobby but not in the room, and it will cost to use the hotel computers for the internet in their business center. Also, sometimes it takes a while to figure out how to turn on the lights in the room as the fixtures are modern. On my first stay, I had a view overlooking the White House lawn, but the next 2 times, my view was of the interior brick walls - but again, the room was very quiet. I'll definitely stay here again if I have the opportunity.

“Typical Biz Hotel” Located across the street from Mass General, you're a 10-minute walk from the north side of the Commons, a little longer to Faneuil Hall and a $10 cab ride to Fenwick. This is a typical business-oriented hotel. The rooms are normal size, the beds are comfortable. The bathroom has been recently renovated but not the rooms themselves. Our room was clean and there were plenty of towels. Service was good - we got early check-in and they answered all of our questions promptly. There is free WiFi and an seasonal outdoor heated pool (neither of which we used but they're nice to think about). The bar/restaurant was mostly empty at night and there is nothing to do in the immediate area. But cabs pass by every few seconds and they can call a car service if needed.

“Pretty good” This is a usual Hampton Inn. The location is great. Perhaps a few dollars overpriced, but if you get an AAA discount, it is not bad. The desk people are great. The breakfast is very good. I had a large room, everything new, and quiet. It isclearly worth the few dollars more than other nearby hotels.

“Quality masquerading as Clarion - Not bad, but definitely not upscale.” Just a quick overnight with spouse. Although it is located in the Tech Center Business Park with few amenities in walking distance, there are ample shopping and eating/drinking choices within a 5-minute drive. Desk staff were friendly and professional. The breakfast and manager reception were more than expected. The rooms are clean and the bed seemed new, but are otherwise cheaply furnished and decorated, sparsely appointed, and definitely need updating. This property is really more suited to the Quality brand - it definitely doesn't feel upscale. I agree with the previous reviewer that there are better options in the area for the price. The pool area is large and well-kept, and there is free wi-fi, a large fitness room and a guest laundy.

“Enjoyed the Comfort Suites-Great location, BIG ROOM” My friends and I stayed at the Comfort Suites April 30-May 2nd. We got a great rate (approximately 170.00 per night). We were heading to the Cubs game on the 30th, and the front desk was kind enough to stow our bags in a locked room and everything was fine when we picked them up for check-in. The hotel is fairly close to an "L" line as we flew in from O'hare. The hotel is also close to the red line (Wrigley Field or US Cellular Field). Location, this hotel for its price is unparalled. The room was quite large. We had a full kitchen, walk in closet, and desk area. I was under the impression each room had wi-fi, which it does not. Hotel does provide ethernet cords. Room also had flat screen tvs. We were given free hot breakfast each day ( Saturday: Eggs, and bacon. Sunday: omlete and sausauge links. Waffles are there each day). We didnt use the exercise equipment. The only drawback was the bathroom. I thought it was small, our toilet didnt flush occasionally, and my friend called for extra towels Friday evening and someone told him that they were out. I asked Saturday morning (at 8am) and had towels delievered within 10 minutes, so I am unsure about the difference 10 hours made in the towel situation. Overall, I would definately stay here again. This is a great hotel for the value. The beds were great (pillows were not). Everyone was very friendly and the location to the Magnificent Mile is great for the price. You also have a 7-11 and CVS Pharmacy very close by for any incidental needs.

“great home base for New York touring” We had a great trip to New York and staying at the DoubleTree made it even better. My 13 year old daughter loved the location, right in the middle of all the action of Times Square. I loved the location with easy access to multiple subway lines, walking to local sights, many close restaurants, tons of shopping, etc. Suite was very spacious for NYC standards. Bathroom fine, but could have used a fan. Excellent, friendly service all around. Spectacular views out of our 32nd floor windows. Noise level at night wasn't too distracting, considering the location. Hotel had a good breakfast buffet, pricey, but we got complimentary from Hilton HHonors. Used the well-stocked fitness room. Mix of business travellers and families during our visit. Overall, highly recommended!

“A Favorite Once But Needs More” I have stayed at this location 7-8 times over the years. It is conveniently located; the manager is very attentive to needs; the staff is top notch; and breakfast is the best. Now the bad... I did a review in August of last year mentioning a need for WiFi in rooms. The local manager responded on TripAdvisor saying they were working on it. Here we are 10 month later and still no WiFi even though the description of the accommodations under Hilton website says: "complimentary high-speed internet access with wireless capabilities". If under accommodations, I assumed the rooms would have wireless access. But no. In order to be online, you need to sit at a desk. Only one person can be online at a time. In order to use the comfortable chair in the room I went to a local tore and bought a 25 foot cable to get online (wired). I believe WiFi in a hotel room these days is important. This location needs to get with it. Two additional comments... When showering, the shower head was not hitting us correctly. I adjusted it for my height then my wife showered and changed it for her height (shorter). The shower head came off while she was showering. The head was not installed correctly.
