Finally, please put a trash container outside the hotel or near door. I'm told corporate didn't want containers outside but it is a "pain" to have to carry empty drink containers and snack trash back to our room to dump it there. It is still a very nice hotel due to the staff but no longer a favorite.

“Nice surprise” In my mind, Hiltons are normally pretty safe bets. Nothing terribly exciting and nothing normally too bad. This Hilton exceeded my expecations by a mile. First, the location is terrific if you want to be close to the Back Bay train station, Newbury Street, the Pru Center, good restaurants, shopping, and places to walk around. The rooms must have been renovated recently because my room was spotless and all of the furniture was new, the bathroom fixtures were new and the countertops were granite. The bed and the linens stack up with any Ritz I have stayed in. What pleased me the most was the service I received the next morning from room service. It arrived exactly on time and the server was friendly and refused my additional gratuity because she said it was already included. Five minutes after she left, she returned because she said that the coffee I ordered was not fresh enough and so she brought me a new pot. And, still she refused the gratuity I tried to give her. I don't normally stay at the Hilton in Boston, but in the future I will. Very nice place for business or pleasure. I did not see the gym, but I heard it was new.

“Great Location and Clean Westin in Georgetown” Stayed here back in July. Very nice Westin. Great location as well in Georgetown. I was on business, but would also have worked well for pleasure. Will stay here again. Did not try the restaurant, but the bar off the lobby was pleasant.

“I love this hotel, but...” I do love the history and heritage of this hotel. It is such a beautiful building and has such an amazing past. It has, for the most part, the typical Westin service, and a great bar. They've added a great steak house since the last time I stayed there. I will disclaim that I am SPG Gold and was the meeting organizer for the meeting we held at the hotel before I talk about my room. That's because my room was fantastic. It was a large corner room with three huge windows overlooking Union Square, a king bed, and a little "living room" area. I LOVED it! The location can't be beat as it is close to the Bart and the trolley cars, as well as all the shopping you could want. You can walk through China Town and if you're ambitious, down to the wharf. I did not use the fitness center or take advantage of their guided fitness (walks/runs) because I was sick, and they charge $12 to use the gym. I hate that anyway, but didn't really feel I would get my money's worth with a chest cold. However (and I did tell them I was going to post this) they currently seem to have a problem with prostitution and street people. I was shocked by the working girls parading through the lobby on our second night there. I heard from others in my group that the same thing I had been going on the first night, but I didn't believe them. Also, there were some street people having a fight in front of the main entrance that night when we came back from our group event. I made it very clear to the personnel in the bar that I was both shocked and appalled by the fact they seemed to be turning a blind eye to the going's on. In fact, the first time I mentioned it, including the fact that I'd stayed here the previous summer and hadn't noticed I was told matter of factly by the cocktail waitress, it was getting worse because of the economy. The second night they seemed to take my complaint more seriously, and the activity seemed greatly diminished. I was told my one of our group members who happened to be there the next week that there was a considerable improvement. Overall, I would recommend this hotel highly. It's an amazing place to stay, just be on the lookout for the street life late at night. I'm hoping the hotel management will beef up security and chase away this activity for good. (For those keeping track this was the last hotel of 4 in 17 days, so I had really high standards at this point.)

“Great Hotel near the airport” Chose to stay my last night in San Antonio near the airport and chose this Hilton based on Tripadvisor reviews. The reviews are correct, this is a good hotel. The hotel sits on the 410 loop just minutes from the airport. Check in was routine and the front desk staff was pleasant. Lobby is large with plenty of places to sit and meet people. My room was on the top floor and was pleasant upon entering. Room was clean and fine for two people to stay in. Had a light dinner in Tex's Sports bar. Plenty of televisions, not too noisy and from the looks of things, lots of business travelers....one person at every table. Food was good. Ordered the nacho's for an appetizer....it was a huge portion. Steak sandwich was good as was a cold beer. Hotel has a small fitness center, hotel signs make it confusing to get to. Outdoor pool, a couple of putting greens and 24 hour business center. This hotel also has a some large meeting rooms and ballroom for a conference. We took the free shuttle to the airport at 4:00am and it only took a few minutes to get to the airport. Good hotel recommend it.

“What a Toss Up !!!!!!!!!!!!!!” Depends on your needs if this hotel will fit your needs. Located right off I 45 (exit 36) just 8 miles south of downtown Houston and only 2.5 miles to Hobby International Airport. Stayed two nights to check out Minute Maid Park ( a must for baseball nuts) this establishment met all our needs. Had room located in rear of building and never heard Highway traffic but did hear a few buffer flights going over hotel. No walking distance restaurants available but we spent our time in the city. My only problem with establishment was no fresh soap, shampoo, or plastic cups were replenished by housekeeping in morning, so you'll have to go to front desk to request. Breakfast is almost non-exsistence so plan on a Denny's 2-4-8 if you must start your day right. Great Bed, very,very small bathroom, but most important a very friendly staff to make you feel welcome........so like i stated it's a toss up as to what fits your needs...mine was a Home Run.......................

“空港に近いリーズナブルなホリディイン” インターコンチネンタル空港に近くて便利なわりに、値段もリーズナブルで清潔なホリディインです。宿泊当日はクリスマスイブで、到着時間が遅くなったためにホテルのレストランもしまった後でしたが、フロントスタッフから、すぐ近くに「ケトル」という名前の24時間営業のレストランを教えてもらいました。ここのビュッフェがまた安くて($7.95)家庭的な味でおいしく、幸せな気持ちになりました。ホテルの内装もモダンで部屋もきれいであり、おすすめのホテルです。ホテルからは高速道路の入り口もすぐで、どこへ行くにも便利です。

“Quite a reasonable hotel in an expensive city” The variability of the reviews for this hotel show how people's expectations can vary. I found this hotel to be an excellent choice when you consider the difficulty of finding a reasonably priced hotel within walking distance of Union Square. Yes, it's an old building, and you can hear street noises, and the neighborhood isn't Nob Hill (although it's nearby). It's a good price; it's well cared-for; the staff members are helpful; the restaurant is good; it's a reasonable walk to all sorts of great places (many straight uphill, of course). I would and probably will return to this hotel, and I suggest that those with reasonable expectations will enjoy their stay.

“This place is a NIGHTMARE!” I have NOTHING good to say about this hotel. It was a total dump! I stay in San Diego a lot (I mean A LOT) and have stayed at a lot of mediocre hotels and a few nice ones... but this was neither. This place is like some Tijuana nightmare. What do I mean by that? Read more below... First, the staff were unfriendly and almost resented having to work. That was the first tip off that something was wrong. The second tip off was the strange smell in the lobby. A super disgusting and cheap room deodorizer that smelled like it came from the 99cent store (in some flavor like LILAC or something very old smelling and too floral). Awful. Okay, I was tired and needed a place to stay and couldn't get on the internet. So I was a walk in. The outside of the place is deceptively retro and tropical. The inside is nothing like that! MAJOR mistake going here. I paid almost a hundred dollars for a room (using AAA -- who by the way should NOT be recommending this dump to anyone!). I was totally ripped off. After I changed rooms from a room that was next to the noisy freeway and which had a window that opened up to a blank wall (nice architecture! .... NOT !)... I was then given a room that was worse. I was told it would be a King and it was a double queen. I was tired and didn't feel like changing rooms again. Started to unpack, went to the bathroom. Saw massive peeling paint and mice feces! (took a photo) There were also strange stains on the carpet that splashed up onto the closet mirrors (and which seemed like it had been there for a while). Unbelievable! No, I am NOT kidding! I tried to ignore it and NOT walk around barefoot for obvious reasons. The room smelt horrible too. Like somebody had died in there. But housekeeping had obviously sprayed OVER the smell with that same gag-inducing air freshner from the lobby! I woke up at 2 am and was choking on the smell and physically got ill from it -- so I had to open a window to air the room out. I KNOW somebody had to have died in this room. It was THAT smell. Horrible. I went down to the soda machine area by the pool to get a soda to calm my stomach and was ripped off by BOTH soda machines which stole my quarters! I finally got one soda after paying for TWO. Obviously someone has rigged the machine to drop coins down into the machine and not into the proper coin area (I noticed this only after I had put in the coins). I know! This is unbelievable. But this is what kind of place this is!I feel COMPELLED to warn people to say away from here! Absolute nightmare in every respect. This is a hotel room that is going for around a hundred bucks too (but should be about $10 for what you get). Total dive. Terrible decor. No coffee maker. No iron even! Dinky little towels that are more like bath cloths and just absolutely unclean and smelly. DO NOT STAY HERE! Unless you are a transient, homeless person or someone who has absolutely no standards. It isn't even the bare bones no nonsense kind of hotel for a tired person for one night. Go to the Vagabond down the street for that (at least that one is CLEAN and the people are friendly). If you have any sense at all and want to enjoy a NICE San Diego hotel, you are going to have to spend a bit more money and go to a different part of town. This place is pure Tijuana standards. Fine for Mexico maybe, but not for San Diego. Oh and this is good. I overheard a girl say that someone's car was carjacked in the lot the same night I was there! Yes! Believe it. Not a safe area. Would rate this hotel an F! ! ! Do not stay here!

“This one needs an upgrade” I have stayed at many Courtyards and this one in my opinion is the best candidate for a renovation. The service was OK and pleasant, but not quite as professional as I am accustomed to. The room was clean and fairly average with a good work desk. The walls were thinner than usual, as I could hear the couple in the next room with too much clarity. The restaurant needs particular attention. It is pretty dark and shabby looking. behind the bar their bottles consist of about 6 different liquors lined up in a row. Despite there being only about 6 people at the bar, I waited about 5 minutes before getting the bartender's attention. She was very busy talking with another waiter. The food I ordered there was actually pretty good. So all in all this was an average stay, but the hotel needs attention and the restaurant needs an upgrade and better hiring practices As other reviews have stated, it is located in an industrial area so there is not much in the area as alternatives for eating.

“High end resort perfect for large meeting” This is a very impressive resort. Was here for a large business meeting but it felt like a vacation. The resort is huge and is more of a large meeting hotel but the convention areas are nicely spaced from the resort pool, rooms, and restaurants. The staff were very friendly and kept the place incredibly clean. The finishes are very high end in the rooms as well as the resorts bathrooms and other facilities (towels to dry your hands). Room was average size but had a balcony, Bathroom in the room was on the larger side and had separate glass shower and soaking tub. Service at the restaurants was responsive and attentive but drinks and food are expensive. From the pool there is a great view of the mountains and downtown Phoenix (about 30 min south). The grounds are impeccable and the outside spaces are beautiful. I would def. come back here for vacation to golf or just relax, in fact there were a lot of couples there. Expect luxury and quiet.

“Not a good value” I generally find Hyatt hotels to be among the best of the large chains, but this hotel does not measure up. The hotel is poorly located away from the city (which does give most rooms good views) but it is about a 10 minute walk to shops and restaurants and you have to cross a very busy 4-lane road to get to anything. The rooms are stylish and modern and the furniture is comfortable, but the rooms are not well maintained (stains on ceiling, damage on walls, mold in bathroom). All of the rooms are sprayed with fragrance which is overwhelming if they have just been cleaned; I nearly vomited when I opened the door to my room and had to move to another room, which was better but the odor was still very noticeable. I will stick to Starwood hotels in the future, their rates are more reasonable and generally a better value. I would recommend the Westin instead, much better location, and similar rates.

“Good if you get on Hotwire” Got this property on hotwire. It was a decent place for the price paid. That said...I would never pay their full price for this property. You can tell that they have updated it but there was mold growing in my tile and to me I thought if you had so much invested in the furnishings...it may be a good idea to spray a little tilex. They advertise that their airport shuttle runs every half hour and this is false. I got to the front desk a quater till and then waited a half hour for the shuttle driver who was rather unfreindly to come out of the hotel. I would reccomend if you get a cheap deal on hotwire but thats the only way. Their service was lacking as well as the cleanliness. I WOULD stay here again if I got the same deal on hotwire (which was $52.00).

“Big Rooms! (but loud). Great service.” Great location on 49th and Lexington. Next to the W and Intercontinental Hotels. Two doors down from the Waldorf. Small entrance on 49th and then you go into a single desk. There is virtually no lobby. One slow elevator. Then you go up to your room - there are only four rooms on a floor - this is a small former apartment complex. I was afraid I had made a mistake. Then we opened the door and here's a 1000+ square foot two-bedroom apartment with new wood floors throughout and a full kitchen. GREAT CHOICE for my family of five - adult kids. Very roomy except only one bathroom. Window unit a/c means that the street and construction noise comes right in. It's very loud. But you can set the a/c units to leave the fan on the whole time and that kills a lot of the noise. Breakfast was included which was a nice money saver. Heavy continental (boiled eggs, waffles, cereal, etc.). The Cafe Linda next door had very good food and was reasonable (for NYC). Sam at the front desk in the afternoons/evenings took great care of us. He got us limos, discounts on sightseeing venues and made sure we had everything we needed. Probably the best and friendliest front desk service I've ever had (and that includes some very high end hotels). This is probably one of the best locations for families that are sightseeing NYC. Walkable to Rockefellar Center and Central Park. Pretty good walk to Times Square - wouldn't want to do it to go to a Broadway show. Just a couple of blocks to the nearest subway station. Taxis were very difficult to get in the afternoon and evenings. We stood in line over at the W and waited 30 minutes (twice). Limos are very expensive but a nice way to travel. The NY subway system has gone downhill in my opinion in the past 10 years. We would absolutely stay here again for a family trip to NYC. I don't think I'd stay here for business (I might stay in a more traditional hotel). Considering the price this was a fantastic place to stay.
“It's all about location” A slightly tired hotel decor wise but in a perfect location for sightseeing in Boston. Very friendly, helpful staff. Would definitely use again.

“Ok Property if Price is right” Definitely better options in Houston. Price was right for a weekend rate but nothing memorable about this property. Rooms are ok, beds are comfortable. Bathroom is very small and rooms themselves are a little tight. One key thing for us traveling with kids was the fact that this property did not have on demand videos. Kids were looking forward to a movie so it was a little disappointing. First full service hotel I have been at that hasn't had this option. Indoor pool is clean but again nothing exciting about it. Close to Galleria but next time would probably opt for something else.

“Homey Hotel: very nice with great location” Selected this hotel based on two factors: 1.for great location to the Galleria Shopping Mall, less than one block walk and 2. plus good reviews, clean, good staff. This is an extended stay hotel, hotel provides 2 laundry rooms, each room or suite has a complete well equiped kitchen, room or suite has living area or living room with sofa, work station desk, chairs, tables, TV, etc. Pros: Great location, homey hotel, nice furniture and decor, very nice but not over the top, clean, well kept common areas, friendly staff, very good breakfast selection. Food station and room is well kept, clean, lots of choices. Three nights they provide a "welcome home" meal which was very good, menu or entree changes, calendar on frig. in room has menu posted. Each nightly meal includes a fresh salad, fresh toppings, very good quality, better than at the restuarants in the Galleria, as they are fresh, two types of lettuce, vegetable toppings of tomotoes, green pepper, cucumber, olives, cheese, etc. Plus a dessert. Also, selection of wine and beer, served on china or paper plates if you decide to take your meal back to your room. Business center with computers and a library, USA newspaper Cons: On site mini-market was somewhat limited on items but nice that it was available to guests. We were very pleased with all that the hotel had to offer, good service, good meals, great location and staff. Nicely priced. Quiet rooms, never heard neighbors, felt safe. Overall, a very clean, safe,homey feel. We stayed at hotel in December, hotel was nicely decorated for the season, very warm and inviting feel, like at home. Would stay at this hotel again.

“Nice Little Tidy Hotel - Somewhat No Frills Rooms” Stayed at the Camelback Courtyard on Business. Overall, the hotel is very nice. Very clean and nice lobby, with breakfast (not free) in the morning - and free coffee to go. Pool, simple workout room. It's just down the road from the Camelback mountain, a mountain that really does look like a camel lying down. Pretty scenic as you have a clear view of it down the road. The actual rooms are fairly simple. I attached some pictures. There's a desk, a place to hang your clothes, a small couch with a table. Nothing overly exciting - pretty standard. But it's all very clean. Some rooms have balconies, other's don't. The staff is friendly and attentive. It has free Internet - wired in the rooms, wireless in the lobby. There's a small snack area in the lobby. There are ice machines on each floor, but no drink machines. The best thing about the hotel is that it's very near a mall (walking distance) with shops and restaurants, a bookstore, a Chili's, etc. And it's within about 2 miles of a trendy mall-like area with upscale eateries and department stores. Just a block or so down the road is a new AMC movie theatre with an upscale fish restaurant (McCormick's and Schmick's). The rooms are quiet with easy access. There is covered mall parking (free) next door to keep your car out of the hot sun. I would recommend it as a nice place to stay in Tucson on business or for short vacations. Related: Traffic in Phoenix is terrible. It's not that there's congestion, but that there are many, many traffic lights on all of the streets and avenues - and they are not in synch. You literally miss every single light. A drive of 5 miles takes 20 minutes. Be prepared for a slow traversal of the city.

“Just fine!” This was our second time staying at The Barclay. We were well aware of the quality of the rooms and the ideal location. The service is pretty good too. Those things have not changed. But, checking in on this Friday afternoon was a little ridiculous. The hotel should adequately staff for peak times, since we received indication that this was typical. Also, we didn't have to park a car the last time, but given the price the hotel charges, I would advise checking around the block for a rate less than the $60/day they charge.

“Great” This hotel was well worth the price, but then again we only paid $50 for it. It beat out the $150 I've stayed in, so would be a good hotel even at $150. Parking was free, but they can charge up to $10 a night. Large and clean rooms with balconies. The bar, hot tub, and fitness center were good, but the pool was just ok. Drinks are way overpriced, and the airconditioner was loud, no in house massuese. Overall it was great. I plan to try to stay there again.

“Great location, not great room” My husband and I spent 4 nights at this hotel. We booked this hotel based on reviews we have read. The location is great for shopping on Robertson - the trendy boutique street, also home of the celeb dining hot spot - Ivy. I was disappointed by the rooms, although the bathrooms were nice. The size of the room was too small. The bed was extremely comfortable, though. It took forever to get our rooms made up each day - at least 3 p.m. before we got daily housekeeping service, which is disapointing. Also disappointing is the distance of the pool and spa from the hotel rooms. It is a LONG walk, no matter what room you are in. We did not try out the bar or restaurant, though the decor was quite appealing.

“Friendly in great location” The hotel staff were very friendly, especially the concierge who helped us sort out tickets for Billy Elliott that had not arrived, even though we did not order them through him. He was on the phone for over an hours for us! The man at check in also put us in a nice room on the 36th floor even though we had booked through hotwire. The rooms are very small, just enough room for a Queen bed, but a good view towards the Statue of Liberty. Just down the road from Macys and a subway stop on the corner. Excellent location and a lovely 1930s lobby. Good stay overall!

“Great Hotel, as you would expect” Stayed at the Biltomore as part of a conference. The service was excellent; from bellmen to front desk, to consierge, etc., etc. Tried the spa, and found the quality to be excellent and prices/value better than I expected. At first I was put into a room with a very noisy airconditioner, but was quickly moved to another room which was fine. Consierge was especially helpful with anything we needed. Overall, I was expecting great service and that is what I got.

“Great location, hotel, and staff” I stayed at OTA back in January for the first time. The location is prime. You only a teeny bit away from Time Square, which IMO is great since you are away from all the tourist traps.There are tons of places to eat, things to do and see around this location. The hotel itself is awesome. It is very clean, well kept, and updated. The room was pretty large, with respect to other NYC rooms, and there was plenty of room to walk around comfortably. The front staff and doormen were friendly and very courteous. Overall, great experience. I will def make this my go-to hotel when I am back in the city.

“Great Boheme” Stayed here for 3 nights from May 22nd and it was fab from the start. We booked a double room and while it was small it was comfortable and spotless. We had a room at the back so we had less noise but more sleep and because it backed almost directly to the next building it did lack natural light and a view however it did not bother us because we didnt plan to spend all day looking out of our hotel window!! Staff were extremley friendly and helpful and the famous nightly sherry was great!! One downside is if youve got a few heavy suitcases the stairs up to the rooms could be a problem. Location for the hotel was the best. Smack bang in the middle of north beach with plenty of bars and restaurants close by and even though it was hilly both union square and fishermans wharf can be reached easily on foot. (Fishermans Wharf is a 10-15 minute walk). Around the hotel are numerous bars and restaurants and small cafes. Ones worth a visit; Tosca and Vesuvio both bars (5 minute walk towards union square) Marios bohemian cigar store is great for snacks and a drink opposite washington square (5 minutes towards fishermans wharf) and for a meal Trattoria Contadina, an italian, and Manga Rosa a steakhouse literally just around the corner are both great. One final tip is if your up to it hire a bike and ride across the Golden Gate bridge over to Sausolito. About a 10 mile ride on paths. We did a guided tour with Blazing Saddles and it was an experience we will never forget!! Dont worry about cycling back because you take the ferry!

“Snooze and Cruise (or fly)” Booked a Snooze and Cruise rate at the hotel website. I thought it was a pretty fair deal for a double queen room, ocean view at Casa Marina building. Although we paid for only 1 night, we got to leave our car in their covered garage for a week without nightly charges. Plus, their free shuttle van took us to the airport in the morning to catch our flight out to Hawaii. (If you are doing the Snooze and Cruise/Fly thing, also check out Humphrey's Half Moon Bay Inn which is located virtually next door to the Island Palms Hotel, and appears to be a sister hotel to this one. Humphrey's also has a similar Snooze and Cruise deal, although the price likely will be a little higher.) The room itself was very nice with reasonably updated furnishings. And the view from the second floor window and balcony was beautiful, overlooking the marina and the hills of Point Loma. After checking in in the afternoon, I spent a good hour sitting on the balcony, enjoying the view and taking advantage of the free wi-fi. Couldn't be more pleasant. The location on Shelter Island is central to a lot of San Diego, but not really walking distance to anywhere. So, don't stay here unless you have a car to get around. For a stay at a reasonably priced, clean and well maintained hotel before a cruise or flight out, you can't really beat this place. As an added plus, the front desk clerk was very friendly and seemed eager to be of service. Seems hard to believe, but too many "service industry" people don't seem to like to serve. Love to patronize those who still know what service means. I can highly recommend Best Western Plus Island Palms Hotel. If you have any reservations about a Best Western, don't hesitate to try this one. Definitely the nicest property carrying the Best Western designation I've run across.

“Très bien !” Proche de l'aéroport (10-15 minutes) et facile à trouver. Grande chambre à la décoration assez classique mais agréable (grand bureau avec fauteuil en cuir pour ceux qui souhaitent travailler), lit king size, sale de bain assez petite, calme, très propre, petit déjeuner copieux et bon (chaud et froid, même des yaourts, pas courant pour ce niveau de prix), 2 PC avec imprimantes à disposition. le tout pour 90 USD avec taxes, Je le conseille sans hésiter !

“Convenient Location, "interesting" Property” Decided to take a chance on a Bloomspot offer for three nights at thie 'boutique' Times Square hotel, though the offer turned out not to be that much better than booking directly. The property itself is definitely different from most Times Square or mid town hotels, with a small one person reception desk at the end of a narrow lobby and tow adjacent buildings with the rooms. The building my room was in required one steep flight of exterior stairs and another narrow curvy flight of internal stairs. Quaint like a an old New Orleans apt but not at all accessible. The room was a decent size for NYC with an exposed brick wall and fireplace facade. The lighting was a problem with the only choice between very bright recessed overhead lights or a very dim desk lamp. No desk area for working but the bathroom was a good size shower.

“Very brand new feeling Westin” The Westin is located in the McNamara Terminal. The hotel has it's own entrance into the terminal which is nice if you are planning an early morning flight and want to camp out near the airport. Several really great things about the hotel. It is surprisingly quiet. Many people have commented on this, but I was somewhat skeptical. There is definitely hallway noise that comes from under the door; however, all airport noise and even noise from the large atrium is non-existent within the room. This was impressive because I had breakfast in the atrium and I could definitely hear planes taking off. I also liked how the hotel felt very clean and new. The TV was a large (46 inch) HD LCD, the bathroom was spotless, the carpet looked clean. Another thing that was helpful is that the hotel staff accommodated my early check-in so I didn't have to drag my luggage with me everywhere I went. Some of the things that I think the hotel could do to improve: the restaurant could be improved. It looks really nice and has a great setting, but the actual food is not great. The only other thing that was somewhat annoying. The hotel has a lounge for guests staying on the club floor, but the lounge is not open on the weekends. I think it would be nice if the lounge stayed open on the weekends too even if only to just have drinks available.

“Easy access to the metroplex, nice business trip hotel” This was a return trip to the Embassy Suites Dallas Love Field. The hotel is in a nice residential area & has good restaurants nearby. It is also very close to Love Field airport, and all the major highways you'll need to get around the metroplex. The hotel is nice and parts of it have been updated. There's a very good complimentary breakfast in the morning, as well. Not a fancy hotel or one I'd probably stay in for a vacation, but a great business trip stay.

“また泊まりたいです” 決してゴージャスなホテルではありませんが、 まず、全て日本語で対応出来るのが最大のポイント だと思います。 お部屋は普通ですが、バスルームは広くてゆったり としていました。これにはびっくりしました。 またホテルの向かい側には定食屋さんやラーメン屋さん もあり、食べるのに不便しませんでしたし、リトル東京 のアーケード内に日系スーパーもあるので、ちょっと した買い物に便利です。

“This is the coolest hotel I have ever stayed in.” This is not your hotel if you want luxury treatment and endless amenities. But if you want something unique with a taste of rock'n'roll, there is no better place!!! A stay at the Chelsea is a MUST! Okay, $200 plus tax for a shared bathroom is maybe not very cheap, but the Chelsea experience weighs it all off. Lots of art in the building, great people, superb and friendly staff, a room that just rocks - honestly, no need to complain about having to cross the hall for a shower. I stayed at the Chelsea for one night after a week of business meetings and have to say: Chelsea Hotel rocks!

“Great hotel on a good location” I stayed here 6 nights because of a conference in the Convention center. The location is great, close to the convention center (20 minute walk) and the hotel is just like the other courtyards. I am not familair with the Courtyard brand but the WIFI is free of charge here which is not the same as in the Marriot chain. The people were friendly here and I even could book a 6th night altough upfront they told me the hotel was fully booked.

“Nice hotel, good location and value, mediocre breakfast, slow elevator” Stayed here over Labor Day. Nice, well-maintained, fairly new hotel with a good location near Times Square. Great value at $153 a night, I thought, though the advertised queen beds were smaller than a full. Main drawback was very slow elevators and a mediocre breakfast (which was free, so it's hard to complain too much). Rooms were small but well decorated and maintained-very clean. Friendly staff.

“Exceptional staff; terrific accommodation, as always.” We are Fairmont Premier guests, and actually go out of our way to stay at Fairmont properties-- which we do at least 5 times a year. The Copley is among our favourites!This is the 2nd time we stayed at this hotel. In fact, this time was a bit of a "destination," as we loved it so much last time we looked for an excuse to visit Boston. We only stayed one night, on our way to Martha's Vineyard, but we were given a fantastic upgrade. The room was spacious and clean, and while a little bit dated, they do their best to make the decor reflect the time of the building. The staff here is so professional and pleasing, always friendly and professional without being obsequious. Most importantly, it is probably the single most dog-friendly hotel we've ever stayed at-- and we travel with our Labrador all the time-- which is one of the reasons we love Fairmont. We had friends staying there with us as well, as a surprise party for my husband. It was an ideal location and destination for a high-end party! Our only major disappointment is that they renovated the Oak Room Bar. It was the most beautiful, splendid bar, reflective of another place in time. It was dark and cozy, with small tables throughout and a joy to sit and talk in. Now, it's large and open and bright and trendy. The service and the drinks are still excellent, but the new modern feel broke our hearts )-:

“first class” I thought this hotel was rated as a 4 star,but it was in my opinion considerably better than that. They do nearly everything right from opening your door to giving rides in the property limo if it is not in use. It does not have a porte cochere at the entrance. I know this is LA but I found this strange. Only noticed because it was raining when I arrived. Of course they don't need one since the valet immediately came out with umbrella in hand ready to fend off any of the unusual bits of water falling from the sky. I see a few negative comments on the rooms. I must have been given a renovated room as the descriptions don't match what I found. I would never pay five fifty for the room but at one thirty on hotwire, it is a serious bargain. I was a bit uncomfortable mixing with the predominantly vainglorious clientele. I felt like I need to have a jacket just to go to the pool. I am sure I was uncomfortable simply being outclassed. Speaking of the pool. this is a very nice outdoor area with cabanas and a large pool suitable for short laps. You will find everything you need here in the well-appointed/maintained rooms including excellent robes. Because this hotel seemed to serve wealthy clientele you can expect everything to cost a fortune from the internet to the parking. the restaurant and bar menu is good and not too highly priced however the dishes seem to be all tapas; but you can't tell that form the descriptions. You only know that when the miniature portion arrives. Eventually I became so hungry after the third day working from the food deficit that I asked the restaurant waiter if they could serve a larger portion, which he happily did. The bar is hit or miss depending on the bartender on duty. If you see a young guy there, expect to wait a bit and explain simple terms like what "neat" means or put up with ice in your whiskey. The business center will do anything form you; again, it will cost you. Property is first class, but you so must you be or you will feel uncomfortable. They can and will do anything to help you, but it will cost you. Do not pay rack rate. You can Hotwire this hotel for one hundred thirty at times. If you don't use Hotwire you should check it out - they give you satisfaction ratings which make it better, (athough a bit higher priced), than priceline. Within (long) walking distance of the Westfield mall with good restaurants or ask for a ride in the hotel vehicle to nearby spots.
“Pretty good stay at Indigo” An extremely cute place. Good value if you can find a rate under $100. Air conditioner loud in room but created a constant noise for me, which I liked. Would stay again.

“A superlative hotel experience!!” I recently stayed at this hotel, and must say that I`m somewhat dismayed by the negative comments about this property. I travel often and was delighted to find that this was one of the finest hotel experiences I`ve ever encountered. Most of the bad comments on this sight are about the hotel`s massive size and the throngs of people. It is no secret that this is a huge business and convention oriented hotel, so a few minutes of research on the net or in the travel section of a local bookstore would inform a prospective client of that infomation. The hotel is ideally located and is central to all that Chicago has to offer to tourists or business people alike. The spectacular multileveled greenhouse style lobby bustles with activity and is enhanced by lush foliage,flowers and dancing fountains. Realizing that this was such a large hotel, I immediately joined the Hyatt frequent guest program. This offers the distinct advantage of a separate check in area, so long lines can be avoided. Also, room upgrades and late check out are additional benefits. Membership is free. I arrived several hours before the actual check in time of 3:00pm. I had reserved a room at a special winter rate, through Hyatt, of $87.20. A great deal! I was immediately upgraded to a room on the 28th floor with an unbelivable view of The Chicago River, Lake Michigan, The Wrigley Building and The Magnificent Mile. The spacious room was stylish,contemporary and immaculately maintained. The large amenity laden bathroom sparkled. All hotel staff that I encountered were, without exception, courteous, amiable,and helpful, even when just simply passing them in a hallway. Those who prefer a small,slow-paced boutique style hotel should look elsewhere. If you`re coming to the big city to experience the excitement, glamour, and energy of it all, this is where you need to be.

“Good rooms, disorganized restaurant” Stayed here one night on business. Rooms are medium sized and well appointed, including a built-in PC. LIghting above average. The room was quiet except for the occasional passing siren (Philadelphia seems to have lots of sirens). Good hot water supply and comfortable beds. Maintenance seemed good but not immaculate. Downsides: the staff seem more obtrusive than in most hotels -- there always seemed to be people with large carts in the halls and elevators. Housekeeping knocked on my door quite early, even though I had not picked up the paper just outside. Breakfast in the restaurant was decent, but the staff seemed shorthanded, disorganized, and overwhelmed. In the morning, the lobby was very crowded, mostly with people with very large backpacks. Overall, I would recommend it, but avoid the restaurant. There are many restaurants and cafes in the immediate area.

“Another great Hampton Inn!” I love Hampton Inns and this one was no different! Excellent spacious and clean rooms. Brilliant free breakfast and all in the perfect location for exploring Chicago. The front desk staff were friendly and made some good suggestions for eating/sightseeing. Although my room was overlooking the fire station, I think I heard one engine leave during the 3 nights I was there.

“Good value” I stayed at this Holiday Inn for one night. My family checked in together for a long layover before leaving that night. The hotel is clean and very convenient because of its proximity to the airport (though not in the walking distance). The free shuttle service is shared by Westin and La Quinta, so the wait between shuttles is 20 minutes or a bit longer. I saw a long line for checking in in the evening. The free wifi internet was fast. Overall, I would definitely stay here again, considering that I had to go through urine smell in my earlier stay at the neighboring Westin (to be fair, that was back in 2001).

“Very close to DFW!” This is definetly a nice place......and being newly renovated is a great thing. LOCATION- If you need a hotel near DFW Airport, this is your place. You can't get much closer. It's possible to walk, but the easier solution is the quick shuttle ride. We waited less than 10 minutes before we were at the hotel. (Please note that the GRAND HYATT DFW, also at the airport is on the airport train route and even easier). However, f you have business outside of the airport this would be a very awkward location. SERVICE- Very professional and crisp looking staff. You definetly feel like you are in an upper-tier hotel. However, I think I may have caught them on a bad night when they were very full. There was quite a line at the front desk. And when I called both the phone operator with a question and room service, I had to wait quite a while before someone answered. However I must say, everyone was very friendly and professional. ROOMS- Absolutely beautiful. One of the prettiest and most lush "chain" hotel rooms I have been in. I was very impressed. Very modern, but also warm at the same time. I think have have done up Marriott as far as the level of luxury. Gorgeous color scheme and a huge plasma tv. The bathroom was equally impressivve with beautiful tile work and lovely amenities. Only two small negatives: The towel quality did however seem a bit chincy (too thin) for such a nice room. Also, the bathroom lighting was a bit harsh. BAR- I didn't have time to stop in, but there was a lobby bar that was hopping for sure. It was gorgeously decorated and looked like fun! For an airport hotel, this place is great. Certainly not cheap but you are getting a very nice room.

“Gutes Hotel in ausgezeichneter Lage” Das Comfort Inn besticht durch die Lage. Wir haben hier zwei Nächte verbracht. Im Hotelpreis inkludiert ist ein Frühstück, nicht jedoch der Parkplatz, der extra kostet ($ 16,--). Die Nähe zum Gas Lamp Quarter ist äusserst vorteilhaft, zahlreiche Lokale befinden sich in der Nähe. Die Zimmer selbst sind nett, sauber und ausreichend gross, auch ein Safe ist vorhanden.

“Great Seattle Hotel” My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights at the end of September. I chose this hotel due to it's good reviews and the close proximity to downtown sights. The hotel is only 3 blocks from Pike Place Market and only a couple blocks more to the waterfront. We stayed in a Deluxe Queen room and couldn't have been happier. Our room was large with a separate bedroom, living room and bathroom. Our room was a 9th floor corner room and it was very quiet, we did not hear anything either inside or outside of the hotel. The hotel is also one block from the entrance to the light rail tunnel and we took the light rail train to the airport as it was only $2.50 per person VS $40 by taxi. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful and it was an overall great stay.

“Wonderful Hotel” I was in town for a major convention, and initially stayed at the Sheraton Hotel & Towers downtown, which, until this visit, was one of my favorite hotels to stay at in Chicago (separate review). I spent my last evening staying at the Westin. This hotel was absolutely wonderful! The staff at the front desk was very welcoming. The room was beautiful and clean and quiet. I was given a corner room with a great view of the river and the city. I can't say enough nice things about this property. I wish I could have stayed longer. I will definitely be back!

“This hotel understands group travel” Recently stayed at the property with a 50 person group. The staff and group director were all very attentive to the needs of the group and were willing to change arrangements on short notice. There are a number of good dining options in the arboretum area. This hotel is situated close to the arboretum but far enough to avoid the traffic issues. The buildings are in need of a renovation soon, but commendations to the staff and management on making the best of what they have. The rooms were clean and the bedding was updated. Some of the common areas just have a older look about them, but it's no reason to avoid the hotel. I would give this hotel a 3.5 if that was an option.

“Worst hotel I've been in years” The only good thing about the hotel is the location. I paid over 350 dollars per night, and got an old room, with a bathroom that was ridiculously small. I asked to change rooms and got another one with an even smaller bathroom (I am talking small that I don't entirely fit in the shower, and I am not a big person). The service was terrible. Staff very unprofessional (the person they sent to help me to change rooms, after 3 attempts to send one, was literally burping while walking me to the next room, unbelievable). Would not recommend this place to anybody, extremely expensive, old and bad service.

“Good value new hotel” Stayed here for 5 night while attending the conference downtown. Had own rental car, which is required, since hotel is located off I35, with no public transport around, and 6 miles from downtown. Nice new hotel with standard Hampton service, decent speed free internet and free parking and breakfast. Very clean and up-to-date. My only remark goes to housekeeping, that is not always doing required job to the standard - my sheets were not exchanged during 5 days, and the bed was not made very well on four out of five days. Also, AC can be rather loud, and walls are very thin, but I guess that there is nothing hotel can do about now...

“Everything that one would expect for a Westin” This is the 2nd if 3 hotels that I stayed in during my 1 week stay in San Francisco for memorial day weekend. Great location, nice rooms and amenities and exceptional service. Everything was within walking distance - dining, shopping, conference facilities (moscone convention center very near), public transportation. The staff was very helpful and we felt welcome during the whole stay. Would definitely choose this hotel the next time I am in town.

“Great hotel in a great location” I just spent the weekend at the Shoreham Hotel in NYC. It was my first time staying at this property and I was a little bit nervous based on some of the past reviews. I think that it is tough to impress me but this hotel did. What I really liked about this hotel is that they don't "nickel and dime" you, free wifi, free use of business center computers and printer, free coffee, tea, espresso (self serve) and free champagne at check in. The room that I had was nicely designed, clean and quiet. It is true that the hotel is starting to look a little tired, but all the positives far out weighted the some what tired design (subjective). Some people might find the room layout a little quirky, it is not a Marriott, it is more like a european hotel. The location can't be beat, you can walk to everything!

“Great place, one small complaint” We stayed at the Hotel Monaco to treat ourselves to a night away, and also to be able to bring our dog with us. A few of the nice touches: our dog's name on a whiteboard by the entrance, where there was also dog food and water, and the staff manning the door remembered the dog's name for the length of our visit. it was also nice to be able to have the dog with us duirng the wine hour, which was fun. We had a King Deluxe room (no other 'cheaper' rooms were available) which was a nice size, nice bathroom. My complaint is that the room was very very dark, and every window looked across a rooftop to another window. there was one window (behind the TV) where, if I leaned just right, I could see the street (and sun).. I wanted to leave the curtains open, but wasn't sure what, or who, was behind the other windows (some of them were alos part ot the Hotel Monaco), so, kept them closed a lot. but i am definitely one who likes having the sun come in, and would have really liked to have a view. But, we were in the room more at night than during the day anyway, and the staff was very friendly and nice, and I liked the vibe, and location, of the hotel, so all in all, it was a nice stay.

“Great value and location” It's right beside Southpark Mall and several great restaurants. Rooms are huge, clean, and comfortable. Staff is friendly. Breakfast is okay. I was in town on short notice and they were very helpful and accomodating- free toothbrush! I'll be back.

“fine for a night at the airport” After missing a connection on the last flight of the night, I was on my own for hotel accomodations at IAH (the new reality of air travel if it's "weather" that causes you to miss your connection). The "distressed passenger" rates that Continental's service was willing to find me seemed pricey for Houston, which usually has reasonable hotel prices. So I fired up the laptop and made a last-minute priceline bid: I got this Marriott for $40 as a 3-star. It took about 15 minutes for the shuttle to come, and then another 20 minutes to reach the hotel. For an "airport hotel," it's pretty far from the airport. But the driver was very friendly and plied us with bottled water and candy. So hard to complain. Check-in was also quite friendly. Rooms were what you'd expect from a "typical" Marriott -- which means they were more than adequate. Our return trip the next morning to the airport was prompt and efficient (which is more than I can say for security, which was a madhouse). I didn't realize we were in a "dangerous" part of town, and I guess most other short-staying guests would have the same experience. The hotel itself felt quite safe. Given the apparent problems with the area, I'm sure I'd choose to stay elsewhere for a longer visit, but if you just need a night near the airport, this property is more than acceptable if you get a cheap rate.

“Good Location, Older "Historic" Hotel” We decided upon the Congress as we had a problem with a previous reservation at another hotel and had to make a last minute selection on a very busy convention weekend. We chose the Congress based upon location and comments that the hotel was clean, which it was and knew it was going to be older. We used the bellman to check our bags prior to check-in and all the staff was quite friendly. After our return later that afternoon they were able to put us into a King room which was not available when we originally made our reservation. The room was large enough and had the traditional high ceilings with a building of this age. The rooms are dated however clean and again, not bad considering almost the entire downtown was sold out. If I had paid the $220+ any other time I would not have been pleased. We did not dine at the hotel but did visit the cocktail lounge on Saturday evening and the one bartender on staff was overwhelmed with the amount of guests trying to get service. I continued to expect help to arrive but it didn't happen and we eventually left and dined and enjoyed cocktails elsewhere. Checked back into the lounge Sunday afternoon and same thing/same gal, lots of guests waiting and slow service. We again opted to dine and drink elsewhere. Yes, the hotel is aged and shows it, but the location is great (across from the park and lake) and there is something to be said for that historic feel at times. Would probably make another choice next trip but in a pinch this worked.

“Still One of the Best Values in the Neighborhood” This hotel is very simple, clean and absolutely worth the price. We have family living nearby, and we have stayed here many times. It is totally safe, with excellent service, new flat screen TV's, free parking, comfortable beds and plenty of closet and drawer space. The pillows could be more comfortable, the soap is teeny, the towels are small as well, but these are minor issues. The pool is small and unheated, but little kids will enjoy it in very hot weather -- there is rarely anyone in the pool. And getting any kind of pool at these prices is a great deal. You are walking distance to all the fun of the Grove and the Farmer's Market. The restaurant downstairs, Fiddler's Cafe, is a great spot with fair prices and good food. You can wander through Pan Pacific Park, walk further to the Tar Pits Museum and LACMA, drive up through the Hollywood Hills to Runyan Canyon Park and hike with the aspiring actors. It's a great location to explore LA on a budget.

“nice place to stay if you are visiting multiple places” We stayed in this particular hotel for three nights based on trip advisor reviews. It is an airport hotel so has that airport feel about it and the other guests. Check in was well organised and exceptionally friendly. It is a standard Staybridge layout/design with the rooms and common areas all well maintained and clean. The room has the standard kitchen configuration with the usual crockery and kitchen utensils. The amenities are all very good and the hotel is well laid out. The gym has no free weights which was the only disappointment. The breakfast is standard bacon, sausage, omelette, cereal, yoghurt, fresh fruit etc. There is plenty of seating for the number of guests using it. We used the laundry facilities here which are complimentary and suitable for a big load of washing. Check out was easy and again the staff nice and friendly.

“2nd time around” this was my second trip to this wonderful hotel. i am only giving it 4 stars this time because i had a larger room the 1st time around. the hotel room was extremely clean and roomy(the 1st time i was there i had a walk in closet.) i am not sure if we received a nice box of godiva chocolates because we were return clients or because everyone gets this. i loved the ammenities also. the location is absolutely the best in nyc because the location is out of the major walking traffic,yet very close to the action. i would stay there again and again.love this place

“Behemoth Hotel” This hotel is a behemoth and its lobby is very busy. When you get beyond that and go to your room the pace does slow down. Get an updated room they are finished nicely, spacious and bed was very comfortable. The hotel is located a couple of blocks away from Union Square but if you go a block or two towards City Hall the area becomes very run down and shady be careful!!! The Urban Table located in the lobby is great for drinks. Over all very good.

“Still .. better than the Hilton” We spent one night here, in transit to Hawaii. Last time we were at the Hilton and found it pretty insignificant. The Westin is a pretty good hotel, clean, good beds, they have a restaurant inside, airport shuttle, quiet area. Not spectacular, but pretty good for an airport hotel. We used the pool to cool off after 10 hours of airplanes, they have a small clean pool and a small hot tub - exactly what we needed and expected. However the greeting at check in was well below average, also the guy before us received the same treatment (the man at the desk whispered questions and seemed annoyed that nobody could understand what he was muttering, and gave me informations regarding the pool only upon specific question: is it outside? Yes (silence). Do you offer towels? Yes (silence). Where is the pool? Third floor (silence) - he seemed happy when we finally went away. Also, when we asked for a car/ prices to go downtown the concierge managed to get us the most expensive transportation mean he could - at his benefit I assume - we spent 70 dollars to the destination, and 35 on the way back (the restaurant called a taxi for us). Generally my reviews aren't filled with these silly details, but I wanted to explain what annoyed me about the hotel - there are many spectacular reviews I don't really agree with - but maybe we just found the wrong people. And it was a one night stay so take the info for what they are.

“Friendly staff, clean rooms & great location” We stayed one night at this hotel - July 23, 2009. This wasn't our first stay (see our previous review for our Mar 2007 stay). We were attending an Eddie Izzard performance at the Orpheum Theatre and the Hilton Suites is about 2 miles from there. The check-in staff was friendly and informative. They offer shuttle service within 2 miles of the hotel but it stops at 10PM so we couldn't take advantage of it to go to the Orpheum. Parking is $11 a day. They share a parking garage with the plaza next door but the garage is very close and accessible. We preferred parking there because it was under cover and we didn't want to leave our car in the 108 degree heat. Our room was on the 11th floor. This is an all-suites hotel so each room has a separate bedroom, living room and a pass-through bathroom. There's also a desk with internet connections. We also had a wet-bar with coffeemaker and single-packet ground coffee, tea and sugar/cream packs. We had a small microwave and fridge. There wasn't a mini-bar in this room. Our room also had flat-screen TVs in both the bedroom and living room. Our king-size bed was the most comfortable hotel bed I've ever slept in! The sheets were clean and crisp and the bed was just the right firmness. Generally, this was one of the cleanest hotel rooms I've ever stayed in as well. The hotel restaurant is located in the center atrium. We had dinner there. Overall, they had a good selection and our pasta dishes were tasty but our garden salads look like they had been sitting inside the fridge way too long. At check-in we were also given vouchers for free breakfast buffet. That was okay. The selection was small - the hot selections included scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage, french toast, pancakes and oatmeal. There was also made-to-order omelets and cereal and pastries. Very little fruit was offered though. If you aren't given free breakfast vouchers, the cost would be around $12.00 per person. The location of this hotel is near several large corporate buildings so there are quite a lot of business people staying here. During our stay, we didn't see any large groups of of kids or young people and we didn't experience any loud or boisterous parties. We would definitely stay here again if we are ever in Phoenix to attend a nearby performance.

“Great Home Away from Home” We live in Dallas and had to move out of our house while part of the remodeling was going on. We stayed at the hotel for about ten days a year ago, and then returned recently for a short stay while the AC in our highrise was out. We looked at several suite hotel properties and chose this one as most upscale room for the price. While the bedroom is very tight on space, it works as the sleeping quarters with great bed and linens. There is a door from the bedroom to the bath and also a door from the living room to the bath which makes for a convenient flow for two people getting ready for work or business. While most of the furnishings are basic, they are well appointed and very functional. Our only wish was that the room had had a DVD player. We brought our own and it was easy to connect to the plasma TVs. Parking is easy. Location is great if you are doing business at Market and/or downtown. Front Desk staff is very friendly and helpful. They worked with us on rate since we were going to be there for awhile. We could have used this room for a month to homebase out of if we had needed to, even though it was not extremely large.

“Albergo da consigliare” La zona dove è situato l' albergo noon può essere migliore, in pieno centro di manhattan, a due passi da lla metropolitana, da Times Square e da tutte la attrazioni tipiche e le vie dello shopping. Consigliato quindi sia a chi va per lavoro sia a chi va per diletto. Consiglio di evitare la colazione, perchè anche se è molto ricca e abbondante costa davvero troppo.

“Nice rooms and conveinent location to the Dallas Market Center” Perfect location if you have business at the Dallas Market Center, not much else around. Hotel was nice and clean, staff very helpful. The one big complaint was very thin walls -- could hear everything that was happening in the room next door.

“Good Times” The Tremont Hotel is an independent hotel in the Starwood chain. My expectations were low considering the negative reviews. We were completely satisfied. PERFECT location. The rooms were clean. They were older, and they could use an update, but in a way that would take away from the “old Chicago” feel you have when you are there and I am sure raise the price. The lobby is very welcoming. Re: the strong potpourri scent, we were there after Christmas, so there were Christmas scented candles burning and I thought it was nice. I don’t know what it usually smells like. The rooms were very warm and large enough for both of us. We slept great on the bed and I LOVED that the windows open -- it was a little warm one day, so there you go. You can tell that once upon a time the bathroom was state of the art, but is much older now. All the fixtures (faucets, lights, etc.) are strange, but functional. We split our stay – first two nights at The Tremont (on Chestnut Street) and last two nights at The Blackstone (S. Michigan Avenue). Although both were downtown, I much prefer the location of The Tremont. There was such a terrific feel to the blocks surrounding The Tremont, and so much to do/see at any time of the day/night. Bonus - there is a Starbucks right across the street and a 24 hour breakfast place at a corner about a block away. The front desk let me check out late with no problem and it was super quick when I did. The elevator is old and slow, but we never had to wait for it, and we were on the 14th floor, room 1405. The price is unbeatable and we had a very nice stay, so I would stay here again without hesitation.

“Average Convention Hotel - Edge of Downtown” Generally a typical Sheraton hotel. I had a room on the corner of the hotel which looking at the map was the smallest room they had available. The staff were friendly. It seems like it's on the edge of the downtown area but you can walk a few blocks and feel like you are back in the downtown area of town.

“Great relaxing stay at this boutique style hotel” Came here on a short romantic break to Philly with my wife. The hotel is very well located in the heart of downtown and close to all the shops and action. It's very stylishly and uniquely decorated and despite being a chain has a boutique feel (loved the wood floors and paintings in the elevators). My Wife told them it was my birthday when she made the booking and they said they would do something 'special'....they didn't. A couple of other annoyances: the mini bar was locked but they didn't give us a key (we had to call down) and there was not an ice machine on every floor ... we had to go to the fitness center on the 4th floor for this (we were on floor 23!). The room was nice, ok size and the bed very comfy. It was expensive and we were a little disappointed we didn't get one of the full size baths. The view was great however. They had a running map of the city with routes leading from the hotel to other parts of the city, including mileage...which was a geat touch and which we used. The fitness center seemed very well equipped. At 6:00pm we went down for free wine and popcorn in reception...the wine was good and you could have as many glasses as you liked! We ate at the restaurant and were not at all impressed..and the bar is just OK. Overall a great stay in an historic and beautiful building.

“Excellent Service and quality” I stayed at the Four Seasons in San Francisco for two nights this week and had an excellent experience. The bed was comfortable and the sheets were nice. The room was larger than I expected and had a great view of Market STreet. The breakfast I ordered was probably one of the best room service meals I've ever had and the staff was great. One of the bonuses of this hotel is access to the LA Fitness in the building which is an excellent workout center. The hotel is in a great location to reach all the shopping in Union Square. There were free coffee and mini-muffins (if you woke up early enough to get them before they were gone) in the lobby and free newspapers (WSJ and FT), as well. I'll definitely stay at this place again.

“If we're back in SF and need a place to stay, we'll look at the Argonaut Hotel.” Fisherman's Wharf might be a cheesy and touristy spot, but the Argonaut Hotel is in a great location adjacent to Ghiradelli Square and the Powell-Hyde cable car line. I was out in SF for a one day meeting at the hotel and brought my family along and extended my stay. Major SF Muni bus lines are near by and getting around town was fairly painless. Hotel staff was friendly and helpful - in particular, they were great with my kids. The hotel has an afternoon happy hour (drinks for adults and treats for kids) which offered a nice segue to dinner and other evening plans. There was also a Wii in the hotel lobby for the kids. Our room was spacious and the internet is free if you sign up for the Kimpton loyalty program. We only had breakfast at the hotel restaurant, the Blue Mermaid, and it was good comparatively speaking. All things considered, if you can get a "decent" rate, the Argonaut is a solid bet.

“the negative reviews were right on” From an unfriendly welcome, to paint peeling in the halls, to a noisy room, (broken air conditioner, raucous bar in the building behind us), and to a dilapidated although free computer room, the independent was a disappointment on almost all counts. Their one saving grace is they did allow us to bring our dog when our dog sitter bailed on us at the last minute, and (I guess that is two saving graces) when we complained about our room they moved us to another - although very dark, and poorly lit, it was well appointed. We travel a lot (from upscale, to b&b, to Motel 6 when we are visiting in the Southwest) and this was on a par with a two star hotel. We definitely did not get what we paid for.

“Old school luxury with a view” While the gold and marble aren't really my style, I certainly appreciated the incredible bathroom with a large shower and separate bathtub. The view from my room spanning from the Golden Gate Bridge to Alacatraz and Coit Tower was breathtaking. The bed linens were soft and luxurious. The only downfall was they only had down pillows which are hard for me to sleep on. Everything else was great.

“Highly recommended!” An extremely nice hotel, very close to the convention center and most major attractions. Cozy, quiet, and inviting, you can't go wrong. The staff needs to be a bit more attentive. Morning breakfast was handled by one person who seemed totally overwhelmed. I was given two restaurant recommendations, and both were closed for renovation. I found out after I arrived at them. Big bummer. They hit me with a $35 fee for not returning my key, even though I returned my key upon checkout. They did remove the charge after I called, but it shouldn't hinge on weather or not the front desk staff remembers to mark you down as returned. I would still strongly recommend this hotel.

“Great service, nice rooms, & wonderful location” From the moment I stepped from the cab Luis made sure to get my heavy bags from the trunk and whisk them to the second floor lobby. I was nervous as it was not even 10:00 a.m. and after a long train ride I was ready for a shower but concerned I may not be able to get into my room until hours later. Within minutes I was being whisked away with Luis on the elevator with the hotel key in hand. Glorious. The room with double beds was immaculate, cozy and comfortable. The huge windows allowed much light and great views of the city. A fun touch was the large "rain" shower that had a huge pane of glass with views of the room and beyond. Not sure how practical that was, as the office building next door probably could get an eyeful if the windows weren't tainted or the blinds closed. Anyway, the room had great little toiletries, thick ample towels, luxurious bedding, and keurig coffee maker. I had some special requests, and the staff didn't blink, providing me with exceptional service. The location was perfect, besides being minutes from the mag mile, there was a CVS, a Starbucks and a WholeFoods just steps from the hotel. Very convenient to pick up items forgotten, or some fresh fruit and coffee. Dana Hotel was definitely a hidden Chicago gem that I would return to in a heart beat.

“Still the same great stay.” I stayed at this hotel back in 2008. I stayed here again in Oct.15-17 and it was the same great place that I remembered. I again got a bunk bed room with the added bonus of a private shower. It's nearby lots of places to eat, bank, & shop! Very convenient! I will stay here again! :)

“Love love love the Palomar. You will too.” Returned for an evening. Comfortable, quiet room with HUGE, tall shower and the usual amenities. Doormen super-friendly and helpful. Great bar. What's not to like? OK, breakfast at Sable isn't stellar, but just hop over to Weber Grill across the street. This hotel is the place to stay in Chicago.

“FABULOUS VALUE” Stayed here during a 1.5 week stay with friends. First time here, but got a great deal on hotwire which I couldn't pass up. Long and short it was fantastic and an excellent value. The suites are large, beds and sheets are very comfortable, location is excellent, service was great, free internet in lobby and restaurant area, very secure. The hotel lobby isn't as large or elaborate as the Marriott, Westin, etc but I would certainly stay here again as it was a great value. The same quality as the higher end brands, but I paid half the price. Hard to find value hotels in a popular location in NYC. Will definitely stay here again when I go back in the fall.

“A lot of potential - but needs some work” We got a fantastic rate on this property, and were given a fantastic room on the top floor with a great view. At the start, that would have been enough. However, a few too many things fell short. (1) We parked across the way at JFK Plaza (which is $20 a day self-park and only $8.50 a day on weekends. When we got to the front door, the doormen stood there as we struggled to open and close the door ourselves. Every other time, in and out, with no bags, they had no problem opening the door. (2) WATER ISSUES. The water stopped working altogether in the middle of our 2 night stay. It was out for over an hour, we were told it the hotel was having pressure issues. 5 hours later, we had no hot water. The next morning, we had hot water but the water in the room was still cloudy and very odd looking. This never happened to us at any hotel in Philadelphia before (we have stayed at Loews, Marriott, Sofitel, Westin among others). (3) Housekeeping: they replaced towels, but never made our bed. We wound up just using it as it was, but this was quite strange and unexpected. (4) Location: We know Philadelphia very well. This location is fine by day. At night, unfortunately, the area right around this hotel does not have the most pleasant feel. This is not the greatest area for walking around after dark - our guess is that will change in the next few years, but for now the location is not as good as many other properties. All in all, even for a fantastic price I would still opt for one of the other properties listed above. I like the location benefits and we experienced better service at all of them.

“Ausreichend” Wir haben im November 5 Nächte in diesem Hotel verbracht. Das Hotel an sich (vor mehreren Jahren fanden hier die Oscar-Verleihungen statt) ist bewundernswert, wie innen sowie von aussen. Jedoch sind die Zimmer sehr alt und schon lange nicht mehr auf dem Niveau eines 5-Sterne-Hotels. Wir hatten ein Doppelzimmer gebucht. Alles sehr einfach eingerichtet. Das Badzimmer hätte auch eine Renovation nötig. Da wir einen Mietwagen hatten, hat es uns nicht gestört, dass das Hotel im Downtown war. Mein Tipp für einen LA-Besuch: Am besten ein Hotel in Beverly-Hills oder Hollywood buchen. Achtung: Parking im Hotel selber sehr teuer, 40 USD. Gegenüber (ich glaube Pershing Square) gibt es ein günstigeres Parkhaus für 15 USD.

“Walk in closet” The smallest room I ever stayed in. So small the tv was placed on a stripper pole at the base of the bed. The bathroom was a joke. I had to step outside the bathroom to put my close on. My car had more room in the garage than we did and was much cheaper than our room.

“Worthy of its lofty ranking” The Conrad is among the best hotels in Chicago and with some minor tweaking could be the very best value in town, if not the top-ranked property. We did encounter some minor problems with staff, as noted by other reviewers. Upon checking in, we were sent to an occupied room. The front desk clerk simply wrote the wrong room on our key envelope (1211 vs 1112, I think) and it was a simple mistake. The guest already in the occupied room was good humored about it, luckily! I also found the concierge to be quite aloof and would agree with other postings about the Terrace restaurant. The one time we went out to have a drink, I felt like we were intruding. Finally, there are noise issues between rooms. Twice we had to call security in the middle of the night because folks from the wedding party next door were still in a mood to celebrate! :-( HOWEVER, a couple of little issues can't take away from the fact that the hotel is gorgeous. Beautiful marble lobby, quick connections to the mall and street (albeit with a bad two-elevator system), perfect Chicago location and stunning guest rooms. Our bathroom was huge and very clean, the bed was comfortable and we really liked the plasma TV with Bose sound system (which may be one reason the TV next door was so loud at times). Overall, would stay at the Conrad again and would recommend it to friends.

“great rooms; nice staff” I recently attended a conference at the Sheraton Boston. I forgot how much I like that hotel. The rooms are comfortable and clean, and all the staff - from the doorman to housekeeping to the front desk - make you feel welcomed. Even the banquet food was fine (no "rubber chicken"). But I do have 2 small complaints. One is that the service in the restaurant at lunchtime was extremely slow. The food was great, but it really seemed that neither the waitstaff nor the kitchen was prepared for lots of guests before the start of a conference. The other is that I don't understand why if there is free internet access in the lobby there is not free internet access in the rooms.

“Not bad...” The location is excellent, next to Northbridge Mall and a block from Michigan Avenue. Room was a little cramped and there are only two elevators in the hotel so waiting is par for the course. Breakfast was pretty good in terms of selection. Only valet parking is available at the hotel. A half block north is self parking garage which is cheaper than valet. The hotel did not have the correct gift cards for our reservation but the manager appropriately resolved the issue to our satisfaction. Bathrooms showed a little wear. Overall, good choice for its location. Just don't expect the Ritz.

“Your best bet on the Upper East Side” Fantastic location, close to the museums and great shopping on Madison Ave. We encountered only the nicest service, from our telephone reservationist Patricia, to the front desk mgr. Channing. The bellman couldn't have been nicer. They took good care of our car and nothing was too much to ask. Rooms are lovely, clean and stylish. I love that they offer 24 hour room service. Bed and pillows SO comfy! Had a great nights sleep and the 77th Street view had minimal noise as opposed to a Madison Ave. room. The only reason I gave the hotel 4 stars instead of 5, is they had no docking station to charge our phone! Even the gal at the front desk said it was kind of odd in this day. We managed to survive the weekend without a phone, and they were willing to charge it for us at the front desk. Also we had some miserable stains on the rug in our room, but I guess that's life in a hotel! We will definitely return to this fine hotel, they couldn't have been nicer. Thank you!

“Nouveau hotel, big rooms, close to the Seaport and Brooklyn Bridge” With full disclosure, we live in NY (Long Island, actually), but stayed two nights here on Hyatt Points in order to go with out-of-town friends to a Yankee game and have dinner in the city. We liked this hotel, and ended up staying at another Andaz - in midtown - only two weeks later. The rooms are BIG by New York City standards. The Andaz "concept" has no check-in desk. Rather, you sit on lounge chairs in the lobby while someone offers you a beverage and does the checking-in for you. So, if you want traditional, you will be disappointed. Parking is in a neighboring garage, and the hotel will give you a receipt to get a discounted rate. I already mentioned the big rooms. Rooms also had nice big bathrooms, with two sinks, and those "Hyatt" showers and lighting. Bathrobes were in the room, and there was ample closer and drawer/shelf space. The only thing I really missed was a coffee maker. However, they had said that coffee was available in the lobby at night; I just never checked it out. We ate breakfast in the restaurant, which was pricey, and had a "German" flair to the menu. I didn't see that the hotel had a spa, which would have been nice, and it did not have a pool. But this hotel didn't really serve that purpose; it appeared to appeal more to business travelers. As the title stated, this hotel is walking distance to the Southstreet Seaport, where we had a wonderful dinner, Wall Street, and the Brooklyn Bridge (which we walked one morning). The subway is not far, and we took the train to Yankee Stadium. Andaz is a relatively new hotel concept by Hyatt. This hotel is new, very clean, and has big rooms. If you're looking to stay downtown, this is for you!

“Loved it! Great value” This hotel was perfect for my 6 day trip and the whole hotel just smells so good!, I loved my Club room on 16th floor, loved the breakfast and evening cocktails served in the Club room and loved the flavoured water in the lobby. I was travelling alone but visiting friends, originally I was a little worried that the location would be too far out for me as I was mainly in the Beverly Hills/West Hollywood area however it was fine. I had a car and the times I was travelling I experienced no traffic. It did not feel like an effort or too out the way at all. The room, bed, bathroom, and service were all perfect I have not a bad word to say. The wifi is free if you signed up to the select guest program which I recommend as its free to do so! Otherwise I think it is $15 per day. The valet parking is a little steep at $30 per night but I think that is pretty much the same for most LA hotels. It was a fantastic trip, great value for money and I would definitely stay again on future trips.

“Suprisingly good!” Thisd is one of those non-descript hotels near an airport. Presumably the only reason you are staying here is to catch an early flight or resting up after a long flight. We took the shuttle bus from the airport (called the hotel, and the shuttle arrived right on time); we checked in (the lobby was crowded with kids in Denver for a basketball tournement) and the room was fine -- and very quiet.
