No airplane noise. And no noise from the kids playing basketball! The breakfast was really quite good. And the ride back to the airport was efficient and on time. Overall -- it is a good deal!

“Nice place, but showing some wear” I was booked at the Fairmont for a conference. I saw the rate that our group paid and if I was traveling myself I would have paid that price. I was somewhat expecting a 4 star place that really shined, what I got was a 4 star place that shined, but was showing some wear. If you are a demanding traveler and expect the best, you might be dissapointed, if you get a a good deal through travelocity or expedia, etc, you might be very pleased here. It certainly was clean and the staff very friendly, expect for one of the female bartenders who can best be described as surly and slow. The drinks were overpriced anyway, so you are best to head out. There isn't much within an extremely close walking distance for bars and restaurants. There is a nice Thai place nearby. A Short walk to Georgetown and there are many nice places, or slightly farther to Dupont circle. The Metro is a decent walk away as well. The room was nice, but is ready for a makeover, could use new carpet, the TV seemed dated as well. Also, you can't watch TV and use the internet connection at the same time since the doors to the Armoir where the TV is store don't fold in. oh, make sure you join their President's club, it's free and you get free internet, otherwhise it is like $16 a day.

“Conveniently located inside airport, a little dated” Comfortable hotel, good for a day use (not bad at $139 plus tax), just inside the airport, corridors and public areas could use a litte refreshing. Wi-fi for free from neighboring ATT hub, air conditioning not working properly (not indispensable), single-glazing windows yet not noisy. Corteous staff.

“Nice Stay, but not many amenities” We were part of a group reservation. It was a nice stay. Staff was really nice. They addressed every thing we asked of them, and did it with a smile. This is an older property, and it could definitely use a renovation. But it was comfortable and clean. Its right next to the freeway, so its a bit noisy. Not in the best neighborhood, but we walked around with no issues. Its not really near much, so you have to walk a ways to get to the main activity areas, and restaurants. Little Italy seemed to be the closest area, and it was 5-6 blocks. You have to walk by some homeless people, which is a little disturbing, but they didn't bother us. The location is about 1-1.5 miles from all the activity down by the conference center/gas lap area The room itself was nice. Beds were comfortable. Nice crisp bedding (I like that). The bathroom had a tub/shower, toilet, and a sink with a nice size counter. There was a magnifying mirror that you could use, which was a nice touch. The towels were fluffy and smelled nice. There was a flat screen tv, which we didnt use. Nice dresser area with drawers to put clothes, also a armoir type unit with an area to hang clothes. I think there were 8 hangers in there. Only 2 plugs in the whole room, though, so bring a power strip. (we did). The carpets were a stained and could definitely use a deep cleaning or replacement. The interior halls of the hotel were kept warm and felt almost moist. Not sure what that was about - the rooms were fine. Each room has an easy to adjust thermostat, which was nice. Small restaurant downstairs didnt have much to choose from, but the prices were decent and the service good. No breakfast included here. Pool only, no jacuzzi. But the pool is quite warm. We heard its heated to 80 degrees. We were the only ones in there, so it was nice. Parking was $17 per day, not as steep as some other hotels in the area, but still a lot! What would I have liked? A bar area to sit and relax and talk to other guests (they do have a little seating area in the lobby), breakfast of some sort included, cheaper parking, and either a deep-clean or renovation. Room rates were high, and I dont think it was worth what we paid, but we did enjoy our stay.

“Average tourist-class hotel; very nice staff.” Stayed here on a 2-night business trip. The staff was very nice, friendly and helpful. The location is not great but alright. The room was quite small and hard to move around in, as others have said, but the bed was comfortable and everything was very clean. Noise problem with the air unit, but without it you hear everything in the rooms around you.

“Heaven!” I love this hotel and would stay her for fun but the reason I was here was business. This hotel has so many perks, nice rooms, amazing pool, great meeting space, right on the marina, quick walk into seaport village, quick walk to the ferry to coronado island, quick walk into the gaslamp district. I mean what more can you ask for the San Diego! I highly suggest concierge upgrade for the breakfast which is amazing and marina view rooms are to die for.

“Absolutely Fine, superb Upper West Side location” Our family of four (ages 17 and 11) stayed at Lucerne on a Friday night, January 2005. This hotel is absolutely fine. The room with two doubles was a little snug (we were four after all) but most rooms in NYC are not spacious. Everything was clean and the hotel staff was very accommodating. The location for the Upper West Side is superb. The UWS is a great place to walk (and this hotel is very near Museum of Natural History) and has great eateries. And you don't have to spend a fortune to eat in NYC. For example, there are several "upper crust" places for breakfast, brunch, etc. such as Sarabeth's and Good Enough to Eat. But, just a block away (on 8th and Amsterdam) is a "diner" called Shing Star. We just had breakfast food and is was excellent on all accounts. Pancakes for $3.95--you can't beat that anywhere in the USA much less the Upper West Side. And they are open 24 hours, a full fledged diner. Plus. it may not be as "fashionable" as some of their neighbors, but it's still a place where neighborhood folks go, so you get plenty of NYC flavor too. Don't overlook this place. Also for cheap eats in the surrounding area: a falaffel place on 79th and Amsterdam, and Zabar's (a NYC institution) at 80th and Broadway, both the corner cafe and the supermarket, with excellent appetizing counter and also prepared foods to go, fairly priced. And for great pastry tre Le Pain Quotidien at 76th and Amsterdam and, fantastic bakery at 90th and Broadway (Georgine's ???). As an alternative to Lucerne, check out Beacon Hotel at 75th and Broaadway (I posted a review there too). Both are excellent choices and values. Becaon rooms are a bit bigger and have a teriffic advantage of a refrigerator and microwave which is great for leftovers. So, for that reason, that may be our first choice next time. You'll do fine at either.

“Very busy hotel” I was here for business and this hotels is very busy with tourists. The location is really nice and close to many restaurants. Elevators were very slow despite the number of elevators in the hotel. Check in was very quick. The rooms are large compared to other NYC hotel rooms and were very clean. The concierge lounge was also very crowded in the morning and it's hard to find a table. The service in the lounge was very good though.

“Great location for a stop over” Room comfortable, staff pleasant and loaction greta for popping in and out of airport. Room comfy, breakfast in room service was expensive for what we had, but all in all a good o/night stay
“Great if you get a good price” Got it for around $250 for 3 in a room incl breakfast. Great location, nice room, good breakfast. I would stay agin if the price was right.

“Nothing spectacular” Got a great rate from AAA. First room we got (6th floor) had a chemical smell that would not go away. Mentioned this at front desk and by the time we got back from a concert we had been relocated to the 8th floor. No problem with that room. Room was on the small side as well as the bathroom but OK. Parking is expensive. Centrally located near two T stops made getting around very easy. Conceirge seemed overwhelmed by requests and to answer a simple question had to go over to the front desk. First asked a clerk who didn't know the area (he was from Germany!) but then got good directions. Skipped the food as the prices were high. Didn't like the VERY slow elevators and having to go up and down a floor to get from/to street level. I've seen better.

“Good but Be Wary!” My husband booked us into a Park View room at the Helmsley Park Lane (and paid in advance) for an important Birthday. He contacted them in advance to say when we would arrive so our room would be reserved and he requested a bottle of wine on our arrival. When we arrived we were given a subpar room (a large area broken and with rusted surface around the bathtub drain, no park view), that the manager insisted had just been renovated. We complained and after a considerable amount of arguing were finally put in a large room with a park view the next day, but also after being told two different stories, the first being that they would move our things to the new room while we were out, and the other that we had to be there while they moved our things, meaning we would be stuck in the hotel at 3pm (the middle of our day in NY!) That morning we had a terrible experience at the continental breakfast. The manager, who did apologize later, seated us after a long wait (getting us dangerously close to cut off time) and then it took four additional requests (I had to get up and find someone as no one would approach us) for me to get a pot of black tea, which was the very first thing I requested to our server when we were seated. To be fair, once we argued and complained (an unpleasant thing to have to do on your birthday!) we were moved to a beautiful room with a magnificent view, and treated to cake and champagne, although they tried to charge us for these "gifts of apology" when we checked out as "room service". The place has some beautiful rooms, with wonderful views but frankly, the management seems to be a mess. If you book, talk to the manager first, check in early to get the room you pay for, go to the continental breakfast early to get any food or drink, and check your bill carefully. If all of these things go smoothly, you might have a stay to remember.

“Nine Zero is A Number One” The Nine Zero is the latest Kimpton jewel I've discovered in my travels. I stayed there for two nights to attend a hockey game at Fenway Park. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone. The room was spacious and clean. The mattress was firm. One minor problem -- the shower leaked a little water. But that was the only blemish to report. The staff was courteous and professional especially Mike at the front desk & Fawn who was gracious & provided me with excellent recommendations. The hotel is near the T & within walking distance of Mike's Pastry Shop in the North End. Bravo Kimpton. You've done it again!

“Nice hotel on the skirts of the main shopping areas” This Westin is definitely nicer than most Westins. The staff was nice and helpful, though for a tourist and from NYC I probably would have preferred to stay right in downtown. The hotel is about a 10 min walk from the busier restaurant area and 15 min walk from Millenium Park, Michigan Ave, and downtown. This is probably close enough for most people, being from NYC I'm especially lazy. The blue line is 1.5 blocks away convenient for taking the train to and from the airport. We ordered room service when we got in late, the chicken sandwich and burger is good. Don't order the sushi, it's not terrible but it's not good. Free Starbucks coffee in the room is always a plus. It was nice of them to upgrade us to the club room levels including free internet with free continental breakfast and snacks in the afternoon. Nothing amazing at breakfast, coffee, yogurt, fruit, cereal, some pasteries and bagels, but it was enough for us in the AM. I booked this using points, I would definitely not pay $350/night which was the going rate. Though it was quiet, the bed and pillows were terrible, really unexpected from a Westin hotel and unfortunate. We did not sleep well and woke up with back aches every night.

“Nice hotel, good location if you're attending a conference” Stayed in a king room with a sofabed. The room was very spacious -- I could spread my stuff out since I was there for several nights. The bed's firmness is adjustable (kind of like a sleep number bed). Great location if you're coming to Philly for a conference at the Convention Center. Reading Terminal Market is right next door to the hotel and the convention center is right across the street. There's also a Wawa across the street from the main entrance. I would stay here again if I came back to Philly.

“quietly sophisticated” 60 Thompson is in a great location if you're looking for the buzz of Soho and the lobby bar is a great place for a pre-dinner cocktail - very smooth. The decor is understated, at least in comparison with some of the other New York hotels, it feels more 'business' than 'cool and fun'. Still, 60 Thompson scores a 'Pink' in the neilsonparc Lust List. I was disappointed that the rooftop bar was closed - ok it was December when I stayed, but other hotels still had operational rooftop bars at the same time....

“Nice Hotel in Chelsea.” I had the opportunity to stay at this property in May 2011 while in town for the BookExpo America show. The hotel is conveniently located close to both my office on 5th ave & 27th street, and it's a 20 minute walk from the Javits Center. The design of the hotel is identical to that of the Hilton Garden Inn which is one block south of this property. I found this hotel to be nice and clean. I was greeted by helpful desk staff. I also watched a game in the bar during the evening and found it to be enjoyable and low key. The room I had was new and had a nice view from the 26th floor. It was a room with two double beds do to occupancy rates, I usually get a king. I was not offered an upgrade because the hotel was sold out. I was offered a free hot breakfast in the restaurant, which was served by friendly faces. I will most likely return to this hotel on my future visits to NY.

“Nice hotel” We stayed here on vacation & requested a river view room. The room was nice, but the river was so far below us that the view was more of the city with a sliver of the river. The hotel was in a perfect location right on the River Walk & had a nice restaurant & a candy shop. The Alamo is located right outside its doors on the street side of the hotel.
“great location - a little noisy” staff was very friendly and helpful - the heat/fan was very loud and while the proximity to the airport was great - you could hear the planes.

“Don't spend more than $79 a night...” I only had a week to find a place and couldn't get anything downtown for 3 nights in my price range. Despite the other reviews I decided to take the chance-- besides I got a discount for 3 nights, about $79 a night. Upon reflection I probably overpaid. The hotel website does not advertise that it's only two blocks from the Hyde Park 51st/53rd St metra stop. Which considering how rundown the place is, you'd think they want to mention the convenience. When I got there my heart sank, it looks really bad from the outside. I checked in with no problems, but on the way to my room the hallway smelled awful. Like a mixture of standing water, mold, and funky feet. It turns your stomach at first but you get used to it. Surprise! My room wasn't that bad. It looked and smelled clean, I thought the carpet would be the same horror out in the hall. There were a few problems: coffee grounds were smeared on the table near the pot and some outlets didn't work. My neighbors looked a little shady, since I was alone I made sure I kept the door locked. But overall I was satisfied with the room. Biggest problem: unreliable wifi. I brought my laptop hoping to get some work done and on the second night it completely stopped working. The restaurant was okay. Stay away from the french fries, they're little grease traps.

“Average” Stayed here for a conference Nov 9 to 11. It's kind of what you expect from a Holiday Inn: Average. The lobby is great, recently renovated and a cool feel to it. The rooms are average, typical hotel room, but the a/c unit is loud, although that does have a plus side as unlike other reviewers I did not hear the trains at night, because I made the a/c loud. And I was at level with the tracks. Bathroom is ok, good bath&body works amentines. Shower pressure fine, yes, some black mold on the tile (just a tiny bit.) But no vent, so after a hot shower, you feel like you are in Puerto Rico in that bathroom. Hotel has some restraunts on premises, which are expensive. The only things in walking distance are a Quizno's and McDonalds, so your cheap options are limited. Good location, nice walk to Capitol. Would I stay again? yes

“Good hotel, great service.” My family and I stayed for two nights at the Serrano Hotel while in town visiting friends. We had a basic room with a king size bed. There was enough space to set up our travel bassinet for our four-month old son. Serrano had cribs available (Pack 'n Plays, I believe), but we opted to use our own. The bathroom was stocked with all of the standards. What set Serrano apart from other hotels was the service and attitude of the staff. Every employee that we interacted with was attentive and considerate. From check in to the room service guy to check out, all people were very nice and helpful. The building itself is fairly old and it shows. The infrastructure of the room looked used although all fixtures and linens appeared new. In my opinion, this was okay as it is an historic hotel and a good value. The lobby appears decadent. There is a small business center and moderate size gym in the basement. The Taylor Street Coffee Shop has above average diner food and is just across the street. Overall, I recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

“Great location, fun vibe” I stayed here for 3 nights recently on a biz trip and recommend it to anyone who's been to NYC and doesn't want to deal with the mid-town vibe (corporate, traffic, noise). The Standard is in a great location; the meatpacking district is fun, the nightlife is unbeatable and it's right by the West Village with great restaurants (the meatpacking district has good restaurants too, but perhaps a little overrated and overpriced?) The vibe at The Standard is pretty distinctive. When i grabbed a cab to the airport on the last day, the cab driver asked if i were from California. He commented that only Californians stayed there (from the US), which I'd agree with...and add Euro and South American bro-types. You know what i mean, yes, you do. It can be a bit much walking through the lobby and past the restaurant on the sidewalk. Meat.Market. The view from the room though, is unbeatable- right above High Line Park; the park is one of my personal faves, and to look out the huge floor-to-ceiling windows every morning to see it was a treat. The room itself was bigger than i expected for a NYC hotel room. The bed, though, was probably the biggest disappointment- too soft and small; it was definitely Not a Queen as advertised. It was a full-size bed. I'm not always the pickiest when it comes to toiletries in hotels, but i have to say that the ones they provided in the communal bottles were NOT pleasant. I smelt like an herb garden my entire trip, and not in a good way. whatever toiletries they used, it made me feel like I'd been rolling around in the grass. Big communal bottles = good (less waste). Smell and quality of toiletries = Not good. I hope they do something about that. Service-wise, everyone was friendly, including the frontdesk and housekeeping folks; i wasn't expecting that for a hotel with this vibe; it was a very pleasant surprise.

“Great rooms, great staff!” Had a nice one night stay at this new hotel which appears to be the closest to the airport except for the Hilton. For a new hotel, they really had great customer service. Everyone was so friendly and helpful. The rooms are more than you expect from a Courtyard. They have comfortable beds, a sofa, a sleekly designed desk, and flat screen TV which can be rotated to point towards the sofa or the bed. Bathroom large and clean. Now I know this is an airport hotel, but when planes are taking off to the north, they fly almost right over the hotel and no soundproofing can subdue the roar. Luckily, Austin airport is not the busiest and usually the wind is blowing from the south so the planes will usually be taking off in the other direction. I just hit the wrong night. Didn't try the breakfast as I was in a hurry in the morning. Nothing much around the hotel except other hotels (about 4 or 5), a Denny's, a Waffle House, and an Exxon station. All-in-all, a good choice.

“Great as always” We have stayed here too many times to count and we always have an outstanding stay....Very pleasant and helpful staff members. Front desk staff was very welcoming upon our check in. She commented several times they appreciate our return visit and our loyalty as a Marriott Rewards Platinum Elite member. This stay we used Marriott Rewards points and our room was the very last room on the 3rd floor overlooking the golf course. The walk was a bit much but most likely because of the use of points on a Friday and Saturday night and not a “paying” guest. Could not figure out why they only have the live music until 10pm on Friday and Saturday nights. The outside patio was pretty busy both nights and it would have been nice for the music to go on a little longer as people really seemed to be enjoying listening and some were even dancing, but 10 came and they packed up. Roy’s Hawaiian Fusion was great as always! Upon check out everyone said Thank you for staying with us. Very nice touch.... We will definitely return to the JW, but if we use points again, we will make sure to ask for a room a little closer.

“Okay convention hotel--nicer choices nearby” This is a decent, but fairly sterile hotel. The rooms are up to par with good beds and decent furnishings. The bath rooms have been "granitized, but the tubs are small (5ft) so it doesn't really feel luxurious. Room service has a limited selection, but it is decent and quick (and the staff is quick to point out that the 20% "delivery charge" was not "gratuity.") The big disappointment was the slow check-in and limited service offered by staff to the guest. I was in a line of five guests waiting to check in through one desk staffer. Two other desk men stood just back from the desk engaged in conversation. This was typical whenever I went to the desk with a problem of question. They seemed to enjoy making guests wait. The hotel was not busy at the time either, being between conventions. There was very little information in the room about hotel services, which was disappointing. No pens or paper to write with either. Very limited amenities (conditioner, soap and shampoo were about it.) No-one at the desk offered any information. Staff going through the hallways were often very loud--you could hear them in the rooms. There was a "Guest Services" desk but it was not manned during my stay for even an instant. I stood in front of it several times and was just ignored by passing staff. The restaurant (there is only one) looked okay, but uninteresting. The hotel entrance is bady designed and crowded. When you leave you have to walk among the cars coming into the hotel in order to reach the street. Good thing they are all jammed up so none of them can be moving very fast. This could be a nice hotel if staff cared a bit more about the guests. Instead you get the feeling that everyone is just going through the motions. The location is next to (attached to) the convention center, so if you are attending a convention there , it is probably an okay choice (better than the scruffy Hilton on the other side of the center). Otherwise I would stay at the Fairmont or the historic hotel just across the street were I to go back to San Jose.

“A great historic hotel” My family and I just finished staying at the Knickerbocker. We had a great time. This hotel was built in 1927, and has been owned by the likes of Hugh Hefner (70's). It has a tremendous blend of modern amenities and historic archictural touches. We had a Junior Suite and the added space for three of us was great. The Knickerbocker is well situated near the Gold Coast (4 blocks), Oak Street Beach (2 blocks) and the north end of the Magnificent Mile (1/2 a block). Walk a few blocks toward Rush and State streets and the streets turn leafy, the restaurants and architecture fabulous. We enjoyed eating at Sprinkles Cupcakes and Lou Malnati's in the area. Not far away Yolk served a great breakfast, and Harry Caray's was fun. My family and I would return to the Chicago and the Knickerbocker in a heartbeat.

“Hervorragendes Hotel” Wir waren im Juni für zwei Tage in San Diego. Das Manchester Grand Hyatt liegt in exponierter Lage direkt am Seaport Village, fußläufig zum Hafen, USS Midway, Gaslamp Quarter ... Es gibt zwei Hoteltürme, die durch den Spabereich, Gym, Pool etc. verbunden sind. Die Lobby ist sehr großräumig, das Personal am Empfang äußerst freundlich und hilfsbereit. Unser Zimmer im 35. Stock hatte beste Sicht, die Einrichtung war gediegen/gemütlich. Wir würden immer wieder hier übernachten.

“Great location, but overall a hairried experience, I won't be back.” It's not often that I am really dis-satisfied with a hotel, and part of that is I travel a lot and I understand when things get a little far out or perhaps the hotel is understaffed. However, after 3 stays at this property, I feel that it is really not well run and I doubt I will be back here under any circumstance. The property itself is beautiful, a grand lobby, great looking decor, a pretty restaurant -starbucks booth in the lobby, comfy beds and linens -what's not to like right? ---Well I'll tell ya. I stayed at this property for a week in June 2008 -taking a class that was south of the hotel. EVERY night that I came back to the hotel there were tons of people in the lobby waiting to check in, or ???. It was hard to get to the elevators. Once upstairs the halls were often full of people and then the room internet didn't work. I called repeadidly to have it fixed -to no avail. The halls remained loud (as they had been on my previous 2 visits) well into the night. So not a restful nights sleep. My room key wouldn't open my room door twice which meant I had to go and wait downstairs with all the others waiting for ?? The gym had broken equipment -which I was told would be fixed -on my first visit in May, in June it was still broken. After a while -everything about this hotel became annoying, waiting for the elevators, not being able to work out on site, dealing with the numb staff, having to use the internet in the lobby -because at the time the lounge didn't have wireless working either, being woken up at night by doors slamming or people laughing/screaming. --Bear in mind I spend more than a third of the year on the road. This hotel really pushed my patience. In the end I checked out of this Hotel a day early and moved down the block to the Conrad. Although the Conrad didn't meet my per diem rate it was well worth the extra $95 to have some peace and to finally sleep.

“I will not return” The cold water offered at check-in and pleasant staff were nice touches. However, noise & location are key factors. I am not a very light sleeper but I chose a suite at this Fairfield so that the A/C fan that's often noisy at Courtyard Mariotts would not be right in the bedroom. Sure enough there it was, right next to the bed! Although I didn't really need the cooling of the air conditioner, when I turned it off there was lots of highway noise from nearby Stemmons Freeway. In addition this location is a commercial desert, with very few nearby restaurants. If there are any good restaurants in the nearby Hilton Anatole, the lists provided by Holly at the front desk didn't include them. The fitness center is in the adjacent Courtyard Marriott, but the first secton of the outdoor pathway is poorly lit and feels unsafe. In addition, the security locks through the pool are (to return to the Fairfield) were not operational. Finally the decor needs an upgrade. The property looks tired.

“Nice, but aging hotel. Great location. Great Staff” Booked on HotWire so the price was nice. Great location. Easy access to anywhere in downtown. Walking distance of 6th St, though we utilized pedi-cabs. Nice hotel bar, friendly staff at check-in. Arrived an hour early and they were happy to accomodate and let us check in early. Parking is a little absured 24 for valet. 16 to self park. But it is what it is, the nicer hotels love to nickel and dime you. Overall, though, a great stay.

“Disappointing for the cost” Reservation was made for me by others. I was schocked at the price ( >$500 with tax even when prepaid via internet) and expected elegance . Checkin was efficient and mechanical. Room was adequate - but no larger than a standard Hampton-Holiday Inn, Sheration , etc. Decorated in modern chrome and wood. No in room coffee pot - but It did have an IPOD docking station - I do not have an IPOD. Desk was against the one window and therefore it was very difficult (impossible without moving the heavy desk) to open the drapes and look out on Union Square or get natural light into the room. BUT the real annoying aspect was not revealed until the morning when I took a shower - there was mold growing in everal places in the shower grout ! UGH! Also the toilet seat was not screwed tight - I fixed that . Should I have to do that I and have mold in the shower in a $500 per night hotel room.!!!!! I will not stay here again and will not reccomend it to others.

“Nice hotel” We got a great rate for this hotel from Hotwire. All around, a very nice hotel. The lobby and bar area were very fancy and recently upgraded. The room itself was pretty regular, and didn't seem to be nearly as nice as the lobby would let on...but it was still a very nice room. But, it was clean, comfortable, and had a great view. Parking was a little steep at $24 per day, but it was valet service, and I'm not sure we could have found anything cheaper. Location was good, but not much within walking distance. All around, no complaints, and I would definitely consider staying here again when I'm in Dallas.

“Hampton Inn” Spent two nights here to visit a customer and see a baseball game. Perfect location for Camden Yards. Great bed, clean updated room with flat panel. Pretty standard Hampton experience which met my expectations. I'd stay here again. Parking was a little tight so plan on valet to save yourself the hassle.

“Inexpensive alternative to nearby convention hotels” If you are attending a convention at the usual hotels in the loop or near the Navy Pier,then the Club Quarters provides an economical alternative. The Fairmont, the Hyatt Regency, the Palmer House and other convention hotels offer on-premises-convenience and larger rooms at a premium price. Club Quarters offers low room rates, with no charges for myriad smaller items that nibble away at budgets. The free internet, free bottled water, free printing and other goodies plus the lower rates add up to substantial savings. This comes at the price of small but functional rooms, views through tiny windows and comfortable but limited lobby / sitting spaces. Hint: If coming from Ohare, take the CTA Blue Line to the Lake Station and walk to the hotel. The CTA is always cheaper and often faster than using a taxi or shuttle service. Hint: For really good food, leave the Loop and head out to the neighborhoods. Seek the advice of Chicago friends or the concierge. Hint: Different booking sites offered substantially different rates for the same nights and class of rooms at this property. Check around a bit before booking. Hint: Do not count on the free printing to work. I was not able to pick up my boarding pass because of a malfunction.

“Loved my stay!” I was in downtown Chicago for 2 days on business & booked this hotel through Hotwire. I got the room for $99/night, but from what I've seen, the rates are generally $225/night & higher. I had never been to Chicago before & chose to forgo a rental car...taking the Blue Line CTA train from O'Hare to the Clark/Lake station. I called & got directions from the hotel staff. They were very helpful. I decided to walk to the hotel from the Clark/Lake station (about 7 blocks) b/c I wanted to see the city & it really wasn't that bad of a walk (I was even carrying a suitcase on my back & wheeling my laptop). My room was really nice (see pics). There were some signs of age, but it was well appointed. It had all the ameneties you'd want (except for a mini fridge...instead they put a mini bar), & had a nice HD flat screen. The bed & pillows were extremely comfortable...which was good b/c I currently have a disk problem in my lower neck. The view was amazing (see pics). The hotel was centrally located. There was a theater & bowling alley & shops across the street. The Navy Pier was a short walk/cab ride away & I walked for about a mile around the city just to see the sights & get some pizza. Since I did not have a car, I can't tell you how much parking was, but true to form, this is yet another upscale hotel that charges for internet access (even though their lower-scale competitors offer it for free)...w/tax it comes out to $13 per day. I didn't get a chance to check out the hotel amenities (pool/fitness), but I'd recommend this place to anyone.

“Great and not” If you are here for the land of pretty (and fake) faces, this is the place for you! if you are the average mainstream American, this hotel will suffice. I felt like the front desk folks were a bit snotty, although we had two lovely servers at the Station Bar on Thanksgiving night that were awesome and took excellent care of us even though we were not "there to be seen" but rather to just have nice drinks and relax with the football game on the amazing huge screen. The coffee service in the a.m. was good and the bath products were great. The room was a decent size, really comfy beds and good tv w/movie selections. I can appreciate the convenience of the top notch nightclub up top with great views and the in-room drinks if you want them; just not the purpose of this trip for us. Our first room was right over the Station Bar so the 2nd night we asked to be moved and the 2nd room was excellent and quiet. I'd not seek out this hotel but if you get it on Hotwire its fine for a couple of nights visit to LA.

“Exceptional stay, as always!” I was in contact prior to my stay by Demi Dalisay. She was warm and welcoming and provided good information for my upcoming stay. She asked for my arrival details and was able to put my travel partner's information on my room as he was arriving before me. We were in a beautiful Landmark Suite and it was simply perfect. Great furnishings, wonderful bath products, an enveloping bed and a terrific view of San Diego and the bay. We've stayed at the US Grant before and we will certainly again. Many thanks for your terrific work!

“Modern and central location + great service” Very new and modern hotel so the rooms are in great shape. Breakfast was excellent and the service first class. Hotel looks at the bay over the highway though views are pretty good. I had a partial bay view looking over hotel pool - bay was hard to see. I would stay here again.

“Great Location & Excellent Value” This hotel is located right in the city center with great views of the war memorial and just a few blocks from the City Center Mall - the perfect location for travelers without a rental car. Unlike other Sheratons, this Sheraton charges for in-room internet access, but wi-fi is free in the hotel lobby and there's a Starbuck located in the hotel lobby with free wi-fi. As a basic SPG (frequent user/customer), I was greeted with a bag of goodies (bottle of water and a couple of sweet treats) upon check-in. Rooms are nice and big with all the amenities. Rates are very reasonable and a great value.

“Exceded my expectations” Clean and mostly comfortable. We had access to the club lounge which had water and sodas at night and breakfast in the morning. Totally worth it. It was close to the Art Museum, Franklin Institue and in walking distance from all the shopping and restaurant area. Pretty easy to grab a cab to get to Old City or Fishtown.

“Convenience and Comfort” This is the 2nd Renaissance hotel I have stayed at recently, and I have to say, I'm enjoying these properties. They really take care of you and service really seems to be a top priority for this hotel chain. I was given a really nice end room with two large windows facing the Chicago theater. The room was very spacious, contemporary and clean. There's a whole mini mall attached to the hotel so you don't have to walk outside in the freezing cold - - there's a small little store attached that serves Starbucks or you can walk inside the building and find a whole Starbucks store. There's a neat little fastfood-like dumpling restaurant that's great for a quick bite. The location can't be beat - - i could practically walk to all my meetings. There was great shopping nearby and the L stops were there too, even though i didn't use it. I really enjoyed my visit. I would totally stay at this hotel again for business or pleasure.

“Beautiful Location and Spacious Rooms” Can't beat the view from the room's balcony. San Diego Bay on one side and the marina on the other. Rooms are large and have refrigerators. Free buffet breakfast in the morning. Staff is very attentive. Great location for sightseeing or just relaxing.

“Average Hotel” The W Chicago Lakeshore Drive is your average chain hotel. While the location (about a 5 minute walk to Michigan Avenue) and view (amazing views of the lake if you get the right room) are pros, nothing else really stands out at this hotel. It is a bit older, there is often a wait for the elevators, and the service is average. We stopped in the lobby bar for a "glass of the house red wine", and needless to say, we were surprised when the bill arrived - $32 for 2 glasses of average wine!

“Old and musty” The good bits first: extremely friendly staff, beautiful public spaces, super comfortable beds and a great location. Now for the disappointing bits: the safe in our suite didn't work when we checked in, you have to pre-order a coffee maker if you don't want to spend mornings in the queue for Starbucks in the lobby (or pay an extortionate amount for room service), the bathrooms look like they haven't been updated since the early 1960s and our ceiling showed clear signs of water damage. Nowhere near as nice as The Peninsula.

“Pleasant Surprise” I’ve not stayed here for decades (I was treated very rudely and memories are slow to fade) but I had business in the historic area and I guess due to a slow Thanksgiving week they had a very good rate. First off the parking is $25.00 and that is consistent or even on the low side for Philadelphia hotels, but you have until 4:00PM on the day you check out to leave your car without additional charge, and you have free “in & out” privileges. And the walkway to the garage elevator is covered which was welcome on the rainy day I stayed there. As noted the hotel is a quick couple of blocks from the 5th street subway and obviously very close to historic area, the US Mint and other attractions. A variety of restaurants are within walking distance on Market Street and a couple will give you a discount if you show your room key. The rooms are fine, older outdated TV’s but nice to have microwave and small fridge. The wireless internet was no charge and was pretty fast at about 10 Mbps for both uploads and downloads. The front desk was very friendly and check in was prompt.. My major complaint/suggestion is they need to have free coffee in the lobby, they didn’t even have that in the morning and the restaurant wanted $3.00 a cup for “no-name” coffee. Comp morning coffee is pretty important to me and almost “automatic” at most hotels.

“Just stay here, save yourself the trouble of searching!” Very nice, very comfortable, VERY convenient! Helpful, pleasant staff! We were able to walk everywhere. Riverwalk is lots of fun, tons of restaurants and great people watching. Market square is a short walk. The breakfast buffet was terrific! I especially want to thank Thomas for making me the MOST delicious omelette (even went in the back to get extra ingredients that weren't out front!) Thanks also to Eugene for making sure it was all to my liking! Would stay here again!

“Great staff and lovely room, a bit far from the U.” We stayed here for three days while moving a family member to the U of T Law School. Everything about the hotel was nice; great beds, quiet, really good breakfast and late night bar food. We found this hotel thru a Trip Advisor recommendation, but it's a bit inconvenient for running back and forth to the campus- right off the freeway but the fwy system can be difficult to navigate. And the Austin traffic can be awful-it's easier to stay downtown.

“Pretty Good ... could have been a bigger room.” So its a pretty nice hotel. I was staying there for an IBM Convention across the street at the Convention Center. The hotel was pretty nice, the staff was nice to. Internet access was good, but they tried to charge me for each night I stayed even if I did not use it that day. They did correct this wthout question, but still seems kinda dodgy. I had room service one night and it was pretty good for soup and salad and cheap for room service. Best thing about the hotel is location location location , very easy access to riverwalk and to the mall across the street. Only complaint I had was the iced coffee from the 24 gift/food shop was nasty. Also I did not here any crickets .... but there is major construction going on across the street for a new Hyatt and that was pretty noisy in the early morning.

“Good location,great staff, little sleep” We had a double queen overlooking the street. The room was amply spacious ( for 2 adults+2 kids),newly renovated, clean and very comfortable but noise was a problem. If you are not on a high floor at the back of the hotel, you won't get much sleep.Unfortunately, the hotel was full, so there was no chance of a change of room. On a more positive note, the breakfast was really quite good,despite the lack of seating at some times, and the staff were welcoming and friendly at all times.

“Just Okay” We had a less positive experience than many who have stayed at theWit. We found the service to be at best average. We checked in during the holiday season and the front desk staff gave us misinformation about a number of things when we checked in. We were able to sort this out later, but this required our visiting the front desk 2-3 times to specifically ask about each piece of misinformation. We also experienced a few problems in the room. The bathroom door was at times difficult to open and one of us got stuck in the bathroom on one occasion. Our room was a king corner room and was on the small side. The bed was moderately comfortable. The exercise room had several treadmills, elliptical machines, and bicycles and was generally good. This would not be a top choice for us in future stays in Chicago. We received a good rate for our stay and would have been quite unhappy if we had paid more typical rates. Of the three similar hotels where we have recently stayed in Chicago (the others being the Dana and the Radisson Blu), we would rank theWit as a distant third in terms of service and the quality of the rooms. theWit is in a central location in the middle of the Loop near Macy's and other shopping.

“Excellent service” The staff at this hotel were exceptionally helpful when we had an unexpected stay due to flight problems. The room was comfortable, the free breakfast was great, and we were very relieved to have such a nice welcome from the receptionist. We definitely would stay here if we ever needed to be near the Denver airport.

“Inviting Lobby, Large Restaurant/Bar and Easy Shuttle” This hotel was perfect for a quick business trip. The lobby is large but warm, with convenient airline ticket printing stations and a nice complimentary coffee/tea station. The rooms are decent size; the bathroom counter space was phenomenal! There is a fair bit of outside noise, but overall it was a very pleasant stay.

“Needs More Than Simple TLC” This is by far the most disgusting Embassy Suites I have stayed in. The place is horrible. I went to my room with my family and stepped no farther into the room than by the sofa. A gagging smell of urine overwhelmed me. I called the desk and the clerk offered to have engineering come up. "No you won't. You will find me another room immediately and I trust you will NOT sell this room to anyone else until the couch is thoroughly cleaned." While I did not give the clerk much choice, he did come to meet us with a new room key and wanted me to follow him to the original room to check on the smell. Nope, I am tired and going to my new room that I hope (fingers crossed) is better. Well it did not smell like urine but I have a list of problems: bugs on the bathroom wall, dirt along all floor boards and vents, couch visibly dirty, old and torn, ottoman leg gone, carpet sticky, hard floor slippery, etc etc. Whirlpool hot but no jets and the pool was freezing. The final insult was trying to open the shampoo and realizing it was used before and not replaced!! Are you kidding me Hilton?? I gave the manager fair warning that I would be writing my review with very strong language. I am also sending a report to Hilton directly. In the mean time, I cannot suggest strongly enough to go somewhere else.

“Basic but great values” I have stayed here twice now, July 2006 and June 2008, and it was much the same each time. On the plus side, the location is great and central, the rates are surprisingly low in what is normally an expensive town, and breakfast is included in most quoted rates. It's not luxurious, and the staff are polite without being overly warm. On the down side, it can be a bit noisy at night (because of the location), the fittings etc are clean but rather threadbare, and the breakfast is minimalist. So, if you're looking for value and a great central location, this place is for you. You can spend your money seeing the sights or enjoying SF's many restaurants etc, rather than handing it over to a pricier hotel. If you want an indulgent experience where the hotel itself rather than the city & surrounds is the focus, then look elsewhere.

“Fantastic find!” I was looking for a simple, clean hotel close to Grace Community Church where I would be attending a 4 day conference. Since the commute would be daily, I was looking foremost at proximity and price. What I got was way beyond my expectations! The hotel is in an area which would have otherwise caused me to pass over it. Even though the grounds and facility are immaculate, I would have been distracted by the rough-looking neighborhood. However, since I went largely by TripAdvisor ratings, I was confident in my choice and didn't flinch when I drove right up. Check in was efficient and speedy. My room was fantastic. I have stayed in Hilton's which were inferior to what I had at this hotel. Clean, crisp decoration, nice furniture, very comfortable bed and excellent TV and wi-fi. My room was right across fromt the complimentary hot breakfast which was great. I didn't bother with the room coffee since I could go across the hall and get the "real thing" without the fuss. The hotel had a small fitness room but I didn't use it. Looked like it would do the job though. I was hungry for lunch and wasn't sure if I could try to walk somewhere or not. I checked with the front desk and was referred to a Mexican seafood specialty restaurant on the diagonal corner. I took the suggestion and was very happy that I did. Do not be overly concerned about the suspicious-looking surroundings. This place is a GEM and you will be happy you stayed at the Best Western Burbank Airport Inn.

“Highly recommend it and will be back” After my conference at another hotel had to stay for 2 more nights in Boston and found this option online. An excellent choice. Even though it is an "airport" hotel, given the location of Logan airport you are only minutes from down town Boston. The rooms are smaller compared to typical Embassy suites. The bed was comfortable. Two flat screen TVs means no fighting over programs. The bath was very small. There is free coffee in the room, a fridge and a micorwave. The check in was excellent, the receptionist gave me free Wifi access for the duration of the stay. Great. Breakfast is excellent. The location is minutes from the aiport with free shuttle and a short walk thru a park to the T station (blue line). Parking is 32/day, a bit steep for guests. Airport car rental lots are right across the hotel. Definitely a good value.

“A great value in New York” With about $200 a night, I got a studio with two queen beds, one rollaway bed, and a full kitchen!!!! Plus, this hotel is right next to the Penn station where I can go Boston, Philadelphia, Washington easily with my luggages. Also, we can easily find meal options around. McDonald, Burger King, etc. Best hotel in NY from a family's point of view.

“Nice Hotel, Good Location” Very pleasant staff, nice rooms, comfortable bed, right on the end of the 16th Street Mall. I stayed in a room in the tower across the street from the main building. Getting to the other builder using the skywalk is sort of a pain if you have luggage because there are a couple of stairs to go up and down. It's easiest just to cross on the street level.

“Bait and Switch” I will be attending the Society of Wine Educators Conference at the Hotel. According to the conference brochure they had negotiated a $129 rate. The Hotel would not honor that rate and gave a rate over $300 a night. To me that is bait and switch. Out of principle I did not book the room. I am in the hospitality industry and would never treat my guests that way. If $300 is the rate advertise that. Be honest.

“There's good and there's bad” I had a mixed experience with this hotel. First off, I have Gold Elite status with Marriott, so I get a few more perks. The exterior of the hotel is very old looking. It looks like a Lego pyramid made of stone. Quebec street is a little hard to navigate if you aren't used to it. On the plus, there is a large shopping center across the road with several eatery choices. Parking is $10 for self parking. Upon arrival, I was upgraded to a Jr. suite. The room is not bad, but it has an odd design. There is a 32" TV in the living room but nothing in the bedroom itself. It's literally like watching TV out your window into your next door neighbor's house. Free HBO. The bathroom is rather small too. The "suite" is just a little bigger than a normal sized hotel room with the space reallocated for a couch and living area. Very comfortable beds with lots of pillows. The Club Level is nice. They have plenty of snack and food options for you. Room service was also prompt and friendly. Nice portion size for the cost. The biggest complaint is that I had a housekeeping person walked into my room without knocking in the middle of the day. Not sure why or what she was doing. She apologized profusely and left. Had I not had a conference at the hotel in the morning, I would have stayed elsewhere. It's too far from the airport and downtown to justify the price.

“Cute Boutique Hotel” Clean & good service. The decor of the hotel was impressive. The size of the room was great and the bathroom was clean and up to date. No complaints really, except that if you are looking for a grand hotel in new york city this is not the place. Oh and the walls are a llittle thin, i could hear conversations of the rooms we would pass in the hall way. if you are looking for something more intimate and quiet this is the place to go.

“Renovated Rooms on the Way” I first stayed at the Westin Bonaventure as a kid ... in 1978. I thought it was cool then, I and I think it is cool now. I stay here frequently ... about once a month. This is not your typical Westin and you should approach it that way. It was built to be architecturally interesting and decades later, it still is. Just don't expect cookie cutter design. Clearly those that have had a problem with the 70's look to the architecture in the lobby areas (lots of concrete here) just want this Westin to be like all the others. The Bonaventure is a very interesting place if you look at it that way. Yes, this hotel was built in the 70's and was pretty bold in its design during that time. As noted in other reviews, the rooms are smaller by U.S. standards. They are pie wedge-shaped and the bathrooms are sufficient, but on the small side. Who wants to spend all their time in L.A. in the bathroom, anyhow? I had noticed that furnishings were getting a bit worn, but voila ... the last two times I've stayed here I've been put in one of their newly renovated rooms (see photos). The renovations and new furnishings are quite tasteful and make better use of the room's space. The desk is a great addition ... clearly a nod to the fact that hotel rooms are more like offices on the road for many more of us now, than when the hotel first opened. Colors are in the earth tones and the rooms are accented by some nice vintage photographs of L.A. There's new carpeting in the rooms with a modern design, set on the diagonal, which probably helps make the room look bigger. Every time I stay here, I eat dinner down in the lobby bar and, in general, I've been pretty pleased with my meals there. The halibut and chips is pretty decent. Plus, it is fun to people watch from that location. There are a couple of items that I feel compelled to nit-pick, even after the renovations: (1) My renovated rooms still had big, black, tube TVs. Surely they will replace them with flat-screen LCDs ... but then again, there's a new swivel stand beneath those black bulky dinosaurs, so that may not be in the works. Drat!; (2) The bedside tables are kind of built-in (or made to look like they are built-in) to the headboard surround and there are no electrical outlets bedside. You can move the bedside table and reach into the wall (or at least into the headboard surround ... see photo) and find an outlet there, but this is really poorly designed. People always complain about the mandatory and expensive valet parking. Hey, it's a big city and parking is expensive ... everywhere. I stay in a lot of hotels and while the Westin Bonaventure is not the most luxurious place I've stayed, it remains one of my favorites and with the renovations currently underway in the guestrooms, it should remain a favorite of mine for some time.

“Great hotel! Stayed for Final Four Weekend” This hotel was a great find for our stay for the Final 4 last weekend. the hotel itself was very clean, the staff was wonderful and we had no complaints what so ever. the hotel was completely full for this big event and the staff had no problems from what i noticed. The breakfast area was great, lots to chose from each morning. The pool was a bit cold still, so we didnt use it, but the hot tub was nice enough and we sat in it nightly after the games. I would stay here again if we returned to Houston. it is also located conveniently to the Galleria area, as well as many places to eat. high marks from our perspective :)

“Perfect Choice for the 4th of July” Booked two rooms through the Amex FH&R program. One room received an upgrade to a king room directly facing the Washington Monument. As such, we saw no need to leave that room for the 4th of July Fireworks. The other room was a double (both rooms on upper floor) that was recently refurbished. It was huge and very clean. The other room was very clean as well however a bit smaller (the hotel is old so completely understand) and what we lacked in space we gained in view. Front desk staff were beyond friendly and super helpful. Concierge the same. Had drinks at Round Robin (so cozy!) and dinner at Occidental, which to be honest, could have been a little better, but good none the less. All in all a perfect location, super friendly and helpful staff in a historic hotel. Recomend completely.

“Not great for a business traveler...” Quick business trip up to SFO and OAK and picked the Sheraton for Starwood reasons. For the tourist crowd, I'm sure this is a choice spot, yet for a business traveler it was severely lacking on a number of fronts. Room -- bathroom made me feel like I was back in a studio apt in Manhattan. Weak shower pressure, no curved shower rod so you are hugging the curtain the whole time, and the toilet is made for a 4 year old (not someone 6' 4"). The ironing board was an embarrassment (see photo) and limited a decent touch up for a suit and shirt. Parking? Self parking or valet was basically 50 bucks a night. Really?!? When will hotels understand that a business traveler is drawn by location, bed, shower and business related amenities (which include a decent iron and board). Too many other great hotel properties to choose from in SF to come back.

“Very nice” We booked our stay through Travelzoo. The hotel was very nice but I would not have paid full price for it. It is very pet friendly from the faux fur throw at the end of the bed to the canine mascot, they know how to do pets! You can even get a goldfish as a "pet" for your stay if you request! Our room was very eclectic with yellow striped wall paper, high ceilings and blue and yellow furnishings. The front desk staff were very professional from the moment we walked in the door. I do agree with other posters though that this appears to be a somewhat "yuppie" establishment. It came as no surprise though based on what I'd read in previous reviews. We had flown into Denver on an early morning flight so by the 5PM wine serving in the lobby we were exhausted and elected to take a nap before heading out to dinner instead. The turndown service was a nice touch, the bed turned down and nice jazz on the strereo when we returned from supper. There was in-room high speed internet and we connected without difficulty. I do have 2 complaints about this property. One, we were on the highest floor (per my request) and while I am not sure that it was a product of being up so high or the high ceilings, the air flow in the room was awful. Best we could tell there was only one vent in the room, very high on the wall (it was open, we checked) but even with the temp set at 68 in our room was warm and fairly stuffy. Second, I had requested a "quiet room". I'd assumed that meant that it was in a quieter part of the hotel (perhaps an area where they don't put families with young children, etc.) but what it turned out to mean was that it was facing an inner courtyard with no view except the roof below. It was awful. Had I known what that meant I'd have chosen a "noiser" room with a view of the street below. We were only in Denver one night in route to Keystone so I didn't bother "complaining" to the front desk about either problem. I'll just know in the future. The location of this hotel is fabulous, it is only a block from the 16th street shopping area. Overall, this was a nice stay and if I ever get a good rate from Travelzoo I will stay with them again.

“Charmer Hotel by the Space Needle!” We reserved two rooms at this hotel and were pleasantly surprised with its charm, location, and offering of a continental breakfast (not mentioned in its ad). To add to its charm, the Tin Lizzy Lounge, adjacent to the reception desk, provided an evening of live music and interesting cocktails and beer. We arrived late, but the performer "Enrique" continued with his performance even though he was scheduled to end a bit earlier! What a great way to end our day. The rooms were decorated in an antique sort of mode, were spacious, and even included kitchens. The hotel is an old school, so the rooms are interesting in their size and shape. Bathrobes were provided and the cosmetics (shampoo, etc.) were of a higher end. Needless to say, if we ever get the chance, we will stay here again!

“Noisy, Mediocore Hotel” We stayed 3 nights while visiting San Diego. Got this hotel on Hotwire and have to admit I was disappointed. Reviews were not good so we didn't have much for expectations. We were in a room close to the freeway so had a hard time sleeping because of the constant vehicle noise - thank goodness I brought ear plugs which helped somewhat. Rooms are very much in need of attention - not in cleaning but in general repair. Peeling paint, torn carpeting, etc. Towels were like sand paper and very thin. On the plus side the on site restaurant Adam's Steak and Eggs served an EXCELLENT breakfast! We ate there a couple of times because it was that good and the service was great. You get what you pay for and at $53/night that's exactly what we got - not much!

“Very comfortable and contemporary rooms” The best part of the room is the recliner. It was a great added touch to a guestroom and made for a great workstation. The room was very spacious. I highly recommend going to the roof top bar for a drink as it offers a fantastic view of Chicago. There was nothing disappointing about this property.

“Nicest hotel we've stayed at in NYC” We've stayed in maybe 10 different hotels in NYC over the last 3 years -- the joys of having a child in college in the city. We usually go as cheap as possible -- given that all the cash goes to pay for college. We picked a one bedroom suite at the Dumont for this trip because with our daughter along we would have had to get two rooms at a regular hotel. So the suite was less expensive than 2 rooms at pretty much any other hotel. The place is very, very nice. We wouldn't think twice about going back when then the economics work out. One thing to consider in the one bedroom suite -- the bathroom is entered through the bedroom. So if somebody is sleeping on the sofa bed and they want to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night, they have to go through the bedroom. This was just the slightest bit awkward for my daughter but worked out okay. Again, I wouldn't hesitate in the future.

“A very nice hotel in the perfect location.” Let me start by saying that in San Francisco you can go from a good block to a lousy one just by making a turn, so location is very important. I have been many times to SF (if I didn't live in Panama, this is the city I would live) and I absolutely LOVE the city. I always try different hotels each time I visit and I think this is the best one for groups. Upon arrival I was greeted in the counter by a very helpful fellow (I should start paying attention to their names to post them too) who made the registration process totally painless and gave me a lot of information on what to do, where to go and what to see. The rooms that we got were very spacious, the beds were comfy, it had a very nice bathroom and a full kitchen (stove, fridge, microwave, sink, dishes and silverware). It even had a table with a couple of chairs so you can eat there. This was a treat! There are many restaurants in walking distance (Thai, Italian, burgers, etc) and a mini market where you can purchase about anything to keep in your kitchen (we made sandwiches for our wine tour the next day). The hotel had a complementary breakfast (very basic, but still something over nothing) and a wine and cheese from 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. (sometimes extended till 6 p.m.) which was incredible. They had great wine and keep your glassed filled up all the time. This was better than going to the wineries LOL! Part of the fun going to SF is using their public transportation system (mainly buses and cable cars). You can buy a passport for 3 or 7 days at a Walgreen's 3 blocks down in Sutter. The 7 day pass was about $24 which was a very nice deal. There are many ways to get around. We crossed the street to get the 27 bus going to Market St. and that one stopped right in front of Westfield Mall. For Fisherman's Wharf we took the 27 going north on Levenworth and then the 47 from Van Ness. Coming back was even easier taking the 47, getting off on Sutter, walking to Post and hopping on either the 2, 3 or 76. Most bus stops tell you the time the next bus is due, and that is awesome. They do have valet parking but SF is not a driving city. You walk around and take the bus. Simple as that. But if you do have a car, expect to pay around $35 a day for parking. I have no complaints over my choice in this hotel and I will most definitely be coming back!

“Was expecting a little more...” For a Renaissance Hotel I was expecting a little more. I was there for a conference and my room was free of charge so I can't complain too much and I don't know how much it generally costs. The room itself was fine and the location being downtown was nice and convenient. There was also a bar that was open late at the hotel. No free WiFi in the room, but they do have it for free in the lobby.

“The hotel is adequate” This hotel "will do" for leisure or business but I didn't feel anything special about this property. I would suggest it is best for business travel rather than leisure. On the plus side, the rooms are well situated for the business traveler, but not a desk, but rather a full wall to work with ample room and plug in's for devices. The flat screen television is nice and it's large. We only at once in the restaurant, for breakfast, and it was just plain bad to awful. The buffet food was "old and cold" the service non-existent, wrong orders brought. Another significant drawback to the hotel is that taxi's don't come to this hotel. The rooms feel on the small side, although they're adequate. This hotel is just fine.

“Solid Airport Hotel” I used to stay at the LAX Sheraton or the LAX Marriott, but the Four Points has become my "airport" hotel. I use LAX to fly internationally and to Hawaii and I like to come in a night early because I usually take the first flight out. The accommodations are clean and comfortable, the staff helpful and friendly. I also like their pool area and the bar. I have also used their park and fly program and it has worked out well for me. Overall this is a very solid hotel when you need convenience to LAX.

“Obviously not the best Hilton, but outstanding for New York” To be clear, my ratings are for the Hilton New York as a Hilton Hotel in NYC. It is far from the best Hilton I've ever stayed at, its room sizes and decor can't compete with ones in other cities. But that being said, in the context of NYC this is probably my favorite hotel in New York City now. I've stayed in a dozen others throughout the city and I actually liked the Hilton Times Square as my previous favorite, but now that I've been here it will be hard to go back. I got a room upgrade because of status to the 44th floor with a Central Park view. The location is convenient to just about everything in mid-town, the upper floors are quieter in my opinion than staying further down in Times Square (although its still NYC never real silence). The only thing thats not the greatest is the elevators since there are only 3 per section of 10 or so floors so it takes a while and fills up on the way down. I definitely will make this my number 1 choice for NYC stays when the rate is good.

“You will be disappointed” The hotel was in need of a remodel. The mattress was sunken on the sides. The carpet was worn out. The hotel has bad breath. The sheets on the bed were wrinkled up like they had not been changed from the last guest. The stuffing in the pillows has kind of petrified. The hotel in general does not look very clean. There is also a musty, stale smoke type of odor at this hotel. The one good thing was a super fast internet connection. It was blazing fast! Also, come to think of it, the room was very large, but the bath was tiny. My advice is to avoid this hotel.

“Great location - cool hotel” Found a great deal for Kimpton's birthday and booked a room with a friend to watch the NCAA Frozen Four. The hotel is right across the street from the Verizon Center - couldn't be a better location. The building is the old post office - pretty cool building. The rooms are decently sized, with really comfortable beds and flat screen TV's. The only complaint about the room was that the bathroom had a pocket door - don't share a room with anyone that you don't want to hear what you're doing in the bathroom. The hotel has a small gym with brand new equipment on the 4th floor. While not big, it's better than 95% of the other hotels I have stayed at recently. Each cardio machine has it's own TV with an IPOD dock. Very cool. It saved us each $25/day that we were going to spend at the gym across the street. The hotel has a cool bar/restaurant that seems like the hip spot in town. I highly recommend it. Overall - great hotel, great service. I would stay here again without a second thought.

“Great Service and Location” Legendary Four Seasons service, but the building itself is a bit under-whelming. Being that the building is a conversion, it misses something in it's architecture. Not a bad place to stay, just not the best within the hotel brand.

“Would probably stay somewhere else” Was booked into this hotel by the company paying for my visit. The room was very small and could use some renovation. The walls were thin and I could hear everything in the next room. Only one of the two elevators was working and it was very slow. I ended up getting my exercise by running up and down the stairs. The small exercise room had four machines crammed into it with barely enough room to get around. It didn't feel like there was any air circulation as another person and I were working out. I guess it can serve double purpose as an exercise room and a sauna. The free breakfast was decent and the free local shuttle was great. The free milk and cookies at night was also a nice touch. Housekeeping did not clean my bathroom one day and also forgot to leave any towels. The front desk was pleasant for the most part but gave me conflicting information when I inquired about a shuttle to the airport. The night before I was to depart, I called and front desk and was informed that I can arrange for an airport shuttle anytime and the cost would be $17. The next morning, I ask the front desk to arrange for an airport shuttle. He gave me the phone number but told me that airport shuttles require at least 24 hour notice and it was too late. He offered to call a taxi for me which would cost $40+. So I called the airport shuttle company myself and easily arranged a pickup. The cost...$17. The hotel calls itself an European boutique hotel but has a ways to go.

“My new favorite hotel in Philadelphia” The Latham, like most of Philly’s buildings, is deceptively small. The lobby almost seems abrupt as you walk in; most of us are used to the grand lobbies preferred by most hotels now. Do not let this fool you, however; what the Latham lacks in size is makes up for in class and style. Who says bigger is better? The Guestrooms are excellent and elegantly designed with a modern twist on classic taste. I found my room, again small, but very comfortable. I was concerned about possible street noise being located in downtown Philly, but these concerns were unfounded. I had no trouble sleeping and heard no undo traffic noise. The location of the Latham is also superb. It is at the center of many shops, restaurants, and cafes so there is no shortage of options to occupy your time. It is, however, a bit of a walk to the historical sites such as independence hall, so a cab ride may be preferable. It is also located near Rittenhouse square, a great place to stroll or dine. All of this would make the Latham an excellent fit for business or personal travel, but the Latham’s crowning attribute was its staff. From the doormen to the concierge, the staff was exceptional. All were extremely friendly, and offered tips and suggestions for everything from dining to sights to shortcuts. In the end it was a vibrant staff to go along with a vibrant hotel in an even more vibrant city. I would certainly recommend the Latham to anyone travelling to Philadelphia looking for a hotel downtown.

“Fab Holiday in a very Friendly City” Stayed at the Hyatt for 7 nights and didn't really have any complaints other than we were suprised that there was no safe in the room. This would make things a lot easier for guests. The hotel as a whole is clean and tidy and the rooms are the same, as well as being very spacious. The hotel staff are friendly and happy to help with any query you may have. It was nice to have breakfast in the hotel before heading out for the day (as many hotels in America only offer "Room Only). We found the breakfast to be more than adequate as you can choose from fruit, cereals, yoghurts, bagels and toast every morning or order something hot (at an extra charge) The hotel offers a free shuttle for anyone wanting to travel within a 5 mile radius and we used this to get to the DART station every day. We found this to be a very convenient and economical way to travel as the trains arrive and depart every 20 minutes and we always got a seat on the train. The journey to Downtown Dallas takes around 35 minutes. There are plenty of eating place close by the hotel and shopping can be found in the Galleria. We ate at Del Frisco's which is just outside the hotel and although a little more expensive, we had a lovely meal. Another place we enjoyed was the Cafe Grand Lux in the Galleria, we ate there a couple of nights. While in Downtown Dallas we visited the Sixth Floor Museam, Holocaust Museam and the Aquarium. We enjoyed all of these attractions however it might be best to try and avoid the Aquarium on a day when there is school trips - can be busy!!! Outwith the centre of Dallas, we visited the Zoo which was really enjoyable and the Stockyards at Fort Worth ( we purchased a Regional Pass for $7.50 and this got us right to the Stockyards as you can travel on the DART, TRE and the local buses with your ticket). We also visited Southfork and toured the house etc which was fun. If you are looking to get to Southfork and you don't have a car (like us), you can get the DART to Parker Rd Station and then phone for a taxi which will take you there. The only down side was that we were glad that we had done our homework (some of the tips which I have added above) before we went, as the city itself isn't set up for tourists and the places of interest aren't really advertised. All in all we had a really great time and we discovered that the people in Dallas where some of the friendliest and most helpful people we had met on our travels. Dallas is worth a visit!

“Very pleasant hotel” The hotel is conveniently located. The rooms are big, with all what you need for a confortable stay, including this dream box for relax that Crowne Plaza has on all their rooms. Conveniently located, minutes ago from Teathers, Shopping Malls and all the action you might look for in Beverly Hills. Staff is friendly and they have a nice self parking lot. I really have very good memories of this hotel, that will be a good option for my next trip to Beverly Hills

“Great hotel and location” My family of 3 stayed here last weekend and were very happy with our choice. Just one block from the holiday hustle and bustle on Michigan Ave, and a short walk to the Navy Pier. The staff was courteous and professional and Neil (bell staff) was superb! Our room on the 20th floor was cozy, clean and quiet. The hotel was busy over the weekend but we didn't experience any issues at all, not even with the elevators. We would stay here again!

“Good deal for a perfect location” The Stay is a rather affordable address given the location and the level of service. The rooms are pretty small (at least mine was) and the decoration is quite minimal, be it the bedroom or the bathroom. It is clean, good grade for housekeeping. You will find bathrobes, iron board and safe in the room. And you can ask for a boiler (but it comes without mugs or spoons... you get ... a boiler) . What I liked : the bedding (confortable), the hall and the restaurant (very lively). The location (right on Times Square: theaters, food, bars...) On the downside: the elevators (only 2) are very slow and you have to be ready to wait and wait ... appliances in bathroom are minimal. It is noisy when your neighbors could not care less about the world around them. The TV channels are few, and many do not work. I would probably prefer a more roomy, just a bit fancier place for a romantic stay, but for work, tourism, and shopping I need no more.

“A good business hotel in Silicon Valley!” I stay in this hotel in January for a week with an executive floor (i.e., with access to a lounge at the top floor). The staff here provides outstanding service - they are friendly and nice, especially those in the reception counter. It makes you feel at home. The lounge is a bit out of my expectation - Please don't expect you have a lounge that is similar to those in Hyatt Regency and Marriott. It is a simple working/relax area with some nuts and selected soft drinks provided, one or two large tables and comfortable sofa, and a flat-screen TV. Nevertheless, they provide you a printer in which you can print your documents and boarding passes free-of-charge! The buffet breakfast is nice - quite a number of choices - and they are tasty! The room is quite large, with a balcony that has a very nice mountain view. More importantly, it is clean and the interior design makes you feel comfortable.

“Smallest Hotel Room in NYC” This was the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. Even for NYC standards it was tiny. I even paid for an upgrade so it would not be the smallest room they offered, but still it was probably 10' x 12'. The heat in the bathroom was always on and poured into the room. You tried to counter with the AC which was noisy and either on full blast or off and the temp was never stable. The bed was tiny also. If you are at all clostrophobic (and I am not) don't stay here! the only upside was that the staff was friendly and the neighborhood is great.

“Great addition to SPG!” Love the W New York Downtown! Its very modern and the rooms are a great size for NYC. We stayed in a corner room on the 17th floor. We could see the WTC memorial site from our room. You can also see it from the living room bar on the 5th floor. When we arrived on Friday afternoon, the lobby and living room bar area was a bit crazy because a lot of people were coming up to get a glimpse of the memorial. There is construction still going on and I know that some people have complained about the noise from the construction - I don't think its any different than staying in times square. It didn't bother our sleep at all. The bathroom is a good size, not much room for storage though. We'll defiantly stay here again!

“The average hotel in a good location” The hotel is well situated next to Grand Central. Station. Checkin fast, friendly and helpful staff. Problem is the rooms that need renovation. Old furniture, dirty carpet on the floor. Room dark and not very clean. The rooms are too small but that is standard for New York. So the hotel has a very good service, but requires renovation.
