“One of the Best in Chicago” Just stayed Friday night at the Burnham (12/14/07). This is our Favorite Hotel in Chicago! Took advantage of the One day Sale in September, and received a great rate on the King Executive Suite. We had a corner room looking over State street, 6th floor. BEAUTIFUL ROOM, very spacious. Staff was Great. Centrally located in the Theater District. Quick trip from here up State to Morton's for dinner (1.5 miles, short cab ride). This is definitely a romantic hotel! Presently it is Noisy outside. They are building a new skyscraper across the street. You do not know what you'll "Hear". We were awoken at 4:30 am Satuday AM, for about 1/2 hour. So UNDERSTAND that this may not be a quiet experience. If you are looking for a First Class, romantic place, right in the loop. THIS is your hotel.

“Great Hotel, But...” My wife suprised me with a visit to Chicago for my Birthday to watch some baseball. We saved about $80 off our room with useing priceline's name your own price. The hotel itself was great! The bed was cozy, room was clean, lobby was nice, pool area and sun-deck was also very nice. I just find it odd that they charge you EXTRA to use the work out facility (aside from the pool which was free). Also, trying to get ahold of someone to bring up a couple of extra cups to the room took about 15 min! All in all, the hotel itself was nice, but service was below average and charging to use the workout room?? Come on.... If you are out of town and visiting Chicago, make sure to try Garrett's Popcorn, there are multiple stores downtown. Yummm....

“Nice Location Near Mall” The hotel itself was pretty nice but you definitely had your good and bad with this place. The good with this place was: (1) A "Large" mall across the street with places to dine inside; (2) Hotel provides hot breakfast with a cook that makes your own personal omelets (the bagels were hard and had to be heated before I could cut them); (3) A Manager's Reception with "Free" drinks and appetizers (i.e. chips, dried fruit, etc.) is offered to guest; (4) A restaurant located within hotel; (5) The hotel has two (2) swans (names Pa & Gram) in a built in swim tank located in the lobby; (6) Nice looking hotel; (7) Hotel shuttle service offered for transportation within three (3) mile distance; (8) They offer flavored water to guest in the lobby area and (9) pretty quick service from the maintenance staff. The bad with this place was: (1) The room was like an icebox (Even after I changed the temperature gauge to 80, several hours later it still read 62); (2) You cannot eat food in the hotel lobby that was brought in from outside (Apparently there is a law that forbids the consumption of outside food within their lobby area. This is the same area the bar and/or restaurant is located. You must either take it to your room or eat right at the front part of the lobby (This is not an ideal setting. There are no signs documenting this information. The staff walk up to you and advise if they catch you eating other food.); (3) Sometimes it takes a while for a clerk to answer the phone when attempting to set up the wake up service; (4) The pool is pretty small and located right off the lobby area; (5) The staff do not advise you of the surrounding area locations (Restaurants, entertainment, etc.) when checking in. This would be a nice gesture for visitors to the area.; (6) The clock was not set (This should be something the maid checks everytime a guest checks out.).; (7) A lamp with an outlet should be located on the desk in the bedroom. This way if you operate a laptop you do not have to get on the floor under the desk to plug up the adapter.; (8) The refrigerator made this loud sounding hum all day/night. The front desk staff were okay but it seemed as if the others you met working the hotel, such as the shuttle bus attendant, bartendar, maintenance and waitstaff, were more friendly. Overall I enjoyed my stay minus the small issues.

“Very Pleasant” Great location. Views from my room were great - could see the Navy Pier, John Hancock, etc. Bar on the lobby level is really nice. The gym is quite nice, but it was an extra charge. I was on the conceirge floor, and the food/drink amenties were a nice touch. Conceirge was helpful The rooms are nothing out of the ordinary, but, all in all, it was a very pleasant stay.

“WOW....The Lazy River was a HIT” WOW...Even though the wether was beastly hot, the "lazy River" brought us out everyday/night! My 8 year old just LOVED it! Nothing but good things to say . We were delayed checking in (check in 3PM but our room wasn't ready until 6PM) they PROMPTLY with out asking gave me a $100 credit to their restaurant. HAVE fun!

“Fantastic hotel, great location, would stay again.” This hotel is great. I stayed for 3 nights. It is a 4.5 star hotel with large rooms, great amenities, great location, etc. I would not hesitate to stay here again but did have a couple of small issues - see below. FYI - The taxi from the airport was around $40. I have almost no complaints about this hotel. It is everything I'd expect in a westin. The rooms were clean, they replaced bathroom amenities daily, beds were comfortable. I just have two complaints - one I wish they had better pillows rather than the ones that go flat when you put your head on them. I had to sleep with my arm under my pillow all night to prop my head up. The second - for some reason every night at 12:30am, perhaps there was a staff shift change, about 10 staff members, all hispanic ladies, seemed to gather outside our room and be chatting up a storm. The noise from the hall carries in really loud you'd have thought they were in our room. The first night we just put up with it but on the second night I opened the door to my room and they all hushed, a couple of them tried to make a break for it and scattered. On the third night of our stay there was a noticeable improvement as they seemed to have carried their conversation down the hall. This hotel is attached to the Prudential center complex, is only a block from 2 different subway lines, a block from trinity church, 5 min walk to lots of restaurants and shops. The business center allowed free boarding pass printing but you had to ask for it. I think they otherwise charge.

“Great Renovation” I really liked the renovation the hotel has had, modern, stylish rooms. I stayed for only one night so wanted cheapest rate, room was very nicely fitted out if a little small but it was only me. Other rooms are bigger and for a longer stay I would definitely upgrade. This hotel has a wonderful location right on Dupont Circle, near cafes, shops, easy walk to Georgetown. The hotel has a lively bar, didn't try the restaurant. I would stay here again. Convenient to the bus that runs between Washington and New York - see washny.com.
“Wonderful stay” "Friendly staff, clean rooms, quick room service, roof top pool with plenty of towels and chairs, free parking, what more could you ask for?

“OK budget hotel” Motel 6 on Military Road was OK. There were 4 of us in 2 rooms. Two double beds per room. The rooms were clean but worn. The bathroom was clean but needed work (broken tiles in the shower). On the plus side were the good water pressure and temperature in the shower. The mattress was good. The sheets and towels were rough but usable. No toiletries so bring your own shampoo etc. They do supply soap.

“Handicapped guests, good luck!” I booked this hotel after I read its reviews on Trip Advisor - believe them when they tell you the rooms are small. Here's proof: I was able to blow-dry my hair in the bathroom, with the blow-dryer plugged into the outlet on the desk. (I wasn't trying to pull a stunt, necessarily. The outlet in the bathroom didn't work.) BUT, I didn't read in the reviews that this hotel is not handicapped-accessible from the street - and that could be very important to your selection process. I discovered it coincidentally: I often travel with a very large, heavy suitcase. Thanks to the Americans with Disabilities Act, (ADA) I am confident that I will be able to roll this boulder into any hotel in the land, including an urban hotel like the Comfort Inn where the lobby is located about seven feet above street level up a set of steep steps. The ADA is a Federal law that mandates equal access to public facillities for everyone - including people who use wheelchairs. Apparently, it doesn't apply at this hotel... BE WARNED: THRE IS NO ELEVATOR from the street level to the lobby! There is a concrete pad on the side of the building where the elevator may SOMEDAY be, but there's no sign of any construction going on around it. (I got the distinct impression that the concrete pad is there simply as a ruse, since I believe that the hotel is in violation of the ADA as things stand now.) Ironically, the agency charged with enforcing the provisions of the ADA are probably in a tall building just a few miles away! I'd love to report this hotel to them but I don't know whom to tell. If you know, do it. The owners deserve to be educated. Oh, by the way: about my suitcase: the desk clerk called her son from the room behind the lobby desk and he hauled it up the stairs for me. I wonder how well he'd do with a 70-year-old!

“cushiest bed; friendliest staff” i normally stay in galleria. this particular week everything was booked and i ventured outside to west loop.... +cushiest bed and bedding. spent a week in hotel Icon downtown (#35) and this was a better sleep. by far. +huge room. i asked for a king single, got a queen double, massive room, good work table +friendly staff. had a little issue with a supplied furnishing... staff followed up immediately +housekeeping left a basket of fresh towels and amenities outside my door everytime i DND'ed. great touch i thought - i like my privacy and noones ever replenished when i DND elsewhere i cant find a single complaint. cant rank 5* cuz its a not a 5* hotel, but for what it was it my stay was flawless. will stay again.

“Excellent, beautiful hotel in a great location” This hotel is in the heart of downtown Seattle, very close to Pike's Market, a very nice indoor mall, restaurants, and a Light Link Rail stop. Beautiful floor-to-ceiling wood walls, updated rooms, and gourmet food. And the Fitness Center was a home run! It's a really fantastic hotel.

“Clean, Comfortable, Quiet, Friendly Staff....” What more can I say ... my title says it all. "Clean, Comfortable, Quiet and Friendly Staff"... Had a big corner room on the 18th floor with 2 huge windows overlooking all the lights of Broadway to one side and the empire state building to the other ... WOW what a treat. Breakfast the next morning was great ... freshly prepared omelets, strong and tasty coffee and friendly waiters. Front desk and porters also very friendly and efficient. Super convenient location. No complaints at all.

“Very nice Marriott” Stayed for one night for business. The lobby for this hotel is really large and beautiful. The center fountain area is a very soothing place to do some work. Room was extremely clean and comfortable, which I would expect from a Marriott. Location was great for me, within walking distance of my client. Lots of restaurants nearby.

“Great Location, Small Rooms” Hotel Mela was clean, quiet (great considering very central Midtown/Times Square location) and the staff were friendly and helpful. Similar to many NYC hotel rooms, if you're looking for space you won't find much more than the minimum here for the standard rooms. I believe there are suites available, which might be better for travelers intending to spend a lot of time working or relaxing in their rooms. Overall a good experience.

“Best Bed Ever” The bed in our "deluxe King" room was like sleeping on a cloud. At home, I have high thread-count linens, a featherbed, a duvet--but this was even better. Great robes, great towels. Large bathroom with good light (picture window over soaking tub made for super bathtime views when the city lights cam on.) Super location for subway or walking. The biggest negative for us was the lack of a bathroom door--a nightime trip to the bathroom meant the light could be seen from the bedroom. The door to the toilet room was partial, so all the sounds were shared. given the attention to every other design detail, I was surprised at this. If they can put a flat screen TV between the bath sinks, they should be able to figure out a bathroom door. Espresso machine and mini-microwave were nice, but no provisions for tea or mugs (just tiny espresso cups.) Lights a little hard to figure out (turns out 3 bulbs were burnt out) but my distress calls were answered quickly, politely, and competently. Small issues. Most of the concierge team were great--good suggestions and directions. One man, not so much--he said there wasn't a way to get to the Brooklyn Museum on the subway (hello, there is a stop called "Brooklyn Museum" on the Red Line.) Maybe what he meant was that his usual clientele didn't take public transportation!!

“Great location,great hotel” Stayed a night here for a meeting, literally there for 24 hours and 22 hours where at the hotel. Checkin was a breeze, four seasons service, theygave me a nice corner suite, but it was just me. Why do I get these when I am not travelling with my wife. Connected to the mall and all the great stores right on Michigan. Room was large and very well appointed, shower tub was soso. Decor was very updated. Interent in the room did not work very well, ended up using my MiFi. Beautiful lobby views, overall very nice. It is the only Ritz run by Four Seasons. Concierge and all staff were very friendly and helpful. I just feel that the fourseasons look needs some updating and not looking so worn in the common areas. Great Location, next door to the John Hancock building with the Observatory and the bar on the 94th and 95th floor.

“Both good and bad” I was more than pleased with my room, which was called a king suite I think. It had a marvelous bath (jacuzzi) tub and shower, nice bath products, comfortable bed and wonderful windows that opened all the way. It was also extremely clean. Really it was a great room and pretty reasonably priced for what I was getting. The TV was good, there was an interesting, decently priced minibar and a free paper, a good gym that was open 24 hours a day (which I love, I hate limited hours on recreation facilities, what if you can't sleep?) I kept thinking the whole time I was there that I was getting so much more that the guests at the Grand Hyatt for a much better price. They are across the street from each other. I had room service for dinner and for breakfast, both provided by the adjoining Dragonfish restaurant (Asian Fusion). Dinner was terrific, huge and hot. I think I ordered some chicken dish with noodles and vegetables (I don't remember what it was called) and it came with a salad. I also had a fancy cocktail which was tasty. I'd been there (to the Dragonfish) before, it's a really fun place for drinks. The breakfast wasn't good at all, undercooked french toast and missing strawberries, would not order breakfast again. I found the food to be quite fairly priced for room service and it arrived quickly both times. The lobby is very attractive also. What I didn't like about this hotel is the staff. They are clueless and not that nice. The person checking me in (may have been his first night) was alright but not that friendly. The person checking me out made disparaging comments about the person that checked me in and kept answering the phone and helping other people when she wasn't done helping me. She was supposedly more experienced than the other front desk employees but seemed incabable of issuing me a credit for missing items (from room service). It must have taken me twenty+ minutes to check out and I was pretty much the only person needing assistance. There was another person there, he was much nicer but seemed to not be that savvy with the computers. There was also a dispute with the woman at the front desk about a complimentary bottle of champagne (it states in their in-room about hotel information book that it's included in the price when you get that particular room), she said that it was only for people getting a certain package but that isn't what their book says. I didn't really need the champagne but I really didn't like her attitude, like I was making it up or something. She is definitely not an assett for this hotel. The main issue was getting my Coast rewards points for my stay, nobody seemed to know when they were to be awarded and the front desk lady didn't want to help me at all, she wanted me to call the 1-800 #, I think the other gentleman finally said that they would take care of it for me but I just checked and it wasn't done. I stayed there May 20th and it's now June 11th. So I did call their main Coast rewards # and that person said it should be fixed within 48 hours but she wasn't very nice either, making me not to keen to stay at a Coast hotel again. The server who brought my dinner was extremely nice and enhanced my positive experience but I think she worked for the restaurant.

“Not what I was expecting” New York was our last destination travelling across 9 cities of America before heading back to Australia,I was so excited to get to New York but that soon fizzled, After checking in which was super quick and the gentleman was so nice we went up to the room, Well for $2700 I didnt think it was worth it, The American express counter where we went to organise our travel back to the airport was un helpful I ended up doing it online my self and mind you not from free wifi , you had to pay and was friggin expensive over $20 a night,We then went to the tickets counter on to find a very rude gentlemen behind there, well lets just say we didnt see any broadway shows. The place itself was clean, and was smack back in the middle of Broadway, buts that where the wow factor ended.Out of the 9 hotels I stayed in over our 6 weeks stay this was the only one I gave a bad review about, the others were amazing.Sometimes staying in well know hotels is not worth it.

“Great Wedding Anniversary Getaway!” The Royal Palms is my new favorite place and probably the best well kept secret in Phoenix. I read all of the reviews on TripAdvisor when planning my anniversary getaway and can honestly affirm the positives. It is worth the money for rest and relaxation. When traveling from Sky Harbor Airport, you will want to get clear driving directions. We missed 2 turns, but once I finally broke down and had my wife ask for directions, we found it. Now that we have been there, it is easy to find on Camelback Road (but you will not find any signs along the way). Once on the property, we found ourselves in a different world. The reception staff welcomed my wife and me with a smile and accommodated us with an early check-in. We enjoyed an awesome Sunday Brunch at T. Cook’s (make reservations well in advance). Our Estate Room was a little dark for reading, even with all the lights on, but very comfortable and quiet which more than made up for it. The grounds are beautiful with orange and grapefruit trees and fountains and fireplaces and seating areas around almost every turn. What really differentiates Royal Palms is the intimacy of being in a smaller resort. Guest services were A+. Dinner at T. Cook’s was delicious (sit outside under the stars near the fireplace if you can). The Lounge was cozy. The Pool service was superb! Try the fish tacos – so good! Fruit and cold water was a nice touch in the fitness room. The hot tub was relaxing. The main pool was heated. The Alvadora spa rejuvenated my wife (try the “Tempting Trio”). Take a morning drive/walk around Camelback Mountain, which is a short distance away and the background setting at the Royal Palms. This place is a photographer’s paradise. Check out was a nice experience, with no surprises on the bill. This is not your kids’ kind of place. Take the entire family to one of the big resorts with multiple pools and structured programs if you’re into that type of experience. But for a special occasion for you and your spouse, you cannot go wrong in choosing the Royal Palms. It is first class. People are great. Prices are fair for the value. I highly recommend it and long to return again!

“Not for me” I stayed at this property a few years ago when it was the Ambassador East. I left after one night because of the small room size (we had 2 kids with us) and the rude service. Decided to give the new ownership a try because of its location close to Rush/Division Street bars on St Patrick's Day weekend. A previous post hit the nail on the head. This is a refurbished property not a renovated one. The lobby, bars and resturant are very modern. Check in was efficient. Asked for a room with a view - got a room on the eight floor with a view of the fire escape stairs, looking into the windows of another room on the 8th floor (hotel is an L shape configuration). Manager said this was best available. Ice machines are on the 8th and 17 th floors only. In a building with old elevators this could be an inconvenience. I get what the decorators were trying to do. Everything in the room is of small scale - apartment size furniture, platform bed (about 12 inches off the floor) , shelving all at a low level tying to give the space a taller feeling, small desk with small uncomfortable chair with a sheepskin throw on the chair. (Really - do I want to sit on a sheepskin and have white fuzzies all over my clothes? ) Room had a fine layter of dust on the furniture (evident because some of the furniture is black. Temperature is controlled by a wall thermostat - but that is somehow hooked up to the old wall unit under the window. There are no ventilation ducts in the entire room. Just this old noisy unit. Perhaps the hotel had not switched the air conditioning on yet - the weather was unseasonably warn and the room was HOT. Thermostat set to 65 did nothing to cool the room. The closet (which is a walk in) and bathroom were very uncomfortable. Bed was ok. No top sheet - which was weird. Towels were luxurious. No hot water in the morning. A call to guest services stated they were aware of the problem. (Previous posts also mentioned this - perhaps a recurring problem?) Maid service left no soap or shampoo despite the original bottles being used up. Towels were just set on the counter not hung up. The ambience of the hotel was just not for me. Seemed like a bunch of young people playing dress up, all trying to be something they are not. Felt like the hotel is trying to be the poor man's Ritz. I would not stay here again due to the arrogant aire everyone gave off. Also it is dog friendly and I try to stay away from places the allow dogs in the lobby - I just don't get that (and yes I have a dog). If you are here to enjoy the bars this is a good location. If you are into the shopping on Mag Mile there are far better locations. Price on Last MInute Travel was about $80 a night. It is worth no more than that.

“A fantastic addition to Denver” Stayed at the RC Denver one night for business. This is an excellent property and I would highly recommend for anyone visiting Denver. The hotel opened in early 2008 and the newness really showed. The rooms were extremely comfortable (although I received two queens despite requesting a king room). Beds were the highest, and among the most comfortable I've experienced. The bathroom was the real standout though. HUGE stand up shower with great shower head and a large soaking tub, separate water closet and double vanity sink. Really well done. Other highlights of the room included a large flat screen, dramatic room entryway and comfy lounge chair. Outstanding. Ordered room service twice and was quite pleased. Prompt delivery, friendly servers and quality food. The hotel provides access to an outstanding health club attached to the hotel. This is not the typical workout hotel workout room. Huge gym with large strength training area, pool, basketball courts, tons of exercise equipment, etc. Only negatives I experienced was a less than helpful front desk clerk early one morning when I couldn't find the gym. Overall, this is a excellent hotel and I look forward to a return trip.

“Very beautiful place. Very good staff (2 reviews in one)” I actually stayed here twice this month for business. 4 nights early in the month and 4 night 2 weeks later. I actually would give this place a 5 star the first stay, a 4 star the second stay for a total of a 4 1/2 stars for both. The hotel is right on the riverwalk. in fact, they have part of the riverwalk going right through the hotel. with a series of bridges and waterfalls, it is beautiful. No question about it. The location is perfect. 1-2 blocks from the Alamo, 2 blocks from the Rivercenter Mall. Lots of nice restaurants everywhere close. The staff is all nice. I can't believe it. If you go other places you will see, it does not compare. I had a situation that happened with a mix up in rooms. It was a big mistake by Hyatt. And, they rectified it immediately. I was impressed. I am 49. I know anyone can make mistakes. How you react to those mistakes makes the difference. This place is #1. They gave my room to someone else. I was disappointed, but they stepped up and did a great job of rectifying this and helping me to feel better about it. Hyatt hires people who care. If you arrive early, Hyatt will do everything possible to get you into the room you want, if possible. The rooms are nice. The beds, pillows, and air conditioners in all rooms I have stayed in this hotel are nice. In Texas, you do not want a hotel whose A/C is "ok" you want one that works good. All I have been in here are great. I have stayed here 4 times total. I really wanted to give this hotel a "5" but I give honest reviews... and really.. a 4 1/2 is due because of the mistake and the charge for internet. If you stay here you are getting a 5 star hotel. Thank you Hyatt Regency San Antonio, you and your staff do a great job.
“Great location and a good value” I have stayed here a few times and would stay again. Good location, simple hotel, but nice new rooms, quiet and the beds are great.

“Great hotel....with a few flaws” I stayed recently at the Smyth hotel with a friend of mine. I had booked us 2 rooms through Quikbook at a wonderful price of 145$ per night. I thought that it was an excellent value for the price. I will list the pros and cons of this newly opened hotel. It is still in a soft opening so it still has a few flaws that they will probably work out over the next months. PROS: *The rooms are just beautiful and huge by New York standards. Attention is paid to small details like a flower in bowl on the night stand. They are also very clean. You have a huge plasma television with a digital signal. Many hotels have plasma televisions but an analog signal, they have the real deal here. I also did not hear the neighbors. It is a very silent hotel, except for the doors that slam loudly. *The concierge Ela is excellent. She pointed us towards great restaurants. I had never stayed in Tribeca so I was not familiar with the area and she sent us to a couple of great restaurants (Marc Forgione, Gigino, Il Buco). She makes great suggestions. Some concierges either want to send you to high end restaurants like Per se or dives where there are 3 tables. She is in the middle of that and it was perfect for us. *Tribeca...I just loved this area! It is filled with great restaurants, shops, beautiful streets. I would stay there again. I heard people say that it is out of the way but you are close to so many subway lines and buses that we never had any problems going anywhere quickly. CONS: *Soft opening...Since they have been opened recently, some of the rooms are still not furnished entirely. I did not have a full length mirror, but my friend's room had one. My friend's room did not have a towel rack so she did not have any place to hang her towels, but I had one. You can see that they are small things though. *Service...The Thompson hotels chain prides itself in the service they offer to their clients. I stayed 6 times at the 6 Columbus hotel and found the employees, except the concierge, to be a notch above the ones at the Smyth. It is only by a hairline, but a hairline none the less. The doormen are friendlier at the 6 Columbus, even if you are not a 20 something supermodel. They treat everyone the same which I did not sense at the Smyth. They were a bit more standoffish. All in all, I would recommend this hotel because I really enjoyed my stay there.

“Great weekend” Stayed at the Conrad over the weekend before July 4th. It was a wonderful stay. This hotel has great service and location. We made reservations about 10 days before our stay. And twice was able to rebook at a lower price prior to arrival. We had an executive king room. It had a bed that made it very difficult to get up in the morning, it was so comfortable. Not often that you can stay at a hotel of that quality for just over $200/night.

“Small, clean, cheap good location. OK for fun but not for work.” I stayed at this property for 1 night while visiting Camp Pendleton and needed a hotel near the airport for the outbound flight in the morning. It is 10 minutes from the airport. They do not have their own shuttle. Shuttle service is coordinated through Super Shuttle and/or taxis which are paid for by the property. This is a Choice Hotels property, so I didn’t expect much. I stayed in room 409 which is a standard King. The room is small but well kept. From an entertainment prospective, it seemed fine. Good location near many restaurants and bars. Only two short blocks to Fifth Street. The room had it’s own, window mounted A/C unit which was noisy, as was the overhead fan which hummed constantly. I shut both of them off during my stay. There was moderate street noise in the room, with an occasional police or fire truck going by. Typical large city noises. The room has a micro/fridge combo with coffee maker and small sink in the sleeping area. The bathroom is the size of a Chicklet , but was clean. It has a 32” flat screen TV. If you’re here for work, like me, this room falls short. The work desk is small and has a horrible chair. There is only ONE outlet for use with laptops, etc. The bed was good but the pillows were cheap and lumpy. The staff was cordial, but not overly friendly. Parking was $16.00 for a surface lot behind the hotel which is not monitored. Overall I would give the property a 78/100 and 90/100 for value. I would consider staying again, but would also see what else was available nearby. PROS: Price, location, good value for price bad CONS: Small rooms, horrible work area, street noise at night

“Nice Surprise!” I booked this room last minute and hoped for the best. What a great surprised on arrival! This is a new, clean and well-appointed hotel. There is a super nice restaurant/lounge/bar in the lobby with TVs in every booth. It was great to watch the news while eating breakfast. The front desk and breakfast staff were all very friendly. The rooms were nice and clean and the whole place had a fresh appearance and feel to it. It's extremely close to the airport which is convenient but can make it a little loud. I didn't notice any noise inside the room though. I would definitely recommend this property - especially for business travelers.

“Omni great as usual” We stay at an Omni in any city that they have one (build more!). This short weekend trip was picked due to the fact that Austin has the Omni. When we arrived, the bell staff and front desk are awesome. Tip them WELL. Valet is very quick and efficient. We are frequent Omni visitors and have stayed at almost every hotel. We were upgraded to a suite that was sweet. They are in the process of updating but you could not ask for more room and the private elevator was nice as well. If I had to complain, the room on the 6th street side of the building can be noisy from the street music but this is no fault of the hotel. Great management as quality like this does not happen otherwise.

“It's Reasonable for a Downtown San Diego Hotel” This hotel sits on top of the San Diego Opera House. We made a big mistake and parked our own car rather than valet. The parking is so bizarre! You wind up through this horrible twisting ramp all the way up to the 10th floor. If you are going to stay here just valet. The rooms are real nice. They have a nice big bed and a nice sized bathroom with a smaller suite area. It is best to get a room with a king bed - the double beds make the suite feel much smaller. We had a nice view. The hotel staff is very nice and they were always helpful. The odd thing is that this hotel doesn't seem to be located in that great of an area. We walked around a lot and it is a little seedy. However I thought the price was reasonable for staying downtown and the rooms were nice.

“If you need to be on 10 west ...” This is an "OK" property. The rooms are large and quiet. It feels "sprawling" because the hallways are long and winding. The food was not particularly good. The staff were fine. The biggest issue I had was location. It is right at 6 and 10. You can easily get on the HOV lane and to the shuttle bus to downtown. You can easily get onto 10 or 6. The only thing that isn't easy is getting into the hotel itself. The entrance is small and located off the side road. There is no entrance off 6. Late afternoon when the HOV exit and buses are running it can be hard to find the hotel entrance behind the traffic.It's not the hotel's fault (although a bigger sign wouldn't hurt). Just look for the hotel and realize the entrance is off the side.

“Great Value in a Great Location” This hotel is in an excellent location. It is walking distance to the convention center, Reading Market, Liberty Bell, and most historical sites. It is also walking distance to many great restaurants and bars. The hotel has no restaurant but does serve breakfast and snacks. The continental breakfast was good and included bagels, good local pastries, cereal, and fruit. And the breakfast hours were very convenient, and breakfast was open late on weekends. The snacks were the pastries from breakfast and fruit which was a really nice touch. The rooms and bathrooms are on the small side but well designed, so that there is a closet and small fold out desk. Most historic hotels in older buildings have smaller rooms, so that is to be expected. There is free wifi in the rooms which is nice. Overall, the room was clean and comfortable. The staff is very friendly and helpful with recommending all sorts of restaurants and places to go see. I will definitely stay at this hotel again if I'm back in Philadelphia.

“Pricey but nice place” The Marriott Rivercenter has a trendy lobby, great service, comfy room, great night of sleep. Close to everything, including being attached to the mall. Pricey but all the big brand hotels in the area are.

“The location can't be beat” Time and time again I return to this hotel when traveling on business. The location is awesome with many wonderful restaurants and bars within walking distance. The rooms are kept clean and the maids do a good job of freshening them up daily. I also looked at their website and found a coupon to be upgraded to a suite for free which was a nice plus as the room was more spacious and included a refrigerator and a small couch, chair, and table area. Bathroom was nice and clean, bed was comfortable, can't complain about much. It is a little annoying to navigate as the hotel is in two building and only connects on the 4th floor. Also shower pressure and temperature wasn't great and I found it difficult to get the thermostat on a good temperature and was constantly adjusting. Staff is nice and helpful and parking is free which is a good cost savings if you have a car. The hotel isn’t perfect and the hallways are semi-dated but the rooms are refreshed, comfortable, and clean. I’ll be back.

“Close to the Convention Center” I stayed here for three nights while in LA for a conference at the Los Angeles Convention Center which is a five minute walk from the hotel. There’s a number of restaurants within a block and the Staples Center is across the street. The staff was very friendly. The property is basic Holiday Inn and shows quite a bit of wear. This is the only hotel I’ve been in that requires you to use your room keycard to operate the elevator.

“Perfect for waiting for a flight!” Hotel is old, but they keep it in great shape. You get a huge room, very clean, everything you need in the room except for fridge, free shuttle service to the airport. Very friendly staff. Just the internet was too slow, but at least for free.

“Muy lejos de todo y con una limpieza muy mejorable” Nosotros fuimos a San Diego para la Comic Con y este era uno de los hoteles concertados con la convención. Como reservamos bastante tarde, había poco donde elegir, así que nos quedamos con éste. Está muy lejos del Centro de Convenciones (por suerte había un autobús gratuito durante la convención) y también de todas partes, rodeado de autopistas. El parking es de pago y también el wi-fi (pero hay un Starbucks y un Barnes & Noble justo al lado con acceso gratuito). No es barato y desde luego la calidad-precio no es nada buena. El personal es atento pero la limpieza es deficiente. La primera noche de estancia (de cinco) se me cayó un trozo de patata al suelo mientras cenábamos y seguía ahí cuando nos fuimos. Unos días nos faltaban vasos (se llevaban los sucios pero no los reponían), otros toallas, y encima de los tres ascensores sólo uno funcionaba, lo que hacía épica cada entrada y salida de la habitación.

“You Can Probably Do Better” Stayed one night during a family reunion in area. Clerk Gloria at front desk very friendly and helpful. Check in easy. Room was much smaller than I thought it would be. I've stayed in La Quinta and Red Roof Inns that were larger. Room clean and very nice, just small. Had to go to desk to get shampoo. Heard another guest asking for coffee for in room coffee maker since his room had none. Bed is so close to AC unit that the bedspread clogged up the intake and the unit cut itself off during the night. Breakfast okay (muffins, instant oatmeal) but I had to ask them to put out more muffins and coffee. Barking dog in nearby room woke us at 11, but staff called the room and I guess they took care of it. This is hotel is not AT and Arboretum, but SOUTH of it four or five exits. Paid just under $80. Would not stay there again because you can stay in larger room in a different chain for less.

“Okay Stay” We booked our hotel through hotwire. It was a decent hotel, nothing spectacular. The main thing is that the check in clerks were very nice and helpful. The room was basic and clean. Parking was only $10, which wasn't too bad for staying downtown. We were only a short distance from the trolley which we took to Beale St. The only negative was that I was desperate for food and ordered room service desserts. It was some of the most awful tasting food! I'm not at all picky, but couldn't take more than a couple bites. Overall, this wasn't a bad hotel for the budget conscious traveler that would like to stay downtown Memphis

“Wasn't here long, but I'll be back!” I was just here overnight, but I'll definitely stay here again. It is a very convenient location to UT Health Sciences Building and Memorial Hermann Hospital, which is why I choose this location. The staff was very friendly and helpful and the Starbucks downstairs was a definite plus! Room was clean, bed was comfy, and no hairs in the bathroom! Great hotel!

“Wonderful Room, But Cold Hospitality” My husband and I stayed here in a suite this past Monday night and were very happy with the decor and space in the room yet very unhappy with the way we were treated. I am not sure if it is because we are a younger couple (I am 24 but look 18) but we were treated very coldly by all the hotel employees *except the concierge* which was incredibly strange since we were staying in a suite. From check in to check out we were treated very unfriendly at the front desk so we made sure to spend almost all of our time away from the hotel. The concierge however was incredibly helpful. He spent a good 10 minutes helping us plan a daytrip up past Boulder to Estes. It was a beautiful drive and I recommend it to other travelers looking to get out of the city. We had free Wi-Fi internet which worked well and did not take advantage of the other amenities such as breakfast and happy hour. Parking was quite expensive, we parked in a lot next door to the hotel and were told that if you planned to go in and out the valet parking was the cheapest but if you did not plan on using your car the self-parking was cheaper. Nearby restaurants were pretty lacking, we asked for recommendations for nearby restaurants and noted that we had three vegetarians in the party, but were recommended three places that had no vegetarian options. Fortunately a waiter at one of the restaurants sent us to a vegan/vegetarian place in uptown called Watercourse (which was excellent). All in all our room was wonderful with a fireplace and fridge, but the service at the front desk was so inhospitable that we will not be staying here again anytime soon. Maybe when I am older as they seem to be ageists here.

“Nice Hotel” Staff needs to be in uniforms (especially night auditor). Stayed 2 nights, a Thursday and a Sunday. Hard to find with construction and when I called the hotel to see where it was from the Microtel, she did not know where the Microtel was - it was just on the other side of the Interstate. Halls and rooms need "edging" - much dust. Airport transportation was convenient - but I was surprised they charge tax on this service? (requirement in IND). Hotel was not as close to the airport - but then the Indy airport is all grown up now.

“lukewarm staffs, garage elevator issues ...” I was locked up in garage elevator P1 for more than 10-20 minutes. Door won't open and then suddenly it went one level down while they working on it. Security guards open the door for me by hand. I notified FD but didn't hear back during my stay. Elevator went on service immediately after the incident. I got an impression that they didn't performing some maintenance. Peoples I talked to seem to be awared that issue. I was granted access to exec. lounge as a hh member. I tried both of breakfast and evening entree. I don't think it is worth to travel to lounge after swiping ten times each to access the lounge and my room. I don't know why my keys are not working correctly even after a reprogramming. Overall, don't use P1 elevator and staffs seemed uninterested.

“Not Just for Fun- This is a Great Hotel for Meetings, too!” I represent an international consortium of cell phone manufacturers. One of my responsibilities is to organize events for 80-100 senior technology executives for one week of intensive meetings three times per year. My customers are frequent world travelers, and are quite discerning regarding the food and services they receive while traveling. My opinion and experience is that the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peaks is by far one of the best North American business meeting locations that we have used in the past 10 years. For worry-free meetings and events, I would not hesitate to again put my full faith in the service and quality of the Hilton North Point Squaw Peaks. Pros: *Excellent Sales Staff: My representative was the same person from start to finish- great continuity. *All-Pro Banquet staff: Some of the best in the business, the core Team has low turnover and superb attitudes and skills. *Superior food: The Pointe Hilton Chef and Staff provide food of the highest quality with "Farm to Fork" style whenever possible. Ingredients and selection are top-grade! *Complete refurbishment of the resort is nearly complete. The property upgrade was planned well as to be virtually transparent to the guests. *True HD television: so many hotels provide updated TV's while still feeding those sets with outdated (cheaper) analog signals. Pointe Hilton provides a wide variety of HD channel selections. *The in-house Audio/Visual team will help you pull off a successful meeting without a hitch! Any minor issues were taken care of with the highest priority. *Fast Internet: property has some great bandwidth to the door and they say they are adding even more capability! Cons: *Limited restaurant selections off-property within walking distance. Grocery stores and services are close by, however. (about 1/2 mile) *Slow elevators: luckily, it's only a three-story complex. *Tap water was "murky" smelling and tasting. This is mostly the fault of the local water utility, but I hope Squaw Peaks Hilton would address this issue. Be sure and drink bottled water, IMHO. *Confusing to navigate on-site. It's a large property, and the North building is identical to the South Building. Be sure and get a map! *Luggage carts are locked up, forcing you to call for a bell-captain. Sometimes I just want to do it myself! *Annoying voice mail SPAM advertising: We would arrive back to our sleeping rooms to see the message light lit, just to find out the message was an advertisement for the Spa services! we have never experienced this in any hotel anywhere in the world. In this day and age of SPAM and advertising overload, I hope the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak would reconsider this strategy.

“Great Hotel and location” I travel to NYC about 7-8 times a year. This is my first visit to the Sofitel. I got an average rate of $240 a night over four nights for a King bed on a lower floor. The overall experience was very good, very comfortable and hospitable. The bed was excellent. I will come back to the Sofitel again soon. NY City hotels have really gone up in price over the last year and I can't find anything in the $250-325 range as good as the Sofitel anywhere in the city. The room was large by NY standards. I can't remember the last time I had a shower and seperate bath in a NYC hotel. The location is great. Although this hotel isn't a "scene", it is relaxing and hospitable. What would I change? The menu is expensive. (Food is good) The workout room needs towels and tuned up machines. The carpeting in my room was starting to show it's age and the room had a strong lingering air freshener smell.
“Nice property” Stayed here for a convention. Walking distance to the convention center and close to 6th street where all the nightlife happens. Nice accommodations but ask for an exterior room.
“Comfortable and convenient” Located downtown, very convenient to convention center and restaurants. Typical room with no frills, but a larger bathroom than average. Loved the Starbucks in the lobby!

“Great Stay! Can't wait to come back” I booked a "Renew Your Soul" staycation. Nevertheless, I was excited to look forward to an excuse to spend a Saturday night out in NYC. To top it off, the rate included a $10 mini bar credit, $10 metrocard, $10 coffee card, 1 free-in room movie, and access to the health spa and fitness center. I arrived at the property around 11 am, and check in was a breeze. At check in, I was not asked to choose my gold amenity, nor was I given my $10 metrocard or $10 coffee card. Once I was settled in my room, I called the front desk to activate my in-room wifi as my gold amenity selection. The woman on the phone kept repeatedly telling me that it would cost me $14.95 for 24 hours, and that wifi was only offered as an amenity to platinum guests. After going back and forth a few times, she finally apologized and told me that wifi was indeed offered as a gold amenity. I’m surprised that such a high-volume SPG hotel would be so unsure about their elite amenity choices. Either way, I told management about that little miscommunication and they made it right immediately. I commend the attentiveness manager, Miguel M.'s promptness of taking care of me - that goes to show you that excellent customer service is a priority at the hotel. I also asked about the $10 metrocard and coffee card that was included in my rate. It turns out that they did not have any available at the moment, and then told me that they’d have to mail them to my home address. That was a bit disappointing, but I’m sure I’ll receive them (or at least I hope I do...). I was given a king room on the 12th floor, and the room itself was wonderful, comfortable, and spacious for NYC. The bed sure did live up to its “heavenly” claims. In fact, I think it has to be the single most comfortable hotel bed I’ve slept in to date! The room was quiet (no street noise what-so-ever), and the bathroom had a double-headed shower which provided amazing water pressure. Before heading out for the evening, I kicked back and watched my in-room movie (That’s My Boy), and I sure was glad that the in-room movie was included in the rate (my movie selection was priced at $16.95). I also enjoyed 2 cans of diet Coke ($5.50 each) to apply my $10 mini-bar credit. As far as the fitness center/spa access, I’m too ashamed to admit that I chose a burger and fries at Shake Shack (...and I even went back for custard) instead of utilizing the health center facilities, so I can’t really provide a genuine “renew your soul” assessment in that regards... The awesome double shower heads provided great water pressure! In-room coffee, minibar, and safe.

“Ce Magnifique” It is difficult to find a hotel to exceeds expectations so regularly as the Sofitel Water Tower. Begin with the "French touch" which shows in the staff, the music, the breakfast service and the room amenities. The location is close to everything and yet tucked away in a tree covered park triangle, if you can be tucked away on Rush. Everything about the hotel is well-planned from the check in to the room arrangements. They have some great deals on rates including an extra night "free" or included in the price for certain weeks. Clean, spotless, well-appointed rooms. Super fast elevators. Great business centers in two locations with no quibbling about printing copies. Valet or self-park next door. A number of local grocers in the same block if you just want some fresh fruit, yogurt and a brioche. Great selection of restaurants nearby. Although didn't eat out much on this trip. Concierge Justin knowledgeable and helpful about all kinds of events. In fact, the entire staff is a plus. Quite a great place to stay.

“Fabulous Hotel” Recently had the pleasure of staying at the Boston Harbor Hotel, in a Harborview Suite. First off, there is the most amazing view of the harbor and environs - the boats, the birds flying, the skyline - it made greeting each morning so joyous. The room itself was immaculate, with every amenity that one could ask for. Service was excellent - prompt and courteous. The pool and spa were beautiful and well equipped. Had a body polish treatment, and it was done with great professionalism and enthusiasm by Marta. Did not find out until we were leaving for the airport, that they have town cars at the disposal of the guests, at no cost. Now that's a service very few hotels provide. All in all, would highly recommend the Boston Harbor Hotel.

“Paper thin walls problematic” The New York Palace is indeed a decent hotel - the location can not be beat. I found it clean although the furnishings were slightly tarnished. The problem we had was the fact that the walls were paper thin. This became a real problem when we were awoken by loud screaming in the wee hours of the morning. I mentioned this to staff upon checking out with no apology from the staff.....

“Very Nice Property” I needed a hotel for a night and booked this at the last minute. I normally don't stay at "courtyards" as I have found most had been pretty basic and beat up. Much to my surprise, this property was quite nice. My room had two very comfortable queen size beds, a sitting area and a decent size, very clean bath. Best bang for the buck I have received in NYC, including some of the "posh" places like the Ritz and Four Seasons. Outside of the room there were not alot of ammenities but then it's NYC, outside the city is full of them. Worth the stay.

“Great location, cool rooms pity about the cold service” The bold industrial decor of the room is very contemporary ad won't suit everyone's taste but if you enjoy design or fashion, this would be a good choice. It's clear from the other guests staying here that it was the choice of the young and hip. The floor to ceiling windows are striking and provide an interesting view of NYC. The bed was comfy and the sheets were a nice thread count. There are monumental backlit white boxes with botanical themes printed on them above each bed providing a focal point for the room and interesting lighting for romantic moments. I stayed in three different rooms and found them all quiet. The thermostat worked well. The 'rain' head in the shower is another feature although it was so high tech we couldn't get it to work at will. The shower is huge - definitely enough room for two. The bathroom is stocked with organic toiletries by Bigelow. I spent my entire stay there smelling like lavender and peppermint. We had fun in the bar on the second floor - there's all kinds of random modernist furniture to roll around on as you get drunk on overpriced drinks. I had the room service breakfast -$48US for two greasy pork sausages, oily eggs, hash browns, oj and coffee. I ate about 1/3 of it. Also they didn't seem to want to take my room service order because I prepaid my stay. I had a lot of troubles with service at the hotel. I think I got poorer service because I prepaid and got a discount through an internet booking site. The room I got was massive and cost about 1/3 of what it should have so I think the staff thought I had gotten my value for money already. For example my television didn't work and it took ten phone calls to get some action on that. I was sick and just wanted to lie in bed and watch TV. That doesn't seem like such an incredible request but the front of house people rolled their eyes, looked at each other and failed to act time after time. The Thomson is a cool hotel in a fantastic location (public transport is across the road, you can walk to the East Village, Chinatown, Brooklyn). Having said that it feels like you are staying in money making machine. The staff are a bit cold but just give it back to them - they work in a hotel after all, not in the fashion industry

“ok, courtyards better” an upscale brand, but I'd prefer the courtyards, of which there are several in DC (I prefer the one around 9th and F. -- loud music everywhere -- no free pc's in lobby (although there is Wifi) -- no coffee in lobby -- room a little small, and bathroom definately small (other marriott rooms larger) -- lobby trendy and cool, but too dark. -- location a few blocks from metros and the circulator bus

“Very Dissapointed” The hotel is actually ok but my experience was negative due to the shuttle service from the airport. I waited over 45 minutes for a shuttle and finally gave up and caught a taxi for the 2 mile ride. Granted the hotel did reimburse me and gave me 20,000 points for my troubles but the wait had already made me vow never to book this property again. I called the hotel 3 times and was told each time that the shuttle was coming- unfortunately I was waiting at terminal 7 (United terminal) so each time a shuttle passed it was full and made no stops. The room was older but quiet and overall comfortable but the 45 minute plus wait is no way to treat a customer. One recommendation for other travellers is to take the Hilton shuttle and walk back to the Marriott (at least 5 Hilton shuttles came by during my wait).

“Great hotel but extras are expensive” I couldn't believe how wide the hallways were (weird I know) and the rooms are very comfortable with great lighting and effective/efficient desk areas. Bathrooms are large. Extras get you: Wifi $13.00, onsite restaurant is a bit expensive for dinner, even the business center minimum $5.00. But this is a full service Hilton (unlike a Hilton Garden Inn where many options would be free) so you are paying for a full service Hilton. Obviously the number one item is the location next to University of Pennsylvania and the UPenn Hospital system. Restaurants are with a block or two of the hotel with many different types and price ranges. SEPTA station is a few blocks away (we stopped at the University SEPTA station instead of 30th Street and it is a bit shorter of a walk (but may not seem like it)). Only issue: UGH - come on: 15 or so television channels! Highly recommended if you have business at UPenn.

“Fantastic Hotel - would stay here again & again!” I stayed at this hotel for 18 days during August and it truly felt like my home away from home. There were too many brilliant staff members to name 'the good ones', they were all fantastic... from the bell hops and security guys who would always have a ready smile, to the catering staff who went out of their way to make sure that I was well fed and looked after, the front desk staff, who vere helpful and efficient and the amazing housekeeping staff who always ensured my room was emaculate and well stocked. I was so happy with the staff that I left a thank you card when I checked out. Being a wheelchair customer the staff went above and beyond the call of duty in making sure I was well looked after, or so I initially thought.. the longer I was there, the more I realised that I was getting their standard treatment of all customers. I was seriously impressed. The rooms were very comfortable with a great kitchen area that had a full sized fridge/freezer and all the pots/pans, toasters, plates, cutlery and other utensils required. The bathroom was kept very clean with a good stock of towels, facecloths etc. There were many free 'extras' provided including a great buffet breakfast, hotel wide high speed wi-fi, free use of their in house computers and a printer, free use of washing machines and driers, which included free detergents, bleach and softeners and 3 nights a week they hosted a 'sundowner' - during which they provided beers, wines, sodas and finger foods - providing a great opportunity to get to know other people in the hotel or a quick bite to eat before catching a play on Broadway. The location was fantastic.... very safe, within the Times Square area without the noise factor. Close to all Metro train lines and buses. Definitely my first choice of hotel next time I visit New York City. Aboslutely nothing even the most jaded traveller could pick on! Loved it.

“Glad to be back” This was our second visit in 6 months, the first having had a couple of service hiccups. This time, the stay was flawless. We arrived at 7:30 in the morning fresh off the Queen Mary 2 and were happy to find a room was ready. all the service staff go out of their way to be friendly and helpful. The rooms are well appointed, and we appreciated the lights being on dimmers. The windows open, but once closed, there is silence. Beds are extremely comfortable. With just a handful of rooms on each floor, the hotel feels like a real sanctuary. We can't wait to come back.

“Clean, comfortable, 2-star motel” To picture this Best Western, it's a 3-story "U" shape, with all rooms opening to the parking lot and tiny pool, and 2-person hottub. The tiny pool (and entire property) were teaming with children, as this hotel is only one freeway exit away from Sea World and inexpensive for San Diego at $150 a night (with AAA discount). The parking lot, BTW, was the tightest and most difficult we have ever seen for a hotel. Cars were wedged in so tightly, that in the morning when we left, someone was helping a Prius (!) back out without hitting other cars. Room 319 was one of only about 3 rooms containing a king-sized bed. (The others have 2 queens.) The room was averaged sized, and contained a small refrigerator, microwave, desk, and love seat. The bathroom had the floor space of a bathroom stall, with the sink outside. The accomodations were very basic, yet clean and comfortable like the old Motel 6 commerical claims. Unlike some other reviewers, we saw no bugs. For the most part, we found the motel to quiet down from the hours of 9 pm to about 7 am, although the ice machine outside our room sounded like a small avalanche. And there were some loud footsteps and luggage dragging outside in the middle of the night. My partner, who can never turn down a free meal, reports that the continental breakfast consisted mostly of cereal, watered down orange juice, unwatered down juices (apple and passion fruit), and packaged yogurt. On day 2, the orange juice machine wasn't working. The breakfast was crammed into a converted first-floor motel room, and when he finished breakfast at about 6:50 am, crowds of parents and children were waiting to get into the small space. If you're looking for a no-frills, kid- and pet-friendly motel that's inexpensive by San Diego standards, you might want to look into this motel. OTOH, I've stayed at many Best Westerns, and this motel is not as nice as any of them.

“Full Service?” Let me start by saying that I like the Holiday Inn chain. Whenever possible, I try to stay with a Holiday Inn property because (at least until this last stay) I get consistantly good service and value. This property is very clean and in a good location, but the service is horrible. I made reservations three weeks in advance for my family of four (2 adults, 2 Middle School types) with 2 beds and "late arrival". Upon check-in around 6 PM, the hotel manager told me that there were not any 2-bed rooms available. We could have a room with a single bed and a sofa, but they were out of roll-away beds as well. He explained that some guests had simply decided not to check out so my family was without a room. There was nothing that he could do about it. I explained that we had driven for 5 hours and asked if they could contact a nearby Holiday Inn. They said there was no need as they were without rooms as well. I then gave him my reservation number (again) and this time, "oh - here it is. We were looking at the wrong number. Yes - you have a room". He then offered me two free buffet-style breakfast tickets for the four of us to enjoy. Upon arrival in the room, we discovered that housekeeping had given us two towels for our reservation of four. The front desk happily gave me two more - that I could pick-up at the front desk. The next day housekeeping left an extra towel bringing the total count to three towels for four people. The property is nice, but the service was a real disappointment. I expect more from a Holiday Inn. Next time - well - there probably won't be a next time at Fossil Creek.

“A Tired, Worn Out Hotel” Stayed here for one night because of its location at the airport. Possibly the worst Marriott I have stayed at. The room was worn and dated. Room service was terrible. It took almost an hour and then they got two things wrong with a simple order. I asked for no cheese on the burger and it came with cheese. I asked for a baked potato instead of fries and it came with mashed potatos that looked and tasted like they were concoted by a Martian. I did not call to complain because I didn't want to wait another hour. The hotel was also grossly overpriced, costing about the same as the JW Marriott I stayed at the night before which was truly 5 star. My guess is that the hotel gets its business because of its location and they don't think they need to update or give good service.

“guter Preis und top Lage” Das ist ein echter Tipp für Kurztrips nach NYC. Die Neighborhood von Murray Hill ist übersichtlich, recht sicher und gut gelegen. Wir haben 4 Nächte in einem small double room gebucht und waren extrem zufrieden - neues Bad, Holzboden, alles sehr ordentlich und sauber. Die Jungs von der Rezeption waren sehr hilfreich und man konnte am letzten Tag das Gepäck kostenlos hinterlegen. Einziger Nachteil war der fehlende Aufzug und die Tauben im Hinterhof, von denen man morgens geweckt wurde... aber ansonsten echt ungewöhnlich ruhig und gutes Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis. Wenn man im Zimmer wirklich nur schlafen will und tagsüber die Stadt erkunden möchte ist das der richtige Ort zum Übernachten.

“Upscale hotel at affordable rates” Le Meridien is among the most upscale of the Starwood brands, and it shows at this property. My standard king room was incredibly spacious, with full-size couch, easy chair, central work area with electronics "hub" (USB, ethernet, etc.), LCD television, and a comfortable-to-the-point-of-luxurious bathroom. The staff was exceedingly professional and pleasant and comped my valet parking because the room was not ready when I checked in. (Note: valet parking is the only type available, unless you want to take your chances in the Galleria garages across the street.) The lobby bar and restaurant is surprisingly affordable and the food is delicious. Best of all, fantastic deals can be had through 3rd party booking sites.

“It seems to cater to North Americans more than Int'l travelers” Spent 3 nights at the Pan Pacific. Aside from the lousy weather, it was a pleasant stay. The hotel is located on the edge of downtown so it is a bit of a walk to Seattle’s major attractions. The hotel entrance is hard to find but the building can be seen from afar. The Whole Foods at its base is a benefit but everything it sells is over-priced. The Starbucks next door is very convenient. At night, that location is very dark and deserted. The room that I stayed in faces Lake Union but soon the views will be blocked by some buildings under construction. The room modern décor is similar to other Pan Pacific hotels but the bathroom is spacious and it has a separate bathtub and shower. The bed was comfortable and the linens were of high quality. The flat-screen TV had a good selection of channels but there were too many sport channels. The desk was large and I really appreciated the charging dock because I only had a USB cable without the socket adaptor. The toiletries were of good quality. The room has a coffee maker but if you would like to have tea, you must call their service number for complimentary tea bag. I wondered who would bother to call just to get someone to bring you one tea bag. I also wondered why someone would bother to make generic bland coffee if a Starbucks is downstairs. The only issue I found really annoying is the front desk people being overly chatty. When I arrived at the front desk to check out, two front desk ladies kept chatting with someone who is checking in, making me wait needlessly long. I could understand if it was hotel related business but they were chatting about trivial things and yet they did see me waiting. Don’t they know that the guest’s last impression counts just as much as the first?

“Disappointed” I expected a full-service Marriott in the heart of a major city to be . . . well, better. It's a very large hotel that gives a somewhat impersonal feel. Check-in was slow -- they had an Elite check-in but, with people standing in front of the sign, I didn't see it and so waited in line for about 10 minutes. Despite several people in line, there was no effort to bring additional people to the reception desk. The room was dingy. No other way to describe it. Decor was outdated, TV was old-style, small (20") and not easy to see from any place in the room other than the bed. The room was dark and small. The bathroom was serviceable at best and the towels were thin and gray. Because it is an old building, the windows are tiny and there is no view, even from the high floors. I felt I was in a Courtyard -- which is fine if you're paying Courtyard prices. Although a Marriott platinum member, my room seemed as far from the Concierge lounge as possible -- several floors and a long, long walk. The lounge was much more impersonal than those in most Marriotts and very crowded. They asked me if I wanted a newspaper (I said yes) and then didn't deliver one. Both keys stopped working, necessitating another trip to the front desk, another wait in line, etc. to get working keys. The hotel's only restaurant was packed with some sort of event/conference; however, there are a number of nice restaurants a short walk away. The lobby bar was less crowded but noisy, the service slow, and the prices a bit on the high side. The staff across the board (front desk, concierge lounge, bar) was disinterested bordering on rude. The Marriott is serviceable but feels much more like a Courtyard and, for the price, is not a good value. If you want a business-class hotel in Philly, go elsewhere. The only reason I can suggest for staying here is a great price and/or Marriott points -- but you can get both at the Courtyard at a much-reduced price.

“Fun place and great rooms” Hotel ZaZa Houston is pretty great. The suite we were in (1003) was spacious and the views from the bedroom over the museum and in each direction were fantastic. Little things (replacement toothpaste, boarding passes, a couple of apples) came quickly and without drama. The restaurant was OK but the drinks at the bar and service there were great.

“Blah” Cashed in some reward points prior to an early flight out of Logan. Rooms were clean and comfortable - flat screen TV was a nice touch. The location is squeezed in between Tufts Medical facilities but easy access to the Orange line if needed and walknig distance to about everything in Boston. Staff was burnt out - not a smile or extension of service to be found. If you are looking for a blah, no thrills experience this is the spot. As noted not a bad value for cashing in points or a priceline deal.

“NIce Mid Town Resting Spot” Hotel has been under re-construction for three months which should be ending in 3 weeks. Rooms have been updated, furniture is great and the bed very comfortable. Window treatments make the room dark and the ac is cold. Staff is handling the construction well and are very helpful during this time. I will be abck at this hotel.

“Great location and family friendly” The hotel is close to the downtown area but is also close to lots of great local shops and restaurants if you go south on Congress. The lake and Bat Bridge (Congress Ave Bridge) are right outside your window and a short walk from the hotel lobby. Check-in was a breeze and our room requests were honored. We had requested a crib and arrived to find it already set-up in the room along with a travel kit of Johnson's baby products - a nice touch. We drove into the downtown area for lunch and then returned for an event at the hotel. The pool was packed but we gathered at Marker 10, the lobby bar, which was quite nice with big comfortable couches. The Perks Coffee bar was great for breakfast as well. Overall, a great stay for families with kids as you are close to all the tourist spots in town, but also a nice hotel with good amenities and friendly staff.

“An excellent 'home from home' Hotel/Motel” We stayed here for three days after Boxing Day and a very long flight to LAX. On arriving we were offered free soft drinks, water and other goodies. A very, very warm welcome. The room was quite basic, but very clean with fridge, shower, large TV, but no bath. The breakfast in the morning was a buffet affair but pleasant. With plenty of car parking space and ideally located I'l certainly stay here again.

“Pleasantly surprised and pleased” I wouldn't normally choose a Holiday Inn Express on my own. This hotel was booked by my company's secretary for a business trip/meeting. I had low expectations and I am pleasantly surprised. The property has recently been refurbished, it seems. The room is clean, simply yet modernly designed and the staff is excellent. The common lobby areas are inviting and up-to-date. Very pleased with my stay.

“Loved it!!” This is one of my favorite hotels in the city. Of all the boutique hotels I have been in throughout Manhattan, this ranks as one of the best. The staff is great throughout. From the concierge, front desk staff, housekeeping, to management, everyone is friendly and professional. So rare to find in the city,,,,trust me. The vibe of the hotel really appeals to me. Its the Kimpton feel, and if you have never stayed in other Kimptons, you really should. The rooms are always well laid out, plenty of nice amenities, reasonably priced, and cleaned. Some people have commented that this was not in a great location, but I disagree. You are only a couple of blocks from the Empire State Building, a short walk from Rockefeller and Park, close to the Shake Shack in Madison Park, and near Bar Breton and Bloom's Deli, 2 of my favorite gluten free restaurants in Manhattan. The hotel is well lit (not like the super dark W hotels) and just has a nice comfy vibe without trying too hard. Give it a try! And,,,make sure you join the Kimpton In Touch program, as you get the internet for free :)

“Bourbon Steak... Wow what a dinner!” We are only in Washington for a few nights during Easter 2012. booked Bourbon Steak way in advance.. Loved the chips and truffle oil bread, had porterhouse plus baked potato and shared baked cauliflower and spinach. Spinach a bit ordinary, but apart from that dinner was gorgeous, service immaculate. dinner to much for us to eat so we had to go and had it for dinner the next night...Not pretentious, just immaculate service, would go back in a flash! Highly recommend. No room for dessert.. Would have loved some the choice looked amazing

“Business hotel” A really nice business hotel. Lots of airline staff - they usually know value. Bistro cafe very nice. Ha -best oatmeal I ever had. Great to have a newspaper every day. Rooms are rather plain and bed just okay. Area is developing and should have more places to eat soon. Will stay again on business. Nice shuttle drivers too.

“Met Expectations and Then Some” Stayed at this hotel last weekend. Excellent rate at $59 a night. For that rate, it exceeded all of my expectations and then some. Nice size room with LCD TV - Bathroom was nice but on the small side. Hotel staff was pleasant and was helpful in making sure I could stay in same room since I had made a separate reservation for each night. Hilton Gold Member and received my extra points and free internet with no issues. Some of the other hotels will throw in a few additional extras but at the rate I paid for this hotel I feel I was treated fairly. Only area lacking was the restaurant. I saw the waiter one time - when she seated me and then when she came by to give me my bill. Fortunately, I was able to flag down the other waiter and he would come by the table and check on me from time to time. Breakfast was good but for the price it seemed limited compared to the selection at other Hilton Hotels. If coming again to Indy I would probably try to stay closer to Downtown but if the price is right I would have no hesitation about coming here again.

“Amazingly large suites in the city!” Excellent choice if you’re looking for a hotel in the city with a lot of space. It’s a converted apartment building, and the suites still look like a one-bedroom apartment – separate living room, dining room, full kitchen, bedroom and bathroom. (It was bigger than my last apartment!) We stayed here for three nights in late August/early September and loved having all the space. Can’t beat the free parking, too. We spent the extra $20 to upgrade to their top-of-the-line suite, the Colorado. It was on the top floor, and we had a fantastic view of the city and the mountains. They also provide comfy robes and bottled water every day in these suites. Our favorite part was the balcony – every suite has one, and ours had two wrought-iron rocking chairs and a table. Plenty of room to stretch out and enjoy the sunset with a bottle of champagne. It was also really nice to have our morning coffee while overlooking the city. Not sure why the last reviewer didn’t feel safe – the hotel is surrounded by apartments that seem to be rented by 20-somethings and 30-somethings with young families, so it has a very neighborhood feel. We walked to several restaurants at night (Benny’s is a hugely popular neighborhood hangout for Mexican, Dolce Vita had great Italian) and never felt worried. It’s definitely a long walk to the more touristy areas though – six very long blocks to the bottom of the 16th street mall. There’s a free hotel shuttle that operates until 11 p.m. and will take you anywhere you want to go, but if you’re looking for super-touristy area, this isn’t it. My other caveat would be to not expect brand-new furnishings and a marble bathroom. Everything was clean and comfortable, but definitely not five-star. Not even four. If they put a little money to upgrade the rooms, this place would be unbelievable. All-in-all, we loved being in the city with so much space to spread out. We stayed at the Hotel Monaco downtown for the first four nights of our vacation, and I much preferred the Burnsley for the amount of room and the balcony.

“A very convenient stopover hotel” Stayed here for one night to break our journey, having received a good rate on Hotwire, and were so pleased to arrive at the hotel after a much-delayed flight. Check in staff were exceptionally pleasant, and helpful with directions etc. Room was fine and very clean and comfortable, there was a great shower, and we slept well without any aeroplane noise to disturb us. Had a snack meal in the coffee shop type restaurant adjacent to the bar, food was very average and the server was rather over attentive, constantly interrupting our conversation to ask if we were enjoying our meal! That was the only negative thing about our stay and we would happily use this hotel again.

“Not up to par” I have stayed in many Homewood Suites properties. They are usually my first choice when looking to book a room, but this particular one was definately up to par. Our party booked two rooms. Both doors scraped th floor when opened and had to be forcefully pulled shut to latch the door. The staff did not speak English, the salt and pepper shakers in both rooms contained packets of pepper and no salt was available. The shower curtains were mildewed as well. I still will stay at homewood Suites, but the management at this one obviously has some work to do, or the management themselves should be replaced.

“Comfy” Very quaint hotel. Central and within walking distance to many of the attractions and shops. Staff is very friendly but be very specific that you want walking directions otherwise you'll get driving directions. Our room was on the 11th floor and had a gorgeous view of the city. The room was comfortable and clean. The bathroom was a bit small. Parking is expensive. Make sure you pay for parking along with your room so you don't have to look for the machines.

“Classy hotel in U-W area” We stayed here for 2 nights in early July 2011. Very stylish hotel with well-sized rooms, nice amenities is the bathroom, a microwave and fridge, and a nwe LCD tv. The continental breakfast was not as big as others I have stayed out but there were enough muffins, pastries, bagels, freshly cut melon, cereals, yogurt, etc. to satisfy all. We received a "back" room which was great because we could see Mt. Ranier out the window. Unfortunately, on July 4 at midnight, some people decided to light some fireworks in the alley behind the hotel which woke me and several members of my family. The hotel also has bikes available for free and I did a morning ride along a nearby bike trail that parallels the ship canal that was quite lovely.
