The neighborhood is not upscale, but with free parking and the entrance ramp to I-5 just a few blocks away, it didn't matter! Only negative comment was it took awhile to get "carts" from the front desk (they have activity carts with games, art, etc).

“Renovated Rooms are Very Nice-- What an improvement” I had last stayed at the New York Hilton in late September 2006 when they had their linen fire. I was very pleasantly suprised at their newly renovated rooms that at this point appear to be given namely to Hilton Gold or Plat members ( I am gold) -- much nicer than the old rooms. Staff was very nice, except for a woman that would not let a friend of mine connect to the free internet on the 44th floor in their Executive lounge, that we had done on Saturday. Location, Location, Location is really the big advantage to the New York Hilton.

“Super location and first class customer service” Truly exceptional staff. From the doormen to the front desk to the housekeeping staff everyone seems to want nothing more than to make sure you have the perfect stay. I had a corner suite with great views and a lot of natural light thanks to the huge windows in the sitting area. My suite was very spacious with a huge sitting room and the all important bed. A very comfortable bed complete with your choice of pillows help to ensure a good night's sleep. Add to that complimentary wifi for Kimpton intouch members and I would definitely stay here again. A special mention for Emil Encarnado who was kind enough to send me through a copy of my invoice after I misplaced my original.

“The best 2-1/2 star hotel” The basic architecture of the EnVision Hotel is that of a townhouse sitting on a hill; it is narrow but long, overlooking South Huntington Avenue at the front and Jamaica Freeway at the back of the structure. Two upper floors and a basement have been added since the satellite photo available online was taken, bringing the total number of floors to six (B,G,1-4). There are rooms on the four numbered floors and there are four rooms on the G floor that the front desk euphemistically calls ‘the garden level’ but that appears to consist of rooms half concealed by the hillside and that share the level with a covered parking portico and, at the rear, a small parking lot. The larger, superior rooms are located in the middle of floors 1 through 4. General pros and cons: depending upon temperament, the location of the hotel out of downtown but on the trolley and bus routes is either an advantage due to lower cost and a quick commute (15-25’) right into downtown, or a disadvantage because of the need to commute and the trolley and bus noise on Huntington Avenue. Other pros: the water was hot with good pressure. All the doors are heavy metal that close quietly and are soundproof, even the bathroom and closet doors within the rooms. Wireless internet was complimentary, easy to log onto and reasonably quick. Since there were a significant number of reviews online that complained about noise on the lower floor, we asked for an upper floor with our reservation and were given a third floor room upon arrival. Room-specific pros: With some careful and persistent internet searching, we were able to get a $109 rate for our room - about half the 'discount' rates available online. For that rate, we were given a room at the front of the hotel, overlooking S. Huntington Ave. We read the disparate reviews online before reserving and asked for an upper floor room as a condition of our stay. We were given a third floor room. The room was clean and nicely appointed with a comfortable bed, a desk, dresser, bed stand with alarm clock, refrigerator and microwave. The TV was a large flat screen with hundreds of Comcast channels. The shower was built-in, marble faced. Room-specific cons: Our front-facing room (#301) admitted the trolley noise starting at 6:15 am every day. We were up by then but a late sleeper might not tolerate it. On the last night of five, a persistent and continuous ‘cricking’, like a dripping faucet but louder, came from an outside wall. It started soon after we fell asleep but when I woke up several times during the night, it was still there. It stopped in the late morning. The marble-tiled bathroom floor was uncomfortably cold (no slippers were provided, but what do you want for 2-1/2 stars?). The HVAC consisted of your typical 2-star under-the-window unit which was typically noisy (not poorly maintained – just inherently noisy). With the extensive renovations throughout the building, it is very unfortunate that a better HVAC arrangement did not present itself. Finally, admittedly minor stuff: Only one bathrobe was provided. No big deal; the Westin that we are staying in today (q.v. review) only has one bathrobe, too, and it is not as nice as EnVision’s. The Xfinity remote control was weird. When it turned on the Comcast cable box, the LG flatscreen came on, and then went off. When pressing a trial of various buttons, the screen would power on, only to have the cable box power off. Sometimes this back-and-forth would go on for several minutes; sometimes both would stay on after only one or two tries. The fault is obviously with me for not understanding the technology; but, hey, hotel TV ought to be idiot proof. I was too embarrassed to call down to the front desk and ask how to turn the TV on. In other news, our windows each had two spring latches at the bottom and two spring latches at the top; this meant one had to have four hands in order to open a window. I never succeeded in opening a window. From the outside, the superior rooms seemed to have different windows, so perhaps this is not a problem for them. Bottom line: I would not adopt this as my Boston hotel destination but I would stay there again if it were the only way to escape the unreasonably steep hotel rates that seem to characterize this city.

“Unbeatable combination of location, comfort and views” Rooms are well appointed, fairly spacious (once you get past the narrow hallway inside door) and quiet with great views. Nice desk and mini coffee bar in room along with plenty of outlets around room for recharging those essential electronic items. Well equipped gym offers great views from the treadmills of the center courtyard or the outdoors. Check in is on 8th floor and will introduce you to one of the hotel’s quirks – you press the number of the floor you want to go to and the keypad tells you which elevator will take you there, it works but does take a bit of getting used to. The View is the hotel’s rotating top floor restaurant and bar with excellent views of the city’s skyline, there is another nice cocktail lounge on the 8th floor. Full service business center is also located on 8th floor. Hotel is located adjacent to the touristy center of the Big Apple – Times Square. Hotel is an easy walk to the Broadway theatres and many good restaurants as well as: Rockefeller Center, and Empire State Building and many other touristy attractions. There is also easy access to NYC subway system for those who want to venture a bit further out. Internet free in lobby and some other areas and wifi is available in room at an extra charge. Far from cheap but this is NYC and you do get more than you pay for, we’ll stay here again!

“Terrible experience” This was my 4th trip to San Antonio in the month and the third Hyatt Brand hotel. I was intrigued when I was booked by it. It was close to work and away from the hustle and bustle of downtown SA. The rooms looked very big in the pictures. I checked-in late and was given a handicapped room. At the beginning, I didn't mind. I was tired and I was staying there for 4 nights. I saw that the bathroom was configured for handicapped people. The next day I saw the bathroom was not clean and the room's carpet had some stains. The sofa had food crumbs and when I arrived at the room there was a dirty tray in there. I had to go downstairs to the restaurant to pick up the food because they didn't deliver. Some of the service personnel were rude.

“hotel” its a great experience, rates are fine, very class and neat rooms. good service. provided good information about city and tourist places, very comfortable beds. prime location and very near to shopping. excellent room service, very good breakfast and food.

“Convenient to the Airport” I was at LAX for a connecting flight and because of a long delay elected to stay in LA and catch a flight the next morning. The United Rep gave me a card for hotel discounts and stayed at the Hilton for $79. The free airport shuttle runs every 15 minutes. There was some sort of labor unrest outside. While the lobby was very noisy due to the protestors outside, you couldnt hear them from the rest of the hotel. The hotel room looked like it had seen some wear and tear, but I was happy to have a comfortable bed for the evening. Would recommend it if you need a hotel convenient to LAX.

“2nd visit to Bedford, Great location!” On a return visit to New York I decided to come back to the Beford Hotel after looking at many other hotels. There were 4 adults, so we booked a one bedroom suite. It was very spacious and comfortable. The hotel decor, furniture, and bathroom are a bit old and worn. We had a room on the 4th floor and had no problems with temperature or noise from outside our room. The small kitchenette was convenient. Walking to Times Square is a lot less stressful than taking a cab there. The free internet was helpful! The staff I encountered while visiting were friendly and helpful. I would come back to the Bedford Hotel again!

“Charming, historic hotel in DC” We thoroughly enjoyed our 3 night stay at the Hotel Lombardy. Our room was beautiful with fantastic historic detailing. We were greeted with first class service by the gentleman working the front door who quickly whisked our luggage up the stairs and up to our room so we didn't have to squeeze in the tiny elevator with our bags. Our room was mostly updated with a big flatscreen TV and luxurious bed linens. The towels need some attention as twice we had bath towels with the stitching coming undone. Our room was spotless and clean and made up timely every day. We were able to easily walk to our choice of 3 Metro stations which were in a 4-6 block range. Our one complaint was trying to regulate the water temperature in the shower. The water would inexplicably change to scalding hot or ice cold, probably due to the age of the building and its pipes. We did not dine at the hotel. We found a great deal on this hotel through hotels.com and would definitely recommend to anyone looking for a nice place to stay in DC close to the Metro line.

“Nice” Stayed in a Suite durring a business trip and my company paid for the room. I was in a suite which was very nice, but it had a view of the roof. Room was very nice. The hotel bar had a good wine menu, but the catered food for the confernce I was attending was just fair. Hotel has a weird layout and in some confernce rooms the AC didn't work, so there were big fans in those rooms.

“Better than expected” I had been really struggling to find somewhere to stay in New York thanks to leaving things late as usual. Without wanting to stay in a hostel, I stumbled across Hotel 17. Although not delighted to have to stay in shared bath accommodation, I was pleasantly surprised by this place. Everything was clean and comfortable, although the room was a bit small for me, at 6ft 6ins. The bathrooms were almost always available and spotless, and the location was superb, being near subways and Gramercy Park. The only downside for me was some very loud plumbing noises from some pipes in my room when we had a cold night. The room also did not have a sink which was somewhat unfortunate, and all of the staff, apart from one, were particularly surly, something which I have since read in other reviews of the Hotel 17.

“Great Hotel!” I recently stayed at the Lakeway Resort and Spa in Austin while doing a site visit for a meeting we're having in 2007. Check in was effecient and my room was located close. The hotel has a rustic "lodge" feel to it. The food was pretty good and the views were excellent. There is a small walk to the restaurant but felt so good in the chilly evening weather. The rooms are very comfortable without being cluttered. I enjoyed my stay there and would stay again.

“Wonderful Westin Coplely Place a Great Value” Another excellent Starwood hotel in the best of all locations when you are in Boston in the winter, especially during the snow storms. I found nearly all of the service here excellent, free WiFi in the lobby helps get you out of your room and next to the cozy fireplace. I really like the quality and modern rooms with great views and excellent linens and pillows. The beds in this place were amazing and room temperature easily controlled for comfort. What is great about this place is the location and ability to walk through a myriad of buildings and passages to the conventions center and mall areas. This is a plus when its 6 degrees outside let me tell you, I also enjoyed Turner Fisheries near by and the 2lb lobsters on Wednesday night. Right nest to the hotel is a great restaurant named Lucca that I reviewed on Yelp, check it out. Everything was great here until the last morning when I sat down for breakfast and had to wait quite a long time for even water, they need to fix the breakfast service. We found the bar excellent for lunch and the servers were very friendly and nice overall we had lunch there one day and I had dinner the first night at the bar as usual. I really liked what they have done here in upgrading and investing in the property, overall service was excellent until I complained about the breakfast service and got a snotty remark from some manager type, but most of the staff were excellent, aside from the fact that they forgot to put my starwood number in the system.

“Nicest airport hotel” Stayed overnight at airport Hilton which was the nicest airport Hilton I've seen. Flew out of US Airways, which was literally across the street from the hotel. Although I expected a lot of noise, it was very quite, professional and restful. Definitely will stay there anytime I have an early flight out of O Hare. It was kind of expensive, but I booked literally several hours before checking in.

“Not a great value” I spent 2 nights at Hampton Inn and I am not sure what to say about it. Although there is nothing really bad about it, I can’t think of something good to say either. Hampton Inns are usually the inexpensive sister in the Hilton family, nothing fancy, just basic decent hotel accommodation. However, the high price and the very enthusiastic comments from this forum made me believe this is something special. Not exactly. This is a very old building that was probably recently renovated. The colors are all dark however. Dark carpet, dark furniture and dark wall paper, a little to depressing for me. The breakfast is nothing special, just an extended continental breakfast with some kind of fake eggs and gravy, cereals, muffins and beagles. I can’t really imagine how someone can eat enough of that stuff to last them till dinner. They offer free wireless Internet and there are 2 PCs in the lobby with free Internet also. The rooms appeared to be clean and comfortable and the staff was extremely friendly and accommodating, probably they are the best thing about this hotel. I paid $249/ night plus tax and I feel that was no reason for that kind of rate. If you can get this hotel for less than $175 and you don’t mind the Gothic look, you might enjoy this hotel more than I did. The location is great especially if you don’t have a car and like to walk. In conclusion, not a bad hotel, but definitely not a good value or worth the money that they are asking.

“Awful” With a Marriot name you would expect at the very least business quality. Not So. This is by far the worst Marriot we have ever been to. We also paid well over $100 to stay at a 30 year old dump! Everything is extremely dated and worn out. The staff were fine, but the rooms are horrible! Tiny beds with worn out furniture and linens scuffed up walls etc.. the list goes on. Also not safe for small children, balconies that appear to not meet safety regulations. Stay away from this one. There is a better Marriot 10 minutes south off the same freeway. Wish we had stayed there! Also do not believe the new pictures on the Marriot website they are so far from the truth its pathetic!!!!!

“Bad Service, Poor Housekeeping Standards, Expensive food and drinks” I was at this hotel recently for 5 nights - if I could have cancelled and gone elsewhere I would have. I knew it was a bad sign when i went into the bathroom and found a woman's long dark hairs on the "clean sink", the "clean towels" and the nest of hairs still on the "clean shower floor." Such LOW standards for housekeeping! Housekeeping didnt replace empty shampoo bottle unless i asked for them. On two days, the pillowcase put on the pillow was dirty when it was allegedly changed to a clean one. Guest services often didnt answer the phone. The bars were charging more for a basic mixed drink ($12 for vodka cranberry!!) which is more than I would pay in NYC at a high end bar - this was NOT a high end bar... The food quality was mediocre at best in the various restaurants, and definitely on the high side for a run of the mill Hilton. I was sending a box via fed ex and it took them 3 days to get the box to fed ex containing my luggage - 3 days! I expected it to be picked up the day i left it with them, which is a reasonable expectation. I am now a Silver level with Hilton HHonors, and quite frankly, having never been impressed with their hotels really, am wondering why I evern give them enough business for a Silver level. Overall, I would NOT recommmend this hotel to anyone, nor would I return to it.

“Nice to see how the other half lives :-)” We are not Fairmont sort of people - we tend to fit in at the Comfort Inn & Suites - however we did decide to splurge for our last two nights in Seattle and stay at the Fairmont Olympic - and it was really lovely. The valet parking was efficient and friendly - those guys outside are the hotel's best ambassadors! The check in was efficient - and although the elevators are quite small as another person mentioned, they were really, really fast so our waits were not so bad. We had 3 meals in the Georgian - 2 breakfasts and 1 dinner. For breakfast - we would recommend the Banana & Strawberry French Toast - forget about the calories and order it - its an amazing dish. The dinner we had was probably the most elegant of any we have had - ever -- and we can't say how it would compare to other spendy restaurants, but we did enjoy it - and were made to feel very comfortable in their dining room. We had a suite on the 7th floor - no view, but when you look out the window you see hundreds of other rooms without a view, so you are not alone. The room was nicely decorated, spacey - especially the bathroom - and truly comfortable. Thanks to this hotel for having CBC available on their TV - we got to stay in touch with the Olympics while there, and didn't miss anything! The pool and fitness area is divine - and if we return, we will spend far more time there. We found Seattle to be a great shopping city - and within walking distance are some great shops - Coach, Nordstroms etc. We left our mark there too :-) My only niggle was room service - it wasn't so good. I ordered fish & chips and expected it to be the "best fish & chips ever". It wasn't. It tasted like any old room service dish from any old Sheraton or Holiday Inn - and cost twice as much. For us, this was a treat - now we go back to our middle class lives and enjoy our memories. We'd love to do this again - and maybe we will someday!

“3-star experience at 5-star price” I'll admit it - I really like a good 5-star hotel. Sadly, the Chicago Intercontinental repeatedly disappoints. On the positive side: 1) it is in a good location, especially for shopping on Michigan Avenue; 2) it is also a short cab ride (couple miles) to business meetings in the Loop; 3) at its core is a grand old building that was the Medinah Athletic Club developed by the Shriners; 4) it underwent a $250MM refurbishment with a new tower and real effort at amenities in the rooms; and 5) it has a large and friendly staff. So much is right, but so much more makes it wrong. If it was a Holiday Inn (and priced like one), it would surpass your expectations. But, it is an Intercontinental and is striving to be 5-stars (and priced as though it actually is). Some of the annoyances are small (but still detract from the stay and make you not want to return). For example, there was just one hand towel and no face cloths in the bathroom, despite other efforts to provide nice bath amenities; there is a flat touch screen in each room (in addition to the TV), which is supposed to offer you information to improve your stay, but it's got a terrible user interface and seems designed to always drive you toward purchasing additional services from the hotel (which might be more simply achieved by calling guest services); the bathroom floor was ice cold (evidently conducting the below freezing outside temperature through poor engineering of the new tower); and the swimming pool, so grandly featured on the website, is closed for renovations for months (but you'd never know that from the website). What is inexcusable is the poor service. While the staff is friendly, they do not seemed to be trained in five star (or even four star) hotel service. To be clear, this is a management failure (the staff seems smart and nice enought to be superb). Instead, the concierge desk is uninformed; maid service failed to clean and prep the room; and guest services seemed at a loss as to how to make things right. In addition, it is just plain annoying in this day and age for a large city business hotel to impose an $18 per day fee for wi-fi. At $380 a night, WiFi should be included (it's not 2005 anymore). I used the cell card in my lap-top to avoid this fee (so this is not sour grapes on being ripped off for wi-fi), but I thought it summed up the hotelier's real lack of concern for the needs and comfort of the guests. That was apparent at every turn. I had been looking forward to my stay here (on a multi-city trip), and was repeatedly disappointed. I now have a new major account relationship in Chicago, but have asked my agent to find me another place to call home in the Windy City.

“Just fine for us!” Just got back from a weekend getaway with my significant other. Sure the room was small (but if you are in NYC you should probably not spend too much time inside anyways) and our window looked onto a brick wall, but the room was clean and the bed linens were amazingly soft! The flat screen TV was a nice touch. The front desk staff was helpful. Very close to 28th street station and Les Halles Restaurant. Good neighborhood.

“Perfect Hotel for First Chicago Visit” Stayed three nights at the Sofitel on a 'third night free' offer - extremely good value. Booked a 'suite' and was upgraded to a one bedroom suite on floor 15. The rooms were great with a good sized living room and a vestibule leading off to the bathroom and bedroom. Floor to ceiling glazing along one wall meant the entire suite was light and airy whilst the orientation allowed it to feel quite private too. Great bed. Good bathroom - although the bath seemed quite high and whilst I wouldn't say it was small (as other reviewers have commented) it is a European size ie deeper than a typical US bath. The service in the hotel is faultless. We did not have to open the front door once, if it rained umbrellas were provided in abundance at the door and the concierge service is excellent and helped with everything from restaurant reservations (and cancellations) to site seeing and TV scheduling....... Well we didn't want to miss the American Idol results. Good location too one block from the John Hancock tower and the top end of Michigan Ave plus easy access to all the stores. Plenty of good restaurants and coffee shops around. Any negatives? well there was no chocolate on the pillow with turndown but I would prefer the cool bottle of Evian provided on my bedside cabinet any day.

“Average for NYC, a ripoff in most other cities” Spent 2 nights here to visit my son. We arrived at 10am and our room was ready so we were most pleased. I think this is only because of my Gold HHonors status and not the norm. The room was very,very small,maybe okay for 2 small people with one suitcase. We are medium sized and had 2 suitcases so always tripping over something. Nice desk with an office chair for computer but no other typical H.I. easy chair. It was quiet and the bed most comfortable, the wi-fi was fast. The location perfect for us,away from the tourists and close to our son in W. Village. A doable hike with luggage to Penn Station. No safe in room which I found unacceptable. Elevators used by cleaning staff so you will compete with them and usually lose during am. The price was an overwhelming $280/n plus tax-- probably one of the worst values in my lifetime but seeing my son was priceless so, what can I say.

“Love this place” What a great hotel! Beautiful property, well appointed rooms, excellent location on the Inner Harbor, and convenient to everything that downtown Baltimore has to offer. The staff at this hotel are excellent, very accommodating, and friendly. Everytime I come to Baltimore on business or pleasure, this is my first choice for lusury and convenience!

“Excellent Rooms, but Lobby Under Construction, Subpar Employees” The rooms in this hotel are excellent -- because of the tower set up, it seems like most rooms have good views of something -- I had a view of the Hollywood sign from my room. Good furnishings, clean. Another positive of the hotel -- great amenities onsite, including some independently owned restaurants (recommend the Bonaventure Brewing Co especially), the typically good Westin gym, etc. Now the negatives: as others have mentioned, the lobby is under construction, which makes it a bit of an eyesore, and when I was staying there, the elevator to my tower wasn't available at the lobby level creating lengthy detours. Another huge negative: I got woken up one night in the hotel, by an employee, who was convinced that I'd ordered room service even though I certainly hadn't. It took him a while to agree that I hadn't, and then when I expressed my displeasure that he had made a careless mistake like this late at night, he didn't seem to care. At all! I would expect better out of a Westin.

“3 bedroom penthouse suite” We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in the beautiful 3 bedroom, 3 1/2 bath penthouse suite. We travel quite a bit and the ultra modern style is my favorite. With outstanding downtown views and spacious floor plan (2,700+ sq ft), we were quite happy. The designers obviously got everything right. The service was outstanding. The management team truly cares. We look forward to returning to the beautiful penthouse suite in San Diego at a future date. One thing that you should know is that the 3rd bedroom is an open loft. It lacks privacy when going up the stairs to the master bedroom but does have it's own private bathroom.

“Port in the Storm” I spent one night at the hotel during Hurricane Sandy, when I lost power at my home. I'm an Accor Gold level member, and they upgraded me to a very nice room on the 22nd floor. I have to admit I was agitated that I had to wait until 2pm to check in, because I wanted to recharge my phone and get some work done on my computer. But the delay was caused by them trying to find me the best room available--comfortable and quiet. The room was all that. I've stayed at many other Sofitels around the world, but this is my new favorite. Of course, it's quite expensive and breakfast wasn't included (typical for most Sofitels). I live in NYC and hope that we don't have another situation where I'm forced to stay at a hotel--but if it happens, this hotel is a nice port in the storm.

“Solid Property” Located in the South Lake Union district, this is a new-build hotel with a lot of attractive features. It is a bit on the edge of the downtown core, but is above a Whole Foods, which is very convenient if you are travelling with kids. We had two different rooms--a regular room and a studio suite, the only difference being the studio suite was quite a bit larger than the regular room. In each case, the rooms were well appointed, with comfortable beds, a fairly generous work area and spacious bathrooms with separate tub/shower. There was only a one-sink vanity, which is a bit odd given how much space has been allocated to the bathroom in the room layout. Service was excellent--housekeeping did a great job, room service came quickly and was piping hot and the front desk and valets were very helpful. They have two computers hooked up to printers, and printing was complimentary, which is a nice touch in light of all of the nickel and diming going on these days. What keeps this hotel from receiving five stars is the lack of amenities. The gym is serviceable--with nice, new equipment--but is located in a low-ceilinged room across the plaza from the hotel. The locker rooms are not special, and there isn't a pool or other recreational-type facilities. Overall, though, this is a solid property that offers attractive pricing.

“My Favorite NYC Hotel Hands Down” This hotel delivers were other 5 Star NYC hotels fall flat. Great in every way. Clean and fresh rooms, amazing location, great Central Park views (Central Park View rooms only), 5 Star service at every turn. I love this hotel. Unlike The Four Seasons Central Park (57th St), this is a true 5 Star experience. You cannot go wrong here!

“Better Choices in Vicinity” Multiple hotel choices in immediate vicinity. Room was clean and roomy. However, initially checked into an already occupied room - never a good experience. Exercise room tiny and dark. Breakfast included, but not worth the effort. Plenty of restaurant choices in immediate vicinity. Many other alternate comparably priced hotels in immediate vicinity.

“FANTASTIC LOCATION makes up for worn hotel” The Tremont has seen it's better days, let's be honest. Rooms seemed to have been last renovated in the 70's and are showing their age. However, this hotel is well worth it. The common areas (including on-site dining and lounge/lobby areas) are classy. The location (half a block from Michigan Avenue, near the Hancock Tower) makes this a great jumping off point for seeing and visiting Chicago. The staff were exceptional! Granted, only one small elevator can make for a wait, but overall GREAT VALUE FOR THE MONEY.

“Great hotel and location!!” This hotel is great value for money and is in a great location especially if you are traveling to see all the sites and attractions DC has to offer. The rooms were a good size with a massive comfortable bed, the bathroom was a good size too. The hotel offers many services such as fast wifi, laundry facilities, business station, free tea, coffee, cookies and newspapers in the lobby. They also have a decent gym and serve breakfast daily for guests. The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. I would recommend this place to stay at as it is very affordable, nice and in a perfect location to see DC by foot.

“James Journey” Our journey to the James was business/pleasure. The hotel is located within easy walking distance to shopping and restaurants. The hotel staff was very helpful and check in was a breeze. The rooms were clean and plenty roomy. The feather bed and comforter were very comfortable. We had a room on the 14th floor on Ontario street a little noisy but earplugs took care of that. The only complaint was the valet parking. I thought 40 dollars per night was a little steep. When we checked out it took over a half an hour to get our car. There is a parking garage on Ontario for half the price which I would recommend. I asked for a good place to have breakfast and the front desk recommended WEST EGG three blocks from the hotel. I had the eggs benidict which was very good and my bill was less than $10.

“Difficult to get to” It is right on the freeway frontage road but very confusing to get to. I wasn't the only one. Others commented as the were checking in. Check in was easy and friendly. Heftiest goodie bag for Priority members I've seen. There is a comp shuttle that will take you to the subway station but it is only a 5-8 minute walk. Room was clean and well maintained but there was some freeway noise at night. Large uncovered parking lot to leave your car and take the subway in to the city.

“Consigliatissimo” Elegante, moderno, nuovissimo, pulito. Lo consiglio a tutti. Il personale è gentilissimo e molto professionale . Le stanze sono stupende. I bagni e le camere sono magnifici. I letti hanno materassi stupendi. Che dire ancora? Anche la posizione è bella. Non è vicino a central park ma è pur sempre la fifth avenue e considerando che a new york si gira quasi sempre in taxi

“Just WOW!” This was probably the nicest hotel we have ever stayed in. Firstly the location is fantastic, right in Times Square, and an easy stroll to the subway at 42nd St, for access to other parts of New York. Our first impression at check in was perhaps a little less than perfect, as the girl on the desk was what I'm sure she would characterise as ruthlessly efficient and I would call borderline rude, however she assigned us a fantastic room on the 34th floor, with a stunning view out over the river, so she's forgiven. Our room was lovely. Really spacious and very comfortable. I have to say that the lifts were certainly an experience and just a little scary. Having never been on such a high floor in a skyscraper before I found it quite daunting, but the payoff is the fabulous view and it was so worth it. We ate in the bar looking out over Times Square on our first night which was fantastic, and the food was good, and on our last night we went up the the rotating restaurant/bar, The View, on the 48th floor for drinks. It is not called The View for nothing and New York certainly did not disappoint, lit up as it was in the early evening. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. It is expensive, yes, but honestly the experience is so worth it. Loved it!

“Average - good location, but in need of an UPDATE and CLEANING” The positives: Good location, close to Beale if you to be close but not TOO close. Nice big HD flat panel TV in the room Negatives: Really in need of an update. Amazingly tiny bathroom - not that I really cared with just one person, but for a family it would be tight. Really in need of a deep cleaning in the rooms. I pulled back the bedside table to plug in my cellphone (which was a good thing I was using it for a backup alarm since my wakeup call never happened!), and Whoa baby,...been a long time since anyone vacuumed the dust bunnies and crud from behind there!!! Because of its age, no outlets readily accessible from the night stand -- which is a big annoyance when I travel on business with various electronic devices.

“Really spectacular” This hotel is amazing. It is my wife's new favorite. It has the feel of a contemporary art museum. Our room was incredible, especially the cool bathroom. Service was top-notch. Do note, it does not have a spa. I wish it did.
“Great place to stay!” Room was clean and spacious, hotel had nice amenties, and was in good location. Would stay there again.

“Excellent service, but needs R&M” Stayed at the hotel in September 2002 for 2 days and July 2004 for 4 days. Good location, as it's slightly off Times Square to avoid the hussle and tourists. Service is excellent. Staff were courteous and fast. What surprised me, however, is the condition of the hotel. While still in decent shape, repair and maintenance clearly needs to be done during my stay in 2004. The standing shower units are kept watertight via a rubber seal. This seal was torn in parts of the shower, resulting in some water being sprayed onto the bathroom floor. I also noted some graffiti on the bathroom wall - minor problems, but something that a first class hotel should deal with. Despite the hotel's minor imperfections, I find that I will still highly recommend this hotel, only if the price is right. Given the amount of selection available in NY, you can't go wrong with the Sofitel, but it may not be the best deal around.

“Excellent Location...Rooms Just OK” We love the Standard NYC for food and drink and go there often. We spent 2 nights there recently and we were slightly disappointed in the rooms and service. The deluxe King is a closet and the space is weird. We knew that going in though. The bathroom is in middle of room with all glass and no doors...OK, I get the glass, but it was so cold and drafty you hated to take a shower. There was virtually no room for a waste basket in the bathroom and no hooks to hang towels. The room smelled of cigarette smoke. Waste baskets were dirty and the house keeping does just minimal cleanup during the daily cleaning....no wiping soap build up in shower and then some......the cleaning is just a touch up really but for the price you would think it should be more...maybe it's pride but I would make sure all my housekeeping staff really cleaned thoroughly. The view of Empire State Building was just OK...You really need to be on the highest floor for a better view and the hotel sits in an area that has a lot of buildings in front of it. Beds were great. As mentioned earlier, the Standard Grille is amazing...one of the coolest spots in NYC. It sits right in the Meat Packing District and right off the West side and a block away from the Hudson River. The food is always great at the Grille and one of our favorite brunch spots. If you are up for a fun loud beer garden, with so much to see...this is the spot. The winter ice rink looks real sweet with the warming house...will be back with my child. The 18th floor bar open to guests only was closed due to a private party. Will come back to the bars and restaurant probably not the rooms.

“This is what a hotel should be” Had a one night stay in Dallas on business and was lucky enough to win this through Priceline. (I have stayed here before at regular rates and loved it then, just love it even more at a bargain price!) Very classic with a wonderful, comfortable room and great service all around. The crazy parking charge is the only thing that keeps them from being absolutely perfect.

“Enjoyed every minute of my stay!” Stayed at the Brown Palace Hotel and Spa for 5 nights in September 09. The location was perfect and the hotel amenities were outstanding. Staying 5 nights as I did, it gave me a chance really experience the hotel. The staff is very accommodating and there were plenty of them walking around which is always a good sign for a hotel. Though I didn't partake in afternoon tea or Sunday Champagne brunch, I did stroll by and all seemed to be having a good time. There were always plenty of locals eating, drinking, smoking at the hotel. Yes smoking! The hotel has a cigar bar and I really enjoyed my time spent there. Let me say this, you will not smell cigar smoke anywhere else in the hotel! There were always plenty of cabs right outside the door but I walked to restaurants, capitol bldg. and to Coors Field, no problem. I rented a car one day to visit Rocky Mt. National Park and the car rental place was just two blocks away. This is a luxury hotel so its full of well dressed men and women but I wasn't one of them. I wore shorts, jeans and tea shirts and was treated first class. If my travels bring me back to Denver, the Brown Palace Hotel is where I'll stay again.

“Very nice place - great service” The London Hotel is in a great location – close to Broadway, Central Park, Fifth Avenue, Rockefeller Center, etc. But you also feel somewhat secluded from all of the congestion and din of the city. Our stay started off wonderfully - the doormen are the best that I have ever experienced in New York City. We were warmly welcomed and our luggage was promptly and expertly delivered to our room. Unfortunately, we didn’t get a view of the park, so I cannot comment on that, but our suite was quite large by NYC standards. Sadly, I can confirm that the hallways of our floor and parts of our room were beat up and the furnishings in the living area of our room were cheap looking and worn. However, we were still comfortable. We didn’t spend a lot of time in our room during the day and it was nice to be able to unwind in a large space after a day full of activities. I especially liked the substantial closet/dressing area between the bathroom and bedroom. And the bathroom was huge – with tub and shower – a separate water closet and double sinks would have made it perfect. And the power curtains were great and allowed us to darken the room for a great night’s sleep. I will say that I received the great level of service that I expected but a little less upkeep and luxury to the decor, but given that I made my travel arrangements through Platinum AMEX (that included a complimentary breakfast buffet for 2) we certainly got our money’s worth. There was a British boy band staying in the hotel while we were there – there were crying and screaming girls milling about the lobby and going up and down the elevators, but after the first day, security seemed to kick into gear and the girls were limited to a space on the sidewalk across the street from the lobby. We could still hear the singing and screaming from our 30+ floor room, but hey, this is New York City – celebrities are part of the experience. Overall, this was an excellent hotel choice in NYC.
“Loved it!!!!” Great hotel. Small, beautiful, old world, great service, incredible location in the heart of the galleria. Great value on weekends - I will be back!

“Mitten in NYC” Das Hotel liegt direkt am Time Square, wenn man also aus dem Hotel kommt ist man mitten im Treiben. Gleich um die Ecke ist auch das Broadway, dort kann man mit etwas Glück an den Ticketboxen am Vormittag noch günstige Karten für Shows ergattern. Das Hotel ist ok, was zählt ist auf jeden Fall die Lage (sonst würde man bei den Preisen mehr erwarten.). Wer also Mitten in NYC sein will, ist hier genau richtig. Sonst kann man auch etwas außerhalb wohnen und Geld sparen.

“Not a recommendation” The stay began with our room not being ready at check-in time. Then, being told, not taken or provided for, that we needed to check our luggage ourselves downstairs via one of the 2 working elevators. Upon returning to the hotel, our luggage was not in our room (after a $20 tip to the bellman who promised to put it there when the room was ready) and was actually LOST when we returned to the hotel. I combed through the luggage room with another bellman until it was personally found. We missed curtain to our play due to the inability to find our luggage (which held the tickets) and change into suitable clothing. We did not have a pleasurable visit at the Hudson; so much so, that we left early and after a fight with the hotel to refund the night we didn't stay. To their credit, they did provide a discount for the portion we stayed and refunded the night we didn't stay. Having said that, this is a Morgan's Group hotel and run as such - it is no longer the Ian Schrager gem it was mean to be. To say we were disappointed that what would be common assumptions for a hotel at that level in a city that prides itself in service would be an understatement. It did not have room service, a minibar, a working restaurant, a top sheet of bed linens on either bed in our room, bottled water / beverages in the room - or even if for only for purchase, or rooms that were cleaned appropriately. The attached photos explain the frayed towels and unacceptable quality of linens, dirty paper cups that were not changed (one dirty before we got the room on a Friday but the sanitise top put on it), the empty mini bar in the room that they no longer fill as well as the empty snack bin above it, or the dirty grout that has been painted messily over in the bathroom. The floor had not been swept during our stay and the shampoos put in our room were previously used (only half full). This is *not* a four star hotel; I travel a great deal and have stayed in many levels of accommodations. Regardless of amenities, there is one thing that should remain true -> clean standards and customer service. Both were missing and cost hours of fighting through both the booking service and hotel after our return home to receive any compensation /reimbursement. Buyer beware. NYC is a lovely city with wonderful hotels - this is not one of them.
“2nd stay...and this one was better.” Enjoyed everything about this place, including the valet parking package I scored...very convenient and great staff.

“Room 936 is a dirty dump, a Sheraton in name only” I arrived at 2am and was exhausted so didn't do my usual room inspection before saying yes and moving my luggage in...what a mistake. Dirt on the bathroom floor, high miscellaneous hair count (not mine) mold and mildew all over show tiles, burns on carpet, left over hairpins on floor, desk chair was a refuge from banquet dept., easy chair had huge tears on both arms, and the carpet hasn't been properly vacuumed in some time. I called the manager's office and housekeeping sent a supervisor who called it "appalling" and moved me to another room. I asked, "who supervises the work the maids do?" Three people cover 600 rooms so they are too busy to deal with many problems. Nobody seems to care in this hotel and it is full of bus tour and airline staff guests who have no other choice so they can get away wit h calling this shabby shack at Sheraton. It's like a roadside motel stacked up 22 floors high. Wisely the hotel did not charge me for my night in room 936. Stay elsewhere the Sheraton NY Towers across the street is a completely different experience. Will I consider Four Points by Sheraton for another stay, anywhere? Heck no.

“First Class Hotel - Felt Like Home” Beautiful hotel, extremely friendly staff, would stay there again in a minute if I go back to LA. From the moment we arrived to the day we checked out we were treated well by the staff. Beautiful lobby, with nice bar and courtyard where you could relax and have a drink or something to eat. Upon checkin we were given a room that wasn't ready yet so they upgraded us to a large room with balcony overlooking the city with views of the mountains. Pool was very nice with a great view and had waiter service. You have to drive to get anywhere and there is no on-street parking near the hotel so bring plenty of small bills for the valet. Every time we returned we were welcomed home and we honestly felt like we were living there. Very convenient location if you drive since it in the middle of the Beverly Hills/Bel Air area and not too far from the beaches, Hollywood and the Sunset Strip.

“Great Family Oriented Place” My wife and I stayed here for a night during our visit to Austin. Very clean rooms and friendly staff. The hot breakfast was great and had many options (from eggs to waffles and fruit). Very clean bathrooms, and overall room cleanliness.

“5 Star” Recently stayed in a 2BR suite on the 15th floor with my 3 young daughters. Overall I have to say it was just ridiculously posh, which is what we were looking for. More space than we needed, fantastic service, good food, amenities like popcorn, sprites and 3 free movies for the kids, kid sized robes and slippers. Too cute! Some wear and tear on the furniture, staff was courteous, but young. Housekeeping and turn down service was above and beyond. Location was great, walk to American Girl place, John Hancock Tower and great dining on Rush Street. Recommend Gibsons for a great steak and Lou Malnattis for pizza!! Very expensive for anyone with a budget, but what I would expect for 5 star and actually cheaper than Trump or 4 Seasons with AAA discount.

“Lipstick on a Pig -- Two-Star Mediocrity Masquerading as a 4-Star Hotel” Reading the reviews on this site, it seems that there are two Soho Grands, a hip, trendy 4-star hotel and a two-star with cramped rooms, spotty cleanliness and rude staff. Unfortunately, I stayed at the second one (and saw no hint that the first exists). The rooms are pitifully small, and not particularly clean. There is minimal space to do anything but sleep. The bathrooms are likewise a tight squeeze. Moreover, their beds/bedding are not up to 4-star standards. These problems were not unique to a single room, because I was moved twice before finally giving up and suffering through a night there. The first room was a smoking room that absolutely reeked, had stains all over the carpets, and scratched-up furniture. The second room, supposedly a non-smoking room, likewise reeked of smoke and obviously had not been well-cleaned since there was a disgusting, rusting pair of tweezers laying in the middle of the tiny table that doubled as the room's "desk." (I have a photo). I offered to leave if they would refund my money, but they refused. Finally, I was moved to what they described as an "upgraded" room, which I guess means "a room that does not stink," because that was the only noticable improvement. Also, don't expect a sound night's sleep. The SoHo Grand is located just above the exit from the Holland Tunnel. Know what comes through the Holland Tunnel at night? Trucks. Lots of them. Big, loud trucks rolling out of the tunnel all night long, their snorting and belching motor and exhaust noises only being amplified by the echo chamber effect of the tunnel. The staff's snooty and unhelpful attitude only adds insult to injury. Worse still, the front desk and guest services were badly understaffed. As a result, several times I had to wait in line or on hold for 10 minutes for the pleasure of being subjected to their shabby treatment. True, the bathrooms have nice toiletries and the room has a plasma screen TV, but this is just smearing lipstick on a pig. If the SoHo Grand were advertised and priced as the 2-star hotel that it is, I would not complain (of course, I would never have booked it). It appears that most of the guests of this establishment are European tourists, who seem not to know what an American 4-star hotel is supposed to be like. (Perhaps ignorance is bliss.) Unfortunately, I have spent hundreds of nights in dozens of New York City hotels over the years, so I know better. Bottom line, this dump compares unfavorably to a Holiday Inn Express or a Hampton Inn. If you are expecting quality, stay away, stay very far away.

“Nice & Basic Amenities In SD; Very Clean” A quick business trip to San Diego and I decided to stay here. The front steps are a little confusing to roll your luggage since the flat part is at the far end, ask the cabbie to leave you there. The lobby is on the 12th floor, two elevators from the street to the lobby. Lobby has a couple of sofas to meet people and the Sheraton Link has a few stations. Wireless is available in the lobby. Front desk staff can be very good or not so good depending on who checks you in. Three elevators to the floors above. Rooms have 2 queens or a king. The rooms with the queens have a smaller sitting room than the king sized configuration. Suites have a couch, a couple of chairs, nice HD TV, desk and chair. Furniture looks recently redone but still Ozzie and Harriet modern, not bad but not SoCal style, more Upper Peninsula Michigan. Desk is basic, almost looks like they bought from a second hand repo company and the chair is comfortable but I could not figure out how to make the back recline (my fault probably versus the chair). Great news is they have a zip strip on the desk so outlets are not an issue. Downside is no wireless in the room so you need to sit at the desk to use the internet, c’mon it is 2011. Lots of lights and they are needed since the living area is not well lit through the windows. Bed is outstandingly comfortable; highlight of the room, and that is a good thing. A 5-8 year old TV is also in the bedroom area. Bathroom exceptionally clean, thank you, six mini-bottles of soaps and stuff. Looks like they just re-did and used Restoration Hardware, all clean lines and much more modern than other room. This Sheraton believes in the 2-towel approach so if you need more ask on arrival. Tub and a separate stall shower but be aware that the stall shower is about 2-feet by 2-feet, i.e. teenie-tiny. Decent water pressure and I was on the top floor. Ate lunch in the Restaurant, I would say lousy to fair at best, almost an in-house version of a low end chain restaurant. Chicken Quesadilla was a combination of processed stuff, not sure I would eat there, walk 1 block down the hill to 6th St for same low quality for half the price. TV check out works fine. Overall an OK place, nothing special, but very clean.

“Great Park and Fly Hotel” We parked our car here before we flew from LAX to Charles de Gaulle and stayed there the night we returned. It was wonderful to be able to pick up the shuttle at the airport after the long flight and then check into a clean, quiet room where we could get a good night's sleep before driving back to San Diego. Staff was friendly and welcoming. For us this cost less than flying from San Diego to LAX, or for just parking our car for two weeks. I almost forgot, they had free water in the rooms! I am so used to seeing overpriced bottled water in hotel rooms that I didn't even read the labels until we were about to leave. Thanks, hotel!

“Idéal en famille” J'ai séjourné plusieurs fois dans cet hôtel situé dans un quartier très résidentiel mais vivant et accueillant. A deux blocks de Central Park et bien desservi (métro 72nd St.). Les chambres sont vastes pour NY et équipées d'une kitchenette. Wifi incluse. Style classique. Supermarché juste en Fairway en face. Café Viand en bas, style diner américain pour petit déjeuner (très abordable). Idéal pour un séjour en famille.

“Beautiful grounds, so-so rooms, ho-hum food” Stayed recently at this hotel while attending a meeting on-site. This is a hotel that on the surface is just gorgeous. The landscaping at this site is the real star. Literally, it's quite hard to beat the landscaping for most hotels in the San Diego area. But enough of the landscaping. The hotels are functional but really in need of an update. The furniture is quite dated. For some crazy reason, the bathroom counters were too low for my tastes. The internet access had several problems during my stay. Along with the beautiful landscaping, however, comes an assortment of "critters" wandering about. We spotted several lizards and a few opossums wandering around. This could be unnerving to some. The food on site was fairly average. Pretty much what you would expect from an average hotel...nothing to write home about. Some pluses...very convenient location to Fashion Valley mall and the San Diego Trolley system. I really wanted to give this hotel a much higher rating based on my first impression, but once you get into the details of this hotel, it's hard to ignore the detractors of the whole experience.

“Very nice” Flew in to Logan by Jet Blue late in the evening to head to the Cape for week in the morning by rental car. I thought we could walk to hotel from baggage claim but not the case. Thankfully I had the hotel phone number for them to send the shuttle to pick us up. The shuttle came quickly and we were in the hotel in a matter of minutes. Freindly driver with an irish accent. Big lobby with tall ceilings very impressive. A lot of airling staff checking in but they checked us in as soon as we arrived. The assigned us a corner room on the eigth floor I think overlooking Delta and the airport. Awesome view with all the windows wrapping around the corner. Big room with king bed, desk, chair and a couch to watch tv from. Bathroom was standard size with shower/tub with grab bars for satefy. The bathroom was very bright which I like. Vanity mirror and nice thick towels also. The room was super clean. Slept well and didn't hear a thing. Breakfast at Berkshires in the morning was OK. Food was good but I have had much better buffets, not much in regards to variety. Waiting for the shuttle from thrifty, I had to call them myself so have the number handy, to pick us up you would not know that you are at the airport because of the nice birch trees and landscaping outside the front of the lobby. Very nice hotel.

“Convenient for short layover” The hotel was clean and comfortable. The lobby area is nice but a little dated. service was generally friendly. There was some noise from the airport but given the proximity you have to expect that. I didnt like that there was no free wifi in the rooms and this cost $13.95, especially when other cheaper hotels in the area have this for free. The shuttle service from airport to hotel is efficient and regular enough. For those with a little more time I reccommend the trolley bus service that takes you to manhattan beach for $5, Tickets are available from the front of the hotel at the valet parking booth. I would stay here again if I got a good deal like i did on this occasion.

“It's a convention hotel, that's why” I stayed at this hotel notwithstanding the reviews about service because I got a good rate for a conference. That would be the only reason I would recommend anyone to stay there. The best thing about the place is the location. It's in downturn Chicago and if you are high enough you get to see Lake Michigan. Yet walk out from the hotel and you are near shops and restaurants. (Having said that, my friends told me that they were awakened by the sirens that seem to go off with greater regularity in the wee hours of the morning. I had a quieter facing and slept like a log.) The hotel service is wanting at most levels. Check-in was fine. Breakfast was at the lounge which must rank as one of my poorest breakfast in a 5-star hotel. Hot food was oatmeal or scrambled eggs. There is no microwave to warm up the muffin. I had to tell them that the coffee was out. One of the most irritating annoyances was the elevator. Everyone complained. Although there are supposedly 6 going to the rooms, I never saw more than 3 at one time--that is, if the elevator is crowded, wait and you will always see one of the 3 coming and going. The most extreme case I heard was a friend of mine who took 10 mins to get from his room to the lobby. My negative experience with service was when my laundry arrived as I was waiting for the elevator. One of the guests waiting with me said--he's knocking at your door. I did not want to acknowledge that because I did not want to miss the elevator. That man refused to budge and shook his head to ask me to open the door for him. He was obviously expecting a tip. The elevator arrived, I left. That evening, there was no turning down of my bed. The fact that the complaints remained the same suggests that management is not taking the service issue seriously enough. And the reason that management does not take the service issue seriously is that the hotel is aiming for the convention crowd. So there is no need to pander; that crowd will merely follow what their leader designates as the convention hotel. So unless you have to be at this hotel, there are others nearby.

“Affordable and pleasant stay” My bf and I stayed at the Old Town Inn for 5 days in the beginning of December. Here are my comments: *Property & Location-Very cute buildings, the location is kinda weird and desolate feeling (especially at night) but for the price I am not complaining! We upgraded for an extra $10 a night and stayed in the newer section which seemed much nicer. The pool was lovely as well as the beautiful landscaping. We took the Trolley downtown (blue line) most days which is an easy walk (easy walk to old town as well) and easy to navigate. (FYI-the pamphlets recommend Old Town Mexican Cafe-not really that good and pretty expensive-seems like a tourist trap) *Breakfast was supplied everyday, got a little repetitive but was a nice money saver and kick-off to the day *Staff-Everyone was very pleasant and helpful. We bought our zoo tickets at the front desk to get a discount. Hotel room- We got a room with a big bathroom and two queens which was definitely worth the extra money when the laundry and souvenirs started piling up. Everything about the room was fine with the exception of a squeaky floor (which gave us something to laugh about) I think overall that people our age (mid twenties) might be better suited at a hotel downtown as more of our activities were focused closer to the city and not as much on other areas of San Diego (mission valley, la jolla) which the old town inn IS very central too ( it seemed as though we were the youngest guests too). Also, younger people might not find the closest neighborhood, old town, as interesting especially since there is not much going on at night(that we could see), with the exception of Harney's, a hipster sushi restaurant. Overall the stay was good, the close proximity of the trolley (and some rides from friends) meant we avoided having to get a rental car which was appreciated.

“Amazing!” Union square is a really nice and convenient area, and this hotel is perfectly situated in the middle. A few blocks from the Powell St. BART station and blocks from Chinatown, this is a great hotel in an amazing location. The king-size bed was just divine, and the shower was so good. I'd definitely stay here again if I find myself in San Fran in the future.

“Carvi-ed Out A Niche in New York” Looking for a discreet, quiet location in mid-town, with stylish, comfortable rooms at an outstanding value? Check out and check in to the Carvi Hotel at 152 East 55th Street. On a recent solo business trip, the Carvi provided all the basics and luxuries that I needed to rest and work. I requested, and received, a room with a lot of natural light. Not everyone wants that “amenity” and not everyone who does would be comfortable to have the shared terrace directly in front of their 7th floor window. With use of curtains at appropriate times, worked for me, albeit it was a little off-putting to notice evidence that guests use the terrace (in this entirely non-smoking hotel) for smoking.... Overall the room is well-furnished and sharp. WiFi worked flawlessly, there was a nice Cuisinart coffee maker and a small fridge with items for sale as well as some room for one’s own supplies. The closet was substantial and included a laptop-sized safe. TV and clock-radio-ipod dock were up-to-date. The bathroom had killer-great water pressure and plenty of space and towel racks. There are a few “new hotel” quirks to be worked out with switches and lighting and finishing touches, like a mirror outside of the bathroom would be welcome. All in all I was very satisfied with what was promised matching what was delivered and the value received for the price paid in an excellent Manhattan location. I would be happy to return to the Carvi and to recommend it to like-minded friends and fellow travelers.

“Solid, standard hotel” Stayed one night, they did a great job of designing the hotel on a narrow lot right on Canal Street. Rooms while small (this is NY), are so well layer out they feel larger. I had a king bed and there was lots of space. Full size bath with shower added to feeling roomier. Staff was friendly and helpful. My only complaint is that they have three small elevators to accommodate 22 floors, I can not remember the last time I continually had to wait for an elevator. Clean room, comfortable space, convenient location and reasonable price make this a winner. I did only give it three stars as for all the positives, it is just a basic hotel. I am surprised it is a Sheraton and not a Four Points.

“Great location, beautiful lobby, San Fran pricing” I had a work meeting in downtown San Francisco and our account stayed at this property so it was easiest for me to stay there as well. It's right downtown San Fran and the rate shows it as well. I got one of the basic rooms overlooking Market Street which is still a great view. I didn't have any trouble with noise. My room with a king bed was very spacious and you can't be the floor to ceiling window. You definitely feel you are in the city. I LOVE the lobby, we just had our meeting in the bar/lounge area and it was comfortable. I love the lights hanging from the ceiling and they have a fantastic sculpure piece in the lobby as well. My bed was very comfortable, the bathroom a bit tight but I didn't really care. I took an airport shuttle in the morning to SFO which was under $20. We had a great dinner across the street and there are multiple restaurants to choose from. I wish I'd had more time to stay and that my wife/family was with me. The location was perfect. A bit out of my usual price range. If I was traveling on vacation I would probably try one of the discount internet places like HotWire to try to save some money. But, I needed to be at this property. I definitely want to stay again with time to enjoy the city. My kids would have loved the hotel.

“Ok hotel, you get what you pay for” We stayed here two nights. The rooms are spacious. And the architecture is very impressive. Hotel needs some friendly up-keep. Some paint chips and has a flavor of a hotel needing renovation. But it is an ok hotel, great location, and good staff.

“Are we all talking about the same place????” I just can't believe we are all talking about the same hotel. Far from being the horrible place some previous users depicted, I found the Ritz Milner great: the location is just fine (just behind Figueroa St, 2 blocks from the Satple Center, 3 blocks from the convention Center, in the hearth of L.A business district) , the staff allright and eager to help you, and the room we got (obviously recently refurnished) was a pleasant surprise, especially after having read some appaling comments! The complementary breakfast (in-house, not anymore at Denys as some first reviews said) is basic, on a -eat-as-much-as-you-like basis. What else? We got our suite for $130 a night during a peak, big meeting period at the C.C. , whereas all aother hotels within a walking distance from the show were at, at the very least, $200. The only downside is that they charge you $2.00/person at the front desk to book a Super Shuttle pick up (that means $8 if you were a family of 4!), which is really mean to my opinion. Apart from that, I definitely will stay again at the Riz Milner, since it proved to be an excellent value for money!

“Wonderful Accomodations with Great Breakfast!” We enjoyed our stay at the Residence Inn at Willowbrook. We would definitely stay here again! The two-bedroom suite was perfect for a trip with extended family for a four-day weekend. We could not have had better accomodations. The suite included a living room/kitchen which was attractive, clean, and comfortable. Each bedroom had a comfortable queen-size bed and its own bath. The bathrooms had separate bathing and vanity areas. Everything was clean and neat with a feeling of being new. The suite included a TV (not flat screen, but good) in each bedroom as well as the living room which was nice for spending downtime at the hotel. Breakfast was a tasty feast every morning! The daily offerings were eggs, sausage, oatmeal, waffles, toppings (pecans, raisins, brown sugar, whipped cream, cheese), yogurt, fresh fruit, cut fruit, biscuits, breads, doughnuts, cereal, milk, juices, coffee, and tea. Some days included items such as pancakes and gravy. The breakfast staff were efficient, clean, cheerful, and helpful. Guests use areas of the hotel were very good. The fitness room was clean and adequate with flat screen TVs to watch during your workout. The pool looked clean, but I never used it. The lobby was spacious and comfortable with a great picture on a large flat-screen TV. The business area consisted of 2 PCs in part of the lobby; the connection was fast and the screen resolution sharp. Guests with wireless laptops were able to work from the breakfast area and lobby. Everyone working at the hotel from front desk, to housekeeping, to maintenance worked hard to make the guests feel welcome and comfortable. We were extremely satisfied with this choice for our stay in northwest Houston. The weekend discount made the hotel affordable for our visit with family.

“Atypique” On sort clairement des hotels standards, formatés.. L'hotel Morrison Clark est en premier lieu, situé dans une vieille batisse, "historique", assez bien située car à environ 15 minutes de marche du national mall. On découvre dès l'arrivée que l'hotel est différent : il faut monter un escalier, aidé par un babagiste pour arriver à l'accueil. Accueil très sympatique. Encore quelque marche pour atteindre l'ascenseur pas tout neuf. Il y a en général un petit coté "charme désué" que j'ai pour ma part bien aimé.. Un peu comme un séjour chez une veille tante avec ses tapisseries fleuries, son mobilier faussement ancien, ses abat-jours, ect.. J'avais pour ma part une très belle chambre au 4ieme, avec coin salon, chambre séparée avec petit balcon. L'ensemble pas très grand est plutot agréabe. Petits défauts cependant : pas de wifi dans la chambre mais connexion filaire, système de chauffage lui-aussi un peu ancien et bruyant. Bon rapport qualité/prix

“Nice, Small Hotel” Hi. I recently stayed at The Hilton Boston, Financial District last night, 05 December 2008 & had a very good experience. The front desk agent, Lourdes, was kind & friendly, as were both Concierges....Charles was excellent with directions & a super nice guy! My room (732) had an amazingly comfortable king bed!!---best hotel bed ever--even tops my Four Seasons/Ritz Stays!, nice, roomy bathroom with excellent water pressure & great hot water, as well as La Source Crabtree & Evelyn bath amenties---nice smelling soaps & creams. The room also had very high ceilings, was quite spacious, offered a large desk & roomy closet with robe, iron/board, etc. The lobby is small, but boutique-y, & has two seperate entrances. I had room service for breakfast, which was good, except for a runny egg--as promised, it arrived within 30 minutes to my room (exactly). Christina, the in-room dining order taker, called me after I finished my meal just to make sure everything was well---very nice touch--they never call at luxury properties, so suprised when they called. She was very polite & a pleasure to speak with! The elevators were a little dirty, with some chipped wood (no big deal), but the room was in good shape...the tub looked ever so slightly brown(nothing big enough to call for), but I'm sure that was just usual wear-&-tear from guests. The lobby had a coffee/tea set-up in the AM, which was also nice. Good location for Fanieul Hall, etc, but about a 20-25 min. walk to Newbury Street, Beacon Hill, etc. Be sure to visit Flour Bakery, Neptune Oyster, & Stephanie's on Newbury..all great places to dine! Boston's street layout is super super confusing, so I was lost quite a bit, so be careful when navigating the city! Warmest Winter Wishes, PW, New York, NY 06 December 2008.

“Plush located downtown close to everything” Nicely appointed with excellent sleeping beds. good restaraunt but at Hotel prices. Workout room is outstanding and it has a pool. Location os what's it's all about at a normal price for Hyatt. several mexican restaraunts in the vicinity along with a small mall with theaters and places to eat. catholic church right around the corner. Overall not too bad.
“it was redecorated so some charm disappeared” now it looks like any other place. the location still remains good. I guess it had to.

“My go-to spot in Dallas” Always a good value and a nice property to boot. It is in the market center area, parts of which can be a little sketchy, but this seemed safe. Also it's got very easy access to downtown/uptown. Free self parking and it is right out front. Ask for a corner room with a balcony.

“Great place; will return!” My wife and I stayed here last weekend for a quick trip. The first room they put us in was next to a group that was getting ready for the a&m game a little early. W called down to the front desk & they moved us with in a few minutes. They also gave us a free breakfast out of the deal. Everyone was very nice even on a football weekend.

“Okay budget choice in a pinch” My family and I stayed in this hotel for one night when our flight was canceled. We were put there by the airline which paid for the stay. The good part is that it's close to the airport with a 24 hour shuttle. There's also continental breakfast, but we didn't eat there. Nothing special about the hotel - definitely a budget option without any extras - checked in at 2 AM and had to check out by 11 AM (no way to extend checkout). I wouldn't stay there again.

“Great Hotel!” We booked 5 nights through Quikbook, and were not unhappy with the results. While the 11th floor room we received was a little smaller than we are accumstomed to in our travels, it seems to be an adequate size for New York. The bedding was perfect, the room was clean, there was a decent sized closet and in-room safe, and the washroom was clean, modern, and had enough shower pressure. The location of the hotel is pretty good for downtown Manhattan. You're not too far away from the Fulton Street subway station, and we found the 2/3 lines most convenient for us. There was also service with A, C, 4, 5, among others that were convenient for getting uptown. You're a few blocks away from Broadway, and there is tons of shopping within walking distance, like J&R and Century 21. The only disappointment we had was that the turndown service failed to fully secure our door one evening. We came back to our room to find that while the door wasn't ajar, it was not fully closed. Luckily, the location of the room was at the end of the hall, so there wasn't much walking traffic. But we only received a couple of perfunctory apologies from the desk clerk. We were told the housekeeping manager would get back to us, but never heard from anyone else, and did not receive some token of apology (like a meal chit for their current dining relationship). All in all, a great stay was had by all.

“Very Nice!” The Hilton Garden Inn was pretty much perfect. The staff were very friendly, the room was well appointed, and the location (right next to the red line and in the middle of River North) is excellent. It was nice to be at a hotel that doesn't nickel and dime you - wireless internet access was free. I didn't need to use the 24 hour pantry in the lobby, but I was glad it was there if I did. The pool was small, however, and the fitness equipment was aging. Overall it was a great stay!

“Great Evening Socials” Looks like the closest hotel to the airport. Very nice. Large rooms with partitioned off living area (big sectional sofa and small workdesk), flat screen TV with MANY channel selections, full size kitchen with dishwasher, two burner stove, large microwave and fridge, toaster, pots, pans, silverware, etc. Hotel appears to be pretty new - nicely furnished and modern decor. No restaurant, but great evening socials Monday through Friday. The night we were there they had pizza and salad - plenty for a meal - and, most importantly, free beer and wine until 7:00! Scrambled eggs, bacon, and pancakes for the complementary breakfast. The front desk is very accommodating and amenable. No problem turning in my rental car the night before my flight, and having the hotel shuttle pick me up at the rental car facility. Normal shuttle service to the airport runs on a schedule every 45 minutes. Dog friendly hotel - I saw two during my stay, but no problems with noise. Indoor swimming pool. Typical of Hyatt, no receipt under the door in the morning, so you have make time to stop by the front desk (no good). Also, typical of this chain, no moisturizer or lotion, so bring your own. No problem staying here again for an early next morning flight out of Denver.

“Budget property - Decent location” First of all, there are FIVE Comfort Inns in Manhattan. I am certain some of the views on this page were written for the wrong hotel. Reviews dated Dec.27 and Aug. 28 for sure, this is NOT the Comfort Inn Manhattan, it is the Comfort Inn on 36th just adjacent to the Javits Center, it has only 56 rooms (only 5 per floor), obviously used to be some sort of housing project or budget apartment building. It is extremely budget, no frills! See photos on Orbitz. I thought I was booking the CI Manhattan. Although we saw workers mopping the floors and doing some maintanence, the hotel was not clean. The baseboards in our room had 3 inches of dust and dirt. The bedspread had cigarette burns. It is just an old hotel, I thought I had read they had renovated it some years back, maybe it sees a lot of group traffic. The hotel is in a great location for the Javits Center, but is on a run-down street with mostly vacant buildings. I felt uneasy walking back to the hotel late at night. Madison Square Garden is 3-4 blocks, Macys and a Subway station. On a good note, the parking (1 1/2 blocks away) was reasonable at $25 per day for an SUV, and the Continential breakfast was Comfort Inn standard and fine. There is no real lobby, staff is friendly, security seems to be in place (we were called at 6am one morning to see if we were expecting a visitor). In addition, EASY in and out of the city, I-495 ends and starts right at the hotel. We had a great time in the city, but I would not stay here again.

“Very surprising hotel!” This is a very nice hotel. Its employees are kind and polite. Well located (you are in the city center), its accommodations are small and simple but comfortable. The breakfast is reasonable. There is just one elevator, but this is a very weak detail to complain...

“lovely hotel but rather small rooms” Perfectly situated in bustling times square, this fun, safe hotel is well priced and full of helpful staff. The concierge is really helpful in arranging anything from theatre tickets to hair salon appointments. The door men were always looking out for my safety and easily arranged taxis.0 Even in the rain, they were there to make sure i didnt get too wet getting in to or out of taxis. Major subway lines are nearby, along with terrific restaurants. The bar scene is lively and the gift shop is unlike others at most hotels. not full of junky tourist items but really good things in case you are looking for a new item to wear out that night. My hotel room which overlooked the lights of times square was rahter small but not unlike other NYC hotels. good products int he bathrooms.

“Nickle, dime, and bait & switch” This is a generic hotel next to an airport. Ok, I expected that when I made a reservation. What I didn't expect was that the pool and hottub as well as all of the outdoor space would be closed. Or that they would charge $13/day for wireless, or $28/day for parking, or that there would be no coffee in the room. I felt like a chump paying this hefty hotel bill but won't make the mistake again.

“Tired, In Need of a Total Rehab, but Friendly and Helpful Staff” I must admit paying 55.00 for this hotel through priceline, for one night following a business trip (couldn't see spending 200+ at the Hilton for one more night; way over-priced there). This hotel, the former "Lord Baltimore" is a "grand" hotel. But it is simply tired. Carpets are worn; paint shows many coats and chips and re-painting. Elevators are ancient.
