But I must say that from the moment I walked into the lobby, the staff could not have been friendlier and more helpful; actually outstanding. My room was OK. Bed was one of those sleep number deals; the last thing I want to think about in a hotel is what my sleep number is. The bathroom was in need of updating; bad and dirty grout in the shower/tub surround. And under the bathroom sink was one of those stainless steel mini-trashcans with the pedal to open it. Really? It was old and filthy. It would be SO MUCH BETTER if this fine staff had a building of which they could be proud. Radisson, it would be worth the money to renovate this aging edifice. Kudos to the great staff. The heart "Good morning, sir!" when I walked into the lobby in the morning was much appreciated. I would not consider paying more than 55.00 per night here.

“Felt I was in a Ritz Carlton or 4 Seasons Here” This hotel was shockingly excellent. I expected a Hilton. I stayed at a Ritz Carlton in another city recently and this was far superior Check in: front desk person had a personality, was attentive, friendly. The baggage porter was a delight as were the parking valets. You can tell these staff really appreciate having a job in this economy and definitely want to keep them. (My pet peeve is hotel staff that act like they dont give a damn). Here, everyone gave a damn. The room was beautiful: new furnishings, tasteful curtains and bed cover. It felt like it was professionally designed by a very high end designer. Super comfortable beds. Large flat screen tv. The bathroom was beautiful, new Carrera marble; digital light switches--really top notch. What I appreciated best is by day there was lots of light, by night, dark. Also, the room was super quiet. I never heard a pin drop the entire time we were there. What more can you want, comfy bed, super cleam room, dark at night and light by day and super quiet? MY kind of room Each room has an ipad. You use this for internet or for ordering room service. So nice to pick you your order, specify the time you want it and voila! no confusion with Room Service on the phone trying to order. The food from room service was just ok. I had chicken salad and the chicken was dry. My daughter had the philly steak sandwich and it didn't have all the things on it as seen on the room service digital menu. She got a raisin cookie instead of advertised chocolate chip. I got the wrong salad dressing. The chocolate mousse cake was excellent. If all that goes wrong on a trip is raisin cookie instead of choc chip, I still declare that an excellent trip. One tiny problem. The shower sprinkler head and the shower "wand" were only like a strong drip. This actually made me late for my meeting. I think this is something they can fix. I would stay here again in a heart beat!!! LOVED this hotel. The staff was super responsive and should be commended. That remodel makes it a top flight hotel for a Hilton price. Best hotel of our week long trip to east coast. I had requested a quiet room and was given a corner room. A corner room is like winning the lottery, light on two sides. Thank you, Hilton Penn!!

“Lacking amenities commensurate with price” I stayed here for 4 nights as part of a conference and was charged ~$250/night at a conference rate. Rooms were well appointed and comfortable and much larger than similar hotels in other cities. Unlike some business/conference hotels, the shower area and sink areas are in the same room, so if you are rooming with someone you can't brush your teeth or do your hair while they shower. As a business traveller, I found the most annoying aspect was really poor internet service. Bear in mind, Austin is a town that touts free wifi in most parts of downtown. However, if you are at the Hilton or in it's conference facilities, you can't get that. Instead, you need to pay for the hotel's exclusive service. Even when we did, we frequently couldn't get a signal or the connections would time out. For this reason alone, I would not consider this an appropriate hotel for business travel. The doormen and concierge were particularly helpful with suggesting restaurants and providing directions.

“Incredible service, completely remodeled new rooms” We held our business meeting here for 35 people. The service was impeccable, nothing was too much trouble. When you walk out the door and re- enter they magically remember your name,so it's like coming back to a private doorman building. The food was sensational, which is not always the case at other hotels we have used. Special mention to Joyce Abrigo who made our meeting run so smoothly

“Lovely Facility” Gorgeous decor that reminds me of MAD MEN, with a dark men's club feel. Only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because the bathrooms seem to have missed the modernization trend. As noted in some reviews, LAAC is right in downtown LA so there are homeless people around especially at night. But less than a mile walk to the disney concert hall, near fabulous restaurants, and a good value. I'll come back.

“Really one of the better hotel stays I have had” I agree with much of what is written in the most recent reviews of the Palomar. It is one of the few hotels I can imagine that suit business and leisure travelers equally well. It does not feel overly corporate -- a huge plus in my book. Service is outstanding all around. Manager's receptions are a great idea: far better to have coffee service in the lobby than to service individual coffee makers in all of the rooms, for economic and psychological reasons (it just feels nice).

“Gute Lage aber nicht das gewohnte Hilton Programm” Ich war mir einem Kollegen in diesem Hotel für 4 Nächte. Das Hotel ist sehr gut gelegen und das Angebot an Restaurants und Bars in der näheren Umgebung ist auch gut. Das Hotel selbst ist leider etwas in die Jahre gekommen. Ich hoffe doch sehr, dass Hilton dieses baldmöglichst renovieren lässt. Das Zimmer und Bad war sehr klein (obwohl auf der Executive Ebene) und ich konnte mich mit meinen 1.86 Metern nur gebückt in der Badewanne duschen. Das Bett leider auch durch-gelegen. Das Hotel eignet sich gut für Meetings mit Kunden, da die Lobby und der dahinter liegende Bereich großzügig und ruhig gestaltet ist. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und die Executive Lounge ist zwar klein aber sehr gemütlich, das Frühstück dort entspricht amerikanischem Standard (d. h. also nichts besonderes). Die Kaffeemaschine allerdings ist 'schon lustig', hier bitte die größte Tasse nehmen und auf der Maschine auf die Taste mit dem 'kleinen Kaffee' drücken, ansonsten gibt es eine Überschwemmung auf dem Boden. ;-)

“generally positive, but those elevators!” My business contact in NYC chose the hotel for me. The positives have been mentioned before: convenient midtown location, spacious room and bathroom. Other pluses: I found the staff friendly (by NY standards) and helpful. I appreciated the free internet in the business center; the quiet refrigerator and the microwave in my room; the closet safe; and the extremely comfortable desk chair. Others have mentioned the European-style platform beds and found them hard, but my bed was just the right degree of firmness. Problems: The bed has sheets and a heavy comforter, and nothing in between. The comforter was too hot, the sheets alone not enough. I used the bathrobe (which was supposed to be provided, but I had to request it) as a light blanket. The "easy" chair was remarkably uncomfortable. The beautiful full-length mirror hadn't been hung, just leaned against the wall. It was inconvenient having no drawers at the desk or in the bedside tables. The door connecting to the next room let through some loud conversations, but ear plugs kept this from being a problem. Though my room faced 52nd street, I was not bothered by street noise. Worst of all, there are only two functioning elevators in this 45-story building, making it very difficult/time consuming to go down at checkout time. Solution: ride up to the top, then back down. (For comparison, the building I work in has only 6 floors, but 4 elevators.) All in all, it was a satisfactory stay, but I'll stay elsewhere next time I'm in NYC, if the choice is up to me.

“Another Great Marriott Property” My family of 3 stayed at this property for a Saturday night at the end of June. We booked at 1 bedroom suite for one night. We paid $37 to valet park our car, we probably could have found a spot for a little less money but after 4 hours in the car it really didn't seem worth it to us. (BTW, the price was going up to $42/night as of July) The only negative I have to say about the hotel was during checkin - there was one person checking people in and that was it. The check in wait was about 20 minutes. I think we were checking in during a shift change, but that is no excuse. The hotel had secure entry to the floors by use of key card. Our 1 bedroom suite was perfect for my husband and our 3 year old. The kitchenette was stocked with everything we could have needed to cook anything we could think of. Full size fridge, microwave, sink, stove and serving ware were all wonderful to have. The bathroom had 6 towels-I am always requesting extra towels so this was a great (and happy) suprise). The bed was very comfortable and we slept well. We needed to make a call to the front desk and now that I think of it that particular staff person wasn't the greatest either. A little on the rude side regarding answering our question. Breakfast was included with our room-hot and cold buffet. Breakfast attendent was very friendly. Assorted fresh fruit, cereal, juices, pastries, eggs, waffle station etc. It was also nice to be able to take some fresh fruit and coffee with us for our long car trip. Complimentary newspapers and LCD TV's all over the breakfast room. Our hotel room and all common areas were very clean. The hotel was in very close proximity to Reading Terminal Market - 6 short blocks to this wonderful emporium of Amish food/gifts, local food favs like cheesesteak etc and farmers market. A great place to walk around and to grab a meal. Upon checkout the wait wasn't as long and the valet attendent was excellent, offered us directions without us having to ask, moved cars out the way to accomodate us. Really great group of attendents at the valet! We would stay here again!

“Exzellentes NY Hotel beim Ground Zero” Waren Mitte Mai im Millenium Hilton. Für NY-Verhältniss recht großes und komfortable Zimmer. Hatten das Zimmer im 54. Stock mit einer Wunderwaren Aussicht auf NY. Super Lager, direkt beim ground Zero. Starbucks gleich um die Ecke, diverse Fastfood Ketten 2 min zu Fuß. Der 21-Century Shop ist auch gleich nebenan (Designer-Klamotten zum Schnäppchen Preis). Vom Baustellenlärm haben wir nicht viel mitbekommen, da wir unter Tags nicht im Hotel waren. Ein gut ausgestattetes Gym ist auch im Hotel. Also ich kann das Millenium Hilton wärmstens empfehlen. Ach ja die U-bahn ist auch gleich um die Ecke (ca. 13 min. zum Times Square).

“Trendy Hotel” I stayed at the Liberty Hotel this month while in Boston for business. The building was originally a jail, but was converted into a hotel. While this may sound odd, the hotel is very modern and trendy. It has a neat history and you can learn more about it by viewing a channel available at the hotel. Below are some of the pros and cons: Pros: Modern atmosphere and nice rooms Location (esplande and shopping nearby) Complimentary Internet (wired & wireless) Complimenary coffee in the lobby during the morning History Cons: Small gym (only a few machines and very light weights - gets busy) Price View - depending where your room is. However what do you expect in a large city. Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel to others traveling to Boston.

“Great for Family Travel; Don't Expect It to Pass a White Glove Test” Recently, my employer used this hotel for a group outing. The hotel is somewhat beat up, but those with kids absolutely loved it. I thought it was OK. It is in an odd location. You actually have to get onto an I-70 on ramp, and then veer off to get to the parking lot. Pay close attention. The lobby looks somewhat like a themed casino in Nevada, tacky decor and all. I think the look they are going for is gold rush era Wild West, but there is a lot of random stuff. Check in was erratic, with printers breaking and staff people looking flustered. The hallways were worn down, with threadbare parts in the carpet. Further, many of the door numbers had worn off the door. When that happened, the hotel didn't even try to replace the numbers with matching ones; instead, they replaced them with mailbox peel-and-stick numbers. It looked tacky. The rooms were comfortible and clean, but also worn and tired. The rooms contained comfortible beds, newly decorated bathrooms, but also threadbare carpeting. As this was a work function, I didn't pay for the room, nor do I know what the rate was. I wouldn't be upset if this ever came up as a Priceline hotel. I would also consider this hotel if I traveled with young children. I just wouldn't use it as a romantic getaway with my wife.

“Sinks go glug glug all night long” Stayed here for a car show on account of a room block with the company I work for at the Car Show. The sink went glug, glug, all night long. The rooms were dirty, and housekeeping lax. No extra toilet paper, bad heating, poor ventilation. I ordered breakfast one morning at the restaurant, $18.00 for two eggs and bacon, come on! I could hardly understand my waiter, the staff was busy watching Super Bowl recaps that morning. This place is nasty, find another hotel. All the high prices without the high quality. Does anyone from this property read these reviews? Yuk, never again. And stay away from a place called "the Wharf Rat", got bad food poisoning from the fish and chips, about died!
“Excellent hotel” Excellent hotel but expensive. Excellent rooms, excellent staff.

“Cramped noisy room” I've always wondered what it would be like to stay in a shoebox on the street. Since I got the room at a bargain rate the hotel put me in the worst room available, and there were of course no other options opening up. Overall, I was very impressed by the service on the front end except for the clerk who made me wait for five minutes without acknowledgement while he shopped for a Nintendo available at the Black Friday advertised price. The staff alternates between the sister properties. The hotel is good for young urbanized travelers. I liked the décor and theme of the hotel. The only time I felt unsafe was when a couple was "jokingly" accosted by one of the vagrants as I walked back to the hotel. The young street savvy man was able to handle the situation while I scampered to safety. Also, appreciated were the free wifi, bikes, and swimming pool and fitness center privileges. The hotel is nicely located if you are city safe savvy and near transit, dining, and shopping. The maid service was very good and my room was clean even if tiny. I would recommend earplugs if you do not get one of the quieter rooms; which did look to be somewhat nicer than the hovel I was assigned. At least I got to get a streetside view of buses, taxicabs, and the homeless camped out outside. The heat was very good, so good that I had to turn on the ceiling fan that I was quite thankful was located in the room. I found plenty of free coffee and tea available in the morning. Would I stay again, not sure. The price was great but I probably would have paid a little bit more for a larger room if something like that was available. Most economy and average rate rooms in San Francisco are "noisy" and surrounded by homeless; so I wouldn't let those factors control in making your hotel determination.

“Good location” Here is my review after staying three nights at the marriott, in August. ( + / positives) * Excellent central location, on Market Street. From there, you can catch the cable car (beware of queues particularly at the terminus), buses and also the convenient streetcar going to the Ferry Building and various wharfs. Also very close to Union Square, and main department stores. A short walk from China Town. Many restaurants and diners around * Hotel is easily accessible using the BART train from SFO. Cost is only about $6, and will take 30 minutes. Station on Market Street only 3 min walk to the hotel * Good modern and clean room, with large LCD TV screen, excellent bed * Good breakfast buffet, but slighly expensive. Lots of choice * Indoor swimming pool and jacuzzi: Not fantastic but adequate and free. Pool is quite large, with lots of loungers and towels * Lots of lifts so no queues ( - / negatives) * Mini bar/fridge cannot be used for storing own food or drinks. One of those models automatically charging when something is removed * Some refurbishing work is currently done at the hotel. Reception area has been moved to the first floor, and is quite small with long queues. Also, can get noisy during the day with the noise of sledge hammers and the likes. However, stops late afternoons not to inconvenience guests * Air conditioning can be noisy * Windows don't appear to be cleaned often: it was even difficult to tell the weather! * No robes, would be useful with the swimming pool * Quite old fashion/70's style hotel. Big and impersonal

“You'd expect more from a Renaissance” Whether or not you like the location probably depends on why you're in Seattle. If you're a tourist and without a car, you might not be too happy. I was visiting a company a block a way so it was perfect. I took the light rail in from the airport. It's reasonably fast and convenient, but be prepared for a steep uphill walk to the hotel. If you walk anywhere you'll encounter the hills. If this will be a problem, do not stay here. Every individual I came in contact with was friendly and helpful, from the doorman to the concierge. My corner king room was more of a suite and very pleasant with a nice view and separate temperature control in the living area and sleeping area. The 28th floor fitness center has newer cardio machines and some basic free weights and weight machines. There are multiple restaurants in the hotel, though one isn't open for dinner year-round. My choices were the lobby bar or the 29th floor restaurant. Both have limited menus, and if you want an quick, light, healthy meal, you won't find it. I did find a Subway sandwich shop a couple of blocks away. As others have noted, internet access is $12.95 per day. Mine was free due to my Marriott elite status. But the connection was so slow that I couldn't do some of my online work. I'd have been very upset if I'd been paying for it. Even worse is the incredible sloppiness in attention to detail. One of my room keys didn't work. I didn't get the newspaper I requested. I didn't get my wake up call. Add this to noisy HVAC (hard to sleep through) and cheapness (you only get two cups of coffee, not the customary four) and the overall sense is negative.

“Excellent Road Stop” Great hotel, right off of the highway. Check-In was ideal, the room was very spacious and clean. Plenty of food available in the lobby. Cambria Suites is an excellent chain, I look to stay at them when I can. Free WiFi as well which was a huge plus.
“期待どおり” 期待通りです ロケーションもよく清潔です 広くはないけどニューヨークでは好きなホテルです 近くにおいしい寿司レストランもありロケーションがいいので夜も出歩けます

“Budget accommodation that's perfectly serviceable” The New Yorker is one of those iconic old school New York buildings that stares back at you from a million calendars and postcards - and the lobby doesn't disappoint, packed with Art Deco features. The rooms are a bit cramped, but the location is what brings you here - right in the middle of the madness. We were advised to ask for a room "higher up" as these should be bigger and more recently renovated - not sure if this is true, because everything looked a bit "tired", though it was all clean and perfectly serviceable. Visit the Tick Tock Diner that's on site, if only to watch the organised chaos that is breakfast! How they make sense of it, I really can't fathom! This is not a hotel for lounging in for hours at a time - but that's not why you go there! Dump your bags and get out into the thick of the action, at a price that's more than reasonable. Staff were virtually invisible, but that's not a bad thing when you're just "in and out" to shops, restaurants, theatres etc etc.

“Very positive experience” Overall I was very pleased with my stay at the Shoreham. I booked a "Superior Queen" room that I got for $199/night via a special advertised from Travelzoo.com. As others have noted, the room was a bit cramped, but that is not unusual for hotels of this class and price range. It was very efficiently configured, and the condition of the room was excellent with a flat screen TV, high quality linens, tasteful decor and a spacious bathroom. The room was also very quiet given it's interior location. There was one small window that looked out to an interior air shaft and the adjacent rooms resulting in an unappealing view. Fortunately, the HVAC worked very well, so I just left the curtains drawn. I did not use any of the hotel ammenties other than the free wireless internet in the rooms (easy to connect), and the free latte machine in the lobby, but the bar looked quite pleasant and seemed active in the evenings. There is also a very small business center and fitness room, but they both appeared to be in good condition. Given the convenient location and quality of the accomodations, I would recommend this hotel as a good value.

“Business comfort” Stayed for business at the Doubletree San Diego - Hotel Circle and enjoyed my visit. The lobby is large and comfortable with sofas, TVs and complimentary morning Starbucks coffee. Just outside is the small pool and a firepit seating area. Cozy. Just off the lobby is a small fitness center, mini-mart and restaurant/bar. The staff was friendly and helpful. Check in and out went flawlessly. My room was large and well-appointed, clean, quiet and (as a Hilton Honors member), my in-room wifi was free of charge. The bed was super-comfy. Bathroom was clean, well lit and had plenty of hot water for the bath/shower . Food at the Panini restaurant was adequate hotel fare. To sum up, this is a business hotel well worth your business.

“Don't you dare touch the bran muffins before 6 AM!” I stayed her last night prior to boarding an early-morning flight out of JAX. As I was checking in last night, I asked about the complimentary breakfast. The front desk clerk, who was nice enough, explained that they had continental breakfast starting at 5 AM and then a full, hot breakfast at 6 PM. This morning, at 5:15 AM, I went to the front desk and checked out. Afterwards, I went over to get someone to eat at the breakfast bar. Suddenly, the front desk clerk bolted from behind counter and positioned herself between me and breakfast bar and adamantly declared, “Breakfast doesn’t start until 6 PM!” I politely explained that the clerk from the night prior said that a continental breakfast was available at 5 AM. She simply stated a little louder, “BREAKFAST DOESN’T START UNTIL 6 PM” as she guarded the bar like a Fort Knox guard protecting gold bullion. So, I said, “I guess I can’t just grab a bran muffin to go, huh?” Now, she became agitated and yelled “BREAKFAST DOESN’T START UNTIL 6 PM!” As, I walked away, she went on some silly tirade about how they had just had a staff meeting about breakfast didn’t start until 6 PM. As she babbled, she repeatedly and passionately pointed to a sign that gave the breakfast hours. She was still blabbering about the breakfast starting time as the automatic doors closed behind me. It’s difficult to describe how impassioned this clerk was about the breakfast starting time, but suffice it to say it was downright bizarre. I’ve never seen anything like it. Okay, I get it. No breakfast until 6 PM. No exceptions. Oh, the room was dated and needed upgrading.

“What a great find for a reward perk in Philly” I happened upon Club Quarters because I was looking for a freebie hotel using points and what a find it was! Club Quarters caters to the extended stay business traveler so the hotel is centrally located and provides services you would not normally find in a city 4-star hotel, such as a laundry room, kitchen area and free bottled water. The beds were comfy too and despite being in the heart of the city, the room was really quiet. I looked it up on Expedia and a weekend night is under $120. It's a great deal and I would definitely stay at any Club Quarters property again.

“Great Location, Very Spread-out” Went here for a weekend with family and friends (taking one family member around Chicago for first time). Perfect location to "set-up shop" in order to tackle most of the places to see in the Windy City. Our room looked out upon the Magnificent Mile as you are right across the street from the start of it. Tough views though as you had to look sideways out of the window to see it. With the way the two buildings are designed, it seems less than half of the rooms have a pleasant view. Very spread-out hotel with the two different towers. Lobby is large with big bar on second floor which seemed to have a fun atmosphere. Rooms were what you would expect from a Hyatt, except a little less of a personalized feel. I think it may just have to do with how big the hotel is...you wonder how much attention they put into every room.

“Nice hotel for the price and value....” I do agree that some of the poor reviews that this hotel has received must be from people used to staying in 6 star hotels. You won't get that here - you get what you pay for - which is a very fine 3+ star hotel. First the room - we reserved a 2 room suite for a family of 4 - great rates made this a good NYC deal at 40% off rack room rates. Not sure I would pay normal rates for the suite, but it was very nice. The separate bedroom and living room were perfect for us as we were traveling with 2 teen boys and needed the extra space. Queen bed was extremely comfortable, sofa pullout was fine for the kids, and the 2 flat screens were nice. We had no issues with an cleanliness - the rooms and bathroom were cleaned appropriately throughout our 3 night stay. Extra pillows, bedding and towels were brought up within 45 minutes our our request. Wake-up call was provided as requested. There is a large volume of people that stay at this hotel so the hotel lobby/elevator area can seem busy at times. However, I never waited longer than 1 minute for an elevator at any time, the concierge desk was helpful (and genuinely interested in helping), and the bellman notified us when our car arrived (we had arranged for a town car in advance - I suggest you do this too if you are concerned about what some of the other reviewers mention about deals between drivers/bellmen). The proximity to the subway is unbeatable. Literally you walk out the door, and the subway entrance is right on the corner. It provides access to the N-R-W-Q lines, which can easily connect you to any other lines you need. Nice cafe across the street for breakfast - Park Cafe - quick service and great food. Also appreciated the Subway (sandwich shop) located across the street for the late night munchies of teenagers. We did not utilize any of the bars or restaurants in the hotel. Didn't use the fitness facilities either but they are large and very nicely stocked with mulitple treadmills, elypticals, etc. Overall, I would recommend this hotel to others. We had NO issues with noise whatsoever - either from outside or other rooms. Also, appreciated the ability to open the windows a bit (hard stop at 3-4 inches) to allow fresh air in the room. This was a great value for the money (mind you 40% off rack room suite rates), and we would definitely stay here again.

“solidly two stars” Clanging pipes all night, mold all over the bathroom, paint smells, ammonia smells, broken elevator, slow bell hops, and when I checked in and asked them to match the most recent price listed on their own website the desk person said no. For $192 per night, you can do much better.

“The Coolest Hotel in Downtown Phoenix” Phoenix is a city of resort hotels -- grandes dames like The Biltmore, The Royal Palms and the Phoenician, and downscale "family" places which are no more than a bunch of nondescript rooms around a pool. As such, a critically important segment of the hotel market was ignored in Phoenix -- the interesting design hotel that had no claim to grandure, but saw itself as more interesting a destination than the typical Marriott familyplex with free eggs and bacon for the kids. Ignored, that is, until the Clarendon came along. This is a well-designed hotel with all kinds of interesting touches -- from the sliding light screens on the windows to the quality and quantity of the in-room magazines. Chic lighting? Check. Plenty of closet space? Yep. Awesome outdoor rooftop lounge? Oh yes. And the pool! Large, cool and smack-dab in the center of it all. Also recommended -- by locals I was visiting -- is the restaurant. Interesting art in the public spaces, comfortable beds, strong showers and quality toiletries finish off the superiori physical attributes of this property. Last but not least is the excellence of the staff. Friendly, young and always eager to help -- including the late night shift, which is typically staffed at most hotels by junior-junior, inexperienced and not-all-that-helpful sfaff. I was pleasantly surprised from the friendly "Welcome!" to the "Thanks for staying with us!" I can't recommend this hotel more. I am a many-miles-traveled businessman and would be pleased to call the Clarendon home at the end of a long work day -- luckily, though, this trip was all fun and the Clarendon was a large part of that outcome.

“Newly renovated hotel” We stayed for one night on a visit to Denver. The reception clerk greeted us warmly and gave us alot of information about the area. Rooms looked to be recently renovated and were nicely appointed. Short walk to the 16th street mall. Good breakfast buffet with lots of choices.

“august USC visit” Just stayed one night at Luxe, so do not have too much to report. Room was modern,very attractive, clean, quiet and had free wireless. That covered our primary goals,so that earned the 4 rating. Location/staff were great so it gets the extra point. The location for visiting USC was convenient, less than 10 minutes drive to reach USC. Sure taxi would be an easy option if needed. Lux is located just about where the downtown traffic begins, so never had much traffic getting to/from USC. Can easily walk about 10 minutes to downtown Macy's/shopping. The valet parking service was efficient and there was never a long wait to get our car. Many eating options across at Staples/LA LIVE. We kept it simple and had take-out from Lawry's Carvery just across the street. Hotel staff were all pleasant and friendly. Luxe seemed to care about the details ...chocolates on bed, disposable toothbrush, apples at front desk, cold "free" bottled water,etc. Probably had a refrigerator in room, but can't recall for certain since its been about a month since we stayed. Luxe was a very good option for visiting USC since the area surrounding Luxe had a great deal to offer. We did not need to spend too much time on campus, so it was nice to be near downtown.

“Style on a budget” Room Mate Grace is a budget boutique hotel located very close to Times Square, and was surprisingly not noisy, but this might be down to being on the 7th floor. I stayed in a deluxe room in a corner of the building (but unfortunately the room was not that bright). The bed was raised and comfortable, allowing you to store your luggage underneath it. The only difference between this and a standard room appears to be the fact that some Deluxe rooms have a king size bed and may be a bit bigger. The other furniture in the room consisted of a small round table (which was moveable) and a chair, and wardrobe space was included behind a curtained area. The bathrooms are a bit different to other hotels, with the sink accompanied by a large counter top, and is not closed off from the rest of the room. There was a waterfall shower in a spacious booth (there are no bathtubs in the hotel) and a toilet which share a sliding door (separated from the sink). The bathroom amenities were: bath gel, shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, soap, shower cap, shoe shine, bath robes and hair dryer. Other amenities include an empty fridge, an iPod dock and a safe large enough to store a laptop. Additionally, you can control the temperature with an electronic thermostat. NB, there is no room service or tea/coffee making facilities, although the room guide does have some suggested restaurants nearby. There is free wifi, but there were no guides on how to use this (I spent some time guessing which of the wifi networks was there's (it's the roomlinx one). For those of you travelling without a wifi device, there are 2 PCs in the lobby, but you have to pay for access. There is also a small gym on the first floor alongside a steam room and sauna. I did use the sauna, but the controls weren't very clear so I couldn't adjust the heat level and there were no instructions on how to initiate the steam room. Beware that the "free breakfast" is not included with all rates, which is confusing as when you visit their website, it suggests that it is free, but maybe you only get it if you book directly through their website rather than via an online travel website. There is a Starbucks across the road, or a deli literally a few doors down which sells hot breakfast items (which aren't included at the hotel). I didn't interact much with the staff except at check-in and the person was friendly and explained the amenities of the hotel clearly. All in all, it was a comfortable stay in the thick of New York.

“Comfortable and affordable” We forgot to book a hotel for our trip to NY and got a really good last minute deal at this hotel. The room was very comfortable, clean and quiet... exactly what you would expect from a Doubletree Hotel. The only things I would mark the hotel down on were that when we arrived and checked in at 1am, the desk clerk told us we had to wait for a few minutes before the room would be available. In the end, it was only about 10 minutes, but at 1am, after traveling all day and needing to wake up 4 1/2 hours later, it seemed like an eternity. It wasn't really clear why we had to wait, but it was a little annoying. At least they gave us a warm cookie while we waited. Then, there was the other kind of weird thing... if we had not had to wait so long in the lobby, we probably wouldn't have noticed the "seedy" element that was coming and going from the hotel. It was a bit of a scene, that is for sure! We are not uptight travelers by any means, but I have to say, I was a bit uncomfortable with the number of women in the lobby trying to coordinate with their "dates" upstairs via cell phone, with phrases like "What was your name again?" I'm sure this hotel is great for some, but I would not recommend it for families or people who are leading sheltered lives... lol.

“Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Amenities” My friend and I decided for a quick weekend getaway over the busy Memorial Day Weekend in Chicago. Searching multiple hotels online, the Hampton Inn & Suites offered a great rate package that included Free Parking. In addition, the hotel also offers Free Breakfast, Free Internet, and a nice pool, hot tub and sauna! That all adds up to a lot of value in the heart of downtown. Our room was very nice and stylish, clean and featured a single cup coffee maker. Our room didn't have a microwave or refrigerator, but I wasn't expecting either. I'm not sure if this is true of all rooms. The bathroom was modern and fresh and Hampton Inn (this is my 2nd stay) have really soft bath towels! The softest of any chain actually. The only 'miss' for the hotel is the valet didn't understand our reservation, and instead directed us to self park. His directions included making a left turn which required breaking the law in order to do so. Upon check-in, we were advised that the valet should have parked the car. The front desk agent at check-in was exceptional, and apologized repeatedly. She really did her best to make up for the mistake, and was extremely professional. In the end however, I had to ride with the valet, to the ramp to locate my car so they could park it properly. Not the best solution. We indulged in the pool, hot tub and sauna, which were all very lovely on a rainy Sunday. Like any hotel, the only downside in this area are parents who are too busy texting to watch their young children run around. One nice feature is the hotel is connected through interior access to two restaurants, including Ruth Chris Steakhouse. Granted, Chicago is home to great restaurants on every corner, but this was a nice amenity. As was the complimentary umbrella, which we scored before they ran out. Complimentary breakfast was as expected, and as always, very busy in a family friendly hotel on a holiday weekend. The staff managed this chaos well, keeping most food well stocked. If I was on business, this would have proved less than pleasant. At check-out, we were genuinely asked how our stay was, and with the exception of the parking dilemma, everything was excellent. I would recommend and return to the Hampton inn & Suites for a leisure visit, or midweek business trip.

“Beautiful Hotel, Small Rooms” We stayed at the Omni Parker House over Valentines weekend. The hotel lobby was beautiful, check in was a breeze. The gold elevators are beautiful and you really feel like you are stepping back in time. Past that not so hot. The room that we had was soooo small. We had two double beds and they were so small we could not sleep comfortably. The wallpaper was peeling and paint chipping. The rooms are in desperate need of updating. If you stay here you have to pay for a bigger room and hope that you get it, not so great! We had the sunday brunch and it was good but not $22 a person good. I do not think I would stay here again unfortunately.

“Couldn't find a single fault..” Had a recent 5 night stay at this hotel and I have to say, I found every aspect of the stay flawless. My room was large, clean and well equipped. The bed comfortable, and the other furnishings were well chosen too. The bathroom was great, with nice toiletries and a powerful shower. Staff were unfailingly helpful and willing to go that extra mile, and the recent renovations made the place have that extra sparkle of "newness" that pushed the hotel up to the top of the league. The location isn't particularly friendly if you aren't able to walk hills - that must be said. All roads to this hotel are very steep, but there is little the hotel can do about the topography. However cabs are plentiful, and a town car service is offered on a first-come, first serve basis by the hotel in the morning which can leave you anywhere in town. The cable car lines also stop right outside - and the California/Van Ness cars are generally quieter and easy to get on, so head to the Embarcadero and take it all the way up the hills if you are heading back to the hotel! I'd recommend this hotel to anyone, and I hope that I get to go back there pretty soon!

“Great Location; The room is lacking” great location, convenient, quiet side street close to theater district, time square, dining,. The front desk staff, concierge and all staff courteous. We walked everywhere. Did not try the breakfast. Room although renovated and very pleasing on the eye, the air conditioning system is really not up to standard and the bed is rock hard. Very difficult to sleep with the sound of the air blower on this bed. The elevator is petite but really not an issue. If the bed changes and the air conditioning does not sound like a hurricane would be back.

“Exceptional! Good find in the Galleria Area.” I just stayed at this hotel and I was rather impressed. I have stayed at many Hyatt Place hotels and really liked them. This was my first time staying at the Summerfield and WOW! Check in was a breeze. The lobby area is very chic but not pretentious like some boutique hotels. This hotel has an adjoining car park and you can drive up to your floor and just walk to your room (prefect for you shopaholics!) The room was clean, bright, and very very spacious. The kitchen area and bath room were clean. This is not much space in the bedroom but the living room area and vanity area more than makes up. The bed was comfy with clean fresh sheets. Lots of pillows to play with!! TWO (2) flat screen tv's, dvd player and the decor is very stylish. Everyone is super friendly and I got a friendly 'good morning' from everyone! It was very pleasant and refreshing. The breakfast is good also. Eggs, sausage, cereal, fruit, you name it. The hotel is located in the Galleria area but a few blocks off busy Westheimer. Easy access to 610 and 59 without having to battle the traffic on Westheimer. Free HSIA and with excellent speed. I highly recommend this property for a quick stay in Houston or an extended stay.

“Wonderful, as usual at the Omni Shoreham” My most recent stay was my second time at the Omni Shoreham. I love this hotel. The lobby is gorgeous and there were huge bouquets of fresh roses everywhere the whole time I was there -- red for several days and then yellow. You can smell them when you walk in! I also enjoyed all the historical information around the hotel about the things that happened there through the years -- presidential balls, the Beatles stayed there, part of Julia Roberts movie Pelican Brief shot there, etc.... Valet, bellmen, concierge and front desk staff were all friendly and helpful. Checkout was at noon and I was just returning from an outing and still had to pack. The hotel was full, but they were gracious enough to give me an extra hour to get all my stuff together and didn't charge me a late check-out fee. Stayed in room with two queens and a view of the hotel's backyard, which is all lit up with lights at night -- very pretty and makes it feel like you're not in such a huge city. The beds were very comfortable with all white linens. The bathrooms aren't huge, but are very nicely equipped. Liked the desk and chair work area, where I spent lots of time doing work on my laptop. You get free internet if you sign up for their membership program -- I did it online a month or so before I went. Well worth it if you stay at Omni hotels even every once in a while. Despite all the great things I already mentioned, one of the best things about this hotel is its location. It's a block from a Metro station and tons of great restaurants -- bistro/bakery, Irish pub, Japanese, Chinese, Thai, Mediterranean, Italian, Indian, etc. It's also not a far walk from the Zoo (6-8 blocks or so). It's not a cheap hotel, but is well worth the price.
“Great, reliable stay” As always, this hotel serves up a positive experience. Very comfortable, very helpful staff, beautiful surroundings. Recommended for business travel.

“Great airport hotel” When I booked this hotel I had never stayed at a Homewood Suites property before and didn't know what to expect. I was flying out of Charlotte Douglas International Airport and wanted a Hilton family, park and ride hotel with free shuttle service to the airport. I was very pleased with this hotel. The suite was generously sized with an almost fully equipped kitchenette - stove, microwave, dishwasher, sink and full-sized refrigerator. The rooms were clean and in great condition. The free breakfast included the usual foods plus eggs, sausage and french toast. For those who fly out before breakfast is served they provide a to-go bag for you. Staff was friendly and helpful. My room, including tax, was $75, so it was very reasonable. I will definetely stay here the next time I fly out of CLT. One possible downside is that there is no room service and no restaurants within walking distance. There are several area restaurants that will deliver and if you fill out a grocery list the hotel will purchase and delvier your groceries for you with no charge.

“Loved It!” Booked through Priceline for $93/night. At first I thought location would be an issue because it it out by the zoo. Not at all. If you're comfortable with using the Metro then this place is a great choice. It has large quasi-resort feel. Room was spacious, clean and updated. Lobby was large with many areas to work or chill. Hotel bar had good food and resonably priced drinks. I would definitely stay here again.

“Rich in history, but poor in amenities.” My daughter and I toured San Francisco and stayed at The Fairmont for three nights. The room was lovely. The hotel is beautiful and so rich in history. It's obviously a place for the rich and famous. Speaking of rich and famous...perhaps there are amenities they get that ordinary tourists don't. But for the price we paid, I felt we were rich and famous for three nights. I would have liked to have had complimentary water available to us at check in, coffee and tea in the room (like The Trump in Chicago), and chocolates with turn down service. This is Ghiradelli country after all. I would also have appreciated access to a swimming pool and hot tubs (like The Trump in Chicago). Overall, this was a pleasant stay and I'm happy we chose this hotel for the history and comfort. However, if I visit San Francisco again, I'll look for a place that is not only comfortable, but rich in amenities. I have rated this hotel as very good based on the reasons given in the review.

“バルコニー付きの部屋がお勧め!” 6月に5泊したのですが、本来は普通のシングルであったところ、事前にオフィシャルサイトでバルコニー付きの部屋へのアップグレードのリクエストを出しておいたところ、運良く宿泊することができました。さらに、「なるべく高層階を」とフロントにお願いしたところ、最上階から二階下の44階(4472号室)を用意して貰えました。その際、部屋の準備が整うまでと10分程度待たされたのですが、そのお詫びとして、無料朝食バフェのクーポンを一回分用意してもらえ、フロント担当の応対は非常に好感度が高いものでした。 建物自体は、さすがに古さは否めないものの部屋の中に入ると、それは全く感じさせず、バスルームなども広さはなくとも、とても清潔でした。 バルコニー付き高層階からの眺めはとにかく抜群で、左手にコイトタワー、有名なトライアングルビルを始めとする金融街、右手にはオークランドに繋がるベイブリッジにサンフランシスコ湾まで一望でき、何よりも湾から吹き上げる風がとても気持ち良かったです。 無料券をいただいた朝食のビュッフェは、標準以上でも以下でも無いものでしたが、オレンジジュースが絞りたて果肉感たっぷりでとても美味しかったのが印象的です。 また、バルコニー付きの部屋にはコンチネンタル朝食が付いてくるのですが、これがちょっと変わっていて、ロビーに併設されているスターバックスから好きなパン一点、果物一点、飲み物一点(フラペチーノもOK)を自由に選べるというシステムでした。 他にも、最近どこのエアラインも導入している24時間前にチェックインできるシステム専用の機械がロビーに二台設置されていたりして、なかなか素晴らしいサービスだと感じました。 もちろん、地の利の良さは言うまでもなく、ユニオンスクエア、パウエル通り、マーケット通りなどどこも歩いて5分圏内で、観光、ショッピングに困ることはありません。 自分は往復とも空港からBARTを利用したのですが、パウエル駅からホテルまで徒歩8分ほどでした。 これほど立地条件に恵まれ、室内設備やサービスも良いのに、近隣の日航やグランドハイアットと比べて割安感があるので、自分は、今後もヒルトンユニオンスクエアを利用すると思います。

“Upscale, Convenient, Great for Harbor Walks but kind of noisy” This hotel is right between the Convention Center and the Harbor. There is a short walk to lots of restaurants and bars around the harbor. It's right by the USS Constellation and the harbor water taxi. The staff here is great. My only real complaint is with the architect who selected doors that don't seal and that close LOUDLY. We kept getting woken up by the banging and our connecting room had not much sound insulation so we could clearly hear what was going on next door (and I'm sure vice-versa). I would try to close a door quietly but by design it has a loud latching noise that is unavoidable. This diminished the quality of the stay quite a bit and is the reason I didn't rate the hotel much higher. Watch out for the cost of internet access. They sell two speeds and the $10/night is kind of slow, the $30/night was a little pricey for my actual needs. The drinks at the bar are kind of pricey too.

“Exactly what you'd expect...” I was in town for a convention. This hotel is exactly what you would expect in a Courtyard. Nicely laid out, clean, good sized rooms. Nice work out area. Very small pool. The restaurant was great, excellent service and a convenient downtown location. It's only a couple of blocks from the convention center and is close to Reading Market and a number of restaurants. There was no downside.

“Great Location, Excellent Hotel” The pluses: excellent location. You can go from mall to mall with cross overs and never go outside. That comes in handy with rainy/bad weather. Shaws supermarket is practically across the street. The Prudential Center is a block away and good place to see the entire city from the 50th during the day or 52nd floor at night (we don't recommend the food unless you enjoy uncooked duck in your salad that the waiter doesn't tell you about. Just have drinks). Good neighborhood and seems very safe for walking around. There is a good breakfast place several blocks away, Thornton's Cafe, where you can get excellent eggs and omelettes. Avoid Au Bon Pain for any hot breakfast unless you enjoy cold hard waffles and ttheir food is expensive at $.49/oz. The restaurant in the hotel, 10 Huntington, is a bar and great place in the back for a Sunday brunch. They have great food. Be careful not to go into a food coma from eating too much. The concierge were very helpful and always available. There was never a wait to speak to one of the two on duty. The telephone staff is very helpful and friendly. We fabulous views day and night from the 22nd floor. Ask for a high up floor. The negatives: The rooms have the most uncomfortable chairs. We requested a different desk chair or even another of the same that might be stuffed better, but they could not give us anything but a plain old chair that was not comfortable either. The mattress was too hard and hurt our backs. The cleaning staff did not do a good job. Some days the bathroom was practically overlooked. The tub was not cleaned every day. They did not leave shower wash until the third day. They did not leave a shower cap until the fourth day. Overall, we liked the hotel and the convenience and will stay here again.

“Too big, too noisy, too little service” Stayed at this hotel for 7 nights in June 2010. Overall, the rooms are small (and the room sizes in each category vary significantly), the front desk is not helpful (seems like they select which HH guests will get the bigger or smaller rooms. The hotel has over 1000 rooms (and if it didn't, it felt like it). In many ways, the staff treated guests as if you were in Las Vegas and didn't need service, just check you in, ignore you and make sure you pay for everything. The lobby restaurant was ok - don't order desserts. The service was good, but slow - really slow. And that was when there were 5 other tables occupied. Imagine what it would be like if it was packed!!! The pool is interesting and small - and will so many rooms and guests, well you get the picture. The only good thing about this hotel were the housekeeping staff. The ones you don't see do a great job of cleaning your rooms, making sure you have enough of everything and make you feel like you're getting something for all the money you're spending. Why is that? I don't get it. Shouldn't the front desk staff be the best? Overall, a terribly unmemorable stay.

“Old Money...” The common areas and lobby of this hotel are beautiful, and I'm sure the suites are too. However, we had a standard room and I couldn't help but think of being at some rich, old relatives house that hasn't been touched since the 50's or 60's. Lot's of "fuzzy" upholstery, pillows and drapes, etc... The bathroom was very standard, with the shower/tub combo (though the Bvlgari products were very nice!). I'm sorry, but as far as I'm concerned, in 2007, a hotel can not be 5 star, or charge $500 a night for a standard room, without a separate shower and tub. Also, ladies, please be warned about the "salon services". I booked a pedicure through the spa (which, by the way, was incredibly screwed up by the reservation dept.). For $125 I was led upstairs, to one of the regular hotel rooms that had the beds taken out and replaced with 2 of their "grandma chairs", handed a remote control to the t.v., and told I could change the channel if I wanted. What? For the next 45/50 minutes I sat uncomfortably upright receiving a pedicure, with a bowl of water at my feet that the poor manicurist had to keep running to the bathroom to change, all the while thinking that this couldn't possibly be a Ritz Carlton. Forget about spa chairs and aroma therapy! This HAS to be some type of temporary arrangement, yet nothing was said about it, and the price certainly was not adjusted. (Oh, and they so "considerately" add the 17% tip to the total for you. Just in case we forget I guess...) The highlight of the hotel was without a doubt the service. Most everyone in the hotel was extremely gracious and so willing to help. The doormen were exceptional.

“Friendly Attentive Staff - a recent make-over adds modernity to the property” The building itself, along with the W and the shopping plazas are a horrendous concrete blight on the Boston skyline; however, the review is about the Marriott Copley ! Uber friendly check-in, with a new lobby that speeds up the process. Associates are well trained and can genuinely anticipate your needs. Brandon was awesome. Franco as the Concierge knows Boston and is the quintessential gentleman - he should be at The Four Seasons. I have read reviews where guests complain on this forum; I have had a couple of issues in the past with this property and if you advise the Front Desk, they do all in their power to accommodate. It would appear that a lot of the associates from the past are no longer at the property- that may indeed be a blessing. The hotel has a new lease on life. Downside -- housekeeping staff is predominantly chinese/catonese - this is not, in any way a racist remark, just it's pretty hard to ask for extra towels - perhaps I should learn the language :) - if you stay, you'll understand.

“Nice Hotel but Front Desk Staff Needs Serious Improvement!” Let's start with the good: The rooms were a nice size. Beds EXTREMELY comfortable. Room is clean, Concierge was very efficient. The hotel itself is beautiful, lovely lobby area, Free coffee and tea at all times, and the location is fabulous for some fun shopping and nightlife. Also the Valet Parking was excellent and efficient, and you have in/out privileges. The bad: For one, the bathroom doors do not have a lock. Also when closing the room door it tends to slam shut very loudly. And thirdly, (most importantly) I was traveling with my family, and we had booked 2 rooms. We arrived at the hotel around 2:00pm. Upon our arrival we were told that check-in is at 3pm and that checkOUT was at 2pm (which did not make any sense). When we asked if at least one room was ready the front desk lady (who had an accent-possibly french) was very rude and said to come back after 3pm. We came back after 3pm to get our rooms and when we asked if the rooms could be beside each other (since we were told they had no connecting rooms upon arrival) she answered very rudely that we were lucky to even be on the same floor. The staff, or at least this particular lady, is in DIRE need of training on how to communicate with guests. My family and I were very turned off by this rudeness and it spoiled our outlook of this hotel. It's sad that we didn't feel welcomed into the hotel at all. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend.... I'm not sure.

“Amazing for the price!” We stayed here for a weekend in September. For $78 a night we could not have asked for more. The room was HUGE! 2 double beds and a pull out bed in the living room! We had 5 people in one room and we were not cramped at all. Absolutely would stay here again. If you can get a good rate, go for it!!!

“Denver Needed This Hotel” Now, when you have an opportunity to stay at a Ritz that’s a month and half old, you take it. lad I did. The service at valet and check-in was top notch. The room was gorgeous. Well laid out, brand new flat screen TV, marble bathroom, glassed in shower, and separate soaking tub. They had overhead lights over the bed that you could turn off with a switch on the side of the night stand. The in room coffee was superb and the turn down service, (providing ice and bottled water at bed side) was great. The beds are comfy. All is top notch about the hotel. The only issue to point out is that the hotel is directly across from the Denver bus station. I find that a bit odd, especially when walking to LoDo, and being hit up for cash by the homeless congregating in front of the Greydog’s lair (bus station). So a word to the wise, if you are uncomfortable with the homeless, be careful around the hotel. Second word to the wise, 7 blocks away in LoDo is Vesta’s Dipping Grill. Highly recommended. Food was fantastic, service was great, and they let you eat at the bar if you are solo on business. I can offer no review of Elway’s, which is the Ritz’s restaurant. However, I was told by my local colleagues not to bother. However, in keeping with the review parameters, I can offer no opinion because I did not grab a beer in their bar or otherwise eat there. Both nights when I returned, the bar sounded crowded, but I did not get an opportunity to go in. In sum, fantastic hotel, fantastic service, and I hope to get a room there on my next run through Denver.

“Stay now, before everyone else finds out about it!” I stayed here this past Friday night, and was thoroughly impressed. For this price point, 6 Columbus is a great, hip choice. It has a kickass location (just behind Columbus Circle), which makes it very convenient. There aren't a lot of large-hotel amenities (such as pool or business centre), but it's high on design (blue/silver/brown trendy decor) and nice boutiquey touches such as Fresh brand toiletries. The staff is friendly, and the hotel small enough that you can get in and get out without long waits for anything. It's not for everyone, but if you like hip boutique hotels, you should definitely stay at 6 Columbus now...before all the rooms get trashed by overuse.

“Worth considering if you need to be in downtown Phoenix” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency for three nights while attending a series of meetings at the Phoenix Convention Center. It’s a very nice property that has been kept up well over the 30+ years of its existence. Having grown up in Phoenix, I watched this hotel being built. It was quite the sensation with its eight-story open-air lobby and revolving restaurant on top. Three decades hence, it’s still a very nice hotel. Obviously, the hotel has been refurbished (probably several times) since its construction so room amenities are strictly 21st century: comfortable beds with multiple pillows and high thread-count linens, flat screen TV, work stations with Internet access (both wired and wireless), iron and ironing board, iHome radio/iPod dock, higher-end amenities in the bathrooms, and bathrobes available upon request. Owing to its late-70s vintage, however, the standard rooms are a bit on the small side. The air conditioning, while a step up from the wall-mounted units popular in so many hotels, is still noisier than it ought to be. And the soundproofing leaves something to be desired; several times, I heard fellow guests in adjoining rooms or out in the hall. Further, I will never understand why upscale hotels like the Hyatt Regency use thin, cheap-feeling towels and then – worse – let them get so worn that they develop spots so thin you can see through them. The first morning, my bath towel had a couple of large thin spots as well as a noticeable stain. The bath mat I used on two out of three mornings had begun to fall apart and had numerous loose threads hanging from them. Generally, though, the property continues to impress. The revolving restaurant on the 24th floor, the Compass, offers great views of Phoenix and some pretty good food and drink as well. If you’re acrophobic, the Terrace Café on the second floor atrium level or the Networks Bar and Grill on the ground floor are more casual but still pretty good, though without the views. There are several shops, including an Einstein’s Bagels, off the lobby and a car rental counter on site. The hotel also offers a pool, fitness center, and business center. Downtown Phoenix, though, is a downtown that has never quite found its feet. Certainly, the Convention Center, U.S. Airways Center, and Chase Field draw crowds for specific events, but when there’s nothing special happening, the area gets pretty barren, save for the area’s homeless. But if you’re going to Phoenix for a meeting or event downtown, definitely consider the Hyatt Regency. If you want to take in a view of the city, The Compass provides that for the cost of a drink, even if you’re staying somewhere else.

“Yes if you want space No if you want tourist location or style” The prior reviews are all pretty much on point. The review posted by "504" on 11/21 was right almost word for word, shabby window treatments, carpets, wallpaper, etc. Another poster described the stuff as "faded." All true. It depends on what you want. For us (a family of 4) the one bedroom suite was by far the largest space we stayed in: the bedroom was around 12 x 14 and the living room was probably 12 x 20 -- huge by Manhattan standards. (see pictures) But the place was a little worn. We're used to Marriott's and this was a couple of grades below that. Location: this is not a tourist area; its more a neighborhood. I don't think theres much to do in Times Square (not into plays, ESPN, etc.) so I prefer not to stay there. This is an exiciting neighborhood with a real urban feel to it and just walking around is fun enough. The hotel is 2 blocks from the 72nd express stop on the Broadway line so its easy to get most anywhere, although at a fare of $2 - the $8 fare for a family of 4 adds up. Cab fare to the Chelsea galleries should be around $14; Canal Street should be about $18. If you want this neighborhood with some style try the On the Ave hotel 2 blocks north: more expensive and much smaller but very modern rooms. Food store: Best and cheapest is to shop in Fairway, the huge (by Manhattan standards) supermarket across the street or its better competitor 2 blocks north same side of the street. All the normal stuff in both stores plus tons of cheeses and prepared gourment foods. Worth a look even if you don't buy. Restaurants: Amsterdam and Columbus (the two street parallel to and east of Broadway) are loaded with restaurants -- walking and looking is fun by itself. Fast Food: The two pizza places north of the hotel on the east side of Broadway were (surprisingly for NY) mediocre to bad. If you want pizza, Little Nicks (2 blocks north, west side of Broadway) was outstanding. Gigi's, about 5 blocks south, west side of Broadway, had delicious quessadillas, and the Jewish deli (3 blocks north, east side of Broadway) was mediocre to good and a little expensive for fast food

“Location. Location. Location” Hard to beat for its location the Fairfax at Embassy Row still has the look and feel of a bygone era, which is not particularly appealing to me. However, I do recognize they do their job right catering to people who want to enjoy this experience. Stayed one night with wife for an anniversary and we were not disappointed. Location is perfect right next to Dupont Circle and a metro station.

“Good location” Stayed here for 4 nights over Easter weekend. Got a great rate from the hotel web site. The check in was good, the lobby is nice, the room was large with a very comfortable bed. The bathroom is very small but the shower was nice with good water pressure. I had to plug the blow dryer in out side the bathroom and open the door to use it. I love this area of DC, you must be very careful when walking due to a large homeless shelter 1 block away but otherwise the Capitol and Union Station are both within easy walking distance.We did eat breakfast at Art and Soul, beware it was not very good and very expensive! Dinner at Art and Soul was much better. I did not come by car so I did not use the parking. Overall staff very helpful and friendly.

“隣が有名な双子のタワー” 場所はクラーク駅から近い。どこへ行くにも便利。隣はガイドブックにも乗っている特長的な双子のタワー。 ポッド有り。TVあり。DVD有り。有線、無線LANあるが無線は弱い。デスク周りに電源が無いのがいまひとつ。歯ブラシなし。髭剃りなし。バスジェルなどはウェスティン共通のホワイトティーアロエで、バスタブ、シャワーは同じ。スリッパなし。バスローブあり。無料水あり。SPGプラチナはラウンジが使えるので、朝食がそこで取れる。設備もよく、やはりウェスティンは安心できます。

“Nothing too bad or good...” Basically, its a standard 4 points that is cat 4 probably due to location, otherwise its a bit subpar and closer to cat 2-3. Valet parking was very quick and convenient, employees were relatively nice and friendly. Rooms are quite plain and somewhat expected, just a bit older than expected and had a musty smell. Pool is really tiny, somehow the elevator always had chlorine smell, but not a big deal. Platinum members get the standard continental breakfast for 2 people. If given a choice, i'd probably choose the Embassy Suites or Grand Hyatt on a return visit, even though Starwood hotels are usually my preferred brand. Nothing wrong with the hotel, just not as nice as i'd hope for or expect of a cat 4 even if it is only a Four Points by Sheraton

“Well maintained but expensive for the room” why would a room have a step up in it soon after you enter the door? Not sure but it reminded me of a room I once stayed in Vegas with a sunken living room. It has to be a safety hazard which is why it's lit at night so you don't stumble down the two steps if you head to the bathroom. The internet connection worked well. The room was clean. The night staff were very knowledgeable about the area. However, the morning person was uninformed about the free pass I could get for working out at the nearby MetroFitness training facility which is just two short blocks away from the hotel. Skip the valet parking and park one block away for $6 at the public lot. And skip the buffet breakfast while you're at it - it's not worth the $8.95 for the eggs and bacon. My main beef with the hotel is the price - it just is not a lot of value for the price.

“great hotel, fantastic location” I was staying at Room 2005 for two nights as part of a three week road trip. US$42 cab ride away from SFO airport. Arrived Sunday eveing, very efficent check-in. no delays. Business Centre 50 cents p/min. Great room, including coffee maker. The hotel is right on Fisherman's Wharf. One minute walk to Pier 39, for great food and shops. I-Hoop and Jonny Rocket's on premises. Short walk to car rental downtown, which we picked up Avis vehicle. Good tour -- if you can't get on the Alcatraz island -- 'Blue & Gold' ferry trip under Golden Gate bridge and around Alcatraz Island with great narrative. Free USA Today. Fully recommend hotel.

“Nice Stat at the Hilton New York” I recently stayed at the Hilton New York. I originally wanted to stay at the Hilton Times Square, but was only able to get into the Hilton New York. I stay at Hiltons to earn points and rewards. First of all, the hotel is extremely large. If you plan on staying here, there will be a lot of people going and coming all of the time. There were two major conventions going on while I was there. The hotel was booked at capacity for the nights that I was there. If you are looking for a smaller hotel, then this is not for you. I believe the hotel has a little under 2,000 rooms. I really didn't have much interaction with the front desk staff, so I cannot comment too much on how polite they were. When I checked out today, one of the ladies at reception complained to a colleague that they were going to be understaffed. They should probably be careful to not let customers hear comments like this. If you stay here, you should definitely ask for a renovated room. Thanks to other reviewers, I knew to do this. My room was very very nice. The bed is extremely comfortable -- I am very critical when it comes to beds. Room was very clean and well appointed. Bathroom only had a shower, which was fine for me, but maybe not for others. I'm sure they have rooms with tubs, but you may want to ask. Shower always had hot water and great pressure. Flat screen tv was in the room with a wide variety of channels to choose from. I would recommend asking for a room that is away from the elevator. Originally I was placed in room right next to the elevator. Though I couldn't hear the bell of the elevator I could hear it going up and down the shaft which would've mad me very crazy!! So, I asked for a room change and was given this immediately with no problems. Taxis are extremely easy to get her. They come into the drive all of the time. If you are going to use the subway you are close to two stops. The F Train and the B, D, and E Trains. If you take the F Train, make a left as you leave the hotel lobby. You will be there in 2-3 minutes. It's on Sixth Ave. If you need the B, D, and E Train, make a right out of the lobby and a right onto 52nd. (I think it is 52nd street. After you make a right out of the lobby onto Sixth Ave., it's the first street. Make another right onto this street.)You'll be there in about 3-4 minutes. I also used the bus that went up and down Sixth Ave. Theres a stop less than 1 minute from the hotel lobby. All hotel incendentals are extremely expensive. I did order room service several times. The food is fabulous. I waited no longer than 20 minutes to get my food. This was very expensive, but costs were well explained in the menu. I have to say the room service was the best that I've ever received. High quality and outstanding service. Just be warned .. very expensive. The hotel was very busy during my stay. I did have to wait a few minutes for the elevator, but never found this to be unbearable. They have different elevators for different levels. The most I waited for an elevator was about 3 minutes. TV in each elevator --- always on CNN. I enjoyed this. Across the street on Sixth Ave is a Deli. I went there instead of buying items from my hotel fridge. I saw a lady in the deli who was restocking her fridge with items she consumed the night before. Thought that was a good idea. I don't know how the hotel will handle this. I did use the business center on the second floor. $10.00 minimum for ten minutes of Internet/computer time. Each additional minute is $1.00. Computers extremely fast. I also noticed that they had a shipping center near the business center as well. I thought this was a nice touch. Room was cleaned each day. I didn't feel any pressure from the maid to leave a tip. I did however have a maid knock on my door and then open my door after I originally checked in. She wanted to make sure everything was okay. I wish she would've waited for me to answer the door. I know she just wanted to see if I was okay. I recommend calling for turn down service each night. Your room is straightened up and prepared for a good nights sleep. Chocolates are left on the pillow. Hotel is in a great area. Many great restaurants around. My room was on the 34th floor. This was a renovated floor. I could not hear street traffic, nor could I hear "my neighbors" next door. Floor was kept clean. I am often disappointed if the area outside of my room is messy. Room service plates were removed promptly. Whenever I called for customer service, I was always greeted by my name. I never had to wait on hold. All my needs were met. Overall, I had a very nice time at the hotel. I found the accomodations to be excellent. Again, it's a very large hotel, so be prepared for a lot of people. Once you are on your floor, there will not be many people. The Hilton New York was a pleasant surprise for me. After reading other reviews, I was uncertain. My stay exceeded my expectations and I would gladly stay here again.

“lovely vacation hotel, upgraded rooms definitely worth it” We thoroughly enjoyed the Dana at Mission Bay. It is extremely convenient to Sea World, without feeling touristy or boxy, and also to Pacific Beach and La Jolla. When I booked I was offered the upgraded room for an extra $50/day, and was glad we did. The renovated and upgraded rooms are FAR better than the others available, which are dated. Beware...there are parking fees that you may or may not be told about! The hotel grounds and pool were delightful and we enjoyed walking over to the marina. There is a free shuttle to Sea World that came in handy . We also really liked the restaurant, and ate there twice. Definitely a great choice for a San Diego vacation.

“Good Conference Venue” We stayed 5 nights during a writing conference. We were upgraded to a South Tower 1-bedroom suite (because it was my partner’s birthday). Lovely large room and excellent toiletries – they use the same brand in the Convent Garden Hotel and Soho Hotel in London. The shower was amazing. Very comfortable bed and everything was very clean. The main hotel rooms did not seem as modern and the roms over there lacked a laptop safe. The A/C was on a movement sensor so be warned. The lobby bar was vast but over-priced. We had Sunday Brunch at The Fountain restaurant – thank goodness for the conference discount of 20 per cent. Service was haphazard and our wine arrived corked. The server didn’t know what corked meant and we had to explain that it had gone off and was not drinkable! Brunch itself was okay but nothing special. The concierge, check-in and check-out staff were friendly and helpful. Good gym. Nice pool area, although it closed the last day we were there, because it was leaking into one of the function rooms downstairs and nearly flooded the Dealer’s Room. We were on a great rate (99 a night) so it was certainly excellent value for money. If you have a choice, go for a South Tower room.

“Loved the Marriott” My girlfriend and I stayed at the Marriott in the beginning on December 2007. We booked the room through Hotelopia and got a killer rate. The Marriott is without a doubt one of the best hotels in Boston. It's huge but it doesn't feel like a big hotel. The elevators are never crowded and the staff is very friendly. We had a room on the 10th floor with a great view of the Back Bay area. The room was spacious (compared to other US hotels) and the bathroom was equipped with a large tub. The hotel is located within the Copley Place shopping centre and it's a shoppers dream. The Back Bay area is packed with bars and restaurants, for example on Newbury Street and the rest of downtown Boston is within walking distance, or a few minutes ride on the T. I would recomend this hotel to anyone going to Boston.

“Nice, but pretentious” This was our second stop in Memphis; we had booked for two nights. You usually know what to expect with Westin hotels, but this time I have to say I was quite disappointed. Location is great, just one block from Beale street - although do make sure to get a room on the other side of the building if you plan to get some sleep! The hotel itself looks great, brand new, very clean. The rooms are very nice, too, pretty spacious, and beds are comfortable. You can pretty much hear anything going on in the corridors though, and we were awakened a couple of times by people coming back to their room late, loud, after a few drinks on Beale Street. The big let-down was service / attitude of the staff / hotel policies. First, the person who checked us in wasn't nice at all. No smile, no welcome look. We didn't feel welcome at all, and had the same feeling all along our stay. What to say about the mini-bar policy? All the items are on a scale, and if you touch something, it will be charged to your room directly. From a customer perspective, either the hotel thinks I'm a thief and I'll try to take stuff from the mini bar without telling them (which feels pretty insulting) or they're trying to charge me for services / products I'm not using (i.e if something falls from the scale, you'll be charged even though you haven't used it). I've never seen anything like this, and I hope not to see it again! Service wasn't really good: we would see trays of food left in the corridors, that would stay there all day. Everytime we tried to get the car out of the parking, we had to wait several minutes, because you need to show your hotel parking ticket to someone... but no one is ever there. People wouldn't even say hi or thank you. When you add this to the fact that everything is extra at Westin hotels (i.e parking not included, breakfast not included, internet access not included, even bottles of water in the room are not free), the whole experience comes out quite overpriced for what you get. The only smile we got from anyone in the hotel was upon check-out. Overall, this is a hotel trying really hard to make you feel like it's a privilege for you to be here, when it's normally the other way round. Being high-end is not about looking down on your own customers. I think there's a big management issue here. I will personally not stay there again, and do recommend other hotels in Memphis instead of this one (i.e River Inn in Harbor town, much better value and service)

“really still love this hotel” although we stayed in the smallest room in their inventory, i still really love this hotel. the initial build out and recent soft reno just makes sense. it's 4 stories of rooms with great high ceilings and a cool vibe. the restaurant is usually packed so make a reservation. we did the imax late movie and returned to a nearly empty bar with great service (perhaps we missed the rush - thank goodness). although winter, i could imagine having a cocktail in the center courtyard of the hotel. what really makes it worth it is the staff. friendly, knowledgable and gracious - a really excellent stay all around.

“Anything but "Common"” This hotel has made a big and impressive impact on what used to be an edgy part of Boston. The entire area has enjoyed new growth, and the Ritz Carlton sits like a crown jewel. The service, style and grace of the property is everything you'd expect of the Ritz Carlton name. We have stayed here 4-5 times over the last couple of years, most recently in early Deecmber 2006. The slightly minimalist style of the lobby and hallways gives way to plush and soothing rooms (including Bose and Bang & Olufsen radios). And the beds are particularly grand, even moreso than some other Ritz Carltons. If you can, splurge for a room on the Club Level, where the Club Room will complete the experience. While clearly not inexpensive, this property's rates are actually more moderate when compared to other Ritz Carltons in the Northeast. In all, a lot less fusty and a lot more enjoyable than its sister property across the Commons, and one of the very nicest hotels in Boston.

“Just ok.” Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights on our first trip to NYC. Location is great....you can walk to loads of places very easily. There's a subway nearby. Can't fault the rooms for size but the standard of cleanliness was just ok. The whole place is desperately in need of a revamp. The bathroom was the most basic I've ever experienced in a North American hotel.The "bell boys" were a bit strange! (All very big men in sharp suits. ) At no time did anyone offer help with luggage. No-one was rude exactly but they were very offhand & just a wee bit intimidating! Go across the street to the Morning Star diner for breakfast. Great food & extremely friendly staff who are more than happy to give you directions & advice on the best way to get around. Definitely do the movie location walking tour of Central Park....great fun !! As I said the hotel has an excellent location and the room was big but if we visit NYC again ( and we'd love to ....it's a fabulous city!!) I wouldn't choose to stay here.

“Great Location, Adequate Service” We stayed at this hotel with our two young sons for two nights in July. The hotel is very central to most of what you'd want to see in downtown Seattle. We found the hotel to be very clean, however while we were there apparently two elevators were broken which meant waits for up to 5 minutes during busy times.
