The concierge was often non-existent, and the staff were okay. It wasn't exceptional, but for the price and the location, it was fine.

“Wonderful Monaco” I stayed at the Monaco for two separate nights on each side of a trip to mom's in Colorado Springs. The first night, the really nice front desk guy upgraded me to a suite. The room service dinner was just perfect. Staff was very accommodating and helpful. And the Tattered Cover bookstore is just down the street!

“Excellent value in a convenient location” The hotel is literally steps from the Alamo, a few blocks from the Riverwalk, and was incredibly convenient to everything I wanted to do. I was in town for a conference at the Convention Center, and found it very easy to get there. A quick 10 minute walk (cutting through the mall and taking the Riverwalk) was all it took to get there. The room was spacious, the bed comfortable, and the staff helpful. I thought the room was very clean, but the bed linens are the old-style bedspreads. I took a taxi from the airport ($23 trip, 20 minutes) so I didn't have the issue with parking that others have experienced. The continental breakfast was tasty, filling, and free! All in all, the hotel was exactly what I needed for my stay: clean, safe, and a much better value than any other associated with my convention!

“A wonderful experience in a hotel that's a bit older than most” I was here for two nights for a few business meetings and while I haven't stayed at many Fairmonts, I knew it was an upscale brand that should be comfortable. Pulling up to the building I had my doubts—the towers look like they were built in the 80s—but once you get inside it's lovely. The FOOD is fantastic and the staff is some of the BEST out there. Three cheers for Donna in the Gold level lounge! (LOVE the honor bar, drinks, and food in there. Worth paying to stay on the Gold level. Also a nice spot for meetings with free internet.) The staff is VERY attentive and even a man delivering my room service added one of my dietary preferences to my client record for my next stay. And the house driver gave us a complimentary lift to Texas de Brazil (a great dinner out if you love meat!). My room was a suite and was nothing super fancy but nice and spacious and mostly modern. Loved the little kitchenette and having a fridge was handy. I do wish the room had more outlets. There is a lovely vanity area and I sat down to blowdry my hair and then discovered there was no outlet in that area at all. Caution: You WILL catch glimpses that will flash you back to 1989 in some places like old phones in the bathroom and an elevator that sometimes acts wonky. And I'm sorry but I can't STAND having to use my room key to access all floors in the elevator (not just the Gold floors). It's very inconvenient when you are carrying files or bags around. I doubt there is that much of a security risk at this hotel to warrant that. Fitness center is in basement but has nice, clean, modern equipment. I do wish they had a real spa. They can arrange services in your room, but I didn't want someone in my room.

“Good for a conference” I spent a couple of days here for a conference (which was held at the hotel). It's a nice place, probably a little older than some, but it seems to have been renovated over time to keep pretty high standards. The room was nice, pretty large, with a good work area/desk. Room service was kind of pricey, but the food was good. I ate at the bar a couple of times (the restaurant is really expensive) and a couple of items were outstanding (pork tacos and the cheese plate). I was there earlier in the week when the tornadoes ripped thru metro Dallas. Kudos to the hotel and it's staff for having a plan in place and for executing that plan for it's guests.

“perfect for stay before an early flight” We stayed at LaQuinta because we had an early flight the following morning. With AAA rate, we only paid $53/night. It was only a 15min drive to the airport. We were able to check in at 11 am and spent the day at the great heated pool! The place was clean and withing walking distance to pick up some food/drinks. The room had a refrig and microwave. The free wireless was a plus and they had a desktop pc in the lobby for guests to use. One problem for us was that the free airport shuttle wasn't available until 7am so we had to get a cab for a 6 am pickup. The hotel arranged the pick up. Also, the continental breakfast opens at 6am so we were only able to grab a coffee and bagels before our cab arrived. Another problem was the somewhat loud air conditioner in the room. We would stay at this hotel again.

“Okay” We stopped here for an overnight on our way though Indiana. Overall, I can't compain. Had a clean room, clean bed, and clean bathroom. But everything seemed slightly off. It's out of the way in a corporate area. However if you check-in after 11pm you have to use the buzzer to get in as if you were checking into a hotel in the ghetto. The hotel is doughnut shaped. The check-in is on one side and you have to walk all the way around to the other to go up the elevator. It was 30 degrees outside and the AC was on high in our hallway. Fortunatly the temprature was fine in the room. I can't really complain about the place, but there were things that just didn't feel right and were quite distracting.

“Good Hotel on the Riverwalk” We took a last minute short Spring Break trip with our boys (18 an d14) to San Antonio. I booked their room with points and then booked one of the suites for my wife and I. The hotel was very busy as was all of San Antonio. But, the service a the hotel was top notch. Especially impressive was the female concerierge, who was most helpful. The hotel gave us connecting rooms which was nice. The suite was very large with a large living area and balcony that looked right over the Riverwalk. We ate at two great restaurants (Bella on the River and Biga on the Bank). Both were very good and I highly recommend them (not cheap, but good). Overall, it was a great experience.

“セントラルパークが見下ろせる高級ホテル” 37階パークビューに案内されました。部屋はきれい。バスタブあり。アメニティはPeter Thomas Rothというブランド。チボリオーディオの時計つきラジオ。ipod DOGなし。このホテルはチェックインに2時間も待たされました。また、SPG Plutinumであっても部屋のアップグレード以外に朝食、ラウンジなどのサービスは一切ありません。またポッドがない。冷蔵庫はあるが、使い勝手が悪い。(動かすと加算されるみたい。)無料の水すらない。年末カウントダウンのため周りは封鎖されますが、かといってボールドロップが見えるわけでもないので不便です。

“Overpriced, small rooms” My wife and I spent a weekend at this hotel as a romantic getaway. Though the hotel was OK, I would say overall it was disappointing, and I would not recommend it for that kind of stay. The room was very small, even though it was one of the more expensive rooms ($429 per night). For this price, I expect superluxury service, which this was not. The number of TV channels was disappointing. Also, there was no turn-down service. And there were tacky touches such as a breakfast menu left on the bed. I didn't like having to take two elevators to get to our room. On the plus side, the location was great if you like Times Square, as I do.

“Location, location, location” We booked this hotel through the blind booking process in Travelocity. We were glad to see that the reviews were not terrible once we found out the name of the hotel. As many others said the rooms are tiny, the bathrooms (private bathrooms) have been renovated and the beds are really uncomfortable, but the location is great and you have free wifi! Also the staff is really nice, they received a few online shopping stuff that we sent and kept them safe until our arrival and they were also helpful providing us with directions to attractions and restaurants. I would recommend this hotel only to budget travelers who can get a very good price deal (as we did... U$ 41 per night)

“Worthwhile option” We needed a place to stay after a show and turned to Murray Hill East after determining several other hotels we patronized at in the past were charging more than $400 a night. On arriving, we were told we would be getting a room upgrade and were given the keys to #1001. As some other reviews have stated, the rooms here are essentially efficiency apartments. This one had a newly retiled bathroom, kitchenette, living room with couch and love seat and dining table. The place was clean, with a decent uptown view, and the bed was comfortable. A winter storm rolled in overnight, but the heating was adequate -- not something you take for granted in some older New York hotels. The lobby and elevator showed signs of heavy wear. The $319 per night rate (before taxes) represented a decent deal, but not a bargain in my book. The overall experience reminded me of getting the use of an old college friend's apartment for the weekend. Grand Central terminal with subways, restaurants and commuter rail is just three blocks away. I'll keep the place in mind for future travel, probably as a second or third choice.

“My New Favorite” I love all of the Chicago Kimpton Hotels but since my last stay at Hotel Monaco have decided the this is my new favorite. Check in was a breeze, I asked about room size and the clerk told me If I wanted a bigger room with no view I could have it for the same price. Huge! two very comfortable king beds, two comfy chairs with ottomans a desk and armoire with t.v.. Bathroom wasn't huge but we managed. Foyer was large to accomodate our luggage so as not to mess up sleeping area. The Decor was very funky and fun. Afternoon wine hour was a hit in the lovely common area with fireplace. Concierge was helpful as was the valet team. The one bad thing and it was bad was after a full day of shopping we returned to our room at about 8:00 for a quick change for our dinner reservations and our room had not been cleaned no fresh towels nothing. When I called they immediately sent somebody to our room w/towels then finished after we left for the evening. Despite that I will definitely stay again.

“Great Location & Great Staff!” My huband,our daughters & I recently stayed at the Nob Hill Motor Inn for 3 nights recently. We were completely happy with our stay. We reserved a Junior Suite & the room was large & comfortable. Two Queens & a Sofa Bed, it also provided a fridge, microwave & coffee maker. They also offer free WiFi which was always working properly. We never had any trouble connecting. Included in the price is a continental breakfast, just pre-packaged pastries & juice, coffee & hot cocoa. Free Parking is another plus. We had a car that lived in the garage for most of our stay. We mainly used public transport which was only about 2 blocks to the cable cars and less than a block to the bus stop. Excellent value for the money!

“Everything you could want!” Renaissance Arboretum was beautiful! Absolutely the cleanest hotel I've ever stayed in. Really large room with comfortable chairs and ottoman and desk. Lovely lobby and hallways. Fast, convenient elevators (a separate one for the pool area). Perfect location for shopping and dining. Can walk outside hotel doors to many great stores like Pottery Barn, Coldwater Creek, Cheesecake Factory (great service and food), Amy's Ice Cream, etc. Can easily drive to downtown in about 15 minutes. Of course, food, etc. is expensive at such an expensive hotel. Valet was the fastest and friendliest I've experienced but expensive. Perfect little indoor pool for children. Totally worth the price overall. Only negative was noise from hundreds of people using meeting rooms and ballrooms. We kept the AC fan running all night and couldn't hear any of the lobby noises.

“Exceeded our expectations and then some.” Business took us to Boston and as usual, I sought accommodations convenient to our meeting site. As it turns out, we were in for a treat. Not only was the inn great in location, it was absolutely one of the nicest we've ever encountered. We travel extensively and this was like being home away from home in the best way possible. For us, the code entry system was a breeze and a delight. For those a little leery of it, there is an intercom and the office is staffed all day. Comforting to know, but non intrusive...nice. Our room was absolutely beautiful. Two large flat screen televisions, plush bed, well equipped kitchen, large shower in the bathroom and a gorgeous turreted living space. Everything was just wonderful and comfortable. A business associate picked us up for dinner one night and he too was blown away by the place. Complimentary breakfast is a huge perk in a large city where dining out three times a day can get pricey quickly. A pro tip: The Nespresso coffee is to die for...really it is incredible. I am jonesing for it as I write this. Convenient to everything in and around Back Bay, Fenway and Copley/Prudential, the neighborhood is living, working and breathing and wonderful to stroll through. Thank you Tom and Michael. Your assistance with our shipping logistics was appreciated as were your recommendations and kindness. All the best and we hope to be back soon!

“Rooms are in need of serious work” Spent 3 nights at conference at the hotel. The staff are wonderful! They are dedicated and helpful to your every need. Bed's in the room were the heavenly beds and I slept very well all 3 nights. Room was highly run down. Wall paper peeling off walls in different places, light bulb not replaced in room and carpet stained. Bathroom floors seems dirty and needed to be regrouted. Food was very expensive in restaurant and just okay. Burger, soda and tip $21.00. Save yourslf some money and eat off site. This is a hotel in the Hilton chain and I was disappointed.....:(

“Almost perfect.” After a month of hard work and travel, I decided to give Paradise a chance to help me up wind and relax a bit. I purchased a 3 day package in one of the Ocean Front Villas. It was very spacious and beautiful. The TV's were massive, but lacked quality picture. I purchased a film to watch one evening and I could barely see what was happening since it was a dark film and the TV was already super dim. Management sent over a tech guy to look at it, he showed me how to change the channels and was very friendly, but let me know that there was nothing he could do about the brightness of the TV. Yes, I tried the menu, and everything else, nothing worked. Every channel was dim and pixelated, but I think this was an issue with the TV service they use. For the price I paid on a room, I would have loved lotion, which was sent over it two little plastic cups when I called reception and asked for lotion. It was a little tacky in my opinion, and so were the shampoo/conditioner dispensers in the shower. I can understand that part, but lotion in a cup? The location is breathtaking, everyday spent there was very relaxing and beautiful. The firepits were great, the ducks, geese, and everything else were calming and non abrasive like they can be at other places. I must say though, the staff was top notch. I'd come back here just to see these people, they were incredible. The food was enjoyable and fresh, and my favorite part about it was being able to take my drink with me anywhere I went. Whisky on the rocks and a little ping pong, why not? All in all my stay was pleasant and the staff was great. The TV's could use a better service provider, and the lotion could maybe be in a dispenser as well, but everything else was excellent.

“Great for meetings/conventions” I stayed here in June for three nights for a conference in the hotel. Here's my quick review: Pluses: - wonderful rooms, flat-screen tv's with high definition programming, great work area with wired and wireless internet access, and perhaps the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. Mini-bar in the room - great restaurants, a bit pricey ($22 for the breakfast buffet), but they had a good selection of items. I had dinner and lunch here as well and both meals were fantastic, especially the seafood salad at lunch. Steaks are great, and every meal seems to come with french fries and multiple dipping sauces - great location for meetings at the convention center - helpful staff, no real complaints - very nice fitness center with new equipment, exercise equipment had built in television and headphones were complementary, the pool was a good size as well - no problems getting a cab, and they have a shuttle to the airport every half-hour (you have to pay for it). - very close to Logan, only about a 10 minute ride. Minuses: - I wouldn't stay here unless I had a meeting at the hotel or the convention center, there isn't much within walking distance (only one decent restaurant, the Legal Seafood Test Kitchen), it isn't on the water, it's about a 3 block walk to the water. It's definitely a business traveler's hotel - Way too far from downtown Boston and the major tourist/dining areas. About a 5-10 minute cab ride to the Faneuil hall marketplace.

“Serviceable but great location” Rooms need updating (time for flat screen TVs) but can't beat the location. Doormen are very nice. Understaffed front desk so forget calling down. Lots of great attractions, restaurants, etc. off the Mag Mile. Excellent rate one of the booking services.

“A gem of a hotel” Silver Cloud Inns has several hotels in Washington and Oregon; but I have not see any others.This one was recommended to me since it was nearest to my relative's house. It is also close to several hospitals and Seattle University. I would consider it a midtown location, very convienient to most of Seattle. The hotel offers shuttle service to several touirst areas, none of which I was going to this trip. $12 for parking in their lot though was stiff. However, in times of bad weather and at night, it's nice to be in a covered, and secure parking lot just under the hotel. This is a new hotel and as such is very clean. It has a comfortable, contemporary style in the lobby and the rooms, nothing looked overdone or pretentious. However, nothing appeared to be very environmental except for the energy saving light bulbs and the request to not waste water by asking for fresh linens daily. The shower heads do not appear to be water saver. Nor were any of the fabrics very earth friendly. Even the pillows on the bed were foam. The staff were all very helpful, courteous, and intelligent. As for the bar and restaurant, I can't say much. I had a drink at the bar that was very expensive, even for a top shelf vodak. The barteneder - Seth was a good guy though and the bar company was pleasant enough. The breakfast buffet was vast. But I felt there were far too many unhealthy pastries and not enough protein choices. There is an International House of Pancackes (IHOP) next door to the hotel, and many other, much better places to eat very close by. The things I found most unpleasant were the cold draft near the elevators coming from the parking garages below, and getting to the pool/spa/workout room. There are what appear to be closed wind block areas in front of each elevator in the garage but, there are large gaps under the doors, allowing the cold to easily seep in. To get to the pool/spa and excercise rooms, you have tomake a short walk across the 1st level parking garage. It was freezing cold so, not the best solution. It would be better to have a connection from inside the hotel. Also,a warmer changing area would be nice too.

“Ok” I stayed here one night when I had an early morning flight. I arrived at the hotel after midnight. The clerk was not at all welcoming. He was simply "flat"--not the usual Southern welcome one expects. I was checked in and went to the room. Being tired, I did not do much more than unpack toiletries, put out my clothing for the following day and go to bed. The room was spacious and I had no problems with room temperature. I was up and downstairs soon after 5 a.m. the next morning. There was no one at the desk but an employee was on the computer in the lobby. I tried to make noise and finally had his attention. He went to the back and the clerk came out. Again, very "flat". I explained that the trip was for business and there had been no receipt under my door, but that I needed one as I needed to complete an expense report when I returned. The clerk said there was a problem with the printer and that the only thing he could do would be to email it to me. I gave him my email address and left the hotel. I turned in my rental car, made the flight and was back in my office several hours later--no email and no receipt. I called the hotel and was told they would fax it, This clerk was very friendly and apologized. I had hoped to get my expense report completed before going to another meeting but was unable to do so . I did receive the fax --and two days after my stay I finally did get the promised email. I was not in the hotel long enough to experience the breakfast or property amenities. It was convenient to the airport and I would stay here again, but I would hope for a better rate than the $123/night I paid.

“Typisches HIE aber in schlechter Lage” Wenn man nicht wegen "at the Stadiums" hier ist findet man die Lage nicht gerade toll. An einer Seite an einer stark befahrenen Strasse gelegen und die Strassen dahinter sollte man gefühltermassen bei Dunkelheit zu Fuß besser meiden.... Die Zimmer sind Holiday Inn Express typisch, wirken aber älter als der Bau an sich, Das Parken kostet Geld, was für ein HIE eher untypsich ist. Positiv sollte man den Shuttle Service zum Harbour erwähnen.
“Ok hotel. Great location” Decent room. Lobby is nicer than the actual rooms. Service was outstanding. We loved the location as we could walk everywhere we needed to go.

“Only If You are feeling Brave” A Week there, 1st time in NYC sdo knew no better, certainly learnt from the experience. Though we had no problems, except the lock on our door was faulty and reported to the staff on the 1st day, nothing done for the week we were there, i would not recommend this place for anyone expecting anything short of a place to sleep for the night.

“Excellent service, Perfect location!” I stay at the Mag Mile Courtyard on many of my trips to Chicago. The location is absolutely perfect. Streeterville, Northwestern, the Mag Mile, the Gold Coast, and River North are all steps away from the property. On this trip, as always, the staff was exceptionally courteous. Since the hotel was sold out that weekend, it's the first time in recent memory that I didn't receive an upgrade to a suite. In any event, the room that I received was nice (clean, flat-panel TV, ergonomic desk chair, etc.). Breakfast in the restaurant was very good.
“Su Nombre Lo dice todo solo para dormir...” falto limpieza. algo de manteniminto en los cuartos nosotros ocupamos tres cuartos y todos les falto limpieza y mantenimiento

“Best NYC Hotel” My wife and I stayed here for a 4 night trip, the hotel was recommended by a friend who found the gem last year. Having stayed in NYC on a few previous occasions we were very pleased with the room, they were large by NYC standard, with a large and very comfy bed. The maid service did a great job daily. Having read the reviews on Trip Advisor we had high expectations of the hotel, I'd have to say our expectations were met. We stayed in room 2305 and what a choice, the views (yes 2 views) were amazing, the comfort was great and really cosy. We would actually disagree with other reviewers comment re. the bell boy, but that depends on who you got. One was very nice the whole time and never forgot who we were and where we came from, the other (taller gent) was a bit gruff for our liking. (I'm sorry I forgot to get the nice guys name really but he gave us more tips and just so pleasant). One of the concierges, David, was a genuinely pleasant guy who was chatty and helpful (as New Yorkers can be). So a few Tips if I may, if you need a restaurant try talking to the Bell Boy (less expensive places for dinner) and they can get you Airport Transfers cheaper than the Concierge - these services seem to be outsourced by the hotel - but as I did say David's service was excellent. All in all a truly great hotel, great location and great service - we will be back.

“Very pleasant!” This Hilton Garden Inn was very clean. The room was comfortable, and I found the staff to be friendly and helpful. The location (a short drive to Town Center shopping and restaurants) was convenient. The gym was very small, but I didn't have problems getting a machine.

“Did not want to leave!” I did not want to leave the Millenium Hilton, as I felt right at home. Though I arrived several hours before check-in I was given a room right away with an absolutely breathtaking view on the 47th floor. I booked a special weekend rate through Travelzoo for $211/night. This is easily THE BEST hotel I've stayed in while in NYC and I've stayed in several hotels in the city. The staff was extremely kind and accommodating, especially the bellmen who had kind greetings for everyone walking through the door. I especially liked the turndown service they had every evening with chocolates, fresh bottled water and a bucket of ice. The only things I did not like about the Hotel Millenium was the room service food was incredibly expensive, but not good at all (I ordered the combination appetizer platter and the food tasted like it was microwaved and not freshly cooked). The mini bar prices are also ridiculous, similar to many high end hotels in the city. Finally, I think the hotel needs to have wireless internet for all customers. This is the first Hilton I've stayed at where wireless internet was NOT available in the room (only in public spaces), nor was the internet free for Hilton Honors members, though it was a relatively reasonable price of $5.95/24 hours (I've seen much worse). Overall, I would absolutely stay at this hotel again and I was sad to leave the breathtaking view of NYC at the end of my stay.

“I guess it was okay” Hotel is old and the rooms are run down. Had asked for a refurbished room upon making the reservation but didn't receive one. Stayed on a Wednesday night, which wasn't busy, so it wouldn't have hurt them to give us a nicer room. We did have to change rooms once due to street noise, dirty sheets, and hairs in toliet. Both rooms were the same condition on 6th and 7th floors Staff was nice, especially the man at checkout. Location was the best thing the hotel had going for it. Parking at $39/24 hours was also a good deal. We didn't arrive until 9:30 pm Wednesday night, and checked out at 8:00 am Thurday but didn't leave the city until 4:00 pm and only had to pay the $39. So many hotels base their rates on the time of check-out and then pro-rate the other hours your car is parked. Probably wouldn't stay here again just because of the room conditions. Wall paper peeling, dusty, especially in the corners, ripped and dirty sheets, scuffed walls. I think the hotel could really profit if it did a renovations to their rooms. Also we did not have a flat panel TV in either room like the site states.

“Perfect!” After whining about not being able to get any real food or food service at the Downtown Amarillo Courtyard (nice hotel otherwise), we ended up here the next night. What a difference a day makes. The room service here was impeccable. Typically we find restaurant room service fare, while expensive, well less than extraordinary and the portions minuscule. Not so here. The food was divine. The service was divine. And fast! I want to live here. Absolutely everyone that we came into contact with: the concierge, Amanda at check-in (truly kind), hotel operator, and several instances of room service were extremely well-trained, poised and professional. The bathroom was literally spotless. Spotless. Whoever is running this hotel needs a gigantic raise. The only thing I'd like to see is a more varied wine list. Thanks for an awesome stay, we'll definitely be back.

“Good hotel away from the madness!” If you are looking for a value for money hotel away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square then you wouldn't go far wrong with the TriBeCa Hilton Garden Inn. Rooms were very good and having stayed in many New York hotels over the years they are above average in size (well certainly the one I stayed in was). The beds have a comfort control system which allows you to select the firmness of your mattress - a nice quirky touch! The adjoining bar/restaurant was also very good with friendly staff and a good selection of drinks to choose from. My one and only real major problem with the hotel was its elevators. They have to be the slowest elevators I have ever, and I really do mean EVER, come across. My friend and I were on the top floor (6th floor) and we literally got to the point where if we were meeting our friends (who were on the 2nd floor) at a certain time in the lobby we would leave the room 10mins early to allow for travelling time! On one occasion we decided to go down the stairs and made it down to the lobby quicker (although a little dizzier) than the people from our floor that were waiting for the elevator! Other than that though it's a very good hotel to stay in and I would certainly consider doing so again.

“Don't Stay Here if You're Handicapped” I am in a wheelchair and make all the reservations for our summer road trip. We arrived at this Days Inn to find high curbs and no ramp for wheelchairs. Then, inside the lobby the counter top is so high that it was on my eye level. I told the guy checking in guests my name and he found my reservation. He then asked MY HUSBAND for ID. I asked him if I was invisible because I was handicapped and it was my ID he needed since the reservation was in my name. He took the ID and then addresses further comments to my husband again. I told him, again, I was the person who'd reserved the room. He completed the paperwork then pushed it over the desk for me to sign but I couldn't reach up that high and there was nowhere to write, except juggle the pen and paper leaning on the vertical side of the counter. He slid the keys over to me. I asked him if they always treated handicapped people that way but he just replied 'no ma'am'. This whole incident really upset me, I've never been treated like this in any other motel and we stay in dozens every year in this country. The room was good and so was the breakfast but I will never stay here again.

“A bit run down” We aren't that picky, but this Days Inn is a bit run down. We were just looking for a place to stay before a morning flight from DFW. Even so, it leaves a lot to be desired. There was mold in the shower, and the bathroom sink drain was clogged and very slow to drain. The mattress was saggy. The TV stations went out (the channels just said "searching for satellite signal"). We did like that it had an in-room fridge and the shower was a massage-type showerhead. The outdoor corridors were noisy with people going by. Overall, this property is a bit run down but is adequate for a quick stay - if you get a good price.

“Don't miss a drink at the bar” This is a very nice hotel in a great location but the real stand outs are the service they provide the guests and the BAR. Room was available at check in. Clean and spacious. Hotel pool is nice for a city hotel outside pool - small but very quaint and staff was very friendly. Nice workout facility. And after you do all that, don't miss the fabulous hotel bar - lots of fun. We went out to dinner and decided to go for a night cap - it was the best part of our stay. Good drink selection, very nice setting and people were lots of fun - no one acting too trendy - just good drinks and lots of nice people. Very hopping place. I have to give a shout out to the valet/doormen - they were so friendly and nice and remembered us every time we passed them - always some nice comment to share with us. Our room was nice and quiet as well - quieter than most hotels.

“Hyatt Regency misses the mark” I stayed for 5 nights attending a conference at the hotel. This is a very large hotel that is relatively easy to navigate. The front desk and bell staff were very friendly, but the stay started to go down hill from there. My first room was located near the elevator and after one night of listening to the elevator grind by every minute or so I requested a new room (first time I have ever done that). The were happy to move me to a quieter room. Unfortantely this hotel has train tracks on one side and the freeway on the other so as noted it is not for light sleepers. The rooms have been updated and have nice furnshings, but they are not business friendly. The only accessable outlet is in the bathroom. If you wish to plug in a computer at the desk, you have to pull the desk out from the wall to access the plug. This could easily be solved with a power strip set up on the desk. The chair looks like a dinning room chair so it sits way to low to the desk. I am over 6 feet tall and still felt like I was at the kids table trying to work on my computer. Overall the rooms are small, partly due that the hotel has to be 25+ years old. I mentioned the great service by the lobby staff, but unfortanetly it stopped there. The bar/restaurant staff was slow and lacked basic customer service. When I ordered a bow of their organic cereal for breakfast, the water simply told me I could go make it myself on the buffet. I also purchased their business plan that provides you several upgraded ammenities including pressing a dress shirt - one for each day you are there. Unfortunately they are not willing to press 3 shirts (for a 5 night stay) all at once. They require you to call each morning and have the shirt pressed. I ended up using the iron myself. It also included wifi which was very weak all throughout the hotel. Overall this hotel has a lot of good, but also a lot of bad. Couple that with a $200+ per night price and it missed the mark.

“Great Location and Comfortable Rooms” The rooms are spacious and the bed is most comfortable. The location is ideal being right at Keystone at the Crossing and therefore convenient to most of northern Indianapolis. The hotel has an indoor pool, whirpool and sun deck which were all very nice. There is free parking if one does not choose to utilize the valet service. The staff was courteous and helpful. I got a deal on Hotwire for this room that could not be beat. There are only two reasons that I did not give the hotel five stars is that they charge for internet service in your room and more importantly the room does not have a self-contained air conditioning unit. The air conditioning unit was one of those central air deals with a supposed thermostat which allows only for minimal control of room temperature. Overall though, it was a great place to stay.

“Very nice hotel Downtown!” Stayed here mid-December for one night. The rooms are very nice. I'm not sure if we had neighbors because we never heard a peep. It was very quiet. The bed was comfortable and the shower had good pressure. We didnt have much of a view but that didnt matter much. The parking is valet as everyone says. There is a parking lot right next to the hotel but I"m not sure if it's overnight parking but it is cheaper than valet. There is a small coffee shop right across from the hotel and a small market around the corner. The roof has a nice pool and jacuzzi. I would definitely stay here again.

“Ok - aber kein Design Tempel” Wir waren 5 Tage für eine Städtetour im W New York - ingesamt ein ok Hotel, aber nicht der Design Tempel für den sich die W-Kette gerne hält. Die normalen Zimmer sind sehr klein - glücklicherweise haben wir ein Upgrade auf eine Junior-Suite bekommen die aus zwei kleinen Zimmern bestand - Schlafzimmer mit je 50cm Platz auf jeder Seite vom Bett und Wohnzimmer mit Schreibtisch und Sofa. Das Badezimmer hatte keine Badewanne sondern nur eine sehr in die Jahre gekommene Dusche. Insgesamt ok, aber alles andere als herausragend. Die Lobby war am Wochenende sehr voll dazu nervt der Fahrstuhl - wir haben teilweise 5 Minuten auf den Lift nach unten gewartet. Unser Tipp zum Frühstück - das Cafe Metro (2 Blocks nach rechts) - super NY-Style Fast-Food Frühstück zum fairen Preis.

“Below average” The hotel lobby is beautiful and up to date. Staff and breakfast buffet were wonderful. Room was VERY HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT. Dingy and dated. If they remodel the rooms the hotel would be considered decent. Another disappointment is the balcony rooms! They aren't private. Two balconies are connected for 2 rooms. You can see the harbor from the balcony bay view room however, you still are overlooking an ugly parking lot.

“Worst Days Inn Experience Ever” First off, the driveway going in and out of the hotel is only big enough for one car, good luck getting thru if someone parks under the portico. Then upon walking in the lobby (which smelled like dirty socks) I found the manager yelling and being extremely rude at a guest asking about a phone number, this went on for about 5 mins with me standing there. The manager has a real attitude problem and provoked me into yelling also during my check-in, BEWARE of the hidden safe fee that is added to your rate and make sure you check it before signing anything. The manager tried to hide my rate by folding the paper in half so I couldn't see it, then upon asking him why my rate was wrong and where is the disclosure of the safe fee, he then became abrupt with me and very rude also, though he was real proud of the contl breakfast in the morning, he kept repeating it like I am suppose to be impressed (NOT). btw, the breakfast was a joke anyways, you'll get a real breakfast down at the Taco Cabana or MacDonalds. Also, the exterior was falling apart and needs a real paint job. Needless to say, I will not be staying here again.

“Nice Location, So-So Service” This hotel is in a great location and you pay for it. It is between Central Park and Times Square. The room was "okay" but nothing special as the attached photos will show. The breakfast was disappointing and expensive. Find a nearby restaurant for better value. There was a verrrryyyy long wait for the elevators. I was attending a conference at the hotel. At the end of one of the days I returned to the room at 4:00pm to find the room not made up. I called the front desk and was assured it would be taken care of immediately. I left to find a place to read for an hour and when I returned at 5:00pm the room was still not cleaned. I called the front desk and was told it was not cleaned because the "shift was changing." The hotel management should remind staff that the customer doesn't know or care that "the shift is changing." For the high price paid a clean room should be provided when a guest returns to it and especially when a guest is inconvenienced. On the night of 11/5 there was a fire on the 4th floor of the hotel. A loudspeaker told guests to stay in their rooms. Well, after 9/11, not too many people were ready to stay in their rooms knowing a fire was on a floor below them. The hotel staff did little to deal with the situation that I could see. There is nothing special about this property except the location. If you are willing and able to pay for that, this hotel will meet your needs but nothing more.

“Buon albergo in ottima” Abbiamo amato il nostro soggiorno a Dallas presso il Stoneleigh scorso anno che siamo tornati questo anno. Si tratta di un bellissimo hotel in una posizione eccellente (a pochi passi ristoranti, un parco auto e negozi ... a breve altri luoghi piacevoli.) Abbiamo goduto il nostro soggiorno la seconda volta, così tanto che abbiamo deciso di prolungare il soggiorno di un'altra notte . Quando sono andato alla reception estendere il soggiorno, mi sono imbattuto in alcuni frustrazione b / c abbiamo prenotato la stanza ad un prezzo scontato tramite Expedia. Il manager junior non ha voluto prolungare il nostro soggiorno con la stessa velocità che avevamo prenotato a ... anche se l'albergo non era pieno come è stato un Martedì. Abbiamo finito per non alloggiati. In seguito, ho inviato una lettera al direttore generale che poi mi ha mandato un certificato per una notte gratuita e prima colazione. Ha capito quello che il manager reception quel giorno non ha fatto. Questo è stato il servizio clienti fantastico e mi ha mostrato che questo hotel vuole davvero mantenere i propri clienti. Sono assolutamente lo consiglio.

“Perfect Location & Hotel” Stayed at the Baldwin Oct. 12 - 14, 2007. First time there. The person at the front desk was very helpful throughout our stay. Checking in was flawless, the room was average size for classic San Francisco hotels. Our 10th floor room had 2 walls of windows that opened and we were high enough to see the city. The location puts you 45 seconds from the gates of China town. You are next door to a Starbucks and across the street from a upscale wine lounge. No noise at night other than a fire truck. We took BART to get to the hotel and from the Montgomery Station you are only 3-4 blocks away. Easy enough to roll the suitcases to the hotel. Will stay here again.

“It was Ok, no real issues” Easy to find, parking wasn't an issue and received a first floor (2nd in US speak) room at the end of the balcony. Locks worked, shower pressure good and room clean. I was a bit tired after the days drive and rocking at Huey Lewis at the Majestic so I slept very well. Check in was helpful and friendly, the site has security overnight if you need to know. They allowed the car to stay in the car park while I went out to see San Antonio's sights as the hotel was quiet, although I wouldn't expect this when busy. The Alamo is about 10 minutes away by foot and I didn't have any issues walking back from the bars at midnight. Its a bit dated but it was a one nighter and certainly value for money considering the location. Breakfast was typical Daybreak affair, I went for steak and eggs at the Denny's two blocks away which was really good. Reception will give you a map and to get to Houston Street follow the smell of manure from the horse drawn carriages at the wall of the Alamo. One last thing and a highligh of San Antonio for me, if you are a blues fan, is in the Sheraton Gunter Hotel. Rooms 414 and 415, the site of Robert Johnson's Recordings - legendary. Oh and Ozzy's site of indiscretion at the cenotaph

“A fabulous historical hotel in a great location!” When reading the previous reviews, I became a little nervous that - although we had booked the hotel through Priceline for an incredible rate - it might not live up to the hype. I'm not sure where the other travelers were staying, or if they're used to the Ritz, but this was a great hotel! Check-in was simple and easy. Our room was lovely - comfortable bed, updated bathroom, nice, large closet. The location was also just perfect: a quick walk to Independence Hall, and other local hotspots. Not to mention, we took a bus to the Cherry Blossom Fest - which picked up just a block away! I loved the hotel. Found it quiet, clean, and - for the price - one of the best we've visited.

“We Were Happy with Our Stay” This hotel has lots of less-than-optimal reviews. We stayed for one evening and found it to be comfortable - and perfect for what we needed - a place to stay in order to catch a 7 a.m. flight. Check in was smooth and efficient. The room was nice, good bed, desk area, two comfortable chairs, and great beds. Bathroom was adequate, with tremendous water pressure! Other reviewers have commented on inability to control temperature in room. We were able to adjust ours. Room had small coffee maker, which was nice. Room was clean and comfortable. We had dinner in the hotel restaurant (sorry I can't remember the name - started with an A) and it was not very expensive and good. Overall, a good stay and I would recommend to anyone needing to stay close to the airport.

“Elegant.” This is a small intimate boutique on the hotel on the River walk. Rooms were very spacious and well appointed. Bathrooms high end. Very quiet hotel with good gym. I do not think the hotel would be worth it unless you are able to secure the river walk view with balcony.

“Great location, needs some sprucing up” Location was great, staff was helpful and friendly, and as always, the cookie was great. The room was clean and spacious (14th floor in the corner) but there was a large area (about 3 feet square) of the ceiling, right over the window (and the AC/Heating unit) that clearly had water damage, was sort of repaired but looked like it was ready to let loose at any time. The walls had lots of big dings. It had poured rain and my clothes had gotten soaked - I tried to turn the heat on to get my jacket dry, and it didn't work. I called the front desk, and they had an engineer there quickly, but he said he'd have to replace a part, and since it was 11:30 pm, I told him not to do it. So, I turned the blower on, and the next morning I was very stuffed up. When I got a good look at the unit in the light, there was lots of black mold/mildew in and around the grate and the unit itself. I do not have a problem with allergies, and because by the end of the day I felt much better, my headache and stuffiness had to have been caused by the cruddy air. Hopefully this was all related to the water damage I saw on the ceiling and not a widespead problem in other rooms. Just a warning to anyone who has a problem with allergies, or just a healthy aversion to blowing mold spores all over, check the AC/heating unit before you unpack!

“a great bargain!” I don't usually stay in this kind of hotels and prefer "lower class", more affordable hotels, but I found an unbeatable offer on Expedia which allowed me to overnight here aexceptional price. I found the hotel to be great: it is located in a very beatutiful area, near the subway and well connected to the bus system. It is near Rittenhouse square, one of the nicest places in Philly, and surrounded by good restaurants and shops. Our room was very big, with flat tv, wi-fi connection, and even a massaging mattress! The bathroom was spacious and they provide good-quality toiletries. Everything was pretty clean. on the downsid, breakfast was nit included. The staff at reception was very kind and helpful, they provided us a map of the city and pointed out the highlights for us. Of course I'd never stay here paying the full price for it :-), but if you find a good offer, do not think twice and book your stay in Philadelphia at the Radisson!

“A great stay” My husband and I stayed here while he was on business. The service was wonderful and the rooms were quite clean and updated. The bed is amazing and I hardly wanted to get out of it. The location is very near Greektown with several tasty restaurants - Pegasus and we highly recommend a trip to the Pan Hellenic Bakery. I walked from the hotel all over the city, straight down Madison. It might be a bit of a walk for some, but the walk to Millennium Park is about 15-20 minutes. Despite the front desk staff who told us it would be too long of a walk, we walked to Little Italy but after a huge dinner, we took a taxi back. The area seemed very safe and staying at the Crowne Plaza Metro is a good opportunity to check out some of the neighborhoods.

“Nice but parking problems” We were there midweek, so we thought there might not be the problems with parking that we had heard about. Not only did we have to pay $13 to park overnight, there were no spaces left when we returned after eating dinner at the mercado. We had to park on an adjacent unpaved lot. We were worried about security and wishing we had parked in the cheaper public lot at the end of the block. The room was very nice. The bed was comfortable and the room was attractively decorated. There was a fridge. The bathroom was small but adequate. We were disappointed that breakfast was not included. The staff was extremely friendly and welcoming. The location is close to the action without being in a noisy spot. If you get a good enough price to offset the parking charge and lack of breakfast, this is a good place to stay.

“A great resort with all the facilities.” All one would expect from a full service Marriott resort. Great staff and usual Marriott hospitality from valet parking to check out and everything in between. Highly recommended and I would be back in a heartbeat!!

“Liked the W a lot” Stayed here at an Amex Platinum Fine Resorts rate of $279 and was upgraded to a one -bedroom suite with a great view. - Room was modern, functional, clean and comfortable. Fruit tray, welcoming card, excellent cookies and complimentary water upon arrival. -The corridors are a bit dark an unappealing but the room shined. - You're right in the heart of Times Square so it's noisy but isn't that what you signed up for? - I needed toothpaste and rather than have to buy it at triple the retail price, I simply asked the registration desk and was given a tube free of charge. Sometimes it's the little things. - I like the ultra sheik lobby (7th floor) with the nice bar scene and trendy feel to it. Dark but well appointed and plenty of available, friendly staff. - Elevator banks to room floors are a little bit clunky - multiple sets of three lifts in two separate corridors that play out back-to-back. This can get a little congested. No big deal to me. - Hotel restaurants is large and you may be seated upstairs, which is beautiful but the stairs can be a chore for those not up to the task. Menu is heavy seafood. Food was good+. Service was average. - I don't care to stay in Times Square when I'm in NYC but if I do, the W will get the call again.

“Great location - excellent room” August 2011 - business stay for a week. Perfect location on Michigan Avenue. Room was outstanding since I had a view of Lake Michigan and South Michigan Ave from the 26th floor. Indoor pool was excellent as well as access to Lakeshore Drive / Navy Pier to run every daily. Very impressed.

“Great stay” Was a little worried given some of the reviews, but really had a great stay at this hotel. The room was great, it was very quiet in my room, and no problems at all were encountered during the stay. Because it was raining, they loaned me an umbrella at the front desk. Superb location for all that I needed to do on my business trip. There is a deli across the street which was great for quick meals. I ordered Domino's Pizza for some of my dinners and it was delivered to the hotel and to the room (the concierge made the delivery person call up before delivery, good for security thanks!) All in all, extremely pleased with the hotel and I will DEFINITELY return. Good job, thanks! (I was on floor 39 by the way.)

“For a Motel 6....it's solid.” No frills here but very clean room, good bed and lots of room space. I had no problem with the area al all just a little far from where I was spending most of my time. Nice people at the front desk. Clean public area and lots of very good parking. I will stay again.

“still hip but service declined” I was here a few years ago and loved it. Since then the lobby and pool area have been updated. Pros: The rooms, staff and clientele are still hip, and that counts for a lot in Phoenix. Pool area is very nice. Adjoining Mexican restaurant and bar are excellent - really fresh, tasty food. Nice amenities and free samples. Cons: Condition of rooms has declined a little. Service declined, also. Though we had arranged for a late check-out, we were awoken at 11 a.m. by the phone and asked to clear our room. (After talking, they re-agreed to the late check-out.) No bathtub plug, and when we requested one they never did find one despite a follow-up call. The jacuzzi was being serviced Saturday when we arrived. We had counted on using this to recover from the flight before a performance - couldn't they clean the jacuzzi on a Tuesday morning or some other low-use time? I would still stay here since I felt comfortable being with unconventional colleagues; the environment in Phoenix can be a little scary.

“Feel right at home at the Affinia Manhattan” This is our second stay in this well-located hotel, right across from Penn Station and Madison Square Gardens. We love the home-like feel, the convenience of the kitchen, and the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff. The beds are so perfectly comfortable and the room is so spacious! This place is a great value! The only downside is that the window treatments are a bit dirty and need cleaning. Likewise the carpet could use a shampoo. But overall, a fabulous and happy stay!

“Romantic Bit of Old San Francisco--With Great Breakfast Buffet” We stayed here two nights and really enjoyed it. The hotel is in a very safe, charming location, the staff was wonderful, the room very comfortable and clean. And the breakfast buffet was excellent--as was the evening reception. Petite Auberge is very "country French," and you get that feeling of cozy fellowship you might find in an old New England ski lodge. The old (1920s?) elevator was really neat; if you have kids, tell them to watch through the small window in the elevator door as the car rises to your floor, to see the ursine stowaway attached to the elevator cable. Our deluxe room was spacious and renovated but kept in the Victorian style. The TV got a lot of channels via cable. (Note: It sits on a sliding platter that pulls out of the armoire.) The gas fireplace in particular was wonderful; it was almost as lively and convincing as a wood-burning one. I was glad to see that in addition to curtains, there were actual shades on the windows. To my surprise, it was not at all noisy at night; one great thing about San Francisco is that people hardly ever honk their car horns. (I did wear earplugs as a preventive measure. The inn provides them if you ask.) The shower water pressure was incredible! I also give them points for putting a recycling bin in the room next to the trash bin. And they have free wi-fi in the lobby! (Plus a computer you can use next door at the White Swan). With historic inns, you're trading absolute consistency and modernity for charm and personality. You have to accept that going in. In the case of Petite Auberge, we could hear the footsteps of the people above us very clearly. But this is to be expected in a building from the 19th Century. There was a tiny bit of wallpaper starting to peel in the otherwise very inviting bathroom. (Wallpaper in a steamy environment never works; someone should get the word out to hotel owners.) One of the window shades was stuck, but they sent the service guy to fix it quickly while we were out. The heat is controlled centrally, so you can't adjust it in your room. But the gas fireplace puts out a lot of heat, and you can open a window or ditch the comforter if you're too warm. We found the temperature comfortable. There is not always someone at the front desk, but the staff were exceptionally helpful, with a genuinely cheerful attitude that is so often missing at big hotels. (You can also call 0 at any time to get someone at the White Swan.) The free breakfast was really sumptuous: several types of pastry, fruit, quiche, cereal, great sausage links, a couple of kinds of juice. They also have a fridge full of drinks for guests to help themselves to. The evening reception has a couple of wines and some nice hors d'oeuvres (cheeses one night, bread pudding the next). It's a good chance to chat with other guests. Before our trip, I had worried that we would find aggressive panhandlers everywhere in San Francisco; however, there were almost none where we went. Nob Hill is very safe, even at night. If you like historic inns, you've absolutely love Petite Auberge.

“Nice Hotel Near Convention Center” Stayed here for a convention and have no complaints. One of the better business hotels I've stayed at and would highly recommend the Omni if you are going to the Convention Center. The bay view room had a balcony that extended out a foot or so. The room was clean, had good linens, comfortable bed, nice size modern bathrooms, and turn down service. Food ordered to the room was delivered when promised and was nicely done. The louvers between the bathroom and bedroom could be annoying for sharing the room because the bathroom light filtered into the bedroom. I didn't have a problem with it --just seemed like poor design and a bit of a dust collector. You do hear an occasional freight train go by-- the tracks are very close. The room with the bay views will probably give you the most train noise, but the views made up for the noise. I've stayed at the Marriott which is also very close to the Convention Center, but I prefer the Omni.

“As always Kimpton Hotels are Great” I have stayed at the Palomar in LA and just like that one the DC property is great. I stayed in a King Executive Suite and everything was great. The internet is free for Kimpton InTouch members. Parking is $38 a night but that is normal in DC. The room has everything a business person needs, large desk, sitting chair, couch, mini bar, and large closet. The reason I didn't give this an excellent rating was the valet. The guys were not very good. When I first arrived they just stood there and did not help me out of the car or get my bags. Then a day later they lost the tag for my keys so they had no idea who my car belonged to. I expect a lot more from the valet at a nice hotel. Other than that the stay was great and I will be back.

“Classy, Modern Hotel on the Upper East Side” I recently stayed at the Bentley Hotel while on business at the nearby hospitals. The hotel location is close to Cornell, Memorial Sloan Kettering, and HSS. It's a quick walk to the bus and taxis are abundant. (About a $25 taxi from La Guardia) The hotel has very modern decor. I had a corner room on the 18th floor with great views of the East river and a comfortable king bed. The room and bathroom were clean with only sparse signs of wear and tear. Internet is $10. Compared to other NYC hotels, this was incredibly affordable and still very nice. The room was quiet. I would definitely stay here again, especially with how inexpensive and nice it was. They held my bags for the entire day after I checked out early in the morning without any problems or charges. The front desk staff was very nice. No complaints here!

“Big rooms and great staff” Thank you to the hotel team at the Seattle Homewood Suites. I stayed for 5 nights and had a great stay. the meals were very large (and for free) I love that where i didnt have to spend anymore money going to breakfast or dinner so i saved a ton of money!

“Great Hotel” I stayed here one night on business. I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel appears fairly new. It is located in an undeveloped business park next to a Hilton Garden Inn; there is absolutely nothing within walking distance. The Hilton Garden Inn has a full service restaurant, however. The staff was friendly and the rooms very modern. I liked the walkin shower with one of the best showerheads I have seen in a long time. The internet is free and is cable. Flat screen TV. Bed was very comfortable with great pillow variation. IT is located near the airport and I started to hear planes land about 3 AM. Breakfast was just average or below.

“Excellent hotel” Martin's Travel Rule No 1 (well one of them, anyway) is never ever stay in a Holiday Inn Express. New addition to rule No1 - except this one. It's pretty good. Clean, modern and my free upgrade room with whirlpool bath was large by NYC standards and very comfortable. Maybe a little off the beaten path for tourists but Chelsea is charming and all the sights are an easy walk. It worked equally well for me as a business hotel with a workdesk, free wi-fi in the room and a decent enough business centre for a budget hotel. Reception was extremely welcoming, fast and efficient as were all the staff. I will definitely stay here again especially as it's just 10 m inutes from the office.

“Excellent service, huge rooms” I travel a lot on business, so I'm fairly discriminating when it comes to hotels. This hotel exceeds in the following areas: 1) staff efficiency and friendliness 2) cleanliness of rooms 3) size of rooms 4) comfort of mattress 5) thick, plentiful towels I'd like to add that I inadvertently left two very important items in my room upon checkout. I called the hotel the next day, was put in touch with housekeeping, and was informed within 24 hours that my items were found. As I requested, the hotel shipped the items to me in a very timely fashion, and they notified me that the package was en route. This is outstanding service by any hotel's standards. I'm quite impressed with the management of this hotel and would stay there again.

“Just the BEST !!!” What a wonderful place ! We had checked in and out of another hotel due to construction noise and had called them and arrived less than half an hour later. We were on the 9 th floor and arrived Tuesday October 17 and left Saturday October 21and they coudn't be more helpful including a free late checkout until 2pm due to late flight. Great big rooms looked out on the street, no other guest noise, comfortable beds and a cute kitchenette as well. Fantastic location just walked to the theatres and this is right in the district with thousands of restaurants too ! From an Aussie girl who was 16 last time she went 27 years ago I LOVED IT. I felt like I was in a very classy but welcoming place with friendly doormen and great staff on the desk . Thank you for having room at 15 mins. notice ! We'll be back !

“Immaculate - Friendly and Helpful Staff” Earlier this summer, I wanted to book an overnight local getaway because there was work being done on my house in Phoenix. I found a great price at this location and booked it. Having checked prior Tripadvisor reviews, I was aware of the possibility of highway noise. So, I asked for a room facing away from the highway and that made all the difference! The room was immaculate and very comfortable! At this location, the rooms really do look like the photos on the Website. (That isn't always the case.) The bed was so comfortable that I didn't want to leave. Actually, I was quite content to hang out in the room to finish up a work assignment. Breakfast was, as another reviewer had commented, healthy - with a varied selection. I gather, from the location - near a suburban North Phoenix office park, that this hotel caters mostly to a business clientele. I was there on a weekend and it was moderately busy. All the staff were most friendly and helpful - providing the feeling of a smaller boutique hotel. This is a terrific place to stay. (Just remember to book a room facing away from the highway.) You won't regret your decision!

“Worst Room I Have Ever Stayed In!” Where did the Hudson get those 3 1/2 Stars? We booked our room through PriceLine, which guarantees the room will accomidate 2 adults. When we reminded the desk clerk of this guarantee she immediately trided to extract extra money from us which seems to be a common practice of this hotel. The room is 9' 6" X 9' 6" with the AC and small window located behind the headboard? The closet is an indentation of the hall which will hold one 21" suitcase on the luggage rack and the other you can put under the rack, on the floor and stand on your head to dress. The bathroom door is 19" wide. There is 12" in front of the toilet, which means you must step over the toilet to get in the shower which is normal size. The sink sits on a stainless frame with a very sharp corner that hange over the edge of the toilet. I will next be contacting PriceLine about the rating of this hotel as well as their guarantee of the room acccomidation. In my 50 years of visiting New York City this is the worst room I have ever seen. P.S. we are both small in size!

“Nice hotel, bit expensive for food, so ate out, nice pool and walk track!” Booked this on Hotwire hoping ot get Hilton but didn't. Still good hotel and great price £60 per night. Food on high side, so ate on Boston, no worries there though. Next day stay ensured all our luggage went to Hilton so well done to all.

“Smack downtown” Big spacious room, but no free wifi when it is available everywhere, even in the park! Disappointed! Extremely good location. McD breakfast, round the corner, is excellent! Walking distance to the Cloud gate aka ' Beam', Willis Tower for the sky bridge

“Very happy with the choice” Stayed here on Sunday night and this was the highlight stop of our five day ca tour. The room was great, the vibe fun and the atmosphere wonderful. The check in was fast, friendly. The pool area is a must see and a great place to grab a drink and relax. We saw a scene being filmed Monday morning. Very modern upgrade to an old historic hotel. We enjoyed our stay and wish we could have stayed another night.

“Treat yourself to an A+ boutique hotel experience in Denver” Twelve foot high ceilings, lounge chairs upholstered in crocodile textured white leather, a jetted tub for 2, sumptuous animal print bathrobes, and a glass bowl atop the desk inhabited by a live goldfish were just a few of the surprises encountered when we opened the door to our room at the Hotel Monaco Denver. My husband accurately calls the decor “quirky without being kitschy”. At the very least, one can tell immediately that they are in a room that was not designed to be duplicated by the thousands. We were at the Hotel Monaco Denver. While unique, the hotel seems as corporately professional as any of its bigger competitors. The service levels are sky-high and from my vantage point the place pretty much hums like a well-oiled machine. It is hard to find nicked furniture, chipped paint or a loose thread anywhere. But the boutique atmosphere also comes through. This weekend (Halloween) the staff had a pumpkin-carving contest and guests were judging the entries. The hotel hosts a nightly happy hour in its colorful and comfortable lobby. Tonight they were playing “Young Frankenstein” as guests sipped wine and nibbled on hors d'oeuvres – priceless!! Centrally located just a block from 16th Street, anything in downtown or stylish LoDo is within easy reach. Valet parking is $29/day. Members of Kimpton’s loyalty program are offered unlimited free wifi access, which seems a super deal since membership is free. The Italian restaurant on the ground floor, Panzano, gets great reviews. I’ve only had the room service and that was excellent. All my raving makes me sound like I work for the hotel (I don’t). My only gripe? Because the guestroom was so big, I would need binoculars to watch TV from bed. Since I don’t, that’s not really a problem for me. There’s no question, we have a new favorite hotel in Denver!

“Great boutique hotel with a wonderful staff” The major pluses: + Location is excellent, between the 6th and 7th avenues, very close to Times Square, a few minutes walk from the MoMA, Rockefeller Center, Bryant Park etc. + Very, very stylish boutique hotel with a lounge bar atmosphere, reminiscent of the Buddha bar and similar places. The lobby and bar area, with the fire place etc are really beautiful. The facade and hotel entrance is quite impressive too, especially at night when illuminated. + The king bed rooms are very nice and OK in size for NYC, at least those with a front view. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived and we were upgraded to the suite on the upper floor - which is fantastic (too bad we could only get it for the first night - we were ready to pay almost any surcharge to keep it). + Rooms are well equipped, with iPod docking station, large flat screen TV, light dimmers, safe, etc. + They have very, very nice and spacious showers. + They have a good, complimentary breakfast buffet and happy hour at the bar from 5 to 7pm. + And last but not least the staff is one of THE BEST I have had in any hotel. Extremely nice, friendly and helpful. Some do speak French. They were kind enough to lend me a laptop to do my online checkin for my next flight, and they printed the boarding passes for me at the reception. ... and a few minuses... - Some rooms are really not so nice! We had originally booked a room with two queen beds, which was very small, was located in an annex and didn't have a true window - only a small translucent opening allowing dim daylight to enter the room - very depressing. Luckily the helpful staff was able to move us to a king bed room with a street view, which really saved our stay! We thank them again. - The bathrooms open directly to the bedroom and can only be isolated by a curtain. You may like it or not... - Some details: I couldn't find the bathrobes avertised on the web site, nor slippers, nor complimentary water in the room. And only the suite had a coffee machine, and even there it wasn't a real espresso machine. And the housekeeping staff seemed particularly parsimonious with the resupply of small amenities like soap and shampoo... But provided you get the right room this is a really great place to stay - the "boutique hotel" concept at its best!

“recommend this hotel” We stayed one night in Feb 2009 and would stay there again. Good, clean hotel. Yes, it is right off the freeway but the noise didn't bother us. The windows are doubled so this blocks alot of the noise on the freeway side of the hotel, which is where our room was. The complimentary airport shuttle was great! The location of the hotel is a bit tricky. The parking is very tight, but most hotels are in San Diego. Atleast it was free. The breakfast was good. Offered breads, cereal, fruit, hard boiled egg, make your own waffle, juice, coffee. They have a convenience store in the lobby. A very nice patio to watch the airplanes come and go at the airport. Highly recommend staying at this Comfort Inn

“Tolles Personal, gute Idee, ein bisschen in die Jahre gekommen” Das Argonaut ist hinsichtlich der Idee und Umsetzung prima. Ein extrem maritim gestaltetes Hotel, blau-weisse Zimmer, ein freundlicher Mitarbeiter der uns schon während der Anfahrt zurief, das ist alles sehr beeindruckend. Das Hotel liegt an den Piers, am Rand von Fisherman's Wharf, einem sehr lebhaften Viertel mit vielen Restaurants. Ums Eck ist sofort eine Cable-Car Haltestelle, ein paar Meter den Berg hoch ist schon die berühmte Lombard Street, die sich serpentinenförmig herabschlängelt. Unser Bay-View Zimmer hat direkt auf Alkatraz geblickt, der Aufpreis für ein Zimmer mit Ausblick liefert wirklich eine spektakuläre Sicht. Das Essen im Restaurant ist zu empfehlen und es ist auch sehr angenehm abends in der Lobby vor dem Kamin zu sitzen. Leider ist - zumindest unser Zimmer - schon ein bisschen in die Jahre gekommen. Die Fugen im Badezimmer sind schon angedunkelt, die Handtücher mit deutlichen Verbrauchsspuren und die Bademäntel fuseln. Von den Pantoffeln, die im Schrank hingen war ein Paar eingeschweisst, das andere nicht. Auch werden Shampoo, Body Lotion, etc in kleinen Einmalverpackungen angeboten, die aber offensichtlich nachgefüllt werden. Mit kleinen Mängeln war es immer noch sehr gut.

“A sophisticated hotel with some rough edges” This is a lovely hotel with beautiful grounds and, on the surface, a very sophisticated place. The reality, however, can be disappointingly less. Starting with the staff: since the grounds of the hotel are especially pretty we asked the registration desk clerk for a room with a nice view and she assured us that the one she had for us had a great view. When we got to the room we found that it overlooked the hotel laundry, a road and a fence (some people must have curious taste when it comes to views). When we complained to a different desk clerk, he took matters into his own hands and upgraded us to a lovely suite overlooking the Paradise pool. Similarly, the waiter who served us our first breakfast was especially accommodating, going over to the (more expensive) cafe to get us some food that was not presently available in the restaurant. The next morning our different waiter was so clueless and useless (how hard is it to bring over coffee and toast?) that we decided to eat outside the hotel after that (try the adjoining golf club restaurant -- it's much better and cheaper). Finally, there were several conventions in the hotel and it was very noisy and very crowded in the public spaces, which clashed with the natural beauty of the hotel and its grounds. Bottom line is if you're lucky and get the right people to attend to your needs, and if the hotel is not so crowded, you're very likely to enjoy your stay. If not, in view of the cost of staying at this luxury hotel, you're not so likely to be pleased.

“Spotty service” This hotel is conveniently located for the convention center and the National Portrait Gallery and close to other museums on the Mall. It's hard to say much about the "value" of DC hotels because each hotel's prices range all over the place, depending on the level of convention business (and special events like cherry blossom time). If your schedule is flexible and you want good prices, look for times when there is no business going on such as around July 4th and other holidays. Since this trip was business paid by someone else (who made the booking) I don't even know what the price was. However, I do know that the hotel was pretty disorganized. The room booked for me was supposed to include breakfast but when I checked in they said it didn't. There were about ten of us in the group, so I contacted the organizer the next morning who spent a considerable amount of time trying to get the situation corrected before the others were denied breakfast - with no success. They did provide us with breakfast coupons for the next morning, but frankly after I ate the breakfast I wished I hadn't - it just didn't taste very good and the fried potatoes left a bad taste in the mouth, like the fat had been sitting around a while.. I used to like Courtyards - they used to have a moderately priced breakfast buffet of cold items with optional hot items cooked to order. Maybe other Courtyards do but this was disappointing. The hotel has an indoor pool, although it is so small as to be a joke as far as I am concerned. You couldn't use it for exercise. The gym was split between two rooms, one with four treadmills and two elliptical trainers, the other with a weight machine and a set of weights. Half of the weight machine was non-functional because of a broken line, and had probably been that way a while. The first morning I was there, the elevator wouldn't respond to the call buttons on the main floor. When an elevator arrived (by virtue of someone having used it to come down to the floor) a hotel employee got off. I mentioned the problem to the employee and he totally ignored me, walking right by and going over to the desk. I went to the desk and mentioned it again and he took my room key card from my hand - although I protested that the card was not the problem, and disappeared. The desk clerk said that he had gone to find the engineer. When the elevators started working again, I had to wait around for the guy to come back with my key. I wouldn't stay at this hotel again by choice.

“Be Careful When Booking this Hotel!” I stayed at the Marriott SF on April 5, and the first minute I arrived, the problems started. First the entrance to the hotel is NOT the hotel address. It's about 4 blocks via one way streets. I missed a turn and spent 10 minutes getting back to the entrance. The parking was an astronomic $45 a day! I am a Marriott rewards member, so I was confident I would get a nice room on a high floor. When I walked in to my 35th floor room, I found that I had a great view of the air conditioner units. I immediately called the front desk, and was politely told I could have a 4th floor room instead. When I complained to the manager, she gave me a 14th floor room, overlooking piles of garbage on the roof of the hotel's other wing. It was terrible! The room itself was OK, especially the bathroom, but the high speed internet costs another $13 a day. This hotel is dedicated to taking your money as efficently as possible. In conclusion, I would not rate this hotel as a 4 star, and I give the management a resounding "F" as in extremely poor. I will not stay at this Marriott again.

“What a great property” We stayed 2 nights and would definitely stay again. The hotel is clean, spacious, has great amenities (nice pool, relatively big and well equipped gym for a hotel, biz center/cafe) and the decor is modern and rich. The staff were courteous and attentive, without trying too hard; and reminded me of what professional customer service should look like. The bar area has a huge and beautiful lounge with friendly happy hour prices and it felt like such a waste with just a handful of people enjoying it. But then again, we visited on a quiet (no convention) weekend when August temperatures were 103+. It was as if we were in a ghost town (just a beautiful one lined with palm trees). Hardly a soul in sight and it felt like we pretty much had the restaurant (and generally that part of downtown) to ourselves. There is a large AMC theater across the street and we were able to catch a late night movie. There was also a city shuttle offering free rides so we got to enjoy a mini tour of downtown. Great experience.

“Is it hot in here?” This was my first experience staying at a Kimpton branded hotel. I had contacted the hotel a few weeks earlier letting them know I had pet allergies and they assured me that they had pet-free floors and would make sure I would be pre-assigned one of those rooms. Upon check-in, I was placed in a wonderful room on one of the highest floors overlooking Park Ave. The room itself was small, but no more so than typical New York standards. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room itself was exceptionally clean. There were two issues that I had with the property, one being the size of the bathroom which is exceptionally small. I’m around 6’2 and couldn’t sit on the toilet without my knees touching the wall in front of me. The second issue was the air conditioning. My stay was during early November which is traditionally when New York starts to cool dramatically. I happened to be there during a warm spell that put temperatures around 70 degrees. When I arrived, I noticed that the room was pretty warm, I adjusted the thermostat but found no change in the climate. There was a card stating to call down if you are having problems with the air, so I did and they sent up an engineer to look at the problem. When the engineer arrived, he told me that they actually turn off the air conditioning during the fall/winter and only have heat available. He said the best solution was to sleep with the window open to regulate the temperature. I spent five nights sleeping with the window open about four blocks from Grand Central listening to Park Ave traffic. I found this to be a really unpleasant experience. I will say that the staff was great and very engaging, the daily happy hour was great, but I am docking the property two stars for tiny bathrooms and open-air sleeping in New York.

“Really very nice” I was very pleasantly surprised by the Hilton Times Square. I stayed at the Hilton becuase it was the best rate I could find at a decent hotel, but I expected an impersonal feel (big chain hotel in such a touristy spot) - I couldn't have been more wrong. My room was large, airy and comfortable and was on a higher floor with a stunning view of the Empire State Building and the Hudson. The staff was pleasant, helpful and personable. Housekeeping was great (it may have been because I left tips, but they kept leaving extra toiletries and chocolates).

“Another Great Sofitel” I stayed at the Sofitel in DC for 3 nights, at an exceptional rate of $179 / night. The standard room was quite large, well appointed, and had a wonderfully comfortable bed. Valet parking was $40 / day. Internet $10 / day. The bathroom had both a shower and a bathtub, and L'Occitane amenities. The staff was very polite, and very helpful.
