The location is great for sightseeing, as it's only 1 block from the White House. Overall, after having stayed at several Sofitel properties around the world, I have to comment that this chain is doing a consistently good job, especially in their US properties. Great value for money!

“GREEDY HOTEL STEALS YOUR MONEY” I booked this hotel a few months ago as a place to stay for national train day. However things came up and i decided to go with another hotel. I been trying to cancell for a couple months by email but got no reponse. when i called to cancell they HUNG UP ON ME!!! by the time i decided to call i had sense lost the email that had the reservation number on it. i had it when i was emailing them a dozen times. SO when i called i said " I made a reservation online a couple months ago,I need to cancel but i lost the number" there was no response on the other end they had hung up on me.they could have asked for my last name last 4 digits of my SS number and last 4 numbers of the card used to confirm who i am but they chose to hang up. I never called back cause why i should i keep calling a place that hangs up when you call. they don't respond to emails and you can't cancel online that should have been a red flag to me. I will dispute this charge.

“Sketchy neighborhood, average hotel” The Courtyard at the U.S. Capitol does not have a lot of curb appeal. To get to the front desk on the second floor, one must first get past the security guards at the desk on the first floor. Luckily, I noticed that they don't look up when you come in - very reassuring given the sketchiness of the neighborhood. The rooms are average, nothing particularly special here - though mine did have a nice view of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives building across the street. The exercise room is a very tiny space next to the 5' x 15' "pool". It has 2 treadmills, a stairmaster, and a rack of dumbbells. If you use the dumbbells, be sure to place them down very delicately. While I was working out, another guest accidentally dropped one from a few inches above the floor. Within minutes, a staff member from the floor below came up to chastise us both for making too much noise. We were both shocked. In general, I was disappointed. I won't be staying here again.

“Great location but do not becomes what pretends to be” + Location was fantastic, from my point of view in the best area of the city. + Really Comfortable Beds! Would prefer shower had glass enclosure, rather than curtain and small closet (in winter will be really scarce of capacity) -Poor attention as expected based on great attention by e-mail. Because it was a special occasion for us. -Not as clean as modern looking as I expected based on the pictures. Poor value for money. Do not becomes what pretends to be. (low level of finishes, furniture and facilities) -The restaurant in the hotel, "Primehouse" too expensive and bad service (big basic mistakes) . Do not becomes what pretends to be. Would recommend this to consider it.

“Very nice hotel in a prime location.” Nice, soft contemporary look. Comfortable beds, cool decor, quite rooms. Pretty simple and good experience. Service was excellent. Didn't eat at the restaurant but there appears to be a decent bar scene in the bar off of the lobby. They are per friendly. I wish I would have known that and I would have brought my dog. Would definitely stay there again.

“A business hotel, but not for kids or family vacation.” The hotel is exceptionally clean in all areas, and i compliment it on that. After wanting to try this property for a long while, i took my family over new years. It advertises as a 5 star property, but it is not up to the level of the Four Seasons, Ritz or Peninsula Chicago. It is essentially a 4 star Hyatt with a very nice location at the Chicago Water Tower and Michigan Ave, and an art-museum, fancy lobby. The pool area is probably one of the best in the Chicago loop area, and the food is very food in both the restaurant and room service. Outside of the these two, very expensive options for eating, you need to leave the property for family style dining. The reason i cant give this property 5 stars is because of staff service. Outside of the bellhops and valet, who were excellent, this is essentially the hotel of "no". I found that most times i asked a question or made a reasonable, simple request, the staff responded "no.". Or "no, the hotel doesn't allow that.". My wife and I sadly coined this property the "hotel of no" during our stay. For example, the hotel brags about its Butler service for every room. Well, when you ask the butler for a toothbrush or extra soap or towels, the butler says "no sir, you must call housekeeping for that.". The hotel brags about it's available car service. But when you ask to use it, the driver works less hours than an out of work school teacher. It was really quite absurd. Even try asking for a second wake up call or, better, for room service to deliver food to the pool area. Every time, consistently, we were met with "no" and then an explanation why they couldn't do it. Try bringing a glass of wine from the bar to the pool.... When my wife did, a very stern manager promptly entered the pool area and, basically, said, "no.". The rooms, while modern at some point in time, need a major rehab. We had a large suite, and the L shaped couch was torn and worn. The hyatt bed needed replacement as it was almost worn out. The bathroom and the locker rooms for the spa and pool were very nice and well stocked. Towel quality was reasonably good and soft. Overall, this is a solid 4 star business traveler hotel, less the staffing issues who probably could use some retraining. But not for a family vacation. Too bad because the pool and exercise room os very nice.

“GREAT family get away or business hotel.” I was here for a convention. The hotel is a bit away from the convention center, either a 20 minutes sweaty walk in the summer or a 6-11 dollar cab ride. That said, it is very new and quite nice. Right on the water, the views high up on the harbor side are stunning. Very easy access to walking the inner harbor, very close to Fells Point restaurants, and a Roy's and Oceanaire just outside the front door. Thick room walls and no neighbor noises, but a toilet that kicked in and ran whenever it wanted to. They have a Krups in the room and only two pods for coffee, so get extra before you go to bed. Rooms are quite large and sheets are lovely, Concierge lounge availabe, Starbucks in the lobby. Was quite busy due to convention I assume. Elevators were quite slow. Business center was temporarily closed. Staff was very kind. I will return again.

“Comfortable bed, hotel showing its age” I stayed here for two nights for a meeting in Santa Clara and I caught the free airport shuttle from the San Jose airport. The hotel is quite close to the airport. I checked-in around 5:00pm on a Friday and there was a long line of people. They were all lining up in a single queue in the Hilton HHonors carpet area. The hotel had 3 agents checking-in people and I didn't realize until later that night that they didn't give me a cookie at check-in. I was given a room on the top floor which is the executive level. The concierge lounge there provides refreshments on a little corner counter. The floor is key-protected so you have to swipe it in the elevator. The room itself is typical of an older hotel. The furnishings are fine and the bed is quite comfortable. My room was large and the bathroom had a sink and vanity area right next to it. One thing to be aware of is that there is a club on the first floor called Club Max (I think) and it's a meat market in the evenings. It was comical (or sad) to see the hotel filled with student groups and aging singles trying to mingle to/from the club and the parking lot. It was an odd combo. The breakfast buffet is fine and the service is ok. They will give you coffee to go. It might even be the Starbucks coffee that they brew from the coffee stand right next to the restaurant. They have a fitness center on the second floor and it is much better than most hotel fitness centers. They have at least 7 treadmills and lots of machines and free weights. I believe that it is open 24 hours with your card key. The hotel is also walking distance to the Karina Station VTA stop and the Airport/Metro stop.

“Nice location” Just completed a 5 night stay in the property. We chose the hotel as it was next door to our meetings and it was nice to be close to the park. In that respect it was perfect. Finding our room was tricky as the signage pointed us in completely the wrong direction.When we found the room at the back but it was bright, the bed was very comfortable and the bathroom a bit larger than usual. We thought that the large vent outside might be a problem but it actually provided some welcome white noise and we were not disturbed at all during our stay. I'm not quite sure what I think about the refurbishment. I don't think they have been very stringent in enforcing a no smoking policy as I thought there was a faint residual smell of smoke. There is lots of modular wood (which is looking a bit tired already) and dark orange accents with a tomato/ orange leather work chair. I'm sure there is a posh word to describe the colour of the furnishings and the doors but whatever it is, I won't be choosing it at home. But most importantly, we slept like a log every night. House keeping was not up to standard. One day they didn't come until the afternoon and left the duvet without a cover. Another night housekeeping came to turn down the bed when we had gone to sleep. All the lights went on, they didn't switch them off and we had to get out of bed to switch them all off again. Apparently this can be done from the phone but I never worked out how. We ate a couple of times in the restaurant and it was quite good. Breakfast was OK but the service was quite personal by the third day which was a nice touch. Service generally (apart from the housekeeping) was friendly. Overall we liked the hotel. I'm not sure that it will become our "home from home" but I can honestly say that we have never slept as well in a NYC hotel.
“Quirky, fun” Kinda quirky hotel. Strange decoration, complete with leopard print robes in the closet.

“Excellent Place!” My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Palomar for a few nights and thought it was a great place. It was recently renovated and everything looks new. The rooms are a good size and are clean with comfortable beds. The bathrooms are also spacious and the toiletries were really nice. The decorating was cool if a little strange...we would have preferred a table and chairs to the chaise...but we loved the big flat screen TV. The business center was really nice offering computers with both a Mac and PC side. My only annoyance was that they charged for it, but a lot of places do. UCLA is nearby so there are quite a few cafes and shops within walking distance. We got an excellent rate that included valet which was great because I'm not sure where else you could park. The staff was super friendly and really helpful. They gave us a late checkout with no problems.

“What You'd Expect From A Marriott” This Marriott Hotel is located right on Alaskan Way, directly across the street from the water. The facility is newer with the antiseptic feel of a large corporate hotel. The lobby is spacious with a lot of natural light, with the expected layout to check people in and out efficiently. This is a popular hotel for both cruise ship departures and conventioniers. That said, the front desk staff was professional and personable in check in despite the numbers of people in the check in queue. The rest of the lobby is comprised of the concierge desk, sundry shop and the bar area. Pretty standard fare for a Marriott. The rooms are of average size and are appointed well, but not luxuriously. The bathroom has good space and the beds are very comfortable. My room had a walkout balcony that overlooked the pool and the marina across the street. Because the room is street facing and adjacent to the pool, beware of street noises and children splashing in the pool. I didn't mind the train so much, but the noise from the pool did go until later in the night. Just be aware. The restaurant downstairs is worth going to, even if the meals don't justify the cost. The food is well prepared, sourced locally and not too bad, though the service was lacking. LIke most hotel dining facilities, the costs are inflated and you have to laugh at spending $16 for a la carte french toast. The valet staff was professional and refreshingly honest. When I asked them where to eat, they gave me honest answers and didn't push me to the tourist traps littering the "boardwalk." I was here for business so the tourist sights were of little importance to me. However, Pike Place Market is only a quick walk away as are many other things to do with the family. Overall, you will pay a premium for being on the water but if you're looking for a predictable experience with consistent service this hotel is recommended.

“first time ever been ripped off by hotel $150” I've stayed at hundreds of different hotels over the years and not one single time have I ever been randomly charged for something a few days after I had left. These con artists attempted to slip a $150 charge for a "so called" damaged comforter. I DID NOT damage a comforter all I did was sleep in it. I never set a bag or anything else on the bed there is absolutely no way I damaged it. At least have the decency to call me and tell me instead of me realizing it after looking my account over days later! I'm pretty sure they were mad that I used my points for my stay and didn't make any money so they figured they'd try and screw me by trying to slip a $150 charge by me. Nope I had my bank reverse the charge. Anybody in a hotel can come up with a dirty comforter long after you've checked out, these jokers have got to be kidding. Well needless to say I wouldn't stay at this dump ever again. I can't believe after all those hotels I've stayed at I've never ever been charged a penny more than I should have, as it should be. The hell with these grifters. If you stay here WATCH your credit card statements closely they may try and screw ya. P.S. The hotel's not that great either, certainly not worth a hundred bucks a night, maybe 70 max. ...and the parking lot is always full at night so you have to park on the street which SUCKS.

“Reminded me of a business man with a grass skirt but great food” This is a convention hotel. The pool is much bigger than it looks. There were very few people in casual clothing however the location can not be beat. Seaport Village and the Gaslamp district are right there. Roy's had such terrific food that we went back again for dinner. DW, the casual restaurant had excellent burgers and great fried eggplant but otherewise had a very limited menu. I would definately recommend it to others but it does not have a tourist or resort feel to it at all. The service was very good.

“Perfect for Visiting Penn” If you are traveling to visit the University of Pennsylvania this is the perfect place to stay. The hotel is directly across the street from the heart of the University and gives you a great snapshot of Penn. If you're visiting Penn and don't want to get a rental car, this hotel is very easy to access from the airport via public transportation (if you have bit of time). From the Airport you can take the R1 train to the 30th street station. From there you can go across the street and take a trolly to the 36th street station which is right next to the hotel. The total cost should be under $10. This is my second time to stay at the hotel. The previous visit was during the hotel's renovation. The project is complete and the hotel looks very nice. The rooms are a decent size, with very comfortable beds. The decor is at the upper end for a Hilton. The bathrooms are standard size but had amazing water pressure. I was surprised how strong the pressure was for a hotel. The towels were plentiful but seemed a bit old. The hotel had wifi internet access for a nominal charge. My room had a strong connection and the speed was adequate to get some work done. The front desk staff was very helpful. They were able to give me good directions, and suggest a nice place to eat.

“A great new place to stay downtown” This is a terrific addition to downtown NYC hotel scene. If you're planning on spending time in the Nolita, Lower East Side, Bowery, SOHO areas, this is someplace to definitely consider. The hotel is very modern so if lots of exposed concrete isn't your thing, then look elsewhere. However, if your tastes run in that direction and you want to be pretty much in the center of everything those neighborhoods have to offer, then this is the place. The staff is awesome from the minute you arrive; as a matter of fact it starts before you arrive. I actually got a call from the concierge a few days before my stay asking if there was anything she could do for me. I asked her if she could get me tickets to a show I really wanted to see but which appeared sold out. She said she'd give it a shot and a couple of hours later called back and I had my seat! On arrival everyone was very nice and helpful and remained so at every interaction I had. The downstairs/lounge area is really stylish and nice and the restaurant serves excellent food. It is a little quiet in the evening so if you want your hotel to have a happening scene in its bar then maybe give it a few months for things to heat up and stay at the Bowery Hotel or the Crosby Street Hotel or the Hotel on Rivington. But, I am sure it will heat up because it's a cool place in a cool hood and probably just needs a little time. Two things about the restaurant/lounge that did bug me a bit: First, the bar closed at midnight on Friday which seemed a little early for this part of the world. Second, the restaurant stopped serving breakfast at 10:30 on Saturday, which also seemed a little early, especially for a town that seems to run on brunch. They really need to keep it going until noon. The rooms are small so be prepared. However, they are very well designed and everything seems to fit just fine. As to the noise issue that many people seem to complain about let me say the following: Street noise was not an issue at all, there just wasn't any. The windows seem to block it all, save for the occasional fire truck which, come on, is to be expected in NYC. The HVAC system is a little loud but not intrusively so; it never bothered me. The one noise issue that was a little surprising was the hallway noise. They evidently didn't use noise proofing doors on the rooms and with all that exposed concrete, you do pretty much hear everything that's happening in the hallway as if it were happening in your room. Of course, the converse is also true so expect whatever you do in your room to be played loud and clear in the hallway. However, that said it really wasn't an issue as it's a small hotel and there's thus not a lot of coming and going. And, I never heard anything from anyone else's room. The minibar is jam packed with good stuff, they have nice robes, T-shirts and even a yoga mat for you. The bathroom is nice too and packed with high quality amenities. They have free wifi throughout and a nice desk which is very spacious for work. The closet is adequate but it is a bit tight so if you're a heavy packer beware. Lastly, there is a killer view uptown (at least from the higher floors); you basically look out toward all of midtown. In summary I really liked this place and would definitely stay here again.

“Fantastic! Cool! Excellent” Stayed there for 5 days. One of the coolest hotel i've been to, even for NYC. Great modernistic design in reception, bar and rooms. Had great room heading south from 20th floor with view to hudson river and the ferry. Incredible. We didnt experience noise from the building site. Great staff who where very helpfull in all requests. Highly recommendable. Got great deal, 4 nights in exec. room for 900$.

“Nice stay - great price - neat history at this hotel” The Menger is a very interesting establishment. Besides being over a century old, the location of this hotel is perfect for tourists visiting San Antonio. Several historical figures (Teddy Roosevelt, Sidney Linear, Oscar Wilde) have stayed at this hotel. Numerous photographs hang on the walls, showing the illustrious history of the hotel. We did not dine at the hotel, though the Sunday Brunch looked pretty good. I have heard that the Menger Bar is quite famous. Also, the location couldn't be better for tourists. You are litterally right next door to the Alamo and right across the street from the San Antonio riverwalk. The room was fairly nice, a big snug and dated but it served the purpose nicely. The A/C was nice and cold! By the way, we actually booked this hotel on www.hotels.com and found a great price for this hotel!

“Nice hotel that is very conveniently located.” Our stay at the Crowne Plaza Hotel was very good. While not as upscale, as some of the other hotels in the area like the Hyatt it is still a nice property. For starters this hotel was conveniently located near the 16th Street Mall and jus a short cab ride from Coors Field. This staff at this hotel was very friendly including the check-in desk clerk and concierge. Our room was nice with two full sized beds, desk/office chair, and coffee maker. Also our room offered a good view of the downtown Denver. On the downside, as with many hotels the hotels in the area there is fee to park your car ($22 a night at this hotel). In conclusion I will consider staying there again the future.

“Pod Hotel Great Concept - Get a Double room for ONE” I needed a room during a large conference in NYC at the Hilton this past weekend and wanted to spend under $110./night including tax. I usually try priceline and use betterbidding.com to advise me on what to expect. They said anything uder $100. base rate would be only a 1 star. They recommended I go to a site to book the POd. I first read the reviews here and saw the renovation was new. They officially change name from Pickwick Arms THIS WEEK. I knew the rooms and bed would be small and so I booked a "double" for $89. plus tax ($101.) even though I was just one tall person. I wanted a quiet room and got it. It's an interesting design concept. Evety space is used. Think of a SMALL dorm room and you get the idea. The double bed was 6' 4" ing and about two pillows wide. But you sleep parralell to the wall (think of a standard double bed turned 90 degrees. The windows open which a lot of redone hotels don't have. Bed was comfortable though only a light blanket. The room was SPOTLESS and BRAND new. I chose private bath. ($20.00 less for shared) but checked out the shared ones. There were 5 I think on my floor (11th Floor - I had room 1124). Each has a toilet,sink and shower.). In morning the flooors were obviously wet. My shower was actually LARGE. Fixed overheard nozzel almost touched my head (I'm 6' 3"). 20 in plasma TV is fixed on wall and doesn't pivot. That's fine. The Clock Radio has ipod docking station but it only accepts iPods, not other MP3 players without a cable. Sound okay. Used the wake up call, service from front desk and it was fine. Especially if you are looking for a room to bunk on short notice, I think this is a great choice. Will use when I can't find a bargain through Priceline or Hotwire. And the neighborhood is great and quiet. Oh I forgot, I heard no hall noise from my room and, as I faced the back, no outside noise even with window open. Now if they keep prices under $100 for a double, I think this will be a great resource. P.S. I took about 6 photos but after trying to upload more than one on this review and not succeeding, I gave up! Steve

“Loved it!” Apparently everything IS bigger in Texas. Our room (on the 7th floor overlooking the pool) was incredibly spacious. I was very surprised when we opened the door to see how big it was. I loved the décor. It wasn’t your standard hotel room in that it had a curio cabinet filled with vases and other decorative pieces, and the room overall just had a very eclectic feel to it. It had a big, sturdy desk, too—again, not a typical cramped hotel desk but one that you could actually do work at if you were traveling for business. The bed was very comfortable and while the pool area was loud a few of the nights, the sound didn’t make it into our room. The pool gets very crowded very quickly on the weekends, so be sure to get there early to stake out your spot. They have cabanas, as well, if you aren’t a sun worshipper like me. Poolside food and drinks were very good and the service was consistent. I’ve been to some hotels where the server gets you one drink then seems to disappear for the day, but not here. Valet parking was a little on the steep side at $27/night. We kept meaning to check parking elsewhere in the area but never got around to it. We never had to wait for our car, though, despite the fact that the valets always seemed to be incredibly busy. Service was great. The valets were very friendly and when we called for extra towels in our room, they were delivered right away. The location is ideal for exploring the museums or if you need to be near Rice Univ. or the medical center, but it’s also close to downtown, too.

“Good, but not without problems” Just returned from a stay of 3 nights at this hotel. Good news - the lobby remodeling is done and the lobby looks great. They were putting on the last coat of paint this past week. The restaurant is also looking good - expected to open in mid-May. The only scaffolding in front is now just used to finish the awning. They removed the rest of the scaffolding. Looking good! The stay was not without problems... The good: - as previously mentioned, the beds are incredibly comfortable. I liked the standard pillows and did not order from the pillow menu. - valet parking and the doorman were efficient and very friendly - The flat panel TV was on an arm and could reach over the bed in my room. Very flexible! - Spacious bathroom with great lighted mirrors - The room was big enough that there were two thermostats that controlled two separate heating/cooling ducts. - The hotel was quiet except for the previously mentioned sirens from the nearby hospital. - Good Aveda products in the bathroom. Nice robes - Excellent location - Bottled water was usually available on the front desk The not so good: - I checked in at noon and they allowed an early check-in. They gave me a disabled room without asking if this was OK. In the past, other hotels have always asked if this was OK. I believe the front desk should have asked. - I paid extra for a suite upgrade and requested a junior suite with two king beds. That's just what I got. The room was very long with two king beds, a desk/chair, a cabinet with three drawers, and a cabinet with two shelves/mini-fridge. That's all the furniture in a junior suite? Maybe this was because the room was for the disabled, but the only chair was a desk chair. There was plenty of room for a sofa or easy chair. - Be aware that rooms with two king beds only exist on the first 7 floors. If you notice from the outside, the hotel has setbacks on floor 8 so the only place with enough room for the 2 king rooms is on the first 7 floors. (You do get two elevators that only serve floors 1 - 7 so there never was a wait.) - I don't know if there are doors/shower curtains on the showers in non-disabled rooms, but my room had an open shower. The bathroom floor was pretty wet by the time I finished showering. - The sensors on the automatic revolving front door didn't work well. Frequently the door stopped while I was still in the door. (No, I didn't touch the door!) I finally learned I just needed to push the door when it stopped - it wouldn't re-start automatically - Hopefully they will re-pour new sidewalks when all the scaffolding is gone. There are a lot of potholes in their entrance concrete - There was no listing of services in the room - just a note mentioning the restaurant remodeling and the delivery available from nearby restaurants. There was a pillow menu on the bed, but no mention of the other Affinia services that are mentioned on their web site - One weekday morning I did find coffee/tea/rolls in the lobby. However, the rolls were really stale. Nice selection of tea, though. - While I could always get fairly warm water in the shower, the water was never really hot. Decent pressure, though. Would I stay again? Yes, if the price were right. I suspect their prices will rise when the the remodeling is finished. Since I'm a price shopper, I'd gladly stay at the Courtyard by Marriott down the street (St. Clair) if the price was better. I still wouldn't hesitate to stay at the Affinia if they had a good price.

“We left the best for last!!” .After flying into Boston on 9/9/11 we stayed in the downtown area for two days and then headed up to Bar Harbor and worked our way back to Embassy Suites for our last night before flying out Saturday 9/17. Embassy is just what we needed for the end of our vacation. Service from the door men went well above what was expected. The airport has put up a barricade so you cannot get to the Embassy without going through the airport. We did not know this so our GPS brought us to the Chelsea Bridge which is also closed so we worked our way around one way streets, closed streets and lack of street signs longer then we liked. Finally finding the Embassy and we could not get to it!!! I jumped out of the car and found the doormen from heaven. They had nicely written out directions and I just sighed when they were explaining them. One of the men said, “I will get in the car and help you". I could have hugged him. Thank you, thank you, thank you. The rooms were spotless and beautiful. I've been in the Embassy in St. Paul MN and was skeptical about booking this one but it seems a lot newer and more contemporary then the Minnesota one. Loved the managers evening reception and complimentary (Large) breakfast. I am a Hilton Honors so I also received free WIFI. They also had a business office to print airline Ticket. I did see a lot of people asking where the subway stop to downtown was and it was very close. Loved, Loved this hotel

“Not a fan” Overpriced and underserved. All guests on the van from the airport had been waiting 25 min or longer. I have stayed at this hotel several times and it never measures up to expectations. A Hilton Diamond member.

“Not as great as 1st stay, but still better than most NYC hotels” My fiance and I stayed at the Andaz Wall Street over Thanksgiving weekend. This was our 2nd stay at the hotel. The front desk service was exceptional and the room was as immaculate as my 1st stay. Our room wasn't ready for early check-in but we were notified via email 2 hours later that our room was ready. Later that day we took advantage of the complimentary wine in the lobby in the evening before heading to dinner; we were glad to see many other hotel guests taking advantage of this, as it created a really nice, fun atmosphere. We also grabbed a nightcap in the hotel bar (Bar Seventy-Five), which is a very unique, modern space atypical of any other hotel bar. Despite the many outstanding aspects of my latest experience staying at this hotel, the areas of concern arose during this time were: 1. Still wish they provided iron/ironing board in ALL rooms. Had to request both again and waited 30 minutes before receiving one. 2. Pillows are way too soft. Didn't sleep well both nights of our stay. 3. Walls are very thin. The young family staying in the adjacent room seriously disrupted us early one morning. We endured 2 hours' of hearing the parents arguing and screaming at their toddler to stop yelling, and for their older child to behave. The children seemed out of control and the parents' seemed at their wits' end. It got so bad that I called the front desk and they had a manager contact them, at which point we heard the parents argue over not being able to control their children and the children further continuing their misbehavior. THANK GOD they were checking out later that morning! (FWIW, this is not the type of hotel that is conducive to travel w/ a young family w/ multiple children. It's quiet, mostly business travelers during the week and savvy, sophisticated urban travelers during weekends/holidays.) Given my familiarity with NYC and my complete distaste for many of the overpriced, overrated Midtown hotels w/ tiny rooms & bathrooms, I'm more than happy to stay at the Andaz Wall Street any time I'm in NYC. Hopefully the next time around we'll have quiet guests around us!

“Disappointed with Service” I wanted to do something special for our wedding anniversary so I booked a room at the Crescent. The price was steeper than I would normally pay, but being a special occasion, I thought it would be worth it. Unfortunately, that was not the case. I requested that flowers, a fruit basket, and a bottle of champagne be in our room at check in. I was assured that this was not an unusual request (all at my expense), and would be taken care of. When we arrived at the hotel, I asked the front desk if my special requests had been noted in the reservation and was told that nothing special had been noted. Told not to worry, that fresh flowers were placed in every room every day, and that the fruit basket and champagne would be on the way shortly. Needless to say, none of the above materialized. We never did get flowers, not even the ones that are supposedly placed in every room every day. After about two hours I called room service and asked where were the fruit basket and champagne. They delivered a bowl of bananas and apples (yawn), and a bottle of domestic California champagne for over $100 per bottle. I would have happily paid for the items that I requested given the chance. My money and business will go elsewhere when I decide to celebrate a special occasion.

“Love this hotel!” My mom and I just arrived home from our trip to Chicago where we stayed at the Embassy Suites Downtown/Lakefront. Love this place! I stayed here about six years ago with friends and it was nice then, and it's still very nice now. My mom and I had reserved a room elsewhere for this trip, but decided it was worth a little extra money to stay at the Embassy Suites. We were able to check in early (at 10:30 a.m. on a very busy Saturday morning) with no questions asked and were given a spacious room on the 16th floor with two double beds. The beds were so comfortable; we crashed in them after a long day of shopping! Bathrooms are fairly large for a downtown hotel. There was a little wear and tear in our bathroom, but nothing terrible - just a little wallpaper peeling off in one of the corners. Had large, fluffy towels in the bathroom as well. Oh, and love the complimentary manager's reception and cook-to-order breakfast. Both were busy on Saturday night, but the lines moved fairly quickly and the staff was friendly. In fact, everyone at this hotel was friendly and polite. And the location can't be beat - just two blocks off Michigan Avenue! I definitely hope to stay here again on my next trip to Chicago!

“Pleasant Surprise!” I booked the Renaissance through Priceline and got a very good deal, more than half off the hotel's internet price. So, I was worried that the hotel would be dumpy. Thankfully it was far from dumpy. It was great! Fantastic location. Excellent service. We booked a king size room and were given a one-bedroom suite. It was nicely furnished, large and very comfortable. I am very picky about bedding and the bedding met my high standards. The sheets were high thread count, smooth and covered the comforter completely (top and bottom sort of forming a duvet). The complementary coffee service in the morning was great. They also gave us parking ($25) for free. The food was good in the restaurants too. I would definitely stay here again. The hotel exterior is under construction so it's hard to see the name as you are driving by. Note: The hotel is right next to the freeway, but the soundproofing makes it hardly noticeable.

“Customer Service and Class” We stayed at the Fairmont for 5 nights the end of July. I booked a Deluxe Suite to have enough sq footage for my teenage son and I. Our first room was on the 11th floor and had not been renovated, It had a musty smell and we started sniffing pretty quickly so I would wager there had been a dog in there since we are both allergic to dogs. Since it was late we used the room and the next morning I expressed my concerns and by the end of the day we were in a lower floor updated room. The concierges were fantastic, the one guy William knew everybody and was the go to person for every question we had. He was a hoot. The Fairmont is lucky to have him. The Valet guys were awesome too. I could tell they tried to remember something about everyone coming and going and since we were there the week of Seafair, the place was busy. I bet The Fairmont was sold out. We ate most of our meals on the go or on the waterfront but the last day we ate brunch at the hotel and it was a nice selection of breakfast foods. The only thing I thought was odd in the Georgian was that we were sat at a bench seat with only one side. We didnt use the Pool and I did get a pedicure and to my surprise they have waterless pedicures. It was odd but OK after you get over the fact that you aren't going to soak your feet after walking all day. My fault for not asking what kind of pedicure I was getting, The spa was very clean nevertheless. Great Location to Monorail, airport, Pikes Place and waterfront.

“Not the cleanest place” The staff was friendly and the stay ok, but there was a very stale odor in all the hallways and the room was not clean. Stains on sofa, smelly drains in bathroom, and the microwave could have used a thorough wipe down. Luckily it was a one night stay...I couldn't fathom staying there any longer.

“A lot of good, but a lot of bad too” On the Pro side of things: Location is great, 2 blocks from Boston Common, convenient to Beacon Hill and the Back Bay. The customer service is very good, the furnishings in the room are modern, great bath products, and every room has a small balcony. They have a small gym and a nice pool. On the cons: I kid you not, the hallways smell like vomit. Either they use the worst smelling carpet cleaner ever, or the Emerald lounge crowd that it caters too has too much fun and can't make it to the bathroom. The hotel caters toward the Emerald lounge, they offer you VIP access for staying at the hotel which means at 2 AM you hear the drunkards running up and down the halls and being very loud. Those 2 things alone really contribute to the downside of things. If you are not young and looking to party all night, I would not recommend this hotel. Unfortunately the crowd it seems to cater to overrides the positive aspects I listed.

“Fabulous stay!” We stayed recently at the Barclay for a weekend and were very impressed. We had a great room that was very spacious and quiet on the top floor. The service was great- the room was absolutely spotless, check-in was a friendly breeze, and everyone we encountered was warm and helpful. The beds were extremely comfortable and we slept great both nights. The lobby was hopping in a good way- this hotel has good energy. If we'd had more time it would have been fun to linger more in the lobby and people-watch. We have stayed further downtown on some previous nyc trips but the convenience to Central Park and the theatre district were fantastic, plus you are close enough to downtown that it is just a short cab ride. Finally, I thought the hotel's.environmental efforts were very cool, and I like that they are focused on being green. We'd happily return!

“Elegant and charming” We stopped into the Drake to ogle its old-world charm and ended up staying for lunch at the Palm Court midst all the folks who were enjoying high tea. Service was elegant, of course; the harpist was playing and everything was beautiful. Food was good, but mostly we were just happy looking around and enjoying everyone else. It was a lovely way to spend some time on a November afternoon in Chicago.

“Great Value!” I stayed in the Washington Plaza for a night and i never regret my decision! All the staff at the hotel are nice and polite - never once i had to open the door myself and they all always greet u with a smile. The room are spacious and very clean. The bed is nice to sleep in too. It is a plus point that there's free wifi in the entire hotel! The toilet is big and i like that the lights are bright enough. The hotel is very quiet too. Never once had i been disturbed by noises or anything.The only negative point is that the hotel is abit far from the Metro so be prepared if u need to take the Metro regularly or if u're moving around with luggages.

“A new favorite in Chicago” I stayed here in July 2011 for three days while on business for a week in IL. My partner flew in to join me for the last three days and we had a wonderful time. I had booked a King room but because I was a platimum member with Marriott I was upgraded to the to the concierge level and given a room that I can only describe as jaw dropping. It was a corner King and must have easily been two or three times the size of a regular King room. Double sinks in bathroom with separate tub and shower. The service in the hotel is really really good. Room service arrived quick and was piping hot, parking valet was quicker than I expected for a city hotel given it's size. The breakfast was great and plentiful. The staff helpful to a fault. I am usually very critical and particular about hotels because I travel so much for work and i like things a certain way and I was a little taken aback that I could not find anything to pick on. I will without doubt stay here on my next trip back to Chicago.

“Beautifull hotel that shines in the shadows of a city of hotels!!” I stayed here with my wife back in 2004 and forgot to write a review but have to say it was one of my better stays in a hotel. this place shines like a jewel in the city full of hotels and trendy spots and it caters to the real upper crust traveler with equisite taste. The whole night from check in to check out was spectacular. The looby is something out of fantasy and just looks the part, really decadent and top notch. the staff is friendly for a 5 star place and helpful. this being part of the Hilton family of hotels, it is apparent they want you to return. The rooms are sort of run of the mill, small in size and all the top shelf ammenities. Hallways are dimly lit and historic looking. It is the only way to stay if you are visiting the city. I was there for one night but wish I had more time. Make sure to book well in advance because it sells out and make sure to take a loan out before you go, this place is not cheap and there are reasons it has been there for a while!!

“Worth the money nicely remodeled property & clean” Checked into the hotel and the clerk at the front was very friendly and helpful, received a room w/ two double beds and the room was nice and clean. This is an older property but has been remodeled nicely, has window units in the back, of the rooms, so the air or heat has to travel to the front, which can take some time. It never really got cold enough for me but I was there in October, and I like my air conditioner on 69 when I am at home, my friends that visited me were quite comfortable. You get a free buffet breakfast with the room, at the restaurant next door, they were quite uncaring or disinterested. They had several dirty tables and it was hard for me to get someone to pour me some coffee and water, the food was OK but nothing special, bacon, eggs, pancakes, etc. I would have preferred a coupon to Denny's or even Whataburger lol.. the service was deplorable. Great food selections around not too far from Target, Kohls, and other stores, this was a very walkable location. Other than that the HOTEL was great value and nice to stay...

“My Mom and I” I have been here before, but I was able to take my mother who is 68, to New York for the first time.She loved this hotel.. The breakfast was great and the location to everything --super.. Nice clean rooms .. I will recommend this to everyone looking for a central location at a good price..
“Great Boutique Hotel” We really enjoyed our stay here. The location is great for walking and exploring downtown Seattle, and the rooms were very comfortable and luxurious. Highly recommended!

“Great budget hotel” Nice location on 33rd, right next to the empire state building and one block from Herald Square. Comfortable beds, microwave and fridge included in the room with a Deluxe King. Right next to a fantastic Korean dumpling place called Mandoo. I stayed at this hotel over a dozen times between 2010-2011 and never had any problems.
“Ok Place” Convenient and recently updated. An ok place to stay.

“Very pleased” We stayed at 2 Hilton hotels in Chicago -- the Palmer House and the Chicago Hilton (using HHonors points, taking what was available each night of our trip). At each hotel, our room was on the executive level. The Palmer House was easily the nicest of the two hotels. Our double bed room had 2 bathrooms, both very up-to-date, clean and reasonably sized. The room itself was slightly larger than your average double bed room. On the 23rd floor, we were not able to hear the L-train, but I can certainly see how that would be a problem on lower floors. The lobby area is beautiful, the staff friendly, and the area very convenient. Our only problem was that our room was too warm -- the air conditioner did a very poor job. We did not complain. If I return to Chicago, I would certainly stay here again. Not so for the Chicago Hilton -- avoid that one.

“Not what I expected” This is a typical case of misleading hotel website photos. Just because the pictures showed a large flat screen TV, kitchen countertop, sofa, and room divider, I was expecting a generously large room to accommodate these furnishings. In reality the furniture is cleverly arranged to maximize the space in an otherwise standard size room. Most disappointing for me is the appearance of the walls and ceilings -- ugly, old-fashioned spongeblot-textured paint. Please put in some color or wallpaper! The room could use brighter lighting. Free wi-fi signal is very weak. I was also displeased with the generic toiletry kit as I have grown accustom to better quality offerings from Starwood and IHG properties. The enclosed shower and toilet space is too small and cramped to move about comfortably. Hotel location is also very poor. Located at the southwest corner of IH-35 and 183, it is far from downtown Austin and even further when you consider the horrible traffic on IH-35. When coming from downtown remember to exit St. Johns, go through one light on the feeder, and then make a u-turn (under 183) right before the second set of lights. The hotel does have its upside. In addition to the items already mentioned at the top of this review, the room is also furnished with a writing desk, fridge, coffeemaker, ironing board, hairdryer, and at least a 46-in flat screen TV (by far the largest I have had in any room I've stayed in). The bathroom sink has very nice Kohler fixtures, and is conveniently separated from the shower and toilet. The lobby doubles as a comfortable lounge and the front desk staff was always friendly and helpful. The free breakfast includes fresh fruit, yogurt, oatmeal, toast, muffins, spreads, milk, juice, coffee, and cereals. For an extra fee they can prepare hot food items for you. It would have been nice if eggs (scrambled or hard-boiled), sausage, and waffles were also offered in the free breakfast. Personally I would not stay here again. It's just a bit too far from downtown. But if you want quick access to north Austin, Mopac, or 360 then this hotel could be ok for you. Considering its distance and quality of room and amenities, I don't think it was worth the $103.

“Nice place” Big place, but service is very personal, its a nice touch. Oversized room with comfortable beds, easy to use TV (sometimes rare for a hotel), and big bathroom. Minimal noise from outside, but some disturbances from neighboring rooms, fortunately not late at night. The Regency Club is very nice, the staff present (didn't catch his name!) was so helpful and friendly and the views are amazing. Easy access to the restaurants and shops along 16th Street. I recommend Rock Bottom Brewery. There is a Rite Aid and Walgreens both 2 blocks away if you forgot to bring any essentials with you. I'll close by saying again that the staff really adds a personal touch to this place that is much appreciated.

“Large room with nice touches” I was able to book a room at this hotel through Priceline at an extremely reasonable rate, so I wasn't expecting much. I was amazed to find a very large, comfortable, attractive room with a huge sectional sofa, the largest TV I've ever had control over, a desk, and a great bed. The staff was friendly enough. It seemed like a nice enough place that it should have had a restaurant, which is too bad given El Paso's dismal dining options. We didn't quite understand if breakfast was free, so we opted out. But the public areas were nice, like a cozy cafe, and the free internet was icing on the cake. Color me very impressed for the price.

“A friendly and comfortable hotel” My wife and I stayed here for two nights while attending a conference. We chose it mostly because it was a good value: we got a better discount rate here than we would have gotten at the nearby Hampton Inn. And it turned out to be awfully nice. We had a comfortable and spacious room with a view of the lake. The staff was friendly and helpful -- Kayla, the reception desk employee who checked us in, deserves special mention. Breakfast in the restaurant was tasty and reasonably diverse. Self-parking is free, and although the lot was crowded (in part because there seemed to be several large Christmas parties going on in the hotel) we always managed to find a space that wasn't too far from the front door. The hotel is a short walk from some good stores and restaurants. And even the lobby had a nice friendly ambience. We noticed only one problem, which is that the Executive Lounge is closed all weekend every weekend. No snacks or appetizers on Friday evening, and nothing at all on Saturday or Sunday. This is something I've noticed at a couple of other small-to-medium-sized Hiltons in the last few months, and it strikes me as a serious mistake. Access to these lounges is among the most powerful inducements for frequent travelers to concentrate their hotel stays within the Hilton chain so as to reach or maintain elite status in the Honors program, and it's even more important to travelers who pay a substantial extra sum for "executive level" rooms. And it makes no sense at all to think that travelers would care more about having access to an executive lounge Monday through Thursday than they would Friday through Sunday. In this case it was a real shame, because the lounge -- which we saw through the locked glass door every time we walked from our room to the elevator -- looked beautiful and comfortable. (We did get coupons for breakfast in the restaurant in lieu of lounge access.)

“Great Place to Stay for NYC” This place is near everything! Its a 5 min walk to Times Square, a 5 min walk to a subway stop, and litterally close to everything! The people who work here are VERY friendly and VERY helpful. We stayed here for 5 nights and they made us feel like we were at home. the rooms are very comfortable and "bigger" for new york standards. Everything is updated, clean and fresh. You can hear street noise from the street below, but that is like any other city you stay in. Will stay here again when visiting NYC. and the Breakfast is very good!

“Way more "Motel" than "Hotel".” Adequate. Period. Apparently was an attempt at a condo complex that wasn't making it--so trying to call itself a "hotel". Claims to be near downtown and near UT Campus....HA!! It's 7+1/2 miles from Campus, and the drive takes a minimum of 16 minutes. The rooms are not bad, but the door/key is very difficult to manipulate. It's setup like a little studio apartment; kitchen, sitting room, separate bedroom/king-sized bed, with a vanity and toilet-shower. The sitting room has a decent sofa---but NOT a sofa bed. In fact, they have No Rollaways available. Breakfast is do-it-yourself packaged oatmeal, smallish muffins, and dried cold cereal. Absolutely Horrible coffee. No skim milk. Apples and bananas. Nothing else fresh, nothing cooked-to-order. NOT a "bed-and-breakfast". Advantages--cheap, easy to park, quiet neighborhood, friendly ladies at the front desk. Disadvantages--Not close to Anything, needs a lot of remodeling, terrible excuse for a breakfast. Definitely NOT a "three-star"; Basically: you get what you pay for.

“Very friendly staff - close to lots of activity options” Stayed just for one night. Room was nice. Staff was very friendly at check in and whenever I entered lobby area. Close to all that there is to do at The Domain.

“Fantastic staff, clean rooms, lots of noise...” I booked this hotel for a reward stay on New Year's Eve when the Marriott Marquis couldn't guarantee my room for the night. It's a block away from Macy's, two blocks from Penn Station, a block from the Empire State Building, and a short walk from Times Square and the theater district. There isn't much around this hotel in the way of restaurants, but it's fairly centrally located to get elsewhere. The rooms are quite small, especially compared to the Marquis. This is a new hotel though, so the beds are comfortable, the linens are new, and the rooms are clean. However, the walls are paper thin, and you can hear everything going on in the hallway, down the hall, in the room next to you... It was a bit frustrating. There was a family that reserved two rooms, one for the parents, and the other for 4 teenage girls who tried to play music and scream all night. I finally called downstairs, as I had to be up early. The security officer came up and told them to "be cool". Not really that effective. However, the staff was extremely nice and helpful. They provide a free breakfast from 6-10, which is a nice perk as well. Internet is free, and there is a computer available for guest use. The noise factor is a huge issue for me though -- it's hard to believe they did so little soundproofing in a new hotel.
“Dreamy bed” The most fantastic mattress I have ever slept upon. Did not want to get up - ever.

“Wonderful service, facilities are somewhat lacking” I stayed here for one night during a recent business trip to San Francisco. I frequently travel to San Francisco and try out the different boutique hotels around the city. When one of my usual picks was fully booked, I decided to try out the Hotel Abri based on its very high TripAdivsor ratings. Overall my stay at the hotel was average. I agree with some of the other reviewers in therms of the hotel strong points. The hotel staff is incredibly helpful and friendly. Out of all the boutique hotels in SF where I've had the opportunity to stay, this staff in particular stands out. When my first room did not meet my needs, the front desk staff did not hesitate to place me into another one and even offered me some honest caveats about my potential room switch (which I will detail later). The location is somewhat of a mixed bag. It is a big plus that it is located very close to the Powell Street cable car turnaround and Union Square. The minus is that the area can be noisy, and there is a popular club located across the street that, from what I understand, can get very loud late into the night. Why should noise be an issue? This leads me to my major point of contention with this hotel. I understand that it is a historic property, but I don't feel the owners made the necessary improvements to modernize it fully. I don't mean this in the sense of decor and style, which without question the Abri has sufficient. It's more in terms of the infrastructure. The rooms are small and updated, but it seems like certain things were left out of the update. Although the window face a busy intersection, there is not sufficient soundproofing. The first room I had faced onto the street, and when I was on the phone in my room, the person with whom I was speaking thought I was out on the street. Also, the air conditioner is mounted on the window, which blocks off half of the light coming in, making the rooms incredibly dim. Rooms also had a musty, old smell. I've stayed in historic hotels previously, and this was not a problem. However in the Abri the room always smelled musty and old even though it was completely redone. I found myself having to turn on the air conditioner to "freshen up" the room even though it was cool outside. And usually I'm alright with small rooms, but these rooms were some of the smallest in which I've stayed. If you're spending most of your time out of doors, it shouldn't be a problem, but be aware the rooms, especially interior facing rooms, are very tight with little room for suitcases. I'd probably not stay here again. I think this hotel is probably better for vacationers or younger tourists. The style and service certainly are there, but as I mentioned in my title, the facilities are lacking.
“Great spot” Nice place, clean, spacious, great bed. Temperature control was so-so. Neighborhood not elegant, but good Chinese restaurant around the corner.

“Modern but missing details of a typical four-star” [This note to Priceline & other third-party guests precedes all my reviews of hotels I purchased through a 3rd party vendor] Like everyone else, 3rd-party customers read reviews and arrive with expectations; high attentiveness to guest needs is what distinguishes one 2-3-4 star from others. Third-party prices fill rooms, and provide the business with opportunities to sell services and win future customers. My advice: pay attention to reviews, articulate your needs clearly (both in advance and on arrival) and speak directly and immediately to management if your expectations are not met. If basic room needs are unmet, ask management for adjustment; if unresponsive, tell the 3rd-party vendor in writing; use snail mail to the company’s street address and direct to Customer Service VP. I’ve found them responsive. Talk to local management directly and pleasantly: they value meaningful guest feedback and often can use information you provide to correct persistent problems. Whatever rate you paid, be courteous and civil to a fault: it never helps to be confrontational. Commend with care what is commendable.] I spent two nights in late December, coming in on the BIG snow day. PLUSSES: This hotel is three blocks from Union Station, easily walkable even in snow. Staff gave me flawless directions on the telephone. Check-in easy, staff knowledgeable about public transportation and challenges in bad weather. Hotel has a gym and many free amenities I did not use, all described on web site. The room was clean and orderly, modern. Big LG flatscreen TV worked well. Bedding, king and wonderfully comfy. Minimal bathroom amenities, no tub in my room--looked like set up for handicap. Terrific reading lights attached to bed back/frame, could be turned to give lower light. Free business center with two stations, busy every time I checked. Free internet in lobby/bar area, worked perfectly for me. Great rate, well under $50, on Priceline. The Art & Soul restaurant owner is a public figure who works for the White House. BIG BUTS: Details atypical of a highly-ranked hotel. Room-based wireless dropped me and made only trouble. My basic personal policy is to stay off “help” lines, which frustrate and rarely help. Front desk said: “It’s working for everybody else.” Note: make a firm rule against such responses. (Charge was deleted from my account.) Bathroom wallpaper peeling; bath soap and shampoo in dispensers inside shower. Room temp controls easy to find and use, good heat but not extending to bathroom: heat source near ceiling blasts warm air over ceiling, bathroom icy cold, perhaps 65 degrees. Towels distant from shower--odd. Typical of downtown DC, very costly parking: $45+ for overnight. As in SF or NY, don’t drive if avoidable. Restaurant modestly busy but we waited more than five minutes at the entrance for any attention. Server tried to convince us it was “policy” not to serve a single order of the famed MD fried chicken, but we talked him out of that and the service and food was otherwise perfect. A breakfast was flawless and lovely.

“Solid choice at O'Hare” I've stayed in several of the hotels at O'Hare, and this is one of the best (even better, if often has very reasonable rates). --Efficient check-in. --Great staff overall--everyone I interacted with, from the shuttle driver to housekeeping, was polite and helpful. --Huge, big rooms. The suites have a large desk that allowed me to spread out and get a lot of work done. The bathrooms are also very large. --Great bedding! I had a great night's sleep. The rooms also have room-darkening shades, which was a lot better than typical hotel curtains that gap open and let in light. --Timely, tasty room service. --I liked that they sold buy-to-go meals in the lobby. I grabbed one on my way to the airport. --Decent fitness center. Would like it better if it wasn't in the basement, but it had good cardio and weight equipment, free water, etc. A couple of the surfaces in the room were showing some signs of age (some chipped wood, some worn fabric on a chair) but not enough to be a problem. Overall, an excellent stay -- a very solid choice if you have to overnight at O'Hare. It is a little farther from the airport than some of the other hotels, but the shuttle ride is still only about 15 minutes, and it's right next to the train if you want to ride it downtown.

“Great San Francisco weekend” We are fortunate enough to be close to SF to come up for the night, this night being in celebration of my in-laws 50th wedding anniversary. We wanted to do something special and stay somewhere they would NEVER stay themselves. I picked the Mark Hopkins for the history, location and also The Top of the Mark bar/restaurant. Our check in was flawless, had rooms next to each other on the 11th floor, facing Grace Cathedral (was supposed to be bay view) but didn't want to complain w/the in-laws along. We wanted an effortless experience. Rooms had great big beds, way comfy! Great mini-bar which of course hubby had to have the probably $8 Corona..whatever. Ordered champagne and strawberries in room to celebrate, then up to the Top of the Mark for a drink before dinner. Beautiful view...wow! Even with a little fog on the fringes, gorgeous! The only downside was that they seem to have no dress code up there. I guess I thought it was a classy place and dressed accordingly. We sat next to a girl wearing what I think was a handkerchief, really...you could see way too much...I'm not a prude, really. Just couldn't believe someone would dress like that in SF.. Anyways, after dinner (which was not at the hotel but the Jardiniere), back up to the Top of the Mark for a nightcap. No cover charge if you show them your room key! Great jazz band, hubby and I danced (even w/his broken toe). They sat us at a great corner bench and table. The view would have been amazing but the fog came in hard and fast. So what...still gorgeous view. All in all I would recommend this hotel. Everyone and everything was above board and I felt like I DID get my moneys worth. Inlaws were impressed so our weekend was a success! I booked directly with the hotel and got a pretty good rate. I definitely left my heart in SF...about 25 years ago! Keep coming back. Have traveled all over the world and this is one of my favorite places! Make sure you walk down California to Grant and see Chinatown. Fun!

“Enormous Room with very small bathroom...but fantastic staff” We had a huge suite (I think they all are) and the view was great. The staff was incredible - top notch! The decor was muted and attractive and the furniture and bed were comfortable. Apparently, when the building went from apartments to hotel, the "size" of the original apartments was retained. It's disappointing, however, that the bathrooms were not enlarged. There is absolutely NO place in the bathroom to place your toiltries, other than a somewhat wobbly, small, square rolling thing (that fits a shaving kit- maybe). While Nob Hill is a lovely location, you have to walk toward North Beach or down toward Union Square to find a restaurant, which can be inconvenient. But that all said, the staff would bring me back!

“Nice rooms, good view” I might complain about the $35 parking, but that's the going rate in Boston these days. The hotel was very nice. The rooms have a small living room and fair sized bedroom. We also had a great view of the Charles River. We pricelined it, and did fairly well considering weekday room rates in Boston lately. It's a bit off the beaten path (about 4 miles from the city center). Overall, no complaints.

“Why isn't the Omni Austin Downtown in the top 5?” Stayed at the Omni Austin Downtown for business - 3 nights. I travel lots for work and this was one of the best hotels and staff experiences. I had the most comfortable and accommodating stay. My one recommendation - ditch the foam pillows, provide feather/down if requested. Thank you for a great stay!

“Newest Hotel in downtown has a LOT going for it!” This hotel opened a little under two years ago and is still seems like it opened just yesterday. It is exceptionally clean, well appointed and comfortable. My wife and I stayed here for two days in two different rooms. We were on floor 25 on one day and on floor 28 on another. The upper rooms are an 'upgrade' and you should try to get these rooms if at all possible. The only real differences we saw were a free bottle of water and a chocolate bar on the desk and a much more confortable bed. The hotel is pretty high tech and eco friendly (this being San Francisco eco friendly is important). Neat eco friendly items: energy efficient light bulbs in all outlets (but not the dim slow to warm up kind...these you couldn't even tell were any different), a special eco setting on the heat/AC that allows you to engage a sensor and if it knows there's no movement in the room it will cycle down the energy use of the heater/AC unit, and what was really cool, an electronic system to notify housekeeping of whether you want to make up the room or not be disturbed....no more of those silly door cards that drop....you just punch the button in your room and it illuminates a light outside). There are some neat amenities like iPod docking station, comfy soft robes and even a bathroom scale. The bath towels are very large and soft....bigger than any hotel towels I've seen in the last decade or so. The room has a huge, excellent flat screen HDTV with plenty of free and PPV options. There is an in room fridge stocks with the typically overpriced drinks and snacks. There's a free coffee maker (Keurig) that brews one cup at a time in a very mess free system. It is located just two blocks from 5th and Market Street which offers a large number of public transit options, including four different rail lines from that location (BART, Muni, Streetcar and Cablecars). You can easily get here from the Airport on BART and only have to walk about two blocks. (The BART fare is only $8.10....a bargain compared to a taxi). It's also easy at that intersection to jump a cable car to Fisherman's Whart ($5 one way) or hop on the street cars ($2) which can take you down Market and down the Embarcadero to eventually end up at the Wharf. But if you want to drive, there is valet options and two self parking lots just one block away ($35/day). It has a good restaurant with an award winning chef and a nice lobby bar. Now some drawbacks.....there's no free internet. It's $14 a day. And, the busienss center charges for everything except printing boarding passes (which are free). The pool is the narrowist I've ever seen. But it is long and ideal for lap swimmers. There are two lanes and if you swin for fitness, you'll love it. If you have kids who want to have fun....it's not that great. The hot tub is nice, though. Public gathering spaces are not abundant immediately inside the lobby. The hotel does have two larger gathering spaces, but they are upstairs and you have to take the elevator. Not a big deal but you can't just loiter easily in the front of the hotel unless you want to sit over the concierges (who are all very, very friendly.....they were great in helping us figure out places to go). The other issue is that the location is just a bit outside of the really active area of SF. If you want to be right in the middle of the action, this might be a few blocks past your confort level, but if you want to be close by without the ruckus....this spot is ideal. But I was most impressed with the overall cleanliness. The hotel still felt brand spanking new. And, this hotel is just a little bit outside

“great staY” Stayed at grand hyatt may 11-13. Chose hotel based on reviews and it lived up to the hype. The hotel was modern, clean, and the service was excellent. Had a corner room on the seventh floor. The bed was comfortable, flat screen lcd tv was just like mine at home and the bathroom was good size for a standard hotel room. The location was extremely convenient for our 11 o'clock in the morning flight home. Travelled all around texas and the location at the airport didnt bother me at all. The staff was courteous and the valet for 25 dollars a day was worth it. Great hotel for the price.

“Good value in a good location, perfect for a work trip.” The suites are well appointed and very well set up for working. Location is an easy walk from Dupont Circle metro and much of downtown DC. Good staff and very comfortable.

“Unbeliveable Value, Caring Management” The Howard Johnson Express in San Jose is a well maintained property. The rooms are good sized with many amenities such as refrigerator, microwave, and safe. They even include bottled water, popcorn, and chips with no charge. Local phone calls are free. The manager Andy Patel is very accomodating. He will make sure to do everything to make sure you are happy. All in all, a great value, under $45.00 with a nice continental breakfast and fruit and coffee available all day. You can even check your e-mail for free in the lobby.

“If you want a W in Chicago - choose the Lakeshore! or even better - the Sofitel!” After having a great stay at the W Lakeshore, we thought we'd give the W City Center a try. BIG MISTAKE! We booked a room with a king bed in the 'Mega' category. We received a Starwood Gold upgrade to an 'Alternative' suite (Room 1201) which had a Queen bed. When I called the welcome desk to enquire if they had any other suites with a King, I was told that they were too busy to speak with me - and they would call me back. 10 minutes later, I was told that ALL of their suites have King beds - and that their engineering dept. must have changed the bed in our room without informing them. (Which sounded a bit like a lie - the bedroom could not accommodate a king bed). We waited another 15 minutes for an 'Ambassador' to come up to our room with keys to another suite (room 601) which had a King bed - but this 'suite' was considerably smaller. (What the W calls a suite at this location is really just two small connecting hotel rooms). It was apparent that our new room hadn't been used in a while - everything was covered in a layer of dust - including the mirror in the parlour room - which someone hand written 'Clean Me' in the dust. We decided to make the best of it and unpacked. The ice machine on the 6th floor was broken, so I had to climb the stairs in search of a working machine. I know that W thinks their dark corridors are 'cool', but when I was wandering the halls looking for an ice machine, I felt unsafe - if their was a fire, how would you be able to see at all? The next morning I was awakened to sound of guest room doors being repeatedly opened and slammed shut. After counting 10 loud door 'SLAMS' - I went out to the hall to see who was doing this - SURPRISE! it was housekeeping! I asked her to to be more courteous - as some people are still sleeping - and she just stared at me - no apology. We decided that we would be happier if we moved to the W Lakeshore - and called downstairs to ask if they could make the arrangements. I was again told that they were too busy to speak with me - and they would call me back. When they did call back - I was told that our rate would not be honoured at the W Lakeshore, nor would we receive an upgrade there. If we wanted a suite at the W Lakeshore it was 750.00 per night. At that point we decided that we were moving to the Sofitel and checked out. Our bill was wrong - double charged for Internet and not billed for parking. They even tried to charge us an 'early check out fee' which they graciously waived. Would NEVER return.

“Ottimo hotel” comincerei con il dire che mi sono trovato molto bene, a partire dallo staff molto cortese ed attento, l'hotel è molto carino, belle stanze,TV da 42", piccola piscina interna, la mattina colazione inclusa con varietà di scelta tra frutta,latte e cereali,pancake,uova,caffè etc... L'albergo è situato a pochi minuti dall'aeroporto e dal seaworld e poco più di 10 dal centro di San Diego,comunque sia nei dintorni si possono trovare svariati fast food e ristoranti messicani(ovviamente) ma io ho preferito quello giapponese,poi Subway ,7 Eleven e così via. Interent è gratuito come credo anche il parcheggio per che volesse noleggiare una macchina. Per chi volesse viaggiare e soggiornare più giorni in questa città non lo metterei forse tra le prime scelte ma solo per una questione logistica di posizione,comunque sia è una scelta che non ve ne farà pentire.

“Best of DC” Stayed here for 2 nights on a business trip to DC. Had a beautiful room that was quiet and comfortable. Was treated well by the friendly staff who was always ready to answer my questions and point us in the right direction. The location is great as the White House is a short walk away and close to many of the other DC sites.

“Super nice” I had a great time staying in this hotel. It is pretty pricey but well worth the money. Rooms are very nice and comfortable. The secret to staying here is to ask for a corner room. Very close to the moscone center (walking distance). Only downfall for me was that it's a little far from union square. But it is close to the metreon which is a plus.

“Difficult to give higher rating” Pre-Arrival: We booked the Hotel via Jet Luxury Resort, who probably had the best rate. Do check back 'cause after I made reservation, the rate went down. The telephone receptionist at the Agency was extremely friendly and helpful, and I was able to get an even lower rate. Before arrival, the Personal Assistant, Kimberly, sent me a e-mail and called me. She sounded extremely friendly and helpful. Knowing we'd be arriving around 6 a.m., she said she'd try to arrange early check-in for us, and had really raised my expectation of the Hotel. On-Arrival: I had to say I was shocked. There was no door-man nor Conciege at the door. This was the very first time we had to carry our own luggages into a five-star hotel! There was only one man at the Front-reception. He did not greet us, and could not retrieve our reservation info. Luckily, I always had the habit to carry a print-out. And of course, our room was NOT ready for check-in, and he, of course, had no clue when our room'd be available. The only thing he could do was to store our luggages. While we were sitting in the lobby planning our day, Kimberly arrived. She was apologetic but insisted early check-in was not guaranteed. She did try to help and offered us breakfast, which we declined. Our Stay: The good thing is, upon our arrival in the evening, our room was indeed ready, and our luggages were already delivered to our room. Most things were perfect - there were welcome fruit, chocolate, cookies, water, and slippers. Things I didn't like : (1) the hand-held shower. The design of the tub and the hand-held shower was extremely poor, and water was inevitably splashed everywhere, drowning the bathroom floor and my slippers were soaked. (2) there was only 1 face towel. (3) coffee-machine area had no lighting, and no instructions on how to use the Nespresso machine. I had to search on the internet. (4) bed was slightly too soft for my liking. (5) Housekeeping quality varied - a few items were not replenished the 1st day, like bath salt, slippers, etc. Everything were replaced the 2nd day. (6) Location of the Hotel was not really that close to the major shopping area on the Fifth Avenue, nor Time Square. Personally, I'd rather stay closer to either one location, and took the sub or taxi to other places. After watching the show, I found it a little bit far away and too quiet to walk back to the Hotel. I could see the Hotel tried very hard to be a five-star Hotel. However, it acted more like a four-star Hotel to me. I couldn't find myself a reason to stay in this Hotel again.

“Best on the Mile” This hotel is truly a top notch property. This was my second stay and I enjoyed this one even more than the first. I was upgraded to a one bedroom suite- if you make a reservation online and are offered an option to upgrade upon check-in, DO IT! For $49 extra, I was given this huge room on the 15th floor. There is nothing I can say that has not been said in previous reviews- this property is outstanding. The only reason I did not give it 4/5 for value is that they do not have a pool. Exercise room, however, is first rate. While running on a treadmill, a staff member was passing out cold water bottles. Combined with the front desk staff, this was among the best hospitality I've received.

“Ridiculously awesome Super 8” I stayed here with my family one night during our move (sadly, out of Austin). After a stressful day of moving, we were hoping for a restful evening. Normally I would not think to book a room at a Super 8, but after checking the reviews here I thought I'd give the South Austin/Airport location a chance. I'm so glad I did. The family running this motel does a superb job. They are friendly, welcoming, and have clearly gone above and beyond the call of duty to put a nice personal touch on the motel. On arrival, the front desk clerk was nice and pointed out the baked goods and other snacks in the front lobby (a small waiting area -- who needs a big empty lobby?), and she assigned our room quickly. She gave us a goody bag with bottled water and snacks - nice touch! We were pleasantly surprised to find ourselves assigned to the "Longhorn Suite," decorated cutely with University of Texas colors and logos. We also had a gigantic flat-screen TV - not the world's best resolution, but fun to watch nonetheless. Our bed was very cushy and we had a quiet night's rest despite being close to the highway. Breakfast the next morning was similar to the typical low-end hotel buffet, but everything was good and fresh, and we enjoyed the added bonus of a fully automated Starbucks coffee machine that makes a variety of very respectable coffee drinks - regular coffee, cappuccinos, and so forth.
