The Texas-shaped waffles were also a cute touch. Check-out was effortless and the generous check-out time meant no rush getting out the door. Had we stayed additional nights we probably would have taken advantage of the up-to-date DVD library or played with the Nintendo Wii they advertised. I will be going back to Austin for business in the future and I know where I will be staying now. Many thanks to Mr. Sam Kumar and his associates at the South Austin Super 8!

“Favorite hotel in DC!” I have previously stayed at the St. Regis and other high end hotels in DC. The Sofitel is by far my favorite. While the location is EXCELLENT, it isn't quite as good as St Regis, but the rooms, service, food, and overall experience far exceeds other hotels. The service is absolutely sensational. The staff is welcoming, helpful, and truly seems to care about it's guests. The rooms are modern and beautifully dressed. I would HIGHLY recommend a stop at Sofitel, you will leave satisfied. Check my review on their restaurant, ICI Bistro, which is excellent.

“Typical Corporate America - unpleasant” We rented this room to watch the Royal Wedding of Prince William and Catherine at 3am in the morning and not disturb our household. The large tv was wonderful. Everything else was average/crummy. The bed is not that comfortable. VERY NOISY from the freeway no matter where your room is situated! Bring earplugs. What I was most upset about was the communication with the maid. We called at 5am before checkout requesting a later checkout. They told us we could stay till 12:30. Well WITH THE SIGN FIRMLY PLANTED IN THE KEY SLOT she barges in at 11:00 am and robs us of our precious sleep. It wrecked our morning. I complained to the management and they did nothing but say sorry... You have to pay extra for parking. There are so many better hotels on this street. I wont stay here again. The Crowne Plaza on the grass side, and the Fashion Valley Doubletree

“Staff made sure we enjoyed our Anniversary” We live in the NYC area and decided to stay in town to celebrate our 10th Anniversary. We booked one of their Junior Suites for a fairly good rate just a couple of days ahead of our stay. I had let the hotel know it was our Anniversary and left a bottle of Champagne and strawberries in our room. Very nice of them. The staff was very friendly and we appreciated their gesture. I work in the area and stay in town a few times a year with either my wife or my wife and children. We' would absolutely stay at the Fitzpatrick again.

“Great stay” Booked through priceline so we thought we would get the worst room in the hotel, not the case. We arrived at 12 lunchtime the lady at reception was very helpfull and we got a room with two double beds. All the staff we had dealings with were very friendly. The pool area was nice and clean and the hotel was in a nice area

“another solid stay” For $83 on Priceline we got a clean an comfortable room, with excellent service at the front desk. Hotel shuttle bus works well to and from airport, and the adjacent Daily Grill's happy hour (4 - 7 pm) is well worth attending if you want great food and drink at a reasonable price. There's a bit of plane noise outside, but nothing that kept me awake at night. We continue to be very happy when we get a four star bid accepted by the Westin Los Angeles Airport.

“A pleasant stay with great service” On my recent cross-country move, I spent two nights at the Courtyard Market Square for a little vacation on the way. The Courtyard fit the bill for a clean, comfortable, convenient, stylish and reasonably priced place to relax. The hotel was done in the new Courtyard design with lots of TV's, seating ares, and a market "bistro" in the lobby. The food was good, but rather pricey and I still missed the old Courtyard breakfast buffet. The room was clean, comfortable, and modern (however, I did had to change rooms after check in since my first room had a strong mildew odor). The service was great, some members of the staff seemed genuinely interested in my well being, and the location was very convenient to the downtown bus loop route (a short ride, but long walk to the Riverwalk). Plus, since I had my bike with me, I discovered the downtown and Riverwalk area was a great place to ride (especially on the weekend) and the hotel was a great starting point. San Antonio is a don't miss town and this is a good choice to stay while in town.

“Beautifully renovated hotel” Stayed here for a conference. Very modern - renovations are wonderful. Only downsides were small size of bathrooms in the rooms & the pillows were too squishy for me. Common areas were great - love the lobby bar. Location is awesome with access to both Michigan Ave & Rush St.

“Probably really a 2 but staff was outstanding” Stayed for 4 nights to attend a business meeting and found e staff to be outstanding. Desk clerks, maids, bell staff, and others were all very friendly and accommodating. Morning wake up call was live, with information on the days weather, and a kind welcome to our nations Capitol. The lobby area is nice and appeared freshly remodeled, the rooms, not so much. I had a king room on the 15th floor and the room was very small. The street noise was unbearable given the single pane windows. Walls were especially thin as you could hear conversations in adjacent rooms. My shower had mold around the top tiles and the room was just generally worn. Rates during my stay were over $300 a night and I saw rates as high as nearly $500. For that price, I really expected better quality.

“Nice boutique hotel” My brother treated his wife and I to a weekend getaway at the Hotel Solamar for our birthdays. Although he'd hoped to secure premium rooms, the hotel was at capacity and we received two standard rooms across the hall from each other on the top floor. The property: This is a new looking and feeling hotel, in a great location for access to Petco Stadium and the good restaurants in the Gaslamp Quarter. The lobby is very nice with fireplaces, comfortable seating and a quiet relaxing vibe. The best feature is the pool deck with its cabanas, bar and seating area. Although the pool is not large and there aren't as many loungers as might be needed for a lot of guests to sun and swim, it is lovely place to spend the day, with a nice selection of food and drinks available and pretty good service most of the time. The standard room: I had a king room facing the pool deck on the top floor. It was a nice enough view of the pool and Petco, as well as the streets of the Gaslamp district. Being able to open the window for some fresh air was a nice little feature, although on Saturday evening, the bar was lively enough that I had to shut the window for some shuteye. With the window closed though, I wasn't bothered by any noise. The bathroom is small with combo tub/show, but pretty and with the necessary conveniences along with nice towels, good shampoos and bath gel and the (best blow dryer ever...) The lighting could be a little better for ladies putting on makeup but other than that, it was fine. The bed was fantastic--The mattress must have been new, but the linens were also perfect. Nice big flat screen TV with many channel choices, but some reception problems from time to time. Closet not huge, but good enough for a few people staying a few nights, and there was also a safe placed in some open shelves in the closet area. Very nice easy chair, and small but serviceable desk with plenty of easy access plugs. Free wireless for joining the Kimpton club (also free.) A cute animal print robe rounds out the room amenities. Look around too for coupons and deals on the bulletin board in the room. We got a discount on breakfast at the hotel restaurant, and my brother had a coupon for a mini bar discount. Everything was clean, good condition and new looking. Housekeeping was terrific. Service was quite pleasant across the board. Everyone was friendly from valet, to front desk, housing and maintenance, hotel bar personnel and cafe staff. I enjoyed the free coffee and newspapers in the AM although we missed the wine social in the afternoon both days. This is a great hotel for business travelers, those who just want some quiet leisure time or someone who wants to explore the city and I highly recommend it.

“Nice .... but PRICEY” Equisitely designed and furnished hotel in the heart of downtown Phoenix. (Unfortunately, the heart of Phoenix is barely beating, and goes into cardiac arrest every day after 4PM ... but I digress ..... ) It is conveniently located next to the Convention Center, but little else of interest. The staff is friendly and courteous. The rooms are very quiet, very clean, and spacious. The beds make you feel like you are sleeping on fluffy clouds. Be forewarned: Not only are the rooms expensive, the hotel further gouges you by charging $12+/day for internet connection - which I find akin to airline baggage fee rip-offs. The food and drinks in the hotel are also outrageously expensive. They only brief relief from the price gouging is during happy hour. The gift shop pricing is nothing less than retail ransom - and there is no other place within a mile to buy snacks, toiletries or sundries.

“Poor Service Wrecks A Great Room” Each time I get on the shuttle, I think to myself I can't believe I accidentally booked this hotel again. The shuttle picks up everyone, not just people staying at the Westin. As a result you are squished onto this shuttle to see none of those people inside at check-in and can see many of them walking away from the hotel. The staff at the hotel are young and act like it with an air that they are too cool. They run around the lobby bumping into guests without saying excuse me and rolling their eyes when they find out you have a package to be delivered. Once you get to your room, all is great as you'd expect from the Westin, but sadly the extra aggravation getting there after a long day of travel is just not worth it.

“Nice Hotel, Better Than Others Close By” I stayed at the Affinia for two nights. As others have mentioned, the attitude and service of the Affinia staff are superlative. I pulled up in a taxi, and the concierge came out to open the cab door with a big "Welcome" to me. The hotel also has doormen, so I was impressed that the concierge did that. The check-in process was very pleasant and quick -- the person at the desk chatted with me for a while about the recent changes to the hotel. I had booked a junior suite; when I got to the room I realized that it bordered on the elevator shaft -- which is something I usually avoid in hotels. In trying to get my room changed, the staff told me that all junior suites are located next to the elevators. They offered to switch me to a different type of room, but I decided to give it a try and found that I could not hear the elevators at all while in the room. The room had a full-size bed, which was fine for one person but might be a squeeze with two trying to sleep there. There was a also a sleeper sofa in the room. The mattress was extremely comfortable. The beds are equipped with feather pillows, but there is also a choice of several other types of pillows if one wants them. These are mentioned in a card that was on the bed when I arrived. The bed had two small focused reading lights attached to it, along with two bedside lamps. One of the reading lights was missing its bulb. I reported it to the front desk the next morning, but this was never replaced during the next day I was there. One of the telephones in the room didn't work when I arrived. It was a cordless phone, and the other one in the room had a cord. I reported the broken phone at the desk the next morning, and that was fixed by the time I came back to the room in the afternoon. The decor in the room was excellent, and of course brand new. The only thing that didn't suit my taste was the orange foil wallpaper covering the bathroom walls. Paired with the round light that was backlighting the mirror, there were odd shadows thrown around when trying to look in the mirror. And, that was the only light in the room. Fortunately, for putting on makeup there was a little sitting area right outside the bathroom that had a small ceiling light and a lighted mirror. So, it all worked out well. The closet had a sensor light that came on most of the times when the door was opened. There was no light switch for it. I found that it turned off at odd times, if I was standing too still in front of it. And it didn't always come on when the door opened. It may have been defective, but I didn't report it. In the closet I found a white terry bathrobe, which is always a nice touch in a hotel room. It was very much appreciated. Others have mentioned the large flat-screen TV that swivels to face the bed or the seating areas in the room. This was one of the best features in the room. Unfortunately, the Channel button on the remote would stick a little when trying to move from one channel to another -- it wasn't a major problem, but I thought it was odd to find this defect in a recently-renovated hotel with such a new television in it. One more thing: the coffee maker had one-cup pods that would go into a cup. This is not my favorite way to have coffee, but it worked out fine. The main problem was that one of the provided cups was filthy one morning. Otherwise, all went well. There was a fully-stocked refrigerator with beverages, and a tray with chips and nuts on it in the room. Prices were posted. I did not try any of them. For those who have problems with stairs, there were three steps in the room. When first entering at the top level, there was a reading desk with telephone and lamp. Then one needed to go down three steps to get into the room itself. Not very many steps, but it might bother some people. One caveat for some, and it is beyond the hotel's control: There is a big construction project currently beginning right next to the hotel, directly to the east. There is going to be a new children's hospital built there as part of the Northwestern hospital system. I heard a little noise once during the day, but it doesn't appear that the construction project is really going very far yet. I expect in the next couple of years there might be a lot more noise next door. But, this shouldn't be a problem on evenings, nights, or weekends -- so for most visits I think it will be fine. And yes, there are ambulance noises related to the large hospital complex a block away. These did not really bother me at all, especially at night.

“Our Favorite Hotel in Chicago right now!” We have stayed at the Wit twice in a Spa King room. The corner rooms in this category are awesome, especially if you can get a deal for around $200. Love the State & Lake restaurant!! And the spa is great- especially the bath cocktails that you can order up to your room. The Wit is by far better than the two W Hotels in this city. The W on Lakeshore is tired and passe, and the City Center W has extreeeemely small rooms.

“Cute well priced boutique hotel” This hotel is about 1 block from Fanuiel Hall and Quincy Market and 1 block from the harbor. So, it is in the touristy area of Boston. The room was unique- exposed brick, industrial lighting, large TV with receiver. There is also a fridge and safe. The great part about the brick is that you don't hear people in the room next to you! There is also a lot of water pressure in the shower- typically something I never find when traveling. You can hear some of the street noise on the weekend, but nothing ear plugs won't resolve (always travel with those!) I thought the price was great considering the area was pretty expensive for November. It is close to several bars- we didn't really find any good restaurants in the area, except when we walked to North End. It was a safe walk. It is also right next to the T.

“Convenient location, old classy style” Location is very convenient for business in downtown - just accross World Bank, IMF, close to State Department, GW University, etc. Nice old style hotel with friendly and competent staff. Spacious rooms - some with kitchenette and fridge. Breakfast for my taste too much old style: ham and eggs, omlettes, sausages; I prefer fruits and musli.

“Very Nice” Great hotel, great location and awesome service. Room didn't have a remote but they brought one up in minutes. Go to Flying Fish down the street, great seafood! Checked in late and the valet was very efficient and courteous. I would definitely come back again!

“Great Value, Clean and Large Rooms” We stayed 3 nights May 2007, selecting Hollywood Celebrity Hotel based on reviews on TA, TA Experts on the Forum and after extensive searching. We wanted location, value, clean and well managed, ease of access. We drove up from San Diego using Google Maps to enter our last lotel location in San Diego to the Hollywood Celebrity Hotel & printed the instructions and maps. This worked GREAT and as a result cut our driving time and we drove right up into the parking lot. We booked on line at their website and got a great rate. We received the room we ordered, which was clean, very large, appointed with 60-70's era furnishings. The room was a low end 3*** in our view - but very acceptable. Toiletries were of a better than everaghe quality. The continental breakfast was basic: muffins, bagels, juice, coffe. No jam etc. There is free parking in the back, but it is as available, and our car was blocked until someone from the hotel came to move it which happened right a way - so no problems. the location of the hotel is incredible - and is the best reason to stay here. The metro is 150 feet through the mall - one stop to Univeral and no hassles to use. Front Desk provided tourist information as requested, but were generally invisable if you were not at the desk. If we were to stay in Hollywood, we would stay here again, it has location, value and is well maintained.

“Nice hotel with great river views” I didn't expect much from the hotel, but was surprised by the hotel and the views my room gave me. The hotel had very convenient parking onsite, and the room was spacious and clean. The only thing about the hotel I didn't like was the location, there simply were very few restaurants open late in the immediate area. Aside from having a tough time with dinner, the hotel was great and I would stay there again if I had the chance.

“Best french fries at Quinns!” Stayed two nights here for the DEMO tech conference in September. Room was mid-sized (if size is a priority, try the Sheraton Suites Symphony Hall) but very comfortable. The wired Internet cost $12 a nite and was on the slow side (maybe I'm spoiled with Verizon FIOs at home), which did impede my work. Amenities were great. Each of the two towers has its own, huge gym (very modern equipment) and pool. I had a burger and fries at the bar, Quinns, and I must say they were very good, esp. the fries (fat, creamy, semi-skinned wedges with just the right amount of seasoning). Location is pretty - right on the water near the airport and rental car places - and great if you want to spend a dirty weekend with a sig other and only occasionally emerge to take leisurely walks along the water. You do need to cab into downtown for a broad food selection, though.

“Good Pick” On the plus side: Great location, very friendly staff, and breathtaking views make this hotel a good choice for both business and pleasure. Impressive lobby and clean rooms. Check out the "View" lounge on the top floor for a drink with an impressive view of the city after dark. Negatives: Beds are stiff and uncomfortable and badly need to be updated to compete with Sheraton, Westin, etc. My room lacked a coffee maker (coffee bar in lobby is probably the reason) and had no minibar.

“Outstanding -- and (surprisingly) a Real Value!” One up side of the down economy is that savvy travelers can enjoy some real bargains. My wife and I recently took advantage of a significant deal offered by The Ritz-Carlton Chicago. The hotel was offering a credit (read: discount!) of $100 per night for guests who stayed a minimum of two nights. Because we planned to drive from Indianapolis after work on Friday anyway, it was perfect: the luxury of the Ritz-Carlton for a room rate of about $25 a night more than we would have spent on a much more modest hotel at the other end of the Magnificent Mile. The service was impeccable. From the bellman who greeted us and took our luggage to our room to the desk clerks, the concierge, and room service attendants, everything was top-flight. The hotel is located in Water Tower Place, kitty-corner from the famous Chicago water tower, across from the John Hancock Building, and adjacent to a shopping mall with the store my wife refers to as her “mother ship”: Macy’s. (Try the Frango mints; they’re a true Chicago treat!) Our room, 2222, was a Deluxe room and included a king bed, easy chair, desk, big-screen TV, huge closet, and a minibar. The room faced south with what real estate agents would describe as a “peek view” of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier, but had shades and curtains that kept the morning sun at bay until we were ready to greet it. The bath was quite large with double sinks; a separate tub and toilet area; generous, fluffy towels; a hair dryer; lighted makeup mirror; robes and slippers; and high-end L’Occitane en Provence amenities. Lounging about in bathrobes, reading the paper, and sipping coffee is a great way to start the day so, on Saturday morning, we decided to treat ourselves to room service. The French Country breakfast consisted of assorted, cured meats and cheeses, artisan bread, a croissant, citrus mostarda, café au lait, and brewed coffee. It was delivered within 1/2 hour of our call and was delicious! Thus fortified, we got ready to head out onto the Magnificent Mile and enjoy some surprisingly glorious November weather. After a day spent doing a little shopping and a lot of wandering through art galleries along the Mag Mile and in the city’s River North neighborhood, we were ready for a nice dinner. Chicago is also home to a number of wonderful dining spots, many are within easy walking distance of the Ritz-Carlton. While my wife and I thoroughly enjoy fine food and aren’t hesitant about paying for it, some of the trendier spots in the area seemed to smack of a “popularity premium,” so we asked one of the concierge staff for other recommendations. The concierge, a member of Les Clef d’Or, recommended a new Mexican restaurant that opened on Kinzie Street in September, just a short cab ride from the hotel. There’s a lot to do in Chicago, from shopping and sightseeing when the weather is good to a broad range of museums, theatres, and other indoor attractions when the weather is bad. I highly recommend considering The Ritz-Carlton as your base of operations, no matter what the weather!

“Luxury hotel ,great location” The Hotel is really a great place to stay. It was very clean . It is located close to the shopping .The room service was excellent and the staff are ver;y helpful. I used the gym and it was unbelievable. New updated equipment. Over all, I had a great trip. The pillows on the bed are down, And the hotel brought me extra pillows and a humidifer. I was very comfortable. The hotel is a little stuffy . Not young atmosphere in the lobby and the dinner in the resturant was very rich, But yet an enjoyable stay.

“A bit disappointing” I stayed here for two nights in February as a break in a cross country train journey from LA to New York (and it is a pity I can't review the Amtrak sleeper as it was brilliant). Anway, the Allegro just didn't do it for me. The service was snarly and it was little things that let it down. At check in we were advised that we were in a king room on a smoking floor. I had requested a twin room on a non-smoking floor and had the confirmation to prove it. I produced the conformation upon request stating that I had booked a twin. From there on the check in process was brutally cold and seemed to drag on forever and involved two people who kept looking at me like I had just ruined their lives. The room was okay except for 4 things. We were on one side of an adjoining room. I don't really want to know what was going on the other side but whatever it was it was incredibly noisy and went on for a long period of time. It sounded like a group of witches and wizards were performing pagan rituals! Secondly, the toilet flush from the floor above produced a roaring sound that was quite interesting the first time but proved capable of waking me from the deepest of sleep. Thirdly, I had to make a call to Australia and as it as snowing outside and was bitterley cold I foolishly decided to use the hotel phone. I know only idiots use hotel phones but I was still shocked to discover that my less than one minute call cost $32.00. Finally, the room service, which we used for a late night snack, was just garbage. The server was obviously disatisfied with her tip as she stood there looking at it for a number of seconds before storming off (it was a perfectly normal tip too). Given the quality and time it took no tip would have been more appropriate. I have stayed at way cheaper places in Chicago (eg. Essex Inn) and come away much more satisfied.

“Great rooms, perfect location for 4th of July fireworks, lots of issues though” First let me start with the positive-- the hotel is beautiful, wonderfully designed and the Marvelous Suite upgrade lived up to it's name-- if only for the fantastic view of the lake and the fireworks. Truly wonderful. Unfortunately, the service in the hotel was nowhere near as good. When we arrrived at the hotel, there was utter chaos in the lobby. There were so many people waiting (to check in? out?) and kids running every which way, no one even greeted us or offered to help with our bags. This is a vast departure from other W experiences I have had. After this we had to wait 20 minutes on line to even attempt to check-in and even though there was a Gold/Platinum SPG line, there was no preference given to elite members. There was an average wait of 5+ minutes (each way) to take the elevator. Particularly in the evening, there was a line stretching out the front door of the hotel, and not a single W employee was in site to guide traffic or assist with the elevators (though the need for such support was clear) and it took 20 minutes of waiting in a hot sweaty queue. We (and many other guests I'm sure) almost missed the fireworks due to this lack of operations management. I realize the hotel was busy with the holiday weekend, but there's only a certain extent to waiting/delays/mismanagement before it becomes unacceptable. On the evening of July 4th, we had to wait an average of 3-4 minutes for someone at the front desk or whatever/whenever to even answer the phone. Also-- there was no corkscrew in our room (crazy when 3 types of beverages requiring one are sold in the minibar) and it took 2 calls and 45 minutes to get one. Later, room service took an hour. Crazy! Finally there were a few issues with the room that made it apparent that housekeeping was not giving their full attention-- the main light in the room (large floor lamp) wasn't working, the TV in the bedroom had its volume limited to about half of the maximum which would be fine except for the fact that the A/C unit was about as twice as loud as that (so impossible to hear TV). The batteries in the bathroom scales were also dead. And the thermostats in the room were completely wacky-- no matter how high we made the temperature, the compressor/AC kept coming on until we were about frozen out. In sum, while our suite was wonderful, the service we experienced was not up to SPG or W Hotel standards. Perhaps it would be better on a regular day that isn't July 4th.

“The best in San Antonio” I have had to be in San Antonio 3 or 4 times over the past year or so and have stayed a couple of different places. The last 2 times [within the past 45 days or so] I have stayed at the Mokara Hotel. By far, the pick of the litter in San Antonio. I travel externsively for business and pleasure and what impressed me the most about the Mokara is the warm and professional staff there. Some places you stay yo get the canned lines like "my pleasure" or :have a nice day." Each of the last 2 times I have been there I felt an unusual real, sincere desire to serve from all I met; from check in to the valet. The rooms, especially the ones on the river are large and clean. I can't speak or rate the spa or restaurants, but I highly recommend this hotel. Thanks!

“Depressing, but good location. Good for Last Resort.” I traveled from out of town to Philadelphia for a few days and after one night, I decided to just go home. There were several mixed reviews about the property, but at the time I was not worried because I am generally pretty minimalistic and easy to please at a hotel, especially knowing that I will only be there for 8 hours of sleep. It couldn’t be terrible, right? Hmm... Situated next to a homeless shelter near the “rougher” part of town, the Travelodge looks everything but inviting. Once I arrive at the check-in counter after a long day, all I want to do is get into my PJs and go to bed. I then notice that the property looks more like a warehouse than a hotel, and 80% of the rooms in the hotel do not have an exterior window. I politely requested a room with an exterior window, saying I really enjoy natural light, especially when I had to wake up super early. The woman at check in said that there weren’t any rooms with windows available. I sighed, but accepted that I’ll be having to experience my first windowless room that night. When I got to my room, it felt anything but comfortable. It was very dated, stale, depressing, had irritating florescent light, a prison window with lovely views of the hallway, thin blankets filled with holes, and my sink was less than a foot from the bed. Was I in a hospital? No, I’m just living my worst hotel experience to date. OK well there were a few perks: since I walked, I didn’t have to pay for on-site parking ($18), there was free wifi, and the bathroom was surprisingly very clean. The exterior of the Travelodge Philadelphia Convention Center I didn’t sleep well that night (who would have thought?). The next night, I ditched the hotel idea all together ended up making the 4-hour round trip commute home just to sleep in my own bed for a few hours. For the complete review including pictures, please visit my blog post at : http://boardingarea.com/blogs/justanotherpointstraveler/2012/05/05/unintended-use-of-wyndham-rewards-points-actorproblems/

“Nice retreat from the hustle and bustle of midtown” I stayed at this Ritz for 3 nights with my husband for my 40th birthday celebration. I come to NY several times a year, and we always stay in midtown or uptown. I decided for a change of scenery, we would try the Ritz at Battery Park. It is a lovely location, right on the waterfront. The evenings were quiet, and perfect for a relaxing stroll after dinner. We had a Harbor view room overlooking the Statue of Liberty, which was very special. The hotel is beautiful...definitely up to the Ritz standards. Service was always helpful and friendly, and there was nothing the staff wouldn't do to accomodate us. This is the Ritz though, and everything is pricey. It was painful to pay $350 for a 1 hour couples massage, although the spa was nice, and the massage was excellent. Breakfast in bed was $90 (1 order of waffles and an order of poached eggs). Dinner in the dining room downstairs was $185 for 2. Unless it is a special occasion, or you are on an expense account, the prices really sting. My weekend was a splurge, so I tried not to let it bother me. Battery Park is located right near the financial district. It is not the most exciting part of town. I was looking for a quiet, relaxing weekend, and I got it. The downside is, we had to take the subway, or a cab everywhere. There is not much in Battery Park to do. My favorite restaurants, shopping and museums are all uptown. Even the Village and Soho are not really walking distance. That will probably affect my decision whether to stay there again or not. I like being able to walk outside my hotel, and having everything right outside my door. The room was very nice and the bed was incredibly comfortable. The bathroom was very large for a NYC hotel room. Housekeeping and room service were friendly, professional, quick and efficient. The conceirge was always right on target with directions and recommendations, and the front desk staff was top notch.

“Spacious room, great location, bathroom needed work” We stayed here for four nights on a recent trip to NYC. I chose the hotel based on the location and Tripadvisor reviews. The location was pretty convenient for a first trip to the city. The staff was helpful. We were allowed to check in early and the concierge gave us good directions a few times. The rooms was large for NYC and comfortable. Though the bed slept very hot we slept well and the linens were clean. The bathroom was tiny and the towels always smelled really mildewy. I think the hotel needs to take a look at how they are drying them because it was pretty gross. Bathroom is also dated with wallpaper. Overall we had a nice stay but I will probably shop around to see what else I can get at this price point next time I'm in NYC.

“grande e comodo” Abbiamo trascorso due giorni di passaggio in questo hotel molto grande ma al tempo stesso molto ben posizionato, elegante ed efficiente. Stanze molto grandi e un servizio di biglietteria per gli spettacoli dedicato. Hotel certamente moderno ma non privo di stile. E' vicino a moltissimi luoghi interessanti e non è molto caro. Bello e suggestivo l'ultimo piano lounge - bar e ristorante che ruota lentamente e dal quale puoi ammirare tutta la città.

“One of the best views of Boston ever!” We were pleasantly surprised by the Sheraton. It's a conference hotel and we never saw the lobby not crowded with people coming and going, but the check-in staff was quick and efficient. And remarkably courteous and helpful. We asked for a room with a view and were given a fabulous view of the Charles River and the Back Bay from the 23rd floor. Very nice touch. If the room weren't so small, I'd have given the Sheraton even better marks. We had a very nice stay and we loved the location. Very close to the T station and all the neighborhood attractions. I wouldn't mind staying at this Sheraton again!

“A Good Place” I havent stayed here in years, the place has obviously gone through some renovations. Everything was nice, clean and comfortable. Great Sleep Number Bed, awesome sheets, pillows and comforter. Staff was friendly and courteous. Only issue is there is nothing nearby, you have to travel a long ways to find a decent restaurant. But that seems to be the way with most places in San Jose.

“Good location and great concierge.” We made a last minute booking during fashion week and were pleased to get a room at a hotel with a good rating on Trip Advisor. We received a very warm welcome from the reception staff and some good recommendations from the most helpful and professional concierge. The location is good, just a couple of long blocks over to 5th Avenue. We asked for a quiet room and were told that we had been upgraded. The bed was very comfortable and the room was quiet but there was very little, if any, natural light through the tiny window.The room wasn't particularly special so I wonder how we would have felt without the so-called upgrade- or is this a ploy to make guests more positively disposed to grotty rooms if they have been told that they have been upgraded? Even my husband who is sensitive to all noise wondered whether we had made the right choice to go for an inner room, especially when we discovered that we could hear our neighbour's conversations through the interconnecting door. The bathroom has possibly escaped the renovations but there was a large bath and nice amenities. We like to try out different hotels in New York and this one was about average. We would like to have tried the restaurant but it was closed for renovations.

“Great hotel” The hotel was great and very convenient location. It was very clean and affordable. The rooms were big and the front desk staff was very helpful and courteous. They were very helpful with any requests and also gave me a free upgrade to suite.. Parking was little bad but overall great. Will definitely stay again.

“Nice place why cheap it on the wifi” This was a really nice hotel and we liked being close to everything near the downtown. Why, thought do they cheap it on the wifi? I just don't get why expensive hotels don't do free wifi when a Best Western can do that. Even the lobby was a fee and they make Starbucks charge too. Just silly.

“Godd & bad....” Great staff & location. Size of the room was a plus as well. The downside was the street noise from L street was very loud even 10 stories up.The elevators were a bit slow & the room & parts of the hotel could use some paint. The big issue though was the AC. It was unseasonably warm in DC and the first 2 nights even though the AC was cranking out cool ( not cold ) air I could not get the room below 80. I complained after the first night but they were unable to fix the problem or move me. Good value for the location & if the AC wasn't an issue I'd book there again without a second thought.

“Could Have Been Better. . . .” My boyfriend and I stayed at this property, without knowing the "Mortocycle Convention" was in town. The hotel is located next to a Waffle House, and the motorcycle attendees were driving in and out of the Waffle House lot, literally blaring their stereos through all hours of the night (2am and 3am!). I sleep with ear-plugs and I was woken up twice. Again, not the hotels fault. And the woman at the front desk could not have been nicer (gave us free breakfast coupons which we SLEPT through!) and she actually called the police twice. This aside, the location is great. Very close to the I-17, which was perfect for us as we live in Sedona. The rooms are spacious. There were some stains on the wall and carpet in the room. And the pillows were not that comfortable. Also, the mini-fridge was "off" when we arrived in the room (to save energy consumption?). I would prefer the setting be kept low, so we could put our perishables in the fridge immediately. Instead we kept them in our freezer bags. I would be willing to give the hotel another try, but I would strong recommend ASKING if there is a motorcycle convention in town before booking at this hotel.
“中心にある豪華ホテル” 立地はニューヨークの中心で、どこへ行くにも便利です。ホテルのロビーは広く、豪華にできています。部屋は古めですが、清潔感があります。バスルームもやや狭いですが、ヨーロッパ調でおしゃれに出来ています。エアコンの音がやや気になりましたが、部屋の設備等は豪華です。フロントも混雑していますが、対応も丁寧でフレンドリーです。

“Getting away with murder” I have stayed in this hotel five times in the last ten years. It has gotten worse, for reasons most likely related to the management and onwner-occupied suites on the upper floors. The female concierge is aggressive and offensive. At my last trip I complained about the broken locks, cracked tub, etc. The man at the front desk actually said, "That's the kind of room you get if you book through a hotel consolidator." This hotel needs to be updated, and the staff needs to understand that travellers, especially to New York, Central Park South, expect to be treated in a decent manner. I will never return to this hotel, unless, of course, it is upgraded, and a change of ownership occurs. It doesn't matter if you get a decent rate -- it's not worth the con! Plenty of hotels exist in similar price ranges, with properly furbished rooms, and pleasant staff.

“Great reasonable find!!” We stayed here for three nights. Free internet and continental breakfast. Very friendly staff. The room was clean and large. Great location. Had a very European feel which was very nice.

“Expected More” We expected more from the St. Regis having stayed at these properties in Rome and Monarch Beach. The location is great for business or pleasure, just a few blocks from the White House. The rooms however are quite small. Our bathroom was cramped and did not even have a tub. The service was just ok. We booked a package and they could not locate it and still had trouble even after we showed them the reservation print-out. That being said, the hotel was just renovated and re-opened in January of '08 so everything is fresh. I much preferred the Sofitel a block away, better rooms and much better service.

“Loved the Millenium” We stayed at this property for four nights in February. The employees couldn't have been more helpful (with the exception of the restaurant staff). Upon arrival, the front desk was friendly, courteous and informative. My husband's a diamond member, so we were upgraded to a Junior Suite, with complementary breakfast vouchers. The room was wonderful - actually two rooms, with a plasma tv, luxurious king bed with soft, quality linens and a housekeeping staff that couldn't have been more efficient. The room had a view of Ground Zero - this didn't bother us at all. It is quite sobering but also uplifting in seeing the way New Yorkers seem to be able to handle anything they're given. My respect and admiration truly goes out to the people of this city - it is truly the greatest city on earth! The consierge couldn't have been more helpful - any question you presented him with he answered, or at least tried. Elevators were prompt - rarely had to wait at all, going up or down. Yes, the lobby is small and the lounge could be a bit larger, but if this is the only thing wrong - please. The location of this hotel is just fine - a subway station 100 feet from the entrance. The subways are quite safe and a great way to get around, but if you're subway-shy, taxi's are abundant all around this hotel. However, we found it difficult getting one - we were there when the weather was quite cold and they all seemed to be occupied! So the subway it was, with no problems at all. Being downtown, I agree with a previous review wholeheartedly - it is quiet down here and away from the craziness of Times Square - you couldn't pay me to stay there! My only complaint towards this hotel is the miserable, bored, unhappy, unpleasant wait staff in the restaurant. And the breakfast ...... if we had to pay for that food....something like $29/person for a breakfast buffet that was as cold as ice coming directly from the kitchen! The eggs were stone cold, as was the bacon, sausage, potatoes, etc. My advice - go somewhere else - anywhere else - for breakfast. Never gave lunch or dinner a chance - too many other great restaurants in this city. We are planning another trip this April and we already have reservations to return here. This is a great hotel in a great city and I highly recommend it!

“Good Place to Stay for a trip to Dallas” Stayed here as part of my rest nights in Dallas, Texas. Being a Best Western, is symbol of good quality. Hotel had plenty of good parking nearby. Easy to find off the Freeway. A Denny's across the street in case you are hungry. Location, I was able to walk to downtown and the American Airline Center within under 20 minutes from here. Room was nice and clean and I could access the pool from the patio door. Very nice. Morning had a nice complimentary breakfast of toast, bananas, juice, coffee etc. There is good fast Internet here WIFI And good computer terminal. There is good pool outside with a clean hot tub. Check in was fast and efficent. Front desk service was very good and quick. Staff were very friendly and helpful. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who wants quality but nothing special to stay at. Overall when in the area. I recommend you all to come and check this gem out. Thanks

“EXCELLENT LOCATION, NICE LARGE ROOMS, CLEAN” Stay here if you are doing Broadway. We saw several plays including the Book of Mormon, Lion King and Million Dollar Quartet. The latter was our favorite. Also saw Karen Akers at the Algonquin Oak Room. A bit boring and I would skip this because although she can sing the music sounded pretty much all the same with little variation in the Sondheim songs she sang. Sights we saw on this trip included Frick Art Museum (great Fragonard room, Gainsborough portraits, Italian masters); The Cloisters, owned and run by The Met, with wonderful antiquities from cloisters of 13-16th century in Europe; also good tours at The Cloisters. Guggenheim, great but the spiral path that leads from the top that was F.L Wright's signature piece here, was closed; check on this before you go there. Whitney Museum, really disappointing and pales by comparison to The Met, MOMA, Guggehheim, etc. Go to Chelsea to walk along The High Line, a fun little hike, go to Eataly afterwards for a wonderful gastronomic lunch at the pasta restaurant; EATALY NY 200 5th Avenue New York, NY 10010. entrances on 5th avenue and 23rd street. The Met is always special and if you go to the Cloisters you get in free at the Met that day; we always enjoy the Impressionist collection at The Met but everything is pretty special here. If you stay at the Marriott Marquis, definitely go to dinner along 45th Street Restaurant Row, including Le Rivage (French) and Lattazani (Italian). Many other choices along this area as well. If you have questions, definitely stop at the concierge desk for advice or reservations at restaurants or attractions.

“Fab location, excellent price” This hotel is a great place to stay for people not wanting to spend over the odds just to be in Times Square, it is only 10 blocks away, about a 10/15 minute walk. The rooms were spacious and we actually had a view of the Empire State Building from our room. Free coffee, OJ and muffins in the lobby at breakfast was a great start to the day.

“Nice resort, away from downtown” The hotel is about 30 minutes from the airport, but an easy drive (you want a car this far out). The grounds of the hotel are beautiful, there are pathways through the golf course with patches of desert that come alive with animals in the evening. There are at least 4 pools, so it is easy to find a quiet one. The cheaper (though not cheap) restaurants in the resort aren't that exciting (Splash, Blue Sage) but the Italian restaurant and Roy's are excellent (I left my credit card at the Italian restaurant, and it was promptly returned). Rooms are very nice, flat screen tvs, fairly spacious (though my view was of the roof of the convention center). There was a balcony off of the room. There is a large and growing shopping area across the street (there is a shuttle from the resort, but a car is much more convenient), so you don't need to eat in the expensive hotel restaurants. I was there for a convention, so it was nice to be able to take the elevator from the down to the meeting. I would consider staying here again if visiting Phoenix (though I didn't find Phoenix that exciting).

“Great bang for your buck, right in the heart of Magnificent Mile” Stayed 2 nights for business, the location is great, its right off Michigan behind the John Hancock Tower and Water Tower Shops. Big suite, flat screen TV (that wasn't as clear as it should be), sofa/bed in living room, nice sized bathroom (drain was rather slow to clear in the shower but otherwise fine). Overall given the low rate I got it was a tremendous value. Nice rooftop indoor pool/health center too. Would suggest going around the corner to The Saloon Steakhouse for dinner, its a gem! My biggest complaint with Hilton is they charge $12.95/day for in room internet access (yet their Hampton Inn brand gives it to you free), come on Hilton at least give your HHonors members a break!

“Excellent Property, Friendly Staff, Great Location” We were in Washington D.C. in April 2012 for a few days vacation. We were fortunate enough to get an upgrade of a room at the Fairmont. It is a modern hotel with an historic feel. The lounge in the lobby is a great spot for a night cap and a quick bite of some locally produced food. The Juniper Restaurant has a great menu and you can dine outside in the quadrangle or in the nicely decorated dining room. The hotel is an easy walk to the Foggy Bottom subway stop. The subway is a great way to get around pretty much anywhere in the city. You can easily get to the Fairmont from the Reagan International Airport by subway. The hotel is near a neat little breakfast place just a half block south. There is a grocery store about a block and a half away called Trader Joe's where you can pick up a little something for the room. Fairmont Hotels are great choices when you travel. I recommend that you join the Fairmont President's Club so that you can take advantage of the extras available. It doesn't take many stays before you make your way to the higher tiers of the programme.

“Nothing outstanding but nice Westin” I had to wait quite awhile to get a government rate at this hotel, but I finally succeeded with only a few days left to go before my conference. At government rate, this is an exceptional hotel. At the typical rate, it's a very nice Westin but nothing outstanding about it. Location is as good as you can find in Chicago - convenient to everything and near some wonderful shopping and restaurants. The room was nice and large, bathroom was nice (despite a bit of a spider problem), fitness center was just average (especially considering the size of this hotel), and service was OK. I say service was OK because staff were kind and friendly, but the lines to ask questions, check in and check out were always long - even for Gold and Platinum members. I'm a Starwood Gold member and can report that I didn't get a thing for my Gold status except perhaps a better view. I wasn't put on a Gold member floor, although I found the hotel had one. I'm an optimist and keep hoping I'll get something for my Starwood Gold membership, but so far it's all been pretty much of a sham. I'd stay at this hotel again, if I were able to get a reasonable rate on the room.

“Friendly staff, nice rooms, good neighborhood, loved bar next door” Usually stay on Upper West Side, but the rate I got thru Priceline was so good, and the TripAdvisor reviews so glowing, had to check out Affinia Dumont. Well, TripAdvisor reviewers are right on the money - as usual. I stayed at Affinia for two nights. Arrived at about 1:30p and was able to check in immediately. I did not like my first room and was able to change with no trouble (or attitude). The front desk staff was lovely and housekeeping and bellmen were friendly. My room was nothing fancy, but for NYC it was very large - even had a kitchen. Large writing desk and comfy beds. No view in room #1106 (unless you count the fire in building behind hotel that I smelled and watched all night). The shower had really good pressure. Aveda products. So-so counter space in bathroom. Room was clean and in good repair. Pretty quiet for a hotel in this area. The #6 subway is just a few blocks away and it's an easy walk to midtown/Penn Station/Macy's. My flight was not until 8:30pm and I was able to easily stash my bags for the day. The Barking Dog is the restaurant next to the hotel. Yummy food, good drinks and really terrific company at the bar. I was traveling by myself and owner George, his crew, and local (colorful) clientele made me feel right at home. The nail salon across the street - Spa Meridian - did a really nice pedicure for $26. If was the perfect way to end a day full of walking.

“Great location and good service” I stay here often when in Indianapolis. Nice gym, pool in the lower lobby. Breakfast is great. I loved the little extras. Room was very nice and very clean. Hotel staff is very friendly and upbeat. Close to a lot of really good restaurants and a shopping area.

“FANTASTIC Hotel, Wonderful Location” We just returned from several days stay at The James. It's only two blocks from Michigan Avenue- Maginificent Mile. Bathroom is stocked with Khiel's products, decorated in very clean lines. The staff couldn't be nicer. We got a very quiet room at the end of the hall- easy to walk either to Michigan Avenue, Millenium Park or to catch the "L"/CTA/Metra. I would definitely return and highly recommend this hotel. The bed is SO comfortable.

“Low rates for fairly decent stay” This hotel is on just the edge of the downtown area. Its about a 5-6 block walk to the inner harbor area, about 9-10 blocks to the Convention Center and Camden Yards. I do not consider this a safe walk after dark, but during the day its fine. The front desk staff, for the most part, was good about calling a cab when I needed one and were generally quite pleasant. The hotel is nicely decored and comfortable, and for the rate $79.00 it was well appointed and has a daily complementary breakfast. The issues with this hotel are that there is only 1 elevator which takes forever to arrive. The air conditioners are iffy; the one in the room worked but blew the coldest air ever, and there was no air in the hallways. Additionally, considering tis location I expected he hotel to have a courtesy shuttle. For the first 3 days of my stay, I did not see one nor was I offered. On the next to last day, I saw a shuttle but was told that it was only available for guests who were going to Johns Hopkins hospital, that it wasn't available to any other paying guests. I was troubled by this considering the location of the hotel and the short distance to so many other tourist locations in the area. Lastly, although the property advertises free wireless internet it is nearly impossible to access it and the instructions to get access are NOT user friendly. Also note that there is a small parking lot just next to the hotel, but it costs $15 a day. Ultimately, I would possibly stay again (if I couldn't get a decent/better rate at some of the closer hotels), but I will be prepared to get what I pay for.
“Nice but overpriced” It's blue, it's neon, it's trendy - just pricey! Room was small but that's New York...

“Great stay at the Days Inn - CT Avenue” Stayed here from June 21 thru June 26. Great value for the hotel. It is a basic hotel but considering the little amount that we were in the room, it was perfect. Hotel was very clean. The staff was definitely attentive. There are 3 computers to use in the lobby with a good internet connection. Positives Price 5 minute walk to the subway Negatives Not much around for breakfast options. Not much in the immediate area for drinks except for the Italian Restaurant next door (while the bar was good and plenty of fun, variety would be better) It is a longer subway ride to downtown. You have to change trains to get to Smithsonian. While seamless, it does take time to get there. You need to accommodate this in your itinerary

“Good example of a Westin” This hotel has a great downtown location, a beautiful lobby, very nice rooms and pleasant staff. It was certainly above average, but a little short of excellent, though. Major issue: Simply put, the internet service sucked. At the lobby it's free, but it's soooooo slow that make you want to scream. You're better off crossing the street to a Starbucks or something. In the room, it's even worse, it keeps dropping and refusing to connect again. Oh, and you're paying top dollar for it! The service was so bad that in the end the hotel actually didn't charge me. I hope people soon realize tha free wi-fi should be a standard service for any 4 or 5 star hotel. Stop nickel and diming... Minor issue 1: The TV was pretty nice and it was the only hotel I've been with HD. Wow! Problems was, due to the way they setup the room, the TV was so far away from the bed that I could hardly see what was going on, it was like trying to watch a 10' TV. It had so much potential... Minor Issue 2: The restaurant was, at best, ok. The food wasn't bad and the service was pleasant, but the menu has like 5 item on it Really? Yep, they couldn't offer much, it was either this, that or the other. A little more freedom of choice wouldn't hurt... Overall, the good things far outweight the bad, so I'd definitely recommend it.

“Switched from a Hyatt mid-trip and loved it!” Superb location. Very lively and happening lobby area with a cool bar and restaurant. Had a great room for a great rate that looked down upon Michigan Avenue. Can't wait to go back to Chicago and stay here!

“Fine for a night or two” We were in town for a couple days visiting family. This made for a good home base while we drove around Indy. Hotel is older and needs to be updated, but rooms are clean and staff is friendly. It's very close to the airport and reasonably priced. The free continental breakfast was great with cereal, eggs, waffles, fruit, bagels, etc. There isn’t a restaurant on onsite, but next door at the Adam’s Mark is the Marker Sports Bar/Restaurant. The Adam’s Mark also has a small convenience store. Besides that, not much else within walking distance.

“Great Views, Clean Room, Convenient Walk To L.A. Live” As a preface, I travel to a limited degree to review rock concerts, and have begun to include hotel and resort reviews as well, which I am republishing here is modified form. This review is for The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites in Los Angeles, during my recent Los Angeles Trip (February 2012). Room Type/Class: Traditional Room Date: February 7-10, 2012 Overall Rating: 4/5 This trip was explicitly to attend two concert events - one at Club Nokia and the other one in Hollywood. I lived and worked in Los Angeles for many years while I was in graduate school, so I'm really familiar with it. Since Club Nokia is part of L.A. Live, I thought it made sense to find a hotel that is within walking distance of L.A. Live, which put me downtown. I considered the Marriott and the Ritz-Carlton that are part of L.A. Live, but they were much more expensive compared with The Westin Bonaventure's Hotwire price. I ended up deciphering a "hidden" discounted offering on one website to purchase on another, and found that The Westin Bonaventure was the hotel being offered within that class range for a highly discounted cost off the base rate, and booked it. So the hotel has valet parking, but it is an additional $35 per night. If you don't mind walking a block or two, I noticed that there appeared to be some other public parking alternatives that would be cheaper; I ended up using the valet, which is underground and you walk down a hallway adorned with movie poster one sheets of films shot at and around the hotel (see photos below), and up an escalator toward the main entry level where the front desk is located. Check-in was quick and otherwise unremarkable. I had originally booked two nights, but one of my events was canceled and rescheduled... I asked if I could add a night at the discounted price, and was told they couldn't sell rooms at that price, but the guy at the front desk looked in his computer to see their occupancy for the desired night, and more or less indicated that if I went on that reseller website again, I would likely be able to add the third night at the same reduced rate (when I went up to my room, I was able to do this and add it on). I was actually really excited to check out the elevators, as there is a scene with Arnold Schwarzenegger in True Lies where he goes up one of the elevators on horseback; the gentleman at the front desk was able to direct me to the exact elevator I was seeking. As for the room itself, I had the basic/base room, and was pleased that it was on one of the higher floors (better views). While on the small side, it was very clean and nicely appointed, as I've learned to expect from Westin properties. Maybe because it is an older property, the shower and bed are maybe not as "Heavenly" as some other Westin properties, but overall the room suited my needs perfectly (traveling alone) with king-sized bed and computer desk. Internet connectivity via WiFi was good but not spectacular. For me, the best bonus of the room was the view. Most of the outward facing wall is glass floor to ceiling, as the view was spectacular, particularly at night. There are some amenities in the hotel that I just didn't have the time to use - restaurant, bar, etc. As noted, I had come to L.A. for a concert at L.A. Live, and found that it was definitely a reasonable walking distance from the Westin Bonaventure - maybe too far for some people's taste, but I walked back and forth several times and I don't think it took more 15 minutes. Overall, I don't have any complaints at all, though it would be nice if valet parking was included, but I knew from my research ahead of time that was a cost to factor into the overall value proposition of the stay. When I attend a future event at L.A. Live, I would likely return to the Bonaventure, unless there is a special deal at one of the competing properties.

“Large modern rooms... good luck getting a view” I stayed here for a few days on business and the property was gorgeous and well kept. The rooms were very large, I will say the light switches in the room were a little odd. The room is by far the largest hotel room I have stayed in while visiting Manhattan. One other problem with my stay was they cant seem to keep room keys programmed. Every time I returned to my room I had to go get new keys. If I return I would fight for a room with a view of central park when checking in. My room was facing a brick wall of other guest rooms.

“Great new hotel - Perfect location” I spent labor day weekend at this Hilton and it was an absolutely the right choice. Hotel opened in 2000 and it's still well maintain and in a great shape. I got a room on 3rd floor [317] and really recommend this room for anyone. This room has a nice view to the pool and also convention center plus coronado bridge. Lavazza coffee is good. Bathroom products are from CrabTree. Location couldn't be better. - trolley is right there! [orange line] - Petco Staduim is about a block - Gaslamp quarter with ton of shops and restaurants - convention center is right across the street Room was quite small but clean and I like 42" TV (^__^) Front desk and bell boy were very helpful. The room wasn't ready when I got there and the front desk guy even offered to call me and let me know when room is ready. He also gave me a room with sofa bed too! Bell boy also gave me the map and tips to explore San Diego. Pool and fitness room are on 2nd floor. Outdoor pool area was really nice! I was worried at first to have a room facing train tracks for both MTS and Amtrak. Hilton has earplugs ready for guests but I didn't really need to use it. I can hear the train noise on my second night but it wasn't too loud to wake me up anyway. few cons; parking $35/night, no breakfast, free wired internet - wifi only available in lobby area. This is my first visit to San Diego and I really had a good time staying at this hotel. I would recommend Hilton Gaslamp to anyone (business traveler, sport fan, tourist, foodies, bar hopper etc. ) for it's location, room quality and everything else : )

“Fabulous boutique hotel-perfect location” Stayed at the Dana for the second time this past weekend and again had a wonderful time. The floor to ceiling windows are amazing overlooking the city. The staff is very friendly and very attentive. Had an initial problem with the wireless but they moved me a different (and better!) room and it was fine. Room service is great as are the beds and amenities. Highly recommend if you're planning a trip to the windy city!

“Best bet in the downtown area” I have stayed at this hotel for business many times but finally took the family for a weekend of fun. The rooms are always very clean and roomy - much roomier than any other NYC hotel for certain. I love the amenities such as the coffee, tea, cookies etc...that are available in the lobby and also the wine at night. The mini bar is all free except alcohol - and although it may sound trivial, it is nice to be able to reach in and grab sparkling water or a juice without giving it any thought. It is a real convenience. I also think this is one of the quietest hotels there is in the city. It's great if you are looking to see the Statue of Liberty or 9 11 memorial. Everything else requires you to travel uptown but I still think it's a great hotel and would highly recommend.

“Struttura e posizione invidiabili ma le camere sono vecchie” Nel ventre di Manhattan, un hotel unico e spettacolare (le ascensori che salgono e scendono sono tutte di cristallo). Purtroppo le camere sono molto vecchie e quindi non esattamente in linea con quanto si spende!!!

“Renaissance Washington Nice Rooms but Service Could Improve” I stayed three nights at this hotel in mid-April. I got a rate of $159.00 which included a full breakfast which is excellent for D.C. The hotel is very clean, attractive, and comfortable. It is a large and busy hotel and does not have a sense of intimacy or warmth. Despite the large number of people staying at the hotel, services were well-organized and operated efficiently. The location is great. I walked to the National Mall in about 15 - 20 Minutes. The National Portrait Gallery is very close and it is re-opening July 2006 after renovations. It is directly across from the convention center. There is a Red Line Metro stop 3 blocks from the hotel: Gallery Place/Chinatown. I requested and received an over-sized corner king room. It was huge - - about 500 - 600 sq feet with a nice sitting area and work area. The breakfast was excellent although a bit crowded. The staff handled the heavy volume very well, however, and there were only a couple of short waits for a table. Although the cafe was totally full each morning with lots of children, there were never problems getting to the buffet or the omelet/ waffle station. I did not have any problems with staff members, but most of them just didn't seem to go beyond the minimum. No one was rude, they just didn't seem to enjoy their work and put anything extra into their efforts. This hotel, however, is a great value and I would stay here again if I received a good rate.

“Mixed Experiences” When I arrived at this hotel, my colleague had inadvertently booked me in for the wrong week and hence I did not have a reservation. The hotel was full due to the rodeo and they did not have a room available for the first night of my planned stay, but due to my HHonors status and the fact that I was scheduled to be there for a full week, they pushed me through in the computer and put me in a suite, which I greatly appreciated after a day of travel. The room was OK, but sorely outdated. It reminded me a bit of the decor in the original movie Wall Street mixed with your standard Chinese restaurant. The room service food was really bad, although the lady who delivered it was nice. One day I put my netbook and my jewelry into the in-room safe and when I came back that evening, the safe was jammed and I couldn't get it to open. They sent maintenance up to fix it and sent a security guard with him, and the two looked and acted like a duo from a bad comedy about inept hotel employees. When the safe was finally opened, the security guard demanded that I tell him exactly what was in it, and when I hesitated, he started to reach in to grab my belongings! Eventually I capitulated just to get him out of my room, but I cannot see why I should have to disclose the private contents of my safe just because they had an equipment malfunction! I would have been happy to sign off that everything I had put in there was still there, but his police-like attitude was too much. The lighting in the bathroom was horrible, and the heat lamp only stayed on for 60 seconds at a time and made an absurd amount of noise. Very convenient to the medical center, but I probably would not stay here again if I could avoid it.

“Better room than last visit” Our last visit to this hotel wasn't up to previous standards but we decided to give it another chance. And this trip was fine. On our last visit we had issues with the air conditioner and toilet in our room, but there were no problems on our recent 3-night stay. As has always been the case when we have stayed here, the room is clean, the service is friendly, the breakfast is handled well, etc. We like having a separate sitting room in case one of us is up earlier than the other and wants to work. The free internet service works well and there is a comfortable desk and office chair. I have read other reviews from guests who had problems with noisy air conditioners (cycling off and on very loudly all night), so there must be a handful of rooms with problems. Given that most of our visits have been positive and this hotel is conveniently located to Rice University (and the medical centers), we will stay here again. But we'll probably check the air conditioner when we get to the room to see if it is a loud one and request a move if it is. Otherwise, this is a very good hotel for its class: clean, friendly, reasonably priced and with generously sized rooms.

“Shiny and bright hotel, let down by bad service” I agree with those recent reviewers who have identified service problems at this hotel. At best, I would say that it is inconsistent. The bell desk, valet parking, housekeeping, and restaurant staff were all very pleasant and helpful. The front desk staff, however, were largely unhelpful, slow, and in at least one instance, unprofessional. Check in took longer than usual, as the person checking us in had to consult with her supervisor on multiple occasions to ask what seemed to be fairly routine questions. We were using a "buy one, get one weekend night free" certificate (from IC's Ambassador program), and the supervisor actually complained out loud about how customers with these certificates never give the hotel any advance notice about using them. She actually voiced this complaint to our faces. I thought that was highly unprofessional, especially since that is how the "buy one, get one" program is supposed to work: customers are not asked to provide advance notice about using the certificates. In the end, even though we had originally booked a room rate that was supposed to include breakfast, the supervisor informed us that we would not be getting breakfast on the second day because we were using the free certificate. Although I can understand the logic behind this policy, the information was conveyed to us in a rather unpleasant and haughty manner by the supervisor, which left a bad taste in my mouth. Check out also took longer than usual. Even though there were only three people in line, it ended up taking nearly 15 minutes for the front desk staff (two different people from the check-in pair) to get to us. Without making eye contact, the front-desk agent mumbled an apology about the wait. Not a big deal, but another illustration of the amateurish level of service -- and probable lack of adequate training -- in some of the front-desk staff. The hotel itself is quite shiny and bright. The rooms, as others have mentioned, were spotless and relatively spacious, with nice views over the city. The bathrooms are large, with a separate shower and tub. The location is very convenient to Union Square and the Moscone Convention Center, although the tradeoff is that you are farther away from the more classically "San Franciscan" neighborhoods such as Nob Hill, North Beach, and Russian Hill. (For a first-time visitor to the city, I would recommend one of the Fisherman's Wharf or Nob Hill hotels over this location, but for a repeat visitor, this location is just fine.) The breakfast buffet in the main restaurant is excellent, with a well-prepared array of dishes. The gym is also well-equipped and spacious. Notwithstanding the solid "hard product," the bad service from the front-desk staff left me with less than warm feelings for the hotel as a whole, and it will make think twice about booking another stay here.

“Pretty Bad” I am a 26 year old male who was traveling by myself to suprise family, I am used to 'nicer' hotels and the wellington does not meet any standard of 'nice'. I took the wellington with a grain of salt as it was one night. If I was traveling with a family I honestly would have been irate, its a nice hotel from the front but the rooms/lobby are simply not ok. The lobby was 3 star at best the room 1 star. I have family who is from europe and they said it was bad but 'ok' compared to a hostel in europe. I figure thats what makes this hotels rating a three, the European vote drags it up. The hotel is not an American 3 star, its a 1920`s no remodel star at best. These are the five main problems. 1) first was booked into a room in which you must travel down some back stairs to get to an elevator. The elevator area is simply gross, peeling wall paper, stained and loose carpeting. The room was seriously tiny to the point I was scared. I have traveled throughout Asia and NOTHING was this small, no more than 150 square feet if that. 2) I was switched to a new room a 'suite' this suite sure wasn't sweet thats for sure. The floors in this hotel are tiny, my sister who visited referred to it as jail size and I thought that was nice. When you exit the elevator the wall is no more than 2.5 feet in front of you. The carpeting, doors and walls in the hall of the 16th floor are simply not acceptable. The room I was sent to was creepy, looks like it hasn't been upgraded for at least 40 years. I seriously regretted having watched the move "room 1408" cause I was a bit scared. There were missing lights loose wiring and drapes that made a 70`s porno look classy. 3) The bedding is gross, I honestly slept with a shirt on to avoid bugs. I am not a picky guy but this place was really bad, I actually brought family over so we could laugh at the room. 4) The elevator is slow as hell and honestly the oldest and most terrible one I have been in for awhile. I was a bit hesitant and considered taking the stairs 16 stories to avoid the 10 minute wait and 3 minute ride in that bucket o crap. 5) for the price the hotel i switched to The Park Central was a blessing and 50 bucks a night less The park central was wonderful, clean remodeled room, clean bathroom, new carpet etc. The staff was great lobby new, fast elevators etc. I couldn't take pictures cause I was to busy laughing at my ill fate and trying to avoid loose wiring, I apologize.

“Very close to SeaTac Airport with reliable shuttle” I had never heard of a Red Lion Hotel chain before and was not sure what to expect, especially when i read some variable reviews on tripadvisor. However, this hotel exceeded my expectations. The room was very clean, had obviously been updated with granite desktops and countertops in the bathroom. I found the beds very comfy. We stayed here because we had an early morning flight and it was just perfect for that. They have a 24 hour free shuttle that departs every 10 minutes. This hotel is very close to airport. Here is a tip that saved us some money. Our last night in Seattle and we wanted to eat downtown. After dinner, instead of taking a taxi back to the Red Lion, we caught a Grayline Airport Shuttle for $11 each and then walked 5-10 min from airport to hotel.

“grand” Excellent hotel, fine location, good staff and service, the food was fine, the sports bar was a great hagn out. The room was good, nice view, good working space and clean. I enjoyed my stay and will be back. The place didn't feel crowded even while it was full for conventions during my stay, the staff remained friendly and helpfull, and very nice.

“Get Away Weekend- With the Kids” I stay at the Houston Hilton on Post Oak quite often. Usually when I need to take my car over to Houston to be serviced. The hotel is located smack dab in the center of the Galleria area, within walking distance of some of the best restaurants and shopping in the world. Each room in the Post Oak Hilton has a balcony either looking over Post Oak, or Over towards the Galleria. We have stayed in the Junior suite many times before, and it is perfect if we bring along the kids. The living room has a sleeper sofa in it, and plenty of room for any additional roll away bed as well. There is a nice little bar area with a microwave and a refrigerator off of the living room. Again this is great when traveling with kids who always want a snack. Having the storage space keeps the snacks wrangled to its own area thereby keeping the room much neater. The Bedroom is large and has a large En-suite dressing area with a normal sized bathroom attached to that. The service in the hotel is top rate. The pool area feels like a roof top pool and it is well maintained. There is no bar, but periodically a server will pass through and offer to get you a cocktail or bring up room service. The food is good although we have never had more than a burger by the pool. The surrounding restaurants make it difficult to want to eat in.

“Great location for one night - walk distance to the terminals” I stayed at Radisson only for one night comming from Honolulu at midnight and leaving next day at noon. The hotel is almost IN the terminals but you can not hear even a tone from the aircrafts - very good sound-proof.... but only outside. The walls are very thin and you should expect to be waked up if your neibourgh should catch his early flight. There are some shops about 500 feet from the hotel and you can get almost everything to eat or drink... or you can visit the hotel restaurant. The stuff is was very friendly and helpfull, only the rooms furnishing ist old and need to be changed but the rooms are very clean. Free Wifi Internet is availible and very good

“Should have Stayed at the Marriott across the street!” While the staff at the Crowne Plaza are friendly, the property is old and not well maintained. The rooms are extremely small for LA. We are in a room with two beds, and the beds are barely big enough for two people. The bathroom is tiny and outdated. The internet connection has been down for two days with no estimate for when it will be up again, so the staff have sent us across the street to the Marriott Beverly Hills to use their internet. If I had to plan the trip again, I would have stayed at the Marriott...it's much nicer than the Crowne Plaza.

“Good, but Slipping a Bit” Have stayed at this hotel many times over the past several years and generally was impressed, but less impressed this time. We had a double occupancy room on the third floor and our bathroom sink fixtures leaked water, persistently flooding the counter top with each hand washing. The toilet seat was loose on the base, imperiling the occupant to falling off the side. Another emblem of the lack of attention to detail: We checked in on a Saturday, and many of the apples available in the large bowl in the lobby were rotten. Like, brown and unambiguously mushy. Yuck! Not a good way to greet your guests upon check in. Nonetheless, on the plus side the desk agent was able to accommodate our request for an early check-in and the linens were clean...We always tear apart the beds in NYC hotels to guard against six-legged bed guests, and everything checked out great. Good, affordable breakfasts can be had at the area diners on 8th and 9th Avenues if you're not into the carbohydrate fest of the hotel breakfast.

“Excellent Location, Slightly Overpriced for the Amenities” This hotel is located in a perfect spot with quick access to the Red Line. I was shocked to find they didn't have flat screen tvs in the rooms, the valet parking next door was slow and tried to overcharge me when I went to leave. Late night front desk staff were less than accomodating. I am undecided on whether I would stay here again or not.
