“Slice of heaven for a weary traveler” I stayed at the Sofitel for one night of a hectic business trip. I was upgraded to a larger room upon arrival. The bedding and shower were amazing. The hotel offered several bonuses for business travelers- direct dial phone number and they did not charge for my incoming faxes. I have stayed at several other D.C.-area hotels and the Sofitel was the best thus far. I will stay again.

“Alt-ehrwuerdiges Hotel, nun aber zu touristisch” Das Waldorf=Astoria ist wohl eines der Urgesteine der New Yorker Hotelwelt, vielleicht sogar eines der bekanntesten Hotels der Welt. Das Hotel blickt auf eine mehr als hundertjaehrige spannende Geschichte zurueck, die uebrigens in einer sehr interessanten Dokumentation zu sehen ist, die im Hotelfernsehen laeuft. Das Hotel ist riesig, erstreckt sich - mit allen Saelen und Konferenzraeumen - ueber einen ganzen Hauserblock zwischen Park und Lexington Avenues. Als Gold-Member von Hilton Honors bekam ich ein (kostenpflichtiges) Upgrade in eine kleine Suite angeboten, welches war annahmen. Die Suite hatte zwei Zimmer, war aber nicht sonderlich spannend, ausser dass es ein Eckzimmer war, allerdings ohne interessante Aussicht. Wir hatten zuvor eine andere Suite angeboten bekommen, die hatte nur ein Zimmer und den Blick in einen haesslichen Innenhof, war kleiner und dunkel, die lehnten wir ab. Es war auch nicht einfach, die groessere Suite zu bekommen, das Hotelpersonal war wenig entgegenkommend. Man merkt im ganzen Hotel, dass es einfach "alt' ist, es lebt vom historischen Ruf, scheint aber inzwischen hauptsaechlich von Touristenhorden bevoelkert zu werden. Eine (allerdings recht negative) Ueberraschung war der Fruehstuecksgutschein, den wir als Gold-Mitglieder bekamen. Er war fuer ein "Fruehstueck" im Starbucks-Café, das im Hotel untergebracht ist, und bestand aus einem Gebaeck, einem Saft und einem Kaffee oder Tee. Das Café hat keine Sitzgelegenheiten, nur ein paar Barhocker an der Wand, und ist sehr klein. Ich konnte es kaum fassen, dass es ein Starbucks im Waldorf gibt, und dass das Hotel seinen besten Kunden einen solchen Voucher gibt. Das Fruehstueck im Hotelrestaurant ist aber auch sehr teuer. Alles in allem, ein Besuch in einem "Grande Dame" Hotel, aber nicht mehr. Fuer den Preis gibt es in New York erheblich bessere und elegantere Hotels.
“Another great Kimpton hotel” I quite enjoyed my stay at the Hotel Palomar in Dallas; wish I could have stayed longer. Room was a decent size and the hotel was lovely--very quiet and comfortable.

“Good location, great rooms” Our eleventh visit to New York but our first at the Chandler. We have stayed at many hotels in the city including big chains such as Novotel, Radisson as well as some independent boutiques. The Chandler is a four star independent and is simply the BEST hotel we have used in New York. It is a three minute walk to the Empire State Building and Macy's, so close to mid-town Manhattan but in a pretty quiet location. The room that we had on the tenth floor was immaculate and really modern. The bathroom was new, contemporary and again spotless. No bath but big glass double shower cubicle. The room wasn't huge but was big enough with plenty of storage. Good sized wall mounted LCD TV and a good quality I-pod docking station. We had one breakfast free of charge that was ok, usual thing - juices, cereals, breads, pastries etc. The hotel provides free tea and coffee making facilities in the foyer all day which is a nice touch. We chose to take breakfast on other mornings at a deli around the corner on Park Avenue rather than pay the hotel prices. We found the front desk staff really helpful, courteous and polite. When we booked we had requested a double room, non-smoking on a high floor and that is exactly what we got but with an upgrade without even asking or having to pay more. We found the hotel quiet, relaxing and in great condition throughout. All in all we genuinely feel that this is the best hotel that we have used in New York and it will be our first choice when we (inevitably) return in 2010. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. Dave and Jacqui.

“Cassa Hotel - comfortable and well located” Stayed here for one night. Very comfortable room. Excellent room amenities and a nice breakfast in the morning. Not super cheap (where in NYC is?) but definitely a hotel I would re-book and return to.

“Problems at check in, but won me over with mints” Girls trip to Chicago booked through Expedia by friend's husband for a suprise 40th birthday trip. The lobby is very classy and has character so we were impressed when we wallked in. Went to check in everything seemed ok, asked for a room with a water view and we were on our way. After getting to our room the front desk called and said the credit card had not gone through and we had to come back down. We thought a good time to ask about the water view considering the only place we could see the water was standing at the far window and craning your neck. When we went back down, my friend was not treated very well since they kept acting like her credit card was no good. After 45 minutes they realized it was their computer system, not her card. They then asked for $200 cash deposit, they were doing her favor because it should have been $300 for the 3 nights of stay. Luckily she had that much cash. I thought this entire situation was handled very poorly. First they made her out to look like a person with out credit then they demanded cash. Instead of saying you are already checked in we will deal with the issues when our computers come back up. Less than an hour passed and they called to say the system was up and the card went through and she could come down to get her cash. The clerk realized that it would be nice if he brought the cash up, so he did. Thank you! The room was nice and comfortable. The bathroom was very large and clean, the only problem was the sliding door that most people have commented about. The bed only had a duvet, so this was problem with temperature control. Too hot with cover on but nothing lighter to cover up with so then you would be cold. A sheet would have been nice. I realized most people don't stay in their room at night and play games but we did and we only had a very little table to put between the beds to play on. The hotel was quiet, the halls and the outside noise. We took advantage of the fridge and microwave. The location was fine. We actually enjoyed the walk. The red line L stop is also close to the hotel. Very easy to get to Wrigley. On our second night we got back to the lobby and I asked if they had any chocolate mints in the gift shop because I had a craving for mint. They said no but then another clerk asked what room we were in. Five minutes later he was at the door with a handful of mints from the club lounge. That is service! Iron Chef Jose Garces has a very nice Barcelona tapas style restaurant in the lobby, Mercat a la Planxa. We stopped in our last night and went to the bar. Kenny the bartender was the best! We enjoyed some tapas, sangria and a few custom drinks by Kenny. A very nice way to end our stay. On a side note Echo Limosuines provided us with great service to and from ORD.

“Ok for a one-night stay” If you need to spend a night in Denver for a connecting flight this is a good alternative. It’s located a 5-10 min drive from the airport. There is a shuttle going back and forth every 30 min, but we took a taxi. We arrived quite late and was surprised to see a huge line to check-in. I understand that airlines use this motel if there are delays or cancelations so I guess that is why these large groups of people suddenly appear here. You get what you pay for and you don’t pay much at Super 8 motel. It was a quiet room with a good bed. It was worn and the air-condition was loud, but kept the room nice and cool. Breakfast is included, but I was not impressed. There is a restaurant just across the street that serves fantastic breakfast all day. There is also free internet with ok speed included. I have no issues recommending this hotel for a one-night stay.

“I-5 never sleeps.” This imposing hotel rises right beside Interstate 5, and if you get a room facing east the ceaseless traffic noise from the highway will intrude no matter how good your ear plugs are. That being said, rooms are comfortable and nicely appointed, with comfy bedding, lots of different pillows, yummy Aveda bath products and a no-fog mirror in the bathroom. Full breakfast is available ($$$) or you can have a continental Starbucks for 7 dollars and change in the lounge. Self park your car for a mere $30 under the hotel and bring your own snacks or pay a whopping $3 for a bottle of water which you will reach for in desparation because the frigobar in your room is otherwise empty. The R-view rooftop restaurant is, unfortunately, closed Sundays. Do what you can to work a discount at the Renaissance Seattle, whether CAA, senior, military or whatever or expect to pay over $200 per night.

“Great suite stay with times square view” We stayed in a great suite at the W Times Square. It was spacious and was fabulous for three guests because there was a divider that separated the living room from the bedroom so there was privacy between the two rooms. There were also large flat screen TVs in both rooms which was great. The room was dim and had little light but that didn't bother us. However, one tv was fuzzy and a bathroom light was burned out and it took three phone calls to the front desk on three different occasions over 2 days to get them to actually show up and fix them. That being said, we really enjoyed our stay and the fabulous W bed!

“Did not exceed expectations” The James Hotel is a small modern hotel. Views are very limited in this hotel, it is not a tall hotel and building is blocked on three sides with large buildings. Courtyard view is poor and makes you feel a little depressing. The staff were nice but check-in did not go smoothly. We checked in at 7pm and were told our room was not ready... and then had to wait another 20min. We booked a "loft suite" but by no means was this a suite. Suite's usually are 1 bdroom separated by a door. this was not the case. It was also not a "loft" Loft = high ceilings, exposed beams, exposed brick walls, and large windows. The television by the bed did not work. The projector in the "media" room also did not work. There were only three towels in the bathroom. At around $385 for the room, I expected more.

“Good location, nice rooms, a bit noisy” Fantastic location for exploring San Francisco, and not as manky as the neighborhood where the other two SF Hilton's are. The onsite restaurant was a bit of a surprise--- much better than the usual hotel restaurant fare and while it's a bit pricey to dine in the hotel, it's on par with hotel dining anywhere. Beds are comfortable and the room was perfectly clean. All staff was helpful, friendly and professional. The only negative was that, like many older hotels, there's a fair bit of hallway noise (I can deal with street noise in an urban setting), and their big event space attracts lots of large groups which can translate to noisy neighbors, but one call to the front desk usually gets things calmed down. Executive lounge was comfortable, well-appointed but a bit small for the size of the hotel so time your visit accordingly. Great views from the lounge and from our room! Overall we were happy with our stay and will be happy to stay again.

“Great hotel for a visit to OSU” Over the past three months my daughter and I have visited OSU twice. Both times we have stayed at the Hyatt Place Columbus/OSU. This is a modern, comfortable hotel that feels very urban. The lobby is warm and inviting yet cutting edge. The guest rooms are huge and offer a comfortable sleeper sofa (a comfortable sleeper is so hard to find in hotels!) as well as comfortable beds. The decor, again, is modern but comfortable. The breakfast is delicious although food ordered from the kitchen takes a very long time and when they run out of items on the buffet, it takes a long time for them to be refilled. The staff could not be nicer but they need to work on their directions to surrounding attractions. On our first visit in April, no one at the front desk could give us directions to the OSU campus. On this visit, only one of the three staff at the front desk could explain how to get to German Village. Perhaps the hotel should print out directions to these important locations then hand them out to visitors. Just a suggestion... Overall, this is a great hotel. If my daughter chooses to attend OSU, I will be staying here often! Moms

“Great service, great fun to stay in Soho” I spent a weekend here between business trips and loved it. It is so fun to stay downtown, rather than in midtown and this is a happening. What impressed most was the restaurant. Seven of us had dinner on Saturday night - local friends and me. I had bad luck. First,I ordered an appetizer that they ran out of and I had to pick again - no problem at all for me but they insisted the appetizer I choose is on the house for my inconvenience. Then I pick a wine they ran out of and when I select a different bottle (again, no problem - such things do not bug me), the waitress advised that dessert for the entire table is on the house. Wow. One free appetizer and seven free desserts and we get great food and great service. Oh and yes, for a real NY moment - even a celebrity spotting - Ivanka Trump and husband were in the lobby - she was dressed early for Halloween a Wonder Woman and he as Captain America (and when we were leaving dinner they had changed and were leaving the hotel in regular clothing. Comfortable room, great location, super service. What else could I ask for? I was sad to jump in a cab on Sunday with my bag and head to the New York Palace to be closer to work.

“Okay...” Traveled here on business. Rooms were outdated (popcorn ceilings) and bathrooms were old. Bad shower pressure and when I arrived the side of the sheet had something that looked like blood. Now the good... Very nice staff and service! Gym was decent and nice outdoor pool. Location is good, and my room was a very nice size. They also have a refrigerator and microwave.

“Very nice” Stayed here last weekend with another couple. We loved everything about this hotel. The service was wonderful, friendly, and very helpful. The room was charming and oh so comfortable. Floors 7 and up are a little nicer, ask for those. The restaurant was excellent (so was Pizano's down the street) The had a nice little wine reception every night. Very close to Millennium Park and the "bean". Couple blocks form the river and the start of the Magnificent mile. Easy walk to Sears tower. What else can I say!

“Great stay, wonderful architecture” This is a true gem. They have done a great job preserving the features of the Customs House. The rooms were huge and comfortable. There were full kitchens and a seperated bedroom for comfort. It was also 2 blocks from Fanueil Hall. Can't beat the location.

“Sweet Home -- Chicago” I had a work trip scheduled and decided to bring my wife and 2 year old and spend an extra night in downtown Chicago. We had been wanting to stay at the WA here and it did not disappoint. The location was convenient being right off of Michigan Ave, walking distance of all the shopping. An added benefit was how quiet it was not right in the middle of Michigan Ave. Regarding the cleanliness, in a word spotless. The room we had reserved was the Deluxe queen – which was a nice sized room with two queen beds, private bar, full closet, separate bathroom with closed off shower and toilet. Plenty of room for our pack and play and stroller. We did eat breakfast in the restaurant, which was adequate but we were not overly impressed with quality of food. The steel cut oats our son had were phenomenal but the salmon lox and also the spinach omelet – were subpar, we would have preferred a diner breakfast over ours. The lounge had a good selection of scotches for the scotch aficionado, coupled with a pleasant atmosphere and with the benefit knowledgeable bartenders. - Amenities: Complimentary coffee – amazing. Gym, spa, locker room – kept very clean, easily accessible and well-trained staff. - Staff: All of the staff members – restaurant workers, turn down assistant, bell man, check in desk - all staff members were over the top friendly. This was our first time at a Chicago hotel to encounter such a polite staff. The only con we had was asking the front desk guy for a dinner recommendation and he wrote down the wrong address. We took a cab about five minutes in the wrong direction and back. - Clientele: Well heeled for the most part. We were surprised at how many kids there were at such a nice hotel.

“check your bill carefully” This is a very nice facility for a conference. We were given a corner suite which was very nice. The bed was comfortable and the view was good. WiFi cost was $10.00 per day. There is no pool or workout room so we had to go to their other hotel a block away. Since I often have a child with me this would be a problem. The bathroom is very stylish but the lighting at the sink is dim. The room was very quiet as far as street noise but hallway noise was sometimes a problem. No gift shop to purchase any necessities or snacks (again a problem when travelling with a child). I had to go to the IGA 5 blocks away to buy snacks and a salad. When I took out some cans in the minibar to put the small salad in, the sensors showed I had taken the mini bar items, even though they were put back in. My company got the bill and paid it then asked me about the minibar charges. I did get it straightened out but it was annoying to have to hassle with it. I also used the Elaia Spa at the Olive 8 Hyatt and charged it to my room. Yikes...the room charge was 42.00 higher than the charge slip I had...so I had to get that taken care of. It was however, the best massage I have ever had and probably the worst manicure I've ever had. Because I am in Seattle 4 or more times a year I have stayed at many of the downtown upscale hotels. I had stayed at The Grand Hyatt one other time. For the money there are better places in my opinion...especially if you have a child. I will return to one of the others next time.

“Nice modern decor in a good location” My wife and I did a one-night staycation here on a Saturday night. We were pleasantly surprised with the modern décor of the room and the pretty good-sized bathroom. The halls on the floor were much bigger than in several Holiday Inn Expresses we have stayed at in NYC so we did not experience any claustrophobia. The bathroom was also much larger. It is easy to see why the Holiday Inns are a step up from the Holiday Inn Express hotels in the chain. The staff was pleasant and the street was quiet, but a short walk to excitement. We will likely stay here again.

“You do live in a hotel.” Spent Christmas night here on our way to visit family. Decided to stop and take in the King Tut exhibit; booked a suite with the King Tut package. The reason for my review title is this-people, you chose to live in a hotel, so don't act all put out when hotel guests are on the premises. This was a nice splurge for Christmas night, but I doubt I would stay here again. The front desk staff, bellman, etc. were fine, but no one really went out of their way. The room was nice, but nothing special. When in our living room we could hear the guests in the next room. The bathroom was better than your standard hotel, but nothing to write home about. Dinner at Fearings was the highlight of the visit. The staff made us feel as if they were happy we were there. We had breakfast there the next morning and the staff was again very hospitable.

“Quality Inn on Westheimer - Quality should not be in the name. The roaches are taking over.” "Roach Motel". Stayed here because I've stayed here before and it was ok, it's amazing how a place can change in a years time. The place was run down like the management or owners don't care. And I saw many roaches(5 my first day), not a good feeling. Pool was murky, tiles in walkways missing, walkways had build up of dirt and could have used a good sweeping or maybe even power washed. Holes in the bedroom walls, empty frames hanging in room, even a bracket with nothing on it. Ice Machine was so dirty, believe that is a Health Dept violation. My last day talked with someone at front desk and they said their changing the name of hotel, I can see why. Sometimes felt like I was the only one staying there, only 2 cars in lot. I would never stay here again.

“Nice but needs a refurb” I stayed here twice this fall due to Loews First Benefits. Both times I stayed in a Suite. The suite was roomy with a queen size bed and little master bath and a sitting room with couch and powder room. The check in area is fancy enough. The staff was adequate (other than housekeeping issues which seems to be a product of recession and I'm find at other four and five star hotels..I guess this is where they cut back) Anyway, the rooms are old looking and need to be gutted. Bathroom shower clogged. Bathroom toilet running. Stains on carpets and couches. Not totally gross and it was clean but not worth the $500 plus rates this place gets. I've stayed at worse in NYC but I've also stayed in better, nicer looking rooms for less in NYC lately. A lot of the boutique hotels and many of the chains such as the New York Hilton and the Crown Plaza times square might not be as fancy but the rooms are cleaner and newer. Service was adequate. Love the heaters over the bell area outside so you don't freeze when waiting for a cab. Also, another note, I stay in hotels all of the time but the room service here may be the most expensive that I 've ever seen. Bring in food or walk around the corner to Lexington for a bite or you'll pay big. I'd stay here again as the location on the upper east side is great. The hotel was quiet and the bed comfy so sleeping was great. I'd only stay though if I could get a great rate as this fading property is no 4 or 5 star as it would like to be.

“Nice Classic Hotel” I just spent two nights at the Hamilton on business. This hotel is exactly what it claims to be a, a restored classic. Yes the elevators are slow, and the rooms are small, but the staff is professional and courteous, the rooms are well appointed and it is in a great location. A few things I didn’t like – the view out of my room was of an office building about 20 feet away (a little weird seeing people working that close to your room), showers both mornings at 7:00 with only warm water (it was very hot at all other times), and the wireless internet connection is $9.95 per 24-hour period, but you don’t charge it to your room, it goes on a credit card (makes it a pain for travel claims). ome other reviewers mentioned the traffic/street noise, but I didn’t notice it much after rush hour. The hotel is in a great location a block away from the McPherson Square Metro station, and there are numerous restaurants ranging from inexpensive to very expensive within walking distance. I would stay here again for business or with my wife. Rooms may be a tad small for any more than two people.

“Nice hotel for family but avoid for business trips” If you are coming for a vacation this hotel is perfect - amazing views, great location. It is not that good for business - business center lacks a lot of functionality, slow elevators, etc

“Perfectly serviceable hotel” We used Priceline and got this hotel. Check-in was impersonal. We requested a room with a King bed and we were accommodated. The room was attractive and comfortable, and noise was minimal. I would stay here again. Minor quibbles: there was no fan in bathroom, so the mirror would fog up and could not be used after showering. We noticed blood drops on the curtain. The sheet was a bit small for the bed. Pool is smallish. No jacuzzi/hot tub.

“Great Hotel” What a wonderful hotel! Great ambience. Just steps off Michigan Avenue. A quick walk to the free trolley stop. The rooms are elegantly appointed and very clean. The Concierge was wonderful in making dinner reservations and suggesting tours. The best part was being a block from the Oak Street Beach in the middle of July. The perfect place to take a dip on a hot July day. Enjoy.

“luxurious experience/probably not great for kids” Loved it! Take a look at the very comprehensive review by Dessup of Pittsburg for a listing of all the little amenities that have been so thoughtfully provided. We booked through a bargain outlet and were still given a room with a partial harborview. It was named one of the best places to work in Boston, and I can see that reflected in the relaxed, yet professional way that the employees conduct themselves. All tips are included which employees readily volunteer. Obviously, someone is doing something right as they all seem to be genuinely helpful and welcoming, All in all, a heavenly experience. One small quibble is that the pool is a lap pool. Just three lanes of humans swimming round and round. No chances of floating around and just enjoying the water. This would not be a good place to take the kids. The pool area is very nice and the health club swanky with classes happening.

“a little taste of old Philadelphia” This is a wonderful old house that dates back to the earliest days of Philadelphia. Our room (3 floor walk up!) was spacious and while not extravagant, very nice. The bathroom had both a shower and separate tub. The TV was circa 1975 but if youre looking for a hotel room based on the tv, you wont like this place anyway. Continental breakfast included; great place to chat with other guests. The location is right in the middle of society hill. Independence Hall 2 blocks away; Walnut Street Theater around the corner. Super restaurants in every direction.

“Passe but OK” Well, the upsides are that the rate is low and it includes breakfast (good) and supper (poor). There is a jacuzzi in the room but we wouldn't have used it on a bet. This is a "has been" hotel that must have been super at its prime. Another plus is free onsite parking. Coffee always available and cookies. What's not to like? Shabbiness. We had some concern about possible bed bugs (bites under the knee of one of us). This is not the place we would choose but it was the hotel included in our conference arrangements...did the world come to a screeching halt? No. But this is not top of the line. And for that couple that wrote to say they spent their wonderful honeymoon here...well, we hope for them better experiences!

“Excellent Value and an Excellent Location” My girlfriend and I stayed at The Michelangelo on Good Friday and received a terrific rate of $199 for their standard room. As soon as we entered the hotel we were blown away by the design of the hotel's lobby. There was a small snafu while checking in as my nightly rate was quoted as $295. I pointed out the difference in price to the attendant and it was immediately corrected when he looked at my original reservation files and saw that I did, in fact, book the room at $199. He was courteous the entire time and made sure we were aware of the hotel's free breakfast. I did have to remind him that I was a member of iPrefer and that I received a late check-out, among other things that I never received/used. iPrefer members are supposed to receive free Wi-Fi and complimentary upgrades at all Preferred Hotel Group properties. I never needed the Wi-Fi and I looked at the hotel's reservation page earlier in the week and saw that the only room type available was a suite. I knew the upgrade wasn't going to happen. Maybe I was upgraded, who knows? We were also pleasantly surprised by the size of rooms. We previously stayed at the Hotel Chandler, which is a very nice hotel but is also extremely small even after being upgraded. At The Michelangelo we had plenty of room to walk around and not bump into each other or anything. The rooms are well appointed and the bed is very comfortable. Our view was of the HVAC, but that didn't really bother us. If you want to see New York City, you go outside and do it! I think the hotel needs to update their TVs to what most hotels consider standards, meaning HD-TVs. The TV in the bathroom that most people rave about is about a foot long with a three inch screen size and an ANTENNA! But, this is New York City, who stays in and watches TV? The only amenity that I took advantage of was the overnight shoe shine. My shoes came back the next morning looking better then they ever have. Hats off to whoever shines the shoes at The Michelangelo. At turn down, the housekeeping staff pulled down the blackout shades and when I woke up at 11 I was confused as to why it was so dark outside. Thanks to my oversleeping (like I said, the beds are really comfortable), we missed the free breakfast so I won't be able to comment on the food at the hotel. I was shocked at how reasonable the mini-bar prices were. I think it was $7 for a Jack Daniels. If I went to a NYC bar for a Jack Daniels it would be at least $10. My girlfriend left a bag of moisturizer and face cream in the hotel room and we didn't realize it until Sunday. I called the hotel to ask if housekeeping found it and was assured that someone would call me back immediately. Two weeks went by and I never heard from them. I called them back to ask again and was told that someone would check and call me back again. I waited about a few hours and called back and they said nothing was found but that they will ask the person that cleaned my room the next day. The people that I talked to were always very courteous and I'm sure they were going out of their way for me, it just would have been nice to have been called back the first time. With all of that said, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone. The room was well worth the $199 rate and I would stay there again in a heartbeat for that price. I think the rooms are easily worth $400 a night, but those prices are out of my range.

“Luxury in Downtown Seattle” The Pan Pacific is most luxurious, from the large scale of the rooms to the quality of the furnishings. The bed is incredibly comfortable and the bathroom is larger than some NYC apartments. The staff is also exceptional, and the property is located near great restaurants and convenient shops, including a large Whole Foods below the hotel. I'd definitely stay here again.

“Great night's sleep - convenient location” We spent the night after arriving on a late night flight on our way to Canada. Check-in was quick and relatively painless - overall service in the hotel is friendly and prompt. Room was large and well appointed - the bed was extremely comfortable and the bathroom clean with plenty of towels. Price was $115.00 for the night which seemed extremely reasonable given the upscale nature of the hotel and the convenience. Prices at the bar and restaurant were on the high side, but on par with other restaurants in the airport terminal. Would recommend if arriving late or leaving early (or both).

“Accommodations for tall people! And at a great location!” Stayed at the Monaco for four nights in late August. Loved that it had creative décor and a boutique feel, but was actually a large chain with great service. The location was perfect - a block from the 16th street mall downtown. Walking distance to lots of restaurants, bars and shops – and even Coors field. Definitely recommend it if it’s your first time to Denver and you want to walk to a lot of the nightlife. The best part of our stay is that we were able to reserve a “tall” room. It had an extra-long king bed and a raised showerhead. My husband, who is 6’5” tall, has never been able to stretch out on a hotel bed, and he was in heaven here. I’d definitely recommend the Monaco for tall travelers. I will say, though, that the extra-long bed was in a room that was already not spacious, so it was a little snug. Parking was pretty expensive - $24 a night – but the valets were always available and were very friendly and helpful. Actually, all the staff was friendly and went out of their way to greet us. We loved that they’ll bring you a goldfish to keep you company during your stay – that was a quirky, unique thing that made the hotel stand out. If we were looking for a hotel in downtown Denver for another stay, we’d choose the Monaco again.

“Avoid The W and its Hostile Staff” Beautiful rooms, but the worst service ever. We were there for a party in the ballroom and stayed the night. Valet left us standing in the cold, so we carried our own bags upstairs. Not typically a big deal, but we paid a total of $34 for the privilege of parking our car at the hotel overnight. There is no other option--valet only. For $34 they could at least acknowledge us. Bartenders at the party were incompetent; there were long lines, and drinks were not mixed correctly. There was a problem with our bill, and the front desk and one of the managers were very confrontational and hostile. We were very excited to stay at the hotel before we arrived, but we left with a horrible experience that cost us $300 for the night. We tried twice to resolve the issue with the bill, but no one will return a call or an e-mail. Starwood needs to intervene quickly. We won't ever return.

“Not in Winter!” Although I requested a quiet room, i was assigned a room across from the elevator. The front desk moved me immediately to a more quite room and then the real problems began. Phone did not work. Toilet did not flush.These things were fixed while I was out on business. Although the staff was wonderful, and the doorman couldn't have been more friendly, the heat in the room was intolerable! With the fan turned off and the heat dialed down to 65, the temp never got lower than 78 degrees, despite the window being open! So I slept in a sauna with street noises intruding in the room. Apparently although there were recent renovations, you either get heat in Winter or air in Summer and there's no in between. Many other guests had the same complaint. The Rare Restaurant in the hotel had excellent burgers and sweet potato fries, but the music level was intolerable! Don't think I can ever do this again!

“Impressive!” I stayed at this hotel while traveling on business. Thankfully I didn't have a car, because I'm not entirely sure where I would have put it (they probably had a parking garage that I didn't see). The hotel staff was undeniably professional at every opportunity, and the lobby was very upscale. The hotel provides free wifi and a fitness center, along with a decent (albeit pricy) continental breakfast. The room was comfortable and clean, with an overhead shower (see picture). I probably would have not picked this hotel on my own just based on price, but as my company arranged the stay, I definitely felt that the experience was worth the value paid for the stay. One nice thing they did was run to the end of the street and flag a taxi when I needed to go anywhere.

“Decent hotel with fantastic ocean view” Pros: We bid the hotel from priceline for $70 (before tax). The view from our room is spectacular. Cleanliness is guaranteed. The Grand Bed is as good as in the advertisement. Hotel lobby appears upscale. There are lots of counters, which really expedites the check-in process. Staffs are quite professional. Cons: Location is not so good for walkaholic like me. Seaport village is a boring place (not Hyatt's fault though). In the morning, there is some noise coming from the ceiling (like somebody is knocking the pipe)

“Average, decent Courtyard - but hot water would have been nice.” Pretty typical Courtyard. Comfortable bed & pillows, and I had good experiences with the staff. There is a Waffle House next door, a full-service Marriott across the street if you want a full service bar/restaurant, and a convenience store across the parking lot. Internet service was free, although my computer wsn't working. The only thing really bad was there was no hot water in the morningt when I tried to take a shower. I had an early plane so this was at 6:00 a.m. - sometimes it takes a while for the hot water to arrive if the hotel doesn't have recirculating pumps and you are the first one up - but it wasn't that early, and when it was still cold after 5 minutes I gave up so I could make the 6:20 van to the airport. Apologies to my seat mate on Delta. On the good side, I watched a movie and didn't get charged for it, so maybe that cancels out the lack of hot water? I'll know when I see the final $ posted to my Amex account.

“Went above and beyond for us on one of their busiest nights of the year!” I just stayed here for New Years Eve because it is across the street from a party I was going to (Big Night Out San Diego--which I also recommend). My friends and I booked a deluxe double double room back in November because we knew that hotels in San Diego sell out for New Years Eve. However, when I checked in, I was told that I had a room with one king bed. I'm not a picky traveler, and I usually just go with the flow. But I had reserved two beds (for quite a bit of money) very far in advance and was not okay with being given a room different from what I reserved. After looking into our reservation, it was discovered that the booking company we had gone through was responsible for this mix-up--not the Hilton. It being New Years Eve, they were unable to provide us with a room with two double beds (as all rooms of that type were sold out). It was explained to us that since we had booked through a booking site, they couldn't refund us any money. It did take some time, but we were finally were told that there was a room available with a king size bed and a pull out couch bed. Obviously pull-out beds aren't very comfortable, but this was an upgraded room with a view and our options were limited. I was content at this point. However, Jason K. at the front desk went above and beyond to apologize for the inconvenience. After our new years' celebration, we returned to our hotel to find a complimentary bottle of wine, cheese plate, cracker plate, and hand written note from Jason (who had handled our situation earlier) apologizing for the inconvenience. The hotel was very nice, but it was Jason's extra effort that impressed me the most. If the rest of their staff is anything like him, I would recommend this hotel to anyone and everyone!

“Nice hotel, good for familes” Stayed here with family for a few days. The room was a little bit smaller than some RI hotels I've been too, but still a suite. The room was clean and quiet. The breakfast added some white rice/dried seaweed options to the typical RI breakfast. The amenities looked well kept, although we didn't use much of it. The location was close to La Jolla which is nice, but a good 20 minutes from downtown. Overall, a good stay.

“Adequate” I don't think the hotel deserves the bad rap it seems to get, although it is at best average for its class. The room was fine; quite large actually. The staff were fine. I resent paying for internet, but that's endemic with 4 star hotels. I got the place cheap via Hotwire, so it was good value.

“Outstandingly helpful staff” Stayed here for one night whilst en route to Fort Worth. Hotel currently being renovated, which will no doubt mean a great improvement as the generously sized rooms are slightly dated decorwise, though the bed was super-comfortable. Location is convenient to the US35 but far enough away not to be noisy. All the staff we encountered were super-helpful and friendly to us, a nice change in a chain hotel - thank you! Bar meal and breakfast food were very good, dining room is cold and souless but presumably will be improved after the refit. A brief but very enjoyable stay!

“Convenient Location - Small” This is now a Holiday Inn Express - operated hotel. General: The hotel occupies a small footprint of real estate. There are 16 floors indicated on the elevator. Everything is small, so keep that in mind. The elevators are on the small side and slow during the morning breakfast time. Everything is very clean and well maintained. Location: Two (short) blocks off the Magnificent Mile. Close to a number of attractions and easy walking distance to a number of eateries. Rooms: The rooms, as indicated elsewhere, are SMALL. That did not bother me as I was only sleeping there. However, if youare wanting to lounge around your room during the day, this is not the place for you. My room on the 4th floor was a king locaed on the interior of the building. The window faced out to a central core (nothing to see, but daylight did come through). The bed occupied most of the room and was very comfortable. There was a desk at the foot of the bed. A flat panel TV was mounted at the side of the bed, best viewed from a small sitting bench. The bathroom was small, but comfortable. A very nice tub / shower was easy to access. A hairdryer was kept under the sink. The sink was a nice deep model with great water flow. As noted throughout the hotel, the room clearly had recently been remodeled. The room included a coffe maker, iron and ironing board, small closet and safe. Wireless high-speed internet was provided (free). Furnishings and decor: The decor and furnishings were bizarre. While the overall appearence is clean and well maintained, the furnishings are straight out of the 60's and the "house of tomorrow" look. Trust me, the furniture was ugly and uncomfortable in the 60's and it still is now. The bench in the room that sufices for a sofa was more uncomfortable than a pew in a Quaker church. The "table" in the room was a moveable flat top mushroom that might hold one plate. The hotel would be well advised to change decor soon. Staff: Helpful and courteous. The doormen were great. The desk staff were all efficient though not neccesarily warm. Value: The room rates went up $80 a night during my stay, so I am not sure the costs are any better than some other nearby well-known properties. You would have to investigate that more when booking. Overall: Clean, comfortable and quiet. Good breakfast. Small rooms that meet your basic needs -- not for lounging however. Elevators (two) are smallish. They are operated by your room key card. Expect a long wait during the breakfast time. Breakfast: The free breakfast is very nice with a good selection. On busy days, you may have trouble finding a place to sit. A large portion of the common area is occupied by flat sofas without tables (seems like a waste of space to me). The staff kept everything stocked and clean.

“Location Location Location on the transition of LES and East Village” We were supposed to go to the Beer Festival in October but pushed trip back to November to see some theater performances instead. The Hotel is very discreet and our Taxi person also had a hard time locating it. The check in was quick and smooth. The rooms are designed very well but very very small (I think our corner king was 1/3 the size of our room at the Rivington). We had a built in desk, small closet with several shelves and a fireplace. We stored one suitcase on a stand in the entryway and the other suitcase under the bed. The bed was nice (like my swedish mattress at home) with at least 300 thread count linens. The shower was a decent size with great water pressure. The best part of this hotel is the downtown location. We walked though the LES, NOLITA, SOHO, Battery Park, Gramercy, Wall Street, East Village and China Town. When we had to go to midtown to meet my cousin at the Four Seasons it was only a 10 minutes cab ride. Ditto for the two performances (Spamalot and Boeing Boeing). We had a wonderful dinner with Kim Watson in the Lower East Side on Saturday night and brunch in SOHO on Sunday. All walkable :) This is definitely a great location for the people who are more downtown (it is also 100 feet from the subway entrance).

“Great place to experience NYC on vacation” We stayed in the Marquis in February for 2 nights with a family of 5 (2 adults, kids 14,14,11). We had two rooms, both booked on points, which were connecting - one room with two queens and one with a king. Our windows looked down on the northern end of Times Square.. it was an amazing view and really fun for our first trip to NY. We arrived via subway and found it very easy to get around from the hotel. We got the subway down to China town, Battery point, and also up to Central Park.. there are two subway stations within 1-2 blocks of the hotel. The rooms were good, well appointed, good flat screen TVs. I would say slightly better appointed than the typical Marriott Hotel. One thing to mention - the windows have full over-lapping block out curtains, so you could completely darken the room for sleeping.. which is just as well because the Times Square glow lights up the room otherwise. We did not eat in the hotel so can't comment on the food. There is a star bucks in the foyer and of course plenty of eating options surronding the hotel. It was Presidents Day weekend while we were there and I will say that the sidewalks were very crowded at night, but we managed to get around (and stay out until midnight) with the kids without ever feeling like it was dangerous. There are police everywhere. We would definitely go back, unless we decide to experience a 'quieter' side of NY away from the tourists.... but lets face it, we are tourists! Very good location for theaters, although we did not go this time. Check in took about 5 mins. I know othersreviews have complained about the check in but ours (at about 4pm Friday) was uneventful.

“Sort of an odd place; below DoubleTree/Hilton standards” I didn't really enjoy my stay at this hotel. I got a bad taste from the very beginning when I called the hotel after a late arrival at the airport and asked for the shuttle. The woman on the phone was VERY inpatient while explaining the layout of the Phoenix airport (confusing!, as the hotel's shuttle only picks up on one side despite both sides having signs for hotel shuttles -- not sure why), bossy (for instance, when I tried to explain at the beginning of the call that I'd already gotten my bags, etc., she insisted on following her script) and pretty gruff. I then arrived and there was a long line in the lobby to check-in -- that happens sometimes, but it was frustrating to see only one person working the front desk even as the line continued to build. I ordered a room service dinner. Mediocre. My shrimp caesar salad had TINY little shrimp, clearly frozen, and it took 40 minutes to get delivered. The average level of service continued the next morning. The hotel does not put bills under the door, as the vast majority of Hilton and DoubleTree properties do. Instead, you have to check-out at the desk or leave your e-mail addresses in a drop box on your floor. When I checked-out, I needed the shuttle back to the airport. I was asked to wait for 20 minutes -- the ENTIRE time, the shuttle driver stood at the bell desk and did nothing. (I understand the shuttle runs on a schedule, but in my experience many other properties make an extra run when it's slow. Sort of annoying to just sit there and stare at the driver as he does nothing while you wait. Just as with the night before on the phone, I got the impression that the hotel is very "by the book" instead of providing personalized service.) I found the hotel's layout to be odd. It is an all external-hallways property with a very 1970s architectural vibe: heavy on the concrete, earth tones, etc. I just don't find a concrete "hallway" with brick walls very appealing. Some of the floors have bridges that connect sections of the hotel while others do not. I didn't necessarily feel unsafe as you do in some external-hallway properties, but the overall feeling was not one of high-quality or luxury. It sort of felt like an old Holiday Inn. The rooms are all suites, which is nice. My room was clean, although the carpet was worn. I also thought the room was dark; this is because the living room window looks right out on the exterior hallway and in order to let in light you had to let the world see into your room as they walk to their rooms, which I don't care to do. I thought the public areas of the hotel looked worn as well -- the restaurant and lobby were utilitarian and the elevators were dirty (fingerprints, etc. all over the glass). The place is also noisy, as everyone's rolling bags make noise on the concrete and the pool is right in the middle of everyone's rooms. A lot of people probably go ga-ga over the free breakfast buffet. I suppose that's a touch not usually included as part of everyone's room rate (although as an elite Hilton HHonors member you are often provided breakfast), but I thought the breakfast was pretty average: a bowl of melon that looked like it came from a can, over-cooked potatoes, rock hard biscuits, etc. Personally, I'd rather pay for a freshly cooked breakfast than go to a mobscene buffet with average food. I imagine a lot of people like this property for the big pool and free breakfast; as a business traveller accustomed to DoubleTree/Hilton properties delivering at a pretty high standard, I didn't think this property lived up to the standard of the brand. Next time I need to stay near the Phoenix airport, I'll look elsewhere.

“Great experience!” The Warwick is a great hotel. The staff are very friendly & helpful. The hairdryer wasn't working in my room on the first morning and was replaced by a brand new one straight away. The rooms are large and very clean. The location is unbeatable - try Astros diner across the street on 6th avenue for great breakfasts.

“Just in for a night but really enjoyed the Joule.” I was in Dallas for one night on business and wanted to try a new place so I took a look at the list of Amex fine hotels and resorts program and came upon The Joule. Great spot! I was upgraded to a suite. Room was great. Very comfortable. Modern but comfortable. Not like a W. Zero complains. And its a starwood property for spg members. Will stay here again for sure.

“Confortevole, ma 35 minuti dal centro citta'” Sono stato per tre giorni a Chicago per un viaggio di piacere e ho soggiornato per tutto il periodo all'Holiday Inn, l'hotel rispetta la buona qualità della catena, quindi camere spaziose e buona pulizia e servizio. Ristorante e Bar annessi all'Hotel con ottime prime colazioni e cene. L'unica nota negativa è stata la prima notte che, entrambi non fumatori, abbiamo dovuto pernottare in una camera fumatori... Attenzione: l'Holiday Inn è a sole due fermate di metropolitana dall'Aereoporto di O'Hare, ma a 35/40 minuti dal centro città.

“Excellent Business Hotel” I have been staying at this hotel a few times each year for a couple of years when I need to be downtown Chicago and must share with fellow travelers how spectacular this place is: excellent location, great staff, attention to detail, comfortable and luxurious rooms and bathrooms, hip lobby, fantastic food, wide screen TVs that are truly wide! It has become my home away from home. Highly recommend to fellow female (and male) fussy business traveleres.

“Renovated rooms are nice” I stayed here the night of 12/15. From reading the reviews of others staying on the very same night, the room quality apparently varies greatly. I was part of a group reservation, and we specifically asked for "renovated rooms" when booking - this seems to be the critical factor in getting a good room. We negotiated a group rate of $103/night. The rooms were very nice, freshly painted in bright colors and new bathroom. My room faced the street, with moderate but tolerable street noise. There was a room safe large enough for a laptop. My room was large enough to fit another entire bed into it, but others in the party had smaller rooms. I'm not sure how easy it is to "guarantee a renovated room" when booking a single room, but that appears to be the best bet at getting a good room.

“Frustrating and overpriced” I needed an airport hotel to stay overnight so I would be pre-positioned for an early flight one night when an ice storm was pending. I chose the Hilton for it's location (right across the street) and quality (I could get some work done). I booked through the Hilton website, where I am a silver member. This hotel, while clean and well-appointed, is far below the standards set for the chain for service and amenities. It is a sprawling horizontal building, rambling over a hillside with very poor markings. We drove around it several times trying to find the entrance. The checking was slow: they were understaffed and lingered over the many questions of confused travelers while the lines grew longer. The room that I was given turned out to be literally a quarter mile away: across the lobby, around the restaurants, down one long hall, through the convention area, down another hall (at this point a hotel employee pointed me onward as I studied a map), around the fitness center, up some stairs, an elevator, another long hall...amazing! The room was huge but spartan. Internet access was extra !! well over $10 for the night. There are lots of outside lights from signs and traffic, parking lots and streets. Bathroom was as-expected, good hot water and pressure. The morning was the same in reverse, a long trek to checkout, endless lines that didn't move because of chronic under-staffing, and no breakfast snack or coffee offered. The shuttle bus was confusing: but was on time. I'm sorry, this experience was rough, and well below Hilton standards.

“Elegant Grand Dame” Hubby likes it! When we checked in we were offered Gingerbread Men Cookies and hot apple cider! The staff was pleasant and very efficient. Our room was kind of old-fashioned, but elegant with 9 foot high ceilings. Very clean and very quiet even though we faced the street. There was a letter on the desk explaining that they were undergoing renovation and re-decorating that would be completed in Feb 2012. Nice robes, great location, and good coffee. We would definitely stay here again!

“Spacious Rooms” Stayed in one bed suite, with excellent size bedroom, spacious lounge area with sofa bed and kitchen area with all neccesities. Only thing on the small side was the bathroom. Rooms clean, but the hallway smelt of smoke, despite the floor being non-smoking. Hotel a couple blocks from nearest subway, 4 stops to Macys! Would recommend for stay over thanksgiving, as found a viewing spot with a good crowd just a couple blocks away from hotel.

“Perfect hotel for travelers on a budget” I stayed four nights while attending a conference at the convention center. It is a 1.3 mile/30 minute walk to the convention center (about 4 blocks of this is up/down hill). This hotel was perfect for my budget. I had a twin room with shared bath. The shared toilet and shower were clean, and I never had to wait to use them. Clean towels were provided daily. The front desk staff were incredibly friendly and helpful. The room was clean - yes, it is small, but my twin room was perfect for one person. I had a table and chair to do some work. The sink, mirror, refridgerator, microwave area was very nice to have in the room. The breakfast room is small, but adequate, and juice, coffee, cereal, fruit, pastries, and bagels were available. There is a Mexican take-out restaurant one block from the hotel. In the Gaslamp district between the hotel and convention center (along 4th and 5th Avenues), you will find plenty of restaurants and the Horton shopping plaza. There were homeless people sitting/sleeping on the sidewalks along 4th Ave., but they were not aggressive or threatening.

“Hip, Trendy and almost luxurious...” Let me start by saying that I really like this hotel. Super-friendly staff, great location, really good food service - both room service and restaurants. And at the price I got through booking dot com I would stay here any time. Only criticism would be that the updated rooms have a bit of a musty feel - like they didn't upgrade the ventilation etc when they did the rest. I stayed in two different rooms and both smelled musty, and the shower in my second room drained a bit out to the room carpet. But otherwise, a very nice stay.

“would return -- just be aware of the train and the valet parking” You like Embassy Suites or you don't; I do, and I would give this a four and a half if it were possible. I am cheap with the fives. You know pretty much what to expect -- cavernous lobby, koi swimming in the stream that runs through it, sounds of dishes clattering and people laughing that echo up in the early evening, smell of bacon and coffee wafting up from the high-end college cafeteria-style breakfast in the morning. The factors that distinguish one Embassy Suites from another are the freshness of the decor, the service, and the location. All get high marks for this hotel. The service was uniformly nice and the building is well kept. The pool is on lobby level and nicer than expected. The location is extremely convenient to much of what might draw the business traveler or tourist to San Diego. It's right across from the Hyatt where we had a great dinner but would have spent far more for the room, and it's essentially next to the "sleazy bar scene" ribs place from Top Gun (which I think is a tourist trap, but some people like it) . The two things you need to know are that valet parking is mandatory and that the hotel is also near the San Diego Trolley. I had no problem with either. The valets were quick, and there was no additional charge for multiple ins-and-outs during the day. I heard the train a little bit when I was awake but did not notice it at night. The hotel does provide earplugs for those who are bothered. Our room was on the other side of the hotel, and we have a train near our house, so in fairness I might be the last person to notice or object. If it's a potential issue, you could ask what time the train stops running at night, or request a room away from it.

“Terrific Stay!!!” We got a really cheap rate using their online booking service. It was a non-refundable net rate...try it out!!! We saved a bunch for a great room!!! We stayed on the 10th floor with a view of the east side of the facility. Really nice place...I've always wanted to stay there as we live a little over an hour from Memphis. The lobby area was a happening place as there is a bar with big screen TVs. Easy check-in and the staff was very nice!!! The bell-hop was excellent!!! We had a room-service pizza for dinner (snowed outside so we got to stay in for the night) and it was pretty tasty!!! Everything about this place was nice, including the very comfortable bed!!! We will stay here again!!!

“Flawless hotel very close to the Gaslamp Quarter” The Omni San Diego is a very nice hotel located close to the Gaslamp-Quarter and opposite the convention center as well as right next to PETCO-Park. The outside look is very sleek and modern. Inside the hotel is dominated by light marble and wood that gives a contemporary and modern look. I had booked a 4 night stay in July 2012 directly through the hotel. The rate was reasonable and as a Select-Guest meber you will get free WIFI as well as complimentary morning beverage service. Check-in was quick and efficient and we were given a room on the 12th floor with an excellent view overlooking the convention center and the northern part of the bay. The room itself was clean, sleek and modern with a large hallway, two comfy beds and still enough space for a lounge chair and a working desk. I am usually very prone to noise but with the windows closed I heard nothing from the adjacent rooms. During the first night some freight-trains crisscrossed in front of the hotel and hooted but that is not in the responsibility of the hotel. Overall we really enjoyed our stay and I would always choose the Omni for my future stays in San Diego.

“Clean, central location” Stayed here for 4 nights with my mom (she was visiting me in NYC). Overall, the hotel was very clean, in a convenient location and the staff was very friendly. The room was a decent size for NYC. Other pluses: free gym, computers/wi-fi in the lobby, no bugs (I obsessively checked) One things I'd like to state for people traveling with pets - Since I live in NY, I didn't check in with my dog. I went back to Brooklyn and got him so he could stay with my mom for a night or two (he is small - 7 pounds). When I brought him, I let the hotel know and they provided a bed and bowl. The first night, no incident. The second night, my mom and I went to dinner and when we came back to the hotel room, my dog was GONE. There was a note on the bed saying he was at the front desk. Turns out, someone complained that he barked so they removed him. This was pretty disturbing. Again, the hotel staff was SUPER friendly - my dog seemed fine and in good hands. But to remove my dog from the room without my consent? They said we had signed a waiver allowing them to do so, but we were never given a waiver (of course they had us sign one right then). I had my husband come pick up the dog then as I didn't want our pup to be a nuisance nor to be put in a situation like this again, however people traveling with pets from out of town wouldn't have this luxury. Make sure you are clear on this hotel's pet policy & what they will do if your dog barks.

“Inn at Venice Beach - Good Clean Stay for the Price!” My husband and I stayed at the Inn at Venice Beach during the week of October 7, 2004 on our way to Las Vegas. I took the advice of other Trip Advisor reviewers when choosing this hotel. Overall, we had a good stay. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful, especially the daytime male attendant. You can't see the beach or the harbor from the hotel, but you are only about a block from the beach. The room was clean, as was the bathroom. Chair, dining table w/two chairs, and good-sized tv in the bedroom. The vanity electrical plugs in our bathroom area did not work, but luckily we didn't need the hair dryer. I used the plugs in the bedroom area for my hotcurlers. Iron provided. Housekeeping was provided daily, and was usually done in the mid-morning. A Continental breafast of cereal/milk, waffles, bagles, muffins, sweet rolls, OJ, coffee, cranberry juice was served in the courtyard. Very odd first floor courtyard, open-air top, but totally closed off to the outside by a number of first thru third floor balconies that encompasses the area. Cute and quaint nevertheless. One elevator that serves guests and hotel housekeeping & maintenance. Parking is somewhat of an issue at $6/per night. About 8 small-sized parking spaces are located in the drive-under deck portion of the hotel. If you arrive too late in the evening (9 or 10ish), you will have to park in the open lot behind the hotel. Okay lighted area, but sort of in an alley. We booked for two nights directly with the hotel's web site for $89 and $99/night, respectively, for the one bedroom deluxe. Good price for the stay - clean and modern-ish upbeat decor. We ventured all over L.A., Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Marina Del Ray, Venice Beach, and Malibu. Hotel is close to the main streets that lead to any of the popular L.A. destinations, quickly with little traffic. Close to the airport and the freeway (if you enjoy sitting in the traffic/smog). You'll find a plethora of fast food places a few blocks away from the hotel/beach. Kinda far to walk to, but if you have a rental, you'll enjoy the variety. Some cafes on the beach, but kinda expensive. Hotel can assist with many of the major tour lines for Hollywoood sites. If you get lucky enough to get tickets to see a live taping of one of the network shows, be early. We arrrived at the taping of the UPN show One on One at 4:30, as the tickets required, but we could not get in - the seats were already taken for that show, Dr. Phil show, and others. A Page told us at Paramount that the line usually starts at least 2-3 hours prior to the time listed on the tickets. I would stay at the Inn at Venice Beach again when in L.A. For the price, convenience, and cleanliness - you can't beat it!

“Last Minute Overnight Stay” Stayed at the Harborside Inn in late March as flooding in Rhode Island cancelled all Amtrak trains out of Boston. Concierge at Train station recommended hotel - which I wanted close to the station for a possible early departure the next day if trains started running again. One problem - concierge said hotel was 3 blocks away from station and along the harbor. He called and I spoke w/ hotel - they had a room that faced the harbor and was reasonable. I said fine. Pushed my rolling bag and brief case for at least 3/4 of a mile to find the hotel across a main thoroughfare from hotels blocking the view of the harbor (Marriott). Nice place though - family run, front desk were conscientious and asked questions and gave directions about dining/etc. Renovated hotel in an old brick facade - rooms had regular keys for locks. Simple room - nice queen bed, two night stands, a small round table w/ 2 chairs and a sofa. Large tube style television w/ a DVD player and stereo system - all placed in a shelf unit. No bureau or cabinet, just open shelves for your belongings. Closet had an iron/ironing board and some shelf-unit and hangers. Bathroom was very compact - walk-in shower (no tub), not much counter space around the sink. Free wifi and computers in the lobby. Free coffee in the lobby. No restaurant, though hotel surrounded by bars and restaurants in both sides. Convenience store two doors down. No obvious parking, though parking was available down the street. Hotel was very nice and in excellent location if I was sightseeing. Surrounded by bars, on the weekend the noise from the street might be a problem. Went less than a block and I found Faneuil Hall and found a take-out dinner there. Didn't walk across the main road to check out the harbor. From my room, if I looked closely I could see a bit of the docks where a few boats were tied up next to the Marriott - that was the harbor view. Overall, a nice emergency hotel, close to the train station at an affordable price. Excellent location if you wanted to see the local tourist attractions. I checked and no room had two queen bed setups, if you wanted to bring a family of four for example. However, my sofa opened up to a sleeper sofa. Might bring my family back to this hidden gem - probably save a good $100-120 from the rates at the Marriott or other chain hotels.

“Super location with service getting better” When I reviewed this hotel a few months ago I loved the location but the service was terrible. The location is still great and convenient to everything in MIdtown - East. Check-in this time was great (thanks to Karen). This trip was just a one-night stay so I am not sure if the service is better or if I just was lucky in getting a better person at the front desk. I can tell you that thanks to the location this hotel is almost always packed. Book early if you want to get in.

“Great hotel” My husband and I stayed here for 1 night in March. I was doing a marathon in Central Park the next day so we didnt get to see too much of NYC or even stay up past 9:00 Pm. The hotel was very good I thought , they had free delicious cookies at the front desk and a complimentary microwave on the 7th floor which came in handy to heat up some snacks. The best part was it was very quiet, and the beds were extremely comfortable. I had an excellent night sleep even though I was nervous about the marathon the next day. It was also in a great location, close to lots of good things.

“Decent Hotel But Not My First Choice Next Time” Overall, the Hilton New York was a decent hotel. We traveled with a large group of girls who were performing in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. At times, this meant 1,600 girls trying to get to practices using the elevators. We were told to expect delays and to allow 30 minutes to get an elevator. This was usually sufficient, but there were still times where the girls had to resort to using the stairs. When returning from events, we had to stand in line to get an elevator. Now this was not just our group staying in the hotel. There were other people there too and they also had to endure the inconvenience of waiting for elevators. It seemed that the elevators designated for floors 1-15 were the worst. They have sets of elevators for other floors and those seemed to move quicker. The staff we came in contact with were all very nice and were always accomodating. Room service was extremely over priced...for just a sandwich, after tax, tips, and other fees, you were probably going to pay about $40. Au Bon Pain is across the way, as is the 53rd Street Deli, which were more convenient for our needs. Nice people at both of those places as well. We were asked not to use the hotel restaurant so it would be available for the other hotel guests, so I can't comment on anything other than the Starbucks that's connected to the hotel restaurant. We only went there once, but Starbucks was good...just like any other Starbucks except that they were busier thanks to our group. As far as our room, it was a pretty decent size by New York City hotel room standards. I've stayed in smaller. The bathroom was really small, but was nice after having been remodeled not too long ago. The room was always clean. Room temperature was sometimes a challenge, but luckily I could open the window to let cool air in. Internet was a bit pricey at $15 a night. For a hotel that expensive, I would think they'd let you have it for free. We stayed at this hotel because we were required to by the group we were with, but it probably wouldn't be my first choice next time. The location is pretty good...about halfway between Central Park and Rockefeller Center...but I'm not sure the price is worth it for what you get.

“Overpriced hotel, convenient to the Convention Center” I've stayed in many Marriott Marquis around the nation. This one offers nice rooms with great views. However, it is more than twice the price of other comparable hotels in the area. Being attached to the convention center is it's draw. When I checked in, the staff were actively trying to get people to go to other hotels and were very negative. The entire pool area was closed for renovation. The price ($289 per night + tax) was outrageous. The staff were the least customer friendly compared to all other Marriotts where I've stayed. It appears they feel "entitled" being attached to the convention center and do not feel they have to offer good service for their overpriced rooms.

“Mediocre Hotel Whose Heyday Was 1991” I wanted to like this hotel, I really did. It has excellent location in Downtown Seattle close to the major business centers, attractions and restaurants but there were just too many things that were wrong for me to enjoy my stay or endorse this hotel. I arrived late Sunday evening after a terrible travel day, and upon entering the lobby on the 15th floor I was horrified to find an extraordinarily long line for check in. As a high level HHonors members, I expected to be able to check in quickly, get to bed in preparation for a very early meeting that I had the next morning. No such thing. There was one front desk clerk working and he was the dictionary definition of slow. He was unsure of the process, how to run credit cards and was unncessarily chatting up guests while there was a queue of at least 11 guests checking in. After a long wait, I waited for an elevator. And waited. And waited. The elevators here are slow. I had to wait 10 minutes for an elevator to get to my room on the 24th floor. Upon entry into my room, the room was small, tired and had a peculiar odor. Too tired to care at this point, I went to bed willing to deal with the situation in the morning. When I opened the curtains in the morning and could see the room in daylight, I took a deep breath and laughed. If this is what Hilton considers an executive room, I shudder to think what the standard rooms are like. The furnishings were dusty, the bathrooms were small and the toilet was stained. The bathrooms are tiny...NYC tiny. Overall the room was very basic, older and didn't even compare to the quality of an Embassy Suites or Courtyard by Marriott. I also wasn't impressed there wasn't a mini bar in the room with a selection of soft drinks. As part of my reservation, I had breakfast included. I went up at 6:30am to the Top of the Hilton to eat and while the view was pleasant, the staff was apathetic and the food forgettable. Eat at your own risk. 45 minutes after eating breakfast, I became violently ill back in my room. Not a good impression at all. The hotel lounge is generic. The requisite barfood is available, and the cocktails are overpriced, though is standard for most hotel bars. The lounge looks like a sitting room of a retirement/nursing home. Tired and worn. It made me think of a waiting room at a cut rate hospital. I was booked to stay 6 nights, but checked out after two and moved hotels to a competing facility a few blocks away whose amenities justified the price. This was a nice a hotel in 1991. In 2012 it is the text book definition of averaged and overpriced.

“Nice Location & Value” Within the last six months I have now stayed twice at the Gunter and each time have been very happy with my experience. Stayed in a corner room on the 11th floor - Starwood preferred guest floor and had access to the lounge. The room was spacious, nicely decorated, great bed, and very quiet. The only negative is the bathroom which is very dated but not intolerable The hotel is located about a 5 minute walk away from the famous River Walk and across the street from the Majestic Theater. Also about 4 blocks is the Alamo and the Children's museum. In the evenings we did encounter several homeless people on the walks back to the hotel but should not be a deterrent from staying here. The hotel does have a restaurant and bar but with all the great options in the city would not waste my time - there is a mini-cafe at the front of the hotel that is a good option to get something to go. While the hotel is not located on the River Walk its a great value and within easy walking distance to many attractions and would recommend staying here.

“Elevator Noise” It's a very nice hotel, BUT: I stayed on the club level, my room was on the opposite side from the elevator. In other words, the elevators mechanisms were right behind the t.v. on the far wall away from the bed. All day and night, there was substantial elevator noise. Fortunately, I brought ear plugs with me and that was sufficient to drown out the elevator. But the fact that this noise exists is unacceptable and points to a design flaw in the hotel. I surely couldn' t be the first person to notice this, and they should only give these rooms to guests after warning them about the noise and offering a discount. If I had been staying more than one night, I would have asked to switch rooms.

“Adorable, Clean, full of fun hotel” My husband and I stayed in Hudson Hotel on Saturday night. I wish it was longet stay. Of course rooms are small - it is Manhattan - unless you can afford penthouse. First time in my life i had a view from the window - and we can see raising Freedom Buildings, Statue of Liberty, skyline. The cleanest room, nicely decorated. The club was unbelievable - the crowd was still dancing when we left at about 3.30am.

“Average” Stayed there one night for a convention. It is ok, nothing special. It does connect to the convention center which is nice. The bath room ceiling paint was pealing. I didn't notice until late at night when we got back to our room. I told the front dest about it and said there was nothing they could do about it that night. I understand that. It was 11:00 pm. But they really didn't care the next day either. Won't be staying there again.

“Swanky!” Ultra-hip, ultra-cool. And full of I hate to say it, jerks. Think spring break in Vegas and you'll have a good idea. Great location!! Seemed like hotel catered to club crowd. Bed was super comfy, check in was a breeze! Nice and quiet, great pool!! Room was very clean and included a turn-down service. Parking is valet only and pricey!

“Great location but not a great value” My wife and I spent two nights here for the 4th of July. We chose this hotel because it was close to the waterfront, it was pet friendly and we could use Starpoints for it. The hotel is quite large despite being only three stories. We booked a king bed and were pleased with accommodations, though we would have liked a refrigerator which are available for an extra fee. The room had small balcony overlooking the outdoor pool. As is the case with most Sheraton properties there are a wide range of services for guests including two restaurants and a concierge and car rental desk. A really neat thing they had was gas firepits with chairs set up to people watch, talk or just relax. These were located near the main entrance/guest load and unload and by the pool. We did not use go in the pool, nor did we use the exercise room. I should also note that free wi-fi was only available in the lobby. It was $14.95 per day in the rooms, though the rooms closest to the lobby may be able to get a signal. Parking was $43 per day self park or valet, no difference in price. There are several garages within walking distance that charge less but make sure they are open 24/7. The hotel location was perfect for exploring the Fisherman's Wharf area. Great access to Pier 39, shopping, food, streetcars, and ferries. Overall it was a great stay. If you are budget minded there are probably other hotels near Fisherman's Wharf that would deliver a much greater value than the Sheraton. Considering we used Starpoints, it was a good value. Had we not had our Starpoints, we most likely would have stayed someplace much less expensive.

“Fabulous!!” I will say, considering the negative reviews I had seen here before, I was pretty surprised to have such a wonderful experience at Loews! Sure, the valet was expensive and, yes, the outside looks like a corporate building. However, it's a historical building, and once inside, we were greeted by friendly and helpful staff. Our room was large, clean and had a terrific view of the city skyline. The beds were cozy, and we spent a couple of mornings lounging in bed and resting it up. One morning, we even felt compelled to get room service breakfast - a little steep, but not quite as pricey as other equivalent hotels will charge. I would have to say - the gym was the best I have ever been to! It was huge, with ample equipment, a spa, sauna, and pool. Make sure to bring your bathing suit! Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel, and I would be thrilled to have the opportunity to return.
“部屋は狭いです。下のバーがおすすめ” 部屋はまあ、こんなもんかっって感じです。狭め。 ダブルは下のバーがいいとおもいます。部屋はいまいち。? まあ、中級ってかんじです。

“Good location for business travelers” Stayed at the JW Marriott for 1 night. The lobby was grand and the hi-tech elevator system was definitely an experience. I have to give the staff credit for customer service--everyone was accomodating. I arrived early--before check-in--and I was still able to get into a room and they were able to honor my request for a fridge. The room had two double beds, was clean, well-furnished, but definitely more "european" in size--which didn't bother me. The beds were very comfortable. The workout room had good equipment. The hotel is definitely ideally located for business travelers--right in downtown DC. For leisure travel, I would recommend another hotel in a more vibrant area of the city. But it suited our needs just fine (not too far from the Cherry Blossom Festival events).
