“Nice hotel in Seattle” We stayed at the Homewood for two nights prior to a cruise. It's located a little outside the downtown area so cabs are needed to get to most attractions, except for the Space Needle area. We walked from the Public Market one afternoon but it was too far for comfort. The hotel was clean and well maintained but there was a bit of street noise, which was easily eliminated by leaving the AC fan on. Breakfast was OK...typical for this class of hotel. With all of the great food we found in Seattle, breakfast was not a big concern for us. The hotel offers transportation to the cruise piers for an extra charge. We reserved a private car but it did not show so the desk called us a cab. This was probably cheaper method.

“Excellent boutique hotel in heart of all the action” Hip and modern hotel that has the style of a W Hotel at a budget-conscious price. It's located in the heart of uptown Charlotte, with tons of excellent bars and restaurants literally steps away. Very clean and new. Bliss bathroom products. I had a great view of the city. Plus 24 hour food service in the lobby. Highly recommended for those who like W Hotels or the boutique hotel style.

“Excellent Hospitality and Perfect Location” We like the location of the hotel as it's extremely easy to walk around the Marina district. Jorge, who manned the front counter, was exceptionally hospitable and even remembered our last stay from over 9 months before. He helped us arrange transportation to Mountain View and also had several great food recommendations. When we come back to San Fran, this hotel is at the top of the list. Hotel is well kept and the rooms have always been clean. Breakfast buffet was a nice touch as well. Thanks again for another quality stay. Ross

“Great value and staff” all ladies trip to San Antonio and Drury was perfect for us. Lots of room, yes the bathroom was very spacious with a shower and a jet tub. All the employees always had a smile and said hi, not to mention very helpful. We enjoyed the pool and the movies at night on the terrace. I would recommend this hotel to everyone.

“Comfortable place, nice flat screen TVs, no Starbucks” Very large Marriott property near (but not all that close to) Columbus Ohio airport, mysteriously they have added Port in front of Columbus Airport though there are no ships in this sea. On the plus side the place was quiet, save for the early morning rain sounds that turned out to be a nearby room shower (no rain outside but it sounded as if it was raining). Flat screen have a few HD channels (ESPN included). No Starbucks in lobby, none nearby. Hotel coffee terrible as usual. Rooms comfortable, have standard household temperature adjustments for A/C and heat, which is nice. Service was very good on check in and check out, friendly polite staff.

“Fabulous location but showing some wear” We got a great rate for this place on Priceline and knew it was historic and small. We like charming places with personality, so we were happy with this hotel. However, for the money they typically charge (and even for what we paid) you don't get much. The location is pretty great though! The wall paper all over our room was peeling, which was very disappointing to see and we had a lovely view of dumpsters and air ducts. We did have free wifi because we joined their loyalty club. There is ice cream in the afternoon - which we only knew about because the 10 year old in the elevator was wondering why we weren't holding ice cream too and then told us where to go to get it - they should really mention it at check in, it's a nice perk. Overall, it's in a great location, but you can't stay here if you're claustrophobic or have more than two people. The rooms are very narrow (only wide enough to fit a bed and one night stand).

“Great location for Johns Hopkins” I stayed at the Inn for 4 days for business. My conference, being across the street on Johns Hopkins campus, made this VERY convenient. For dining, etc. it was not as much. There was a small “bistro” at the corner “New World Café” that although being a bit eclectic was quite nice – lots of locals. A little Italian restaurant is located nearby in a residential condo, not in a commercial area. Also, just down the street from the bistro is a great little market for snacks, wine, etc. All within safe walking distance. Also, I ate at a restaurant on the water in the industrial area called Frankie’s on the Pier. Very authentic and a great outdoor patio. This hotel has a nice bar and restaurant, a bit high, but typical for business clientele. They don’t open until 5:00. There is a nice business center with complimentary printing. The rooms are fabulous and great bedding, etc. All in all, great for a Johns Hopkins business locale.

“Good Hotel if The Price Is Right!” This was our third stay in this hotel...all three times we stayed thanks to a Priceline bid, or a Hotwire deal. This time was a Priceline bid for a three-star/Downtown Charlotte hotel for $55. Staff at this hotel have always been friendly, and they were this February night as well. Parking is in an adjacent parking deck, which is okay with us, as we are a couple. I might be uncomfortable parking there as a woman alone. You have to park, catch the elevator, then lug your luggage along the parking path to get to the hotel...again, no big deal if you're not alone....the lobby is small, with small birds in a cage in the corner. Cute! Check-in is always friendly, in our experience. This hotel has been undergoing renovation for quite some time. Last time we stayed there, we were given a room on the 15th floor. It was very very nice, but getting there via the elevator was a bit tricky. (you had to use your card to access that floor via the elevator, and it didn't work most of the time) This time we were given a room on the third floor. It had also been renovated, but yet, it looked older than our last room there. Again, our only tiny little complaint about this hotel is the elevators are incredibly slow and feel, well, not overly safe. I'm sure they're fine, I'm just saying what the feeling is when you're waiting for one/riding in one/getting stuck in one that isn't quite responding to a button-push. The bed was very comfy...all was quiet. Parking is $10, by the way. There are two BEST parts of this hotel...one is the location...right in the heart of everything downtown Charlotte. The other is the wonderful Italian restaurant in the lobby. We had dinner there one time, this time we just had drinks and an antipasto. Service was friendly, and the antipastofor just $7 was incredible! Amazing olives, artichokes, eggplant, mozzarella, salami, prosciutto...all on a balsamic bed. If the price is right....get a good deal! and this hotel is just fine.

“Undergoing a needed renovation” Hotel is in a good location. It's about a five minute walk from the Convention Center and Reading Terminal Market. Positives: * room was very clean * bed was comfortable * one of the largest hotel closets I've ever seen * sofa had a pullout bed * balcony * kitchen suite was helpful * very friendly staff * free breakfast - I've read some complaints about this in other reviews and I thought the food was pretty average free hotel breakfast, but they did have an omelette station * managers reception - we didn't partake, but there was an option to drink on the house Negatives * building is oval shaped so rooms are shaped like pie pieces and the entrance doors were three or four inches apart * kitchen suite was looked dated (although clean) * bathroom towel rack and shower curtain rod were both loose * didn't have a business center * all the vending machines were on the second floor * there was a concierge station, but no one was ever at it * the elevators were very slowly and at one point, only one of the three elevators was functioning Hotel is undergoing renovations that will likely address some of the negatives. For instance, a business center is being built. All in all, I've stayed at nicer Embassy Suites and I imagine you could find better hotels for the price in that downtown area.

“James Thurber would approve!” Grand old hotel renovated and lovely. We stayed here in August for a family reunion, and at a special rate of $119/night it was an excellent value. The staff was exceptionally friendly and helpful. Beautiful large lobby provided a warm place to meet and greet. The restaurant was able to accommodate our large gregarious group for breakfast with ease- the servers were very tolerant of our table-hopping and visiting. Our room was on the 6th floor- nicely furnished with a "heavenly" bed. We were a bit worried about the street noise, but leaving the fan on seemed to take care of that problem. In-room safe, good bath products, but only one robe? I am sure i could have requested another but never got around to it. This hotel reminded me of the Davenport in Spokane. It seems like they could have done a better job on noise insulation as we were able to hear the street and loud passersby in the hallway, but it wasnt really a problem for us. Also the parking is $20 per night! We paid more for parking than we did for the rental car! We had drinks in the Thurber Bar which was fun and friendly. Also had a nice catered brunch in a private room on Sunday morning with a delicious and varied spread- loved the French toast! Location-wise it is about a miles walk to German Village. We walked toward the river and COSI (kids science museum) and found a great restaurant-bar overlooking a small water-feature park. I will end with a quote from James Thurber: "It is better to have asked some of the questions than to know all of the answers."

“Mixed feelings!” I'm just back from a four night stay at the Westin, as part of a conference, and have mixed feelings about the hotel. The room itself was nice; usual size, comfortable bed, flat screen tv. As others have mentioned, they charge to use the fitness center, which seems over the top for their usual rates. The room service dinner I had one night was fine (but it was just a chicken caesar salad) and it arrived very quickly. I had breakfast in their restaurant one morning and it was ok .... and around $20. This is definitely not the place to stay if you're in Chicago on vacation. It's a bit of a walk to Michigan Avenue and while there are some restaurants in the area, nothing is very close. It was fine for the conference since the shuttle bus picked us up every morning and brought us to the convention center. The staff was inconsistent. Sometimes there were too many bellman in the front, and other times none (yesterday when we left, nobody was there for about 10 minutes and we got our own cab to the airport). The maid service was very inconsistent. I guess I'd recommend it if you had business in the area or are in town for a conference.

“Stylish Rooms and Lobby” Visiting as one of a group of 4 friends celebrating a 50th birthday. Nice location (not business/financial district of Dallas). Shopping nearby. Hotel features very good contemporary design elements. Feels like a place with a lot of energy but not frenetic. Nice bar area. Attentive service throughout. Will return.

“Fabulous!” Awesome hotel. Great service, very clean. Well worth paying an extra to get a lake view. The restaurant had amazing food (breakfast and dinner). The lounge on the 33rd floor was small and only had one client...I was disappointed to see that, thinking I would be partying there. The bed is very comfortable too! The only real negative that I am seeing is that even though it is right beside the lake and the navy pier, it is a bit far from public transport. You have to walk quite a bit to reach a subway or train station. The living room (lobby) is great! I am looking coming to the W Lakeshore again!

“very nice property, friendly with small kids” Stayed for three nights over fourth of July weekend and had a great time. Were staying on priority club points and got upgraded to a Deluxe Suite. Had wonderful views over LA, Fox Studios and saw all the way to the Ocean. We had breakfast at the hotel and each morning enjoyed wonderful service in the restaurant. We were travelling with our 13 months old daugther and were very grateful that they were so accommodating to her. I would definitely go back to the hotel again.

“Good Contemporary Design” I stayed at the St. Regis for several days in mid-November based on the recommendations of some colleagues who travel to SF frequently and told me about this new hotel that opened this year. My usual place is the W, which I stay at about 2 times a month, which is just down the block. Positives: The hotel's lobby area is excellent. The design is contemporary but warm, and makes you want to congregate. I would rate the overall friendliness of the staff as generally good, though not overly exceptional for this type of hotel. The reception area did tend to get backed up and did not seem properly staffed. The hallway decor and color scheme is nicely done. I was happy with the size of my room, on the 18th floor. A control panel controls the drapes, which is something I just saw last month at the Royal Riga in NY. No problem connecting to the WiFi signal in the room. Rain showerhead in the shower is a nice touch. The lighting seems about right. The desk is generously sized and a good work space for business travelers; the desk chair is also very comfortable. Negatives: The quality of the room service food was simply horrible. I ordered the chicken caesar salad, which is something that should not be difficult to prepare. The chicken was terrible -- dry, hard and tasted like it had been sitting out for hours. I was so offended by my dinner I walked around the block to a nearby Chipotle and bought a burrito. The closet space is also very small -- and there is little shelf space for clothes. No coffee in the room, nor is any offered in the lobby. Also, although there is a nice 50" HDTV flat screen in the room, it does not get any HD channels, which was perplexing. Finally, the speakerphone on the control panel does not work well -- I usually had to pick up the handset to talk.

“Great Location. Walk or Bus To Local Fun Places.” I placed two friends in this motel for their two night stay in Austin. I went down to check out the motel before I helped my friends make their reservations. I was shown an open room in the lower level of the motel and it was a retro design, sort of like an old adobe looking structure with older, but comfortable furnishings and nice Southwestern decor. I felt I could stay there OK. The desk clerk was very helpful and I selected information about Austin from the tourist brochure rack in the small lobby, The motel is right in the center of all the hip stuff to do on South Congress which is one of Austin's most interesting entertainment and shopping and restaurant districts. In fact, Guero's Oak Garden and restaurant are a stones throw away as is Jo's Coffee Shop, The Continental Club and more. You can walk around a mile to Downtown Austin or take one of the many Cap Metro buses that run on South Congress. Location is the reason to stay here! When my friends arrived, I helped them to check in and that went OK. The next day I asked how their stay was going and they said "So so". I asked to see the room. Well, lo and behold, they were staying in an upper level room - up some stairs and it was nothing like the sample room that I saw. The room was small, felt cramped for space and the furnishings were way downscale. It was the type of room that I would not want to spend time in. This is the risk of staying in boutique, one of a kind motels. But, location cannot be beat. Be nicer if the room was not so mundane and cramped.

“Comfortable & High Standard Chain Hotel” We stayed for 2 nights a Friday & Saturday. We stayed in a room on the executive floors - top 2 floors. So the experience may be slightly different to the standard rooms but the executive floors were only slightly more expensive than the regular floors. Well worth it. Check the prices but I imagine it was cheaper on a weekend as this is a conference hotel. The hotel is huge with a HUGE foyer and a large bar and restarant. The rooms were spacious and the bed comfortable. The bathroom was large and clean. The executive floors have access to a lounge that serves free breakfast and free snacks throughout the day. There is also free soft drink & water and an honour bar. It also has a free computer terminal in the room with internet access & printer. There is a good size pool with spa and lots of pool chairs. very spacious. The gym was really superb, fully equipped with weight training & cardio equipment, an attendant on full time and plenty of water & complimentary headphones for the TVs. The location is fine being within walking distance of all the night spots and also to the Capitol & museums. Austin was also a very easy city to drive around, although beware of some one-way streets. There is also a turn down service. The standard of service in general was much higher than I expected from a Hilton.

“Luxurious Bedding and Views, Skip the Food” My husband and I stayed one night to celebrate our wedding anniversary. We have stayed at the Peninsula, Four Seasons and Ritz in Chicago, so we thought we'd try something new. Our room, upon check in at 4, was not ready we were told. It was supposed to be ready at 3 and I was not interested in the drink coupons to be used at the bar, so "another" room was found for us. I was told it was not an upgrade, but I could not have been happier when shown our room. It was 2701 and had spectacular views of the Chicago river, the Wrigley building and more - could not have been better. The furnishings were understated and luxurious, the room itself was very spacious as was the bathroom. We LOVED the bedding, the terry robes, the slippers and the TV "in" the bathroom mirror - truly wonderful. The pillows were scrumptious, and the pillow "menu" of complimentary upgrades was a nice touch. We had a drink on the LOVEY terrace on the 16th floor and each ordered a $20+ salad. You are absolutely paying for the view, because my salad was inedible and I ended up sending it back for another that was very over-dressed. My husband's salad was forgettable. So, my advice is skip the food and just enjoy a cocktail and the view. Another tip is the terrace has no heaters and gets brisk quickly as the sun sets. I wouldn't get there any later than 6 if you don't want to be cold. The pool was lovely on the 14th floor (although nowhere near as spectacular as the Peninsula) and the work out area was huge and well equipped with great views. Overall, a terrific experience and a great location.

“perfect location for midtown” We stayed at the Hotel 373 for 1 night as a stop over on route to the main part of our holiday in San Diego, California. Having been to New York on several occassions, we selected the hotel mainly due to its central midtown location and close proximity to Penn St Station. We were flying into Newark Airport from the UK and for a one night stay and did not fancy paying the standard $70 - $80 each way cab fare to and from Newark Airport For those unfamiliar, the suitable alternative is to take the train from Newark Airport to Penn St Station and from here it is literally a 5 minute walk to the hotel. Sure its is a little more hassle if you have mountains of luggage but you save over $100 and its actually quicker timescale wise than getting a cab. The Hotel itself was perfectly adequate. As I mentioned, great central location, maybe 1-2 blocks from the Empire State Building and bang on 5th avenue for shopping etc... Walking distance to times square, central park, rockafeller and broadway shows. If you don't fancy the walk then there is a subway 1 block from the hotel which will take you uptown to central park or indeed downtown as far as Brooklyn Bridge, Wall st, staten island ferry etc... The room itself was typical New York in that it was very small and compact. In terms of decor it was fresh, modern enough and the bed was very comfortable. The vast majority of tourists visiting New York don't want to spend any more time than is neccesary in their hotel room and instead are basically needing a centrally located, clean, comfortable room to crash out in after a long, tiring days sightseeing... If this applies to you then you won't be disappointed in the Hotel 373.

“Huge hotel. Don't turn left out of the hotel. Nice pool and hot tub!” Big hotel (apparently largest on west coast). Great heated pool and hot tub outside and comfy loungers. Internet very expensive. If you come out of the hotel and turn right towards the main shopping area and downtown it is fine. If you turn left then be prepared for a really nasty (and potentially dangerous) walk. A bit faceless but OK. Staff were good.

“Great value - great location” This hotel is all about cost and location. Compared to most hotels in Boston with such a good location, this is great value for money. Yes, the standard rooms are small but more of a problem was the small bed. However the rooms are very clean and well equipped. Great shower, good bedding and towels and the room cleaned and re-equipped each day. Above all else this hotel is in a great location. You can literally walk anywhere and the subway, which is safe and efficient if a little shabby, is right across the road. Overall, excellent value for money for Boston.

“Very nice hotel.” I thought the hotel was very nice. The location was a bit East..however during the day, it was easy to walk all over Austin. We had a high corner room and the view was very nice. We were unable to open the windows which was a bit disconcerting and stuffy. The engineer took us off the sensor system so the room stayed cool. The food and service on the club level was only okay. The Hotel Staff was very nice and helpful. Christy was exceptionally nice.

“A "cool" place for grown-ups.” The Positives: Great location in Midtown. I usually avoid the chaos of Midtown, but found The London to be a peaceful oasis. Excellent bedding, decor, and amenities. Suites are large by New York standards with excellent use of space so it feels even bigger. Housekeeping was excellent and super-friendly. The staff was also friendly, but they aren't intrusive. The Negatives: Only that Gordon Ramsey has two restaurants here. Not the forum to get into it, so I shall simply say that if you enjoy the value of hotel mini-bars you will love his eateries. All in all, a terrific hotel and an excellent value for New York. A suite with the same amenities in comparable hotels will generally cost you significantly more. And the hotel does have a "hip" and relaxed feel which I really liked. Classy without being stuffy.

“Great hotel” Great hotel clean, great location, great staff, transit system on 50th and 8th, times sq. 5 min away, theatre district 5 min away, oh before I forget nice continental breakfast every morning, I can't say enough, I wish I had more time to stay.

“Believe what they're saying...this is a great place to stay.” We had a very nice experience at this Best Western. The hotel was easy to find and close to loads of restaurants, attractions, etc. Check in was easy and the staff honored our room location requests. Speaking of the staff: very nice and welcoming. They were helpful when giving us directions to the restaurant we were looking for. The free breakfast was what we expected. Gotta say, the pool was the best on our entire trip. The pool is large, clean, and has a nice deep end. Too many places nowadays have these pools that max out at 5 feet. Too shallow! There was plenty of room in the shallow end for the younger kids...and plenty of room in the deep end for the big kids. And it was WARM...the warmest we've found. This is a motor lodge, so we were able to park right next to our room. Nothing like being able to crack the blinds and see your car safe and sound in the morning. The free internet worked fine. Highly recommend this Best Western if you're in San Diego.

“Lacking in service” Room was ok, but not practical. Where is the dresser? Why is the desk completely covered with W Hotel items for sale and office supplies, leaving no room for my laptop? Also, the Acura car service that is advertised runs at odd hours and is never available. Concierge is no help and acts like he's doing you a favor. Got interrogated on Saturday night by the doorman. Can I just get to my room please? I understand you have a nightclub on weekends, but as a paying guest, I shouldn't be harrassed. Final straw: restaurant on Sunday has the odd practice of closing for breakfast on Sunday and then reopening for brunch an hour later. I have never heard of that and because of that we couldn't eat before we had to check out.

“Very Pleasant Experience” I stayed at the Fairmont for 2 nights in May 2010 while attending a conference. It was a piece of cake to get to by cab from DCA, and is walking distance from the Metro (Foggy Bottom, Dupont Circle is further away), although probably not with more than 1 bag. Service was impeccable - my bags where whisked into the lobby (rather long and horizontal, but nicely decorated and well-lit, I was checked in by a gracious front desk staff that explained all the hotel's amenities, signed me up for the membership program (which got me free internet and gym access) and showed me on a good map where to go for dinner. The room was very pleasant, great bathroom, and the bed was very comfortable indeed. I didn't actually eat in the hotel, but there are many restaurants nearby in a variety of price ranges - GWU is to the west, Dupont Circle and the Golden Triangle to the east. The gym is a very large, multilevel affair with modern equipment, highly recommended. I'd definitely stay there again - if it were right on top of a Metro station it'd be perfect.

“Another excellent visit” This was our second time in Boston and second time at Jurys. Check-in staff and porters were as friendly, polite and helpful as we'd remembered them and the room (deluxe doubles, 9th floor) was spot on. I like this hotel because there is very little (if any) noise from adjoining rooms. However, here was a fair amount of noise from the street on this visit (commencing around 8am and continuing until tea time) because of a big building project going on just along Stuart St. If you are staying in the next few weeks I'd advise that you ask for a room that does not face onto Stuart Street. Some free tourist stuff for you: Fort Independance (South Boston),open at weekends only and easy to reach by T and bus #9. Historic fort with great tours, pleasant beach and views of harbour. USS Constitution is also free to visit and easy to get to. If you have a week saver T ticket it is also valid for the boat trip from Long Wharf to Charlestown Navy Yard at no cost. A great way to arrive. This is easily combined with a climb up the Bunker Hill Monument. My husband highly recommends the Samuel Adams Brewery Tour (few dollars donation requested). Trip round the brewery and a generous sampling session with souvenir glass (word of warning - children are admitted on the tour but not allowed in the bar where the sampling goes on). T to Stony Brook and a couple of minutes walk at most.

“Not the W, but not the price either” I travel for work every week. I have stayed in some great places and I have stayed in some dumps. This place falls right in the middle. I almost didnt book due to the reveiws but I am in Denver for two seperate weeks and booked for both of them knowing if the place sucked I could change to a different hotel. Well, I wont. The location is next door to Invesco field, I would double check to make sure there isnt a game because I could see traffic being an issue. The location while seeming a bit seedy is actually pretty decent. Its a short drive or a long walk to the entertainment district, I think its called lower downtown. The river is close and I found an amazing trail next to it for running, its about 2.5 miles to the 15th street bridge and back along the trail. It goes farther but that was enough for me. The room itself is pie shaped due to being a small round hotel, but seems larger than it actually is. The furishing are nowhere near luxurious but they arent rubbis either. the bed was only decent. The bathroom is okay sized, but the faucet in the sink is a bit trickey to get warm water, it was hot or cold, no inbetween. The staff I came into contact with were all freindly and chipper. I have no complaints about the VQ, I paid about $100/night which is darn good for a hotel near a downtown. The place would make an AMAZING boutique hotel if they went that way, as a moderate hotel it os okay. I am here again next week so it cant be bad.

“Good value hotel, well located.” For a midtown hotel it was as good as you could expect; it was clean and well located. The hotel looks old and dated in areas, and there was no coffee making facilities in the room, but these are fairly small drawbacks. Reading other reviews I'd imagine I wouldn't have been so happy at paying $300 a night, but for what we paid, I was happy.

“A modern business hotel but also good for tourists” Spent 4 nights on vacation in San Francisco with my with and daughter at the Westin. It was the peak of tourist season (or so it seemed) and all of the public transportation and the restaurants were packed with out of town visitors. The concierge service at the hotel was exceptional given the near constant line at their desk and provided helpful informaiton and even got us a good deal from a local rental car company that delivered it to the hotel and allowed drop off at the airport for only a minor fee. The room was adquate for the three of us, the bath was very average but was clean and had lots of towels and other amenities. No free internet. The place looked pretty packed while we were there but it never seemed to impact the service. All and all a good place to stay. Not near the main tourist areas, so be prepared to walk about a mile to the embarkadaro or take the historic street car line, also city bus service and cable car is only a short walk. Lots of coffee shops and small restaurants nearby.

“Great location, excellent service and decent rooms!” I was very pleased by the service at this Courtyard as well as the location of the property. Excellent access to shopping, restaurants, etc. Decent price considering the location although I'd argue the room rate was a wee bit high for a Courtyard. Regardless, I'd recommend it.

“Comfortable but not really in downtown San Diego” I was there 3 nights for a convention. The meeting had contracted with 6 hotels in the area, but I was late registering and the Residence Inn was the only one left. After staying there, I imagine the main reason is that it was the farthest hotel away from the Convention Center. Another reason to think twice about staying here is that train tracks run nearby and all trains blow the whistle as they pass by. At the airport, I called and requested the free shuttle van, which came promptly. The van will take guests anywhere within a few miles, so I signed up a couple of times to get back and forth to the Convention Center. The first time I walked there and back, which took 20 minutes moving briskly. As the weather was great, it was an enjoyable long walk but not if you're dressed up or carrying a briefcase or laptop. Walking back at night was ok - I went through the Gaslamp shopping/restaurant district. Lots of people and I wasn't nervous walking on the busy streets. The hotel has a nice food area in the lobby. I ate there one evening which featured free beer, wine, and soft drinks and make-your-own burritos and tacos. If I remember correctly, the free "dinner" is only M-Th. The daily breakfast buffet had plenty of choices including eggs, meat, fruit, cereal, yogurt, etc. A fitness room had several cardio machines and weight machines but nothing fancy. I didn't visit the pool but it looked fine. I was upgraded to a suite because I arrived early and none of the regular rooms were ready. I don't know what it cost normally, but it was large enough for a family on vacation. It had a full-size fridge, stove, microwave, and dishes/silverware. Nothing to complain about in the room, but location, location, location - always ask for a room away from the railroad tracks. There are free earplugs on the nightstand, which should tell you something. It's a short walk to the harbor with the large ships on display. There are a few fast-food places nearby but I recommend walking up the hill to Little Italy, for better restaurants. I ate at Filipi's, which had great food and a little grocery store with hard-to-find Italian foods. This was my first trip to San Diego. I'll probably choose a different hotel if I return - something closer to downtown and the Convention Center - but the Residence Inn is certainly a good choice.

“Great stay” Stayed here for one weekend night in November. The room was small but very comfortable and quiet. To me the most important aspect is the shower, especially after walking all day in the cold city. The Hilton definitely delivers with a spacious shower and plenty of hot water. The problem area was breakfast: the menu choices were great but they ran out of basic things like yogurts and milk (!) so it remained a good breakfast in theory... The staff explained that some deliveries were missed that day so I guess that's not the usual breakfast service you would get.

“Spacious and brand new” The old IC (The Barclay, which is still open and still an IC) was one of the worst five-stars in NYC. This brand new hotel is easily one of the best. Large rooms, especially impressive given the usual NYC options, with lovely Four Seasons-quality decor, your own in-room computer, a very comfy bed with hign-end linens, decent toiletries, rainfall shower and, if you are high enough, a good view. Room-wise, you really won't get better for the money in New York. And the subway (E) from JFK exits directly outside the front door (take the 44th St exit). There are 2 downsides. Firstly, Times Square is not for everyone and I'm not sure IC's business clientele want to be pushing through tourists everytime they leave the hotel. The area is still a bit down at heel, with an adult store and gentlemans club being directly adjacent to the hotel on 8th, and the Port Authority Bus Terminal being close. Secondly, there is not a huge amount of public space and only one restaurant (plus a take-away coffee outlet) - a 2nd eating option would have been good, although obviously you have literally hundreds in walking distance. All in all, though, IC has done a great job here and finally has a NYC property to match the London and Paris flagships.

“Great Memorial Weekend stay” We had 4 teenagers and 2 rooms. Excellent stay. We requested 2 rooms next to each other. Arrived at 11am Saturday of Memorial Day weekend. One room was available and they said they would get our other room as close as possible. We ended up with the room next door which was great. Not so great pull out beds but you don't expect they would be that great. Excellent location to Navy Pier and the Watertower and Michigan Ave. shopping. Would stay again when we visit again.

“Clean room & great service at the Roosevelt” I stayed at The Roosevelt Hotel in October 2004. While traveling around the city, I enjoyed the close proximity of the hotel to Grand Central Station and to the great shops along Madison Ave. All of the front desk and baggage clerks were polite and helpful. The room was small, but clean and well-maintained. It was bit pricey, but I would definitely stay here again.

“Overall great hotel; a few things to watch out for” I found this hotel by carefully combing through the hotel reviews on TripAdvisor. Overall, I was pleased, it did not let me down. Things to appreciate about this hotel: 1. Free breakfast in the morning, until 9:30 This includes cereal, fruit, muffins, and hot items. The staff did not rush us out of there, which was nice -- some hotels eagerly close up the breakfast at 9:29. I was also impressed that it appeared that the hotel staff was able to eat breakfast as well -- it's such a good sign when a company takes care of its employees -- they are much happier workers that way and do a much better job. 2. Internet access in the hotel rooms. It was ethernet, which worked fine. They are in the process of installing wireless as well. 3. Friendly front desk staff. They were particularly helpful in researching local dining options. 4. Clean, comfortable rooms. I appreciated how this room included both a king size bed and a sofa. 5. Quiet. I asked for a quiet room and got one. In general, it's in a quiet area of the city, so any room probably would have been fine. Some rooms face the pool, which could be noisy in the summer, I suppose. 6. No sleep number bed. Some Raddisons have foolishly (in my opinion) hopped aboard the "sleep number bed" bandwagon. This had a regular bed. 7. Free newspapers in the lobby, including USA Today, The Wall Street Journal, and the Financial Times. 8. Windows that can be opened for fresh air (very important in any hotel). There are a few things to be aware of when booking this hotel: a) It's considerably north of San Diego, in a suburban office park area near Sony and HP office complexes. I wouldn't stay in this hotel again if I had daily business in San Diego. I didn't fully realize it was a solid 30 minute drive away from the city until I actually did that that drive. b) They charge 75 cents a day for USA Today "delivery" to your front door. Be sure to ask in advance for the newspaper not to be delivered and added to your bill. c) The staff will happily provide a map of local restaurants, but the map is poorly drawn and can lead you on a wild goose chase. While it's wonderful that they have a map -- I was impressed by the number and diversity of local restaurants -- be sure to confirm that the restaurant is still open and exact directions to where it is located. The front desk staff were very helpful in calling 411 and getting me the information I needed. The hotel is in a suburban area on the side of a mountain, so all the streets curve around in strange directions -- it's easier to get lost then you'd think. d) We paid $116 a night, which didn't feel like the best bargain in town. Then again, it did meet my expectations, so it was worth it.

“Strange Concept But Very Cool Staff” Their slogan goes something like this: "Live Life Aloft". Strange. The theme is more like 2001 Space Odyssey meets Disco meets College dorm. I just didn't get it as a lodging option but I appreciate the effort. The property is situated about a mile from Philadelphia International Airport in a fairly nice gated complex that houses two additional Starwood hotels, the Four Points Sheraton and the Sheraton Suites. I chose Aloft because I was awarded it after a $90 Hotwire selection. The other two run about 140-160 per night during the week and appear comparable in quality. The main floor of the hotel has all of the standard amenities of a Marriott Courtyard with the addition of dance music blaring in the background, billiards table, a little grocery market, "new wave" bar and a swimming pool with a similar ultra-modern design. It actually felt like a place where you would go to pick-up a lonely flight attendant. The staff actually greet you with "Aloha" when you check-in or ask them a basic question. I couldn't decide whether or not to answer with an Aloha back or break out with a "Buenos Dias". That being said, everyone was really nice and took time to answer questions about the local area. My room resembled something similar to my dorm when I was a freshman in college. It had a bed, a work table and little else. It was tiny and there was no tub. Rather, you get a stand-up shower, a sink and a toilet. I was waiting for a Resident Assistant to assign me a roommate. The only thing resembling a perk is the flatscreen. This is not what I expect in a room design. Upon my return to retrive my car (you can keep it parked there for 6 dollars per day so long as you prepay) my car battery went dead and I forgot one of my bags at the airport. Staff were great. They immediately called for a driver who took us back to the airport where I found my missing luggage. They also called for a maintenance engineer from one of the adjacent buildings who was kind enough to give me a jump with his cables. My car started immediately. I am going to contact the management to let them know about their kind actions as they both went beyond the call of duty for me. Overall, this place will probably work for single guys or men on business who are looking for a place to crash without their wives or girlfriends. I would stay again if traveling by myself but would not recommend for older couples, female professionals or familes traveling with children.

“Not my favorite HIE” We got a great deal at the HIE, Fisherman’s Wharf, so I can’t complain. The room was clean and comfortable and that’s most important. One of the features at the Holiday Inn Express is the free breakfast. It’s a light buffet, usually with cold cereals, breads, juice, fruit, and yogurt. Plus, they have some hot items – usually scrambled eggs and bacon or sausage, biscuits and gravy, and sometimes a pancake maker. We usually take advantage of these free breakfasts and we did again at HIE, Fisherman’s Wharf. However, this was the most chaotic breakfast at any HIE I have ever stayed in. I presume that it is because it’s the biggest HIE I’ve ever stayed in. We finally managed to make a couple of plates of food, but then had to take it back to our room to eat because there was nowhere to sit due to the breakfast area being completely inadequate for the number of guests the hotel can accommodate. The elevators were also an issue – just because of the volume of people trying to use them. We tried to find the stairs, but had no luck. Worth it for what we paid, but not my favorite HIE.

“Standard stay, nothing too special or too bad” Stayed here on the way from Pittsburgh to Myrtle Beach because we got a great rate from Hotwire. The hotel seems standard in everything it does and offers a decent free breakfast every morning. Neighborhood doesn't seem to be as bad as everyone else suggests, but I brought all my luggage in for the night regardless. We needed a crib/pack and play for our daughter and had to request it several times from the front desk, but that was the worst of it. Also, if you're looking for a fun dinner and you don't mind Mexican, I definitely recommend Azteca about a mile away; fun environment and great food. (Get the fresh guacamole!)

“Best choice downtown” Yes, it is a half mile to downtown. And get a room facing away from the freeway. Great breakfast. 2 free computers. Free use of the 24 Hour Fitness across the street. A short walk up the hill to Capitol Hill with many restaurant and bar choices. Free shuttle to downtown area. Have stayed their many times with no complaints. (I enjoy the CBC Canadian channel on the TV). Did I mention the friendly staff?

“Better Marriott options in NYC unless you really want to be in Times Square” I spent two night here in mid July since it was close to the office I was working at ... Perhaps this hotel works well for some folks and families but not really for me - First the lobby reminded me of a mediocre Vegas hotel lobby ...: too large and to busy. The elevators are crazy - you enter your floor and it "assigns" you to an elevator - perhaps high tech for 1985 but seemed contrived now. My room was in theory upgraded but just ok / bathroom small - Worst of all the converge lounge was insanely crowded on a Sunday night .... Took 10 minutes to stand in line for some apps Overall I will return to the hotel 57 renaissance the next time i am in manhattan

“Very Chic Boutique Hotel on the L.E.S.” What a nice stay at the Cooper Square. The customer service was excellent. Everyone we encountered was friendly and helpful. Sleek and modern rooms, a bit on the small side for us, but lovely, none the less. Beautiful lower Manhattan views from a high floor room and a super comfortable bed. Another plus was that we hard ZERO noise from the street below (and that's rare in Manhattan at ANY hotel!). The bar, Tilbey's was terrific. Nice friendly staff and excellent light bites. We shared a nice cheese plate, warm olives, roasted Brussels sprouts (yum) and the short rib sliders (excellent). Nice young vibe later on in the evening. It's definitely a younger, hip hotel, as most downtown hotels are. Hard to find the reception desk to check in (hidden in the back), but once checked in, smooth sailing. Excellent location, walk to Soho,Nolita, Little Italy (Torrisi Italian Specialties!), Katz's Deli, Russ & Daughters, DBGB.........everything within a 5 minute walk. Definitely a nice weekend destination. We would definitely come back.

“Great price, central location” We stayed here for four nights in early May. There were four of us travelling so we booked a room with two double beds and its own bathroom. The price was great and the hotel itself is located within walking distance to Grand Central Station, with 33rd station being the closest subway station. The purpose of our trip was mainly to sight see so the hotel room was mainly used just to sleep in and it served that purpose quite well. The room was cleaned on a daily basis and cable tv and air conditioning is also included. If you are not planning to spend the bulk of your trip staying indoors in your hotel and it's not meant to be a romantic getaway, then I would definitely recommend staying at Hotel 31. The price is right and the neighbourhood is central and safe.
“Not a quiet hotel” I heard sirens all night long. Guests were loud also. Parking was pricey.

“Really nice hotel but a bit overpriced for what it is” Went to Seattle for the Chargers/Seahawks football game. Splurged on hotel at Olive 8 because it got great reviews online. It was nice certainly but nothing super fancy. My fiance thought the late night happy hour in the bar was superb. The room's walls were a bit bare and it almost had this feel like they just opened. When we got there we were told the only way we could get a good view would be to upgrade. Since we booked directly with the hotel we were already paying full price for the room and opted not to. Our room faced an office building which we could see right ito. You can easily walk to our hotel from the Public Market so the location was great...just not sure the hotel was worth the money.

“Unfortunate service gaps bring hotel down” Let me start on a positive note: The Michelangelo is a decent hotel. It is located just close enough to Times Square...a few blocks away from the mayhem and noise but still in an area that keeps the theaters and many tourist sites in walking distance. Our rooms were clean. The lobby is nice and the elevators cruise between the floors practically at jet speed. Some of the staff that we encountered were very helpful and friendly. If we had been paying to stay at a Holiday Inn, I would have mentioned all of the above and chalked this up to a decent review. Our expectations of this property, however, were on par with the price of the rooms. I'd suggest that you can do much better for your money, even in the same area of midtown. The downsides? We stayed in one of the pricier rooms, and it was weirdly lacking in many of the basic amenities that you'd find elsewhere (in NYC or Iowa, for that matter). No coffee pot, no safe, no iron/ironing board. Though we did have at least one towel per guest, there was one day where we were left to arm wrestle over a single washcloth. When our early-risers ventured downstairs to look for coffee at 6:30am each day, they were out of luck -- they had to leave the hotel and travel a half block down for a cup o' Joe. Those of us sticking to colder drinks had to search the floors for an ice machine (Handy tip: It is on the 5th floor). Coffee did finally appear in the lobby a little later in the morning alongside a tray of small, dry pastries. This is the 'Continental breakfast' advertised with the room rates. Not a huge deal to us, but I haven't ever stayed in a hotel where anyone tried to pass this off as a 'free breakfast'. The hotel would be better off not promoting it this way and just offering it in the lobby as a nice amenity. I also just noticed that we had almost the exact same experience mentioned by an earlier review here on TripAdvisor. I had confirmed a room with two king beds a few days before we arrived. Upon check-in, we were told that there was a problem with the reservation and that a room with two beds was not available. The manager showed us up to a one bedroom suite with a single king bed, and offered to upgrade us and provide cots. Our kids are willing to sleep pretty much anywhere and the manager was graciously allowing us to check-in early, so we agreed. He called up a few minutes later to offer a larger suite for an additional $100/night. Still just one bed, but the living room was much larger and we wouldn't have to be climbing over cots. We agreed to the upgrade. The problem? The first night they brought up a single cot, but no blankets or pillows. Second night? Blankets, but no pillows. It was totally fine for one kid to sleep on the large sofa, but it would have been great to have the linens to make it into a bed. Though I still feel like the additional room charge was reasonable for the extra space, the room certainly didn't feel like an 'upgrade' when we had to sort out basic sleeping arrangements for two people every night. A stay in a hotel charging over $300/night shouldn't be that much work.

“Clean, spacious but noisy” We stayed at this property January 13 - 16. As many of the previous reviewers noted, there is construction across 57th street from the Salisbury and on Sunday, 1/15, they started jackhammering before 8:00 AM. We had a one bedroom suite that consisted of a living area with a sofa sleeper and two full sized beds in the bedroom. Our daughter slept on the sofa sleeper and complained the first night that the bed was uncomfortable. She ended up sleeping on the couch (unfolded) the last two nights. The mattresses on the full sized beds were very firm. The bathroom was small but clean. The suite had a small refrigerator and microwave. There is a market nearby (the Dali Market) where we were able to stock our fridge. Continental breakfast is available for $9/person. It was a little disappointing, I think they could learn from the Hampton Inn or Residence Inn how to do continental breakfast. Biggest complaint is that the only sources of protein available were cheese slices and hard boiled eggs. With Styrofoam plates and plastic utensils it was difficult (and entertaining) to trying to crack the hard boiled egg.

“Dated hotel, but good location” The best part of this hotel is its convenient location - for baseball fans, conference attendees, or people looking to walk to the harbor. I also liked the computing center in the lobby which offered free limited printing. Otherwise, the lobby and rooms are looking worn and aren't kept very clean. In my room there were several missing light bulbs, red stains on the curtains, lots of dust on furniture, and the sink was missing the drain/stopper. Not exactly what I was expecting for the price I paid. The food options in the hotel are decent. There's a small food shop for a quick breakfast, a bar/grill, a Morton's steakhouse, and room service. Morton's has a nightly happy hour which is very affordable.

“That is all you needed” This is one of the three major hotels connected to the Copley Place, so one is right in the center of action. The room is quite adequate and modern. If anything the bathroom is small but it has good tub and shower, nothing fancy here. I like their indoor pool and fitness center with sun parlor amid them, when the weather allows you can enjoy the sunshine. If you like to shop or have fun, the Copley Place and the surrounding can let you lost for hours. It is also walkable to Boston Common. Certainly don't mind to stay here again when in Boston.

“Great Location” OK ! I first booked a Kimpton hotel few blocks away from this hotel and then changed it !Anyway, I am not comparing this one to a Kimpton hotel, but overall it was a good stay. The room is clean and updated. The free parking is a HUGE plus, cause we had two cars. The location is great. Can't be better for me. I just grabbed a cup of tea from the breakfast bar, but it was usual breakfast. It is interesting that somebody said he skipped it because it wasn't organic !! I am not sure even Ritz-Carlton offers organic food for free ! The lobby is not as clean as the room and has a strange smell. Also the front-desk had problem with communication. If you want to be in the area and don't want to spend a lot of money book this motel. It is not disappointing at all !

“Expect to be staying at an apartment” I think most of the disappointments noted by other travelers is that they may have expected a hotel. THE ENVOY CLUB IS NOT A HOTEL. It is much more like an apartment building with short term rentals and a few extra services to make your stay more enjoyable. We stayed at Envoy Club May 29-Jun 3 and absolutely loved it! We had a studio apartment and used the loveseat sofa bed for our daughter. (The bed was not that comfortable, but we were all dead tired each night.) The limited service provided clean towels each day and tidied up our kitchen for us. Our bed was also made. This service is optional, but we accepted it to get the clean towels. We loved the full kitchen, espeically for reheating wonderful restaurant meals which were just too much to eat at one sitting. Microwave popcorn was also handy. The bathroom was clean and well equipped with a great shower. Once we learned how to use the cross town M34 bus, the location was great. If you're only using the subway, the hike to the 6 is several blocks. The cross town bus is a breeze. High-speed internet (wi-fi) in the room worked perfectly. The rooftop deck is fantastic! Great views day and night. Didn't use the fitness room or the laundry. Great bagel shop around the corner and Rocky's on Second Ave for Pizza is excellent. I also enjoyed Ali Baba for Turkish food on 34th...a very short walk.

“Great location for Broadway shows and the remodeled rooms sleep 5!” This hotel is currently undergoing renovations in the lobby and guestrooms. I believe the rooms are being remodeled from the top down. We stayed on the 36th floor and had a remodeled room. We stayed for five nights (July 25-30). Our room had two doubles plus a chair that converted into a bed to sleep an additional person. We had plenty of room for two adults and three kids. There are very few rooms in New York that will fit families of five, but we were thrilled to find this one did. The rooms are also quite large and include some good storage, too. Even with the five of us and our "stuff" we were not cramped. Decor in the new rooms is very chic. The bathrooms are not fancy or luxurious, but they are large, and the counter has plenty of room for your stuff. Housekeeping was good as well. I'd requested extra towels on the reservation, and each morning, when they cleaned the room, they automatically included six towels (rather than the standard four). One day, the maid even arranged my daughter's stuffed animals on the beds. We were just around the corner from (and literally the second closest room to) the elevator bank, but the room was very, very quiet. We never heard elevators or people next door or in the halls, so as others have noted, soundproofing is really good here. We did not have trouble with the elevators at all, and we actually found that they worked pretty well handling the crowds. We had breakfast twice at the Starbucks on the 8th floor. The other days, we went over to Junior's (which is a reasonably priced place with good food and service), so we never ate in the hotel's restaurants. The lobby is being renovated, but that did not impact our stay at all. We were too busy enjoying New York to care about some construction. We also used the valet parking. It's expensive as expected ($65 for our SUV), but the valets were quick and pleasant on arrival and departure. The location is excellent if you want to see shows. We were just a few steps from several theatres. It was great to see "The Addams Family," walk around to the stage door to get autographs (my kids were thrilled with this--and Brooke Shields and Roger Rees were very nice to them) and then literally cross the street to enter our hotel.

“Redefines the term 'pet-friendly'” It's difficult to find fault with this hotel. The location is great, the rates are reasonable, the service if fast and friendly and the rooms are clean and comfortable. And they are truly a pet friendly property, probably the most pet-friendly I've ever been to. Upon arrival to m room, I was greeted with welcome 'gifts' for my cat and dog, special dog bowls, pet treats and a note with their names (and mine) welcoming us. One thing I noticed too is that the rooms seem to be sound proofed. One night when I was walking down the hall, what sounded like 2 bull mastiffs about to break the door down with their loud barks as I walked by, and then when I got into my room, I heard nothing. The bed was comfortable and the room was very clean. I'm a stickler about clean hotel rooms, and this room really was spotless. The gym is adequately sized, and the equipment is nice. It's a good sign when you have to wrack your brain to think about what could use improvement, so I'll say that the queen sized rooms are a bit on the small side. The king rooms were a better size.

“Many Hassles” This is a great elegant building but I found that despite the charm there were many inconveniences. First, the rooms are small which I found typical of New York style rooms and it was hard to find any room for bathroom accessories. For check-in you have to ascend a flight of stairs and there was a long line unless you were a Hilton Honors member. There was a certain level of arrogance among the staff we encountered (check-in, bar, valet, luggage check), possibly due to the popularity of the hotel. The common areas always seemed to be very crowded. There was an $18 fee for the gym and the spa was prohibitively expensive. The room had modern furniture and bathrooms and was kept very clean. We did see room service items in the hallway the entire weekend however. For those not familiar with Chicago, it is right downtown and close to all the CTA lines and major Chicago attractions (as well as shopping). We were not disappointed given that we paid a cheap Hotwire rate and given that we have never stayed here but in the future I would stick with a property with more personalized service and less hassle.

“Great location, but.....” We were disappointed with this hotel. We usually love the Marriott chain, but this hotel was a bit of a fail. The staff is very friendly and very helpful. But the state of the hotel is really bad. The carpets are all stained and filthy looking. Our room looked tired and rundown. The bathroom was full of black hair. Housekeeping was nice, but I did clean the bathroom floor because of the hair. The pool area is downright ghetto. I did not want my kids swimming in that pool which was too bad as that is something we really enjoy. The location is so great, right on the riverwalk and we spent most of our time there or visiting family. Love San Antonio and can't wait to get back, but it will very certainly be at a different hotel.

“Great Airport Hotel” I have no complaints about our one night stay at the O'Hare Hilton Got a really good deal using Hotwire.com for about $60 per night. Great airport location, walk to the terminal. Check in desk in the lobby for most major airlines (demestic) Nice on-site sports bar. Clean large rooms. Even though this hotel is on the airport property you can't hear the planes landing ot taking off! Some rooms do offer a view of the runways.

“fantastic hotel!” The location of this hotel can't be beat. Right in the heart of Nob Hill, way up on a hill with views of the Bay Bridge, Grace Cathedral, this hotel is great for someone wanting to explore SF. The room is small but clean and modern and comfortable. You'll of course pay for the location but its worth it.

“Another excellent stay at the Hyatt” I was fortunate to get a good deal on Priceline for our 10th anniversary weekend. I let the Hyatt know it was a special occasion and they treated us like royalty. We were given a corner king room on the 17th floor with a great view looking up and down the Delaware River. Many thanks to Mike Costello for providing us with a bottle of wine and a chocolate covered strawberries upon arrival. We could not of had a nicer room. There was water in every direction. The room had a comfortable king bed, mini fridge, LG TV and a large bathroom that also included a window looking over the river. It was quiet sleeping at night. I paid $12.95 for very efficient internet for a 24 hour period. We ordered breakfast to our room and it was delivered promptly and was satisfying. The staff was helpful and friendly throughout our stay. We did use the fitness center and it had all modern equipment. The cardio machines had TV’s and plugs for I-Pods. There was a sauna and all the extras one would expect from a quality gym. The pool area was plenty big enough and connected to the fitness center. We did not eat at Keating’s, but stopped at the bar for a nightcap and found it to be welcoming and relaxing. The only negative I see is the Hyatt is not close to downtown. Being January we did walk downtown but took a taxi back to the hotel. Society Hill is close and we ate at Bistro Romano one night and it was fantastic. We would have no problem returning here in the future.

“Elegant Detail” Great hotel with excellent staff. The rooms are really well decorated. The free shoe shine is a fantastic bonus, and they have the most frequent elevators. Never once did I need to wait; press the button and the doors open. The location is not remote. It is easy to walk everywhere, and they have plenty of taxis waiting.

“Curious Hotel” Seems to have promise, but I have stayed here 3-4 times and it is very inconsistent. The construction next door is a real issue and will be for a while! It seems to have undergone a management change at least once over the last year.

“Great stay @ Marriott Marquis!” Booked 4 nights stay at this hotel sometime in January and got a real good rate. Liked that the hotel was in the middle of theatre district and very close to the theatre we went to. Close to a lot of good restaurants like Sardi's, Juniors, Carmines, Bubba Gump Shrimp. Close to Good Morning America, Virgin Megastore, the heart of Times Square. Beds were smalller than usual double bed but we made do. As long as it was clean and comfortable, we were happy.

“Great place for a business meeting, very attentive to detail.” This botique hotel is only a couple of blocks off the seafront/docks in downtown Seattle. Also it is only a few blocks south of Pike Street Market, as well as many restaurants. The staff is extremely friendly and will go out of their way to indulge whatever you need. The rooms are quite amazing, with bathtubs that fill from the ceiling, well appointed granite tile, and interesting lighting combinations. Each room is equipped with a French Press for making coffee. Truly light-blocking curtains that overlapped easily on the windows. Complimentary WiFi, which way too many upscale hotels charge for is a nice touch. I was there for a business meeting, which was held in the hotel. Excellent cocktail reception, moving through a curtained door to the dining area. The dining area had lots of glass, including the ceiling, with retractable panels that allow for those rare too-much-sun days in Seattle.

“Great Stay at this Times Square Area Hotel” This hotel is located one block away from Broadway and 48th St. It is a very easily accessible hotel from Eighth Ave and has a lot of great things here. Rooms are very comfortable and the staff go out of there way to say hello and help in any way they can. The front desk staff was just great and kept me entertained each night i was there. My room looked out at Eighth Ave, and to the exception of the Firehouse next door there was no noise that i could hear. The internet access was good and the tv selection was good as well. Only about a 5 min drive from NY Penn Station and less than a 10 min drive to Javits Convention Center. This hotel is very popular with groups and business travelers. There is a business center located in the front lobby and there is a small store that have the usual luxuries. The restaurant is good and if you are a preferred Hilton Member you get a free breakfast included in your stay each day. I would stay here again.

“Nice Rooms for the price” I loved our room at this hotel. I got a great deal directly through the hotel's website (it was cheaper than Priceline and other online travel sites). We had a separate living room w/ couches, flat screen TV, and pull out sofabed. It was pretty roomy and cozy. The bathroom was very spacious but I hated the pedestal sink. However, there was a mantel above the sink so I was able to throw my stuff on there. As for food, the hotel has a great restaurant bar/grill. Great menu selection and reasonably prices for the area. We grabbed some dinner there right before we headed out to the airport. It was a good choice. The location of the hotel is pretty good. It's not that close to a metro station but def w/in walking distance. The hotel is nearby to clubs/bars if you're into that kind of scene. Also, very nice staff. No complaints and would stay here again :)

“Bring ear plugs” Bring ear plugs and you will be fine! It is noisy outside and the walls are paper thin, but apart from that it is fine. Good location, huge rooms, fine service, some extras like a yoga kit delivered to your room - and I paid 60 dollars per night through Expedia! That is good value! I

“Loved the Bulfinch” Recently stayed at the Bulfinch while in town to see Madonna. The hotel was fantastic. Unique, boutique style hotel located right downtown Boston. Walking distance to everything. Just around the corner from the TD Banknorth Center which is great if you are in town for a show. The rooms were spotless and nicely furnished. Very stylish. The beds were SO comfortable and the air conditioning system was amazing. It was really hot in Boston while we were there so it was GREAT to return to such a cool room. The bathroom was gorgeous and again, spotless. Loved this hotel and would absolutely stay again.

“Good quality budge Hotel without the Frills” Stayed at this hotel during our family vacation to Seattle/Vancouver area for 2 nights. Overall the hotel is not bad consider the fact that we got a good deal to stay there for 2 nights during our trip. The hotel is nice and spacious, the room was spacious as well, clean and the beds were very soft and comfy. We ate out at the upstairs restaurant for dinner the second night, the food was not so bad but could've been much better. The service was supar and there was nobody to greet us for few minutes. I would expect better service for this type quality hotel or restaurant. I can see why the place looked empty. If you are here for a family trip, this place is somewhat close to the shopping and restaurants area nearby. However, it is not the most convenient place to stay due to the uphill climb if you are out of shape. My kids were complaining due to the walking and the shops/restaurants is a good 10 minutes away which is not so bad. I would stay at the Red Lion hotel which was our second leg of the trip, a much better location, when you step out of Red Lion, you will be with the crowd and all the coffee shops and stores and the mall too. Overall, I would rate this a 3 star, would probably not stay here next time.

“Manky” I found the service efficient and fine, but the room was pretty manky. The furniture was pretty beat up and the carpet, although vacuumed, seemed pretty dirty. The bathroom's shower curtain was moldy and there was shower gel or something stuck on to it. The biggest problem is the lack of ventilation. There are no controls for air circulation, not even an air vent for the bathroom, which is desperately needed. The location is good, but the moldy shower curtain was a huge turn-off to say the least.

“Nasty and rundown!” My company puts us up here so I have no say so in choosing the hotel and I have to go there 1-2 times a month. Like the pics show, water stains on the ceiling, missing baseboards and worn carpets and dirty floors are de rigeur here. But to lift my toilet lid and see urine stains was downright disgusting. DO NOT pay money to stay here. I have seen cleaner Motel 6's.

“great location and nice price” Hyatt was offering a 30% discount from the best available rate on their website, which made booking here very attractive. It's only a few blocks from the Boston Common and right next to the theater district. It's walking distance to the Back Bay and Beacon Hill. The Boston Ballet (at the Opera House) is right across the street, which was very convienent. The room itself was nice, with very comfortable beds (my friend said they were a little too soft though, but I thought they were great). Their fitness center is also decent, with a selection of cardio equipment (4 treadmills, a few ellipticals, bikes and rowing machines), as well as weights and weight machines. There is a small pool, designed for laps (not very children-friendly if that's what you're looking for). Overall, it was a great experience for the weekend and I would definitely stay again.

“Convenient for Business or Family Travel” I have stayed at this property 3 times now (November 2011, March and May 2012) for business travel and have not been disappointed. There service is exceptional, especially by the dining personnel. If you are not familiar with Homewood, these are all-suite hotels. The rooms have a full kitchen and living room, separate from the bedroom, so there is plenty of room to stretch out. There are two televisions with a variety of channels - not just the standard news and sports channels. I was staying during a business trip, so was not in the room during the days at all. The hotel is adjacent to a large business park and gets a lot of business travel. It is also close to the baseball stadium and was FULL during spring training. As the other reviewers have stated, there is only fast food places near-by. There is a nice manager's reception in the evening (mon-Thurs) with a meal and drinks. Again, the service is impeccable. Breakfast - the service is great but the various baked egg concoctions leave something to be desired. While there was a different variety each day, it just isn't great for a "big-breakfast" person. If you are good with toast and a yogurt, it will be fine.

“Great Hotel !!! Hyatt Mission Bay is the way to go!” Wow another great hotel. The pool was fantastic! Love the tower rooms and the view was fantastic ! This is the first time and it was great. Staff was very nice and friendly, the spa was fantastic and the food was good in the Red Marlin? I would highly recommend this hotel!

“Lovely lobby but don't stay here” Stayed here for one night and I won't be staying there again. The lobby is stunning , so very beautiful and the bar is very nice too. The check in staff were perfectly pleasant on check in and check out in a prerequisite form filing way. The room and hallway to the room were a different matter. I'm all for artistic shabby chic or for historic hotels - but this was neither. The wallpaper outside my room in the hallway was peeling away in huge sheets, the carpet was badly worn and faded both in the hall and in my room. Then of course the dark "old" furniture was in dire need of some beeswax. The bathroom looked like it hadn't been updated since the 1930's but not in a cute retro way, cracked paint, the air vent had 20 years worth of dust attached to it and the toileteries were all mismatched different brands and half used! It's in a useful location and I can understand the desire not to stay in a "chain" hotel with bland decor but there are nicer rooms to be had in New York - go to the Waldorf for drinks and have a look at the lovely lobby.

“Great location for a good deal” Room-small rooms, but updated decoration. Room was clean and functional. Wish it had a fridge. Location- excellent location. Easy access to public transportation. Parking lot next door. Trader joes across the street was very convenient. Good deal for the price, booked this for the price, location, and breakfast included.

“Wonderful clean, safe, place to stay” I took my mom to NYC for her 65th birthday to go shopping. I come here quite often with my girlfriends and we usually stay near Canal Street, but this time my mom wanted to stay closer to downtown. This hotel was so clean and nice and was such an excellent location. Walking only a few blocks to Macy's, and a ton of stores! Subway was also a few blocks, near Macy's actually. The room had two nice double beds, and was pretty large for NYC. The bathroom and shower were pretty small but were very clean. The staff was very nice. This hotel is great for the price!

“Rooms in Need of an Upgrade” When entering the hotel you are greeted to a gorgeous lobby. It takes you back to a time where the Roosevelt was a top notch hotel that catered to aristocracy. Unfortunately this is where it ends... The rooms are in a definite need of an upgrade. There is a sign in the lobby saying that each room has been upgraded, but I am not sure that I see what progress has been made. The bathrooms were a bit hideous. Mould growing everywhere, urine smell and extremely compacted. Chips in the tile and a bit of a crack in the mirror. The room itself was showing wear on the wallpaper (peeling and dirty). The bedding while clean, had stains on it. We were in a room with two double beds and they were very comfortable. The room was well air conditioned and thank goodness for this! It was unbelievable hot out during our stay. The staff were very friendly and willing to help out! The hotel gets an A+ in this regard. The hotel does not offer free internet anywhere. I spent $30 for two days of internet. I was not happy at all. The biggest point that this hotel has in its favour is the location. 45th and Madison! Loved where we were. We are huge theatre fans and loved being within walking distance of the theatre district, but not directly in the middle of the madness. No evidence of bed bugs! Thank goodness. Only stay here if you get a really good deal! There are much better properties in the area.

“Incredible View” I absolutely adored my room at the Hyatt Regency in Chicago. The view was incredibly amazing. The hotel is in a very convenient location. Great choice when visiting the Chicago area.

“Great Location, Fair Price, Nice Hotel” I spent one night here, while in Chicago for a business trip. I believe the hotel just recently opened, so everything seemed pretty new. The check in was quick and easy, and Leo the doorman was very friendly. My room was clean and comfortable, especially the bed. I loved the FREE wireless internet service (nowadays, far too many hotels gouge for that) and the FREE breakfast was more than sufficient. I had dinner with an old high school buddy, so I can’t speak to the restaurants, but Starbucks and Dunkin’ Donuts were in close proximity. The best thing about the hotel? My room rate was $116/night, which is pretty hard to find in downtown Chicago! The hotel was an easy train ride from Midway (at $5.50 round trip, why take a cab?) and the walk from the El, depending upon which station you exit, was just a block or two. The only flaw was my failure to ask for an “inside” room. Chicago is an all night town and the street noise was a little irritating for this fairly light sleeper. Overall, a good stay and I would not hesitate to return to this La Quinta.

“Don't Bother” I stayed here via a win on Priceline - good thing i didnt pay full rack rate for this hotel! I had one night that I just wanted to relax after a business trip in Chicago and should have continued my stay at the Affinia around the block! I arrived on a rainy Friday, tired and exhausted from the work week. I was here alone, just wanted to chill and relax and take in the Michigan Avenue sights. The hotel has a very odd entrance. You arrive into the hotel to the bellman's area - - the bellman gladly took my two bags and gave me a ticket/receipt. I figured he would just bring the bags up to my room. NOT. They were SO busy with hundreds of bags in this small area -- and then that particular area leads you to a whole other section of elevator banks -- taking you up to the lobby on the 2nd floor. I figured that out....went to the registration level and checked in. (Check in process took forever - the line was very long). While i was there, this poor guy, (father of the bride) was already complaining about his very small room. I was thinking...OH NOOOO - i just got here and there are problems already? I got to my room on the 19th floor and it was TINY. Very poor layout, not very updated just a little box and a very small bathroom that was just looked like they attempted to renovate it, but it was still old. Only one person can fit i there at a time, put it that way. The noise level wasnt bad at all compared to the Affinia around the block. My room faced Michigan Avenue and not the hospital down the block...that was THE only good thing - the room was quiet and i managed to sleep well. The bed was just OK - -nothing ultra comfy/modern. Oh, and internet was additional at $9.95. This was the first time that Priceline has ever disappointed me with a hotel. I wouldn't ever stay here again. And, if I paid full price for this hotel, I would have been really angry. Do yourself a favor, find another hotel in the city.

“Love this Hotel , So I will Forgive Its Few Trespasses” My daughter and I stayed here for a college program held at the Palmer House in February. Although the place was jammed between our program entering and a Model UN convention departing, check in was well controlled and quick. Our room on a Hilton;s Honors Floor was not huge but was very well decorated and had great beds, and updated fixtures. Maid service was spotty but minor problems were quickly renovated.. The hotel of history as mentioned by others. A favorite feature are the photos of the performers who played the Empire Room from Sinatra to Pearl Bailey , Jack Benny and Buddy Hackett. I upgraded to a package that included internet and gym membership. Since I brought work with me, the upgrade was well worth the cost .The gym is fantastic with many machines and loaner ipods. There is also a great spa.. Our last morning the internet was not working and their really was no hot water. However a quick request yielded a discount of my bill. The location is of course perfect,close to several El and subway stations, and literally a block to the Art Institute. Three are many restaurants to choose from in the area (Miller's Pub two doors down is just great and open through the wee hours) so there is no need to dine in the hotel's mediocre restaurants. Staying at the Palmer House was a great part of our Chicago experience, and I look forward to returning.
