“Great location but very expensive parking” Second time we visited this property and we weren't disappointed. The rooms are large and well laid out. The bathrooms are functional. The rooms are kept well cleaned. The location is excellent as we were able to walk to the Wharf, as well as to North Beach. The only drawback to this property is the parking. It is very tight and very expensive but the valet staff is very friendly.

“Good Spot, particularly for business travel.” Equally close to the business district, shopping and AT&T Park, the W is a nice choice for most folks. The lobby has just been remodeled and is very nice and funky. At night it terms into a serious lounge with club music and bar. The rooms are typical W rooms but are closing in on their due date for a refresh. Still, they're nice and comfortable, and the W bed is always terrific.

“Exceeded expectations!” We had a one night stay - everything was just great. The breakfast was your standard hotel fare. Room was very clean and comfortable. Staff very nice. Slightly difficult to find as the I-465 exit is closed.
“Probably not the usual Hilton standard but no real criticism” We stayed for 3 nights and found the hotel perfectly acceptable. Most Staff were friendly, hot tub and gym were good. Room very clean.

“Unique Hotel - Great Location” The hotel was defintiely unique - it looked like it was from the Adams Family. It was in a good location next to the House of Blues. The parking was pricey - $49 per day; luckily it was included in our rate from Travel Zoo. The hotel staff was very friendly. The hotel was clean and the beds were very comfortable.

“Comfortable, clean, and awesome customer service!” My mother and I arrived very late... a little after midnight. The girl at the front desk was so nice and even gave us a voucher for complimentary breakfast in the morning since we were only going to be staying for one night. It was a very appreciated gesture and the breakfast in the morning was better than the buffet breakfast that I've had at other hotels! The room was very nice and updated! The beds were very comfy,my mother stated she had not slept so well in such a long time. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and are looking forward to returning again!

“Great one night stay near union square” I came into SF last night for a conference and stayed at the Hotel Frank. Great location near union square (where I normally stay when in SF). I had the king room, which was very sizable for a boutique hotel off of union square. Big TV on the wall, nice desk, and clean and modern bathroom. Overall the hotel has a more modern feel, actually. I definitely recommend if staying in SF and you want a great location and nice hotel.

“Unless House of Blues is in your cards - the hotel is a WILDCARD” Although very cool with hip decor - I could envision having a party here, but not a long weekend with my girlfriend. UNLESS, i was in a band playing at the House of Blues then it would be perfect. I can smell the place now just thinking of it - if youve been there, you know the smell - just kind of an odd place - not bad, but certainly not my taste

“pretty good- likely to come back” the hotel is brand new, so i think the rates are still relatively low- i paid $200++ for a Large King-sized room. The Restaurant si not open yet, but who cares- plenty of options nearby to choose from. The room was nice, spacious, new (of course) and everything looked fab. enjoyed the ipod docking station. I had no problems with the shower, unlike other posters here. I used the well-equipped gym every day. Used the hotel's umbrellas, because it rained every day.. Wireless internet at $10 a day (it should be free, really...) but it worked a charm. I like Tribeca, so the location was good for me, and subway access is excellent. My only comments were that housekeeping needs some improvement- but i left a comment note so i hope they wisen up. I used to stay at the Tribeca Grand, 2 blocks north, which i would rate slightly higher but which was 90$ more expensive so Smyth provides better value for money, at these rates.

“Nice stay at a Luxury hotel that is showing some wear” My husband and I returned to the Mandarin in New York recently for our anniversary. We first stayed there 2 years ago following our wedding. The first stay was amazing - the property was still "new" and everything about it seemed luxurious. This time around we noticed a few things were lacking. The furniture is beginning to show wear, especially in the Lobby Lounge. We were given a handicapped room, of which the only problem I had was that the shower had a regular plastic curtain instead of glass. Diminished the luxe somewhat for me. The bathing amenities were very nice, as were the towels, robes and linens. The LCD TV was o.k - the HDTV channels went out several times which was quite annoying. We had to call IT to come reset it. The bed is extremely comfortable - definitely a highlight! The service is still pretty high-level, but nothing that I haven't experienced at other hotels. The Lobby Lounge is great! The view is fantastic and unparalleled- I definitely recommend stopping there for a drink or dessert. The location of the hotel is very convenient. Great shops in walking distance, and the subway is around the corner. Overall, our stay was pleasant and the accommodations were nice, but I do not think we will stay there again. It doesn't seem as luxurious as it once was.

“Service and Location!” I just spent a night with a bunch of girls at the W Seattle this past weekend. It was a great spot to convene and rest our heads after shopping and eating out. And because of its central location in DT Seattle, you can walk to everything! I was mostly impressed with the hotel's service, as the facilities were on par with other Starwood properties. The front desk staff were helpful and happy, and almost every other staff member I came across had a smile on their face. What I Liked - the lounge area below the lobby - free wifi in the lounge - the Acura car service that would take you around the city - the lobby's coffee by morn, and infused water by day - the mattresses and sheets were ultra comfortable - the rooms are a good size, and include a long and comfy banquette beside the window What To Know - the Acrua car service only runs until 6pm on weekends - if the valet parking is busy, you have to line up on the street to get in as the loading area is tight - there's a beautiful Parisian bakery across the street called Belle Epicurean {in the base of the Fairmont} - the valet parking is $45 with taxes which is on the high-end of what city hotels {not including NYC} charge for parking. - pets are allowed.

“Very good stay!” My husband and I stayed in this hotel on our recent trip to Memphis. Located in the heart of the city, it is within walking distance to Beale Street and some great restaurants. The hotel is new and modern and we had a great room with a comfortable bed. We appreciated especially the washer and dryer on the second floor. Coming from Europe, it was such a luxury to be able to do our laundry in a hotel!!! The complimentary breakfast was phantastic and had just about everything your heart desired. The only negative thing was the noise from the loud music coming from Beale Street! Although the hotel states that it is not a "quiet" hotel and if you want to have peace and quietness, you should look elsewhere, it bothered us. Surely putting in sound proof windows would make a difference? Fortunately I always have ear plugs with me.

“Wyndham Boston was Perfect” Long weekend with the kids and was the perfect location. Walking distance to most everything, convenient to the subway for everything else. Room was much bigger than an average hotel room and concierge was very helpful. A great spot.

“Top Notch Hotel in a A+ Location” Stayed at the Muse hotel on Saturday night of Martin Luther King weekend. We arrived several hours before check in and were given a good sized room on the 14th floor. While the express elevator to the higher floors was a little slow, the 14th floor has the advantage of having both the express and the "regular" elevators and we never had a problem getting to our floor. Because the Muse is a boutique hotel each room is different. Our room has rather large with a king size bed, a sitting chair and a large bathroom with good counter space. In the morning, we ate breakfast at NIOS restaurant in the lobby. We both had the buttermilk pancakes, and they were excellent. I look forward to our next trip to New York and hope that I can stay at the Muse again.

“Good but not the best around” I have stayed here before and decided to stay around the holidays. I got a great deal being a SPG member (their hotel rewards program). I can't complain much about my stay based on the price but here is some info for others. The hotel is in a great location for shoppers, tourists and nearby conventions. The rooms are small but the beds are nice, clean and comfortable. Water in the bathroom was loud but the bathroom was clean. The work area was small and would be cumbersome for those on business. Do not get a room on the same level as the pool, the hallway smelled like chlorine. The only advantage to a lower floor was that I did not have to wait for an elevator- it was slow and crowded. The lobby was crowded and confusing to get to from the mall level. Staff seemed nice though I had little interaction with them. This is not a bad hotel, I would recommend staying there if you can get a price is right. For the same price you may be able to stay at the nearby, nicer Marriott or Westin.

“awesome location and price, but far from perfect” I stayed in this hotel for 5 nights on a business trip to NYC. The location and price were my main reasons for choosing it, and it could not have been more convenient to my business needs (all in midtown) and to restaurants. There is a subway stop (blue line) just around the corner, plus red, yellow, and orange trains within 2-3 blocks' walk. Plenty of eating and bars extremely close by, and the price (in January) was fantastic. However, the overall quality could improve. The room was very small, which didn't bother me, but also very dark-- no overhead light, only two small lamps. The bathroom had ample light, and I often left the bathroom door open to better illuminate the room. Wasn't working in the room, so again, not a huge issue. My room was on the third floor facing the street, and on one night, there was significant street noise from a bar opposite. Drilling in the street directly outside starting at 9am on several mornings-- annoying, but not severe, since I was getting ready for work by then. Bed was great, very clean and comfortable. Bathroom amenities excellent. Soft towels changed daily. No intrusive housekeeping service, but always efficient. The hotel advertises a 24-hour fitness center, but half of the equipment was busted and unusable. Lock to hold the seat in place on the exercise bike was broken, and the treadmill had an out-of-sort, "sorry for temporary unavailability" sign on it for my entire stay. Were they making an effort to get it repaired at all? The free weight bench was not broken. Room was a bit cold the first night, but fine all the others. The staff were very friendly, helpful, and efficient. On the whole, I would stay here again if the price were in this range. Next time I might personally change the lightbulbs to make the room brighter, and I'll hope that weather permits exercise in the Park. I've stayed at a Holiday Inn nearby, with much bigger rooms and fewer issues, but this definitely had an even better location.

“Excellent!” The Omni in San Diego was fantastic (unlike the Omni in Phila - old, dark and dusty). The service was exceptional, the rooms reasonably spacious and immaculately clean, the restaurant delicious with some of the best waiters/waitresses I have encountered (although expensive for dinner), and the rest of the facilities great. The view is fantastic, overlooking the water. It is right next to the Gaslamp district (lots of shops and restaurants) and the trolley. The only minor downsides are 1) No indoor pool, 2) strange system for valet parking in which every time you valet park, they have to go through the whole routine of getting your name and room number and writing it down, giving you a new ticket (instead of giving you 1 ticket for the entire stay), and 3) the lobby is a bit simple and small (not the grand lobbies in many of the hotels nearby). However, these are all truly minor flaws in a near flawless hotel. They do accept pets, a plus for pet owners (although if you have allergies, not sure if they have pet free rooms - they never brought it up nor did I). A few of the rooms on each floor have balconies (ask specifically if you want one). Overall, wonderful experience which will bring me back to them when I return to San Diego.

“Good value and airport parking.” Staff was very helpful. This hotel was formerly an Amerisuites and was converted. It was a comfortable stay for our purpose which was to get a good nights sleep, be close to the airport and leave our car in the parking lot. I found a better rate on Expedia and the hotel took off 20% which made for a great rate. The shuttle doesn't leave until 5am which is cutting it too close for some of the early flights. The shuttle was also out of service upon landing in San Antonio but the cost of leaving the car was worth it.

“One of the worst hotels in the world” OK. So I needed a hotel for a somewhat reasonable rate and everyone on here was quite kind. So I booked it. Well, we get in on Tuesday eve, late, 3 July and there is one person at reception and simply crazy goings on in the lobby. Low class people. White trash, Others you can figure out for yourself. It was like a circus. If I were 19, this might have been fun. Sorry, been there, done that. We go to our room. A jr. suite. Well, you get off on the floor and it's dimly lit. Bordello's are better lit than this joint. And it stinks. We get to our room and it smells like fee, a&& and cigarettes. Mindyou this is a non-smoking room. The room is dimly lit, spiders are hanging outside the windows, the furniture is old, the carpet reeks of wet feet and I-don't-know-what-else. I can't go on. Simply DO NOT STAY HERE. If they pay you to stay here, say NO THANK YOU. Absolute pit. They should implode it and start over. What was once a flagship hotel is now a hole. Period.

“Super small room in need of repair” I booked a two night stay for business and I can say with certainty I won't return. While the doorman greeted me warmly, the surly front desk clerk was among the more rude employees I've encountered at any hotel I've ever stayed at. The problem was that the room I booked, a non-smoking queen size bed was unavailable. She offered me a regular double or twin beds instead. If I wasn't 6-2 with feet that hang off of a double bed, I would have be okay with that. But when I asked if I could be moved the following day to the room I reserved, I got nothing but excuses as to why it couldn't be done. I even offered to check all of my bags with the bellman the next day, but the clerk insisted that I couldn't be moved unless I was physically present at the hotel -- even though ALL of my belongings would have been with the bellman. When I got the room, I saw paint flaking off the walls, mildew in the bathroom and a room which would have been considered super small, even by European standards. All this for more than $250 a night? No thanks.

“Great place to stay for price” Rooms were clean and the staff was friendly. Downtown San Diego was easily accessible from the hotel. Old Town was within walking distance. The continental breakfast was more than your average continental breakfast, you can cook your own waffles and it lasted us until the afternoon. I have stayed at top of the line hotel and this room was the same size. Good value for your money.

“Excellent NYC ROOM for Traveler” Stayed here for 2 weeks. If you have never stayed in a room in NYC, do not expect a spacious room. Square footage costs are high, so soace is expensive. The room was well thought out (though I wish I had a small fridge). Bathroom was big enough for me (6'2", 250+). Room was always clean. Elevators was very fast. You are south of midtown, but can easilt get most anywhere, with Madison Ave going all north on one end of the street and Fifth the other end going all south.

“Reserved room type not available” On Hilton HHonors website I made a reservation for a twin-bedded room but upon arrival to the hotel no such room was available. The lady at the front desk told me that I did not "reserve" but only "requested" certain room type which sounds as a weird argument to me. I may understand that a hotel is sold out but at the same time I do not understand why it cannot meet "requests" from HHonors members (I am Silver this year) especially if the reservation was made two months earlier (it was not a "last minute"). The front desk secured a room in nearby Hilton family hotel but it was quite inconvenient to move to another hotel after almost 24 hours travel from Europe.

“Everything you want - except exciting design” Much better than expected! It was one of the more economical options in Midtown at the time of booking, and since the rooms were said to be very big (and they are), I was expecting a catch. Looking at the pictures on tripadvisor, I thought the catch would be that the rooms were in fact old, outdated, smelly, noisy. Well, they're not! Newly refurnished, but in a very oldfashioned bland design. So, good location, very big, well equipped rooms. On first day we went to the $4 breakfast at 7am. Was okay. Next days we went there later (8ish) and then it was way too busy. Not worth the wait (not that good) so went to countless breakfast alternatives in the area. Would go back although usually I tend to go for bit more exciting design.

“Location” This was my fifth or sixth visit to the Inn at the Market. The property is better than most: the lobby is handsome, the rooms comfortable (though a little tired and ready for renovation, especially in the case of the bathrooms), the sun deck overlooking the harbor is a treat, and the staff is welcoming. The related restaurants, including not only Campagne but the related bistro in the basement and the lively breakfast place located separately within the same building, are really good. But the whole ballgame here is the location. The views, if you are fortunate enough to have a water-view room, are simply stunning -- not only because of the comings and goings of ferry boats, freighters, liners, Coast Guard cutters, fishing boats, and pleasure craft, but also because of the astonishing mountain range visible across Elliott Bay, which catches the sunset in truly glorious ways. It is also a pleasure to be able to walk half a block down the steep hill to the Pike Place Market, with all its produce and its bustle of activity. There are countless restaurants and clubs within walking distance. As gentrification neuters most of downtown Seattle, this area remains edgy, even a little challenging if you go in certain directions at certain times. The area is not for you if you are uncomfortable with street people and occasional strong smells. It is also a little inconvenient for business; and the business services in the hotel are not comparable to those in a Hyatt or a Marriott. But the tradeoff is a real sense of place, something you can't get in other cities or in Seattle's uptown hotels.

“Great location for family sightseeing” Right in the middle of the historic district, this hotel has recently been refurbished and the rooms were fine. If going in summer, they have a large rooftop pool that the kids will love. Self parking was $25.00 with unlimited in & out. Great front desk (Bryce?) comped our 1st night parking as Priority Club Platinum members, and dedicated convenient parking spaces for same. Great bars and restaurants right around the corner on Market between 2nd and 4th and all the historic sights within a two block area. Our room faced the Mint which offered an interesting tour for the kids.

“Convenient and comfortable” At just under $75, including taxes, from Priceline, we felt the room was a good deal. Room large enough and comfortable. We did not rent a car until the next day (walked a mile to Hertz rather than relying on shuttles), so did not have to content with high parking fee. We arrived late and were glad the lobby /bar was still open and serving food (and not just snacks) at 1 a.m. Only breakfast option, apart from the main restaurant, was a Starbucks. I did hear some aircraft and auto traffic noise from our room in the morning, but nothing major (my wife heard nothing). Not sure if the beds were as comfortable as those at the nearby Hilton but the price was better, at least by using Priceline. We waited perhaps 5 minutes for the hotel shuttle at LAX at midnight. You do need to look carefully, since many shuttles are shared by several hotels; you might find one bus serving 3 different hotels so you need to look carefully at the electronic signs. This hotel is one of the very closest to the hotel entrance.

“Central” Nice hotel in a good location in Downtown Philadelphia, close to Walnut Street and the convention centre. The room was very well appointed, with a chaise longue and large bathroom. Didn’t try the restaurant as there are plenty of good ones in the nearby Walnut Street area. There’s also a Starbucks in the hotel across the road. One tip – check your bill carefully at check-out as a number of mistakes were made on ours.

“Quiet and convenient in Murray Hill” I'm always up to trying a different location when I go to New York. This time we stayed at the Affinia Shelburne in Murray Hill. It was an easy decision after I secured some very good rates and the knowledge that the hotel had undergone extensive renovations. At first, things did not look too promising as our room was not ready for us at the 3 o'clock check-in. When it was available, the room, while spacious, faced the courtyard with a brick wall several feet away. Just too dark and depressing. So, having requested "open views", I asked for a change of room. The new room turned out to be a 1-bedroom suite with a view of the Empire State Building and the East River. It had a spacious living room with sofa, desk and chairs. The small bedroom had an immaculately sheeted queen bed. The cute kitchen was equipped with a very nice little fridge that had an automatic ice maker. Since I think NY tapwater is the greatest, this made for many refreshing glasses of ice water. (No need to open the $7 bottles of Fuji water!) One drawback to this room was a tiny bathroom. The shower was reminiscent of ones found in Europe: with only a partial glass enclosure. This meant taking a shower inevitably resulted in some splashing on the floor of the bathroom. Not really that big a deal. Another small quibble was the line of bathroom toiletries. They came in rustic, hard-to-open containers. Labels made one think they were some esoteric European brand but on closer examination, we saw that they were "made in China". All the staff was friendly and the maids were especially welcoming and had impeccable timing --- they knew just when to make up the room. There is a well-equipped fitness center on the second floor. The hotel restaurant, Rare, serves very good burgers and a nice breakfast, too. For future visits, I would not hestiate to stay here again, especially if the rates were similar to what I received on this visit.

“nice location, large rooms, but that’s it because VERY NOISY” First of all I realize it is difficult to find a good hotel in San Francisco for a good price. I paid around USD 200,- (taxes included) for this one and as the hotel is not that new, the room internet and parking could be much less expensive) Stayed here for 6 nights Positive: - good location (next to the shopping area, union square, market street, trams, cable car...) - pleasant and nice people at reception and at the reservation desk when calling - a lot of elevators (so you never wait too long to get one) - a bit expensive as the hotel is quite old - Burger King just across the road (convenient when travelling with kids) - good bed lining - lat flat screens (in new rooms) Negative: - very very noisy (even when on 17th floor and above), you can hear the police and ambulance sirens as if you were sitting in it (I than understood why there were free Quies ear plugs in the bathroom :-) : because of the bad thin windows - very big hotel (more than 1000 rooms), therefore always very busy and crowded. I know some people do not like it - bathroom not cleaned very well (a lot of hair found everywhere etc ...) - no safe in the rooms. The hotel offers a safe room (like in banks) but the problem is that you better be very well organised as you have to queue each time at the reception between the people check-in in/out to have access to the room - valet parking is not very well organised and very expensive (above USD 45) I would not specially come back to this hotel or recommend it to friends but again hotels are very expensive in S.F. Also be aware, that not all the rooms are renovated !!!

“Customer service excellent and hotel very nice” Stayed here one night - got a great rate on Expedia (around $50). Checked in before 1:00 because we were going to a Dallas Stars game at 2:00 and they were able to accomodate us. First room they gave us on the third floor reeked of smoke (despite not being a smoking room), so we called to inquire abotu switching rooms and without asking they upgraded us to a deluxe room which had a larger bed and a couch, which was very nice. The room was immaculate and very comfortable. One thing they might do to improve would be flat screen LCD televisions but other than that we had a great stay. They have a great business center, always have hot coffee in the lobby (its good too), and the staff is friendly. Location is also excellent for the AA Center, and many other downtown attractions. Would stay again.

“Trendy Party Hotel Near Airport” I was being bumped from hotel to hotel due to the ash cloud from Iceland and lots of travelers stuck in the east. I had to get out of the hotel I had been in so I found a great deal on the aloft hotel, which is a very trendy hotel in many ways. I enjoyed the atmosphere, I liked the rooms. The bar was excellent, very friendly and lots of locals come to visit which is always a nod to the quality of the service. The front desk is very pleasant but confused. I think they are still quite a young brand, sister to W in many ways.
“Simply Excellent” Simply excellent. Great room, perfect location and excellent service. The staff bends over backwards to accomodate their guests.

“Good stay” OK location, I enjoyed walking through Elfreth's Alley several times. Close to several restaurants. Walking distance to the historic area. Close to one subway station and several bus lines (one right in front), altho I believe SEPTA is on strike by now. The free shuttle van is pretty convenient and took me to the 30th St. Station even though their policy seems to be only for a 20 block radius. The cleaning was so-so, one day I noticed that the maid went through some of my papers, but of course you wouldn't leave anything valuable unlocked in your room. The reception tries hard but seemed to be short on help at times. I chose this hotel for the price, location, and the smoking room, which was really big by the way.

“Cheap & Cheerful” You really don't need anything more than this when staying in downtown Seattle. Hotel Max is close to everything and you can walk to all major spots downtown. Hotel Parking is expensive and will help boost what could have been a very good room rate. We didn't find the rooms or the bathroom to be too small after all we were not holding a ball in the bathroom! The room is just the right size if you are using it just to sleep. I don't recall front desk staff being particularly welcoming, helpful or concerned about us or our dog. Hotel Max is pet friendly for a fee.

“Exactly What You Expect When You Combine A Ritz Carlton and Four Seasons” When you stay at a Four Seasons and Ritz Carlton you expect more to say the least. The hotel staff were amazing! They catered to our every need and actually exceeded my expectations. We stayed in a Lake view Suite which were two rooms and a parlor room with amazing views. The rooms was really nice although the bathrooms still could use a more modern feel to it. Bed was super comfortable. I highly recommend this hotel and room! We were here on business and the hotel provided us with a printer and everything we needed to work out of our hotel room comfortably. We will be back!

“Wanted To Like It More Than I Did” My wife and I stayed at the Hotel George for 2 nights while attending a conference at the Convention Center in DC. We paid a Priceline rate of $65 for both nights - a great deal on a boutique hotel. The hotel is located near Union Station, the Capitol, G'town Law School, and numerous other points of interest, but is a bit of a hike to the Convention Center. The lobby area is fairly small but attractive enough, and the staff seemed very pleasant to deal with. The hotel's restaurant, Bistro Bis, is well respected in the city; however we were only there for breakfast (nice but a little expensive) and drinks. The room (611) was clean and fairly attractive, however I couldn't get over the view out of the windows - we were surrounded on all sides by other windows facing our room. So much so that most of the time we just left the blinds closed (something I'm usually reluctant to do) rather than be on display. Other disappointing aspects of the hotel included the slightly shabby carpet in the halls and the sense that the hotel's a/c was having a hard time keeping up with the DC humidity. On the plus side, the wi-fi was free (as an In-Kimpton member - which is free to join), the staff were very nice, and they supplied the Sunday NYT for free (a $6 value in a $65 room). One thing to note for you out-of-towners is that they charge a ridiculous amount for parking ($40 I think). However if you are here over the weekend you can find street parking for free nearby (even directly across the street from the hotel) - just be sure to read the signs very, very carefully and be aware that by 7am on Monday morning the free parking will inevitably revert back to metered or permit parking only. Please don't blame me if you get a ticket, I'm just saying that careful parkers can escape the Hotel's insane parking costs. Overall, not a bad hotel, and certainly well worth $65 on Priceline. However, I was expecting a better experience from Kimpton and I feel like 3/5 stars is a fair assessment.

“Great Central Location; Disappointing in Some Details” [Note to Priceline & other third-party guests] Like everyone else, 3rd-party customers read reviews and have expectations; exceptional attentiveness to guest needs is what distinguishes one 2-3 star from others. Third-party prices fill otherwise unsold rooms, and provide the hotel with opportunities to sell services and win future business. My advice to Priceline customers: pay attention to reviews, articulate your needs clearly (both in advance and on arrival) and speak directly and immediately to management if your expectations are not met. If basic room needs are unmet and you bought from Priceline, tell Priceline in writing; use snail mail to the company’s street address and direct to Customer Service VP. I’ve found them responsive. Talk to local management directly, pleasantly: they value meaningful guest feedback and often can use information you provide to correct persistent problems. Be courteous and civil to a fault: it never helps to be confrontational.] COMMENDABLE: Exceptional central location: two blocks from the Space Needle, close to other Seattle Center theatres and monorail (which gets you to 3rd and Pine, central downtown, nearby the Public Market and all downtown. and exceptional public transportation all over Seattle. Queen Anne business district is 5 minutes away on #8 bus, only needed if walking is challenging. Big QFC market, 3 blocks; bigger (and pricier) Metropolitan Market in Queen Anne. Seniors note: Reduced fare “Orca” card, good on all busses and light rail, available at manned kiosk inside Westlake Rail Station. Paid street and lot parking nearby (expensive at hotel). There’s a Walgreens at 6th and Denny, one block. In room: one-use wrapped plastic glasses and paper coffee cups; refrigerator and microwave, excellent hot water supply; good bedding and pillows. Good and responsive below-window heat and cool control. Substitutes wall dispenser in bathroom for individual toiletries, an "eco" nod. Primary downtown stop for QuickShuttle bus to and from Vancouver. Hotel does not have self-service coin laundry but will direct you to “Loyal” Best Western, sister hotel 3 blocks away, for this. Working printer in business center (off lobby). I can recommend this hotel with some caveats below. CHALLENGING: “Complimentary High Speed” internet is meaningless because system has inadequate bandwidth to serve too many users: consequence is poor download speeds and very frequent failure to open pages. Complex pages and downloads are especially troublesome with pitiful speeds (17-25 KB/sec, way below industry average. Frequent failure of door key cards; staff will tell you “your fault, demagnetized in your wallet” but unless you are carrying magnets, this is diversionary and the real issue is likely old, faulty coding equipment or door readers, both expensive to replace. Often long waits at front desk for small issues, easily solved by devising communication between staff to respond with backup when it’s busy. Non-working remote, pointed out to the (tipped) housekeeping staff but then ignored. TRANSPORTATION TIPS: Cars are a hassle unless you must drive through or out of city. Plan for arrival without a car: light rail from SeaTac airport, exit at Westlake (terminus) then cab from 5th and Pine--too far if you have luggage. Tip: Use “Maps” and “get directions” feature of google to reliably plan in-city transportation. At all costs avoid “GO-Shuttle Express” shared ride service from airport, utterly chaotic dispatch in terminal gets my award for worst of airport shuttles. Company does not respond to customer service issues, leaves its harried drivers and dispatch staff to field complaints, does not return calls. You’ll wait hours in the cold to be “dispatched” even if you have a (meaningless) reservation. Tip 1: take a cab if you don’t want to take rail. (GO is reviewed at transportationreviews.com. Tip 2: If you reserved, insist on a refund if they can’t dispatch you within ten minutes, and explain you'll dispute the prepaid credit charge if you are refused. Big, inexpensive buffet in hotel restaurant, breakfast only. A cab extravaganza and some good protein options. Waitstaff will rush you if you are anywhere near closing time. Be firm. Closed at lunch; dinner is tough for vegans: ask for a plain baked potato with salsa and chives, about $3.

“Outstanding Service” We recently spent 2 nights at the Hyatt Place. What a great hotel! Easy check-in. We had a very comfortable 2 queen room on the 9th floor. Loved the idea of a separate living room area for relaxing. The complimentary buffet breakfast was nice every morning. What we loved the most was the free shuttle service. They provide a complimentary shuttle service within a 1 mile radius of the hotel. While the hotel is located in an area that is walkable to the Seattle Center, downtown shopping, and Pike Place Market, the shuttle was fantastic to take us back and forth. Especially after an afternoon of shopping! Would definitely recommend!

“I really like this Hilton brand” My brother spent a couple of days at this hotel six months ago and told me it was really nice. So among the many hotels available for the conference I was attending, I decided to chose the Hilton Garden Inn. I spent some time at another Garden Inn property and was really pleased with the result, and this stay confirms that I do like this Hilton brand. The hotel is perfectly located. Just a couple of blocks from the White House and many other attractions, and with a subway station across the street. The room was big and the bed was comfortable. Although I didn't use it this time, they have a small fridge and microwave oven in the room, and there was a self-service washing machine in my floor. Another great thing is free wi-fi in the hotel. The hotel had a small lobby but a spacious breakfast room, as well as tables and sofas. There is a coffee machine in the room and also free coffee at the lobby, so you can grab one cup if you don't have breakfast at the hotel. The breakfast buffet was complete and with lots of options, though the eggs were not that good. Maybe a cooked-to-order omelette is a better option. A couple of things I didn't like about my stay: - I got a room on the second floor facing the street. It wasn't that bad considering that those rooms are far better than the internal rooms (I checked my colleague's room and the layout was odd and significantly smaller than mine), but I would prefer a higher floor. - The room wasn't ready when I arrived and had to wait. Actually, I left my luggage and went out, but it's so good when the room is ready, specially after a 12-hour flight on couch. - A 10-dollar deposit for an umbrella... really? Anyway, besides the above, I enjoyed my stay. The hotel is simple, functional and unpretentious. Would definitely return and choose a Hilton Garden Inn again.

“Soho Grand was great!” We stayed at the Soho Grand over American Thanksgiving. It was our second time there and we had a really good experience. The woman who checked us in was very friendly -- big warm smile and a "welcome back". We had booked a regular Queen size bedroom and were upgraded to one of the newly renovated rooms. Very comfortable bed -- three or four different types of pillows -- from soft and feather to harder and foam -- nice duvets, a welcome plate of cookies and water and a personalized note from the manager -- generous bath products, windows you could open a titch to get some fresh air. They also threw in a free continental breakfast. All good. Small complaints -- not very good hot water pressure in the shower, especially in the evening for some reason. Hair dryer old and smelly (hard to explain, but the warm air coming out of it had an odd smell). We'd periodically see our check-in woman -- always very warm with a big smile. She was great! All of the staff were open and friendly, including the guys on the door, though the concierge(s) could be a bit stiff. Great drinks at the bar with a really good D.J. spinning fun tunes. Fabulous location. I've read some negative things about the Soho Grand, but both times (and especially this one), we've had a positive experience. We'll go back in a flash! Love the location.

“Great Prices, great location” I just stayed here for the third time this year for business. The hotel is in a great location - it's very easy to get here and the location is perfect for out-of-towners. If you want restaurants or tourist destinations there are a ton within walking distance, and a skywalk into the inner harbor. The hotel was clean and well taken care of and the staff was extremely nice, helpful and accommodating. I had a great view of the inner harbor, too.

“I liked the place very much” This property is very conveniently located in a clean and tranquil street, away from any traffic. The charming Dupont Circle area is within a short walking distance. I have always favored the Kimpton family hotels because of the unbeatable value for money they tend to deliver (see my review on the Monaco Hotel in San Francisco). The hotel is a classic Kimpton establishment, decorated in darker shades of earthy colors, with standard size guest rooms and bathrooms. As most Kimpton properties, they tend to keep their rooms rather poorly lit, creating a very soothing and relaxing atmosphere, as compared to most supermodern hotels with wall to wall windows and office-like rooms. My bed was wonderful, the linens were great and the overall quality of sleep was exceptional due to the lack of any noise at all. Several additional remarks. Valet parking is free for low emission vehicles. They allow dogs (extra fee). Most taxi drivers do not know this hotel implying that this jewel is REALLY well hidden. Overall, I strongly recommend this hotel. The value it delivers for the money is exceptional.

“Very nice hotel” We were in town for a wedding and decided to stay at this Fairfield Inn. We were greeted warmly when we arrived and the room was nice and clean. The bed was firm, but comfortable. The breakfast area had plenty of room and the food selection was good. The location of the hotel is good (just off Bell Rd at I-17). I've stayed at this same hotel while in the area on business and had the same experiences.

“Emplacement idéal” Cet hôtel vaut surtout pour son emplacement dans le quartier des théâtres, un peu à l'écart de l'agitation de Times Square. Ch. à la déco basique, équipée d'un frigo et d'un micro ondes. Petite salle de bain un peu fanée. Bonne literie. Wifi payante. Accueil impersonnel. Supermarché "Food Emporium" à deux pas.

“Great food, not really an hotel” You arrive at a small desk to check in, there is no public area and no hotel atmosphere but the staff is nice and involved. The room was extremely small even for NY, not mint, dated with a view to a wall. You can hear the noise from the corridor only covered by the noise from the street in the morning. There is no reading light. The TV set can only be seen standing! Room service from the DB restaurent is efficient and excellent. The breakfast, its brioche and the whole menu is to die for. Nicely located on 44th street, but prefere the Sofitel next door, better value, better rooms, better atmosphere you can go to DB for breakfast next door.

“Talmente perfetto da diventare un po' noioso ;-D” Posizione chiaramente eccellente, categoria decisamente alta quindi pulizia, ordine, e comfort di ordinanza. Personale gentile, molto disponibile. Però queste soluzioni cosi perfette sono sempre un po' noiose perchè non capitano mai imprevisti o scocciature che movimentino il soggiorno ;-) Del resto se non ricordo male per avere questo genere di tranquillità il James si fa pagare. Ad ogni modo è adatto per chi non si accontenta e vuole qualcosa di simile al top. Super adatto per famiglie o viaggi di lavoro.

“Nice Hotel” Stayed at this hotel one night for Business after four nights at the Hilton NY with my family. Interesting contrast. This hotel is quite old but a very well done boutique type hotel, with a smaller well appointed room. Very friendly staff and a good Midtown location.

“Perfect Boutique hotel without the bad bits and a non designer rate” On the surface this looks like a fun hotel, the best fun, each floor has a different theme from Horror (13) to Music (15) . The rooms are wittily and engagingly thought out, but what makes the hotel super special is that the staff are super super friendly and go out of their way to help. The restaurant is great, and there's lots of choices in the immediate area. A lot of Boutique hotels do not have a great welcoming atmosphere, but you get it at the Curtis, I would now not ever stay anywhere else in Denver Rooms are super comfortable, I did not want to leave!

“You get what you pay for - and its a good thing!” Second stay at Plaza, I do like it. Clean, comfy, nice location next to the park and plenty of restaurants and cafes around. Dated a bit - I don't care much about furniture, but the showerheads are definitely the cheapest variety (replace with massage ones, please, management). Long hallways, so you can hear many people closing their doors and walking in and out. But for the price - a really good value.

“Business plus personal trip all in one!” We had a great JW experience here. I was here for 4 days for work, and extended it to add 3 days of vacation. It was off season in Phoenix, so the traffic at the hotel was moderate at best. It was perfect for us,,,plenty of room in the pools, less screaming kids running around, no real wait for service anywhere, and great access to the gyms. I enjoyed the free internet, free access to the spa, and free parking (Marriott membership does pay). We loved the available Happy Hours in the restaurants. Roy's was amazing. I highly recommend. The Blue Sage lounge is nice for your basic lunches, etc. Excellent service here, although I will say my biggest complaint here was wait time during one lunch. It took 20 minutes to get my food, and 15 minute to get my bill. And it was very quiet in there. If you are active like I am, and want to be close to the Spa gym, ask to get a room near the spa. The free parking is just past the spa, and you are very close to the outside entrance and can walk to Albertson's and the Desert Ridge Marketplace in 10 minutes or less. Super convenient. I never paid for parking, so it must be because I am a Marriott member. The spa restaurant is very good too. Lots of healthy options, with a cheeseburger option available, for those people who just want to pretend they eat healthy. We also got couple's massages at the spa. Check to see if they have any discounts, as they did when we booked. I had Vera, and my boyfriend had Rosie. We loved them, and I would HIGHLY recommend them for your massage. And, if you book something in the spa, you get access to the spa pool and sauna, which are beautiful and QUIET! You can get a fridge in your room, so if you plan on staying awhile, ask for one. With the grocery store not far away, you can easily save some $$$ by getting some food and keeping it in your room. Front desk staff and concierge are wonderful. Ask about the Ping plant tour, or anything else you need. They will take care of you!! My only complaint would be that they cleaned my room late in the day, typically after 3:00pm. I wish it would have been earlier.

“Slightly dissapointing......” As most of us do now we read the previous reviews for the W Seattle prior to booking our stay, so we knew to expect the dim lighting in the hallways, the fee for the internet in the rooms and the trendy bar type scene at night in the lobby. All minor things in our opinion. We booked this hotel based on location, value for money, and the overall appearance of the rooms and amenties. Our room had all the modcons you expect from any hotel these days. TV, fridge, couch, comfy beds and pillows, a huge selection of bathroom amenities, mini bar, and so on. There was even a music cd to play and a trendy clock radio and ipod charger. Unfortunately not compatible to the iphone which would have been really handy. However the housekeeping let us down. For the first 2 nights we had to request them to come and makeup our room after we returned late in the day to find it unserviced. On the third day we actually spoke to the lobby staff and asked them to ensure our room was madeup before we got back as we were going on a day trip and would be tired . The staff not only ensured this was done but gave us a complimentary cheese and desert platter and a card advising they hoped we had a great trip down to Mt Rainier. A wonderful thought which really made up for the previous days lack of service. If we ever return to Seatlle we would look for alternate accommodation as we have never had to ask for housekeeping in all our travels throughout the world and have stayed in hotels with much lower rating and received better service. Overall just an average experience that could have been excellent with better attention to detail. It was very dissapointing to find the room not mad up on day 2 after our request the day before. We thought that after having a problem the staff would have addressed it.

“Very nice place” I enjoyed my stay here, the room was very clean and comfortable and the location is great. The Internet service worked well and the complimentary morning coffee was excellent. Yes, the building is old and the rooms are small. That's the way it is in Chicago. The walls are thin, but it didn't cause me any big problems. The only thing that was a little disappointing was that there was no dresser, not even a few drawers for clothes underneath the TV. I don't think I should have to fish my clothes out of my suitcase every day at a 4-star hotel. But very nice overall, I'd stay there again.

“Not the best location for tourists.” Lots of positives about this hotel...BUT tourists beware, the location of the Hilton is not ideal for such attractions as Navy Pier, Magnificent Mile, etc. I disagree with other reviews which praise its location. For tourists, expect to spend a lot of time and money on taxis--both for attractions and restaurants. Chicago traffic is unbelievable-a taxi ride from the John Hancock to the Hilton was 30 minutes and $20-even at 7:30 at night! I recommend tourists seek another property about a mile or so north. This especially so if you are like my family and shy away from public transport while on vacation. Now for the hotel itself... Positives-a beautiful older hotel that is huge and generally well-maintained. Staff was all friendly and helpful. We upgraded to a small suite-a decent bargain at around ~$200. The pool, exercise area, track and locker rooms were really nice. Also, tons of elevators and never a wait. Negatives-the room was nicely furnished with one glaring exception. Beneath the sink is a cheap $20 cabinet with peeling paint. It looks so out of place in this otherwise nicely decorated room that it is laughable. Management - check out what I mean in rm 1563--really very silly for this hotel to have such a shabby piece of cabinetry. Also, we noticed the first day that not all the hallway lights outside our room were lit which resulted in a very dingy, almost creepy feel. This would not be so big a deal but the hallways seem to go on forever so they need to keep all the lights on all the time or the hotel reminds you of the one from "The Shining." However this partially lit hallway was only observed once during our stay-thankfully. Finally, I'm not overly impressed by the room's desk computer which is supposed to be an information center-I found navigating it difficult and the info limited in its utility. Did not try the restaurants but the restaurant dinner menu looked very limited. In summary, I would highly recommend this hotel for the business traveler but not for the tourist due to its location.

“Good value for the money and pet friendly” We selected this property for three reasons: 1. very pet friendly 2. good Trip Advisor reviews 3. proximity to I-70 We hadn't stayed at Red Roof Inn before before, but we liked the price ($65 with tax!) and how friendly they were to our large, well-behaved dog. Since we are used to higher-end properties, we did not particularly like the linens or towels, but it was sufficient for a roadtrip. The bathroom also had some water damage around the tub but was very clean.

“Stay only if you have to...” As I start all my reviews, a 5 is hard to get. It's reserved for those that exceed expectations. With that said, the Galleria was an average hotel. The location: I can't complain about the location. Only 2 blocks from the Montgomery Bart Station makes it very convenient to go to either OAK or SFO. As far as shopping, it's in prime real estate - it's surrounded by any store that you can think of. Also, it's a short walk to the cable cars. Lastly, its close to good restaurants so we ended up walking to a majority of places which helped work off some of the extra calories... The service: The service at the hotel was great. They helped us get cabs, recommended places to eat, stored our bags, and even let us check in at noon! This is probably on of the friendliest hotel staffs that I've encountered. The same holds true for most of the San Francisco guest services - much better than the east coast! The room: Here was my only gripe with the hotel. It claimed to have undergone a $7 million renovation. Well, I couldn't see them spending more than $7 to renovate that room. The carpet was dark and questionably dirty. The paint job was horrible, the TVs were whatever (and yes, I know that's not what you go to SF for, but at least upgrade them somewhat), the cabinets and furniture were all worn out, and lets not start with the bathroom. The paint was chipping everywhere, the tub was dirty, the tiles were kinda gross in places. The only positive of the room, which was a big one was that they had nice, comfortable beds. Outside of that, don't expect much. Luckily for us, the only hours we spent in the room were for sleeping. Overall: I booked this place through hotwire, which has this place listed as a 3 1/5 star for approx $125/night (after taxes). Personally, knowing what I know, I wouldn't have spent more than $100/night on this place. The staff and location are great, but the room needs quite a bit of help. I've stayed in large cities before (NY, DC, Philly) so I know what to expect from a city room, and this was below par. The room is about a 2 star and the location and service are about a 4 star. If you're looking to sleep and shower at this place, it's an okay bet, but if you want more, look elsewhere...

“Wonderful” I loved this hotel. The rooms were so quiet and peaceful. It was very busy but managed to be very quiet. The staff was polite and helpful. I had the pleasure of eating at the J Bar and Staff was out standing..Debbie and Yon were awesome.

“Tiniest bathroom” We chose this hotel because of its proximity to the airport. We stayed on a Saturday night when a wedding reception was taking place so the hotel was packed. Our room was located on the 9th floor in the tower. The room was spacious with the exception of the bathroom. It was the tiniest bathroom I can recall at any hotel I have ever stayed at. I just didn't expect this sized bathroom at this caliber of a Marriott, especially when we were on a concierge level. It was so small that only one person could be in there at a time. That was problematic when both my husband and I are getting ready. The sink was partially blocked by the toilet so my husband and I had to keep going in and out to let the other person in. The other drawback was the parking. Because of the crowd, we ended up in the overflow lot. While there was a hotel entrance relatively close to the overflow lot, it forced you to walk through the indoor pool area which was humid and smelled like chlorine. If staying in the area again, I would try another hotel with larger bathrooms.
“Always my top choice when traveling from ORD” Great great location, room is not always so nice though.Airport view rooms are nice, fitness room pretty awesome

“In town for Zoobiliation/Customer Service Excellent” This was a very nice stay. The transporation to the zoo was done very well and enhanced the experience. We stepped out limo was waiting and was easy to get back to the hotel when we wore out at Zoobilation. What really stood out for Customer Service was the valet from start to finish. It's rare that when leaving someone actually offers you a bottle of water for the road and is every bit as cordial as upon your arrival. Of course I realize it is the last time for a tip; however it wasn't forced as you find in many cities and hotels. The hotel restaurant had excellent staff also and the breakfast buffet was Fantastic.

“Nice, Clean, Good Service” Location: Opened in late 2010, the hotel is about 20 minutes from the airport. It's about 5 minutes from convention center and downtown where some of the best restaurants are at North High St. There are also plenty of places to eat within walking distance at the complex. Reception/Room: I have stayed at many Hyatt Place hotels nationwide due to business reasons, and this is a very new one vs the other locations so it's a bit nicer with better furniture. The A/C unit is also much quieter than many other Hyatt Place locations. Like other locations, you get a living area and a sleeping area with a very large room but there is no door to separate the two. Free WiFi plus two free internet terminals in the lobby. Breakfast: Typical Hyatt Place fare which is continental with good fruit selection. You can pay to order additional hot items and those are not too expensive. Service: Excellent throughout from check-in to check-out. We had a very early flight the next day so the evening before, we were standing in the reception line wanting to reserve a cab. A staff member voluntarily came up to us, figured out what we needed, and told us he would take care of it. The cab was there on schedule the next morning. Everything was done with a smile. Overall: Great place to stay.

“Very difficult to fault and great staff....” We stayed here for one night prior to our flight back to the UK from Seattle and paid £40 ($64) for the night. The hotel is rather hard to find as there are just so many properties along International Blvd and with some major traffic as well you really do need to have eyes in the back of your heads. Once found we parked easily and there were many spaces on this Friday teatime and we checked in with a very friendly member of the reception team who made us feel very welcome. Our room was on the 2nd floor with an ATC view which was rather nice for the geek in me. We have stayed in Red Roof Inns before and although they are aimed at the budget market the rooms have often exceeded expecations and thankfully this was the same. Two nice queen beds and a very spacious room with great air conditioning and a well maintained if basic bathroom. Absolutely no issues with cleanliness either, it was pretty much the perfect airport hotel room. We had to print off boarding passes for our next day flight and in reception there is a free to use internet terminal and printing comes out from behind reception. A nice touch I thought. There is also free hot drinks in the lift lobby area as well. Overall I would highly recommend the Red Roof Inn to anybody wanting a cheap overnight stay near SeaTac. Sure there are better options with a bigger price tag but for one night it is difficult to find fault at all, and you are just minutes away from the airport terminal as well. Highly recommended.

“Trendy and well-located” Of the different neighborhoods in ny, soho/tribeca is my favorite and this hotel is right in the thick of it all. Bubbly upon checkin was great and the room was the most spacious of my three stays in various hotels in the city. Khiels amenities were luxurious and the coffee/hot chocolate stations on each floor was nice. Staff and doormen were great and most didn't hesitate to run into traffic to hail us a cab. Yes, the lighting is miserable and I found myself doing my makeup in the dark but I couldn't be bothered to stress too much about that. I'd happily stay there again!

“Great Stay” I'm in total agreement with other satisfied travellers for this property. Rooms are spacious, clean, and service here is great. Location is great for shopping. I will definately stay here in the future. If you are a light sleeper, be warned that the hotel is right next door to a Fire Station - which might be a concern for some. They have complimentary ear plugs available at the front desk.

“As Close to Perfect as I've seen at Marriott” I stayed here for one night while recently in San Diego, and wish I could have stayed longer. Having stayed in several Marriott hotels, this is my favorite. Location: The location of the hotel in San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter is hard to beat. There are countless bars and restaurants within walking distance. Petco Park is across the street, and the Convention Center is close as well. If you plan to visit other areas of San Diego - beaches, LaJolla, San Diego zoo - they are within a reasonable distance. Rooms: Nice, modern, clean. The only thing they need to do would be to transition from the older tube TVs to flat screen models. Otherwise no complaints about the room. It had everything you'd expect. Hotel: Nice facility. Relatively "hip" feel, especially for a Marriott. Nice rooftop bar/views. Great staff. Will definitely stay here again if/when I'm back in San Diego.

“Great LoDo Location + Customer Service” The Monaco is located in a renovated historic building, and they have maintained the high ceilings, grand lobby and facade. Funky, hip decor, Our room was very quiet although it overlooked Champa St (we were on the 7th floor) with a good-sized bathroom, plenty of room at the desk for work, and a chaise lounge. Robes are thick & comfy. There is a MP3 player docking station, as well as a CDplayer. Very comfy bed, and soft sheets. towels a little tatty. The only amenity I missed was a coffee-maker, although there is complimentary tea & coffee (good coffee & a great selcetion of teas in the lobby each morning.) I appreciated the wine reception each evening, and the package we booked included a welcome bottle of wine, also (actually decent wine rather than plonk.) Since I am a member of their loyalty program, WiFi was free (worth joining just for that.) Also, you can specify a choice of newspaper. I had e-mailed a request for a quiet room away from elevators (I'm a light sleeper) which was well accomodated. It was our anniversary, and bottle of bubbly with cookies and a balloon were waiting in our room--nice touch. We arrived late and hungry (plane delay) and the front desk called around to help us find an open rest for soup & salad. front desk was very helpful, and the employees seemed empowered to actually make decisions and take action. We had a business dinner in their wine cellar which was not as good as the hotel experience. For $125/each, i was disappointed in the watery, tasteless pasta and mediocre (and scant) appetizers. Service was also a little scant. Very different than the Front Desk team! Location is close to many resto's, 1 block from the free shuttle on the 16th St Mall, and within walking distance of Coors Field. Can't be beat.

“Fantastic” Spent one night there before an early flight the next morning. The convenience can't be beat especially if you are flying American Airlines. The front door to the hotel is actually part of the AA terminal building; go up the escalator to the lobby. When you go to your flight just go back down the escalator and the AA checkin counters and security are right there. If you have a car you can park in the terminal parking and the hotel receptionist will give you a coupon so you don't have to pay for parking (at DFW you get a ticket when you enter the airport grounds and pay on the way out). The hotel's common areas and rooms are topnotch. Modern, clean and new. The rooms are spacious and beds very comfortable. Windows are very soundproof so you can't hear the airplanes--it was nice to watch them take off and land, though. No coffee maker in the room, but there is a card that says they will bring you one. Internet is T-Mobile, $7.99 for 24 hrs. The health club is also modern and new--it has six treadmills (which is how I gauge the size of a health club) with built in TVs, weights, etc., all late model Lifefitness. The outdoor pool is somewhat small so hard to swim laps, but you may not want to swim outside in the jet fumes anyway. You pay a slight premium for the location, but it's definitely worth it. One of the best airport hotels I've stayed in.

“great location...very soft beds” the hotel is the place to be seen. The lobby is off on the 7th floor near the hotel bar which is a hot night spot and very crowded at night and is very stylish/modern. the rooms are beautifully decorated however small but probably large for NYC. the bathrooms are modern with a waterfall basin sink and a gentle rain shower. All rooms have a flat screen TV and there are two towers. One tower goes up to 30 something floors and the other starts at 30 and go up to 47 or more floors. The beds are very soft and not firm. My wife prefers a soft bed but I need a firm bed or I wake up with back aches. Water pressure is good and the water is plentiful for showers and everything you need. If you are spg gold/platinum, you get 2 free bottles of water/day which is nice. In room/hotel internet is affordable with options as low as 6.95 and daily rates of $14.95. A message to all Pplatinum guests, do not expect an upgrade at this hotel. I have been here 3 times recently snd have not been upgraded once.

“Charming, unique and great location - couldn't ask for more!” The service at this hotel is immpecable. The setting is really unique and the rooms are clean and spacious. As with all Kimpton hotels, I love their eco-friendly policies, the evening wine hour, and overall "can do" attitude of the staff. Would definitely come back here again.

“Another hotel that just gets it” I agree with what the others have said and I'll highlight just a few points: - Location. Close enough to Times Square without being trapped amongst its jammed sidewalks. From JFK take the A or E train to the 50th Street Station (plan an hour each way) and you are a block from the hotel. - Bed. Excellent. - Check-in/Check-out. Fast and friendly. As with most other hotels in NYC there is street noise (specifically car honking at ridiculous hours) to contend with and I would request a room away from the street. Unlike like most NYC hotel rooms the ones here are fairly spacious.

“December 30 - January 5th - LES was just Meh.” I had the opportunity to spend New Years in NYC. Obviously there are 100's of choices available in NYC, but the LES is limited for well priced options. Here's what I found as drawbacks: 1.) Found a pair of eyelashes (yes, sticky glue fake eyelashes) affixed to the black lacquer bed when we arrived. Not a big enough deal to call housekeeping, but still uber gross to have to get tp and throw them out. It was like the bed was staring at me. 2.) A prior guest left what I can only assume was toothpaste on the back of the door and housekeeping did not remove it during our entire stay. 3.) Bed had a ledge of sorts on the back (facing window) that had mounds of dust on it - stayed there for all nights of our trip. 4.) Fire alarm went off on night/early morning of day 4 (I believe) and upon return to our room door was unlocked/open. Ran around to make sure we hadn't been robbed and luckily we weren't. Highly annoying because we were tramping down the stairs from a higher floor and did not receive any direction from staff. Finally decided to go back to room when alarm went off and didn't see or hear even ONE other person. Guess it was a false alarm, but firetrucks did arrive and could see them quickly leave. 5.) Front desk called me one evening when I was out enjoying dinner and asked some random question - tried to get more info, but I guess they realized their error and HUNG UP on me. 6.) Only 1 elevator appeared to work. 7.) Not really a negative for me, since it was NYE and I like to party with the best of them - but upon arriving back to our hotel around 3 AM on NYE found random drunken females riding in elevator trying to get off on the 7th floor I believe. Once we arrived back to our room we could hear a party going on. Again ONLY happened on NYE, but I can only imagine how annoying that would have been on any other night. 8.) Shower doors were ever so loud and made a huge slamming sound that would make you believe the glass was about to burst on top of your head. You could also hear this sound from other rooms. Positives 1.) Hotel is newer than most other hotels in LES and for what we paid well worth it.. 2.) See negative #7 - could be positive if you are looking to party 3.) Elevator required a key card to get off on your floor. 4.) Subway stop across the street 5.) Other than #5 all contact with employees was nice and I noticed one of the doorguys from 6 Columbus was now working here. Actually the employees were super nice - so double plus. 6.) Our room was absolutely amazing. We had a corner room which if you stood on the bed (how I came to notice #3 above negative) you could see the Manhattan and Brooklyn bridges - or perhaps just the Manhattan bridge. Have to check pictures. Awesome - awesome view of lower Manhattan and if I pressed my cheek against the floor to ceiling windows I could see the ESB. 7.) Other than slamming shower door from above NEVER heard a peep from any other guests. I only saw one other person on our floor the entire time we were there, so I'm not sure if the hotel was at capacity, but I would assume not considering the bargain basement rates this hotel had even the day before we arrived. I didn't try the restaurant, but I loved this restaurant one block south of LES on Allen street called Kampuchea. It's a Cambodian restaurant - yummy. Sugar next door was also very tasty - ask the guy why they don't have strawberries hehe. Whole Foods is about 2 blocks away and has many great options and a cool place you can sit and eat and enjoy street views. There's a crepe place a few blocks away that you should try (but only order one) I suggest a desert crepe. Pianos was fun in the LES as was the burlesque show across the street from Kampuchea. So all in all - not sure if my negatives (mainly surrounding housekeeping) would keep me from recommending the hotel to a friend - but, I probably wouldn't stay there again because I got the eery feeling that in a few months the housekeeping issues would turn into maintenance issues and the whole place would be a dump with great views. Actually I am headed back to NYC for Labor Day and I didn't even look at Thompson LES rates, because come to remember it the bed staring at me was just too gross and everytime I see a black lacquer bed now I'll just think it's winking at me.

“I'm a Hilton honors member and I would not stay here!!!” I arrived at 300am and booked and call to let them know I was coming in at that hour. It took an hour to resolve this matter. They said hotel was fully sold out, thank goodness I had all my email correspondence and they finally checked me in. I am also a hilton honors member. I usually never pull that, but I was so furious with how they handled the situation. The room is very basic for a Hilton. Unless you stay on their club floors. And to me that is pretty standard also. The club lounge is always always packed and over filled with people. Not comfortable at all. It would be better to be downstairs eating. The elevators are always full and packed. The door men were helpful with directions and also getting a taxi but expected to get tipped. I would not recommend this hilton location. There are better places to stay in that location and for the same price too.

“Like the location” Stayed here for one night in June, but have stayed here before when on business in Chicago. Great location for business/shopping/sightseeing. In between Michigan Avenue's Magnificent Mile and the Loop and next to the Chicago River. Rooms very spacious and clean. Gym has a wonderful view, as it is situated on the top of the hotel. Bar next to lobby, very busy with good atmosphere. Cannot fault the hotel. Prefer it to the Westin - my previous address when in Chicago.

“Nice hotel” Stayed here for a night while on business. Hotel is easy to find, but parking is tight. Nice enough valet service, though. Service was great,. Wine bar at 5:00 PM was a nice touch. The atmosphere of the hotel is very zen-like, and totally relaxing. Room was ok, with two issues: hole in bedsheet and bathroom shower could use a spray of Tilex to cut down on slight mold issues. Or maybe the installation of a vent fan in the bathroom would help, as my room did not have one. Otherwise, room was clean and very comfortable. Spa was WONDERFUL. Make sure to get the discount coupon for massage! Ryan was great, and I felt totally relaxed. thanks Ryan!

“Very cool hotel for the UWS!” Nice lobby. Very modern feel. Room was nice. Not huge, but it's NYC. GREAT rooftop terrace with a wonderful view. Internet in the lobby. And I got an amazing deal on it through expedia. Totally worth the stay.

“Trendy and fun, but also comfortable, great location” We stayed here twice within a week because of my daughter's college auditions in New York. The hotel entrance and lobby are very interesting. Our first room, with two queen beds, was actually spacious and very comfortable. The rooms are also very clean-- I know because in order to find the electrical outlets I had to hunt around behind furniture for a power strip. No dustballs on the hardwood floors! The first room was very quiet; our only problem was that it was over-heated; even turning off the heater did not seem to help. Friends stayed in rooms that were extremely tiny; the difference was striking. There were no double queen rooms available for our current stay, so asked to be upgraded to a "superior" queen. The room is small, but not nearly as tiny as some. I found the staff to be friendly and helpful, although a sweater accidentally left in our room a few days ago has never turned up :(

“Nothing special” My husband & I stayed at this Holiday Inn for one night recently. We slept alright & felt safe (that's mostly what we look for in a hotel on a short trip like this), but the hotel is showing it's age and just wasn't that inspiring. The rooms have been slightly updated, but the decor was not current and felt slightly worn. The room still had a slow-loading tube television (instead of a flat panel). The fact that the TV was outdated was proudly broadcast by the flyer placed on top of our TV promoting the Nintendo GameCube, a gaming system that was discontinued 5 years ago! The bed was mostly comfortable, with 4 small pillows. The bedroom area & most of the bathroom seemed clean, but the bathtub cleaning was not up to par. The toilet had a water-saving feature that seemed efficient but which was excessively loud -- any time one was flushed within a few rooms of us, we heard it. Other than the flushing noise -- and hearing our neighbor's TV a few times -- the hotel was quiet. Though the hotel is a tall tower very near a major highway & the airport, we didn't hear any traffic noise, thankfully. And, they have free parking -- a definite advantage over staying downtown! The staff was nondescript; they were a little slow at checking us in & out, but not too bad. The location is just fine, near the airport, easily accessed off the highway, across the road from a nice mall & near quite a few choices for local dining. There are lots of hotels in this area. The Holiday Inn wasn't bad, but next time we choose to stay in north San Antonio, I think we'll try another hotel.

“This Is A Great Hotel” After experiencing some problems with my car, I had to find a place to stay and many hotels in the area were booked due to special events. I tried this Holiday Inn Express and was treated so warmly from the moment I walked in the door, I just had to share that experience with others who might be considering this hotel. The front desk staff were wonderful. I had called a cab to go to a restaurant and it arrived sooner than I expected. Instead of calling my room, one of the desk people took the time to walk to my room and inform me the cab was waiting. Checkout was smooth and efficient, and I was asked if I needed any help with a future reservation as well as being told that my business was appreciated. If I am ever in the area again, you can be sure this will be my first choice for lodging.

“Much bigger and better than the numbers chains” Definitely an oldie that has seen refurbishment over time. This and basic cleanliness makes it an acceptable stay. Furniture and everything is old. Bathroom a space crunch. But everything works. Definitely deemed a safe choice for an overnight rest. Just don't expect a Holiday Inn. It is a mom-pop deal afterall. And don't expect to swim in the dry pool. A safe one star.

“Old California Opulence” Arriving at the Fairmont, you first find doormen in 1920 swank garb. Cool! Inside the lobby, you get the feel that I can best describe as "old California opulence." There is a light grandness, not the East Coast or Midwest dark woods grandness. Lots of light colors and light marble. The front desk could have been a little better staffed, but the wait wasn't too long. The room, however, was incredible. It was almost as big as the first apartment my wife and I rented out of college when we lived (in all places to compare) in Palo Alto, only a bit up the road. Lots more light marble. A separate make-up room and an almost walk-in closet. A separate water closet. A bath tub separate from a glass enclosed shower. The only small sad detail was the water fixtures were clearly dated and worn by abrasive cleaner. (Important to note: on leaving, I checked with the front desk: this was a STANDARD room) Upon returning to the hotel after supper at Maggiano's Little Italy (review to come), there was an incredible jazz quartet playing in the lobby. There was an enthusiastic audience gathered. I was sad that I was still on East Coast time and needed to get to bed... I would have loved to stay and listen. I was granted a late checkout which was efficient and non-eventful. Every staff I spoke to was articulate and courteous. Other reviewers have noted that there are PLENTY of eating options near by. I can saw that that was my observation as well. Kudos to the Fairmont and their staff. It is a pleasure to write a review of a great place to stay and recommend.

“Average Hampton Inn” This is a decent Hampton Inn, which means that in Memphis, it's about as good as it gets! The first floor lobby and breakfast area are in the midst of major renovations, so it is dusty and chaotic. The room was a typical Hampton room, and clean enough. I will consider staying here again, after the first floor construction is completed.

“Great Hotel in Midtown” Due to Sandy and the Nor'easter we were stranded in the Tri-State area. We had to scramble to get a room. Boy were we lucky to snag one here!! We were given a corner room that was done up very well. These rooms are very clean and decorated well. We will definitely be staying here again.

“Truly amazing hotel in a great location” Just wanted to write a few lines here after staying at the Mandarin Oriental in Boston during labor day weekend. I drove down to Boston from Montreal with a few friends to see a Red Sox ball game. We only stayed for one night, but I wish we had stayed longer. This hotel is totally awesome. Granted, it was built just 2 years ago I'm told, so it's still very new and modern looking, nothing is out of place, no scratches, paint chips, marks on the carpet, etc. But regardless, they know how to take care of their guests. From the time you pull up in front with your car, the doormen & bellhops are super friendly & polite. Same for the staff at reception. The room was truly perfect. From a huge, super luxurious bathroom, to a very big and spacious room, to ultra comfortable beds, and of course tons of TV channels (so we could see all the game highlights when we can back from the game!), this hotel has it all. Oh and the turn-down service at night was pretty classy too. The bar downstairs is modern and was pretty happening, even on a Sunday night. I've been to Boston several times in the past few years, and this was the best hotel stay I've had. I'll certainly look to stay here again next time, and would recommend it to anyone, without a doubt.
