“Nice hotel, slow internet” Hampton Inn hotels are usually cheaper, so I was a bit surprised to pay as much as I did, especially since there are hundreds of hotels in the Houston area. However, the rooms were nice, the service was good and the staff were very friendly. Internet access was free -- excellent! -- but somewhat slow (didn't matter whether I tried the wired or wireless connections; both were not optimal).

“Excellent Stay” Great location, great staffing, great room, and great candies at the front desk. Clean and professional and quiet, I would not hesitate to stay here again in Seattle. We stayed in a "Sorrento Suite" and have no complaints.

“Beautiful Remodeled Holiday Inn, Near DAL & Downtown Dallas” Holiday Inn, Harry Hines Blvd, Dallas Market Center. Apparently this location had problems under a previous brand, and just opened in January 2008 after a two year remodel. The new Holiday Inn looks nothing like the old photos posted on this site. We found all beautiful new remodeled rooms, lobby, parking lot, outside deck and pool, common areas, fitness center, restaurant and bar. All new, and clean. Staff was very friendly and hospitable. We were picked up at DAL by their complimentary shuttle, and continued to utilize all weekend in tandem with the #44 DART bus which stops directly outside, and will take you downtown in under 9 minutes. We had a Queen-Queen, and were very pleased overall. Room is new- carpeting, bed, tv, et al. Nice shower pressure with their unusual looking Moen massager nozzle. Only negative is that window is sealed shut. We would have liked to open for some fresh air. Nice outdoor pool, deck and seating area. Very nice pub and restaurant on property. Menu is typical Holiday Inn for breakfast, and offers their new limited lunch and dinner menu. We chose not to rent a car, and still managed to get around handsomely. We took their shuttle to the light rail station, and then took the train to the Dallas Zoo. We also took the free McKinney Uptown Trolley (McKinney & Ross, near the Fairmont Hotel) to a great neighborhood, full of shops, restaurants and pubs. Dealey Plaza - probably a must see- is also within the 5 mile radius of this hotels' complimentary shuttle. There is not as much to do or see in Downtown Dallas proper- as one would expect in a city of this size -go and see it for yourself. Exercise caution at night, especially in the West End neighborhood. Not much in the direct vicinity of the hotel. There is a 24 hour convenience store appx three blocks away, and a popular breakfast and lunch restaurant directly adjacent. Over all- you won't go wrong here. Free parking for guests with a car.

“Budget place but EXCELLENT choice!” I booked a room at the Pennsylvania because in Manhattan it's one of the cheaper places you can stay at and because it's right in the centre of the action. Pennsylvania is sooo convenient! 10 minutes on foot by Times Square, right in front of Penn Station, near many subways and fast foods.... If you can't afford the Hilton or other 4* hotels in the Big Apple, this must be your hotel of choice! The room is not filthy assomeone else described it! It's low key, not with the best facilities, but it's quite clean and ok. You can also have a great cheesecake NYC style at hotel's Lindy's branch! WOW, simply AMAZING! Avoid to arrive early in the morning, as the hotel charges for luggage storage and as it's always full (meaning you won't get your room before 1 pm!). All in all, a good choice! RATING: B-

“Size does matter...sometimes.” I recently stayed at the Hudson Hotel in New York. My first impression from the lobby of the hotel was a chic trendy hotel, but when I got to my room I felt a bit like the giant Alice in Wonderland. I travel to New York often, and this by far was the tiniest room I have ever stayed in. For example, when using the toilet, my knees hit the wall, and I am not unusually tall (5'9"). My bed was a queen, which had about 4-6 inches on either side. The room was, for lack of a better word, a shoebox. The room was also quite loud and I could hear noise from my neighbors and the hallway. I do compliment the hotel for using the vertical space in the room- however, there wasn't much vertical space to use. I recommend just visiting the Library Bar or the Atrium and skipping a stay here. You can find better rooms for your money.

“Comfortable enough” Next to the freeway so easy access to other destination although hotel directions can be a bit hard to follow via GPS. Check-in was slow. Late afternoon and rooms are not even ready. Many families were waiting for kids suite. We were sitting in the lobby waiting for our suite to be ready but were annoyed that two other guests who came in after us were given their suites before us. Anyway, once we checked into our family suite, we were really impressed with the cleanliness of the room, the king bed and bunk beds and the two TVs. Beds and pillows were soft and comfortable. Plenty of towels provided. Good water pressure in the shower. Size of the kids suite is almost similar to a normal hotel room except that there is a sliding door separating the king bed and bunk beds. Although we were not given a room of our preference ( at time of reservation had requested for a quiet room away from the freeway), thankfully noise from the freeway was minimal. We were given a suite facing the freeway! Free Wifi in suite was very fast. Free Breakfast was the typical fare of most hotel chain and it was the same food every morning of our stay. Breakfast room was very crowded at 8.30 so finding table was hard. Because there were so many guests, tables and food counter tops were quite dirty and messy. This hotel charges for unsecured parking. Therefore, we chose not to park in the hotel because there are plenty of free parking along the road outside the hotel. At check-out, we were charged for parking and when we asked for this to be taken out, the receptionist did not seemed to believe us at first and asked whether we had a rental car. We explained that if we wanted to park inside the hotel, we would have been given a parking pass on check-in to display on dashboard. So this makes me wonder whether the hotel security, if any, ever patrol their car park to check if all vehicles are authorized to be parked there?

“Comfy” I arrived in a foul mood after united's best attempts at making me never fly with them again. I was met by a smile by a staff member who looked exhausted (it was 2am) but she immediately put me in a better mood and seemed genuinely interested in me. Room was nice, breakfast was a little curious as they have an einsteins bagels in the hotel, but good all the same. I can't put my finger on it, but I liked this hotel. I left with good feelings regarding the Phoenix hyatt.

“Cooles Hotel - Coole Bar” Der Bryant Park Cellar ist ein jetzt neu hipper Club in NY und zwar im Untergeschoss des bekannten Bryant Park Hotels. Die Drinks sind sehr teuer (USD 18.-- vor Trinkgeld für einen kleinen Vodka-Red Bull im Plastik-Becher ) somit solle man schauen, ob man nicht einen Promotor kennt. Die Leute im Cellar waren jetzt nicht so wirklich mein Geschmack . Vor dem Club hat man immerhin free Wireless von der Bryant Park Org.
“Airline Crewmember” Great hotel bad location just don't leave the hotel. Hotel airport transportation can be unreliable at times.

“Lovely Arts & Crafts Hotel” Stayed here for 3 nights Nov 2006 & had a very good experience but since then management has changed so not sure what else might have changed too. Had a 1 bedroom suite that was lovely & spotlessly clean. Very large bathroom. Whole suite was beautifully decorated, including great prints/artwork & very comfortable bed. Only negative, not much natural light, as I choose to go with room at the back vs. front, which overlooks & hears the El. Very good italian restaurant across the street, food to-go or dine in. Pro: loved hotel decoration style, historic building, close to EVERYTHING (due to EL), 1 block from Fine Arts museum, M Park + suites are really nice, good price Con: rooms at front have natural light but very loud; ones at back are dark but quiet.

“For the price, excellent!” The Mediterranean is an older hotel, two short blocks from the Key Arena side of the Seattle Center in Queen Anne. It has been lovingly remodeled in warm yellows and browns, and shows obvious care. Unfortunately, it still retains a couple of the negatives from its former life. Rooms are smaller than most (except the corner queen suites, which are large and beautiful), and there can be a residual smoke odor. The hotel is completely non-smoking, but smells as if it didn't use to be. It's not a quiet place, and you may be able to hear the baby crying in the next room (we did). The positives include very comfortable beds, flat-screen TVs, and excellent staff. They are top-notch, especially Guadalupe, who seemed to bend over backwards for every guest. Amanda was nice, but a "loud talker". I didn't see more than two people on duty at a time. They were busy, but appeared to be in control. There is underground parking for $15/day. A very large and well-equipped business center, plus two computers in the lobby for quick use. Starbucks is accessible through the lobby. A decent fitness room is on the bottom floor, along with a laundromat and snack room. The front door is secured at night, accessible only by key. The Med rents rooms by the night, week, or month. A furnished studio for a month is $1065, less than most rents in the area. Safeway is half a block away; Dick's burgers across the street. We booked through Hotels.com, and were surprised to find that we could've gotten the room more cheaply through their Web specials on their site. Make sure to check. Unless we got a great deal at the Westin, we'd likely stay here the next time we're in Seattle.

“Avoid the car traffic” If you're going to a sporting event in Philadelphia, this is the hotel (and only) hotel within EASY walking distance. It is in the process of being renovated so there are no on site eateries. (July 2004) We were on an upper floor and had a view of the new baseball stadium. It was a good size room with a comfortable king size bed. They have stadium event parking in their parking lot and we thought we'd have a hassle but the gal had our name on a sheet of paper and in we drove. It's very convenient on and off the highways and an easy drive into downtown Philadelphia. They had no shuttle service to the airport. The Turf Club across the street served a good lunch and was good entertainment to see what a lot of men do for leisure activitiy (play the ponies and anythiing else with four legs that they could bet on).

“Very Nice, Easy parking , nice rooms” Easy location, lots of free parking, friendly service- only issue for me is I prefer to have some type of restaurnat in the lobby of hotels I stay at- this one does not (yet) however plenty nearby. Overall terrific value.

“Best of the Best” For someone who spends over 200 nights a year in a hotel, I can honestly say this property exceeded my expectations and then some! Great staff, great food and a spacious room made my last trip to this property quite enjoyable. Located near the old Stapleton Airport there is an abundant supply of local and national eateries nearby. My room had a very comfortable bed and was quite spacious. What sets this property aside from the rest is the genuine feeling that the staff really cares about keeping the guest happy. Everybody from the housekeepers, desk clerks, waitstaff and management all great you with a smile and hearty greetings. I really got the feeling that these folks were happy to see me and wanted my stay to be enjoyable. Well, it was. Special kudos to Molly Flagg, and Jason in the restaurant. (And a few others whose name escape me at this time.) I'm returning to this property on March 24th. If there are any changes to my feelings about this property I'll post a follow up review.

“Upscale Hotel with a few problems” Beautiful hotel but we had a few problems. The room was just refinished - very nicely. The tub did not drain - had to call for repair. Room service was a little spotty for a 5 star property - missing multiple items and the condiment jelly had already been used. Never had that happen before. When we pay top dollar we have high expectations.

“Not bad !” There are nicer W hotels in New York but nonetheless this is an ok one. Its starwood category is lower than the other Ws in New York, so if you book with points, it does require fewer points. Rooms are generally small but clean and modern. I'll stay here again if I get a good rate.

“Serviceable Hotel with the Basics” Currently staying at this Hotel over Labor day weekend. The hotel front desk staff is very accomodating. The Lobby is very small, the elevators are small, the hallways are small. I can see when they built this hotel from the ground up space saving was a big priority. The hotel was built from the ground up, and finished three months ago. ( June 2008) The rooms are very small, and of course the bathrooms are tiny. The shower has almost no pressure, do to watering saving device. The " SInk" is a Joke. Its the smallest sink I ever saw. Furnishing are nice, bed is good. When you put your clothes in the armoire it is so tiny, you cannot close the door property. There is a very nice flat panel LG TV in the room. Overall the room is in good shape, and very clean. Bed Linens are upgraded, and the carpet in the room is nice. Very Modern, and updated room. The doors are very thin, and you can hear everything going on outside in the hallways. If you are traveling alone, then the space issues are not too bad. A couple will be cramped. Three Forget it! The hotel rooms are very close to each other, so you can hear the opening and closing each time someone comes in or out. There is no closet in the room. Bottom line is that if you can stay here for $200 or under I would take it. Anything over $200 I would look elsewhere. I would rate this a 3.5 star property, only because of the small area in the rooms. The property is well located, and close to train stops.

“Standard Good W, Times Square can be a Pro and a Con” Spent 4 nights at this hotel as part of a group. Location-wise, it can be great, or horrible. It's loud, you're literally right off of Times Square, but for some people, that's perfect. I was on one of the highest floors and had no problems with street noise (I was facing a side street and NOT Times Square though). Others in my group who faced the square complained of noise though. Service was very good, all the staff was really nice. It was a bit annoying to have to take 2 elevators to get up to the room. Reception is on the 7th floor so you have to take one up to that level, then take a different one to your room. The room was rather spacious for NYC, big enough that I could do yoga in the room one night. The bed is comfortable (actually, I have the W mattress at home, so it's perfect!). Don't love the bowl sinks as stuff gets lost behind them, but all in all, it was fine.

“Awesome W Hotel in an awesome city” I was so impressed by the W in Austin. Excellent service from everyone from the minute I arrived. The decor and amenities in the hotel were some of the best I've experienced in any W hotel (and I've stayed in a ton.) The designers managed to merge a modern feel with Southwestern elements, to make it feel both contemporary and appropriate for the city and its heritage. The public spaces were beautifully designed and there were a ton of them. One room was wall-to-wall records, to keep with the live music reputation of the city. My room was large with a huge shower and I believe I had one of the standard rooms, so I assume they only get better as they change in levels. The W Austin has the largest hotel gym I've ever seen. I'm not exaggerating when I say that you could fit every other hotel gym I've ever seen into the W's space. It's got a ton of weight training machines and free weights along with a variety of cardio machines. All in a space with floor to ceiling windows with an excellent view of the city. (They also have a yoga room that is as large as my gym's yoga facility at home.) The pool space is excellent, although at 4 feet deep, it's more of a standing and cooling off pool than a pool to swim in. Great lounge chairs and cabanas if you're interested. I had excellent breakfast at the Trace restaurant. (Try the watermelon mint aqua fresca!) There were also many hip restaurants with excellent food within a one block walk from the hotel. I can't recommend this hotel highly enough. Can't wait to return to Austin to stay there again!

“Highly Recommended” Although we only stayed one night, our experience was excellent. The valet was so helpful and getting our car the next day was super fast. Love the hallway decor in this hotel, soothing and the paintings and lighting make it a nice walk to your room. The bathrooms are really big, the beds very comfortable. The pool looked amazing, we didn't have time to use it. Hope to return again soon.

“Clean, great service, good location” I've stayed at this hotel twice in the last two months. The service is excellent and the hotel is immaculate. The rooms are very clean and spacious. The complimentary bar in the evenings is great, with good appetizers, wine, beer etc. The bar area (which is also the breakfast area) is very large, with windows that allow for some great people watching. Breakfast is good and the staff at breakfast exceeds expectations. They pick up dishes as you are finished, check to see if you are satisfied with everything and keep the buffet and breakfast dining area immaculate. I wish they had some rooms with king size beds though.

“Nice Hotel in a Great Location” Location: The location is perfect for launching into Philadelphia sightseeing. We had no problems hailing cabs when needed and there is plenty of great stuff to do nearby. Positives: Our room had two queen beds, clean and comfortable. The room also had a mini-fridge, LCD HD TV and ihome alarm clock. The bathroom was average with a single sink and bathtub/shower combo; very clean and included the usual toiletry items. Overall the room size was larger than expected for this level of hotel. There was a really nice bar/lounge off of the lobby, while expensive, the service was prompt and the atmosphere good. Negatives: The city noise (trucks, sirens, etc.) came right into the room through the closed windows on the 7th floor. It's mostly quiet at night but activity outside started early and was persistent throughout the day. The area in front of the hotel is small, so during peak check-in time we found that we had to wait on a long line of cars. Overall I was happy with our stay here. The hotel was clean and well appointed for this price level. Service was good and the staff friendly.

“Nice romantic getaway” Stayed here last night for our anniversary getaway. The hotel is very cool, hip and urban modern. Very nice. The bathroom looks cool but is not very practical. Service was wonderful, very attentive and fast. We had the romance package which included an upgrade room, champagne, chocolates, late check out and breakfast. Only complaint was the AC did not cool the room as much as I wanted. Pool scene was happening. Small pool on the 10th floor that overhangs the building with clear side overlooking the street. Was jammed packed with a lot of 20 somethings. Not a quiet scene but interesting. Pool bar was fine. Ate at Charlie Palmers at the hotel. Very good food but had to wait 40 minutes even though we had reservations.

“Good Value” The Marriott Courtyard on Fifth is a great value! Centrally located in Midtown with excellent shopping and cultural experiences located nearby. The subway is several blocks away (which is a little inconvenient) but certainly walkable distance. The staff was very nice, helpful and attentive. The doormen were especially helpful holding bags for us after we checked out and arranging for a car to the airport. The breakfast buffet is served at the adjoining restaurant and is pretty standard for a Courtyard breakfast- the service was exceptional though. The rooms are not huge but I have been in smaller. The bathrooms are similar. I found my stay to be quite quiet despite other users reviews. It is nice to have the deli next door for cheap snacks and meals. I think the Courtyard is an excellent value for such a prime location.

“Fun and Memorable!” We really enjoyed our stay at the Liberty Hotel. Our only negative was the reception desk; it was frequently backed up and seemed to have inadequate staff for the size of the hotel, given that the hotel was filled when we were there. It is a unique and fun atmosphere, and the rooms are nice. Loved the location; close to the River, and not far at all from downtown attractions and very convenient to the T. The lobby was hopping in the evening, but we did not experience any noise in our room. Would definitely stay there again!

“Not a Ritz Yet, but Not Horrible” We spent 1 night in a club room at the new Ritz Carlton Boston Common. The doorman and front desk staff were very friendly and they made efforts to find me an upgraded room for booking via AMEX. However, no explanation of the Club lounge or AMEX package benefits were given. The Club lounge was one floor away and required a card to enter. The lounge was poorly stocked and staff fairly inept. We had difficultly communicating in English terms like grapefruit, tomato and onion. Food selections were a small step better than some airline club rooms and a proper cocktail could not be made as the staff were inept and could not make drinks like a vodka cranberry, in Boston! This is the worst club lounge of any Ritz Carlton I have visited. Our suite was large and comfortable featuring a bang olufsen sound system, 2 bathrooms and one large bathroom with a deep soaking tub. The AC system is a loud and hummed all night. The service we got was spotty at best. The maid removed towels at night but failed to replenish them. The internet connection in my room was broken and nobody bothered to fix it. The bell desk did not answer the phone. In the club lounge the staff were inattentive and lacked professionalism. The one positive note I have was they gave us a good North End restaurant referral. I mentioned my issues to management which promised me a special stay if I return. I may try the hotel again but do not waste money on the club floor. The value you receive for money is poor here overall. Our rate was $408 for the above service. The lobby is small. The restaurant Jerne is small and loud. A Pay per View movie is $15.99, wow! Room service and mini bar prices are very high. However, the rooms are still probably the best in Boston but I find the Copley Marriott or Westin better value if their rate is under $200. The area around the Ritz is also a bit scary.

“walks the classic/dated line” The Taj, formerly the Ritz, is amazingly located and steeped in Boston history. The running of the hotel seems to be slipping. I stayed here a few times when Taj first took the property over (they had a great package through Amex Platinum FHR) and had nice stays. This week the hotel was particularly expensive I think because so many parents are in town dropping off their children. The hotel was charging more, but didn't seem to have more staff on, so everything was off. The door key-cards weren't working so I kept needing to go get new keys, room service took an hour to arrive, and it took the doormen 45 minutes to get my car. Even though my paper was hanging on my door, the cleaning staff barged in--morning after morning. Then I guess because I had been in my room at 8, they never returned. If you're in a nostalgic mood—for a pre-frour seasons, pre-aman idea of luxury, this is a nice choice in Boston. I'd have a hard time putting up with the sloppy service if I were paying more than $450/night.

“Average everything, except the price which was very expensive!” A group of us spent 2 nights at the W City Center in early September. Let me be totally honest, the place is very hip and very cool. The lobby is beautiful and well appointed. There are beautiful flowers and candles everywhere as well as a very cool video show that is shot from a projector onto the massive walls. In the lobby, every detail is cared for perfectly. When you enter, a mat outside the hotel welcomes you with the specific time of day (i.e. Good morning in the morning) and the mat is changed in the evening to say Good Evening. Upon check-in we were offered a cocktail almost immediately, which I found unique. At check in we were advised that our room (booked through Priceline) contained one full size bed and that in order for the room to sleep the two grown men sharing it, we woudl need to pay an upgrade fee of $70 a night. Come on, who would expect two buddy's on a football cavation to stay in the same bed. The front dest clerk was wearing a suit jacket with what appeared to be a dirty Nike t-shirt underneath. We proceeded to the upgraded room and it was fine, but nothing special. I suppose teh PRiceline room was previously a closet based on the upgraded room size. The hotel is conveniently located near the orange line L so transportatoin is easy. On night 2 of our stay, we went to the hotel bar about 12:30 a.m. or so. When we tried to order a drink, the snappy female bartender motioned her hand horizontally across her neck and shouted, "we're done". I asked the occsional W person floating around the room what time the lounge closed and he indicated 1:00 a.m. Not sure why you can't get a drink in 30 minutes but in any event, the cry of "we're done" is certainly less than welcoming. All in all, the stay was well below average and well below expectations for a hotel of this nature. Others have said it before and it is exactly true, there is a reason the W in Chicago is ranked #76 out of 150 area hotels. Finally, at check out, one of our two rooms had an incorrect bill which took 15 minutes and two additional bills to straighten out.
“A waste of money.” Nice room. Terrible location. Slow Internet. Dirty common areas. Rundown. Way too many other options to flush money down this property.

“If you get stuck here on Priceline...” My girlfriend and I stayed at Gild Hall this past weekend, not by choice, by courtesy of Priceline. Granted, it was a really busy time in NYC, so we had great difficulty finding a good hotel at a reasonable price. So we tried Priceline and were placed at the Gild Hall. Would never stay here if I had a choice. Rooms were average at best, no service whatsoever (very shortstaffed), terrible location, very few cabs available. The one plus is there wasn't any real "city" noise. But there were a bunch of partiers taking advantage of the cheaper rates making noise late into the night... I say spend a few extra bucks and stay near the action.

“Pretty weak” Location is good. Room reminds me of a college dormitory. Repairs to the marble in the shower didn't match. Plus the Tv didn't work. Although the guy made a good effort to fix it, still not TV. Overall, a big yawn.

“Great Location and Beautiful Hotel” This is a great hotel. We were in San Antonio to for a girl's trip to celebrate a friend's birthday! This hotel is in a good location. Not right in the middle of all the restaurants on the RiverWalk but only a couple of blocks away. It was a surprisingly easy walk to the main attraction on the River and there were also a few cute bars and restaurants along the way. I think you can also walk on the RiverWalk to get to the attraction but we just stayed on the street level. The hotel itself is very elegant and the lobby is decorated beautifully. Check-In was great and we were able to save a few dollars by self-parking in the lot across the street. We just dropped off our stuff at the door and ran the car over to park. The rooms are a great size and clean. I would absolutely stay here again!

“Even better than the Benjamin” We stayed last year at the Benjamin, another Affina hotel. We loved our experience there (see my 3/24/05 review). We wanted to stay in a different part of town so we went with another Affina property. We loved our stay. The Dumont has a hip but cozy feel. In the two days we were there, I felt that the staff (especially the bell hops) got to know us well. They were very helpful with suggestions about restaurants. We had a lot of luggage and two kids, so when I asked the bell hop what he thought about the best way to get to the airport, he volunteered to come up to our room and survey our luggage. He then made arrangements for a driver and coordiated everything from there. That kind of service was common throughout our stay. Our room was on the 33rd floor and overlooked the river. The "L" shaped layout of the one bedroom until gave a great view. The room was beautiful and very large. It had a full kitchen with a dishwasher etc. At $369 per night, the rate was lower than small rooms in many other hotels in the area. It was also about the same price as a small room that looked directely into the side of a building at the Westin Times Square, which we had stayed at earlier in the week. The room has a lot of nice touches, such as a stereo, two tvs, a large desk area etc. The hotel has a pillow menu and "fit kits," which consist of portable CD players, pedometers etc. that can be borrowed by the guests. The beds were very comfortable. What I liked most was that the room was extremely quiet. We brought our kids (9 & 12) and never felt like we had to police them as we often do in hotels where the walls are thin. The hotel is in the Murry Hill area, which we ended up liking a lot. Despite it's 34th & Lexington location, it has a smaller town feel. By that, I mean that there aren't any hot dog vendors or packs of tourists roaming the streets. There are a lot of restaurants in the area serving a wide variety of cusine, but they mostly appeared to be filled with regulars. There was a 24 hour drug store right across the street. There is also a Guy & Gallard, which is a fantastic place to grab a quick and economical breakfast. I have nothing negative to say about this hotel. It was fantastic. At worst, being tourists, it was a bit far from many of the sights (Central Park, Theater District, Park Ave etc.) that we were visiting. Nevertheless, we liked returning to the area in the evening, so that we could leave the hustle of our days' adventures. On the way out, we were waiting by the elevator and a familiar looking woman was standing there. I did a double take and then realized Carolyn, Donald Trump's advisor in The Apprentice TV show was standing there. She apparantly stays there from time-to-time. She obviously knows good value, as the Dumont offers an outstanding experience.

“LOVE the Embassy Suites! Great Location! Highly Recommend this for families!” This was our second stay and we loved it even more! They are in process of renovating, although we thought it was just fine before! We asked for high floor cityview, and recvd 12th flr bayview! Breakfast is great! Manager's reception could be better...fritos, chips, ugh! More snack choices to go with drinks would be nice, but hey! its FREE~! We love this location, right across from harbor and seaport village. We did not have a car...So we took the Old Town trolley tour and got off and on at various stops! Another night we walked to Petco park to see baseball game! One day, we even took public transportation for a day to go to Mission Beach and Balboa Park! FUN! LOVE LOVE LOVE San Diego!

“Overall an excellent experience!!!” This is a beautiful hotel, in a great location, with wonderful service. The hotel was spotlessly clean. The bathrooms were a bit small; but overall I enjoyed our room. It didn't have that neutral "hotel look" that many rooms have. I would stay again in a heartbeat!!!

“ZaZa Different Every Time, That's what makes it fun!” ZaZa was our place to stay for a meeting we were attending. We booked a theme room, Bohemia Suite, and liked it. It was clean and comfortable. Since we did not do to much it was a nice little get away. I did ask them for no room spray, and I think they forgot to tell the cleaning service. Other than that all was great. I booked a massage and that was good too.

“Would stay here again” Stayed here for 4 nights during the first week of May. We requested a quiet floor and we were assigned a double bed on the 20th floor but away from the Puget Sound view. The room was fairly large, was quiet at night, and cleaned well by housekeeping. There was one morning that the water did not get warm enough but it was fixed in no time. The bed was comfortable, bathroom was well appointed, internet speed was not a problem. The location is unbeatable with its close proximity to Pike Market, Westlake Center, Pacific Center, a walgreens, Bank of America, several restaurants in the area, and the many shops. I do agree with one reviewer whose child's shin was injured by the bed frame. The metal bed frames supporting the mattresses stuck out a few inches beyond the mattresses albeit covered by the bed skirt. My 13 month old daughter who was playing at the foot of the bed also hit herself against that corner, and my shin hit the same particular bed frame corner a few times. On our last morning we splurged with the breakfast buffet at their 5th floor restaurant. The morning manager was very sweet, accomodating and friendly. She was the definite super star of the hotel with her sunny personality.

“Good value in DC” Spent 3 nights at Holiday Inn Georgetown for the Biotech Convention in DC. The hotel was a bit old with typical Holiday Inn styling so don't expect anything glamorous. Room was of good size and clean. A Safeway is nearby so easy to get groceries. Choices of buffet or made-to-order breakfast. The hotel does have a shuttle service but apparently only limited to the Georgetown neighborhood. Still need a car or a cab to get around to downtown DC.

“Good value, comfortable, convenient” Decided to get a hotel for the final night of our vacation after spending the previous nights at a friends apartment. Tried Priceline for downtown/copley but was unable to get anything for under $200 on only a few days notice. Saw the Embassy had vacancy at a nice AAA rate and took it. We had an excellent experience with this hotel. They stored our baggage in a secured room both before and after our stay, our room was clean and fully stocked with towels and toiletries. Breakfast was fantastic (they were running out of things near the end at 10:30, but that was to be expected). Airport T stop is a brief walk across a very nice new sports/park area, and the shuttle took us directly to our terminal when it was time to go. Seemed like if you needed a pickup, you might need to call the front desk or else you'd be waiting a bit.

“Rooms were small and not modern for the price” I stayed at this hotel for two nights, for the price it wasn't worth it AT ALL. Some floors were under construction and it was really nosey during the day and morning. I accidently got a one bed which I requested a two bed. They charged me $30 extra dollars a night when I had reserved one. The staff was friendly and delivered good service. I didn't really like this hotel for a few reasons: there was NO views, the bathrooms look very old, the elevators are really slow, taxi's really do not stop at this location, and the AC/heater in our rooms did not work. For what I paid a night I could have stayed at a better, nicer hotel in Midtown.

“Great Location for Downtown Chicago” The hotel is right across from the river and the river view rooms have an amazing view. The lobby is quite large. The guest rooms are large and bathrooms are quite well appointed. Flat screen TV, of course. Refrigerator and safe in room as well. The gym is not a bad size. The concierge lounge is not the biggest, but had tasty offerings for breakfast. The front desk staff was friendly. The location is top notch with easy access to everything downtown Chicago has to offer. I would stay there again.

“we'll stay again” Stayed here while our son was at the hospital (the hotel is an easy walk from Mass General Hospital). Although the room was small and a little claustrophobic (next time we will try asking for an exterior room), the staff was lovely, the room was spotless, and the bed was extremely comfortable. Our only complaint was with the telephones. We slept comfortably knowing our son had the hotel phone number, only to discover that our son had been trying to reach us for hours on end from the hospital but kept getting a busy signal and that even those at the Kimpton Hotel Group's main 800 number had been unable to get through to the Onyx for him. When we shared our concern with the front desk the next morning, another guest had just complained as well. The hotel had been open less than a month. We received a follow-up email from the hotel's manager, assuring us that they are going to install more phone lines. Our son will need more surgery soon. We have decided to stay there again, but will keep our cell phone with us to be certain we can be reached.

“Suites offer good value” Stayed here for 2 nights in a King Suite. There are 8 suites per floor, all on a corner (the hotel is H shaped), and they are twice the size of standard rooms. The reception room has a three-piece sofa, second TV, CD player, desk and work chair; the bedroom has its own TV and Bose CD player. Room furnishings were high quality albeit 'traditional'. The bathroom was surprisingly small with no separate shower and only one sink - presumably the same size as standard rooms. Being a corner room, it had more light than a standard room although it was still relatively dark and needed the lights on during the day. Overall, I recommend the Kings Suites over the standard rooms. They are twice the size and lighter, but often only cost an extra $50 per night because there are so many of them (8 per floor) that the hotel cannot charge much of a premium. Compare prices with a one-bed suite at the Waldorf next door, however, as these are bigger, brighter (if you get a high floor) and have two bathrooms.

“Very pleasant stay” We stayed at the Contessa for two nights in March 2006, and had a great time. The Contessa is a contemporary hotel located on the Riverwalk. (Be sure to walk to the left when you leave the hotel on the Riverwalk. It leads to the active part of the walk. To the right is the Westin and then there's not much.) It is not right next to the bar scene. We found this a plus, as it is a very short walk to the bars, but the noise of the bars won't keep you up. I found the architecture and design of the public areas to be serene and relaxing. We had breakfast at the Hilton one morning and the Contessa the next. The price of the breakfast at the Contessa was half of the Hilton's, and 100% better. Internet service is free, which we also enjoyed. The staff was very friendly and informative. The pool is on top of the building in a contemporary setting with views of the city. Our only complaint was there was not poolside bar service. In order to have drinks, you must go to the bottom floor, where the bar is located, purchase your drinks, and then bring them back up. We went with our two children (ages 7 and 4), and the size of the suite was perfect for our family. The room was nicely decorated, but I will say that the suite portion was a bit dark. The beds were extremely comfortable. Parking was a bit expensive, $24 day. I don't know how that compares to other hotels. All in all, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Contessa and would stay there again.

“Marriott West Loop Excellent Value” I just stayed two days at this hotel over the Thanksgiving weekend. I received a great rate of $71.00 per night on the hotel's website. I've noticed that this hotel frequently has great rates on the weekend. For a reduced rate, this hotel was excellent. It's an older property - - built in the early - mid 1970's at least - - it not a little older. I would not pay the rack rate for this hotel and there usually is no need to do so if you do your homework. Service: excellent. Every staff member was polite, professional, and helpful. Decor: Dated and in need of an update - - but in good repair. Nothing was worn out, broken, or dirty. Room size: adequate room - - about average for a corporate hotel these days. It was not huge, but not cramped either. The room had all of the usual ammenities but did not have a mini bar or laptop safe. It was equipped with high speed internet for a fee of $9.95 per day. Views: This hotel is surrounded by other buildings so you won't get much of a view in most rooms. My room overlooked the wall of the parking garage next door. Limited direct light into the room. Cleanliness: Very clean - - everywhere I went, the hotel was clean and in good repair. My room and bath were very clean. Bed: excellent. this hotel has the new Marriott bed and it's very comfortable. Restaurants: I did not use the hotel's restaurants as there were lots of options in the immediate area. Concierge Lounge: Fairly typical of Marriott Concierge Lounges. It was clean, comfortable and offered a very nice breakfast buffet. Parking: $10.00 per day for self parking in a connected garage. Location: Very good but not excellent. It's about a 20-25 minute walk to the Galleria Mall and about 15 minutes to the stores and restaurants on Post Oak. It's about a 7 to 10 minute walk to the shops and restaurants at Uptown Park. All-in-all, this is a good location that allows you to walk to lots of shopping and restaurants - - although you'll be the only one on the sidewalk. People just don't walk anywhere in Houston. You can stay at the Westin Hotels at the Galleria or the JW Marriott at the Galleria - - or at the Hilton on Post Oak which puts you right in the middle of all the shops and restaurants there, but you'll pay a lot more. The 15 - 25 minute walk was not a problem for me as the weather was excellent. Also, the hotel has a complimentary shuttle that runs at scheduled times that can take you to the Galleria and back. In summary, if you're willing to give up newer, more upscale furnishings and be a few minutes' walk away from shopping, this is an excellent choice. It's clean and comfortable with excellent service. I will definitely stay at this hotel if the occasion arises - - as long as I can get a discounted rate.

“Good deal in midtown Manhattan” It's practically impossible to find a decent hotel in midtown Manhattan for under $200/night, but I kept checking until I ran across the La Quinta on West 32nd Street and jumped on it. The location absolutely can't be beat--less than a block from the Herald Square subway station between Broadway and Fifth Avenue, only a few blocks from Times Square and almost directly behind the Empire State Building, and only a couple of blocks from Penn Station. The room was small, as are most NYC hotel rooms, but the bed was comfortable and the bathroom and shower were very good. A couple of nitpicks--it's VERY easy to walk past this place; unlike other hotels in the area there's no banner sign, only smallish plaques on the facade. The elevators are pretty slow, but I was on the second floor and mostly used the stairs. The outlets on the desk didn't work but I'm used to using my laptop on the bed so that was no big deal. The free internet worked fine until the last full day of my stay, Sunday, when it was down all day. Fortunately someone in the area had an open connection so I hooked up on that. If you like Korean food you're in luck, as the hotel is on "Korea Way" and is literally surrounded by 24-hour Korean BBQs. If you don't there's a small deli called Speedy's down the block that makes good sandwiches and hot food, and the usual fast food suspects plus some Irish pubs are very close by. For being so close by hot spots the room was pretty quiet. If you're by yourself or with someone with whom you don't mind sharing close quarters you're probably not going to do better than the La Quinta if you want to stay in midtown--I'll definitely keep this place in mind next time I come to NYC.
“Funky nice hotel with pleasant staff” You could play basketball in the main room, but the bathroom is claustrophobic. Other than that, excellent experience.
“awesome!!” awesome hotel, very modern, super clean

“Value Pricing, First Class Service” Just came back from a four day stay here and really liked it. Great location, across the street from Carnegie Hall, convenient to theaters, Lincoln Center, and shopping. At first glance, hotel looks very basic--none of the impressive lobby spaces you see at other, more expensive places. But, the important things are there, we had a large (by New York standards) clean room. The plumbing looks dated, but it works. Room came with a pantry--microwave, fridge, and coffeemaker. Staff / guest ratio here is higher than at similar hotels; they have courteous and quick bell service. All you can eat continental breakfast at $6 is worth it--quality of rolls and pastries was very good. You won't hear noise from your neighbors as the building is older and well-constructed. Street noise is another story--W 57th St is a busy cross-town throughfare, and you will hear it even if staying on an upper floor. One other small drawback is that there was no place to plug in a computer at the room desk, although this may not be a big deal if you're in NYC for leisure. Overall, the postives here far outweigh the rather small negatives.

“Decent place, dated decor but otherwise good hotel” Overall a good hotel and decent choice to stay, particularly if you have a good discount. However, if you are paying full price, you might want to reevaluate your other options first. Pros: - Location: steps away from the Mile and right in the area with a good mix of nice restaurants and boutique shops. Taxi stand is right next to the building, making catching a cab at an inconvenience hour very early morning a breeze. - Soaker tub and separate shower in a 4 star, i guess that's a plus? Cons: - A bit dated decor in the room and in the hotel hallways. - The soaker tub is a bit small in comparison.

“Not up to Kimpton's Standards” I'm a native to D.C. and enjoy the area's hotels, especially the Kimpton chain, but I wasn't impressed with the Madera. Stayed for 1 night, 3/25-3/26 and was disappointed. The front desk staff was extremely courteous and helpful, however the room wasn't up to par. Our King room was clean & stylish, but very small compared to the other 3 nearby Kimpton hotels (Topaz, Rouge & Helix). The decor is stylish, but the color scheme is bland. As a previous poster mentioned, the molding on the doors & walls is gouged & looks sloppily painted over, not repaired, and the sink/counter was outside of the bathroom ....something I'd expect in a Days Inn, not a Kimpton hotel. The in-room honor bar was merely a large Igloo-type cooler that wasn't even cold, however, it was fully stocked with juices, sodas, beer, vodka & champagne. The bathroom had the usual Aveda bath products, a shower cap, large towels & a bathrobe. There was also a Madera logo-ed umbrella in the closet, which could be purchased for $25. We had lunch at Firefly, the hotel's restaurant, and it was fair. A little overpriced for what you get, but again, the service was very good & staff were friendly. The best thing about Madera is the location on Dupont Circle - it's close to many restaurants, lounges, bars & the Metro (subway). But for the money, I think Kimpton's Topaz Hotel, which is on the other side of Dupont Circle, is a much better option.

“Great boutique style hotel in a convenient location. . .” Overall, I had a great stay here. The front desk was exceptionally polite, and very helpful in arranging for a taxi and guidance on restaurants. This neighborhood is probably considered downtown/financial district, but it's just across the street from Chinatown too. Plenty of good restaurants within walking distance, but the immediate neighborhood does get quiet pretty early in the night. This is largely an area that people commute into for work, and then go back home elsewhere. I walked to North Beach a couple of times, and the walk was easy and interesting. You're also not very far from a handful of bus stops, so getting around shouldn't be a problem. As for the hotel, it was very clean (a must for me), quaint, well decorated, just trendy enough, and the rooms were done well. They're not extraordinarily large, but you have to expect that in NYC, San Francisco, Europe, etc. . . Having said that, I had plenty of space. Overall, great stay. My purpose was business and it was perfect for me. It could probably be in a more "lively" area for vacation, but you are not far from lively areas at all. I would recommend this to friends/family for sure.

“Ottimo hotel con vista sulla baia di Boston” L'hotel InterContinental si trova su Atlantic Ave a Boston, una zona molto comoda rispetto ai trasporti, in particolare all'aeroporto raggiungibile anche in taxi-battello. L'hotel ha una ampia lobby con 2 ristoranti ed un bar che offrono specialità soprattutto a base di pesce. I prezzi dei ristoranti sono piuttosto alti ma il servizio e la qualità del cibo sono ottimi. L'hotel ha molte camere disposte su 12 piani, di cui buona parte con una splendida vista sul mare che offre delle albe e tramonti eccezionali. Le camere fronte strada possono essere un po' più rumorose a causa della stazione dei pompieri proprio di fronte. Il servizio in generale è molto buono e le camere ampie e molto pulite, così come la SPA e la palestra posizionate al secondo piano.

“Good location, Nice Room but some dissapointments” This is the third time I have stayed at this hotel - although the previous stay was over 5 years ago. The main reason for choosing was the location - at the heart of Fishermans Wharf - very good transport - at the end of the F line and the Hyde - Powell Hyde Beach Cable Cars (suggest you go early to Hyde - Beach line to avoid queue and to get best seats). All the benefits of FIshermands Wharf (attractions and restuarants). Also around the corner from the Citysightseeing bus tour to the City and Golden Gate Bridge. I paid for a business room - and whilst the lift implies that key card access is required - anyone appears to be able to access including the PCs and Printer (free board pass printing in Lobby for all guests). The room was big and clean - good views of the Bay and Alcatraz - (and the bins below but not really disturbed). The decoration is dated but overall clean and more than acceptable. Good size LCD TV with good selection of channels. PC Platimun membership recognised - some nice freebies for members. The only real dissapointment was the Internet - for what was a Business Level room. The spead at best was 100kbps (which is not really highspeed) intermittent connection so could not log on to work via a VPN or steam from my slingbox. The only compensation is that I could get one of the Free Street WIFI signals for 15 mins at a time that gave me over 10MBPS. As long as you dont want the internet other than for e-mail this is a good holiday hote.

“Top Lage und (für New York) bezahlbar bei rechtzeitiger Buchung” 2 Blocks vom Central Park entfernt liegt das Hotel in einer Seitenstrasse. Wir hatten ein recht großes Zimmer im 21. Stock. Der Straßenlärm war also nur entfernt zu hören. Das Personal war nett, konnte/wollte allerdings die Minibar im Zimmer nicht reparieren. Bei den Minibarpreisen war das allerdings kein richtiges Problem, zumal um die Ecke ein kleiner Supermarkt und direkt gegenüber vom Hotel ein Starbucks war. Zimmer 279 USD/Nacht geht für die Qualität des Hotels. Kurz vor Abflug wäre es das Doppelte gewesen. Das rechnet sich dann nicht mehr.

“"Liked Hotel a Lot"” Stayed at the Hyatt for business. Took a cab to hotel. Don't know if the subway will get you close to hotel. Checked in went smooth even thought hotel was very busy. I had a room with a wonderful view of the river and the Navy Pier. Room was clean and bed comfortable. This is a business hotel during the week, but can see how it would be a good tourist hotel also. I like the service and prompt attention. You can check out via phone, menu on tv or down at the the desk. There are limited places to eat around hotel but walk down Wacker and there are lots of choices. Ask at the front desk. There is an underground area with all kinds of places to eat..Starbucks, fast food, etc. connected to the West Tower. Enjoyed my stay and would return.

“Clean & friendly, not much of a pool” I don't like traveling to cities where you have to drive everywhere, but I had to go to Austin for work. Colleagues suggested the Springhill Suites, and it is a good hotel. Nothing fancy or inspiring, but clean, with the basics for a "suite" hotel. The daily cleaning service hasn't forgotten anything all week, which is unusual in my experience. The hotel is right next to several other hotels, and lots of chain restaraunts and stores. The views are of the freeway and parking lots. The swimming pool as a way to get any exercise is a joke. The front desk staff is friendly, parking works, and they have some "room service" menus from local restaraunts.

“Pretty sweet place” I thought this was a pretty darn nice Holiday Inn. It has some character. The location is fantastic....easy walk to Beale Street and right next to the Rendezvous ribs restaurant. (sorry, but that place is overrated). The room was on the small side, but was very comfortable. It's not cheap, but very competitive with the other properties in the Beale Street area. The front desk was friendly and helpful. Recommended.

“My favorite get away” I in love with this hotel. The rooms are comfortable and stylish, I want to move in. The beds are amazing. Service is warm, friendly and professional. The Woodward restaurant and room service are both the tops. I have spend two long weekends there in the past six months and will be staying again. My only slight negative is that there are only two small elevators that can be difficult to get up and down with luggage. This is the one of the best boutiques I have ever stayed in. I love the hotel and staff, both are something special.

“Off the beaten path” Not in the downtown area, nut close to my relatives. If you want something different, try put this historic location (accommodations are in new facilities. Great for Sunday Brunch.

“Le moins bon de tous les Novotel de la planète?” ...et il se trouve dans une des villes les plus excitantes de cette planète. Clientèle française nombreuse et service client médiocre. Bras croisés. Sourires à la demande. Amabilité en sus. Je suis désolé. Séjournant à la fois pour des raisons professionnelles et ainsi que pour le fun dans les hôtels du groupe Accor régulièrement, je constate que la sélection et la formation des équipes n'est pas au rendez-vous ici. S'agirait-il d'un franchisé? Réveil oublié donne rendez-vous professionnel manqué. Pas d'excuse de l'opératrice: juste un 'ok' et téléphone raccroché! Au petit déjeuner, c'est comme si vous n'existiez pas...Petit souci technique dans la chambre: réglé sans m'adresser la parole et avec un regard méprisant. Tous ces incidents font oublier le reste qui pourrait être positif: lit confortable, chambre plutôt rénovée. Emplacement central. Certains rêvaient de l'Afrique...et moi de l'accueil probable au Sofitel à quelques blocks.

“Great hotel” Had a fantastic weekend in Dallas and the Renaissance. Staff were really friendly and helpful and the view from the room was simply spectacular. You wouldn't walk from the hotel to downtown, but it's only a few minutes away by car. I was expecting a little bit of a dated hotel, but everything was in tip-top shape. Clean, comfortable and the staff make all the difference for me. They're happy to advise you on where to go and what to do.

“Loved the Westin!!!!!!!” Our family spent one night in Boston to celebrate my husband's birthday and for the Rocketts Christmas show at the Wang. We have always been to loyal to Hilton but I came across a Winter special rate of $159 for a stay (two double bed) at the Westin so we booked it. Prior to our arrival I had faxed the hotel and asked for the possibilty of a room on a higher level overlooking the Charles River as it was my husbands birthday. We arrived at 11am on Friday during check out and were given the option by the valet jockey to park for around $20 across the street at the Claredon Garage. We dropped our luggage and opted to park in the garage. Upon checking in we were upgraded to a corner suite (Thanks Westin!) with one king bed. Requested a roll-away for one of the kids and off to the room we went. Our suite was a spectacular corner suites with two near walls of windows overlooking Boston and the Charles River. My seven year old son was in his glory as where the two windows met in the corner was a small circular interior rail that he would sit on and overlook all the bustling in Boston-a perfect "inside perch" with the best view in Boston! The room had a "heavenly" king size bed with pull-out couch and chairs along with a desk area. The following day we did have to agree that the bed is truly 'heavenly" with all the pillows and fluffy covers. The pool and fitness area is top notch. The gym is not a typical hotel gym but a full work out facility with flat screen TV 's at all units and Bon Appetite and Runners world magazines all lined up and ready for reading. The pool was good sized and the temperature was perfect. We were able to work out in the gym and overlook the kids in the pool from the glass window. Then when we returned to our room after dinner we found a chilled bottle of Moet Champagne and a tray of chocolate covered strawberries and confections along with birthday wishes for my husband. How very nice!! We only stayed one night but oh how one night changed us now to Westin people!!! Everyone we came into contact with was curtious and willing to assist us with anything and we had an exceptional stay.

“Location Location Location” We booked a modern POD room for our stay. The room was 175 square feet with a double bed, but hey, it's New York. Sometimes size does't matter. We were not planning to be in the room much so it didn't matter. The room was efficient and well laid out, but the best part of the room was the bathroom. It was modern with sleek blue tiles and a large four foot walk-in shower. The room had windows in the room and bathroom. However, our view was less than stellar. The view was of our building's interior air shaft. Could be an issue for some, but we've stayed at many NYC hotels over the years, you just need to take these things in stride. If it was the TRUMP Tower, I'd be upset. Hotel staff was attentive and pleasant. We had an early flight, so when we arrived in the morning our room wasn't ready. However, the front desk stored our bags and asked for my mobile phone number. The front desk called a few hours later to notify me our room was ready and that our bags would be taken to our room. Nice! 6 Columbus is conveniently located one block from Columbus circle which has access to Subway lines 1,A,B,C and D and the TimeWarner building. TimeWarner Center has many shops, and restaurants. You can find the top rated and my all time favorite restaurant Per Se at Time Warner Center. You can also find a large Whole Foods with a full grocery store on the lower level that also offers healthy take out options for breakfast, lunch and dinner. If you're in NY and want to stay in a small boutique hotel near Central Park with convenient access to transportation, shops and food, check out 6 Thompson.

“スタッフは最悪。あの「マンダリン」と思ってはいけない。” チェックインの際、チェックアウト日を確認したにも拘わらず、チェックアウト前日夜に部屋から閉め出されました。1日早いチェックアウト日のデータをルームキーに入力されていて、且つ、フロントもそう思い込んでいました。 当然クレームを言いましたが、謝罪の一言もなし。(アメリカ流とは言わせません。「マンダリン」なのですから。) 使えるようになったルームキーで部屋に入ると、バスルームの私物が全て捨てられていました。怒りは頂点に達し、フロントにブチギレ! そもそもチェックインしたときから部屋のランプの電球は割れたままだったり、シャワーヘッドは壊れていたり、数々の不満がこのホテルの部屋にはありました。 眺望もいい部屋をとリクエストしていたのに、たいしてよくもなく。 朝食は無料でルームサービスのプランだったため、これだけが唯一よかったこと。 それ以外は「マンダリン」を名乗るに値しないレベルのホテルでした。ものすごく高かったのに。 日本のホテルは、客の私物(ゴミ箱の中味)も1週間くらいは処分せずに保管しています。 なのに、このホテルは本当に「棄てて」いました。 チェックアウト時に、私物代として100ドルのディスカウントをしてくれましたが、気分的には最悪なままこの「マンダリン」ホテルを後にしました。

“Average but dreary” Stayed here one night with my small daughter. We were en route to England and I chose it because it was the closest hotel to the American Museum of Natural History (a two-minute walk). If you just want a cheap place ($199 and they gave me an upgraded, renovated room) in an excellent location (a few hundred feet off Central Park in one direction, and off Columbus Ave and all its boutiques and restaurants in the other direction) then I would recommend this hotel to you. It is clean but not pristine (moldy shower head and line of mold on top of shower). And it certainly feels safe. But the room renovation is dog's breakfast of clashing styles that just makes you think the owners bought whatever was on sale. Plus, they left the old carpet in the room. I couldn't wait to turn out the light. Staffing is uneven. We experienced both warm/cordial and abrupt/grumpy. Nobody at the front desk seems like a serious hotel person. My guess is that everyone is en route to "a better place" and this is the day/night job. The whole thing is a shame, because this hotel--given the fabulous location--could be one of the great boutique hotels of New York. The lobby still has all the beautiful old tile and woodwork. The elevators are glamorous. If someone cared about historic renovation and design and customer service, they could really do something special here. (Milestone Hotel London people, how about coming to America?!!!!) I would only stay here again if I were looking for a bargain.

“Great for business, probably not a vacation place” Can't quite understand all the negative reviews. The rooms here were spotless and fresh smelling. Sure the decor was a little 70's, but they must have gotten a deal on it recently. No wallpaper was peeling off the bathroom walls, there was no crud in the bathroom. The hallway carpet looked a little tired, but not too bad. Service was polite and helpful. Sure, you could hear the freeway outside, but not with the a/c running. The room had a great, powerful shower that pounded away the days toils. Breakfast was a buffet for $13.95, which seemed crazy as lunch buffet was $9.95. I did have a quesadilla from room service and it had fresh guacamole. Now, the surrounding area is a little more ethnic than some and I can't imagine bringing a family here for a vacation. I'm not sure what attractions would be around the hotel, but there were plenty of chain restaurants, as well as some highly rated Indian food places.

“Hampton Inn does a good job” The Hampton Inn has made my business trip to Denver much more tolerable. The hotel does a great job with everything I've asked them to do. The hotel is very quiet, I've never been disturbed by noise at all. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. The bathroom is good sized. My only complaint about this stay was that one of the two elevators was down for service for almost my entire stay. The property is fairly new; I hope the staff does everything they can to keep the place looking great. Location might an issue for some travelers. The hotel kind of on the easten edge of downtown Denver. There is no onsight restaturant, but the a.m. breakfast is a winner. Finally, valet parking is expensive, but there is parking on the street (free between 6 p.m. and 9 a.m. right now) and in couple of cheap lots less than a half block away.

“Great relaxing family weekend getaway at Westin Copley” Travelled to Boston for a quick weekend getaway from NY and found myself staying at the 1st hotel I stayed in more than 8 years ago when I first visited Boston but instead of my parents it was with my family...Drove in and arrived around 3pm on Friday to a full valet lot which had us wait for about 15 minutes until the valet guy collected our car and info...Went to check-in soonafter and was told our preferred room was not available so we went to kill time in the nearby Copley Plaza mall until they called us back to confirm it was ready. After more than an hour of shopping, I was concerned our room was still not ready and called back to inquire and was told our room still wasn't ready!!? I was very surprised to hear this given I didn't request a special room, especially being a SPG Gold Member but before I could react further, the front desk guy decided to upgrade us to a corner junior suite with 2 queen beds and a river view, which was a very nice gesture. As such, we quickly returned and were relieved to find our room on the 18th floor near perfect in terms of space/view/ and decor and promptly we rested finally after being up all day. Otherwise our entire weekend stay was great as the room and the unbeatable views was thoroughly enjoyed by my wife and infant daughter...The bathroom was a bit tight but we liked the overhead rainshower instead of the typical heavenly shower installed...Our queen beds were as heavenly as can be and the pillows were just soft and plushy enough for us. Room service did a great job cleaning our room and replenishing our water bottles and Starbucks coffee regularly! People we encountered from the front desk to concierge to bell valet were all courteous and helpful to us during our entire stay...The Westin is extremely convenient to walk to the Back Bay station and also well connected to the adjacent Copley Mall and other interconnecting shopping plazas so we hardly had to step outside in the chilly weather. Had a minor issue with the double billing on the valet charges when we checked out but it was quickly fixed in a NY minute! All in all though we will definitely return to stay at the Westin Copley again with my family when the weather is warmer next year for sure. Thanks for the relaxing weekend!

“Noisy, Tired Hotel, Great Location” The location is fantastic. The room decor is somewhat updated and rooms are certainly serviceable. The staff are helpful and service oriented. Sleeping rooms, meeting rooms, and "public" lavatories could be much cleaner. The hotel seems a bit old and a bit tired overall. Trolley noise outside can go into the wee hours. If you get a great price for a few nights, this hotel may be a good choice. Breakfast is very nice: remember if you just stick to the cold buffet it is cheaper.

“It was a perfect stay at a nice and pet friendly hotel.” We are so happy to have discovered the Candlewood Suites chain on our roadtrip. On our trip we stayed at three different locations of this chain and each time had a very good experience. We checked in with our three beagles with a small pet fee and no problems. We made our reservations on the road from about two hours away. The desk staff was friendly and helpful. The parking lot was well lit and there was a nice designated dog walking area. Our room had a full size fridge, stove, dishwasher, dishes, etc. There was a workspace area, and a large tv with a DVD player. The room was spotless and smelled very good, especially for a smoking room. The bed was comfy. The hotel has a full pantry area (toiletries, snacks, tv dinners, etc.) and the prices are very reasonable (50 cents for a soda). There was a gym and a laundry facility with free washers and dryers.. you just provide the soap or buy some it the pantry. We had no outside or hallway noise in our stay. Several places for food, shopping, and gas nearby. The only negative thing I can say about this chain is that you have to make ice with the icemaker in the freezer in your room. The icemaker is very slow. We just know now that when we stay with them we need to stop for a bag of ice nearby. Not a biggie for us. After two stays in a Candlewood Suites we have decided that whenever we are on the road, dogs or not, it will be the hotel we look for first.

“amazing rooms!!!!” the size of the room and charm of the hotel were great!!! a bit touristy area but that makes it exciting. best feature of room???? a long hallway away from the door which minimizes the hotel hallway noise. looooooved having a fridge and microwave in the room!! and was able to walk around the beds, had a sitting area etc. highly recommend.

“Great Hotel for Century City Business Travelers” Overall this hotel was great for me as a business stay. Rooms were clean, comfortable and quiet. Unlike most other hotels in LA you couldn't hear your neighbor in the next room which is nice. I do like the fact that they have separate showers and bathtubs. The house car was always convenient going to and from the office down the street. All the staff were very nice and most called me by name, which doesn't happen very often at hotels anymore. The only downside to staying here is the lack of restaurants in Century City but it's only a 5 minute drive and there are plenty. There is also a Ralphs down the street which was nice for getting some soda and snacks on the cheap. You pay for parking just like everywhere else, $36 per day. You do have to pay for internet which is hit or miss with most hotels in LA. It was $12.95 per day here. Overall I would definitely go back.

“Dated property that is not convenient to major sights” Stayed here for a convention. An easy cab ride from Reagan National. Clearly an older property but the common areas have been well maintained and updated. However, the rooms and bathrooms are very small, reflecting the age of the property, and in need of a facelift. The property is a block away from a Metro stop, so you could in theory use this hotel as a base for sightseeing, but the DC subways are packed during rush hour and I did not feel as safe as in say Boston after dark. There is a small commercial area near the hotel, with a few restaurants and a CVS drugstore but no grocery store. Otherwise the property is quite isolated. We had a reception at the National Zoo and it is a long walk from the hotel to the zoo proper. Far better choices in close to the Mall area, especially if traveling with a family.

“Nice change to stay in SoHo” I get to New York quite frequently, and usually stay on the Upper West Side or in Midtown. On this trip, I was attending a meeting at NYU, so I decided to stay close by. When I chose this hotel, I had some concerns because it is part of the Choice Hotels group, which I associate with downmarket motels. However, the Solita Soho is part of their boutique Ascend Collection and is absolutely fine, and not a bad value. The room and bath were well-equipped, though it's time for them to replace some of the towels. The staff was friendly and helpful. For me, the main negative point was the flaky Internet service. The hotel's location is great for lower Manhattan. The hotel is surrounded by Little Italy, Chinatown, Greenwich Village, and SoHo. It's only a 20 minute walk to the WTC area with shopping at J&R and Century21. About 8 different subway lines stop two blocks away on Canal Street, so it doesn't take very long to get around the city. But most of what you might need is within walking distance. Would I stay here again? Definitely yes.

“Amazing” Hotel 1000 was a wonderful choice. Location is right downtown so it was great to go right outside and walk around town. I was a bit surprised by the "adult" store next door though. The rooms are really something not to be missed. I received a bowl of WA apples as many others did. I had no trouble with hot water or water pressure as others did. I personally didn't like that the only in room coffee option was french press. It is just to strong for me. So why not 5 stars? The room wasn't ready!!! As many, many others stated previously, it is crazy that they can't turn the rooms around in time. They gave me sister and I a drink coupon for their bar, which was nice. But after slowly sipping our drink, we still had to wait in the lobby for 20-30 minutes. Very frustrating. That said, I'd go again. The rooms really are that nice! Oh, valet service. There is a charge and the guys expect a tip each way. (FYI) Enjoy your stay!!
“Great” We had a suite and it was fab! Great concierge by the name of Philip.

“Amazing Service, Awesome Food and Comfortable Rooms” I have stayed at this hotel more than 150 times and I can honestly say it's my favorite hotel overall in the world. Oh, there are fancier ones with bigger rooms, but it's the overall service and consistent quality of the food that make it great - not to mention FREE self-parking! The staff do an amazing job of knowing your name and I often witness first-time guests getting called by name right away as well. Their room service menu is teriffic and their new restaurant may look trendy, but it's excellent. Everything is low-key and the relaxed staff make it the opposite of a Ritz-Carlton property, which has always felt kind of snooty to me. No one EVER treats you that way at the Four Seasons - and everyone from the front-desk staff to the maids to the operators - are friendly and classy. If you have the money or just want to splurge, this will be an unforgetable stay. Their beds are so nice, you'll want to take one home - we did!

“met expectations” Nice hotel, up to date rooms, helpful polite staff. Restaurant is good. Just what you would expect from a Marriott. Health club is only average. no pool or hot tub. Concierge lounge serves the exact same food every night.

“Good hotel in all respects” Moved here from their sister hotel when the phones there went out. This is a hotel of excellent value in a terrific, central location. Well-trained, professional staff. The hotel does a good job of providing amenities in the room that satisfy most needs, and they will quickly provide other necessaries, e.g., shaving cream. The towels were a bit threadbare for what I would have expected. They have a machine down the hall that provides chilled filtered water that flows at a very slow pace into plastic bottles they supply. Nice touch, but it takes a while to fill the bottles. The bar was very nice and had a good view. Comfortable bed. My room had a sensational view. It did not have a minibar, which was a surprise, but when I inquired, they brought one within a few minutes.

“Wonderful Hotel” We stayed here on the tail end of a trip to Sedona, the Grand Canyon and southwest Utah. This was a great hotel. The pool area was nice, the room was large and clean and the breakfast was good. The location was excellent. My son and I walked to the Diamondbacks game in about 10 minutes and my wife and daughter walked to the Arizona Center to eat and shop. I would stay here anytime!

“Great hotel, good location (3/11 - 3/14)” After several reviews here, I was somewhat hesitant to stay at the Westin Grand. My fears were unfounded - I had a wonderful 8th floor room. I assume this room was recently remodeled, as everything was in good shape. The bathroom was outstanding. Huge tub and a glass-walled shower. Nice finishes as well. The bed had the usual Westin comforters and sheets, although it did sag a bit in the middle. The front desk staff was wonderful - they allowed me to check in at noon, and throughout my stay gave great service. All common areas appeared to be recently remodeled, so the hotel looked to be in good shape. Excellent location - Metro is about 3 blocks away. Safe area, never felt unsure even when walking with my two young children.

“Lovely hotel, good value” What a breath of fresh air after spending the previous night at the Intercontinental a half-block away. The interior of the Omni is gorgeous, the hallways very pretty, and the room well decorated and maintained. The bathroom is clean and updated and the view spectacular. The artsy pool, which is on the small side, was lovely and my young daughter spent most of her time there. I used the well-appointed fitness center several times and was impressed by the set up. The equipment was all in excellent shape. There was a variety of equiment: stationary bikes, ellipticals, treadmills (with personal TVs), free weights, pilates balls, and more. And the service! The front desk is manned by the most competent, agreeable staff I have ever come across! After reading previous reviews, I joined the loyaly program before booking the hotel and received some nice perks, including a bottle of water and welcome letter, an exercise kit in my room, and a child's play pack. Do yourself a favor: join the loyalty program: it's FREE! The hotel also set me up with a nanny to watch my child while I was at an all-day business meeting. The only negative is that I found our bed to be too hard for me. I like softer, plushed beds. I think a plush topper would make it perfect for me, but that is a personal preference. Because of that, I am giving the Omni a five-star rating and will plan to stay here again.

“Compact, OK location, but are there any better?” We stayed at The New Yorker Hotel for four nights arriving on 17th July. The location of the hotel is OK but in a slightly seedy part of 8th Ave. The rooms are typical NYC: compact with the bare essentials. I expected a room safe and there was none and same for a fridge which would have been useful during the heatwave of the east coast. The bed was comfortable and filled a lot of the room. The 'wardrobe' was not as deep as a clothes hanger but there were enough drawers. I would suggest bringing your own wash products as their's are not very nice. Breakfast is good at the Tick Tock Diner. TIP: Shake Shack on 8th Ave and 43rd St is a good place to eat english-sized meals and delicious yoghurt ices. We did Top of the Rock instead of the Empire State- down side was that there weren't signs to show what many of the buildings were. TIP: Virgils on W44th nr Times Sq serves great southern ribs and burgers and Plataforma Churrascheria on W49th St nr 8th Ave was the best meal we had in 2 weeks if you are a carnivore - don't fill up on the starters though! Don't miss Ellis Island, book online to skip the queue. We also really enjoyed the USS Intrepid and found it all very interesting for about 3-4 hrs. We went on to Boston by train so a short walk to the station was brilliant.

“Outstanding Stay” This was my 5th stay at the Hyatt La Jolla in 2-3 years. This is a great property. It was clearly built as a luxury property and it shows. Rooms are luxurious and in good condition. There are some very popular restaurants across the hotel's courtyard (Flemings Steakhouse, Japengo - great sushi!). I got take-out sushi from Japengo on Tuesday night and the place was packed! The hotel staff is very accommodating. The health club next door is fabulous! They are going to be renovating parts of the health club soon to make it even better. Great Jacuzzi, steam and sauna in the men's locker area. I always look forward to staying at this Hyatt.

“Convenient but avearge” The first room we had had a great view, but the handicap shower was awful, so we got another room. Good response from management, but no king bed available so had to go to two doubles. Bathroom is barely big enough to bathe in. A water hose has more water pressure than our shower head, very poor shower quality. The hotel amenities smell like men's fragrance so as a female I prefer neutral scents. Bed was comfortable and pillows soft. Room sound quality was good given we are right next to airport. Convenient yes, but would not stay here again unless that is what I am looking for. Lamp shade at bed side is as big as a satellite dish, why? Wish the Hilton family would keep their standards the same.
