“Somewhat disappointing” My wife and I stayed there one night, on the basis of 35K Priority Club points. We had a standard 2 bed room on the ninth floor. It felt smallish, about 240 SF, including bathroom. The furnishings were good. The shower was strange, as the opening was about 5 feet, with a fixed glass panel blocking only about 3 feet, leaving water to get out onto the floor. This was the fourth hotel we have stayed at in this area, to visit family. We considered it "very good", but we expected better. We had mixed emotions.

“Way overdue for renovation” Stayed here twice so far this year, looks like the place hasn't been touched since the 70's. Well they do have flat screen TV's but only analog SD and in the wrong aspect ratio. Also this place is at the top of the list for worst food in a full service marriott concierge lounge!

“It could have been worse” I was returning from Europe on a buisness trip and missed my connecting flight in Philadelphia and had to quickly find a room near the airport. US Air offered a voucher for another hotel near the airport, but I had unfortunately stayed there the last time they cancelled my flight and knew better than to return to that dump. I called the Hilton and got a room right away. Caught the shutle from the airport and it was quite easy. Check in was quick and I was assigned a room on the 8th floor. I was exhausted so the room was comfortable for one night. The room had a few updated items like the bedding and television, and the desk chair. But when I was in the elevator or walked through the hallways it still felt a bit outdatted. Not sure if it was the carpet, the walls or what. The bathroom was "okay" but my tub didn't drain well (a big pet peeve for me). I ordered a bowl of soup from room service and although it tasted pretty good, it looked like it was in the bowl overnight and reheated in a microwave before bringing it up. All that said, after my last experience at another Philly airpot hotel that will remain unnamed, the Hilton is a prize. If ever in a similar situation when passing through, I'll choose the Hilton again.

“It's an intercontinental, how can you go wrong?” My girlfriend and I stayed here for 2 nights in August. The hotel is located in a pretty nice part of town, however you are in pretty close proximity to some setchy areas. It is easy to walk to the big famous square (name escapes me right now) and there is easy access to all the main amenities of San Fran. The hotel is apparently a very historic hotel, and you can tell by the architecture. The lobby is nothing special, but the rooms are large and elegant. Our room was not in the best location (2nd floor right above the main entrance) but everything worked out okay. Asked front desk about moving but they were fully booked. Oh well. Overall the Intercontinental lived up to its name. The staff were friendly/knowledgeable, and always recommended great restaurants. We got a nice room for $135/night, so it was superb value. I would say anything under $180 would be of good value for this place. *Please note: parking will cost you an arm and a leg and there is no restaurant in the hotel.

“W done right” W hotels are meant for young travelers looking for a trendy scene and hotels furnished with modern/hip amenities. This hotel had that covered. The location is great if you want to be in Hollywood and if you're staying here I strongly recommend going to Katsuya nearby for dinner. The gym on the 11th floor was well equipped and spotless. The rooms were great and beds were fantastic! You know how sometimes you sleep in a hotel bed and wonder 'Wow - this bed is REALLY comfy!'...yep, you get that SAME FEELING here! The only complaint I have is that the front desk is sometimes undermanned and for simple things like getting another key you could be waiting in line for longer than you like.

“Solid hotel and good value” My business was with Seaworld, so this hotel is very well located. I have stayed here several times before and always left with the sense that this is a very nice property...especially for the price. My only issue was that when my neighbors ran their showers it transferred to my room very loudly. Fortrunately, this was early in the evening and did not prevent me from getting a good night's rest. There is reasonale shopping and food close, and the hotel is just off the intersection of the 5 and 8 freeways making it convenient to most of the San Diego area

“値段の割りにサービスがよい空港ホテル” 深夜11時半に到着。翌日早朝出発なので空港に近いホテルでここを選んだ。料金自体もあまり高くないが、貯まったポイントで支払えるのでそれを使った。あいにく日付変更の解釈の違いで1日間違った予約であったので初めは満室と断られてしまったが、フロントに掛け合った結果機転の利く担当者のおかげで宿泊できた。こうした無理が利くのもポイント会員の利点だと感じる。ホリデイインとしては室内の整備がすこぶる良く、またWIFI無料サービスやシティーホテル並みのレベルの朝食ビュッフェなど値段の割りにサービスがよい空港ホテルだった。航空会社スタッフが多いことでも納得した。ただ低層のつくりで部屋の位置によっては相当館内を歩かされる。

“The most disgusting and scariest place you will ever stay” Seriously, just stay away. This is kind of in a bad area, but that is nothing compared to the rooms and the staff. The front desk staff is so rude and obnoxious. The room we stayed in smelled like cat pee and throw up! Don't even think of complaining, the staff doesn't care and will tell you to go somewhere else if you don't like it. Several complaints and letters to the owner went unanswered. I filed with the Better Business Bureau, but the owners failed to reply to that s well.

“Fabulous....I love this place ... it's perfect!” I stayed here in late July. I love this hotel. There's not much more that can be said about it. The street is a bit sketchy coming from 8th but with four brand new hotels in a row it felt safe with lots of tourists and activity travelling up and down the street. There's also a shortcut door out of Port Authority right across from the Four Points if you are coming out of the subway. I flew into Newark which was perfect because the airport shuttle stops first at Port Authority inbound and pickups last outbound at Port Authority Bus Terminal. Steps from the hotel entrance. I arrived super early and was perfectly willing to store my luggage but they let me check in at 10am without any hesitation. I got a a room on the 8th floor and was very happy with it. Sure it would be nice to have been higher but I didn't ask. In my room was a welcome letter and an organic brownie (maybe this is because I'm a Choice member not sure). Nice treat to arrive to! The room was small as to be expected in New York but everything was well laid out and the bathroom (shower only) was quite roomy. Free Internet, beautiful furnishings, a mounted 32" LCD TV and turndown with chocolates and newspaper. My room was cleaned everytime I returned to the room and the windows and doors seem quite soundproof as I barely heard a thing during my stay there. The morning coffee and afternoon iced tea is well appreciated and the coffee was really good. It's conveniently situated for exploring all areas of New York via walking/public transit with most lines having quick access at Port Authority/Times Square. I did not eat breakfast in the hotel but highly recommend Westway Diner (I think that was it's name) up on 9th street. Avoid the restaurants on 8th street and head west instead to 9th. Staff were friendly and greeted me always - I felt recognized! Elevators with good security - you must use your room card to access the elevator. I will definitely stay here again for my future New York trip hotels. The wonderful reviews are to be believed.

“Ok, not special” I pricelined this for $40 and it is a good value for that price. Nothing out of the ordinary with this property. It's clean and well maintained though its a little on the older side. There are plenty of restuarants nearby all within walking distance is necessary. I should have eaten at one of those nearby places, but because it was raining/snowing, I just ate at the hotel. Food was below average at best. I got a Ribeye, and for some reason the chef elected to smother it with gravy. There was nothing on the menu about a gravy on the steak. When I eat a steak, I want a steak alone. I ate half of it and just went back to the room. About 9pm, I ordered room service because half a steak did not fill me up. The Club sandwhich was also terrible. I ate half and tossed the rest. The hotel itself was fine, and the front desk was helpful with a fax I needed, but the restuarant sucked so I am dropping this to three stars because I paid for $35 of bad food. Maybe the chef just had an off night, and if he wants to smother a steak in a mushroom gravy he ought to let the customer know in the menu.

“VERY small rooms... overall just OK hotel” I have gone to San Francisco several times in my lifetime and wanted to try a new hotel. After much research we settled on the Argent for its location to the BART station, proximity to Union Square and Chinatown, and some good reviews here on Trip Advisor. We were really questioning why we decided to try something else from the moment we walked in the door. Nobody offered to help us with our bags which seemed odd but whatever. We then made our way over to the check-in counter. There were two people in front of that were waiting in line. They did not appear to be together and both looked quite puzzled. After waiting 10 minutes with nobody at the front counter to help us, I fear that we had the same puzzled looks on our faces. I finally asked them how long they had been waiting... 1 said about 10 more minutes than we had and the other simply said too long. My boyfriend then took a tour of the rather small lobby area to see if anyone was working that evening after no offer on the bags and a empty counter at check in. He found someone who must have made a call because only then did someone come out of the little office adjacent to the check in counter. He looked as if we had woke him up from a nap. We finally were helped after a 30 minute wait and the gentleman that checked us in was quite nice but still looked a little groggy. On to the room! We thought... THIS HAS TO GET BETTER. Well, not so much it turns out. The room was very small and very outdated. We were in 3224 which did offer a decent view but that is the only plus to this room. I completely agree with the other reviewer that said it was possible to change the channel with your toes from bed as it was that small. It is worth noting that we were in what was considered to be an "upgrade" room which is the deluxe. They have three categories standard, superior, and deluxe before getting into the suite category. So the deluxe was the best of the standard so to speak. I would have hated to see the other rooms. In closing, the only pleasant experience we had was with the doorman on our way out on the town two times. He was very nice. Who knows where he was the night we came in. There are far better hotels in SF for the price of this one. We will NOT be returning to the Argent. Thank goodness there are many choices so as not to be stuck with a sub standard hotel.

“Newly Renovated” This is not a glamorous hotel but the rooms have been very nicely renovated. The room decor is upscale and sophisticated. The hotel is about 5-10 minutes from the airport. Very nice lobby lounge. Bathrooms have granite countertops and curved shower rods a’ la Westin's Heavenly Bath. High speed wireless in the guest rooms is free. One side of the hotel has a direct view of the end of the main runway...as a result, you are in the flight path which can be interesting if you like planes. Due to the renovation, this is a great hotel.

“Incompetent Staff, Questionable Billing” Oh my, where do I start? What a horrible experience. So, I guess we'll just start with the most senior staff member I had the misfortune of dealing with, Londa. This woman wouldn't know customer service if it walked up and shook her hand. Lied to me about not being able to reverse charges at the hotel (this was confirmed by a call to IC Hotels Customer Relations), lied to me about her role at the hotel, condescending and rude. Treated me like a child who never travels and doesn't know how to make a reservation (I stay in hotels at least 3 nights a week for work). Dear Londa, calling a customer a liar is probably a bad idea. After my first call to Customer Relations I was assured that the GM of the hotel would be contacting me and my billing issue would be resolved before I ever checked out. It's 3 days later, I'm checked out, and I still haven't heard anything. Now, about that check out. The woman at the counter was unable to even give me receipt (something I need to be able to do my expense report for my company). She told me that I'd have to call when the manager was in on Monday to get it. They have a pool, but it was out of service the whole time we were there. Sleep quality was poor because of the noise. When I called the front desk about the noise, she told me I should go knock on their door. One night the TV in the room next to me blaring until I finally called and asked him to turn it down at 4 in the morning. The other nights it was the room above me apparently moving furniture or hosting WWF event. Silverware in the room looks like it was purchased in the bargain bin at a garage sale. The rooms were pretty clean and the gentlemen working a couple of days at the front desk was really friendly. Run away. Very quickly.

“Lots of freebies” I stayed at this hotel with colleagues for a conference and my boss booked three rooms for five people on hotwire for something like $90/room/night. Considering the going rate was about three times that amount, we got a very good deal. We were pleasantly surprised when the rooms did not have glass walls around the bathroom. All three of our rooms were king beds for five colleagues, so sharing beds was enough for us. I agree with many of the other reviews about the service, noise, rooms, etc. One thing that is very impressive is the amount of things that are "complimentary." There are two computers in the lobby for you to check email and there is free wireless throughout the property. They have a happy hour with wine from 5pm to 6pm. There is coffee and pastries in the morning. About half of the things in the minibar in the room are complimentary including water, juice, candy, and snacks. The minibar even has an erotic kit thing. I can only imagine what is in it. The toiletries in the bathroom were excellent and there were lots of little packets of creams and lotions that smelled really nice. Of course the only drawback was the noise from the club downstairs. The rooftop party space was closed because of the rain. Since we hotwired the rooms we were given low, third floor inside rooms all around the small atrium that opens to the club. I had ear plugs in and the music was still loud. I didn't fall asleep until the music stopped around 2:00am I think. I certainly wouldn't pay the going rate to stay at this place again and if I did I would make sure that it was indeed a quiet room. If you have a car, be prepared to pay $30/day for valet. There is no self-parking.

“A good nights sleep for a good price” I stay here once a month for business, The price is good, the rooms are clean and considering the planes fly right overhead you do not hear them. It is a busy hotel, nad could do with some renovating.

“Too hip for its own good” This is an unremarkable hotel that attempts to be more that it is. The front desk seems totally indifferent and overall the hotel seems to be understaffed, especially in the food and beverage area. Rooms are nice and comfortable but nothing over the top, espeically given the price. Public areas are strangely design and not very welcoming. On the plus side was a well equiped gym and a nice lounge for high level rewards members. The hotel did some annoying things like blocking out close parking for a group that never seemed to use it. There are many food options close by along with shopping.

“Convenient and touristy” I was in NY for only 2 nights and was planning to watch a broadway show so a hotel in Time Square made sense. Checking in was functional but chilly. The lobby is neat but small, with a convenient ATM and free apples (in vogue these days). The room was slightly larger by NY standards, and had a flat screen tv thankfully. But I still don't like the bathtub shower and lack of bottled water so prevalent in American hotels. However, in room internet was nicely complimentary. Convenient to Rite Aid next door and very close to Time square, good for tourists.

“A curious reasonably pleasant surprise in Korea town” This is a surprising hotel. Not as good as their rating but not as bad as I thought it would be. The place is very clean but reminds me of the hotels in small city centers in europe. The rooms are very small but the toiletries were nice as was the help. The hotel is located in an interesting part of Manhattan that is overwhelmingly Korean. Needless to say try the Korean restaurants espeically their barbecue. Also there are good japanese and Thai as well. I was there when NYC was having a mini heat wave the ac was not really equal to the task but it is really an ok hotel

“Very nice hotel, excellent location” I stayed at this hotel with a friend last month and had a very enjoyable stay. The Magnolia is well placed for those visiting downtown Houston, which is within easy walking distance. Public transport is also nearby and there is a hotel shuttle which comes in handy for further afield. Our bedroom was nicely decorated. Wifi access was free with good speed too. The complimentary breakfast each morning was very good. The only slight quibble was that the hotel staff seemed to think that everyone drinks coffee and I had to go looking for teabags almost every morning. Milk and cookies each night was very welcome at the end of a long day.

“Pleasant stay overall....” This hotel had its grand opening on December 4th 2008 and without any reviews posted, I really wasn't sure what to expect outside of previous starwood experiences. The staff from registration, valet parking, and bar/restaurant were all very friendly and helpful. While there are plenty of self parking lots in the vicinity, the valet parking fees were reasonable (call ahead to verify the price), for the area since in/out service was available. While there is a no stopping at anytime sign in front of the hotel entrance, supposedly hotel guests are able to stop their car in front and unload while the front desk calls for valet to park your car (supposedly there is some unspoken agreement between hotel and police authority). I was using GPS to navigate to the 1201 race street address, which gets me to the other side of corner of the hotel on a one way street so using the alternate address on the other side would be better for valet parking drop off unless this was just my GPS unit. The location is very good, about 1 block from the convention center, reading terminal, and the heart of chinatown's race street. I did not see the negative aspects loitering in front of the hotel mentioned in reviews of other hotels. Perhaps it was too cold, or somehow being just a block away was enough of a difference to make the area more pleasant. There are 2 internet stations in the lobby with a printer, and free wired/wireless access in the rooms. The rooms were all obviously clean with the 4pts standard amenties and appearance which is fine for most people. No refrigerator in room, but w/coffee machine and ironing. I suppose this is basically a business hotel for the most part during the week. Of note: I believe the bedding available is 1 king or 2 doubles eventhough the website description shows 1 king or 1 double at SPG as of new years. Also, the features and amenities showed a picture of water with description of "pool" underneath. There is no pool in the hotel and management was contacted to correct this egregious error. While this was inconvenient during my 2 night stay with 2 kids expecting a swimming pool, I was given a very minor pittace by the GM. This hotel in my estimation is only a Category 3 property by starwood standards, though perhaps the extra star is justifiable due to the convenient location in downtown Philly. Platinum amenity of 250pts per stay or free movie, etc. was offered upon check-in. Don't believe there are any real upgrades to be expected.

“One of the top 3 hotels in Chicago.” Rooms are very cool, like most other W Hotels. It has awesome views of Lake Michigan and the city from the rooms and from the bar at the top of the hotel. I actually can't remember if it was at the top of the hotel or close to the top. :( That reminds me, the drinks are very good. Very nice staff. But everybody in Chicago is nice anyway.

“Wouldn't go back” We had such a negative experience at the Radission Austin that by the end of the weekend we started to ignore further problems. Advertisements for this hotel promise a "Sleep Number" bed and a view of the lake or the city. After checking in we learned that the Sleep Number beds are only available on a limited number of floors (less than half) in the hotel. Because the hotel was full with weekend events, no switch would be possible. Additionally, our room looked out on a dirty rooftop with a piecemeal view of the lake - between parked cars in the adjacent parking structure. So we kept the drapes pulled for most of the weekend. Despite leaving the room for several hours during the day on Saturday, our room was never cleaned during our stay - so Sunday morning we were still looking at wine glasses from Friday night. The front desk promised to bring some amenities right away that we'd forgotten and called about - 45 minutes later, we had to come up with another solution or risk missing the event we were in town for. Overall, for the price that we paid and the service we expected from a hotel chain of the class that the Radisson likes to advertise, we were severely disappointed and would reconsider booking at another hotel chain in other cities, much less in Austin again. It might have a good location, but so do several other hotels.

“Great deal for a weekend getaway to NYC” Great room, great service, great location near the subway. Only negative point: hotel restaurant wasn't open for dinner, and the breakfast buffet was sparse. But there are plenty of restaurant and diners in the area.

“Nice Play-Would Stay Again” I stayed here during a business trip. This was a wonderful hotel. They provide: Continental Breakfast (There was no belgian waffles) and Happy Hour -3 drinks "FREE" per day (There was a specific drink list) with Nachos/Pretzels/Chips. The Cust. Ser. Reps were always friendly and the hotel seem to be kept pretty neat. The beds are nice. The only thing I noticed was the cleaning crew "Never" put the iron & board back up once it's taken out and set up. You can access the Riverwalk from the lower portion of the hotel. The Pool is located (2 levels) above the roof. Yes, you read correctly. You go onto the roof, then have to walk up a set of stairs to access the jacuzzi and then another set of stairs to access the pool. The roof top pool is not a place for kids to be left alone. A parent should always be there for safety reasons. If you stay at the hotel, you will see exactly what I mean. Enjoy your stay. I would definitely stay at this hotel again if the situation presented itself.

“cheap for reasons” Sheraton LA Downtown is a strange place for its highs and lows. Rooms are spacious and nicely appointed as other posters have stated, but are not well-kept. Room service is very prompt, and surprisingly so is valet parking car retrieval (usually a pet peeve). Room service food is good, too, but remarkable for the added charges, which almost double the cost of anything you order. This becomes a bit more problematic in that there is no restaurant in the hotel (!), so for those times you don't want to go out, room service is all there is. Housekeeping is very sloppy, which could account for the stained rugs throughout, but we noted that crumbs dropped the first night remained at the end of our three night stay. This is the kind of place that, because most rooms are high up, people go close to the windows to look out at the city (no great views to speak of), leave hand and nose prints on the windows, and nobody cleans them off for weeks at a time. Even the office center was in total disrepair, with no machines functioning at all. One other issue is that the place seems to be on or near one or both of LAX's flight approaches, so about every 30 seconds or so, a jet passes over, with the accompanying roar and echo all night long. For the price, i would only stay there again if attending a meeting in the same building, for convenience sake. But since LA has virtually thousands of hotels, many of them very good to great, and comparably priced if you look hard enough, i would definitely stay elsewhere next time. I will not recommend this place to anyone i like.

“Best price for location” This is a very good choice for midtown Manhattan if you want to be within walking distance to the main attraction sites and close to the subway stops. It is a new hotel, smallish rooms, good prices. Breakfast is included, which is good since other hotels charge up to $30.00 per person; however, the quality of breakfast is so and so (coffee and omelettes should be avoided, they were really not good). Our room was clean, no view, bathroom small but OK, with good hot water. Overall it is probably the best price/quality hotel in midtown Manhattan, just do not expect 5-star service. One small annoying thing on the bell service: when you try to get a cab, they will sway you towards private limos, which are more expensive. Ask for a yellow cab, instead, even if they may not be too happy about it, or just use the subway to go anywhere very cheaply.

“Good Location, Property and Service (Especially Housekeeping)” I recently stayed at the Park Hyatt Washington for four nights for a combination work/personal visit. The location of the hotel is great and close to the downtown, restaurants, museums and nightlife. The hotel grounds are well kept and very clean. I stayed in a suite which was spacious, clean and had a modern decor. The bed was extremely comfortable. The hotel gym is large by hotel standards and has adequate equipment for a good workout. One downside to the physical attributes of the property was that the internet service was spotty at best--both wifi and ethernet. This was problematic because my internet connection kept dropping while I was attending work-related webcasts. Another downside is the noise. Because most buildings don't exceed a certain height in the District, the rooms are relatively close to street level and all of the traffic noise. I believe this is a common problem with District hotels, especially if you are a light sleeper. The hotel restaurant--the Blue Duck Tavern--seems to get rave reviews. I ate there a few times during my stay and it was good, but a bit overhyped. As for the service, it was good and met my expectations for a Park Hyatt. The doormen and front desk staff were attentive and friendly. Everyone was quick to acknowledge and recognize my Diamond status and the perqs that go with it. The Diamond breakfast was great and generous. The only criticism I had with respect to the breakfast is that management should let Diamond members enjoy it wherever they want--whether it's in the restaurant or brought to their room. On some of the days I was able to get my breakfast delivered to my room, but the staff made such a big deal about this and they seemed to have to jump through so many hoops to make this happen. As the Hyatt's top guests, management should let us enjoy our perqs wherever we like as some other high-end Hyatt properties do. In my opinion the highest marks go to housekeeping--they bent over backwards to cater to my needs and did a great job of keeping my room and the property in great shape. Few people realize the critical role that housekeeping plays and I hope that management will reward the housekeeping staff for doing their job consistently well. I'll be back.

“Great choice for Medical Center area” If you are doing business in the Medical center or there as a patient or relative with a patient, this is a great place to stay. Patient rate are available and there is a free shuttle to all the medical facilities in the area. Highly recommend.

“Inconsistent” The Homewood Suites is located on the quieter side of the Riverwalk, but still an easy and pleasant walk to where the action is. We stayed here for two nights to visit San Antonio. We were originally given 1 bedroom suite with two double beds, which was very dark (only one small window in the bedroom only). We found it kind of depressing and went back to check-in to cancel the reservation. The manager offered to move us to a brighter suite, which turned out to be a spacious 2-queen 1 bedroom corner suite on a high floor. Service was OK - staff moved us to a nicer suite although they didn't have to. But valet parking was aggressive and pressured us to go away when we unloaded the car because we wanted to self park. Valet parking is $20/night or self parking just opposite the hotel is $13/24 hours with no in/out. Complimentary breakfast was good and so was the evening light meal - but you need to be there early! On one day there wasn't enough tables and food for everyone. The dining area in the lobby is very nice with floor to ceiling views of the Riverwalk. The 2-queen suite we ended up staying in was pleasant and gave a real sense of space. Beds were comfortable and the living area was equipped with a small dining table, large sofa-bed, fridge, microwave oven and dishwasher. The dishwasher and fridge were very loud, which could make it difficult to sleep on the sofa bed. This hotel is showing its age and feels very basic, but I suppose that's what you get in a Homewood. The building was originally a pharmaceutical factory and was not designed to be a hotel. I would warn people booking here that a large number of suites (presumably the 2 double beds ones) do not have windows in the living area. Avoid these and the Homewood is probably a good choice if you want space and like to save on food or prepare your own.

“Highly recommended” This is a clean, comfortable, safe and quiet hotel in the heart of Times Square. Our rooms (standard double bed rooms) were spacious and had fantastic beds. Our northside room had a great view of the midtown area, and the southside room had an awesome view of the Empire State Building. Bathrooms were very nice -- excellent water pressure and hot water availability. NYC was 90 degrees during our stay. The A/C worked well in each room, but we wished they had been slightly more powerful. The rooms never got warm, but never got as cool as we wanted. All elevators are very fast -- I don't believe we ever waited more than 10 seconds for an elevator. Very convenient subway access. Internet service was very good, and cost $10 per day. The breakfast buffet was $19 per day. The buffet could have had a better selection, but the available items were all very good. As other reviewers have mentioned, Dallas BBQ across the street is a great place to stop for large portions at very low prices. The staff was exceptional. We stopped by the front desk often to inquire about luggage that our airline had lost. The staff was always patient, friendly and helpful. We asked for a late checkout, and were immediately offered to stay until 2:00. I can't say enough about how impressed we were with the service. I very highly recommend the Hilton Times Square.

“Great service, Bad Room” The staff at the Sheraton bend over to take care of you in every way. I was very impressed with how well I was cared for. The staff were perfect in every way. However, there are two towers that make up this hotel. DO NOT stay in the tower that is accross the street from the main lobby. The rooms were so very small, and the bathrooms were even smaller and outdated.

“Very satisfied” The hotel itself is wonderful in appearance, in cleanliness and in decor. It is centrally located in Back Bay, connected to Copley Square mall, which is connected to the Prudential Center and is easily in walking distance to Downtown Crossing, Fenway, Fanueil Hall, Waterfront, South End, etc. The hotel lobby is very posh, and Bar 10 has the best martinis I have ever tasted, no matter how overpriced they are, they were worth it. The room itself was a good size, the bathrooms a little small, but still acceptable with granite countertops and typical Westin toiletries. The heavenly bed, mini bar, tv, etc was key and the view from the 29th floor was wonderful. Parking expensive $40/day, and doors to room shook a little bit when other doors down the hall would slam shut. The walls werent as thin as we were expecting, so it was all good. The staff was VERY accommodating, didnt seem to care we were Priceline customers. I would definitely book again. For sure.

“Great!!!! Loved It” This hotel was wonderful!!! location is the best for time square, staff cant be more helpful and bedding is outstandingly comfortable Rooms are very small, so i wouldn't recommended it if you're traveling with s lot of luggage (really, you wont fit!)... Breakfast is pretty poor, but enough to start the day and don't go out on an empty stomach. I really liked it this place and would go again and recommend it any time! I think they should get a little more diversity for breakfast, besides that, a big 10!

“Barely average” This hotel is extremely convenient for me when I go to Philadelphia on business, but due to so many different problems I simply cannot stay there any longer. I'd try, Four Seasons, Sofitel, Marriott, Westin. I've stayed at al of them plus a few others and they rate much better than Wyndham. For some reason they just can't seem to get it together here.

“Just the Greatest Time” Stayed her for two nights last week. We were far enough out to be over the ocean most of the time. If you want to experience the true feeling of being over the ocean, ask for a room that is. We were in number 5. I would say the room behind us was also a good location. Behind that ,not so much. Go to Ralph's on the way in a get barbeque. Ask for a grill when you get there. I hated to leave. It is really pricey though.

“blood on the sheets” When I checked in, all seemed in order. When we pulled down the sheets of the bed that night we found blood on the sheets. The people at the desk offered to change our room but the kids were already in their bed. (we looked carefully at theirs too, no problem there.) So I had the housekeeping staff come up to change the bedding. This took nearly an hour. No call from a manager. In the morning as I checked out the staff did not have any idea about what transpired. They offered to take the parking charges off of the bill. No manager came out to discuss this and I received no call from anyone. Not happy, no not at all.

“One of the best comfortable room I have ever experienced” My second stay in Boston was promised to be short but maybe too short for a stay at Ames Hotel. I have really enjoyed this hotel from the warm welcome at the reception to the neutrality and calm atmosphere of the room. First of all, when I arrived, I realized that I messed up with my arrival day and was expected to stay in the hotel only the day after. Because the hotel was fully booked, the 2 receptionists were kind enough to find me a room. After several phone calls, they found the last room at their neighbor 4* hotel. The next day, I couldn't wait to see what my room looked like. What I like about Morgans Hotel is how they choose carefully furniture and the colors of the room. When you enter the room, it kind of gets you relaxed and calm. Neutrality of colour have been carefully chosen. The power shower was a real treat in early mornings of my stay (meaning 4am with the jetlag). Also, I have enjoyed the big TV screen for insomniac like me. I ordered also breakfast which was delivered within 20 min even before the opening of the breakfast service. The breakfast was really good with salmon and scrambled eggs. Also appreciate the fast check out service when my taxi was waiting for me at 6am to go to Boston Airport. Thank you again Ames Hotel, You made my short stay in Boston a great trip.

“Really? Couldn't you have bolted the toilet to the floor?” We got a spanking deal at this hotel for $99 a night. It's in a good location to the Loop. Excellent transportation options abound. My gripe comes from the fact that we were obviously put in a "crappy" room. It overlooked the back of the building and the roof of a building next to us. The toilet in the room was not bolted to the floor. Other than that, if I needed to stay in the Loop again for something and I knew I wasn't going to be put in a undesirable room, I would stay here again.

“A great place to stay and convenient to Downtown!” Went to a meeting at the San Diego Convention Center, unfortunately had to change arrangements and had to stay outside of the Downtown area. Stayed at the Hilton Hotel in Mission Valley, which turned out to be a great choice for me. It is not that far from the Convention Center and trips from the hotel to the convention only took about 15 minutes via freeway, probably 6 miles. It is very convenient to get to via Interstate 8 and hwy 163. There is a mall area across the freeway with many nearby restaurants--Chevy's, Gordon Birsch, Baja Fresh to name a few and several stores--Borders, Target, Nordstrom Rack. Parking not an issue. Room was spacious, bed comfortable and the staff was very accommodating. It was very quiet, I was on the 10 floor. Did not eat in hotel, did not use exercise room or pool. Self parking is convenient, although $14/nite, unlimited in and out. For the price, I was very pleased with the hotel, the distance from Downtown was insignificant and would definitely recommend staying her again!

“The key to enjoying the Marriott East Side is take the time to meet the staff” I just returned from a stay at the Marriott East Side in Manhattan. I am a frequent traveler to New York, and have stayed at many of the most highly reputed and expensive hotels in the City, but if you ask me where I really like to stay it is at the East Side Marriott. Why? because the staff there treat you as if you were a guest in their home, not as if you are just someone paying money to receive a service. My advice, get to know the doormen, who have a wealth of information and are extremely friendly. Talk to the front desk staff, like the extraordinary Paulina, who I saw in action greeting guests, remembering their names, welcoming them to the property, and establishing a bond with the guests. The housekeepers and the room service waiters are also very friendly and accommodating. In spite of the reputation that some service businesses in New York City have of brusque interaction with clients, this hotel is a place where you can feel at home in your enclave very quickly if you take the time to talk with and get to know the excellent staff, most of whom have worked there for years.

“A Modern Hotel.” The Pod is a well located hotel, with modern room with flat panel TV, Ipod dock station and a style bedroom. Its lobby look like a boutique hotel. Very fashionable. It worths the price.

“Excellent location; very nice hotel” It would be hard to go wrong with this hotel. The location is excellent: you are within a 15 minute walk of much of downtown Boston. The rooms are of average size and comfort. It's not a large hotel, so I rarely had to wait for more than 30 seconds for an elevator. The room was average in size and comfortable. The bathroom was also average in size. As far as complaints, they are few: the bed wasn't as comfrotable as I would have liked, but it wasn't too bad. The selection of tv channels wasn't as large as most other hotels. There are no ice machines on the floor, so you have to call for someone to deliver ice. -- These were minor flaws. The staff were very friendly. Overall, I enjoyed my stay in this hotel and would happily stay here again.

“Exceptional Customer Service” We bookended our stay with this Marriott, and the convenience factor was wonderful. Sooo nice to walk right into the hotel from the terminal upon arrival and not have to worry about renting a car 'til the next morning. Also great to return the car the night before departure, because the car return is right there!!! More wonderful than the convenience factor, however, was the friendliness and outstanding customer service of this hotel's employees. It's easy to see that they take pride in their work and go out of their way to make guests feel comfortable. We got a great room at the end of the hall (11th floor) with a fun view of the airplanes taking off and landing ~ kept my 5-year-old mesmerized!! Used the workout facilities and treadmill was operating perfectly. A good variety of machines as well. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel.

“Great Location, Price, and Quality” I stayed 2 nights at this hotel during a weekend trip to Denver. It was a great location which allowed you to walk to most of the stuff on 16th street. While the parking was not free I was advised by the front desk that simply parking across the street by a meeter was in fact totally free on weekends. The hotel was new and had updated rooms with nice tvs. The breakfest space was large enough to accomidate everyone and best of all the price was exceptional given the value. A top notch Hampton Inn.

“Great As Always” This hotel has something about it that everytime I go there I feel at home. Rooms are great, staff even better..... Even though LA isn't my favorite destination, I always look forward to staying at this property. Parking is expensive but then again this is LA so what else would you expect..... DEFINITELY WORTH IT!

“Nice hotel, friendly staff” I have stayed at the M. Energy Corridor many times over the last two years and was never disappointed. The beds are great and I noticed last week how friendly the staff was (helped me with cinema recommendations). It's the best Marriott I have stayed in so far in Houston and has a new feel to it. Highly recommended.

“Solid for an extended stay.” Pleasantly surprised when arrived and stayed for two nights when the nearby JW was booked. Several others in our party were also impressed with the cleanliness, size and value of the location. The only drawback was the location itself. Not much around within walking distance...except for the Mayo Clinic.

“Central location, fine hotel” Just back from a 2 night stay at the Omni. This was my second time staying at the hotel and I plan on staying there again in the future. Rooms are of average size but there are no closets. A wardrobe is provided for you to hang your clothes in. The room and furnishings were in good condition and clean. If you join the select guest program, you have the option of choosing up to 2 beverages (hot or cold) to be delivered to your room in the morning, free of charge. This is a more understated hotel which lacks a grand lobby. If you like the sort of hotel that is designed to "impress" you with sensory overload when you walk in the front door, then this may not be the location for you. The main draw of this hotel for me is the central location. Located on 52nd St at Madison Ave, it is close to many things. It is close to Rockefeller Center, restaurants, shopping and about 2 blocks away from several different subway lines.
“Pleasant Experience” Property is located in a very desirable area of town. Rooms are neat and show no signs of wear. For the location near the Baltimore Harbor, room prices are great.

“Tiny room, but convenient!” I had to stay en extra day in New York last month, and I didn't want to spend a lot of money as I would not be there except to sleep. this hotel is quite fone for that, but would not be good if it was 2 people who had lots of stuff. Like most rooms in Manhattan, it is just a bed and a small bureau in lieu of a closet, and a rack that will fit one suitcase. But it is clean and convenient, and a block from Times Square, the Broadway theatres, 20 minutes walk to central park, close to subways, and the Port Authority bus Terminal. It is right off of restaurant row, so you need not look far for great little restaurants. Staff were friendly and nice. The room and bathroom were clean. The street below was a little noisy due to a window airconditioner being in the window permanently for the summertime, but all in all, I couldn't complain. And for what I needed, it was safe and fine. there is a little help-yourself breakfast in the morning down in the lobby - O.J., coffee/tea, bagels, donuts, croissants, cereal, etc. My room was ready when I checked in at noon, and they were able to let me have a late check out (by 2 hours) when I asked the next day. A great little place for a night or two!

“Location, location..” Beautiful hotel, friendly in a good location. We stayed from 10/15 - 10/18. Too bad the weather were not permit us (with a 9months old baby boy) to walk around. Metro (Red line) is really close. CVS very close also some restaurant because of the rain we didn't eat out. Robert's is ok. Ronald Reagan airport is only 15min drive from the hotel. This hotel is the cheapest valet only $28/night compare with others.

“Great hotel but location not great for walkers” Stayed at this hotel as part of my birthday vacation - location is not the best if you are travelling by method other than car - it's a bit of a walk to the train and especially so in the cold of December. The lobby and rooms were quite elegant - I can't believe how big the room was they gave me! Staff were for the most part okay, excellent in the business center, but had some difficulty trying to connect with a concierge, The only restuarant I saw was a sushi place - not what I'm looking for when I dine out. I don't remember internet access being free so I will say it was not. For $67 a night through Priceline, a good deal.

“Its awful and More like a Motel 6” When I finally got to room I was really disappointed. The Park Hyatt in Chicago is exceptional in every way, and the Park Hyatt in DC is like a Motel 6. Please see my blog at http://talesfromtheroad-mwalno.blogspot.com Let me tell you a story about service....the guy I was traveling with was staying at the Westin DC City Center (1400 M Street NW) and we walked 10 blocks there after our appointment ended in the afternoon (it was really hot and humid). When we arrived we were hot and sweaty (not a pretty sight); one of the girls behind the counter welcomed us with a big smile and asked us to wait for a minute - when she returned she had two cold/wet face towels and 2 bottles of water. She said the weather was terrible and she wanted to do all she could to make us comfortable. My buddy checked in ($205 a night) and I caught a cab to the Park Hyatt. When I arrived, the bellman helped me out and I noticed he had an ear piece in. He asked my name and I told him - I kind of expected him to tell the front desk, but he didn't. I still don't know why they have them. The front desk couldn't find my reservation and it took at least 10 minutes to get checked in - no towel and no water bottle. It is NOT WORTH THE MONEY!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I would stay in that Westin every time in DC without a second thought. Its all about the service, and there is little (if any) at the Park Hyatt. A few of things that I hated - there was a QT storm (Ozone) machine in the room running when I arrived - that is usually a sign that someone smoked in the room - I called the front desk to inquire and was told that is just done to keep the rooms fresh -- I have NEVER had that happen to me in a few hundred nights on the road in the past 2 years---and it ran the entire time I was there. There was definitely a funky smell in the room. Oh, that is just one thing I hated and there are many more: the clock is a cube and its impossible to see the time and doesn't light at night, the shower blows - there is a rain shower and a wall shower and neither has much water pressure, there was NO PAPER on my door in the morning - I saw a black paper bag on other doors (PH Chicago asks which paper you want at check in) and the fitness center elliptical machines all squeaked. The room itself was sub par. There is NO LUXURY HERE. It is a complete waste of money to stay here. And if you are a preferred member of Hyatt's loyalty program you are just another customer rolling through the door. Total - $345 + 49.66 tax + .36 DC Package tax = $395.02 (remember the story about my buddy at the Westin for $200)

“We Couldn't Be Happier With Our Stay!” The Mr. & I stayed in the Affinia from June 24th - July 1st. We couldn't have been happier with our stay. Annie greeted us warmly on our arrival and cheerfully stored our bags when we weren't able to check in right away. This set the tone for what was to be a wonderful stay. We were thrilled with our corner room on the 21st floor (room 2103)! We appreciated the 'split level' arrangement of the room. The closet, bathroom, and bar area were on the top level with the bed and dresser on the lower level. The bed was extremely comfortable and as I'm a night time reader I loved the reading lamps that were attached to the headboard on both sides. The hotel is well located for sight seeing, shopping and eating, but if walking isn't your thing, the Affinia was just minutes from a Red Line or a bus stop. If you plan to eat at Gino's East, don't forget to ask the front desk for 'priority passes' which allows you to skip the more than likely long line waiting for a table. In addition to Annie, I must brag on all the staff particularly Peter who was helpful when we wanted to book a Chicago Architecture Tour and the super friendly front door staff. We always got a nice greeting whenever we left or came back. If we make it back to Chicago, we will definitely book the Affinia again. It was a delightful home away from home!

“Loved This Hotel” Daughter, Grandaughter, Daughter's Mother-in-Law and I spent the night here in celebration of our birthdays. The hotel is in a great location, very close to and within walking distance to Time Square, the theater district and subway. It is a lovely hotel with an attentive staff ready to help you in any way they can, be it delivering ice, storing luggage or getting a taxi, The room was clean and though not large, easily accomodated the 4 of us. Others have remarked about having to walk past some "not too desirable" establishments.......we were 3 women + an 8 yr. old and never felt uncomfortable on our way back to the hotel. Windows of these establishments were covered so there was no concern about the 8 yr. old being exposed to questionable activities. Hot coffee was available in the lobby in the mornings then switched over to hot cider in the afternoons. This was great for those of us who have to have their coffee first thing + a warm pick me up after a cool day of shopping. There is also a computer station in the lobby. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and I hope to visit again.

“Easy access” I enjoy staying here when I have early flights. Service is good, clean, easy in and out, imcludimg separate parking access. Club lounge a bit small, but friendly and boarding pass printing available. Not sure why previous writer complained about getting to united in terminal d, I use united all the time. You can access terminal b security directly from hotel and once inside access all terminals easily. You can also use the c garage access ramp and connect to c security. Anyway, good place, one of the few positives at Philly intl!

“Comfortable, clean and great location” I stayed at the Vintage Park for a week while on business in Seattle. My flight got in early and they were able to accomodate me, but in a very small room. Being that I was going to be there for so long, I asked if I could be moved to a bigger room, which they did without hesitation. Needless to say, the staff was extremely friendly and accomodating. The location of the hotel is great - across from the public library and within a few blocks of central shopping areas, and the public market. Their restaurant, Tulio was also very good.

“Great Location, nothing but tourists” 33% of San Francisco revenue, according to our cabbie, is generated by the hospitality industry. I selected this hotel because it was in Fisherman's Wharf and every one of those tourist dollars were lined up waiting for cable cars, streetcars, traffic lights, etc. SFO has turned into a Disneyland operation where people wander around lining up to spend money. Every sidewalk shop in Fisherman's wharf was selling cheap SF logoed jackets for $20 and the tourists were identifying themselves by buying for each member of their party. So while it would seem that this was an excellent hotel location, it was at ground zero for tourist density. Next time, I'll look for an inn closer to everyday San Francisco living rather than the Disney-esq processing at the wharf. That said, the hotel was fine. Recently rennovated, it feels fresh and clean and the staff is very attentive and responsive. There was no street noise, although the room above held a jumping person that was annoying. The MAJOR complaint among guests is that WiFi in the room is not free, it costs $15 per day. The hotel offers free WiFi in the lobby which creates a buzz in the lobby, which was perhaps the intent. It's just odd to stay at low end hotels with free WiFi and then encounter charges at an upscale property. The other cost was $43 per day for parking - we returned our car before checking in because SFO is one of those towns where a car is really unnecessary. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone who was visiting for the first time, but the real San Francisco is a mile or so back from the water line - and I'm sure it's still charming...

“Great stay. Da price cannot be beat!” Stayed here in December. It's an historic building that reminded me of days of yore. The amenities are limited, vending machine downstairs, but what do you expect for such a bargain price. It's centrally located so most of the "touristy" attractions are within a short driving distance. Staff was extremely friendly. No elevators so travel light. Kinda reminded me of an upper scale "youth hostel." Parking is plentiful and free. The only downside would be that it's not in the best of neighborhoods so I don't recommend this hotel for families that are using public transportation. If you have a car, no problemo. Will definitely stay here again.....

“Schon etwas älter, aber sauber.” Das Hampton Inn Philadelphia International Airport lag für uns ideal. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und die Zimmer ok. Wir wünschten ein Zimmer im obersten Stockwerk und bekamen dieses auch sofort. DAs Hotel ist schon ein bisschen älter und die Möbel und Teppiche könnten erneuert werden. Unser Zimmer war sauber und es gab keinen Grund zur Klage. Das Frühstück entsprach den anderen Hampton Inn Hotels und für uns vollkommen ausreichend.

“Gutes Boutiquehotel an Toplage” Grandiose Lage zwischen 5th und 6th Avenue - Die Zimmer sind für Amerikanische Verhältnisse auf einem hohen qualitätsniveau und nur deshalb kommt die gute Architektur auch zur Geltung. Bar und Lobby sind nicht riesig, aber durchaus gemütlich und angenehm zum verweilen. Eines meiner 3 - 4 lieblings Designhotels in Manhattan - Vorausgesetzt man möchte in Midtown hausen.

“Monstrously comfortable hotel” Most comfortable beds I have found in Downtown Houston - rooms and hotel monstrously large - bar, 2 x restaurants, Starbucks + very handy convenience store (which seems to stock anything for all eventualities) all on ground floor. 26th floor pool / jacuzzi and outside terrace lovely.

“Great location, spacious rooms, and excellent customer service” I wanted to start off by saying that the Back Bay Hilton treats Price Line customers the same as full paying customers. Many hotels treat price line and hot-wire customers like second class citizens assigning the smallest rooms with the least amenities. Not the Hilton. Upon check in (They let us check in at 9:00am) we were treated like royalty. The bellhop, front desk staff and concierge all provided excellent customer service. We were assigned a high floor with a fabulous view. The spacious room was clean, linens were high quality, and the bathroom was spotless. (also there were no bedbugs!!) The concierge was very gracious with her time spent with us planning our Boston itinerary and recommending restaurants in the area. Housekeeping did an excellent job keeping our room spotless. I agree with the other reviewers in regards to parking and internet prices being high. However, I have found this to be true in most upper tier hotels I've stayed at. I know that I might get free internet and breakfast at the holiday inn but by doing so I give up other amenities that are important to me in a quality hotel such as the Back Bay Hilton. Overall, highly recommended..

“Not a shining star in Chicago” The concept is great but this hotel had awful beds, postage stamp size pillows, I asked for a duvet and was handed a ratty old blanket, the breakfast was minimal at best, not enough newspapers for guests staying at the hotel and finally.. a call to a taxi company outside 312 area code for 2 mins was a whopping $5.00. I'd take a pass on this hotel as usually a five star can be had for same amount 300. per night elsewhere

“Wonderful getaway” I've stayed here before, so i knew what i was getting. It's a bit of a walk to Times Square but, i don't mind. NY is a walking city and if you have issues with walking, then this is not your kind of town. This time i was with my mother, a little weekend getaway filled with lots of theater. I liked having a little walk after sitting in the theater for so long. After a very rough start, patiently waiting for my room, i had taken an over night flight and well, the room wasn't ready, but i was more than thrilled!! We were on the 14th floor in a Hudson Suite!! Fabulous views of the cruise ships and the Hudson River. Lots of room for my mom and i to relax and spread out!! The regular rooms here are also very large for NY standards. Had breakfast twice in the hotel and one dinner, all very good. The chocolate bread is fabulous!! Had a drink at the roof top bar, this is a must, the view is spectacular!! The rough start was soon forgotten and a wonderful weekend was thoroughly enjoyed!!

“Strictly for business” This hotel is located 13 miles from downtown Denver in a hi-tech business park. It is surrounded by other large chain hotels, franchise restaurants, parking garages, office buildings and empty lots waiting to be filled with more of the same. If you have business in the area, it's a great location. If you there strictly as a tourist who wants to see Denver, keep looking. You can do a lot better either right in the city or much closer. A cab ride into town is going to cost you anywhere from $25 to $40 depending on which part of the city you're going to. The good news is that it's a 15-minute walk to the nearest light rail station, although I was warned about walking there alone or at night. I believe, however, the hotel has a shuttle. The restaurant was surprisingly good for a chain hotel and the wait staff were very attentive, if a little slow. The hotel itself is no great shakes -- just a large, 12-story high rise. In short, if you're wearing a suit and doing business in the area this is fine. If you're in shorts and looking for a day at Coors Field or Invesco Field, you can do a lot better and for not much more money.

“Very quick ride to the airport” My father and I stayed at the Hampton Inn Austin-Airport on Christmas night. Our rental car was not available as planned, so it was lucky the hotel was nearby. On Christmas night, the shuttle service ended earlier than normal, so we did have to take a taxi there, but got back to the airport the next morning through the shuttle. The front desk staff was friendly, the room was clean, and the wireless internet worked well. I would recommend staying there if you are arriving late or leaving early.

“Stylish with good value for money” The hotel is situated in a quiet area, near the Childrens & Music museum. It is very stylish with large rooms and a small pool/gym. Free parking great Make sure you ask for a room away from the elevator though as ours was next to it and all I could hear was a loud 'biiiiing' whilst I was trying to sleep!

“Not bad, but you can do better in Houston” I stayed at the Houstonian because of some of the favorable reviews on this site and its setting on wooded acreage in town, assuming it would be an elegant hotel in a beautiful location. I must say I was somewhat disappointed. You definitely aren't on the freeway or anything (like a lot of the Houston hotels, such as the Intercontinental), but the setting isn't all that memorable, either. There's a reason you can't find one exterior photo of the hotel on any website. It looks like a four-story high 70s all-glass office building set on an awkward angle very close to other similar vintage office buildings. That would be okay, but it's laid out oddly on the small piece of land it takes up. Half the rooms have views of the parking garage (unforgiveable, really), which is less than 50 feet away from most rooms. The other half look into another office building. There are trees everywhere, but once the leaves come out this spring, you will be looking into foliage and nothing but. Not to say that looking into other office buildings this time of year is all that attractive. The windows are floor to ceiling and the width of the rooms (which aren't very wide), but the whole feeling is vaguely claustrophobic. And I stayed on the top floor. The rooms are nicely appointed with very good beds, although the carpet was stained by the door. And, as others have mentioned, the bathrooms are ridiculously small. I mean, insanely so. Motel 6 bathrooms are larger. They are nicely appointed with some marble tile, but you just can't believe how tiny they are. If the rooms had been better designed, there is entry space that could have been alloted to make them normal-sized at the very least. At these prices, the bathrooms should be better. The club lounge was very well-stocked and nicely designed, with a roaring fire going all day in the fireplace. The staff there was exceedingly friendly, and you get free internet access and printing. A classy touch. The concierge I had (a young woman) was one of the least informed individuals I have met in her profession. When I asked about dining at a restaurant that would be unique to Houston, she recommended "McCormick & Schmicks," a national chain based in Seattle. She also made vaguely rude comments about how I was not suitably dressed for dinner in a nicer establishment in her city. I ended up dining at Brennan's, (I found out about it myself and called them directly), a very nice local restaurant and got a great table, dressed exactly the same way I was at the hotel. So my experience with her snobby attitude and lack of knowledge was quite the waste of time, not to mention off-putting. Next day, I checked out the pool area. Very large. Sort of like a 70s resort pool. No staff in attendance. Had to walk quite a ways to get a towel. A Mom with three annoying children descended on the hot tub as soon as I got there. Had to save her youngest from drowning as she was not paying attention. Location is very convenient to the nicer areas of Houston and good shopping. The walk from self-parking to the hotel is extremely confusing, as others have stated, and I got lost several times. All in all, they treated me quite well. But this place feels like it's hanging on to former glory. Everything is well-maintained, but it just doesn't feel like a real four-star hotel. The decor is "Western" in the lobby, but the rooms and narrow hallways are really nondescript. All in all, not bad. But I doubt if I would return when back in Houston. It felt claustrophobic, dark, and past its prime.

“Clean and modern” When we arrived we were greeted by a very helpful gentleman who helped us check in. The hotel design is very impressive and I loved the contemporary look. Our room was quite small but very clean and I liked the moveable bed quite a quirky feature. The toilet/shower room is separated from the room by a glass partition and curtain so not an awful lot of privacy but we didn't find it a problem. On each floor there is a galley kitchen with free coffee machine (and the coffee was good!), fridge and microwave. The light breakfast was a nice touch, just muffins and coffee/tea but was great for us. Downsides: was difficult to get the lift in the mornings as they were all so busy! Breakfast was pretty crammed and had to push your way through to get a muffin! All in all a good hotel. The rooftop bar was definitely my favourite part, don't miss it. The guests seemed like a good crowd too.

“Better Every Year” I've had the opportunity to visit the Grand Del Mar each August for the last three years as part of a small conference that includes serious half day meetings and fun interactive afternoon events. Every year that I return, the hotel gets better. The customer service is unequaled. One morning I needed copies of an outline I had prepared for a presentation. I went to the concierge to ask where I could find the business center. Instead, the concierge volunteered to print out my documents on the spot. She did so quickly, with a smile, and free of charge. One more example, upon checking out of the hotel early one morning, the person at the check out desk encouraged me to review my bill. I noticed that there was a charge for one of the hotel restaurants on my bill and I had not visited it during my stay. I mentioned the $60 charge and without hesitation the check out assistant waived the charge. No "I will need to speak with a manager" or even a follow up question or two. It was prompt and decisive. Impressive. Similarly the help by the valets and attendants at the golf course were stellar. When I noticed that my golf bag did not include my wedge (grandchild strikes again), the attendant went and got me a brand new quality wedge at no charge. Speaking of the golf course, it is one of the best that I have played. It's fair and fascinating, with each hole offering a unique challenge. Greens are fast, the conditions are outstanding, and the caddies are energetic and knowledgeable. It's pricey, but worth the experience. Lastly, I have to add that the hotel itself is gorgeous. The grounds are immaculate. Forget the fussy comments elsewhere, this is a first class hotel with great, plush rooms, expansive bathrooms, very comfortable king beds, and nice furniture. The common areas are attractive, nicely decorated, and rarely too crowded. Next year, despite the business meetings, I'll want to ensure that my wife joins me. This is too nice a place to experience alone.

“Good quality hotel” My wife and I were in Boston for a few days around Paddy's weekend after previous nice breaks here. We had never stayed in the Langham previously but decided to give it a go. When we arrived the lobby was under construction which did detract from the impact and comfort of the hotel - a detail that was not disclosed prior to us making the booking. However, the room was nice if somewhat dated and the location was very handy. The pool was nice if small. The staff were generally friendly. Overall, it's a reasonable hotel but certainly the rooms are due a facelift. My favourite hotel in Boston remains Jurys and the steakhouse across the road from it is excellent and I certainly recommend it.

“Great Location, Great Hotel” If I had one thing to say to recommend this hotel, it's location, location, location. It's located just across 57th Street from the Russian Tea Room and just down the block and across the street from Carnegie Hall (so you don't have to ask how to get there and get the response "practice, practice, practice). The lobby can get a little crowded, and it's not much of a lobby, but who wants to stay in the lobby? The rooms are all good size, with any amenity you'd want (although having to pay for internet isn't the greatest...but then I've been to hotels with no internet at all!), and are all pretty quiet. They're nicely furnished, with a nice bathtub (which is something I really appreciate) and are perfectly adequate for a nice week in the Big Apple. There's a buffet restaurant that you can go for breakfast, although it's not included in the room rent, and I heard mutterings that it wasn't very good. But in a town full of splendid places to go, who needs it? All in all, I'd recommend this place, although one little caveat is that the lobby seems to be always full of youth groups either checking in or checking out. I didn't have any problems with noise that you'd usually associate with youth groups. If you're interested, the hotel is owned and operated by the Baptist Church, which is right next door. I enjoyed a fine Sunday morning service there.
“excellent” Nice restaurant, nice stall, shuttle service. Bus stops along side hotel to take you to areas of L.A.

“I like the charm of this hotel” I like the Old World charm of this hotel. It has a really nice lobby area and a lot of details are still there from years ago. Even though we had a large upgraded room, it really needs an update-mostly in the bathroom area. For some reason our room had two bathrooms. One had a tub/shower combo and the other had the smallest shower ever! One nice bathroom would have been better. The tile is old and the doors/trim have been painted over so many times--they really need to be stripped down and refinished. The room had the strangest odor too-like body odor or something-not to mention the weak air conditioning. We set the thermostat at 64 degrees and it was not really cool at all. I have to say the staff is really nice and helpful. Our room was not cleaned at all the first day and I called to complain. After waiting a while for some towels, I called back and spoke to the manager Luis. He apologized and offered us breakfast the next morning. It was a wonderful buffet. Thank you, Luis! It still took a while to get the towels, but for some reason they had changed the room numbers and no one knew where the room was. The hotel is located in a good location-It is close to Newbury street and shopping, the T-stop, the Boston Common. We even walked over to the movie theater nearby. There is an Au bon Pain around the corner and they even sell coffee/bagels/fruit in the hotel lobby in the morning-very reasonably priced.

“No complaints except the breakfast” An excellent hotel to which I would gladly return. I found the bed to be especially comfortable and, contrary to the experience of some other reviewers, my room was very quiet. Maybe it depends on location. I was on an upper floor well away from the highway and facing away from the airport. My room overlooked a huge parking lot for commuters and office workers, but I couldn't hear any noise from that, despite my staying there a Thursday night. My only complaint was the breakast - the food and service were very mediocre.

“Can't beat the location, but you can probably beat the service..” This stay was not the first time I've stayed at this hotel, but it's my first since joining as a reviewer of this site. The Marriott Marquis has many things going for it - some good, some bad. First of all, if you are a theater-goer, you cannot beat the location of this hotel. The Marquis is within 4 blocks of most theaters, not to mention the literal location of one (The Marquis Theater). To be so close to all the shows is incredibly handy, however even if you don't go to a performance, you are still at the doorstep of everything. TKTS, shopping and restaurants surround this property. On the inside, this hotel is immense. Right away you will encounter my biggest pet peeve with this property - the elevators. Once heralded as 'New York's Smartest Elevators!', the system to work them is not only a pain but also incredibly annoying. Operating them involves putting your desired floor on a keypad and having it tell you which elevator to go to. If you understand the system, it works ok. The problem is, many people don't so they enter your elevator, cannot find the keypad and then are stumped with what to do. Furthermore, some put their number on the pad, miss the elevator location, and then re-enter it. By doing so, their floor is called on two different elevators so there is the potential for you to be on an elevator by yourself with 6 stops. I find them incredibly unreliable and wish they would go back to regular keypads in the elevators. Aside from that, the hotel rooms are large, some of the largest I've ever stayed in in New York. The beds are incredibly comfortable and lots of rooms provide wonderful views of Times Square. Bathrooms are also quite big and the Bath & Body Works products are a nice touch. One place this hotel is lacking is the service. Marriott is typically dependable for good service however this property generally lacks it. I've encountered pompous and rude front desk staff in previous stays who act like it is the best hotel in the city. Also, pressing 'At Your Service' on your phone, the only button in which to contact anybody, often results in waits of around 15 rings, and many times, no answer at all. The fitness center is large and overlooks Times Square - a huge plus. Also open 24 hours a day, at with most hotels these days. I haven't ever eaten at the restaurants in the hotel - there are far better ones outside the front door. Two Starbucks inside are convinient, though the one in the lobby has minimal hours. You are better off going to the one on the 1st floor. In terms of connectivity, you can purchase Marriott's 'Wired For Business' program for $15.95 a night, which includes high speed internet and free calls to anywhere in the US. I suppose some people may find this handy, although as someone who would just like the internet, the cost is a bit steep. I think this hotel really is an equal combination of good and bad. It has a lot of positive points - its location and rooms, and some things to be wary of - its staff and the elevators. I would stay here again, no problem - but it would probably not be my first choice.

“Perfect for a romantic tryst” I live uptown, but was looking for a romantic evening away from home (with my wife!) for an anniversary, though I'm sure this would be suited to any romantic assignation. It's comfortable and the rooms, from lighting to details, exude a comfortable romance. Others have suggested the lobby is imposing, but I think both the location and the lobby set it apart from some of the "mega" lux hotels in the city. It's tucked away in a location that is off the beaten path while still being central to restaurants, theaters, etc. Staff were friendly and efficient. And frankly, the price was right as well. I guess I should note that some notes painted on the walls in the bathroom--apparently by the builders--showed through the white paint, which was a strange discordant note. In any case, though, will definitely stay again.

“Good Choice” This hotel was very adequate for our vacation from June 29 to July 8. I had requested two robes when making the reservation and again upon check-in. When I requested them again along with a lot more hangers when we got to the room, we got them. We were in the "New Tower" which is about 30 years old. The room was small (deluxe king) on 20th floor with a great view. The bathroom is minamalist, only the very basic amenities (no brand) are provided which only included shampoo, conditioner and body lotion and thin bars of soap which looked like Ivory Soap, but weren't. No shower cap is provided. The shower in in a tub, but it was a "Heavenly Shower". The toilet has no tank, it has that metal foot pedal thing in the back - ugly. You must be sure the bath towels that hang behind it don't hang long otherwise they touch the toilet seat when it is up. The concierge desk constantly had a very long line except very early in the morning or on a rare occasion, so do your homework so you don't have to rely on them for much. They are very helpful when you can get a chance to speak to them. Like everyone says, the location is the best. The stores are just steps away which includes a seven story Macy's. It was a pleasure to shop there. Union Square in right in front of the hotel. They had a great art show there the first weekend of July. Musicians are playing on street corners. Sears Fine Food restaurant is right up the street and is the best breakfast place. All the hotels recommend it for breakfast. There is usually a line, but it moves fast. It is definitely worth the 10-15 minute wait. We liked the St. Francis and will stay there again. They are being bought (again), so it will not remain a Westin/Starwood hotel for long, but that is ok and doesn't matter.

“Good base for busy sightseeing trip, but concierge issues” My husband and I stayed here for a 2-day sightseeing trip before heading to Napa. Because of Starwood points, we had stayed her for free. The hotel is in a good location and convenient to travel back and forth to the airport. Our room was small but we also chose a queen size bed/room in order to check-in earlier. Overall it was updated and clean. We didn't need much since we barely spent time in the room. The bar there was nice as well. The biggest issue we had with the hotel was the concierge. Having never been to San Fran and really not doing a lot of research, we depended on the concierge for directions, restaurant recos, etc. Everytime we went we had to wait FOREVER to talk to someone and when we did the restaurant recommendation was not great. When we told them it wasn't great, they didn't seem to care. They did provide a map and some good direction for getting around, but overall was not pleased with the service. One morning we decided go out on our own instead waiting for help from them. Granted it was Labor Day weekend but they were definitely understaffed.

“Great downtown location especially for Colts games.” My son and I attended our first Colts game in Indy and stayed here. Great location, historic venue, good clean average rooms, computers available and just good unusual hotel that my son really liked. We parked and walked everywhere that we desired to go. We dined at St. Elmo's Steakhouse. Recommend for a good meal and we fit in perfectly after the game with all the other football game attendees. We hope to visit again next season!
“Great Hotel” Great Hotel in Austin - close to everything. Comfortable beds - stayed on 26th floor with Executive Lounge - very nice Woud certainly stay here again!!

“Great stay!” We stayed at the Doubletree Times Square 8/12 - 8/16/06 on a Hilton Honors reward certificate. The staff on the ground level entrance/security checkpoint and at the front desk on the third floor were pleasant and helpful. We were checked in and in our room within minutes. The suite itself is very good sized by NYC standards. The living room area included an arm chair, pull out couch, desk, tv on a storage credenza, a wetbar/storage counter area that housed a sink, coffee maker, fridge, microwave, and a safe. The bedroom had an armoire for the tv and clothing storage, two end tables, a blanket chest, and the bed (which was very comfortable with great pillows and linens). The bath had about six feet of counter space, a hair dryer, full tub, and was stocked with bath amenities and plenty of good sized, soft towels daily. Housekeeping did a great job, keeping the room tidy & providing turn down service each night.
