As Hilton Honors Gold members, our room included internet service, which was was reliable and speedy, and free breakfast buffet at the hotel cafe, which we tried once & thought was good (typical hot & cold breakfast items with an omelet station and juice/coffee service). The hotel is very centrally located to all subway lines and within walking distance of many of the popular destinations in midtown. While this can be great for the first time or infrequent visitor, making travel around town fairly foolproof, this was the one con for us. During our past visits, we have typically chosen to stay a several blocks further east or west from Times Square where the neighborhoods are a bit quieter. We simply found it to be a bit overwhelming to have to always exit the hotel directly into the throngs of people traveling the street and jostling through several blocks of that, along with the massive exhaust fumes from all the vehicle traffic, to escape the crowds. But, especially considering our stay was free with our reward points, this truly is a minor gripe. Overall, we really did enjoy our stay at the Doubletree and would recommend it highly, particularly for first time visitors who haven't experienced the excitement of the crowds in Times Square and who want to be centrally located for easy walking/subway access to the city. The cleanliness, spaciousness, security, and service in this hotel are some of the best we've had in NYC; better than some much more high brow establishments we've tried. It is truly a great bet for NYC!

“Uniquely Fairmont” Not the nicest Fairmont you'll encounter, but a comfortable retreat in a great location, with awesome views. I'm not a big fan of the "contemporary-modern-meets-Austin-Powers" lobby thing they have going on, but that's just me. Many reviewers here seem to like it just fine, so take my monkey chatter for what it's worth. The location is hard to beat and in a city the size of Chi-Town, location matters. It's right next to Millennium Park, The Miracle Mile and The Navy Pier, so you can't get much more central than that. It's worth it to get an elevated floor if views matter to you - the views are stunning in every direction. As in many hotels in major cities, day rates for valet is not cheap and the Fairmont is no exception - $50 per day, self-parking is less. The rooms, while not in the most elegant Fairmont tradition are very comfortable, but the usual Fairmont amenities apply - Robe, slippers, safe, iPad in the breakfast dining room for reading the paper ...

“Nice hotel in financial district” Located in the heart of the financial district, this hotel is convenient to many offices, but still a cab or trolley ride to fisherman's wharf. YOu can walk 4 blocks to the Ferry Building, and walk or jog along the Embarcadero. Not much is open in the area after 5pm, however. The lobby was large with ample seating. Relatively fast elevators. Fitness center could use a few more treadmills, but is definitely more than adequate. My biggest complaint is the lack of coffee in the room; of course, there's a Starbucks just across the street. Overall, I found it to be a good business hotel.

“Solid hotel with great service and views of Chicago” The hotel overlooks the Hancock Building and Michigan Ave. The rooms were in good shape, except for the bathrooms, which were ancient looking, but functional. Upon arrival, the staff was incredibly friendly and cordial. There are an abundance of good restaurants nearby including everything from upscale chains like Cheesecake Factory to Chicago's local favorites at a variety of price points. Beware if you are driving in, parking is around $60/night, which is terribly pricey, even for Chicago. There are alternate garages around if you don't mind walking a few blocks.

“Fabulous Upgrade and Great stay in a good NY location” Arrived Tuesday 16th for a 3 night stay, I had booked what i thought was a good deal via Quickbook for a studio suite worked out at $203+taxes, i was to very pleasantly suprised to be upgraded to a huge duplex loft suite that had great view over Time Warner.Room had two flat screen TV's, great shower and bathroom facilities,very comfy bed and pillows and a great fridge and freezer with Microwave and hob if you need it. So great start to a good break.The Location for uptown is superb, MTA just cross over the road, only a few minutes to walk to Central park and 5-10 minutes across to 5th Avenue and it's many and numerous shops. Whole foods in the basement of Time Warner building just across the road is good to buy grocery for breakfast. Hotel staff were very friendly, and kept good humour in some very unseasonal wet weather in New York, good recommendation for lunch from staff Really enjoyed my stay at 6 Columbus and would be very happy to return

“Good, no frills hotel 2 blocks from Union Station (Amtrak)” I have stayed here a few times and have been quite satisfied. This is a good, basic, no frills hotel with nice size rooms and baths. My rooms have been clean and quiet. TV channels are very limited. For the price, this is a great value in downtown Los Angeles an easy walk through Olivera Street to Union Station. There is a nice Continental breakfast offered at no extra charge in a small room off the lobby. There are restaurants and fast food outlets nearby.

“Chic Hotel in a GREAT Location!” The Copley Square Hotel has a great location in Boston's Back Bay. It is in close proximity to the Marriott and Westin and for me, that was critical as I was in Boston to attend a convention being held at both the Marriott and the Westin. The hotel is within very easy walking distance to plenty of shopping along Boyston Avenue and Newbury Street. There are also tons of shops at the Prudential Center. The rooms are small but that is to be expected in such a historic hotel and as I was rooming alone, I had plenty of room. The area is thriving and there are lots of options for entertainment and the staff is quite happy to help. I plan to stay here again when I return to Boston next year.

“Really not very good” They could use alot more attention to detail here! The hosuekeeping is pretty poor I have to say. They do the BARE minimum (make the bed and stock the towels). my room had maintenance issues, some of which were never fixed. Including a mirrored closet door dangling dangerously from its hinges, a scribbled on ottoman and AC that did not work one night. Yeah, for a 100 degree day, their AC did not work that evening, though when I called maintenance, they insisted it was fine. Sorry - i know the difference between an air conditioned room and not when it's 100 degrees outside. by the next morning, when they finally admitted their entire system was down, the whole building was STEAMY. yuck. The front desk staff was nice but after all the issues I had, it seemed like it may have been the YES program, to just get me to go away. Free breakfast but it ends at 9. I would defintiely not stay there again,

“Nice hotel close to Riverwalk!” Nice hotel close to the Riverwalk and former World Fair Park. About a 5 walk to the southern Park of the Riverwalk (quieter part). The location is safe, but the hotel has an ugly parking right in front of it. The hotel itself is your avg Four Points, rooms are in decent condition. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Would recommend.

“Accomodating and Good Location” The hotel is located in a great shopping and restaurant area. We were in town for a function down town, and this hotel was only a 10 minute drive from the convention center. The staff was friendly and helpful and the rooms were very spacious and accommodating. Will probably stay here again for the next event in Columbus. There is a train close by, but we were never bothered by it.

“Terrible Service” Let me say that San Diego is a great city with lots to do. However, if you plan on stayin at a hotel with ZERO service and overpriced atmosphere, then stay at the Hotel Solamar. There is a general sense with the receptionists that having an attitude and lecturing guests is "OK" in the hospitality business. Just ask receptionist Rebecca who instead of rolling with the flow, berated us about luggage checks and even had the audacity to ask "if we've stayed with them before" prior to switching from a $500 a night suite , to a room with 2 double beds. Please look at your guest index to see that when guests have already spent $2000 in 4 nights, that yes, they have stayed with you before. And I havent even mentioned the techno DJ by the pool blasting music nightly till 10pm and even on Sundays! Overall, do not stay here. Stay at the Hilton which is much nicer as is the Omni. San Diego is a very laid back place but if you feel like spending a lot of money for a lack of service, then the Hotel Solamar is yours

“I've stayed several times and always enjoy my stay.” This particular Comfort Inn is one of my favorite in the country. It's got beautiful views of the Ben Franklin Bridge and within walking distance of many of the touristy type of things like Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. The continental breakfast is always well stocked with a nice selection of times and the front desk staff has always been courteous. I will be back for sure.

“Great San Francisco Experience” I've stayed at the Chancellor Hotel twice while in San Fransisco and would happily stay again. Sure, the rooms are a little small and oldish. But the space is plenty comfortable for one or two people and the design feels very historic rather than tired. Speaking of comfortable, the beds here are fantastic for crashing after a long day walking around the city. Everything is very clean and the housekeeping seemed very thorough. The service is great too, as the people at the front desk went out of their way to accommodate me upon my arrival. All this for about a third of the price of the other hotels that are right in the heart of San Fransisco makes staying here a terrific choice.

“Good Hotel - Good Location” I do not agree with all the negative reviews, maybe they have corrected the problems cited. We found it to be a very good hotel with excellent service, good location for 'streetcar' and plenty of free parking. I thought breakfast was a bit better than most Fairfields I visited recently with two very attentive attendants.

“Nice Hotel in a Great Location” Clean, quiet and situated perfectly in downtown. Every member of the staff was absolutely terrific ... excellent customer service. The kitchen had all the necessary items in great working order. The parking, though, costly, was a good investment, as this hotel is in easy walking distance to all the downtown attractions. The only downer was the breakfast ... fruit had run out or was not available each day we were there, and seating in the breakfast area was at a premium. In fairness, this was a very busy time and the entire facility was sold out. Overall, a great experience, and we look forward to staying here again.

“Excellent quality and service for the price!” We just stayed here for 3 nights over Memorial Day Weekend. They only charge half price for overnight valet parking on Friday and Saturday which was nice. Parking in this town can be expensive. The service at this hotel is top notch and as good as I have experienced anywhere including Four Seasons. We arrived late on Friday night and Kendra at the front desk greeted us with a smile. She was super friendly, curtious, and even helped us find a great place to grab a bite at 11PM just a block away. The staff here goes out of their way to make sure you feel comfortable. Lex at the conceirge is a wealth of knowledge and gave us some great tips on things to do in the area as well as some super restaurant options. There is a free walking tour on Saturday mornings that leaves from the Omni at 10am (check to see if that is all the time). We had a great tour of China Town and it lasted about 2 hours. It was super convenient meeting in the lobby for the walking tour. I was concerned about the location in the financial district when I was first considering options for lodging. However, the excellent reviews on Trip Advisor for the Omni kept bringing me back. The location is actually excellent as many reviewers have commented. The bus and cable car lines are right out the front door. Cabs are everywhere and easy walking distance to North Beach and Nob Hill. The rooms are recently updated and very quiet. The beds are comfortable and there is a good size desk with wired and wireless internet. My only complaint would be the wireless service was spotty and slow. I chose to plug in my lap top with the provided wire connection and then I was good to go. The bathroom was updated and spacious. We had a free morning beverage and newspaper included each day. The beverage was delivered everyday exactly at the time we requested. The juice was fresh as was the coffee and cream. I would highly recommend this hotel whether for business or leisure. The combination of updated rooms, quiet location, public transportation, and excellent service put this on the top of my list! I plan to stay here again when we come back to San Francisco.
“nice, clean hotel close to sea world” Got a free night stay with hotel points. Was given a suite. Very nice room, very clean with large bathroom. Service was good.

“Pretty Good - but watch out...” We enjoyed our stay at the Hamilton Crowne Plaza. The room we were in was nice - but was a little small. Everything was perfectly clean. The location of the hotel was perfect for us for a weekends sightseeing. The only problems we encountered were that the room was quite noisy: there was a lot of noise late at night which sounded like people were in the room with us. I guess this is the downside of an older building - the sound insulation is not great. The staff that we came across were very friendly and helpful. Probably worth avoiding the offer of cars arranged to the airport however - the price charged was very different from what had been promised.

“Sleepless in seattle” Truly, if you stay at this hotel you will not get any sleep .The freight trains run past here almost every 20 minutes with their horns blaring. At 10:30 pm we asked to be moved to a quieter side of the hotel and even there we could hear the trains. The hotel itself is nice and new, rooms are good but bring ear plugs. The location is not convenient if you want to go downtown.

“Nice, But Not Up to Conrad International Standards” My stay did not start well. I got off the airport shuttle with four (4) bags, while the Bell/Door personnel did nothing. Even the shuttle driver remarked how rude the door staff were (the evening door staff, as it turned out, were much friendlier). The following is a run-down of the "other-than-goods" for this property: --Check in was efficient, although there was no acknowledgement of my status and no welcome back. --The "city view" room was a partially obscured view of an air conditioning complex and other nearby buildings. --My breakfast vouchers were ignominiously shoved under my door whilst I slept. --Fitness facilities are adequate, but nothing special. Standard Hiltons have better. --Breakfast in the bar area was, service wise, pandemonium. A Taiwanese student group tied up the restaurant for private morning functions. However, the food quality was great, as was the coffee. --There were two rubber bands on the floor, in the hallway of the 15th floor, which convinced me that the housekeeping staff is lackadaisical about their responsibilities. Now for the "Goods": --Room size is terrific. Plenty of area to feel comfortable. --Bathroom. Fantastic. Shower, tub, scale, and separate toilet. Bath amenities were replenished regularly. --Room amenities! iPod docking station, Bose Sound System, Flat Screen TV, and complimentary internet. --Eddie the Server in the Lounge! Excellent, personal service. --French Fries. Some of the best I have had. All-in-all, the Conrad is a nice, decent hotel. I would stay there again, but I do not think it is in the same class as the Peninsula or the Four Seasons. In fact, the Chicago Conrad is no where near the same class as the Bangkok or Tokyo Conrads--not even close. The Chicago Conrad lacks an Executive Lounge, and the majority of the staff could probably use some training on how to provide a higher level of service. Being able to do the "little things" (e.g., vacuum carpets, specially welcome loyal Hilton Guests, and display a little more courtesy/friendliness) would go a long way to elevating this hotel to the class it in which it should be.

“正直、安心しました” 改装する前(ラディソン時代)のトリップアドバイザーでの評判はとても悪かったので、心配していましたが、ダブルツリーになり改装も行われ、結構いいホテルでした。値段もかなりお安かったです(1泊朝食付税込で80ドルぐらい)。部屋のエアコンの音がちょっとうるさいとか、朝食がシンプルすぎるなど、ダブルツリーの標準に達していない部分もありましたが、値段を考えれば問題ないと思います。ロビーがとても綺麗で、そして快適で、大画面テレビの前で、ビールとパソコンをもって、長時間くつろぎました。場所が悪いとの指摘もありましたが、Streetcar のイエローが中心地に行くのにかなり便利で、バス停はホテルの目の前、5~10分で中心地までいけます。そして、ハイシーズンだったからかもしれませんが、かなり頻繁に運行しているようで、5回以上利用しましたが5分以上バス停で待つことがありませんでした。ちなみにホテルの周りはコンビニなどないです。

“Yes, it is too cool for its own game. Way too cool.” I checked in for a four night stay. The i-pad in the room was not working so I could not order room service, and not one of the staff told me I could use a paper menu. There is no restaurant in this hotel, but there is one that will be open either the next day or in a week, depending on who you speak with. The beds are platform beds with no box springs, and I had to request a top sheet, the bed is made without one. The staff are very interested in being beautiful and cool, but not in customer service. I would have liked to take a cup of coffee up to my room from the lobby in the morning, but it did not seem to be available. The location is great.

“Great location” We changed hotels at the last minute because of the health issues at the JW Marriott. The Marriott operator lead us to believe we could have a waterfront room, on a high floor, possibly a suite due to the problem at the JW. Sorry to say, that did not happen. We received a room facing an alley on the 9th floor. So much for being a Marriott Elite member! The hotel was packed but we were checked in fairly quickly. Our room was clean and comfortable and housekeeping staff was wonderful. The restaurant has a lovely view and an outstanding breakfast buffet. The bar in the lobby is a great spot to relax after a day of sightseeing. The hotel is located across from the river and close to all that downtown Chicago has to offer. We were able to walk everywhere and take in most of the sights. We would return.

“Great Stay” Stay there for a night. Got a great deal on Hotwire. Check in was fast and the front desk people were very professional and very helpful. The room was spacious, well lit and clean; it was decorated in a modern style, and it had a separate area with a desk, great for working in the room. Two very comfortable beds, I would have rather had a king size, but I did not even try to ask for a change, since I was just there for the night. Very large bathroom with lots of handle bars for people with disabilities. However to get to the elevators you have to claim a few steps and I did not see a ramp or a different elevator, but I am sure there is access for wheelchairs, etc. One strange thing, in the bathroom there is something like a closet and you will find there some hangers with night garments for sale (for males and females), which are animal print inspired, and some socks... I thought it was strange, but nothing wrong with that, just not what I expected to see in a hotel bathroom. Did not check out the restaurant, but it seem quite busy even after 11 pm. The hotel does not have big lobby. My room faced the inside (as in towards where the air conditioners units were located), which was fine with me, since I imagine you may get some street noise if your room faces the street. Dupont Circle Metro station is less than 5 minutes walk. So Location, Location, Location. There was a mini bar, for which I did not asked for the key. And when I came home at night after going out, there was a jar of cookies, Oreo like, in the lobby which I thought it was a nice touch. I guess my only disappointing comment would be the fact that I would have liked a little coffee maker in the room. I believe they do have coffee in the lobby, I just did not check it out, since I was in a rush to leave the next morning. I liked this place, I recommend it and I would come back if I have a chance.

“Convenient but much too expensive” I was treating my sister to a trip to the Chicago area as it was her first trip back there for 40 years since she spent a year at a High School on the North Shore. I was astounded at hotel prices, but I chose this hotel as it was to be brand new after being refurbished at great cost. It was formerly the Hotel Cass and reviewers rave about that hotel, but what they emphasise is the low price and great location. We arrived after a minor fire, the receptionist kept answering the phone instead of dealing with us and then we had to walk up to our room on the sixth floor. The room was small, with very little space for our luggage and virtually no hanging space. The safe didn't work. The bathroom was tiny. The free daily newspaper did not materialise. The worst feature was the breakfast which was included in the price ($229 plus lots of tax for Saturday night and $329 plus tax for Sunday and Monday nights). The newly opened hotel advertised its 'Signature hot cinammon rolls'. these were available on Sunday morning but not on the next two. We asked for them and were told that there were none. When I checked out, I was asked whether we had been happy with everything and when I mentioned the breakfast she took absolutely no notice. On the plus side, the beds and bedding were very comfortable, but I feel that I paid far too much for what we got and I feel let down. On reflection I ought to have paid slightly more to be in a really classy hotel or considerably less to be in an acceptable Best Western or similar in a slightly less convenient location. We bought CTA passes and these allowed us to travel anywhere, so getting from the Loop to the Magnificent Mile was not a problem.

“I'd Stay Here Again” Very nice hotel that is very close to Penn Station and I would recommend staying overnight here if you travel by train as it is within walking distance and not have to worry about hailing a cab. Should I come again for an overnight in New York City, I would patronize again since it is also close to Macy's.

“Great location and price - eclectic but interesting decor!” Stayed here for the price and location for business. Quite interesting decor - large and bustling lobby where everyone congregates. Loved the library bar in the evening and for breakfast in the morning. The place felt very comfortable and cozy and full of life! The room was quite small - but that is to be expected in Manhattan. I had a nice view looking north towards 8th Avenue. It was minimal, but clean - and the bed was fine for a good night's sleep. Easy walking to Times Square, Theatres, and restaurants in Hell's Kitchen.

“Great value!” I enjoyed my stay at this hotel. It is in a great local, Walgreens across the street, my bank a few blocks away in both directions, Jamaba Juice next door and my favorite coffee shop Intelligentsia in Chicago only a few blocks north. Yes the rooms are small but I have stayed in smaller (Beverly Terrace in Beverly Hills). But I found the room very clean as well as the bathroom. The front desk folk were great on advice on transport and local eats. The only issue I had with the hotel is at least with my room there should be a sign posted next to the bathroom watch your step. Upon entering I had to use the restroom and almost killed myself since I hadn't turned on enough lights and tripped on the step up to get in the bathroom. The second , third and forth things I didn't like about the hotel was the lack of water pressure, hot water for the shower unless it is morning but even then it is lacking and the VERY SLOW drain in the bath tub. As for the very slow drain in the bath tub I just chalked it up as having old pipes. I unfort. forgot to mention this upon check out as I had an early morning flight and was still half asleep. If anyone mentions this to the staff what is/was their reply? Over all though I did enjoy my stay and just now booked a room for a couple days to let my hair down in Oct.

“Still cool to me” Stayed here for business and after haivng lived in Manhattan 8 years then moved away I have to say, it's still a cool hotel. I can't vouch for what the scene at the bar is like anymore but the lobby area is cool. And the carrot cake cream filled donut is TO DIE FOR and worth going back just for that. Also the outdoor terrace is so pretty. The neighborhood is fine - not the coolest in Manhattan but fine. And I'm sure 5000 people before me have alerted everyone to this but the rooms are BEYOND tiny. Smallest I've ever seen in NYC. But they have a cool look to them at least.

“Staff went above and beyond” I can not actually review the hotel rooms, as I was unable to stay here. However, I want to commend the front desk staff who were kind and helpful when I showed up looking for a room due to weather canceled travel. After trudging around in the cold with my luggage, trying to figure out the best thing to do, they were welcoming and helpful in ways that they did not have to be. Many thanks.

“Great Sevice and Location” We stayed at the Jurys from Saturday-Wednesday. The service was excellent. The location is ideal for getting anywhere in Boston. It is a $24 (including tip) cab ride from the airport. I was traveling with my daughter and the first night they gave us a King size bed rather than two queens. There was not another room available until Sunday but they moved us as soon as a room became available. No inconvenience to us at all. The rooms are spacious and the beds are extremely comfortable. The housekeeping staff did a great job daily and turned down the beds at night. The blankets are wrapped between two sheets for those who enjoy this. Personally, I can't stand it if the hotels do not do this so notice it right away. The rooms have empty refrigerators which was great too. We were on the 4th and 9th floors during out stay. The pub in the hotel, Cuffs, was very busy on Saturday night but we did not hear any noise in our rooms as mentioned in other reviews. Our departing flight was not until 7:00 pm so the hotel held our luggage so we could get in another day of sightseeing. We had dinner at Cuffs one night which was very good and relaxing with the fireplace. We had breakfast one morning in the restaurant in the hotel too. Just a light breakfast which was ideal. Full breakfasts were available. Starbucks is two blocks away for those who need that kick. About a 5 minute walk. The subway stop is right beside Starbucks. The Consierge service was great. Take advantage of this service as they were all very helpful. The doormen were very friendly. (other than the one who couldn't pull himself away from playing solitaire on the computer) I would highly recommend this hotel!

“Quite Nice” This Crowne Plaza is quite nice and the location is absolutely fabulous. We generally visit Manhattan 2-3 weekends per year, stay in Times Square and pay $200-$250 per night. We’ve been happy with the hotels we’ve chosen over the years, but feel that this one is a little better for the price. We booked directly with Crowne Plaza on line and had a King Superior room at $249 over Labor Day Weekend 9/2/06. Some of the hotels we stayed in before would not allow us to book for just one night over the holiday weekend. The room was spacious, very clean, nicely appointed, like new and very peaceful. We actually slept late! We seldom do that. One very minor complaint I have is they could use better ventilation in the bathrooms to keep the mirrors from fogging. The staff was friendly and accommodating. They changed our room upon request (excessively noisy children next door to the first room). Elevator service was great and security seemed decent. They required all to show a room key before entering at night. The lobby was nice and we got to enjoy some live piano music there. Our stay was short, but excellent. We will definitely return if we can find similar rates here in the future.

“Walking distance to UCLA, Print boarding passes at business center” Really comfortable rooms and beds, bathrobes, but NO SLIPPERS : ( 24-hr room service!!! Complementary coffee in the am. Restaurant. Good map of campus. Good value hotel. Relaxing quiet atmosphere throughout hotel. 24-hr business center access.

“Overpriced!” We recently stayed at the Mark Hopkins for a much needed vacation. I travel to San Fran frequently for business and we decided to treat ourselves by staying at a 4 star hotel - unfortunately we were disappointed. For the same cost you can stay at the Fairmont across the street which looked like a much nicer place to stay. The Intercontinental was equivalent to a Hilton in my opinion but the food quality was worse. We paid extra to be on a club level floor and the room was nothing special, nor were the amenities. We dined at the hotel restaurant for dinner and the food quality was one star at best. The waiter noticed a $17 appetizer left uneaten and asked what the issue was as we were the 2nd guest to not eat it, we explained the issue and were still charged for it. So on Sunday we decided to try brunch at the Top of the Mark and it missed the mark, $128 for a nice view with very bland, unimaginative cuisine. You can do better for this level of cash outlay.

“Great place to stay for families” Our family (dad, mom, 14 y.o. boy and 10 y.o. girl) stayed here for three nights on our most recent visit to San Antonio. Knowing that we would be out during the day walking alot (we went to Sea World), we needed a comfortable, reasonably priced place to stay and spread out. Having two TVS and a separate bedroom is what makes this ideal for families with older children/teens. Our room had two double beds and a pull out sofa where our teen slept. We also liked having the small kitchen and refrigerator to store our drinks and snacks. It's about a 15 minute drive from the Riverwalk area but since we've been to San Antonio many times that didn't matter to us. The breakfast served each morning had make-your-own waffles (in the shape of Texas) and another hot entree in addition to the usual cold breakfast fare. The pool area is quite small though and didn't appeal to our kids. Overall, this was a great place to stay and we would stay here again.

“Great Place to Stay On Someone Else's Dime!” Stayed here in a hurricane-induced haze. My employer put me up here at the height of Hurricane Sandy because much of the Northeast was shut down and I work a few blocks away, and they wanted me in to work next day. An elegant, well-appointed hotel that offers comfort and luxury. Not sure if I got a typical room with a king-size bed, but it was big! I did not sample the restaurant because there was an hour wait for a table and a 90 minute wait for room service. No fault of the hotel, in fact it actually gets praise, because at least its dining room was OPEN at the height of the storm when everything else in the neighborhood was closed. Front desk guy was extemely kind and accomodating given the circumstances surrounding the storm. Would definitely recommend this hotel, even though I checked in at about 8pm and was out by 7am. A nice luxury hotel and if I wasn't so wed to the Marriott or Hilton places, I'd love to stay here again. Alas I live in NYC so it's highly unlikely that I'll be back. But for anyone visiting NYC, or staying on business, this will prove to be a highly reliable and comfortable choice. Location is excellent, close to mass transit and right on Lexington Avenue. Only thing that was a tad annoying was $7 for a bottle of water in the room! Am I out of touch or what? How do hotels get away with charging so much for bottled water and WiFi? Wait, I know the answer. Expense accounts and companies that pick up the tab!

“There is no other place I would rather stay in NY!” I stayed for the first time at the 6 Columbus hotel when they were in their soft opening a couple of years back and have been going back ever since. I travel quite a bit and have never encountered a hotel with such great customer service. Everyone goes out of their way to make you feel welcome. Here are some of the great points for this hotel: *I am going to repeat it...the staff...they welcome you back warmly. From the bellmen, Peter and Cesar just to name two, and the front desk staff, Adriana and Linda who often give me upgrades, everyone is professional, courteous and efficient. I was quoted in the Zagat hotel edition as saying that the bellmen greet you like you are a 20 year old supermodel even when you are a 40 something high school teacher;-) *The restaurant...Blue ribbon serves incredible food and cocktails. Keith makes the best yuzu margarita but the others make incredible cocktails also. Everyone in the staff is professional and the food is great. I always have dinner there for the dumplings and the sashimi. *The rooms......I always book a pod room. It may be small but it is well designed and the beds are comfortable. There are not too many rooms per floor so it is usually quiet. I was upgraded quite a few times, even though I don't expect it I am happy when it happens, to incredible rooms. They are very clean which is important. *Location...you go out of your hotel and you have subway and bus lines just a few feet away. *Restaurants....many great restaurants in the vicinity *Cons.....I have to leave to come back home I love going to NY for a couple of days and am lucky enough since I am able to do it a couple of times per year and I don't even consider staying anywhere else now!

“It is what it is” We stayed at the Tabard for one night recently. It is in a very nice location in Washington, near Dupont Circle and easy access to the National Mall. The Tabard is charming, quirky, and old. And it's all the things that go along with that. Slightly dingy (though you should not interpret this as dirty), a little tired, but not bad. It's a very different experience from a chain hotel, and if you want something unique, it's probably worth a stay. POSITIVES: Location Price Restaurant (excellent, with a lovely garden) Breakfast included NEGATIVES: A little worn Light in rooms is TERRIBLE (all energy-saving bulbs--I challenge you to put on your makeup in these lights and not come out looking like a clown) Price (yes, I know that was a positive, too--it's not too expensive, but you can often get a room at The Mayflower for the same amount and you'll get a more reliable hotel experience there)

“Nicer than I thought, but HVAC has small problema” We were in town for the Girls Volleyball Junior Nationals. The league books all the hotels close to the convention center so it was impossible to get a reservation without going thru them. The Blackwell was not on their list, so we were able to get a room. It was not far from the Convention Center if you drive. The Blackwell was much nicer than I thought it would be. I've been at other Big Ten school hotels and this one is much nicer than, for example, the one at MSU, the Kellogg Center. The rooms are nice, well appointed, and huge. The beds are great. Service is generally good. Our room had a king bed, with two work stations with work lamps & outlets, flat screen tv, built-in drawers, nice closet, relaxing chair (to watch tv). The view is pretty bleak---lots of parking lot and cement around. My husband commented that at least at the Kellogg Center you get a view of trees. Nice things; students run the place and they are as nice as can be. Parking was free because they didn't have anyone manning the ticket booth (not much demand, so made sense). Place is well kept up. One problem: we were there when it was about 100 F and 100% humidity. The AC was going full blast and it was really chilly. Because of the AC or HVAC system, the room had a damp, musty smell to it. I smelled it immediately and thought it was disgusting--kind of like wet, dirty socks. My husband (who has no nose I suppose) said it wasn't so bad. I wanted to move, but we decided to see if it improved when you turned the AC down. It didn't--at least to me. The only saving grace is that you get used to the smell after awhile. Everytime you enter the room though, you smell it all over again. I wouldn't say that the hotel was a really good deal, given that we were in Columbus. We got a OSU Visitor rate of $153/night including 2 breakfast buffets. We forgot about the buffet though and went out to eat! Bummer! Didn't even notice the restaurant! Food hint: If you love ice cream go to Jeni's near the convention center. This ice cream is to die for!!! Best flavors: plum sake sorbet, grapefruit frozen yogurt. i want to buy their cookbook!

“Beautiful hotel.” Members of my extended family stayed here for a wedding weekend, and I could not have been happier. I travel for work a lot, and wish every hotel I stayed in could be this perfect. Room was large, clean, quiet, and very well decorated. Great flat screen TVs and iPod docking station. Comfy bed. Fitness center had everything I needed, and TVs on the cardio equipment. Pool and jacuzzi looked nice although I did not have time to use them. We ate in the restaurant a lot, and the service was delightful. The breakfast buffet was nice. Food was decent. Two minor complaints: the cab service is extremely spotty and slow. The hotel should warn guests to call for cabs well in advance. We asked the front desk to call a cab, and 30 minutes later he was still not there. Hotel should be aware of this problem and sort it out for guests. Also, a very kind person at the front desk, with the excellent intention of helping my parents with an early check in, referred to them as an "elderly couple." They found it embarassing.

“Nice Place” As others have noted, the rooms are small, but this will be an issue in any older hotel. My room was very nicely furnished and clean. If you are staying on a weekend, be sure to get a room away from the club that is located on the first floor; my room was far away from it, but I can definitely see it being a problem. My only problem with the stay was that some baggage that I checked on the last day of my stay was not stored properly and could easily have been stolen, but I guess that this was an isolated incident. If you don't mind walking, you can park for much less money on your own at the Radisson around the corner than having the valet park for you (there is no self-parking at this hotel).

“I love this place!” I go to New York city often for business and I always stay in hotels on the Upper West Side since it's near the location of my meetings. On the Ave. is my new favorite NYC hotel. I was very impressed with the high level of customer service. When I arrived, a doorman immediately took my luggage out of the trunk of the cab and another doorman opened the door for me and welcomed me to the hotel. I was checked in right away and when I went in my hotel room and turned on the TV, there was a message on the TV welcoming me by name to the hotel. I felt like a celebrity! The room was small but most boutique NYC hotels are small so that wasn't a problem, I was the only one in the room so I didn't feel cramped. I love the ultra modern decor of the room and the stainless steel sink in the bathroom was an unexpected and stylish touch. I also liked the glass enclosed shower. The room was very clean and housekeeping did a great job tidying up my room while I was out. Everything about this hotel was very modern and "jazzy", even the over sized photos covering the walls in the elevators. I also liked how the doorman would open the door for me every morning when I left and say "Have a great day". One evening when I was in elevator searching for a floor with ice, I asked a staff member who was in the elevator which floor had ice, he not only told me what floor but took my bucket and filled it up with ice for me so I didn't have to get out of the elevator. When other staff members entered the elevator they were eager to know if I was enjoying my stay and if there was anything they could do to make it more enjoyable. I guess the only downside to the hotel was the outdoor sitting area on the top floor. I thought it would be a great place to take night time photos of the skyline but to my disappointment, it wasn't up high enough to have a good view of the city. My room also didn't have a city view, it had a nice view of a brick building next door but that was a minor thing. I found On the Ave. to be very close to the Subway, (it's right around the corner from Broadway) within walking distance of Central Park, Midtown/Broadway, museums, shops and food markets ( a good lower price alternative to eating in restaurants everyday). It was also much more affordable than hotels in Midtown. I also liked staying in a hotel in a neighborhood, it was less "touristy".

“Nostalgic Hotel” The Drake is a nostalgic hotel located just a block from the Water Tower. The lobby is beautiful and continues to hold the grace of which has made it famous. There are breathtaking views of Lake Michigan and a myriad of upscale boutiques. The hotel Christmas tree was erected in the middle of the lobby during my stay and was absolutely gorgeous, surrounded by animated Santa's and angels flying overhead. During lunch in the Palm Court restaurant, a harpist played adding a bit of magic to the overall ambiance. Overall, the rooms were nice and clean. One bit of information for Hilton Honors guests that difers from other HIlton properties is that you must be booked in an executive suite in order to be allowed onto the concierge level- no matter if you are Diamond VP or not. Although it did not impact my stay, I found it interesting. Overall a great stay.

“Great place, great location, a little tight” The staff and service were great. The location is as perfect as can be, steps from shopping, all the site, the common, freedom trail. The hotel is steeped in history and the place is beautiful. the room was nice, but a little small. But its diwnrown boston and is advertised as european so its basically what i expected.

“Central location, clean, good staff, moderate price, good sleep NO free internet, NO major luxuries, Noise from street” I was first upset the hotel suggested I take the Super Shuttle from the airport (they do not have a courtesy van). It did not take 20 min as they said but an hour and a bit. Shuttle costs 18 bucks cab can cost 40. The hotel is close to a very posh area when exiting to the right of the hotel (Tiffany's and all those stores) but do not wander to the left. The area is full of homeless people and drugged up weirdos. You are close to the streetcars (take the Hyde one going up the hill to the tourist areas...they cost 5 bucks per ride) The rooms are clean, but a bit old. The TV is top of the line, bed is big and comfy, pillow-top Serta with cushy pillows and nice sheets. There is a decent room and a good desk to work at. The price was reasonable compared to other hotels but dont expect major luxuries. Room service was good. I had a filet mignon that was tasty and well presented. Internet is NOT free in the room or in the business centre. The room rate for internet is far more reasonable 10 bucks per day than the business centre which runs like a cab fare on those PC's and is minimum 5 bucks.......flies up to ten bucks in minutes. Lots of noise from thecrazy homeless people on the street at night. I wouldn't venture far (particularly do not walk left from the hotel). In the daytime everything is safe. Staff was generally friendly and helped with everything I requested. They did screw up a wake up call but apologized after. It wasn't a big deal that day but could have been a huge deal otherwise. Go to the hotel across the street and ride the glass elevators to the top for the cheapest tour of the city.
“Very nice staff and great location!” Enjoyed my stay very much and I thought the staff was all excellent. Highly recommend to everyone!

“Wow - It was awesome!” The Manager has taken on the task to make the service level at this Hotel a 10. There are signs and letters about it in the lobby and rooms. Front Desk checkin excellent and helpful printing out driving directions for me. Our room was spotless and every piece of furniture brand new including the flat screen tv, Beautiful bathroom. 2 free internet access computer stations in lobby and free wifi in lobby area. We got a bed and breakfast package. Choices were excellent. Buffet style eggs, potatoes, bacon etc as well as all the usual items or made to order omelettes. Pool area and fire pit with lots of brand new furniture and always loads of towels. Only complaint would be the Freeway noise in the pool area, not too bad in the rooms, for us the location was excellent. 10 mins to airport, 5 mins to Old Town, 30 mins to Wild Animal Park, 30 mins to Legoland. If you want a quiet hotel, stay somewhere else - all the hotel circle hotels are going to have the freeway noise. Fashion Valley Mall 5 mins away - California Pizza Kitchen - yum! Will stay here 100% next time. Parking lot a bit sketchy, but they are doing the best with what they've got. No limos or Hummers, but my Jeep navigated the ups and downs and corners just fine. Sounds like past negative reviews were as all the changes were being put into place. It is fabulous now - no worries!

“Much Better Than I Expected!” I had a convention at the Town & Country Hotel in San Diego & just couldn't see spending $160/night for that run-down hotel. So I booked the Best Western, knowing that they were both in Hotel Circle but not knowing how close it would be. I wasn't thrilled about staying in a Best Western since I'm a Marriott gal, but for $69/night, I thought I'd give it a shot. All in all, I'm very happy with my decision. First, the Best Western is about a 3-minute walk to the Town & Country Hotel, so the location was perfect for me. Right behind the Town & Country is a big mall with lots of good places to eat, including a California Pizza Kitchen & Cheesecake Factory. You can walk there in less than 10 minutes. In addition, you do have free shuttle service to major sights including Sea World, not to mention free airport pick up & drop off. My room was fine - it was a king room with a big new TV. Yes, the sheets were thin, the dressers were a little old, but overall everything was very clean and everything worked fine. It wasn't luxury but it wasn't run down or dingy looking. The mirrors on the wall made the place seem bigger. The shower worked fine, as did the sink. The hotel's landscaping is gorgeous, and the pool is really nice. I also enjoyed the hot tub. The restaurant was quick & convenient for breakfast. Also, I can't forget to mention the free high-speed internet connection in every room. My goodness, Marriott charges $10/night for this! It was really great to have. Overall, this is a great place to stay if you are looking for a clean, better-than-decent hotel in Hotel Circle. If I had another conference at Town & Country, I certainly would be calling the Best Western Seven Seas!

“Excellent location and value” My husband and I stayed in this hotel for one night because we were going to a show in the area. For the price, the location of this hotel really can't be beat. Our show (in the Chase Auditorium) and dinner were literally around the corner. The next morning we went shopping on State Street which is a 1/2 block from the hotel. Great restaurants, great shopping, and great entertainment all within minutes of this hotel. Grant park, the Art Institute, and Michigan avenue are also just blocks away. The rooms were nice, clean, and modern. Although they were a little on the small side, they were definitely large enough. I think Internet access is complimentary in the rooms but we didn't bring our laptops so we didn't test it. They also have free computers in the lobby (along with coffee, hot chocolate, tea, and juice complimentary 24/7). Breakfast is also complimentary in this hotel. However, they don't exactly have room service. A nearby restaurant provides room service (but only from their menu), and they do not serve breakfast in your room. You must go to the lobby for the breakfast. Not really an inconvenience, just a heads up if you like breakfast in your room as we were hoping to do. Valet parking is $42/night; but we were able to park there beyond the check-out time the next day, which was nice. For the price, it's hard to find a better hotel in the loop.

“Spacious” Our family of five just returned from a four night stay at the Salisbury Hotel. We were extremely pleased! Our rate was $379 per night. The total taxes per night was $58.19. We arrived around 9:00 AM on a Saturday. A doorman helped us unload luggage from the taxi. We were expecting to be able to check our bags and return later to check in; however, the front desk checked us in immediately. A bell hop took our bags up within five minutes of our arrival in the room. I purposely did not request a room in the back, because I actually wanted to hear NYC. We stayed in room 1404. I chose this hotel because I wanted something with NYC character. These rooms certainly have that. They look as though they were once apartments. There were exposed beams in the ceiling, furnaces under the windows, old doors, and molding. I loved the charm! Immediately upon entering there was a small table and two chairs on one side and a small kitchenette on the other. In the kitchenette there was a small fridge, a microwave, a bar sink, and a coffee maker. Just past this area there was a spacious coat closet. In the living room area there was a writing desk with chair, a pull-out sofa, end tables, a coffee table, three chairs, and a TV in an armoire with three drawers. The sofa and upholstered chairs were old, but not dirty. One great feature was the door between the living room and bedroom. This allowed us to have two TV's going at once. In the bedroom, there were two very comfortable beds with plenty of pillows. The bedding was old hotel style. There was also a large dresser with six drawers, two chairs, a TV, two luggage racks, and a spacious closet with mirrored door. In the small hallway to the bathroom, there were closets on either side. In one closet, there was an ironing board and iron. All four closets had hangers. The bathroom was small, like you would expect to find in an older apartment. The plumbing worked great. There was a small basket of spa-like bath products. There was also a hair dryer. There were old furnaces in both rooms and they definitely worked! We turned on the two window A/C units each night, because the rooms were too warm for us. Because this is such an old building, there is no individual control for the heat. The rooms were clean and spacious. We tipped the maid service $2 each day. We also left a note to ask for extra towels one day and they left extras each day. They replinshed the bath products each day. Each morning, a voucher was placed underneath our door for the continental breakfast. Our charge was $4 per person per day. 5 and under is free. Breakfast began at 7:00 AM. We were there close to 7:00 the first three days and there were two or three other families in there at that time. The dining room is spacious and in the front of the building, so there are plenty of windows. The food was great. There was a large selection of pastries and bagels and muffins and fresh white and whole wheat bread (in bread sacks that indicated they were from a local bakery). There were two kinds of cereal (no kid cereal), boiled eggs, two kinds of milk, three types of juices, and coffee. A couple of days there was a large bowl of fruit salad. On the days with no fruit salad, it would have been nice to have bananas and apples. The coffee, bagels, and fresh bread were wonderful! On the last day, we didn't arrive for breakfast until around 9:00. The dining room was almost full, but still no waiting in line. The dining room attendants were polite and helpful. There were two elevators. They were a little slow, but no real delay. I believe there were 18 floors in the hotel. There were two computers in the lobby. I used them twice and paid $3.95 for 15 minutes of Internet usage. It was quick and easy with a credit card. I printed five pages of boarding passes with no additional charge. Another great thing about this hotel was the location. Two blocks south of Central Park was perfect for us. There are subway stations on each corner. We did use these to go across town; however, we walked to Carnegie Deli, FAO, the Met, Times Square, Radio City Music Hall, and Rockefeller Center. We walked at night and felt perfectly safe. Close by were a Duane Reed drugstore, a brick oven pizza restaurant, bakeries, a Star Bucks, and a Jekyll and Hyde restaurant. Across the street is the Director's Guild of America Theatre. One afternoon we saw a crowd gathering and stopped to watch. There were barricades set up, an extra awning, red carpet, and a backdrop with Target logos. This was the premier for Mr. Magorium's Emporium, and we saw Dustin Hoffman and Natalie Portman arrive and walk the red carpet. It was amazing to see the difference in the number of flash bulbs going off for these two celebrities as opposed to the other cast members. Check out was quick and easy. When departing from the hotel, the doorman hailed a taxi for us and assisted us in loading our luggage. I would definitely stay here again!

“Pleasantly surprised overall” We usually stay in Downtown Boston but we’d arrived at Logan late and were off to Vermont the next day, so picked the Embassy Suites for its proximity to the airport and the free shuttle. Except we didn’t realise we had to call for it and spent a long time hovering around the shuttle departure bay before phoning the hotel. The receptionist had never heard of Swiss (the national airline of Switzerland) but after repeating the terminal number and our carrier’s name a few times we finally got our message through. Not the best of starts. The building, when we finally reached it, was rather nondescript (the street we pulled up in was dark and deserted and we wondered what we’d let ourselves in for) as was the lobby, but the receptionist who served us was efficient and courteous and we were soon on our way to the room which was a pleasant surprise - well appointed (though we didn’t really need two flat screen TVs), spacious, clean and quiet, located as it was at the end of a corridor, far from the lift (very far it seemed with our four big cases and two sets of hand luggage). We had requested a king bed but got two queens instead. We decided against asking for a different room and headed for the Porter Grill and Bar where we had a very average tuna salad and a slightly better chowder and something else which can’t have been good or I’d have remembered it. We slept well however (which is after all the most important thing in a hotel, or should be) and heard nothing despite the jet lag and proximity to Logan airport. Breakfast was complimentary, copious, varied, balanced (fresh fruit salad is a big plus in my book) and very good. There was even a chef on hand to prepare made-to-order omelettes and there were plenty of free tables to choose from despite the warnings of possible crowds and delays. Things got better when we decided to nip into downtown Boston, asked for a late check-out (and were granted one) and discovered that it really was a short walk to the subway (the park does shut, so best to find out when exactly or you might be in for a long detour) and a very convenient train ride into town which spared us the prohibitive parking costs. When we returned to the hotel we discovered our electronic keys were no longer functioning as the receptionist had forgotten to reprogram them for our late check-out but all was set right in the end. All in all we were pleasantly surprised. The youth and inexperience of the receptionists we encountered was a small price to pay for an excellent night’s sleep in a very conveniently located hotel for a very reasonable price. We’d definitely stay here again. To sum up - pros: spacious, clean room; comfortable bed; quiet (at least when we were there); excellent sleep; location near the subway and airport; pleasant staff; reasonable price; good complimentary breakfast. Cons: shuttle could be more efficient; dated lobby; inexperienced staff; and it would be nice if hotels honoured customer reservation requests but this seems to be the norm rather than the exception in most establishments.

“Bring a Sense of Humor” Read the reviews. All true. The good: Great location right at Lincoln Center. Asked for and was cheerfully given an upgrade. Had a king room with two windows. Lobby has hip vibe. The not-so-good: Our upgraded room had about 2 feet on either side of the bed and about 1 foot to clear the end of the bed. Can't imagine what the original room looked like. I'm 5' tall and my knees touched the wall when using the loo. Absolutely no room for anything. You better be very good friends with your roommate as you can lay in bed and watch them showering and doing all their bathroom chores through the glass wall and sheer curtain. Halls are dark and not as clean as they ought to be. And yes, it's noisy and drafty. Priceline lists this as a 3-1/2 star hotel. I'd give it 2 stars. You can do better.

“Outstanding Service” I spent two nights recently at the Hyatt Regency in Austin, and I was quite impressed by the fantastic service given throughout my visit. First, the hotel was incredibly busy, but check-in was fast and efficient. My initial room was on the third floor, and I noticed there was an odd odor coming from the plumbing. One quick call (actually to just ask for someone to look at it while I was out), and I was immediately upgraded to a nice city-view room on the ninth floor. The room itself was spotlessly clean and well-maintained. The beds were beyond comfortable, and the internet was fast and reliable. Best of all, despite the 110+ heat outside, the room was cool and comfortable. The staff at the bar just off the lobby was beyond friendly and polite. And, the Sauvignon Blanc was spectacular! I did notice a bit of noise from a party in the atrium Saturday night, but Sunday was calm and quiet. Now, the best part - one of the managers apparently heard that I had to change rooms due to the maintenance issue and personally called me. Having worked in management for several large hotels in Nevada, I know these things happen, and I personally dismissed it. She, however, went far above and beyond anything I could have ever expected to ensure I was happy. I wish I could remember her name - she is a great example of outstanding, guest-obsessed service. And, for that, I'll be sure to return (in fact, I'll be back in a few weeks!).

“Centrally Located Hotel” I loved the location of this hotel. It is centrally located in an exceptionally walkable section of Philadelphia. Upon check-in, I was given a room in Headhouse Tower. The room was exceptionally spacious and well-appointed. It's a good thing I don't mind the hike from the main hotel entrance to Headhouse Tower, however, as it is a bit of a walk. For me, I appreciated being away from the main bustle of the hotel. I love the fact that this hotel has an on-site Starbucks and FedEx Office as these are key elements for business travelers like myself. Security was adequate inside the hotel and they were even diligent about trying to keep the immediate outside area clear of vagrants. I never felt threatened or uncomfortable while staying at this hotel. My only complaint is that on two days, my room had not yet been cleaned when I returned to it at 5pm after being out since 8am. I would definitely stay at this hotel in the future.

“Is this a safe location?” Well, I guess the security guard at night and the numerous security cameras should give you a sense of security but I do not recommend this place for families. If you cannot park directly in front of the hotel, you end up parking on the side of the building which is under the interstate. There's plenty of homeless nearby too. The hotel is new...it opened in October 2008. So if you are only concerned with the rooms and cleanliness then I definitely recommend this hotel. It also has nice flat screen tvs. The breakfast bar was average. The pool and hot tub are outside and there's a small putting green outside too. The exercise room is set up wierd...the exercise equipment--one elliptical and one treadmill do not face the tv. Speaking of below average value...The laundry costs $2.50 for the washer and $2.00 for the dryer. No free hotel shuttle unlike other hotels nearby and parking is $10 a night. Overall, I probably won't stay here again unless Choice Hotels is running another promotion.
“Older hotel...” Older hotel. The showere head was loose, There was some water damage from the leaky window. The carpet had a stain and there was an odor in the hallways. Not worth the $200.

“Apparently we stayed at the 2 star tower of a 4 star hotel. Who rates these places?” First let me say, I try not to be too critical, but in some cases the truth is warranted! We checked in and things seemed fine. Location was excellent. Woke up the first morning, to a slightly rumpled bed covered in "stains", I hope-filthy and not 4 star hotel quality. Requested a linen change and heard a knock on the door- a gentleman was there to let me know if I wanted it done to take off the privacy sign, I did and no one even came until later in the day. The room was big enough, had no drawers, suposedly remodeled but carpet didn't reach the wall, toilet paper holder fell off constantly and shower head was broken. The mirrors were great and the water was always hot! The walls were paper thin, I heard every conversation the guests next door had. They were not noisy but you could hear everything including the t.v. through the walls and vents. Internet was $13.00, worked for a bit and then not again, I called customer service and spent 25 minutes on the phone and they asked if they could work on resetting the system and call back later. The hotel did give us a credit for the charges. At this point, enough was enough, we packed our bags and checked out. The front desk was very helpful- kudos to Rocco for caring and being the only friendly staff we saw other than the bell hops!!

“Not bad” This is an older property that needs some freshening, but if you find a killer deal then it is well worth it's cost. It is so close to the Medical center and all the major thoroughfares that one can get to anywhere in Houston relatively easy. Our room was clean and comfortable. It was your standard Residence Inn-small kitchen, sitting area, no frills bathroom. The sheets and towels were soft, the bed was comfortable. The carpet was stained and worn looking, but looked otherwise clean. There were water stains on the ceiling above our bed, and the ceiling creaked and groaned while we were trying to sleep from the people above us. There was also a colony of strange small flies populating the room that seemed to emanate from the water heater closet. But bugs don't really bother me much, so it didn't disturb me. The free wifi was nice, and they serve a hot breakfast for free every morning. I would stay here again.

“Avoid the rooms facing the parking lot” Overall, this was a very nice hotel. The staff were very friendly and the gym is the YMCA that is connected by a walkway and elevator to the hotel. The room was functional. Unfortunately, the suites are at the end of the hall and are next to a public parking lot. When the W hotel's bar closes, the partying begins. Car stereos were blasting and generally, a boisterous crowd is having a bunch of fun. Unfortunately, that translates to interrupted sleep. I had read the reviews about this in the previous posts, but even ear plugs were not enough to muffle the sounds. Otherwise, I really liked the hotel. The location is fantastic. It's easy to get around from here. I would stay again, but definitely in a room away from the parking lot.

“Charming Downtown Boutique” The Madison is an interesting boutique hotel in downtown Memphis. Built in an old bank building, the hotel utilized the vault as it's gym. The lobby has a grand staircase, and the rooms are large and comfortable. Additionally, the bathrooms are very nice (which my wife really appreciated.) The service was good, not great, and the location was pretty good for access to Memphis' street cars. If you are traveling to Memphis and want upscale accomodations without the Peabody price, the Madison is a great alternative.

“Good sleep at Sleep Inn” I slept good, parking area felt clean and safe, check in was friendly carpets modern and furnishings nice and seemed new. Now for my grips, none very serious. Main grip was shower, head was to my neck (short), very short and water pressure very bad, took about 2 min to get hot water so while you wait cold water is splashing on you. might be smart to turn on water, use stool, then when done will be warm. Also room is very small, there are a few a bit bigger but most are tiny. Also lots of airplane noise but was tired and able to sleep well. If traveling alone and goal is sleep good choice, if with more than yourself it will be tough to move about the room. Also breakfast was not terific, yet on par with other freebreakfast places. Mostly annoyed how small breakfast area was. There was about 5 people in breakfast area and it felt shoulder to shoulder, but hey, its free, if you don't like it skip it.Overall better than expected for price paid. I think the Patel family runs this hotel and most hotels run by the Patel family cut lots of corners as do most Choice hotels. This hotel really isn't that bad and didn't cut cost that affect service and would stay here again if needed.

“Great hotel right on the Riverwalk!” This was our first visit to San Antonio. We wanted to stay somewhere within walking distance of the Alamo. This hotel was right off the Riverwalk & was a quick & easy walk to the Alamo. We asked for an upper floor with a view, and they put us on the 20th floor. Old style room, but very clean. It had a ceiling fan in addition to the A/C. The shower head was very powerful (appeared to be an adjustable flow type, but didn't work). Enjoyed the kickback food in the evening & the breakfast in the morning. We were excited about the rooftop pool & waited until 9:30 PM (pool closed at 10:00), both to be up there at night & also to avoid some of the kids. Turns out the kids were there at all hours (very loud & hard to find some place without splashing), so we didn't stay long. Overall a very good experience. We'd go back.

“Ottima posizione e ottimo prezzo (senza fronzoli)” Questo hotel molto semplice e' situato su Sutter Street, a due passi (5 min a piedi) da Union Square e dalla fermata del cable car per il Fisherman's Wharf. A 10 min. a piedi si trovano Market street, la fermata del tram F. Le STANZE sono piccole e modeste ma assolutamente pulite e adatte a un soggiorno di pochi giorni. La nostra (con due letti singoli) era al quinto piano e dava sull'interno e la finestra aveva una pessima vista-muro ma era tranquilla. L'albergo ha un generale "stile inglese" del milleottocento ma e' pulito. I primi due piani stanno subendo una ristrutturazione ma i rumori dei lavori iniziano solo dopo le 8 di mattina. COLAZIONE: inclusa nel prezzo e comprende di tutto: donuts, muffins, succhi di frutta, cereali, yoghurt, caffe, the, marmellata. Ottimo affare. INTERNET: non e' disponibile internet wireless nelle camere, ne' gratis ne' a pagamento. Non e' disponibile neppure una presa ethernet nelle camere. E' invece disponibile una rete gratuita wireless nella lobby oltre ad una postazione PC in un mini salottino da cui e' anche possibile stampare (a pagamento). PARCHEGGIO: nota dolente. Non esiste parcheggio gratuito, potete provare a cercare parcheggio pubblico nella zona ma e' molto difficile e con il lavaggio strade dovreste spostare l'auto ogni sera. E' disponibile un valet service che per 24 dollari a notte (+ 3,5 dollari ogni volta che volete spostare l'auto) vi garantisce la custodia completa dell'auto e la sua consegna in 15-20 minuti dal momento in cui lo chiedete al banco reception. PERSONALE: tutto molto cortese, dalla reception alle donne delle pulizie. Hotel da consigliare, soprattutto se per un breve soggiorno di vacanza. Noi abbiamo prenotato su Orbitz.com trovando una tariffa molto piu' conveniente rispetto a quella pubblicata sul sito dell'albergo.

“Stay Away-- Poor Value and Not a "Real" MO” I would rate this as one of the worst (supposed) 5 star hotels I have stayed at. There were several problems during my stay (see below), but above all, the hotel simply has none of the Mandarin Oriental "vibe" which makes the chain special. Except for a few asian themed pieces of furniture, and some asian menu items, it could be labeled "Sheraton" and cost $200 less a night and you would never know the difference. This hotel, unlike other Mandarin properties I have been to, has no soul. The location is very strange, as others have remarked. The hotel is really isolated among several non-descript office complexes. If it were a stand alone resort with interesting places to lounge it would be one thing-- but all that there is to the common areas of the hotel is a small, simple lobby and conference space. Service was very spotty in many respects. Multiple calls to house keeping were needed for nightly turn-down service (and other very simple requests). TV and internet hookups in the rooms were overly-complex and did not work properly. (I had to be moved to a second room after even the hotel's engineer could not figure out how to use the internet service (which they charge about $15 a day for by the way). (P.S. Inever was able to get the volume to work on the flat screen in the living room of my suite). The water view, which they charge a premium for, is not really a water view. It is more of a marsh the size of a football field (barely). But, I suppose it is better than the city view, which is of non-descript office buildings. Also, for a 3 year old property, it was in very poor conditions. Marks on the walls of the halls ways, damaged furniture etc. Not what you would expect to see at this type of property. Save the money and stay at a sheraton or Hilton, of stay at a real 5 star property.

“Gut und günstig in Hollywood und mitten drin” Das Hollywood Best Inn liegt an einer Querstraße zum Hollywood Boulevard und man kann den Walk of Fame in 5 Minuten erreichen. Persönlich hat uns die Stadt nicht gefallen, jedoch kann man das Hotel für wenig Geld und guter Sauberkeit in zentraler Nähe weiterempfehlen. Parkplatz im Hof vor den Zimmern. Frühstück gibt es Kaffee und Donuts. Wir waren schon ein paar Tage in den Staaten unterwegs und haben wir uns an das eher karge Frühstück gewöhnt und dann unterwegs immer gegessen. Man bekommt ja hier an jeder Ecke was. Die Zimmer waren geräumig mit Kühlschrank und Fernseher.Für Hollywood kann ich das nur empfehlen.

“The SLS Receives My Nod for Best Hotel” I travel to Los Angeles two to three times a year for work and I typically stay at the W Hollywood Hotel. I decided for my next five-night trip that it was mandatory that I stay somewhere else (the W Hollywood is unbearable after two nights). After some research and a reasonable rate negotiated by my employer’s travel agent, I decided on the SLS Hotel at Beverly Hills, a hotel of The Luxury Collection by Starwood. The SLS is located on La Cienega Boulevard, near the behemoth shopping center - the Beverly Center. Upon arrival, I was warmly greeted by the valet attendants and quickly entered the outdoor lobby, which is quite striking (i.e. crystal-like deer heads). The lobby, although dark, is nicely appointed with animal sculptures that double as lighting fixtures. Don’t be alarmed when you get into the elevator. The well-dressed people staring at you when you get on the elevators are only pictures but will require a double take because of their life-sized appearance. I stayed on the fifth floor in a Premier King room facing La Cienega where I could hear the hum of cars whizzing by the hotel. The decorative room with its large windows, mirrored walls, and moody lighting made up for the noise. The bathroom has two sliding doors: one that peeks into the living area and another one, which connects into the small hallway. The Ciel products in the bathroom were refreshing and I made sure to stock up upon checkout. The gym, located on the 2nd floor near Ciel Spa, has enough equipment to conduct a full workout. Altitude, or what I call it, a “Super Chic Pool Deck,” is abundantly staffed with affable waiters including a guy named Alex. What makes this hotel so amazing is its stellar approach to customer service. Everyone from the valet guys to the front desk attendants exude niceness. The SLS or “See Life Sideways,” according to its marketing materials, isn’t cheap (I dinned on a $40 dollar breakfast consisting of a pressed croissant and juice) but its well worth the price.

“Great Stay” Great hotel in a good area. I have business at Ohio State University Medical Center and it is very convenient. The room was very clean, room service was good. Great cookies at the front desk when you check in:) Staff was very helpful. Will continue to stay here when I travel to the area.

“Horrible” Booked a room a month in a advance with two double beds. Once we got there they said they only had rooms with king beds left and all they could say was "sorry." What's the point of a reservation?

“Safe choice in Chelsea” This Hampton Inn is predictably like most Hampton Inns - clean, safe, helpful staff, no restaurant, nice breakfast included, rather rigid about checkin times, etc. The Hampton Inn on 24th is almost a clone of the one on 34th near Madison Square Garden. Great location in Chelsea in easy walking distance from flower district, many nice restaurants, High Line, etc.

“Hotel d'aéroport...” Pour une nuit de transit à 10mn en voiture de l'aéroport O'hare! La chambre que nous avons eu était très confortable, une literie excellente. Un bar restaurant est disponible. Personnel de l'hôtel moyen.

“Housekeeping Removed Items from Our Room” We have stayed at this hotel prior to our stay last night. We liked it before. Very convenient location, clean rooms, and a Stabucks right in the lobby. We came into town again for an annual Christmas Parade and we really disappointed this time. We had called the Front Desk to request a late check out and we were granted a 1:00pm check out. That was perfect. No need to really rush when we wanted to enjoy the parade that went by the hotel at 11:00am. We started packing up our belongings and taking things here and there down to our car. We placed a "Do Not Disturb" sign on our door knob as we were packing up our room. When we came back to our room we found our refrigerator completely empty. The room was clean with the bed made and new toiletries in the bathroom. It was very clear Housekeeping had been in our room - why???? We had the "Do Not Disturb" sign on our door and a late checkout time. The housekeeper took our children's milk and our adult beverages. That was over $40 stolen from our room that we still had until 1:00pm. We immediately called the front desk and they had us wait in our room for the manager to come by - no one came by! We had to go down to the front desk and when we asked four different employees where are missing items were we were told "I don't know." This was more upsetting. We were compensated with $4 from Petty Cash. The milk items purchased from Starbucks cost well over $4. A lady finally returned some of our adult beverages. We left the hotel still angry and frustrated. A whole lot more should have been said and done from the Hotel Management.

“It's not dingy but it's not luxurious.” The bathrooms are old and outdated. The rooms are spacious if awkward. The view (we had a river view) is very nice. The gym is well equipped. The location is good. The lobby is modern and the staff is welcoming. No minibar/fridge, 2 glasses in the bathroom, but free Keurig coffee in the room. The free wireless internet is slow. Considering the options for hotels in Chicago, this may not be the best value depending on the time or other places available. Would not stay here again.

“Loved it! Very surprised for my last minute weekend getaway!” Stayed here for a quick very last minute weekend rendezvous and the hotel was perfect. The room was beautiful and spacious for the two of us, and very clean. Ismail at the Front Desk was very helpful! The parking structure was a little confusing, but pay close attention and you'll be fine. It is >$30 a night so plan when you're figuring out your cost. The location was convenient and we enjoyed the closeness to eveything. I will be back!!

“Large rooms” This is a nice place to stay, especially if you are going to be staying awhile and new a kitchenette. The location is decent, about half a mile from the downtown bar area and driveable to all the rest of the major sites. The rooms are quite large with a big living room area, seperate shower/tub and seperate bedroom area. Check-in was fast and friendly. The cost is high but you get a big room. One major cost factor is the parking- $30 a night for valet ($26 for self parking) which is high but relatively on par with similar hotels in the area. I would recommend this hotel and would stay here again but if you are looking for a "happening area at night" be warned, the area immediately around this area was dead at night.

“Worked fine for us...” This was our first stop on a 2 week road trip. We love Hampton inn's and especially the most-excellent Hilton Honors program. Do yourself a favor and join. That said, this stay was a reward night, and fine for our needs. The room was clean, as was the entire hotel. No surprises at check-in. The pool area was clean. The wifi worked fine. This is in the Castleton (N.E. Indy) area, which is a great for shopping and dining. It's a safe area and we've never had problems walking the streets at all hours. There is a lot of traffic, however. The free breakfast was typical Hampton Inn (good enough for us). I would definitely stay here again.

“Good location + Rooms but expensive?” Good location, can't fault the staff or rooms If you're on a budget though there are probably other hotels that will suffice but if you want luxury this will do you fine

“Cherry on the cake that was NYC” My husband an I fell head over heals in love with NYC. We were here for a week and we are ready to spend the rest of our lives there! Staying at the Grand Hyatt made the stay just that extra special. We were treated like royalty by the staff, it was so great to walk in from the hussle and bussle of the busy streets into our wonderful hotel. The check-in was super friendly, it was our anniversary while we were in NYC, which was not written anywhere, but the lovely check-in lady asked if we were here for a special occasion. Low and behold when we got back to our room from our first day out, there was a cake and champaigne and a handwritten card from the staff. Very special! The rooms are clean and nice. The hotel is a bit older (but this just means that they are quality built and you don't hear your neighbours or the street below). The decorations and everything was new however!
