Nice lobby and breakfast was delicious too. Loved staying here!!! - would have been nice to have free wifi

“Things aren't always what they seem!” I am very disapointed in my stay at The Westin, especially considering the price I paid. Several things were not up to par. Housekeeping never showed up and when I called at 530 pm to check on why my room had not been serviced yet, I was told housekeeping was still making their rounds. At that time of day, I would expect my bed to already be made. And beware, staying here when there are nearby concerts or Beale st activites. My husband and I had to stand in line to use the elevator to get to our room, with the hotel full of intoxicated people, yelling, one man even hollering for marijuana, all this right in the lobby of a Westin. Not what I would expect of a luxury hotel. Will never stay here again.

“What can I say, revisiting the place I was engaged” The Fairmont San Jose is a wonderful place for a vacation or business trip. I returned for a business trip 6 years after proposing to my wife in a wonderful suite there, so even though I may have bias towards this hotel, I felt compelled to do a review. Was on business in January in Palo Alto, normally stay in the Four Seasons, but it was booked and a really cheap corporate rate $164 per night was available. Checkin was great, friendly service, food was great. Couple of tips: Bijan--great bakery across the street. Avoid the pricey hotel breakfast and if you want to stay there, opt for the coffee bar in the hotel lobby, they serve breakfast items...got a egg sandwich and juice for $6, unheard of for a luxury hotel. Parking is expensive at $26 per day, if you have a hybrid vehcile it is half of that. Valet parking do allow 10-20 minutes to get your car especially if the hotel is busy.

“A pleasant stay” Booked through Priceline for 80 all inclusive. Check in was very friendly and attentive, with a smile. The location is great for anyone into baseball and football, as it is in walking distance to both stadiums. The building is an ugly 1970s structure which pales in front of the Hilton in front. The room was ample although I was given a room with a view on the back of the building. The king bed was very comfortable, with again a LCD TV. The work station is kind of awkward, with very little place to put a laptop. Internet connection is around 12$. The bathroom is large and well supplied. The restaurant in the hotel is typically expensive, but there is not much in terms of places for breakfast...I wouldn't try that greasy spoon next to the strip joint. It is close to the Wharf Rat, if you want a good beer. The gym is well equipped, however the pool is smallish and claustrophobic. Overall, enjoyed my stay.

“Great room, BAD service” I begin by stating that the minute we walked into the lobby I told the receptionist that I we had to be at a dinner whom reservations we might loose if we weren't in and out of the hotel within an hour. This would be an extraordinary feat considering we were driving to downtown San Diego from the hotel which is about 5 miles away and we were not dressed for the occasion. The somewhat friendly receptionist smiled and stated that there were no room ready for us to be able to change in. The next available room would be in about 45 mins. To make things worse after 20 mins of back and forth of room guarantee's and the fact that they wanted us to desperately get a double bed we misunderstood him that he had a king available. So as he was handing the keys to us, I realized he had just mentioned that the room was 2 queen beds. I proceeded to give him the keys back and told him that if my now canceled reservation would charge me for not showing up to the dinner reservation then I will proceed to get his name and the name of his supervisor so that I can call corporate and file a complaint. The supervisor whom was right next to him told him that there were rooms available and proceeded to open a block of rooms whom had been available from the start. My head by that point was close to the boiling point for which I proceeded to just get the keys, run upstairs, get dressed and get to my dinner an hour 45 minutes late. This has to be the most incompetent hotel staff that I have ever encountered! I will make it a point to never stay at that hotel again.

“Love the Ritz, not sure if this is Ritz-quality” The location of the Ritz-Philadelphia is right in the heart of the city. It is within walking distance to the Terminal Market, and various restaurant and shops nearby. Outside, the property makes quite the statement with its roman columns. Kind of funny, but behind the property it looks like a 1-star hotel, all unfinished (ha, ha). Nice sized room, beautiful bathroom, cleanliness was 5 stars. Check in was very nice, too--I even received a cold towel to refresh my hands upon check-in. Some things I wish the hotel had: indoor pool (like the Ritz-San Francisco); double-paned windows (let's just say every driver in Philly uses their horn, and it doesn't matter what time it is); bigger room service menu (and the food is just average, unfortunately); and gift shop. I agree with other reviewers--the lobby area has been transformed into a Euro-chic type of bar-restaurant, and for some reason, this seems so awkward. Overall, I still love the Ritz, will return.

“Some things great....others poor” This is a difficult review because the level of service and amenities were so variable. This is not a 4 star hotel and I would not pay full price but it is worth a Hotwire or Priceline booking. Positives: Great conference facilities and food service, free fast internet (wireless and wired in rooms), good location for medical school meetings. Not a terrible location for the museums and stadium when the weather is nice and if you enjoy walking. Not so positive: Almost $20 per day parking charges are a total rip-off for a location more than a mile from downtown. You can park for $5 per day around the corner in the medical building underground parking garage. Negative: The front desk supervisor should find a different career field. She was extremely rude and unhelpful. She acted as if people at her desk were imposing on her time. In contrast, the other front desk staff members I spoke to were pretty good once they warmed up. I think that supervisor creates a poor workplace environment and they all suffer as a result. No doubt that she affected my overall rating as well.

“Nice bar and cute doggy” According to the locals, this is a great location in Dallas. Nice hotel, comfortable rooms, got one with a balcony which was a plus. Nice bar, nice restaurant, nice people. Especially the doggy in reception! Interesting mix of stuff in the mini bar! To get free internet use, you need to sign up as a lumen hotel member which also gives you a free pick in the mini bar. Nice touch.

“Great location, average everything else” I stayed here two nights with my husband for a conference. The hotel is ideally situated in the middle of the Texas Medical Center and is a great location for access to the hospitals and clinics and Rice University. Location-wise, I don't think you could do better than this if you needed access to most areas of the medical center. It's also in a good central location that is convenient to some of the nicer areas of central Houston, and the Houston MetroRail, for all it's worth, has a stop just across the street from the front door. The self-parking situation was difficult to figure out and the garage is a bit distant from the hotel, though not inconvenient. Had we needed in and out privileges, however, we would have been disappointed to pay the garage fee with every exit. Consider alternatives to this parking garage if you need to leave and come back often during your stay. The check-in process was smooth and we had no problems finding our room. On entering the room, we were greeted with stale, musty, mildew-y air that was not resolved with changing the room temperature. The thick, somewhat ugly carpet felt almost damp when walking on it in bare feet, and we occasionally heard dripping sounds from the air conditioning unit. The room itself was reasonably well appointed but small, and I have stayed in far nicer rooms for less than these rates. The beds were soft and comfortable, and the lighting in the room was fine (though perhaps a bit on the low side for people who like a lot of light). The bathroom was adequate, though small and dated. The shower head - the large round rain-shower type - was a nice touch, however. After my husband left early in the morning for his conference, I ate alone in one of the hotel's restaurants for breakfast. After scanning the menu I decided that the $15 buffet was the only thing approaching a reasonable value. I know overpriced food is ubiquitous among hotels, but come on! The service and food quality was average; having had a pretty good breakfast at a Marriott hotel in Atlanta I was not impressed with this one. On the morning of our departure, I took a dip in the indoor pool, which was small and warm-ish but fine for the purpose. The pool area is adjacent to the fitness center, and as expected there were plenty of towels for the guests. There is also a hot tub that looked to have equipment to accommodate guests with mobility impairments, but I didn't check out the hot tub more closely. Finally, check out! Check out was a little slow on a Sunday morning as there was one staff person helping guests who had some sort of issue with their bill. After waiting several minutes with no apparent acknowledgment, another staff person appeared and helped me with check out - she was very friendly! All in all, this hotel was just OK when you factor location out of the equation. I'm glad someone else paid for our stay because the rates I saw online were outrageous relative to the very average level of comfort and room quality. Ours was not a bad experience, but I would NEVER pay more than, say, $150 a night to stay here, no matter how close I needed to be to the medical center. Even then, I'd look for something nicer and a bit more modern.

“Very comfy for overnight stays in Philly” The hotel looks a little daggy on the outside and the decor is a little dated, but for an overnight stay it's ideal. We stayed here overnight on the way to Washington after flying into NYC earlier in the evening. The king bed was very comfy and the bathroom was a decent size. A few minor complaints: Car park seemed very dodgy, air con was too loud to sleep with, and the pool outside the balcony created a fair bit of noise in the morning with children swimming which isn't the best post-jetlag wake up call! All in all though, hotel serves it purpose and it's only a 20 min drive to the old city to visit all the tourist sites.

“Perfectly Soho w/ Rooftop Lounge” The outside of this hotel has you feeling like your pulling up to your residence with the doorman awaiting your return. It’s a tall slim building. It’s located right next to one of Soho’s best Thai Restaurants Kitticha (?) It was my second time dining there and I recommend the Red Curry Sea Bass w/ side of vegetables. Checking into the hotel the staff was extremely friendly & informative. It was a Sunday so the hotel was a bit quiet. Plenty of seating in the window lined lobby that boast a brown and cream interior, very earthy. There is a restaurant off the lobby. After riding the elevator up to room 44, I was admiring the wood surrounding the hallways and the corridors leading to the few rooms that occupy each floor. This was one of the smaller rooms I stayed in but, the décor & comfortable luxury made up for that. No view but a spacious beautiful bathroom you want to spend more time in. The shower was very cool. Around 5pm the rooftop bar opens, a great place to come after you dined a Kittichai for a cocktail over looking the Empire State Building. The vast view with very little building makes you feel like you stepped outside the city; very pleasant. The décor is carried all the way upstairs and is elegant, sophisticated with a woodsy feel. I loved this space. Warning... if you plan on catching a cab to the airport arter 4pm “Forget-a-bout-it”, I waited 40 minutes for a cab, then decided it was too late to catch my flight. Now the bellman stood out in the rain that long trying to hail a cab. A few car services came by but they will charge you between $75 and up when the far is only $45. The hotel offers a car service for $115 that includes all tolls & tips if you can afford that. I love the location of this hotel, it was 4 walking blocks to Trump Soho & it’s also right around the corner from my new favorite pizza place: “Bens”. You must get a slice here, perfection. There are so many shops to visit in this trendy, artsy area. I will definitely go back to this hotel. For you “Foursquare “ users, be sure to check in and show them you did. They offer a free room upgrade if you do. I paid about $175. (w/tax $240.). I booked this hotel from a company called Magellen Vacations. Because of this, I got a free room upgrade and or complimentary breakfast. I suggest calling them first because they always beat the hotels prices by at least $10-25. Plus they don’t charge a fee since the hotels give them referral fees. You have to call them because they don’t post prices on their website, it’s how they can keep the prices down. You will call them first on all your vacations, I do. They booked two hotels for me and when there is a problem with the bill, they take care of it right away for you.

“A great hotel if you don't mind taking the Metro” Location: The hotel is not really located in the central core of Washington DC. The area appears to be a very new business district, so everything has a new feel to it. However it is a 5-10min walk from the NY Ave metro station on the red line, which is 1 stop north from Union Station and also connects you directly to important metro stops such as Judiciary Sq, Chinatown, and Metro Center. There is a CVS pharmacy (not 24hr) and a great Harris Teeter supermarket very close to the hotel entrance. Area seemed safe despite earlier reviews. Lobby: A bit small, but clean. I think the doorman should be replaced, since he is not that helpful. He even walked away from the door when we were approaching. Check-in: Fast and effortless. We arrived around 1pm, and we were happy that the lady at check-in allowed us to have an early check-in. And she was friendly and offered a map of the city. Room: Big and clean! I was surprised by how good the room was. The decor is tasteful (pleasant shades of green), the furniture and hardware new and reliable. The bed was big, comfortable, and clean. Plenty of floor space. A desk and lounge chair by the floor-to-ceiling window looking out over the adjacent street. AC was working fine and reliable. TV was a flatscreen with plenty of channels. There is no ceiling lights in the main bedroom, so you have to turn on all the lamps and bedside lights if you want a more pleasant in-room ambiance. Bathroom was great! Clean and modern fixtures. Housekeeping was done everyday and was reliable. A great room. Check-out: Fast and problem free. Overall: A great value hotel, new and clean. Definitely much better than 3 stars. Only drawback is location, which is not a problem if you don't mind walking to metro and taking a 5-10min metro to get into central Washington DC.
“Great location” This hotel is centrally located, clean rooms and very well priced. We have stayed here about 3 different times over the past few months and think it is a great deal.

“立地最高なエコノミーホテル” 友人がパック旅行で泊まるので、それにあわせてこのホテルを利用した。ユニオンスクエアー地区の中心にあり、地下に駐車場(1泊32ドルとこの地区では格安)もあり、施設が古いがとにかく便利。部屋はまずまずだし、無線LANのインターネットも無料なので寝るだけなら充分なレベル。1階のレストランは料金は安くないが雰囲気もよいし、一定レベルの料理を出す。スタッフがいい対応をしてくれる。エコノミーなホテルでは及第点だろう。

“Very Nice. I would recommend” My husband and I spent one night at the Magnolia July 23rd. The staff was very friendly. The location is perfect if you plan on taking in some theater or maybe a show at the Toyaota Center. They even offer transportation. He had a suite. It was big comforatble and clean. My only small issue is that the TV could have used an update to a flat screen. RM 1901

“Basic hotel, perfectly functional” I stayed here for less than 12 hours (late check-in and early flight) with my boyfriend. We both really liked it. I had stayed at the Ace in Portland and been to the one in NYC. This is worlds apart, there's no hip bar or coffee place or really much of a lobby. The rooms were just right, nothing unnecessary, comfy beds, friendly staff. The neighborhood had some bums loitering around, but it wasn't super sketchy. I would stay here again.

“Good Price, Decent Place” I arrived at the Hilton Garden Inn around 7:00 PM on a Tuesday night for one night's stay. My first exposure to the hotel was an exceptionally nice, helpful desk clerk (LaShanna?) who went out of her way to ask how I was doing and direct me and others to restaurants in the area. I even called the manager the next morning to provide her with positive feedback about the desk clerk (unusual for me). The hotel had a big, airy lobby, and my room was quite large - maybe more suited for two double beds than one kingsize bed. The bed and shower were fine. I didn't use it, but was pleasantly surprised to find a restaurant available for dinner in the lobby area. They also served breakfast, but I don't believe it was complimentary. I found this hotel to be fine... kind of typical of the moderately priced chains springing up all over everywhere. Not great, but OK for me. I paid the Government rate of $100 per night.

“Good location but..” Stayed at this hotel for two night. Location is great. The standard rooms are tiny (was expecting this but did not realize quite how small.) and more suitable for 1. They do however contain everything that you would need although in my room the TV was not working & it was not as clean as I would have expected, I went to reception to complain & all issues were dealt with promptly. The bar is great and the restaurant nice - food is tasty and filling. For me, the hotel was quite good value but I found an internet deal.

“Convenient Location, New renovation” Stayed one week during a business trip. Very quick and easy to get to from Airport, although was slightly confusing to find initially because I thought it was still the Radisson (as was listed on all my confirmations). Close to Little Italy. Complete renovations inside, rooms very clean and nice.

“Good business hotel. Nothing more.” Spent 3 nights here on a recent business trip. The hotel was good, nothing out of ordinary. And w some hiccups. Good central location. Check-in was quick and smooth. Ample cab access as they are always waiting across the street. As Starwood member, I was on the 11th floor for members with gold status (or similar). When arrived in the room discovered cordless phone was not working properly, plus ironing board was screwed up. Apparently the attendant informed front desk not to use the room until fixed. So I get to the room and cleaning lady comes in surprised new guest staying there. So an hour or so after arrival, I was interrupted while someone came to fix the items. Fortunately was not in middle of work call or nap, etc.... but this is not a way to welcome a new guest. Room is clean and good bathroom, particularly shower. Morning breakfast room service was decent and efficient. Hallways, wood paneling, elevators all look a bit warn, scuffed, scratched and in need of some upkeep. One night tried to get a wakeup call and could noboday answered the phone. Exhausted, tired wanting to go to sleep, but I had to call back 3 times until someone answered wasting 15 minutes of my night and desire to sleep. Asked for change from front desk at one point to tip the bellman hailing taxi. She informed me she could not make change and go ask the bellman. Talk about odd and very awkward. Never experienced that before. Overall, the hotel is decent room, good location, but only OK service and need of upkeep and attention.

“Riverwalk at Christmas Time” Timeshare exchange, our first trip to San Antonio since husb in Army 1958! We had 1BR unit on top (7th) floor, looking down on rooftop across street. Located next to Landrys Seafood Rest (part of same bldg) on busiest part of RiverWalk; access to RW out front (College St) entrance, then walk around block and down stairs. Riverwalk beautiful with Christmas lights, busy with the little boats (and noisy that weekend with crazy football fans.) We had no problem with noise in our unit, which was plenty roomy for the 2 of us. Very nicely done with Southwest colors, glazed concrete floors except carpet in bedroom. Full size refrig, range burners, microwave, dishwasher, adequate dishes and utensils of good quality. Cabinets too high for me to reach. Hallway connected living room with smallish bedroom and past the nice big bathroom with lovely rustic decor (maybe too rustic; lights more for decoration than use. We bought a small shaving mirror. Euro style washer/dryer unit in bathroom. We had encountered one in London and knew that it would take about 4 hrs to do a load. Armoires with TV in 2 rooms, DVD in LR. Lobby decorated for Christmas. Computer available for guest use. Meet and greet one morning, coffee and donuts, mostly a stand-up gathering to meet other guests. All personnel including maid and porter were very friendly and accomodating. Towels changed on Tuesdays, trash taken daily, otherwise no maid service for timeshare guests. Not luxurious and roomy as some timeshare resorts, but we found it entirely satisfactory and a good restoration of an older building. Did not find lack of activities a drawback in an urban setting. Easy walk to Alamo and RiverCenter area, trolleys ($1) for tourist area easy to understand. Sightseer bus #7 to art museums, zoo, botanical garden, etc. We used SATRANS airport shuttle satisfactorily.

“Better than "Good" but could not give it "Great"” Stayed for two nights in June and overall it was better than good. Customer service is better than most SPG hotels. Had access to club lounge, which i think it a must. They serve drinks and small plates in the evenings which is nice but the space is kind of tight. Continental breakfast in the morning is decent. Its nice that its already included in the price. Nothing over-the-top fancy but still pretty good. Good place to get some bottled water and soda if needed. Location is great, first time in SA and the hotel was close to Alamo which was very cool. Also close to riverwalk but not too close that the noise gets to you. Ordered room service one night and it was good. Food was tasty but it took longer than expected for food to make its way to room. One thing that kind of confused me was that there were no safes in the room and the closet was super small, I mean smaller than a linen closet. So overall hotel is nice, service is good, but place needs some updating. Bathroom caulking starting to turn black and carpet looking a bit rundown. Would I stay here again? Yes b/c I can look past those things. Unless you are super picky you'll enjoy your stay overall as I did.

“Great staff, great location, average rooms.” My first trip to San Diego and the US Grant. An old world, historic hotel that is not my kind of thing but has a great location for a first tour. The staff is what makes this hotel great or better than average not the rooms. the staff here are very welcoming and make you feel welcomed, will try and do anything for you right from the valet to the front desk. I really like having good service and at the US Grant you get this. we were here on a Monday and Tuesday which weren't that busy but I simply hope that on the busier weekends the service doesn't alter. The rooms feel old and although large just don't have any "wow" factor. We were on the 6 floor and looked out over "Broadway". One thing to point out is that it seemed like a huge number of homeless people reside close to the US Grant and that end of town. As soon as you enter the street from the hotel the begging etc would start. it didn't seem as bad the closer you got to the water. Some nice restaurants are close. the valet charge of $32 per day I felt to be a little steep. I am not a US citizen and don't know if that is the norm. If you like service stay here if you like nice modern rooms with all the mod-cons keep looking. Still a nice stay. SPG points accrued at this hotel.

“Time for a makeover” I have been staying at this property since it first opened a decade ago. The first W to open in the city and it was a great place to stay. I expect properties to slowly start to become run down but then I expect the hotel to reinvest in their property and make sure the guest doesn't notice the aging of everything. This last trip, I could not wait to leave. The bedding has become so tattered that the sheets would no longer stay in tact on the mattress. I woke up every morning to find myself sleeping on a very dingy old mattress pad, the mattress as well was greying and had bad stains on it. The walls in the bathroom had collected years of debris from toothpaste to makeup to small bits of toilet paper. The air conditioning units leaked onto the carpeting. The carpets are worn. The TV is massive in the tiny rooms (I'm Platinum and they told me 200 SF was an upgrade) so you are constantly dodging the TV to go to the bathroom. They need to forget about 42" plasma TV's and make things more size appropriate for the space. The staff was great however. Breakfast was good every morning in the Heartbeat restaurant. The powers that be that decide when its time to spend money on updating - listen up, ITS TIME!

“It feels like home” This latest stay at the Omni was probably my 15th! Our company stays there each year for our spring conference. So I know the layout and the restaurants, which is comforting. It's an older property and the rooms are spacious - truly making it feel like I'm "home" at the end of the day. Staff are friendly, beds are comfortable, rooms are fairly quiet if you get one closer to the end of the hallway. The location is fantastic -- close to public transportation, the zoo, many wonderful restaurants. The area has many trees making it beautiful and relaxing. Roberts Restaurant features a daily morning and noontime buffet with good choices. Dinner options are excellent, well prepared. My leadership dinner was a huge success - starting with cocktails on the terrace, ending with superb service by private dining. The Omni still has the special touches for me!

“More Than Satisfied” My wife and I stayed at the Radisson LAX for one night after a long overseas flight. For an airport hotel it was clean, comfortable and affordable. It was also super convenient being probably the closest hotel to LAX. I would not hesitate to recommend it. Now if one wants something for a longer stay, I'm sure there are as good if not better properties further from the airport and more convenient to other So. Cal. attractions.

“Great Business Hotel” This was my first stay at this downtown LA hotel which I surprised how close it is to the Walt Disney Concert Hall. I will definitely consider staying here if attending an evening concert or event. I would rather stay at an Omni than the nearby Westin Bonaventure. Being a member of their free Select Guest program gets me fresh orange juice or coffee delivered to the door in the morning with the newspaper. I chose orange juice because they had a coffee maker in the room with decent coffee to use. The large flat screen TV was also a nice addition to an already nicely appointed and modern room.

“Wow!” I have stayed at a few different hotels in NYC for business and have to say that this is by far the best one I've stayed at. I was on the 38th floor and my room was so spacious and had a fantastic view. I had a rate that included breakfast, all I can say is that the breakfast was fantastic. I wish I had a bigger apetite because the food was plentiful. Bagels, eggs, bacon, pastries, fruits. The location is the best you can get, right in the heart of Times Square. A few downfalls, no bellhop service in the front to hail a cab (I think all major hotels need this) and the elevators are very slow. Other than that, great hotel. The beds are awesome!

“A Little Stuffy For My Taste, Great Price Though” I travelled to Washington DC at the beginning of to view the Solar Decathlon competition and to visit friends. I have been to DC over 10 times and have stayed at some other Starwood properties (W, Westin City Center and Four Points). This was my first time staying at the Fairfax and was mainly drawn to the property by its price ($127, a bargain and not a corporate rate), its proximity to Metrorail and the neighborhood (Dupont Circle / Embassy Row). Travel from DCA airport to the hotel via Metro took about 20-30 minutes and the hotel is two blocks away from the Dupont Metrorail station on the Red line (make sure to exit at the Dupont Circle NORTH / Q Street exit). When I arrived at the hotel, I was surprised at how small the lobby and check-in area was. There was a minor issue during the check-in process, as another guest with the same name was also staying at the hotel. This issue got resolved after a minute and I proceeded to my room. Be aware that there are a couple of steps to climb before you get to the elevator to get to the rooms. The hotel has employees to assist guests with getting luggage up the steps. Also at check-in, I received a pleasant hand-written note from the Business Travel manager at the hotel. When I arrived to my room, music was already playing, which was a nice touch. The room itself was a fair size and had great trim details on the ceiling, but the bathroom was quite small and will be mentioned later. The room faced Massachusetts Avenue, a semi-busy street with a bus stop near the hotel. I did not notice the traffic noise, but did hear the bus when it went by. While unpacking, I noticed baby carrots through the mini-bar, which piqued my interest. When I opened the mini-bar, I was surprised to also find blueberries and half of a rotisserie chicken, which were leftover from the previous guests. On my way out to meet up with friends, I informed the front desk of my mini-bar surprise. When I arrived back at the room, a few hours later, the mini-bar had been cleaned. The bathroom was quite small, with the toilet less than three inches from the side of the bathtub. I did not enjoy of the scent of the shampoo and conditioner provided by the hotel (which smelled like plastic to me). The bathroom did contain very plush and big towels. I attempted to use the Wi-Fi in the guest room, but had significant problems while trying to access it (it may have been related to another guest with the same name staying at the hotel?). The front desk was eventually able to get Wi-Fi working. The front desk was also able to accommodate a late check-out of 4PM (Note I have Gold SPG status and not sure if they normally accommodate a late check-out at 4PM) I did not use any of the dining or athletic facilities at the hotel. Dupont Circle, and neighboring Georgetown and Logan have many restaurants to chose from. There is also a Farmer's Market in Dupont on Sundays. I would say my stay at the Fairfax was average, but not sure if I would return again unless I was able to get a similar price of $127.

“That's a pity..” ...its stunning views and its prices deserve more. The hotel is not clean enough and it's a little too kitch, maybe (at least for me). The bar welcomes a great crowd at night, tough. Staff was ok. Just not warm. Quality of the things that you'll find in the rooms is for a 3 star hotel, not 4. Curtains were not working well and the moquette was very dirty. Too dusty place, even if I understand that all the light coming from the fantastic large windows can make the room look more dirty than it was...

“Can't go wrong with Madera” I've stayed at Madera several times and have always had a pleasant experience there. The location is conveniently located in the Dupont Circle area. The rooms are nicely decorated and appointed. My only slightly-negative comment is that the bathroom was a bit tight (Room 309). Other than that, everything else is great. You can book at Madera with confidence of a great stay.

“It's OK!” This relatively new hotel is in a relatively desolate area by the new airport, and as a result, it's easy to get lost. One cab driver from downtown Indy took me to the wrong hotel, while another had no idea where to go and insisted that I look up directions on my phone. Yikes. So make sure you know how to get back here yourself if you don't have a car. The hotel itself is comfortable, if without frills. The shuttle service from the airport is reliable, parking is plentiful, and if you do end up getting stuck at the hotel, the in-house restaurant is affordable and better than you might expect. Service was above-average, but you would never leave this hotel and think "I can't wait to get back!", which is more a function of its lot in life as opposed to anything wrong about the hotel itself.

“Great Family Resort” We enjoyed a very nice four night stay; a spur of the moment getaway from the Chicago cold. FH&R rate through AMEX got us a "Hill Country Suite" for $230/night. The room was about 800 sq ft- with a separate bedroom- small frig, dining table, sleeper sofa for our two kids (7 and 5). The room was reasonably nicely appointed. Strangely it was missing a few seemingly routine things: a luggage rack, an exhaust fan for the very small bathroom, clean glasses. Sorry; maybe I'm knitpicking. The most remarkable thing about this resort is the people. Everyone was incredibly friendly and helpful, from the front desk folks, concierge, valets, waitresses, maids, even the maintenance guys who were taking down the xmas displays in the lobby (they gave huge lollipops to our kids). I'm pretty picky but this place was unbelievable. What a fantastic staff! We got breakfast thrown in as part of the deal- they set up a huge buffet in the restaurant- absolutely perfect for the kids. It normally costs $16 bucks/person but our free breakfast coupons were accepted instead. What a deal. The downside was that they only had the buffet on two of the days since hotel occupancy was relatively low. A couple of the restaurants were closed, which forces you to go out- but that's good (see below)! The facilities were fantastic for the kids: a lazy river with a small sandy shore, multiple pools, hottub, bike trail (with free bikes), ping pong, a dedicated kids club. You can use the kids club for babysitting which we used one night so we could go out to dinner- they were great in that they didn't park our kids in front of the TV! There's a small "nature trail," along with a playground and sand volleyball court. Suffice to say, there's plenty for kids to do. The golf course looked great, although I didn't play it. I did take the kids out to hit balls on the range, which was a lot of fun. My wife went to the spa and gave it a passing grade, but she wasn't blown away. It was very expensive. The only real complaint I have is how overpriced everything is. I understand that I have to pay a premium for buying things on the resort grounds, but I think they take egregious advantage of you. Golf balls on the range, water in the store, a massage, etc. They really kill you. There is a gas station about 1 mile away, but other than that, there isn't anywhere convenient to walk to, to pick up small items. By the way, the resort is about a 20-25 min drive to downtown/alamo/riverwalk. That said, we had a fantastic time and would happily go back anytime. The weather wasn't perfect when we arrived, but it was in the 70s by the time we left. Can't miss restaurant: we are total foodies. The BEST meal we had was at La Fogata. This is a locals place (i.e., NOT on the riverwalk), and is something of an institution. Absolutely incredible. Do NOT miss the margaritas. Wow. It is out toward the airport- you can ask the concierge- they will know all about it.

“Would love to stay again” The Erwin is beachy, cool, and clubby. The front desk staff was pleasant, and when they found out it was our honeymoon (well, our honeymoon was ruined by United, but we were trying to salvage it) they offered us our choice of their two best remaining rooms. We chose the Sunrise, which was airy, pleasant, and had a nice balcony where we could see the ocean. The bar was upstairs, and we could hear the bass from the music, but they closed at 11pm that night, so it didn't bother us much. If you are sensitive to noise, ask to not be placed on the 6th floor. You'll be fine. We ordered some room service which was really good. Highly recommend the fish tacos and the burger. There were also some cute refreshments in the room for purchase, as well as sunnies in case you left yours at home. While we didn't enjoy the rooftop bar while we stayed there, I have been there before, and it is really great. The cocktails are tasty, and the view is unbeatable in Venice. Come as you are or dress up. It's chill but chic. Also, the sheets on the bed are really soft. Like, so soft that we pulled them up to look at the tag, and we now have them on our bed at home. Yeah, maybe we're weird, but they are amazing sheets! I look forward to my next stay at this quirky, boutique hotel. Just keep in mind, Venice is a bit grungy in places. If you're looking for fancy, try driving north a bit. :)

“Great Locationa and Service” The hotel is located in downtown Ft. Worth, directly across from the Ft. Worth Water Gardens and the convention center. While on the outer edge of the downtown area the hotel is still very convenient to shops and restaurants that you can either walk to if you don't mind a little exercise or using the free Molly Trolley which stops directly outside the hotel. The staff is very helpful and I received service above and beyond by Steven , one of the bell captains who has been working in Ft. Worth hotels for over 20 years. My room was clean and comfortable and with free wi-fi, a pretty good value as well. If I had one complaint it would be the lobby coffee shop which served up overpriced pastries and drinks, but that is pretty common amongst most hotels. If you are staying in Ft. Worth this property is definitely worth considering.

“Modern and clean” I liked the stylish modern decoration. The room was extra clean and spacious (we stayed in a suite). It is close to the airport but no noise at all. Breakfast was better than the regular hotel stuff. The city center was about 15min drive, so I can recommend it even if you would like to visit downtown.

“Good Deal for Manhattan” Didn't what to expect when I booked my stay at the Hotel Marrakech - in fact I had heard some not too great things prior to my visit. However after my weekend visit I will stay there again. The hotel/rooms were clean, staff polite and helpful, location was great, plenty of places to eat, subway a block away. The rooms are small but again for manhattan on a summer weekend in june you cannot beat the $ 100 rate plus tax (I booked through priceline). I would recommend this hotel for singles or couples..the rooms are small and would not accomodate families in one room. There are no elevators so ask for a low floor, if you are not good with climbing stairs - I stayed on the 2nd floor so it was perfect. Also the Internet was FREE, once in a while got disconnected but you can't beat the "freeness". Again i would stay here again..

“Great views!” Stayed for just one night, came over from the East Bay for a concert. I think our first Hilton experience, not bad at all. Comfortable and very clean room, actually a pretty good size standard king for the City. Yes, a big hotel and somewhat impersonal, but staff we dealt with were all very friendly and helpful. Check-in/out fast and courteous. Great views, with large windows that can be vented for fresh air. Very comfortable bed and linens, big HD TV with loads of channels, reasonably quite, modern furnishings and a general fresh feeling to the room. Reasonable AAA rate included buffet breakfast for two, a very good international spread at the Urban Tavern. We would definitely stay again for one our nights out across the bay.

“Really liked the hotel, but I had one concern” There are a few obvious things to note that others have also mentioned. Yes, they do have wonderful access to the airport. They also have a free shuttle to the airport. The good thing about this is that it can also serve as a shuttle to the CTA station. Yes, they do have a parking fee and internet fee (in the room). I never see a reason to charge a guest for parking in a parking lot instead of including it in the rate if you have enough room for all of your guests. With that said, a lot of places do it. My best guess is that they want to encourage you to not bring a car. I spoke with the manager on another subject, and he mentioned that their primary weekend business is weddings. That might be a reason to encourage not bringing a car (to make room for the wedding guests). It's also something to think about if you are staying the weekend. The midweek guests are mainly corporate travelers. Our package included parking, internet access, and access to the lounge. I really enjoyed this last amenity. The food was good, and the staff was great. All of the staff at the hotel was great. If you're looking for a place to spend a few weeks, this is a great choice. The fitness area and swimming pool were great too. I liked the rooms with one exception. I stayed 3 weeks, and 2 of my rooms had strange noises (I think it was the air conditioning). Several of my coworkers also mentioned this, but it sounded like their rooms were worse than mine. In the 2 rooms where I experienced this, it sounded like something was dripping or ticking in the wall. It was a very faint noise, but I felt like it kept me from getting a complete sleep at night. The other room that I stayed in was very quiet and did not have strange sounds.

“Loved it!” There is very little not to recommend about the Days Inn Chicago. Although not in the heart of downtown, the transport system in the Windy City is good enough that you are never far from anything either by bus or the 'L'. DIC is a matter of a few minutes walk from the Brown Line and only 20 minutes from downtown if you hit things spot on. The hotel itself is surrounded by bars, cafes, pubs and restaurants of varying nature and should really satsify just about every taste you could think of. The room I had on the second floor was very near the tiny lift, but I never heard it at all, and the hotel in general was quiet despite being obviously fairly busy during my three nights there. The beds, as another reviewer commented recently, were ultra comfortable and my only slight complaint, being tall and fairly stout, was that the toilet in the bathroom was very close to the wall and very uncomfortable to sit on properly. Facilities were, in general, superb and the breakfast was worthy of having every morning I was there. Plenty of choice and nothing ever seemed to run out. My only other observation - if you have a laptop and want to carry it with you when on holiday, then take it to the DIC - their public access computer is, frankly, hopeless and crashed every time I tried to use it after only a couple of minutes. But I am not going to let small details like those spoil what was an excellent stay in a quirky little hotel with excellent staff and comfortable rooms. I'll be back!!

“Good hotel, though a bit pricey” We stayed here, even with high prices (close to $300 for a regular room) because my wife was attending a conference there. The good: Very comfortable beds (my wife has grown to really like the beds in Hilton beds, which are not found in sister properties such as Double Tree or Hampton Inn). We got a room on the 19th floor with a great view of Telegraph Hill and San Francisco Bay (didn't mind time I had to spend on our PC since I had the great view). The restaurant was surprisingly good, especially the wild halibut and salmon. There are free PCs and you can have something printed at the concierge desk. The concierge was very helpful. When we had something faxed to us we were able to get it right away. The hotel is near public transportation. And close to several reasonably-priced restaurants in Chinatown. If you like Tai-Chi you can probably join groups in a plaza across the street. We walked to restaurants and shops on Market Street. Fairly short walk to the trolley that went to Fisherman's Wharf and a bus that went to the Golden Gate Bridge. Hotel is almost next door to the iconic Transamerica pyramid building (which has a small grove of redwoods, in case you can't make it to Muir Woods). It is a bit far from BART if you use that system to get to SFO or Oakland airport. The not-so-good: Wi-Fi is $10. The four elevators were woefully inadequate for a hotel of this size (they seem to be underghoing renovation, but unless the number of elevators is increased I don't see this avoiding delays up to several minutes or more at peak times). Parking costs, which we thankfully did not have to pay, are obscene. As mentioned, the room rates are high. The building is far from new and, frankly, rather ugly from the outside. The room was comfortable, though not large. Breakfast is not included in the rate (a Chinese restaurant next door has American breakfasts for about $4-5),

“Cheap hotel. Just for sleeping purpose only.” This is my first stay in Microtel's faciliity. Mmmmm, the price is cheap needless to say, but can find many minor points. I feel that Comfort Inn is still better. (1) Micorwave and refrigerator are not in the room. It is my small pleasure to have beer before sleeping but can't make it. (2) Breakfast is .... Don't know what to say. I don't like to eat cerial or corn flake but I took some because of no choice . (3) Shower is little spoilt, so I have to adjust it to use very very carefully. Even reported to front desk, they don't have any action. (4) There is no convenient store or restaurant. Must buy something before you come back here. My company's administration is very stingy for business trip expense so that I had to stay here, but must ask them to change some better quality hotel. The purpose of hotel is for guest to take rest, but I feel tired to stay here. Just stay one night only, this hotel may have meaning.

“It might be marvellous but there's something in the detail” Lovely quiet and well designed rooms (though the usual lack of attention to details - scuff marks on the walls, stains on carpets and furnishings - so hey everyone, there's a business here for hotel detailing because so few places do it!), excellent service and a great location. But for the price, you would expect that rooms would be pristine.

“just as expected for Hilton, super cute, for the price, & distance from city” This airport hilton used to be a military control tower. Converted into a cute eclectic hilton. Round funky building with a huge rotunda, restaurant. Everything you expect when you walk into a hilton. Of course, knowing you are at the airport and plane traffic, I didnt have a problem with any noise. Updated furnishings with mild texas twist, not country or anything too crazy, but I'll call it southern touch. City was close with a car and this hilton was half the price as the one downtown. I enjoyed my stay, and my meal.

“Great Staff, Location and Pool” I was in town for the BIO 2008 conference and moved here from another hotel (Bristol-see review). I lucked out on them having a room as the city was full. Here is what is odd. I liked this hotel despite the trains and rather plebian decor (light white oak pressboard....with plastic chrome strip). It was the staff and their friendliness. And despite the fact the hotel rooms were BORING, it was super clean and that matters a lot. Breakfast was fine- I mean it is free, how can you go wrong? Free shuttle around town if you ask and he is free. Again, a plus. Pool was absolutely beautiful- overlooking the harbor and nobody was ever in it///how NICE! Adequate but small fitness center. Anyway-take a chance on this place-I am glad I did.

“歴史が素敵なホテル” 9月17日から2泊しました。 少し思ったより小さいとても素敵なリゾートでした。 リゾートフィーが35ドルかかりますが、一応、すべてにおいてチップを挟まなくて良いシステムだとチェックインの際にいわれましたが アメリカのサウスウェストのスタッフの親切さにはチップを払ってしまいました。 清潔さと自然の良さを保たせながらとても親切なホテルで気持ちいい過ごしが出来ました。 マイナスポイントではアリゾナ一のレストランであると聞いたホテルのレストランの味は日本人には少しヘビーな気がします。

“Exceptional service and facilities” Omni typically has nicer than average hotels and this is no exception. With a great location right on Michigan Ave, the all-suite property is upscale yet accessible. Staff are well-trained and service oriented. I did not experience any problems during my stay. My room on the 19th floor had nice south views of the city; the condo construction next door did not interfere with the view but I was almost to the other corner. The room was laid out comfortably and was very quiet, at the end of the hall. Wireless internet access was sketchy in the living/office area of the room however, with signal strength improving only in the bedroom. Note that if you sign up for the loyalty program, internet is free and you also get complimentary beverages delivered to your door each morning, a very nice touch. I had two meals in the restaurant, which is expensive but typical for downtown Chicago (esp on Mich Ave). The breakfast buffet at $20 includes many choices, food was well prepared, and you get to look out over Michigan Avenue. Valet parking is the only option and be prepared to wait 10-15 minutes to retrieve your vehicle since the garage they use is two blocks away. Valet staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful; I was even provided a complimentary bottle of water while I waited. There is a roomy fitness facility with changing area and single shower, but no spa-type services. In short, this was one of the nicest hotels I've stayed in in Chicago and would definitely return, esp when promotional pricing is offered.

“Very impressed, nice nice hotel.” Never had stayed at a doubletree, and I was very impressed with the hotel. First, this is a HUGE hotel. I believe I read it has something like 900 rooms. Makes it one of the larger hotels in the Seattle area. The cookies were nice, and I got a room in wing 5 which has a little view of a lake. I enjoyed having that. The pool area was really nice, it was 95 degrees outside, so an outdoor pool was PERFECT. I am told the pool is open year round too. Overall I enjoyed it. Be aware it can be a very long walk to the lobby from your room if you get put in a wing, although I think the wings are nicer myself (they are a little newer).

“I love this place!” I stayed here after I was told about the hotel and frankly I LOVE it! Fabulous location, tucked away, close to airport, great food, bar, near ground zero, wall street, statue of liberty and FABULOUS SERVICE!!!!!! The rooms are spacious, it is literally tucked away and you would not know it was there unless you were looking for it. It is close to restaurants but you need to know if you are there on the weekend not all of them are open on Saturday and Sunday. If you go out the bar door there is a Crumbs!!!! They do offer snacks in the morning and wine and snacks in the afternoon!

“Not so great....” Run down, hot tub broken, pool freezing, overpriced. The neighborhood is a bit out of the way and across the street from project housing. We were a one night stay and quick to leave.

“Always a pleasure” This is my favorite hotel in San Francisco! Great location near Union Square, public transportation, and everything the city has to offer. I've stayed here many times, and always find the staff to be overwhelmingly helpful and courteous, and the rooms to be clean and well appointed. The lobby is bustling and has a great city vibe, but the rooms in the tower are quite and take you away from all the hype. The concierge lounge staff is TOP NOTCH!! You can't go wrong with this hotel!

“Buona ubicazione” Ho soggiornato un paio di notti a luglio presso The Opal Hotel a San Francisco e devo dire che è un buon hotel. Le stanze non sono molto grandi, noi eravamo in 4 e stavamo un po'strettine, però alla fine dovevamo solo dormirci e non è stato un grandissimo problema! Unico inconveniente è che accendendo il phon si è attivato l'allarme antincendio fortunatamente senza conseguenze!! La camera è abbastanza pulita e la colazione non abbondandissima e con poca scelta. Situato a due passi da Union Square e dai mezzi pubblici.

“A Boutique in Need of a Revamp” BE FOREWARNED: 6 COLUMBUS IS NOT ON COLUMBUS CIRCLE, JUST CLOSE TO IT. Its actually on 58th which can be confusing for people who you tell to meet you there. I was recently at a W hotel which has improved upon the idea of boutique (see review of W in Boston). The reason for staying at 6 Columbus is its location. It is a typical boutique in style, which is dark, contemporary and lively, with an overall modern feel. I have been in some boutique hotels that have small rooms, yet they were very functional. I was in room 66 and it was small and very non-functional, Poor task and room lighting, a desk that is unusable and a bed that is sufficient, but with lousy pillows. Room: The room is cramped in a NY style kind of way. It has adequate power outlets. The TV was just okay with a poor selection of channels. There is sufficient (barely) storage, but it would be inadequate for two people. The view is not much to talk about. There is a desk with very poor task lighting and the windows let in very little light. The worst part is that to use the desk you have to sit on the bed and have your laptop sit in the drawer. It is simply unacceptable. The bathroom is small, but otherwise adequate. Location: If you are not staying at this hotel for location then don't stay there. The hotel’s location is near Columbus Circle a block from Central Park. Food: I only had a snack at the bar, but having stayed and dined at this hotel previously I was pleased with the food. The bar is small, but very lively and overall enjoyable. The menu is not expansive and is Asian in nature.r Hotel Overall: The lobby is small, but has a nice seating area. The staff is young and friendly. I have stayed at other Thompson hotels and have found them to be better choices than 6 Columbus, though the location is hard to beat. For the money, if you don't have to have a boutique hotel i would recommend staying at the Le Meridien which is nearby. The money is about the same on many days and the experience is a lot better.

“My second fave in Philly” Great location just 1 block north of city hall. Brick exterior with modern interior. Usually 2-3 doormen at entrance, they handle the valet service, luggage and front door. Courteous front desk staff. Keycard elevators are very fast. Stylish small room with a queen bed, a lounge chair & small table, a large lcd tv, functioning AC & elegant large bathroom with glass enclosed shower stall. Fully stacked minibar and one robe are available. The towels and linens are superb. The bed is very comfortable.

“Nice Hotel, if only the staff were nice too.” I stayed here for one night following a night out with my wife. Checking in was not a quick process. Staff seemed like we were bothering them. They needed some serious motivation. Room was clean, a good size and did the job for a good price. The door to the bathroom was an opaque glass that you could see what people are doing but not the details. Not the best idea for all travelers. The location is central if you are visiting midtown. Also a short walk to many of the subway lines and Penn Station Check out was much like check in, unmotivated staff.

“Durchschnittshotel mit miesem Service” Das Marriott Copley Place zeichnet sich dadurch aus, auf dem Gebiet der Hotellerie sich immer wieder einen Patzer zu erlauben. Das gewünschte Zimmer war bei Anreise nicht verfügbar, Checkout nur durch eine Person besetzt und mit Wartezeit verbunden, der Concierge Service war recht langsam, angeblich wegen einem PC Wechsel, das Zimmermädchen vergisst eine/ihre Haarspange auf dem Tisch, das Zimmer lag unter Lärmbelästigung der Klimageräte von außen, Falschauskünfte über das parken seitens des Bell Service....... Insgesamt also ein miserabler Service, den ich in der Fülle der Aneinanderreihung noch nirgends vorher erleben musste. Das Preis Leistungs Verhältnis steht zudem in keinem Verhältnis.

“worst Hilton property” I am a HIlton fan so I was terribly disappointed with this property. The location was not good. I arrived late and tried to stop at a few gas stations, fast food restaurants to pick up something to eat but couldn't get out of the car. I'm pretty brave when traveling but the location didn't feel safe. At the front desk the clerk told me not to go to these spots at night. I was starving. I had to buy something from the hotel cooler. The hotel was old and smelly. I depend on the computers at Hilton properties for last minute work and the two machines didn't have internet connection. The front desk clerk in the morning insisted it was working because the screen would come up but she didn't try to go onto the internet. Her attitude was "oh well" When I pressed her to find out if she was going to report it, she said it was the first time she heard of the problem. Was she going to report it, Yes, and when I asked how long she anticipated for someone to look at it her response was I had to wait a couple of days. I then asked her to check if the computers were working at the Hilton property down the street and she said she didn't think they had computers. I insisted she call and of course they did. I wanted to check out and move to another location but I would have lost my deposit. Unless you have busines at market place or the nearby hospitals avoid this part of town.
“Location is awesome” Clran and comfy this hotel is close to n Michigan ave the magnificent mile. Tons of good shopping and restaurant Choices. Rooms Are standard but offer everything one needs

“Great Property!” I was there with a group of ladies for a Holiday outing! The property is very nice and extremely clean! The staff was wonderful and so accommodating. The location is wonderful, easy walking to everything! Bonus ... Trader Joes right next door! We had a ball!

“Nice property, a little hard to find” Just returned from a night at this hotel and it is a nice property. Everything looks new and clean. Rooms are nicely decorated with a gold accent wall, flat screen TV, and a small kitchenette that has a fridge, cooktop, microwave and dishwasher. And there's a nice little swimming pool. As new and clean as it is, I will say it was difficult for us to find. Not impossible. But with Mapquest directions printed out, we still ended up doubling back and looking really hard for it. Once we spotted it, we almost passed the entrance, which is just past the hotel. It is located near the airport at the intersection of several highways, and is almost directly underneath one of the flyovers from one of the highways. That being said I would stay here again for certain things. We were visiting relatives so we weren't looking for a place to vacation. If that's what you're after, I wouldn't choose this hotel. The view out of our window was a wall from another part of the hotel. I didn't mind too much on this trip, but it's not what I want to see if I'm staying for several days. And at 5 a.m., the place is like Grand Central Station. I thought the entire hotel must have been leaving between 5 and 7 a.m. (Such is the plight of an airport hotel) But for our purposes it was fine. Last year we stayed at the Residence Inn Marriott/Stone Oak up on the 1604 Loop, which is a less congested, quieter, prettier area of San Antonio (albeit farther away from the Riverwalk and not in an area where there seems to be much to do). But that hotel wasn't as nice as this one, so I think we made the right choice in moving to the TownePlace Suites this time. The breakfast is also pretty good, with eggs, sausage, toast, yogurt, Oatmeal, and cereals.

“Never again GEM hotel” Make sure you are not staying in the basement rooms – they try to trick you by numbering these rooms starting with #7. I had my hopes up but found my room in the basement with almost no window, broken cabinet, only 2 hangers, and, worst of all, the small window was facing right onto a busy street. Every night around 3am, the noise from the street was unbearable and it lasted for about an hour. Not sure if they do cleaning outside or it’s just people coming out of bars. Never again, GEM hotel, at least, not in the basement rooms. p.s. the room really was unbelievably tiny p.p.s. and I am a preferred member of the Comfort Inn chain...

“Stayed twice and still not impressed” I originally stayed here in Aug 2009. Chose the W strictly because of the location and the alluring roof top terrace. The first visit was a disaster but I will not write about that one since I did complain to management and was offered a complimentary weekend in order to give them another chance. I thought that was very nice and took them up on it. So I gave them another chance and went back in Oct 2009. The service had definitely improved. The workers were older and more professional as opposed to the surly "teens" they had in August. The rooms are very small and I agree with several comments from other reviewers especially the one about it looking like Trading Spaces designed it. To further that looks like Hilda from Trading Spaces designed it (those who watched the show long ago know who I am talking about). Don't get the design--almost feels like a brothel. The housekeeping still had not improved. Trash can in the shower, clogged drain, unmade rooms, hair, etc. Just not very attentive at all. Lobby is still a disaster at night since everyone comes to go to the swanky lounge/rooftop terrace/bar. I have not problem with that but the problem I do have is that they do not treat the guests in the hotel as the number one priority. You are supposed to be able to bypass the line going up to the roof but we still have to wait even after showing our key. Then once we got up there, 1/2 the tables were reserved for people who were coming later that night. They were not hotel guests. Usually when you stay at hotels you take priority not locals. So I completely agree with the viewer who stated it needs to decide whether it is a nightclub or a hotel. I understand that the W has this concept of being a local hangout but that is clearly not my thing. When I go away I want to be treated as a guest and have some privileges. I think it is crazy to put the local scene as your top priority. If that is business model then just rent rooms by the hour.

“Très agréable” Un hôtel très agréable, bien situé dans l'Upper West Side, à deux blocks de Central Park (métro 79th St.). Accueil personnalisé, chambres spacieuses, confortables et calme. Que demander de plus ! Wifi gratuite dans le lobby seulement mais on peut la récupérer pour la chambre aussi. 2 restaus sympas dans l'hôtel : Serafina (italien) et The Fatty Crab (americano-malaisien). J'ai pris mon petit déj chez Crumb à l'arrière du block, sur Amsterdam Ave. Voir aussi à côté la boutique pour enfant Giggle ou jouets et vêtements sont fabriqués avec des matériaux testés et non préjudiciables à la santé.

“They charge just for breathing.” Pros: Nice comfortable beds. The room was spotless. The view of Navy Pier was awesome. We went to our room and the fan in the A/C started making a horrible noise. The people next door even started knocking on the wall. I called the front desk and they sent a maintenance man, (I wish I could remember his name) he showed up in less than 10 minutes and he said the fan would have to be replaced. He told us we would have to change rooms. He got our room changed, with a better view, brought us the keys and offered to help us take our luggage to the other room. He was awesome. We told the people next door what the problem was and they were cool about it. I did make sure the A/C was turned off as not to bother them. The girl at the front dest was very friendly when we checked in. It was really hot in Chicago, July 4th weekend and they had ice water dispensers and cups in the lobby for no charge.(that's all that was free) Cons: They placed an invoice under the door that we were being charged for a bottle of Vodka, $38.00. That was weird since no one in our group (we had 2 rooms) drinks alcohol. I went to the front desk and they removed it. They said it is based on weight and if we had moved anything in the refrigerator or placed anything inside of it, you can be charged. That was resolved with no problems. The curtains don't keep out much light. They charge $15.00 per day, per person to use the pool. That's highway robbery. They charge for internet service $9.95 per day. Parking $48.00 per day.How can you enjoy your stay when you get charged just for breathing? If economy motels can offer internet service for no charge, so can 4 star hotels. If your wanting to be close to all the action on Michigan Ave, this hotel isn't for you. Overall the stay was good. It was quiet at night compared to the hotels around Michigan Ave. The hotels around Michigan Ave are by the hospital and you'll be kept up all night with sirens blaring. I grade 4 start hotels down when they charge for what economy motels give individuals for free.

“alternative to crowded mid-town weekend” We stayed here for a weekend, selecting this hotel for weekend price--about $75 per night lower than comparable mid-town hotels. Comfortable king room; view of the Hudson River. Quiet. Accommodating staff. Other views might include the East River, Battery Park, etc. WTC memorial construction is literally next door. This location is a reasonable alternative to mid- and uptown occasionally. Downtown has more buzz than 12 years ago. Walking distance to Soho and Tribeca restaurants. Easy access to various subway lines. Great walks along the rivers. Ferries nearby. The only restaurant in the hotel is sort of a sports bar, but there are many others nearby.

“Nice Hotel” Booked this room last minute and were not disappointed. We will stay at this hotel again in the future. Price was great for NYC. We had a King Suite, which was plenty of room for two people. Location was good, room was clean, staff was pleasant, bed was comfortable, shower had good water pressure, what more could you need? Requested an early check-in and room was ready when we arrived.
“よくあるヒルトン” デュポンサークル駅から少し坂を上るとあります。さらに上ると丘の上のほうにもコンビニがあったりしました。よくあるヒルトンホテルで、部屋も施設もとにかく及第点だと思います。がっかりはしませんでした。

“Great hotel for business travelers” First of all this hotel is massive. Probably the biggest one I've ever stayed in. I stayed there for 3 nights on a business trip and I can definitely recommend it. There are 2 bars, one on the top floor which has a great view but oddly no beer on tap, and one in the lobby which had a huge seating area and excellent service. The fitness is pretty large for a hotel. Overall service was very friendly and of the highest caliber. The concierge loaned us umbrellas for our whole trip.

“The James is a great downtown getaway hotel.” You know, if you want a great kind of getaway but stay withing New York, what is now referred to annoyingly as a "staycation", you could not do better than The James. Why? well, I do not think that it is the greatest location despite being on the two different subway lines, but you are very much in New York, on the edge of SoHo. I adore the lobby and the warm reception although the over thinking of the uniforms is far too much effort to try to have "style". The art books also add the usual effort but it is the homegrown art work, some of bad, some of it good, that lends real city credentials to this hotel. A galpal came into town and I wanted to not crowd my apartment. The room was wonderful with floor to celing wondows that look over the entrance to the Holland Tunnel. I know it may sound a bit odd, but never have so may cars going away, been so relaxing. Yes the rooms are perhaps over-designed, including a clear bathroom which one can push a button to make a shade come down. It can be sexy, ( or frankly not) but here it is not too onnoxious. Is it a turn on to have friends see you on the loo? The shower is out of control with pressure- so you are getting your hair wet. The seating area was nice and it although the halls felt corporate, the fact that there was local talent on the walls made up for the harsh lighting. The restaurants are fantastic, elevating this hotel to a great spot to hunker back for a weekend, read and get a little work done and relax without leaving. I cannot speak enough about the service and on top of it all they are. I travel a lot and wish that I could get the level of service, minus the odd outfits everywhere I go. Now, if the hoards of people begin to come to Jimmy or the Treehouse, well, then the effect could be out the window. Let's hope not.....

“The Giraffe has animal magnetism.” The Hotel Giraffe is a well-groomed boutique hotel in the less touristy, more real New York, Park Avenue South neighborhood. The lobby comprises the entire ground floor and is one of those “active” lobbies where people come to meet each other and enjoy the hotel’s fairly liberal guest policy for their free continental breakfast and wine and cheese hour. The rooms are reasonable in size, though not recommended for those who require spaciousness. They are well appointed, as is the bath. Each room has a floor to ceiling set of French doors that opens on to a tiny balcony. The views from most rooms are typical NY views of adjacent buildings. There are lots of nice touches throughout the hotel, ranging from your choice of free wired or wireless high speed Internet access, free bottled water in the room, and large flat screen TVs. There are also lots of electrical outlets in convenient places for those of us who travel with lots of electronic gear. The halls are very dark, intentionally so I suspect, as this seems to be something that “cool” hotels must do these days. I would urge management to turn up the lumens in the halls. I stayed there one night on a business trip and everything went perfectly. This is a great hotel when being a bit off the beaten path of midtown is acceptable.

“Well appointed rooms - great location for a Moscone Convention Center Event” Great location with business orientation or Union Square shopping. Large rooms. Nice lobby. For Gold and above members of Marriott Rewards - free Internet and great suite with desserts, continental breakfast, honor bar, etc. Nearby theatre. Sadly the kosher food place in Chinatown was shut down this week - so limited food choices.

“Average or worst” We stayed at the L'Enfant Plaza because of its location to the mall and metro. It scored very high on both of those accounts. The lobby is very nice - new, bright clean crisp feel and the staff were very nice. The room -- like so many have said needs up dating. Although clean -- the chair was terrible stained, the ceiling was patched so often from leaks we were concerned there might be another one. The bathroom was very adequate, the faucet dripped and was very old, but the counter top was marble. The hotel is not setup for chargers, however there were enough plugs. The wall paper is very dated and peeling in some places. The TV channels included HBO, but not the weather channel. If you are not spending much time in your room this hotel works at a good price. We did not get internet but we didn't need it this trip.

“Bugs in the bathroom!” We chose this hotel based on several good reviews but were disappointed with what we found. This hotel feels old and worn. The elevators were the slowest I've ever encountered so far. Our room had double beds that were lumpy and uncomfortable, although it seemed clean enough. The bed sheets, curtains, and carpets were fraying and had old stains in places. There was no climate control when we stayed, just one of those old style air conditioners that attached to the windows, but it sounded like a missile silo when turned on so we mostly just decided we'd have to live without the thing. The walls were very thin (I know this because I could hear the couple in the next room...). Also, the door to our room didn't quite reach the floor, there was about a half-inch gap, which was a bit disconcerting. And yes, there were tiny wormlike bugs crawling around in the bathroom. This hotels one redeeming feature is that it's close to Times Square if you're thinking of visiting there.

“Buon soggiorno” Il soggiorno era cominciato malissimo: nonostante avessimo prenotato con 5 mesi di anticipo, la stanza non era disponibile per la prima notte. Siamo quindi stati dirottati per la prima notte all'hotel Elan (buon albergo, ma di altra categoria): bisogna peró dire che il wilshire hotel ha pagato la nostra stanza all'Elan e non ce l'ha riaddebitata, facendoci pagare solo le due successive notti passate presso di loro. Comportamento molto corretto. Le stanze sono molto moderne anche se non grandissime; sul tetto c'è una piccolissima piscina con solarium e bar: il panorama è bellissimo e si vede l'holliwood sign

“Nice hotel, but subpar customer service from management” The hotel itself was nice - lobby was great, my room was nice but I was not happy about the customer service and the elevators that I have to give this hotel only a 2 star. When I checked in, the front desk manager was extremely rude to me. I have Marriott status but was told that this particular Marriott does not consider status when putting you into a room. I was put into a room that faced directly at the Hyatt and made me feel super claustrophobic and had to switch rooms. The staff is not knowledge about the layout of the hotel and don't know what views the rooms have. This was not a cheap hotel so I expected some sort of customer service here. The elevators took a really long time - up to 40 minutes! I went back to my room to pack to find the same people still waiting for the elevator! I finally got onto one and the squeaking was so bad that I had to get out of the elevator because I really thought it was going to break down. I almost think not all the elevators were working because the wait was so ridiculous. The starbucks line downstairs was understaffed as well.
“Motel 6/Central Denver” I was not impressed within properties appearance, service or location. It was one of the worst properties I've ever stayed at. It should be demolished.

“Very Nice Hotel” I stayed at the Hotel Monaco May 12, 2005 for a conference. Check in was painless. The staff were friendly and helpful. The room was quiet, non-smoking, spacious, furnished with a king bed, reading chair, desk and chair and television hidden in a large cabinet. The bed had a down comforter and many pillows. There was a wildly colored bathrobe in the closet. Towels were large and thick. There was an in-room safe, no refrigerator. Wireless internet was free and fast. The offer of a goldfish to keep company for the night was too interesting not to try, but after calling twice at 9 and 11 PM and being promised a goldfish, one never showed up. One of my colleagues reported a similar experience. I took advantage of the overnight complimentary shoe shine. In the morning, going to an 8 AM meeting, my shoes were not back. They came back about 15 minutes after I called requesting them. Meeting rooms were fine. The service with the food for the meetings was terrific. Food at the meetings was abundant and very very good. It was a nice hotel to stay in and a good one for a meeting.

“Average stay for average hotel” We stayed 3 nights at this hotel. We were greeted by a friendly staff which serviced us with s a smile continuously throughout our stay. A few of the reception staff do need a quick refresher on client relations and perhaps a briefing of Boston's restaurants and surroundings. The staff gave us a list of restaurants that catered to our dietary restrictions etc. The first, Tapeo was good and interesting but no upscale dining. The second was Hamersley's, which we had to travel to and from only to realize that this restaurant served primarily fish dishes (which we do not eat!). Quite disappointing the staff would send us there despite our dislike for fish as indicated. 2 hours later, we ate at another restaurant. The third night, we ate a Meritage and it was fabulous..we found this restaurant ourselves. Room: Clean, ikea-contemporary , nothing out of the ordinary. We requested quiet room and they placed us right beside the main hall coming out of elevator..we did not sleep the first night (doors are like paper!), 2 other nights were not too bad. Smell of cigarettes in hall which staff promptly addressed. Bed VERY comfy! Restaurant: average but make sure you get their french toast! Bell hop and concierge: excellent, always willing to help. No free Wi-Fi..in this era, c'mon! Would recommend but interested if other "newer" hotels are nearby with better amenities.

“Excellent service, not just an "airport" hotel” I had a 6:45am flight out of LAX and I live over an hour from the airport so decided to take advatnage of an excellent weekend special and spend a Saturday night at the hotel and afford myself a little extra sleep in the morning. Check-in at the elite desk was seemless, my gold status was recognized instantly and I was given a room on the 16th floor directly overlooking LAX. As an airplane enthusiast, it was pretty nice getting to do some airplane spotting before going to sleep. Shuttle service in the morning was excellent - the shuttle I made it on filled up quickly and the hotel had a back-up right behind for those that did not make it on the first. I didn't have a chance to do more than sleep, but the pool looked quite large and resort-like, not a typical airport hotel pool setup. The fitness center also looked well-equipped. I have no hesitation recommending this particular Marriott.

“Slightly missed it's mark” I stayed here for business in July 2012. While everyone on site was very friendly I felt the room was a little musty and didn't feel as modern and clean as they were touting it to be. For example, the curtain was stained with something icky like chocolate when I went to open them- I know it's hard to prevent those types of issues. It felt like a remodel that slightly missed the mark. It was fine for a couple days for work, but I've stayed at other Chicago hotels that I preferred (see other reviews). The breakfast was standard- waffle stand, some fruit and yogurt, etc. I would liked to have seen some bottled water or sodas and fresh OJ instead of the machine.

“Customer Service rocks here” I arrived late after a really long day of flying - When I walked in the lady ask if she could do anything for me to make my stay better after the day I had - all I wanted to do was sleep. The room was big - and super clean. The couch had a stain on one pillow, that I moved and set on the floor. From the house keeper who worked on that hall to the people at the front counter the customer was great. I ate two meals in the "Fresh Dining" and the servers were super. I never had to ask for a refill - or for a finished plate to be removed. Room Service has the fun-ist guys delivering breakfast ! Smiling and friendly. The 2nd morning when breakfast was 15 mins late arriving - he smiled and said enjoy it is on us we are so sorry. The only down thing I experienced - I could not use their internet.

“Solid business hotel” Stayed for two nights.
