Very good location (near financial district, but also walking distance to great shopping -- speaking of which, Westfields shopping centre on Market has the most plentiful shops, plus the Embarcadero has good shopping as well). My room on the 7th floor appeared to have been recently renovated. Was a little loud, though, with the window open as the cable car was right outside. I thought the front desk staff were great. My air conditioning wouldn't work and as a result I had a poor night's sleep, but I should have let the hotel know and asked them to fix it.

“One of the most run-down Embassys I've ever encountered” As a frequest traveler who prefers to stay in Hilton brand hotels, this is perhaps the most disappointing property I've been to. I'm not one who typically writes bad reviews, but the entire hotel is poorly lit and is way past it's prime. It appears they may be just starting to begin some room renovations whch are desperately needed. The heating unit in my room was the loudest I've ever heard- louder than those window-type A/C units and the heater wasn't even that style- it was a central heating unit that rattled and vibrated all night long. The bathroom was tiny, but the rooms were larger than a lot of the other Embassy Suites I've been to which was a bonus. The very worst thing about my stay was the room next to me had their refrigerator die out on them causing a horrible burnt stench for my entire overnight stay and into the next morning. The fitness center is about the size of a walk in closet at best. The only thing this hotel has going for it is a very friendly staff.

“Die ausgezeichnete Lage allein rechtfertigt den Preis nicht” Wir haben im Oktober 2011 für zwei Nächte hier übernachtet und wir waren ziemlich enttäuscht über das angebotene Preis-/Leistungsverhältnis. Als wir im Hotel ankamen, wurden wir nicht einmal begrüsst von der Receptionsdame, sondern wurden gleich aufgefordert die Kreditkarte bzw. eine gültige ID vorzuweisen. Man merkte gleich, dass dieses Hotel aufgrund der ausgezeichneten Lage so gut ausgelastet sein muss, dass sie es nicht mehr nötig haben, ihren Hotelgästen Sorge zu tragen. Das Zimmer war sehr klein und die Matratzen waren durchgelegen und somit butterweich. Das einzig Positive am Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square war seine Lage, aber wir würden nie wieder hierher zurückkehren.

“Great hotel” This a great property, excellent location and wonderful staff. Everyone was very accommodating and polite. The room I had was on the 23rd floor and was like a suite, with a living area and a bedroom. The living room was spacious, with a plasma TV, a desk and a couch. The beds were very comfortable and the toiletries of very good quality. In the closed they placed an umbrella, which came in handy, it rained the whole time I was in Chicago. The internet connection is $9.95/24hrs. Great place, I will return for sure.

“Great 4-Star Luxury Hotel” I stayed two nights in August, 2007 at this hotel. I was very pleased with everything. ROOM: I was assigned one of the renovated rooms and it was beautiful, quiet, comfortable, spacious, and had lots of ammenities like separate shower and tub, electronic laptop safe, large functional desk, and large flat screen TV. The bed was outstanding as were the linens, pillows, and duvet. SERVICE: Service was excellent throughout my stay. There is a button on the wall in your room that you can push for just about any request. Someone appears at your door in a few moments - - service was efficient and fast. Every staff member I encountered was very polite and helpful. FITNESS: The hotel has a very nice fitness center with great equipment. CONCIERGE LOUNGE: The concierge lounge provides an excellent extended continental breakfast. TIP: the lounge gets crowded so I recommend you show up for breakfast early. LOCATION: The location is great - - right off Union Square behind the Westin St. Francis. RENOVATIONS: Although this hotel is going through a total renovation, you hardly notice it. I was impressed with how quiet the workers were. They hardly made any noise and certainly had no effect on my enjoyable stay. They are closing one floor at a time for renovations starting at the top and working down. I think the top 5 or 6 floors are done. The lobby is scheduled for renovation beginning in November. VALUE: This is not the most luxe, beautiful, or celebrated hotel in S.F. but it's an excellent choice and an excellent value when you consider that its rates are 1/2 or less than those at some of the 5-Star luxury hotels nearby. I've stayed at some of these hotels and they are amazing but I think the J.W. Marriott matches most of their quality and services at a much lower cost. Highly recommended.

“Fine choice, price depending” RECOMMENDED. Easy/safe walk to nearby restaurants and events, my room on the 6th floor is showing a bit of age, room size is very small and bathroom extremely small. Lighting only OK. Decoration is not my style, "think little old lady". Bedding comfortable but nothing special. Staff friendly and efficient. Got this hotel on Priceline for a low rate so it's was an excellent deal. Had I booked normally and paid >$200, it was over priced.

“Passes the "Keep the Wife Happy" Test” Unlike most of my trips, this was a short vacation- 5 nights using points at the W Lakeshore. When my wife if with me, the priorities shift from functional room and good gym to the bed, the towels, the location and the "vibe." Despite the whole town being booked and busy from a large convention, this W passed the Wife Test with flying colors. I know some folks have complained that the rooms are small and the property itself unimpressive given its prior life as a lower end hotel. While the building was minimalist, it felt like a W, from the candles and lighting to the clean lines in the lobby and the rooms. The staff was attentive and helpful from the start. I was not counting on much since we were staying on points, but we received a small upgrade to a higher level lakeview room as a SPG Platinum member. We also received coupons good for free continental breakfast (there is no lounge) and two drink coupons for the bar. The breakfast was confusing. Wife requires a hot breakfast each day, while I usually just enjoy a donut, so I asked whether we could upgrade using the coupon. The clerk had to go check with the manager, but returned to tell us we could have either the continental breakfast or a $10 credit each , each day, towards whatever we wanted. The first morning, we were pleased to see that the regular breakfast menu offered some interesting combinations, and nothing was over the $12-$13 range, which did not seem bad for hotel like this. The confusing part was when I asked the server, he also had to go check about the $10 credit. He came back and said ok, but when the bill came, it was for the full amount. I asked him why it was not deducted and he said we were just supposed to subtract the $20 ourselves from the total. The second day, mostly the same story,but the server did write in the $20 deduction by hand. Apparently the system does not allow them to input the discount. Either way, the final bill at checkout was correct. The room itself was small, but functional. A nice walk in shower, but no tub. No door on the shower, so the floor got wet every time, which was a bigger deal than normal because we were trying to do the green thing and not get new towels all the time, so the bath mat was always wet. The good news was one quick phone call quickly brought new towels. The bed was comfortable, although the duvet cover weighed a ton, so that might be an issue for some people. The gym had a nice mix of ellipticals, treadmills and bikes, along with weight machines and free weights. Anyone tall might have an issue with the free weights, since the ceiling was low. I saw a few surprised guys hit the ceiling with lifting overhead. The location was great. It is a few blocks away from the busier parts of town, in a mostly residential area, but close enough to walk. Navy Pier is almost right across the Lakeshore Drive. Cabs were always available. Like most W's, the bar was lively, even though this one was small. There is a very small lounge on the top floor with a great view, but it was mostly empty, so we stayed downstairs and chatted with new people late each evening. Wife was happy, so I was happy.

“Adequate for a stopover” Spent a few hours overnight prior to an early-morning departure at LAX. Not one of my favorite hotels in the LAX area, but adequate for one night. Lobby and elevator are pretty depressing. Fortunately, the room was nicer than the lobby's appearance had suggested might be the case. Paid $77 plus taxes for two beds. Considering the cost of the room, parking is expensive at about $15 plus tax. Parked on the street across from the hotel for free -- but this only worked because the flight was departing before the daytime street parking fees kicked in. Not worth more than about $85 or $90 per night.

“Great business location” Excellent room, friendly and helpful staff, right in the business heart of San Jose. Great restaurant. Internet access needs to be updated and there is that nagging charge, but other than that, highly recommend for business traveler.

“Outstanding hotel” We stayed at the Denver Hyatt at Colorado Convention Centre for a conference in November 2008. From the minute we got out of the hotel, it was an exemplary visit. The gentlemen at the door were very welcoming and kind. Josh at the front desk was efficient and knowledgeable when we checked in. Our room was excellent, spotless clean, very comfortable bed with a variety of pillows so you could find one you liked, great amenities including travel size toothpaste - we have not seen that before and loved that! We had a discussion with John, the Housekeeping manager at one point when we were waiting in line at the front desk (he was quick to approach us so we were not waiting long and assisted us with our request), he told us more about the hotel and how it was striving for a "green" status. The hotel goes to great lengths to recycle, you see recycle bins everywhere, and also use energy efficient lighting and appliances. The gym at the hotel is excellent with at least 10 cardio machines with TV's for your entertainment. The decor through the hotel is modern and tasteful. The staff were pleasant at every turn, and for a North American hotel, it was truly outstanding (we travel for conferences a lot and this hotel has stood out as the best we have been to for business travel). The hotel also has very reasonably priced foods and drinks. Drinks at the conference social were under $6 (we have paid $8+ in other hotels), and the extensive continental breakfast buffet (with tons of fresh cut fruit) was great at $10.50 per person including coffee. The location of the hotel is excellent - we went to the most amazing Peruvian dinner while there - ask about the name of it at the front desk, it's about 4 blocks away. Plus, the Rioja restaurant on Larimer and 14th was completely beyond excellent. We would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Very Good Location for D.C.” I stayed at this hotel from 6/13-6/17 and the location was excellent. It was close to everything. I easily walked to the White House and all of the Smithsonian Museums. Chinatown was only 5 blocks away. The Convention Center was a mere 15 minute walk. The hotel staff were nice, although I found that the cleaning staff was MORE nice if you gave them a tip. After I did that, they gave me 6 bottles of shampoo and 6 bags of tea in my room. The noise level was ok. I was on the 11th floor, but the street noise in the mornings were loud. I didn't have many neighbors, so it was mostly quiet. I did wear earplugs, as usual, so my opinion may be flawed. I was on a conference rate at $295 per night, so it was steep. But, the location was definitely the best. Safe neighborhood too. Rooms were nice and clean. Bed were excellent and soft with down comforters and pillows. Bathrooms were a good size. No refrigerator though. Rooms included: flat-screen TV, 2 queen beds, 1 dresser, 1 desk, and 1 sofa chair. Bathrooms had regular amenities (Bath and Body Works), hair dryer, coffee maker, etc. No shower caps though.

“Nice stay, very good hotel” So, its the Ritz, and you expect a lot. We got in on a group rate for a wedding, so the price was very reasonable ($139). At that rate, the hotel was phenomenal. On the other hand, if you pay street rate on a busy weekend and its more like $400, Its decent but not spectacular. Details... THE GOOD --Room was spacious, well-appointed (though a bit worn in a few places), comfy bed, nice lake views, very nice bathroom --Customer service was up to Ritz's reputation - excellent --Bar and common areas very nice --Turndown service is always a nice bonus --Location in the heart of Streeterville is great THE BAD --Breakfast at the little cafe in the main lobby was overpriced, but decent --Valet parking was exorbitant ($45 a night) Overall, I'd say if you can get a competitive rate to other local hotels, go for it! If not, you might get a bit more for your money elsewhere. But you won't be disappointed in this hotel in any case.

“Almost Perfect!” I've been in DC a lot of times. Went to different hotels. But this August I found the best of all: Hotel Palomar. There is a problem though: at about 3am, a big truck unload all its stuff in front of the main entrance of the hotel and if you are a light sleeper, you are going to hear it for sure.

“Good Airport Hotel, Courteous Service” On a very long, absolutely dreadful travel day of cancellations, reroutings, and delays, we ended up in Columbus, OH at 2:30 a.m. after the car rental agencies had closed, so we were stuck. So were many, many other people. So I didn't have a lot of choice on places to stay, but was happy to get a room in the Hampton Inn. For a decent place to stay near the airport, the Hampton did nicely. It's pretty much the same as any other Hampton Inn I've stayed in -- same decor, recently renovated, all the usual amenities in the room & free wireless. The bed was pretty comfortable, and the room was clean. The warm food in the free breakfast wasn't much to write home about, but there was yogurt and fruit and coffee, so that was fine. I do want to commend the service, however. As it was quite late, there was only one woman working at the desk. But since so many people had gotten stranded, there were probably 20 people trying to check in, all at once. The woman working remained quite pleasant under the pressure and made sure to cover everything, including getting our wake up call time (and it did come on time). I've seen staff at other hotels get surly with far fewer people to check in; I appreciated her positive attitude, especially at that point in that day. All in all, I was happy with the Hampton Inn in Columbus and would stay there again.

“Good Business in San Diego” The Hilton in San Diego is a big hotel, I was recently there for conference for a week. I usually dread the really big hotels because they are hard to operate and sometimes guest service suffers. Not the case at this Hilton. Every staff friendly and efficient - every single one I ran into. The room was clean, quiet, nice linens and the building appears fairly new so the problems associated with older hotels are not apparent. Heating and cooling was good, nice flat screen TVs. Elevators were adequate, and the meeting space was nice. Self parking was easy to navigate. The hotel is set on the water, so views are very nice. I got room service one morning, the food arrived before promised, and was better than the room service food I am used to. Again, hard to run in a big hotel but they seem to have it down pat. Lobby is clean and bright, high celings, color scheme is contemporary and pleasing. Fitness room is a little undersized, but I had no problem getting on machines. Two cautions, this is not an intimate hotel if you are looking for romantic get away. Also, you have to walk a little to get to to bar district and cross railroad tracks. Not a big deal, but about a 10 minute walk to get to business and bar district. Overall, much better than I expected, especially for a hotel of this size.

“Unbelievable! Highly recommended!!” I have to say that this is THE place to stay by far in Chicago! From the staff to the room to the valet to everything!! The beds were VERY comfortable, I wanted to sleep all day in that bed! The goldfish they brought up was a very nice touch and was super cute. You have to ask them ahead of time that you would like one. I brought my cat to the hotel, and they had rooms with LARGE pillows, right by both windows in my room for my cat (or your dog) to sit and look outside. My cat, who is usually terrified of staying in hotels, felt so comfortable and fell in love with the hotel too! She actually felt like it was home instead of hiding out all day and night! The turndown service was fabulous. We requested to have them clean while we were there (in the case my cat got scared) and they came fairly quickly. She did a great job though of cleaning up. Bed sheets were clean and bright white, they even had animal print robes for you to wear! The shower amenities I absolutely LOVED! The concierge was great! Gave us some fun things to do and maps so we wouldn't get lost. LOCATION: I MUST say that this is a GREAT location. I read some reviews before booking about how you have to cross the bridge to get to magnificent mile, but honestly, it's like a 5 minute walk and you are right at the beginning of the street! I would never stay closer than where this hotel is located. It's not too busy where you hear fire trucks and loud noises on the street from teenagers coming home from going out, yet it's COMPLETELY safe. Lots of people walking during the day, and even night (as we did some walking at night from a long day of shopping!) Oh, and if you haven't done this already, while you are in Chicago, you MUST go to Bobby's Bike Hike! Amazing time, cheap and such a GREAT tour of the city! You can rent the bikes on your own, but the tour is so worth it, and our tour guide was just so funny and entertaining! If you're there in the summer months though, i'd recommend doing a morning bike ride so your beat the heat! All i can say about this hotel is you MUST try it. It's not the cheapest, but it's well worth your money. You can't go wrong with this hotel. PURE luxury.

“Okay if cheap” Stayed here for 1 night on Sept 1 before heading to HI. As others have said, hotel is aging. TV was actually on a tv stand! (no armoire or anything) We were only there for about 6 hrs and the shuttle service to/from the airport was worth it. I wouldn't pay more than $120 for this place (we had a freebie) and wouldn't actually stay here as a vacation but for a quick layover, it was fine. We stayed at the Westin LAX airport about 2 yrs ago and it is much nicer, fyi.

“Fun hotel but better options nearby” I have stayed at Hotel Rouge quite a few times, as it is the closest hotel to the office I work from when in Washington DC. The hotel has a very distinctive personality - be prepared for a riot of red styling and leopard print carpet in the hallways! Probably not for everyone, but I thought it was fun and a nice change from generic beige chain hotels. The rooms are spacious and some have nice district views from the upper floors. The hotel restaurant is not great, and you have to walk a few blocks for other dining options and to get to the metro. The hotel staff are enthusiastic but not always very helpful. The hotel often has excellent promotional rates on offer, in which case it is great value. However if given a choice I would generally prefer to stay at Hotel Palomar or Donovan House, which are both slightly more upmarket options.

“景色をもとめなければOKだと思います。” 仕事でこちらのホテルに4泊しました。 ・立地 ミシガンアベニュー沿いでモールに隣接しているため、ショッピングも楽しめるロケーションです。また、ミシガンアベニューやその付近にたくさんお店やレストランがあり、スターバックスやウォルグリーンズも近くにありました。ホテル付近は歩き回れる好立地です。危ない雰囲気もありませんでした。 ・部屋 部屋は広くて、きれいでした。お水が毎日2本コンプリメンタリーでついてきました。 また、アメニティーがアロマセラピーアソシエイツのもので大きめのサイズだったのがさすがコンラッドという印象です。他、マウスウォッシュがあり、ありがたかったです。 バスタブとシャワーが別でしたが、バスタブにお湯がたまるのが速く、 バスタブの形も首が疲れないように背もたれのカーブがついていてとても良かったです。 足がむくみやすく疲れていたので、これはありがたかったです。 ただ、窓の外の景色がイマイチでした。高層階(17F建ての16F)にしてもらいましたが、となりのビル(オフィスでした)のオフィスフロアーが丸見えで、カーテン必須という状態です。 低層階の部屋も景色は良くなかったです。 朝食付きにしなかったのですが毎朝、フロントにコーヒーが置いてあり飲み放題でした。 フロントのフロアーにバーとオープンテラスになるラウンジがありました。 お天気が良かったので、オープンテラスでも全く問題ありませんでした。 雰囲気も、良かったです。 このエリアはたくさんホテルがあるので、例えば向かいのインターコンチ等も 泊まってみないなと思いますが、コンラッド自体はビジネス利用でしたら とても満足いくホテルだと思います。 コンラッド=リゾートのイメージだと少しがっかりすると思います。

“Okay Airport Hotel” So this hotel really doesn't have anything going for it other than that it is close to the airport and the rental car returns of Avis and Hertz. It is a standard Hilton without really any charm, including the views, which are nothing compared to the Hilton Bay Front a few miles south. Do not stay here if you are visiting San Diego for pleasure, as it is too far from anything but the airport. The rooms are fairly standard, perhaps a little bigger than the average Hilton room, though the furniture is a bit older, and the bathrooms certainly small. Air system is fairly loud and the top floor rooms are alive with the humming produced by the hotel's HVAC system part of which sits on the roof of the hotel. So at the very least avoid the top floor, which also has a low false ceiling in the hallway, making it feel dingy. They charge you here even if you park your own car a hefty $15 fee. This seems a lot when their is ample parking and no one is there to greet you at the door anyway. Customer service was fine, check-in efficent. Check-out the same. Stay here if you have an early morning flight, otherwise seek the Hilton's further to the south.
“Great Atmosphere, Great Hotel” This hotel is quaint old charm yet is very modern, the rooms are super modern, the hotel is super clean, the front desk staff is great.

“I'm in love with this hotel” I don't know how Kimpton is able to be "chic" yet warm, but they really pull it off in all of their DC properties. The interior design is just...so...cool. Lobby and rooms are squeaky clean, everything is contemporary with a twinge of retro, and it has a cool spy theme. I recommend signing up for the loyalty program - lots of perks. The staff is just amazing. They're sincere and friendly and really seem to be happy at work, as well as make you feel appreciated. I feel like I'm just shuffled through many chain hotels, but the staff is attentive and seems to care that you have an experience, not just a stay. SICK roof-top poo/bar.

“Not too thrilled” I paid in advance with points, but the clerk swiped my debit card and put an unexpected and extremely unwelcome $108 hold on my checking account. I think $30 would've been reasonable. At first I was glad they upgraded me to a suite, but I ended up with one extra bathroom and a Jacuzzi that didn't fill even after 90 minutes. I eventually gave up on it. I was also gifted with one really long hair stuck to the edge of the tub. The supervisor I talked with was nice, but the manager who replied to my feedback wasn't very responsive. I'm a Platinum member with Best Western Rewards, but I'm pretty sure I'm going to let that membership expire. I've had just too many disappointments at their properties, not that my hopes are ever too high. This property was cleaner than many of the Best Westerns I've stayed in, but there were too many surprises for my taste. For me it's a tarnished brand, even with their relatively new three-tiered structure that makes expectations a little more clear. The location is great. If you like sports bars, the Tilted Kilt is an interesting place to go.

“A great stay awaits!” I stayed at the Millenium Hilton over the Labor Day 2003 holiday. Except for a few billing errors that were promptly taken care of, everything about our stay was flawless.Our room was spacious and comfortable. The view overlooking the World Trade Center site was breathtaking and somber. People pass by the site all hours of the night. A highlight of our stay was enjoying watching the awesome plasma TVs after a long day of activity.I highly recommend this hotel. Hilton has spent a fortune sprucing this place up after 9/11 and it shows.The staff was wonderful--very friendly and without a big city uber-attitude.

“First time here” So I stayed here this past weekend for a conference. (Previous conferences had been at another hotel just down the street for the previous three years). The lobby, the bars, banquet rooms, and guest rooms all looked great. I was in a room on the 14th floor facing the freeway and really didn't have any problems with the freeway noise (make sure the window is closed all the way and the lever handle is closed). While we had a discounted rate for parking and internet access, the regular rates are the market rates in the downtown core.One option that is offered here is self parking, versus valet only at many downtown locations. They need a "overnight hotel guests only" policy for the self-parking - especially on busy weekends (or they already have this, then they need to enforce it). The single elevator into the 5 floors of the basement parking garage was quick. Valet parking takes 15-20 minutes to retrieve your car, so they are not using the same self-park garage The only real complaint from this weekend was the elevators,There are 5 elevators. At some point through the weekend, we were in 4 of them. 2 of them are newer, the other 3 older. The waits were long though..... 5 to 10 minutes most of the time.

“The best service” My 2 favorite things about the hotel: 1) friendliness 2) rooftop pool and hot tub The concierge, the bellboys, the valets, all were extremely personable, helpful, and friendly. Very professional. Always remembered us. Went out of their way to help us with our needs. I don't think you could have slapped the smile off the concierge's face. The rooms were upscale and clean. We had a gorgeous view from the 10th floor of the Bay. I highly recommend you request a Bay view. The free in-room safe was ample and a nice perq that we took advantage of by using. The beds were heavenly to sink into. It's a great location, convenient to lovely fountains, and an easy walk to nearby Seaport Village, where there are lovely outdoor restaurants and shops. I absolutely loved the 6th floor rooftop pool and hot tub. Definitely not enough chairs for the guests, though. Wonderful spot to sit and have a drink. I would also bring my kids to this hotel and enjoy the pool. Hotel is kid friendly. Price kindof high.

“Room with a View” We recently stayed at the Baltimore Waterfront Marriott for one night during a business trip. It is a very nice hotel, fairly new, beautifully done. We arrived at 7 pm, were welcomed cheerily, and I was given an upgrade, VIP status with a corner room and a beautiful view of the Harbor. Very nice room , super clean and nicely arranged. We had dinner in the hotel as well, at the 700 Grille, very tasty. Overall, great stay for a business trip.

“Wonderful airport hotel” The Hyatt Harbourside is located near the airport and offer a wonderful view of Boston's skyline or of the airport. In either case, it's a fantastic view. There is a free and very efficient shuttle service from/to the airport. The lobby offer a great view of the city's skyline. The check-in was courteous and quick, but not more (not especially friendly). I received the room type I had reserved (Sheraton doesn't always do that). At check in I requested to receive the Wall Street Journal instead of the content free (!) USA Today. I was told no problem. But of course the next day I received the USA Today. When I went back to front desk to ask for a WSJ, they told me that they don't carry it at all in the hotel, except at the gift shop ! Room was spacious, clean and very well decorated. Bed was confortable. The view of the airport was fantastic and strangely enough no noise from airport was heard in the room. The meeting facilities are modern and confortable, but Intenet access that you buy in the room doesn't work in the meeting room ! Very disappointing. Of course, in term of location you have to be aware that there is nothing around since you are on airport ground. The easy solution is to go downtown using water taxi (17$ round trip). So a very nice, modern, confortable and up-to-the-standard hotel, but with a few minor glitches. The Intenet one though is hard to swallow.

“When in NYC this is the only place I want to stay.” At first I was expecting a big let down,all the hype on TA I was bracing for disapointment. As soon as you walk in you are greeted by the smell of fresh flowers.Everyone was super friendly and helpful. We got a 1 bedroom studio on the 333rd floor.The view of the Chrysler building at night as well as a glimpse of Times square was awsome.The room was large and the bathroom was large also. We took advantage of the kitchen. We would eat a large lunch and bring the leftovers to the fridge.You are a block from the subway and if you have a unlimited subway card you can bolt to the room really quick to put the food in the fridge. The housekeeping was great they did a good job cleaning all our junk in the kitchen. We would go to the Duane Reade and stock up on Cokes.We would also buy bottles of water and freeze them so the next day when we were all over NYC we would have cold water for a cheap drink.I took a small backpack with me. If we needed a snack the Murry Market is next door and have the best salads and sandwichs for the price. I will be back in NYC and I will only stay at the Affinia Dumont

“Nice location and nice facilities” Very nice facilities. Not having a pool wasn't popular with the kids but they survived. We walked to Beale Street and there are many restaurants close. Nice location right across from FedEx Arena. Free Internet was a plus.

“Beautiful grounds” The grounds of this property are the most beautiful we have experienced in the Phoenix area. Unfortunately our room, a valencia casita, was not the most beautiful. I made the mistake of not reserving a designer casita, which apparently are updated. Our casita was old, the lay out was odd and the bathroom was just like a best western. I really enjoy having a beautiful room with a great large bathtub in the bathroom. We were offered to upgrade to a terrace room but it was a bit small, the japanese soaking tub in the room was like a small jacuzzi but the way it is you are not able to lay down in the water. You have to be sitting upright as though you are on a step in the very deep end of a pool. Our lunch that we had in T-Cooks was good, cocktail hour in the bar was fun and I will definitely be back so long as I book a designer casita. I was sad to leave the gorgeous grounds.

“A Business Travelers Delight” Conveniently located in downtown Phoenix. Superb and friendly staff. Extremely clean. Lots of common area. Great bar and the restaurant is very, very good with a decent menu. The rooms are comfortable but average in size. I'd highly recommend for business. But I think the rooms are a little small for a couple looking a romantic weekend.

“Basic, great location and a little dated.” Stayed here at the end of October, booked in with a group of students. Had heard varying degrees of negative reports in regard to the condition of the place, unclean beds, bathrooms and really poor hotel. To begin with it was very average, ideal for a group of students who would only be using rooms for rest at night. They were not rooms to lounge around in, those comforts do not exist here!! The rooms were huge, basic facilities, showers ideal for someone four foot high!!!, clean towels and beds made everyday, that was our experience, but did not hear this from previous people who stayed there. Old style bathrooms, old enamel baths. All rooms had tv's. The location of the hotel is brilliant, across from Madison Sq. Garden and Penn Station, Macys is one block away and Empire State likewise behind hotel. Ideal place really to stay for a short break were little time is spent in the hotel. All we needed was a clean bed and clean bathroom, we got that. Doormen were excellent and bags were all sorted at a small charge from the bus. Shop on ground floor good for soft drinks and coffee. Checkout was depositing keys in a box, so no queuing. A very busy place, when we checked in there were only 19 rooms left out of the 1700. Lobby always busy, all sorts, from business men, to shoppers and tourists. Obviously alot of people like this hotel. Would stay here again with a group. Perfect for that. Basic hotel, great location..

“Old world elegance in NYC” The Pierre is classic old world elegance. From white gloved elevator operators, impeccable staff, and excellent service. The hotel underwent an extensive renovation a few years ago. Like all older hotels, there is only so much room you have to work with. That said the rooms are small and so are the bath rooms (at least in the standard size room that we had). Of course this is NYC and most rooms are on the smaller side. Not spending a lot of time in the room, this is no big deal to me. From the moment I entered the hotel, I felt like I was stepping back in time. In todays world, what you pay generally does not equate to good service, here it does. I don't require much, but I do expect friendly staff, quick response to room service and house keeping requests, and overall professionalism. They hit the mark on all of these. The accommodations were comfortable, good lighting, and it was clean. The location is excellent, across from Central Park and by some of the best shopping in the world. I tend to lean towards hotels that are a little more contemporary, but I would definately recommend staying here and would stay here again.

“Great hotel in a good location - wine bar...Yum!” This a terrific hotel for business travel. The rate - $139.00 for a king room - was a terrific deal. Free internet available as well. The continental breakfast was more than adequate and satisfying. Service staff at the breakfast, front counter, and bar was very quick and professional. For the wine fanciers, Penn's View is in the Guiness Book of Worlds Records for having the a huge wine selection. You can order dozens, if not hundreds, of wines - by the glass . The sommelier was thoroughly knowledgeable. Its location was good with many restaurants nearby, the Market-Penn subway line about 1.5 blocks away and with cabs right around the corner. As a "chain" hotel follower, it was great to see outside of the box chains for a switch!

“Nice Hotel...Great Location to Gaslamp!” This hotel is right by Petco Park, Gaslamp, and everything in San Diego you might want to do in the downtown location. Walk outside the door and you are in Gaslamp. The hotel itself, as one other reviewer mentioned, is like a casino without any machines or gambling. The lobby is bright, flashing lights, strange front desk comprised of 4 individual stations. In spite of the annoying lobby, the check in and out process is very efficient. They take your cell number if your room is not ready, entering on the computer screen, twist the screen around so you can verify your cell number. Checking out, they simply spin the screen (if you've prepaid) and verify your e-mail to send you a receipt. Now, for the rooms....very modern, stark. The rooms have everything you need, except instructions on how to operate the shower, where the plug in is by the sink....(p.s. you pull out the drawer by the sink and it is to the right behind the door face). Very strange. Apparently they are all individually privately owned. This hotel is nice for a convention attendee, you can walk around safely. There are a million places to eat and little shops nearby.
“Nice hotel” This hotel is very nice. The staff is great, the rooms are spacious and clean, and the food is wonderful.

“gutes Hotel der Mittelklasse” Gutes Hotel der Mittelklasse, mitten in der Stadt - sehr gute Lage, freundlicher Service und hilfsbereites Personal , gutes Preis- Leistungsverhältnis Ich würde es buchen. Die Lage - direkt im Herzen von Manhattan (ca. 200 Meter bis zum Times Sq.) - ist einfach ideal. Das Hotel verfügt leider über kein eigenes Restaurant. Der Gast kann allerdings das direkt neben dem Hotel gelegene Restaurant - der Zugang ist sogar über das Hotel möglich - benutzen. Die Preise sind aber überzogen. Beim Frühstück sollte ich sogar eine zweite Tasse Kaffee bezahlten. Dies ist in den USA vollkommen unüblich.

“beautiful new rooms” Have to agree...this is a super place to stay, especially on business. The breakfast & the gym are very nice and security is pretty tight. Staff is friendly. Try to get a corner room on a high floor. Overall, very comfortable and good location.

“Needs Some Updating, But Would Return” The staff at this hotel is wonderful! From check-in to their Oakley's Room where we had breakfast to Derrick's Bar.....friendly and helpful. We were greeted warmly at our 9pm check-in and given 2 huge, warm chocolate chip walnut cookies! Before we left, we were given 2 bottles of water and put on the HHOnors floor and recognized as members. ALL OF THE CARPETING needs to be replaced in this hotel, but we would stay again. The common areas are very spacious and this hotel offers a nice fitness room, pool and even one washing machine and dryer! There is also a small gift shop on the way to the elevators. Our Rm. 623 was very well appointed; nice bed linens and good mattress. The bathtub is rather "low" and there is nothing to keep you from slipping so be careful. Liked the nice grab bar!!! Really good toiletries provided. Our room had a microwave and sm. fridge. I would have like more lighting in the bathroom; hard to get make-up on in such dim lighting. We had a buffet breakfast one morning and it was very, very good. $14 and there was everything you could have wanted; the fresh fruit was divine! Even bran muffins were tasty. I really enjoyed their smooth, creamy grits. Our waitress was very attentive and her early morning smile was a welcome site! We did use the bar one night; I think it was Derrick's. We just ordered a couple of appetizers and both were DELICIOUS. The Tex Mex Quesadillas were out of this world delicious and came with a huge bowl of sour cream, guacamole (YUM) and pica de gallo. (Not sure about the spelling, ok?) Also ordered the coconut shrimp which came with two different dips. Both of these appetizers were delicious and plenty for our party of four. We would stay here again in a heartbeat. We paid $84 on the AAA rate.

“Excellent airport hotel in Seattle” This is the airport we stay at whenever we fly out of SeaTac. It is one of the few airport hotels with “extended park and jet” rates, so if you are going away for a couple of weeks, for just a few dollars more than you would spend to park your car at an off-airport lot, you can get a room for the night across from the airport and not have to get up quite so early for your morning flight. There is a 24 hour shuttle service to and from the airport, and we have never waited more than 10 minutes for it. On your return to Seattle, when you call the shuttle from the airport you also give your valet number, and your car will be waiting for you at the front of the hotel by the time you get there. The rooms themselves are of average size and clean, with all the usual amenities. The beds are comfortable, and staff are friendly and helpful. The fitness room has lots of treadmills and ellipticals, plus free weights. There is a restaurant on site, though we have not eaten there so cannot comment on it. We have stayed at several hotels near SeaTac in the past, but this is the one we inevitably return to and have the best experiences with.

“Location, Location, Location and pretty nice as well.” Simply put, you can't be closer to Times Square and Broadway then the Millennium Hotel, the hotel has been built around the old Hudson Theater and half a block away is Times Square, it's truly in the middle of it all. The lobby is striking, old Deco look that's been updated, lobby bar is the first thing you see from the 44th street entrance and does fine breakfast and has only one beer on tap, huh? Front desk and service were friendly and helpful, I stayed in the premier towers side, so was a bit strange that the main front desk sends you back to another front desk in the premier elevator lobby. Room was good sized, clean, the shower stall tiling/grouting could use some attention, and man, does the AC work, it has two settings, off or freezer mode. I guess this is good, the day I checked out the temp was tilting to 100 degrees. Needless to say, turning off the AC is any easy solution. My firm put on an event in the Hudson Theater, it's truly a historic old venue, you cater food in to the old lobby area, there's curtains that divide up the lobby from the theater seating. Catering was great, the local hotel technicians were great to work with as well. We also had sessions in the conference rooms in the main tower, these were fine as well. Would gladly return to the Millennium, and for those of you who are constant dwellers at the Marriott across the street as I was, this is a great alternative stay.

“Great place to stay!” My husband and I had a weekend getaway Dec 17-18 and we stayed in room 606. Location: It's great. I usually prefer to stay in midtown, but this is a great option too! It's right across from the Lincoln Center, which looked especially gorgeous decorated for Christmas. The subway is also just across the street and Central Park is just a short walk. Lobby and hotel itself: It's swanky. The lobby is very impressive and fits the boutique label. The bar was hopping and looked fun, but since I'm pregnant, we didn't partake. Check-in was fine. I asked for a quiet room since I'm a light sleeper and preferably a king or queen bed. Room: We ended up on the 6th floor in a small room with a queen-sized bed. There really was not a view - just saw another building since we were in the back of the property. I understand why the guy who checked us in put us there though - it was quiet. We didn't hear cars honking or traffic sounds, and we were at the very end of the hall. Yes, it was small, but it was perfectly fine for us for 1 night. The bed was awesome, so comfortable! Be aware, if you are allergic to feathers/down, let them know. There was a feather bed, feather pillows, and a down comforter. Fortunately, we're not allergic and I love the softness of down bedding. Linens were high quality. The bathroom is tiny. The sink is poorly designed and placed. It was very challenging to wash my face and even washing my hands was difficult due to the strange design. It looks nice but the functionality is lacking. The bathroom amenities are very nice quality. We had plenty of hot water but the shower pressure was just ok due to the rain-style shower head. Again, it looks good, but not the most functional. Other thoughts: This is an old building. It gives it plenty of charm, but there are also quirks. When the people in the room next to us took a shower, dang, it was loud. It sounded like a loud sink was running right next to my head. Fortunately I was able to fall back alseep, but it was annoying. Overall, my husband and I really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely visit again (if the price is right).

“Great stay!” In my last review, I pointed out the executive lounge wasn't up to scratch, well, they've improved it! Great lounge, good choice at breakfast, always staffed with friendly people. Room was spotless and spacious, staff were friendly, couldn't do better! Free upgarde to executive floor as a platinum priority club member, didn't have to ask! Great five day stay!

“convenient - nothing special/post-stay customer service could use improvement” Stayed here on a Saturday night. Didn't use any hotel services, so can't comment on those. The door staff were great. I recieved an upgrade from a two bed one bathroom, to a two bed two bathroom room. Of course my luck, the shower in my bathroom was broken, so I ended up having to use the other one (thankfully I did have that option). The only negative experience I encountered was post-stay in that I received a charge on my credit card for a dinner at the restaurant, on the eve of the day I checked-out. While this was dealt with quickly upon calling the hotel a few days later, the person I spoke to, did not go out of their way to apologize for the inconvenience. I also got a sense from the tone of voice and the general manner with wich the person interacted with me that their going in attitude was this was a correct credit card charge and that it was going to be to me to prove otherwise. Luckily for me, it was easy. If you are a walker, then, the walk to and from Giordano's Pizzeria on Rush is definitely doable, allowing you to experience Michigan Avenue.

“Excellent Stay. Better location than you would think.” We stayed here four nights in November and had a great stay. Really liked the kitchen in the room with a full refrigerator, freezer, dishwasher, and microwave. Room was of average size but this hotel is pretty new and in great shape. Lobby is beautiful and breakfast area is clean and spacious on the level below the lobby. The breakfast was well stocked and contained many hot and cold items. We ate breakfast every day and there was always seating available and the breakfast area was not insanely crowded either. However, I am not sure how booked the hotel was. The hotel is located on the border of the nice area of downtown and a more run down area. North of this hotel I would guess is an area few tourists venture. However, we never felt unsafe and we walked many times at night. The hotel is less than a five minute walk to the Alamo or the Riverwalk and less than a block from the Buckhorn Saloon. There is a continuous fan in the room that will help block out any unwanted noise while you are trying to sleep. Valet was decent, if a little bit pricey at $23. Usually took about ten minutes to retrieve the car as there is no parking garage in the hotel. They park your car about a couple of blocks away, which accounts for it taking some time for the valet to retrieve your car. The valet drop off is on the southbound Broadway St. side of the hotel.

“clean, friendly, convenient” great hotel in a restored historical building. Very clean rroms and our king suite was very spacious. Be sure to ask for a room on floors 10-15 as they have water views. Happy hour at the Bistro was nice and affordable. Indoor poll was also nice and clean. 20 minutes to the market and the baseball stadium.

“ok” The hotel was clean and very pleasant staff. Beautiful lobby. Very clean and all were large rooms! Area recommendations Georgetown is wonderful. Full of activity and excellent restaurants! Getting around Staying at the Melrose allows you to get around on the Metro. It takes you all over the city so you can park your car for the trip!

“Good place to visit NASCAR race shops” It is very close to downtown Charlotte as well as most of the NASCAR race shops. i visited 19 different shops, had some great BBQ and some drinks at Whiskey River before spending a half day at the NASCAR Hall of Fame. Most Embassy Suites are good and this one was no different. Clean, good size and a good breakfast. The staff here was more friendly that most and that is saying something since most of the ones i have been to have really nice folks. My only downside is that they charge you $10 per day for internet. Mid-level hotels need to give away internet.

“Fun Boutique Hotel that Loves Pets” I stayed at the Helix hotel in Washington DC when in town for a conference in June. I was looking for a hotel that was close to the conference but reasonably priced. I remembered that each of the Kimpton Hotels I've stayed in had a unique design and offering but that they all had complimentry coffe and tea in the morning and a happy hour at 5pm. Little did I know that they had a pet happy hour! They have an outdoor patio space where hotel guests and local residence brought their pets to enjoy happy hour. It was a lot of fun and everyone was really friendly. I would definately come back here with my dog. The hotel rooms were a decent size for a regular room. The way rooms are designed the bed was in an alcove with a sheer curtain at the end of the bed so it felt a little seperate from the rest of the room. The bathroom was very clean but small and there wasn't a closet but rather a rack to hang your clothes as you walk into the bathroom. The hotel staff was very friendly and even brought us a complimentary glass of champagne when we missed the end of the happy hour. They also have a nice restaurant which serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, however I didn't eat there. The hotel is walking distance from shops and restaurants so you can explore the neighborhood and feel safe. I would stay here again.

“All of the good, none of the bad!!” Had made reservations at another downtown hotel, based on price, but still read every Intercontinental review, wishing and hoping we could stay there. Shortly before the trip, I found an ad on Travelzoo for the IC for a price less expensive than we were paying for a hotel two blocks off Michigan, and booked it immediately. Got in after an early flight, and the doorman met our taxi. He gave us receipts for the bags, and told us they would bring them to our room when the room was ready, so we were pleasantly surprised when we were told they had a room on the 25th floor ready for us then. We were checked in, and on our way to the room before 11am! AND, our bags beat us to the room! No upsell attempts, no glares because we had booked through a third party website, just a pleasant, quick, and courteous process. The room was small, sure, but no surprise there. It was, however, clean, comfortable, and very well laid out. Not much drawer space, and a beautiful flat screen TV that we put on for a total of 5 minutes to check the weather report. The view was facing the other tower, so nothing great there, but, I wasn't there to sit and look out the window. The room was quiet, even though it backed up to the elevators (didn't hear them, even once). The room was made up perfectly by the housekeeping staff...everything immaculate, everything fully stocked. Beds were extremely comfortable. The location is the prime #1 reason to stay there. Walking distance to everything, and overall, I have to say, this was the best hotel stay I have had in a long time. Highly recommend the Corner Bakery (they are everywhere) and, before you go here, do your homework, read the reviews, and go in with an open mind. You will be glad you did.

“Second time around - still great!” I just visited this hotel again for the second time on a trip to San Antonio. Awesome service, everyone is friendly and pleasant. Rooms were clean and we had enough room for the kids and the puppy. The kids slept on the sleeper-sofa and they were comfortable. Their pet policy is great, just 15.00 for the first night then 10.00 after that. Plus there's a large pet area in the back of the hotel to walk them. There was a strange mystery meat during breakfast the first day but that was just 'odd' not bad. Everything was fresh and the staff refilled all the items constantly. I will stay here everytime I visit San Antonio and will highly recommend this to my clients.

“Hard to rate... The good and bad.” I am currently staying at this hotel. Here's the run down. DO NOT stay here if the following is important to you: 1. Internet - None and the phone line pulls a 21.1 connection 2. Unlimited phone calls/talk or dial up - .15 a minute... period 3. Modern furnishings - I think the decor is from the early 80's ... it's almost back in style, modern retro, loads of chrome, good enough shape, though. 4. Concierge services STAY HERE if the following is important to you: 1. Room, plenty of it, too! We have a full 1 bedroom apt with a large patio overlooking 38th St. 2. If you like to feel like you are staying in a residential building. 3. Need a decent clean place in Midtown for very little $$ 4. Are fed up with being nickled and dimed with tips at other hotels (but be sure to tip the cute Polish doorman when you arrive and leave) 5. Like NO snobbery... zippo, none I am used to 4 and 5 star hotels. I just could not pass up the deal here, less than 100.00 for a business trip that was hard to justify without it! I will not stay here again for business. I need better business services. But it is perfectly fine for those on vacation trying to save $$$

“Wonderful stay-4 1/2 stars” We had a wonderful stay at the Mansion del Rio. The decor in the common areas perfectly reflects the uniqueness of San Antonio as does the evening turndown service.The concierges , bell staff , wait staff, maintenance and front desk personnel were uniformly helpful. This is a very well run hotel. When we called for a maintenance issue late on a Saturday night it was resolved efficiently and within minutes. We had a room with a shared balcony (which was not a problem at all) overlooking the Riverwalk which was the ideal spot from which to view "Coffins on Parade". The food in Las Canarias was excellent and the bar tenders in the bar were very accommodating of special requests as well. The hotel is very convenietly situated and many attractions are just minutes away on foot. Our room was a bit on the small side.

“Satisfactory Hotel” Stayed at this hotel last fall while visiting my daughter. Although the hotel was fine, it wasn't as nice as other Kimpton's I've stayed at. The room seemed old-- stained carpet, just a little dark and dingy all around. Scratchy towels. The staff wasn't even as friendly as Kimpton employees usually are. Location is fine.

“Classic Hotel with Modern Amenities” Upscale lobby, restaurant, great food, service, classy hotel. Only worth it if you can get a deal. The top restaurant (top floor) is outstanding and has a great dance scene where the locals apparently dine out and dance. Very upscale, dinner dress/suit type of deal. Nice staff, elegant, marble lobby, old world charm in a modern hotel. The celebrities stay here, like Connery and others, and for no wonder. Highly recommend this place to anyone staying in SF for business or pleasure. Very expensive overall, but very exclusive, private, quiet, and accomodating staff above all. Well-run place, we loved the place.

“Nice adult hotel in Chelsea” Stayed here for one night after seeing Oprah at Radio City. This was a great location away from the craziness of Times Square. The rooms are small, but very well put together with a kind of upscale feel. They do seem to cater to the gay crowd or business crowd, rather than families. The area is chock full of great restaurants and stores and you a a couple of blocks form the High line park. The bathrooms were very nice with a walkin shower with a rainfall shower head. The sink area did leave little room for toiletries. The service was GREAT!!! Everyone we encountered was very welcoming and warm. On the roof there is an open air deck with lounge chairs & tables to have your morning coffee or justt relax with a stunning view of the Empire State Bldg. I highly recommend the Gem Chelsea if you are looking for a laid back, upscale, quiet hotel in a great neighborhood.

“Beautiful View - Nice Room” I enjoyed the view from the 20th floor, which was overlooking the bay. (A photo is attached.) The room was comfortable, clean, like you'd expect from a Westin. The closet is a bit small, and like most hotels these days, pre-stocked with too much crap to allow you store much in them (Blanket, pillow, safe, ironing board, iron, luggage jack, etc.) I really appreciated the work desk with numerous outlets, but the chair doesn't go high enough to make the whole scenario functional. I'm typing uphill at the moment. The lobby is very nice with dramatic two story escalators. The service is excellent here. And the food that I've sampled was quite good!

“Good location, average hotel” The hotel is centrally located in Philadelphia. There is free wifi which worked just fine. The hotel offers valet parking (25 USD per night), however be aware that the garage is very tight. The rooms were spacious, but a very small bathroom with toilet and tub. Thw hotel also offers a roof top pool which was clean and nice enough. The breakfast was free, however very basic.

“Great hotel” Hotel is nice and rooms are very clean. The hotel staff was wonderful, from the minute you check-in to the minute you check out..The staff is extremely friendly. Had some food in the bar and it was ok. The coffee shop is not good at all. The hotel is baout 15 minutes from West Hollywood and 10 minutes from Warner bros. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Nice but didn't like nickel and diming” As others have said, this is a well kept, nicely located hotel for a pre-cruise overnight stay. Was here on a priceline reservation for three rooms since I was taking children and grandchildren on a Disney cruise to Mexico. When checking in we were informed that in order to get a room with two beds, an additional $10 fee was required beyond the priceline bid. I have NEVER before encountered a surcharge for a room with two beds and I travel on a priceline reservation all the time. To use the computer in the business center required a $5 fee, even to print out a boarding pass. Again, a first. Too bad such nice facilities are marred by fees that almost all hotels provide for free.

“Unless you get a great deal, stay somewhere else” The hotel was fine. But you can probably do better. It's about a 10-minute walk to the nearest metro stop, so if you plan to take that a lot, opt for something closer. You also have to walk about three blocks to get to the nearest coffee shop. The hotel itself just doesn't quite have it together. The rooms are definitely tiny and could use a refresh.The staff was friendly, but slightly inept. I didn't get the type of room I'd reserved, so had to go back to the lobby to change it, then was sent to a room that was still occupied, so had to go back and change it again. The clerk kept saying "my pleasure." I wanted to tell her to drop the script and just fix the problem. We also had problems with hot water, the air conditioning, and our shower curtain was held together by a safety pin.

“Überraschend gut” Das Hotel liegt wie der Name bereits vermuten lässt nicht in der Innenstadt, sondern einige km von dieser entfernt in der Nähe der Marins bzw. des Internationalen Flughafens von San Diego. Zum Erreichen den übrigen Attraktionen der Stadt braucht man daher ein eigenes Auto oder ein Taxi. Das Hotel verfügt über zwei voneinander getrennte Gebäudeblöcke, die angeblich über einen unterschiedlichen Raumkomfort verfügen. Das mir zugewiesene Zimmer überraschte mich aber positiv.

“Great Central Location, Charming Rooms - Great Staff” My husband had to go to Seattle on Business so I tagged along. Hotel Monaco had a special rate and we love kimpton hotels - so we booked. We were very happy! Cozy room with living room and bedroom, lovely bathroom with great products - our little fishy kevin passed away during our stay (not due to anything we did!) but we managed to enjoy ourselves despite this traumatic experience (totally kidding) This is in the center of everything, staff so helpful - and always love the kimpton's wine happy hour. You will not be disappointed with the stay if you chose Hotel Monaco!

“Superb” My wife and I stayed for a combination business meeting/couples weekend. On line reservation process was easy and, from what I could tell, truly the lowest published rate. Prior to arrival the concierge recommended restaurants and travel arrangements from the airport. On arrival our room was ready, bags serviced with tip offered but not accepted, as this is a no-tip property. Welcome half bottle of wine arrived after our luggage drop.The room/suite was luxurious, clean, and updated (see pictures). Bed slept well. I did not appreciate any road noise or disturbances. All of our requests were answered without issues. They do have a first-come-first-served 'local' car that is complimentary within a 2 mile radius; we did not opt to use it but a very nice touch. We tried the Cognac lounge, it was nice, but no desserts or finger foods offered. We brunched at Balsan, their restaurant, which was certainly an above average place. The location is great; easy walk to restaurants and the 'Mircale Mile' shopping. While we did not have any spa treatments, we did enjoy the lap pool, fitness area (very large and well equipped), eucalyptus steam room, jacuzzi, and sauna. All are well up-kept, peaceful, and not overcrowded. Yes, it is quite pricey, but the location, property, service, and spa amenities are truly in a class of their own.

“Fine hotel ... not "great" by any stretch of the imagination.” I recently stayed at the Red Lion in downtown Seattle for three nights. I read the TripAdvisor reviews prior to checking in and knew from what I read that the "paper thin walls" would probably be an issue. Believe me, the notes about the walls are not exaggerated. They are incredibly thin. I couldn't believe how well I could hear everything (*every* thing) my neighbors did. It made for restless nights. Beyond the walls made of balsa wood, the hotel has a bit of a dated feel. Colors are the typical golds, ruby, and forest greens. The polyester bed spread seemed cheesy, the bath towels seemed too thin, and the bathroom fixtures themselves were quite poor. My bathtub filled with water when I showered and drained very slowly. The toilet took 3-4 flushes to get everything taken care of ... oddly enough, since it made quite a stir with its mighty sucking action ... which seemed to do little. The iron in the room is cheap, cheap, cheap and left brown smudges on my company shirts I needed to wear to the tradeshow I was attending. The ironing board was quite stained and burnt. The front desk staff are quite nice and helpful. They are every bit as helpful and friendly as you would expect at a finer hotel. The hotel's fitness facility is fairly good. There are treadmills, elliptical trainers, free weights, and a few machines. Towels and water are provided there. My only issue here was that it was very stuffy in the room. They need some fans in there. The hotel also provides guests with the option to purchase a pass to a full service health club nearby for a nominal fee. As noted in many previous reviews, the location is superb. But Seattle has many fantastically situated hotels with much better room facilities and upkeep. Personally, I'd shell out a few more clams and choose the Mayflower Park, the Andra, or the Hyatt.

“Second try a charm in Charm City” Thanks to TA reviewers, I checked on this hotel in Jan 2012 and three days before arrival in March 2012, to see if the pool was in order given the TA disrepair comments. Of course after a 3-day prior to arrival call, it was out of service for the entire week of my stay. They were kind enough to offer me a night back on them. We arrive on the weekend of the Grand Prix Baltimore. Although the pool closes at 9 pm and doesn't open until 10 am on weekends, I appreciate the fact that this pristine pool setting is guard by an extremely courteous lifeguard. The rooms and beds are immaculate. If you can, ask for a 7th floor room in this restored 1900's bank. The 7th floor rooms numbered in the 7teens thru 720's has gorgeous vaulted ceilings with redoux marble. Full self service breakfast, awesome staff, convenient valet service, really nice business center and proximety to Inner Harbor (2 1/2 blocks), restaurants and on this weekend, the Grand Prix is within walking distance to Little Italy and the main attraction too! Beds! Beds are the comfy pillow top softness of the Courtyard, Holiday Inn Express (updated of course) quality but comfortable firm type FYI. Adequate Fitness Room. Still thumbs up.

“Our suite was "sweet"” Reserved a suite at the Amalfi, May 16-18, 2007, for a family vacation. The suites are advertised as being "spacious", but it was a little smaller than I had anticipated. The king bedroom was quite large and one wall is nothing but curved windows, which is quite dramatic, but the living room (with sofa bed) was a little crowded for four people (with luggage, etc.). The bathroom is spacious, good lighting and nice amenities. It was quite expensive, but many of the hotels were booked due to the Restaurant Association being in town, so maybe that's why rates were higher. They provide turn-down service with chocolates and our suite had two honors bars, two coffee makers and glass coffee mugs, two ice buckets and four wine glasses. When we arrived at 2:45 p.m. the computer was down and they could not check us in. But within 10-15 minutes, it was up and running and the front desk staff (called experience designers) were apologetic and accommodating. They have a very nice cocktail and appetizer hour in the late afternoon with free cocktails (try their lemon martini) and meats, cheeses and breads. The atmosphere in the lounge is intimate, with candles and music. Each of the hotel's six floors provides a continental breakfast on each floor where guests feel comfortable enough to come out in robes or pj's to grab coffee, juice, nice assortment of pastries, and fruit. They provide wire basket trays for your convenience to take food back to your room and it's available for a nice timeframe (two hours). The Amalfi is in a good location - only 3-4 blocks from the Wrigley Building on Michigan Ave. and a couple blocks from the Loop District. It's a short walk to catch the Red Line. If it's raining when you're in town and you're looking for a fun inside activity, the 10 Pin is just a little over a block away. Located in the House of Blues, the 10 Pin is an upscale bowling alley and martini bar. This was our second time there and it was as fun as our first visit. They have great, inexpensive food. Last year, we went in the afternoon and got right in, no crowds. This time we didn't go until about 8 p.m. and all the lanes were full, so there was a 30-minute wait. It's a little pricey, but the atmosphere is great and it's a lot of fun. If you have children, I would go in the afternoon. Another great family place is Ed Debevic's, a 50's style diner at 640 N. Wells St. (about a 10 block walk from the hotel). The waiters sing and dance and are a real "hoot." All the small kids were having a ball . . . and the food's not bad!
“景色最高!さすがっという感じでした。” やはり、さすがマンダリンという感じでした。46階のパークビュウーの部屋に滞在しましたが、セントラルパークとビルが両方見えて、昼間、夕暮れ、夜景、朝焼けとそのときによって雰囲気も変わるので、よかったです。1日に二度の清掃もよかったです。まあ、それなりのお値段ですが。。。

“Wonderful” Got a great offer to that hotel and didn ́t think to long about taking that chance! When I got there I even got a complimentary upgrade to the Waldorf Towers and really loved it. Spacious room, wonderful lobby, great central location. Always again, but i doubt to get a similar offer!

“Nice Little No-Frills Place Near the Beach” Priced a bit on the high side for a place without the "extra" amenities (restaurant, bar, exercise area, pool, etc.) of a bit chain hotel, but it's clean, relatively recently renovated, and close to a number of restaurants and the beach. Location, location, location may make up for the missing stuff. Right next door are Mexican and Thai restaurants. As you walk a couple blocks toward the beach you'll find more restaurant choices and a number of drinking spots. There's a Cold Stone Creamery, a Starbucks, a liquor store, and a convenience store, too. They have parking right at the hotel and across the alley in back, fairly reasonably priced at $7/night. There's a basic continental breakfast starting at 7 a.m., too. Traffic's a bit noisy on the Washington Street side, but it's not too bad.

“Great Service, Very Noisy” I really like this hotel. Everyone we had contact with was friendly and helpful from the valet to the engineer who came to fix the thermostat. But, wow, the noise is maddening. Our room was bright and clean with a desk that ran all the way across the room. The view was Coit Tower to Alcatraz and beyond. The thermostat didn't work and an engineer was there within five minutes of the call. Service everywhere in the hotel was beyond expectation. But beware, it is one of the noisiest hotels I've ever experienced. The room to room noise level is bad. From 9pm to 11pm we were treated to the giggling and yelling of the family next door. Noise from outside was about as bad. We were on the 21st floor and it sounded like we were at street level. Still, it is a very good hotel in a great location. I have to recommend it. Just bring your noise cancelling earphones.

“The hotel is a 10 in general, but the room is a 6” The hotel is excellent, very well located in N Michigan Ave, great food, restaurant, breakfast (very expensive) fitness center, service and etc, but the room needs to be better. It's small, tied, the shower is old and not good, and the worst is the lack of space (a good table) to work with your computer. There is only a small table and believe me or not, but without any power plug around.

“A Really Nice and Dependable Hotel” As a native of Austin, my family and I return frequently for pleasure and business. A majority of the time, we stay at the Renaissance. For the sake of comparison, we've stayed at the Four Seasons, the Marriott Capitol, the Hyatt, the Omni, the Driskill, the downtown Embassy Suites, and the downtown, Doubletree. Without a doubt, the best hotel in Austin is the Four Seasons, but the cost prohibits frequent stays there. The Renaissance is our definite number two, closely followed by the Hyatt. The rooms are quite large, furnished in "Central Texas Chic", and have excellent bedding and more than adequate bathrooms. On site dining is above average, and the staff are dependably helpful. The hotel is "small dog" friendly. There is good adjacent shopping and the neighborhood, removed from the central city, is quiet and scenic. We've never had a disappointing stay. The only potential negative for new or infrequent visitors to Austin is the northwest location, quite far from the airport and a good 15-20 minute drive from UT or downtown; taxi fare one way is $50 from the airport, so car rental is a better option. We enthusiastically recommend the Renaissance and always look forward to returning.

“Great location” I attended a meeting at Hynes Convention Center. The Hotwire price was about 40% off the convention rate. Rooms were clean. Elevators were easy to get. Easy to get to subway. Lot of shopping and restaurants around. Maid staff was honest - I left my wallet in the room when I checked out. I got back to the room and found the tip had been taken but my wallet was on the table without any contents missing.

“ペン・ステーション最寄り” 鉄道・地下鉄のペンステーションから徒歩圏内5分程。 部屋は多少狭いが、設備はインターナショナル・チェーンのレベルにあり、 ニューヨークを朝から晩まで楽しむ人ならば十分なレベル。 早朝(ペン・ステーションからの移動)、夜間(ミュージカル鑑賞後)も人通りがあり、 徒歩圏内ならばとても便利なロケーションであるといえよう。 近くにはミニー・マーケットや軽食屋が深夜まで開店しており、 何か欲しいものが出てきた時も問題ないであろう。 ビジネス・観光客、双方とも使い勝手が良いホテルであろう。

“Convenient Westwood Area Hotel” I stayed one night on business at the Palomar. The hotel is nice clean, safe and well located for the Westwood UCLA area. My only real complaint was they put in a handicap room, which is not particularly comfortable for a tall guy, since every thing is lowered down. The front desk didn't tell me that I was getting a "special room" which should have been done at check in. Most of the staff was very nice, a number of us staying there for the same meeting used the complimentary car service, "tip of the hat" to these guys they did a great job.

“Very nice hotel, but noisy” The Indigo is a very nice hotel and within walking distance of a lot of restaurants. It is also one the best smelling hotels I have been to. The staff was very helpful and the rooms were clean. My only complaint was the level of noise in the hotel. The staff does not turn off the elevator chime at night and you can hear it going off all hours of the night. Also, the peopledown the hall were having a party and were out in the hall being loud well past 12:00am.
“nice hotel” lovely hotel. nice room. helpful staff. decent location in the city. ran out of some food at breakfast, which seemed odd for an otherwise upscale hotel.

“A solid choice” I've stayed here a couple of times. This property is a renovated hotel adjacent to the historic part of Philadelphia, so if you want to see Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell etc you're all set. The interior is all new, modern. Service was very nice generally (athough the bell staff get busy with cars, so I had to go flag my own cab from across the street). The "waterfront" is a block away, but IHMO its not very nice. I did go running "along the river", which means past warehouses etc; little foot traffic. The hotel has a decent fitness center. One night I had to book the "club" rate, which does offer free internet and access to the lounge--overall a pretty good value if you have breakfast there. While you can walk around the old town area, its a long walk or cab ride to the city center or the arts area. Overall, this is a solid hotel for both leisure and business. I'd stay here again.

“Historic DC Hotel. Two Great Stays Here.” I stayed at the Mayflower for the second time recently when I was in DC for a weekend getaway. If you arrive during times of heavy traffic (which seems to be always in DC), expect to get honked at a time or two as you wait for the valet to get to you. After that, your worries are over. The hotel is beautiful, and the staff was so friendly and helpful. I got the room on priceline.com, and didn't expect to get the best room. However, I got a room on the top floor that was really nice. The girl at the front desk was particularly nice, and welcomed me to the Mayflower despite the fact that I probably booked the room for considerably less than most of the other guests. The door staff can catch a cab for you in no time so I would not at all recommend driving your own vehicle around DC. Traffic is terrible, and parking can be brutal. Also, there is a Metro station within 2 blocks of the hotel that makes catching the train overly simple. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Mayflower, and look forward to staying there again.

“zentral gelegen, geniales Hotel” das Sheraton ist optimal im Zentrum von Seattle gelegen, Man kann alle Sehenswürdikeiten und zum Hafen, wie auch Shopping zu Fuss machen. Parken ist wie überall dirket in der City mit 28 Dollar nicht ganz preiswert. Das Hotel hat Wireless in der Lobby frei und wenn man ein Zimmer in den oberen Stockwerken hat, eine super Aussicht. Hotelbar angenehm und der Poolbereich für ein STadthotel super. Die Zimmer sind überdurchschnittlich gut ausgestattet. Ein Tipp geht unbedingt zu BIERSCH zwei STrassen weiter in einer kleinen Mall gelegen im obersten Stockwerk zum Burger essen. Ist ein Ableger einer deutschen Brauerei.

“Generally a good value” This hotel is a pure businessman's hotel, make no bones about it. It is not near any walking district, nor any sights to see. It is in the middle of an office park. The clientele reflects it. Notwithstanding all that, for all its pedestrian aspects, it is very consistent. Having stayed there on multiple occasions over 12 years, it never varies. As it is a Marriott, you know it will not be fancy. There is no turndown service, and the menu is, um, quite limited--they even have flyer sheets from local pizzerias for take out! The beds are clean, so are the bathrooms. The plumbing and the internet work fine. The heating/cooling is a bit severe--decide before you want to use it. It has always been thus. The staff are cheerful, and will take care of you. It is a bit on the expensive side ($240 all- in, including tax and internet), but that is the businessman-premium, if you will.

“Nice, Nice, Nice” Only have good things to say about this hotel. Located near Metro Mall, about 1 mile away, which is where we needed to be. Clean rooms, nice plasma television, nice linens and beds, nice bathroom. Breakfast included downstairs. I have no complaints and would definitly stay here again, without hesitation.

“West tower, like a boutique hotel.” I stayed at the West tower for a business function and loved the intimacy. I did stroll over to the East tower and it was hopping! Beautiful lobby, bar, internet cafe, and restaurants. However, for me it was too busy. The airport is very close so be prepared for prompt 6:30am wake-up calls!

“Good time at the Fairmont” My friend and I stayed 3 nights at the Fairmont and would definately return. The room (2 queens) was plenty big, enormous walk in closet, well appointed bathroom. Nice view of the city from room 608. Room service was speedy, but quite expensive ($27 in food ended up costing $45 with tips, fees, taxes, etc). Reception was speedy, friendly, helpful. The concierge service was fabulous--tips, advice, tickets, anything our hearts desired. Baggage service took extra precautions with my lap top, and immediately produced our stuff when we needed our bags. The health club receptionist recommended I join the President's Club (------------, took about 2 minutes and they only wanted basic demographics). My President's Club number saved me the $10/day gym fee and the $13.95/day internet access fee. It also got me clean work out wear to borrow (I forgot my running shoes). The only service problem was waiting over an hour for a maid to bring me the shoes. I'm sure the rack rate is steep, but I would return to the hotel without a second thought if I could get a deal. The Tonga Room is a hoot--don't miss the rain storms with buffet and 1/2 price drinks at Happy Hour.

“Nice hotel; close to DART” This was a nice hotel. The staff was friendly and helpful. It’s not the best Holiday Inn I’ve stayed in, but I got a room for a great price so I can’t complain too much. The hotel was clean and quiet. Overall, I enjoyed my stay. There is a hotel shuttle which will take you anywhere within a 3 mile radius for free (no exactly sure of the distance, check with the hotel). There run on a specific schedule so you will need to plan ahead if you want the schedule. There is a DART station within walking distance of the hotel. Make sure you get a pass. You don't have to scan it, but you have to show the pass when one of the police officer walks through. And they check at random. I saw one person get kicked off for not having a pass. Basically, they take down your information and you can even get a fine. The hotel is located a few blocks from the hospital district; so if you get really sick, you don’t have to travel far. I did not get a chance to use the pool or workout room, so I cannot give a fair assessment of those facilities. FYI, there is no continental breakfast. There is a $10 charge for a breakfast buffet, which is a fair value. I did enjoy happy hour in the bar. There had a few drink and appetizer specials.

“Good conference venue, but a bit far from downtown.” I attended a conference at this location in June 2010. Good venue for a conference, but a bit removed from downtown Chicago. Plenty of room for meetings in the hotel and the adjacent conference center, but there were limited places to eat at the the hotel and immediate area. The room was good size and clean, so no issues. However, it was a bit noisy. Interestingly, my room was next to the elevators, but there was really no noise from that direction. But in one of the adjacent rooms, there was a baby that was crying at night and that was very noticeable.
