The Hyatt is walking distance to the Soldier Field, the Field Museum and Shedd Aquarium (a bit of a hike, but doable). I did get a "city view" room, so I had an excellent view of theChicago skyline from my room.

“Convenient and attractive” In spite of the weird entry situation, the hotel is attractive. It used to be a bank and has retained some of the architecture in an updated format. Rooms were spacious with the usual amenities. Like many hotels, had the ipod clock radio which seems to do everything except set the alarm (function was broken). TV remote and one phone needed new batteries. Was expensive the week I was there but slightly less than comparable properties. Parking is $36 (or $30 with package). Internet hiccuped a few times and lost connection, but otherwise OK.

“Big character, amazing views, exceptional service” This property has so much character, and is so well done, it really made for an unexpected surprise on a recent business trip. I travel a lot, and spend a good amount of time in data centers which are cold and loud. Ink48 was warm and welcoming, the perfect polar opposite experience to return to after long hours, and now will be my first choice when returning to NY. The staff were courteous, acknowledged my frequent stay membership, and genuinely cared that the stay was positive. From the first contact greeting and assisting from the cab to front desk, everything in-between and through check out, the staff were nothing short of exceptional. Having arrived early, I checked bags and went to the on-site restaurant "Print" for some breakfast before heading out. My breakfast sandwich was very good, though what stood out to me was the French press coffee. Maybe it was early, but that coffee left such an impression. More impressive was the loft style room, and a breathtaking view of the Manhattan skyline. I spent three nights here, and was fortunate to have a upper floor which featured a high ceiling, big windows, and amazing view. The roof deck can be somewhat of a scene, though the view and experience are a must see. Overall, looking forward to returning and enjoying Ink48 on a non-business trip!

“Nice Hotel, but didn't live up to expectations” We stayed at Hotel Palomar for two nights in early January over a weekend. Overall the hotel was nice and the service was great. I wanted to give it 3.5 stars, but I can't figure out 1/2 stars, and based on service gave it 4. The hotel is very well located for visiting San Francisco, many parts of the city are an easy walk, the Bart is right outside and it is a very easy walk to the Cable Cars. It is probably the best location I've found for seeing multiple parts of the city. The lobby is well appointed and the front desk is easy to access, with a sofa to sit on if you need to wait minute or two. They offered different waters (plain, lemon, and strawberry) which we really enjoyed. It was nice to refresh yourself after being out and about. Service: The service was great, everyone was extremely friendly and helpful. Checkin and checkout went smoothly, and all my interactions with the front desk were great. The restaurant was closed for most of our stay and the only service issue we encountered was that they did not stock the continental breakfast well or maintain the lounge it was served in. Room: We apparently had an upgraded room, from a garden view to an outside view, but I wouldn't consider it much of an upgrade personally. The room was definitely on the small side, even compared to other San Fran hotels we've stayed in. The set of the room could have been better. The entry to the bathroom was a pocket door right next to the bed, and I'm talking less than 3' from one side of the bed. Definitely not a good situation for bathroom privacy. The bathroom was well enough appointed, but there was absolutely no ventilation so it was steamy and again the privacy issue if you get what I mean. The toiletries were nice though. The room overlooked Market St, which at this location, there isn't much look at, and you get a lot of street noise in my opinion. We got there on a Saturday and there were high school bands playing right under our window, we wanted to unwind a bit after a cross-country flight, but it was more relaxing to leave the hotel. They did mention they are frequently there. The furnishings in the room were in good shape and the bed was comfortable. The room was showing wear and tear though, the carpet was threadbare/ripped in someplaces, which is something that makes me a little crazy in hotels. It just gives it a shabby, Motel 6 atmosphere. The room had a safe, mini-bar, iron and blow dryer. Food: The restaurant was closed when we were there. I am still undecided about my recommendation as to whether or not to stay at the hotel. For the price I am not sure that it is worth it, given some of the room conditions. Based on the location and service, yes. Based on the condition and overall condition of the room, no. So you'll have to weigh what is important to you.

“いいホテルです” 5月のGWに宿泊しました。 全室、スイートタイプで、アップグレードしてくれたおかげで、リバービューでした。 朝食付きプランは、2Fのレストランでとりますが、 コーヒー、オレンジジュース+5種類の中から選ぶことができます。 (それ以外は、別料金となり、残念なことに、パンが付いているメニューがないので、1Fのデリ、あるいはレストラン入り口で購入し、部屋で食べることになります) 基本的には、シャワーのみ。(お金を出せば、バス付もあり) 2重窓でないので、若干外の音が気になる感じもあります。 食事は、近くにいっぱいありますし、スーパーも近いし(惣菜を買い、部屋で食べることも可能)、1Fのハンバーガーは絶品です。

“Great location, weird room, less than stellar overall” This really is just a cleaner than average 2 star hotel. Room was taller than it was wide - the ceiling had to be 20 feet up. Felt like living in a fish bowl. Room was sparsely appointed (as are all CQ hotels), bathroom was cramped, furnishings were old. Room was clean. Location is great, though - right off Wall Street. You can walk to anywhere downtown from here.

“No ifs ands or butts--this hotel is perfection.” Where to start--the neighborhood is an upscale suburb of San Diego with white fences and tree lined streets. The entry drive to the hotel is spectacular with lush forests and beautiful landscaping. As you can see from the website, the architecture is faux Tuscan and beautiful. The public rooms are spectacular with the highest quality carpets, marble, woodwork, art, etc.--no detail left out. The bedrooms and bathrooms are simply exquisite. From the beautiful and exceptionally high quality furnishings to high tech amenities, to totally comfy beds, linens and pillows, this hotel strives for greatness. The bathrooms are simply the best I have experienced with perfect bathtubs, showers, marble, exceptional woodwork, etc. The closets were large with plenty of room for all of our luggage and clothes. Added touches: There is a fun and delicious coffee shop/gelateria with very high quality coffee and gelato. The golf course, practice area and service at the golf club are second to none. Unlike many resort golf courses, this course is in perfect shape. The location of the resort is perfect being close enough to San Diego that it's not difficult to reach downtown, Sea World, the Zoo without too much driving and yet it is in such a nice leafy suburb with outstanding views. It is also only a 10 minute drive to my favorite beach and beach town in the San Diego area--Del Mar. I walked every morning on this spectacular beach. Let me finish with a comparison. Two years ago we stayed at the Four Seasons in Aviara and this resort blows it away. There are four of us in the family and we all agreed that, if given the choice, we would select the Grand Del Mar over the Four Seasons every time.

“Very convenient” Although this Marriott is getting old in the tooth and needs to be remodeled it is a great place to stay for an overnight or so. What works for this property is the convenience to the airport terminals. There is a small subway in the basement of the Marriott (almost reminds me of the "people mover" at Disneyland) that comes every 3 minutes and stops at all terminals. Not used very much as it is outside of TSA security but a great way to get from your baggage to the hotel or to checkin counter with minimal hassle and time. The hotel is heavily used by pilots. Besides the convenience of the hotel, the staff is absolutely outstanding! I am a Marriott life time platinum member and I can truly say that their courtesy and willingness to to make your stay a great experience is as good as the best JWs I have ever stayed. The dinning room is superb under the direction of Edgar Cabrera and Tom, the general manager, is alway around and easily assessable for any of your needs or special request. If the hotel didn't need to be updated I would definitely have rated it excellent but will continue to stay there because of it's other qualities and advantages.

“A little disappointed...” Two girlfriends and I stayed in a suite the weekend of 12/20. Upon their arrival, they had help with their bags, where I had to schlep my own. While the suite was quite spacious, the furnishings were miminal and more modest that I would expect at the Ritz. We were able to get down to the spa for a manicure at a moment's notice and delighted in the company of "Joey" and "Dee". Spa services are expensive and include an 18% gratuity. The highlight of our stay was Sunday brunch at Fearing's. Again, expensive, but well worth every penny and not to be missed. When we do our weekend getaway again, we'll probably pass on the Ritz and try the Mansion.

“Modernes Designhotel” Das neue Yotel war zu unserem Besuch noch nicht vollständig fertig, es gab diverse Kinderkrankheiten, die aber sicher bald behoben sein werden. Die Zimmer ähneln Schiffskabinen und sind für eine Städtereise völlig ausreichend. Badezimmer haben keine Tür, lediglich einen Vorhang. Lage: zu Fuss zum Port Authority Bus Terminal (Subway, Newark Airport Bus) 3 Minuten. Das in der Rate inklusive Frühstück ist ein US-Continental, d.h. Kaffee, Tee und diverse Muffins, es gibt aber auch "richtiges" Frühstück im Restaurant. Die Atmosphäre im Haus ist Clubartig, riesige Terrasse mit Bar. Auf jeder Etage gibt es eine Küche mit Getränkeautomaten (Softdrinks 2 $, nimmt Kreditkarte) und Gratis Kaffee Insgesamt entspricht das Hotel der Beschreibung auf seiner HP, für Jugendliche und junggebliebene ist es zu empfehlen, erwachsene Reisende finden zum gleichen Preis (wir zahlten 250 $ incl. Tax) in der selben Gegend echte 4-5 Sterne Hotels

“cool hotel, great staff” This hotel was really nice. I mixed-up my reservations, coming in on Friday when I booked sat. They were really nice and found a room for me at a discount rate. Came in for a sox game. Only down side is that the hotel becomes a local club at night on sat night. We came in from the sox game dressed for the game and felt awkward with the crowd all over the lobby and bar dressed for clubbing. we went to our room because we were not dressed for the "club style", but really had wanted a nightcap in the bar. This hotel is so pretty in the lobby and very nice?friendly. I'd stay again.

“Exceeded expectations” I was here for several nights in December. Really enjoyed my stay. The room was pretty small, but the way it was arranged made really efficient use of the space. It was immaculately clean - nice bedding, clean bathroom. I had two minor issues when I was there, and both were addressed promptly once I brought them to the staff's attention. This isn't a hotel with super-mega frills - wi-fi is extra - but it's in a great location. It's near a lot, but not in the midst of it, so if you want to steer clear of the hectic parts of Times Square you can. I'd stay here again in a second.

“Was really nice for years... that has changed” For over $300 a night, they might want to have better customer service. When we checked in and went to our room, we got a huge surprise upon opening the door. Of course it was probably a bigger surprise for the people who had arrived at the room five minutes before us and were already camped out on the beds. One would think that the front desk would respond diligently to such a problem of double booking, but after a curt "we'll do what we can" reply on the phone, the other family called with a little more fervor. After twenty minutes, someone arrived to give the other family key cards to their new room. They didn't help them move, didn't apologize, and didn't offer to tidy up our soiled room. They did manage to deactivate our room keys though. When we went to the front desk for new keys, the lady proceded to give us a lecture on proper key usage like we were kids. While the location is beautiful and San Diego is a magic place for our family, this stay ends a six-year routine we have kept. Something changed drastically in the way the property is managed. The hallway smelled of mildew like we never smelled before. The staff attitude was indifferent and rude, when it used to be very friendly. The kicker is that two months after the fact, I got a form letter from the property manager saying something along the lines of "we appreciate your feedback and will consider your input" or something like that. When I emailed back to say "don't bother," it was clear she had no clue what the problem we encountered was. I got a form response about "improvement and change" with all sorts of corporate buzzwords like "synergy" and "teamwork." It thoroughly explained why we had the experience we had. No one in management listens. The vibe from the staff was one of indifference and being there solely to collect a paycheck. While the property is beautiful (despite the sometimes polluted bay), it is not worth the huge prices they want. To top it off, parking is extremely difficult, because with a full hotel, packed conference rooms, and sections of the parking lot closed off for their storage and events, there are not enough spaces. It was sort of ironic to pay for parking and end up on the street a couple of times. Granted, we always had a space at night. It really is a shame, because the location is great, the building is beautiful, and the rooms are great for beach front. It's just that they semeed to have stopped caring.

“I love this hotel!” This is one of my favorite hotels, I always stay here when I visit San Diego. Close to where you want to be. Great service & ammenities. It gives you a feeling as if you were in a Hacienda in Mexico. Very comfortable suites, great views of the city. Lots of things to do near by.

“Hotel 480 - Great Union Square Location” I stayed at Hotel 480 late in December after booking an overnight stay using Priceline. I think it used to be the Crowne Plaza and now has a banner over it saying Hotel 480. I get the impression it's still undergoing a remodel, but not sure. First off, the location is great. Right across from Sir Francis Drake, the Disney Store and Borders. The lobby was nice and clean and looked like it's gone through a recent transformation. Once you step off the elevator and onto your floor, you can tell the upper floors have not been remodeled. The decor in the halls and rooms were not what you expected from the lobby. I assume they are still renovating. It was mostly clean and comfortable and appropriate if all you need is a place to sleep. The staff was nice and the one big drawback was the parking. I valet'd and when I checked out Sunday I had to wait 45 minutes to get the car. I tried calling the valet desk in advance but couldn't get through, so just went down. It was obvious they were short staffed, kind of disorganized and aplogetic. It was somewhat frustrating as it appeared people who turned in their tickets after me got their cars before mine. One gentleman before me had been waiting much longer than me though. This could be because I went on a holiday weekend though.

“A Disappointment” Having stayed at this hotel a few years ago, with vaguely positive recollection about it, I figured I'd book it again for a one night stay for business this month. Maybe my memory is faulty, or more likely, the hotel has gone down hill ... a lot! When I checked in, I was given a room in the back building, which requires a walk through the ballroom area to a very remote bank of elevators. No big deal, but that building seems to have been annexed onto the main building (because the upper floors don't line up. Perhaps the distance from the main building is a problem for the housekeeping staff, because when I got there (to a very hot room), the bathroom was short some towels and soap, and worse, there was a wet dirtly towel lying on the desk!! So, frustrated (and not wanting to collect my things and trek back to the front desk, I called housekeeping and let them know that I needed some soap and clean towels, and asked them to remove the dirty towel. They said they'd send someone up ... and when he arrived, he had the coffee that (he thought) I'd requested! (What? ... Coffee? ... How does "Soap" sound like "Coffee"??) (He did bring some, but not all the towels). Anyway, after asking him to remove the dirty towel (which evidently they hadn't told him about), he did go back and get the bar of soap I'd requested. After that, I went down to the (mostly empty) restaurant for a quick dinner. When I got to the restaurant reception desk, there was a very frustrated couple having a heated conversation with the gentleman behind the counter. When they stormed off, he showed me to my table and appologized that I had to hear the dissagreement with the previous patrons (although he placed all the blame on them). The waiter brought me a menu and some rolls. Then I waited, for about 15 mins, until another person was seated near me, and the waiter finally came back to take my order. When I asked what the "catch of the day" was, he said "tilapia". When I hesitated, he said the also have "fillet of sole" ... which I ordered. Imagine my surprise when he brought my dinner, and it was swordfish! Not a problem, really, but he didn't seem to notice until I called him on it! After dinner, I asked the waiter what time breakfast was served (since I had an 8:30 flight out). He said they open for breakfast at 6:00 am (which would just about give me enough time to have a quick breakfast and catch the shuttle to the airport (about a 1/2 mile) in the morning in time for my flight. Also, at a hotel at this level, you don't expect to see an old curved screen CRT television ... maybe it's a "retro" thing? Oh well, I only needed to stay for the one night, so the next morning I got up early enough to get ready and go down for breakfast (which was included as part of my room package). I arrived back at the restaurant at 6:00 am but was surprised to see it was dark. So, I went over to the hotel front desk and asked when and where they serve breakfast ... the woman there said that the restaurant should be opening about now and I had gone to the right place. So, figuring I might be a couple of minutes early, I went back to the restaurant and waited for about 5 minutes when a gentleman came out from the kitchen and (looking at me like I was in the wrong place) said the cook was "sick" that morning and to come back at 7:00 am (which was too late for me ... I told him that, but he didn't seem to care, and offered not alternatives). An airport hotel doesn't have more than one cook (it's a major international airport, so people are coming and going at all times ... and leaving early to catch a flight should be expected ... but they don't have a back-up plan!). I was more than happy to leave and have breakfast at the airport while waiting for my fligh! I don't recall any negative experience at a Starwoods hotel (some are better than others, but this one needs to lose its "flag" to get their act together!!). Unless there are no other options (there are dozens of hotels in close proximity), I'd avoidl this hotel!
“A great place to stay” New property and excellent location and shopping. Staff was also excellent. I would highly recommend this Courtyard to anyone.

“Older but well-maintained resort, spacious suites, ample conference facilities, professional staff” Traveled to this resort for a business conference of roughly 120. We will come again. All food and all services were excellent. The rooms are suites - well-maintained, spacious, with work tables and couches for reading and work offsite. There is a great Mexican restaurant on the property called Aunt Chiladas. Do not miss it.

“Great location plus nice customer service” We spent the Christmas holidays at the Nolitan. Our room was on the smaller side, but so nice and clean and cleverly designed that we really did not feel that cramped at all. Somehow the room design just works. The housekeeping is great too. Our room was perfect every single night when we returned and that fact was much appreciated. The front desk and restaurant staff were also gracious and helpful. The location is really great too. Close to the subway, right by Little Italy and Chinatown and generally in a nice neighborhood. We spent a day in Brooklyn and it was super easy to get there on the subway too. Reasonable rates too. We did an internet deal where we prepaid and thought that we got a great value for NYC.

“Tolle Lage an der Bay” Das Bahia Resort Hotel in San Diego bietet seinen Gästen in typisch amerikanisch eingerichteten Zimmern einen unbeschwerten Aufenthalt. Das Hotel bietet verschiedene Zimmertypen: im 4 stöckigen Hauptgebäude, in den motelähnlichen Gebäude oder in den Pavillions mit eigenem Strand. Das Bahia Resort Hotel ist ein idealer Standort, um San Diego zu erforschen oder einfach nur, um sich an den Stränden zu erholen.

“Wonderful Christmas Holiday” We stayed here between 22nd December 2007 and 5th January 2008. We checked in at 9pm and it was really easy! We were given a corner suite overlooking Times Square on the 22nd floor. I must say, I wish we were higher. During the day, we could hear street noise and traffic. At night it was quieter, we only heard a few sirens or horns. The view was great! But the flashing signs in the windows did bug us a little, but at night the curtains blocked all of the light so sleeping was easy! The rooms are big for NY hotels. They have 2 rooms - sitting room with a couch, desk, chair and TV. Also a sink, microwave, mini bar, fridge and coffee maker. The coffee maker had take-away cups (like starbucks) so we made our morning coffee to go! The stay was great, housekeeping were wonderful and helpful and the front desk and concierge were great. HOWEVER do not book show tickets with them! We used broadwaybox.com and got 1/2 price tickets for Chicago and Hairspray. We had 3rd row for Chicago and 2nd row Mez, for Hairspray - Awesome seats at half the price! Concierge wanted to charge $152 per ticket and we got them for $62. New Years Eve was easier then we thought. We were at TGI Fridays a few doors down and left at 1am. Took around 1 hours to get back to our room. The staff were great and it was very well run! Christmas in New York is magical! Even though it didn't snow it was such a wonderful experience and the Doubletree was great!

“Very Historic and nice hotel” I stayed at the Copley for business recently and was pleased. It's a bit dated and the continual renovations were a bit of a headache, but the staff and facilities were very nice. I took advantage of the Gold level and was surprised to find charges for the offererings in the concierge loung, other hotels do not do this on their concierge level in my experience. The rooms were spacious and were nicely decorated though the heating unit in the hotel could not be moderated so the temps in the hotel were quite high throughout the stay. Nice hotel but not exceptional.

“Very nice property and fantastic location close to UNCC and shopping” We stayed for one night here and chose this hotel because we are huge Residence Inn fans and the location was a mile from UNCC where my husband had a meeting. This Residence Inn did not disappoint in any way. We used marriott points for a studio room which was very spacious. Full kitchen and living room area. We enjoyed a happy hour when we arrived with wine and Yuengling beer on tap! They had a few snacks as well but we were headed out to dinner so didn't have any. We had breakfast the next morning and they had the usual nice selection of hot and cold foods. Eggs, ham, potato pancakes, waffle iron, assorted bagels/breads/pastries, cereals, fruit, yogurt and also yogurt parfait made up with granola, etc. Very nice selection as we have become accustomed to finding at Residence Inns. My only complaints would be that we were on a first floor room which I usually like because of convenience but I would likely choose a 2nd floor here next time. We didn't have to be up early and the person staying above us was up at 5:45 am and you could hear every step back and forth across the floor. Very loud! Woke us both up and I honestly don't think they were stomping around or anything. Just thin floors and walls. The bed was rather firm for my liking as well which I tend to find in most Residence Inns. All that aside we would definitely stay here again without hesitation.

“W is for What a rip off” Stayed there for business. Lobby is on the 7th floor and the rooms are TINY and not very clean. For $369 plus tax they had the courtesy to charge $8 for a bottle of water. A rip off even for Manhattan standards.

“I love the Historic Wardman Tower” This is an old-fashioned sprawling convention hotel in the leafy Woodley Park Neighborhood. From the sound of the other reviews, the main hotel appears to be a challenge--but the historic Wardman Tower, where I managed to snag a room for only $159 per night, is a real treat. The tower is connected to the rest of the hotel by a sun-drenched corridor filled with comfy chairs, potted palms and what I’m guessing is historically accurate floral carpeting. (The tower is probably a not good place to stay if you hate walking; you might need a sherpa to find your room the first night.) My room was large and beautiful with a walk-in closet. Great view of the city. Water pressure like a fire hose. Real windows that open. Friendly front desk. Metro station right across the street, easy walk to the National Zoo and the Adams Morgan neighborhood. Only downside is that there isn’t a ton of counter space in the bathroom.

“Great Value for the Weekend” I booked this hotel for $109/night on Hotwire for a weekend stay. The room was clean and luxurious, and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was fine but less than luxurious. As other reviewers have mentioned, the bathroom has a shower/tub combination and is not very large. However, it is adequate. It did have two sinks with one located outside the bathroom. The website says some rooms have Hill Country views. I requested a high floor room with a Hill Country view. I received a high floor room, but it did not have a nice view. I'm not sure if other rooms have better views. The surrounding area is suburban-like and nice but not too scenic. The location is good. It is not too far from the airport or from the attractions in San Antonio. Room service was quick and not too expensive compared to other hotels I have visited. The lobby and bar downstairs are very nice, with live piano music in the evenings. I would recommend this hotel.

“A solid 3-star NYC hotel experience” My partner and I spent two nights at the DT Metropolitan in late July. Prior to our stay I had previously contacted guest relations about my concerns regarding disruptions to guests from the ongoing construction/renovations in the hotel as well as other concerns I had gleaned from reading recent TripAdvisor reviews. Within a few days, I received a courteous reply from the Guest Relations Manager and contact information for head of housekeeping. I was assured that my stay would be pleasant and enjoyable. We arrived at the hotel shortly after 3:30 p.m. Even though the lobby was very busy, check-in was very efficient and we were in our room very quickly. The room was a pleasant surprise. In an apparent effort to assure that we would have a pleasant experience, the management had upgraded us from an Upper Floor Deluxe Room to a Junior Suite. The DT Metropolitan is already known as having large (for NYC standards) guest rooms for a 3-star hotel (it was built as a 4-star Loew's Hotel). Walking into the Junior Suite was like winning the jackpot. Enormous by NYC standards with two ample closets, it had a pullout sofa bed in the seating area in addition to a very spacious walk-out terrace facing 51st Street. The only thing on the small side was the bathroom (which held the toilet and combo shower/tub)--the sink/vanity is outside the bathroom and was more spacious. Upon returning from a lovely dinner nearby at Brasserie the first night, we entered the room to discover a note left by the GM with a bottle of wine and a cheese and crackers plate. It was an unexpected, pleasant surprise but I suppose the management is really serious about generating positive interest and reports about their property after some negative reports this spring and early summer. I did have a minor gripe about the delivery of the wine and cheese. We had left a do not disturb sign on the door but the sign was apparently ignored. Now, my general critique of this property. Hotel has recently been renovated/"refreshed" but it is difficult to tell what is new on the guest floors and what is legacy. Renovations appear to have been done quickly but not very carefully. Still, hotel is pleasantly appointed for an older 3-star hotel in NYC. I think the 3.5-star rating is pushing the limits a bit. Cleanliness is good, but public areas have high traffic and show it. Buffet breakfast was included in our rate, but otherwise I would not have eaten breakfast at the hotel--it was just adequate in quality and given the price if you had to pay for it, there are much better options in the immediate vicinity. Elevators were usually fairly efficient except for one morning when there appeared to be some sort of event on the penthouse level which tied up all the elevators. HVAC was a little problematic in our particular suite--despite adjusting the thermostat, our unit was constantly running and the room was rather cool (better than the 90 degrees F outside, though!). Validated parking through the hotel is an excellent value for this part of Midtown ($30 for 24 hours with no in/out privileges). Even though we were directly across the street from a fire house and police precinct, up on the 18th floor the noise was not too bad for this part of Manhattan--compared to the even older Radisson Lexington Hotel a few blocks south, noise levels in the room were very acceptable by Midtown Manhattan standards. Most of the staff encountered seemed friendly, helpful and accommodating. My request for an extended checkout to 1 p.m. needed because of a delayed business meeting was met without hesitation. I think high speed internet access was a bit pricey for a hotel at this price point and star-level--charging $14.95-16.95 per 24 hours of access. NYC is a very competitive hotel market. At the time I booked our reservation, the DT Metropolitan was very competitively priced. It's strengths are a good Midtown location for business, large rooms, and an apparent can-do attitude by a good portion of the staff and management. It isn't luxurious but is comfortable for a large, somewhat older hotel in Midtown.

“Nice location but you get what you pay for” I hadn't stayed at a Residence Inn in quite some time. I knew they had kitchens with separate bedrooms along with free breakfasts. The room was fine, nothing fancy. Be aware that the bathroom sink is part of the bedroom so if someone is getting ready in the morning while the other person is sleeping, well, let's just say they won't stay sleeping much longer. For some reason we were given a handicapped room which had a huge shower but the shower head was so low I had to bend down. Furniture is slightly worn but not too bad. There is no closet, just some shelves and hangars in the bedroom area. Our son slept on the fold out couch which was fine for 1 night. I don't think he would have liked to sleep there more than that. Overall, the room was quiet and if you are staying in DC long term on a budget, this would be fine. They have laundry facilities on each floor and a gym on the 2nd floor. Food is sold in the lobby which you can cook in your room, plus there is a small market next door. Easy walk to Dupont Circle Metro station.Plenty of restaurant options nearby. The Palomar hotel is across the street so if you need a taxi, they are lined up there. I liked the Doubletree in Foggy Bottom much better.
“Good centrally located hotel” Went for work. Very good staff. clean room. Good 3 star hotel. Good Value

“Relaxing hotel in the nicest part of Manhattan” First, let me be clear, this hotel is not in the center of the "buzz" in Manhattan. If you are looking to stay where you can walk in 10 minutes to Times Square or Saks, this is not your hotel. However, if you don't mind taking a taxi or the subway to those areas and you want to spend the night in a place that is quiet and in a beautiful part of the city, than this is your hotel. We were greeted with a warm towel and a bottle of water which were much needed after our flight. When we went into the rooms they were immaculate and well-decorated. The bathroom was large but did not have a tub. The bed was huge and so comfortable. There was plenty of closet space and drawer space for our belongings. The blinds were two layers thick so it was plenty dark in the morning to sleep in. The concierge and the bellman had great suggestions for local restaurants. The bar at this hotel was also fabulous. It was neat, comfortable, and had a nice menu of drinks. Of course the drinks were a little pricey but that is to be expected when you are staying in a nice hotel in the Upper East Side. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay here and would most definitely stay again.

“Ok - great location for IAH - but tired” I stayed here for one night after flying in from the UK. First thing to say is that this is a great hotel if you want to stay near the airport, I picked up my rental car & was in the hotel within 5 minutes. Plenty of free parking. I was upgraded to a Club Floor room, but it was very tired. For example, the cupboard under the TV was missing a door which appeared to have been ripped off. Bed was comfortable & the room pretty quiet. I had the buffet breakfast which was ok. Overall - great location, but needs some work

“Location, Location, Location” This is my first time to stay at this particular hotel, but I will return. I felt very secure coming with two young teens. There is security as you walk in who allows you or doesn't allow you to proceed to the lobby and top floors. The rooms were very ample, the bathroom clean, the beds super comfortable.

“Kids had fun......” Stayed here for 3 days with 2 kids age 6 and 5. This place is good for kids but the pool is just ok and older kids would be bored quickly. We were very dissapointed with the pool. Its small and not much to do there. Upkeep of the pool was just average. The towels provided at the pool are a joke and can best be described as big hand towels. They have a bee problem at the pool and you will attract a swarm if you get a sweet drink! Night time activities for the kids were great and they loved it. But plan other activities during the day like Sea World etc. The rooms were ok but really starting to show wear. The beds were terrible and pillows were worse. The pull out couch was very worn and not very comfortable. The bathroom was nice and big in our one bedroom suite. But had some maintenence issues. The shower has a shower head and rainfall shower head on the ceiling. Our reg. shower head sprayed water all over the place and was useless so we had to use only the rainfall head which was ok but a pain to have water falling on you and no room to get out of it. We had a package that included champagne, turn down service, free movie and champ. glasses. We never got the champ. and no turn down service or glasses. They took off $50 after we complained. they also charged for the movie but took it off the bills when we pointed it out. We had breakfast included which was average at best but the kids loved it. Service was spotty at all service areas. Overall we had a good time but next time we will pay a little more and stay at the Hyatt or La Cantera.

“No wifi issues. Comfortable hotel.” Wifi worked. A bit remote from some things. If this location works for you, this is a decent hotel. Clean. Nothing fancy. Breakfast was fine. Handy laundry machine, but yes, having change available would be helpful. Covered parking spaces on the back building (two buildings). Generous with late check out.

“Great Stay” We have just returned from staying 4 nights at the Westin in Denver - we had a fantastic time and the hotel was ideal for what we wanted. The hotel was centrally located within a 1 minute walk of the 16th Street Mall which is surrounded by a number of different eateries - in fact, we commented on how many different eating options there are in Denver City. We requested a room with a view and they kindly gave us a room overlooking Invesco Field and the mountains, much to the delight of my husband because he is a huge Denver Broncos fan !! The room was great, large, clean and contemporary. The hotel has a swimming pool which is inside and outside which was fantastic and it opened at 5am which was perfect for us because of the time differences we kept waking up early, so this helped fill the time !! This hotel is great for exploring and the concierge lady was fantastic and helped us out a couple of times. There is a starbucks and they even deliver to your room !! We caught the light rail from Union Station to Invesco Field (you need the E to Lincoln train going there and the E Union coming back) and it only cost us $6 (for both of us) which was ideal for when we went to see Denver play the Jacksonville Jaguars. We also caught a bus from 15th Street, California to Golden, so we could visit the Coors Factory tour - When you find the bus station, walk around the corner, you are looking for 16L and not 16 - get off in Golden when you see the “Howdy Folks - welcome to Golden sign !!! And then turn right, the factory is just down there - you cannot miss it. Returning to Denver, you need the 16L which you can catch opposite the Coors factory tour gates (there is a green booth by the liquor store). We had a fantastic day at the tour as it was interesting and we were glad that we visited Golden because there is some history there (although the town itself does not have much there). For both of us it cost $9 for a day pass which we brought from the Denver Tourist Board on 16th California. We can definitely recommend both the Westin and the Coors Factory Tour. One last tip, we would recommend exploring the riverfront park area which was beautiful - you just need to walk to Union Station and then you will see a big white bridge they are building (it is call the Millennium Bridge and looks identical to the one in London - lets hope this one doesn’t wobble!!), walk over that and you will then see it all. Have a good vacation !

“Functional airport hotel-convenient with frequent shuttle” I took a room for a long layover- the airport shuttle runs continuously so doesnt have to be called and it only stops at one other hotel which is efficient.The room -nothing special- basic and a little dated but proper blockout curtains so you can rest in the day.The airport hotels are all clustered together in an area devoid of anything other than a few fast food restaurants.I had a breakfast included package- it was fine but again just what you would expect form an airport hotel. Free internet and boarding pass print facility are good offerings. One of their points of difference is you can book for a 24 hour block of time- great for an early morning arrival from Australia- saves the hassle of trying to negotiate an early checkin.

“Comfortable room, warm staff steps from The Capitol” Stayed here for an in-town getaway focused on the food event Cochon 555 that happened to be held in the hotel. The king room was ample with a cozy bed, a welcoming sofa, and a modern desk and dresser. Eclectic DC photos dot the hallways and stylish contemporary pieces adorn the lobby. The staff is very pleasant and most accommodating. Art Smith's eponymous restaurant Art and Soul is located just off the lobby and offers puched-up homey cuisine and a charming bar.

“Location and ...um...and then there's the location” good: 1. comfortable bed 2. excellent a/c 3. perfect location 4. good shower 5. easy card swipe to enter room 6. very pleasant staff 7. the manager responded to my comments on booking.com by saying that they are undergoing a massive renovation and offered me an upgrade on my next stay. Nice. meh: 1. no sign out front 2. long escalator is not welcoming 3. the distance between the toilet and the wall was as narrow as could be 4. several items were pretty chintzy - the plastic soap dish, the stained mirror under the sink, the plastic sliver "aluminum" desk chair 5. the elevator buttons were so dark that you could not find your floor

“No Way a 4-Star Room” Our room was like a thumbalina room - truly the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in, and I travel often for business. This combined with the fact my husband is over 6'4 and over 300 lbs, it was almost comical watching us trying to maneuver around the room and bathroom. If the size of the room wasn't bad enough, the caulking in the bathtub was mostly missing around the tub, and the header of the closet door was mostly rusted and unsightly. The only seating in the room was one straight chair at the desk, so one person was forced to sit on the bed or floor. We inquired about changing rooms and were told (albiet in a very friendly manner) that they were sold out and having to escort people to other hotels, so while they apologized for the room, there was nothing done about it. The bottled water in the mini-fridge listed at $5.50, which I would expect in Chicago and New York, but not in Indy. We felt we got an okay deal through hotwire (93), but to be honest, although the Westin has been downgraded on the hotwire site from a 4 star to a 3.5 star, we will not return to the Omni and will choose the Westin on future get aways. We didn't try any of the restaurants, the check-in and check-out were smooth and friendly, the lobby looked fine and large (if only our room was the same!).

“Our family reunion was here....it was great!” I cannot attest to the food poisoning incidents, but I can attest to the fact that our family reunion was held here last June, a total of 19 rooms/suites were booked, and no one got sick, everyone was happy with the accommodations (all 70+ of us from all over the nation), and the service was admirable. The lobby area was beautiful and served as a nice gathering spot for our group. Lots of pools and space for everyone, great for the little ones as well as our 92 year old Grandmother! The concierge went out of their way to help us with activities for our group as well. This property feels intimate and tucked away, yet is right next door to Six Flags, and easy distance from shopping and other restaurants. Nice golf course as well. Overall our experience was superb!

“Good Location” The Omni Chicago is in an excellent location close to Michigan Avenue and the Magnificent Mile. We stayed here for more than a week in July 2011 and found the location to be the best aspect of this hotel. We found our room decor to be dated and in need of refurbishment. Although our room was a suite with a separate living area and bedroom area, both areas were quite small. Even combined, both rooms were smaller than other hotel rooms where we have stayed in Chicago and elsewhere. Our room had nice views of the Chicago skyline. We had breakfast a number of times at the hotel and found the breakfast options to be generally good. This hotel has two separate elevators, one from the ground floor to the lobby, and the other from the lobby floor to room floors. Elevator capacity was often insufficient to meet demand for elevators, which meant that we at times had a long wait for one or both elevators. In general, better options are available in the Chicago both in room size and price.

“Cabana rooms are great” In for 4 days on business. Booked the newly renovated Cabana Room around the pool. Room was great. They opened a new Restaurant called Public recenlty and the food was very good. Breakfast each morning at 25 Degrees was excellent, good food and served very quickly. Room Service was also very efficient and delivered very quickly.

“Great location, fantastic staff” I stayed at the Argonaut for two nights beginning December 16. I arrived very late (after midnight), so I didn't notice the valet parking when I pulled up. Luckily there was a spot around the corner. The valet met me at the door, let me in, and was very pleasant. The desk clerk was equally friendly and I was on my way to my room (482) in a minute or two. Upon entry, I was surprised at how small the room was. It was also pretty cold. Otherwise, it was nicely decorated and cozy. The iPod-dockable clock radio was on and softly playing some classical music. Because I am an inTouch member, a gift of a bottle of water and a bar of chocolate were waiting for me on the nightstand. Another pair of chocolates lay on the pillow. I thought that was a nice touch. I turned on the heat and the room was at a comfortable temperature by the time I had finished unpacking. The bed was extremely comfortable. The room was very clean. The shower was hot and the water pressure strong. The bathroom amenities were L'Occitane. The only lapse in the otherwise excellent service was at breakfast the following morning. I had been given vouchers for a continental breakfast at check-in. I was hungry for a bit more than that and ordered eggs and sausage. The waiter brought eggs and bacon instead. When I pointed out the mistake, he returned with sausage, then disappeared. I had to flag down the hostess in order to get my check. The food was excellent. With that sole exception, the service was every bit as good as I've come to expect from the Kimpton brand. Thanks to a busy work schedule, I did not get to spend much time in the area around the hotel. From what I saw while driving, the neighborhood is very picturesque. This would be a great home-base for exploring the Fisherman's Wharf area. A note for the budget-conscious: the parking rates are outrageous - $39/day plus tax (and tip) for valet parking. In their defense, it's my understanding that parking in San Francisco is uniformly insane. I would definitely stay here again.

“Good hotel for convention attendees” I was attending the IFMA show in the convention center and stayed here for 2 nights. Overall this is a fine hotel for conventions and its location directly across the street is a plus, particularly if you are carrying items. A big plus is that they don't have a fee for accepting packages sent to them in advance for exhibiting at the shows. I had a few hiccups in checking in. First, I am not too fond of their terminals at the check-in counter; they are confusing and the people behind them end up helping you anyway. I had booked an upgraded corner king suite with balcony, as I had anticipated my wife coming along and thought she would enjoy the view and sun. Plus, I like a room with lots of light. Unfortunately when I got to the room I discovered several things; first, it was a handicap room, which I hate. My feeling is that at this price in particular I should have been notified; I definitely will ask at hotels in the future. Second, this was not a corner and looked out onto a sitting area at the same level. This was a problem because there was basically a sidewalk outside my window, so anyone waling by could look into the room. This meant that I had to keep my curtains closed constantly, which made the room tomb-like. See my photo below of my view of Phoenix. In addition, the walls transmitted noise from the room next door, apparently being used as a meeting area for some convention people. The room itself was large and fairly well appointed with a large flat TV. the bed was very comfortable; the work desk was fine. A minus was that there was no minibar. By the way, there is no bar at the hotel pool either. The tap water tasted unusually bad, to the point that I didn't want to drink it or make coffee with it. They must realize that, as they had 2 bottles available in the room, but charged over 5 bucks each; forget it, I bought some at the store below. On the plus side, the entire staff was very upbeat and helpful. The facility was modern and clean. I think in general visitors will find the rooms to be fine. The surrounding area was clean and safe, but at night the area is dead. The selection of restaurants is fairly small. People seemed to linger at the Networks lounge on the ground floor.

“A Good Choice” Fine hotel with an excellent staff. We changed rooms twice before we got one we liked, and they were more than accommodating. Be sure to request a room at the front of the hotel overlooking the parking lot (free) and street. The back overlooks the expressway and is noisy. Excellent rooms and beds, good breakfast. They have a free shuttle to the convention centre where you can get the bus to Juarez. We walked back. Hotel is convenient to the I-10 and is a good spot for exploring Juarez, Old Messilla, White Sands. We ate in the north part of town at Geo Geske which was great. The El Paso Art Gallery is free and worth a look.

“Clean, efficient, everything you need” I like Hampton Inns in general. They provide all the basics with a minimum of fuss and hassle, and this one is no different. Good quality bed. Minimal hallway noise even though we were RIGHT in front of the elevator. Good TV, lots of outlets, plenty of lights, good water pressure in the shower, and plenty of space in the bathroom. There is also an indoor pool (which we didn't use) and a fitness center (which we did use). The location is pretty good. There is a Safeway two blocks away to buy groceries, and a CVS down the street as well. The Red Circulator line is a block away ($1 to get down to the National Mall), and the Yellow Circulator line runs outside the hotel to go toward the White House or to Union Station. Chinatown and the Metro station are a 5 minute walk away with plenty of restaurants. Or you can walk down to the National Mall as well (1 mile, maybe 15 minute walk). Free breakfast is what you would expect at any other Hampton. Eggs are kind of tasteless and the pastries/bagels are store-bought. But it's free, there's lots of juice, cereal, Yoplait/Activia yogurt, and even hard-boiled eggs. Internet is free, both Wi-Fi and wired (cable provided). The business center computers kinda suck, and I had a hard time printing my boarding pass one morning (got it eventually). But the staff are excellent and helpful and you can tell they're working hard to service you. Would definitely come back.

“Very nice, convenient and professional.” First, I have to say that I am a bit surprise by the quality of this hotel. I wasn't expecting this at all. The staff is nice , they have FREE shuttle 24 hours a day to airport, Free WI-FI, nice outdoor pool and the neighbourood is very quiet. This is a little gem hidden in Phoenix. The room are very nice and very clean. The layout of the room is quite original actually , i really liked it. I would definately stay there again.

“We were pleasantly surprised” After reading some of the other reviews, we were trembling as we checked into the Hotel Monaco. We were pleasantly surprised. All the staff were friendly and professional, and went out of their way to accomodate unusual requests - which, in our case, included extra garbage bags for the baby's diapers and a city map at 3am (we were jet lagged). The night clerk even went online to find a restaurant open at 5:30am for breakfast. Our room was in good shape, and very nicely decorated. Room service was also quick and the food was tasty.

“Great Stay!” We stayed at the Residence Inn for a July weekend and had a great time. Our suite on the 16th floor was spacious, clean and comfortable. We looked over City Hall and loved the view. We could hear no noise from the hotel, but you could hear city noise outside, even from the 16th floor. Breakfast was excellent and the dining room was spacious and clean. We walked everywhere - Independence Hall (15 minutes), Rittenhouse Square (15 minutes), Phil. Museum of Art (25 minutes) and the Franklin Institute (20 minutes) Neighborhood is fine during the day but do keep alert at night, especially around City Hall. Staff was helpful, and we appreciated that our room was ready for us when we arrived at 11 am. Tiny quibbles: only one shampoo, conditioner, etc. provided for two people for the weekend - we could have used a refill. Also, the lobby is pretty sparce - no sitting areas or bar. Regardless, we would definitely return.

“Great location and good value” I've stayed here on several trips and it's become my go-to choice in the City. It's tough to find a place this close to Midtown and a few subway lines without the madness of Times Square. This fits the bill. Steps from Madison Square Park, the Lexington Ave. and Broadway subway lines and the more residential areas of Murray Hill and Grammercy, this is a great location. One of the most gorgeous lobbies in New York that I've seen, too. Rooms are comfy and quiet. I've been in rather spacious rooms and some smaller ones, but never anything that I couldn't set up an ironing board. There are several good little delis right nearby, which is great in the morning... cheap bagel breakfast is right there. Would definitely recommend.

“Surprisingly nice” I don't usually choose to stay at Sheratons but I do like this one, and it's a Starwood. I found rooms very quiet (light sleeper) and area very convenient...small mall adjoined to it. Nice rooms, very pleased.

“Great place to stay in Seattle” We arrived late at night so 24 hour check in was great. Staff were friendly and helpful. I had a package forward there several weeks before my stay, It was there waiting for me ready for my arrival. Room was clean and spacious. Great laundry facilities. Hotel had access to the Roof top giving a great view of the City. Location was great, walking distance to Space Needle and Mono Rail. Would stay here again.

“Wonderful experience” The rooms in the Fairmont were just amazing. Clean, spacious and well decorated. I thoroughly enjoyed the large bathroom with a separate shower, bath and toilet area as well as a large makeup area outside of the bathroom and a nice, large closet. I couldn't believe how little I was paying for such a great room. The front desk was just ok friendly, but the valets were great as were the cleaning crew and room service personnel.The hotel was booked solid the weekend we were there, but it still ran very well and it didn't feel stuffed due to the size. They definitely accommodated the masses well. The biggest downside was that parking was pricey and you had to valet. Even with how busy the hotel was, the valets were fairly quick with the car. They did lose my car one time but were able to find it within a few minutes.

“Surprisingly good for business” I stayed at this hotel for a conference and, after reading the favorable reviews from tourists, was a bit concerned about whether the room would be set up more for leisure travellers than for those of us stuck on business. I needn't have worried. The wifi signal was very speedy, the chair and desk were very comfortable for working, the lighting was just right, and best of all I could plug in 3 devices easily and all in my workspace! No hunting for outlets in dusty spaces better not seen. The room faced the NJ shoreline and offered quite a spectacular view, though I found it disquieting to gaze from the comfort of my room over the WTC site where so many died. The location is great and you are guaranteed not to get mugged or panhandled no matter the hour as the police presence was massive during my stay - sometimes there were so many it was difficult to walk - but be prepared to be "surveilled" yourself in trade-off.

“Good hotel, good location” I stayed in Philly for 5 nights and could not find a hotel closer to downtown (e.g. on Broad or Market St), so ended up near U of Penn in the University City area. This ended up being a pleasant surprise, given the college town atmosphere and nice walking paths in the area. The hotel itself was solid, if not outstanding. The staff were friendly, but could have been a bit more helpful on local attractions. If you are going to Philly on business, try to find a spot closer to downtown, as it is about a $20 cab ride from this hotel. Otherwise, this is a good alternative.

“Not as luxurious as I was expecting” I was excited about staying here, but the property did not live up 100% to my expectations. The lobby area is nice, although somewhat small. Everyone was exceptionally nice at check-in, so that was good. When I got to my room, I immediately got a poor impression. The decor was a bit 80s, the furniture was chipped in obvious places, the ottoman was missing a button, there was a glaring stain on the chair, the drapes made a loud squeaking sound when opened. And the 'view' was of the building across the way. There was no CD player, as is standard in hotels these days, no coffee maker, the mini bar was unimpressively stocked. The bed had no flat sheet, as many people have noted, which bothered me. The bathroom was nice, though, and a fresh orchid in a pretty vase was a nice touch. At first the mattress seemed very cheap, but I did sleep well on it. The featherbed helped. It was very quiet on the floor, which was nice. The building itself felt very sturdy and solid in construction. I liked that there was a bar/lounge that served food on the ground floor. The gym was small but decent. The little 'business center' -- more like a walk-in closet -- had 3 PC computers that were free to use. So that was good. The lack of security late at night concerned me somewhat. We got back at around 1 a.m. one night and there was no one minding the front door. Since the elevators to the rooms are right near the front door, we asked the man at reception about security and he told us that they had "cameras." What use are cameras, though, if there is no physical security to stop an intruder. Overall, I enjoyed my stay, but it could have been better and certainly more "luxurious," as the hotel chain touts itself.

“nice hotel, felt safe” We found the positive comments about this hotel spot on. The hotel is located halfway between the downtown/airport and U. Phoenix stadium. 11 miles to everything - no trouble getting a cab. Even though the hotel was full and very busy, staff was extremely helpful, rooms and breakfast were at highest level for a Hampton Inn. We were able to check in at 10am with no questions asked. The location is right off the highway, with several other similar chain hotels nearby. Although there is nothing charming to recommend the area, we walked around a little and didn't see anything to suggest that it would be unsafe. Our view is not typical, though, because we were there for the Super Bowl and the adjacent hotel was HQ for the auxiliary state troopers brought in for the event.

“New Stylish Hotel - Great Views, Not So Great Location” We got a great low rate on this hotel via an Internet site. The hotel is only two years old and still looks and feels very new. It is located in the completely renovated Seaport/Waterfront district of South Boston. It is only a few blocks from the new convention center, the federal courthouse, the Institute of Contemporary Art, and the design center. The silver line of the T is across the street. Unfortunately, the neighborhood is T or cab ride away from almost everything else in Boston. Look on a map before you decide to stay in South Boston. In a few years, it will probably be very trendy with more restaurants, bars, and apartments. As for the hotel itself, it has a real Starbucks in the lobby, a terrific concierge named Peggy, and an extremely friendly front desk staff. The beautiful shallow pool, whirlpool, and fitness center is in a secluded section of the fifth floor. Hallways and rooms have a modern, nautical design. rooms are extremely comfortable, airy, and clean. Our view was of the financial district as well as the water. Ask for a high floor with a view and you will not be disappointed. We self-parked in an underground garage in a new apartment building adjacent to the hotel.

“Very Nice Hotel in Great location” Spent 3 nights at the Conrad in June. Very nice hotel with a great location on Rush St & 1 block from Michigan Ave. Very nice room and nice bathroom. I would stay here again. Only complaint, I have diamond status with Hilton Honors & I had to ask for breakfast coupons.

“Huge Property, Very Good Service” I was here for the second time in 2012 for a conference of 1700. I actually live in the city but was helping manage the conference so needed to be onsite.The hotel staff provided excellent service, the location is great for folks from out of town wanting to explore the city. Rooms are updated with comfortable beds, nice bathrooms and amenities. It is such a big hotel it can be confusing to get around. Rooms are in three different towers, all connected to the conference spaces. Most rooms have a view of at least part of the city. If you want the high-rise view or a room with a balcony, you'll need a suite in tower 1. I visited a suite and there was an amazing view of downtown and the bay from the balcony. So an excellent hotel and with San Francisco being such a popular place to visit, the prices naturally reflect that, but I was happy with it both as a guest and conference manager/attendee.

“Nice place in boston” It was my first visit to boston, great location very near to harbour.It was a pleasure to stay in this hotel as it was very well connected, friendly staff not very expensive. The food was nice and the room was very comfy, a must visit.

“Ganz gute Wahl zu erschwinglichem Preis!” Das Hotel ist schon in die Jahre gekommen, die Gänge sind recht weitläufig, man legt schon einiges an Weg zurück. Die Zimmer sind tw renoviert, wirken aber dennoch nicht recht schön, die Lage ist sehr zentral der Service sehr zuvorkommend, der Hauptgrund für meine Übernachtung was der günstige Preis für Chicago, wofür man natürlich gewisse Defizite in Kauf nehmen muss.

“A good value, but not as nice as some of the reviews imply” The Good: Rooms are spacious, clean, and comfortable. The Deli has good food at a reasonable cost. The breakfast at Tug's was adequate. It's an easy walk to the Inner Harbor (down hill), not so easy on the way back. The neutral: The closest access to light-rail isn't in the greatest of neighborhoods and is a pretty good hike. Although it seems that the city of Baltimore doesn't want you to go anywhere but the Inner Harbor! It 's the only part of town they really promote! The Bad: Knowledgeable and Friendly ARE NOT terms I would use to describe the staff. There is no Concierge service and the Bellman and Front desk are clueless on local transportation options. Forget about any type of special requests such as high floors or late check-out. Can't do it! There was not one question about baltimore that was answered confidently(and correctly.) Including, 'where's the nearest post office?' there is one that is the size of the US capitol within a block of the hotel! Don't count on the "shuttle" to local attractions, did not see it over six days! Money saving tip: MARC trains to DC only run during weekdays, so plan accordingly. Taking Amtrak on the weekend will cost over twice as much. Mick Oshea's pub on charles street is a nice contrast to the tourist "harbor scene".

“spacious but busy hotel” This review should be taken in the context of the fact that I was staying here during one of the busiest times of the year, the week just before new years. Midtown is a madhouse before the new year. Consequently, the hotel was crazy. We had to leave our bags with the bell hop for a couple of hours after we could check in. There were lines of people at various bag storage areas which were full to capacity. Needless to say the checking in process was a nightmare. Once in the rooms were spacious . The bathroom was not very large with a small basin area upon which to place your toiletries. The room was tastefully decorated. However my biggest complaint was the temperature of the room. I attempted to lower the thermostat to 65 degrees but the room would not cool down. It was at least 70. I tried calling the front desk and they said they would take care of it but it never got taken care of. Location of hotel was great near many attraction and close to subways. However don't stay here during a busy time because lines were everywhere and restaurants were packed.

“Great hotel wonderful people” The JW is an outstanding hotel. I really enjoy staying there. The facilities are great. The gym is great (there are spots where the lighting could be better). I really enjoy grabbing a quick meal at the bar. The only poentially negative comment is that the restaurant is very noisy so it is difficult to have a dinner and discussion.

“Great music! Great location!” Don't read this review if you're looking for a quiet refined experience! This hotel isn't for you. If you want friendly staff, good service, proximity to great music and good food--keep reading! We stayed here based on trip advisor reviews. Beale Street is outside the doors and steps away. You can hear the music from the hotel at almost all hours. We did not hear anything in our room, not sure about other rooms, but I didn't hear any complaints at breakfast. The room was comfortable and clean (pretty typical Hampton Inn room.) Breakfast was also pretty typical. There is a bellman but no valet parking. The parking garage is conveniently located just outside the hotel and easily accessible. There is a charge and it is secure. Zac's is a little bar/restaurant on the premises. One night we were too tired and hungry to go to a restaurant. Zac's makes all their food fresh and we decided to try it. The menu is somewhat limited but it's very good. One of the best Cobb Salads I ever had. Beale St is great. We are blues fans and we just walked and listened. Stopped in a few clubs. The best music we heard was at the Pepsi Pavillion--outdoors and free. People listened, people danced, some sang along. The folks perform for tips so be generous, they play and sing their hearts out! The Hampton is close walking distance to several museums and venues. The hotel is not too far from Graceland, about a 10-15 minute drive. I'm not a big Elvis fan but Graceland is something everyone should see. It's a slice of America frozen in time, well worth the trip!

“Cheap, Bad Layout and Paper thin walls!” I cannot see how most people give this place a 4 or 5 star rating. The place is new and it is nice but the cons outweigh the pros here. The hotel's layout is very bad and requires you to be a topographer or have a GPS to get around the building. There is no direct passage to the lobby and the only way to get there is to walk around the building to the front entrance or to go to the first floor in the elevator and then walk across the pool/courtyard area. The breakfast is free and that is all it is worth. There is very little hot food and whatever hot food there is, is usually cold and dried out. The juices are made from powder or frozen concentrate. The make your own waffle area becomes a total mess once one of their sloppy guests gets through with it. The breakfast is not good for more than a quick coffee or juice or bowl of cereal in the morning. There is very little good stuff to eat. The location of the hotel is fine and it is close to all the shuttle points for the various tourist attractions. There is free wireless high-speed internet in the lobby and an ethernet port in the room for you to access the free service. There is also one computer in the lobby for the guests use which is fast and has most of the programs people would need to use to finish up small projects, etc. The rooms have full kitchens and a sitting room with TV set as well as a TV in the bedroom. The washroom is actually 2 seperate areas. One vanity with drawers, sink and mirror and a seperate room for the toilet and bathtub/shower. I never saw one like that before. The walls in the bedroom were paper thin and you could hear the people in the next room talking. I heard quite a bit of mumbling from the person in the room beside mine who seemed drunk. No apology or discount from the front desk after we complained. Just a "We heard that from a few guests, we will tell the manager". It's a good thing we stayed her for only two days as we would have checked out and gone to a better place. For the price we paid (179USD) we felt this place was far overpriced for what we were getting. Unless you can get a rate below $150USD avoid this place. It may be new, but it's badly designed and cheap.

“Exceeded my expectations” I stayed here with my family(husband, toddler and a grandmother). I have previously stayed at several hotels on the riverwalk, the Crowne plaza, La Mansion and holiday inn. I wanted a quick one night budget trip so i chose this hotel. I love that it has its own parking lot, right by market sqaure and a trolley in front to the riverwalk. First off, i love the cancellation policy that allows you to cancel up till the day off at 4pm as i had a cancellation that morning for my inlaws. Upon check in, i was blown away by the renovated spacious lobby with technology nooks on every corner. My favorite were the booths that fit about 3 people with its own personal flat screen tv and hookups for laptops and electronic devices what a neat concept! Check in was quick and easy, very low crowds compared to the bustling riverwalk hotels. I got the rooms i requested and was able to check in by 11am as requested. There is no doorman or any type of help but i expected that. There was a side door next to the elevator that helped out with the unloading of the car. Arrived at our room, and this is one of the two reasons they don't get a 5 star review, the layout is plain akward. There is a large king sized bed, a wonderfully huge 40 inch flat screen tv, fridge, couch with pull out bed but it is placed so very akwardly they need to switch the bed with the couch to allow more room and better visibility of the tv, i doubt they can though as it seems this is an architectural flaw and the bed wont fit that way. Anyways moving on, the room was spotless, carpet was spotless so were the bathrooms and closet, trust me i inspect closely as i have a small child who touches everything. We had a view of the lovely courtyard and the pool. Let me talk about this courtyard, it is so cute! modern wicker couches and an outside fireplace, it is simply adorable! i hope in the spring they would have better landscaping to even better it. Its a great place to drink a glass of wine from the bar in the lobby and hear the birds chirping. Okay the trolley, which is not owned by the hotel so i wish people would stop complaining to the hotel staff about it, it runs very slowly and you have no idea what time it will come, i waited for about 10 minutes luckily and i caught it to the riverwalk $1.10 must have exact change, the rest of the time i caught taxis $6...trust me with the extra $4 each way the taxi was a much easier ride with all our shopping bags and stroller. So i spent about $20 more for 4 trips in a taxi vs waiting on a trolley or driving getting lost and fighting for a parking lot and paying crazy parking fees, well spent! Okay finally breakfast, it is a bistro set up, it is actually a Starbucks with hot food, you can order french toast and eggs and bacon and toast all the works made to order. The food was delicious, the prices were reasonable (about $8 entree) but the service and setup left much to be desired, one cashier, long lines, they forgot to make my order it was very chaotic and i am hoping they can improve on this at a peak breakfast time 8.30am. Besides that, when i am looking to save at least 50-70% on a riverwalk hotel i will always book here!!

“Location can't be beat” Stayed here for 2 nights in Sept 2011. The room was nicer than I was expecting. Clean, comfortable bed, good selection of TV channels and strong WIFI. The location near Sunset and La Brea was ideal for me. Prices were higher than normal because it was Labor Day Weekend, but no complaints.

“EXCELLENCE ACROSS THE BOARD IN ACCOMMODATIONS AND SERVICE” We had a wonderful stay at the Hotel Palomar. The room was very clean, reasonably spacious, and well appointed.The service, including free morning coffee and evening wine tasting, was appreciated. We were allowed to check in early. The restaurant on the premises is staffed by cheerful people and the food, if not gourmet, is quite acceptable. The ambience is a little dark for our tastes but nothing that bothered us. There are nearby restaurants on the UCLA campus that were good for casual food.The hotel, which is on Wilshire near UCLA, has an excellent location. The front desk staff is knowledgeable about tourist destinations and helpful with maps and brochures. We used The Palomar as a base to see the Getty Villa, the Getty Center, LACMA (largest museum west of the Miss. River), Huntington Library, Walt Disney Concert Hall, Manhatten Beach, Santa Monica Pier, and the Hammer Museum. The valet parking was $30 which appeared pretty reasonable for LA. This is our third Kimpton Hotel and we have found each of them to be delightful and very well managed.

“Very Nice Hotel” My wife and I stayed at the Parc 55 for 4 nites in September. Overall it was a very good experience. As noted in several reviews, its location is terrific being central to the BART, buses, and cable cars. The BART from SFO is $8.10 and has a stop at the hotel near Powell St. We walked everywhere and to Chinatown about a 1 mile and up to Nob Hill. Our car rental was through Enterprise which was located across the street. Valet parking is $45 per nite which was the standard for the area. A very touristy location with plenty of high end shopping (Nordstrom’s, Saks etc) and the very large Westfield Mall, all a few steps from Parc 55. This is a very large hotel 1,000+ yet the service both at the front desk and housekeeping was very good. We booked directly through the hotel and their special 20% off for 3 nites worked out to $120 per nite. The room was a king deluxe that was good size and the bath was large with strong shower and all the amenities with good quality towels. HD TV was in all rooms. In house safe was complimentary. The room was made up on a timely basis. The elevators were fast and for a hotel this size, (it was sold out) never had to wait. The 4th floor business center had complimentary internet with a bank of 5 pc’s and there was always a free one. In room internet was $12.95. One foul up was our room on the 9th floor had a distinct smell of smoke that required an aerosol that was promptly delivered by housekeeping. The front desk offered an upgrade but we were so tired passed on their offer and the aerosol did wonders to correct the problem. We did take them up on the offer for our last nite and got a Club Concierge room on the 27th floor which came with continental breakfast. The front desk was very accommodating in some of our minor requests as well.. There is plenty of places close by to grab a coffee in the morning. There are a fair amount of homeless people in the several blocks around the hotel so be aware when walking. In sum, a great value and would definitely return to the Parc 55.

“Double Billed, Beware” I read other reviews where this hotel double charged or wrongly charged their guests, and the guests had a terrible time getting the incorrect charges reversed. I ignored them due to the seeming abundance of good reviews. Wow, am I ever sorry. This place is a nightmare. Suddenly nobody knows anything (I don't have access to that, my supervisor is gone today, blah blah blah) and can't even confirm exactly what they billed to my credit card, let alone why. I show them my credit card statement and even then, they say they don't see where they billed for the charges that are clearly listed on the statement. Its like falling down the rabbit hole; zero accountability. They are incapable of doing ANYTHING but charging credit cards and then pretending like they didn't do it. Frankly, its unbelievable. Which is why I ignored the previous reviewers who had the same problem. Well, believe it. I travel at least 40% of the year and have *never* been subjected to the degrading run-around these con artists have going. There are tons of places to stay in San Diego, choose somewhere else if you value your sanity and/or expect an ethical hotel management system.

“Love-Hate” We loved this hotel at the same time as it made us really mad. The tiny room (over $600 a night with taxes) was uncomfortably small for two people but definitely the best tiny room we’ve experienced. A huge window overlooking the East River, and a window between the bedroom and the bathroom helped opened the room up. However the queen bed, pushed into a corner, made sleeping uncomfortable for the inside person...and ridiculously inconvenient when it came to getting up in the middle of the night. I’d be very comfortable here by myself, but for two grow-ups it felt downright silly...not to mention utterly overpriced. That said, the bed was comfortable, the bed linens and towels great, and the lighting well thought-out. The big TV at the foot of the bed, in front of the huge window, seems gigantic in such a pint-sized room. However, design is everywhere...every little bit of this place is designed for visual interest. I especially loved the black tiles in the bathroom and WC. However, turn on the faucet in the bathroom and water cascades out of the sink soaking an unsuspecting handwasher. And try to plug in your computer and you have to either unplug the radio or a lamp, or perch awkwardly on the bed. (I consider the lack of convenient electrical outlets totally unforgiveable in a new, purpose-built hotel.) I also thought the lack of a cordless phone was very lame. To continue, the closet was so tiny that there was barely room for one day’s worth of clothes next to the thick robes and ironing board. Frankly, hotel developer Andre Balazs should know better by now. The staff was friendly and accommodating, and being in such a creative environment balances, somewhat, the annoyances. My two favorite features were the video collage in the elevators and the knitted cozies slipped over the steel stanchions outside. The location is lots of fun. The meatpacking district seems to be getting better all the time. The elevated Highline Park is a big draw. The area is full of New Yorkers but hip internationals seem to dominate. Are they the only people who can afford The Standard?

“Very good location, but a bit too skimpy on extras” I have stayed here for a business meeting. The price was under $150, which is ok for the location - 1.5 block from Time Square. It is short walk to subway too. The hotel is small, which is probably why it is not possible to have early check in (before 3pm). The front desk staff is attentive, but not flexible. My request (during reservation as an option) for a refrigerator into the room was ignored.
