The waiting area of foyer has marble columns, seating chairs, coffee, WI-fi, newspapers, and a bar (open on weekdays only), and free internet computer stations. The room was small, while adequate. There is a small LCD TV, free internet (plus), a few books (nice touch), phone, iPod dock, Keurig coffee maker w/pods and tea The walls not too sound proof - heard the kid crying next door and some conversation in the corridor. The temperature control is ok, AC is not loud, but next to your bed, so close the duvet well, so it is not cold. The bed was narrow (the narrowest in US seen), while of right length and very comfortable. Do not panic if you cannot find a door to a bathroom first - it is two-fold narrow white one - looks like a closet door. The bathroom has shower; shampoo, soap, but no gel, and no - they will not replace shampoo or soap with new ones when shampoo runs out (forgot may be?), there was just enough towels (definitely skimpy on that). The water pressure and temperature were good. The hotel has a fitness center with one treadmill and a few yoga items; no pool. There is a coffee/tea in a waiting area as well as water-stations on different floors with ready-to-fill empty water bottles (w/caps) - nice. The carpets thought out the hotel definitely look dated (especially next to fitness center) - they probably should consider changing them. Internet is fast and printing is available. The breakfast is continental on Saturday/Sunday (juices, coffee, pastries, boiled eggs, some fruit (no berries), Greek yogurt, cereal) for $11 ($13.95 real after taxes and non-negotiable and not disclosed 18% service charge???) and full American (as option) on weekdays (same as continental + sausages, scrambled eggs, potatoes, bacon) for $16 ($20.30 - real). There is no other food service on weekends. If you want to stay past check out time of 12 noon even by 1 minute, there will be automatic extra charge - no flexibility (very big minus); they of course, will store your belongings (at no charge). Overall, I am giving 3-stars because although, the bed is very comfortable and hotel has many good amenities, there are equally enough shortcoming such as absolute inflexibility on check-out time, too few bath items, and light breakfast choice among others.

“Fantastic place to stay” We stayed at the Buckingham 15-17 August based on the reviews for a family hotel here on TripAdvisor. It certainly didn't disappoint - we had a one bedroom suite which was more like a large apartment - huge lounge with a pull out bed - well resourced kitchen - large master bedroom and good sized bathroom (I agree with the previous posting about the shower - it was brilliant). Staff were lovely. If I was looking to complain - the main bed or pullout bed were not particulary comfortable, and the air conditioning unit in the bedroom was noisy - but both of these I'm sure would have been sorted out if we were staying out for longer - I didn't even bother notifying the hotel of this. Not having a resaurant in the hotel was not a problem as there is the Green Cafe about 1 minute away which has an extensive eat-in or take-away menu. Duane Reade is opposite for milk, water and basic supplies for the kitchen. The hotel itself is in a brilliant location - we were near central park and shopping . I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel for a family and we will definately be staying here again next time we cross the pond.

“Brilliant location for sightseeing” I stayed here for a few night a few weeks ago. The hotel is a couple of hundred yards from Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39. It couldn't be handier for restaurants and one of the sighseeing buses is based just around the corner. Because of its location it was a wee bit noisy at times but on balance the location trumps this. My room was a good size with a marvellous view over the Bay. The hotel staff couldn't have been more helpful. The hotel itself doesn't have a restaurant but there is a lovely wee 1950s type diner just out the backdoor of the hotel which serves the most delicious breakfasts.

“Good value, but very basic!” Excellent price (under $45 a night), but the room was vry small as was their older TV. Small room towels and bedding needs updating; as it's quite old. Nice smaller pool and good sized jacuzzi that are rarely used. Parking lot has lots of oil spills and some of the people staying here were, shall I say, probably were not employed? Solid value and a good location, but proably only a notch or two above Motel 6 for the quality of the room and only a single bolt lock. Not recommended for a family or business travelers unless on a low budget.

“I'm sorry to say I wouldn't stay here again!” I have stayed here many times over the years so when I read all the reviews I thought "it can't have gotten that bad". In the end, I decided to Priceline because I was going on a short shopping trip, needed to stay out by the airport and I thought I'd go less expensive. I got the Doubletree. I would not purposely stay here again at this point. I was so negatively motivated by my experience I even filled out a comment card at the front desk which is unusual for me. First of all what cookies? Once you are a priceline check in, you are dirt. No cookies. No room in the tower. Valet parking was ridiculous it took so long. Sometimes there was nobody there. Checking in I needed bellman assistance. I waited FOREVER and I do not exxagerate. They explained there is only 1 on duty and they get really busy so they would "try" to get one for me. The front desk service was inadequate, and several staff members were hard to understand. In the bar (which is being remodeled) the waitress was far less than courteous. They have 3 computers available for internet access. One was broken the whole time, another was broken most of the time, and they were VERY SLOW. And people sat on them all evening instead of minding the time limit. Nobody on staff noticed. I paid for an extra 1/2 day in order to check out at 6pm. But they didn't tell me I'd need to get my key reactivated so with my arms completely full and in a hurry to catch my flight, I go to access my room from the wing I was in (far far away from the front desk) only to be locked out requiring me to put everything back in the car, drive all the way to the front desk, stand in line while TWO people waited on one guy who wanted quarters, and then have to drive back to my wing. The rooms are marginally clean and there is an "old hotel" smell in the hallways. I left one day at about 8am and there was a room service tray outside the room next to me. It was still there at 9pm that night when I came back. The beds are comfortable. The bathrooms are nice only in that they have a seperate vanity outside the actual bathroom. The nicest thing I can say right now is that this hotel USED to be nice.

“FANTASTIC HOTEL” I stayed at the W in SF for four nights in Nov 04, and I found the entire experience fabulous! My room had an awesome view of the Bay Bridge, everything in the room was super-comfy (esp. the bed and the bathtub), the hotel is quiet in the halls, I loved the Bliss bath products, the room service was DELICIOUS every time and always arrived within 15 minutes of ordering, and all of the service was wonderful, from the front desk to the room service to the maids. I have spent a lot of time South of Market, so I know the neighborhood well, and this is a great locale! I did not want my W experience to end, and I can't wait until I check into the W Seattle in January! I highly rec. this hotel--it's a wonderful sanctuary from the hectic SoMa world outside.

“Holiday Inn Express, so wie man es erwartet” Recht nah am Flughafen gelegen, daher gut für Stop-overs geeignet. Man kann direkt am Hotel kostenlos parken, was bei Hotels am Logan Flughafen nicht immer so ist. Direkt neben an ist ein Countryard, das hat eine Bar, die Abends geöffnet hat, wenn man noch einen Schlummertrunk sucht. Zu Fuss erreicht man schnell ein grosses Einkaufszentrum sowie ein Applebees Restaurant.

“Great stay” We stayed for three nights,our room was on the fourth floor and adequately big enough for the three of us, my husband and adult daughter.The staff were friendly and helpful,it was a good base from which to explore San Francisco. We took an evening Alcatraz tour and a City tour with Shuttle tours which I would recommend if you have limited time in town.

“Joining the chorus of praise” My daughter and I stayed here in a pair of connecting rooms. We had a view of Lafayette Park. The service was first-rate and I thought the rooms were very comfortable. We took advantage of every aspect of the hotel: the first-rate breakfasts, lunch, and dinner in the restaurant, the Off the Record bar, and a room service breakfast. Room service was just fine, but I found it more interesting to have breakfast downstairs, where you can try to guess which famous politico is at the next table. I even used the laundry service, because in hot weather you have to change your shirts, etc., much more often than you'd expect. I suppose there are other great hotels in D.C., but I can't imagine wanting to be anywhere else.

“Amazing Stay” Everything about this hotel was perfect from the location, to the rooms, to the staff, to the bar, and to the amazing restaurant. The hotel is just a short walk from the Whitehouse, and close to a metro station. The rooms are well appointed, stylish and functional. The beds are amazing and the rooms are sound proof so that noise from outside is not a problem. I would stay here again without hesitation.

“As good as rated in TripAdvisor” The Cedarbrook Lodge is as good as rated in Trip Advisor. The Lodge is located on a quiet and peaceful wooded property within a mile of SEATAC airport and is a good value. My honey and I stayed in a huge suite and loved the quality of the room. A nice touch is the high quality snacks that are located in each building that included Haagen-Dazs ice cream. I made the reservation online at the Lodge’s website and took advantage of the prepaid discounted rate. The included breakfast was first class with oatmeal and fresh fruit in addition to regular breakfast fare. The only downside is the new charge for parking.

“Very good hotel, great location for diving in the Apple” I regularly go this hotel on business trip. For a long time I was boarding hotels in quieter areas (3d av/Lex) , I was fearing the crowd of Times Square. But once in the hotel and especially on higher floors you are away from the crowd. The rooms are spacious, quiet, well decorated. Many were renovated lately. Staff is nice but but just - It is a very big hotel so quite impersonal. and lots of traffic. But it is the case of most New York hotels. I would 'complain' about the long and slow lines at reception - happens too often. I do not use the hotel services much and could not comment on that. So much available in the city, why eat or drink or spend time in the hotel ... Well that's only my point of view. Higher floors offer great views to Times Square or the Hudson.

“Too Many Unpleasant Surprises” A little background – during a weekend in New York, my traveling companion was admitted to the hospital. There was no firm date for release so I had to book hotel rooms at the last moment. After staying at four hotels, I finally checked in to the Marriott East Side. I had a series of one night reservations so that I could cancel and leave with only a day notice (reservations required cancellation the day before arrival.) Some of the nights used Marriott Reward Points and some were paid. The stay extended into the weekend of the New York Marathon so hotels were full or very expensive. When I arrived at the Marriott East Side, all went well. Check-in was easy and I mentioned that I had a series of one night reservations. No problem or so I was told. My room was exactly what I had requested. Since this would be my home for the next several nights, I unpacked and was relieved that I’d not need to pack/move/unpack again. I had done that four days in a row and it gets old. As an elite member of Marriott Rewards, I enjoyed a visit to the Concierge Lounge before departing for the hospital to visit my friend. The next day, I returned in the afternoon from a hospital visit and found that my key no longer would open the door. I went to reception to get new keys and was informed I’d have to change rooms. At check-in they had forgotten to block me into the same room for all of my reservations. They had already blocked my room for another arriving guest so I had no choice but to move. I don’t know what they would have done if I had not returned until later that evening – my stuff was in the room. So, for a fifth day I packed and moved to a new room. Now the problem began. I could not get WiFi reception in the new room. I called and was connected to their technical support service who seemed to know about the problem. They said it was most likely the router on the floor and they’d have that reset. However, the next morning I still could not establish a connection to the Internet. In the hallway, I had no problem establishing connection but my room was a dead spot. On my way to the lounge, I saw another guest sitting in the hallway with his laptop so I’m guessing the problem occurs with more than one room. That’s inexcusable for a business hotel. I thought I would simply use the computers in the lounge or at least connect to WiFi while in the lounge. I then learned that the lounge would not be open after breakfast hours on Friday until Sunday evening. In other Marriott properties, you can at least access the lounge even if there are no other services available in the lounge. Not at this property! When the lounge is closed, no one can access the lounge. I asked about breakfast on weekends for elite guests and was told there was no option. That was a surprise and I learned a “loophole” in the Marriott Rewards program. If a hotel does not have a lounge, certain levels of elite members are given breakfast in the dining room. If the hotel has a lounge, you’re given access to the lounge instead. If they have a lounge but it is closed, you’re simply on your own for breakfast. After complaining, I was comped breakfast for the two days the lounge would be closed. I was very surprised to learn the lounge would be closed on the weekend. The hotel was sold out and they were charging premium prices due to the marathon. Seems to me this would have been a good weekend to keep the lounge open. Even though this is an older property, they do have the new Marriott beds and they were comfortable. Housekeeping did a decent job of cleaning the rooms. Water pressure and temperature in the shower did vary a bit during a shower but not enough to make me get out of the shower. There was very little counter space in the bathroom. Wake-up calls arrived on schedule. Overall, the hotel and rooms feel older, dated, and occasionally shabby. Internet service was spotty as mentioned above. Even when I tried using the wired computers in the lounge (when it was open), the response time was terribly slow. There frequently was a line at reception but my waits were not overly long. Maybe I was being overly critical because I was preoccupied with my friend’s hospitalization. My stay in New York had become unexpectedly extended and I really needed the Internet to keep up with issues at work. This was a time when I needed Marriott to come through and provide the services I’ve come to expect. Usually that happens, but it didn’t happen at the Marriott East Side. On Sunday (the day of the marathon), I was happy to check out and move next door to the new Hyatt Lex58 . But that’s another review.... Overall, I was disappointed in the property, their handling of my reservations, and the awful state of Internet service in the hotel. I’d certainly encourage others to look elsewhere at this price point and in this neighborhood. There certainly are plenty of other options within several blocks.

“Top Lage!” Hier zählt in erster Linie die zentrale Lage auf der Powell Street (Cable Car Haltestelle vor der Türe, Union Square wenige Meter entfernt). Das Einzelzimmer lag zum Hinterhof, so dass man vom Straßenlärm nichts mitbekommen hat. Das Waschbecken befand sich direkt im Zimmer; Dusche und WC waren in einem kleinen abgetrennten Raum. Das Zimmer war sehr klein und es gab keinen Safe im Zimmer und keinen Kühlschrank. Für einen kurzen Aufenthalt ist das sicherlich ok. Einen Safe gibt es an der Rezeption. Hier könnte die Kontrolle allerdings etwas besser sein, wenn man sich den Briefumschlag mit den Wertgegenständen geben lässt. Insgesamt war das Personal freundlich und hilfsbereit und das Zimmer war sauber. Ich würde wieder hier übernachten. Aber: Vor 2 Jahren habe ich im Hotel Fusion übernachtet, das nur wenige Meter entfernt ist. Das Zimmer hatte bei gleichem Preis einen Safe im Zimmer, einen Kühlschrank, Frühstück war im Preis inbegriffen und das Zimmer war mehr als doppelt so groß. Wenn ich wählen könnte, würde ich bei gleichem Preis das Hotel Fusion bevorzugen. The Stratford punktet durch die Lage direkt auf der Powell Street.

“Great weekend in Boston” The location cannot be beat in Boston. We walked everywhere easily! Steps from Government center, right near the common, and only 5 minutes to the North End. Also, with a T stop right there, everything is easy to get to. We had an upgrade to a room with a view, which was great. You could see the entire common and beyond, as well as the river. Room was clean, bed comfortable, bathroom great (love the bath products at Kimpton hotels), wine reception great. My only complaint was the first night the group across the hall was slamming their door all night. We physically tried to close our door that loudly just to test how hard it was, and we could not do it as loudly as they were so I don't know what was up with that. Though that's nothing against the hotel, just the rude group that was staying there.

“Nice large convention hotel in a good location, but check-in can be a challenge” Overall, I really enjoyed the Sheraton. Got a great rate and had very well done (but small) renovated rooms in the north tower. My biggest problem is the sheer size of the hotel. Check-in took 40 minutes at 5pm and only one room was available. There were two of us and we didn't get the second room until 8:30pm! (No kidding). The front desk staff was very nice but just completely overwhelmed by the numbers of people in the lobby Rooms are typical of most upscale hotels. Flat screen TV, expensive TV offerings (internet, movies, etc), nice bath, good toiletries, etc. I would stay at this hotel again if the price was right or if I was attending a convention here or nearby. Otherwise, I may try for a smaller more "human-sized" property.

“Good Place to Stay Near the Alamo” The Residence Inn near Alamo Plaza is a great place to stay while visiting the Alamo/ Riverwalk/ downtown San Antonio area. The location is not on the Riverwalk but is close enough to be very convenient as well as several dollars cheaper. The one bedroom suite provides much more space than the typical hotel room with a queen-size bed. After hours spent exploring San Antonio, it is good to return to a private sitting area to relax. The suite has upholstered couch, chair, and TV in the sitting area with a work desk and internet access. The area is open to the kitchen with full-size refrigerator, microwave, sink, 2-burner stove top, and mini-dishwasher. The bedroom and bath has the convenience of the sink and vanity area outside the tub and toilet area. A full-size closet allows guests to hang all clothes and put away the luggage. An iron and ironing board are also provided. The one-bedroom suite has a second TV in the bedroom. The lobby is functional, but the best feature of the first floor is the complimentary breakfast each morning. An attractive, spacious area allows for multiple food stations, and plenty of seating is available. Breakfast choices prevent guests from having to eat the same menu every morning. Choices include scrambled eggs, sausage, bread to toast, muffins, bagels, cooked oatmeal with pecans, raisins, cinnamon, and brown sugar toppings, yogurt, make-your-own waffles, cold cereals, and fresh fruit. Beverages included coffee, hot tea, orange, apple, and cranberry juice. On Monday morning, additional items were French toast, fried potatoes, and doughnuts. Considering the quality, quantity, and variety of the breakfast, the room rate is a good deal, especially for a family on a weekend rate. The room, public areas, hallways, and elevators are all clean and attractive. The hotel is not new, but the condition of the furnishings is still good. The central heat/air unit is controlled by a thermostat in the bedroom, and the operation is quiet. The only noise that might affect sleep was from a night club next door, but the volume reaching our 12th floor room on Saturday evening did not prevent our sleep; the club did not appear to be open on Sunday night. Two computers are available in the lobby for short-term guest use. The outdoor swimming pool is small. The hotel has a parking garage with either self or valet parking. Self parking is $22; valet is more. We just parked ourselves and left the car sitting in the garage all weekend since it was so easy to walk everywhere we wanted to go. The view from our room on the backside of the hotel was unobstructed; the view from the rooms on the front may later be affected by a new hotel that is under construction across the street. We enjoyed our stay at the Residence Inn on Bonham and would definitely return again.

“Flawless execution” I stayed here for a business convention and it ran at 100% capacity. Their execution was flawless. The rooms were clean, service fast. My room had a spectacular view of the lake and the Navy pier. The bath tub was comfortable and the bathrobe plush. The elevators have the new controls where you punch the floor number into the control and the screen directs you to an elevator, rather than choose the floor inside the elevator. It takes a little getting used to, but it is much more efficient than the old style. Thy Hyatt Regency next door was part of the same conference, and it has the old system. The difference was remarkable, as there were long lines and slow rides at the Hyatt. There is a bunch of construction going on, so the site is a bit confusing. The breakfast buffet ($26) was great. No omelette station, but the usual hot foods in a high class hotel breakfast buffet. The location is an easy walk to lots of great stuff in downtown Chicago. Internet was nice and fast at 6 Mbps, and $10 per day. I had a problem with the internet and they sent tech support to my room instantly, and the guy fixed the problem fast. Parking was expensive at $52 per day, but you don't really need a car if all you are doing is a downtown convention.

“Can be hit or miss -- but very nice when it's a hit” Beautiful hotel. Renovated rooms are very nice. Spacious fitness facility. Spotty service, which isn't all that surprising at a property this huge. I stay here regularly for business. Shop for good rates, which you can get when there is not a huge meeting. I'm a Hilton Gold. Do not get consistent treatment (upgrade, etc.); the Lounge is spacious and staff very nice, but the food options are only average.

“Honey I shrunk the room” Yes, those who have written reviews about he size of the rooms - especially the "double" - are correct. The double room is a bit snug, and the blue "mood lighting" does not make it any bigger, albeit the Bose Radio, the flatscreen TV, and those great bath products do add to the overall experience. Yet, the other features of the hotel, from the helpful staff, a free NYT in the AM, to the very soothing spa/yoga/meditation rooms and the very decent restaurant, make you want to forget that one shortcoming. Breakfast was quite good, a nice waffle with real fruit, and a hot cup of herbal tea hit the spot, and the waitress actually smiled and was very attentive - not a bad way to start the day. The location is also quite good, especially with a subway station literally a few hundred yards from the front door. I stayed in room 1307, and there was very little road NYC street noise filtering in. If there is a loud party on the bar on the 14th, you may want to stay a floor or two lower. Overall, a solid B+.

“Excellent location and service” One of my favorite locations in NYC, right in the heart of everything. Hotel is no thrills modern and rooms are spacious and comfortable. Highly recommend it if staying in Midtown.

“Good location but not worth what you pay” We were in Washington and Oregon for a week, and this was the most we paid for a room and the least satisfied we were. To be fair, the location of this hotel is fantastic and the staff was friendly. Unfortunately though, that's where it ends. We were paying close to $300 a night for our room and did not feel like it was worth it at all. Here are my specific complaints: 1. Our confirmation said we would have a "spectacular view of Elliott Bay." We were able to see the bay, I'll give them that. Spectacular would be overstating it, though. If we stood in one of the corners of the room right up against the window and looked off to the side, we could see the water over top of a couple of parking garages. Spectacular? Not really. This alone would not have been enough to make me complain though since we don't really spend a lot of time in our room. 2. The bed was not comfortable AT ALL. I usually like Marriott beds and think they're very comfy. This one was awful. I read another review saying they felt like they were bouncing around all night any time their spouse moved. Yup, I'll agree with that. I don't really have back problems, but by the end of our 3-night stay my back was killing me and I really hadn't slept well because of all the bouncing around. 3. The third morning of my trip, the shower was ice cold. This was the last straw for me. $300 a night for a cold shower? Really??? At this point I filled out a comment card for the manager. I would have called and talked to someone directly but we were in a hurry to get on the road and my husband didn't want me to take the time. I was very specific on the comment card and left all my contact info hoping for something in response, and I have heard absolutely nothing in response to my complaints which makes me cranky. I may still call although I don't know what I would expect to happen at this point. To sum up, the location was really great and for that reason I could give it 2 stars instead of 1. Otherwise I felt like it was a total rip. One more tip: I wouldn't really advise paying a lot of extra money for the concierge level unless you get a good deal and it's not too much more than a regular room. You get free breakfast which is always nice, but it's basically bread stuff (cereal, muffins, etc) and scrambled eggs and bacon. It's the same thing every morning. They have free muchies in the afternoon and you can buy drinks, but the drinks are just as overpriced as they would be in a bar. So it was nice enough and all, but not worth a whole lot of extra money. . \

“Dated by about 100 Years” The Algonquin hotel is OLD, and they seem proud of it. The decor is all turn-of-the-century (20th) themed. For those who are into that sort of thing, it's probably a great hotel. The rooms were actually more nicely appointed than I thought they would be, although I still wouldn't write home. There was an LCD flat panel TV, probably about 32", however there was no HD programming. There was also an MP3 clock radio -- the same model you find in Hilton hotels... terrible sound, but it gets the job done. The room was very small and a little uncomfortable. All in all, I would not stay here again. However, if early 1900s decor is something you would like, then this is the place for you.

“Nothing unexpected...high standards, great bar!” Thanks to reviews at Tripadvisor I choose this hotel. Free shuttles from Midway---and the first stop of the several hotels, this place did not disappoint. The staff was more than friendly, willing to look up locations and print directions. The bar was always hopping, a good mix of interesting travelers. Breakfast was outstanding! High quality ingredients, really fresh fruit and custom omelets. Room service was very prompt. No surprises from the room, four star quality. A quick trip back to the airport and for 2.25 you can be on the Orange Line right into downtown. Beats a $60 cab ride, and much faster.

“Different and fun and interesting” The beginning of a six-night trip to the Northwest began at the MarQueen Hotel in Seattle (600 Queen Ann Avenue North, Seattle 98109 – 1.800.614.1750). I picked this hotel because it was close to a restaurant across the street that I wanted to try -Toulouse Petit Kitchen & Lounge - and it had great ratings on the Trip Advisor. The price was excellent. The night before departure I googled the “street view” of the hotel and was filled with apprehension. It looked like a run-down neighborhood, no tall buildings and generally pretty iffy. But, it was too late to cancel and it was just for one night... On arrival I discovered that I was totally wrong in my first internet impressions! The hotel was an apartment house converted into hotel suites. With three floors (no elevator) and a grand double stairway, it felt like an intimate European hotel. The staff was very gracious and gave us a room on the third floor overlooking the street. Our room was actually a suite with a bedroom, a sitting room with sofa and chair, an entry hall, full kitchen and several closets. The bathroom was large and spotlessly clean. The bed was comfortable. The floors were hardwood with rugs and tile in the kitchen and bath. It was comfortable, clean, cozy and inviting. We unpacked and asked the front desk clerk about the restaurant across the street and got information about the history of the building and the neighborhood. I recommend this hotel highly. It’s not Mariott or Hyatt or Doubletree, it’s different and fun and interesting –which is the whole idea in travel and having new experiences. And our dinner at Toulouse Petite was amazing!!!

“I Love The Pod” I have stayed at the Pod many times now, it is my place in NYC where I feel you get a very good value. I have stayed in all size rooms from a single bed, a bunk with shared bath and queen size beds with private baths. I enjoyed every stay. My last stay was a little disappointing because the room was not clean. It needed to be vacuumed and when I moved the mattress from the was there was a lot of dust and crud. The shared bathrooms are never a problem, they are private and usually very clean. My only complaint is that the front desk people are very rude and not friendly at all, they make you feel like you are bothering them. This has been the case with every stay. If you can get over rude front desk people, the location and the rooms are great.

“Great quaint hotel in the middle of the Gaslamp Quarter” This small Hilton can be mistaken for an apartment complex. We stayed there for one night and were very pleased with the room and the help that we received. The rooms are larger than the ones at the Hyatt Grand Manchester, and the location cannot be beat! The bellman even told me of a great place to park the car (parking structure next to the ballpark, in front of the omni), and its only two small blocks away. So the next time you are there forget the expensive valet parking, drop off your luggage with the bellman and run over to that parking structure.

“OK. A few hiccups, but good value in a great location” Stayed here with my family -- they were touring while I was in town on business. The location was perfect for both activities (on Penn Square, near Reading Terminal). Rooms were spacious and very well-priced for the location. The housekeeping was a bit suspect -- there was a layer of dust on top of each television. Also, if you valet park your car, expect an unreasonably long wait for your car. (We waited over an hour on a Friday afternoon.)

“Great Location. No Additional Fees.” I stayed here for 4 nights during a recent business trip. The hotel is in a great location near major highways and tons of restaurants. The interior looks a little dated but I would recommend if you can get a good deal (i.e. priceline)

“Time travel to the 70s in the heart of Boston” The Midtown is a budget-traveler and bus tour standby because of its "cheap-for-Boston" rates and proximity to major tourist sites. The hotel itself is really nothing special and you feel as though you have stepped 30 years into the past when you walk in. It can get a little loud and feels a little outdated but overall it is a decent place to stay and a true bargain for downtown Boston.

“Marvelous accomodation, salvaged our anniversary” Stayed here for one night for our silver anniversary -- not the place we had PLANNED for such a special night, but our original choice had left us in the lurch upon arrival that afternoon, and this place was highly rated AND had vacancies. Glad to report that this second choice hotel was not second rate. Rate for suite was $207 per night, tax included. Suite included kitchenette, lounge area, phone, full bath, free WiFi, and TV with about 50 channels. Like all EmbS lodging, free "happy hour" drinks and huge breakfast buffet are included. Hotel had enclosed atrium in spanish style, a pool, and a gym. Staff was professional and very pleasant -- got to have a wonderful conversation with the general manager. Hotel was located close to I-35, but not much else -- you'll need a car to get to anywhere in Austin.

“Superb location, high prices” Located on the main tourist transit system, the property provides superb views of the riverfront area and is within walking distance of old town. The common areas are not well executed being small and compartmented resulting in an "ant hill effect" as you negotiate from the front to elevators. Too, it is a three elevator ride and two walks to get to the parking garage. The bar patio is a narrow affair not capitalizing on the views. I found the bar service and kitchen to be below average on two visits. Expect to pay an extremely high tariff to park, eat or drink. Rooms were clean, well appointed and comfortable. Bottom line: on the next visit I will explore another property.

“Nice notel. Great location” We really liked this hotel. We got a great deal direct from the hotel website. The room we had was massive and the bathroom was amazing. Although I really did not like the sliding window between the bathroom and bedroom ..... but that was just me. The location was great. South station is only a few mins walk away from the hotel. In the other direction, you have a 10 min walk to the restaurants down at the aquarium.

“I love it” Yeah the rooms need updating But they are big, clean, great beds-and the pool area is still one of the best ever at a non resort. The trees planted 64 years ago, ringing the huge pool, with the poolside bar, just reek of classic Hollywood. And the coffee shop, completely remodeled in classic mid century style, looks great and has wonderful breakfasts. We paid $83 (+ approx $20 in taxes and parking). You can't beat that

“Good value, excellent location” The hotel is an old building: simple and old fashioned, but clean and comfortable. The room is big, though it has an old tv with not too good reception. But internet is free. You also have breakfast included, simple but ok. No frills, but good value for your money. The location is excellent.

“A complete bargain for NYC!!” I am a self-professed hotel snob, and am still mourning the closing of the Plaza. I have since stayed at the St Regis, Trump International, Waldorf Towers, and Four Seasons. They are all "nice," and expensive. That's fine. . .you get what you pay for. I saw the rates of the Sofitel (booked on their website for around $250/nt) for three nights in late July. I didn't have the highest of expectations given the price for a hotel in NYC, but boy what a pleasant surprise. I was able to check in almost 2 hours early, and took advantage of their late check-out, and I greatly enjoyed the location in midtown. The twice daily maid service was wonderful, including morning service on the day I checked out! I echo everyone else's comments on the beds, the great Roger & Gallet amenities, the huge bathroom, and I greatly appreciated the peace and quiet (and I was in a room right by the elevator) and rarely heard anyone outside in the hallway. Finally, my room on the 14th floor didn't have much of a view, but it was nice and quiet and comfortable. I believe I may have finally found a new home base in NYC!! Merci Sofitel!!

“Best Location for Airport, nice amenities” The Hilton at Logan Airport is the best place to stay if you need quick access to the airport - good shuttle service and great parking deals if you need to leave your car for a few days. Standard Hilton services - clean, nicely decorated room, good room service, nice restaurant and a safe, well maintained property. It is worth a few dollars more to stay here rather than struggle to the airport early in the morning! Shuttle drivers are invariably polite - even at 4 am!

“Location - but that's about it” If you want a real "pot luck" experience in San Francisco, book into the King George. The major selling point is its location: just a block from Union Square and surrounded by diners and bars - though the streets of San Francisco in this area have a very high concentration of people rattling a cup under your nose for some spare change. Nevertheless, it's cheap compared to other hotels in the area - but be aware that your experience is likely to reflect the relatively low price. Because the hotel is narrow and stretches back from the street, the views are mostly to the sides. If you're lucky enough to get a high room on the north side you'll get a view up the hill; but you're more likely to end up on the other side with a terrible view or no view at all. In my case, the first room I was given had a tiny window which looked directly on to a wall. Since I was there for nearly a week I asked for something better and was given another room on the 3rd floor with a view on to the back alley. Since at least it was quiet (well, apart from one night when a drunk guy sat and hollered late into the night), I settled on that room. A family member who joined me the next day was given a room on the same floor in which the window actually had FROSTED GLASS to hide how ugly the view was outside: it looked directly on to the building next door's rooftop, complete with all the machinery you find on top of commercial premises. Next, infrastructure. The King George might look charming, and to be fair, the decor has been renovated; but it fell short in a number of ways. One was the elevator: just one and incredibly slow. Secondly, no air conditioning: fine in early June but I wonder about July and August. Thirdly, the internet - admittedly free - was most definitely not high speed: it was almost impossible to log on and incredibly slow once I finally got a connection. And most strikingly for me, the hot water system was totally inadequate. The first morning I ran the shower for more than five minutes waiting for the cold water to turn warm. Eventually I called reception and asked if there was a problem. I was told I had to "run both faucets until I got hot water then turn off the one I didn't want". After 3-4 more minutes finally the shower ran hot and I adjusted the mixer tap - but within a few minutes it was cold again! For six mornings I endured the same thing: waves of hot and cold water as I showered, almost always ending with me rinsing my hair in cold. And it wasn't the mixer tap: the same was true in the sink as I tried to shave: one stroke warm, the next cold. All things considered, I wouldn't go back to the King George and wouldn't recommend it to other people. If price and location are all that matter, go ahead: but go knowing that the old adage applies: you get what you pay for.

“I have stayed here twice and enjoyed it both times.” My most recent stay at the Millenium Hilton was in March, 2010. My prior stay was about two years before that. My first stay - booked through Priceline - caused me some concern in that there were online reviews that commented about the Ground Zero construction noise. Fortunately, I arrived early in the day and had the ability to request a room facing away from the construction. The second time around, I booked directly with the hotel. However, since the hotel was fully booked, I could not succeed in requesting the side facing away from construction. Granted, during the day, there was discernible construction noise. However, by bedtime, the noise had stopped. Regardless, the view overlooking Ground Zero was incredible. When my friends came to meet me for dinner, we spent at least half an hour comparing the construction site map with what we saw from the window. The area immediately surrounding the hotel is bustling with activity. There is a Starbucks downstairs and the Century 21 Department store just across the street. Subway transportation is conveniently nearby. This area of Manhattan may not be an obvious choice for NYC visitors. But, if you stay here, expect a comfortable stay in a safe and convenient part of town.

“The Worst” I would Not stay here again. I thought how bad could it be? It was a good location and the price was right. How much time do you really spend in the hotel? It was Dirty - Really dirty. I don't think they even change the sheets. The light fixture wires were just hanging from the ceiling - that can't be safe. Alot of the bathroom tiles were missing and I don't think it had been cleaned between guests. The TV would not turn on. The front desk was RUDE, Rude, Rude!! It seemed so dirty we didn't even sleep between the sheets and used our sweatshirts instead of the pillows, which didn't have pillowcases. I wasn't expecting a 5 star, but I think it would have been cleaner to sleep on the street.

“Great for early morning flights” I have stayed here on several occasions before an early morning departure. Living 30 miles outside of Boston, you never now what the traffic will be like. Instead of getting up in the middle of the night, stressing about traffic and then arriving way to early for your flight why not stay here? Rooms are nicely decorated and clean, there is a nice pub where you can have a decent if not overpriced meal and a shuttle that runs every 15 minutes that takes you to your terminal. Heck you can even check your bags and get your boarding pass the night before.

“Surprisingly wonderful” Stayed at Houstonian over last weekend for a wedding. The hotel was packed with several wedding parties. I thought it would be awful but I was willing to put up with it as the whole wedding arty was staying there. I could not have been more wrong. While the hotel is dark and outdated physically that does not stop it from offering guests a first rate experience by deploying excellence in service and amenities. The bedding is first - rate, the toiletries are very good, the room is totally comfortable, housekeeping service is impeccable, the room was spotless, cleaned at convenient times, stocked with everything you might need. On that crazy busy weekend we could have been dealing with frazzled valets trying to figure out the bus services of the various groups but no, they were incredible and went above and beyond keeping us informed on the whereabouts of our missing bus. Luggage was smoothly brought to and from our room without any sense of rush or disorganization despite the mad crowds. Brilliant. One of my favorite things when I stay at a hotel is to order room service breakfast. Unfortunately it is often a letdown in terms of quality and service (long waits etc). The Houstonian delivers the best room service breakfast I have ever had (including the ones we had at the best hotels in Asia). The pancakes were so good my daughter and I ate the, with ought syrup. The bacon was crisp and not fatty in the least. Everything looked and tasted beautifully fresh. The omelet was piping hot, the yoghurt cool and delicious. We were still asleep when it was delivered and the waiter whisked the table in quietly and slipped put without fanfare or bill signing. Bliss. I don't want to chat with a stranger in my nightie. They get it! One morning I misordered and when we called to get the right t hings they were quick to deliver the new order and totally took the blame- charging us only for the right order. The pool area is not very luxurious but great for kids and loads of space is available for everyone ( three pools), and it's great for kids. I would take this kind of perfectionist service and quality over a cooler, hipper decor any day. I have a cool hip home, what I want when I travel is this kind of white glove service, with no sign of how all my little and big needs are being met! This place is just great, so look past the dated endlessly brown furniture and go and treat yourself to old fashioned great hospitality and the best pancakes ever!

“OK, Poor Location, Fair Customer Service” I stayed here for one night in a Suite. When I arrived the agent told me he was upgrading me to a suite which I thought was odd because I had booked a suite which included a free appetizer and a full breakfast. I asked about the appetizer and the breakfast and if I needed a coupon at check in and was told that I "did not" and just to tell the people in the restaurant and everything would be fine. So when I went to the breakfast buffet the next morning and started the order breakfast, I was given this "horrible attitude" by the young woman behind the counter about "I NEED A COUPON" or else! I tried to explain to her what I was told but she told me she wasn't "listening to me." So I went back to the front desk and got a coupon. By that time there was a long line at the buffet. When I finally reached the front of the line she said to me: "OK now I will LISTEN TO YOU." I placed my order.... I am a Starwood Gold Member and I have never been treated like this in any Starwood hotel ever before...... The manager said "they like to keep the coupons behind the desk...." There was a paint cart in the hall abandoned when I checked in right in front of my room with uncovered turpentine, paints of different colors, that I had to move down the hall to a more ventilated area. I have asthma so it was really smelling up the hall. I went back downstairs and asked that it be removed from the hallway. Eventually it was....an hour or so later.... The air conditioning in the room was fair....not enough to cool both rooms... I had ordered extra pillows and towels but they never were delivered to the room... I think I'll give this one a miss next time....

“Not bad if you get a good rate” I stayed here for a 3-day convention. Overall the hotel isn't bad depending upon what you pay. Anything less than $125/night in my book is a great deal. Hotel staff - This is a very busy convention hotel so think twice before staying here for leisure because you won't get a lot of personal attention. Location - Good location just a few blocks from Michigan Ave. Fox & Obel (upscale grocery store rumored to be where Oprah shops!) is right around the block with an in-store cafe. This is the closest place to walk for a quick breakfast or lunch (opens at 7am everyday) if you don't want to eat hotel fare. $4 fare in cab from Union Station. Room - As other reviewers claimed, the beds are seriously fabulous - maybe one step below the Westin's Heavenly bed. Rooms are clean and quiet. Housekeeping does not restock amenities so hide the shampoo and conditioner (Pantene products) if you want more. Wished I had read the reviews beforehand and knew that you have to deadbolt your door to make the a/c run cold. I thought I was having hot flashes! Gym - They charge you $15/stay to use their rather limited gym. Pool is free. Gym has the usual bike, ellipical trainer, treadmill - but are all state of the art. The attendant never seems to be there so I somehow wasn't charged even though I signed in everyday. Most of the women employees of the hotel use the gym locker room for social time which explains why there wasn't much hairspray or lotion left for the guests. Restaurant - Denny's quality at Morton Steakhouse prices

“Most comfortable bed ever!” This hotel was fantastic! Great location, hip bar, modern decor. Rooms aren't enormous but are roomy enough, and the bed, pillows and down comforter are amazing! We also got a very reasonable rate on-line. Plus there are Bliss products in the bathroom! I would definitely stay here again.

“old and tired, resting on its laurels” This place has totally gone to the dogs since Taj Group took over. While the place still looks nice from the outside, the little details are all gone. The carpets are dirty, there are dusty fake plants in the public bathrooms, fixtures that are chipped, chaulking that needs to be redone. They're cutting corners and prices are still high. The high tea service, for $42, advertises loose tea, but instead you get a tea bag in your tea pot, albeit a big tea bag, but still, it doesn't steep as well. Little things matter at this price point. Take you money and go to the Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental or some other luxury hotel where they know what they're doing.

“Great staff, average hotel” I hate to say bad things about this hotel, given firstly that everyone else loves it and secondly the pride that all the staff clearly take in their hotel. However I found it pretty average. The staff were absolutely great - both welcoming and helpful. However, I found both the public areas and the rooms very basic and not appealing. I'd stress again that the staff were great. It was just the hotel itself that I wasn't blown away by. Sorry guys.

“Good enough for a few nights......” My family, 2 adults , 2 teens just spent 3 nights at this hotel. Rooms: We booked a Jr.Suite and a room with 2 doubles. (Suite 1421 & room 1416) The rooms were clean and roomy. The beds were comfortable enough because they are topped with a feather bed and a down comforter. The mattress itself was rather old and in desparate need of replacement. Room Service: We ordered several room service items rather late at night on 2 evenings. The "T.V. dinners-American with burger and fries=not good at all Steak frittes with mushrooms=not good (missing the mushrooms) 2 pizzas=very good (The Philadelphia & margherita) Turkey Club= good Reception: Check-in, quick and thorough Valet: professional and prompt. (each time we called for our car, it was out front by the time we got downstairs) The room doors are what appeared to be solid wood with no type of insulating factor, nor do they close quietly whatsoever. You have to take special care to close them as quietly as possible. However, in every hotel there are always people who seem to have no consideration for others and let the doors slam. Doors slammed at all hours on the top floor of this hotel. I would like to add that the location is convenient to everything and being on the top floor , we didn't hear any street noise. The next time that we fly in for a hockey game, we would probably not choose the Sofitel as we would prefer a little more luxury.

“Very nice hotel” Your typical well appointed city hotel. Staff was VERY attentive and helpful. Hotel was spotless and clean. Rooms were large and modern. Workout room was weak. Food again was higher priced hotel food but good. Overall I would recommend it.

“Elegant Hotel, Good Customer service” A Colleauge and I stayed at the Four Seasons, Philadelphia at the last minute for a conference we attended (9/28/07- 10/2/07. We had booked our double room at another hotel from May '07 but we were informed that the room we booked was unavailable when we checked in. Our Organization called the Four Seasons and they got us a room immediately.. Although initially extremely disapponted with the poor service we were subjected to, we were very happy our original hotel did not have our room because the Four seasons was far superior. This is an elegant hotel with very attentive, customer focused staff. The concierge was very helpful and informative , bell service was fast and efficient. The rooms are not as luxurious as one would expect for the price , the rooms are rather basic, but they are uber clean and comfortable. The beds were outstanding in the level of comfort they provided; and the interior of the hotel's public spaces and rooms are simply beautiful. I don't think I could afford to stay here if I had to personally pay, but If I have the opportunity to do Business In Philadelphia again, this would be the hotel of choice.

“Michelangelo -- really wonderful!” Stayed here for nearly a week in late September for a work event (along with 50 or so work colleagues, not in the same room, fortunately). I thought the Michelangelo was wonderful. Very clean, large rooms, very quiet considering the location. Bathrooms had wonderful huge soaking tubs, and the location was really good -- right next to Times Square, but also close to good restaurants and shopping. I've stayed in other hotels in NYC, and this is by far the best. Staff was very nice, gave excellent restaurant recommendations.

“Quiet, great value, close to attractions.” My wife and I stayed here 3 nights -- we used priceline and got a great rate (under $100 per night) for a Fri, Sat & Sun night in April. Our room was small but was a corner room - even had an East River view - nice. The room was clean - well lit. There was a safe in the room (set your own combo, no fee). Unfortunately, the internet was not free (Something like $14 per night) -- too bad. Also, the business center had a $5 min (even to just print boarding passes) - it is open 24 hrs. The bed was only a queen and the linens were okay - nothing bad, nothing special. The AC was not wonderful - mind you it was 90-degrees outside in April so perhaps it was not prepared for the heat. Bathroom had a nice shower and toiletries. The hairdryer left room for improvement -- it was mounted to the bathroom wall and did not work too well -- plus it kept overheating. Still, the room was quiet and very private with views so not much to complain about - especially given the excellent price. The hotel is right on 42nd street - it's a few blocks west to a subway station - but that station is Grand Central, giving you access to pretty much everywhere. Plus, there are two bus lines right outside that take you to the station (they come about every 5 minutes - we never had to wait more than that -- even on Sunday & late nights. One Bus actually takes you all the way to Time Square (actually, it's only like a mile) but then goes North on Broadway all the way up the West Side -- getting around is very easy. The UN is a 5 minute walk as are several consulate offices. The Tudor Village area is very quiet, scenic and residential -- tucked away from some of the busy streets. There are some nice little parks with river views just upstairs outside the hotel. Despite the few minor limitations, this hotel was perfect -- can't beat the quality and price. Felt very safe and staff were always at the door. Would return for sure.

“Days Inn Gracelands” Ok this place is pretty rank. Its not pretty to look at but it is very well located... just opposite Graceland’s and the free tour buses that run into downtown from there. We asked our room to be changed once but the alternative room was of just as shoddy a state (grim beds, scaly bathroom, stained floors, carpets and sheets), at least it was facing reception so felt a little more secure. I’d recommended to someone looking for a short stay but its no palace at all, its location and ease of transportation are to be noted though.

“At your service” This hotel in midtown is excellent. It was our 20th anniversary and they gave me a discount off my room rate and then offered me the best suite in the hotel for a nominal upgrade fee. Fantastic. The bellman and front desk staff were excellent. They coulnd't do enough for you. The rooms are a little tricky though in the fact that the hallways offer a lot of twists and turns. It would be easy to get lost (and I did - and I've been to MANY hotels). This hotel is a little older, but it has been kept in top shape. You can't really go wrong at The Michelangelo

“A dishonourable establishment” I booked this hotel through a reputable travel site but when we went to check out they produced a bill that was higher than it should have been. I told them the rate was incorrect and showed them the confirmation but they simply said we'd have the pay the higher rate, that it really wasn't their problem and we should sort it out with the travel site ourselves. We didn't have time to get into a prolonged debate as we had a flight to catch so we had to leave and I then had to waste time during my holiday writing a formal complaint and chasing them up several times before they finally agreed to honor the rate we had originally been given. It's shameful that a hotel of this calibre should behave in this manner. If there is an issue with the rate then the hotel should take it up with the travel site directly. Not their paying customers. What makes this more disgraceful is that it absolutely isn't a one off because there is at least one other reviewer of this hotel who had a problem when booking with a 3rd party travel site. In his case he had to pay more for a lesser room. Disgusting. Anything positive that I might otherwise have said about this hotel is negated by the shoddy service and dishonourable practice that I experienced. In addition, you might be interested in the following: * Air condition unit is noisy. * The bathroom wall is made up of glass so when you turn the light on during the night, the whole room is illuminated. * Wifi is not complimentary which is a real bugbear of mine in this day and age. * There was no room service or restaurant although that will have changed by now as they were about to open one. * The checkout staff were just rude and unhelpful. * And finally, it's the only "high end" hotel I've ever stayed in where they only provide shampoo & conditioner but no body lotion. There are plenty of other hotels in New York so go for one of those!

“Middle of Nowhere but perfectly OK” Like many accommodation choices in Houston, the Renaissance Greenway Plaza seems to be stuck out in the middle of nowhere, surrounded by roads, freeways etc. and little else! This is definitely a vehicel-oriented town, (and I've stayed in quite a few areas of the city...finding a sidewalk/pavement on which to walk is a hard task!) To say it is located in a 'shopping centre' is something of a mistruth..yes, there are a few shops/eating options across the road, but choice is very limited and the road in question is a busy, multipl-lane freeway which would necessitate transport to cross! I wonder quite why this place is where it is...I suppose there are quite a few offices etc. nearby but usually I find Renaissance hotels are more centrally-located, (I get the feeling it was built on the premise of other great things following on, much of which never materialised!) It's not a visually stunning place, darkened glass and slender and little else. Yes, it is a little tired, (especially in the public areas, e.g. lobby, lounge bar etc.), and could do with some TLC. The outdoor pool is reasonably-sized and a welcome addition when it gets hot and steamy down in Houston, but it's right beside yet another road so not exactly a haven of tranquility! My room, on the 8th floor, overlooked offices and more offices, (but you don't come to this area for a view!) It is in the accommodations where this place hits the mark. The room was spacious and well-kept, clean and neat and featured many pleasant little touches. As always, I'd have liked a mini-fridge as standard, (I believe you can call and request one, but my time here was short so didn't think it was worth the bother!), as it's nice to be able to have some cool drinks on hand without heading out to the ice machine! But apart from that, the separate walk-in closet with 'tall boy' was roomy, and the vanity/basin unit, (separate from the shower/bath and WC), again had plenty of space. There was a small vanity table, with adequate lighting, for you to be able to use as a hair/make-up 'station' without any danger of your products getting wet, (it's away from the sink), which is handy. All tiled floor is separared from the rest of the carpeted room, which had a lovely comfy king-sized bed, (pillows of dubious quality though - I had to use all three to get any kind of support, so if anyone else had been sharing the bed I'd have had to call for some more!) There were two armchairs and an adequate work desk with plenty of power sockets. I managed to access a free wireless network, but of course this could be down to chance so cannot comment on the reliability etc. of the hotel's 'wired for business' package, (standard to the Marriott chain at US$9.95 plus tax, noon to noon). Huge floor-to-ceiling windows let in a lot of light, which was welcome as you can often feel a little 'hemmed in' in places like these! I cannot comment on any food/beverage services as I didn't partake of either, but I did find the complementary shuttle van to be useful, (if not a necessity - with no car of your own, it's a lifeline to get anywhere!), and reliable. All in, a good option if your priority is a good nights' sleep in a comfortable room, (and even better if it happens to be close by something, or someone, you've made the trip to see!)

“Put up family here for a weekend visit with great results” I live in Washington, DC and was looking for a reasonably-priced, centrally-located hotel to put up my sister and her husband for a weekend visit focused on Lincoln and Ford's Theatre. My brother-in-law also happens to be a banker, so the fact that this hotel is in a retro-fitted former bank building fit the bill. They and I could not have been happier with the choice. First off, the location could not be better, just a block's walk from Ford's Theatre and across 9th Street from the Smithsonian's National Portrait Gallery and Museum of American Art in the historic Pension Building--my favorite Smithsonian museum. Other sites, like the Spy Museum, the Verizon Center sports arena and the Shakespeare Theatre's two houses, are immediately nearby, as are two metro stations--Gallery Place and Metro Center. There is also an abundance of quality Penn-Quarter restaurants in the vicinity. The hotel has retained the high-ceiling/marble column grandeur of its former status as a prestige bank building. The rooms are small but cozy, and my picky family members reported that the bed was extremely comfortable. Most of all, the staff was among the friendliest and most helpful we have encountered in any hotel. (For a hotel in this price range that appeals to tourists, friendliness is sometimes in short supply.) My guests had a top-floor room facing the back, which meant that there was not much of a view, but they avoided the noise of both 9th and F Streets, which can be very loud, especially on weekends. We had one meal at the popular Gordon Biersch restaurant on the ground floor, and we found the food to be mediocre, despite the bustling crowds. Valet parking is available at the F Street entrance, which is great whether or not you plan to use your car in the city. We were happy to leave the car for the weekend and depend solely on walking or public transportation and taxis.

“Rooms are OK - Food Service is very Marginal” This is a perfect representation of many W's - A tired old building that was revamped, made darker to hide the flaws and presented as tres-chic. While I have no particular issues with the rooms at this W. My biggest issue is with the restaurant - IPO. The menu is just wierd - not that I am a steak and potatoes person but Eggs Benedict with Pork Belly? Come on. I was rinsing my mouth out all day to get the greasy taste out. This week, I had the fish sandwich from Room service (good but not avail in the restaurant), a burger from room service (again good but not available in the restaurant), then tried to have dinner and couldn't find anything that appeared palatable (pork belly hanger steak, etc. - It is like they are telling Chicago come look at us because you wont find what is on our menu anywhere else (gee wonder why - maybe it is the same reason the place is deserted). Then I ordered shrimp tempura in the bar - what appeared was not tempura but more what you would expect from a cheap chinese place - shrimp so heavily battered that you cannot taste the shrimp over the bread and grease. I have no eartly idea what the dipping sauce was but it may have been worse than the shrimp - took one bite ate the seaweed salad (1 bite of it was what came with the shrimp) and left the rest uneaten. The fascinating thing was that when I complained they told me they were very good at preparing stuff off the menu.... hmmm My suggestion to the W - Shut down IPO fire all the people involved in that concept and try again. I will walk across the street to the JW Marriott and eat there if I stay at that W again. My advice to people staying there - go eat elsewhere.

“great hotel and location” this hotel is in a great location. rooms are very nice. Bathrooms are large and well appointed. Bay views in some rooms. Right next to stadium and across street from convention center. Staff is friendly and helpful. Mccormick and Schmicks is a great restraunt and breakfast there is good also. The Tin Fish next door has awesome food. would definately reccomend this hotel.

“Sonesta Replaces Crowne Plaza” Four night stay for business at the Sonesta, which is the old Crowne Plaza. Location, location, location is the star here - in the heart of Center City, near all major businesses and a quick walk to most tourist attractions. Pool has nice lounge chairs and is popular in the summer. Hotel also has small workout facility and laundry room which are nice touches. Elephant & Castle restaurant/bar in lobby has stout drinks but so-so food. Bathrooms are very small - you need to be fully inside before you can close the door - with sink outside the bathroom. Beds are comfortable, hopeful that Sonesta will spruce up the rooms in due course. Would stay here again given the good value and excellent location

“Whatever” Just another generic business hotel, nothing very special. In-room wireless Internet costs a bundle (Hilton's own Hampton Inns give it away for free). Room service prices are criminal - $26 for bacon and eggs, plus tray fee, room service fee, tax, and tip - works out to about $40/person for a Grand Slam without the pancakes. Lots of diners within 2 blocks do the same thing for $10+tip. Furnishings a bit worn out but not really bad. Bathroom access is tricky because it has a double door but one half is hinged to shut immediately so that it doesn't interfere with the room door. Which leaves a slit always open. The bathroom was best entered if I turned sideways. Half-asleep and in the dark, that was tricky. My room was over O'Farrell St so had a great view of the big parking structure across the street. Which has a loud horn that blares every time a car exits. Good for pedestrians, noisy for hotel guests. If you're in SF for business, probably not a bad choice, especially if it's the venue for your conference. Location is good, in the middle of everything. If you are traveling for pleasure, this is not a good option.

“Great hotel in DC!” Stayed in this hotel for 3 nights with 3 other people, we were in Washington for sightseeing and we had a great time. The room was very comfortable and spacious, we had quite a few bags with us but there was plenty of room for everything. The hotel location is great, we were able to catch the Circulator bus almost in front of the hotel and it would take us to some of the biggest attractions in Washington. Although the price isn't the cheapest, the service is great and definitely worth it. We had high speed internet in the room, cable channels (some in HD) and a delicious breakfast. I would definetely recommend this hotel and if I ever return to Washington this will be my first choice!

“Not all that impressed” Spent one night here in December. Its a hotel with character. I like that typically. The hotel itself was fine... but the whole experience was lacking. The room was small. Typical city hotel. Room only slightly bigger than the king size bed. Nice desk, love the Courtyard task chair. TV is mounted to the wall, off-center from the bed. Like previous posters, yes, this is weird. Internet is wired, and is sloooooooow. Noise is typical for a city. You can hear sirens, cabs honking, etc. I'd imagine if I was on an upper floor, it'd be better. I was on 6, which I believe is their lowest floor for guest rooms. You could hear music coming from one of the clubs located in the hotel proper. Roxy maybe? The area is nice. Its the theater district. Close walk to either the Orange line, or the Green line subway (the T). Don't drive in Boston. Its nuts. Parking here is $36 for valet. The valet was useless...only one person on duty at a time. Wait to retrieve you car is 15+ minutes. Plan accordingly. Price was decent for the city... anything less that $200 in downtown boston is decent, IMHO. I guess you get what you pay for.

“Always Very Consistent” This was my 4th or 5th stay here and it is always very consistent. Clean rooms, no nonsense airport hotel. You simply can't beat the price, and the handy airport shuttle, free (hot!) breakfast, and free internet make it a tremendous value. If you're looking for fancy, look elsewhere. If you're looking for value, this is your place.

“The perfect Chicago hotel experience” My wife and I had the pleasure of spending a week at the Hotel Burnham. This is a small boutique hotel created from the 1895 Reliance Building. Probably our finest hotel experience. Situated in the middle of the Loop, so you have quick access to the elevated trains and attractions like Grant Park and the Sears Tower. Excellent staff with attentive service. The building itself is magnificent, having been the benefit of a meticulous top to bottom restoration. All of the original details are there, with recreations made for those that were missing. The intricate iron grillwork of the original elevators is there, as well as the original iron staircases on each floor. Each room is actually fitted into what were office spaces in the original building. The Atwood Café off the lobby is first class and deserving of its own review. The hotel provides a complimentary wine tasting each day from 5 to 6 PM. Tiny bathroom, but we were so blown away by the rest of the hotel that we can overlook this!

“Almost Perfect.” I traveled to Memphis on a one night business trip. I've stayed at this property in the past and had a great experience. First, location is amazing. One block from Bealle St and in the heart of downtown only 15 minutes from the airport. You really can't pick a better location. The TGI Fridays stays open late and is connect to the hotel lobby for an easy bite. I was checked in very smoothly and the staff is super friendly all the time. Once I got to my room, which was a very roomy, clean and comfortable but a little dark. So, I settled in to do some work. The only outlet by the desk did not work. I had cell phones, iPad and laptop plugged in on the floor under the bed and around the room. The bed is super comfortable (I snoozed about 5 times) and the towels are clean, fluffy, and fresh. In the morning I brewed my coffee in room (they don't provide water in room so you either use tap or bring a bottle) and used the half/half provided only to have it curdle in my coffee - pretty gross. The valet and bellman are awesome. They really strive to get you what you want. Overall a good stay with subtle nuisances.

“Good Overall Stay” Location great for all venues. Comfortable bed and clean room as well as quiet at a reasonable rate. It's a historic old world place with great service. Not our first time here and I would definately return.

“This Time Just An Average Stay” I have stayed at this property before and always raved about it. This stay was different. Not bad but nothing that stood out either. We arrived at 11pm and stood at the front desk for almost 10 minutes before anyone came to wait on us. Not a sole at the front desk for that time period. No welcome or thank you at all. And at check out no thank you or how was your stay. While I would stay here again I do wish the service level had been up to speed as in the past.

“Good Conversion, great view, friendly staff” Location - one block off of the Little Italy main street, Easy access to the 5, airport, shopping, and the bay. Room (407) - Newly redone, clean, clean common areas too. Comfortable bed, lots of lighting, very small balcony (no room for a chair). Tons of hot water! View - beautiful view of the bay from the 5th floor common area. Bring a towel if you're sitting up there in the morning - cushions are wet with dew. No pool, no hot tub, parking $14 a day. We did enjoy our stay at the hotel, but would not stay again because of the lack of pools. It was cute, staff was very friendly, felt safe in the area, and plenty to do within walking distance. We did not try The Glass door, but heard it is good food. For awesome (quick and cheap) mexican try El Indio on Washington - Tacos are to die for and they have a special parking area.

“Nice Hotel, Great Location” Stayed for one quick night on business. Short taxi ride from the airport (~20 min.). The location is great - right near a lot of restaurants and attractions like the aquarium, Quincy Market, etc. You can definitely walk to a lot of sightseeing and dining. My room was very large, 927. It was on the end, and it felt like it was an apartment. The room was booked through my company, but I payed the same rate as everyone else that I was traveling with. Try asking for an end room - it is worth it! I did not try the restaurant because of a private party.

“Hard Rock Suite was a great birthday treat!” To celebrate my birthday, me and my girlfriends headed down to San Diego to enjoy some partying at the Gaslamp. I booked the Queen Hard Rock Suite on travelocity for a great price of $185 (the room usually retails for $319 or so on Saturday nights!) We bypassed the insane $35 valet charge at the hotel and parked for $17 across the street (literally about 20 second from the hotel and half the price!) The desk agent was super sweet and helpful and we recieved great customer service from everyone at the hotel-- it's so different than the Hard Rock in vegas, where everyone that works there thinks they're better than you. The San Diego staff was great! Our Queen Suite was smaller than I expected but still nice. (However, if I had paid over $300 for it I would have been sick! Totally worth $185, totally NOT worth $300-$350!) The good: Super comfy beds, unique shower that was separate from the toliet, a GREAT view from our huge balcony and a nice lounge area that we used to get ready to go out in. Despite it being smaller than expected, it was still big enough for 4 girls to stay in without being cramped. We loved MaryJane's inside the hotel...what's better at 3 am than veggie chili fries?! Yum! The bad: The suite had no fridge....seriously? You get a fridge in your room at the Days Inn! For the price of the suite, they could have stuck a mini fridge somewhere in there! There's really no sink area or bathroom area to speak of in this suite so there's nowhere to get ready. We used the cocktail bar. Also, it's a little noisy because you're literally over the main street of Downtown, but who comes to Hard Rock to sleep?! Overall, great hotel with a great atmosphere and staff! I'd be back if I could find a discounted rate again!
“Very good hotel, excellent value for money” Its a nice hotel, comfortable and clean. I did enjoy my stay there.

“Great Staff, Nice Hotel” Stayed at the Doubletree Metropolitan over July 4th weekend after getting a good rate on the Hilton website (including breakfast) and because of the mid-century modern architecture. The staff was very friendly on check-in, even though we were a couple of hours early they found us an available room. I was also able to get a late check-out without any hassle. Unfortunately, the bathroom in the first room we were given was in very bad shape, so after going back down to the front desk we were moved into a different room. The desk clerk had to speak to a/the manager, who I saw in the front desk area almost every time I went downstairs. He was very gracious, apologized for the bathroom, and even followed up with a phone call once we were in the new room. The rooms are decent size, although I'm not a big fan of the sink being exposed and separate from the shower/toilet. It was obvious that parts of the hotel had been refurbished and other parts had not, as the room and sink area looked new, but the shower area didn't. The location is great for getting the subway (6), and a fairly easy walk to Times Square. But if you want to be right in the "action", this probably isn't the best place to stay. The area is very quiet, although there is a 24 hour CVS a couple of blocks down, not much else is available at night. The lobby is compact, and even though it's a large hotel I rarely saw anyone having to wait at reception. Every single staff member I encountered was extremely nice, and the fresh cookies were an added bonus. The complimentary breakfast buffet was great, and the wait staff there was very cordial, with no one ever put out that we had coupons for the breakfast. You are charged a minimal gratuity to your room if you book with the complimentary breakfast. Would I stay here again? If I got a good rate I definitely would. The hotel is clean, fairly convenient, and the staff is great.

“Great Location and Friendly Staff” I've stayed in San Francisco before, and I was happy to find that the Drake was different from the other hotels. The doormen were extremely friendly (even though they looked uncomfortable in their Beefeater attire), the desk staff was more than accommodating, and concierge was top notch. I even need to applaud the hotel manager that came to my aid when he saw that I was waiting for the concierge, he was quick knowledgeable and knew what he was talking about (Bravo). The location was ideal - right next to the trolley (entertaining to see, but noisy at night), and the only issues I had with the hotels were the very small bathroom and the old windows. The windows were very old and drafty - San Fran in December isn't always the warmest, so the drafts were noticeable and the windows didn't muffle any of the street noise (and I was on the 14th floor). The staff, price, and location all made up for these minor inconveniences. I will stay at the Drake again when I return to San Francisco.

“I am now a Hyatt Place Fan, see you later Marriott Courtyard” As a regional manager, i am many times in a location with few better quality lodging choices, and over the years prefer the Marriott Courtyards, but these new Hyatt places are great, the rooms are better, nice lounge/couch, great TV, free Internet and Breakfast, and they have free computers/printers too. I have been staying 3 times year at the Marriott next door, but for almost $80 less, the Hyatt is fine, I have stayed there 4 times in 4 months, with 2 more in end of Feb.
