Though my company will pay whichever I choose, why? The Marriott nice, no gripes, just the Hyatt a better value, especially the Breakfast and Internet and huge plasma.

“Not a bad choice” Got this through Priceline 140$ a night during a weekday. Wouldn't have paid more. Price on site was 350$. Hotel is your avg 3 star hotel. Stayed on the 3rd floor and it smelled like smoke. Try to avoid rooms near elevators as they have the ice machine as well and it can get noisy between people wanting to get ice and those going to the elevators. The room itself was acceptable. Location is good and not far from subway station and other attractions. Staff was courteous and check-in was a breeze. Did not eat at the hotel so cannot comment.

“Nice for an airport hotel” The hotel was nice but the rooms and bathrooms are tiny. There wasn’t a mini bar but the hotel offered to bring a mini fridge at no charge. Our room (471) over looked the pool area. The only drawback is that voices echo in the pool area and it can get a bit loud in the room but thankfully the pool was only used one afternoon while we were there. No free WiFi in the room. In this day and age, that should be free in every room. You could get free WiFi in the lobby. The staff was nice and helpful. They printed off directions for us anytime we asked. They helped me get connected to the free WiFi in the lobby and called me when I left my coat in the restaurant. We ate lunch and breakfast at the hotel restaurant. The lunch was great. The breakfast was not. Overall, if I had to stay at the Seattle Airport again I would stay at the Marriott.

“Great hotel in great location.” The Sofitel was a beautiful hotel. The room was comfortable and roomy with a very nice flat-screen tv and amble lighting. The bathroom was particularly nice, with a separate tub and shower (however, the handmitts instead of washcloths were a little annoying (although a nice little touch of exoticness)). Service was outstanding from the welcome champagne (a nice touch) (well, actually bon jour champagne, the occasion French greeting was also a nice little exotic touch) to the helpful concierge and the efficient doorman (very effective at getting cabs). The free internet connections on three computers in the lobby available for use by guests (with attached printer) was very helpful for doing quick research on places to eat and for printing out directions. Speaking of which, the room service food was delicious (although expensive). The same for the hotel restaurant's breakfast--good but costly. On the other hand, the cost of the rooms was surprisingly reasonable for such a good hotel in such a great location. The location was ideal--near all the action but not in the middle of Times Square so relatively quiet; a lot was within walking distance--particularly convenient to the Theater district. This hotel has earned its high rating.

“Comfy, clean hotel near airport” My teenage daughter and I snagged a room at this near-the-airport hotel for $55 on a Priceline bid ($50 bid rejected; going rate on Priceline was about $150) for one night before a 6 a.m. flight heading back to RI. We ended up not getting to the hotel until about 11:30 p.m. and were surprised to find several people waiting in line to check in even thought there were 2 clerks. Once we got to the head of the line, we were efficiently checked in. Even though it was a Priceline room, they asked whether I preferred a king or two beds; usually hotels don't ask so this was nice. They were patiently providing lots of advice to guests who were concerned about the morning airport shuttle and to some who were looking for food since the restaurant was closed by then (they knew just what pizza places would still deliver.) Parking was convenient in the lot, and we weren't charged to park (someone on this site mentioned they were, can't imagine). The lobby feels a little odd; it's sort of a big room with a couple of desks and a little service kiosk with newspapers and aspirin, etc., and it leads into another large room with some sort of huge rock structure behind which are the elevators. Maybe it just seemed odd at midnight. The room was very comfy, nice bed linens, super comfy beds, very clean bathrooms, no complaints. AND THE INTERNET WAS FREE IN THE ROOM. Lately, with 3 star hotels and above, that hasn't been the case especially if you book through Priceline bids or through Hotwire. Kudos to them. They woke us up at 4 a.m. as requested, and checkout was super-speedy. Though not particularly luxurious, it seems like a fine place to spend a night when coming to or going from the airport.

“Zwei Zimmer mit Kakerlaken und unhöflöiches Personal Don`t Stay Here” Super 8 Downtown8 Ursprünglich wollten wir zu einem anderen Motel fahren als wir uns dort die Zimmer anguckten waren wir damit nicht so einverstanden.Räume zu klein,Kopfkissen platt wie eine Flunder und das Fenster zur lauten Straße hinaus.So entschlossen wir uns zu dem Super 8 zurück zu fahren wo wir vor bei gefahren sind.Zimmer gab es war ja noch mittag.Raucher oder Nichtraucher?Raucher!Das erste Zimmer lehnten wir ab weil es in der letzten Ecke lag also ohne Tageslicht!Ein zweites hatte er auch noch,womit wir einverstanden waren.Die übliche spartanische Einrichtung ziemlich abgewohnt dafür aber ohne Kühlschrank und bei dem Preis?Naja wir wollten nun zum Riverwalk und dachten uns für eine Nacht wird es wohl schief gehen.Ich wollte mir noch ein paar Kekse essen bevor wir los wollten und da sah ich sie,das grauen auf mehreren Beinen Kakerlaken,igitt sie lief unters Bett.Ich dachte mir nur du gehst weg und sie teilen deine Kekse mit dir,das geht gar nicht.Bin zur Rezeption gelaufen und dem Angestellten „Harry“das erzählt.Es gab ein Problem mit der Aussprache ich erzählte ihm was von „cockroaches „sprach es wohl falsch aus und er wollte zuerst noch Geld haben weil ich ja Tiere mit hatte.Das wurde geklärt und er gab uns widerwillig ein anderes Zimmer diesmal Nichtraucher.Nach dem ganzen Koffer schleppen gingen wir zum Alamo(ein muss)dem Govereursgebäude(na ja)und dem Riverwalk,der war wiederum wunderschön.Ein wirklich tolles Ambiente das ich nur jedem empfehlen kann.Spät abends kamen wir gut gelaunt zurück und bemerkten das man uns ein Pizzaprospekt unter der Tür durchgeschoben hat.Dachte mir noch,was für Zwischenräume und da waren sie wieder“cockroaches”Nun war es Nacht und wir konnten wenig unternehmen und freuten uns das es bald wieder Tag wird.Aufgewacht,geduscht und zum frühstückstraum wo auch ein für Hotelbewohner zugänglicher PC stand.Meine Frau brauchte noch etwas und der Frühstücksraum mit satten 3 kleinen 4 Personen Tischen gefüllt und die Gäste standen Schlange davor. Frühstückzeit von 6:00 Uhr bis 9:00 Uhr im Hotel für Urlauber?Echt ungewöhnlich,früh.Meine Frau kam es war 8:50 und es waren Tische frei.Wir setzten uns hin,tranken hastig einen Kaffee(oder was es auch war).Dann kam der Angestellte “Harry”,frühstück wäre vorbei es ist nach 9:00 Uhr,ja genau 9:10 Uhr.Da er ausgebucht war wären wohl ca. 120 Leute hier und das mit drei Tischen in dieser Zeit? Da fragte er noch was wir noch wollten,wir sagten Toast und fing damit an aufzuräumen.Wir standen auf und gingen für so was was dort angeboten wird braucht man nicht sitzen zu bleiben.Das Schild über dem Buffet”Super Breakfast”ergab absolut keinen sinn.Ich verlangte die Rechnung,die sowieso für so ein Zimmer um 50% zu teuer war und bemerkte eine Versicherung über einen Safe für 4 Dollar,darüber wurde niemals gesprochen eraber zeigte mir ein Schild was verdeckt hinter anderen Stand.Das ist für mich glatter Betrugund werde die Managerin über ihren durchaus unhöflichen Angestellten informieren und rate nur jedem.”””Don`t stay here”””

“Great Stay!” Excellent location, service, amenities, pool in the lobby open 24 hrs. is very sexy cool..the rooms are spacious, with large bathrooms. There is no restaurant but they offer many menus of local restaurants that deliver to your room (after they pass hotel security, of course) I stayed here 3 nights and enjoyed EVERY MINUTE OF IT! Don't even think about it, JUST BOOK THAT ROOM..

“A+” Where do I start...I absolutely adore this place! I had a suite (flat) and when I tell you that the room (1406) rocked, it so did! I am still raving about this place. When I entered my room, I was greeted by soft Jazz playing all throughout the suite and the lights were dim. A fresh bucket of ice sat on the dining room table, which was lit by a fashionable lamp. Ahhhh, I felt like I was in a movie. By lifting the shade slightly, from the living room to the bathroom, I had a view of downtown San Diego, with huge windows. I had a balcony that could fit 8-10 people comfortably. Two robes, one (large) in the closet(Leopard) and one laying on the bed (Zebra). Three closets, one in the living area, two (small) in the bedroom area, of which one had an elite Keurig coffee machine with contents. Two flat screen t.v.'s, one in the bedroom and one in the living room area. Two bathrooms, one when you initially walk into the suite and the other in the actual bathroom area. The bedroom bathroom, which was huge, had a separate tub and rainforest shower. And I did use both. I liked the hardwood floors throughout the suit and also the retractable glass sliding doors. Each day, my room was cleaned and one night, I was on my balcony and I heard some noise in the room so I went in to look around and I was scared at first, but then I saw a woman who was only putting a fresh bag of ice in the room. How nice?!?! I didn't eat in the restaurant, but I did use the commentary happy hour in the lounge area. It gets pretty crowded too, which is nice for socializing. Be careful is you aren't used to the modern way of doing things, this hotel has unisex bathrooms in the dining area upstairs... I have to give it up to the Palomar. I didn't want to leave. The staff greets you with open arms and you can tell that they love their jobs. They made me feel comfortable beyond means, which is important when you leave your home.

“Plush and comfortable in a very convenient location.” A very nice hotel. Our room had a great view looking west. Located just a short drive to Beverly Hills, UCLA, West Hollywood, etc. The area around the hotel looks like a financial/business district, a lot of very large office buildings. The adjacent outdoor shopping mall has up-market stores and restaurants, movie theater. If you need a nice place to stay within driving distance of Hollywood/Beverly Hills attractions, this is a great choice. I got a terrific room rate by bidding on Priceline, but parking is expensive. They were filming an episode of Monk in the lobby of the hotel when we were there... a real L.A. experience!

“Nice Getaway” My wife and I wanted to have a romantic getaway. We stayed at the Hotel Teatro. It is close to the arts center and within walking distance to Larimer Square, LoDo and the 16th Street Mall. We have stayed at several luxury hotels and resorts that cost twice as much as the Teatro, but the Teatro staff was equal or better than any we have stayed with. Free internet was great to have as well as a wide variety of channels on the t.v. The room was small as we knew from the website, but it had a great feel to it. Strategically placed mirrors help expand the room and make for some romance too. The bed was quite comfortable (my wife said it was like sleeping in a cloud). The fitness room has two treadmills, a stair climber, recumbant bike, and dumbells up to 35 lbs. The equipment is top quality. If I get picky I would say the place is starting to show some age- some mildew in the tile grout of the shower, scratches and a crack in the basin countertop, stains on the linens and bed cover. The rain shower head adjustment did not function properly and resulted in dribbles of water rather than "rain", but the position that did work was fine. There was a scale in the bathroom, but it did not function (probably dead battery). I did not care if there was a scale, but why have one if it is not going to function properly. However, these were minor and overall we enjoyed our two nights quite well.
“コスパ最高” 最近ポートオーそりティ近辺にホテルが多く立ってきた。ここも隣はマリオット系、その隣はシェラトン系で、裏手にも同じようにホテルがある。サービス劣悪なNYのイメージがあったが、ここは違う。ネットは無料で、料金も手ごろ、火、水、木の夜はレセプションと称して、アルコール(ワイン赤白、生ビール2種類など)を含めたもてなしを無料で受けられる。大助かりだ。

“Super Bayblick” Unser Zimmer in der 25. Etage bot einen unbeschreiblichen Ausblick über die gesamte Bucht. Ich war vor vielen Jahren schon mal in diesem Hotel, als es noch ein Holiday Inn war und kann gar nicht begreifen, warum das Hotel nicht viel besser bewertet wird. Die Lage ist perfekt. Chinatown, North Beach das Financial District und auch der Union Square liegen in nächster Nähe. Das Zimmer ist sehr schön typisch Hilton und auch sehr groß. Das Bett riesig. Sehr schön war, dass wir ein Upgrade in den Executive Floor bekamen. Dort ist auch die Executive Lounge, die abends kleine Snacks und ein Continental Frühstücks-Büfett bietet, das keine Wünsche übrig lässt. Uns hat das Hotel sehr gefallen. Leider wird der Bayview durch ein neues hohes Gebäude für viele Zimmer eingeschränkt sein. Parken kann man günstig (28 $) in der öffentlichen Garage gegenüber.

“Wonderful Hotel...Great location!!!” Stayed here for a long weekend over Mother's Day. This was one of the best places we have stayed in the city. Extremely clean. Staff was more than helpful and friendly. Room was great size for myself, husband and 2 children. Had no problems with noise. We were on the 35th floor so I am sure that helps. Had room service one evening and it was fast and tasty. The location is what really put this hotel over the top. We were able to walk to everything we wanted to do. If we needed to take a cab there were always plenty out front. This will be our hotel of choice from now on.

“Thanks for All Your Help!” Major disaster averted thanks to Westin Seattle's super staff! I raced to Seattle to give a talk after tending to a family major hospital operation. Technical materials and resources for my talk were, unfortunately, sent to my twin grandsons' birthday party while I received the boys' presents and party favors--not a good day, but funny! Concierge Richard sent a car to pick me up. Ms. Helms along with arranged a room where I could work to collect materials and meet with colleagues. Concierge Judy told me where to find replacement materials. The bell staff are great! They hauled boxes, taped them, Sorid, only recently hired, actually moved furniture to arrange the suite to meet my needs and the bellman on duty overnight taped my boxes and handled my Fed Ex shipment, packed my cab to the airport this morning and mailed the presents home.. Vardo at the business center reprinted my handouts and immediately rushed to help me drag my suitcase out to the curb when he saw me struggling down the hall. Thank you all! This one day whirlwind trip worked out because of you! It is what makes me such a loyal SPG fan! The staff even reminded me to remember to eat "to keep up my strength." I am literally old enough to be their parents! Thanks guys!!!

“Would not choose this hotel again” We were fairly disappointed with this hotel during our one night stay over the weekend...starting with check in. The front desk attendant was not friendly AT ALL and was borderline rude. I've heard and read before that people feel they may be treated differently when the hotel sees that you've booked on priceline or a similar site, and while there's of course no way of proving it, I tend to feel the same way now. We got 3 rooms on Priceline for $50 each...our first time booking rooms on Priceline. Sounded like a great deal, but now would have rather paid a little more and stayed at another hotel in the area that we know we like. We were not allowed to check in when we arrived around 1pm that afternoon. We were told that check in was 3p and someone would call us around "3 or 3:30" when the rooms were ready. When we said that "oh we thought check in was at 3?" The attnedant said "it is, but maybe 3:30." He just had a really snippy attitude about it. He also seemed very put off that we requested one room with double beds and the other 2 with King beds. I didn't think that was too confusing or an odd request! We stored our bags there and headed out for a while. We never received the call that our rooms were ready, but decided to head back to check around 3:15 and they were ready. Check in #2 took just as long as check in #1...which was ridiculous because we had already done everything the first time...we should have just been given our keys and been done with it. We were not at all impressed with the room...it was actually kind of small. The bed was comfortable, TV was old, I spotted some dead bug on the nightstand, and the room had a really strange odor...almost like a combo of mold and the faintest hint of sewage...who knows. When it was time for us to get ready for the evening out that was planned, I discovered that the only outlet in the vanity/sink area did not work. Looked like the wall around it had been opened up and repaired before as well...annoying that it didn't work and the repair job looked really sloppy. The only other outlet I could find available and near a mirror was at the desk...the plug was in the base of the lamp. Couldn't get much power out of that so it was like blow drying my hair on low...took twice as long! We tried the breakfast buffet the next morning. It wasn't bad, I've definitely had better. The biscuits and pancakes were very hard and the gravy that was for the biscuits was NOT gravy...some strange sauce with a yellow tint that had a chicken flavor. Other selections on the buffet were decent, however the buffet was way over priced. $41 for two...and that didn't include the tip. Way too much for what was offered. I don't think this hotel deserved the "4 star" rating that it has...we will not stay here again.

“Great Stay!” My wife and I decided to stay in Washington one night on our way home to Ohio from the Outer Banks in North Carolina. Booking on Priceline we didnt know what to expect using the name your own price and we were very pleased. The room was clean and very comfortable and in a great location. The only negative was the $25 bucks per night for valet parking. Thanks DoubleTree Washingtion DC for a nice end to our vacation!

“What a lovely gem of a hotel” I'd heard so many great things about the Elan Hotel, I was almost afraid to believe them. But happily, it is a wonderful boutique hotel with just the best service I've seen anywhere. Simple but nice breakfast in the mornings, stylish rooms, comfortable work stations. More important, I felt well-looked-after and could count on the staff if I needed anything. No restaurant, but twice when I arrived back in my room from a long, late day of work, I just ordered from Jerry's, an excellent diner that delivers.

“Slips in Service” Friendly staff and attractive rooms. Service is lacking- waited 3 hours and bags were still not delivered, booked a package and items were not delivered. I also had to request the champagne that was to be delivered upon arrival. No turn down service. Too many slip-ups at this price. If you expect service, try another hotel there are PLENTY in SF.

“Very nice Hilton at Easton” The hotel is very nice, looks very new and the rooms feel clean and new. The location is also very good at the Easton shopping area, within walking distance to many restaurants and stores. The only negative is that the internet service is terrible! It's expensive (about $10) and terribly slow. (The internet service at the Columbus airport (free wireless) was actually faster!) If internet access is not a priority for you, this is definitely a good hotel if you are in the area.

“Renovated rooms = Outstanding” I have stayed here twice in the past 2 months and yes, they are undergoing an enormous renovation. Because of my status, I got a renovated room both times -- they are gorgeous -- high tech, great big flat screen, comfy beds, lots and lots of electrical outlets, clean carpets, etc. Internet worked perfectly, so I could get my work done. I love the executive lounge -- Mr. Smiley takes care of us well, and even at 10 minutes to closing the appetizers, he called down to have them replenished -- outstanding!!! The views from the lounge are nice -- planes taking off and landing. Gentle readers: yes it is an AIRPORT property -- meaning there will be airplanes nearby! I felt my room was very quiet. I dined in the restrauant for first time and was delighted. An attentive staff -- you have two choices -- either the Italian side or the American side. I chose Italian and had a lovely meal from appetizer, beverage, all the way to dessert (love the shot glass sized desert portions -- cuts down on the guilt -- "just perfect") Check in was a breeze, so was check out. I like to drop my rental off -- the valets are accomodating to watch it while I check in and run up to drop off my luggage. I then come back down and drive the rental car to nearby Rental agency. It's a nice 10-15 minute walk back, and I don't have a car to juggle in the am. Their shuttle service to LAX is good -- super busy, long line -- so give yourself extra time. They get you there quickly and with a smile. To sum: I love this property!

“Great business-class hotel in the SF Valley” I had a business trip in the San Fernando Valley and found there were not that many choices in the immediate area - particularly among the Marriott brands. This is not prime tourst LA, so unless you have business or friends/family nearby, the location may not be that great. For the SF Valley, it's great and I had an easy (non-freeway) commute to my client. Every staff member I encountered (front desk, restaurant/bar, concierge) was friendly and accomodating. The room was fine and to typical Marriott standards. Another review mentioned the lack of power outlets, but mine had four outlets as part of the TV patch panel near the desk. The TV actually offered hi-def channels. Internet (wired and wireless) maintained pretty good speed. I had a couple of meals in the restaurant and found them to be very good and reasonably priced (by hotel standards, at least). There are plenty of other dining options nearby with some of the mid-upper class chains like P.F. Chang's and Roy's. There is a shopping center and movie theater directly across the street.

“Top Spot In Downtown San Diego” The newly restored US Grant is simply the nicest hotel in downtown San Diego for business people in my age range (40-60). The lobby has a grest understated elegance. The rooms are smallish, but very well appointed and the staff is amazing, there is seemingly nothing they will not do to make your stay more comfortable. The young Hollywood crowd is probably heading to the Keating or the Ivy (goodbye W as hippest hotel in San Diego), the old crowd is still going to the Westgate, but the Grant will be my business hotel of choice in SD.

“Great location but levaes a lot to be desired” I recently completed a two night stay at this property in a corner suite (X04 units) and was slightly disappointed. I came in excited to try this new property and the unique pied-à-terre styling after many great stays at other Hyatt properties including the two nearby Andaz locations and Park Hyatt locations worldwide. Upon arrival, the front desk area is incredibly small without any real space to wait or desk to speak of. Check-in was fairly efficient although no assistance with my luggage was offered. The room was fairly well laid out with a separate living and sleeping area. I found the room to be adequately sound proofed despite the fact that the bedroom is all glass. Bathroom was disappointing especially the weak shower pressure. Living area had a unique kitchenette with microwave, honor bar, Nespresso machine, Fisher & Paykel drawer dishwasher and a display of eight overpriced mini bottles of cheap wine. The second floor contains the Lexicon Lounge which is the heart of the hotel. There is an espresso machine and water available around the clock and that's about it. Mini muffins and petite pastries are available in the early morning in limited quantities, hard pretzels and assorted cookies in the afternoon and cheese in the evening. Not quite like the Andaz with complimentary wine, juices and other refreshments available around the clock. The fitness center is adequate and contains treadmills, recumbent bikes, and ellipticals (all Life Fitness with integrated LCD TVs) and a combination unit in the adjacent strength room. Overall I was disappointed with this hotel and will stay elsewhere in New York. It's worth noting this property is a category 4 in Gold Passport (unlike other NYC properties) so it may be a good value for points redemption or annual Hyatt card free night award.

“Cheap room and they let you know it” My wife and I travel to DC fairly often and it is an expensive city to visit. Nice hotels often go for $350 a night on the low end so when I saw rooms for $250 at the Sofitel, I grabbed it. The hotel is centrally located with lots to do in the area, close to the museums as well as the metro. The lobby is rather functional with no feeling that you are in a high end place. When we checked in, I got a feeling we were tagged as cheapskates. The person at the desk asked whether I had a preference for a floor. I said I would like an upper floor so they gave us a room on the second floor. The doors leading to the room were just painted so the hallway stank of paint. The room was directly above the entrance which concerned me about noise but it was reasonably quiet. The room was small considering I paid for the "upgrade". I don't want to know what the really cheap room looked like. The minibar was unusual. It was missing. There was one robe in the room even though we reserved the room for two. The staff were almost nasty, at best disinterested. The room was clean, reasonably quiet and the bathroom perfectly fine in an ordinary way. If I paid $700 plus for this room (standard rate but with a view of the Whitehouse), I would NOT be happy. Try somewhere else.

“Great Stay” After our recent 2 night stay at the Marriott Marquis, it seemend to us that the elevator problem has been fixed. This is our 3rd stay at this property in the last couple of years and we experienced absolutely no long delays waiting for the elevators. We had a nice room on the 32nd floor overlooking Times Square and it was well appointed and quiet. The bathroom was a good size and the 2 double beds were quite comfortable. All the staff that we encountered was very pleasant and helpful. Breakfast at the Encore Rest was good and efficient. Location is right in the middle of everything with all the activity of the masses outside the hotel. We beat the $50 daily parking fee by going online to [--] and using a parking lot a couple of blocks away. Left our car there for a couple of days since we didn't need it in the city and saved more than 1/2 of what the hotel charges. We booked the online AAA rate and felt that we got a good deal. No complaints about the Marquis.

“Plush, modern hotel” The decor in this hotel is definitely really modern and neat. Top of the line. The rooms are small, but what rooms aren't in NYC. We fit 4 people for a weekend in one room and were just fine. Sound proofing here must be amazing because we came in to a very loud concert in the lobby but couldn't hear a thing just a few floors up. Lobby bar also has fabulous food. Definitely a good location for shows on Bway. I was also impressed with their service. They accidentally overcharged me for a room upgrade, but when I called about this they quickly rectified the problem.

“I would not recommend this hotel” While I understand NYC hotel rooms need to be small, I do believe hotels can provide thoughtful ways to make small areas more user-friendly to travelers. I don't think this hotel does that at all. The room was pretty small with just enough room on either side of the bed to fit nightstands. A dresser, a good sized closet with mirrors. The room itself wasn't terrible, but the bathroom took the (small) cake. It had a pedestal sink, a stock shower/bath combo, and a toilet. The pedestal sink had no counterspace around it to put things out, there was no storage underneath, virtually nowhere to put your toiletries. There was a very narrow shelf that went across over the sink and toilet (I kept waiting for my curling iron or blowdryer to fall into the toilet). We stayed here two nights and it was two too many. If they put up a few shelves or areas to store stuff, it would be a little different. However, there were many other negatives as well. The lobby was huge but unbelievably crowded every time we walked through it. This hotel obviously has a ton of rooms - and yet all the elevators are only accessible through a narrow corridor off the lobby, which makes everyone pack into a mosh pit mess trying to get to or out of the elevators. The bar area was VERY expensive for drinks - I expect a higher price but $20 for a glass of (cheap) Chardonnay was just ridiculous. The location was just ok. Overall, I've stayed in places where I don't feel like a number or a sardine - I'd recommend the Omni over this any day. Service is so much better with the boutique Omni chain that this giant corporate chain. By the way, New York was sweltering in July - to the point that meeting our family here to do some touristy things was just not pleasant. No one wanted to be outside during the day. I wouldn't plan a walking trip this time of year even if prices might be best at this time.

“Glorious - and good value” This is almost certainly the best deal currently available in SF. From what I can tell, the Omni opened in 2001/2 (a $100m conversion of a 1920's office block) into SF's worst recession in decades. The result - a brand new luxury hotel with no guests. They appear to have slashed rates to get occupancy - $140 seems the norm at weekends (I paid $179 B&B). The rooms are beautiful and (obviously) brand new - the standard shoe-box shape but big and probably the loveliest you will ever have been in. Staff are also exceptionally friendly and keen to help. If you enrol in their frequent guest scheme (no charge, form on website) you get free coffee brought to your room each day and a 2nd free newspaper. Whilst officially in the financial district, its on the border with Chinatown and close to Union Square. Very strongly recommended.

“Clean, friendly and good value, but lacking in atmosphere” Recently spent the first night of a holiday to the US/Canda here. We received an upgrade to a suite in the Casa Del Mar for $11 (an option when booking online). The suite was large, quiet and spotlessly clean, with a very comfortable bed, much appreciated after 39 hours in transit. My partner found it very "dark", and felt it needed more lighting. The property is located in a scenic area on the marina, however it is not close to the downtown region and it was necessary to drive to see the main attractions of San Diego. We felt that the property lacked atmosphere and was a bit sterile, like something was missing. Perhaps this is due to the location of being part of a large chain? We had breakfast in the restaurant the morning after our stay, which was tasty, but not cheap. Staff were all very friendly and helpful.

“Good value” We stay in SF at least five times a year and found this to be a good value and location. Rooms are small but feature a microwave and refrigerator and there's a small store across the street. Bath was nice and big and clean. Some noise from the busy street but if we'd asked for a back room that wouldn't have been an issue (and it didn't keep us up -- just noticed it during rush hours). Desk staff were professional and polite. Free parking was a blessing -- and we took advantage of the great transit connections within a block or two. Good steak house across the street called Bobo's, also.

“Enjoyable stay” First stay in a Sofitel, and based on this experience, it will not be our last! The room was a good size as was the bathroom. Love the L'Occitane amenities. The bed ranks as one of the best I've slept in at a hotel. Both the Front Desk and Concierge service was very efficient, friendly and helpful. Outdoor pool looked nice, but we did not have time to use it. Food at SimonLA was good with a nice variety. Restaurant service was good with the exception of one afternoon (we were having drinks on the patio, and were forgotten after being served). Bar was lively with creative drink options. Hotel location was good, very central to getting around. There is a Hertz car rental two blocks away which we used. Would stay here again, and recommend it to others.

“Alloggiare a NY senza svuotare il portafoglio” New York è notoriamente una città tanto straordinaria, quanto cara negli alloggi. Avendo previsto tre giorni nella Big Apple durante il coast to coast che è stato il nostro viaggio di nozze, cercavamo un hotel econimico ma gradevole in quanto luna di miele, e centralissimo per poter sfruttare al meglio i pochi giorni a disposizione. L'Herald ha soddisfatto tutte le nostre esigenze: ottima posizione (ad un isolato dall'Empire State Building), pulitissimo e molto spazioso (altra rarità a Manhattan!!), ci ha permesso di visitare tutta la città a piedi o con la vicina metro spendendo una cifra tutto sommato contenuta. Con 15 minuti a piedi eravamo in Times Square! Abbiamo dovuto chiudere un occhio sulle finestre che davano su un muro, ma considerando che in hotel ci andavamo solo per dormire, nel complesso è stato molto meglio per il nostro sonno il buio cortile interno, ad una rumorosa strada della Città che non dorme mai ;)

“affordable no frills” I spent the two previous night at the dump that is the Congress Plaza, over on Michigan. What a relief to come here. Yes, it's smaller etc, but it makes no pretence that it is anything other than what it is: affordable, clean, friendly, and central. If you aren't spending a lot of time in your room, it's perfect. But the bed was comfy, the shower etc working just fine, and so on. I got this for $50 on Priceline, and would pay the full price (about $95) if I had to. Compared to what you can get elsewhere in downtown Chicago, this place beats all the others hands down. Everyone knows Red Roof: you get what you pay for. And that's fine with me. But here I got even more. Bonus!

“Friendly staff, aging hotel” I stayed at this Marriott for a conference, and it does a substantial conference and wedding business. This is my third time at the hotel. The Good: The staff is exceptionally friendly, warm and just pleasant to be around. They really try to make you feel welcome. The location is close to some of Houston's best shopping and restaurants. The food in the hotel is quite good and the bar is lively. The not so perfect: I'm Marriott Silver and hotel failed to give me any of my standard requests related to location, pillows or towels, despite the fact that they weren't fully booked. The hotel is aging -- it looks a bit dated and the bathroom is not only small but mine was stained and had a cracked tub. Many rooms -- including mine -- look out on to a brick wall. This is also not a pedestrian friendly neighborhood (not the hotel's fault -- that's just Houston) and the parking garage is difficult to negotiate. I appreciate how warm and friendly the staff was -- that's excellent management. But I wish they'd spend a little to update the rooms (particularly the bathrooms) and I wish they'd pay attention to my Marriott preferences.

“Very nice hotel but thin walls” Wonderful location. Marriott rewards member and received inner harbor view without an upcharge. No issues with bedbugs. Staff very nice and friendly. Convention area no problems-typical convention hotel with associated fees. My issue is the walls are thin and seems like you hear every door opening and closing down the hall. Wear ear plugs and you should be fine.

“Good downtown location” I found this hotel quite comfortable for a couple of nights, and got a good last minute deal so happy with the value for money I got. It is a great location for Union Square and the shops and, as I wasn't driving, I found the public transport & taxi options (and walking) more than sufficient to get around. I didn't have any issues with cleanliness of the room as other reviewers did, and I found the staff friendly and welcoming.

“Pretty Standard Hyatt Property” This Hyatt is located right downtown, on Wacker near Michigan Ave and the famous Miracle Mile. It's a great location if you are going to be spending lots of time in the central core of Chicago. This is a huge hotel, so be prepared for big crowds and lots of commotion. I believe the largest in the City of Chicago and it caters to groups and conferences. My check-in was uneventful. The clerk was very friendly and helpful, getting me off to my room with no wait. At check out I tried to beat the line and use the kiosks. They weren't working, but a very nice chap at the counter cleared my account quickly. The room is tastefully decorated in a standard business class hotel contemproary style. It looks like any recently renovated Hyatt, Sheraton, Hilton or Marriott. There was nothing remarkable about the rooms. Comfortable size. Air Conditioning worked very well. Water pressure and temperature were good. Room was clean. Bed was quite comfortable. No noticeable noise transmission from the hall or nearby rooms Amenities are pretty pricey.....$52 a night for parking, $13 for marginal internet service, and mini bar prices through the roof. I was there 4 nights, however a morning newspaper only appears at my door on two mornings. Their feature restaurant, Stetson Chop House was closed for renovation. Bistro 151 sits in the center of the main atrium and can be very noisey. Food is average at best and it's pricey. The price of the breakfast is crazy. There's a Starbucks stand in the main atrium that is open 24 hours a day.

“Very good value” I booked this hotel because it was close to the interstate. My husband and I were on our way home from Florida, and Charlotte is about halfway between Jacksonville and Columbus, Ohio. The room is designed for business travelers with a wall between the bedroom and the "miscellaneous" room, which had a sink, microwave, small fridge, sofa, and a table that could double as a desk. The TV swivels so it can be seen from either the bed or the sofa. The bedroom is small but has a large dressing area. The bed was comfortable. The miscellaneous room is rather dark. Both my husband and I thought breakfast was above average in quality and variety. PS: no bedbugs or bugs of any kind!

“Top spot” A decent hotel in a perfect location. Staff are apathetic, but helpful when required. The rooms are big, with all mod cons apart from a safe. It's not luxury, but it's clean and functional.

“Dirty, rundown property” having stayed here 3 x past 2 years, figured its time to comment. Rooms are not clean. Worn out carpet, smelly and security is lax , although I never had anything taken. Twice though have had perverts roaming around the premises ratting keys and bumping up against door looking for who knows what..Was forced into smoking room due to oversold...and honestly it was unreal how bad the smoke was and how nasty the bathroom was. The internet works ok and the front desk people nice only reason i gave it 2 stars!

“Amazing Staff and Amenities” My husband and I were staying overnight for my birthday. Although our room was not immediately ready (we arrived at around 2:30p hopeful), we waited nearby at the Intrepid to pass the time. All of the staff greeted us and stored our luggage with ease. The front desk was offering cool towels while we waited due to the heat. They also have water all day and iced tea and lemonade during certain hours. When we got to our room, it was fairly large and had a great view of the city- very quite. The animal print robes were fun and the toiletries in the bathroom smelled amazing. The bathroom also had a large counter space and had plenty of lighting (not enough hooks to hang wet towels as the only one I could find was next to the tub and blocked the light switch- but this is me searching for something to pick on). Wine was served from 5-6p in the lobby area and they offered a glass of red or white. Since we had the birthday note on the reservation, my husband and I found a bottle of champagne and a plate of amazing cookies in our room after we came back from the wine, and was such an nice touch and suprise. The rooftop bar was open to the public but as a guest, had immediate access. Breakfast in Press was great and found the prices to be pretty resonable for the city. Location isn't in the middle of the city action but there was always a cab waiting outside the hotel. We found the hotel to be such a nice suprise and perfect for what we were looking for.

“Great Hotel: Clean, spacious and professional” I stayed at the Affinia Manhattan for four nights in June 2009. First of all, the hotel is only steps from Penn Station, which made it very convenient to get to from JFK airport via the Long Island Railroad. Its location is close enough to Times Square that you could walk, or take the subway (which is only one block from the hotel). My room was the largest NYC hotel room I've ever stayed in. The room had three closets! Strangely, it had a tiny bathroom. The size of the bathroom is the only reason I give the hotel 4 stars instead of 5. The shower stall had barely enough room to turn around in! I wish they had enlarged the bathroom by taking away one of the closets. However, the room was very clean and comfortable. I had a corner room on the 23rd floor, so I had windows on two sides. I could open the windows a bit and let some fresh air in, which was very nice. The staff was extremely friendly and professional. I would definitely recommend the Affinia.

“Great Location and Views, but......” My husband and I checked into the Hotel Vitale for a getaway weekend to San Francisco. We had heard that the hotel was terrific and certainly well located...right across from the Ferry Building at the Embarcadero. As we pulled up to the valet, I got the impression that this was another one of these "chic, hip hotels" when I saw lots of 20 and 30 somethings in head to toe black. Our room was exactly as promised....lovely view, nice king bed and modern bathroom with Fresh amenities. As I began to look a little closer, however, I noticed a fairly heavily stained carpet, and a rather austere look to the room. I sat in a comfy chair near the window while my husband was connecting our laptop. While reading, I realized that I was hearing lots of conversation and chatter. I looked out the window and there was the 20 something crowd just a few floors down enjoying a very busy happy hour. The noise was disturbing, so we called downstairs to request a room on a higher floor. We were told that there were no other rooms similar to the one we had booked, but the front desk was suggesting that we take a room without a view and that we would be credited for the difference in price. We decided at that point that we did not want to stay at the hotel anyway....it just seemed like it might not fit our style. We're a well traveled couple in our early 50's and we've stayed at lots of different style hotels...but this was not exactly the kind of warm, inviting hotel that we usually stay at. True, the views are lovely and the location superb.....but at these prices, I want a quiet, clean room that is really catering to my needs. Next time, I'll opt for the non-trendy hotel. We were lucky to be reimbursed for our deposit and moved elsewhere.

“Good accomodations - Outstanding Location” We stayed for 2 nights over the Labor Day weekend. The hotel was packed due to the holiday, the Boston College/Wake Forest game and also parents escorting their kids to area colleges. The front desk managed promptly and courteously. The rooms and decor are nothing special and the Lobby has a nice looking bar. However, we stopped in for a drink during the late afternoon and were ignored by the bartender (hate that) so we left and had a better experience at the Marriott across the street. We were able to get a decent rate, so we cannot complain too much. Overall, a good place to stay if you want to be within walking distance to great shopping areas, Duck tours, bars, restaurants, etc.

“Functional with a boutique touch for a large chain” Helpful/receptive staff, pleasant room, in a relatively quiet part of Manhattan while it's walking distance to any midtown destination, and Grand Central. Will return.

“Classic Older Hotel - Pros and Cons” Very large hotel, with an elegant lobby. It's an older hotel, that has retained its classic style. Rooms are very big with comfortable beds, small (empty) refrig so you can fill with your refreshments. Really liked the window in the bathroom . Noisy hotel. We could hear the bed / floor creaking above us, could hear the conversations in the room next door, could hear noise from the hallway. The room had a slightly musty odor - not sure if it's the room itself or from the bathroom. Good location, near Connecticut Ave. Metro stop very close. Some casual restaurants directly across from the hotel. About a 10 minute walk to Adams Morgan. About 1 mile to Dupont Circle. We had a reasonable rate for a DC hotel for our one night stay. Didn't use the pool, health club or any hotel restaurants so I can't comment. I would stay again if rates were better there than other DC hotels.

“We loved this hotel---the rooms, location, and experience were great.” We stayed at the Residence Inn Chicago Downtown/River North for 3 nights. I was very happy with the size, layout, and quietness of our room. We were on the 19th floor and had a beautiful city view out our window. The location was perfect as shopping on Magnificient Mile was a few blocks away and restaurants were plentiful within walking distance. Public transportation was a short walk across the river from the hotel and we easily made it to the museums without much extra walking required. The employees were all helpful and provided tips on dining available and directions. My only negative comment would be on the cost of parking $44 per day, but this is Chicago.

“Cool Convention Hotel.” We normally do not like to stay at large hotels, especially if they are attached to a convention center as this one is. We chose the Grand Hyatt because it is a brand new hotel and we wanted to experience the new hotel in town. Overall this decision worked out well for us and the size of the hotel did not turn out to affect our stay. The hotel does sit on the river walk, but other than the main restaurant which opens onto the river walk, the hotel’s focus is away from the walk. This area of the river walk is nice and quiet and it is a beautiful less then ten minute stroll to center of the walk. The main areas of the hotel are modern and colorful and this can make you feel like you are in a smaller boutique style hotel with a cool vibe. Of course that is only the case if the hotel is not full. Our room was good sized with a modern décor that although nice, felt a little sterile. The room had a lounge chair with a table that hung over the chair that reminded us of a hospital bed, but was comfortable. The color palate was yellow with dark wood furniture and there was some nice art work on the walls. The attractive bathroom had a marble countertop and good lighting. Even number rooms face north and get limited direct sunlight which may be a good thing during the summer. Our room did not have a safe but we are not sure if that is by design or that the safes did not arrive in time for the opening. There was also no mini bar and there did not seem to be a place for one. A highlight of this hotel was the gym. It is large and bright with lots of windows and enough equipment to get a full workout. The pool is also very nice, long with a raised infinity edge. The pool deck is a tight area with a fair amount of lounge chairs but probably not enough on a busy day. The stark look of the area will improve over time as the limited landscaping fills in. One issue to note is that in this end of town, there seems to be a constant flow of trains off in the distance. Although not loud, it may get to you after a while. On the first morning of our stay, the lobby was already a buzz with a group that was meeting at the convention center. The second morning during our stay the elevator stopped on every floor as members of a large group all converged at the same time for breakfast at a ballroom in the hotel. After about three floors there was no more room. Other then these encounters, we did not feel like the hotel had been taken over by a group. The Grand Hyatt is a cool, brand new hotel - but for leisure travelers, we would only recommend staying here if the rate was lower then some of the other nice hotels in San Antonio that are smaller and offer a more intimate environment.

“Average Hampton Inn” I've stayed in a lot of Hampton Inn's and this one must be one of their older hotels. Not bad just not quite as nice as many of their others. Friendly staff. No happy hour like I've experienced in some of the others. Very close to Hobby.
“excellent” Great value- free breakfast, clean and spacious rooms...couldn't ask for anything better!

“You will not feel at the White House, but you will experience 4S Service Quality” This is absolutely not the New York or Istanbul 4S. Its kind of old, brick and mortar building, right in Georgetown. There is no lounge to have a drink, just a steakhouse with an inside bar. BTW, the steaks there are lightly boiled in butter first, then grilled, good but not worth the cholesterol damage! But the seared Foie Gras is remarkable and worth the unhealthy chemicals! The fitness and spa are surprisingly large and well equipped, at the end of a long way to get there. The pool is a lap pool, nothing fancy, rather small and inside only. The rooms are somewhat contemporary, but somewhat traditional as well. As a location is is just outside of the downtown buzz, but very close also. There are nice cafés and shopping around the hotel, and the service is 4S quality. We visited other properties while we were there, like the W, the Jefferson's and a couple others, and that confirmed our first choice on the 4S. We did not see the Park Hyatt inside but it seemed well located and it may be a good option to try as well. So overall a good choice if you value the 4S exceptional service. But do not expect the typical expansive lobby and lounge, contemporary design that other 4S offer.

“Very nice area! great Penthouse Suite!!” Great Penthouse Suite No 2102!! amazing terrace and views! great Mini-bar offer and best interior design. Bathrooms are great. beautiful art books and pictures in room. In room Internet should be a must for this Hotel category.

“Great to stay again” We just stayed here again for 3 nights. It is a great property, perfect location, and very good service. Previously we have stayed in the Mediterranean King Corner Suite with RIver View. LOVE THIS SUITE. When we booked this time, none of these were available so we got a King River View Room. View was great, room was great, but noise from hall was awful - early every morning we began hearing the doors slam in the hall - byt the 3rd morning we realized it was the maid'scloset which was just outside of our room - I will never stay in one of these rooms again b/c of that and will only choose this hotel if we can get the Med Corner Suite - difference is there is a living room off the hall and then the bedroom isolated from the hall noise. WOrse case is I will let the hotel know about this problem and definitely always request a room away from the maid's closet.

“Clean rooms, great service - good location” Stayed at the Kitano in May while on business travel in NYC. It is a small property just a few blocks from Grand Central station in a quieter part of Manhattan - yet convenient to just about everything.... I think this hotel is a fantastic option in NYC for the price - particularly given the rates of most 4 and 5 star properties that have small/old rooms that are in desperate need of some TLC. The front desk staff were impeccable. Rooms were clean and comfortable. Bathrooms had a heated towel bar which was a nice touch - although bathrooms could use with more lighting in the shower area. Room also had slippers and a bathrobe which was greatly appreciated. I did not eat at the hotel but there was a jazz bar that seemed packed and had live nightly bands/entertainment for a nominal cover charge. I have already booked this hotel for my next stay in NYC in June.

“My favorite choice in area for business travel” Hilton Gardens overall tend to be nice, moderately priced choices for business, and the Del Mar property has some extra touches. Like most in the chain, rooms are spacious, nicely furnished for the business traveller, and feature a comfortable signature bed. The bistro style restaurant is more interesting than the basic "American Grill" found at most others in the chain. And there are many good restaurants within a five minute drive..ask at the desk. The hotel even has a spa..a somewhat curious additon for this type of hotel. Slightly off the freeway (get directions your first time coming here), but is easy once you know the slightly confusing freeway layout here. I've stayed here many times, and this is my top choice for business travel in the La Jolla/Del Mar area. Would be nice place for vacationing couples as well.

“Very convenient to NASA JSC and didn't tarnish the Hilton name.” It had been awhile since I stayed here and was pleasantly surprised to see that the lobby area had been remodeled. Overall, this is a good hotel; nothing fancy, rooms aren't all that big, but great customer service, and very convenient to JSC.

“Great facility. Great staff. Great location.” I stayed one night for a business conference held on site. The facility is exactly what you would expect from Marriott. The staff was very friendly and welcoming. The food served during the conference was average; I've had better at other Marriotts. My room had a wide-screen HDTV and digital cable. When I first turned the TV on it had sound but no picture, but the front desk helped with a simple fix and everything was fine. Plus the clerk gave me 500 extra reward points!! The hotel is located within walking distance of the Keystone Crossing Fashion Mall and several restaurants. The Castleton mall is a short drive down the road. Very nice and safe area. The hotel is located right off of the 465 loop on Indy's north end. Highly recommended.
“Great hotel, very hospitable!” Great location. Great room with diamond membership - 42nd floor. room was very clean. view of the hudson river and chrysler building. front desk was very hospitable.

“An excellent value” There are many pricier hotels nearby. The River Hotel may not charge as much. But the room was clean and comfortable. The location very convenient. And the service could not have been better. I needed a handicapped room and had forgotten to reserve one in advance. They cleaned a room for me very quickly and then brought some needed ice.

“lovely affordable hotel on the Upper West Side” I've stayed all over NYC over the past decade and had yet to find a hotel I loved on the Upper West Side. Now I have. The Lucerne had it all--quiet rooms, comfortable beds, free internet, and very affordable prices. We will definitely go back. It's hard to find quiet, comfortable, elegant and, for NYC, cheap in the city. The Lucerne is a gem.

“Fabulous Starwood hotel experience!” My recent stay at the Sheraton Seattle more than met all of my expectations for a Sheraton property. The staff was friendly, the service and food in the Daily Grill was spot on, my room was very comfortable and clean. The location is very convenient for my business travel. I look forward to staying at this hotel for future business travel to Seattle.

“Good, not great.” This is the largest JW Marriott in the world. Knowing this, I was expecting to be wowed by the hotel. I wasn't. The hotel and complex is large and aesthetically pleasing, but the rooms are seriously lacking. They're just normal hotel rooms. Even as a Marriott Platinum member, we couldn't get a suite or even a corner room. Heck, we couldn't even get a room on one of the top 3 floors. I was rather disappointed to see this. I ran into a friend in the exec lounge who is a gold member and had checked in an hour prior to me and he had been upgraded. Maybe the hotel should hold some of their nicer rooms for their platinum guests instead of giving them away to the first check-ins of the day. Honestly, the room was no different than any standard Marriott room I've stayed in. The bathroom tried to be swanky, but it didn't pull it off. The exec lounge was very nicely set-up, but the evening hors d'oeuvres didn't do anything for me. I tried a couple of their obviously heated from frozen appetizers and decided to go downstairs to their sports bar to get a decent snack. Maybe that's the point behind it, they serve subpar snacks in the lounge so that people go buy stuff from their other areas. The evening snacks were so bad that we skipped the morning breakfast. As a huge breakfast fan, it's very rare that I'll pass up on a free breakfast, but I just wasn't in the mood to be disappointed again. We called for a late check-out and were offered noon. That's barely a late check-out at all. They reluctantly offered 12:30 as a thank you for being platinum members. Again, it just rubbed me the wrong way. The service was hit or miss. The valet team was exceptional. I don't think the $32 charge for overnight valet is overpriced... it's actually $3 less than the Conrad. But, the Conrad beats this hotel in just about every area. Their rooms are spectacular. Their lounge is phenomenal, and their service is impeccable. As a HHonors gold member, I'm frequently upgraded at the Conrad but couldn't receive anything other than a standard room as a platinum member at the JW. Oh well, back to the Conrad for future visits.

“Good Stay” This is a lovely, quiet, clean, well-appointed hotel on a side street right off of M Street in Georgetown. The room (a junior suite) was large with two sofas, a microwave, sink, refrigerator and bar in the living area. The bedroom was separated by a set of French doors. Very well-equipped: safe holds a laptop and there was a small bottle of wine, two bottles of fizzy water and a package of dried fruits and nuts on the house. The staff was very friendly. I got a good weekend rate of 129.00 which included a continental breakfast that looked good but I didn't try. I did not drive, so I can't report on the parking situation but Georgetown is a tough place to park a car.

“Not a single good thing to say” I am used to great quality from Westins, but this particular Westin property brings shame to the entire brand. Awful!! Check-in and check-out was slow and rude. The room was not clean, lots of hair leftover from previous guest. Shower had no water pressure. There was so much dust that you could see it on every surface and throughout the air space. Elevators were supposedly being renovated, but they were shaky and nerve-racking. The lobby seemed okay, until I looked at the lights and there were shadows of dead moths in the light covers (really gross.) Don't even think about staying here unless you really have no other choices. I'm still cranky from staying at this site.

“The absolute BEST hotel experience I've ever had!!!” My husband and I went for our 10 yr wedding Anniversary and stay two nights this past weekend. When we entered our room the Concierge- Ms. Elaine had a beautiful set up of wine and chocolate covered strawberries with a card to us waiting for us. Along with that there was slow music playing and rose petals all over including in the bathtub and even on the bed shaped in a heart. It was a beautiful and romantic set up and much to our surprise. I had let her know that it was our Anniversary but never expected her to do all that she did for us. Aside from her amazing hospitality the rest of the staff was very nice and helpful as well. We loved the pool and the breakfast buffet at Bolo's was very yummy too! They even allowed us to check out late at 1pm. I will definately be staying at this hotel whenever we visit San Antonio in the future and can't wait till our next visit! Thank you again to the Concierge and Staff of the Omni San Antonio for making our Anniversary/Celebration trip better than anything we could've imagined!

“Clean, Comfortable and Exceptional Staff!” We just spent two nights at this property and had a wonderful experience. Neah at front desk is AWESOME! She is professional, helpful & friendly -- we really enjoyed talking with her. Check-in was quick & easy. Our room was super clean & bed was very comfortable -- the jacuzzi tub was a nice surprise and such a treat. Great flat screen tv -- plus the air conditioner worked great on the hot San Antonio days (Our only room issue was with the lock -- each time we came back to our room we had to have the key reset.) Jimmy and his staff in the breakfast area are so much fun -- we enjoyed waking up each day to their sunny smiles & exceptional service plus breakfast was super fast and really good. Parking was free and we had no trouble finding a parking spot. (The pool is indoor and on the small side -- but very clean) Exercise room was nice & clean. Property outside was well maintained & welcoming. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and will return on our next trip to San Antonio!

“Neither bad nor brilliant.” We selected this hotel after an internet search. There were mixed comments on TripAdvisor but the negatives (parking costs, restaurant promotion and distance from Central Park etc) did not concern us. Other comments were positive. We confirmed our booking as suggested by the manager responding to a tripadvisor comment. Arrived at 3.10 pm as advised to find the room was not ready. After a few minutes I mentioned the previous email conversation with the manager and a room was available with upgrade. The hotel is older and the external appearance is a bit off-putting. Inside is better but the need for refurbishment is evident. The room was spacious and everything worked OK. The A/C unit was noisy but we put up with it in case a relocation meant the original room which we were certain would be much smaller. The bed was comfortable and the room roomy enough to enjoy a meal in the room at the table. There is a good food market close under Queensboro bridge that sells prepared salads etc. The bathroom was very small. Stay here again? Probably not. The crowning point was when I asked for help to get a taxi to go to Penn Station at 6.00 am. Response was basically my problem. The doorman was more enterprising and earned his tip.

“Great hotel, superb experience however it can be a tad noisy” Beautiful hotel, great views, stellar service. Beware the "New York experience" having a club in the hotel. When all you want to do is lay your head down on the bed, having to push through the throngs of club-goers can be a bit off-putting as the front entry to of the hotel is always a "scene". The scene outside can be noisy, but don't be afraid to complain. The staff is great as is the service. This is not a budget hotel -- be prepared.

“Convenient For Business - Not For Leisure” This is your best choice of hotel if you are traveling on business. Should you be traveling as a tourist, or for pleasure note parking is $26 daily (self park) and $38 valet, no exceptions. They will also charge you for all of the amenities to include an extra packet of coffee?! (one pot for your entire stay), amenities etc.. again, if you're going on business I would recommend this hotel, otherwise based from experience you can find a better or similar quality hotel near the airport without the hassle of parking at the airport and paying the extra cost.

“Did not met expectations” I was really looking forward to my trip to Philly, I hadn't been in 15 or 20 years. The last time I was in town, I also stayed at the Marriott downtown. Sad to say--nothing's changed. It looks and feels just like it did all those many years ago. Tired, outdated, drab, and very businessman looking. I don't think anyone has informed this hotel that there are now many women who travel for business also. And we have needs. So, here is my version of my stay at this hotel. First off, the front desk was rude, unfriendly and not accommodating-- at all. I had asked per reservation for a kingsized bed, called twice to confirm, but upon check in was told that all there were was 2 double beds. Unless of course we'd like a handicapped room. We took that room, which meant that everything was lowered for wheelchair access. Low closet bar, low shower head, which would not stay locked into place and kept sliding down as you tried to shower. The water temp kept going from hot to cold and the water pressure was nonexistent. The only amenities offered in the bathroom were shampoo, conditioner, soap and lotion--no q-tips, cotton balls, nor a make-up mirror in sight. Bare bones. Even the towels felt doled out--2 of everything. The room itself was nice sized, the bed was pretty good, as were the sheets. The TV was a large flatscreen. The coffee maker though? It's a 1 cup system, so the hotel gives you 1 cup of regular coffee and 1 cup of decaf, I guess you get to fight over the 1 cup of real coffee if there are 2 people staying in your room. Again--very tight with room amenities! The coffee wasn't very good anyway, but they threw in 2 teabags! There isn't really too much left to say, other than there was a small safe in the room along with an ironing board and very cheap iron, which would not get very hot. No mini bar or mini frig. We did have access to the upper level, which meant free breakfast. I will say the the food and coffee (Illy) was great as were the staff. The tiny little saucers to put your food on though was down right laughable. I guess they didn't want you to take too much--again, very stingy! Would I stay here again? No way, there are too many other hotels in the city center to try. I'm sure they are friendlier, have many more amenities, and hopefully are updated for the female traveler. The location of this hotel is excellent. The Reading Market is fun and also there is a cute little restaurant about a block away called The Corner--it was awesome!

“Great hotel for the business traveler. You can count on Westins!” I love this hotel for business. Rooms are spacious, clean and comfy. Love the fluffy beds. Room service is always quick. Good place to spread out my stuff (laptop, folders, etc.) I can always count on a good night at this clean, consistent, friendly yet sophisticated hotel. Bar is good, food is good, prices are very reasonable for Chicago. I have stayed there for a few years now and try not to stay anywhere else in Chicago. Great location too. For a large hotel in a rather unfriendly city, feels like home and I have honestly never experienced anything less at this particular hotel.

“Convenient Location - Good hotel” Stayed 04/29/05 - 04/30/05. Exactly what you would expect from a Holiday Inn Express: Clean Rooms; High Speed Internet; Good cable selection; Good front desk staff; Breakfast;

“Magic Castle, Magic Staff, Magic Service.” We returned to LA this August for a Neil Diamond concert at The Greek Theater and we spent 4 nights at the Magic Castle Hotel. Right from the outset all of the staff made us feel most welcome and this continued for the entire stay. From the excellent complimentary breakfast around the pool to the complimentary late night snacks this place is excellent. Add to that the fact that all of the staff really seem to want you to stay there and care about what they do and it makes this the only place in LA that we will stay in the future. The location is great being just 5 minutes walk literally from the Hollywood walk of fame etc but not right in the busy part of town, so you get the best of both worlds. Also a special mention for Darren, the General Manager who is certainly a man of his word and stays in touch with the guests on a daily basis.Thanks.

“Better Then I Expected” I stayed at this property for only a couple of days and it was actually very nice. I was in room 202. The rooms are huge! The rooms were quiet and clean. The breakfast was very nice. Not as good as Embassy Suites (where I tend to stay), but good none the less. The evening desk clerk was so friendly and polite. The hotel is located not far from "resturant row", which offers a pretty decent selection of mid-priced places to eat. Its also not very far from the down town area. There is a Whataburger adjacent to it, if you just want a burger.

“On the way to perfect” Assuming they don't raise their prices this will be our new home away from home in NYC. The good: location, location, location. Great walking neighborhood on a quiet street in the upper west side. This place is quasi hotel and quasi residence as you feel apart of the neighborhood staying here. Rooms are comfortable, spacious by NYC standards and a great value for this part of New York. The Hotel is still a work in slow progress. Business center access was spotty. No Bar, No Restaurant. But we are told both are in progress, though it matters not. The wonderful diner across the street and Mecca of a marketplace on the other corner make this place an easy comfortable stay. Anything you need is available at a bevy of 24 hour markets. Staff are ok. Need to polish up a bit but nice overall. My advice, catch it while you can. This place is on the way up.

“Just Creepy” Room was small and not very clean. Breakfast was continental at best with lots of carbs and bad coffee. Front desk person was so hard to understand I still am not sure what he was asking so I gave him my license, credit card, and Gold Crown card. Neighborhood on the west side of I-35 is downright scary. Don't stay here.

“It is a good hotel but could be better” We stayed here prior to leaving on an Alaskan cruise along with my 2 brothers and their children. I selected this hotel because of its location and also because of the suite concept. On arrival we had problems with the check-in. We were told we had booked 4 rooms even though the confirmation said we booked three. After several minutes the woman at the check in agreed to cancel the "4th" resevatioin without penalty. Only one room was available when we arrived at 1PM; my brothers couldn't get into their rooms until about 5PM. There was additional confusion at the front desk when they tried to get their keys. It was resolved but still annoying. The rooms are very large and nicely decorated. However there are a number of maintenance issues: one lamp in the living room didn't work because the switch was broken; there is a fireplace in the living room but it was not operating. In the bedroom, one lamp wasn't plugged in because there was only one outlet and it was taken by a clock that could not be set to the right time. We did like the location and the fact that coffee was served 24 hours per day. The lobby is small but very attractive as was the room where complimentary breakfast was served. The kitchen had glasses, plates, etc along with a microwave, refrigerator and dish washer. This would be an excellent feature for a long stay! If they can figure out how to straighten out the reservation issues and better maintain the rooms we would definitely recommend this place. Right now I am not convinced that we would stay again.

“Excellent - highly recommend!” The staff was incredibly accomodating! They got us a room at the last minute and the concierge helped us find local places to eat and printed our boarding passes for us. The room was great and the beds were comfy. We never ate in the hotel (to save money) but walk down Mich. Ave and you will find excellent places. Great location. They have a free shuttle service to the Magnificent Mile. We couldn't have asked for a better stay. (Well...maybe if the elevators were a little bit more timely.)

“Bland and average property” Not a bad property with an OK location and easy access to public transportation via subway. The area around the hotel is quite nice too. I would not recommend this hotel to HHonors members though. When we checked-in we received no recognition, no upgrade, not even a welcome. I never bothered to ask if an upgrade was available but did ask to be moved to a higher floor (not sure why I was assigned a room on the 23rd floor when my profile says 'high floor' and with a room on the 50th floor being available?). The room was basic (no slippers or bathrobes). The restaurant and the bar (especially) misrepresent themselves to a great extent. All in all the hotel served its purpose (we needed a Hilton property in that area) but I would not volunteer to stay there again. Nothing especially horrible but not what I expect at a Hilton property.

“Liked It better when it was amerisuites!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!” I've stayed here before in 2005 and the rooms were more more comfortable. This time I walked in the hotel and I was very shocked at the horible colors they used to renovate this hotel with it is truly unberable. My room was not very comfortable and the tv was to big for the room. The rooms were clean both time but they ruined this hotel bad. The people that worked there were alright but when I was there before all the people were nice. I just did'nt like the new decor it's to alaborate . The rooms Aren't as bad. I wish they would change it back

“Spectacular, better than the New York Palace” This inn was wonderful, beautiful and spacious rooms and bathroom. Our room had a great view of the harbor, I really cannot say enough good things. The breakfast had a large selection of fresh fruit, bagels and cereal with coffee, tea and hot chocolate available 24 hours a day. Ok the negative was, in Fells Point there are really only pubs and ice cream shops you must walk (20--25 minutes) or water taxi to the inner harbor for restaurants. But then you can return to the Inn and escape.

“Will return!” Just stayed for four nights and have to say what a great hotel in its category!!!! Staff are wonderful! Always helpful and very pleasant! The manager had flowers waiting for us as per my request! Wife loved it! This hotel is very well run in every aspect and the beds are so so comfortable! Flat screen tvs are a very good size. Located near subway close to Madison park and the Flatiron building. In Madison park (2 minute walk) try Shake Shack for a great f(ast food) burger and fries! Ice cream milkshakes are also tops. Get the subway pass for $27 for 7 days if you are in town for more than two days and forget the taxis. This hotel is well located for the average tourist or even people on business since it is near enough to business district and the same distance to times square. Just a couple stops on the subway.

“Less Than Ideal” My first stay at a Club Quarters, and it was a bad experience. The set-up is screwy: you walk into the building and are confronted with an elevator and stairs. For whatever reason, there is no lobby on the first floor; you have to go up to the second. The elevator is nightmarishly slow, so I usually took the steep stairs. Good for the heart and all that, but I'd hate to be handicapped in any way and stand there waiting interminably for the elevator. The room was loud and the floorplan bizarre, and one could make the case that's just the nature of real estate in big, old Northeastern cities, but I've been in enough hotels to know that is not the case. I've stayed in two Club Quarters, this and the one in Boston (see my review of same) and found them both terribly unpleasant. Based on these two experiences, I do not recommend the chain and will scrupulously avoid it myself in future.

“Crowded, good location, average service” The rooms are tight, good location on 50th, no breakfast buffet, free wi-fi (at least for me) and a crowded hotel.The staff could not handle that many people. Overall, an OK 4-star, nothing more than that.

“Nice hotel but location not ideal” The hotel appears to be quite new, was clean and nicely furnished. The staff was very friendly and helpful with restaurant suggestions. The breakfast bar was well stocked with standard breakfast items plus two waffle irons for making fresh waffles. But the location is in an industrial area and about 1/2 mile from the closest restaurants in Market Square, and about a mile from the Riverwalk area. Not ideal for sightseeing on foot from the hotel.
“Best location in Good price” i like river view ,location, very clean hotel , very good price i miss swimming pool

“a great choice” My husband stayed just one night and we would definitely return. The rooms were clean and modern with nice bedding. Everything you would need is close by- shopping, restaurants, public transportation. The staff was super friendly and helpful. Good breakfast included.

“Great Hotel! The LOCATION is perfect” I loved this hotel! The location is perfect! One block off of Michigan Ave. I was here on a workshop/mini vacation. When we (myself, sister, sister's friend and my sister in law) checked in I asked to be upgraded to a jr. suite, which we were. We were also asked if we wanted a refrigerator delivered to our room, which we accepted, at no extra charge. Everyone from the bellman to the front receptionist to house cleaning were very nice and made you feel like a special guest. Excellent recommendation to a sushi restaurant right down the street! The warm cookies put out in the lobby was a nice touch after a long day of shopping and sight seeing! I would not hesitate to stay here again! Great Experience! Keep up the good work!

“Perfectly fine for the price” The rate here was almost half what I was seeing at most other properties in Dallas, so my expectations weren't too high. Even after arriving, I wasn't completely sure about it, just because the area is kind of blah. Not bad, really. Just blah. But check-in was easy as could be and they put me in a queen bed suite. The good thing about that was there was a sitting room of sorts that separated the bedroom from the hallway. If noise was an issue, I didn't notice it. Room also had a fridge, two televisions (one in the bedroom, one in the sitting room). The AC was kind of loud, but I personally like to have a slight bit of room noise. Everything in the room worked fine. Only two minor complaints- the fitness center is in big need of a remodel. They just need to replace everything in there. And the breakfast buffet could use some work. But for $80, there's not much else to quibble about. It was better than I expected.

“Needs some bed help.” My husband and I stayed here for two nights. Check in was fast and pleasant. The room was clean and decorated nice. It was the bed I had issue with. A feather bed was on top of the pillow-top mattress. Could have been great, but there was not a mattress pad in sight and the feathers from the featherbed poked us through the night. Sanitation - The mattress didn't have a waterproof pad on it either. Seems unsanitary to me and it is often required by health codes. Room service was prompt and the food was warm, fresh, and tasted very good. The price was very good at $159 night from the Hyatt website. Location was perfect, within walking distance to theatres, many restaurants, and Chinatown.
