“Fun decor; Great Location for Japantown or Fillmore St.” If you want to shop on Fillmore Street and go to Japantown or the Kabuki this is the place to stay. It is very inexpensive. The lobby has fun decor with 3 TVs running cartoons that are all different. The room itself has queen beds and lots of wood. It was very quiet. The only thing negative was the room wasn't ready after check in and the housekeeper sent me down to get another room.

“Great Time” Just got back from a one night stay at the Hilton Garden Inn and it was great. The location was only 3 VERY short blocks to the White House, and a mile from most attractions. The room was the same as pictured on the websites, there was no let down. The staff was great and caring espically the Valets. The parking was a little much though, $24 a day, they should of made it cheaper for hotel guests. It would of been a few dolllars (around $2) to park around the corner. We got a king size bed and it was very comfortable, they give you 3 pillows on the bed and 1 in the closet, so if you like to sleep on 2 pillows at a time bring extras. The three they give on the bed just goes straight across the bed. The pool was very tiny, it was about the length of the hotel room. The fitness room was even smaller, with about 6 machines in total. The bathroom was average size, never really felt cramped in it. The room rate (about $84/night) included breakfast in the morning which was pretty good. It was just a little breakfast buffet but it hit the spot. You had to get the passes from the front desk when you check in but they didn't give it to me when I first checked-in, but went down and got them later. We stayed on the 11th floor looking out at 14th St, and you could still hear the cars honking the horns and police sirens going off. It woke me up on two ocassions, but I am a light sleeper because it did not wake my girlfriend up. Everything was great about the hotel and for the price was a complete steal. I would defintly stay here again if I am ever in D.C. None of the staff were unpleasant which is espically good considering we are 20. Some of the expensive hotels would treat someone that young as though they didn't belong there, I never got the feeling from the staff there. I felt very safe in the area, as we were walking around till about 10PM. You of course see some homeless people, but that is with every major city. I am use to walking around NYC and D.C. is much nicer. I never once feared that I was in a bad neighborhood and we did a lot of walking.

“After multiple stays we still LOVE this property!!” We have stayed here many times and the service is always great! Mike at the front desk was very helpful on this reservation! Hotel is in a great location in the middle of everything! We will continue to stay at this property. Good service always starts at the top. We received an email after our stay from Melissa Henry making sure our stay was great as usual. I have worked in the hospitality industry before so understand the service aspect.

“A legend in its own time” The Palmer House is a gorgeous, historic hotel in the heart of Chicago. Rooms are good-sized, staff is friendly, restaurants are excellent, and public areas are exceptional. I was very pleasently suprised to see that Trader Vic's (on the lower level) is still serving up exotic cocktails and delicious food after all these years. Make sure to stop by and spend some time at this American Institution. This truly is a huge hotel, so it's easy to get lost, but if you do, there is plenty of security and other staff members to point you in the right direction. The only downside is that some of the hallways can be a little bit loud with comings and goings all hours of the day and night, but if you are a sound sleeper you won't be bothered.

“Wonderful Property” Overall, I would un-hesitatingly give this property the highest rating. I was there for 4 days and have only one, small complaint and needs qualifying. Everything from the condition of the grounds, the cleanliness of the entire property, the quality of the service from the staff, and the ease of check-in/check-out was first rate. I’ve been to several high-class properties around the world and can honestly say this place is top notch! I would have absolutely no hesitation to stay there again. The rooms are as advertized and the amenities are all top-notch. The bedding and condition of my room was very, very nice and I enjoyed the ability to hook-up my iPhone to the bedside clock and the abundance of wall sockets to plug all my electronics into. I’m also one of those people who un-packs if I’m gonna be anywhere for more than an overnight, and you’d be surprised how many times you find the cleanliness of the dresser/chest of drawers to be lacking. Not here – it was immaculate! I also had the pleasure to utilize the chauffer service the property provided and it was very, very well done. The location of the hotel was very nice as well – right across the street from the convention center, about three short blocks from the downtown business district, and a short, 10 minute drive to the historic, famous, (and totally cool!) Ft. Worth Stockyards. Easy access to all major highways was another plus. I did have one issue. On the Wednesday morning I was there, I took advantage of a late-morning meeting and slept in a bit. When I got down to the Flat Iron restaurant for the breakfast buffet, it was about 10 minutes before close. Realizing this fact, I wasn’t expecting much but I was pleasantly surprised to find near-full platters of everything......BUT, it was all cold. Apparently, while the staff was diligent in keeping the containers full, they did turn off the heat prematurely. As I stated previously, I had expected less than 100% since I was late to breakfast and I certainly cannot knock them for this. It certainly wasn’t enough to discourage me from a return visit.

“Nice hotel in great spot” Stayed here while on business... Great location... close to a lot of authentic places to eat. Hotel has free breakfast on site in the morning - which was a nice touch (including glazed donuts, which I had never seen on the HI Express breakfast bar menu). Teri - who checked me in - was super friendly and gave me a nice rundown of what the hotel had to offer and what was nearby. Overall - great experience.

“Good location, super large rooms” This Hilton is downtown in walking distance to many businesses and state offices. The hotel is fairly outdated, especially the rooms. However, they are huge, almost too big, but good for families. Most rooms have a larger bedroom and then a large sitting room. Again they could use an upgrade but are ok. Hotel has both it's own restaurant and a McCormick & Schmick's. The breakfast and lunch buffets are very good and good value. Parking is very high for Indianapolis so recommend self-park.

“It'll do!” I came here on business as a solo traveler. It is close to all the major amenities. I can't say enough how great the location is. This is a nice trendy boutique hotel, with a nice upscale lobby. It is very clean and comfortable and reminds me of the hip hotels in Europe. The AC works great here, it was easy to find a comfortable temperature, the beds are ok for comfort. The reason I gave it 4 bubbles instead of 5 is because of a few things. - I think they went on the cheap with the towels and linens. The beds were ok, but the sheets feel cheap (stiff, scratchy and don't fit well) and some of the towels have holes in them. - The hotel staff does not seem as friendly and accomodating as some of the other hotels I've stayed in of the same class. This may be a cultural difference perhaps. - I think the rooms are small and kind of industrial. I know some people like this look but I feel like i'm in an office cubicle. Everything is nice and everything but, its just not homey. They have these very nice plantation shutters instead of curtains, but the room is really bright in the morning. It doesn't work to block out the sun when you want to sleep in. - there is some noise all night long from Dupont circle. Not much the hotel can do about this but I have not slept well as a result. Overall, I would recommend this hotel based upon its convenient location and cleanliness

“Very Comfortable, Great location” This hotel was great. The rooms were large and clean. The beds were unbelievably comfortable with nice linens. The bathroom was large, clean, up to date, and loaded with soft towels. And it's worth mentioning that the hotel had real, high-powered hair dryers -- not those terrible wall-mounted ones that you see in other hotels (I'm a women with thick long hair so I care about things like that). The view from my room was great. It looked out over the river. The staff was very accommodating, which you'd expect in a 4-star hotel. It was the fastest check-in I've ever experienced. Also, the concierge had great recommendations. The lounge/bar was expensive but very nice. They had a great wine list, appetizers, and friendly service. The location is fantastic. It's a very short walk to the Magnificent Mile, plenty of restaurants, the Navy Pier, the train, and there is a cab stand right in front and a Dunkin Donuts next door. A cab from Midway Airport was $35. A cab from Wrigley was $13. My only complaint about the hotel is that the mini bar has a weight sensor. So if you move around bottles in the fridge so that you can store your own food/personal items, the sensor will send a signal to the hotel and you will be charged. Or that's at least what the front desk told me. Considering how much this hotel costs, it would be nice if they provided you with a fridge large enough to store your own items in it. Through hotwire, I paid $200 per night for Thursday-Sunday. It was a great deal. I get the impression that normally it is much more.

“albergo assolutamente sopravalutato” vado spesso a New york per lavoro e non ero mai stato prima al Parker Meridien. Ne sono rimasto deluso. Il rapporto qualità-prezzo è assolutamente negativo. le stanze sono piccole e con una strana console centrale nella quale è inserita la televisione che ne riduce ulteriormente lo spazio. Il personale è poco cortese. La connessione internet costa 16 dollari mentre in un albergo così caro dovrebbe essere gratis. La posizione è ottima. Insomma, si trovano alberghi migliori ad un prezzo decisamente più conveniente.

“Nice place, and QUIET!” i was fearing my stay at this hotel, due to it's location on the airport property. but it was very well insulated, so there was no aircraft noise in the rooms at all. Quite a remote location. Nice walking trails alongside the harbor, leading to a neighborhood.

“Won't go back” I stayed here a few months earlier and thought the hotel was okay, so the next time I had to spend a night by LAX, I booked this hotel again. Big, big mistake. I stayed here because I didn't want to drive the hour and a half home that late at night (around midnight). When I tried to call to gaurantee check in that late, I was transferred no less than 7 times and hung up on twice before they finally figured out how to get me to the front desk. When I arrived at the airport I called the hotel to ensure that a shuttle was running. I specifically packed for that trip so I would not have to wait for baggage claim in LA- what a joke. Everyone had claimed their luggage and was waiting for the shuttles before any showed up. Actually we waited and waited and waited and waited. After over a half hour another shuttle driver for a different hotel took pity on us and dropped us at the Hilton. Then there was the check in. There only appeared to be two people ahead of me in line so I thought it would go smoothly. Over an hour later I was checked in. The man at the reception desk kept helping people from a tour bus that pulled up after we got in line before he helped us. Whe it was finally my turn, I commented on the wait, all I got was an extremely surly attitude. Way to treat any customer, let alone one of your gold members Hilton! Then the bar closed early- luckily the bartender took pity and made me two drinks to take out into the lobby. All the poor people behind me in line who tried to get a well needed drink were turned away. Needless to say I won't stay here ever again. By the way, I could have been home sooner than the Hilton got me into a room right next to the airport.

“Average hotel, good price and great location” My 17 year old son and I stayed here for the weekend to see a concert and a White Sox game. The hotel is very well located being two blocks from the Red Line and a easy walking mile to the Navy Pier. Lots of good restaurants around the corner. Pizzeria Uno, Harry Caray's, Rock Bottom Brewery and a couple of dozen others within a short stroll. Shopping is close also but was not on our agenda as we were bachelors. The price was competitive and came with a passable breakfast. The only downside was the room. While it was clean and comfortable a few problems existed. The bathroom fixtures, i.e. toilet and shower head, need repair and the mattress on the sofa bed would give a Chiropractor some business. The in room A-C unit had vents that blew directly on the bed and the sofa making it hard to regulate between arctic or off. The vent slates were adjustable but this made little difference. If you are use to sleeping with a fan blowing on you, this is your hotel. I would stay again just for the location and price but plan on making some "architectural" adjustments

“Great stay, awesome view & locaton” My brother & I booked through American Airlines' site for a concert at Key Arena and we loved this hotel. The location is fabulous - a block from the south monorail terminal (which takes you to the Space Needle/Key Arena at the other end) and within walking distance of Pike Place Market. It's smack in the middle of the high-end shopping district (Nordstrom, etc.), but we weren't there for the shopping. (It's also a block from Cinemarama - DEFINITELY check out what's playing in this restored retro cinema. We caught Tron!) We didn't use the health club, restaurants or concierge services, but the free WiFi in the lobby was a big plus. (Would've been nice if we could have gotten signal in our room). Speaking of room, we asked for a view of the Space Needle and our view from room 4233 was incredible (see photos). The bathroom was a little outdated (water stains on ceiling, 1980's doorknob) but it didn't ruin our stay. For $220/night, we were very pleased.

“Great place to Stay and one of the best locations in NYC” My husband and I celebrated our 12th wedding Anniversary this past weekend and decided to stay in NYC.We chose the Trump International based on it's location and reviews on tripadvisor. I also got a amazing rate on Luxuryhotels.com..We had stayed here ten years ago and did not love it.This time we really loved it. We were warmly greeted upon arrival and for our Anniversary they sent up a bottle of Champagne with some cheese.They really make you feel welcome. The room was beautiful and we thought it had everything one could possibly need.We did ask for some large wine glasses and they were there in 5 minutes.(When we stayed at the Waldorf Towers they told us they were to busy to send anything to our room and we should uses our water glasses)The full kitchen is a nice touch although we did not do any cooking. The hotel is in a great location located right next to the subway which made getting around so easy.The Time Warner center,Lincoln center,and CP nearby are extra perks as well. We did not have dinner at the Hotel's restaurants this time but we have in the past.Both excellent.For this trip we had dinner at Asiate-Amazing view and Food and Marea-Amazing food.Both are in walking distance from the Hotel. Overall this is a five star hotel with a warm feeling.I would definitely book this hotel again.

“Great location and views” I stayed here in late May for a conference and enjoyed a very comfortable stay.Check in was flawless and staff were very friendly; as SPG gold I was offered a choice of rooms including club level. Though my room was not yet remodeled, it was still comfortable and had great city and lake views to the northeast. The only real disappointment was the quality of the food and service in the club lounge. It wasn't much different than the happy hour at Embassy Suites. This is the first hotel club level lounge where I've had to sign a tab just to partake of the complimentary snacks, with a strong push for tips. Wine and beer are available for a charge, but only on request -- none is set out. No liquor is available at all, so forget an evening cocktail. I usually partake in the SPG "green choice" initiative, but the one day I wanted my room serviced here, and so didn't put out the door hang tag, no service was provided. This is a newish program for SPG and it seems they still have kinks to work out. Though in general, I'd gladly earn a few points or the $5 voucher for skipping maid service most days. As others have noted, Shulla's steakhouse is very expensive and better meals can be had elsewhere in Chicago. The burger place on the lower (river) level looked great but was super crowded the day I tried to go, so passed it up. Wifi in my room worked just great, and is complimentary for SPG elite members. In short, this is a great place to be for a meeting. The location is excellent for families and business travel, and the views can't be beat. Just don't expect anything terribly luxurious. And for those of you who complain about the parking charges -- welcome to Chicago :-) . No need for a car here anyway.

“Grand lobby, but the rooms desperately need a facelift!” I went to SF with a friend. I booked a room with two queen beds at a promo rate of $244/night. Not particularly cheap, but it seemed average for the (very desirable) Union Square area. I was pleasantly surprised to get an upgrade (I'm only SPG Gold). I requested a room in the new tower and we had an amazing view. However, the room itself seemed very bland and dated. The beds were made up in all-white linens, but some of the pillow cases appeared to have yellowed. The pillows were underfilled and seemed very old. The layout of the furniture made it impossible to stand in front of the window and appreciate the view. (A chaise and a heavy floor lamp were crowding the area). There was only one accessible electrical outlet (near the desk). There was one in a corner and another in the bathroom, but I really could have used an outlet near the bedside table so I could charge my phone and use it as my alarm clock. The bathroom was large but pretty sparse on amenities (I really wish Westin would stop using that "leaf" shaped soap. It's hard to hold on to once it gets wet. I'd much rather see a liquid soap). We didn't utilize many of the services in the hotel. As stated in other reviews, the internet fee is ridiculous. The concierge did recommend a nice place for breakfast (Scala in the nearby Kimpton hotel). Everyone I encountered was very pleasant though. In summary, the Westin St. Francis is in a great location if you're visiting SF. Close to the BART, shopping, dining, etc. However, for that kind of money, I like my room to have a bit more style and i'd probably choose a different hotel next time. There's nothing really wrong with it and if you get a good rate here, I'd say go for it!

“Perfect location for Times Square and the heart of New York” My husband and I stayed here July 4-7, 2010. This hotel is a great place to stay and the customer service we had was wonderful. The doormen were VERY nice and the front desk people were great. One day our room did not get cleaned, because we where in and out of it all day, so we called down to the front desk to let them know we would like it serviced while we went to the Mets game and when we got back it was done. They also left us a message on our hotel phone making sure the room was serviced. GREAT JOB!! There is a small little store next door open 24 hours if you need ANYTHING!! The bed was ok and the room was typically small for NY, but I would have no problem staying here. The shower, no tub, did smell like mold & mildew, but I could not find the source of it. Very trendy and beautiful! Did not eat at Blue Fin in the lobby during our stay, but it was always busy. Would highly recommend this hotel! Happy Traveling!!

“Comfortable hotel for a family” My family stayed here one night while returning home from a longer trip. The hotel is very comfortable, convenient and friendly. The room we stayed in was clean and quiet but showing signs of age. However, the whole complex is undergoing renovations so hopefully this will improve the condition of the rooms. This was the only thing that detracted from my overall rating and I would give it a higher rating otherwise. The staff was super friendly and helpful. Everyone from the manager on down went out of their way to help us. The breakfast buffet was quite a bounty as one might expect from a Residence Inn. My son enjoyed the small outdoor pool, which he had to himself. We stayed in a suite that was essentially a large studio with an additional bedroom/bathroom -- great for a family. The full kitchen was nice. The TV had an assortment of cable channels including HBO. Free high speed internet is available and there is an ethernet cable on the desk. The room was clean but there were scuff marks on the walls -- which I assume the renovations will remedy. It was very quiet and we didn't hear a noise all night. The hotel is on the edge of a large office park (between the interstate and the hotel). There are many chain eateries in the area such as Applebees, Chili's, TGI Fridays, etc. for dinner. Overall, a nice, family friendly hotel and we would stay here again.

“Nice Airport Stay!” We stayed at this hotel when we had to catch an early flight. It was right by the airport and easy access for in the morning. Staff was friendly and parking was easy. Lobby could use a little updating but is functional. Rooms were nice and clean the only downside is it's 2 Doubles and not 2 Queens for 4 people. Pool was good and so was the breakfast. I would return.
“Earned the Ranking” Wasy to see why this hotel is ranked #1 in Boston. Perfect in everyway!

“Excellent customer service” I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at this La Quinta. This hotel was clean and conveniently located in a decent area of Jacksonville. When I asked the desk clerk where the nearest supermarket was he pulled out a map and patiently gave me detailed directions. Now that's customer service !
“最高のロケーションで、部屋もとても広く綺麗” サンフランシスコの街の中心にあり、ユニオンスクエアまで徒歩5分、鉄道駅やケーブルカー駅のすぐ側という抜群のロケーションにあります。ホテルのエントランスも非常に豪華です。何より驚いたのが部屋でした。一番安い料金の部屋に泊まったのですが、上層階のビューが良く、とても広い部屋でした。いつも出張時に泊まっている部屋の2倍の広さはあり、本当に大満足でした。

“Second Stay.” This is the second time that my family has stayed here in the last 8 months and I will still recommend this hotel. Here are the pros: Courteous, helpful staff; clean accommodations; very good breakfast; comfortable dining area; convenient downtown location; reasonable price; just an overall quality place. A few cons: There is still a large construction project going on on the north side of the hotel and still many months from completion. If your room is on that side of the building the noise cranks up early in the morning and it can be very annoying. If you book a room be sure to book one with odd numbers (Riverwalk side). Also, the parking garage is nice to have but beware of your vehicle height because the overhead clearance is only 6'6". The parking spaces are also very narrow and the garage itself is simply very cramped. Not necessarily a deal-breaker, but something you should know.

“Very bad staff” I wound up changing hotels after expereince two major problems here. First, HGI is a very inconsistent brand with Hilton. Some are great (Houston, Mountain View, Las Colinas) others are a real mess (Montebello, Dallas/Market Center). Frtont desk here had two women who were much more interested in cracking each other up than in checking in the LINE of people waiting. One woman had such bad command of the english language that I had no idea what she was saying. Note to Hilton: Most of your business guests need someone who speaks proper English. I don't understand hip hop and don't feel I need to Schnizzel my nizzel to cjeck in to your hotel. Front desk was actibely unhelpful. Ignoring requests and generally dismissive. They were treating guests like thyey were an inconveneince to their personal conversations. Internet didn't work in the room. After 20 minutes on the line (a paid call) with tech support. no resolustion was eminent. BTW, most HGIs use Wavport which seems to work concsistenyl but this hotel does not. After telling the desk I needed a room with working Internet and would have to change hotels, they agreed to cancel the room, and then proceeded not to. Big surprise! Billing issues was finally resolved my the GM after a note to Hilton Gold Customer service.

“Mark (at front desk) was exceptional!” I can only echo what others have said about this property. Customer service was outstanding -- Mark, at the front desk, gave us much personal attention and advice, and even gave us partly-unused Muni Passes when we were hurrying to catch bus 47 for our Alcatraz tour. We paid a bit extra for a top-floor room to take advantage of the bay and bridge views. The view is grand (although the bridge was a bit further away than I expected), but the windows could have used a good washing. The room had average motel-type furnishings, and the bathroom was very small, but everything was clean and the housekeeping staff was very nice. The breakfast room was very crowded, (the hotel was full) and finding a table for the four of us was quite a feat. Breakfast was quite substantial and kept us going for a good part of the day, though a little more protein and less starch might have been a good idea. I'm not sure this establishment offers a good value for the rates charged, but San Francisco hotels (unfortunately) seem to be uniformly overpriced.

“Welcome to hell!” Dont do it! We booked over the phone from Vegas and got quoted a price of around US$90 per night in a standard double room and trusted the lady at the front desk regarding how good the value was. When we arrived we noticed a large sign board stating the price was US$45 per night! When i asked them to refund the difference they said they wouldnt and nor could they provide a refund. The sign was also removed very quickly. Anyway, we realised we had to settle for this motel since they were not going to refund us at all. We were then put in a room on the street. Extremely noisy, but we dealt with it. The next morning our toilet was severly blocked and we couldnt use it. Asked reception for help which took a good 45 mins. Asked to change rooms to move away from the street. They said they were full. Then I asked to see the manager and all of a sudden, a room was now available off the street! Rooms - small, dark and musty. Very noisy if facing the road. They were however, reasonably clean. Service - the brochure promises 'San Dieogos' friendliest service. Wrong! Unhelpful, and generally lazy. Location - Point Loma is a good location, however, being on one of San Diego's main roads is not! Stay away. You'll definitely be dissappointed.

“Okay Hotel - Should be nicer for a Marriot” I have stayed at a few Marriott’s over the years and I have to say I wasn’t very impressed with this location. The Lobby is nice and the staff was friendly. Check in went quickly and was easy. Our room was on the 64th floor and we had a great view of the city. I enjoyed the floor to ceiling windows. The room itself was kind of small and seemed a bit outdated. The chair in the room was very small and low and not comfortable. We had a room with two double beds and they were just okay. There was complimentary water and coffee which was nice in the morning. The bathroom was clean, however a little small. All in all the room was okay, but I expect from a Marriot and for what I paid. I have gotten a way better value from the Courtyard and the Hilton Garden Inn in the city. The location was good as the people mover station is located right in the GM building. There are also more than a few restaurants located in the building. This location is a short walk from Greektown and a safe walk as well. If you plan on using the valet then make sure you plan accordingly. We had an 11:00 brunch reservation and called for our car at 10:15. At 11:05 we still didn’t have our car. It was very busy and valet seemed to be well staffed. There were just so many people exiting at the same time that it became quite the cluster and took some time for our car to be retrieved.

“The place to stay !” Another visit to Boston and another stay in the Long Wharf. Why? The answer is easy it is all about location,location. loaction. Long Wharf sits next to the bay, most rooms have a great view particulalry on the higher floors, and next to both the Aquarium and Fanueil Hall market place the center of Boston's tourism. It is an easy walk to most of the key tourist attractions and also the T the Boston MBTA. the nearest station being the Aquarium stop on the Blue line just next to the hotel and the more useful Government Center stop being a short walk away. The Blue line give a direct two stop connection to the airport. The hotel itself is rtaher grand having undergone several rounds of renovation. The public spaces are great and there is a lively bar/restaurant for nights you dont want to venture far. Rooms are standard Marriott - clean, well furnished with a really comfortable bed. Downside is that the bathroom is rather smaller than usual -but how long do you spend in the bathroom? Very friendly staff - this hotel is very good.

“Great Hotel -” Stayed here for one night on the third floor. Had a beautiful, well-laid out room with a sofa, king size bed and desk. Had a microwave and small refrigerator. Great flat screen tv with lots of channels. This is probably the nicest Hampton Inns that I have ever stayed in... Unlike the other reviewer, I did not hear any noise from adjoining rooms. This hotel is set back off the highway - so even tho there is a little traffic noise, it is not bothersome. The bed was very comfortable and linens felt wonderful. Breakfast was ok - with the horrible pre made cheese eggs that most Hampton Inns serve. However, there were a lot of other choices. Front desk people were all very friendly. I would certainly stay in this hotel again and I would recommend it to others..

“Hilton Palacio del Rio – It’s the location” Recently completed a stay at the Hilton Palacio del Rio and what stood out was the location. It is located on the riverwalk and directly across from the hotel’s riverwalk entrance is the dock for the river boat tours. It was great taking early morning walks on the riverwalk and it was so convenient to have so many nice restaurants nearby. Also, the Alamo is only a two block walk on the street level. However, the hotel itself was nothing special. The room had the comfortable Hilton bed which I have come to expect but the accommodations were dated. The bathroom was also on the small side. A plus was the balcony which overlooked the river walk. Thumbs down to the pool scene as the pool and deck are very small and there were not enough chairs to handle all of the guests. The fitness rooms have all new equipment and I thought were very nice. I received complementary breakfast at the hotel’s Ibiza Restaurant due to Diamond status but I would not have paid $19.95 for the buffet. All of the staff I encountered had a great attitude and were very helpful (I was surprised by those who found otherwise). If I return to San Antonio, I may stay again as I have heard from one of the staff that a hotel renovation has been scheduled.

“Hidden Gem in the "bad part of town"” I have been going to races in Indianapolis for almost 15 years. I never stay in the same hotel/motel because I have never really been satisfied with the accommodations or the location. Most of my stays have been in the Indianapolis East area, but I had stopped staying there because of the level of crime. well this marriott solves this problem. It is in a "marriott compound" with another marriott and has a guard. the hotel is beautiful, the suites are HUGE- 2 big TV's couch, fridge, microwave, coffeemaker and lots of room. I actually made reservations for next year already!

“Superior Sofitel” Using Jetsetter, I got a top floor junior suite (Rm 1421) with an open north view towards Liberty Place complex (and the Westin hotel, which is also nice!) for $120/night, which was an incredible deal. The hotel is located in a prime area within a couple blocks of Rittenhouse Square, and not terribly far from the historic sites and museums. The room was nicely furnished with small, but acceptable, signs of wear. The layout and size were great, with a bathroom that could be accessed from the room entrance (like most hotels) or via the dressing area with two closets on the far side (UNlike most hotels!). The bathroom had a separate stall shower and tub, expanses of marble and L'Occitaine products everywhere--many of which came home with me. The bed was feathers above, below and under your head. There was only the feather duvet on the bed, no blanket or sheets, which made regulating temperature an all or nothing proposition in the warm weather. But it was luxurious nonetheless. I ordered one cheese and fruit plate from room service, which was delicious, well-presented and delivered exactly at the promised time. I did not use the valet parking or need the concierge's assistance, but the Front Desk staff I dealt with briefly were all very friendly, though the "bonjours" delivered with a pronounced Philadelphia accent were amusingly over the top. Overall, I was very favorably impressed with this hotel and could recommend it to anyone, especially if they can score one of the junior suites.

“Exceeded expectations” From the time I checked in till I left, the staff was really friendly and helpful. I was upgraded to a glorious room on the 16th floor, with big windows and views out to Lake Michigan through buildings and towards the Chicago river. Comfortable bed, groovy furniture. Bathtub a bit small given all the amenities, but no complaints. Loved the Keurig coffee maker also. Beautiful old building, glad it is getting used.

“Exceptional Customer Service” What a wonderful stay this was! From checking in the hotel desk person walked me to the elevator. To every time I had valet get the car they always had cold bottled water for each person in the car. Housekeeping filled the ice bucket each day. Room was wonderful bed very comfortable. Upon checking out my luggage was graciously taken to the concierge while I stayed for breakfast. Had a River Stone Massage in the Spa - it was incredible. Spa facilities wonderful. Every one I encountered offered exceptional customer service. Truly a wonderful stay. Will stay every time I go back to Austin. Which I hope is often!

“No frills, basic stay” If you’re in Washington to see the sights and restaurants, this is a good base. About 6 blocks north of the White House. The usual extended stay type room with a separate seating area and a kitchen area. The areas are in one big room, not a separate room for sleeping. Furnishings are in good shape except for the chair in the sitting area which was well worn. The room was very clean. The hotel does offer a great breakfast. A much better selection than the usual breakfast offerings that pretty much all hotel chains offer now. Choice of USA Today or Washington Post newspapers. There supposedly is an evening reception as well but only 3 nights a week and I was there on the nights where it’s not offered so I can’t review it. Business center and free Wi-Fi are available. Nice touch since a lot of downtown hotels charge for either. No gift shop or anything else in the small lobby area but there is a 24 hour CVS right next door so who needs it. Parking is $28 a night which is on par for the area. Only trick is its valet only, not self service so you have to call ahead for your car and of course, have a tip ready. TV lineup is above average though the internet is V-E-R-Y slow. All in all a very good basic stay. Price is on the high side but comparable for the area.

“Impeccable” I love each experience at a W hotel. I am not as loyal to Starwood as I am the Hilton brand, however, the W in Fort Lauderdale and this one in Dallas are great. The staff is so accommodating and attentive and even come to your room 5 minutes after missing your wake up call to knock on your door (which saved me from being late to a meeting this time). I love the toiletries from the spa (who doesn't?) and the beds and style of each room. Very comfortable and chic. The bar downstairs is fun and I love the patio when the weather is nice. This hotel is across from the American Airlines center, as well as some great restaurants down Victory Park Lane (try Medina - Moroccan cuisine, amazing).

“Great value and service” While attending a convention stayed at the hotel. I was surprised as the spaciousness of the room and the evening reception made stay very enjoyable. Price also included free wireless internet connection and full breakfast.

“Great Location, Good Idea, Fair Execution” We stayed at The Austin for two nights in August. We knew going in that it wouldn't be like the more comfortable chain hotels that we usually go to, but that it would be an Austin experience. Our room (The Zen) was clean and the air conditioning was LOUD but functioning. The pool was really nice and often empty, so very enjoyable, even if the chairs were kind of uncomfortable. Our experience with the staff was fine, and the guy we spoke to most often was more than willing to make suggestions for things to do, places to eat. The location is great, especially for visiting the South Congress area, and you can't beat free parking at the hotel. In general the stay was fine. What I'd have like to have seen was the general quirky idea of the hotel with a much better execution. Nicer fixtures and furniture, rather than the "my first apartment" feel, better towels, etc. All in all, a good step outside of our comfort zone.

“Albergo bello ma posizione scomoda” L'albergo è molto bello, elegante stanze molto spaziose attenti ai dettagli (ti regalano un cookie al cioccolato quando arrivi). Non c'è wireless (stanno ristrutturando e pare che nelle stanze sarà disponibile da fine 2009) e internet è a pagamento. La metropolitana è proprio sotto l'albergo purtroppo la zona (praticamente a Chinatown) non offre granchè in termini di locali dove cenare (tranne ristoranti cinesi che però chiudono le cucine abbastanza presto, intorno alle 9 - 9.30) e la serà benchè tranquilla è piuttosto deserta.

“Great Location..Tiny Room” To be fair we ended up staying here because we were stranded in NYC because of the volcano. It would not be my first choice. We had to hunt around to find a hotel that was affordable for a few unplanned nights. The location is superb....just off Madison Avenue...with plenty of good value places to eat within walking distance. Scotty's Diner is great. Our standard room was tiny. The king size bed filled the room almost entirely. Hotel staff told us they don't turn on the air conditioning till summer !! The bathroom was a good size but needs some money spent on it to cover up previous attempts at redecoration. It was clean enough ... although not spotless. I could have done without the man coming to the room every morning to ask what you'd used from the minibar. Very old fashioned tv with poor reception. The lobby is very grand looking with a nice bar and desk staff were helpful enough. The hotel is owned by an Italian chain which explains the European feel to the rooms. It was ok but I don't think I'd bother to stay there again.

“Value-able!” So...If you wanna B%T€# and complain...Do them a favor, just don't bother staying here...If you enjoy value, please.....By all means, book TODAY. This place has everything a great little motel has to offer....Friendly staff, nice cozy room, cleanliness, and a place to rest your head at days end. (I recommend Cabrillo Monument. It's AWESOME!!!!) I personally, don't see why people complain about "HOW SMALL" the rooms are...I thought it was perfect in size (Plus I was able to rub elbows with my honey) It's in a great location, it's California! Great ocean air (Which I am sure the locals sometimes take for granted)....I personally feel inspired travelling to San Diego. (I guess it's not for everyone)...I would recommend this place to my best friend.

“Location!” I stayed at the Handlery on 07/25 for a run in San Francisco. The location just off Union Square was fantastic. The staff was extremely helpful and courteous. I would and probably will be staying here again.

“Times Square up the road” Bit late with review as we stayed Jan 11 but just wanted to get a few words down for likely travellers to this hotel. We stayed there to take advantage of New Years Eve and the rate was so well priced the other hotels could not begin to compete. The location is excellent literally walk up distance to Times Square and a Subway over the road for that cheap filler meal. Brkfst came with room, was heavy carbs but hey did the job for a family of 5 to start the day without having to look for bkfst. Rooms are quite small so definitely do not recommend for a family our size but for a couple of people perfect, and they were a little on the warm side which I didnt like but very cold outside so perhaps others would enjoy the cosiness. The rooms were very clean and the bed comfortable as were pillows and the lift functioned well with the level of traffic. I would definetely recommend based on price and location but keep in mind if you are wanting to be in Times Square for New Years Eve you still have to get there early afternnoon before they block of your roads access, that was just not possible for us with 3 younger kids so we ended up near Central Park, keep that in mind as next time I would probably pay the crazy prices for a hotel on Times Square so as to be able to walk down at an appropriate time to enjoy the New Years Eve festivities. Other than that this hotel is an obvious choice for the traveller looking for price,cleanliness and safe area close to Times Square, its geat to be a part of Times Square without the level of noice and crowds that come with it.

“Excellent Airport Hotel” This is without doubt the best airport hotel that I have stayed in: this isn't really saying much because airport hotels are in my experience almost always souless places - this one still feels a bit like that but much less so than any others. The location is of course excellent - it's fantastic to be able to come off an international flight and to be in your hotel room in less than 10 minutes. The room itself was excellent - very large and comfortable and beautifully clean. The bathroom was big enough to be a hotel room in it's own right. The room had a most fantastic view over the airport and runways (if you like that sort of thing...). The service in the restaurant was excellent - the staff were very attentive and the food was very good. The hotel is fairly expensive - the extras seem to add up - but overall definitely a place to stay if you need to be in DFW.

“My Second Review of This Hotel” This is my second review of this property, my first being in May of 2007. Since my last stay there have been a few improvements. The bath products are now "Davies Gate" brand, and are quite nice. There were 5 pillows on the bed to choose from. And the courtyard seems a bit more alive, but there are still some empty "for lease" storefronts. Front desk staff seems genuinely friendly and personable, not just "put on." This time I stayed two nights, and I did notice the early morning dumpster noise coming from Beach Street (in front of the hotel), although it didn't bother me too much--I had the heater on, so the fan sound acted as a buffer. Double pane windows would greatly help with the noise issue. The windows are in need of replacement anyway, they are the one thing showing age in the room. Otherwise the room was clean, simple, tasteful, and in very good condition. Maid service did a great job of refreshing the room for my second night. I came by ferry and without a car this time, and it was easy to catch busses to everywhere I needed to go. I recommend walking over to see the fishing boats on the pier near Scoma's restaurant--it's a quiet escape, and a different world in comparison to the noisy din of the tourist area. I hope this hotel continues to improve.

“Very good service, great location near shopping mall” My luggage was lost by the Airline Company and reception staff made anything possible to help me while waiting my luggage! Well done guys, trully appreciate! Hotel is also located near a big shopping mall!

“A nice surprise off Copley” Very nice but small hotel very near the larger Marriott Copley Place. Hard to locate -- my cabbie tried to drop me at the main Courtyard by Marriott downtown. Evidently, this hotel was recently rebranded as a Courtyard. The rooms were normal large-city sized rooms -- in other words, they were a bit small. But for one person or a couple, they are fine. The shower was excellent - large with a good spray. All the room amenities were fairly new and functional. The bed was veyr comfortable and the room very quiet. The only complaints were that the room was quite cold. The thermostat seemed stuck on full air conditioning. This is NOT a full service hotel. No bar or restaurant, but there is much nearby. Cabs are not easy to catch; it's on a side street, but the bellman ran a block away to get me one. Hotel staff were very pleasant and helpful. Nice place to stay.

“Charming Blakely” We just returned from a week in NY, my agent got a good price at the Blakely and it was indeed an excellent choice. For the price we got it, it beats most midtown hotels where I usually stay (like the Mansfield, which I like by the way). Location: very nice. I myself like streets around the 44th better for a wider choice of restaurants, but this was so close to Central park that made us forget about the rest. Hotel: small enough to be cozy. Warm welcome and helpful concierge at all times. We had complimentary continental breakfast which was good (staff at bkfst a bit brisk but they are probably just understaffed). Rooms: very clean. Bathroom was spotless. Rooms have a kitchenette w/ microwave, refrigerator and freezer which is very nice if you have kids. It allowed us to stop in the room to get a rest and snack. TV with Dvd player. Ironing board (not that I used it but I appreciate it). Beds: rarely I have slept in such comfy beds, they hug you. The pillow was small and soft (my neck gets usually stiff when I sleep in hotels, but not here). Large closet/s. And most lights dim, which is so nice especially in the bathroom, I hate strong lights when I get up. The rooms facing the bach (Hilton side) are a bit noisy, but it seems to me that most hotels have the same problem in NYC. It was not a big issue to me anyway.

“3 Tage in einem super Hotel” Wir waren zum Abschluss unserer Reise in diesem Hotel. Unser Navigator fand die Anschrift nicht, da alles noch neu war. Kevon von der Rezeption lotste uns per Telefon weiter. Klasse! Unser Zimmer war sehr geräumig. Schreibtisch, doppelter Fernsehsessel, Kommoden, kleine Kitchenette, Wandschrank, geräumiges Badezimmer mit allen Schikanen. Alles supersauber. Ein Frühstück zum Träumen. Warmes und kaltes Buffet und dazu den besten Kaffee in ganz Texas.Ständig wurden neue warme Zimtschnecken gemacht. Herrlich! Das Hotel liegt außehalb, doch da Fort Worth/Dallas so gorß ist, benötigt man auf jeden Fall ein Auto. Alles war von dort aus gut zu erreichen. Für unseren nächsten Aufenthalt haben wir bestimmt hier wieder unsere Reservierung!

“Solid 4 stars, and quaint with the perfect location” I liked the Back Bay Hotel quite a bit, but even more after spending a single night at the relatively nearby Marriott Copley Place. The minute you walk through the doors, you can't help but appreciate the modern decor. And the entrance and lobby areas are neither huge nor sterile so you don't feel like you're in a mega-hotel/warehouse, which is how I felt the minute I walked into the Marriott. And front desk service is prompt and very friendly and quick to help when asked. As for the room, we had a Superior Room with two double beds and it was plenty large enough . . . not small at all. The room was clean and attractive, the beds comfortable with nice linens and a typical flat screen tv as you expect to find in any decent hotel these days. A/C worked just fine too. And there was plenty of closet and drawer space for clothing. But the best part of the room in my opinion was the over-sized bathroom. There's no tub, but the shower was great, modern and featured a light body sprayer. I appreciated the fact that the high glass shower door prevented the bathroom mirror from getting all fogged up. There was a heated towel rack which although of little use at the beginning of September was still a nice touch. The bathroom also featured high end Kiehl's toiletries. I was also really pleased that the hotel provided free high speed internet service, and it was plenty fast. I'm tired of getting nickeled and dimed at hotels so make sure you take into account the free internet when comparing hotel rates. Location was great in the heart of Back Bay. You're a very short walk to many restaurants, Newberry St., the T, Chinatown, and more. Even if you plan on seeing the historical sights and the Freedom Trail, this is the perfect location because of its proximity to both the T and nightlife/restaurants. When I return to Boston, I would definitely stay at this hotel again. It's certainly a solid 4 star hotel which may not necessarily wow you, but will certainly please and impress you.

“Huge apartment, with great staff.” We had split stay here, we had a 2 bedroom apartment booked for the both stays. Our first apartment was an interconnecting one bedroom/junior suite. This had a view of the Empire state from the bedroom, bathroom and kitchen. This was huge for our group. The second stay we had a 2 bedroom apartment, no view this time and the apartment itself seemed not quite as well maintained. The doormen at the establishment are excellent, they are very knowledgeable and give great information. We relied on them for recommendations for dining and transport and they were spot-on. Grand central station is an easy walk, although we found the subway ticketing system complicated and ended up relying on taxis! There is a great supermarket close by, that has everything including a great range of fruit and vegetables, also a Walgreens. Basically, everything you could need is close by. We felt absolutely safe walking at night, even on our own.

“Tiny rooms, but good rates” The MAve is well-located and well-priced--these are its main recommendations. The place has some style, the free wi-fi, flat-screen tv and iPod dock are nice touches, and the staff is friendly and helpful--but in the end, the selling point is a clean room in a prime Manhattan location. We are former New Yorkers coming back for a visit, and we just needed a place to sleep and leave our stuff in an area convenient to everything we wanted to do--and this fit the bill. We had the most basic room category, which has a full bed--not a queen, as another reviewer said--and is about the size of a decent walk-in closet. But that was fine--we knew what we were getting into. The room was very clean, with crisp white bedding and a modern bathroom. A couple downsides: the humidity in the room was never quite right, so the sheets often felt damp, and the blinds let in a lot of light come morning. We got a lot of use out of the free wi-fi and certainly appreciated that amenity. One suggestion I would make is not to have such sharp corners on the beds in such a tight room, which invites people like me to smash open a toe on them. But whatever, I am clumsy. The part that concerned me was when I asked for extra pillows to elevate my foot and a staff member (who had come very quickly with band-aids and antiseptic wipes) told me there were no extra pillows in the entire hotel. Seriously? In a hotel? To be fair, he managed to produce some fairly quickly after that. Despite any such issues, overall it was decent value in the amazingly overpriced world of Manhattan hotels. The location was really the selling point--right in the very central Gramercy area, easy walking distance to Union Square, close to the subway.

“Great stay” This is beautiful, luxurious hotel and property. I had a room overlooking the 18th green, which provided beautiful scenery. The room was very plush - plenty of pillows, comfy mattress and nice linens. Big executive desk to work at, and a comfy chair with blanket to get cozy and watch TV. Bathroom is huge, and included a stall shower and soaking tub. Turn down service with chocolates were a plus. We were at a conference, so buffets were the meals, but everything was cooked well and at the appropriate temperature. There are 2 different bars - one right in the lobby, and one at the far end of the hotel in "The Gallery" restaurant. Service in all areas of the hotel was terrific. The fitness center was one of the better ones I have seen. At least 3 treadmills, 4 elliptical machines and a few bikes for cardio. Weight machines, and then plenty of space and yoga mats if you wanted to do your own stretching. Hotel also has a spa but I didn't have a chance to use any of these services. The only weirdness about the hotel is it's location. It's about 20 minutes away from the airport, but it is in the middle of a corporate business park area, surrounded by office buildings. There is a small shopping center nearby but from what I could tell it had just a few stores like a drug store and a Five Guys. Otherwise, it was a great stay at the Ballantyne.

“Be wary of freeway side of hotel” Pros: -Standard Holiday Inn fare. -Free Internet -Close to Wal-Mart -Close to Freeway Cons: -Freeway side is quite noisy. I'm a deep sleeper and I still felt it was pretty dang loud. Not ridiculous loud, but enough to bother me while i'm lying there trying to go to sleep -Bed was a little firm for me. Courtyards and Residence Inns have softer beds. -Parking is a bit of an issue. Instead of double white line dividers, they're single, and quite compact, so if theres a suburban parked in one spot, unless you drive a small car, you won't be able to fit in. Neutral: -Construction was going on in parking garage and lobby floor but didn't create a disturbance for me. Overall: Standard Holiday Inn fare. Decent room, decent price, decent stay. Stay away from the freeway side if you can, but won't ruin your stay if you do.

“An excellent place to stay in the bay area” The Argonaut sits at the far end of the Fisherman's Wharf area close to Ghiradelli Square. It's a slightly quieter spot on Fisherman's Wharf which may be the best spot on the wharf depending on your view and being just around the corner from the trolley terminus it was easy to get into Union Square too. Check in was good and the room was beautiful keeping with the nautical theme, very clean and well appointed. Staff, particularly the door staff, were friendly and helpful. In fact such was the professionalism of the hotel there is little to write about as everything went so well. The hotel is a rectangular building which means 50 % of the rooms face inwards and have no view. Windows have shutters rather than curtains and this did seem to let a lot of light in, not best for a hangover I'd guess but for a healthy early start to a day of sightseeing it's fine. Overall an excellent hotel which does everything well without ever hitting the very highest standard. I'd recommend it in a heartbeat.

“Good place near Wall Street” If you are looking to stay here for business and your travels are going to keep you near the New York stock exchange, this is a very good choice. The rooms are average- for New York standards- and the breakfast is nice. The staff is very friendly- not your typical New Yorker at all- and the breakfast staff is super nice! Don't expect to get any type of a view of any of the New York famous landmarks. That being said, there are 2 subway lines that are very close that will get you anywhere. Battery park is walkable as well. The ride to Time Square was a bit longer and had me on the subway much longer than I wanted, but I think the New York Subway system is one of the most disgusting creations every made by man. There is little to no night life around this hotel and you will most likely have to travel to get a dinner. There was a really nice quiet Irish-esque type bar that served ok corned beef and they had Guinness on draft.

“Great Location, Good Room, Friendly staff” This location is on the Magnificent Mile and is close to everything. There are subway stations close, too, so you can get to and from the airport easily. The room was clean, looked modern, and was comfortable. They only had one towel in the room, so we had to call for more, but they were brought up promptly. The room was expensive, so I'm not sure I'd stay there again because of that, but it was a great place to stay. They do not provide free internet. I can't believe there are still hotels charging for internet use. This is one of them.

“Exception Service Convenient to Airport and Subway to Loop” Room 1118 (8 October – 10 October 2010) 2 double beds desk with chair and lamp, flat screen tv, small microwave, good sized refrigerator, safe, chest of drawers, comfy chair with reading lamp, and something to hold suit with mirror to dress by (didn’t use). View towards airport but noise rarely heard in room even though on top floor with planes landing overhead constantly. Remote control for TV had low battery so I called front desk-new one brought in about 10 minutes. Early 1990’s bathroom-nothing special with tub/shower combo, toilet, and sink. Ameniteis provided and restocked second morning. Shower had rain head which was nice. Upgraded to Executive level since Priority Platinum member-always a nice treat. Rate included buffet breakfast each morning and 2 drink coupons. Breakfast is one area for improvement. Buffet consists of scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage links, French toast, potatoes, and a few types of breads and juices plus coffee or tea. Food was ok, but it would be nice to have eggs made to order like in European hotel breakfast buffets. It wasn’t worth $12.95, but since it was included in rate and only about $5 more per person than the rate w/o breakfast, I can’t complain too much. Everyone at desk and in restaurant very helpful. We were allowed to check in 2 1⁄2 hours early. Guy forgot to give me my drink coupons and breakfast coupons but I was rushing him since I had to be downtown in less than an hour so not his fault. When we returned, I stopped by the front desk and was given the coupons. A/C worked well. Near Cumberland L stop so we decided to take from O’Hare since we were buying a 24 hour pass anyway and didn’t have time to wait on shuttle. It is a nice hike-best route by crossing bus drop off area and then narrow sidewalk next to parking garage to cross Cumberland at entrance to I-90 and then down Cumberland to just past the hotel and then through hotel parking lot. Obstacles: Parking garage, crossing Cumberland at only one intersection, and fence around hotel preventing a short cut. It was not too bad. We also did it about midnight on Saturday, and the area was well lit and safe. We took shuttle to airport on Sunday morning and didn’t have to wait more than 5 minutes since it was already loading up. I had a tip ready for shuttle driver, but he hopped off bus to help someone else get their luggage and just pointed to our airline so no tip given. There was some banging on one of the doors nearby about 2 am the last night, but no one bothered us. There was a guy wandering around 11th floor at midnight on our return with ice on his shoulder. He went into the Executive Lounge so I went in also to see if there were any free soft drinks or anything, but nothing. I think he was in the room next door where the banging would occur later. I don’t know why the lounge was unlocked. It was simple with sofa, chairs, and a regular bathroom-not too businesslike, in my opinion. To summarize, it was a good hotel and served its purpose. The staff were all professional. Those at the front desk were well trained in customer satisfaction. The restaurant staff were enthusiastic but didn’t speak perfect English or understand college football, which was our purpose for this trip. I would stay here again if in the area. No major negatives, but the hotel did show its age.

“great option for San Antonio” Obviously, expectations play a huge role in how someone "sees" a property. We just got back from The Watermark, and really liked it for what it cost... My party consisted of me, my wife, 5 year old, and 7 month old. I had business in San Antonio, and the family came along. We stayed in room 471, a "Premier River Walk View" room. Coming from the jaded NYC metro area, we're always skeptical about how good a $250/night hotel can be.(Pathetic,isn't it?) Well, the hotel was definately worth the price. It was more expensive than most in San Antonio, but we want service and amenitites. Room was very large.High (12 foot? ceiling) Had a king, with room for a roll-away, chairs, and desk. Bathroom was enormous, with fantastic water pressure. Glass doors on shower, seperate spa tub. (in fact, only dissapointment for wife was toiletries. They skimped a bit, and she did not like the hotel hawking the better toiletries with a stand of goodies - if you open them you buy them - in the bathroom. She felt that was a bit ridiculous) River walk view and balcony was key for children. They loved looking down at the river and the commotion. Housekeeping was OK, they blew one turndown service (they forgot), but staff did a good job cleaning. Concierge helpfull as well. Liked the fact that you needed your room key 24/7 to access guest floors. Room serivce was good, although menu was somewhat limited. They will, however, go across river to sister hotel "La Mansion?" and get things from there also if you ask. Pesca, the restaurant, was good. We ate breakfast there daily. Wait staff did have some problems understanding our orders though...ex.: got "double expresso w/cream on side" wrong 4 of 5 mornings... Dinner was good also. I liked the gulf snapper... Wife loved the spa, and its late hours, so she could go down there after kids were alseep! If we return to San Antonio, we'll most likely stay again.

“better than i expected” i stayed here for a night on 9/24/2010. i wasn't thrilled with the price we got, and i don't like the location since the financial district is so far away from nightlife, but i was very impressed with the room. it was probably the biggest room i've ever had in a NYC hotel, it was very nice, and very clean. and the beds were awesome. (the night before we had stayed in the sheraton four points in SoHo - to give a baseline for comparison, that room was a bit smaller, and not quite as nice, but still a respectable sheraton so it was fine. so it was basically a trade off between the slightly nicer marriot and the sheraton in the great soho location.) and in retrospect the marriot's location wasn't as desolate as i thought it might be, since there are still plenty of restaurants within a couple blocks that stay open for dinner (after all the wall street folks go home after 5) and the subway stop is right there. the view is also worthy of comment - our room was right overlooking ground zero. we could also see the hudson river and NJ skyline from our room. so if you're okay with the rate you're getting at the marriot and don't mind taking the subway or paying for a cab, then i strongly recommend this hotel.

“Good and Bad at Hyatt Hill Country” The Hyatt Hill Country Resort is still a nice and unique place to stay... but this will likely be our last visit. The good: -The hotel's public places, especially the lobby and the grounds, are simply beautiful. Flowers everywhere. The buildings and really all resort features fit beautifully within the Hill Country setting. -Nicest resort near SeaWorld. Westin's LaCantera Resort is a nicer hotel and will likely be our next stop here, but it is closer to Fiesta Texas and is a bit more expensive. We have also stayed at the Radisson near SeaWorld and its okay but not really a resort. Its a decent hotel with a couple of pools. It is significantly less expensive than the Hyatt and may well be a better value. -Tons of kid-centered activities. Hard to beat the movies on the lawn each night, s'mores every night, the pools, the "Ramblin' River", great kid food options, Camp Hyatt, all the options for hair braiding, face painting, pony rides, (at extra cost) etc. Kudos to the staff who had puzzles and games and crayons and all sorts of other stuff set out in the grand lobby the day it rained. You really could spend a week here, never take a trip outside the resort and keep everyone very busy. -Friendly staff. Everyone... front desk, valet, pool staff, really everyone... very kind. Never spoke to a person who was rude or inappropriate. All went above and beyond. -Convenient everything... everywhere. Meaning only that you never have to leave the hotel. Its all here. Every meal option, every snack food, every toiletry, every item of clothing, everything... -Good variety of meal options: Pool side grille, buffet style meals at one restaurant (Springhouse Cafe), higher end at another (though Antler's is not near as nice, exclusive, unique as it used to be). -A couple of really nice bars. Drinks at a premium but the settings are fantastic. The less good: -Value is a relative thing. If you are stretching to pay for a room here, then everything is going to seem VERY overpriced. So, instead, I will just spell out what we paid, a few surprises, etc. And you can decide on your own the value. We arrived on a Saturday and left on a Friday. $329 for the first night, $269 for each additional... with one of the five at $269 "free". A stay 5 night and one night is free deal. It felt very expensive for what this hotel has become. Ten years ago, this was a REALLY nice place. It just doesn't quite feel worth this to us now. Our room was a double double. It was my wife and three children. They allow for three kids in a room but cannot put a roll-away bed in these rooms due to "fire code". We knew this ahead of time and our 10 year old son was fine with a sleeping bag we brought along on the floor. Camp Hyatt is more expensive than it used to be. $45 per child for a 6-10pm time slot. That $135 for one 4 hour blocks makes you think twice about making that reservation for 2 at Biga, Acenar, etc. if you want one night of your trip alone with your spouse. Springhouse Cafe buffet breakfast is $20 for adults, $10 for kids. There are slightly less expensive a la carte options. Poolside grill burgers, nachos, adult meal options are about $10 each. Kids meals about $6. Drinks extra. Sodas are $2.50 for a 20oz. Bottled water about the same. Beer is $5.50. Pina Coladas, Margaritas etc. are $8.50. The "General Store" is fantastic for less expensive eating options. Yet, granola bars are still $4. Bagels about the same. $5 for a Starbucks Mocha Tall. Breakfast tacos $3.25 each. You can get things like KrispyCreme donuts, pop-tarts, etc. if that is your kids style for food. They serve pizza, sandwiches too. Valet is $15 a night. The bad: -Its just not what it once was. Not as polished. Not as clean. -The walls either seem thinner, or our neighbors are just remarkably noisy. We could hear almost every word of conversations next door. We try to be SO tolerant... but did have to put in one call to the front desk when the family next door came in at 1130 and the two boys were screaming and wrestling, and the parents were just laughing along. -Pillows smelled musty, sweaty... like a gym. -Housekeeping seems understaffed. They could never seem to get to our room in a normal fashion so on several occasions were still at it after dinner. Neither good nor bad, but you just need to know: -I cannot FATHOM coming here as a honeymooning couple, a senior couple, really any kind of couple unless you have a slew of kids. -Again... this place is absolutely OVERRUN with kids. They are everywhere all the time. I've stayed at a lot of really nice resorts where kids fit well within the overall setting of the place. Not here. You cannot escape. Again, we are here with our 3 (ages 10, 7 and 6) ... but its tough when you find that yours are amongst the best behaved. There are kids screaming in the restaurants at all meals. There are kids screaming in rooms at all hours. There are kids running up and down the halls at nearly all hours. -Did I mention there are just a ton of kids here...? -The clientele has just changed a bit. Don't want to come off sounding elitist at all. It just feels less Nordstrom's and more JCPenny's. And don't miss the point. I may shop at Penny's sometimes too. But if I am paying Nordstrom's prices... I want Nordstrom quality. So overall, great place for kids. Not as nice as it once was. Hard to call it a value... in fact, feels pretty overpriced. Other favorites on this trip: SeaWorld still shines. FiestaTexas feels like it nickel and dimes you for everything. Loved La Fogata for dinner. Loved Acenar for lunch. Did the Rio River Boat tour for the kids sake and it was fun. Hadn't done it in years.

“Great location.great staff,clean!!!” Really nice hotel. the rooms are not that big bug enough. Really clean rooms and fresh.staff is great. the bathroom is nice and big. internet is a bit expensive but doable. the only negative was that i could hear the people next door too clearly.only a door separated the rooms.otherwise great location,across from Prudential mall.

“Great Seattle location average honors perks” My wife and me spent two days here and enjoyed it. The hotel is central to the Pike Market, walk there and the mono rail to the Space Needle. There are plenty of restaurant and shopping options in walking distance. The staff is friendly, rooms are updated and beds comfortable. We were on the 27th Hilton Honors Floor. The fitness center is nice with free weights and weight machines. There are 3 thread mills, an elitptical and recumbent bike. The cardio machines are showing some were but worked fine. This Hilton has a Top of the Hilton Resturant that doubles as the concierge lounge. No special access needed. I am not a snob but missed enjoying bottled water and soft drinks that come with a member only lounge. Breakfast and the evening reception were well done even with all access. Bery good staff at both. This was the only opportunity and a small one at that. We will stay again. There is a frig in the room, a plus.

“Wonderful renovated rooms” I recently stayed at the Embassy Suites North and it was wonderful. They have just renovated and the rooms and I dont know how the hotel was before that, but now they are first rate. The beds are very comfortable, all the furniture is modern and new. Fantastic amenities, nice bathroom, nice lobby. The fitness center is a bit small but I think they are updating that next. This was a very comfortable place to stay for a couple of days on business. I wish all embassy suites had the same decor and amenities this one has now.

“Enjoyable San Antonio stay” My boyfriend and I really enjoyed this hotel during our visit to San Antonio for Thanksgiving last year. The hotel has the feel of a boutique establishment. The decor is very modern but still very comfortable with just a touch of Texas charm. The rooms are a little on the small side, but they are laid out in a Loft Apartment fashion which maximizes the utilized space. The bed was comfy and the room clean. I would definitely recommend this hotel for a single traveler or a a couple. There was an opaque window between the shower stall and the sleeping area which was great for me and my boyfriend but probably wouldn't be ideal for a family. It is also very close to the airport, making it ideal for business travelers. I would definitely stay here again!

“Character, quiet and great food” Really enjoyed this hotel--the room was small but well appointed. Really good location and elegant feel to the hotel. The service restraunt has outstanding food and this has a bit of a European feel to it. I was there for business but would definately visit for a leisure trip as well.

“Uber hip design and location, small flaws that won't matter to you.” The location: heart of the Meatpacking District with all it's pros and cons. High-end shopping, bars and clubs galore, various dining options, easy access to the High Line. Not super convenient to the subway, but if you're staying here you're probably a cab person anyways. The rooms: Modern and stylish, with great views. Small, but good use of space and attractive furnishings. The shower must be mentioned: great rain shower-head, only separated from the room by a glass wall. There were little things where they decided style was more important than function -- the lack of a shower door means water tends to splash on the bathroom floor, the stylish sink splashes a bit, and the toilets don't flush with enough water volume. But frankly, if you chose to stay here, these things probably matter less to you than the quality design and happening vibe of the hotel anyways. Room service food was also quite good (though there are so many good restaurants in the area you shouldn't use it often). The Standard Grill is decent and usually quite happening (especially the beer garden when the weather is nice). Overall, if you're looking for a metropolitan escape feeling (food, shopping, clubs, music, models), the Standard delivers, though it's a bit over-the-top.

“Passsage to nowhere.” The best thing about this hotel is the outside balconies and the overall effect they have on the exterior of the building. But once inside, things become claustrophobic, cluttered and confusing. One guest told me he felt like he was in the interior of a cruise ship, with passageways to nowhere. Multiple banks of elevators scattered here and there, hallway graphics that clash and cryptically inform. To top it off, every move you make has to be done with your room key card, even getting towels at the pool. Only James Bond would be happy with this set up. Checking in the lobby is for some reason is something of an afterthought, in a cramped area to the left of the main door. Yet there is a huge volume of space when you first enter extending into infinite space dedicated to just sitting on large sofas and chairs looking cool and very Blu. Maybe these people have given up looking for their rooms. The rooms themselves are light, airy, and very over lit. A dimmer would have been nice. Bathroom doors slide but never really close, and you have to enter the shower to turn on the water as it rains on you overhead. A perfect symbol to the many minor annoyances that this hotel offers.

“As Close to BWI Airport As You Can Get” I was apprehensive about staying at a Four Points but this is a very nice property! Ample free parking and super close to BWI Airport (in fact, this property is considered the "Airport Hotel" and you can literally see the parking garage and the tarmac / runway from your room). As a result of this close proximity, it can get a bit noisy from the airplanes. Our room was clean and well appointed and appeared to have been recently renovated. We checked in very late at night and the front desk staff was busy but friendly. We requested extra pillows and the housekeeping staff brought them within 5 minutes! The hotel has a restaurant on-site and they have late hours. You can view all arriving / departing flights right on your in-room t.v. too! The bed was comfortable, the room was clean and I had a good night's sleep. This is a great choice before or after a flight.

“Great hotel, great price.” I booked this hotel for my husband for a recent trip to chicago. His colleagues all stayed across the street in the other marriott which was more expensive. He said the courtyard was great and he was glad he saved 180 a night over the other hotel. He stayed on a high floor and was upgraded to a corner room with a good view. The only downside was that the breakfast bar was not open at 6:20 when he wanted to have breakfast.

“nice hotel” Staying at this hotel was a truly wonderful experience. Our room was comfortable with a view of the city. We enjoyed dinner at its restaurant and drinks at the bar. We walked around downtown and enjoyed the area, the city, and the hotel very much.

“A really great option- design-y but comfy near Grand Central.” I checked in with a cousin for a night and found this hotel to be really cute and in a great neighborhood near Grand Central. What I appreciated were the clean lines and the spacious hallway which made the room seem bigger. The hotel was designed by David Rockwell so there is a well-thought out Murphy kind of furniture set up but fortunately the bed is separate. We slept quite fine even though the mattress was a bit on the soft side. The bathroom had a tub which was not expected. No Occitane amenities as described before, but Philosophy instead. Nice lighting near the bed and doubled-glazed windows to block the light were very helpful. The staff is very warm and there is a sense that someone is minding the store which is cool when the lobby is very small. I did have someone smoking in the hall and that was very unpleasant. The Alex is quite alright and one could do much worse. I did not try the restaurant or the gym as we had places to go. There are a few places to eat nearby and to have coffee in the morning.

“great design small rooms” liked this property i am a fan of schrager-design-boutique concept so my review must be readed in this context loved very much the restaurant bar and lobby area one of my favorite places in new york like friendly and trendy staff must clarify that we are not service intensive i think that everyone visiting must stay or at least have dinner in this property you can have a great experience for average budget only complain is room size but must visit at least once so you can complain as everyone does

“An Excellent Choice for Luxury, Service, and Location” My first stay here. Centrally located right at Gas Lamp district. Lots of restaurants and shopping nearby. Quiet hotel inside and out. Lobby furnishings a little dated, but heck the place is 100 years old. Smiles and greetings from all staff. Bar area was very pleasant to sit and read in the morning with free newspapers and complimentary tea or coffee. Elevators were small but no waiting. Suite room was large with huge bathroom and first quality linens and towels. Bose radio was a nice touch. Overall, very pleased with my selection. As a Platinum SPG number, got the upgrade and points, so could not be happier. The only negative was the outrageous price to use the business center computer. No need to charge 50 cents a minute plus printing costs.

“Not bad for Philly” I had to stay at this hotel for a conference. I have stayed here before in the past and it is a little pricey. I actually like the Loewes Hotel across the street and they tend to also have cheaper rates too. It looks like they finally remodeled the rooms.
