I was pleased that they had a separate check in for Elite members. My room was clean but there was a layer of dust on the tissue holder in the bathroom. I did also notice that for some reason, my room always smelled like breakfast...almost like syrup and the hallway smelled like the grill so ventilation isn't the best (and I was in the main building-they have a separate tower as well for Elites). They offered me a room in the main building so I didn't have to schlep back and forth which I did appreciate. The bellman and the valet staff were very, very nice and extremely pleasant. Its not a bad hotel for a Marriott but there are some better places with cheaper rates.
“Another Quality Starwood Hotel” Lovely new(er) hotel located three blocks away from convention center. Superb staff, comfortable rooms, lovely facility. A positive experience from start to finish.

“Average Hotel” This is an older hotel...but well maintained. Pros: Great Location, Nice ammenities, comforable beds, nice bathrooms, bottled water provided daily, Keurig coffee maker, clean rooms, great customer service. Cons: Older hotel, slow elevators, dated rooms.

“Good service, old-fashioned style, comfortable.” Checked in late at night after walking out of the nearby awful Hotel Monaco. They had a room available for me immediately, had quick room service dinner brought up promptly that was excellent. Room while old-fashioned for my trendier style preferences was very comfortable and great to sleep in. Recommended.

“Very, very, very loud” This hotel *would* be great: Nice location, good rooms, helpful staff. However, no matter how nice they make the hotel itself, that can *never* offset the shear noise of the rooms. From rooms on the 12th floor, you can clearly make out conversations that people are having in the street below at normal voice levels. The garbage trucks and sirens during the night are so loud that they feel like they're in the room with you. It's so bad that they leave ear plugs on the bedside tables.

“Some Mishaps but mostly good!” Okay, let's get the negative things out of the way first. When I made my reservation I made it clear that I would be arriving very late, around 1:30-2:00 a.m. Imagine my surprise when the very nice, friendly and helpful manager (Chad Nathan) told me my room had been given away and I would have to go to another hotel. Although he couldn't have been nicer about it, and couldn't have been more apologetic or sympathetic, it still meant I had to take a cab from the west side to the east side at around 2 in the morning! He did explain that (a) they would provide me transportation to this other hotel and (b) the other hotel would be a complimentarty situation, (c) they would provide me transportation back in the morning and (d) they would give me a complimentary upgrade, it still meant that I would not get to bed until pretty much 3 in the morning! The other hotel, the Omni Berkshire, was lovely, with a nice lobby and pretty rooms, the room they gave me, on the fifth floor with a view on the street, meant it would be very noisy. The room also had a bathtub (an essential with me) which had a stopper that didn't work, entailing a visit by the janitor at nearly 3:00 a.m. I will be writing a review of that hotel at another time. Suffice to say that arriving at 2:00 a.m. after a ten-hour flight from Honolulu and having no room available was NOT what I wanted to have happen. About the only positive thing about this situation was that both the desk clerk noted above and the gentleman who met me at the cab were extremely nice, sympathetic and helpful. The latter especially was extremly nice and helpful and would have gotten an extremely nice tip except I never saw him again. He even told me that he was "devastated" to have this happen to me! Okay, now that that's out of the way, when I arrived the next morning I was given a corner room on the next to top floor with a great view of lower Manhattan, the Empire State Building and the Hudson River. It was an exceptionally large room, very comfortable, with a great king size bed, a nice bathtub and pretty much all the amenities. If I had any criticisms about the room, it would have to be that the bathroom itself was pretty small, but at least had enough space to put shaving gear, etc. around the sink, which can be a luxury, as not all rooms give you this kind of space to put your personal stuff. Sometimes you can't even put your razor anywhere. The bad thing about this size was that if you didn't want to shut the bathroom door when you were using ... the facilities, the door was pretty much in your face. Nice amenities such as shampoo, etc. The room was very quiet, being high enough that the street noise, which can be quite cacophonous, was almost completyely deadened. There were also nice thick curtains which could cut out all the bright lights from the Times Square side of my corner room. I didn't use the expensive internet in the room, but later in my stay used the business center which gave me everything I needed in internet use for a lot less. Now the only complaint I have from here on is the bar and restaurant employees. In the restaurant I was given uncaring service, but in the bar it was surly, snotty and not at all pleasant. I know I arrived at the bar fairly late on a Saturday night, but when I was told in no uncertain terms that the bar was closed, and they weren't even pleasant about it, and when I found that the "official" information of the hotel said the bar would be open until 1 a.m. on Saturday night, I was very unhappy. At least the desk clerk gave me two free drinks for the next day. Believe me I used those coupons, even though I ended up not drinking both of them, and the hotel had to pay for them PLUS the fact that the bartender had been so nasty meant he did not get a tip. How much easier it would have been had they kept the bar open until the time they were supposed to keep it open. The old excuse, "well, we just haven't changed our brochure" does NOT work! Everything else at the hotel was fine. The staff was very friendly and helpful except, as I've noted, the bartender. Everything else was up to the standard one should be able to expect from a first class chain like Hilton. One more thing: at least I was not charged for the one night at the other hotel. I would probably stay here again, and there will be plenty of chances, as I travel to New York quite often for the theater and opera. One more little comment: it would be far nicer to have everything the way you want it rather than to have them give you complimentary breakfasts or other such things by way of making you feel better about bad things that happened.

“Headhouse Tower” Did a Sat. night stay, got a great prepaid Marriott Rewards Members rate directly thru Marriott website. The hotel is huge, modern, clean and at a perfect downtown location. When Marriott emails Rewards Members virtual concierge reminders for upcoming stays, I requested a room in the adjacent Headhouse Tower based on other TA reviews. Staff was friendly at check in, and we were informed that we had received a room in Tower. You take an escalator up 1 level and then walk across a catwalk. King room was HUGE, and according to the Marriott maintenance people working on my floor was twice the size of a king room in the regular building. Everything in Tower was brand new, even the hallway carpet smelled new. Room was spotless, 15 foot ceilings with a separate living room area with sofa, chairs and coffee table. Bed and bathroom were both great. Plenty of good restaurants in area (stay away from the chains and try Marmont Steakhouse), and one of the parking valet guys even told us what street to walk down for our dinner reservation, since he thought it was safer. Everyone on TA says parking is way too expensive, go to centralparking.com and print out coupon. Garage 2 blocks from Marriott (up the street from Loews Hotel) was only $5 for overnight weekend valet parking with coupon. I will stay here again in future.

“Great Affordable Hotel in Excellent Memphis Location!” I spent one night at this hotel on a road trip to New Orleans, and upon a return to Memphis, I would not hesitate to stay here again. This hotel is very clean, with a friendly and accommodating staff. One of the best things about this hotel is its proximity to Beale Street-- it's right around the corner. You can partake in all the clubs, restaurants and action of the area, and be back at your hotel (on foot) in a matter of minutes. Also, in case anyone is interested, it's also very close to Memphis' Orpheum Theatre, in case somone needs to come to town and catch a "Broadway" show, or concert, etc... I highly recommend this hotel if you're looking for clean, comfortable lodging, right in the center of the liveliest area of Memphis!

“Excellent option in Chicago” A great choice- well located and well priced. The rooms are brand new and the facilities are great. Hotel is paperless so that I found unique and the gym/ spa facilities are great- even have an outdoor running track! Highly recommended and just a good hotel- well done!

“Fabulous hotel, bring a white noise machine to sleep” This is a great hotel. However on windy nights, there is an incredibly annoying creaking noise. Seeing as Chicago is called The Windy City, this is a problem. Download a white noise iPhone application, use the ear plugs they provide and you might be OK. Light sleepers should my favorite hotel in Chicago -- The Talbot.

“Had a good time with family” After some problems with a connecting room, Sarah was very helpful in getting my entire family (19) into convenient rooms. The connecting rooms with an oversized standard king is fantastic. More than enough room in our King Suite with bath and kitchenette in front. The other King Suite was a little cramped. Very, very friendly staff. Pool a little small, morning buffet was excellent but evening could use a little more veggie friendly additions. Free coctails not very big but welcome after dealing with 11 small children. Will be better when San Antonio finishes their lengthy construction on 281 and 1604.

“Design oriented boutique” We spent 5 nights at the Adagio. We booked an executive corner room. This was touted as having wondeful city views - it didn't! We had a room on the 12th floor at the rear of the building. One side faced a large flat roof and a few apartment blocks. The other actually faced the neighbouring empty building. When this is occupied your neighbours are going to be pretty close and personal! Other than that you should know that this is very much a design led boutique hotel. It's form over function in every respect (and if you like practical over fancy then this place may drive you nuts). The bathroom has lovely Aveda products to use, but the shower is a dud. No settings and not great water pressure. There is no where to have breakfast in the hotel, but there are several options within walking distance. They provide free coffee and tea in the lobby, but not in the evenings (which is just when I fancied a cuppa). Location is OK I guess. It's close to Union Square and near large hotels like the Hilton and Parc55. However, anyone who knows the city will know that these are very close to Tenderloin. This is the city's roughest and most unsavoury area. Adagio is only a block away from all this, so make sure you head towards Union Square everytime you leave the hotel. (Also as an aside, I would say that anyone with kids should to avoid this hotel. There's really nothing there for them.) I have visited the city numerous times and have stayed in quite a few of the hotels. I can't really say that I recommend this hotel to anyone other than young hipster types. Older guests and families just don't quite fit in with the mood of this place.

“From Hero to Zero in just over a year” I have stayed that the Times Square Crowne Plaza two or three times a year for about five years, and have written reviews about it before. I think this may be my last stay. I used to love the hotel, but it's gone down hill. I arrived earlier than the 3 PM check-in time and my room was not ready. That's fine: I had no expectations that it would be. But the relish with which the front desk clerk told me this, and then the joy she had telling me that "we used to upgrade platinum members but we stopped" was really offputting. It was as though she was waiting for the opportunity to put a frequent guest in his place by reporting that things had changed. And on her lapel she was called "Front Desk Trainer". This kind of surly, service with a snarl was fairly frequent; perhaps half the staff did their job but without any kindness. There were gems though: the woman who checked me out caught a billing error I missed, and one of the bellmen was great. But for hundreds of dollars a night I'd expect more consistent warmth. The room felt dirty and was not properly cleaned. The coffee maker was wet when I looked at it when I arrived, and soap was not replaced, nor trash removed, during my stay. The internet was unusable. I believe that guest usage has outstripped the hotel's bandwidth and it needs to be expanded. The room was musty when I arrived and just did not feel clean. When I checked in (after 3 PM) the woman at the front desk told me that the internet was complementary with my rate plan. But the internet was on my bill when it was slipped under my door. I did not notice this, but the clerk at the desk at check-out did: she told me that it happens all the time and she looks for it to reverse the charge, which she did. I wonder how many people just pay for the internet not realizing that is a mistaken charge. Anyway, for years I've looked forward to my stays here. Now I am looking for an alternative place to stay.
“Unbeatable convenience” Incredible location, not bad for a hotel in the airport. Rooms are a bit dark and small, but otherwise friendly staff and good service.

“Ottimo hotel posizione non proprio ideale” Ottimo hotel posizione non proprio ideale in quanto collocato in prossimità della stazione centrale. Consente di raggiungere i principali negozi e di scendere a Soho. Un po' lontano dal parco e quindi non ideale per chi vuole fare running la mattina; in questo caso unica alternativa è di scendere in zona ONU. Modernissimo con stanze techno dotate di tutti i confort, stanze pulite ma proprio la pulizia potrebbe essere migliorata (un po' di polvere qua e la'). Discreto servizio ristorante e discreta palestra.

“basic hotel” This is a basic hotel so don't expect too much. When we first walked in the room there was a musty smell. The smell went away after we turned on the air conditioner. The cons are the room is small, there was a $3 charge for the in room safe, 4/5 lights did not work....only the bathroom light and desk light worked, the continental breakfast was very basic of cereal, bread and packaged muffins, the bed was newer but very cheap. This motel is in the poorer area of the city and yes there can be "poorer people" in the area but not always. The pros was that it was clean, wireless internet worked and we were at the end of the hotel, bus #174 is a bus that runs from the airport to downtown and the new light rail station is a 3 minute walk, there is a microwave and fridge. Would I stay here again? Well I paid $55 with a coupon so you have to compare what you are paying and what you get. I checked the prices of motel 6 and americas best value based on one of the reviews and their regular rate is $55 to 59 so I should have tried them instead.

“Excellent In All Respects” This is a superb hotel and part of an excellent group (although do not go for the Pear Tree Inns which are not as good). We had a two roomed suite which was roomy, clean and had everything we could wish for except crockery and cutlery. However, as is the norm in this group and others in the USA, paper plates and plastic cutlery are readily available in the bar/breakfast area. We loved the free drinks and nibbles in the early evening, and the complimentary breakfast was great with plenty of choice. There are a selection of chain restaurants nearby. Don't expect 5 star hotel service but for friendly, efficient service and comfort, I would always choose this hotel if in the area again. Only an hour's drive from her to Luckenbach, which Country & Western fans will know all about.
“Great value” Large very roomy suites. Great price for AAA members over $100 off. I've stayed before and will come again.

“Decent Property near airport” I stayed here one night prior to outbound flight. Shuttle was good, runs every 1/2 hour. Some areas of hotel shows signs of high use. Such as carpets and walls. There are worse properties out there. Good service. Decent beding. fairly clean. Some highway and airport noise, but tolerable. Notice warning of numerous vehicle break ins attached to key was concerning, although i had no issues.

“Outstanding, again!” We stayed in 2006 and have been at many different hotels in NYC. Our favotites are now any Affinia (best for small groups or families as the space is LARGE) and W New York as a COUPLE! Again, this lobby and hotel were very hip, "Sex in the City" youngish, professional 25-50 crowd. Room was EXCELLENT, right down to special features like nice robes and FREE luxury bath products from the BLISS spa (on site). If you plan to visit the spa, plan ahead and make reservations NOW as they were very busy, as BLISS is one of the best spas in town, known to NYC locals as well. The small room is more than made up for - by the EXCELLENMT AMENITIES: Plasma TV, bath prodcuts, CLEANILNESS, and service! Nice desk with internet, CD player, DVD, TV, etc. The bed, is in fact, HEAVENLY, as the advertising suggests. Nice mood, throughout the hotel. Excellent, large work-out facility, with personal training available, as well as a BLISS spa on-site (no pool). Free access to steam room and gym, even without SPA service. Drinks and small meals and apps are available in the lobby bar, as well as desserts. They were were very good at $12-15 per cocktail, but well worth it for the atmosphere and people watching and the fireplace. If your are a SCOTCH specialiast, the WHISKEY BLUE bar is on site with many speciatlity and single malt Scotch offerings. ($12+). GREAT location, on Lexington at 49th. Five minute walk to Grand Central. 10 minutes to Rockefeller Center, 20 minites the theatre district. Very active lobby with free Granny Smith apples and champagne (at specific times)! Helpful and cheerful front desk and concierge desk. Enjoy your stay at this EXCELLENT hotel! We will return, again! In fact, this has become our destination of choice for NYC, most due to the attention to detail provided by Ed, SAMI, and JASON - W SuperSTARS!. THANK YOU! Our HIGHEST recommendation, ever. A+++++++++.

“Håller bra standard” Börjar bli lite ålderstiget men håller fortfarande bra kvalitet. Läget är bra med gångavstånd både till Michigan Av och Navy Pier. Bra executive rum och en frukost som ej gör en besviken. Luftig och behaglig lobby med bra personal. Ett plus för baren som är härlig att slå sig ner i vid efter en hel arbetsdag

“Great Value, Location, Amenities!” My wife and I were in Boston for three nights to see a Red Sox game and do some other sightseeing. I had never been to Boston before and really had no idea about hotels, but I kept coming back to the Hotel Buckminster. I had read some very mixed reviews on TripAdvisor and was a little hesitant going in, but the price was right and location couldn't be beat, so we gave it a shot. We were expecting an old, archaic type building but were pleasantly surprised to see the inside was quite modern and welcoming. The front desk staff was extremely pleasant and helpful and we were granted our request for a room facing Fenway Park! The room was perfect, far beyond what we anticipated after reading some other reviews on here. The view was great and the room was clean, cool, and comfortable. We were happy to have a fridge and microwave in the room as well. It also benefited us to have a laundry room with coin-operated washer/dryer right next to our room as we were in need of doing laundry. The location was great, literally right across the street from Fenway Park, and within a block of the Kenmore subway station. There were a lot of great bars and restaurants right within walking distance. The price was reasonable considering other options in the area. I think we paid $545 for 3 nights. I can't really think of any complaints or anything negative at all. The continental breakfast was a little weak, but adequate. Overall great experience. Would definitely stay here again!

“Defnitely a rip off!” Overall, this hotel is over rated and nothing but hype! The quality and service definitely do not measure up to its "reputation". My partner and I arrive at the hotel after a 18-hour long flight at 8am. Despite our request through email for an early check-in, we were told to come back at 3pm. In their own words, "it's only a request". Can you imagine that we had to comb the streets of new york looking like zombies?? The receptionist was not helpful at all. The hotel was not well kept. The carpets (along the corridor and room) and the place just look OLD! When we finally got the room, it was not the colour theme that we had requested for (if they can't get this right, why bother to ask us in the first place when we did our booking?). But that was the last thing on our mind since we were both dead tired. The first impression of the room was BAD! Carpet is dirty (I wonder how often do they vacuum clean the carpet!). Necessities such as the bedroom slippers are also missing. The toilet door is faulty. The sheets are not even neatly pressed. The gym is pathetic! The treadmill's really old and they have limited equipments. It's okay if you just want a quick cardio exercise and get out of the tiny room or gym . Don't bother about the in-house breakfast! It's US$15 for a continental breakfast... way too pricey. Thank goodness, we didn't pay for the over-priced meal. My recommendation is try the deli around the area. Starbucks, Food Empire and McDonald's are just round the corner. I wonder how on earth does the hotel justify its rates?? There are better hotels in that area. The only consolation is that the hotel is located in a prime area and is near to the subway. The asian doorman is really helpful and friendly (the rest of the staff does not even know what does good service entail). Frankly, the review would have been better if the room rates were at 3-star prices (or even 2-star). Unfortunately, it's not the case. Having stayed at better hotels around the world, the Time DOES NOT offer good value for money. We will defnitely not return to this hotel. A hip hotel? Definitely far from it!

“FIND SOMEPLACE ELSE!!!!!!!!!” I am a business traveler who stays at hotels 50+ nights a year. This place is the worst. OLD and in bad need of upgrading to the elevators, plumbing and cooling systems. My room was so stuffy and musty that the assistant manager called it "suffocating" when he came up to see why I was complaining. They moved me to a new room and the cooling systems was sub-par and the plumber had to address shower issues twice. I rarely complain but these problems were unacceptable. Never did a manager call and say sorry for all the problems. Never did they offer a complimentary breakfast. Truth is they don't care, they are busy with wedding and convention business and could care less. They don't care about repeat business. Also, the elevators are so slow that you must allow extra time if you need to be somewhere on time. If you need to be in this area, stay at the W across the street or the Marriott Eastside.

“Great for the price!” Stayed here two nights with my husband at the end of December (Wed and Thurs). We checked in around 10:30pm without any issues. It was quick and easy. They did tell us that parking would be $10/day and internet was $9.95 or $14.95 depending on which speed you wanted. We were assigned a room on the third floor, king bed, non smoking. Our room was great. There is a living room with couch, desk, and TV that is separated from the bedroom and bathroom. There is a little sink area outside of the bathroom with mini fridge and microwave. The bedroom was a little small. The bed took up most of the space, but it was fine. The bathroom was average in size and came with crabtree & evelyn shampoo/conditioner/soap/body wash. Do keep in mind that there is a train nearby in the area and you will hear it periodically throughout your stay. You will also hear noise in the atrium if you are in the living room area. We couldn't hear the atrium from the bedroom. This seems to be the hotel of choice for high school and college teams. There were a bunch of teenagers gathering in the lobby and atrium area at night talking and having fun. Breakfast during the weekdays is from 6-9am. I don't know why breakfast ends so early on the weekdays. On the weekends, breakfast is served from 7-10am. We had breakfast on one day and it was really good. There was a line for the hot food, where they take your omelet order. You also get to choose from pancakes, hashbrowns, scrambled eggs, sausage, and bacon. There is also the usual stuff like muffins, yogurt, and fresh fruit. It's a really decent breakfast with good selection. There seemed to be enough seating for everyone. If you miss breakfast, there is a bunch of fast food restaurants down the road. I think I saw a Jack in the Box and Taco Bell and a 7-11 store. The hotel is also close to Southcenter Shopping mall, a Target, and Costco. The hotel is right off the 405. We found the hotel's location to be very convenient. Parking spaces are a little cramped and some cars parked crooked or took up 2 spaces. It was a little annoying having to pay extra for parking when there is a lot of parking available. I also think that internet should be complimentary. We got this hotel through priceline for $41/night. It's a great deal and would stay again for that price.

“A wonderful choice, especially if you can snag a good deal on the price” My first choice for a place to stay in NYC is the Affinia Manhattan. Sometimes you can get a really deals through Hotels.com or directly through the Affinia booking site (which has a best deal guarantee). For the same price or less than a regular room at many other 4-star hotels, you can get a studio suite or a one bedroom suite. The hotel is perfectly located if you are coming in and out from Penn Station (it's across the street) easy to get to other parts of NYC by subway. It's not so long a walk to the theater district, about a half mile. The hotel staff is competent and housekeeping was pretty swift with requests for extra towels. The only reason I don't stay here every time I go to NYC is that sometimes the good deals are not available, and it can be pricey during a heavy demand time of year. (Or sold out when the price is most attractive). There is a charge to use the internet, though. If I could change one thing about the hotel, it would be to offer free wifi.

“Very convenient, pretty restful hotel” Only here for 2 days and nights, it was pretty convenient to my office location. There was a girls’ volleyball tournament nearby so the place was crawling with teenagers with minimal adult supervision. That said, it was still fairly quiet and I never had any complaints about noise. There are several other hotels on the same street and several restaurants and a movie theatre nearby for dining and entertainment. Not a bad stay at all.

“Good Stay” I stayed at the Marriott Wardman Park in early June for a conference. The hotel gets high marks for convenience. It's right next to a Metro station, making it a great starting point for sightseeing. The National Zoo is within walking distance. There are lots of cafes and restaurants in the area, too. I had a room in the renovated tower. Though the bathroom was small, the room itself was nice. My room overlooked the a/c unit, so there was no traffic noise. The only real complaint I had was about signage and directions to the fitness center. The sign in the elevator and the note in the hotel directory both said the fitness center was on the second floor. I wandered around for a few minutes before I realized both were wrong. It's on the first floor. The signs need to be changed. I did not eat the food in the hotel, though I hear it's not bad. I'd stay here again.

“a room with hi-tech features” The hotel is located in mid town area of Mahanttan and about a mile from Times Square. The location is fantastic as it is close to many restaurants (located in lexington ave) and shopping areas such as Macy which is half a mile from the hotel. This is a boutique hotel which has huge round shaped marine aquarium and a beautiful corridors. The check in was not very smooth as we were in for shock when the reception staff told us they could not locate our booking which was done thru expedia even though we had the confirmation, and there are no rooms available at that time. After talking to expedia directly, the matter was finally resolved at the intervention of the Hotel Manager, Mr. Benjamin who informed us personally that we will will able to check in and our room will be upgraded to superior room. He also apologised for the delay which lasted for about Hour and half. The room was in the sixth floor, corner of the buliding with full size windows on both sides which provided excellent view on both sides outside. It had hitech features such as mirror with lights and small TV screen in it in the bathroom, bath tub with Jacuzzi, button to open curtains near the bedside, electronic display button for do not disturb & for house keepin, etc. The mattresses and the pillows were fantastic and the lights in the room were excellent and much more than sufficient. As our flight was late in th evening, the hotel cocierge staff were glad to keep our luggage in the storage area. At the the time of check out, Mr, Benjamin, Hotel manger enquired about our stay at the hotel and informed that he is looking forward to welcome us at the hotel next time. One area of improvement is certainly the reception staff who I think should be more friendly and provide service with a smile. I will certainly stay here next time I visit New York.

“Friendly Hurricane Sandy shelter” We were supposed to depart the day Sandy hit NYC, and had to extend our stay a couple extra days due to flight cancellations. The staff were friendly, helping us bring our luggage to our rooms. Checkin was efficient through the machine. The double set of elevators is a little annoying, but we never had to wait long. The rooms were sufficient and fairly well designed, for the price it was worth a stay. Location is pretty easy to get a taxi at, but a 10-15 min walk to the nearest subway station.

“Classy Hotel” The Peabody lives up to it's reputation as THE place to stay in Memphis. I booked on priceline and after reading the reviews here on tripadvisor, i was hoping to get the westin. But, when priceline accepted our bid and we got the Peabody. As others mentioned, the hotel architecture and lobby is amazing. However, my experience with the check-in was perfect--no line up and a very nice staff person. I had requested a coffee maker and they brought it to the room within 15 mins of our check-in. The room was lovely--large big screen LG tv with high def and nice furniture and decorating. The washroom is a bit tiny, but managable. I would definitely recommend staying at the Peabody!! There is a separate $10 per day charge for wireless internet, newspaper and free local calls. Unfortunately, there is nothing that you can do about this. And, we opted for the valet parking ($21) vs. self-park ($16) after reading about some potential problems with safety issues if you find your own parking. Overall, i would definitely stay here again--it's great.

“Luxury Hotel meets expectations” We spent two nights here in January 2012 in connecting rooms (a suite connected to a regular room) which was a great set up for our family. We had a spacious living room in between the two bedrooms. The hotel is pricey but it was a good value for the space and the location and quality. We had breakfast in the hotel one day and it was disappointing. A basic buffet and overpriced a la carte entrees in a room without atmosphere (in the AM). Drinks at the bar in the evening was much more pleasant. Go out for breakfast. There are lots of options nearby. The fitness center was not big but sufficient and clean. Of course, the location is outstanding. The service was very good overall.

“Good Hotel, Just A Little Far Out” This is a nice little hotel, with really friendly staff that will help you anyway they can. We had an issue with the people in the room next door, and we were literally moved that same day to the other side of the hotel with no problems whatsoever. The only issue i had is that although it's near the Golden Gate Bridge, some rooms have a slight view, it's pretty far out from everything else! Taxi's dont cost too much though, so if being far out doesnt bother you then stay here! There was parking available although we didn't use it, and there is no free internet - you have to pay for that. The rooms were clean and tidy though, although we were concerned with the space around the door and i imagine that would create quite a draft in the cooler months.

“Good value, good location, very friendly staff” We stayed at the w on our first 3 nights in san diego. We arrived quite late on the first night and were welcomed very cheerfull and warm. We got a room on the 9th floor. The rooms are ok size. The decor is great! The beds are really comfy and the bathroom we had was huge. One downside is that the waterpressure of the shower is really low. So no nice hot shower. Wifi is good, fast and free in the lobby. Location is good. Just around the corner of little italy, the trolleystop and the ferry to coronado. Forcpartying you should find a hotel more to the gaslamp quarter.

“Attentive Staff, Spacious Suites” This is a great hotel for couples, singles, or girls' weekend. We had a corner junior suite, which was very spacious. The suite comfortable and they also have a Keurig, which is what we have at home. The service was great, from the valets to the front desk. We had the breakfast buffet, for the price you can't beat it. We also at dinner at the restaurant one night (I wouldn't recommend the calamari). All in all, good stay, excellent location if you want to shop at the Galleria Mall. It's trendy, and although I saw families there, I wouldn't bring young kids. We were able to get a great rate of $79 per night.

“Will stay here again!” We booked a hotel near NYU and completely hated it and we went to Priceline.com and got this room. MAJOR UPGRADE! OK, it had a hair dryer which means a lot to me! This hotel is one block from Grand Central Station and easy to get a cab anywhere in the city. The staff was nice - a little too responsive, but that isn't a bad thing. Rooms where clean and well taken care of. We where on the 7th floor and the rooms weren't tired. Being that I stayed in many NYC hotels over the years, this was one of the nicest. Seriously, how long are you in the room when you are in the city?? The line at check in was long, but it was a Friday and expected. Check out was fast and easy and they held our luggage until our flight later in the day. The only sad thing is the hotel is booked for our next trip in December to the city! For $100 a night we where pleased!

“Overall a nice stay” Stayed at the Universal City Hilton last night rather than drive home after a concert at the Gibson Amphitheatre. The staff at the hotel were very attentive and pleasant. The room was spacious and comfortable. We ordered room service after the concert and it was promptly delivered and good. The beds were comfortable. The only down side was the bathrooms. The room does not have hair dryers and we had a issue with the shower (couldn't get cold water or turn it off). Engineering showed up quickly to remedy the situation. With that in mind, I would not hesitate to stay at the Hilton again.

“great place” As a frequent and impatient traveler, I have a few odd quirks that I look for in a hotel. First, I hate paying for parking, second, is there a nice food option available within walking distance, and finally and perhaps most important, can I get in a decent run in the early AM. With those challenges, this makes staying in Houston somewhat difficult esp.. the running part. This hotel meets those criteria. Great choices to eat across the streets (Red Onion) and there is a very nice residential neighborhood within a half mile so one can easy get a 5 miler in the early AM with lighted streets. Parking is great and (free)...this is a nearly renovated hotel. Nice lobby and rooms are clean. Located off 1-10 it give you access to many points in Houston. People were friendly--off course its Texas ya'll--and I had not problems. This has become my permanent Houston place to stay. This is not luxury but very practical.

“Great Value” This was my first time at the Sofitel. I have stayed at many NYC hotels, and I think that this is my favorite overall. I have stayed in rooms that cost twice as much that were not as beautiful, clean, and quiet as this one. Our twin room was fairly large and very clean. The bathroom was beautiful, well laid-out, and spotless. I was surprised at how quiet the hotel was. We slept very well and did not hear a sound all night long - not from other guest rooms nor from the street. I will definitely try to stay here on my next visit to NYC.

“good, could be better” good and not as good - i stayed many times here and am hilton gold. convenient location to everything, kimmel Center, rittenhouse, washington sq west. restaurants, theater and easy access Braod street line to stadiums. rooms, nice, typical Dble Tree. Bar - terrible, one of the worst hotel bars. concierge lounge, below average. low tables and attendee uniterested. this past stay, they have a new hilton honors check in. you are asked to go to the desk which is also a concierge and wait for your packet. Meanwhile, the front desk is handling non honors guests at a much faster pace siince there are more agents and quite frankly checkking somone in takes less time then giving directions and advice. My advice, remove the honors check in. i waited behind someone for quite some time and ended up going back to the front desk. the front desk person treated me rudely and said my packet was over at the other desk and i would have to wait for someone to get it. Really odd as a gold to be treated that way. bottom line, good location, good price, need to get back to treating better customers properly and please improve the bar.
“Great Facility” Great value. super location. Staff was extremely nice and helpful. Room was somewhat small but well maintained.

“The updated Casitas are great!” I stayed at the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak May 1-3 on a business trip and was able to book a low pre-pay rate thru the Hilton website. Upon check-in, I was upgraded from a king room to a king Casita since I'm a Hilton Diamond member. The first Casita they gave me smelled old and musty and looked very dated so I called the front desk to see if I could get a casita that didn't smell. They switched me to a newly renovated Casita which was leaps and bounds better than the initial one I had. New, contemporary furnishings, flat screen TV, new carpet, updated bathrooms-granite countertops, etc. Great view of the mountains from the upstairs bedroom. I really liked having a covered parking space-almost like a garage to keep your car out of the hot sun. The pools are terrific and the property is beautiful. I found the property to be very quiet and it felt like we were miles away from the city even though the airport and downtown Phoenix are both about 15 minutes away w/o traffic. The staff at Hole in the Wall was very friendly and eager to please. Good breakfast there too. I really hope to be able to return to this hotel again soon. One of the more impressive Hiltons I've visited.

“Enjoyable stay” I stayed at this hotel on business in January, 2010. I wasn't blown away by the hotel, but I thought that it was pretty nice and it met my expectations. If you like big, tall, urban hotels with glass elevators and that business-like (but not necessarily "hip") vibe, you'll like this hotel. My room was one one of the higher floors and was in nice condition; the bed was very comfortable and everything was in good working order. I thought the hotel had pretty good style. I worked in the atrium one night and enjoyed the change of pace. I thought the service in the restaurant at breakfast was excellent, and the buffet was good. I was very impressed with the fitness center. The service at check-in was a bit slow, but polite. I had dinner one night at the Wolfgang Puck restaurant that is in the ball-shaped tower next to the hotel, and that was great.

“'Nice little find” The last few Christmas' my husband and I have spent a day Christmas shopping and then spent the night in a somewhat local hotel ... kind of a little getaway during the hectic Holidays. This year we choose Hotel Indigo in downtown Dallas. On the outside the hotel looks old and stately (it HAS been there a long time). But once you walk in the door you are transformed to a bright, cheerful updated interior. Everything is done in blues, yellows and greens. There are alot of beach motifs. On a gray December afternoon it was quite a transformation. We loved it. We stayed on a Monday night so it was very quiet. Our room was a little small but everything was updated and very comfortable. The bed was VERY comfortable and plush. Hotel Indigo was a nice little find! 'Very relaxing and cozy after a long day of shopping.

“Great design, but location is far from Times Square” Stayed in Premium View cabin for three nights.ergonomics of the room is amazing, you can find place for all your stuff-bags, coats, clothes, computers, cosmetics and whatsoever. Hotel is brand new and still clean, but materials used for rooms are not of the best quality, which is obviously seen by the stains on washbasin, which can't be washed away. Free coffee is available. on every floor. Location, though claimed to be near Times Square (as can be implied from the name), is pretty far from the latter. Takes you about 15 minutes of walking in the suburbs which are far from friendly. Still, very nice and yobot which takes care of your bags is pure fun. One more thing-don't put any of your stuff under the bed! Mechanism folding the bed tends to chew things in- lost my fav blouse, because of it (((

“Nice hotel in a nice location.” This is a very nice, clean and huge hotel. They've got several sections to the hotel, so it's like walking through the airport to get to your room. The service is excellent. One of the gals at a service desk in the West Tower actually checked me in. The room was clean and very nice. I had a king bed, sort of corner room (room 951). One entire wall was windows, almost floor to ceiling. I was near an elevator, so that caused a bit of night time noise, but not much. Overall, the hotel is very quiet. Special marks for the bathroom. I loved it. Spacious shower/tub, marble floors, backlit mirrors, and very large. One other good point about such a large hotel is that they have a huge lobby bar. I walked by and thought it was a concert. There was dueling pianos, dancing people, and plenty of libations going around. Looked like a really fun place if you wanted to stay close for the night. As far as attractions, well, it's right corner to Michigan Ave and just across the river from the whole River North area. If you can't find something to do there, well...then you don't need this review. The only low mark I'd give would be regarding the hotel's proximity to parking. There is public parking close by, but it's easy to get yourself twisted around on Lower Wacker or Michigan Ave searching for it. Overall, I'd say this is a great hotel for just about anyone's needs. Whether you be traveling alone like me, for business, or with your family, you can't go wrong here.

“Everything you could ask for...and more!” I've stayed at the Sherry several times the past year. They have a BOX of chocolates in your room with a personal note. The rooms and suites are immaculate. They sent a Christmas card. I need not say any more! Oh, yes, the service is top notch...always.

“Great place at the airport!” All you have to do, is step out of baggage claim and you are there! You only hear airport noise if you are walking around outside. Pool is to die for! Great big pool and waterslide AND kid pool. Best out there! Staff was very helpful. Rooms were nice and big. Beds were ok. The only con I have is that the Breakfast Buffet was not very good... On the other hand, the lounge and lounge staff was GREAT!!!!!! Overall, a winner in El Paso!

“"THE" great low profile place to stay in LA” Stayed 7 nights & loved it:- Very friendly & efficient staff, nice elegant room (too bad 107 had no view) free wifi, good no frills breakfast, happy hour and long list of emenities. This boutique hotel offers all ypu need for a pleasant stay. Great location for business or shopping. Good restaurants and diners near the Elan. After the horrible experience at the nearby Orlando hotel last year, will go back to the Elan anytime.

“Excellent hotel, Highly recommended!!!” Stayed at the HI Express Boston for 3 nights in June 2006. This was a really amazing hotel!!! The staff are extremely helpful with questions about sightseeing or attractions. Lobby is huge and beautiful with an Internet station for checking email. There is a huge, clean, wonderful breakfast area for the delicious breakfast served--tons of choices including warm cinnamon rolls. Besides being used for breakfast, you can use this great seating area throughout the day to lounge, meet friends, or watch the large TV. I loved that coffee, tea, and hot chocolate were served 24 hours a day AND warm cookies were served in the evenings. Entire hotel is clean, well-kept, modern, and stylish. Area appears safe for walking around, at least in the daytime (not sure about after dark). Parking is free (saving you tons of money in Boston). My room, although quite small, was super clean and modern. The Beantown Trolley will pick you up in the morning right in front of the hotel, take you downtown and to all major sights, and then take you back to the hotel in the early evening (just call them to confirm a pickup). Or you can take the T (I didn't take the T from the hotel, but I think the station is pretty close, within walking distance). So with these options you can basically avoid driving in Boston, which is total chaos. The hotel has a nice location next to a huge shopping center with Target if you forget any necessities. Now for the downsides.....you are definitely not in the downtown area, but like I mentioned the public transportation is convenient and easy and will get you downtown in no time. Another thing I didn't like was that my room was $125 per night, higher than I usually pay. But this was one of the absolute cheapest rates I could find in Boston. Plus the free parking made this rate worth it. One other note is that, as mentioned above, driving in Boston is insane, and I thought the hotel was difficult to find. Then when exiting, you can only turn right and this could be confusing. I suggest not using your car until you check out! Lastly, my room really had no view and my windows wouldn't open (next time I would ask to face the downtown, maybe those rooms had better views). But the windows that don't open drive me crazy!! Overall the positives outweigh the negatives and I would definitely stay here again when visiting Boston.

“Great Location” I stayed here with my boys the night before an early flight out of Boston Logan. We arrived around 5 PM and the boys found the T station an easy walk and headed into Boston for a few hours. I decided to stay back and head to the local shopping area behind the hotel. There is some decent shopping and a few casual restraunts within the short walk. The boys took the free shuttle to the T but just walked on there return said it was completely safe and a short walk. The rooms were clean and appeared to be updated. Front desk staff was friendly and professional. I would stay here again in the future.

“Really great service, very good value, good location, nice rooms!” Have stayed here a few times over the last few years, but first time under this management and I have to say that the service was super great! The staff could not have been more helpful or courteous, the location in Japan town is wonderful, with plenty of amenities nearby. The rooms well decorated and clean, overall very good value for money.

“Depends on what you're looking for!” Really off the beaten path. I needed a room fairly quickly, and needed to be uptown. This hotel was reasonable for Marriott in Manhattan (i.e.< $400). It is very miuch in a residential neighborhood, but there are places to eat nearby. It is VERY far on the East Side, and no easy way to get to anything touristy. The staff was very friendly, and the room was adequate. Small, but comfortable, with very comfortable bed. Very quiet. There is also a small bar/restaurant in the lobby which was suprisingly good. In summary, it is an average hotel. Stay here if the price is right, if the location works for you, or if you need to be on the East Side.

“the view is too good to waste your time sleeping...” Our room was a little 'cozy', but well-designed ,and had a great minimalist retro style. The rooftop Boom Boom Room bar (not sure if this is officially part of the hotel or not, but it is an essential part of the Standard experience) was awesome. The highlight though was the view from our Liberty Room. Watching sunset over NYC was superb, then the city lights at nightime, and then dawn over the Hudson... all added up to a 'well-deserved Pink' rating on the neilsonparc Lust List.

“A Very Strange Hotel Prefer the Teatro by Far” I thought for Valentines Day and my one year anniversary with my partner we would splurge and stay at the Brown's because of its historical appeal. I wanted to stay in the Teatro however, I thought I would give this a shot because I ALWAYS stay at the Teatro in Denver. However, my heart still stays with the Hotel Teatro. It is simply not up to par with the Teatro at all. The service does not feel as personalized. The Sunday brunch was mediocre at best that we attended. The room was huge however, just very very dated compared to other hotels in the area. The car service was not very well organized compared to the Teatro. The furniture in the hotel lobby was embarrassing because some of the legs were missing off of the chairs. The beds were not very comfortable I found. The sheets were too scratchy for me and the bed cover generated so much static and often shocked me. I think the Brown's has appeal to another generation, just not my style at all. A little too old and not up to par with other hotels in Denver. Overall to be honest it is a FAIR hotel nothing very special.

“Textbook HGI in a great location” Advantages: - Great Center City location - Good value - Clean - Good work area - Each room has refrigerator and microwave - Helpful staff - Wired Ethernet for Internet Disadvantages: - None that I can think of

“Good location, unfriendly staff” This is an average hotel. I stayed here for 2 nights. I go to New York about twice a year to visit family so therefore am familiar with the city. I booked here based on the reviews but guess people have difffent expectations. My experiences were as follows: Pros: Good location, close to 2 subway lines. King size room which was small but clean. Breakfast was nothing to write home about in a very crowded room. Cons: The staff. This was the most unfriendly, unhelpful staff that I have encountered. Luckily, I did not require much service. The review which said not to get a taxi from the front desk was vey helpful. They get you a private car which costs a lot more. Also, no computer in lobby to print off boarding passes. The management here has a flyer that says they encourage especially postive reviews. Well, they are something that have to be earned and a friendly staff would help greatly. I had a fanastic time in New York but I will try somewhere else next time.

“Arrived on short notice” My plan yesterday was to travel by train Washington to Chicago and continue to Arizona. Three hours before departure, Amtrak called me that the train was cancelled. Not wanting to ride Greyhound overnight, I quickly booked a one way flight to Chicago, and figuring that Amtrak owes me a hefty refund, booked the Hotel Monaco, so these should balance out. I was delighted with the Hotel Monaco, this being the third Kimpton Hotel in which i have stayed. I appreciate their sleek, artsistic decor and nice little touches. The staff were most helpful and I was recommended Andy's Jazz Club a few blocks away, where I spent an enjoyable evening. Referring to some of the other reviewers comments, I was on the back of the building and looked into a bick wall. Not a problem - the room was gorgeous. Now I don't mean to be too picky, but for the price of the room I do note these two items: the curtains did not completely close and the bathtub was very ordinary looking. Considering the thoughtful decor and fixtures, I am surprised that they decided to leave a bathtub which looked like the house I grew up in. Small matters - even though my travel plans were changed, my time in Chicago has been very good.

“Great Times Square Hotel” I absolutely love staying in Times Square so this hotel proved to be great. I found the service excellent and attentive. The beds are comfortable and a great place for a weekend getaway. Close to Broadway shows and shopping. Loved the place and will go back!!!

“Consistently good” I stayed based on the recommendation of a coworker who has used this hotel about monthly for the past few years. I stayed four nights in the past two weeks. The rooms are nice, clean, the front desk is professional, friendly and competent. Room service works like a charm - fast hot good quality food. The lobby restaurant is good for breakfast but there are less expensive options In the food court area. The Boniventure lounge is a great view with excellent service.

“Decent hotel with poor housekeeping” Stayed for four nights. Rooms are newly renovated, clean, flat screen HD TV and complimentary wireless WI FI that worked perfectly. In the four nights I never heard a sound from the other rooms. Once in a while heard jet noise but it was sporadic and didn't disturb me. Biggest negative was housekeeping. One day we left the room and did not return until 4 pm and the room was not serviced. I had to call housekeeping for service. The next day we had the do not disturb sign on the door. I heard housekeeping across the hall and asked if they could just take the garbage and change towels. The two employees said I had to call housekeeping. To just get towels and take the garbage?? Bull!!

“Zentral gelegenes Hotel mit sehr kleinen Zimmern und sehr freundlichem Personal” Wir waren für 2 Nächte im Hotel Bijou. Perfekt ist die Lage. Nur wenige Schritte bis zur Cabelcar Haltestelle - man ist einfach Mittendrin,... Die Zimmer snd sehr klein, aber man will ja eigentlich auch die Stadt genießen und nicht die Zeit im Zimmer vergeuden. Die Zimmer sind sehr sauber - gewundert haben wir uns nur über die Öhrstöpsel auf unserem Nachttisch. EIn Blick aus dem Fenster brachte Aufklärung: Direkt vorm Fenster wurde ein Haus gebaut, was bedeutete, dass wir pünktlich mit den Arbeitern dort auf der Baustelle aufgestanden sind. Der Frühstücksraum ist leider viel zu klein und wir mussten meist eine kleine Weile auf einen Platz warten. Zum Frühstück gibt es die üblichen Bagels mit Marmelade und Frischkäse. Der Personal ist sehr, sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Hier wirklich ein großes Lob!!!! Toll ist das kleine Kino in dem jeden Tag 2 Filme angeboten werden. Wir haben das zwar nicht genutzt - aber es war sehr hübsch und gemütlich. Die ganze Einrichtung des Hotels - alles hat irgendwie mit Film und Kino zu tun ist wirklich sehr schön.

“Great hotel” Stayed at the Four Seasons for a few days while attending a conference. This was the second stay in two years and I continue to be impressed with the property. Another poster mentioned Amanda and she is exceptional. After checking me in on Saturday, she walked me to the elevator. I thought, "nice touch," but was truly impressed when she greeted me by name four days later! I sent my booth & a box of documents directly to the hotel before arriving to save cost and everything went smoothly. I was dubious about leaving the booth in the exhibition hall to be shipped back, hoping that someone would get it to a loading dock and to UPS, but when I tracked the package on-line, it was picked up within 90 minutes from the time that I left the hall. The room was comfortable, not high-tech, but very nice. Big flat-screen TV, MP3 docking station on the alarm clock, CD/DVD player, wide shelf above the sink to put your stuff. Oversize L'Occitane shampoo, conditioner, lotion, and body wash. I do wish there was a coffee machine in the room. The best part of the stay was the service. The staff were sincere and genuinely friendly, no one made me feel that they expected a tip except the fellow who put my bag into the taxi upon departure. Some higher-end hotels feel snooty but this one did not. Maybe it's because it's Austin. Every evening, turndown service prepared the room with low lights and classical music. A tray with a book & CD on sleep, TV listing, complimentary newspaper order form, and complimentary shoe shine bag was on the bed. The shoe shine service was great: put your shoes out by 1 am and they're back on your door by 7 am. I didn't eat at the hotel or use the fitness center. It's worthwhile walking around the lake and watching the bats in the evening. No complaints--I thought it was a great hotel.

“Still working out the kinks” As many have noted, this place still hasn't worked everything out. The restaurants? I stayed away from Sauciety based on other's reviews. Other than that there's not much close by, but it's not impossible. The walk to a restaurant was about the same as I usually take in other towns. The only difference is that in other towns I am usually passing other restaurants along the way. Other problems? They have no price list on the phone usage or the snacks in the refrigerator. When we called to ask the prices on the snacks, we were told that the value of the entire contents was $500. That didn't help us much in figuring out the price of a diet soda. After I checked out and verified my bill, I received a second charge for $15.75 on my credit card. I called back to ask about it, and I was told that it was for food taken from the refrigerator. I assured them we didn't take it, and they refunded my card. The Starbucks didn't seem prepared for large groups, because they ran out of food every morning. As a note, more restaurants are opening in the hotel next year. There were also some problems with the locks on the doors. I got locked out of my room twice. The second time I was getting a new entry card, they gave me 3 cards just in case there were more problems. So for the rest of the week, I had to carry 3 cards around and of course the card never stopped working after that. Other than that, I really liked the open airiness of the lobby and the proximity to the train.

“Convenient Location Standard Downtown Marriott Hotel” Stayed at the Seattle Marriott Waterfront for 3 nights for a conference. Convenient to the Bell Harbor Conference Center, Pike Place Market and the Downtown Waterfront. My wife and son stayed with me and visited Seattle while I attended the conference. That meant a room with two beds and the beds were only full size beds. For 250+ a night you would think they could at least make the room large enough to accomodate double size beds.

“Nice Hotel” Picked the Hilton due to its central location to Times Square. 5 minutes walk got you to so many attractions. Price was compatible with other hotels in the area. You could get free WiFi in the lobby. For the price you are paying per night, you should be able to get free WiFi in your room. Didn’t have breakfast at the hotel as this was $36 for full breakfast. Fed the three of us for less than this in one of many breakfast cafe’s in close proximity. It was a shame there was no fridge in the room. Stayed on the 36th floor with no view. Was noisy with the window open at night but i think this would be the same with any hotel in the area. Would recommend to others.

“Posizione super” L'allegro hotel è situato in una posizione centralissima all'interno del loop di Chicago, a pochi passi dal Millennium park e da altre famose attrazioni. La struttura non è nuovissima e le camere avrebbero bisogno di un po'' di ammodernamento, ma sicuramente un ottimo compromesso per la sua posizione. Il personale è stato gentile e la colazione compresa nel prezzo viene effettuata in un Cafe adiacente all'albergo.

“Expected more.” I really wanted to love the W. we were having a mini in town vacation while floors sanded. Had a suite. Was plenty big, with a big terrace, but many things didn't quite work. Door to terrace wouldn't lock. A molding tile missing in bath. Door to room stuck. Carpet not perfectly clean. The pool area was cool, but really for twenty something's. Not one comfortable chair in the pool area to read. Recliners had no settings and chair backs too low. Room service breakfast was awful. Dry omelet, pasty pastries and expensive. Bell guys for parking were great. Very easy and fast. Spa was very nice, if a tad expensive for Dallas. Rooms that look at city are good. Suite 315 costs less than terrace suites and has a big terrace, although the furniture on it is not comfortable. More for posing on than using.

“Great place to stay in downtown Denver.” My husband and I try to stay in Embassy Suites when we travel. This one is the most modern looking one we have stayed in. The lobby staff were very nice and let us check in early. Our room 1520 was larger than other Embassy Suites we have stayed in. The beds were very comfortable. I did notice some stains on the bathroom floor and some chips in the wood furniture in the living room. Hopefully the staff will fix these things to keep this hotel looking shiny and new. The mangers reception was crowded but we were able to get some drinks and humus and chips. There is a lot of seating area outside the reception area. The breakfast was crowded but it moved along fine and had a good assortment of choices and made-to-order omlet station. We felt safe at this hotel since you had to use your hotel key in the elevator to go up to your room. The valet staff was very nice. If your in the mood for dinner food, there is a Sam's 3 just two blocks away on 15th street that has great food. Shopping and dining from 16th street is a short walk from the hotel.

“Nice hotel in a nice neighborhood” I always try to stay here when I visit Chicago, even though weekends have a two-night minimum. Walk 2 blocks down Roscoe to N. Halsted, which has some great gay clubs. Broadway between Roscoe and Belmont is very quaint, lots of small shops and restaurants. It's a nice walk. If you have a car it's a short drive to N. Michigan Ave and the museums. Parking at the garage next door is convenient, but remember to keep your ticket stub from the front desk, as you will need it to go in and out. The only suggestion is to avoid rooms next to the elevator, unless you want to hear dinging sounds all night. They couldn't turn it down, so the manager moved us to another room. Don't expect much of a view unless you're on the top floor. The breakfast is decent with your typical pastries, bagels, and cereal. If you're looking for things to do, there are brochures and local papers in the lobby. The staff is friendly and helpful.

“Expected more” Great location for Penn Station,our first criterion for this stay. The newly refurbished rooms are pleasant and clean but smallish and the bathroom- as others have said- is tiny, especially if you're staying any longer than a night or two and need to set out your toiletries. However, our overall impression was not good. Our electronic key refused to open our door and after numerous trips to the front desk - where the apologetic staff did try to deal with our problem - we just gave up and went off to bed, tired after a transatlantic flight, but ultimately with no key of our own. The following day, however, and after a full day in Manhattan, we ended up asking for a change of room as the problem had still not been fixed. Frustrating to say the least. Maybe there were on-going problems following the thunderstorm that knocked out the hotel's computer system, internet and TVs the night we arrived.. In addition, the tiling behind the basin in our first room seemed to have been done by an amateur DIY man with two broken arms. Having stayed at Affinia properties in NYC in the past, I think the most disappointing thing was the impression of uncleanliness in the hallways and even in the lobby. While I understand that housekeeping can't be on the go at all times, it did seem that vacuuming was not a top priority in some areas.The hotel overall just seemed tired, even given the historic nature of the building. For the rate we paid, I wish we'd gone for the Eventi, which is not far in distance from Penn , but is WAY further in terms of style, comfort and efficiency.

“Excellent location” Situated 2 minute walk from Pudential " T " station, by a $15 weekly travel pass and take public transport its cheaper and surprisingly easy ( as opposed to $30 taxi) hotel is under renovation a the moment, but that doesn't get in the way of the experience, the only real issue id the paper thin walls, but the room does have flat screen TV's , ans a great view over Back Bay. The Prudential Centre/ CopleyPlaza and Newbury & Boylston street, are literally on the doorstep, so great food, cheap shopping and a brilliant talking tour around Boston

“Fantastic flawless hotel” This hotel offers the right amount of luxury and service. I love everything about it. Check-in was smooth with professional and pleasant staff. The room is large with modern amenities: Keurig coffee machine, flat screen TV, Bose clock radio with AUX cable to connect your iPod, Gilchrist and Soames pump soap, shampoo, conditioner, and lotion. FREE INTERNET WIRED AND WIRELESS! The fitness center is super nice with plenty of equipments, steam room, and lap pool. Breakfast buffet is very well done and reasonably price ~$20. Check out is quick and oh so efficient storing and retrieving your luggage for the remaining of the day. The hotel is so close to the airport by the $2 fare bus Silver Line 1. Location is not immediately downtown but if you have to attend an event at the World Trade Center, the location can't be beat. It is also easy by bus connecting to the T (free transfer) to go anywhere in Boston. This is luxury the way it should be. Love this hotel!

“Great, if at Convention” The Hyatt McCormick is in perfect location to McCormick Place convention center. But if you need anything downtown prepare for a cab ride. Rooms were clean, Staff was very friendly and helpful. This is my favorite Hyatt.

“Very nice budget hotel, perfect location” I made a spur of the moment trip to NYC and needed a hotel fast...found great rates at the New Yorker Hotel. It's about a block from Madison Square Garden/Penn Station. The first thing I noticed was that it was clean, well kept and well secured by all-night guards...nice when you are traveling alone. I came in very late, and was kindly received at the front desk and upgraded to a renovated room (I didn't see the unrenovated rooms, so I can't comment). It was small but comfortable. Bathroom fixtures were all new, and the bedroom furniture was new. There was a window air conditioning unit which was pretty loud, but I got used to it. It worked fine. The bedding was very comfortable and higher quality. It was extremely quiet in my room except for my A/C unit. I was extremely pleased with the stay. Knowing that New York hotels are unbelievably expensive, this was a great option at under $200 a night. The location was fantastic. I would stay here again.

“Great place for business meetings!” My company hosted 100 guest at this wonderful resort. From check in thru meetings, dinners and golf you could not ask for a friendlier, great place to get away. The rooms have been redone, are small but nice. The only downside is they did not redo the bathrooms. 20 year old tub and comode as well as old composit sink surrounds. Not bad enough to say don't come here, just a surprise because the rest of the resort is great. Definatly would recommend

“What can I say... Poor, Poor & Poor” Stayed here over the weekend for a short business trip and although I loved the location I was absolutely appalled with almost everything else! I don't know how to begin but here goes. Arrival: As I was driving a rented car, I needed to park my car temporarily to check-in (for about 10 minutes or so) but the gentlemen at the driveway insisted that I can't do that. In the end, I have to return the car 3 blocks away with half of my luggage (I dropped off 1 bag and left it at reception) and walk to the hotel with the luggage. Appalling! Check-in: Check-in was relatively efficient. Concierge: Appalling - I asked a relatively simple question - i.e. What time does the Smithsonian museums close during summer. She informed me it's a 5pm. Luckily I took the chance and went there anyway (as I thought they have longer hours in summer) - they were open until 7pm! I found out later that that information is on the front page of their website! Concierge should verify the information! Service to the rooms: My room was missing a in-room dining menu and I requested for it. It took them one and a half hours to bring them to me. Also, housekeeping did not add an additional shower gel on the 2nd day and I requested for one. Took them 45 minutes to bring it up and the gentlemen told me that if I want more, I can get them myself as the trolley is parked just down the corridor. Is this what you call Service Express??? On the day of my checkout, housekeeping showed up at 9am (on a Sunday morning) to prompt me that I am checking out. As a gold SPG member, I have 4pm checkout rites (which I have informed the reception and got confirmation of that). It is rather intrusive and rude. Reception: It is common practice that the reception of a hotel should carry change for the convenience of their guests. This one does not. In fact, the lady at the counter informs me (rather rudely) that they have only 100 dollar notes and I should buy something at the shop to get change. Which I did. This is not acceptable for a Starwood hotel. Food: Breakfast is good albeit without variation. Had dinner once at the same restaurant and I was surprised to see a grasshopper in my salad (after I finished half of the salad). If I was not paying attention, I'd have consumed a rather exotic source of protein. However, the waitress was apologetic and they gave me a complimentary desert. Best service I received in my entire stay. All in all, poor, Poor & POOR!

“Fair at Best” I stayed here for a few nights and it was not all that great. I had been at another hotel in hollywood the week before and wished I had stayed there for my entire stay. This hotel at one time was most likely a luxury hotel. Not anymore- It really needs to be remodeled very badly. The carpet in the hallways was worn out and the entire property feels worn. It was built in 1979 and some parts like the curtains in the rooms are original. The front desk person was very nice but the bartender did not say one word when I asked for a bucket of ice .Not all of the floors have Ice machines. Also you must valet park and they charge for parking. The hollywood hotel did not. Until they redo this property, I do not recommend it in its current state.

“clean and centrally located near shopping strip” good clean place to stay in. hotel could do with some modernisation but overall it is a pretty good shape. very clean and pleasant staff. location is closed to market street where all the shops are. walkable to some of the tourist spots like the piers - but depends on which pier you are after. Fisherman's wharf is reachable over a hill, otherwise take the trolley cars which is a must do in SF anyway. also has a pretty decent gym and wifi service which i think was complimentary as well

“High End Marriott San Diego Gas Lamp & Convention Center” I've stayed at this location a couple times. It's an excellent hotel directly adjacent to the Convention Center and two blocks from the Gas Lamp District. Views of the bay are amazing.

“Reminded Me More of a College A-partment” My husband and I (late-20s) had a flight that arrived in Philadelphia at midnight, so we decided to stay at the aloft for the night before moving to a hotel downtown. We travel often and love this brand, so we knew to expect trendy and modern with some fun quirks. All that with a free airport shuttle and a great price, and we didn't think twice. While the hotel was similar to others we've stayed at, the environment was TOTALLY different. I don't know if it was our late arrival or what, but there was pretty much a party everywhere -- tons of people at the bar, playing pool, in the courtyard, running around the halls (including children). We also had plenty of time to observe this because there was only one person working at the front desk. Side note: I understand that you only "need" one person at midnight at most hotels, however being by the airport, at least two would be helpful. After all, there were three people ahead of us checking in, two people trying to buy snacks from the refreshment area, and another woman standing to the side who needed a taxi. (The front desk was also responsible for keeping up with the shuttle, as well as responding to guests calls -- including a guest that called for security to be sent to a room.) Granted, the woman at the desk worked as fast as two people; but wow! Fast-forward through check-in and getting into our room. We were... unimpressed. The carpet seemed a bit dingy, the bathroom shower wasn't all that clean (soap scum on the floor and the shampoo pump had dripped a large metallic-blue puddle), and the walls were thin enough to hear the people in the hallway and those next to us. We didn't really care because we were exhausted, so we just decided to get into bed and crash. However, the sheets were also thin and scratchy! At this point my husband looked at me and said, "Doesn't this remind you of a dorm room in college?!" We both laughed because EVERYTHING about it did -- the party scene, the overworked front desk, the just-clean-enough room, the thin walls, the scratchy sheets, and even the cool decorations and really nice television/technology set up. It was like a well-decorated, large, college dorm suite. In the morning, things were a bit different. There were two, really relaxed, super-friendly people at the front desk, nice music playing, a few people enjoying the pool and fitness center (great features), and everything had calmed down a bit. The treadmills were busy, so we went for a run around the airport property -- not scenic, but it got our heart rates up -- before checking out. Overall, for our late arrival and the price, it was a totally adequate stay for one night. If we were staying longer, we would have switched to the Four Points across the street.

“Nice room but skip the free breakfast” The room was nice - plenty of room. The rate was a lot higher in person than on the Best Western website, so be careful...but they do take AAA. There are a few flights of stairs as the property seems to go on forever. The room was quiet and the location is in the heart of Old Town - touristy area with lots of Mexican restaurants. The free breakfast voucher stated 2 eggs cooked to order, ham/bacon or sausage, homestyle potatoes, toast, coffee/juice. But what you get is buffet style with only scrambled eggs or scrambled eggs with peppers/onions and only sausage links on the day I was there. The worst part was the bread for the toast was MOLDED. We made ourselves instant oatmeal instead and got outta there.

“Great stay - again” I rebooked at this location after a great stay in March. I was very impressed with this hotel especially for the value. On this stay we had an excellent suite for only $107/night. It was nicer than most hotel suites I've stayed in with full kitchen, comfortable bed, large... The location is great as it's near just about everything. There is an Embassy Suites just next door with a restaurant/bar that served good food and drinks - a little pricy but very convenient. The staff is very helpful, it's in a very nice area in Memphis - very safe. I highly recommend this place.

“Service and Convenience” Reasonable rate found on website for hotel. Sleep number bed and nice floor plan for a room with a king size bed. Quiet and comfortable. Furniture a bit tired in the rooms but for an $89 rate, no complaints. Front desk and restaurant staff very friendly and helpful. So convenient to the SEATAC!

“Not terrible but I won't be back” I stayed one night at Holiday Inn LAX because of an early flight I had the next day. The hotel is not terrible but with so much choice around the area I would not stay here again. The hotel looks shabby inside and outside. Pretty much only one elevator worked so you'd have to wait ages and then when you got an elevator you'd be crammed in because of all the people waiting. My room was actually okay. Nicer then I expected compared to the public hotel areas. Though when I got in both lamps beside my bed did not work. One lamp did not have a lightbulb in it and the other had a bulb that didn't work. So i had to unscrew a bulb from my desk lamp to put into my bed lamp. Ridiculous. As well there is apparently free wifi in the hotel but my signal was almost non existent. I called the front desk to tell them and they said it was because I was in a room at the end of hall, and I couldn't use ethernet because only the top floors had ethernet connections. So I had to go down to the desk to pick up some ridiculous internet kit that didn't make my signal better anyways. I was also annoyed that they put a $175 charge on my bill for the kit. I later found out the charge would be taken off when I returned the kit but no one told me of this charge in the first place. A hassle. As well my toilet didn't fully flush properly. I'd have to flush a couple of times for it to work. And I had a lovely view of the back of McDonalds from my room. The pool was pretty depressing. It overlooked another dingy looking hotel across the way. The service at the bar was nice though. Even though the bar area doesn't have a lot of character. And it was convenient they had frequent shuttles to the airport but I'm sure all hotels in the area have that. For dinner we went to Flemings steak house which is a short drive away. Excellent food and service. Would recommend making a reservation. So with all the choices there are in the LAX area I would not recommend staying here.
