“Nice hotel, cool lobby” This is a typical W hotel, which, for us, made it a LOT of fun. It's got a great, hip lobby with lots of stuff going on all the time. They have a good restaurant, and it is right within walking distance of lake Michigan and Navy Pier. The Mag. Mile isn't too far (several blocks), so it is a little trek...but if you're young and don't mind walking a lot, then it is doable. The rooms are fantastic. The beds, as always are wonderful. The view was good, as well. Overall, if you can find it at a good deal, I'd recommend it. It was a little pricy though.

“Convenient basic hotel” This hotel is a typical american Courtyard Marriott. Nothing fancy, but convenient and you get what you pay for. Rooms are bigger than average, and being on the 28th floor there was no traffic noise, so getting a good night's sleep was not a problem. Walking distance to most places in mid Manhattan, and a subway station right ouside the door. Many restaurants nearby and a few drugstores. Workout facilities and business center. Free wifi. All you need basically. Nothing to complain about, except the key card, which stopped working all the time and had to be reloaded. Staff friendly and service minded. The only thing missing is a restaurant/bar. Would not hesitate booking this hotel again.

“最高でしたが、お値段はそれなりに張ります” お部屋は数少ないバルコニー付きのお部屋でした。 そのバルコニーからは下の通りを見下ろせました。 広さも十分な広さで、ゆとりのある時間を過ごすことができました。 バスのお湯も直ぐに溜まりますし、お部屋には不満はありませんでした。 但し、それ相当のレート設定になっていますので、利用者は限られるでしょうね。 あと、タクシーではそれなりに渋滞にはまりますので、地下鉄を利用したくても駅が目の前というわけではありませんでした。

“Exceeded Expectations” I recently stayed here during extended business in Philadelphia. I was awarded this hotel after blind bidding on Priceline, and was very surprised with my stay. This hotel is well situated around a lot of restaurants and bars. There is plenty to do within walking distance. Upon my arrival, I was greeted by very friendly and polite service who immediately grabbed my bags from the cab. I arrived at 8:00 AM, and was just looking for a place to stow my bags while I was working, but the Hotel checked me in early. Great service. When I needed a cab, the doorman was vigilant in his efforts to hail one, and also in his efforts to secure a shuttle back to the airport. The lobby was warm and inviting. The attached restaurants looked busy, but during my stay I only ate at the coffee shop, which was decent. The decor and furnishings were classic. The rooms were adequately sized, with a comfortable bed and nice television. In the lobby was a free business center, which I used extensively. Overall, nice stay. I look forward to returning.

“Its got everything I needed and more...” I stayed at this hotel for 8 nights and paid 106 total with all taxes per night. For this rate this hotel is unbeatable. It has 820 rooms, a pool, and all the amenities of a 5 star hotel. It is located 5 mins to LAX. I’ll start with the negative since I only have a couple. The shuttle service is extremely slow and you will wait for almost half an hour when they say it is only 15 mins. So make sure you allocate enough time when you rely on this shuttle service. I wouldnt bother with valet service as they are soooooo slow and I feel are inefficient. Just park in the lot behind the hotel on 98th stree for $13 in and out priviledges. Service – this is what makes this hotel shine especially the guest services folks nothing is too much to ask, if they can do it they will accommodate you. I especially want to mention Diane and Merlie Pickett, these two ladies provided me with the best service during my stay. I even stopped by to meet them in person. They go above and beyond. Rooms – they are very clean and well appointed, modern décor and oh so comfortable beds. It is very clean and the soundproofing is very adequate. I am a very light sleeper and I did not have any problems whatsoever. This hotel is along century blvd but they have rooms that are facing 98th street where the parking lots are located this is the quiet side. Housekeeping never forgets to clean up the room even when I ask them to clean it up later in the afternoon. The room doesn’t come with a safe. It also doesn’t come with a refrigerator unless you request one and they would charge you for it. Even if the location of this hotel is by the airport if you have a car you can go to so many areas around it. Manhattan beach is 15 mins away and so is Marina del rey. If you plan to rent a car go with midway rental which is 2 blocks from this hotel, I had the best rate with that company although the battery died on the car on my last day. If you go left or right on Sepulveda blvd theres a lot of grocery, estabilishments etc I would definitely stay in this hotel again only if the price is around 150. You can get this through hotwire. Im not sure if I would pay more than 200 for this hotel. If you are looking for a hotel to WOW you this is not the one, if you are looking for a practical, clean, value for your money place then this is a great fit. In fact it exceeds expectations if your expectations are not that high.

“Great location for NYC shopping, mixed service” We stayed here for 2 nights in May 2012 with our small dog. The hotel does not have much in the way of pet amenities - I had to call a few times to see if they had a dog food and water bowl, which they finally procured, but nothing in the way of little treats or other nice touches. They do have a non-refundable $150 pet fee. Not the best pick for traveling with a pet. The service at the front desk and the bellboys left much to be desired - after signing up for the Omni loyalty program, I still had to call the desk each morning to remind them about the perks. One of the bellmen was super rude and couldn't be bothered while doing push-ups back in the luggage storage room. That said, the concierge staff and one of the valets was absolutely lovely. The location is unbeatable for shopping - directly across from the Cartier mansion and right in the heart of all the 5th avenue shops. The decor is rather bland but the beds were very comfortable and our room was exceedingly quiet (we had an end unit that overlooked 4 corners of other buildings so not a great view, but very nice and peaceful.) The concierge gave us great delivery recommendations so we enjoyed some delicious sushi and Indian delivery food which was the highlight of our trip. The concierge staff was also unfailingly kind to my dog which I appreciated!

“WE loved it and would stay again.” My sister and I were traveling and unable to get back east after the hurricane Irene. Traveling by train, from Union Station, just outside the station we could see a Holiday Inn. WE took a chance and walked to this hotel. We we were delighted. The staff was VERY friendly and helpful. The hotel was clean. The attached restaurant was excellent. We would definitely stay again.

“Great staff, excellent hotel” Right on the edge of downtown, within walking distance of all shops and restaurants and also the Mariners and Seahawks stadiums, I was met by the nicest people you'll ever meet at the front desk. As it was 9am and my room was not ready, they gave two of the famous Doubletree chocolate chip cookies (now warm!) and went out of their way to be helpful. The hotel has a 1930 touch, very classy and stylish. Room was great, HD tv (to make it makes a huge difference, even if I might not watch it for a long time), spacious bathroom, minibar, all the amenites you might need. They also feature a car service to the airport for 40$ (Sea-Tac is not near downtown), less than I paid the cab that got me there. I'd definitely recommend this hotel to anybody.

“Clean & Safe” A little shabby in the common areas (lobby, elevator...) but my room was lovely. The neighborhood is great because it is near all the posh hotels and a beautiful park. Some of the staff were friendly and some were, well, typical Chicagoans!

“NEVER Going back!” Let me start first by saying that the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers used to be one of my favorite hotels to stay at while in Chicago. I have good memories from prior stays. All of that changed the minute I stepped into the hotel for this stay. I came in for a spine conference at Mc Cormick Place, and this hotel was one of the 'preferred providers' to choose from. My check-in took almost an hour! The girl at the desk asked me for payment for all 4 nights. I informed her that my company had made arrangements with the hotel ahead of time to use their credit card for everything, including incidentals (My office mgr is very anal about these things and she had even called earlier in the day and was told everything was fine). I explained to the girl that my company had made arrangements for me (and I should add that 1 night had been paid for up front as a deposit when making my reservation). Of course there was nothing notated on my reservation! I asked her to go and check for a fax or other communication. When she returned, I was told no, nothing found. A night manager then came over, and he informed me nothing could be done for me, and I would have to pay for my stay. I then pointed out that 1 night was already paid for, and that I would give them my Chas debit card for the 100.00 incidentals, and we would straighten everything out in the morning. There were several people waiting in line to check in and overheard everything. It was very humiliating to say the least. The next morning around 5:30a.m., I looked at my phone and saw a text message from my bank stating that my account was overdrawn! I logged onto my acct. and discovered that the Hotel had charged my card for the ENTIRE stay, and incidentals, so over 900.00 had been taken from me! I contacted my office manager as I was in panic mode, and she was livid. She confirmed she had spent alot of time making sure everything was set for my stay. She contacted the hotel and spoke with the front desk manager, and she couldn't understand or explain what had happened. After alot of prompting from my office, the hotel contacted my bank and asked them to remove the charges asap so I would have access to my money! For my troubles, I was awarded 10,000 spg points (big deal!). My room was dirty, and outdated. It is past time to renovate the rooms at this hotel! Very outdated bathrooms with old, dirty tile; hair in the bathtub, and the tub itself was chipped and stained. The room was dusty, the phone hadn't been cleaned in a very long time (eww!), the drawers were filthy and had several unidentified things in them; the curtains were missing hooks and hanging down; the air conditioner did not work properly and we sweated our first night. Also absolutely no place to plug in your computer or phone charger! A big pet peeve of mine! We asked for a mini fridge to put our water in and were charged 25.00 for that luxury. The internet is 12.95 a day, and is very very slow. Don't waste your money on room service. The food is terrible, and each time it came up ice cold, or items were missing that were ordered and charged for. Almost 80.00 for breakfast for 2 people?! Seriously?!! The 2nd morning I woke up to find that ONCE AGAIN, my card had been charged for the entire stay, and my account was again overdrawn! I called my office and they noted that the charge on their American Express card had been reversed! Here we go again!!! I call the front desk manager, and she tells me it is my bank's fault and there is nothing she can do! It was all I could do to not go downstairs in person and have an epic meltdown at that desk! My office called and also got nowhere quick. We ended up contacting Sheraton's corporate office to get someone to help us. I am so disappointed, pissed off, fed up, and worn out over this! I will NEVER give this hotel a penny of my business again! I am also planning on letting the head of the conference know my experiences, as well as everyone I know! Save yourself the grief and go elsewhere!

“Excellent Hotel” With spacious, modern rooms and a host of amenities, this hotel does a lot of things right. The rooms at this property are generously sized and were spotless, with a large LCD TV and a spacious bathroom with a stand-up shower and a one-sink vanity. Note that there are no tubs in the standard rooms, which may make bathing difficult if you are travelling with young children. The rooms also offer an expansive work area, with complimentary WiFi. The hotel has a full suite of amenities, with a large, modern and well-equipped gym and a clean, attractive pool area to fully equipped locker rooms and a pretty good restaurant with reasonably priced happy hour options. The hotel should be commended for not charging guests extra to access the locker room areas with steam and sauna. Service was friendly and efficient. Though the hotel is not as centrally located as some properties (it's a 10 to 15 minute walk to the market, for example), all of the other advantages outweigh that fact.

“Very nice hotel in a great area” I stayed 2 nights for a business trip. The hotel is very nicely appointed with many modern conveniences despite being old and historic. It was built in 1924 and at the time it was built was the tallest hotel of its time. Room had ample drawer space, coffee maker and safe. Window view of the side of hotel. The elevator is beautiful and was always very quick. The breakfast was great and I was given a smoothie sample and a free orange juice to take with me. The room was on the smaller side but actually had plenty of room with a queen bed and a small sleeper sofa. This hotel is in a great area. It is a 4 block walk to 30 Rock and Radio City Music Hall and the Waldorf Astoria us right around the corner. The concierge really helped me with a show ticket issue which was much appreciated.

“Great Location, modern and comfortable” This hotel was all that I expected. Excellent location (1 block away from petco park) Great staff, and a very comfortable bed. The rooms are spacious, with a great modern decor. And the free Internet is always appreciated. The parking fee is overpriced, but that didn't affect us as the park meters are not in service during the weekend.

“A good choice” I have spent a week end and, to summarize : - reception and services were efficient - the size of the room are good for new york, which is quite remarquable in Manhattan - breaksfast is not exceptionnal but it will help you to avoid the starvation up to the lunch - hotel location is excellent to visit Manhattan - the room might be a bit noisy because the islotation is a bit weak between the room. If your neighbourg are noisy you might be disturbed, but for me, it was OK! A good choice for Manhattan where hotel are not perfect, I will probably come back there

“Great hotel for a trip to Chicago” Every door man, every receptionist, every from room service, everybody was great. It didn't, at all, feel like the staff was told to be nice. They just all seemed nice. I love Chicago anyway. Super close to all the bars, restaurants, skyscrapers, everything. Great hotel.

“Great location. Beds very comfortable.” It's definitely on the high end of 4 TripAdvisor circles, overall. The pros: the beds, the location, large-ish bathroom with separate tub/shower, nice gym, basic rooms are ok size for NYC (although the basic room is a queen not a king-sized bed). Everyone was very polite and attentive. The cons: cushy hotel room carpet might be a benefit for some but to me it's just...ick. Also, for my taste, they went a little overboard with the whole "we're a French hotel" thing. All basic greetings are given in French (on the phone, at the desk, in the corridors). Amusingly, when I replied in French with more than a brief response, one particular employee seemed stunned (maybe it was my accent). Overall, the hotel has the potential of being a good value for the right rate and the location really is very convenient.

“Great hotel, albeit too busy!!” We stayed here because we had an afternoon performance of Wicked, and we also had tickets to see the New York Yankees in Game 6 of the American League Championship (The Yankees won the pennant, by the way). We booked this hotel on short notice, and were surprised they had rooms available, given that the city was very busy!! This hotel is HUGE, with almost 2000 rooms. This is very evident in that the lobby is CONSTANTLY busy; with queues for checking in, storing your luggage, and even for taxis. We were upgraded for a small fee to the Executive Level, with access to the Club Lounge on the 44th Floor. The Club Floors occupy the top 12 floors, and have their own set of elevators. Our room was located on the 42nd Floor. It had a great view of Central Park, which was almost ablaze in fall colors. The room was a bit small, but this is New York, and spaciousness is hard to come by. The beds were very comfortable. The Executive Lounge is very nicely appointed. However, it is often busy, given the size of the "club level" of this hotel. They offered an assortment of cheese and finger foods during the evening, as well as a continental breakfast in the morning. The hotel is in a great location; just a few blocks from Central Park, Times Square, and Rockefeller Center. Several subway stations are also within walking distance, and so this hotel can be a great base for exploring all New York has to offer. All in all; I was satisfied with the Hilton New York. The only thing I really did not like too much was how busy the place was. However, this is the largest hotel in New York, and that is not the staff's fault. In fact, the staff was very accomodating.

“Eh, Holiday weekend bust!” We stayed here on Saturday September 3rd, checked in late around 9 pm and were told we weren't going to be able to receive the room we requested because they were booked. We received one bed instead of two but we could use the sofa sleeper, ew.. It was old and dirty and we couldn't even get any extra pillows. We all 4 squeezed into the king bed and made it work, thank goodness we brought our pack and play for our 2 yr old. There were ants comming out of one of the plugs in the room and we also couldn't get any extra towels, 2 towels for 4 people and a baby just isn't good enough. At breakfast, the line was wrapped around the breakfast area, which itself was very small. The breakfast consisted of, Fresh fruit, cereal, toast, and bagels. There was a pot of sausage gravy where a sign in front said oatmeal, there were a couple of bowls full where people though it was oatmeal and then realized it wasn't. If you wanted sausage gravy you would have to get creative unless people smother it on their cereal, toast or bagels. After getting through the line (20 min) There was no where to eat so we walked to our room to where once we sat down the power in the hotel went out. Maybe it was a fluke but from the minute we got there we just had issues. This hotel was far inferior to the other Hyatt's we have stayed at recently.
“Very Nice Hotel, Great RIverfront Location” This hotel is in a great location on the riverfront. Great front desk staff. Rooms are clean, large and quiet.

“A terrific stay at Legacy Golf!” We are SVC owners and this was our first trip to the Legacy. It really is a wonderful resort, convenient to everything you'd want to do in Phoenix (helpful as we are not golfers). The rooms were really well done and you can't beat the jacuzzi tubs. The grounds are immaculately maintained and it was a very quiet location. I've read other comments about the surrounding neighborhood and didn't get any negative impressions myself. It is in an older part of Phoenix but by no means unsafe. There's actually a nice private farm next door which has its own restaurant. It's just a short drive down 32nd to Baseline drive, where you can go left to catch I-10 or right to get to supermarkets, restaurants, etc. We highly recommend the Legacy and will plan a return trip next year!

“Lovely Kimpton service in a slightly faded package” We always stay in Kimpton hotels when we travel, but we'd never stayed at the Vintage Park before. The decor isn't really our style -- deep jewel tones, very traditional -- and the finishes are getting dated. Also, the bathrooms, even in the larger rooms, are plain and small. But the beds are comfortable, and the service is A+. The first room we were in had a problem with the A/C compressor (so loud it sounded like a jackhammer in the hallway; needless to say we didn't sleep much). When we called to ask if something could be done, the front desk proactively offered to move us to another (and, as it turns out, larger) room, without any hemming and hawing about sending someone up to fix it. The front desk attendant asked us to pack up our bags and said a bellman would come at 1pm to move us. At 12:59, there was a knock on the door! Needless to say, I was stunned: Even the best hotels are rarely so on-the-mark with time estimates. One day we came back from the market with a big bouquet of flowers, and the front desk agent asked if we needed a vase, without our asking. We were taking the flowers to friends, so we didn't need a vase, but it was a typically thoughtful gesture, a great example of why we choose Kimpton hotels.

“Second stay - Not disappointed!” My husband and I stayed at this location for the second time this June. Since he is a frequent traveler he gets free-room certificates from RRI regularly. We were very happy b/c we were able to use them for the NYC RRI. (It takes two vouchers for this location since it is higher priced than the average RRI.) We were not disappointed this stay. Our room was large enough to accomodate us. The air conditioning worked great and the flat screen TV and ipod doc are nice to come back to after a long day of walking the city. We are anxious to stay here every year we travel to NYC for our anniversary.

“Terrific” This is a mega hotel, which I don't usually like, but stayed here for a conference & was very pleasantly surprised. It is worth the extra money for a bay view room, because the view was fabulous. I had a room in the North Tower with a small balcony & it was delightful. The only downside is that all the bay view rooms also face the pool area so you can expect some noise during the day. It also happened that some noisy fools decided to head for the pool at 3:00 AM one night & woke me up. I called the front desk & they responded right away by sending security out - noise was stopped & problem resolved immediately. The room was comfortable, quiet, clean & the decor fresh. The hotel was extremely busy, but I was impressed by the professionalism, and smooth flow of check in/out & the bell men who practically ran to keep everyone happy. Great location - you can walk to Seaport Village & to Gaslamp easily. Overall, definitely exceeded my expectations & I would return.

“Good Budget Option Close to the Action” Very comfortable bed, we had a relatively (for NY standards!) spacious king room on the 27th floor with great views. Would definitely recommend requesting a high floor, as well as the view, it helped considerably with the traffic noise which was also good for the location of the hotel. Bathroom was also nice - enjoyed the big, walk in shower. Overall room was clean, furnished with everything we needed. Free wi-fi was also a plus, we had good signal and it was easy to use. In terms of location I got what I was expecting. To the west of Times Sq (where the hotel is located) the neighborhoods are a little mixed, and yes the hotel shares a street with some Adult DVD stores (with tastefully whited out windows of course!) and the Parole Office, however at no point did I feel unsafe, there was so much foot traffic around and everywhere was well lit. The hotel is next to the Fairfield Inn - which has the Sky Room on the 33rd floor which I would recommend. Nice bar with cool views - think it would be awesome in the summer when you could sit outside. Overall for the price we paid (got 50% off our second night via a Starwood offer) felt we got good value for money, and it was great to be able to walk everywhere and be so close to the action.

“Friendly staff, speedy internet and almost new” Very nice property to stay at when visiting San Antonio. For those visiting that aren't familiar with the area, this location is not close to the Riverwalk. However, it would make a great place to stay for those visiting both Six Flags and Sea World. Also, there are shops and restaurants very close by to suit most any taste. The hotel is very clean and shares a large pool with the Residence Inn next door. If you are staying for business, as I did, this is a great location. I'd imagine that it may not be the best choice during the tourist season if you want a little quiet though. I was impressed with the speed of the internet here. Although most hotels have adequate service, this hotel provided a strong wireless signal and great download speeds. The rooms are basically standard Courtyard style with the red and white color scheme. The bathroom did have a full size walk in shower, complete with full glass doors. This is something I've only seen at the newest Courtyards. Friendly staff and great lobby. My only complaint was that the business center printer was low on ink. Not a big deal when everything else was great.

“Would Stay somewhere else” Just spent two days at this hotel. Booked it on Jetsetter for $149 a night. I would have been annoyed if I paid anymore than that for the room. For the money I cant complain. The location is excellent, right next to the Hancock Tower and just off Michigan Avenue ( Mag Mile). The only taxis I took were to and from O'Hare. The room was small and had an overlook of fire escapes ( probably a result of the $149 a night so not important). The front door was hard to close. The refrigerator was poorly placed and kept hitting the door frame of the bathroom when you opened it, it was annoying. The bed was comfortable and pillows were fine. Unfortunately, something in the wall near the A/C vent kept rattling and woke me up both mornings. I had to hit the wall to make it stop. Sure this was not in every room but all I cared was it was in MY room. The bathroom was small and modern. Good water pressure in the shower. NO BATH TUB. The shower had one of those glass dividers that only goes half way across the shower. Looks cool and trendy, but lets water get all over and it did. Bathroom did not have glasses or little storage space for toiletries. The people at the front desk were very polite and helpful. There is nothing to complain about the staff, they were excellent. I did not eat at the restaurant, they gym was small. It had some treadmills and ellipticals which is fine if you just want to run. Dumbells go up to 50lbs. Gym had TVs and water bottle. Internet is $9.95 for 24 hours in the room. In the business center the computer is $6.95 for 15 minutes of use. Like I said, for the price it was fine, I was only in the room to sleep, but next time I will stay at the Ritz Carlton, Peninsula or Westin.

“First Class All the Way!” The Orchard Hotel is a first-class surprise! Located in the busy Union Square district of San Francisco, it's close to cable cars, shopping and lots more. A special tip of the hat to Cornell the doorman, who smoothed out a small problem with car parking with ease and aplomb! I've stayed in pricier hotels on Bush Street and elsewhere in SF ... but the Orchard beats them all! Nice breakfast buffet ... and as a sign of an active hotel ... lots of people in the bar area on a Saturday night! The rooms are spacious - I had a room on the top floor ... and a great San Francisco touch .. I could hear the clinging of the cable car as it went by! Just a friendly place all around!

“A Pig with a Neon Dress is Still a Pig” There are three items that are key to a stay in a hotel; quiet, good HVAC and a good night's sleep. This hotel failed on all three. The rooms with an "odd" number face a very busy street with busses going by all night, the HVAC was broken (temperature would not go below 75) and the maintenance department failed to fix or return as promised, and the bed is nowhere near Starwood quality, merely a matress on a platform, no box springs. Likewise the two, only two, elevators are slow, there is no service elevator and you can spend several trips with garbage, dirty laundry and lots of lengthy discussions without any regard to the hotel's customers. Some may also like the mini-mart eating facilities (I knew that when I reserved) but it is not a selling point. Placing sarongs in the hallway may try to, but fail to cover the old and ugly halways. The set-up of the rooms are also strange in that the sink area is fully visibly when the door to the hallway and when you sit at the desk, it is difficult to see the wall mounted TV. There are also no drawers for your clothing. On the positive side the staff is super-friendly as any I have encountered, the location is fantastic, and the fitness center had very nice equipment (although the major piece was broken). This is a nice place for some college kids living out of a suitcase but for business travel, this is just not the chain for that purpose.

“Nice stay at The Roosevelt” We stayed at The Roosevelt for three days and the visit was pleasant. We were in New York for business and the hotel was ideal for us. The hotel is located near a lot of what New York has to offer. The rooms are typically small for New York hotels. We arrived early at 9 am and while check was at least six hours away we advised to try back after noon as the room maybe ready. The service was par with the cost of the hotel and everyone we dealt with was friendly and helpful. The costs were a bit extreme, but this is New York and if you don't mind walking out the front door and down a block you can find reasonably priced "New York" meals and drinks. Overall a good visit and we will return.

“Disappointed..much better options in Phoenix metro area” Stayed at AGR July 1-5. Had suite directly over entrance to waterpark. Staff was nice, but follow thru on any service was absymal. Waterpark OK but very overcrowded. Rooms dated. Some of the equipment in fitness center crummy(but they had the hottest looking blonde personal trainer n the west!) Noise in suite above us at 1am not taken care of after call to front desk. Light bulb that burned out NEVER replaced all 5 days. Wrong room service order after re-confirming 3 times. May be decne t place to stay with samll kids, but for couples or older kids, there are far better resorts......Westin Kierland; Doubletree Paradise Valley , etc.

“Good and the Bad” The staff is great, the location so close to everything but...The Courtyard Tremont House has the smallest rooms I have been in. The rooms are about 10 x 10 and the bathroom is only about 5' x 5' and only had a shower stall. If you do choose to stay at this hotel ask for a room on the back side of the hotel. Unfortunately there is construction work going on across from the hotel and they are working all the time. Personally, I would not stay here unless there was no other choices.

“Maybe if you are only staying for one night.....” Stayed at this hotel for 1 night in May 2010. Thank god it was only for 1 night because you can hear EVERYTHING from your room. We heard baby crying, car noise from outside, people taking shower, people talking in the hall way, and etc. I've stayed at many hotels and I know you are bound to hear some noises when staying at hotels but this was probably one of the noiest hotel I've stayed in by far. There are many people walking around late at night and I'm assuming it's becasue this hotel is being booked a lot for "events" such as weddings. I heard a lady talking very loud (waking most hotel guests along the way to her room probably) walking by our room at 2 AM. Some people just are too ignorant to know what it is to be courteous. I'm glad that we used our Hilton Hhonors reward points to stay here and not actually paid for it. Outside: Looked a bit old. So-so looking. Lobby: Old style marble floor but otherwise clean and nice. Check-in/out: Check-in was done fast and pain-less. We were off to our room on the 6th floor in a few minutes. Our room number was odd number. Rom was facing a reservoir in front of the building which was good (well at least that's what we thought before we heard car noises at night). Check-out was done using the tv so again fast and pain-less. Room: Looks like they did "partial" remodeling. All the furnitures (headboard, night stand, chest, lamps, and desk) were old, yet chest had brand new black granite on top. Carpet was somewhat modern style but ceiling had one of those old style splatter texture. There was only 1 electric outlet on the desk. I didn't bring my laptop this time (since we were only away for a night and I had my blackberry so) but if I had all my "gadgets", I don't think having only 1 outlet would've been very convenient. They had a coffee machine and 2 coffee packets. One odd thing I noticed was that this room did not have any mirror (they had one in the bathroom but not in the room itself). Perhaps they thought, having mirror door for the closet area by the door was enough? Still, I found it a bit uncomfortable not having any mirror in the room. Other hotels usually have one by the desk area. No fridge in the room but I read that you can ask for one for a fee (it was $12 or $15 I think). Bathroom: This is the smallest bathroom I've ever seen in the hotels on the same level as Hilton (so I'm talking Marriott, Hyatt, Westin, and etc.). Two adults cannot use the sink at the same time and me and my hubby both are really on the skinny side. Again, I noticed "partial" remodeling done here too. The sink area (granite counter top, new faucets, new mirror) and tiles on the floor seemed modern. But bathtub area was another story. Bathtub itself was old and again on the smaller side. The tile by the bathtub was one of those cheapest white tiles. It showed mildew between the tiles as well. There was a metal towel rack by the tub and it was pretty rusty. The ammenities they had were shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash, body lotion, 2 soaps, and hair-dryer. Bathroom door looked like it's been painted many times over. Dining: We only had breakfast at the hotel (about $15 per person). Breakfast buffet was good. Made-to-order omelet, waffle, fruits (about 4-5 different kinds), various bakery items (muffins, croissants, and etc), freshly squeezed orange juice, cereal, oatmeal, smoked salmon, cheese tray, meat items (bacon & sausage), potato, and etc. Service: Most workers we enountered seemed nice. We didn't have to ask for anything or have any issues so that's about all I can say about their service. Pool: They have a heated indoor pool. But they do not have a whirlpool which was a bit disappointing. Workout area looked ok but we didn't actually used the facility. Overall, this was definitely not the worst hotel (or even close to it) I've stayed but I would not go back to this hotel or recommend to anyone.

“Good mix of elegant and practical” I stayed here 5 nights for a meeting. The lobby, corridors, and meeting rooms were beautiful with chandeliers, artwork, and a historical but not musty ambiance. Checkin was fast, but checkout was delayed because the person in front of me was charged for parking even though he didn't have a car! So be sure to look at your bill before paying because it took a while to correct the error. The bedroom was small by modern standards but as long as you don't clutter it up, there's room to work at the desk, sit in the chair (with a nice round ottoman), and of course sleep on a comfortable bed. Instead of a closet there was a wardrobe which is nice but when the doors are open they take up a lot of space. There were pocket doors on the TV cabinet so they didn't stick out. As it was the usual hot and humid Washington weather, it was nice to be able to adjust the temperature and AC with a wall control. Sometimes older hotels don't allow this but the Mayflower has been updated to digital thermostats. The bathroom was narrow and long with mirrors on 3 walls. I find that annoying because things we do in bathrooms are not necessarily supposed to be reflected everywhere we look. Toiletries were high-quality and the tub and shower were modern, clean, with plenty of hot water and water pressure. Towels were variable in thickness and absorbency. Elevators were slow because of the many floors. I didn't use the exercise room but my friends who tried it said it was crowded and extremely hot. All the food and drinks served during our meeting were excellent. I'm not sure of the exact cost of the room so I can't comment on the value, but certainly if you want a luxurious stay in this section of D.C. you won't be disappointed.

“A very average hotel” We were rather disappointed in this hotel. We chose it partly owing to it having the Forbes 5 Star rating - how have they held onto that I wonder? - and also for its location (which is extremely good). Other than its position in Boston, this is an OK, but definitely bog-standard city 4 star hotel. There is nothing that distinghishes it. Not the rooms, nor the restaurant, nor the service. There's nothing especially poor about it, but neither does it have anything strong to recommend it.

“Bring your earplugs and be adept when walking around bed” I agree with the other Tripadvisor comments- clean, small room, and NOISE coming from the outside city streets at all hours thru the flimsy plastic on the sides of the window a/c- heat unit (even on a higher floor). "Breakfast"- small variety of danish and coffee served only until 9 am even on weekends ( a guest on the single tiny elevator complained to me). When this hotel opened summer '09- the light breakfast fare included several imported cheeses, french rolls, and coffees until 11am. No storage area in the bathroom-only one small glass shelf, use the top of the dresser in the bedroom and no mirrors in bedroom(would help alot!) Very friendly at front desk with greetings,bringing water to room, wakeup calls, etc. Great location- near great shopping and wonderful restaurants- away from the hustle of Midtown.

“Very nice hotel!” We took a quick trip into Manhattan for the evening and stayed here. The hotel is tucked away just outside the Theatre district and Times Square area, just enough off the street where you felt a little removed from the hustle and bustle (which was very nice). The front desk staff was swift, courteous and quickly checked us in even when there seemed to be a lot of people in the lobby. They have two elevators and they were so slow (my only real gripe to this whole post), it seemed like it was staff members holding up the elevator moving things on and off the elevator. In any event, after waiting 5 min for the elevator, we got to our room and it was bigger than what I thought it was going to be. Only 8 rooms per floor (which is nice) and the room was modernly furnished. We went out to times square which was about 5-6 blocks away and we got to see all sorts of things along the way. We ate at Beer Authority and enjoyed a great filet minon and cider beer and then retired for the evening. It was strange because when I went to get under the covers it felt damp at the end of the bed. I closed my eyes and told myself its because it was washed earlier and not dried entirely... lol! Anyway, in any event its a great place to stay,a little off the beaten path (good for noise level), I highly recommend it.

“No complaints” This is an above average business hotel. There are restaurants nearby. The pool looked decent. There was plenty of parking with the new garage next door. Front desk staff was friendly. Free newspaper. Positives: Free breakfast included hot eggs. Negatives: Free Internet was slow during the evening.

“Excellent in its category.” I did'nt know Drury hotels before and I was amazed by the level of service offered at least at this property. Free breakfast, free food in the evening, free drinks, free newspapers, free powerful wireless internet. The room was big and perfectly clean, as well as the bathroom. Don't expect any "charm" from this business oriented hotel but just a great place to relax while travelling. And it is at walking distance from Northlake Mall.

“Average Hotel, But Convenient” The O'Hare Hilton is an older, tired looking hotel. It is average in almost every respect. However, if, as is often the case for me, you have a layover at O'Hare, it is a good place to grab a quick night's sleep, as the hotel is connected to the terminals.

“Once and Never Again” I went to Washington for a getaway weekend. I thought it would be fun to have pretty, panoramic, iconic views for this stay. I booked a special water view room that was $525 a night. Expensive but I had heard that Mandarin Oriental really understood luxury so I felt sure that they would make the splurge worthwhile. I could not have been more wrong. I checked in on Friday evening. The nice lady at the check-in said, "You are only with us for one night?" To which I replied loud and clear, "No, there must be a mistake, I am staying until Sunday morning." She looked at her computer and said, "My mistake." I was not offered a bellman to take up my bag which surprised me but in fact I only had a small bag so that was fine. I arrived in the room which did have a very pretty view of the basin, Lincoln Memorial and some kind of marina. The room was not on a high floor as I had asked but high enough to appreciate the vista. I took a bath before going out and was surprised turning on the tap to get sprayed by the tub's shower. Obviously the cleaning lady had left it at the shower setting after cleaning the tub. Really unpleasant surprise. The bath itself seemed very dated and in need of recaulking. The venetian shades in the bathroom looked more appropriate for an office than a luxury bathroom. The toiletries are Gilchrist and Soames and not luxurious and exclusive at all. I went down to the bar to meet a friend for a drink. No one was there to lead me to a table, the place was packed and clearly understaffed by rather unpolished waitstaff. I made my way to the only table that was outside, which was fine, and ordered a martini. Waiter was gone before I had a chance to say if I wanted it dry, dirty, with a twist... wow, they read minds? I had room service delivered to my room that night. I asked, as a vegetarian, for a fried rice with tofu instead of meat, I was told, no problem, and then it arrived with pork and tofu!! And lukewarm. No flowers on table, no bread. Incredibly basic. Next morning I went out at 9 AM for a run expecting room to be cleaned by the time I returned (no sign available on door to ask for servicing btw) at 11AM- nope. Went out to lunch and returned to find room being cleaned at 4PM!! I went down to pool area to wait for my room to be cleaned. Pool is very much an afterthought. No music, no ambiance, one little door open to the outdoors to a very lackluster patio. Spa is much nicer and the hot tub was nice although in this day and age I think it's sad not to have a mixed-sex spa tub. Unless you're having a mother-daughter weekend who wants to sit in a single sex tub? Needed to get on interned and found out that Mandarin Oriental charges a fee for this. Lots of places to do but when you are spending that kind of money don't you think they could throw in the internet connection? So cheesy. Back from the pool my key no longer worked so I went down to the desk and asked for it to be fixed. Desk man fixed it without comment. I was in the bath at 7:30 PM getting ready to go out when they came by for turndown service. Asked them come back in an hour. They never returned. At 2 AM a loud banging on the door woke me up. I nearly died of fright (well, not really, but you can imagine). It was security announcing I was illegally occupying the room and should have left the day before. Mystery of non-functioning key now clear to me but why desk clerk didn't catch it at 5PM instead of 2AM we will never know. I explained that it was the front desk's mistake and that I always intended on staying 2 nights and not one. The next morning when I went to check out I asked for an explanation of events. I was met with great defensiveness and only the most lukewarm and insincere apology. Certainly no refund or rebate was offered. I was completely offended by their attitude. There was a man lurking about during this exchange and as an afterthought the desk clerk asked this man, a limo driver, to take me to the airport "for the normal charge of a taxi". How generous!! This creep took me to the airport and had the gall to charge me $25 which was $10 more than the cab charged me go from the airport to the hotel. Talk about one final kick in the teeth! I was going to have dinner at the hotel's restaurant, just for conveniences sake, but after the cocktails arrived 20 minutes after the almost inedible oysters (full of grit, lukewarm, and a tasteless variety - only type offered), we decided to go elsewhere. I was completely unimpressed by the decor, the inexperience and poor training of the staff (who seemed in general a nice if hapless lot), and the general lack of warmth and luxury. Something is dreadfully wrong with this property. I don't know if it is a problem only with this hotel or across the board with the chain but it certainly takes it off my list of hotel brands to consider when I travel.
“可もなく不可もなく” HHのDIAなので、ラウンジアクセスと朝食券を頂きました。 部屋は普通、TVがブラウン管であったのにはびっくり・・・ ジムは地下にあり、一通りなそろってました。 ラウンジに関しては、カクテルタイムには人が多くなり 持ち帰っている人も・・・・ ただし、アルコールは有料・・・ホットミールは2品のみ・・・ ラウンジ朝食は完全なるコンチネンタル・・・ 一階でのバフェの方が良い。

“Fine for the price” We recently got a rate of $66.00 per night through hotwire, and stayed 2 nights. The hotel lobby was a bit outdated, but the rooms were very nice. The had all of the amentites of a 4 star hotel, but, the overall feel was about a 3 and 1/2. The location was excellent, right off of the tollway, just north of the Galleria. For the same price, I would stay at this property again. You can barely get a Motel 6 in Dallas, Tx for $66.00. Had I paid the rack rate of $189 and up, I would not have been pleased.

“Good Enough but could use some renovations” Not bad actually, particularly since it is well located to my Houston office. The gym is fine; breakfast is fine and the rooms aren't bad. Could use new elevators and the junior suites are located right next to the elevators which makes them a bit noisy. Otherwise, the hotel is good enough for its price.

“Awsome stay” Will always go back it was the best service,location and really clean. Just amazing the inside of the hotel and the suites were huge i will always reccomend it for any one who likes luxury and treated the best.

“Historic Gem” Stayed here three nights on a business trip. This is an old New York gem, lots of history. Sure, they are small rooms, but it was built that way in 1919. So know what you are getting. First, if you hit at a busy time, check-in is long,. There are 1,400 rooms, so it can back up. Second, service is good, rooms are CLEAN and it was relatively quiet, so I could sleep well at night. It is not a Hyatt, it is not a Hilton. It is an historic hotel with a killer location that does fairly well despite it's age. I plan to be back in two weeks.

“You get what you paid for” Pros: - proximity to Muni/Bart station (across the street) - great rates (booked for $70 on Labor Day wknd) - helpful staff Cons: - area is largely inhabited by SF's homeless - no great restaurants/bars within walking distance

“Nice, but quirky” I stayed at this hotel one night for business. First the upside..it's a newer property, very modern and updated. Desk and staff service is excellent. The common areas and rooms were clean and bright. The bed was the very comfortable Doubletree sweet sleeper..but there were a number of quirks as well. Even though close to the freeway, the property is tricky to navigate to..It's in the midst of a commercial development, you need to approach from the right entrance. Get directions!,.. Second, whoever painted the parking lot sized the spaces for subcompact cars..spaces are tight..if you have a larger rental and worry about getting hit with extra charges for dings, you won't sleep well here! The room layout was odd. First, it was smaller than comparabily priced rooms..fine for one person, but a couple would be bumping into each other. Beyond that, the furniture arrangement was weird! The king size bed directly faced a large picture window..which would have been nice if one had a great view of the beach or sunset. But the room faced directly into an office building..kind of made you feel like the bed was a stage. Adding to the effect was a sofa that directly faced the bed (and got in the way of access to the window blinds which I had to close)..the whole layout reminded one of an eighteenth century betrothal (where the kind and queen were watched to make sure the marriage was consumated). OK..I'm overdramatizing, , but the bed felt like a stage..I didn't especially like it, and I'm sure my wife would have hated it if she had been along. FInal good point, they have a nice breakfast buffet. Even with the quirks, I'd stay here again, but they'd rank a lot higher on my preference list if they'd address the issues they can fix (the location is something they're just stuck with)

“Great First Time in New York” Although I travel quite a deal, this was my first stay in New York. I chose this based on location to another hotel our friends were staying at so we were close, but I was very pleased. Some of the goods and bads: Goods: Rooms were new and clean Although the rooms were small, it wasn't overly so, and I'm sure it's on par with other NY hotels The king bed we had was very, very comfortable The shower was nice, strong Great flatscreen HD tv with good channel selection Great location, was able to easily get to many parts of the city and our favorite - Eataly! Bads: They act like the rooftop bar is a nightclub...it's not, get over it. They announce parties coming up on the elevator, and late night, instead of a cool place to chill, they had a DJ blaring music for like 10 people. It didn't fit the vibe of the place The elevators themselves were ridiculous, it seemed to take forever and had no rhyme or reason to their pattern, not to mention they commandeer one elevator just for the "nightclub" It was a bit loud Overall, I'd stay there again and was very pleased.

“Decent if a Deal” We stayed for 1 night in a Deluxe King on the 16th floor with a (partial) river view. We got a good deal so it was acceptable to us. I would not spend $200 or more for this hotel though. It was clean and the staff were friendly and gracious.

“No good reason to go here, no reason to stay away.” If this Travelodge is near where you want to be--it is near Millennium Park--and you don't want to spend a lot of money, this is fine. It is better than the bigger more well known Congress Hotel across the Street. In fact, I stayed here because I saw it when staying at the Congress and being so unhappy there. Travelodge was clean, quiet, simple. Nothing spectacular but for about $125 you get a bed, bathroom and the usual SMALL room. Had trouble with reservation but don't know if it was the hotel or the online booking. I had printed off confirmation so I was ok. They have one computer downstairs where you can print off boarding passes for major airlines for free, everything else requires credit card.

“Perfect for Theater” The location was perfect for the theater. Room was quiet and clean. Service was great. There is a high turn around and they know how to deal with it. Quickest breakfast in town in the lobby cafe. Do not hesitate to stay here.

“Great Location and Value!” I took a gamble on the "unpublished rates" through Expedia- this gives you a hotel rating/area/rate but no name until after it is paid and booked. Well, it turned out to be great! The Hotel I stayed in last time in Austin rates were too high for what they offered so this hotel was better in cleanliness, rooms and certainly service. Location was also great! On the river- My only complaint and its just a learning experience and a newly found preference (or not) I do not care for the adjustable "sleep number" beds. I simply could not find my number.. (sounds funny but it was a bit frustrating) I eventually fell asleep and I do prefer this hotel over my last for service, staff, rooms, views and value.

“Service makes it # 1” We recently spent one night at the Lenox Hotel after a fall foliage trip through New England. I see now why everyone rates this hotel #1 in Boston! From the moment we stopped our car at the door, we were greeted as though we were special guests of this lovely establishment. The doorman, Peter, was extremely gracious and helpful and set the bar high for the service to follow. Well, the bar never dipped and everyone we encountered during our stay was extremely friendly, always helpful, and NEVER too busy to attend to our needs. We were upgraded to a junior suite which was a fabulous corner room with 2 beds that were absolutely some of the most comfortable I have every slept in. The room was very spacious and the cold bottled water waiting for us in the fridge was a nice welcome. Other hotels could learn a great deal from this establishment. I highly recommend spending a few extra dollars when in Boston and stay at the Lenox. You won't be sorry!!!!!!!!!!!

“Small rooms; misleading photos on Best Western Website” We stayed here Thanksgiving eve night, based on the rate from the Best Western web site. I opted for the "suite" with the sofa pullout. Hah ! Fooled again ! It was actually smaller than most standard hotel rooms. Also, the water heater was out that night and the front desk played dumb. Don't you love it when they do that ? Thankfully, it was repaired the next morning. Having said that, the exterior was extremely cool and the breakfast was outstanding. There is no lobby to speak of and the parking is minimal. Don't know what they do when the 15 or so spaces are filled. The bathrooms were spacious and clean enough for me. The rooms surround the open courtyard which looks nice but any conversation going on can be heard by all and you definitely do not want a room on Robertson Blvd, which is a high traffic road. This property is on the "fringe" of Beverly Hills, which accounts for the lower pricing. A better option, for about the same money as I wound up paying for my "suite", is the AAA rate at the Crown Plaza on Beverly Blvd. But this is an acceptable property, and I would stay here again. Just don't pay extra for the "suite".

“Nice Surprise” After reading some of the reviews concerning the Hudson, we were a bit worried. However, a double bed room proves to be roomy enough for three individuals. The staff was friendly and prompt. Overall, I would gladly stay here again.

“Good conference hotel” This is a nice conference hotel. The rooms are clean and spacious, there are several restaurants on location, but all are quite expensive. Numerous heated pools outdoors are nice. Overall there's not much to do and a long drive to key attractions. I wouldn't have picked it for a family vacation. Pricey and boring.

“Very comfortable / convenient airport hotel” I spent one night at this hotel before flying out of Seattle. The hotel is well located across the street from the airport and the light rail route into central city Seattle. The hotel staff was very friendly, helpful and eager to serve / please. This certainly was very noticeable and one of the highlights of the hotel. Both the front desk and the room service staff get top marks. The staff at the restaurant for breakfast were also very cheerful and helpful and personally attentive, even though it was obvious they were busy and I had a free breakfast voucher (I did leave a tip, but the staff had no guarantees I would do so). I had a courtyard facing room and it was very light, airy, comfortable and spacious. The bathroom was well stocked, but a bit on the small side. I could hear hallway noise, but as the runways are parallel to the hotel, I do not recall hearing any airplane noise. I also did not hear any noise from adjoining rooms. The only negative about the hotel was the internet connection. As I am a Hilton Honors Gold member, I got free internet. I do not know if this was the problem or not. But the connection to the Hilton Honors network from my laptop must have dropped 10 times. Basically every time I opened a browser, I had to re-log in. I have stayed at many different Hilton properties and while it seems a number of them now require one to re-log in every 24 hours, I have never had this experience before. I also had just spent nine nights at a budget hotel in Lewiston ID and never once had a dropped wireless connection, so I have to believe the problem is the hotel's, not my laptop. The garage is a bit of a hike from the front desk. This is one hotel where you definitely want to stop / park at the main entrance while you check in. Overall: great service, great location, very nice and comfortable rooms. Just needs a better internet connection.

“Small but great in every other way” Not much to add here: Great hotel with cool amenities. Rooms tend to be small, but you've got everything you need: Comfy bed... TV if needed... FREE (!) wifi that's actually fast for a hotel (7Mbps down)... free purified chilled water near all elevators... automated check-in/check-out... business center with dedicated boarding pass printing... EXCELLENT location... Shares a property with Club Quarters. Not sure how that works out, since it's one building, but no complaints here.

“Good hotel, poor service” Actually I wanted to score this at 3.5 not 4, but this is not possible! The hotel is in a good location at the heart of Manhattan - though very busy outside so if you prefer a quieter location would look elsewhere. The rooms and facilities are very clean and comfortable and I had a room with a good view. The bathroom was a bit small, but not a big issue. The room itself was on a high floor and therefore no street noise; but I had a corner room near the ice maker and this creates a lot of noise. Corner rooms come at a premium, so make sure you ask for the ones at the end of the corridor away from the ice machines (i.e. not rooms ending 01 or 02). The service I received was poor - and out of keeping with what I have experienced in the same chain before. At check-in the clerk was all set to charge my card for the room, which was pre-paid; I made a few small requests - clock to be fixed, for slippers, mini-bar to be restocked - and on each occasion I had to request at least twice. In the case of the clock, once it was sorted the engineer left all manner of debris - boxes, spare parts etc. - in the room and I had to ask for it to be removed. The concierge was often not on duty and had to be prompted to provide me with a confirmation number/receipt for the car I booked to the airport.

“Good Value and good location” The hotel is located very close to Hobby Airport, but is very quiet with no noise from air traffic. It appears to be a relatively newer property and has the amenities expected of a three star hotel. Good breakfast, eggs, pork products, biscuits, etc. I would stay here again, but would note the following negatives. The room had two double beds, but very little storage space for clothing. There was a refrigerator and microwave in the room however. I expected most of the guests to be business types, but we were there during Spring Break. There were a large number of children who could be noisy and disruptive. There were, what appeared to be, a large number of families from the lower socio-economic levels of society. They seemed to lack the basic behaviors and disciplines we have become accustomed to in middle class travel. They were often loud and all hours of the night and rude and defensive when requested to be quiet.

“Cute and Cozy” They gave me a queen room facing the inside of the building so my view out the window was a vent. Well I was only there for 2 days, so it didn't much matter to me. I was planning a conference at the Bridgewater restaurant venue space and so the walk was only 2 blocks, which was more important to me rather than the view. Perhaps you may want to ask for a Street View room, but I'm not sure how the noise factor would be. After the conference I didn't want to walk back to the Best Western to catch a limo, so the front desk was kind enough to oder the airport limo to pick us up at the Bridgewaters venue. Very good service. Ok tasting cookies at 3pm daily at the front desk of Best Western (although Subways are much better). Showerhead was new, so that's was nice. Old TV and cabinetry, but decent. Good rate and good area. For those of you who have been to the Distillery District in Toronto, it's very much like that - cobblestone streets closed off to the cars so great for pedestrians shopping. High end stores, very trendy area.

“Comfortable” This hotel is in the heart of it all in the Chelsea, Flatiron area of NYC, but it is on a quiet side street, so you can get away from it all. My relatives stopped by before we went out, and they live on a noisy NYC street. They made the claim that they couldn't sleep in our room because it was too quiet! I used frequent stay points for 3 nights for Halloween and the NYC Marathon, and I was given the top floor (11th floor) in the back (quieter than street noise). The room is bigger than any other NYC room I have ever had, and there was plenty of room for both of us to walk around and live comfortably for the 4 days, 3 nights. The room I got has a seating area with a full-sized pullout couch, a small closet, refrigerator, coffee maker, safe, desk, ironing board and iron. In the sleeping portion had 2 double beds, a night stand and cable TV. The beds had good sheets and were comfortable for me. The bathroom is small, but it has a full sized tub and shower. There was plenty of soap, shampoo, conditioner, and moisturizer for us, and 4 sets of towels. The windows open in the bathroom and bedroom in this hotel, so it was nice to get air in the room, and air out the bathroom after a shower. There is free wifi in the room, and there is an hardwire internet cord if you don't have wifi on your computer. There is a business center on the 1st floor, and there is a minimum $3 charge to use the computer and printer (we printed out tickets to the Empire State Bld). There is only one ice vending machine on the 1st floor. There are 2 well maintained elevators in the building, but they are slow, so going and getting ice from the 11th floor took a while. So, as we were going out for the evening, I took the ice bucket plastic bag in my purse. When we got back for the evening, I got ice from the ice machine on the 1st floor in the plastic bag to save me a trip back and forth on the slow elevators. There is vending on the 1st floor for soft drinks and snacks. Conveniently, there is a CVS at the end of the street if you need anything CVS carries. There is also a "Greek Deli" convenience market almost across the street from the CVS, so if you want any type of snack, soft drink, fruit, prepared "Greek Deli" foods 24 hrs/day, there you go. There is also a Chinese takeout place next to the lobby of the Comfort Inn. I don't know if it is good or not, but it is convenient. There is free breakfast at this hotel which includes breads, hard boiled eggs, cereal, juice, milk and donuts. The breakfast room looks like it used to be a bar before the building became a Comfort Inn. There is also a small but efficient and free workout room with a treadmill and 2 other cardio machines, and a bottled water. The street this hotel is on is quiet, and not a main road where taxis drive, and our stay was very quiet! Along the street are some well established antique stores. On weekends, across the street in a parking lot, is NYC style flea market that has been there since the 1980s (or as long as we have known about it), and the trinkets, gifts, antiques, carvings, art, jewelry, jade, records, etc are well worth taking a look at on your way in and out of the hotel on Saturday or Sunday afternoons. Down at opposite end of the street from the CVS is Madison Square Park (where the original Madison Square Arena used to be). It appears for the month of October is a street fair with food vendors, and artisan shop vendors. There were crepes, beer, wine, frites, bbq, apple dumplings, Belgian waffles, and other tasty treats that were so good! The shop vendors had hand and artisan made jewelry, craft toys, hand bags, dolls, clothing, home decor and a lot of other craft goods. After Nov 1st they all were moving to Union Square for the holiday shopping time. Because we were there on Halloween, the Halloween Parade came down 6th Ave and ended about 2 blocks away from the hotel. Surprisingly, we heard no noise from the parade at all, inside the hotel! It was fun to people watch along the parade route, and it was almost better than N.O. during Mardi Gras. We were also there on Nov 1st, All Saints Day, and down 6th Ave again was this long street fair with fair food vendors and lots of trinket booths for as far as we could see! It was great fun!

“still awesome” spent the weekend at Towers. still amazing place. this was a return trip and my second review for this hotel. consistently high service. private elevators to top floors and the peace from regular NY, love it. suggestion- ask for luxury suite, great size and elegant suites. If you are looking for new and mordern, this is not the place. this is old school classy yet very upto date

“Stylish and modern” We had two rooms for one Wednesday night. The rooms were large, clean, and stylish. The room was in earth tones--very calming feel. The beds were comfy, with a ton of pillows. We had the buffet breakfast downstairs--a nice spread, though a bit pricey. The only major knock is the $12.95 charge for using the in-room Internet. If we had wanted to go someplace for dinner, the hotel was a ways away from downtown--but we didn't need to eat, so no problem. Got the hotel at a nice price (less than $50 per room) on Priceline. The going rate for the hotel on Expedia and Travelocity was $174 per room, which would've been an excessive price to pay.

“A True Grand Dame!” What a beauty! I had stayed there over 20 years ago so I was really excited to go back and see it again. Has a suite. It was superb. Roomy, great view.The staff truly helpful. One of the beast locations in Boston. I would love to go again!

“The best accomodation to visit downtown San Francisco” We stayed there early july with husband and 2 teenager daughters. Contrary to other HIE, this one is outstanding. Rooms are quite large for 4 . The breakfast area is also pretty big. It is the perfect place to stay for families, withnthe fisherman wharf just around the corner. Groceries are also near by . walk distance from beach and girhardeli square. while you are there , do not miss the hop in hop off tour bus to have a full appreciation of this wonderful city.

“Looks good from the outside” The good is you can easily walk over to the Plaza of the Americas and Westin for lunch. There is a trolley stop close by to head to the West End for dinner. Rooms (some) have a wide screen hi-def tv. Reviews about the location are correct. Downtown Dallas is on a down turn and the areas around this hotel show this. The lounge was nice, pricey but thats how it goes with hotels. Rooms facing the bus depot will be entertained by numerous birds singing all night long. Its not a la la singing either, but loud screeching. The birds hide in the trees that surround the bus depot. No free wireless in the rooms. You can print boarding passes in the business center but the staff get huffy because you are not paying like others do to check email. I think the hotel was used to serving the larger conferences and everyone else could take a jump. Haliburton was there having a big shindig. The worst thing about my stay: as I turned in one night, I noticed something on the wall. It was a cockroach about 2 inches long. Im not usually queasy or picky about insects, but not cockroaches and no way could I sleep while that was in the room. I should have called the front desk but didnt want to have to get dressed and wait for them to respond so I knocked the roach off the wall with the phone book then beheaded the roach with the trash can before it tried to hide. As both parts still squirmed I picked up the pieces with the do not disturb card and flung it outside by my door. In the morning the card and bug pieces were still there, which was understandable as they wouldnt vacuum at night, but when I returned to my room at 4PM the card was gone but the roach was still there. It stayed there until I checked out. The halls are NOT cleaned on a daily basis. As you might expect, that made the rest of my stay uncomfortable. I shook out all of my clothes and kept them in my bag, zipped up tightly. I would spot check the walls the rest of my stay on a regular basis. I had some snacks from a reception that was inside a drawer, but threw it away as I kept imagining the roaches eating the food while I was out. Adams Mart was set to become a Sheraton shortly after my stay so hopefully they will improve the business aspects. Also they should call an exterminator and make sure the cleaning schedule is followed precisely.

“Disappointing service” Stayed in one of the Lafayette Suites with wife and baby. Check-in was fine; room was OK but rather ordinary. Small mini-bar fridge with sensors absolutely packed with stuff - so no room for any personal storage eg. milk for baby. They initially wanted to charge us to bring up another fridge but relented in the end. I must agree with another reviewer about the room service charges - automatic 18% gratuity plus a 'delivery fee' of about $4. It's either one or the other. Why don't they just add on a 'removal of plates fee' and 'dish washing fee' too. Breakfast was uninspiring with somewhat limited selection from the buffett but the service was good. Unfortunately the same can't be said for housekeeping. As we were heading out for lunch, we met with one of the housekeepers who was cleaning a couple of doors down. Explained that we'll be back in 3 hours as the baby needs to sleep then. She said she'll clean our room next. Upon return 3 hours later, room not done yet and it seems like they were also done with this floor. If my baby wasn't asleep I would have called them back. Check-out was also sub-par; she seemed annoyed that I asked a question about the invoice. In summary, I think you could definitely do better at a different hotel. Unfortunately for us, hotels in Boston were fully booked due to Graduation Week and also a number of conferences in town.

“There is nothing elegant about this hotel.” There is nothing elegant about this hotel--the lobby is less tasteful and more trammeled than the average shopping mall. In fairness, other than the mega hotels in Las Vegas, Hyatt Regency Chicago (HRC) is one of the biggest hotels in the country. You will wait in line for most things, and calling the switchboard is like calling an airline--press 1 for X, press 2 for Y. Rooms are small, though the desk agent "upgraded" us to a room on the top floor with river, skyline, and lake views--still, hard to believe some pay $300 a night for this room that gets swallowed up by the king bed. Positives--the beds are comfy, and the soap is nice. LIke the curved shower rod. Then again, internet is ridiculously priced at $14 per 24 hours. . .and it didn't even work well; they rebated it for me. If you've got a car, you'll pay $46 plus tax to park, per night. . .Location, a block off Michigan Avenue, is an asset, as is the well maintained, nicely appointed fitness center--free to guests. All the same, only stay here if you get a great deal on Priceline--I got an $81 rate--or if you are staying for a convention. . .and then, don't eat there.

“rooms not as nice as Westin” I stayed at the Four Points for government business and was disappointed that the "free breakfast" offered to government employees was certainly not offered at this location, despite the fact I paid the same amount of $$$ to stay here that I paid to stay at the Westin Michigan Avenue, and the amenities at the Westin Michigan Avenue were far nicer. The hotel is new and work is ongoing. Despite the fact that I'm a Starwood Gold Member I was given no upgrade of any kind. I'm beginning to realize the Starwood Gold program is pretty much a sham. The hotel staff was nice, and the hotel is well located. Rooms are small and the hallway was way too long - took quite awhile to find my room and a long time to get out of building, etc. Although small, the room was sufficient. The #1 thing that I can say about this hotel is that I loved the fitness center. Although it's not huge by any standard, the equipment is brand new with TV screens, and they even have headphones available for travelers like me who forget to bring the headphones. Also, I'm having problems getting my Starwood points for my hotel stay. Guess the hotel screwed up. I'm having to submit all kinds of documentation, etc. to ensure I get my points and credit for the stay. To what avail??? Stay here if you must, but there are much nicer hotels in the area.

“If you want clean and location on a budget” I visit NYC frequently and used to stay in over priced hotels which surprisingly lacked service and cleanliness. I actually found it when I was staying at the Waldorf and had a really bad experience and realized I am overpaying for a name. I looked across the street and saw the Marriott Eastside and asked to see a room (the hotel was renovated the previous month). Marriott Eastside is no frills however the rooms are surprisingly larger than your average NYC shoebox and since they were renovated a few years back...new and clean. The location is great, right across the street from the Waldorf-Astoria and within walking distance to everything Midtown has to offer. No frills to me means they do not have a grandiose lobby, restaurant, etc. I have stayed in hotels that were twice the price and not as clean or large. I go to NYC to see the city and I am a stickler for cleanliness so if the room is clean and the location is nice I am sold. I gave it 4 stars because it lacks the "bells and whistles" of some hotels (dining, spa). Give it a try, the rates are fantastic and you will get something many of the other area hotels lack.

“Not a fan of this hotel” I've stayed at quite a few Kimpton hotels and have always been impressed, but not with this one. As other travelers noted below, the lobby location is awkward, up a flight of stairs and difficult to locate, and the rooms are very small. When I checked into my room there was a large dog cage at the end of the bed. In such a cramped space it took up a lot of room, and I called down to the front desk requesting to be moved to an animal-free room. I like dogs, but the thought of sleeping in a room where a dog has been staying in such a cramped space didn't sit well with me. The front desk said they would move me to another room. My new room was a few floors up but the same layout and very small. I was traveling alone but if I was with my husband I don't know how we would have managed to get ready at the same time due to the extremely small bathroom. I barely had room to put my things on the bathroom counter. The building was very old and the heater near the window was loud and made the room look outdated. The view was not great either - I looked out at a parking garage and I could hear the train. My room was also right outside the elevator and I could hear people coming and going late night and early morning. My coworker said she could hear a couple fighting next door to her room as the walls were very thin. There were some pros - 312 restaurant downstairs had delicious food, they had free wine hour each night (this is standard with Kimptons) and since I'm a Kimpton InTouch member I received a $10 voucher to the minibar and free internet. The rooms were very clean, great shower pressure, comfortable beds, and the staff was very nice. I love how they use Aveda bath products. Great location too. However, I couldn't get over the size of the rooms and bathrooms and wasn't a fan of the decor or thin walls. I have stayed in many other hotels in Chicago (Kimpton's Monaco, Intercontinental, Omni, Sofitel) and will definitely choose one of those next time.

“Nice Boutique Hotel” I love the decor of this property. It is all updated, recently re opened with a complete remodel. the bathroom is tight and the room on the small side, but the location cant be beat and the staff is friendly. It is a good value and great location for a traveler on vacation or holiday. My stay was for business and I prefer more space in my room. When I travel for vacation, I dont spend much time in the room, but for business travel, I do tend to work at a desk and spend more time in my room. The complimentary breakfast was very clean, lots of selection, above average for a continental breakfast. The front desk team is always greeting you with a smile and I appreciate that.

“An average "W" experience” GOOD: Staff = very friendly and helpful without that "W" attitude Acura shuttle service was a plus Location = very close to everything, easy access Beach/Bar = roof top beach/bar was cute and fun Lobby = turns into a club/lounge on Saturday nights. Music was quite loud. AVERAGE: WET = It's more for looks, way too small for swimming SHOWER PRESSURE = on Level 6, not very strong BAD: Our room's windows were very dirty (see pic), did not expect this from this level of hotel. Parking must be done by valet each time, all courteous, but a bit annoying to have to wait for them to drive the car around the block. Furniture, Decor - were a bit beat up.

“Location Location Location” Right around the corner from the Mall and all the museums, this place served it's purpose. No 'real' food around unless you want to eat in their restaurant, or 'Bucks, or across the way in a French bakery (which is not bad, but it's not really dinner, if you know what I mean) However, Metro is right there (L'Enfant Plaza I believe) and you can go pretty much anywhere with that or a quick cab up the Hill. Our room was just a room, and that was fine. You're not in DC to lay around at watch TV (which was difficult in this room, as it was a corner room, and the TV was catty corner to the bed) The room was clean, the bed comfy, and checking in and out wasn't a hassle. The room prices are completely out of line, but it's Tourist Central, and is what it is. The parking sucks. In Washington, parking sucks, but this was awful. The garage below the hotel was full, but most of the cars were government vehicles with reserved parking spaces. (But what did I expect) Be aware that if you try to park on the first level near the hotel elevators, there is a dead end, and you will have to back up to get yourself out of the maze. We ended up parking in the last space the furthest away from the elevators. We travel light, and don't have strollers or anything like that to deal with, so it wasn't a really big deal (grumble-worthy, but not a big deal) but I could see where it'd be a hassle if you had to pack in a ton of stuff from the furthest reaches of the parking garage. And it's an additional $30 plus tax to park overnight. Overall, if you're going to DC to take in all the culture and don't want to go far from 'home base', this would be a great place to stay. Buy some snacks or breakfast stuff and keep in your room. The breakfast buffet is another $19 a person.
