I think the next time we go to DC, we'll get a room further away from the middle of the universe, simply for the $$ aspect. Holiday Inn is getting a little carried away with their room rates anyway, so we may also have to think about changing venues.

“Stayed Multiple Times” I've stayed at multiple Thompson hotels in NYC and the Smyth hnds down is my favorite. Extremely friendly and attentive staff. The door boys are very attractive :) I'm on my way back in October for the 4th time. Great central location for shopping in Soho. Always a wonderful stay at the Smyth.

“Minor disappointment but still OK” Stayed there for 6 nights in October’07. I was expecting something a little bit more “fancy” based on the webpage, so perhaps four stars instead of three stars actually received. Certainly didn’t except full luxury hotel, but still something slightly more. Maybe this just is the normal level of Homewood Suites chain that I simply wasn’t aware of since it was my first stay in any Homewood hotel. Breakfast was not something to write home about, in fact it was pretty poor. Just a small hot section, one sort of bagel, one sort of muffin etc. Vegetable/fruit selection extremely limited. There was free food (such as spaghetti) in the evening which was OK, including African Amber in the tap which was a nice surprise. Huge two room suite, probably ~70 square meters with e.g. small kitchen and large flatscreen TV. Windows facing Puget Sound and Space Needle on the other side (top of Needle visible behind houses). Location is OK, though not certainly in the downtown. ~5min walk to Space Needle area (museums, restaurants, amusement park etc) and monorail service to city centre. Nearest convenience store right next door, a nice sports bar a block away. So maybe a minor disappointment, but still pretty OK. No major complaints as such. Would I return there? Hmmm, perhaps, but would check also for other options.

“Still a wonderful place to stay in DC in DuPont Circle” I had last stayed in the Washington Hilton in 2003- heading back there for this year's BIO conference I looked around eager to try something different- the reviews for the Hilton were not that great but I had really enjoyed my stay all those years ago....ultimately, I cancelled all of my other reservations (inlcuding the other Hiltons) and decided on going back. GREAT CHOICE! Even with the snafus of not having a king room available upon check-in-although admittedly I was a bit early. I took a double and requested a king as soon as it became available. All the staff was professional but the most amazing standout was the maintenance engineer...my tv did not work that first night and when he came in I was already a little ticked at the double room- when he found he could not get the satellite feed right he offered me another double and I explained why I did not want to that....he felt horrible that I was unhappy and I said no big deal, I don't watch much tv. He followed up with a kind offer of a one free room-service meal for my troubles which was a delight and made sure I was in the right room the next day- which I was- a beautiful corner king that made me feel like I was in my own private place. SUre it was a long walk from the elevators but I loved it- the windows all opened and housekeeping was excellent. All in all I truly enjoyed my stay. After seeing me buy my diet coke with lime two evenings in a row before heading up to the room, the clerk in the gift shop was so pleasant and friendly the remaining nights- even asking where I had been when I skipped a visit. The gym was well-equipped and clean, and the location is amazing- walking distance to a nice blend of Dupont Circle shops and cafes-feeling very safe by myself...the concierge floor was great for stopping in and grabbing a cookie or a some coffee. Nothing fancy, but well-staffed with friendly folks and handy. It is a great choice and if you believe some things improve with age, this would be the right place:)

“The best experience in the best Hotel, Period!” I have a special place in my heart for this hotel. The staff was the greatest I have yet to encounter. There are no words nor description I can create to give you an idea of how amazing this place is. If you have the opportunity to stay here, do it. Make sure you eat in the restaurant, and go to the gym. Full size basketball court, amazing pool, rock climbing wall, you name it, the fitness ROOMS have it. The people I met in the elevator were A list celebrities, the Power players I met at dinner were heavy hitters, and being in the same room with these individuals gave me a great sense of pride. I could talk about this place for hours and compliment them, and when I see my colleagues, we still do.

“Will stay here again” Great property if you are here for a convention. Two hotels in one, you pick if you need a room or suite. I stayed on the Residence Inn side and enjoyed the extra space and included breakfast, which was better than the usual Residence Inn fare. Extra afternoon snacks, good little gym and small market made it a good stay. I will stay here again in January.

“Room and view was great!” Well, when you go to Philadelphia you don't except to have a nice view of a navel ship and water way..but I did. The food and staff were very friendly. Oddly, I was arrived during a bad snow/ice storm, and the valet service was perfect! I actually have to return to his hotel for business in September...I have booked it already!

“Excellent stay and great staff attitudes” I stayed for one night on a business trip, and was pleasantly surprised at the quality of this hotel. There was nothing particularly special about the nice king size room - it looked like many nicer hotel rooms I have been in - but the bathroom was SPOTLESS! Not a stray hair or water stain on any surface. I was amazed. The front desk staff was cheerful and pleasant, and gave a great recommendation for dinner nearby. Free wifi was a plus, and a taxi stand is just around the corner. I highly recommend this hotel - for business or for pleasure.

“great location” We stayed at the prescott for 6 days, we traveled from Ireland, and wanted some were central. This hotel has great location rooms small clean and comfortable. Mini bar expensive so give it a miss, nice bar with the lovely Brian mixing a mean margarita, we found him very informative.all staff very friendly and helpful we were happy with our choice and would saty here again.We even had th epleasure of an earthquake lol,

“Modern, clean, good service and good location” Great location 1 block from 6th street ...3 blocks from the capital. very clean and modern building, with large atrium. the rooms either face the atrium or outside. Enjoyable stay, and would stay there again.

“Had Fun On Splurge” My 84 year-old dad picked me up at DFW and on a whim I asked if he would mind hanging out with me at one of the newer hotels downtown. I knew one of them had a terrific infinity pool, so stopped by the W Hotel, and that was the one. SO decided to go with whatever they had as far as a suite went, so they gave us a WOW suite on the 14th floor (1401), and it was terrific and terribly expensive ($629) for me. The receptionist gave us complimentary breakfast for 2 since we were having a boys' night out. Dad thought it was silly and fun (though I didn't devulge the cost; told him my boss had given me a bonus, haha). The room was all odd angles, but really bright with floor to ceiling windows and great views of DT Big D and the freeway and industrial area (you have to be from Dallas to even begin to think this is pretty). It was fun just looking at the skyline which seems ever changing with all the building going on in this area. The pool was wonderful, and good stiff drinks at the bar. VERY WINDY, but OK with me. Almost blew my old dad over. Had very good hamburgers in the room and a bottle of red wine for about $60, but breakfast was terrific: eggs benedict and french toast for absolutely free (was about $50 on the menu). Way too much money, but the room was so weird it was cool. Separate bedroom with chase lounge, big bathroom, huge heavy curtains everywhere, big windows, strange sliding wooden doors; i kept getting lost; at least 2 bathrooms; the terrace was HUGE and had this fun round sofa that spun around. Directly across from the American Airlines arena. Gave us late (2:00) checkout without asking. It was a fun mini-vacation that I couldn't afford. I'll do it again sometime.

“A diamond in the rough” Finally, a decent hotel in Manhattan! I’m almost hesitant to give this hotel a great review, because selfishly, I don’t want it to become so popular that I’m unable to book it myself the next time I’m in NYC :) In all seriousness, though, this hotel deserves a great review. There are so many awful hotels in NYC – run down, old, ugly, dirty, uncomfortable and all of that for a disgustingly expensive rate ... but this one is actually a diamond in the rough. The hotel is located in Chelsea, right near the famous Flatiron building. It was a perfect location for me, as it was only 3 blocks from where my business meeting was, but it may be a bit far for tourists, depending on what area of the city they want to be in. Regardless, the subway is never too far away in NYC, if walking isn’t an option. The building itself is rather small and narrow, but it’s brightly colored and modern looking. Each floor only has about 8 rooms, so it’s not a huge hotel by any means; it felt more like a boutique hotel, with the benefit that it’s operated as part of the Wyndham chain (a bonus as far as quality, and loyalty programs). There is a restaurant next door which provides meals and even room service, and there was a small patio out front for dining and drinking. There was also a small reach-in cooler with snacks and drinks for purchase in the small (but bright and cheery) front lobby, with an internet station for those who need it. I had a room with a King bed on a mid-level floor, facing the back (not the street). It was a small room (typical of NYC), but I was pleasantly surprised at how clean and updated the room was. The large bed was very comfortable, with lots of pillows and a nice cushy down coverlet. There was also a comfortable work desk with complimentary wired internet (almost unheard of in NYC!) and 2 small complimentary bottles of water (nice touch!), a flat screen TV mounted to the wall, a small safe in the nightstand, and a stand-alone wardrobe, which had iron/ironing board and coffee/tea making machine inside. The bathroom was updated with modern fixtures, it had nice soft towels, a hairdryer, and “True Blue” bath amenities by Bath & Body Works (shampoo, conditioner, lotion, mouthwash, 2 kinds of soap, shower cap and ‘grooming kit’ – an impressive array for a mid-range hotel). The hotel was surprisingly quiet (or, I just lucked out and had quiet neighbors), and I thought it was in a good part of town. I was even pleasantly surprised that about an hour after I’d checked in, the front desk representative personally called up to my room to see if I was happy with the room, and if there was anything else I needed. She also reminded me that the temperature control was on the wall rather than on the device by the window (which was nice, as I was just trying to figure that out!). The air-conditioning is really just about the only ‘negative’ thing I experienced in my stat at this hotel – and it’s really not something I’d grade the hotel too harshly on. I couldn’t get the room to a comfortable temperature at night; the room was either too hot or too cold. That may have been an issue with the thermostat, but considering all the other good things about this hotel, I didn’t really want to harp on that. The room rate was a little high (ok, a lot high) for my personal preference if I had been on a leisure trip, but it was on par for what I’m willing to pay for a business trip. Overall, this was a great find, and I will definitely try to stay at this hotel again.

“Pretty good hotel” This is one of the older Residence Inns, however, it is well maintained and the staff is friendly and helpful. The suite was spacious and had everything we needed. The free breakfast was very good. I would recommend this hotel for longer stays because of its pod-like layout. There are maybe 15 different buildings each housing maybe 4 units. One thing to look out for: if you will have trouble carrying your suitcase, make sure to request a bottom-floor unit because I didn't see an elevator (although I could have missed it). Although this layout isn't ideal for a one-night stay; it would be convenient for a longer stay as you can go straight from your car into your suite, just like you would in an apartment.

“Wow! What a fantastic stay!” My stay at the Conrad Chicago ranks very high up on the list of my best-ever hotel stays. I have stayed in hotels on four continents, in several different countries, and this was one of the most enjoyable stays that I have ever enjoyed. Top marks on all counts.

“Totally average but great location” I agree with pretty much everything enofile1 says (review below posted on Sept 3). This a typical Hampton Inn so nothing fancy. The rooms are quite small. The beds are the typical Hampton beds. The location is great. You are close to Greenwich Village/Tribeca area which is by far the best part of NYC--fewer crowds and great restaurants. The gym was average but for a Hampton Inn it was excellent. The lobby was clean. There was a small bar that we tried to go to but the bartender kind of ignored us and was still learning how to make drinks. The bellman--Shane was the highlight. He was friendly (unlike the others) and went out of his way to help out. There is a great 19th floor outdoor terrace that cannot be missed. The view is spectacular and a great place to sip some wine.

“Confirmed: Top pick” Stayed for the second time within a 2 months time frame. This time, I booked a standard room. Upon arriving, was welcomed very heartly and got a better room, at the 54th level. The view of the Hudson River out of my bath tub was amazing. Breakfast was fresh and tasty, the pool is a must see/must do. The bed is heavenly, the entertainment system in the room is unique. Turn down service is great with little attentions like cards with wise words on them. But also cookies and a big bottle of Fiji water. The concierge services are top. Last time I was in the elevator with William Shatner, this time in front was P. Daddy. Once again, a 9.5/10 and if you can book a promotional rate or package, go for it.

“Very good hotel for families and Priority Points Break” We booked this hotel on a points break special at 5000 points a night, the hotel is dated but is trying very hard at being a first rate hotel. I have stayed at many other Crowne Plazas and this one reminds me of a Holiday Inn. The room was decent sized although we changed from a King to double to accomdate our 6yo and newborn as there was not a couch/love seat in the King room. The breakfast was good, omelets and typical buffet fare, the pancakes were a little soggie one morning. When staying on the executive level you get access to a little lounge with some drinks, snacks very good for bringing water along when we where seeing the city. I would stay here again and I felt very safe at this location. There is a Target, Pei Wei, Calf Pizza Kitchen, Chipolte and Potbelly's next door as well as TGI Fridays and TD Bank

“Very nice staff” I thought that the staff was extremely nice. No matter who it was, everyone was more than helpful. As far as the hotel I thought the location was great, but I got it on priceline as a "4 star" option, not really what I'm used to as far as "4 star" quality. But not a bad hotel overall.

“Superb value for money” I stayed here for a week when I was attending a convention at the Moscone Convention Centre, which is a few blocks away. The location of King George is great. It's about two blocks away from Union Square, but the street the hotel is on, is not as busy as the blocks around it, which is nice. There's a great restaurant next to the hotel, the Cafe Mason, which served an excellent breakfast. There's also a convinience store on the corner, a Starbucks...everything is in the surrounding area, literally a few metres away. So the location of the hotel is awesome. The room I stayed in was a twin and it was small as expected. The bathroom is clean and sterile, but small as well, so there's no space for your toiletries but there were plenty of towels every day. The beds are narrow, but much better than they look which I was happy to find out. I slept allright here. If you are in town for sightseeing and not spending much time in the room, the hotel is great, but if you gotta work and spend time in the room, definitely not so great. The work desk and chair are basic and the room isn't that comfy, but for the cheap price, I really cant complain, I couldn't believe the location and quality for the price. There was only a ceiling fan and no air conditioning in the room, but that was only a godo thing as most of us Europeans hate the usual air conditioning cold. Keeping the windows open in March kept things cool. It did get a bit noisy in the night as our window faced an alley, but nothing bad. The staff were very friendly as well and I'd say the King George is great value for money.

“First Class” My wife and I and our little 2 year old just stayed at the Westin September 17 and 18. I have to tell you, it was one of the greatest hotel experiences we have ever had. It started with Kevin at valet parking to Troy taking our bags up to our room. When we checked in they even gave us a "goodie bag" for our 2 year old daughter. She thought that was the greatest. We upgraded our room to river view once we got there. I would suggest something around the 6th floor. If you begin your journey from the hotel on the river walk it is quite the walk to get to everything. I suggest going street side for a block and a half and then going down to the river walk. It puts you right in the middle of everything. You're there in less than 5 minutes. As for the gym, it's one of the best I've ever seen in a hotel. The pool, well it's small but keeps you cool in the San Antonio heat. We ate at the hotel restaurant for breakfest and it was ok. The prices weren't too bad but the food was only average. We travel to San Antonio every year and I will not be staying anywhere else. They have mastered customer service. Good job Westin.

“Elegant Accomodations - Outstanding Service” I stayed at this hotel recently with a large group visiting historic theaters in the Philadelphia/Baltimore/Wilmington area. We travel every year to a different US city and we have always been highly impressed with Radisson Hotels so came into our stay with high expectations. We were not disappointed. We booked our block of rooms more than a year in advance and found the hotel sales staff to be professional, courteous and genuinely interested in our group's satisfaction. The hotel itself is extremely elegant with many "small touches" that make it feel like home. (Chilled water set out in the lobby in the late afternoon, flavored lightly with lemon slices and mint leaves was an extra special touch!) The lobby is welcoming, bright and the front desk staff was extremely professional. It was very busy at the desks when I arrived for check in yet there were more than enough stations open, the desk personnel did not seem fazed by the crush of people AND ringing phones AND crying child (make that tantrum-throwing child!). They were smooth and unruffled. My room was very clean, nicely furnished, large screen TV and oh those beds! Sleep number adjustable, softest comforters and pillows imaginable, nice view. After i arrived, i invited several officers of our group to a last minute planning session in my room. One of the housekeepers arrived to do the bed turndown and spent a few minutes chatting with us, learning about our group and giving us a few tips on morning traffic, interesting sites we would encounter on our walks to and from various points and generally making us feel quite taken care of. As we have seen at other Radisson properties, every single hotel employee I encountered had a smile, nod and "good morning" etc greeting. It shows a well trained staff who are very conscious of the guests in their hotel. However, since i notice that hotel management reads and responds to comments left here, let me make one important suggestion.... those sinks!! I am short (5'1") and it was like morning exercise brushing my teeth every morning! Those sinks are just a few inches too high for ease of use for a shorter person. Please consider step stools in the bathrooms. I am only half kidding...... Our yearly conference ends with an awards banquet and the hotel menu was especially good. Diverse selections, served hot and promptly. Can't ask for more. Also the room layout was very well done with ample room at and between each table. Overall, I am happy to give this hotel a very enthusiastic thumbs up and highly recommend it for group or individual travel.

“快適に過ごせました” 地下鉄駅から出てまっすぐEllis St.を進むとホテルの裏(駐車場)に 着き、ここからも入れますが正面玄関はO'Farrell St.にあります。 タワー1の41階Taylor St.側の部屋だったので、窓から遠くに ゴールデンゲートブリッジが見えて感激でした。 こんな街中なのに周囲には意外と高い建物は少なく、眼下に シティホールやオペラハウスも見渡せます。 部屋のクローゼットとバスルームのドアが木製の観音開きだったり、 エレベーターの内装にモザイクのタイルが使ってあったりして 他都市とはちょっと違う、サンフランシスコ感を感じました。 朝食はケーブルカー乗り場近くにあるTad'sの、アーリーバードが おすすめです。

“Good Service and was better than what we expected” Stayed during the summer of 2009 as we passed through Philadelphia for a night during our summer vacation. Obtained through Priceline and a deeply discounted rate. Difficulty finding the hotel parking lot and there is valet parking only. Parking is pricey but expected for any location near downtown (Close to $30/night - from what I can remember). Valet staff was quick in the morning. Primarily wanted this to be close to downtown and also to Citizen Bank Park. Easy check in. Large two queen bed. Addtional sofa, flat screen HD tv, dresser with desk. Free internet. Clean updated neat rooms. Great size for a family for four. Hotel front desk and bell staff helpful in providing directions to the ballpark and tourist attractions. 3 block walk to the subway to get to the Citizen Bank Park. We enjoyed our one night stay but paid through Priceline $55/night. I would not have stayed if I had paid over $150/night.

“Truely wonderful stay” We sayed here for 9 nights. The location is perfect for exploring NYC. We had a junior suite and it was spacious and comfortable. The staff were friendly and helpful and we would certainly stay here again. The only thing that would have been nice was a coffee maker in the room for that early morning cuppa in bed but apart from that everything was perfect.

“Great stay” Stayed here for business in April 2011. The workshop i was attending was located in the hotel. Great location to shopping and good food and easy access to downtown via taxi. Rooms were clean and spacious and breakfast was satisfying.

“Loved it, first rate all around.” I will continue to stay here from now on, as I am often in the area. Had the choice of several hotels in the area, and I have stayed at most of them. Luckily, this time we chose this one. Although our room was not ready, we got there early, they made us feel comfortable and welcome. Brought us water while we waited in a comfortable area. Brought our room keys when it was ready and apologized for any inconvenience. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable. The room was clean, bright, well maintained and perfect. It is across from the mall which is an added benefit. The area it quiet, as was our room. The bed was amazingly comfortable. It was hard to wake up, it felt so good. I have no idea why others rated this anything but excellent. As a seasoned traveler, my advise, stay here!

“WALDORF ASTRORIA CHICAGO HAS RUINED ME FOR ALL OTHER HOTEL” One word sums up the Waldorf Astorua Chicago...CLASSY! The service was effortless and friendly helpfulness, without being highbrow or overbearing. 5 star service is about making every guest feel comfortable and at ease and this place delivers. I think the no tipping policy is very classy, although I had to keep reminded myself not to. When we pulled up to the hotel, the valet took the car and someone else took our luggage in. The hotel rooms were sold out (that's what happens when you're #1 on so many lists!!!) and the housekeeping staff had some difficulty with having all the rooms ready by 3pm check-in. When we arrived, we had to listen to some spoiled guests complaining about this and the fact that they could not get the upgrades they wanted. Get over it, people! We took kids to the pool. The staff took our luggage to the pool for them to change and brought our keys to the pool when the room was ready. It is not hard to make a room look nice on the surface, but his place went well beyond that. The finishes are what you would find in million dollar homes, including refrigerator and freezer drawers and custom wardrobe with leather lined drawers. I didn't even start with everyone's dream bathroom with pocket doors, wall to wall carrera marble, the TV in the mirror (I know you're sick of hearing about it), beautiful mosaic floor, deep Tea for 2 cast iron Kohler tub (a mini pool for my girls), hugh shower, and creative way to hide the water closet with frosted glass doors. It was very spacious and I had to remind myself that I could walk more freely around the room. The lighting system is great...you can even turn off the doorbell if you don't want to be disturbed. No "do not disturb sign needed. Very classy. I did not schedule a spa treatment but did have the opportunity to use the spa which was an amazing treat. The staff was very gracious and brought me tea. I love the snack spoon set up...you have to see it to know what I mean. We had brunch at Balsan and it was wonderful. The macarons for turndown were a wonderful treat. Classy, classy, classy! We brought our 3 and 4 year old girls with us. I would not consider this a family hotel (I think it is ideal or a romantic trip or a getaway with your girlfriends) but the staff was very accommodating with our girls at the pool (gave them pool toys to use) and Balsan (with postcards for coloring.) They also received a toy at turndown which was again, very classy. I will be spending a small fortune to take my husband to Pebble Beach for his 50th birthday. I already know I will be disappointed with the Inn at Spanish Bay regardless of how well rated it is because of my experience at WA Chicago. I can't wait to come back here.

“Convenient location, but the quality of the stay felt a little cheap” I stayed here in May for a reunion and was a little disappointed. First, the benefits of the place: I was upgraded to a suite, which had a great view of the Christian Science complex. There was a small sitting area. Internet access (which I had to pay for) was fast. Room service was fast (really fast) and pleasant. But, the minuses: scratchy, polyestery sheets. Windows don't open. Chintzy towels (like the kind you get at the gym), and cheap toiletries. And the upholstery on the furniture in the sitting areas had several stains on them. I chose the hotel because I was offered a really reasonable rate, and the reunion was taking place downstairs in the ballroom. But, I had just spent the prior weekend in the Washington Hilton, which served a similar purpose (large conference hotel) and felt that the quality of the rooms were far better. Boston hotels are more expensive than other large cities. But next time, I would rather spend a little extra money for a little more luxury

“Super cute in Hollywood” While not a luxury hotel, this hotel is in a great spot with really cute rooms. Our room was decked out in uber-Hollywood memorabilia mode. Tons of framed movie posters and signed stills. The room was clean and the bed comfy. Free parking!... which is unheard of in LA hotels. Perfect place if you want to stay somewhere VERY close to Hollywood, close to freeways and other great LA spots. Added bonus: the 101 Coffee Shop is in the lobby and a great hip place for breakfast or a late night snack/meal. I'm a vegan and had no problem eating a hearty vegan friendly-breakfast and lots of mid-night snacks. We will definitely return back to this hotel.

“Where was the "JW" in this Marriott?” I was expecting more. This hotel seemed to be more a full service Marriott than a JW. The Renassaince across town seemed to have more luxury in it than this hotel. The service was fine but sterile. For the money we paid I thought it would of been better.

“I'd go back!” This is not a fancy hotel. But there are a lot of great things about it. The location on the riverwalk is excellent. The staff is genuinely friendly. There's free dinner, free drinks, free breakfast, free one hour long distance in your room, even a nice gift bag when you arrive with snacks and water. You know, the kind that they charge $6 for at other hotels. It's clean, relatively quiet and the pool on the roof is a real plus. Nothing opulent but it's a great family friendly hotel.

“Great service, appearance needs updating, but would stay again.” I cannot say enough good things about the service at this hotel, especially the valet service. These young men were quick, personable and professional, the best I have experienced at a hotel. The hotel staff was likewise, professional and friendly and truly made me feel welcome and appreciative of my stay at the hotel. Everything I asked for when making the reservation was honored when I arrived...high floor, city view, extra towels. My check in process was the fastest I have ever experienced. This hotel is serious about it's customer service. If you are a member of their rewards program, you get free wireless internet and to me that is a big plus. There are no coffee pots in the room, but complimentary beverages are brought to your room each morning at your specified time. To me, that is much more enjoyable and definitely more sanitary than the cups and pots that are never cleaned in other hotels. The one thing I would suggest is to begin a renovation of the appearance of the hotel. Walking down the hall to our room, the doors were badly marked up and dirty looking. It just looked very worn. Our room was very clean, but was beginning to show a lot of wear. The tub had been "patched" where the porcelain had worn off and the caulking was beginning to look bad. Even the telephone looked very old and discolored. This is a great hotel in a great area. It is at the Epicenter and there are lots of excellent restaurants within easy walking distance of the hotel. I managed to get what I thought was a great rate, and if I could get that rate, would definitely stay again. but I hope there are plans to make the hotel itself as beautiful as the people who work there.

“a bit creepy” As others have mentioned, the parking is VERY tight, and the construction was a bit noisy. We had a room facing the construction. The front desk staff said the construction noise would start around 9am, but of course it started much earlier. We were up early so it didn't wake us. There was limited parking right outside the front door, with the majority of parking under the hotel (I hate underground parking). We had to go through a construction zone to get to that camera-secured parking area, and then once parked we took the elevator directly to our floor. The elevators and elevator doors were jerky, and didn't always stop even with the floor. One day, my husband was checking the tires on our vehicle, and a maintenance guy came out to see what he was doing- basically making sure he wasn't doing anything illegal. This made me feel better knowing they were actually watching and following up on any "suspicious" activity. Housekeeping left something to be desired. After the first night (we stayed two), they took the soap and didn't leave any replacements. We didn't have enough towels, so called the desk for some to be sent up but they never came so we had to go get them. The hotel is directly across from a motel with "questionable" clientele - it made me a bit uncomfortable walking by, especially with small kids. The hotel is a 10-15 minute walk to the Seattle Center, which was very convenient.

“Ottimo per il costo che ha” Hotel con più di una pecca, che però viene ampiamente compensata dal prezzo (meno di 80€ per una doppia ad agosto) soprattutto il relazione alla location: ad un isolato dalla via più trendy della città e da Union Square, due dal Financial District, al centro di tutti i mezzi di trasporto. La pulizia è accettabile e la cortesia del personale anche. La colazione è servita in quella che sembra una sala comunitaria con i tavoli rivestiti in plastica, ma è gratis e c'è un po' di tutto. L'hotel nel complesso è vecchiotto, l'isolamento delle finestre nullo e il letto rumoroso, ma se non vi interessa il lusso e vi adattate ad un paio di tappi per le orecchie, potete dormire con vista sui grattacieli ad un prezzo ridicolo per la carissima San Francisco!

“Loved The Hotel 41” We stayed for 2 nightsat Hotel 41. Upon check the girl at the front desk was extremely friendly and explained they had two rooms left, a very small room on the 6th floor or a larger but still small room on the second floor, but it was right above the bar. She let take a look at the larger room and even though you could here the music from the busy bar below while walking in the hallway, you could not hear it at all in the room. We stayed in room 206. The room is small - yet honestly not the smallest room I have ever stayed in. The room was spotless clean. The bedding was comfortable and the bathroom was very modern with a stand up shower. Included in the room was a small TV and DVD player. The rooms have their own climate control which was great because we could warm up the room for our return after wandering in the cold. The free breakfast is served in the bar in the morning and consist of pastries, bagels, juice, and coffee. The staff through out the hotel and bar were very helpful and friendly. Always opening doors for you and greeting you in all the common areas of the hotel. The location can't be beat for a short NYC trip. It's right off Time's Square, close to chain and local resturants and coffee houses, subway right across the street and the hop on hop off bus tours stop right across the street from the hotel. You can walk to any of the Broadway shows and to Macy's. Upon check out they held our bags and offered to ring for a car for us to the airport, but we had already booked. I would definately stay at Hotel 41 again!

“One of my favorite hotels!” On my first stay, I found the Conrad a bit too stuffy. I switched to theWit for a while, dazzled by its newness and trendy style. But once you stripped away the newness, theWit lost its appeal and we went back to the Conrad and absolutely love it. It's professional without being stuffy. On my most recent, they apologized that they had no Hilton Diamond upgrade for me. No big deal. I could live without it but they then sent several bottles of very good wine to our room to make up for it. They didn't have to do anything but they did. I liked that. Rooms are decent sized and the bathrooms are huge. Love the showers at the Conrad. Valet is always quick to bring our car around and room service has never blinked an eye at any request, no matter how bizarre. The Conrad has become our "go to" hotel when staying in Chicago.

“Nice Room, Poor Service, Difficult Staff” I stayed in this hotel on a Saturday night with my boyfriend. The room was beautiful with a huge comfortable bed and large bathroom. The linens were clean and soft. The location was nice. It was in walking distance of Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. The hotel itself was a little crazy. First there was a wedding and a prom so it was a very busy night, but that is expected in most hotels on a saturday in April (wedding and prom season). What I didn't appreciated was the huge crowds of people that hung out in the lobby until 3 AM acting loud and drunk. There was even a group of teenagers smoking indoors next to the front desk. I'm not sure what the smoking laws are in Maryland, but I didn't think this was acceptable in any hotel lobby. I woke up in the middle of the night thirsty and looking for a bottle of water. I was on the 6th floor. The vending machine on the 6th floor was out of service. So I went to the 5th floor. The machine on the 5th floor ate my change. So I went to the 4th floor. The machine on the 4th floor was out of water, soda, juice, everything. So I went to the lobby to see if the front desk could help me out. They told me there was nothing they could do because the kitchen was closed. After arguing for several minutes and speaking with the manager, they eventually gave me two bottles of water that they wanted to charge me $8 for. I refused to pay and after a few more minutes of arguing, they gave me the water for free. To sum it all up, this is a hotel with great rooms but poor service.

“"At the airport?" Great idea...horrible logistics.....” When I say this hotel is at the airport, I literally mean it is at the gates of the Austin airport. Very convienent, if you're going no where else but there. But, with $15 to park per day (that's not including valet) or $15 for a round-trip shuttle and nearly 11 miles into downtown (and all the requisite time, traffic and navigational directions), I give this hotel a thumbs-down. It is a nightmare if you want to go anywhere else but this hotel. There is NOTHING within walking distance....NOTHING. So, don't expect to eat, see, hear or do anything without expensive and time-consuming transportation far away from the hotel. As for the hotel itself, the circular design of the hotel requires walking (perceptually) in a large circle, endlessly, until you finally reach your room. The interior, open circle of the hotel is the dining area, bar and lounge. It is the farthest description from cozy or secluded that one can get. Having a drink at the bar? Expect large, cavernous, drafty open spaces behind you with no sense of spatial privacy. Having dinner? It's like eating in a large, empty warehouse with poor lighting and gigantic tables. Room rates were decent. Wi-fi DOESN'T exist in rooms....only in the circular, central open spaces of the hotel. And it is terrible. As for the fitness room, I didn't get to check it out this time. As for the pool, TX was in the middle of a 4 day crippling ice storm....enough said. As for the room itself, it was adequate. The stocked coffee area was a nice necessity. The bathroom was spacious, gorgeous and stocked with name brand products. Customer service was good and the concierges were on top of all weather related questions across the entire country. Kudos! On the whole, I would not stay here again. Austin is a vibrant, colorful and 3-D city. This hotel isn't. And it isn't even proximate to anything that IS Austin.

“Makes You Feel Special ;)” From the moment we stepped out of our taxi from the airport onto Hilton property, we were smitten! A gentleman bell-hop greeted us; we experienced considerate & efficient check-in & even though we did not have an executive room or lakeside view ~ we enjoyed a clean, good-sized comfortable one on the 8th floor. The hotel dining is elegant & delicious & the wait staff couldn't be more accommodating. Our every need was met, including needing a dress bag (long story)! We only stayed one night (for an Irish dance competition) but left feeling like we had a mini-vacation too.

“Exceptional Customer Service” Every once and a while you find a Marriott Courtyard with the heart, soul, and service of a high end Marriott property. This Marriott Courtyard has exceptional service. From the friendly greeting, followed by saying hello by name when you come and go, to the tremendously friendly lady with warm cookies awaiting your return after a long day - this Marriott property delights at every opportunity. The rooms are neat, clean, and - at least Room 622 - had a deep, whirlpool bathtub. The hotel has a nice restaurant (I had a great breakfast) - and while not right next to a Metro stop - you can easily walk from the McPherson Metro stop to the hotel. The soap was so unusual - I've included a picture. The lobby has a coffee, latte, tea machine that is also a welcome amenity.

“Hotal was fair, could have been great with better front desk” This hotel was convenient to the Austin airport and also just a short drive away from downtown area's sights and sounds. Location was excellent for all areas of Austin. The road in front of the hotel can get backed up during rush hour, so you may have troubling getting out if you’re going to dinner around that time of the evening. This hotel also has bad signage, its difficulty to find, you have to cut though a now defunct Hawthorn Suites parking lot to make it into the Courtyard's parking area. The hotel itself was pleasant enough...but where I feel fell it fell short was the front desk staff. The person attending the front desk for my check in and check out was not pleasant in the least. I felt attitude from him the second I checked in. After check in we made it to our room and discovered we were given double beds,, after a requested for a King a check in,,so back down we went to the front desk, this time I had my wife speak to the gentleman as I thought maybe he just had a problem with me for some reason, , turns out my wife felt the same coldness and lack of interest from this front desk employee. It’s really unfortunate because we liked the hotel for the most part, nice location, comfortable beds, and would have taken advantage of the free breakfast if the front desk employee would have informed us about it. Hotels need to know that you only have one chance to make a first impression, and this hotel failed miserably. There are far too many hotels in this area of Austin for me to want to come back and put up with a rude attitude of hotel staff. To be fair, everyone else that was employed by the hotel was pleasant. The bar tender in the lobby was very friendly as well as the cleaning personal. But the attitude of the front desk employee was enough for us to look else where while staying in Austin in the future.

“Grand hotel that has seen better days” I spent four nights at this Biltmore and have to say that the lobby and meeting rooms were impressive and opulent in the old world Hollywood way. The staff was attentive, polite and professional, however the rooms are in serious need of an update. The beds and pillows were very hard. The comforter reminded me of something I have seen in budget hotels. The restaurant and room service was extremely overpriced! I ate at the restaurant three different times and the service was SLOW and the food exceptionally overpriced. If you enjoy being a part of a historic hotel, then I would suggest a night here, however if you are looking for comfort and luxury, look somewhere else.

“Great For The Budget Traveller” We selected this hotel based on price. The hotels near Fisherman's Wharf are more than double the price of this Days Inn. I wouldn't recommended this hotel if vagrants intimidate you. There are lots on the street outside. However, they are harmless and didn't hassle us. The location is not in the most desirable area, but I did not consider it dangerous. The front desk staff were polite and efficient. The room was clean and functional. There was some internal remodelling work going on while we were there, although I couldn't see any proper evidence of what was being done. The rooms have internal front doors and the lift can only be accessed from the ground floor with a key card. The hotel offers free parking, which for a hotel in central SF was a bonus. We had no trouble parking, but we were there over the quiet Christmas holiday. The breakfast at this hotel is limited to donughts and muffins and coffee and juice. There are also complimentary copies of USA Today. Union Square is around a 15 minute walk from the hotel. We generally travelled around the city by bus, and there is a bus stop (which has services to Fisherman's Wharf) only a couple of blocks away.

“Gute Lage, Preis Leistung ok!!” Wir waren sehr zufrieden mit diesem Hotel. Die Lage war fantastisch, direkt am Empire State Building, U-Bahn auch gleich um die Ecke, und unten in der Strasse gleich gute Verpflegungsmöglichkeiten (lecker asiatische Diner) Wir würden hier wieder wohnen!

“Best Bed Ever!” I love this hotel. It is old style luxury with thick walls and the best bed and pillows anywhere. The location is fantastic sine you are minutes from the airport, walking distance to the Gas Lamp District where there are many restaurants and bars, directly across the street from the Westfield shopping center, near the state and federal courthouses, close to the embarcadero (walkway along the Bay), etc. The staff is very friendly and willing to help with anything you need. The windows are old and you can hear the traffic and people outside so ask for a room that does not face Broadway or Third St. Construction on the neighboring Westgate hotel can be very loud, which is why I recommend avoiding Third St.

“Fantastic Hotel! Fantastic Location!” I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights and also hosted a cocktail reception while there. The hotel is gorgeous, and the rooms are very spacious / clean and well appointed. I will stay at this hotel when my travels return me to L.A. Kerry's restaurant in the lobby, L.A. Market, is also fantastic. Please do try it when you're there!

“Great stay” Overall, we had a really great stay. Here's a breakdown: -Parking: They offer valet parking, but it's pricey. You can park in a lot caddy-corner to the hotel for about $10-$15 less which is great - good options for parking. -Check-in/Check-out: Our experience checking in was great. The front desk clerk was very friendly and ensured we had a double room since there was 4 of us. He made us feel very welcome! When we checked out, the clerk (different guy) was also very friendly but it did take a long time waiting in line. -Room: The room we were in was huge. There was a kitchenette area with a mini-fridge, microwave etc, but for some reason we didn't have a coffee pot. We had to call for one the next morning. There was a little dining area and also a living room with pull out coach and flat screen tv. The bedroom was in it's own room with a door. We had 2 double beds which were pretty comfy. The bathroom was pretty small though which is surprising considering the size of the room overall. -Amenities: We weren't there long, but they seemed to have everything you'd need there including a free breakfast at TGI Fridays. We didn't take advantage of this, but it's certainly a nice perk. -Location: It's kind of on the outskirts of Center City but still close enough to the action. I like that it's separated for all the hustle and bustle actually. There were some good Irish pubs close by too.

“Love this Hotel!” If you are travelling with you dog this is the best hotel ever! We stayed in a luxury suite that had a living room and large bathroom with 2 person jacuzzi tub and walk in glass shower. Bedroom was large too, and had sofa, desk and flat screen TV with DVD. Staff was extremely accomodating, and spa treatments were also great. Only problem was pool is not very big and you couldn't have fit another person out there Saturday afternoon. There is a very nice neighborhood just to the west Highland Park that is wonderful for walking your dogs in the morning. We took our two large dogs rather than finding a dog sitter for one night. The staff was wonderful, except for the snotty concierge that was working the night we went to ask directions to the nearest dog park. Someone even went out and bought more dog bowls because they ran out for us. Location is great for shopping and dining.

“Value!” I've been on this trendy/boutique hotel binge for so long that I forgot what a solid choice Embassy Suites is. I grew up coming to ES as a child, it was my parents "go to" hotel and now as an adult you can see why. Everyone gets a suite automatically HUGE rooms, cooked to order breakfast buffett, managers recepetion not just wine or beer but Open Bar! This particualr ES looks new and modern and the location is great. The biggest selling point was they have smoking rooms. This day in age I get it it's a faux pax but when I found out they did I couldnt believe it main reason I booked actually. You'd be hard pressed to find smoking rooms in DC let alone a beautiful suite. It was my best friends birthday and as two cigar afficainados it was a convience and a luxuxry to be able to indulge in the comfort of my own room. This is an asset even if its a just few rooms. Gives you a competitive edge. Overall great product and most bang for your buck.

“Great room, great location” I got a room at the Sheraton through Priceline. After reading the terrible reviews on Trip Advisor I was very worried. I called the hotel and asked them if I could pay extra for an upgraded room to avoid any problems. They told me that I would have to wait until I arrived to see what they had available. I was worried! When we arrived the lobby was beautiful. The line to check in was long, about 10 minutes. Once we got to the counter we were treated very well. We were asked if we wanted to upgrade our room but we decided against it. We were given a corner room that is a little smaller than most but it was BEAUTIFUL. The beds were big and comfortable with soft down comforters. I would be happy to stay at the Sheraton again.

“Like most of the reviewers of this hotel I will say there are disappointments” We travelled to NYC for business and pleasure. We paid over $800.00 for a "suite" for three nights (we also paid a month or more ahead of time for this!) - Though the decor was nice, and the size of the suite was adequate, we found the inside location of our suite to be not suitable for what was promised. We literally had no idea what time it was because it was always nearly night time out the windows, due to brick walls a few feet away from all windows. We also had the smell of sewer gas in the bathroom, to the point that we closed the door of the bathroom so that we didn't sleep with the smell. The refrigerator situation is silly and very short sighted on the part of the management. ALL SUITES SHOULD HAVE A SMALL REFRIGERATOR FOR GUEST USE! NO COFFEE MAKER! AGAIN SHORT SIGHTED ON PART OF THE MANAGEMENT. The lobby was lovely and the complaints lodged about the elevators being inadequate seems to me to be from people who don't understand that this is an older property. In general the public areas were very nice. This is a lovely hotel, situated in a wonderful location with very stingy and short-sighted managment. I am sorry to say, being from Boston and traveling to NYC often, that I won't be booking into this hotel again.

“Thanks again trip advisor!” We weren't sure exactly when we'd arrive in NYC so we couldn't take advantage of some other hotel deals or advance reservations. We checked trip advisor and based on the reviews made a reservation. The location is very convenient to everything. Although other reviewers expressed concerns about the proximity to Port Authority and the parole office we never felt afraid. There's plenty of pedestrian traffic and lots of people around. The free breakfast is quite good although it's so crowded seating becomes an issue. At the same time we shared tables with friendly folks from around the world! The staff is very nice and one night 2 of the folks at the desk broke into song and entertained us with their lovely voices! The rooms are quite clean although small and cramped once your luggage is in. I'd do without the kitchen (also small) to have more space. The hotel doesn't have a service elevator so guests and staff use the 3 elevators and wait times are rather long. The free washers and dryers were quite wonderful to have after a few weeks on the road. It gets a bit busy so you have to be patient! I've spent a lot of time in NYC, most hotels are quite expensive and don't offer even close to what this hotel does. I spend most of my time in NY out and about so most of the inconveniences I found are minor. This hotel is a good value!

“モダンホテルにリニューアルしました。” ロスの超豪華高級住宅エリアに燐しています。 木々のしげる住宅街にこのホテルはあります。 このあたりは有名人の豪邸が多々あるようです。 ココに行く時は安っぽい車で行きたくないと毎回タクシーを利用してしまうほどです。 笑 このホテルが好きで今まで何度も足を運んでいました。 (まず、レストラン、BAR 大人のホテルという感じで落ち着いている。 味、サービスがいい) 去年リニューアルオープンし楽しみにしていましたが お部屋はまさにモダンスタイルという感じ。 もちろん全てが新しくサービスもいいですが 私には前の雰囲気の方が落ち着けたのでモダンタイプがお好きな方には とてもいいのではないかと思います。 レストラン、Barも私は前の方が好きでした。 自分の部屋のバルコニーでお酒やTEAを頂けるのはいいですね。

“Not good” We had two rooms for two nights at the Stanford Court. The rooms were booked approximately 6 months in advance with a request for two rooms together on a high floor (as the trip was to celebrate my Father’s 70th Birthday – so we wanted it to be special). When we arrived we were told our rooms were not yet ready as the previous guests (Virgin airline staff had a late check-out arrangement) – therefore we had to wait in reception for the rooms to come free (great for the people in the rooms but not good for us). After about 45 minutes one room came free, so my parents moved into that one. A further 45 minutes later our room became available – but the rooms were neither together or on a high floor (one was on floor 2 and one on 3). The room we were allocated was right at street level (due the hilly disposition of SF!) therefore it had no view and was very noisy. We queried this with the desk and they basically said that there were no other rooms – after further discussion they gave us one new room on the 7th Floor - this was classed as a ‘Parlour Suite’ – little did we realise that this meant two uncomfortable nights on a sofa bed in a room that never seemed to get warm. The rooms here aren’t cheap – but I would certainly not class them as value for money based on our experience. The hotel is obviously keen to keep it’s customers who have large contracts with them happy rather than individuals like us. The location of the hotel is spot on – but I wouldn’t stay there again based on the experience we had - I was very dissapointed.

“Nice value for long family weekend, downtown Memphis” I stayed here for an impromptu overnight last week, with my wife and 9-year-old daughter. We were passing through Memphis and decided to stop for dinner downtown and stay the night. We found this place on Expedia for $97. For that, we got two double beds, nonsmoking, and clean. The room was warm -- and the AC off -- when we checked in, but it cooled off quickly. It's a motor lodge with free parking and pool on the back side of AutoZone Park and a few blocks to the heart of downtiown. Those few blocks are a little rough, but we felt reasonably safe. I'd recommend this place for a long family weekend getaway where you want to be within easy walking distance to Beale Street and everything else downtown. (I even went out for an early morning walk and walked down to the Civil Rights Museum south of downtown. Again, some of those blocks south of downtown are rough, but I felt safe.) The motel has a very limited free continental breakfast, but, believe it or not, the Greyhound Bus station next door has a very good and cheap breakfast buffet that we tried and enjoyed. It has a full range of choices, from eggs and bacon, to fruit, yogurt, and bottled juices and milk. The motel is three blocks to the famous Peabody hotel, known for its 11 a.m. March of the Ducks from their rooftop aviary to the lobby fountain, where they swim for the day. This exercise will keep the kids interested and occupied for a good couple of hours, and it's air conditoned and free. The motel is also three or four quick blocks to Beale Street. We asked the Peabody concierge to recommend a rib joint, and he pointed us to the Blues City Cafe on Beale Street, which was fabulous.

“Nice botique hotel” This hotel is great! The rooms are avg. size, very clean, stocked with all the ammenities you need. Staff is very helpful. Location is near shopping, cable car turn around and convenient to public transportation which is so reasonable. If you get a room away from the street it's very quiet. Their top rated restaurant has fabulous food with astronomical prices. Wait staff is enthusiastic tho a tad young. Omly drawback that being on Market St. you see a lot of pan handlers.

“Plush/Excellent Location” Overall a beautiful room at a very convinient location. We did not use any of the facilities, so can not comment on them. Note: valet parking is $40 (fourty bucks) per day, which is a shame. You should be able to find plenty of free parking on a same block :) High Speed Internet did not work in our room.

“Great hotel” As noted in previous the hotel service is great and so are the rooms. The hotel is by far nicer than the other SPG properties in Houston such as the Sherton suites or the Westin by the Galleria. If you are a platinum SPG member you are almost always guaranteed an upgrade to a one bedroom suite. The hotel used to give a free breakfast for platinum members but I noticed they dropped that amenity which is too bad. Yes the parking isn't the most convenient but it isn't terrible. I also recommend calling the hotel first before arrival to ask which exit to take off the highway since it can be tricky.

“A Nice Staybridge Suites but not #1 in San Antonio” Great hotel for an extended visit or if you are traveling with a large family, you can definitely save money by eating their free breakfast buffet and then again, enjoying their 6 pm weekday social which includes free drinks, alcohol, and a light snack such as meatballs, chicken wings, etc. For more details, read tutupr24’s detailed review. The rooms are huge and you definitely have privacy however, the bathroom is very small. The business center includes scanning and fax capabilities which I used. My only complaint is the laundry...although the machines are brand new and free, you have to walk through the gym to access the laundry room. Okay, maybe not a big deal to some people but when the gym is crowded, the smell...you get the picture. Wal-Mart is nearby so if you forgot something, you can definitely drive a couple of blocks and pick it up there. Overall, a great Staybridge Suites but not my first choice in San Antonio.

“Nice courtyard; location good for airport but not for downtown” I stayed here for a few nights while traveling on business. I chose this hotel because of its proximity to my work location in northeast San Antonio, and because it's on a list of hotels that my employer requires me to choose from for business travel. Overall it's a nice hotel with typical amenities one would expect at a Doubletree. Pros: The hotel has a nice courtyard with lots of trees and a pool. Each room has a recycling basket. (First time I've ever seen that in a hotel.) The restaurant has a good breakfast buffet (not included in the rate) with bacon, sausage, made-to-order eggs, fruit, cereals, etc. Staff at the hotel and restaurant were friendly and provided good service. Cons: They offer a limited number (less than 20) of TV channels. My TV didn't work at all one morning. The room clock cannot be adjusted without a screwdriver. I've seen this in other Doubletrees, and it's annoying when the clock is incorrect. The hotel does not offer wireless internet, although high-speed wired internet is available for $10 per day. I would stay at this hotel again when traveling to northeast San Antonio, mainly because it's the closest full-service hotel (that I can stay at) to my work location. Those wanting to visit downtown San Antonio should look elsewhere, unless convenient access to the airport is desired.

“perfect stay” I lucked into this hotel through Priceline which I use often when traveling to NY. This hotel had never come up before and I was curious to try it out. First, for the tourist, the location could not be better, right on 42nd St high above all the craziness of Times Square and right in the heart of the theatre disctrict. For me, is was perfect as my meetings were only a few blocks away. Check in and front desk very helpful and professional. Room was spacious and comfortable although I could have used without the two beds. I didn't ask to move as it didn't matter. View from my 30th floor room was terrific and virtually sound proof. Never heard a sound from the hall way either. The only complaint I have is with the carpets. The hotel is fairly new, but the carpet choice has already dated the property. Minor, minor issue. I did not eat at the hotel as there are countless other choices in the area. Coffee service is provided in the rooms which is a nice touch. Internet rates were the typical rip off at higher end hotels (although the front desk clerk did tell me I could get it for free at Burger King) Bottom line - if you get a good rate at this hotel - book it.

“Lovely and Well Located” This hotel is well located right opposite Library of Congress and a great restaurant area only a few blocks away with something for every budget. Union Station is not far away and there is another metro stop near Library of Congress too. I stayed in the deluxe one bedroom suite, it was kind of weird to walk in and find that BOTH TVs were on when I arrived along with the clock radio tuned to the classical station. Seemed a waste of electricity. The bathroom was small but had great shelving and the hot water pressure was good too. It took me until the second night to find the cupboard in the bedroom which had the bathrobes in it, (the cupboard is behind the bedroom door, didn't even notice it on my first day!) I also couldn't find the light switch to turn off the ceiling light in the living room, I ended up just leaving it on rather than looking like a goose and calling the front desk. Seriously, in 3 days I never found the switch. The bed was really comfy but I seriously hate the floppy pillows, I would love a firmer option. The hotel says it provides a "continental breakfast" but this is nothing but a plate of danishes along with coffee and apples. Being a cereal or toast sort of person, I was disappointed to discover these sugary snacks in the morning, it meant we had to eat around the corner which we had to allow extra time. So, definitely beware if you're expecting a "real" breakfast. Overall a comfy, quiet and friendly hotel and would definitely stay here again.

“Nice hotel, small rooms” This nice hotel on Indy's northeast side is next to Community Hospital's medical campus and short drive from the Castleton Mall shopping area. The hotel is well appointed. My room was nicely decorated and had a flat screen TV. But the room was no bigger than some budget priced hotels I've been in. The bathroom was definitely not what I would expect at a Hilton - small and only big enough for one person. The beds were comfortable, but were also small for two people. So if you want to get four to a room you might not like it. And the room lacked the now-standard mini-fridge and microwave. The wi-fi was free and easy to access. All the staff were extremely pleasant. For the business meeting part of my stay, the food was good and hot, but nothing remarkable.

“Not Good” Our stay at this hotel was not good! My husband and I arrived at 5 pm on a Saturday. We were in Philly for a friend's surprise b-day party and we were already running late when we tried to check in. Believe it or not - our room was not ready! We waited for about 45 minutes and finally a room became available - we had reserved a club level room but got a regular room. We were so late at this point that we did not care. Once in our room - I immediately jumped in the shower to get ready for our party. OH NO - there was no shampoo - only 2 bottles of conditioner. I was really mad at this point! Then I noticed that there was thick yellow pee on the back of the toilet bowl - the kind that had been there for a while. Yuck. After a great time at our party I was looking foward to sleeping in - something we don't get to do very often because of our children. Too bad for us, the bed was so old & worn that my husband and I kept sinking into the middle. It was very uncomfortable. We left the Sheraton really unhappy with all aspects of our stay. It is a really disorganized and dirty hotel. They need a complete overhaul and new managment.

“Clean, Quiet, Close to Medical Ctr.” I used 60,000 hilton points to stay here for two days. I requested a double bed room, and got a room with a suite. It included a sofa, three chairs, desk and two tv's and an additonal half bath! This hotel looks old, but everything inside is new. Furniture, bedding, fixtures, carpeting - everything was recently added. I was in Houston to viist a relative in ICU at St. Luke's The free shuttle service to the hospital was great! Sunday, the driver took us to the hospital, picked us up, took us straight to a restaurant, picked us up and took us back to the hospital. Monday was a different story. It was extremely busy at the hotel and at the hospital. Traffic was awful and the shuttle service was crowded with other hotel guests needing rides to the hospital, creating a long wait. 2 pots of coffee and danishes from room service costs $28. Bath robes in the room were a nice touch and so was the refrigerator. I was in room 1212 and had a fantastic view of downton Houston. No free newspaper on the weekends. Parking is $15 a day if you have a car. No shopping is walkable. Shops at the university village were nice and we had an excellent breakfast and a manicure. My only complaint was the smoke alarm test at 7:00am my last morning. Someone came over the loud speaker in the room saying, "This is a test"! I called the front desk and complained,but other than that, I had a very nice stay for a stressful, health related visit.

“In a Class By Itself” As far as I'm concerned, this is in a class by itself. First off, the grounds are amazing, romantic, and beautifully manicured, you almost feel like you're in a tropical jungle all your own. There are swans in the man made streams that add to the romance of the place. You wouldn't even know that you were ten mins. from gridlocked Los Angeles if you didn't know where you were. This place is very special for its impeccabley decorated and comfortable rooms, with the feeling of total privacy and the staff's attention to detail and eagerness to please. Nearly every monarch has stayed here from Princess Grace to all the Scandinavian Princes and Princesses, and Queen Juliana of Holland as well. The grouds are perfect for weddings and the hotel is smart to only schedule one at a time; many hotels do not do this, so you have to compete with other wedding parties for any space. I have been coming here for nearly thirteen years now and always enjoy my stay and visits immensely. The food is great (the best hamburgers) and awesome drinks made by my fave bartender, Gus. If privacy, civility and pampering are what you have been yearning for, make a stay here a top of the list priority, you won't be disappointed. I prefer this to the Beverly Hills Hotel (also a "10") but with less feeling of privacy. A real gem!

“One Night Stop - LOUD LOUD LOUD” There was a wedding at the hotel the night we stopped in on our way home during our travels. This was a mistake. All the rooms around us were loud, in the middle of the night we called security and in stead of going to their room he came to ours and told us to be quiet! The bustle continued, including the drunken bride screaming at the top of her lungs, hope she remembers it... It was okay, not really worth the money, though

“Pretty good for the money” Not a bad place. Good location, close to the Empire State Building and not too far from the subway. Recently remodeled, so everything's nice and new. Only problem was that even though the front desk guy said that all the rooms were nonsmoking, my room still smelled like smoke. Sorry to all you smokers out there, but you know it's true...Smoke is the worst and most persistent stench there is. My clothes all stank like I was a pack a day smoker after two nights here. Never waited for the bathroom. Never even saw anyone else using the bathroom.

“Outstanding Rooms and Service” I stayed at the Ballantyne Hotel for a two day conference in October, and was thoroughly impressed with finish and size of the rooms, along with the outstanding service. This seems to be an ideal location for golfers, and regrettably I was unable to play while on business. While not in downtown Charlotte, there is a outdoor mall which is located just across the street. I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Nice enough, big room, a little dated” This hotel is well located on the mall and for other things in Dallas. I arrived late and was given a very large room which was nice but a little dated. The bed, flat screen etc were fine. Furniture in room is art deco selected. Coffee in foyer was good. The bathroom is a tribute to travertine - double sinks and large shower with hot tub enclosed - difficult to get in and out. The shower had the hair-trigger hot/cold yips so I could not get temp set (room 1530 westin folks). I got speedy after hours room service but the staff brought jelly, jam and honey rather than ketchup, mustard etc for my cheese, egg, patty sandwich on bagel. The bed, as usual at westin was comfortable. Allinall a good option depending on the deal.

“This is an exceptional hotel” The service, from the singing doorman to the front desk clerks, to the bellman was wonderful. It is an eclectic hotel in a great location. The rooms are roomy and it was a very enjoyable stay during the last week in May.

“Very pleased with the Holiday Inn” I was very pleased with this facility. It has been completely redone recently and felt like a brand new hotel. The location doesn't lend itself to walking and sight-seeing, but is very convenient by car to most attractions and the interstate. The front desk was helpful and courteous. Amber was delightful when we checked. I would stay there again in a second and have no problem recommending it.

“Slow and unreliable internet, few early food choices” This is a clean little boutique hotel in the gentrified South of Market area of San Francisco, right on the embarcadero. It is close to the Embarcadero BART stop and the bus lines on Mission.. It is also close to the downtown office core, but don't mistake this cozy little place for a business hotel. The internet is very inconsistent and often quite slow. If you want real food early in the morning, either because you have early work meetings or are just jet lagged, you are out of luck. The hotel offers a healthy start "continental" breakfast, but their idea of healthy is pastries. There is no taxi stand here, so if you need a taxi plan to wait while they call one for you. The room was clean. The time on the digital clock is almost impossible to see.

“Verrrrryy Basic” I can't honestly say this hotel was even CLOSE to being worth the money. However it wasn't a terrible experience. Cons: Super simple, TINY rooms, no free internet (just wifi not wireless?) Pros: Good location, friendly staff, right next to the subway Basically, if this is the cheapest place, and you're not fussy when it comes to luxury as far as hotels go, OR if you just need a (small but clean) place to sleep- this is going to work for you

“Please avoid” Haaa. When I got to this motel, they found my reservation but did not have any room available. They told me they could not honor the reservation and I was on my own. They gave me the phone number of another Motel 6 ten miles away. After calling the central reservation phone number, they finally found a room. The room was moldy ans stinky. I hate the colors and plastic flooring they now put in the "refurbished" rooms of this motel chain. The hotel is not too far from the Riverwalk. You can walk there but this hotel is in a sketchy area of the city. I would personally avoid at all costs.

“Solid business hotel” I stayed here for a few nights on business. The hotel is very nice, and has a helpful staff. The rooms were a good size, and very comfortable. The only downside is that it is a little off the beaten path- pretty far from the stadiums and casinos. However, I would stay here again when I come back to Detroit.

“Felt like a Queen” Never thought I'd stay there, although I'd heard so much about the Round Table, etc. My friend had an extended stay at a Marriott out-of-state and had a free night. We came in to see a show and stay only one night, regrettably. Walking in we met Matilda, the hotel cat and she was so dignified. Friendly, too. We were upgraded from a Queen Room to King, and given vouchers for 2 free cocktails and 2 free continental breakfasts. We went to the lounge before our show and came back after, and I can't tell you how wonderful it was to sit in a lovely chair and be waited on by such gentlemanly waiters. The entire staff at this hotel is incredible. It was Old World, and my friend and I have stayed at about 18 hotels in NYC in the past 6 years. This was one of the best. If you like fruit and croissants and muffins, the free breakfast was great. The bed was comfortable and the shower easy to use and satisfying, as well as the soaps and amenities. Really nice place.

“Great Airport Hotel, Albeit hard to find” A very nice hotel, nicely updated. Reggie at the Mgr. Reception was fantastic. The hotel is hard to get to, yet close to the airport. Super value for the money. Very quiet.

“Fantastic Hotel!” I had a one night stay at the Fashion 26 Hotel as I was in the city for business meetings. It is in a great location a few blocks from Penn Station, which is convenient when you take the train into NYC. Check in was fast and there were free cupcakes to be had (though I did not partake). Lobby is stylish. My room was huge by NYC standards and really well-arranged. The work station was excellent with mutliple outlets for plugging in and charging electronics and free wi-fi. Flat screen on the wall. Comfy bed. Large bathroom with high quality toiletries and great shower. It was very, very clean (and I am very Type A about the clean factor). This will be my go-to hotel whenever I am in the city, especially considering the very reasonable rate.

“very disappointing - not 5 star” Following a 10 day trip driving around Arizona we decided to end with a stay at this advertised luxury 5 star resort, but were very disappointed. Previoulsy we have stayed at the Fairmont scottsdale princess & the Biltmore, both in Scottsdale. Firstly the resort is huge - 585 rooms and very impersonal. People at the check in desk were very impersonal (I am a silver VIP member of Hilton's loyalty club) and mistakes were made on our booking, with no hint of apology. We had booked a romance package which included a premium suite with view, champagne and b/fast. We had to ask repeatedly for the wine and as they do not have 24 hour room service then we missed our pre paid b/fast as we had an early flight, as this resort is a good 25/30 minute drive from Phoenix Airport - don't believe the blurb that is it closer. When we asked the resort staff if they could organise something for us they said no! No assistance was offered with bags and the bell desk was unhelpful and gave wrong info. The room (No.4130) was Ok - nothing special, although it was quite spacious. We did have a view - but we also had a view of the air con units and they were very noisy at night. The bathroom was small & basic and the bath was just a standard issue with very low & small hotel bath - no good if you are over 4 feet. The suite was supposedly recently re modelled but the carpet was stained and furniture scratched, and hard to beleive but all of the ornaments/accesserioes were actually glued or nailed to the surfaces - and as we had booked a 5 star hotel and paid $280 for the package we were insuted that the hotel has pre decided that guests could not be trusted! This resort is called the ciffs for a reason - it is built into the side of a cliff and a lot of the suites are up several flights of stairs and along balconies, there are elevators but they are old and not located next to the suites. Parking is a nightmare - there are main carparks which are quite a way from the rooms but there are not enough car spaces for the suites within a close proximity. If you had a large car or had a lot of unloading to do or you have mobility problems then you may struggle. It took 10 minutes of very careful manovering to try and park our car in a very small space- very fustrating. Whist the resort grounds were well kept, the surrounding area was not great and we ended up traveling back to scottsdale to find somewhere where we wanted to eat. There are no faciities outside of the resort within walking distance and the area to the south is not one you would want to be in late at night In all very dissapointing, overpriced and we will not be returning. If we had another night in Phoenix we would stay at the Fairmont or the Biltmore both if which advertise great deals via their websites or Hotels. Scottsdale is a much better location for the airport and facilities, we are frequent international travellers and would not recommend this hotel.

“Dags för renovering” Bodde i en av Tower sviterna som var helt OK, stort rum med alla bekvämligheter du kan tänka dig men hotellet är i behov av en renovering då det mesta kändes gammalt och slitet. Läget är perfekt alldeles vid Union Square och kan Hilton få till en uppfräschning av hotellet kommer jag garanterat att checka in snart igen

“Nothing to write home about” Based on the TripAdvisor Reviews, I expected to be really WOWED by this hotel. Unfortunately, my experience just didn't measure up to other reviews. I arrived at the hotel at the same time as many other guests for a very large conference. Most of the guests were young, college students. In any case, I had a couple of bags and there were several bellmen standing in front of the hotel and not ONE of them offered assistance. They just pointed me to the front desk. Whatever. I can deal. The physical lobby space is absolutely gorgeous. Very tasteful and elegant. I loved it. The check-in process was easy and the desk clerk was friendly. My room was in the main bldg (there are two towers) and I was on the 16th floor. My room was neat with two double beds (even though I booked a King room, but again...it wasn't important enough to me to make a big deal about it). One criticism I noted right away was that there wasn't enough space on either side of the double beds to get in from both sides. You could only get into both beds from the center. And the beds had built in reading lights, but only on one-half the bed!? That was strange to me, as well. My room was obviously an older room. The tile and faucet fixtures had seen better days, but the room was clean, so I was fine. My bathroom sink had a slow drain, so every time I washed my hands I had to turn off the water, let it drain and resume. The bath had a separate tub and shower stall and there was a separate toilet closet. I'm sure when the hotel was built these rooms were breathtaking. Now they are starting to look dated. One HUGE plus is that the bed was heavenly. No complaints on the quality of the bed. It was super comfortable. They also had room service menus in my room, but the pages were falling out of the book from the torn tabs, and the "specials" were dated Fall 2011 (it's now Nov 2012). Also, they had options from their Asian restaurant Pagoda, except I was told the restaurant is no longer open.
