Also, my clock had the wrong time set (they hadn't reset the clocks for daylight savings time), so I had to reset that myself. The staff were ok. I honestly can't say that customer service was their forte. I went to the concierge desk shortly after arriving to find out how to take the light rail that stops by the hotel to the convention center (the convention cntr is literally like 2 1/2 blocks away, but I have a disability, so that short walk was difficult). In any case, the girls pointed me to the back of the hotel and couldn't tell me much. They had no literature or schedule for the rail station. They couldn't tell me for sure if the train went there. It turns out that the train in back of the hotel came FROM the Conv Cntr, but not to. I digress. The Concierge desk should have been able to tell me SOMETHING. They were clueless. Also had a "run-in" with hotel security. As I was rounding a corner, I noticed a hotel employee approach a room door and mumble (literally mumble) "security," and he just went into the room and closed the door. He didn't knock. He didn't wait for a response. He didn't even project so that anyone would have heard him! He just went into the room. So I stood outside and waited because I wanted to see if he left with anything and he came out with a bag (it looked like one of our convention bags), so I confronted him and asked him if it was normal for them to just go into guests rooms like that. He was sarcastic at first and said, "Yeah, that's what we do all day." And then he got angry and said, "No, it's lost and found!" and walked away. I was kind of weirded out by the entire thing, but I let it go. They have a couple of restaurants and a lounge. The Grill is a like an upscale steakhouse almost. Very pricey. I didn't eat there. I did have lunch at The Fountain restaurant (which I didn't even know was there until I'd been there a couple of days. It's kind of in an obscure part of the hotel, and not as visible as everything else. The decor of The Fountain was very bright and just a great environment that you'd want to have a formal brunch in. The restaurant was completely EMPTY though at lunch (and every hotel downtown was sold out). The staff were...odd. I was seated and given a menu. The waitress started asking too many questions about why I was there and where I was from. I didn't want to give this woman a life history. I just wanted lunch. Then she noticed that I'd brought in a little box from the bakery across the street, and said, "I see you already brought dessert. What is that?" Now, I may be a little weird, but for some reason I didn't want to tell her what I'd bought. I just wanted to eat my lunch, and I thought she was being too comfortable with me. That's just me. On the plus side, I had the salmon with orzo and peas, and it was delicious. Salmon was moist and flaky, and everything was flavorful. The lounge bar in the middle of the hotel lobby was interesting. They had music a couple of nights we were there. The bands were very good. A couple of people looked like they were ballroom dancing. The crowds looked pretty swanky. I did enjoy seeing people enjoying themselves there. I don't get to see people gussied up and partying like that very often. Overall, for the cost of the hotel (my first night was about $265, the 2nd night was $200-something, one night was $199 and the other night I can't remember), but this hotel wasn't cheap, and I just felt like it didn't live up to the hype. I think the hotel took our business for granted and just completely lacked in customer service for our group.

“Not the usualy Grand Hyatt standards” The staff is very attentive and handled any issues immediately. We have stayed in several Hyatt properties. I must say that the reason we selected the GH was because of the killer rate of $139.00 per night which included $20.00 per day for food and beverages. This almost canceled the $25.00 per night parking fee. The Denver property is a bit tired. We had a large room with a mountain view. The bed was not as comfortable as most. The bathroom was small and outdated. While already showering, discovered that housekeeping had neglected to provide shampoo. This property is more suited for business travelers. We were on a relaxing long weekend. Next time, we will stay in the LoDo area because of the variety of better restaurants and shopping. The GH is a great location for checking out the museums though.

“Great hotel, location, staff and vibe. We will be back...” My wife and I stayed here in June '11, and had an excellent stay. The hotel itself is obviously a great conversation piece in that it was once a prison, and the hotel plays this up just enough. The decor is minimalist and modern without feeling cold, and the hotel staff proved to be very friendly and helpful. We were there for three days, and two staff members were already addressing me by name! They offer free bike rentals, and we took advantage of this as well. Boston is pretty easy to get around and the bikes proved to be a cool little add on. There are a couple of dining options in the hotel, but we didn't get around to them. However, we did order room service and the food was good and the service was prompt. The rooms were well decorated, clean, and our view of the city was fantastic (12th flr). Boston is relatively small for a big city, and it's easy to get to any part you desire. But you still can't beat the Beacon Hill neighborhood you're in at the Liberty.

“Tragically Hip!” W hotels have a brand all their own. They are stylish, modern and very hip. If this is what you are searching for then you will not be disappointed. In addition the room was surprisingly large for a boutique hotel in New York. The sleeping area was superb and the bathroom was a real luxury. The staff were all very courteous and attentive. That being said there are one or two drawbacks. First of all I a, not a fan of the financial district. It is a soulless part of an otherwise vibrant city. In future I would opt for a hotel in Soho, the Village, or possibly closer to Union Square. Second of all, I personally feel that the W chain takes itself too seriously and often feel that the modernity comes at a cost of some basic practicalities and creature comforts. The room was marvelous but the bathroom lacked some basic fixtures for hanging up wet towels for example. The darkness in the lobby and bar areas seem cool at first but when black greets you in every room even at 9am it becomes a little tired very quickly. The most irritating aspect of the stay was the so-called complimentary Accura car service. Upon check-in you are told that there's is one free complimentary drop off in the city with the hotel's Accura fleet for each day of your stay. We tried to book this on three separate occasions without success. We also witnessed other guests being told that the service was unavailable. One of the basics rules of hospitality is under promise and over deliver. By turning this old adage on its head the hotel left numerous guests feeling disappointed.

“Wonderful Hotel” Stayed twice in June and both visits were wonderful. Staff very friendly, rooms comfortable with great bathrooms. Had room service one night and did take a very long time and food was poor quality which would be our only criticism. Great location walking distance to everywhere and near subway Wine hour was fab Gym looked good but did not use Kimpton in touch bar credit is great

“Fabled Waldorf Astoria Impresses” Although I'm not typically a fan of older hotels, one cannot help but be impressed by the old world charm this fabled New York City hotel holds, and the art deco architectural details both outside and through out the property are truly amazing. I did not have a chance to enjoy the hotels' amenities or visit any of the three hotel restaurants, but I did appreciate my slightly quirky but spacious corner room on the 11th floor with high ceilings, large closet and small work space. The hotel is very convenient to Midtown attractions but beware that this iconic property means that the lobby is always busy. Hotel guests mingle with curious visitors coming to photograph the lobby and or attend one of the many events the property seems to always host.

“Hyatt by the Ferry Building” I recommend this place. The room was very large, especially for a big-city hotel, and the housekeeping was excellent. The location is terrific--a block or so from the spectacular Ferry Building. The atrium is quite dramatic. My only criticism is the really odd entrance--you walk in through a respectable entry, only to run smack into a cramped area with an escalator as the focal point.

“Great location and staff” I stayed at this hotel for one night - great location! You are right in the Stockyards and can easily walk to everything. The staff was very helpful when we had a problem with our rental car, and went above and beyond to help us. My only complaint would be that the rooms are a bit outdated for the price of the hotel - the bathroom was shabby and definitely needed to be redone. The room was a bit dark due to the fact that it felt old. However, it was all very clean and unique - loved the theme of the room!

“Unique place” Stayed 2 nights in March 2007 to attend a conference in downtown. The Inn consists of a cluster of old restored buildings each with its own unique history and architectural style. I'm certainly no expert in architecture but I found the buildings fascinating. The rooms have been refurbished and updated and were spacious and clean. The free breakfast had a nice selection of fresh fruit and other items. There was free parking and the free shuttle service was convenient. The immediate surrounding area appeared safe. I am certainly glad I had an opportunity to stay here and recommend this place to anyone looking for something beyond the average cookie-cutter hotel.

“my favorite hotel in the world” Everything about this hotel is thoughtful. The lobby is large and clean with great modern art. Rooms are INCREDIBLE! Plush bed, Bowers & Wilkins iPod dock, fireplace in nearly every room, huge soaking tub, tv in mirror in bathroom, shower and tub separate, refrigerator separate from minibar, wet bar, great views. If you can think of it, it's probably set up here. Staff is incredibly friendly and the no tipping policy is great.

“Hotel Rooms Well Past Their Prime” Very disappointed in this Waldorf Astoria. While the public space was elegant and wonderful, the rooms were far from that. My room had stains on the carpets and draperies. The carpet had obviously been patched due to stains that couldn't be removed. There was a phone jack next to the toilet, there was easily a quarter inch of dust built up on the edge. The tub didn't drain properly so while you showered, you were standing in 2-3 inches of water. I will say the service was excellent as was the room service. But, the room was well below the standard of a four star/diamond establishment. The internet was a per day charge. I was happy that I was a premier customer with Hilton so that I didn't have to pay because it was spotty at best and non-existent at worst. The only two good things I can say about the room was the air conditioning was excellent and the bedding package was great. But, the housekeeping was poor. I stayed at another Hilton brand last year that was almost half the rate that was far superior to this hotel. The only reason I am giving the third bubble on this (as opposed to two) is because the service was great.

“Trains! Lots & lots of trains!” I should have heeded the warnings of previous reviewers. This is a nice hotel, with very pleasant staff, but just after getting to my room I began hearing the trains. They come through CONSTANTLY. And blow their horns all the way by. I asked for another room, and was told that it would not make a difference. A printed note on the nightstand said that many guests comment about the trains, so free earplugs were in the drawer. I used them, but was still awakened by blaring horns all night long. In a 12-hour period at least 20 passed by. I checked out the next morning and moved to a Hampton Inn close to the airport. The room was clean and comfortable, but I could never recommend this hotel to anyone. Look elsewhere!!!

“Disappointing for a Homewood Suites” There are some pros and cons with this hotel, but I cut my stay short because of some issues I encountered. I’m a Hilton Gold honors member, who travels six to nine months out of the year, and I was very disappointed with my four-week stay. Pros: * Great location; walking distance to Red Line stop at Grand/State; shops; restaurants; Jewel-Osco grocery store one block away. * Good breakfast and dinner options; healthy. * Friendly, helpful staff (with a few exceptions noted below). Cons: * Smoky smelling on some floors and in the hallways. * Housekeeping is a hit or miss. I switched rooms because because some of the bureau drawers were dirty and had hair in them; another room/hallway smelled like smoke. Housekeeping the rest of the stay was hit or miss. I came back to the room a few times around 5-6pm and the room had not been cleaned, yet I did not have the "do not disturb" sign on the door. When they did clean, sometimes they didn't replace all the items like towels, soap, dish detergent, etc., so I had to call down a few times to have items brought up. * No desk or chair provided in the room. I've stayed at several Homewoods over the years and this is the first time the room has not been equipped with a desk or chair, which I consider a necessity for business travelers. The building engineer brought me extra kitchen table and chair, which was adequate. * Spotty internet service, which comes and goes. It was very hard to work from the hotel with inconsistent internet service. * Very crowded hotel with families and tourists, which makes it noisy at times. * Slow elevators - expect to wait a bit to go up or down. * Good breakfast and dinner options like I mentioned, but the hotel is crowded, so food runs out quickly. Get there early to beat the crowds. I also wish they had more variety at breakfast - it was eggs, sausages, and potatoes six out of seven days of the week. Other Homewoods offer omelots, French toast, egg mcmuffin-style sandwiches. * Laundry is on the 7th floor, which is also the smoking floor. It was gross having to walk down the smelly hallway with my clean laundry. There are two washers/dryers, but one washer was broke the first three weeks I was there. They also charge you for laundry detergent (Tide and Downy), which hasn't been my experience at other Homewoods. My second week, however, they had run out of Tide, so I had to go out to buy some. How does an extended stay hotel run out of laundry detergent?! Again, this shows me this hotel is not geared toward the business traveler. * Problematic billing, which ultimately caused me to leave early. I realized they had charged my credit card two different charges, but I hadn't received a bill. I called down to the front desk and spoke to a lady who said she would send up the bill. The next morning I still had not received it, so I called again. The manager on duty interrupted me as I was explaining the situation and said "hold on, I don't know what you're talking about; I wasn't working yesterday." I told him I had two charges on my account and had asked for an itemized bill but I had not received it yet. He looked up my account and starting rattling off charges that were not mine. I verified he was looking at the correct room account and he said the charges were only authorizations. I explained to him I had a copy of my credit card statement and indeed, I had been charged. He again said the charges were only authorizations. I asked to speak to the manager on duty and he responded quite gruffly, I am on the manager on duty. To make a long story short, he was looking at the wrong computer screen and located the charges. He apologized and said he would send up the receipts. He called back a few minutes later and told me the receipts had been printed the day before and were laying on the desk, but had not been brought up. I'm a Hilton honors gold member and I've never had problems like this getting an itemized statement. The employee was extremely rude and ultimately, I cut my stay short because of the treatment I received. This hotel is definintely geared more towards families/tourists than a serious business traveler. I wouldn't stay here again and don't plan on returning.

“Nice Stay - Room Taxes!!” This hotel was fine; excellent room, very clean with great comfortable bed. Lobby was well appointed with a little bar, Starbucks, snack grill and comfortable seating with flat screens. What was not fine was the whopping 14.5% room tax tacked on the bill (no fault of hotel). Tax on a room for $289 added up to $41.76! Add the $10 parking fee the hotel charged and it adds up to 17.6% above the room charge. I usually don't notice hotel taxes and understand why they are imposed but $41 bucks on top of a $289 dollar room certainly got my attention. Positive criticism; the hotel would do well to put a young person at the entrance at minimum wage as a doorperson to help guests unload and load bags and keep the cars moving. It would be a nice addition to a nice hotel.

“Rather Disappointed” This is the second time we have stayed here. I keep being disappointed. We love the Mandarin, but the DC Mandarin is just not there. Our room was annoying. The closet was half size; the bath was European style in terms of the shower, the tv was on the side, and did not work that well. Even though we were hotel guests we could not get spa bookings, or CityZen bookings, and we made our reservation in advance. I may return, but I'm not that happy with the place.

“Worst, dirtiest, smelliest, Hilton in the US.” Last year alone I stayed around 90 nights in Hilton hotels. I have been in the majority of Hilton branded properties in the US. The Philadelphia airport property is so bad I scarcely know where to begin. The shuttle bus to the hotel took over an hour to pick me up. I watched as the Sheraton busses went past dozens of times before hilton's bus finally showed up. The bus should have scared me off. It was filthy, smelled bad, and the air conditioning didn't work. Entering the hotel I immediately noticed the smell of old rot. There are chunks of the ceiling falling and dangling down ready to fall. The staff was pleasant, but when I got on the elevator there was a new unpleasant odor of powerful cleaning solvents on top of a nastier rotten smell than the lobby. Getting off the elevator on my floor, the corridor smelled worse than the lobby or elevator. It smelled like musty dirty laundry which must be thrown away as it can't be washed clean. This is not a subtle odor but a pungent stink you cannot escape. My room was slightly better in aroma than the corridor. Slightly. It also had chunks of plaster falling down in the bathroom and above the room's window. The towels were a dingy color. I went to the vending machine on my floor to get a bottle of cola and it smelled as if someone had been urinating in the corner repeatedly for a long time. The smell was as bad as anything you'll encounter on Bourbon street in New Orleans. As bad as the rest of the place smelled, this was an order of magnitude worse and made me gag. I was originally planning to stay four nights at the Hilton. I checked out after one night and moved across the street to the cheaper A-Loft which still had dirty hallways but smelled clean and had no signs of decay like the Hilton. I would not recommend this Hilton to an enemy. Unless your sense of smell is disabled and you don't mind rotting filth, stay far far away from this Hilton. I am AMAZED that Hilton allows this place to use their name and logo.

“Looks can be deceiving...” My best friend & I stayed at the Moderne in July 2003 during a girls trip to NYC. The hotel looked interesting on the websites we searched & the price was $115 a night so we booked 3 nights. The location was excellent & the staff were very pleasant but upon opening the door to our room we were taken back. The room was clean but extremely small, much like a college dorm room with a large futon like bed & very dark, you couldn't tell if it was day or night when you woke up in the morning & forget about trying to look out the one small window in the room, it faced a brick wall. The best part of the hotel was the 24/7 coffee lounge with huge windows looking out on to the street below. The coffee lounge was a great place to unwind after a busy day & plan for the next day. Looking back I wouldn't change our hotel choice as it has become a funny memory of a fun trip to NYC but trust me, if you must stay at the Moderne do not pay more then $100 a night, there are plenty of other NYC hotels that are a better value. I would not stay at the Moderne again nor would I recommend it due to the room size vs. the price. If you want a decent priced hotel in a great location I would recommend the Quality Hotel Times Square or Milford Plaza.

“comfortable, clean & great location” This was a last minute crash pad for me. The room was small, but spotlessly clean, had a great mattress and linens. Toiletries and a coffee/tea maker are in the room. Continental breakfast was included. To top it off, I was on the top floor and had a view. I have been in some small hotel rooms in NYC and this one was small, but you do not have to be a contortionist to move around the room. There is an abundance of restaurants and entertainment within walking distance.

“I would stay here again” I stayed here for four nights while working in the area - I was there at the same time of the pageant girls that the reviewer below described but they must not have been on my floor because they didn't bother me. The rooms are fairly large and modern - I especially liked that the work desk was large enough to actually do work on. I liked the fitness center a lot, it seems to be newly updated but it is a little strange that you have to walk out into the mall to get to it. I was kind of worried about the crowds since the hotel is in the mall, but it worked out well for me that I was able to walk somewhere to dinner and not have to get out into houston traffic. The room has a mini fridge. There were only a couple of downsides - they have valet, but if you choose to self-park, it is mall parking. It didn't bother me since i had a rental, but if I had my own car I might have valeted. Also the housekeeper on my floor was just okay - the washcloths were never replaced so I ran out and did not have one my last day, and the drinking glasses were never changed out (this could be part of the hotel's "green" initiative). Other than that it was a good stay.

“Good value and helpful staff” This hotel opened in August 2008 on the site of a former senior living center. It's on the edge of downtown Ft. Worth in a location convenient to the interstate, but a few blocks away from most downtown attractions, which keeps the room cost down. There is no restaurant onsite or adjacent; if you have a car, however, there are plenty of restaurants and attractions within a short drive from the hotel. They've done an excellent job of renovating the building. The lobby and breakfast area are attractive and there are an exercise room and a small pool and hot tub on the ground floor. The rooms are well furnished and comfortable, ranking among the best HI Express hotels we've visited. We had no problems with noise, and the beds were comfortable. The staff was a real plus - every staff member we interacted with went out of his or her way to be helpful. A small error in our room rate was quickly and happily rectified at checkout. The hotel's rates compared very favorably with other similar hotels in the general vicinity. We would certainly stay at this hotel again.

“Uncomfortable bed.” We have stayed at this hotel a few times when we visit with family; we choose this location because it is a good value and proximity. The beds are very uncomfortable because there is only a mattress (poor quality) on a platform bed without a box spring. It is bearable for a one night stay, if you are looking for comfort, do not stay here. The window shades let a lot of light in; you might get a better night’s sleep if you choose a room that overlooks the front parking lot and not the back with the pool view. The pool view side of the building has bright lights to illuminate the back of the building and parking lot structure. I think the rooms have a good layout even though the rooms are small, you don’t feel too cramped. One thing I really don’t like about the layout is that if you turn the light on in the bathroom it will illuminate more than just the bathroom area. I think it is an average hotel if you know what to expect, if you stay at this hotel and expect it to be comparable to other Sheraton hotels you might be disappointed.

“Second stay here still as good” On a whirlwind tour of the west coast following a stay-over from a business trip, I ended up with one last night to spend in SF before heading back to the UK. Choosing the Marriot Marquis was a pretty simple step, as my previous stay there had been a good one AND I had to return a rental car to Hertz, who have desk within the hotel itself. I got the same level of service here as I had done previously, the staff were equally as helpful as before and my room was spacious, clean and comfortable. Another hour or so spent in The View confirmed it as a great spot to share a bottle of wine while staring out over the city. One very minor quibble came from a breakfast meeting i had been supposed to have there one week earlier, when I was kept waiting for a table for half an hour only to find that after asking me for my name and party size, no one had bothered to add me to the waiting list. Annoying, but a simple human error that I won't be hugely critical of, given the solid level of service normally seen.

“Very nice, but ...” The hotel is very nice, the staff is very friendly and helpful, and everything is kept very clean. The room was fairly small, but very comfortable and the bathroom was larger than many. Street noise was a bit of a problem in the night as the hotel is bordered by three busy streets. The property is on the riverwalk, but is at the far west end, with most of the restaurants, the Alamo, La Viata, etc. on the east loop of the river. It is a bit of a walk, but pleasant along the river.

“the diamond on the hill” We've been a lot of times in LA but this was our first time at Bel-Air Hotel. Everything has been AMAZING! When we arrived we had the warmest welcome ever and we understood early the very high level of service compared to many luxury hotels that we visited, this why the hotel is managed by the rare and magnificent General Manager Denise Flanders (all the staff love her). The cost per night is high but it is worth every single penny, this is not "only" a hotel, here you can live a wonderful experience that u will never forget. The hotel is surrounded by a beautiful garden on the hills of Bel-Air, its totally renewed (re-opened one year ago) for the exteriors they kept the 50s style and the interior has been superlatively modernized. Rooms are cozy and luxury and we were impressed by incredible beauty our Bel-Air Suite. Outstanding service in each area of the property, stunning pool and the best food ever in any restaurants. Try the inimitable Marilyn's Passion Cocktail at "The Bar & Lounge" and have the best LA burger ever. We didn't dine at Wolfgang Puck Restaurant but this is one of the many reasons to return to dream at Bel-Air Hotel as soon as possible. The best place to stay in LA!

“THE BEST! OUR 4TH STAY in 4 years ...” This hotel is a gem. We visited Chicago at Thanksgiving every year for at least 10 years before we found the Monaco. Now it's our hotel of choice. Perfectly located betw/ Mag Mile & State (and close to Ronnie's Steakhouse for breakfast). The window seats w/ the river view are to die for. Staff is always very nice. No waiting for elevators. My only complaint is that I can't get the Hot Rates, Hot Dates in the summer so I could really enjoy Millennium Park, which is only a short walk. Wish I could afford to become a permanent resident of the hotel.

“Decent Location for Conseco Fieldhouse” We set off from Lousiville to Indy on a rainy and then snowy Saturday (December 15) to attend a college basketball game. Access from I-65 north was easy off the Marekt Street exit. Our room was ready at 12:30 p.m. We were on the top floor in a large corner room. I would guess that the corner rooms are the largest in the hotel. With two large sets of windows, we had plenty of natural light. Sadly, the color scheme was an "icky" gold with heavy curtains at the windows. The bedding was very comfortable on our two double beds. TVs are not flat screen and still reside in the out of date "armoire". For us the location was excellent. We were 4 blocks from Conseco and one block from the main shopping street. The breakfast was OK. The cook was able to do simple eggs, pancakes, etc., but was cooking on glorified hot plates. The result was slow service! Personnel were young and very friendly. For a one night stay in Indy, the Hilton Garden Inn is reasonably priced and has a convient location.

“Fantastic Hotel” I stayed at the Affinia 50 for 4 nights in a one-bedroom suite in March with my husband and daughter. It was an overall great experience. The suite was huge--bigger than most apartments, especially those in NY! It had a large living room, separate dining area, small kitchen and a large bedroom. Only the bathroom was small--but the size of the rest of the suite made up for it. While it was not a super-luxury hotel, it was very clean and functional. The staff was always friendly, the location of the hotel was great, and the service was great. I travel to NY often for business and have stayed in many high-end hotels (often based on tripadvisor reviews). This was definitely deserving to be in the Top 10 list--I think it should be in the Top 3 myself. I would highly recommend it to anyone for business or personal travel.
“Very simple” Stay here. Nothing negative to say about this place. My first stay at a Garden Inn. I will try others when I travel.

“good location, great food, good service, not for the money savers” Stayed here two nights during a conference. They have a walkway that led to the meeting rooms in the Convention Center so it was quite convenient. There are several food options ranging from expensive to a little pricey, however, I must say the food was very good. Also, during my stay the hotel had a special dinner buffet that was very inexpensive but quite good. Check in/check out was quick, everyone was very friendly. My only problem was that there was a mistake with housekeeping and I didn't get my room cleaned until the 4th time I called down to the front desk which was around 4:00 pm. But the Housekeeping apologized for the mixup. The rooms were average Hilton but clean and comfortable and sound proof. The park adjacent had live music which also made the visit relaxing. The parking is about $25 valet plus tips and in room Internet is about $15.00 a day.

“Salto nel passato...” Hotel, che ha preso il posto del vecchio Comune di s.Francisco, che lascia sorpresi per l'opulenza della hall: lampadari in cristallo, tappeti e marmo in ogni angolo fanno immaginare che le quattro stelle siano riduttive; invece quando si giunge al piano e si esce dall'ascensore si manifesta un altro mondo: moquette che chiede un passaggio di aspirapolvere, qualche lampada fuori uso che rende i corridoi molto cupi, e camere non proprio extra large. In particolare in bagno i movimenti risultano un pò difficili. Ciò che invece è invidiabile è la posizione strategica su Market Street. Unico neo della zona è la presenza di persone non proprio idonee a diventare amiche: attenzione la notte.

“BRAVO - A Really well done job !!!” Excellent value for money!!! Great location, 7 minutes drive from the 101and 15 minutes from the 405 (the two arteries of LA). Staff - true pros. Juan Villa - the shift manager is a true canonball - efficient, curtious, zeilous.. The room was very nice and clean. The breakfast was fair (lets have some more vegetables) Handicapp: there's a fire station nearby - judging from the amount of exits with full horn and sirens, LA must be on FIRE!!! But be sure - I would come back again... Well done HOJOS..... I enjoyed the stay and would come back for sure

“Good for business” Stayed here in March 2012, while visiting Chicago on business. Check in and check out were quick and professional. The room was on a higher floor, with a great view of the city. The room was large and had all the needed modcons. The bathroom was also very nice, but I could have used more counter space, if I want to nitpick. There were a couple of notes and ear plugs for the noises from the building creaking and swaying in the high winds, but I didn't notice anything. Didn't eat at the hotel but did have room service. The food was appetizing and delivered in a timely manner. The hotel is in the middle of everything...so easy to get around. I would stay here again.

“Worth it” Well located downtown and easy to get to this large hotel is well staffed. Had a Vista Suite provided by the Company for business meetings at the hotel, The Vista suites are giant w/large bedroom; bathroom w/separate shower, and gargantuan living room w/dining table. Clean & comfortable. Meeting rooms were set well. Valet parking. Small and busy lobby bar. OK restaurant.

“Great Location for a Giant's Game” We stayed here when in town for a Giant's game. It's a beautiful, sophisticate hotel and I strongly recommend it if you want to be close to the south side of town. LOCATION: Close enough to walk to some excellent shopping on Union Square, close enough to walk to the Giant's game or to Moscone Center. ROOMS: Very sophisticated, automated blinds, all the touches you would find in the best Four Seasons. FOOD: We always order room service wherever we go, and the food was excellent, and the staff very professional and endearing in their earnest hard workingness. STAFF: Well served by all of them (the front desk people were the exception -jaded. OTHER: I stayed here when it first opened. The front desk made me feel so welcome and as if it were a true honor that I chose that hotel. They were proud to be there and that made me feel like I'd landed someplace really special. Now it's more "yep, same old, same old. here's your room key." Also, when you're an SPG and paying $650/night, please provide complimentary internet access.

“Gangbanger Central on Saturday night” Booked one night on priceline since my usual hotels were full and didn't feel like using Hilton points. Will never make that mistake again. Pulled into hotel lot on a Saturday night about 10:00 p.m. Lot was COMPLETELY full even at that fairly early hour, lot spaces are very inadequate to the number of rooms. Finally managed to find a place after circling four times. Just as I was only pulling my bags out, three cars in the lot, all vehicles carrying "gangbanger" types drove by (looking to park at the hotel, not leaving), looking at me and scoping out my car. Similar type patrons in the lobby and around the exterior corridors of the hotel. I am not shy about travel, I have walked and worked in rough downtown areas, but I do expect to feel at least a modicum of safety for my person and belongings/vehicle. As I was walking to the lobby, two police cruisers came into the lot, one to circle, the other to park for awhile. At that point, I had it -- I informed the management that I would rather waste my priceline bid and go stay somewhere else, which I did. I am very disappointed that a Best Western would allow this activity on its property. The police did not seem to act like this was an isolated incident, but rather one of their regular patrols. I do not leave a negative review unless I feel it really warrants it, and this one wins first prize for me. I will never book this property again, let alone stay here. It is unsafe-feeling, and I would never take a family here.

“Great Hotel with even a better staff” The JW marriott Union Square is my new favorite in San Francisco. If provides a good location & spectacular views ( upper floors) but is still small enough to have great service. Rooms are spacious ( for downtown SF) with seperate tub/shower along with a entry area and a workspace. The concierge lounge was very large with wonderful views of the city/bay in addition above average food.

“True 5 star hotel, beautiful facility, super friendly, helpful staff” This is one of the most beautiful and well run hotels we have stayed in over the last 20 years (and that includes very fine hotels from Japan to Europe, and all over North America). The hotel is beautiful inside - see pictures http://www.hotelpalomar-dc.com/index.html There is, as others have noted, a free wine hour each evening. The superb facility is exceeded in only 1 way - the extremely helpful, knowledgeable and friendly staff. Typical was "Rick" at the front desk, who patiently and skillfully answered questions for 10 minutes about a variety of area restaurants. He pointed us to several terrific restaurants, starting with Scion (see separate review). There are, within 1 block, more than 15 (really) restaurants, including several that are award winning. The DuPont metro is a 5 minute walk (although be sure to get directions because one of the station is closed as of early Oct, 2012) In some beautiful hotels, the staff is impressed with the hotel and themselves. In this hotel, the leadership has picked and trained people very, very well. They are committed to the highest levels of service, done in a very friendly manner.

“Wonderful hotel but watch out for the East and West...” A very good friend of ours found this gem of a hotel on Priceline. We didn't realise it was between $400 - 500 a night! So considering that we got a room at this hotel for nearly 1/3 of the price, it was well worth it. The hotel is situated close to 42nd street and 1st avenue. So you are situated slap bang on the East River. No ugly buildings to obscure your view. The hotel entrance is outstanding. Dark green marble decor with mirrors reflecting beautiful lit chandeliers. The reception area can be a bit frustrating as there is a seating area slap bang in the middle of it making queuing slightly awkard, but this didn't pose much of a problem . We phoned in advance in search for the highest level of the hotel and when we arrived, the receptionist gave us a suite on level 41 - the highest level on the East block of the hotel which we were extremely happy with. However, upon closer inspection of the room, it clearly was not as nice as one would have expected. The bedding was slightly torn, TV, furniture and carpet were old although the room was very spacious. In the bathroom, we found many disgusting long strands of hair wrapped around the shower head. We quickly complained about this and then we were put into another room (level 31) on the West block. This room was significantly better than the previous room. Everything was newer (see pics). The furniture all had glass tops and wooden cupboards and this theme also extended to the bathroom. We were situated on the corner which gave us pleasant views of the East River and of the Chrysler and Empire State Buildings. The bed was very comfortable and again the room was very spacious. This hotel has a swimming pool, fitness centre and also a tennis court (the only one in NYC). We would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone. It is slightly further out than other hotels from Broadway, but if you don't mind an extra 5-10 min leisurely stroll, then go for this hotel. Getting it on Priceline made it a fantastic bargain. I would suggest you ask for a room in advance for the newer (and cleaner) renovated rooms in the West Building. Without thinking about the bad experience in the East Building, we definitely give this hotel the thumbs up.

“Not as Advertised” How this hotel was rated a 4-star, I'll never know. It's a 3-star at best. Although we booked on Priceline, and could not choose the type of room we wanted in advance, I called the hotel two weeks prior to arrival to request a king-size bed. The gentleman who spoke to me assured me that it was noted in our reservation. Not so. First, we were sent to a room with two doubles. Second, we were told that no kings were available, and the best we could do was a queen. We settled for that, but were just dumbfounded at how TINY the room was. When we again inquired about moving, we were told that our current room was the largest size in the hotel! The bathrooms are so small that they cannot accommodate two people at the same time. The maid service was shoddy - one day she only left us one "glass", i.e., plastic cup. My husband liked the location, but for me, five blocks off Michigan Avenue is three too many. Never again!

“Fine Place--Not The Grandeur You're Led To Expect--But Still Worthwhile” It can be difficult to get a good, comfortable location in San Francisco at corporate (i.e., fairly cheap) rates so I was pleased that the Fairmont on Nob Hill was available for business travel. My expectations were probably higher than they should have been but I still had a good stay and would do it again. My pros and cons this trip: The lobby didn't inspire me. The restaurant and bar behind the lobby was generic. The concierge desk is constantly busy, expect to wait up to ten minutes for assistance most times of the day and then get limited results. The door man at the entrance to the hotel will provide the same information you need with some real insider detail--so tip accordingly. Overall, the staff, while busy (there's always a crowd in the lobby) remained professional and courteous. Room: My room was large enough, but surprisingly sparse with standard furniture that really didn't do justice to the hotel's reputation. I had to do some work at the desk in the room and it was shoved into a cramped corner next to the bed. On the plus side, personally important criteria were met: The bed was super comfortable, and the location was surprisingly quiet even with a room over the main entrance. Housekeeping was very good. For the business/conference traveler: The business center was lame--you are asked to pay for computer use even to print an airline boarding pass. Wireless internet in your room has to be paid for, of course, but if you join the Fairmont membership program (free) the service is complimentary. Also, the wireless was quite fast. Side note: The Tonga Room and Hurricane Bar is to be found a few floors under the lobby. I checked it out for a cocktail. It's like Disney's Tiki Room attraction for adults. It's kind of tacky, the food is supposed to be fair, and my Mai-Tai probably ripped a hole in my esophagus--it may have been mixed with rubbing alcohol. In other words, I liked this place a lot and hope it stays around for many years. Summary: If you plan to spend top money on a property in San Francisco, you may be let down a bit by the Fairmont. However, it's still a very good option for a short stay, say two to three days. It's also a good base for a family vacation, and it beats the tourist madness around the Wharf. I had the sense that corporate may be trying to catch up to some of the amenities other brands offer, but give them credit for trying.

“SPG opens all of the right doors so that local properties slam them in your face - especially SPG Platinum Guests” I decided to give this Sheraton property another chance being that it is one of my least favorite Starwood properties mostly because as a Platinum guest, this hotel has NEVER tried to earn my business nor even recognize my status. First, parking is still $22.00 for self park in an outdoor lot. The hotel has an outdoor pool and has two towers or wings. I drove up to the main wing where the club lounge is and was told that my reservation was for the other tower and when I arrived at the other tower I was told that I had a room reserved at the other tower and this would have continued if I did not end it and ask both towers to just assign me a room. Needless to say, they put me in the tower that does not have a club lounge nor did they want to compensate with a drink coupon. They did not seem to care and the checkin desk did not have a gold/platinum desk so there are no perks for being platinum. When I got to my room, I had a wonderful view of Harbor Drive and the airport. The other side overlooks N. Island and downtown. I guess that these rooms are still unavailable for platinum guests. The rooms are nicely redone but very small. The rooms all have electronic minibars and I did find one bottle of water was free as per the tag on the bottle. Typically, folks do not open the minibar for fears of being charged up to $5.00 for a bottle of water. Here, the complimentary bottle is free so I recommend getting it. The decor is nautical in nature and colors and they did a good job redecorating the room. The bathroom was also updated and the sink has a white marble top with porcelain sink. The rooms all have motion sensors that tie the cooking and lights together and when you leave, they will shutoff the power as a means of conserving energy. The rooms are dark due to low power energy efficient bulbs.

“Great room, staff and price.” This is a great central location. We had a wonderful large room and an early check in. A room on the opposite side of the hospital is optimal. There is a Whole Foods, CVS, and a bagel resturant a few steps from the hotel. The staff couldn't have been more helpful.

“It just simply WORKS!” If you are travelling to do business in downtown Philly (and particularly if you are attending an event at the Philadelphia Convention Center) and are on a budget, this is the place to go. A quick one-block walk to the Convention Center saves your feet. Free WiFi saves your budget. And like all Courtyards, it is predictable -- the rooms are spacious and well appointed, the lighting is good, it comes equipped with a coffee maker and mini-fridge. Luxurious? No but a strong contender for efficiency and cost-benefit!

“what a view - great staff - great hotel” Ok - it is an older hotel but we were given a renovated room on the 22nd floor. The hotel does have that old smell to it...they should see about that. The room was lovely and all upgraded bath items. The view from the room and from the bar on the upper floor was fantastic. A nice walk to the downtown area and we had no trouble finding our way around. Parking is $28 a night and the drinks at the bar a bit pricey, but the view at night is wonderful. Staff were very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel for adults who want to see downtown Seattle.

“Good location, room not the best” The location couldn't be better: very close to Michigan. The male staff is friendly, female staff less so. Expensive valet parking. The lobby is not impressive at all. The room had no view, was small, lacked most toiletries, but was clean. A major complaint was the heating that didn't let us sleep at night, turning on and off all the time. Breakfast (if you want to call it so) doesn't deserve your time: go out and use the closeby Starbucks! For what you get the price is barely acceptable, but if you consider that you are at least getting free internet, I'd say, go for it, if you want the cheapest acceptable hotel in the best location!

“Wonderful Stay” Was warmly greeted and welcomed. Had a delightful stay. The staff was helpful and courtous. The rooms were well appointed, quite, and spacious, for NYC. Turn down service was a bonus. No problems at all. A warm and welcoming lobby to greet you.

“I'll Be Back” I like this hotel. It's small, cozy, and comfortable. The staff at the front desk is exceedingly friendly and very competent. There is an evening wine reception from 5:00 to 6:00 in the lobby, accompanied this time of year by a nice fire in the fireplace. I was upgraded to a King Premier room, which had a full size sofa and armchair, a small desk, and a flat screen TV in addition to the king size bed. Check out the closet for animal print bathrobes! A nice perk for members of the Kimpton InTouch program is a "Raid the Mini Bar" card for up to $10 worth of your choice. Unfortunately that doesn't buy much at the mini bar prices. One downside to this and most really nice hotels is no in-room coffee. However, morning coffee service is available in the lobby... along with a big fire in the fireplace. Tulio is a pleasant Italian restaurant providing service to the hotel. The food was delicious and service was very good (Efren). Especially notable were the orecchiette with spicy Italian sausage and a scrumptious pork shank that falls off the bone. I felt bad because there was no way I could eat it all. Definitely a highlight of my stay. One minor downside - I was a bit surprised that I could still hear traffic on the 10th floor. Not enough to affect my sleep, though... I'll be back.

“Extremely impressive staff, great location!” Had a fantastic Valentine's weekend stay at the Hilton. This is a huge property so there's always a lot going on but everything seems to be well controlled. Security is omniprescent at the hotel so it made me feel safe and secure. There are a lot of beggars and homeless in San Francisco (the worst part of any visit here!) so security is important. Check-in was easy. The friendly check-in clerk asked if it was my first time staying at this Hilton. As a first time guest I was given free Internet for the whole stay at a Ghiardelli chocolate. A very nice, thoughtful touch that started everything well. I was easily accomodated for two double beds instead of 1 queen. Hours after checking in I received a phone call asking if everything was satisfactory and the person seemed genuinely friendly and nice...another great touch. I didn't need anything but it's nice to know they care! The rooms themselves are a bit old with CRT televisions, wired internet, and some old looking furniture, however, everything was clean and well kept. Beds and linens were extremely comfortable and the hotel was very quiet. Bathroom was small but made a great use of space. Everything is smaller in San Francisco so these were actually good sized rooms given the location. Ate at the Urban Tavern and it was delicious and has a cool ambiance. Go for their happy hour specials and you don't be disappointed. The meatloaf sliders were expensive but quite tasty. There's a good selection of local beers on tap. An erroneous mini bar charge was quickly corrected upon check out and I was able to stow my luggage all day while I enjoyed the city. People could not have been nicer or more friendly.... excellent staff! Obtained this hotel on priceline for an exceptionally good rate and was still treated first class. This is a FAR better hotel to get using priceline than the Hotel Nikko across the street (where I stayed last time). The Nikko shoves you in a tiny spit of a room with a double bed. If you want a bigger room you have to pay to upgrade. Not so with the Hilton, they don't have rooms like that so you get a standard room whether or not you booked on priceline. Will be back at this hotel in a second the next time I'm in San Francisco! Thank you for a wonderful stay.

“Very Pleasant Stay...Terrible WiFi” Upon check-in the very gracious Palomar staff upgraded me to a pretty nice suite. I don't know what I did to deserve that but I wasn't asking. The suite was very clean and spacious, the bed was super comfortable and the jacuzzi was a blessing after a long day. My only complaint was that the WiFi was pretty horrible and my plan to put in a few hours of work before an event went down the drain. Even after signing up for the Kimpton membership for free WiFi, it was just a nightmare. I ended up working on my BB which was very time consuming. As a business traveler, Wifi is super important. I'm not sure if I could stay here again.

“Not for Couples/Great for Families” Spent a few nights here with my spouse the week after Christmas. Things we liked Room was very nice and spacious & clean. Full Breakfast & Free Happy hour were a terrific value. Location was pretty good. Things we disliked Downstairs atmosphere, Gone is the open air courtyard in this new embassy suites design. Atmosphere in the attatched restaurant for breakfast was hectic/overcrowded dodging kids to get back to your table to eat. Atmosphere in Happy Hour area was bordering on tacky, overlit Basement kind of feel, crowded and noisy. Our bottom line. Would highly recommend this hotel for families with kids as this seems to be their clientele. For couples & singles or business travelers there are better places to stay. We much preferred the Grand Hyatt Across the way.

“Schmutzig, unsichere Gegend, teuer” Hotels in San Francisco sind teuer, aber über $ 100 für ein altes, teils verschmutztes Zimmer in einer sehr heißen Wohnlage sind zu viel. Die Matratzen in unserem Zimmer waren vollkommen verschmutzt, der Schmutz kam sogar durch das Bettlaken nach oben. Das Wlan ist kostenfrei aber total instabil. Der Empfang ist in vielen Bereichen schwach, die Router müssen oft neugestartet werden, unbrauchbar. Positiv zu erwähnen ist die MÖGLICHKEIT (!) kostenfrei zu parken. Sind die wenigen Plätze weg, muss man teuer in der Nachbarschaft parken (ca.$ 20 pro Tag).

“Consistently Good.” I've stayed here on a number of occasions over the past eighteen months and have found the experience to be consistently satisfactory, despite the disruption from renovations. However, what really sets it apart is the genuine service culture among employees, consistently excellent in my experience, and adding a lot of character to the hotel. Now that the rooms have been returned to a good standard, it's a great place to stay if you want a downtown location.

“Good Hotel in Downtown Denver” Admittedly, the Grand Hyatt was not our first choice of properties for our second visit to Denver. However, because of a very good room rate we decided to give it a try. We ended up quite pleased with the level of accommodations received and service provided. The hotel is conveniently located on Welton and 17th Streets, just one block from the 16th Street, so a short walk to the Mall and the free shuttle bus which we used extensively during our stay. Our room was very quiet and good sized for 3 people, clean and neat with a nice bathroom. We received excellent service from the front desk personnel, bellman, the maids and we had some great dining advice from the concierge. I especially appreciated the elevator security system which required a room key to access the guest floors. There is also a Starbucks in the office tower next door which is accessible by a covered walkway, great when the weather turns. The only quibble with the property was with the lobby area which I felt was rather sterile and underutilized. There wasn't anyplace inviting, where I felt like sitting down to relax, have coffee or drinks, read a newspaper or use my laptop. But other than that, this is a hotel I would definitely consider again when visiting Denver.

“Great Courtyard” Stayed at the Courtyard San Diego Downtown for one night on business. It is in a really neat old bank building (make sure you go down to the "safety deposit" level to see the meeting room made out of the old vault) that is just a few short steps from the Gaslamp district. The rooms are very large and comfortable with adequate space all around. I would definitly stay here again when I return to San Diego.

“First time back in 5 years.” We used to stay here quite frequently and liked the closeness to Sea World. So we planned a Labor Day to Sea World and stayed here because it's right across the highway, a great location. We arrived and were greated by old friends from the staff that were still there and still recoganized us by name, what a great feeling to be truly welcomed and cared for! We were upgraded to a presidential suite and treated like royalty, the staff went over and way above to ensure we enjoyed our stay. The resort does need an update but as of this writing a $35 million update is underway. So next season this great service will be coupled with greatly improved rooms and amenities. One new item already in place were the pool cabanas and the personnel service that goes along with them. It was a bit pricey but well worth it in the heat with children and grandchildren. Special thanks to Lindsey, Karen & Alex out at the cabanas. And to Gilbert the guest liaison rep that we have been aquented with for many years, he and all the customer service staff at the front of the house were excellent! Thank you and we can't wait to see the new and improved version next season.

“I love this hotel!” Great style and service and value. The suites are awesome and a terrfic value. Good location for business or pleasure, right off the 16th St. Pedestrian Mall and a light rail stop. The free breakfast, happy hour and late night cookies add a lot of value and warmth. I never stay anywhere else in Denver!

“The Staff Makes this Hotel Great!” I was a guest at this Aloft because I was taking a class at the Culinary Institute of America at San Antonio. I chose this hotel specifically because of the shuttle service to and from the CIA. I did not have a rental car and needed transportation. The School is probably 10 miles from the hotel. This hotel also offered a special rate for CIA students, which was also good. Also, the shuttle service is also provided to and from the San Antonio Airport. Ramses was the driver who assisted me upon my arrival. He was super professional, friendly and very timely in helping me to and from the Airport and to the CIA for my class. Upon checking in with Arnold, I stayed in a room (#410) for three nights. Arnold also assisted with areas to eat and shope close by. I like the Loft feeling of the hotel room and side bathroom area. It is a good size for one or two persons. Pamela assisted me with coordination of the Shuttle. Roger was great about picking me up from the CIA Class Saturday afternoon, super friendly and very prompt. The housekeeping staff did a great job and room was clean with plenty of towels and supplies. My only complaint would be that the trash pickup at 3 a.m. or so, is noisy and some guests arriving back from an evening out, can slam the doors quite loudly. Congratulations to the Aloft Hotel, San Antonio for a great location, superior employees such as Ramses, Roger, Arnold and Pamela!

“My favorite hotel in SF” This is our favorite hotel in SF, and we have stayed in at least a dozen. Maybe you have to be a frequent visitor to appreciate the luxury and history of the location on top of Nob Hill. I especially love the marble bathrooms and the elegant sophisticated room decor, as well as the magnificant hotel facade on a clear day with the brilliant CA sun and blue sky backdrop. The Top of the Mark is great for a nightcap or afternoon cocktail. Grace Cathedral with its magnificant choir and labyrinths is across the street.

“Good, but not what I had expected” I was very surprised when I discovered I had to pay $14 a day for internet access in my room. I think free internet access is the least you can expect from a Hilton hotel these days! The room was nice, newly re-decorated and very inviting. However, the walls were paper thin, and I woke up early because of the noise the children in the next room made. When we had closed the door to our room, we could still hear people talking outside fairly clearly because of a 2 cm opening under the door itself. The staff was really nice, especially José at the concierge desk. The breakfast was awesome as well, it provided a full choice of healthy alternatives, as well as the more indulgent ones.

“Great Service. Excellent room and decor.” The service was professional and excellent at all times. Great rooms and decor. All the touches you expect from a 5 star hotel. Nice location in the District. Really liked the free garment pressing service. My suit was wrinkled from the plane. This was a life saver!

“Great Hotel. Perfect Location” Great Hotel. Everything you need. Close to all the Theaters and Times Square (only a 2 minute walk!). Very clean. Room was made uo every day with fresh towels etc. Friendly staff. Great bar on corner called "Social" if you are a sports fan! Food great there too. Highly reccommend!

“Couldn't really ask for more.” I got this hotel room on Priceline for 45 dollars, so no matter what I felt as if I was getting a great deal. I still went in with high expectations though, and I felt they delivered. The pros: - EXCELLENT location. This is basically near anything downtown you're going to want to see...Monument Circle and Circle Centre mall are right there, and Conseco Fieldhouse isn't far away. - Very quiet hotel. Walls and floors are very solid...should have no issue sleeping. - Very courteous staff. I was standing around for 15 seconds trying to figure out where to check in, when somebody came up to me very politely and directed me to a very friendly person who checked me in. They were very accomodating. - Definitely up to standards as far as cleanliness goes. Cons: - The only thing I can think of is that I thought the room may be a bit bigger. It seemed about as big as a Motel 6 type place...but it isn't anything that upset me. I'd definitely recommend it, but try getting it on Priceline.

“Great Getaway Weekend” My husband and I stayed at Jury's from 11/18 to 11/20 to celebrate our first wedding anniversary. We only live about fifteen miles away from the hotel but wanted a "getaway" experience. I booked the hotel based on these reviews and I was not disappointed. We traveled by the T (public transportation) and only had to walk one block from the Back Bay station. Upon check-in, we found the front desk staff to be very friendly, Actually, everyone who works at this hotel is very friendly. When we got to our room we were pleasantly suprised by chocolate covered strawberries and a bottle of champagne. Soon after, the front desk called us to make sure we were happy with our room, and we were!!! The room was an adequate size with a big, comfortable king sized bed! We loved the bed and the large bathroom with Aveda products, very impressed! The shower had great water pressure and we liked the added heated towel rack. We went to the bar area for a late lunch/snack and were very happy with the ambience and service, We both ordered delicous mushroom soup and split an order of lightly fried calamari while watching college football on their two flat screen televisions. After going out for dinner, we returned to a very crowded bar scene but we lucked out and were able to get two seats at the bar. Some people have criticized the crowd but we found it to be very electic. The next day we wanted to stay in bed and enjoy the Patriots so we ordered room service which was very good (same food as bar and same price) The room had a good sized flat screen tv and a mini cd stereo system. We also liked the mini-fridge b/c we could put some of our leftovers in it! That night we were meeting friends to go see a show at the Coloniel Theatre and we could easily walk there. Actually, you could easily walk to a lot of places from the hotel. We were both very happy with our choice to stay at Jury's. The next time we want to play tourist in our own city, we would not hesitate to return to Jury's and we would make sure we eat at their restaurant (we will actually be back next time we are in that area) If you are a tourist, not only is the hotel beautiful and clean, AND the staff very friendly, it has a GREAT location. Highly recommended!!!!!

“Nice hotel with huge pool” The hotel looks like it has been recently been redone. Rooms are modern and clean. Beds are comfy. Bathrooms well appointed. (They are small, since it looks to have been an older hotel built before gigantic bathrooms were in vogue.) There is a lot of street noise though. The windows are not very sound proof and a couple sides border a busy street with sirens blaring all night. Staff are extremely friendly. The best part of the hotel is the pool. It is huge. At least 3 times the size of a normal Courtyard pool. And warm.

“Great price-value. Very romantic.” We celebrated our 27th Anniversary at The Adolphus Hotel & The French Room restaurant. Two years ago, we had done the same at the Mansion on Turtle Creek. Over the years, we’ve been to The Mansion for lunch and dinner on several occasions, typically when family come to town, but never the French Room at the Adolphus. Well, let me say that our dinner and guest room accommodations were superb. Upon check-in, the front desk clerk asked if we would like to upgrade our $199 deluxe room to a junior suite for an additional $34.50, so we did. For $234, we thought our Junior Suite accommodations offered great price-value (see my pics). The hotel is beautiful with its dark wood paneling, antique furniture and accents. This is a very romantic destination. Our dinner at the French Room was also terrific. We met chef Jason Weaver and Sommelier Gregory Cheval was able to pair some great wines with our three courses. I’ve written a separate posting for the French Room, along with additional pictures. For three courses, paired with wines, our dinner for two, before gratuity, was $260. The following morning, we had breakfast in The Bistro. The service was snappy, and our breakfast was hot and tasty. We highly recommend the Adolphus Hotel and the French Room for a romantic evening.

“Small but comfortable room with great service and location” We stayed in a standard double for three nights at the end of May, getting a fantastic "name your price" deal through Priceline. Though the room was small -- often mentioned by other reviewers -- it was by no means too small for two people; and we found it to be larger than many where we have stayed in Europe and in New York City. The double bed was comfortable and the room spotless and well appointed with new fixtures. Our 12th-floor location gave us a very distant view of the Boston Harbor. We appreciated the fast elevators, which always seemed to get to us within a few seconds of pushing the button. The room's big drawback was the air conditioner. We found it impossible to adjust to our liking and thus we were either too cold or too warm. The windows couldn't be opened. The hotel's location by the Freedom Trail was perfect to enjoy Boston's history -- near Beacon Hill, the statehouse, Faneuuil Hall Marketplace, Boston Common, etc. There are many restaurants in the area and many places to find a reasonably priced breakfast. All staff stood ready to provide excellent service with a smile, and the concierge service was absolutely phenomenal, far exceeding our expectations.

“Capital DUMP, Nasty- Worst place I have ever stayed at” Let me first start off by saying- It was Spring Break and this was the only hotel around with availability (I now know why). We checked into our hotel late, 9:30 and it took my husband 20 minutes inside before he came back to the car. We get to our room and there was one bed made up and the other had no linens on it at all, my 7 year old said- aren't they supposed to make the beds? Not only that but there were no towels and the bathroom had not been cleaned, Ewwww.. At this point I was on the phone praying someone had cancelled a room at any other hotel but had no luck. My husband called down and they said that Spring Break was so busy and they couldn't keep up but they would send someone up to clean the room. I sat there and watched her clean the bathroom, make the beds and clean the room. The noise level outside was loud, you could hear everyone outside and everyone outside could pretty much see inside. We got up first thing, checked out went to see their mini hot breakfast- not sure where the hot comes into play unless you are toasting bread- they had stale bread and bagels, fruit loops, cheerios, apples, oranges and that's about it. Unless you are in a dire situation I would avoid this place! I will NEVER stay at another Howard Johnson after this experience.

“Lives Up to the Hype!” We stayed at the Palomar DC for four nights recently and were very impressed. The staff was genuinely warm and helpful. When we arrived we were upgraded to a huge room. (Be sure to be a Kimpton member--free WiFi and raid the minibar up to $10.) We were looking over P Street, but never heard any traffic. Everything in the room was very comfortable--bed, sheets, easy chair, ergonomic desk chair, robes. We also liked the breakfast buffet (we had a $1 breakfast deal). Everything on it was very fresh and there were enough healthy options. (Don't sit near the outside door on that end of the restaurant, as there is a cold draft.) The hotel's location cannot be beat. We had wonderful, reasonably priced food every night right nearby. (Great Thai, Japanese and French.) Transportation is right outside. The place runs like a well-oiled machine, only nicer!

“GREAT Value & Location” This was our 2nd stay at the Best Western Bayside Inn and we would definitely stay here again. We chose this hotel for the great value + location. Little Italy and Harbor Drive are a few short blocks away. The America Plaza & Santa Fe trolley stops are in easy walking distance. We used the public transportation system exclusively on this trip and found stops close by and the system easy to navigate. Staff was very friendly and helpful in answering any questions we had.

“Historic Hotel with Great Location” Spent a couple of nights as part of a longer trip to the DC area, great loation for sightseeing and peple watching. Rooms were nice and spacious with traditional decor. Be careful with mini bar as they charge for for just moving an item in it. Did not sue the restaurants for anything except breakfast. Would stay here again if I had the chance.

“Great Location and Clean” Stayed at Holiday Inn Fisherman's Wharf Thursday October 2 and Friday October 3 2008. Arrived early and checked in immediately. They had a room ready., I had been told about the possibility of getting a room in the Beach building across the street and down the block. I was a little dissapointed when she told us we were in that building, but we did not ask to change it, as the main building were smoking rooms, Ours were nonsmoking. They offered to take our luggage over, but it was really just a short walk. We went to our room and were very satisfied. We loved the free wireless internet. We were only at this location for 2 nights, and we did get a ground floor room. There was a little street noise, I would recommend asking for a higher room if this would bother you. The desk at our building was open almost all the time and the employees were very helpful. We had to fax some papers for our balloon ride and something was not working. She tried and tried. She would not give up, even called the company and finally got the papers faxed. We did not eat in the restaurant in the hotel, because we have a strict rule for not going to any type of chain restaurant while visiting other cities,. The location was perfect to visit the Fisherman's Wharf area. There is a most wonderful (5 stars out of 5) restaurant just down the block called Beach Street Grill. I highly recommend eating there for breakfast. We both had excellent food, outstanding friendly service and great Momosa's. If I were to stay near Fishermans Wharf again, I would definately look into this place again.

“Convenience was the only positive” Stayed at the Colonnade for a business meeting at Hopkins for a few days. The location of the hotel was realistically the only redeeming feature. The decor of hotel was dull, dated and uninspiring. Not only did the plug in bathroom not work when I wanted a bath, but the bath didn't drain when the plug was out! I've lived in the US for 10 years, and the restaurant served quite possibly the worst ribs I've ever had - and they were ordered on the recommendation from the bar maid! The wait staff was surly, unintelligible and not that useful. Be prepared to seat yourself for a limited breakfast selection - though the breakfast wait staff were really friendly and should be commended. I think I've worked out where all the old cathode ray tube televisions have been placed...

“Standard Fairfield” This hotel does not differ greatly from other Fairfields at which I have stayed. The room was quite sizable. Everything was in working order. Strong wifi. Very weak shower pressure, unfortunately, but otherwise a good stay and a good value. The shuttle runs every twenty minutes in the morning. No restaurant, and very limited options within walking distance -- Village Inn, Ruby Tuesday, and the restaurant inside the Courtyard.

“Good Marriott Experience, but small room” Stayed at the Marriott Union Square on business a couple of weeks ago. It was my first visit to this property. Not my favorite Marriott property, but definitely up to standard. Checkin Fast and efficient. Staff was friendly and helpful. Room Got what had to be their standard room -- but it felt REALLY small. You couldn't open the closet door and the door to the room at the same time. Bathroom was so small that the sink / vanity was less than 18 inches wide. Just very crowded. Room was clean and bed was comfy. Concierge Lounge Lounge was really nice at this property. Breakfast was great -- eggs, pastries, fruit, and hot / cold cereals. The Chocolate mini muffinsare great! Staff was friendly, and lounge was decently sized. Never made in for appetizers, but desserts were also nice -- there were a variety of items available. Room Service Quick and tasty --- although at standard room service rates. Their clam chowder is to die for and the cheese platter makes a great compliment! Overall --- nice business hotel.

“Great Deal” Stayed a week on our first vacation to NYC. Priceline bid of around $100 a night for a double/double room worked well. Ask for a corner room as those are the biggest on each floor. The Executive Lounge is a good idea espeically if you have a family with you.... good deal for breakfast and snacks in the evening. I would recommend it for anyone staying on the cheap and wanting something downtown.

“A bit over the top in decor, but great service and amenities” My family and I stayed four nights in this hotel. As a local suggested..it feels as if a Las Vegas hotel got dropped in north SD. Not a lot right there, so really meant as a full service resort and that succeeds. A bit of a rabbit warren and gaudy Italianate designs. Other than that, the service was outstanding. From the valet, to the front desk, to the restaurants, to room service and housekeeping...we could not have asked for more. Really like the service, but the location is just OK. I have to admit that I like the ocean when in SD, or some other services/character around me.
“Nice hotel, great location” Nice hotel, updated rooms, great location. Within walking distance to restuaurants, shops, and the convention center. Overall a great value.

“A business trip that felt like vacation” This is a stunningly beautiful hotel in a wonderful location. I was there for a meeting and the service by the banquet and conference staff was excellent. My room was lovely with great amenities (except an iron) and the latest conveniences for the traveler with multiple mobile devices. The bar is very busy (I guess people in Baltimore get off at 4:30??) but if you can snag a sofa - it's a great, lively place for a drink. Service was excellent. The concierge arranged to have a rental car delivered to the hotel for me. Every request was answered with a smile and wonderful service. I hope I get to go back soon!

“Not recommended for women traveling alone.” I frequently travel to NYC -- and there are very few areas of the city that I do not feel safe in. While the hotel is good with great views form the Club Level and a fun vibe, I would did not feel comfortable with the neighborhood. When I was dropped off by the cab -- and asked him if it was safe to walk around, he hesitated and said, "it's ok". You know that hesitation of not wanting to say something bad. I then got a call from my boss who was in the cab with me when I got dropped off that said, "you definitely should not walk around this neighborhood by yourself." She is a lifelong New Yorker, so I trust her judgement.

“In the middle of it all” The hotel is a bit on the pricey side, be prepared for the 53 dollar valet/parking costs, but when you think of the service that you will receive the second you pull up, it def. makes up for it. All of the staff went out of their way to make sure you had everything you needed from the second that you check in. The hotel is beautiful. They've maintained alot of the architecture that you will see in the pool area and its really makes it a sight to see. But again, everything does come at a cost. Be aware to use the fitness area it is another 16 or so dollars a day. So make sure to understand the fine print. As well as wi-fi...but with wi fi bein such a necessity now a days, it wouldve been nice to have that at least be included. They do have spa type services available that they do not advertise too well, but they do have massages available. We did take advantage of that. The downside of it, was it was in this small room that they had to keep the door open. You could hear all of the noise of the pool area and feel the draft. They do not provide any warm tables, or even warm neck pads or anything with the massage at least to warm the guests up while they are on the table. For the price of the massage, I have to admit I expected ALOT MORE. We did take advantage of room service. It came very quick, and it was tasty. But again, your best bet is to get lunch. You can get a lunch plate for under 20 dollars, breakfast will cost you 30 for a basic breakfast. Location, Location, Location, can not be beat. Its in walking distance to all the great spots and the chocolate wine bar in the hotel was a nice place to be at as well for a nightcap. Visit the PURPLE PIG if you have a chance. I kept hearing so many great things about it but did not realize it was across the street. It is worth the hype.

“Lovely 5 star experience” We stayed here for one night in February and found it to be a lovely experience. There was a line to check in when we arrived early on a Saturday evening, but another staff member quickly arrive to assist and reduce then wait. The check in process was smooth and our room type requests were honored. Staff was friendly and professional. The rooms are quite beautiful. I have stayed at numerous other Denver area Marriott properties but this was our first time at the JW in Denver. The rooms at the JW are a step above the rest (although the Boulder Marriott remains my favorite in the Denver area for its charm and warm quaint atmosphere). The rooms have large bathrooms with bathtubs and separate showers and finer quality toiletry products. The bedroom space is well appointed and very spacious with high quality bedding. The coffee service in the room was well stocked. The glassware in the minibar area was of high quality. Good quality robes were provided and plenty of hangers and closet space. Service in the concierge lounge was exceptional. Very attentive with a wide variety of appetizers, alcoholic and non alcoholic beverages and a nice variety of breakfast buffet items and a great view of the mountains.
