The service level of the hotel was exceptional. We had a minor issue we addressed with the staff which was resolved promptly. There is a nice work out room and a jacuzzi area. We didn't eat at the restaurant or order room service so cannot comment on that aspect of the hotel. I definitely plan to return. Broder

“Wonderful” I paid $20 for 2 rooms in an auction and really enjoyed our stay. We stayed the night before a flight out of DFW. They allow you to park your vehicle there while you are gone and have a shuttle to take you to and from the airport. The shuttle was nice / efficient. The rooms were VERY nice. We requested adjoining rooms and got a room with a king and the other 2 doubles. The bedding was wonderful. They have a resturant onsite - which we ate at that night but they were very slow and the food wasn't very good and they weren't busy. After waiting over 45 minutes for our food it was cold. I do not recommend the resturant. There are a couple places nearby to eat. They have 2 computers in the business center with internet access and printers. They have a pool also but we didn't have time to enjoy it.

“Very strange hotel” I am so torn about this place because it was so bizarre, but I can tell you that the bad outweighs the good. I arrived late in the evening, tired, and was ignored for a while even though 2 ladies stood at the counter 2 feet from me having a conversation. When 1 of them finally looked up and addressed me, she was aloof and borderline rude. She got us checked in and after a series of questions I finally had the vital info you need when ckg in to a hotel, which basically was: no free breakfast, no pool, but there is a restaurant on site. Great! I'm hungry. Well, sorry, but we're closed, and even though the counter of the restaurant was 15 feet away and the case was packed with granola, muffins, and other snacks, she would not open it and give us a little something to eat. Hmmm... bad first impression. However, the outside architecture was really nice and the lobby was a colorful, chic boutique-looking place that was light, airy and happy, so I was hopeful. Went up to the room and one key didn't work but thankfully the second did. No big deal. Opened the door and was confused. As you walk in, to the left, is a "kitchen" looking place with a 10' X 10' kitchen area with counters and cabinets on 3 sides, but there is no kitchen stuff except for your typical mini-fridge and a miniature coffee pot. Looking to the right of the hotel room is a desk, lamp and free internet. Cool. Straight ahead is a couch, a foot stool, a lounge chair and TV which make up a living room. Not plush and not overly comfortable, but a separate room from the bedroom, bath and "kitchen", so thats cool. Then you walk on thru and there is a bedroom with an on-suite bathroom. The bedroom is what I would consider perfect, with the exception of the old TV. The bed is to die for, as is the bedding. The bathroom was cute and it had Aveda products, so that's definitely a bonus. The drawback to the bathroom -- the shower is unacceptable. It is only a shower, and the shower head is insufficient. Also, there is only one door and it is stationary, so it does not contain the water sufficiently from the shower. (my guess is that's why the shower head is purposely limited). There is ALOT of wasted space in the room, and in the hotel for that matter, and my family members and I couldn't help ourselves from spending the next few days visually gutting the room and rehabbing it to maximize the amazing amount of space. That was fun and kept us entertained! lol.. Anyhow, will I be back. No. The nail in the coffin was food that I ordered the following night from the restaurant was inedible - greasy, nasty, low-quality garbage. And it was very high priced garbage I might add. I really just wanted to take it back and say thanks, but no thanks, but by then I had decided I was done with the Hotel Indigo and it wasn't worth dealing with the folks at the front desk or the restaurant any further. I must admit, however, that if you are in Houston to shop til you drop at the Galleria, you can't beat the location without paying the really big bucks at the Westin. And the rooms were indeed quiet and spacious.

“super Preis- Leistungs-Verhältnis” Wer ein zentral gelegenes Hotel zu einem bezahlbaren Preis in New York sucht, wird hier fündig. In der Upper East Side gelegen, nicht weit vom großen Geschehen (Manhattan, Broadway, Central Park...) befindet sich das Ramada Eastside. Ein tolles Hotel, das für knapp 100 Dollar plus Tax für diese Lage absolut erschwinglich ist. Die Ramada Gruppe zählt ohnehin zu den nicht zu verachtenden Hotelketten, insofern ist man auch in diesem Hause gut aufgehoben. Auf Wunsch erhält man einen Kühlschrank für das durchaus großzügig geschnittene Zimmer. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich, das Badezimmer gepflegt und sauber, nur das Frühstück würde ich nicht empfehlen. Fußläufig sind alle großen Sehenswürdigkeiten erreichbar, wenn man mit gutem Schuhwerk und Stadtplan ausgestattet ist, steht einem Erkundungstrip durch New York City nichts mehr im Wege. Ich kann das Ramada Eastside nur empfehlen.

“Love it!!!” This is a great hotel. The rooms are big, the service is exquisite. The breakfast is great (but not included). If you go in summertime make sure you always wear a jacket in the Lobby because the A/C is very cold!

“US Grant is a great LC Starwoods property” Recently had a two night stay at the Grant. Booked a standard room and was upgraded to Deluxe corner room four days prior to arrival on SPG.com. Location was great and easy to get to from airport. Arrival was nice, great entrance and employees. Check-in was fast and efficient, no line! Was on 7th floor. Got a great running map from front desk on a small laminated (around 3 by 5) card. One route took you 3 miles and another 5 (to the sand and some sights). TV had no HD channels to speak of. Work out room was on the small side but adequate, free water and fruit. Grant Grill was nice place to people watch and have a drink. Two drinks and dessert set me back 45...Wife asked for blue cheese stuffed olives and they didnt even blink! In fact the employee said she made some fresh ones earlier in the morning!!...pricey, but had fun! Great pictures all over this hotel of Grant and other iconic figures. My wife and I will be back.

“beautiful and comfotable” As a Hilton HHonors member, I had earned several bonus nights due to travel for business this year. We stayed here on our way to a conference in Pittsburgh. The hotel is beautiful, spacious and elegant. Our room had a king size bed and a large bathroom. Bed was comfortable. Hotel is very close to shopping, dining and a movie theatre. Internet is free only in the lobby -- Gold level members will begin to get it free as of 9-1-10. Lounge on the club level was nice-- pleasant attendants and nice amenities. Cheese, crackers and hot wings, along with soft drinks and liquor were available in the evening. Fresh fruit, bagels, pastries and scrambled eggs were available for breakfast. Overall, a very nice hotel, but would never have paid te $249 rack rate for this property.

“Extrordinary Hotel” The Trump Hotel Chicago is amazing! Our room was more like an elegant condominium rather than a hotel room. The fully equipped kitchenette was a nice touch. The health club is out of this world with high-end equipment. For some reason, cell phone service was very poor in this building...many of my collegues had the same issue. This is THE hotel to stay in when visiting Chicago.

“Terrible experience. Will never never go back.” My room was completely filled with COCKROACHES at night. I had a balcony room and they came in through the french doors leading outside as well as from the room next door through the conjoining door. I called the front desk and their only solution was to just send a staff member with a vacuum!!!!! Eventually I was able to transfer to a new room but the manager at the time made it seem like a chore. The next morning (when checking out early), I asked to not pay for the room in good faith for the experience and a different manager said the best they could do was take $100 off of my two night bill. This is the first 1 star review I have ever given and I don't take it lightly. I did so not just because of the experience but because until really pressed, the staff seemed like they could care less. Bugs happen unfortunately but a hotel can change the way they deal with these situations. Beautiful hotel but I will never stay there again.

“Predictable, reliable Intercontinental!” In the city only one night to rendezvous with friends from abroad. The IC SF is well-located in SOMA, within walking distance to just about everything downtown (SOMA is not to everyone's taste, having been a "transitional" area for the last 30+ years). I've paid to be a Gold Ambassador, so got upgraded to a spacious corner room on the 22nd floor with outstanding city views to the north and west, and removal of that awful, overpriced internet nuisance fee. Checked for bedbugs on arriving in the room (previous reports in this property) and there was no sign of them. The bed was extremely comfortable. Slept quite well. Loved the floor-to-ceiling windows in the bathroom in the morning! The Keurig coffee is always welcome, too. The layout and amenities were exactly as I've come to expect in IC hotels. Predictable but reliable!

“Not so hot” We did get an okay price for this hotel ($100/nt.) on Priceline. Parking was $30 a night, and the staff always had their hands out for tips. When we arrived in our room (the only "update" was a flat screen TV), there was a fridge still full of someone else's food, and items remained in the drawers. When we called staff, they did take care of it right away, but with zero apologies or compensation (drink coupon???/coffee coupon???). The mirrored wall in the bathroom had a large crack in it. The lobby was very nice with an open bar area and lots of seating. We didn't use the pool area at all. The view was excellent, and it was very quiet. The beds were very comfy. Upon check-out, the desk attendant didn't inquire about our stay, say thank you or good-bye (and I had a pleasant enough look on my face). I'd sooner stay someplace with a bit more personality and not so much stuffiness.

“Very relaxing” The downtown El Paso Doubletree is a very comfy hotel. The beds are perfect! The service is always great. I do wish that they had a nice coffee lounge but I don't think any Doubletrees do. The parking is self parking in the parking garage which is very convenient. The rooms are very clean. Next time I will try to remember to hang a 'do not disturb' sign on the door the night before because housekeeping will wake you up at the but crack of dawn if you forget. Other than the lack of a coffee lounge and the early housekeeping annoyance this is a great place to stay.

“Nice place, friendly staff” We stayed a few days in the Mark Hopkins and liked this old, prestigious building. The lobby is surprisingly small and you sort of would expect a bar down there. Standard room is good, some people may find the sounds of the cable tram outside annoying (we liked this 'couleur locale') and HD TV would have been nice for that big LCD screen. Staff very friendly: great people outside, excellent concierge, efficient reception desk, very helpful cleaning staff, etc. Breakfast on the 18th floor is ridiculously expensive, but hey: you can't beat the view and the quality is good.

“Value!!” For $109 a night, I feel the Beacon Hotel did just fine. The good: Comfortable king bed; huge room with seating area and several chairs; flat screen TV; lots of windows (that actually open a bit) and a view that includes some greenery; clean; bathroom with 2 sinks and tons of space; a great location near Dupont Circle. The mediocre: the sheets, while fine, are not top of the line; the love seat in the room looked a little ratty; some confusion with the staff about the hours of the Sky Bar; no mini fridge in the room. The bad: well, I can't really think of anything bad! Is this place perfect? Not by a long shot, but I don't expect perfection for $109 a night. If I had paid Hay Adams prices, I would have expected (and demanded) a lot more. For what I paid, I appreciated a cool, spacious, comfortable place to sleep 2 nights. Oh- the bar downstairs makes some good cocktails and appetizers, too.

“Very Average Hotel In Crime Ridden Area” Rooms were okay, free wifi, the restaurant was a little overpriced. The main thing for travelers to Los Angeles, dont stay near the airport if you can help it. Century Blvd and La Cienega is known for the homeless, prostitution, and overall crime. Try to stay at least 5 miles from there in the cities of Manhattan Beach, Redodno Beach, and Torrance near the Del Amo Mall.

“Location Location Location” The hotel was beautiful and except for a grumpy breakfast staff the second day (not the first; they were great) the employees were all cheerful and helpful. Good breakfast that was included in the room and the room itself was LARGE with terrific views. My favorite part was the location and ability to take great long safe walks. Go down to 13th and hang a left. Lots of great shops and restaurants. Will DEFINITELY return.

“Nicely Remodeled - Great Value” We stayed at this location to be close to a sporting event with a very early start. The location was easily found by my GPS and the hotel in a commercial / residential area on I-10 but set back a bit, so does we did not experience freeway or other surrounding noise inside the hotel. There is plenty of parking near the hotel. Check in was quick and easy. There is a nicely decorated, moderate sized inviting lobby with a small front desk and nicely appointed common area. (Breakfast area) They have coffee and tea available 24 hours a day. The hotel has a small guest laundry. (Coin operated) as well as a small gym with few pieces of cardio equipment, weight equipment, etc. There is outdoor pool and sunning area. They have a nice business center with two computers and a printer/scanner. The hotel has free internet access for guests and we found it to be speedy for hotel service. The rooms are nicely decorated roomy, and appear to be recently remodeled. The beds are typical Hampton Cloud 9 (nice beds) but have old 27" CRT TV's, but plenty of channels. The climate control works well and you can leave the blower motor on for white noise while the climate control is still functioning. Bathrooms are well equipped with plenty of storage space but a tiny amount of counter space. Our room had a microwave and fridge. The room was quiet and had no noise from outdoors. The area has many types of dining options nearby. (IHOP next door) The breakfast area had plenty of seating in the morning and they were even accommodating enough to start breakfast at 5am due to the early sporting event starting nearby. Typical Hampton breakfast. The day we stayed it was omlettes, sausage, biscuits, pastries, cereal, juices, coffee, etc. They did not have the "on the run bags: with an apple, muffin, cereal bar, water, and mints as it was the weekend but they do have these available on weekdays. Checkout was easy. We would absolutely recommend this location and would stay here again if we needed to stay in the area. The staff was always very friendly and always asked if we needed anything. Room rate was very reasonable given the area. Given the mixed review's I was unsure what to expect but was very happy with this location.

“Slept very well” This is a good hotel if you have things to do around the San Antonio airport area. The room rates are very good. One note..jets do fly over this hotel in the morning and at night. The pool is nice but the hot tub needs some serious cleaning. We slept very well and will probably stay here again.

“Hotel Room is a Pampered Destination” We planned a quick weekend getaway into NYC within less than 7 days of the trip. We just needed a clean room that was affordable, received good ratings on TripAdvisor, and relatively close to our destination (NBC Studios). Affinia 50 became our pampered destination versus a standard hotel room. Signed up on the hotel website to get offers and discounts. Called the hotel to ask about the room type and was greeted by my name because of my profile on the hotel website. That was a great 1st impression of the type of service the hotel demonstrates. Upon getting to our room, we were given a complimentary chilled bottle of champagne with 2 flute glasses. Not sure if it was being a part of the hotel website, but we definitely enjoyed it! Asked the concierge for breakfast recommendations on Sunday after 12pm. We were given a great restaurant Morning Star Cafe which was 2 blocks away. Rome, the bellman was excellent! He greeted us warmly upon checkout and took our luggage into storage. We notified him of valuables. He made a note of fragile care and told us his when his shift ended for us to feel secure he was watching our luggage. All personal care and touches that made our stay a destination and not a hotel. We wished we could have stayed longer to see the Sunday Movie Night in the lounge with free refreshments and drinks.

“Time has not been kind to the Mansion at Judges' Hill” I really wanted to like this place, with its fussy old-ladyish rooms and its throwback atmosphere. But instead I felt encroached upon by the neighborhood that has grown up around it--it sits on a busy, boring road and is surrounded by charmless businesses. (Nearby roadwork, although clearly temporary, did not help.) If you need to be near UT this is probably a decent choice, but on my next trip to Austin I'll look elsewhere.

“A little small for my tastes” I'm usually a diehard chain guy, but with the last minute timing and travel costs for a meeting I decided to book on Hotwire. This hotel fell under a "4 star" classification which I would consider a tad high for this property and interesting enough the pricing was identical to what I could have reserved directly with the hotel or on their website. Good Upper West side area with lots of options close by. Typical apartment - boutique hotel conversion where the rooms are smaller than your average NYC hotel and the bathrooms are very small. Staff was very friendly but the perfumed smell in the lobby area was brutal compared to other hotels. I had a headache every time I walked through or sat in the area and that alone would have me going elsewhere on my return trips.

“Let down by old style public areas” We stayed here for a conference taking place at the Grand Hyatt, but the Grand had no rooms, and the location of this Hyatt on the River Walk appealed. However, this hotel seems to date from the 60's with a concrete atrium making it look very dated. We had upgraded to a room with a city view, which is important, as a lot of the rooms look into the atrium, and we were upgraded again to a river view as they had no room ready for us at 3:30pm. It was a reasonable size, with floor to ceiling windows and a nice view of the river. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom a decent size, but the overall look was a bit gloomy and dark. Other things we weren't keen on included: there was a connecting door to the next room, which meant we could hear normal levels of conversation from that room; the air conditioning seemed only to be on or off, with no temperature control; bizarrely, the hairdryer was on a short lead of only about 8 inches, which made it very difficult to use; and there was no small mirror in the bathroom. The restaurant was closed in the evening most of the time we were there, which isn't a problem as there are loads of places to eat on the River Walk, but it did serve excellent buffet breakfasts.

“not a typical Hilton” This isnt a typical Hilton. The rooms are very old and not too comfortable. The hotel itself is in need of some updating. I was on the top floor and had a queen bed room. My bathroom was very small, and the shower/tub was one of the smallest I've been in. I hit my head on the towel rack inside the shower, twice. The a/c was also pretty loud and I could hear the "water pump" room across the hall whining all night. The location is near the airport, on harbor island, but if your set on the local, try the Sheraton down the road which is a lot nicer. For a Hilton, this isnt a very good example.

“Service, location, hotel, food -- all great!” We had a marvelous stay at the Hilton Financial District. Check-in was fast & friendly. As a Hilton Reward member, we received coupons for free continental breakfast for both mornings & coupons for other freebies and/or discounts at the hotel. The lobby is very spacious and welcoming with two complimentary computers with Internet access. In the morning they had a coffee bar and in the afternoon and evening there was a bar for adult drinks. Our room was amazing with a great view! The room looked newly decorated and was immaculate. We had two comfortable queen-sized beds with lots of types of pillows. The bathroom was quite large with a full range of amenities. Free Internet access was included with our stay, but I'm not sure if this was one of the perks for being a Hilton Reward member. The room had a built-in desk which was quite large to put all our stuff on. We found the Financial District a very good location for our vacation. We were within walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, China Town, Cable Car Museum and the cable cars. We walked most of our trip and this was with two children, 8 & 10 years old. My only complaint about the area was that it was somewhat loud at night, but I'm guessing it's loud almost everywhere in the city. I'd recommend asking for a high floor to get away from the street noise. We parked in the underground parking area and I think it was $30.00 a day. One thing that stands out in my mind was the exceptional service we had. The receptionist went out of her way to help us get something printed for our trip. We also found the people who worked at the breakfast buffet to be very helpful and courteous. All-in-all it was a great stay and I would definitely stay there again. I found it a true bargain for San Francisco.

“Avoid in the near future” I would avoid this property. I checked in very late in the evening (i.e. >2AM) and requested a quiet room. The desk person said that all the rooms would be quiet because everyone was asleep by this time. However, what the desk person did not say was that floors 5 and 6 in the hotel were under renovation that begins at 9AM every single day (including Saturday and Sundays). So I was woken up by loud hammering and drilling literally above my room. I may have been a little more understandable if I didn't request a quiet room to start due to a late check in, but the desk person was too lazy to insure that my request was fulfilled. The room itself was pretty spacious. The TV was an older tube model. The walls were pretty thin (I could hear the next door neighbor coughing). Also, there was a damp smell (moldy) in the room. Not sure where the smell was coming from as the room looked pretty clean otherwise. The property itself is situated in what looks to be an industrial office complex. Parking is free.

“Fantastic stay!” Found this hotel shortly after they opened because my regular hotel in New York, the W, was booked. It has become the only hotel I stay at when I visit the city. The staff has always been helpful and very friendly. Having a great market a few steps away comes in handy. A couple of Duane Reads within walking distance was extremely helpful when my niece became ill. We were able to get to all of our destinations easily. I love this hotel and now my friends and family love it to. The rooms are extremely clean and the beds are so comfortable it is very difficult to leave the bed. The free breakfast is great!
“Exceeded Expectations” Stayed here for work after getting a deal on Hotwire. Location, service, facilities far exceeded my expectations given the price.

“Nice Boutique Hotel in Great Location” I like it! From a strict starring perspective, the hotel is probably a 3.5. This is an old building that has been "funkified" with an urban interpretation of East Coast seaside-cottage decor. Just like a coastal cottage it is slightly worn, but fun, fresh, and casually quirky. Nice, not luxurious. My room was small, but charming. The bed was extremely comfortable...which made for a great nights sleep. The location is what seals the deal!! The hotel is in the middle of a quiet, classy, tree-lined residential brownstone neighborhood. It is about a block away from several restaurants, coffee shops, and drug stores. The lake shore (beach park) is four blocks away (an easy five minute walk). There are also several health clubs within walking distance. All the benefits of downtown, with the serenity of the burbs...thumbs up!

“Good Place to Stay in City Center” I stayed at this location for a work conference, and have nothing but good things to say about the hotel and staff. We arrived early and the room we had asked for was not ready. The front desk clerk apologized and upgraded us to a nice corner room overlooking the historic city hall. Every staff member we met and spoke to were friendly and helpful. The location in the city center was close to many restaurants and historical sites. The museum area was about a mile away and we walked it with ease. The room was clean and comfortable, and the hotel provides turn down service each night. There is a charge for Internet ($9.99 for a 24 hour period) and worked very well. The gym was a little small, but the do offer the use of an off site workout area if needed. The floor we were on (11th) did pick up a little street noise, but wasn't too bad. I would recommend this hotel when in Philadelphia.

“Location best asset” Pros: located centrally to Mag Mile, Navy Pier, Millineum Park, Loop; boutique type hotel with large rooms well furnished. Cons: for those with children did not have a pool or breakfast.

“Nice Property. Great Location. $35 a Day Parking?!?” I always feel a little taken by hotels that offer competitive rooms rates and then stick you with outrageous add-ons like overpriced room service, parking etc. In this well run property, the only add-on of note is the $35 a day parking fee which seems ridiculous. Beyond that, the staff is excellent, the room service menu abundant, creative and well-priced and the breakfast buffet perfect. My room had a little post-convention (ComicCon) mustiness that cleared up after a day with windows open and a scented candle burning. The hotel is well situtated for anything downtown, including the Gaslamp, Horton Plaza ot the Embarcadero and Seaport Village. I walked nightly until my legs ached. There is a small deli right across the street and a World Market 1/2 a block away for more interesting snacks, wines, bottled water etc. I will stay here again as I always enjoy my visit.

“The Benjamin is Function over Luxury” While visiting New York City in January we stayed at The Benjamin. While it is a fine boutique style hotel, it does lack a true feeling of luxury. The suite we had was nicely appointed with the space well utilized. The "kitchen" is tiny and barely able to manuever in. The bedroom was nice with a decent view of the city. The pillow menu was a hit with my fellow travelers. The bathroom is fine although small. The lobby is quite small and unimpressive. The staff was helpful with the exception of one gentleman at the front desk. Overall, there are better choices for the $315 room rate. Others in my party stayed at the New York Palace for only $225 per night and I was much more impressed with their room and staff. It may be comparing apples to oranges. Depending on what you require, The Benjamin could suit your needs if you crave function over luxury.

“Great new hotel with great rooms, beds, towels and service but needs work with in room computers and food was not great” Stayed for business - good facilities for group meeting - only negative was food was not good; rooms were great-beds really comfortable with beige sheets like your own home; bathrooms were good and towels were in white and in blue of thick and absorbent towels (only caution is no bathtub but kids can be bathed easily with removable shower head)-color made it feel like home actually-only con was in room computers (new) but never worked-had to call for service everyday-hotel took care of it when I checked out but still if you're going to offer an amenity pls make it work! Service very good and friendly as well although one doorman was overtly begging for a tip when it was not warranted. It's b/w 8th and 9th so if you need to be on the west side it's great w/access to lots of food and ACE subway lines right there.

“OK but Top Ranking is a Mystery” Usually stay in the Mandarin Oriental in NYC, but tried a short stay here as a cheaper option on business, mainly because of high reviews on Tripadvisor. Thought I'd put in a review now, as I am bemused by the Library's exalted ranking. The hotel is small and cozy. Rooms are small (petite really means petite!), and nothing exceptional in terms of design and comfort, though nicely appointed. The literary theme is fun and carried through more thoroughly than similar gimmicks in hotels elsewhere eg. arthotel in Rome etc. Service was relaxed, friendly and helpful enough, again without being remarkable. Communal areas, complimentary wine and cheese, free wi-fi etc. are all nice touches. One big drawback is the breakfast - it's quite basic and, inexcusably, there simply isn't enough room. I felt sorry for the queue of people coming down for breakfast in the morning and unable to find any space to sit down. All in all nothing to write home about (for good or ill) and I am confused as to how this hotel has achieved and retains its no. 1 ranking. when you have some truly amazing hotels in new York. Confusion is heightened by the Library's sister hotels monopolizing the other top ranking spots for NYC hotels.
“Good solid 4 star hotel” Good place - nice views of the Rockies from the top floor suites. Exactly what you would expect from a good quality business hotel - doesn't disappoint.

“Great Hotel!!!” Don't understand all the complaining about how small the rooms are. Rooms are more than adequate for the price in this high priced area of Chicago. Rooms within a half block ate all in the $300+ range. Facility is clean, furniture new and comfortable. Excellent wireless internet service. If you want something bigger and fancier then go pay for it. Rooms may be smaller in the "tower" above the 20th floor.

“True - there is both good and bad here.” I stayed at this property for 8 days in March 2012. Since I flew out of town every other day, I wanted to be near the airport, and I found this hotel on a travel web site. It's a very nice place made up of several pavilions connected by elevated walkways. The main six-story pavilion faces the airport and is where most business travelers stay. I was in the "Plaza 4" pavilion at the rear of the property. First off, we had our own parking area away from the 'grab-the-best-spot-fast' lot in front of the hotel. And since unmarked police cars regularly congregated there late at night (I stared at them - they stared at me - we all went about our business) I felt perfectly safe. We got a lot a young couples who had (apparently) left the kids with the parents for the night, but I got a couple of invites to dinner at various people's homes, so that turned out *not* to be a bad thing either. I began calling our maid "Sarge" since she, by force of will, kept the place organized. If you slept past 10am, you didn't get your room serviced. But with both a microwave and a cube fridge, I didn't care. My *only* complaint is the off-and-on Wifi signal. The desk clerk said it was "interference" from both the airport and the Fort Bliss Army Base which borders the property. I only know that my phone company high-speed USB Internet device worked just fine with my laptop the two days the hotel's servers were acting badly.

“Stately but not my style” I am in NYC on business almost weekly, but this trip was pure pleasure with my wife for her birthday! She liked it, but I rather a more modern boutique hotel. The non-existant lobby, relatively stand offish staff, and the old world style furniture in the rooms left me wanting my regular hotels, but hey, she liked it! We had friends over for drinks before heading to dinner and the theater, so the suite was nice. I just think you get more for your money at other hotels.....

“Great Hotel” I stayed at this hotel for two nights last week, and thought it was first class in every respect. It reminded me a lot of the Polynesian Resort at Disney World (one of my favorite hotels). The rooms in the tower, where I was, look out onto a beautiful setting: trees, birds, flowers, miniature lakes, even a small waterfall. The room was clean, spacious, comfortable. There was a problem with my reservation and, once my travel agent faxed information, the front desk staff admitted that the mistake was theirs and promptly fixed the problem. I was quite pleased with their resolution of the problem.

“Good location, nice staff, noisy rooms, poor shower” The building is very narrow. There are about ten rooms per floor, so the minute people get off the elevator, you can hear every single word they're saying. On the plus side, most of the room are corner rooms, so you'll encounter little foot traffic. I had no trouble sleeping. My room had a very poorly designed shower (no tub). There was only a plastic strip on the floor, and the shower curtain was too short. As a result, water went all over the bathroom floor. On the plus side....very friendly staff and a convenient location. I didn't dine at their restaurant, so I can't comment. There are decent options nearby. On the corner of 26th St and 7th Ave there's a Mexican grill and also a Whole Foods a block to the left. If you turn right towards Madison Square Garden, there are plenty of places to eat. It's a 15 minute walk to Herald Square and Macy's. The hotel is between two subway stations, and it's a short ride to Times Square and the West Village.

“If you want to splurge...” What a gorgeous hotel! We love places with a story & try to stay at member hotels of the Historic Hotels of America. The Drake lives up to its reputation. From the building itself, the linens, the service, to the couch in the elevator, everything was beautiful. The hotel thankfully was up to our cleanliness standards. We've found sometimes the older hotels need to be updated, but the Drake is not one of them. The only negative was the price. Our room was almost $500 per night, including taxes. If we hadn't had a free night with our Hilton reward, we would not have stayed there. Hopefully, we'll be able to stay there again.

“"THE hotel to stay in"....especially during a hurricane!!” We stayed in this historic hotel during hurricane Irene. Check in was good, but unfortunately got mixed quotes at the reception desk on our rate extended by the historic events around "irene". All airports were closed and we were forced to stay another two nights. Rooms were large for New York, detailed, and grand. Still not sure why toilet paper holders are so far from toilet??? and plumbing and hot water "tricky"...but I expected that because of the age of the property. Concierge desk is obviously one of the best in New York, and they were knowledgeable and professional. Maid staff were the best, even with a minimum staff kept on during the weekend, because of the storm, we were completely impressed with the cleaning of the room. Location is great, and free wifi in the lobby is a real perk. Starbucks conveniently located in the hotel was THE only starbucks open during the hurricane. We got adventurous, checking out stairways and an evacuation plan, stumbled upon the Grand Ballroom, wow is all I can say!!...Just breath taking!! Have been to New York on many occasions for leisure travel, and happy to say...we hope to return to the Waldorf with my husband next time.

“Great views and a few downsides” I stayed here on the 27th floor for 3 nights. There was a lot to like about this hotel, especially the fantastic location with great views and the oversized (by New York standards) guest rooms. The room was very clean and the staff were all pleasant and helpful. I also liked that there's a Starbucks on the 1st floor--that gives a quick and relatively cheap option for breakfast or coffee. The beds were comfortable and even on St. Patrick's Day there was less street noise than I expected. The room had lots of outlets and things that are helpful for a business traveler. There are a few downsides. One is the cost, especially when you add in $16/day for internet. And the wireless internet service was spotty, which was annoying. I ended up switching to wired. The physical layout is also a bit odd. The check-in lobby is on the 8th floor, and the elevators, while fast, use a system which takes some getting used to (and which seems to confuse a lot of people at first). And of course there's none of the charm you'd get in a smaller boutique hotel.

“Great little hotel in Suburbs” I was going to a conference being held at the JW Marriott Resort but it was sold out so they suggested a few nearby hotels off of 281 & 1604. There were a number of hotels in this area and TripAdvisor suggest this as the "best" rated in the area. While it is a bit difficult to access due to road construction in area once found the hotel was great for the function. When I walked in the front staff gave me a tour of the pantry and front, was very friendly and welcoming and gave me a good room that I requested. When I got to the room it was more like a small studio suite than a hotel room, sofa sitting area, cubicle computer work area, mini-fridge micro wave and comfortable bed. Very comfortable room and hotel and more than1/2 the price of the JW resort, just not the amenities. I was able to get into the JW spa as part of our convention group so I got the best of all worlds, cheaper sleep and use of the resort. Great option in the NW San Antonio area.

“Nice, convenient, great shuttle service.” We recently stayed near Logan to catch a flight the next morning after our vacation in Maine. The Hilton couldn't be more conveniently located, and the shuttle drivers, valet manager, front desk, bell staff -- virtually everyone we encountered -- were wonderful. Nice, clean, well-appointed room with a lovely view of the harbor and the city skyline. The shuttle picked us up from Hertz Car Return, and we even took the shuttle to/from Logan Terminal C for dinner at Legal Seafood.

“Quiet hotel for exploring upper Manhattan” We stay at this hotel every time we go to NYC for a family vacation for 4 reasons: 1) location It is right across the street from the Museum of Natural History and Central Park. The Met and museum mile are a 5 minute taxi ride. 2) quiet The hotel is a little off the beaten path and in-between apartment buildings so it is very quiet versus other touristy areas. 3) awesome local food Right around the corner from the hotel are several blocks of teriffic places to eat - including Canteen 82 for great Asian food. 4) good price Since the hotel is off the beaten path, the price is hundreds less than touristy areas. For a 2 room suite with two full beds we paid $180. You may pay $10 more for a taxi to get to midtown, but well worth it.

“Very Pleasant Stay” Stayed last weekend while visiting son who goes to Northeastern. The location is terrific. Attached to the Pru Center so very convenient since we took the T several times. I got a great deal on the room, and I requested a view if possible when we checked in. It was no problem and were given a room with a beautiful view. I was looking forward to going swimming since they have an indoor/outdoor pool. The water was very cold and the air in the pool room was very chilly. The only way to get in and out of the pool was to climb up or down a ladder. There was no area with steps to just walk in. This surprised me because there was no way for mothers with little children to enter the pool easily. Despite the pool situation will happily stay there again.

“Perfect stay” I stayed there for the 4th July holiday and it was my second at this hotel. My brother and me had a lovely stay right from the beginning! We had a lovely and clean room on the 5th floor facing the front entrance. There was no problem sleeping at night, even with the little noise of the closing room doors. Breakfast was really good with a lot of choices! As it is complentary you cannot ask for more! The free wifi is perfect to check your Emails or even look for some directions! I am sure we are going to stay at this hotel the next time we'll go to NYC! For us there is no reason to stay at any other hotel in the city!

“Average” My wife and I stayed both at this hotel and the Courtyard downtown and based on just hotel quality, cleanliness, and comfort the downtown Courtyard is far superior. Location is the real wildcard. If your in the city to do the tourist thing and love the Warf this would be a great place to be and has easy access to the neighborhoods tourist venture to most (North Beach, China Town, etc). The downtown Courtyard’s neighborhood doesn’t have much going on unless you’re into clubbing but all areas of town are super easy to get to by bus from this hotel. Place like Hayes Valley, Noe Valley, Castro, and the Mission are much easier to get to then the Warf, plus super easy to get to the Warf, North beach, and Chinatown, plus downtown is cheaper all the weekends I have checked.

“So Much Potential” Several years ago my wife and I stayed at the Fairmount in San Antonio and had a wonderful stay. The room was filled with antiques but still provided the modern necessities a traveler needs. The restaurant was incredibly good and was rated one of the best in all of San Antonio. The bar provided an elegant respite and the customers were friendly and refined. On my return to San Antonio this past Spring, it was a foregone conclusion that I would stay at the Fairmount Hotel. To my disappointment, the Fairmount Hotel seems to have emulated the apparent decline of the city of San Antonio. My room, while appearing much as it did several years ago, had not been updated at all. What was once modern conveniences have now fallen into disrepair. The antiques are lovely as ever, but the rest of the room has become to look a bit shabby. The elegance of the lobby was not matched by the staff which had a type of lassez faire attitude towards service. They were nice, but very slow and somewhat unprofessional. I still think the hotel is nice, and after seeing what some of my colleagues were staying in for more money, I felt I had made a decent choice. However, there is so much potential for greatness for this establishment, that it pains me to see it fall out of five star status. The location is perfect, basically it is near everything you would want to see in San Antonio including the esteemed Riverwalk which seems to have lost some of its spark and panache over the years. Is all of San Antonio in decline? The bar had live entertainment, but it lacked the refinement and aplomb of past years. The restaurant did not seem to have been refurbished in years, and it was frighteningly empty every time I peered in. In summation, while the hotel is not bad for a decent low price, I yearn for the days when the Fairmount was the absolute elegant hotel choice in San Antonio.

“Excellent hotel for North County SD!” This hotel was in a quiet, safe, and clean suburban location, yet close to CVS, all the major banks, etc. I enjoyed the immaculately clean room, free parking, and free buffet breakfast (fresh fruit, omelet station, coffee, tea, juice, pastries galore!).

“Average Four Seasons” We stayed at the Four Seasons in Austin this past weekend. The service was perfect, Four Seasons style. The rooms were small and average with very generic bathrooms. The linens and robes were superb and the concierge, Daisy, was wonderful. She helped us with dinner plans and a day out of the city with a car and driver. It is a nice location - within walking distance of all the Austin action, but not so close that you can hear it!!! I think this is the best Austin has to offer, but just not anything like the Four Seasons NYC - or any other new property.

“Superb Value! Great Service! Perfect for Med Center travel” I have been to the Med Center several times and normaily stay at the Marriott on Fannin. This Holiday Inn is just down the street and approx 1/3 the price for much more value. The package I got included a great cooked to order or buffet breakfast and parking and the King Suite. Everything was above average and to be brief they have a new client.

“Excellent service” I read some of the comments after I did the reservation and I was kind of scare of some of them. We had 11 rooms because we run Chicago Marathon and everything turned out to be great. The hotel is very nice. The rooms are very well decorated, good space. The front desk, the bell boys, the concierge very very helpful and really nice people. Excellent attention from the staff. It is true that it is not in downtown but a cab of 14$ or the bus in front of the hotel is not difficult at all. The reception desk even sold the metro cards. Very nice detail of the hotel to have a pasta dinner the previous night and a shuttle for the runners and family to the start of the marathon.

“Adequate for a quick trip to DC” Good location for a quick trip to DC when your surroundings don't matter. Was very glad to have the free wi-fi. Stay here if you are independent and can navigate DC by yourself.

“nice place” Beautiful hotel with a really neat wine/chocolate/cheese bar adjacent. Our room was clean and quiet. We had a view of the lake which was nice. The pool was gorgeous!!! We didn't use it but we did go down to check it out and were impressed--the pool water was warm. The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because the hotel charges extra to use the workout room--I thought that was a little lame. The pool was free though. We'd stay there again but I would be disappointed if I paid a lot for the room and then couldn't workout.

“Love, Love, LOVE this hotel!” This is our second time staying at this hotel and it has not changed in the 8 years that we stayed. The rooms are beautifully appointed with tasteful decor. Clean. Great toiletries. Great location! We were able to drive everywhere easily. The staff is amazing and so nice. I love the feel of this hotel because it has that european flair. The breakfast is yummy and great choices. And I love that they have an afternoon wine after a long day of sightseeing. I will definitely stay here again when I go back to LA!

“Inexcusable problems” I booked this hotel for a short 2 night stay. The rooms are decent. The location is OK - it's close to Union Square but it's on the border of the Tenderloin, so be careful not to go the wrong direction. But I had 3 problems that flat out should not have happened at a JW Marriott. 1. I walked into my room and the temperature was at 78 degrees. The AC wasn't working. I told them, came back later and it was fixed. 2. My TV wasn't working. I called, they came up and fixed it. 3. My shower was scalding hot. I called, them came up and fixed a valve and it worked. For a short 2 day stay, you shouldn't have a 3 very basic things go wrong.

“Great service, decent location for the airport” I spent a single night here before the Memorial Day weekend. Although the hotel itself was typical for an airport Marriott (which is usually quite good), the service I received was far better than I had expected. The shuttle from the airport was prompt and friendly - the driver handed me an ice cold bottle of water as I boarded. The desk clerk checking me in recognized my name immediately because my wife had called ahead and faxed my kids' report cards - she was excited to give them to me. Though these were small gestures, they made me feel welcome and valued as a guest. The room was very comfortable, clean, and most importantly, quiet. The restaurant was nice but definitely overpriced. Internet access is NOT free. The concierge lounge on the 12th floor has a free continental breakfast in the morning and an honor bar in the evening. The shuttle runs continuously - the ride to the airport takes about 15 minutes.

“Close to Convention Center and Ballparks” Easy hotel for the business traveler to use downtown. My taxi fare from Sky Harbor Airport was around $24 with tip. I was in town for a convention for four days. You are pleasantly greeted at the door by hotel staff. Check-in was quick and pleasant, I was handed a cold glass of water by hotel staff while checking-in, nice touch. My room was a standard room with two beds. Clean and well stocked with all of the standard amenities you would expect. I met friends at the outside bar on the fourth floor. Great place to grab a drink, enjoy the weather and shade of the early evening. There is a nice lap pool on the fourth floor outside as well. During my four days I also took advantage of the workout facility on the fourth floor. Excellent place to run on a treadmill, bike, weights, stretching area....etc.....very nice facility. Breakfast at the hotel is very good, buffet or order off the menu, there is a Starbucks across the street behind the Hooters if needed. Avoid the Hooters across the street. Food was cold and terrible....beer was warm. Go to the Tilted Kilt several blocks up the street which has good food (Shepards Pie!), good sports bar and great "atmosphere." The convention center is a few blocks straight up the street....nice easy walk. I would stay at the Sheraton again if I needed a place downtown, great hotel!

“Perfect Place to Stay” I had to stay here on business technically. I had a one night stay to facilitate an early morning work date. Checked in a few minutes before 3pm and didn't return until early the next day to sleep in. The women at the front desk are more than helpful and full of information. I was allowed to have a later check out time and checked out very quickly. My room was on a high floor away from the elevator, exactly as I'd requested. The view wasn't spectacular but my room was spacious enough for one person and nicely decorated. I know other reviews point to the dated linens and decor but it fits the hotel in my opinion. Everything is clean and comfortable. The bathroom is very big and has more than enough space for one to spread out and not feel cluttered. I turned the heat up a bit and used one of the extra blankets in the closet when I felt too cold. The television was clear and full of great channels and I definitely enjoyed my complimentary cup of hot tea. I would stay at this Hilton location again if I need to stay in the city because it is in a prime location and offers great service and comfortable rooms.

“Excellent stay” Was in Chicago for a quick 2 night stay for a conference. This hotel is in an excellent location within walking distance to a lot of great restaurants and the major conference hotels. I loved the lobby and the overall vibe of the place... very busy but in a good way. Here are the room highlights: Room- regular king-size bed room with ample size. Bed: very comfortable Bathroom: curtain tub/shower combo with excellent lighting and size AC: worked very well, was able to maintain comfortable room temps throughout stay Miscellaneous: flat screen TV but not HD cable... sadly, you come to expect this for a 4+ star hotel... my only gripe really. Great closet space and a nice desk/area for work. I would very much recommend this hotel for business or fun.

“Excellent location!” First off the location of this property is perfect! Ideal location and we were able to easily walk from the train station after flying in. There were 6 in our family so we had 2 rooms that I was able to obtain for an amazing rate by priceline. I had assumed with the fact my rate was so inexpensive that when I asked for a water view room on a higher level I would not be accomidated..but I was wrong and plesantly surprised! Asked for one room with a king bed and a second connecting room with two double beds~thrilled when we went to our rooms! Beds were very comfortable, rooms were spacious and the kids were thrilled! You should be aware that this place is HUGE!!!!!! Its also connected to an underground shopping area with many stores and restuarants so with bad weather you almost do not have to leave the property. We did choose to have the breakfast buffet one day which was wonderful but overpriced. Tried The Yolk for breakfast the next day and had the best breakfast food of all time for a third of the price. An added conveniance was the grocery store right behind the Hyatt which was excellent!!

“Disgusting!!!!!!” Disgusting in every sense of the word. From obnoxious check in personnel, to sewer like bathrooms and rooms. Stay as far away as possible. They should condemn this place and send the management to prison.

“Best value on CLub Level” Just returned from 4 nights at this wonderful hotel if you stay on the Club Floor. I was upgraded from an already ridiculously low rate (see dchotels website for the best rates ever; they negotiate with the hotels!) to CLub Level for $100 total (thought it was that each night, which would have been worth it, but only sharged that for 1 night). it pays to ask for an upgrcde at this hotel. the food service on the club leval is without parallel; who needs to go out and eat when you get 5 superb food servings per day. the best is the hors d'oeuvres (?) from 5-7 with full open bar including fine wines and liquor. i am tellling you , this is a great deal. i don't know what it would be like in a regular room without the club level amenities, but the rate also includes acces to the finest gym in d.c. this is a terrific treat, especially if you negotiate! th serviced is fine otherwise, though the staff can be a little young and over-enthusiastic.

“Excellent K Street business or weekend hotel” Was passing through Washington DC, and was able to get a summer weekend rate at the Capital Hilton. This Hilton is a refurbished classic building, originally constructed in the 1940's. The refurbishment is up to Hilton brand standards, with a beautiful, palatial lobby area, and professionally furnished rooms. It's "elegant" without being too over-the-top. Being an older facility, rooms are actually slightly larger. My "deluxe" room had a large bathroom-shower area, and even room for a couch and ottoman. Internet is via Wi-Fi, and is charged at market rates. The location of the Capital Hilton is very, very central. K Street is close to many commercial buildings, a reasonable walk to the White House and George Washington University, and a few Metro stations on the red, blue, and orange lines. It is a bit of a hike to the National Mall, though if you Metro your way down, it's not bad. Also note that K Street is basically a central business district, which means that weekends and evenings it's relatively tame and quiet. If you're looking for interesting restaurants and cafe's, you'll have to go a bit north to Dupont Circle or 14th street North. These are all Metro'able or walkable, so it's perfectly fine, but it's important to note. The room itself was clean, air conditioning was adequate, and my upper-floor (7th floor) room was relatively noise-free. All generally good in quality and service. I'd recommend the Capital Hilton on a reasonable price-point. I had absolutely no issues with this property. It's not a "must-visit" hotel -- more like a place to sleep, but it certainly suits the task.

“Enjoyable stay, nice hotel” Rooms here are quite large by Boston standards (or really any large city in the Northeast/MidAtlantic corridor) and the floor plan sets the bed back quite a ways from the door, meaning very little hallway noise bleeds into the room. A major plus. Bed comfortable but not outstanding. Room decor is very muted, almost bland, kind of like they're going for the Colonial feel but took it a little too far. Room was nice, fresh and clean. The breakfast buffet is underwhelming especially at that price, but surprisingly the hotel bar is one of the best bargains in Boston, with $6 pints of microbrews. The bar closes a bit early (11pm if I remember correctly, on a weekend) but you can carry your drinks to the "library" across the hall and relax there. The room price is high but in line with other Boston hotels of the same caliber. It's a very expensive city. I would stay here again though!

“Location, Location, Location!” My husband, son and I stayed one night at the Marriott as we were in town to see The Lion King. We arrived an hour before check-in time and were able to check into our requested room ( Times Square view) right away. The room was very large for NYC and the furnishings were nice. The bathroom was well appointed, but a little on the small side. Would have liked a mini-bar or little refigerator in the room. We left the hotel several times and never had a problem with the elevators. Most of the time the elevator was available within seconds, and our longest wait was a couple of minutes. There did seem to be some people in the lobby having difficulty understanding how the elevators were assigned, but the process was very straightforward and my nine-year old had no problem grasping the concept. There were plenty of places to eat and shop within blocks of the hotel. We have stayed at other hotels in the Times Square area, but we enjoyed the Marriott the most.

“excellent...that says it all..” I have 183 reviews on here and only 18 of them are excellent ...so I do not give ratings if they are not deserved..this place deserves an excellent rating..I have stayed here quite a few times and have never had an issue with anything..It may not be the newest or the fanciest but it is as clean and comfortable as any brand new motel anywhere..rooms are always clean,beds comfy ,showers are clean,great water pressure and unlimited hot water..nice size parking lot easy to get a semi into and restaurants next door but what really makes this place shine above the rest are the people..everybody I have dealt with here are hands down the greatest people anywhere especially the manager..so if your ever in the Columbus area this is your place...you wont go wrong staying here ..I have stayed in quite a few motels in this area some were good and some were not so good but if you want the best at a fair price this is your stop...

“A good hotel” We spend three days at this hotel, two adults and two kids. The room was quit clean but besid that, regarding other relevant aspects, our review is much better. The hotel is in a good location to universal studios and food stores, helpful staff, free parking. Would stay there again.

“Charming.” I was a bit unsure of how the accomodations at the Madera would be as we don't typically choose Boutique hotels, but my husband and I were pleasantly surprised. The front desk staff was VERY friendly and helpful with directions in the area, maps, etc. Our room was huge and had a balcony with sliding door. There is construction going on at the Firefly restaurant just below our room, so we left the door closed in the evening so we could have some quiet. Others have metioned the bathroom, but it is just fine. The shower was great with a large vanity with sink, mirror and plenty of counter space. There is also a huge, draped closet with safe. We are certain this hotel used to be an apartment building. Other great things... 2-hour wine time in the lobby from 5pm-7pm. They serve serveral wines with some snacks. The lobby is a bit small but is always fine for a few mingling guests. They also have coffee, juice and a light continental breakfast each morning. Close to Dupont Circle metro 15 minute walk to Georgetown Close to Reagan airport I think the only half way negative thing we had to say was that there was some pet fur on the carpet in our room. We love pets and are fine with a pet-friendly hotel, but there was something a bit underwhelming to have pet fur on the carpets in your hotel room. Otherwise, all was great! Next time we may stay closer to downtown D.C., but for the price and easy access to metro, we would definitely stay a second time at the Madera.

“Attenzione, un hotel orribile” Ecco un hotel al limite della decenza e della truffa. Ho pagato ben 145 euro a notte per una doppia con le seguenti caratteristiche: muri scrostati, aria condizionata mal funzionante, bagno vecchissimo e doccia con porta cigolante, mobili sporchi, vecchi, dozzinali, e soprattutto biancheria da letto lisa e con buchi ed il materasso che odorava di urina. Il mio voucher comprendeva la colazione ma sapete in cosa si è risolta? un buono di 5 dico 5 dollari da spendere nel vicino Dunkin Donats, una ciambella e un caffè americano. Perchè vendono la colazione se sanno di non poterla offrire? Non ho parole e francamente non riesco a credere alle recensioni positive che ho letto.

“Loved the Hilton” Just returned from a weekend in Boston at the Back Bay Hilton. It was very enjoyable. The hotel is very well maintained and the room was extremely clean. Bed was comfortable. Had a standard room with a great view of the city. Staff were very efficient and friendly. Breakfast was good as was the supper in the bar. Location was very convenient to the Prudential Center complex and Copley Place. Also, the green line subway stop was within walking distance. Would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

“Glad I picked it” I'm very glad I chose the Renaissance. I have been here for two weeks now and the staff from the front desk to the housekeepers are wonderful. The rooms are large, most with balconies. King bed rooms have a sofa and table while queen rooms have two queen beds (choose which works better for you). Each room has a nice flat screen TV and a large desk. As a gold member I was upgraded to the club level and the lounge has a very nice spread in the AM, snacks throughout the afternoon and evening. Coffee and tea are available all day long. The hotel is located between DIA (20 mins shuttle ride) and downtown. There are closer hotels to the airport HOWEVER, this hotel is across the street from an outdoor shopping center with several food choices which is extremely convenient. Most other airport hotels while closer to the airport have NOTHING around them. Renaissance also has a private shuttle that will take you anywhere within a few miles of the hotel, such as the beautiful tennis courts about 5 minutes away. Overall a great hotel, nice views, wonderful staff, good amenities... did I mention the nice gym?? Also if you are here for an extended amount of time, there are FREE washers/dryers for guest use ($1.00 for detergent if you don't have your own). Some have complained about the noise and while yes, you hear the trains honking once in a while it was hardly an issue and I am a very light sleeper.

“Great value, helpful staff, free shuttle, complimentary breakfast” Great service started with the shuttle driver. Offered us all kinds of information about the area and the hotel and gave us lots of help with our bags. Check-in was slow due to long line and only one employee, but employee was very helpful. Got a snack and a few drinks before the restaurant closed at 10:00pm. For a Best Western, the room was nicely updated. Large granite bathroom countertop in the larger-than-expected bathroom, new furnishings, beds, and bedding inside, dare I say almost a Hiltonesque look to it. It had a private balcony overlooking a parking lot. Didn't use the balcony on the short "layover" stay but did verify the locks on the door worked well. The complimentary all-you-can-eat breakfast was better than expected. Hot and cold food options, fresh fruit, cold and hot drinks. Was really surprised at the quality. The only real "cons" I can think of was that there was really nothing of interest around the hotel. I asked the hotel if there was a convenience store nearby and was told it wasn't safe to walk there but they would be happy to give me a free ride. +1 for the free ride offer, -1 for the sketchy neighborhood. Another con was all the hallway noise. Both people talking were very loud and the room doors slammed very loud. Whenever somebody in the hallway came or left their room the door slammed loudly, waking us up. The only other negative was that the business center had no internet. I don't know if it was just "down" during my stay but I tried all 3 computers and none of them had internet. The free return shuttle to the airport left right on time. Every part of the hotel was clean, the staff were very friendly and helpful, the complimentary breakfast was great, and the rooms were nicely updated and decorated. This hotel has a great value and I would stay here again. I was treated like a valued customer throughout my stay by every employee. The hotel management has done a really good job ensuring a very high level of service, far beyond what you would expect at a "budget" hotel.

“Immaculate, large rooms, good staff, reasonably priced” Spouse and I and an Australian couple visiting stayed here (2 rooms) for one night before they flew from Charlotte to the US west coast on the way home. This is a very good Fairfield Inn – immaculately clean and reasonably priced. I have stayed in several “lesser Marriott’s” in the last few years and this in the top three. Desk service and staff, most helpful, the room was the largest we have seen in any Fairfield. As in all Fairfield’s the towels were “thinish” – but that is the way it is! The breakfast was an excellent hotel lobby breakfast, fresh eggs, hot biscuits (and gravy – if you like that), fruits and the standard hotel lobby continental breakfast stuff. Very convenient to restaurants – good Ruby Tuesday’s 1⁄2 mile away and but 15 minutes to the airport (albeit on a Saturday morning with little traffic). So having had an unsatisfactory experience at another Charlotte Airport Hotel (see my Trip Advisor review of March 10, 2012), this is where I will stay in the future when I need to be in Charlotte overnight. Rate it a 4; only luxury hotels get a 5!

“Nice bed but otherwise a drab hotel with views...” My wife and I stayed at this Hilton for two nights earlier this month. The plan was to stay for four nights, but the blah and drab atmosphere turned us off, and we switched to the Manchester Grand Hyatt. We were glad we did, and I'll write another review shortly on that hotel. As for this Hilton, I picked it due to the superb pictures of the skyline and bay views from the balconies shown on other reviews. The views are as advertised, however prepare for lots of noise coming from the bay in the form of boats and helicopters, etc. During the day, this is not a quiet location due to all the activities from the military base across the bay and powerboats on it. Can't comment on the other side overlooking the boat harbor, but that's the side where the airport is, and I can't imagine no airport noise would be heard. We also heard noise from a very loud ice machine that had a low vibrating buzz that could not be blocked. Also, the room doors are on springs that cause them to slam hard. This is an annoyance as well as danger, and I accidently lost my grip on the door while entering the room one night which caused the door to swing hard into my wife who got a slight shoulder bruise! I can't fathom why designers of hotels in the 1970's (or whenever this was built) would have installed such difficult and noisy room doors. The facility is very dull and drab, including a small dated lobby. The best thing I can say for this place is that the bed is quite comfy, and I slept well both nights here. Of course, I use earplugs, which are a must at this location. Also, the wireless internet worked quite well and is included in the room rate. However, breakfast was not included. In sum, unless you are flying out of San Diego and need a nearby hotel, other hotels in downtown or elsewhere in San Diego would be a better experience with more ambience than this Hilton, nice views notwithstanding. You'll be able to sleep here, but won't enjoy it that much.

“Ummmm...” I chose Hotel Abri because my daughter and her friend were attending a concert 3 blocks away. PROS: So convenient to the cable cars, Union Square, shopping and nightlife, very friendly staff, reasonable rates for San Francisco, refrigerator in room, coffee maker in room, 2 tv's in the Urban Suite, free wi-fi. CONS: Panhandlers greet you as you enter the hotel, long waits for your car when you valet, very noisy due to the club across the street, urban suite = no phone next to the bed thus you must leap out of bed and run to the other room if it rings, musty smelling room. Although it seemed like it would be a hip hotel, it ended up feeling old and run down.

“Mixed opinion.” I stayed two nights at this property in Jul12. The hotel is set in an old building and rooms are adequately well done. decent complimentary breakfast, functional exercise room and friendly front desk staff provide essential comfort. Housekeeping is not up to the mark (we found cutlery left unclean after the housekeeper's visit to the room) and on the second day morning, I had to cope with exceptionally hot water from both hot and cold outlets in the bathroom shower!

“Absolutely Fine with the best Concierge” This was the first hotel I stayed in San Francisco, and my experience was very positive. We arrived and the door staff took our cases, the check-in process was fine and they were happy to upgrade me as my travel agent had made a mistake. The room was clean and adequate. There is free wireless in all the rooms, which is an added bonus. The hotel is located on the doorstep of the Chinese quarter and this was great for getting Chinese food and it is a short walk to the shopping district. The hotel is not served very well by public transport. As it was our first visit to San Francisco, we approached the concierge who had to be the most helpful man I ever met. He provided some great anecdotes about his various stays around the world. He spent almost half an hour guiding us through the map of San Francisco. You have to ask him about the 'NO' area. He really made our stay. The decor of the hotel is very pleasant and the bar is very atmospheric in the evenings.

“Give it a miss while the renovations are on !” Checked in and then out within half an hour ! They are re concreting the underground carpark and all day from 9-5pm the horrendous jack hammering noise apparently happens and this has already been happening for 4 months they said ! We were on the 10th floor and were still disturbed by it even with the television on. I asked why we weren't notified of this as we had made a phone call from Australia and emailed just the week before (which wasn't answered). You even had to talk over the noise when checking in, I don't know how they can work in that environment ! There was no explanation given but never the less we were not charged and phoned and stayed at The Belvedere around the corner which was stunning ! This hotel is in a great location and the size of the room was nice but expensive and at US $369 a night certainly wasn't going to pay this and be disturbed !

“We Liked the Whitcomb” After reading reviews on TA we booked the hotel through Travelocity. Overall, the hotel was nice. The location was central and could not have been better! We loved walking out the door and being able to hop on the F-Train or the MUNI [subway]. It was a short and nice walk to Union Square and many other touristy areas. The only real complaints we had were the THIN walls...every sound from the neighbors was audible. We slept with the door closed in the bathroom and let the fan run all night to cover the sound. It worked well. The only other thing [and it is minor] was that the concierge would not print our boarding passes and we had to use a pay-terminal in the internet lounge. The staff was helpful and the front desk staff was willing to answer questions and point us in the right direction. We would book here again without hesitation.

“One of the best Seattle hotels” We had a third visit to the Grand Hyatt, once again for business. It's proximity to the Convention Center is great, and this hotel is much nicer than the Sheraton which is a wee bit closer. We have had excellent, exemplary service here and appreciate it in this current environment. We booked an Executive suite with an adjoining room, which happened to be another corner suite. The combination is great for a family. The Executive suite has a small bar with sink, refrigerator, etc, as well as a second bathroom off of the sitting area. The corner suite has a work area, a long hallway, then a bedroom with wall to floor windows on 2 walls. Bathrooms have great soaking tubs with waterfall faucets, separate dressing areas, and aveda amenities. We were on the concierge floor, with access to a lounge with concierge (very nice and helpful lady), internet service, good breakfast, sodas, fruit, water, and hot snacks, a good cheese selection and drinks at night. There's always espresso, coffee and mochas available as well, which is a favorite in our family. Room service is quick and efficient. The location, again, is good for the convention center or shopping. There are many good restaurants within walking distance, and if you don't want to eat breakfast in the concierge lounge try to get the b and b package; it includes a hearty breakfast in the adjacent Ruth's Chris steakhouse. Parking is expensive, valet or self, but that's unfortunately par for Seattle. The furniture is a bit worn, with the occasional stained pillow or scraped desk. The bed was very bad, the worst I've slept on in a long time - had we been there longer I would have requested some kind of stabilizing board under the mattress.

“Request a high floor” The Peninsula is a well-located property on 5th Avenue - easy walk to shopping, Central Park and Broadway. Make sure you get a high floor room. We stayed in a Grand Luxe Room on the 4th floor for the first couple of nights. Very spacious and well furnished (except for the tv/drinks cabinet which was very bashed). The problem was that we were directly above the front entrance - very gloomy outlook. We were moved to the same room type on a much higher floor afterwards - vastly different experience. The main highight for us was the rooftop indoor pool which directly overlooked the 5th Avenue "canyon" leading downtown. Surreal. This is the reason for the 4th star of our rating. The service was patchy. Friendly until we had the "affront" to complain about the first room. The Jumeirah Essex House is a much better NYC option - in a different league.

“You are better off sleeping in your car” We spent 4 nights in the Seattle area and since we were flying out early in the morning, we thought we'd save money and stay at Motel 6 Seattle Airport. This was the biggest mistake we made. Our room was a health hazzard. There were blood stains in the bathroom and we found a drug syringe in the roll of the toilet paper. I complained to the hotel manager and she didn't even apologize. You're better off sleeping in your car.

“Good hotel in a great location!” Got this hotel via Priceline, but could have booked direct for $5 more. Smallish room, but that's New York. Great location! Subway stop on the corner. Walking distance to many attractions. Room was clean and quiet. Ordered a refrigerator, which they brought up quickly. Bed comfortable. Everything worked. Plenty of outlets and flat screen tv. Lobby average. There was a bar with people hanging out at all hours, but we didn't use it. No coffee maker in room, but plenty of coffee shops nearby. Security at night by elevators was appreciated. All in all, we recommend and would return.

“Its a good hotel” Its a good hotel and it is with in your price range as its not as much high end or low end . Its a clean hotel . staff is good rooms are fine. its near to times square but you have to walk 15-20 min for that

“Everything - PERFECT” I have stayed at more than a few NY hotels for wkend trips and the Benjamin has been the best for the price by far. Great Midtown location (if that's what you want); impeccable service; clean, modern room; easy check in/check out; and did I mention great service? To get a decent room these days, it's going to cost between 200-300 per night - at least that's what I have found. Decent to me is: clean, fairly quiet, up to date facility, quick, efficient service, no non sense. I got a last minute rate for $249 and it was worth every penny. Do not hesitate to stay here.

“Couldn't have been happier.” What a remarkable little hotel. Friendly staff, great restaurant, eco friendly bathrooms and energy. I was just delighted to be in a place that used space wisely without skimping on comfort. If you've stayed on a boat, you'll think these rooms are enormous and well fitted. If you're used to space, this my be a shock. The single bed was immensely comfortable. I stayed for a weeks and had plenty of storage space. Being a basketball fan and staying there during the playoffs, I was incredibly thankful for the flat screen and cable in my room with free WiFi. The elevtor broke a couple times while I was there and being on the 5th floor it was a pain, but not a trip killer. The subway is about a half mile walk, but lovely in the spring and I got to pass my favorite soap shop each time (Soapology). You're right on the river if you want to go for a run and the resturant's salmon pot pie was just KILLER. So good. Honestly, I felt like I might not have been cool enough for this place with all the hipsters running around, but I will be back. The service, the rooms, the locale, you can't beat it. Read up on the history of the place as well. They hosted the Titanic survivors for crying out loud! So cool.

“Coulda found a nicer place for the price...” The carpet was old and dirty. The furniture and bed comforter needs to be updated. The bathroom looked old and the lighting was terrible. The plastic runner at the bottom of the room door was torn and dragged the floor. I have stayed in 2 star hotels much nicer than this one..... Customers should be warned that they have to pay for parking! This automatically increased my total cost by 17 dollars. It's 13 for non-hotel parking (as the hotel doesn't even have it's own lot!) or 17 for valet in the front of the hotel! I feel that not including this additional charge is essentially false advertising for the cost of the "hotel stay"!

“Classic old hotel, great location, executive floor worth extra cost” I have stayed at the Palmer House many times over the course of several decades. The fact that I keep coming back says something about the hotel. The location is great and you do feel like you've stepped into another era...until you see someone walk through the lobby wearing a t-shirt and baseball cap. We had a great stay in a room with 2 beds and 2 baths on the Executive Floor. The Executive Floor cost $40 more per night but it included a private elevator that skips most floors (this is a huge hotel and the elevators are full and slow), complimentary soft drinks, snack mix, and cookies all day. Complimentary hors d'oeuvres during the happy hour (my glass of wine was $10) included cheese, fruits, crackers, spinach dip, and hummus.
