Complimentary breakfast which included cold cereals, coffee, juice, bagels, hard-boiled eggs, meat, cheese, muffins, croissants, and granola bars. Words of warning. The room sizes vary a lot so your room could be not much bigger than a closet or extremely spacious. If you are next door to a wedding party that is in and out of their room all night, you will get a lousy night's sleep. The check-in line is always slow (though they handed out free popcorn and bottled water while we were in line). Internet access is outrageously priced. As in all city hotels, parking is also very expensive.

“New, worth staying at.” Like the other reviewers have said, great shower and bath room. We had a minisuite with a couch so lots of room. Appreciated the large 42" TV and the mini one in the bathroom. Continental breakfast was great. Only slight negative was the young staff, not very knowledgeable about the area or the hotel. Also, the outside door staff enjoyed each other more than their jobs. Staff needs to be schooled better. Room was clean and the bed gave me a perfect night's sleep.

“Not the best hotel we've stayed in” We stayed at the Residence Inn for 2 nights back in June. We had never been to Colorado before so decided to get away for the weekend to Denver. The location of this hotel is great, within walking distance to a lot of restuarants and attractions in Denver. Check-in was easy, the staff were friendly and very helpful. The rooms were clean, but quite small, both the bedroom and the living area were tiny and we found it a struggle for the 2 of us with our 1 year old daughter to move around. We also had asked for a portacot which we didn't end up using as there was no room. The entry to the bathroom is in the bedroom, which disturbed people that had already gone to bed. The included breakfast was sufficient and again, the staff were great, providing information about Denver and talking to us about the effect altitude has on little ones and their sleep (or lack thereof). Carparking was for a fee, but very convenient. But beware, on Sundays they do high pressure the car park and if your car is left in there expect it to be wet and dirty! But you are warned about this. We probably won't stay at the Residence Inn, but would recomend the hotel to budget travels, perhaps couples, but defintely not families with small children (if you want space).

“Felt like the 60's and not in a good way!” We bought this room through Hotel tonight and it was a great price! The lobby is plain and sort of drab and grey. It reminded me of hotels we stayed in Europe, only the rooms were much larger. Our room had a tiny bathroom with a sink outside the bathroom. But......it had a pretty nice flat screen. Hopefully you are not going to spend your time ib Boston sitting in your room, the location is great, and very near some very pricey hotels. Near the Prudential building and shopping/restaurants. Parking is available for $18 on property. The staff were accommodating and the Bell Captain was from Ireland and had worked at the hotel for 43 years. He was very sweet. I would probably stay again for the right price.

“Beds not acceptable for this price (but love the decor)” The Royalton is a beautiful hotel--the renovations in the lobby are great. The front desk staff was very good--some of the most personable I've been around. However, given the prices, the stay really isn't worth it. We paid $449 (before tax) for a Superior room, on a weekend. The room was running $749 on a Thursday (think how this compares to your mortgage payment. And this was just the 2nd level room--not close to the most expensive.) At these prices, the experience should be perfect. No matter how nice the front desk staff is, no matter how beautiful the lobby is, or some of the elements of the room, this place is not worth that price. The reason--The beds--hard. The sheets were rough, as if over starched. I've had better sheets in a Hampton..at much less per night. They were scratchy, crinkled. Not posh at all. The toilet paper is rough. The halls are noisy. There was a birthday party in the room near us...going on until 2am...with cigarette smoke wafting in. (did I call the front desk--no since 1--the desk should be verifying people are guests before they go up, and 2--I had a food poisoned partner I was taking care of (not the fault of the hotel)...I didn't have time to argue with a night clerk.) Doors slamming until 2am. There was a fireplace in the room. How to use it? Don't know since there were no instructions in the room. Wireless internet? How to use? Don't know--again, no instructions in the room. (why should I have to call the front desk? I'm paying you a fortune...don't waste my time having to call up and wait.) But there was a menu of all of the items for sale in the room, as well as info on the other Morgans hotels, and the minibar pricing...which was good to know since on check out I was charged $38 for mini bar usage I didn't use...and none of the items I was charged for matched anything on the list (and they never told me what the items were.) Yes, they corrected it, and indicated that there was a problem. But I had to call to correct. At these prices? At $449 (or think of paying over $700/night for this--I doubt they gave you better sheets)--this is totally unacceptable. I love the style at the Royalton. Take a look at the photos--very cool place. But I can't recommend this place anymore at these prices. Their in-room quality doesn't justify it. Check out other hotels for a better bed and a better night's sleep--you won't be as trendy, but you won't have those nasty bags under your eyes.

“小さくてかわいいホテル” フェリービルディングからすぐそばで、便利なところでした。 空港からBARTで30分(先頭で下車しましょう)、Embarcadero駅から徒歩5分程度でしょうか。 部屋はスーツケースの開ける場所に悩むほどとてもとても狭く、建物は古いもののHPの写真の通り小ぎれいで私は気に入りました。 ハーバービューの部屋数はかなり少ないようです。 バスルームは部屋の狭さの割には普通の広さでAVEDAのバスアメニティーでした。 アニマル柄のバスローブがあります。 1Fには和食のOzumoというお店です。 また近所にはCHAYAという日本人シェフのいる日本食レストランがあり、口コミを見る限りでは良さそうです。 部屋にコーヒーメーカーはありませんが、毎朝ロビーに無料のコーヒーがありました。 夕方はロビーでワインレセプションがあり、誰でも気軽にワインを楽しむことができました。(赤・白・ノンアルコールドリンク1種) さらに20時ごろフロント前にはクッキーとミルクが用意されており、ホスピタリティーは素晴らしかったです。

“Perfect combination of great location and decent rates.” We came to Nashville on a college tour trip with my daughter and her friend. We would have loved the Peabody but didn't want the exorbitant rates for smallish rooms. The Hampton Inn was a perfect alternative . Check in had a big sign saying something on the order of, "If you want peace and quiet, don't stay here...." and we were there over Mardi Gras, so it could have been loud. But we hardly heard a thing from our third floor room. Only complaint I'd have is that we could never figure out how to get over to the shopping mall on the other side using the bridge. I think the bridge was closed. Otherwise, great location, nice staff, comfortable bedding. We were happy.

“ok, not great” My family of 6 spent 2 nights (thanksgiving) at this Hilton. The lobby is very small by HIlton standards. Check in was smooth. Got to the room to find that the double beds were smaller than standard size. So we called to the front desk to order roll aways. No problem, $25 per bed per room. Yikes! Our sons room mini fridge was full of old and smelly food. Housekeeping came up quickly to remove. Later that evening I called for more washcloths as there was only 1 in our room. An hour later they were delivered. Plasma screen tvs don't impress me like they seem to impress so many other guests. tv is tv. We go to NYC to see the sights not watch things we can watch at home. Exercise facilities and pool are very nice. Having to pay for internet service is ridiculous! I find it funny that Hampton Inn's don't charge for internet service and yet the more upscale Hilton properties try to grab more money from you for something that should easily be included in your hotel quote. Location of this Hilton is only a minor inconvenience. Subway is just across the street and taxis are plentiful. Valet parking only at $45 per night. No in and out parking available. Takes about 25 mintues to get your car. Had desert in the hotel restaurant. Very good and staff was very friendly. Breakfast was suppose to be included but my husband had to go to the front desk to have the charges removed. Being across the street from the World Trade Center site was humbling and my family spent some time just looking out our windows at the site as well as walking around the area. No real perks at this Hilton for belonging to Hilton Honors. Would I choose this Hilton again, probably not. I wouldn't mind the distance to main sights if the hotel itself was more appealing. We have stayed in many hotels in NYC that had more ambience. However, if you get a good rate and it's price you are interested in than you'll probably be okay here.

“A very cool hotel in a hot city” Temperatures exceeded the 100 degree mark while we were in NYC but this hotel was a great refuge. Wonderfully sexy, very chic, terrific service. Great location, situated not far from Bryant Park (fun , outdoor reataurant) Broadway, Fifth Ave. The beds are REALLY comfortable. The bar has interesting drinks. The bartenders are great at putting together drinks with ingredients you may like that are not on the menu. Nibbles at the bar are delicious! Try the tuna tartare. No real view out of the window. Showers are good.

“Basic accommodations - great location” I read the reviews before I booked so I was prepared for the worst. Having my expectation set before my arrival made all of the difference. Yes, rooms are tiny and yes, it's dark - but it's a good price and a great location. The rooms need to be updated but they're not dirty. They ask you not to bring food or drink into the room which I think is weird. I stayed one night - it might have been uncomfortably small for a longer stay but I thought it was just fine

“This hotel has a great location but not much else.” The location is great for tourists to Chicago. Right on the Magnificent Mile. Otherwise for a business traveller it would not be a great choice. My room, a Standard, is very, very small. If you have a lot of luggage you will be tripping over it. The bed is fine for one but for a couple it would be too small and if the couple were a little on the large side a disaster. The bathroom is also very small and does not have a bath tub. The sink is cracked but the towels are thick and fluffy. There is a full length mirror behind the door which requires you to work your way around the bathroom door and then shut it before using. The room has no phone next to the bed. The bed does have an i-pod docking station on the bedside cabinet. There is a flat screen tv, safe and a mini bar in the room. It is not possible to sit and look at a mirror to do your hair as there is no mirror in the bedroom and the bathroom is too small to sit in. The desk is far too cluttered up to be able to work at. There is no jotting pad or pen to use when taking a phone call. Aside from the room the reception area on the second floor is small and had only one person working resulting in quite a wait for service. Stay here if the price is right and you won't be spending time in your room or needing space for luggage/shopping.

“Fantastic Hotel, Great Location” I just returned from a six day business trip in Chicago and stayed at the Conrad Hotel. Attached to Nordstrom, it's the perfect location. The staff were wonderful. Very kind and extremely professional. I enjoyed the peaceful nights and the pillow menu (a must). I loved the complimentary slippers and bottled water, especially after working all day. Great for business, but I wouldn't recommend it for families with little kids. This hotel is now on my favorites list. You won't be disappointed.

“Good Location, Comfortable Stay” Nice to come 'home' to a Courtyard, although this one had not been upgraded with a Bistro, the only reason I didnt give it a 5, the location was perfect for access to the Medical Center district, off a main road on its own drive. The staff were friendly and very helpful, local restaurants deliver, or there are many spots to eat within a short distance. I must admit, this is the first time the Courtyard view was nosier that a street view, no fault of the hotel, just lots of children really enjoying themselves in the pool until 11PM. It did get quiet after that, so no real complaints, just an observation. I enjoyed the space and the newer amenities. Will stay again.

“Almost Best Western” We stayed 1 night in a 2 queen room overlooking the outdoor pool on the second level. No elevator so be prepared to carry "everything" up the stairs. Not a big deal for me but beware for those not adept for that. We didn't use the pool but it seemed very nice and those that were looked to be enjoying it. The room was very comfortable. Everything was clean and overall the grounds were well kept. A minor bug is the hot water in the shower was not consistent. You had to be on the ready to adjust every minute as it would seem to fade away. Another minor annoyance is that we booked the room for 4 people and it was only stocked with 3 bath towels. I'm not in the hotel business but there has to be a way to match the room stock to the customer coming in. Anyway no big deal again to go to the front desk and ask for another towel. The noise level could be a bother to some. You are right next to the freeway and the airport and can clearly hear both in the evening quiet. We live near railroad tracks at home so we are accustomed to noise and weren't bothered by it but you could be if you are a light sleeper. The biggest downer was the front desk friendliness. There seemed to be a cloud of gloom hanging over a couple of the people working the desk while a couple others at least tried but seemed to be restrained by the gloom and doomers around them. At least crack a smile for the love of pete. The shuttle to the airport was nice and the driver was very courteous and friendly. He should be in charge of the front desk. We did eat breakfast at the connected restaurant. It was very good and our server was great. Overall I would stay again for the convenience to the airport.

“A Great Choice Any Way You Look At It” This is a little gem in the big city of Chicago. The location is very convenient to a number of sites, both tourist and business, and there are plenty of places to eat within walking distance. The staff is very friendly and of great service, the room I was in was spotless and well-kept, and the free breakfast has a wide and healthy selection. If you're going to Chicago, you need to consider this hotel!

“Better Choices” Priceline booked me with the impression this was 3.5 stars. In reality it eas 2.5 at most. It's hard to locate. When you find it, you go up a long escalator to the lobby. Unique and inviting - like a rainforest. Checking was simple. Went to my room. So small it reminded me of a cruise ship. lots of wood. Very awkward layout and had a cheap feel. During the night, the heat went off and it was cold. Also, the Internet stopped working. I called earlier and there was no response to my complaint. I ate at Hudson Hall. Very different. Expensive and forgettable. The location is quite nice near Central Park. It is access able to all forms of transportation. I saw the manager at checkout. She was quite nice and comped my dinner in Haddon Hall. I also received an apology email with an invite to come back. I appreciate that, but the facility is just not what Priceline rated. It really is 2.5 stars.

“Very Nice Stay and Great Location” My family loves to stay at Embassy Suites and this one did not disappoint. Very nice atrium, clean rooms, 2 TVs (kids were thrilled). The usual great breakfast. The manager's reception was disappointing compared to others but we were meeting people for dinner anyway so all we really wanted was a free drink. The pool was very ncie (and warm) but there was some leaves and bugs in the water, though not enough to keep us out of the water when it was 107 in the shade! I tried to talk the desk clerk out of the $6 parkign fee but was not successful. Since the room was only $79, I decided I could afford the $6. The hotel is next door to an upscale shopping mall and about 20 minutes from the airport and well-located to downtown and Scottsdale.

“BW Plus-Hotel mit guter Lage nach Downtown” Das Hotel liegt optimal nach Downtown (incl. Zugang zum Underground) und zur Interstate. Parken ist kostenlos, die Zimmer sind sauber und geräumig, mit Safe, Mikrowelle und Kühlschrank. Das Bad war neu. Es gab kostenlos 2 Fl. Wasser und 2 süße Snacks (weiß jedoch nicht, ob das an meinem Rewards Diamond Status lag). Tageszeitung u. WIFI (gute Verbindung)gibt's ebenfalls gratis. Das Frühstück ist neben Toast, Bagel, 3erlei Kellogs und Kuchen zusätzlich mit Rührei, Wurst. Der "europäische Kaffee" ist allerdings dann doch eher "American Standard". Das Fitneßcenter ist modern u. es liegen Handtücher bereit. Es gibt neben dem klassischen Getränkeautomat auch ein Automat mit Tiefkühlprodukte (die in der Mikrowelle zubereitbar sind) Chimichanga kann ich hier nicht empfehlen ;-) ca. 0,5 km entfernt befindet sich Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, diverse BBQ Restaurants. Zum NASA Space Center sind es ca. 45 min. (öffnet erst um 10 Uhr) Negativ: Unsere Toilette war verstopft u. das Personal hat uns einen Pluncher in die Hand gedrückt mit dem Kommentar: Helf dir bitte selbst! Heute ist Sonntag und kein Handwerker im Haus.

“Convenient location to Inner Harbor” Stayed at the Hilton during a business trip. The hotel is very conveniently located next to the convention center. There is a covered walkway from the second floor. The hotel is about 10 mins walk from Inner Harbor. The hotel has dining tavern in the adjoining building and a bar near the reception. My room had a view of the harbor. Clean and spacious. Excellent housekeeping and room service and very friendly staff. Parking was a little expensive but I guess it is comparable to the rates in the Inner Harbor area. Great hotel, especially if you are in town for a conference at the convention center.

“Dreadful Room, Fantastic View, Great Service” We live in the Hollywood Hills and are remodeling. Needing a place to stay for a couple of nights, we ended up at the Hollywood Hills Hotel. It is a dump. With the outside temperature over 100 degrees, the room heater would not shut off and the small bedroom air conditioner barely worked. There were other uncharming attributes to the room. However, the staff of the Magic Castle/ Hollywood Hills Hotel(s) -- they are jointly run with a single check in office -- was fabulous. They could teach many superior places how to handle problems. Although we will not recommend this place, we will recommend the service, the attitude and the manager's equitable solution. And, the view is stupendous.

“Nice, but...” Sought a hotel at the last minute for a quick weekend getaway, and found this hotel recommended on Tripadvisor. Excellent price, and a superb location in the theater district. Very good first impression with curbside staff. No-hassle check-in. 3(?) elevators for the facility. Not enough, but the infrastructure is what it is. The room was pleasant enough, but the carpet layers should be banned from the trade. The carpet was beginning to be pulled loose from under the baseboards in our room. One wonders if housekeeping ever reports this kind of thing. The bathroom had nice furnishings, and very nice linens, but was very small. The bed was first rate; comfortable, and nice sheets. The lack of a comfortable chair for lounging is a major bummer. The desk chair itself isn't particularly comfortable, and unsuitable for reading. It was very quiet at night. I was surprised, since it was quite easy to hear hallway noise. A superb location for out-of-towners going to the theater. Within easy walking distance of many fine restaurants north of the Chicago River. Overall, a decent choice based on location and price. And by the way, the several dogs in the room next door kept the barking to a minimum. Appreciated that...

“Great place to stay, good location, close to nearly everything” As a family, this hotel served us well. The rooms were spacious, clean and quiet. We took a room at the back side so that we weren't facing the freeway. Our girls loved the pool - it wasn't huge, but was large enough with a great space around it for lounging around as parents. Best part of the hotel is the lobby which served food at what we'd consider to be very reasonable prices and good quality choices. Also served Starbucks products, and had great spaces to relax, watch your own private tv, do work, or just hang out. Getting to other attractions (Old Town, Coronado, Mission Bay) was super easy and close. Good shopping nearby as well, within a 15 minute walk.

“go for the view” Stayed here for a nearby family function over Saturday night a few weeks ago. We had two rooms, one a harbor view overlooking the Statue of Liberty, the other a city view, which was limited by the other high rise apartments nearby. The harbor view was definitely worth the extra price, which was on par with other hotels of the same caliber, such as the Peninsula and Four Seasons. The rooms were large and refined, not over the top but had a quiet elegance; the beds were most comfortable and the bathroom full of marble. Be sure to check back on the hotel website as the reservation nears, as the price booked a couple of months back actually dropped as our date neared, and the hotel changed the rate. Overnight parking is steep ($60) and the Sunday buffet brunch at the hotel restaurant likewise ($45) though top notch; the hotel is close to the ferry and downtown attractions, but a haul from midtown. Service was helpful, and all in all the stay was most enjoyable.

“Faded” We've never been fans of Doubletree hotels and this property did not change our minds. The lobby was very nice, but strangely empty and full of unused space. The hallways are definitely in need of attention - stained walls and carpeting held together with duct tape everywhere. Our room had been fairly recently updated and was tolerably clean - though the furniture was a bit banged up and there was no flat screen TV. There were NO towel racks in the bathroom - just one hook on the back of the door. Where is one supposed to hang wet towels?! And they were stingy with the towels. In our double room we had exactly 2 bath towels, 2 hand towels and 2 wash cloths. The second day we only had 1 of each - apparently we were supposed to share? The housekeeper said she was out of hand towels, but did deign to give us an extra bath towel as a substitute. The same was true for drinking glasses - there were only 2, and those were in the bedroom, not the bathroom. Soap and shampoo were never replenished - we had to go look for housekeeping to ask for more. Lighting throughout the room and bath was pretty dim, and the water pressure in the shower wasn't great. The shower curtain needed cleaning and/or replacing and the grout in the shower was dirty. The chocolate chip cookies they advertise - we were each given one when we checked in and that was all we saw. The food at the dinner we attended was pretty good and the staff throughout the facility was friendly and helpful. Overall, we'd stay somewhere else next time.

“The W -- Trendy Hotel in Times Square” W Times Square is a very trendy hotel. Upon entering the lobby from the ground floor, you experience a water fall on the ceiling. It's cool! You have to take the elevator to the 7th floor to check in. The elevator plays cool, funky music, not the typical Muzak you here. On Floor 7, you will find the Whatever, Wherever congierge, the living room/bar and check-in. You have to take separate elevators to your room--it's an added safety feature so that bar-goers do not go up to the floors with the rooms. You will have to put your room card in the slot for the elevator to work. The hallways of the room floors are dark--that is one of my only complaints. It goes with the trendy vibe but I think the walls are black, lending to a cavelike feel. If you have poor vision, beware! The rooms are great. The mattresses can't be beat. The linens are soft and the satin comforter is wonderful! Loved the flat screen tv. My only other complaint was the shower. There is only half of a glass door. Kind of strange. The water won't flood over even though you think it will. I would have enjoyed the shower more if there was a full curtain or shower door. There are sliding doors to the bathroom without a lock. There's no fan in the bathroom. I did miss turn down service. For the amount of money, it should be something that is included, not something you have to ask for. I also enjoyed the Bliss products. The Blue Fin offers a tasty breakfast menu. It is a bit pricey but it is located right on the ground floor of the hotel. It's convenient. There are tons of Starbucks around if that is more up your alley. Overall, our stay was great, comfortable and we would return.

“Nice Hotel with a Really Good Restaurabt” Loved the historic feel of the hotel. Really nice boutique feel. Huge rooms with fun decor. Everything was well kept. Service was impeccable. I loved the restaurant and bar. We were also at a great location - right across the street from Madison Square Gardens. We had a Dunkin Donuts right around the corner for great cofee, too! The only drawbacks were the fire station on one side of the hotel (side street) and the police station on the other side street. Thank God for our fireman and policeman - just wish everyone in Times Square could keep the criminal activity down so we could sleep a bit more. But what is New York without sirens?! Good proximity to all Times Square and theater attractions, Macys, tours and lots of Irish pubs!

“Not the greatest.” I chose the Hilton Garden Inn in Philadelphia for our three night stay due to the reviews on Trip Adviser and the location of the hotel. I have to say that I was VERY disappointed. My disappointment was due to the uncomfortable bed, lack of housekeeping and noise around the hotel. Pro's * Good TV with many channels * Fridge and Microwave in room * Good size room * Location for us was good although I understand the area is not desirable. * Fast Wi Fi * Good shower Con's * The noise around the hotel was terrible. There seemed to be constant noise in the hotel including early hours of the morning (4.00am) * The bed was very uncomfortable - the worst i have ever slept in and we have traveled a lot. * Room as very hot - They did have air con but the unit was very noisey * My biggest complaint was the housekeeping. On our first day we returned to our room at 6.00 pm to find our room had not been cleaned. After many attempts of calling guest help ( first 5 times no one answered) I had to ask them to bring fresh towels. The next day we returned at 3.30pm and our room was currently being cleaned. The hand towels they left in the room were dirty. * 4 pm check in

“I've never heard of a hotel putting $2,000 worth of holds on a credit card!” I booked my room well in advance and paid for it! When I got my room bill there was some what I consider minor incidentals billed to the room. Upon check out I paid the majority of the incidentals in cash and put a little bit on the credit card. When I got home I saw that there was a $2,000 hold from the palace hotel on my credit card. I've NEVER EVER seen this at all in my entire experience with a hotel especially one that considers itself to be a 5 star hotel. The facilities are alright, the room is dated, beds were way too soft and springy, hall ways echoed, and the bathroom wasn't even luxurious. The location was just fine and the service was a best spotty. Internet was $15-20 per day!!!! I've never ever seen internet and I go to England and Japan quite a bit. If it was up to me I wouldn't stay here again.... I think for what I spent I would have much rather stayed at the Le Meridien (I should have booked that in the first place). I'm offended because I am a littler younger than most people on average staying in a place like that. But NEVER judge a book by its cover and just assume that a young adult cannot pay for a room when it has already been paid for in advance and also be able to cover the incidentals. Trust me what I spent was merely just a drop in the ocean and I'm sorry I spent ANY money with the Palace. As an SPG Gold member I am extremely upset over this! NEVER EVER AGAIN and I come to San Fran once a year. I hear the Mandarin Oriental is quite nice. So I'll be staying there next time! To all you considering to stay here do not you will be disappointed in the value for the money.

“Convenient and clean” We stayed here for one night before flying back to Dublin. We drove from San Diego to LA and arrived approx 1pm. The first major problem was the lack of signs showing us where to leave our rental car. We ended up lifting a chain to a space marked Hertz and dumped it there. After queing for over 15-20 minutes at the Hertz desk we were told we were late returning the car...........hmm maybe thats because you left us standing here for the last 20 minutes and now we are 15 minutes late returning the car, anyway after explaining the situation the Hertz rep said it was ok and would ignore the charge and said where we parked the car was fine.....ok then! The queue for check in was approx 10 minutes and eventually we got to our room. The room was what you would expect from an airport hotel, compact but comfortable. The only thing about this hotel is, when you are there, you are there, there is nothing else around, no shops, restaurant etc hence the reason they can overcharge you in there coffee shop and restaurant. The pool area is actually really nice, the noise of aeroplanes taking off and landing did not bother me and it was nice to squeeze in one last bit of sunshine. There are also 4 lovely hot tubs to relax in. The food in the restaurant was quite nice and we also had some drinks in the sports bar. The lobby of this hotel is constantly buzzing and I liked the busy atmosphere. The free shuttle to the airport was also appreciated even if it was a squeeze. Overall its an airport hotel and the pool is an added bonus 7/10

“Repeat Satisfaction” This was my second visit to this great property on the upper west side of NYC. Traveling on business is the purpose of most of my travel, but I would take the Belliclaire for either business or pleasure. What a terrific property for those looking for a great hotel in a wonderful part of the city. I have had the deluxe room on both visits and found it more than satisfactory. Beds are comfortable and the room has always been very clean. If you expect to have a meeting in the bathroom, Belliclaire might not work. The bath is plenty big to do all the functions intended. I also need to say that the staff has always been very friendly and willing to help with any questions or needs. With some best restaurants anywhere in the city, including Big Nicks( best burgers anywhere), the subway a block away, and plenty of shopping and services, the Belliclaire gets my vote for repeat satisfaction.

“Service Oriented Staff” The woman at the front desk was excellent. I called for directions because there are two Hilton Garden Inns, I asked for a early check in and a room at the end of the hall. I recieved all of my requests. The shuttle drivers were prompt and helpful. The food in this hotel is actually pretty good. There is a Waffle house right out the front door as another choice for dining otherwise that is it unless you have a car. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The only complaint is it is near a busy highway and you can hear the traffic at night. great place to stay if you have an early flight. They also have a business center with 2 computers for printing out your boarding pass

“Decent stay” My boyfriend and I stayed here while attending a college graduation. The hotel is one of the older Best Westerns, and does not have some of the more modern ammenities that the newer ones have, but I did not have any serious complaints about the stay. It is easy on easy off the freeway, close to downtown, and near restaurants. Not far from the Dallas Farmers Market, Museums, and the Dallas World Aquarium. Bu, being that it is one of the older BW's, it felt more like a motor inn instead of a hotel.

“Luxury, location, service: the complete package” We stayed for three nights in a Theater room at the Chatwal, and loved it. The rooms are elegant and beautifully appointed. Soundproofed, leather clad hand stitched luggage finishes on the closets, desk and bureaus. Suede covered walls. The room was all quality, including the bedding. Hi tech phone and electronic controls. Our room had a view worse than most prison cells, with almost no natural light, even on a sunny day. If that bothers you, ask for a room facing the street. I'm sure it will still be reasonably quiet. The lobby and lounge are equally elegant. Service is just what you'd hope for in a five star hotel, seamless and personal. The bathroom was a special treat, complete with chocolate brown marbled flecked with sparkles of blue, huge mirrors, and a high tech toilet that washes and blow dries your bottom (I kid you not!) Asprey toiletries and a package of spa moisturizers at turndown each night. Room service was quick and the food well prepared, although some of the food could have been hotter. The prices are high, as they are in hotels like these. A house salad costing $14 was no more than a few leaves of lettuce with some high end dressing. The Chatwal was originally the Lamb's Club and has a history of hosting some great theater folks in its heyday. It remains a place of complete elegance. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Great stay!” The Conrad was a great hotel ... good location at the south end of Michigan Ave. It was connected to Nordstrom, which includes a casual food court. The service was great, room was very clean and the bathroom was amazing! It was large with a huge shower and all of the amenities. There was a bar in the hotel, which had pricey drinks, but that is to be expected I guess. Overall, a very good stay! And, they allow for late check out.

“Served our purposes” My sister and I went to this hotel as home-base, from where we could explore Cambridge and Boston during her birthday weekend. I did get a good price on Priceline, and since budgetary concerns were more important to us than a fancy hotel, I suppose it did serve our purposes. The hotel and the room were immaculately clean, and the room itself was ginormous (a big living room, big bathroom, and big bedroom - all separate!). On the flip side, I did find the hotel to be lacking some personality, somewhat stripped of any major decor, and in a really odd location....we got off the freeway and were right at the hotel, which would sound ideal, but in actuality we had to maneuver our car into the hotel's driveway despite being surrounded by other drivers going a billion miles an hour. Once we were in the hotel, however, we found it to be relaxing and quiet, with comfortable bedding, and a fairly receptive staff. We did use the shuttle service, which is wonderful and convenient. On the other hand, it runs on a fixed schedule, so we found ourselves having to plan around the shuttle schedule (still convenient, but important for other guests to be aware of). I did feel that it was worth the money - however, in contrast, I have had the wonderful experience of staying in another hotel in the heart of Boston that was bursting with personality and staff members who were eager to help. Would I stay here again? Yes, but only if I got a good bargain again.

“True definition of a hip boutique hotel, wonderful location” If price is not on your mind, this hotel is spectacular! Lots of hotels spend thousands on a snazzy lobby but shabby rooms, but City Club Hotel did something out of the ordinary. It's a very simple and small lobby to check-in, just adjacent to an excellent restaurant, but the rooms are elegant and dramatic! Ipod alarm clocks, marble bathrooms, Hermes bath amenities, extremely comfortable beds and a free business computer on the 2nd floor made my stay very enjoyable! The lobby is light and airy; in contrast, the rooms are quite dark and masculine, but still comfy. I would not recommend to stay here on business, just because they focused on mood lighting, and not desk work stations. If you want your own quiet corner of NYC just steps away from Times Sq, you need to stay here. The staff were accomodating and helpful.

“Great hotel - location and quality” We booked 2 rooms (one for my husband and I and one for my parents). We've been to DC a number of times but because my parents who are sr citizens were visiting too, we wanted a comfortable hotel in a good neighborhood and this hotel certainly delivered. We tried to check in early at 2pm but we could only get 1 room. However at 3pm, they got us 2 rooms on a higher floor so we appreciated that. PROS Location - right on Dupont Circle, near the RedLine subway, restaurants, good neighborhood. relatively easy access even to Georgetown by catching D2 or D6 bus on Q St. Free wifi 24 hr gym Nice rooms, modern decor, liked the wooden shutter window blinds. Iphone/ipod station. Free water bottles (replenished each day) - we really appreciated this convenience after a long trip and after a full day's walk in the Smithsonian museums. There is a CVS nearby and of course Starbucks but it's something you'll appreciate when you don't have to worry about being charged 10bucks for something so essential as a bottle of fresh water. CONS Super NOISY if you stay on 19th Street side from the hotel bar on the ground floor. It was probably the loudest hotel room I've ever been in! My parents stayed on the New Hampshire Ave side which was more quiet. Make sure to ask for rooms on that side if you want to get some quiet sleep esp on a weekend! Bathroom only has showers - not a huge issue for us but some ppl prefer tubs. I had read the reviews about the bathroom - and lack of privacy. We didn't have any concerns and felt it was private enough with the frosted doors but also can see it can be a bit uncomfortable if you're not a couple. Also other reviews on the NY Times said that they provide Kiehl's amenities but they had Aromatherapy goods when we stayed - if you are into quality of amenity goods. Also they didn't give us replacement soap/shampoo on our second day/night.. The hotel's restaurant Cafe Dupont was pretty good -and reasonably priced. We enjoyed breakfast/brunch there both days. Overall, we were very pleased with our stay - and the convenience of the location. The upgrade they made certainly has paid off!

“Worst bed ever” I organized a luncheon for 250 people at the Biltmore and spent the night at the hotel the night before. We ate a late dinner at the Grand Avenue bar. The waitress mixed up our order & the food was bland. My bed (on the club floor) was horrible -- I could feel the individual springs in the mattress. The bathroom is really small, but it's an old hotel. The club floor breakfast was nice. The customer service (outside the club room) left a lot to be desired. I'd think twice about hosting an event here -- they sent us a room diagram with 25 tables & then insisted they would only set 24 until I threw a fit 45 mins before the luncheon began. Also, they couldn't find the twenty-one 24"x36" foam core boards that were delivered to the hotel the day before the luncheon. The boards did not appear until 90 mins before the luncheon & until they were found the staff insisted that they didn't have them.

“Great location, many amenities, some noise” I participated in a conference at the Park Hyatt this week. The rooms are well appointed with extra amenities that make a difference. The bathrooms are mid size, granite, mid size hair dryer with shampoo, conditioner, body wash, soap, bath crystals, and a full box of things like a sewing kit, toothpaste and toothbrush, q-tips, cotton balls and more. The paper was delivered each morning. The fridge had a well stocked mini bar with room for my own beverages. the windows had Both shutters and black out curtains which kept the light and noises pretty low. The Internet access was great, I could log in with my phone, iPad, laptop all included, the lighting was good,nthe bed was comfortable, and the tv channels were well organized. The staff was exceptionally helpful, for example, when I asked which room the conference was in, they got up and walked me to the directional sign. I only ate conference food here, which was good. The room was set up a bit tight, crowded. It was cold for me. The hotel is within walking distance of Georgetown and the waterfront with a lot of shopping options. There are hotels on each corner if this one is not available. It is about a one hour drive to BWI, which I found is a lot cheaper to fly into if you want to splurge on the hotel rather than plane tickets.

“The place to stay downtown” My wife and I stayed at the Solita Soho in October and November 2006, three weeks apart. We know the city well and usually stay at her father's apartment in midtown east side, when he's out of town, but downtown is really where we spend our time (Soho, Tribeca, Chelsea, the Village) so we were looking for a downtown hotel that is not 500 dollars a night in the fall (or more). I discovered this place on TripAdvisor (what a great site this is) and decided to give it a try. The best thing about this hotel is the combination of location, quality of room, and price. Price: Hotels in NYC between Labor Day and Xmas are insanely expensive--it's high season--but we stayed here for roughly 260 a night (just under 300 after taxes). In NYC in the fall, you could spend more than that and end up in a dump--star ratings are notoriously useless for NYC. There are _lots_ of crappy 250/night hotels. Quality: small but sharp lobby, smallish rooms (though not unusually so by NYC standards--I've stayed in smaller rooms for double this price), but very nice furnishings, linens, bathroom, carpet, flatscreen Zenith wall mounted TV--and free high speed internet (just ask for your cable at the desk). Small, boutique-y feel. Staff is fine--not bad, not great. NYC bored but competent. Location: Unbeatable. There aren't that many hotels downtown (compared to midtown). This is midway between the Spring St. and Canal St. subway stops, two blocks from Broadway, and within easy walking distance of many of the best restaurants and funkiest retail in the city. Safety is not an issue. For breakfast, just walk to Broadway, take a right and Cafe Miro is right there--along with lots of other places. Spring St., three blocks to the north, has fabulous restaurants, including the famous Balthazar, Lombardi's pizza, and Spring St. Natural, among others. I only have one caveat about staying here, and you must pay attention to it: there is a bar/club in the basemant of the hotel, adjoining, and on weekends it is REALLY LOUD until 4 a.m. On our first stay, we stayed on the 6th floor and it was no problem. On the recent stay, we were on the second floor and it was insanely loud; I would have requested a room change but I knew the hotel was full. So: you need to stay on the highest floor possible. Next time I book, I'll tell them I'm not staying below the 4th floor, period, and if they can't guarantee it, I'll go somewhere else. Otherwise, when we go to NYC, this is where we'll stay.

“Pleasant, conveniently located, nicely remodeled” Stayed for one night on recent biz trip and will return. Comfortable bed, clean and nice river view. Easy 10 minute walk to downtown restaurants/bars. Unfortunately, they whack you for parking charges so that inflates the price a bit. Overall, very nice

“Nice hotel that is close to a lot” I stayed at the Westin Denver downtown because 1) it was a Westin, and 2) downtown Denver has a lot to offer. The location of this hotel is great - you can't get any closer to restaurants and activities in a first-class hotel as you can here. I didn't have to walk any more than 3 blocks to hit-up anything that I would have needed. My room was a couple of doors down from the fitness center, and as part of the roof on that floor was used for outdoor space, my room had an outside patio that had an incredible view of the mountains and Mile High Stadium. The fitness center included a pool and a basketball court. Anything I needed from the staff was met with attention quickly, and the room itself was what you would expect from a Westin (including a waterfall shower-head in the shower) The only drawback to the facility was the parking fee ($24 / night for self-parking). In total, this was a great property and hotel and I will for sure stay there again on my next trip to the Denver area.

“Luxury at a price” My husband and I stayed here for our anniversary this past weekend, and it was a beautiful, low key place to be for the weekend. I don't know why there are so many complaints about the lobby--yes, it is not the Waldorf, but it is not trying to be an old-fashioned grand hotel.with gaudy chendeliers and tufted sofas with fringe, It is sleek, modern, wood-paneled, understated and elegant with a most gorgeous etched-copper tile art installation behind the desk which is almost worth the price of staying overnight itself. Everything is quiet, and no-drama. Our room, a superior king, was on the small side, but well -designed and well-equipped. The bathrooms, dripping with quartz surfaces; read cool and understated again, with a TV behind the mirror, and sumptuous absorbent robes. The tub was wonderfully deep, and the Grohe fixtures beautiful. The Duxiana beds were sleek and low to the ground,(others had a problem with this, I didn't) and oh so comfortable. I loved that you could actually open the windows and feel the breeze outside. The room's ac/heating was the most incredibly sophisticated system I have ever encountered. Whether the heat or AC was on you could not hear the system working, yet it achieved the correct temperature quickly, as if by magic.The room was soundproof, and the hallways serpentine, so that some rooms don't even face other rooms accross the hall. There were only a couple of negatives--we were never given the soft pretzels I read about and was so looking forward to after my long day hiking all over Manhattan, the personal assistants were sometimes very difficult to reach--the phone would ring off the hook, and the room had not one color photograph or print, or other art item to punctuate the sort-of monochromatic color scheme in the rooms.Other than that, I found the staff welcoming, warm and personable, as well as highly professional. We even had a view of the Empire State Building from our room--a sight which is wonderfully emblematic of NYC.If you can afford the rates, and likea cool, modern vibe, this is a great place to stay in Midtown.

“Good location” The Grand Hyatt at Union Square is a good location. The hotel itself is average. The staff was helpful, and the rooms were clean. I don't understand how several rating groups rate this hotel a 4 star hotel. I would say 3 stars easily, but the rating of 4 stars is not accurate. You will be disappointed if you think you are going to stay at a real 4 star hotel. If you book an upgraded room ,make sure that is what you get, it seems like Hyatts' try to down-grade the room you purchased. The location around Union Square was really good, we felt safe,plenty of shopping,and food that you could walk to. The cable and trolleys were ony a block or two away.

“Great Stay” I thoroughly enjoyed my trip at this hotel. the location is great. The Front Desk's customer service was excellent.The only negative is the size of the room,but, it is downtown Chicago.I would most definitely return to this hotel.

“Good value and location” My husband and I checked in for just the night as we were attending a function at the Indianapolis Museum of Art. On arrival, the desk clerk was courteous and efficient. We enjoyed the cookies and bottled water in our room and muffins and coffee in the morning. The room was a spacious, queen suite, with a small kitchen. My husband enjoyed use of the free wi-fi. The location, near I-465 but far enough from the noise of it, made it easy to get around. My husband thought it was a great value.

“Another vote for Sofitel” I based my decision to stay at Sofitel based in part on a price comparison between it and The Library hotel and based on the reviews of Tripadvisors for both hotels. In the end Sofitel was slightly more expensive but the rooms were bigger. I was really pleased (although I was jealous of those who had rooms with better views!) My room was a Classic , a little more than $200 USD over Sat. and Sun. It's a very nice hotel. Clean, great location, the room was an excellent size and well supplied and maintained. Great bathrooms. I wouldn't dine at the hotel when there are so many better deals very close. The location is excellent in midtown, between 5th and 6th, with banking machines very close. I found the staff very helpful and courteous. I did have one complaint and that was that the bed was too soft. I don't know if you can request a harder bed or not. Comfort for me is a stone slab with about an inch of padding. But that's a personal preference, no fault of the hotel. The room was clean, in good condition, not any signs of wear and tear. The place was quiet, too... no traffic sounds or sounds from other rooms. All in all, a great hotel and a very good value for money experience as far as I am concerned. I would happily stay there again.

“Not for Me!” I had a conference at the Gonzales Convention Center in San Antonio and decided to try something different from either the two Marriott’s across the street from the convention center or some other nearby hotel. We came across the Valencia with my travel agent and it sounded good. It was less then I expected. Here’s some thoughts. •It’s a hike from the convention area, so don’t try it if your going to convention •The place is very dark; both all the common area and the rooms. Great for sleep, but not good during middle of the day. Unless you keep your blinds closed at all time, I would not recommend. •It’s in the middle of downtown, which was good. However, when I was awaken at 4pm by the garbage dumpsters being dragged across the street that was not good. Ask for a courtyard room and you will be quite. •The service was adequate at best. •It seems out of the way from most activities. Ok. So you’ve heard my thoughts. The seem to be many better options in town.

“Nice but overpriced” Location to the airport is great. Welcoming lobby and common areas are well maintained. Our room is literally above train tracks which they've tried to mitigate the sound factor with double pane windows - alas, it has failed so you wake to the sound of the trains. Tonight is our final and third night as we're here for a conference. The reputation of the hotel led me to believe we would be delighted with our stay. I have to say average is a good overall description based on my expectation - which was supposed to be above average. Tried room service for breakfast today, nice presentation but upon closer inspection I discovered overly done spinach (my personal enemy veg) and dinky burnt english muffins. Oh, and no receipt so I can't wait to see the final bill tomorrow. I know this is trivial but it must be stated as I believe it is their dirty little secret - one of the supposedly nicest hotel chains in the world use the cheapest one-ply toilet paper available to man or beast. I'm not kidding. If you're paying rack rate and are accustomed to shelling out that kind of money it usually follows that you're using toilet paper at home that is nicer than what they use in public schools. Maid service leaves a lot to be desired. I think the best thing I can say about the maid service is that she didn't steal anything that I'm aware of. Toiletries are 3rd rate. Bed is comfortable. Bathroom is nice (when it's clean). Easy walk to the Smithsonian and some other sites. So off I go so that someone can "clean" my room.

“FIRST CLASS CUSTOMER SERVICE” Shelly was great. Shelly provide 'WORLD CLASS SERVICE' on my recent visit to this hotel. The room was great, and Shelly made it even better with information, advice and just a all out wonderfull person. I will definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Very unimpressive hotel” The hotel looks nice, but that's where the plesant experience ends. The staff are unexceptional, there is no fridge in the room. How can a hotel be four stars without a fridge in room? The rooms were otherwise tiny, valet parking is 42 dollars a night!! 4 stars is not an appropriate rating for this place, 3 star is more appropriate.

“Great Stay at RenCen Marriott” I stayed at the Marriott Renaissance Center over Memorial Day weekend. I am an architecture nut, and had always wanted to stay at this John Portman designed hotel, so this was a fantasy for me. The positives - Room 5015 had spectacular views of Detroit and the River. Even though the adjacent office building blocked the direct view, the side views were great. The elevators were very fast and I rarely had to wait more than 20 seconds. The trip up to 50 never took very long. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. For a cylindrical hotel, the room was spacious. Renaissance Center has great restaurants, a few shops and a food court. Beware that many shops and parts of the food court are closed on Sunday. The problems - Finding the hotel entrance is a challenge. Read the hotel directions carefully. The entrance was very congested and not nearly big enough for all the cars. I wanted to self park, which I discovered is in the independent garage across the street, not affiliated with the hotel. I had no problems in the garage, but you have to haul your luggage across a busy street to get to the hotel. Forget valet parking, the wait and congestion are not worth it. Once in the hotel you enter a motor lobby, but it is not the hotel lobby. You have to go up the very crowded and slow elevators to the main lobby two floors up. Once in the lobby, I had a 10 minute wait to get checked in, even though I had Marriott Rewards. The actual checkin took another 20 minutes. I was using Marriott Rewards for two days and 1 day I was paying for. Apparently this was too complicated for the clerk. While hauling my luggage into the hotel I discovered you could skip the lobby elevators and go through unmarked doors to the left, straight into Renaissance Center and then take the hotel elevators up to your room floor. They don't like you doing this, but it saves 5 minutes. The hotel restaurant was OK. Great views of the river, but overpriced and slow for breakfast. Other Comments - Renaissance Center has very nice restaurants facing the river and a large food court in the lower level. The food court is great, but it takes some effort to get there from the hotel. While Detroit has a reputation as a dangerous city, I felt perfectly safe in Renaissance Center and the river promenade. I walked the surrounding streets until 9pm and had no problems. I would not recommend walking in downtown Detroit after dark, and in general you just need to be careful in the downtown area. Renaissance Center allows the public to wander in the atrium, and photography is allowed (no tripods). The security guards are very friendly and very visible. Unfortunately, the GM renovation has not solved the circulation problems of the large circular atrium. It is still very confusing and difficult to find stores and move between floors. It took me three days to find the movie theaters! The hotel ballrooms are all on the upper floor next to the skylight, somewhat isolated from the public floors. There is direct elevator access from the ballroom floors to all hotel floors. The pool is gone (now the winter garden) but there is a health club on the 40th floor. Note that GM films commercials and other videos in RenCen so certain parts become inaccessible when filming. I would definitely stay at this hotel again, but I would not pay more than about $120 a night.

“Great hotel, tiny tiny rooms.” Lovely hotel. Awesome lobby, cool funky restaurant wtih GREAT breakfasts. Great location and very helpful staff. Luckily I stayed by myself while in NY for business as I don't think that my husband could have fitted in the room with me at the same time - he would never have been able to get in the bathroom! Seriously. I really liked the hotel as it is beautiful and upscale but its best for very (very) short people or those travelling alone - good luck trying to fit two people into the rooms.

“Good location, great breakfast, tiny room!” We stayed at the Hampton Inn Soho for 3 nights last April, we booked there because of the location as we wanted to stay in Soho instead of Midtown where we had been on last March, but were dissapointed, first of all the lobby was the smallest I ́ve ever seen, the staff was very kind, the room was tiny, it was impossible to open our suitcases and not shut them if you didn`t want to jump to get to the bathroom. The bathroom was minimal too. The bedding was ok, the beds were small but confortables.The best thing was the breakfast, everything was there! you can get variety of coffees (regular, strong), toasts, eggs, hotcakes, etc., etc. The internet access was free in the room but wasn ́t a wireless conection, so we just could use one at a time, also there were 2 machines in the lobby with free internet conection. Tip: check carefully the metro station near the hotel , is quite complicated as there are various streets that intersect each other, we got the lost the first night. If possible I ́ll choose another Soho hotel next time, but don ́t mind booking there again.

“Nice hotel, great location” The only thing this hotel is lacking is white noise in the rooms, and next time i'll bring my own. My room was very quiet (no a/c or fan noise), but when there was street or hallway noise it seemed louder because of that. If you are a workout fanatic, there is a nice health club across the street that allows the Hyatt guests to workout for a small fee. This is a nice hotel in a great location, and I recommend it.

“Only as a last resort should you stay...” Only as a last resort should you stay here. The only good quality about it is that it's a couple blocks over from Hollywood Blvd. & the walk of fame. We were afraid to take our shoes off because the carpet was sticky & dirty, the AC & t.v. didn't work, & the refrigerator didn't get cold. Only the bare minimum was provided. We couldn't wait to leave. I don't know how the other moteld were on sunset but I'm sure there are better ones than this one.

“It's a W, not the best one, but not the worst either” Older W and is a bit worn, but the rooms are "W" appointed; however property is showing age. GREAT location if you work at Willis Tower (sears tower) as only a few short blocks away. Food options are somewhat limited adjacent to the W and you would have to hike it several blocks to find something edible (meaning NO to Mickey D's, Dunkin D). Lobby is smaller than most W's but bar is adequate and they try hard to get you serviced. One complaint is the L train (way above ground subway) runs alongside the W and if you have a room on the wrong side you will hear it all night long. Would stay here again for business but not so much for vacation. Great rates here though. Sweat gym is tiny and pathetic in a today's world of staying fit.

“The Hyatt charges you for EVERYTHING!!” I think this place takes advantage of business travelers with expense accounts. It was nice, but I really felt like they were nickel and diming its guests. Parking (valet only) was $30/night, continental breakfast was $13. (Our breakfast was complimentary with our AAA rate, but we were charged an additional $3 b/c we took warm food) Internet access was expensive and I think you had to pay for the pool and fitness center. Late check-in was trouble free. I stayed at the Wyndham on M St on my previous trip to DC and I thought it was much nicer than the Hyatt and a lot cheaper.

“Needs a facelift....badly” Really outdated. Wall paper is coming off the walls, furniture is chipped, various strange odors (including natural gas), plus the toilet in my room wouldn't flush. No counter space in the bathroom. Really handy to Hobby airport and it was quiet, which provided for a good sleep. Breakfast was the exact same thing served for free at Fairfields, but we had to pay $10.95 for it. No wireless in the rooms.

“3 1/2 Stars Tower vs 2 Stars Tower vs 5 Star Lounge” I was at this hotel in March for a business conference with functions in the hotel. There were about 130 participants at the meeting including clients. We knew going into the weekend that the hotel was sold out the night before the meeting began but at the last minute the hotel determined they did have some rooms for the few of us and the clients who were checking in early. Here is where the tale of two towers begins..... The hotel has 2 "towers" as they call it and the majority of the group was checked into the Bay Tower. I got a room in the Marina tower along with 2 others. Usually when a hotel has 2 towers you assume they are in the same building just using separate elevator banks and at opposite ends. However, these are really two completely separate hotel buildings separated by a 5-8 minute walk outside. (Two of my posted pictures show a view from my room and the lounge and the view from my Marina Tower room looking at the Bay Building so you can see the distance.) Note that the hotel does provide free shuttle service. You can see the map of the buildings and layout on the SPG page for the hotel under "Meetings & Events" and then "View Floor Plans & Capacity Charts." I asked the front desk staff who checked me in what the difference was between the two towers and she said "Well the rooms in the Bay tower are generally 30% larger." That may be true but some extra space is all you will get and it's not worth the trade off. Because I was a Platinum member after asking "Well check me into a room YOU would prefer..." I was given a room in the Marina Tower. As we met for dinner that first night naturally everyone asked how comfortable the rooms were and for the three of us in the main Marina tower (the main hotel building/entrance) the rooms were clean, renovated, and just fine. (Pictures of my Marina Tower room are posted) However, I heard nothing but bad comments the rest of the weekend from any meeting participant that was over in the Bay Tower. Distance was a problem but they commented how the hotel was old and run down, bathrooms were not as clean as they could be. They really had a completely different hotel experience than anyone who stayed in the Marina Tower. It's also not a quick trip to get between towers should you have a short break in your meeting and want to "run back to your room." When booking rooms on the hotel website you do choose which tower you would like a room in so BEWARE. In my opinion, if you are not staying in the Marina Tower, do not stay here or at least be prepared. The unexpected highlight was the Club Level Lounge (Marina Tower)! I have also posted pictures of the lounge. Many people who go to the lounges can tell you that most of the time, it's just a sleeping room on a standard floor at the end of the hall with some sofas and chairs in it - small, cramped, dark and not relaxing at all. Maybe there are some cold drinks but it's really depressing and pretty useless. However, the lounge here could not be more enjoyable. As I arrived at the hotel at 11am (and room not available) I asked to have access to the lounge as a Platinum member. The lounge is the entire top floor of the hotel. It's almost all windows with 2 TVs, lots of workspace and comfortable chairs and sofas, and times where food is provided. It's bright with lots of light and comfortable. Internet is also free in the lounge. It was really relaxing and what a great place to work especially since I couldn't check in until 3:30pm. I didn't mind working with a great view of the Marina and Bay. In regard to hotel location - It's DIRECTLY across the street from the airport. Yes it's a short commute from the airport but you can't walk to ANYTHING around there. Look this hotel up on the map before you book so you aren't disappointed.

“Book through iprefer to get an upgrade and free wireless” I stayed at the Stay. in February 2012. The price/value is actually pretty good for New York, as is the location (if you want to be close to the Times Square tourist madness). But I've stayed at a couple of nicer hotels in NY, therefore I just can't give more than 3 points. But it is close to four. The best tip I can give you: Book through the iprefer loyalty programme (iprefer.com). Then you are entitled to a room upgrade if available and free wireless. Problem is that the receptionist had no idea about this, so I had to stay in a standard room the first night, which was probably the tiniest room I have ever seen. I couldn't even open my suitcase properly. The next morning at least they upgraded me with no discussion. The Wireless is actually free anyways on a 1-hour connection cycle, but convenient to have it free for the whole stay so you don't have to log in again all the time. Windows seem to be rare, even my upgrade room only had a tiny one. All in all: For that price certainly one of the best deals you can get in NY. But if you want to stay in a really nice hotel, it may be worth investing that 50-100 bucks more per night.

“Good, Unique, Low-Frills Option” I stayed at the QT over a cold weekend in February and it was a great choice. I booked the cheapest available rate, $199/night, through the hotel website, and when checking in was given a complimentary upgrade. The room, on a high floor, had a bit of a view of the lights of Times Square. It was small but perfectly arranged, with a small table, a very small TV, and a large king size platform bed with one of the most comfortable mattresses I've ever had the pleasure of sleeping on. The bathroom was minimal with a rain-style showerhead, overall lighting could have been better, and in the extremely dry NY winter a small bottle of body lotion would have been appreciated. The pool/bar area was a bit overwhelming on check-in. It's right there by the elevators and was full of good-looking, cavorting youths when I stumbled through after my long flight. But the next afternoon, after a freezing walk around the city, I came back and sat in the steam room, took a swim in the little pool (actually more like the size of 4 hot tubs) which was all deserted, and felt like a new man. Who these people are jumping in the pool at 2am, though, I have no idea. The lobby bar is cute and a great place to arrange to meet friends. Just a half-block from Times Square, the location is almost too central, and the area is very touristy, thus it's a bit tough to find a cheap breakfast or whatever. But, that's New York. The subway isn't exactly right downstairs, but Times Square entrances are just a couple blocks away. It was a good compromise between downtown clubs, midtown art, and uptown friends. For 200/night, it's a great, hip place with a fun, unique style, and if you dont' care about people watching you, a jump in the pool can hit the spot.

“Exceeded expectations - Great Hotel” We were concerned when we read other reviews with bad reports about this hotel - we need not have worried. On checking in we were offered a large room or a smaller but recently renovated room. We chose the renovated room and were very happy with it, clean, comfortable and enough room. Staff were good and check-in/out where no problems although the reception is very busy most times. We really enjoyed our stay in NY and at the Pennsylvania. This is a large hotel with >2,000 rooms and I believe the room quality can vary a lot depending on how recently they were last renovated, ask for a renovated room at check-in. The hotel is old (1916) and has had 27 million visitors since then. The location is great and we would not hesitate to stay there in the future. See the photo for the view from our room. Enjoy New York.

“OLDER, SMALL ROOMS AND NOT THE PICK OF THE LITER” Went back to the Seattle Hilton for one night this week and now I know why I stay elsewhere especially with so many nice Hotels in downtown Seattle. Rooms are small. Bathrooms are beyond small. Think New York but its Seattle and even New York has bigger rooms. Elevators are slow--and overall its just a tired Hilton. Great location. Just not a thrilling property. Stale. Tired. A non descript property.

“Beautiful historic hotel (bring your wallet)” This is an historic hotel in a great location on Michigan Ave (close to the Magnificent Mile, convention centre, restaurants). The public spaces are gorgeous but the rooms are nothing fancy (on the small side, could benefit from some renovations, no safe or refrigerator). Another thing to consider is that there are numerous things that are not included in the room rate (parking, gym/pool use, luggage storage, wireless, local calls); this is not uncommon, but a bit disappointing considering that price. Bed was comfortable and staff were very helpful in this busy convention hotel. Stayed for five nights in May 2012.

“A Well Kept Secret” I have been a frequent visit to San Francisco for many years, and have made the Cow Hollow my 'home-away-from-home' for the past fifteen years or so. I've stayed on the motel side, and suite side. (Note, they are two separate buildings about a block apart, but share an underground garage.) For this trip, I stayed in a 2 bedroom, 2 bath suite. Since I've been returning for the past 15 years, it's obvious I am quite pleased with the Cow Hollow. Here's my opinion on my most recent stay. Pros: Suites are fantastic, very comfortable, and quite clean. Everything you could need is steps away from the door, and the area is not touristy. Cons: booking the suites has becoming increasing difficult (I guess the secret isn't so well kept anymore), and there's some signs of some wear and tear in the suites. If you're looking for a large, comfortable, no frills room, in a great location, this is the place! To sum up, I can say I already have my reservation booked for my next trip.

“Good location, alwasy clean” I often stay here on business. Its only a couple blocks from Grand Central and very convenient. The rooms have always been clean. The desk clerks are pleasant, and they serve a nice breakfast,

“A Home Away from Home..... with b'fast,dinner & wifi included what more could you ask for!” Drury Inn at Galleria in Houston was a home away from home. With breakfast, dinner snacks including 3 alcohlic drinks, wifi, free parking and the fastest friendliest checkin staff what more could you ask for. The hotel is of course not 5 star but honestly why would you want to bother going anywhere else with all the inclusions and wonderful staff we are hooked. And of course its at a bargain price too. The room was great with a huge bathroom and separate vanity. The rooms furnishings were so comfortable and there was even a fridge and microwave for your free popcorn downstairs. We had a wonderful nights sleep and felt so relaxed after a long drive the day before. The breakfast was a mini buffet with everything you want and more ! In the future we will be staying at Drury Inn & Suites on our travels throughout America....with all the inclusions and convenience of parking too it will be Drury all the way !

“A Whole Lot of Other Choices in the Area” I booked this hotel because the location was going to be very convenient to the event I was attending. I really should have checked Trip Advisor first. This place is bad. Stay away! I am normally a pretty easy-going traveler. Read my other reviews. However, this hotel disappointed in almost every way. The front desk staff was rude and unhelpful. The room was in very poor condition. The door lock looked like a last minute improvisation. The bed was one of the most uncomfortable that I have ever experienced. The grounds of the hotel were in disrepair. The highlights of my stay were that I was only there for one night, and my car was still in the parking lot in the morning.
“Not Ravable” Had a small noisey room with a view of a roof covered with garbage Hotel could have been cleaner Short changed on towels as well

“Loved this place! Brand new!” The manager told us they had only been open 4 months and we loved that. Everything was new. Fitness center equipment was new. The service was great, really made you feel welcome. They said this was one of those new Courtyard designs - works very well. So CLEAN too!!! Near shopping and convenient to other parts of San Antonio. Very happy - hope to go back soon.

“For the money, needs updating, stay at the Ritz Carlton instead” Location is fine, centrally located, but this large Westin is showing its age and is "nothing special", hence the poor to average rating. The room had been updated to Westin standards of about 4 to 5 yrs ago and is consequently OK, but showing its age, but the bathroom had original, aging tile at the tub. New vanity and lav, but oddly out of place in an otherwise older bathroom. For the rate, valet parking was pretty much a mess, with overwhelmed staff, cars piling up, and a sense of disorder. I would guess this property gets by with what it has based on large group business. The rate I paid was competitive with the Ritz and Browns Palace (OK, maybe I am a chump and paid too much), which seemingly are more updated, modern properties. Just FYI. I am a Starwood points accumulator, hence my choice of this property, but given the Ritz and their rates, I would likely consider some refresh on my Marriott Rewards points and stay there. Sorry Westin Denver. Time to renovate and take things up a notch to stay competitive.

“DO NOT GO!!! STAY AWAY AND KEEP DRIVING!!!!!!” pros: inexpensive rate nice front desk person Waffle House walking distance(open 24 hrs) cons: I asked for non smoking room and it reeked of cigarette smoke dirty carpet,would not walk barefoot on it roaches crawling by the TV noisy place,if you value sleep don't stay here bums hanging around the place I rather had gone to a rest area and slept in the car.

“Well-priced hotel in Soho” This hotel could not be in a better location. Close to China town and Soho, great restaurants and shopping. The rooms are tiny , a little worn but but very clean. The valet staff are a great bunch, super helpful when it came to parking and storing luggage. Concierge service was a bit lacking, I called for someone to fix my air conditioning unit but no one ever came. But this hotel is certainly the best value in the neighbourhood.

“decent hotel, problems with fire safety” Rooms are well furnished and laid out. Corner rooms on each floor are especially nice with great views. Front desk service is barely adequate. The restaurant and room service are overpriced for this area, and seem to get used only by the desperate. While I was at the hotel, there was a fire alarm on another floor, and members of my group who were on that floor reported that exit doors from the stairwell were locked, and they ended up trapped in the stairwell where they could have died from smoke inhalation had there really been a fire. This was reported to the hotel, and hopefully rectified.

“Week of Calm” A week long stay at Hotel Solamar could not have made for a better end to the year. THe hotel is uber chic and modern, the room (a Vista suite, I think?) was extremely spacious with separate living area, mini bar with quality products, awesome restaurant/room service. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful in moving me from one room to another (because of the length of stay they insisted that I have a suite because of my Kimpton membership level) but it was not available on the first night of my stay, so they moved all my things for me (packed, of course!) on the following morning. Nearly every person at the front desk could speak to me by name and the room service attendants were perhaps the MOST friendly exhibiting actual social skills while standing there waiting for you to sign-off on the bill. Very rare! The hotel's location is amazing and offers so many opportunities for dinner and other strolling around town. Highly encourage anyone traveling to San Diego to stay at this hotel! Not to mention that Kimpton often runs great specials like the one I received for this stay: stay 5 nights or more and receive 50% off your entire stay. That's INCREDIBLE!

“Great location and service- needs remodelling” Arrival experience: Great staff. Very attentive and friendly. Room (general): Huge suite (room 1012). Full kitchen (full size refrigerator, oven, dishwasher), living room and two bedrooms and two bathrooms. Furniture was worn and old. This hotel is in major need of a remodel, but the location and size of the room makes it tolerable. Bathrooms: Good size, old fixtures, in poor condition. Wallpaper peeling and some mildew. Bed: OK bed. Housekeeping: Above average. Leave a tip, and the housekeeping staff really takes care of the room. Restaurants: n/a but free breakfast in the morning. Bar: n/a. Grounds: n/a. Pool: n/a Staff attitude/service: excellent and very helpful. Perks for status: Free breakfast and room upgrade to a suite. Parking: Available but took the Metro instead. For some high-res photos of this hotel, check out my photos on Flickr. My username on Flickr is utfiero.

“Good for the price. Small rooms though” Look, it's a Fairfield Inn and that makes it one of Marriott's lowest end property. I usually only like to stay at Courtyard and above, but I knew this was a newer property so I gave it a chance. Place is very clean, with a Fridays connected to it. So that was nice. The rooms were tiny but modern with a new 32" flat screen TV. I stayed in a room with two beds, and they were double beds, not queens. I would not want to stay in a room this small with an extra person as it would be crowded. Not a lot of frills, but clean, new and a good value. There is a Courtyard next store and I would probably elect to stay there next time as I prefer a larger room. I pricelined this room and got is 2.5 stars for $45 a night.

“Great Location!” Had a great stay at the Omni Chicago! The staff was very friendly and you can't beat the location! Also, the rooms were clean, quiet and really comfortable. They do look a little tired as other have mentioned. I'm OK with it especially since I got such a good deal... if I would have paid the published rate, it would have been a bit disappointing.

“Nice, upscale business hotel” Stayed three nights for business meeting. Our room was in the tower. Very spacious room with two double beds. Bathroom was large with two sinks and plenty of countertop and storage. Small coffee maker, fridge and safe in room. Large closet. Parking was free with our meeting but it looks like they normally charge $17/night for self-park. Short drive or taxi ride to downtown Dallas with many restaurants to choose from. Our favorites were Trulock's for nice dinner and Sonny Bryan's on Inwood for BBQ lunch. We paid $18 extra a night for access to executive lounge on 25th floor. Nice quiet spot for continental breakfast in morning and snacks in the afternoon.

“Decent” Stayed one night - not a bad hotel. Rooms large, clean, plenty of light, good water pressure, quiet, nice location.
