The staff - not "overly friendly" - especially Erin at the front desk and it would have been nice if the staff informed guests during check-in that a shuttle available to local restaurants/shopping. Nice to be swimming in the heated pool during the snowfall. NO vending/ice in the hotel - they give you "a key" for a mini-bar - that could become costly for the guest and a big money maker for the hotel. I'd stay again - but this would not be my first choice of hotel.

“Very Nice hotel, thin walls” I stayed here on a Tuesday night which you would you expect to be somewhat quiet. However, the people in the room next door were somewhat noisy. I had to place earplugs in my ears just to get a good night of sleep. With that said, everything else about the hotel is wonderful. The staff, the rooms, the amenities, and the grounds. I do agree that the restaurant and food is overpriced. I have already recommended the place to friends and I will return. I have stayed at the Peninsula, Mandarin and other top hotels. This is a really nice hotel but not of that scale. Oh, you will definitely need a car since it is a good distance from both IAH and HOU.
“Cool” Nice hotel with easy access to local ammenities. Neato grounds had peacocks and pheasents roaming the area.

“Love it!” This is a great find in NYC. There are a lot of great restaurants around and it was a new neighborhood for me to explore. I had a small cabin the first two nights and paid for an upgrade to a suite the rest of the stay. The suite was big and lovely. Pros: free wifi, a techie's dream, complimentary breakfast or hot one for $9.99, great staff, work rooms and great food. Cons: Staff is a bit overwhelmed and could not anticipate when my room would be ready and kept giving me conflicting information and thanking me for my patience. No room service.

“Great location - great hotel” Loved our stay at the Westin St, Francis. Staff was very helpful and friendly, and the rooms are super modern and clean. nice decor and ambiance. Very much the modern style that "W" hotels are also known for.

“Glitzy lobby but everything else pretty basic” I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights recently with my husband. We had a room on the 20th floor facing the front of the hotel. Initially we were assigned to a room 2 floors below but it was so dark and drab in there given the price were paying, I knew that they could do better. Our stay was just okay. The worst part about the room is that the walls are pretty thin, we could hear everything that was going on with our neighbours next door including a nasty fight they were having at 2 o'clock one morning. The room was spacious by NYC standards but the bathroom was woefully inadequate with very little if any place to store our toilettries and it was a hit and miss in terms of getting hot water in the shower. We did not eat at any of the restaurants in the hotel so I cannot comment. The location of the hotel is first class and that is probably its best feature. I definetly do not think this hotel is value for money when paying full price, and the only way I would stay there again is if I copped a deal on Priceline.

“Indepently owned. And it shows!” At the risk of gilding the lily, I must join the legions who have remarked about their positive experiences at the Old Town Inn. I arrived in San Diego with a reservation for one night only. I was anticipating having to return to the city two weeks later for two additional nights, but hadn't made any plans about where I'd stay upon returning; figuring I could figure that out once I was in California. I'd looked at lots of San Diego hotels on-line before I went west, and wasn't satisfied that I'd found something that covered all the bases for a reasonable price. One night staying at the Old Town Inn, however, convinced me of the obvious wisdom of making a reservation to return there when I came back into town. The location is a big part of its appeal: handy to the airport, walkable to the Blue Line Trolley and Historic Old Town with its restaurants and shopping, easy nearby access to I-5, I-8, Point Loma, Presidio Hill Park, Mission Beach, Sea World, downtown. The hotel's own service and amenities are also nothing to sneeze at, with charming flower-filled grounds, beautiful pool, friendly and eager-to-help staff. I needed border-crossing advice for a trolley visit to Tijuana. Done. I needed directions for getting to Cabrillo National Monument. Done. I needed an early-morning wake-up and ride to the airport. Done...and not just a taxi, but a Town Car that charged me a flat fare ($16) and was waiting for me ten minutes PRIOR to when I needed it. The rooms are smaller than a standard chain hotel-by-the-Interstate room. But both of mine were clean, comfortable and quiet, despite being adjacent to a multi-lane road. I'd eagerly return to the Old Town Inn. It's value is unbeatable.

“4th visit & still perfect!” I stayed at the Sofitel 8/17-8/21 with my mother. This was our fourth stay at the hotel in the past two years and like the others, it was perfect. We didn’t have any major complaints. We will definitely return. Our room was nice and our beds were super comfy. The hotel is soooo quiet! Even at night. They have changed their bedding somewhat so it was a bit odd because instead of having a top sheet on your bed you just had a thick, down comforter. As luxurious as it was it was WAY to warm of something to sleep with in August so we requested “regular” sheets and housekeeping complied. Also, housekeeping kept shorting us on towels and wash cloths but they gladly brought extras up when I called. I’ve never mentioned it before, but the lobby has a very nice seating area . It’s a great place to wait after you’ve checked out and you still have time before heading to the airport. There’s free internet access off that part of the lobby too. Also, I would recommend the Red Flame Diner just down the sidewalk for breakfast, lunch or dinner. We headed there every morning and got excellent food and service.

“Close to everything!” The hotel is close to the stadium, the arena and the convention center. There are lots of food and entertainment options within a very short walk. The bathrooms are very small, but there is lots of water pressure in the shower (so much that it almost hurts). Front desk staff very friendly and helpful. The maid halfway made up our room one day, replaced towels, but did not make up beds or leave coffee. Lots of good free starbucks coffee in the lobby! Would stay again! Hotel staff wants to make guest happy and comfortable!

“Awesome Stephen F.” We booked a standard queen room via Priceline for 90 US dollars, but upgraded to a deluxe king on the Continental Club Floor for an additional 59 US dollars. Well worth the upgrade. The room was palatial and spotless with a beautiful large bathroom and the most comfortable bed and pillows I’ve ever slept on anywhere. Two large windows overlooked 7th Street yet we did not experience any street noise at night. There was construction in the area, but it didn’t crank up until about 8:30 am. Rooms on the Club level came with access to the Continental Club room, which in the morning served a fabulous upscale Continental Breakfast, all day soft drinks and bottled water, evening hors d'oeuvres and top shelf cocktails. Factor in the cost of breakfast and drinks in the hotel bar or outside of the hotel and it was well worth it to us. The desk staff was a bit on the snooty side, the 25.00 a day valet charge was steep, but the most awesome and helpful bellhops and valets ever experienced made the cost more palatable. Hotel is on the corner of Congress and 7th with a view of the Capitol Building from the 2nd floor terrace. There is only a tiny lap pool and a Jacuzzi in the basement. Very damp and hot down there, but the workout room was great and well equipped. The only drawback we experienced was not of the hotel's doing. Downtown Austin has a severe homeless problem. They gathered, slept, argued, panhandled, screamed and shouted at the bus stop on the adjacent corner of the hotel. You could not walk anywhere without being hassled, and it was a bit scary to walk from 6th Street after 10:00 pm. We would stay here again in a heartbeat if the price was under 175.00 dollars for the same level of accommodation.

“Superb location” Had a room with two queens, not a large room, only chair in room was desk chair, very comfy beds, 24 hour coffee in lobby, only about 7 or 8 rooms per floor very quiet. Easy walk to Broadway area, or just hang out in Bryant Park.

“Small rooms at the Hudson, but not terrible experience” booked three nights here in with my husband through a deal on Travelzoo. first impressions: great staff, attentive and helpful. great lobby. DARK hallways. TINY - but clean - room. you can tell it's a converted Y. I don't know why they decided that dark grey carpet and dark grey walls were a good way to go for their long tunnel-like hallways - but that's the way it is. After reading reviews here, I knew the room would be small, and it was, complete with a tiny 13-inch television. No refrigerated mini-bar. TINY, CRAMPED BATHROOM. If you weigh over 180lbs or have long legs, be prepared for a struggle to use the bathroom. Thankfully, my husband and I are both average height and weight, but even so, I found myself sitting sideways to use the commode because my knees were literally two inches from the wall when I sat down. Yes, the glass wall between shower and bedroom is there, but that novelty lasts for about oh - two seconds - before you wish that the shower floor drained water better and that there was more space in that teeny tiny bathroom. There is free internet, windows are not sound-proofed, and there is a big, loud party every night downstairs in the bar/club. We could not hear the party, but we could hear the street noise, and we were on the 10th floor. Still - I would still consider staying here again. Why? because if you are prepared for these considerations (tiny rooms, dark hallways) because for the price we paid, ($229 a night), you will find that the best part of the Hudson is not the hotel itself, but ITS LOCATION. it was a bargain to stay in this neighborhood - COLUMBUS CIRCLE is a great location, and close to all the trains, Broadway, Rockefeller Center, CENTRAL PARK IS RIGHT THERE... and the neighborhood is a safe walking area at night. You also have a CVS that is open 24 hours kitty corner on 9th Avenue, and the Time-Warner center with the Whole Foods just down the block. You can't beat the location, so for this reason, the Hudson Hotel redeems itself.

“Location. space, peace and quiet, at a cost” Got a good 3 nights for 2 (6 nights for 4 in fact) deal on a junior suite. Even with that this is an expensive hotel. But you are smack in Midtown between 5th and 6th, and a few minutes walk from most of the major subway lines. Our junior suite on the 26th floor had a sizeable lounge separated from the bedroom by a short corridor, the bedroom had a grandstand view of the Empire State and Chrysler buildings. Big bathroom, separate shower, no skimping on the L'Occitaine toiletries. And it's QUIET. We've done the Times Square stay twice and there's no getting away from the fact that's noisy. Times Square is less than 5 minutes walk away, and yet the Sofitel is an oasis of calm. Didn't do breakfast in the hotel ($54 for 2 is not cheap): I'd recommend Gregory's Coffee over the road or the Red Flame diner a few doors up. Decent gym (24 hours). Free internet (you may need to be patient though) in the lobby. Staff are polite and helpful. Beware the compulsory 15% service charge in the bar: it's not made clear up front. At these prices you may as well schlep along the road to the Algonquin, who do better cocktails. Overall: great room, much more space than most midtown hotels. great view, but pricey. Brilliant location. Go room only and get the best deal you can. It's the best hotel by a long way of those I've stayed in in New York. Highly recommended.

“Beautiful, historical hotel -- excellent food” Our national sales meeting was held at the Adolphus in January. At first, I was leery of the hotel based on the reviews posted here. However, after four days of constant meetings, I was pleasantly surprised by the level of service and the overall feel of the hotel. First, this is not a brand-new hotel. There will be some quirks to it, which perhaps is some of its charm. Check-in was pleasant, although I was surprised that no one offered to help me with my baggage until after I had trekked up the short escalator to get the elevators for my room. I stayed on the 8th floor and was a bit confused trying to find my room. The halls are winding and, if you look at the evacuation plans posted near the elevator, it seems as if each room on the floor has it's own shape/size. I stayed in a double room, which was a nice size for a downtown hotel. What made it special was the walk-in closet. Since we had to share rooms with our co-workers, an extra changing area/storage space was most welcome. Sure, the carpeting was a bit run down, but the rest of the furniture was okay and spread out enough so it didn't feel entirely crowded. The bathroom was a decent size with plenty of towels. The counter was big enough for us to share with all our toiletries. Housekeeping did a nice job of keeping our room clean. Since I was on business, the internet was vital and it was nice to (finally) have wireless that didn't cost $$ per day to access. Our meeting rooms were in the grand ballroom as well as the mezzanine levels. Again, it is tricky to navigate the floors and the elevators, especially if you are lugging equipment (or even your laptop roller case) from session to session. If you are planning a meeting here, be sure to bring plenty of signs to direct your attendees to the right rooms. Again, navigation can get a bit tricky to the meeting rooms. The banquet staff was outstanding as was the food. For our three day meeting, it was the best hotel buffets (breakfast, lunch and dinner) that I have ever had! Everything tasted fresh and full of flavor, and the staff was very attentive in clearing dishes and keeping coffee cups filled. Except for the first day, when we had a half-morning general session and we kept running out of coffee in the meeting room, the service was on point. The business center was decently equipped and, thankfully, had an attendent. Everything was automated through a touch-screen terminal. You have to swipe your credit card and then select what you want to use (fax, copier, computer). You were charged by the minute instead of say, per page, which in some ways is better than being charged per page for a fax (I once spent $50 on an outgoing 50-page fax because it HAD to go). Incoming faxes, however, were sent to the bellstand instead of the front desk, and I had to wait several minutes until someone showed up and I could get my faxes. After that, they began delivering them right to my room. Since we were there during the NFL playoffs, we crowded into the hotel bar to watch the last few minutes of the football game. One bartender was super-friendly and helpful; the other bartender was obviously in a bad mood, since she ignored several of us until she was ready. Also, when I ordered a round of drinks, she informed me somewhat nastily that what I was ordering was very expensive. While on one level, I appreciated the alert that the drinks were expensive, but her angry attitude was completely off-putting. Our awards dinner was held in the French Room, which was rated as the #1 hotel restaurant in the US by Zagat. It was an incredible experience and the food and service were absolutely outstanding. Finally, check out was easy and the staff eager to help me with my bags (unlike when I checked in). Overall, I had a pleasant stay.

“Very good base in Philadelphia” We stayed here for a weekend of sightseeing, with our three children in connecting double bedded rooms. This is a fine central location, next to the glorious city hall and Reading Terminal Food Market (fantastic -- don't pay for Marriott breakfast, go there to eat anything you like!) It's walking distance to all the historical sites and Rittenhouse Square area. The hotel is set back a bit, so there was a nice bright view of surrounding buildings outside our window, and it was quiet for sleeping. The rooms were clean and upbeat -- good Marriott beds, etc. My only complaint is that in spite of our "preferences" in our Marriott reservation, no rooms were assigned until we actually arrived -- ie, if there had been no connecting rooms left at the moment we arrived, we would have been separated from our children. (I have found the same problem before and often call the front desk a day in advance to have them block rooms; still, what is the point of the hotel asking for our preferences if they don't actually use them until we ask for them again at check in??)

“Best location in Boston, nice rooms too” Location near all the shops and nightlife is a plus. We were also given a nice room way up top so we were able to see the Boston skyline. This is a large hotel so it was busy while we were here this summer. Since they have so many rooms, everyone's experiences will be a little different but we were lucky to be given one of the nicer rooms with a nice view. The beds were comfortable, the room spacious, and bath was clean - all that we need. The metro is also convenient in the shopping areas nearby. Everything is within walking distance so we didn't even need a car. Overall a great stay.

“Great Location!!” If you can afford it, stay here!! The rooms are pretty expensive ($270+ a night) but it's worth it to able to walk out of your hotel right into Times Square!! This hotel is near top notch restaurants, the theatre district, and the subway is not a far walk at all. The rooms are of average size. It's a huge place and pretty busy. The staff was always very helpful. The restaurant in the hotel is pretty expensive so I would try some of the local cuisine if you are up for walking before I spend my money here. I hope to go back soon!!

“Read This Before You Book” I had high expectations for the "Hotel California," maybe so high that they couldn't be met. If you're looking for a hotel with NO hot water, this is the place for you! But I have to say, a nice cold shower after attempting to sleep in a sweltering room was nice. See, they have no air conditioning. Just a ceiling fan! If you get to hot, be sure to open a window so you can hear the serenades of homeless people peeing on the street and yelling at their imaginary friends. Hotel room was filthy! I found no less than 4 socks underneath the bed. Did I mention the socks weren't mine? So, no hot water, no air conditioning, but they do compensate you with used socks.

“Looking forward to my return” I must admit that I was super-hyped about staying here since we scored an unbelievable rate for the Memorial Day weekend, not to mention that it’s a brand new property. Sometimes that can lead to disappointment, but not so much in this case. For it to be a holiday weekend I expected the hotel to be bursting at the seams (especially since it's rated so high on TA) but surprising only saw a few guests come & go while we were in the common areas. We felt as though we had the hotel to ourselves since we always rode the elevator alone...we sat at the hotel's bar alone (kudos to bartender Ashley - so friendly & genuine). And we never had to wait for the Apple desktops located in the lobby (bonus since we left our laptops at home). We reserved a Queen room on the 13th floor and although it’s tiny, it’s fine for an intimate weekend for 2, and it’s comparable to other standard rooms in NYC. No view (didn’t expect one since we’re on a lower floor) and very quiet. If thinking of booking the Queen rooms please note there isn’t much room between the foot of the bed and the wall. Also, pack light since there’s limited storage space. The room comes with an iron, a mini ironing board, docking station and a hair dryer. Location wasn’t a problem for us and very convenient to public transit. We even caught the E Train/Q33 Bus back to LGA since it was so convenient and we were traveling light. I read that there’s a probation office on that block but I never saw it. The adult stores are there but I’ve stumbled upon those on other blocks in Midtown and there wasn’t anything overtly offensive; but I understand the concern if travelling with the little ones. I would like to rate this hotel a 4.5, falling between very good and excellent but it’s not an option. On my next getaway I will definitely plan to stay here again and I’m already telling my friends to check it out if given the opportunity.

“Suite was long with a surprisingly full kitchen, bed comfy.” Located in walking distance of GWU, this hotel was very comfortable and upgraded me to a suite. The room had a waffle robe, but no slippers. There was a full kitchen which means there was a stove, a microwave, a 3/4 fridge, and a dishwasher, sink, and coffee maker. There was no minibar or drinking water in the room. Room and bath were clean. Watched movies but at $17 a pop were too pricy. Added touch, free shoe shine if you hung them on your door before midnight. Late check-out meant only one additional hour without charge. Front desk was friendly, cheerful as we're doormen. Restaurant in lobby. Amenities were not special, but Zi liked the citrus-scented bath soap.

“A gem of a hotel” Stayed at the Embassy Suites Riverwalk for 3 nights and would definitely stay there again if returning to San Antonio. The room was huge, clean and quiet. I was at the very end of the hall on the 14th floor and couldn't hear any of my neighbors. There was a large living room area that included: the sink, microwave, fridge, table, couch, and flat screen TV. It was such a nicely laid out space that made you feel at home and gave you some room to work and sit and not feel like you are constantly in your bedroom. Plus, I never heard the refrigerator making noise during the night because I was able to close the bedroom door. The bedroom was very large and had a small desk and another flat screen TV and ample drawer/closet space. The bathroom was clean, well lit and had a great walk in shower. The free breakfast at the hotel is wonderful. They have an excellent selection of hot, made to order food as well as cereals, bagels and fruit. Plus they have really good coffee which is rare at most complimentary breakfasts. The front desk staff were extremely friendly and were very enthusiastic about helping with directions. A staff member even walked out of the hotel with me to show me where to pick up the trolley. After a few days in San Antonio, you may get tired of tex mex and BBQ so think about eating at Luke's, the restaurant attached to the hotel. It serves amazing German food. I had one of the best meals of my entire trip there. Wonderful spatzle and schnitzel. The hotel is very convenient to all things San Antonio. The Riverwalk is right outside, Houston street has lovely shops and restaurants and leads you straight to the Alamo or to the Mercado depending in which way you go. Plus, you can hop on one of the city trolleys right outside of the hotel if you are tired from walking. Parking is the only downside to the hotel. Parking is always a bit pricey the closer you get to the Riverwalk, but you only have the option to valet park at the Embassy Suites. You do get in and out privileges and my car was always ready when I needed it and in great condition so no complaints there. Overall, I really enjoyed my stay. It was comfortable, convenient, clean and relaxing. I would definitely suggest it to anyone headed to San Antonio.

“Nice view, close to trains” I've stayed at the Holiday Inn Mart Plaza twice and was impressed. The hotel is on top of the Chicago Sun Times building, so all the rooms are on "high floors." Priority Club members get a $5 off coupon towards breakfast or parking. I used it for breakfast which was quite decent. If you take the train, your best bet is the Brown line. Get off at Merchandise Mart, walk through the building, take an escalator down to ground level and then the hotel elevator up to 15th floor. I don't remember many signs, so you might get lost. But at least you're insulated from the heat or cold (depending on time of year). The Brown line is convenient to the Loop as well as the Lakeview/N. Halsted area. Connect at Clark St station for the Blue line to/from O'Hare or Orange line to/from Midway. If you don't have much luggage you can't beat $2. For N. Michigan Ave, you can walk, take Bus 125 or a taxi ($7-10). There's a business center but they charge for internet. You can also use the TV internet for a fee. But, for simple e-mail and net surfing, head over to the Apple Store on N. Michigan Ave and do it for free! There's a Starbucks, Klay Oven Indian restaurant, and a pharmacy down the block on N. Orleans, as well as several places in the merchandise mart for a quick bite.

“Nice place close to airport” Just had a one-night stay and needed to be close to airport for 0600 departure. The place was clean and friendly. Checked in just in time for the hamburger/hot dog dinner buffet. Just what was needed after a long day of work and I did not feel like going out to a restaurant. Very early the next morning, the complimentary airport shuttle was waiting for me.

“Best Hotel. Great fitness center.” You have to stay here. It had one of the most friendliest staff in any hotel. They actually decline tips. Service is first here. We stayed in a huge suite that is bigger than most people's apartments. Everything about this hotel is upscale. The fitness center has more equipment than most. Even a yoga room. The location is ok. Was a bit challenging finding cabs. But nothing really bad enough to not stay here. A must while visiting Chicago.

“Courteous Service” I had the fortune of staying at this Embassy Suites as a layover. This hotel in currently one of the closest in the Hilton family to DIA (about 10 minutes via free shuttle). The hotel was well maintained and appeared to be recently updated. The compimentary breakfast was served as planned. For those early departures, there is a continental breakfast bar available starting at 4:30am. Be sure to sign up for the return airport shuttle ride as it fills up quickly! HHonors benefit (diamond): internet access + two bottles of water.

“Camere minuscole, ascensore lento, corridoi claustrofobici. Sconsigliato” La mia esperienza è stata negativa, la stanza era decisamente angusta e rumorosa. Pulizia appena sufficiente. Arredamento nuovo. Personale cortese, ma non ha risolto il problema della camera. Ascensore di una lentezza snervante, e i corrodi talmente stretti che la valigia passava a malapena. Posizione ottima, un paio di blocchi sopra al Madison Sq. Park.

“It's noisy, dirty, and the staff goes back on their word.” I came in town for a marathon and was told I could have a late check-out and when I got there, their story changed and I had to be out by Noon at the latest. I managed to negotiate 1 pm with the manager after putting up a fight. Other issues: Bathtub too big for bathroom. It was poking through the walls. Window sills not clean. There were bugs all over them. Very noisy. I was up every hour due to the street noise or maids in the hallway speaking Spanish to each other.

“Good hotel but not upto standards of other Renaissance properties” Rooms are a mix of the 80's/90's/ and the 2000's ( layout 80's/bathroom 90's/room de-core 2005/ tv's 2009). Hotel is close to ,many of the fun areas of Houston ( rice village/galleria) but they all require a car or cab to get to. On the plus side they have a full service Starbucks in the lobby, the best concierge staff in the city, and a full food court in the underground office complex which is attached to the hotel. The Renaissance houston is a nice property but not on par with the majority of the other renaissance properties and more inline with a marriott/sheraton.

“Would Not Stay Here Again” Check in was ok with no problems. The room was clean and neat. There was an air purifier on the ceiling in the hallway that made a electrical crackling sound each time we walked under it that scared my 8 year old. Maid service was spotty at best. The breakfast was ok in the mornings but at times no place to sit. Check out was not good at all. We had a $42.00 refund due and I stood at the front desk for 20 minutes waiting for the clerk to complete the refund. Our cab was waiting and I was told I had to sign something. The general manager came over and even then the clerk could not figure out the way to check me out. I had to leave as our train was getting ready to leave soon. I do not advise walking at night with small children in this area. It is close to the Space Needle. About a 15 minute walk. I would not stay here again due to location and service issues.

“Good Choice for LAX not for LA” I stayed here for 4 nights. I wanted to be in the LA area but most hotels wanted a lot of money for rooms and many only had valet. I didn't want to spend a fortune. Room was a bit small. Cleaning was iffy-some days we got coffee, some we had to ask, same with other items. Even though hotel is on the flight path we did not hear much plane noise, our a/c was sort of loud and we either were too cold or too hot. If I were going to LA again, I would just pay the money and stay where the action is, but to get to LAX this was very convenient. If you go up Sepulveda a few miles there are many dining options but really nothing right near (other than Burger King). Had breakfast at the restaurant one morning (pricey), just ended up getting Randy's donuts (overrated) for the rest. Self parking garage was good, but we got locked out the morning we were checking out, thank goodness the valet guy let us out. To me, that's really not acceptable since it wasn't close to checkout time. I think others had the same issue, because I got stuck behind a couple of cars on previous days. Fitness center was nice and pool may be small but it's nice. Hotel has shuttle service to LAX every 20 minutes but it looked crowded when we left (we took our rental earlier since rental locations are close) so we ended up getting a taxi, which only cost $8.

“Very clean, good location, excellent service, top health club ameneties” This hotel is putting the finishing touches on being remodeled, there's fresh paint and a place or two where they're doing some work. I didn't have any problem with noise at all, and it really is just a few places where you even notice they're finishing things up. The decor is updated and everything is new. That does mean, though, that they're not quite a Doubletree yet, so it's true, they don't have cookies yet, and I couldn't get our stay registered for points. These and the lack of free wi-fi are the only downsides of staying here. Its a quick walk to Michigan Ave, and very close to a grocery store and a couple of really nice places to have breakfast and coffee, beyond the bagel shop attached to the hotel. Great location. This time we didn't bring our car, instead we flew and rented a zip car, and the zip car is located near the hotel, too. More points for location! The rooms are nicely laid out, with plenty of seating, good for relaxing in the room. The decor is all updated and contemporary, and the bathroom is well-lit with attractive granite countertops. Great shower and lots of fluffy towels. I have to mention how great the service is. The blankets are down blankets, and when I told housekeeping that I preferred something other than down, they were fast and friendly about remaking the bed with fresh bedding. The housekeeper even came by to check in later and ask if the remade bedding looked alright. There's a great health club, with exercise machines and a terrific pool attached to his hotel, and a decent service center where you can use the internet if you'd rather not pay the $10 for internet access in your room. But you can also get free wi-fi all over the city, including at the contemporary museum of art, which is a 10 minute walk away. I booked the stay online at a decent discount, and if you can get your stay for a reasonable price, the location, cleanliness, updated contemporary style, nice health club amenities, really excellent service make this a good all-round hotel for visiting Chicago.

“American Girl Dream” We just returned from 4 nights at The Fitzpatrick with our 2 daughters, ages 10 and 8. I had found a family package on the hotel's web site for a King suite for $219. The package included the suite, a buffet breakfast, free movie and a $50 gift certificate for American Girl Place. The suite on the 28th floor was spectacular...14 foot ceilings, beautiful decor and a fantastic view. I stayed in a suite at The Venetian in Las Vegas about 6 weeks ago and I thought the suite at the Fitzpartick was even nicer, except for the bathroom which was too small for a suite this size. The hotel is only 1 1/2 blocks from American Girl Place which we visited every day during our stay. The staff is friendly, especially in the dining room. We would definitley stay there again.

“Gigantic rooms, Pet-friendly!” Stayed here with my husband and our two small dogs during New Year's Eve 2012 in a junior suite. The suite was incredibly spacious and clean (including the bathroom) and the location was perfect. The bed was soft and comfortable and there was more than enough room for the dogs to run around. The suite had a little entry area, separate sitting area with desk and a television, and the bedroom was very large with an attached dressing area that led into the bathroom (which has another door leading from the entry). Only minor complaint was that we had to wait about 15 minutes to check in (our room was not ready) and the front desk gave us complimentary drink coupons for the hotel bar while we were waiting. Having stayed here and Hotel Palomar (in a deluxe one bedroom suite) across the street during the prior New Year's Even, we would choose Sofitel for the size of the rooms and overall value.

“Not for me, but a nice enough hotel” I’m not a huge fan of this hotel, it’s fine for a night of business if you have a meeting close by. I stayed at this hotel on Business for 2 nights. It seems pleasant, the staff we good. The bar downstairs was quite lively and nice. The hotel is set on a business park and there are no shops or restaurants within 1⁄2 mile, probably closer to a mile, some would say reasonably typical of LA. That’s not ideal for me, I prefer to be able to easily walk to a coffee shop. The rooms were ok and probably refurbished 2 or 3 years ago. Balconies but no real view. For me, I won’t stay again, I want things to be a little closer.

“We love all the Kimpton Hotels we have stayed in” We stayed here for a few days at the end of August as a base for our short break to Washington D.C. and we loved it. HUGE room on the top floor with views of Washington and the Monument. The windows in our room were floor to ceiling and wall to wall. It was great sitting with a glass of wine or cup of coffee and watch the sun go down over DC. We used the pool (which was pretty cold) and had cookies and milk sent to the room every night for our kids. All in all a great stay and while the Nine Zero in Boston and Argonaut in San Fran remain our fav of the Kimpton hotels, we would not hesitate to stay here again when in DC

“Close to Airport” I would only recommend this for travelers who need to be close to the airport for an early flight. We've stayed here several times after staying in Monterey when we've had a flight out of San Jose at 7 am. But other than that, I do not recommend it. It's a bit expensive and hard to believe that it rates 4 diamonds from AAA. The service is lackadaisacal at best. Our room was hard to find and I could barely get the desk clerk to give me directions. The $18 you pay for parking (in a nearly empty self-serve lot) is completely ridiculous. Also, the Sunday night Detox party might be appealing to some, but it left us with a rather seedy impression of the place. When we pulled up, there were a lot of police officers in the lobby and they appeared to be interrogating party goers or dealing with some sort of altercation. Bikini-clad young women roaming the halls and elevators might attract a certain clientele, but the first time we stayed here, we didn't realize it was a party and I wondered if they were prostitutes. All in all, sort of a "party hard", seedy, Vegas-like atmosphere.

“A True Find!” I really enjoyed my stay at Hotel 41. It is clean, attractive, perfectly located and modern. My boyfriend and I decided to spend a night in the city so we could both have a few drinks and relax instead of making the trip back to CT. I looked at many different web sites and found Hotel 41 for 129.00 on expedia. The reviews here are all right on the money - the rooms are small but really nice. The staff was very friendly, we got a free bottle of water when we checked in and a free ny times in the morning. I was a little nervous that it would be noisy as it is in the middle of times square but I never heard a peep, except for noise from the hallway. If I had to say something negative about it I would say that the tv is small, far away from the bed and too high up for serious viewing but since we were only there for one night it didnt really matter to us. I also would prefer to have had a fan in the bathroom. I recommend it highly and will definitely stay there again, you cant beat it for the money!

“Great location and great place” saw a 3 nights for the price of two promotion and booked. Saw another promotion on Travelzoo for $115 per night in August, could not beat that and booked. Arrived via the blue train and got lost. Tons of cabs and rode the cab four minutes to the hotel. It's noon and I wanted to check my bag because I scored a ticket to Wrigley on a Sunday. I'm standing in line for the desk when I spot two bellman walk onto the lobby. Tell the guy my situation and boom, claim ticket and down to the Red Line, off to see the Cubbies. Back to the hotel after 5pm and checkin not problem, in fact I think they pre assigned rooms, king non smoking. Same room design as my last stay, clean except for the drinking glasses. Microwave, mini fridge and comp pass to a real fitness gym one block away. Jewels grocery across the street. Rental car not needed as public transit is pretty fast. Did rent a car the last day to drive outside of downtown and returned by 5pm. Scored a parking meter one block away from the hotel, leaving by 7am, so free all night. Second stay in this city at this hotel. My third will be here too.

“First time at a Sheraton and am impressed!” Stayed a Saturday night. Location is great! 5 minute walk to La Villita and Riverwalk, few more minutes to Hemisphere Park and Rivercenter Mall. Check in & out was friendly and fast. Lobby was nice with coffee shop/deli, breakfast area and bar with flat screen. Didn't try breakfast because there was a charge. Also a charge for parking, which the lot was small but they had extra in the lot next door. Room was immaculately clean and actually too big for us. We never used the seperate sitting area. A/c, 2 flatscreens, free bottled water, microwave, fridge and lighting were all very nice. No view. The best thing by far was the amazing bed and pillows. I wanted to stay an extra night just to sleep. Would have given this 5 stars if parking and breakfast were included in the price, but for cleanliness and location, you can't beat this in SA downtown.

“Great Hotel, Great Value” Just a one night stay this time at the Cosmo, as I stayed at a different hotel for the best part of a week. However, I have to say, I probably won't stray away from this hotel. Checked in shortly after 11am, and my room was ready, and got a nice upgrade to a room that was bigger, street view (which i prefer, as noise does NOT bother me). Ice delivered to my room which is always nice, and friendly staff, who looked after my luggage for no charge for about 6 hours, while i did some shopping, and had lunch before departed to the airport. I've reviewed this hotel before, but keep coming back to the same place, and it's kinda nice that nothing changes about it, I know what to expect, and it's always a great stay. The area it is in, makes it probably one of the best hotels in NYC in my opinion. I stayed midtown east earlier the same week, and there really isn't much around there, apart from hotels, and more hotels, and overpriced restaurants, attached to hotels... the beauty about the corner of Chambers and W Broadway is that you have mudville 9 across the road for food and beers, and just a block away on Reade St, you have the Reade Street Bar & Kitchen, for much the same. Also, Morgans Deli is a great place for breakfast, just grab it, and head back to your room.. Excellent stay and can't wait til my next stay there in September!!!

“Another Great Experience + Travel Duck Tips” We recently stayed at the Grand Hyatt San Diego for the second time and had a great experience. Let's get right to the Travel Duck tips: 1. There are two towers - the Seaport Tower (built 2004) and Harbor Tower (built 1992). I have stayed in both towers and highly recommend the newer Seaport Tower. The front desk person was very helpful in finding us a room with a great view in the Seaport Tower. 2. The hotel charges $20/day for self park and $28/day for valet. Self Park is a pain as you have to go to at least the third level to find a spot. I would choose valet next time for the extra few bucks a day. 3. In San Diego, you must have a "fish taco." I recommend Baja Rockin Lobster in the GasLamp district on 5th Street. 4. For the best breakfast in San Diego, try Kona's on Pacific Beach at the Pier. The line is long but moves quick. and you will be full all morning. 5. There are often long lines at the hotel upon check in. However, if you are a Gold Passport member you can go to a special line - saves precious beach time. 6. You can walk from the hotel to Gas Lamp district (10 minutes); Petco Park (15 minutes); or Seaport Village (2 minutes). You can also take a bicycle cab - no need to call one since 20 of them will harass you when you leave the front door. 7. The hotel pool is very nice but it was tough to find a chair. Get there early. And, to the nice gentleman smoking a cigar which blew all over the pool area - I suggest the Cigar Bar in Gas Lamp Quarter. 8. I found the bellman from Baltimore (forgot his name) very helpful - he even printed me out directions to In and Out Burger. All the staff were very pleasant. 9. Are you still reading? Aren't you bored yet? If you want more San Diego tips feel free to ask. TD

“Nice hotel, great Chef” I have stayed at this hotel twice. The first time I wasn't as fond of the stay because I was in a very large room by myself. My 2nd stay resulted because the hotel I was to stay in had several rooms flooded from children setting off the sprinklers from having a pillow fight. (Only mention because it caused serious problems for this hotel) My luck was it all worked out, I was in a very quaint room that the bedding was so lush and comfy. The chef prepared great dishes for the days that I was there without garlic due to my allergy. I'm traveling back and look forward to staying again.

“The Best of the Best” I love this hotel. The rooms are so luxurious and they have great views. I've also had the pleasure of being there several times for events and the service has always been top notch. SoHi at the top of the Trump Soho has 360 views -- the lighting in that space is really remarkable. Oh and did I mention the views? Just yesterday I sent my team to Koi for a group dinner and got rave reviews. The food and service were great. They have a private room so it was just perfect. Stop by for a drink. The lobby is very inviting and you may just run into a celebrity!

“Very Good” Quirkily decorated rooms, Fantastically comfortable bed :) Just a short walk from the whitehouse puts this hotel in a nice location - not far from Metro either to connect with Union Station and Metro Centre. All staff very professional, polite, friendly and with great recommendations. Bath deep enough to take an enjoyable one - and the Bath robe for after was a nice touch. Would mosty definately be staying again. Cleaning was to an exceptional standard, and down to doorman and maintenance staff I was made to feel welcome.

“Impressive Hilton stay--best in a while!” I recently stayed 3 nights at the Hilton Austin near the Austin Convention Center for a national conference. For business purposes, I often stay at Hilton and Starwood hotels; for pleasure purposes, I usually stay at Four Seasons and Ritz-Carleton and similar luxury hotels. I must say that the Austin Hilton was the best Hilton stay I've had in many years. First, the hotel is a beautiful, clean, modern property, directly across from the Austin Convention Center. It was also convenient to the University of Texas and most downtown area restaurants, both via walking and via taxi. Second, the service was quite impressive. And trust me--I'm quite demanding and hold any hotel to a high standard for service! I had booked an executive level non-smoking room and knew the hotel to be sold-out for my conference. After a speedy check-in, I got to the room and realize that someone may have previously smoked in the room. I called, and was immediately brought an ionizer to help defuse the smell in the room, as well as a can of room freshener. I was also told they would attempt to switch my room to another if I was still uncomfortable. I couldn't have asked for more. I also needed more hangers, and was promptly brought those. Room service and every other request was handled quickly, diligently, and with a very courteous staff. When I was in the lobby bar and needed directions to a nearby restaurant, the bar manager walked across the hotel with me to the concierge stand to make sure I had a map and clearly marked the directions for me. I was quite impressed. Third, I found the room to be very comfortable. The bed was nice and soft (but not too soft) and the pillows were pleasant, too. I had a nice view of the University of Texas campus/stadium, not that I cared! All in all, I would highly recommend this hotel for an Austin convention stay or to visit the University of Texas. Well done!

“This JW Marriott in the Texas Hill Country is very nice but there is nothing exceptional here except its size” I am writing this as I am staying in the JW Marriott Hill Country. We have been to several JW Marriotts, and this is comparable in many ways. It is definitely Texas size! The outside is rather pedestrian looking. The interior layout is very much like the other JW's but with a Texas flare. It is a bit more rustic and less "flashy" than the JW Desert Ridge, Great Lakes Orlando or Desert Ridge. Keep in mind it has been opened than less than a week. Most of the interior seems to be done, but there is a lot of exterior work to be completed. The staff is friendly but still understandably tentative and unpolished. The food thus far has been very good. Only two restaurants are open at this point, but they are very large and nicely decorated. There are many nice inside and outside seating areas. The soaring Texas limestone fireplaces outside will allow you to stay outside many nights even in the winter. The rooms are decorated with what I call "Texas modern." Indeed, many cows were killed to decorate this hotel. There is leather everywhere. The bathrooms are relatively spacious. Most rooms have a nice balcony. The rooms are nothing incredible but typical JW Marriott. There is no hotel directory in the rooms. The gym is nice with good equipment but like many gyms, it is very hot and stuffy. What differentiates this resort is all the water features. There is a huge lazy river, a large main pool and several water slides. There are countless chaise lounges with comfortable cushions. Best of all, there is a nice adult’s only infinity pool with a fantastic view of the hill country. There is also an adjoining hot tub. It is a great feature to have this adult only oasis considering the hordes of screaming children who are sure to come. The maid service was relatively slow and the turndown service showed up late. The concierge was very friendly and made a great recommendation for a good Thai restaurant. The spa looks large but we did not have a treatment. The spa does have a nice outside pool with comfortable pavilions. The spa also has another fitness center. The grounds will eventually be great once all the plantings mature. There is a gallery of nice shops and a Starbucks which lead to the massive conference rooms. Indeed, this will undoubtedly be a resort that caters almost solely to conference attendees. Of course, the resort hopes to pull in many golfers with the grand and expensive golf course. It is in a nice location as it is not too far off the highway and close to the airport. It is also close to other restaurants and shopping, but because this is Texas, the resort still has plenty of open spaces surrounding it and is in a quiet locale. There is plenty of free parking and the WI-FI is free (even though there is a $20/day resort fee to pay for it.) The essentials are in place for this to be a nice JW Marriott. It will appeal to many people but is still at its core a conference resort. Nonetheless, it is a nice addition to the San Antonio area which has so much to offer.

“Nice, Location kinda is hard.” I surprised my husband with a trip to see Seattle. The W is beauitful, we were checked in quickly and they had a birthday cake for my guy in the room. I was kinda of upset that I asked for a suite and they messed up my room so we ended up with a delux but no biggie. The concierge was helpful but not the best I have had. Room was nice, looks like any W we stayed at. The bar was fun but quiet, had a good late night scene since the tourist wuldnt venture to far at night. Shopping was a walk but the same stores I have in NYC. We did a lot of walking since the location isn't prime but we were okay with that because what better way to see a city. I liked Seattle and the outskirts but the people were very quiet and there were a lot of homeless kids there. I wouldnt go back but would go to Vancouver next time. Maybe just for a couple of days but move on.

“Cheap Chic - FABULOUS CONCEPT !!!” I'm not sure what to say... Other then I love the concept and I think Starwood is on to something big here. I am a Gold SPG member and this was my first visit to an Aloft property. I was impressed with the swanky lobby, funky decor and friendly service at registration. The hotel is a great deal for the price and as long as Starwood keeps it reasonable its a real value. But SPG Gold/Platinum Members beware. This is not a full service property and only room types here are Queen or 2-Dbls. There is no upgrade, there is no recognition other then level key card holder. There is no SPG floor. There is a sign at the front desk. But there is no dedicated check in for Elite Members. Basically they don't really care here weather you are Elite or not. The front desk agent that greeted me with a loud "Aloha Sir" was wearing a Aloft branded polo shirt and khakis with a peace sign pin on his lapel did not really care if I was SPG member or not. If this is part of the concept or not im not sure. If it is its a bold move for SPG which has traditionally valued its elite members more then any other chain. I was really out of by this. Not to mention that at check out my SPG number was not even added to my folio so I was not going to get my points. What you get is a funky, groovy hotel that works. Its a great lobby scene. I stayed for 2 nights and the lobby always had a crowd. Young and energetic. Room was new and very functional. Firm and comfortable bedding. You get 2 bottles of water complimentary each day and there is a refrigerator in each room. The hotel is in a secured compound with two other Starwood property's. Very safe to park at night. Very well lighted and convenient to airport and I-95. Pool and gym are great. Better then some full service hotels. Snacks and fun stuff available for purchase 24 hours a day at reasonable prices. In room amenity's are from Bliss and they are fantastic. The rooms all have a free safe and digital climate control. The A/C is the wall type under the window and while ti works very well. It is very loud. But I guess you can drown it all out with your 42 Inch - wall mounted - LG Plasma TV with surround sound. It was all HD cable and it was awesome. I am concerned that the hotel opened in October and already its showing some tear. My housekeeper did a terrible job of cleaning and the floors in the bathroom you can tell don't get cleaned much. They look ok now because they are new. But this time next year they wont be looking so good at the rate they are going. Carpets in hallways (5th floor - top floor - Is where I stayed) where not vacuumed properly and always had dust and debris. The elevators where not very clean. The door to the back room/office that's opposite the check in pod was always kept open by the night clerk. This looked terrible and really took away from the experience. There are already light bulbs that are being replaced with different bulbs then the original ones used. Also some bulbs are just out. Clearly not a very good maintenance department here. This is a new property and a significant investment or the Starwood brand. I am surprised there is not better upkeep. The service is friendly and relaxed. But don't expect a whole lot. They are always understaffed and have only one person for a 150+ room property at night. This presents a real challenge as this person checks in - answers phones - and does everything. I recommend staying here and checking it out. The concept is awesome. The rooms are comfy. The value is unbeatable. Its just a shame they are not keeping it as clean and well maintained as such a beautiful hotel deserves

“Great experience” Usually one tends to notice when a hotel stay is less than satisfactory but I found myself noticing how much I enjoyed my stay at the Doubletree. Mind I was here for work so there is a limit to one's pleasure but I would like to note that the food in the bar is quite good - when is that ever the case? - the hotel staff exceptionally friendly and helpful; the beds extraordinarily comfortable; the toiletries better than average (giving sunscreen is a great idea! why don't more hotels do this?).

“Nice facility, staff not up to unusual disruptions, convenient but removed” The L'Enfant Plaza" is an interesting choice. On the one hand, the facility is nice, the rooms are large, nicely appointed, and quiet. It's only a few stops from DCA on the metro. Walking from the station to the hotel is all inside so weather is no factor. The hotel is only a short walk from the Washington Mall. That said, it's on the quiet side of the mall which means there's not much entertainment or decent dining within walking distance, but it's all a short cab or metro ride away. The day I arrived, I wanted to check in early to get some work done. Unfortunately, the reservation system was down making it impossible to get a room or a meal. Not a tragedy, of course, but the staff did not deal with this well. I set up in the lobby with cellular internet. So far so good, but when my battery died, the staff was more worried about my cord on the floor. than in suggesting solutions. Hyatts, Hiltons, and Marriotts, in contrast, seem to have better training in this regard. But that's an uncommon occurrence and should not dissuade a stay. This is my fourth stay in two years, mainly because it'soften a good value compared to similar properties in DC. I've noticed, though, that they do not recall prior stays, again a notch below other better properties

“Nice rooms. Terrible service.” The rooms at this hotel are a step over your standard Marriott room and definitely feel more luxurious. No issues with comfort and cleanliness. Location is great whether you're walking or driving (there is a parking garage right across the hotel so you do not have to pay the hotel's inflated valet prices). I did run into problems with a member of the front desk staff who rudely asked me to produce a paper confirmation of the reservation I made on Marriott.com (I have never been asked for a paper confirmation in over 300 nights with Marriott) and threatened to not honor the stay 2 get the 3 night free package I booked. Luckily Marriott customer service solved the situation. Didn't think service at this hotel was up to the standard you expect from Marriott.

“Excellent hotel in the financial district” Most of the well-known hotels in Chicago are found on/near the Magnificent Mile (i.e. North Michigan Ave, just south of Lakeshore Drive) or on/near The Loop (downtown). The JW is on the The Loop, but about a mile (or so) west of the lakeshore and not far from I-94. Theatres and other cultural attractions in the downtown area are also reasonably close to the JW. The rooms, beds and bathrooms are very comfortable. Typical JW Marriott style and quality. There's nothing particularly special about the lobby, but the lobby bar is fantastic. Just what you'd expect in Chicago. I really liked the fitness center and the Concierge Lounge. The fitness center has Life Fitness state of the art equipment. It has everything you would expect of a hotel of this quality and room rate. I didn't wait for anything. The Concierge Lounge was "off the hook". The evening selection of cheeses and other snacks might have been the best I have ever experienced at a hotel concierge lounge. Breakfast in the morning had a superb array of charcuterie, fresh and dried fruit, a few hot items, pastries and breads, and very good coffee. It's everything you would expect of a high-end, JW and more.

“Not at par for the Westin Brand” I recently stayed at the Westin on Market for 5 nights for a conference, being held the Moscone Center. Let me start by saying the first lady we encountered at the front desk was extremely friendly and did her best to make us feel as welcome as possible. She even gave us 2 vouchers for breakfast the next morning. It basically goes downhill from there. The first night we were in a corner room. Extremely small room shaped like a V, with an even smaller bathroom. Although be view was ok, definitely not worth it on the lower floors. The next day they moved us to a Starwood preferred guest floor with a king size bed. The room was a little roomier, with a desk, and 42" LCD TV. The bathroom was a normal size, but no big by any stretch. The room seemed very dated, like it hasn't been renovated in about 15years. The bathroom much the same, not what I expect from a Westin charging upwards of over $300. The sad part is they only gave 2 towels, and 1 piece of soap, again not what I expect for $300 a night. The other things that I find sad is that such an expensive hotel really rapes you when it comes to parking and internet. Internet is about $15/day, and parking is nearly $50 a day, more expensive than the rental car itself. If you are smart, you will park in the parking garage across the street where the parking is $21/day. Using the 1 complimentary breakfast voucher we got, I did enjoy the breakfast buffet at Ducca. The buffet is huge with a large assortment of food and drinks. The other nice thing about the hotel is it is center to all the downtown activities. Moscone center is only 2 blocks away. There is a great breakfast place call The Grove, across the street. There are a multitude of restaurants in the surrounding area. Overall, will likely not stay here again when in SF. If it was $100-150, it would be acceptable. Westin in my mind holds a higher standard, and this hotel does not fulfill that.

“Good Rooms but Poor Shuttle Service” Spent three nights while attending a conference in the hotel. The room was great and the staff was enjoyable. The conference rooms were great and the breakfast at the restaurant was above average. My only complaint would be that they need to be more lenient on the shuttle service. There were 300+ people in town for a convention and they would only do a drop off/pick up at the Galleria every hour. It wasn’t that far but if you showed up at 10 past the hour you had to wait the 50 minutes or pay for a taxi. And the shuttle and the driver would just sit there as well.

“Best Courtyard I have been to!” I have been to many courtyards, and this was by far the best. It was newly remodeled, and it was very modern looking. The rooms were clean and frest, and the lobby was relaxing and nice. The snack/drink bar is a great idea as well as the open business feel. It is within a few blocks of the trendy Easton mall, which has lots of cool restaruants and bars (and shopping). Great hotel for the price - I wish all courtyards could be like this one!
“The staff make it special” Take a great boutique hotel, add a super staff and a good rate, equals one great experience.

“Nice accommodation, not luxury” This is a decent accommodation in Manhattan, not luxury, yet well positioned to walk to Times Square. Tiny rooms, clean. Common areas need better maintenance. Overall recommended, if priced right. Staff member very friendly and welcoming.

“excellent business hotel” My four night stay at this hotel is unusually long for me, so I greatly appreciate the consistently helpful assistance from the staff, including a very early check in. My room had a comfortable and spacious work station as well as a reading chair and excellent lighting. Outlets for electronics were helpful, too. The location was great with the adjacent convention center and good restaurants and other hotels all around. Shopping within walking distance was a mixed blessing as I spent more money than I had planned to spend! Conference rooms for my meetings were well staffed with good food served for breakfast and lunch meetings. I will support this venue within my organization for a return visit for our annual meetings.

“Not the Worse, but Far From the Best” I’ll start with the positives. Location, location, location! If being close to all of the main tourist sites is very important to you, Hotel Mela won’t let you down. It’s literally one block away from Broadway – you can see the Minskoff Theatre from the hotel entrance. The hotel is in Times Square, and one can easily walk a few blocks to other prime areas such as New York Penn Station, the Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden, subway stations, etc. Another plus (for some of you) is that the whole hotel is non-smoking. They also have a gym, but I didn’t get a chance to visit it, so I can’t comment on the condition of it. The bad news is that those are all of the positives that I can say about Hotel Mela. The saying “you get what you pay for,” rung true for me in this experience, and ran through my mind as I checked in. As for the negatives: first, when I arrived to the hotel, a woman in front of me who was leaving had a red face and wet eyes; she was visibly upset and had just finished crying. Someone who looked like the manager was apologetic to her, which let me know that something had definitely gone wrong at this hotel. When it was my turn, he was very nice to me; probably in light of whatever mess had just fallen into his hands beforehand. I was about 45 minutes early for check-in (I’m usually always able to go ahead and get a room, but not here) and he said I could either get a room immediately, a small room with a full-sized bed (he noted that me and my guest would probably have a hard time fitting in the bed, which is strange to me if it’s a regular full size as we are thin individuals) or we could wait until check-in time and get a larger room with two twin beds. His facial expression and tone made the second option sound much better, so I opted for that and checked in my baggage, and then walked around until check-in time. When I got back, he was heading outside to smoke and two others were at the desk; neither of them looked very friendly. A few people were in front of us and I’d never waited so long to check in before. Finally, when it’s my turn, the guy at the desk couldn’t find my information / reservation in the computer. I explained to him that I was just there 45 minutes ago and even signed the necessary papers and provided my credit card for incidentals, yet he still looked perplexed. At least 10-15 minutes had passed when he finally found me in the system, even though the previous guy found me immediately. When I asked what had happened, he acted as if it was of no concern to me since it was cleared up. As far as I’m concerned, you do what the customer asks, no matter what. If they want to know something, then you tell them. He mumbled that my name was misspelled, and wouldn’t answer any more of my questions. When we entered the elevator, we were so pleased (sarcasm) to see the elevators could fit four people max. When we reached our floor (15), I came in contact with that squishy, somewhat dusty looking, thick carpet you find in those boutique hotels who advertise to be so much more than they really are. Upon entering the room, we wondered what the heck the smaller room looked like if this was an upgrade to superior. The aspect that irritated me most about the room is the fact that (well, maybe it’s not a fact, if it’s just me!) the curtains did not pull closed. At night, people can definitely see through the light curtain, and the heavier designed one wouldn’t shut. Who wants to be visible to the hotel across from them?! The room’s cleanliness was so-so. The bathroom shower had a few strands of hair that definitely were not ours, and the television remote was a bit grimey. Mostly small complaints, but nothing shocking as far as the cleanliness. Overall, the room wasn’t too bad, but I wouldn’t have wanted to stay longer than my allotted 2 nights. I didn’t see any bugs in the room or stains on the bed. I did bring my own blanket and laid on it on top of the bed, since I read about bed bugs at Hotel Mela from other reviews (I read about the bugs after I made the reservation). A small inconvenience, but there were not many towels in the bathroom, and the two pillows on each bed were pretty weak, I sank down in them and I wished I’d had another. I even folded two of the rough towels under the pillows to try to prop the pillows up. When the house keeping staff cleaned the room, they one of the decorative pillows on the so-so looking carpet and another on the windowsill, which is was lawbreaker but seemed nonsensical. The bathroom was small, but that’s no shock in many cities. Overall, I wish I’d paid another hundred bucks or so and stayed somewhere better. My goal was to have comfort and savings in NY which didn’t really happen. The street that Hotel Mela is on has other hotels too, and two (Millennium and AKA) looked like they would have been more clean with customer service staff that acts like they care. This experience was lukewarm at best, and confirms for me that this is my last trip trying to salvage a few dollars by staying in one of these types of hotels. I picked it based off the savings compared to other nearby hotels, and the customer reviews, but have to say that for the second time now, the reviews didn’t reflect the full reality. Of course that’s not always the case! I’ve picked plenty of good boutique hotels with the help of reviewers, but not in my last few experiences. Anyway, if you only need the bare minimum, this place will work great for you. If you are used to staying in nice, luxury hotels, and want to save a few bucks in NY, dump your dream. Spend the extra money and bypass Hotel Mela for something better. I know that’s what I’ll be doing next time. I’d rather have peace of mind and a slightly lower bank balance, than a good balance but unsettling feeling in the hotel.

“Location, Location, Location” The Willard Intercontinental is a very nice hotel with probably the best location in Washington DC, just steps from the White House, Ford's Theater, and the National Mall. The are few hotels in the country or perhaps the world with a deeper history. The most impressive part of our stay was the friendliness of the people at the reception desk ... bright, cheerful and helpful. The surley bellmen have lot to learn from them. Our room was large and bright, well-appointed and quiet. The beds were comfortable and the blinds kept the room dark helping us sleep in. After staying at an Hyatt-Andaz Hotel recently, though, I expect more from a $400 per room-night hotel. The charges for internet access and mini-bar are dinosaurs that I no longer expect or accept from a hotel whose rates are stratospherical ....especially as a Priority Club Plastinum member.

“Don't choose this one!” This hotel is oddly arranged with a lobby that has only hard benches. The parking is too expensive. The consierge was not helpful -- no one EVER welcomed us to the hotel. We were not given the type of room we booked, and after playing phone tag with the manager, we were told, "We overbook king rooms, and someone has to be moved." We were offered NOTHING as compensation, not even a free drink. The restaurant on the Riverwalk is very good, and the hotel is near the Rivercenter Mall, but CHOOSE ANOTHER hotel on the Riverwalk and get better service and comfortable rooms!
“What a hotel!” This is a class act of a hotel. I also liked how close it is to Minute Maid. I'm coming out to Houston in April 2009, but I'm not staying here due to the price.

“Very disappointed” I stayed at the hotel for a conference. It was not a pleasant experience. The furniture was old and shabby, both lamps were malfunctioning. My window (Room 3335) was facing some sort of a maintenance facility, may be even a garbage repository. Just awful. The service was even worse even though they charge $20 per day for resort service + $10 for vallet service (to carry one bag) + $3 for maid service. I spent 15 minutes on hold for room service to order breakfast. The bartender at the lounge bar seemed to ignore me completely. And now looking at other reviews i am not surprised. What does surprise me is that several travel magazines rate this as the best property in Arizona. This just shows you how unfair these rankings are.

“Comfortable stay in the midst of Hurricane Sandy!” We travel to Boston often and usually stay in the back bay area, but since we often travel to the north end for the delicious restaurants and pastry shops, we decided to stay closer to that area this time. We stayed for three nights and waited out the Hurricane in the comforts of our nice room here at the Residence Inn. We had a one bedroom and it was quite roomy-Loved the little kitchen, especially the full size fridge seeing that we had to stock up on lots of waters and a little food just in case...My Son loved swimming in the indoor pool and I loved the hot tub. The breakfast was very good with plenty of hot and cold options. We did not get to eat dinner on Monday night because they completely ran out within 30 minutes. It is not very close to the T, about a ten minute walk, but if you get the Trolley tour (which I highly reccomend) it has a stop very close to the hotel at the Navy Yard. The view of the water was beautiful and though it was a bummer to not be able to sight see much this time due to the weather, I was very glad we chose this hotel for this trip because it really was so comfortable and the front desk could not have been more helpful, nice and accomodating. We will be returning again.

“Unable to upgrade” We were welcomed at the Conrad Chicago by the words "we are unable to upgrade you. The hotel is sold out." After a long trip, to say I was disappointed was an understatement. Everytime I passed the check in desk I kept hearing those words. The hotel itself is in a great location for everything. It takes two elevators to get to your room no matter what floor you are on. My room was more than adequate with a large bathroom and separate shower and tub. My wife mentioned she like the Chicago tribune and a Chicago tribune was delivered to our room with a USA today each day we were there. Hotel breakfast is good but expensive. Chicago is the best city in America and there are many good hotel choices. The Conrad is nice.

“Good, not great” Service was quite good, except for the fact that they were not able to fix the a/c properly for 4 days. Rooms & lobby look great, but very little storage space in the room (no drawers, one small closet) or in the bathroom for toiletries, which was pretty uncomfortable. Pretty good value for NYC.

“Da evitare” Attirati dal sito web abbiamo prenotato questo albergo. Nè le parti comuni nè le stanze hanno nulla a che vedere con le foto proposte dal sito. Le camere sono piccole, arredate con mobili vecchi e rotti, uno diverso dall'altro. Bagno piccolo e scomodo, senza neppure un piano d'appoggio. Il servizio è pessimo, lento e scortese. Il personale non risponde neppure al saluto. Pessima pulizia e manutenzione e muri scrostati. Posizione accettabile ma, comunque, non ottimale.

“Stylish, in a great location, friendly.” I stayed here for a business trip (at the convention center), and it was my first time staying in a Kimpton Hotel. Overall I was very pleased--the room decor was very stylish, and the bed very comfortable. Even the bathrobes in the room are stylish (leopard print!). The hotel is centrally located with respect to the Gaslamp, restaurants, shopping, and the convention center, so for this trip it was ideal. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and the free coffee in the lobby was a nice touch. It was also great to have free wireless (if you sign up to be a Kimpton member, which is no cost). I can see how this place would be fun for a leisure trip, but even for a business trip it was great. It was also more reasonably priced than the other hotels in the area.

“What I was looking for” Hotel hallways are oddly decorated, but who cares- the bathroom was roomy, the one bedroom was clean, the bed was comfortable. It's nice- not luxury but very practical. Staff was friendly. The valet car process can be off- putting if you aren't used to it- but i lived in an apartment complex in Chicago that had it so I get it. They were very good about it- ran it well- never had to wait for my car. Oh, and Beverly Hills is not that fancy place that Jethro lived in- looked like a typical neighborhood, although there are nice parts- this is located in a normal part. Factor's Deli across the street is really good.
“Great hotel and service” Ffor any hotel in this price category, $15 per night for WiFi, and $14 for a drink-is just sleazy. And AT&T is almost impossible to make calls from the room.

“I felt safe there.” As a woman traveling alone... I felt safe over night even on the 1st floor with a large window facing the parking lot. I'm not super picky but I need a place to be clean and safe. I booked this room for my first trip for a new job. I checked in around 6 pm. They told me they were having a 'social hour'. It was free wine and beer and some chips and salsa. Nothing great but very nice that they provide this. The hotel is in a great location but I was too tired to go out. The room was very clean, the king size bed was very comfy. In the morning the shower was awesome. No sudden change in the water temp. The breakfast was complimentary. The scrambled eggs were cooked just right. They offered sausage patties, cereal, and pour your own waffles in the shape of the state of Texas. For work I would stay here again.

“Good Location, good Value!” THE QI Downtown Baltimore is in the city center and walking distance to the convention center. Parking garage is right next to the hotel, making it a good option for travelers with own vehicle. The lobby is a bit dated but ok. The staff is very helpful. The rooms are on the small side but clean. The decor is a bit strange with a combination of classic and modern. Walking distance on Charles Street are numerous small restaurants.

“Great hotel in a great location” This is my favorite hotel in El Paso. I visit El Paso on a regular basis for work and have stayed at over 10 hotels in the area. By far this is my favorite but it does have issues. For a hotel that was gutted and rebuilt you would of thought they would have put insulation in the walls. Plan on hearing your neighbors and the sound of toilets flushing. I usually put the "white noise" from my iphone on so I can sleep. On the plus side is the room decor, very modern and the bed is fantastic. The flat screen tv is huge and has a lot of channels. I love the restaurant for breakfast...dinner is great but pricey. The outdoor pool on the 7th floor is great so is the gym. Good luck with the free parking if you drive a car bigger than a mini cooper!

“Hotel remodeling in January 2008” This hotel was undergoing renovation in 2008, so part of the first floor was closed. The hotel was generally better than other Club Quarters I have visited in DC, New York and Chicago. The staff is very professional and attentive. The hotel also appeared very clean and well kept. Problems with my room were fixed on the day I reported them. This is a good hotel to choose if you are working in the financial district; many things in the area close down at night, and the usual Chicago attractions are far away. Nevertheless, the hotel connects to an "Elephant and Castle" restaurant, and there is a Starbucks on the corner.

“Very Convienent” Stayed here for one night for convienence to the airport. I must say, it was very convienent and easy. Since the hotel is directly linked into the airport terminals, all I did was wake up, and go down to 2nd floor, and walk accross into the airport, couldn't be much easier than that. Plus, I believe that the security check in through that bridge was immensley faster than the one downstairs at the ticket counters. A friend who stayed in the same hotel on the same night, had a later flight, but had to go to the ticketing counters, his security check lasted over 30-40 mins, mine: less than 5. It might have been that particular day, at that particular time (6:30am), maybe the stars were aligned just right, but boy was it an ease.

“Still love the Comfort Inn--just not the disco” I reviewed this hotel after a weeknight stay in Nov. I stayed there again this past weekend and while I was still very pleased with the hotel overall, the noise from the weekend disco next door was a problem. I was on the 4th floor (double room-very nice) and could barely hear the beat of the music Sat night. It was the people noise outside at 4am that was really loud. There was yelling, laughing,etc. The next morning when we left the hotel there was TONS of trash (food wrappers, cigarette butts,etc) on the sidewalk outside of the club. There is no name on the disco--just a metal garage door--surely they have to violating some sort of noise or trash code. Hotel management should be calling the police when things get really loud. I would definitely still stay here again but would ask for a room facing the back of the hotel if it was a weekend.

“Price and Location” We chose this hotel for price and location. It is walking distance to the Art and Rodin museums, an organic market and Wawa. The parking is free. Breakfast is not included but there are a restaurant and bar on site. The hotel is basic/standard, nothing special.
