If you are willing to risk it, pick up a coupon book at a fast food restaurant and get a better hotel for the same price on a walk-in basis.

“休日はちょっと閑散と、、、。” 09年12月25日に1泊しました。ギャラリア地域もさすが、クリスマスだけあって閉まっている店もありましたが、ここハイアット周辺は何とファーストフードも全部閉まっており、開いているのはHOTELのレストランだけでした。綺麗なHOTELではありましたが、休日はあまりにも閑散としており、寂しい気持ちになるのがマイナス。また、湯船につかるとお湯がぬるく、ちょっと辛かった。

“Great hotel, great location, great price” I'm usually loyal to Hilton family properties but ventured out of my comfort zone to stay at the Courtyard Marriott in Copley Sq Boston - and what a great property - great value for money, they have a Sam Adam promotion where you get 6 beers, bucket, beer openers, 2 glasses and buffet breakfast for two for $35 on top of your rate. Rooms were great, love the Paul Mitchell toiletries - great quality! Room was very comfortable, has a solid gym and great location. Friendly and very helpful staff. Valet parking is $45/night or $30-35 self parking across the road.

“The best value in Phoenix!” Let me just start by saying that I've been staying at this hotel for 6 years, back when it was a Wyndham. I was impressed at first, but noticed that things started getting a little worn and dated the last time I stayed there, one and a half years ago. When I found out that it had become a Radisson, I was excited to check it out. Unfortunately, when I walked up to the front desk, I was quoted a rate of $89 dollars, which was about $30-40 more then I normally paid when it was Wyndham (they always had super saver rates of 49.99-59.99 a night!). Then I found out that people were getting this room for $36 bucks on Priceline, so I went ahead and put a bid in and got it accepted. Radisson updated everything in this hotel that needed to be updated. They replaced the carpet, fresh paint everywhere, all new linens on the beds including a down comforter. In addition, they put in new curtains and automatic thermostats on the wall, which is a very nice touch. They kept some of the cool Wyndham features, including the FREE HIGH SPEED WIRELESS INTERNET, and the Herman Miller work chair and desk in the rooms. These have always been a big plus in my book, since I spend frequent amounts of time on my laptop while in the room. Down at the pool, the surprise became even better. It had been completely re-done, and was VERY clean and refreshing. The water temperatures in both the pool and the jacuzzi were PERFECT for a night time swim or soak. I was able to stay in the hot tub for half an hour without getting roasted out. And, even though it closed at 10:30, no one kicked me out, so I really appreciated the extra latitude there. The bathroom was clean, and had a brand new messaging showerhead which seemed to have great water pressure. The shower curtain is one of those new ones all the hotels are using that extends out so you don't feel like you're being wrapped in a curtain while taking a shower. Ventalation in the bathroom was adequate with the door OPENED, causing only the top part of the mirror to fog up. My only complaint is the bed. They didn't replace the old Wyndham bed in my room, and I didn't really feel like I got a good nights sleep. The bed is obviously several years past its life, and I'm not sure why they decided to only replace "some" of the beds with those new sleep number beds, but they need to do all of them. Also, the fitness center still has the old dated wyndham equipment, and is in need of an overhaul. Other then that, great experience and an awesome value!

“Great get away” The Lakeway Resort is a hidden jewel in west Austin. The property is beautiful. It is perfect for a weekend get away. There are good golf courses nearby. The breakfast buffet was a good value and the balcony seating offered spectacular views of Lake Travis.

“Resonable option for Financial District” I stayed at this property for two nights on business travel. This hotel was a good option for the financial district. You are a short walk to the World Trade Center area. There are good quick dining options close by (as well as a Starbucks). It is close to the subway station if you need to head uptown to a show or shopping. The rooms are small but have a new and updated decor The front desk staff was friendly. I arrived around noon and had a meeting at 1p. My room wasn't ready but when I explained my situation (needing to change for my meeting), they were able to quickly find me a room which I was grateful. There was adequate desk space to work in as well. The hotel room was very quite (which is important for me in NYC) and I was able to get a good night sleep in this hotel. I recommend this hotel for guests who need a safe, comfy place to lay their heads each night. It is a good value for NYC.

“Excellent Customer Service” I stayed at this hotel again for two nights on the 17th & 18th of May. Our company has corporate rate, but when I went to try to book my room at our corporate rate I was told “sorry the hotel is very full for these two nights and our normal corporate rate rooms were not available, if I wanted to stay here I would need to upgrade to an ambassador suite size room, and they would apply my corporate discount to the higher priced room but that was the only type of room available and it would be more expensive. Because I have stayed at this hotel previously and others from my company were already staying here I decided to go ahead and book the higher rate room. Upon arrival check-in (early check-in) the clerk behind the counter informed me the room type I book was not available yet, (had not been cleaned) but to give him a few minutes and he would see what was available. He came back to the counter and asked if I was paying my own bill or was it company paid, I told him “company paid” and asked why. He informed me there was a lower priced room available and if I did not need or want the Ambassador Suite, I could take the standard guest room at a significantly lower rate, or I could check my bags in and come back later and take the room I had booked. I choose to take the regular guest room as this would be what I would normally have booked anyway and told him my company would be very happy with the lower bill! I was impressed with his attempt to get me checked in right away and save me money. My stay was perfect. My only complaint is the restaurant staff is slow to bring the bill at the end of the meal, especially for breakfast which is when most people are in a little more of a hurry, I should not have to flag down a wait person and ask for my bill but I had to both mornings.

“Not worth the savings” To save money, my colleague and I booked this hotel on Priceline. The location is excellent, near a T stop, Boston Common, and the Theater District. The staff was very cordial and friendly. We had some issues with the room, that lead to us checking out the next morning and changing hotels. Have you ever left a tissue in the dryer with your clothes or sheets? This hotel did, and as a result my top sheet was covered in shredded tissue. Covered. I called housekeeping, and since it was around 11pm, no one was available to change the sheets, but they did bring me a clean sheet promptly, that I replaced myself. In the bathroom, the sink handles leaked when you turned them on. The cord for the wired internet was broken and did not stay in the computer. It was a Friday night, and although we had read reviews about the nightclub below the hotel, we were relatively unconcerned, because we live in NYC. Unfortunately we had business meetings the next morning, so we had to get to sleep. This proved difficult, because the throbbing base of the nightclub was unavoidable. The hotel lobby sounds like it IS the club. The noise from the club seems to travel up the elevator shaft and permeates throughout the hotel. The gracious staff offered us a different room, and we spent about 15 minutes there and decided that it was still too disruptive. The next morning when checking out, I provided a list of the issues to the desk receptionist who was very apologetic and professional. The staff at this hotel from the doormen to the receptionists are wonderful. Some additional attention to detail would eliminate the minor issues with the room. The noise is unavoidable, but might not be a problem for some travelers.

“Good Location and San Fran Rate” Check in was very efficient. Staff was fantastic. It is a historic property with charm but like most older buildings it has its quirks. The beds were very comfortable, I had an awesome city view (1606), LCD flat screen TV, comp internet. The bathroom was tight. Furniture was nice. Fitness room is down in the basement but was fine. Coffee and hot cocoa in the morning, wine and cocktails during happy hour in the lobby. Walking distance to great restaurants. Had to wait for valet to get the car, give them 30mins notice to be safe. All in all in was a pleasurable experience. Safe travels.

“Great choice for many reasons” This property is just a block or two east of the Mag Mile, about halfway up the Mag Mile. Got a rate through Marriott of $109 for the Friday after Thanksgiving, which is a steal for anyplace in that location. Lots of things going for this property: 1) For comparable properties, cheap onsite parking (the first 9 stories of the hotel are parking) 2) Great location for shoppers and dining (Streeterville, River North, Mag Mile), and plenty of choices within a block or two in either direction. 3) Friendly bellhops, concierge, and front desk folks. 4) QUIET....did not hear a peep from the street (I was on 12th floor) or from people above, below, or next to me. 5) Rooms are tastefully decorated, comfortable, and clean. Appreciated the good lighting and comfortable chair and the desk chair too. 6) Viand, the restaurant next door, is a nice, attractive place for food and drink. An easy place to pass over in a city with thousands of restaurants, many of them worth going to. It was GREAT after a hectic Friday after Thanksgiving to pop in there (there is a door directly from the hotel) and have a nice drink or two with pleasant jazz going on the sound system and a nice quiet atmosphere. The breakfast there the next morning (I had the buffet) was very good, my server was excellent and I could see there were regulars there who come to the city aroudn the holiday, as well as locals. Only down side was at check out, it took a while to snag an elevator that had space for me. But, it is a busy travel weekend and the hotel was full, so this is a minor thing. Notes: There is a piano bar on the other side of the street, one block east, that looked fun. Ask the hotel for a 20% off coupon for Timothy O'Toole's, a sports bar two blocks east. Very good burgers and salads if you are looking for something quick and inexpensive.

“Loved this hotel and the staff was awesome!!!” We just stayed here this past Saturday for my husbands b-day! I had a bouquet of balloons and a cookie cake delivered to the hotel and the hotel staff made sure to have it all set up in our room for our arrival! Thank you so much for whoever did that for my husband!!! He loved it when he walked in the room and he was so surprised! The room was very big, clean, pretty, wonderful view, comfortable bed, just loved everything about it! The hotel is very nice and couldn't be in a more perfect location. We left our car parked at the hotel and walked around the Stockyards the entire time! We had so much fun, will definitely be back again!

“Too pricey, and no amenities” I stayed here for a conference in the hotel. I would never stay here again. It was outrageously priced, and offered me nothing in return. The room was nice, and the people were okay, but they were going to charge me $10 to use their lack luster gym. It was just not worth it, and their big sale is that they are two blocks from the White House. Okay, well there are plenty of more reasonably priced hotels two to three blocks from the White House. It was also under construction, that should have afforded me a discount, but no and it was tacky. Don't even think about getting a $20 drink in the lobby "bar." Horrible service and awful cocktails ensued.

“Wonderful location and a pleasant time” I was in Chicago for a conference and chose the Renaissance based on past stays in this hotel. I wasn't disappointed. From the professional, yet friendly check-in, to the efficient housekeeping, my stay was lovely. The room was spacious, and even with a streetside view, I could see the lake and the river. And it was blissfully quiet. The location is fabulous and even on the hot days I could walk just about anywhere I needed to be.

“A good option in Fisherman's Wharf” Radisson The location of the Radisson couldn’t be better, just a few blocks from the Fisherman’s Wharf, Pier 39 and the pier where leaves the boat to Alcatraz, close to restaurants and the Cable Car stop. The most expensive ride by taxi was from the airport: about US$ 45. To Union Square it was about US$ 8. You can also get the Cable Car to downtown (US$5, 25 per person), the stop is 3 blocks from the entrance of the hotel. But we enjoyed a lot walking around instead of taking cabs. Our room was very clean, we had a king bed with nice and clean linens and extra pillows. The bathroom had complete set of shampoo, conditioner, soap and body lotion replaced every day. It also had a hair dryer and iron in the room. The service was great from the front desk to the housekeeping. We got the best rate in our entire trip! And again: very comfortable and very close to everything. For my first time in SF it was great to stay in a place close to tourist attractions, but maybe next time I’ll try a different neighborhood.

“Great location. Very nice hotel.” Stayed here over Memorial Day weekend. Actually located in the West Loop just west of the river on the Sears Tower side of the city. Kinda nice since you are not in the overcrowded Michigan Avenue area and can breath a little bit. Right next to Greek Town with great Greek restaurants within a block of the hotel. Very nice rooms and main areas. Would definitely stay there again. The only negative was there is only valet parking and it was very expensive. I want to say $39 per day but check the hotel's web site to verify this. Beds were too hard but got used to them.

“Emplacement tip top” Hôtel très bien situé (magnificient mile) avec toutes les boutiques, restaurants et attractions de la ville. Personnel accueillant et à votre disposition à tout moment, vous pouvez commander vos billets pour les matchs depuis l'hotel et vous les feront livrer. Chambre calme et propre. Nous recommandons cet hôtel!

“Great Location, Nice Amenities - some quirks” I stayed for 6 days in mid March for a conference. The hotel is comfortable and in a perfect location for access to the convention center. I enjoyed my time there. Staff were friendly and always greeted me. That said, some quirks: It is obviously a downtown urban location - there was evidence the the common areas are used a lot - especially in the lobby. Upper floors were nice. There is obviously a problem with folks coming in from the streets who do not belong in the hotel. One early morning I witnessed an altercation between a janitor and a homeless man who was getting some coffee from the always stocked beverage area. Yelling ensued. Other reviewers have noted the use of loud walk talkies in the lobby. This does happen but it wasn't as bad as I thought it might be. Some desk staff seem to like to use them for everything! My room was at the end of the hall - near the storage room for the cleaning carts. EVERY morning I was there the cleaning staff would congregate for 45 minutes - an hour and chat while prepping their carts for the day. This usually happened at 8am - like clockwork! I was up so it wasn't a big deal but do not stay in rooms that end with 01, 02, or 03. I heard from colleagues it happened on their floors as well!

“Great DC Experience” We stayed here recently for three nights to attend a wedding and enjoyed a quiet respite from the DC hustle bustle evident in so many other DC hotels. We stayed in a corner suite which is a bit larger than the regular suites and away from the noise of the courtyard. Being Labor Day weekend, there was lots going on with several large groups staying and having events there, the breakfast was busier than usual (long waits for omelets) but still great nonetheless. Same with the evening managers reception. But the hotel staff was wonderful, very helpful and accommodating. No problems there! This hotel is located about 3 1/2 blocks from the Foggy Bottom metro station. There is no shuttle so if you take the train in from the airport (approx 15 min ride), be prepared to "lug" your luggage those city blocks (unless you opt for a cab- but the walk is really not that bad!!). This is in a very nice area of DC (Georgetown University) and walking around it is very pleasant. It's also a short walk to the Lincoln Memorial, WWII Memorial, Vietnam Memorial, White House and other popular sites. Many restaurants in the area to choose from and some are quite reasonably priced. Not inexpensive to stay here but definitely worth it for an enjoyable visit to our Nation's Capitol.

“Very nice new hotel with a bonus - a cafe” This hotel, which opened in late 2009, is very attractively designed. Both the public areas and rooms are attractive and spacious. All of the employees I encountered were friendly. My king bed was very comfortable and had very nice bedding. The TV was large and the room contained a desk, large TV and a sofa and coffee table. The rooms offer both WiFi and wired Internet. The bathroom was spacious and shower water pressure good. Unlike many mid-priced hotels, there is no breakfast included in the room charge. However, this was fine with me. I'm happy to pay for a good, hot breakfast. The cafe serves a variety of hot dishes, and is also open at dinner serving light meals such as sandwiches and soups. The food was good. The lobby also included many comfortable couches, chairs and computer stations complete with printers. I would have given the hotel 5 stars except for two things. Marriott may have cut corners on the insulation between the rooms. For a hotel with the upscale look and design of this one, you wouldn't expect to hear the TV, coughing and children's voices in the room next door, which I did. Also, I would have expected a higher quality coffee machine in the room. The single-cup one provided is very poor, as is the coffee that comes with it. Despite these shortcomings, I am likely to return to this very nice hotel.

“Very average airport hotel” I arrived very late and checked into a standard room that had not been fully serviced, I was quickly moved to another room by a very pleasant and efficient security man. Very good breakfast with efficient staff, however front desk staff although pleasant were not comfortable or confident (seemed lost) when dealing with my comments.

“Best Hotel in San Francisco” My headline says it all. It is by far significantly cheaper than any hotel of comparable quality in the city, and for you get it is such an excellent value. I attended a conference at the Westin in Union Square, and Orchard was half the price for a much bigger and modern room. It's very quiet, and not prone to the street noise you'll get in other Union Square hotels either. Small, friendly, intimate, clean, huge bathroom, and the restaurant and room service are really good. I ordered a burger from room service and it was one the best I have ever had in my life. Cable car right outside and short walk to Union Square. Stay here!

“Clean, good location, friendly staff” Stayed one night. Room was small but that was expected. Bed was quite comfortable. Room 103 in the back is very quiet and dark. No noise from traffic or other rooms. Steam heat was noisy, but that was also expected. We balanced out the heat with air conditioning which worked. Room had a little fridge which I didn't expect, although it wasn't working. As we didn't really need it we didn't complain. Ice is available from the restaurant downstairs. There were 2 computers for use in the lobby. There are a lot of restaurants and convenient groceries and pharmacies in the area. We also walked to and from the theater (11 blocks, about 15-20 minutes). It is only a few blocks from Central Park.

“SPG should cut them loose!” Obviously, since I'm an SPG Platinum member, I'm loyal to SPG hotels. The hotel location is great; walking distance to Broadway, Times Square, 5th Ave. shopping, and amazing restaurants. The hotel lobby is in need of a renovation (as well as the ENTIRE HOTEL)! The lady at check in was very kind and offered me my SPG Platinum amenity, as well as an SPG Platinum upgrade, informing me that a room was "reserved for me on the 21st floor". The room, a King bed room, was dark, horrible, and dirty. My thermostat and satellite TV weren't working, so I called the front desk. Maintenance came promptly. The maintenance man was very apologetic, saying that my thermostat was broken, replaced it with a new one and apologized for the satellite TV. He said that "it happens all the time". His exact words were, "call the manager and complain. They should comp you in some way, especially that you're a platinum." I didn't bother to call the management. In the lobby I asked one of the staff at the side desk located next to the check in desk,an older gentleman , whom I assumed was a concierge (later I found out that the hotel doesn't offer a concierge service) a question, and he was extremely rude and dismissive. Out of all the travel experiences I've had throughout the world, I've never had a hotel employee be that rude to me when I was asking for help. As for the room cleanliness... Poor to say the least! When I first got to the room, the floor clearly hadn't been vacuumed for awhile. I saw dust, particles of things, etc... The bathtub even had hair in it! The gift shop in lobby doesn't accept room charges and doesn't really have any set hours of operation. It closes when the shop attendant wants to go home. No in-room wireless internet, although there is in the lobby. Walls paper thin, you can even here when your neighbor is hanging things in their closet! I talked to 2 of the hotel's employees and they themselves said that the hotel is terrible. One of them actually said that it's "embarrassing". Overall, I don't recommend this hotel.

“Another great Kimpton property!” I've stayed in a number of Kimpton properties in Boston and Washington, DC and have never been disappointed; the new Palomar in Philadelphia continues my great experiences. From the valet greeting me and telling me to let the front desk know that I drive a hybrid car because it would get me a discounted room rate to the beautifully appointed, super quiet room, I couldn't have asked for more. The staff is so kind and friendly, the rooms are thoughtfully laid out and filled with little conveniences, and the bar and restaurant were excellent. We even had a celebrity chef sighting in the bar! Overall, another excellent Kimpton experience and one that reinforces why the brand is my absolute favorite among hotels.

“Restin' at the Westin” Westin hotels seldom disappoint and this is no exception. Check-in was a bit slow but front desk staff is superlative. Standard room was spacious. Great lounge area adjacent to the bar. There is also a terrific outdoor seating area. Better than average fitness room. Slow Internet connection in room and business center. Good restaurant service and food. Staff is exceptionally friendly. Even the cleaning staff went out of their way to brighten the day. Location is terrific for shopping and Chinatown.

“Great Location For Business Travelers” I usually stay at this Hampton when I am in Denver on business. Its not really a hotel for families , mostly business people. The rooms are always nice and clean, Parking lot is kind of small but there is overflow next door. It across the I25 from downtown, not much in that is close for restaurants but since its so close to downtown there are plenty to choose from but you'll have to drive. Great downtown views and pretty easy to get to.

“Great price but, things u should know first” The Hotel was built in 1922 and was recently remodeled. It is what the 20's era offered. Small rooms, narrow hallways....etc. The elevators can be quite slow at times. Go to second floor to go up otherwise you will be waiting on 1st floor for a while during peak times. There is a separate elevator for floors. If you book on line and a room size is not offered, it will be a very small double bed room. You can call the Hotel direct shortly after and ask for an upgrade to a King, IF they have one available. It's 15-20$ a nite more but well worth it. Our room was very comfortable. I have read complaints about noise. Our AC was very quiet. The street noise can be a bit much, after all you are ON Michigan Ave. The higher the floor the better. Parking and food are very pricey. I suggest using parkwiz.com and look for a garage near by. I got 4 days for $96 total vs, $45-50 a nite thru the hotel ans was only 4 blocks away. There is a Corner Bakery right around the block that is very reasonable for breakfast. I would stay here again but would book thru the hotel website direct. That way you can choose your room and make request for higher rooms and or rooms opposite side of Mich Avenue. Oh ya, there is a Star Bucks just down the street in NW Univ Hospital.

“Nice hotel, large rooms, but may not be your ideal location” If you are visiting DC for business and want to be in a nice area like Georgetown, I highly recommend the hotel. If you are in DC to tour the capital, maybe you want to be further downtown. Tip - go to the restaurant across the street - I believe it's called the Blue Duck Tavern. It's expensive but good. The Westin's service was average - neither good nor bad, just average. They rushed me out on my check out day, even though I am a Starwood Platinum member. Regarding the rooms, they are large, clean, and have whatever you need for a comfortable business trip. I do think there are better values in DC though, as my rate was rather high.

“Get'em In, Get'em Out” This is a great hotel is you are looking for an attractive room and a nice bed to grab a few hours of sleep on an airport layover. The beds are very comfortable. However, this is NOT the hotel to consider if you need anything more than sleep. This was my third stay at this hotel and unfortunately, my arrival at Logan, was after midnight. I was informed the shuttle bus would arrive in 15-20 minutes which was reasonable. But after three hours of traveling I was hungry and thirsty and eager to get to this hotel. The ride in the shuttle bus was just short of terrifying. It seemed as though the driver was late in leaving for the night and weaved in and out of the maze of roads at Logan to reach this hotel. This hotel lives up to the old New England adage, you cannot get there from here! How the luggage did not fly from its storage area amazed me when the driver appeared to take the corners on just two wheels! It appears "full service" airlines and hotels is now defined as getting you from point A to B with no services in between. As frequent travelers know, the food service on a multi-hour flight is now limited to a one ounce package of pretzels, the thought of a late night meal once getting to the hotel was not to be. What I really wanted was a cold beer which was not possible, in spite of the fact there were two bartenders behind the bar at 12:30 AM. When I approached the bar and requested a beer, the bartender simply gestured by waving his hand across his neck signifying the bar was "cut off". Not a word was uttered or a simply apology saying the bar was closed. I had to settle with a bottle of soda from the closet gift shop off the front desk. I guess all that “service” forced the price of soda to $2.50! I wonder why they could not have offered a cold beer in this little closet? Surely they would have made at least $10 for a beer if a soda costs that much. One would think this hotel might think about having some sort of late night snack available for late arriving guests. I have had more considerate service from a Residence Inn. But Hyatt, a supposedly high-end hotel that caters to business travelers? At least they might have suggested a late night pizza place that offered delivery service. I am sorry but this hotel has totally lost sight of who their guests are and what there needs might be. Especially if you arrive at midnight and leave by 7 am. Sadly, service is not something to expect from this hotel or its staff.

“Exceeded expectations” This hotel exceeded my expectations and I would recommend it. The rooms are clean and nicely appointed, and a decent size for NYC. Location is also solid. My only complaint is the thin walls, which make it fairly easy to deduce what is afoot in the adjacent rooms or hallway. If you happen to find yourself next door to a room containing a baby and/or an especially amorous couple (I experienced both), you may be in for a long night.

“Go-To DC Hotel” The Palomar is my hotel of choice in Washington DC. It has a great location, top notch service, a good restaurant, and is a good value. This most recent hotel was a one-night stay while visiting family in town. The Dupont Circle location is perfect. It is only a couple of blocks from the red line Metro station which provides easy access to Union Station and many DC sights. The Dupont Circle area is chock full of restaurants, shopping, cafes, bars, etc. When I checked in they greeted me any my wife by name. They made conversation about where we were travelling from and allowed us to check in early. The room was large and we were high enough (9th floor) to not be bothered by any street noise. One drawback was that our room was connected to the neighboring room by a locked door. That allowed a bit more noise through from the people in that room which was annoying. I probably could have asked to switch rooms but was too lazy.

“Great hotel!!” The hotel is nicely decorated. The room is large. The staff is helpful. The location is conveniently located just few blocks from shopping malls and westlake light rail station. It lists as 4 stars but it is definitely nicer than most 4 stars hotels.

“extremely nice” We stayed here while in town for a friend's wedding. We were very impressed with the location and the room, and will absolutely come back when we are in town again. Check-in is on the third floor. When we first arrived, we wandered around for a bit before we realized that we had to go upstairs. The one thing that the hotel does need to work on is its downstairs bell-staff - not only when we first arrived, but every time we entered and left the building, there were very few employees on the ground floor, and they seemed to be making a concerted effort to ignore the guests. Otherwise, service was very good. At check-in, the front desk gave us a masterfully worded note from the manager, explaining that it was the weekend of the gay pride parade, so there were a lot of wonderful activities in town, but guests needing to travel on Sunday should allow themselves extra time - it was beautifully done. The hotel decor was very nice, more modern than the typical JW Marriott, looked like it was just renovated. The lobby spaces, bar, etc. were very nice and fairly busy while we were there. The room was a good size, beautifully furnished, very large bathroom, good amenities, linens, and a very comfortable bed, large window, pretty good view, and very quiet. The location was great - close to Union Square, but a block or two away from the hectic masses.

“Decent Hotel at Reasonable Prices” Stayed at the Columbus Motor Inn for 3 nights. We stayed in the 2 bedroom room. In the bedroom there was 1 double bed, dresser, and TV and closet. In the othe room (there was no door to this room so there is no privacy) there was 2 double beds. There is a TV, dresser, and a small table with chairs to sit at in this room. There is also a coffee maker located in the room. The bathroom is decent sized. The sink is separated from the toilet/shower. The room is OK in general. It was clean and there was daily maid service. We got facing Columbus and at night it was pretty loud --- between buses, cars, trucks it was noisy. The room could definitely use some upgrading and modernizing. But, given the price we paid it is a good value and decent place to stay. The best thing about this hotel is the free parking! It would be nice if they offered a continental breakfast, but that isn't a big deal. Free internet access is also very nice. The hotel is located about a 5 minute walk to the Powell Mason Cable Car turntable. I recommed buying a 3 day pass if you will be using the SF Muni trasit as it only costs $18. A one day pass costs $11. A one way ticket on the cable car is $5!!! So, a definite savings is to get one of the passes. Also, the number 30 bus stops right in front of the hotel and that goes up to China Town and Union Square. Also very convenient and the passes are good for the buses too. Fisherman's Wharf is about a 10 minute walk away. There is also a Safeway and Walgreens within 10 minutes walk.

“Walk Philly from Ideal Location” If you can get a room with a spectacular view of City Hall's William Penn, you'll overlook any accomodation shortcomings (squishy, sinking bed, old tv in bedroom, etc.). *Best* location to walk the city (Murals, Chinatown, Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, Logan Square, Museum Row, Love Park, and scads of architectural & sculptural delights, including city hall (photo opps)) -- just keep walking/exploring. Standard RI breakfasts/dinners (above lobby on 2nd floor). Two computers & printer in sitting area also on 2nd floor. Bank of peppy elevators minimizes long waits during busy hours of day. Renovated lower level has gym & laundry room with rows of washers & dryers. If you're driving during rush hour, call down ahead of time to allow valet enough time to retrieve car. (A standard quoted time of 15-20 min. can take quite a bit longer -- 45 min.). Tight, congested auto drop off at front of bldg. with steady stream of traffic. ($45 parking; ouch. Valet parking only option.) Maintenance promptly responds to requests. (Keep in mind it's an older building.) Adequate size bedroom, living room, & kitchenette -- not as spacious as some RIs, but good location makes up for it. (Trader Joes & Whole Foods nearby if you've a long stay & like to eat healthy. Kitchenette helps.) If you enjoy walking a city, RI Center City is a convenient starting point; you know your back home once you see City Hall. ---------------- Addendum: As much as you enjoy the location & fall in love with bustle of the city, there's the heart-aching side of homelessness. Being in the heart of the city, you'll sadly see people sleeping in parks (on benches/grass) & even lined along the bldgs of museum row. (You realize how fortunate you are to have a safe hotel room in which to sleep -- no matter what the room's condition.) (Unless you're inured to panhandlers, poverty, & mentally troubled people speaking to themselves on the street, the inner city can be disturbing to the sensitive & can be overwhelming to genteel souls. It is eye opening & hopefully won't deter you from walking the city -- merely be aware.) Franklin Square (6th & Race Streets) has amazing miniatures of Philadelphia's historic attractions (Liberty Bell, City Hall, Ben Franklin Bridge...) along a miniature golf course. (The *actual* BF Bridge is steps away.) Whether you golf or not, young & old will have fun identifying each iconic site. RI's central location makes it convenient to venture forth & the many maps posted throughout Center City (identifying where you are) help you navigate your way (without panic of being lost). Ask front desk for map (always handy to keep in pocket) before going on your adventure.

“Perfect for our family” We have just returned from a week at the Argonaut Hotel in San Francisco. We booked a special advanced rate on an enormous corner suite for our family of five. The suite, which included a king room with bath, twin double bedroom with bath, and enormous living room with double pull out couch and dining table, is probably the most comfortable accomodations we have ever had with the children. The location, at the calmer end of Fisherman's Wharf , is absolutely perfect for a family vacation -- we were within very easy walking distance of the cable car, duck tour, fire engine tour, biking over the golden gate bridge (not to be missed!), Alcatraz ferry, and historic boats (the submarine audio tour was excellent). Numerous restaurants in the area appeal to famlies and the views over the bay are spectacular. The hotel rooms are stylish and fun; the only drawback was the noise -- we had a third floor suite facing away from the water, which I hoped would be quiet, but was in fact rather noisy in the early mornings. The water facing third and fourth floor rooms and suites must have great views but might also be noisy, since they overlook the wharf area. Beware that the interior rooms in the hotel (which i don't believe are suites) face a very bland concrete courtyard -- they must be quiet but not exciting. Finally, there is no pool (which would have been nice, but wasn't essential to us)

“Excellent Stay...” I just stayed at the W Times Square with my wife and 3 other couples, and I think I can speak on behalf of all of us saying that we do not regret it. I has hesitant on choosing the Times Square location because it is not one of my favorites parts of the city but the hotel itself makes you forget the crowds that you found down below. Rooms in great shape, small yes, but it is New York so, rooms ok. The only complaint could be lack of drawers for cloths but other than that, rooms are great and clean. The shower awsome. I believe we were upgraded to a corner view room on the 40th floor so the views are fantastic.

“Cool place on the Marina” Stayed here 3 nights for work. The hotel is very secluded and semi private. Right in the marina on the breakwater but still close enough to walk to Starbucks in the morning. There are several good restaurants close by as well. The hotel itself is landscaped like a tropical jungle and maintained very well. Although it is an older property it has been updated many times and is very comfortable without being worn. The room was large and the bed was comfy. The bathroom was decent sized as was the closet and coffee area. The heating and AC was a bit aged, either on or off with very little control but the weather is so temperate in SD that I only used it to heat the room for about 20 minutes when I got in it then turned it off completely the rest of the night. The restaurant was decent and the bar very lively. Many locals (those that live on the boats in the marina) party in the bar as there are bands nearly every night. A quiet drink and conversation is out of the question as the volume is fairly high. I could definitely stay here again for a quiet weekend away. Not the most glamorous but very comfortable and clean.

“Another great Kimpton Hotel” My wife & I stayed for just one night before leaving SF. The Palomar is very nice hotel. An urbane, fashionable lobby. The staff was upbeat. The room was smartly appointed & roomy. My one quibble was the bathroom. A bit tiny & easy to bump into things. We didn't dine at the famed Fifth Floor restaurant but the decor looked great! The location is good. The area is not attractive. But the hotel is close to many galleries & funky stores. Overall, an enjoyable stay & we would highly recommend the Palomar. FREE WIFI. A HUGE PLUS since hotels like the Stanford Court charge for daily use of the internet.

“A real disappointment” We booked to stay for 3 nights at Hyatt Fisherman's Wharf on the understanding that this was one of the best hotels in the Fisherman's Wharf area. If this was one of the best, I dread to think what some of the others are like. In hindsight, it was a mistake to stay at Fisherman's Wharf anyway. Myself and my husband spent part of our honeymoon in San Francisco three years ago but stayed near Union Square. At the time, we seemed to be travelling down to Fisherman's Wharf a lot for Alcatraz, Pier 39 etc so it made sense just to stay down there this time. In fact, we ended up spending nearly all of our time away from there! I don't know what has happened in three years, but it seemed to feel more unsafe, more seedy, more tacky and there were certainly more beggars down there. We could hardly walk out of our hotel without getting hassled by someone, and therein lies the first problem of Hyatt Fisherman's Wharf. As for the hotel itself, that too, was extremely disappointing. The lobby was beautiful but unfortunately, not maintained well. The carpeting was filthy and all of the public areas just felt like they needed a good clean. There was a strange, musty smell that hung in the air too. I'm not a prima donna in any way and I've stayed in plenty of lower class hotels that were clean and well maintained, but this hotel just screamed 'unloved' and it is clearly ageing before its time. Our room I would call fairly basic (and certainly not 4*) but at least that was clean and I guess we spent more time in the room than public areas so it was more important for the room to be clean. However, it shouldn't have to be an either/or situation. The decor made the room feel dingy and dated even though it probably wasn't done THAT long ago. The bed was very comfortable though, and we made good use of the numerous cable channels on offer. There wasn't a coffee maker in the room but the hotel did offer complimentary coffee at a station down the corridor which was handy. We ate breakfast at the hotel's only on-site restaurant, "Knuckles" for convenience more than anything else. The food was ok, nothing special though. We felt it was overpriced for what it was. The staff overall were trying their best but were mainly young and inexperienced. They also weren't very forthcoming with a smile or cheery hello. On the whole, we found our whole experience at Hyatt Fisherman's Wharf very disappointing and it's for certain that if we return to San Francisco, we'll be staying neither there, or at the Fisherman's Wharf area in general.

“Doubletree Experience!” First of all I need to start by saying that these are the best cookies. When I arrived, the staff was very helpful and welcoming. They gave me a cookie right away and the check-in was flawless and very quick. The room was very clean, the only thing is that the bathrooms are not very spacious, but this was no problem to me. The location is very central and the restaurants at the hotel are also very good. The continental breakfast downstairs had a lot of different options and the quality was excellent. The only thing that I did not enjoy was that one night we could hear someone snoring next door. On the other hand, the Metro station is only a few blocks away and the experience was overall very good. The stay was wonderful, I would not hesitate to go back!

“Could Have Been Better” I had booked a petit suite. It turned out that it was really 2 rooms with the wall between them removed. They didin't take the opportunity to increase the size of the closets or bathroom, which I feel is a major mistake and makes the room not worth the money. There is a Starbuck's coffe bar in the lobby that is supposed to open at 6:00 AM every day. But nobody showed up on Saturday so it was closed all day. I agree with a previous reviewer that service at breakfast is slow. The hotel is not near public transportation (the closest metro stop is Old Town) so you will need a car. They will charge you to park it and street parking is limited. This hotel is convenient to the University and Scripps but is too far from downtown.

“Best Westin Ever” I arrived at the hotel and was immediately impressed with the kind young woman who helped me check into the hotel. She was pleasant in all pleasantries... and I soon found out that every single person employed at this hotel is the same. Without exception, I found everyone to be helpful, forthcoming, and thinking outside the box. The staff is just superb. Other than the employees, though, it is really a great hotel. I stay at Starwood hotels often and this one was above par. Their foyer/atrium rose to multiple floors and the glass elevators literally went through the ceiling, creating stunning views. The business center, fitness area, and all common areas were just at the standard you would expect from a Westin, which is to say, were great. They were all modern, well-maintained, and easy to access. The rooms themselves were also highly comfortable. There was adequate space, abundant resources of utilities and necessities, and are again very modern. The entire experience was just as comfortable as could be. I was upgraded to a bay-view room, affording me nice sights. I enjoyed watching the boats and the sunsets. The location was also better than I expected. On my last trip to San Diego, I stayed at the Westin in the Gas Lamp quarter, so this time I was expecting a bit of a walk to get to that area. However, the city blocks are small and this hotel is only about 10 minutes' walk from the same Gas Lamp area. It was a pleasant walk, too, and in a very safe area, well-lit, and easily navigated. There were multiple restaurants and convenience stores nearby, as well as a trolley station, so everything was easily accessed. There is even a micro brewery located one block away. The airport, too, was only about 10 minutes away by car, but I was never even awoken by noise! All-in-all, this is a fabulous hotel. I liked it better than the other Westin I mentioned, too.

“Glad I stayed at a Holiday Inn Express last night!” Spent one night here on business. This is one of the best Holiday Inn Express hotels I have seen! My room (and I think all rooms) had a 42-inch plasma tv mounted on the wall - nice touch! It also had a fridge and microwave. Everything was very new and clean and worked well. The internet service is hard wired. I didn't try the pool, but it looked okay. Breakfast was typical HI Express and well-stocked. It's right on I-10, but at the far east end of town. There are a number of restaurants nearby, but nothing special I can recommend - except for the french silk pie at the Village Inn. Yes, it's a chain, but the have great pies! I definitely recommend this hotel.

“Lovely property and experience” Visited in March- very low tourist season. Not many other visitors at this time. Grounds and facility are stunningly beautiful, well manicured grounds and very clean facilities. Room was a bit small, esp. the queen bed. Nice views though. Loved the kitchens and free snacks. Breakfast (free) was a nice way to start the day--- good granola. Looked at the restaurant for dinner, more than we wanted to spend. Very interesting concepts with the different buildings- it felt very chic and classy!

“Typical airport hotel” I stayed one night before my very early morning flight. The front desk service was efficient and friendly. The service at Landings Bar in lobby area was too. Pleasant surprise! I would rate higher, but for the price I paid there are a few things about the property that I didn't love. The building is obviously older and very highly trafficked since it is so close to LAX. It's been updated, but it's kind of like dressing up an old pig. You can tell its age when the in-room thermostat is an old plastic dial thing from the 1970's and the room just doesn't cool off properly because building mechanicals are old. It was a sunny day and what looked and sounded like raindrops were hitting my window outside. Clearly something mechanical was dripping outside, another sign of the building age. I'd stay again only if I had a very early flight because it is super convenient to LAX. Otherwise, I'd look elsewhere.

“Perfect location for Family vist to Chinese New Year” We were thoroughly pleased with our stay at the Omni. We had adjoining rooms (a King and a double) and were assistd at every turn by Omnii staff. We have stayed in more than a dozen hotels in S.F. (St. Francis, the Palace, the Milano, Hyatts, Mariott, Sir Francis Drake, Kensington Park etc.) over the years and this was definately among the best. Many hotels will have nice lobbies, but have very ordinary rooms . The Omni had beautifully furnished luxurious rooms with every imaginable amenitiy. I would recommend it to anyone. As San Francisco is developing more and more to the east of Union Square, restaurants, shopping and attractions are near the Financial District location of the Omni. Plus, the California Cable Car line is right outside. We were in S.F. for the Chinese New Year Parade (a block away), Prom Dress Shopping, (5 min walk) and to attend an event at MoMA (10 minute walk). Nearby Belden Place offers some of San Franciscos best restaurants and a truly european bistro experience, that is entirely family friendly. We had dinner at Brindisi. Make reservations for weekends at any S.F. restaurant.. The hotel valet parking is $45 , high even for San Francisco. However, around the corner on Kearny is a 24 hour city parking lot with security. A bargain. If you join the Omni's "club" before your stay, you also get real pampering including morning coffee delivered to your door with the paper and free internet. We loved it!

“Not that pleased” I keep going back and forth between whether this is an "okay for the money" hotel vs a "they should have given me my money back." Staff was courteous, the room is a nice-size for New York, but things were not as clean as they could have been (the bed ruffle was stained, carpet wasn't necessarily vacuumed), and there were big time issues re: the bathroom. For starters, not all rooms have a tub, so be sure to ask for one when you book. There is no upcharge, though, for them to move you, which is good. Bad news, though, is that my bath water was brown. Evidently, it's because the pipes are older and chemicals build up in them when water is not run often. My question was why they aren't running water between guests to clean the tub. But my tub had a grimy, white substance in the bottom even when I arrived, almost as though the cleaning solution had dried in there and not been wiped out, and I had to wipe it down myself. When I called the front desk to tell them my bathwater was brown, it took a bit longer than it should have for them to send an engineer, who then had go on the roof and do something with a pump before it would run clear again. The engineer acted as though this happened all the time. The next day, after the water was fixed, I took a bath and was already in the tub before I realized that housekeeping had not left any shampoo in the room. I called the front desk & told them I was there with wet hair & needed shampoo. Two more calls and 35 minutes later, they finally brought some. Things were not rough enough here for me to leave, but I do not plan to stay here again. On the bright side, the breakfast buffet staff were very nice.

“Elegant and worth every penny” Elegant and plush hotel. Tall building and I believe the lounge is on the 35th floor. Sterile entry and security approaches immediately. You can't get to the elevator unless you have a key. Nice restaurant..very unaffordable. In other words, nice but overpriced. Great views. Room was clean, decent size, floor to ceiling windows, comfortable bed and clean shower. Flat screen TV - had WebTV which I used for the first time. Helpful staff. Hotel is near Columbus Circle and attached to Time Warner Building. Many nice restaurants in the area and 24 hour Starbucks directly across the street. Hotel is a very short distance from Central Park which is great for joggers. Shopping mall is located inside Time Warner Building. Hotel is modern, plush with great views and great dining options. Staff will bend over backward to get whatever you need. Great location too & very near subway station.

“Got an unclean room” The impression that the hotel left in us was very disappointing after having arrived late and entering a worn down room, that hasn't been cleaned thoroughly. We asked for a new room and it was better. But if it wasn't for this, it would be a nice hotel, with spacious rooms. Better than the average motel. The continental breakfast was also rather good.

“Pretty Nice.” Stayed here for one night. Hotel was overall a pleasant experience with an extremely friendly and helpful staff. There is a free continental breakfast and the hotel provides a shuttle to and from the airport. I would suggest this hotel for families or for a quick stay. Nothing over the top at the hotel, but a good solid room and comfortable bed that is sufficient for the basic stay.
“Muy correcto Bien situado” Buen hotel. Bien situado. Amplio parking. Buen desayuno.

“W ホテルにしては落ち着いた雰囲気” ボストンでは、同じスターウッド系列のリバティホテルにも泊まりましたが、リバティより部屋はやや広いものの、シャワーのみでバスタブなしでした。それ以外は、シティホテルとしては標準的な感じです。低層階だったので、部屋からの眺望は隣のビルが見えるだけでした。パソコンを持参すれば、インターネットは1階ロビーで無料で使えます。観光には申し分ない立地で、ボストンの史跡巡り「フリーダムトレイル」に行くにも便利です。

“Grande Old Dame in want of a redo” I remember having my high school prom at the Park Plaza and thinking it was the most elegant hotel ever. But now, 25 years later, the gilding is off the lily. It's still lovely but the rooms are very small and it's in need of some modernizing. The bathroom is tiny with only enough room for one person (which is fine since I am here visiting my mom on my own) and there is room for a double bed in the room. The closet is miniscule and the door to the bathroom does not open fully into the room with room to get around the desk. So it's a tight squeeze. Additionally, the heat could not be turned off so the room was literally 79° which is not quite comfy at night. But that said, there is a grand elegance to the golden swans on the curved elevator doors, the chandeliers in the lobby and the flower arrangements which harkens back to the age of elegance that the Park Plaza comes from. And no matter how cramped the room is, there is something nice about staying in an historic hotel.

“Service much improved” I've stayed here a few times over the years, and always thought their service was pretty dismal. It would appear that someone has decided to remedy this. Was also pleased with a relatively large room -- stayed in the front of the hotel this time rather than towards the back. Rooms are clean and beds are comfy. My room only had a shower -- no big deal for me but I think a larger person would have difficulty fitting in the rather small space. If you like more space in which to shower in, suggest that you ask specifically for a bathtub.

“Ett av de bättre Courtyard hotellen” Detta är ett jättebra Courtyard hotell mitt i pulsen av downtown Chicago, endast ett kvarter från Michigan Av. Hotellet ät litet och familjärt med en väldigt bra service, rummen är fräscha och har normalstorlek. Extra plus för Viandi, den italienska resaturabgen samt en väldigt bra lobby bar med skickliga bartenders. Ett hotell jag kan rekommendera, dessutom med hyfsade rums priser

“Beautiful property for families and couples” This amazing Westin Property (we learned is actually owned by USAA) is located on a cliff overlooking the beautiful topography of the San Antonio Hill Country. The resort is large in size and the layout somewhat confusing. There are multiple elevators, some of which only service certain floors or certain wings, but you quickly learn how to get around and the staff helpful in guiding you in the right direction. The staff make you feel like you are the most important guest at the property. The drinks by the pool are $10, comparable to other resort properties and the poolside menu similar to most resorts. Hamburger around $13, I ordered the Chicken Quesadillas ($10), this item was not on the menu but offered to the guests, delicious! The rooms are consistent with Westin quality, Heavenly Bed, Rain showerhad and large flat screen television, etc., a complimentary water is offered to members on the preferred floor, along with a flourless brownie from the chef, absolutely delicious! My FIRST room, 6045 on the preferred floor, had food on the ceiling (looked like someone threw their pizza on the ceiling) so they moved me to another room, a "PUR" room, 4024. The concept is fabulous, designed for those who suffer from allergies, however the room I was placed in had AC problems and I poured sweat all night. I was moved to another room in the morning (facing the delivery driveway to the kitchen) not acceptable and then finally landed in room 6065, which also had food on the ceiling. Many families with small children stay at this property, as it so close to Fiesta Texas and Sea World, so I would imagine it is difficult to maintain the rooms. Tired of being moved and the fact it was digging into our R&R time, 6065 is where we decided to stay. This room on the preferred floor faced the amazing pools, which was beautiful and peaceful. We found the adult pool, no one under 21 admitted, and hung out there for the following days. It is just off the other pools, but overlooks the hill country. We were very surprised how quiet it was just feet away from the other pools, very relaxing! The gray cushions on the chaise lounges around the pool are more plush than some other Westin resorts, an added plus. This property offers valet or self park, I chose valet and was never disappointed when I called for my car, they seem to have this service perfected. As a 4 Star owner and elite members, we were given access to the Hacienda Club lounge on the 7th floor for continental breakfast and appetizers and wine or beer in the evening. The appetizers were boring, olives and cold olive oil soaked cut veggies every night and a candy bar (guess this is for the kids) the continental breakfast was nothing special either, bagel, toast, oatmeal and a few pastries along with coffee and orange juice. There were many families with children running around in the club lounge, we have kids so it did not disturb us, however there were guests there on business that were not pleased. The club lounge in Westin in NY and Sheraton Norfolk, VA have obviously spoiled us. Our overall experience was very nice, we will definitely give this property another visit and would recommend it to our family and friends.

“Decent Conference Hotel” This hotel is fairly good. The room had the necessities, with HD TV and a very comfortable bed. Nothing special beyond that. The overall feel of the lobby, restaurants, concierge, etc. is large, crowded and noisy. When I walked into the lobby and saw the very long line to check in, I was astounded but fortunately they had a separate line for elite members so I could use that. There were long lines for everything. And, for some reason their restaurant wasn't open for lunch. With the crowds, I found that strange. So, don't go here if you want cozy feel, attentive staff, or special attention. It's a classic conference hotel and they do a decent job at that for the size.

“Very small rooms” The service was very good. Complementary breakfast was nice. Rooms were very small, could hardly move around in the bathroom. Did have a coffee maker in the room which was very nice. The whole hotel was in need of renovation. Hotel is in a great location, right near central park.

“Pros and cons” I have stayed a this hotel at least a dozen times over the past 10 years for busines. It would not be my choice, but this is where my business colleagues wish to stay. However, I have more good than bad to say about this hotel. First, the good: The location is excellent, The hotel is across the street from Penn Station and Madison Square Garden. You have easy access to the trains and subways. I take the subway most of the time; it is perfectly safe to do so, and not very expensive. The subway can get very crowded. The beds are extremely comfortable. It is very nice to have a kitchen area with full size refierator to store snacks and leftovers, and keep beverages cold. You can walk to Times Square, or take take the subway Now the bad: The area is very noisy, the windows are old and have window air conditioning units. I have been as high as the 17th floor, and still heard honking and sirens all night. Also, I have had rooms with maintenance issues. (For example, during one recent trip, a window in the room had no shade. )

“Fine for 1 night” We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn for 1 night and it was fine. The room itself was very nice. The bed was comfortable, the bedding was nice and there was plenty of room to move around. The bathroom had a jetted tub which was nice but the high walls might make it difficult for some people to get in and out of the tub/shower. The lobby was nice. The hotel is set up in an atrium style so all the rooms open onto the area overlooking a small pool and the breakfast area. It was quiet enough when we were there but I can imagine it could get noisy. Speaking of noise, there was a lot of road noise from 281. In fact, I couldn't believe how noisy it was! When I investigated further in the morning, I noticed there was an opening between the window frame and the glass itself which would explain the noise. THe hotel has scaffolding on that side of the building so I hope they are in the process of replacing the windows. It wasn't bad for one night but would not have been tolerable for more than that. It was definitely fine for the price (around $40 on Priceline) and I would stay there again for that price for one night.

“Great Hotel” We booked based on TripAdvisor reviews which were accurate. We were upgraded to a King Suite on arrival for the first night and allowed to stay there even though our original reservation was for a smaller suite. Staff were extremely friendly and went out of their way to be helpful. Yes, it is a little crowded in the breakfast area and the business centre is tucked behind a wall, but these are minor issues. The suites are large, clean, quiet and comfortable. The hotel has excellent parking,easy access to expressways and downtown, and is very convenient to the Arboretum and a Whole Foods. There is a decent fitness centre with a free laundry located behind it. An added advantage is that two good restaurants - North by Northwest and The Iron Cactus - are right next door about a 2-minute walk away. We would absolutely stay here again when visiting Austin.

“WATCH THOSE "LITTLE EXTRAS!"” Our family stayed at the Sheraton because my husband was a speaker at a conference there. We got a reduced (conference) rate and I have to say it was a fair price for the value. Their beds are terrific! Even the rollaway bed (an additional $20 per day) is terrific! It was very quiet, and I always appreciate that. The morning coffee and tea setup on each floor was nice. We were annoyed at the $16 per day parking fee. Seems like conference participants, in particular, should be able to park for free! We could not afford to eat in their restaurant, and the prices of bar drinks was out of sight in comparison to other area restaurants and bars. One morning we had no water at all, and one of the two elevators was out of order. Check-out took forever because of a $100 billing error. Management finally removed the five $20 "extra" fees because they could not provide proof of what the fee was for. We didn't appreciate them trying to get away with this. The location is splendid. Others on-line have complained about the airport noise--it did not bother us at all.

“Loved every second” I can’t say enough positive things about this accommodation. We stayed here for 3 nights, one month into our holiday, and it felt like being at home. There’s a kitchen/dining and lounge area, a big desk, separate bedroom (with a huge bed) and a good sized bathroom. It was spacious and immaculate. There’s a coin operated laundry on one of the upper levels. And the rate included a full buffet breakfast and secure parking. The buffet had a heap of variety and the food tasted really good. The service from all staff was of a very high standard. Having never been to Denver, I found their directions and advice very helpful and accurate. They also ensured that a delivery of a birthday cake reached the fridge in our room while we were out exploring. These people care about their customers, and for that I would recommend the Residence Inn to anyone staying in Denver and would most definitely stay there next time. Don’t even bother checking out any other places, just stay here.

“Schöne Zimmer, gutes Hampton Inn Frühstück” Das Check-In lief super. Wir hatten eine sehr günstige Rate und bekamen das gewünschte ruhige Zimmer. Das Frühstück war sehr vielfältig und lecker, allerdings war alles in Plastik eingepackt. Das Hotel liegt 5 Minuten zu Fuß von der Space Needle entfernt, allerdings ist die Innenstadt etwas weit, deshalb sollte man dahin mit dem Bus oder der Monorail fahren. Seattle ist wunderschön, dennoch war es selbst im Juni ziemlich kühl. Das Hotelzimmer und vor allem das Bad waren ein Traum.

“Just a Doll” Because that is the size you need to be to fit in the room. I can honestly say it was the smallest hotel room I've ever seen. Plus, the staff is simply functional. Not rude, but not warm either. Admittedly, the hotel has several positives. The price is reasonable. The decor in the room is nice and the bed is comfy. The major positive is that the location is not in a busy area. No taxi horns. No sirens blaring. Really quiet. Unusually quiet for NYC.

“Excellent location, excellent hotel” This hotel was oversold my first night. I arrived around midnight to find that they didn't have a room for me. They gave me $20 for cab fare and sent me to the Courtyard at 53rd and 3rd for the night. That hotel gave me a room, no questions asked, without even asking for my credit card. (An aside: that Courtyard was very nice; if I need to be on that side of town, I'll definitely consider that hotel.) I returned to the Courtyard Times Square South the following day and got a room. They apologized again, and gave me a voucher for free breakfast the next day, as well as some bonus Marriott points for the inconvenience. My room was large, with a LCD TV, comfortable bed, excellent linens, and free internet. The room (and entire hotel) looked completely refurbished, and the hotel is spotless. I was in the back corner of the hotel, so I didn't have much of a view, but it was very quiet - I never heard noise from the street. The location is excellent - between 6th and Broadway on 40th Street. Bryant Park is half a block away, and Times Square and Rockefeller Center are close by. I got one of the best night's sleep I've had on the road the first night I stayed in this hotel. I'll be back.

“Right in the center of Times Square” We stayed at the hotel in the past and knew what to expect. The convenience of its location in Times Square could NOT be any better. Of course, by staying in Times Square some things are to be expected (e.g. people, slightly higher prices, etc...). But the Marriott worked perfect for our family of four. The daily breakfast on the concierge level can be bit of a chore given the number of business travelers and events that typically occur at this hotel so I suggest you arrive early to avoid the wait or the left-overs. The rooms are clean and typically what you’d expect from a Marriott.

“Was wary, but ended up being an excellent selection” With the whole idea of "theme" floors, we were a little leery, but selecting the Curtis ended up being a good call. First, the themes aren't nearly as overpowering as they might seem. In fact, I think they could have been a bit more dramatic to be honest! But it made the atmosphere a bit different than just any other standard hotel, and yet as a Doubletree, we enjoyed Hilton Honors perks. The staff was very friendly and helpful, our room was a nice large corner room, and the fitness room was large and had lots of equipment. One morning there was a fire alarm and we had to evacuate from many many floors up, and that afternoon found a certificate under our door to use in the adjoining restaurant. A nice touch. But the best part about the Curtis is the location. It's on a street that is quiet, but it's only 2 blocks away from the action. If you are attending a performance at the performing arts center, this would be the place to be. You are just two or so blocks from the 16th Street Mall. And we actually walked to Coors Field for a game as well. A nice property.

“So noisy” I will start at the beginning I had booked a limo through the hotel i thought it would be a nice way to arrive at the hotel maybe not the car was over 20 minutes late it would have been much quicker not to mention cheaper to have got a cab I and my PA call the hotel who said it was 5 minutes away it took another call to figure out that the limo was at the limo stand even after telling the hotel that I was waiting at the international arrivals entrance. I located the driver who made no attempt to help me over the roads with my luggage and then was very sullen all the way into the city. Upon arriving I went to the front desk where a lady clerk had just finished with a guest and then started tapping on the computer she said one minute and then with out looking up said my collegue can help you. I checked in with no problems and had been upgraded ( all this meant was a higher floor ) the room that they gave me was in a quiet location at the rear of the hotel and I must say that there was no noise at all from outside. The same cannot be said for the floor staff who went in and out slamming doors the maids were the worst the noise started at around 7.00am and literally went on all day long, it is just laziness not to close a door quietly especially early in the morning. The majority of the staff are very very pleasant and efficient apart from two front desk clerks the first I have already mentioned the second was when I asked for a slightly later check out and was told I can tell you on the morning that you leave well that's no help when packing is it after a few more words he eventually agreed why not have just said yes no problem the good points are the location and on the whole the service.

“Nice Stay” Our stay at The Dupont last weekend for 3 nights was just fine. It is fun to stay in a non cookie cutter hotel room. The hotel is very convenient to the Metro and lots of things in the area. We even walked to the Kennedy Center and back. Only complaint is the towels, when we arrived there where 2 bath towels, 2 hand mitts and a bathmat. The next day we got 2 bath towels and a bathmat, so we asked for additional towels -- something to wipe our hands on. On the 3rd day we had 2 bath towels, 2 hand towels and a bathmat. It would have been nice to have a hand towel everyday. Also ESPN wasn't coming in on the TV -- not a huge thing because we were outside, but if not we would have complained.

“Nice hotel , interesting location” I recently stayed 4 nights here. The pros.: Nice Georgetown/GWU location, nice rooms with full kitchens and comfortable beds & seating in room, very friendly/attentive staff, complimentary internet. The cons: Rooms seem a bit outdated, in close proximity to GWU Hospital & a police substation so a lot of sirens at night, with lighting in bathroom the shower was pretty dark. None of these cons bothered me but if you are a light sleeper make sure to ask for a high floor 9 I was on 2). Overall it was much more a plus then a minus for me I will definitely look at staying there again.

“Will keep coming back!” The Essex House has become our home away from home in NYC. It's grand but not overwhelming, gracious without snobbery, and luxurious, comfortable and livable at the same time. The price is right most of the time, with park view rooms hovering between $280 and $380 per night. We stayed in all three types of park view rooms, the superior queen (small and cozy), the deluxe king (wide and spacious), and the suite (the size of an apartment). Black marble bathrooms are all the same size, with the Westin Heavenly bath and shower. Here's a tip I don't think anyone else has mentioned: don't order room service. Instead, ask the concierge for recommendations for very good local delivery places. My concierge pointed me to two amazing delivery eateries: the redeye grill, for american fusion seafood cuisine, and rue 57 for french/japanese food and amazing sushi, all of which I viewed the menus for online. We've already got our park view reservations for spring 2006!

“EXCELLENT CUSTOMER SERVICE” Fantastic staff ! I particularly felt pampered by Anthony, the front desk manager. My entire family was there for the weekend of 06/22/2012. Very sensitive to customer need.

“Great Location” As mentioned the staff were all very friendly. The breakfast was delicious, fresh and appetizing. The seating area was somewhat oddly arranged at the bottom of the stairs, but that may improve once the hotel is fully operational. Bathroom was fine except there was no place to put anything, not a single shelf or even a hook for the robe they nicely provide. The rooftop bar should be a great spot in the warmer months, last weekend it was somewhat deserted and way too dark. Will gladly return if they can keep up the level of service and the breakfast selection once the hotel is completely open.

“Would stay here again” I have stayed at the Hilton Times Square, the DoubleTree and now the Hilton Garden Inn. The Hilton Garden Inn was in a great location on 8th Street with lots of shops and eateries near by. It was one street away from Broadway, so seemed a bit quieter. I loved the bed and had a nice view of the city. A couple of quirks: Instead of giving me water in my room they had a voucher to turn in, that was a bit strange, I thought, but still better than nothing. Staff was very nice and check in a breeze. One star deduction because they were really slow in picking up the phone when I called to ask a question about taxis being available. First call was at 9pm, second at 10pm and finally they picked up when I called at 11pm. As these don't seem like busy check in times, I would have thought that they would have picked up their phones! And this was mid-week, not on a weekend. Aside from that, everything was nice and the room was a nice size with a microwave and minifridge. Also free wifi, which I love. If I was a tourist, I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Good value, useful location in Mid-Town Manhattan” Ideally located on 3rd Avenue and 52nd Street, this hotel is close to Bloomingdales and other stores for shopping, as well as being in a prime Business district. Rooms are a decent size, only downside being the air conditioning /heating can be very noisey when it turns on. Pleasant friendly staff. The restaurant that provides a decent breakfast. This hotel is good value at reasonable room rates.

“An overall very enjoyable stay” After driving down busy streets in Seattle to get to the Mediterranean Inn, I wasn't sure what I was going to find. The outside of the hotel might be easy to miss at first. Once inside, I was greeted very kindly by the front desk staff. They were very helpful in checking in. There are charges for parking and wireless internet, and the staff took great care to ensure that I understood that a charge was associated with those items (which I appreciate). The room itself was surprisingly nice. There was a microwave and sink. The room was very clean and the bed was very comfortable. While the room was not extremely large, the ambiance was very comfortable. The scenery around the hotel is not spectacular, though it is also not bad. I did like that there was a grocery store only a few hundred feet from the hotel, and many restaurants were within walking distance. From some of those roads, you will be able to see the Space Needle.

“Good Location but it felt old” The staff was really wonderful and my room had a lot of space, but it just felt old to me. It wasn't due to the furniture because the hotel had modern furniture. Maybe it was the light colored walls throughout. I do recall walking down the hallway to my room and thinking to myself that this felt like an older hotel. The location was really good. Many places within walking distance.

“Good solid service and they are keeping the place looking good” This property has always done right by me. Clean, comfortable, and friendly staff have always been a strong factor to return. This hotel is very busy in the summer especially on weekends. the staff has always handled any questions professionally and earnestly. Yes the elevators are smallish and overtaxed at peak times. That' s not going to change. All and all still my "goto" while in downtown Chicago.

“Classic style and low key elegance in downtown Houston” There are a couple of downtown Houston hotels that continually draw me back and the Icon is at the top of the list. I'm actually not a big fan of the downtown area, so the location itself isn't really a draw - other than it provides convenient access to the rest of town. The hotel is very quiet and an feels like an oasis in the middle of the big city. I haven't seen a lot of weddings or parties taking place here on the weekends and it doesn't seem to draw the party crowd, so it always feels quiet and relaxing any time of day or night. The rooms are clean and well decorated. There are several different bath configurations available. The basics happen to be fine by me, but pick a jacuzzi room if it suits you. The service is top notch without being intrusive. If you are looking for a hotel where you are pampered every step of the way - Icon probably isn't your place. If you are like me and prefer a nice hotel without the fuss, Icon proves to be a good choice time and again.

“Beautiful Bay Views from Balcony” WOW - I really enjoyed staying here because of the great views of the river from my balcony. I stayed here for business and the hotel staff was great and had an overall good experience. The hotel was nice, centrally located and very close to the river district, and the hotel's restaurant (Ruth's Chris Steak House) was fabulous. I'd definitely recommend this hotel and I'll stay again when I get back to JAX!

“Fantastic All Around” I read some of the reviews of this hotel and I was nervous. I don't know if there has been a drastic change but I couldn't find a single thing wrong with this hotel. Check in was a breeze and the staff was very friendly. I asked for a king size bed and they were super accomadating. She also gave a lot of detail about restaurant and shuttle:-) The room was lovely. Very clean and well maintained. I was pleased with the sleep number bed and the ample pillows that were provided. The linens and towels were great quality and made the comfort level very high! I found the location to be very convinient. I also was impressed with the restaurant and their pricing was very reasonable!! I would stay here again in a heartbeat. They were a hit with me in every way:-)

“This is a really nice hotel” I stayed here two nights in May, just before Memorial Weekend for a business conference. My wife tagged along to visit old friends who live in SA. The hotel itself is very nice. Top notch. Our room was really great. Clean, comfortable, spacious. Shower has really good water pressure and the hot water is instant. Upon check-in, I uttered the same script I say at check in at every nice hotel, "can you upgrade me to a better room at no extra charge?" The front desk gal obliged and moved us to a "Riverwalk View" room, which had a small balcony and overlooked the Riverwalk below. Nice.
