The happy hour and breakfast buffets were "ok". nothing to write home about but nothing to complain about either (except for the birds if you sit outside), especially when it's included free in the room price. Location is unbeatable. Walk to everything you need, including the Market, Alamo, restaurants and shopping, and of course you're right on the Riverwalk for strolling. The Internet worked as expected but even though I selected the faster speed would not play YouTube videos without stalling. Seems like if they are going offer a "faster" internet option (for $5 more), it should be at least as fast as a typical home cable connection. That said, as a "club" member, the internet is free, which I appreciate. My main gripe was the $27 valet parking fee. Even the nicest hotels in Austin are $20. And the self-park option, which Im normally happy to do, is in an uncovered lot in the hot sun across the street. What would have made my rating a 5? 1) Don't gouge on the valet parking. 2) "Make the "faster" internet truly fast. 3) Do something about those birds at the outside patio. Made dining out there unpleasant and we quickly abandoned the spot as we weren't look for an Alfred Hitchcock experience. Those are minor things, I know, so my 4 is a strong 4. Finally, if you are not a member of Hilton Honors, join before making your reservation. That gets you the free internet, morning paper, and some other perks.

“Lovely place to stay & free parking!” Booked Cow Hollow last minute on a recommendation from a friend. I was very pleasantly surprised. Lovely, large room with a view of the Golden Gate Bridge, located in a great little neighborhood with shops, restaurants, etc. and Free Parking (a rarity in San Francisco!) One block from the Muni stop that goes to Fisherman's Wharf/Cable Cars so we could travel all over the city and leave our car at the hotel. Had I known about the Cow Hollow sooner, I would have spent more nights there. I will definitely stay there again whenever in San Francisco!

“Nice Little Place” Had to make an unexpected trip to San Antonio for a funeral. Booked this Comfort Inn at the last minute as it was central to where we needed to go. It's a nice little place. It was clean and the rooms are a nice size. The breakfast is adequate, not anything special but they do have the waffles! The best thing was the front desk. VERY friendly and helpful. We would stay here again if in the area.

“Wow, what a beautiful place.” Me and the missus stayed here for two nights in December 2008. Very nice property. Big, clean, comfortable room. Very nice on site restaurants (also quite pricey). Do not play golf and we did not use the swimming pools, but everything we saw looked first rate. I might choose something closer to downtown on my next stay in Austin, but this resort had nothing wrong with it.

“Great Energy and a Great Stay” I stayed at the Aloft Tapestry Park for 7 nights in May 2012. I love staying at Aloft hotels because they typically provide consistently good service and value. This is a newer Aloft which was just built a couple years ago. This Aloft is built a little different than others that I've stayed at, but still follows the same concept and has a fun and exciting atmosphere. Aloft rooms are on the smaller side, yet they feel open by the way they are designed (built in desk, built in closet space, wall mounted tv, tall ceilings, etc). I absolutely love the showers and the sliding door used to separate the bathrooms. Each room has a mini fridge, built in safe, free wifi, coffee maker, and a 42" wall mounted tv. The platform beds are not necessarily the most comfortable beds in the hotel world, but they are slightly better than average, especially for a mid priced chain. This Aloft seems to have upgraded pillows compared to others I've stayed at which helps. The lobby and shared spaces set the Aloft apart from other hotels. This place definitely markets to a younger crowd and I'm all for that, you won't find any floral print wall paper here! The lobby is fun and hip with the WXYZ bar, pool table, snack area, and plenty of couches and chairs for hanging out. Their outdoor patio features more sitting areas and there is an outdoor pool built off to the side. The fitness center is fantastic with free weights, several cardio machines, and a weight machine. The service is great and the manager Scott is dedicated to make sure all my needs were met during my stay. I can't wait to return the next time I'm in town.

“Super depressing” The pictures posted here are of the better rooms. Good if you're 19 years old and on an adventure around the world, with only a few bucks in your pocket and lots of friend. Otherwise, stay away. One of the more depressing low-budget experiences.

“A Place to Be Seen” If you fancy yourself to be a high-powered, ultra-modern business executive, this is the hotel for you. The hotel looks like an office tower, the rooms look like converted boardrooms and the place has all of the charm of a Fortune 500 executive suite. My only (and major) complaint was that the wrap-around glass offering views of office-dwellers in the towers nearby extended into the bathroom. If you weren't very careful office workers who came in early or stayed late would get to see more of you than you likely meant to share doing things that are best done alone.

“Good location - Tiny rooms” Older hotel in a good location right by Lincoln Center and a subway stop (Route 1 train). There are some nice restaurants within a block, as well as a movie theatre across the street. I booked via Priceline for 1 night and was alone, so the tiny room was adequate for me but certainly not for a couple. The room was clean with updated decor and a good heating system, but I did have to get the low water pressure fixed, and lighting is not good if you need to work at a desk. Lobby looked great but there was a bad odor around the elevator bank on the Sunday I checked in. It was gone Monday when I checked out but I've not run into that issue before at a big hotel. NET: I would not seek out this hotel but it's certainly adequate with a good price deal.

“Location Location Location” As others have said, it is a fabulous location. It rained for 1/2 our recent stay but we could easily get back & forth to the hotel while others waited for cabs & got wet. We had an older room & tho a bit shabby it was perfectly adequate for our needs. The bathroom is tiny - beware if anyone has mobility (or size) issues. The cleaning staff does a great job of making old look newer & clean. Bring earplugs - the walls are very thin - we could almost hear the actual conversation of the people in the next room. This is not a luxury hotel , it is a serviceable, clean place to sleep in a great location.

“NICE LOOKING HOTEL” We had a nice room at the hotel and it had a very nice courtyard, gazebo and pool. the entrance to the hotel was also very nice. Our daughter told us that her room had dirty water and bugs. The front desk was very nice at check in and the shuttle driver was very pleasant as well. Housekeeping was good until the last day when we did not get our room cleaned. We had taken the sign off the door and had seen housekeeping staff walking around for the two hours while we hung out at the pool. We then left for the day and came back to a room that had not been cleaned. They did take the tip and thank you note however. We got a call from the head of housekeeping while waiting at the airport to say how sorry they were. She said she would look into what happened, We do not know what the outcome was.

“Great NYC Hotel” Frankly, staying in the "best hotel in NYC" is beyond our reach. This hotel is convenient, clean, quiet, professional, and not uber-expensive. We usually reserve a family suite, which is reasonable, which has a kitchen, which we do not use. Geesh, it's NYC, so who's cooking in their room? Nevertheless, we've stayed here many times. There is no street noise, which is unusual for the city, and we've never had problems getting a room, even during peek periods.

“Exceedingly large rooms for NYC” Spent one night in the Royalton. Great bar and lobby. Had expected the room to have the normal NYC size (i.e. cubbyhole with shower), but was very pleasantly surprised to find a normal sized sized room. Staff was helpful and forthcoming. The location on 44th street between 5th and 6th is quite central - which is also an issue in terms of sleeping quality: you will be witnessing to the 4 a.m. garbage removal outside the hotel. Not sure if they have rooms not facing the street, or if the others are quieter, but it might help asking.

“Hidden Inside a Business Jungle” If you blink flying by Hwy 163 you would miss this place, as it is hidden amongst office buildings, but it is worth checking it out. The prices are good for the area, and you are right in the middle of inexpensive shopping and dining, and not too far from Downtown San Diego itself (about 10 miles-7 to Old Town) The inside is very business like but also pleasant, the rooms are good sized and only a few face the freeway. The staff was friendly but I felt the food prices were kind of high. I will back to this location again.

“Good Location, Average Hotel” We were booked at the Intercontinental Times Square through our cruise line for a pre-cruise stay. We were given a handicapped accessible room, though neither of us are disabled. It had this weird closet configuration which had the rod for hanging clothes only 36" off the floor, which meant our hanging bag drooped on the floor. The room location was awful...third floor, overlooking an intersection. It also had two queens, rather than a king. Others on our trip thought their rooms were spectacular - high floor, nice view of the Hudson, for example. So, I guess we just got a bad room. Bar area is okay, though noisy, and the restaurant is adjacent to this noisy bar area. We only had a drink at the bar and dined elsewhere. The buffet breakfast, included with our pre-cruise package, was average at best and we had to hunt for someone to bring us coffee. We also were told there were no New York Times left (it was only 9:00 am) and they directed us to a convenience store blocks away, who were also sold out. When we returned to the hotel, another employee said there were NY Times available and he delivered one to our room. We gave him a huge tip. I have stayed at the Westin, which is about a block away and it's much nicer.

“Head to the Edgewater” I stayed at the Edgewater for 2 nights while attending a business meeting that was held at the hotel. This was actually by second stay at the hotel and while my first experience was not bad I beleive my most recent experience was better. The hotel is located on the waterfront in downtown Seattle and feels like (and is decorated) a lodge rather than a corporate hotel. It's walking distance to Pike Place Market and a few restaurants. Restaurant 67 is located in the hotel and there is also a bar which has a pretty extensive wine and drink list. Unfortunately, I did not have a view of the water from my room but I found the room to be quite enjoyable. The room was very clean; each room has a fireplace; the bed was very comfortable; and the bathroom has a beautiful stone shower. Guests can also find an umbrella in the closest which comes in handy given the frequency of rain in Seattle. The hotel offers wireless internet for a fee. The things that aren't so great include the business center and the gym. The equipment in the gym is a bit dated. Overall, I was pleased with my stay and would patronize this hotel in the future.

“Many Other Hotels to Go Nearby” With what you pay for this room, you're better off someplace else nearby. At $149 a night, they're trying to make this a real nice place, but it still looks like the old retirement home it once was. If you're looking for a calm quiet place hidden in the middle of nowhere land, it's ok. But it has no pool, no view, and its not exactly near anything special.

“Great Deal in the Galleria Area” I had a quick trip planned to Houston and needed a Galleria area hotel. The Hotel Indigo was a wonderful choice. It is literally steps from Nordstrom's but is in a quiet little alcove that you wouldn't even notice if you weren't looking for it. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful and parking was easy and free. The rooms are modern and welcoming with laminate floors and a blue and white almost nautical look. Although there is only a shower in the bathroom it didn't bother me at all. The bad was pretty firm but not uncomfortable. I really liked this place and the price was a bonus- I will definitely stay here on my next visit to Houston!

“Nice, nothing extraordinary” The hotel is among the most conveniently located from CMH airport. It's a typical Hampton with a nice breakfast bar. My room was clean, though the door was not in good working order (it either jammed or didn't close completely.) That was the only negative. A security guard noticed my door wasn't closed and alerted me to it (at 11:30 PM) Please don't view the "3" rating as negative, it isn't. 3 is average -- perfectly adequate -- and that exactly sums up this property. My needs were minimal and staff was friendly enough. I wouldn't consider this stay especially memorable, good or bad. It's almost exactly what you should expect when you book a room at a Hampton Inn.

“Wonderful hotel for my journey to the Pitchfork Festival” I stayed at the Palmer House Hilton to attend the Pitchfork Music Festival (I stayed July 16-19, 2009). I booked through Priceline.com (very cheap!) and was pleased with the hotel. Comments: - I thought the location of the Palmer House in the Loop was perfect. The hotel takes up an entire block, and there are three entrances, each of which is right next to a subway or EL stop (the blue, red, and all the loop trains). It was so easy to get around. The hotel is one block from Millennium Park (where the Bean is) and also about one block from The Art Institute of Chicago. - The hotel is huge. It was packed with guests the entire trip. - The room was clean, stylish, and comfortable. The queen-sze bed was firm, with nice bedding. The bathroom was immaculate, and had a wonderful bath tub. The only strange thing was that the TV was on the dresser in the corner of the room, but I only watched for about 30 minutes the entire trip. - There is no free Internet wireless, which was kind of disappointing. You could pay for one hour in the lobby (about $7) or $15 per 24 hours in your room. But, there is a 24-hour business center where you can print our your boarding pass for free. - There is a Starbucks on the ground level. (No coffee machines in the rooms.)

“Good stay at the Helix” I stayed at the Helix in February 2007 for 5 nights while on a city break in Washington DC, and found it very satisfactory. I flew into Dulles Airport, and got the Washington Flyer coach from the airport to West Falls Metro station, where I picked up the Metro into Washington itself. I initially got off at the wrong Metro stop as directions to the hotel on its website aren't that great, and with hindsight it's probably better to arrange a shuttle bus or taxi transfer from the airport. The hotel is colourful, funky and professionally run. The entrance has an automatic curtain (as opposed to an automatic door) leading into the lobby, where check-in was uneventful. My room was spacious and bright with a medium sized desk; a comfortable sofa and footrest; large TV (on a swivel stand); a large open space area; sleeping area with a large bed separated from the main room by curtains; and a coffee machine on the way into the bathroom. Perhaps best of all, there was a leopard coloured bathrobe for guest use! The breakfast was overpriced and probably not worth the hassle with so many little cafes in the immediate vicinity, but for the evening meal it's definitely worth trying out the half price deals once in your stay. They also have a (free) wine reception in the lobby every evening for all guests. Staff were friendly and responsive, and were happy to advise on local attractions, nearest metro stations etc. The hotel is in a good location, only a few minutes walk to the White House and Mall, and near a few Metro stations enabling you to get around the major tourist sites in the city. If I return to Washington I'd definitely consider the Helix again, and would recommend it for your stay, be it business or pleasure.

“Rooms are basic. Common areas are fun. Location not great unless you need to be near MGH” The hotel is not in a great location unless you are going to MGH. The rooms are very basic and the beds are not comfortable. The rooms are definitely due for a renovation. The bottom sheet is not fitted and, thus, the bedding is a mess by morning... which is a pet peeve of mine. The hotel is in the old charles street jail, so that is a draw. The rooms are so boring that the hotel only gets 3 stars.

“Enjoyed our stay at the Omni but not sure about its location” I booked this hotel because of the recommendations on this website but I did not feel as strongly in its favour as other people had done. On arrival by car It was quite difficult to access because of the one way system. Our room was lovely. It was large with excellent amenities although the bathroom was showing its age. After checking in we went for a walk to have a look at the surrounding area. We walked downhill to the jewellery district and I did not feel safe in this area. There were several people sleeping rough on the streets and one was shouting abuse at passing pedestrians. I was glad to get back to the hotel and considered moving to another hotel the next night. On a plus side the hotel is very handy for the theatres (they are in the opposite direction) and we went to see Jersey Boys which was excellent. We found the staff very pleasant and the buffet breakfast was excellent. We also had a meal in Noe restaurant and this was excellent. The hotel is at California Plaza and there is an area where open air concerts take place. This is very enjoyable and many locals come along to enjoy the music. If this hotel had been situated in a different area I would have enjoyed it more but I did not feel comfortable venturing far from the hotel particularly at night.

“Nice lobby and facilities, not the best value” I stayed here for 4 nights as part of a conference at the hotel. My room in the tower was spacious, inviting, and clean, with a nice view and surprisingly nice balcony with chairs and table. The waterfront suite that a colleague was put in was actually not as nice. Their couches were dirty, the bathroom had no fan, and the balcony was too tiny to use. The Red Marlin restaurant is outrageously expensive, but the food was quite nice. If you need something to eat and don't have a car, there is a little grill type place in a fishing supply store down the marina a ways that was actually pretty good and cheap (keep going past the "fish and chips" restuarant, do no go to that one). Otherwise, head across the bay to Mission Beach and find something there (but don't trust the concierge's recommendations if you're really picky). The pools and hot tub are nice, and towels are always available. It's nice to be out of the city if you have a car, but of course they charge you $20 a day to park! Aside from pool towels, it seems like they charge you for everything they possibly can, I definitely got the "nickel and dime" feel. Would I stay here again? Sure, just wouldn't be my first choice. If you can get a good price and want to be out of the city, this is a nice place, but don't expect a 4 or 5 star luxury resort. Otherwise, you might want to stay somewhere downtown and be closer to the action.

“Great central hotel” We arrived at the hotel by car and knowingly paid the high valet parking rate (if you don't want to pay it, street park - it's a major city). The Staff were welcoming and the room was available on arrival, despite being early. We passed through the dimly lit hallways (trendy, but I prefer to see) to our room. Spacious room, comfy beds, modern lighting / decor, large flat screen TV, safe, iron & board, small bathroom (shower over bath, not separate). Nice touch was a printer in the room, great for business use. Views are not brilliant, as the hotel is surrounded by other tall buildings. The bar is bustling and trendy, as is the lobby area (free WiFi for guests). Hotel location is great for shops and restaurants. If you are not into trendy style, try the more expensive Fairmont next door. If you like this hotel, I recommend 'Purple' for lunch, a great wine bar just down the road from the hotel and Barolo for dinner (take a cab, it's opposite the Westin but you will need to book).

“Sit in the Garden Court & Pretend it's the 1920's...or stay when the rates are cheap!” This hotel is knocked for rooms, B/Rs being too small or looking old. The whole idea of staying at the Palace is to experience a bygone era of San Francisco. Let's face it, a Hilton/Marriott/Sheraton doesn't change that much city to city. The truth is the rooms and bathrooms are small-it reminds us of a time when you went to the city to be out in the city not to measure the square footage of your room. This is a great location for visiting SF. It's walkable to Union Square and The Ferry Building. There is a Bart Station Right out side the hotel. It has a very nice pool area with a glass conservatory like roof that you can see the surrounding bulidings. The Garden Court Restaurant is decadent but amazing. Again it takes you back to a time when no expense was spared. The brunch, Jazz brunch & High Tea are $$$$ for my budget but I had wanted to stay here after I had read about it and previously walked thru it. So heres a few tips on how to do it on the cheap: watch for low rates(I got a room for $109), Instead of breakfasting at the Garden Court, grab a free tea or coffee in the lobby that they serve in the morning. Also grab a complimentary San Francisco Chronicle and head for the Garden Court. While you can't sit in the restaurant proper, there are tables in the Garden Court that are considered part of the lobby so you can sip coffee, read the paper and soaked up the ambience of the restaurant. You can even sit here and listen to Jazz on Sunday morning ( Once you decide you are ready for breakfast walk to the Hyatt on Union square and go to their restaurant for breakfast. Get there before 10:00 and you can probably get a window seat. This restaurant is on the 36th floor and offers an incredible view of SF. They serve a $23 buffet or a menu breakfast) Another tip is to request an exterior room-you want to be able to see what is happening on Market St. The hotel garage is $48. We used the Mason garage for $29 (if you ask for in & out privileges it's $30)it's about a 4 block walk but if you are travelling light-no problem. We used the bus for $2 with 90" transfer. So again if you want to experience a bygone era of chandeliers, glass roofs, history & elegance stay here, if you want modern, large- stay at the Hilton on O'Farrell.

“Nice Hotel. 1.5 miles from the Mall. Metro station 5 blocks away” Friendly Staff...Valet parking only @ $25 per day. No wireless internet, just CAT 5 cable only. During my 4 night stay, my internet did not work in my room and was never resolved by calling tech support. Was lucky enough to find an unsecured wireless access point and connected or connected via their business center. Requested king non smoking room via reservation and was told only a smoking king available. Settled for a room with double beds which was not as comfortable, but was not about to switch rooms after unpacking everything. This was like a nice small 1 bedroom apartment. 2 TVs. 2 phones. Everything you need. Nice modern furnishings and décor. No separate work area/desk. Just the kitchen table. Kitchenette – D/W, frig (w/ ice maker), microwave. 24 hour convenience store. DVD player. Complimentary breakfast and Dinner is served Mon-Thur. Check-out time 12 Noon. I would stay here again.

“An Excellent Hotel” I stayed there for two nights on business in March. I found it to be an excellent hotel and reasonably priced. The room was crisp and well laid-out. It had clean lines and plenty of light, and had a sleek and modern feeling that avoided being cold. The exception to the ample illumination was the work desk, the light for which offered very little illumination and was far from the window. It was a minor inconvenience for me, however. The lights on either side of the bed were both on dimmers, which allowed me to find a pleasant level of light, and, most interesting, the lights in the bathroom were also on dimmers – a joy at night when you can’t find your way around the bathroom but don’t want to be blinded by an attempt to re-create daylight. The bathroom was roomy and well-appointed. The clock radio was great – it had an iPod and MP3 connection, but it also brought in a number of Philadelphia radio stations and the alarm was easy to figure out. The TV was a good LG flat screen and, contrary to recent hotels in which I have stayed, it actually carried broadcasting in high-definition rather than analog, although the stations were limited. The room’s two telephones were both cordless. The closet had an in-room safe, and it offered two terry cloth robes (leopard-skin and zebra-skin patterns...), slipper-socks, as well as a complimentary umbrella for use while walking around Philadelphia. My favorite aspect, however, was the mesh screen that lowered over the window. It could be raised if you wanted to see the somewhat routine view of the roofs of adjoining buildings and Philadelphia’s skyscrapers around you, and there were regular drapes you could close if you wanted more complete darkness. However, I found that, with the screen down at night, I had sufficient privacy to lay in bed and see the lights of the skyscrapers in an impressionist cityscape that was muted enough for me to sleep and was a pleasant way to end the day. The bar and restaurant were, like the room, sleek, modern, and a little trendy, but they still had a measure of warmth. I didn’t eat in the restaurant, but it seemed well-populated. The staff was very pleasant. I wasn’t able to leave the hotel much, but I was able to walk around the area and find a couple of good and inexpensive restaurants. In short, there was nothing to disappoint me in this hotel. I can’t wait to go back.

“This hotel literally stinks!!” You can't seem to go anywhere in this hotel without having to smell the noxious chemicals they pump into the air to make the place smell better. The hallways and elevators get spritzed along with the rooms and restrooms. It's enough already! I know this is a part of a broader trend in the industry but it's simply over-done at this property. I even caught them spraying in the gym - the place was packed at 6.00 pm and some guy came in and started spraying a nasty blue spray on the carpets - I had to stop my work out. If it hadnt been for all the headache-inducing smells I would have rated this place higher. The staff are friendly and responsive and the rooms are functional and nicely furnished (although no safes). It's still in transition as they remodel in different areas so be prepared for some disruptions and noise.

“Nur für Kurz..” Zum Start meines Denvertrips wählte ich das HI ,da es Verkehrsgünstig gelegen schien, und bei HI kann man nicht viel falsch machen, dachte ich. Doch dem war nicht ganz so. Es war etwas kompliziert dorthin zu kommen, selbst als erfahrener US- Reisender, und somit gibt es für die Lage Minuspunkte. Das Hotel selber war ein Relikt der 70er und man kann nur sagen...bitte renoviert es...Die Zimmer durchschnittlich muffig... Es gab auf Anfrage einen traurigen Frühstücksgutschein, da in unsere Buchung Frühstück inclusive war, doch vor Ort teilte man uns mit ,das gäbe es nicht... nun den ..

“Stayed here many times, but its time for an update!” I have probably stayed at this hotel 6 times or more. What I like about this hotel is location, easy parking, comfortable rooms. But it is beginning to show its age and in my opinion needs some refreshing. The carpet walking back to the hotel rooms is in need of replacement. One of my biggest complaints this past trip is not being able to plug in my phone charger next to the bed. There is no outlets, unless you pick one near the desk, which isn't even close the bed. Most hotels now days have outlets in the lamps or at least closer. Overall I still enjoy this hotel. I just feel they need some updating to keep up with the times. One recommendation is have breakfast at "The Good Egg".

“Great View” I am generally not a big fan of Hyatt, but this hotel changed my mind. The front desk was very welcoming and helpful, and I got a wonderful room with a good view. I came during a fairly un-busy week, so that probably helped in my options. The room had a sort of business traveler sensibility, but was quite comfortable, and the bed was superb. The Penn's Landing location is a bit off the main drag of Philadelphia but there is a lot to see in this area, especially if you are the nautical type or interested in history. The only negative in my experience was the restaurant, which seemed really overpriced and lacking great service.

“In the center of it all in the Circle City!” My husband and toddler just came back from our weekend stay and had a spectacular time! The location can't be beat - really. Steps from shopping, restaurants, Consact teco Fieldhouse, Lucas Oil Stadium, Bars & other awesome tourist attractions. You don't need a car at all!! Room was ready early. Beds were super comfortable, and breakfast was quite tasty! I appreciate the fact that they changed the food around on our second day...simply for variety sake! Staff was really pleasant - especially the ladies in the breakfast room. Overall, you can't go wrong here.

“Great Location!” Since I am in the middle of a platinum challenge, I decided to try the Union Square W due to its proximity to our NY office. This was my first time staying at this property as it’s always on the high side for price around the area. After a less-than-average experience at the Gansevoort Park during my last stay in NYC, it was refreshing to have a fantastic stay this time around. All of the rooms have now been refreshed and the hotel staff upgraded me to a mega-room with a partial view of the park. The refreshed rooms were well equipped. The bed was comfortable and there is plenty of space in the room. The Wi-Fi was free in the hotel, which was great because almost every other Starwood I’ve stayed at charges you. Some have mentioned that the lobby staff was not very friendly. I had the opposite experience during check-in, where I was greeted with a very warm and hospitable welcome. Even the maids and the person who brought my room service (try the risotto tater-tots with truffle aioli) were pleasant. Overall, it was a great stay; I will definitely be back as long as the prices are manageable

“Decent accommodations but crappy breakfast” We booked a double room at the Holiday Inn Express using priceline.com so we certainly can't complain about the price. Overall, the room was clean, but the bathroom was a bit small. I also found it odd that the coffee pot was in the bathroom - kinda gross, but at least there was coffee. The service was friendly as well. The biggest disappointment was the breakfast - it was swamped with people and the room is certainly not big enough to accommodate the crowds. The coffee had a burnt taste to it and the food was stale. The rooms come with free breakfast so I guess I shouldn't have extremely high expectations but at the very least expected decent coffee. I'd stay here again due to the convenient location, cleanliness and friendly staff, but would just make coffee in the room and go out to eat for breakfast.

“Sorry, service at frontdesk was not o.k.” I have booked 6 rooms at my local travel agent. One week before we left Germany I called the front desk (her name was Renee) to make sure, that all was o.k. with my reservation. I was a little worried, as she could not find all the names and rooms I have booked. So I made a rooming list and faxed it together with copies of all the vouchers I had. I called again 1 hour later, and Renee confirmed me, that the booking and rooming list would be fine. When we arrived after an 9 hours flight, waiting time at customs,etc., all very tired and in need of a room quickly, nobody at front desk did know about my faxes from last week. All was mixed up, some rooms were reserved for 4, some for 2 nights, names of room mates did not fit. All of my vouchers showed the correct names and times. So we had to make the rooming list again and each check-in had to be made individual. It took us more than 45 minutes until we could go to our rooms. Renee was not on duty at that day. And nobody else did know about my reservation. It is hard to believe. Something else happend: they wanted to charge me for parking and it did take me 2 days to get the costs down from my bill. I didn ́t even think of a car in Philly... Other than that, the rooms were nice and clean, beds comfortable and breakfast o.k., but I don ́t think a mass like this should happen, when you call ahead and want to make things quick and easy.

“Hotel Carlton and Theo are da bomb” We used to live in SF and travel back from the East Coast to visit friends and family annually. Normally we stay with family but since we didn't want our family subjected to our new baby's crying (sorry Room 616) we booked a room at the Hotel Carlton. For those who know SF, the hotel is located on the periphery of the Tenderloin, a pretty shady part of Downtown, but in general the street the hotel is on feels pretty safe and was fairly busy with groups of students from a nearby Art School and guests from the hotel out fairly late. There is a bar next door that was busy with great, cheap Asian food (Thai, Vietnamese and Chinese) down a few blocks on Larkin St. We had a car so we used that to get around as public transportation (BART) was a 15 minute walk away. A bus runs West on Geary Street about 2 blocks away and the Eastbound return is 3 blocks away on O'Farrell. We parked Valet through the hotel which was $10 more expensive per night than the lot across the street, but we were told that at the front desk. It was late the first night when we pulled in and it was easier lugging the baby things to and from the car each day, so we stuck with the Valet.The staff was great about having the car ready for us in minimum time. We just called the front desk before we were leaving for the day and the car was waiting for us when we got off the elevator. The hotel itself is an older building but was clean and the rooms were a little small but comfortable. The elevators were very small and sometimes it was a squeeze to get into it with the baby carriage, but not much of a big deal. Free Wifi was available in the rooms and there were also free computers just off the lobby. The hotel advertises itself as "Green" and I noticed recycling bins in our room. They also offered filtered water which my wife used to refill a plastic bottle daily, so we did our part in conserving resources. There was also a restaurant in the hotel that received good reviews called Saha (Middle Eastern) but we had plans for all days and nights (and breakfasts too) courtesy of Yelp so we didn't try the place. The staff really makes the place though. They were friendly, knowledgeable and very helpful. We had asked for a crib in our room by email prior to arriving and it was in the room when we arrived. They hosted a Happy Hour with wine tasting which I happened upon one late afternoon when I wasn't eating, which was well-attended by the guests and Theo, one of the front-desk staffers was jamming on his electric organ, entertaining the crowd. Overall the hotel rates somewhere between a 4-5/5 and was a good value and a fun place to stay.

“Gut gelegenes New Yorker Hotel mit Flair” Das Hotel "The Roosevelt" liegt zentral im Herzen Manhattans. Der Grand Central Terminal ist zu Fuß (wenn man für sich den schnellsten Weg herausgefunden hat durch einige Bürogebäude hindurch) etwa 5 Minuten entfernt. Von dort aus fährt ein sogenanntes Shuttel im Subwaybereich direkt nonstop zum Times Square durch. Sehr praktisch. Zu Fuß zum Times Square sind es 12 Minuten. Das Hotel liegt auch unweit der 5th Ave. Vom Hotel selbst waren wir sehr überrascht. Wir hatten ein Double Deluxe Room mit 2 Betten gebucht. Das Zimmer war RIESIG für New Yorker Verhältnisse. Das Bad war super riesig mit seperater Dusche und Badewanne! Wir waren zu dritt im Zimmer und wir hatten wirklich genug Platz. Das Zimmer könnte schon mal renoviert werden ( das Bad sah aus, als wäre es schon einmal renoviert worden), aber das Zimmer war wirklich sauber. Die Lobby ist sehr ansprechend gestaltet und wirkt wie in einem 5 Sterne Hotel. Schönes frisches Blumenbouquet! Tolle Bar auf dem Dach ist ein Besuch wert! Ich würde wieder herkommmen! Super!

“Better than expected” Was a little concerned as we approached the hotel is right off the freeway, but actually very decent place. Newly renovated spacious rooms, prime downtown location, friendly staff and a good view of the Capitol. If you get a good rate here, it's worth it.

“Typical Big City Hotel” I stayed at the Hilton Austin for a conference in September 2008; the conference was also held at the Hilton Austin. It's a high quality, business hotel; everything was nice as is typical in the large, city hotels. I had no issues at all with my stay - check in, the room, the bathroom were all fine; the room was clean, bellhop great, no problems at all.

“Convenient location and great restaurant” I stayed here while attending a seminar at NYU. The location was great. It's a one block walk from the subway (N, Q) which will take you to/from LGA, with a short ride on the bus. The room was small like every hotel room in New York, but it was laid out efficiently and the decor was hip. There is a very nice rooftop bar and a couple of business center computers and printers that worked well. The best surprise was the restaurant. There was a $25 dinner with 3 courses (lots of choices) & a drink. The arugula salad was just the right mix of bitter and bitey. The seared tuna melted in my mouth. The flan was topped with pumpkin ice cream...yummy. I would go to the hotel restaurant even if I wasn't staying there.

“Our 3rd stay at this terrific hotel!” You just can’t beat the location of this hotel, right in the middle of Times Square! There are dozens and dozens of shops, theatres, restaurants, museums and other attractions within walking distance or short cab ride from this hotel. The large pedestrian walkway directly in front of the Doubletree has a TKTS Discount Booth, as well as bleachers that seat several hundred persons. We felt very safe during our 4 days at the Doubletree, and highly recommend walking the area near the hotel at night to see why NYC is a “city that never sleeps.” 45 stories above Manhattan, every two-room guest suite has a living room with a refrigerator, microwave, wet bar, desk that can serve as an eating area, sofa bed and a separate bedroom. What amounts to a mini-kitchen really come in handy for storing leftovers, or buying groceries and eating meals in the room. Roxy’s delicatessen across from the hotel on Broadway serves huge deli sandwiches and pastries that we ate for several days – it gets quite a few negative reviews from people who eat in the deli, but we had no problems ordering at the register and taking our food back to the hotel. Pax Wholesome Food is just a couple of blocks from the hotel and we also did take out from there. We had a room on the 44th floor and loved the views. Every member of the staff with whom we worked was friendly and professional. Very highly recommended!

“Not exceptional but would stay again” Spent two nights in courtyard-facing room with double beds. The rooms are for the most part updated with a contemporary vib, except the bathroom shower which was dated and had some mold around the caulking. I have stayed at several other hotels in this area over the past several years and this is one of the better options. The room was quiet (I could not hear other guests & the doors close quietly). The flat-screen TV, the white comforter duvette, abundant counter space in the bathroom, and make-up mirror are all bonuses. There are no luggage racks in the room--there is a built-in area you are supposed to use (I guess?). Check-in was easy and fast, staff were friendly. I led a two-day conference at the hotel and the banquet staff were excellent--and the food was very good. My only complaint was that our meeting hall was pretty cramped--but it was quiet. The elevators either stop at the conference level or the hotel lobby level--1/2 floor difference. So you have to pay attendtion to the button you push. The hotel is about three blocks from a Trader Joe's, four blocks from the curvey Lombard St, and in the heart of Fisherman's Wharf and cable car rides. So great location for walking around after your meeting.

“Zwischenstopp in Charlotte” Auf dem Rückweg von einer Urlaubsreise in die Karibik legten wir noch einen kurzen Zwischenstopp in Charlotte ein. Das Sheraton Airport Hotel ist nur wenige Kilometer vom Internationalen Flughafen Charlotte Douglas entfernt; kostenfreie Shuttlebusse stehen zur Verfügung. Das Hotel hinterlässt einen gepflegten Eindruck, etwas besonderes ist es jedoch bei weitem nicht. Der Pool lädt zum abendlichen Schwimmen ein, die Zimmer sind gepflegt, jedoch etwas altbacken. Was mich persönlich ziemlich stört, ist das Decken-Neonlicht im Eingangsbereich des Zimmers, welches definitiv nicht für überragende Gemütlichkeit steht. Unser Zimmer war zudem recht klein. Ein Duschvorhang im Bad ist m.E. in der heutigen Zeit ein No Go, daher auch dafür Punktabzug. 10 Dollar selbst für Mineralwasser auf dem Zimmer steht ebenfalls in keinem Verhältnis zu anderen Hotels dieser Preisklasse. Das Personal an der Rezeption war kam zwar unseren Wünschen nach, schien jedoch gelangweilt und bestach daher nicht mit sonderlich gutem Service. Aufgrund der Flughafennähe sicherlich für einen kurzen Zwischenstopp geeignet, sonst eher weniger empfehlenswert.

“This Dolphin flips but doesn't flop” Very nice personal service and the owner went out of his way to provide excellent area directions to both attractions and good spots to eat. The room was tiny, but very clean. Had a bit of a connection problem with the WIFI, but maybe it was just me. Coffee and pastries were provided but we chose the Denny's up the street instead. Small, safe parking lot in between the two buildings. Very nice to be so close to the harbor, with many great restaurants in the area within walking distance. The staff were very accomodating and we really appreciated the kind service after experiencing so many cold faceless chain motels over the years. Felt very safe at the Dolphin. Don't expect much in the way of frills or large rooms but the price and smiles are just right.

“Ganz OK” Unschlagbar ist die Lage des Motels. 3 Gehminuten vom Starwalk und von Manns Chinese Theatre entfernt. In der Umgebung gibts alles, was man braucht wie Shops, Fast Food, Restaurants etc... Das Motel selber ist nichts Besonderes. Ich hatte ein sehr düsteres, muffiges Zimmer, indem man sich ziemlich eingesperrt fühlte. Aber es war geräumig und sauber. Das Personal ist mehr oder weniger freundlich, macht aber einen eher desinteressierten Eindruck. Es gibt einen Pool mit Sonnenliegen (hab ich nicht benutzt). Garage für das Auto ist vorhanden und auch ein funktionierendes Wifi. Frühstück ist sehr basic, aber immerhin hat man was im Magen. Preis/Leistung... mag für Hollywod recht gut sein, aber dennoch sind 130$ die Nacht sehr viel für dieses Motel. Dennoch würd ich hier vermutlich wieder mal hingehen, wenn sich nichts Besseres anbietet.

“Hotel good. Noise bad.” I have stayed in San Francisco countless times. I have a little group of hotels I usually rotate between but for this particular weekend the prices at my regular places seemed way too high. So I tried a new hotel based on location, price and good reviews. It was called the Crescent at the time of booking, but has now changed names. We arrived around noon which is 3 hours before check in, but they were kind enough to give us the key early. The man at the front desk was very nice in fact. He said he was also upgrading us to a king room on a higher floor. Since we were in SF for the Bay to Breakers race which began at 7 am and lasted till an unknown time, he also offered us late check out. He said breakfast was included even though booking.com said it was not. Unfortunately, we couldn't partake in the breakfast because we had to leave before breakfast was served. The room decor was nice, modern. The bed was comfortable. I like that it had a mini fridge for my beverages. It was a corner room so we had windows in two directions. However. Our room faced the back of the hotel, which was totally fine. BUT, something was going on in the back of the hotel. I don't know if the bar had an outside patio or if it was just a bunch of people standing around in the alley for hours but we could hear LOUD talking and glasses clinking till the wee hours of the night. Then, after the bar closed and the talking quieted down, the bar poured all it's bottles into the dumpster and omg did that make a racket! I think I finally dozed off after that. What would that have been? Around 2:30 or 3? At 4:30 I was awakened by someone whooping it up. The stone buildings and the alley ways act as echo chambers. I never did get back to sleep after that. Did I mention I had to run a race at 7am? I'm not blaming the hotel for the noise at 4:30. But I do have an issue with them moving me to a room at the back of the hotel when they must be aware of the bar and bottle noise. Oh, if you do stay there and think the noise won't bother you because you'll just sleep late in the morning, forget that. The garbage trucks come at 6:15 am and dump all those bottles into their big empty trucks. Other comments about the room, the sink area was uncomfortably small, no counter space, but not a deal breaker. Most of the bulbs were out in the really cool light fixture, there was no do not disturb sign and the cool dyson fan didn't work. None of those things would keep me from staying there again, EXCEPT the noise.

“Under-staffed hotel where design is more important than substance” We were rather disappointed with the hotel. It is a nicely designed property, which has many shortcomings. It seems to me that the property is terribly under-staffed which is reflected in the house keeping standards and service staff levels. You do not a door man at all times and the cleanliness of the property was poor. Because we were there with friends, I have seen several rooms and all of them were only clean on the surface with dust and dirt in the corners. Where to start? Carpets were not fully clean, there was dust on the bed-side tables and the TV. The bathroom had hairs from other guests on the floor, the sink was dirty on the edges and the shower glass door was not kept clean so that the bottom bit had already a lot of grease on it. Overall, the house keeping department was not doing a good job. Internet is not free, neither is water. The gym is a small room with essentially no weight machines and it is, again, not cleaned properly (there were sweat marks on one of the workout benches for our entire trip and the cleaning staff never caught it). Rather disappointed with this Le Meridien property.

“One night in LA” I had missed a connecting flight coming in from overseas and decided to stay at the Sofitel as I didn't want to stay at the airport hotels. Front door/lobby a bit too trendy - with about 4-5 men standing at the door all dressed in black. The lobby is basically black too - a bit intimidating and doesn't make you feel relaxed and welcome. The guy at the front desk was really friendly and check in was efficient. First impression was the room was small. Could just fit between the hallway to get to the bed. Distance of bed from TV was about 1 metre. Lots of wasted space with the covered balcony/window but the view to Hollywood Hills was impressive. Missing bottled water in the room, so had to drink tap water. Not even sure if you could do that in LA. Did not get turn down service so was very surprised getting back to room at 10pm. The bed was comfortable with duvet cover and mattress top. Bathroom had a nice huge rose shower head about 10" but the light in the shower didn't work so it was pretty dark in the bathroom. No bath - just a shower, so if you need a bath, I suppose you have to tell them. My bathroom did not have the glass separating it from the bedroom. Ordered room service breakfast - brought on a huge tray with little nice touches and newspaper. Generally a good stay but for $300+ you would expect to. I had stayed at the L'ermitage a few years ago and the Sofitel rooms are newer and much better designed, but smaller. The room itself was a bit dark at night even after turning on all the lights. The hotel is very busy because of the Stone Rose lounge but once you get upstairs it can be quiet, except some guests would come back at close to midnight and you could hear them talking then the doors slamming shut. Wifi connection was $9.99/24 period. Regret not trying the food from Simon|LA but hope to be back again soon as it's probably the newest hotel in LA right now. No problems with service at all and staff wasn't snobbish or arrogant.

“If you want to sleep, don't stay here” I've stayed at this hotel many times for business and this was the worst. My room was on the 5th floor over Whisky Park which is an in-hotel bar/nightclub. It's right next to the check-in area. I checked in at 10:30pm and when I got in the room, I could hear and feel it vibrate from the bass from the music in the bar. At 11:15pm I called down and asked when the music would stop. Very soon I was told. At 12:30am I went downstairs and the music was so loud I could hardly talk to the person at the front desk. They said that nothing could be done and the bar closed at 2am. I spoke to someone at the front door of the bar and I think they actually turned the music up. 4 floors above the bar and my room was vibrating and I could hear the bass. The hotel will do nothing. If you want to sleep before 2am, avoid the Park Plaza.

“Excellent hotel with great service” I was down on Hyatts for a number of years after practically living in them around the world. It seemed that things had gotten too variable--especially the service. If this Hyatt is any indication, they have corrected that. The hotel was nice, clean and well kept. Good work surfaces and lots of charger plugs on the desk. The staff went out of their way to take care of you. I had to call about one minor problem and it was fixed within minutes, they called to make sure I was happy and gave me some credit against my bill for something that was just a minor annoyance.

“Excellent hotel, excellent staff” Friend and I were going to the New York Auto Show so we decided to spend the night at the Mandarin. I normally choose the Four Seasons when I'm in Manhattan but they don't offer double bed rooms, since we were only spending one night this was the best option for us. I've relaxed in the Lobby Lounge and eaten at Asiate before but had not actually stayed at the hotel. It was absolutely worth it! This is the third Mandarin I've stayed at in the US and was up to par with the others. The location and view is perfect here. Excellent staff that could not have been more professional with handy house car available for the ride to the Javits Center. The hash for breakfast at Asiate was awesome!

“Great rooms, so-so location” It seemed for awhile that the Marriott brand hotels were falling behind their subsidiary brands in comfort and amenities - if my stay at this Marriott was any indication, it seems like the flagship has finally caught up. The beds and pillows were very comfortable (always a plus for me as a business traveler, since really the only time I spend in the hotel is to sleep), the bathroom amenities were much better than previous Marriott experiences, and the front desk staff was great - even when I arrived at 1:45am. Concierge was helpful in getting a taxi on my way back to the airport as well. Only problem with the hotel is its location - great to be near some business parks, but no where near downtown or the airport.

“Stayed Here for the 2009 Columbus Marathon Good Hotel” Stayed here overnight. When all the downtown hotels are filled up early for the Columbus Marathon you have to start looking farther out. This hotel was only about I think 5 miles away. Jump on the highway and you're downtown in plenty in a few minutes. This is a nice upscale hotel...not budget or old. It did NOT have a complimentary breakfast but there was a McDonalds and Waffle House within walking distance. My daughter was racing so we ate oatmeal in the room by heating water in the coffee maker which was rough since it only made 1 cup of hot water at a time. With regards to the room I thought it was small. It had a queen bed and a sofa bed and barely any room to walk around. The bedding and flat tv was nice although the remote for the tv didn't work. I also had to pull the plug out of the wall for the tv because it kept continually going thru all the channels and wouldn't stop. We had to get up at 5:00 a.m for the race so didn't watch tv anyway. One last thing was that the sink area was located outside of the tub and toilet room and was very small single sink. With the coffee maker being on that single vanity it was very small and if you were standing in front of the sink doing anything another person has to squeeze by to get into the bathroom. Other than that, the hotel is quite and nice, in a safe neighbor hood and up to Marriott standards. and I WOULD recommend to family and friends!:) TiP: Went to Easton Center to eat. Very crowded but fun. Not far from this hotel.

“Always excellent service, comfortable and gorgeous” We've stayed here several times. We always book through priceline and usually are able to get very low rates (last time we paid $65/night). Even so we are always treated very well. The rooms are spacious, comfortable and also nicely appointed. The beds are comfortable, cosmetics were Aveda. The last time we stayed, we were bumped up to a junior suite for no reason. Not too shabby that! Best part is that there is a public parking lot directly across the street which will save you about $20 off the price of valet.

“HORRIBLE RUDE & RACIST FRONT DESK BY NAME OF GISSELLE !” I will not recommend that anyone use the Holiday Inn at Market , W Durango , San Antonio, Texas, as It is by far the most terrible hotel I have ever lodges in due to my last experience there. I was insulted for being an African American that paid through price line by a front desk clerk by the name of Gisselle. I merely called to inquire on if some breakfast cards were waiting for me. All I expected to hear was a yes , no or I dont know, but this clerk started yelling and referring to my African background ( from my booking information) as wanting to fraudulent obtain "free breakfast". I asked for a manager to which she answered - " I am manager you have to deal with me". She hung up the phone on me close to four times, then laughed as she finally transferred me to the kitchen manager. The most annoying thing was the management trying to cover her actions ups as she could not have said "that " and telling me they were sorry ' I felt that way". They also said they could see the phone conversation over a "no audio video" and she appeared calm". No audio meant they did not hear what she was telling me. They also said another "guest volunteered a witness statement that he overheard the clerk answering to a complaint" . The worst thing was my call was not a complaint so obviously it was all doctored. REALLY BAD HOTEL INDEED. Except for a wonderful clerk by the name of Nia , who I had spoken to earlier.

“Slippery slope....” I've lost count of the times I've stayed at this property as the Elysian, but my first as a Waldorf Astoria. While many or indeed most of the staff are the same, the experience is not - Reservations are a disaster, dont know availability, get reservations wrong and apparently have not transferred data on previously loyal Elysian guests. The staff weren't smiling or indeed as friendly as they used to be....Although if this was my first visit I may not have noticed as much. It's ranking just "average" with me now. Would flowers in the lobby kill them ( token gesture on the front desk noted)???

“Needs some TLC, but Regency Club is great” I had accumulated many Hyatt points on business travel. We used them for a regency club room on the 16th floor and booked a room on the same floor for our grown daughter. Her room was nice, fairly roomy. Ours, not so much. Musty smell, dust in the corners, stained carpets, hair in the bathroom. This was all taken care of when the room was recleaned. But the room was small, with one small fainting couch and a desk. The desk holds a fridge, but the wood door was warped and would not close. There was a small table by the couch but no lamp. My wife called for one but it never came until we asked the concierge in the regency club. I also accidently signed onto the Internet using the paid service when we had free Internet. My wife called to have that taken off the folio. They said they would, but the charge was still there on the day of departure. The regency club concierge took care of that as well. The regency club was very nice, with excellent food and service and a beautiful view of the bay. This hotel is very well located and gets a lot of wear and tear. It desperately needs some updating, and a better job responding to guest requests and cleaning during turnover.

“Classic Old World Hotel” I stayed at the Hay Adams in early May. This is a classic small boutique hotel in a perfect location across from the White House. In a world of look-alike hotels, the Hay Adams has its own style that is very elegant. I loved the "Off the Record" bar in the lower level---very clubby bar filled with locals . I also went to the rooftop and glimpsed at the tented party space overlooking The White House---just a gorgeous spot. The tiny lobby was elegant too---funny, I noticed someone else said they felt underdressed in the lobby in anything but a dark suit--I felt the same way. Staff was very friendly and accommodating though. The only thing I didn't love was the room. I booked a standard room, and I had one of the rooms on a lower floor facing the alley and another building just across the alley. There was very little natural light and due to the unattractive view I ended up keeping the curtains closed at all times and using lamps even during the day. The room also had a bit of an unusual, small bathroom. The garbage trucks in the alley were fairly noisy early in the morning. The room was nicely decorated so no issues there. I appreciated the free internet. I am sure my experience would have been different if I had a White House view room, but that is not what I experienced. Word to the wise---probably worth the money to upgrade to a preferred view. Still, I would give the hotel 4 stars overall---just don't feel I can give the room 5 stars based on the room I experienced.

“Beautiful architecture & setting, So-so rooms, Pretentious service and policies” Like many landmarks, the Biltmore is an experience you should enjoy once, then decide whether it merits a return stay. The main buildings are “Frank Lloyd Wright influenced” designs (built in the late 20's, but Wright is not the architect of record - although he was associated with the project), the grounds are stunning and maintained meticulously, and the surrounding views are spectacular. I found desk, concierge, restaurant and poolside service alternately harried and aloof. My sense was that line staff were too few and lacked proper training, while managers were generally indifferent to routine operations and most interested in cashing in on added-charge, personalized service opportunities. Event and guest self-parking (traveler beware - this is an extra charge NOT noted when reservations are made!) is atrocious - long distances to lobby, meeting and lodging areas. The shuttle is too infrequent for the territory it has to cover. Vehicular traffic in the lobby and meeting areas is heavy at times, and pedestrian areas are not well marked nor protected. I chose not to entrust my vehicle to the valets after watching another guest's car being used to bulldoze speed bumps and potholes en route to the (very conveniently located) valet lot. Standard rooms are smallish for a resort setting and furnishings (also FLW-type craftsman designs) look dated, with visible wear and neglect. Ditto the bath plumbing and appointments - the sense is high-dollar, but aging. Beds were comfortable, with proper pillows and comforters, but the luxury effect was ruined by cheap, thin sheets. In-room dining is Holiday Inn standard, not resort-style by any means, with standard plastic trays littering the corridors. Our family ordered pizzas; they were expensive, soggy and delivered in the standard cardboard box. Used service items were not removed promptly (actually, not removed at all prior to our departure)! We settled our account at checkout, then were surprised with a late charge to our credit card for mini-fridge items we did not use. It took three phone calls to reach someone in the accounts department with authority to remove the charge - and this was done grudgingly and with implied disbelief. This is a beautiful, elegant but aging resort property trading on location, its ”Wright-influenced” architecture, and a reputation for service it may have deserved at one time, but does not merit now. While the facades and public facilities may be timeless, time has passed the Biltmore by in terms of service and amenities.

“great hotel” I am joining the chorus for this hotel. Large, comfotable, rooms and bathroom, interesting decor, clean, etc. Front Desk very polite, professional, accommodating and friendly. We chose the "commonwealth" room, a mini-suite with curtained sitting area, and were very pleased. Good rate through hotels.com; 2 young laides at the front (Crystal and ??) weekend of 7-18 were especially gracious. Left jacket which was promptly delivered.

“Pleased with Hotel will stay again” We recently stayed a weekend to attend a Detroit Lions game. We couldnt be happier with the choice. I was a little nervous after seeing some of the more recent reviews. However I found it to be a very enjoyable hotel. Other reviewers noted the noise, we were close to the elevator and the only time I noticed anything was if I was awake and our room was comletely silent. Maybe we lucked out. The bed was incredibly comfortable and we did pay extra for a room with a view, no regrets there as it was worth it. Check in and check out ran smoothly for us. The hotel is large and my wife did seem to have a little bit of trouble navigating through. We took advantage of the movie theater located inside. A bit small but very convenient. The Volt bar was a nice place to have drinks. They serve food there as well. We did wish for a bit more on the menu as the other restaurant was closed. The coach/sig bar on the 70th floor had a nice view, but service was a bit under par. May have been because it was late. Overall everyone was extremely helpful and friendly. The food court below had a different feel (grouchy service) and we wondered how closely they were affiliated with the Marriot. But we dont feel we can hold that against them. We look forward to another stay next year.

“Excellent hotel” Very comfortable hotel - while the rooms are on the small side, there are plenty of amenities - free Internet, TV, CD player, minibar etc. The desk chair (Aero style) was very comfortable. Quality of food for dinner and breakfast was excellent. The level of customer service is high; all staff encountered were very curteous. Downsides - I had a rental car which had to be valet parked because the hotel is downtown, had to wait a while for it. Also, noise level can be high - windows are not sound insulating. Would definitely consider staying here again.

“Great 4*hotel in the right location of Boston” After a transatlantic flight, it’s always nice to be welcomed properly in a city you don’t know and this what exactly happened at the Fairmont Copley Plaza Hotel. The doorman welcomed me and I needed some change for the taxi so he directed me straight to the reception with my luggage. The check-in was very quick since my booking was already pre-paid. As always, I needed to provide an ID and a credit card for incidentals. I was on the 5th floor in a Queen room with a shower/bath room. The bathroom felt tiny but good enough to have a bath or a powerful shower. I thought the washing basin was a bit small and there wasn’t enough room for leave your toiletries by the sink. The room itself has a lot of furniture to accommodate your clothes for a week. The TV was a big flat screen which plays plenty of channels especially the HD channels like HBO or ESPN. Also a big choice on video on demand. The Internet WIFI was of good quality and you would have the choice of paying the WI-FI for 13$ for 24 hours or pick up the signal for the free WI-FI for Fairmont Gold members. Guess what I have chosen after day 3? This hotel overall is an old Lady that lives up to its high standard with a very good service throughout my stay. I had to extend my stay for one more day and the reception was happy to do so. But I found the room cheaper via an online travel agent, so I was told to book online and check at the reception whether they receive my reservation. The hotel is in a prime location of Boston in Back Bay area. This is where you want to stay if you want endless choice of restaurants, shopping and nice streets to wander about.

“Not great” When you think W you imagine design, urban, trendy and an experience. This W caters more to camper/surfer types. The staff is much too familiar and lax, the decor has a garage sale quality and seems unfinished, and no bell/valet is ever to be found. The pool is very small and has only 4 chairs, wifi is free in the lobby but the signal is always low. The lobby music was merengue 24/7. the location leaves much to be desired. The room itself is comfortable but the decor is very hamptons/boat. Don't recommend.

“Two thumbs DOWN, from a Marriott SILVER Rewards Member” This is an older hotel which must have been a remodeled former hotel of another brand, and borders a very suspect part of town (I had my tailgate stolen in broad daylight from the nearby Sheraton Brookhollow). The layout is very peculiar, with exterior (outside) entrances to many rooms. These exterior entrances allowed unobserved access to guest rooms, which is a very poor security risk in this area - a total stranger could walk directly up to my door. Additionally, the layout allows for several unlit potential hiding places for criminal activity. When I arrived to check in, I noticed several rather unsavory-looking characters loitering in the area. I always stay at Marriott, typically Residence Inn for the value and comfort. This is definitely the worst of at least 15 Residence Inns I'm familiar with. My room does not have basic silverware. I'm sure I could get some if I called the front desk, but I shouldn't have to. My neighbors are in an out of their room continually, and my whole room shudders as their door slams. The kitchen is tiny, with a two-burner electric range, instead of the typical four burners. If you need an extended stay hotel near the medical facilities, and take into account the security concerns, this place may serve you well. As for me, I'd rather try a Fort Worth Motel 6 before I stay here again.

“Pleasantly surprised on first trip to NYC” I was braced for the worst. I heard that rooms are terrible, small and expensive in NYC. My corporate rate was under $200--not sure what this goes for otherwise. I chose a hotel close to Penn Station (34th & 7th). I was able to walk to this hotel no problem (26th between 6th and 7th) from Penn. I had a great view of the Empire State Building. Room small but had all appointments--desk w/ chair, bench for suitcase, king bed, closet, etc. Bathroom small on counter space but nice; big shower. Would definitely stay here again. Staff friendly. Walked up 7th avenue all the way to Central Park (30+ blocks)--through Times Square. This is "Flower District"--good Midtown location. I felt safe.

“Good staff, location for west Fort Worth” I always like the staff here; specifically the front desk and breakfast servers. This is your typical Hampton Inn, no surprises. The location is right off I-30 making it a good location for NAS Fort Worth or Lockheed Martin but probably a poor choice for meetings downtown since you would be traveling with the traffic during rush hours. I've never noticed any road noise from the highway. Limited on the surrounding food options since the hamburger place across the street closed. There is a mall and grocery store you could walk to just across the bridge over I-30.

“Newer hotel, very quiet and comfortable” Normally I stay at the Embassy Suites but this hotel is closer to my family's home in Indy. It's basically adjacent to an office park, and there isn't much to do nearby, but it is a newer hotel, very quiet, no highway noise, and has a great exercise room. The staff is also friendly, and if you have time for a drink, you can relax in the very pretty lobby area or even sit on a little terrace. Breakfast is just OK here and the "bartender" that served us our drinks in the evening didn't know how to make a chocolate martini but he mixed up something chocolately and cold "on the fly," and I respect that.

“Good business hotel in the Seaport District” As stated, the Renaissance Boston Waterfront Hotel is located in Boston's Seaport District, which can be somewhat of a hike to the more touristy areas of Boston. This hotel caters primarily to groups and convention business, is located right next to the Boston convention center and a short cab ride from Logan. The quality of the property is above average, with spacious clean guest rooms, expansive lobby, bar / restaurant and business center amenities. The service however was rather spotty in areas (front desk, valet and phone). This could be due to the hotel catering primarily to corporate guests, but a friendly smile and welcome from the valet wouldn't have hurt. A quick call on the "Let us serve you" phone button rang for what must have been 5 times, and my request got a "yeah no problem *click*". Not exactly what I am use to from Marriott branded hotels. Also, the addition of a Spa would be a nice perk for the hotel. Overall though I was satisfied with my stay, and would stay there again if attending a convention or corporate function. Quick dining tip, the Legal Sea Foods next to the hotel is outstanding - stop by and check it out if staying in the area.

“you get more than you paid for” from the moment you step in you feel relaxed, friendly staff, front desk area that will not make you clustrophobic, pleasantly lighted and decorated. You will have the same feeling once you reach your room. from the lobby you can can go downstairs to meeting area and to bar and resturant area. Resturant area must be expanded because sometimes it is difficult to find seat. the hotel is clean smoke free and pleasant and it is the place to begin enjoying Rocky mountain.you can join tours at the hotel door as well as airport shuttle service (not complimentary)

“Great hotel and great location” This is a great hotel and the second time I stayed. They've done significant room renovations since my first stay in the late 1990s. The location is fabulous - walking distance to alot of great restaurants and shopping and easy access to public transportation. Convenient also to the airport (about a 10 - 15 minute cab ride). Only disconcerting thing was that a foreign diplomat was staying in the hotel while I was there and there were police, dogs and secret service agents everywhere! And none of the hotel staff seemed to know what was going on (or weren't allowed to say)! Rooms are small but very comfortable. Wonderful beds and great showers with two shower heads. Fitness center was adequate, but it was much nicer walking in the Public Garden and the Boston Common, which are about a block away. Definitely recommend this hotel.

“OK but I would stay elsewhere” This is my second stay at a Springhill Suites. This hotel was just like the other one. Nice enough room - very similar in quality to the Fairfield Inn's - just more room. As several other reviewers put it, this place has nothing nearby. No walking to a restaurant or anything else is possible. It is at the intersection of an interstate and another very busy road. I had a room on the interstate side and it was noisy, and the planes overhead did not help either. As another reviewer also put it, their internet connection was poor. I was involuntarily stuck at the airport one extra night - I chose to stay at a different hotel....

“Poor location but nice rooms.” We stayed here for four nights in March 2011. The rooms were clean and had all the standard amenities of a budget hotel, plus free cable TV and free WiFi. Our room contained a king size bed which was incredibly comfortable. The staff were friendly as well. The location of this hotel is not the best; it is quite a dodgy area and we definitely did not feel safe enough to walk around at night. Also, on the Friday night some guests in other rooms decided to have a party in the parking lot, right outside our room (this continued past 2:00am). I think in this case the staff should have asked them to return to their rooms or leave. All other nights, though, we did not experience any noise issues. I would recommend this hotel only if you have a car or do not mind taking taxis into town. (From there to the National Mall is approximately a 60 minute walk.)

“very convenient location and nice hotel” Right on top of the metro center subway stop, this is a very convenient and nice hotel. Rooms are nice, and they also have a nice health club facility, although you have to pay extra for it.

“Better hotels available nearby” Was in town on business during fall of '03. Seemingly, all of the $ on this hotel was spent on the lobby. The rooms were older and in need of renovation. I had to change rooms once b/c of an ant problem in my room. The staff was happy to accomodate my change, however. The older hotel also had the typical musty smell.

“More Good than Bad” Stayed here for one night on business. Stayed here after receiving this on Priceline. After reading some of the reviews here, was prepared to be disappointed. Overall though, it was hard to find too many faults wih this property. The room was a remodeled one, and was very clean. Room was decent sized, and the decor was pleasant. The desk chair was good, and the bedding was comfortable. For a place built in probably the 1970's, they have kept it up well. There is a Starbucks in the lobby, plus there are coffee-makers in the rooms. I must compliment Darryl the concierge, he is truly professional, and will go above and beyond to help the guests. Negatives were the front desk staff, which were rather cold and distant. A smile or a welcome would go far. The bathrooms are indeed teeny-tiny, but they have put in Speakman shower heads and raised them to above 6'4" level. The closet is located behind the bathroom door, took some searching to find it! And lastly, was given a room by the ice-machine and overlooking the street. Talk about noisy! I had no idea so many large trucks went down Cesar Chavez street in the middle of the night! I'm a pretty heavy sleeper, and this was at the threshold of being too noisy for me. Bring earplugs if you are a light sleeper. Overall, for the price paid ( ~$70), it was fine. If paying normal rates, I would stay at the Hyatt across the river.

“Not so great.” I stayed at this hotel one night in the summer. The rooms are dated and noisy. I think they had one of those bath-fitters bathrooms put in. No view, no charm; just really a in need of renovation. The location is pretty good near many eateries and bars. Spend your time out in the city, not in the room of this place.

“Great place to sleep” We arrived late - about 12.30am, after a flight from NYC. We wanted a hotel close to LAX as we were flying out the next day for Las Vegas. The Embassy Suites was a great place to stay as the suites were spacious, the bed comfortable and it was easy to get to and from LAX. Complimentary breakfast was good too - the usual assortment of bakery items, choice of hot cooked to order breakfasts or for something quick, cereal, fruit, yoghurt etc. The Business Centre had complimentary internet access too which was great - hotel internet access in the suite was about $10 for 24 hours. We checked out at 11am and caught a shuttle back to LAX for the next leg of our trip, however we felt that we could have stayed another night or two to explore the beach side suburbs or perhaps to get the shuttle into LA for a look around. NOTE - the shuttles to various LAX hotels pass by the airport pick up/drop off point at a fast and furious pace so keep an eye out for them and some have multiple hotels so the Embassy Suites isn't necessarily displayed when the shuttles approach the pick up zone.

“Watch your wallet at the W” This hotel charged me $500 for a reservation adjustment five minutes after making the original booking. I got nowhere with the staff over this. A complete fraud. Also the neighborhood surrounding is devoid of nightlife . So many other hotels to choose from.

“Solides Flughafenhotel” Dieses Hotel bietet ein gutes Preis-/ Leistungsverhältnis für eine Übernachtung am Flughafen. Es ist sehr gut mit dem Auto zu erreichen und bietet auch einen kostenlosen Shuttle von und zum Flughafen. Die Zimmer sind geräumig, sauber und gut ausgestattet. Auch das Internet funktioniert tadellos. Das Frühstück ist ok, ist aber kostenlos.

“Quite an enjoyable stay.” I arrived at The Holiday Inn-Fisherman's Wharf after a coach journey from Yosemite National Park.The hotel consists of two buildings,the Beach Street building and the Columbus Avenue building.I was allocated a room on the 2nd floor of the Beach Street building.The room was large and spacious with two double beds,wide-screen T.V,coffee/tea maker,iron/board and a safe deposit box.The en-suite was a good size with a plentiful supply of clean,fresh towels. The rooms have complimentary Wi-Fi and there is a computer for guests use on the 4th floor,which during my stay ran very,very slow.There are two lifts in the Beach Street building and during my stay only one was working and it was,just like the computer on the 4th floor,very,very slow. There is a coin operated laundry for guests use on the 2nd floor with two washing machines and two tumble dryers.There are also ice-making machines.The hotel has a 24 hour diner called 'Denny's'.I had breakfast on one occasion in 'Denny's' and it was a basic breakfast,just a bit expensive considering what was served up.I went elsewhere for breakfast for the remaining days of my stay.
