As the hotel is situated in the heart of a very busy Fisherman's Wharf,many attractions are only a short walk away.All in all,I quite enjoyed my stay at The Holiday Inn-Fisherman's Wharf and would probably use again in the future.

“Excellent value and great service...” We were easily able to check in with a cash deposit ($100) instead of a credit card and for $20 above the lowest rate we were offered we were booked into a jacuzzi suite. Their check in time is 3pm, earlier than most Seattle hotels. The in room jetted tubs at Quality Inn are far superior to the single person bath tubs with weak jets found in most hotels. It's basically like a small hot tub and it isn't in the bathroom, it's across from the bed. Ours had chocolates and roses on it when we walked in, but a man immediately showed up and took them as they were apparently not intended for our room. The continental breakfast is pretty decent, with the waffles you make yourself and various hot food options. The pool is large, very heavily chlorinated and insanely popular with small children. You also have to walk through it occasionally to get to the lobby, which is odd. They let us check out at 3pm and returned our entire deposit... they even held our luggage for a few hours with no issues. Overall, excellent value and by far the best jacuzzi tubs in the city. They also have this huge suite that takes up a whole floor, is pretty reasonably priced and great for parties. The neighborhood is not one where you want to walk around too much, but it's okay once you're a few blocks away.

“Everything is true and then some !” A little difficult to find at first, but once we arrived, it was great. Recommend that you find a package deal to include valet service because there's no hotel parking and the cost is about $32 per day. There is a large garage two blocks away if you want to self park. The second you enter the lobby, the fragrance will immediately take over and you just know that this is a special experience. From front desk, bellman, and concierge, the on boarding is terrific. We were celebrating our anniversary and the concierge ordered champaigne and chocolate strawberries for us - nice touch ! When booking, request a room with a view of the riverwalk and ask for a high floor as it can get rather loud at night if you're on the lower floors. The top floor has a hot tub, cafe, gym, and small pool with nice views of the city. The spa did not wow me with the facility or treatments - steam room was under repair, hot sauna was not working, and my masseuse left me feeling a little worse than better. My wife enjoyed her half day treatment and had a better masseuse who can make all the difference. We had breakfast included and it was a bit confusing as one morning, it was a $36 credit for two, and next morning, it was all inclusive. The beds are very comforable and rooms are spacious. I would come back here for the right room floor level and view, and hopefully a better spa experience. This is probably one of the best locations you can find right on the river walk.

“Great location, very basic gym” I stayed here for 8 nights whilst on holiday. The location is this hotels draw card and it is very good You are a couple of blocks from the heart of times square, which is good because 8th Ave is much quieter but you can be in the heat of the action within a few minutes. There are also a few subway stations close by. The neighbourhood feels very safe, even late at night. As for the hotel, checkin was quick and easy. The room was nice a clean, you get a coffee machine, a microwave and a fridge with no mini bar items (there is a vending machine in the corridor and a 24 hours convenience store in the lobby. The bathroom felt a little dated, and had a bath/shower but was fine overall. The bed was comfy, though the pillows were very soft. The room had very little street noise, but there was a little bit of hotel noise. In pariticular there wa an occasional thud, it sounded like some thing thudding against the room door (it wasn't though) and i heard it most nights, though it never woke me and I'm a light sleeper. My travel partner felt the aircon was loud. I think it was a bit loud, but it didn't bother me at all. Overall I had good sleep, so the noises didn't bother me. If noise gets too bad I sleep with ear plugs, but didn't need them here. The gym is basic, a few cardio machines and a very limited selection of dumbbells. But there is an excellent gym around the corner. The breakfast buffet is good, there is also an a la carte menu but our breakfast was included so we always hit the buffet. Had no problems with checkout, and the bellhop organised a car for us to go to the airport. Overall it was a good stay, a better gym would be nice but the close gym was excellent, and the hotel noise was disappointing but really didn't bother me. The location is excellent and definitely makes the hotel worthwhile.

“Gutes Hotel mit weniger Interstate Lärm” Hallo, das Hotel ist noch sehr neu. Die Zimmer sind sehr schön und gut ausgestattet)LCD,Internet). Auch ist eine eigene Küchenzeile dabei. Verstehe aber den Grund nicht, denn Frühstück und Abendessen(Mo-Do) ist inklusive. Beim Abendessen sogar Bier und Wein. Ist sehr selten in den USA. Die Interstate ist weiter weg und daher nicht mehr so laut. Der Lärmschutz ist also gut.
“Nice hotel, great breakfast.” We spent one night here on a family vacation. Very nice and clean hotel. Great breakfast, nice staff. Highly recommend this hotel. Rooms were nice and very quiet.

“Beautiful lobby, expensive terrace bar, decent room” Stayed here one night with friends. Not overly-large room, but big bathroom and the pillow menu is very interesting and fun. Downstairs, there is a beautiful lobby and a terrace bar that's cool to sit in, great food, but mixed drinks are $14 or $17! Each. That's a lot higher than most Chicago places. Mints mentioned by other posters: we received no mints at turndown.

“Worked out great” We got this hotel on priceline at the last minute and ended up in the new tower on the 24th floor. My only complaint was that the sheets on the bed were horrible, for some reason they did not go all the way to the foot of the bed and my feet were on the mattress. I am not sure what they were doing with that concept. Other than that, avoid the valet parking if you can, we did and were directed to park a block away at a rate of $28 vs $39 for the valet parking. Not only did we save $11 we also saved what looked like 30mins with all the people standing out front in the morning waiting for their cars. The location is great, it is a short (definitely not long as someone else said) walk to the market and all of the stores are right in the area around the hotel. I would easily stay here again as was a good overall experience for us.

“tough Reviewer, Great Location Value for Money if you like soft beds” We stayed 3 nights and only didn't like the extremely soft beds, other than that, the hotel is ideally located to explore the mall area Capitol Hill and the Smithsonian Museums. a 10 minute walk to Union Station. Hotel had Free WiFi in the lobby which was also a vibrant cocktail bar to boot. a great social location to hang out and catch up with people back home on line while enjoying music and a drink.

“Yet another wonderful Kimpton hotel!” I really wish Kimpton would expand to more cities (and Europe!); they have been universally excellent and a tremendous value (and no, I don't work for them!). As with all other Kimpton properties I've visited, the staff were uniformly friendly, efficient and fun; every employee seems genuinely interested in making sure you are happy, from the doorman to the reception folks to the managers. I had booked an 'executive Queen/Queen room, and it was huge, over 500 sq ft, and very nicely furnished, with a very comfortable bed. As others have mentioned, the bathroom didn't match up to the standard of the room, in size or luxury, which was surprising... As usual, the evening wine hour was staffed by an assortment of friendly employees, and while the lobby seating was limited, this served to encourage mingling among guests. The restaurant was excellent and very reasonably priced, and the location near DuPont Circle was great. Being pet-friendly is a plus for us; even though our dog did not accompany us, it is nice to see and pet all the cute pooches in the lobby and elevators, but if you are afraid/allergic, then this could be a problem. I will definitely try to stay in this property the next time I visit DC!

“one of the best if not the best in Manhattan” This is probably the freshest/ cleanest feeling luxury hotel in Manhattan. Since NYC can be so gritty we really appreciate that about the Mandarin. The service is definitely not as warm as others we have stayed at but certainly efficient. We did have a problem every day reaching the concierge from the outside, though. The rooms are very nicely appointed with some great park views for a price. We paid with Amex Plat and the hotel was not full but we were not offered an upgrade. The rooms are not huge as you are in NYC. We loved having the access to the basics of the Time Warner Center - reasonable food, bank, etc. The location is not NYC's poshest (Columbus Circle/ Lincoln Center can feel very commercial), but gives you access in all directions.

“The best hotel in New York!” Stayed here last week based on Trip Advisor reviews, it was the best hotel I've ever stayed in whilst in NYC. The room was huge and extremely comfortable, with amazing amenities and a fab view and the bathroom, wow the bathroom! The staff were stunning, so helpful and friendly. I've stayed in many hotels the world over, but the Distrikt is my new favourite, it's so good that I can imagine once the word gets out, rooms will be booked up well in advance! So I shall be sure to book well ahead to secure a place at my new favourite hotel. Cheers Distrikt hotel & staff for a fabulous stay in NY!

“Excellent Hotel!” Walking distance to Pier 39 and 33 (Alcatraz Tour) Hotel was flawless. Staff was friendly and helpful Immaculate Service. Would stay here again. Valet parking was a little pricey but it was in and out 24 hours.

“Excellent Staff, Great Restaurant, Near Arts District” Just stayed at the Fairmont Dallas for a convention meeting and trade show. We were greeted by name at the car valet, the bell service and the front desk. We had breakfast two days in the restaurant, which offered both buffet and full service, we enjoyed the bar in the afternoon, and the Pyramid Restaurant served foie gras (yum) plus an excellent cod for the entree. Tony Bennett is a character in the bell service. Very, very friendly.

“Cute, quaint, and a bit on the pricey side” Loved this little place. Have been numerous times during the concerts and decided to stay one night recently. With a concert ticket around $100 and the junior suite for just over $200, it only made financial sense to check it out for two of us. We didn't really want to "see" the concert so much as "hear" it. So we picked the lineup, grabbed some veggie munchies from a local restaurant, and sat around the pool and jacuzzi area during the concert. There is a small bar and they have snack service by the pool for guests. Wonderful! Room: Nice room. Reminded us of a glorified Best Western or Quality Inn. Certainly not something we want to do more than once, but was fun for this particular occasion. Since the venue doesn't sell the rooms with balconies at the back of the concert area, it only makes sense to get a less expensive room if you're just staying for the concert. Parking is a bit interesting during concert nights, but the hotel does a good job with reserved spaces and ensuring there is room for its guests. Bar is a bit overpriced. Go around the corner to the liquor store and make up your own bar in your room. Great place to walk, bike, explore on foot. Wonderful rentals (bikes, jet skis, sail boats, motor boats, segways) are available so you can go out and enjoy the beautiful sun.

“Low value, depressing rooms” I was staying for two days in Austin for business and had to take my daughter with us. We wanted to stay at the Omni, but they were booked full for the first night, so we stayed half a block away at the Stephen F. Austin. The front desk and bell staff were suberb -- very personable and competent. The restaurant was overpriced but excellent -- the best queso (with mushrooms!) we have ever had. But our room was, frankly, very, very poor for what we paid. As another reviewed mentioned, this is not what I expect from an Intercontintal! We were in a King room, which was barely large enough to fit the King sized bed. The tiny window gave us a perfect view of the window units of the neighboring building. The carpet was worn and dingy. The only positive thing I can say is that the bathroom was huge -- they seemed to have divided the room in half and made half the bathroom and half the bedroom. In contrast to the depressing bedroom, the bathroom was gorgeous: It had a nice cubby with a beautiful red marble-topped vanity, marble sink top, marble-tiled shower. I found myself periodically escaping the dreariness of that awful bedroom by retreating into the bathroom. If you want to spend time in a $220+ bathroom, this is the place for you. If you want to spend the night in a clean, comfortable bedroom with a nice view -- avoid this place like the plague. I travel to Austin several times a year. I will never stay here again.

“Perfect!” The Park Hyatt's are always wonderful - and the Washington property is no exception! The restaurant is superb and the staff is wonderful.....plus, the rooms are very spacious and comfortable.
“Really cool hotel!” I enjoyed this hotel!!! It was modern and very clean. The staff was super nice. The rooms were also very spacious! I will deff return again!

“Good Value” You get a lot here for your money.We had a 2 room suite with a balcony that gave a partial view of the river. The rooms are a little dark and dreary for my taste, but they were comfortable enough,and considering that the room cost much less than most hotels on the Riverwalk, it was a real bargain. The Belgian waffles for breakfast, and the afternoon drinks were very good.There is free internet use in a room off of the lobby. The rooftop pool was nice enough, although not heated. The gym was really bad-only 2 treadmills and 1 bike. Parking was reasonable.I think housekeeping could have done a better job-the carpet was on the dirty side, with candy found in the corner and under the beds. All in all, I would stay here again.

“Great hotel” Right by the BART station--transportation hub. Lots of food steps away, from fast food to very upscale. At the terminus of the cable cars that can take you up to Fisherman's Warf/Tourist Mecca. Was here for a conference, and it was just about perfect for that. Great beds, nice shower. FAST elevators. Friendly and helpful staff across the board. Would be nice if it had a fridge (I didn't ask for one--I'm sure they would have provided.) And the room was quite clean and new, but--well, I'm fussy and the furnishings needed to be more carefully cleaned. It can get a bit noisy on the street on the weekends, though I didn't need the provided earplugs. Overall, I would happily stay here again.

“Good Hotel/Great Location” I visited The Palace with my 3 kids--we don't usually travel without my husband--but I felt very safe at The Palace. We considered the Fairmont--but I am glad we chose The Palace--I loved the location. We took BART in from the airport & it is right across the street from a BART stop. Also, walking distance to Chinatown--which is nice for an inexpensive dinner. There is a Boudin bakery across the street--we had breakfast there each morning--Boudin is amazing--great food & the people working there were exceptional. The Palace is an older hotel--lots of charm. The room we had was a bit noisy--we were put on the pool floor because of the kids & it did get a bit loud at night. The room needed a deep cleaning--lots of dirt in crevices & corners. Beds were doubles--not as comfy as they could have been--but ok. The pool area was nice--but the air temperature in the pool area was chilly. The concierge was grumpy--but the front desk staff was fairly helpful. Check out took longer than at most places--they don't have a quick check-out option--which I love. Also, the preferred guest desk was not used for preferred guests--so I had to wait in line with everyone else. All in all it was a decent stay for the price--I would stay again for the location. If you go to Chinatown, I would advise finding a good restaurant in advance---we chose to wander & find one that looked good. The first night we tried the Floating Sushi boat which was pretty good--but the second night we had a bad experience at Four Seas restaurant--it is right on Grant (the main drag of Chinatown)--& they get a lot of business because of the location--but we hated the food there--it was served cold--meat was way over cooked & service was extremely slow. It was a bad eating experience--I would avoid & find a place that is recommended by someone local. I would recommend Chan's Art & Gifts for touristy shopping--the owners are very nice & have great deals for purses, jewelry, etc.

“Nothing to write home about” Stayed here two weekends ago. Hotel is covered with scaffolding so, at the moment, not very inviting. There was nothing on the web site indicating that this was the case and that any room facing the street on one side of the hotel would have the scaffolding as the view. Room was small, standard Hilton. Could not understand why there was only one bathrobe available in a room with a king-sized bed. Restaurant had decent, but overpriced breakfast. The wait staff was very friendly, desk staff helpful when we reported something broken in the room (actually two things were broken. They were repaired quickly.) While the hotel was a short distance from most major attractions, the area was fairly dead at night. On the positive side, it was quiet and there was not a lot of street noise. Hotels in Boston are very expensive (surprisingly so) so we chose this hotel because of a favorable rate, but we would not choose to this property again, because it felt flat and a little worn out.

“Very nice” Stayed here one night in February 2008...great beds, large, spacious room, and the breakfast was one of the best i've ever experienced at this class of hotel - sausage, eggs, it was great. This La Quinta is centrally located yet off the main street, so its quieter. Pretty good price too considering the location, amenities, etc. Would stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Great hotel in convenient location” Registration process was flawless. Arrived at hotel before 9:30am. No problem. No waiting. Finished registering a minute w/o having to sign anything. Room was good - comfy bed, clean, all amenities. Bathroom light went out and hotel had someone fix it within 15 minutes of calling front desk. Only "complaint" was that the LG flat TV only had analog channels. If hotels upgrade to large flat TV screens, why in the world do they not provide HD reception? Internet access $10/day with a fast connection - wired or wireless in rooms, wireless throughout hotel. The hotel is connected to Copley Plaza shopping center and and Prudential Building with its shops and Sheraton Hotel, and across the street from the Fairmont Hotel and its Oak Room bar and restaurant. Guests have 24/7 access to a computer and printer in the lobby for printing airline boarding passes. We asked for and got a late check out (2pm). We'd definitely come back to the Westin Copley.

“Charme e Cortesia a New York!” Ecco un BELLISSIMO hotel nel pieno centro della Grande Mela. Si tratta di un albergo storico con arredi di grande charme e atmosfera a cui si unisce una grande comodità (funzionava proprio tutto), tra cui segnalo un letto favoloso. Lussuoso senza sfarzi ma con grande buon gusto, di questo hotel mi ha molto colpito la cortesia ed affabilità del personale, cosa rara per NY, e la posizione perfetta, 5 minuti a piedi da Times Square e da Gran Central Station. Non ho fatto colazione in hotel, anche perchè esattamente di fronte di trova una bellissima caffetteria, nel caso vogliate ottimi caffè e squisiti croissant in ambiente di design, e subito a destra c'è una tavola calda nel caso preferiate sontuose colazioni americane. Ottima la concierge per la prenotazione di tour e biglietti. Simpatica la presenza della gatta Matilda. Il migliore indirizzo che finora ho trovato a New York.

“Beautiful hotel” The is the best of the LA hotels I have stayed in recently. The rooms are beautiful and clean and recently updated. The hotel seems to be a little quieter than some of the others in the area (in a good way) but still has the same amenities and feel. I would recommend, and will stay here again when visiting LA!

“A great place......” I have been here about 5 times in the last five years...and have enjoyed it. The staff is a little pushy, but the rooms have been recently renovated and I will stay here again. Great location!!

“Average overall; horrific self parking” The hotel itself is clean and relatively modern. I would consider it a 3.5 star, though. There is a bar, a very helpful concierge, and decent views. It is a medium walk to the historic sites, far from the art museum, and in a safe area. The room was at first glance very good, but small things (that don't necessarily bother me) were evident - tears in the carpet, nicked and worn furniture, etc. Room service prices were reasonable, TV reception good, and the bathroom was large. They are not pet-friendly, which is outrageous in the current hotel climate. Almost every other 4-star property has some type of pre-planned accommodation for pets. This is a shame and may keep me from Hyatt in the future. Other review have pointed out the parking, but I have a DIFFERENT take. It isn't the walk that bothers me (it really isn't that far, just pay attention to well-marked paths and you will be in the lobby quickly). The first issue is there is ONE elevator from the lobby to the parking, and it is very small. At various times the wait was more than 5 minutes to get on the elevator. Imagine this at check-in/check-out times. There is also no quick way to walk to the parking garage, which makes it very difficult to get your car. The second issue is enormous: After checkout we waited THIRTY MINUTES to leave the garage. There is ONE way out, with ONE lane, and ONE parking attendant. It was a complete madhouse (this is not an exaggeration). People were trying to pass on the up ramp, causing many near accidents. Horns were blazing, etc. This issue could be easily fixed - especially since the hotel knew about it (they finally sent someone who, with seemingly no rhyme or reason, started letting people leave through the out gate while making others wait). They could 1. notify people that at noon the parking garage is insane, so plan ahead, or 2: change the system by which you leave. You have to give them your parking tag number, your last name, and your room number. The attendant writes this all by hand. It is an astoundingly poor way to leave the garage (even when NOT checking out). Of course, you could avoid this by paying for the valet service. I would recommend doing this. But it does NOT excuse the poor handling of the self-parking. OVERALL: I would not pay full or even half-price for this hotel again. The lack of pet accommodations, a decent parking structure, service related to parking, breakfast, 4-star accommodations, and shuttle service to other areas of the city make it unreasonably priced. You could find deals on many other 4-star properties for around the same price (albeit higher parking charges), but they will have better overall service and accommodations.

“Buona posizone” L'albergo è davvero carino, pulito silenzioso e a 4 passi da diverse linee della metroplitana (1, E,..). Ha anche una grande piscina e un'ottima palestra. Colazioni (da pagarsi a parte) discrete ma non eccezionali.

“Reasonbly good deal” I've stayed at this hotel several times, and it remains the same. The rooms are a typical layout with a bedroom area and a "living room" area. The rooms are large, but bathrooms are very small. Lighting is good; there are lots of outlets and plenty of space to spread out. A real negative on this trip was the lack of temperature control -- some people found their rooms very warm, and some very cold with no way to alter the temperature. Those who complained to the front desk were told that they couldn't change anything -- at least one person got a space heater. There is a complementary breakfast that is well above average, with someone there to make custom omelets. There is also a complementary cocktail hour with some minimal snacks. The hotel is located across the street from an up-scale mini-mall with green space that is good for people watching. The mall also has several very good restaurants. There were lots of pillows, but they were all identical and not to my liking.
“Stylish hotel” Friendly staff, great location to times square, very expensive room rates, not worth the premium over comparable hotels.

“Decent hotel, great location....I would return....” Stayed overnight in NYC with a friend for a pair of Yankee’s games. When traveling, I try to stay in Hilton brand hotels since that is where I focus most of my points to, and I am a little bit of a “hotel snob,” meaning I will pay more for a decent place, especially in NYC. I know NYC fairly well and whenever I stay overnight there, I try to stay in Midtown and close to Times Square if possible. It is hit or miss....if you are traveling at a peak time; any room in Midtown will probably be out of most budgets. There haven’t been many times I have gotten a decent “business class” hotel in NYC for under $300 a night. Welcome to the Big Apple! Since I was trying to keep costs reasonable, I looked at hotels in Lower Manhattan and the Millennium Hilton was the best deal going, and for much less than the midtown hotel rates were going for. All in all, the Millennium Hilton is a decent business class hotel and I would certainly stay there again. The lobby is fairly basic....there is a small bar and seating area that serves perfect as a meeting place before you go wherever you are going to. The location is awesome....right next to the 9/11 exhibits and memorial. South Street Seaport is less than a 10 minute walk away and we went there for dinner. And best yet, the PATH and NYC Subway (several lines) are within a 5 minute walk. To get to Yankee Stadium, simply grab the E train (2 minute walk) to Midtown and switch to the D train (several transfer options below 59th St) which will take you right to the Stadium. About a 30 minute Subway ride. You can also walk a few minutes and grab the 4 direct, but that seems a little longer since the D is express after 59th St. The hotel is very tall but there are only about 12 rooms per floor....so it is pretty quiet from a “hallway noise” perspective. We were about 1⁄2 way up the tower on the 25th floor and we could hear “street noise” in the background. The A/C works well, but is dead silent so if you like “white noise” when you sleep, bring a noise maker. Since the tower is over 500 feet tall, odds are you will probably have a decent view. The room was decent, modern and clean....average size for NYC...but on par with any Hilton business room in a major city. There is a mini bar stocked with $7 beers and the bathroom was nice. I learned from a bellman that after 9/11 the entire hotel was pretty much gutted and remodeled so everything has a pretty “new” and modern feel to it. If you are looking for all the “hustle and bustle” of Midtown, stay there. Lower Manhattan is clearly more “Wall Street” and businesslike in nature. But within a 10 minute subway ride, you can be in Midtown, and there is still a lot to see in Lower Manhattan anyway.

“Good Hotel / close to Metro” Did only stay for one night in a Studio Suite. The room was clean and spacious. They offer free dinner and breakfast with the room rate. The Metro station is around the corner. Friendly front desk. Would return for longer.

“Tolles Hotel mitten in Downtown” Ein super gelegenes, tolles Hotel inmiten von Downtown. Hatte ein Zimmer mit zwei Queen Size Betten, supersauber, tolles großes Bad, sehr nettes Personal. Hatte über Priceline gebucht und einen gigantischen Preis erzielt ( 4 Sterne Indianapolis Downtown für 59 $ plus Tax). Wer nicht im Taxi zum Flughafen zurück fahren möchte, kann gegenüber, am Convention Center (der direkt über eine Brücke mit dem Hotel verbunden ist) den IndyGo Green Line Bus nehmen, der einen in 25 Minuten für 7 $ direkt zum Airport bringt. In der Nähe befinden sich zahlreiche Restaurants und tolle Shopping Möglichkeiten. Würde jederzeit wieder in das Hotel zurückkehren.

“Elegant stay, attentive service” First things first - if you're going to stay in a hotel that's in it's second century of operations, expect the floorplan NOT to match your expectations of a newly-built hotel. In fact, the architectural uniqueness of the Brown lends to making your stay so memorable. EVERYTHING about the Brown is elegant - but Denver casual-elegant, not uncomfortable stuffy foo-foo elegant. The staff is calm, poised, and attentive. I cashed in airline miles for my stay at this Denver landmark - a dream of mine for years. (My Grandmother actually worked here for a time!) Using points usually means small room with a view of a dumpster. Not at the Brown. I was in 703 - a Superior King room - spacious, with historical details like period light fixtures in the foyer, with the most luxurious updated rain shower bath! Don't forget to enjoy your personal pitcher of artesian well water drawn from the hotel's own spring, placed in every guest room. My stay exceeded my expectations. I just wish I'd been there longer than one night!

“Good value, great transportation options, so so street life.” My wife, infant son, and I spent two nights at this Hilton Garden Inn while visiting family in DC. We enjoyed the stay and will definitely be back. The hotel is located in NoMa neighborhood which is primiarly filled with large office buildings. The hotel is only a block from a red line metro station or a fifteen minute walk from Union Station. In the same building as the hotel is a supermarket, coffee shop/bar, and restaurant. Across the street is a drug store. Other than these ammenities though it seems that there is not much else in the neighborhood. I overheard a hotel employee recommend to another guest to take a taxi to Chinatown for the best selection of restaurants. We had originally booked a room with a king sized bed. Upon check in, seeing our baby, the hotel staff recommended we switch to a room with two queen size beds. It turns out that all of the king sized rooms are located at the front of the building and across the street from the hotel is a club that seemed to be very loud on Friday and Saturday nights. While we were grateful for the suggestion and enjoyed our quiet room, it would be nice if there were other king size rooms elsewhere in the hotel. Our room was nice. We were located on the 14th floor which was quiet, even with both rooms on either side of us being occupied. There wasn't even that much hallway noise. The bathroom was standard and fine and the beds were pretty comfortable. There was an empty minifridge and a microwave for our use. The hotel staff were very nice, always greeting us and asking how we were doing. We had a package mailed to us at the hotel and it arrived w/o a problem. Although we didn't use, there is an indoor pool, restaurant, and gym for use by guests. Also, there is a Capital Bikeshare station in front of the building which made getting around DC very convenient. We will definitely stay at this hotel again when we are in town. The service and facilities were good and the location was great. I probably would not stay here if I wanted things to do w/in walking distance, but its proximity to the metro and Union Station are great.

“nice hotel” we booked 2 double rooms - for a week- with priceline but when we arrive the rooms were not ready so they give us a choice: wait or pay more to get a bigger room - expencive rooms are always ready, remember- we take a bigger one. the rooms were quite big (one of the two was bigger than the other one but the price was the same), clean, with a very confortable bed but a little dated furniture. There was also a small kitchen. Service is ok. Probably the whole property is a little overrated, but it can be a good choice for a nyc stay, good location.

“Valentine's/President's Day In Chinatown” It's not a hotel, hotel, it's more laid back. No doorman, no bellhop, ok by us, just very little work to get settled in. Room was big, Queen Deluxe, (2 beds). The heat took a little patience on our part, bein from NYC we want everything quick, just take your time, it takes a few minutes to kick in, red light will illuminate, rutters will move, very slowly, then we were sweatin once it kicked over. Nice flat screen TV, view out the window of E. B-Way, nothin big, trains on the manhattan bridge, noise did not faze us. Spotless nice size bathroom, all said and done, 275. Balloons for NYC on Presidents Day/Valentines Day weekend, can't beat it. Cabs were hard to find, drinks too, no bars in sight, not after walking either, oh well. We found a nice dim sum house called Golden Unicorn downt he street, 18 E.B-Way i believe, 2nd floor, get there early if ya don;t wanna wait, they open 10AM, 9AM weekends, wild aggressive loud atmosphere/ambience, however, good food. We would def go back to Hotel 91, clean, great price, what more do ya need?

“Quiet respite” Overall, a pleasant experience. Love the Grohe shower head and huge towels. Loads of hot water. Room service was spot on. My spa experience was excellent. Turndown the first night was terrific; not so the second night. Room was a bit small for two people. Valets could have been more attentive.

“Crash Pad” The room was clean & tiny. The bed was comfortable. The front desk staff was friendly. The bathroom was hard to navigate in. The walls were thin. The entrance is industrial and clubby with weird lighting and loud, pulsating music. I was not expecting luxury after reading previous posts Tripadvisor, but this room is suitable if you have activities in the area and need a place to crash. There is a charge for using the standalone pc on the floor, which I think is unusual. The toiletries were nice. There was no coffee station in the room but plenty of options if you step outside.

“small but good” We have spend here 3 nights. The staff is very helpfull, the rooms are small but clean. The breakfast whas very good and also the dinner in the restaurant beside the hotel whas good. This is a nice and safe aria with a lot off shops and restaurants nearby and they have a nice terras. If we come back to New York we will choose this hotel again.

“all was good except no coffee...” I arrived at 300pm for a 10 hour stay..semi truck parking next door at the Mcdonalds...room was $99.99...about $25.00 higher than the motel across the street..although this place is almost new and the Clarion is fairly old...lobby was beautiful...room was great ...comfy beds...great water pressure..clean...everything was top notch...just wish they could have dropped the price a bit more since i was only staying 10 hours and would not be eating breakfast...only real complaint was they did not give bottled water to gold members or have coffee when I checked out at 100am...

“Needs Some Upgrades” The Riverwalk Hotel is in a convenient location to downtown Detroit (although a bit out of the main business area). The rooms are spacious and clean. The grounds of the hotel are contiguous to a river front trail that offers a decent place to run. Finally, the hotel offers a shuttle service that is really generous in their transportation. There is, however, something "off" about the hotel. It is not anyone thing - but more a general lack of attention to detail. An example of what I mean by this statement - we went to the bar in the basement of the hotel. The bar was sparsely populated. The server worked hard to get us a couple of drinks - but had a difficult time getting a beer as they were sold out of almost every brand we ordered. Given the lack of amenities around the hotel and the older decor of the facilities - I would suggest that anyone with business in the downtown core of Detroit consider staying closer to the city center.

“コストパフォーマンスはよいと思います” 激安ツアーで泊まりました。サンフランシスコの中心ユニオンスクエアからはバスで移動します。15分ほどかかりますが、バス停からは近いのでさほど不便はありませんでした。ホテル自体は可もなく不可もなくといった感じです。 TCをフロントで現金に交換してくれるのが便利で毎日やってました(ただし一日$50まででした)。 寝るだけと割り切ればコストパフォーマンスはよいホテルだと思います。

“Top Notch Staff” It's a hotel's staff that make or break a stay, and the staff at the Westin Michigan Avenue made my stay memorable. Each interaction left me smiling. The hotel staff seemed genuinely eager to serve, and appreciative of my business, and they remembered my name even after only one interaction. A true mark of attentive service. One thing I might mention is the hotel restaurant, "The Grill On The Alley" appears not to process room charges when presenting your check. You're not given a pen, nor is there space on the ticket for a room charge, but if you ask the server for a pen, you can fill in your details and they will do a room charge. A hotel this size really ought to have a pool, but the Four Seasons spa is across the street, so there's no need to fret.

“Winner” I get to San Diego somewhat regularly, and this hotel is becoming my go-to. You can typically find good rates (use AAA to cut parking in half), and the location is great. The free wine/sangria hour is a good way to start the night, and this stay I was greeted with a $10 mini bar voucher simply by being part of the loyalty program. There are so many dining options within 3 blocks that you will never go hungry. Maybe not the best choice on family trips, with the modern vibe and rooftop bar noise, but otherwise a great stay every time. Plus it's 10 minutes to the airport and the freeway; great spot.

“touristy hotel” Perhaps not surprisingly given its location, this hotel is rather touristy. Also, I have found domestic Sheraton hotels to be a bit downtrodden, which applies here. Having said that, they always recognized my Starwood status and treated me well at this hotel.

“Stayed here 5 times in 6 years for a reason” This is my wife and my favorite hotel. We love SD and this hotel has no frills but a location that can't be beat. This review for an overall 5 is because of the excelent views. I've written a review on this hotel before but not since the remodel. The rooms and hotel are very clean. Get a full ocean view room to get the spectacular effect of the beach and ocean. And best of all enjoy the beautiful so-cal sunsets. The hotel is centrally located within walking distance to restaurants and bars. The rooms are remodeled with a new flat screen tv (like you would ever want to watch tv). The staff is very friendly. If you want a deal get on their newletter and they run pretty good deals. We will be back to San Diego and we will stay at Ocean Park Inn. AGAIN.

“Great if you can get a good rate” Staying at the InterContinental San Francisco was a sharp departure from where I normally stay while vacationing in San Francisco. I have had the pleasure at staying at all three of Mobil-rated five-star hotels in San Francisco and wanted to try something different this time around. I gave the hotel five-stars in consideration of the how much I paid for the room and all the amenities I received. If I paid, say $300 or $400 for the room only, I would have gave the hotel three stars. I wanted to share some of my tips for staying at this particular hotel. For California residents, IC offers a “Staycation” package which is inclusive of valet parking ($46 + tax per night), buffet breakfast for two including gratuities and taxes (otherwise, $25 per person) and a $10 credit to your guest folio. I HIGHLY recommend this package to California residents. You have to find the package on the hotel’s website under the “Experience More” tab and book from there. I was given a rate of $159 for a Standard room—this rate is the same as their “Best Available Rate” which is normally reserved for the room only. Since this hotel is buried within the city, there are really no “views” to speak of. There are only different vantage points depending on what floor you are staying on. I believe the hotel goes up to the 33rd floor? I recommend booking the room with the most appealing rate and asking for an upgrade at check-in (whether it is gratis or you pay a small “upgrade” fee). Keep in mind you need to add 14% accommodations tax (this is the “sales tax”) to your room rate. This hotel has a club lounge and here are my thoughts about it. Generally when you book a room with Club Access (for two people), you will be on the 31-33rd floor and it will be about $100 more than a comparable room. If you want Club Access and want to save some money...when you check-in (if the option is available) the supplement is $80 (for two people)- you save $20. The caveat is you could be on any one of the 33 floors of the hotel. The club lounge is open from 6:30 AM to 10:30 PM. Unless you’re staying on a corporate account, this option really does not seem worth it to me. Can two people really eat $80 worth of food? Each additional guest is $40. I would much rather pay $100 for club access if it were the Ritz-Carlton (this option is available at the Ritz San Francisco). Club access affords you food presentations throughout the day, internet access WITHIN the club lounge, and various reading materials and possibly garment pressing (not sure). Other reviewers have mentioned the amenities in the room so I will forgo my usual review and give a synopsis of little quirky things about the hotel. Check-in is at 3 o clock PM and check-out is Noon. Your room is fully equipped with an automated mini-bar (similar to Las Vegas) and it will charge you when you remove something almost instantly (even if you put it back). A Snickers bar costs $6.50. A small coke costs $4.00. When you order room service, you are automatically accessed a $3 delivery surcharge, 18% gratuity, and local sales tax (8.5%). The hotel offers a complimentary shoe shine. Housekeeping did not turn down the room (so no bottled water available although Evian is available for $8). Make sure you make a reservation for breakfast if you receive a breakfast coupon as there was a wait at 9 in the morning. Although that time is generally when people eat breakfast anyways, I normally never have to make reservations because a table is usually available. I tried to check-in at 8 in the morning but no room was available. When I came back at 12, the helpful front desk agent was able to put me in a room then. I did not look at the fitness or pool facilities so I have no comment. When I was checking-out I tried to contact the Bell Desk to have someone help take my luggage downstairs to no success. Each time, the line was busy. My car was brought up in 5 minutes. Overall, if I gauged what I paid for the room and the amenities I received, it was a GREAT DEAL. If I could procure the same rate again, I would definitely jump at the chance. I would not pay more than $250 for the Standard room I stayed in.

“Nice hotel, good location, but siren noise is a negative” I have stayed in several hotels in Foggy Bottom and this is one of the nicest, but also the loudest by far. Positives: Large, clean room with full kitchen and separate bedroom. Convenient to Foggy Bottom Metro and Georgetown and Bus Stop. Very close to Starbucks, Bruegger's Bagels, Trader Joe's and other small take-out places. All of the staff that we dealt were friendly and helpful. The internet was free and worked fairly well except the morning it didn't work at all. Negatives: Sirens were very loud and frequent. Both L St and Washington Circle have a lot of traffic. The bed wasn't very firm. The stocking of bathroom was a bit odd. We had 2 or 3 bottles of conditioner and never got a bottle of shampoo. The kitchen was stocked with coffee beans and a coffee grinder, but I don't like the hassle of grinding the beans and I often drink decaf and the only decaf was instant. I would have preferred packets of both regular and decaf. I would recommend this hotel, but would warn them about the noise.

“Great historic hotel!” I love the Mayflower Park! My room was extraordinarily comfortable. Great furnishings, good layout and everything worked! (This is not typical in many hotels these days). I love the location, too. Very convenient to all Seattle has to offer.

“Bring your own laptop - or pay!” Things I liked about this hotel: Hotel has a convenient location, it is rather upscale, I received an early check-in, free Sangria reception from 5-6PM. Things I disliked about this hotel: No free continental breakfast (only coffee and juice), 800-number toll free calls from room are charged 10 cents/minute after 30 minutes, the lounge ran out of tonic water for mixer at 6PM, and worst of all the "Business Center" is one PC located in a hot 90 degree temperature closet where you pay $5.95 for 15 minutes of PC use and pay 49 cents per page printed - far more for color. Also be aware that this hotel is pet friendly, so pets in the rooms and in the halls can be a good thing or bad thing depending on your outlook. In the end, I found the petty fees to be annoying at a $200/night hotel. I would look elsewhere next time for a hotel with better amenities.
“Great hotel” Hotel great huge rooms! Excellent pool - views over fox studios! Limited food and bev options though and location need a car but I guess that"s LA!

“Great Location” Very nice stay at the Grand Hyatt. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The first room we were assigned the bathroom smelled of cigarette smoke. The woman at the front desk changed our room. The second room had a leaky toilet, which the staff was able to fix so we did not need to change room again. We had a charge of 12.00 on the bill for phone calls. They charge for 1800 calls. The woman at the front desk removed the charges. We had a king room and I thought it was a decent size.

“Walk Through the Lobby Quickly...and get to Your Room with a View” We knew getting this hotel for this price had to have a "catch". But we were desperate...a last minute decision to attend a conference and no legitimate hotel rooms were available in the area of the convention center. So we opted for the congress plaza since it was right on the bus line to the convention center. For that reason it was good....but for other reasons not so good. This hotel lobby reminds me of a poorly made movie set...just enough to get by. The word that comes to mind is "seedy" Rooms perfectly acceptable but badly in need of a remodel Electricity very old lightbulb in bathroom was flickering off and on View was gorgeous...right on the lake...so if you close your eyes and focus on the lake, you'll be fine, although not all rooms are on the lake. I suggest going the VRBO route when you're in this situation.

“Charming but ultimately marginally OK” I spent two cold, snowy nights at the Algonquin Hotel when I was in NY on business. Overall, the experience was really uneven – all of the previous reviews are basically accurate. While nothing rose to the level of being truly disastrous, the whole experience left me a bit frustrated and disappointed. It wasn’t all bad, however: The Good 1. Great Location. For sure the best thing about the hotel is its stellar location on 44th between 5th and 6th, within walking distance of the Theater District and Grand Central. 2. Historical ambiance. The Algonquin is a charming old hotel. The lobby has an unmistakable ambiance – it’s not that big and a tad dumpy, but throughout my stay there were people hanging out enjoying themselves and there was actually something of a scene there, if you could call it that. The cabaret was busy at night. There were quirky quotes on the fronts of each of the doors. 3. Clean rooms and comfortable bed. I thought the bed was exceptionally comfortable. The room was small but no worse than plenty of other NY hotels. I thought the bathroom was fine – not great but fine. My colleague even had a renovated room with new furniture. The flat screen TV was also a nice touch. 4. Decent food. I had one dinner and one breakfast at the hotel. Although the prices were unmistakably NY high, the food wasn’t bad. We ate another night next door at Café DB, home of the $75 hamburger (in which I didn’t partake). 5. Good prices. I paid in the low $300’s for my room. Had I stayed at the swanky Royalton across the street it would’ve cost me more than twice what I paid and for a room which was much smaller. 6. Great door men. I thought the door men did an exceptional job, particularly given the cold, wet, snowy weather. They were friendly, they helped out with the luggage in the cab, they made a great first impression. 7. The Algonquin cat. I guess there’s a legend about a cat that lives at the Algonquin. Sure enough, the cat was there at the front desk. I thought it was a nice touch. 8. Lots of papers to choose from. I liked coming down the elevator and having my choice of the Wall Street Journal, New York Times, USA Today or NY Post in addition to the USA Today at my door. The Not as Good 1. There is construction going on next door. I was out by 7 and not back until after dinner each day so I missed the noise, but if you want a quiet night’s sleep or to sleep in, this isn’t the place for you. My colleague got chocolates in their room each night. I got ear plugs. Seriously. I will say that the hotel told me upfront when I checked in about the construction and they indicated that they moved me to the back of the building so it would be quieter and they warned me of the hours of construction, so they made the best of it in my opinion. 2. Rooms don’t have all the fixins. No coffee maker. No mini-bar. Plugs aren’t well located. Wi-fi didn’t work all the time – first night it was free and the second night they tried to charge me. No business center. 3. Not a lot of style. There is a fuddy duddy-ness to the lobby and the rooms. Perhaps this will be corrected in their renovation. The wallpaper on the upper floors was positively garish (not to mention peeling in a few places). 4. Slow elevators. I ended up taking the stairs from the third floor. 5. Funky front desk policies. At one point I asked for an Advil. They said that they wouldn’t give me one, and no hotel would do that because of the liability. I’ve had lots of hotels give me lots of over the counter drugs. Also, I had to sign something on my registration form in which I acknowledged that I would have to pay half if I checked out early. I’ve never had to do that before. The bottom line, you get what you pay for. In a City where everything costs an arm and leg, even a hotel room for under $400 can be considered cheap. Fortunately, I slept great and didn’t have a bad experience. Nonetheless, I was still pleased when I got home to my own bed, even if it wasn’t quite as comfortable as the one at the Algonquin.

“The door slamming hotel” Brand new property where space is a commodity. There is not much common space. Rooms brand new but small. Shower is tiny. Water pressure is limited by water saver. Free breakfast every morning. Free wifi. The biggest negative of this hotel is that you can hear a lot of noise in the hallways and tons of door slamming, especially when house keeping starts about 9.

“Comfortable Accommodations...If You’re A Savvy Traveler” Le Meridien Dallas by the Galleria is a comfortable hotel that offers a great location for Galleria Dallas shopping. The hotel offers spacious well-appointed rooms that invite lounging and relaxing. The public area is filled with couches and chairs that create a sense of community. I spent a couple of hours enjoying a book and people watching in the lobby/bar. As previously referenced the property is well situated next to the Galleria and nearby restaurants and bars. Shopping and dining at the Galleria are mere steps away. The restaurants that populate Beltline Rd. and Alpha Rd. will meet most diners’ tastes. One restaurant in particular, Maximo, Cocina Mexicana & Margarita Lounge, should definitely be on one’s dining list and it’s only two blocks from the hotel. The only complaint I would offer about the property is the dungeon like indoor pool. The confines of the pool are dark and cramped; so much so that the overpowering build-up of chlorine in the “pool vault” makes it difficult to breath. There is definitely a need for the property to redevelop a pool and patio area either adjacent to the property or better yet on the roof of the building. As for parking and breakfast that has been criticized by other travelers as being “overpriced”, of course it is. You’re parking and dining at an urban hotel property. The savvy traveler takes a moment to simply pause and consider her/his options. For example, park across the street in the Galleria-Nordstrom’s indoor parking garage. It’s free! Another example, walk across the street to the Galleria, walk down the street to the Starbucks, or get in your car and make a run over to the fabulous “Original Pancake House” or “The Egg and I” restaurants and enjoy a delicious and reasonably priced breakfast. Replace your complaints with a bit of thinking. It will take you far in life. By the way, for the weekend I only paid $45 a night for a king room by bidding through Priceline. Once again, the savvy traveler can always find a way.

“Weekdn getaway with the kids” Had a great stay with our two kids over the week of Christmas. Price was right ($93 through Hilton website), location was great (Nordstrom's for the wife and daughter, ESPNZone for my son and me just around the corner) and the staff was efficient and friendly. There are probably a dozen restaurants withina one block radius. The exercise room wasn't huge but had three treadmills and some other machines. The pool was very small and overly-chlorinated but the kids loved it just the same. I would recommend this hotel if you can get a good price on it!

“Not Bad But It's Falling Apart!” Not really that bad a stay. The hotel is old and is literally falling apart. It must have been beautiful when it opened but it's glory days are long gone. My ex-girlfriend and I stayed here since she wanted a weekend in New York. We had a heck of a time find our room! The place is huge and it was quite a walk from the elevator to the room. The room was old and desperately needed work. We had a bedroom, living room and kitchenette. The window view was of the alley on the side of the hotel. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. It's a quiet area at night and not too far from Times Square. We had a decent stay and they had pretty tight security at night. You need a pass which they give you at check in. I don't think it was worth the money we paid but we made the most of what was there.

“the way a hotel should be” Picked up at the airport by the hotel shuttle near the baggage claim area in the evening. Alternately, the hotel is attached by skybridge to Terminal E - other terminals require a short walk. Lobby sits in the rear of a spacious atrium - check-in went smoothly. There is 24 hour room service and two restaurants in the lobby area that cover most of the daytime hours. The breakfast restaurant gives you the option of buffet-style or order-from-menu. Food is good and plentiful. The health club is spacious and contains workout appartus, locker rooms, television sets, a indoor heated lap pool (about 15 yards long) and a large jacuzzi. Service in the bedrooms is prompt and excellent. There is a coffee maker and a newspaper is delivered to your room each weekday morning. On weekends you can go to the gift shop in the lobby (after 7am) to buy a newspaper. The hotel shuttle will take you to the local subway (Airport) station - called the 'T' in Boston. For $18 you get a three day pass good on all city transport services. If you don't mind walking you can take the skybridge to Terminal E - go down to the surface level and catch an airport bus to the 'T'. The buses run all day and are free.

“Harbor Magic at Brookshire Suites” I recently stayed at Brookshire Suites in downtown Baltimore over the holiday weekend. The hotel is one block from Harborplace at the Inner Harbor. Being in Baltimore for the first time, this was a perfect location to see as much of downtown Baltimore and several scenic locations on my list. The hotel is at the intersection of two free bus routes called the Charm City Circulator that takes you around downtown Baltimore. A water taxi stop is also located at Harborplace which will take you to Fells Point and several other attractions - more in season (April - September). There was a mix-up in my reservations with Travelocity (expedia, etc., same company - overbooked). Susan, at the front desk was extremely kind and offered water and assistance while Travis worked with other Harbor Magic Hotels and the local hotels to find me another suite of equal quality and only one block away for the night. The effort was outstanding whereas many others would leave you to fend for yourself with your travel agency. The next day I was relocated back to Brookshire for the remainder of my long weekend where the beds are comfy with extra thick mattresses and flat screen TVs in each room. There were also free breakfasts every morning and on weeknights the first couple of drinks are complimentary at their top floor lounge. There was parking available at the Hotel but, not having a car, I took the "Light Rail" from BWI Airport which was only 4-5 blocks away. The Harbor Magic Hotels also have a shuttle to take you to local sites and restaurants, upon availability. Within a block or two you also have restaurants, nighttime entertainment (10 Min. walk to the Power Plant), convenience stores and sports bars (like Dick's Last Resort, Hard Rock), not to mention the proximity to Camden Yards (Oriole Park) and M & T Stadium where the Ravens play football. You are a short 15 minute walk from "Little Italy" and Federal Hill. Make sure you take the Water Taxi ($10 all day) to Fells Point for steamed carbs at Riptide, O'brycki's or Mo's Pasta in Little Italy or just great mussels at Bertha's.

“This Sheraton delights in all aspects of your stay.” As a platinum SPG member I have stayed at my share of SPG properties. Sheraton universal is now at the top of my favorite hotels. This location is great for accessibility to Universal Studious. I had business in Northern LA and brought my 12 year old son along. The front desk manager found out he was with me and went out of her way to make us comfortable and him feel welcome. I had the opportunity to request help from management, bell & concierge staff. All could not have been more accommodating. The room was bright and shower pressure was good (pet peeves). Restaurant service was attentive and food was good. I am not in the habit of glowing reviews, but this property earned it. I will make this my home base when working north of LA.

“Top Notch service” Stayed for a couple nights on business trip. I am Platinum SPG member. Was not upgraded to suite as they were sold out that week. Did get access to lounge. Standard breakfast items in the morning. eggs and sausage and other cold items. Hotel was very clean and all the staff were very friendly and helpful. Rooms are large and clean. Beds very comfortable. Central air so nice and quiet. Large flat screen TVs with HiDef. Wifi was strong and fast. Only issue I could say needs fixing was water pressure in the shower. Would definitely stay here again when in town.

“Great budget hotel” We just returned from seven nights in NYC over the New Years holiday. We chose the Chelsea Lodge because the reviews were great and because they did not raise their rates at all for the holidays unlike many NYC hotels which raise them to astronomical levels. For the price I very much doubt you could beat the Chelsea Lodage anywhere in New YorK City. Yes the rooms are tiny, but they are very clean as are the bathroom facilities and the rest of the hotel. Chelsea is a wonderful neighbourhood from which to explore the rest of the city and a great part of town in its own right.

“Perfect to Catch an Early Morning Flight” Our flight back home left at 7am, so we had to get there around 5:45am the latest. This hotel's shuttle service runs 24/7 so it was no problem. What surprised me was how close the hotel was to the terminals. It was just a few minutes. The room was up-to-date, quiet, and clean. A plus was the separate check-in desk for Marriott Platinum and Gold members. Staff couldn't have been more helpful. I would stay here again going in and out of LAX.

“Luxury...Worth the Money!” One of my top 3 hotel stays of all time! I booked this hotel at the airport due to my flight was delayed 4 hours and I was going to miss the last Ferry of the day to Provincetown. I normally read all the reviews and search for the best price but obviously there was no time for this. It was close to Logan’s Wharf where the ferry departs from so I booked it. The cost was a bit expensive but it's Boston and the prices weren't any more or any less than any other hotel in that same area. Needless to say, I was really impressed once I arrived to the hotel. The lobby was very updated and decorated in a modern traditional style. The front desk staff and the doorman were super helpful and nice...it took the desk less than 3 minutes to get me checked in and sent on my way. Once I arrived to the room I was blown away with how large the rooms were...was I really in Boston with a room this size? There was a very large closet, a separate space for the sink and bathroom, and I had a balcony overlooking the Clock Tower, the Pier, and Downtown Boston. The true king size bed was very plush and amazingly comfortable with large firm pillows that provided for excellent sleep throughout the night. I decided to order room service and it was a bit costly but the food was excellent and sometimes you have to indulge. The next morning I woke up pretty early and opened my balcony door to be greeted by the Farmer's Market right in front of the hotel. Wow, what an amazing site to see and smell all the fresh fruits, vegetables, homemade desserts, and fresh baked breads. This unplanned Boston overnight stay turned out to be one of my best hotel experiences ever. I would absolutely recommend this hotel to other travelers and I plan to go back and miss my ferry to Provincetown just so I can stay in this hotel again.

“a fantastic stay” my wife and I spent 3 nights at the hotel burnham and it was hands down the best experience we have ever had at any hotel. we were upgraded to a suite (1503) on the top floor of this wonderful hotel housed in the reliance building(1895) smack in the middle of the loop! the kimpton group, pioneers in the boutique hotel business always do it right! we are on the top floor with these huge baywindows looking out at the lake,millenium park, marshall fields across the street (now Macy's but what a building!) spacious hip well appointed furnishings/lots of space/ extreme comfort on all levels. kimpton spent lots a bucks lovingly redoing this famous old building and what a gem it is. go on their website or google the reliance building . they can say it better than I can. ny times every morning! free GOOD coffee in the morning! a great restaurant (4 star).the atwood. Ill review it separately after I kick this back to california jet lag. great service also. really clean. i actually looked forward to getting back to the room and looking out the window. thanx to the hotel burnham for making our trip to this world class city (my home town so im partial) so special.

“Wonderful place to stay in NYC” We were very impressed with this hotel - they let us check in early and leave late - staff were incredibly friendly and accomodating (Randy the bellboy was very helpful and didn't appear to expect tipping every time we saw him but just enjoyed his job which we were very impressed with). We had a spacious suite on the 10th floor - it was overlooking office blocks and was very quiet and absolutely spotless. Location perfect for sightseeing. Free internet access on the lower ground floor and breakfast was a bonus. Everything else has been said in the other reviews - but we will certainly be returning to this hotel!

“Wonderful stay! Can't wait to go back!” We took a chance and booked this hotel through Hotwire. We were so glad we did! We got a fabulous rate at a fabulous hotel. The hotel is in an amazing location and offers a super-helpful staff! The facility is beautiful; very well-appointed and maintained. The rooms are very comfortable and the bathrooms are very spacious. True, parking and Internet are extra. We can certainly understand paying for parking in Boston, but we have to admit, we would have much preferred to spend the Internet fees in the spa or lounge. Having to pay for online service at a hotel in this day and age should be considered criminal. Despite the Internet fee, this hotel is worth it. Hands down!

“As all Kimpton Hotels, I wonderful experience” Beautiful Boutique Hotel!!! All the staff at The George were wonderful. I love the wine hour and the gentleman the first few days I was there was charming, helpful and genuinely cared about all the guests. What great group. No wonder Kimpton was rated so highly in employee relations. Great company. I will be heading off to Nine Zero in March and can't wait for another wonderful experience.

“Great location, rooms lacking” Great location for the price. Can't get any closer to the monuments and museums. Also close to a number of metro lines. Room itself was average. We specifically asked for an outward facing room and our room had a sliver of a window, which coincidently partially faced a wall. The only way to get a "real" window is to pay up. Like the other reviews mentioned, this really was not "JW" quality, but for the location, it can't be beat.

“Ruhig obwohl sehr zentral gelegen” Weil ich von den Embassy Suites enttauescht war, wechselte ich in das Hampton Inn, was mir von einem Kollegen empfohlen wurde. Ich wurde nicht enttaeuscht: saubere, moderne Zimmer und der uebliche Hampton-Standard machen das Hotel zur Empfehlung. Obwohl das Hotel voll belegt war, war dank des guten Managements davon wenig zu merken. Fuer Geschaeftsreisende in jedem Fall eine gute Wahl in Chicago Downtown.

“A Class Act” I stayed for two weekends in December. Early on in the month and the weekend before Christmas. On the initial visit I had booked a "Flash Room" as it had internet access. When I arrived the computer had a virus and was not working. I initially found the desk unhelpful but the next day I was promptly moved to a room that had a working (correctly) computer. At checkout I was charged the full rate for both nights. I did not quarrel with it at the time, but mentioned on the post stay survey. Within days I was contacted by the Manager, stating she had given me a refund for both days, and offering me an upgrade on my next stay. I went two weeks later and while not taking the upgrade did get exactly the room I requested. To me this is what customer service and service recovery is all about. Kudos to both Ms. Clymer, the Manager and the front desk. As for the hotel, it is an older (maybe 40 years) apartment building converted to a hotel, so there is no lobby to speak of. That said they rooms are large, well decorated and with a full size sofa thats great to stretch out on. Cleanliness is above and beyond. The actual bathroom is somewhat small, but the sink is outside the bathroom and there is lots of room on the vanity for your things. There is a large televison and writing desk. The bed is comfortable and linens are above average. There is Starbucks coffee with a coffeemaker; nifty animal print robes and an umbrella in the rooms. The location is excellent, within walking distance of the subway, Dupont Circle and many good restaurants. It is not even that far to walk downtown if you are energetic and the weather is nice. The hotel has an excellent restaurant - Firefly- where the decor is perhaps overly cute, but the food is excellent. Albeit desserts need work. The bar is small but fun and friendly. All staff are helpful and responsive and it was wonderful being greeted by name everytime I came in or went out. As far as I am concerned the Madera is my hotel of choice whenever I am in DC.

“Huge rooms (for NY) .. would stay again.” We received a very warm welcome to the Affinia Shelburne. The check in was smooth and we were shown to a large room with two queen (nearer uk king size!) beds, which were very comfortable after a long day walking around New York. There was plenty of storage, a lovely little kitchen area with fridge/ice maker, microwave oven, sink and coffee/tea maker with complimentary coffee/tea which was replenished by housekeeping everyday. The bathroom was small, but adequate, although it could have been cleaned to a higher standard (don't get me wrong, it was by no means dirty, but there were small dusty areas - corners and behind taps and suchlike). One point, which is more a fault of other guests, is that, although our room was quiet (no street noise at all), banging doors were a little irritating at night. Surely some mechanism could be fitted to ensure that doors close quietly? The previously mentioned "problems" with elevators didn't bother us one bit, we never had to wait long for either the main, or service elevator. The surrounding area of Murray Hill is a lovely, mainly residential area with lots of places to eat/drink. The nearest subway station is a short walk (four streets) away. We didn't use the hotel's restaurant/bar, "Rare", as there are just too many good places to eat in New York to fit them all in, but we presumed it must be good, as it was often busy. There are a couple of internet pcs (attached to a printer) in the lobby and although there is a charge for internet useage, you can check on flight times/status and check-in for free. We would stay here again, no problem.

“Perfect for a night- Comfortable Bed, Great Free Breakfast” Stopped on the way to San Diego for a night. Easy, friendly and affordable. Only complaint is a small tv. Bed was really comfortable, free breakfast is always a nice perk as are the fresh baked cookies available at the front desk. Parking could be an issue if crowded....

“Andaz 5th Avenue” The Andaz 5th Avenue is part of Hyatt's new, hip Andaz chain, with each hotel having a different personality. Our stay here was top to bottom, fantastic. We arrived early on a Saturday morning, after getting up at 3:30 to catch a train from D.C. We were able to get into our suite, which was nice. After the host showed us the room and wished my son a happy birthday, we went down for breakfast. It was very expensive, but it was good food and nice to have a view of the Public Library. We had room 1106, which was a loft-style suite. I can't find what room it was exactly, because it has some elements of different room types. Anyways, we had one king bed and a sofa bed. My son slept on the sofa bed, which was king sized and not slept on before as shown by the tags still on the mattress. It was as comfortable as the regular bed, not your standard sofa bed. We had a lovely kitchen area, with a full fridge with food and drinks in it, which were free and you could request more. We had 2 different huge closets, one in the bedroom area and one in the entryway. We had two gigantic TV's, one in each area. The blinds and lights are controlled by a few master switches, but it was easy to use. There was a desk and chair, which we didn't really use. The bathroom was huge and beautiful, with very nice toiletries. As it was my son's birthday, they sent him dessert. He got two, and I think that one was because we had it on the reservation, and one was from the host who checked us in. Upon departure, sad as we were to leave, it was a little bit okay because they offer a departure gift, we chose the delicious brownies. We also had a high sense of security, as you need a key to use the elevator. All in all, a great place and we will return.

“Not your typical Embassy...” Was at this Embassy Suites for a 4 day long weekend. The hotel is situated on Freeway 10 going towards San Antonio. This is a high rise Embassy Suites, very new and extremely elegant. Beautiful lobby with an impressive wall aquarium. The usual amenities known to Embassy Suites are all here, with added convenience of a small store and Starbucks. Service from checking to checking out was impeccable, everyone of the hotel employees I encountered, even just walking by were very friendly and said hello. In the dining room several employees would come by and ask if everything was ok. As far as I am concerned this was flawless customer service at all levels.

“Comfortable, convenient & good price” I stayed here for 2 weeks December 08. Upon checking in I was told that there may be some minor Hurricane Ike damage in the room, but if it bothered me, I could switch to another room. The room had a piece of drywall cut out on the bottom of a wall near a window, with plastic sheeting covering it, but it was not a problem. The room was always clean, the bed comfortable. The wireless internet was very good save for one night for some reason. Unlike may of the HIEs I have stayed at, this one had 2 elevators, which is always a plus... maybe because this was was 5 floors it had to have more than one. Breakfast was the usual HIE fare....reasonably good, though no waffle maker as some have there. The staff was always friendly, accomodating and helpful. The location was uff of US59, so it was convenient to get many places. The area is many typical off highway, with stores nearby, with fastfood near to the hotel. Good place to stay at a reasonable price. Not fancy, but comfortable & clean.

“Fantastic Priceline Stay” We got a lovely 4* room for $71/per night. The hotel was perfectly wonderful--clean, pretty rooms, great service, excellent location. We are big fans of the Westin Heavenly Bed, and the Renaissance bed we had was just as good. Our room was spotless and fresh, and more importantly, available at 10:30am. We had arrived after a nightmare red-eye from Seattle, and were expecting only to check our bags with the bellman, but the staff assured us a room was waiting for us! We went straight to bed, and slept great! Room service was delicious and prompt. Starbucks in the lobby was a real plus for 2 Seattleites! We also enjoyed the lounge, although the Cosmopolitan I had was pretty sweet--but strong! The staff was helpful and courteous. This was so worth the price...in fact, it was worth much more than what we paid. Location is between the Chinatown and Convention metro stops--a bit of a walk if you have lots of luggage or aren't comfortable walking 2-3 city blocks. But it's also right on the Circulator Bus Route to Georgetown and the corridor there. Very convenient! The area is up and coming with regards to nightlife, and there are several hot restaurants and nightclubs within walking distance. Seriously, you can't go wrong with this hotel--I would recommend it to anyone.

“VERY PLEASANT SURPRISE” Stranded due to ice storm on way back from a golf outing. Six of us were sent to this property. Excellent rate and we'd only be there one night. GREAT VALUE. The desk staff, Monte and Danielle were simply outstanding. Very professional, friendly, and efficient. Rooms were fresh, clean, large, and excellent cable package. Nice free breakfast - variety of bagels and breads, fresh waffles, juices, coffee, etc.- Lobby had a free internet computer for guest use. Free long distance phone calls and free toiletries ( USAir had run out). Free shuttle to and from Charlotte airport. Excellent property for the night before a flight or for a base during a visit to Charlotte.

“Convenient, clean and efficient” We stayed here for a busy weekend in December using HH points. We had about a thirty minute wait for our room (it was 2:30), so we bought tickets for a play from the concierge and requested maps, etc and sat in the lounge. I wish there was more light in the reception area (it is on the third floor and yes, if you get in after certain hour, the door man downstairs requests to see your hotel key), but the front desk staff was courteous and efficient. She told us we could be placed in room on 41st floor but it wasn't ready at 3:00 and it was an adjoining room which she said we wouldn't like as much (I agreed since I had read on this site that it can be noisy), so we put in a room on 37th floor. We heard nothing and had great view of Times Square. I had requested an upgrade but the hotel was sold out. We were given three hot cookies which we ate while waiting for our room and then we were given three more when we were able to check in (!) even though we had told the girl we already had them. Delicious! There were three of us, and even though I enjoy at least queen size beds, my husband and I slept perfectly well in the double (NYC tires you out!) and my daughter was in the other bed. It would have been better if the toilet was seperate from the rest of the bathroom, but I did like that the bar area had counter and sink space. I think underneath the sinks in the bathroom could have been utilized more with storage, but that's so minor. We had plenty of room to spread all of our toiletries out. It's funny that the bottom windows do open (could reach camera out through them!) so fresh air can come in if it gets too warm. The elevators are VERY fast and there are many of them. It was a clean room and comfortable. Subway is right next door, there are diners around the corner for breakfast (we ate a Cranberry Deli and Evergreen Diner), there are restaurants all around the hotel and McD's within minutes of walking and TKTS is across the street. Everything is easy to walk to and I didn't have any problems with "congestion" at the main entrance. It is a busy entrance but you just move people out of your way. I just don't know if I would ever pay the exorbitant prices for any NYC hotel, but if I did have to pay or did stay in the heart of the city again, I would not have a problem booking at the Doubletree at all.

“Customer Service at its finest...a lovely stay.” Stayed at the Sofitel Los Angeles while in town for a friend's wedding - they had reserved rooms at a very reasonable rate at the hotel. The line was long for check in at the front desk but the staff was very efficient, appropriately apologetic and very welcoming. Wedding gift bag in tow, we headed to the elevators through a very nicely appointed lobby: modern and sleek but not cold and formal. Up the room - which smelled like old baby diapers. As in, probably the guests before us had stayed there with a small child and since the windows don't open, even after a proper cleaning, the odor lingered. It was impossible to ignore, so we called down to the desk. Matthew answered, we explained the situation, and he told us to stay put...housekeeping would come up to "deal with it" and he'd look for another room for us. WIthin 10 minutes, housekeeping came up and asked what the problem was. Oddly, he couldn't smell anything but since we were already waiting for a new room, he poked around and then left.
