Moments later, another of the staff came up with new room keys and many apologies. He wrinkled his nose and said "I see what you mean" and we headed out. Upstairs two floors to the exact room without the smell (ahhh!), and we settled right in. Reason for pointing this out? Hotels handle things like this in many different ways, and the staff at the Sofitel was efficient, gracious, and extremely accommodating. What could have been a headache was merely a small bump in the checking in process. The rest of our stay was delightfully uncomplicated. Important things worked: wonderful water pressure, soft bed (but not too soft!) with luxurious linens, products from l'occitane in the bathroom (yum) and a lovely view of the hills. Didn't hear any hallway noise, the elevators came in a timely fashion, and our car, when retrieved from valet, appeared in a very reasonable amount of time. The fitness center is very well laid out with ample equipment, soft towels (not the usual gym scratchy variety!) and complimentary water and fresh fruit. There is free internet access in the lobby with a printer that works - another bonus. WIthout the option to rate 4-1/2 stars, I'm giving this hotel 4, but only because they charge $10/day for in room wifi which, in this day and age, seems somewhat unreasonale. Cable is free - why not the web? Additionally, the rooms aren't well laid out to handle luggage (no valet in the closet) and therefore our stuff was everywhere and that was a bit of a nuisance. Really, though, a 5 star stay in many respects, most noteably due to the outstanding service from the bellmen to the housekeeping staff to the front desk. Would highly recommend. Plus, lest I forget, the location can't be beat. We walked to the Farmers Market, Rodeo Drive, and shopping all along Melrose. Very well situated.

“Always Get an Even # Room” This is actually a fine property. The employees are very friendly. They give you the extra service, and the rooms are all enhanced. The main problem I encountered was the terrible highway noise from IH 10 They were full, and we had an odd numbered room which fronted on the highway. There was lots of noise all night long. The desk clerk said that the hotel is planning on soundproofing the highway facing rooms in the future. He also gave me some Holiday Inn points for my trouble.

“Exceptional Service, Fast Valet & NIce Rooms” Enjoyed my stay to drop my daughter off at UCLA - was there for 4 nights. On arrival, we were tired from long drive and decided to relax at the pool; to our surprise there were 2 business meetings going on there. Not sure why they allowed this, as it made us as "guests" feel a little uncomfortable lounging in our suits and swimming. Lounges at pool are great and albeit there is limited sun, we were able to relocate to sun. Pool was a little cool but refreshing. Service was absulutely astounding; everyone was really ready to please - so refreshing. Didn't really like having to valet park the car at $33 per day (with tax), but the service was very fast. Enjoyed the location, as it gave me an incentive to walk around the area between the hotel and UCLA; loved the walks! Was a little hard to remember the location at night when driving back - all the high rises on Wilshire look the same at night - luckily I remembered the cross-street (Selby) with the light! Room was comfie, but it got a little warm at night - finally changed the AC fan to "hI' and this helped a lot. Used the mini-bar as my personal refrigerator (put the stuff in the closet) and liked having a room safe and easy access to ice. Would stay here again. Free internet would have been nice (instead of $10 per day). But the front desk did my searches for me, and printed me out directions as needed. Check-out day was pirate day which looked like a fun idea!

“Missing just a little!” Stayed in a Superior King room on the third level in April for 5 days....spacious, but bathroom had only one sink and the shower had a very outdated shower head!!! Hallway baseboards were in desperate need of paint and the carpet needs replacement! You could smell and feel the dust than no shampooing can aleviate! FS, these are easy to change! Hotel is only 8 floors, which has a more cozy feel for a city hotel. All staff encountered were extremely gracious and professional...from the doormen to the conceirge. The location was perfect and quiet, as other hotels in town, ie: Ritz, Rittenhouse is noisy. Addtionally, the window of the room opens, which I REALLY appreciated...a big plus as the weather was wonderful. Will never stay elsewhere while on business in Philly.

“Charming Small Boutique Hotel Well Located in Midtown East” Hotel Elysee is a classic small boutique hotel well situated in the heart of Manhattan's midtown business and shopping district. The hotel is located on 54th street between Madison and Park. Although, this is a very busy part of Manhattan, the location itself was quiet. The hotel's decor is styled in French provincial. For Manhattan, the rooms are "relatively" roomy; which may seem dated to some, but I found them to be consistent with the French provincial theme. The Hotel Elysee serves a complimentary continental breakfast on the 2nd floor with a wide variety of breakfast foods to choose from in a charming room. I only wished they would open up the complimentary breakfast or at least some coffee service priot to 7:00 am. I stayed in a room that was located immediately off the elevator but I never really heard the elevator. The one elevator on the property served all 12 floors so at times there was a longer wait than you might expect for a small hotel. All in all, given the room rates, location and fabulous complimentary breakfast, I would definitely seek to stay at the Hotel Elysee again.
“Great place” I attended a conference at this hotel. The staff was great and the rooms are wonderful. My room had a wonderful view of the desert.

“Undergoing renovations, looking much better. Still one things to think about....” Reviewed this hotel almost exactly a year ago ( please feel free to read the much longer and extensive one I wrote!). But as I'm only travelling with an iPad this time I can't be bothered to type too long.... But wanted to review this hotel again as its undergoing some major renovations.! I am giving the hotel a rating of 4 this time around as opposed to the 3 it got the last time mainly because of their much improved internet which can be a total dealbreaker for me. Improved: * Internet is much better this time around fast and stable wifi! * General freshness and comfort of room much improved * Quality of tech stuff in room great Sill not great: * They have done nothing about the windows of he hotel. And as its located in a busy intersection o town in can, and will most likely be, super noisy! So if you have problems with noise make sure to get a room facing inwards! * Cold... Although I do believe that they have vastly improved their AC system as well Things to think about when booking: * The bathrooms all seem a little bit different. Som with bathtubs and sep. shower. Some with just a tub. Plus the size of the tubs vary, so shop around * The noisy streets should be considered But all in all it's in a great central location with lovely staff.

“Would stay there again” Stayed five nights for a conference. Paid to upgrade room to 16th floor on opposite side from bridge view so I wouldn't be looking at and listening to the huge Dole container ship being unloaded and loaded - had a view of the Bay and over the roof of the Convention Centre. The hotel still feels new - it's clean and not cruise or convention worn...yet. The bed was very comfortable, somewhat limited tv channels when you're not interested in sports. The bridge over towards the baseball stadium is still not finished so you have to walk alongside the Convention Centre to 5th before you can cross the tracks. As a solo traveller, I didn't really want to be out and walking around after dark as there are a lot of street people hanging around but not as aggressive as the ones in Seattle. I ate in the sports bar twice, first time the food was good, second time so so. You can't access it from the hotel which is very strange, same with the Starbucks. I ate dinner in the Vela and found my food tasteless and expensive - having the discount coupon made it slightly more palatable -- and you can look at the Dole container ship when you're put in a not prime seating area as I was. Staff were all very friendly and helpful. A little too chilly to use the pool and you're staring at and listening to the container ship being loaded/unloaded. Make sure you take all your toiletries with you - I paid $5 for a travel size tube of toothpaste at their Gift Shop. I didn't feel like walking for 15/20 minutes to a drug store. $20/day for the "better" wireless access is downright extortionate - I needed it to access my work VPN. Went to the zoo, took a taxi there and the bus back [$2.25]. Zoo admission is now $40. SuperShuttle was the most efficient I've encountered, $16.00 round trip, they showed up on time, were extremely professional, left a message on my cell to remind me of my return trip.

“Lots of potential, but a long way to go” Ok, I am a Dallas native, I had some time off and wanted to get away just by myself. I booked a hotel/spa pkg that included a bunch services (details to follow). I am familiar with this hotel from it's days as the old Hilton and have drinks there quite a bit currently. The Review: The hotel lobby is so stylish, the pool is subdued, but kind of cool. The desk clerk was terribly rude, I was really excited about my stay and she could have cared less. I got to my room and it was just claustrophobically tiny. The bed hit the tv stand. I went back down to try and get a larger room which I was even willing to pay for. Rude Desk Clerk Girl told me I had to go to spa, through which I booked the room to get a room change. I thought this was incredibly poor service. Regardless, I did it. The spa manager could have cared less as well. I went back to the hotel front desk, told Rude Desk Clerk Girl that the spa manager had nothing for me and she told me there was nothing she could do. I asked for her boss, he was incredibly nice and accommodating and upgraded me to a larger room. I must admit the room was still quite small. The decor in the rooms was interesting, modern Kimpton style. The spa experience was terribly average. Dallas has a ton of spa/hotel experiences and this one is just so not up to par with them. The massage therapist didn't listen to what I wanted or my requests. The facialist was just fine. The manicurist/pedicurist tried way to hard to sell stuff to me. The manager of the spa just wasn't a welcoming/inviting person. They really made me feel like a nuisance (which I might have been), but regardless, I was still a guest and should have been treated as such. This is a very stylish hotel, with terribly average services and save for gracious hotel manager (Elliott, i believe his name was), terribly below average staff all around.

“Fantastic!” I had the pleasure of staying here for 12 days in November. First let me say the location is fantastic with shops and restaurants within very close walking distance. Now for the hotel! My room was wonderful with a great view of the bridge, contemporary decor, cozy bed, and a great sofa window (not sure what it's official name is). I used the window every morning while having my coffee. The blinds open completely giving you full city views. Hideaway plasma tv, vodka, patron, and lots of other spirits in the room are sure to keep you niiicce. Beautiful lobby, nice lobby bar and great gym. My room was clean, private, peaceful and soothing and the ipod dock helped assure that my stay was very peaceful and calming...and I was there for WORK! I would absolutely recommend you stay here if visiting San Fran!

“An unexprected pleasure” Our preconception was that the hotel would be old, worn and out dated. To our joy, this was an absolute great place tpo park for a couple of days while we toured DC. As soon as we arrived, the grand lobby blew us away. It kind of reminded us of the Greenbrier, the Fairmont in San Francisco and a few other older grand hotels we have visited, but the common areas were lighter and brighter. Check-in was a breeze and the room we were assigned was at least 30% larger than we expected. The room was clean, well appointed and absolutely great. the bathroom was very spacious. We are into comfort, and this was a comfortable room. It may bother some people that the hotel is a cab ride from DC tourist center, but we prefer its location at the top of Rock Creek Park. The most expensive cab ride was $8 and the Metro was right down the street making access to anywhere in DC very easy. there are lots of little places to eat in the area also. The only negative of our stay was a loud HVAC unit. It kicked on and off too often a rattled a bit. We appreciated the history of the hotel and really appreciated the fact the hotel owners had renovated the place completely. Everything was clean as a whistle and in its proper place. Great pool and spa area, beautiful dinning area and great service. I will seek to stay here during my next visit to DC.

“One night and catch a flight” Our one night stay before we flew home was a rewards night. When we got to the room at 10:30 at night, the lights were on and a small snack bag had been left (apple, chips, water). All very nice but at a price. It was Thanksgiving weekend and the lack of parking was a problem. Valet full and garage even had double parking blocking cars. We parked at a red (fire??) curb and the hotel advised us that it would be fine - and it was. There is not a fan only option on the heating system so we listenend to the fan go off and on all night. The bathroom does have a granite counter but is not scrupulously clean and a little tired appearing. Like we were in the a.m. before our early flight. The convenience to the airport was the biggest plus and I am glad the price was right.

“Typically comfy Hampton” Stayed here for 4 nights for a work trip, and enjoyed my King Study...good size room, bigger than a typical hotel room, which gives you some space between your bed and the door, making it a little quieter in bed. Front desk staff extremely helpful and nice. Breakfast was ok, better than some Hampton Inn's, but not as good as others. Beds comfortable of course. Only problem with location is that it can be a pain to get some places due to SW Loop 820 being a one-way, but just use side streets...tons of restaurants and a mall around, so it's a nice area. Will stay here again!

“I was Surprised” I had a meeting here, otherwise I generally prefer other hotels. I have been in some Hiltons that were in need of some TLC. I was surprised by the comfort of the beds, the soft towels, the ease of a very late night check-in, and the cleanliness. No doubt the hotel manager cracks a loud whip! The only complaint was the cost of the food in the restaurant.

“Atrium was an Oasis” I was staying at this hotel because I was in town for a conference at the Javits Center. Upon check in I was put in the Atrium room section which looks more pleasant than the other sections of the hotel I walked through. The atrium is light and bright, open and the colors of the walls in the hallways are a light blue with artwork along the walls. The hallways in the rest of the hotel seem to be the dark somber colors which are a little dark and depressing. The room was of good size and had a mac computer available for use in your room. You can’t beat the location being in Times Square. If in NYC again I would want to stay at this hotel in the Atrium Section. Pictured of the Atrium section and rooms are included with my review.

“Excelente hotel ,Ubicacion perfecta” Es un hotel que esta a pasos de Union Square .El hotel es excelente ,las habitaciones son enormes y la atencion es muy buena.Tiene wi fii gratis ,pero el garage tiene valet parking y es un poco caro pero el hotel es totalmente recomendable.

“Great place to stay in Seattle” We stayed at the Inn at El Gaucho for 2 nights (11th – 13th May) and had a really pleasant stay. I won’t say we were completely wowed by it, hence the 4 stars but it’s certainly a great place to stay. Its location, I would say, is half way between Pike Place Market and the Space Needle – so about equal walking distance to both depending on whether you turn right or left out the door. You wouldn't know it was a hotel from the outside, it doesn't really look like one at all. Just a word of warning (thankfully, we were prepared for it), you have to climb a flight of stairs to get to the hotel itself so don't take really heavy suitcases with you. We did book a Bell Town Suite and when we checked-in we were very happy with it but we soon noticed that there was a lot of road noise. The hotel is above a restaurant all on one floor so it’s close to the road. We asked if we could be moved and the hotel moved us straight away to a lovely quiet Atrium Suite on the inside which was equally nice. The rooms are spacious (the ones we saw) and have wonderfully comfortable beds. They are well equipped with robes, slippers, nice toiletries, stereo systems and large flat-screen televisions. I can’t fault them. It was really quiet when we stayed there; I think there was only one other room occupied. I think that meant that the service was a bit quiet too. The first day we went through to the lobby area for breakfast and it wasn’t there, we ended up just going out for something. The next day we double-checked what time breakfast was again and the receptionist told us that because there were only a couple of rooms booked that they would bring it to our room. It was slightly delayed whilst they ran to the bakery but it wasn’t a problem. We did eat on our first night at the El Gaucho Steak House downstairs. It was Mother’s Day in America that day but it was still fairly quiet. The food was excellent and the service was fantastic. It’s very dark in the steak house and it’s a big place but it was lovely, we recommend it. On out second night we booked a table at Sky City (the revolving restaurant up the top of the Space Needle). We had an amazing evening, it was lovely. Again, great food and great service and this is highly recommended. The views are fantastic. I would recommend this hotel, however, I think if we stayed in Seattle again I would maybe try a different hotel. I loved the hotel but it didn’t wow me as much as I thought it might from the reviews I had read.

“Good Location.” Very good hotel whichis what you expect from a "Chain" Hotel. Staff friendly, rooms a good size. Location was very good. Good value for money. Pool was a bonus. Would definately stay there again.

“One of the BEST!!!!” Stayed here in June 09, worst weather ever for new york but this hotel was fantastic. Bit difficult to find but once found fantastic. Subways literally around the corner, as is Wall Street, having been going to new york every year for 10 years and this is the first time that I have made it to this area. I found it amazing, there is even a Tiffany store, Trump Hotel but not the same as looking at them in 5th Ave. Going go get the only real negative out of the way.. BATHROOM - OMG.. Four girls in the one bedroom, four crazy irish shoppers into the mix and a bathroom that you can see right into.. Feel sorry for the person who is on the right hand side of the bed, your nose is literally squeezed into the glass, and boy, there is nothing left to the imagination here. Immediate call down to house keeping to tried to do something with a double bed sheet and thumb tacks which kept falling each time some one entered the bathroom but we had to put up with it.. Why on earth cant they just put something on to the glass like a perspex decal or something.. It really is unacceptable. Front desk where always very friendly, the bell hops at the front door where in a league of their own. On the last day they could not have been better. One of the guys went round the block until he got us a taxi van rather than pay for 2 cabs to take us all plus numerous bags to airport. Weekends, this place really does go to sleep, but come monday morning it is bouncing. On arrival we all received complimentary vouchers for drinks which we forgot about. Didnt eat here, but used one of the carts just across street which was gorgeous.. Room service was fantastic, loads and loads of snow white crisp clean towels, shower really powerful and any amount of hot water. Mini bar in room which we emptied to store our own drinks which was a pity. The bedroom was big enough for four, would love to stay again at xmas but the prices are crazy, so if anyone has any good low cost hotels they can recommend please do so.

“They get it right down to the smallest detail” I researched my hotel choice before booking the Residence Inn. The glowing reviews here were right on the money. This is a terrific hotel choice for a visitor to Denver. Pluses: Location:Close to public transportation, restaurants, clubs, 16th St. mall, the fabulous biking/walking trail by Cherry Creek, convention center, Larimore Square. Clean. The housekeepers are very good and my room was spotless. The staff at the breakfast and wine/beer/light dinner service was very good. Tables were cleared and cleaned promptly. Rooms: The rooms are generously sized and attractively furnished. The kitchen is very well equipped. Free internet in the rooms is nice, but the real plus was having a good sized desk on which to work (with good lighting!). I like the suite idea when traveling on business. It is much more comfortable when colleagues drop in to have a place to meet and talk. Specials: The nice wine and beer socials and the included breakfast were really great touches. Why I would go back in a minute: The staff. Wow, these people are really trained in customer service. Every time you go to the desk they are anxious to help make your stay a pleasure. Always friendly and professional, every person on this team was hospitable and polite.

“Nice Place, A Bit Remote from Town” Hotel was what you would expect from Marriott/Renaissance. Good service, nice amenities, up to date, clean. I stayed for 5 nights while attending a conference at the convention center. The room was nicely decorated, with a partial view of waterfront/bay, but nothing spectacular, view of most of the city is blocked by another building. Walking distance to the convention center, and several nearby restaurants. However, if you want to see the sights in town it will require a cab or some other form of transportation, and with a city like Boston, I doubt you would want to spend all your time in this rather isolated area of town. Room service was good and prompt, and as others have indicated, Starbucks on first floor for coffee and quick breakfast. I would stay again, if going to a conference at the convention center, but there are many more convenient nice hotels to stay at if you want to get a better feel for what Boston has to offer.

“Convenient Downtown Location” The location is the selling point here, if you are in town for meetings on the north end of downtown. It also is reletively close to the symphony hall, and just across the expressway from the restaurants of the McKinney Ave corridor. It is connected to a small mall area with a decent food court (and ice rink). The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. The room is comfortable but nothing all that different from most hotels at this price range.

“Repeat customer” This was my second stay at the Belleclaire, and it has only improved. The renovated rooms are beautiful and comfortable; loved the ipod docking station and flat screen TV. I had a room facing out onto the street and was able to get free wifi from somewhere in the neighborhood. The staff are outstanding and always very helpful with directions and advice. The location is excellent; only a short walk to the crosstown bus stop and to the subway and more great restaurants than one has time to sample. Consistently the best value on the Upper West Side.

“Better Than Vegas” Who would have thought that not only did MGM spend $700 million for a 400 room resort hotel in the city known more for coney's and Greek salads, but that it would create a property that rivals any Vegas one including Bellagio and Wynn? You drive up to the hotel valet entrance and you are instantly whisked away to the front desk. The well trained and efficient staff checks you in, asks what newspaper you want and you are ready for relaxation. You walk through private doors to the hotel lobby featuring a fireplace wall, comfy seating and 24hr deluxe coffee service. Rooms are well appointed, we love the corner suite with two rooms. All feature rain showers, incredible beds, bottled water, and nice amenities. The crown jewel however is the Immerse Spa. Think Canyon Ranch and you get the picture. Situated on two levels, service is impeccable. The check in level features mani/pedi room, full gym, and relaxation area with fresh fruit and beverages. The lower level is pure paradise. Perhaps the best hotel indoor pool with cabanas and comfy lounge chairs. Full locker rooms with steam, spa and sauna, deluxe toiletries. Treatment rooms feature al the services you want but massage is king and they have the best therapists. It's easy to spend hours here alone. Food is special as well. Again, who would think that a Detroit hotel would feature both a Wolfgang and not one but two Michael Mina restaurants? It's true. Wolfgang has all the traditional offerings and service is top rated. Bourbon Steak offers a full menu and burger bar menu at the bar. If that's not enough, Ignite Sushi is fresh and amazing. There is also a good buffet and food court (great turkey burgers). Yes, there is a casino with 4000 slot machines, table games and a well run poker room. However you can enjoy yourself immensely without the casino but I will admit it's great to have. Only downside? Leaving. But the friendly valet staff will wish you a good day and welcome you back soon. Good thing.

“Another good hotel in River North” We go to Chicago quite often, and recently stayed here for 2 nights as the place we normally stay was all booked up. Now we have another good option in the River North area. The rooms were spacious, and the decor was a little more modern. I liked the layout of the room a lot. We were on the 22nd floor and had a nice view of the city from the floor to ceiling window. I would stay here again!

“The full 5 stars!” Gotta love this place - yes it's kitsch, and the Elvis theme wears thin very quickly if you're not a devoted fan, but look at it objectively - it's clean, it's got a pulse, the pool is great, and it's in the best part of Memphis, with decent shops and food all nearby. Considering what a dump the rest of Memphis is, I'd have no qualms about staying here again even if I didn't want to visit Graceland. Staff are friendly and breakfast is more than adequate.

“Quite good value” The hotel is somewhat on the outskirts of Downtown, but that area seemed safe and it's only a couple of blocks from the bars and restaurants on 16th Street mall. The rooms was somewhat tired and lacked some common amenities (e.g. in-room safe). Free breakfast, wifi and gym were welcome though.

“VERY CLEAN and comfortable too!” I stayed at the CM Cherry Creek in Denver for 4 days while travelling on business. The front desk staff is very polite and professional. There is no outside access to your rooms - you must pass through the main lobby to get to the elevators. The hotel is 100% non-smoking and does not alllow pets. My room had a microwave, a refrigerator, iron, ironing board, hair dryer, queen bed, a wardrobe for clothes, a nice desk with plenty of plugs and lamps, a sofa with living room table and a flat screen tv. Oh, the alarm clocks even have the ability to hook up to your ipod! The rooms are very clean. It looks as though the hotel was recently built or remodeled b/c it appears to be very clean and updated. The bathrooms were also very clean. I did not have a problem walking in my bare feet at this hotel and since I'm a germaphobe that's pretty amazing. :) The hotel has a pool, hot tub, exercise room, a business center (with complimentary printing), a bar/restaurant, complimentary coffee, tea (and cookies in the afternoon!). The hotel has free wifi so you have internet access everywhere. The hotel also has a "market place" where you can buy frozen dinners, ice cream, candy , trail mix, soda, etc. The breakfast is very good, but pricy at the restaurant. The cold breakfast buffet is $9 (includes coffee and juice) and the hot breakfast buffet is $12.95 (includes coffee and juice). Regarding location, the hotel is located in a very commercial area so there are a ton of stores and a few places to eat at. In the immediate vicinity is Black Eye Pea, Hooters, and local asian and hispanic restaurants. A whole foods is located just down the street, near the Barnes and Noble and Target. The hotel is about 20 minutes from the federal courthouse in downtown Denver, 5 minutes from Englewood and about 30 minutes from Morison. It's also about a 30 minute drive from the Denver airport. Overall, I am very pleased with this hotel.

“Modern, but very comfortable.” We booked this hotel for four nights. We arrived there a bit early but could check in straight away, we were given breakfast vouchers which we were not expecting. The receptionist came around to the front of the desk to show us where the lifts were, which was a nice touch, and told us that wine was served between 5.00 and 6.00pm every day in the reception area. The room was excellent, lovely large bed with feather pillows, I was a bit worried as the interior is very modern, but all the furniture was very comfortable, including two lovely armchairs in the bedroom. The only downside was that we didn't have a view, but there again we were out every day. We went down to the reception area at 5.00pm and had more than one glass of wine! a very nice touch. Benjamin the "bellboy" was more than helpful, he really couldn't do enough, he would suggest where to go and eat and he always asked us if we had enjoyed our day. Would we stay there again, definately.

“A cool and comfortable new hotel” Stayed here for two nights and wish it were more. Chose the hotel because I got a great deal on the hotel's website. Saw some reviews that commented on the tiny rooms - my room was spacious and fit the queen bed, desk/chair, sitting chair and end table comfortably. Bathroom was also spacious and stocked with great products from H2O+, a bathrobe, and miscellaneous toiletries like cotton pads and q-tips. Decor was sleek/modern, bordering on funky. The bed and pillows were both very comfortable. Only negative was that the heating system was a little noisy when turned on. Free wireless internet was very convenient, but there is also a business center with free access and printers. The hotel lobby area is small, but both nights there were people lounging around the bar area. The entire staff was incredibly friendly. One negative was the area - hotel is a little more than "steps" from Michigan Ave. Hotel seemed to be a lot closer to great restaurants than great shopping.

“not for a weekend getaway” Stayed at this Embassy Suites over a weekend. i forgot what the Embassy suites are like during that time period. This Embassy Suites was well kept. It is clean, and the front desk people are easy to work with. They have a nice reception at night, and the people working it even know how to make a Long Island Ice Tea. Can't tell you if it's any good or not as I just drink beer. Small work-out room, but they have three treadmill machines, some free weights, as well as a cable machine. A nice amenity. The pool are is well kept also. They have the standard cook-to-order breakfast that Embassy suites are known for, but in apparent anticipation of a large amount of guests that night (Saturday), they had a side buffet ready to go on Sunday morning as well. It had a separate, small line, where you could get eggs, meat, potatoes, biscuits, rather than wait in a rather large line (9:00 am). Nice touch by the management. The room are typical of an Embassy Suite, and the bedroom walls are paper thin (which is also a trademark of theirs). Which again is typical of the ES construction. About 3:00 am, I was awakenend by the people next door who were "on a roll". Not only did the chatter go on, but everyone needed a shower. I called the front desk about 3:30 am, and they said they would send up security. Nothing happened. I called again about 4:15 am, and the front desk said that they would call and give a "final warning" or words to that effect. It didn't work. The hotel does have some sort of security as they like to drive around the parking lot with their green lights flashing, but I don't think they are allowed into the hotel. And in fairness to them, it is hard to reason with a bunch of drunks at 4:00 in the morning. About 5:00 am, the party finally died. I complained to the front desk the next morning. I had checked in for 3 nights, but after 2 hights, I was done. They were polite enough to comp the room for the second night. It's partially my fault, as after all of these years of traveling, I should know better than to check into an Embassy Suites for the weekend.

“Modern hotel with great amenities and a convenient location” We really enjoyed our stay at the Hyatt Regency. The lobby is impressive and there is a beautiful bar/restaurant on the 27th floor with amazing views of the mountains and city. We loved watching the sunset from up there. Our room was clean and modern. The doors are quite heavy though, so expect some slamming in the middle of the night or morning from other people. This is not the hotel's fault, however you may want to ask for a room away from the elevators or at end of hall to minimize it. The location is perfect for exploring Denver. You are one block away from the 16th street mall, close to the Capitol buildings, and if you're after a Rockies Game or want to get to the LoDo area, it's a ten minute walk or you can hop on the free shuttle that is a block away and goes up and down the 16th street mall We have stayed in a number of hotels in downtown Denver and this is our favorite so far.

“At the Center of Times Square!” What I loved: Location Super fast (and fun) elevators Suite on the 40th floor Concierge lounge for breakfast and evening cocktails Front line service associates The bagel shop that is about a block away Location, location, location! What I didn't like: The crowds

“Not Bad at All” Not a bad place at all. Very large room, comfortable bed. The living room area of the suite wasn't plush, but was comfortable, (We weren't in there a lot, though, so it really didn't matter.) The kitchen is efficient and met what limited needs we had. (The tap water isn't the tastiest, though.) Bathroom small, but tidy and efficient; shower not bad, not great. Overall, we had a great experience. The desk clerks let us do an early check-in, which was very helpful. The room was immaculate and comfortable. The breakfast was tasty and simple, which was fine. The laundry facilities were very helpful in that I'd spilled tomato juice on my pants on the plane trip to Seattle and was able to wash it out. Negatives are few: The lobby could use some lighting help, though, as the sodium lights in the atrium make it very unfriendly in the evening. The parking garage is a bit cramped. We were given an SUV by our rental company, and parking in such a tight space in the evening was a bit of an adventure. (Getting out in the morning was no problem.) The gym and pool were overrun by noisy teens the first time we used them, but the other times we used them, they were fine. Location is good; very accessible to everywhere we were going. I'd definitely stay here again.

“Great choice at JAX!” What a great surprise! We stayed one night at the Residence Inn and enjoyed every minute of it. The property is in great condition and the staff is terrific. It is the nicest RI we've ever stayed in. The apartment layout was great, the decor beautiful and the beds were extremely comfortable. The breakfast was a step up from the usual "free deal". We will certainly go back!

“Great Location, Minimal Perks” We were tempted into a package to review the timeshare plan for this location in NYC. The hotel is very modern with few perks. The lobby is extremely small, the rooms are actually average for New York. If you like the whole green, modern look then this a hotel for you. There is no bar or place to have a drink and they have the audacity to call the hotel room a studio. The concierge was truly novice and has not pull for the finer dining establishments in NYC. The location is outstanding to be able to enjoy the city. If you are not ready to spend a minimum of $50,000 for a time share, not sure I would waste your time taking the package. This took 3 hours out of the middle of our day and we were only there for the weekend. The time to view the tineshare was non negotiable. The Spa Merge was also thrown into the package. For both my husband and I the spa was quite happy to tell us that it would be a minimal facial because it was Free and 30 minutes was too short to truly get the full spa effect! As for the time share sell. It was classic NY and high pressure. The Manager that attempted to close us when the salesman could not, literally slammed her binder shut and quickly told us to get our spa certificates and leave. Extremely unprofessional and truly rude. If you want a clean , great location,in Manhattan this might be for you. I would not stay at this property again based on my experience. I felt it was extremely quid pro quo. I will not be bought again for program like this. There are many other plush, lovely hotels in New York. By the way check out time is at 10:00 am!
“Great Hotel” This is a GREAT HOTEL!!! I have stayed at this hotel a few times now and each time I enjoy it more and more. This is a newer hotel with a great location, great staff and great design.

“Updating "a classic" -- very nicely done” Booked via Marriott.com and got a price quite a bit lower than the super-luxe hotels in the Financial District and/or the high-end tourist hotels on Russian Hill or Union Square. Interestingly, the location of the Stanford Court is just as good, as it is essentially within a 5~10 minute walk of all of these points!. This is an older building, built around a courtyard, without the 40 stories that offer spectacular views of the Bay or Telegraph Hill, but it is 2nd to none regarding location, appointments, convenience and service. Biggest test in these older buildings are the bathrooms and the "corner" areas -- bottom line, they passed. The property has been nicely updated and all the modern amenities are in place. . In very few cases, I say this, but I would DEFINITELY seek and attempt to stay in the Stanford Court on my next trip to San Francisco. . Granted, the property is still a bit challenged by the history (this can be a plus, if one likes that sort of thing) so there isn't a super-sleek multi-story lobby, or a chi-chi destination restaurant or bar. (they happen to be just outside less than 2 blocks away!). In my too-brief 14 hour stay, I also experienced EXCELLENT service by a staff that obviously gives a hoot about the comfort of its guests. Several above & beyonds that made my too-brief 14 hour stay quite comfortable and leaves me wanting more. Great value for a perfectly located hotel that does not disappoint.

“My Wife Loved It...Enough Said” My wife and I spent three nights at the Argonaut Hotel during January of 2005. We loved it! The California King bed was great, as were the feather pillows and overall room decor. Location is everything, and the Argonaut Hotel has a great location at the corner of Hyde and Jefferson on Fisherman's Wharf. Although a little large for boutique hotel status, we loved the place and recommend it highly to anyone wanting a great place to stay in San Francisco. The only negative is The Blue Mermaid Restaurant in the hotel, which we found to be tacky and expensive. Do yourself a favour next time you are in San Francisco. Stay at the Argonaut Hotel.

“Excellent hotel with friendly staff.” Very large hotel with very friendly and helpful staff. The rooms are large and clean with 42 inch flat panel TVs that work, and have numerous channels . Excellent concierge lounge. Reasonalby priced valet parking, but self parking is just as convienent as valet parking. This hotel is located on Westheimer, and there are numerous quality dining places located in this area. if you are driving, you have easy access to all parts of Houston via Beltway 8. i have stayed in this hotel many times and will continue stay here when I am in Houston.

“Bring your own bottled water” Well, what should I say. It basically is one of the very few hotels around Logan Airport, so here we go. The hotel is a good 5min drive from the airport and the (car) rental stations (which is great). The service was quite good and pleasant. Rooms are clean; but somewhat noisy - you can go with the runway- or the highway-side. The latter probably a little more convenient. The walls seemed to be quite thin as I could hear other guests almost clearly well. Hallways are dark and dim. I had to check out about 5 (!!) floors to find a vending machine either working or not sold out.Thus this was an average stay.

“Nice views” We stayed here on a recent vist to Seattle because they took our Marriott Any Time certificate which I received for credit card miles. It came with free breakfast for 2 which the waiter extended into a full breakfast for 3. I think what makes this hotel stand out is the staff. They were all very friendly and accommodating and this made our stay. The room we had was large and well ventilated away from I-5. The roof level pool had great vistas of Seattle. The palce was very clean. The only drawbacks were the off center location and the colorless lobby. For us it was a good deal. For full price try for a more close in location. However it should be noted the hotel sits right on the free dwtown bus loop so that makes getting anywhere downtown easy

“Good location, good value” This hotel is surrounded by many other hotels, which I think makes the Comfort Inn try harder to remain competitive. From the outside, the building is rather plain and almost sterile, but I don't choose a hotel because of its external appearance alone. The lobby is inviting with a cozy sitting area and breakfast room. The hallways are a little dim, and the carpet in the hallway looks worn but acceptable. The room was great. Spacious; clean. I was on the third floor and faced north. I found nothing to report as a problem with the room. The hotel has wired and Wif-fi Internet access. I used the wireless the first evening I was there. Reception was perfect (5 out of 5 bars). I had trouble connecting the next morning, so I plugged in to the Ethernet cable, which was long enough to reach the hallway. The desk staff was fine. They were curteous and helpful. I booked two nights through an online site and received 20% off my total stay, which made the hotel very affordable. Without the discount the rate was comparable to other hotels in the area. I would gladly stay here again. (CS)

“Not what I expected” I spent 5 days at the hotel during a conference. I know hotels tend to be chaotic during such times, but you survive. Having said so, I will never stay at a Westin again. Sure there were good things, but that ́s what I expect for $280 plus tax per night!!! My room was spacious (not the bathroom that was tiny) and had a comfy bed. But what made my stay unpleasant was the service. Or should I say the lack of it? My room key demagnetized three times, and even when they replaced it, it still didn't work. Then, before I arrived I contacted the hotel to ask whether they would receive some packages for me. They said they would do so, but they never told me that they would charge me $7 per package! I stayed at Intercontinental and Hilton hotels and they never charged me for that service. In any event, I would expect to be told if there are charges when I ask!! After complaining with staff and the manager, they didn't charge me. And I almost forgot: My room was next to the floor's service area, and the door was constantly being slammed by the staff. I guess it was bad luck to get that room, but I had no time to change room or to complain about it.... I had breakfast at the hotel a couple of days, but it was not good either. I also had breakfast at the Intercontinental during a meeting, and it was way better than the Westin. Anyway, I think there are better options in San Francisco for the same price and with better service.

“Glitzy Four Seasons best for Young Urban Professionals” Four Seasons hotels are great. The amenities and service are so far superior to what you find in even a nice Hilton or Sheraton that it feels like splitting hairs to complain about anything. I spent three nights in the Baltimore Four Seasons for work last weekend. My birthday just happened to fall over the weekend as well. Not only did the hotel make note of my preferences (pillows and coffee maker) from a previous stay at at Four Seasons property, but they upgraded me and left a delicious piece of cake in my room with a note wishing me a happy birthday. My room was spectacular: quiet, with big windows (city rather than harbor view) and very, very large. There was an excellent d.j. at the pool on Sunday afternoon playing exactly the right tunes for the time and place. The sushi was great in the sushi restaurant. And the staff, without fail, was spectacular. From reception desk, to doorman, to bartender- everyone at this Four Seasons seems to know their job perfectly. So now my very minor complaints: aesthetically this is not one of my favorite Four Seasons. The lobby decor was glitzier than I like (lots of mirrors and gold), the bar was completely overrun by young drunken stock-broker types every night of my stay, and some of the guests at the pool were very loud (and I am not talking about children). When you are in the hotel you have absolutely no sense of being in Baltimore as opposed to anywhere else. And I don't think the location is really the best, either for business downtown or for sightseeing, since it is a good twenty minute hike to the Inner Harbor. I also wish the car service had better hours. But that's really all I can say against a really amazing world-class hotel. Overall I think this is probably a better Four Seasons for young urban professionals than for families, but I look forward to bringing my family here to find out for myself.

“Location Location Location!” I have to say -- Trip Advisor does it again! I can't say enough about what a great site this is! After booking a great price on Priceline, i went to Trip Advisor to really see what I got! Sure enough - - the reviews were true -- great location - close to all the museums and Metro -- and even told me that a certain part of the hotel was noisy and to stay away from that part of the building. At check in, the hotel clerk knew exactly what I meant and put us on the other side of the building - we heard nothing. I would rate it - 3 stars- the hotel needs some updating, but it's clean and the Starbucks in the lobby is very convenient - especially in the cold winter months! I'd recommend it for a good price - don't pay too much or you'll be angry :)

“Beautiful views from Harbor Tower” I stayed here two nights while attending a very large seminar. I agree with the prior comments that this hotel frequently features large crowds of conference-goers, but it seemed to me that the hotel staff is completely capable of handling these crowds. The staff was consistently very pleasant, attentive, and helpful. I was on the 20th floor of the Harbor Tower and the views were just stunning. I could have just stayed in my room, ordered room service, and enjoyed the views of Navy vessels and sail boats in the bay. The outdoor pool is smallish, but the entire patio area is quite large, and, again, has a great view of the San Diego Bay. The hotel is very nicely located between the Seaport Village (which has good, if not great, restaurants) and the Gaslight District (which has great restaurants). The Embarcadero Marina park (just out the hotel's back doors) is beautiful, with great running/walking paths. The hotel is also quite close (by bus or car) to Balboa Park. Overall, I would certainly stay here again, and I think it would be a good hotel for a family's vacation.

“I liked it” I stayed here oct. 20-22 2008 Great place, welcomed by very friendly, informative staff going out of their way to make me feel welcome, they covered all my needs at check in Room was a studio on the 9th floor very well appointed, comfortable, roomy, and clean, with a full kitchen there was not a view to speak of but I wasn't there for that. Breakfast buffet was very nice and appreciated The negative would be that it's location area is not well lit, and a block off on Union ave which is a bit more busy The front desk said up to around 11:30 pm it is mostly safe........ I did not feel like it was a sketchy neigborhood but late night caution would be advised....... This hotel was a great help to having a great visit to memphis

“A very mixed response” I used to live in NYC, and we visit it several times throughout the year. We love staying at the Four Seasons where the level of service and comfort is extremely high. We got a nice rate at the Plaza for our Spring trip and decided to experience it. The bad things first. The decor is very Vegas. It's not classy at all. The service is mediocre. We're usually laid back about things. We arrived early at the airport and called to find out if we could have the room. We showed up and were told the room wasn't ready. The front desk person gave us attitude. We were promised a paper, and it wasn't delivered. We had a suite - and the bathroom does not have two sinks. It's roomy but no room to put your stuff down. Too much gold and to much "belle epoque" gaudiness for our taste. The room service food is outrageously expensive. We're used to paying extra for food at hotels, but these prices are exorbitant - and the food is just ok. If you're staying, walk towards the corner of 6th Avenue and 57th street and the RUE 57 restaurant will serve a better breakfast at a third of the price. The bar scene is like something out of Caesar's Palace in Vegas. As we were checking out, the front desk person told us to be careful on our flight "because it's been crazy up there." I asked him what he meant. He mentioned the recent Air France crash. I walked away sick in my stomach (I'm a terrible flyer.) The good stuff: The room is extremely clean, and spacious. The location couldn't be better. They're offering some great bargains. Would we ever come back? No. The service and decor is very Vegas. You do not feel special. If you want true NY luxury and great service look somewhere else.

“Sleep Tight” We have stayed at this Doubletree on several occasions as we travel out of the country. It is close to the airport and has an excellent shuttle service that will deliver you on a timely basis. On our last trip since it was a special occasion we upped our room to a two room suite and it was wonderful. Nice furnishings and the beds rank as one of the best on my list. The rooms are well sound proofed and quiet. On premise is a pretty good restaurant with resonable prices and room service. At this time they also have parking for those leaving Charlotte. After the first seven days I think they charge you a nominal fee and pick you up upon return. A fine hotel that will let you sleep tight all night.

“Trading on past reputation” Stayed here several times about five years ago and rooms were nice. But z- nothing has been done in five years. Romans are now old and slightly shabby. Carpet has been cleaned so much you can feel the cleaning solution in bare feet. Nice mattress so got good sleep but glad we were there for just one night. Had bath with jacuzzi. But - no hot water except the sink. When we told them on checkout they just passed it off. - didn't offer a discount or apology. Taking a shower in tepid water not fun. There are many newer chain hotels in area and will pick roc them next time.

“Slow check in, but great location at BWI” The check in process is very slow, it takes a shorter time to get from BWI. The re were four people working the front desk but the process still is slow. I travel every week plenty much and this was the longest check in time by far. The location is so close to BWI I might stay again at this Four Points. The propery is fairly good condition for an older propery. There are many better choices in this price range if you don't need to be right next to BWI.

“Surprisingly not bad....” We were a little dubious about staying here from all the reviews! On arrival for 8 nights we were told that the only room they had booked for us (we booked back in Jun 11) was a double bed.....um there are 2 adults & 2 children. It wasn't looking good but in the end he rearranged & we got 2 doubles - phew!!!!! The rooms are like a matchbox but hey we are in NYC & we only sleep here! The free breakfast is great, limited seating but we have not had trouble getting one & the hotel is completely dull! Location is good we are walking everywhere & it's about a 10 minute walk to Times Square (kids are 8 & 5!). The diamond district is interesting & if your not interested I suggest u avoid as they all stand outside trying to hustle u in. It's an absolute must to do the 9/11 memorial but make sure you book your tickets online that's the only way you can get the tickets. Also we used a go pass which yes saved us time buying tickets but there wA no express line as promised for any of the attractions! Also as we were here for so long we were desperate for a coin laundromat which noone could help us with - if you go to 9th avenue between 50th & 51st there are heaps of them!

“Great location and views. Inconsistent service.” We stayed at the Westin Seattle for 3 nights in late early September 2011. Room on 39th floor of North Tower faced West (towards water and Space Needle) which made for amazing sunset views. Very comfortable bed and spacious bathroom. We had requested a quiet room and were given a room at the very end of the hall. This location turned out to be not quiet because the doors are thin and/or noise travels very well (when we returned and quietly opened our own door one night, our next door neighbor thought we were opening his door). So we ended up listening to housekeeping using the utility closet every morning. Somehow it was quite loud in what was a not very populated hallway--if you want a quiet room, ask to be away from both the elevators and housekeeping. When we arrived around 6 pm, I asked the front desk to send sheets/blanket up for the sofabed right away and they said they would do so. An hour later, we had to leave for a dinner engagement, but there were no sheets. When we spoke with the concierge about this on the way out, we told her that we had waited an hour and housekeeping had not appeared; strangely she did not ask for our room number nor took any action, but simply assured me they was coming. Four hours later when we returned, there were still no sheets. In essence, the hotel was sold out for a conference and while the staff were always polite, they were not particularly friendly nor did they step up to make our stay feel more than a standard experience. The location was great, but I got the impression the guests were basically on their own. Some tips: If you go to Pikes Place Market, keep in mind that the vendors close up around 4-5 pm --and start early. You can buy huge beautiful bouquets of fresh flowers for very reasonable prices (nice romantic touch). Great take-out sushi can be had at the food-court at nearby Westlake Mall. The Westin charges $41 for self-parking, but there is a lot right next door that charges $22 and it has a skyway that links into the Westin. We had a 12 year old who really enjoyed the Boeing Museum of Flight, the ferry cruises, the EMP, and of course, the Space Needle.

“good deal in the heart of downtown Seattle” The Pacific Plaza is a good deal in the heart of downtown Seattle. The rooms are small but nicely decorated and extremely clean. It is comparable to many other landmark hotels with small rooms -- charming and pleasant. Seattle is a fantastic city with not many inexpensive lodging choices. So this makes the Pacific Plaza quite a glorious find. The service was incredibly friendly and knowledgeable. I had a great stay at this hotel.
“Great Location” We enjoyed our stay at the Sofitel. Everyone was very helpful and the location was perfect for us, not too close, but not too far away. Room was typical NY size, but very nice!

“New favorite place in Seattle- Good location” Last time we were in Seattle we stayed at another Homewood Suites property in town but not this property. While there was nothing to complain about the other property this is where I will stay from now on. The hotel is pleasantly situated in downtown Seattle. It is about 8 blocks from the Pikes Street Market and perhaps 4 blocks away from the heart of downtown and the monorail to the Seattle Center. Its price based on location cannot be matched as your stay includes breakfast and happy hour during the week. The hotel is nice and clean, modern, and has all the extra amenities one would expect from a Hilton property and especially a Homewood Suites. My only mild complaint about the hotel was that parking is only valet and the price was a bit steep at $33 a night however parking in Seattle itself is a nightmare and the valet staff did wash our car. Overall as much as I travel to Seattle I will be back here again.

“Excellent facility” Great property. Beautiful building. Really nice suites. Well designed, high ceilings, complimentary fast internet. Room service fabulous. Excellent staff, friendly, efficient, very professional.

“Déprimant et bruyant” Attention au nom, il n'est pas à Soho, mais à Chinatown. Ce qui ne serait pas un problème en soi, du moins pour les personnes qui sont à l'aise un peu partout... sinon s'abstenir. Eviter d'avoir un bagage un peu lours, ar pour entrer il faut grimper un escalier haut et raide avant d'atteindre l'accueil, cependant professionnel et irréprochable. Ambiance d'ailleurs plutot sympa. Mais lorsqu'on vous conduit à votre chambre - car sinon, on se perd des couloirs alambiqués et étroits - vous vous demandez un peu si vous êtes dans un remake de macadam cow boy... et la chambre est totalement encombrée par le lourd lit qui vous permet de toucher la porte allongée en tendant le bras. Déco hyper vieillote, mais ça peut avoir son charme, propreté ok, mais un bruit de rue juste insupportable. Pas fermé l'oeil de la nuit !!! Hors deprix pour la presation comparée à des "gros porteurs" mieux situés et très confortable. Pour moi, un piège à touriste, notament en raison d'un nom évocateur et trompeur.

“Solid but losing its luster. Watch out for twin beds” This used to be one of the top properties in Chicago but it has been eclipsed by new entrants and needs updating. That said, it is still a good property in an excellent location and is good value for money at its current rate structure. The pluses: - Fantastic location - Reliable Ritz / Four Seasons amenities and service levels - Free wireless internet (surprised me) - Great views of Hancock and Lake Shore Drive (North view) - Very reasonable rates during the period I stayed here The minuses: - Lobby area and some elements of the room are a bit dated - Service is of an older, stuffier, and more formal variety. I didn't find the staff to be warm / friendly nor were they proactive in anticipating needs. That said, they were good on the basics Also, watch out when booking a room with two beds. My room had two twin beds. I was very surprised. I have never seen a twin bed at a luxury hotel outside of Japan.

“Beautiful Hotel” This hotel is a bit dated, but it is beautifully maintained, and in a great location. The hotel staff is friendly and welcoming. The rooms have kitchens in them as well. The swans are beautiful and I love the birds! They are out from morning to early evening. They are well cared for by the staff. The food is very good, and the pool is nice. The hotel is right across the street from the beach, and the backside of the resort is on a little bay. It's within walking distance to several restaurants and stores. I had no issues with the staff or my reservations.

“Loved the waterfront location and all the top-flight amenities” Got a decent Hotwire rate here. We were both a bit worried about staying at this hotel based on some tepid reviews. But we really had no serious problems. The desk clerk was very nice when we arrived at 11 a.m. and gave us a spacious room on the 8th floor with a view of Fort Point Channel. The room was very comfortable, cool, and quiet. We both liked the huge bathroom with separate shower, which had great water pressure. The translucent window that slid open above the bed was an odd accent, which meant if we got up in the night to visit the bathroom we had to grope around in the dark, so as to avoid illuminating the bedroom and thus wake each other up. But really, no big deal. To avoid the steep hotel prices, on the first morning, Sunday, we brewed cups of coffee in the room (wished there was enough coffee for more than one cup apiece!), then walked over to South Station, 4 minutes away, and had breakfast at the Au Bon Pain for a total of $10 for two. The second morning we went to Scali Deli across the street, also around $10 for two. Since we had prebooked the Provincetown ferry for a daytrip this was a perfect location; we could walk there in about 10-15 minutes. We also walked to the North End, Park Street, the new Harbor Walk, and the ICA. People who have never been to Boston may find the location a bit remote, but we loved being by the water and enjoyed the super-easy airport access via the Silver Line bus to/from South Station, $2 per person each way. We also enjoyed the water view at the back of the hotel, very pleasant. The only negative was an insanely LOUD post-wedding party that jolted us awake at 2 a.m. in a nearby room the first night. Security visited them and told them to quiet down, but they didn't shut up for an hour. People can be so rude!

“Great for group travel” We stayed here with our girl scout troop and enjoyed the great service. The front desk was quick at checking us in. The best was location, location, location! Close to fisherman's wharf, Pier 39, Ghiradelli, and the cable car turnaround. The muni stop was located at corner of hotel and the F-train stop was one block up, perfect for our needs. The hotel was recently renovated and it still had the new smell. Rooms were nicely furnished, we had a coffee maker & refrigerator. The girls enjoyed the pool which is heated and the fire pit area was cozy & inviting. This is a great hotel for a group to explore the area.

“Great Hotel, great service. Definitely stay again” Booked high-level Executive King-bed room, and not disappointed. Twice as good as our previous hotel, the Crowne Plaza Times square, and far less cost. very friendly and helpful check-n. Changed rooms to get the best view for us. Room was not large, but great ambience and decor. Wonderful bathroom. Excellent Flat sceen, mini-bar and all amenities. On same floor as Executive Lounge which was convenient. really wonderful breakfast included. helpful breakfast staff. easy parking. Stored luggage whilst we went away for two weeks. Would higly recommend. Also a very convenient area, teo blocks to times Square, Macey's etc.

“4 Stars and deserves it” My wife and I spent only 1 night in the hotel in july 2012. We were coming back from Napa and needed a 1 night spot before our flight out of SFO. The hotel meets all the standards you would expect from a 4 star hotel. Nice rooms, good sized. comfy bed and bedding. Bathroom was normal size with all the amenities. All the hotels in SF are a little pricey but we found a good deal on priceline, we bid $135 per night and got it. So it was a good deal for us. After staying in the Intercontinental in SF earlier in the week, I think most of the 4 star hotels in SF are about the same. The hotel had a large bar and my group of 4 had a couple delicious cocktails before retiring to bed. I even remember the waitresses name, Cecilia. She was fun and provided great service. It is nice to recieve friendly welcomes and she was great. we didn't eat in the hotel but the menu looked pretty good. We rented a car from enterprise right across the street which was convienent. The only downer to this hotel is that the back side of the hotel is the start of the tenderloin district (worst couple blocks in central SF) but the hotel does a great job of keeping you on the "nice" side of the street. just a few blocks from Union Square. really good location. there is a great Italian restaurant across the street (Pincelli & Puccelli or something like that... great pasta). I would stay here again.

“La prima impressione non è quella che conta” Appena arrivata in questo hotel sono rimasta un po'sconcertata perchè essendo situato al porto di Philadelphia credevo che fosse molto decentrato e di riuscire a raggiungere i luoghi importanti della città con molta difficoltà. In realtà mi sono dovuta ricredere! Infatti in circa un quarto d'ora a piedi si raggiunge facilmente la zona centrale! L'hotel è un buon hotel, con camere ampie e pulite e davvero un ottima colazione, anche se il servizio è un po'lento: dopo l'ordinazione c'è chi ha dovuto aspettare anche più di mezz'ora! Io me la sono cavata in un quarto d'ora per fortuna! Nota negativa: internet a pagamento, 24 ore = $ 9.95!! Mi sembra eccessivo! Per il resto tutto ok!!

“Choose this one!!!!!!!!” Beautiful lobby, quiet, clean rooms, and wonderful indoor pool. I stayed with the kids while my husband was at a business meeting, and we had the best time. The complimentary breakfast is full of wonderful options and a cooked to order menu including omelets, eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes, biscuits and gravy. The pastry bar even had a sprinkle donut for my little boy! We spent all morning in the spotless, warm indoor pool and spa. We were given a late check out time of 1:00 and drove to nearby Ball's Hamburgers for a tasty lunch. The area was very easy to get around and is beautiful. A small town feel in a huge city! The best part of the stay was Cindy at the hotel restaurant who served us a great meal when we arrived the first night. She was so kind and generous to my hungry sleepy chidren and told us all the area stores and restaurants. The fabulous North Park Mall is nearby and the hotel will provide a shuttle! This is my hotel of choice for Dallas, Texas now!

“Lasciate perdere” Non posso assolutamente conservare un buon ricordo di questa sistemazione: é vecchio, le stanze sono spartane, i gestori non sono il massimo della cordialità. Ma la cosa peggiore é l'odore presente in stanza, di legno umido, veramente nauseante. Le colazioni, se non altro, sono buone e abbondanti.Troppo alto il costo rispetto alla qualità. A mio parere l'unica cosa da salvare di questo albergo é la posizione, a Nob Hill, veramente a due passi da Chinatown,Financial District e Columbus Avenue. La zona non é peggiore di altre, c'é molta vita e la sera si può uscire tranquilli.

“Can I take the bed home please?” The renovation of this hotel is flawless. They even managed to make the lobby fireplace look new and fresh. It made the evening wine hour an even more lovely experience. The rooms are spacious and I was lucky enough to get upgraded to a corner suite on the 8th floor. Although it was just me and my boyfriend this suite would be lovely for a family traveling together. The sitting room in addition to a queen sofa bed was big enough to have a table for four and plenty of room to walk around. The bed was incredible! I may have to see what vendor they use the next time I'm in a market for a bed. They are almost done with the elevator replacement which will make it much easier to get up and down easliy.

“Lacking a bit for a Hilton” Our regular hotel was booked and this was closest Hilton property to use my points. You need to look carefully at it's location to find it easily. It's on a 'non traffic' part of Travis St., block west of Main. I found the signage a bit confusing and wound up trapped in the parking (front desk came and 'rescued' us). There was no bellman, but the desk clerk that rescued us, filled that job too. We were there on a Sa. and Su. night. The gift shop was never open and you couldn't get a paper. The breakfast buffet was not I expect of a Hilton and was overpriced. We had a two room suite which was really nice.

“Good NYC alternative” We were looking for a reasonable place to stay in Manhatten and this seemed a good bet. We chose the renovated room with two Queen beds and were very pleased with the comfort and cleanliness. Hostel prices but better quality. We phoned ahead to inform them that we would arrive in the middle of the night and they held our room as promised and checked us in at 2am. The desk staff on duty throughout our staff were always friendly. I don't believe they have a full maintenance staff so when we had no hot water in our private bath, we were forced to use the shared facility because there were no other comparable rooms available and we didn't want to give up our two beds. Short of running into dripping people wrapped scantily in towels, running between shared shower and their rooms, we had no real complaints. The neighborhood is safe and quiet and restaurant selection is wide. Proximity to Riverside Park, Central Park and the subway are all nice features.

“Give this hotel a pass” First the good: hotel is well-located and the rooms are large, especially for Manhattan. My room had a great view. Now the bad: The room, while large, was not in the best shape. It needed to be painted. The bathroom was gross-lots of hair on the walls and in the bathtub. The walls were thin, too. I was kept awaken by television & loud chat most the night. Reception was not up to snuff. My room was not ready until 4pm, and my first two attempts at using the key were unsuccessful. Reception apologized - a large group had checked out late. In fact, housecleaning was still at it with other rooms on my floor. Was this my fault? There similar noise issues at a recent New York Hilton stay. I would avoid both. By contrast, my Sofitel stay last August was perfect from check in to check out. No view, but it was clean, quiet, and the check-in staff perfect.

“Great hotel in a so-so city” I met my son in Southern California in mid-October. We both wanted to visit San Diego and chose the Gas Lamp District based on Trip Advisor reviews. We also chose the Solamar for its great reviews and the fact that I am a Kimpton Rewards member and love the Kimptons. We loved the hotel with its cool pool area and great decor. Beds are amazingly comfortable and rooms are spacious. The only drawback is the weekend party scene at the pool bar area on the weekends. I was fortunate to asked to be moved and as the hotel was not full, they moved me to a quieter room on the side away from the pool. We found San Diego to be very touristy with mostly chain restaurants and convention type attractions with no authenticity or charm. We did love a little side trip out to Coronado Island. Would recommend the Solamar highly but probably won't go back to San Diego!

“Nice Stay at Ritz Denver” Stayed here for one night in October. Arrived late and left early, so didn't get the full experience. The front desk staff was very professional and check-in went quickly. The room was clean and very nicely appointed. The N'espresso machine was a nice touch. One thing to note is that if you're traveling on your own dime, there are several parking garages and lots within a block of the hotel that are substantially cheaper than the hotel's valet. Would definetly return to this property the next time in Denver.

“Probably the worst hotel i've ever used...” Shoddy decor, unloved uncared for - left to decay, After 24 hours of tepid water in my room, I went to reception to see if there was a problem, yes you have to run the taps for 20 minutes for hot water.. room service ? didn't you look at the black book in your room, explained no black book - one was requested but never arrived. Breakfast staff tried but couldn't keep up, thing's missing and people walking out after bored of waiting. Sad as place could be great, but tired and worn. Expensive for what you get, and as my card had already been charged fully upon booking online, I couldn't see me getting a refund and had to stick it out. I didn't eat here as everything else was too depressing to even try.

“Relish the quiet side” The Drisco is located almost at the crest of one of the high hills of the city, a couple of blocks from the Presidio Park, in a quiet residential neighborhood with fabulous views down many of the streets. It is a welcome escape from the usual frenetic hotel districts in SF. The Drisco is pleasantly dignified but not stuffy, attentive but not stifling, elegant but not fussy. The building is from 1903, and the rooms vary substantially in their layout and orientation, so if you want a view or something specific, call and ask. The included breakfast is not hot, but they offer a nice spread of yummy pastries, meats, etc. Internet is also included. On weekends, parking is a snap and free on the streets. During the week, the streets have a 3-hour limit, but the staff do what they can to provide advice to work around this. Many fine neighborhood restaurants are a moderate walk from the hotel, but note well that if walking up steep hills is difficult for you, prepare to take taxis! It's been a while since we've stayed in a hotel we enjoyed more than the little Drisco.

“Good Location-Nice Hotel” I stay at this hotel at least 10 times per year and it is always nice. They hotel is nothing special, much nicer Omni's but for a better price than downtown and easy location close to I-35 it is fine. The Omni Select Guest manager at this property is very helpful to Select Guest members. They go out of the way to make my room choice and other request possible. Self parking, decent food and easy access to the airport and downtown make this hotel a good choice.

“Needs updating” Although in a great location on the marina, and just a short walk to the gaslamp, this hotel is too dated to be so expensive. There is a great view of the water, and a great pool scene, if you want to fight for a chair. They were giving out bracelets to people permitted in the pool area. It was hard to navigate through all the furniture at the pool's edge. I have never been in a property with worse elevators. The lines to get an elevator caused arguements, pushing, and all around unpleasantness. It was completely unacceptable. They should have set up stanchions to form lines for the elevator.

“Acceptable - What I Expected” A decent property with about what I would expect for the price ($161 per night including taxes). The room was clean and spacious. Bed was comfortable. In room coffee. Staff seemed professional, but not particularly friendly or warm. Parking fee and internet charges are a bit high. The doors to rooms seem very loud when they slam shut (even for a hotel) - woke me up a couple of times. The location is very close to downtown and the football stadium. Overall, I think it is an average property. Nothing to set it apart as good or bad. I would be okay with staying here again.

“Just Perfect!” We have visited NYC a few times & have stayed in a different hotel each time, usually in the Midtown area. This one is now our absolute favourite and we would love to stay there again. The good reviews posted here played a big part in our decision to give it a try. New York is a fabulous, vibrant city and after a busy day, The Beacon is just a great place to come back to. The neighbourhood of the Upper West Side is stylish and safe. You feel like you’re part of the real New York. There are loads of lovely shops, restaurants & bars. We spotted the restaurant used in the movie “You’ve Got Mail” just a couple of streets from the hotel. We enjoyed having a drink at the Amsterdam Ale House after seeing a show on Broadway. It’s just round the corner from the hotel. Breakfast in the diner next door is a brilliant experience. The omlettes are fab. The hotel itself is calm and welcoming. The rooms are a great size with everything you need for a very comfortable stay. Our room had a kitchenette area with microwave etc. Everything is spotlessly clean. The desk staff/ concierge were always happy to help out with information. They have the right balance of friendliness & efficiency. The hotel is located a little way out of central Manhattan but it’s SO easy to reach the wonderful chaos that is Times Square etc. using the bus or subway. Both are really close to the hotel. All in all it’s a great place to stay in NYC. Highly recommended.

“OK stay at a large and busy hotel.” We stayed here for a couple of nights at the beginning of our trip to the US. The hotel was full and very busy due to a Red Sox game and conferences. The hotel felt more than a little 'faceless'. We were checked in quickly and the staff were polite. Our room was very small with a large bathroom, but suffice for our stay. The room was very clean and comfortable. - We may return to this hotel if we are able to get a particularly good deal. The hotel is well located at the Prudential centre, but we needed to use the subway to get to the more central aeas. Prudential station is accessed through the attached shopping mall and is below the hotel, but it can only currently be used for travelling to uptown. On travelling back to the hotel, it is necessary to get off at Copley Square and walk the 10-15 minutes from there.(Beware of travelling to the hotel by subway if you have heavy bags as Prudential is on the green line and this consists of underground trolley buses. You have to lift your bags up three steep steps into the carriage.) There is a Starbucks outlet in the lobby and Starbucks coffee is provided for the coffee maker in the room. There is also a Cheesecake Factory restaurant located near to the access to Prudential station. - It is an easy walk to the Back Bay area and the Boston Ducks leave from near to the hotel.

“Great Hotel but There Are Better in This Price Range” This is a lovely hotel. The service is great, the rooms were clean, spacious and they graciously accommodated my request for a room overlooking the river. They Aveda amenities in the bathroom and lovely hacienda style decor. I would have been happy with this hotel if the price was a little lower. They are missing some of the amenities (like comfortable beds, soft towels and flat screen TVs) that come standard at other hotels in this range. I would recommend this hotel if you can get a good deal online.

“Mixed Review” My husband and I stayed overnight, as his company had it's annual party at the hotel. For a Boston hotel, I found the price to be very reasonable.
