The hotel was very pretty (still decorated for the holidays), clean, and our room was a very nice size, clean, well appointed. The bed was comfortable. Robes were included (love that!). And that's all the nice things I can say. Upon check in, the desk person was very pleasant and cheery, but she sounded very robotic in telling us about the hotel amenities. One thing that really makes me "like" a hotel I stay at, is the friendliness of the staff. I didn't find the staff friendly at all. The servers and bartenders at the party never smiled. One waitress was snippy with the people seated at the table when she brought out the wrong food. She "insisted" there were 3 salmons at the table, when no one ordered salmon. The look she gave us was that someone must have changed their mind and wanted the filet mignon. The following morning, hubby and I decided to try the brunch that the desk person at check-in raved about. Hubby *loves* going out for breakfast. The hostess didn't smile or welcome us. She asked us if we'd have the buffet or regular breakfast. We asked how much was the brunch buffet? Her response, "Um, I don't know---low 20's." She seated us, and our waiter wasn't very friendly either. And 2 waiters started to have an argument near our table. Although the food at the buffet looked nice, we opted to order just the omelettes (since it wasn't clear if omelettes were part of the buffet price). The breakfast was bland and tastless. The chef decided to make it healthy---no salt, no seasoning. The hotel has a "no tip" policy, but 18% is automatically added to the bill. Hubby hypothesized that the staff isn't motivated to be helpful and friendly since they won't get an extra tip. But this review isn't of the food--it's of the hotel. So, it has it's good points, and it's not-so-good points.

“Actually better than average...” I would call the hotel good, not average. The rooms are nicely appointed and very clean, as was all the public areas. I give this a "good" rating primarily for the size of the rooms vs. cost of stay. The rooms are pretty small on the average (I've stayed here about 5-6 times) with even the suites being on the small side. Excellent location and the service has always been attentive when I've been here.

“Good hotel and location for business travel” I stayed at this hotel while in Indianapolis for business and found it to be convenient, clean, and well-appointed. The hotel was close to both the airport and downtown Indianapolis, and the staff was very kind and helpful. The room was a standard Hyatt Place room, with separate work space, a mini-fridge, etc. I'd definitely return to this hotel the next time I'm in the area.

“I could live here” When staying in Jacksonville, we usually stay at the Omni downtown. Unfortunately, there isn’t much to do downtown and the Jacksonville Landing is practically a ghost town so we decided to stay in an area where we knew there were plenty of restaurants and shopping and the Homewood Suites fit the bill. Our stay at the Homewood Suites was really exceptional. The rooms are large and comfortable and have a full kitchenette. Check-in was a breeze and the staff were friendly and helpful. Ideal for a long-term stay.

“Definitely not for everyone!” I stayed here for one night, 2/9/07, and was very pleasantly surprised. I arrived at 6:30 on a Friday night and the place was buzzing. That may turn a lot of people off, but on a Friday night during Fashion Week, I'd be disappointed if it wasn't. The staff at check-in could not have been more pleasant. I am a Starwood Gold member, and maybe that's why they were so nice, but it was as smooth a process as I've ever had. I even received a call about 20 minutes after I got into my room to see if everything was okay. The concierge (Wherever, Whenever) tried to help change some hard-to-get dinner reservations without any luck, but at least he tried. My room was large and very comfortable, and the bathroom was, by NYC standards, a pretty good size. My only complaints were the shower cap that was never brought by housekeeping and the door men, who were not much help in at all. No one opened the car door on arrival and not one of them offered help in carrying my bag into the hotel. There were several gypsy town cars out front blocking cabs from picking up fares and I saw one of the drivers hand the doorman some money in exchange for this "service". When I left he following day, I had to hail my own taxi - the door men were nowhere to be found. The door staff at the Union Square W were much more professional and helpful. Also, the spa is okay, but not nearly as good as the original Bliss downtown. I had to wait almost 1/2 hour for my service because the client before me was late, and the desk staff said nothing - they just let me sit there the entire time offering me bottled water. They could have at least told me the cause of the delay. Oh, and the elevators are very, very slow and very very small.

“Fantastic” Beautiful, modern, large and comfortable room. Delicious meals in the restaurant. Helpful and accommodating staff. Quiet Wall Street location and comfortable bed allowed me the best sleep I have had in months. Slight quibble-check in took a bit too long, due to non working gadgets. Staff while friendly, were not prepared to print out a statement with room rate for me to sign. I'm fine with modern and all, but that is a basic logistic I do need to happen to ensure appropriate billing. Apart from that, lovely stay. I will come back again as soon as I can.

“Two Stays - Nice Place” We stayed here Thanksgiving weekend before going to Vail, and then again on our return. The hotel is first class in most every respect. We stayed on the club lever the first stay, and it was one of the best club lounges I've seen in a long time. Overall, staff were professional as expected. We were somewhat disappointed in the Thanksgiving buffet held upstairs in a ballroom. The food was standard fare, far, far from exceptional. Our table was wobbly and unstable. The entire room setting seemed like an afterthought with very little compassion or care; certainly not worth anywhere near the $75 cost. Dinner that night at Elways was much better. Overall a good hotel, but certainly didn't wow me like other Ritz Carltons have in the past. Considering the cost, it's doubtful I"ll stay here again.

“Great choice for West Houston” A new hotel, attached by walkway to the Memorial Mall (and hospital). Staff friendly & efficient, great rooms (our suite was spacious & very well equipped), and a small but good pool area on the 18th floor (quite windy and noisy). I only ate in the club lounge, so can't comment on the restaurant or bar, but they both looked good. I would stay here again if in the area.

“Don't bother” My issues: Thirty minute wait at the aiport for the hotel shuttle pick-up. Only one night stay. Business purposes. The smiles were friendly but the customer service was unacceptable. We arrived around 10 am (exhausted from the morning that began at 4am -- much too early for any sane person), the hotel was not busy but the hotel desk refused anyone the opportunity to check in until after 1pm. Really needed to get some shut eye due to a huge presentation just hours later. Others arrived...mostly business travelers...some pilots/flight attendants...it didn't matter. No check in until after 1pm. This would be understandable IF there were no rooms available but this wasn't the case. It seems that this was just a policy that couldn't be altered. Made no sense to sleep ole' me. Was anything OK? Sure,the staff smiled a lot. The exterior/interior were clean. The equipment in the Business Center was operable. There are a handful of eateries within walking distance (next door).

“Un po’ rumoroso, anche al 6° piano” Un po’ decentrato, ma la distanza dal centro è ampiamente compensata dal servizio gratuto del bus navetta per due zone di Boston servite dalla Metropolitana e per l'aeroporto Logan. Mentre la colazioneè molto buona, non altrettanto si può dire del locale che la ospita che è sottodimensionato per il gran numero di ospiti dell'albergo-IL sesto piano dell'hotel, dove si trovano le stanze migliori, viene riservato quando possibile ai clienti Best Western e la stanza dove abbiamo pernottato aveva due letti e due divani con tavolino in un altro ambiente separato. Gratuito anche il servizio della colazione in camera se soci BW. Particolarmente gentile la Manager Daniela DePina che ha risolto un problema che abbiamo avuto in città. Compreso nel prezzo il parcheggio ed il collegamento wi-fi. Unico neo potremmo trovarlo nella pulizia, ma forse l'inserviente, un pò avanti con gli anni, non stava molto bene.

“Brand new!” Beautifully designed hotel. Swarovski lobby chandelier, winding hall to living rm with fireplace and multi sitting areas with comfortable inviting vibe. Don't miss the complementary wine nightly. The room is beautifully furnished. Nice bar choices and cute rocky robe. Red owl tavern quaint and so is rooftop bar. Love this new boutique hotel overlooking independence park! Shout outs to bell staff... especially James and Shawn...really nice accommodating guys! It's the real deal here! Will be back!

“Great Location! Tons to do!” Hotel is located inTimes Square! It was great to be in the middle of all hustle and bustle on the streets while within minutes one can escape to a comfortable, good-sized, quiet, and clean room. Was in town for on vacation with my daughter, her friend, and my wife. They all loved the easy access to shopping. Also it was just a short walk to reach subway stations to get anywhere in the city. Though the hotel eleveators are frequently mentioned as a source of pain at this hotel, I found them quite simple to use. Plug in your floor number and go the elevator designated. Right next to the hotel are the MTV Studios. My daughter and her friend had a great time watching the celebreties exit the building. Quite a crowd was there for the event but they loved it. Plenty of food options nearby - one night we opted for Junior's (good offering of food) and another we picked up a pizza at John's (just two blocks away). The ladies all attended Legally Blonde Two show and it was right across the street. Overall, a very positive experieince.

“Nice Hotel - Would Stay Again” We stayed here from 4-6 Jun 08. Only a couple blocks from the China Town/Gallery Place metro stop. The hotel is very nice. The staff accomodated us with an early check in and late check out. The conceirge was helpful in getting us a shuttle from the hotel to BWI. Cost was $49 1st person and $10 each additional. Shuttle was right on time. Hotel was $175 a night through priceline. Rooms were very clean and we had a view of the National Monument. Bathroom size was fine, it was the door that opened right on top of the toilet was my only complaint. Internet was available in room and down in business area. Located about 6 blocks from the National Mall. A couple nice restaurants right down the street. Spy Museum a couple blocks away. I would definitely stay here again, as it was a great location to get around to all the sights.

“It's aall about the location!” I stayed here for 4 days in June for some pre tour sightseeing.MY freinds had a arrived a day before and got a smoking room which is odd as they are non smokers and their room stank of cigerette smoke.Thankfully I had a non smoking room.The room was extremely large and more than enough room for luggage etc The bathroom was very very small but the showerhead was amazing!We chose this hotel due to it's location.Midtown is the perfect place to stay for NY sightseeing.The subway is close by and it is an easy walk to times square.Overall this is not a posh hotel by any stretch but it is clean and close to everything.

“Clean, good but not great location” The location seems great on the map as it's next to the Convention Center but the immediate area is not so nice (Chinatown) and there was a loud argument that took place outside my window at 3 A.M. The staff is friendly and the hotel is clean. Except for the ambient noise, it's a great place to stay. I booked this hotel via Hotwire and got it for under $100 a night which was a great deal for the conference period.

“Great overall” I stayed just one night as part of a work trip. No complaints. The rooms and public areas alike are clean and well appointed. I was given a room on the 20th floor and was shocked by how good the view was. As a Bay Area local I've only seen San Jose/Silicon Valley from the ground, where it like a somewhat run-down, endless strip-mall. The price was great as well.

“Nice Hotel - Great location” I have stayed at this hotel on a few occasions and twice in December 2009. This hotel is just great. Located close to the gas lamp district (about a 10 minute walk) and many rooms have a great view of the bay. The hotel has a grand lobby and 2 towers. The front staff are very nice and helpful. The check in and out process was a breeze and very easy. The rooms are very clean and adequate. A bit outdated though and no LCD TV but still more than comfortable. There is self park and valet parking. The self parking was at $22/day. There is a beatiful pool outside, chairs and games. The gym is alos great. I would certainly stay at this hotel again.

“Home Away From Home” We stay at the Cow Hollow at least once a month and it is our home away from home! The rooms are always fresh & clean, and it is in a fantastic location ~ the heart of the Marina District! Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great value and location.

“Great Location and Great Service” I have stayed at this property several times and always have a excellent experience. The rooms are big clean and comfortable. The food is fantastic room service, banquets and the restaurant! The staff is top notch a real pleasure to deal with!

“A good sound hotel in Washington” We stayed at this hotel at the start of our American road-trip. An easy walk into town and parking provided made this a good location. Friendly check-in staff and prompt check-in with complimentary drinks for priority club members. Very clean and well equipped rooms made this a comfortable stay.

“Room was large but grubby.” We stayed at the Roger Smith last fall in a large suite. The bedroom was nice and there was also a tiny 2nd bedroom with a twin bed that was fine. Our complaint was that the living room was made up of mismatched pieces of leftover furniture and the overall effect was that it was grubby. We have stayed in the city 4 times since then, but won't go back to the Roger Smith. I have found the Rihga Royal to be consistently better.

“Nice common spaces, subpar rooms” I booked my mother and grandmother here when they came for a visit. (small NY apts = hosting out of town guests in hotels) I had them a few blocks away at the Hotel Giraffe for most of the trip, but had to move them to here for the final few nights because the other place didn't have a room available the entire time. The location of the hotel is pretty good - not in the middle of tourism chaos, but easily accessible to it, and close to the 6 and N/R subway lines. There are a few good restaurants in the neighborhood. The in-house restaurant (Country) is good for dinners and the bar has some fantastic house cocktails. However, when I took my family to brunch at the restaurant, we were thoroughly underwhelmed. The lobby and the restaurants are very impressively decorated, and I had high hopes for the rooms. Unfortunately, the room was quite disappointing. It was nicely furnished, but small and dim, even by NY standards, with a small window and very little natural light. The way the room was laid out, the bathroom was by the end of the room closest to the windows - the bathroom had a very small window with some natural light, but this layout meant that one of the beds was only three feet away from the door between the room and the hallway. In addition, the room was so small that it did not even have a closet or place to store suitcases - it had only an armoire with a bit of hanging space (not long enough to accommodate a dress or overcoat). After two nights, my family started to feel very claustrophobic in the room. The service was decent - efficient and businesslike. I dealt with the front desk for check-in and check-out and thought it was fine. My mother and grandmother (who are from a small town) thought the people they dealt with were a bit cold and impersonal. Bottom line - if you're not planning to spend much time in your room, and if you plan to meet people in the lobby or the restaurants, this hotel should suit you. If you plan to spend much time in your room, stay away. I don't plan to book out-of-town guests here again.

“Typical Meeting Hotel But Great Location” This is a typical business hotel in a big city but the location is fabulous! Room was very comfortable and clean. Despite being sold out, the elevators were quick so waiting was minimal. No problems getting a taxi. The hotel connected to the River Walk mall so I could buzz over to Macy's for a little shopping inbetween meetings or Starbucks for a quick latte. The Alamo was maybe a 15 min walk thru the mall and across the street from the Dillard's exit. Efficient, clean with great restaurants and attractions within walking distance. Don't I wish all business hotels were like this one!

“Good Experience” The bellmen were friendly and helpful, but it is odd to have a taxi drop you off to the entrance to the hotel, then be surprised by having to take an elevator to the 6th floor lobby. The lobby was small, although hotel front desk staff were efficient. Elevators (only 2) were slow. Hotel room itself was pleasant. Large TVs in both rooms, functional kitchen with refrigerator and dishwasher too. The daily breakfast was good, but ran out of fruit and there were few healthy choices. Coffee and tea were never hot, only lukewarm. Plenty of tables to choose to eat, but beware if the hotel is full then so is the breakfast room. Small pool on top floor and a small exercise room. Location is probably the best part of this hotel. A few blocks north of the river and a few blocks west of Michigan's Miracle Mile. Huge number and type of restaurants within a few blocks. Overall, a good experience, but not "very good".

“No Umbrellas!” The other reviews here are all correct - this is a nicely located hotel with overall friendly staff. Decor is ok. Check-in and check-out were both quick and easy. The included breakfast buffet is really weak, but Ann Sathers across the street is amazing so no need to eat at the hotel anyway. We stayed three days/nights, including the single rainiest day in Chicago's history. I took it for granted that a hotel that bills itself as an "elegant boutique hotel" would have umbrellas for guests to use. Our bill averaged over $300/night with taxes - for that money I would definitely expect some umbrellas sitting near the main door or in the room. Nope. Not a single one. I had to run down the street in the pouring rain with my 11-month-old to get a cheap one at a local store. And here is my other hotel-related rain complaint. The ramp that comes into the hotel is fully visible to the front desk staff. It's curvy and takes a little while to navigate with a stroller or the luggage cart. There were numerous times when I was trying to navigate a stroller with one hand while carrying an umbrella with the other hand. Approaching the lobby door, the 2-3 otherwise unoccupied people at the front desk would be watching this. Never once did one of them come around to help with the door. It wasn't just me - they never helped with the door with anyone else either - old people, people loaded down with luggage, etc.... NOT what I would expect for $300+ a night. So would I stay here again? Maybe, based on location. Definitely not, based on overall service for the price you pay.

“Great Place” If you have a chance to visit San Diego make sure to stop at the Omni in the Gaslight District. The views from my room was wonderful. I really appreciated the cleanliness of the room and the ability to check-in early. Imagine my surprise when later that evening a knock came to my door asking about turn down service. The hostess left a bucket of ice, bottle of water and reminded me to make my breakfast request. The staff was marvelous. I needed to ship a box back to my office and the Bellman took a FEDEX box and turned it inside out in order that I could use the box. The next morning my flight was at the crack of dawn and the door man waited outside with me until my ride came. The one great thing I also appreciated was the attitude of providing service. When I go to San Diego I will stay at the Omni.

“Decently Reliable” Me and my friends travel to NYC several times a year, and the Millennium is one of the "regular" properties at which we stay. Overall, it's a solid choice in a great location. Honestly, I prefer the beds in the main hotel over those in the Tower, and the lobby bar is a bit expensive (even for NYC), but overall you can't be the location, price, and amenities offered by the Millennium. The rooms are clean, decent size, and the staff is usually friendly and helpful.

“LOVED this place, would definitely recommend.” This place was lovely! The decor was beautiful with a fun nautical theme without being too tacky. All the staff were very helpful and seemed to have a great attitude. The room was clean and in good condition, my only (minor) gripe was that there wasn't a fan in the bathroom and it got a bit steamy. They have free Wifi if you join the Kimpton members club (free, you just need to fill in an online form) and each day they had free hot chocolate hour and free wine hour in the afternoons, a great start to our nights out. Great location in Fisherman's wharf near plenty of tourist attractions and three different types of public transport within about 2 blocks of the hotel (including cable cars). Would definitely recommend to anyone!

“great experience” what a great hotel, excellent location at the wharf and 1 block from ghiradelli sq, right at the cable cars. Despite the busy location, our room was very quiet and had ample room for 2 adults and 2 teens. The staff could not have been any nicer or more helpful, great decor and very clean, we enjoyed the evening wine reception. Highly recommended

“A reasonable option in Boston” An older building, nicely restored, with plenty of character. The staff at the hotel was very pleasant. Our room was spacious and pleasant. Unfortunately, it was a low floor overlooking Exeter Street. This was a problem at night as there is a club next door which seems to attract some significant street noise around midnight. As with all downtown Boston hotels, parking is expensive.

“Wish I could always stay at this hotel when in Chicago” This hotel is not covered by my company's travel policy -- so the only time I get to stay there is when traveling for vacation. It's a really great hotel. Wonderful views, great decor, cool bathroom, and very good staff. It's such a great room that you want to spend time in it! Only had drinks at the bar so can't comment on the food. Didn't try the spa because I'm really love the spas at the Peninsula and Elysian hotels.

“A charming spot.” The bf and I stayed at the Hotel Indigo from December 30th until January 2nd and were very content here. The building retains its original charm and the staff was very attentive and friendly. The original terrazzo floors are in the hallway as well as the glass from the previous offices. The wood floors are very nice too. No nasty carpet to deal with. The rooms are left in the original size of the previous offices so you can end up with an oddly shaped room. We had a room on the 6th floor and it was spotless. We overlooked the Alamo and Christmas tree in the plaza. It was lovely. The bathroom was very clean and there are Aveda bath products. The A/C unit is a bit noisy but not unbearable and we just turned up the radio which had a jack for my IPAD. No biggie. The beds are very comfortable with crisp white linens. My only complaint is the pillows are super large and super hard foam that does not give. We ended up with a sore neck a couple of nights. My bf actually used the pillow on the chair because it was more comfortable. The hallways can be a teensy bit loud when full of drunken revelers so be warned. The valet was prompt and courteous. To the people complaining about the fees, have you ever valet parked in a major city before? The fees are normal. If that is your only complaint, please be quiet. All in all, it was a great stay. Thanks for helping us start our new year on a great note!

“Great clean and well-located hotel - great value!” I am giving this 4 stars mainly because it exceeded expectations for what I paid. It's more if a 3-star hotel - with excellent value. I believe I paid $100 including taxes due to a special they were having. First of all, this is walking distance from the tram from the airport which was $1.60. They allowed me early check-in at noon so I could drop my stuff off and go the the Orioles game with my cousin at 1:30. There is only one person at the front desk, so a small line each time I got there, but they were fast and attentive. You are close enough to see the harbor from the hotel - and I would say as a single female I felt safe walking around by myself, though it was mostly during the day I was outside. The room was large with a comfy king bed. Coffee / tea facilities, microwave and fridge all available in room. My room was not the best located - 210 - second floor facing a side alley and brick wall about 10 feet away - but like I said - I paid $100 which I think was the cheapest hotel around for this weekend. It didn't bother me. Lastly I will say there is free breakfast, located in the Cloud room on the top floor. Great views of Baltimore's Inner Harbor. The food was great - selection of breakfast meats, eggs, omelet, homemade waffles, juices, coffee, yogurt, bagels, donuts, etc. I would say in a restaurant this would cost $20 easy incl tip. So i absolutely got a bargain. To top it off they allowed me a late checkout at 1:30 so I could take a tour of Camden Yards without rushing. I will definitely stay again if I return to Baltimore, unless the Renaissance has a fire sale, which of course will never happen :). There is also a shuttle to John Hopkins for those who are there for medical treatment. Luckily I was not in need, but it's worth a mention for those who might need it. Oh - and you have access to 2 computers in the lobby with a printer - this helped with boarding passes!

“Great Luxury Value - Downtown Houston” Hotel is right downtown, so for anyone having business there it is a great location. Overall, pretty good location. However, one of my colleagues was robbed in a neighboring parking lot, so be aware of your surroundings if you park in the area.

“The Dead Bunch of Roses in Vase at Front Desk Should Have Been 1st Clue” As a first time visitor to Seattle, I was disappointed to realize that this hotel isn't in downtown but rather the college part of town (my fault - should have read the reviews more closely). Despite poor location, this hotel has done nothing to endear myself to this city. I am eagerly awaiting checkout time. This place is quite gross! The dead roses really should have been the signal to find accommodations elsewhere but I gave them the benefit of the doubt. Bad decision..... Getting off the freeway, the hotel looms tall, old and tired (it was probably nice in the 80's). The lobby, though very dark, gives one hope that the rooms will be equally as decent. Not even close. This is a rundown facility in need of major renovation. A flat screen TV does not make the place modern and upgraded. The carpets in the hallway and room are filthy. The room and bathroom are small. There was interesting patchwork done to the wallpaper in the bathroom. The bathroom ceiling and windowsill have lovely peeling paint. The towels are one step above threadbare. The smell is odd throughout. Quite musty. On the pro side: the bed is comfortable and sheets are soft. Just don't look too closely at the cloth headboard...anyone who is a bit of a clean freak and has a vivid imagination may lose some sleep wondering about what the stains are. If you have any electronic devices, good luck charging them. It takes an enormous talent and creativity. There are two outlets (lower than knee level) on either side of the room. They are so old that the chargers constantly fall out. Try the outlet in the bathroom - it is slightly better. One would think that there might be an outlet near the desk - not the case here. They boast free wifi. Service and reliability are spotty. You get what you pay for, right? Skip the "restaurant" in the basement if your frat/sorority days are well behind you. The food is awful and oddly attempting to be fancy in a place that looks like its your parent's old, musty basement. It falls quite short. The ensuing stomach pains throughout the night weren't fun. The staff is great. Super nice kids running the place - hotel and restaurant.

“Perfect location; nice lobby; great price” Stayed here for two nights for $63 per night - parking was $45 per night, plus taxes...but still great room rate. Lobby and bar is really nice with friendly staff. Check in with FourSquare and you get a free cocktail! Our room was a corner room and fine, except I usually prefer central air, and our room was a window unit...with window units, I'm always worried about mold/cleanliness issues since I have a child with asthma. The bathroom was small, but towels were nice and everything was very clean. Terrace is really a great thing. Location is amazingly convenient. At this room rate, I will definitely be my first choice for where to stay in Chicago on future trips.

“Top notch hotel in a convenient part of the city” Everything was terrific at the hotel, and for a business trip, they provided all the needed services and more. We ended up renting one of the meeting rooms on the third floor, and they took care of all our needs. My only regret was not taking advantage of the 24-hour gym.

“A bit of a letdown, but I would give it another try” SO, I should start out by saying that I stayed at the hotel immediately next door to this several years ago, and I found myself spending my evenings in the Hard Rock bar wishing that I was staying at this place. I had stayed in the Hard Rock Tampa before and had adored the experience so I had a lot of high hopes for this trip. While the rooms were well furnished, I found the general decor to be very dark and did not make me feel welcome in my room. Also, the chair, while cool in design was abysmal in function. Some the things in the snack bar had been there for ages, firmly coated in dust. There were many good things about the hotel. The food was pretty good and given is sufficient quantity (though I would not recommend either the cinnamon vanilla french toast or the hashbrowns). The room service was quick and the staff was very friendly! The quality of bath products that were supplied was very good. The bed was fine and had plenty of pillows! The shower was spectacular and soothing with great acoustics for those who want to rock out while you are in the shower. The nicest part of the stay was the fact that they take you to the airport in a towncar for $15...slightly cheaper than a taxi and much more pleasant. So, I was not entirely disappointed with the hotel, it just was not the hotel I expected given my previous experience with Hard Rock Hotels.

“Buona posizione e buon rapporto qualità-prezzo” L'hotel è situato ad un isolato dalla michigan avenue,vicinissimo alla zona dei musei e alla famosa fontana Buckingham, così come alla fermata della linea metro, molto comoda per raggiungere le varie zone a nord della città.L'hotel è comunque abbastanza vicino(1.5km circa) al cuore pulsante della metropoli, e sotto l'hotel si trovano vari ristoranti di famose catene di fast food americani, così da lenire alla mancanza di un ristorante interno all'albergo che serva la colazione. Per il prezzo pagato (48euro a notte) non posso lamentarmi,la camera era semplice con una finestra vetusta ma non ho avuto problemi di alcun genere, sennò per l'invadenza delle camerirere al mattina che sembravano non leggere il cartello "non disturbare) nemmeno alle 8 di mattina. Il personale non conosce altre lingue al di fuori dell'inglese, il chè potrebbe essere un problema per chi a differenza di me non parla quella lingua come lingua madre, in quanto sono piuttosto distaccati e scocciati di fare anche un comune checkin per la camera.Lasciare la vlaigia in hotel per il giorno in cui si parte costa un dollaro, una caduta di stile far pagare un servizio ovvio e gratuito in quasi tutti gli hotel del mondo.In definitiva, soprattutto per via del prezzo e della posione consgilio questo hotel per visitare chicago rimanendo in un budget ridotto.

“We would stay here again” We stayed here with a park and fly rate and then returned here for a night after our trip. There was a sign in front that said newly renovated and that certainly appeared to be the case. Check in was efficient and cordial. The first night we had a standard king room. Vanity was inside the small bathroon and set at an angle. Not a lot of space on vanity top but the lighting was very good. The room appeared freshly painted and the light fixture in the bathroom was new. It was odd that after the old light fixture was removed, the new one was put up without painting where the old one had been. Left the area behind the light looking dirty and it would have been an easy fix. The coffee maker is on a small corner shelf inside the room. It was very easy to find room for our luggage in the decent sized room. Complimentary breakfast begins at 5:00 am which was great for early fliers. Cereal, sausage, scrambled eggs, waffles, etc. The shuttle, which we signed up for when we checked in, was right on time. We did have to stop at the nearby LaQuinta which had quite a number of passengers to load and we were full going to DIA. We only had a short wait to catch the shuttle to return to the Quality Inn.We checked in around 10:30 pm for our 2nd night and were upgraded to a king mini suite. There was a fridge, microwave and coffee maker on a counter in one corner as well as a couch and chairs sitting area. The vanity was outside the bathroom and had lots of room on top. It was in large enough area that our suitcases also fit in there. Although the vanity area had plenty of light, the bathroom light was very limited and dim. Due to the arrangement of the room, the flat screen TV was to the side of the bed and not the most convenient bedtime viewing.The air conditioner worked great and it was a comfortable bed and sleep.The fitness room needs to add an elliptical. One of the best things had to be the efficient shuttle system with the pleasant drivers. We would be fine with staying here again.

“Another great Westin in Chicago” Great location on Michigan Avenue. Walking distance to all the best restaurants, bars and stores. Across from the John Hancock Building and a block from Water Tower and close to State, Rush and all the fun streets. The rooms were large, quiet and well appointed. The hotel staff was fabulous.

“In a Class of Its Own” Having stayed at various venues in Washington over the past few years, the Willard is in a class of its own. It has all the elegance of an old style (but refurbished) classic hotel with all the efficiency and comfort of a top of the line brand new property. I was particularly impressed that although the check in desk retained all the old key box pigeon holes behind the counter, the air handling system was one of the quietest and most efficient I have encountered recently. Although we had a spectacular conference rate I noticed that their online rate for the weekend we checked out was particularly competitive and attractive. Would I pay the rack rate of $400 to $500 per room per night? Probably not. Will I check for last minute online deals the next time I am Washington? You bet. This is one of the few hotels I've stayed in recently that was, in itself a tourist attraction. You do have to put up with folks wandering through the lobby and common areas taking pictures. But there are amazing real bouquets in the lobby that are worth your time to admire and a splendid harp-accompanied high tea each afternoon. Glad we were there and will look for an opportunity to return.

“Historic Property = Teensy Rooms” We were wow-ed as we entered the lobby...we were thrilled to step around the corner and be right at the center of the 6th Street action, perfect location. We were not so wow-ed when we entered our room and barely had room for our bags or ourselves. I understand historic properties, but come on. It might be time to consider a renovation where some walls are torn down to make larger rooms or suites. We literally had to crawl across the bed to get anywhere. The bathroom was a better size. View was nice, price was not for the size of the room. Staff was friendly enough. But hey, you don't come to Austin to sit in the room....this being the case, I would choose something less expensive next time, except that there isn't much in the true 6th street vicinity, you start getting several blocks away, which in the Texas heat, can seem like miles on foot.

“Good for laborers, not so hot for business or tourists” Another experience with a hotel that treats Hotwire and Priceline customers as second class. Hoped for an east facing non-smoking room. Got the west facing (and hotter than hell) smoking room. Asked about being switched the next day, "Sorry - we're booked." How come I was able to call the 800 number to their reservations and able to book a non-smoking room? Built as cheaply as possible, and the cheap products are showing signs of the wear and tear. Matted stained carpeting, warped/bubling countertops in the kitchenette. The flatware provided was DIRTY! What can you expect - they provide no dishwashing detergent. The flatware looked like the previous guest licked it all clean. I went to the nearby grocery store and bought plasticware. On two previous stays, I was billed $39 to my credit card I gave the desk for "incidentals". They were quick to take those charges off my credit card, but they never should have been made in the first place. The blanket and spread on the bed all had many burn holes (presumably from cigarettes since it was a smoking room.) I bid $39 and got this place. I think it's worth the $25 more to have solid control over the hotel choice. I'd rather pay $65 to to West Fort Worth La Quinta, and at least have a Denny's right at the hotel. This place is in SERIOUS need of a thorough DEEP cleaning, and structural refurbishment. Wireless internet is cheap - only $4.99 per STAY (not per day). But, it was completely useless my first nigt at the hotel, everything timed out - couldn't check personal email, work email - nothing. The desk clerk knows nothing of the system, and refers calls to the service's 800 number - which is answered in India of course. Almost an hour on the phone with those guys yielded no results. That's an hour out of my life I'll never get back.

“Long overdue...” As i have said in past reviews i am in NYC alot ...why i have waited so long to write this review is beyond me.... The St Regis is in an awesome location...right in the middle of everything...and shopping galore...so if you are bringing your significant other be prepared to walk and shop... good this is that after a day of shopping you can utilize the Spa at the Hotel and experience pure bliss :) hotel has an European old world charm and oppulance to it... if you are a regular chances are the curb staff will remember you by name as well as the frt desk staff... they profile you so they will know excatly what type of room you like as well as what type of fruits to use in your welcome basket... the staff are extremely friendly and accomodatng and very discreet by nature...the hotel bar has a great late nite vibe to it with people watching potential everyday... The St regis is the standard suite...it is small but very cozy...the bathrooms are large with a super soaker shower and marble everywhere... the concierge's are always on thier A Game...and if you have any problems at all upper Mgmt never has an issue with getting involved and resolving any issues you may have... in NYC the St Regis is absolutely one of the best properties for you to visit and one of the best SPG properties in NYC by far....

“Not Bad” This was the beginning of a two-week trip throughout WA / OR, and wasn't too bad for starters. Our rooms were basic and clean, just what we were hoping for. The location was quite good, with the space needle an easy ten minute walk, and many restaurants of several ethnicities within one square block. Check in was easy and the staff was very helpful. The Mediterranean has a great view from the rooftop deck, which is where we had breakfast one morning and enjoyed the views of the Sound. However, if you're sensitive to ambient noise this isn't the place for you. The walls are a bit thin, but worse is there is no air conditioning, making it necessary to open windows for ventilation, allowing city noise to fill the room. On top of that we had an apparently heavily drugged - or drunk - homeless person sleeping on the street across from our side of the building, yelling obscenities throughout the night. I know for a fact I was not the only person to go to the desk and complain about it, but he was still there in the morning. In their defense, the hotel staff checked their records and said that someone from the desk called the police, but nonetheless he was still there in the morning. As a basic, relatively inexpensive city hotel this is an adequate facility. I personally enjoyed the neighborhood (for the most part), but it's not everyone's cup of tea.

“You can depend on this one” Stayed here for a weekend conference at the other airport Hyatt and took the shuttle back and forth. I am glad i did. As a very frequent traveler I can say this is an excellent hotel. Very clean, well-designed, comfortable rooms, quiet (very important at an airport hotel), professional and courteous staff, good food, excellent fitness center/pool area on top floor. As a Hyatt Platinum Passport member, I was upgraded to a larger room and was very pleased with the stay. If you have to stay at DFW, I recommend the Grand Hyatt!

“Nothing special...pretty standard” Stayed at the Harbor Island Hilton for one night on business. It's rather small for a Hilton but the rooms were quite big (was more like a suite with a separate living room/bar area and then the bed room (had 2 bathrooms as well). The location was great...literally a 5 minute drive from the airport so it was the ideal location for our conference. However it is RIGHT on the water so good to take a quick stroll. The hotel is only a 5 minute drive from downtown San Diego, so easily accessible. The restaurant was pretty average as far as hotel restaurants go (only ate brakfast there) and the bar/lounge was a little on the small side. Overall grade - standard Hilton hotel.

“We highly rate this hotel.” This is a very pleasant hotel in an excellent location. The staff could not have been more helpful. Good breakfast. Drawbacks: Self parking is across the street but not too bad. Follow instructions to the letter or you'll drive around the block twice like we did. Charge for parking with a Hilton goldcard - $14.00 a night, more without the card. Internet in room free with Hilton card, otherwise $15 a day ( I think). The Irish Pub under the hotel has an excellent fiesty pianist/entertainer. Good atmosphere even on the slow night when we were there. Word of warning: lots of cigarette smoke which will affect you if you suffer that way. Overall a very good hotel and would recommend with no problem.

“BUSINESS TRAVEL” Stayed at JWM Indianapolis for business meeting. Nice room overlooking city on high floor. King rooms have walk- in showers with multiple shower heads in wall. Breakfast buffet very good and not overly pricey. Also ate at High Velocity Sports Bar....good food, too. Will stay again on future visits to Indy.

“Great breakfast and friendly, helpful staff!” My daughter had spent a night at this hotel in May when she came for a job interview and loved the property. So when we moved her to DC for her new job, we stayed here for three nights. The staff are all amazing - they go out of their way to help. And the breakfast isn't just cold cereal and danish - full hot and cold breakfast. Amazing! We used the business center and my teenage son used the work out room. We were within just a few minutes walk to everything, including the metro. And there are all kinds of restaurants nearby. The room was very comfortable for three adults. I will definitely consider staying here again when I return to DC for a visit.

“Lovely but small” The location of this hotel is brilliant and the man on the front desk was really friendly which was nice after travelling for ages. My girlfriend and I stayed here on the 30th december and it was quite cheap compared to other places on this night. The room was clean but absolutely tiny, it literally fit a small double bed and that was it, the bed was tiny, im 6ft1 and my legs were hanging well over the end, the other downfall was that the room was freezing! it had a heater in it but i didnt do much so we spent most of the night awake and shivering. Overall this hotel was convenient, clean and reasonably priced. We were booked for one night and I would say that if you are on your own this room is fine but if there are 2 of you then 1 night is enough, its too small but I would stay there again

“Whatever/Whenever....maybe/maybe not” This is the original W Hotel, but this is certainly not the best. The first room I was given was in a nook...literally. It was in a tiny side hallway behind the ice maker. I could touch 3 of the for walls while sitting in the bed. The front desk staff attendant mentioned that it was one of the 'cozier' rooms. I asked to switch rooms and the request was accommodated. I just wondered why the hotel would even put a guest in a prison cell sized room. The Acura service is a joke. The acura desk attendant continued to text and take a personal call on his cell phone rather than help me. Once he finally wrapped up his personal business, he said, "what do you want?" No eye contact. No greeting. Just "what do you want?" What I really 'wanted' at that point was to tell him to go to "non-heaven." The Acura service only goes about 20 blocks from the hotel. Basically, it goes where you can walk. The restaurant has pretty good food but the service is hit or miss. One day, i had to go to the hostess for everything I needed because my waiter was M.I.A. There are plenty of delicatessens in the area if you don't want to eat in the restaurant. The front desk staff is great. I think they have the toughest job at this hotel. No matter the time of day, there was always a line waiting to check in or check out. And the hotel is amazingly clean. The housekeeping staff does a great job. Because of the location, it's noisy. The street noise is almost unbearable at night. Police sirens, taxi horns, sanitation trucks can all be heard all day and night. I could easily see how one guest could have a great experience and another guest could have a terrible experience. The service and amenities are not consistent from person to person, from room to room and from day to day. If the W experience is important to you, don't stay here. Unless, this W is offering deeply discounted rates, stay at the W Times Square.

“great location, neat space” I booked the Hotel Nikko on Expedia and got a great deal. Although the room was very small, it was perfect for one. The bed was comfortable, the water pressure strong, the room neat and clean and I had a very good night's sleep. I loved the decor in the public areas and the Japanese feel of the hotel. Public transportation was easy with the Powell Street MUNI stop only 5 minutes away. I would definitely stay there again!

“Five star treatment at a two star price” We booked this hotel for a long weekend and a family visit in DC. We love the Dupont Circle neighborhood, along with Columbia Heights, Adams Morgan, Federal Triangle, and Georgetown, all within a short distance of this property. I got a great rate on Expedia for this property, and I did some research as to why, and found out that the hotel was under renovation. We pulled up and a security guard instructed us to self-park in the garage and then check-in (valet parking is available). We parked on the second floor of the garage and had a short walk to the elevator. We ascended into a galmourous lobby with numerous friendly employees waiting to greet and assist us. Check-in was a breeze (we arrived right at check-in time) and were given a "city view" room on the 5th floor. We had a bit of a walk from the elevator, but we had a nice plush carpet to traverse. The room was mostly renovated and seemed to have "new car smell." The bathroom had Kohler fixtures and there was a crystal-clear HDtv at the foot of the comfortable queen bed. The main drawbacks to the room were the visible water damage to the ceiling that had yet to be completely repaired and the noise-level from the air conditioner at times. Additionally, the room was not completely sound proof, as I could hear conversations from adjoining rooms depending on where I was. The shower temperature was a bit diffcult to control as well. Otherwise, our stay was without incident and the hotel was quite friendly. The staff provided flavored water for the guests at the main entrance and a very friendly bellman helped us with our luggage at check-out. Once nice feature about check-out was the ability to do auto-checkout via the television by 11AM, but have your key still active until noon in order to give you plenty of time to get your things organized.

“A couple oddities, but overall great!” Although the Sofitel near Times Square has a couple odd quirks that keep it from gaining a 5-star rating, my daughter and I thoroughly enjoyed it on a recent visit and would gladly stay there again. Among the MANY positives of this hotel: -Wonderfully comfortable beds -Plush bath robes and great, thick towels -Very quiet atmosphere -Complimentary computers in the lobby to check e-mail -WONDERFUL bathroom with separate tub and shower -Great amenties and complimentary Evian water -Great location about 4 blocks from Times Square and 5 blocks from Rockefeller Plaza -In-room safes that are easy to operate -Great air conditioners that truly cool the room (a rarity in NYC, where most don't cool properly) -Friendly staff and housekeeping With all these positives, you might think this the perfect NYC hotel, but then a few little missteps make you scratch your head and wonder what they were thinking: -NO COFFEE OR COFFEEMAKERS IN ROOMS!! An astoundingly strange oversight. -Evening turndown service, but no chocolates or mints on the beds. Picky, but for $350 a night,....? -Bathroom doors DO NOT have locks! This invites the uncomfortable possibilities of a couple "oops" moments on your vacation. -$350 a night seems about $50-$75 a night to steep for this quality of a hotel. -They took a $900 deposit on my credit card for incidentals, even though I had a PRE-PAID room!!!! Did they think I was going to eat the entire mini-bar,....twice?!?! This is a great hotel and worthy of staying at on your next trip. However, they've certainly left some t's not crossed and i's not dotted in their lack of attention to detail. With that said, however, very clean, very quiet and very nice.

“Very nice” Very nice hotel with excellent service. Stayed here twice for business in the last couple of months, and each time was quite good. Had a couple of service requests, such as broken remote or blown light bulb. Service was at my door before I hung up the phone. Beds comfortable, and restaurant is just excellent with great food, and wonderful service. We ate almost all of our dinners at the hotel after exposure to the touristy dumps on the River Walk. Internet nice and speedy. Would definitely stay there again.

“Very good” We are 4 English couples and stayed here for 3 nights for our sons wedding on 4th July. I cannot praise this hotel too high, we were charged $89 a night including breakfast - the rooms were spacious, clean and very, very comfortable. The prices for the drinks and food were good and the service was very friendly, the pizzas as a snack at lunchtime were very good. The location is not ideal for the centre of Columbus (but it was for our family wedding) and it is right next to the Interstate highway with a very good shopping center within 2 minutes walk. It is unlikely we will need to stay in this area again but if we did this hotel would be our first choice without doubt.

“Good but not inspiring” The location is good for access to Hollywood and the Valley. Great location if Uni studios is your destination. It's nice having the restaurants at Citywalk within walking distance. The hotel is pretty whatever. Competent but not inspiring. The decor is very 1980's. Wallpaper looks old, Furniture works but there's no sense of style. Exec floors have many b-guys there with families and kids taking advantage of typical Hilton C-Level Carb breakfasts. This is my fallback hotel for LA if things go bad somewhere else. Showers work. Internet works. Parking is adequate.

“Funky & Fun Boutique Hotel!” We booked this hotel months in advance via Hotwire. We needed four rooms, and got them for $103 per night, for a pre-cruise stay. This hotel was listed as a 3 1/2 star boutique hotel, which I would say is exactly what we got. We arrived before 1pm from the East Coast, and were very happy that we had no problems checking in that early. All eight of us loved the Hotel Max! Yes, the rooms are small, especially the bathrooms, but it's great preparation for the cruise bathrooms. This hotel has character! From the guys standing out front, to the front desk, they're young and friendly. Artwork throughout the hotel is unique and sexy. The bed was comfortable, and we got a kick out of the extra amenities in the room. (not that we used them...perhaps, if we hadn't stayed up so late in the hotel restaurant for late-night happy hour :) ) This hotel reminded me of unique boutique hotels I've stayed at in San Francisco and New York. It is NOT for anyone wanting a cookie-cutter hotel experience. The location, by the way, is PERFECT. Less than a $10 cab-ride to Pier 66 and the boarding of our cruise. An easy walk to Pike's. It's very close to the Westin, and Il Fornaio (great Italian restaurant, if you're hungry for Italian). We actually went back to the Hotel Max after our cruise to take a few pictures, as we had failed to do so when we were actually staying there.

“Very Nice” Stayed here for three nights the end of September with a group of colleagues and clients. Everyone was happy! Rooms were nicely appointed and bathroom was large and well lit. Bed was very comfortable. Hosted wine hour was nice. Wine was only fair, but it was nice to mindle with other guests. On site restuarant, Sazerac, was good but service is VERY slow.

“A bit on the dumpy side” I've stayed at the Millenium Bostonian twice in the past couple of years through Priceline which advertises it as a 4 star. Priceline nowadays is an outlet for distressed hotel rooms so it should be no surprise that this hotel is a bit shabby. Why they insist on not replacing the carpet years after it has decayed and started to smell is beyond me. Also, there is a fair amount of noise that enters the rooms from pipes, toilets, etc. Otherwise the location is great and the staff accomodating.

“Your extended stay business travelor review” As with most the other reviews: excellent location. How does a hotel right on a trendy outdoor mall sound? Just about every mainstream dining chain is here. Pf Changs, Cheesecake factory, J Alexanders, more. Like the mall itself, this Homewood is new. With modern touches like flat screens, well appointed kitchens and rooms. This property is definitely worth putting on your list regardless of the duration of your stay. Highlights follow: Pros: 1. Outstanding location! Shopping and dining, this can't be beat. New and clean. 2. Very well appointed modern rooms. 2. Outstanding hosted breakfast and evening meals. This hotel has dedicated employees that are very friendly and helpful. In particular the breakfast host is very warm and thoughtful. Cons: 1. The "high speed" internet is the only tarnish here with this hotel. Most of the time it's as slow as dial up on both wireless and cabled. As a Networking Engineer I called their contracted tech support. They told me the hotel had 152 users accessing their service at once. The problem here is the pipeline the hotel has leased. It's simply not enough bandwidth for the amount of guests. An upgrade is badly needed.

“Clone this and put one in every city!!!” Great design. The rooms are not huge but employ thoughtful design to provide a kitchen, living area, bedroom and bathroom. The tv swivels between living area and bedroom. The kitchen is small but you could truly cook meals for a small party with no problems. Design is modern but does not try to be overly hip like an aloft hotel. Is modern but still comfortable. Breakfast in morning was better than average and staff was courteous. Good value for what you pay. Wish every city had one of these!!

“Have stayed at the Library Hotel and the Casablanca but would choose Chelsea Pines any day” We've been to NYC several times and stayed in a variety of hotels including some that have very good reviews on Trip Advisor. However, we had never stayed in the Village and this hotel appealed based on the reviews we'd read and the price. We were not disappointed. We booked a standard room, and asked for a high floor with a room at the back of the inn. We were given the Ann Margaret room, which was on the 4th floor overlooking the back garden. It was larger than we expected and had room for 2 armchairs in addition to the bed. There was also a built in wardrobe, safe, fridge, flat screen tv and i-pod docking station. There was also plenty of room to strore our empty suitcases (behind the armchairs). The bed was really comfy and the room was nice and quiet with no street noise (being at the back) and no noise from neighbouring rooms despite the inn being pretty full. Yes, it's a long climb up 4 flights of stairs, but it got easier as the week progressed and helped us work off the generous (free) breakfasts of muffins, bagels, pastries, fruit, cereal, cheese, yoghurt, juice, tea and coffee (no we didn't eat everything!). The extra touches include free wifi, 2 computers with internet access and printer (also free) and the excellent daily newsletter with suggestions of things to do. The inn is in a great location, less than half a block from the subway station which has the A,C,E and L lines, enabling you to travel north/south or cross town. There are plenty of good places to eat within walking distance, including the Chelsea Market, which is certainly worth a look. However, the absolute best thing about the inn is the staff and owners and in particular Jay and Al. Al is a real comedian and should have his own show. He was funny, interesting and above all helpful. We felt very at home and were made to feel really welcome. We were sorry when our week came to an end and will certainly stay here on our next trip to the city.

“Exceptional with some exceptions” We selected the Fairmont for our recent stay based on the TripAdvisor reviews and other information, although it was slightly further away from the convention center than other options offered. Bottomline -- we made the right decision and friends visiting from the other hotels (such as the Hilton and Marriott) wished they had booked into the Fairmont. The hotel offered many, many pluses. However, there are a few items that keep this hotel from achieving truly world class status. Lobby -- this is a big, active lobby. Dancing going on one night, other activities in other evenings. Nice option for the evening and quiet during the day if you want a spot to meet someone. Size -- when booking, note that this is a big hotel that books large groups. However, the rooms, location, and pool are very nice for smaller groups and families. Check in -- relatively fast. However, one of our two reservations was fouled up. We did not get exactly what was specified but the end result was close enough. Room -- Exceptional in general. The bathroom is among the best I have seen in the States -- separate WC, shower and tub areas. Bathrobes, great amenities, plenty of towels. Beds were very comfortable. TV was old, lacked premium channels and the remote sometimes did not work. I also had to climb under the desk to reach an AC outlet for my computer. We had to move other furniture to find outlets for cell phone chargers, etc. Separate dressing area by bathroom. Super nice touch -- valet stand in room. Both hardwire and wireless internet connections. Hardwired is faster. ADVICE -- join the Fairmont President's Club (free online) and internet access is free during your entire stay -- a savings of about $14 per day. Also, membership ensures a paper at your door every day. Pool -- very, very nice but lacked hot tub. Front desk and concierge staff -- mixed in customer service levels, ranging from indifferent to very helpful. BTW, only car service offered is through their on-site Virgin Limo, which required a 3 hour minimum at $81+/hour. Not a good option and no alternatives other than using a regular taxi or mass transit were offered by the concierge. Location -- two blocks to the convention center and very close to a number of very good meal options, as well as a great movie theatre for evening entertainment. Food -- ADVICE -- do not do the daily breakfast buffet. One of the most expensive and least satisfying selections I have ever encountered. Frozen bagels that were still frozen, eggs that were undercooked, no waffles or pancakes, no omlette station, and you may be charged extra if you want a fruit (such as a banana) that is not on the buffet. This was a big disappointment after hearing of the very nice breakfasts at this hotel. A much better option is to go across the plaza (about 20 steps from the side entrance of the hotel) to the wonderful pastry shop. Fresh pastries, decent bagels, freshly squeezed juices, excellent coffee and a very good value. Room Service -- pretty good. Seems to come from several of the restaurants in the area attached to the hotel. Price -- very good in comparison with the Marriott and Hilton. The St. Claire was another hotel that we considered (priced about the same and also with exceptional reviews). However, we selected the Fairmont based that we were traveling with teenagers who would appreciate the bathroom and pool at the Fairmont more than the charm and history of the St. Claire (which has a very good Italian restaurant). If we travel to San Jose again, we are likely to select this hotel again.

“Special!” Easy peasy check in, great staff, very friendly and efficient! Excellent rooms, very clean, heavenly bed was heavenly! Nice big bathroom, we must have had an oversized balcony! Great breakfast! Jesse was our waiter at breakfast every day and he was fantastic! Location is brilliant, this place was worth every penny! Thank you Westin Riverwalk!

“Fabulous hotel and location!” I am a frequent business traveler and stayed at the Fairmont Olympic 2 nights Feb 29 and Mar 1. The rooms were very big with a superbly comfortable bed. My view wasn't great, but I wasn't there for that (view of buildings across the way, no water from my room at least). The work desk was okay - not huge, but decent with one plug nearby. The room had an armchair with a little table as well, a minibar, coffee and such, a big closet with hooks and a small safe (in which I couldn't fit my big laptop). The bathroom was a big size with a separate room/door for shower and toilet. The toiletries were nice and there was a bathrobe, and a nice extra of two sets of slippers - that's very rare. Room service was quick and good - I had a turkey club with fries and all was hot/cold where supposed to be; it came delivered on a rolling table instead of a tray, which I always think is a nice touch. Everyone was extremely helpful - fast check-in, email my check-out folio, called a cab quickly, directed me on the walk to my business meeting, etc. Capitol Grille is right across the street for finer dining, and there seemed to be some places nearby for quicker and less expensive meals. All in all, I thought it was a great hotel and I'd definitely stay there again.

“Decent, for the price.” Stayed for 6 nights, and thought it was an ok hotel in a great location. To find good hotel deals in Chicago is not easy, I learned that even an ordinary hotel room can cost more than $400 a night, which I find absolutely insane. This hotel was the cheapest Marriott option in town. We paid around $250 per night, not too bad. Continental breakfast included. The room was nothing special. The interior was nothing to write home about, but the bed was comfortable (Marriott's beds are the best). The room was of standard size, but I guess small for american standards. Desk staff seemed very busy, and not particulary helpful. They seemed almost annoyed when asked a simple question. When we asked for an adapter they just gave us an adress where we could buy one. I think it is very strange that a hotel in a major city don't have adapters. Anyway, we loved the location, walking distance to many of the main attractions, including Navy Pier, and would recommend this property if you do not wish to pay the ridiculous prices some of the other hotels are charging.

“I loved everything at Sofitel LA, especially the amazing beds!” Really enjoyed my stay here! The most incredible, cloud-like beds. I've traveled a lot and these beds made such an impression, I slept so well which is rare in hotels for me. This hotel is very nice but has a few freebies thrown in so you are not ripped off at every turn. Like the free coffee every morning in the lobby. Nice touch. Or the free fruit in the gym. Or the free cold beverages throughout the day. All really nice little touches of convenience. The rooms are really nice. The beds, yes, amazing. Bathrooms top notch and the toiletries are L'Occitane, my absolute favorite. Even the towels at the gym are super soft Frette towels. The Fitness center is large and like a real gym, not an afterthought like at many hotels. I loved the robe, the slippers, everything about this place. The courteous staff, the good housekeeping, the nice doormen and valet. It was all amazing and I'd stay again! Location isn't bad, right across from the Beverly Center and my favorite, Loehmanns. Fairly central to LA as well so many neighborhoods are accessible. You can walk up to the many restaurants on Melrose like Lucques and Ago. Or check out The Roger Room on La Cienega for some good cocktails. There are also good cocktails to be had in The Stone Rose, their bar off the lobby. Just beware of peak times as it can fill up with wanna-bes with a shirt-button-too-many undone! Great hotel. My first stay in a Sofitel, and I can't wait to try others!

“Sofitel Is Hands Down Philly's Best” Great hotel--a standard room with doubles felt exceptionally large. Stunning bathroom with frameless glass shower doors. Very comfortable bedding, awesome Bose wave radio with Ipod jack, nice LG Flatscreen. I've stayed at the Ritz and Four Seasons in Philadelphia before and I think the Sofitel is more luxurious than both and in a better part of town. One small issue--it took 15-20 mins for my car to be retrieved from valet parking. So just be sure to call far enough in advance. All and all, I'd recommend the Sofitel to my out-of-town guests without hesitation.

“Great location and amazing breakfast at Urban Tavern” I stayed here for three nights recently while in town for a conference. I stayed in a city view suite in tower one, which had the most amazing view of the Golden Gate Bridge and Marin Headlands. The location is great. It's close to Union Square, but not right in the heart of it. Close proximity to Russian Hill, North Beach, and the 4th street Caltrain station (all within about a $10 cab ride, including tip.) The room was very spacious with a sofa, coffee table, desk, king-size bed, mini bar, and dresser and flat-screen TV. The bathroom was nicely-appointed and even had a scale in it. The double doors to the bathroom were a bit difficult to navigate in the middle of the night, but overall, a great room. The bed was quite comfortable and there was a decent little closet for the excessive amount of clothing I brought with me. My only complaint is about the internet service in the room. The hotel was experiencing problems with the connection, but the hotel was kind enough to waive the internet service fee for me on all three days. The best part about the stay was the breakfast buffet at Urban Tavern. The room I stayed in included an upgrade to the buffet for $10 per person and it was worth every penny! I'm so glad the front desk clerk encouraged me to upgrade. The breakfast includes everything imaginable from dim sum to smoked trout, a huge cheese platter with brie, amazing blue cheeses, etc and several fine cured meats. Scrambled eggs were light and fluffy, tons of fruit, and an amazing pastry display along with small shot glasses of concentrated vitamin C and baked yogurt (sounds weird, tastes wonderful.) I'd stay here again (especially if my company is footing the bill!)

“Gutes Hotel am Rande von Downtown, ein wenig abgewohnt” Das Hotel liegt etwa 15 Gehminuten von Downtown Memphis (Bealstreet). Es ist ein Full Service Marriott mit den ueblichen Marriott Zimmern. Besonderns hervorzuheben ist der Service, dass man bei Pizza Lieferdiensten in der Umgebung Pizza bestellen kann und diese direkt vom Hotelpersonal aufs Zimmer geliefert wird. Super Service! Die Zimmer sind schon ein wenig abgewohnt, allerdings nicht komplett runter geritten. Immer noch ok und sauber.

“ヨーロッパ調のホテル” ホテルは街の中心で、どこへ行くにも便利な立地です。少し坂を上ったところですが、サンフランシスコ自体が坂の街なので、特に気になりません。1階のレストランは有名なヨーロッパ風で、朝食もそこでとれます。宿泊についている朝食は冷たい物ですが、暖かい食事を追加でオーダーでき美味です。部屋は清潔でスペースも十分です。夕方にはワインのサービスもあり、宿泊客で賑わっています。コンベンションセンターへも歩いていける距離で、ビジネスにも便利です。

“Outdated Property needs work on guest rooms” Allegedly the hotel is embarking on a multi-million dollar campaign to upgrade and renovate the guest rooms. I sure hope so because it is surely needed. I stayed at the Roosevelt for business last month for 5 nights and the quality and cleanliness of the room left a lot to be desired. Peeling paint, stains on the carpet, outdated and tiny bathroom, and multiple light fixtures that were not working. All this for about $340 a night. Linens and towels were clean but I didn't even want to sit my suitcase on the floor or in the closet because of the look of the carpet, dust, and stray hair I saw. Hotel staff was generally unresponsive and acted like they could care less about the guest. Front desk agents in particular were curt and unaccomodating. On a positive note-- the workout room on the ground floor was large and spacious--- lots of weight and fitness machines and open 24 hours. The hotel is also just a block from Grand Central Station so catching a train or subway anywhere is quick and easy. This is a 3 star hotel at best. Nowhere near a 4.

“Fabulous Hotel” This hotel has been completely refurbished. The rooms are great - a mix of art deco and high tech (the photos on the web site don't do them justice) and the staff helpful and friendly. Convenient for the Met, Guggenheim etc and easy to get a taxi anywhere else. Thoroughly recommended.

“Great experience Here But SF Needs to Clean Up Area” I stayed for 6 nights at the Parc 55. Check in was relatively easy. I requested a top floor but got floor 15. Room was relatively large with views out two sides since it was on the end. Room was clean and staff was acceptably friendly. Be forewarned that they are constructing a large building next door so the noise starts pretty early. I use earplugs so it didn't bother me. Lots of homeless all around but it still seems safe as they were harmless. Just don't go very far to the immediate west from the hotel because that area is not safe. Very convenient to cable car and subway (BART). Major disappointment was not the hotel but the amount of homeless begging in a major tourist area. SF leadership really needs to clean up their act. Very little police presence noticed anywhere around the city and that was very disappointing. Saw more homeless begging on the 100 yard walk from the subway to the hotel than 2 days in NYC. Not the Parc 55's fault though. I think eventually this will come back to bite tourism there.

“Really good for a Hampton” I got upgraded to a suite. Had a good kitchenette, a balcony, decent size room. A great room for the price I got. The staff was very cordial as well, and it is in a good location. It was by a lot of places with outdoor music, so if you had a door or window open you could hear it quite loudly, but I couldnt hear it with those closed.

“Overpriced, stinky bathroom, rooms that are beyond tiny” Bottom line: wouldn't stay here again. i stayed here because i like the central location and the sofitel was incredibly expensive. this place was no bargain but $200 cheaper than the sofitel. Nice people - doormen, guy at front desk - but a pretty lackluster hotel. The rooms are beyond tiny. I was asked if I was going to be using a desk in my room because rooms that had queen size beds didn't have desks (don't fit). I was so i got a full size bed that was squeezed into a corner. the shower was less than 3' x 3' and the shower head sprayed out into the bathroom as you adjusted the water. The real ick of the experience was opening the door into the bathroom - the stench of mold/mildew/must was overpowering. If it wasn't so late in the day and I had already prepaid I would have switched hotels and paid more. Another traveler I met in the elevator said his room had the same issue with the stench. the smoke alarm also decided to start beeping at 3am (needed a new battery) and there was a houseekeeping cart seemingly permanently stationed on the floor, but not the biggest issues.

“bello” albergo in centro attacato al centro commerciale copley dall'interno dell'albergo si raggiunge il centro ed i suoi numerosi negozi. camere molto belle e confortevoli con vista sulla città se situate ai piani alte bella vista di sera soprattutto. Ci si muove facolmente per raggiungere ogni angolo della città. Buona la palestra anche.

“One of the Best Hotels” The Omni hotel is, quite simply, one of the best places I've ever stayed. From the time you arrive you are treated with tremendous service. There is no line to wait on when you arrive and no lengthy check-in process...simply tell the front desk your name and your key is waiting for you. Once in your room, a warm note awaits along with a bucket full of ice and two complimentary bottled waters. For Omni awards members (free to sign up), wi-fi is free, as are two complimetary beverages each morning (I chose a pot of coffee and an OJ). These two conveniences alone saved me over $50 over the course of my four days there. As mentioned at the outset, customer service could not be better. The staff is attentive to your every need. I booked tow tours through the concierge and both were great. As for location, the Omni is located downtown, about 4 blocks north or Market Street and about eight blocks from the Embarcadro. It is about two blocks from the TransAmerica Building. Needless to say, this is an excellent location to explore virtually any part of the city. Union Square is probably a slightly better location, but this is a close second. I will look to stay at the Omni every time I'm in SF in the future.

“Nice hotel but...” I tried this boutique hotel based on tripadvisor reviews. The location is great, only one short block to the subway stop (Lexington line 23rd stop). At $200 p.n. (inc tax), the room size was acceptable (Madison type). Decor is modern & simple. On the negative, no refrigerator in the room, and window air-conditioning which is a bit loud. I was on a lower floor so you could hear the traffic as windows are not double glaze. Only one of the two elevators was working so if you are on an upper floor, you have to wait a long time. The hotel provides complimentary pastries and coffee in the front lobby which is good but many of the guests hangout by the tables giving the feel like you are a fast food restaurant. I think there are plenty of new boutique hotels that have opened in NYC for around $200-250 p.n. (inc tax) so I will try another hotel for next time.

“Over-priced roadside hotel” Decent staff, few services, property getting a bit long in the tooth, and nothing attractive/special about the property (to the rear is a massive, sprawling, un-unsed parking lot, to the front is I-40). For a roadside stop driving cross-country it does the job. I noticed that this is where older Courtyard furniture seemed to land to live out its final useful days. However for nearly $100/night, find a Motel 6 - aside from a wanna-be breakfast and small indoor pool, there's not much difference. The value just wasn't there.

“Wonderful view, quiet room” Thank you, Priceline, thank you! Hotel Nikko is in an excellent location in Union Sq. just a few blocks from the Powell Muni station and near lots of shopping and restaurants. The spacious, white marble lobby sets the tone for this elegant hotel. Our spotless room on the 19th floor provided a wonderful sunset view and was very quiet. The room was relatively small and decor was minimal--there weren't any paintings on the wall, which seemed a bit odd at first. I appreciated the in-room safe, nice bath ammenities, and comfortable bed. The shower was also great. Only quibble was having to pay for wireless access at such a high-end hotel. Seems almost ironic so close to Silicon Valley. Hotel Nikko provided a great haven at the end of each busy day of exploring the city. I actually looked forward to going back there to sleep!

“Perfect Gem of a Hotel in the Heart of Dupont Circle” After a long drive from New York City in a stressful rainstorm, we checked into the Madera Hotel and, suddenly, all of our worries immediately went away. The hotel staff is extremely nice and they appeared to be genuinly happy to see us. Our room, on the 6th floor was spacious, clean and pleasantly decorated. Our room featured two wonderful double beds, each with 2 soft feather pillows, 2 large square pillows and one funky zebra-print pillow. There was a regular-sized television, a CD player and an ipod docking station. There was a small area with a desk and couch and a lovely balcony overlooking picturesque Dupont Circle: a fantastic neighborhood with lots to see and do. To make up for the small bathroom, there was a medium-sized sink area with a mirror and a great makeup mirror. This hotel was just perfect for our needs. Though it wasn't exactly cheap, it fit within our budget and was definitely worth every penny. To make things even more enjoyable, the hotel provides little perks like a bathrobe, wine glasses, free wifi, a cordless phone, a free wine hour in the evening and milk and cookies at night.
