The hotel's location is centrally-located in the heart of Dupont Circle where we were within easy walking distance to great restaurants, shops and monuments. It is about a 15 minute walk to Georgetown and a quick Metro ride to the National Mall area. I hightly recommend this hotel. It has a great vibe, a positive attitude and down-to-earth service. I will definitely stay here again.

“Decent hotel for the price paid...very close to LAX and car rental” Stayed there for 2 nights...paid $70 a night (inc tax) on Priceline. Older hotel but the decor and facilities have been updated. Staff is helpful and polite. Crown Plaza also provide a "sleep/relax" kit with eye masks and pillow mists and relaxation CD - which is nice. On-site parking costs $12 per 24hrs...so instead of picking up the rental car and paying parking....we return the car to Hertz at night (rental is less than 10mins walk from hotel) and pick up the car again in the morning. Most of the other rental companies are within walking distance. Internet access (wi-fi) cost about $10 a day...There is a business centre in the hotel and it cost $5 for 1/2 day for internet and PC usage.

“business stay” Most recent stay was 3rd week of March 04. As usual, always nice. I had a small room during this stay but still nice. Poster beds, turndown service with chocolate covered strawberries (yum), and complimentary soft drinks, juice, and water in the refrigerator. Breakfast at the resturant and room service for dinner. Excellent each time. Can be noisy on a weekend night from the crowds in the street. Not much to do after 10:00 and quites down quickly. Have stayed here three times and enjoyed a wonderful stay on each occassion.

“Nice Overnight in Downtown San José” The Sheraton Four Points San José is well-located, directly downtown San Jose, near restaurants, cinema, and other amenities. Santa Clara Valley streetcars stop in front of the hotel and it is within walking distance of enough to occupy for a quick overnight, without a car. Check-in was smooth and the staff were friendly and welcoming. As Starwood Gold I was offered 150 extra points or a free drink at the hotel's restaurant. I took the latter and was surprised to find that it wasn't a cheapskate offer (like house wine or well drink), but instead a free wine, beer, or drink up to $15. A small thing but still nice nonetheless. My room was on the top floor of the four-story building. In the room I got the sense that the property had been an old hotel or apartment building. My room was almost large enough to make a junior suite, but not quite. It was clean, comfy, and the bed slept quite well. The bathroom was small but new and quite functional. There's a pocket-door between the room and bathroom, which keeps the bathroom from being encumbered by the door. I had dinner in the hotel restaurant, which was tasty and served by kind and conversational staff. If you're interested by the menu, don't dismiss dinner there because it's a hotel restaurant. The free drink brought me in and the menu made me stay, which is certainly the idea. A good one-night stay at The Sheraton Four Points San José.
“Good value, poor location” A bit far to get downtown, but the room and the price made up for that. The staff was helpful.

“Great NYC hotel, low rates to boot” I took a chance by waiting until a couple of days before going before booking a hotel, found this gem and booked two nights for under $150 a night including taxes. Hotel is on a fairly quiet side street off Lexington, yet buses are close by and Grand Central Terminal is just a block away for subways and Metro-North trains. Rooms are comparable or maybe a bit larger than the usual NYC room, make good use of the space and are very clean and visually appealing. I was told at check-in that my room was recently renovated, and it looked quite nice indeed. Bathrooms are clean, compact and functional; shower only, but that wasn't an issue at all for me. Beds are very comfortable and restful; the comforter was actually too warm for me, but there's a good blanket that's not as hefty already in the closet ready in case of that. The staff is very courteous, friendly and welcoming. This is a hotel that really gets it right and you can't go wrong staying here.

“Great location but not a true non-smoking hotel” We stayed for 4 nights in August 2001 to visit family and sight see in Chicago. The hotel was great location close to family and tourist attractions in the city. The hotel is funky in a positive sense. We has a queen bed room and had plenty of room. To recieve a discounted rate I had 3 reservations, so when I checked in I was give $30 credit to use in the room bar..great! I signed up as Kimpton memenr and ercieved free wi-fi in my room whihc was great. My only concern was the hotel is considered non-smoking however, we and other guests complained for several days since other guests were smoking in thier rooms. The smoke smell was very strong in the hallway, however we couldn't smell it in our room. The hotels staff after the first day was to spray perfume in the area which we and other guests determined it was worst than the smoke. The staff responded that they would handle it and charge the guests a fee for smoking, but that didn't stop the smoking. My thougths are how about asking them to leave the hotel? You could tell when they checked out since the smoke smell was gone. Overall, the stay was a great location for us, but I'm not sure I would recommend to other to stay at this Kimpton property. We have stayed at other Kimpton's in ther cities and the hotels were very different.

“Historic hotel copied poorly by so many others” You can feel the history of this hotel from the main entrance to the pictures on the walls of the hallways upstairs. The walk from the outside doors builds excitement as you approach the main lobby, which is beautiful, but perfectly sized, and with little alcoves that make it feel intimate. Other hotels in emerging markets try to copy this but get the scale and intimacy wrong. The staff is efficient and available, but with a New York brusqueness that is part of the culture of this city...they are NOT rude...but don't expect midwestern charm. But you feel you are in New York just as you feel the local flavor in the great hotels of Paris and London. The rooms are nothing special. Internet is not free, but at least they spent some money on a generous number of power plugs mounted on the side of the desk, and each room has its own wireless hub so the speed is pretty good. Those planning confererences will be pleased with the quality of the food. Meeting rooms on the main floor are perfect for black tie affairs, but not great for business meetings as they are lined with mirrors which can create glare from reflected spotlights, and in general, can take focus away from the main speakers. Seating is pretty uncomfortable after a couple of hours, but not unusual for hotels. Overall...a memorable stay in a historic hotel.

“Media Hilton con hertz e starbuck all'interno” Un ottimo Hilton in media con gli standard hilton, all'interno si trova sturbuck (ottimo per la colazione, anche se dovete andarci massimo alle 10 altrimenti non ha più niente), e la hertz. Per quanto riguarda la hertz la donna non è molto garbata, ma la comodità di poter lasciare la macchina a qualsiasi ora (anche quando è chiuso) perchè ha la cassetta "notturna" non ha prezzo. L'hotel ha la navetta gratuita dall'aereoporto (mi raccomando appena uscite cercate i cartelli dei bus navetta, si trovano davanti ad ogni terminal) all'hotel ogni 15 minuti. La pulizia è nella media hilton, non vi fate mettere fronte pista, perchè non tutte le camere sono insonorizzate bene. La camera è abbastanza grande per starci per più giorni (io ci sono stato 5). E' un ottimo hotel per prendervi tutte le garanzie dell'hilton, e non spendere molto. QUesto è fattibile, però, solo noleggiando la macchina. Ha anche il parcheggio interno (20 dollari più tasse). Ha il bancomat e le persone al check-in sono quasi tutti cordiali. Appena entri sembra di stare in un hotel di primissima categoria, poi quando vai nelle camere, la qualità diminuisce ma rimane comunque ottima. Forse dovrebbe essere un pò ristrutturato, ma nel complesso lo consiglio a tutti. Ma sempre con la macchina al seguito, anche perchè avete circa una trentina di minuti da hollywood (ma in questo modo vedete veramente la città). La connessione ad internet è a pagamento (wifi), gratis quella a filo.
“very loud” Extremly loud. Not worth the hassle even if you get a good deal.

“Parfait !” Nous sommes arrivés sans réservation un samedi soir à 20h avec nos 3 jeunes enfants de 7 ans, 4 ans et 2 ans. En moins de 15 minutes, nous étions installés dans une chambre, les draps étaient mis dans le canapé lit et le lit parapluie du bébé était installé. Chambre très confortable et très propre, spacieuse et fonctionnelle. Calme malgré la présence d'un bar sous nos fenêtres. Lit et canapé lit de grand confort, petit déjeuner buffet varié offert le matin, wifi dans la chambre .... tout était vraiment parfait !

“Very pleasant stay in a wonderful location in San Antonio” We had a 2BR, 2BA condo with a king bed in the master, two doubles in the guest room and sofa bed in the living room. Front desk staff was friendly. After I requested a room with a view they offered # 601 if we could wait about an hour for it to be cleaned. If you are in rooms x01, x03, or x05 on floors 2-5 you will not have a view but will face the wall of the adjacent building. The other (south) side of the building faces the driveway/garden area and the condos next door. They did try to set up a timeshare presentation, which they tried to disguise as a 15 minute meeting “to fill out a survey” offering a “free gift packet” of discounts plus $25 dining coupon. We declined, kept our phone unplugged and the Do Not Disturb sign on the door so we were not bothered by salespeople. The master bathroom was en suite with a private toilet room, large 2-person bathtub with bubble jets and a separate shower stall. Guest bath off the kitchen was standard small bathroom with tub/shower combo. The kitchen had granite counters, full size appliances including dishwasher and a granite bar area with two stools. They provided dish soap, dishwasher soap, a couple of packs of coffee, filters, etc. In a closet off the kitchen area was a stacked washer/dryer with two packs of soap. Both bedrooms had flat screen TVs. Master closet had a small wall safe, fine for cameras or small items but not for a laptop. The decorating scheme was nice with a Texas/Southwestern flair. We found the bed too soft but other furniture was comfortable. Living room also had a flat screen TV and DVD & CD players. The dining table seated six. A small balcony with two chairs was off the living room. Our side of the building faced north with great views of downtown but below our balcony was the roof of the building next door with loud AC fans making it unpleasant most of the time to sit outside. Also weekdays at 4 a.m. a garbage truck comes by to empty dumpsters making loud banging noises. After two nights we thought to leave our AC unit fan running all night to provide “white noise” to muffle the disturbance. The complex had a small workout room, pool table, game tables, free coffee in the lobby all day and 2 public computers. There is free wifi in all units. Swimming pool, 2 hot tubs and sundeck were on the 6th floor rooftop with great views of downtown. Parking is in an underground garage, valet only, $15 per day (in/out privileges). The front desk readily offered directions to cheaper self-park lots but we didn’t want that hassle. Since this was a timeshare exchange we did not have maid service. La Cascada has a great location on a quiet part of the River Walk. It is about a 10-minute walk along the river to the King William historic district, or in the other direction to the main part of the River Walk with many restaurants. Also about a 10-minute walk on the street level past the courthouse to Market Square with Tex-Mex restaurants and Mexican souvenir shops. The resort offers a free shuttle around downtown if you don’t want to walk. There is a small Hippos Grocery on the ground floor of La Cascada for basics but if you have a car I recommend Central Market just north of downtown on Broadway.

“Great Murray Hill location” this is a great hotel for business travelers and tourists alike. good neighborhood with terrific indian restaurants and local watering holes. easy walking distance to Madison Square Park and Flatiron. the bar is friendly and a great place to unwind in the evening. wonderful breakfast included in the price. rooms can be small and nothing special, but it's quiet. i wouldn't go here for pampering, but for sheer utilitarianism, it's tough to beat

“Great Location, good price” Overall our stay at the hotel was good, it's NYC so you don't spend much time in your room other than to sleep!! The elevators are a bit weird but they ran quickly and we had no problems. The rooms could use some updating, there were water-marks on the ceiling and some of the wallpaper was peeling, carpets coming up etc, but the tv was a nice flat screen and the bed was comfortable. Walking distance to Times Square and we even walked down to the Gerswhin to see Wicked---which I HIGHLY reccommend! :0)

“Super Duper!” Very friendly staff. Massive en suite rooms with wireless internet,fully stocked kitchenette with a refridgerator, microwave, dishwasher (!!), and a lovely little dining room section. Beds were huge and comfortable. Location puts you in the heart of Georgetown, walking distance from most of the amenities and within 6 blocks of the Metro station. Breakfast was complimentary and satisfactory with the usual continential type offerings. Would highly reccommend this place- a real gem.

“Empty shell” Nice location but felt like staying at a zero soul everykind of hotel anywhere in the world: - lack of natural light everywhere in the hotel - no windows in public areas and windows in the rooms can even not be half opened - design very minimalist, not a trendy way, a bad way - housekeeping knocking at your door to clean your room at 9am a Sunday morning, and shouting in the corridors all morning - 1 coffee pod in the room when we are 2.... - no bath gel amenities, just soap, shampoo and conditioner - zero personalisation - cherry on the cake : you have to pay wifi in the rooms : SO OVER! Not even a free access computer at the business center... Only free Wifi in the lobby. No comment. I still regret not to have chosed the next door Kimpton which looked fab Avoid this one, others facilities in Philly much more sympathic, or another hotel

“Isolated but a nice stay nevertheless” We arrived after 9 p.m. after a long drive from north of Los Angeles. Fortunately, we found the hotel with minimal difficulty with help of our Garmin. Check in was effortless, which was a pleasant surprise given that I had two reservations - one for a seminar I was attending and a second for an extra day after the seminar concluded. No problem, and no need to change rooms (which has happened at some hotels in the past). Despite the hour a bellman was standing by and took us immediately to our room. I expected a "room", given that I was attending a seminar at a group rate. Instead we had a king corner suite. Clean and nicely appointed with a large work area. The bellman took time to explain the lay out of the property and to show me on the hotel map the room in which my seminar was located. We had rented a car for the first portion of our trip and intended to return it the morning after we arrived. After studying the maps to find some of the places we wanted to go to in the evenings after the seminar, we realized that to get there we would have to take cabs. So after a call to the car rental company, we decided that it was less expensive and more convenient to keep the car because of the relative isolated location of the Hyatt at Mission Bay. The stay was uneventful. I was impressed that staff members often inquired if they could do anything to assist us. Housekeeping did a nice job and responded to several special requests, including one for a hair dryer, which apparently should have been in the room but was not. Because I don't do well with the lack of protein at the continental breakfasts offered at seminars, I ordered room service on several mornings. Delivery was right on time, and the food well prepared. The Concierge Desk was very helpful with suggestions and directions and printed out our airline boarding passes. Our biggest disappointment was the weather, which of course was beyond the Hyatt's control. I enjoy swimming and, after checking out the hotel's web site, was looking forward to swimming in its three beautiful pools. The temperature never got above 70 degrees, so I never went in the water. A fee was charged for internet service. Since I was on business and had to remote to my office during the day and in the evening, this was a minor annoyance. Since this is a resort and not a business hotel perhaps the fee is understandable. But free internet is always appreciated. Our visit was after the summer season at Sea World, so I assume that the hotel was quieter and less busy than in the summer months. When I visit a hotel "out of season," I often have a very positive experience with plenty of individual attention. But I wonder what it is like when it gets hectic? If you have read some of my other reviews, you know that busy hotels sometimes result in a less than optimal experience.

“Awesome Chicago stay!” We just got back from a magnificent stay in Chicago. I wish we could have stayed longer. The hotel was excellent in just about everything--but the absolute best is the service of their staff! The location is fabulous, it is on the main vein of downtown and within walking distance of many attractions. Being that it is at the Magnificent Mile is a treat in itself. Their facilities are great, and even though there was construction going on during our stay, I wasn't even aware of it. I think another great aspect is their concierge lounge--one of the very best I've seen. I could easily go on and on about how great it is. We know that we'll definitely stay there on our next trip.

“Great place for weekend stay” Staying at properties that style themselves for business on weekends is a key travel mode for me - you get high touch, high amenity hotels for a bargain price (tourist spot hotels during week is the same, but in reverse). The Andaz line are reliably nice, great service, and for Manhattan, this place has rooms that are gargantuan. Excellent gym facility as well. Very service focused folks in the lobby, and a great location to explore lower Manhattan, far away from the teeming masses of Times Square area, but still with plenty to see and do, great places to eat & play. Solid hotel. I'll be back.

“Very positive staff” We travelled across the USA on a tour organised by Great Rail Journeys of York between the 7th and 27th October 2009. We stayed in Denver for 2 nights at the Warwick Hotel. The hotel is about a mile from the main mile-long promenade lined with cafés and shops (16th street) and the staff tried very hard to make us feel welcome. The sales manager welcomed us to the hotel with an introduction and lemonade and cookies and rooms were available early in the morning which was very welcome after a night on a train! This was a good hotel with large comfortable rooms, including a walk-in closet. Very smart and contemporary decor, everywhere was clean with very positive and friendly staff. A complimentary car service is available to guests. We breakfasted in the hotel – this was a buffet, that was ample but not extensive (scrambled eggs were unusual – decorated with peppers!) and ‘special’ orders were met with some unwillingness on one morning (‘I think the Chef is otherwise engaged but I will ask’).

“Great Hotel but a bit impersonal” Spent 5 days in July at the Swissotel and found the facilities excellent. Our room had a view of Navy Pier and the lake and was comfortable and spacious. The hotel was well situated for exploring and catching buses to various attractions. My only criticism would be that perhaps due to the size of the building and it was busy that staff appeared a bit impersonal. There are numerous excellent eating establishments nearby and its an esay walk to Navy Pier.

“Disappointing in details for what is promised” [Note to Priceline & other third-party guests] Like everyone else, 3rd-party customers read reviews and have expectations; exceptional attentiveness to guest needs is what distinguishes one 3 star from others. Third-party prices fill otherwise unsold rooms, and provide the hotel with opportunities to sell services and win future business. My advice to Priceline customers: pay attention to reviews, articulate your needs clearly (both in advance and on arrival) and speak directly and immediately to management if your expectations are not met. If basic room needs are unmet and you bought from Priceline, tell Priceline in writing; use snail mail to the company’s street address and direct to Customer Service VP. I’ve found them very responsive. Talk to local management directly, pleasantly: they value meaningful guest feedback and often can use information you provide to correct persistent problems. Be courteous and civil to a fault: it never helps to be confrontational.] If you are buying on Priceline an airport-area hotel of 3-stars, this will generally be what you get for $45-$55 depending on season. COMMENDABLE: The E-W Light Rail fronts the hotel, right out the front door; it’s accessed by crossing at a close intersection with traffic signals. Clean basic rooms, airport shuttle, pleasant employees, functional computer for boarding passes in lobby; free functional wireless in rooms [many CPs charge for this}. The employee who handled my baggage to the room showed me controls and went to get ice. Excellent and reasonably-priced breakfast buffet with made-to-order egg options; the only bad thing was coffee, watered-down and old. Front desk employees helpful in recommending places to eat near Arizona Center. I went on rail, ate at Restaurant 1130, able there to find quiet and had a great server, Tino, and a lovely, perfect salad meal and the best housemade key lime pie ever. The hotel doesn’t charge for 1-800 calls. Quiet despite airport proximity. Temp controls on the unit, difficult to make comfortable. NEED FIXING: One person covers front desk at 5 AM, can’t do everything; the phone is slow to answer; I stood for 15 minutes waiting to check out and leave a package for Fedex. Employees shouldn’t ever be put in this position. Security finally roused the clerk. Bathroom break? Someone else can be cross-trained to cover for that break. Beginning at 8 pm, evening before I left, no hot water. Ditto middle-of-the-night, ditto at 5 AM. Mentioned at checkout; I was given a long explanation, boiling down to “the hotel knows” but “we don’t know why this happens” and “you have to run it a long time.” [Guys: 20 minutes of wasting water, following this advice, produces no hot water.] Engineering needs to solve this basic-needs problem so the clerks do not have to make excuses; it’s unacceptable for any hotel. Hotel web site and room literature offers small amenities, but a comb couldn’t be found. CHECK HOT WATER when you check in, or ask when you check in. If the problem is only happening in certain rooms, they will know which ones.

“Beautiful views” Overall the experience was OK. The view from the room was the best part. Included the bay bridge and most of the wharf. The room itself was tiny and awkward - and we were upgraded (thank you). THe room was clean and nice but it lacked a coffee machine. We never really felt welcome almost like the staff didn't care we were there. Oh, the baby crib provided (thank you) was pathetic. It was barely a pack and play. No blankets, no pad, and not clean. We paid about 119 for the room and that was reasonable. Anything more than $200 and you should look elsewhere as there are far better hotels in SF such as ST Regis and W for about the same price.

“Hip hotel; beware of parking” This is a beautiful, hip hotel. Very nice accommodations. Great rooms. Comfortable beds. Excellent bathrooms. Got a great price here through Hotwire. If you're driving, beware of the steep parking fees, however. There's no self-parking, only valet at $52 a day. Lots of restaurants nearby.

“What you would expect from a Marriott” Came for a conference; otherwise would try not to stay at a large chain. My room was clean-- except my tub floor always felt a little gritty under the foot... I had no complaints.... but this is not my type of hotel for leisure travel.

“Miss the Righa, but London NYC Is Fine” I had been a long time fan of the Righa and loved it. This was my first stay after it had converted to the London NYC. In contrast to the Righa, the London NYC is hip, stylized and fun. The aesthetic of the rooms is visually stunning. The living room portion of the room is much more work friendly than the Righa was but the couch is very uncomfortable and not very much fun to sit on. The bed is nice; great foam mattress. Our bed was a California king and not the traditional king. The linens are top notch. The bathroom again is visually pleasing but the bathroom I had was smaller than the ones I had at the Righa. The tub was taken out but the shower was made larger. All in all, the hotel was still very nice and great location. I think the new hip stylized look will not wear well (my stylized couch already had stains on it) but it is still a great location and great room size.

“Great Location, Friendly Staff but some drawbacks” This hotel was very friendly and efficient. You may need to use some earplugs since the train crossing is behind the Hotel. Walking distance to little italy and the gas lamp is less then a mile away. The parking is very very crazy, small not well marked spots and it is easy to get turned around the wrong way in the lot. Would stay again.

“Reasonable and Nice” This is a very nice and reasonably priced hotel. The rooms are pretty quiet, very clean and, for New York, my room was very spacious. The only thing it is missing is a gym. Overall it was a great stay.

“Historic Hotel” We stayed here for 2 nights in Jan. while on vacation and were quite pleased overall. Don't be afraid of the negative reviews here; just read up and know what you're getting into. This is a great historic hotel with a wonderful history and a definite charm, but it is not fully renovated and has quirks unique to older buildings. The bathrooms ARE tiny (NYC-sized), and the walls ARE thin. (Earplugs took care of this problem.) We didn't have the hot water problems others did, thank goodness. POSITIVES: We enjoyed the overall ambiance, found the front desk folks to be friendly, and we really appreciated the guided tour of the hotel that Tina cheerfully gave us, explaining all the wonderful history and movie star visits and the alleged ghosts. We wouldn't have wanted to spend a whole week here, since it's not a luxury hotel, but the 2 nights here gave us what we knew we were going to get, and we came away quite happy.

“Great Location” The Salisbury Hotel is worth considering for two reasons: 1 )It is in a great location and 2) it is insxpensive compared to the surrounding hotels. The compromise is that the hotel rooms are dated and a worn looking. However, our room was clean and adequate size. The staff wasn't outgoingly friendly but professional and took care of our request for more towels promptly. The continental breakfast is a good buy at $3.00 per person but its all carbs. A breakfast for 4 at the Brooklyn Diner across was about $80.00. The eating establishments around the Salisbury (including Angelo's and the Brooklyn Diner) are over priced and offer mediocre food. Your best bet is to seek out restaurants on either end of town (1st, 2nd and 3rd Aves on the East side and 9th Ave on the West side). The bottom line is that for families traveling on a modest budget the Salisbury's location and price are ideal, but don't expect the same appearance as a better hotel.

“2+ star masquerading as a 4” First - the location is great. Right near the south end of Central park and walking distance to the Broadway Theaters (12 blocks more or less). and there is a lovely deck where you can enjoy the air when the weather is good. This is not a terrible hotel but from what I was led to believe this was supposed to be a 4 star property. The rooms are TINY. No place to put your clothes (no drawers, one tiny shelf) a 12 inch cheap TV, broken alarm clock, a toilet that overflowed and no tub. I also had trouble with my wi-fi but the bill was corrected by the front desk on check out. The design is best described as Ikea. The whole place reminded me of a HGTV design show where they go in and remodel on a budget. At first it looks great, but after a closer exam you see how cheap it all is. I understand this was a converted YWCA.

“Second visit was good” My husband and I slipped off for a weekend recovery trip (college kids home for the holidays!) and stayed at the Chandler again. Our room was smaller than on our previous visit but how much time are you planning to stay in your room when you're in New York City? Bed extremely comfortable; nice bathroom; windows actually open; very QUIET hotel. We really love the location- easy walk to the subway, bars and restaurants but not noisy or congested. For the price you can't beat it.

“This Kimpton hotel gets it right!” I wish all Kimpton hotels were as good as this one! - Awesome, genuine staff - Really awesome pastry chef - An AC system that actually keeps the proper temperature - Updated bathroom -Sound proof windows -Great decor And unlike many Kimpton hotels (70Park in NYC, for example) which has some of the cheapest and worst mattresses anywhere, I think they invested a little more here. Will return for sure!

“The not so Grand Hyatt San Antonio” If "Grand" Hyatt means a big hotel with lots of rooms, then the title fits; however, if "Grand" means on par with other full service hotels, it is a misnomer. First of all, the hotel has no store. If you are in need of a new shirt or if you forget your contact lens solution, you will have to wait for the Rivercenter mall to open at 10AM. For a large hotel, the parking valet and bell staff appeared to be a little off their game when we first drove up. Instead of opening our car doors, they just kind of stood there until I told them we wanted valet parking and help with the bags. As far as the rooms go, we found the accommodations lacking. The bath towels are thin. I have seen better towels at a weekend car wash. The bathrooms don't have the separate tub and shower. It is combination bath/shower like a Hyatt Place. Moreover, this property just opened this year and the furniture had already been beat up quite a bit. The front desk staff appeared friendly but again a little clueless. When I went to the front desk to get the morning paper which is usually outside my hotel room door as it is supposed to be for all Gold Passport members, the front desk acted as if they didn't know what I was talking about. On a positive note, the breakfast buffet was excellent and the restaurant staff was outstanding! Curiously, we weren't offered the little smoothies that we have grown accustomed to getting at other Hyatt properties. We started to sit outdoors on the Riverwalk for breakfast to enjoy the fine San Antonio weather. Sadly, the patio chairs were soiled and dingy so we sat inside. Overall, it wasn't a bad experience and I would stay here again. I think it was a fair value considering I paid the government rate; but, had I paid the prevailing rate or even the "Hyatt.com rate" I would have been pretty upset because this Grand Hyatt just doesn't measure up to the hype.

“AWESOME AWESOME AWESOME!!!!!” I checked the rates almost daily and finally found a deal. Got it for $199 per night, king suite. Got there at 9am and checked bags (tipped $1 per bag later). We were able to hit the city for sightseeing. Checked back at noon, no rooms available. Came back at 330 and our room was still not ready (check in is 4pm) the desk clerk upgraded us to a king suite with a corner view. Had an awesome view of 5th Ave and the Empire State Bldg. Was awesome at night. We were on the 14th floor. The room was great. The maid did not replenish the coffee/toiletries. Was not a big deal to us though. The hotel had an awesome free breakfast. A bit crowded and there was a wait for the elevator at breakfast times. The hotel was in a great location. Couldn't be any better. It was one block from a subway stop. Five blocks from the Empire State Bldg. It was about five blocks to the heart of Times Square also. Great Chinese restaurant next door. Pax for salads a block away also Mc Donalds. Several local markets were available to buy beer and soda to keep in our fridge. The hotel also sold beer and wine in the lobby. I usually have compaints about hotels but I was kind of at a loss here. I just loved this hotel and the location could not have been better. We flew into Laguardia. It was about $38 plus tip on the way from the airport to the hotel at 8am. And the way back was about $34 plus tip. Cabs were readily available in front of the hotel. All the hotel staff were friendly and readily gave directions or restaurant recommendations. One recommended Ray's Pizza to deliver to the hotel and it was excellent. If I could give it a better than excellent rating I would! Loved it! Would go back and stay there in a heartbeat. And go see Wicked! It was awesome!

“Excellent hotel Stay” Stayed here for a business conference trip and glad I did. I was greeted with kindness from upon my arrival by the bellmen opening the cab door to the doormen greeting me farewell on my departure. All staff were full of smiles and seemed to be truly glad to work there. Even the housekeeping staff smiled when they greeted me with "hello". The hotel itself was beautiful and clean. I didn't notice a speck of fault with the cleanliness. Rugs/flooring looked new and the hotel looked new as well. Room was a decent size. The bed was comfortable with plenty of pillows. Bathroom had marble-finish with a walk-in shower and a tub. Turn down service was plus. LA was warm in the day then cooled rapidly at night and the rooms air system worked well going from "cool" to "warm" in an instant. Or, if you enjoy the cool air, the room had a pull-out window if you want to enjoy it. Hotel is located in a quiet area of downtown on the opposite side of the "action" of LA Live and the Convention Center were my conference was held. But the distance and hills made it too long of a walk and $10 for one-way taxi fare was too much for such a short trip. Luckily, a Metro subway station (that's right 'subway' in LA!) was right around the corner. Tip: the walk to the station is down a steep hill (OK for the morning), but when you return to the Omni, take the cool "Angel Flight" incline train to avoid the steep walk up. I asked for a high room with a view and was provided one facing Grand Ave with the Walt Disney Concert Hall in the distance. I was able to witness a few TV commercials being made as Grand Ave. seems to be popular road for filming car commercials. All-in-all, it was a terrific hotel for my stay. I would rate it as a luxury hotel, without the luxury price. It was great for my business stay and I would bring my wife there if we wanted an LA "get-away" couples trip. She'd love it. One last tip: Join Omni's Select Guest program before you arrive and get free water upon arrival, daily turndown service and clothes pressings - this was a big savings & convenience on my business trip.

“Excellent new Doubletree with highly problematic elevators” This new Doubletree (converted from a Wyndham) has extremely pleasant and helpful staff, the hotel has a small hotel ambiance, and the rooms are well equipped for a business stay (with many outlets, large desk, etc.). The room I had on the 22nd floor was small but quite comfortable and functional. My only complaint is the elevators: With 24-26 floors, the hotel has only two, relatively slow elevators. I don't know how they were programmed, but we waited almost 20 minutes for a down elevator to arrive on the 22nd floor at 8:30 in the morning. Because of this delay, I was unable to eat breakfast in the hotel and was late for a meeting.

“Pratique pour un décollage matinal !” Très pratique car situé juste à côté et navette gratuite à toute heure du jour et de la nuit. Il y a aussi une agence de location de voiture (Midway Rentals) au pied de l'hôtel, pratique pour venir de Downtown et déposer sa voiture à l'aéroport. Restaurant Subway à 50m de l'hôtel si vous ne voulez pas tester le standing du restaurant Radisson. Chambre spacieuse, bonne literie, bien équipée, propre. Juste eu une panne d'eau chaude pendant quelques heures, pas très agréable la douche à l'eau froide :-(

“A nice little midtown treasure” I go to NYC about once a month for brief business trips. I feel comfortable navigating the city so I don't really care where in Manhattan I stay in terms of location but want to get the best price on a 4 or 5 star hotel. I go for clean and safe which is not easy to find in NYC in anything below a 4 star rated hotel. I chose this hotel because I had a promotional code from Kimpton and the price was under $200 a night. This is a small little place. If you are going for atmosphere in the lobby or a great street, this is not really the right thing. The room was clean and luxurious. The bed was comfortable. The room had a huge flat screen television. My room was on the 7th floor and faced Park Avenue and was actually quite noisy. Other than that, it was a great, clean, nice place to stay. The staff was very friendly. The location is great, a couple of blocks down the street from Grand Central. I would definitely stay there again.

“Historical Elegance” The hotel is beautiful, something old and historical like you would find in NYC. The property is well maintained and perfectly located in downtown Dallas. We were upgraded to a suite and enjoyed the remodeled ammenities. My co-worker was on a different floor and in a different type of room, which was very old and not remodeled. We really enjoyed our 2 night stay and the staff was very pleasant.

“More like staying in a fine home than a hotel” The moment you enter this hotel, you can tell something is different. It doesn't feel like a hotel. There is little of the lobby craziness of most hotels, and there is only a small desk. They take your luggage and provide you with at tag that states, "don't worry, we will treat your luggage like it is our own." There is an elegant European feel to everything. The staff is extremely friendly. We were fortunate to get upgraded to a small suite, which was beautifully appointed, in an elegant an contemporary style. Great fireplace to keep warm in the cold Chicago winters. During our stay, we truly felt like we were living in a condo on the Gold Coast with great service. Te mini-bar is unlike any we have seen with drawers that are refrigerated (and one that is a freezer for ice (very nice). We have stayed at both The Four Season, and The Talbott (among other downtown Chicago Hotels). This hotel is our new favorite. The perfect combination of service and quality in an outstanding location. The hotel also has a no tipping police (which staff members informed us of - or a gratuity was included and notated on the bill...in the bar for example). We tipped a few of them anyhow, but it was not expected. All in all, this is one of the finest hotels we have experienced.

“Great downtown at reasonable price” 4 of us stayed in 2 rooms. A reasonable price for the rooms especially considering location in downtown Austin. Walking distance from restaurants and bars. Bathrooms are looking a little tired but not a bad stay. Great valet / bellman with a fabulous personality! Helpful in every way!

“Good and Bad” My experience this week at the Marriott was good and bad. I arrived after a nightmarish day, with my flight getting cancelled, 11 hours later arriving in Houston and lost luggage. I arrived and the valet greeted me and looked for my bags. I told them what happened and they got me to check in and they went to find a security person who was going to put the package together with the needed toiletries. I was greeted by the front desk by a very pleasant lady who seemed sympathetic to my bad day. She offered to open the sundry shop for me for purchasing any items. I thought that she was a very good sales person and not very sympathetic after. I guess that is what they have to do. But I can't imagine if you had a serious illness, she would just ask you to go buy something instead. I needed contact lens solution and they charged it to my room. 10 dollars for a small bottle, about the price at the airport. The items were delivered upstairs to me. The room was decent but on closer inspection, you can tell everything is very old. I had a mini fridge from 1970 and the dresser and drawers were very old as well. The flat screen tv was new LG. Bathroom was clean and updated. The mattress was one of the hardest I have ever slept on in a Marriott. It was probably the most uncomfortable night I spent in a Marriot and added to the fact I had no clothes, there was not even a robe in the room. It was one of the worst days/nights i have ever had. Room service arrived promptly the next morning. Food was decent. Not anything to write home about but overall I would rate it good for the convenience and promptness of the service. The shuttle and valet are the best things about this hotel. The valet driver acts like he came from nyc, swerving in and out and making sure you get to your destination EARLY! He got a good tip from me! and valet as well. They were very courtesous and professional and my car was always ready. Huge tip for them. So there are good and bad things about this hotel. Convenience to the medical center is the best. I didnt have the most comfortable room or the most sympathetic front desk lady.

“Nice Hampton” I stayed here for work for one night then over the weekend for fun. I used Hilton points for the weekend so I actually stayed in two different rooms. The first had two double beds and was fairly large for a NYC room. The second was a king which had less room in the actual room itself but a bigger bathroom. Definitely enough room for two but I wouldn't try to fit in a roll-away. If you want a big room, check out the Hampton Times Square North. The rooms were clean and tidy - no complaints there. The elevators are a little slow in the mornings, better if you are on a higher floor as they go up first and we saw lots of folks waiting for our too-full elevator as it stopped on its way back down. The only thing I really did not like is that they do not secure checked luggage. It sits behind a pillar in the lobby and on Sunday in the unlocked breakfast room. I checked luggage twice with no problems but I would have been happier to think my bag was out locked up or at least in a closed room somewhere. Very close to Macy's, Empire State Building and an easy walk to Times Square. Breakfast was "ok" but for better food, walk over to the Tick Tock Diner next door to the New Yorker for a real diner breakfast.

“Quietest hotel I've ever stayed in” Let me start my review by explaining that I am not an experienced big city traveler and I usually stay in chain hotels in the suburbs. So my whole experience at this boutique hotel was a first for me, and I often felt like a "yahoo from the sticks". Thank goodness the staff is so professional they didn't make me feel uncomfortable. I'm sure I didn't tip the right amounts, sorry. Your first impression of the hotel is quiet elegance. Then your stress level is greatly lowered when you see the famous brown lab Maverick sprawled out in his bed in the lobby. (he tolerates pats and picture taking). I asked for a quiet room so I was given one overlooking a central area instead of the street. The room was amazing, I don't know what others expected as to size, but I thought it was the same as any other hotel, although the bathroom is a little small. But that is all overcome by the sheer comfort and deluxe decor (although a wall of mirrors is a little retro). The bed was heaven, so plush you climb up into it. Nice reading chair, small desk, flat screen tv on the wall. They allow you to use the honor system mini bar as a refrigerator, which was helpful. I never heard another quest, no slamming doors, no loud a/c unit, just peace and quiet. Location was a little inconvenient if you wanted to go downtown to Union Square area or out to Golden Gate Park, took me my whole stay to figure out the buses. Hotel is at the Ferry Building, and the trolley up to Pier 39 runs close by. There really aren't any inexpensive eating places or mini marts nearby. What makes this hotel so unique is the staff. Dulce was on duty when I had an issue with an internet charge (I used the computer in the lobby and the directions were not clear as to how to get the 15 minutes free), she promptly reversed the charge and didn't make me feel like a cheat or liar. I asked about an airport shuttle, they arranged for the pick up (am I supposed to tip for that??) After I got home I completed an on line survey from the hotel and mentioned an error in my final bill of about $3.81, which I wasn't going to hassle with. The manager sent me an email saying he had investigated the charge and was crediting my charge card; now that is service. When I told Dulce she was as famous on Trip Advisor as Maverick, she thought that was the greatest thing ever. If I come back to San Francisco I would definitely stay here again, now that I have the buses figured out.

“underwhelming for cost” As previously reviewed, Michelangelo provides a great neighborhood, beautiful lobby in classic old NYC building style, room and bath well furnished, mostly attentive efficient service. But there were also alot of small problems. A very nice desk with an ugly cheap plastic email jack stuck on-no WIFI and no cord provided (they brought one quickly on request). I didn't really mind the extra charge for internet, but after paying $595 + various taxes per night, I do object to local and even "toll free" calls that cost up to $32 each!! They also have heat regulation issues-the usual adjustable thermostat was there, but no matter how low I set it, the heat from the radiator kept coming in. In late Nov, I was able to sleep by leaving a window slightly open, but would have preferred a better temperature control. Finally, although the coffee and croissants were ready well before the official breakfast time of 7am, the attendant wouldn't let me pour a cup at 6:50. Then 2 minutes later someone else just helped herself, and after he didn't object, so did I. Mostly minor issues, but other hotels in this price range (Four Seasons, for example) are much closer to perfect.

“Great value for money in NYC” Great location, within walking distance to Flatiron District and the Empire State Building, green subway stop right outside the door, making trips to Soho and downtown easy. Free breakfast every day was fantastic. Our room was typically New York small but had nice boutique style finishes. Service was good, however on our last two nights they seemed to forget about us, with no turn-down service being provided. Not a big deal, but we did notice as they had done this on the first four nights of our stay. Laudromat is also close by, which was handy for avoiding exorbitant hotel laundry service fees. Overall, great value - I don't think we would have found a better hotel for the price we paid.

“My second stay here and I plan to keep coming back!” I stayed at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront in August 2011 (as well as May 2010) and I enjoyed both stays tremendously. The service is at this hotel is top level. The employees are very friendly and helpful. Every person I came in contact with was warm and friendly. The hotel is also immaculately clean. I believe the hotel is fairly new and it has been kept up very well. It is located right next to the convention center and across from the Gaslamp Quarter. There is a pedestrian walkway that will take you from the 3rd level of the hotel's parking deck right over to the Petco Park area, so getting to and around the Gaslamp Quarter is very quick and easy. My suggestion is that if you are driving to the hotel and you have an older GPS, use the address for the convention center (111 West Harbor Drive) instead of the One Park Blvd address, but my GPS could not find One Park Blvd and it made getting to the hotel the first time a bit confusing.

“Good location, great for elvis lovers” The Heartbreak Hotel just sounds cool when people ask where you are staying. It is a kitchy little hotel, the lobby is the best part!! They also have a great free breakfast and 24 hr Elvis movies in the room. They show screenings of Elvis movies (we watched the '68 Comeback Special with a blue hawaii drink!) downstairs in a sitting area. Bar is very small (called the Jungle Room). the rooms to be honest are nothing special. If you go in expecting Elvis wall paper and 1950s furnishings, you will be disapointed. It is just a regular room with 1 Elvis pic on the wall. The cool part about the hotel is the hotel itself, not the room. I found the rooms standard, not dirty as some said. The location is great in regards to Graceland. Just note it is about a 20 minute drive (you have to get on a freeway) to get downtown where the bars and nightclubs and other attractions are. I like it, I am a huge fan and it was nice to go right outside my door and walk across the street to look at the mansion at night. I would stick right to the graceland area though, don't wonder around too far. The area is Ok, but not great. Graceland area is very safe though. Hope that helps!!TCB!

“Cool room/convenient location” took advantage of their buy one night/50% off next night offer, bringing average cost per night to around 80.00. Very reasonable for area and super close to PHL airport. Very sleek, ultra-contemporary concept. Bar/lobby area is quite loud at night , but fun. Everything was super clean and very new (property only open a few months). No free continental breakfast but items available for purchase in lobby. didn't look at the offerings so cannot comment on that. Staff is highly energetic and friendly, but the "aloha" will get to you after awhile. I feel they are still working out the kinks, but this is a wonderful concept and young business travelers should really enjoy the property. A few service issues (room never made up, coffee never replaced), while not major, should be noted. When I went to lobby to request coffee packet for next morning since room was never serviced, staff very apologetic, however it took nearly one hour for coffee packet to arrive. Only other issue is the paid-parking. Having stayed at several other PHL airport properties (Embassy Suites, hampton Inn, Hilton) which do not charge to park, it seems like the 6.00 per night can be waived?? All in all, my teenage son really enjoyed the stay, it is quite fun and reasonably priced, but I probably would pick a different place next time I needed to be in this area, unless the Aloft priced out MUCH lower than the others.

“Beautiful luxury Hotel unfortunately lacking good consistent service” Beautiful room overlooking the lake! The large flat screen was positioned right in the middle of the beautiful view though :( . Great location on Michigan Ave by Watertower. Very pretty lobby and bar area, once you go up the elevator to the 12th floor. You must take another elevator to reach rooms. Front desk staff were friendly and professional, but did not follow through on requests.Other staff were unprofessional and many lack understanding of the English language.Yes this was Chicago.Concierge was helpful and friendly. Horrible perfumed amenities, please switch to unscented or natural. Bad service at restaurant, waitress disappeared.Food oddly was EXTREMELY over salted and over peppered (black pepper).Green salad entree was truly inedible and sent back twice (never have I sent food back twice, but I was hungry and you really could not even take a bite of it-and I like spicy food). We were one of 3 tables at restaurant and staff was busy setting up for next meal, and no one but our waitress spoke English. Request for removal of down and feathers from room due to allergies was not done, though this was confirmed at check in. A man who barely spoke English was sent to change pillows and disputed comforter was down until I pulled out a feather to show him. Very unprofessional and inhospitable. Spa and pool area had many young (under 5 years) visitors on the Sunday we arrived. Not very relaxing, maybe it was a special event?

“One of Better Hampton Inns” As a Hilton Diamond member, I get to stay at a lot of Hampton Inns. This is definitely one of the newer and better ones around. The place is very clean and very up-to-date in decor. I got upgraded to a suite which is very roomy with a small kitchen. The overall layout of the hotel is unusual and the free parking spaces somewhat limited. I think they tried to maximize hotel space on small lot. Location is in the midst of many medical centers and there is a Luby's Cafeteria next door, with many better dining choices down Old Spanish Trail. The light rail is a block away. Place is very busy - I guess everyone knows what a good choice it is.

“Great convention center hotel” I recently stayed at the Hilton Austin which is directly across the street from the Austin Convention Center. This is an excellent hotel! The rooms were in excellent condition and were very clean. Hotel guests can use the heated salt water pool and hot tub on the rooftop for free, which was excellent considering it was cold while I was there. Wireless internet is free in the lobby and in the Java Jive coffee shop. If I had any complaints it would be that parking is too expensive ($16 per day for self-park) and that Java Jive was too expensive. $6 would get you a stale pastry and juice for breakfast. Liberty Tavern is a great place to eat and the prices were reasonable. Service throughout the hotel was excellent. However, the best thing about the hotel is that it is across the street from the convention center and is an easy walk to several nice restaurants and 6th street. So if you are in town for an event at the convention center, this hotel is in the center of it all. If you are in town as a tourist, however, I am not sure I would pick this hotel as downtown Austin can become choked with traffic. If you you plan on touring the Hill Country you'd be better off staying in a hotel on the edge of town. Otherwise, I strongly recommend this hotel.

“Consistent and Very Good” I visit San Antonio annually for a convention and this is my third stay in as many years. Over the years I have stayed closer to the convention center but find these to be noisy and congested, and not worth the higher rates just to be a bit closer. This business-friendly hotel is clean and the staff is very helpful and efficient. I do not need a full service restaurant and the cafe off the lobby is perfect for my needs. The convention is a short distance by River Walk or closer by street level. In addition, a walk in either direction from the hotel affords a scenic and non-commercial view that should not be overlooked.

“Love this Hotel” Stylish hotel in the downtown San Jose area, a stone's throw from many entertainment venues and restaurants. The hotel is a chic blend of old and contemporary. Rooms are crammed with amenities. Wonderful brasserie style restaurant on the first floor. Oddly the entrance to the hotel is off to the side facing a patio area and there is no way to directly drive up to it so you will have to carry your own bags or use the bell hop. If I had to choose between staying here or the Fairmont, I would choose the Hotel Montgomery in a heartbeat!

“Great location” We stayed at the Hotel Deca over the long weekend for three nights. The rooms are decorated beautifully and were very spacious. I would recommend a room that is high due to street noise. The bathroom was small and did not have a lock or a fan. This may not bother others but it was an issue for me. We did not find noise to be a problem. The best thing about this hotel is the location. We walked to a fantastic Italian restaurant and lots of really cool shops. There are all kinds of things to do within walking distance. This is a college area so it is quite colorful and I don't know if people with small children would like it. We have teenagers and they loved the area. All in all it was a good value for the money and we enjoyed our stay.

“Five Stars” My family and I stayed here for two nights in January 2007. I had grown up in nearby Pacific Palisades and had come here dozens of times over the years for special occasions, Thanksgiving or Christmas dinner, etc. The Bel Air Hotel has always been, and continues to be, a fabulous place. It's just a few miles off busy Sunset Boulevard but feels far removed from the hustle and bustle of city life in Los Angeles. The grounds are lush and immaculate and the swans in the pond are as beautiful and feisty as ever. The restaurant has undergone some major renovations over the years and the menu has been completely overhauled. The wine list is stunning. It is, to be sure, an incredibly expensive place to stay but it is an experience not to be missed. Our connecting rooms were spacious and delightful. The pool has always been a great place to relax but it was unseasonably cold during our stay and could have been heated to a much warmer temperature. The front desk staff has always been remarkably efficient and, for this stay, I showed them some of the old, black and white photographs my parents had taken of me on the grounds when I was a kid. (The dining room receptionist and maitre 'd also enjoyed seeing the evolution of the restaurant over the years in other of my old, family pictures.) The bar scene is "old school", lots of wood and plush carpets, a very cozy clubby environment. The true star of this hotel has always been the grounds and walking paths. They can take you to a different world. It is a real treat to be able to stay at this legendary Los Angeles hotel and enjoy its peace and serenity.

“Garden Variety Hilton Garden Inn” Stayed here for one night on business. Reminded me of all other HGIs I have stayed in before - acceptable but not memorable. Location is convenient if you are going to the convention center. Everything was clean, service was just ok. If you can get a room at a good price, then this would be perfectly acceptable although I prefer other hotels in Center City by comparison

“Bad value” The first thing we did when we got to this hotel was get on the internet and book a different hotel! Not much to say. First impression - the room had a musty basement type odour. There were zero comforts - (have to go down to front desk to borrow a hair dryer.) I understand it's SF, and therefore expensive, but we paid the same price for this 2 star motel, as we did the next night for our 4 star stay at the Intercontinental.

“For the price, this place could use some work.” I stayed here with a date and we did the Van Gogh package. Overall this was a very good value and we had a nice time. The hotel has very stifling and dry air and you could not open a window. Woke up feeling like I had slept in a sauna.

“Modern new hotel” IHG opened new good Intercontinental within central NYC. Pretty nice rooms, everything as usual in these hotels. The problem: the hotel in the narrow street and you have to go ahead 100 m to catch a taxi ti the airport. NOBODY, even staff dont care about it. No good view. But very recommended, especially if you Ambassador member.

“Good value, no frills, so-so location” I would say for a family looking for a great place to stay that is clean and affordable, this would be the place from my experience with DC. My only problem is if you want to visit all the fine restaurants, this place is way out of the way. However, if you are visiting Capitol Hill (which we were) it is the best location. The rooms were clean, the bed was better than my bed at The Willard later in the week. They have mini fridges in the room for your own items! I love that! I stay at a lot of upscale hotels and it irritates me that they fill it with THEIR overpriced items and leave no room for anything I might have! LOL I think & heard that the neighborhood is a little dicey at night so take a cab if you go out. There is a CVS almost right next door for convenience items - no wine and beer sold there. The hotel niteclub was VERY crowded on Wednesday night and it was obvious white women were not welcome to enter to even buy a drink and walk out. OVERALL, though, a great value. They have a lovely courtyard and lobby, and a quick breakfast/Starbuck's buffet.

“O.K.” Very nice hotel, a little overpriced. I do have to agree with a previous write-up, in saying that the front desk help are not very nice. You would think they would be a bit more courteous. Just remember there are plenty to choose from.

“Fabulous” This hotel is great! The lobby is unique and artsy - in fact, the whole hotel feels a bit like an upscale, hip art museum. The staff is friendly and helpful. The ballroom area is much more interesting and inspiring than any other hotel ballroom that I've ever seen. The guestrooms are spacious and well-accomodated, and the bathrooms are very clean. I had room service, which was very quick, easy, and delicious.

“Do not come here” I am Priority Club Platinum member (highest possible level) and I often use Holiday Inns and Intercontinental hotels. I have been to many, but have never seen such a SMALL rooms. If you are traveling with someone, there is barely enough room to stand together by the bed or in the bathroom. Did I mention that rooms are extra-small? Then imagine bathrooms... even SMALLER. The locations of the hotel is OK, on the 26th Street West, I would say that this is the main positive thing, I would also praise friendliness of employees; another problem is housekeeping, which is one of the most slow services everywhere... We stayed here for 5 days, but on three the housekeeping managed to come after 4pm. You have also free access to "high" speed internet, but this is no HIGH speed internet, but extremely slow speed internet. I have even meausured the speeds, and the speed is between 8Kb and 20Kb per second, depending of the time of the day. SLOW. Another thing is that there are no glass-glasses in the rooms, only plastic ones. The hotels only has 2 elevators, so at times you can wait for one for minutes... The hotel actually feels more like motel, not a real hotel. And for Priority Club Platinum members... there are no upgrades. I even asked manager about this, and got the answer that we were upgraded in the high floor (19th out of 25)... not breakfast/dinner upgrade or larger room upgrade... strange... one ask himself about Priority Club membership...

“Nearly in NJ!” Loved the staff. Rooms large by NY standards. Clean and comfortable. The street and construction noise was so bad, we asked to move to a higher floor. Where the heat vent rattled loudly. Wifi was nearly useless. It is soooo far west I spent much pf my trip walking across town. And back. Price was great and I generally love Kimpton but the are 0 for 2 in noisy Manhattan.

“Caught in a 1960's Polynesian Time Warp” The lobby tells you what you're in store for: an indoor waterfall, a dark koi-filled pond, lots of palms and tropical plants. Inside the complex you'll find a maze of pathways lined with lots of overgrown tropical plants/trees, streams filled with some huge koi, and a multitude of ducks (and lots of duck crap...so watch where you walk and don't go barefoot!) Our first impression inside the room wasn't much better: we had two stained comforters on the beds, carpet that was in need of replacement, bathroom tile that needed some serious re-grouting. We were unable to get a king bed (hotel was booked solid they said) so they gave us what they called 'two queens', which in reality was two full-sized beds. The place needed a fairly significant face lift and freshening up--and perhaps a good hosing down as well. It did look like the hotel was replacing carpet in the rooms across the courtyard from us, so perhaps they're underway with the cleanup. On the plus side, the pool was very nice, there is a large hot tub, and the hotel is in a convenient location, within walking distance to many restaurants, bars, etc. and Mission/Pacific beaches. We did not use the restaurant or spa services; however, we would not stay here again.

“Hits and misses” There are some very good things about The Palmer House and some "just okay" things. First the very good. The central lobby (of course) is stunning, a masterwork of classical architecture and a landmark in its own right. Service is excellent and the staff is friendly. The "crown jewel" from a guest perspective is probably the fitness center, one of the very best I have ever seen in any hotel (but would be better if it were open 24 hours). Even the valet service is reasonably accurate in its estimate of a "5-10 minute wait" for your car to be brought around to the door (although 10 min is probably more reasonable). The "just okay": the rooms. The carpets look worn, but I'm not certain it's correct to say that they're "old". Maybe it's the weaving or design, but they look dingy. The overhead lights are flourescents, giving an anticeptic (think "doctor's waiting room") cast to the room. It doesn't help that the color scheme in my room (black, olive green and copper bedding and carpets with cream-striped walls) is just, well, odd. Finally, the I could hear the guest in the room next to me like the door was open; doesn't make one feel like they've got privacy.

“Très bien” L’hôtel est situé dans le quartier français de la ville à quelques minutes des principales attractions de la ville. Ces dernières (mairie, Independence national historic park, Musée d’art) sont toutes accessibles en marchant. L’hôtel est d’un aspect extérieur plus que quelconque. Il ressemble à un immeuble assez banal. Il propose un service de voiturier qui est le bienvenu dans un quartier où la circulation est difficile et le stationnement un vrai casse-tête. À l’intérieur, le hall grand. Le personnel vous accueil en vous disant « Bonjour » en français. À la réception certains font même l’effort de parler en français. La chambre est grande, assez lumineuse et très confortable. La vue sur les toits de la ville laissait par contre quelque peu à désirer. L’équipement de la chambre est au niveau de ce type d’hôtel : système audio Bose, produits de Bain « L’occitane », bouteille d’eau tous les soirs. Le service est très réactif. Les lits sont ouverts tous les soirs, les serviettes remplacées. La climatisation se fait sentir tout en restant discrète et agréable. La salle de bain est grande avec douche, et baignoire. Si l’ensemble est de très bonne qualité, la chambre laisse une impression de « fin de cycle ». Bien que l’on ne trouve rien à redire, les murs, le sol, les plinthes commencent à vieillir. Je vous recommande de payer le petit-déjeuner à l’avance ce qui vous reviendra moins cher que de payer les plats à l’unité. D’autant qu’ainsi, vous pourrez choisir n’importe quel plat au restaurant « Chez Colette » dans une carte mélangeant plats classiques américains et spécialité françaises : assiette de viennoiseries ou assiette de fromages (en français dans le texte).

“Only one problem......” There was only one problem with the hotel.......the sleep was not the best because of how loud everything was out in the hallway. Between the doors slamming, people walking up and down the halls and people in their rooms, the walls seemed paper thin. However, considering the price of the rooms, especially since in was near the Galleria (all the rage in Houston), it was worth the inconveience of the sleep. The breakfast included with the room was not bad, some items were terrible, but that is to be expected with a continental breakfast. The hotel was friendly and clean with a great location overall for Houston. I would rate this a 3.5 if I could, but since I can it gets a bump up to a 4.

“This hotel is a hidden gem!” Was very pleasantly surprised by this hotel. In the heart of downtown philly within walking distance to the business, shopping and little italy districts. This small boutique style hotel also offered free internet/computer use, free breakfast and free fruit and snacks all day. Was worried about staying at this "no name" hotel but they staff was very helpful and the clean rooms came through with shinning colours. Please note that this hotel is in the heart of the gay community, a detail I did not see in any advertising.

“Good Stay at the Holiday Inn-Express” The Holiday Inn-Express is a nice hotel in a nice part of town. It is a couple blocks South of the Outerbelt and there are some eateries nearby. It is a little difficult to enter the property from Southbound East Street and you have to turn after the hotel and come back or work your way through other lots to get to it. The breakfast was excellent with the signature cinnamon rolls and biscuits and gravy, and more. It was clean in the room and in the breakfast area and seemed to be quiet as I slept well through the night both nights I was there. Check-in and checkout were a breeze and the clerks were pleasant and accommodating. It is good for a stopover or for a longer stay. I didn't get to try it, but the pool looked nice.

“Pleasantly surprised” I had low expectations. My wife and I decided to stay here because we had an event nearby the next morning. I ended up being pleasantly surprised. The room was clean with everything that you would need including a microwave, full kitchen, and dishwasher. Staff was very pleasant and helpful. Morning breakfast buffet was ok at best but I didnt expect much. I would actually stay here again.

“Great location but ...” We recently stayed at the Harborside Inn for 3 nights while visiting Boston - on arrival we struggled with the front door with our luggage as there was no doorman. Once inside, the Reception staff were disinterested and barely glanced up to check us in. Our room was an Atrium view but not the view shown on their website - ours was of ducting. The room was small and dark with no tea/coffee making facilities, but this was available in the lobby. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. The bathroom was clean but small - we are not large people but they had put the loo between the sink and the shower, so a large person would have had difficulty. It was a large walk in shower, but was spoiled by a small shower head. There are free computers in the lobby. The same lack of interest from Reception on check in was the same throughout our visit, each time we went out or came back. Even when we checked out at 5.30am and needed a taxi, we were told that there was probably one round the corner. The location is great with lots of restaurants and attractions almost within sight. The T stop is just outside the door. We would not stay here again.

“GREAT LOCATION” This is a very nice hotel in a great part of Chicago. I was here for business and stayed for the weekend with my husband. The hotel is so close to everything and anything. Would stay again.

“Great location for national/international meeting” I was there for a work meeting with approximately a dozen other people located around the US and Canada. The hotel was very accommodating for our needs, especially Eric (?) in the restaurant. The internet for our meeting was a bit pricey, but a necessary part of one day of our meeting. The location was great and central for all members. Chicago in February can be dicey with the weather, but it worked out for us. The check in counter was a bit slow, mainly because there were only two people at the desk. We would seriously consider returning for other meetings. The only problem with convenient workplace meetings was that we never left the room.

“A real lack of communication and secuity” I stayed at this property in July and had an unsettling set of events happen on the afternoon on my departure. Let me say, there was NO criminal activity involved. However, what did occur showed a complete lack of coordination between hotel departments and a laissez-faire attitude toward guest secuity and comfort and this hotel. At appx. 2:00 PM (I had pre-arranged and paid for a late check out since I had a late flight) my room phone rang. The person identified themselves being from "engineering" and "even though I had a 'DND' on my door" they needed to come in to work on the alarm speaker in my room. I told them it wasn't a good time because I was napping, but that I 'd be checking out a little later. The very aggressive person argued with me, insisting they needed to come into the room. After saying no 3 times, I finally had to hang up. About 45 mins later, it started with another phone call, which I ignored. 2 mins later, a knock on my door. It got worse. Over the course of the next 10 mins, I had (between knocks and rings) about 10 attempts to get in my room. Having already stated it wasn't a good time, I ignored them all. Finally, I called the front desk and explained what was going on. I asked if there was an emergency or something urgent why they would need to get into my room. The front desk clerk stated "I don't know anything about engineering". Impossible to nap, I decided to get into the shower and get ready for my pick-up. After about 10 mins, I heard what sounded like someone trying to get into my room door. After quickly getting out of the shower, I discovered my room door open, with someone trying to flip open the security bar to gain entry. I immediately slammed the door shut. I called the front desk and asked to speak to a manager immediately, but they were "in a meeting". The assistance of a security guard was not offered. I was anxious at this point to get out of my room, which I did. On my way out, I went by the front desk and asked to speak to a manager again. After waiting 15 mins, the Assistant GM appeared. He was courteous and listened to my situation, but could not offer any explanation for what happened. At this point, I headed to the airport to catch my flight. I immediately followed up with an message on the hilton.com website which was unanswered and unacknowledged. Through an internal investigation department where I work, they were able to get some answers. They found out there was a contractor working in the hotel doing "fire equipment testing," which included compoents in guest rooms. That day, my room was the last room on which they were working and the contractor was over-zealous and was going in no matter what.. He had a master key. It looks like some of the basic components of hospitality, and guest safety, security, and respect had not been imparted on these workers. I guess what concerned me more is that others in the hotel, including the front desk the others members of management didn't even seem to to know they were there working in the hotel that day. When I still had not heard back from Hilton after a couple of weeks, I sent them another email, asking why I had not heard from them. I finally got a short email back. They explained to me that the matter was closed. The property had explained to them that the 90-second conversation we had the lobby had finalized the matter. No formal aplogy. No formal explanation. It's a real "oh-well" kind of atmosphere. Other chains would have handled this much more professionally and more rapidly. I don't upset or rattle easily. I think many other guests would have been MUCH for upset than me by all this!!!! This hotel is the the center of the city with a lot of activity swirling around. Guest secuity and safety should be first and foremost!

“Fantastic hotel, brilliant service and very close to Times Square!” We stayed in this hotel for five nights earlier this month and found it to be fantastic. The front desk staff are eager to help and give five star service. The hotel itself is a new, trendy place about 100 yards from Times Square and the heart of all NYC's action. I doubt any of the rooms have a fantastic view and (like all other NYC hotel rooms) they are quite small - but they are cleverly designed to make the most out of the space. The furnishing was new and the room was immaculate and modern, we really enjoyed our stay here and would recommend it to anyone. It's a hotel with service that far exceeds what you'd expect from the star rating. Only complaint was that the air-con could be a little noisy at times and the housekeeping staff were quite loud in the corridor, communicating from one end to the other! Big thanks to the front desk staff who were helpful, polite and gave us some fantastic advice with Central Park.

“Off the hook” I cannot say enough great things about this property. The staff is wonderful--very friendly and not pretentious despite the fact that a celebrity or two is either staying or hanging out at PHD Rooftop Lounge here any night of the week. There is a freaking DJ booth in the lobby! We never ended up going out to any other clubs or lounges the entire three days we were in NYC--we just ordered bottles of Champagne and hung out in the lobby jammin' with the house DJ. Their house DJs were all excellent. Did I mention the views from PHD? Epic. So, if you are traveling on business and looking for a quiet place, maybe this isn't the hotel for you -- but I can say that I stayed on the second floor and it was very quiet. The rooms are sleek and hip -- actually spacious by New York standards. Internet worked well. There is also gym for working out. The downstairs lobby cafe/restaurant was packed during mid-week. Yes, I said the one in hotel lobby. I'm going back next week to eat there. Definitely THE PLACE to be. If I had to make one complaint -- and it's totally minor -- it would be that the shower curtains with the sheet of metal hanging rings on it was a little hard to open and close, and the bathroom got very stuffy due to steam and seemed to stay muggy for a while. I couldn't find a ventilation fan in the bathroom.

“Good Stay Overall” I was in El Paso for two days on business and stayed at the El Paso Marriott. The staff was outstanding - very friendly and helpful! As a Silver Elite member of the Rewards program, I was given access to the concierge level of the hotel (even though I did not reserve a room on that floor). Free breakfast every morning! Room was quite and clean. I received a call from the front desk to ensure my stay was going well. Location of this property is great - very close to the El Paso Airport and Interstate - 10. My only issue was that this property is really starting to show its age. It could use an upgrade to bring it up to speed with other Marriotts.

“Nine comfortable days in D.C.” The Omni is a very comfortable hotel with a great staff. Spent 9 nights on a business trip. Comfortable rooms and beds. The staff is very accommodating and I love that they deliver hot or cold beverages to your room for free in the morning if you're a Select Guest member.
