Free Select Guest membership also gets you free wireless internet. Good location with lots of restaurants in the area and close to the metro and Woodley Park Zoo. I really like this hotel.

“A boutique hotel with elbowroom” Maybe I'm used to tiny NY hotels, but this was as modern and stilish as many boutique hotels, while leaving enough room to move around. We were in 4 using a 2 double queen, so the extra space was well welcome. It is a few blocks from Union Square where we took the cable cars to move around town. Tip: if you plan to use the Muni system, get the 'passport' which is a day (1/3/5) ticket for all transportation and you'll save a lot of money. Reception was nice and friendly, checking in and out was made easy. Valet parking is a rip off but I guess that's SF. The room had nice elegant furniture and a nice and extremely clean bathroom. Beds were comfy. The room offered a water heater to make coffee or tea but they also had free coffee in the hall where the wi-fi system worked very well. We were on the 6th floor and we had no noise there. Their a/c system is indeed a bit weird, it's basically like a portable unit, which tends to be a bit noisy - but we are europeans, and SF temperature was good for us without needing to use it. I doubt it gets very hot there, but if I had, I would rate it like just above an average a/c unit noise - it would not scare me but not everyone sleeps the same way. We had breakfast twice at Dottie's true blue café, I'd recommend it but get in line early and skip weekends. Sears also was ok, they have the dollar pancakes which kids enjoyed. We dined once at the Grand café in front, very good food and nice ambience (but a smaller menu). They have good pizza for the kids. We may return next year, to SF definitely I'll book here.

“Great Downtown Hotel for Business or Families” I recently spent a night at this Downtown Denver property and was very happy with the hotel and service. First the pros: very friendly clerks who went out of their way to provide great recommendations and directions. The rooms was a great size and clean. The bathroom was newer and spotless. The location is terrific, two blocks from 16th Street, which is close enough, but just far enough away to be quiet. The breakfast was MUCH better than other Embassy Suites I have visited, and everything was delicious. The cons: the only parking option is very expensive valet. There was also a slight odor in the hallway in the morning (before and after breakfast), but that very well could have just been a guest or misplaced room service trays. Overall, this hotel is a great choice if you need a place in downtown Denver. I will certainly return if business brings me back into town.

“Beautiful but beware of noise and gym” I stayed here for three nights and was overall pleased. It is one of the most beautiful facilities (think Titanic or Daddy Warbucks) with a charming aura from the 1920's-1940's. I marveled over the architecture and wonderful artwork. The location is perfect; there are tons of places for cheapskates to eat (such as Subway, McDonalds, 7-11) right outside of the hotel and is within walking distance of major attractions. If you choose to stay here, be aware you must pay to use the gym, which also has limited hours; this was lame, and I would not stay here during the winter due to the gym usage fees. I used the pool and got plenty of exercise walking to and from work. If you stay here, make sure to ask for a room away from the elevators and as quiet as possible. It is true you can hear people through the vents and doors. If I had not been lucky and had quiet neighbors, I would have probably made the staff's lives hell. Check-in man was a little condescending, but everyone else I encountered was quite pleasant. No free internet at this time, but you could probably go to Corner Bakery and get free wi-fi.

“Great place to stay in NYC” I am very picky about hotels, and was very satisfied with my stay here. I selected this hotel after reading the reviews on Trip Advisor, and was not disappointed. The room was VERY clean, the bathroom was great, and the hotel was in a great location. The price was very reasonable too. I would definitely stay here again for future trips to NYC.

“buona posizione” hotel motlo centrale a pochi passi dallo stazionamento dei cable cars i famosi tram di san francisco e dalla strada principale ricca di negozi . nelle vicinanze anche macy's. buone le camere silenziose spaziose e buoni anche i servizi offerti dall'hotel agli ospti. Internet a pagamento anche in camera.

“Excellent location noisy aircondition” Nice and convenient location. Clean and nicely decorated. The only negative was the noisy aircondition . Well equipped kitchenette. Nice pool, polite staff Because of the labor day holiday the price was higher that it should be. I suggest the breakfast hours during the weekend to be till 11.30 am.

“Great place, perfect location.” They gave us a corner room on 32nd floor, which was extremely quiet and comfortable. The hotel has a great breakfast buffet, that operates very efficiently, in a nice atmosphere. The beds were comfortable, room quiet, despite the fact that there was a huge crowd in the lobby for conventions. Great view from the lobby bar. And you can do Michigan Avenue, from across the river, not to miss any sightseeing. The River Walk is romantic at night, and the hotel is close to many business locations. Wished we could stay longer than a day. Front desk staff was very very friendly and accommodating.

“Excellent saty, odd location” Recently stayed at Embassy Suites Boston Logan Airport for 1 evening. Looked for a hotel to end a great vacation in the area and wanted something comvenient to both downtown and the airport, this certainly fit the bill. From check in to drop off at the airport, can not say enough good things about everyone we spoke to. All were smiling and helpful. Rooms are a little small when compared to other Embassy Suites, but they are clean, updated and comfortable. Airport subway stop (2 stops to downtown) is an easy 5 minute walk through the park, or the shuttle will take you/pick you up. Very odd location, they have blocked the street from the area, so the only in/out for traffic is pass rental car lots. Unfortunately (for me!), GPS did not know this, and kept routing me into the area. Finally parked outside the barrier and walked into the hotel to check in. Being so close to the airport, we all commented on our surprise there was no airport/airplane noise at all. All in all, a good stay. PROS *Convenient location *Comfortable room *Full breakfast, was a bit crowded though *Great staff *Great city view from the 9th floor *Big bathroom CONS *Odd access by car *Smaller size rooms *Noisy air conditioner

“Simple, small, but central” We stayed at the Iroquois because it was close to the theatre district, and within a reasonable walk to my husband's office. I had read all the reviews on-line, which were positive, and knew it was a member of the Small Luxury Hotels Group, so I was not too surprised when we walked into the rather simple, small lobby. It is not a place to see and be seen; if you want that, try one of the many other large hotels in the area. It was clean, with a lived-in look. By that, I mean not modern or high-tech, and with the bonus of friendly not snobby staff. Our room had all the right moving parts, but it was very small. Aside from the welcome gift of fruit, nuts, and chocolates, there was a large flat screen TV, comfy bed, safe, mini-bar, desk, and a chair, but as two people we felt a bit cramped. We had to be creative about placing our suitcases in spaces that would not block anything. (One went into the closet, and the other behind the bathroom door.) There was free Wi-Fi, movie CDs at the front desk, and free morning newspaper of our choice. The bathroom was very clean, and had Molton Brown bath products, plenty of Frette towels and robes, and a well-placed mag mirror. The shower was nice and strong, but when I showered late in the morning, it took a very long time for the hot water to come up. (My husband said his shower was fine.) There was a modern AC unit in the room that was efficient, but not silent. It did act as white noise to drown out the noise of the city, which is certainly a factor at certain times of the day no matter where you stay. Let me also say that because this is an older building, it is quiet. There was no flushing noise, loud echoes from the hallway, or sounds from next door in the middle of the night. Some of that can also be attributed to the lack of convention and large group clients, but it is certainly a plus. Triomphe, the restaurant connected to the hotel is lovely. We had pre-theatre dinner there one night, and enjoyed every bite. This highly rated small gem of a restaurant is soothing, with attentive service and a sophisticated french menu. We did not try their breakfast, but from the looks of the fresh-squeezed juice we saw when checking out, I think it would have been a treat. Would we go back, probably. I think we'd try to get a larger room, if it was not too expensive. Our rate was reasonable compared to other hotels, and we were not there to be in the room too much, but for the convenience. It is close to the subways, major shopping avenues, Broadway and many restaurants. When you list your priorities, The Iroquois comes out looking like a good choice.

“Feels like an apartment complex” I don't know for certain but this place feels like it must have been an apartment complex before it became a hotel. That said, I've stayed here twice so it isn't too bad. Actually the rooms are decent (the lighting is a little dark). The biggest issue is the way that the place sprawls and has lots of other entrances besides the main entrance. Overall, it's a clean enough place with good space (handy if you are travelling with kids). The price is frequently at or below $100 which makes it a bargain.

“Not Bad. Just Not #7” Something has to be done about Tripadvisors Hotel ratings. There is nothing wrong with the Homewood Suites by Hilton in San Diego, but to have it ranked as the #7 hotel out of 245 in the area is misleading. This is a very standard suite hotel with nice, but generically appointed rooms and facilities. If I was traveling with a family I might even consider it except that it’s in the middle of nothing except the airport. But the staff was nice and the breakfast was adequate, but not the “wonderful” spread I’ve seen other people mention. It’s a standard decent breakfast with sausages, scrambled eggs, omelet station, grits (I think. Maybe Cream of Wheat). There were a lot of families here with little kids and they all seemed comfortable. If you need a place for one night to crash near the airport, go for it.

“Pass Up This Hotel” I stayed at the Parker Meridien this past weekend, Sunday night the 15th of January. The room was nice and clean. The swiveling TV stand was a plus. A vcr and dvd in the room was nice, too. I paid extra for a Parkview room. The view was nice but underwhelming. The tall buildings in front of the hotel and closer to Central park impede on the view. Not really worth the extra money. My biggest complaint comes from when I checked out Monday. The clerk told me there was a 54 dollar minibar bill. I never, ever, use a minibar but I do look to see what they have in there. Found out that this one is on a sensor system and if you move the item around it counts as being used. I was quite annoyed and said someone should tell you at check in. They told me that housekeeping would inventory the minibar and they would either call or email me once that was done. Well it is Thursday evening the 19th and still no call or email or credit to my debit card. An alleged 4 star hotel should have better service than this. I will be disputing the charge straight away in the morning. I would use another hotel since New York has so many better offerings and if you want a parkview book the Essex House, it actually overlooks Central Park.

“Bien, sans plus, mais correct.” La chambre est bien, grande et propre, quoiqu un peu désuète. L'hotel est bien situé dans le centre ville de LA ( en plein chinatown ), cela dit, LA est tellement immense que tout est relatif et je conseille donc au client sans voiture de prevoir de partir pour la journée, et de ne rien oublié. Le gars de la reception n etait vraiment pas sympa.Sinon bon hotel dans l ensemble, sans surprise.

“very good W hotel” It might not be the best W hotel I have stayed at but it is up there! I stayed there for 3 nights and everything was very smooth from check-in to check-out! The staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was very clean and spacious. Highly recommended!

“Very nice hotel” I was here for a conference. Although the Riverwalk portion of their title is a bit disingenous (it is near the Riverwalk, but not near the spot where the restaurants and clubs are), my stay was extremely pleasant. My room was quite nice. The staff were uniformly pleasant and attentive. The grill's food was pretty good--and the food provided for the conference was surprisingly good.

“Good Stay” This Hyatt uphold the brand reputation by providing excellent and friendly service from check-in to check-out. Personnel is attentive to guest needs and met my expectations. Room was spacious and everything worked properly, the bed was good but not as good as other top brand hotels. Location is excellent if your business is in that specific area. The gym, bar, and restaurant were adequate.

“A true five star experience” Thanks to frequent work trips to DC I had the pleasure of staying at the Park Hyatt six times during the past couple months and I really enjoyed my stays. Staff were very friendly and attentive, check-in was quick and efficient, the breakfast benefit for Diamonds was amazing, and I loved the food at the Bar & Lounge and the Blue Duck Tavern. The wine list seemed quite comprehensive and heavily emphasizes local wines, but perhaps it might be nice to feature a few more traditional choices, say a red Bordeaux. Service in the Lounge is perhaps one area that might be improved, as more than a few times it was a little slow and inattentive. The rooms were extremely spacious and I enjoyed the Tony Chi design. I mostly booked Premier Park Deluxe rooms, so I can't really speak much to upgrade success. During my first few stays I did receive upgrades to corner rooms, but oddly enough after I mentioned in passing at check-out that I like those rooms I was put into non-corner rooms with really odd floorplans on subsequent stays (my last stay was in room 1031 in which the bathroom felt a little bit like a cave). On other small issue was that the maids seemed to have only very limited English skills and didn't seem to be able to understand that I was asking them to return later when I happened to be in the room during turndown service. A wonderful property and my hotel of choice in DC! By the way, the hotel is hosting the Masters of Food and Wine this week, which promises to be a wonderful culinary treat.

“Ok for a 3 Star Hotel - This is NOT a 4 Star property by any means.” I made a mistake and used Priceline to book a 4 Star hotel in Wasington DC and I ended up with the St. Gregory Hotel. In no way, under anyone's check list is this adaquate property a 4 Star hotel. It is an "OK" 3 Star property that was overpriced and forgettable in a city of memorable hotels. The staff was friendly, the place wasn't dirty, but it is a glorified mother with AC in the window that blows on your face during the night. There is an awkward Marily Monroe satue in the lobby that looks out of place. The location is good for Georgetown and Dupont Circle, but not very close to a metro stop. I felt betrayed and ripped off, but that was my fault for booking it through priceline.

“Good place to stay if you're visiting IU” I stayed here for a business trip to IU. If that's the reason you're coming to Indy, then this is a great place to stay. Location is great. Rooms are nice. Restaurant is mediocre. I ate lunch there and ordered the pappardelle. I didn't get pappardelle; I got spaghetti, and it wasn't cheap. My dining companion asked for a grilled cheese sandwich w/o tomatoes and got -- tomoatoes! But other than that, I would recommend this place to anyone who has work to do at IU.

“Good if you are at a conference there” It is great if you are at a conference there or get a good rate. The room was fine-not great, and it was fairly clean. You could easily hear noise through the walls and the people next door stayed up late. We had a good breakfast in the restaurant and a good dinner at the Irish pub that is on site. Location is not ideal if you want to do sightseeing around Boston.

“Doesn't Deserve Its Reputation!” I've read the wonderful reviews of this hotel, but frankly, my experience was an utter disappointment. You are forewarned: your mileage may vary! They tried to put us in a smoking double when we arrived, which was completely unacceptable. In fact, I wasn't even aware that any decent hotels in the DC area still allowed smoking, but apparently the Omni has a block rooms set aside for them. Then they tried to stick us in a King size with a rollaway, but the clerk hesitated for a moment and said she 'found' a double for us. It turned out that the double was located in their remote building, which they rather euphemistically call the "Parkview" section. It's called the "Parkview" section because it's so far away from the hotel that you pretty much need to drive your car to get to it! We had a lovely view of the hotel's backyard and the freeway, though. As to the Parkview room itself, it's fairly mediocre. Don't expect any of the opulence you'll see in the lobby--that is set aside for those lucky enough to stay in the main building. The Parkview wing was built in the plastic fantastic 1960s, and it remains as stylish and modern as your average Courtyard by Marriott. What do I mean by that? It's a room. That's all it is. Don't think just because the front of the hotel is neat, and (apparently) the rooms in the historic section are neat, your Parkview room will be neat. It won't. Our numerous attempts to move to a better room were a complete waste of time. For the price, you can do much better--The Palomar on Dupont Circle offers a far better value for the money. And the Marriott at Wardman Park across the street has better views if you're a convention-goer. Long story short--your mileage may vary. Why risk it? Stick with a known quantity, and avoid the Shoreham. Unless, of course, mediocrity is your thing. Then you'll LOVE this hotel!

“Paper thin walls in a lovely hotel” I have stayed at the Double Tree before and remember some problems with several rooms. Old beds, dusty. This time I was impressed with how clean and modern the room was. However this hotel has 2 problems that can be quite annoying. The first thing is that there are 4 small elevators for 26 floors. That means that at times, and especially during the weekend you could spend 20 minutes waiting for an elevator. I am not kidding. The second problem is the thin walls. You can hear EVERYTHING. At 4 am there was a couple fighting. Really fighting. It was scary and security came up. At 6am I was woken up by my next door neighbors that being intimate with each other. It was very uncomfortable because it wasn't mattress noises or screams but everything...Too much information. So all and all, if you can sleep with earplugs and have the time and patience waiting for an elevator you will like this hotel. Otherwise, look for something else

“Nice find!” Very pleased I stayed here two weekends past. Location is very desirable, about a half block from the heart of Times Square, but also next to a church, so fairly quiet. There is a convenience store across the street, which comes in handy whilst you come & go. More importantly, the hotel really helped me out (on a stressful weekend, as it turned out) with an early check-in - actually a very early check-in. The staff was professional and informative, even as I passed by them in a lightning bolt at 350 AM for a 600 AM flight out of LaGuardia on Monday morning. The decor is beautiful and helped make up for the fact that I had no view whatsoever. Would definitely stay here again.

“Better than you'd expect from Doubletree” I've had some so-so Doubletree experiences lately, but the Doubletree in downtown Houston was top notch. Only strange thing was that the hallway reeked of cigarette smoke even though I was on a non-smoking floor: is the hotel not really all non-smoking? Fortunately, the room's air was clear, so it was more a bepuzzlement than a problem. Nice hotel, nice location, I will stay there again when in downtown Houston.

“Okay, not spectacular” In some ways this was a nice resort; in others, it was not. This resort is very spread out, and I thought it was very strange that they didn't have a bell boy on duty when I checked in. My room was several buildings and parking lots away, and they seemed annoyed that I expected them to find someone to drive the golf cart with my luggage and myself to my room. The restaurant is in the main building. I had the physical ability to walk there, but I think it would be extremely inconvenient for an older person to walk that distance. (As I said before, there is no transportation between the buildings.) My room, a junior suite, was gorgeous. The furnishings were beautiful, and my room overlooked the marina. There was a party going on in the room next to mine, and the sound carried through the connecting door. The weight/exercise room was very well done. There were many weight machines, as well as free weights and treadmills. The restaurant was also good. The hot tub was broken. The resort is located on a marina and has a beautiful setting. I preferred the public beach to the hotel beach. My main complaint about the location is that it is rather isolated and not near any other restaurants or shops, so once you've seen the resort there's not much to do. The free airport shuttle was very convenient.

“Typical HyattPlace” This is a typical hyatt place, very clean, organized well and easily locatable from both the interstate and local roads. Across the street, Jack in the Box and Starbucks can be accessed from walking but I cannot remember if there is a crosswalk or not painted on the road, so be careful. Negatives: My room had a smell to it, not sure what the funk was all about. Price was a little higher than the airport Hyatt House No managers meet and greet with snacks and drinks (unlike Hyatt House) Workout room is pretty small, 2 treadmills and 1 bike. No free weights.

“Nice and Hotel and close to Downtown” This hotel is nothing fancy and for business is a perfect location. They do charge $10 a day for parking, but if you are there just for a nice there is easy parking on the street. The rooms a little dated, but you are paying to be downtown.

“Expensive and not that nice” I stayed in this hotel because I was trying to earn Starwood points. If you're going to charge over $300 a night, you shouldn't have tacky plastic cups in the bathroom that fall over when you put your toothbrush in. You should have a safe in the room for guest valuables. You should not claim to be in Tribeca when you're really on Canal, without much interesting around. Next time I'm staying elsewhere.

“I love Sofitel” I travel to New York for both Business and pleasure about every two weeks. This trip was a combination of both. Usually when I travel I stay at Starwood hotels and have stayed at the Westin and almost every W hotel in New York. I have also stayed in the Mrriot Marquis, the Millineum, the Plaza, the Four Seasons, several modern boutique hotels and some other 4 and 5 star hotels over the years. This trip was during fleet week so the hotel I wanted to stay in was booked. Since I had stayed at my first Sofitel in Philadelphia recently and had a good experience (they gave us a suite for the standard rate because all of their standard rooms were booked) I booked the New York Sofitel through Perfect Escapes. I booked a standard queen room that came with a guaranteed upgrade (upon availability), early check in, late check out, and free breakfast. I arrived at around 1 pm and they checked me right in to a large suite on the 26th floor (not a junior suite) which had a great view of the Chrysler building and where a welcome card awaited me. The room was really nice, had plenty of closet space, and was very quiet. Everything was really clean, no foul smells, and no wear and tear was apparent. I love the Sofitel feather beds and our bed had both down and synthetic pillows already on it. At turn down we were left with a large glass bottle of Evian and two small plastic bottles in addition to a box of chocolates. The towels were replaced, the music was turned on, the drapes were closed in both the living room and the bedroom, and certain lights were turned on. The bathroom had a fresh orchid and candles for around the tub. The water pressure in our room was really good so I cannot explain why others have had problems with it. Room service was fast and efficient and not anymore expensive than I had paid elsewhere. The concierge was polite and helpful and our wake up calls were exactly as requested, I do not care that it was a recording. The gym was small but well equipped. I ALWAYS put my valuables in the safe (which this room was equipped with) and would not leave money unsecured in a hotel room. It doesn't matter the class of the hotel, thefts occur everywhere, so I did not have any issues with items missing from our room. Breakfast was good and at the end of it the waiter discreetly told me that I would not get a check because my breakfast was included in my rate. I inquired about the gratuity and he said that was taken care of. I was left alone all day and never asked when I would be leaving which has happened to me before when I have had late check outs at other hotels. They did not slip a bill under my door which I think is great. At check out I was asked to confirm my charges and then I was given a copy. Overall I found the service to be very good but not great. The bell men do not greet you like they do at other hotels but I received exemplary service everywhere else. The decor is not modern and clean like a W but I found it very attractive. I liked this hotel and would definitely stay there again.

“Below Average Sheraton” Not great, not terrible either. The hotel is in an area that is undergoing major highway/street construction so the exit closet to the hotel is closed and required a slight detour. As for the hotel itself, the highlight was that parking is free. Overall, the hotel felt a little run down and tired. The room's AC worked well. Beware rooms that face the highway will get traffic noise from passing cars. One issue at check-in. We had booked one room with double beds, and instead they gave us one room with one king bed. We had to carry our luggage down and recheck in. The staff should of run a card upstairs as it was clearly their error upon check-in. Other than that the hotel was not that memorable.

“Not the best experience, but probably not representative...” My company recently added a sales office in Chicago, so I made the trip out from NY to Chicago. Our office is 1.5 blocks away from the W, so I decided to book here instead of at the Westin (the other approved hotel on the list where we get a special rate). I've had good experiences with W properties in the past (San Diego, Los Angeles, Tuscany in NY), so I expected something similar. It wasn't great. The good news is that my original trip was canceled because of that horrendous NY-area weather. My flight was canceled by air traffic control, and I ended up calling the W at the last minute and telling them my predicament. To my surprise, they waived the cancellation fee, even though it had nothing to do with them. That was a big plus in my book. The bad news is that when I made it out a week later, the only smoking room available (I smoke cigars and thought it'd be nice to be able to smoke in the room) was one with double beds. The beds were so soft that if someone told me that two elephants had sex in them the night before, I would have believed you. That was really disappointing. The condition of the room wasn't great, either--scuff marks on the walls, molding come off the base of the walls, etc. On the plus side, room service was good (the bucatini is phenomenal) and generally prompt (May, the person who brought up my food the first night, even went out of her way to give me a card with her name on it). I travel a lot for business and so I'm willing to chalk it up to a bad one-off experience, so I'll try it again in the future with the W. However, I'm staying at the Hard Rock Chicago next time to see what else is out there.

“Excellent Hotel, Much Improved” Two years ago I stayed at this hotel and at that time rated it as average. Well, much has changed in the last two years. All of the rooms have been remodeled and are very attractive and the bathrooms have been given a wonderful marble shower. The rooms are still on the small side but what they lack in size they make up for in luxury. The wireless internet works perfectly. Sevice at this hotel continues to be top notch with a very friendly staff that tries to make your stay as perfect as possible. The hotel is in a wonderful and quiet neighborhood yet is within (long) walking distance of the Dupont Circle Metro station, and numerous restaurants. Overall this is one of the best hotels for the price in the DC area!!!
“Excellent view and a very nice hotel” good staff, nice breakfast, lovely view from the rooms, overall a very pleasant stay..

“Stay here for the ideal location not supreme luxury” The Back Bay location is excellent, and is convenient to Newbury Street, as well as Copley Place/Prudential shopping (connected so you don't have to step outside). T stop is a 5 minute walk away. It was the most competitive rate I could find for a brand name hotel in a good location, though the hotel seemed crowded with families and tourists as a result. Rooms were clean and functional, though you could tell from the hallway/room decor that the building is an older one. Elevators were a bit slow. Room service was very prompt and easy to work with. Parking is expensive: $34/night in the connected parking garage; $45/night for valet. A few doors down from Lucca Back Bay which serves a good bar dinner in the late night.

“Great location walk everywhere very clean” Rooms very clean. Beds excellent. Staff very friendly. Walk to the beautiful circle, mall or many excellent restaurants. If you drink Coke and that is important to you, the vending here is Pepsi and accept credit cards only no cash in vending machine. If you order coffee to your room in the AM be aware the $12.50 listed in the room service menu is actually $20 after all the add on items and tax they charge. Elevators slow during prime time. Outside of those few little issues this is a great property currently going through some light renovation so you will see some covered area around the parking and drop off area and a few inside. Pool and Hot tub were open and looked to be very clean.

“Fabulous stay and a fabulous deal” I received this hotel deal through a Travelzoo promotion with the hotel. I paid $59/a night. The offer was for $15 parking which I did not use....and a upgrade to a view, a gorgeous view or the skyline and the river..a $25 food and beverage voucher for the first night which included room service and alcohol...and a buy one/get one free entree the next day which I did not used. I have never felt like things were so great that I owed the hotel money. Noteworthy things: The hotel gave me early checkin....and 2pm checkout for being a Priority Club member. To me the location was a great distance to where I wanted to go...Union Station, Magnificent Mile, and Chicago Cultural Center. The hotel is in Merchandise Mart and the lobby is on the 15th floor. So you have 2 elevator rides to reach the lobby. Room service above averages. I thought the prices were decent. Told me it would take 35 minutes and a knock was at the door at exactly 35 minutes. The spring rolls...yummy. The Italian KOBE burger and sides....extra yummy. It did not taste like a "free" meal and I tipped the server 50%. Room: Bath a little dated...I love the recycling options. I loved the soft vs firm pillow selections in the room. My room also has a sitting area. Very large area. Enough towels to keep me happy the entire stay. Quiet unless someone was outside the door. The not so great: The WIFI...blech..it kept going in and out, in and out, along with my phone reception. That was the only issue that I had. I will note that there were no offers to help with my baggage although I was flirted with...I had no problem but the offer would have been nice. Front Desk provided EXCEPTIONAL service.

“Visiting in Philadelphia” This hotel is right across from the back of the bus station. It is convenient for traveling. The staff is very friendly and helpful with directions and events in the city. The hotel is clean and comfortable. I stay here often when visiting the city.

“Very comfy hotel” Chicago has way too many hotels downtown than it needs... and that being the case you can always find a good rate downtown rather than in the burbs. That being said, I stayed here because of a great rate offered on a Saturday night. I was really impressed by the hotel. Great service and nice rooms, halls, elevators etc... This is a boutique style hotel which is located in the loop area. It is on a very quiet section of the street. FREE wifi internet - which was fast and easy! Only cons: not much to walk to or eatting around the place, but restr. and lounge in hotel. parking of course is valet or self garage - around 35-40dollars over room rate... but that is in any city.

“What an excellent place!” I have recently stayed at this property for more than 3 weeks. We had a 2 bedroom suite- with a king bed in one room and 2 queen beds in the other room. Being a Platinum Elite member, I have seen an assortment of Marriott properties but this Residence Inn really shines up above many other properties. One of the main factors is the attitude of the staff. Everyone was wonderful!!! From the time we checked in, Tabitha was one of the most efficient front desk staff I have ever seen. Nothing was impossible or difficulty for her. What mattered to her was customer satisfaction and it showed! The location of the property ids great- yes- it is not facing the inner harbor – but so what?? It’s just 2 blocks away and a 5 minute stroll. Loads of restaurants nearby as well as a 7’ eleven and CVS pharmacy right next to it. Many of the restaurants do home delivery as well. The suite itself was spacious and free internet was a bonus. Valet parking was 29 dollars but thats what it is in all the downtown hotels. The valet staff were so nice too. Housekeeping was again very good. The hotel was running almost full occupancy everyday of our stay but nevertheless the staff managed it very well. The hot breakfast was ample and containers were being refilled rapidly. The evening meals served form Mondays to Thursdays was also very good. Another bonus was the free use of internet in the lobby along with free printing service. Excellent! Overall, this property shines out as one of the finest Residence Inn properties I have stayed in and I would definitely stay here were I to return again to Baltimore.

“would not go back” I love desin but it must fulfil certain basics!to me it was not cost-effective. you should avoid room and stay in public areas which are really great. I guess it did not match my expectations at all. Technowall is just a plastic design with an imput to connect Iphone to TV. No dockings station, wardrobe doors wouldn ́t slide (so drawers inside could not be used), bathroom connected by not full door with the room so if you need any privacy your partner will need to leave the room. If you a re a woman you won ́t be able to do your make up in the bathroom, your cosmetics cannot be placed anywhere! no bins in the room. lights need a manual to be operated! if room is on bathroom is off, if bathroom is off purple light is on but entrance is off... uffff!!! please, basics first! If all you want from a Hotel is beautifun areas to hang around, maybe this is your place, otherwise, choose another hotel. No cost-effect at all.

“Excellent stay in Memphis” We booked this hotel based on reviews we read on TripAdvisor. We arrived at the hotel and were quickly checked in. We had a two bedroom suite that we were sharing with friends. We had a lovely living room with a couch, chairs, a television, and a coffee table. There were even sucking candies on the coffee table. There was also a table and chairs to the side of the living room and a full kitchen complete with utensils. We also had two bedrooms and two bathrooms. The bedrooms were not large but each held a queen sized bed, a closet, a television on a chest of drawers and two night tables. One bedroom also had a private bathroom with a tub and the second bathroom was outside of the bedroom and had a shower but no tub. The suite was very clean and we were more than satisfied. Every evening from Sunday trough Thursday a modest dinner is served in the lobby along with free beer, soda and wine. A very nice touch. Also, breakfast consisted of a buffet that included not only cereals, bagels and pastry , juices, coffee, etc.but eggs, meat and potatoes as well. The hotel is close to Beale Street and if you make a left outside of the hotel, cross the street and walk down a block - down the alley to your right is a restaurant called the Rendezvous. We really enjoyed their dry rubbed ribs. Also, the trolley stops right by the hotel and it only cost a dollar so we happily left the car in the garage and used the trolley to take us to certain tourist spots like the Civil Right Museum.

“No problems” All in all, a good stay at the Tudor. I chose this place based on getting a good price on Expedia, though it was still around $200. As expected from a NYC hotel, the room was teeny. It was fine for me since I was staying alone. I imagine that room style is for single travelers...I couldn't imagine having shared it. Overall, it was clean and the staff was nice. A few stray hairs in the bathroom, but nothing alarming. Great water pressure in the shower. The pipes make loud thumping noises, but luckily that never happened while I was trying to sleep. For some reason, my laptop didn't like the hotel...it took forever to turn on, yet once I left the hotel it worked fine. I don't know if there's something in the walls or whatnot. I thought at the time that maybe it was my computer acting up, so I didn't think to ask if others had had similar problems. The bed was comfortable. AC worked fine. Location was good. I would stay there again if necessary and if the price was right.

“Best customer service I've experienced in a long time.” Got this hotel on Priceline for $60/night ($216.64 for 3 nights with fees/taxes). As other reviewers have said, the nightly parking rate almost cost as much as the room. The hotel charges $48/24 hours for parking with no self-park option. Nearby I was able to find a lot for $35/24 hours. I'm sure there are cheaper options if one is willing to walk further. Arrived well before check-in time and was able to check-into room 369 (East Tower) right away which was well appreciated. Room itself was a pleasant surprise. Modern, clean for the most part, and comfortable. Huge flat screen TV, two beds, one easy chair, one additional chair and a desk chair with wheels. The bathroom was spacious; however the counter space was somewhat limited. My only complaint about the room was the hot/cold water situation. Often there was no sufficient hot water in the morning for showers. In the evening there was no cold water, hot water came out of both taps, even the cold. The fix for this was to run the bath tub on cold and let the extreme hot water drain off. Even the toilet pipes were piping hot during the evenings. Strange situation. The hot water in the morning was adequate, but not as hot as I would have liked. The hotel itself is huge with over 2000 rooms, countless meeting rooms and several massive conference/convention rooms. The hotel is divided into east & west towers with indoor connecting a connecting bridge on floor 2 and tunnel on floor -1. Check-in is located on the second level with several food options on the lower level. Nothing at this hotel is inexpensive. The coffee bar, second floor bar, steak house, lobby restaurant are all very expensive. There is not a lot in the immediate area, but lots of options if one is willing to walk 10 minutes away. There is a good convience store/market behind the hotel. Prices there are reasonable for water, alcohol, snacks. The business center charges offensive rates for internet use: $7.50 per 15 minutes and $0.75 per page if one wishes to print. That said, free airline check-in and boarding pass printing is available at the conceirge desk on the second level. There are also internet terminals across from the lobby coffee shop on the first level which may be a cheaper option. As other reviewers have stated, there is a lot of noise that can be heard. Although I was not disturbed by guests on either side of me, the doorway to the hall allows a lot of noise transmission. Even with the ear plugs in that I brought, I was awoken the first day by noise in the hall: a first for me when traveling. Usually in northern hotels in the winter I find the hotel rooms very, very dry. Somehow this hotel has solved this problem. The air was always very moist. I'm not sure how they do this on such a massive scale, but I certainly appreciated it. The air always smelt 'fresh' and always had a pleasant smell. I can't say enough about the staff at this hotel. They are trained well. Everyone I encountered went out of their way to be pleasant, say "hi", and ask if there was anything they could do. I saw one employee walking by an open elevator door stop and place their arm in the closing doors so a couple could make it on before the doors closed. I was allowed to make a long distance call using a phone in the lobby. Every single staff member was a plesure to deal with at this property.

“Good hotel, poor communication” This is an edited review - I deleted my earlier review due to what happened after we checked out. Service - top notch, room - very comfortable, clean. Size of room - on the small side, but well appointed - coffee, TV, ice only on certain floors. Size of bathroom - ok, shower only, but only 18" between edge of sink & wall of shower - large people are in trouble. Back to service - have to mention how helpful the doormen were. They held bags for us before we checked in (after some discussion), and again on our return. Concierge & doormen were great with directions & looked up bus routes as well. Why the edit? We were here on a group rate and entered a special code into the website. The quote I was given had tax = 0.00. Since the regular website quote showed tax, I assumed tax was included in the special rate. When I questioned it on check out, it was taken off (I had the e-mail confirmation), but then charged to my card two days later. Though they were correct that the tax was due (I was going to challenge it on my credit card but checked the group's site & it did say "+ tax"), I feel a call or e-mail was appropriate explaining the re-charge. Thus, 1 star taken off a 5* review.

“Just an average hotel” I had one night weekday (Thurs) stay. It's rated a Marriott "2" (1-5) and that is about right. A simple breakfast buffet is $10 and not impressive. Small workout room (2 treads, 1 elyptical and one lifecycle). The service is adequate, but not up to Marriotts high standards. A basic hotel but nothing else

“Good choice” This hotel seems to be trying very hard, with an extensive happy hour spread, lots of breakfast choices, and free long distance phone service. Our room was clean and comfortable. A couple of minor complaints: The Internet service was spotty. Also, for some reason the staff seemed to be hoarding the nonstick spray for the waffle iron. They would come by and spray it periodically and then remove the spray, so that guests' waffles were often a stuck-on mess. Overall, though, this is a nice motel.

“European style boutique hotel--delightful stay” Our friends met us in NYC for a theatre weekend and booked us into the Michelangelo. We are from NYC originally, and come in from CT often, so we have had many varied hotel experiences over the years:from the Plaza to the Royalton, We were very pleasantly surprised and pleased. Our friends arrived first, and received an upgrade on both our rooms to a Jr. Suite. Our suite was quite spacious, well appointed, quiet and sound proof. Our room was tastefully decorated as were the halls and the lobby area. All rugs were plush, and everything had a feel of quality, not like cheap hotel furnishings. We overlooked 51st Street, but heard no street noise.There were blackout shades in addition to shears and curtains, wonderfully dark and quiet for a good night sleep. Toiletries were nice, service was quick and pleasant. Yhere was a complimentary shoe shine, but we didn't notice until it was too late to avail ourselves of it. The chocolates and turndown service as well as the morning NY Times, were signs of a first class hotel. Morning continental breakfast was an added plus, and included cappucino or espresso. We truly felt as if we were in Itlay! The location was wonderful, as we had tickets to "Wicked" which was less than a block away. Le Bernardin and China Grill are both within a couple of blocks and are highly "Zagat rated" restaurants. The MOMA is only a couple of blocks away as well and Carnegie Hall, Rockefeller Center and Lincoln Center are within walking distance. We had a wonderful stay and would definitely return to the Michelangelo.

“Historisch wertvoll” Das Doubletree Hotel San Diego Downtown liegt in der Nähe der bekanntesten Attraktionen der Stadt – ganz nahe beim historischen Gaslamp Quarter in der Innenstadt, Little Italy mit seinen schicken Geschäften und auf alt gemachten Restaurants, dem Old Town Petco Park – Heimat der San Diego Padres, dem San Diego Convention Center, dem San Diego Financial and Business District, der Symphony Hall und dem San Diego Concourse sowie dem San Diego Cruise Terminal. Auch der internationale Flughafen von San Diego ist mit dem kostenlosen Hotel-Shuttle gut erreichbar. Auch andere Attraktionen von San Diego wie der bekannte San Diego Zoo, die Museen im Balboa Park, das historische USS Midway and Maritime Museum, die Hafenrundfahrten und Angeltouren, das Seaport Village, Sea World, Coronado Island und Horton Plaza – das schönste Einkaufszentrum der Stadt. Das Hotel bietet moderne Zimmer und Suiten mit geräumigen Arbeitsbereichen, Datenports und kostenloses Hochgeschwindigkeits-Internet (kabellos). Die meisten Standard-Zimmer verfügen über Glasschiebetüren, die sich zum eigenen Balkon mit Blick auf den Hafen und die Innenstadt von San Diego öffnen. Weitere Ausstattung: Dual-Line-Telefon, Schreibtisch mit ergonomischem Stuhl und Kaffee-Angebot von Wolfgang Puck. Alle Hotelsuiten haben HD-LCD-Fernseher. Außerdem bietet das Hotel das Ariana Restaurant mit kalifornischer Küche. Zur Erholung und Entspannung stehen der beheizte Außenpool und Whirlpool, die Sauna und das moderne Fitness Center mit Precor-Cardio-Geräten zur Verfügung. Das Personal ist freundlich uns sehr bemüht. Eine gute Wahl für San Diego.

“Very Average Marriott with Below than Average Service” I stayed here one night in November 2009. The last time I was at this hotel was July of 2004. The hotel has not changed much since 2004. The service was really bad. I stood in line to check in for about 20 minutes. There was only one person working the front desk. I had been told, via email, there would be a guest ambassador for quick check in.... this person was MIA. I saw the counter the ambassador would use, but it was tucked away and not in service. The room was dark and a bit on the small side. I do not like when I am working at the desk and I can reach to my side and touch the bed. The room is way too small when that happens. The gym was nice and was the highlight of the short stay. I checked into the Hilton on the other side of the convention center from this hotel and it is a much better value than the Marriott. I would stay here again if I could not get into the Hilton. It has a great location to the convention center, but thats really the only thing that would bring me back to the hotel.

“Not Worth the Price, Disappointing” At $525 USD a night, this is an expensive hotel even for NYC. The hotel caters more to the tourist than the business person. There is no coffee in the room (nor amenities like tooth brush). When I asked about a cup of coffee (for the early morning), they could do it for $10, but not at 05:00. When I went out the night before to get a cup to keep until morning, they said that was a good idea!. Interestingly, the plugs were loose (not holding the power cords well). There is a difference between minimalist and cheap. The furniture falls into the latter. The staff's replies were a bit arrogant, but that may just be my interpretation. Good location, and the bed is comfortable, but for that price much better options exist.

“Was going to give it 3* but it's worth 4” Stayed here with my husband during a 4 night stay while attending a concert. I was going to give it 3 stars but realized that when rating the location, rooms and sleep quality I had to give it 4. Location terrific. Our room was very large with a super bathroom. Nice closets in the hallway with plenty of space, comfortable beds and it was quiet. Looked to be recently updated. Cons -- concierge lounge had very limited hours for us and it had the worst quality of food we've had in a lounge in a long time. The front desk staff while kind of friendly (but not necessarily welcoming) all seemed to be "filling in" from other departments and I can't say it was a smooth check-in. We had several trips to the front desk for several reasons and no one seemed to know answers. The concierge was either never there or there was a very long line. She did give us excellent tips and directions for our weekend concerts. The lobby bar was fine and the bartender was nice and late night food was good. Not a lot of late night options for a place to grab a drink in the immediate area.

“Great value for promo price in Midtown” Exceptional bedding and very comfortable new beds, internet and business center w/ printer for boarding passes a plus. Small rooms typical in size for NYC, no view. Broken coffee maker replaced upon request. Free bottled water is one bottle per day for a room accommodating up to 4 people. Dirty street, adult toy store, scaffolding acceptable tradeoff for proximity to Times Sq and Broadway. Lines to check in. Tiny congested lobby but clean and new. Friendly staff. Initially told reserved room w/ two double beds was not available and that I would have to either share a bed with my grown son or opt to have one sleep on a chaise. I pushed the issue and got the room reserved well in advance and guaranteed with a deposit. First night, maid service didn't happen until 9pm. We were told they were running a bit behind. This wasn't a horrible thing and late check out privileges more than compensated since ability to shower midday before heading out during brutal August heat wave was priceless! Floors tiny, elevators slow, everyone required to travel to the basement for ice machine. Not worth current pricing of $255 per night given immediate competition in the area with better aesthetics. Would return in a heartbeat for the promo rate.

“'Three cousins from Massachusetts'-loved The Hudson” Three of us stayed in one room for one evening. Yes, it was extremely tight and luckily none of us are large people! The room was fantastic, but very small. The experience was outstanding from locating the hotel along the street to the rooftop garden. Basically, we were there for an overnight, so didn't spend much time in the hotel/room. We purchased a bottle of wine (outside of the hotel) and enjoyed that in the lobby. The following morning, we bought our lunch at Whole Foods, which is within walking distance and enjoyed it at the rooftop garden. My cousins and I plan a trip every year for an overnight and we have been pleased with the hotels each time. I've made reservations (via Hotwire) for my daughter and myself and as luck would have it, it will be at The Hudson. She will throughly enjoy the atmosphere and happenings around the bar scene.
“Highly recommend Irish breakfast” Highly recommend the Irish or American breakfast at the Fitzpatrick. Beautiful cafe with excellent service. Excellent food, great tea. Wonderful experience.

“Dingy, Dark and Dirty” We stayed for one night in this hotel as we decided at the last minute to extend our stay for a night. We pricelined the hotel for $100, and I feel that we overpaid for what we got. In direct contrast, we stayed at the Intercontinental San Francisco for the previous two nights and what a difference. Let's just say that in shopping terms, the Intercontinental is like Saks Fifth Avenue, and the Parc 55 is like Macy's (the non-designer Alfani and INC floor). It wasn't good. I almost cried when I saw how gross the Parc 55 was in comparison to the Intercontinental. We were given a room on the 8th floor and looked out at the roof of another building. The room was very dark and had a grungy quality. For instance, the light switches were caked in dirt; the door looked yellowed (and had an old-fashioned chain security lock rather than the newer bars); and the blanket on the bed was like a yucky terrycloth towel. The decor made me want to just stay standing; I was afraid to touch anything. The couch in the room and the bed were both very hard and uncomfortable. The linens were not of high quality; the closet door was grungy and outdated. Everything about the room screamed for a makeover. It was not a pleasant place to spend your time. The clientele also left a lot to be desired. I was happy to leave the place behind after a night, and I won't be back.

“The only thing nice about this place are the building, security and location.” I was in Indy for dinner and a show with the kids. I priceline a room my offer was acceepted at the Hyatt Regency in downtown Indy for June 14, 2008. I was very pleased as I had recently stayed at a Hyatt Select south of Nashville which was fantastic. So, I get to the hotel and find out that in order to park I have to either self park for $18 or pay a valet for $25 for the night. I get to the room to look something up and the internet is $10.00 per day. I made a toll free telephone call and that was $1.00. Do you see a pattern? I hate supposedly "better" hotels that nickle and dime you to death. The building is very nice looking. Check out and check in are automated. I suppose to save on staffing and customer service. The rooms are small and almost spartan. Most hotels in the two star or better category have nicer rooms. Next, I go to shower and the water that comes out in brown and cold. I call and they tell me that they are having an issue with the water. While I shave with this filthy water, my daughter trips and hits her face on a piece of furniture. I call to the front desk and ask for help and they say that they will send security and an EMT right away. 25 minutes later, I call down and tell them to cancel the EMT and that I would take my daughter to the hospital myself. They apologized and said that the person who took the call did not take note of what room I was calling from. Maria from security then came up while I got ready to leave and she was as nice as she could be. She helped me find directions to the hospital and even had complimentary ice cream brought up for my kids by way of apology when we got back. Maria was also the only person that I had personal contact with during my entire stay. I would not stay there again.

“fabulous” The only problem here is that some of the rooms have bathrooms without a door so if you are up before your partner and want to wash up, you need to turn on the lights and they are bothered. One day, they will fix this. Otherwise, a terrific hotel.

“Everything is average except the price!” I stayed here for work and was surprised by the mediocrity of the property. The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. Everyone went the extra mile to help (When they could). However, there were several things that were downright poor: First and foremost was the gym. It is small and dark and dingy with only 7 cardiovascular machines. The TV's on several of these machines only displayed one or two channels. Second, the showers. We had about 150 in our group and for some strange reason the hotel ran out of hot water by 7 every morning. Last and most disappointing was the business center. The hotel charges $1 a page to print. No, not for high quality, high res color...that is for black and white. You can only imagine my shock when I needed to print a draft copy of my presentation that was a 100 pages. At this point I asked fro the General manager who was not available. I then left a message requesting he call me. I know your shocked to hear he did not call me back. So, to sum it up. If you want to chat with a great staff and then stay in a very average hotel that is right on top of the 101 freeway and like to wake to the roar of traffic then this is your place...but make sure you also like to be gauged!

“Another good stay!” This is a great location in the middle of Ohio for our state VFW conferences. As with other stays, the hotel staff takes wonderful care of us. I love the soap products. The rooms could use some fine tuning. The light between the beds was not plugged in and the fineal(sp?) on top of the lampshade was missing. There was a washcloth with brown stuff hidden behind a rolled up towel on the countertop in the bathroom. I checked for bed bugs and found none. Nice fluffy towels. The hospitality rooms(12 total) were located together on the first floor and the rest on 6th floor. One staff member, Levi, has been a real help with our group for the past few years. Because of the location of the two towers, it's a pain to have to take two different elevators to get around. The only elevator to the basement floor, where all the meetings were held, is the slowest in the building. I have to give a thanks to the staff at the desk. Upon leaving on a Sunday, my vehicle wouldn't start. The staff called a rental car company for me and then shuttled me to pick up a car. I left my keys with instructions at the desk and the following day, I received a call from them saying the tow truck driver had picked up the key. I'm sure our organization will be at the Ramada again in the future.

“A letdown.” The Standard is much to hip and trendy for my liking. I mean, they try too hard, some of the othe guests also try too hard, the service tries to hard, theres just so much tension! Building is lovely, really. A wonderfull highrise, boasting magnificent New Jersey and downtown views. Rooms are quirky, fun to be in, allthough not very good for a 3+ night stay. We stayed there for a week and we struggled with the lack of space for clothes, luggage, shopping, etc... The breakfast is a 25 dollar joke. Fortunately as a Tablet Plus member I had it on offer. The public areas are pretty much unexisting. The lobby is overdesigned, cold, uncomfortable, and looks like a 2001 Space Odissey dentists waiting room. The bar next door is terribly dark, and the waiters are just too ignorant. The obviously fake old New York brasserie "Standard Grill" is lacking in service but fairly competent foodwise. The Boom Boom Room is a fabulous bar and works great as the main hotel meeting place. Unfortunately it's closed for guests at night, and what could really be the absoute highlight of the property, quickly becomes it's most remarkable flaw. Every night, hotel guests returning to their rooms have to show security their key cards, being then shown the "other" elevator, as the main one is for the guests of the boom boom room. This is of course no way to treat guests. Intolerable. What can I say, gven the hype, it just had to be done. But I'm not coming back.

“A totally unexpected pleasure” From the time we were welcomed to our room by Danny, to the time we left, we felt most welcome. Danny greeted us by name each time he saw us and treated us as well as he possibly could. The hotel is very unusual and pleasing, pleasant and clean. Rooms are noise-free and large. One of the managers, Scott, was also extremely friendly and chatty at the right time. A great hotel for the discerning guest. The only thing I can fault would be the dark bathroom. Old eyes have a hard time applying makeup:)

“Sanctuary is a wonderful escape from the chaos of NYC” The Sanctuary is a very pleasant, serene hotel just minutes away from times square and the heart of the city. Upon arrival, we were immediately upgraded to a Deluxe Queen, and they fulfilled both our requests for a high floor and being away from the street. The room was very pleasant, spacious, and had a particularly clever layout. The bed was very coomfortable and spacious, and the room was bed bug free, which is extremely important and a rarity these days in NYC hotels. The only minor setback about the room (it wasn't really that bad) was that the A/C system was quite loud, but again, not a big issue! The staff were generally very friendly and attentive, and were always able to fulfill special requests. The breaakfast wasn't spectacular, but (contrary to many previous reviewers of this hotel) was very pleasant considering it was continental. The hotel is in a great location for shopping, tourist attractions, and theatre (just up the street from the TKTS booth), and is very nicely styled. Another factor that seemed to bother other reviewers was the low lighting and "nightclub feel," but this is actually quite calming and serene, especially after a day in the chaotic bright lights of Times Sqaure. In essence, this hotel is very pleasant, quite spacious, bed-bug free, has a good location, and nice, comfortable rooms. I highly reccomend it, especially to couples and tourists, and it is now very high on my list of nice hotels - and I have stayed at higher-rated hotels than this! Once again, an excellent stay!

“Fantastic Hotel in the perfect location” The Willard is a landmark hotel and has probably the best location of any of the DC high end properties. The lobby is magnificent with a long corridor from the back to the front lined with elegant decor. The rooms are good sized for a big city, comfortable bedding, nice working space and large bathroom. Service was top notch. When staying at this hotel, it is not unusual to see heightened security and what could have been Secret Service as it is a frequent destination of dignitaries. It is a short walk to the mall and the White House. Plenty of restaurants in walking distance. I did not eat at the hotel (there are two restaurants part of the complex) but did have a drink at the Round Robin & Scotch Bar - pricey, as you would expect. Did eat close to the hotel at M&S Grill (decent, not too expensive, part of the McCormick & Schmick's chain) and Chef Geoff's Downtown (had a great lunch there, nice place).\ Valet parking was $39, about what you would expect. DC is a great place and the Willard is the right choice.

“Good Value for Location” This hotel boasts a terrific location. My room was NYC-sized, but fine. It was very clean. Free internet worked well. Note that I was kicked downtown to the Club Quarters / WTC hotel my first night because of overbooking. They ordered a car and gave me some compensation, but it was a real pain with meetings scheduled in midtown. Other than that, all was great. It's not super cheap (I paid $279), but costs slightly less than I would have expected for the quality/location combination. Would stay again.

“Really enjoyable stay” Stayed in Kimpton Hotels before and this one sure no slightest disappointment. Great location, super staff making our big group check-in in a swift. Friendly front desk staff were really helpful in many occasions. Wine tasting at around 5 pm made our daily warm up great. Tried the roof top bar twice and not disappointed, great atmosphere and even more of great staff who worked more to serve us best. Rooms were great, ample space. I had slight problem with the clogged wash basin but that was very minor. Stayed on the 6th floor which was very close to the noise of the roof top bar but that was not a problem. I did not get any problem in this place and our days here passed quickly. Will no doubt consider this place first for the next SD visit. they are also dogs friendly, by the way....

“Riverwalk Convenience_DvB” I was attending a conference for school officials with late notice. The hotel at which the conference was being held was full. I do not usually pick Four Point hotels but thought this price was very reasonable. Excitingly, this property is conveniently located to allow walking to great restaurants, bars, and the Riverwalk itself. The staff was very welcoming and even provided a nice welcome gift. The rooms are spacious and clean, and I had no trouble with any aspect of the hotel.

“Great Property - Very Few Problems” I stayed at the Westin Tabor Center for three nights as part of a corporate meeting. The hotel was selected and arranged by corporate travel. Documents indicated that the room rate was $119 per night for a king room, but this may have been a special rate given the number of rooms purchased. The property is located in a clean, safe area of Denver. It is located within easy walking distance to many restaurants and attractions. The exterior is well maintained and appears secure. The lobby is a little complicated. It is a two-story affair with the main entrance and a Starbucks on the ground floor with the check-in area; concierge etc. located one level up. Check-in was flawless with everything ready upon my arrival. A bellman was happy to move luggage to the room where it was waiting following check-in. The property has obviously been remodeled and has a modern, attractive interior. The hallways are a little dark, but are easy to navigate. The room was spacious with a king bed, sitting area, work desk, wet bar and large bathroom. The room was well stocked. All room lights, and appliances worked well. Close attention had been paid to cleanliness as the room was, and continued to be, spotless. Bedding was typical for the Westin chain but I found the mattress to be too firm for my liking. The bathroom has received the upgraded dual showerhead feature, which was a nice touch. I did experience intermittent problems with the hotel’s internet system. For $11 per day on top of room charges, I expect better. In a great customer service “save”, the front desk assisted me in contacting the Help Desk. While helpful (and obviously not in New Delhi), they were unable to correct the issue. I promptly received a full credit for the length of stay. This being said, internet service at this level of property should be included. If the Holiday Inn Express can do it, surely Westin can. Food service for our entire meeting was above par for this level of property. I was pleased with the service, selection and quality of each meal. I must assume that the hotel restaurant offers the same. Check-out took thirty seconds and was just as organized as the check-in process. This area of the hotel is staffed with friendly, competent employees. This is a quality property in great town. I would recommend it.

“Excellent Service and Room” Having stayed at the Palomar DC, i already had high hopes for the Palomar SF. Although the lobby wasn't near that of the DC version, who really cares about a lobby in a boutique hotel? Besides, the 5th Floor restaurant lounge area kicked major @ss over anything at the DC Palomar. Very swank and innovative how it is placed amidst the rooms of the 5th floor. Very neat. The staff (especially Lauren) were uber friendly and knowledgeable. The wine hour was great. The free internet and USA Today were major plusses. I got a super rate of $143 during the work week!! I took advantage of the $15/night upgrade (if available...and it was my week), and glad I did. I got an oversized room overlooking Ellis St. on the 8th floor. The room was very comfortable and the bed one of the best I've stayed in since the Ritz-Carlton St. Louis. It made it very difficult to get up for work in the morning!! Overall, a terrific stay and I would definitely stay here again!

“way better than expected” Having been to NY before in a more expensive hotel, but this time on a budget, we weren't so sure what to expect. Coming from JFK airport, the shuttle didn't even want to go to West 20th, said he was 'limited' to 25th. After negociation he would drop us in front of Chelsea Lodge after all. It's in a charming, relatively quiet street with trees. In a safe neighborhood near the gay community, which was not a problem for my gfirlfriend and I. If you're homophobic then you may want to avoid the area. But we found the people very friendly. Then we entered the building. First impression was the smell of... clean laundry. I like it. The lady at the desk gave us the keys. The room, upstairs, was just what we needed. Small but clean and comfortable. It has a shower cabin and a sink inside the room, and paintings of ancient america's settlers. There were two toilets in the corridor, which are cleaned regularly and were never occupied. The staff is distant but friendly when approached. There are many (asian, italian) restaurants, a supermarket at the corner, and murray's bagels for breakfast. Can't beat that. The subway is one a half blocks away. Conclusion: Why pay more? Chelsea Lodge's got all you need for a wonderful stay in NYC.

“Rooms could use a makeover, lobby is nice.” Stayed here this week (10/29). Have stayed many times here but like the W NYC, the rooms could use some updating. The lobby is very cozy, staff are relatively friendly and notice you when you walk through the lobby. The rooms have the nasty brown duvets that I cannot imagine get washed each and every time a guest leaves. The walls are paper thin and I heard a couple getting it on next door. They went out partying and I woke up at 3 am to hear their ridiculous radio thumping and I assume more getting it on. I called the front desk but nothing was done. I might return, but Seattle seems to be getting some cool boutique hotels that will give this place a run for its money unless they step up their game.

“NYC - Normal rules don't apply!” If this were anywhere else, I'd be giving it a lower rating, but New York is New York. Even by European standards, New York hotel rooms tend towards the small side, so the rooms at the Marquis are comfortably large. When you add to that an outstanding view of Times Square then there is more than enough to compensate for: - a hotel that needs substantial remodelling and refurnishing to drag it out of the 1980s - a bar that we left after no service for 10 minutes - slow and expensive Internet - coming back one day at 16:50 to find the room had still not been serviced - check out where the desk staff don't bother asking how your stay was (at least the bell man did!) Notwithstanding these gripes, we enjoyed our stay. Though the room (Concierge King) was outdated it was clean, large and the bed was comfortable, and the location of the hotel is a central as you could hope for. We put up with this, at a not insubstantial cost, because it's New York! If we'd been in Vegas I would not have expected to pay more than $70 (if at all) for this standard of room. We did not eat in the hotel - there are far too many other options in this city.

“Great location” This hotel is in a great location. Plenty of dining options in the area. 3 separate METRO stations within a 2 block radius. The room was very spacious & clean. The bathroom was small but adequate. Room lacked black out curtains but we were never awaken by the sunlight. I hope I can find another deal like this next time we visit DC. ($60/night)

“Cramped, noisy and convenient” The Sherriff and his lady have sampled quite a few Holiday Express hotels in the last year. They seem to fall into two types - relatively new and rather soulless out-of-town properties with ample space, parking, etc. and rehabbed older properties in city centres. This is one of the latter - and not the best of its kind. When giving the old Hotel Cass a makeover, it seems there was no real attempt to rethink the internal layout or accommodations so that a veneer of modernization has been slapped on a rather tired property. Our room was very cramped with virtually no wardrobe or storage space, which meant we were falling over our own suitcases all the time and the bed was pushed right up to a wall with not much in the way of lighting. Chicago was pretty hot but the air-conditioner was so noisy that we couldn't run it - although the windows did open and we were able to get enough ventilation without street noise. This is a quiet property in that sense but the sound insulation between rooms and corridors was poor and other guests caused a fair bit of disturbance just coming and going. The decor verged on the shabby, although relatively new. On the positive side, we enjoyed one of the best complimentary breakfasts we have had with this chain, the staff were bouncing with enthusiasm to help us make the best of our stay - and a little disappointed that we were such old Chicago hands that we didn't need much help - and the location is brilliant, just a couple of blocks off Michigan Avenue and very close to the subway.

“good value, good location” Booked at the Affinia after debating many different hotels and booking/cancelling somewhere else. At first we were disappointed that our room was on the 3rd floor (we'd requested a higher floor in hopes of avoiding street noise) but our room was very quiet even though we faced the street and were across from the elevators. Our sink and tub flowed very slowly the 1st day, but we notified the desk staff and it was immediately fixed. The "club" feature was nice, as we left our luggage with the staff on the last day, but went back and freshened up, got some coffee, etc., before catching a cab to our late afternoon flight. Every time we approached the staff, from front desk to doorman to concierge, we were served quickly with a great attitude. Everyone was very accomdating. Rooms were very comfortable, terrific beds, tiny but functional and nice bathroom, and convenient to have all amenities (shampoo, toothpaste, etc., even breath mints!) provided what with airline restrictions. In-room coffee and tea were a nice touch, too. We would definitely stay again.

“キャピトル(議事堂)は徒歩で行けるし、他の観光スポットも歩いて行ける” 家族で2部屋予約、スイートとメンバー用の部屋、部屋がそれぞれに違う棟にあり合流するのには不便、フロントが近い部屋を本来アレンジ出来ると思うが、フロントのスタッフの対応も人により格差がある。 スイートの部屋は前の宿泊者の忘れ物がカーテンの下にあったり、深夜まで騒音が他の部屋からして古いせいかうるさかった。メンバーラウンジは飲み物サービスとかコンチネンタル朝食のサービスはあるが狭いのでのんびりと出来ない。 車はバレットだったので、出庫されるのに時間が掛かるので早めにリクエストしたほうが賢明。 キャピトルの内部見学を初めてしてみたがお勧めです、ホテルから歩いてすぐなので早見に行くと行列の少ない。他の美術館など、徒歩圏内、Union Stationも近い。

“I'd give it a solid "B", maybe even a B+” Good location, clean public and private areas, (mostly) friendly staff, decent rate. Good-sized room. Stayed here for a weekend with my adult daughters for a "girls getaway". Enjoyed the proximity to the lake, Mag Mile, Navy Pier area, and eateries. We usually shop a fair amount when in Chi, but because we hit a fabulous stretch of weather we spent a lot of time at the beach, which was a nice change (and cheaper!). It's only a few blocks to Lake Michigan. We also enjoyed having a bite to eat and a drink at the rooftop pool - quite a large pool, clean, heated, nice for sunbathing. Good "perk". This is a "tourist class" hotel but one of the better ones IMO. I've not had good luck with Doubletree in the past, but this one was pretty nice. I was satisfied with the value for the dollar.

“Room somewhat small but nice!” Hotel lobby looked really new. Staff was really nice. We got a king guest room which is somehwat smaller than other hotels I think but the room is nice. It looks like the ones in the pictures of the website although slightly smaller. The bathroom is big but does not have a bathtub. Free breakfast does not really have hot food but does have some Asian offerings (Miso soup, noodles). Did not have any problems with noise! Walls feel nice and solid.

“A Perfectly Acceptable Downtown Business Hotel” The Charlotte City Center Hilton is in a great downtown location, near great restaurants and bars. The hotel is large and clean, and the staff engaged and helpful. I have no complaints, though there is nothing particularly outstanding either. I would have no problem staying here again while on business in Charlotte.

“Nice hotel for a business trip” I stayed here for 4 nights in June for a business trip. The room and was very nice and comfortable. There was a nice chair to relax in at the end of the day. Very busy area. There are some nice places to check out nearby like the Reading Terminal Market, Hard Rock Cafe and the Liberty Bell. The neighborhood is a little iffy...a lot of major stores (like Macy's nearby) close at 5 or 6pm. There's also a pharmacy nearby on Market street where you can pick up some items if need be. I liked the restaurant for breakfast as well as having the option of a starbucks in the lobby. My only complaint would be the internet charges - at 12.99 plus tax per day that seemed a bit steep to me. Other Marriott properties I've stayed at don't charge at all. Overall a good option if you need to be in that area for business.

“Very comfortable and friendly hotel” I like NYC very much, it's the most European like city in the US, and the Upper West Side with the Beacon Hotel is a charming part of NYC's atmosphere. The museums, cafes, restaurants, foodstores, travel agencies, boutiques, Central Park, subway stations, - just a step out of the hotel. I stayed at the Beacon - very comfortable hotel with friendly staff - for one week in July 2001. I'm planning to visit NYC this summer and to book a room at the Beacon Hotel again. I'm happy that almost three years after my previous stay the visitors of the TripAdvisor still rank the hotel very, very high. And surely it deserves that!

“Lovely decor downstairs but only decent rooms” Like many of the hotels in the area, I would imagine, Hotel Adagio is an older building that has been updated, at least on the surface. The front desk, downstairs lobby, bar area and computer room are beautifully decorated but the rooms are rather simple, albeit clean and comfortable. The bathroom sink drained very slowly and we were on the go so much we did not ask for them to fix it, which I assume they would have. At one point, the toilet simply did not flush but kicked into action about 15 minutes later. All of these things I imagine are indicative of older plumbing. Again, everything was functional, but definitely not luxurious. One thing that bugged me about the rooms are that there are no drawers anywhere. There is a closet space where you can hide your suitcase but we were there for three days and it is my personal preference to kind of move in when I stay anywhere more than a day or two.
