Lastly, one morning we woke up and headed out around 8 or 9am, we returned to the room around 1 and no one had been up to clean the room. We stayed in the room for a few hours and then, upon leaving, my husband asked the front desk for "turndown service". He misspoke as they don't do turndown service, but when we returned later that night, we still had not received any maid service. We were not clear in asking for the hotel to fix some of the problems we ran into, so I cannot dock them too much for these things as they were not given a chance to make them better. Nonetheless, it would have been nice if they hadn't been problems to begin with. As for location, the hotel is about a five minute walk from Union Square which is the hub for a lot of transportation options and the beginning of a long shopping stretch. Having stayed closer to Union Square before, the street noise at Hotel Adagio was much less and the rooms much quieter. All in all, this is a nice base for exploring the city. Breakfast is available for a reasonable price although there is also a cute diner across the street. There are several computers available for use, although there is a fee. The bar area is a nice little place to enjoy happy hour. The rooms include a comfortable bed and the basics. The room we were in was no frills and its age crept through, but it was quiet and the beds were comfortable.

“Met our needs but some problems” We got this hotel through a $75 bid on priceline on Labor Day weekend. We had attended a wedding in DE and decided to make a quick trip to Washington since I had only been once and my wife had never been. The hotel was in a good central location between the white house, the monuments, the museum, the capitol, and the restaurants downtown. We ate and watched some football at the ESPN Zone which is only a few blocks away. We were able to walk to all the attractions although my wife ended up complaining after a few miles on each day. There is plenty of local transportation if you're not up for the walk. The hotel room was clean and the hotel lobby was very nice. There were a few restaurants within the hotel. Parking was $27/night for valet and $22/night for self park. We had a problem the first night since they gave us a room near the elevator on the 15th floor and every time the elevator passed by there was a strange moaning sound that was quite annoying. We called and complained and were moved to a room away from the elevator and were told that the noise was a problem they were aware of but had been unable to remedy. We found it kind of strange that we were told that we were given a "quiet" room when we first checked in without even asking for one and then afterwards were told that they were aware of the noise issue. But the 2nd room they gave us was much better and faced the outside of the hotel. The bathroom was somewhat small and did not have a fan so it steamed up pretty quickly. The hotel seems more adequate for business travel with one occupant per room than for families. Overall the hotel met our needs but the noise issue really bothered us and we would not stay there again.

“Enjoyed the stay” I did not have a pet but enjoyed meeting all the pets that were staying here and the attention they received by the hotel. I loved having a goldfish in my room too! My room was small but clean and worked out ok. I was there 8 days so I would have liked a larger space. There was nowhere to sit except at the desk or on the bed and that was a pain for such a long stay. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean and in good shape. The evening 'reception' was always well attended and pleasant except there were always so many people that I never did get an appetizer the whole time I was there. The location is convenient to 16th St. Mall shopping and not too bad a walk to the Convention Center. The fitness center was very small but never crowded and the machines were in good shape and clean.

“Grand!!!!” I stay here each time I come to San Diego. It just keeps geting better and better! Bar on top of hotel has amazing view. Staff is very friendly. Rooms were beautiful and large. One of the best Hyatt'sI have ever stayed in--it has the air of Four Seasons, but a much better value!

“Very Comfortable Stay” My wife and I stayed at the W for a weekend vacation. The room is well appointed with softer-than-usual carpeting, a very plush bed, and the inviting window seat. The flat screen TV was nice, but the picture was fuzzy, as if it was receiving the signal from rabbit ears. The shower was attractive, but not very practical. A single, unmovable glass pane divides off the shower, but a hole in the glass (so that you can turn on the water without entering the shower first) allows water to go everywhere in the bathroom when you're in the shower. The pool area is nice, but tiny. The pool itself is roughly 15 feet by 25 feet. There is room for only 5 or so lounge chairs, and the open-air fitness area is nearby. All in all, though, it was a nice place to relax for an hour. The location is very convenient to the trolley and bus to the airport. While we like the location of the Omni hotel better, if we hadn't stayed at the W, we wouldn't have found St. Tropez, a french bistro (highly recommended for breakfast and lunch). Overall, we were very happy with the W, and even happier with our rate from Priceline (I don't think you can go wrong with any 4-star hotel in downtown San Diego)!

“Beautiful hotel: not quite what you would expect from a W.” When I think of the W hotel chain, I think of sleek, trendy and modern. The new W in Washington DC is all these things but it also retains the charm and elegance of the Washington Hotel which pre-dated the W. I was visiting this property for a site tour and was surprised by the architectural detail which normally is missing from the W hotels. Fire places are found in the most unexpected places and the rooms while not quite spacious are more than sufficient. Be sure to check out the view from the bar at the top of the hotel which provides excellent views of D.C. including the White House.
“Solid hotel choice” Nice hotel, Clean, efficient and well-located. Very close to the convention center. Service was great and front desk was helpful. A good choice for a business hotel.

“Can expect good things at Springhill Suites” Springhill Suites is my favorite Marriott "chain." The rooms are clean, comfortable, and roomy. The staff here, as usual, was efficient and accommodating. Check-in was speedy and when a group came in, a second desk staffer jumped in to keep things moving. Having traveled far, I was glad to be able to have a take out from nearby Olive Garden to have in the room. Their breakfasts and happy hours are good, too.

“Good hotel, central location!” I stayed here for a conference in 2003. Since I just recently joined Tripadvisor, I thought I should offer my two cents to members on this one! The Swissotel Chicago is a great property for business, leisure and individual travelers. It is centrally located, and their staff is knowledgeable and able to provide you with very good ideas on activities as well we good input on where to dine, etc. We had a very enjoyable conference and I still have a vivid memory of the entire stay, though it has been a while since I have visited. Taking Swissotel ́s operating standards into consideration, I am pretty sure that the service, quality and value provided than is still the same, or even improved to date. I would definitely stay here again if happen to return to Chicago.

“Good hotel” We stayed here while in Austin for a family get together over the holiday. We weren't particular about which hotel we stayed in so we Pricelined downtown hotels. Glad we got the Omni. The friendly receptionist recommended an atrium view for a quieter room which was perfect. It was roomy, well-furnished, spacious and spotless. The bed was very comfortable. This is an attractive hotel with a huge atrium where the bar and restaurant are situated. Valet parking is $25, self-park is $18 in the parking below the hotel which is conveniently reached by an elevator in the lobby. We joined the loyalty program and got free wifi. We would stay again.

“Decent Hotel, Nothing Around It” If you're not going to a game, you may want to look elsewhere. This hotel is nice. But there is nothing around it. There is an overpriced steakhouse next door, and some cafes that look abandoned. Manly baseball theme everywhere. However nice Aveda toiletries. Getting in touch with their "accounting department" to get a check-out receipt is like pulling teeth. Very poor service. They don't do a check-out receipt under the door. Overall nice accomodations, but they take themselves too seriously.

“A predictably superb stay” The location is ideal — on Market Street, a few minutes from Union Square. The view from your room through those massive windows is everything you can imagine. Most important of all is that, in keeping with the Four Seasons philosophy, the lovely hotel offers a civilized stay. From the pleasantness of the people at reception to the friendliness of the chambermaids, to the warmth of the bar and restaurant staff, this is a hotel eager to guarantee you a comfortable, enjoyable experience. And unlike some so-called luxury hotels, there is no pretentiousness or snobbery here. The bedrooms are comfortable, functional and tastefully appointed. There is a work area and easy chair with proper lighting for reading and recreation. The room safe is unusually large. The bathrooms are marble and well-stocked with soaps and shampoo etc. The bathtub looks luxurious, a temptation to anyone in the mood for a long soak, and the lavatory and shower sensibly occupy separate alcoves. My single experience of room service was excellent. I used the restaurant for breakfast and when I ordered pancakes, the waiter suggested I might want the short stack rather than the full amount. I took his advice, the serving was ample, and I was impressed by the fact that he went out of his way to make a useful suggestion. This is a hotel in which everything meshes exquisitely.

“Good, If you have business at McCormick Place” Spent two nights here for a trade show. The upside first, hotel is clean, my room offered a pretty nice view of Lake Michigan, the bed was quite comfy, the staff was nice, and it is attached to the convention center. The downside, there is nothing to do around this hotel and it is about a 10 to 20 minute cab ride from downtown depending on time of day, the hotel is in a tough neighborhood, if fact I advise people do not go outside at night except to get a cab. There is no need to go outside between the convention center and the hotel since they are attached and well secured. I was also pretty surprised to see a $9.95 per day fee to use the internet. In 2008 you would think this would be included in the room rate especially at $275.00 per night.

“One of a kind experience in a Texas classic” I stayed at the Driskill on Easter weekend because of a special rate they offered for using an AmEx. The bottom line is that it was worth every penny. The service of the hotel was exemplary and just what I would have expected from a top notch hotel. I specifically mention the concierge (I believe Christine was her name) who helped us out on a couple of occasions promptly and always with a smile. I also commend the valets for having our car ready within the 10-15 minute window they ask you to call ahead. My only complaint with respect to service came when we had breakfast at the cafe on our last day. The croissant I ordered was terrible and overpriced and the waitress short changed me. I also asked the hostess to call ahead to the valet, but somehow she did not know the number and then brushed me off when a call came in. I felt both of these incidents were unacceptable and registered my complaint. As for the room, we had a standard room. The decor was beautiful with a great balance of old and new. The bathroom was tiny, which I read about in other reviews, but I expected it and it did not bother me much. We had no problem with noise, despite having a room overlooking 6th street. All in all a wonderful experience and I would definitely consider staying again.

“N.Y. city's best kept secret!” I couldn't have been happier for choosing to stay at the Affinia Shelburne. This was my first time visiting N.Y. for vacation purposes and I my hotel experience was great. I would highly recommend this hotel to all. Read below for more information on how I rate this hotel. Location: One of the big reasons this hotel has so much charm is because of the quiet, clean, and quaint neighborhood it is located in. Traffic noise in this neighborhood is surprisingly quiet, so nights are very relaxing. Just walking distance from the hotel you will find the Empire State building, Grand Central Station, Chrysler building, Madison Square Park, and the N.Y. Clock Tower. There is also a ton of shopping that is walking distance (about a mile) such as H&M, American Eagle, Uniqlo, Levis, the largest Macy's in the world, and more. Rooms: Either this is a new hotel, newly renovated, or just very well taken care of. The room decor and furniture is very nice and clean. The room size is larger than normal especially for N.Y. hotels which is a big plus in my book. Beds are California King size and very comfortable. There are 6 different pillow choices that they let you choose from. Plenty of desk space. A small chase lounge couch. Small refrigerator. Bathroom is small but clean. Toilets are new and will not clog on you or make loud noises while refilling. Bathtub included which is also a rarity in N.Y. hotel rooms. And lastly, what ranks high for me is the water pressure on the shower head. The shower head has great water pressure! Yay! **Oh I forgot to mention, the soap and shampoo products are made by Philosophy!! Restaurant & Bar: The bar was nice but didn't spend too much there. The restaurant was very good. It had a dark and romantic feel to it. The food was spectacular! When I checked in, they told me that they were rated by the New York Times as having the best burger in New York. I thought, "Really? in a hotel restaurant?" I had to try this famous burger for myself and I have to say that it definitely was a fantastic burger and awesome fries too. Staff: Staff is very profession and courteous. They are very attentive and friendly. Staff all around from the bell hop to the waiter/waitress to the maids are grade A. Andy at the front desk, you rock brotha! Other: Rooftop garden is very cool during the day and night. You really get a great view from up there. The gym is located on the 2nd floor and is free of charge. It is modern and clean. All the equipment is in working condition. You will find all the basics here. Conclusion: I will definitely return to the Affinia in the future. I have already recommended it to friends and family. You just don't find hotels like this in N.Y. without paying a fortune. The Affinia is fairly priced and I believe you get more from the hotel than you pay for. Great find!

“Mixed review” Upon arrival to the W for a bachelorette weekend, I was immediately happy to be greeted by the wonderful candle scents that the W is famous for. After a long trip from the east coast the scent was enough to make me feel at ease. However, as I put my bags down to wait for the rest of the girls to arrive I was dismayed by the worn furnishings in the lounge area. Some of the couches and ottomans need to be replaced and I was disappointed that they were there for guests to see. That being said the rest of the experience was steller. We requested connected rooms but did not recieve them although we had been told at the front desk that the rooms were connecting. The rooms were certainly next to each other but not connected as we had been told. The conceirge was outstanding and recommended Amber for a great Indian dinner. He booked a fantastic last minute reservation for us there and hands down it was the best Indian cuisine we had ever had before. The front desk staff was very polite and courteous. The restaurant on site was great for breakfast. The service was slow however but our waiter accomodated us when we asked for our food to be packed up as we were headed to Napa and were on a schedule. You have to allow more than an hour to eat in the restaurant. We returned the next day for breakfast when we had more time and enjoyed it very much. We found the prices reasonable and the portions plentiful. The rooms are okay. I think the W is still figuring out its clientele. We were a young group but are in our early 30s and late 20s so did not find the dorm room decorations appealing. We kept joking that it looked like a college dorm. The water pressure in the shower left much to be desired. We were staying in a room which can hold four people (there were only three of us in the room), yet there were not enough face cloths and wash cloths in the rooms. The maid service was good in that unlike other hotels they did not come around bothering us early in the morning. The on site gym was pretty decent and included free ear buds for the equipment televisions. Too bad we did not notice the ear buds until we were leaving the gym. There needs to be a better indication that they are there. There is a night life at the hotel but we never hung out there but there was always a crowd when we returned each evening. Overall the stay was good but I can not rave about the hotel the way I had hoped too and I certainly would not reccomend it to couples or groups. Lastly, the hotel is very accessible from the BART (about 3 blocks away).

“*Horrible* experience” The hotel itself is nice. Convenient location, nice rooms, comfortable and clean. However, the stay was a nightmare. I arrived at about 9 PM to check in, and they told me that they didn't have my room ready and that it would be 30 minutes or so. They gave me a $10 coupon for the bar. Okay, not too terrible... 10 PM rolls around and they still don't have a room. Come 11:30 PM, I'm getting pretty annoyed. They wouldn't put me up at another hotel (and I had pre-paid through Expedia) or accommodate me in any way. I didn't get a room until 1:30 AM. They didn't offer any kind of compensation. They wouldn't even refund the cost of the room for that night! Outrageous!

“Fine overall ...could have better windows to reduce outside noise” Staying here right now Couldn't sleep well two nights. The windows don't block all outside noise. Today I moved to a higher floor. Still can hear the noise. Unfortunately they cannot move me elsewhere because they don't have the same type of room. Paid good money for this one though Staff are very friendly. Rooms are nice and clean. I have a petite queen size room. Its really petite!!! Did not try restaurant or the lounge. Nice location Overall its a good place to stay.

“Second visit was also very pleasant” A mid-week business conference brought me to Indianapolis for the second time in 3 months. I was more than happy to again select the Hilton Garden Inn as an alternative to the property where the conference was being held - a larger newer hotel. I was able to check in early which was extremely helpful because of the midday start of the conference. The complementary breakfast coupons made it convenient to get a quick and nutritious meal to begin each busy day. My experience included a nice, clean room, easy to access free wifi, and very responsive room service. The staff, especially those in food service were very friendly and accommodating.

“Interesting, but don't look too hard for quality.” Having stayed at W Hotels in Sydney (now called Blue), Los Angeles and New York, I was looking forward to my 3 nights at the Chicago version. Based on the previous stays, this one simply fails to meet the standard. Staff are eager to please, but the place itself is a let-down. Room decor was trendy 10 years ago, about the same time as the noisy air-con units were last serviced I think. Rooms are small, poorly maintained (eg wet stain on carpet on arrival) and generally "tired". So, is the hotel chic? Hardly. Chic is more than decor, it is the guests as well. Sharing a lift with a drunken guy in cut-off jeans maybe considered chic in Chicago, I have no idea, but not my idea at all.
“Extremely nice hotel” Very nice and clean hotel! Great location for shopping ladies!! Macy's around the corner and the mall is 1 block down.

“Nice area, easy to get to” Stayed at the Omni in DC for the first time November 15 and 16. The hotel itself is impressive and historic. From the moment you step into the entrance it seems like a special place. Like most DC hotels, the rooms are small and a bit sparse but clean and comfortable. The Omni Shoreham also has free wireless internet in the rooms, which is becoming the deciding factor for the business traveler. There were several international travelers staying there along with older tourists and conference goers. There are swankier hotels to be had in DC for a lower price, but for the regular traveler who is accustomed to staying in these types of hotels, you will not be disappointed. Exploring the stores and restaurants nearby was one of the best parts of the trip

“Just like the other reviewers!” Palomar is located right off N 75,I exited Mockingbird Lane and almost missed it. as it is right off the Freeway....even though it is right off Freeway it was very quiet. Great air conditioning, quiet and personal. Robes are fun. I ordered Room Service twice and it was at my room within 15 minutes...Not cheap, but tasty. I have booked the Palomar in Washington DC for a christmas trip and had decided that depending on how things go in the Dallas Palomar, I may change my decision on Washington, but I will keep my reservation. Good Find!

“Another good experience - on the whole!” Become a big of a regular here. Its the 5th time I've stayed in the last few months. Lets face it - this a budget hotel and I don't expect anything other than a clean comfortable room and high speed internet access. It provides this and more. The hotel looks and feels clean and well maintained. The rooms are clean, comfortable and everything works. The free internet access (wifi) works perfectly. Generally I find the staff friendly and helpful. The courtesy bus to & from the airport is prompt and efficient - when they don't 'forget' you called that is. This last trip was the 1st time this has happened and apparently the lady behind the desk failed to inform the shuttle driver I was waiting (the shuttle doesn't just come round - you have to call) so after 20 mins I called again and eventually (after 35mins wait) the shuttle appeared. To be fair they did apologise (after I complained to anyone who would listen) and give me a 'goody' bag - I'd rather not have waited though. So, my advice, if the shuttle isn't with you in 10 mins, call again and keep calling. The free breakfast is limited to cereals, bagels, other bits & juice and coffee but is perfectly adequate. Small gym with a jogger, two bikes and some free weights. Pool and spa. The Ruby Tuesdays just across the road provides a bar and menu for evening meals. Sure its a bit isolated (your choices without a car are Ruby Tuesdays or a restaurant in the nearby Courtyard apparently - haven't tried that) and I wouldn't want to spend days there but for an overnight at the start or end of trip it is fine. I'll be happily staying there again.

“A long weekend in San Diego” I met a group of friends in San Diego. We booked the Sofia. $99 per night for a room with one or two queen beds, $149 per night for a suite. The rooms are very small, so the suite worked best for those who were sharing. Good value . What we liked: front desk staff: very nice and accomodating amenities: great linens and free bottled water, microwaves, fridge and coffee maker in room (7/11 nearby)free internet in lobby and three computers plus a printer for guest use beds: VERY nice, quite comfortable Rooms are as noted very compact. They are well decorated and efficiently planned. The curtains are heavy and I was never disturbed by street noise (room 304) Common areas are well decorated and make great conversation areas (despite the Christmas decor which is still up...a little wierd but tasteful) Walking tour offered for free on Sat and Sunday morning. Excellent, just over an hour touring the Gaslamp district, Embarcadero and waterfront. Very well done. Location: It was very easy to walk to shops , restaurants, and clubs. Train and trolley very near by. Taxis always at the stand. On site restaurant, Currant, and the bar: Loved this. The bar is very attractive, albeit rather noisy when the Charger fans are in high gear. Good happy hour. The dinner at the restaurant was excellent. We had the breakfast buffet every morning. Good strong coffee, house made pastries of extremely high quality, fresh berries, melon and pineapple, house made granola and french toast, and yogurt for $9.99. Perfect for us. Restaurant staff is very good, well informed, courteous and helpful. What we didn't like: Housekeeping, capricious at best. Some days they came, some days they didn't. I left most mornings by 7 and twice returned to change for dinner around 6 and the room had not been cleaned. Several of our group had delayed checkin and two were checked into rooms which had not been cleaned. (there are some management issues at the hotel, staff communication is not good. Checkout was slow for several people.) Bathrooms: nearly all of us commented on this. They don't have a complete shower closure, a half wall of glass in the European style which yielded a wet (as in soaking) floor after showers The bathroom door is a sliding glass (frosted) door which never fully shuts. Not a good thing in a shared room. No exhaust fan. The sink is on a stand outside the bathroom and is sloped so that if the water comes on a bit fast it will slosh all over the floor. The best thing about the hotel is the very pleasant and accomodating front desk, in particular, Brian. The worst thing about the hotel is housekeeping. Although the rooms were well cleaned, the problem was they were slow and not consistent. Also small maintenance issues which housekeeping should note and have resolved before check in of the next guest weren't addressed.

“Loud train and very dated room” Got to the hotel at midnight after a very long cab line at airport and no cabs. Hotel offered no assistance or advice whatsoever when I called from the airport wondering what to do. Was then awakened the next morning at 4:45 am by what sounded like a train literally coming through the hotel. Train's horn blew for over 20 minutes straight at nearly point blank range. As soon as the train sound stopped at 5:10 am, the phone rang with my wake-up call. Fine, they can't control the trains. Whatever. They can control the rooms, though. And this room in the Harbor Tower looked like any Best Western or La Quinta we have stayed in on the road through Wyoming and Nevada. Cheap polyester thin quilts on the bed. Late 70's early 80's dark wood decor. Worn sink and bathroom tile. Not worth 1/3 of the $349 my company was charged to put me here. If I had arrived earlier in the evening, I would have switched hotels. I called down to the front desk to ask if there were any more updated rooms - maybe in the newer tower - she said no they all look this way. Wow. This hotel has a beautiful lobby and wonderful bar area and great water location - rooms and train noise obviously make this a place to avoid for sleeping over. Avoid.

“Basic, but good” I booked this hotel with a little trepidation because it's been at least 20 years since I had a good experience with a Ramada Inn. Usually they're a bit shabby. However, all the usual mid-range hotels I like to stay at (Courtyard, Hampton) were either booked solid or $600/night, so I gave this one a shot. This hotel is pretty good. It's not luxury, but the room was spotless, the furnishings recent, the Tempurpedic bed was comfortable, and the room was fairly quiet once you turned on the air conditioning. I have no real complaints. Like pretty much everything in New York, this is an older building that has been refurbished. I had a room with one queen bed, which was a little claustrophobic, but the closet was big enough to put my luggage in there so I wouldn't trip over it. WiFi Access is free and works well. (Call the front desk to get the password to login.) The shower controls are a little tricky. As you turn the knob at first, it goes from cold to lukewarm to no water, back to cold-ish. If you stop at the lukewarm before you hit the spot where the water stops, you'll get a surprise when the water heats up! The trick is to open the valve all the way and wait for the water to heat - it will be cold at first, but will be perfect in a couple of minutes. I'm not sure if every room is like this, but it's what I experienced in mine. The neighborhood is great - very residential. You feel like you're living in New York walking through this neighborhood, not like you're a tourist. The hotel serves a free continental breakfast if you want to carbo load on bagels, donuts, and cereal. There is a coffee shop next door to the lobby that serves eggs, and the excellent Murray Hill Diner is a couple of blocks away on Lex if you'd like something else. I'd stay here again. I'm still a little skittish on Ramada Inns in general, but this is a good one.

“Central Location, Perks and Price” Central Location, Perks and Price In the many times I have been to San Diego, this was our first at this hotel and in this neighborhood (Liberty Station). The price is reasonable, accommodations clean and location central to everything. Some Highlights/Things to Know: *Free parking and plenty of it. Not the case in downtown yet you have such quick access to downtown and Seaport Village via N. Harbor Drive (for those not familiar with the area, many GPS will route you back to I-5 to get downtown, don’t follow that, much quicker and prettier to drive back around the airport and bay front). *Free internet (wires and wireless), High Def Flat Screens, very workable desks with lots of plugs and lighting. *Great running/walking trails and parks right outside your door. *Well equipped exercise room (yes it’s on the smaller side but they really make good use of the space and give you everything you need). *No in-room safe. *Not all rooms have balconies but all have opening windows, I would definitely try and get a balcony room, however, so you can sit out and enjoy the weather (albeit small, probably 2 people max). *Good common areas (especially the outdoor space). *A few restaurants in the immediate area (walking distance). A mix of options, nothing I would call a culinary sensation but good for families (i.e. Thai Place, Sports Bar/Restaurant, Sushi, Subway, Fast Food Mexican). Trader Joe’s in the hood as well as a Von’s (I would walk there but most would probably call it a 2-3 min drive). *My room seemed a little more wear and tear than I would expect for a newer hotel, however, this place is popular and the wear was fairly minor (i.e. some nicked furniture, a stain on the couch). *Housekeeping is good, place was clean and refreshed well. Bathrooms were especially kept very clean. *Pool and spa were well maintained and just the right temperatures. *Noise level – lots of reviewers speak of this, yes you are in the flight path but I never heard it inside and even outside, it was not disrupting to the peaceful feeling of the location. I only once heard a neighbor (and it was a full house) but for the most part never heard people in halls, or elevators opening, etc. *Self valet service so if you have lots of luggage, grab a luggage cart from the front desk. *The location is central with good access to all the places you probably want to see and the immediate area feels safe but as in any large city, you can go a short distance and be in a great area or a not-so-great one. You can always ask, however, as the staff is happy to help (we especially cared about this for long runs in the early AM and wanted to make sure we stayed in the better areas). *Hotel crowd seems to be mostly families or business /military folks, no groups of young partiers (like you see in Gaslamp or some of the Beach Areas). So for us, that’s great. If you like the nightlife scene, consider Pacific Beach or Gaslamp. Have fun and enjoy your SD visit!

“I'll take my history at a museum, please.” Traveled to Chicago for two nights on business, and arrived at the Palmer House around 10pm. HHonors Desk was closed, but was checked in quickly nonetheless. This hotel boasts that it is the oldest continuously operating hotel in the country. The first room I was checked into must have been the oldest continuously operating room in the hotel! It looked like it hadn't been renovated in about 20 years (the green tile in the bathroom was quite charming... really.) and had a lovely view of an A/C compressor that was bigger than my room! Went back to the reception desk, and asked if an HH Gold upgrade to the exec floor upgrade was available. Was upgraded to exec floor, to a room with one double bed. Room was nicer than the last one, but you couldn't have parked a Yugo in there with enough room to open the doors! Stay was pleasant enough afterwards. A bit noisy during the night. Lobby is undergoing renovations. Exec lounge was fine. Not bad for a business trip, but next time I'll be staying somewhere that has a bit less "history" in my room!

“A good choice - small and older but well kept” Not bad and a good break from the standard Marriotts and Hyatts. A smaller hotel and it feels it - positively so. There are no large impersonal conventions here. The rooms are smaller but well kept; room service is prompt and the food good; front desk service good; bell service spotty - it is not staffed as heavily as the larger hotels and it shows. Internet is free - bravo for that. Location is excellent just at the north side of the loop and close to Mi Ave,.

“Great location, odd room” I stayed here for only one night while traveling by myself. Upon check in, I was told I was upgraded to a suite, which got me excited. However, when I went to the suite, it was sort of creepy and inappropriate for a solo traveler! It was essentially a one-bedroom duplex apartment, with the first floor as a living area and kitchen and the second floor the bedroom and bathroom. Not only was I left to lug my huge suitcase up the stairs, not realizing I was getting a 2 story room, it was just eerie being in that huge, poorly lit room alone. The front desk should've realized this before putting me in that room... It would've been better-suited for a group of even 3-4 travelers! The room itself showed lots of wear (marks, chips, and dents in the walls, counters, and furniture; dirty, worn beige carpet) and was very blandly decorated (everything was brown or beige). There was nothing on the walls or tables. The room phone looked like it was from 1986. The bathroom mat was ratty on the edges and worn flat. The great thing about my room was the view of the market and water. It almost made up for all the rest of the things I mentioned above. It's obvious this hotel's location is its draw, and, if that's your main concern, I would recommend you absolutely stay here.

“Good location if you want to stay near Times Square” We spent one night here in July. The location is very close to Times Square. The hotel was ok, the front desk staff were very nice and helpful. They are very helpful in storing your luggae if your room is not ready at checkin. The room itself was nothing great. I do realize that for $249 you don't always get a lot in the Times Square area. The room was older and dated. The bed was ok, but the mattress was wrapped in some sort of plastic cover and you could feel/hear it when moving around during the night. The breakfast was a disappointment. One of the reasons that I chose this over other chain hotels in the Times Square area was because of the breakfast that Holiday Inn Express usually serve. This was an exception. The pancake maker was out of order. There were no cinnamon rolls, when I asked the staff they told me that they have been out and would maybe have some the next day. They had been waiting for a shipment to be delivered for a couple of days. For the same money I would recommend staying next door at the Element hotel. Their breakfast is free and is excellent!

“Excellent boutique hotel hideaway in central Boston” I am in line with other reviews of this property. Attentive service; very nice rooms and decor; excellent location just off Boston Commons right by the state capital building. The rooms are like apartments; I had a corner studio. Other smaller rooms were perfectly adequate. What you aren't getting here are rooms with great views (and the view from the rooftop isn't much to see either) but the window and indoor lighting is decent, gym is a bit sparse (cardio machines plus some small free weights), and the elevators are slow so you often have to wait for them awhile. Dining room for dinner was rather good if you go for steakhouse fare (i wasn't thrilled with the menu but it was fine); breakfast service was a bit off as the servers didn't speak English well and had difficulty understanding what I wanted when I went off the center line. Rooms offered good value for money; the Amex platinum program is especially good value but you should know that "dinner for two" as an amenity really means an $85 food and beverage credit which will serve dinner for one in their restaurant. I would return and recommend highly this hotel as good value especially considering the negative reviews that others are getting in somewhat similar price point territory such as the Langham and the Taj.

“I got a good rate so I was happy” I stayed one night at the Marriott at the Philadelphia airport because I got a very good rate. It was fine; nothing special, but for what I paid it was a great deal. I walked to the hotel from terminal B and back again, which was great: I did not need to wait for the shuttle. There were a lot of people at check-in because of the canceled trans-Atlantic flights (due to the Iceland volcano) and so check-in was slow. The staff were friendly, however, and doing their best by a lot of guests at one time. I was downgraded.... I had checked my reservation before I got there and it said I had been moved to the concierge floor; when I got there they'd reversed that. Perhaps it was due to the influx of walk-up guests, but I thought that was kind of tacky. I don't really care about upgrades but.... well, I guess I do. But again, I had a cheap rate.... The service was pretty mixed. I tried to break a $5.00 bill for tips; the front desk seemed baffled by the request (made at a quiet time for them): they could not find singles. I asked a bellman if he could break a five. He had the gall to take my five and give me three singles, saying that's all he had. I had to ask him for my money back. Tacky. Tacky. Tacky. The room was large and clean, with a great view of the rental car parking lots. It felt dated in decor and set up, with an old non-flat screen TV and dark wood furniture. The bed was too soft for my tastes and I suspect the mattress may be old and in need of replacement. In fact, that's what I felt about the stay: everything felt old and in need of replacement. I ate dinner and breakfast in the restaurant. Both meals were very nice. Worked out in the fitness center, which is larger than most hotel fitness centers and had a lot of weight machines, which is unusual and was a pleasant surprise. I'd stay again for a cheap rate because it is adjacent to the airport and the food is good. Otherwise, I'd put up with a shuttle ride and stay somewhere else.

“Best Hotel In Boston” I just came back from a cold weekend in Boston and must say that this is the best hotel experience I've had in quite some time. I took my son to watch the Celtics vs. Lakers game, at the TD Garden, and seleceted this hotel based on price, location and reputation on Trip Advisor. The three elements on which I based my decision for this hotel were exceeded by far! The price was very competitive to other hotels around the same area, including other Marriott hotels. The location could not have been better, specially considering the temparatutre that we had over the weekend (20F). The historic sites are within walking distance, the best stores are within footsteps and the restaurant variety was superb. As for the reputation on Trip Advisor I think that this hotel was a bit underrrated. This hotel has very big rooms, excellent service throughout the hotel and the most clean and comforable room I've been in a long time. Even though our favorite team lost that weekend, the Marriott Custome House gave me the perfect excuse to go back to cheer for my favorite NBA team again.

“Very Old, and small” Pros: The Lobby is nice, conference area is nice. In a very nice location Cons: VERY OLD hotel. The rooms are small. Our first room had a view of the AC unit. We asked for another room. This room had a electrical outlet hanging out of the wall. The restrooms are VERY tiny. The elevators creek as they go/down. No Jacuzzi/hot-tubs on the property. The restaurant is way over priced. Hard beds. I will prob never stay here again.

“Fabulous bargain on priceline” I think at priceline prices (under $100) this is an amazing llittle hotel. Like other Kimpton hotels it has coffee and tea in the a.m. and wine in the p.m. The rooms are clean and bed linens cozy. The location couldn't be better...very central with good access to public transportation, city walks, restaurants, whole foods and entertainment. There is no concierge but the business center has free internet service which i enjoy as i can do my own research on city events. On checkout, I left behind a drawer full of clothes (hard to admit, but true) and they put my belongings in the mail the next day.

“I have to say only ok” The location of this hotel was good - walking distance to the attractions. The bell boy was very helfpul when we first arrived. We were surprised to find our room had a kitchen which was good to buy breakfast from the convenience store next door and eat it in the room. We stayed for 3 nights and had VERY hot weather, so when the airconditioner didn't work it made for sleepless nights! We rang the front desk to ask for the problem to be fixed and we were asked if we had the thermostat set to cool - OF COURSE WE DID! The solution was for a fan to be brought up to the room which helped us sleep a little better but still not great when the thermostat read 85 degrees plus! For the price we paid to stay here we really weren't happy in the end and would stay elsewhere next time.

“Rooms with soon-to-dissapear Bay views; rooms outdated.” The Hilton Financial District is a mixed experience. An older tower hotel that's at once in the Financial District, Chinatown and North Beath neighborhoods. Positives: -Service was professional, friendly, accomodating; special thanks for upgrading us to the highest room possible, and helping with my rewards points number. -Lobby is modern, renovated, with attractive restaurant. (i did not eat there) -Location is both functional for business in the central Financial District (or SOMA, too), as well as good for tourists, as it is just down the street from the storied North Beach neighborhood that is Littly Italy, Chinatown, and the literary Beat-generation all wrapped up into one. Within walking distance of Coit Tower, the Ferry Building (and waterfront), and a bit further (20min) to Fisherman's Wharf. -Views: some rooms on the highest floors still posses amazaing views northward over the entire San Francisco Bay, and right in front of you, Telegraph Hill and the North Beach neighborhood. You can see north to the mountainous coast of Marin, and east to the hills of Berkeley. Negatives: -Views: Sadly, a new tower is rising right in front of the former view formerly afforded to most all rooms for so many years. As construction continues, more Hilton rooms loose their view. -Rooms: Needing a refresh, ours was a bit tired for today's Hilton standards. Bedding was quite clean and nice, but carpets, furntiure, bathroom show their age. -Construction: Currently, the construction of a neighboring tower is cause for a lot of noise during the morning and day. -Parking is super expensive at the hotel; opt for the public garage directly across the street for half the price.

“Very Enjoyable!” Upon first impression the Westin New York at Times Square is lovely; it's nice to have an "entrance lobby" at street level, and a quiet, removed lobby on another level. Definitely appreciated. The hotel decor is modern and tasteful. There are many check-in desks with a well marked area for Starwood Preferred Guest Gold and Platinum members. There was not a wait at check-in for any agent. I'm always pleased when a hotel has my room ready before the stated check-in time. The rooms are excellent! I admit the television was a flat screen which was particularly subject to light from the window, but that was easily fixed. The rooms are very well decorated and have that squeaky clean feel I expect from large chain hotels, but manage also to be comfortable and "homey" at the same time. The only problem with my stay was inattentive service at breakfast. The service staff didn't offer any beverage refills, and the staff was rather mechanical. Take order, bring order, bring check. I understand breakfast service isn't incredibly complex, but a little intuition on the part of guest needs would be appreciated. I mentioned my displeasure with the service to a front desk agent, who apologized, but made no other gesture. At Sheraton, any complaint is usually handled with some form of compensation. I was not *completely* satisfied due to the situation of service in the restaurant, but I'm sure it was a fluke. Westin at least has their concepts down right, and the facilities are wonderful.

“Bad service” Upon arrival we were greeted by the friendly and helpful doorman. At the desk things weren't running as smoothly, it was busy and the staff behind the desk were very unfriendly and unattentive. The staff had this attitude the whole week we stayed there, if you would ask something they would role their eyes and sigh ... very unprofessional. Actually I have never experienced this in any hotel and I do quite a bit of traveling. Housekeeping and the doormen on the other hand were very helpful and friendly. The room, a serene king, in itself was ok and well fitted except that it was missing a safe. Bathroom was big, with nice big fluffy towels and a good shower. The window could be opened and free-wifi is always a bonus. The room is on the noisy N State st side, which didn't bother us too much but be warned if you are a light sleeper. All in all the stay in Chicago itself was great, the city has a lot to offer and we were lucky with the weather. I will definitely be back, but not at the Dana, way too much attitude.

“Great New Theater District Option” We spent two nights here in late July and had a very nice time. The hotel location is wonderful if you are going to the theater. No need for a cab back home. Restaurant row is one block away with plenty fo decent pre theater choices (actually, we were suprised by the improved quality there and on Nineth Avenue.) The hotel itself is clean and new, with a mid century modern chrome and wood look. The rooms are smallish, but not unusually so by New York standards. But, the rooms are very sleek, with clever adaptations for small rooms. The beds are good. The bathrooms are very good, with high quality showers and toiletries. No tubs. Very high quality towels and linens. The corner deluxe rooms anywhere above about the 20th floor have terrific views of the city, and all the way to New Jersey if you are facing west. Very international group of guests. Most guests were European or Latin American. I thought the addition of the deli like food service area off the lobby was great. All in all, we really enjoyed the hotel. Head of its price class in the city, certainly the Times Square area, I think. Our only complaint was that the bellmen and doormen are obviously at war with each other (two tips to get the bags through the door) and the doormen are at war with the local taxi drivers (comical scene of cabs waiting in front of the hotel, but the doormen will not let you get in one - instead, they hail one for you. I guess a better tip?) But, that is not so unusual in New York, and it isn't much of a problem. All in all, a great value (its all relative of course) and a great location.
“Excelente ubicacion” Remodelado , cerca de tiendas , restaurantes. Elevadores pequenos.

“Nice but a few problems” We stayed for three nights and had a good experience. The location is great and it was easy to get to attractions like MoMA and Fifth Avenue. The hotel is very nice and has a very modern look and feel to it. The staff is helpful but seem to not have the same "can do" attitude you find at larger hotel chains. However behind this pretty "window dressing" were a few problems. The shower made a horrible shaking sound any time you turned the water pressure up. I notified the front desk of this problem and they said engineering would look at it but nothing was fixed. I heard the same noise from surrounding rooms several times during our stay. The elevators were incredibly slow and one even broke down for several hours on Saturday night. And I would not recommend eating at Moda, the restaurant in the lobby. While it may look nice, you would get a much better meal at any of the restaurants located within walking distance of the hotel. Overall, it was a nice hotel but they really need to work on making it a "complete" establishment.

“Great service and in the middle of river walk” I have stayed at many properties on the river walk. This was my first time to stay at the Hyatt and I was impressed. When reading about the hotels on the walk, this property is always one star better than most of the others. After my 3 night stay I have a better understanding of why. The service here is tops. Check in was super easy and friendly. The bellman helped me with my luggage. I asked when he would arrive since he was using another elevator and he said he would be right behind me. No more than 3 minutes after I entered my room, there he was. He put my hanging clothes and suitcase in the appropriate place all while telling me about the exercise room, room service, etc. I actually felt my tip to him was indeed earned. I opened the refrigerator to put some waters in there that I had brought along this trip. The min-frig was stocked full. I called down to see if I could remove some items to make room for my bottle waters. The operator told me I could not, but would bring a refrigerator up for no additional fee. I agreed and asked how long. She told me ten minutes. In less than ten minutes it arrived. The room was clean and completely functional. NO mold or torn wallpaper, etc. There is 42" LG LCD television. There are a few not so great things. My room was at the end of the hall with a great view. The hallway is like a vocal amplifier to those conversing in the hall. On the first night, at 2 AM, I was startled awake by a young woman drunk cussing in the hall. Even when her door closed, which I guess to be about 6-8 doors away, I could still hear the rumble of her roar. Later she opened it for a friend, and there again were her choice words. It was a problem even for the person has a casual cell phone conversation while walking down the hall. The other thing was the $30 valet parking. OUCH! Self Park was $23.

“Fantastic Stay - First time at a Hyatt Place & we will be back!” This was our first time at a Hyatt Place and we will be back! We loved everything from the staff to the size of the room and the breakfast. As frequent customers of the Holiday Inn Express brand we were pleasantly surprised with this chain the breakfast was far superior to the HI Express brand and the rooms here were amazing so large with a massive couch that one could actually sleep on! Everything was modern and fresh and we loved the free wifi! I hope that all other Hyatt Place properties are as good as this one because I think that will be our new brand of choice!

“Poor service” We arrived quite tired around 9:00 in the evening from the east coast, and the front desk found our reservations, (We had booked two rooms.) They had not have the rooms we booked and woman at the desk had to look for rooms for us. I always find this amazing. I have never worked in the hotel industry, so I don't understand why if you have a reservation (And if you don't cancel, they will charge you!), but they don't have rooms set aside for you. The desk clerk did give us free wireless for our stay because check in took so long. In 2012 I will never give a hotel an excellent rating if they charge for wireless (even if I'm not paying for it). That's like asking if we want hot and cold running water. The clerk gave us a choice of rooms. Of course they did not have connecting rooms for our family. If you've booked two rooms under the same reservation, why would you not want the rooms to be near each other?! We took the rooms that were at least on the same floor. The first night was fine. The second night we discover our room was part of a VIP suite! The party was inches from us in the connecting room. As it did not proceed past 10:30, we did not call security. The next morning the breakfast reception in the connecting lounge area started at 5:45am! Yikes! Now we do call the front desk and security. Of course they can move us, but not until later in the day, but who wants to pack up all their things in the middle of their vacation, but we did it and they moved us. Now we're in a room where we have to take an elevator to the lobby and a different set to get to our son's room. Unacceptable, so they move us again. The front desk did comp buffet breakfasts for our party for the length of our stay. If only the woman who checked us in had explained about the VIP suite, I would have chosen the other offered room. Poor service. Oh, and I found trash in the middle of the floor of the second room. It had obviously not been vacuumed.

“My new LA home away from home!” Where do I start? This was such a pleasant stay...very pleased. Started off being greeted by a nice sangria for check-in and then off to a lovely room. I was expecting a smaller room and was surprised at the actual size. Everything was clean and comfortable. The bathroom was very spacious and the shower was so relaxing. The staff is very hospitable, the halls were well lit (compared to other W properties) and it made the stay feel more "homey" to me. Great rooftop pool and in a nice area for shopping and restaurants. Will definitely stay again!

“Excellent Hotel - great location” I stayed one night at the Hotel Valencia. The hotel has the perfect location - there are plenty of shops and restaurants around. The hotel itself is absolutely gorgeous! They were nice enough to upgrade me to a room with a balcony - I had a wonderful view of the area and of the stores. I would highly recommend this hotel. Only draw back - no business center there.

“Great Location & Service” Stayed at the Conrad Chicago for four nights in a King room. Check-in was efficient with Amelia. It's amazing that she remembered my name and greeted me every night when I walked by. Housekeeping was very efficient and observant - I drink a lot of water, and in one night, they caught on and provided me with extra bottles of complimentary bottled water. I'm hesitant to recommend the Concierge as she was unable to provide good restaurant suggestions and seemed to just read off the descriptions from a restaurant reservations website. I ended up researching and making reservations myself. The doormen were generally unhelpful as most times, I ended up getting my own luggage and packages out of the car and opening the hotel doors myself. They seemed more engaged chatting with each other. The room was very clean and comes with complimentary wireless internet access. Slippers were provided along with two complimentary bottles of water. Unfortunately, my room faced a high-rise office building; the offices were about 10 feet away, so we could watch each other. This was very uncomfortable as I prefer natural light and like to keep my curtains open. I tried to switch rooms, but the hotel was sold out. The marble bathroom was spacious with separate tub and shower. The Acca Kappa bath products were a nice touch. I took a shower at 7:00 a.m. and that must be prime time for showers, as water pressure suffered greatly and the temperature was only warm. Hotel location was excellent, as it's connected to The Shops at North Bridge (Nordstrom is an elevator ride away). The hotel ground floor lobby is off Rush Street, though you can cut through to Michigan Ave. by exiting through the mall. All the major stores are nearby and the hotel is well-positioned so you're within 10 minutes walking distance from the Art Institute to the south, and Water Tower Place to the north. There are many nice restaurants nearby - i.e. Volare, The Purple Pig - and others such as Spiaggia are within walking distance. I was able to obtain a corporate group rate, so didn't mind the hiccups with the Conrad Chicago. However, if I were to pay full price at over $400 a night, I will likely look elsewhere. Overall, quite a nice stay; the great service I received from certain members compensated for the other shortfalls.

“a 'glass wall'” I've stayed twice here, both reserved via a discount web site and I've had twice nothing to complain. First time, room was with view on the river, 2nd time on the lake... Hotel's architecture is nice, location near all point of interets and rooms are large, clean, quiet. bathrooms are some of the nicest I've ever seen... An adress to recommand and to keep in Chicago.

“One of my worse Hilton experience” Weekend escape with best friend in Boston and as a HHonor gold, I chose to stay at a full service Hilton. Yet it turned out to be like a nightmare. Pro 1. Gave free oral-B tooth brush Cons 1. Kindly asked whether an upgrade was available, front desk saids they are fully booked, but I still saw reservations for better rooms available everywhere. 2. Told I was given an water view room with a great view of the harbor, but I could only see bricks and 100 year old buildings. Called and asked about the view and was told its called waterview because back in 1970 you can see water from that room. 3. Told fridge was already in the room, as I need to put a birthday in the fridge for my friend. NONE, had to call room service. Guy came in with fridge seems to not have showered for weeks... 4. Called and asked for complimentary bottled water as Gold member, given 100% at other Hilton's. They brought two bottled water and charged me $15 plus 15% room service and $3 delivering. 5. Waited 15 mins to be seated for breakfast and almost everything was cold at the buffet, coffee was warm. 6. Waited 30 mins for a taxi on a rainy day 7. $41 Valet parking, and waited nearly 30 mins to get my car. 8. Asked for amenities such as toothbrush, toothpaste, and shave cream to be placed in room prior to arrival. Nothing was there, had to call twice to get them. Multiple boston trips in the future, none at this Hilton. I love Hilton hotels, but this is certainly the exception.

“Very convenient downtown choice” As others have noted, this Hilton is excellently located - almost next door to the convention center, close to many of the bank headquarters, and easy walking distance to lots and lots of restaurants. It is also next to the transit center and the light rail. My room was great - the HD television was terrific and the workspace was wide enough I could spread everything out. The bathroom had the standard Hilton soaps and shampoos, but that's OK. The lobby is a bit small and there is only a few chairs to wait in as your group gathers in the foyer. But, if the weather is nice there is plenty of space in the courtyard outside the Wachovia Center. The hotel registration desk was speedy and accurate. I didn't use the fitness center, since the hours were quite restricted, but one of my colleagues did and he said it was well worth $20 for five days. A couple of things could use improvement - I couldn't consistently access the wi-fi in my room and when I mentioned this to the front desk they said something like, 'oh, you must be in the middle of the hallway - there's nothing we can do about that'. Well, actually, there is - you install a stronger system so there aren't dead spots in your hotel. Secondly, the lounge breakfast could have more fresh and higher quality ingredients. The bagels seemed like they were three days old, and on the weekend it seemed as though the staff couldn't keep up with all the kids munching on the pastries. There was a line at the coffee machine, which could only make one cup at a time. Still, all in all, I would probably choose the hotel again if I wanted to stay downtown Charlotte.

“It sucks, Super 8 is nicer” This place SUCKS.....joke is on you if you stay here. Only reason we did is because we hosted a customer seminar here the next morning. However, if you like staying in your great-great-great-great grandmothers old time shack you would enjoy it. Please see my blog at http://talesfromtheroad-mwalno.blogspot.com/ We arrived late (around 9 pm) and the valet guys were pretty good. I don't know if you can self park the car anywhere close. Valet asked my name and spoke into his headset, but after I walked the ten feet to the front desk the clerk had no clue who I was or what I was doing there (basically no clue at all). She couldn't tell me where our event would be (I like to check out the room the night before) or if anything had arrived for us (we shipped some things). I headed up to the room and it reeked of fresh paint. I was going to call down, but decided I would stop on my way to the fitness center. The itself was AWFUL - could have really used a good cleaning and some new wall paper.....it just looked old and beat-up. Don't ever get suckered into staying in room 827. Headed down to front desk and asked if the room was just painted, answer was "I don't think so", and instead of asking if they put me in a new room that was it. Service = Horrible. The "newly remodeled" fitness center was weak -- very, very small, limited free weights, tread mills/ellipticals, and old weight machines. It would be a disaster if they had a house full of people who wanted to work out. Might be a nice spot if you were over 100 years old! Headed back up to the room and was unimpressed with the shower and bathroom. I would say it was on par with a Super 8. Although breakfast was included in our package, I headed down early to our event. I will say the food for that was great, service was top notch and the coffee cake was so unbelievably good...I also liked the free shoe shine. No way would I ever stay at this location or any Ritz for that matter. Total - $231.80 (room was 208 for the Schwab rate - including $18 breakfast)

“I don't know what some of the other reviewers are talking about!” The Westin Los Angeles Airport is located near LAX. A free shuttle service will take you there first before going to the La Quinta and Holiday Inn right across the street. The ride takes about five minutes and runs 24 hours a day in 15 minute intervals. It is a small bus and the driver accepts, but does not expects tips. The hotel is on Century Boulevard in the direction of the airport. There are some fast food (Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and McDonald's) across the street near the other hotels mentioned above as well as a Denny's nearby, but not much else. Fortunately, rental car companies are close (there is a Thrifty rental right next door). The hotel appears to have been a luxury hotel in the 80s and is well-kept. The lobby is very nice and the bar is upscale. Guests are middle-class or above, but not upper-class. Many international visitors and there was a conference for Korean American Amway and a semi-formal for some Japanese college kids. I would say on average the hotel is somewhat below the Westin average in quality, but not by much. I liked it just fine. The front desk staff were generally attractive and professional. And they were friendly enough. I experienced no problems whatsoever at this hotel, so perhaps they could turn ugly as other reviewers have commented. However, nothing close to what happened to others happened to me. I reserved an Executive Room located on the Starwood Preferred Guest floor and it was excellent. Very spacious and nice. The view was a city view consisting of only the empty lots and cheap apartments across the street. My colleague's room overlooked the main entrance and the Hilton and other hotels as well as the airport. I noticed the roof of the entranceway was dirty and had lots of pigeon droppings (the only unclean factor of this hotel). The TV was not a flat screen, but a large brownvision. The window stretched all across one side of the wall. The bathroom was a bit like 80s-style Los Angeles, but nice enough. All amenities were provided. And, of course, you can't beat the Heavenly Bed which is the signature mark of Westin hotels. I saw in a sales brochure for hotel items that was in the room that you can order the mattress and bedding set for about $3500. I was tempted to order this set. Once again, I want to commend Westin for the best bedding ever! I slept so incredibly well here. A beautiful sleeping experience! I did not order room service, but I met my friends at the bar and we had a great time. The bill came out to nearly $100 plus a $20 tip for the three of us. They could mix any drink, I imagine since I ordered Tom Collins all night and they didn't blink (many bartenders need to ask what that is and they don't know how to make it). The servers were good, but could have came by more often. At least they didn't bother us or pester us by keeping asking us if we wanted more drinks. The bar is definitely what you would imagine an upscale airport hotel bar would be. I felt very comfortable there. Self parking was $18 per day and $28 per day for valet parking. There was a large BMW and some kind of sports car parked outside the hotel, but the cars in the self parking lot were varied in class. The weather was not that great (shocking for Los Angeles), so I did not see the pool. But another guest told me it was nice. SUMMARY: The hotel is located about a 30 minute drive on the 405 freeway to Beverly Hills, West L.A., and West Hollywood. So that is inconvenient for going out and shopping, etc. But if you are looking for a hotel by LAX, I would recommend this place. I have not stayed at other airport hotels in the Los Angeles area, so I can't compare. But I really enjoyed staying here. Although the next time I would probably stay closer to where the bars and shops are located and where all my friends live, if I had to stay near the airport I would most definitely stay here again. It's hard for me to believe these other reviews that are so negative, but I did not stay in a Standard Room and perhaps they were unlucky with service or something. The rate for the room, which I got directly through the Starwood Preferred Guest site, was also unbeatable for Los Angeles. It was unrefundable though. Nevertheless, I think the overall value is excellent.

“Great stay on the Wharf!” My daughter and I chose this hotel for a visit to San Francisco. We were SO glad we did! Looking at all of the other reviews you can bet this hotel is located in a prime spot for tourists! It is about a block and a half from the wharf so you can EASILY walk it in less than 5 minutes and far enough that you don't get any wharf noises or smells! I feel like this is the nicest hotel I could get for the low price of $149/night. Yes, it stinks that they charge $45/night to park here ($51.30 w/tax) but even at $200/night I couldn't find a nicer hotel especially with this great location! I drove all over the area looking for alternate overnight parking. There is a shopping center across the side street but they have signs that they'll tow for non customers and the parking meters all around hotel (and town) are 1 hour maximum and $3 per hour! It just costs money to park in SanFran! The staff was very friendly and accommodating. It was my daughter's 21st birthday so they sent up a bottle of wine and a lovely bowl of fruit. We also requested a mini refrigerator and it was delivered happily and quickly with no extra charge! The rooms were very clean and the beds were very comfortable. The shower had great pressure and I had no complaints. The hotel has been renovated, however, the hallways are dark and show signs of age. (That is just nit-picky.) The hotel is clean and nice and a great value. Also, the free wireless internet is a plus and was not taken for granted. So many hotels still charge and we had great service! We didn't eat at the hotel restaurant but did notice there was a Denny's across the street. Also across the side street is World Market where we got bottled water, liquor, snacks, candles, etc and next door to that is Barnes and Noble with a Starbucks and a Starbucks across the street from that!! (Yeah! TWO right there!) Right next to where you can catch the trolly. It turns around right there!! Go! Enjoy!

“Pro: Good Rate. Con: Older property, bad neighborhood” Not used to staying in 3 star properties so take my review with a grain of salt. That said, the rate was good, the staff was very nice and they upgraded me to a suite which was spacious. Additional plusses, a toothbrush and razor with toothpaste was in the room...I had left mine in the previous city by accident, so this was nice. Weirdly, they made me sign a "no smoking" pledge. I say weirdly because the room was clearly very recently a smoking room and had a deep smokers aroma in it. My guess is the hotel was remodeled last in the early 1990s. The major drawback to me was location. I stayed here to be close to downtown where I had meetings. My normal choices were all booked and featuring rates over $349 (outside company policy). While it was close to downtown, it was in a much seedier neighborhood than I had expected. Many prostitutes and other seedily clientele were observed wandering the property. So, on the whole I'd say stay somewhere else if you can afford it.

“First Class for Great Price!” We got this hotel from the Mystery Quick. Hotel was lovely! Restaurant was nice. Staff was friendly. Hotel was new and had great amenities. They had discounted parking available near by.

“Renovations, schmenovations--this one's a keeper” I'd booked the Carlton as a cancellable backup in case I couldn't get anything through Priceline and after staying there, I am SOOOO glad Priceline didn't work out. The Carlton is one of the nicest hotels I've stayed in in New York. Yes, it's undergoing renovations, most of which seems to be confined to the ground and first floors plus areas right next to the elevators on several floors. And yes, the 9th floor full bed room my partner and I stayed in was small, but I've stayed in smaller rooms at the Super 8 and Red Roof Inn and it was perfect for two. What sets this above the rest is the plushness of the rooms-white and gold with thick white comforters, plenty of pillows, two armoires and a bathroom with the same color scheme, ample, fluffy towels and a magnifying mirror that lets you see every last pore whether you want to or not. The room was immaculate except for one tiny detail we didn't comes across until we were packing to leave ourselves--a pair of Calvin Klein socks in the back of one of the armoires that didn't belong to either of us. They made a quick date with the garbage can. The front desk stuff was very friendly and efficient, making a great stay even better.

“Reasonably priced; central location” I booked this hotel at the last minute. Because of it's affordable price, I was skeptical about the space. Fortunately, Club Quarters exceeded my expectations. It's centrally located, just a few minutes walk from shops, bars and restaurants. Since we were driving, having the hotel so centrally located was difficult because there was no where to pull over, unload bags and check in. There is an underground parking lot located 2 minutes away. Make sure that you have someone at the front desk validate your parking stub because you pay the "lower" rate of $24 as opposed to the ridiculous $34/night rate. The rooms are a decent size with fast wifi and cable tv included. The hotel also featured nice touches like the refillable water bottle station. It would be awesome if all hotels had this! However; one major downside of Club Quarters is the very slow elevators. There are only two elevators with no service elevators which meant a long-ish wait time for staff and guests. Once the elevator does arrive, you have to jockey for limited space.

“W Hotel San Diego, New fave for my friends and I” Our recent stay at The W Hotel was a wonderful experience. We checked in to celebrate two birthdays and enjoy San Diego, we came in from the East County. We were searching for a happy hour that would not be too loud or rowdy. The Concierge, a gentleman by the name of Joseph informed us about the W's own happy hour, we enjoyed a great time in the Living Room and did not even venture from there. The Living Room does need a bit of a face lift, don't get me wrong, it's still a pleasant place for Happy Hour and Joseph informed us that there are renovations planned for the hotel. Our rooms were nice although a bit smaller than I expected yet much larger then the W Hotel's in New York. Another wonderful experience was breakfast in The Restaurant. As we planned to venture out for a late breakfast, we checked in with Joseph the Concierge. He recommended The Restaurant and described the "Benny", we tried The Restaurant and enjoyed delicious meals, I also must recommend the "Benny", it's an amazing presentation of the standard Eggs Benedict. All in all I must rate the W Hotel as one of the best in San Diego. From the Front Desk Staff at check-in, to the informative and friendly Concierge Joseph, to the cleaning staff and Restaurant. This will be our new "ladies" getaway and I will certainly also bring my husband into this hotel to spend a few days away from the East County.

“Great downtown location, nice staff, a few minor flaws” My wife and I enjoyed an extended stay in the City without our children. We picked the Trump Soho because we wanted a location near our favorite haunts in Soho, close to a subway line, with a pool, and an American Express Fine Hotel. We live in the NYC area and work in NY, so we are familiar with the pros and cons of that location. We were upgraded to a one-bedroom suite, with the 7.1 Floorplan configuration from their website. Room was spacious, well maintained, and with a nice bar wet bar in the living room. We had a great view of the Hudson and downtown NY from our room. Open bathtub is a nice feature. The staff was very friendly. From the doormen, to the front-desk staff, to the people at the pool, to the staff at the breakfast cafe almost all were universally friendly. People at the pool were really nice and the setting was great. Drinks were good - which given the price they better be. If you know NYC and intend to visit different parts of town, please recognize the no area is perfect. You will either need to take a taxi or be comfortable with mass transit unless your intent was to confine yourself to the area of your hotel. If looking to go to different parts of NY, I think the location is great. You can walk to numerous restaurants, shopping, and bars in Soho, the Village, or the Meatpacking District within 5 to 20 minutes. You are 1/2 block from the Spring Street Station on the C/E line, which is a line that can take you up the West Side or to the East Side if going across Midtown. One stop away is the West 4th Street station which is major transit hub. So, the location isn't a problem UNLESS you really just wanted to focus on things in Midtown and above. If so, that's where you should stay. In terms of noise, it's New York. Very few hotels will be in areas of quiet. The Trump Soho is located next to the Holland Tunnel entrances. But, in the morning rush you're not going to hear it. The evening rush can be busy, but I didn't notice much noice from a 29th floor location. We had looked at two hotels in the Meatpacking district as alternative options. I am REALLY glad we ruled them both out. While those hotels are certainly in the thick of the downtown nightlife - unless you're intent is to avoid going to bed before 3:00 a.m., I think the TrumpSoho is a much better option. Close enough to enjoy the nightlife, far enugh away to not hear it. The issues we had were minor. I was still going to work while on our stay so I needed to be up and out early. There is no bathroom door so it is likely you will wake up your spouse or SO. I understand from a design perspective why they did it as it creates a more open space in the bedroom, but did just want to point out that open layout. We had breakfast included with our room. But, if staying here without that feature I really would suggest you can save a lot of money by walking a block or two away. A breakfast of two eggs, toast, bacon, coffee and juice will run about $36.00. I am used to NY prices, but at any neighborhood spot you can get the same thing and pay $10 or less. We had a few minor issues during our stay and all were quickly corrected. Every hotel has a few minor things that can go wrong. To me, the better hotels make sure they get fixed right away, which the staff here did. With the rate we paid and a promotion of a free night, I thought this was a really good deal and we will certainly look to stay there again.

“Aging Property in Need of Maintenance” The property is centrally located in the Arboretum area convenient to shopping and restaurants, though not to downtown. The onside sports Bar has 30+ TVs and offers good ambiance. The property needs a facelift, however. Peeling ceilings in my bathroom, and an elevator that had me stuck for 10 minutes will keep me from coming back. When I informed the front desk that the elevator was inoperable and I had been caught inside, I was told "it does that when it is cold." no other help or apology was offered. There are better options nearby.

“Good hotel, recently renovated” I stayed at the Millennium Knickerbocker over Memorial Day weekend. I got this hotel through bidding on priceline resulting in more than 50% savings off the regular rate. Like the Intercontinental, the Knickerbocker is an old hotel that combines historical charm with modern luxuries. Pros: * Free wireless internet in lobby, with grand piano performance * Close to Michigan Avenue * Great location for downtown * Recently renovated rooms Cons: * Rooms may be small and would feel cramped for families * Small elevators - can fill up fast if you have luggage

“Not worth the price” The ONLY reason they get 3 stars is because I arrived at 8:30 AM after a red-eye flight and the guy at the front desk was able to get me into a room way before the real check in time, which was great after flying all night. Stayed here on a business trip - hotel was planned by my company, so I didn't pick it. The rooms are microscopic (literally, a bed and 2 small side tables.
