That's the room), there was a hair in my bed when I checked in, my curling iron, etc was always left on the floor by housekeeping (gross), phone didn't work, internet worked eventually, street noise was excessive (and I sleep with ear plugs). If I was paying $100 a night, I might overlook these things, but for nearly $500 a night (that includes tax), the place should be perfect. Location is fine, staff is fine, rooms/attention to detail is a miss.

“Lovely hotel, nice location” My mother and I stayed here in October for two nights and overall the experience was great. Very clean, quiet and the rooms were spacious enough. The location was close to union square shopping (yea!) and we had a very pleasant stay. The staff was extremely friendly and accomodating and overall we had a great experience. The restaurant was good and the atmosphere was great.

“Awesome hotel” I have no complaints about this hotel. It's beautiful on the outside and even more on the inside. Staff is very helpful. The rooms are big and the beds very comfortable. I didn't know what to expect after the numerous negative reviews, but I have nothing but good things to say for this hotel. To all those that complain of the price, learn to use priceline. We only paid $70 for our beautiful room. No complaints here. I highly recommend this place. It's in a wonderful location.

“Good Choice” Selected this hotel because I was in town for a day visiting my Dad and flying back home to Europe the following day. Brought Dad in to Boston so that we could take in the sights. We used the Embassy Suites as our base-camp. Funny, I didn't see mention of the fact that the T station (subway) is within walking distance of the hotel. This was a great added bonus. Even though the hotel shuttle bus will take you over there, we opted for the walk at night and felt safe all the way there and back. It's only about 15 minutes walk. Might not be the right choice to walk if you are on your own. The hotel is good. Our room was in good condition and the breakfast was excellent - love those omelettes. I used the exercise room, but was a bit dissapointed that they didn't have an elliptical trainer. I made do with the treadmill. The exercise room was small but very clean. Would have liked a shower room so that I didn't have to scare the guests in the elevator on my way back up to my room. As stated in other reviews - there is nothing around this hotel. If you want to go out, you'll have to get on the "T" and go just a couple of stops find the action. Shuttle to the airport terminals was good and fast - same for the pickup. I will stay here again.

“One of the most difficult properties I have reviewed...” I have reviewed a good number of properties, and the moment I unlocked the door to my room, I said to myself - How in the world am I going to review this property? The property is a little hard to find - you can see it from the interstate, but it's down a side road, so my GPS put me on Zumstein Dr - but it didn't take me TO the property, I found it after assuming that it was further down the road. Upon arriving, looking at the outside of the hotel I asked - What did I get myself in to? The property is an old Residence Inn by Marriott - it was Marriott's first concept for an extended stay property. It almost feels like a timeshare resort when you pull up. The welcome I received from another guest was the first indicator that this would be an overall odd experience - "Can I have a cigarette, buddy?" - Uhhhh - yeah, I don't smoke. Very tiny lobby some basic food and drink items available for purchase in the shop in the lobby. Along with some personal care items locked with a chain in a glass case. The young lady that checked me in was very busy - but she was very polite and checked me in very quickly, explained how to navigate the property - and I was on my way. The hotel is built like an apartment complex - there are 1st and 2nd floor rooms, no elevators to 2nd floor rooms. So, if it rains or snows - you're walking from the parking area in the rain or snow. All around the resort you can see why Marriott would have sold the property - it is in rough shape. The steps up to my room on the 2nd floor were crumbling - and the wood landings were less than well maintained (peeling paint, over-sprayed blue spray paint outside the door) Some of the sidewalks were crumbling, and the building exteriors weren't very fresh in appearance. I had reserved a Queen Bed Studio room - I was upgraded to a suite - 2 br - 2 ba - kitchen, fireplace, and living room. As soon as I walked in I was hit with cooking odors (fried onions) - not a pleasant smell! The upstairs bedroom is loft-style, with a double bed (it looked like a double anyway) - and the master bedroom had a king bed. Since it was just me, I slept in the master bedroom, and the bed was very comfortable. The chair and sofa in the living room were very well used and broken down. The seat back of the chair was almost completely collapsed, and the arms were very stained and dirty looking. The sofa was VERY uncomfortable, very sagged in the center. Overall - was the resort clean? Reasonably. I say reasonably because the surfaces, bathrooms, linens (except for a cigarette burn on the bed runner), carpets, draperies, and walls were all clean. Were they spotless? No, but they had been cleaned - and the carpets and window coverings are all fairly recent replacements. Overall the units are dated and in need of maintenance - the secondary lock on my door was broken. The area seems very prone to vehicle break-ins, and they make sure to collect your vehicle information at check in. The hotel is near the end of a dead end access rd. At one time this property was amazing, you can tell that it was cutting edge in the extended stay business when it was built. It is still a nice property. Would I suggest this property to someone else? It totally depends on what you are looking for. If you are OK with a great value priced hotel that is a little rough around the edges - then by all means, this property offers an excellent value! If you are a very picky hotel guest and totally freak out when something isn't as clean as it would be in your own home... then this property would not be a good match for you. If you are looking for a temporary long term corporate rental on a limited budget, this property provides a great price and plenty of space for the price paid. The accommodations are clean, comfortable, and livable. However, don't expect the same type of accommodations that you would find at a Homewood Suites or a Candlewood Suites. I only stayed for one night for an overnight through traveling through the area - but it met my needs, was very easy on the budget, and they did upgrade me to a huge suite! I can't lie, I wanted to go buy a couple fire logs and enjoy the fireplace - it was snowing during my stay. The free wi-fi worked well, there is free breakfast but I didn't take the time to stop into the gatehouse for breakfast. If you aren't incredibly picky when it comes to hotels, give this property a shot - as I rated, it is an average property - nothing stellar.

“It's located on Hazard Center Drive for a reason” It was raining the night I arrived at this Doubletree. The sliding glass door on my room was a few inches open and their were sheets by the door to soak up the water coming in from the balcony. The door wouldn't lock (or even close for that matter) so I was given another room; both rooms were outdated and smelled like someone had sprayed cheap perfume in them. The Double Tree Club hotel San Diego is a better value with plush, updated rooms. Parking downstairs in the garage is $14 but street parking is readily available and I had no problems parking on the street.

“Big, Busy Hotel” A nice, clean and comfortable hotel with friendly staff. The location of this hotel is great if you are visiting Fenway Park as it is only a 20 minute walk away, and also there is a trolley tour bus which stops right outside the hotel. Breakfast was very nice but also quite expensive. you have to pay for WiFi in your room but there is complimentary WiFi in the lobby area, which is useful.

“A comfortable stay with no frills” I stayed here for 2 nights to attend a conference nearby. While I did not get to do any sightseeing in NYC, I found the location to be ideal. It is only a few minutes walk to Times Square and many great restaurants in midtown. The hotel is on a safe street, while being very quiet at night. My room didn't have any view to speak of (next building), but I had no street noise from the 7th floor. The room was small, but that's to be expected from a hotel of this price range in NYC. I had stayed at a few HGI's in Manhattan and the room size is comparable. My room had a King bed and a work desk with plenty of space to move around. The wardrobe had plenty of hangers. The bathroom was adequate. I didn't have much time to have breakfast, but it was nice to get a cup of coffee, pastry and fruit and get on my way. The staff at the breakfast area was very helpful. The reception staff was courteous and always proactive about my needs--asked me if I needed a late check-out (as a Gold member), a map, a taxi, luggage storage, etc, before I asked. I especially want to thank the young lady who escorted me to an ATM machine next door when the machine in the lobby wasn't working. She could have just told me where to go, but she showed me the way. It took 2 minute of her time but a small gesture like this makes an impression on me! With all this said, I'm taking one point off because of the elevator. No, not because there are only 2, I never waited more than a couple minutes for one. The building is very narrow and tall, much like many hotels in Manhattan, so all the rooms are fairly close to the elevator. This meant hearing the dings of the elevators all day long... and all night long. Needless to say, this prevented me from falling asleep at night. If you are sensitive to noise, I'd recommend bringing some ear plugs. I always request rooms away from the elevator, but in this type of building, there are no such rooms.

“Beautiful View of California Plaza” Ask for a corner room to enjoy the view of California Plaza and the Hollywood sign in the distance. Rooms are oversized as is the bathroom. Walking distance to food shops, post office and convenience stores make this a better location than most downtown LA hotels. To the critics of this Omni I say - try staying one night at the Bonaventure before being critical! The Omni LA is very very good......

“Not worth the location, the price, your time” Bottom line....rooms were dirty, staff not knowledgable, hotel over priced, never again. The food in latitude 41 was fine. When I pointed out the mold and mildew in bathroom, housekeeping supervisor told me that is what one expects in Columbus. My previous stay at the Hampton Inn, just around the corner had no mold or mildew. My niece stayed in a different room, she found a pack of cigarettes and dirty socks. This is not expected in an expensive hotel. The wall paper in bathroom was dirty and peeling. Everything was just a bit dirty and the service was a bit off. The staff in the rest of the hotel was a beat or two off as well. There was something amiss with the hotel's management.

“high quality modern hotel” Stayed for two nights in a king club double room with a city view which we really enjoyed. The room was modern, well furnished and spacious by city centre standards. The bathroom was excellent but we were puzzled by the opaque sliding window between it and the bedroom. Even when closed it flooded the bedroom with light if the bathroom light was switched on during the night. We made use of the club lounge for breakfast each morning and were delighted with the choice and quality of what was on offer. We also popped in one rainy evening and had dessert and a glass of wine in comfortable surroundings. After we checked in at the hotel late in the afternoon we were hungry and decided to get a quick bite to eat at the downstairs bar - this proved to be less easy than we thought as the service was very poor. Although we sat at the bar and it was not busy the staff were more concerned with chatting to each other and checking on their phones which did not make us feel good about the place so we did not return. All other staff we met during our stay were efficient and pleasant. This is a very good modern hotel in a good location and we thought it was good value for what we paid - particularly the use of the club lounge.

“nice place for quick trip” Very nice hotel. Was just here for a quick overnight and didn't really get a chance to explore the neighborhood due to heavy rain, but not a lot seemed to be going on in the immediate area. But good for a business trip in the rain where we cabbed everywhere anyway. Rooms were small, but very clean and the hotel was really quiet. Comfy beds, nice shower and I love that warm cookie you get at check-in. In-room continental breakfast was sufficient but pretty pricy ($38 for two people). I would stay again if the price was right.

“Nothing is included - not even printing a boarding pass” I have in the past ranted about charges for high speed internet at higher priced hotels being ridiculous, but this property added a new level of wringing out the last dollar. This is an airport hotel, and I wished to print my boarding pass. In room internet - $10 or so, so I went to the business center - NOT FREE - they charge for use! So I went to the lobby kiosk for printing boarding passes - this charges both for the time on line and by the page. I had $2 in my pocket, so I figured I might as well do this as it appeared to be the cheapest option, but by the time the boarding pass was ready to print (2 pages, thus $1) I had less than $1 remaining - when I tried to go back to print just the first page, the system would not allow it and simply kept asking for more money until my time ran out. The good news, however, is that when I explained my frustration to the desk staff, she printed my pass immediately (no charge) and offered her apologies. Otherwise, an OK hotel very close to the airport and close enough to car rental return that you can drop your car off the night before and walk back to the hotel. Be aware that the shuttle stops at another hotel on the way to the airport and at all terminals, so it can easily be 15 minutes plus before you get back off. Check-in was slow as well - only 1 clerk working at arrival. Rooms need updating soon. I would likely try something else the next stay at LAX.

“Very Nice -- Designed more like a 4-star tropical resort” I was a bit reluctant to stay at a Fairfield Inn and Suites. However, after reading several Trip Advisor reviews I decided to give it a try. What a surprise. The relatively new property with ultra modern furnishings is designed more like a 4-star tropical resort! This hotel has the best hall and lobby art and decorative work for a moderately priced hotel. In fact, the art would give many upscale properties a run for the money. Check out the impressive piece in the lobby leading to the rooms on the third floor. Rooms face highway 101 or the pool. Request a room facing the pool if you don’t want to hear traffic. Everything in the room seemed to be brand new. The rooms included a huge flat screen TV although some Marriott more expensive properties still have 19” old fashioned televisions. You’ll do some walking to find your room. I guess that’s why they went the extra mile to place great art work to make your trek more enjoyable. Aside from walking or jogging around the property, you’d also have access to a nice pool and fitness center. The fitness center included a good amount of equipment such as new treadmills, stationary bikes and brand new free weights. I was upgraded to a suite, which included a sitting area with sofa and other standard features. The room also included a “wet bar” with refrigerator, microwave and coffee pot –even though Starbucks is a stones throw from the front door. I still don’t get it. Who needs a coffee pot or microwave in the room? Also, the room included a very nice work desk, but the desk chair didn’t fit very well. The free buffet breakfast was far better than most hotels of this type. I glanced at the boiled egg with no shell, perfectly round yellow egg patty and paper thin bacon. All sat next to a microwave on a medium size table for a quick warm up or final cook. On another table sat the high protein energy food including Kellogg’s Raisin Brand, Low Fat Granola, bananas, strawberries, raisins, apples and more. Food also includes donuts, bread and pastry. They had waffles sitting in the case with the bread and pastry. Penny and the rest of the front desk staff were friendly, professional and courteous.

“Great Location - Close to Space Needle” Stayed 7 nights here and haven’t been in Seattle for some time. The hotel was Marriott quality. Although it was an older hotel it was updated in 2008 and is still in great condition. 7 Floors in a “V” shape with a large lobby area. You can catch the electric Zipcar/cable right out front of the hotel and located about 5 minutes (15 minute) walk is the pacific seattle center (space needle). I was not able to get a room upgrade they told me due to the length of my stay. Weather is warming up and had a couple of jogs outside along the waterfront. Back to the hotel. No Complaints and would stay here again. Goes without saying... Video on my Youtube Channel. Thanks for reading. Pros : - Great Breakfast , Location, One ay Dry Cleaners - Great Staff including the housekeepers! - Monday thru Wednesday is evening Social snack meals Cons: - Really the only one was the fact the front desk clerk forgot to give me a parking permit for the garage. Correct next day. Marriott Gold Rewards Member RetiredArmyRANGER

“Used to be Better” This used to be one of my favorite Hilton's, but things have changed and I'm not convinced it's all for the better. Not too long ago, when times were better, I would stay here four or five times a year. But I hadn't been to San Francisco in two years, and it was nice to see the lobby once more. I was disappointed to learn, upon check-in, that the property had done away with the Executive Lounge and I was given chits for breakfast upgrades instead. My room was spacious and clean. One change for the positive was that Starbucks now occupied a corner of the Lobby; the negative is that is so understaffed that I gave up on the wait more than once. I think what I am most disappointed in is the very mediocre food offered as breakfast in the Urban Tavern. The chit provided upgrade from Continental Breakfast (at the understaffed Starbucks) to an American breakfast for about $10. The thing is it that the food was bland and never changed. On the left was pre-cooked French toast (from Frozen?), and to the right was scrambled eggs. Move over one more and you get Vegetable Frittatta. Then bacon then sausage. I would hope that the menu would change and that they would have an Omelet station. They really should. I don't know, maybe I've been here too many times and I am getting saddened as both the hotel and I grow old together.

“Good Value for near Mich Ave” We stayed here Thanksgiving night since we were joining family at Lawry's two blocks away for Thanksgiving dinner. We booked using Hilton points and called ahead for early check in. Arrived about 1:30 and the room was ready; there was free pink lemonade and snack mix in the lobby along with hot drinks. The front staff was very friendly and efficient. The lemoade was gone in the evening but there was a small store behind reception where you could but drinks, snacks, and souvenirs. Our room was on the 15th floor facing south with a great view of the downtown buildings including the beautiful new 90 story Trump Tower and the back of the Wrigley Building. We're long time Chicago area dwellers so it was nice to see the new addition to the skyline, especialy at night. The living room of the suite had a small kitchenette with a table and two chairs, a sofa bed, and an easy chair. The kitchen was simply but adequately stocked for cooking/dining ; the sofa bed felt "springy" but our 20 year old son seemed to sleep fine. The living room had a flat panel TV; the bedroom an older CRT. The entire suite had interesting art of Chicago architecture. The bedroom was a little small (you had to close the dresser drawer to get around the end of the bed) but nicely decorated and the bed was very comfortable. There was a single sink across from the closet and the toilet/bath in a separate room. It would have been nice to be able to get to the bathroom directly from the living room but they did fit a lot into a small space. The breakfast buffet the next morning was crowded and we had to wait 10 minutes for a table, but the food was good. The waffle maker had the longest line so that held up the meal. Everything else was being constantly refilled. Overall it was a step up from Hampton but not as good as Embassy Suites. Oddly enough we could smell the 6th floor buffet in the hall on the 15th floor. We picked this hotel because of its rating, and the proximity to Lawry's, Michigan Avenue, and the Loop. The location was perfect; we strolled N Mich Ave a for an hour after checking in, walked the two blocks to Lawry's (GREAT Thanksgiving meal), and the next morning walked to see the <Macy's> windows in the Loop (nothing like the old Marshall Field windows).

“YUK!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!” This has to be a total disaster. I would never stay there again. The rooms were really small and there were virtually no amenities. I woudl NEVER stay there again. It was a total rip off.

“Location, Location, Location” Good value hotel in an excellent location only a short walk from Michigan Avenue with many excellent bars and restaurants on your doorstep, as well as easy access to the FREE Navy Pier trolley and the Gangster tour only a couple of blocks away. The bedrooms themselves were clean and spacious and I have to say the bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept in. The only downside to the bedrooms I thought was not having free wireless internet which this day in age is usually pretty standard. I was very impressed with the evening free drinks reception and the breakfast was far better than expected with a good variety to suit all tastes. I will certainly be staying here again.

“Not your typical Westin + great location” Stayed for one evening on business travel and really enjoyed this elegant Westin. Decor is much more upscale than the typical Westins I've stayed in. Gorgeous lobby and friendly staff. Awkward transition from room to lobby down to street level with multiple elevators, but it is at least a lovely walk. Rooms were nice. Would definitely stay again.

“Cool website - dumpy hotel” This is one of those remodeled ancient hotels/crack houses/flop houses - except all they did was re-paint and make a cool website. If you're into partying bigtime, are going to the Rockie's game, and/or are blasted drunk, this place is fine. For a normal stay, stay away as this is a dump.

“Not as bad as the reviews would have you believe.” Got this hotel on Priceline and was a little nervous after reading the reviews, but we did not have any of the issues that others had. The rooms were nice, clean, and of a good size. The hotel itself is about a mile north of the Galleria and is located near a reasonably nice shopping and dining area on Belt Line Road. The only issues that we had were that the coffee shop was closed when we arrived in the early afternoon (apparently, due to illness), and that there was still some construction going on in lobby. However, neither of these issues were more than a slight inconvenience. Oh, and some reviewers had said that they had to pay for parking, though I expect that was in the parking structure and not in the main parking lot. We never paid for parking during our stay.

“Fantastic! Highly Recommend.” We stayed at this hotel when we first arrived from Australia. We were given great service by the front desk staff and valet staff. The room was a really good size compared to most hotels and the air conditioner was great too. The pool was very clean and nicely set in the middle of the hotel and was a great place to relax. Even though pool closes at 8 if you are quiet they do not kick you out after that. Breakfast had a great variety to choose from including very nice fruit and yoghurt. Service staff were exceptional and helped us out at all times, especially the spikey haired latin guy. It is in a great location and easy walk to walk of fame (3 minutes max). If you are looking for a great hotel choose this one..

“Bloß keine Ansprüche stellen” Das Stratford hat eine hervorragende Lage direkt vor der Cable Car Station. Leider ist es daher auch sehr laut. Die Zimmer sind klein und unmodern, es war auch recht kalt im Winter. Die resolute alte Chefin meinte, sie hätte jetzt ordentlich geheizt und wenn uns immer noch kalt wäre, bräuchten wir einen Arzt. Das hatte schon wieder was. Ebenso wie das dürftige Frühstück. Soviel erträgt aber nicht jeder. Daher leider nicht zu empfehlen.

“Hotel website was very misleading!” The website for the Henley Park is misleading. They claim they are a luxury boutique hotel. There is no luxury here. We were going to the Verizon Center so wanted to stay in the Penn Qtr neighborhood and found this hotel on a website listing hotels within 1 mile from the Verizon Ctr. First I will say the positives: The lobby and common areas are beautiful, and well maintained. The restaurant looked lovely, though empty on a Sunday night. The bed was very comfortable and the breakfast was not terribly overpriced. Now the negatives: The construction around the hotel and area was AWFUL. Even on Veterans day, which is supposed to be a holiday. The trucks and noise woke us at 5 a.m.! I see another reviewer commented about this, but we thought since it is Nov., and his review was Aug., it would not be an issue. My main complaint was not the service, though I did not use the bellman or front desk for anything, my gripe was the room. We had a suite. Large, cold looking room, NO armoire or dresser for clothing, just a stand w/ a 19" tv! In a big room, this little television on a table. Ridiculous. We paid a suite price, and no big tv in a cabinet, and no where to store your clothes. This was odd. Also the bathroom was more like a highway motel. Very unappealing and outdated, very bare bones. This hotel makes a lovely first impression when looking at their website and lobby, but lookout! There is no luxury here. Very misleading.

“New Hyatt concept hotel, in great location” I just wrote a review for the Andaz Wall street, where we stayed two weeks before we stayed here. My husband and I stayed here one night at the end of July for our anniversary, taking in a show on Broadway and dinner at Times Square. We had a good experience at Andaz on Wall Street, so thought we'd stay here again. As I mentioned in my other review, the Andaz concept is to eliminate the traditional check-in desk. Rather, you relax with a beverage that they offer you while someone checks you in and gets your key. Then they accompany you to your room and give you a tour. The woman who accompanied us was very nice, and when we mentioned we were there to celebrate our anniversary, she returned with a complimentary bottle of wine! Andaz rooms are new, clean, and rather large by New York standards (although I'd say the Wall Street rooms were somewhat larger than the ones mid-town). Rooms come with bathrobes, and this one had a minibar and a safe. Again, although hot beverages are supposedly offered free downstairs at night, having coffee makers in the rooms would be nice - so I don't have to leave the room. We had room service for breakfast, and the portions were very ample. As I mentioned in my other review, Andaz is meant for business travelers. However, couples or families would also enjoy their big, clean rooms, attentive service, and good locations. I will definitely be staying at another!

“Pretty good....” I found the hotel through Hotwire- I got a really good rate. The hotel room was very good. It was clean and I think it's been renovated recently. It's a good location; right next to the freeway, close to the airport and downtown. I thought it was fine for a night. Parking is a problem. There is street parking but it's at least a block away- if you're lucky. I didn't see any eateries close by except for the restaurant in the hotel. It's fine for a night, but I'd want something better for a vacation stay.

“Reasonably good value with nice architecture and location” We were visiting Philly for my nephew's graduation from Penn. After scouring tripadvisor.com and various hotel websites, I finally found a great price for this hotel ($149/night government rate +$20 tax/night + $40parking/night). Beware when booking this far in advance, however, as I booked less than a month before the trip while my sister booked the same hotel last October and paid nearly double! When we arrived on Sunday afternoon, we were greeted by the valets/doormen and checked in inside with no problems. After reading about the ridiculous valet parking prices, I decided to try to find suitable parking nearby. Unfortunately, all the other lots were either full or had lower rates only if you remained parked all day (if you were coming and going as we were, you were out of luck). The room was your standard hotel room. It was clean (I'm a neat freak), had new furniture, a reasonably comfortable king bed, and adequate work space. There was some wasted space near the door and a weird setup whereby the bathroom door opened against the closet door. The walls were quite thin as you could easily hear the guests in the room adjacent to ours. Our room was on the left side of the hotel and we had an obscured but still visible view of City Hall. The rest of the hotel seemed to be well-appointed with a nice lobby, conference rooms, and adequate on-site restaurant and exercise rooms. The reading room was a nice touch as were the flowers in the lobby and the strawberry-water. The valet parking was a bit slow but, if you called them in advance, it was not too big of a deal. The location next to City Hall and across from Macy's (in an old John Wannamaker's department store that had fabulous architecture and a pipe organ) was really cool. You can walk to several attractions from the hotel though the historic district is too far. However, the location also makes it difficult to maneuver to the hotel entrance. Overall, we had a positive experience with the hotel and I would recommend it to others if paying less than $200 per night.

“Excellent hotel” Stayed here one night in September and really enjoyed this hotel. Classy, with great service, and lovely restaurants. Do try the wine tasting bar, it was great to have a chance to sample a lot of wines! Compared to Conrad Chicago, this hotel is IMO actually better. Very attentive staff, nice breakfast area. Pricey, but worth it. I must admit I didnt find Indianapolis all that interesting, but locationwise this hotel is hard to beat.

“i love, love, LOVE this hotel” Let me tell you why I LOVE this hotel. And it's not just because the rooms are nicely sized, clean, comfortable, and even a bit luxurious. Earlier this month, I came into town late at night to do a media appearance for a book I had written (aside: I'm not at all famous or anything, so this was a huge deal for me). My wife and I arrived after midnight, and I had to be over at Rockefeller Center for 8:15 a.m. At about 7:50 a.m., I realized I had forgotten the dress shoes I planned to wear with my suit! I was left with a choice: Be known forever as the goofball who wore orange sneakers with a gray charcoal suit on MSNBC's "Morning Joe," or find a pair of black dress shoes in the next 10 or 15 minutes. I called down to the front desk and explained my situation. I'm desperate, I said--can you help? Check this out: the doorman took off his shoes, had them shined, and called to say he was sending them up to my room. I was so nervous that I waited in the lobby, and changed into them straight away. So this is the hotel where the doorman literally gave me the shoes off his feet. (I tipped him pretty well when I came back at 9:30, of course, but he had no way of knowing whether I'd do that!) It's a great hotel. I'd stay there again in a New York minute---and I definitely will.

“Fun, hip place” We stayed at the Standard for one night over the Memorial Day weekend after deciding to check out of the Trump SoHo a day early [didn't really enjoy our stay at the new Trump - too quiet]. Our experience at the Standard was great. We enjoyed the ambiance, rooms, breathtaking views of the Hudson River and the City, and the amazing people watching on the patios. Good workout facility as well. Loved the ping pong tables and the wenches!

“Classy, modern, nice touches” This recently renovated hotel had just about everything you'd want in a hotel. The location is great (3 blocks from Boylston T station) and service is over-the-top helpful. It's like the W but without that pretentious, faux- European flavor. Little things like this were nice: 2 bottles of comp'd water on night stand; a flute of champagne at check in; free, strong WiFi signal. I got this on Hotwire.com for $140/night, which was an absolute steal for high season. The only thing close to a downside is parking. The two closest lots are both $30+ a day.

“Good room, good price !” Ottima sistemazione nella sterminata L.A. a un prezzo molto buono, stanza non fumatori con doppio queen bed ben tenuta e pulita, colazione abbondante e varia inclusa nel prezzo. Hotel oggetto di un recente cambio di gestione, i nuovi gestori sono gentili e si nota l'impegno per un progressivo miglioramento. Le stanze valgono comunque più delle due stelle assegnate all'hotel. Passate 4 tranquille notti a L.A., e questo hotel lo ricorderò per tutta la vita, visto che a distanza di quasi un mese posso dire di averci messo incinta mia moglie...

“Great Hotel, Very Satisfied With Stay, But I think There Are Better Choices” Stayed here for 3 nights on a business trip to Columbus as my usual hotel was booked. Saw the positive reviews and thought I'd give it a try. There are a lot of positive to the hotels. It is brand new so everything is very clean. The staff is super friendly. Breakfast is good, Fitness Centre is very nice, but small, pool looks to be a good size as well. The rooms are very nice, but small. The bathrooms are great, good size, granite counters, large showers. However, I'm used to a fridge and microwave in the room, which this didn't have. Also, the Heating/Cooling/Fan was quite loud and never seemed to work properly as it would "lose" the temperature setting. Admittedly, it may not be fair to compare this to other hotels in the Columbus/Dublin area since I get a very good corporate rate at Embassy Suites. So this Hampton was very nice but not as good as the Embassy, and it was more expensive for me.

“Nice Location- Small Rooms” The St. Anthony is located in a great location in San Antonio. You are very close to the Riverwalk and other little shops. The rooms are very small and hardly any space to do anything but sleep and watch tv. This hotel reminds me of a business office that was turned into a hotel room. Very few electrical outlets. Large bathrooms very luke warm water(not hot). Very small closet space. You can park the car yourself and pay a $9 fee or they will park for a higher fee. Hotel staff very nice and helpful.

“Great part of town, room was disappointing” My last stay at a Hard Rock was in San Diego, which I loved. I've also been to the one in Vegas (though never stayed there) many times. So my expectations were understandably high for the Chicago one. Unfortunately, I'd say the location is probably the best thing about it. Mind you...there was nothing wrong with the service, the staff, the booking process, or even checkout. It was just that the room was incredibly mediocre and average, and for the $299/night I paid, I definitely had other choices. I stayed five nights, so I think I had a good amount of time to experience the hotel. I requested a smoking room, which may have been one of the issues. The view from the room was great--I saw right onto Michigan Avenue and was fairly high up. However, the room was pretty dark, and you didn't have more than a few light sources to illuminate the room. As a result, the room was perpetually as lit up as a club--but without the cool ambience of a club. The bathroom was set up strangely. You had a window that looked onto the street that was in the shower/bath. I guess that's cool if you want to soak in the tub and look at the buildings and skyline, but if you're taking a shower, it's strange to have to pull the shade and then put the shampoo, conditioner, and shower gel on the window sill. Some people with voyeuristic streaks might like this, and maybe if I were there with a female friend, it would have been different. The minibar was not well-stocked at all, and I ended up just going next door to the pharmacy (Walgreen's or Rite Aid or whatever it was) to get what I normally would have gotten at the minibar. The China Grill downstairs was good for food, so I liked that. Would I stay here again? I dunno. It's not a bad place, but it wouldn't be my first choice.

“Location, Style, No Sleep” You couldn't sleep closer to Obama unless you were a guest in the Lincoln Bedroom - amazing location adjacent to the White House and near all of downtown DC. Very stylish hotel with accomodating staff. Rooms are dark, which is part of the style, but a bit annoying. Plenty of amenities in room. This is not a hotel for sleeping - doors slam, people party, ice machines used constantly, many rooms so close to elevator that you can hear it boinging all night. I had earplugs in and still was woken up several times a night for all nights I stayed. Food was delicious, and rooftop bar is a must for an early (4-5 pm) drink - gets chaotic in the evening. Have to scale the "velvet rope" to get to your room weekend nights. Everything is astronomically expensive.

“Nice hotel, decent location” This is a nice hotel with no frills, but was clean and neat. Staff was friendly. There is a gym and pool. I was there for a meeting and the conference rooms were nice and large. Rooms were average size. Kind of creepy that my room looked out and directly accross from an office building, so I kept my blinds closed the entire time. Location was not that great. The neighborhood was nice with several restaurants close by, but not close to a metro stop. Closest is about 4 or 5 blocks at Foggy Bottom.

“Great location” Stayed here for one night on a quick trip to Chicago. Picked the Knickerbocker because it was in a great location—close to the lake and Michigan Ave—and reasonably priced. The lobby may be a bit outdated, but it's an old hotel. The rooms, as others have noted, are tiny. With the bed and a small table and chairs there wasn't much room to maneuver. But despite it's size, the rooms were nice—they seemed recently renovated and the furnishings looked new. The bathroom was clean and bright and a decent size. If you're looking for a 4- or 5-star experience I probably would advise staying elsewhere. But if you don't plan to spend tons of time in the room and you want to be centrally located, I highly recommend the Knickerbocker.

“The place was first class all the way” They did ask when I checked in if I was going to be dining tonight, this is run like a big buck hotel (for as as I know about big buck hotels). Lots of help, addressing people by name when you call the front desk, high ceilings, glass and shiny stuff everywhere. The couple ahead of me looked as out of place as I did, a young couple in their early 20’s with just one small backpack between them. Anyone who has read my other reviews knows that I'm often staying in motels that are $30 or less if I don't fear for my safety. Cheapest online rate for this motel tonight was $185, but I'm here on an airline voucher. The place was first class all the way, my only issue was when they wanted to charge me $12.95 to use the internet, sorry, I can wait until I'm back to the airport. (Remember, I'm cheap) This is the kind of place you go for special occasions.

“A great hotel” I stayed at the US Grant for two nights for business in July 2007, and I was very impressed. The hotel has been beautifully restored, and no detail was overlooked. The lobby is stunning, and my room was just as nice: clean, quiet, wonderful bed linens, flat screen TV. The hotel is in a great downtown location, within walking distance of almost everything. The hotel gym is quite small and stuck down in a far-off corner of the basement, but still better than nothing. And I was disappointed that the hotel charged extra for Internet access; it's a big peeve of mine that so many hotels still do this, especially when you're paying the kind of rates that the US Grant charges. A tip: If you're sensitive to noise, be sure to ask for an inside room, as I did. Broadway can be noisy, so I'd imagine that the rooms facing that street would be quite noisy.

“So good I felt guilty!” I'm already a huge partisan of the whole Hilton Garden Inn concept. Having stayed in a LOT of HGIs, I can confidently tell you that this HGI is way, way, over the top! I was traveling with a client who is subject to "company-preferred" list accommodations; this hotel was not on that list, but I'm hoping that's just because it's so new. She came over to pick me up for dinner the first night of our trip and was awestruck, and all she saw was the lobby. I would have been uncomfortable about how much nicer this place is (than her "preferred" Doubletree about 6 miles away) but my room rate was so reasonable that this qualifies as a "lucky find" rather than as "consultant living large." Nevertheless, I've bestowed four rather than five green dots (as a rating) because the printer in this hotel's business center was not working for any of the three weekdays I was at the hotel. (I know tech support is hard to find, but...) Given how wonderful this place generally is, it's hard to imagine this problem was not addressed during my stay. I love this hotel's beautiful surroundings and consistent HGI rooms, but if I can't print out my bording pass (without the needless complexity of emailing it to the front desk, as the sign on the printer suggested), that's not a small thing.

“great location, but....” We had a great 2 double bed room, comfy beds, & large bathroom. The room had wear and tear with stains on the rug, there were food crumbs which made me think it was not vacuumed. There was a stale, musty odor in the room. The location was very good.

“La Quinta served us well” We stayed at this property for the weekend while we were in town for a wedding. This was an above-average La Quinta. The rooms were clean, the staff was helpful, and most of all, the location was very convenient for everything we were doing that weekend. We like that this hotel is pet- friendly, as we travel often with our little dogs. Close to the drag and downtown, we would stay here again if we needed a centrally located, inexpensive room.

“OK for Company Conference - Not Otherwise” I was here for business. This hotel did a nice job accommodating my company's conference. Food and service was fine. But since most rooms face an atrium style core, where all the shops and restaurants are housed, it makes for a really noisy night. I would not want to stay here for leisure travel.

“Second Review & Update” This is my second review of this property. I stayed here many times and our stay was for seven days this time. The Hotel is still an excellent choice. Below are some points both positive and negative that are different and may need attention: Food: The complimentary dinner contained better quality food and also tasted better. The breakfast was the same. Rooms: Clean with excellent sleep quality Service: Front desk and management are very friendly, service oriented and responsive. Housekeeping on this visit was less efficient. Don't keep your "Do Not Disturb" sign out past noon. We left the room at noon and took the sign off at that time. The explanation I received when returning to an unserviced room at 4:30 pm that if they pass by twice and see the sign they do not return, regardless of the time. We found this odd, but called to make sure we get service on days we had the sign out in the morning past 10 am. Pool: The pool and hot tub were not as clean as I would like. Dead insects and debris on the bottom of the pool and floating on the hot tub on all three days we used the area. Also, guests use the area for smoking and leave cigarette butts on the ground and full ash trays on the tables. One person was smoking cigars while we were swimming and we had to leave. No pool towels. You have to go through the Lobby and request them at the front desk. We swam three times. It was not bad enough to avoid the pool, just not as well cared for as in the past. Turnover: We noticed several new people. In the past we always had the same folks and we knew them and they knew us by name. That may be the issue with house keeping. We still overall like the Hotel and will continue to use it for our business needs.

“Nicest hotel in the Airport area” I travel to Jacksonville frequently on business, staying at many hotels downtown and sometimes at the airport, depending on flight times. Out of all of the Airport hotels, this one is definitely the nicest and has a downtown feel. It used to be the Hilton and has since changed to the Clarion...nothing has changed since the rebranding of the hotel, still just as nice, clean, and friendly. Great business center and adequate gym...love the cocktail lounge/restaurant, food court, room service, prompt shuttle service, and whenever having spare time, it's nice to relax in the 24hr pool and spa. The Clarion gets thumbs up as far as airport hotels go. (And definitely request a room in the tower as the other reviewers have mentioned...the poolside rooms aren't quite as nice and it's a long walk back to the lobby and cocktail lounge).

“Marginal for the price” I recently stayed here because I was attending a seminar for business at the same hotel. Check in went fine and the valet service was quick and efficient. I was given a quiet room on the 8th floor away from the ice machine and elevators per my request. The room was small but comfortable--no problems with the bed linens or towels. Unfortunately, at 4:45am, I awoke to the sound of something rummaging through a plastic bag I had brought with me. I turned on the light to see a mouse scurry behind the TV armoire. I didn't panic, but I did call down to the front desk to let them know. A man named Joseph answered and asked me "what I would like him to do about it since the maintenance people don't arrive until after 6am". I told him he could just send them up when they arrived--apparently this was nothing new. When I went down to the donrt desk a few minutes later, the front desk director Amr promptly moved me into a much bigger room upon hearing about the mouse. I am happy to report no more mice appeared during the rest of my stay. Other than that, the parking was valet only which was $26/day. I thought that seemed like a lot. The general demeanor of most of the staff was indifference--no one really went out of their way. However, the conference room where my seminar was held was nice and the food served throughout the day was decent. All in all a very unimpressive stay but not terrible.

“Excellent hotel!!! You won't regret staying here!” My friends and I booked 2 rooms when we went down to Philly last weekend. We were interested in doing some restaurant-hopping, as well as visiting Eastern State Pen for the Halloween event. After a five hour drive to Philly, we were exhausted and were so thrilled at the sight of this beautiful, elegant hotel. Later that evening, we decided to pass out early, and immediately fell asleep after hitting the comfy beds. The rooms are gigantic and well-decorated. The staff was so friendly, and it seemed as though each took great ownership of his/her job as well as pride in the hotel (which I find unusual and a pleasant change from the norm of US hotel staff). We did not eat at the restaurant, so I am unable to comment on that. Like any annoying group of disorganized gals, we forgot a number of toiletries, including our razors, toothpaste, and a couple of toothbrushes. The staff brought them up without skipping a beat. My only concern was that, on Sunday afternoon while everybody was rushing to check out, I had to call the valet more than once to remind them to bring out our car. But otherwise, the weekend went off wonderfully, in this supremely well-located hotel! If you do stay here, make sure to eat at the Amish market for breakfast at the Reading Terminal Market, which is located immediately across the street. You can also head out to Chinatown or Maggianos which are, literally, around the corner. When I return to Philly in a month for my upcoming conference, I will stay here again, hands down.

“Excellent rooms and service” My friend and I arrived around 1pm and there was no problem with an early check-in. Even though I had booked through Hotwire, the clerk was very welcoming. They even gave us a late checkout of 3pm. My travel partner was traveling with an elderly service dog (Brock). This was no problem for the hotel as they are pet friendly. Later to our suprise a dog bed, and dog food bowl were sent up to our room. Outside the lobby was a large silver dog bowl that said "Welcome Brock" These were such a classy touches! The room was large, clean with a balcony that had a city view. There was an IPOD-dock and flat screen tv. The beds very comfortable, The tolietries in the bathroom were awesome!! the only minor complaint is that the toilets are loud when flushed, could actually hear the tolietls above and below. There is a large indoor pool that has a city view, The location was great as there are several resturants within a block of the hotel. If your a dessert fan, check out Finale. I hope to stay at the Revere Again.

“Sofitel, one of the best hotel chains in the world, delivers!” Our second stay in Sofitel Chicago. Sleek design, great location, wonderful service, modern and elegant rooms, super all around. Had a great diiner in Cafe des Architectes, but that is for another review. Sofitel is simply one of the best options anywhere you go: I stayed in Sofitel NY, Paris, two cities in China, and was never disappointed. As a SPG.com Gold Member, I can only wonder when any of SPG numerous brands can beat Sofitel... at least once. Stay in Sofitel Chicago, at least once, for a special occasion, and you won't regret it!

“Westin Market Street - Great Location” We stayed at the Westin Market Street for a long weekend this spring, and were very pleased with our time there. From the second we got out of our car, the staff was so nice and helpful. The room was very nice and clean, and while it was slightly smaller than an average size one, it wasn't cramped for the two of us. The floor-to-ceiling windows definitely make it feel larger. As with other Westins, the bed was so comfortable. Every morning during our stay, we had breakfast in the hotel restaurant, which was good. And of course there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. It's in a great location - easy to get anywhere you need to go. We had redeemed Starwood points for this trip, but I would definitely consider staying here my next time San Francisco.
“Nice hotel” Nice hotel but costly. Nice rooms, excellent staff.

“Very Comfortable, world class service” A very comfortable hotel, service is world class. You will feel a difference when you stay here. The artwork in rooms and common areas make the hotel feel less like a hotel, a little less industrial than most. Highly recommended. Capital Grille is in the hotel, so if you like steak this is an outstanding place for dinner. Breakfast is terrific too, no need to leave hotel for that. HIghly recommended.

“Good reasonable hotel with great amenities” This hotel has some nice features which are reasonable if all you need is a place to crash for the night. It's not a resort, nor is it a mega-hotel. It's a small quaint hotel ideal for spending the night. The complimentary breakfast, internet access, and friendly staff make this a good hotel to spend the night in. * Free parking too and right next to several stores, restaurants, and even a movie theater. You definitely do need a car to stay here though.

“Loacation, location y servicio” La verdad es que no me puedo quejar, recibi exactamente lo que esperaba y por lo que pague. Ademas las opiniones de los viajeros me habian anticipado de antemano el hotel asi que no hubo sorpresas. El hotel lo contratamos por Expedia unos 6 meses antes de viajar y pagamos para 4 una habitacion con 2 camas dobles, desayuno y wifi incluido por usd300 la noche final impuestos incluidos.El dia anterior a la llegada, llame al hotel y solicite que nos dieran una habitacion que mirara al contrafrente ya que me molestan los ruidos para dormir y que en lo posible nos dieran un early check in ya que nuestro vuelo arribaba a JFK a las 6am. Cuando llegamos al hotel los 2 pedidos fueron cumplidos, la habitacion en el 4to piso daba a un parking trasero sin edificios, asi que vista abierta y tranquila y pudimos dejar nuestras maletas en la habitacion, ducharnos y luego bajar a desayunar siendo las 8am, asi que mas que felices con esta bienvenida. Durante el check in nos explicaron como utilizar la ducha que tiene su truco, es solo bajarle del grifo de la canilla un tirante para que salga de arriba el agua. La habitacion standard en tamaño, cuenta con caja fuerte, localizada bien incomodamente en el piso debajo del escritorio, una heladera bastante grande, 1 placard, 2 cajoneras y un par de sillas y un tv plana. Lo primero que hicimos fue ordenar nuestras cosas a fin de tener la mejor convivencia posible en el espacio dado y luego de 7 noches puedo decirles que lo logramos. El baño es pequeño pero todo funciona y ademas brindan articulos de tocador. Las toallas son muy finitas pero suficientes para la ducha diaria. Nos limpiaron, y cambiaron sabanas y toallas a diario. El personal es muy amable, el desayuno variado y si bien el espacio es pequueño jamas nos falto lugar, los dias de semana sirven hasta las 9.30am y los fines de semana hasta las 10am, si mal no recuerdo. Luego hay cafe y te durante too el dia, ademas de vasos por si uno necesita llevar a la habitacion. El hecho de que el comedor sea pequeño hace que el desayuno sea una actividad mas comunitaria y asi nos encontramos cada mañana conversando con los disitntos huespedes. El publico me parecio muy bueno, amables y respetuosos. Baños extras hay en el subsuelo. La ubicacion del hotel es formidable, a 2 cuadras de Time Sq , y caminando hacia todos lados, Estacion de subway en la esquina y varias lineas de buses en la otra esquina sobre la Av.9. Varias noches regresamos al hotel caminando luego de la medianoche y jamas nos sentimos en peligro. El hotel no es romantico y no lo elegiria para ir con mi marido, pero me parece ideal para grupos de amigas/os buscando una opcion bien localizada, a buen precio y limpia y con personal muy amable (son todos hindues, asi que el entendimiento cuesta un poco) en el corazon de NY. En los alrededores comimos en excelentes lugares como Carmine ́s, Tony di Napoli, Shake Jack, y crepes sobre la 9 ave.

“Great Experience” Stayed here for two nights, we were upgraded upon arrival to the executive suites. The room was huge if a little dark, howver the huge comfy bed and aveda products made up for it. Perfect location however found room service to be very pricey.

“Great stay in a great city” I arrived at the hotel at 9:30 am after traveling all night from Hawaii. I was greeted with a smile and a beautiful room overlooking the marina. The staff could not have been more accommodating, even granting me a late checkout so I could sleep a few hours before my meeting started. Kudos to the Hilton staff-- this hotel is head and shoulders compared to the Hyatt I visited in Maui for a medical convention.

“Another great Sofitel” The superb Sofitel was our base for a couple of nights in this wonderful city, booked on the strength of our previous experience of the brand and the hotel's extensive, positive reviews. Our room was very spacious and tastefully decorated (if a little dark) and the service throughout the hotel was excellent. We also loved the bar, which provided a nice atmosphere to relax in after a day on foot and a night on the town. I could go on, but a couple of hundred people have already said enough. This is a great hotel and definitely THE place to stay in Philly.

“Great place to stay in downtown Seattle” I recently stayed at the Red Lion while in town for a meeting at the Convention Center. The location was perfect -- just a couple of blocks away from the Convention Center, not far from the waterfront (great if you're a jogger like me), and near plenty of stores and restaurants too. My room was spacious and clean and included free wi-fi (I hate when hotels charge for that!). I was really impressed with the lighting in my bathroom which actually was flattering and good for applying make-up, unlike most hotel bathroom lights. My room was missing an ironing board, but housekeeping brought one up right away. I didn't try the restaurants but I did work out in the fitness room which was small but pleasant and had all the basic necessities. The desk staff was for the most part very friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay there again if I were in Seattle and recommend it to fellow business travelers.

“Amazing historic hotel with beautiful detail” Beautiful hotel in the heart of downtown chicago. Just blocks from Millennium Park, next to all the metro lines you could ask for, and near lots of food options. Quick access to all you could want in Chicago. Also near to the main conference centers, but this is more of a destination hotel than a conference mill. The hotel was extremely clean, beautiful, and well kept. Staff was very nice, and the amenities were perfect. Just wish we could have had more nights there.

“great location...decent upgrade chances” Great location in copley connected to a few malls. Upgraded to their typical decent sized suite as a platinum guest. Not the newest or most modern of rooms but no problems whatsoever. Valet was fine, pool and workout room were fine, though the machines could use a slight updating. Overall, there is some value here and the service was fine overall. Not as fancy as the W which is newer or fancier, but for kids and family probably better overall.

“Needs a refreshed look” Since I am a Marriott Rewards gold member, I try to stay at Marriott hotels when I travel for business. I have stayed at the Philadelphia downtown Marriott many times and I realized in this last stay that I am really tired and disappointed that Marriott has not modernized this hotel over the years. Yes, it is clean, comfortable, has the feather topped bed...but the room still has that "old" Marriott feel of dark old wood armoires, old green club chair, formica counter in the bathroom, etc. I feel as though I am going back in time.......and it gets depressing if you are staying in this type of room for more than one night. I think I might try the newer Courtyard across the street next time to see if that is better.

“Upper class” The name itself tells you that you are visiting a piece of history. Elegant, sophisticated and one of the best locations in Manhattan. You are right in the center of things, both for business and pleasure. Old world charm, mixed with modern facilities. We rented a suite and had a fantastic living room with fire place and a separate bedroom and bathroom. Ample, comfortable and elegant. Service is 5 stars and the facilities are excellent. The only thing that bothers me a little is the amount of people in the lobby as it is full o visitors and onlookers, but this is the price you pay for being a New York visitors attraction on its own right. This is one of the 5 hotels I would recommend to stay in New York if price is not a real consideration :)

“My first Ritz-Carlton visit” Our delegation was housed at the Ritz-Carlton for the National Education Association meeting held in Philadelphia, July 1-5, 2007. Because of the conference, the rates were reasonable for this upscale hotel, but still quite high for someone who has never stayed at a hotel for more than $130 a night! Anyway, the $184 rate not including taxes wasn't too out of line considering what other conference participants were paying at nearby hotels. The Ritz is a beautiful hotel and located very centrally to Philadelphia's attractions as well as the convention center. My room was a superior king that was extremely spacious, probably 450 square feet. Gorgeous bathroom and a separate room for the toilet. Only room detail that I noted that was a disappointment was the carpet, very stained in places -- needed replacing. The room amenities were good, free water, coffee and daily turndown chocolates were all welcome. The stocked refrigerator was very pricey, in fact one of the maids told another delegate that the amoire had free stuff on the left side and way overpriced on the right and STAY AWAY from that! It was a cute viewpoint and quite true. The people were very pleasant, the other rooms I visited were not nearly as spacious as mine, I would not recommend a corner room in this hotel, those seemed to be the smallest. Would I stay at a Ritz-Carlton again? If I had a good rate, I would probably be willing. But the standard rate on their website for this time period was $399 and up. It wasn't worth that.

“Great place. A little pricy but very good service” Rooms are great. Hotel quality is good. Sleep quality is very good. And if you are going to be working in the vicinity. Walkable to everything. Just that you will have to dine at the chinese center close by & breakfast at a local deli. But both are pretty good too.

“Good Location - Problematic Design” I recently spent four nights at this Hyatt during a conference. The hotel is in a nice location right on the Riverwalk and convenient to all "the sight" including the Alamo. The room was clean and the beds quite comfortable. The service during the conference was also nice. What I did not like, and this was a big issue, is the design of the hotel. Many rooms face and inner atrium. The views of the inner atrium are nice, but the atrium funnels noise upward like a chimney. Thus our room was always noisey with meeting attendees standing outside their meeting rooms and partying well into the evening. If I were we stay here again I'd ask for a room facing the outside of the hotel. However, I believe they charge extra for those rooms. It's a nice place, BUT. You might want to consider something else.

“Good spot for price” Comfortable bed especially for someone traveling alone, could be a squeeze for two. Good desk space and very comfortable chair. Not overly fancy but I like that. Great filtered water help yourself with supplied bottles, nice lounge downstairs. Staff helpful and not in your face, Irish pub on ground floor noisy inside but really good cheap food. Biggest downfall for me was thin walls, but didnt prevent me sleeping well. I'll come back!

“Excellent Staff and a very nice room” We spent the night in San Francisco after a baseball game and decided to try to JW Marriott (we are frequent Marriott patrons). The location of the hotel was great (just one block off of Union Square) and the staff were very friendly and accommodating all around. Due to our Marriott status we got an upgrade from the standard room we booked to a Jr. Suite on the 9th floor. Very nice room with all the standard amenities. For a hotel in San Francisco, the room was huge! Lots of room and even a little sitting area with a pretty comfy chair. We booked a package that included valet parking (which saved us $30..usual valet rate is $50/night...ouch), which I would highly recommend since parking in San Francisco is an expensive nightmare. Upon arrival we had a personalized note from the hotel manager welcoming us to her hotel (VERY nice touch). The rate at this hotel was lower than some of the other standard hotels in the area, so that was a bonus. We would have liked to take advantage of more of the hotel amenities (fitness center, hotel bar, etc) but will have to try next time instead. We would definitely stay here again on out next trip to the City.

“Absolutely perfect!!! Get it!!!” I booked my room on hotels.com for a very reasonable price. I got the 303 room. Lake view. It was absolutely amazing!! The room was spacious, very clean, trendy, had comfy bed and posibly one of the greatest view ive seen at night. I thought it might be noisy because it was next to the elevator but surprisingly it wasnt noisy at all. We definetely had some rest and slept like babies :). Our room also had a mini CD player which thought it was a plus. The location was great! We had the Wrigley Building, Mag Mile and Hancock observatory at a walking distance. Navy Pier it was also close, you can make it closer if you take the water taxi!!. The staff were friendly and always tried to help us. I just had an incident with my credit card. They charged me twice the parking cost even when my boyfriend payed them with cash at the moment of getting the car so i when i checked out the front desk guy gave me my receipt and of course i noticed it. Thanx Gosh i realized and they cancelled the double charge but this guy were so willing to help and give us the best service because of course it was a misundestanding. In a few words, you wont regret if you get this hotel. I can almost guarantee you that! and please note i didnt get paid to post this comment :) This hotel has almost everything except pool. I would be great though. Great hotel, great service, great location, great staff, great decor, great view, great cleanliness. My grade is 9/10.

“Great place” Been staying at this hotel since 2006 and they have always done me right. The hotel is in a great location next to NASA, Clearlake of course, Keamah, shopping, great food, and the beach. Not toention the hotel price is right compared to lesser valued hotels in Galveston. This place is always our first choice when we're wanting a quick get away.

“Nice” Received this hotel on a priceline bid. It is convienent to the U. Checin was quick and the employees friendly and helpful. The room was nice but the bathrooms are small. It is an old hotel that has been remodeled nicely and has an art deco theme. There is free wireless. The workout room is a joke. The breakfast in the basement restaurant was just OK but it may have been what I ordered. The beds are comfortable. Rooms on the upper levels have great views of the sound, the U, space needle, etc. My son tells me opposing teams stay here when they are in town. All-in-all it is a nice, mid-range hotel and I would return.

“The Hudson is fabulous!” The Hudson is not for everybody. I repeat: The Hudson is not for everybody. But I absolutely love it. LOVE IT! When I travel I don't like to stay at chain hotels if possible, and I especially love hotels with style. The Hudson obviously has plenty of that. Yes, the rooms are small. But when I'm in NYC I don't plan to hang out in my room much. I'd rather stay in a small, fabulous room, than a huge, floral bedspread-clad one. Just a personal preference. The Hudson is in a great location, right by Time Warner Center and Columbus Circle. But that obviously doesn't matter too much, since you're in NYC and you can take a cab or the subway somewhere else if you'd like. If you feel cramped in the small rooms but you want to hang out at the hotel, just grab a chair in the lobby and relax there. Great music to listen to, which is also a plus for me. For anyone interested in a generic chain hotel experience, The Hudson is not for you. If you want a swanky, modern hotel, go with The Hudson.

“If you are disabled--dont even think about staying here!” I stayed at this hotel because of a business conference. First they ran out of room block rooms so we ended up paying full rack rates. (I had to stay there or would have to taxi back and forth several times each day because I cannot walk a full block on unlevel ground without being in a wheelchair.) The conference rooms were extremely small and cramped. Since this was our first trip to San Diego, we also stayed for the weekend. We paid even more for those two days! Normally a conference rate continues after the conference is over for at least one night. Food at this hotel is outragiously expensive. The breakfast buffet for two, including tip, was over $40. A soft drink and sandwich at the Sky Bar (restaurant was not open on Sunday after breakfast) ran over $45 for two. I travel with a companion who has to help me physically. The handicapped suites ONLY come with one king bed and a sofa bed. The king bed was so high I could not get onto it from my wheelchair and had to be helped physically from a standing position to hike myself up onto the bed!!! The sofa bed was too low. Once down in it I would never get up again. The bed was not only high, but so full of pillows that they took up half the floor in the bedroom when we unloaded them at night. Not too good when you use aids to go from the bed to the bathroom in the middle of the night. The handicapped bathroom was fairly typical and very large. There were two doors one from the living room and one from the bedroom. Because of all the doors it was difficult to navigate once in there. There was no where to put my personal items in the bathroom....no shelves, no flat area around the sink, etc. So I have to carry them back and forth from the bedroom everytime that I went in there. And had to put them on the floor to use them. There was no comfortable seating in the so-called living room--even for regular people. There is only the sofa bed which is too low, the cushons are too soft, and frankly uncomfortable for two people. There was a desk chair. There were no other chairs. We really needed at least one upholstered chair with arms that would allow a handicapped person to get up and down with ease. Or allow a normal person to sit comfortably to watch tv etc. I wrote a lengthly letter to the hotel manager about the problems that I left with my card at the front desk on check out. To date I have received absolutely no response. I am a frequent Starwood guest. I have never ever in all my travels found a handicapped room that was more challenging than this one. Note: the desk staff were not well trained or knowledgeable. However twice we found very helpful informed staff handling the luggage. They gave us info on taxis, directions, recommended selection of restaurants at the Del Coronado hotel, etc. We had a bad experience with the shuttle from the airport. It turns out that this hotel is so close to the airport that taking a taxi is cheaper and much easier. The shuttles involved going up and down in an elevator and over a bridge at the airport.

“As much as I want to knock this, I can't. People are great here” So, if you follow my reviews you will notice my travel the past month has been insane - more hotels than nights at home. So I'm likely a bit cranky from the travel as I write this review. So here's what happened and why it ends well (hint hotel managers: it's all about the service): So I get off my flight tonight at about 9:15 pm after a very long day and a week full of different cities. I walk down to the shuttle pick up area and wait 30 minutes without ever seeing a Hilton Shuttle. So, at 9:45 pm I'm tired and cranky. I call the hotel and they look up my reservation and say, "Oh, okay, Mr. Needham, we will send the shuttle over." I keep my thoughts to myself (like "and why are you waiting for us to call, isn't it normal to have it running every 20 minutes or so at the airport...thus the "Airport" in "airport hotel?"). So I'm not thrilled at this point. About 5 minutes goes by and here comes the shuttle. Chante (I may have misspelled her name so apologies) jumps out of the shuttle with boundless energy an a smile, grabs my bag and insists on putting it in the shuttle herself, jumps in the van, smiles again and asks, "how was your flight, Mr. Needham?" Excuse me?? Service with a smile?? This sure beats losing my luggage on Air France in Paris last week! And it continued. Walk into the hotel and a manager is standing there greeting me and asking how my day was. Walk up to the desk to check in and there are four, FOUR!, people behind the desk ready to check people in. Stop in the bar on the way up to the room and a very busy bartender sees me with my luggage and quickly asks what I would like. The service was fantastic here and it paid off. They took a grumpy old business guy and made me feel a little better about traveling for a living. Well done. As for everything else - what you would expect. Decent bar/restaurant, rooms in great shape, etc. Won't try fitness until the morning so no comment there. Very convenient to airport (just a few minutes on the shuttle) but quite a hall to downtown if you are planning on going (although you can catch the train from the airport straight downtown for a few dollars). Well done, management and staff!

“Standard Westin, good location” We were in NYC on a no-kids long weekend. The pros - location, comfortable beds, relatively quiet on the higher floors, nice views of the city. We thought the TV in the elevators was amusing. Cons - small bathrooms, cosmetic furnishings, mediocre food (but who wants to eat here anyway). It was very convenient to most shows, and a block from Birdland. Quick cab ride to good restaurants in soho or the village (loved Il Mulino), close to subway, and had good service overall. We would consider the Westin again if visiting New York.

“Nice Spot --” We stayed at Barton Creek for three nights last month and were very impressed. The property is beautiful and well maintained and the service was good. Our room and bed was comfortable and the view of the mini-golf course, pool and rolling hills were awesome. The hotel is located close enough to down-town that it's not too much of a drive, but far enough away that you can really get a feel for the life-style in Austin. We would definitely stay again, especially at the discounted rate we found.

“DC during the Holidays” We arrived on Monday December 27, and were greeted by a very friendly doorman and concierge. The initial check in experience was a little unorganized, we weren't even given our room number. Once we figured everything out, we found our room on the 12th floor, a junior sweet with a king and sleeper sofa. Our view was of office building, to be expected. Our first night we ordered room service because we had a tour to make around an hour after we checked in, My son and I both ordered burgers, My son's medium and mine well, room service arrived very quickly, but both burgers were very very pink. Fine for my son but I don't do well with red meat. So I had my burger sent back even though we were in a rush, they brought me an entirely new burger and fries, that was very good. Once we came back from our tour, a very nice tour that the concierge recommended (the moonlight monument tour), and again greeted very pleasantly. We got a lot of good information from the concierge (Andrew and Sofia are the best), that helped us plan our week. We were told good restaurants that we ate at the rest of the week. As we got ready to go to bed we noticed that there was no sheet between the duvet and matress, we called guest services and asked for one, but were told that this is normal. (They brought us the sheet anyways) The next day we got a call from one of the directors of the hotel (Anna) apologizing from the previous nights room service and were comped the entire meal (both plates). Wow! Throughout the week we started noticing things that hinted we were in a handicap room (extra bars on shower and bath, very low beds, a peep hole at the bottom of the door instead of top and we had the only room on the floor with a doorbell nothing that affected our stay, but odd that we would get that room because the entire hotel was very empty). We asked guest services if it was a handicap room but were told that all of the rooms are very handicap accessible. OK? The rest of the week we were greeted pleasantly by all the employees and had an overall excellent experience at the Sofitel. We will stay here again the next time we are in DC! Heres a list of the pros and cons of the Sofitel... Pros: Good location (2 blocks from white house), very good customer service (all employees were very helpful and friendly), very clean and updated rooms, great cleaning service, great restaurants with walking distance (Old Ebbitt Grill, Potenza), small and empty fitness center Cons: unorganized check-in, very quiet at night time (if you are looking for a night life this is not the place for you), handicap room, nickel and dime you (be careful we were charged for local calls,wi-fi and opening the mini bar) Overall EXCELLENT!!!!

“Second time and still excellent” It has been five years since we were in Chicago. We stayed here before and we loved it so much last time we came back to the same place. I love the location and quality of this hotel. I will not hesitate to stay here again. It is in an excellent location, well maintained, good views, good sized room, good sized bathroom, comfortable, lots of restaurants nearby, theater, the loop, etc. A useful tip: it is an easy 5 minute walk from the blue line so don't take cab form the airport. For $2 per person, hop the subway to Clark/Lake. It's about 45 minutes and and $45 cheaper than a cab. I only gave it a "Very Good" last time. It is still consistently good in every way so I'm bumping it to Excellent.

“Great Boutique Hotel - Make sure you get a high floor” The Monaco is everything a boutique hotel should be. Excellent amenities, all the fine touches. Great staff. You will not be disappointed with your stay here, but you need to know two things... 1. Hotel WiFi is crazy expensive. Not to worry. Go out the front door, turn left, walk 10 feet (literally) and there is the nicest Starbucks I have ever seen that will give you all the free WiFi you want. 2. The lower floors are subject to street noise. I stayed on the 7th (out of 8 floors) and slept like a lamb. As soon as you get your reservation I recommend you pick-up a phone, call the front desk ((206) 621-1770) and have them set aside a room on the highest floor you can get.

“great location, very clean and comfortable rooms” If you are going to be spending a lot of time around Times Square, Central Park, and Rockefeller Center, this location can't be beat. We go to a lot of Broadway shows, and this is super convenient. On the weekends it can obviously can be packed with tourists, which can be annoying...but you're in Times Square so just expect it. The downside of the area is the food is awful - all overpriced chain restaurants with terrible quality food. So make sure if you stay here you get out of the area and eat at the great places NYC has to offer! The rooms themselves were very spacious for NYC - extremely clean, really comfy beds and high quality sheets, and flawless bathroom.
