I like "boutique" hotels as much as the next person, but in NYC they can be hit or miss. A big 4-star chain like the Crowne Plaza is much more of a sure thing, and you know what you're going to get every time. We had nice views of the city as well. Don't expect to check in before 3pm - but when you do, check-in was quick and easy. Staff were really friends and always checking if you needed anything in the lobby. It's also super easy and quick to leave bags with the bellman.

“South Austin Marriott” Stayed here as an overnight in Austin. Got in late, so didn't really have the chance to explore beyond the room. Check-in folks were cheerful and helpful even at a relatively late hour. Bed was quite comfortable and room was cozy (a bit small) and quiet. Enjoyed having free covered parking in the underground lot rather than outside. Location of hotel is a bit boring - right on the Interstate and 3-4 miles from downtown - but hotel was pleasant enough. As with all Marriotts, disappointed in the cost of in-room wireless but didn't hinder my stay too much.

“A funky interesting alternative” I spend one week in this area of Houston per month, and I've stayed here as an alternative when those my company partners with are booked. The hotel is interesting/fun/funky. The decor might be considered Ikea turned up a few weird notches. Think metal link curtains in the lobby and faux fur. I found the room size more typical of what you find in Europe, and the space saving design of the closet opposing the bathroom sink and toilet also very Euro. The tile shower and glass door were quite interesting and natural light port for the shower also interesting. The hallways were almost a bit dark/eerie. It was a different experience and if you want to try something chain funk boutique, this is a quite fun and interesting hotel. The quick pick up food options met my needs, the parking garage was big, bright, safe feeling and clean. The bed was comfortable. There was some mold on the wall near the air conditioner outlet, but I'm sure this was a strange/rare/uncommon occurrence and I let the front desk know about it.

“Nice view from upper floors” I have stayed at this hotel a handful of times for business, it is a really nice Sheraton hotel. I would probably consider this one of the best Sheratons I've stayed at. It is very conveniently located right next to the airport, however not so close to restaurants and shops. Rooms on the higher floors have amazing harbor or city views... although the harbor view rooms can also be quite noisy when the pool is busy. It is a little confusing with the two towers, and if you're a spg platinum expecting to use the lounge, make sure you're in the tower that has the lounge, otherwise it's an annoying trek each morning. Self parking is also a bit awkward, on the far side of the hotel, requiring you to walk all the way around.

“Blame it on the third party” I booked an Oceanfront Two Room Suite through a third party, confirmed my reservation with central Hyatt reservations and twice with the Guest Services personnel at the hotel. At check in they had me wait 10 minutes due to my reservation being a different night in their computer. They blamed the third party for the mix up and the option they gave me for a different room was not comparable. (made me feel like I was an idiot for booking through a third party as well and the manager wanted to get back to me in 10 minutes when I called because she was too busy working the phones-at a 420 bed fully commited hotel) We ended up with two rooms (standard) and after complaining about the service; free breakfast. If this is a four star property I would like to say that the service was not. Third party buyers BEWARE.

“Amazing stay!” I went to meet a friend in Chicago and we stayed here for 3 nights. It was heavenly! Service was great, all requests were delivered promptly and with a smile. The bed and room was comfortable and it's convenient for shopping, especially in the winter when you don't want to go outside. Lovely hotel.

“Average Hotel - Expensive for a RoomView, But Worth It!” Spent 2 nights in Chicago for a leisure trip with my wife. Using my PC points I received a king bed with view on the 20th floor. The hotel starts on the 15th floor of the building it sits on. Slept pretty good, the room view was great as we had mostly clear skies. Bed was just right. Water pressure was weak. However, the staff are like any other "Big City" hotel. Short spoken, get to the point, no room for conversation and unlike some of the other reviews I read before booking this trip; NOT helpful. Beware of the Chicago Parking Scams while your there if it's your 1st time (Ticket your car, even though you paid because your out of town) (YES, THIS HAPPENED TO US). Average cost is $3.00 for 2 hours for the "Pay to Park". Easier if you find a all day garage (Usually around $14 a day). PRO: Location CON: Parking fees $36 a day Thanks PC Gold Member

“Nice respite from the noise and bustle” I stayed at the Westin last week while up there on business. Check in line for Starwood members was longer than the line for "regular folks" (15 min wait) and I almost switched places, but someone kept beating me to it. Staff was very gracious. Room on 26th floor was very nice and spacious although I was surprised to hear how loud the noise was from doors shutting in the hallway, folks walking around, etc. Was charged $6 as a "handling fee" for having the Business Center send out a package via Federal Express. Room service was excellent (nice service, yummy), but equally expensive. I find it somewhat odd that one can only get a bathrobe upon request and the newspaper is not left at your door, but instead is left in a stack by the elevators. The combo of the two could result in some weird moments if folks caught you grabbing your paper first thing! :) I did hear other business folks talking to each other about how they prefer this hotel over others as well...one benefit to standing in the check-in line for so long. Overall, I agree and I'd stay here again because the bed is deliciously comfortable and the folks were so nice, but there are some rough edges that could be corrected.

“If Washington slept here- I hope they changed the sheets!” Actually, I did find this hotel to be very clean, and I am a bit picky when it comes to stuff like that. This hotel met all my expectations for a small boutique style encampment. Check in was lightning fast and the small old fashioned elevator matches well with your small old fashioned room. The ambiance of the hotel is not that great, as it has a boarding house feel to it. I also hope you like Japanese food, as the adjoining sushi restaurant wafts tempura smells down the corridors for most of the evening. As I stated, the room is tiny, and the walls are fairly thin. There doesn't seem to be much more than your headboard separating your bed from the hallway behind it. Ear buds and an I-Pad will come in handy for your beauty sleep, particularly if Washington and the troops are in town!

“Small but perfectly formed” Stayed at Club Quarters for 2 nights. Had heard that the rooms were small, so booked a standard rather than a club room. Still on the small side, but stylish and well equipped. Good value for money for a city centre hotel. We did valet parking for convenience, but we saw that our car was parked in the open air, public car park which is just about 100 yards from the hotel on the opposite side of the road. Good coffee was available in the lounge area on a complimentary basis all day. The reception staff were very friendly and helpful. You are able to help yourself to extra coffee, coffee mate, tea bags, bottled water etc. at any time. Downtown Houston is not very tourist-friendly. However, the theatre district is only about 10-15 minutes walk away, where Bayou Place offers a variety of restaurants and bars.

“Nice room, shame about the lobby” I arrived in New York on 6 March 2004 to find my hotel full, so they had checked me into the Carlton. The location was fine, as were the rooms. The lobby area though was being renovated. The lobby was tiny therefore and only one of the lifts seemed to work. A nice touch was the complimentary coffee first thing in the morning.

“Comfortable Stay” I stayed at the Doubletree Washington from July 22-28. The front desk person that checked me in was friendly, and I was given a room on the third floor (The bedroom itself was spacious, but the bathroom was very small). I did not see any mice while there, and no one from the group that I was with ever mentioned anything about seeing mice as well. Hopefully, the mice incidents are a thing of the past. I ate at the 15 Ria each morning, and was paying $12-$15 on average for each breakfast. I was always seated right away, but the level of service varied. The two male servers that I had were often attentive and friendly. However, the female server that I had a couple of the days would just take my order and give me the bill right after I started eating my meal. Although the food was good, I would recommend for families that you head next door to the Holiday Inn where they have a breakfast buffet for $15.95. Washington is a very expensive city; therefore, be prepared for high food prices (and slow service in many places). Some of the more affordable restaurants are in Union Station (off the Metro red line), along with some restaurants off M street near 17th Street. If you are coming to DC and are on a tight budget, I suggest heading to Pentagon City a couple evenings where there are plenty of affordable sit-down restaurants in the area. I had a great stay at the Doubletree, and would stay there again if it was for business purposes. Otherwise, I would consider staying at another hotel with a swimming pool if I was travelling for pleasure.
“何かと便利です” 皆さんが書かれているように日本語のサービスがありますので安心です。 建物自体は年期が入っていますのでチョット気になる所もありますが、清潔ですし場所も便利なので何回か利用しています。 いわゆるマンハッタンまで徒歩15分程です。 利用者はビジネスマンも結構います。 部屋の広さは決して広いとは言えませんが、インターネット環境など設備には問題ありません。

“If there was an option of no stars, I would have opted for that...” I stayed at this motel for one night in October before an early flight out of the country. I really didn't want to pay that much considering I just needed a place to "crash" before my very early AM flight, so I put bad reviews aside and went for the cost factor over ratings. I am so so sorry I did... The first impression of the hotel I had was the horrible service I received checking in. He was very short with me and didn't really help me answer any questions I had. I asked him twice if my frequent flyer number was on my reservation and he assured me it was. I should have asked for my money back the moment he told me to go through my car and make sure I had nothing sitting out in it, everything was locked, and that they were not liable for theft. This should have really forewarned me for what was about to come... The elevator ride up to our floor made me feel like I was in a prison. More foreshadowing of my stay...The room was ok but really worn down. I didn't use the shower because I didn't get the impression that this was a very clean motel. Parking was right underneath the rooms and within eye view to the hotel office. The parking, however, was not secure so anyone from the street could walk through. So this is where my story truly begins... For the remainder of the night I was serenaded by streetwalkers, crackheads, and heroin addicts arguing with each other and even sometimes themselves. Things were so loud I could not sleep at all. I think I got about 30-45 minutes of real sleep. Did I mention they have wake up service??? It's called waking up to your car windows being smashed in at 4am RIGHT IN FRONT of the main office! I notified the manager what happened and he seemed to not really care. He didn't even come out to look at the damage on my vehicle! I was parked inside of the parking area in the stall literally right in front of the office. When I asked him why he didn't run out and do anything or even take the time to peek out there he casually mentioned that this happens all the time and pretty much that it wasn't their problem. This was a really nice farewell from the U.S. the morning of my 3 week trip to China too. I don't think I ever have had such a bad experience at a hotel. I know my windows being broken were not under the manager's control, but his reaction to it most definitely was. You don't need to be the trendiest and most expensive hotel to wow me, but I expect some level of respect and professional hospitality, especially to make up for the fact that your hotel is run down, in a horrible area, and unclean. Please do yourself a favor and book elsewhere. I could have stayed at a 5 star hotel for the price I paid to replace my windows!

“Great location” Great location, had to use room key in elevator to get to floor the room was on and everyone had trouble with that at first. Nice rooms, clean, a bit noisy on the Market Street side but still in a great area right across from the Ferry Building and the best felafels right across the street. Great shopping too and loved all the art in the area!

“small rooms with a political agenda” I have never stayed at a hotel in the USA where the politics of the franchisee controls what the hotel offers before i stayed here. The rooms are small and very dark as the windows are two feet from the building next door so it looks like midnight at noon in most of the rooms. The cable offerings are scant, and FoxNews network is not offered. When i asked why, i was told that it is because it is not fair to Muslims, and the internet access code was Sept 11 per the bearded ( and scary) front desk clerk. the hotel is clean but i can see why the rates are consistently lower than any others in a very high-rent part of Park Ave. And the Clarion on 23rd, which may not be run by the same franchisee, seems to never have Fox New network "working" when it supposedly is offered. and you have to be a very agile person to reach the air conditioner located at the top of the window standing on the bed. I'm over 6' tall and could barely reach the controls, and in a very dangerous reach where i'd go through the window if I slipped. I won't be coming back here again.

“Great mix of luxury and history” This was our first trip to Detroit. This hotel is beautiful and accommodating. We had a lovely room, they easily and graciously allowed a very early check in and the staff was friendly and professional. We only stayed one night and didn't try any of the restaurants, but would certainly go back if visiting Detroit again. Got a great rate of $84 on Hotwire.

“Modern escape in a city of old-world charm” We spent a weekend in Boston and stayed at Nine Zero Hotel. We are big fans of Kimpton Hotels. They are generally well-kept, modern and in great locations, without being ridiculously overpriced. The hotel was across from the old graveyard which is a big tourist attraction, and is close to the Freedom Trail, Boston Common and a short walk to Feneuil Markets. The room was spacious, clean and modern, and the decor was gorgeous. If you get a chance make sure you visit the Old Oyster House, which they say is America's oldest restaurant. The clam chowder there can't be beat!

“It's okay” I stayed at the Radisson on the Wharf for 3 nights. Like all the previous reviews said, the location is great. It is right there on the Wharf (being the only true "oceanfront" hotel) and it is less than a minute's walk from Pier 41--where you catch the blue and gold fleets to Alcatraz. Public transportation is also only a minute away from the hotel and the surrounding area is nice and safe. I had a clean room with 2 standard beds, a fridge and coffee maker. Compared to other hotels I've been in, the room was a little small, but it was fine. However, the walls are paper thin and I stayed on the second floor in a room facing the intersection of Powell and Beach so I could hear the cars and busses go by. (this was no fun since I was already adjusting to the East-West Coast time change). But other than that, it was okay. If you are looking to really soak up the city and set up base from the Wharf, I really recommend this place. I booked through a major hotel consolidator for $70 a night, and so for the price and location combined, I would stay here again.

“Uneven” Just finished 4 nights at this hotel, my client's choice &, overall, 'uneven' is about the best way I can think to describe it. The beds are comfy, though I don't know why Hilton has moved away from using fitted bottom sheets on the beds when so many other hotels do, including Hilton Garden Inns & Hampton Inns, both members of the Hilton family. They have done away with both the 'don't steal me' hangers & hair dryers & though the bathroom is on the smallish side, it is very functional. Unlike other hotels that encourage guests to hang their towels for re-use, & then change them anyway, mine actually were left hanging to be re-used. Our room rate included breakfast each day & though it's a buffet, it's a very substantial one w/cooked to order eggs & waffles (no pancakes, though) as well as plenty of breads, fruits, cereals, etc. Now for the not so good. My room was missing the bedside phone & desk phone was not working-both of these were brought to the attention of the housekeeping supervisor w/in an hour of arrival in the room, but nothing was ever done about it. The only plug in the vicinity of the desk was literally under it-not pleasant having to crawl under the desk twice/day to plug/unplug the laptop. Lighting in the room, overall, is very low. It took two requests, & two days, to have the missing box of tissue in the bathroom replaced (also pointed out to the housekeeping supervisor on day 1); my colleague 2 doors down had the same problem, in addition to the toilet in his bathroom stopped working the night before we left (ugh!). They no longer deliver papers to the guestroom in the morning, claiming the papers 'weren't being used', however, it was an adventure to find papers for each of us each day & we did resort to sharing twice. We had dinner in the restaurant, Delmonicos, one night (as it turns out, the night before the 'official' opening) & while the food was ok (wouldn't recommend the crab cakes, though), the service was incredibly slow. Our first night there, we ate in the Polo Lounge as Delmonicos is closed on Sunday (sweet potato fries were very good, btw). The bartender in the lounge, when asked about other restaurants in the vicinity, recommended CHOPS Restaurant about 2 blocks away. Since one of our clients also made the same recommendation, on Wed evening, 4 of us walked the 2 blocks, downhill, to CHOPS for an early dinner, arriving at approximately 6:15. Despite there being exactly 3 people sitting in the dining room, we were told they were 'booked completely until 7:30'. Needless to say, we took our business elsewhere that night!

“Great Location!” Stayed there for our Spring Break trip to NYC. We have visited many times and try to find something that has good access to the subway but not sacrificing comfort. This was a great find for us. Very comfortable rooms, great beds, breakfast was plentiful - something for everyone. Just around the corner from the red line and a couple blocks from the yellow. A stones throw from many of the theaters. A nice walk to Central Park. Very good location for us. Staff was great - friendly and nice. Will go back! Probably ask for a room on the back side, though - 8th is busy and LOUD!

“LLL - Location, Luxury, Location” The room was very modern, yet very comfortable. The staff was great and friendly, making a wonderful recommendation for breakfast, El Pueblo on Queen Anne. Within a block of Key Arena. Highly recommend!!!

“Fantastic location for the price!” Our room was of a good size, comfortable & very clean. We had 2 queen beds & it fit our family of 4 perfectly. Parking's rather limited but we managed to get a park every night. The complimentary continental breakfast was more than adequate - bagels, croissants, bread/rolls, tea, coffee, hot chocolate, juices. You can help yourself to free coffee & tea available throughout the day. A PC with free internet access (in the lobby) is a wonderful service for guests. Staff are very friendly & helpful. Kudos to Alben in paticular! Lots have been said about him already & we throroughly agree. Love the location as it's in the heart of Hollywood & very easy to get to the different attractions. Universal Studios is only 1 train station away. Leave the car in the carpark & take the train! Would definitely stay here again.

“A Gem in San Diego” Located smack in the center of downtown, across the street from Horton Plaza and a block from the Gaslamp District, the US Grant is a beautiful old dowager hotel. Rooms are spacious, service is great, and the hotel is registered as a landmark. As with nice hotels in the downtown areas of a number of American cities, one does come across a significant homeless population, but these people are (mostly) not dangerous. There is a great "happy hour" each afternoon in the restaurant, where one can sit back and relax while people-watching.

“Einwandfreies Business Hotel!” Wenn Sie beruflich in Houston sind, ist das Renaissance wirklich eine Empfehlung wert. Für Privatreisende ist es ein wenig entfernt von den Happening Points gelegen. Das kompensiert das Hotel jedoch mit einem vorzüglich orientierten Shuttlebus-Service. Ein weiterer Pluspunkt: die superschnelle Internet-Verbindung, die gratis angeboten wird.

“Best Stay/Park/Fly value” i have stayed here several times when I have a morning flight. For $100 pre-pay I get a nice room, free shuttle to the airport every 20 minutes and secure parking for my car. The staff is always friendly and helpful - and the warm chocolate chip cookie is such a treat. Several computers (no waiting) ready for boarding pass printing, a Starbucks in the lobby and a restaurant/room service. A wonderful way to start any trip.

“Great Location! Great Hotel! Can't wait to go back” We arrived at the Omni and were immediately greeted by Joe, one of the doormen. He loaded our bags on a cart and escorted us into the reservation desk. Check in was quick and the front desk staff was friendly. The hotel lobby is exquisite with the ambience one would expect from the early days. Ornate crown molding adorns the walls. Our room was on the 4th floor room 462; we didn’t have a view but didn’t need one because the view in the room itself was fabulous with two beds, a sofa sleeper, two chairs, a desk, two closets, a small changing room. While the bathroom was small it worked fine for the four of us. The bathroom was very nice and clean. We parked at the Post Office parking garage, it’s in walking distance to the hotel. The cost was $9 from Saturday evening until Monday morning as compared to the $40 per day for Omni valet parking. Stop in at the Parker Lounge for famous Boston cream pie you won’t regret it.

“Bait and switch, customer service doesnt return emails since their phone reps give out false information” This place looks nice, but keep in mind a $17+ Resort fee for things other properties in san diego would give you for free. Really Hard rock, i dont need the latest issue of rolling stone. Hotel bait and switched me and countless others and then had the nerve to not try and mend the problem. Contacted the tripadvisor review guy (Mdufor) after hotel asked me to do so, but he didnt help me at all, then I replied to him with the information necessary for him to help as the hard rock stated he would but that email wound up being bounced back to my inbox the next day? Maybe he blocked my address rather than try to help me. Always had wanted to stay here thus my reservation. I will stick to the great 4 star properties located nearby that DO NOT have resort fees and have great customer service! As for the room, quite small and there were HAIRS in the shower! Come on hard rock, i dont need some other guests hairs. Obviously I expect a response from tripadvisor guy now, but what good is it unless i was to return. There was potential to return given a ridiculous rate/offer, but hard rock messed that up too, that is a whole other story, that i will refrain from mentioning here on tripadvisor, you can look up their twitter account regarding their "black friday promotion" and see for yourself.

“good for some families!” I stayed at the W with my preteen and teenage daughters for a weekend of shopping and sightseeing. The location was walking distance to both Navy Pier and Michigan Ave. shopping. My daughters really enjoyed the hip atmosphere of the hotel. The pool was great, because there were so few families there. The water was warm and there were not lots of out of control children screaming and taking over the pool. It was quiet and the girls had the pool to themselves. They didn't want to leave it! The rooms are small but we had a great view of the city. The girls also loved the bath products. So for this family, the W worked and we would stay again.

“Updated Rooms, Good Location” One of the easiest hotels to find in Dallas, right off I35 near AA Center and Victory Plaza. Recently updated hotel rooms and lobby. Restaurant I would rate as average for this level of hotel. Good news it plenty of great restaurants from 2-3 miles away. Rooftop (31st floor) pool and gym. For sure will stay again The massive Hilton Anatole is across the street. Big advantage for the Renaissance is that you can go from your car to any room in 3-4 minutes its a tall hotel, at the Anatole it can literally be nearly 10 min from the car to your room.

“Fabulous hotel with great service” On our way back from skiing in Maine, checked in on a FREEZING cold night with plans to walk to a restaurant in Copley Square. Instead we checked out the bar area of the Jurys, which seemed to be the place to hang out. Nicely dressed crowd of interesting people. Ended up ordering dinner off of the bar menu. The lobster bisque was some of the best I've ever had. Reasonably priced menu and great atmosphere. The decor at the hotel is very modern, nicely appointed and boutique-like and the rooms, although not oversized, are comfortable. Great mattress and the shower was heavenly. Wish we could have stayed longer.

“Sufficient if you cannot find anything else” Boston was busy this week and hotels were booked out everywhere seemingly. The double tree was not a hotel of preference, but it was available and close to where I was staying so I booked in there for one night. The lobby is quite nice and the staff friendly. Check in was a breeze and the cookie they give you was delicious actually. At times the lifts were a little slow, but there is a hexagonal staircase that you can take as there is not many floors in the hotel. The furnishings are 90s and dated, but there are signs stating that they are currently updating. My first impressions of the room were that it was spacious enough and neatly presented. The bed was very comfortable and large in size. There was a full size duvet that you could pull up which is rare these days and welcomed in winter for example. The AC unit was old and a little difficult to figure out, I think an lcd touch system would be much better. The room itself was nice enough but the bathroom was a let down. Small, with no bathrobe and only 2 thin towels. There were neutrogena shampoo, conditioner and body lotion and a bar of soap and shower cap. There is no bath and it is an old, ugly shower. The roof in the bathroom is like an office roof. There were hotels in the corners of some squares, quite unattractive and I question if disease can breed etc.. this way.

“Great Family Hotel” We stayed here three nights with family members. We had a total of three rooms. The rooms were small, but nice enough. Each room had a small living room area with a connecting bedroom and a small bathroom. The toilet and bathtub/shower were in one room, and the sink was outside. Works out well when multiple people are getting ready to go. There were two televisions, which the kids love - no fighting over tv shows. The rooms also had a refrigerator and I think there was a microwave also, but we never used it. Breakfast included a large selection of items - cereals, breads, sweet breads and rolls, fruit, waffles, eggs and sausage. No one went away from breakfast hungry. A computer was available free of charge off the lobby which comes in handy for checking area restaurants and directions. The beds were comfortable, however the bed linen was very wrinkled, worn and tired looking. I would recommend updating the sheets. All in all, a great stay.

“Couldn't have been worse....” You know what they say: "I wouldn't stay here if it was the last hotel room in the city...." Well, I needed a hotel at the last minute, didn't have a lot of options since it was a peak period for tourists, and, unfortunately, ended up at the Braxton. When I checked in, I was given a room on the first floor with a single bed and not much more. There was a small television (with sub-par reception) at the foot of the bed, wedged between the bedframe and the window, and nothing else. There wasn't any space! The room was considerably smaller than the typical college dorm room - there was barely enough room to open the door next to the bed and only 18-24 inches between the side of the bed and the wall. The room lacked a closet and, all told, I think it was even smaller than the closet in the mid-priced hotel I'd stayed in the previous week. The good news, if you could call it that, was that the room had its own bathroom, admittedly a closet off a closet, but at least it had a shower with running water. Bad news? I wanted my shower shoes. I asked to change to a different room, but was told that there were no other vacancies. The only real upside was the location - it was a short walk to several good restaurants. I picked one and took myself to a nice dinner - a brief reprieve before heading back to the hotel for an unpleasant evening of tossing and turning on a thin, lumpy mattress. I thanked my lucky stars that it was just a single-night stay - and that my wife wasn't with me. She really would have hated this place, and might even have suggested scoping out one of the benches at a nearby park. Next time, I'll fight the traffic to commute in from Baltimore or even Richmond before I'll stay at the Braxton Hotel.

“Nice boutique hotel.” It's a nice boutique hotel about 15 min walk to the liberty bell visitor center. However the 1st room they gave us had some mechanical problems with the bathroom lights which made it creepy. They were able to move us and upgrade us to a bigger room so it wasn't so bad except the following day the bathroom lights was having mechanical issue. The breakfast included was great. They only have one elevator so it can be quite a wait. I left my amtrak ticket when i checked out and I am so glad the housekeeper left it with the front desk staff instead of throwing it out. Points for that! There's free coffee and tea in reception. The staff were okay. You can tell the hotel is newly renovated so it's clean. Overall, I recommend this hotel. I paid 179 per night via visit philly website.

“Convenient - Super location” Stayed here while visiting colleges with my daughter. The room was large and well appointed; the staff was very helpful and you can't beat the location. We walked just about everywhere!

“Good Value Hotel For Those Looking to Save Money” My wife and I stayed at this hotel in room 312 from August 11, 2010 to August 15, 2010. Although we did encounter some issues, we were pleased with our stay. The hotel is located just minutes from the airport, but you do not have to worry about jet engines roaring above the hotel. There’s a Wendy’s and a convenience store across the parking lot. They have a free shuttle to and from the airport, but we had a friend pick us up. If you do not have a car, we took the number 16 bus directly into Downtown Columbus for only $1.75. The ride took about 30 minutes and the bus stop is right across the street. Check-in was very quick. The room was of a decent size and very clean. We found the bed and pillows to be very comfortable. I was particularly impressed with the large selection of television channels. There was a sofa, desk, chair, refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker, and room safe. The AC worked great. Unfortunately, the maid forgot to clean our room one day. The bathroom was on the small side, but I liked that the sink was located outside. The main sink faucet was not attached or fixed. The shower pressure was great as well as the complimentary shampoo. The soap bars were not that great and were small. We had plenty of towels. This hotel has an indoor pool and hot tub. The hot tub was great with very strong jets. The pool was a little chilly for me though many others swam in it and said it took a few minutes to adjust. The Best Western does not have to worry about guests stealing the pool towels. That’s because they were so tiny. I felt like I was drying off with a large dish rag. I did like that the pool area was open until 11 pm every night. I was very impressed with the free breakfast. Similar hotels only have a cold continental breakfast. The Best Western had a waffle maker to make hot and fresh waffles as well as hot sausage and egg patties. They had apple juice, orange juice, cereals, bagels, fruits, toast, and fruit salads. They had free coffee and tea 24 hours a day. I was glad they had two free internet stations. I very much enjoyed my stay and believe this hotel represents an excellent value for the money you pay. Marc T. Hardekopf

“At $181.00 it was a steal for DC. Loved the Starbucks in the Lobby. Very friendly staff. Great location.” Located right at the Metro, walking distance to many restaurants and the White House. A little older but the bed was extremely comfortable. I like the nicer shampoo and amenities in the bathroom, they provide cotton balls and q-tips and use Bath and Body Works Aromatherapy shampoo and soaps. There is a concierge level with free snacks if you are a member of the frequent user program.

“Excellent value, location and stylish” One day trip - arrived late evening to a warm welcome. Quick trip to the room which was small but not cramped. Everything was clean and updated. Window unit for AC worked just great and even provided white noise from the street below. I'm a Kimpton FT so the two free waters were very nice after a 4 hour flight as was the free wi-fi. Great location at the entrance to Chinatown and close to Union Square. Very friendly and helpful staff. Would definitely stay again!

“A Diamond in the Rough” I had seen this hotel as we pass Texas Motor Speedway and had always wondered what it was like. We have pondered going to a race and with the traffic being what it is on race days, this would be PERFECT to attend the races. So when we were invited to a party at the hotel, I was happy to accept so I could check it out. The "excellent" rating I'm giving it is mostly for the wonderful service we received on several different occasions throughout just this one night stay. I made reservations to stay the night before I knew that a special rate was being contracted for the party guests. By the time I called about the special rate, the 20 room block was full. The clerk on the phone asked the manager and I was given the special rate. No fuss, no muss. After a horrendous hour long drive up I-35 from Fort Worth (this drive should take 30 minutes), the cocktail hour was already starting and we still needed to check in and change into proper clothing. I walked in apparently with the drive written all over my face and said something to the effect that we still had to change. The clerk at the desk had me checked into that room within 3 minutes. We got to the party in plenty of time. Our room was 8th floor, great view of the Speedway and we could kind of see the Gift of Lights event they have going on. The room was clean, bathroom clean, everything working, quiet hallway, comfortable bed. Hooks in the bathroom are a MUST!!! That's the only thing I had a problem with in the room. The party was great. The food was very good, the table placement and ambience was lovely. My husband went out to get us drinks after supper and being the super party animals that we are, the buy a ticket order your drink thing was confusing. Plus he didn't realize the denomination of the bill I gave him ($20). So after being confused, he put the bill in the tip jar for some reason that I still don't understand other than to thank them for trying to help him. But he came back minus $20 and minus anything to drink. This really put a pall on the evening... he was very embarrassed. But about 10 minutes later, a girl came in with the two drinks he had ordered. And the night was saved. So I don't know who recognized that an error was made, but thank you for saving the evening for us and helping him feel better. Check out was smooth (be aware they put the bill on the doorknob, not under the door). We didn't use express checkout in the room because I didn't see a bill. All in all a great night out to be grownups. Now I have to figure out how to get a room during a race weekend.

“Good size room for NYC” One of the better rooms I have stayed in in New York. Good size. Comfortable. Great location near Grand Central. Friendly service. No complaints. We had a lot of baggage and they were very helpful.

“Great Stay...Restaurant Fantastic” We stayed at the Adagio for 5 nights and would highly recommend it. The room we were given on the 6th Floor was very spacious and quiet. My husband even commented if we brought our two kids along we would not have been cramped in this room. The location is convenient, it did seem close to shady neighborhood, but we just didn't venture there. Several good places to eat nearby, but make sure to try Cortez. We didn't expect much from a hotel restaurant but the food was one of the better meals we ate in SF & we went to several high end places. We had great drinks (love the cucumber gimlet) & snacks one night & it was so good we went back the next night for dinner- equally as delicious. The staff was friendly & accomadating even recognizing our 20 yr anniversary with wine & chocolate. We would not hesistate to go back there again.

“Well located Nice North Dallas Hotel Close to the Galleria” Picked this hotel up bidding priceline.com for $40 great value.As an SPG.com preferred member they were forced unhappily to supersize me to best available so I got a GREAT suite overlooking the Galleria for that price.Rooms were perfectly renovated bed was the usual AWESOME sheraton bed I slept very well.Staff was not terribly friendly I think probably because I had gotten such a great deal and knew they had to give me an upgrade and held their feet to the fire.Restaurant downstairs had abysmal serivice and mediocre food.Fitness areas were old and poorly laid out.Still for value for me it is a very nice play in a great location.I will return if I can get a great deal again.

“Try the Aloft if you are looking for a different hotel experience” I love the Aloft hotel chain and stay at them frequently during business trips. This is a great mid priced hotel and is a newer property which was built in 2009. The lobby area is fantastic and full of energy and wide open spaces. Everything about this place is modern and they definitely market towards a younger crowd with dance music, neon lights, and bold colors in the lobby and public areas. The rooms are on the smaller side, but they find ways to make it work with a built in desk and wall mounted TV. The room design is unique and I love the walk in showers. Each room has a refrigerator which is great and I was told that some rooms are now getting microwaves. The entire property offers free internet which worked great during my stay. I also loved the fitness center which has several cardio machines, free weights, and a weight machine. This hotel was having some issues with their TV's when I arrived and I had to move to a couple different rooms to find a TV that was opperational. The front desk staff was polite during this process and we eventually got things worked out. This hotel is in a great location and within walking distance to several restaurants and shopping. I'm looking forward to staying here again when I return to San Antonio.

“One bad night, two good ones” We stayed at four places during a week vacation of Washington/Oregon and this was the only disappointment. It started off well enough. The check-in process was easy enough and our room was very nicely appointed. As others have noted, the parking charges are pretty outrageous (though standard for a downtown location), as are the various charges for "extras" such as wi-fi. The first night we had dinner nearby (tons of options within walking distance) and came back to settle in for the evening. At about 10 p.m., we noticed quite a bit of noise in the adjacent room. It sounded like a group of young women. But the noise diminished by 10:30, so we figured they had gone to bed. Wishful thinking. At 1:30 a.m., we were awoken by the sound of several men and women in the adjacent room. Turns out the women hadn't gone to bed, but had gone out to find some friends. Not only was the now larger group very loud, but their room's smoke detector was beeping intermittently. We called the front desk and reached a clerk who sounded like he was expecting the call. He sent security up, who warned the group to quiet down. About 20 minutes later, we heard slamming doors, a barrage of profanity (many f-bombs) and realized security was back to escort the men from the room. Unfortunately, the ladies continued talking and laughing till 4 a.m. (My wife had managed to fall asleep, and I didn't want to get back on the phone and wake her up. So I just hoped the women would eventually fall asleep.) First thing in the morning, my wife visited the front desk to ask if the party group would be staying another night. The clerk said yes and that the partiers were hotel employees! To her credit, the clerk appeared very embarrassed by what she'd heard and promised to contact security to get the whole story. So they eventually moved us to a new room far away from the partying employees. And we enjoyed two restful nights after that. I hate that a couple hours marred what otherwise would've been an acceptable stay. But those few hours are, unfortunately, what we'll remember most about the hotel.

“Polite Service & Historic Hotel, But Rundown Accommodations” I was fortunate to visit San Antonio on a business trip in late June. The assigned hotel was the Omni La Mansion, and I was looking forward to experiencing this historic hotel and the Omni brand for the first time. Upon arrival, I was professionally greeted and promptly checked-in. Throughout my stay, service overall was excellent – notably the Bell Staff, Housekeeping and in Food & Beverage outlets (mostly catered events). Everyone in these areas smiled and/or greeted me at every opportunity! Although the layout was odd (I had to walk through the parking ramp to get to my wing), I enjoyed the historic status of the hotel. It does sit “on the River Walk” (as do many San Antonio hotels downtown), so one can walk out the rear door onto the walking path. Unfortunately, the room was well below average, and unacceptable for such an esteemed hotel. The room smelled uncomfortably musty, and every time the ventilation fan was on (which was almost always in Texas), the smell was that of a poorly maintained 1970s motel. On my 2nd day, I explained this to the front desk, and as I sat in the lobby to access the Internet, I heard the guest service member relay my concern by phone (to engineering I presume). However, the 2 follow up messages were related to "your AC is working now". Yes, the AC was always working, but the room smelled (assuming maybe a drainage or filter issue). In regards to the Internet, I never had a working Wi-Fi connection in my guest room. On my first night, I spent nearly 30 minutes with the 800 number support, before telling them I needed to go to bed. They assured me (as did the front desk when I reported the issue the next day) it would be corrected. It never was, and I had to sit in the lobby to use my computer. This was the case for other business associates attending the same meeting. For an Omni Hotel, these 2 events were unacceptable. While I should have requested a different room, by now, it should have been offered. My room (153) didn't even have a work desk/area, so my only option to use my laptop was literally, on my lap! The room featured a nice single serve coffee maker. When I went to use it, it had no power, so I dug the cord out from behind the credenza and plugged it in on a bathroom outlet. One shouldn’t need to do so at such a caliber hotel. Aside from my room issues, the hotel has an outdoor pool, but it didn’t look particularly inviting during my stay. There is a lovely hotel restaurant, but I didn’t dine at it during my visit. When I checked out, I was asked about my stay. When I told the young lady the service was great, but my room was not acceptable, she said she was sorry, then completed the transaction and thanked me for staying. I might expect this at a mid level or economy hotel, but at the Omni, the next step should have been to ask me what was not correct. I would have respectfully shared my concerns with her or a member of management, but no one asked. The history of the hotel was so appealing, however, it is clearly in need of updating. After responding to the hotel survey, I was contacted by phone, and offered a free night on a return visit. This was nice of the hotel, and a sign of their fine customer service. However, with so many other lovely and historic hotels, I would first choose another hotel option.

“One of the best choices in Times Square” Among NYC hotels, this one, along with the Time Square Hilton, are two of the very best I've stayed at. The only issue with this hotel is the check in lines, which are often very long and somehow progress slower than other hotels (much much slower). The rooms are clean, up to date, with nice furniture and housekeeping does a nice job (compared to some other NYC hotels). The noise level is suprisingly low, especially considering how booked this hotel usually is. The location is fantastic. It has a nice lounge which tends to get very busy, but is very convenient. The staff all seemed very helpful and I noted there seemed to be a high security presence monitoring the public areas. I would definitely recommend this hotel, especially if you can get it via [--] for reasonable rates.

“Budget hotel at a good location. Slightly over-priced.” We stayed for one night at this hotel. We chose this based on its location - the cheapest available in the area! Location: Excellent. Five minutes to the downtown shopping district. about 15 minutes from Pike's Place Market. However there is a gentlemen's club at the back side of the hotel and the area may not be that safe to walk around late at night. Amenities: Exercise room is minimal but equipment is functional. No cleaning agent for wiping down the machines after use though. Room: Old but adequate. The bath tub is really narrow and small. Problems with dialing outside calls. Complimentary internet access but the wire (wire only, no wi-fi) is very, very short and is awkwardly located in between two beds... I couldn't put my laptop on a desk and had to kneel down to work with my lap top. very inconvenient. Like: LOCATION Dislike: Across from Gentlemen's Club, feeling a bit unsafe to talk around at night

“Nice Hotel, but thin walls and expensive” The hotel was nice. I stayed there for a conference, so I was less concerned with the price than if I was there on vacation. If I was paying, I would say that it was on the pricey side (over $400 a night). Actually, I wouldn't have paid that much for a room. The room was nice, clean, and I had a king bed. The location of the hotel is great...within walking distance of Union Square, SOMA, and the Ferry Building. Overall a good stay, except when the patrons in the room next door woke me up in the middle of the night as they were...how should I say this...getting to know one another...if you know what I mean.

“Great Location, Huge Property” Hotel is in the heart of the theatre district and in the middle of times square. The rooms are very nice and updated. During my stay they forgot to service my room the first night but they do give you plenty of towels and it really wasn't an issue. The hotel is very large and depending on your rooms location could require a great deal of walking but if your coming to New York you usually expect to walk. All in all a great location for a business or leisure travel destination with quality beds for a great nights rest.

“good location and value, does small things right” Nothing at all to complain about, Barclay is materially less expensive than most 4-5 stars in the neighborhood, room not huge but more than sufficient, very comfortable bed, some street noise but nothing a decent pair of earplugs can't handle. As for the little things, rarely had to wait more than 30 seconds for an elevator, free newspapers, quick check in. Only minor complaint is that like most in NYC, they charge for wireless. Perfect for someone who wants a hassle free NYC hotel experience in great location, reasonable price, with no surprises.

“Good enough for a few nights.” Hard to find, hidden behind a Wendy's. Price was great! Check in and out were fine (except that the 1st room we went in had someone's clothes in a pile in the corner and cigarettes on the nightstand with a small baggie next to it). Immediately called front desk and was moved no problem. Room had lots of furniture, almost too much. Flatscreen worked fine but had no HBO (eventhough there's an HBO guide in the room). Air was great! Bed was a little stiff but manageable. There are a few restaurants in walking distance (try the Red Onion Cafe...it's good!). Bathroom is small but very clean with good water pressure (but the water drained slowly and you had to hold the handle to flush the toilet). Hair dryer, iron and board, microwave, fridge but no coffeemaker. Lots of cars in the parking lot at night but never heard a peep. Cheap, no frills or drama. Had everything we needed.

“As expected no good/bad surprises” Relative to other Crowne Plazas worldwide, this is very similar. Staying 4 days on the 33rd exec floor it was a nice view for sure, and the location is excellent for walking to major tourist attractions. Room service is expensive as expected, but the food is of a higher than usual standard. I did not have a vehicle so cannot comment on parking. Room for improvement: Definitely something up with the HVAC system. A 2 degree change would cause it to alternate between AC/Heating which led to some loud night time ventilation. I ended up switching it off so I could sleep. The lifts seem to be programmed obscurely and there can be long waits for lifts at peak times.
“Good Meeting Place” Nice hotel, great service. Location wasn't ideal. It was close to the convention center, but that area isn't the best in town.

“Great Location and Service, Physical hotel is not that nice though” The location is right next to the airport- it is extremely convenient. Parking is free too! I needed a place to stay before an early flight so I gave it a chance. I've stayed at the Embassy Suites and had a great experience, but this was actually a couple bucks cheaper so I gave it a shot. The rooms need major help. They look and feel dingy at best. The lighting was bad, the room was small, and they were noisy- no apparent sound deadening despite the proximity to the airport. I was surprised that my HHonors Diamond status got me one double bed in a small room. That being said, the service was great. The front desk person was solid at check in, the security guys were very friendly, and the wait staff at breakfast was extremely helpful. Breakfast was good by the way. Normally, great service would earn at least 4 stars, but the rooms (or my room anyway) are truly that bad.

“Low pressure showers” I stayed here a couple nights with colleagues and we all had low pressure showers. There's no worse way to wake up than to a weak shower spray. Room cleanliness was also dubious as the desk in my room was covered in dust like it hadn't been wiped down in a couple weeks. The room decor was the blandest of any W I've been. Nothing special bed, bathroom, or furniture-wise in my room...in fact it could have been a Hampton. TV channels were not in HD despite the set in the room being an HDTV. It wasn't all bad, thus my 'average' rating. The hotel is centrally located downtown within walking distance to several attractions and restaurants and a short cab ride to others. The staff was all friendly. The restaurant's breakfast was decent if expensive. The bed was comfortable. And it gets a plus for its tv entertainment - several movie choices of every genre, all in HD, with the ability to charge it to a credit card instead of the room. Too bad the regular TV/cable channels were not in HD as I mentioned earlier. Overall, it is a pricey place to stay, but I think you are paying the premium for the location and not a clean room or a decent shower. Would I stay here again? No.

“Good value in Downtown NYC” I stayed for one night after an event in the city. If you're looking for a trendy, hip hotel, well this is not the place for you but if you're looking for a strictly business hotel without any bells and whistles (except for the kind of cool lobby/atrium), then this isn't a bad choice. I checked in very late and was upgraded to a suite. The rooms were very clean and the bed was very comfortable. Located conveniently across the street from the Wintergarden. I also know there is a rooftop space -- although I didn't check it out...this time.

“Consistency” For years, the Palmer House has been one of my favorite hotels in Chicago. I appreciate the consistent service and the excellent recognition of Hilton Honors status. Without fail, I can count on a room upgrade to a suite or at least to an executive room with two full baths. Service with a smile is what I encounter everywhere in this hotel. The hotel location cannot be beat. There is an El stop nearby and plenty of shopping.

“Beautiful place to stay, pity the staff have a lack of knowledge of the area” My partner and I stayed there for three nights in May. The suite was spacious and tastefully furnished and the kitchen had everything a family would need to prepare meals rather than go out. Sadly, the young front desk staff didn't seem to know the area or its attractions despite having lived there all their lives. They knew nothing of the steam railway (which was actually out of commission at the time) and they managed to misdirect us to local Outback Steakhouse which was about a mile and a half away, but somehow they sent us on a seven mile tour! The Manager's reception was very good. The food was fresh, well-prepared and hot, and so too was the breakfast. At $89.10-$125.10 per night it was excellent value, and the setting was all that one would hope it would be.

“DO NOT STAY HERE UNLESS WANT TO BE TREATED LIKE GARBAGE AND HAVE YOUR PERSONAL SAFETY THREATENED BY THEIR STAFF” Without a question, Inn of Chicago is amongst one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in. I typically spend ~50 - 75 nights a year in hotels for both business and leisure purposes, ranging from $100/night hotels to $1,500+/night hotels. Comparing Inn of Chicago farely to its direct comps, this is by far the worst. While the hotel is conveniently located near Mich Ave, everything else about this property brings down the overall experience. For the $150/night that I paid (3 nights over the weekend), my expectations were appropriately managed so the room is what you would expect for the money. However, what I found absolutely absurd is the service. Sean at the front dest fielding the night shift is probably one of the worst front-line service employees I've encoutered. I ordered food for delivery and even though I gave permission for the delivery person to deliver straight to my room or even wait for him at the elevator on my floor (speaking directly with Sean while the delivery person was waiting in front him), he refused my request. He said only "registered" guests were allowed to go up to guest floors (keep in mind this is a 2-star hotel, not the Peninsula). When I asked if his "delivery" person was my friend, would he then be allowed to come upstairs? Sean said, "No, there is no way this person could be a friend of guests here...". So much for providing any form of service to your guests. Ironically, when I stay at the Peninsula in Chicago (where I typically stay), I have NEVER had an issue with delivery service at any hour of the evening. If it is late, the Peninsula either a) accept the delivery on my behalf and have one of their staff members deliver to my room or b) have someone escord the delivery person for delivery. Of course, the staff at Inn of Chicago did no such thing - neither suggested it nor think of it. But that's not even the bad part of the story... When I came downstairs in my pijamas to pick up the delivery (since I was forced to do so by Sean at the front desk), I was confronted by the night security person who works for the hotel. He quickly walked directly up to me and stopped 3 inches from my face as if he wanted to fight me! He then said, "...WHO ARE YOU?! WHO ARE YOU!?". Amazingly, telling him that I was a "paying guest of the hotel" was not sufficient to calm down his roid-rage to challenge his guests to fist fights. Unbelievable. I have never in my life of stay at hotels for 30+ years received service and treatment such as this. Honestly, given the number of hotel options available in Chicago within this price range, NEVER, EVER stay at this hotel. I was in town for a wedding and unfortunately this was the hotel where most guests were asked to stay.

“Are you sure this is a Hilton?” I do not have a lot of time to elaborate on this hotel, just that the best thing about it was the Cookie on arrival! No bell man came to the taxi ( Actually Car service ) to help me with my luggage, and he could SEE me and still did not come. Check in was pleasant but I got stuck with a Smoking room although I asked for a Non Smoking room. When I wanted to leave, I had to wait FOREVER for the Elevator and when one did come it was stuffed full of people and you could not get in! I finally forced people to move so I could get in after the FIFTH elevator opened its doors and I could not get in! I needed to catch a plane and could not believe this situation. Once again no Bell Man to help me at all. There are a lot of places to stay in New York. Do not make this one of your choices! ( And I am a Hilton Member! )

“Not a typical Homewood Suites” We have stayed in Homewood Suites in many other locations around the country and this particular property is simply not up to Hilton standards. The furnishings and decor is in desperate need of upgrading. The wash cloths are thin and of very poor quality, the kind usually found in a much lower class hotel. The garage is very small and the key card entry is very awkward & inconvenient. Be very careful when exiting the lower level garage if your car is low to the ground or else the car will scrape and drag! The pillows are way too soft and the bed is very uncomfortable... too hard. Be aware that if you require a room with 2 beds, the 3rd floor is the highest floor with 2 beds. We were told eveyrthing about the 3rd left had only 1 bed. The best thing about this hotel are the very friendly staff who are exceedingly helpful. Nick at the front desk was very patient in trying to answer all of our questions. His recommendation of Buckley's Restaurant, which is in walking distance,was excellent. We walked several times to restaurants (despite the hilly streets nearby), simply because we were concerned that there wouldn't be sufficient parking space in the garage upon our return. Since we were paying for garage parking, we did not want to park our car on the street. There is a Safeway grocery store only a few blocks away if one is looking to purchase food items for use in the room. Incidentally, although most kitchen items were present, there were no paper towels in the room... which was a bit odd and unlike other Homewood Suites. Most Homewood Suites are much more spacious. This looks as if it may have been an older Homewood Suites or perhaps even another chain originally, that was converted. It's laid out very much like the old style Embassy Suites, but without an atrium. Although there was no charge for the Internet (we're Hilton Honors Gold members), I had continuing difficulty in accessing the internet. Basically each time I tried while in the room, my iphone would freeze up on the hotel website. I've never had this problem previously at other hotels. I'm not certain we would stay here again, although the convenience is a strong factor.

“Average, but nice” The best way to describe this hotel is average. The rooms are dated but very clean, customer service is excellent and the valet is one of the fastest I've ever encountered in a hotel. The bed was comfortable. The dated rooms in the tower are probably what gave me the just average feeling. Honestly, I've stayed in lower star rating hotels with rooms equal or nicer than my room at the Fairmont. However, it was very clean and the staff was very pleasant. Over all I would stay there again if I got a great price, but at the full regular rate I might select a different hotel downtown. Also on a side note, I was traveling for business and frequently use room service for my dinners. The room service was some of the most expensive that I've encountered and the quality was just average. On the upside, the gentleman who delivered it was prompt and friendly.

“Something out of the ordinary” The Helix was a very pleasant discovery that I would choose again. I selected it based on the hotel's website and ended up with a large specialty room that included a DVD/plasma TV setup, high-speed internet, and a decent stereo. The decor is great and the room was in good shape. Overall, it was a great value. The neighborhood is fine, although there's not much close by. The hotel has a few rough edges--the website promised things like bathrobes and in-room safes that weren't there. It didn't bother me because the room was such a nice place to come back to, but why advertise extras if you don't have them? On the whole, the Helix is different and fun, definitely worth a try.

“Tolle Lage, Zimmer jedoch schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen” Im Handlery Union Square haben wir die Silvesternacht verbracht, da wir ein zentrales Hotel in San Francisco für diese Nacht haben wollten. Und die bekommt man mit diesem Hotel auf jeden Fall. Es befindet sich in unmittelbarer Nähe des Union Squares (keine 2 Minuten) und damit mitten im Zentrum San Franciscos. Über den Service kann ich mich nicht beschweren, wir wurden an der Rezeption sogar auf deutsch bedient. Leider ging es dort eher langsam voran, aber das lag wohl daran, dass das Hotel komplett ausgebucht war. Das Zimmer war ok, aber nichts besonderes. Die Einrichtung schien schon relativ alt zu sein (vermutlich war dies auch Absicht) und traf damit nicht 100%ig unseren Geschmack. Einen Ausblick gab es nur auf den Hinterhof. Ansonsten gibt es aber bezüglich Sauberkeit, dem Bad oder auch den Matratzen nichts zu beklagen.

“Nice, quiet, friendly.” I originally booked the Doubletree Del Mar, but then changed to this hotel due to its location. It is located adjacent to the Hazard Centre which has a cinema, restaurants a few shops and a trolley stop. Our main purpose of our trip to San Diego was to visit Tijuana and you can get there via the trolley out the front with only one trolley change. The front desk staff was very friendly and welcoming. The room was nice, quiet and clean. The breakfast buffet was OK, it was included in our package so we just had cereal and fruit but there was the usual scrambled eggs, bacon but also had french toast. The hotel has two pools, an outdoor and an indoor and both are heated. It also has a print facility which was handy to print our tickets to the zoo. The trolley also provides easy access to the Gaslamp Quarter and waterfront. Overall we had a great stay at this hotel, the staff were great, the location is great if you want to use the trolley and the room was quiet.

“Great airport hotel” After a week in my old home town for business, I decided to stay at Logan the night before my 6 AM flight home. I returned my rental car and the car company's shuttle dropped me right off at the hotel (as opposed to leaving at the terminal to call the hotel's shuttle). Check in was quick and easy...there was a flight crew checking in as well and the three people behind the desk took care of us all within a few minutes. The room was a big surprise. I used to stay in Embassy Suites hotels for work and this one is nothing like the ones I remember. Inside, it's completely new. The rooms are large and bright with good kitchettes and HUGE bathrooms. The bathroom had a door into the living room and a door into the bedroom...nice touch. There was enough furniture to allow a few people to lounge around and watchin TV, but not enough to crowd the room at all. The walls were solid and I never heard a a neighbor or a plane (any business traveler who has stayed at an airport hotel knows how important this is!). I was only in this hotel for about seven hours, but they were good ones. When I checked out at 4 AM, the guy working the front desk was cheerful and upbeat. There was a security guard there as well and the shuttle driver was equally chipper. It was a quick stay, but one I'd say tops those I've had at Embassy Suites hotels.

“Shame, shame! Foreign travelers beware!” Although I have stayed at Palmer House before and have had a nice stay, out of town friends that my family was hosting, recently had an experience that is worth sharing. This is the first time I have awarded a hotel 1-star in one of my reviews and I don't mean to suggest that this is a one-star hotel but rather that we had a terrible experience. I always have read one-star TA reviews with a bit of skepticism that the reviewers were just malcontents, I hope this is not taken the same way. Friends from Chile were traveling to the U.S. and booked a room a month in advance at the Palmer House for their Chicago leg. Their credit card was charged for the room. Three days before they were to arrive in Chicago from Wisconsin, our friends received an e-mail that the hotel was not able to verify the foreign address on their credit card and therefore canceled the reservation three days before their arrival. This although the credit card had already been charged for the room. We called the hotel to straighten out the problem but were told there were no rooms available now and that they were unable to do anything about it except refund the amount already charged. The only room our friends could find in downtown Chicago on three days notice was a run-down Travel Lodge -- a far cry from a hotel like the Palmer House. There were so many better ways for the Palmer House to handle the situation and they should be ashamed for their complete lack of customer service. As a Chicagoan, I am embarrassed as this reflects poorly on the city (country?) as a whole to a foreign visitor. Shame on Palmer House for not taking responsibility! As a side note, I looked through other TA reviews of the hotel for similar problems and noticed that although there were numerous one- and two-star reviews, there was no response from management on any that I saw (perhaps there are responses to some I did not read?). On the other hand, for a number of the five-star reviews, Palmer House management responded, thanking the reviewers for their comments. As manager of a large hotel, wouldn't you be more interested in addressing poor experiences guests have had rather than thanking happy guests? I guess not.

“Excellent Hotel, Lousy Location” My wife and I stayed here for two nights in December. We booked this on Priceline, we bid $55.00 and would up paying about $72. per night with taxes. First the positives. -The room was very large and clean. -It had a full kitchen that had a microwave, a two burner electric stovetop and a full size refrigerator. The kitchen also had very nice selection of utensils, dishes, pots and other cooking implements. -The breakfast buffet is one of the nicest that I have seen. People who are on Atkins or other diets should have no problems here. -Parking (valet) was $20.00 per night, which is about $10.00 cheaper than other locations in DC. Now the negatives -Noise.The hotel is on a triangular piece of land and there is a lot of traffic on the streets. We were on the 9th floor (which was great considering that we booked the room on Priceline) and I still heard traffic noise. One morning garbage trucks came at 5:30 and woke me up. Their noise continued for about a half an hour. -Homeless people. When we came back to the hotel at night, there were homeless people in front of the hotel begging. I don't expect this at a hotel that bills itself as a 3 or 3 1/2 start hotel. -Safety. My wife and I went to dinner Sunday night at Georiga Browns several blocks away. We walked back to the hotel, which is only about 3 blocks away from the restaurant and I thought we were going to get mugged. The streets were deserted and what few people who were on the street looked like they were sizing us up. The next night when we went out to dinner, we took a cab back and forth. I have walked in many cities at night, but this was the most uncomfortable I have felt at night in a long time. I can excuse the noise, but because of the safety issues, I cannot give this hotel a higher rating. I hate to rate this hotel as "okay". We got a great rate and their staff is terriffic, but because of the safety issue, I cannot recommend this hotel.

“Excellent Location, Good Amenities, Pleasant Service, Needs Some TLC” The Nikko San Francisco is well located a few blocks from Union Square. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all major points, including SFO, which is just 25 minutes away by BART. The hotel is decidedly 1980's in its appearance and decor. The spectacular lobby is spacious and quiet, a nice oasis in a bustling neighborhood. Despite numerous complaints on this website about small rooms and lousy service, we were warmly greeted and offered an upgrade for $20 above our Priceline rate of $89. We were given a corner room, on a high floor, with stunning floor to ceiling views of the Financial District and Nob Hill. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom had been upgraded. The furnishings are all tattered, walls are scuffed, and there is visible wear and tear just about everywhere, including the spacious gym and pool area. Even the lobby furniture and elevator doors are all banged up. It's not pretty, but you don't really mind it much when you are in a very quiet, comfortable room.

“Good value but serious caveats” This hotel is a good value for being somewhat close to downtown. Excellent location if you're going to IIT MCormick Place or Hyde Park. Good things: free parking; large room (handicapped accessible so that may be an anomaly); good bathroom light. Bad things: do not walk to anything at night (and I grew up on Chicago's southside so I'm no scardy cat); expensive wi-fi that didn't work; terrible bed & pillows that smelled used; HVAC system that smelled like it was on fire when the heat was on. So, just balance off price w/location & amenities.

“Much Less Than Expected” Le Meridien has managed to transform an old "Y" into a modern, sleek hotel with courteous, professional staff. The hotel is entered by two short rows of stairs. Not a problem for us, but be warned. Also, at all costs, avoid an "atrium" view. It is the old air shaft and the open corridors let everyone stare into your room. We fortunately missed out on this treat. Our bathroom was large, modern and nicely designed and appointed with a smallish sleek shower. No tub. The bed area in our deluxe king room, however, was around 215 sq. ft and had no desk. The guest is expected to work on a high table using the 3' that are left over by the TV. The stiff raised "desk" chair that belongs next to a 1960's basement bar and the plastic cups in the bathroom summed up the disappointments. Will not return and will again stay at my usual haunts the Omni and the Palomar. Just no comparison.

“Decent accommodations, good breakfast, good location” Stayed for one night while in town for business. Got the AAA rate of ~$185 U.S. The Good: - Free wired & wireless Internet - Good A/C with a real thermostat. Too many three star Manhattan hotels have those cheap dial-based fan units so this was good. - Great LCD TV with a ton of channels. - Complete breakfast with lots of choices. - Good bathroom amenities The (somewhat) Bad: - No room safe - would have been nice to have one -

“Home away from home! Perfect stay near historical sights!” Spent an awesome 5 nights at this property to see the sights of Philadelphia. The room was clean and spacious. The bathroom had plenty of counter space. Housekeeping was excellent. Our corner room had plenty of light and and nice view overlooking Independence Park. We couldn't really hear any street noise from the 9th floor. And the noise from the neighboring rooms was minimal. The elevators were quick. No problems with the A/C unit. Large LCD TV. The bed was comfortable. The staff were all friendly. I would definetely recommend this hotel for anyone wanting to see the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall. Plenty of place to eat on Chestnut. We were able to walk to two Philly cheesteak places, Campo's and Jim's. (Campo's being the closer of the two) For fancy places there was Buddakhan and Morimoto. For casual food, there was Cosi's right across the street or at the Bourse. We also ate at Jones, Spasso's Italian, and Han Dynasty. Plenty of transportation nearby. We used the Philly Phlash and buses. We didn't have any issues with homeless in the area. We felt safe the whole time we were in Philadelphia. The only issues I had with the hotel was that the pool was tiny and our in-room safe ran out of battery twice. But this was no big deal. Taxi to and from airport was around $30.

“A good choice” Back to writing a review on a top rated hotel in NYC. I had previously stayed at the Library Hotel which belongs to the same group and was not impressed at all. However Giraffe is a different story, to begin with location is very good if you want to be around Union Square. I think the spot on Park is an excellent compromise for everything New York offers. Service is good, above average for NYC and for properties in this price range. Nice room, excellent bathroom. Very good wifi included in rate as are breakfast and the reception in the afternoon. Newspapers available in the lobby (NYT and WSJ not US Today). I paid an all inclusive price of $300 a night for 2 nights. Good but not excellent value. I don't want to sound too jaded but the hotel feels more like a brand new well managed Holiday Inn rather than an upscale boutique hotel. Still certainly a recommended hotel in NYC.

“Worst Hampton Inn I Ever Stayed In” I stayed for two nights but wanted to leave after the first night. fortunately no rooms were available in the other nearby hotels. My room's furnitures were shabby, the walls were tired-looking and the bathroom looked old and tiny. I asked for a fridge in advance but found out my room didn't have any. My requests for a fridge was all but ignored. My pleas for a change of room was turned down. The evening front desk girl was pleasant but the manager and the rest of the morning staff were grumpy and unprofessional. I stayed in three other Hampton Inns before which were all very nice but not this one. As a business traveller I would have stayed for two months but because of my negative experiences II would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

“Great stay!” The Hilton is super close to the airport with excellent airport shuttle service. Hotel has two courtyards (one with the pool and the other that's more a garden & sitting area). Workout facility was great -- new equipment, large and clean. Breakfast was great - I got a coupon at check in for complimentary breakfast which was GREAT! Parking -- is $20/day and the garage is a long walk from the lobby. BUT it's safe & clean. Room was nicely decorated, flat screen tv, great ac/heat. Bathroom small but functional. Overall, a great experience.

“Couldn't have asked for anything better” We stayed at the Hyatt Regency recently when we spent a night in San Francisco for Giants baseball games. It is so convenient to the park, walking to and from the park. The hotel itself was great. The room was so quiet that we didn't even know we had neighbors on either side or up or below us. The room was very roomy and the bed and bedding was very comfortable. The best thing was that we got the room through Priceline for only a $100.00. Another review mentioned the ridiculous amount charged for parking. Right down the street was a parking garage where we parked the car for a whopping $7 for the night. This was a great stay for an even greater price.

“Comfortable professionally run Sheraton with focus on tourists.” Set along the water's edge of San Francisco Bay, amidst the popular San Francisco's neighborhoods of North Beach and Fisherman's Wharf, the Sheraton is certainly a comfortable, clean and convenient hotel, keeping with what you'd expect of a Sheraton. This hotel has a larger focus on tourists than business-people, due to its location. While the Fisherman's Wharf area is quite tacky and cheasy and may be uninteresting to anyone but the novice tourist or a family in need of a multitude of distractions for their kids, the hotel and neighborhood puts you in walking distance of most of central San Francisco's neighborhoods (get ready for those hills!), and a taxi will get you everywhere when your legs get tired. There's also the option of the charming San Francisco cable car which conveniently stops just blocks from the hotel! (overpriced for transport, it only carries tourists today, but is fun to do once!) Rooms were quite spacious, though were in need of a slight refresh when visited in 2006. Nothing amazing, but certainly space, comfort and location. Staff was very professional.

“originale e ospitale” Il primo impatto con l'hotel, dopo il lungo viaggio da Milano a Los Angeles via Parigi, non è stato dei migliori. Avevamo prenotato due camere doppie attraverso Booking.com, ma alla reception ci dicono che è disponibile solo una stanza. Dalle ricerche della receptionist risulta la copia della prenotazione: effettivamente si tratta di due stanze. Dopo un tempo a noi parso troppo lungo, le due stanze vengono finalmente "trovate". A parte questo inconveniente, per fortuna risolto, le cinque notti passate in hotel sono trascorse senza problemi, o quasi. Infatti l'ultima notte si è intasato il bagno di una delle due stanze. In ogni caso l'hotel è una struttura originale, un motel riadattato a tema "agricolo", a pochi passi dal Farmer's Market, per l'appunto. Non cercate il lusso in questa struttura, ma le stanze sono grandi e pulite, dotate di frigo, coffee maker, tv a schermo piatto, aria condizionata, un po' rumorosa; bagni grandi e puliti.
