Il valet parking è proprio di fianco all'hotel, molto comodo, visto che a Los Angeles ci si sposta in auto. La posizione è veramente buona, in una zona tranquilla e vicino al centro hollywoodiano della città. Personale gentile e disponibile rendono la permanenza piacevole.

“Sehr guten Hotel mit bester Lage” Das Hilton Times Square ist im Zentrum von New York gelegen, nur ungefähr 2 Minuten vom Times Square entfernt. Das Hotel hat die Lobby im 8ten Stock, was aber nicht weiter stört. Die Zimmer sind Hilton Standard, und ich würde ein Zimmer in Richtung Financial District empfehlen, mit schönem Blick auf das Empire State Building. Frühstück ist auch Hilton Standard, das Restaurant haben wir nicht probiert.

“Incredible property with great staff!” Very lovely property with standing showers! Very clean and a luxury feel! Staff was incredible helpful and friendly. Will definitely stay at this property again if given the opportuny! Check-in was fast and easy and property has a number of amenities.

“Great location trumps small bathrooms” We got it for a good price and only used it to sleep, shower and regroup. The bathroom is too small and the wooden vanity pedestal made it hard to even get in or around in it. However we were steps from breakfast, late night snacks, meals, Magnificent Mile, river etc. It worked good for us.

“A brilliant hotel in a superb location” A wonderfully situated hotel, very friendly staff, surprisingly large rooms which are tastefully decorated. Within a minute's walk of a subway station and very safe at night.

“Good amenities, friendly staff” I stayed here with my boyfriend for two nights on a very busy weekend in Seattle. I was happy to snag a room here for a better price than a lot of other hotels in the area. Kimpton never disappoints. Definitely join their 'in touch' program. I got upgraded a room level and a mini bar credit. The front desk staff was super friendly. The decor is a bit overdone, but the room was a good size, clean and the bed was comfy. The wireless was not good, I just used my 3G all weekend. The restaurant serves a surprisingly good breakfast. Valet parking is expensive, but I think that's standard downtown.

“My Kids Loved the Exectutive Floor” I used some Hilton points and stayed here last year. We stayed on the executive floor. My kids loved the breakfast and the light dinners. The pool was great but it was kind of cold. The shuttle/walk to Universal Studios was very manageable. It was a fun stay for my family.

“Old and beaten” I have to assume that this was the cats meow back in 1985. Not much has been done since then. Old tube TV's, loud AC's, dark wood and wallpaper, etc... This place needs a remodel. If you are Asian, this is a great location for you and the hotel offers Japan TV as well as Japanese bathroom amenities. If you are a American, go find a newer more modern hotel. PS - July 2012 fitness center is under renovations.

“Great location. Design over function. Service variable” The location is great ; near bars & restaurants, and a short walk to Pike's market etc but relatively quiet. Attracts stylish young guests . The room was lovely and spotless but sacrificed usefulness for looks. Example: akward & noisey pocket doors on the bathroom and a bed with a frame that juts out in a way perfectly designed to attack your shins. Service was mixed. When we checked in, the desk was rude and clueless. Luckily after a while, a manager swooped in and sorted things out. My rating would be much lower if that had not happened. Overall, I would not hesitate to stay here again but it would not be my first choice.

“Basic, Very Clean, A bit noisy” My daughter and I stayed here June 7-9, 2005. As others have said, this is a basic hotel with few amenities (e.g., no pool, no business center, etc.) but it is CLEAN and was renovated about 5 years ago. The bathrooms were fairly large, by nyc standards, with new tub, toilet, and sink and hair dryers. We found the staff to be pleasant and helpful. They told us that the hotel was built in 1850 and Abraham Lincoln stayed there before he was president. On September 11th, they were working and the entire hotel shook when the towers fell. They were closed to the public for 5 months afterward, but housed the Salvation Army volunteers. The main negatives were street noise, noise from the window air conditioner, and the big lumpy foam pillows. We had a room on the highest floor (7th) on the corner of Chambers and West Broadway. The room was pleasant and sunny and we had a great view of the Woolworth Building and expensive Tribeca real estate. As many others have said, the location was great for walking to many downtown sites and convenient to many different subway lines. Also, the staff had a room to check bags.

“For the Price, Better than Expected.(Pets Welcome)” This is an older motel, much like you would see built in the 70's. The rooms are small and furnishings outdated: But what do you expect for $69.00 a night in Austin. I was afraid it would be a coackroach inn but I was pleasantly surprised by the cleanliness of the room and no bugs. The water was hot in the shower and the bed was comfortable enough. There is nothing plush about it, but that isn't what you would expect at that price. If you are just looking for a place to lay your head and aren't going to spend alot of time in the room, this is an excellent choice to save some money. It has apool that looked fine and has a basic continental breakfast. There was free WiFi in the room. It is convenient to St. Edwards Univ. (about 1 mile), and about 5 miles from UT. It is 25 miles to the San Maros outlet malls. Pets are allowed at no charge.

“Decent value, slightly inconvenient location” Nice, clean, large rooms and generally no complaints about the facilities themselves. Based on previous reviews I asked for a quieter room and ended up getting one of the best nights of sleep of my two-week roadtrip. A slight problem with the wifi connection (try refreshing the page when it says "do not refresh the page" - go figure) was revolved quickly and over the phone. Overall, a good option if you're looking to save a little money, but it's a bit inconvenient for visiting the main sites. I did walk all the way to the Alamo and back over the course of several hours with several stops along the way (would probably be 20-30 min in one shot), but ended up driving back to the Riverwalk at night and valeting my car at the restaurant ($7). Per the front desk, the streetcar, which I had originally planned on using a lot, was inconvenient because it's only every 20 minutes. I think if/when I return to San Antonio I'll book a hotel closer to the Riverwalk - the cost would probably end up a wash considering the money you could spend on parking/taxis, plus the added convenience of being right in the middle of it all.

“Great Dupont Circle Option” Excellent Dupont Circle location within 1 block of the Dupont Circle metro stop (Red line). Easy walking distance to restaurants, bars, coffee shops, grocery markets, and shopping. Really enjoyed the neighborhood. Within 1 block of Rock Creek park with lots of green space and running trails. This hotel gets a lot of traffic and it's starting to show it in wear and tear. The Kimpton In-Touch program is worth the sign-up for free internet and mini-bar credit. The hotel lobby is very crowded during the wine reception in the evening, but there was minimal noise near our 5th floor room. We had a Executive Queen-Queen room with lots of space except in the bathroom which is tiny. Overall, the room is spacious and well-appointed.

“Redone. Sets the standard for Courtyard by Marriott” Great team. Check in was so pleasant. Like I was visiting home. Newly remodeled property. Suite was great great location. Definitely returning. The location is close to everything. The staff makes the difference here.

“Nice Marriott” I do have to say that I stayed at the Marriott Suites mainly because that is what our agency booked for us, and most likely because a couple of our other favorites were completely booked. Pros: This hotel was immaculate. There were four elevators that got me up to the 8th floor in a matter of seconds. Also, the staff was very helpful: I called the front desk at around 3:30 AM for a packet of regular coffee and got it in about 3 minutes. Cons: The pillows, probably in an effort to be fashionable, were squares, and smaller than a standard pillow. They were quite comfortable, but only when my head was completely on it, which was a challenge. Also, the towels are similar to those you'd find at a Quality Inn or some other lower level hotel -- definitely not what I'd expect to see when paying over $200 a night.
“Good hotel well located” Another good hotel on our trip across USA. Good location, nice room, well maintained. Balconies to rooms.

“Muy buen hotel” Estuvimos tres noches alojados en este hotel y debo decir que es perfecto. La situacion es muy buena, para nada me pareció una zona peligrosa a pesar de lo que dicen otras criticas y eso que salímos hasta tarde por la noche. La habitaciones no son muy grandes pero es muy moderno y limpio y tiene todas las comodidades. El personal de recepcion fué muy atento. Además siempre está incluido el desayuno con cualquier tarifa y el Wifi es gratis. Sin duda volverá a alojarme en este hotel.

“It is what it is...” No matter how good the staff, the management or the web designer.(don't believe what your lying eyes see)..you cannot get away from shabby rooms, cheap finishes, mini fridge decorating the corridor, surly doormen, smelly corridors and a room reeking of bug spray before we were moved, mold on the vent in the next room, if the owners or shareholders don't care at all or are using this as a cash cow.Nice bed and towels though. All in all it must have been a gorgeous Statler but now is a hideous old hag Park Plaza....like painting over chipped, chewed nails. Not staying again.

“Nice Hotel” Stayed here 2 nights for a work trip. This isn't the closest to the convention center, however if I were to go back for personal reasons I'd stay again. The layout of the room makes it feel very spacious and the bathroom is huge with a sepearte shower stall and bath tub. The bedroom has doors which is nice if traveling with family and need privacy. The staff is very friendly and room service was good. Everything you expect from a starwood hotel. There are a lot of great hotels all within a few blocks, but again I'd go back. Try The Fish Market for dinner. Excellent seafood.
“Nice modern” Veru nice. Rooms very modern and comfortable. If you are working downtown very good place to stay. A quick train ride on the 23 gets you to time square and all the shows.
“サンフランシスコのハーバーを楽しむならここに泊まるっきゃない!” フィッシャーマンズワーフ近くのこのホテルは立地もさることながらハーバーの眺めも良く プールも広々としています。ホテル内のレストランのシーフードメニューは豊富でお勧めは やはりクラムチャウダーです。これを食べなきゃアメリカ旅行は始まりません。 ただ高層階のヒルトンが希望の方にはお勧めしません。

“Good hotel for a meeting” Attended a business meeting at the Omni in mid-June and spent two nights. The meeting facilities were excellent. Maybe the best I have been at. The microphone system was great for a large roundtable discussion. Food provided for lunch both days was top notch. The second floor where the meeting rooms are located was somewhat dated, but the inside of the rooms was fine. Meeting rooms were very quiet. There was a loud, large meeting next to ours. When in the hallway we could hear them, but in our meeting room we could not. I had a corner room with a king bed. Room was large with a couch. As others have noted the large TV in front of the big picture window is somewhat a turnoff. In the corner room the TV is to the side of the bed, somewhat harder to watch from bed. The rooms were dark. I had to turn all the lights on and it still seemed dark. The shower area in the bathroom had no lights. Only four lights above the mirror to light the room. I like bright bathrooms, so this was a turnoff. Did hear some noise in the hallway at night. Had a hard time cooling off the room at night. On the plus side, the bed and pillows were comfortable. Plenty of extra pillows and some very heavy comforters. The desk was large, ample electrical outlets and dataport for my laptop. Maid service was prompt. Staff I dealt with was friendly. Parking is on the top floors of the adjacent garage. The hotel charges $14 per night and you get in and out privileges. If you simply pay with the ticket the maximum daily charge is $10 per night. If you are not going to leave or are only staying one night, pay the $10. I did not feel unsafe in the hotel area, although we were in a large group both nights when we went out.

“Uncomfortable, noisy, rude staff” Sadly, our recent stay at this hotel was one of the worst experiences we have ever had. We stayed in the "jacuzzi room". This room had a king size bed, an old style tv, a desk, a chair, and a separate jacuzzi area that included a shower. We paid $145.00 for our one night stay there. We checked in around 6pm and had the shuttle driver (Darryl) take us to dinner before, exploring our room. (he was very professional and the only employee at the hotel that seemed to care) This was our mistake. When we returned around 8pm, it was so noisy I knew it was going to prevent me from sleeping. I called the front desk and spoke to Elizabeth. I told her the issue I was having and asked to be moved to a different room. The hotel was full and she was unable to move us. I told her that I would be calling some other locations to see if we could switch hotels because, the noise was so severe. She informed me that if we moved they were still charging us for the night because, there was no housekeeper on staff to clean the room to be rented out. I thought that was ridiculous. Unfortunatley, there were no other available rooms in the area so we had to stay. We found that the jacuzzi wasnt working, the bed was hard as rocks, and the noise naturally continued all night long. We got zero sleep and on top of that had sore necks and backs from the bed. We had a 3pm flight so we checked out around one and took the shuttle to the airport. We will never stay at this location again. PROS: free shuttle CONS: noisy, uncomfortable, maintenance issues, rude staff

“Business Traveler's Perspective” Most other reviews of this property are spot-on. Here's some info I would've liked to have known. I stayed in an Executive King room, which is one step up from the basic room. There's a bit more square footage, and a set of French doors to separate the sleeping and living room areas. If you're planning to work on a laptop during your stay, the size of the desk is inadequate and the outlets are on the wall under the desk. That's a bit of an inconvenience compared to the chains you probably stay at in other cities and expect outlets in the desk lamp or something. Wi-fi is spectacularly unreliable. You can log in and maybe get one or two actions to complete, but then it freezes up. Had I paid the $13.95 for it, I'd have been furious...but it's free for Presidents Club members. No issues with the cable, which works fine but chains you to that tiny desk. Not really sure it's worth the upgrade from the basic level room (which is why I'd chosen this room type...more space to work). Excellent service in the business center. I rented a room for meetings and the staff was impeccable. Always professional, with a friendly comment or funny quip here or there to keep a smile on your face. Breakfast service at the Georgian Room is hit-or-miss. Sometimes fantastic. Sometimes phoned in. Buffet is repetitive...eggs benedict four days in a row? Maybe it's because there was some sort of kitchen renovation going on, but still pretty lame for a hotel of this caliber. Food at Shuckers is awesome. Great local seafood goes into some really great chowders, and a crab louie salad that is as huge as it is amazingly tasty. Easy walk to malls (Pacific Place, Westlake Center), monorail to the Space Needle, and Pike Place Market.

“Will be back again soon!” I booked this hotel for a business stay, but would certainly come for leisure as well. The hotel is located right on DuPont circle so a great location for walking to all the sights of DC as well as Georgetown. It is a little challenging to find if you a driving a car and don't know the layout of the city, so I would suggest doing a little pre-planning. Traffic downtown is very heavy and there a lot of one-way streets and circles. The rooms are beautiful (great bathrooms with heated floors) and the staff couldn't be nicer. The bar is great for happy hour cocktails and very reasonably priced. The gym is sparse, but is 24 hours a day and has TVs attached to the cardio machines. I booked through Hotels.com and got a great rate of $175 a night.

“Great location at a good price” Just returned from a week at the Cow Hollow after researching many other choices, and we're happy with our decision. We paid $125 per night less a 10% AAA discount ($112.50) for a standard king room. We had a car, so the free parking was a huge plus, especially for a 6 night stay. Our friends were paying $28 per night for parking at their hotel. As others have said, the location is terrific, perhaps the biggest plus for the hotel. There are tons of great restaurants and shops within steps of your door, and there is much more of a local flavor than the Fisherman's Warf area. "Mel's" across the street may be more famous; however, the hotel restaurant, Bay Watch, was even better for breakfast. Excellent breakfasts at reasonable prices. The room was average size for a city hotel, very clean with a very comfortable bed. The a/c heating system was very efficient; however it was also pretty noisy. Not noisy enough to keep you awake, but noticable until it blends into the background. The elevator was agonizingly slow (we're from NY, so maybe we're a bit impatient?), but there are only 3 floors, so the stairs are always an option. I guess when you list the speed of the elevator as a negative, things are pretty good. We'll stay here again on our next visit, which is the bottom line for any hotel. Nice room, fair price, free parking, great reatuarant for b'kfst, in a great location.

“One of the best values in NYC” I've been here two times and love everything about the Beacon. It feels like a true NYC hotel, with its old elevators, some residents and their dogs, and a location that can't be beat. The fully equipped kitchen is a bonus and their recent renovations are tasteful, on par with the latest look in small luxury hotels. My only minor complaint is they haven't taken the extra step of upgrading bed linens, still maintaining the old blanket-style coverings and lower grade pillows/sheets. I feel like a true New Yorker instead of a visitor when I stay here - very comfortable. Even though we are on a busy section of Broadway the windows and doors provide excellent sound insulation. Try the great breakfast at Viand Cafe next to the hotel, fresh eggs, OJ, HOT coffee, homefries, and toast for less than $6. Zabar's is 5-6 blocks north and Fairway supermarket is across the street, both outstanding places to purchase goodies to bring back to the hotel. Beacon is within walking distance of top shopping and restaurants, and a 2 min walk from the restored 72nd street subway stop, which connects you anywhere in NYC.

“Excellent staff, comfortable rooms” It's the staff that makes this hotel special. They were incredibly helpful and friendly. The rooms are nice, though as other reviewers state, vary quite a bit. Avoid the x14 rooms if at all possible--we were in 814, which was much smaller than the other rooms, and also had a loud banging noise recurring throughout the day. Luckily, this didn't affect our sleep (I don't think, anyway). The restaurant attached to the lobby (Sazerac) is great, and the service there was outstanding as well--they even will give you coffee in the morning when it runs out in the lobby (which it did every morning we were there, about an hour before the end of coffee service). The location is incredibly convenient, in walking distance of basically everything you'd want to see (though my wife and I are walkers and have no problem walking a mile to get somewhere).

“Always a favorite” The Mark Hopkins is my favorite San Francisco hotel. It has great views (Top of the Mark is fabulous!) and classic San Francisco charm. The hotel is located in one of the best neighborhoods in San Francisco with easy access to Union Square, Fisherman's Warf, and the Financial District (minus the chaos). The hotel is lacking on customer service and the rooms aren't the most luxurious in San Francisco (no down comforters, but the bathrooms are nice). However, the hotel has a great gym and the restuarant/lounge on the top floor makes up for all the hotel's shortcomings. It is great to have brunch or an afternoon cocktail at the Top of the Mark. This timeless hotel warrants a visit in San Francisco and is always at the top of my list when staying in SF. It's one of the only hotels that local San Franciscans visit for cocktails and entertainment. You can't beat it's charm!

“Good, but not Great, Place to Stay in the Heart of Chicago” I stayed at the Raffaello for a one night business trip. Because my client booked the room, and they have a lot of people stay here, I was upgraded to a suite. As others have said, the hotel's location is excellent. Right across from the John Hancock Tower and only a few blocks from Water Tower Place and shopping on the Miracle Mile. I'd sum up the hotel by saying that it is generally nice, but has some limitations that might make or break it for you: You notice the first limitation upon walking into the lobby. There are only two elevators and they are slow and are not air conditioned. This is made slightly worse because the hotel has a very popular roof top bar. In the evening, the elevators are mostly full of 20somethings coming and going to the bar. The rooms are generally clean and comfortable. In my room, the air conditioning was not overly cold and the room took a long time to cool down. The chairs in the living room section showed some signs of wear and some curious stains. One of the sitting chairs had what I can only describe as a "salt ring" around it, as if someone very, very sweaty sat in it and left a white ring of salty sweat. I didn't use that chair. The bed was comfortable and did not have any signs of bed bugs, etc. The bathroom was small, but did have a nice rain shower head. I was able to get a very hot shower. Overall, I'd probably stay here again, especially given the price and the location. I'm not sure if I would bring my family here for an extended stay.

“Once is enough” We booked our room for a 2 night stay on Priceline (name your own price) and had a decent enough (for Chicago) rate of $140. The location is good, being close to lots of the action in Chicago. The decor of the rooms is modern and tasteful. The beds (2 full sized in our room) were VERY soft...which I am not fond of at all. The room was very clean. We enjoyed having a small fridge to keep drinks cool. It seems that the rooms that have a view of the river (just ask for one) have this little extra. On our check-out day, we got the customary slip under the door of our "extra charges." We expected none as we had not purchased services or merchandise during our stay. I was shocked to see a $60+ charge for breakfast the previous day. I immediately called the front desk and inquired. The man I spoke with replied right away when I told him we had NOT had any breakfast, "Well, I have the slip here with your name on that you signed for it." I asked, "Who's name is on it?" He said, "Yours, Ms. Blah-blah-blah." I told him that we were being scammed. He then replied, "I'll call you back in 5 minutes." When he called back he said, "I can't find the slip, so we'll just remove the charge." WHAT A LIAR...he'd just told me minutes before he had the signed slip in front of him. I can handle honest mistakes, no problem...but you don't go lying to customers to cover your own backside!!! WOW. On another note...what the heck is the deal with being charged for Wi-Fi when I can get it for free at McDonald's? That is soooo annoying and is just total evidence of wanting to nickel and dime customers to death. I will make sure to NOT stay at a Swissotel in the future based on the crummy customer service.

“Disappointing but not many options in this area” Upon booking online, we put in a request that all down bedding be removed from the room due to an allergy. On our way to the hotel about an hour before checking in, we phoned to make sure they got the note. They said they did see that in the computer and that it was all set. Upon checking in, again we confirmed (as there was no mention of it by the staff at this point) and the gentleman at the front desk said "Oh, well, there's a note in the computer but it isn't in a place where we would notice it." Tired from driving since 6AM, all I really wanted was to wash up and take a nap, but now I would have to delay that to wait for housekeeping to come change my bedding. The room smelled like diesel fumes, but I was so tired I figured I was overreacting. After they changed out my bedding I went into the bathroom to wash my face and hands prior to settling in. The hot water never came. Again I called down to the front desk and two of their engineers came in and turned on the water and let it run for about twenty minutes before it was hot. At least it got hot. The shower curtain rod was about to fall off the wall, there was orange and black mildew hanging out with it's soap scum buddies, and the toilet looked like the inside had never seen bleach ever. The pseudo sleep number bed was either too hard or too soft, the AC was either too hot or too cold, and I was choking on the diesel exhaust smell so badly that after my nap I went to a nearby Target for air freshener. Some people like to highlight the proximity to 95, but with that comes the noise. Beautiful view of the parking lot and plenty of drunk people walking up and down the hallways at all hours (since this is such a classy joint). I had to feel bad for the poor bride and groom checking in at the front desk. This is not where I'd want to spend my honeymoon night with my husband. In close proximity to a mall and terrible food choices unless you enjoy fast food and gross chains (i.e. Chilis, Red Lobster) Needless to say if I ever have to stay in this area again, I will risk getting shot and stay in Baltimore proper.

“Great location, small rooms” My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Palomar for four nights in June. As may be expected in downtown San Francisco, the rooms are quite small, but they were very clean and nicely decorated. The bathroom is also small. Also as expected in downtown SF, the hotel is expensive. If you're already spending that much, I'd suggest the chain hotels like the Marriott and the Westin nearby for larger rooms. The location is great. Right around the corner is the Powell BART station, makes it easy to get around the city and to the outskirts. About a 1/2 mile walk to Chinatown and a mile to the Embarcadero. Definitely walk-able if the weather's nice, although that's asking a lot of San Fran. Very nice shopping and restaurants nearby. Everyone in the hotel was friendly and helpful. The hotel offers free coffee/tea in the morning and wine in the evening.

“Feels a Tad Tired” I spent a night here at a conference and the hotel just feels a tad tired to me. It could use a little freshening up. Positives - location was very good, the staff was really nice and helpful (kudos to everyone of them that helped me or just said hello when I walked by). The restaurant and bar was also a nice size and didn't feel at all like a hotel bar/restaurant. Negatives - My TV didn't work and my phone volume was very low. That was very frustrating because I had little time for relaxation and I all I wanted was to plop myself on the bed and watch a little TV. I will admit that maintenance was very quick and responsive.

“Best location in SF” I was arrived at this hotel at 2 PM and was informed my room won't be ready till 3 PM. I got my room which is facing the street. It's loud and quite often I heard the sirene but this is a tipical SF downtown. Overall, this is a nice centrally located hotel in the Union Square. The PRO: The room is clean and spacious. The location is the best. It's the central of Union Square. Just 2 minutes walking, you will find a westfield mall where you can get your lunch or dinner easily (the foodcourt in this mall is great) and it;s very closed to cable car Powell street station. Within 5 minutes walking, you are in "Sugar Daddy" park, where you can join hop on and hop off tour bus easily and also within walking distant to china town to enjoy asian food and get souvenirs. The CON: The location is very good but in the same time, it's very noisy. If you are a quiet sleeper, then it would be hard for you to not wake up couple times in the middle of time. Oh, did I mention that the parking here costs around $50/night (not including tips - because the parking here has to be valet).

“Unbeatable inner harbor value” This hotel is very clean and comfortable. The decor is nothing special, but the free internet, the excellent fitness room, and the low price make this a pretty compelling choice in the inner harbor area.

“Great Stay” The Fairfield Inn New York Manhattan/5th Avenue is a great new hotel. It was very clean, the staff very accommodating and even though the rooms were small it was very quaint and had everything you need. Breakfast was good and the location great (37th Avenue between 5th & 6th).

“Nettes Hotel am Stadtrand von Denver” Das Red Lion Hotel Denver Central liegt etwas abseits der Innenstadt. Zwischen Flughafen und Hotel verkehrt etwa alle 30 – 40 Minuten ein Shuttlebus, des Weiteren gibt es einen Shuttlebus, der kostenlos 2 Einkaufscentren anfährt. Das Frühstücksbuffet ist sehr gut. Die Zimmer sind sehr geräumig, sauber und zweckmäßig eingerichtet mit Fernseher, Mikrowelle und Kühlschrank. Das Personal war sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Ich hatte das große „Glück“, nachts durch einen hupenden Zug geweckt zu werden, denn in der Nähe des Hotels verläuft eine Eisenbahnlinie.

“Great bargain for budget travel” I stayed at Hotel Riverside Studios for two nights (9/10/06 - 9/11/06). I was traveling on business by myself and needed a cheap place not too far from the Lincoln Center. I was skeptical of any place with shared bathrooms and these prices (around $70 per night), but I saw decent recommendations at tripadvisor.com, including one from a single woman who said she felt very safe here. The place is no frills whatsoever, but if you are just looking for a place to sleep, it's great. The hallways are reminiscent of an old fraternity house - drab, sterile, stark. My room was narrow and tidy - double bed, clothes rack, fridge, TV, desk. The pillows are flat as pancakes, and I brought my own expecting this. I slept just fine. The one thing the room was missing was a mirror - difficult for a girl to dry her hair. The shared bath was as nice as the ones at my friends' apartments in New York - and looked just like theirs - black and white tile, old tub, pedestal sink. The shower was always hot, and I only had to wait once for five minutes for the shower. The front desk recommended a car service and even gave me a band-aid when I had a blister on my foot. I would definitely recommend this place and will probably stay here with my husband in the future to save $$$ so we can spend it on great wine, food and clothes.

“Ottimo soggiorno e prezzo congruo” Ho trascorso due notti in questo Hilton mentre mi trovavo a San Francisco per una fiera. L'albergo si presenta bene, in posizione centrale e con personale molto cortese e disponibile. Ho apprezzato tutti gli aspetti del soggiorno - anche il prezzo ($180 a notte, tariffa flessibile annullabile fino al giorno precedente). Un punto di penalizzazione per la spudoratezza dei prezzi del minibar: $7 per una bottiglietta d'acqua, $12 di spese di "pulizia" del frigo se si dimentica qualcosa di proprio nel minibar, e anche un dazio per rifornire il minibar. I prezzi sono esplicati chiaramente, e non si può pretendere che sia tutto a buon mercato, ma così è veramente eccessivo: equivale a non avere il servizio a disposizione.

“NIce Hotel. CLub Level a bit weaker than many other RC's” NIce Hotel. Prompt service. Very helpful and on top of it staff. They go the extra mile, and they were all full of smiles and kid friendly. This was my third stay, and is was another great relaxing time. Easy to get around on foot from the hotel as well, and only minutes from the airport.

“Consistent high quality” I stayed at this Mandarin when itnfirst opened years ago and HD tv was a novelty Rooms still elegant-- not worn. Lobby lounge good scene of drinks, view and people watching. Convenient to have Whole Foods in the buildingnfor health food regime. Prompt checkin and room service.

“Nice hotel, great rooms, but has some quirks” Overall, I rated this hotel 4/5. While I did like the hotel, I had a few complaints/warnings. First the positive, the rooms are big and nice, they are updated and even have nice flat panel tvs. The location is good for getting around, one block from the blue line. One thing to keep in mind is that you are at a local stop, not an express and you will have to transfer if you need a different line. Also we were able to control the temperature in the room with no problem. The free wifi worked great in the room. This is a big deal for most. There is also a keyed safe in the room. We paid $185/night during Easter week and I was happy with the value. On the negative side (some of these may seem petty), the room was loud. We were high and not facing 8th, but we had neighbors who were loud and the walls seemed thin. The breakfast is almost not worth it when showing up after 8:30 or 9. It is truly a madhouse. We sleep in every day and did not enjoy the breakfast crowd (the line actually went into the lobby), plus the breakfast ends early at 10. Lastly, while the location is good, the hotel isn't really in a tourist "spot." You aren't really in Times Square, you aren't in the Villages, you aren't near the Park, etc. This just means that you'll have to walk a lot. All in all, this hotel was a good value. Would I stay there again? Probably not, I was really disappointed in the breakfast. However, I might try the Hampton Inn SoHo as I really like that area.

“Good hotel, great location” This is a quality hotel with standard size rooms (for a major city hotel). The service was very accommodating as you should expect from this level of hotel. Bell hops were great and very helpful with directions and suggestions. Instead of breakfast at the hotel, check out Mary's Cafe right around the corner on Grand.

“Not a bad stay, but the hotel could use more renovation.” Stayed for business for three days. The catered food for our meetings was great. The lobby area with food and drinks was nicely furnished, and the outside seating area with the gas fueled fire pits was wonderful. However, the hallways to the rooms looked like an old battleship, and the rooms didn't look much better. The hotel had a very "old" feel to it. The drinks at the lobby bar/snack counter were pricey so I mostly walked a half block to the 7-Eleven for drinks. The hotel will get away with whatever they do since there are in the heart of tourist area and just a block from the bay and all the area where the action is.

“Very friendly Staff !” When I arrived, my reservation was not listed as a ‚smoking room’, although I had sent an email the week before to re-confirm. I was immediately assigned a smoking room, the down-side was that it had 2 queen-sized beds. Can’t have it all, I guess. The concierge was very friendly and apologized for the mistake – so no hard feelings ! The bedroom was normal size by New York standards, with a large living room (has an extra pull-out couch) and the bathroom was of sufficient size. There were two walk-in closets and a kitchenette. The rooms and the bathroom were clean, the air conditioners a bit dated, as is the ‘decor’. All in all good value for the prize and a very central location (bus from Newark stops 2 blocks away). 40th Street can be noisy late into the night and early in the morning, but there are not many ‘quiet hotel rooms’ to be found in New York and nobody expects that.

“Difficult to Review-Depends what you want” This hotel is very difficult to review and, depending what you are looking for in a D.C. hotel, you will love this hotel or hate it. On the plus side: The rooms are large, clean and modern. For the money, this is really a great value. Just make sure that you do not get a room on the side of the hotel that faces the Metro tracks. If you do, you won't sleep. The Metro comes by about every 10 minutes and it sounds like a muffled plane. I didn't have a problem with it, but I can see how someone would. By the way, another plus is that the Metro is right out the front door of the hotel. You don't have to search for it. And, it is one stop from Union Station. Another huge plus. On the negative side: This hotel is not close to any atractions. If you don't like taking the Metro-Do not stay here. There is nothing that a tourist wants to see in this neighborhood. In the daytime this is a reasonably okay safe area. But, as the sun goes down the area gets more gritty. And, it becomes more gritty right at and inside the Metro stop. If you are traveling with children, you may want to keep this in mind. I noticed that one reviewer said that the ATF is located nearby. This is true. But, the ATF does not patrol the area. It gets no more and no less attention by the police than any other Metro stop in the D.C. area. My personal opinion is that I like the hotel and I don't mind the area (after dark) as long as I am with my business associates.

“Good Value and Great Service” Hampton Inn is a "discount" chain associated with Hilton Hotels. I generally avoid Hiltons as I find them run down and poor value (like Paris, haha). However I normally have good experiences with Hampton Inns, and this Denver location was a good example. For business travelers this hotel is exemplary - no parking charges, free broadband service fast and useful, and I always love the free hot breakfast. The neighborhood around the hotel is undergoing a "renaissance", which means that it sometimes might not be the safest. But Denver overall is a pretty safe big city, so worries are minimal. Rooms were clean and very new, and daily service was performed very well.

“This a rate on the hotel, but overall just don't stay in the wharf” Let me run this down real quick without making this into a review about staying in fisherman's wharf instead the hyatt. All the really nice hotels are not in the wharf even brands like the top chains their locations down here are lacking, not special, old, dirty etc.. The wharf is not lets spend everyday for a week there place anyway... theres a day or day and half of stuff to do and see there and thats it. then you will driving, cabbing or trolleying around the different areas of the city that are actually more appealing. Taking a bus tour is a good way to get a grasp of where you want to spend time. ok... sorry. To the Hyatt... When i'm traveling and staying at what i think will be a nice hotel i want to have the "this is nice" feeling when i walk in the lobby and the room. Anything can happen from there based on luck really. But, if you don't start with that you're in trouble. Pulling up to a small hard to locate, small cove of a drive entry there was no valet in sight. ok.. maybe getting a car, but you should have more than one just because of that. after getting out my own bags, then standing there for about 5 minutes here he comes and looks at me like i am going to go park it myself. So i "talk him into valeting the car" then i wrestle my bags(heavy) into the very small lobby(i thought it was the concierge desk). i booked a king standard room, i have someone that would prefer to sleep in the bed with me like normal. Well that was to much to ask and they could only put me in a two bed room(not queens) i'm talking small beds. keep in mind i booked a king. its beautiful view of the brick wall was amazing... the beds were decent to sleep in, by decent i don't mean great. I hindsight its amazing what kind of night sleep you can get in your own bed at night. lol. In the morning i went and looked at the breakfast, knowing how service is so far and decided to skip a 50 dollar breakfast and go get food in the wharf. smart choice plenty to pick from whenever. checking out i was going to stop and complain but said why bother.. so getting off the elevator to get into the lobby and i have two 60 lbs bags, then there is these three steep stairs to actually get on to the lobby floor out right out of the elevator, no ramp.. so i a wrestle the bags up the stairs(ok not ny first time), but the point there are bell hops watching me do it. didn't move a muscle, then when i got to them " is there anything i can help you with"? (yes please get fired, is what i thought). then back out to the valet where asking for your car is like asking for then to help you move two states away. same attitude as when i got there. I am always an over tipper even when my better half says to give them a bad tip. I don't believe in no tip, so i gave him 50 cents. I hoped it woke him up a bit, to see is worth. Stay downtown... trolley to the sites and the wharf. A mistake is to think staying there is in the heart of the action or sites its not just one. If you really want to stay down there save the money and go for a hampton/fairfield level hotel free breakfast at those places and will be just as nice as their parent hotel.

“Well Done!” This was the former Park Hyatt Hotel in San Francisco. Recently the hotel changed hands and is now Le Meridien. It's a perfect business location in the heart of the financial district and near the embarcadero. Business travelers will love the location, however leisure travelers may find it just a bit too far from the heart of the city, things like Union Square. The hotel's lobby feels a little cold to me. It is all marble and chrome and seems a little dated and a little sterile and cold. However the staff is great and very helpful and warms up the cold lobby with their smiles. The rooms are nice, they are a bit on the small side, but have nice amenties like cozy comforters and great products in the bathroom. Some of the rooms have stunning views of the bay. We were not so lucky as our view looked into buildings and you could just make out some of the bay. The service level was good, I personally like the location that is a little out of the hussle and bussle of the tourist mobs. However I think the lobby is dated and the hotel could use a make-over. This is a good choice for San Francisco, but not my first choice.

“Comfortable Stay for a Weekend in Austin” We stayed at the Embassy Suites Arboretum while in Austin for a college graduation ceremony. Our room was neat, clean and ready upon arrival. The hotel is close to chain restaurants and a short (and easy) drive to downtown Austin and the 6th Street nightlife. The evening reception was a nice way to unwind after a busy, travel-filled day, and breakfast the next morning was terrific. It's hard to beat cooked-to-order omlets!

“V ERY AVERAGE” I read this had been refurbished? I don't see any. It's old,smelly and not good value for money. Carpets stained, cannot think when aircon is on, beds hard. Saving grace is very large rooms but not great at all.

“Clean, Simple, Great Location, Friendly Service” The title of my review says it all. The only things I would add to it would be that the Internet access is a bit unreliable. I had a room that faced the parking lot, and I would guess that the rooms facing main street would be sort-of loud until the trolley stopped running at 1am. I was happy with the friendly and relaxed atmosphere and service, and the clean and comfortable no-frills room.

“Great hotel” We booked a one night package for the Philadelphia Flower Show. It included 2 show tickets, breakfast for 2 and our room. Parking was extra. Checkin was a breeze, no wait at all Our room was beautifully appointed. Comfortable beds, nice bathroom amenities and a great shower head. Internet was not free but we knew this before booking. 13 served a great breakfast. Despite, it being busy the service was friendly and effecient too. And the walkway to the convention center was a big bonus. I would definitely stay here for future flower shows. Highly recommend for any convention or a Philadelphia visit.

“Staff get an A+; for the rest, oy vey” The experience at this hotel can be summed up in two words: risky venture. The staff are fantastic for the most part but the hotel is a piece of crap. The lobby is old and and worn, not to mention the elevators, corridors, room doors, rooms, bathrooms, beds, bedding, desks, desk chairs, carpet in the rooms, towels, toilets, bathtubs...need I go on? I get the feeling that the staff are trying real hard to impress guests but one gets the feeling even at check-in that it's going to be a lackluster experience. Reception is tucked away back in a far away corner and seems to have not been renovated in a dozen years, at least. The rooms are exceptionally dirty and the decor an assault on the senses (all of them, including smell!). I made sure to remove the quilt from the bed before sleeping in it - seems they don't change them on a guest-by-guest basis and it was, uh, stained with somethin'. I don't know what and wasn't about to find out. This isn't a four-star hotel in any way more than the staff and it's history. It's present day condition warrants a complete makeover. That said, if you are lucky the price is right on Hotwire, Priceline, etc., and for the location, maybe that's the trade-off. But for me, I'd rather stay elsewhere at higher cost with improved hygiene and room experience.

“Gediegenes Haus” Das Novotel am Times Square biete amerikanischen Durchschnitt zum fairen Preis. Aufgrund seiner Lage direkt oberhalb des Times Square und direkt am Broadway ist es ideal gelegen für Sightseeing in Manhattan. Mehrere U-Bahn-Linien sind bequem und schnell zu Fuß erreichbar. Unten gibt es einen Supermarkt mit Snacks und Getränken für die schnelle Nahversorgung und wer’s fleischig mag, findet nebenan gleich ein renommiertes Steakhaus.

“Back again and will be back for more!” This is my 2nd stay at this hotel and only because I liked it. Te service is great, thy bumped us up when we arrived late too. Clean and nicely appointed rooms and not bad on size either for NYC. Parking garages goodies and transportation are all nearby. It is a non traditional hotel but I took a gamble once went back again and will be back again if I need, special thanks to Ramona at the desk!

“Suprising service, but smaller rooms.” Loews Regency has bigger rooms, but this was kinda like a boutique. Rooms were a little bigger than the rooms over at the Morgans, and had a similar flair to the Morgans. Platform bed, but super comfy with THE BEST pillows I have encountered. Bathroom had the modern edge to it, but the shower stall was pretty small. The bath tub, of course, is huge. The view was of a building under construction across the street, but you could see the lights of times square. Free internet, but no WIFI. You have to connect via LAN. Getting on the internet took a lot of time, but they eventually got it sorted out. At the end of the day, the room was doable - clean, a touch small, but a very comfy bed.

“What can I say, that I have not said before !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!” This was my 16th visit to NYC, but my 4th visit to the little gem that is "The Distrikt", I have found this and I will never go anywhere else now. The hotel is right smack bang in the centre of Manhattan, right opposite the Port Authority, where you can get the bus to/from the aiport and be right there ! (no taxis to take when you get into the city). It is only a short walk to Times Square, 42nd Street where most of the shows are, and Macys ! The rooms are gorgeous, and the beds are sooooo comfy !!! There is a coffee machine in the room, and iced tea downstairs in the reception. The staff are the best I have come across while travelling, they would do anything for you !!! Jennifer and your staff you do a wonderful job, thank you for yet another stay in "The Distrikt"

“Great location- average hotel” I'm not a big fan of the minimalist noveau trendy decor. Some of you hipsters might appreciate it, but i find it cold and unwelcoming. That being said, the hotel is in a great location. You are central to everything. The room size is also exceptional for NYC. Staff was friendly and efficient. My biggest negative is the ambience and no coffee maker in the room, although free coffee is available downstairs. They have free wi-fi as well. My room was a bit worn, but I understand that some have been refreshed, so you should ask for one of those rooms. You could do worse!

“That cookie is more expensive than you realize!” I think it is absolutely ridiculous to charge 18/day for parking if you are a guest! It is one thing to charge if someone is parking at your hotel and grabbing the shuttle for the nearby airport. But, this is outrageous! I'm complaining to Priceline and complain about deceptive practices.

“AMAZING HOTEL IN NYC!!” Our stay with our family here was amazing. From Mary at the Diamond check in area all the way down it is run top notch. We loved the location and our room. The service is great. Any request was addressed instantly and completed. We will definitely be staying here again and can't wait to go back!

“Down a star” We still love this hotel and were happy to hear that they are taking the hint to renovate their dated televisions and rooms. They are up to floor 9 as of 3/10/2012 and are working their way up. They also completes some renovations to the pool area- new flooring and new floor to ceiling windows. However, it will cost you! As of February, they now charge $15 EACH DAY you use the pool per room. I found this to be a tough pill to swallow as we stay here regularly and it had been free to all guests prior to these renovations. They have been also adding other vendors such as a nail salon and "dry bar" for hairstyling in the basement- where I, admittedly, have never been. Beware of the prices listed on the mini bar too- I was charge $9.25 for a Heinekin that was on the menu for $8.50. Overdue renovations should not be reason to make your guests feel ripped off.

“Great option for visiting Universal Studios” Got upgraded to a suite being a Priority Club Member and got a bag full of cookies, water bottles etc. The welcome to Hollywood was nice. The room was huge & the restaurant in the hotel is very nice. Free Shuttles to Universal studios is what makes this hotel even more attractive. Though was here for only 1 night I am sure it worked well for visiting Universal Studios. Hollywood was next & closeby.

“Great find downtown” This is a modern design Hampton Inn with all the high speed amenities business travelers expect. Terrific location for all types. Two blocks from metro center. I especially liked the cool color schemes for the rooms and in-room high speed internet for free. Good complimentary breakfast. Everyone was terrifically friendly; very convenient to good dining too! Go eat at Poste in the Monaco (three blocks away). The beds are truly excellent (and I am way picky). Complimentary in room safe also was a nice touch. They will keep your bags for hours if you have meetings on the day you check out. Top Pick.

“Good short stop-over hotel” I chose this hotel for its convenience, also it is relatively affordable for SPG members. The hotel is overall very good, I can't complain and would definitely be back since I usually stay for a short business trip.

“Standard Marriott fare but with a good location” The hotel is located in a good part of town. A little walk to the metro (5-10 mins) or to the main attractions (15-20 mins) but the walks are through pleasant parts of town, more residential areas and you are not really far as you are sort of between the White House, Rock Creek Pkwy/Georgetown, and Dupont Circle - a good location for sure. There are places to go nearby the hotel (Starbucks and Walgreens right next door; gas station across the street, 2 other hotels right there, and very close to restaurants and shops). The hotel lobby is nicely decorated but it is not very interesting nor inviting (because of the layout). It does have a gym and a pool. The gym has good cardio equipment but the weight machines are more limited though it has a good amount of free weights. It is not as nice as gym rooms in the Renaissance hotels around town but it is better than the average hotel gym. The pool is indoor and also has a hot tub. Very nice. The rooms are the standard Marriott-branded fare which means good in my book but nothing revolutionary if that is what you want. Bathrooms dont feel as luxurious as Renaissance brand's are. I could hear my neighbors alarm clock and wakeup call go off every day at 530AM (when I had another hr or more left in my sleep) - thin walls... The elevators are slow which seems a petty thing to point out but there it is :) The executive lounge is the standard type. All good. Its staff is super friendly. Staff overall was effective and friendly.

“Location is Fabulous!!” This is not the Plaza...but the price is right and the location is fabulous!! It is a very walkable neighborhood with fun shopping in Chinatown and eating in Little Italy. The subway is right down the block for access to the whole of Manhattan. The subway ride to 42th street Broadway shows is 5" away. It is a easy subway ride to Coney Island to check it out. It's close enough to walk to ground zero. The rooms are so-so...who cares? Have a great breakfast at Baltazar then go for a walk over the Brooklyn Bridge...then explore all the NYC sights..The staff was wonderful and extremely helpful. I would definitely stay here again

“great location for the Boston experience...” We rec'd a great deal on Priceline ($110) for a 1 night stay - on the busiest sports weekend in April. Location of the Westin is great - an easy jaunt to the T stop and a reasonable walk to places like Newberry St & Fenway Park. We chose to park our car at Alewife station & rode the T in to avoid the valet parking & hotel charge (check online for spots - the Prudential Center garage is there plus the Copley Place garage - you'd at least save the tip) Hotel staff courteous & room with king size bed extremely comfortable. In room coffee was Starbucks w/Coffee Mate liquid creamer (fellow coffee drinker get my drift here) which was a nice surprise. We didn't eat in the hotel restaurants so can't offer advice on that.

“Friendly staff” The staff here really is friendly. The beds are comfortable and our stay was quiet. But I really missed some amenities that I normally take for granted: counterspace in the bathroom! There was just a tiny rim encircling the sink which disappeared into a six-inch ledge over the toilet. Two females traveling together need more counter space in the bathroom, most definitely. The glasses were plastic, the air conditioner noisy and there weren't a lot of outlets to plug in our various devices. And the room smelled disconcertingly like a dentist's office. That said, I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again (we were visiting Rice University). But first, I will try to find a hotel with more counter space in the bathroom! Oh, and the breakfast was fine in the morning. You can make waffles shaped like the state of Texas.

“Average hotel convenient to the convention center” We stayed here while attending a professional conference. The rooms were more reasonable than the Sheraton. Tom size was fine. There was a coffee machine and refrigerator. The hotel was very clean. Staff were very responsive to our requests. I would recommend this hotel instead of the over priced Sheraton. There is a charge for wireless in the room, but I skipped it and used the free computers in the lounge across from registration. There was a printer, too, to print my boarding pass.
“Nice, but not distinctive” Nice stay, but nothing to set it apart from others in the area unless you can get a special price. Parking is ridiculous: valet only and $55.89 (incl tax) per night.

“I have a soft spot for neglected beauties” This is a decent hotel, far from the action. That might appeal to some people. The room was in decent shape, although I could have done without the cigarette holes on the comforter. I loved that there was both a DVD player and a an iPod charger in the room. The view wasn't much to speak of. The staff was very friendly. The only real downside was that the front desk gave someone else my room key, and that person walked in on me in bed. It was awkward, and could have been very embarrassing. That should have been avoided. Overall it's a very out of the way hotel, and you will need a car to get there and around. It's located next to a big Broadway-style theater, so you should check out a show if you're there. But if you're looking for a grand hotel, this isn't quite it. It was at one time, though.

“Another perfect stay -- this time just for a weekend for a family wedding and reunion!” I'm a repeat customer with high expectations, and Wes and the Chancellor delivered again! Small but comfortable rooms, perfect central location, and consistently great service! We also like the little touches like the free coffee and cookies in the lobby, free use of a computer & printer, a small but wonderful hotel restaurant for breakfast/lunch, and candies in the room (my kids and their dentist love this!). The only reason this hotel doesn't always get 5 star reviews on TripAdvisor is because some people don't realize that the Chancellor is an old hotel and there are a few things they CAN'T have or do. The Chancellor fully discloses these limitations so it's not their fault when people don't read and get these amenities. The Chancellor does NOT have the following: (a) large rooms (thus no double double bed rooms for example), (b) large modern lobby, elevators or hallways, (c) air conditioning, (d) on-site gym or (e) pool. Air conditioning is virtually unnecessary in San Francisco and even during 90 degree plus days (and we once stayed during such a summer "heat wave"), the hotel was very comfortably cool. If that isn't sufficient, each room does have ceiling fans. As for working out, the Chancellor has an arrangement with one of the best downtown private gyms located just around the block, so if you don't mind the one block walk (hey, you're going to workout right?), then this is actually an asset! And they have everything that we consider important: quiet, comfortable and clean rooms; free building-wide wifi, wonderful service (front desk, housekeeping, bellmen and restaurant staff), and nice other amenities. Anyhow, thanks for another super stay! We'll be back again soon!

“Excellent service makes up for the dated design” The Ritz certainly has an incredible location! It was a tranquil escape from the crazy throngs of people over St. Patrick's Day weekend. We had two adjoining suites with friends which was very convenient. The service was impeccable. The concierge was particularly helpful and efficient. The staff was very friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. The restaurant had wonderful food and terrific service. The only issue with service was there was no evening turndown service which is a cardinal sin at a Four Seasons! The only weakness of the hotel was the suite itself. The huge windows brought in a great deal of light which was wonderful. It was also very well maintained and spacious. That is where the superlatives for the room end. This Four Seasons could be renamed the Four Decades. The wallpaper was from the 1960['s (at least the style) and I swear it came from my grandparent's wallpaper and paint store. The curtains were from the 1970's and had to come from my great aunt's Florida condo. The furnishings were from the 1980's and the bathroom was from the 1990's. The bathroom had a shower/tube combination with a shower curtain. (Yes, a Four Seasons bathroom had a shower curtain!) YUCK! Except for the carpet and the flat screen TV's, there was no hint of anything contemporary in the room. The Four Seasons Chicago caters to well paid businessmen and rich housewives who either don’t care in the case of the former or decorate their 1980 McMansions in the same manner in the case of the latter, so most people will have no issue with the decor. The gym was very large, air conditioned and had a good deal of high quality equipment. The access to Water Tower Place was very convenient. You cannot find a better location in Chicago as it is centrally located along the Magnificent Mile. Be prepared to pay a whopping parking fee of $52/night. A garage adjacent to the hotel has parking for $28/night but it fills up quickly! We were very fortunate to snag the complimentary hotel limo to take us up to North Halsted for a show. We got a decent deal on the hotel and have no regrets. This hotel is stuffy, pretentious and dated (despite the "refreshing" designed by my grandmother's Bridge club), but it does have top notch service, a great location and is obviously well maintained with quality materials.

“LOVELY and FUN A+” WOW, what a GREAT hotel. Love the whole JAIL theme. Being the former Charles Street Jail ... wow, the genuis behind trying to keep the theme is amazing. The entire 4 days we stayed here it was just so wonderful. Bellmen running to you as you arrive to get your luggage out of the car to the champagne as you approach the Front desk. Awesome. Before I get to the fabulous room, Concierge was wonderful in assisting us in restaurants in the North End. So go to her if you have any questions at all about Boston. A+ Our room was on the 10th floor. Bright, spacious, very clean and simply LOVELY. Upon walking into our room, the tv was on the channel giving you an entire HISTORY of the hotel from the days back when it was the Charles Street Jail. The bed was very comfy and the bath was huge. Complimentary water was in our room. I love the fact that they have umbrella's in your closet for guests to use. It rained almost every afternoon we were there and we always remembered to grab it for the day. A+ A very quick walk to Faneuil Hall. Also Whole Foods is a block away for snacks for the room from fresh fruit to great bakery items. I also loved the way the Doormen JUMPED to open the door to the hotel every single time you went in or out and always had smiles on their faces. A+ Our room had a few minor issues upon check in ... light out over the sink as well as the make-up mirror ... I told the Front desk and it was all handled very quickly. A+ My DH has to go to Boston every 5 weeks for work ... while there are TONS of hotels to choose from in Boston, the LIBERTY will be our first choice!!! A+

“Many functional problems affecting comfort” I wrote a positive review of this property a year ago, but unfortunately a year later I have to give a significantly more negative review. Stayed at the Omni for an annual conference. My room, though spacious and clean, had several functional challenges that drove me crazy, including: -a tiny pedastal sink with not even enough room for the soap dish, with no shelving or countertops around even though the bathroom was quite large and there was plenty of room. This meant that there was no place to set so much as a hairbrush (and the toilet was so far away I couldn't use the toilet seat cover). There's no excuse for this as there's plenty of room to install a shelf or counter. -backwards faucets - that is, the hot water is the RIGHT faucet, but there is no marking so it takes time to figure this out. In addition, shower controls are baroque and complex and led to me having to call engineering to figure out how to get hot water -ran out of hot water at 9 pm in the bathroom sink -housekeeping, for some strange reason, set my A/C to 60 degrees on a mid-March day, so the room was icy -housekeeping uses two flat sheets and tucks them both in, which means that when you turn down your bed, you inadvertently yank out the bottom sheet as well. Why do so many hotels annoy their guests this way? -long waits in the taxi queue as this is not in the middle of the normal taxi circuit By far, though, the most annoying thing about this property was the plethora of 1950's vintage lighting, with zillions of incandescent lights burning away in every guest room and common space. Folks, compact flourescents last longer, burn exponentially less energy, don't generate a bunch of heat that causes the A/C to kick in during the wintertime, and doesn't hurt the human eye. This place needs a serious lighting retrofit and there's no excuse for not doing it. Besides the dreadful environmental impact, I wonder why I am paying so much for my room when the hotel management blithely pays energy bills that are probably triple what they need to be. Here are some good things about the hotel: -the service is uniformly pleasant, plentiful and competent -good mattresses and many types of pillows included in the room -one block away from Connecticut Ave, jam-packed full of great ethnic restaurants and antique stores, with great neighborhoods and Rock Creek park for walking nearby -wifi in the guest rooms, though not free and on a low signal strength, is easy to use -lots of comfortable common spaces that encourage networking Will be back next year for the same conference, and am very much hoping to see better lighting then!

“Great for anyone needing LAX hotel - clean, comfy, quiet, CLOSE!” We had a flight out of LAX way too early, so booked a night here. It is the closest to the airport, and the shuttle was easy and fast. You could probably walk to LAX from there. The rooms were very clean and bigger than I expected based on other airport Courtyards, and quieter than I expected being next to the airport. The bed was comfy. The fridge was a nice addition too. There is a Subway (restaurant) less than a block away. We didn't try the food/bar at the hotel. Overall, would we stay again? Absolutely - no need to look anywhere else if you need something near LAX.

“Lovely Hotel” My family - husband, wife and four children ranging in age from 6 to 22 stayed at this property from 12/25 through 12/28. On arrival, there was a problem with my rate which was quickly cleared up. It is always wise to remember to bring a written confirmation of rates with you. All of the hotel rooms are built around an atrium. The atrium is lovely with ponds filled with huge goldfish. There is plenty of seating in the atrium and to the side of the check-in counter there is a computer room with three computers for guest use. Near the entrance inside the hotel are several more computers but you must use those standing up. Our suite consisted of a living room with a pull out couch, a stuffed chair, table and chairs, a sink and an armoire with a flat screen television. In a closet was a small fridge and microwave. The bedroom had another sink and two queen beds, a television, night tables and a dresser. My only complaint was that more drawer space would have been appreciated. The bedroom also had a closet. The rooms, including the bathroom were very clean and we were very pleased with the accomodations. Every morning there was a full buffet breakfast consisting of scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage, home fries, breads, pastry, fresh fruit,bagels, cereals, milk, juice, french toast or pancakes and made to order omelettes. At night, there was a manager's reception with free drinks (including mixed drinks) and snacks (pretzels, popcorn, salsa and tortillas, etc.). The only problem was that the hotel personnel has not come up with a way to manage the crowds at breakfast and at the reception. By the second day at the hotel, the lines at breakfast were so amazingly long. The omelette line must have been over a city block long. Also, it was almost impossible to get seats. Even the line for bread and bagels was unbelievably long and we just decided to do without. Same story at the manager's reception. You would think a hotel of this caliber could come up with a solution! The location is very good. A 10 minute or so walk to Georgetown and under 10 minutes to the Foggy Bottom subway station. There was a nice Chinese restaurant about two blocks from the hotel on M street. Probably M and 20th. The hotel also has a small pool and a health club. I was very pleased with our choice of hotel and my only wish was that somehow the hotel management figures out a way to accomodate all of its guest s during peak periods so that they can enjoy the very nice breakfast buffet.

“Histortic hotel in San Francisco” This was my 2nd time staying in Hotel Whitcomb. I loved the charm in the historic hotel. Steps out to the MUNI/BART busses/trains. Love Sam's Diner (opens for breakfast and lunch). And, don't forget to ignore the homeless. If you wanted trains outside of the hotel, you will have homeless. The police will be there if you need them. The room was small, excluding the smaller bathroom (2 feet x 6 feet). You will step out of the bathroom to change your mind. ;-) Also, there was one outlet to plug your laptop, cell phone, or iPod. Need to have more plugs.

“great value, good rooms, helpful staff” We stayed in room 505 for one night. We usually stay on Upper West Side, but picked this hotel because it was well priced and well reviewed on Trip Advisor. Room was large for NYC. Staff was helpful and helped us arrange transport to JFK early am for $40 (a good deal for JFK). There was a small continental breakfast in the morning. Hotel was quiet and well maintained. The neighborhood is quiet and close to shopping at Century 21, the World Trade Center site and Wall Street.

“Ask for a room toward front - you'll be fine” Wife and I stayed there before/after a cruise. Before the cruise we were toward the back and the big trains like Amtrak do come in loud and clear especially when they blow the whistle whilst crossing streets. On Sunday night after cruise we were in the front on the street and the noise was barely noticeable. The value and location of the hotel far outweigh the noise factor - unless you are in the very back right next to the train tracks. Plus you are right at the "trolley" (actually light rail) stop and about 4 blocks from the cruise ship terminals, Midway museum, etc. Two Tips: (1) Cabs are cheap in SD. The rail trolley is $5. A cab ride from Gas Lamp district to hotel is about $5 for two people. (2) Go over to Coronado Island either via ferry or other means (we took the Old Town Trolley tour which was nice) and eat at the little Greek place called "Spiro's Gyros" at the Ferry Landing Marketplace. Great food, good beer, an excellent view of downtown SD, and nice price. Outdoor seating is available.

“Great location!” A Westin, is a Westin, is a Westin... and I happen to think their beds and linens are comfortable so they are my "go to" chain. Upon check in it was going to be 48 to park (which I knew) and 15 extra for my "oversized" vehicle (Chevy Tahoe) which I wasnt expecting. ugh! A sweet guy mentioned to me quietly that there was a parking garage right nearby where parking for 24 hours was only $25... perfect. THAT's the kind of help I appreciate! :) The hotel was comfortable, clean and we had an incredible view of the financial district that my kids got a huge kick out of. Our room service breakfast wasn't cheap but it hit the spot and their pancakes off the childrens menu got rave reviews from my boys! I love their cofeee and we were all happy. Upon checkout, they offered to hold my bags until we were finished sightseeing for the day and did it with a smile. Their $100 rate on travelzoo made this a great bargain... we were out of there for $200 with the room, breakfast and parking... cant do too much better than that in SF for four people in a room. (One mom, three kids.)

“Generally what I expect from Kimpton” I really enjoy Kimpton hotels and this physical property did not disappoint - pretty/funky lobby, nice space in the rooms, and the attached restaurant was very good for breakfast. However, the staff was not particularly helpful or friendly. When we checked in there was mass chaos due to a cat adoption event, and while I love cats, my husband is very allergic. I expressed concerned at check-in and got an eye-roll and a sigh "it's all contained in the restaurant area." Luckily the attitude didn't ruin the stay. What almost did ruin the fun was the absurdly slow valet service. After a long wait at drop-off and another long wait when we retrieved the car, the valet parked the car in the rain away from the awning--so I got a little shower slogging over to the car. I know hotels outsource their valet services so I'll stick with the 4-star rating but the Palomar should really address that. It was NOT a nice welcome to the hotel. A note on the location, it was a good part of town for our trip to the west side, the Getty, and a play in Culver City (all driving of course). There is nothing in close proximity to the hotel but in good weather Westwood is walkable (but nobody walks... nevermind). If you're looking to cruise Sunset or see Grauman's Chinese, etc., then this won't be especially close. While it didn't knock my socks off, I would definitely stay there again - it's a good value for a good room.

“Very nice, but very busy.” I was in Boston (from Kansas City) over the last several days for a conference on behalf of my company. I stayed at the Marriott Copley Place hotel for three nights and had a great experience. The hotel is connected to two nice malls, has many dining options, and is an overall classy establishment. My only complaint would be that it always seemed to be very busy and hectic in the atrium/lobby area. My room itself was on the 34th floor and I had a great view of Boston. The king-size bed was extremely comfortable and the room and bathroom were appointed nicely. The hotel's location was great, considering the abundance of shopping, great architecture and dining options in the area. The Copley Square T Station was about a 2.5 block walk from the front door. The historic library and Trinity Church were also within walking distance. Overall, I had a good experience here. The general feel of the hotel was very business-centered and at times hectic, but well-executed. The staff was helpful, the accommodations were clean and classy and I would stay here again given the opportunity.

“Second stay - very nice” I chose to stay at this relatively new Hampton Inn again after a successful stay in March. This is a lovely property, very near Chinatown. I have stayed in two rooms - one a spacious king executive room with a sofa and one an average king. Both were quiet and well appointed. Bathtubs are small and shallow, but since most of us shower these days, it's not a big issue. Free high speed internet is great - but it is only wireless in the lobby. Tip - if your traveling cord is short, ask to borrow one from the front desk - they have very long connection cords for the room that will enable you to work from somewhere other than the desk. On both visits, this was a very popular hotel with tourist families. Breakfast is noisy and despite the staff's best efforts, they can't keep up with kids' spills. On my second trip, the ac wasn't working in the first room I tried. They responded quickly, moved me within 20 minutes and were very, very nice. It is easy to catch a cab on the busy corner nearby.

“Can't wait to return!” We stayed at the Shelburne due to the fantastic Travelzoo rate and the hotel's quiet but convenient location. We stayed in a one bedroom suite which truly felt like having our own apartment. Ours had a wet bar area with fridge and microwave drawer, living area with comfy sleeper sofa, flat screen tv and step out balcony. Bedroom had a king bed and flat screen and 1 bathroom with big soaking tub and shower combo. The renovations here were amazing. All the fixtures are very modern and stylish and lighting was very good. A lot of the lighting had dimmer switches which are very useful especially in the bathroom area if you want to have a relaxing bath. One thing I noticed especially was the sound proofing. I think this is the first hotel in recent memory that I heard no noise at all from any adjoining rooms. We were very satisfied and would definitely return if the price was right.

“Great experience” The hotel had a special rate on the internet for $156, and that got us a nice, clean cozy room. Very nice firm mattress, free internet connection (though the hotel next door actually had a stronger signal), bathrobes, etc. The bathroom was very small and looked a little dilapidated., but that was the only slightly negative thing about the room. It's located on a quiet street within easy walking distance to a number of restaurants and two metro stops. The manager kindly let us check in early, and remembered our names throughout the stay. We asked for a razor to be brought up (having forgotten that we can take them through airport security now). After about 25 minutes, they brought up a small pack of cheap, single blade razors that drew blood. We ended up buying a better quality. The bar downstairs seemed quite lively, though we did not go there. The restaurant at the Tabard Inn right next door is excellent, though. Reason enough to stay at the cheaper Topaz. Overall, a great experience, and would definitely return.

“5-Star” I was not at this hotel very long (late check-in and early flight out), so I did not fully explore its amenities. I am not a 5-star price kind of guy when it comes to hotels, but I could definitely see the justification for the price differential at this hotel. The room was quite clean, the bed comfortable, and all the 5-star amenities on hand. For reference, it was a very easy and quick cab ride to Midway at 6:30 the next morning. Whether that was good luck or the norm, I can’t say. Apologies for having little to report on, but I can confirm that this hotel seems to be all that it is supposed to be.

“Nice people, ok property” The people at this Hilton are very friendly and helpful. The property itself, while ok, seems a bit tired, and a lot of it has to do with the very seventies style of architecture--the typical center atrium style, very echo-y. The rooms themselves are clean and the bedroom was very nice, the bath very large; the "conference suite," which I chose to have a larger space, was a bit awkwardly furnished in the living room, somewhat crowded, with a too-big table off to the side. Unlike other Hilton properties, there is a charge for parking--no parking lot, really. it's unfortunate that there is also a charge for internet. The fitness center had very good equipment, but was very, very small--more like a room than a center. Apparently the hotel has an agreement with a larger health club very close to the hotel, which I didn't have the opportunity to try.
