“Boring, no frills business hotel” This hotel has a few positives: - Immediate proximity to the Washington Convention Center (but not that close to main tourist attractions though, with the exception of Chinatown which is located a couple of blocks away). - A great and stylish lobby, with various lounge areas and a nice area equipped with several sofas and bookshelves (despite the presence of a Starbucks and a junk food store; those unfortunately make the whole thing look a bit like a low-key shopping mall...). - Comfortable beds and pillows. - A welcoming staff. Besides the bed, the rooms are however more than disappointing... Very basic and standard (a carbon copy of any Marriott Courtyard room...) – standard furniture with no particular style, noisy and ineffective air conditioning, very basic and slightly run down bathroom (very old fashioned tiles, no separate shower – a simple showerhead in the bathroom and a curtain...), no courtesy water bottles, no minibar or espresso machine in the room, no slippers, no bathrobe, no iPod docking station, no central control of lights etc (my usual complaints about so many hotel rooms in the US...). My room was a reasonable size, but one may wonder about the presence of two queen or king beds per room, which could make sense in a family hotel but really not in a business hotel... only one bed but a sofa, a table and a couple of armchairs would have been a much more effective use of the available space. Finally, they charge an outrageous 12.95 USD per day for wifi access. This is really over the top, considering the already excessive prices this hotel charges for the rooms. Service at the hotel's restaurant was courteous, but exceptionally slow.

“The Westin Copley Place to be!” We wrote ahead to let the Westin Copley Place know that we were coming for an all-too-rare family reunion, and they were kind enough to reserve a wonderful accommodation for our group that would be comfortable for pre-dinner cocktails and more! And comfortable it was...with spectacular 180 degree views over all of Boston! The newly renovated rooms and public spaces are Westin high style...no more tired or thread-bare for the Copley Place...this is top of the Brand! The WCP also enjoys an enviable position in Boston...literally connected to a wonderful indoor high-end mall, and nearby many fine restaurants, galleries & shops (think: Newbury Street and beyond!) We enjoyed the SPG platinum complimentary buffet breakfast (with an option to upgrade to "full" declined, as the cold buffet was plenty.) The valet parking was a bit hectic around typical check-in time, but in their defense, it was a deluge out! Patience.... Thanks to all the management and kind staff for a wonderful weekend!
“A standard Hyatt” This Hyatt was close to everything but was just OK in amenities. I am a Platnium Gold passport member and expected more. But everything was nice, clean and close.

“Ok, but not the best for this price range” Since this is meant to be a 5-star property, I was slightly disappointed. On the plus side: * Brand new property * Good location - in the Loop, 2 blocks next to Sears/Willis Tower * Comfortable bed * marble & wood bathroom - somewhat standard for this class * Separate glass surrounded shower area and a very large bath-tub * Concierge person was helpful On the negative side: * On the shower wall, a few small spots of mold/mildew - surprising for such a new property - their house-cleaning needs to be more thorough * Some tiny pieces of lint on the bench next to the bed - again surprising for this class of hotel * The bedroom - while not tiny wasn't especially large either * Since it's an old building, my room looked out on the inner "courtyard" with not much view. At a lower price level, this would be a great hotel. But at this price level, I would have expected more thorough cleaning & maintenance. I liked Chicago though - felt a lot less crowded than other cities I have been recently.

“Fine for a convention” I stayed at the Hyatt McCormick Place for two nights at a convention in August 2007. Paid $169 a night for the 'business plan' - I don't think it was worth the extra $20 for breakfast at the restaurant. The rooms are standard Hyatt, decent bed and sheets, but nothing fancy. No room safe and $10 a day for high speed internet. $24 a day for parking. The public areas were bright, airy, and clean and seemed to handle our group well. Not so for the one line coffee stand and the one restaurant for breakfast. There are no other options close to McCormick Place, so the food there is the only game in town, unless you want to drive or take a cab elsewhere. The guest floor hall on my floor was dirty and was not cleaned during my stay. All in all, fine for the purpose but I would not go back for any other reason.

“Very Accomodating with Clean Rooms & Nice Breakfast” We stayed at the Sheraton for an AAU basketball tournament. We stayed three nights. The rooms were nice. It was obvious that they had been renovated recently. The bed was comfortable. The entire room was clean. We took advantage of the small bar at night to unwind. It was a nice place to meet other parents. The breakfast was included in our rate which saved us quite a bit. Overall, there was a good variety of selections. As mentioned, we had a basketball team staying at the hotel. The players were well behaved overall. One night we needed to feed them after a late game. The hotel was gracious when we ordered pizza providing us with an area to feed the hungry boys. The hotel is very conveniently located near the Galleria mall. This helped us stay busy during the "down times" in the tournament. It was good to have access (within walking distance) because the traffic in this area was congested at most hours of the day. The traffic in the area and road construction limited our desire to explore Dallas.

“This place is fabulous” What's better than a room with floor to ceiling windows and a view of beautiful gardens, luxury count sheets, always helpful and cordial service, fabulous food (locally sourced, often organic), a continental breakfast that includes all kinds of pastries, fresh fruit and smoked salmon, excellent service, and a shuttle to the light rail right into Seattle as well as a shuttle that leaves every half hour for the airport. Make a reservation quick - this place is fabulous.

“Hopefully a fluke, but a very poor stay” Traveled with my family for a single night recently. When we arrived, there was a large drinking party with loud music going on in the pool area, making it unusable by children and families. I was told the following morning (by another family with small kids who had been unable to use the pool) that they complained about this the night before to no avail. Likely the same group were up and slamming doors until about 2 in the morning on our hallway. The hotel is right next to I-30 and the sounds of motorcycles racing down the freeway early and late transmitted through the walls very efficiently. And our air conditioner (window unit with wall controls) rattled loudly every time it turned on. Between all of the above, there was very little sleep to be had. The following morning, the pool area was completely trashed with dozens of Corona bottles floating in the water, laying all over the deck, and broken glass in several areas. Towels, leftover food, etc. were strewn all of the place, and it smelled strongly of alcohol. I reported it again to the front desk and housekeeping did come and clean (3 large trash bags full of stuff.) Also, room key worked fine on room and exterior doors, but wouldn't open pool area -- which was annoying. The good side: Convenient location, newer Comfort Suites design and decor, comfortable beds, above average quick service hotel hot breakfast, and nice staff that I spoke to about the problems. I realize the hotel can't control everything about unruly guests, but this was out of hand, and it was an embarrassing mess for far too long with apparently little to no effort to stop it. That, coupled with the symphony of noises, will keep me from returning to this location.

“Great Location and Service” This is my go-to hotel when I go to Boston. Great atmosphere; love the wine in the lobby in the afternoons. Right on the Common and convenient to the T. The bathrooms are great, and the service is always stellar. Another great Kimpton property that never disappoints. PS: My review is a bit late; finally contributing to Tripadvisor after lurking for so long, but I have been here about 4 times in the last 2 years, and it has always exceeded expectations.

“A disgrace to the Morgan's brand” I don't know why they haven't sold this place and let it become a youth hostel. The Hudson gives "boutique hotels" a bad name and what's odd to me is that they've done nothing to improve it in the decade or so it's been open. I'm sorry but in a city like New York, you need to get a good night's sleep and it seems that they've done everything possible to ensure that won't happen! Must be a cash cow . I stayed here once several years ago and again this year, but never again. I was reminded that in this economy, with occupancy rates at all time low, I can do much, much better in NYC for a comparable price.

“Good location, good value for downtown” Good value for the money. Location is only a block from the Riverwalk and several minutes walk from the Alamo and shopping areas. La Villita area is directly behind the hotel. We had a room in the back of the hotel which was very quiet and the hotel was clean. We had a few small problems over the three nights but the staff was very accomodating and addressed them immediately. Continental breakfast is included, but there is no room to eat although trays are provided to take the food to your room. Bathroom was small but O.K. You can leave your car parked as downtown attractions are within walking distance. San Antonio's trolley service is good for reaching areas farther away, such as The Market.

“Average La Quinta” Beds were comfy, Room was large. the breakfast was fruit, yogurt, juices, waffels and cerial. staff was friendly and helpful. we requested a fridge and got it minutes later. This hotel is right next to a mexican restaurant, and cracker barrel is within walking distance.

“A fine hotel shaped like a big box” This hotel is fine. It is a full service hotel that caters to business travelers. It has everything you would want: on-site restaurant, gift shop, coffee stand, bar, etc. One complaint is the layout. All rooms open onto a large center common area. Feels like you are in a big box. Be careful with some of the rooms as they look out over the center of the hotel. As a result these rooms never see the light of day. Literally.

“Nice hotel, clean rooms, good service” I was ready to bash this hotel at first, but thanks to two dedicated employees (Nicole at the front desk and Floyd the concierge) I changed my mind on this place. I would have given it a five star, but still not happy that you have to pay for Internet! This is walking distance to the Lake, very nice!

“eh, it was okay... here on business” I was here on business and the 'business center' was expensive! Pretty big fee for using the internet etc. Room was clean, service was good, food was mostly good (don't order the oatmeal, it's NOT good and it's expensive). Staff was friendly. However, I could hear OPP (other people's plumbing) all night- showers and faucets running etc. Pillows were lumpy and the mattress needed replacing.

“Good Hotel, Location was good and bad” Hotel is very nice and clean. It is one of the nicer Residence Inn's I have seen. Breakfast was above average and included. Our suite was very spacious and nice. The location was good and bad. First the good. It is about two blocks from the Rivercenter and the Alamo. The river walk's easiest access is either from the Rivercenter or across from the Alamo. The bad. The immediate area around the hotel is not that great. The hotel is surrounded by empty pay-to-park parking lots and next door to a local poolhall/night club. All Friday and Saturday night we heard and saw people enter/leave the club. We heard people shouting and cutting up outside in the streets and in front of the hotel. FYI, the hotel charges $12 a day for parking. Even though the nearby self parking lots charge about $5 a day, I would strongly suggest using the hotel's garage. It is restricted access (room key only) and has gates. The garage clearly indicates that it is a park at your own risk so I am assuming that they have had some problems with the nearby pool hall. During the daytime we noticed nothing unusual and the staff was very friendly. If you are new to San Antonio and on vacation, I would suggest staying at a hotel right along the riverwalk. You may be putt off by this location.

“Very nice stay, and SPACIOUS room!” I checked into The Muse on the 23rd Nov for a two-night stay. We were a party of four (two adults and two teenagers). Overall, it was a very nice stay. The Muse is a very good hotel, true to its Kimpton connection. I would not hestitate to return. The room we had is categorized as a Double Double Premium. It's very spacious, and not just by NYC standards. It's room XX12. Not only is the room spacious, it's also very nicely decorated -- their $15 million renovation was well-spent. Beds are very comfortable. Large flatscreen TV on the wall. Good sound insulation (except from some street noise, which cannot be avoided here in NYC). XX12 faces the back, so it's not right on 46 Street and we had less street noise. Still, this IS Manhattan. Also, there seems to be some construction going on around the hotel, and we'd hear loud banging noises (like a dump truck unloading or something) even into the wee hours of the morning. Have no idea what it was. But it really wasn't a big deal. Good closet space in the room. Lots of lighting. A/C works just fine and is pretty quiet. Bathroom is very large and marble tiles and floor. L'occitane toiletries. There's a relatively large digital safe in the room (though not quite large enough for my laptop). I usually chain down my laptop in a hotel room, but there really isn't place at the desk to do so. So I chained it to the chair... There's WIFI and wired as well. It's free for Kimpton InTouch members. Otherwise I think it's 10? Despite the description on the website, there is NO in-room coffee. No coffee maker can be found. Surprisingly, there is only 1 telephone in the room, and it's by the bed and not the desk. And it's corded. So if you're expecting to make lots of line calls, this can be an issue. CD player in the room description is NOT really a CD player. It's an MP3 docking station. L'Occitance toiletries are fine, but I was surprised that there's no bath gel, and not even mouthwash. The fridge in the room is one of those with an electronic sensor. Touch anything and you get charged. So if you're planning to put anything in it, you may wish to contact the Front Desk first. Over the 2 nights we were here, I don't think there's turndown service (which is fine for us, but very surprising). The directions on the hotel website is WRONG. The hotel is on the SOUTH side of W46 Street. Not the north side as listed on the website. Anyway, when we arrived, there was no doorman to be found outside the hotel. And lots of traffic. I stopped the car in front of the hotel, but there was a whole line of cars behind me honking away. What a symphony. I asked my wife to go inside the hotel to get someone, and that took at least 5 minutes before someone came out to valet the car for us. I don't mean this as a negative of their service, but as a note to fellow travelers that parking is a bit of a hassle. Found this 24-hour covered garage about 100 feet away, BEFORE the hotel, also on the south side of W46 Street. For 24 hours, it's $10 less than the $43 that the Muse charges for valet. So, I think I'll do that next time, just to save me the trouble of being stuck in front of the hotel. We arrived shortly after 2. Had emailed ahead of time asking for early check-in, and also noted that they still had double double premium rooms available. So I figured arrival at 2 would be safe. BUT no. We were made to wait at the lobbly and cool our jets. We were told XX12 is a much better room than others available, and that's why they wanted us to wait for it. I have no way to ascertain the validity of their claim. True, XX12 is a nice room. And true, we did get in when 3 pm came around. But I was also rather annoyed that all the communication I had with them prior to arrival seemed to mean nothing.... No welcoming amenity that I could see when I went into the room -- unlike my other Kimpton experiences. Though later that evening a box of Godiva biscuits was delivered with a nice little hand-written note of welcome. Unlike my other Kimpton experiences, I have the feeling that at the Muse, the management team doesn't really want you to have easy access to contacting them by email. The only email address publicly available is that of the concierge. During our stay, all the staff we encountered, especially the bell staff, were very pleasant. The hotel is very nicely located. It's close to but not right in Times Square. Lots of nice restaurants around, and given that we're in the Theatre District (pretty quiet these days, with the strike), lots of nice pre-theatre fixed price dinner specials. I think The Muse is a very nice hotel. If I find a decent price (say around 300 or less) it would be a very good deal.

“Room smelled bad” I stayed at the Doubletree for one night (thank goodness it was only one night) when I went to Manhattan for a business trip. My room was unpleasant. It smelled like a dirty, musty restroom. Seriously. I didn't want to touch anything. I wore slippers the entire time and never touched the floor. There was no luggage rack for my suitcase so I used the ironing board to place my suitcase atop. The carpet was too gross to leave it on the floor. The room was small, the tv was tiny. I am a Hilton Honors Gold level member and I was placed on an executive level floor, but the room didn't reflect anything special. It was tiny and the desk was very small. There was a free breakfast in the Executive Lounge the next day - the usuals of ceral, muffins, etc. I wouldn't stay here again if it were my choice.

“A good place to be trapped...but trapped you are. Beware of the expense report.” I stayed at this hotel in April, 2010 for a variety of business meetings, including a couple at the hotel. The hotel's facilities were fantastic: stylish lobby; roomy guest rooms with great design, wonderful and flexible desk area, and comfortable bedding; and a huge conference center that appeared to be recently renovated and avoided some of the typical hotel-ballroom-blandness by having several locally-themed displayed on Texas businesses and leaders that were actually pretty interesting. The fitness center was great: a wide range of cardio equipment and free weights, open 24-hours, nice towels, even a wine refrigerator filled with cool towels to use post-workout! I was very impressed with the physical plant of the hotel; it's significantly nicer than its 1980s-looking exterior would suggest and certainly was a refreshing change-of-pace from usually design-less airport hotels I've stayed at in other cities. Service-wise, I had a mixed experience. I had dinner at the fancy steakhouse in the hotel; the service was superb. The front desk and housekeeping service was good. The meetings staff seemed to do a good job. I had a more mixed experience in the business center, where the staff was laughably inflexible. I had dinner in the restaurant off the lobby one night, and the service there was horrible -- I waited forever to be taken to a table, and once at the table my server was slow and disinterested. Nothing is more frustrating than watching the staff be more concerned about re-setting the tables for breakfast than it is about clearing your food or bringing something out while it's still warm. The hotel is attached to DFW's parking garages. There's nothing nearby -- all restaurants, stores, etc. are either within security at DFW or outside of the (huge) airport complex (WAY beyond walking distance). So, in one sense, the location is very convenient, as no other hotel (except the other Hyatt) is on the airport's grounds. The downside, though, is that the on-airport location means that the hotel has you trapped when it comes to services and meals. It knows this...even though the room rate was reasonable, everything else was NOT. The most ridiculous was the business center, where computer access to print cost a minimum of $9.00 (plus a certain amount per page). An envelope cost money, as did copies, etc. I had some documents to copy that were sort of complicated (i.e., some pages needed to be copies, others didn't; some had to be blown up, others shurnk), and it was my strong preference to do the copying myself. The staff in the business center initially wouldn't allow me to do that, saying they couldn't be liable if I were injured by the copy machine. Come on. When I promised not to sue they agreed to let me make the copies so long as the business center associate stood next to me; this showed me that they were less concerned with liability and more concerned with nickel-and-diming me. I bet they sure are glad they didn't miss out on one chance to charge me $.10. The restaurant prices were also absurd. There is an a la carte, classic steakhouse attached to the hotel. It was a lovely meal, and a very nice restaurant at which you expected the prices to be elevated to match the quality of the service...but the prices were crazy expensive; it was nearly $100/person for a salad, entree, and glass of wine (and that was ordering with caution!). The regular restaurant wasn't that crazy, but my chicken breast entree was $26 -- add a salad and an iced tea, and you're talking a $40 dinner. The coffee bar's prices were similarly high. So, being connected to DFW is very convenient...but you PAY for that convenience! Overall, absent the bad experience in the restaurant and the bean counter in the business center, the hotel was very nice, but the hidden costs were higher than normal. So, balance the great facility and desire of being connected to DFW with the off-airport properties that are less expensive and have access non-hotel owned stores, restaurants, etc.

“Great Location, average room” We chose the hotel because its great location, just next door to the Grand Central station. The room we got was smaller than what we had in other Hyatt's but our local friend said it's big per NY standard. The lobby was large and opulent. Service people were helpful and courteous. We did not look closely under the bed or mattress but the room and bath look clean enough. There was no view to speak of, no complimentary internet connection and no coffee maker in the room.. We would stay in this hotel again if we could get the same discount rate

“Wonderful hotel” The location is excellent: close enough to the Union Square area without being right in the middle of the hassle. The rooms are clean and modern, and the desk staff was extremely friendly.

“Great Hotel...Stong Mgmt” I really enjoy this hotel as the price and service re great. Alianna( I hope that I spelled your name correctly) is the best.While she was training a new employee, she managed to engage with guests and offer great service.

“Good Stay in Fells Point” My husband and I booked a one night stay in September at the Admiral Fell Inn because several conventions in town made it impossible to find any other hotels closer to my husbands meeting downtown. Although it wasn't our first choice, overall we enjoyed our stay. The location in Fells Point is both a positive and a negative. On the plus side, you are close to restaurants and bars and in the heart of this little historic district. The hotel does a nice job with their wine/beer and cheese happy hour which features a costumed storyteller who offers historical accounts of life in Fells Point from its founding onward. The tiny lobby actually becomes a bit of a party with the storyteller bringing the disparate group together with her tongue-in-cheek/somewhat satirical , but historically accurate delivery. The hotel also is attached to a well-reviewed tapas restaurant where we had a drink pre-happy hour (starts at six.) On the negative side, the location in Fells Point is noisy. We were awoken at 3 am when the bars let out to screaming, laughing and I swear someone was playing a saxaphone.... And this was mid-week! I can't imagine what a weekend night would be like. Our room did face the street on the third floor so there may be quieter, higher floor options. The area also feels a bit dangerous, which didn't stop us from walking to dinner across the square, but was reinforced the next morning when we were having breakfast at the Fells Point market on the square surrounded, I kid you not, by a parade of at least seven policeman in full swat team gear (bullet proof vests etc). The rooms at the Inn are on the older side with tiny out-of-date bathrooms, but the bed was comfy and the free water bottles were appreciated after the generous happy hour. The Inn staff are also very friendly, not overly professional, but I appreciated their humor and their casual vibe. All depends what type of experience you are looking for, whether or not you will enjoy the Admiral Fell Inn.

“An Absolutely Beautiful Property” Great property, but service could use some help. Room was still being cleaned when I checked in and arrived at my room. Then, housekeeping failed to leave toiletries in room or bring them even after I called. Valet is also extremely slow and understaffed. Nevertheless, it's a beautiful property and I'd give it another try and would still recommend.
“beds were mushy, uncomfortable, hotel staff was nice” The beds were soft and mushy - my back was aching the next morning. The hotel staff was helpful and friendly.

“Convenient to several San Diego attractions and close to food!” I recently stayed at the SD Marriott Mission Valley and was given a room on the 17th floor which had an outstanding view of San Diego. The room was nice, but was not as big of a concern for me as I was in meetings all day. I will say that when I returned to my room in the early evening and looked out the window I was sold on this room. I will include photos from the room so you can see what I am describing. The pool seemed nice, but I did not use it while on this stay. If you stay here you will be close to shopping at local malls as well as close enough to get to Old Town San Diego. If you stay here you will also be close to where the San Diego Chargers play. I did have a chicken sandwich on the go and it was outstanding. The chicken was thick and juicy. If you are looking to get to Petco Park or the Gaslamp District you will have to drive or get a cab as it is not close. Overall I truly enjoyed my experience at this hotel. I hope you enjoy it as well.

“Good Kimpton hotel” The location is excellent. The rooms are larger than I would have expected, and comfortable. The bathrooms are quite small, but that was ok with us. Didn't have much interaction with the staff, but when we asked for a broken iron to be replaced, it was brought up in less than 15 minutes. The attached Italian restaurant had a slightly impersonal, commercial feel to it, but we had a great experience with the quality of the food. I'd recommend it to anyone staying at the hotel. One tip - if you have a car and don't expect to be in and out much, it'll be much cheaper to park at one of the nearby public garages, instead of the very expensive hotel parking.

“Altes, heruntergekommenes Hostel an ausgezeichneter Lage” Wir haben Ende August bzw. anfangs September 2011 vier Nächte im AAE 11th Avenue Hostel in Denver verbracht. Es liegt ziemlich zentral in Denver Downtown und man erreicht in rund 5 Gehminuten das Denver Art Museum oder das State Capitol Building. In zehn Gehminuten erreicht man die beliebte Fussgängerpassage an der 16th Avenue mit vielen Restaurants, Bars, Kinos und Einkaufsmöglichkeiten. Beim Hostel handelt es sich um ein fast hundert jähriges Gebäude und leider wird einem dies während eines Aufenthaltes schnell bewusst. Mit Ausnahme des modernen Aufenthaltsraumes (mit Küchenzeile, Mikrowelle, Computerstation mit Internet, Sitzecke und grossem Flachbildschirm-TV) ist das Hostel sehr heruntergekommen. Unser Zimmer war zwar sehr geräumig, aber ansonsten eine grosse Enttäuschung. Es war sehr muffelig, hellhörig und mit direktem Blick auf die stark frequentierte 11th Avenue (dementsprechend laut). Zudem war die Matratze stark durchgelegen und resultierte in starken Rückenschmerzen bei uns. Wir hatten ein eigenes Badezimmer mit Badewanne/Dusche und Toilette. Leider war der Wasserdruck so gering, dass es für meine Freundin ein Ding der Unmöglichkeit war sich ihre Haare richtig zu waschen. Loben können wir dafür das sehr freundliche und zuvorkommende Personal, die uns einen guten Service boten, und natürlich die ausgezeichnete Lage des Hostels.

“Excelente” Estuve en este hotel dos noches, puedes caminar al riverwalk 5 minutos, , tiene una parada de river taxi en el hotel $5 una Ida y $15 dolares 24 horas. El hotel esta bueno, tiene desayuno buffet Los fines de semana, una barra en el lobby, en el tercer piso esta el gym Es 24 horas, piscinas y jacuzzi. Lo recomiendo.

“Central property, great value for money” Great customer service. Extremely friendly from the minute we walked in, to offering us some bottled water for our long drive ahead on exit. Big rooms, yes they're not the swankiest but remember, this is the Embassy Suites. Staff quickly put together our sofabed and crib for my kids. This means a lot when you have tired, jetlagged children. Decent buffet breakfast with a large area to sit. There is also a good cafe at the front of the hotel. Valet parking is expensive. On Sunday you can park opposite for free and round the corner is a cheaper carpark for overnight. If you want a suite in the heart of downtown Fort Worth, I highly recommend staying here.

“Wonderful Historic Hotel, Oozing with Nostalgia” My husband and I love to travel by train and when doing so we make a point to stay in vintage old nostalgic hotels as part of the experience. We found the Biltmore to be perfect! I could feel Old Hollywood in every room. The hotel is opulent and grand. The lobby area and downstairs must be seen to be believed. Opulent molding, painted ceilings, carved wood, flower, fountains...just amazing. Our room was beautiful. Lots of room and a comfortable bed. I especially liked the old curved-edge bathtub and glass handle on the door. We have stayed in the old "Grand Dame" hotels in most major cities and the Biltmore is among our top five. Folks who want modern convenience and 21st century amenities should realize that older nostalgic hotels may not be what they are looking for, but for those of us in middle age who love history and the early 20th century experience the Biltmore is fantastic. I whole-heartedly recommend it!

“Perfect location--perfect hotel!” We booked 2 rooms for our weekend stay--one for us with our small children, one for my in-laws. We drove straight from SFO airport with no trouble, and it was easy to get to the hotel. Parking garage staff, doormen and check in staff were all very courteus and personable. Our rooms were both on the 26th floor. They were clean, stylish and spacious, as was the hotel lobby. At nighttime, our children were pleased to see a superb view of the star which was lit up on the top of the adjacent building. We had a great night sleep, and never heard any neighbors. I am very happy with Marriott hotels. Their frequent stay program always gives us an incentive to choose them wherever we go, and they are yet to disappoint! This was a stellar hotel, and the location was a great starting point for our walks around town.

“Nice boutique hotel.” Stayed for two nights. I usually stay at Starwood properties, and haves stayed at the Westin TS, but wanted to try a smaller boutique and also wanted to be away from Times Square. The lobby is small but quaint. The elevators and hallways however were very dark! My room was a one bedroom, felt more like an apartment than a hotel room. 2 of the three phones in the room had problems, I just swapped them around. I like to have the tv on while working but you cant do this here cause the desk is directly below the tv! I ended up on the sofa working on the coffee table. Staff were friendly and helpful. Remembered my name and said hi every time I entered the hotel. There's a 24/7 deli next door that came in handy for room food and beer!

“Great conference service-rooms average” I recently attended a conference at the Westin LA Airport. The free shuttl service from the airport was great. The meetings were set up nicely, but the rooms were very chilly so bring a sweater. The staff was friendly and attentive, especially in the restaurant, bar, and at conference lunches and breakfasts. The room left something to be desired. The makeup mirror was grungy and dusty, there was dust on the lamp, and the furniture had multiple large gouges and dings. I had a room that had a door to the adjacent room. My neighbors stayed up late and I could hear them clearly, not to mention the bright light that shone from under the door until they decided to retire. Make sure to ask for a room without an adjoining room. The noise from the planes could be drowned out by turning on the fan.

“Nice location, good play to stay” The location is excellent for easy walking to restaurants, around the corner is the Slippery Noodle, just blocks from convention center, Lucas Oil Stadium, downtown shopping, and a short drive to Eli Lilly, which is where I was visiting. I stayed in an executive room, it was very roomy, nice sized desk for working, large nice flat screen TV and a sofa. The bathroom decor is a bit dated but otherwise, it was functional. The continental breakfast is excellent. The staff were friendly and helpful. Finally, the hotel is a quick drive to/from the airport.

“Comfortable, quiet conference hotel” This Sheraton is an upscale airport hotel. Situated on the harbor, it's literally within walking distance of the airport terminals (about 1/2 mile away). It's surprisingly quiet though (with patio door closed), and if you're facing the water you probably wouldn't know you were next to an airport. If you're here for a conference you won't need a car (the free hotel shuttle from the airport runs continuously) but if you want to explore the city or eat off-property, you'll need a rental car or a cab. Unfortunately the hotel charges guests for parking, in an outdoor gated lot. There is almost nothing else to do in the immediate area except take a walk along the harbor. The two towers are really very separate buildings about 1/4 mile apart. The grounds are attractive and well cared for. Rooms are average sized, but all of them have a small balcony with room to sit and enjoy the view (at least from the higher tower rooms). Supposedly rooms have been recently renovated, but my room had quite a few signs of wear and tear, though none were serious. The desk and chair were comfortable to work at. The bathroom is well lit. Plastic drinking cups made it feel budget though. The bed was comfortable and I slept well. The HVAC system was efficient and quiet (a major plus for a good night's sleep -- no window AC units here). I didn't eat in the restaurants, but did stop by the Tapatini bar and enjoyed the drinks and atmosphere there. Scott, the bartender on duty, was excellent. Don't mistake this for a real tapas bar though -- it's an ordinary hotel bar with some pretty conventional appetizers. There are about 20 wines by the glass, though only two of them are of Spanish origin. Like most hotels in this class, they charge for internet in your room (two speed options) unless you have SPG elite status. It worked well. There was a minibar in the room with the usual high prices, should you prefer to enjoy a snack in your underwear and pay for the convenience. Tip: get your glass of wine down at the bar and you can take it back to your room. Though after you tip the bartender, the price probably comes out the same :-). In summary, this is a pretty standard hotel with comfortable and quiet rooms. If you get a good rate and don't mind paying for parking, it can be a solid choice. I for one appreciated the peace and quiet of the marina, and not being surrounded by chain restaurants, traffic and street noise.

“Fine for what we needed.” This is a budget Motor hotel. We took advantage of their stay and cruise package. We drove in from Phx, spent the night, walked to our cruise and left the car for the week. Came back a week later, picked up the car and left. No problems and excellent price. We did find it odd that they do these fly, cruise, and park packages, because they have very few parking spaces. In fact, they don't guarantee that guests will be able to park on premises. If your on a budget or just need a place to easily reach the airport or cruise ship pier, this place will meet those needs.

“extremely spacious” i booked through corporate and got excellent corporate rate, so the value for me was extremely high. if i got the price of 180 (averaged) shown here, i would give still give it 4.5* suite is very large. nice closed-off kitchen. main room spacious, with large granite dining table, separate work table, and flat panel 32".. storage/closet/bathroom is nicely segregated from bedroom. bedroom is also large, with 2 queen sized bed. i was on the 18th "hhonors" floor, so perhaps it is an upgraded room. the decor is much more modern than shown on tripadvisor user-submitted photos. would highly recommend this to colleages.

“This place knows how to treat a business traveler” This is a very impressive hotel. The public spaces are roomy and beautiful; the room was awesome -- spacious, comfortable, and a great mix of modern elements but design that remained true to Ft. Worth's aesthetic. Large and well-lit work area; really comfortable chair; roomy bathroom; fantastically comfortabled bed. The Select Guest program has great service. My room key awaited me at check-in, and -- as is true at all Omni hotels -- I was given the option to have coffee delivered to my room in the morning. I also ordered room service for dinner; it arrived quickly and was delicious. I also appreciated that the room service menu had some regional items. All in all, a fantastic stay; highly recommend.

“Quintessential Seattle” Inn at the Market was an absolutely exquisite experience, made all the more so because it was a surprise gift from my teenage daughter. She knew that I had been lusting to stay at this jewel of a boutique hotel ever since I read the wonderful review which Sunset Magazine gave it. Every time we passed by it when strolling through Pike Market, I would say: I wish we could stay one night at Inn at the Market. We live less than an hour's drive from Seattle in the Tacoma area, so we don't usually do overnights in Seattle. Besides, we are loyal Best Western guests, and Inn at the Market is more than double the rate of even the finest Best Western motel. Inn at the Market is quintessential Seattle - friendly, casual yet elegant, pleasing to the senses, practical. For reasons unknown, we were upgraded to a suite with gorgeous water views (my daughter insists she did not tell the hotel that we were celebrating my 55th birthday). The location can't be beat - in the heart of Pike Market, next to a fine (but pricey) French restaurant. The hotel itself houses a breakfast and lunch cafe which we wish we had tried, as the food fragrances were yummy and the place was packed. All day in-and-out valet parking (extra charge) made it easy to tour Seattle without fearing the loss of precious parking. In short - this wonderful Seattle hotel is worth the splurge in every way, shape, and form. Claire B - thanks for leading me to this place. Nancy W - your love and generosity made this hotel an added beautiful experience.

“Do NOT stay here” My company booked me here while I was in town for a tradeshow. The service at the hotel is terrible. I switched rooms and they had me sit in the room for 20 minutes waiting for them to call me back. i finally had to go all the way back down to get a new room. the second room smelled. the water for the shower changed temperature every few minutes, and the internet was spotty. I left my room in the am and by 2pm it still hadn't been cleaned. as a business traveler, this is completely unacceptable. management didn't seem too interested in fixing any of the issues. stay somewhere else!

“Way Overpriced” Stayed one night as a Hilton Honors member. Room rate was $223. Even though I had almost 50,000 points, I had to pay $14.95 for internet. A full breakfast will cost you $20 plus tax. Parking will also cost you $20. The hotel is spacious and has some elegance, but it is an older hotel that shows its age. The room was spacious and comfortable. The bed was very comfortable. Standard tub bathroom with an additional sink outside of the bathroom. It is a huge hotel, so be ready to walk and walk to get to your room. Chaos seems to be the norm in the lobby. Nothing is near. It only has two washers for this huge hotel and one was broken. Lots of aircrew, so good luck trying to use it. If you are a loyal Doubletree customer, the much better value is the one at 16500 Southcenter Pkwy., Seattle, WA 98188-3388. It is within walking distance of everything from restaurants to shops. Upon my arrival tonight I received a code for free internet and vouchers for breakfast as a Hilton Honors member. The only major drawback is that it does not have a laundry room. It is an older hotel but it has been kept up nicely. Finally, I can not recommend the Doubletree at 18740 International Boulevard. Just go down the road a bit to one at Southcenter.

“Good Convention/Business Hotel.....BUT!” This is a decent convention and business hotel property. Excellent convention facilities and accommodations for those purposes, and conveniently located in San Antonio for business meetings. The staff was excellent - friendly and always helpful. In my opinion however, two major flaws prevent this from being a good hotel. First, it has no gift shop or place to buy sundries. According to the staff, the gift shop is currrently under construction. I had to walk several blocks to buy some aspirin - and then had to wait for the drugstore to open. A good hotel would have made that trip unnecessary. Second, the Marriott Rivercenter charges for its internet access. That's so 1990's. Charging for internet in a business hotel is like charging for a desk. It's critical to do business in the current environment and a needless and aggravating add-on. I get it that some hotels are charging for amenities - but internet access is too fundamental in the current environment. I cannot recommend this hotel to anyone because of its policy of charging for internet access, and won't consider staying there again unless that practice is changed.

“Non è la fine del mondo, ma può andare” Il sito dell'albergo battezza impropriamente questa proprietà "Georgetown hotel and suites". A dire il vero l'albergo non è a Georgetown, anche se si può raggiungere a piedi in 10 minuti. La mia camera aveva una forma strana ma era molto grande. Pulizia e servizio nella norma. La posizione dipende da quel che si deve fare a Washington e dove si vuole andare - la cosa importante è che si trova nel quadrante nord-occidentale della città (quello sicuro). Non ci sono molti ristoranti nelle immediate vicinanze ma in 10 minuti a piedi si può raggiungere un po' di tutto. Direi che è un albergo americano medio a un prezzo accettabile.

“Good Hotel to Begin a New England Fall Trip” We enjoyed our one night stay here. The hotel is walking distance from Logan. It is a beautiful, modern, clean hotel. Our room was perfect for our needs and we found the staff to be accomodating. My single major complaint was the only restaurant open for dinner - Connollys Public. The very overpriced food was almost inedible!! After a long flight from the west we were very hungry and were more or less stuck there. I am surprised at Hilton for allowing such a restaurant in one of their hotels.

“Puts the Intercontinental to Shame” On a recent trip to visit family in Chicago and Milwaukee, I was able to stay at the Intercontinental in Chicago at the beginning of my trip, and to stay at the Omni for my last night in Chicago. Let me say, for some reason they are ranked as 5 star hotels, but the Omni is a TRUE 5 star hotel! It made my experience at the Intercontinental seem like something you would get at a Holiday Inn. The room, a very clean, functional, modern and comfortable suite. Room service food was promptly delivered, of excellent quality and of the correct temperature. Staff, friendly and competent. Location is perfect. Right in the middle of it all on North Michigan Avenue. In short... when in Chicago, stay at the Omni!

“A good Hyatt property” Only a 5 minute walk along the quiet section of The Riverwalk to the "main" section, so no disappointment there. Typical "big box" Hyatt convention property: marble floored bathrooms w/nice fixtures & good quality room furnishings. Nothing special, but good. Very dirty & stained hallway carpets that should have been cleaned long ago. The room carpet & upholstered chaise & pillows, were WAY past-due for a GOOD cleaning. Raises questions about "routine" cleaning schedules, & does not meet expected Hyatt standards. The $25 nightly self-parking fee would encourage a look at other properties. Would return, but probably not the 1st choide next time.

“Good, well located, contemporary hotel” Ive stayed in his hotel several times for business purposes. It is well located just off Market Street near BART (the subway system), is clean, contemporary and within the general price range for San Francisco hotels of this class. Service has generally been good. The rooms are acceptable, and there is nothing about this hotel that will disappoint, but equally there is nothing particularly special or memorable. Recommended.

“Fantastic rooms, still working out a few service kinks” I stayed here while on a business trip in Denver as we were able to get a great introductory rate. My room was large and comfortable, decorated in a clean, modern style. The beds were extremely comfortable and there was a nice workspace in the corner as well. The best part was definitely the bathroom - huge double sink area, fluffy bathrobes, great towels and bath amenities, tv in the mirror so you can catch the news while you get ready in the morning, large soaking tub, and separate shower with extra large rain shower head - awesome! I ate breakfast at the hotel as well as one dinner. Breakfast was good but nothing amazing, decent service. Dinner however was excellent - one of the best steaks I have ever eaten. Service was a bit over the top but friendly and informed. The bar seemed to be something of a hot spot, very busy all nights I was at the hotel. The few issues I would have with this hotel are small service issues that are likely just due to the hotel being new. One - some crumbs on the room floor were not vacuumed up over the course of three days. Everything else was spotless, so this stuck out as an oversight. Also, lobby staff was nice but I wouldn't say above your standard decent hotel chain. While this didn't really bother me, I could see how people who are used to VIP treatment might find it less "5 star" than comparable properties. I don't think I would pay the normal price to stay here, but it was certainly a great value for the price I paid and if I were able to get a comparable deal another time, I would definitely stay here again.

“Great Place to Stay, Friendly Staff” I stayed 3 nights for a business trip. I was very surprised by how friendly all of the staff were, including the housekeepers and night shift! That was unusual. The room was comfortable, and there were lots of pluses (like complimentary internet access). I was not "wowed" by the bed and linens, but they were reasonably comfortable. It was a good value.

“Hotel tres agreable idealement place” Une nuit en suite junior. Hotel idealement place a 2 pas de market street. Le batiment est superbe et charge d'histoire (rare pour SF). L'accueil et le service etaient de haut niveau, tant en terme d'efficacite que de courtoisie. La suite etait un peu decevante car le salon et la chambre ne sont pas separes. Le valet parking coute $48 HT mais de toutes facons tous les parking sont hors de prix a SF. Les prix de l'hotel sont tres raisonnables compares au standing.

“Stay Here!” We just returned from an 11 night stay at the Park South Hotel and had a very good experience. Our room was spacious for New York - a king executive - and although we only had one chair at the beginning, housekeeping provided us with the extra chair and small table as shown in the picture on the hotel website. Sandra at the front desk was responsible for this - she was so friendly and helpful, as was Jesus (pronounced Hey-soos) who arranged our return ride to LAG. We also requested a full sized ironing board since we were staying for so long and this was provided immediately as well. The closet was small but there were hooks by the door and if you hang your long things on hangers and then hang these on the hooks, it works. The room was very clean and smelled good and the bathroom was spotless (and I am a picky person who notices these things). Toiletries like shampoo, conditioner, shower gel and lotion are provided as well as a white robe, which was handy. The bed was very comfortable and we slept well every night. The a/c was loud but not enough to keep my husband awake and I use ear plugs anyway. We loved all the extras like the chocolates at the front desk (we ate many), the free videos (we watched several) and the breakfast which is every bit as wonderful as the reviews say and served until 11:00 for late risers. Also, we did not see any sign of gang activity and we were out some nights as late as 11:30 p.m. We took the subway everywhere and appreciated that it was so handy. There are scores of restaurants of every nature and kind close to the hotel, especially on Lexington and Third Avenues. My only disappointment was that we did not have a view of the Chrysler Building as shown on the Website but we probably wouldn't have had time to look at it much anyway. In any event, we certainly recommend this hotel and would probably go back.

“You have to see the picture!!!” A picture is worth a thousand words!!! #1 I arrived at midnight. Had to use the courtesy phone and it took 15 minutes for someone to come and check me in even though I already had a reservation. #2 I was so tired i just walked in and laid down on the bed without even unpacking. #3 I dozed off but was awakened within 15 minutes. My back, my neck, my arms and legs below the knee where covered with fleas. I could see them jumping all over. #4 I jumped into the shower, put all my clothes in a plastic bag and changed. By then even my suitcases had fleas. Called the front desk. The night lady was very courteous and did the best she could and she changed me from room 102 to another room. #5 In the am I asked to see the manager very politely and showed the reception lady the flea bites. She was RUDE and unpolite. They did not offer any type of apology. I had to ask them for a refund of one night. VERY RUDE SHIFT MANAGER AND LADY DURING NOONTIME. Also, hotel is nextto the freeway and there are no restaurants within walking distance. Parking is an issue at night. You may end up parking far from your actual room.

“Perfect for my needs” Checked in here for a one-night stay on a short business trip. Bell staff were welcoming when I drove up, but there was only one person manning reception with three people waiting to check in, which was a drag. This seems to be a feature of several of the Kimpton hotels I have stayed at. At least the guy apologized for the wait when I did finally get to the front of the line. One of the things I like about the Kimpton brand is that they have cocktails every evening in the hotel; another is that as a member of their InTouch program, you get a $10 mini-bar voucher and free internet access. The room I was allocated was on the top (19th) floor and had a nice view across LA. Though not especially large, for single occupancy it was absolutely fine and was nicely furnished. The bathroom likewise while not huge was sufficient for my purposes and both clean & well organized. I didn't use any of the hotels facilities so I can't comment on those. Check-out was early morning - there was a skeleton staff operating and once I located someone, everything was completed efficiently. Overall a satisfactory stay and a decent choice for anyone looking for a hotel in this part of LA.
“部屋によるみたいです” 場所は文句なしで、施設も古い感じはあるけど、いいです。 予約したときの値段によるのか、ずいぶん古くてミシミシという感じの部屋でした。 きっと、いい部屋を取れば、それなりなんじゃないかと思います。
“ne pas y aller!” hôtel vieux et en décrépitude. beaucoup trop cher. robinet de la baignoire grippe. chambre tres vieille, sale. heureusement que ce n'était que pour une nuit!attrape touriste!

“Fabulous room and location but without fabulous service” Second time staying at the Hyatt Regency and the first time since their remodeling. I love the location of this hotel and the new remodeled rooms are great. My husband is a Diamond member so we used one of his upgrades for a Junior Suite and the size and configuration of the room was perfect. Great beds, great pillows and a shower with strong water pressure. Those are the big three in my book. The reason I can not give it 5 stars is due to the attitude and service of everyone we encountered; except for one employee in the Club Lounge. We stayed there 2 nights to attend a wedding over New Year's, so that might be why we encountered so many problems. On the plus side, a manager called my husband the day after we returned to say that he had been told of our experiences and was calling to apologize and see what he could do to make the situation right. Very, very impressive. Needless to say, we are headed back to the Windy City this summer to take in a Cubs/Cardinals game and I have already made our reservation at the Hyatt. Also, food in the restaurant was really good as were the refreshments in the Club Lounge.

“Great hotel for families with kids” We stayed at this hotel for three nights in June and wished that we could have stayed longer. We have stayed in Embassy Suites close to 100 times, and I would put this Embassy Suites at the top. The rooms were large and the furniture newer. There was no smoky smell that I have found in a lot of Embassy Suites. The beds were comfortable, and the fridge and microwave in room were great pluses. This hotel has two swans in the lobby. I had read the reviews about how much kids love these swans, but had no idea how true this would be. Our kids had to go see the swans at least five times a day. They were allowed to feed the swans, and looked forward to this every morning. It amazed me at how entertaining the swans were! We would go down to the lobby for the evening snacks, and our kids were entertained for an hour or more with the swans during this time. The hotel has a free shuttle to the Galleria. The Galleria is great because it has a big food court, an indoor ice rink in the middle (fun people watching), and a kiddie play area on the top floor. We ended up going here every day for lunch, and the kids would spend a good hour playing in the play area. One day I walked back instead of calling for the shuttle. It is not a bad walk, but with two kids and shopping bags, I don't recommend it. There is a drug store in the parking lot of the hotel. This was great and we ran over at least once a day for snacks, water, etc. I think that this is one of the better Embassy Suites out there. Be warned that the place is filled with children, at least when we were there. We never had any problems with noise, but people without kids and looking for a relaxing stay may be annoyed. The pool is indoors, but a very nice one, and although we found times when it was empty, there were plenty of times when it was full of kids!

“Location, Location, Location” I got an excellent deal at the Hotel Fusion and spent a week there. They will match any rate you find online so do the research before you call to make reservations. I got a queen bed room for less than $70 per night based on their stay seven days and pay for five promotion. The hotel is in a perfect location only two blocks from the Powell Street BART station (at Market) as well as all the streetcar and bus lines that run along Market Street. The room was very clean and well furnished. The bath was a little small but very clean as well. All of the folks working at the hotel were very friendly and helpful. They have two computers you can use for free and a free continental breakfast as well. My room was very spacious with a queen bed, desk, two bedside tables, minibar, and flat screen TV. The room was large enough it probably could have been set up with two double beds with space to spare. The only downside is that there is no air conditioning and I happened to catch an unusual warm spell so open windows were a necessity. I chose a room facing the street so noise at times was a problem but more so during the day and I was rarely there during the day. They have inner rooms that I assume would be quieter. I knew all this before booking based on the reviews here and I had a choice of rooms but thought the street side would provide more of a view but really all you saw were the buildings across Ellis Street. If I am lucky enough to return to San Francisco, I would definitely stay at the Hotel Fusion again but would try one of the inner rooms this time.

“Great Experience At Homewood” We are a family of 5 so we try to find suites when we travel. We previously stayed at Embassy Suites in Philadelphia and were so disappointed we knew we had to find something else. We read the trip advisor ratings and decided to try this homewood suites. We had an excellent overall experience. We stayed in their huge 2 bedroom suite. This included a full kitchen and 2 bathrooms. The hotel building appears to be not new but a rehab. with rooms updated. there is a business center but the pool and exercise room are next door in the adjoining hilton. The breakfast was nicely done with continental items plus waffles, scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage. The evening reception was a great surprise. they had what could be an entire meal and most were eating it as such. We like to dine in Litlle Italy, but it was hard not to eat at Homewood. They had spaghetti, meatballs, garlic bread, rolls and salad bar one night and philly cheesesteaks with salad bar the other. This also came with all the beer and wine you could drink. The hotel was booked the days we stayed there, but we never had a problem getting a table. the staff was excellent in keeping tables clean and food replenished. The staff were so efficient and friendly, all of them, from housekeeping to the front desk staff. There is only 1 $5.00 charge put on your bill for the entire stay. You are not charged for leaving and returning to the lot. The only negative thing at this property were stained carpets in rooms and common areas. They should invest in a good carpet cleaner.

“Hotel rooms show there age” Staff was exceptional from arrival till we left. Overall the hotel is very nice, beautiful lobby and well appointed rooms. Bed was nice and mini bar was stocked with all kids of different stuff. Overall we had a very nice time, only complaint was the shower. Fixtures were dated, whirlpool tube looked old and very used. Shower head height is 6 foot, requiring most people to have to hunch over to wash your hair, for me that is a deal breaker. It is a very nice hotel, but not #2 in Dallas by any means.

“Very Good if it were not for the serenade outside our window” We stayed here with our 22 month old for 5 day vacation. I have stayed at a number of more modern hotels in this area and the embarcadero area and I was very pleased with this hotel. The one thing I would warn against is the noise level outside your window. Yes we had a decent view, but each night we had the bad drummer and the awful singer on the street below our window. I would also add that we were on a high floor and still heard the noise. So it is a give or take with the window and view. Our room was a 1 bdrm suite in the older section and it was on the large side. Both the bedroom and the living room were very adequate for our almost 2 year old to run around and play. However, the bathroom was a little on the small side compared to other rooms. Because we were in the old part there was a little upkeep that needed to be done. There was a place that looked like an old water leak in the ceiling that had not been repaired. The concierge and staff were very helpful in setting up a tour of Muir Woods and Saulsalito with rates very competitive to others we checked. The location was excellent with the exception of the noise level at night. So if noise is an issue when you sleep, you may want to move a couple of blocks up the street from the square. We enjoyed having Bart 3blocks away, you can catch the street car right in front of the bldg. Our daughter enjoyed playing in the park across the street. It is a very comfortable walk to Chinatown and Little Italy.

“rooms are huge but can be noisy; no door between the sleeping and sitting areas” first off--the good: the rooms are enormous and nicely furnished and the location is very convenient. it's walking distance from many of the downtown restaurants, just down the block from a mall w/a nordstrom's and carson pirie scott, and an easy drive to the zoo. we used the valet parking and it was great--well worth the $22. the $15 that the hotel charges for parking w/no in and out privileges is the same as what you'll pay at the surrounding garages and lots. breakfast was well-stocked and not crowded. and there was free internet in the room. however, it can be quite noisy esp if you get a street side room. we were on the 2nd floor, right on meridian and both fri and sat night the noise of bikers, revving car engines, thumping music, etc. lasted well past midnight. also, one of our main reasons for getting a suite is to be able to stay up after we put the baby to bed. however, there is no door in these suites between the living area and the sleeping area. the 2 are separated by a bathroom/closet area so you could sit quietly on the couch and read w/a dim light w/out too much light filtering back to the bed area, but still--it's essentially one big room (the rooms are laid out in a straight line, living rm/bath/sleep area). otherwise, the decor was quite nice and everything else was in excellent condition.

“Solid stay at the Marriott” Stayed here for two nights in Oct 2011. Hotels location is pretty good, very close to City Hall, 10 minute walk to the Historic District etc. Having paid $60 for the room on Priceline I was not surprised to have a view over the roof but the room itself was just fine. I suspect it is one of the rooms that has been refurbished, with nice decor, and a comfortable bed. I didn't eat in the hotel due to the nearby Reading Terminal Market, which has some outstanding options at very reasonable prices. Do not waste money paying for the hotel parking at around $40 per night - I printed a voucher from Central Parking System and left the car (at 12th and Sansom, around three blocks away)from Friday evening to Sunday morning for $23. Drop your bags at the hotel with the Bellman before parking. Overall the hotel was fine, and at $60 represented good value for money. At $150 bucks a night... maybe not.

“A very good hotel with excellent service” Stayed for 7 nights in mid July having prepaid on a good rate through British Airways. We were allocated a room with an internal view which was very nice but had a very small bed and only a chair at a desk as sitting space. As we were staying for a week we waited until later in the evening and spoke to reception to state that we would pay to upgrade to abigger room. The very helpful lady on reception agreed that it was a small room and said that as they were fully booked that night they would move us to a better room the following morning at no extra cost. Following lunch the next day we were allocated a corner room on the ninth floor with lots of space and a lovely view. This made a huge difference to the rest of our stay - a big thanks to Amy on reception for her assistance in this. In general the vast majority of the staff we encountered throughout the hotel were friendly, helpful and a big change from some of the big chain hotels we have visited. We had breakfast some mornings in the restaurant which was good value and importantly for us wasn't a buffet. One evening we ate at the bar in the City Table and the food/wine were excellent. In fact the only area in the hotel which we did not particularly like was the City Bar where the service by the waitress was slow and offhand but i suspect we did not meet her criteria for suitable customers in what is quite a trendy bar. Our room was very clean and well decorated and this is a hotel to which we would be delighted to return as it is in a great location - near to the "T" and close to a great choice of restaurants plus the Prudential and Copley malls for shopping.

“Good and clean but don't eat here” Good clean room and well proportioned. Staff very friendly. The restaurant is a disaster. We went for dinner at 7.00 and were told there were no potatoes left, then there were no crabcakes and other things. One of our party ended up with a dry chicken breast and a few fries. Thankfully they didn't charge her. They just aren't equipped for more than 10 for dinner. The breakfast next morning was fine but the waitress slammed the check down on the table and loudly announced that it didn't include a tip. I was tempted to give her a tip and I don't mean the monetary kind. She got the bear minimum.

“Believe the review” We stayed here fir 2 nights. Great place. Rooms lovely, but could do with triple rather than double glazing as NYC is pretty noisy. Great location, massive rooms, stunning service, think 4 seasons level, free wifi, decent gym down road and great location. Would recommend

“Charming” The Drisco is a charming and friendly hotel, in a quiet residential area. I was upgraded to a large and comfortable suite. The staff are friendly and accomodating, and they have a sunny sitting room on the main level and a large lower level dining room that serves a nice breakfast. The lower level has a small fitness center and a computer station. (guests have access to the local YMCA) Tripadvisor readers shoule be aware the Drisco is not particularly convenient to Union Square, Downtown, or the tourist attractions in S.F., but the City is compact and has good public transportation. I would definitely stay here again for a stay in SF.

“Never again!” Well. I had thought that the InterContinental was an upscale chain, having stayed at the one in Hong Kong (formerly the Regent). I was mistaken. I stayed at this one for 2 days while attending a meeting and was very disappointed. The positives first: location, staff, lobby, food/drink. A Starbucks in the lobby. These were all fine if not better than fine. I suppose the $276/night was for these features. And then the negatives.... The room was just deplorable. The Crowne Plaza in Minneapolis I stayed at last month was far better. I was in the "nonhistoric" side of the hotel--the room was tiny and in need of serious renovation. The bathroom was small, dingy, with peeling wallpaper, cheap or worn fixtures, scratchy towels, and sink faucets that went in the wrong direction. The bed was fine, however, comfortable with good linens. The fee to use the hotel gym was another unpleasant little surprise. I don't even know where to begin with that one, as I have not encountered that problem before. At what is basically $300/night, it seems insulting to ask hotel guests to pay extra for that. I guess I was shocked at the discrepancy between the attention to the nice lobby area, public spaces/services, customer service (excellent at the front desk and at the curb), and the very poor conditions of the room. I understand that this is a big city and that the hotel is in a great location, but I felt like I had been deceived. There are plenty of hotels to choose from in Chicago. Next time, even if I have to spend a little more, I will go elsewhere.

“Not your average Courtyard” This property is unlike the business park Courtyards from the 80s/90s, the layout and feel borders on a "full service" ambiance. It has been kept up to date over the years with tasteful renovations and the rooms are always comfortable and a great value. Travelers coming in on the BART or CalTran do have a few block walk, but cabs are a good option if you have plenty of luggage or there's always the 10 or 12 MUNI lines that run up 2nd Street from Market. Valet Parking is VERY expensive so if you must have a rental, it is always wise to try to find street parking or maybe a lot down the street. Lastly, the service the F&B outlets especially The Whispers lounge does seem a bit impersonal and overal lacking. Overall though a good solid stay each time.

“Upscale tasteful hotel but small rooms” The Monaco is very centrally located, stylish decor, excellent service, but rooms (at least some) very small, with little storage. Ours had besides the king bed, a desk and one small desk chair, basically no place to sit besides the bed and priced at $300/night. If you cant get an upgrade and a better price I'd look elsewhere.

“You get what you pay for” That is not to say that we didn't have a good stay - we did. But make no mistake, this isn't the Plaza. We booked through Hotwire as it was the least expensive option for the number of stars - 3&1/2. Thus, it turned out to be a good value. As others have commented, the location is great. An easy walk to Central Park and the subway stop at Columbus Circle where we boarded the express train to see the Yankees game in the Bronx. The following day, we used the subway to travel downtown to see Ground Zero. No transfers were needed on either trips. Times Square was also not a bad walk with lots to see along the way. The hotel is in need of some refurbishment. The elevators are way too small. On one occasion, the line for the elevators backed up into the lobby. The hallways show signs of neglect and part of our hallway was shut down as there was a water leak somewhere and the carpets had been soaked. But our room was fine. More importantly, it was clean. No bedbugs - thank God. The A/C worked fine and the outside temp was near 100. Our room with 2 double beds was quite spacious and our two teenagers had plenty of room. The gal at the concierge was pleasant helped us get Broadway show tickets. We had a good time and I would stay here again.

“Good 20 Century experience” The location is great for a tourist/business trip. Michigan Avenue is right there. The nearest subway station is about 6/7 blocks away, but the bus runs right next to the hotel. The service is great, thou the hotel is quite old; which has it pluses and negatives. The rooms are spacious and we had a great lake view, however the decor itself is just what I would call "granny like". You can tell the hotel was the "it" place 50 years ago, I just think it needs some bringing it to the 21 century. Room service was fairly quick. I was there because of a conference my partner was attending, but for the same money I probably would stay somewhere less "old flashy" and more substance, such as a place with a good gym or wireless internet in the rooms. Again nothing wrong with the hotel, just personal preference.

“Very nice Hilton as always” I stay at this Hilton Property several time a year, and find it is always up to standards of the Hilton Family. The staff is friendly, accommodating, and customer service oriented. The food service in the bar/restaurant has always been excellent as has the food. (Note to buffet breakfast food service mgr. I know it is difficult to keep food hot for an extended period of time, but the eggs, potatoes, and sometimes the breakfast meats are lukewarm, not hot.) The breakfast buffet has a variety of hot and cold breakfast items. The rooms (s) have always been clean, neat, well organized and have upgraded flat screen televisions. There are plenty of outlets for computer, phone, iPad etc, and the reading light on the nightstand is bright enough to actually read a book by!!! The hotel is located near a major shopping center/retail area with numerous choices for dining/entertainment/and shopping. The hotel is also close to downtown and Old Town San Diego. This is an excellent Hilton that I will stay at again, and recommend to anyone.

“Excellent Staff, Solid Business Hotel” I gave them 5 stars not because the Downtown Marriott is the best of the best -- it's still no Ritz or 4 Seasons, but for what it is -- a major chain convention center hotel, it's excellent. The staff is eager to please, the rooms are clean and the F&B was good. Aside from a cheesy lobby, it's a well-designed and quiet hotel. For $10/day you get unlimited hi-speed Internet and Long Distance, which is a deal. My only complaint was with the valet company they use -- they were slow (almost 10 minutes on average) to retrieve the car and for $32/day I expected a higher level of service from them. But since they're an outsourced service, I won't deduct that from the superb level service the Marriott provided.

“Great Anniversary” This was our second time staying at this hotel and was just as nice as the first time. I booked on Hotwire and still got a bay view room. The rooms and bathroom are big and well appointed. The beds are very comfortable and the coffee machine is an added bonus. It was or 12th anniversary and they bought us drinks in the lounge which we thought was very nice. We will definately stay here again.

“Flashy but hard to deal with” I just stayed here on business, and I had forgotten how hard it is to get around the Times Square area. If you are in town for shows and glitz, then this is most definitely your spot. TKTS is at the foot of the hotel. If you are there to try and get to other locations, not so much. It's not as close to the subway as other hotels, and you have to fight through the throngs of tourists just to get access to the lobby. Elevators for the upper floors are difficult to get, and you find yourself stuck with 5 and 6 floors of tourists before you find yourself at your floor. The check-in is on the 8th floor. It reminded me of a cross between the Contemporary at Disney World and a large Las Vegas casino hotel. Staff is very nice and helpful. The view was breathtaking, and I wasn't paying, so at the end of the day, fun place in the middle of a lot of action. But if I was floating my own bill, $400+ a night is not worth the hassle.

“GHOST TOWN?” Hotel new super clean rooms are a little small but well equipped.The bed was a little hard for me.Staff is friendly & efficient.During my stay I only saw 1 other person hmm.Easy access to shops,eating places.Hotel also has a restaurant in hotel but I never saw any one there.Kinda creepy as I felt we were the only ones staying here.

“Fantastic location, great views from the 33rd floor” The hotel itself was nice - what you'd expect from a Westin - but the location is what I'd rave about most. It's so convenient to everything, and the hotel is even attached to a mall. Newbury Street is only a few blocks away, and if you're feeling feisty, you can walk most of the city from there. Free wi-fi in the lobby. Cant beat the Heavenly Bed. The bathroom was only meh. Also, if you're not registered as a Starwood Preferred guest, I'd advise signing up (it's free) and there's always a good chance you'll pick up a few perks (higher floors, better amenities, etc).

“Great Choice for Uptown / Downtown Dallas” This was my first stay at the fairly new Ritz Carlton in Dallas. The rooms are nice and the common areas and restaurants are first-rate. It is definitely one of the best hotels in Dallas. The hotel service was what you'd expect from a top end hotel. The employees were helpful, friendly, and out-going. The room was nice. I was in a junior suite with a good sitting area. (While it was spacious, I think the Stoneleigh down the street has a slightly better junior suite in terms of layout.) The bed was very comfortable. It had a goose-down mattress pad which was a bit soft for me, but I think most people would like. The bathroom was very nice. It had two sinks, a separate commode, a bathtub and a stand up shower. The water pressure was acceptable and the towels were fresh and plentiful. While at the hotel we had an excellent breakfast in the Fearings restaurant. It was pricey, but worth every penny. Some of the folks I was traveling with had dinner there and said it was also excellent. In the evening we had some drinks at the bar and it was very lively and had great service. The hotel has good valet parking and the valets were helpful with directions, etc. If you have friends or colleagues coming to uptown or downtown Dallas, this is a very safe bet.

“Great location, great value, very small rooms” The location of The Mosser is phenomenal, it is right at the hear of the city, walking distance to most attractions. The value is unmatched for this location. The hotel is clean and comfortable. So this is a great pick for anyone who is there to tour the city. But if you want to spend time in your room, this is not the hotel for you as the rooms are unbelievably small (see photos). Also, print your reservation when going there, they had our rate and dates incorrect on file and our printed reservation saved us from the pain.

“Typical Marriott -- Fine Property but Nothing Special” Stayed at the San Diego Marriott Gaslamp Quarter hotel over a weekend in June 2011. It's a fine hotel but nothing out of the ordinary for a Marriott. The location is good -- especially if you are baseball fan since Petco Park is literally steps away from the front door and we had a view of the field from our room. Unfortunately, the Padres were away for the weekend. The room was comfortable but nothing to brag about (the bathroom in particular was pretty small). The bed was too soft for my taste. Our reservation included the breakfast buffet, which was excellent, as was the service. We also ate dinner there on our last evening (a Sunday) when the restaurant was dead. There was only one other party seated at the same time. The Gaslamp is one of San Diego's hip areas but it is not for everyone. Plenty of restaurants and bars, which is both a plus and a minus. There are tons of options but there were a lot of drunk people as well as pretty aggressive homeless people around. I never felt unsafe but some people may be very uncomfortable staying in this part of town. I had combined a stay at the Marriott with one at the Del Coronado across the Coronado bridge. Nothing against Marriott, but for the extra $80 a night I wished I had just stayed at the Del.

“Better than average Residence Inn” Typically I would skip reviews on standard business class hotels like this, but this Residence Inn was better than average for a Marriott property in mid-town.
