In fact, I would venture to say that for room size, comfort, location, and amenities that this is my new "go-to" hotel for NYC. You can't beat free wifi, breakfast, and well-equiped rooms with a kitchen. The location is excellent and is well suited for both business and leisure travelers. If for some reason you find yourself driving into mid-town -- you may want to call the hotel to understand their parking policy -- I gathered from a co-woker that it can be troublesome.

“Loved this Hotel” Excellent Embassy Suites. This one is a little different in that it does not have the typical atrium - love the atriums in the others but not the noise that you find in the other Embassy Suite locations. Outstanding staff who provided personable attention. Each staff member from front desk, to maid, to valet went out of his or her way to provide personalized service. Great rooms - comfortable yet with a modern touch. Free internet access was an added bonus. $28 to valet park but understandable given the downtown location. Breakfast could not be beat and the breakfast guy truly went out of his way to get each guests morning off to a right start with the great food he prepared and his friendly energetic demeanor. This will be my first choice in hotels when in downtown Houston.

“absolut okay” das B.W Roundhouse Suites ist für Bostoner Verhältnisse eine gute Adresse. Zentral auf einem Verkehrsknotenpunkt gelegen,erreicht man alle Sehenswürdigkeiten in Minuten, mit dem Auto natürlich. Wenn man ohne Auto unterwegs ist, kann man den kostenlosen Shuttleservice in Anspruch nehmen. Durch diesen Verkehrsknotenpunkt und der angrenzenden Tankstelle, wo ab und an Busse warm laufen, ist es teilweise etwas hektisch und die Fenster sollte man schon zu lassen(ohrenstöpsel nicht vergessen)..aber das historisch Gebäude hat trotzdem seinen Reiz. Die Zimmer sind zweigeteilt ,2 tv sets, und recht gemütlich, grosse frühstück incl, was braucht man mehr...

“Very clean, friendly, rooms just a bit small.” We stayed here with our 4 month old and had trouble with space as we had both a stroller and a portable crib to squeeze in. So, factor that in when I say room was a bit tight. We had a neat view of the Baltimore baseball stadium. I enjoyed having the free city shuttle bus stop right outside the hotel, very convenient. A nice, very big lobby made the hotel feel spacious. Lots of conferences are held here as it ajoins to the Baltimore convention Center which also was the reason for our trip. Solid 4 star, no real complaints here.

“Funky, Chic, Unpretentious” My colleague and I had been traveling nonstop for several weeks, and we always lamented that our standard corporate Hiltons and Sheratons were a bit boring. Fortunately, our company sponsored hotel in San Francisco was booked, so we checked out the Phoenix! The location is give-and-take - it's near the Civic Center BART stop, but the surrounding area is a tad, um, gritty. I didn't feel unsafe at any point, but my colleague was solicited by an, ahem, lady of the night while waiting for a cab at 5:30 AM the next morning. Definite plus - the hotel has ample free parking! Check-in was a tad sluggish due to only one agent and a constantly ringing phone, but the agent was very friendly and made plenty of dinner suggestions and cheerfully arranged a cab for us. The adjacent courtyard/pool area is vibrant and fun with plenty of lounge chairs and dining/drinking area nearby. I was concerned that this would be loud at night, but, fortunately, it was dead silent (but, I was there on a Wednesday night!). The room was tropical in theme and had virtually everything needed. The bed was comfortable, and the in-room local coffee was fantastic. The bathroom was clean, yet it did lack counter space for personal items. The ceiling fan was a great touch to circulate the air given the hotel doesn't have air conditioning (not that it was needed). The only bad part - the room seriously smelled like incense. I got used to it, but it is overpowering at first. Overall, it was fun - I wish we had time to check out the pool and bar, but perhaps another time!

“Over the Top Service, Outstanding Property” Stayed at this property for two nights with my wife, while we were in town for a wedding. Weekend rates were a bonus,as was the bump to a club level corner room. What an amazing property. You will not be disappointed choosing this property. Check in was great, however our room was not ready but that was ok considering we arrived before published check in time. Front desk staff took my phone number and called within 45 minutes to let us know it was ready. The Room, furnishings and views were fantastic. Fun to see the Dodger Stadium lights off in the distance in the evening. The Bathroom was huge, but that comes with the corner room. Not sure a standard room in the middle of the hallway would be the same. I must say I am not a good hotel sleeper..usually takes me a night or two to get comfortable and to block out noises..I also hate the constant door slamming that goes on at hotels. At this property I didn't hear a door slam once, and slept like a baby both nights....That was awesome. If you are similar in your pet peeves about hotels, stay at this one..you'll sleep great! We visited the club lounge on the top floor each morning for a great breakfast and evening for light snacks and beverages (adult ones too!) Great service and hospitality from all staff in the club lounge. We used the valet service for our rental car. Parking is a bit steep, but that's typical for L.A. 20 bucks a night Friday and Saturday and 40 a night Sunday-Thursday. We stayed on labor day weekend, so was disappointed we had to pay 40 for the Sunday night before Labor Day since it was not a business day on the following Monday...but, that honestly would be my only complaint. Make sure you become a select guest member, as you get some great free perks. It doesn't cost anything to join and provides some neat services. Morning beverage service, newspaper, and the ability to get clothes press and shoe's shined. We took advantage of all of those services. It's a great example of all OMNI properties and what they do to please their guests. Compliments to the general manager of this property and the fine folks that work there. You will not regret booking and staying at this Omni. Have a great time! We sure did.

“Classic but she's showing her age............” I travel to this city often, so often that I have my regular places that I eat and I don't need a map to get around. I usually stay at the Hilton, but most recently I have been staying at Kimpton properties, as they have a more competitive rate that fits my corporate budget. My usual hotel was booked, so I decided to try the Drake. I have always passed it and even enjoy the starlight room countless times, but never stayed. My overall impression is good, but there are some obvious upgrades that are needed. Lets' start by my experience at check-in. I was able to get a room early (9:30 am), the guy who helped me was cordial and attentive and I was surprised I was able to check-in so early. That's a huge plus for me! However, when I entered my room my smile turned into a frown. The room was spacious, but on the 3rd floor, which meant very little sunlight. The room is nicely painted, but some of the furniture is old and the areas of the wall that are white; need to be painted immediately. I checked my bed, as I always do for bed bugs. The sheets had holes in them. Not good. Luckily, there was another bed in the room. Overall impression of the rooms; it is OK for a short business trip, but I would really have a hard time staying here for pleasure with my other half, until some upgrades are made. For the rate, you can't beat it. $157 in June is great, when other hotels are charging rates in the $200. Location wise, you are in the middle of it all, there's a walgreen's and a starbucks right outside the hotel. The staff was very nice and attentive, but like other reviewers, I was not told about the complimentary drinks at the lobby; however being a Kimpton member, I knew what to expect. For the price, this is a bargain, but if you are looking for something more elegant or newer, this may not be the place for you, until management makes the necessary upgrades that are required. The hotel itself is beautiful, built in the late 1920's. Ask for a higher floor, but not too high, as there is a nightclub on the top level. I always ask myself, would I stay again? Only if the rate is competitive and it is a one night trip, but I don't see myself staying multiple days. I rated this hotel very good, but in reality, it is a 3.5 stars!

“Wish I could have given more stars.....except for that one thing!” First of all - Indigo is not really in the Gaslamp - it is just a few short blocks away in what is referred to as the East Village - but that did not really effect us. In fact I really like the location/neighborhood. It would be the must stay place if in town for a Padres game with a very cool gastropub (Knotty Barrel) across the street. The room was nice and clean - I really liked the wood floors. The whole reason we stayed here was because it was a LEED hotel and wanted to check that out. The one thing that people should be aware of is that it is a pet friendly hotel....that did not bother me - but it may some people if they have allergies or not into animals. There was some barking on our floor but it was not disruptive - but something to consider, again, if you are not an animal lover. We had a drink at the roof bar - great views - but limited selection. The staff was friendly and helpful from check in to the valet drivers. When we stayed there I was thinking that I was all set to give 4+stars, but then we had a negative situation with the management/housekeeping. Upon arriving at the airport my husband realized he left 2 shirts behind laying on the bed as he was packing. Yes, it is his fault that he forgot them - but he immediately called the hotel and they said he needed to email the manager of the lost and found as he was not working at that moment. He emailed him requesting that the shirts be mailed and that he would cover the cost for the shipping and any inconvenience this caused. When we did not hear back - so we called the hotel again and they said he was the person we needed to speak with and he was off. 2 days later we received a succint email saying the items were not found and to call the housekeeping manager if we had further concerns. We called her immediately and she said she did not have the items in her lost and found, but would check again and return my call. She did not return the call so I called again the next day and left a message and still we have never heard back from her. This was disappointing on many levels. Yes I realize that it was our responsibility to remember the items - however - we callled immediately and were sent through a lengthy process of days where obviously someone saw the items and claimed (stole) them. I find this very disturbing that the housekeepers or other employee would find it "okay" to take something left behind in a room. I understand if something goes unclaimed for weeks or months the hotel has to have a way to deal with the items, but we called the day we checked out, sent emails and followed up to no avail. It is not that the items were expensive or unique - it is more the principal of the matter and how poorly Hotel Indigo handled the situation. I think they may want to set a policy for their housekeepers/employees that taking something that is left behind by a paying guest is theft and not acceptable. So if not for that incident it would have been a 4 stars - but could not give more than the 2 stars because it left a bad taste in my mouth!

“Give it a Shot...Nice Stay” I remember this hotel was part of the Pan Pacific collection, from years back. Public areas were clean. Valet was fast and efficient. The front desk agents were professional and cordial. I asked for an earlier check-in, and they obliged without hemming and hawwing. We used the shuttle for the ballgame and were dropped off very close to Petco Park. Only bad thing in the room is that the cordless phone unit was not wired to the wall. The business center had a broken printer. Breakfast was amazingly nice and the price was very good for the buffet. Free local newspaper for a Sunday morning was a good touch. We will return to the hotel, whether it is during the baseball season or not.

“Terrific Phoenix Airport Hotel” I live in the Phoenix area. However, faced with an early morning flight, there was no way that I was going to get up at 4:30AM, drive fifteen miles or so, search for airport parking, etc. So, thanks to a great deal on Priceline, I spent the night here. Happy Hour the night before was great. Dinner was absolutely delicious. The staff was most courteous. The bed was quite comfortable. The room was quiet. The shuttle bus to the airport left right on time and my car remained parked – safe and sound – in the hotel parking lot for the duration of my trip for $5 per night. Excellent! I highly recommend this hotel!

“very mediocre Sofitel” I stayed 5 nights at the Sofitel Washington DC. Overall I was not impressed. Problems started at the check in with the requested room not being available and staff being very rude. Eventually I got the room but after 8 hours of flying I was not in the mood for rude staff especially considering that I'm an A-Club Platinum member and last year stayed over 90 nights at Sofitel hotels. They also had no clue about the rate I booked (50$ credit offer). There was no luggage service so off I went with my luggage to my room which was small and definitely showed signs of ageing: wall paper peeling near the curtains, stains on carpets and for whatever reasons you can't open any of the windows in any of the rooms. None of my Platinum perks arrived throughout the trip. There is no proper turn down service, except a bottle of water, compare this with any other Sofitel around the world where you are showered with sweets and chocolates. Breakfast is made to order and at least twice they got it wrong and another time I received the wrong check. Not overly impressive and expensive. Room service was marginally better and the staff very friendly (probably the best throughout my stay). The bar can be a bit overpowering if you don't like obscure loud Jazz. Not what I was looking for to have a quiet drink. Bathrooms are large and feature a pleasant large shower (same as the Sofitel NY). The Sofitel MyBed still is the best in the market and very comfy. On my last day I had ordered a taxi and when it arrived I got a call saying that it was waiting for me and again no offer of a porter collecting my luggage. Rather than chatting to each other and only occasionally opening the front door for you they should do their jobs and helping guests with luggage. The real problem with the Sofitel DC is that the staff don't seem to care and are far from enthusiastic. I am afraid the DC Sofitel gets my award for the worst performing Sofitel in 2009.

“If you don't require a lot of service, it's PERFECT!” Stayed here during our recent visit to San Diego. It was one of those times when the hotel was just as good as we hoped! We weren't expecting a five-star luxury resort, but we still thrilled with it. We got a two-room suite (well, a bedroom and a sitting room with a faux kitchen and a good-sized bathroom) and it covered our needs quite well (two parents and two girls so we wanted some separate space). Everything was very clean and comfortable, we had a fabulous balcony/deck looking towards Mission Bay, and the staff responded quickly the couple of times we had minor needs. Bear in mind that the hotel rooms open to the outside, not an enclosed hallway - not a problem, just thought you should know. We were very happy with it and will most likely stay there again next time we visit SAN (it is located about three minutes from Sea World).

“Outstanding Service” Seamless service from start to finish. I don't know how they do it, but the service is on par with any Four Seasons in the United States. I was most impressed that every staff member acknowledged me when in passing, and some even by name. The deluxe patio room was a good choice but unusable at night due to the streetlights, but a great place to relax in the daytime. The restaurant was a treat - great ambience, creative menu, flawless service, and definitely overpriced, but definitely worth it for the overall experience. Here's a tip for guests arriving by car and from out of town: the entrance is NOT on Turtle Creek Blvd. Enter from Gillespie street. Go figure. I would stay here again....and again.

“Great beds, incredible service, dated bathrooms” The service at this Marriott is impeccable! They will upgrade you or provide lounge access...all you have to do is ask. The beds are very comfortable - on par with any upscale Marriott. The bathroom is starting to show its age and lacks granite or other personality for a semi-upscale hotel. They recently upgraded the gym to all high-end equipment...nicely done gym! This is a safe bet for a comfortable stay on the North side of Indy.
“Great Location and Very Comfortable” I like the location and amenities. If you are focusing on Marriott properties, it is worth the difference in cost to the Renaissance.

“Hip & Centrally Located” Like its sister hotel in the Meatpacking district, this hotel very much airs on the hip and cool. A great Italian Restaurant, Rooftop Pool & Bar Scene and stunning views of the city (especially from the upper floors). As with hotels that concentrate on the nightlife aspect, the rooms are a little disappointing. Certainly smart, spacious (which is a plus in New York) and with everything you could possible need - but the decor is a little cheap and corporate (you would have thought that they would have pushed the boundaries more). However, this downside is compensated with great staff and service - all are incredibly friendly and helpful. There is also a great gym and spa (with lots of classes). The hotel is also in a wonderful central location in the city.

“Facilities nice, reservation management needs improvement” I am a Kimpton fan, and found this hotel, overall, in keeping with the brand's image and execution. However, they mucked up my reservation pretty good, caused significant inconvenience, and then mucked up their apology. Net, a lot of muck ups. I extended my reservation by one day, the reservations agent assured me that this would be included in my original reservation, no need to change rooms or check out and re-check in. When I checked in, they had the right dates, everything seemed fine. I returned to my room to get materials for a meeting and found I was locked out (because they did NOT extend the reservation as promised and as indicated when I checked in). The ensuing chaos resulted in my being hugely late for a meeting. They attempted to compensate by giving me extra coupons to use with the minibar, but then wouldn't honor them (you can only use 1 per stay!). When I brought this up to the front desk staff, they said there was nothing they could do. Really disappointing. Not sure I'll stay at this Kimpton again.

“Liked it” This hotel was perfectly fine and we had a good stay. It's nothing fancy, but it's clean, comfortable, well-located, and the staff is super friendly and helpful. The room was a bit small, but I've seen smaller elsewhere. The bathroom was clean and the shower worked well. We were given a free breakfast, perhaps because of my Hilton Honors status or perhaps the nice man at the desk generously provided it. The breakfast was good, but I wouldn't have spent $14 on it otherwise. I'd stay there again. It's definitely nice to stay in a place that's quiet and not a madhouse. The neighborhood has a lot to offer, but at night the street is dark and a bit abandoned, but not unsafe. In daylight it was busy and fun with the flower shops.

“Perfect for visiting Washington. In front of Convention Center!! Perfectp para visitar Washington, al frente del centro de conve” Es un hotel que satisface todas las necesidades para un muy buen viaje. Cerca de todo, 2 estaciones de metro cerca, buen precio, muy buen ambiente, excelente trato, buen gimnasio con sauna y minipiscina/jacussi. Mi proxima elección!!!

“Had to change rooms but did not get better!” Good location and fair price but not up to SPG standards. Several bulbs out in room including bathroom. Toilet did not flush all the way. Elevator issues for several days. Hotel is need of a restoration.

“Great suite and location, nicest staff ever, but sadly no more ESB view” Stayed for six nights in a 1BR suite. Living room and bedroom are EACH larger than most NY hotel rooms. Very clean suite in good condition. No torn wallpaper, no mold, no beat up furniture, old style TVs but we never used them. Very comfortable king size bed with the softest linens. Window unit ACs are a bit noisy but made for good sleeping. Yes, there is a fire station next door on 31st street so you hear the sirens (but the AC mostly drowns them out). We were on the 25th floor and after a week in NY at another hotel we were already used to hearing traffic and sirens so it didn't bother us at all. Our bathroom was smallish but had a large shower, granite countertop and lighted makeup mirror. Big fluffy bathrobes were provided. The hotel has changed from Aveda products to a lesser brand that I didn’t like as well but the Italian olive oil soap was nice. I also thought the hairdryer was great, much better than most hotel hair dryers. Keep in mind that every suite in this hotel is configured differently so room sizes and layout are described differently in every review. Liked having the small kitchen. It had cheap cabinets and dishware but was fine for basic dining. Although we did not cook we did eat in several meals utilizing the microwave and fridge. The best food hall we found was the Grand Central Market in Grand Central Terminal. Didn't care for the quality of food at the Cucina in Macy's although it was the most convenient. Didn't try the Wholefoods that is just a few blocks south. This month a new food hall is opening in the Plaza Hotel shopping mall so we'll try that next time. Wolfgang Puck brand coffee was supplied and replenished every day. Our hotel package included breakfast vouchers at Niles Restaurant next door. Good breakfast buffet and nice trendy decor. Niles also provided the hotel with room service. The room had good wi-fi for $14.95 per 24 hours. The desk chair was a good quality ergonomic chair, better than we’ve had at higher end hotels. The desk rolled out to make into a dining table. Lighting in both living room and bedroom was very good; lamps on three way switches and dimmer switches so you could set your mood but could be turned up bright enough for reading. The artwork above the bed even had a dim-able picture light. We didn't try the pillow menu (the standard pillows were very comfortable) or any of the MyAffinia offers (iPod walking tours, picnic and wine accessories, etc.) but plan to do that next time. We had a corner suite so it was very sunny with five windows. Great view of lower Manhattan from our south facing windows. We had lots of storage space with three closets, a six-drawer dresser and drawers/shelves in two bedside tables. The hotel lobby is the only part of the hotel that harkens back to its historical roots as the 1929 Hotel Governor Clinton (named for DeWitt Clinton who was mayor of NYC and NY state governor in the 1800s). The large art deco lobby is still quite lovely. Rooms on the east side of the hotel used to have grand views of the Empire State Building but within the past year a new modern glass tower is under construction that completely blocks the ESB from the Affinia. All we could see from our room was the spire. But the hotel celebrates the locale with a toy King Kong doll in every suite. The location and staff are the best things about this hotel. Front desk staff and bellmen are friendly in a genuine way; some of the nicest we've encountered in many years of travel. We will be back and would highly recommend. Would also be willing try any of the other Affinia hotels assuming they are as well managed at the Manhattan.

“Kimpton hotels never disappoint!” I love Kimpton - you always get a modern, clean, trendy hotel in a good location for a fair price, The Hotel Palomar was no exception. The rooms were average size, comfortable and pristine. Location was perfect to explore the area and the best part is Sable Kitchen and Bar in the lobby - amazing cocktails and food!

“Teeny tiny rooms. This used to be the Doral Inn and not expensive” Over 20 years ago, I worked at the front desk of this hotel when it was called Doral Inn. It was an inexpensive business hotel with a large airline crew and South American tourist business. For this guests got a low price in a great location for a tiny room. The only thing that has changed today is guests get a high price in a great location for a tiny room. The room I am in right now is the same layout as when it was Doral but just funkier and the lobby was noisy. I am glad the elevator has key control to allow guests only as when I checked in last night at 11 pm two people were refused rooms as they did not have proper ID. This is not a short stay hotel. Tiny rooms, noisy lobby that is more night club than business functional. It works for me but I prefer the Grand Hyatt and NY Palace where I usually stay in NY: Very expensive internet which they had led me would be free.

“Great Hotel..... best in Indianapolis” Have stayed here many times this year on business and thought it was time to write a review. This hotel is awesome and by far my favorite in Indianapolis. The staff is top shelf. The hotel is new, rooms are great and the concierge floor is one of the best I've ever experienced. The gym is better than most health clubs. Just thought you should know... Don't stay anywhere else in Indy... this hotel takes First Place!

“Disappointment” Although the hotel's mid-town location is great and the room size was adequate, they've lost control of some very important systems. They issued us incorrect keys and then couldn't make their computer acknowledge we were staying for two nights, not one. Thus our keys failed twice more. Both nights a fire alarm went off in the next room. (The second night it went off three times). Although the peeling wall paper and chipped paint wouldn't have been fatal flaws if everything else was OK, it wasn't.

“Fantastic hotel and service” The hotel was very nice and the service extremely professional. Check in was very smooth and efficient. I did not make the reservations- a firm I was visiting handled all my travel. I was given an upgraded suite and it was fabulous. Huge and nicely decorated in a very sleek modern kind of way- not my thing but still it was a nice room. It had a gigantic living room, a small dining area, a large bedroom, a large bathroom, and a smaller powder room. Really more space than I needed! The service was very friendly and exceedingly professional, I was very impressed. I had room service for dinner one evening and it was quick and the food was excellent and not that expensive (for room service!), but really worth it. I ordered coffee every morning and it was excellent and brought to my room very promptly (within 10 minutes). There were many nice touches- great towels, newspaper of your choice in the morning, fresh flowers in the room. I was very impressed with the hotel and would stay here again.

“Excellence by the sound” This is a stellar hotel sitting right on the edge of the sound. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, with excellent appointments. All just what you'd expect from a Four Seasons. The service is equally charming and attentive. This the kind of hotel that makes travelling the perfect mix of adventure and creature comforts.

“A very comfortable bargin hotel” We stayed here to catch an early morning flight, and we were very satisfied as it served the purpose well and was VERY cheap. The bed was very comfortable. As far as the noise, we didn't notice much (but we habitually take ear plugs with us to hotels just in case). The cleanliness was fine, with the exception of dust and hairs along the baseboard of the bathroom. The shuttle to and from the airport was very prompt and easy to use (they gave us a business card with detailed instructions). We left eariler than breakfast was served (starts at 5:30 AM), but they have coffee and tea 24 hours a day, and had dry goods out for breakfast at least by 3:30 AM (bagels, muffins, cereal with milk). The manager was very helpful about telling us how to use the public transportation. It is just a short walk to the bus stop (the R1 train was closed for service; bus #37 goes by the hotel twice and hour; tickets are $2 each way or one can get a pass / pay on the bus with exact change; we got off at the end of the bus line at Snyder and Broad and took the orange line subway at the bus stop to City Hall to see the Liberty Bell, etc.). We ate dinner at Ruby Tuesday, which is also just a short walk from the hotel. The hotel seemed safe. Our car was there while we were gone and it was fine. One thing we really liked is that the manager said "long term" parking was in the back of the hotel, but we could park our car anywhere in the parking lot we felt comfortable leaving it.

“Hotel idealement place, decor tape a l'oeil mais service luxueux !” Nous avons sejourne du 11 au 14 novembre dans cet hotel, idealement situe en plein coeur de Washington DC, a deux pas de la Maison Blanche. Le decor des parties communes est ostensiblement tape a l'oeil version annees 80, avec des lustres grandioses genre emissions d'Ardisson :) Malgre notre arrivee tardive, le check-in fut facile et rapide. Le tarif auquel nous avons reserve avec Priceline ($100) nous laissait a penser que la chambre serait mediocre : pas du tout, elle fut de tres bonne qualite. Ma partenaire souffrant de mot de tete, le receptionniste s'est propose pour trouver des medicaments. Ce qui fut fait, il nous les apporta dans notre chambre ! Un sens du service exceptionnel, digne d'un palace. Comme dans tous les hotels de ce niveau, les prix du room service et des petits-dejeuners sont prohibitifs. Neamoins, la carte du restaurant est abordable au dejeuner comme au diner, et la cuisine de bonne qualite. La chambre est bien equipee : peignoirs, cafetiere, fauteuil de relaxation avec Ottoman. Les lits sont de bonne qualite, mais sans plus (ce n'est pas un point fort du groupe Marriott). Check-out simple et rapide sur television. Bonne surprise, donc.

“Very Nice-Free parking if you know where to look*” Very nice property, clean, spacious, lots of choices for breakfast. Some things I haven't seen in other reviews. Directly past the hotel less then 25 yards is Aloha Street on one side, Valley Street on the other side. Both of these streets border the hotel. Parking is FREE from 6 p.m. to 8 a.m. AND Parking from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. is $1.25 an hour with a TEN hour maximum. There are machines that take credit cards. So even if you were to park there for 24 hours it would still only be $12.50 compared to the 20+ they charge inside the hotel. Also directly across the street from the hotel are numerous seafood restaurants right on Lake Union. We ate at Joey's one night and C (something) the next night. Both were excellent. The hotel is less than five minutes to downtown and ten minutes by car to Pike's Market. Reasons the hotel didn't get five stars. Like most properties, their fitness facilities were only okay. Two Life Fitness ellipticals, two treadmills, and a few free weights. There is a very nice 24 Hour Fitness at 1827 Yale Street, approximately five minutes away by car. Their "evening food" was plentiful; however they only serve it Monday through Wednesday; what is up with that?? And they only offered beer and wine on Tuesday. Also, during rush hour from downtown this hotel takes a while to get to with a lot of traffic trying to get on I-5. Non-rush hour is a breeze. Staff is very friendly which is always a plus. Internet is free as it should be. Overall, an excellent place where I will stay again. Cheers. Marius

“warming up to fairfield” I am feeling my way along in selecting moderate accommodations for business travel in mostly the south-southwest. I have been through Hampton, Hawthorne, Holiday Inn Express and most recently tried Fairfield. I found it a cut above the rest. They seem to take the Marriott lessons learned and policies and apply them to their more budget properties and it works. The Austin South/Airport Fairfield is not at the airport. It is on the access road of I35, and from there you go a few blocks, get on highway 70 and drive a few miles to the airport. In pre-rush hour it took me a half hour and I got lost once. At rush hour the location is rough if you are driving from the north to the hotel from downtown Austin. It is located in a Marriott "campus" with several other Marriott brands like Courtyard etc. You apparently can use some facilities in the other Marriotts (like a 24 hour store and work out room) though I did not follow through on those after asking them about it. This Fairfield has a small excerise room with a treadmill according to the desk, but I did not get the chance to use it. The Marriott training program is the big difference in my mind between Fairfield and the other economy chains. Instead of a tired, bored front desk person hired through a want ad, such as you find at Hawthorne, you have a vibrant, excited and informative clerk who acts as though he is the concierge at the Waldorf and obviously has been trained in the Marriott ways. The guys were full of suggestions and directions when I inquired about the Austin music scene. The room was thoughtfully designed and maintained. Fairfield has ditched the nasty bedspreads which never get washed and are pulled up over your pillow. They wrap your blankets in clean, soft and seemingly new sheets. There are little touches like outlets installed in table lamps so you don't have to pull out heavy furniture and crawl under tables to try to plug in the iron. My room also had a refrigerator in it. The breakfasts weren't quite as hearty or hot as the competitors...no hot egg dishes. But the rest of it was plenty for me and of course it was free with a friendly hostess. I am pretty much a Fairfield guy from here on until something goes wrong. They do sell out sometimes quickly, so I plan to try to make early reservations for work trips.

“Nice Hotel; Excellent Service” This hotel is what you would expect from Fairmont: above average rooms (they are showing a bit of age but very well maintained) and excellent service. A few pointers: 1. Internet is free if you sign up for their frequent guest program. This is a no brainer. It took me about 2 minutes and saved me about $15 per day. 2. The room service is very good but expensive. I didn't order that much and my bill was around $70 for dinner. Once again, the food was great but expensive. 3. The hotel is located in downtown San Jose so there is a lot within walking distance: a bakery/cafe next door, a starbucks, museums, and several places to eat. They have valet parking available but if you are at a conference here, there's really no need to rent a car.

“Very Nice Old School Hotel But With Reservations (Pardon the Pun)” I first stayed at this hotel in May of 2010 after hearing that this was the place that the late actor Freddie Prinze ( was a big fan of "Chico and the Man") spent his last day/nights here. Yes, for this was the place where Freddie Prinze committed suicide in January of 1977. Well, even weirder, upon checking into this establishment a second time recently in August of 2011, we got room #217 which is a huuuuuge (nearly 1500 sq. ft room) right next to the room #216 where Freddie spent his last days (or nights). I have to say that while this hotel which was a former apt. building back in the 1970s era, is kind of old school glamour and has very nice front desk staff, it may not be for every one. However, being that I am intrigued by true crime and the old Hollywood crowd, I just had to stay here yet another time. Our room was on the big suite side which features the one and two bedroom suites which range from 1200-2000 sq. ft. The smaller studio style rooms are on the other side of the hotel by the very beautiful hillside waterfall and koi fish pond. While we absolutely loved the room which also features a kitchenette and gorgeous living area, dining room and beautiful one-bedroom, we found the hotel to be rather noisy at night. Most of the rooms in the larger section (floors 1-3) face the pool and cabanas, we ran into a different if not unusual problem. Be it because our room was adjacent to the infamous Freddie Prinze room or whether other factors were at play, during our three night stay, every single night (like clockwork) at 2:33 AM, yes in the unGodly hours of the morning, our neighbors who were at the very end of the hallway, would let their children (under 10 years of age) run amok and scream at this hour. My friends and I very peacefully hung out in the lounge area of our deck in front of room #217 and the kids from these seemingly Middle Eastern (nothing against them) neighbors let their kids run shrieking past our windows. On three consecutive nights, I was awakened by them at that same time, and went down to the front desk to complain. I was amazed that 1). people would let their small children run around the hotel screaming at that hour and that 2). the parents didn't seem to care. The response from the front desk was "we'll take care of it" and though they were very diplomatic, despite my rather forceful language, they didn't seem to take active measures to stop the disturbance which other guests noticed and complained about audibly upon hearing these obnoxious and unruly kids. It is amazing to me that, in an establishment that is ostensibly an upscale one ( no, it's not the Hotel Bel-Air nor the Beverly Hills), the management cannot control the outlandish behavior of their guests. Overall, we LOVED the room and the staff was superficially nice, this party hotel seems to not want to get involved with quelling their unruly guests and from what we noticed, has had quite a few unfortunate happenings with various patrons that have come to stay there. I am not saying that this is not a good place, but something very odd is happening at this hotel and I say enter at your own risk if you are sensitive to noise. Granted, this may have been an isolated incident what with the people that caused my party this grief, but if you want a good value for the BH area and don't mind possible noise, I think that this is a good place for what it is and is very convenient if you want to explore the Beverly Hills area. STill, I AM PUZZLED AS to why the management allows loud parties and children to disturb the other neighbors at wee hours of the AM. Yeah, I'd probably go back, but I would bring the ear plugs and hope that I wouldn't be awakened by screaming kids at 2:33 AM, LOL.

“If you want this neighborhood try the W or the Marriott 2 blocks south on Lex” pretty shabby: -- peeling wallpaper everywhere, -- bathroom so small its hard to turn around in, and you have to get out of the way of the door to close it. -- water stains around window and soiled carpet -- no coffee in room or lobby -- billed for calls that we shouldn't have been billed for -- lobby small, unattractive, and annoying to maneuver through location might be good depending (its on the 6 subway and two short blocks from the E). internet was $15/ day

“Good location, typical Days Inn” We stayed 2 nights in this hotel as part of a wedding party. The location is great - close to zoo, beach, Sea World, and Old Town. This is a motel-style place, with doors that open to the parking lot, so we had a lot of road noise coming into our first-floor room. Cleaning service was a bit slow - they didn't clean our room until after 4:00 pm, but service was basically fine. The room is typical Days Inn - not fancy and kind of dark, but seemed clean and the price was good. If I stayed in this area again, I would price the Holiday Inn next door because it seemed newer and nicer. This is a decent place to stay but don't expect it to be anything but a typical Days Inn, even if it is their "hotel of the year".

“PLEASE READ !!!!! This review was WELL Earned” I have been an SPG member for 9 yrs and a Platinum member for over 7yrs (over 200 nites a year) so i would like to think i am qualified to give a precise and accurate review...why i didnt do this sooner is beyond me but here i am now :) Of all the SPG brands i prefer the W 1st and of all the W's "Worldwide" (yes i have been to most) .. i would rate the W in Westwood the best ... what they may lack in Luxery amenities (sorry no Phantom waiting or Butler at your beckon call) they more than make up for in EVERYTHING else...the rooms are all spacious and very comfy...bright colors..and most importantly everything works...and if it doesnt it will after one phone call....from their Welcome Ambassador that will greet you most times by name when you arrive to a very effecient check in and a world class "Whatever Whenever" (yes they really mean that) i guarantee that you will not find anything or anyone in the W Staff lacking...i am a bit partial because at one time i lived there when 1st moving to LA but even if i wasnt a Platinum SPG or a known regular the service would still be the same because everyone from the GM to the maids or wheel is there to help make your stay memorable...even if it is not their job that you are asking them to do... And "if" by chance you may have a complaint or be dissatisfied with any part of your visit, you will never have to go thru a myraid of buffers to get to someone that will actually care...just pick up the phone and even the GM would make himself personally available to address your concerns.... Now about the spa .. I am there with my Fiance about once a week and we would NEVER go anywhere else...service is outstanding and staff is impeccably trained...its a very cool place even just to hang out and eat the brownies :) The pool....hhhmmm ... all i can say is watch "Entourage"...yes it is the same pool and it is just that fun...people watching is the order of the day if you can find a cabana open or a lounger that doesnt already have someone beautiful already getting sun... The food is great with awesome variety...whether its on the Patio...the lobby restaurant or just plain old room service...you cant go wrong... well i think that this covers all i have been wanting to say for the past few years....one last note...I have lived about 10 miles from the W Westwood for a few years now, but i dont let that stop me from staying there 3-4 nites a month... thats how much like family they have become to me :) Ssssooo go, visit, endulge, enjoy....and i promise....you will return again :)

“Nice Hotel, Great Value, Good Location” This was my second stay at this particular HIlton GI, and I would say it is one of the nicest ones I have been in..... and I have been in a lot! Staff - Above and Beyond friendly, courteous, and helpful Room - Upgraded to a 2 room suite in second tower past pool. Room was nice and spacious. Small wetbar area. Couch and club chair. Nice king bed, very comfortable mattresses, nice linens, great pillows. Bathroom was nice, clean, well equipped and with above par soaps and shampoos. Pool Area - Very Nice in the center of the hotels towers, and looked to be clean and well maintained. A lot of people gathered there in the evenings. Restaurant - Nice, a little bit expensive, but not out of the ordinary for a hotel restaurant. Room service was offered. Parking - Yeah, as you have read by other reviews, its not the best. You basically park in a lot shared by a high rise office next to the hotel. plenty of spaces, so that is not an issue. It is not a long walk, but it is a walk, across a small access road in front of the office. BUT IT IS FREE, and for any hotel in any major downtown area, that is a rarity. I just paid 30.00 to park at the Hilton GI in New Orleans this week !! So its free, its ample, but its just a short walk away. Get over it. :-) Note - Lots of road construction going on in front of the hotel for the new trolley system phoenix is putting in, but it does not in any way effect the noise or the access to the hotel. just a small annoyance when driving to the hotel Will I stay here again. Absolutely! I believe I paid 90.00 or so, and it was well worth it.

“Great beds” This is an older Hilton and it shows in places but the beds are very comfortable and the rooms are quiet. Don't miss out on the restaurant. I was positively surprised about the food quality. Basically everything is good on the menu. The hotel has a free business center with computers and printers that actually work. On the downside my toilet seat fell off on the second day. The hotel bar has only 4 bar stools and the whole bar area is poorly designed. The free breakfast at the Executive Lounge was a joke. Any Hampton Inn offers a better variety. If you can get a good deal I would recommend this hotel for the excellent sleep comfort and the restaurant food.

“Fantastic” Stayed in May of 2010, the hotel was under going some restoration and at first I was worried due to it looking shabby, however I couldent be more wrong, it was excellent all the way. Great staff helped me with some tour bookings, very friendly and good value for money. Rooms were tidy and clean, the hotel is a brisk walk from nice locations and close to the BART. I'd stay again for sure!

“Fine Hotel” One of the nicest places I've ever stayed at (on the company tab, of course). The front desk was courteous and efficient. The room was spotless. And while this hotel must be about 35 years old it is very well kept. This was my first time in Denver, and personally, if I went back I would stay in a suburb, because downtown empties out quickly after work, and has an empty, eerie feel to it at night. But if you are staying downtown, this is the place.

“Large Conference Hotel” The Hilton is a very large conference hotel with a cavernous reception area. We spent a couple of nights there in March but not at a conference. It's a great hotel, breakfast in the Hilton's adjoining building was excellent and the staff are very friendly. The room had two double beds and was spacious with a very good bathroom. For a view we were overlooking Camden Yard but there was no game on, I can see these rooms being popular in season. Hotel is very clean all round and I couldn't fault anything. It is a good stretch of your legs to the Inner Harbour but that wasn't a problem and there are lots of restaurants there. A few bars nearby, not plush but a lot cheaper than the hotel's very nice cocktail bar. Highly recommend this hotel

“Older hotel, a little worn but classy” Room was plenty big except for the small bathroom. The lobby is ornate. What you'd expect from an older hotel that used to hold the academy awards. Ok option if you have to stay downtown.

“Nice budget hotel” Stayed for 2 nights during weekly business in NYC. Location is super although I had walked past the hotel many times during previous visits and never noticed it. Check-in was quick and very efficient in the intimate lobby. Only one elevator during my stay but it was fast plus the stairway is open and very convenient. I was given a room on the Fifth floor right next to the stairs so I was concerned about noise however I never heard a sound from the halls which was an extremely pleasant surprise. Room was a basic square with king bed and hardwood floors. Temperature was very good although the unit was loud. Bathroom located right next to the door --- small in size but everything was extremely clean and the walk-in shower was well designed so that surprising little water collected outside the opening. I also appreciated the drawer in the bathroom vanity -- excellent for stowing toiletries out of the way. Because I was a registered member of the Desire Hotels loyalty club, two cans of soda and two snacks were waiting for me along with a welcome note from the staff. Desk was next to the bed and was a good size. Lighting was either an overhead fixture or two bedside fixtures -- very good for reading in bed. I also really appreciated having the television station listing so easily available on the desk --- sometimes so hard to find the specific program you are looking for. Bed was loaded with pillows and a nice down comforter --- unfortunately there was a stain right at the top of the comforter -- looked like coffee but who knows. Also wireless was free and strong signal. Bed itself was very comfortable and would have thought a good night sleep was in order however the street noise was terrible even though the rooms overlook 27th and not Madison Ave. Sirens until very late at night and delivery trucks starting at about 5 in the morning. They also offer a complimentary grab-and-go continental breakfast in the lobby in the morning which was a nice perk however a little difficult to navigate all of the rolling luggage. My final impression is that this is a good budget choice --- room was clean and basic --- especially if you are a heavy sleeper. The location is great.

“No dinner room service” I have stayed at the Waldorf many, many times over the years for both business and pleasure. The hotel is centrally located in Midtown East, and is very convenient to my office. It’s also well located for walking to Broadway, Rockefeller Center and Fifth Avenue. One thing I kind of like about staying here is that I never know what kind of room I will get. They are all different but for the most part a good size for New York. I’ve had some really fabulous rooms and also some normal nice rooms. The hotel is old and most of the rooms could use some updating but still they are just fine. The bathrooms are hit and miss. Some of them are quite small but others have dressing areas and are larger. The bathrooms have been somewhat updated, not a total redo but updated. On my most recent trip last week I had a few glitches, which surprised me. The first glitch was that the smoke alarm did a beep beep every five minutes. I called to have it looked at and ultimately there was a problem that could not be fixed so I was moved to another room at 11 at night. Ok. They did move me, so that was good. The second glitch which took me by complete surprise is that during the month of January and February the hotel has decided, for economic reasons, not to offer room service for lunch or dinner. What?? This is not a small hotel. I am a female travelling for business and I don’t want to have to eat alone at a restaurant when I don’t have dinner plans. So, if this is important to you just know that you can only eat in your room for breakfast until March. Overall I like the Waldorf, and I will continue to stay there. It’s not hip and ultra-modern but then neither am I so it all works well.

“Learnt many lessons” After I landed at o'hare airport and started my search for the renaissance, my lessons started. Firstly i looked up the wrong section in tripadvisor for an airport hotel; on hindsight i should have searched in "rosemont, illinois", rather than "chicago, illinois" . After i walked past the hilton in the airport on my way to the blue line on the "L", my regret started. At the L station, the station workers told me to go to P1 instead where they have hotel buses pick us up. You may be wondering why i never called ahead to ask. Well, this is a strange hotel with no phone number on their website. And of course, they never replied my email. I should have seen the red flags. Unfortunately for me again, by the time i saw their number at the bus bay and called them, i just missed the hotel bus and had to wait for another 30mins in the cold. Go to door 2 by the way This "airport hotel" is a rather far 20min away from o'hare airport and the entrance is a very strange, small and non-descript door. Front desk was thankfully efficient, as it was already 1030pm and i didn't have dinner yet. The rooms are all indeed suites, with a seperate living area, but it's not 5 star or anything. The shower stall is large, but the 2 tvs smaller than Apple mac screens. The sink seems to leak, and there's no bathrobe. Room service was ok Will try the airport hilton next time

“Room with a view” Great lobby, modern and comfortable room with incredible views!! Room was a bit small with the TV on the side (always hate that) but all in all a great spot to crash. Not the greatest location but if you want a comfortable room this is it!!

“OMG....Can I just live here please!!” Spent .long weekend with spouse here over Memorial Day Holiday weekend. We had just a standard room on the 24th floor. The most comfortable bed I've ever slept in. I slept great here and I frequently do not sleep well. The staff was absolutely charming from the host that greeted us to the bar tenders. Perfect location for exploring Times Square and Central Park on foot. Room service was to die for....New York Strip and Grand Marnier & Chocolate dessrt. So much fun to have room service from a Michellin Star rated restaurant while sitting in the comfort of the bath robe. Drinks were delicious and bar snacks like cheese straws and spiced popcorn fabulous. Loved just wandering around the property and marveling at the historic architecture. The room that was formerly the library of the mansion and now is the bar for the upscale restuarnt is a study in contrasts between the gilded high arched ceiling tiles and renaisassance paintings (?) and the ultra modern bar. Go here for pampering, Go here for confort, go here for convenience, go here to have an amazing time time NYC. We'll be back soon. Great reccomendation on casual Italian restaurant within easy walk from Concierge, Luna Piena. Yummy. Can't wait to do it again.

“Average Airport Hotel” If you are staying at the Philadelphia Airport there are not a lot of good options. Marriott is the best of the bunch among very average choices and ofter prohibitively expensive. When that is the case I choose either Sheraton Suites or Aloft depending on price with Sheraton being my preferred choice. Sheraton suites is certainly showing its age these days and could use an update. It is in the same part as the aloft and 4 points and all hotels share the same shuttle service. The hotel is a standard American Airport Hotel and cannot be recommended as a must stay but cannot be faulted either as it gets the job done. I look forward to when the hotel is refurbished but at $120 AAA rate there are much worse options.

“Great Location” Traveled to NYC for a quick overnight before year end. Given that I was in the city the day before New Year's Eve, most hotel rates were extremely high. I found The Manhattan to be moderately priced and upon arriving amazed by the fantastic location. You are truly in the middle of it all between Central Park and Times Square. Great restaurants and of course theaters all within blocks of the hotel. It is no secret that this hotel is in need of a refresh as compared to other hotels it is dated, but kudos to housekeeping as the room was extremely clean and smelled fresh. My biggest surprises were the comfortable bed and the great bed linens. The pillows were amazing! so soft and thick they felt like clouds. A very large plasma screen and generous desk workspace. The Comfort Zone Italian-Made bathroom amenities were a definite treat! The room was extremely clean. All the employees were genuine and very welcoming. Guillermo at the front desk was a delight. The housekeeping personnel on my floor was very friendly and smiley.

“Outstanding!” My husband and I travel quite frequently, and I have to say that the Driskill is absolutely top of the line. There was not 1 bad thing we could say about the hotel or staff or food! Our room wasn't ready when we arrived, but the front desk called us when it was and they already had delivered our bags to the room, We were there about 30 minutes and a knock came on the door and it was room service delivering us a huge bowl of fresh delicious fruit. I don't know if this is the norm or if they were congratulating as we were celebrating our 35th wedding anniversary. But we really appreciated it. Too much for 2 people though:-))) Plush complimentary robes, plush towels, top of the line amenities......I could go on and on. And when we returned at night, the room was straightened up, the bed pulled back and a real yellow rose was on our pillows. We chose the Cityscape room type and the room was a little on the small side but it reminded us of European size rooms. And the hotel is older so we expected that. Should we have the opportunity to stay in Austin again, we wouldn't choose any other hotel except the Driskill. Thank to you everyone there for making it a special stay!

“Reasonable, comfortable and convienent” This downtown hotel is in close walking distance of the COBO Center and other downtown attractions. Friendly staff, comfortable rooms, good hot breakfast daily and a separate bar/restaurant next door, (Big City Grille) Too many smokers allowed at the entrance of the hotel makes a bad impression. Television stations did not match the in-room guide so you surf the channels forever to find your desired show. Overall, a worthwhile hotel when staying in downtown Detroit.

“Grand Old Lady!” What a gorgeous hotel. All staff we interacted with were so friendly. We had an issue with a/c and everyone from engineer to manager were professional and apologetic. They didn't just move us to a new room, they escorted us to ensure the room offered was suitable. Can walk from here to everywhere in downtown Chicago. Convenient to L Train stop if you want a cheap ride in from the airport.

“Trendy Hotel in an excellent location” This hotel is really nicely located in Seattle. You can walk to all shopping areas and to the Piers from here. Ask for the superior rooms. They are very nice and nice view. Don't go there if you want to relax or if you are looking for a quiet spot. It is a very busy area and the hotel itself attracts a lot of people and very active bar scene.

“Terrible Hotel” Ok, here is the usual preamble; I am a frequent traveller, with more than 120 nights a year in hotels across the globe, usually on the corporate credit card and usually at top tier hotels such as the Peninsula in Hong Kong, the Four Seasons in New York or the George Vth in Paris. But I have also stayed in my fair share of Express Holiday Inns and Comfort Inns, so I have a very acute sense of what makes a good hotel. I normally stay in NYC every other month in the Four Seasons or my favourite, the Ritz Carlton at Central Park, but both were full, so I headed to the Barclay, thinking my Ambassador Priority Club membership would land me a nice upgrade and the reviews on here were okish. I have stayed over the years in more than 20 Manhattan hotels from the trendy Soho Grand to the spectacular (on your wallet as well) Mandarin Oriental, so I thought I would give the Barclay a try. The car pulled up and the two bell boys watched me struggle with my bag up the steps. Checking in at the front desk was nice and efficient and the lobby area is typical large New York hotel. Not the intimacy of the Four Seasons or RC, but smart and elegant nevertheless. I was upgraded to an executive room. Not quite sure the difference with a regular deluxe room. For a New York it was quite large, with two windows. The bathroom was tiny and the whole place looked a little tired. There were marks on the carpet and the bathroom was tatty, cracks in the basin and bath. The wallpaper was a bit ragged in places too, but the bed and the linen were fine. I logged in the internet on the fixed LAN which was so temperamental (I travel with two laptops so know its not me) I tried a local wireless I could pick up-but that was so slow I gave up. The front desk kept telling me that nothing was wrong with the system, despite the same problem reported from a number of other guests. Then the guest in the room next door room returned. I had an interconnecting room and I can only conclude that they insulate the rooms with paper, as I could hear everything from the next door room. And I mean everything! Including a detailed financial discussion with his bank. I put in the IPOD and tried to ignore him, and once in bed, managed to get off to sleep-despite the terrible noise from the road (which seems to be a particular problem in this hotel). I was then awoken with his coughing at 3am, and gave up sleep. The next day, on my return from work, weary and tired, the room had been cleaned but utterly stank of sewage! I had to open the windows for two hours, and when I couldn’t log on, simply had enough and called the front desk. My annoyance was only compounded by the new guest in the room next door, and after hearing about her wedding plans (seems like its going to be a nice do) through the wall. I demanded to move rooms. This was met with a grunt from ‘guest services’. Eventually, after four calls, I tracked down the Manager, who moved me to the other side of the hotel. This regular room was ok, but again the street noise was deafening, the décor getting grubby and the internet occasional art best. Had no apologies from the manager and I skipped out as fast as I could the next day. This is NOT a five star hotel. It is hardly a bad four star. The service is terrible, the technology broken, the rooms shabby, the bathrooms small, the insulation paper and the service non existent!

“Excellent, plus cheap airport parking” Booked on Priceline, got an "upgrade" to the tower with my Hilton Honours membership. Desk agent provided cookies and directions to the closest parking spot to the elevators for our room. The car stayed there for a few nights while we were away and picking it up was really easy with the fast pay machine. The shuttle was fast and the drivers nice. Everything was great here and 1000times better than the Hilton down the road that we stayed at the other day.

“A Unique, Fun, and Classy Hotel with Great Service” My daughter and I spent the weekend in Chicago and thoroughly enjoyed the Blackstone. It is both funky and beautiful all at the same time. We also appreciate the all of the history that has happened here. The check-in was efficient and pleasant, with excellent service throughout our stay. The doormen always greeted us as we had lived there forever. We enjoyed being walking distance to Millennium Park and the Art Institute of Chicago (and it was free on Thursday evenings--helpful hint to fellow tourists). We also highly recommend The Gage for dinner, across from Milennium Park after you check out the art. Also, grab some breakfast at Yolk, a few blocks south on Michigan. It was delicious and very reasonable. Back at the Blackstone, the beds were excellent and I was very pleased to have Aveda amenities. I would most definitely stay at the Blackstone again.

“Superb location; but tired rooms” Stayed here for a week for work. Superb location, right in the middle of Manhattan just off 5th avenue of just south of Central Park. Very elegant, grand old style hotel with some lovely period features. Check-in quick and painless - apart from the constant handing out of $1 bills to various people who 'help' with your bags! Was in a standard room; asked for an upgrade and offerred to pay but the hotel was full. Room itself clean, but nothing special. Bed comfy but not on the large side. Bathroom fine, but lacking in amenities. Towels fairly miserable (though i left a small tip for the chambermaid the next day, and there was a marked improvement!), but again nothing too bad. Dreadful aspect though, looking into a dark courtyard so even during the day there was almost zero natural light. The room seemed to be in a 'new' wing. See below about the 'old' wing. Had dinner one night in the bar off the lobby, Fives. Very ordinary. I was jetlagged and in a weak moment ordered a pizza. Dreadful, especially for $20. The menu itself was poor, and the ambience of the place awful, like a business lounge in an airport. Staff were great though. Granted, it is all about the roof bar, but that isn't great either. Its FULL of tourists, the drinks are outrageous (4 beers, 1 soda, $95 with tip) and the view isn't that good. Overrated, with a lot more cooler, hipper and cheaper places to go. Again staff were fine, but they are working for tips so you come to expect this. I didn't go to the Gotham Lounge, which is oft touted in their website. Its tiny, and more of an after thought. Certainly not somewhere you'd be settling in for a few pints. Had a night in Boston mid-week, and when i came back i complained again about the standard room courtyard facing, but this time right by a/c units. They moved me to another room in the 'old' part of the hotel which was much nicer. View onto the church across the street; massive bathroom, nice lobby, proper bed, high ceilings. Might be worth the extra few dollars when booking. So overall, its a good hotel in a great location. If you can get a deal it certainly is worth it. But you don't need to eat or drink there really, with so many other places to go and explore in this fine city.

“Simple, friendly, pleasant Hotel with terrific diner” We were very happy with our stay at the Seven Seas. Rooms were pleasant, clean and well maintained. The staff were very helpful arranging our hotel pick ups and transfers. The diner was terrific! Loved the pizza! We were repeat customers there. The big breakfast was delicious!! Great service and great food.

“Outstanding” The location is good...I wouldn't spend the extra money to have a riverwalk view though. The room was clean and spacious. The managers special in the evening was great! they had lot's of snack food...chips, dips and free drinks for 2 hours. The morning breakfast was incredible. Made to order omelets...pancakes ... TONS of food! My only dislike was the parking. They charge $28 per day to park there. There is a parking lot across the street but it's the same price.

“Brilliant!” Stayed here August 24th for 1 night - we met up with friends and spent a nice evening in the bar/restaurant and had a lovely meal there. Had breakfast in the morning which was expensive but was nice. Staff were friendly and helpful - even giving out 13 year old son a gift of a terminater toy - which being autistic he loved (we noted the little girls were given My Little Ponys) - this was a very nice touch. The room was clean and large. The location was perfect for the Airport - we just had a 10 minute walk from the terminal - which we took our trolley straight to our room!!!! We never even heard the Planes even though we watched them go off from our room!

“Still a Treat for the Eyes” No matter how often you see it, the moment you enter the lobby/atrium of the San Francisco Hyatt Regency, the 150 foot high expanse is always a stunning visual experience. Everything in the hotel, takes a back seat to the soaring vistas of the lobby. Located on the Embarcadero, at Market Street, this hotel is ground zero for access to everything from the SF Cable cars to Fisherman's Wharf. The location could not be better. Service was excellent and unobtrusive. Rooms were modern, clean and comfortable... and, as a plus, many offered striking views of San Francisco Bay. Our only complaint - the price. For a soon-to-be middle-aged grande dame, the Hyatt Regency still demands a high financial commitment from her guests. Even so, for the business traveler or the vacationer, this hotel remains one of the truly memorable San Francisco experiences.

“tres bon hotel que ce soit pour affaire ou pour le tourisme” tres bien placé a deux pas du centre de dallas belles prestations dans cet hotel moderne et tout neuf des restaurants agréables avec une cuisine correcte un tres bon rapport qualité prix , petits dejeuner copieux belles chambres , bien equipées le service reste correct , rien d extraordinaire , mais ce qu il faut le service du laudry n est pas vraiment performant , ilfaut sans cesse reclamer la livraison nd ece que vous avez donne a laver c est parmi tous les hotels grand ensemble du coin certainement un des meilleurs

“Meets expectations” I stayed at the Sofitel in downtown philly for 3 nights on business. The staff is very friendly and accomodating from bellman to concierge. The room was a regular size King room and bed was very comfortable with fluffy comforter and pillows. The room has complimentary Keurig type coffee and security safe. I did not dine at hotel restaurant because there are so many great restaurants within a few blocks walking distance. There is only valet parking and its very expensive at about $40 per night and there's no guarantee your car will be parked indoor or outdoor. I parked at a nearby indoor garage for a little less and parked my own car knowing it was indoor and free of dents.

“GOOD VALUE HOTEL” Took ipod room it is small (NY size) but well appointed very modern and place to put clothes even drawer under the bed, bathroom is good size quiet large for size of room was surprised. (no lotion...but bathrobe no slippers) For the price 150$ you cannot get better The location is great for visiting Turn down service very appreciated and morning newspaper The ventilation when is on is making noise like in most hotels of that category as well you hear the next room open and close door because doors are making terrible noise Bed confortable Staff efficient Internet 10$ per day should be free especially when I stayed was not working in the afternoon Will go back if rate max 200$

“Great hotel, great service” Stayed here for the second time this past weekend and it was even better than the first. Stayed in a harbor view room. We were celebrating my niece's 16th birthday. The woman who greeted us, Mitch, was amazing. When she found out that it was her birthday, she arranged for a lovely dessert sampler for our room when we returned from dinner, and left lovely, personal notes for both of my nieces. The room was wonderful -- some of the largest in NYC and as usual the beds are more comfortable than ever. We did treat ourselves to the breakfast buffet which, while not inexpensive ($35) was excellent with a great variety. Freshest and tastiest berries I've had in a while! The location is a bit out of the way, but other than more expensive cab rides this is more of an advantage than a disadvantage. It is such a relief in the middle of the tourist season to have such an oasis.

“The Westin in downtown Seattle is a...” The Westin in downtown Seattle is a perfect location for any kind of visit. It's steps from Pike Place and a 2.50 ride on the rail from the airport. Shopping is all around you- from a mall to downtown to Pike's. It's comfy, loved the fitness center! It has a great view and a Starbucks is across the street. Okay, it's Seattle- there are StarBucks everywhere! The very first one is a few blocks away. Shop ahead for a deal. Advance rates were the best.

“Great Room in Downtown Austin!” I stayed here for business was thoroughly impressed with the room. I was put up on the top floor and had a magnificent room with an extremely comfortable bed. The room was spacious with plenty of seating and closet/drawer space. I only stayed for two nights, but this would have been an awesome plus for me if I were there longer. The drawbacks of the room were the TV and the step into the restroom. The TV was extremely small, old, and was barely watchable with static and snow on the screen - no matter what channel I went to. The bathroom had a small step or threshold to go from the bed area to the bathroom. While this wouldn't normally be an issue with the lights on - it was an issue in the middle of the night when I stubbed my toe a couple of times! Other than the two above issues with the room, I was very pleased. I will make sure to make this my regular Austin hotel!

“Would not stay here again” Stayed 1 night in Nov 04. The place was undergoing some repairs and it looked like it needed some. The room was very basic and did not look well maintained. Parking is free and there is the basic free breakfast. Noise from the street very noticeable in the room. If you are a light sleeper, bring ear plugs. Not much you can do about the vibrations, especially from the cable cars. We decided to look at other hotels in the nearby area and found a better room at the Best Western Flamingo 2 blocks away for a lower price.

“Nice hotel, great location!” If you are going to a concert or game at either coliseum or stadium, this is a perfect location. And they've got a Champions for decent bar food/drinks and some other upscale dining choice I didn't check out. Across the way is a Hooter's and there are plenty of bars around. I'd definitely stay there again for an event!

“Another Great Kimpton” I stayed here with colleagues including some customers and everyone had a great stay. My room had a comfortable bed and was very clean, the two most important things in a room! Beyond that I wasn't in the room enough for room service or lounging. I loved the breakfast here and we got vouchers for free cocktails. nice touch. Very fast check-in and it was hassel free. Valet parking was expensive but quick. I like staying in different parts of the city on each visit but if I'm back in this area I would definitely stay again.

“I'm sorry to say that it was pretty terrible” I am sorry to say that this was a pretty terrible experience. First, please know that the resort is stunning and the staff couldn't have been nicer. But, my room was so overwhelmingly bad that I cannot recommend this hotel to the average business traveler. I do not know what type of room you get when you pay full rack rate but the room that I got under my corporate rate was pretty bad. The area behind the sink was torn out due to construction, the air conditioning kind of worked and the room smelled pretty bad. Why the hotel put me in a room that was under construction is just a mystery. The construction work continued in my room (without my knowledge) while I was in meetings. I learned about this around 9:00 pm on the second night of my stay when the housekeeping staff called to tell me that they needed to bring me towels. Apparently, I had no towels because they needed to remove my towels when doing the repairs. It is unnerving to learn that people have been in your hotel room when you are not there. This is not a small resort. I am sure there were other rooms avaiable (that were not under repair) during my stay But, I am equally sure that the hotel was happy to leave me where I was since I did not complain or make an issue about the construction. Shame on the Waldorf. You do not treat customers who complain with respect. You treat everyone with respect. When I submitted my on-line evaluation form to the hotel, the general manager called and offered me a free weekend certificate to "make up" for my experience. I turned him down. Why would I return for free? If a hotel does treat me with respect when I am paying...why would it treat me with repect when it is footing the bill? I'll pass.

“Simply the Best!” What an awesome hotel! What an awesome location! What aweome staff! I can't say enough good things about this hotel! The rooms are great - especially if you can get one with a nice view! The location is perfect - close to everything DC - the white house, monuments, museums! Great restaurants in the hotel, and in the surrounding area. Rooms are great - well appointed and up to date. The staff is very attentive and welcoming.

“A good altenative if the price is right” We needed to go to NYC for what we now realize is major tourist season. We tried all means possible to get a nice hotel for under $500-600/night for a weekend in between Thanksgiving and Xmas to no avail. We decided to blow our entire hotel point account on 2 nights at a different hotel which was not ideal but it got us there. I continued to search however, for some break though or last minute deal. Hotwire was listing a 4 star hotel in Soho for $249. Bingo! I examined the description (which mentioned a pool) and searched to find that the only 4* hotel in Soho with a pool was the uber-hip Gansevoort. I jumped at the chance and booked it, only find, out after committing, that the reservation was for the Millennium Hilton. We were quite disappointed (I'd even say a bit mad) since although this hotel is South of Houston....it is no way Soho.We have had many opportunities to stay here in the past but declined. But....we sucked it up and checked in and wrote it off to "it's only a place to sleep and shower". I have to say that we were pleasantly surprised. The proximity to the subway and path trains made it an incredibly convenient location. Since we are Gold members, we were upgraded to a room with a fantastic view of all downtown and the river. Sunset was spectacular. It was fascinating to watch the activity going on in the rebuilding of the WTC across the street. We checked in to a decent sized, modern and clean room with nothing really to complain about. The staff was helpful and friendly. While we did just sleep and shower here on our busy weekend, I would consider staying here again if the price was prohibitive at some of our more favorite locations.

“Classic charm” Having spent the previous night in the W across the street, this hotel was a complete opposite in terms of it's furnishings. The candid photos (by others) do a great job in displaying the traditional classic floral decoration of the rooms, with comfy sofas in lieu of trendy cushion seats. All the usual amenities that you would expect from this class of hotel, but in a more sumptous format: high count cotton bed sheets, robes and slippers in the bathroom, quality toiletries, expensive mini-bar, safe, non-plasma TV, CD player etc. The shower was over the bath (prefer a separate unit) and the bathroom itself a little small, but the large bedroom (had upgraded to an executive room) made up for this. Nice touches like an umbrella in the wardrobe and friendly staff, made the place feel homely. The hotel is looking very slightly tired in some areas, but these large vast traditional places must take some upkeep. Views from the rooms are poor, as the hotel is surrounded by other large buildings on all sides. In summary, if you want trendy and modern go to the W, but if its classic sumptous comfort you desire, this is the place. Oh and try to get a high floor, away from the city noise below.

“Good except out of the way” The hotel itself is new and therefore clean and well-maintained. Courtyard is a budget line of Marriott properties. Nice desk, bed, TV, A/C, bathroom, etc. The hotel is about a 10-minute walk from the "Andrew" T-stop. Once there, downtown is quick. The restaurant situation near the hotel is inadequate. Room service from a nearby restaurant ends at 10:00 pm. We got to the hotel at 9:45 pm. (The food itself was way overpriced relative to quality.)

“Housekeeping dropped the ball...” I booked this hotel because of a perfect location for my three day seminar at PHL. It had best ratings of all in vicinity and I believe at the end I made no mistake. I did like it's modern twist, I liked design of the room and public spaces. It is an airport hotel with all the drawbacks an airport hotel comes with and when compared with other airport hotels this one is actually pretty good.
