Hotel shuttle runs between PHL and three Starwood hotels every twenty minutes or so, no problem there. Aloft was a first stop. Checkin was quick, a girl working there is professional and does what she suppose to do well. Housekeeping is another story. I found the room being not well cleaned. Found some takeout leftovers in the fridge, left probably from previous guest. Small smudges on the walls, little spiders on the ceiling. Nothing criminal but definitely not spotless. Called front office and they sent someone to take care of problems. One day I was out all day but no one came to make up/clean the room. The bed was good and I had no issues with my sleep those three nights I was there. I read complaints about noise from the bar but actually my stay was very quiet, I had no issue with the noise at all (my room was on the 3rd floor). All in all, efficient hotel, chosen for location and if I ever need to sleep near PHL airport, I'll probably book Aloft again. But they have to train their housekeeping staff better, their part was definitely below par for such a hotel.

“Quiet, Spotless, Luxurious, and convenient.” You could not find a better deal than the Bay Club Hotel & Marina. I am writing this review after my first nights stay (of two nights) and so far it's been absolutely perfect. The rate was low and our room has not one but two large hd televisions (accompanied by many hd channels.) Furthermore, the nights were absolutely silent as the location is a few blocks removed from the main drags nearby - not so far removed that one can't take a 3 minute drive to food and supplies, however. The rooms also have mini-fridges which were quite helpful for storing some of our food and drinks we brought with us. Heating, air conditioning, you name it - these rooms have it pretty much. So overall, I would certainly recommend this to any traveler looking for a great value in their hotel choice.

“Good hotel for a good price.” I stayed at the Salisbury for 3 nights with a family member at the end of September/beginning of October and found it to be an all round positive experience. We had requested a room on a high floor non-street side and this was accommodated with no problems (we were on the 15th floor). The staff at the front desk were very cheery as were the bellhops and we instantly felt welcomed. We had just arrived into our room when our cases very promptly arrived too. The guy who showed us around our room and showed us how things worked was really polite and helpful and gave a good impression of the friendly service by the staff at the hotel. The room itself was large, particularly by New York standards, and clean. It had everything that was necessary for a weekend stay at a comfortable hotel- decent air conditioning system (albeit a little bit noisy), ironing board and iron, safe (although it was one which locked with a key, not an electronic lock), cable TV etc. The only thing I would have liked to be in the room aswell was a coffee maker but this was only a minor quibble and for the rating of the hotel, I think the facilities in the room were very good. The bathroom, although could do with an update, was clean and tidy with nice toiletries. The closet space was immense, which was particularly helpful for 2 women on a shopping spree! It was easily the most closet space I've ever had in a room (ranging from 2* - 5* hotels). The beds, although a little firm for me personally, were also very comfortable. It was without question, the quietest New York room I have ever stayed in. I can be a bit of a light sleeper but I always accept that when staying in New York, there will always be some noise. But in the Salisbury, it was really quiet. We may have been fortunate but I heard no noise from any of the other rooms the whole time we were there and as for street noise, it was pretty much non existant. At times, it was almost easy to forget that we were even in New York! The day before we left, I asked the front desk if there was anywhere I could get internet access as I needed to check in online for our flight home. They didn't think twice in going onto the particular website for me and checking us in on their front desk computers, even printing out our boarding passes. Of course there was no charge for this which I was pleased about- much better than some of the money grabbing chains who charge an exhorbitant amount for just a few minutes online. The staff at the front desk really couldn't do enough for me, which again showed that the service was excellent. We didn't eat breakfast in the hotel (we headed to a cafe a couple of doors down which cooked hot breakfasts) but we did order take outs for dinner whilst in our room. The Salisbury doesn't actually have room service but instead, a file with about 6 or 7 different local restaurant menus where you can order take out and have it delivered to your room. We tried this (after a couple of long days sightseeing and shopping when we had no energy left to eat out!) and ordered from the Italian and the Chinese. I have to give them both a huge thumbs up as they both arrived within 20 minutes or so of me placing the order, steaming hot (indeed hotter than most if not all room service meals I've ever had), very plentiful, tasty, and good value for money. In fact, it made me almost prefer that method than having room service in the hotel. The location of The Salisbury is absolutely outstanding. Almost exactly opposite Carnegie Hall and Russian Tea Rooms, round the corner from Columbus Circle and Central Park, 5 minutes at most to 5th Avenue, 5 minutes to Rockefeller Center and 10 minutes to Times Square as well as a Subway station literally a stone's throw away. For people on a sightseeing and shopping trip, it really doesn't get much better than that. All in all, although I tend to stay at 4* - 5* hotels more commonly these days, I'd say that the Salisbury is a very good, solid, all round choice. There was very little to complain about and the combination of comfort, location and price makes it a real winner.

“The typical Kimpton Experience - My "default" hotel in Boston” Whenever I can, I stay here. Consistent experience, friendly service, and great location. Rooms are comfortable, clean, the amenities are from ETRO. Out of a dozens hotel is Boston I stayed at still the one I return whenever I can.

“super clean, great comps, but small rooms” I stayed at the Magnolia Hotel during a recent 3 day business trip to Denver. It was conveniently located within walking distance of the convention center and the 16th street mall. The hotel is in an old building that has been tastefully restored. A very good hot breakfast, cookies & milk, and cocktail hour are included with the room price. The staff was always courteous about shuttling me to my destinations. As a frequent traveler, I have to say that this was probably the cleanest hotel I've ever stayed in. Now, the down side... my room was super small... with approximately 3 feet to spare, on each side of the queen bed. The decor was really dated... heavy brownish-maroonish crushed velvet draperies covering the large old windows, a dark brown carpet, and an orange, brown and white 70's print bedspread. I commented on the smallness of the room, when checking out, and was told that it was their smallest. Although I enjoyed the comps and the staff, I would not stay there again, because of the room being way too small and very claustrophobic.

“Fabulous stay at The New Yorker Hotel” Stayed in the hotel in Sept 09. Rooms were absolutely great and LARGE by NYC standards. Loved the art deco feel of the hotel, and the new renovations and refurbishment keeps the theme. The hallways and rooms were spotlessly clean. Staff were very friendly and helpful. The elevators were great - no wait time at all! That can sometimes be a real problem in other hotels we've stayed in in NYC. Beds were very comfortable and linens were new and fresh. Bathroom had a hairdryer. Closet size was small but certainly adequate for two people's week's worth of clothes. My advice is don't overpack - amazed at the size of suitcases some people drag along with them! There are stores within two minutes' walking distance where you can buy anything you may need - be it toiletries or clothing. (Example, if you just want some cheap threads, right around the corner is a Conway store where you can get an entire outfit for about $10.) The location of hotel is very convenient to two subway lines as well as the train and bus station. Quite a few restaurants in the area, including fast food if you want a quick bite. If your stomach can handle it, suggest you go two blocks down to the Gray's Papaya for "The Recession Special" - two hot dogs and a drink for $4! The business center in the hotel has a few computers and one or two printers. Workout room was nothing spectacular but who needs it after walking around all day. Would highly recommend a stay at The New Yorker and hope to be a guest there again myself someday.

“Great place if you wear Ed Hardy T-shirts and party all night” I had the opportunity to stay at the Hard Rock Hotel San Diego for a conference and overall had a good experience. Staff: Very friendly and professional staff. They are consistently trained to provide a high level of service, although you do notice that many of them, if they are not providing service, have their heads down looking at their phones as they furiously text message their friends. If they looked up more, they might see more service opportunities. However, still, very good service. Facilities: The design is very interesting and engaging. Great use of videos, lighting and neat furniture. Of course, the memorabilia everywhere is great and you’d often see people stopping to look at displays on the wall. The bed was comfortable and I loved the shower! Only issue with the bed is that they are on platforms that stick out, and although the corners of the platforms are padded, I bumped into or tripped over the corners all the time. The pool area and party deck on the 4th floor are really neat. The gym is a decent size. I didn’t use the spa but it looked nice. Highlights: The location of this place is great. Right across from the convention center, a 10-15 minute stroll down the marina promenade to Seaport Village, a block from Petco Park and right at the entrance to the Gaslamp Quarter. Derrick, the guy who checked me in, was terrific and the housekeeping staff did a good job of cleaning up after me and the party animals who ran amok. Areas for improvement: The signage in the hallways is very hard to read. The lighting is dim and the signs are very small in dark metal tones set against brown walls. My eyesight is pretty good, but I still had to get up close to read which way to the gym or verify the room number. I also had two different young people ask me which way to go in the hallway because they couldn’t see the signs. More direction at the front desk would be helpful when there is a crowd because it’s not always clear which of the little pods that serve as the front desk is open. The biggest concern I had was the noise level late at night. After the bars closed on two nights, it sounded like the party moved into the hallway right outside my room. That was confirmed the next morning when I saw a lot of feathers and other detritus outside in the hallway. There’s not much you can do when 10-15 drunken youngsters are yelling, singing, smoking and carousing in the hallway. It didn’t last long so they would have been gone by the time security came up to investigate but there were numerous groups of them coming in over the course of a few hours and the combined effect added up to about 2 hours of lost sleep. Overall impression: The Hard Rock has a great setup and a true focus on the customer experience. The facilities are nice and the staff is very professional. If you like a place that is very much a “scene”, you will not be disappointed. If you’re staying here on the weekend and you go to sleep before 3:00 am, you may think you’re in the wrong place. I’m in my early 40’s, and looking at the people who were walking around the hotel in bikinis and swim trunks who were young enough to be my children, I just don’t think I’m the target demographic. I like to sleep at night and this isn't the place to do that. Nearby transportation: There is a trolley stop right outside the hotel that can connect you with downtown, old town or even Tijuana! Additionally, the city bus (#992) stops at 4th Avenue and Broadway, just a 10 minute walk from the hotel. That ride takes less than 20 minutes and is only $2.25. There is also a luggage rack on the bus. If you’re carrying on, it’s an easy way to go!

“Affordable choice in Center City / City Hall area” Stayed here for two nights after obtaining a good rate online. The hotel is in a good location, with clean rooms and free WiFi - pretty standard Courtyard decor. Walking distance to most attractions, restaurants, transportation options and the "Gay Village." Only downside is the expensive valet parking although it does provide unlimited in and out privileges. (Parking is notoriously hard in Philly) If parking expense is a concern there are cheaper lot options about 4-5 blocks south.

“Essentially a Nightclub with Rooms to Rent” The ZaZa has a lot to recommend it. However, the ineptitude of the staff and the tendency to be overwhelmed by the parties they allow to take over the entire first floor make this a hard hotel to recommend. The staff is mostly cheerful, and ready to help, but you'll find they have to do a lot to correct housekeeping and other service errors that shouldn't occur in the first place. Our first night, we had to have the sheets replaced, because the existing ones were damp. Second night, the entire first floor was full of a party with extremely loud music. OK, but it was a private party that completely precluded us from having dinner or even a drink with friends (and, we had to stand in line even to enter the lobby to get to the elevators). That night, the airconditioning was non functional. The staff cheerfully fixed it. The bedside lamps were similarly non functional. That couldn't be fixed. The wired internet was non functional and couldn't be fixed. The wireless was adequate. The room service hamburger was quite good, timely delivered and reasonably priced. In general, the rooms are an odd combination of luxe and cheap. Perhaps just what happens when you retrofit an old building. Some rooms are decorated in a very fun, if ridiculous manner. Some are very large, multi room affairs. But, If you are expecting to be able to shave or put on makeup in the bathroom, or read a book or do some work, you'll find the lightling quite inadequate. I've seen six rooms. None of them has an adequate work space for a business traveler. The windows are not double glazed, so even on the 11th floor you will hear a lot of traffic and other street noise. I would beware of the valet parking. They lost our car the first day, and when it was finally located, I noted that someone had driven 25 miles since I handed it over (I have a habit of noting milage when I give the car to a valet). The next day, the car hadn't had any adventures over night, but, someone had cleaned our my change drawer and explored the storage spaces rather roughly. Despite promises to make it right, we've never recieved the promised claim form, and the hotel carefully explains that they have no responsibility for the valet service, which has been outsourced to another firm. Overall, the ZaZa has potential. Good location, fun atmosphere and nice rooms. But I don't think being a hotel is first on their business plan. Even the front desk folks show a notable lack of enthusiasm for guests, while going out of their way to greet folks entering to attend functions. I think they just want to run a nightclub, and provide rooms for revelers who decide to stay over.

“Great Hotel for the Bachelorette Party!” I stayed at Hotel Vitale for a bachelorette weekend and it was wonderful. The service, decor and beds were awesome. The staff was at our beckon call and we loved sleeping in the beds!! The hotel was kind enough to give us a bottle of champagne and a tray of gourmet cupcakes for the group which was super sweet. We loved the rooftop terrace (what a view!) and overall the hotel was great. Overnight parking was $$ at $40/night but that was my only complaint....we went to the bar in the hotel and had a lot of fun there as well. Next time I go to this hotel, I am going to do a more romantic trip as the hotel is good for both scenarios...great stay overall. Thanks Hotel Vitale! (more specifically Nicole Muller)

“Very nice, very large suites, good value” This is a very nice hotel about 15 minutes from downtown, but easily accessible from Billy Graham Pkwy. Has a beautiful lobby and the rooms are exceedingly large, with a separate living area and sleeping area (door between), and nice large tiled bathroom. The living rooms have a window looking out onto a nice cathedral lobby , and contains a small refrigerator and bar area. There is a desk in both the living room and bedroom and TVs in both as well. The bathrooms are stocked with Aveda products . Place looks new and was spotless. They have a nice bar downstairs and a dining area with better- than-average food. Only downside was internet not free ($12 per 24 hour period) but considering the quality of the place this was minor. Been here only first of four nights, but would definitely come back. The living room in this hotel is larger than the whole room at the Sheraton Four Points@Woodlawn.

“its a best western and maintains the standards you expect from the brand” Stayed for 4 nights in december 2010-took a bit of time to find hotel-still getting used to the road system in Texas-but once found easy to find after. Location is fine and its easy to get around to all areas 635 goes to 35 and around Dallas/Fort Worth and 75 goes up through Plano etc. Hotel staff we met were polite and helfull the rooms were cleaned adequatly and the breakfast we did try once was fine-perhaps a menu card on the table would explain that you can order bacon/sausage etc to go with breakfast. Not over keen on buffet style so we did our usual trip to the nearby diners the other 3 days. Computer/buisness area were good and always available. In all a good experience-our thanks

“Historic hotel with a modern twist fantastic” Our fist visit to Chicago and what a great choice of hotel we made. The hotel is full of history which is evident from the photographs of some of the greats that have stayed there over the years however it doesn't live off past reputation and has a modern twist having undergone a refurb, a real class act. The rooms have everything you would want including a really comfortable bed and powerful shower. It is spotlessly clean and the staff are friendly and helpful. One of the best hotels we have stayed in anywhere in the world and we will most certainly be returning.

“Very well located, rooms over looking Chicago River are best. Will become my hotel of choice in Chicago” Great property well located. Rooms over looking Chicago River are best. Will become my hotel of choice in Chicago

“Loved how we were treated while we were here” The whole family of 15 stayed at this hotel the night before the UCLA graduation. Conviently located, short walk to an awesome mall. The property was sold out the night we arrived so they upgraded our reservation to a penthouse suite. Even though we didn't even stay 12 hours in it, it was AWESOME!!! Loved the upgraded ammenities! I wish we could have stayed and enjoyed the pool/cabanas. They looked great. Valet was fast and being a hyatt gold member got us complementary starbucks! Great time at the Hyatt!

“Run down” The hotel is an old, and I mean old, W hotel. The lobby is nice as are the elevators. Thats about it. Once you get onto the floor your staying, you'll notice how dark the hallway is. The hallway is narrow, beat up, and in need of new carpet. Once we got into our room, we did find a thing of luxury. The carpet was coming up everywhere and separating. The furniture was beat up and old. There was no coffee maker. The bathroom looked like an upgraded subway bathroom. I was not impressed at all. While the room was big, it was in desperate need of renovation. The front desk was helpful and the service was good. The location was excellent. I would come back once the hotel goes through a renovation.

“Feels brand new” New renovation style feels sleek, efficient and smart (but not warm and inviting). Rooms and bathrooms are good sized, and the lobby area is also very large. The elevators have difficulty keeping up with high occupancy. Indoor pool area is small and very pleasant. Since this hotel is so far from downtown Austin (25 minutes when IH-35 traffic is flowing), outdoor parking is free and plentiful. We stayed 3 nights, and all staff members were super friendly and helpful. Austin is a good city to try a Segway tour that includes a ride along Ladybird Lake. Also, check out the music scene at Flipnotics Coffee House.

“OK hotel, terrible location” First, let me say that the staff members at this hotel were very good. Some of the best I've run into lately. But the hotel has several severe drawbacks. To start off, it's in a very ugly area, nearly tucked under some highway ramps. I booked it thinking I could reach the mall without a car. Good luck on that! This is an area solely designed for those with autos and to walk is taking your life in your hands. Second, I was to meet a business colleague there and soon discovered that if you ARE driving, it is very hard to reach. He drove past it several times. Finally, the room was OK, not exceptional and this hotel shines huge lights on the hotel at night (perhaps so it can be seen from the highway) and curtains can't keep the glare out. I've always wondered what idiot decides to build a hotel so travelers can rest and then decide to bath it in blinding light all night? Would I stay here again? NO.

“Ideal location for everything Phoenix” If you want to do anything in Phoenix this is a great hotel to stay at. The property is two blocks away from the metro line, convention centers, and arenas. Staff is very friendly and rooms are fairly large. Just an FYI, if you're going to Phoenix, food is fairly scares after people go home from work. Thankfully the bar attached to the hotel is a decent option.

“A comfortable, pleasant stay” I stayed at this property during my tenure on a consulting project, which lasted from July 2007 through August 2008. This is a newer property near the Charlestown Navy Yard, along Boston Harbor and the entrance to the Charles River, but right up against the old Charlestown Bridge. This means that half the suites face the bridge and have virtually no view, while the other half has a very pleasant view. Fortunately, I had an upper-floor room with the harbor view during my stay. The facility and suites were very safe and secure, and the property is in a safe part of the city. If you drive, free parking is exceedingly limited, so in all likelihood, you will find yourself utilizing the valet service. For those who choose to walk and/or utilize transit, the facility is within easy walking distance to Bunker Hill and is practically within a few minute-walk from the USS Constitution. It is a 10-minute walk across the river to the TD Banknorth Garden - which also houses the closest transit station - and the historic North End neighborhood. Taxis are frequently queued outside the property, so for those not inclined to walk, access to the rest of the city is easy. The weak points are that - while there are some good full-service restaurants in the neighborhood - quick-service restaurants were non-existent. There was a servicable - albeit unspectacular - grocery store that was also about a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Overall cleanliness of the property was very good to excellent. The suite was somewhat small, but as a solo traveler, it was spacious enough, and was comfortable. The suite was clean, and all was in good working order. If something did happen to break or otherwise go wrong, maintenance services were responsive and made things right in short order. The bed was very comfortable. The kitchenette was fine, although a bit impractical to do anything more than microwave cooking. The suites were quiet, so external disturbances were minimal. From time to time, hot water in the suite could be hard to come by. But usually that was in the morning during the time that they were making their breakfast and when those guests heading to work were likely to be up and getting ready for the day. Laundry services were plentiful, albeit a bit expensive. There was a free breakfast service served seven days a week, which offered a good variety of food and was generally satisfying. On Mondays through Thursdays from 5pm to 6:30pm, they served a free hospitality snack and/or beverage, which often times was hearty enough to be an evening meal. The facility did have a cafe, which in the warmer months had the bulk of its seating outside on the pier, that was decent. In the summer months, the hotel also offered free movies that were shown on the pier. The front desk staff was overall very pleasant and responsive to all guest requests. They were also very knowledgable about the area, and the best options to access them. The housekeeping was also very pleasant, and even the property managers were pretty cordial and responsive. Overall, I had a very good lodging experience at this property. I did have colleagues who worked with me at various times during my tenure there who had different experiences with suite quality and such, but I cannot speak to those individual opinions. All I can say is that I would recommend this property with no qualms - particularly if you can procure a room with the harbor view.

“EinHotel mit seiner sehr guten Lage” Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral gelegen mitten in Boston im Financial District. Das Hotel befindet sich in einem ordentlichen Zustand es ist sauber und stillvoll eingerichtet. Die Zimmer sind sauber aber etwas klein, ansonsten befinden sich die Zimmer wirklich auf einem vier Sterne Nivenau. Mit auf jedem Zimmer gibt es sogar einen Wasserkocher und eine kleine Minibar. Das Badezimmer war etwas klein geschnitten aber sauber und mit allem eingerichtet was man benötigt, Haarföhn und Kosemtika. Wir haben ausserdem einen Mietwagen mit dabei gehabt, dieser wurde immer bei unserer Ankunft vom Hotelservice in ein Parkhaus gefahren und wenn man das Fahrzeug zurück benötigte, dann musste man nur kurz bescheid geben und in 5 Minuaten wa das Auto vor dem Hotel , dieser Luxus kostetse uns dann auch 38 USD die Nacht war aber sehr bequem und würde ich jedem empfehlen. Das Frühstück kostet 26 UDS pro Person und Tag ist aber sehr zu empfehlen, denn man findet alles was man braucht das Buffet ist wirklich mit allem bestückt was man für einen guten Start in den Tag braucht. Alles in allem emofehle ich dieses Hotel jedem der Boston zu Fuß erkunden möchte. Denn diese Hotel besticht vorallem durch die Lage.

“Simply put, horrible” I thought hard before writting this review, but at the end the result was the same: this hotel is not worth its price, or even a portion of it. The lobby and other public areas are very nice. It is a historical building and those areas are well kept. But after you make it past them, it's a nightmare. The hallways look like something out of the movie The Shining. There is duck tape holding down the carpet - and I checked with other guests in other floors, this is true on every floor. It is very dirty. You see cobwebs in window sills and pieces of paper and trash on the floor. The rooms are small and ill-equipped for the price charged. Two of the lamps in the room didn't work, and calls for repair went unaswered. The air conditioning was very loud, clicking on and off all the time, making it hard to sleep. This might be a minor thing, but for the price (over $225), I expected to have a sleep timer function in the TV. The bathroom is very small and the bathtub had chunks of ... paint? porcelain? pealing off. Tub was stained (dirty?) and there was mildew in many places. Closet doors didn't close properly and the carpet, again, very old, torn and dirty. I had dinner here once and the food was mediocre at best. Breakfast was acceptable but very pricey. Save yourself a bad stay and select another hotel. The Hilton and Westin are both within walking distance. Just come and see the lobby, if you want to.

“Recommend Highly” My family and I had the pleasure of staying at this hotel and received superb service in every way. From the accommodations, to the staff, everyone goes out of their way to see to it that you are comfortable. And we were. The area is wonderful for vacation as well as business. I would definitely stay there again. It is a beautiful city with a lot to offer, and the Hyatt is in an ideal location for all your travel needs.

“Great location of Ravens Stadium, Harbor etc” Stayed here for a soccer match recently. Area is really nice, one of the nicest US cities I've been to (and I've been to a lot). The harbor area is walking distance and very pretty. The Ravens stadium is pretty close too if you're going to a sports game and the baseball stadium isn't far away either. So ideal location, the rooms were very nice and spacious. As a Hilton Diamond member got a great room, coffee, fridge, wireless. I think the only thing I can say wrong about this place is the pillows. The bed was great but the pillows ha me waking up every 5 mins.. utterly awful, like bags of air. Don't hesitate the stay here though, i'd say again (just bring my own pillow)

“Same W nonsense, even higher price tag” As I was sitting in a very large, very expensive ($600+) room at the W Union Square I looked around at the pallid, sparse furnishings and decided this was the last W I would be visiting. Did all the furniture break during a party? Or was there never any there to begin with? At least a Holiday Inn will normally provide two chairs so guests can comfortably chat. At any W it's all about profit (you know you get the feeling you're doing them a favor by staying there) and in this huge room I had ONE chair. Unbelievable. It was just representative of the complete lack of passion or real investment in these truly mediocre hotels.

“Nice room. No frills but clean.” Small room but adequate. Somewhat overpriced but that's because of the area. Overall pretty clean and staff was very friendly. Very convenient location, decent parking. Would stay here again for business but not a destination by any means.

“Wonderful stay...spacious, nice room with great view...friendly staff...central location” I had stayed here a couple of years ago, but since then the hotel has remodeled and it looks great. My room was superb: I was first astonished by the SIZE (HUGE). The bed was comfortable with a choice of firm or soft pillows. Room was quiet for a good night's sleep. There was a flat-screen TV, lots of closet space, a comfortable chair and footrest, desk area, in-room safe, big bathroom with lots of countertop space - - everything I could ask for (except a refrigerator). I also enjoyed snapping photos of the wonderful view from the small room balcony...and it was great to step out there for some fresh air... Staff was extremely friendly, and someone from customer relations even called me during my stay to make sure that everything was good. This was appreciated! I had meant to use the pool and workout room, but kept so busy during my stay in San Francisco that I never had time to do so. Location is very central to everything I needed in San Francisco - public transportation, South of Market nightlife, downtown shopping, Civic Center... I got a good rate during my stay here and the Holiday Inn Civic Center will be my first choice for my next visit to San Francisco. For snacks and such, make sure to go to Urban Market a couple blocks away on 8th Street - - it was a great place with a nice salad bar, prepared foods, juices, fruit/vegetables, organic snacks...

“Classy Hospitality” At the corner of 17th and Stout Streets, the Magnolia is within walking distance of many downtown Denver venues, including the Denver Center for the Performing Arts and the Paramount Theatre. Denver Pavilions, which includes a shopping center, bowling alley, night clubs, and a multiscreen cinema, is also not far away on the 16th Steet pedestrial mall. Denver's financial district is just to the west and north on 18th and 19th Streets. There are several good restaurants in the area. A free shuttle runs up and down the 16th Street Mall connecting the downtown with lower downtown ("LoDo"), and is easiliy accessible from the Magnolia. The urban tram, which Denverites call the "light rail" stops just outside the hotel on Stout Street. We found the hotel to be very quiet considering its downtown location. You will be able to hear the streetcar clanging from some rooms facing Stout Street, but not to the point of it being annoying. The hotel is in a solid old building that originally held the offices of a bank. The retrofitting some years ago was very successful. Adapting the hotel to the existing space created rooms of varying floor plans and sizes, making it an interesting place that is not uniform or bland. My partner and I stayed in what the Magnolia reservations website calls a "king suite." Because we intended to cook, I called ahead and asked if king suites include a full kitchen, and I was told yes. However, when we checked in we were given a suite with only a microwave and small refrigerator. I requested a change, and the management did reassign us to a suite with a full kitchen. Both suites are classified the same way on the website and rent for the same rate. There seems to be no way to know for sure when using the online hotel reservation site that one is reserving a suite with a full kitchen instead of just a microwave and fridge. After we moved one floor down to a different suite, everything was fine and we were able to have a couple of friends visiting Denver come to the room the next night and cook a holiday meal with us.. The suite was spacious with a dining area, a large sitting room with sofa and upholstered chairs, the full kitchen I mentioned earlier, including a standard size refrigerator, and a separate bedroom with king bed, off of which is the bath. There is no writing desk; however, the dining room table is large enough to accommodate that purpose. I like the high ceilings, the big tall windows, and the comfortable, roomy feel to the place. There are television sets in both the living room and bedroom. The bathroom is small but accommodating, with an oval-shaped tub-shower combination and attractive modern fixtures. The bedroom comes equipped with an i-Pod player, so we plugged in our own music. The hotel provides nice fluffy bathrobes, which are hanging in the large closet off of the bedroom. There was always plenty of hot water and thick towels of good quality. One of the best things about the Magnolia is the bed. It was luxuriously comfy and very conducive to a good night's sleep. The wireless internet service comes at no additional charge. The clerk will issue you an access code when you check in. The signal was consistently strong, and we had no problems getting and staying online. Unfortunately, the hotel does not have an exercise room. I believe it's possible to use a fitness center elsewhere in downtown Denver as part of the hotel package, but I didn't find that convenient. There are a number of extras that can be ordered to enhance the stay, all of which are explained on the website and all of which are fairly expensive. If you want a massage, be aware that it is also provided offsite. A hotel shuttle vehicle takes guests a short distance away to a massage therapy business. I did not find it to be worth the trouble. We found the service efficient and courteous. The maid service was prompt and thorough. The hotel offers a complimentary wine and beer hour in the spacious downstairs lounge and sitting room, which is also where the complimentary breakfast is served. The bartenders were very friendly and kept topping off our glasses throughout the happy hour. The complimentary service includes only four different varieties of wine and two kinds of beer. If you would like a cocktail or other beverage, there is a charge for it. We met several other guests at these happy hours before having dinner and found the atmosphere very pleasant. The breakfast served in the mornings is expanisve, including several hot dishes as well as cereals, fruits and breads. I believe cookies or snacks are also offered in this downstairs space at some point in the afternoon, but we were never in the hotel a that time to take advantage of it. There is a bar in the Magnolia known as Harry's, accessible off the lobby or from 17th Street. Its retro mid-20th century design and narrow, cramped space do not particularly appeal to me, though, and we chose not to spend much time there. If you're bringing a car, here's a tip for parking at the Magnolia: After turning into the covered entryway off of 17th Street, just keep going past the hotel entrance and valet stand and drive on into the parking garage adjacent to the hotel. Pick up a ticket from the automatic dispenser on the way in and leave your car parked there during your stay. There is an $8 per day charge, which you will pay on your way out. This is much cheaper than having the valet park the car (most likely in the same garage), and the elevator down from the parking garage brings you to within a few feet of the hotel entrance. I enjoyed the Magnolia's classy hospitality and would definitely consider staying at the hotel again.
“GREAT HOTEL” Love staying here! Comfortable and a great location.
“Beyond Expectations” Stayed here during a business conference. Outstanding!

“slow service” I have been to this hotel multiple times over the years and I will not be there again. It was used by United for many years for the First class passengers as a place to refresh and as a day room I liked it. Having stayed there 3 times in the last 2 years the hotels service is not improving and the restaurant food is barely acceptable for 2 star let alone 5 star. Room service is very good in so far as service but food is not much better.The hotel does have nice rooms a little dated and the shuttle service to LAX is okay. The hotel is quite clean and the swimming pool is quite good. It is quite good value at $110 but I could not do 4 days again with that food.

“average hotel; you get lost in the building” room was ok with a nice view over downtown. the windows are thin so even on the 20th floor you have quite some street noise. there is supposed to be a huge area with restaurants in the hotel but unfortunately most of the shops are empty and there are only some fast food places and a brewery place. but it's hard to find something as it feels like a labyrinth. parking is super expensive and this applies also to the parking lot across the street. we drove in but there was no sign outside showing the prices. inside we saw a sign and we wanted to leave the building literally within 3 mins and they wanted us to pay like 30usd. we argued with them until they opened the barrier without charge. they must be nuts. put a sign outside and you avoid this.

“Not bad for a Marriott” Free WiFi. In-room coffee. Clean pool and hot tub. Friendly front desk. My only problem were teenagers, as my room was near the pool/hot tub. Don't get a room there if you need to sleep. Complaints to management didn't help; they were loud and noisy well after 11pm. That said, the front desk people were first rate otherwise. There is the problem of the insanely priced breakfast there. Go down the street to 96th, where you can find much better deals at fast food or sit-down bakery cafes or coffee shops.

“**Would never stay here again**” HEALTH WARNING - do not stop here if you require relaxation and a sound nights sleep! We stayed here for 2 hell filled nights, the hotel is right next to the freeway which is busy and noisy 24/7. We asked to be moved but were told that there were no quiet rooms. The rooms were dark, dismal and miserable as were the staff, not a single member of the staff spoke to us until we were checking out only to check we were paying with our MasterCard. The wine bar was friendlier with the bar tender being very clued up and willing to help with your choice of wines. In all I would never stay here again or advise anyone else to.

“No problems at all” We recently stayed at the Omni Parker House. We were able to check in early at 11am which was great. The room was nice with a king size bed and nice size TV. The A/C worked well and the room wasn't too small. The bathroom was very small, but this wasn't a major issue. The food that we had at the hotel was very good and the drinks were strong in the Last Hurrah Bar. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

“It's like your college dorm ... and that's good!” You'll be on the campus of the University of Washington. It has a fun, 70s dorm-like feel with bright colors and formica furniture. It has a Hampton Inn-esque breakfast so you get to interact with your dorm mates. The rooms are spacious and clean. WiFi and parking are free. We didn't use a free shuttle into downtown but that wounded promising. We were here on a busy weekend with Pike/downtown hotels going for $300-$400 a night. We got this at $180, definitely a great deal.

“Modern comfort and cleanliness at the right price!” I booked this hotel for a very last minute weekend getaway to NYC and was pleasantly surprised with my choice. The location on 28th street between Park and Lexington Ave was nice. There is a subway station right on the corner of 28th and Park Ave serviced by the 6 train, which made getting around a breeze. The hotel itself was exceptionally clean. The rooms of course were a little on the small side, but that is to be expected in a major city. They were still comfortable enough and spacious enough for two people though. A nice perk was the complimentary breakfast at the hotel's restaurant, which is Zagat rated.

“Good base for sightseeing” My wife, 8 year old daughter and I spent a long weekend in DC in March to see the sights. This hotel is ideally located for sightseeing, across the street from the McPherson Square Metro stop, and two blocks from the White House. Other sights like the Smithsonian museums are a good 15 minutes walk, which you can do on a nice day, otherwise take the Metro. We took the Metro everywhere including Reagan airport. The hotel itself is nothing fancy but is functional and clean. Our room with two double beds wasn't cramped but certainly wasn't spacious--there wasn't much extra room. But it didn't bother us since we spent most of our time sightseeing. We asked for a quiet room away from street noise and ended up with an inward facing room 25 feet from an office building and overlooking the air conditioning units on the ground floor. Even though we were on the eight floor we could hear the units' constant drone which was a little annoying but still better than car noise for us. Everything else about the hotel was fine. Service was very friendly. There are four elevators so never a long wait. The indoor pool is pretty small and cramped but we didn't use it. Buffet breakfast was about $15 a person and half price for kids and it was complete, including an omelet station. We got a great weekend rate (which more than doubles during the weekday) and would definitely stay here again.

“Very good” I booked on Priceline, and got an excellent deal; I bid slightly below what I thought Hotwire was offering the room at. The room was really nice, the workout room was good, and it had a heated indoor pool. The bathroom amenities were nice, and it smelled like fruit potpourri. Great location. Parking is expensive.

“Happy Returns for Us” My spouse and I stayed at the Taj Campton Place in mid-March for a long weekend. It was our 5th stay at the hotel and we will keep coming back. It's a small luxury hotel, with extremely capable staff who are concerned and helpful but not overly-intrusive, as sometimes can be the case at high-end or resort properties. It has a terrific open-air gym, a very good restaurant and a little gem of a bar staffed with friendly, experienced, knowledgeable and creative mixologists. And its location we believe is perfect: a block from Union Square, in easy walking distance to the Ferry Building, and readily accessible to all of the major modes and lines of transit (BART, MUNI trains and buses, cable cars, and of course taxis). Last but not least, when you return to your room at the end of a busy day and late evening, you find your room ready to welcome you-- with the bed turned down, lights low, bottled water at bedside, and slippers and a floor mat at your bedside. It's pretty easy to travel when you feel this well cared-for. There are certainly newer and probably "fancier" hotels in the city, but we'll keep coming back to the Taj Campton Place for our visits to San Francisco.

“Very nice, convenient hotel” My recent stay at the Embassy Suites in Washington, D.C. showed that there are companies that still practice the old-fashioned value of customer service. Traveling to Washington, D.C. for a conference, I chose the Embassy Suites at 900 10th Street NW for a couple of reasons. First and foremost, I’m a fan of Hilton properties. As a Hilton Honors Diamond Member, I receive some additional perks and usually a little special treatment (who doesn’t like that?). Second, the room rate was more favorable than the conference hotel just a block down the street, and all Embassy Suites include breakfast, which makes my comptroller just a little happier with my expense account. Staff is uniformly professional and quite polished. Whether it was the valets who greeted me upon arrival, the desk clerks, or the housekeeping staff in the hall, everyone consistently offered a "Good morning" or "good evening," which is an excellent embodiment of Hilton standards. The rooms are undergoing a "refresh" and, having stayed in one of the redone rooms, I can confirm they are lovely. The furnishings, carpeting, and additional items including flat-screen TVs are all state-of-the-art. The bathrooms feature high-end amenities and bathrobes are standard in each room. This particular property has a restaurant on site. Finn & Porter was a nice place to grab a cocktail or a quick bite. The restaurant is also the venue for the Embassy Suites' included breakfast. The included breakfast was, in a word, predictable. The steam table featured the ubiquitous scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, home fries, pancakes, juices, cereal, fruit, and yoghurt. The hotel also offers a station where guests can get made-to-order omelets, freshly-prepared fried eggs (and freshly-scrambled eggs, too, for the fussy like me). I was there for five nights and breakfast offerings were identical all three mornings, with the sole exception being the pancakes and waffles. If it was pancakes one morning, you could be sure it would be waffles the next. Consistency is fine as far as it goes, but a little variety would be welcome. Mixing it up a little – offering French toast instead of pancakes, for example, or corned beef hash instead of one of the other breakfast meats - would be nice. My only criticism is reserved for the nightly Manager's Reception. Taking place from 5:30 to 7:30, it offers an extremely limited selection of complimentary beverages and even fewer snacks. A nut-pretzel mix and chips and salsa were the only nibbles I saw during the couple of times I popped in. Based on what I saw, I thought it worth the extra expense to pay a few bucks to enjoy a genuine happy hour at one of the nearby establishments. The Embassy Suites is a few blocks away from the Gallery Place/China Town Metro station, and a few blocks from the Metro Center station, so it's convenient to many places in central DC and is, of course, within easy walking distance of the White House. Embassy Suites tend to attract a lot of families with kids, especially on the weekends. However, the management at this property had the presence of mind to post large signs on the weekends, urging people to observe "quiet time" after 9 p.m. It must have worked, because my floor was very quiet indeed. If you need to be in the area of the Washington, D.C. Convention Center, I definitely recommend the Embassy Suites.

“Well located, nice hotel” We were looking for a quick overnight getaway and bid for a Philly hotel through Priceline. Check-in was easy. Our room was slightly smaller than average but well decorated. I don't know whether Priceline customers are assigned smaller rooms or if all the rooms at this hotel are for the most part small. The bathroom was on the small side as well. The hotel rooms must have been renovated not too long ago because the bathtub was a bit worn looking but the rest of the bathroom and the bedroom looked fairly new. The bed was extremely comfy with lots of pillows. The room and bathroom were very clean. I found the service in the hotel to be friendly and efficient. Parking is expensive at $38 a night. The location is very good - right by the Reading Market and within walking distance to many nice restaurants, tourist sites and Rittenhouse Square.

“Clean, comfortable, quiet, huge suite in the middle of Time Square.” I could not have asked for a better room in Time Square than this hotel. The location is by far the best selling point, in Time Square. Although the location is in the middle of a very busy tourist area, I had no problem with noise or any disturbance at night. The hotel room suite is huge compared to other hotels I've stayed within the area. 2 flat screen televisions, one in bedroom and a larger one in the living room. The sofa also converts to a bed. Large desk in the living room and large bathroom, great lighting, this hotel has it all and I'm very happy to have made the right decision. Hotel checkin was friendly and fast. The signature cookie upon check-in is always very welcoming. Wifi connection is good throughout the hotel. Hotel breakfast offers basic hot and cold food. But there are so many great restaurants around the area there is little reason to eat at the hotel. You do not have to worry about going hungry because many of the stores around the area close late. Ask for a high floor room overlooking the square.

“Decent hotel but poor service.” We stayed here for 3 nights, and the room was decent but nothing special. The staff was very friendly and tried to be helpful but we consistently had long waits getting our car from the valet (once they forget that we had asked for it), and room service often botched our order (once they forget to send it and then said it was too late). There were strange, loud noises coming from our refrigerator which kept me awake at night, and the proximity to the hospital er kept us awake due to the sirens. It's on the GW Univ campus, and close to Georgetown and American, so it's convenient if you're doing college visits as we were, but not walking distance to DC attractions.

“Marriott Platinum member recommends - Great location” Marriott Platinum member traveling through DC on leisure found the hotel met and/or exceeded expectations. Room supports business traveler as well with suitable plugs and flat screen tv. Easily accessible to the Metro and amenities in the area. Staff were very attentive to details, and the concierge in particular was helpful in identifying the location of the restaurant where we were meeting friends. Recent renovations did not impact our stay, although we are not one to stay in a hotel for hours when visiting a City for a short period of time (or on business!). Only annoyance was lounge not open on the weekends (looked up to standards, and would stay for business purposes), but DC provides many alternatives for breakfast (we opted to eat out instead of remaining in the hotel...).
“手頃で便利” 立地が非常に良く、値段も比較的手頃です。サブウェイの駅、バス停に近いので、大抵のところはすぐに行けます。食事の場所を見つけるのにも困りませんし、徒歩圏内にゼイバーズなどのスーパーもあり、買出しにも行けます。セントラルパーク、自然史博物館も近いです。

“Elegant Luxury and Superb Service” This is a beautiful, elegant, classy hotel. It's not huge and almost gives you the feeling of staying at someone's gorgeous home. The lobby is elegant and there are fresh flower arrangements on almost every surface...including the guest room bathrooms. The hotel is famous for their service and we were not let down. The valet service was the best we have ever experienced. They were fast, efficient, friendly, and called us by name. The concierge was equally wonderful booking us spa appointments at the neighboring Rosewood Crescent Court. (which was lovely too) The gym is full of new equipment and stocked with water and fresh fruit. We enjoyed a drink at the hotel bar which had a great bartender who offered us complimentary light snacks with our wine. Our room was the most basic the hotel offers but still had a small balcony and was decorated in soothing pale peach and rose colors. The shower and towels were wonderful and so was the bed and down comforter. My husband called and asked for their "complimentary shoe shine" and his shoes were picked up and returned to us polished in under 15 minutes! Like I said...the service was amazing! We will stay here next time we have a reason to come to Dallas... we felt relaxed and pampered the entire time!

“soho style” On most trips to NYC I usually like midtown locations or the upper-east side. My last trip I decided would be nice to have a change and stay in Soho at the Mercer. It was a small hotel but it makes up for the size with charm. The lobby had a cute bar, (only hotel guests and friends could hang there). That makes it special. I did see a few stars having cocktails. The lounge was comfortable and had soft couches and chairs, it was a nice place to have drinks and chat. The staff was very helpful in making dinner and theatre reservations. The room wasn't ready when we checked in. We had to wait until 4pm. That was not a positive thing, but the shops next to the hotel kept me busy while I was waiting for my room. Soho is a relaxed environment so It didn't really bother me. Once I finally go to my room I was very happy. We had a junior suite which is about 500 sq. ft. It had a large bathroom and a deep soaking tub with louvre doors that looked out into the bedroom. The housekeeping staff took care of all my requests for extra towels, soaps and pillows. The pillows where down and the bed was very comfortable. The only complaint I had was that they couldn't change the heat to air conditioning, the hotel was a little warmer than I like at night. The streets where quiet enough to crack the window a little to let in some cooler spring NYC air. The room had a large couch and dining table which was very convenient for room service. The location was great, we just walked out the door to all the soho shops. The hotel didn't have a gym, but provided Equinox passes which was one block away. I was having fun one night with my music a little loud late night with a male stripper, The hotel security did tell me to keep it down, But I still loved the hotel, I get out of control sometimes, especially in NYC.

“Great Stay After A Long Flight” No problems here.....we arrived at about 11am and were able to check in immediately. Great room, very spacious, clean and nicely decorated. We had a small balcony but unfortunately it overlooked the parking garage so we didn't use it. Airport noise was minimal. Bed was super comfy and even had a nice afternoon nap after our long flight . Ate lunch at the on premises restaurant. Very good food and value although service was a little slow. The managers reception that evening was also great, with drinks and snacks like popcorn, a pretzel mix and chips & salsa (which served as our dinner that night!). The breakfast next morning was just what we have come to expect of Embassy Suites: fabulous. We probably are more than we should have since everything was so good. The staff is very friendly and helpful, especially when we asked about things to do in the area. The only thing we felt was overpriced was parking....$22/day. We did not use the hotel facilities but the pool looked nice although small. Only one set of elevators, however, and that seemed a bit odd. We enjoyed our stay and would definitely stay there again when in that area.

“travelled with 3 kids...had to all sleep in one king size bed....” booked online then quickly called to confirm...told them we had 3 small kids and needed 2 queens or at the very least a rollout.Arrived to find the hotel booked and no rollout available? Like Hello..I called to verify this?? Stuck us in a room with only one king size bed?? NICE!! needless to say our night was sleepless and our stay was disappointing.On a plus side we parked on the street so there was no need to pay the $45 a night the hotel wants?? ....walked to Safeway for breakfast items and got out of there asap!! Hotel was nice..rooms were nice and clean...customer service was a big disappointment though!

“Quirky, Friendly, Comfortable” On a "we got to get away" weekend we chose to stay at another Kimpton hotel in San Francisco. Our first impression was that of the great mural wrapping the walls of the lobby. Bright colors with amorphous designs depicting the history of San Francisco's beat, hippie, cool and cosmopolitan history and cultures. The hotel is on Grant Avenue near the city's Chinatown Gate. Good restaurant and shopping are just steps away from the hotel's big double (and heavy) double front doors. Wine and juices are served each afternoon between 5 and 6. Because Kimpton's is a pet friendly hotel chain we were entertained during the happy hour by the antics of the bell man's well behaved pet dog. Vintage movies and classic MTV videos play on the lobby's big TV screens and as soon as we walked in the hotel the vibes were set for an entertaining and fun experience. After taking the light show motif elevator to our floor the experience calms down to to reflect a more conventional older, but well kept up property. The hallways are painted in subdued colors while the hall carpeting gives thought to a wild Las Vegas casino style pattern. Sounds like a culture clash so far but believe me the designs seem to work. Our room was small but every amenity was provided. One wall was a deep red and the other three walls were painted robin's egg blue. Hotel room colors never interested me before but with this hotel chain I have learned to look for the unusual in decor. The rooms main lighting fixture was a three pronged, three color globes or orbs. I won't try to elaborate further. Service was great. Location is right down town. The room rate was very reasonable for the quality of the experience and for the location. Although we here on an entertainment only basis the hotel is just a short walking distance to the city's financial center, and a weekday morning shuttle service is provided from the Triton to the financial district. Anything negative? OK, because there are water flow devices on the bathroom fixtures the toilets run slow and the water pressure is a little low. But geeze they provide leopard patterned bath robes - so what do you want? Will we return for another visit? We need to see what the lighting fixtures in the other rooms look like! You bet we will be back!

“Excellent Location, Beautiful, but Not Worth The Money” Clift is a very beautiful hotel -- the lobby is stunning, the furniture is gorgeous, the elevators are sexy, I loved the periwinkle and silver decorations and thought the hotel room was very pretty. The location was terrific -- great restaurants within steps from the hotel, excellent shopping. Great front desk service. That said, I did not think it was worth the near $400 we paid for the night. The bed was not very comfortable although the room was quiet. It was our first trip to San Francisco and I'm glad we stayed there, but next time we'll probably look for a hotel that places more emphasis on comfort than style.

“It was decent” The Renaissance is a very pretty, centrally located hotel. The lobby and restaurant are both very nice. The rooms themselves were decent, although the bathrooms are sorely in need of a remodel. Both me and another business companion found the bathtubs to be dirty (they may be stained). But the bathtubs at motel 6's have always looked nicer then here. The staff is very helpful and friendly, and the cafe downstairs is good for coffee in the morning. Another negative is that the Renaissance feels a need to gouge you on prices for little things. Internet is $10 a day, although it is fast and works well. Don't expect to save money buying water in the lobby, they only sell $4.33 Norwegian artesian water (Tastes like tap water to me).

“Basic Room with no Frills” The 2 double bed room was large for NY standards, but there was nothing trilling about the room. It reminded me of a Best Western room in California that would cost less than $60. Staff was nice and it close to the subway. I would only recommend if you get a good deal on the price.

“Great value, convenient to airport, very nice staff” I held an internal sales meeting here over two days in August. Jim M. handled my reservation quickly and professionally and the price was right, too. (We had the 'Boardroom' conference room for two days and several hotel rooms for us out-of-towners.) Besides being a very friendly and professional person, Jim was also very helpful, as indeed was everyone on the staff there. The rooms were clean. The wifi was remarkably fast for a hotel system. The only reason I withhold 5 stars v 4 is that there were some issues with my room (toilet didn't work properly, shower made a very loud noise and the desk chair was very squeaky), suggesting they need to pay a bit more attention to maintenance. But I would definitely stay here again when in Denver, just because of how helpful and professional the staff was. For example, by the time I returned to my room in the afternoon, they had fixed the toilet problem. And in a very good indicator of dedication to customer service, when I filled out the post-stay survey and noted the maintenance issues, I got back a person response within hours. Bottom line: definitely recommend this hotel in you need an airport hotel in Denver.

“Experience San Jose Package” We booked the "Experience San Jose" package as we were planning just a one night stay and seeing the Winchester Mystery House and the Tech Museum of Innovation - so this was perfect. The price for the room was fair with the tickets included which were 2 adult tickets. We had to buy 3rd tickets for our 8 year old son but it still was a bargain. When we checked in, the desk person asked if she could "upgrade" us to the tower. I was slightly suspicious but it turned out alright. The room was nice with all the amenities except the bathrobes. They gave our son a little instamatic Fairmont camera which he thought was very cool and he took pictures all week-end with it. The downside of the rooms in the tower is you have to go to 2nd floor and cross over a walkway and go up 2 floors to get to the pool. Since it was only one night - no problem but if you're planning to swim a lot this could be a problem. Also it isn't "as" convenient to their restaurants. If you have kids there is a Johnny Rocket's diner right behind the hotel plus other options in the area. We didn't do valet parking but parked right next to the Fairmont and paid total of $12 for 1 night and one day. We did the Sunday brunch in the restaurant and it was fabulous but expensive and most people just ordered off the menu. Overall, we loved the Fairmont and it worked out nicely for our plans. The second day we left our car in the parking lot and walked over to the Tech Museum and left when we wanted to. I'm writing this for families as I had trouble initially deciding if this would work with our son - but he loved it too.

“Hotel Tranquillo e pulito in centro” questo hotel si trova a pochissimi passi da Union Square,e alla fermata del cable car,la pulizia è buona e la mattina offre una piccola colazione fatta di tè brioche e caffè,intorno ad esso vi sono molti punti di ristoro,come la pizzeria che fa angolo dall'altro lato della strada;il personale è sempre stato cordiale e pronto ad aiutarci nelle nostre domande;lo consiglio per coppie giovani e per chi come noi è sempre fuori dalla camera per viversi la città!!

“Solid Choice” Most impressive for me was the hotel willing to accommodate an extremely early check-in due to a red eye flight the night before. I had requested early check-in prior to my arrival and it obviously cannot be guaranteed, but upon arriving at 6:00am I was given a room immediately. This made sightseeing the day before my conference so much more enjoyable than if I had been unable to crash for a few hours before spending a day walking DC in such sweltering heat and humidity. There was no extra charge for such an early-check in either. Based on how friendly they were at the very beginning of my stay, some of the small annoyances were loss bothersome. Such as the kids running up and down the halls beginning very early in the morning and the loud noise the doors make as they slam shut. My biggest disappointment was the service at Harry's Pub within the hotel. Took minutes to get acknowledged by a hostess who seemed to care less that there was a line waiting to be seated and the service was slow once I was seated. Of the four desserts listed, they were out of two of them (and this was only 9pm). And I had asked the check to be split between cash and a room charge. They took the cash and when I received my bill upon checking out noticed that the entire amount had also been charged to the room. I am in the process of trying to get this straightened out. I had a much better experience with breaskfast and the Stone Throw restaurant. Excellent location as far as convenice to the Woodley Park Metro Station and a short walk to the wonderful ethnic cuisine of Adams-Morgan. Top rate fitness center as well (its actually large enough that I would call it a gym). So with the exception of Harry's Pub, I would give this hotel two thumbs up.

“Pleasant stay” Stayed for one night at this grand old hotel. The room was large for New York City and the bathroom was nicely marbled but small with no place to put your toiletries. King bed was very comfortable. Room was very quiet. We had a good rate for a room with no view (which we were aware of when booking). It is in a great location; we only had about a 10-15 minute walk to the theatre at Lincoln Center. If I got the same rate, I would stay here again.

“GREAT EXPERIENCE!” Great location if you want to be in the middle of it all.. nice, BIG soundproof rooms, good service, wonderful ammenities, beautiful bar, it's like being in your own little world right in the middle of it ALL! ENJOY!

“Hotwire says 4.5 stars, I say solid 3 star” Don't get me wrong, there is absolutely nothing wrong with this hotel, especially for the price and location. It's just that it doesn't approach a 4.5 star rating. The rooms are large and well appointed. Free parking, free internet, free shuttle from airport and 10 minutes from downtown. What could be better? Well, minor things like bellhop service, it was non-existent on arrival and departure for me. consistent housekeeping, sometimes she left wash clothes, sometime not, i had to call 3 times. the elevator was very worn, needs remodel. Front desk staff were not very knowledgeable about their own hotel. Couldn't answer how long the gift shop was opened, couldn't offer any recommendations of what town tour to take, things like that. all in all these things are minor, but in a 4.5 star hotel, it would have been disappointing.

“Beyond Overrated!!!!” I was really looking forward to this one night getaway from LA we were going to have and I just got back tonight. I have to say from the moment we arrived my experience began to go downhill. When we pulled up at 8PM on a saturday night there was no valet or bellman to greet us. I simply opened my car door and my girlfriends and opened up the trunk and got my luggage out and waited for a few minutes and finally saw someone and I said, "Excuse me we are checking in." No one opened the door for us or anything. We finally got to our room and I have tosay the room besides the very nice TV looked like the room PRIOR to the multi-million dollar rennovations. The outside and inside decor of the whole hotel resembled a motel. HONESTLY!! The pools were outdated and had no real ambiance at all. The sheets and pillows were the worst I have slept on in so many years. The massage today was pretty good but I can tell you one thing, the spa that is supposed to be #1 in America is definetly not #1 in America! The food was actually pretty good and this morning we sat outside and had breakfast in the Veranda and the nest thing we all knew, a golf ball came flying at our heads. No warning or nothing so be careful. I am a golfer but did not golf this trip and the greens were nothing of a private country club that it is said to be. Very inconsistent with color and a mix of brown and dried grass every few feet. Overall, I have been to some pretty amazing hotels and this was suposed to be a great one, however I have truly no desire to go back here again and would be truthful to say I wouldn't feel comfortable reccomending it to people who wanted an incredible experience. Decent at best.

“had to stay again but it was much better” I had reviewed this hotel in June 2012. I had a filthy room back then. I was booked at the Quality Inn but all the power was out there and at the Econo Lodge. I knew I could afford the Microtel and I knew it was in a safe area and close to the airport. They also have good parking. I checked in and told the front desk of my dirty stay last time. They assured me that would not happen and if I had any problems that they would change my room. I was happy with my room. It had a few minor cleaning issues but overall okay. The best part of my stay was that the shuttle driver took me to the train stop that is very close to the hotel. He explained how to use the train (my very first train/subway ride) He told me where to stop and how far to walk to see all the downtown tourist places. I had a great day. He also said when I rode back to the train stop I could either walk a short distance back to the hotel or I could call and he would pick me up. so I rate this now average only because it still lacks a bit of cleaning but this stay was So much better for me.

“Decent enough” Ok, there have been plenty of terrible reviews on this property. Come on, people, what are you expecting? When you stay at a property that was built back in the 80's (or whenever), it's going to LOOK like a property from that era. I stayed for almost a week during a conference, and my experience was ok. Granted, this isn't the best place I've ever stayed, but the staff was VERY friendly and helpful, and my room was clean--and plenty big enough. You can't beat the location--one block to Camden Yards, and a block the other direction right into the Inner Harbor area. I paid about $190/nt. conference rate, and I do agree with those who say it's way overpriced for the level of comfort. However, if you travel at all to larger cities, you find that's now the norm. I would recommend a stay here if you get a really cheap rate on one of the travel sites...but don't pay full rack rate.

“Love it as long as I don't have to pay full price” We enjoyed our stay here. We stayed in two different rooms. The first room was great the second one showed signs of wear. Loved the courtyard area and hotel vibe. There is street parking around to avoid paying the valet. You can park at parking lots for $8 or street parking for free in the evenings. There is a sandwich shop next door that is good. The bar was nice and relaxing. Drinks were average price. We would definitely stay again with a discounted rate.

“Good stay but very noisy AC” I came back to this hotel after staying here a few times last year. The staff is friendly and service oriented, rooms are the usual 4 Points standard, the location is very good... my only issue was that the AC in my room was as loud as a 747 turbine. Other than that, this place is a good option and offers attractive value for money.

“Failed to Take the Lead” For the second time I was desperately looking for a San Jose hotel connected to their annual Rock N Roll half-marathon that would be "the one." The Marriott is connected to the San Jose Convention Center as was the Hilton Hotel, where I had previously stayed. Perhaps that unique location, almost guaranteeing high occupancy, has made them both complacent. Neither hotel excelled. Check-in at the Marriott was seamless. There were plenty of registration agents available as they anticipated the onslaught of marathoners and another convention starting Sunday. But that other convention also posed the problem of the Marriott informing us the only way you could get late check out (after 12 pm) was by paying half again of your room rate. The half-marathon was slated to take place from 8 am to 1 pm. So it became incumbent upon us to immediately return to the hotel to take a shower if we wanted to avoid the late charge. So much for the after event entertainment. Thanks for spoiling the party, Marriott! As a Marriott Rewards member my profile asks for a high floor. They put us on the 6th (of 25) floor. The room was basic Marriott although with a sliding door that was annoying and noisy at night. We had to keep the door closed because a low level fan ran constantly. We found the room to be tight with the standard king bed, corner chair, two piece desk and entertainment/dresser arrangement. A better design could have opened the room up a lot. We ended up parking in the convention center parking lot, maximum of $20.00 a day. This beat the Marriott's $36.00/night rate and, as it turns out, since we stayed less than 24 hours (due in large part to their being no late check out) our parking fee was only $20.00. The dining options were what they were. If you like a loud bar or a fancy-schmancy restaurant, this is the place. We wanted neither so walked to one of the ample options within within a couple of blocks. What passes for a coffee shop/convenience store in the lobby was disappointing. It was almost sad. A few day old Danish, some packaged cereal and a couple of spotted bananas. While it had good traffic the morning of the race (perhaps too much, all those runners trying to get caffeinated) overall it was a below average convenience store. So no big kudos for the Marriott. It could have been so much more but it failed to take the lead. If I attend next year's half-marathon my search will continue.

“WOW downtown NY location” If you are visiting 9/11 memorial, this is a perfect hotel to stay in. The hotel faces the entrance to the memorial and be sure to sip at the lobby bar or even better, the outdoor balcony for a superb view of One WTC and the other upcoming WTC towers. Inspite of the the on going construction (which doesn't really bother me) the area is bustling with tourist and within minutes of Soho and lower east side. The WTC subway station is minutes away nearby century 21, or the Lexington line is a couple of blocks on broadway. The 5 th floor lobby is ideal and feels isolated from the main tourist traffic and 9/11 memorial crowd, unlike the other nearby hotels. The wonderful/spectacular rooms are fairly designed and seems normal with enclosed bathroom unlike some of the other Ws. We had a corner room facing south east. The service is just about average and somewhat 'cold' at the front desk, but that didn't really bother me since I'm not a high demanding guest and don't expect too much in terms of service and attention. However, some may find it to be rude and unattentive. At night, ther area tend to be on a quiet side after the memorial closes. Nevertheless, you could gawk at the brightly lighted 1WTC tower from the lobby bar balcony. The lobby has a good selection of costly drinks and nibbles. we we fortunate to have a package deal which offered complimentary drinks. Heading out to nearby soho is about a 15-20 min walk or a short subway ride. I give this 5* Just for the location and property but 4 * for the service. Would consider staying here again when in NYC. Note: if visiting the memorial , make sure to reserve free online tickets for designated time slot entry to the memorial.

“Great hotel. I'd return in a heartbeat.” Fantastic hotel. Wonderful service. Plus: * Great location * I arrived early, and while my room was not ready, they were very accommodating regarding my desire to change and freshen up. * I had a corner room, and while other corners would have a view of the water, my room was great. Lots of room, big TV with art/music channels, very very comfortable. * Very comfortable bed. Prompt room service. * Nice area for breakfast and drinks * free high speed internet, wired and wireless. Cons: * Parking was pricey * None that I can think of. For any business/pleasure downtown, this is a great place to stay. Highly recommended.

“Average hotel in a great location” The Marriott Marquis is probably at the bottom in terms of meeting corporate Marriott standards. Towels and sheets are cheap quality and the bed isn't the Marriott "dream bed". Bathrooms are barely clean. But - wow! - what a great location! Elevators are unbelieveably efficient. You don't press and wait but rather enter your floor number into a central station and then you're directed to one of maybe 15 elevators with others going to similar destinations. All of us with rooms in the 30's rode together. Never waited more than a few minutes despite hoards of peopel.

“Not flash...” Staying here at present, wasn't choice, more due to cost. SF isn't cheap this time of year, this was on the lower end Rooms are ok, bathrooms are tiny..the size of a bath and thats it..tries to be funky, but its tired, noisy AC units, one set of elevators, single point of failure and yep one was broken... Fishermans wharf is quiet at night, better off staying in town if you can and cable car it out here for an hour or two during the day.. Breakfast service is blunt, pay first, buffet only and move on, no smile..bar is non existent really...sorry but I try and avoid this hotel but came back for SPG points only..

“Fun, funky Kimpton” Stayed at this hotel a number of years ago before it was a Kimpton property - still very similar - fun, funky decor that is starting to show its age just a bit. The neighborhood is great - walking distance to several good restaurants/bars/coffee and just a bit further to Dupont Circle, the White House, and about 15-20 min walk to the National Mall. Its about a 10 min walk to the nearest Metro stop, which is somewhat unfortunate if you are looking for that to be in close proximity. Rooms are good size, the exercise facility has some good machines, and the free champagne happy hour is definately a plus. Recommend Logan Tavern/Commisary for breakfast/brunch and Churchkey/Birch & Barley for dinner - both just a minute or two walk.

“Not Your Typical Super 8 Much Better Than Expected” I have always avoided staying at Super 8 motels, but this one is outstanding.The staff is very nice and accommodating, all area are very clean and well kept.
