The rooms are large and nicely decorated, breakfast has a large selection of items. Not really to near anything but easy to get to from the airport. The same management also owns other Super 8s in the area that might be more convenient to the area you are visiting.

“Wonderfull attentive staff combined with a beautiful hotel!” I attended a small conference at the Dallas Omni. This recently renovated hotel is georgious. The staff and management did everything possible to ensure our conference was perfect! Lots of TLC. Food and beverage operation was excellent! This is where you want to stay, dine, relax, and entertain.

“We'll be back” We've stayed at many NYC hotels, but this is our favorite. Convenient location, comfortable rooms, cheerful and courteous staff, wonderful complimentary breakfast and other small snacks throughout the day, free wifi, great rooftop bar, and an overall relaxing vibe throughout the hotel. It was always a relief to walk into the lobby, grab a cookie and tea or ice water and collapse there at the end of a trek around the city. The rooms are large by NY standards, the thick robes and slippers added a nice touch, the push-button shade blocked the early light and helped muffle street noise. We spent two nights here and wished it could have been a week. Nicest staff too--they made every encounter pleasant. We will plan future trips around the Hotel Giraffe.

“Very good hotel in SFco, great location...” Grand Hyatt was a Priceline win bid, based specially in the strategic location of Union Square, and that is the first good thing about it: it is located just steps away from the square. The hotel has partially attended my requests, since they have assined us adjoining rooms(four persons, two rooms), but not a special view, what I had asked informing them it was a special occasion. The view from our rooms in a lower to medium height floor facing the city was not bad, but not special. To have a nice view we went one morning to the restaurant on the top floor for breakfast, which was average in quality for the price. The rooms and bathroom are very clean, comfortable, with a nice size and decor. The lobby is small and bland, though. Value overall was great for us.

“Great location!” I stayed at the Hotel Beacon because of its wonderful location on the upper west side and the great reviews on TA. We were there for 3 nights during the Christmas madness. The location is fantastic, with a Starbucks right across the street and the subway 2 blocks down. I particularly love the mini kitchen with the fridge to keep my bottled water super cold. The seperate living area was also quite nice and gave the place a larger feel than many hotel rooms in NYC. The bathroom was really tiny, but no big deal. I would stay there again.

“Excellent hotel!” My wife and I stayed here over the NYE weekend, and we liked this hotel! Pros: * Quiet rooms. We upgraded to a corner on the 17th floor, and the bedroom is very quiet. * Almost-new rooms. As you can see in the photos, the condition of our room was excellent. * Good service - everyone we interacted with (check-in, check-out, other folks we talked with, etc) was very courteous and helpful. * Location - we arrived very late our first night, and didn't feel the least bit unsafe. Just a few blocks from the market and downtown. Cons: * Dining is a bit limited. There's Ruth's Chris and Starbucks (or in-room dining, priced like Ruth's Chris), but no breakfast buffet or hotel restaurant. (The spectrum is wide, but not a lot in the middle.) But that's about it. Overall, we liked this place. We'd definitely stay again.

“Nice big room, great view, weird bathroom” We stayed at the Blackstone over Memorial Day weekend. We flew in at around 1 PM and took the Blue Line train from O'Hare to Jackson Street and then the Red Line to Harrison. It would've been better just to walk from Jackson since we waited for about 10 minutes and it was only one stop which we could've walked more quickly. It was raining and was only a few blocks from the train stop to the hotel. We got to the hotel a little after 2 and were able to check in. We had booked the room through Priceline a couple months ago and had called and requested 2 beds but they said there weren't any available. We asked for one when we got there since there were 3 of us sharing the room and they offered us a lake view room with 2 queen beds for an additional $30/night so we jumped on it. The room ended up having a fantastic view that we were able to enjoy off and on over the weekend since it rained a lot. When we left on Memorial Day the view was stunning since the weather was perfect. The room they gave us was huge, so big in fact that the 37 inch LCD HDTV looked rather small while sitting in the bed. Maybe it was a bit smaller but the picture was great nonetheless. The beds were extremely comfortable. The only real issue we had with the room was the bathroom. This bathroom needs its own paragraph since for whatever reason it had a sliding door that didn't even cover the full doorway! A horrible design and completely ineffective. Basically the door provided zero privacy so if you have this room to yourself it's not a problem, but I just hope that you're REALLY comfortable with whoever you're with if you're staying there with anyone. Not only did it give a straight sight line into the shower from the main room with the door slid shut, it also did nothing to muffle any noise. A fan or something would be nice. I was woken up on Sunday morning by the shower which sounded like a dang waterfall right next to my bed. A little common sense in room design goes a long way, people. Something I guess I've taken for granted all these years at other hotels. The actual shower in the bathroom was nice as it was a rainfall design, but the wallpaper is a bit of a question mark. OK well enough about that since I really did like the hotel. We had a 9th floor room that looked right out to Buckingham Fountain and we could see towards downtown and the Navy Pier to the north and down to Soldier Field and a few nice looking museums to the south. A great view of Grant Park. A big plus to get a room with one of these views. We had a perfect in-room vantage point for Saturday night fireworks that were going off around 10 PM in the Navy Pier vicinity. The location of the hotel is a bit south of most of the Chicago hotels we were looking at and we did end up walking a lot over the 3 day weekend. We took the Red Line to a baseball game at Wrigley Field and it only took about 45 minutes or so to get there. We definitely recommend going to a baseball game if you're in Chicago. We had a great time and met a bunch of great people while sitting through a 3 hour rain delay waiting for the game to start. The housekeeping was great and the people at the hotel were all very nice. We had a few meals nearby, one at Yolk which was about 4 blocks south on Michigan Ave which we would highly recommend for breakfast. We also ate at a nearby Lou Malnati's on State Street that had some really good deep dish pizza. Overall we had a nice stay at the hotel and look forward to a return visit to Chicago at some point in the near future.

“Surprisingly small rooms” First, all of the comments about taxes and hidden costs are true. My special group rate was $129/night for 2 nights. Total bill came to $359.60 after taxes and $27/night for valet parking. Internet access charges are absolutely ridiculous. Coffee shops can offer this service free, but large hotels must nickel-and-dime? Marriotts such as this should at least waive the fee for its Silver and Gold Rewards members. This Marriott has one of those services where the 24-hour period you buy for $9.95 goes from 12 Noon-to-12 Noon. Well, I check in late one night and didn't get online until early the next morning. So, the first day I was on I really paid for 2 days of service. Obviously, this was a business function and not my money - and maybe they count on that, charging what they want. Still, there are certain perks I think they should extend for Elite members of their Rewards program. Back on valet parking - call ahead for your car with plenty of time to spare. It took forever to get our car both days. The room was surprisingly small. The room was clean, but once you put a suitcase down, put a laptop and some other things on the desk, the room instantly becomes cluttered. In the bathroom, there was a used wash cloth hanging over the shower curtain rod - and of all the housekeeping oversights, that is the one I absolutely DESPISE! One other major problem - there are 5 elevators. From the lobby, one only offers access to the ballroom and gym/pool floors. So that leaves 4 elevators for the rooms. There is a constant crowd around them, and you sometimes need to wait 5 minutes or more. One day, waiting on the 8th floor to go back down to the lobby, I eventually gave up after at least 6 or 7 minutes and ended up taking the stairs. Some co-workers even up on the 14th and 15th floors had done the same and traded that experience for a morning jog. Location is great - but as I tell people, especially those in a tourist mode looking to enjoy the Riverwalk - hotel location really means nothing when the point of the Riverwalk is to walk around and experience different areas. With good shoes and a good attitude about taking 10-15 minutes-plus to walk somewhere, the Alamodome is also strutting distance from here.

“Ok hotel--evenly in the middle” The Magnolia suffers from its location in Dallas. Sure, Neiman Marcus is one block down, but so what? The best thing about the Magnolia is Jereboam across the street, but that is closed on Sundays, so if you want to eat on Sunday, bring lots of snacks, because nothing within walking distance, except maybe a Togo's, is open. The room has intermittent wireless Internet access (on lower floors only), and zero room service. The beds are good, but the rooms are a bit empty, and there are no Kimpton type amenities, like stereos, cds, and novels. I found it difficult to keep the room at a decent temperature, and frequently wanted to run down to the street to gulp real air. But the jacuzzi is lovely, and the lounge on the second floor is nice. A decent hotel in a dull downtown, although I had hoped for more.

“It's all about the LOCATION!” I booked two rooms here for one night. We took an overnight trip to NYC to see the Christmas decorations. We were delighted with the hotel's location! It was just two blocks away from The Rock and Saks. It was also within walking distance of Times Square and Central Park. The staff was very friendly! My children were each given candy canes when we checked in and every single time they walked by the front desk and smiled (much to their delight) We were able to get hot chocolate and coffee in the mid-afternoon too. The rooms were small but very clean. The only thing that bothered me was the fact that the window had a sheer curtain and only one very small section of drape so the room was pretty light all night. The drape did not cover more then 1/4 of the window. That was rather strange. The other room did not have a window so that was not a problem. Breakfast was good. We were down at 8:00 am and did not have trouble finding a table. It did fill up rather quickly after we were seated. There is a deli almost next door that offered a tasty and inexpensive lunch. Although we were able to get a taxi from Penn Station to the hotel, we were unable to get a taxi back to Penn. A very helpful staff member stood in the street for a good 20 minutes trying to hail us a cab but the taxi drivers only wanted to take trips to the airport. It was the Friday right before Christmas so I really should not have been surprised. It took us about 30 minutes to walk to Penn so that wasn't too bad. Of course the taxi issue was not something that the hotel could do anything about. They tried their best.

“Such a place, such a location!” Great place, great room, great location. Even though there was a big meeting going on (Rainbow Girls in all their enormous gowns) the only consequence for us was slow elevators. Ballroom is amazing, shops on ground floor a nice throwback. Lake views from upper floors -- we were on 17 I think -- are worth it. Concierge advice about restaurants etc was excellent. Definitly would return.

“Great Price for the Location” You will not find a more affordable, family-friendly hotel in this part of DC. This hotel is in the heart of most of the things you want to see in DC, just a short walk to the White House, the Mall, lots of restaurants, and a Metro stop. The hotel is very basic and shows some wear and tear. The rugs on the 10th floor where we stayed are long past their prime. But our room was spacious, clean and quiet. After a long day of touring around the city we came back to a great night's sleep. Like other reviewers, we ate breakfast at the nearby Waffle Bar across from Ford's Theater. It was another great value, serving a hearty breakfast at excellent prices. The staff at the hotel was accomodating and efficient. They stored our bags for just the cost of a gratuity (a MUCH better deal than the rip off baggage storage room at Union Station). I highly recommend this hotel for families on a budget.

“Excellent!” This hotel is a great option with a great location. It is very clean, the elevators are very fast and the staff was extremely friendly. I would definitely recommend this property to anyone looking to stay in the Copley Square area.

“Overpriced and impractical” While I wanted to like this hotel in this incarnation, it was not a comfortable hotel to stay at. The lobby had no place to sit so several of us ended up sitting on a hard stone fireplace while waiting. Lobby was also dark. The room, although with large windows, was poorly designed for work or comfort and the bathroom wa minuscule with no counterspace for toiletries. The closet area was very small and designed so you could not unpack or see what was in your suitcase since the light was blocked by the clost insert. The tv remote did not work from the bed because the tv was angled badly. The lighting to read or work was entirely insufficient

“Very expensive Hyatt Place” It's obvious that the hotel has had a very recent makeover so it is clean and tidy but nothing special. Front desk staff are great - couldn't help enough. The room is OK but small compared to other HP properties I have stayed at and the sound proofing is only adequate - there is construction work across the road and they started before 6AM. No pool but can use the Hilton pool across the road. No Business Centre but 3-4 high spec PCs and printers are available. Breakfast was very good and was constantly refreshed - this is a huge improvement that Hyatt have made. But for a fairly average hotel a single night at the AAA rate plus parking plus the multitude of taxes was over $220 - thats just not reasonable.

“Comfortable hotel, near CLT” Stayed three nights on a Priceline bid. This was the third time I stayed at this hotel. Located just a few minutes drive from CLT and a responsive shuttle helps that happen. Hotel itself could use some TLC but, in general, it's in good shape. Breakfast is not on par with other breakfast included chains such as Wingate or Holiday Inn Express. Pool was not filled so can't comment on it. Fitness center has minimal equipment but appears not to be used much by guests. I'd like to comment on past reviews stating that this property is located in a "bad neighborhood". As I said, I've stayed here three times over the past few years and cannot understand where the "bad neighborhood" rating comes from. Yes, there is an unattractive strip mall across the street that is frequented by local people of color but that doesn't make it a "bad neighborhood". And, yes there is a Shoney's in front of the hotel and I'll admit that Shoney's is one step down from Denney's. But that doesn't make it a "bad neighborhood". I can only guess that some reviewers are uncomfortable in neighborhoods where not everyone looks like them. SAD.

“Surprise Birthday Trip - Awesome” Should of written this review when it was fresh now that a year and half of past and the memory seems to get a little foggier each year. I spent a lot of time review and deciding on what type of hotel (almost went w/Sofitel) for this surprise birthday trip. Couldn't of been happier w/the decision. This boutique hotel has tons of charm and the staff especially Derick Speight went out of their way to make this trip memorable and special for my wife. We felt very safe in the area and you could walk 3-5 blocks to lots of restaurants and things to see and of course the metro makes getting around super easy. Would be nice if the place was a little closer to a stop but the hotel was built first. If we get another chance to come back to the DC area this place will at the top of the list.

“Nothing Special” This hotel was adequate, but nothing special, in my opinion. It was adequately clean, safe, and in decent repair for a relatively older property. As usual, I cannot comment on the breakfast, business center, fitness center, or swimming pool, as I did not use any of these. I did have one big negative. The Internet connection was horrendous and completely unusable. It was no faster than 56k Dial-Up. Connection was no better in lobby or any other public/common area of hotel. In the year 2012, this is inexcusable. A front desk employee tried to tell me that the hotel's only modem was broken and this was why the speeds were so slow. If the hotel's only modem (very unlikely) were broken, the speed would be zero. Quality Internet connections do not seem to be a priority at most hotels, as is the extreme case with this property. Assuming the rest of a hotel is clean, safe, and good repair, this business traveler will stay at a lodging property that is concerned with equipping its guests with adequate Internet speeds and reliability. Overall, I paid $119/night for several nights. This is way overpriced for value received. $89/night would be more like it, in my opinion.

“A little below average” The good thing about this hotel is location. It's right on Magnificent Mile (Michigan Avenue) so if you like shopping, this may be the right one. However, The Allerton Hotel did not meet my expectation at all. I booked a double junior suite and expected to get a nice, if not, a quite nice room. Turned out, the room was pretty ugly looking. The wall was painted yellow. Mind you it's not the yellow you see in the photo gallery on the hotel's website. If you really want to see how your room would look like, check out the hotel's virtual tour. It looks the closest to the real thing. The staff were ok. Though, the concierge was excellent.

“Great deal in a great neighborhood” We spent a Friday night at this hotel, which is located on the edge of Cow Hollow and the Marina District. The room was spotlessly clean and pretty large for a budget hotel. The man at the check-in desk was very friendly and helped us with directions around the neighborhood. A huge plus is that each room gets a free covered parking spot. This hotel was very reasonably priced, and the area has a ton of bars and restaurants. It's a bit off the beaten path in relation to most tourist attractions... But honestly, you could stay here and take a cab down to SOMA or the Embarcadero and back and still have more money leftover than if you were to stay at a hotel in one of those neighborhoods. My next trip to San Francisco I am definitely staying here rather than one of those exorbitantly priced hotels downtown.

“Excellent Value for the Price (in Manhattan)” Small hotel on West 24th Street between 6th and 7th Avenues. Typical NYC hotel in terms of room size, tight hallways, etc. View out my window was right into apartment windows about 20 feet across an alley. Rooms have nice, modern decor with flat screen TV. I had a problem with the HVAC, but the hotel quickly sent up an engineer at 10:00 at night - he replaced the battery in the thermostat, and it worked fine after that. Nice complementary breakfast buffet with scrambled eggs and bacon... plenty of room to sit in the nicely maintained breakfast area. Hotel is one to two blocks from the #1 subway line; $2.50 for a single ride ticket. No problem staying here again, except no restaurant... you have to go out to eat dinner (or order delivery).

“Great hotel, good location” Stayed here for two nights to attend a conference at the DC Convention Center. The hotel is a few blocks from the Convention Center -- it's not too bad of a walk. I really liked the hotel decor -- it was perfect for Chinatown. Lots of great shopping and restaurant choices nearby, and the metro is just a short walk away. The free breakfast was good - they had breakfast sandwiches you could heat up along with the standard free breakfast fare.

“Lacked friendly first class service” We chose to stay at a small hotel because we did were looking for a hotel with less crowds. We anticipated we would get better service in a smaller hotel, than some of the other larger high rise hotels. We did not experience very good service at the Talbott Hotel. When we checked Irena seemed very robotic and aloof. The front desk clerks were neither welcoming nor gracious. The lobby is small and the front desk is just a few feet from the front door. Each time we came into the hotel we were never greeted nor even received a smile from the staff, just a blank stare and gaze. The front desk staff was chilly and stiff, no greetings, no smiles and no personality. They had difficulty answering simple questions or requests. On the other hand the bellman Perry was great. He was sociable and very service oriented. He was aware of what is going on in the area. He recognizes the guests and he offered suggestions about things to do in the immediate area, and where to eat in the neighborhood. He is authentic and he even asked us upon our return “how was that restaurant?” Tim the concierge was also supportive. He gave us 10% discount coupons for shopping at the major department stores. We had the largest suite. We requested a rollaway (extra charge) when we made our reservation and we had to ask five different times to have the rollaway bed delivered to our room before it came after 10PM. When the rollaway finally came we had to call back the front desk because they did not deliver a blanket or pillow with the bed. What made our Talbott hotel experience most disappointing was that we may have never received any housekeeping unless we had asked to have our room cleaned. We were out of our room from 8AM and when we returned to our room at 4PM the rooms had not been cleaned. We called the front desk to ask to send someone. The maid rushed to clean our room while we had to shower and change for the evening. The room itself was pleasant. It did have a moldy smell and some Frabreez would have been nice to bring along since the windows do not open much. We were next to a noisy neighbor and the walls were thin. We really liked staying in this area of Chicago but expected first rate service. The service was very weak and unacceptable for this class of hotel.

“011100110011 - Silicon Valley Decor - Cool!” One night here was enough before my eyes got over the 70's decor (it was new decor too) - the Hotel has a retro style to it which is pretty cute. Unfortunately the aircon unit in my room had not been replaced since 1972 so it was quite a din until I moved rooms. Certainly a convenient place to stay - right near the tech museum. Onto my pro's and con's Con's Aircon needs upgrading, Beds average. Pro's Great for tour groups or families. Pretty funky environment. I 'could' be back.

“Impressed with the renovations noted” Stayed here previously in April 2010 in the South Tower. That room was a huge corner room on the top floor but had been only partially refreshed. It was pleasant enough, totally acceptable for a Sheraton in my opinion. This stay, we had room 2122 in the North Tower. It was a relatively tiny room and tiny bathroom, but the room had an amazing view towards the Charles River and Cambridge. Room and bathroom had been extensively and tastefully renovated. TV didn't work correctly during our stay (remote wouldn't control the TV) and was never fixed even after calling about it. Bed was wonderful--what I expect from Sheraton Sweet Sleeper bed unlike my experience at the Sheraton Portsmouth the night before. Because of Hurricane/Tropical Storm Irene, we were forced to cut our two-night stay short and checked out at 5:30 p.m. after the first night. Having prepaid for the hotel in advance, I wasn't expecting any concession from the hotel. However, at our unexpected early checkout I was told we would be credited one of the two nights because of our trip interruption due to the approaching storm. If the credit makes it through to my credit card, I will be more than pleased. On the other hand, the hotel did charge me for parking ($44) which was supposed to be included in my rate. However, I didn't ask for a correction to the bill since they were giving me a credit for the one-night forfeited. We didn't eat at the hotel, not even breakfast. During our last stay in 2010 breakfast was expensive and mediocre quality--didn't want to chance it again this time.

“ottimo rapporto qualità/prezzo” Abbiamo pernottato per 4 notti in agosto in questo hotel/residence. Eravamo al 23° piano, camera molto ampia, abbastanza silenziosa, pulita con cucina attrezzata e bagno. Nella nostra camera non c'era nessun odore di umidà come scritto in altre recensioni. Sala colazioni piccola ma abbiamo sempre trovato posto. L'unico appunto che possiamo segnalare è l'aria condizionata un pò rumorosa ma noi l'accendavamo quando non eravamo in camera perchè poi non era più necessaria e sicuramente le camere ai piani bassi sono rumorose come in tutti gli hotel americani. Lo consiglio per il buon rapporto qualità/prezzo e la posizione.

“More like a 4.5 hotel!” If I could give this hotel a 4.5, I would have. There are only a few little flaws in the hotel that deducted a few points. Stayed in Seattle the first weekend in November and chose The Edgewater due to its proximics to most of the major attractions in the city. We were without a car and are walkers so this was a plus. If you are not the hotel offers a free shuttle that runs every hour and will take you anywhere withing two miles. We only took the shuttle once and realized they don't pick you up (not a problem in our case) but...if they do they never mentioned it!! The hotel is older and at first glance may not be up to everyones perfection but it is well kept and does actually sit out over the water. It's next to the cruise line building, near the Aquarium, the wharf, and ferry buildings. Not to mention Pike Market and some amazing restaurants. The hotel offers wonderful views from the sitting area which comes complete with fireplace and from the lounge as well. Our room was a water front room and the views were wonderful to awake to. Our room was of decent size with comfortable bed, warm gas fireplace. docking station for and iPod and big bathroom. That bathroom was one of our low points. Our photos showed a soaking tub and I requested one when I called to confirm. I did not receive one, rather a very nice walk in shower. I was really looking forward to the soaking tub as we were staying there for three nights! Another disappointment was the cost of INTERNET. In this day and age I really do expect free Internet?! Most of our better hotels do offer it! Our room was right near the railway so we had a constant rumble. If this is going to bother you, ask for a room closer to the main of the building. I don't know how the rooms on the upper levels might fare with the sounds. Everyone at the hotel was very pleasant. Room service was fast and efficient. The food was very good as well. The one thing I would advise is if you ask for a cab; don't let them tell you to come down and let them call. You will sit for twenty minutes. Tell the front door man you will be down for a cab in ten! It's a $32 cab ride to the airport or a $40 town car ride. So if you are a tipper ~ you do the math?! It was clean, comfy, good food, good views...and a walk to everywhere! Enjoy. I'd go back in a heart beat!

“My "go-to" hotel in Dallas” I visit Dallas for work often and have stayed here over 8 times. I personally like this hotel for a few reasons: * I get an amazing rate on hotwire.com every time * Convenient location for my work * Rooms are huge - feels like a mini apt * Have never had bad service (although bartender was once a little off putting) * Front desk people (especially Fancy) are courteous, helpful and welcoming * Modern design but comfortable * Parking attendants are always hustling and professional (and funny) * Free WiFi - very important when you are a business traveler * sometimes when you book a room on a discount site, you may get a bad room or lowered service - NEVER at this hotel. I am sure this place is not for everyone but for the rate I get this is an amazing deal for me. The only problem I have ever had was that I had a broken bed - literally broken. They moved us promptly to a corner suite and checked in on us the next day. Am staying again next week.... and recommended it to all my coworkers.

“Man liebt es oder hasst es” Das Hudson Hotel in New York ist an der Upper East Side gelegen, in der Nähe des Columus Circle sowie des Central Parks. Das Hotel besticht durch sein Design sowie durch sein sehr junges Publikum. In diesem Haus ist in der Regel 24 Stunden Party angesagt. Tagsüber in der Lobby, nachts im Innenhof. Die Zimmer sind SEHR klein aber reichen zum Schlafen und sind sauber. Wer damit zurecht kommt bekommt ein gutes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis für NYC.

“Excellent location to Financial District / WTC Memorial / Battery Park!” Basic but new and clean rooms. Great rates and very friendly staff. I love this hotel as it is dependably good! Two things though: 1) No hair conditioner 2) Bring earplugs because the construction on the WTC Memorial can be heard throughout the night (literally the entire night)

“No major issues. Average hotel.” Stayed here on business recently. Overall, was a nice stay, but nothing all that special. Perhaps I've gotten a little spoiled at other properties lately! Checkin Smooth and efficient. Very quick. Probably the most friendly of staff members I encountered. Room Was upgraded to a junior suite. Really surprised how tired the room looked. I thought all of the Marriott's recently remodeled. These guys got the new beds and technology stuff, but the carpets were still really worn. No issues with housekeeping. Concierge Lounge Decent selection at breakfast and happy hour. VERY small seating area -- not really setup for breakfast -- there are maybe 5 tables total -- the rest are more lounge areas which aren't that functional for breakfast. In 3 days, never once did anyone in the lounge speak to me. Even when I was the only person in the lounge! I don't think I've ever had this happen in any other property! Overall, was just ok. Probably would stay again.

“Trendy oasis in a busy city” I stayed here for 2 nights in April. I checked in very late (midnight) as my plane was late arriving in LA. I was greeted by a very friendly valet who carried my bags in for me. Check in was efficient and friendly and I was upgraded due to my Gold status with SPG. Now that was nice! The room was great - a two room suite. The bedroom was a little small but fine. It was very clean. I had all meals there and the food is excellent. I even when back there for dinner after I had checked out before getting on the plane again. It was pretty trendy but not over the top. I really liked it and wished I could have stayed longer. I would 100% stay there again!

“Why stay anywhere else?” When I walked into Palmer House, I felt like I was walking into a movie set. It was so luxurious and beautiful. Grandiose and amazing. I paid a pre-negotiated rate for $85 and never was I treated like someone who paid a negotiated rate. I took advantage of an upgrade to a double room in the executive suite on floor 23 for an additional $55. The room was wonderful. I am a HUGE fan of two beds/two baths. The room had two closets, safe, bathrobes, a flat screen and IPOD clock. Amazing showers and pressures. The beds were very comfortable. The only thing that could have made the room better was free wifi.... HOWEVER on the exec floor there were computers available. Also on the exec floor was a bartender, free non alcoholic beverages, snacks, appetizers, and breakfast. The parking is ridiculous but we paid overnight parking up the street for $12. The hotel is next door to Miller Pub which had great food for the value and a wider variety than I thought for pub food. Location.....wonderful for sites and shopping. I DEFINITELY will stay at Palmer House again.

“Bellissimo” L'hotel è di gran lusso, circondato da un bellissimo giardino e con una splendida grande piscina, che abbiamo apprezzato tantissimo, data la temperatur quasi torrida. Ottima la dotazione di sdraio. L'accoglienza è stata ottima, anche nei confronti della bimba, cui è stato consegnato uno zainetto con dei giochini. In camera abbaimo trovato il latte e i biscotti per la bimba. La camera bellissima, pulita e con un grande bagno in marmo. Vicino al centro commerciale Galleria.

“Clean, Comfortable Room” The bed was so comfy. Location could be better if your are tourist. The hotel is well decorated and kept. Quiet and relaxing. I would definitely recommend this hotel to friends and revisit this hotel.

“Perfectly fine, but come on...” I stay in Los Angeles all the time. I stayed at the Orlando once. It was perfectly fine. The desk staff is WAY above average on the NICE meter, which is why so many people rave about this hotel. Truth be told, if you're looking for a great boutique hotel, this is not it. It's a dressed up Quality Inn. Nicer furniture and fixtures, but the rooms are cookie cutter. In addition to the uber friendly desk staff, the chief advantage to the Orlando is the proximity to hip/cool restaurants. The rooms DO have balconies, which give them an automatic 4 stars from me, but the rooms largely face the very busy W 3rd st. There are far more interesting boutique hotels in LA for similar money, but the Orlando is absolutely a respectable choice.

“A Mixed Bag in the City of Brotherly Love” Our stay at the Sheraton in downtown Philadelphia was a mix of the pleasant and not so pleasant. Check-in was efficient and I was given a room on a high up Starwood floor. I noticed that a layer of dust covered the furniture in the room and the toilet did not work. Although the view was nice I didn't want to deal with hotel repair people and asked for another room. Although I am a Starwood member, I was given a non Starwood room much lower with no view. They told me there were no better rooms available. Later, my son and daughter in law arrived ( also Starwood members ) and were given a suite when they asked for an upgrade. I was so exhausted from traveling that I didn't create a fuss. I would like to point out in this forum that the front desk staff had a chance to do the right thing for one of their members by recognizing the hassle I went through and giving me a nicer room to compensate me. Instead they didn't bother. The hotel is a bit "frayed around the edges" but basically nice. It is within walking distance to the new Barnes museum as well as a number of other great sites. The restaurant is decent but expensive and the lounge area is pleasant, but in need of a furniture upgrade. I would return, but only if I could use points for my stay.

“Great location” Stayed here 6-24 to 6-26 for 3 nights. Great location. Staff is very friendly and helpful. It is only about 15 min. from Times Square and the theatre district. Lots of room for 3 ladies with lots of shopping bags. Not too expensive when you really do need to take a cab, as you are very close to the middle of Manhattan. Loved the roof top. The breakfast is more than enough to send you on your way for the day. If you love a big breakfast though you'll need to go somewhere else. Beds comfortable, and we did not have a noise issue. We were near the back facing a parking lot. I'd rather get some sleep and take in the views while I'm awake. Loved the city and certainly this hotel. Would come back again!!

“not my favorite marriott hotel” We waited over 2 hrs in the lobby for our room to be available when checkin time was at 4pm. Front desk help were snooty and couldn't have cared less. Finally got to our room around 6pm, but someone had smoked in it, so now we needed to change rooms again. They also had messed up our reservation dates. As a loyal Marriott rewards customer, this place was a HUGE disappointment. It is too big and impersonal. Room service dishes were left in hallways for 4 days until I called the front desk and complained. Only saving grace was the hotel's prime location. If given a choice, I would NOT stay here again.

“Lovely Hotel” A reasonably priced, clean Hotel. Very Friendly staff, especially the Concierge who would go out of his way to help. The room was a good sized room and the cleaners were very friendly and did a great job. The restraunt was decently priced and the food tasted good. The only bad thing I can think of with this hotel is the price of a beer in the bar, more expensive than most. Great location, a short walk into the centre of Georgetown and a bus journey to Washington DC Mall.

“Good 'ole hotel, great location, cute dog” The Fairmont Copley is one of those grade old hotels that every big city has. The rooms are a little small, but they've been renovated with the expected amenities. I had a 'larger' room that was still on the small side. So make sure you try to upgrade to get a decent sized room, but this is often the case with big city old hotels. The location can't be beat. i'd stay here over the newer Westin, Marriott or Sheraton in the area. The service was a little under par for a Fairmont. But the Fairmont Copley has something that no other hotel in the area has - the beautiful dog (black lab) who hangs out in the lobby to greet guests - what a sweet dog.

“Good Location” I was here with a friend, and we both liked the location. The rooms were just adequate, nothing too special. We had two double beds, both sleep number beds, but only one of them worked properly (mine). My travel partner could not get the bed number to change on hers. Lots of places to eat nearby, and lots of shopping close as well.

“Great location” After reading some reviews, we had some concerns about the room and staff. But to our suprise, we had a great stay, with friendly staff helping us check our bags early and returning later to our rooms 9th flr. We didn't get a free upgrade,but the rooms were very decent and beds comfy. The pillows could be better , but we agree the hotel was alot better than some other high end ones that we have stayed at in Union Sq. on past visits. Rooms were large/ Bathrooms didn't have air vent, which caused mirrors to steam up alot. But price was great through priceline for the room/location. Otherwise asking $200 for standard room was high for this hotel. Especially during the renovation. For those who complain alot, please pay more for the upgrade and realise that you get what you bargain for. I would return to this hotel for future visits when the renovation is done because of the location.
“Great for inexpensive family stay” Well you can get 2 beds or a King but still small rooms. Rooms were cozy and Clean. Service was Great and amenities was a nice plus.

“Spacious downtown Baltimore hotel” We have been staying here for many years. The accommodations are one-bedroom suites with lots of space. The staff is very accommodating and helpful and the price is right. The rooms include a full kitchen. You are within easy walking distance to the Inner Harbor and Cambden Yard. I almost feel like I am in an apartment instead of a hotel - very relaxing. There is also a small deli and carry out near the lobby. It is also a very quiet hotel. Fitness facilities are nearby.
“Half of Block from the the theatre!” We stayed in Hampton Inn for 2 night - as we had tickets to "The Book of Mormons". Hilarious show, very nice hotel.

“Quality hotel and convenient to Staples Center” Top of the line for the Sheraton brand. Business atmosphere, but rooms are spacious and upgraded. Not much in the way of views, but it's LA, so not a priority. The best part is the location with 10 min to Staples Center and LA Live dining area, it's ideal. Easy and hassle-free stay. Expect to pay $32 for valet parking overnight.

“Great Place In a Great Location” After leaving Tucson and staying the night in a regular "Holiday Inn" in Phoenix (the worst ever,) I was weary about downgrading to the Holiday Inn Express brand. I was surprised by the amazing service and polite staff at this hotel. From the moment my family arrived, we were greeted, treated with respect and afforded every amenity available without hesitation. Upon entering our room, it was extremely clean, its smelled clean and was neatly arranged. Our view out the windown was of downtown San Diego and the front door of the 'El Cortez' hotel. It was beautiful. The only drawback to this place was paying $12.00 a day for parking. Its location, however made that understandable. You are located smack dab in the middle of the gaslight district and withing a few blocks walking distance from everything including, clubs, restaurants and sports stadiums as well as the train that takes you into the rest of the city. The breakfast buffet was well maintained although on the weekend when it was crowded, it wasn't always stocked immediately. i'll give it to the staff though, they did their best to keep it stocked as the place was packed and human nature dictates gluttony instead of compassion. Not too bad though. Overall, I would definately recommend this hotel to friends, family and anyone else who is interested in a reasonably priced hotel in a great area.

“Calm and Relaxing Hotel” I stayed here with my husband for part of a 5 day getaway to Seattle. Upon arrival the service from the doormen to check-in was excellent. Very welcoming and not too formal. Our room was quietly luxorious. Just a beautiful and comfortable room to relax. As others have stated the location just can't be beat. So close to the market and lots of terrific restaurants. Art is a nice place to have a drink with friendly bartenders. I asked doorman for a recommendation for a place close by to get a drink and he recommended the ZigZag, which we had been to before and loved, so I knew I could trust him not to send us to an overly touristy place. I would definately put this at the top of my Seattle hotel list.

“I love Westin!” I'm so glad I decided to splash out a little and book this hotel. As I was travelling alone I wanted to make sure I was somewhere safe and fairly central. The location is excellent, in walking distance of the Gaslamp quarter, Seaport Village, public transport stops and the ferries. My room was very clean and was well maintained during my stay. Toiletries and complimentary water bottles were replaced daily. Hotel staff especially the concierges were extremely helpful in planning my days and even came up with discount coupons for some attractions. I saved $20 on Seaworld! The rooftop pool was an added bonus after long days on my feet. I loved the elevators on the outside of the building - brilliant views on the way up to my room! I also felt safe walking alone at night back to the hotel. Overall I couldn't have had a better stay!

“This Silver Cloud doesn't live up to others” Well...chose this Silver Cloud based off our other great visits to Silver Clouds (Bellevue and Stadium). I was a little disappointed in this one for various reasons which I will mention. It served its purpose for our overnight stay, but I booked so far in advance, I should have just chose somewhere closer to what I needed for cheaper. Maybe I am being a little picky on this visit, but I have come to love the Silver Clouds and this one fell short. Check in: easy, no issues. Parking is free which is nice but getting even a compact car in to a spot is like threading a needle...I was just glad not to have any dents when I got back. Rooms: I was fine with the room and impressed with the space. King bed, fridge, relaxing chair, table, etc. Didn’t see a safe anywhere unless I’m blind. I like having a safe these days. But the room was clean, although there were only two towels in the room. Really, two towels? Usually these days you get four. Probably because they were actually full they shorted to make up for it. The hallways leading to the room is like a maze and I have never seen anything like it in a hotel. It was confusing and not enough signs saying where rooms, elevators, etc were. They have a free shuttle you have to sign up for. They have 14 seats on it which is fine unless the hotel is full. We decided to cab it anyway, but front desk couldn’t get a hold of a cab for us. We walked down towards the restaurants and found one. Breakfast: free breakfast is always nice, but whoever designed this hotels breakfast area should be slapped! And it is obvious this hotel is not prepared to be full. It was an absolute cluster. Not enough seating, not enough food, not enough dishes, etc..people everywhere, no rhyme or reason to how you line up to get food, people shoving in from every which way. Not good. Like I said the room served its purpose but I’ll pass on this one in the future. oh and if theres a pizza flyer in there from Pizza & Pasta Roma don't order from them..got delivery, screwed it up twice..never did get the right pizza

“Parking and Hard Beds” The Good: Beautiful interior. Very stylish. Excellent banquet/facility rooms. Good breakfast. Polite helpful desk staff. Terrific workout room, in fact one of the best workout areas I have been in. The work out area is spacious and their machines (treadmills) have a tv screen on them. The view of the pool from the workout room is peaceful. The rooms are very clean, spacious and well appointed. The Bad: The hotel is in a prime location, unfortunately this is part of the problem. It is on Colorado Blvd. A very hard street to traverse in the best of conditions but they were doing road work/construction while we were visiting. It wasn't busy at just rush hour but anytime after 11 AM. Each time we left the hotel it was an ordeal. The Ugly: Parking? What parking. You were FORCED to valet park. You did not have the option of parking your own car in an open parking lot on the property. We felt compelled to tip the valet when we gave them our keys. It was uncomfortable to say the least. When we booked this room I didn't see anything about the construction going on directly in front of the hotel entrance. It was inconvenient. It was an eyesore to look at while waiting to get our car for the day's activities. We saw dumptrucks and tractors working about 100 feet away from the entrance to the hotel. The beds were like rocks. They were supposed to be adjustible beds (hard to soft, etc,) and they didn't adjust at all. We talked to another guest staying in the hotel and he said he had the same issue in his room. We didn't sleep well while staying at this hotel. Overall impression: Hard bed. Difficult to navigate the roads (Colorado Blvd.). Forced valet. It will be a better experience once they finish the parking lot and subsequent shopping center planned for the same area.
“Excellent” Pricey, but excellent in every way. Rooms, staff and atmosphere are all wonderful.

“small rooms, pre-historic bathrooms, old tube TV” Utterly forgettable business hotel. The standard rooms are very small (okay, it's Manhattan...) and the bathroom size, decor and appliances belong to another era. Room was equipped with an old, tired, flickery TV. The gym is windowless and sad, but thankfully it has loads of treadmills. The positive sides are the location and the impeccable standards of service and cleanliness. Overall, it depends on what you pay. For $200-250 you cannot go wrong with the InterConti, but pay any more than that and you will likely be sorely disappointed.

“nice suprise” Booked this hotel thinking it was another Hilton property - glad I made the mistake. This is right on campus and very nice - the junior suite rooms are very modern and a step above for a Hilton. Staff was young but very nice. There is no fitness center at the hotel - you are given a pass to the university wellness center. It is a great facility but one that does not open until 6 AM. Being on east coast time with an office that opens at 8 AM and a longer distance runner, would have liked to worked out a bit earlier to log a few more miles but it seemed to be a fair trade in this case. Would stay here again if I was in the area.

“Lo consiglio” L'hotel si trova di fronte al centro congressi di Boston per cui per arrivare in centro o si prende la navetta (ogni 15 min dal lunedi al venerdì dalle 9 alle 7) gratuita oppure si fa una passeggiata di una 20 min - comoda- La struttura è grande, moderna con un buon bar-ristorante interno. La prima camera prenotata tramite booking la Delux aveva una vista interna - muro- con arnie di api per il miele sul terrazzo sottostante ma con 25 $ in più abbiamo effettuato un upgrade e la situazione è cambiata totalmente, 16° piano, camera più spaziosa e vista sul mare. Il personale gentile e disponibile, lo consiglio!!

“OK for a one night stand” My travel schedule required a one night stand (haha - I wish) at LAX so I shopped around. Radisson was about the cheapest in my quick survey. It's OK for this purpose. The room is clean and very functional, except for a broken desk chair. The bed is a little hard. Free internet access. The sound proofing is very good. I am overlooking the corner of Sepulveda and Century, and two active runways, and can't hear a thing. Maybe I'm becoming hard of hearing. However, the heater makes loud clicks when it goes on so you probably want to turn it off at night. The restaurant downstairs is very pleasant and surprisingly good. It does not seem like an airport establishment at all, more credit to them. I recommend this if you are stuck at LAX for one night - good value.

“Great hotel” We stayed at the Beacon Hotel for Valentine’s Day and were very pleased. I originally booked a corporate quarters king room through the hotel @ $219/night. They allowed us an early checkin, and to our surprise we were upgraded to a one bedroom suite (room 425) at no extra cost. The room was very spacious, modern, with a boutique/feng shui vibe. There was a full kitchen (stove, micro, fridge, pots/pans), and adjoining living room that had a huge flat screen TV, dvd player, and working gas fireplace. The separate bedroom also had a flat screen tv and long windows which wrapped around the room, and a very comfy king bed. The bathroom was enormous, had nice amenities, a walk-in shower, and was very clean. Staff were very courteous and knowledgeable. We didn’t eat at the Beacon's restaurant, but ordered room service which was very good. The location is great, walkable to the Metro's red line, and there are plenty of restaurants/bars/lounges to choose from within walking distance. All in all, I’d highly recommend the Beacon and would stay there again.

“Just okay....” Stayed two nights at this hotel earlier in the week. Nice rooms, comfy beds and excellent service. The one bad thing I noticed was that my bathroom was not that clean upon arrival. I would have changed rooms, but I had already unpacked. Overall, for a Four Seasons Hotel it's just okay, but the service is above average, so I think I would consider staying here again in the future.

“Great value, quiet, comfortable, convenient” Needed a place to stay for one evening in midtown and chose this hotel largely from other reviews. It totally met and exceeded expectations. While the location is in a very busy corridor, once inside the property you can escape the street noise and hustle in a relatively low-key lobby. I asked for a quiet room and was not disappointed - while I did have to draw the drape to block out a flashing billboard it was pleasantly peaceful for the middle of Times Square. The hotel seems to cater to a mix of corporate guests as well as tourists - bell service and front desk were friendly and efficient. The bathroom by any standard, especially NYC, was terrific - a very large counter area with wooden tray to store toiletries, and a nicely tiled, large shower with seat. Everything was very clean. For those visiting not familiar with NYC, there are many options for quick dining in the immediate area including a very large Starbucks, several cafes and a Duane Reade with good, reasonably priced takeaway food items similar to UK Boots. Not to mention every chain restaurant imaginable within walking distance. Would definitely stay here again if the need arose. Liked the fact this was a Marriott property without the hectic feel and price of the Marquis flagship.

“A perfect combination of classic elegance and city chic.” Wow, what an amazing stay! This Firmdale “design hotel” is an intimate, 11 story, 86 guest room gem located in the heart of SoHo. The hotel is just the right size to offer exceptional personal service as well as seclusion. From the moment we entered the Crosby Hotel, we felt pampered by the wonderful staff. This standard of gracious personal service was the norm from all the hotel staff we encountered during our entire stay. It was just the right balance of attentiveness and privacy that’s really hard to describe, but I just know and appreciate it when I experience it. The hotel’s common areas, lobby, Drawing Room (guest lounge), Sculpture Garden (inner courtyard), restaurant and bar are very stylish, welcoming and tastefully decorated with original artwork and sculptures. If you visit here, make sure to get downstairs to check out the private event rooms, screening room and bar too. It’s very clear that a great deal of attention to detail was put into the design and decoration of this hotel’s common areas and guest rooms. The hotel is truly an intimate space in the middle of SoHo, akin to a peaceful, carefully designed, visually appealing art gallery. We booked a King “Luxury Room” for our 2-night stay. Although these are among the hotel’s smaller bedrooms at (350 square feet), the room was refined, comfortable and spotlessly clean. Our 4th floor room had a floor to ceiling window directly overlooking cobblestoned Crosby Street, and our room was very quiet. We heard no street noise or hallway noise during our entire stay. The room was attractively decorated with lots of natural light and an excellent King bed with soft sheets and very comfortable pillows. The bathroom was luxurious and impeccably clean. The marble and glass shower was amazing with water pressure approaching that of a medium-sized waterfall! The bathroom also had two pedestal sinks and a heated towel rack which were nice touches. The quality Miller Harris toiletries and Turkish bathrobes were nice touches too. The service and food at the Crosby Bar were wonderful too. On Friday night we sat on the terrace and ordered Mojitos and small plates from the bar menu. It was a great space to talk and unwind after our hectic journey to New York City. Our “Summer Promotion” room rate included complimentary English breakfast each morning (basically a $40 dining credit per person per day). The Full English breakfast offers a choice of 2 eggs any style with potatoes, roasted mushrooms and tomato, black pudding, sausage, bacon, fresh fruit, dates, figs, yogurt, granola, pastries, juice and coffee or tea. The breakfasts were too abundant to finish, but absolutely scrumptious nonetheless. The perfectly brewed Illy coffee they serve is delicious too. As frequent visitors to Manhattan, my wife and I prefer the more vibrant and dynamic “downtown” neighborhoods of Chelsea, Flatiron, NoLita, SoHo, TriBeca, Union Square and the West Village because of the many activities available. We also feel much less “touristy” in these neighborhoods. The Crosby Hotel is in an ideal location close to upscale shops, world-class restaurants, galleries, museums and the many cultural activities available around SoHo, NoLita and Greenwich Village. We’ve stayed all over Manhattan in some very nice boutique hotels over the past few years, and there’s no doubt that the Crosby Hotel is now our favorite by far. It’s truly a world-class property that perfectly combines classic elegance with city chic. The hotel provides its guests with superb service, charm, style, quality, cleanliness and complete attention to every detail. In fact everything about our stay at the Crosby Street Hotel was absolutely perfect and we thoroughly enjoyed our two wonderful nights of comfort and relaxation at this truly remarkable and beautiful hotel. This is our new standard for subtly sophisticated deluxe accommodations in Manhattan. The Crosby is a truly exceptional hotel and a remarkable value. We will definitely be back.

“good stay” Stayed here for a meeting, and the rooms were clean, the airport is close or nearby, and the people were friendly and helpful. I agree the hotel is "tired" but the beds were soft. Food was okay, nothing to brag about, so we walked over to the restaurants across from the hotel. To get to the restaurant, we had to walk down the street as the train separates the traffic and it is fenced. Would come back.

“Great Location - Great People” Kudos to the staff at this hotel, starting with Jose Rosales for getting me a room with a view of the Riverwalk! This is an expensive part of San Antonio to visit, but if you're going to indulge, this hotel is great place to stay - location can't be beat! I was there for a conference and the hotel's staff went out of its way to accommodate our large group. Food was really good. Some of the fare was a bit too "authentic" for my taste, but it gave me a chance to try some foods I never would have tried on my own. Hotel Kudos: rooms nicely decorated, self parking garage is right across the street, lobby is really nice and connects directly to the Riverwalk, lots of great restaurants closeby - though food at hotel was excellent too. Room for improvement: wireless internet was very inconsistent, thin walls, business center was a bit pricey.

“A Disgusting Dump Where People Can See Into Your Room!” First off, let me say that I'm a Starwood Preferred Guest Platinum member (highest tier in their frequest stay program) and was shocked at the room I stayed in at the Four Points Los Angeles International Airport hotel. I can't imagine what the room would've been like if a customer who is not a top tier frequent guest would be like. The room was located on floor 5, the Starwood Preferred Guest floor, and was tiny, the bath tub had mildew and the only window faced the hall were other guests walked right in front of it (see photos I posted). The fact that the only window faces an inside hallway meant that you had to keep the blinds closed or others could see into your room which also meant that you could not get any natural light nor get any fresh air. Since the window could not be opened, the only option for circulation is the air/heating conditioning which is loud. The mildew tub was truly disgusting and something that a good cleaning could remove. Do yourself a favor and do not stay at this Starwood Hotel not matter if you're a Starwood Preferred Guest or not. It's a disgusting dump.

“Modernized hotel in fabulous location with mostly amazing service” For those who don't know, the W used to be the Hotel Washington, a legendary & world-famous hotel. "The Godfather 2" was filmed there. It is deceiving b/c it is the same hotel on the outside, but with a completely modern interior, except they kept the original check-in desk off to the side. All the other historic touches are gone. You can't get a better location. Walking distance to everything in great weather or a short cab ride in foul or humid weather. If I'd written this after my 1st stay in November, the rating would have been off the charts. I stayed once more, and that (as well as some housekeeping shortfalls) knocked it back. I found the vast majority of staff to be incredible, helpful, kind, warm, inviting and fun. They remembered us, laughed with us and made sure our visit was spectacular. The rooms are large and the location is great. The hotel is smaller than the Willard, which is next door, making it more intimate. Housekeeping was lax and needs a wee chat. They forgot a lot of bathroom items - not only in my room but my brother's as well. Some of the "Wheels" staff that park cars were fine and friendly. Others were useless. One told us we couldn't leave the car for 20 mins without paying $25 when my parents dropped me off (my father was recovering from quadruple bypass and this was one of his first outings, and he wanted to see the hotel & my room). It was petty and stupid (especially as I'm a platinum). I told the front desk, and they immediately said not to worry - they recognized my status and need. The amenities for SPG platinum were great - including terrific upgrades. The room service is standard W. The upstairs/rooftop restaurant, which is legendary, was overpriced (way overpriced). Again, service was uneven, with some of the staff incredible, while others were indifferent. The biggest problem was the music was too loud during the weeknights when it wasn't crowded - almost as if they were trying too hard. The lobby was a zoo on Friday night with live music. Not sure why, but whatever. It is easy to get away from it. The Bliss Spa is incredibly small, but they are great there. Very responsive and welcoming. This W blows away London and San Fran and Westwood (one of the original). On par with Boston and NOLA French Quarter. Still think Hollywood is the best, however.

“Pretty good for what you pay” We got the room through Priceline so we only paid $80 per night. The hotel is Italian themed with nice attendants. Having valet parking was a big plus. The lobby and entrance of the hotel were kept clean at all times. Rooms were serviced everyday by polite employees. We definitely got what we paid for.

“Very nice hotel” This was a great hotel. It was a little difficult to find after a long night of flying but its a beautiful well managed property. The rooms were wonderful and the beds were very comfortable. The hotel is very pricey I actually paid more for a night at this hotel than a night at the JW Marriott in Palm Springs. The breakfast at the hotel was average, the food was very greasy and I had a hard time finishing my meal, my toast was burnt as well. All things considered the hotel was very nice, the front desk was extremely pleasant and helpful.

“Exterminator needed” This place has gone down hill considerably in the last year. They are in serious need of an exterminator with cockroaches on the second floow on the west side. Probably they are all over. The health department needs to take a look at this place.

“A Business Hotel” Spent one night at this hotel as we flying into Boston and then heading out the next morning. It was fine for that. I would not stay here for a vacation to Boston, however, as the location is fairly remote and there is not much there except the attached convention center. The whole area is under construction with new buildings and you could be anywhere - no feeling of being in Boston. If you are attending a convention it would be fine. The hotel is fairly new, clean, pleasant enough. It was quiet. Staff was fine. It feels like a scaled down Westin, though. Not as nice as some other properties in the same chain. The lobby bar is nice and has a decent wine selection. Oh, and the parking is very expensive.

“Another great Kimpton” I love, love, love these hotels. They always make me feel at home. The Helix was actualluy my first ever Kimpton visit and it definitely made me a believer in the Kimpton experience. I love the wine/beer hour in the evening. It gives time for business associates to wind down for the evening. I always look for Kimptons when I'm in DC now.

“very difficult to work with...........stay away” My colleagues warned me these people were difficult to work with. Said he would never stay here again. I had the same experience dealing with reservations. Lot's of controversy and discussions on obtaining my corporate rate for vacation. Don't know whether they'll honor it..."at the discretion of the front desk". Well, there are too many good hotels in seattle to deal with that. I'll take my business elsewhere. I'd do the same if I were you.

“Pleasant stay” We stayed here one night while we attended a wedding at another hotel two blocks away in Philadelphia. It's an older hotel, but very nicely decorated. Check-in was fast with pleasant staff. Room and bathroom were on the larger side and very clean and comfortable. We got a good rate on Travelzoo that included parking. I would definitely consider staying here again.

“Lovely place” We stayed for a couple of nights ilast mid-November. Room was well-appointed, quiet, and staff was very accomodating. We paid $79. a night through Priceline, making the Allegro among the least expensive hotels we have ever stayed in. Nice place--bravo to Kimpton!

“Excellent choice” Very nice hotel adjacent to Times Square. Accommodations were excellent, everything was in perfect working order. Room and hotel in general were immaculate. Very nice toiletries. Fast internet, $14.95 a day. Subway station next door, easy walking distance to most Broadway shows. Staff very friendly, check in was a breeze. It is pricy. Very quiet in room, bed was extremely comfortable. Highly recommend this property.

“Great location, great service, comfortable room” Just recently wrapped up a weekend in NY with my wife as we celebrated our wedding anniversary. The room was spacious, clean and comfortable. Service was excellent and you can't beat the location if you want to hit a show or have business in Midtown. When we're back in NY, the Pearl Hotel is definitely on the short list of places to stay. We'd love to come back.

“Orlando is a great locale” I usually stay at the Kimpton, but had to choose a hotel next to my meeting site. I was pleasantly surprised by Hotel Orlando. It has a 'brand new' feel to it and the rooms were spacious with great bathrooms. The hotel is located right by a street full of organic delis and cute boutique shops. There is Magnolias Bakery right across the street and only 2 blocks away from Beverly Center Shopping and Yogurtland. We stayed there for an entire week and ate at a different place every day within walking distance. The Churchill, the restaurant inside the hotel, is great and they have tables reserved for guests so you never have to wait during a busy Friday or Saturday night. I was very pleased with the service too, everyone was super nice. I will def stay here again

“customer service so terrible I never even got to book a room” Called the new W Boston to book a WOW suite for a specail anniversary. Got the run around from reservation clerk who tranferred me to someone else. That person told me to "hang on as the phone is ringing off the hook"- I waited for about 5 minutes when he returned he told me he couldn't reserve a WOW suite without going to corporate sales? On hold again, he came back and said could he call me back. Unbelievable. He NEVER called me back. This am I called and spoke to the W Boston, hotel reservations manager and he barely appologized. That is it for the W- what horrid service. I have booked at the Four Seasons instead.

“SW Hotel will do in a pinch if you need a place to stay and other reasonable options are limited” On a recent Friday night when hotels in San Francisco appeared to be almost fully booked, SW Hotel came to my attention. Upon checking out a room, I thought it was just fine and checked in for the night. Yes, the rooms are small and yes, the decor may be a tad dated for those who are picky about such things, but the price and the location cannot be beat should you happen to be in San Francisco during a period when hotel rooms in the area are in heavy demand. For some reason, the en suite john was absolutely massive in contrast to the small size of the bedroom. It looked like the owners had considered making it a wheelchair accessible bathroom, but either had a change of heart or did not bother completing the conversion. Do try to get a room that does not face Broadway, and if you are squeamish about staying in an area with packs of drunken merrymakers roving the streets at night, then you might do well to look elsewhere.

“Works for Me” Stayed here on the recommendation of a friend's husband. The grounds are well cared for with lovely plants and trees. Happy hours drinks and snacks are a nice and welcome touch. Breakfast is really some of the best I've had as far as free breakfast goes. But, when breakfast is very busy, they can run out of seating, food and plates/napkins/silverware/glasses. They do their best to keep up. The clean-up staff can be a little over-eager to clear tables (lost my plate a couple of times when going for a drink refill!). Front desk and cleaning crews are very friendly and helpful. The rooms are very clean but dated with some signs of wear and tear. The kitchen is great for when you just want to eat in. Noisiest dishwasher ever, though. Wifi works great. My only other issue was being awoken 2 out of 3 nights by people clomping up the stairs at 3 am in heels.

“Clean but shabby” This hotel is right in downtown Boston, near to everything. The staff was wonderful. They were professional, friendly and attentive. The room was fairly good size, and had the usual appointments and It was very clean . The air conditioning worked well, which was great considering it was in the 90's during my trip. The bed was very comfortable, but the pillows left something to be desired. They had pillows labled as "soft" and other labled as "firm", but you really couldn't tell the difference. I called for better firm pillows, and someone came right away, but the pillows weren't any firmer than the ones I had. The furniture looked like it was picked up at a consignment shop. It all had scrapes and gouges and looked like the finish was gone almost all over the front and sides. It was pretty shabby. I traveled here with several colleagues, and they all reported the same shabbiness with the furniture, as well as the pillow situation. The bathroom, although very clean, smelled very musty and moldy. There was breakfast avialable, which was very nice. Aside from the few negatives, this wasn't too bad a place to stay in Boston

“superb value and location” Great value for money, good sized room, all amenities, excellent location, concierge assistance first class. We stayed on a pre cruise stop over and on our return got off the ship 9am with a flight home at 10pm, they held our luggage all day at no charge. Thoroughly recommend this hotel

“Awesome stay” I stayed at this hotel for a government conference and the rate was $147/night. I understand that the normal rate exceeds $200/night. The food that was set up the conference was exceptional and surprising. When I made the reservation I joined the Omni Frequent customer program. It is free and well worth it. I recieved free internet daily, a daily complementary morning beverage (x2) delivered to the room free, and the view was amazing. The staff was very personable and great. I had a great stay here and would return again.

“Great location, service, and value” Good bang for the buck. The location was great; shops and restaurants within a few blocks. The room was clean and spacious. The bed was a bit too soft for my taste, but that's just my personal preference.

“Pricey, but has advantages!” Stayed here for one night and the locale could not have been better for doing lots of things. The room was very nice, and comfortable, and most importantly was clean and felt very safe there and in the area around the hotel. The Front Desk was very helpful at check in and out, and with questions. The concierge, Sheb (hopefully spelled correctly), was helpful with ideas when I called weeks before and could not have been more pleasant. Had exactly the same experience with him when we arrived. The other concierge we talked with was the exact opposite and made us feel like fools for our questions. The T is steps from the door, walked to Fenway in 20 minutes. The best thing is that Sheb told us that there was an Enterprise rental car place across the street and we got rid of the rental car there even though we picked it up at the airport and used for a few days outside of town. Hint: they did not charge us for dropping off in town and not at the airport, merely asked and they said "sure." Went to the rooftop pool but it was very crowded and did not stay. There is a very nice little restaurant at the corner, had a great reasonable breakfast there twice. Was fast and good.

“Excellent 4 star urban hotel” The Westgate is a true four star hotel. Doormen, handsome lobby, attentive and friendly front desk staff, and a good restaurant. The rooms are large and well furnished. (My son ranks hotels by the number of telephones, and my room had three.) Each of two adjacent guest rooms has a small private vestibule. Housekeeping was excellent and included nightly turn-down service. Good, though not extensive, set of bathroom amenities. Complementary Starbucks coffee is provided until 9AM in the bar. Wireless Internet is free. This is an urban hotel in the downtown section. The hotel is near Horton plaza, the in-city shopping center. It is a 40 minute walk to Balboa park and the Zoo, and surrounded by a number of restaurants. My only complaint is that you can hear the street noise, and my room overlooked the streetcar...but that is what you get with an urban hotel. This is a first-rate hotel in the traditional style and you will like it.

“Deterioration of A Good Hotel” This is my second review of this facility. I have stayed here four times this year and many times in prior years. This used to be my Hotel of choice in the area. The quality control in the Hotel has deteriorated, particularly in the housekeeping area. The issues are as follows: Four out of ten nights we did not get service. Housekeeping claimed the "Do not disturb" sign was out. That is true on some days, but never past 11 am, other days we left early and the sign was not out at all. Limited dusting and vacuuming during the entire stay. Hallways were not vacuumed during our entire 10 day stay. The Hot Tub was cold the entire time. Hallways very hot - Management said they are waiting for parts for HVAC system, but this has been an issue during our past three stays. Motion Detector in the room turns air off/down when not in the room. This causes a very hot room when returning at the end of the day and also in the morning, as the motion detector is above the entry door and it sees no movement during the sleeping hours in the bed rooms. Finally, we had uninvited guests ten minutes after we checked in, as our room was assigned to a second family. We did not have our chain in place, so they walked right in. The Hotel still has many good points, like location, the size and the lay-out of the suites, The friendly service of the front desk staff and good coffee.

“A good Time” Traveling with a group & staying most of last week at the Crowne Plaza, we couldn't get a reservation there the last night & moved to the nearby Time. Based on the very mixed reviews, I was expecting trouble. HOWEVER, I was plesantly surprised at the comfortable room & incredible location. The hotel has a strong European feel, so Americans expecting a large room will be disappointed. The bed was comfortable, the toiletries were above average, and the Sunday breakfast buffet was one of the best values we experienced our entire trip! The desk staff can be stiff & blunt...they need some lessons in US customer service. While checking in, we overheard the experiences of someone who arrived late the night before to find The Time oversold. While they were sent to the Roosevelt that night, it appeared the communication regarding availability the next day was not good. The bar on the 2nd floor is very loud. Fortunately, we were not on the 3rd floor, as it would have been miserable. Floors 4 and above are unusually quiet for NYC, however. Either the music needs to be turned down, or the 3rd floor shouldn't be rented. All in all, great value for the money, and therefore, the "above average" rating. During Christmas a Sat. night stay other places would have been 2x the cost. Superb location. Diamond in the rough, and with an increased focus on customer service (checking in plus the noise issue), this place could shine!

“Great value at the Renaissance” I booked this hotel through AA.com and got a 79usd fare per night. For that price, this hotel was highly satisfying. The location wasn ́t glamorous but it was very convenient, close to the airport (I arrived by midnight so that was a good thing) and with easy access to most freeways. The room wasn ́t particularly big but it was comfortable. The bed was what you would expect for a chain hotel like this one -great sleep. Bathroom and décor were just average. I didn ́t request much from the hotel staff so I can ́t say much about the service. I had a nice stay and I would definitely stay here again if I got a similar rate.

“Fun, unique hotel experience” This was a very nice hotel with all kinds of unique, special touches. The beds were incredibly comfy, the shower was excellent, the details all very upscale. (Granite countertops, flat screen TV.) And the location is fantastic. We stayed for two nights and didn't need a rent a car since we were a very short walking distance from everything worth seeing! The staff is friendly. Two complaints: thin walls (bring ear plugs if you're a light sleeper) and the gym wasn't available while we were there. So if you want a place with a gym, call before you book to make sure you can workout.

“Hot hallways / AC problem” Let's be clear this is a very old hotel on a very pretty river. The staff was excellent and aimed to please from housekeeping and the front desk to engineering who stopped by my room very quickly after calling. My main problem was the air conditioning. The hotel is very old with poor insulation for the balcony doors on each room. During a hot Florida summer I prefer to have my room cool for sleeping, the AC unit never really cooled off the room, in fact even though we set it low, it would just randomly turn itself off and before even trying to reach our desired temperature. Maintenance just shrugged it off and said it was hot outside that day and the room would get cold in the middle of the night. It doesn't help that management keeps the hallways at 80 degrees. Otherwise it was a typical 3 star wanting to be 4 star, old hotel that has been renovated decently with a great staff. If you like a warm room in the summer and can grab this place for a little over a $100 a night you will be fine.

“Decent for an LAX connection, but a bit noisey and worn” LAX Hilton is literally across the street from the runway, very close to the airport. There is a complimentary shuttle every 15 minutes, which is nice. Lobby is nice, staff reasonably friendly. Rooms very standard, slightly worn, but clean and comfortable enough.
