We got a deal coming and going to Hawaii, under $100 prepaid. For budget and reasonably-minded travelers, there is a Carl's Jr. (AKA Hardee's for people living in th eastern US)one block away. The concierge provided us with a list of pizza, chinese, thai delivery places nearby. The in-house restaurants looked nice, but were generally outrageous ($21 for a hamburger. Really?).

“Disappointed” Firstly, the location is great, as are the staff. The rooms are adequate but need to be updated. I stayed in a supposed city view room on the 19th flloor, I actually looked directly into the building across the street, so there was no view. The hotel is very clean, but the furnishings are very old and dated. The room was tiny, but I expected that. I could not see my self staying here for eight nights as was originally booked, so am glad I left after the first night and moved to the Hampton Inn Soho.

“Nice Digs in Time Square” I'm consistently happy with my service at Marriotts and the Marriott Marquis in Time Square was no different. The staff was extremely polite and helpful. The rooms were a good size, especially for NYC. The beds were unbelievably comfortable as I have become acustomed to at all Marriotts. Some other note worthy items: 1. The gym facilities are fantastic. You can literally run or glide yourself into oblivion overlooking Time Square, so cool. Little know fact, if you work out, you can fill up your empty water bottle as many times as you need at their water cooler. Beats paying $7 for a large bottle of water in the hotel! 2. Anyone who has stayed in a very large hotel like this one in NYC during conventions or any other big event knows about the "elevator situations." Waiting 20 minutes and elevators never coming or they're all full when they finally get to you. This problem has been solved, in my opinion, ingeniously by the Marriott (although I'm sure there not the first place to provide this technology). The "computer" assigns you to an elevator so you're never left wondering if you're going to get one. The longest I had to wait during a very large convention was 3 or 4 minutes. Obviously, the prices are an issue because the hotel is on Time Square. However, the smart will venture a few blocks away from Time Square and find that prices drop dramatically.

“Yuck” The hotel’s website states, “Fresh from a multi-million dollar renovation, the Four Points by Sheraton Houston Southwest is ready to welcome you with uncomplicated comforts and a great central location between downtown and the Galleria, with easy access via U.S. 59 at Kirby.” The hotel should demand a refund from the contractor who handled the multi-million dollar renovation. This place is a dump. The rooms are grimy and unkempt. The sheets were just plain dirty. I don’t even think they were fresh sheets. The towels were threadbare and felt like sand paper. The staff was functional, but they were definitely more concerned about chatting with each other than helping guests. I was there for less than 12 hours, and that was too long. I picked this hotel because of its proximity to the location of a funeral I attended. Thanks goodness I only stayed there for one night. I’ll never stay there again. Lesson learned.

“Good Clean Room, airport location” Room- this was a standard Marriott hotel. Room was clean. Bathroom was spacious. Location- it was right by Midway Airport. It was in like a parking lot full of other hotels. There was a TGI Fridays in the lot. I didn't see much else within walking distance. My husband ate at the restaurant for breakfast and thought it was average. We stayed here for a wedding due to the location near the reception. If I come to Chicago as a tourist, I would stay downtown versus here.

“Not bad” I read the reviews, and while I read the negatives, I found the hotel to be in a great location for the mall across the street, and not far from the 101 freeway. This is a business hotel, so don't expect kids to enjoy this place much. Rooms are typical Marriott - nicely appointed, and clean. Safe as well. This place can be full, so make sure of your Reservation! People are friendly, a the breakfast was no surprise, and expensive, like nearby restaurants. I was here for a meeting in the complex next to the hotel and the parking is not free. I would stay here again.

“Great location, but poor hotel” Before staying at this hotel, I had a very positive opinion of Kimpton from previous stays. However this hotel substantially reduced my opinion. The Topaz has a great location near Dupont Circle, but the hotel itself has terrible views. Outside my window is an alley, a dumpster (which was dumped last night at 6 am and woke me up) and another building... and I'm on one of the highest floors. Next to the hotel are buildings with boarded up windows. The rooms are very large, but old. The material of the building is cheap, for example there are popcorn ceilings and the paint in my room is chipped. The amenities are terrible - no gym, and the room service menu is unacceptable, especially for a vegetarian. During a week, I'll normally eat 2-3 room service meals, but this week I've had none because nothing on the menu is even remotely appetizing. Also, the staff does not pay attention to detail. When checking in, I registered as Dr. Soandso, not that I care, but their registration form asked. During the entire stay (approximately 10 interactions with the front desk), I've been addressed as Mr. Soandso. Again, it doesn't bother me and I never say anything, but high end hotels (which Kimpton claims to be) usually pay attention to these details (for example, who is on vacation, who is on a honeymoon, etc). The hotel staff apparently do not care at this location. All-in-all, the Topaz is about equivalent to a Holiday Inn in terms of service and room quality, and that may be a little generous.

“Fight for a nice room and you'll have a great stay!” We booked the Huntington hotel on points and the first room they gave us was very big but dated and the bathroom was horrible. It was also right across from the elevator and behind the staircase, which was far from ideal. It looked nothing like the pictures on the website. We went to the front desk and told them we did not want to be close to the elevator and they moved us to a different, upgraded room with no argument. So, please be aware of this if you booked this hotel on points and/or are younger than maybe their average guest (we are in our late twenties). We do think they try to put people in the un-renovated rooms first when they think they won't complain. Be vocal and tell them what you want and hopefully you'll get it. The room we wound up with was great - it was HUGE with a separate seating area, the bed was comfortable and the bathroom was gorgeous. All marble with a great area to do hair and makeup. We also went to the pool at the spa and it was gorgeous and relaxing - a very pleasant surprise for an indoor pool. The location is great in some ways but be prepared to tackle some nasty hills. There is a hill literally any direction you come from to get to the hotel. I think it's part of what makes San Francisco neat, but if you aren't up for walking them just hop in a cab.

“Classic Chicago Hotel” We stayed at the Drake from May 15-17 and liked the hotel very much. The hotel has great history and tradition and displays it very well. Our room was comfortable although the plumbing was a bit old and the a/c a bit noisy. But those were the only minor quibbles we had. The staff is very accomodating and friendly. The room was spacious and the hotel was very quiet. Our king bed was very comfortable and we slept great. The location, at the start of Michigan Ave. is convenient to shopping and great restaurants. The restaurants in the hotel are superb, possibly the best collection in any hotel we've stayed at. We ate at all 3 of them, and liked the Cape Cod Room the best. The bar at Coq D'or is also excellent. We will stay at the Drake again next time we are in Chicago.

“Best Hotel Experience I have ever Had” I did not hear another guest the entire time I was here (from within the room). The place is private, secluded (compared to the Mile area) and is the best hotel I think I've stayed in. The food was great, business services great, and the location is truly great if you have business in the downtown area. I would certainly return to this hotel anytime as the staff were cordial, polite, and seemed to care about the guests. The room had a large TV, nice bathroom, hairdryer, was clean, and had a great mattress (compared to other places we've stayed in). The place called taxis in a timely manner and made great dining suggestions (they were brutally frank in their opinions, which was nice). I really had a relaxing stay at this place. I was in the middle of business areas, but heard little noise while actually staying within the room. And the hotel was sold-out, I was told. Amazing hotel, great experience for a business traveller in Chicago. This is not really a romantic hotel for a vacation trip, but is an oasis for any business traveller or a person in town for a cheap, quick getaway. Breakfast was included with the rate and was very good. I really enjoyed this place.

“Treated Like a Queen by a Staff that Cares” We spent a “staycation” at this hotel during a four day regional power outage. I had never heard of it before but will be sure to sing its praises to anyone coming to the DC area. This boutique hotel is big on style and customer service. A special shout -out goes to the Managers, David and JoAnn. Each day I returned to the hotel, I was greeted by “Welcome Home!” from David. It sure did feel like home. The room was spacious with nice, well-appointed kitchenettes. Thick walls prevented me hearing my neighbors. The Tempur-Pedic bed was heavenly. The art deco styling was gorgeous. This is a pet friendly hotel with a nice dog park a block away. It is unobtrusive on a beautiful, quiet street in a great neighborhood. The hustle and bustle of Dupont Circle nightlife, the Metro and a great farmers market is just a few short blocks away.

“Awesome Bed!” The hotel is nice and convenient to everything, including the markets and shops in the downtown district. The room was comfortable & quiet; it had a nice view and the bed was awesome; very comfortable. Previously, we had requested extra pillows and they had been placed on the bed prior to arrival. Earlier than expected check-in was greeted warmly. The staff were helpful and courteous. A last minute city tour booking was handled with ease. Room service was prompt, although they forgot part of the order and charged us for it. I called and they took the charge off our bill and then unexpectedly brought the remaining dish at no charge. Although booked by internet, we found the hotel through friends. The total cost for the night was $391 USD, which is probably in line for this part of the city.

“Not for everybody, website photos misleading.” We were booked to stay here for four days, but ended up staying only one night. Like all Kimpton properties, they have a great pet policy and the price (under $100) was very reasonable. However, we were put in a really dingy room with horrible lighting on the ninth floor.... nothing like the sleek, modern rooms shown on the website. It had that distinct gummy-paint-won't-dry feeling that reminds one of undergraduate apartments. We were there with our dog and found that downtown San Francisco is just not a very easy place to stay with a dog, so we moved out to a suburban hotel. Valet parking was expensive and a hassle, and it's important to note that this was a hangout for GenX types. The rickety elevator and very narrow halls made me think that this would be a deathtrap in a fire. For the hip with budget constraints, not a good choice for families.

“OK Hotel if you like Candlewood Approach” I stayed at this hotel for three nights in January for a conference. The hotel is situated within walking distance to Times Square, but is not on the Square. My floor had six rooms on it and I was about 2/3 of the way up the building. I did have a couple of longer waits for the elevator but not really bothersome. The lobby is fairly small and the staff helped me with my check-in without incident. The Candlewood has a pantry that operates on the honor system. They carry soft drinks and snacks and such. I tended to walk around the corner to a small convenience store and pick up items at a lower price. The room is small (see my photos) yet clean and filled with amenities such as microwave, hotplate, dishwasher and refrigerator. My fridge was not turned on when I entered the room, and I noticed it the following morning when I went for my now tepid soda (breakfast of champions, right?). The room was icy upon entry as the heat-A/C unit was turned off. It warmed quickly but I was a bit put off by this reception. The hotel provides an information sheet that claims a DVD player is in the room but mine was absent (not that I brought any DVDs with me anyway). The bathroom has a commode, sink and tub with shower. No super-duper showerhead in the Candlewood; you should stay at the HI Express or Hampton next door if you want an upgrade on the showerhead. There was nowhere to hang a wet towel except over the shower curtain rod. The towels were good and I had enough for my entire stay. Candlewood Suites do not provide housekeeping service except once a week. During my entire stay they did not enter my room to empty the trash, make my bed, or provide new towels. The information sheet tells guests that the housekeeping service is done once a week and to contact the front desk if you require any service before then. I did not know this extended to trash service so I find this unusual. I didn't see any roaches and I didn't suffer from any bedbugs. So I guess they respected my privacy! The exercise room in the basement has a TV, elliptical, two treadmills and two stationary bikes along with a nautilus in a cramped room. The equipment all appeared to be in good working condition during my stay. The wifi worked fine for my needs. The hotel has no business center so you have to go next door to print your airline boarding passes or have the front desk staff do it for you. I walked to the Javits Convention Center, 5th Avenue, Times Square, Hell's Kitchen all without feeling threatened although NYC in January has a curious gift of the wind blowing in your face no matter what direction you walk. There are several good restaurants around the area, as well as pubs. Depending upon your tastes, you can find virtually any kind of food. John's Pizza was good, Stitch was comfortable, Houndstooth is similar to Stitch, and dive bars like Rudy's and Smiths by Birdland are fun. Other than the housekeeping aspect I found this hotel to meet my expectations and needs based on price and location. If you have more than two people I would seek other accommodations, or if you prefer more service or a more central location expect to spend more. I will recommend this hotel with these caveats.

“Great stay...but make sure you have a Do Not Disturb sign” My husband and I stayed two nights at Hotel Felix after booking for a great rate on Priceline. I read reviews leading up to our stay and wasn't quite sure what to expect based on various experiences and notes about the size of the room. We were pleasantly surprised! I contacted hotel management ahead of our stay indicating that were celebrating our anniversary during our stay, and he immediately wrote back guaranteeing a room with a king size bed. Upon check in, we received two complimentary drinks in the lobby bar and bon bons. We were checked into an "upgraded room" on the 12th floor, and while small, it was a comfortable room. The bed was great, and based on the room size, the bathroom was decent size with a walk in shower. There is no vanity on the bathroom sink, but there is a shelf on the wall to store your toiletries. I also noted that the towels were made in the USA... that is not something that I typically note, but I thought it was worth mentioning. The hotel staff are also extreamley friendly, and all spoke to us about our stay as we would encounter them in the hallways or on the elevators. The one draw back that we faced both mornings was an early morning -- about 8:30am -- knock on our door from housekeeping. We didn't have a Do Not Disturb sign in our room, which I am sure would have fixed the issue, but we would hear housekeeping knocking on all of the doors surrounding us too at the same early hour. Otherwise, we had a great stay and the hotel is within a 7-8 minute walk of Rush St and Michigan Ave. There is also complimentary coffee each morning until 10am in the lobby, which is great as you head out for a walk.

“Wonderful location and service” Stayed at the Distrikt Hotel for a short work trip and was very pleased with everything. Location is an easy walk to anywhere (pleasure or work) you would need in Manhattan. Quick walk to the subway as well. Upon check in they had a welcome letter personally addressed waiting in the room with a brownie. The staff were always very friendly whenever I was in the lobby although I never had to ask for anything. Very nice rooms. For NYC standards they are spacious. Comfortable beds, nice looking furniture and great hot water pressure. The bathroom is actually what surprised me the most since NYC hotel bathrooms are usually small. This one was very nice and I didn't feel like I was in a broom closet. Overall, great property in NYC.

“Great hotel in a great location” My husband, daughter and I stayed at this hotel for six nights. Origionally, we had a basic room with falling plaster and poorly cleaned but, after one night, we were upgraded to a deluxe queen room which was lovely. It was a much bigger room and in good condition. I like this hotel. The staff were very helpful. The restaurant was lovely. There are several shops on the ground floor and a good food court on the level below which makes it easy to grab a snack or cheap meal.

“The People Here Make It Great!” The front desk folks could NOT have been more accommodating! They truly seemed to want you to be happy!! When they learned that it was our wedding anniversary, they gave us both little "goodie bags" of snacks and a drink. That was appreciated!! The restaurant on property is a real "sit down" restaurant - and the breakfast was excellent. Jean, the breakfast chef, is an experienced cook and a charming man. I would recommend that you pay a couple of extra bucks for the "Junior Suite" - it was very roomy and gave us a lot of room to stretch out. The only "downside" of this property is that it is in a fairly scary "neighborhood" - being right by the subway, regional rail, and bus stops. I would not recommend going out alone after dark - many homeless and crazies roaming around. BUT - having said that, the hotel rooms and ATMOSPHERE of this Hilton property make it "recommendable." They can't help where they are located, so it seemed to us that they worked that much harder to make sure every other aspect of your stay is PERFECT! Also, concerning location, you are in the heart of everything you want to see and do in Philly - within walking distance of all the historical things you want to see. It is also right next to the Reading Terminal Market - which is a destination in itself! When we were ready to checkout, Marcel (?) the assistant manager of the front desk was especially attentive and wanted a "full review" of our stay at checkout so she would know how they could improve! It's that attitude of customer service that sets this hotel apart!

“Acceptable Stay at a Nice Looking Hotel” The Madison has recently gone through a renovation, and the room I had was impressively new and shiny, as was the lobby and the very nice cafe. The room was a little on the small side but had all the nice amenities and was quite comfortable. Most of the hotel staff were warm and provided good service. There were, however, a few notable exceptions during my 6-day stay that detracted from the entire experience. I spent almost 20 minutes at check-in because the front desk staff couldn't find my reservation. The problem turned out to be that the hotel had me arriving and departing a day early, and so had me as a no-show, despite a confirmation email that had the correct dates. The front desk person seemed quite at a loss as to what to do and got a bit defensive when it became clear it was the hotel's mistake. The cafe staff were always attentive whenever I dined there, but taking orders to go seemed to be problematic, involving either long delays, or, on one occasion when I ordered bagel lox, finding out later that they gave me everything in the take out box except the bagel. Upon check out, I was given a bill that had my name, but someone else's home address completely. When I asked the front desk staff whether this was truly my bill, the attitude was a rather dismissively "don't worry about the address; everything is fine." When I insisted on their correcting the address for the bill, my address was misspelled rather badly, but I didn't have the inclination for a third correction. The hotel management did send me an email afterward apologizing for these problems and offering a complimentary future stay, which was a very nice gesture. It would take some convincing though for me to consider staying there again to risk encountering similar problems, so I hope to see the hotel management take active steps to step up training of its front desk and restaurant staff.

“Just O.K. - It's Style over Substance” I decided to stay here because it was "new". The Hotel is just o.k. It is a renovated Amerisuites. I would have muched rather stayed at a Hampton Inn or Holiday Inn Express for what I received for the $98 price. The only "free hot breakfast” they have is toast & bagels. Everything else hot you have to pay for & yes it's at hotel prices. For $98 I could have gone to Hampton or Holiday and got a full free hot breakfast. I was very disappointed with this. The noise levels of the AC and doors were horrendous. I am talking about all day/night the heavy doors would just hit and shake the walls of the room. The doors do not have springs were they close quietly. The AC in the rooms are old wall AC's that are DIRECTLY ON the bed. It is very loud and VERY noisy. Pros: Bed is great Large Flat screen Nice Decor Cons: Breakfast not as nice as cheaper hotels (just because you have real plates does not make your product any better). Heavy doors hitting & shaking the walls Loud AC unit Thin walls Room layout is not that great (think old school motel sinks on the outside directly in front of the bed). I probably will not stay here again unless the price is a steal. The cold plain breakfast alone was a major turn off. If your into style over substance than this is cool place.

“Really dated” This is one of the cheaper 4 star properties in Union Square. You get what you pay for. Our friends on the trip stayed at the Westin St Francis, and I thought it was significantly nicer. On the lower end of compared to other Hiltons I have stayed at. Will not be back!

“A great value, espically with upgrade!” I can't say enough good things about this hotel. Great location at Bush & Powell. Trolley to Wharf on Powell St. Quiet street, but only three blocks from Union Square and two blocks from Chinatown/Grant St. All staff members were helpful. The valet even told us where to park cheaper than hotel offered. Nice size room, which is the reason I chose it, plus we were upgraded to a suite! We travel alot and this was the first place we ever been upgraded, except for our Honeymoon. Their beds were super comfy too, we had 2 great nights of sleep. I Highly recommend it. On a side note, we ate at Millenium for dinner and Greens on the Marina for lunch both excellent choices, especially if you are vegetarian.

“Great Location, nice hotel” this hotel is a great location. very walkable to all over downtown and the loop. lots of all types of restuarants. my room was not but nothing special. standard hotel room. nicely appointed but no extras--yoga rpogram on tv or even a coffee maker. i had to ask for one. the bed was very comfortable. bathroom is very nice. nice size with good counter space and a nice tub. the gym is open 24 hours so that is nice. the eliptical that i used was very old and the tv did not work. thehead setswere the older type and hard to hear from. the conceriege was helpful and the staff was very nice. over all nice hotel but nothing to really set it apart as special.

“Westin comes through again!” I got a great rate as a Starwoods Member over the internet and enjoyed two wonderful nights at Westin on Michigan Ave. The person who checked me in, Mayra, was extremely accomodating and helpful. The concierge pointed me toward a great restaurant just down the street and was very helpful with other directions. The room was a good size, quiet and extremely comfortable. It was just what I needed as I was in Chicago to take an important exam. I ate breakfast at a wonderful and very European coffee and pastry shop each morning and then enjoyed the Magnificent Mile whenever I could. I highly recommend this hotel for location, service, and value (if you look hard enough!)

“Great location, wonderful service!” We were lucky to get the weekend rate that included breakfast each morning, and were surprised to find that the train station let us out right outside the front door of the hotel - the location couldn't have been better! Plus, with some distance between us and the convention center area, the hotel was quiet and much more personable. Lobby decor was reminiscent of the 60s with orange and pink rings in the carpet echoed by the furniture, accompanied by a funky chandelier that changed colors. But it was vintage! And the concierge located in the lobby was tremendously helpful when we asked about how the St. Patrick's Day parade would affect the bus routes. She called SEPTA directly! Although our room wasn't available, we still got our warm nut and chocolate chip cookies. In fact, we asked for some every night to enjoy as dessert. Because every room on the Broad Street side of the hotel had a corner window, we enjoyed two-way views. Plus, thanks to Hilton Honors, we were upgraded to an Honors floor (the top). After 9 pm, it was quiet even with the ventilation turned off. The bed was a bit lumpy and seemed to be an older model, judging from the fact that the frame was on wheels, and not on a solid foundation as in newer hotel beds. The breakfast buffet in the Academy Cafe on the second floor was more than ample. We could go until dinner time with a small snack. Wait staff were very friendly, and the Sunday morning made-to-omelets were great! Plus, they had soy milk for those who are lactose intolerant. The fitness center featured Precor equipment, and the temp was a bit hot, probably due to having the hot tub and swimming pool next door. Only challenge was getting the sanitizing wipes out of the container in one piece. The business center was small but adequately furnished. We were able to check e-mail as well as print out boarding passes for free. Back to the location. You can walk or take mass transit to practically anywhere. We walked back from the Philadelphia Museum of Art as well as from Yards Brewery - albeit both of them were long, leisurely walks. And we took the bus to several locations as well - with the routes going either from the hotel's front door bus stop or just a few blocks away. All in all, it was a wonderful stay!!!

“Very Nice Stay” We have really been traveling this summer and I must say this is one of our favorites. The service excellent. The room was small, but very quiet and comfortable. We did book priceline and were treated very well.

“Very classy hotel” We had a free certificate for a Loew's hotel because of a bad experience at another Loews hotel. This hotel is just lovely. The lobby is understated, the staff very, very welcoming. The room was gorgeous--nicely appointed with home touches, something you would see in Metropolitan Home or Elle Decor Magazines for a master bedroom. The room was huge was an entry way which included a large closet and large bath with double sinks, a separate shower and deep bathtub. The room had several chairs, a lounge, king bed with lovely linens. We were given a nice fruit bowl and two bottles of Fiji water and Hannukah chocolates at turn down. The location is wonderful. We were able to walk to Lincoln Center in 20 minutes at a leisurely pace. It was a most pleasant experience and Loew's redeemed itself.

“Very Impressive” Stayed 3 nights at the end of July 2004. PLUS SIDE- friendly helpful staff, great location with lots of tasty eateries within walking distance, wonderful views from balcony rooms, free parking across the street, valet parking available, luggage storage until room is ready if you get there early, clean spacious rooms, very comfy bed and pillows, huge soft plush bath sheets, beautiful peaceful Asian decor, hotel will immediately hush noisy people if you call the front desk, totally wired for all communication needs, yummy free continental breakfast each morning. MINUS SIDE - (all minor) lots of costly snacks easily accessible all over the room, shower head beyond my 5'2" reach, bath sheets not within easy access when getting out of the shower, bath robes to small for us oversized Texans, were not told about free breakfast until last night of our stay, light sleepers need to request rooms away from wedding party rooms. WOULD I STAY AGAIN...IN A HEARTBEAT. The rooftop wine bar is amazing at sunset, the inside of the hotel is serene, the front desk afternoon staff are the very best, service is fast and 24 hours a day...ask and you shall receive.

“Inconsistent and one really bad night” I found what I thought to be a decent price on this 3.5 star hotel through Hotwire. The reviews from this website left me feeling a bit uneasy. It started off fairly well. The lobby was ok and the front desk looked like it was in transition. Check in was straight forward and our room on the 26th floor was acceptable, not opulent but ok. It had lots of good appointments but was rather run down. The bed in "this room" was very comfortable. My friends who checked in later felt about the same-"it'll do". The 3rd night of our 5 night stay was Horrible. Those who checked in next to us decided to stay up until 4am, party hard and loud. At around 3pm my husband put a towel under our shared door to keep the smoke out. I now have really bad feelings when I hear Gangnam Style. I should have called but I kept thinking it would stop. I requested to change rooms and was moved to another floor. This was a smaller room all around but the worst part was the bed. It was as if they put a mattress pad on top of a box spring. Ouch. House keeping services were very good and the location is great. The other hotel guests is not under their control although I should have insisted that "they" move, not us. The bed however is unacceptable. Can't say that this meets the 3.5 stars it's given.

“What a gem!” We booked this hotel via priceline. We got a great rate and wondered about the quality. We were greatly impressed! The staff were tremendous as we were traveling with 2 teenagers and a 10 year old. The hotel is within walking distance of Liberty Hall, and the Constitution Museum (which I highly recommend). I highly recommend this hotel for the service, value, and friendliness of the staff.

“May be our new favorite LAX airport!!” We had a red-eye out of LA having arrived a day earlier so we needed a place to stay between 4pm and somewhere around 8pm the next day. We didn't want to pay for two nights at a hotel and found a great deal offered by the Four Points LAX---a 24 hour rate! If you go on their site, they offer a 24 hour rate, but you have to request this at least 48 hours before you arrive and it is not always guaranteed. Received a yes on our request within 8 hours and when we got there, the helpful gentleman at the desk let us stay over the 24 hour limit so we didn't have to spend another 4 hours at the airport! The rooms are great, WiFi is free and there is a really nice bar on premise. As with many LAX hotels, there is a free shuttle that comes every 15-20 minutes. With the 24 hour offer this is sure to be our go to spot for future international and red-eye flights out of LA.
“Great service, nice cosy room” Exceptional friendly service at this midtown hotel. Cosy, quiet clean room with very comfy bed, though tiny bathroom the only downside.

“Conference facilities” I did not stay at this hotel, but attended a conference at the Sheraton for two days. The hotel lobby and meeting room areas are beautiful and very roomy. The conference facilities are vast but organized well with a lot of room for information areas. The food at the conference was great and the waiter at our lunch was probably the most attentive server I've ever seen at a conference luncheon. There were a few session rooms that were really small and remote. The hotel would do well to invest in some ceiling mounted A/V projectors so that screens could be raised - at times (in the smaller rooms) it was difficult to see the presentation with others' heads in the way. The location is the Sheraton's best asset. The promenade along the Chicago river was a great place to take a break from the conference. My husband ate at the Chicago Burger Company and said it was a great meal.

“Don't stay just for the POOL!!” My family stayed at this location for one night before the tree at Rockafeller Center was taken down. From the outside, the hotel looks great and is located in a prime location - literally 3 blocks from Rockafeller center. Right in the middle of the hustle and bustle of Times Square with plenty of sights to see. We picked this hotel mainly because it is one of the few in NYC that has a pool. Since we were traveling with two children ages 7 and 8 it is always good to have in case of bad weather, etc. Upon entering the lobby, we were impressed, very nicely decorated, clean, and rather impressive. Check in was fine and even though I booked a room that was to be on the 44-46 floors, I was placed on the 42nd. No big deal there, still had club access. I believe that this is a waste of money. We did not use it enough to make it worth the extra money paid. We had two rooms each with 2 double beds. My room had a fabulous view of the river and the cruise ships, One of the major problems was that the window would not close, so the wind would be howling and whistling until the engineers came up to close it. Our other room had the same trouble with their window as well. The room was a good size, bedding was not up to par with Marriott, and was a little on the hard side. The room appeared to be renovated, but the bathroom was an obviously last done in the 80's. Dark Brown painted cabinets, flourescent lighting in the ceiling, mirrors everywhere, and old fixtures. Clean but just not new or updated. The biggest complaint I had with the room is that the entire hotel turns off it's air conditioning in the fall and doesn't let you cool your room until they turn it back on in the spring. However, when we were there it was over 60 degrees during the day and the room was so hot that it was nearly impossible to sleep at night. I was able to open up the window about an inch but it did not cool anything. So, a couple nice days and you may be very uncomfortable. And there is nothing that you can do about it. However, the other room that we had that was down the hall was not as warm, so maybe the temperature varies in the different rooms? The kids were excited to go to the pool which was on the 15th floor. So we went. That was when we realized that we were going to an actual NY Sports Club not just a pool for the hotel. Upon checking in at the front desk the kids were given "swim caps" that were mandatory. ??? They had never been asked to wear those before. Anyway, the pool was about 20 feet long and 4 lanes wide. There was a lovely (NOT) lady that appeared to dislike when children use the pool. She told them to stop at everything they were doing. No Kidding. They couldn't do anything without getting the evil eye or a warning. It was not very fun for them nor was it relaxing for us. We left after 20 minutes or so. SO if you are staying at this hotel for the pool DON'T. Stay at Le Meridian, or another hotel. All in all it was a decent stay for 1 night. Would I stay here again, probably not. There are many other hotels in the area that are cheaper and nicer. Sure they may not have a pool, but maybe there are enough things to do that you don't need a pool anyway.

“We liked it!!” We enjoyed our stay at this hotel. The staff at the reception desk was friendly and helpful. We got maps and informations about SF when we checked in. No problem with our luggage to store as we were there before check-in-time (3 p.m.). Our room was nice and clean and size was o.k.,too. We did not have a view but who needs a view in SF when in town all day long... Wi-Fi was free. We liked the free beakfast. Plenty to choose from. The location was just perfect: minutes from Fishermans Wharf, close to cable car stop, a Trader Joes was around the corner (we loved it!) plenty of restaurants and shopping possibilities. There is a pool at the HI next door which can be used from guests of the HI express, too. We were glad the we stayed st the Wharf. Yes, it is a tourist area, but aren ́t we tourists?

“Perfect for Conventions and Business Travel” I’ve stayed at this Sheraton many times over the years on business to the Seattle area and it’s a solid choice for business travelers and perfect if attending functions at the convention center just next door. The location is close to major business/office locations downtown not to mention large retail areas, restaurants and a short walk to Pike’s Place Market so you can’t get much better. The hotel was renovated in 2009 and still looks new from the lobby to rooms and function areas. Room service was good and probably some of the fastest I’ve seen anywhere. The restaurant (Daily Grill) is good for a business lunch/dinner was decent and quick for a low key meal if you didn’t want to venture out to other great choices in the area. All in all I would recommend and stay again at the Sheraton.

“Quaint Place to Stay” We stayed at the Tabard Inn for one night, mid-August, mid-week and were generally pleased overall. We're native DCers and needed an affordable hotel quickly. I found the Tabard Inn had the best prices for such short notice. The front desk person quoted me a rate of $103 for a small room w/shared bath, but assured me I would be upgraded to a better room when I checked in for no extra cost. Apparently when I arrived 15 minutes later, she forgot and put me in the $103 room. It was in the front of the hotel, and was very small and dark. I immediately went back and reminded her of the upgrade. She was pleasant enough and upgraded me to Room 56 (which normally runs $178/night). Their website has pics of all the rooms, and the more expensive ones in the back section of the hotel are bigger. Tabard Inn has a european/slightly upscale hostel feel to it. You're given a real key (not a keycard) with a huge piece of wood attached with your room number printed on it. Our room had a small foyer/entrance with a writing desk, a queen bed with massive headboard, another writing table and an old-fashioned rotary phone (which didn't work, but who uses hotel phones anymore?). The faux fireplace added a nice touch, as well as the armoire & the funky divan, & chairs with animal print throw pillows. The bathroom was a mix of new and old: the pedestal sink and loud-flushing toilet looked new, but the bathroom itself had an old (but clean) feeling. Plenty of towels hung on racks, there was toothpaste & jars of shampooo, conditioner & body wash in a basket (but not in their original containers, which seemed odd) . The shower/tub didn't have a curtain, just a drain in the floor and a splash guard on the window, and the doors to the bathroom were ventilated french-type doors.... so no room for modesty! Room 56 was painted a soothing peachy color, had very high ceilings, and was shaped like an octogan, or sometihing similar, which added to the airy feeling. There was a wobbly ceiling fan over the bed, which we turned off, and 3 tall windows, one of which looked out onto the pretty outdoor patio of the restaurant. As a previous poster noted, there is no TV, no radio, no blow-dryer, or iron, but that's part of the charm. It was a little confusing finding the room, the staircases are narrow, but once we got the lay of the land, and the restaurant & lounges, it's wasn't a problem. The bar scene was hopping, even on a Wed. night, and of course Dupont Circle is a great location for restaurants, bars, etc. I'd recommend Tabard Inn if you're not into creature comforts. If you are, the Topaz is right next door (a Kimpton boutique hotel).

“Every Holiday Inn should be like this...” Good Location near the airport, but out of the skanky neighborhood that surrounds most airports. Front desk was quick and friendly with the check in. The rooms are huge with a separate sitting room/desk area. Perfect for doing some work in the room. Beds were fantastically comfortable and the whole place just felt clean. The landscaping in the central courtyard was nearly resort-like with gas rock fireplaces, upholstered furniture, lots of plants and greenery. Very friendly bartender in the lobby. Shuttle driver was so friendly and helpful that he should be training all hotel shuttle drivers. About a mile walk north to the nearest full service restaurant (Applebees) I think this used to be another hotel brand, but they really did a nice job on the remodel making it somewhere special. I could see using this place for conferences or meetings.

“Great hotel” I only stayed for one night, but my experience with this hotel was great. I was in San Francisco for my birthday and on check-in was pleasantly surprised with a cake and 2 bottles of wine! I have never gone to a hotel that will do that! The staff was very friendly. We checked in late but didn't have any problems with that just a questioning staff member on why we were late. Checked in at night and felt very safe. I didn't have any problems with noise that night at all. I was able to find street parking, but valet parking is available for a price. The nice thing is that they have a complimentary evening wine reception where you can mingle with other guests in their cute lobby. I would definitely stay here again as it's a cute hotel with great value.

“Wonderfully comfortable and well appointed rooms in a good location with friendly and helpful staff. I will stay here again.” This hotel met my expectations of a Crowne Plaza...furnishings and little touches are very nice. But, the friendly front desk staff, providing helpful information about the great neighborhood, make it special. The beds are very comfortable, the rooms spacious and the HVAC works well. I had no noise problems.

“Pleasant and good location” Stayed here recently while attending a meeting at the Convention Center, which it is very conveniently near. Room was not spectacular, but more space than many big-city hotels, and VERY comfortable bed (wimpy pillows, though). I did get a laugh out of the card in the room inviting guests to forgo ALL housekeeping services for a daily $5 gift certificate. Hardly seems like a fair trade! Location is also close to Pike's Market, waterfront, and lots of downtown attractions.

“I stay here often.” The corporate rate we have is amazing. The service is great. The people are very friendly. I enjoy the crazy decor in the lobby. The rooms are always clean and I really appreciate the eco-friendly work that Kimpton is doing. The desks, sadly, are propped up next to the AC, so you'll be tragically cold while attempting to work. Not the most comfortable for business travelers, but you can make do. Lots of pluses! Loved the Hagen Daz suite, complete with free ice cream. And the Jerry Garcia suite!

“Fits with keep Austin Weird, but misses some basics” I travel a lot and this hotel is one of the stranger ones in which I have stayed and while expensive, not an easy room to live in. We were there as part of a wedding party, so we saw many other rooms and spoke to other guests about their rooms. Everyone complained that their room did not have enough light. I'm talking so dark that when I dropped the car keys on the couch in my room after dark, I thought I was going to have to find a flashlight to get them. I finally found them by feel. Almost all the flat space in our room was devoted to selling very expensive things. Most hotels in this price range offer free "disposable" slippers. The Hotel Saint Cecilia has very odd black felt slippers in the closet with a note that if you break the string, you have purchased them for an outrageous sum. In the bathroom there are just the basic toiletries (shampoo, creme rinse, shower gel, and lotion), but there is a huge medicine chest with high priced goodies like a $10 toothbrush and an $8 chapstick. Condoms were for sale, but I don't remember the price. Another large counter in the bedroom is filled with mini bar items including a box of pornographic tapes. The commercialism went way too far in my opinion. The closets are too short to accommodate dresses, which creates problems for guests at weddings. The plumbing is problematical. In our room the water seemed to be a single temperature no matter how you set it. The guests next door said that the first night they did not shower, because they could not get hot water. The service ranged from very accommodating to non-existant. We recieve lots of assistance with problems we reported with the room immediately after our arrival, but when we tried to check-out , they could not produce the final bill and offered to mail it to us later. On the night of the wedding the room was not straightened up and the service was limited to dropping the room service breakfast menu on my rumpled pillow. The best things about the hotel are its lovely grounds (which is why people like it for weddings) and the fancy mattresses. The front desk said they are Swedish horsehair mattresses that sell for $15,000 to $30,000 depending on the room.

“Amazing Service” Special thanks to Jake and the staff at the W that made my business stay ridiculously awesome. I stayed in a Fantastic on the top floor, and had an amazing view of the space needle. The staff here went out of their way to make my stay perfect. I will definitely stay here every time I come back to Seattle.

“Great Location but Watch Out for Nickel and Diming!” This was my third stay at this hotel. Here's the good. The location is unbeatable, putting the Loop, Aert Institute, Navy Pier, River North restaurants, and Magnificent Mile shopping, within blocks. The pool, which is in a Moorish themed room of palatial size, is the grandest I have ever encountered in a downtown hotel in an American city. Beautifully tiled, immaculate and up to ten feet deep. The buffet breakfast is of high quality with made to order eggs and omelettes, warm quiches, bread pudding, and a meat of the day, The rooms are comfortable and elegant, if not quite luxurious Here's the not so good. Parking was $53, not the quoted $50 when I made the reservation. I made the reservation through the property, as an Intercontinental Ambassador, but I did not receive the requisite upgrade. (Maybe I should have used Priceline and paid a lot less if this is how they treat "Ambassadors"). When I complained, the hotel did offer a suite in the less desirable new wing, instead of our two connecting rooms, but the bed configuration was unsuitable. Free internet which was offered as part of the Ambassador package was not available. The hotel offered a free in-room movie instead. Although the pool was free, the fitness center imposed a $12 daily charge (or $16 per stay) On departure, we discovered that we had been charged a gratuity for the breakfasts (which were included in our package). We had left cash gratuities each morning and were dismayed at this charge, which was imposed without our knowledge. The hotel also charged for one day's breakfast, claiming we had eaten after 11, nearly two hours after we had left the hotel. All these charges were removed, but we had to get past front desk staff, and speak to a supervisor. The whole experience left a very bad taste in our mouths. Also, it cost me over $20 to print four boarding passes and check my e-mail in the business center/ So go with your eyes open and your hands on your wallet. Ask for the historic tower. Don't bring a car unless absolutely necessary,

“Great City Choice” Choosing big-city accomodations can be overwhelming due to the number of choices, especially if you are not overly familiar with that city...and they can also overwhelm your bank account. This Hampton Inn is a fine choice for city affordability and getting your bang for your buck. Bottom line is this: 1. Clean and comfortable. Rooms are updated, great condition. 2. Good staff service. Bellman are exceptional. 3. Location to several "El" lines are within blocks - some even closer. Both lines that get you to/from either airport are also within walking distance, luggage and all. Completely doable - look for the elevator entrances to make it easier. 4. Continental breakfast is decent for a quick start to the day. About what you expect - cereals, toast, muffins, juice, some hot choices etc. - remember the city always has plenty of local choices for a real breakfast, still this does just fine - fresh, clean, carbo loaded to get you going. 5. Location "in the loop" is great - walkable to Millenium Park, River walks, trolley's for tours, Magnificent mile, Chicago Art Museum etc etc. You are right in the theatre district here. Plenty of restaurants - sit down and faster food and local choices. Plenty of transportation options - free trolley, tour trolley, all loop lines, taxis etc. Affordability + accomodation + location = great choice for the Windy City

“I Usually Love a Ritz...” I was very excited about my last minute trip to Washington and that the conference I was attending had a "special rate" ($498/night) at the Ritz Georgetown. I usually love a Ritz Carlton, but I didn't think this measured up, sad to say. One major exception however, was the staff, who were possibly among the nicest and most professional I have ever encountered, especially the front desk person who check me in and saw me to my room, then said good bye to me by name - impressive. Also, I had to walk from the main building to my annex building to get to my room. The night I was there the staff was offering to make S'mores over an open fire they started as a nice gesture to clients. They were so cute and seemingly excited about the S'mores...very different and made an impression. I just think I didn't like the rooms that much. They seemed less opulent than a usual Ritz, less refined, too simple. (but the Bulgari toiletries were nice). They were nice, and clean, but just a little spare for my taste. I would also complain about the lack of free wireless in the open areas - what is that about at $500/night?! Quite slow service in the lobby bar too and a glass of basic merlot will set you back $16 - but it is the Ritz. But above Manhattan prices for drinks in a recession seems greedy. I suppose I'd give it another try, but it's obvious I found this an uneven experience. Step up the glamour, Ritz Georgetown! (or lower the prices :-) The Georgetown Ritz is in a great location - a stone's throw from beautiful Georgetown and right near the C&O Canal.

“Perfect higher end version of a Holiday Inn” Had some last minute travel which put me in NYC on short notice and needed a room. Found Indigo on the search engine and read up on the reviews. I was skeptical at first, as it was fairly a newer brand a few steps better than a Holiday Inn, but decided to use none-the-less. The service was exceptional, the room was clean and updated and looked fresh. Definitely would stay here again.

“Great Hotel, Great Location!” I recently stayed at the Hyatt Regency Denver for a Conference. Wonderful hotel, nice rooms and amenities. The lobby bar is awesome and pretty much everything is within walking distance from this hotel (restaurants, shopping). The rooms are also very well appointed. This hotel definitely stays up to date with repairs as the room perfect!

“Much better than I expected” This hotel is located only a short shuttle ride from Houston's Hobby Airport. Compared to other airport hotels, the hotel shuttle is very prompt an efficient. Very much enjoyed the excellent airconditioning and the comfort of the beds. The staff also was much better than your average Hilton staff and offered me to drop my rental the night before. That way I could take the airport shuttle in the morning. The shuttle driver followed me to the Dollar rental lot at 11:45 p.m. so that I did not have to wait once I dropped my car. Not many airport hotels would do that. On the downside the hotel starts serving breakfast at 7 p.m. which is a bit strange for an airport hotel. Afterall people stay at an airport hotel since most have an early flight. So there was no breakfast for me. Also beware of the ice machines on each floor that are super loud and located close to the elevator. The lobby bar is in an excellent location but the bar was closed the entire time. This Hilton is actually a very big hotel and they had a bar in the back between conference rooms that was open. Since there was no conference, there was nobody in it. It seems starnge to me that the Hilton would not open the front bar during normal days and then open the back bar during conventions only. Bottomline, this is a very good hotel and management just needs to work out a few kinks to make it excellent.

“Promising hotel” I chose this hotel because I received Hyatt gift certificates as a prize for a work related contest. We chose this hotel over the older Hyatt because it was brand new had alot of amenities that suited us as we are used to hotels in the San Antonio area that we have stayed at before like The Emily Morgan and Hotel Valencia. We stayed during the last week of the Fiesta festival which if you do not know, is a 2 week long party. It is a Texas style Mardi-gras. Valet is about 20 bux a night , but right across the street is a parking garage that is only 8 dollars all day. Just park there and if you plan on just hanging out at the riverwalk or the market, just use the trolleys. The all day trolley pass is only $4. The hotel sits right next to the convention center for all you convention-goers .We arrived and since this was a special occasion that I mentioned on their website check in, they upgraded us to a bigger room. After arriving, they also sent up a bottle of champagne and strawberries. Very nice. The room was good size and has a big flat screen tv, chaise lounge and was decorated nice. It did have a chain hotel feel to it, but nice. The room has a long entry way to it, which isnt decorated at all, kind of a big waste of space. We had a room that faced the freeway, which didnt offer much of a view. Shortly there after our toilet overflowed and our cable didnt work. They promptly moved us to another room which actually faced down town and had a nice view. They had hot water problems the 3 days we were there. My final day there I had no hot water. That was the fastest shower I have ever taken!!!! They also to appear to have Sat TV. One night there was a bad t-storm and our TV cut in and out during the storm and flat out didnt have a signal for about 20 minutes. I did callthe front desk and they sent some one up, only to say there was a loose connection. In their defense of the hot water deal, they did try to give you a heads up with a voice mail and note, but if you weren't their to receive it, you would have gotten a real surprise. On the final day, early in the morning their was work/construction on the floor above us that woke us up, and we are very heavy sleepers. The hotel does have a very nice workout facility on the 5th floor and a nice size pool on the same floor. The hotel actually sits on a quiet corner of the riverwalk and their restaraunt has out door seating right there on it. Which brings me to the point that there was no continental breakfast. At this price point , in my opinion, should should at least be that , especially at a "chain" hotel. They do have a breakfast buffet with normal buffet items, but it is pricey for what it is. When it came to checkout time, I told the hotel agent my problems and they were more than fair with an adjustment to the room rate, and gave me breakfast for 2 at the restaraunt. This is a good try by a chain hotel to be a boutique style hotel. The hotel was very clean and the staff were all very very pleasant. Once all the bugs are worked out this will be an excellent place to stay. But at the price point, you may want to compare this to the Contessa,Emily Morgan, and Valencia if you are lookinig for a true boutique style hotel.

“Great Hotel” I stayed at this hotel recently and I had a great experience. I am a Starwood Gold Member so I got the room free through points. At check-in, the employee wasn't too great or nice but did get the job done. I checked in very fast with no problems which I always enjoy. I especially liked the room that they put me in. There are 15 floors and I was on the 14th overlooking LAX with a great view of the runways and the airport itself. The room was good size, the sheets, bathroom and everything was clean so I was very satisfied. The only dissatifcation I had was the desk. It was made of wood and there was a lot of chips on the top and the side which were very noticeable. Just a little paint would make it look much better but that was just a minute detail. Everything else was way above satisfactory. I strongly recommend you stay at the Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles. It is very close to LAX and everything around and in Los Angeles.

“Friendly staff & great value” This is an old hotel showing its age. However, you can't beat the location, value, cleanliness, friendliness and excellent service. This is known as our third home; we visit our UCLA student frequently: just ask the welcoming committee Leo (aka Leon), Scott, or Lupe at reservation and front desk. (Ask Lupe for a beach front room, a standing joke) There is a spacious visiting area, communal kitchen, free coffee/tea, and free WiFi. Basic room, no TV...so it's quiet. Lots of international visitors, we feel at home. At $69 a night, you can't find anything for that at Westwood.

“Good for a cheap stay!” Overall this Candlewood Suites is acceptable. I normally prefer Holiday Inn Express or Hampton Inn when choosing a mid range hotel, but given we were just looking for a cheap night to get an extra promotional credit, we were happy with this location at less than $60 this location is a good value. We knew we would have fewer perks, but would also have all we needed for the night. Candlewood is a designed as a limited service extended stay so do not expect your typical mid range business traveler perks. However the location is clean, staff is friendly, and if you know what to expect with the Candlewood brand you will not be disappointed with this location. I would imagine in most instances you would have a car at this location as we did, but if you do not have a car there are plenty of dining options within a 5-7 minute walk. With a car you have nearly unlimited options within 10 minutes. Right next door is a Denny's and McDonalds if you do not want to venture out. This Candlewood, as all others, does not have front desk staff from 11pm till 7am, though they do say that they have on site staff all the time. We booked a studio suite and that is what we were given. If you are staying for more than one night there is limited housekeeping service. The room and common areas were clean though a bit dated. All rooms have a nice size fridge, microwave, sink, kitchenware, microwave, and kitchen table. The room has a work desk, leather chair, and Queen size bed. The bed was comfortable, though the bed is very close to the wall on one side. The rooms are not very large, but are comfortable. The climate control system worked well, and the blower can be set to on for white noise while still using the air conditioning. The room has a TV, VCR, DVD Player, CD player, etc. The TV is a old CRT style TV but had plenty of channels. The free wifi service was easy to connect to and was relatively fast for a hotel. Carpet, furnishing's linens, and furniture are all clean but showing some wear and tear. As for the common facilities, they have quite a few unique offerings. Outside there is a nice sitting area with a gas grill available. (No pool at Candlewood.) Inside, they have a small but sufficient workout room with treadmill, weight machine, bikes, and some other equipment. They have free use of washers and dryers to do your laundry. They also have an honor system for convenience foods - just choose and charge to your room or pay cash. Also, they offer free video and DVD checkout. One major thing that I always find lacking at Candlewoods (thus the reason I do not choose them for business trips often) is that they do not have a business center or guest printer. Keep this limitation in mind if you are in need of printing. I would recommend this hotel for either an extended stay or a quick on night stay if you are looking for a budget option in the Clear Lake area.

“Fabulous Thanksgiving Stay” My husband and I stayed at the Fairmont on Thanksgiving night for a short little get away. We had a great time! First of all, because of it being Thanksgiving, we got a fantastic deal using the Fairmont's website ($129/night excluding taxes). Check-in could not have been more quick or efficient. I even commented to my husband in the elevator up to our room that I have never checked-in to a hotel so quickly! When making the reservation on-line I wrote in the "special request" box that we would love a fantastic view for our quick romantic get away, not knowing if anybody ever reads them or if it makes any difference. Well, they read them, and the woman who checked us in read it back to me (which sort of embarrassed me) and then gave us a free up-grade to the 30th floor with a wonderful view of Lake Michigan. The room was beautiful, as you can see from our pictures. It looked brand new and was spotless. The room was spacious, had a large flat screen TV, and was just overall lovely. The bed and pillows were comfortable as was the temperature in the room. Our bathrobes were cozy, the water pressure great. Anything you can think of was just what you would expect from a five star. The only thing that was not perfect was the coffee maker. It was some sort of fancy espresso deal and we think it was broken. We had very bad cups of coffee. But that wasn't enough to ruin our good time. Location is perfect! It is just north of Millenium Park. That means that you can park in the Millenium Park Parking Garage for $20.00 a day (instead of the outlandish prices charged at hotels) and walk just under two blocks to the hotel. The hotel is just a few blocks from Macy's (formerly Marshall Fields) and is a short walk to the river. We went out Thanksgiving evening and had a fabulous walk north of the river to see the Christmas lights and then found a little pub to enjoy a few drinks in. Wonderful time. The next day we walked to the Christkindlmarkt (which is lots of fun...you should go if you're in town around Christmas) and saw the Macy's window displays. Chicago is just so great anyway, but we had a fantastic getaway! And the Fairmont was icing on the cake and was a nice home base for our activities. Check out was smooth...but we were charged $20 for items that we never took out of the mini-bar. I found this when we returned home. No big deal. A quick phone call and the charges were promptly removed. We were really lucky to get such a bargain for our room. It made it that much grander. But, I would definitely recommend this hotel to any vacationers or weekenders.

“Internet doesn't work” Sometimes, I feel like a stuck record. But gadzooks! Seriously, how hard can it be, in the year 2012, for Sheraton to build hotels with fast, reliable Internet? That's twice in two months they've managed to ruin a business trip. Aside from that, this place is OK. Has all the ambience of a motorway service station, mind, but rooms are cheap and Fine and the staff perfectly cheerful. Just don't plan on using your computer here

“Too much noise in my cramped room with clammy, musty air” There was a lot of hallway noise that got into the room and I could clearly hear people talking in adjoining rooms. The room was really cramped and it was not comfortable to work on the computer at the desk. The room air was damp and musty, I don't think the a/c worked very well. The biggest problem was I inadvertantly booked at the prepaid rate. When traveling on business I always book for flexibility. So of course my plans changed and I only stayed two nights and paid $185/night for three nights. They should modify their internet site to keep people from falling into this trap. I did not get my money's worth on this stay.

“What you expect from a Hilton” If you are looking for a hotel near O'Hare, this is THE PLACE to go. The hotel is very convienently located on the airport property. Despite the proximity to the runways, the rooms are very quiet. The rooms are small, but nicely furnished with very comfortable beds. The work/desk area is larger than usual, making it much more useful for the business traveler. The room and bathroom were clean and well-lit. There is no executive floor offered- but high floors are marked as "hilton honors" floors. I'm not sure if these floors are any different than the others. There are no real restaurant options nearby other than those offered within the hotel. The sports bar in the hotel offered average food (typical hotel prices) with above-average staff. Service was very friendly and fast. The same cannot be said for the steak restaurant. The service was slow and the high-priced food was below average in quality. Frankly, I have had better steaks at Outback. As previous reviewers have stated, be sure to block out plenty of time if you plan to travel into the city. A ride on the blue line will take you close to an hour, and a taxi could take longer during peak traffic hours.

“A long hike to the action” This a good value hotel with no major challenges other than it's location. From our view of the Boston landscape the action centers on (from east to west) the Boston harbor front, the North End, Fanuil Hall Marketplace, Boston Garden and Boston Common near The Four Seasons and Ritz, Beacon Hill and Back Bay including the Charles River, and the Copley Sq area including Newbury St.. Although my (awesome) wife and I are avid walkers this hotel requires a $10-20 taxi trip to get to any of the aforementioned area attractions. Also Kenmore Sq., where the hotel is located, really has nothing going for it except Fenway Park and many, many sports bars. Only other comment and this is probably in the nit picking catagory: the rooms could use a refresh (mattresses, drapes, wall paper, etc).

“Terrific in tribeca” This is the place to stay when on a budget and want above NICE. Love the improvements that have been made, flat screen TV (nice touch) small room, but super clean. Plus, it's perfectly located to all the terrific restaurants, bars, and comedy clubs. Enjoyed dinner at Mai House and drinks at Pegu club (very cool) plus some comedy on Mc Doogal street. Bubbys for breakfast, of course! Under $200...now, that's a WOW! in NYC on a SAT night!

“The location does it” I choose this hotel because of the proximity near a metrostation. I have read other comments about the hotel being in a bad neighbourhood but I don't think that is true. Yes, it's not the best area in LA. During my stay I saw people sleeping on the street and some beggars. But they are not dangerous, just ignore them. When I entered my room I found out that both the fridge and microwave were not working. After calling the frontdesk the problem was solved. I believe the hotel staff is friendly and helpful. Note that this hotel is rather a motel. But the rooms are OK and have everything for your needs. WIFI is free but sometimes slow. Breakfast is also free but simple. But good enough to start your day well. There are quite a lot of restaurants near the hotel. There is a big supermarket not far away at 1601 Vermont. This hotel is perfect if you are not a much demanding person and want to be in a good location.

“Average hotel” The hotel is nicely located with parking, which is good for business travellers. Arrived at 2am, surprisingly, the lobby is still busy with lots of people come and go. But the staff at the desk is great, good service. The room is ok, shower is not as clean though. Given the price, I expect a better place actually. Noice is an issue though, the walls are thin, you can hear almost everything next door, even walking. Fortunately I arrived at 2am, so I just crashed even with the noise. They have a simple breakfast ready, nothing much really. But again, the good service from the staff made it enjoyable still.

“A lot to like but not everything” I have a love/hate relationship with the Palmer House. I have stayed here more times than I can remember because of business travel in the area. So let’s start with the positive. It has quick access to the subway lines and is located within a few blocks of the Art Museum, Millennium Park, and the Theater District. It is also within easy walking distance of some good restaurants (but be aware, it takes notably longer to walk to shopping areas and other places on the north side of the river). It is an old, classic-era hotel that has managed to retain much of its charm and early-style luxury. The lobby remains a work of art, the service is always courteous and efficient, the hallways and bedrooms are nicely decorated and always feel fresh and clean, the beds and chairs are reasonably comfortable, and the rooms offer almost all of the amenities you would expect in this price range (though they could work on wifi access). So what is not to like? The room size can vary widely though I have yet to find a reliable way to predict from the going rate whether the room will be surprisingly large or uncomfortably small. Now days, by habit, I ask for a larger room when I check in because it seems to depend primarily on what is available at the time. I also ask for a room away from the noise of the elevators and the elevated train track. Getting an interior room usually takes care of both of issues but then you’ll have a window that looks directly out into other guestrooms. That makes for great Hitchcock-like entertainment but it will force you to use the blinds more than you might like. It also seems like all the bathrooms in the place are remarkably small -- something I have come to expect as part of the Palmer experience. All that aside, my biggest pet peeve is with the elevators. The wait for them, up or down, can be excruciatingly long and then you have to squeeze into the (reluctant) space between the armpits of everyone else who has been waiting with you. Management is well aware of the problem and has tried everything it can over the years to try to address it. Unfortunately, this is a problem that was literally “built” into the hotel when the early-era designers drew up plans for so few elevators in such a large place. These days the elevators are selectively programmed for access to some of the floors but not others. That has helped ... a little. More recently, they have installed small screens into each of the elevators that show lots of advertisement and a historical Q&A clip about the hotel. That’s entertaining for a short while. Familiarity and comfort level will keep me coming back here (as it always has) but you might want to weigh your options and priorities when signing up for the Palmer House experience.

“non corretto” hotel in una posizione molto tranquilla a fianco del bellissimo balboa park. la struttura e in fase di ristrutturazione di conseguenza ci sono notevoli disagi, ma superabili. le stanze sono enormi con tanto di salotto e mini cucinetta. danno la connessione ad internet compresa nel prezzo ed anche la colazione e compresa. niente di grandioso ma adeguata al prezzo che si paga. io penso che quando sara ristrutturato completamente questo puo essere un ottimo hotel. ed ecco la nota dolente. siamo arrivati e ci hanno detto che la stanza era libera per solo una notte. il mattino seguente controllando in internet per trovare un altra stanza, lo stesso hotel ci dava disponibilita, infatti i il portiere ci conferma per 3 notti, cambiandoci stanza. fatto il "trasloco". andiamo allo zoo. dopo circa un ora ci chiamano dall hotel che la camera non c e piu, e che loro non sapevano indicarci nessun altro hotel. cosi abbiamo dovuto vedere lo zoo in fretta e furia perche dovevamo andare a ritirare i ns bagagli e trovre un altro hotel che per fortuna non un po di telefonate siamo riusciti a prenotare.

“Going to miss this place” I stayed here for 5 weeks in April and May. The rooms are smaller for an Embassy Suites, but that is a non-issue. The staff (front desk, housekeeping, dinning, and coffee counter) were all great. They were the most friendly and helpful staff encountered at an ES. I would recommend you ask for an outside room, as the inside rooms are huge, but are lacking in the window department, and avoid the 14th for sound purposes. Hail storms sound like a parade of elephants.

“Still a great hotel after 150 years” The Menger is a "grand" hotel, and it is not your spiffy, modern, sleek, yuppie-style lodging. It is a classic place, enshrined in its incredibly historic past, yet full of most of the modern conveniences one expects in a fine hotel. I was visiting the Alamo and walked across the street to see if any rooms were available. The front desk clerk was extremely courteous and diligent in finding me two rooms that met my needs--and then, without my asking, he offered me a discount. Both rooms were excellent values. The room I chose had a nice balcony overlooking the interior courtyard and pool area, and while the room's furnishings clearly dated the place, everything was in good working order. It has been more than forty years since I last stayed at the Menger. Staying there again was like returning to an old familiar place and finding it much the same as before. Despite its age, the Menger, like a few similar historic properties, has managed to retain its splendor while keeping up with the needs of today's traveler. I highly recommend it.

“Don't believe the hype, slightly abv avg hotel” After reading the glowing reviews I decided to try this hotel out. My background is that I stay in a lot of high end hotels around the world and this converted Radisson was disappointing vs. the reviews. It would be an ok hotel if I got the room for $150-200 as some did here, but not for >$300. Location - poor; rooms - just fair, the mattress is poor (thin) and the room layout is maybe the worst I've ever seen in a hotel. I could set up bowling pins and roll a ball down the room, it's half empty! Bathroom is also a motel bathroom with a nice sink. Shower/tub is from 1970. I'd avoid this place unless you get it cheap.

“Great Location-Average Hotel” Stayed at this hotel for 3 days with teenage son recently. It is very well located in central Copley square, only 1 block each from both the Green and Orange lines of the "T". I should add that the subway is the best way to get around Boston. Anyone willing to compete with the aggressive drivers is nuts. The hotel is old and ornate, with a beautiful lobby, but it's aging and the Deluxe room we had was a little tired and faded. The bathroom was small with a door that would not fully close and the walk in closet had a defective light that they could not fix. The hotel was busy and noisy with lots going on like meetings, proms, etc. so be prepared. I also thought the staff, particularly the concierges were not that friendly or extremely helpful. The hotel has one very formal restaurant and no casual coffee shop, so we ended up having breakfast at a Starbucks on the corner. Bottom line: We paid a discounted corporate rate so I was happy with the value received. But I would fell differently if I had paid the rack rate.

“Beautiful historic hotel” I would recommend staying at the Menger if you appreciate history. Stay here if you think old buildings have more character than new. The lobby has many amazing antiques. The antiques did not seem to extend to the rooms as the furniture in my room looked to be made in China. I enjoyed browsing the lobby and viewing the photos of all the famous people that have stayed here. The hotel is old and not as well kept up as it could be. My room was dingy with many areas of peeling paint. The room was small. As I was travelling by myself and was working most of the time, I did not mind the small rooms. If you were stuck in this small room with a family for many hours, it would be unbearable. My room had a great view of the Alamo. I overlooked the area where the horse-drawn carriages line up and it was fun to watch in the evenings. The hotel's location could not be better. It is only three blocks from the Convention Center. There are many nearby staircases to access the Riverwalk. The area seemed pretty safe, even for a woman travelling alone. The walls are paper thin. Honestly, I have camped in canvas tents that filter more noise than these walls. I could hear the clippety-clop of horse's hooves outside (with all windows shut). I could hear people tapping on laptop keyboards next door. Thankfully I had earplugs to sleep with. My bed was comfortable with decent linens. Bring a converter as most of the outlets in the hotel only have two prongs. They had new coffee pots with three-pronged plugs and nowhere to plug them in. I thought this was odd and they should have attached a converter. There was no way to plug it in in my room.

“All the right ingredients, exceptional hotel” Location is excellent right on Ghirardelli Square with direct access through the hotel. We stayed in a two bedroom suite + living room + kitchen, very high standards throughout. Free internet and breakfast. Complimentary Maseratti Quatropporte to drive or pick you up to a 2 miles radius. Small, less than 100 apartments. Unbelievable value. I will not even bother writing further. Take my word for it, this is the place to stay in San Francisco.

“Quiet location, good value” The location was good for staying out of touristy Times Square area, but with easy access to the square, and other sites via a quick subway ride or a leisurely stroll down Broadway. The staff was very friendly and professional, from the doormen to the housekeeping staff. The rooms were modern and quiet. I have stayed in New York many times and I could always hear street noise, but even though I was on the fifth floor the only street noise I heard was at 4:30 a.m. when a garbage truck pulled up. The bed was ultra comfortable with a variety of pillow choices. I had a few issues with the room, and they are minor. No channel information was available for the television, and the TV, even though it was large and placed on the wall, had substandard picture quality.
