That could be because at home I'm used to high definition. I also had to pay almost $15 a day for wireless in my room. I should point out wireless is available in the lobby where there was comfortable seating, but not much privacy. I also missed having two bed lamps. The alarm clock was on the nightstand without the lamp, so I had to creep across the bed in the dark after turning off the light on the opposite side. The switch on the wall by the alarm clock didn't operate anything, and I have a feeling that it was supposed to operate an overhead light. Anyone staying there should note a second set of elevators off the right side of the lobby. The elevators to the left of the lobby are smaller than those elevators on the opposite side of the lobby, and they run slowly. Two terrific guest balcony areas offer private seating and a place to enjoy city views, although not spectacular views. I would stay here again as the room was modern, clean and quiet. This is a good value for New York.

“Decent Marriott, Slow Elevators” This is a pretty decent hotel. The rooms are large for Manhattan, and were clean and comfortable. The location on West Street isn't great, but it's lower Manhattan so everything is close anyway. The elevators were brutally slow. I waited about 15 minutes in the morning waiting.

“Great Property” I was welcomed immediatly by the staff and check in went very smooth and quickly. Our room was upgraded due to being a member of IHG Priority Club and a fruit backet, bottled water & chocolates were awaitng our arrival. The room had a georgeous bathroom with plenty of ammenties, oversized room and the bed was very comfortable. We had a drink in the restaurant and it was very well appointed. A perfect stay and great value.

“Newly renovated rooms” I stayed at this hotel on business for a few days in October. I had a room on the 6th floor that was newly renovated. The woman told me she "upgraded" me to one of these renovated rooms when i checked in. For a NYC hotel room, it was very spacious. King size bed with a pullout couch and a roomy bathroom. The bed and pillows were very comfortable and the room was not loud at all. Some of my coworkers that had older rooms said mine was much nicer - so get a renovated room if you can. The cafe on the first floor is crazy expensive... but this is a hotel in NYC, so that's to be expected. If you want a less expensive breakfast or lunch, walk across the street to the West 53rd St. Deli where you can choose from a huge variety of fruits, veg, sandwiches, breakfast items, etc. The deli was really good. The cafe in the hotel, meh. Transportation at this hotel was fabulous. Because it's such a large hotel, it's not difficult to get a cab. I've stayed at other NYC hotels where getting a cab is like pulling teeth from a cow. There is a nice port cochere so if you have to wait for a cab and it's raining, you don't get soaked. That alone is worth its weight in gold. Great hotel for business travel, couples on a trip, a family vacation, friends, solo, etc. Fabulous location blocks from Central Park and Times Square with tons of restaurant options.

“Out of the Ordinary Hotel...In a Good Way!” This hotel was a nice change of pace! We stayed here one night after attending a concert in town during the week and didn't want to drive the 40 miles home late at night...plus it was close to work so my S.O. could sleep in a bit the next morning. I checked in on a Thrusday afternoon, close to 4pm. The free parking was nice and I didn't have any trouble finding a space. The lady at the front desk checked me in promptly and was very friendly. The lobby is decorated with bright blues, greens and white...really different, but I really liked it. I went up the the 5th floor and my key didn't work. Luckily, housekeeping was in the hall and noticed I was having trouble. She radioed the front desk to ask if it was ok to let me in, they said yes and were up to my room with a new key in less than 2 minutes! The room I booked (through Priceline for $45 a night!!!!!) was a standard room with 1 King bed. The entry way was nice and spacious with one closet and a nice long countertop/bar with coffee maker and mini-fridge and a sink. The entrance to the bathroom was in this area as well. I really liked the bathroom...very clean and spacious. The shower was big too and was a walk-in with no door...pretty cool...and I didn't have any problems with water getting out of the shower onto the floor. The rest of the room was nice...love the unexpected decor. There was a good sized desk, wonderfully comfy King bed, small chair with ottoman, bench, and an armoire with hanging space, drawers and a TV. The TV was kind of small and a little older, but I didn't have a problem with that...it worked fine. My one and only complaunt with the room was the A/C unit...unusually loud! It didn't keep me from sleeping since it ended up being a constant "white noise" but got rather annoying the next morning when I was up watching TV and trying to relax before it was time to leave. It would make me think twice about staying here again for an extended period of time. As far as hotel services...when we came in late from the concert the bar was still open so we bought a bottle of water and a muffin to snack on. The muffin was a little dry and crumbly, but the two guys working down there were super frinedly and fun to talk with for a few minutes. We ordered room service the next morning for breakfast and it was delivered promptly in a cute picnic basket. Everything seemed fresh and tasted really good. What I loved was that the food prices for room service were no different from what they were if you dined in the cafe. That was nice! When it was time to leave, I stopped at the front desk to check out and pay the balance...it was quick and the desk attendant was friendly. All in all, I'd definitely stay at this hotel again for a quick over-nighter. Any longer than that and I'd think twice because of the noisy a/c....if that was corrected it would be PERFECT!

“Well worth the time” There are lots of hotels in the Chicago area, and every February I spend a night or two at the Four Points. The location is perfect, the staff is great, and the parking is reasonable. I would strongly suggest that anyone wanting to be in the thick of Chicago without spending a fortune to look at the Four Points, you won't be disappointed.

“nice quality hotel, but would have preferred being closer to Gaslamp District” Pros: clean, nicely decorated (nautical theme), free shuttle to/fro airport, nice staff Cons: location - would have preferred being closer to Gaslamp so that we could walk there; restaurants in the hotel left a little to be desired I stayed here for a work conference. I think, if I wasn't bound to the location, I would choose somewhere with a better location and food offerings.

“Great location, needs a little work” Hotel is within walking distance of Reliant Stadium which is a plus. The room was clean and comfortable, beds were comfy. Some of the staff were helpful, but we didn't get the warm, fuzzies we usually do from other Hamptons. The breakfast was almost inedible. Canned fruit tasted tinny, scrambled eggs tasted odd and the other basics just didn't seem to have the TLC that other Hampton's have. We love Hamptons, but this one just didn't meet our expectations. Not planning to return - will try our luck elsewhere.

“Clean Modern Family-Friendly Hotel!” This hotel is located in the hotel circle area of the San Diego. Generally you can find the rates of the hotels around this areas to be slightly cheaper than downtown areas due to lack of view and adjacent to the freeway. However, to offset this, the rate (as mentioned before) and the proximity to the malls/shopping centers covered up. Location: As Mentioned above, located right next to the freeway, easy access to La Jolla, Convey, and Downtown San Diego attractions within 10 mins of driving. Parking: Gated, no valet available. I believe it was $12/day. Bit on the expensive side. Gym & Pool: No fitness center, there's a nice swimming pool (its heated so its warm to swim even at night and Jacuzzi). I always heard kids having fun at the pool. The pool opens til 11pm at night. Restaurant / Bar: Closed at 11pm. There's a continental breakfast bar for club level guests on weekends else it'll be served at the bar. Lobby: Clean and fresh looking sheraton 2.0 look. Sheraton Link terminals available for use (2 computer terminals) and gift shop located adjacent to the lobby. Check in was very smooth and quick. Was upgraded to 1 Bedroom corner suite on the 12F. Room: Clean and modern. Bathroom is on the smaller side but still adequate. Living room and Bedroom both equipped with a 42-50" LCD TV. Work desk , sofa with pullout bed available for extra guests. My bedroom had a balcony too which I can walk out and see the views of the freeway and the malls across the street. Some people complained about the noise of the freeway. Yes I can hear them but it didn't bothered me much. I had a good night sleep there and I did enjoy the pool a lot. For the value minus the charge for parking, I would like to return to this hotel again in a later time when I am visiting San Diego.

“Much improved...but will it last?” It goes without saying that this is a high-traffic hotel. With 1,800+ rooms, people are EVERYWHERE. Tons of business-traveler traffic (which was my trip purpose, as well). The renovations are very noticeable and very nice...however I already noticed telltale signs of wear-and-tear in my room (and I believe the renovations were just completed within the year). Tub was scratched, grout on the floor had stains, glass tables & desk were scratched, newer carpet already showed traffic markings. I received an end room on the center 1 tower. The end rooms are about twice the size as regular rooms at the same price, so ask for one if you can. It is a little noiser due to service elevators and staff doors down on the end, but the extra space is heavenly. The room had a 20ft wall of windows overlooking the buildings & pool (and excellent blackout curtains for sleeping). Toiletries were provided, but none stood out (typical watery hotel-fare) besides the little tube of thermal shaving cream...it was a nice touch. Starbucks single-use coffee was provided in room as well. The biggest thing this hotel did to impress me was provide an ACTUAL hairdryer!! Not one bolted to the wall...but an actual Conair handheld hairdryer!! With decent settings besides "hot as fire". What a treat for this weary business traveler! A few quick reasons I did not give 5 stars: -The lobby with the coffee & ice cream shops had a nasty smell (sewer) throughout my entire stay. Not appetizing. -Not much to walk to. There is a CVS pharmacy and a few bars within about 2 miles but nothing really touristy and fun. -Cab ride to the airport (or Marriott car) cost $50. Each way. Yikes. -A map or guidebook to the hotel was not provided in-room. I had to go down to the lobby to try to figure out where my conference room was. -Internet was $15 per day. Business center charges $1.50 per page (!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!) for printing.

“Good Choice; Can Be Pricey” Newer location that's comfortable and clean. The location close to the airport is great. Staff was very helpful. Rooms are very comfortable and clean. Bathrooms are stocked with a full line of amenities. Rooms in the Houston area have seemed to climb over the last year and my rate of $159 seems a little high.

“If location is important STAY HERE” $99 per night on Hotwire. We were told we couldn't have a TWIN room because there were none available however we know it's really because we're on the Hotwire super saver deal. Staff on reception were nice & very helpful. Doormen / bell boys watched us try to lift our cases out the back of a cab so ZERO potential tip for them. Great location however and you really are in a safe area of town. We were allocated a room on level 12 and the shower took something like 10 minutes to get hot. I think this place has sme plumbing issues. The rooms are nice though. Ours is HUGE and very well appointed. Great photos of Boston all over the walls, clean and well maintained. They are doing the room up over the hall however and the work men are singing as they work. Other than that it's a good place to stay. Do ask about the water / plumbing situation and don't expect too much help from the bell boys.

“Room quality may vary” I was on an overnight stay on business and chose this hotel due to my late flight arrival into LAX. I rented a car and parked it in their garage; it's not cheap - something around $20. Luckily, my employer was paying the expenses on this trip. The hotel is large, maybe too large, which means as an airport property, a lot of people are arriving an leaving at all hours. Check in was smooth. As a Hilton Honors Gold member, I got a room near the top floors facing south towards the south runways of LAX. I found very little noise creeping into the room. Overall, the room was 3.5 stars, definitely not a 4 star, due to its very basic room, amenties, decor, and bathroom. The desk area was not the best lit for work but not so dark that I couldn't see my paperwork. The bed was comfortable, with good lighting on the nightstand. The carpets were clean and the furniture not all beat up like what one often sees at airport properties. The bathroom, which can often make or break my star rating with a hotel after the bed and the room cleanliness, was quite basic, nothing to brag about or a place where you want to leisurly take care of your bathroom and vanity responsibilities, but was efficient nonethless. Due to my status with Hilton, the room had upscale bathroom products (Peter Thomas Roth), which are very nice and I'd say a step above the standard C&E products at most Hilton properties. The following morning around 7:30 am I went down to the lobby area to partake of the complimentary breakfast buffet that was included in my rate presumably due to my status. It seemed to be chaos with no one at the front podium to handle the greeting, and a lot of people surrounding the buffet tables piling on the food like most buffet lines. I immediately left, went up to the Executive Club, and partook of the Continental breakfast offering up there with a nice view of the airport runways to boot. It was the best decision I made that day. Another drawback: The elevators in this hotel are clearly inadequate in capacity and number, which can lead to long waits for an elevator car, especially during the peak morning hour when everyone seems to be heading to the restaurant. I waited close to 5 minutes for an elevator on my way down to the restaurant. Several hotel staff were waiting for an elevator car to transport their service carts to another floor and when I left the downstairs restaurant and went up to the Executive Club, those hotel staff were still waiting to get themselves on an elevator (not sure why they weren't using a service elevator, if they are available). Check out was quick and painless. It's a good airport hotel but not much else. Best part was the Executive Club where it was quiet and peaceful with a satisfactory Continental breakfast spread. Worst part was the long elevator wait. Would I stay here again? Yes, if I did not have a car with me (and have to pay parking) and surely for not more than 24 hours.

“This is a good Sheraton” Stayed here in August for 3 nights. It is easy access from the freeway. Easy access to shops and restaurants. We stayed on a Preferred Floor. The breakfast is nice and convenient. The pool is great for kids.

“Excellent King suite on the backside of HOTEL” The room was nice and clean and nice sized and the staff was very nice and helpful and pleasant to interact with at all times. I was able to book the room w/ my points which was wonderful, at the last minute I needed somewhere to stay in El Paso, so this worked out wonderfully. Breakfast was a nice selection of scrambled eggs, sausage links, bread, oatmeal, cold cereal, hash browns, yogurt and fresh fruit and some other items. The bed is comfortable and adequate towels were provided and the daily service was exceptional. The kitchen has all the basic utensils, pots and pans needed to cook a simple meal, but why cook meals when food is served for breakfast and dinner almost every night. When I checked in I requested a room on the top floor so I would not have to deal with people walking over me, which is a good thing because some other reviews stated they heard the people upstairs, which I did hear the people slam the door underneath me at times so I suspect they could hear me, so I tried to walk softly. :>) ... Overall this was a great value for the monies paid!!
“Basic but decent. Exactly what you would expect” This is a decent commuter hotel. It's clean and the service is decent. I would stay here again for the convenience of its location.

“would not stay here again. Too many good hotels close by” Good location. OLD old plumbing and the slowest internet service I have ever seen. Just unusable and I did need to do work while staying at the hogel. When I called the desk, the gentleman said "well, what can I say?". I went to Starbucks to do my work. Breakfast was a low class affair. Tablecloths full of crumbs, a few hard boiled eggs and biscuits and sausage gravy to clog your arteries at the start of your day! Bed was hard, TV didn't work correctly. I couldn't get HBO or other cable channels and that again seemed to generate no action or surprise from the desk. There is lots of competition in the area for $250 per niight, so I would not pick this property again.

“Relaxing stay with everything at your fingertips” We picked this hotel as a romantic holiday getaway. As soon as you walk in, you can feel the warmth of the fireplace and were greeted by a nice staff. Hotel Valet is 42.00 but if you park your car yourself in the lot across the street its 32.00. It was a good tip given to us by the bell hop. We used the fitness center which is extremely up to date with all new equipment, tvs attached to each machine. We even paid a visit to Asha Salon which is onsite. The entire hotel was redone so everything is brand new and beautiful. Do not expect the largest spaces in the world, but they did a great job of keeping the decor minimal but modern. The location was extremely close to shopping (state street) and to the Daley center for us to be able to visit the Christkindlmarket and check out the giant christmas tree. We ate dinner at Elate restaurant which is next door to the hotel. You do not have to walk outside of the hotel for it. The menu is not the largest in selection, but what we ordered was very tasty. It was a beautiful stay for my husband and I.

“Nice Hotel Good location” I stayed at the Hyatt for two nights in March. Rooms were decent and clean, and the location is good....just 1 block from Michigan Ave. many resturants are just a short walk as is shopping.

“Trendy and right in the middle of the city!” My husband and I stayed for two nights during a road trip in California. The hotel is perfectly located at the Union Square surrounded by great shopping and restaurants. The parking fee was expensive but the same as the other central hotels. The room was very big and affordable, but we were there during off season.

“Eh” Its location to downtown Chicago is superb but the hotel itself would suit a business traveller or a group of friend that just want somewhere to leave their shopping bags. I stayed here with my husband who was in Chicago for work. The weather was freezing, and had that Christmas feeling to it so I spent most of my days walking around Michigan Avenue and out of the hotel. It was perfect for what we needed but don't expect anything plush.

“Best Luxury Hotel in Indianapolis” The Conrad Hotel (a Hilton Brand) sits on Prime, Grade A real estate directly across the street from Circle Center Mall and is completely surrounded by the bustling restaurants and retail of downtown Indianapolis. The service is impeccable. The staff are outstanding. Sometimes when you stay at a high-end hotel, you get staff who confuse snobbish and unfriendly behavior with providing first-class service. At the Conrad, you get first-class service without the attitude. From the moment you step off the elevator onto your floor, you know you are lodging in luxury. This hotels theme is elegance, and they paid attention to the little details. The soft lighting. The glossy, wooden doors. When you open the door to your room, you are immediately taken in by the timeless, classic styling of the furnishings. Granite top on the dresser. Beautiful linens. Sumptuous fabrics. The bathroom has an lcd tv a stand alone shower and a deep, tub. It's like a small home away from home. If I were finding a place for a celebrity or important client, *this* is where I would put them. Hands down. I've stayed here twice. Once for a birthday gift to my husband not long after they opened. They prepared a beautiful plate of special desserts for him (that I'd pre-ordered). This time we just had a weekend getaway. Just a lovely place to be. You will feel SPOILED after a short stay here.

“Location, Location, Location” The Inn at Virginia Mason is the only hotel connected to the hospital complex. The rates are lower than most city hotels. The best part is the wide variety of high quality food from room service and the onsite restaurant that are very reasonable in price. Because my honey had surgery scheduled the second day of our stay I booked a junior suite. The hotel is a converted apartment building and our room was very generous for an older facility. Be careful not to stay on the end of the hotel near the service elevator. We were in room 806 and the noise from the elevator was obvious and went late into the night. Overall the Inn is perfectly located if you are using the services at Virginia Mason Hospital. WiFi is included in the hotel rate, but parking at $20 per day is extra. The staff is very pleasant and as they say “location, location, location” is the most important element of choosing a place to stay.

“Belated public thanks for sending forgotten items to Berlin after us and much more...” In NYC October 21 to 24 and chose the Andaz after a good stay at the Hyatt in Amman, Jordan. We left the NYC Andaz in a rush for a conference in Berlin and are forever indebted to the Andaz staff for express-mailing my husband's computer charger to our hotel in Berlin in time for his presentation, all arranged by a panicy, static-filled cell-telephone from the cab to the airport. Not only that but Kyle from the front door raced with me to the room to grab our bags while my husband got the car--a total save by compassionate staff. Also enjoyed the casual lobby and its Barista, who was informed about store hours, etc. I have been meaning to write a personal thank you to the woman who took our call, but have since lost her name. In NYC we heard one of Hyatt Hotel owners speak about his hotels' service--and his respect for Hyatt employees--and we suddenly became believers. Using the Hyatt Visa card in Europe was a plus--no FX charges--and we have just scheduled our 'two free nights' at another 5-star Hyatt for opening the card account, no blackouts. The NYC Andaz room was as others have described it--very modern, a glass wall to the bath, mirror/wardrobes which swivel, very comfortable and clean, free water I think, and the windows open, a priority for us. We had free internet, another priority, but not sure if it is always free. Farmers market on Saturday a plus, make sure to walk to the battery and along new river-side path up west side. Relatively inexpensive parking at Pier 40, a hike, but October weather was lovely. Enjoy--the Andaz in NY is great.

“Overall the room was fine, but breakfast was a disaster!” I've stayed at this Hilton in the past, and again, had a very nice room. We were given a handicapped accessible room (don't know why) and it was humongous! There was a downside though – the bathroom is very large and as there was not heat source, it was COLD. I was tempted to turn on the hair dryer just to warm it up a little. Otherwise, the room was nice, bed comfortable, linens very nice, down comforter was cozy. We were lucky to be able to take time in the morning before our medical appointment to eat breakfast in the hotel. That’s where it all went very bad. It appeared to me that the staff was busy doing everything BUT seeing to the needs of the patrons. We stood for nearly 5 minutes at the entrance before any one would seat us. Someone actually walked up and asked us if we were being seated (it was very obvious we WEREN’T), then looked over and saw the waitress half a room away walking toward us and said, “someone will be right with you”. Well, why didn’t YOU seat us? Then the waitress did all but force us to choose the breakfast buffet. We didn’t bite on that and she looked obviously perturbed. We ordered coffee and I watched her wander all over the restaurant, doing everything BUT getting our coffee or the coffee for the guest next to us (who made the wise decision to go for the bird in the hand and eat off the buffet). After waiting 10 minutes for the waitress to return with our coffee and to take our order (was she testing how long our resolve would hold out against the buffet?), we got up and left. HIGHLY disappointed in the breakfast restaurant.
“Great hotel for the price I paid” Got this room thru priceline great room clean convienantly located two thumbs up

“Beautiful Hotel, Disappointing Guest Service” Overall, the Millennium Hilton is very close to being a very solid hotel. The facilities are excellent, but serious guest service problems keep this hotel from reaching its full potential. It is very unfortunate that such a lovely facility is held back by repeated gaffes on the part of the staff. If they could iron out these wrinkles this property has the potential to really shine. But, as it is, the disappointing treatment by the staff is enough to take this off of hotels that I would return to. We booked this hotel for three nights at $180/night via Hotwire.com. This was an excellent value compared to similarly priced hotels in Midtown (where we prefer to stay) which were running in the $250+ range during that time. I did not penalize the hotel because of the location, that is not their fault and we had a good idea of what we were getting into by choosing to stay downtown on a weekend. Simply put, this area of NYC is dead on the weekends because it is the business center of the city. During this time restaurants and even the drug stores close very early--if they are open at all. Also, subway travel is very hit or miss to this area because they are rebuilding two of the stations and service is frequently suspended or re-routed during the weekends. Cabs are available at the hotel, with a ride to Midtown running $12-14 each way, plus tip. Ultimately, we felt very removed from the city and probably would not stay in this area again. Upon arrival we were checked in by a very friendly efficient staff member. The lobby, while compact, is beautiful. The rooms are quite spacious by New York City standards. Decor is very clean, almost minimalist in a palette of neutral colors. Furnishings are of upscale quality and in very good, almost new condition which makes sense as the hotel only reopened (after a full renovation) in 2003. The closet was small but did have plenty of hangers, a full-sized ironing board, and even two umbrellas (though I'd gladly trade the umbrellas for having robes in the room). The large flat screen television was nice, but we were disappointed with the poor picture quality on several channels and a remote control that only worked half of the time. Also, the on screen hotel services menu (where you can check your folio, check out, etc.) did not work. Because of the building's small footprint the rooms are only on the ends and one side of the building (as opposed to both sides), with end rooms being suites and middle rooms being the standard sized rooms. All standard rooms (such as the one we stayed in) view the WTC site and World Financial Center buildings (striking views). Windows near the elevators have superb views of the lower east side, Brooklyn Bridge, etc. Our service problems started almost immediately. We called guest services to request two additional pillows. They said they would be right up. After 45 minutes we received a call from guest services to confirm that they had arrived...which of course they hadn't. They apologized and said they would be right there. After another 45 minutes I called guest services to let them know we STILL hadn't received the pillows. Again, they apologized and said they would be right there. After 20 more minutes they did. Two phone calls and nearly TWO HOURS for extra pillows is ridiculous. This property touts "The Bed" by Hilton which is--supposedly--a premium bed. I found the mattress to be entirely too firm and NOT EVEN CLOSE to a Westin Heavenly bed. This is not a "pillow top" type of mattress but rather a regular inner spring mattress with a little add-on pad strapped to it. The linens were acceptable, though nothing special. Another disappointing issue for us was the lack of an in-room coffee maker...even Motel Six offers this basic feature. You shouldn't be required to get dressed, go downstairs and get coffee in the morning (and the coffee place is probably closed anyway because this is downtown on the weekend)...or be forced to pay $10/carafe with a $4 delivery fee and 15% service charge. Bathrooms are spacious and bright. Toiletries are Crabtree & Evelyn. The towels are very nice, designer type ones; however, I did notice that on the third day housekeeping started mixing much cheaper, lower quality, non-matching towels in with the good ones. Robes and slippers are only available by request and even then it took 45 minutes and two phone calls to get them (yet another problem with guest services). The robes were very scratchy and uncomfortable...I had not idea you could get cotton to feel that way. We dined using room service twice. The first time was perfect. Unfortunately the second time was a disaster. We called and they said they would call right back to take our order. After waiting 35 minutes for them to call back (unacceptable) we called again to find out the reason for the delay. They apologized and said they would call us right back to take our order (what is with the calling back thing, why can't they just take the order right then?). After another five minutes they did call back to take our order. The meal itself, was pretty much inedible (the french fries were mushy, and the burger incinerated). After returning to the hotel on our final night neither one of our keys would work so we had to go all the way back downstairs to have them recoded. The front desk person rather than simply apologizing and recoding them started implying that we must have done something to demagnetize them (what this might have been I can't even imagine). But apparently it was our fault by the way she reacted. Also related to staff issues, the doormen are VERY inconsistent with some bordering on rude. Once we even had to open the door ourselves while a doorman stood right beside the door.

“Very Nice Stay” My wife and I had a 1-night getaway in a one-bedrrom suite, and thoroughly enjoyed the hotel. The furnihings in the room were very nice, and the addition of the fireplace added to the atmosphere. The staff was very helpful, and the car valets were especially speedy. The only negative concerned housekeeping. When we entered the room, there was "Happy 30th" material leftover from the previous guests. In addition, there was a wad of Kleenex wedged into the security peephole of the door (am not sure why someone would do that). Other than that, we had a great stay at the Magnolia.

“Nice stay for business.” Spent 2 nights at the Doubletree for an annual conference for my company with about 100 other attendees. Rooms were nice, very comfortable bed and good pillow selection. Bathroom was a bit rough with old brackets still on the wall from something that was removed awhile ago and the ceiling looked a little yellow and was bubbling from moisture. I really can't complain as I got a steal for only $66 per night on the hotels website if I prepaid (which I did). Customer service was spotty as me and several of my colleagues experienced conflicting information refarding everyhing from parking fees to late check out. The meeting facility was good and the in-house food was excellent. All in all a good stay in a great location.

“Customer service review only (I did not stay)” I would like to comment on the excellent customer service of Travis Jones and his female colleague working the night of the elections. The Hilton was fully booked so I was unable to stay there, I had arrived late and had had a long flight. They did there upmost to contact other hotels for me to see if they had any availability and directed me when I was lost to that hotel. For this reason the Hilton would always be my first choice for Airport Hotel when staying in Philly, due to their staffs incredible customer service.

“Great location, clean room” My wife and I stayed at the hotel for a conference. positives: It's in a great location; two blocks from the Convention Center and a block from the 16th Street mall and pedestrian mall. The staff was very friendly. The room was clean. free wireless (although it wasn't password protected and that was a bit disconcerting). Two computers and free printing available 24 hours a day in the lobby. The beds were comfy, although a bit too soft for me. Bathroom was clean with great water pressure in the shower. Did like the fact that the room was completely dark when the curtains were pulled (they provided a handy little clip) and the door was closed. It was also quiet. Our room temp was just fine and we were in Denver when it was 65 one day and below zero four days later. The AC/heater would kick on erratically; running for 30 seconds and then stopping; but it wasn't that obnoxious. negatives: The sheets were a bit abrasive. All the pillows were soft; I'd prefer a firm pillow or two. Not much to look at from the outside because the rooms are in a high rise above a parking garage. Room had a crappy 27" CRT television with a curved screen. They didn't offer a program where you could designate that the cleans and towels shouldn't be laundered. So we left a note for housekeeping and they honored our request. I can't speak to the elevators, because I'm claustrophobic and use the stairs.

“The Return” I was given a room with private bathroom (the type I booked online) that was facing the street (Grant) because it was the only one available at the time that I checked in at approx. 11:30 am. I liked the brightness due to natural sunlight but since it was facing the street, city noise was a constant. The noise was the most disruptive during my 3-night stay, at times being awakened in the middle of the night. Next time, in ANY of my trips, I would remember to try to bring ear plugs, just in case. My room, just like my first time stay at the hotel in June 2011 visit was adequate for my needs. It was very basic but clean and well kept. There was a box TV (with remote control, this time!) and a refrigerator where I primarily kept water that I purchased from Walgreens. The hotel was a reasonable budget lodging during summer time (late August). I always appreciate a clean and safe place to stay for sleep, showering, and staying in to a comfortable bed after a full day of sightseeing and exploring. The price also fit my budget.

“Hotel Does a Disservice to Doubletree Name” Five night stay the week of Christmas. Did I make the wrong hotel choice? For me, the answer is YES. For others, maybe not. This property was originally built as a condo development and the design flaws therein are self-evident. This place would have been called a "traveler's hotel" when that term was widely used to describe lower-end, budget hotels that had a high transient rate. But let me start with the positives. The staff was gracious, polite, professional and helpful. The hotel and rooms are clean. The bed was comfortable and there is a large flat screen TV in each room. It has windows that open enough for fresh air. The climate control works well. The street is very quiet for Manhattan. So, in essence, this is a very nice BUDGET hotel. Now here's the problem - I don't consider Doubletree to be a budget chain and I hadn't planned in staying in one on this trip. I've stayed in tons of Doubletrees, mostly on the West Coast. They tend to be comfortable, upscale properties. Not this one in New York's Chelsea neighborhood. This one has budget written all over it, from the tiny lobby to the two overworked elevators to the tiny hallways and tiny rooms. Not only are the hallways tiny, but the noise is awful. People slamming doors and talking loudly like they're right outside your door. It reminded me of living in a dorm or rooming house. As Hilton Diamond member, I thought I'd get upgraded to a larger room. But no, not here. They seem to attract a sort of Eurotrash family clientele and younger visitors to the Big Apple. Even though the staff has been most pleasant, I would not ever stay here again or recommend it.

“Spacious for NYC but faded” The room was much larger than NYC standard, no claustrophobia. Fixtures were old but in fine shape, and I very much like having a mini-kitchen for breakfast and midnight snack. The bed itself was below average in comfort (also true when I stayed at the Beekman Hotel sister property). The location is several blocks from the nearest subway entrance.

“Perfektes Airport Hotel” Ich war nur eine Nacht im Juli 2009 zu Gast in dem Hotel. Wir benötigten ein Hotel in der nähe vom Flughafen, und da passte das Hotel perfekt. Da wir über hotwire buchten, war es sogar sehr günstig. Airport Shuttle klappte sogar noch kurz vor Mitternacht perfekt. Checkin um 1h Nachts war kein Problem. Sehr sauber, und netter Service.

“A delightful little hotel in a wonderful location” The Jewel is on the northern border of Rockefeller Center, within easy walking distance of all of mid-town Manhattan's greatest attractions. Yet it's quiet enough to be relaxing. Price is fair. Our room was small, but the furnishings are extremely well thought out, ultra-modern, and of high quality. The service is cheerful and efficient. The lobby is small, but there are additional facilities on the next level -- but you'll want to be out and about most of the time, anyway. Great way to start a visit to Manhattan is to take the Rock Center architectural tour (great guides) and then go up to the Top of the Rock for a marvelous "overview."

“Not the Worst, but wouldn't come back” I stayed at the Westin on N. Michigan Avenue during Memorial Day Weekend. First off, we landed in O’Hare and took the subway to the hotel. After switching trains in downtown Chicago and walking 6 blocks we finally arrived at the hotel. There are only two things going for the Westin on Michigan Ave, it’s location to shopping and the Westin Heavenly Bed. One of which you could get at another Westin or Starwoods property and the other via taxi. Check in was quick and since I am a “preferred Starwoods Member” I was told I was upgraded to a higher floor reserved for “preferred members”. The room did not appear to be “preferred”. It was directly behind the service elevators and I could hear the elevators operating all day and night. Luckily I brought ear plugs to wear while sleeping otherwise I would have gotten no sleep. Additionally, the rooms themselves are not quiet. You could hear anyone and everyone in the hallways (and there were lots of unruly screaming children running down the halls too). The room itself was on the smaller side, a king size bed, two night stands, a bureau with TV on top, desk and soft chair with ottoman. My one complaint about the furniture, which I don’t usually comment on, was that there were not drawers on the nightstands only doors that opened to the space below. Additionally, there were no drawers in the desk either. The only drawers in the room were the 4 small drawers in the bureau under the TV. The other part of the bureau housed the refrigerator with stocked overpriced items. The bathroom was standard for a hotel room and appeared clean although the housekeeping staff never gave us an extra towel or soap or shampoo. Being a preferred member I also got free Wi-fi access, however, the wi-fi here was pathetic. I had faster service on my 3G phone than the wifi, it was a worthless benefit. A big beef I have with hotels is that the beds are not completely made. After sleeping in the bed once I once again found that the sheets did not reach the bottom of the bed and the mattress and the small mattress pad were exposed. I had to pull off all the sheets and covers so that the staff would correct it. Additionally, the Westin usually gives you extra pillows in the room, this Westin did not, however, housekeeping did provide us with a few extra pillows. Westin offers a workout facility in each of their hotels. I’ve been to some really nice hotel facilities and some not-so nice ones, this hotel ranks in the middle. They did provide dumbbells but had no cable machine and 4 plate type machines. There were also a couple of aerobic machines (treadmill/ellipticals) but not many. Our room did not have a view either. We overlooked another building across the way. As I stated in the beginning, the Westin Heavenly bed was the only plus to our visit. Would be stay here again? No, while we like Starwood properties, we would try another first. When you pay more money for a Starwood property, you expect higher service and quality. This property did not deliver.

“Great Rooms” The rooms at the Intercontinental Boston Hotel are on a par with the best luxury class hotel rooms, such as Four Seasons and Ritz Carlton. The only thing this hotel lacks is the level/quality of service and attention to the "little things". The rooms are fantastic. Spacious, well designed and very comfortable. The bathrooms are even better. Great tub and a separate shower; both with great fixtures. The sliding window between the bath and room is an innovative design that we enjoyed. But here is an example of a "little thing" that separates the great hotels from the very good. The IC linens are a 60/40 cotton/poly blend. Why not spend a few extra bucks on fine quality 100% cotton sheets? Other reviewers have made points about there not being a coffee maker in the room. I can live with that....Ritz Carlton and Four Seasons don't have coffee makers in their rooms either. I was glad to find complimentary coffee available in the lobby on Saturday (between 5:00 am and 7:00 am). However, when I went down on Sunday morning, I was told "we don't put the coffee out on Sunday". Why not? Another "little thing" that separates the great from the very good. Some other pros and cons. Pro: Nice outdoor area on Boston Harbor with an outdoor restaurant and benches for relaxing. Con: Music from outdoor restaurant was annoyingly loud. Pro: Great Location: Close to South Station MBTA, easy walk to North End. Con: $39 overnight parking. Tip: If you are there on a weekend and don't need your car, skip parking at the hotel. Drive cater-corner to the hotel to International Place. $9.00/day covered parking on the weekend and after 4:30 on Friday. Con: Most (not all) of the front desk and just about everyone else we encountered were not overly friendly. Not rude, but certainly not warm. Just sort of disinterested. Bottom Line: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at our Priceline rate. Had I paid rack rate, I might not feel the same way.

“Great weekend” We stayed at the Palmer House in Chicago on Friday and Saturday nights at the end of October 2005. We had adjoining rooms, one for us, and one for our 2 college-age daughters. Location couldn't be better. Moderate-priced shopping near the hotel, Nordstrom Rack, Filene's Basement, and better goods on North Micigan Avenue. The hotel is immaculate in the entry and lobby areas. Once upstairs, the age of the hotel, and the wear and tear are starting to show. But everyting is clean, and everything works. Still charming, but definitely not new.

“Convenient, Clean, Nice - Odd Vibe” For $52, the room was nice and clean. This place was standard renovated La Quinta, with the black and white tiled bathroom floor and room walls in various shades of white. Everything worked, including wi-fi. The bed was comfortable with nice linens. All basic needs were well-met. Breakfast was adequate but I've seen La Quintas do much better. Instead of waffle machines there were pre-packaged toster waffles which were surprisingly good but odd. There were just enough minor issues to make this place not worth more than about $60 per night. Among them: old-style hole-punched key cards, a cramped breakfast and lobby area, very small bathrooms, and a room heating unit with an automated fan that turned on and off throughout the night, making it difficult to sleep. This motel covered the basics quite well and was a very good value. For some reason, I just couldn't get comfortable.

“Great Decor, Good Service and Location” After a less than pleasant stay at Copley Square, I was not keen to stay at another Fairmont, however I was a guest of someone who booked this hotel so I did not wish to seem rude. Hotel is newer so rooms are are in a better condition.Well appointed bathroom as well. Staff were pleasant . Hotel is good for access to Faneuil/Quincy and North End. We ate all meals out , so cannot comment on food. Not too far a walk to get to Mikes for pastry or to Pizzeria Regina. Rate was actually quite cheap especially when comparing it to the poor experience we had in Marthas Vineyard which was more for motel type of accomodation. I absolutely do recommend this as an option in Boston.

“Okay...but try Priceline for a nicer hotel at a better rate” I list this hotel as 'Neutral/Average'. It wasn't great, but it wasn't horrible either. I'd like to see it after the updating is complete. It was pricey at $215 a night, but every hotel I looked up, either directly or through Travelocity, Expedia, Hotels, etc. was much more expensive. Apparently we were there a very busy weekend and most hotels were booked. I did happen to see another guests hotel receipt at $99 a night...not sure how they got it, but that's about what I would expect to pay at this hotel. If you stay here, request a corner room. We were in 928, so any floor w/ the room # ending in -27 or -28 will be a corner room and bigger than the others. It's a pretty good location too...in the Theatre District, just one block away from Boston Common. We found it easy to walk anywhere from here. Cab rides to/from the waterfront at night will run you $8. But walk everywhere during the day! The Freedom Trail starts not too far away from the hotel. I'd say it was an okay stay, although I'd probably try Priceline and book a nicer hotel at a better rate for the next stay.

“Nice” Stay in Hyatt Regency Chicago for my Christmas holiday. The deal is very good - USD$114 per night for a king-bed room with breakfast - I think it's because there is no conference/event in this hotel during this holiday period! Check-in is very efficient - the Staff is very nice and flexible. He realized that there are a few people checking-in in the dedicated gold-passport line and therefore, asked me to proceed to the general check-in counter because no one was there checking-in/out. Check-out process is also awesome - I did it through an Express check-in & out kiosk - it's very efficient and the bill is accurate! I was allocated a room at mid-level with a partial river view. The room is nice with ceiling-to-floor window and I like the design of the room, especially the work desk. For the Hyatt hotels that I stayed so far (except Hyatt Regency Shatin and Grand Hyatt Hong Kong) - the work desk is fixed and face towards the wall - which I usually feel not comfortable with. But for this hotel, the design is awesome - the work desk can be moved not to face towards the hall! The only drawback is that the room is quite dark. There are not enough lights especially at the corner close to the work desk. The location of this hotel is good - it takes only around 10 minutes to reach a train station (Clark/Lake blue line) in which you can take the train to the two airports in Chicago. It's also very close to Magnificent Mile and the Pier for taking water boats (but it's closed in winter, sadly...). The buffer breakfast at BISTRO At 151 is very good - Good quality of food and nice staff. The customer service at Stetson's Chop House, however, is poor. Though the food presented by this Chop House is very good and tasty, I will not take it again 'cause I do not feel I was served friendly.

“Great Marriott Property, obviously operated with the customer in mind.” I am generally a pretty laid back review writer. I tend to get a little more critical depending on the price of the room. I think that the more that when you pay top dollar for a room, you should have top expectations. I have stayed at plenty of Marriott properties, and generally, they are pretty average compared to other "luxury" properties. On this particular trip, I stayed a little further south than normal so I booked at the Marriott near the Hobby Airport. Considering where the property is, my expectations were not that high for this particular stay, however, every aspect of this hotel as far exceeded my expectations. The front desk staff were very warm and friendly, which I did not expect as there were only two of them and there was a line for check in. What a pleasant suprise. The room is typical for a Marriott property. Nice beds, comfortable appointments and a spacious restroom. The room was very clean and appeared to be exceptionally well maintained compared to other Marriott properties. Room service at the hotel is reasonably priced. The menu was simple but offered things for most tastes. I ordered a simple cheeseburger, and paid what I would have paid at a Chili's or similar place. The food was excellent. Why can't Chili's burgers be better than a late night room service burger? All things considered, this hotel is at the top of my Houston list for now on. It is easily accessible to the freeway, and heck, it is one of the nicest properties I have stayed at in a long time. I am very impressed. My hat comes off to the management and staff here.

“Better places to stay in Seattle..” Stayed here with my husband for one night. We booked through a third party deal, which included valet parking. Service was alright. We had to circle the streets and got honked at when we were trying to get valet to take our car. I actually had to run into the hotel while my husband circled the block yet again to let someone know we wanted to have our car valeted. Front desk was polite, although I had problems with my reservations in the beginning when I called to confirm; they had lost my reservation, but were able to rebook us. Decor was quirky. Our room was small. The washroom was TINY! Cleanliness was a bit of an issue. There was dust on the ledges and water marks on the table. It was quite stuffy in the room with very little light since there was only one tiny window. Our "view" was of the ducts and ventilation and we could see right into other people's rooms across the way. Location was the only saving point; it was centrally located. We were in Seattle to see the Symphony, and the Benaroya Hall was within walking distance. It was easy enough to explore Seattle on foot. Pike Place Market and Pioneer Square Mall and other shopping were in the area. When we're back in Seattle, we won't be staying here. There are better places to stay.

“Very cold all night” We printed the directions off of their website. We got severly lost and ended up on the other side of town. When we called for directions, the front desk agent gave us directions that had us heading into downtown Boston. You would think that if someone works there, that they would know how to get there? When we turned around and started heading back to where we had come from, we saw one of their vans SPEEDING through town. We followed him back. We got there an hour after we should have there. When we walked in, we were informed that there was a parking fee, when on the website, it had said nothing about it. When informing the clerk of this she did not apologize, just handed us a ticket to put in our car window. When we got up to our room, it was next to the stairs, firstly. That bothered me. It is known in the hospilatly industry that you save those rooms for sold out nights, and they were not sold out, far from it. Our entrance light did not work and our room was frigid. It wouldn't hurt if they turned on the heat before someone checks in. We turned the heat up to high and it took the full eight hours from 10pm until 6am when we got up, make the room warm. Luckily, when we go to a hotel, we always bring an extra blanket, because there is never enough blankets. and they are always so thin! Also, we were there for first night in Boston. The parking lot was extremely icy. I had sneakers on, but most of the other guests were going out the clubs and the girls had heels on. There was no salt on the parking lot anywhere. Someone could have slipped, I was afraid I was going to. I hate ice! The breakfast the next morning was cold, the eggs were cold, the coffee was burnt and I asked for sauages and I received bacon. I left a letter at the front desk with this information when we left and a comment card in the room and I have not received a phone call or an email. I worked in hotel for three years. I know how it runs. If my GM had received all these compliants from one person, he would have been on the phone personally apologizing. I am not impressed. We almost turned around and went home, just because the directions were so horrible. But we wanted to see the fireworks, so we went and we stayed and we ffroze. It was warmer outside, than it was in our room. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone!

“A Happy Accident” We pre-paid for 5 nights at The Palomar but due to overbooking we were moved to The Sofia for the last two nights. We were reassured that they would take care of everything, including moving us, the additional pet-fee and an upgrade to a suite. TOTALLY worth it!! This boutique hotel is much more beautiful on the inside than the outside. It's been completely renovated, and the service is not only personal, it's impeccable. Even our Cavalier King Charles Spaniel got her name on the Welcome Board - along with a lovely bag of treats and a hanging door sign (ruff or meow).....the only negative we can say is that the suites only come with a queen-sized bed. But also: 2 daily water bottles, a mini-fridge, a microwave, a sofa-bed, 3 overstuffed chairs w/ottomans, several huge plush bath sheets, great bedding, 2 (small) flat screen tvs, free wireless Internet, a hairdryer, assorted products and a coffee maker. There are also several coffee shops within the surrounding block, and The Horton Plaza Shopping Center is across the street. Great location, although parking is $$$ and there's a less-than-desirable indigent population all over downtown San Diego.

“Bestens” Dieses Hotel ist ein echter Lichtblick in einer Stadt, die sich gerade wieder selbst findet. Die Lage ist sehr zentral, innerhalb von Downtown ist praktisch alles innerhalb von rund 10 Minuten zu Fuss erreichbar. Die nähere Umgebung bietet zwar wenig Erfreuliches, dies gilt für andere Lagen von Detroit aber ebenso. Der Service war freundlich und problemlos. Die Zimmer sind nett und für amerikanische Verhältnisse freundlich eingerichtet sowie ausreichend groß. Die Gastronomie überzeugt mit einem Spitzenrestaurant, einem gemütlichen Restaurant sowie einem schlichteren Restaurant für Frühstück und Lunch; dazu die nette Motorbar. Dieses Westin dürfte zu den absoluten Tophotels der Stadt zählen.

“Good Hotel but be aware of the construction....” I stayed at the Hudson for business and followed up with the Millenium for pleasure as I stayed the weekend. The Millenium is pretty far. It's in "Soho" (although, it was very south of Houston Street.). in fact, it's literally beside the World Trade Centre. I could see the construction taking place from my hotel room - interesting but yet sad... There is a lot of construction going on in the area. Contruction at the WTC seemed to be 24/7 and you could hear it (and I believe there was a notice in my room indicating that - no wonder, I got such a good deal on a 4 star hotel in "Soho"). The room was a very good size (especially, compared to the Hudson). Modern decor (large flat screen) and a good view (WTC, water, etc.). Hotel lobby was decent as was the hotel bar. There is a Century 21 store across the street if you're into cheap shopping with brand names. Not sure if I would stay that far south next time, especially given the construction noise but it was reasonably priced for a 4 star in NY.

“Nice room.” Nice room. Nice bed. Nice bath. Well kept and clean. The common areas seemed very small. The exterior shows some wear and sandwiched between a couple of low rent motels with Dennys and a asian massage parlor across the street.

“Huge suite! Great Bar! Lovely Hotel!” I stayed at the Hotel Helix on a business trip and booked it through the Kimpton site. It is great little hotel and reasonably priced. The hotel was about a 25 minute drive from the Reagan airport in morning traffic. I stayed in one of the suites (room 1020). It is a huge suite. The living room area is really comfortable. It has a nice desk and work area. The free wireless worked perfectly. The mini-bar area was well stocked. The suite had a separate area with a huge closets. Of course they provide the standard Kimpton robes that I love. They also made sure I had my Kimpton amenities in my room when I arrived. It really is worth joining their members program. The bedroom is also quite large. The beds are firm and the linens were very nice. You should really look at their website. It gives you a perfect idea of what the hotel is going to be like. You either like that "hipster decor" or you don't. If you like what you see on their site...you will like the hotel. The bathroom was of average size. There were no outlets in the bathroom which was odd. They also didn't provide a blow dryer, but they did bring one up. They stock Aveda products in the bathroom. The towels were nice and there were plenty of them. We had drinks in the fun bar downstairs. There seemed to be lots of locals mixed in with the guests. The drinks were good, food was good and all reasonably priced. Valet parking is $33.60/night. The valet guys were quick and very nice. The front desk people were awesome. Check-in was quick. I loved staying at the Helix. It is a great hotel and I would highly recommend it.

“Comfortable and well located” The location is close to perfect. It's on a quiet street just off the GWU campus, yet a block from the Watergate complex and a half block from the GWU/Foggy Bottom Metro station. It's on a direct line from Reagan Natl Airport (takes maybe 15 mins) and anyplace else is quite easy to reach as well. Rooms are large, well they are suites, with kitchens, dining area, desk, living room, and bedroom. Wifi for $9.95 per day worked great, and my only complaint was the placement of the desk in the corner, looking away from the TV (I like to watch TV and work at the same time!). The staff was very friendly. No restaurant but the Notte Bianchi across the street was quite good, and the Watergate complex has a variety of places for food, takeout or eat-in. I plan to stay there again in a few weeks, but the rate went up $40.

“Thought We Were at a Hostel” Wow what a bad experience. It felt like a youth hostel in Europe which is not a good thing when your over 35! We stayed one night and left at 7 AM because we wanted to get the heck out! To make matters worse the parking was truly horrible.

“Four wonderful days of stay” I stayed at this hotel while I was attending a training seminar in Indianapolis. I had absolutely NO complaints whatsoever! Extremely quiet area, you get discount coupons to the Golden Corral restaurant that is right next door. I had a great nights sleep and everything was extremely clean and well maintained.

“great hotel” Tripadvisor is right. Thisis a great hotel. I paid $210 x 3 nights, at hotels.com, linked through kayak.com, for a weekend. I expected the lowest grade room. I don't know what I got, but it was great. King sized bed, not-so-great view, which is meaningless to me, and the usual 5* amenities and service. The staff is obvioulsy very well trained, as both the doorman and bellhop gave us an orientation. large room, especially for NY.

“Very Nice Experience” We stayed at the Downtown Courtyard over a weekend. We checked in very late/early Friday night/Saturday morning. Front desk staff greeted us enthusiastically. Our room was very spacious and the bed was very comfortable. However the previous warnings in previous customer reviews about the fitted sheets not fitting very well turned out to be true. Every night the sheets snapped back to expose the matress pad. Seems like an easily fixable problem - Marriott, buy some bigger fitted sheets to fit the king size beds! Problem solved! We ate in the hotel restaurant twice for breakfast. The wait staff were very friendly and accommodating. The food was quite good and better than average for hotel fare. One bit of advice though for anyone seeking room service dining - room service is only available between 5:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. The lobby and ground floor areas are quite grand with high ceilings and chandeliers. The building was originally built in the 1920's as the annex to City Hall and the hotel has kept that era's architecture intact. We were quite impressed with the hotel for its beauty and the great service we experienced. We would definitely stay here again. (Even with the "short sheets"!)

“Great property in great location” Stayed Labor Day weekend, 2011 for 4 nights total in two rooms. 2118 and 1624. Excellent and very modern property. 2118 is a King located on the 21st floor with a water view and direct view over the Roosevelt Hotel Sign across the street. This room is very spacious and comfortable. Ice however is not located on this floor. The bathroom is extremely large with a separate marble shower and large soaking tub. Includes all needed toiletries including toothpaste. A concern though was the lack of adequate lighting for applying makeup and the make up mirror with only a very small percentage of zoom. Internet and bottled water are available for an additional charge. Electronic minibar, Robe, large closet, iron, iron board, safe, large flat screen, radio with iPod player, electronic curtains with remote near bed. Concierge extremely helpful. This particular Hyatt did disappoint us with their lower end bedding. The mattress was creaky and very very uncomfortable. We asked members of our traveling party about their opinion on the mattreses, and they also felt the same way. Strange as other Hyatts we have frequented have never had this problem. Our 2nd room 1624 is a corner unit with a separate area for the living room and bedroom. The view was very nice as the bedroom has a corner window. This bathroom is smaller but gorgeous as well. Noticed some "stains" on the bedroom wall above the bed that should have been easily noticed by housekeeping. This room has two flatscreens and can be a used as a connecting room with an adjacent one. Bed was a little better but the same quality. This property is located in a very good location which allows easy access to all downtown areas including the monorail to the Space Needle. Taxis around the downtown/pier area run from $4 to $8. Very inexpensive. There is a Bus that runs near all the attractions that is free (Orange Line on your maps). Regency Club sort of surprised as we were charged $5 for drinks $4 for beer during their cocktail hours. I don't know if this is a new policy, but never had we paid for drinks before at any other Regency Club. Room is quite small. Breakfast was ok, typical continental, bagel, toast, lox, cereal, oatmeal, coffees, juice and a small selection of fruits. Staff was extremely friendly! I do recommend this hotel for a few days in Seattle or for a pre/post cruise stay.

“It’s Okay if You’re Okay with Just Okay” The Marriott Courtyard is just about as neutral as it gets for a downtown hotel. I found it to be “just okay.” But for the price, the Courtyard is a reasonable option. Yet even with a good rate (for Chicago in the summer), the total tab was over $500 for two nights’ stay including room, taxes, and parking. This was a work trip but being from Indy, I drove and took my family. Check-in was very friendly, as were the bellmen and doormen. The hallway had a bit of an odor but the room did not. The room was nicely decored and good sized. Beds were comfortable but only had down pillows (I hate down pillows, just a hangup I have). Climate control worked though it was hard to cool down the room even when cranking the A/C all the way. Room amenities included a coffee maker, mini-fridge, cheap hair dryer, iron, and ironing board. No room safe. Wired internet was free and worked well. Hallway noise was not good and I was awakened a number of times by people in the next room talking and coughing. The toilet was what I call a EuroFlush – powerful, industrial-strength flushing that sounds like a 747, often seen in Europe but rarely in the US – and could be heard through the walls. Cleanliness was neither bad nor great. An assortment of hair of various colors was pasted to the shower wall and even the ceiling. Corners of the shower and floor were grungy. Walls were stained and discolored in places. Caulking was messy. The shower room had no vent, so condensation collected on everything. Hotel amenities include a small pool, hot tub (which had some unidentifiable funk on the bottom that looked like sand or salt), and a nice outdoor deck with barbecue grills. A small business center had equipment that was all out of order. There is a lounge, a small commissary, a Starbuck’s in the lobby, and a restaurant called State Street Bread Company with surprisingly good food. Situated on the corner of State and Hubbard, the location is very good and only about a block from the intersection of Michigan Ave and Wacker Dr, from which you can see what has to be one of the most phenomenal cityscapes in the world. It is a short walk to much of what downtown Chicago has to offer. Like all of downtown Chicago, parking cost is an absolute nightmare and if you are driving you have to factor this in. The Courtyard charged $45 (self-park was $37) per night. Unlike many of the shameless downtown parking extortionists, the hotel does not try to trim more money off you by charging for “in and out privileges.” If you’re not familiar with this concept, it is the practice of charging you an exorbitant sum to park and then charging $5-10 each time you want to use your car. I doubt I would stay here again, simply because of the many other options available downtown. But if you are okay with just okay, I would recommend it. Hope this helps.

“Nice large resort like a country club” Stayed here one Weekday night in June for work with a great corporate rate. The resort is huge and has a country club feel to it. Checkin was easy and was upgraded to a terrace room for being a gold member. Room was large, and bathroom was huge with a separate shower and tub. Since I didn’t want to pay for valet parking, I parked myself in the parking garage, and it was a long walk to the room. The resort has all different types of rooms and villas and it can get a little confusing walking around, think I should have used my GPS I didn’t use any of the pools, but there was one around every corner. They also had several lounge inside and outside areas with water spray coolers which was a nice touch. As a gold member I got 2 free drinks (no free breakfast) at Wrights Bar, so I went down there to eat. They had a very good drink selection. Ended up getting escargot and a burger for dinner. Escargot was great and burger was ok. Their grounds are extremely well kept with a lot of trees, which brings a lot of birds around. One woke me up chirping around 5am. Went for a run about 6am, and there is a very nice dirt/gravel trail just outside the hotel entrance to the right which was crowded with runners and bikers at 6am. I definitely hope I get to stay here again. The hotel was very clean but furnishing were a little dated. Since I didn’t get to experience all the resort has to offer, I am only giving 4 stars...

“Best Hilton property at the airport.” If you need to spend an overnight near the San Antonio Airport this is the place to stay. Transportation to and from the airport with very nice rooms in a property that is not to big or small. Rooms are well furnished and very clean. The front desk staff are friendly and are very genuine. Cookies are still warm at check inn and they don't give you a look if you take more than one. The desk person even told me to "help myself there are plenty!" As a Hilton Diamond I get a free breakfast and the omelet that I was served was very good. Staying at the airport in San Antonio is boring but when the need arises this is the hotel that I would recommend.

“Decent Airport Hotel” This hotel is a five minute drive from the San Jose Airport. The free hotel shuttle service is very convenient. Rooms are decent size but otherwise unremarkable. The hotel common areas were clean and service overall was friendly. This is a good business class hotel if you have to catch an early flight out of San Jose.

“Camp for Grown-Ups - the kind of camp where you never want to leave!” My husband, Alan and I were looking for a place to get away and to recharge and we found it in Travaasa Austin. We just returned to Oklahoma City last night after spending three days in Austin. We brought so much knowledge about important life skills and just an overall peace with us that we had lost recently in the hustle and bustle of our daily lives and work commitments. I title this "camp for grown-ups" because it was the first impression I had on night one of our experience. You drive up a long drive in anticipation of what your "home away from home" will be the next few days and see separate buildings and beautiful grounds. The "cabins" are along the trail and you walk everywhere (short walks) once you are there. In walking to Jean's Kitchen, where you eat all your meals, I commented to my husband, I feel like I am at camp! We had our flashlight and were talking in whispers because it is so quiet and pretty dark but I realize that setting caused my mood to kick in to relaxed state and it stayed there for our three day experience. When talking about our time there, the one thing that Alan and I realized was so different from anywhere that we stayed is that we really felt like we connected with people there, mostly staff but some of the other guests. The atmosphere really encourages that. Because of the personalities and the wonderful talents, I want to recognize this in hopes that anyone reading this review will watch for your encounter with any of these people. Meeting them is worth your while for sure! We spent most of our time with Jillian, the activities coordinator. Jillian is highly talented in so many areas of health and fitness. Her knowledge is vast and her heart and willing ness to share and teach is unmatchable. I did the Resistance Ball class with her first off and it was a challenge for me but a good workout and I enjoyed learning some new exercises. We also did a Vision Board class under her instruction and it was such a good activity to focus on what we should be thinking about it in life instead of the incidentals of daily life. Jillian teaches a class called Serenity Stretch that I would love to see on DVD and to be able to use at home. It was wonderful. The last class we attended by her was on juicing. She used a Vitamix blender and we sampled three different blends from greens to almonds to fruit and about the tricks and important benefits of using this great tool. I really feel like I had a month's worth of good nutritional classes and will change some of my habits for the better. In the kitchen, we enjoyed the warm welcome and fun, wonderful service of Nick, Veronica, Craig and Drew. Meals were something to really look forward to so that you could see what was specially prepared that night (there are usually three entrees and a few appetizer and dessert choices). Seeing the friendly faces at mealtime was an added bonus. Loni and Janice were our massage therapists at the spa. We both had a deep tissue and for us both, it was one of our best massage experiences ever. Janice was able to increase my husband's range of motion in a long time frozen shoulder. It was amazing. Alissa and Jessie were most helpful at the Welcome Center with reservations, questions or any special accommodations that we needed. Susan did a Guided Meditation class for us the last day and it was just the experience to take home with us. It was held at the Solidago Gardens and I highly recommend going to this space while you are there for quiet mediation if nothing else. It is beautiful. The bedding is so comfortable that we may purchase some of it. After our wonderful experience and feeling so connected with the wonderful people at Travaasa, we plan to make this a two or three times a year recharge for us. It takes you out of your normal world and worries and I have found few places that do that and it is important. They said the experience differs from middle of the week vs weekend. Middle of the week is very quiet, less crowded and fewer activities (but still plenty). If you want the feeling of more camaraderie, weekends might be better. I think we will try both ways. Last few things to mention: the pool, hot tub, dry sauna are all very nice and we enjoyed them. Also we went with the Total Travaasa package and really enjoyed it. It took all the worry out of signing checks, adding gratuity, etc. It was nice to focus only on recharging. They make it easy for sure! Alan made the comment that the website doesn't paint the picture of how wonderful this experience is. I am pleased to see all the comments here on Trip Advisor because the website tempts you but doesn't answer many questions. In closing, like my younger years at leaving camp, I feel very protective of my experience at Travaasa and hope to keep that spirit alive and incorporate what we learned there into our every day life. I can't wait to return!

“One of my favorite hotels in the world...PERIOD!” I speak often of customer service. From Asia to Europe, to here at home....I often have the opportunity to talk about what it means to provide exceptional customer service. For many years, i have shared not one...but SEVERAL stories of where this property made an impression on me. This hotel is simply WONDERFUL! The location cant be beat. Its on the doorstep of Chicago's best.... The decor is terrific. I prefer a hotel that is not too 'fluffy', and this hotel features stunning artwork, classic furnishings...and a 'WOW' factor that makes me happy every time i walk in the doors. Nomi is a dining option that is rare in a 'Chain' hotel. Its a Chicago DESTINATION. From the view, to the incredible bar vibe...to the AWESOME food offerings, this is and continues to be a very popular Chicago TRADITION. Even if you arent staying here at the Park Hyatt, drinks at Nomi should be part of EVERY hotel stay. I have tried the Peninsula, The Four Seasons, The Ritz, and so many other Chicago hotels. I keep going back to Park Hyatt. The staff is what really sets this property apart. Wow...the stories i have to share. Wonderful, caring stories that will always make this hotel a favorite for me. Downside? None.

“great location, somewhat worn inside” Perhaps it's because we arrived soon after the local flooding, but the carpets smelled a little musty. We received a large room on the 10th floor. Everything was clean but seemed just a little worn. The bed was very comfortable, and the room was quiet. The staff was friendly and accommodating. Conveniently located near many shopping malls and the river. We got breakfast with our room upgrade, and the buffet had eggs, meat, potatoes, oatmeal, cereals, breads, cut fruit. Our evening drinks at the bar were expensive - about $9 each, but we got generous pours and there were cheaper options available. I'll stay again for the location and friendly staff.

“4.5 stars = remains an exeptional hotel, but room design is the only flaw” previously stayed in 1 of the standard rooms, but this time we went for the XL King Suite & purchased the pre-paid upgrade. we were upgraded to the buttonwood suite. positives: - amazinging space ... probably 1200-1400sf, with high ceilings & excellent design/layout - extra half bath (or WC to some) was great - plenty of windows with views of the river & city - hotel maintenance & service are at the typical 5-star level (though it is considered a 4-star, which i dont quite understand) - exceptional value ... suite would cost 50% in a similar quality hotel & the pre-paid upgrades are best value for money i have ever seen (though, part of discount due to location) - location ... as a former new yorker, i get that people want to be central (midtown) or in the trendy areas (village/soho/trbeca), but i like the financial district ... slightly undiscovered, and a 10 minute walk to tribeca, with execellent subway access negatives - the room design is just silly ... huge clear window on the shower room, directly facing the bed & no proper doors on the bedroom (separating from the living room) ... really? why? if you have gone to expense to get a suite with separate rooms, this is usually for a reason! (for me, i needed to work london time while my wife was sleeping)

“a bit disappointing” Just stayed @ the Residence Inn Charlotte Uptown this past weekend. I selected it because of the high reviews on Trip Advisor. The hotel was not full, but we were placed in a room overlooking the parking structure and empty field. Not very exciting, but the room was quiet and spacious for 2 (no room next door, only the stairwell). This hotel would be a good accommodation for longer stays because of the separate kitchen/living room setup. The bad: 1) the bed was not very comfortable --- experienced pressure pain from an unsupportive mattress 2) the carpets were not clean --- the soles of my slippers were very dirty when I returned home. The good: Very close to B of A Stadium, relatively close to Uptown. It was good, but it didn't impress me.

“Easy, clean business hotel” Such an easy business hotel. The rooms are clean and comfortable - great beds. I stayed in both March and October of 2011 and the upgraded corner suite is worth the request. In March the room I had was a joined room and the parents with two children adjacent were quite noisy. The hotel staff was quick to remedy and handle one I said something. The check-in and check-out is pleasant and efficient. This isn't a frills hotel however it is a clean, comfortable and convenient place to end a long business day that is nicely done and kept. Super easy and used to the business traveller. Great value.
