Perks and plusses include the small necessity shop inside and coffee/deli counter/bar for quick bites & drinks. Being across the street from a Walgreens was convenient and the myriad of restaurants within short walking distance is ideal. Flight is a 2-minute walk and a must for a drinks, appetizers or dinner. The nearby Mesquite Chop House did a fantastic job on porkchops and steaks with a funky little bar. Walking distance to Beale Street - it that's on your agenda. Car service to and from the airport runs around $40-50.

“A cozy boutique hotel with a restaurant and wine tasting that is excellent.” I totally enjoyed my stay. Everyone was courteous and kind. The wine reception exceeded my expectations as did the restaurant. I will certainly return.

“Good basic hotel in downtown Chicago” We looked for something downtown for our visit to Chicago, and the location of this Holiday Inn Express was perfect. The room was pretty small, but had recently been renovated and looked good, was well organized and had all the standard ametities. The staff at reception were friendly, and the breakfast was basic but perfectly acceptable.

“A few quirks” Just back from 2 nights at this hotel, our client's choice. I suspect this is a 'independently owned & operated' HGI, which would explain some of the very un-HGI quirks I noticed while there. 1. Mattress' aren't even pillow-topped, much less Select Comfort which are now standard @ HGI's. For a property this new (allegedly) I would expect the pillow-top at minimum. This is, for me, the biggest draw back to this property, but then, I am a self-confessed hotel bed snob :-) My colleague & I had just finished 3 nights @ the HGI in Shreveport, which does feature the Select Comfort bedding, so it was even more noticeable to both of us. 2. Daily newspaper is El Paso Times, not USA Today as is the norm & as is even listed on the hotel's website. 3. Complimentary bottled water is direct from Albertson's, not the HGI-branded bottles one usually receives. 4. Officially there is no hotel shuttle, however, there is a large van parked right outside the door w/HGI markings. Front desk said it could take guests to the airport but that 'drivers rely on tips'; again, not HGI standard. It was impossible to get truly hot water out of the bathroom sink & water pressure was an issue. The restaurant downstairs was a bit on the hit/miss side-dinner the first night was fine, but breakfast the first morning was not. A 20+ minute wait for omelets & only 1 actually arrived; to their credit, mgmt comped that breakfast as we didn't have time to wait for the 2nd one. The lobby, lounge, & restaurant are lovely with very nice fittings & plenty of seating, however. All in all, not bad but definately not on par w/other HGI's I have stayed in simply because of the bedding & because of that I'm not able to recommend it.

“GREAT Location! Clean. Walking distance from Union Station” I stayed here for 1 night. I arrived by train and it was a 10 min walk from Union Station. Check in was very easy and the staff was great. The room was clean. the bed soft and the bathroom was big. The water hot water was very hot. This is a big plus for me. The buffet was $23.00 and was pretty extensive. The wifi was $10.99 for 1 night. Walking distance to the US Capitol and subway stops. I would stay here again.

“Good hotel in fashionable Back Bay” I came here recommended by TripAdvisor's reviewers and I am happy I did. I stayed for a week while working and all was good. I particularly enjoyed the location close to 'everything that matters'. My room was huge and think it was a free upgrade to a junior suite, but they never said. It was a corner room (911) with nice views of Copley Square and other parts of Boston. A huge canape full of crisps, chocolates, peanuts and other goodies was waiting for me in the room and I thought it was part of the paying bar. It took me two days to realize it was a present from the hotel. What a treat! The restaurant and the bar downstairs are both very trendy and good and the lobby is smallish but nice. Service was excellent but the concierge and limo service could have been a bit better. The corridors are very wide and it has that charm of a by-gone era, which also means that the furniture is very old, not antique, just old, and depending on your taste you may want to prefer it a bit more contemporary or refreshed. A well-known local designer friend of mine called it ' a bit tacky'. Other than that very good but a bit pricey.

“nice location and very good rooms” i was here for a small conference and it was perfect. the rooms are small but very comfortable, clean and nice. there is a great restaurant that has a nice brunch on sunday. it is close to the historic walk which takes you through all the Boston landmarks so the location is excellent. it was also close to the pier so can walk there as well.

“How does one get hairs on the ceiling?” While traveling over 2,000 miles in five days with a pregnant wife, sister, brother-in-law and their cat to visit the parents for Thanksgiving, we decided to stay in Memphis for a night's rest. I got a room at this hotel via Priceline, and it was not one of my better Priceline experiences for either quality of price. First of all, it is unclear how to get to this hotel from the freeway (you have to make a U-turn and go into a gated entrance), and there isn’t any signage to help one out. Late night check-in was efficient but not courteous. That being said, the located in a median between the lanes of a split highway is very safe and well lit. Most of the common areas were dirty, especially the stairways, and no carpet, fixtures, etc. seems to have been refreshed for at least 5-10 years. The double beds were comfortable but too small for me, a pregnant lady and a twenty pound feline. The carpet and furniture seemed dingy and there were unpainted repairs to the woodwork. While the bathroom seemed clean, I noticed that a few hairs (and not the ones found on your head) were somehow adhered to the ceiling, a fact I did not point out to my companions until we were back on the road to protect their gag reflexes. I have stayed in freeway motels that were classier than this place and do not know how Priceline rated it at 2.5-3 stars. I can say, however, that the wireless internet and TV worked fine and that we successfully sneaked the cat in and out without incident. I was disappointed with the room for the rate I paid and would have been really peeved if I had shelled out for rack rates.

“A Great location for an NYC visit.” We stayed for 8 nights last month. At first our rooms were on the 6th floor but we moved after 1 night because of the street noise. Our rooms on the 27th floor were not connecting but next to each other and it worked out fine. It was much quieter and a bit more spacious. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The refrigerator and microwave came in handy. The staff was friendly and helpful.

“Beautiful Lobby, Good location” Just returned from a 3 day stay in Boston (July 2004). The Fairmont Copley Plaza is located in a great area just in between Newbury Street and Boylston Street which are two major shopping streets. The hotel has a lot of old world charm. We stayed in the newly renovated rooms, are room was actually one of the smallest rooms they have. The room was fine and bathrooms just fine as well. This is an old building, so it is not sound proof, but, when your in a large historical city, it's nice to stay in a historical hotel. The only complaint we had was the business center. We did not bring our laptop because we had read about their business center. This was a mistake. The business center which consisted of one computer, was only open until 5pm and seemed to close periodically throughout the day. For such a large property this was a little disappointing. This hotel is a good choice for it's location and I would stay here again. Enjoy Boston!!

“Great value” I got a room for an amazing price on Hotwire and was very pleased. The hotel has a 21/2 star rating that I don't understand. The rooms were large and clean, the staff was friendly and the breakfast of waffles, sasuage gravy and biscuits among other offerings was good. It is a short distance off the highway as well. The only negative was the sound from the hall did carry.

“Good room for NY” I stayed in NY for 3 nights and this hotel was worth the price. Ok, the rooms are not very big, but it's NY. I have stayed in a more expensive hotel in NY where the rooms are even smaller. The location is excellent, the staff are very nice and helpful and the rooms are clean. Since I'm not in NY to stay in an hotel room, this was great.

“Convenient location in Soho” This Sheraton is very conveniently located on Canal St between Wooster & West broadway. It is one of the newer SPG Sheraton and therefore, the hotel lobby and rooms do look somewhat new. The service is good and better than the nearby W downtown, which I stayed the previous week. Keep in mind, Canal St is busy almost all day with crosstown traffic congestion due to the holland tunnel access. So it may not be for everyone! In addition, Canal street isn't one of the pretties street in NYC. On Sunday early mornings, it can be quiet but that is when you see all the litter. Otherwise, the hotel is perfectly located minutes from centre of soho and within walking distance to WTC and 9/11 memorial. We walked to brooklyn bridge from here in 15 min. If you wish to avoid the crowd and Chinatown activities, exit the hotel and cross Canal Street into Wooster or West Broadway for a more pleasant walk. Avoid walking along Canal St. We had to request for a room change due to noise from the traffic on a lower floor. The upper floors do have a remarkable view of midtown depending on which side the room faces. The wifi Internet is good in some rooms but can be spotty on the corner room away from the routers. Bring your own router to connect to the Ethernet cable and off you go at blazing speed. We didn't dine at the restaurant but the breakfast buffet option for $14.95 seem reasonable. The beds are comfortable. The rooms size are reasonable for NYC. Some reviews complained on the size and noise. This is NYC and not the adirondacks. I wouldn't eat anywhere along Canal St. Walk a few blocks into soho on Prince St. or Elizabeth St. for better options. I would stay again if the rates are reasonable and if there are deals.

“>Consigliatissimo. Ci tornero' sicuramente” Posizione ottimale. a pochissimi passi dalla metro Grand Central Station. Staff cordiale e attento nel risolvere i problemi. Stanza ampia e ben arredata con bagno pero' piccolo. L'hotel mette a disposizione gratuitamente, la mattina il caffe' per la clientela, idem due bocce d'acqua fresca a disposizione tutto il giorno, al gusto di arancia e limone nella hall. Che dire, il prossimo anno devo tornare a new york, e senza dubbio ci andro' ancora. Consigliatissimo

“Excellent hotel, SHAME about their care for members” I have been going to many dIfferent Marriott hotels, generally they are very good, people that work there are very friendly this time , in general, it was no difference except by the crazy RECEPTION personnel that stick to their rules that your check up can NOT be extended longer than 2 hours or you mustr pay. I find this to be totally out of place, particularly considering that I have been a member of the Marriott and as such they should have more consideration for regular clients and particularly when the hotel is more thyan half empty anyway.

“Great Location, Odd Hotel” I love a boutique hotel - as a matter of fact i prefer them. But this one was just odd. The decor is reminiscent of a hip hotel designed in the 90's - but I hear that this one is actually rather new, so I'm a little confused. The beds are quite comfy, so I'll give credit where credit is due. That said, the remainder of the room is eclectic to the point of annoying. The green dresser, the obnoxious book shelf stereo, the oversize lamps hanging over the bed, it was all just, well.... odd. And possibly trying too hard. But, to Kimpton's credit, I did just stay at their Eventi in NYC, which was awesome, so I wouldn't rule out Kimpton Properties, just maybe not this one...

“Grand lobby, horrible room” When I first entered the Grand Hyatt Hotel in NYC I was very impressed. There was a beautiful waterfall, a wonderful lobby, little shops, a coffee bar and an inviting atmosphere. Also, the hotel was connected to Grand Central Station. Unfortunately, it stopped there. There were bellhops—but, I guess they were on a break, none of them offered to help with our luggage. And the coffee bar, no one to man the espresso machine either. Oh well, with a Starbucks on every corner, we decided to get coffee elsewhere. Since we were staying on points, we opted to upgrade and stay on the concierge level for a few extra points, we figured we were pretty safe—you know, a little extra TLC. No, wrong. First off, our room was the size of a walk in closet; our bathroom was so small that when trying to blow-dry my hair, I kept hitting my elbow on the door jam. And forget about taking a relaxing bath, there was mold in the corner, and random hair on the walls and floor, so I decided to shower instead. It was quite disgusting. And the beds were not that comfortable. I am very glad that we didn’t stay more than 1 night; it just might have ruined my trip! Now I’ll say something nice. They did serve Starbucks coffee and the food was pretty descent. That’s about it for me.

“Great hotel for a stay by the airport” The service at this hotel is great. We arrived late at LAX and calle the hotel for the free shuttle. It showed up quickly and the airport was a short ride away. Check in was easy and the room was nice. A great way to start an LA weeeknd. The next morning we were able to walk to the car rental places (only a few blocks away) and we were on our way quickly.

“Good location for mid-town business” This Hilton was updated just a couple of years ago and looks and feels great. It's a busy mid-town hotel with great lobby bars. The rooms are compact, but have all the necessities that you need and some of the luxuries that you want! The front desk is well staffed and the elevators are fast!

“Very good "bland" hotel...” Don't expect any charm, flair, or ambiance - the Hilton Garden Inn in Philly is located next to a drab, exhaust filled street tunnel where buses and cabs idle all day and night. About a five minute wait to check in with a desk clerk who was efficient but only perfunctory polite. The view from my room (I requested a quiet room away from the elevator and ice machine) was of the parking garage - none of the Philly skyline and no greenery was visible. Despite the borng, sterile, concrete environment, the locale is a convenient walk to Chinatown, convention district, and Center City. And the room fulfilled my three primary criteria: it was quiet, mattress was comfortable, and plenty of hot water in the bath . I also appreciated the large flat screen TV, mini-fridge, and microwave. Absolutely nothing in the room or bath to complain about. A late night "Wawa" convenience store is just across the street but use extreme caution (do not let children venture there alone) as both the Wawa staff and many of the patrons are surly ghetto types - watch for pickpockets and purse snatchers especially when at the ATM. However, the Hilton itself is safe and athough the locale is hardly upscale, my stay at the Hilton Garden Inn was completely stafisfactory and represented probably one of the best priceline deals ($66 total with tax and fees) I've ever booked for Philly...

“Close to Luxury” this hotel has a great location for getting around Seattle. Our room was comfortable, but there was no hardware on bathroom sliding door, so it would not stay closed - there is very little parking in this area - Hotel parking is $28.00 a nite, pricey We did book a travel "deal" and front desk - wanted to remind us that we were getting a special "rate." they did let us check in early. We would stay here again for a special occasion- but not at full price.

“Excellent location for a car free traveler” I stayed three nights at the Wilshire Crest Hotel and liked it very much. The room was big, quiet (I didn't notice any neighbor noises), and dark at night. It certainly wasn't fancy--there wasn't even a radio (and blessedly no minibar). The furnishings are perfectly fine, but not stylish. The Wilshire Crest is a two story hotel with no elevator, and there are no views to speak of, although the Orange St. side looks out on a pleasant residential street. There's free wireless internet, unlikely some fancier places I stayed. Staff was helpful. I almost never eat free hotel breakfasts, they rarely seem to be much good, and there are lots of good places close by for breakfast. At $125 per night, the money you save compared to other area hotels will fund your breakfast. There were a couple of hiccups, the room door one room required some jiggling of the key to open. The flush handle on the toilet was a little loose--it worked OK, but it should have been fixed and wasn't. I actually stayed in two different rooms because there was a break in my stay--both were good. As previous reviewers have noted, you can walk to a lot from here--the Los Angeles County Museum of Art and "Museum Row", the Farmers Market/Grove, restaurants on 3rd St. There's a strip mall with several restaurants a block away on Wilshire Blvd.--Cafe Latte is a very nice breakfast/lunch place. Walkscore--which rates how accessible stores and services are by walking--gives the Wilshire Crest a 97 out of 100, putting it in the top 2% of walk-accessible locations in the city of Los Angeles. Transit here is very good. I stayed without a car with no problem. Wilshire Boulevard has very frequent bus service west to Beverly Hills, Westwood (UCLA) and Santa Monica, and east to Koreatown and Downtown LA. Wilshire & Fairfax, about a 5 minute walk away, has a Rapid bus stop, and the Rapids move along quite nicely. Fairfax Ave. has good bus service north to the Fairfax commercial area (if you don't feel like walking) and Hollywood. There are also connections all along Fairfax to east-west bus routes like Beverly Blvd. Because the Wilshire Crest is very central to the visitor-oriented parts of LA, the travel times to these places are reasonable.

“交通至便。ホテル内も快適!” 主人の出張に付き添って宿泊しました。夜遅くの到着だったのですが、空港から近くなので、体が楽でした。空港からホテルに行くためには、自分でホテルに電話して呼ばないと、シャトルバスは来ません。ターミナルによっては、少し歩きますが、徒歩でホテルまで行くことは可能でした。 観光に行くためにダウンタウンに行くには、15分置きに出ているシャトルバスサービスを利用して地下鉄駅まで行き、ダウンタウン中心部までトータルで1時間以内に到着できたと思います。 部屋は快適、清潔でした。

“Pricy but good airport hotel” I had to attend a large tradeshow in Boston in September 2008. The only option I had for the dates I was attending was the Hilton. I don't normally stay in airport hotels because I find them overexpensive and usually underdeliver service. I was glad that this hotel, although really expensive (likely due to the tradeshow), was a decent hotel. You cannot beat the convenience of the hotel. You don't ever have to step outside Logan Airport if you arrive in Terminal A. I walked from the plane directly over to the hotel via a skybridge in less than 10 minutes. The skybridge dumps you off by the conference area of the hotel. A little extra signage would have been helpful, but I managed to find the lobby to check in without too much hassle. Check in was quick and the staff helped me with understanding the bus routes for the tradeshow. My room was on a lower floor with the most dreadful view of roofs, pipes, and a slice of road. Fortunately, the noise from the airport was minimal, although you could hear the occasional jet taking off. The room is done in a minimalist style, very cool and gray. It was pretty masculine looking, but the bed was comfortable. The desk was useful for getting work done but the chair was a bit difficult to sit in for long periods of time. The hotel pub restaurant is a good option for those staying here. I was hesitant to eat there, because you really are a captive audience. But the portions were huge, prices were reasonable and the service was really good. I ended up eating there twice during my stay and the waiter remembered me on my second visit. I really liked the convenience of the hotel. If I absolutely had to choose between one of the Logan hotels for a future visit, I would want to return to the Hilton, as long as the price was not too outrageous.

“Very nice hotel in a nice area” My husband had to travel recently to Austin on business, and since I had never been there I decided to accompany him and we stayed at this hotel, which he frequently stays out while on business in Austin. This is a nice hotel. The people were all very nice and the room was clean and well appointed. The "courtyard" of the hotel is very nice, a huge ceiling with rooms facing the inter courtyard. It is close to lots of nice shops and restaurants (Cheescake Factory comes to mind). There seemed to be lots of business travelers here as there were several conferences going on, so this would be an ideal place for a business traveler. I recommend this hotel and hope to someday accompany my husband there again.

“Location, Location, Location!” This hotel is in the heart of downtown Denver, right on the 16th Street Mall. There are many shops, pubs, restaurants nearby. I was there for a race, and the convention center was just a couple of blocks away. The hotel is clean, modern, and safe. The heated pool on the 4th floor offers great views of the surrounding skyscrapers. I was very happy with this hotel.

“If you hate the Times Square crowds, use a different exit.” But I loved the hotel, had a room on the 32nd floor with a river view, two double beds. Luxurious bedding, great service. The View Bar, is not to be missed on the 48th floor as it revolves. Also a great bar on the 8th floor overlooking Times Square. You must also check in on the 8th floor. A huge bank of elevators, never a long wait.

“Nothing special” Ask for a renovated room! I was staying in a renovated room, while my friend was not, so I got to compare them both. They have great beds and I got a good night's sleep. That is always the priority to me! Some of the hotel is a bit dated and unstylish, but if you are travelling on business and a good night's sleep is your priority, you will be happy. Towels and toiletries are nice too. The hotel is on the Riverwalk, which can be convenient, but can be loud at night. If this is a concern, request a higher floor. The balconies are large and a nice touch. The breakfast buffet and parking are ridiculously expensive. I pay less for both when I travel to New York City! The fitness center has great weights and some nice machines, but half of the cardio machines were broken during my visit. The best benefit of this hotel is they have a free washer and dryer for guest use! It's in the workout room, so you can babysit your laundry and workout at the same time. They sell laundry soap for only 50 cents. The pool stays open late, but is small and plain. If I were travelling for leisure and had time to enjoy the hotel, I prefer the Marriott Plaza. This is fine for business though, if you are on someone else's dime!

“Great value in the middle of everything” We were a bit disappointed when the boutique hotels were all booked and we were left with the Omni as our best alternative. Now we see how lucky we were. We had a large spacious room with the best of Philadelphia right outside our door. The service was friendly and helpful, as well. We will now be disappointed in future visits if the Omni is NOT available.

“Nice spot on the riverwalk” Checked in on Saturday afternoon for 1 night. It's easy to find just a few blocks from the Alamo. If you walk downstairs you are literally on the riverwalk. Our room faced in on the inside of the hotel but was high enough that we didn't hear anything. Pros - Location, dark room (good to sleep in), very comfortable bed Cons - Parking $27, AC never went below 70 degrees, small pool Booked on Priceline which saved almost 50% off advertised price (name your price). Compared to the other hotels in the neighborhood I'm glad I was at the Hyatt.

“Great location, but guest room is like a 3 star hotel...” I stayed at this hotel for one night last November on vacation and one night in June for a trade show at convention center. I really like the location; it’s very close to China Town where I love exploring food and only a block away from convention center. However the room I stayed at this time was terrible. The bath room is very outdated with a very cheap sink like you may only find at a motel. To my disappointment, the bed was not only uncomfortable, but a bit unsafe in my opinion with the sharp corners of the steel bed frame sticking out (bed frame is oversized for mattress). When passing the narrow area between the bed and work desk, I bumped into the steel corner of the bed frame and bruised myself. I reported the incident to the hotel management for them to rid this safety concern. Anyhow I guess I will try to avoid this hotel next time even the location is such a plus. By the way, D.C. hotels in summer time can be very expensive. If you're planning a vacation there, I'd suggest avoiding summer.

“Very nice place and a great value.” A nicely refurbished classic old hotel with elegant public areas and modern, comfortable, spacious, well-supplied, and well-operating rooms. Friendly staff in the lobby. Just three blocks to the Art Institute and a few more blocks to State Street shopping and some of the business centers. All in all a very pleasant place and a great value (though the tapas restaurant inside was overcrowded and overpriced). Highly recommended.

“Couldn't have been nicer!” Enjoyed a three night stay here over 4th of July. My first room faced an inner courtyard and was very noisy. My request to move was honored and luggage moved for me. Concierge was very helpful with restaurant recommendations. Wine hour was great -although busy and they didn't enough glasses for everyone all at once. Oh well, a cold beer tasted good, too! Great location and pleasant staff. Give this hotel a try!

“Good Location” Friendly greeting and no problem with checking in early. Had information to hand regarding the Texas Fair and how to get there. Generally a very positive first impression. Our room was smaller than most of those on our Texas trip, but certainly adequate. The bed was very comfortable and there was a nice squishy leather settee. Bathroom was quite spacious and well equipped. Initial impression of room was that it was very dark. It needed better lighting and lighter paint on the walls. Breakfast is included in the room rate and includes a hot buffet, plus cereal, yoghurt and fruit juice. 2 free glasses of good house wine or beer are also included during "cocktail hour". Breakfast and cocktails are taken in the lounge bar area. There is also free wi fi throughout the hotel. Bearing this in mind, it seems a shame that there is a charge made for the bottled water left in the room and for internet access on the business centre computers. Valet parking was also the most expensive that we encountered. The hotel was not busy, so we were able to have a late check out (3pm) we appreciated this, although thought that the $50 + taxes charge was a bit steep. The hotel is in an excellent location for sightseeing. The fascinating 6th Floor Museum and the Arts District are an easy walk away. The Dart light railway is also very close - we used it to get to and from the Texas Fair. There is a good Iron Cactus restaurant and bar immediately behind the hotel, which does excellent appetisers and cocktails. For a better choice of drinking and dining, it could be worth taking the free trolley uptown (leaves from the Arts District, near the Sculpture Garden). The trolley runs every 25 minutes throughout the day until about 10pm. Overall the Magnolia provided a comfortable stay in an excellent downtown location. We would recommend it.

“Good Stay” I recently stayed 4 nights at this location for a conference. The hotel is going through a renovation on the main level. They are adding a waterfall behind the elevator and making changes to valet area outside. The staff was great. The location was wonderful. More than enough places to eat and shopping within walking distance. The room was great. Alot of space which is a plus for me. My only negative was parking. The hotel only offers valet at $30 a night. They do tell you about a self service lot that is cheaper but it does not offer in and out privileges. My issue with parking is that with the renovation. When valet brought me my vehicle, the cars have to park in a single file line. So I had to wait for the car in front to load or unload before I could leave.

“Finally, a good, inexpensive way to stay in Manhattan!” SUMMARY - Although the GEM Hotel is associated with the Choice Hotels chain (Quality, Comfort, Econo, etc.) this is the first time I've heard of this particular branding. They are billed as a "Botique Hotel" and certainly fit the bill as much as a chain can be considered a "Botique". The place is very bare bones and minimal, yet very stylish and modern. They just give you the very basics of what you need and not much else, but the price reflects that. So it's hard to complain. There are 10 floors and approximately 4 small rooms/floor. It's not the kind of place I'd spend a whole week because it's rather small, has limited storage, and very few of the "extras" you'd need for an extended stay. But for staying a night or two in NYC when you just need a place to sleep and shower it does just fine. I forgot to take photos this time, but as of today the photos the hotel has provided on various travel websites are fairly accurate. You just have to take a close look at them to see how small the space really is and understand that the photos really show the WHOLE room. There's not much cropped out! BATHROOM: Clean, basic, and modern. It was pretty much a standard hotel sized bathroom, even though the main room was small. BEDS: Two double beds. Very comfortable, leaning towards the soft side of hotel beds. Sheets were clean and more modern/stylish than you'd find in most chain hotels. BILLING: Reserved via choicehotels.com only a few days ahead of time. The front desk had no problems getting us checked in, and the taxes/surcharges only added up to another 16% of the cost of the room itself. BREAKFAST: There is free coffee/tea in the room, but i never looked for a continental breakfast. There were vending machines in the basement with the ice/water machine. CLEANING: The room was as clean as it gets. While the building is obviously old, it seems that the entire interior is brand new. CLIMATE CONTROL: There was a brand new heater/air conditioning unit that was very quiet and easily adjustable. ELEVATORS: One main, new looking elevator in the lobby. It worked just fine and was fairly large. FRONT DESK: The front desk was helpful and competent. We had to wait about 15-20 minutes for a room to be cleaned. They may have had the smallest, most basic lobby i've ever seen in my life. But if you're looking for water fountains and gold trim you're not going to get it in a hotel with sub-$200 rates! GYM: None. HOT TUB: None. INTERNET: Didn't try it. I was too busy enjoying the city. LOCATION: On the west-side on 36th very close to the corner of 10th. It's a much more sparsely populated and quiet area than most of Manhattan, as it borders on more of an industrial zone. However, it's only a few blocks to Times Square, Penn Station, and Madison Square Garden. It's a block from the entrace to the Lincoln Tunnel. It was nice to be so close to everything, yet just off the "beaten path" in a calmer area. There's a gas station on the corner (one of the few in Manhattan) and a few other random bodegas and restaurants nearby. NOISE: It's NYC, there's always going to be some noise, but there was nothing excessive. Lots of trucks roll down 10th avenue at night, but they mostly just blended into the background. PARKING: None. It's best to find a park & ride outside the city and take a train in. Penn Station is just 2 short blocks and then 2 long blocks away. POOL: None. RECREATION: None. RESTAURANT: None, but it's New York. I'm sure you can find something to eat. For the less adventurous, I did notice a McDonald's on 10th, just a short walk from the hotel. ROOM: The room was small and there wasn't much room around the beds. I'll admit, for 3 people, it was a bit cramped. If you like your space I'd limit occupancy to 2 or find another, bigger, hotel. There was limited storage, just one small wardrobe with 2 drawers underneath, a small nightstand, alarm clock/ipod player, desk, desk chair, and flat screen TV. Again, the decor was very modern. SHUTTLE: None. STORE: None on site, a gas station on the corner, several bodegas nearby. SUPPLIES: Standard Soap, Shampoo, Conditioner, Mouthwash & Towels. ===== ===== ===== RATING NOTE: My ratings are generally based on value vs money. Thus, sometimes a simple hotel will receive a 4 or 5, while a fancy hotel can rank a 1 or 2 if I don't feel it was worth the cost. Also, a hotel can do everything right and still only rank as a 4, unless there's something really exceptional about it. 5 = Hotel gets everything right, and goes above and beyond. 4 = Hotel gets everything right. 3 = Hotel is acceptable value for money spent. 2 = Hotel isn't worth the money spent. 1 = Hotel should pay ME to stay there.

“Simply Average” Stayed 3 Nights for a family wedding. I found the standard king size room small compared to other similar properties. The location is convenient to the 16th street Mall and other downtown locations. The front desk staff seemed indifferent to simple requests, which I found strange based on my experience as a Marriott Rewards Platinum Member. I felt other hotels that people in our group stayed at provided much better value.

“Buon Hotel, piccole camere, ottima colazione” L'hotel è molto pulito ed organizzato. Alla reception sono gentili. La colazione è ottima, per chi piace il cappuccino, qui si trova quello veramente italiano (infatti solo nel reparto ristorazione) ci si trovano gli italiani. Inservienti molto gentili e proattivi, puoi lasciare le valigie tutta la giornata (quando stai per partire) senza pagare 1 cent. La stanza è piccolissima, ma molto pulita. Oltre il letto matrimoniale non c'entra più niente :( E' un hotel di Manhattan, ma non si trova vicino al centro nevralgico. Vicinissimo all'empire, un pò più distante da Times Square. Intorno all'hotel non ci sono molte tavole calde, solo un paio di pizzerie. Inoltre se volete mangiare, non uscite troppo tardi, perchè a differenza di Times Squadre e dell'empire, in quella zona il reparto ristoranzione non chiude tardi. La sera, non rientrate tardi, perchè la zona non è molto frequentata. Anche se, a noi è capitato di fare tardi, ma non c'è stato nessun problema. E' solo un pò isolata.

“Great hotel; a bit less expensive than others” I chose The Curtis Hotel because it is near the Denver Convention Center and was about $50 less than the nearby Hyatt and Embassy Suites. The hotel is very cute and the staff is extremely accommodating. I would advise against renting a car if you plan to travel within the area. A cab ride is about $50 each way to and from the airport, but it's $22/day to valet at the hotel making it much cheaper to cab then get a rental car. The rooms are well appointed and all include free wifi. There's a pool, a business center, and decent fitness center. For such a small, boutique hotel it definitely has all the amenities you come to expect from the big chains (probably because it's actually a Double Tree). The only negative I found was that the black-out curtains weren't designed to close completely meaning that you're going to be up with the sun. I did find the bowl of water and dog bones at the front entrance with a sign reading "Welcome Dogs!" very adorable. I didn't get a chance to try the onsite restaurant, but it was packed almost every night. Even though there was a trade show going on, I take that as a good sign. I will definitely return to this hotel when back in the downtown Denver area. It seems a good bet for business travelers and families as it's outfitted with pop-culture themes; each floor being a different one. I was on the 8th floor, also known as the sci-fi floor. The hotel is also within walking distance to the 16th Street Mall, convention center, other restaurants, and right across the street from the Denver Performing Arts Center.

“Standard Hyatt allerdings nichts aufregendes - tolle Aussicht auf die City” Das Hotel liegt mitten in Phoenix, das Personal ist sehr bemüht. Check in hat nur 30 Sekunden gedauert, war selber verblüfft. Die Zimmer sind geräumig. Sehr große Fenster, für eine tolle Aussicht. Allerdings leider nicht zum öffnen. Dusche lässt zu wünschen. Die Stadt Ansicht ist eher langweilig. Für ein. Zwischenstopp sehr zu empfehlen!

“Great Vacation” We went with another couple and had a great time. Great location with trolley access and went to the Warf several times. I got to see a ball game at ATT Park and went to some of the local Irish pubs...lots of fun except my Dodgers lost. I thought the rooms were nice and clean...and trust me for my wife to approve of a hotel is a big thing.

“Trendy Belltown Boutique Hotel” Located in the trendy Belltown area of Seattle this boutique hotel has it's pros and cons. The hotel has been renovated over an 8 year period. The decor is trendy with a contemporary color scheme of brown and tan with plush white linens. Their designer has done a good job in making the best of the space in the rooms. The designer either left the bathrooms in the 1960 original design or created this look. The showers have been nicely upgraded with lush robes for your use. When booking your room you should consider that there are no king beds only queen beds available. Their staff is very friendly and offer a very personalized service with a full coffee bar in the morning from 5:30 am to 11:00 am and a self serve lemon water dispenser through out the day. The hotel is close to many good restaurants and other activities and away from the main core of Seattle. Like all urban hotels valet parking is expensive $25 for overnight. Quiet area. Good value for the price that we paid.

“The terrible, the rude and the nasty!” The staff was unaccomodating. Melissa the Assistant Manager was a "gem." -NOT!! She had an attitude of a fickle child. After debating with her about a room mix- up, she gave me the best room in the house-25th floor next to the noisy elevator. She is a "sweetheart." This is an establishment where prior club member privilages DON'T EXIST. Please search for another hotel. There are many in the area.

“dissater hotel” We satyed here in nov just over night before long haul flight. The only thiing u can say is its the cheapest hotel close to the airport!!! other than that it is a dump dark dirty and smelly, low rise buildings with little lighting in side or out, go some were else!!!!! remind u of scene from physcho

“Some problems. But I would return.” Stayed for two nights on business. Managed to secure a room on the "Concierge Level" (15th Floor), however the concierge lounge is down on the second floor. Room was standard issue Marriott. No hot water one morning. Later received a card on my pillow explaining a broken pipe. Hot water returned after about two hours. Iron didn't work, and desk chair wouldn't lower. I'd like to think that all of these things were anomalies. The location is great, walking distance to most everything and right above Metro Center subway station. In room internet $12.95 per 24 hours, however Starbucks in the lobby offers it for free.

“Excellent location” Excellent location. Can walk everywhere and reasonable price. Breakfast was good. It is nicer than staying in the noisy downtown pricey area. We are platinum members and this hotel was better than A JW Marriott.

“Loved this hotel!” We had a wonderful, spacious room with an exceptionally comfortable bed. The location was perfect for sightseeing, and every staff member was friendly and helpful. We especially appreciated Kristen in the bar area (which had great happy hour specials, by the way). One small suggestion: There was only one trash can, in the bathroom. It would be nice to have one in the bedroom, too. Other than that, however, this hotel feels generous and welcoming. We would be happy to stay here again.

“Nice hotel, decent location, small room” I stayed at the NY Marriott East Side (49th and Lexington) for a business special event on Dec 7th. Pros: This Marriott's location is one of its best features. It is within walking distance to Grand Central Station and a bit longer walk Rockefeller Center. I chose this hotel based on its proximity to our special event. This hotel is within 1/2 block of The Waldorf-Astoria, The W and the Intercontinental. The room was clean, contained a comfortable queen-sized bed and a large flat-screen tv. Cons: The heater was very noisy and woke me up every time it came on overnight. I asked for, and was promised, a rollaway bed which never came. I'm not sure where we would have placed it if it did arrive as the room was very small. We also paid an obscene rate for this room, even with AAA and guest block discounts, due to the holidays. I may stay here again, but there are many other close options as well.

“Great Location” Stayed here for a quick trip. The location was great. Easy to find and easy to get around. Lots of restaurants and shopping 2 blocks away. Rooms were well appointed and clean. Breakfast was good and internet access was free. Had valet parking and the staff was courteous

“Houston Marriott Westchase is a Great Hotel: Bring Your Bathing Suit” I am completing my third stay at this hotel in a month for a total of 11 nights. This hotel was previously an Adam's Mark that converted to a Marriot in July 2004. There is a previous posting on this website from 2002, I believe, that complains of a bad experience. Since the Marriott take over, everything has been excellent during my three stays. The standard rooms are a little small, but very nice with every ammenity. They are tastefully decorated in blues, and maize with butter-colored walls and granite countertops. If you can get a larger room, the extra square footage is nice to have. The hotel has ample complimentary parking. This hotel also has a great indoor/outdoor pool and very nice outdoor lounge chairs. I was here in December and one day it was almost 80 degrees and sunny. The pool was fabulous. I recommend you bring your swimming trunks in case you are here on such a day. Service is very polite, prompt, and professional. The location of the hotel is excellent - - right near the intersection of the Sam Houston Tollway and the West Park Tollway 1 block south of the intersection of Westheimer and Briar Park. This is critical for Houston because these toll roads make access to almost everypart of the city very easy. You will need to buy an eztag at the Harris County Toll Road Authority but it's well worth it if you're going to be in Houston for any amount of time and will be driving around. Go to eztagstore for information. Otherwise, you'll have to take the regular interstates and roads which are very crowded most of the day. This hotel also has a business center with free computer access. I believe you can print out up to 20 sheets at no charge. This was very nice. The restaurant is average, but there are so many restaurants right in the area that it's not a big deal. The hotel is located right off Westheimer which is a main east-west thoroughfare with tons of restaurants, shopping, etc. etc. right near the hotel. Possible warning: The only possible warning is that the rooms do not have a fan control for the air conditioning/ heat. There is a thermostat for each room, but you cannot raise or lower the fan speed. Air circulates continuously at one speed. I was here during very mild weather so the system kept all three of the rooms I stayed in very comfortable. I would wonder about the summer when Houston is very hot and humid. Tip: If you stay here during hot weather, I would request a room with an eastern exposure to avoid the blistering afternoon sun baking your windows. Other than this caveat, I can heartily recommend this hotel. I plan on staying her for at least two more trips to Houston in January.

“I don't think a Kimpton can get any better!” After a lot of great stays at Kimptons across the country we were really hoping the Eventi would really be their flagship in quality and service. I'm glad to say the Eventi really lived up to everything we could hope for. I didn't pick the Eventi for it's location, but when I was looking on how to get to the hotel, I may as well have chosen it for it's great location. The best part is it is literally 2 blocks from Penn Station, so no need to grab a cab or hop on the subway after Amtrak. Also means it's easy to catch just about any train to the rest of the city. During this visit to New York we had to do some shopping in the garment district and the Eventi was also just a quick walk over. Once we made it to the hotel, we were quickly greeted by Stephen at the front desk. He was amazing. He was excited to hear about how we were doing and really was glad to hear us use the magic code word for the summer. Each time we came and went during our stay, when he was at the desk, he greeted us and asked us how we were doing. We really enjoyed having Stephen there to help us out and it really felt like he cared about making sure we had a great stay. At checkout the gentleman at the front desk was also great. He double checked to make sure we enjoyed our stay and made check out super quick. At both check out and check in I was thanked for my loyalty as an IC member, which is always a nice, simple touch. To go along with that simple touch, came an amazing set of welcome amenities. We got a great bottle of wine, delicious snacks and to top it off, we even got a bottle of champagne. This was really great after a long day of work and traveling to the hotel. I had booked a Premier One Bedroom Suite and really didn't expect an upgrade as the only upgrades were named specialty suites, but I don't think I could have wanted much more from our room. We were given a suite on the top floor and while we didn't have the exciting Empire State Building view, it was still great to be so high up and look down on the other buildings. The room itself was set up really well. There was a long entrance way, which put us away from the hall and helped keep the bedroom quiet and that's always nice. The room is full of darker wood and furniture. It all worked very well together with the lighting and simple art pieces. One thing my girlfriend really liked were all the nice reading lamps on the bed and chair. And one thing I really liked is that it was a real suite. None of that executive room with a sofa dividing the space and calling it a suite. The living room was separated from the bedroom with a solid door, which just added to making the bedroom quiet. All over the suite there were plenty of outlets. I really like the outlets that Kimptons are adding next to the beds and the Eventi has this set up in a very classy fashion, built right into the bedside tables. The bathroom was spacious, especially considering we were in NYC. The toilet had it's own little room, which is also always a nice design feature. The bathroom is full of marble and was well lit, making getting ready in the morning and evening easy for both of us. The only very minor complaint is that the shower was a bit small. This is probably due to sharing some space with the bath, but it was all set up very nicely. Overall it may not be the best bathroom we've ever had, but was easily one of the best in NYC. The entire hotel was very clean, which is not surprising for a Kimpton. One really nice part about the cleaning at the Eventi was the housekeeper left us a little note thanking us for the tip and for staying at the Eventi. Like usual for a weekend stay we enjoyed some in room breakfast one morning. Ordering was easy and it arrived a little before they said it would. The person who brought our breakfast was friendly and handled our small problem perfectly. The eggs on my girlfriend's order did not come as ordered and he immediately went to fix it and came back up after just a few minutes. Overall the Eventi really seemed to take all that Kimptons stand for and do it perfectly. Every staff member seemed like they honestly wanted to help us and make our stay great. It's obvious that Kimpton is really empowering their employees to have the freedom to provide their guests with a great experience. There is no doubt in my mind that we'll be staying at the Eventi next time we're in NYC.

“Could be nice, but it's not great.” Seriously, Boston is a tough city in which to find a reasonably priced, nice hotel. The Westin is only the epitome of this problem. I made a last minute switch from the Hilton to the Westin since I thought I would get an upgrade with my SPG membership. Alas, a $50 higher rate bought me nothing more than an average room, no upgrade, and wallpaper that must date back 15 years or more. The room had a strange temp control and was either hot or cold. The bed could have been a "sweet sleeper", but it seemed like a garden-variety bed. The pool was small and the internet... Well, let's say 45 minutes of clicking here and there and calling the service desk (twice) got me nowhere, so I gave up to tackle it after some meetings. Same problem until the service desk put me through to IT who had to have me reset several settings on my computer. This has never happened at any of the othe Starwood hotels where I've stayed. BUT! Complaining about it got me 5000 points, so chalk 1 up to the SPG program. Compared to othe Westins where I've stayed, see San Diego or DC, this rates more in line with a Sheraton or Marriott. For the prices they charge, you should get complimentary coffe, a foot massage, happy hour drink or three, and free internet.

“Reliably excellent” I love this hotel because every time I stay I can count on excellent service, a clean room and a great stay. The restaurant is fabulous, and the staff really goes out of their way to help you.

“Nice hotel with lots of amenities” This is a large hotel located within one mile of SEA. The main building has two restaurants/bar/and a small store. I stayed in the main building on the 12th floor and had a great view of Mount Renier and the surrounding area. My room was located in what I could call the back of the hotel, and there was no traffic/airport noise. My room also had a nice balcony. The food and service at the bar was fine with a selection of local wines and beers. Only negative on the bar is it is very dark and you could not read a paper if you wanted to. The shuttle service to the airport is very popular and was filled to capacity, so I would recommend arriving a few minutes before it departs to insure yourself a seat. The pick up at the airport was slower than I would have liked, but did finally arrive after about a 25 min wait. This property has several out buildings and if you are housed in one of them you will have a short hike to get to the main building. Only negative is the elevators in the main building a pretty slow so it takes a few minutes to get up or down. Near the bar they have three computer stations with a printer (very nice) which makes checking in on line very easy. This is a full service hotel and overall I was very satisfied.

“Great Modern Style Surrounded by History and Class” I came into town a little early to see my sister but found that I really did not want to venture out of the hotel! Being a top tier VIP, I was allowed a very early check-in and upgraded to the Executive Floor. The room has the classic Hilton bed that you can melt in with expensive linens for class. There was a nice working desk. I found the remodeled bathroom to be cramped when using the commode being a bigger guy. The lobby is exquisite but all is quite expensive within the hotel. Nearby, offerings were few as well especially if you were interested in going away from chain food. Services were all expensive including internet and parking. There was a large TV with a DVD player in my room on the 23rd floor. I did notice considerable train noise even up that high so I imagine it is louder on the lower levels. For a business hotel, this is perfect with easy access to the trains both above and subway level.

“The 2007 renovation didn't last long . . .” A tired, worn-out convention hotel that has seen better days. Even a stay on the Club floor was disappointing. The rooms are cramped, the hallways noisy, and the service is almost non-existent. Almost 5 hours to get the room made up (5 hours after a call requesting the service, that is); a Club room that ran out of amenites every day of our stay, and was often not re-stocked; and generally unengaged staff for whatever else one might need. The 2007 renovation changed the colors and the carpets, perhaps, but this aging hotel needed a good deal more to be competitive in the Inner Harbor market.

“Unreal New York Hotel” Stayed at this hotel for a business conference and it was great in all aspects. The whole experience was one of the best I have ever had in NYC. The staff were accommodating and very customer service oriented. Grand Hyatt is also in one of the best central locations in New York City. The rooms were very clean, modern and spacious. Although probably more a business type hotel I would definitely come here for a trip with family and friends as it is really a central location and high quality for a Hyatt Property. Well done!

“Nice Hotel-Walk To Stadium & Subway” Holiday Inn, 10th Street & Packer Avenue, near Philadelphia Stadium. Took the free shuttle from PHL for a one night stay. Reception was quick and pleasant. Room was on an upper "executive floor." Had a spectacular view of the Stadium. Found room to be exceptionally clean and in order. A ten minute walk through a safe residential neighborhood, past private homes and a park, brought me to the Oregon station of the Broad Street line. Four stops later, I was exiting on South Street- for an afternoon of sight seeing. On my trip back, I stopped at Medora's Mecca- a South Philly Italian Restaurant on 13th & Packer- for a few drinks, a snack, and atmosphere. The staff and customer base made me feel like I was already a friend. Saw many other such "local" restaurants on and around Oregon Street Station. (Note: Tony Luke's is on Oregon & Front- perhaps too far to walk from this station.) Based on my positive experience here- I would consider this hotel for a future trip- for use as a home base- owing to Airport Shuttle and it's proximity to the Subway. Found pool very clean. Hotel had a restaurant & lounge- that was crowded due to game. Overall- a very pleasant experience. Oh, after some investigation- I found the Oregon Station to be much closer than the Packer Station on the Broad Street line.

“Hard to believe hotel has not been condemned!” My husband and I needed to visit the city on a day hotel availability was scarce. We usually stay at 2.5 -3 star hotels in Manhattan (for example, Holiday Inn and Hilton Garden Inn). Unfortunately, all hotels ranging from $175 - $350 per night were booked that evening. Thus, we had a choice between $130 for a one star and $350 for a 3.5 star hotel. The HOTEL CARTER was SO DISGUSTING we left at 8 pm without checking out. Though we're courteous people, we didn't bother to do so as we had prepaid anyway and the lobby was littered with the following: a jumpy looking street hood making a rather obvious drug transaction and a sadly young prostitute whose infectious state was apparent from the lesions on her face. We ended up at the Marriott (the lowest price available room spur of the moment) charging on our credit card $380 for a box-like room. We're not at all wealthy -- are middle class parents of college aged kids living frugally. However we ended up spending over $500 that night for the two hotels because the small mountain of bugs in our room noshing on on some previous client's piece of banana in the garbage (yes -- they were red-tinted and appeared to be blood suckers) , the brown-stained bed cover (it looked as if someone with uncontrolled diarhhea had sat on the bed previously) and the rat racing in the hall outside had us thinking we'd need medical attention the next day if we stayed. Please don't stay here.........perhaps if they lack clientele they'll shut down. Honestly, even if my husband and I were homeless, we'd prefer to sleep in Port Authority than here.

“not bad” Stayed here two nights while my husband was in a training session. The first room we were given was right next to the freeway - very noisy with traffic. I went back downstairs and was given a much quieter room with a partial view of the pool. The room was quiet and reasonably clean. The wireless internet worked fine. The air conditioner was working well. The continental breakfast was okay with cereal and bagels. There is a good little mexican restaurant next door that we ate lunch at.. I did not have my room cleaned as there is a big sign by the front desk and in the room that says that the hotel is not responsible for valuables left in the room - so I just got fresh towels from the housekeepers and left the do not disturb sign on the door. The ladies at the front desk were very friendly and accomodating..

“Clean, welcoming contemporary hotel in midtown with great amenities” This hotel is just a short walk from the theater district and Times Square, with a mid-block location that is remarkably quiet for NYC. The rooms are decorated in a cool, contemporary style. For NY, they are relatively spacious and for me, and this is critical, they are extraordinary clean. Great comfortable bed, super restaurant off lobby, and the typical and fabulous Kimpton amenities. Great place to stay while touring NY or doing business in mid-town area.

“Loved the cookies for turndown” Great rooms, clean and functional. The first night when I arrived there was a thunderstorm so I left the curtains opened in the fishbowl room and enjoyed watching the LES light up. For turndown they delivered different cookies every night, much nicer than chocolates. I loved the shampoo & conditioner (Momo by Davines), I've seen them sold in hair salons but never tried it before, I loved it so much now I have a full size bottle at home! The location is great if you spend most of your visit in downtown. I had several meetings in midtown and it was a bit of a pain to get up there and cabs are difficult to grab around there in the morning. So many restaurant hot spots as well as funky galleries, ideal for those who have the energy to enjoy their time after business is over for the day.

“It's easy to reccomend this hotel” This property goes well beyond HIE’s reputation of a Spartan & no frills approach to room amenities and locale. As a platinum Priority Awards member, I stay at many IC properties every year, and this was the best property I stayed at this year by far (sorry Holiday Inn SFO Golden Gateway). This property doesn't look like a Holiday Inn Express except for the "Holiday Inn Express" signage above the front door. A doorman opened the door and welcomed us, leading us to the very impressive and simple décor in the front lobby. I arrived at 1000hrs and was promptly checked in with my traveling companion without incident. The front desk staff weren’t snide or rude by any means, but were rather quite proficient and genuine I must say. Some properties you can get great service and understand how they can be rude to other travelers that submit reviews on here, but I really didn't see how that could be possible, with the front desk clerks that I dealt with, at least. The front desk staff were not abrupt or rude, neither were they obnoxious or phony. After the entire checkin process, they even asked if I have "any questions about the local area", and a map was offered. We were assigned room 605. The hallways were extremely small and cramped and so was the room. There was enough space to walk and leave my luggage. The usage of a flat screen tv (with HD channels!) was a good choice. Despite the small size, the room made very good use of space. The double bed was spacious, that’s all I care about. Remember that this is central Chicago, not suburban Kansas, so the rooms are going to be sized accordingly. The decoration of the room was incredible and way beyond what you would expect for a HIE. The bathroom was small but the usage of a wall mounted counter was wise. The shower was great but the inner shower curtain was full of mildew. Otherwise, no complains with the maintenance. The view from the room was, well, claustrophobic. I didn’t mind it too much and I think it was kind of nice and a bit charming, to be honest. Everything in the room worked; plugins, 802.11, lights, climate control, everything. I always find holiday inn express hotels to have the best service due to the simple approach to the manner in which they operate. However, ‘The Cass’ went way beyond what I have experienced with past HIE properties. The property’s doorman acted way more professionally and genuinely than doormen that I have seen at a Westin or Hyatt. He would offer to summon cabs, ask if you knew where you were going, he would even say 'welcome back' when I drunkenly stumbled into the hotel at 9pm. Service all around was great. I wasn't very demanding this trip, however, so I cannot say how good the service can get. The breakfast area was superb; at any hour (even after drinks at the late hour of, yes, 9pm) you can help yourself to coffee, tea, milk, and yogurt. There were even two computers that you can use (gratis) which are hidden behind the breakfast lounge. What I think would be a nice touch for this space that’s largely vacant 20 hours a day is if they had evening snacks, maybe even an honor bar? I know it's not very holiday inn express’y, but it would be very boutique. The breakfast was also great, albeit of no nutritional value except the bananas. There was cereal, cinnamon buns, and a "hot food coming soon!" sign where the hot food should go. Along with the lack of any nutritional breakfasts, my beef is that this breakfast only ran from 0630-0930, but I suppose this caters best to their business traveler/middle aged tourist demographic that dominates this hotel. Check out was great. Hours before checkout, we asked for a late check out of 1600hrs, but we were told that we would have to pay a half day rate for this. I asked the latest free check out that we could get which was 1330hrs. I played the 'I'm platinum' card and they pushed over to 1500hrs. I think that was a fair compromise (although it's a long stride from the westin's 4pm no questions asked guarantee). The check out was under 60 seconds and without incident. The location was amazing, you had a jewel osco for your grocery and cheap liquor needs four blocks south west, CTA three blocks (grand/state station?) south and west, mag mile three blocks east, and lots of great places to eat within blocks. the Hancock Observatory and MCA are very close to the east as well. Tip with the Hancock Observatory: go to the bar and buy a $12 (triple) martini. Not only do you get a drink for the same price as one in Toronto or some other Scandinavian/Canadian city, you can enjoy it from the 95th floor overlooking Chicago in a very unpretentious environment (dress business casual at least, unless you want to look like an [--]). Besides, it's the same cost as admission to the family-filled observatory anyways. Apart from my suggestions that the breakfast should run later, evening snacks would be a nice touch, and that the shower curtain in 605 needs to get changed (badly), nothing could have gone better. This property will be my first choice for a future stay in Chicago at any rate. The managers here know how to run a hotel and it shows. Book this property, you will not regret it. And if the other reviews deter you: remember that this is a Holiday Inn Express, not a W. If you pay $150/night, you get $150/night in amenities. If you want the W, fork over $400/night.

“THE REAL NYC” We have recently stayed here (left yesterday) We saw many positives by staying here, at the Cosmopolitian. We loved the location (right near the Subway) we were able to access cabs & the Subway so easily. Everything was a short walk away & mostly it was fantastic to beat the hustle bustle of Times Square/Broadway. The rooms are very small, as expected in NY. The bed is clean & comfy, TV great & rooms were cleaned conveniently each day. We thought being on the road side would be a bother but because it's a quiet neighborhood, there were hardly any beeps or sirens. The locals are friendly & the staff were helpful. The air con can be quite loud but when it's as hot as it is in Summer, it shouldn't bother you. The bathroom was quite minuscule - I'm a girl & really like my mirror space. I coped fine, just a warming. The lift is VERY slow but we were on level 3, so we were able to zip up & down the stairs! We loved the 'Cosmopolitan Cafe,' next door to the hotel. We had breaky there three days in a row. The first two days were great but sadly the last day was less enjoyable due to a grumpy lady serving us, meal presentation being poor & the heat in the cafe. I would recommend this hotel to those looking for a quiet part of town & for those who are comfortable getting the Subway everywhere.

“Still a bargain, but noise/staff problems” I've stayed at the Standard Downtown numerous times in the last year (most recently in April 2007), and while I've often enjoyed it, things have slipped a bit. Cheap rates are often to be had on the hotel site ($119 seems to be the best), but beware: that price will likely put you on a lower floor, and both times I've stayed on the 3rd floor, the noise has been astounding. In August of 2006, a party in the next room featured top-of-lungs screaming and banging on the walls at 4am; repeated calls to the front desk were met with indifference and mockery. On the most recent visit, a party a few rooms down featured drunken carousing in the halls until 5am. I understand the Standard is not the Holiday Inn, but it's also not a frat house, and the staff don't seem to care if it becomes one. However, perhaps staying on an upper floor is the answer: when I've either paid for a better room or been upgraded (only once in probably 15 stays!) it has been extremely quiet, even on weekend nights. Maybe they throw all the partiers on the 3rd floor? Next time, I'll try requesting a higher floor. For the price, I still think it's one of the more interesting and practical hotels for the traveler interested in unique experiences and good modern design. Sure, the decor isn't the jaw-dropping surprise it was a few years ago, but the rooms are still very clean, the beds are comfortable, and a glassed-in shower is pretty cool. My experiences with room service and the restaurant have been mostly good (although trying to get breakfast at 6am before an early flight was practically impossible, due to missing wait staff and "computer problems"). The food is pretty good. Understand that the weekend bar/rooftop scene is part of LA nightlife and thus pretty pretentious, but you're staying in the hotel and it's free, so why not go enjoy a rooftop cocktail with the trying-to-be-beautiful? Yes, there's wristbands/cards/whatever, but it's not Omaha, and it wouldn't be as fun if it was. Anyway, there's so much more to do in LA you shouldn't be hanging at the hotel on a Saturday night. In general, I still applaud the hotel's existence, as a fine example of creative reuse of its former bank building, and as a pioneer in the reemergence of downtown LA. Plus, focusing on what current, young travellers really want and need (some quality snacks in the minibar, instead of crappy coffee and a dirty coffeemaker, for example) make it much more practical than comparitively priced hotels. So, I guess the biggest concern is the extreme level of noise, and the staff's lack of response to it. It's my hope that the indifference the staff has recently shown is not a sign that the Downtown Standard has started to slip in general. The hotel can still be lively and fun without degenerating to anarchy, and in my opinion, paying $120 for a room should guarantee a basic level of quiet, at least from 1 or 2am to 7 or 8am on weekend nights. For staff to laugh off complaints is just insulting.

“Spectacular” My Minneapolis flight came in very late and I booked a stay instead of driving over an hour home at midnight. What a beautiful hotel. It is easy to find through a catwalk at the airport. They also provde a shuttle if you dont want to walk. In the lobby there is a nice pub and all business amenities. The room is absolutely beautiful, new furniture, updated, with a pretty view of the airport and water. In the morning, I went to the health club. There are towels, a locker room, a lap pool and updated equipment. TV's were everywhere to offer distraction and individual TV's on each machine. I am a Silver Hilton member and I was immediately offered services of the members lounge, even though its usually for Gold or Platinum members. there was complimentary breakfast, newspapers, magazines, concierge and another business center. Beautiful setting. The staff were all excellent and to be commended for their attention to detail. I have been in many Hiltons due to business and this was absolutely the best. I will definitely go back, and my thanks for a wonderful stay.

“Convenient Stay for Downtown Dallas” Good location for downtown and the DART especially when visiting the Texas State Fair and also excellent position to walk to visit the Grassy Knoll, 6th Floor Museum and Market and Main Street where there are places to eat and drink. Staff were friendly enough. The breakfast was adequate but not particularly presented very well and the breakfast area/tables seemed a little jaded/tired. The room itself was adequate and the shower curtain design in the bathroom was great.

“A True STAR in the Lonestar State!” My husband and I had a staycation at the Hotel Valencia Riverwalk and were overwhelmed by its modern charm and sexy ambience. The hotel is a real gem in the heart of Alamo City. Its mood soothing decor, client conscious staff, modern architecture, escape worthy views and delicious full service restaurant make it a must visit hotel!!! We were incredibly impressed with the bar and balcony...both of which set the mood for romance. The drink selections are plentiful and the bar staff are eager to let the libations flow making it easy to transport you to another place...you forget you're still in TX after a while! The rooms include beautiful, sleek, dark furniture, a full length mirror, flat screen TV and a nice bathroom. The bed was super comfy and our view of the atrium's fire pit was super cool! My honey and I noshed on some of the most delectable Texas culinary concoctions at Citrus. The restaurant offers a three course and four course menu that's chock full of delicious foods like crab cakes, blackmore wagyu beef carpaccio and quail eggs. We thoroughly enjoyed EVERYTHING ABOUT this TRUE STAR in the Lonestar State!!! A MUST visit if you ever find yourself in the Alamo City!!!

“little things good and bad = average rating” I liked the free internet, free bottle water, and the hotel being close to the metro. The staff is also very friendly. Little annoying things included, an unreasonable long wait to get checked in (3 receptionists 2 helping one guest and the third seemingly chatting with another about other hotels?), no local TV stations working, a somewhat tricky room key (remove slowly), and very hot hallways (it was an unusually warm Dec. day). I'd stay there again if the price was right, but wouldn't pay a premium.

“Won't stay again” October 15th we spent the night at the Tremont in Chicago. Never again! Staff was nice enough, but the room was dirty and falling apart. Paint chipping, soiled chairs, mold in the shower, not enough towels, etc. Web site is very misleading, absolutely nothing like what you get. It shouldn't be rated as a 3 star, it barely makes it as a 1 star. Traveler be ware.

“great experience -- this is the place to stay!” I stayed at the Castle Inn while at a conference this past July. Like many of you, I spent a lot of time looking for affordable places to stay in SF that were in a decent neighborhood and accessible to most attractions. I decided to go with the Castle Inn and was glad I did. The rooms are clean and basic, but had everything that I needed. The free parking was a huge plus, and there are interesting shops and restaurants within walking distance. The staff were also very friendly. Our flight was delayed and we didn't arrive until 2am. We had given the front desk a heads up and it was no problem at all.

“Good location and views” Stayed this past weekend and had a nice stay. *The location is right in the center of downtown so you have access to all the restaurants and night life if that is your thing. *The views are also very nice if you are lucky enough to face the circle. *They are going through a remodel right now. I am ok with that and hardly noticed on our stay. *Would stay again if I am in downtown Indy again.

“it's only getting worse” PLEASE DON'T STAY HERE! I've stayed here 3 times because you can get it for cheap on priceline. I won't stay again though. There is no attention to detail here. there are dirty areas everywhere you look. We had to move from our 1st room because the bathroom was dirty. THIS IS NOT A 3* PLEASE DOWNGRADE IT!

“Small but nice” One night stay recently. Front desk service was attentive, quick and thorough. Rooms were much smaller than conventional hotels, but quite comfortable. Free wifi. Pleasant European design. Clean and quiet. Windows opened, which is a plus in my book. Small workout room with only three treadmills, two ellipticals and some dumbbells. Overall, a good stay at a decent price.

“Location is the main appeal” The rooms are sufficient but the bathroom could have been cleaner. The location is great for tourists. You can get to every little tourist trap place right from your doorstep. I did not eat at the hotel as there are so many great restaurants in SF. Stay here if you are on a budget. I will go back to the St. Regis or the Mark if I had a choice.

“Hotel war eine schöne Überraschung” Wir genossen unseren Aufenthalt bei Aufenthalt Bridge. In der Nähe von Geschäften und Restaurants. Sehr sauber und ruhig. Das Personal war freundlich. Als ich in mein Zimmer ging ich war sehr beeindruckt. Es war schön, geräumig, und die Erwartungen übertroffen. Wir wurden in eine Suite, die wunderbare aktualisiert wurde! Warmes Frühstück war groß - fantastische Auswahl an Speisen und alle frisch und heiß. Unser Aufenthalt war sehr angenehm und entspannend. Hilfsbereites Personal. Leicht zu finden. Ich habe Zeit in vielen Hotels verbracht, aber das ist derjenige, der mehr wie zu Hause fühlt! Wir genossen unser Wochenende besuchen und würden wieder kommen.

“Well equipped, friendly staff, good breakfast” Hotel is located next to Willowbrook Mall, and there are some restaurants in walking distance (walk under the bridge to the other side of 249). The hotel checkin was easy, even though they were overbooked (may have been due to Silver status). Bananas and apples were available 24h. Breakfast buffet with good selections. Did not attend their evening meal choices at managers reception. This hotel does not offer free airport shuttle. Yes, would come back here. Room was quiet, was able to turn off the fridge over night. Complimentary Wifi Internet speed was good.

“Perfect spot for a weekend in NYC” We stayed at the Omni Berkshire Place last weekend for a long weekend in NYC. It's really a perfect spot to stay for a weekend hanging out in the city. It's close to the subway, a short cab ride from Penn Station and a quick walk from almost anything else you'd like to do. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and didn't feel cramped at all even though it's a city hotel. The room had a safe big enough to keep our laptop in, which is always nice. The bathroom wasn't big, but was still great, had a good shower, etc. There's a gym on the 17th floor, which was also great - it had several ellipticals and treadmills, free weights, etc. Even when it was a little crowded, there was still room for everyone to do what they wanted. We were on the 15th floor and so were able to easily take the stairs up to the gym - which mattered only because one set of elevators was out, so it was kind of a wait to take them at times. There's a cool little sun deck area right outside of the gym, which was fun to hang out on for a few minutes and check out the view. The Fireside Restaurant in the hotel was all right - it was definitely convenient and was a good stop-off point to grab a drink before or after going out. I would say that, aside from the broken elevators which obviously were known about and in the process of being fixed, the restaurant was the only real area where there's room for improvement at the hotel. It certainly wasn't bad by any stretch of the imagination, but it also didn't have a very fun or welcoming atmosphere. If they stepped that up, they might get more non-hotel patrons hanging out at this hotel bar like others in the city. Overall, it's a great hotel and we would 100% stay there again next time we're in the city.

“Roomy, but typical” This is a typical Marriott property, nothing too special. The room was roomy, however the hallway noise and outside noise were loud. Since the air/heat was so quiet, you can hear everything around you. I was also in a room that had an adjoining room and I would hear everything in the next room. The service was good, and the location was perfect for me, also close to the Art Museum. There is an ice skating rink in the adjoining building and a food court. However only one restaurant is usually open in the evening, there is also a restaurant in the hotel. Just as a side note, watch out for the Dallas taxis as twice on this trip they tried to rip me off!!

“Great Location, wonderful hotel” We loved this hotel! The location was excellent. Easy walking to Navy Pier, Magnificient Mile, and tons of restaurants! Hotel was clean and the staff was so friendly. They have computers on the second floor with free high speed internet also. The only downfall is that it is a highrise and there are only two elevators. They are very slow. Sometimes I would have to wait 5 minutes or so for an elevator. That is really irritating if you forgot something and wanted to run back to the room! Plus we were on the 15th floor so we couldn't take the stairs! Other than that, the hotel was wonderful!

“Location location” The staff at the Palmar were friendly and efficient. The atmosphere is hip. The hotel is in Dupont Circle which is a great location in DC. Wine in the evenings is appreciated. We found the rooms to be small and the hallways even smaller. We find ourselves in DC often and typically stay elsewhere only because of the room size. That is our only complaint.

“You Would Be Surprised” For a very good hotel in New York City during the pre-Christmas week, this was a really great deal.
