I booked this through Hot Wire and was concerned when I read some less than great reviews, but got inside info from my brother who said he had stayed there before and it was fine. After hoofing the 20 blocks up 7th Avenue in Christmas gawker pedestrian traffic and near freezing weather, I was happy just to get inside. The lobby was splendid by most NYC hotel standards and check in for a prepaid room was fast and the reception cordial. I took the elevator up to the 25th floor after having to get out of the car and find the code that allows you to pick your floor and then an assigned car. No big deal, but reception missed telling me about this. I encountered other mystified travelers who had the same problem. As I put my key into the door, I heard a woman's voice inside the room sasy: "Who's dat?" I said: "the guest assigned to this room," and went in to find two maids goofing off in the easy chairs. They said they were "just finishing up the room," but they clearly didn't expect me. The rest of the 2 night stay went fine. The room was as good or better than ones I have found in major chain hotels at three times the Hotwire price. Flatscreen TV, coffee maker, nice king bed with linens that fit, plenty of new towels, marble top on bathroom sink, clean, new shower curtain, plenty of hot water and not a bad view either. The key here is that at $109 a night, plus tax and fees, the hotel is in a great location: a few blocks from Central Park and 59th Street, reasonable walk to Grand Central and Penn Station, plenty of nearby delis and restaurants and overall, a great place to stay. Great deal if you can get it. I would love to stay there again, but I'll bet I don't find this rate again!

“Funky and cool” The Crescent is not a chain hotel which is a good thing. It is an older building that has been nicely remodeled with updated rooms but retains its old fashioned charm. The downside is a slow older elevator and single pain windows that let in a lot of street noise. The staff is friendly and it is in a good neighborhood close to lots of transit including the cable cars. Continental breakfast is really ordinary but overall I was very pleased with the value for the money.

“Luxury pretense, but no substance” I have stayed at the Soho Grand on repeated business trips throughout the past year. My company has agreed corporate rates with them, so I am forced to stay there. I believe the Soho Grand has all the veneer of being chic, exclusive, luxurious, but fails to understand that this needs to be backed by the same level of service. While I could forgive the tiny rooms, their customer service is consistently bad with every visit. The check-in staff are inattentive and unhelpful. They make you feel like an intruder, rather than a guest. By comparison, I have stayed at different W Hotels in Manhattan, and by the second visit, I was greeted by name. Room service is poor, with cold arrivals and mixed orders. The Soho Grand has no idea of how to run a hotel, especially with repeat clients. It's sad that even when I'm not paying, the hotel is horrible.

“TRACE - restaurant review” Restaurant Trace is newly opened place within W hotel. We did not stay at the hotel but found an advertisement for the restaurant and decided to visit. We did not regret the choice. The food is incredible. The whole premise is that the origins of every ingredient can be traced back to the local farmer or producer. The dishes are very inventive and one can taste their freshness. The chief does not overwhelm the food with spices and allows natural flavors to mix and melt in your mouth. Wine selection perfectly matches the dishes. Servers are very attentive, polite and not overbearing. Overall - great experience and high recommendations for the place!

“Well placed, comfortable, friendly 3-star hotel” We stayed here for the final 4-nights of our 3-week tour of the west-USA following recommendations on Tripadvisor. We booked the stay through Expdedia and got a great rate as a part of a sale event. The hotel is situated near the downtown area of San Fran and ideally placed to catch the public transport system. The Carlton is a very good 3-star hotel with very friendly and helpful staff. There have been some comments on previous Tripadvisor entries regarding the hotel and the street noise at lower floor levels. We stayed on floor 6 and heard first-hand from a guest who was on the 1st floor, finding the street noise unbearable. So, thanks to those who pointed out that the higher floors are better! Also make sure you have a room that isn't next to the lift shafts! The on site restaurant, SAHA offers arabic-fusion food - highly recommended! A great atmosphere in the restaurant and the food was brilliant. There are bars and restaurants around the hotel; a supermarket right around the corner "Walgreens" (on the corner of Larkin and Bush), and Union Square is a 15-minute walk down Sutter Street. To get around you must use the public transport system - "Sutter Fine Foods" sells 3-day passes for $18 per person and it's well worth it. Free internet access another bonus to the hotel, and there are two PC's near reception with a printer (first 20 minutes on internet is free). No fridge in the room which would have been nice, although there is a safe. There is no air-con, but the windows can be opened fully. The ceiling fan offered good air circulation and the temperature in the city during our stay was pretty comfortable, but I can imagine the room being quite uncomfortable in the height of summer! Free wine evenings from 530pm for an hour in the lobby - a nice touch offered by the hotel - and a good way to mingle. In summary - a real gem in the city, a good quality 3-star hotel and we'd definitely recommend and would go back if visitting San Fran again!

“Friendly hotel with good accomodations” Very helpful staff makes up for a less than optimal location unless you have a need to be in NW San Antonio. Rooms are standard Marriott issue but well maintained. Be prepared for a large family and military contingent staying at the property.

“High on the Hyatt” Stayed two nights at the Hyatt with my husband, our son and my in-laws. Our rooms were ready on time and exactly as requested - one room with two doubles adjoining another room with a king. The rooms were spacious and quiet - they looked exactly like the photos on their website. The bathroom was nice and the toiletries were great. I was initially concerned about the size of the hotel, but we never had much of a wait for service (check-in, check-out, taxi, etc.) We odered room service once and the food arrived within 15 minutes! We did not eat at the restaurants, but we did grab a quick breakfast at the kiosk downstairs and had snacks one afternoon in the bar area. Food prices are a little on the high side, but comparable to other hotels. Location is great - one night we we walked over to the Wrigley Building and caught a boat tour of the Chicago River and Lake Michigan. We also enjoyed shopping and restaurants that were within walking distance. We look forward to staying here again on our next trip.

“Decent hotel, minor issues” My husband and I came here for a few days to visit his company headquarters. I worked for two solid days in the hotel. Generally the stay was better than expected, given some of the reviews on Tripadvisor. Pluses 1. Rooms were pretty clean, lots of space, and had appropriate amenities. 2. I was in the room when housekeeping came each day and they did a good job cleaning quickly and quietly (I was on the phone most of the time). 3. Hot breakfast buffet was included each day, although choices were relatively limited. We opted not to have breakfast the second day. 4. Room service for lunch was fast and hot. Menu has some good choices. 5. Customer service was generally courteous and friendly. 6. Fantastic location downtown, just a few blocks from Pike Place and one block from Westlake. Lots of great restaurants and shopping around here. Minuses 1. We had problems with outbound calls. First night we tried one phone and had to have the front desk "release" the line for outbound calls. Second day I tried another phone and had to call again to get it released. This one never worked, so I usedmy cell phone the entire time I was here. 2. The room is not really set up for working. No speaker phone or mute capability. 3. TV didn't work one morning; all the channels were snow. 4. Pay movies didn't work; got a message that the movie had to be ordered at the front desk. Called to ask them to order it and they said they'd take care of it. Movie never started. 5. Water pressure and heat are acceptable but lower than we'd like. 6. We were two doors down from the elevator, so we could hear people noise when they were waiting outside. Fortunately not too much noise from neighbors (although the headboards rattle anytime you move on the bed). 7. Within a few blocks of the hotel you can find a lot of vagrants and other people at loose ends. When we had dinner last night just a couple blocks away, two bike cops were frisking and interrogating two young men right against the window where our table was situated. 8. Pike Place Market shuts down at the end of the day, so don't wait to see it at night. I would consider staying here again if the rate were right ($250-300 seems steep).

“Ok hotel, but i didn't like the location at all.” This hotel was fine, but i hated staying in Hollywood. I found all the tourist attractions in the area pretty tacky and not at all impressive. Getting around is also a bit of a pain. For a much nicer LA experience, head to Santa Monica or Venice Beach. These two areas are beautiful, relaxed, easy to get around and full of great shops, bars, restaurants, beaches and people watching.

“Excellent location and unbeatable price” I was positively surprised by this property, managed by Hersha. It is clean, recently refurbished, well kept. The lobby is non existent, and the room is narrow and small-ish. But for 90 usd per night in Nassau St, downtown New York I can take a little bit of this and a little bit of that. Bed was very comfortable. Only negatives were the shower curtain (not long enough, some water spilled on the floor) and the a/c system (noisy). All in all, a great experience and would definitely consider it again should I need to stay downtown once again.
“Classy Hotel all the way around....” This is my second stay here. This time, it was a layover to our honeymoon.....great service, gorgeous room....I highly recommend.

“Studio is not enough” This is my 3rd stay at this resort in 15 months. No doubt it's one of the best pool resorts in Arizona for kids. The on site pool is huge with lots of seating and shading on deck. We were placed in the furthest building away from the main pool but even then it is only a 3 minute walk. We stayed with another family of 6 and used 3 studio rooms between us with 4 in each room. We got a rate that I cannot complain about. But the king bed was too firm (both of my shoulders hurt and arms fell asleep) and the queen sofa bed was crazy uncomfortable both to sleep on as a bed and to sit on as a couch. The room is clean and modern but it's still not sufficient for 2 adults and 2 small children. Spend the extra money and get the 1-bedroom. Also, I was the youngest adult here by at least 30 years. I felt I was staying at a retirement home. Which was fine because we often had the pool to ourselves. At any rate, Marriott is usually a safe bet for quality. But it's time for an upgrade to pillow top beds.

“Good position and would stay again” The hotel was easy to get to, using BART and taxi from Embarcado. Reception was welcoming and staff helpful, we got offer that included 2 free cable car tickets and breakfast. Every evening includes wine and nibbles. The room was clean and had 1 bed and TV. The bathroom was clean. I would stay here again if deal is good as very near Wharf and cable cars. Free WIFI in bedrooms

“Good Solid Hotel” We stayed at Affinia Manhattan for 7 nights at the end of March/start of April '09. We actually only stayed 6 nights as our first night we were delayed in LA and didn't make it to NY till the next day. The hotel was exactly what we were expecting, grand lobby, dated rooms but nice and clean and a decent location for sightseeing for a first time visitor. We had a studio room (room 1918) on the 19th floor which was at the end of a corridor so no neighbours on one side. Room was large, one queen bed, desk and chair, arm chair, dated kitchen and a tiny but completely serviceable bathroom with fantastic water pressure in the shower! Room was very clean and kept clean during our stay. We found the staff to all be very friendly and extremely helpful whenever you needed them. We ate at Niles restaurant one night and really enjoyed our meal and drinks, we ate up at the bar farly early one night pre-theatre. Food was good and was reasonably priced for a hotel restaurant. On the whole Affinia Manhattan was what we were expecting and for a great price from Travelzoo ($119 weekend $149 weeknights). It was one of four NYC hotels we stayed in and even though it was older style it still measured up against more pricey accommodations in the Thompson group. We would definitely reccommend it to anyone if you can get a good price like we did.

“Excellent Rate, Great Location” I am a SPG member and would normally stay at The Westin Michigan Ave or W Lakeshore, however both had rates much higher than this property so I decided to try it. Excellent location in the shopping district, one block off the heart of Michigan Ave. Great breakfast restaurant attached to the hotel with amazing prices straight down a hallway off the elevator. A Trader Joes on the same block! The rooms were easily as nice as The Westin, bedding is not the heavenly bed but decent enough, rooms were clean, good size bathroom, flat screen TV, free internet for all. Order up some extra pillows and a bath robe and you are set. Not fancy but more than adequate for a great location.

“You're missing the boat if you don't consider this one....” Stayed there on a web special - two adjoining rooms for parents and teens. Coming off a few days at the Olympics, this was a great last stop before heading home. The staff was outstanding - always friendly and asking if they could help in any way with any needs. Walk down the stairs at front door and you're in a Whole Foods Market. Restaurants everywhere - try the pizza place next door! I would definitely recommend. You pretty much need to valet park, and next time I'd ask for a higher floor - 5th floor I could still hear street noise. We will definitely be back.

“Faded yet wonderful” August 15-17, 2005 my husband and I spent 3 nights at the Intercontinental Hotel in Chicago, whose locaiton is perfect for walking to the river, the lakeshore, Grant Park, Mich. Ave, and even restaurants in River North. We opted for the rooms in the old portion of the hotel where room and bath were large, beds comfy and we loved overlooking lively Mich. Ave. Decor was a bit worn but on two afternoons at 3 PM, tired from walking the city, we had their glorious old tiled pool to ourselves and felt like we were staying in the Hearst Castle. It was simply wonderful. Beware the hotel bar which couldn't make a drinkable Manhattan.

“Service and Location” We like to stay at Starwood hotels because we are elite members of the SPG Program. We chose this facility while in Dallas because of it's location (almost within) the Galleria. We will be back because the staff provided us with exceptional service despite the fact that they were almost 100% full. The rooms are a little stark and modern for our taste. But since the Heavenly Bed is always so consistently comfortable, we wouldn't let that influence us. We love to feel special and the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome and comfortable. Their warmth was heartfelt and very much appreciated!

“AN AWESOME HOME AWAY FROM HOME!” Just in town to de-stress and enjoy some family time, and needed some hill-country views, a walk around beautiful Town (Ladybird) Lake , and some delicious barbeque, of course. The spacious 2-bedroom, 2-bath suite was a perfect fit for two couples and a toddler. The hotel is in a lovely, park-like setting and very quiet, set back away from the main roads, but in a very convenient location to Mopac and 360. Parking is plentiful and free. Our suite was spotless, and the living room furniture was cozy (loved having moveable cube ottomans to put our feet up on, instead of a hard coffee table). We did not bring a computer (time to destress) but Wi-Fi was free too. The beds and bedding were very conducive to a great night's sleep. Esther at the front desk was one of the friendliest hotel staff we have ever encountered, and very knowledgeable about the area as well. They anticipated the toddler and had a pack and play already set up for us, even though we did not request it because we brought our own. The buffet breakfast was plentiful and yummy, with the hot foods hot and the cold foods cold, and the woman running the buffet was very friendly as well, greeting guests as they came in and making sure everyone had what they needed. Compared to the price of some of the standard hotels in Austin, we got a great deal on top of everything else. Management should be very proud!! Looking at the Monday through Thursday evening menu (posted on the frig door) for a 'complimentary light' repast, I would choose this hotel if I had to travel to Austin for business--the menu looked terrific.

“Plenty of Space & Free Parking” The lobby was really clean and looked very much more high quality than I expected for the price. Upon arriving at our room it appeared to be clean and included a refrigerator. There was a small sitting area with two small couches and double beds, which was perfect since we were not really close to public transportation. Typically I like to stay closer to the trains, but parking was free and there is not much going on in this neighborhood so I probably won't recommend walking last at night alone for the average tourist.
“Good but under construction a bit.” This is a very good value and location for a NYC hotel. Rooms are very comfortable and large and the staff were very good.

“Felix has a fantastic location!” My college age daughter and I stayed two nights at the Felix and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We had a room on the 12th floor overlooking the Rainforest Cafe and McDonalds. Nice city view. I'd like to compliment the hotel staff. Everyone from the front desks clerks who gave us directions and maps to the doormen who always greeted us and took care of our luggage on check-out day were just great. Our room was on the small side but we expected that as it's an older building. It was spotlessly clean and we liked the contemporary colors and decor. No bathtub in the bathroom but the shower was perfectly adequate. We were pleasantly surprised at how centrally located the Felix is. It was no trouble walking to Lincoln Park, the Loop, or the Magnificent Mile. We had a good stay overall and we'd go back again. One last thing--my daughter was very happy at having free internet service in the room!

“Good Value clean and close to a T” Great Shuttle service to the airport, close to JFK/UMASS T Stop. Rooms are big and clean, everything works, generally good value. Internet access is not free apart from in the lobby, but if you leave laptop on after you have connected, it does stay connected in your room.

“Great Location, Average Hotel” There is no doubt that this hotel is in a great location sandwiched between the Chrysler Building and Grand Central Station. There is walkway link from the lobby directly to the station, which has a great market/deli area, along with lots of decent restaurants and bars. There is also a handy drugstore on the next block. The hotel lobby is impressive, but our room was rather a let down after the grand entrance. As we were travelling with our 6 year old son we had twin queen beds, which didn't leave space for much else in the room. The poor lighting made the room look drab and dim, despite being recently refurbished. The bathroom had peeling paint on the ceiling and the bath plug didn't really keep the water in the bath. Although we had read it in an earlier Tripadvisor review, we were still surprised to find that the room didn't have tea/coffee making facilities or a fridge. We enjoyed the big buffet breakfast at the hotel Skybar (and so we should at $25 a head). The hotel is primarily a conference venue and most of the guests were business people, consequently the hotel services are very much aimed at business travellers, making it very impersonal with few leisure facilities. Fortunately my husband was at a conference here so we didn't have to pick up the tab - this hotel is certainly not worth the rack rate. If I were making my own travel arrangements there are plently of hotels I would choose before this one. All in all, the hotel is fine, but not worth the rack rate and not over-exciting for tourists/leisure guests.

“Top place - central location - great BF” I liked: - very central location - just minutes to the White House - spacious room. I was offered a corner room, which was fantastic - good view, huge windows, clean - food. I had breakfast on 14th floor in concierge room - good choice and service I did not like: - spa - there is no spa. There is an unattended gym/pool. for the hotel of this caliber, not having a spa is a disadvantage - bellboys - some could be more friendly - concierge service was not extremely helpful when I asked him to help

“Good hotel, very over-priced for Formula1” This hotel is large, modern and very nice. The staff is very polite and hard working. I've stayed here a few times and have always liked it. I was part of a business event for the Formula1 this weekend......normally the hotel is $100-200 a night. It was $440 and you had to stay a min. of 4 nights. I think they really went over board here and gauged clients badly. In fact, the pricing and term was just embarrassing for them - staff even looked sheepish about it. I did like the Internet policy of 1 payment and you can connect up to 5 devices. I would also comment they they have small but very nice gym.

“Historic Hotel with Convenient Location” Stayed at this hotel for one week while in Boston for a work conference. It was conveniently located near the Government center, Fanueil hall, Boston Commons - all walking distance. Several subway (T stop) stations nearby. Great location. Rooms were remodeled, on the smaller side - but with great historic charm. Service was higher than other hotels.

“Decent hotel” This was a decent hotel. We chose it because so many of the other hotels in the Gaslamp area were extremely overpriced, and we were looking for a hotel with a nice pool. We booked this online through expedia for about 150 per night, and it was certainly worth that amount. The rooms were clean, done in a pretty beachy decor, and were comfortable. The maids always did a good job of keeping the room in order, although they never seemed to leave us enough towels (2 towels for 2 ppl isn't enough in my opinion)...so we just requested more, which was no problem. The hotel is busy. There are lots of people there at night, especially in the pool area. Our friends had a room over the pool and they said that the noise at night wasn't an issue. The pool is beautiful and gets great sun. However, there isn't much space for lounging. They have about 6 lounge chairs out, and 3 cabanas. One day we arrived in the afternoon and there was no place to lie out. When I asked the bartender where we were supposed to sit, he kindly offered up the cabana for free (for which they normally charge $250 per day). On our last day we also noticed that they had a stack of lounge chairs behind the bar, which you can take and set up if you want to. The pool was pretty and a lot of fun! The hotel is within walking distance to some clubs, restaurants and bars, and they offer you free coffee and tea in the morning, which is a nice touch. Now for my gripes. I didn't find the hotel to be overly functional. I compare it to a really hot girl without a brain. The rooms looked nice but there was no good area for putting on makeup, and there was a lack of counter space and shelving. The pool looked beautiful, but the lack of sitting space was a bit annoying and somewhat stressful. They have sex kits for purchase in the room - lubricant, condoms, etc. I guess paying $7 for a sex kit when in dire need is worth it, but I don't need to be reminded of the thousands of people who have had sex in the bed that I'm paying $150 per night for! Yuck! They also have these strange leopard housecoats for purchase. These two things made me think that the hotel might secretly be frequented by pimps and people with weird sexual fetishes. Finally, parking was $30 per day - insane! We had no real problems with this hotel, but I just didn't find it functional enough overall. See what else you can find, but if this is the hotel you end up with, then that's certainly okay, too, and I'm sure you'll have an enjoyable stay!

“I had a mixed experience” The staff and room were great. The location is next to fast food and I ate the check-in cookies for desert. I asked for a 5am wake up call for an early flight, but I got the first (of 4 wake-up calls) at 4:18, the second at 4:20 while I was in the shower, third at 4:22 on line 1 of the phone, and the fourth at the same time on line 2 of the phone. The front desk explained that it may have been a problem caused by the recent power outage. Since I was already going to miss breakfast, I just caught an earlier cab to the airport. Aside from this, I would recommend this place.

“Charged for everything!” Every business starts on the wrong foot when you are charged a significant amount of money and then informed that you aren't really getting everything they have to offer with that rate. So on top of our $300+ room, $10 pp/day for the fitness room, and $13.95 per day per device for wifi. That means we pay an extra $167.40 for wifi and $60 for the gym! Really? This review is done in the first hour of my stay. Not a very good first impression!

“Convention Convenience with Class” Checkin at the HHonors desk was pleasant and fast. As a Gold member, I was upgraded to the Executive Club floor with a lakeview on the 24th floor. The room was smallish but very well appointed with beautiful travertine, classic wallpaper, and high-end furniture. There is a bit of noise from the street, but certainly not a problem and to be expected in a large city. The executive club offers a good complimentary breakfast with some nutritious options like oatmeal and hard boiled eggs in addition to baked goods. The coffee is very good considering it is an automated espresso system. In the evening there are hot and cold hors d'oerve (sp) and soft drinks for free plus beer and wine that they charge for. The conference center is huge and spread out. Staff are helpful in providing directions. Wifi coverage is better than most venues. Acoustics in the breakout rooms are very good, although the ballroom sound is rather muffled. Restaurant prices are high but in line with other big-city conference hotels. The food itself is reasonable. The lunch buffet is a sound choice. All in all, if you are scheduled for a conference here, you should expect to be comfortable. Do be prepared for crowds.

“Graceland or Bust” It was my best friend's birthday and we met in Memphis for a pilgrimage to Graceland. We really enjoyed our stay at the Residence Inn. Although our room was a bit cramped and oddly arranged, my friend and her husband had a nice spacious suite on 13, which was twice the size. (He is a Marriott Platinum member. ) But, the location is ideal. Minutes walk to The Peabody, Beall Street and The Rendezvous for ribs. The staff could not have been more pleasant or helpful. The breakfast buffet was great. Our visit to Graceland took us to Memphis in the first place and did not disappoint. It turned out to be a perfect celebration.

“4 Seasons in Houston--as good as ever” I had not been to Houston in about ten years. I stayed again at the Four Seasons and found it even better than I remembered. I had a nice suite with a very comfortable bed. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Location is outstanding for business. I give it my highest recommendation.

“quiet, comfortable, friendly” The free breakfast, with order-made omelets, waffles, cereal, bagels, fruit, etc., was one of the best I've had in a less-than-sumptuous hotel. The free wi-fi, proximity to a metro station (Vermont/Santa Monica) and the Hollywood Freeway are other plusses. Our room (including bathroom) was clean and comfortable. The front desk staff, especially Michael, was helpful and friendly. I asked for an especially quiet room, and the staff went to some trouble to make sure I got one. A plumbing problem was fixed quickly. The fitness center is well equipped. The immediate neighborhood is uninteresting, but Los Feliz, Hollywood, and other more interesting areas are easy to get to from here. All in all, a good value.

“Nice hotel in centralized location” After reading some poor reviews on Trip Advisor for this hotel, I was dreading staying here; however, I was pleasantly surprised upon arrival. I was able to check in much earlier than anticipated, the hotel staff was hospitable and helpful! My room was clean, and I felt safe. Which are my two top priorities when traveling alone. The lobby at times can be a bit hectic, but any lobby is when you have a convention going on in town. I was on the 16th floor with an interior room facing the pool. Even with people partaking in the pool my room was not that noisy. At times the hallways seemed a little maze like, but I quickly found the short cuts. My only complaint was that if people were talking in the hallway you could definitely hear them in your room; however, that only happened every now and then. Not a big deal.

“Great Location for a Cruise” We stayed at this location before leaving Boston on a New England cruise. The hotel is not directly downtown, but easily reachable via a cab, subway, or by walking. The hotel is attached to the convention center, and close to the airport and cruise terminal. The hotel was neat and clean, and the hotel staff was helpful, especially the valet who helped us find a great restaurant in Boston to celebrate a birthday. The hotel has a Starbucks in the lobby and the Wi-Fi was free in the lobby, but there is a charge in the room. Overall we were happy with the hotel and the way the staff handled our visit. The price is a little high considering the hotel was not directly downtown, but not unusually high considering its location (a major city). We would stay here again if in the Boston area.

“Ottimo albergo!” Il punto forte di questo hotel è senza'altro la posizione! Nel bel mezzo di Union Square, ha la tradizionale presentazione dei Westin di tutto il mondo; con il classico maggiorgomo vestito di rosso subtio fuori la porta, sembra di entrare in un'altra epoca...pavimenti in marmo, soffitti altissimi, affreschi e hall molto curata; la camera era grande e spaziosa, sempre molto pulita. La wii fii a pagamento non è un problema visto che a 100 metri c'è uno Starbucks. Al piano terra sono presenti alcuni negozi e ristoranti, Il negozio più grande è quello di Victoria Secret, Possibilità di noleggiare auto, in quanto all'interno è presente uno sportello della Hertz. Io lo consiglierei.

“Spectacular Room!” Terrific experience from the time my loyalty ambassador Ashley contacted me until we left! I got into town early and Ashley had my room ready by the time I got from the train station! It was fabulous. It was on the 20th floor, out of the front window was the bay and the side had a balcony with Petco Park. The room was very large, clean, just perfect. They attended to our every need. The location is super. We were in town for an anniversary trip and also went to the Padres games. So easy to take the walk way over to the park, no lines, no waiting! I sure hope that I will be back in the future!

“Great location for a great price” We stayed in one of the non-renovated rooms on the 2nd floor. The room was old, but clean and comfortable. No complaints about the decor or quality as we knew it was not one of the newer rooms. The location was within minutes of union square and extremely accessible to the cable car and BART. Tons of great food options withing 2 blocks in all directions. Especially delicious was Golden Coffee right across the street. Walls are a little thin- but only affected us once and that was due to ridiculously loud neighbors that no wall could keep the noise out :) Staff was courteous, and for the price we couldn't have asked for more!

“First-class hotel” I stayed here on my most recent trip to Chicago and was very pleased in all respects. The front desk staff upgraded my room without any special pleading on my part, they switched the duvet for a blanket without asking, etc. Probably the best, most consistently attentive service staff I've encountered for a year. My room was good, as usual. The location is excellent, the facility is very attractive and all around the Sofitel Chicago gets my highest recommendation.

“Great hotel. A must stay...” Just stayed here after growing tired of my standard NYC places. Wow. I am so glad I pushed myself out of the box. Very good hotel. Great staff. Will stay here again. At subway. Easy ride to Penn station. Theaters right down the street. Only thing that put a bad marked on the service, was the upgraded room. While nice, it dumped my corner room for a skyview room a fraction of the size and no glass on two walls. It was only 3 floors higher. WTF. I paid dearly for a corner room and was "downgraded". The plus was after a quick trip to front desk and the problem was very quickly resolved.

“You simply cannot do better” I don't stay at a lot of really top end hotels. For me it's mostly Hiltons etc. However, I've stayed at the Drake in Chicago, the St. Francis in San Francisco, The Four Seasons in Atlanta and The Ritz in Pasadena. In my experience nothing compares to the Trump. The hotel itself is not what you expect. The footprint is small so there's no grand entrance. However, the rooms are very very nicely appointed - I can honestly say that I have never felt sheets like that before. The location - a block off Michigan - is fantastic. However, what makes the Trump so much better than anywhere else is the service. With the exception of the St. Francis (which is awful) top hotels like those listed above always have great service. However, the Trump is in a class above the rest. I stayed two nights. Every single time that I encountered a hotel staffer they were open, friendly and helpful. Not once were they on the phone with a friend, chewing gum or acting like the clerks that I am used to seeing at Hilton class hotels. I went into the gift shop one morning and, as my foot entered the doorway the girl behind the counter said "I have to go into her cell phone" closed it and walked up to see how she could help me. Each time I entered or left the hotel the bellstaff were first class. Each time I called for assistance with whatever the phone was answered immediately and whatever I needed was done instantly. Call to order breakfast - fast, exactly right and tasty. I'm not saying that there aren't better hotels somewhere in the world. I'm sure that the super rich stay in places that I can only dream about. However, the super rich don't bother with Trip Advisor. This site is for people who don't always get pampered. And, for those of us who don't travel by Gulfstream, I simply cannot imagine how a hotel could be better than the Trump. If you get the chance - stay there.

“Unexpected pleasure in the heart of Chicago” I admit I wasn't sure what to expect. I needed a hotel room for a conference in Chicago and everything else in the vicinity was well in excess of $200 per night. I looked at the reviews and the photos of the tiny, tiny, room and figured, "What the heck?". I arrived in Chicago, took the blue line downtown, and walked two blocks to the hotel where I was pleasantly surprised! The lobby was clean, modern, and the staff friendly and helpful. I quickly checked in and went upstairs... the filtered bottled water was another great surprise (and one i've used every single night of my stay!!). The room is small - yes... but well laid out and perfectly adequate for me as a solo traveler. It is very comfortable and immaculately clean. There is a Starbucks in the same building, an Elephant and Crown pub downstairs, and a Potbelly's sandwich shop next door along with dozens of other restaurants within a few blocks. Great hotel, HIGHLY recommended! Thank you for a terrific stay!

“Absurd room configuration” Our Junior Suite had plenty of space, but much of it was unusable. An L-shaped room, one complete section was almost entirely unfurnished and unlit. In the usable section, the desk and dresser were jammed next to the bed, giving it the feel of a Motel 6. The bathroom was equally cramped. One sink with no counter space in a Junior Suite? Upsides: reasonably priced, convenient to the Convention Center and clean, with friendly service. Comfortable pillows and more creative furniture placement would make this hotel a 4.
“Time square jewel” Stayed 6 nIghts. Great value considering location and size of room. So close to shows. Only drawback was noise from slamming doors in hallway. Other than that was perfect.

“Not sure why folks like this hotel.” My second worst room short of the decrepit Manhattan in the Starwood system. Check in was awkward with weird explanations of construction being done on some floors despite hotel being "finished". The room I was assigned is smaller than any of the NYC Four Points and even smaller than the original W on the East Side. So small in fact that the only way to set up an ironing board was in the doorway and I had to stand in the bathroom. Calls to the front desk were not answered for 30 minutes. Everything's new but that's the only thing this place has going for it. I'm Starwood Platinum and got stuck next the maid's closet and ice machine with smallest room on the floor. . Hate to think of the kinds of rooms non-status SPGers get. Trying to get a manager to help but not overly hopeful.

“Courtyard by Marriott is a Gem!” This is the best place to stay in Center City. It really is the best location in the entire city. The staff is helpful and friendly. The rooms are great with some awesome views of City Hall. The Reading Terminal Market is around the corner so eating wasn't a problem. All the historical sites are within walking distance. The only problem is parking. I ended up using their valet service ($40 a night!) because I wasn't going to battle the parking problem in the city. Unless you are going to New Jersey to visit relatives like we had to do, I say don't even bother renting a car, use public transportation and save some money!

“Great hotel & value” This is a perfect place to stay if you are going to be in downtown Houston. The rooms are spacious and the shower is great. Another bonus is the free breakfast on the second floor. The staff was courteous especially the valet guys out front. Couldn't be happier, and will definitely stay there again.

“Great hotel, great location!” This is a small, modern boutique hotel located just one block from Chicago's magnificent mile. I couldn't have picked a better location for a quick overnight stay in Chicago. We were upgraded to a suite and it was just perfect. The staff were wonderful--gracious and courteous. I usually don't consider my experiences with staff when giving a rating but everyone was so exceptional that I feel they deserve some accolades. I will definitely stay here again the next time I'm in Chicago.

“Beautiful classic old-world style hotel...with a couple of glitches” We just returned from a 3-night stay at the Fairmont. We stayed in room 675, which is the older main building, not the tower. The room we booked was a queen sized bed, interior courtyard view. There is no view to speak of - you're looking at the room across from you. That was fine and I knew that when I booked the least expensive room. Check-in went smoothly and they were able to accomodate our early arrival time of 11 am. The room itself was gorgeous and fairly large. The bathroom is a bit small, but nicely appointed in marble and the shower pressure is excellent. Great walk-in closet. Has the usual overpriced minibar and the dresser was kind of small if you were staying for more than 3-4 days, but the closet space more than made up for it. Very clean. The beds are the BEST I have ever experienced at any hotel (sorry Ritz Carlton!) and were so comfortable that falling asleep was effortless. While falling asleep was effortless, actually STAYING asleep provided to be the greater challenge. The walls in the main building are paper thin and the couple in the room next to us on our first night there was having the most major of arguments, complete with things being thrown around the room and profanities abounding. We called security at midnight and things did seem to calm for awhile, but picked up again with the same behavior. We could hear everything. Granted, these people were completely inconsiderate, but even when the tenants changed the following day, we could still hear talking - so just beware that while the rooms are indeed beautiful, your conversation and activities are not completely your own. The lobby is indeed palatial and deserving of its place in grand hotel history. Complimentary coffee was offered in the morning. We did not eat at all in the Laurel Court, although it did look quite nice. The other hiccup in our Fairmont stay was the Tonga Room - the lower floor bar complete with fake rain, thunder and lightning. We went on Friday night for happy hour, since we had read multiple times that this is the best happy hour in the city. What a joke. The buffet is a waste at 9.95, nasty frozen egg rolls and overfried chicken wontons with salty noodles on the side. Don't even bother. We were definitely disappointed in the Tonga Room. The "thunder and rain" effects appeared super-cheesy as well - to be honest, they do a better job with that kind of thing at any Rainforest Cafe. The staff was very friendly. Maid service was great. We requested a wake-up call our last evening there and it was promptly administered the following morning. Location is wonderful atop of Nob Hill - really can't ask for anything more with the location of the Fairmont in San Fran. I'd stay there again with a couple of things I'd change now that I have firsthand knowledge. I'd spring for a room in the tower with the hope that the walls have to be thicker since it is a newer structure and I'd avoid the Tonga Room at all costs.

“Not that grand hyatt” My husband, six year old son and I spend four nights here over my son's spring break. I picked the hotel because I got a really good rate and it was in Union Square. First the good. If you want to stay in Union Square it's a very good location with public transporation/foot travel within easy distance. The staff were all great and immediately helpful. There is a place at the front desk to print out boarding passes for free. My husband said the work out room was very nice but there's no pool. Now the not so great. The room is cramped. There is not really a good workable space ie no desk. There is a table but it's not positioned well and it's too high for a workspace. Internet is $10 a day and that irritates me. There's a fantastic view from the restaurant but it is very pricey to eat there. We stayed on the third floor and had to wait for elevators. I can only imagine if the hotel had been booked full what the wait would be like for higher floors! There is plenty of shopping within a few blocks and several restaurants. You can also walk to car rental offices within a few blocks. Bottom line we enjoyed our visit but I doubt I would overwhelmingly recommend this property unless you want to be in Union Square specifically.

“Great stay in convenient location” We stayed in this hotel for 5 nights in a Superior queen room. The room was as described on the hotel website and they were very comfortable and not too cramped. A couple of things were not working properly such as the door latch was broken to the bathroom and water pressure in the shower-over-bath was lousy as it came out both the bath and shower head and couldnt be adjusted. We had room service one night which was quite ordinary, very greasy and not worth the money. The female concierge was very helpful making travel and tour arrangements whereas the male concierge didn't seem interested in helping us. There were no noise disruptions during night although as some other reviewers have noted, it does get quite noisy around the pool and cabana rooms especially on Friday & Saturday nights. I was happy with this hotel as there are not many around in the central Hollywood Blvd area for this price and quality and I would stay here again.

“Above Expectations -- Good Value -- location Not an issue” When I booked this hotel for a 1 night stay I was not excited about the location (preference was north michigan avenue), but I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms, and restaurant were very nice. Access to grant park was extremely convenient. The room was ~$200/night, which was about $70 dollars less than the north michigan avenue. $10 cab ride to shopping area was not a big deal at all. Consider as a great value hotel in downtown Chicago.

“Nice room & helpful staff - food could be better” I stayed here for 2 nights on a business trip. It's close to the airport and within walking distance to quite a few restaurants. When my colleague & I arrived our rooms weren't ready, so they wound up finding us two different rooms right next door to each other. We mentioned that we were in a hurry to change our clothes and go to work, so they offered to box up our dinners and have them for us when we returned. We were surprised to learn that dinner was included in our stay! When we returned from working for the evening they brought our dinners to our rooms, but I couldn't eat it. I warmed it up in the microwave (rooms have a small full kitchen), but it made the steak rock hard and not edible. The veggies and mashed potatoes were ok, but tasted like cafeteria food. We wound up walking across the street to a restaurant to bring food back. Breakfast is also included and was a small buffet - decent eggs, meat and potatoes. My room on the third floor was nice. There were a bunch of families with teenage girls staying there for a softball tournament, so everywhere we went there were people. I didn't notice people being loud from room to room or in the hallway, a group of parents sat out in the courtyard (which my room looked out onto) until after 1am and I could hear them talking & laughing. After getting to the airport the following afternoon (I checked out that morning), I realized that I had left something in my room. I panicked and called the hotel, but of course it took them time to track it down, but eventually they did, so I had them ship it to me. The first girl I spoke to didn't seem to understand that I could get a tracking number for the Fed Ex package, but when I called to make sure it shipped the next day I was able to get one. Of course I had to pay for the shipping, but it arrived in one piece within 2 days. I would probably stay here again if I needed to be in that area, but I think this hotel would be best for people needing an extended stay.
“Great Hotel” Great Hotel in LA. Nice rooms..

“Met My Needs But Can't Enthusiatically Recommend for Long Stay” Perfectly adequate hotel located in Chinatown, Little Italy. While this hotel technically meets the geographic description of being in Manhattan's Soho neighborhood, it really should be calling itself Chinatown as it's one block from Canal Street. Rooms, as other reviewers have noted, are small. My wife, son and I stayed there for one night so she could go out with girlfriends in Chelsea and my son and I could do other things around time. We were booked into a room with 2 beds, but had requested a room with a king and a sofabed, if available, but it wasn't. New York City was dealing with Hurricane Sandy aftermath so hotel rooms were at a premium. If you're visiting Manhattan, and staying for a period of more than a night or two, you probably want to be in Midtown, Upper East Side or Upper West Side. That said, if you have Priority Club points, or enjoy the Holiday Inn chain, there is nothing fundamentally wrong with this property. Staff were friendly, room was clean, but all in all an average stay. Nothing bad, nothing great. But think about your average Holiday Inn from over a decade ago and that's what you're going to be getting at this location.

“Best SPG hotel for the price” Booked the hotel using our SPG points for a Sunday night with my wife and 3 month old. While the l The building itself is very beautiful as it's converted jail. The real gem about this place is the staff everyone he encountered greeted us by name and went above and beyond for everything we asked. The valley cost $42 which may seem expensive, however when you factor in that they were willing to go to our car retrieve items and bring them all up forerun all is part of the service it was well worth the price especially because we had our three-month-old In tow. I look forward to the next time we get to stay. One more thing the views of Boston from our room 1307 were insane!!

“Elegant Hotel” We stayed at the Melrose over the Christmas holiday, and loved every minute. We had a lovely King corner suite. The room was well appointed, a nice size and a good view of the skyline. The staff were friendly and helpful, the public rooms were very nice as well. The valet was prompt and helpful when our car arrived with a slight icy coated windshield. We enjoyed a fabulous Christmas brunch in the Landmark. We look forward to staying there again in the future.

“Expected More” I love nice hotels. I have never stayed at a Four Seasons before and found it very nice but not what I thought it would be. Very clean, well appointed, friendly, helpful but not Fantastic. Now if it was half the normal rate it might be Fantastic. I base alot of my review on price compared to quality. I have stayed at some Fantastic places for little money (I like Chicagos Hotel Burnham better) and I have paid a fortune for incredible places like the Pebble Beach properties (well worth every dime). The location can't be beat. The beds are incredible. Will I stay again; maybe but not likely.

“Comfort like you can't imagine!” My husband and I spent two amazing nights at the Four Seasons Chicago in October 2008. First, the view: We were on the 42nd floor with a view of the lake on one side and the city on the other. The sights were breathtaking and ever-changing. It was a real challenge to pull myself out of the room. Second, the bed: Wow! It must have been the combination of the featherbed and sumptuous linens because I have not been so comfortable or slept so well in a really long time. Leave yourself a few extra minutes before heading out for work or sightseeing to enjoy just laying there and taking in the views. Third, the service: As you can imagine, it was incredible. Everyone was extremely polite and helpful - always going out of their way to make our stay as easy as possible. Other pluses: fantastic spa and pool (you can use the spa sauna, hot tubs, showers, etc. even if you're not getting a treatment that day) and connection to shopping from the 6th floor (Bloomie's at your finger tips for everything you forgot to pack). One downside - I was not crazy about the food and while the oak bar was beautiful, the drinks were pretty pricey compared to the quality. Really, though - who cares? You should be out and about sampling all the great food Chicago has to offer anyway!

“Not all it's cracked up to be.” Very surprised this hotel is #1 on tripadvisor - very surprised. I booked this hotel based on its rating. I travel frequently on business...this is NOT I repeat NOT a hotel for the business traveler. The room is nice, it's upgraded with a nice layout. BUT: -I waited in line at checkin for 10 mins. Finally checked in and was given my key, went all the way up to my room with all my stuff and the key didn't work. I schlepped everything downstairs again, received a new key with no apology. -The carpeted stairways are dirty. Visible crumbs and whatever else. -An elevator door opened to see two 'bell racks' the racks used to transport luggage. Just two bell racks, no bell person. Thought was a strange occurrance only to have it happen again with another elevator. So they just leave the bell racks in the elevators...don't put them on service. You can't get in unless you're very small. -The sheets in the room are flimsy, and thin. Surprisingly they spent money on the refurbishing of the room but not a penny on the linens. There is no duvet on the bed - just a sheet and cover. If you have a tendency to get cold, prepare by asking them for extra blankets. -There are no toiletries provided except for a mini shampoo, and it's cheap. I can see how this hotel appeals to families on a budget with the convenience of free breakfast, but if you're used to traveling and staying at 3 plus star properties, this is not the place for you.

“Nice Hampton Inn” I stayed here on a recent business trip. It was convenient to the meeting location. As Hampton Inn's go,this one was very nice and the staff was exceptionally professional and friendly. I gave the location only a three, just because I'm a runner and this location seems to be bounded by highways and very busy streets with a lack of sidewalks.

“Comfortable Hotel, Wonderful Service” The W provided comfortable accomodations, reliable and friendly service along with extra touches throughout my stay. (Everything from Hot Cider at check-in to fortune cookies at night). Rooms are small, yet pricey. CD and DVD player included in rooms was easy to use and wonderful. Hotel offers complimentary use of CDs and DVDs during your stay via the Front Desk. Pool (Refered to as "Wet") is small, yet very clean. Excercise Room (reffered to as "Sweat") recived and equipment upgrade during my stay. Overall, great service and comfortable rooms yet pricey. I will return next time I am in San Fran.

“Great location” Stayed one Saturday night. Check-in was the fastest I have ever had anywhere. Had a room on the 17th floor overlooking the 16th street mall. Great views! The room was comfortable, clean, stylish. Unlike other hotels that charge $4.00 for the bottled water in the room, their bottles were complimentary. You can't beat the location for the Market Street bars and restaurants, and the shopping on the 16th Street mall. Valet was $21 but downtown you are going to pay at least that. There is a Starbucks in the lobby and you can even have it delivered to your room. This is a great hotel and I will stay here again!!

“A very pleasant, historic hotel in San Francisco” I was at the Beresford on Sutter Street, in February, 2012. I enjoyed my room on the 6th floor, with just a bit of a view. Room was very decently sized, and comfortable. Front desk was helpful. Did make use of the computer near the lobby. Breakfast was very serviceable. This hotel gives an excellent value. I liked the Sutter Street location, just a couple blocks to the west of Union Square. Also, convient to the public transportation. I am a repeat visitor of at least 8 visits, and truly enjoy my experience at th Beresford.

“Nice, clean room for area” I've stayed twice now at this location. The facility was clean both times. Breakfast buffet is normal for chain hotels but good. Honestly, the only problem we had this time was shuttling to and from the Reliant Center for the Houston Livestock show. My family used the shuttle several times last year and was excellent. This year, preference was given to the medical patients. Shuttle is supposed to run on the hour. It did but for medical only. After waiting for 20 to 30 minutes each time, we ended up driving. The good---this hotel takes GREAT care of the medical patients (I applaud them for this). The bad---we really wanted to utilize the shuttle but "free" shuttle service was not very accomodating each time we tried to use it because they had medical runs each time. No, location is not great but neither are the places I've stayed before in this same area. The rooms are clean and the staff is courteous.

“Fun Decor, Great location by Fisherman's Wharf” Stayed here for July 4th weekend, 2008. Hotel is 4 story building, conveniently located right by Fisherman's Wharf. At check-in, they placed me in 4th floor King bed room. Decor is colorful and fun. Room included a 42 inch LCD tv and even offered a few HD channels. Parking was expensive at $43/night but that is pretty standard in cities like San Francisco. We were able to walk a couple blocks to get to Fisherman's Wharf - a great area to stroll around and browse the various seafood, shops, and views off the piers. We were able to get to Chinatown with a 15 minute walk. The two things I loved about this hotel - the breakfast buffet and the outdoor firepits. Outside there are several semi-private sitting areas, each of which included a firepit. We bought a bottle of wine and just chilled outside, a fantastic and cozy way to finish off the night. The next morning, the breakfast buffet was pleasantly surprising. They offered small personal frypans with cooked veggie omelettes and home fries. My gf got a strawberry yogurt parfait while I was scooping up the salmon lox with capers. There was plenty of the standard continental fare in addition to the fresh mixed fruits. We had two complimentary passes but I saw from the menu it was rather expensive at $22+ per person. I would recommend based on value, location, and the firepits!

“Very nice boutique hotel” We recently stayed here and really enjoyed it. Service was great...not snobby like you sometimes find.The cappucino machine was broken 2 times while we there but that's not a major deal. We loved the wine/cheese reception in the evenings. The breakfast was good but not outstanding. Still nice to have something in your stomachs before you begin your day. We had booked a double/double by mistake and they still gave us a king when we checked in without charging us extra. Would stay here again. Location not really that central. I would say the nearest subway was easily 6 blocks away so be prepared to use cabs a lot or walk. We had a great stay though in our favorite city in the US.

“The best place to turn 40!!” My husband and I used 120,000 points and spent 5 fabulous days at the St. Regis for my 40th birthday last fall. I had planned the trip for months and wasn't disappointed. We were given a large, beautifully appointed room with an over-sized bathroom on the 3rd floor, and I couldn't believe how quiet it was given that the hotel is located right in the middle of downtown. The service we received from every staff member was outstanding, especially from one of our butlers, Anna, and the doorman (whose name, I'm sorry to say, I did not get) who had then Bentley town car take us to our restaurant, on my birthday, when he had been unable to hail us a cab. So, thank you everyone at the St. Regis for helping take the sting out of turning 40 and for making the trip so memorable!

“Relaxing Airport Stay” My partner and I spent an evening at the Sheraton Gateway before a next day flight to New Zealand. Customer service by everyone from the front desk to the hotel restaurant was friendly and efficient. The continuous airport shuttle was frequent and reliable. Our room was spacious (though the bathroom was comparatively small) with modern furnishings, very comfortable bed, and an entertaining view of the LAX runways. The overall feel of the public areas was like...an airport! The lobby and adjoining lounge were modern in design--clean, cool lines, but had little or no soundproofing. In the evening, the lounge pulsated with "techno" music and lots of twenty-somethings were drinking the night away. The noise level made it impossible to talk and relax. We arrived at the hotel late in the evening after flying in from Portland, OR and wanted to have a glass of wine before trying to sleep. We decided to take our wine back up to the room where relaxation was more likely. The fitness center is excellent with up-to-date and well maintained equipment. The room looks out over the pool area, which is nicely landscaped. When sitting by the pool, you can almost forget you're steps away from LAX. Only the roar of jets taking off and landing keep you in the moment. Overall, if staying at LAX is appropriate for your travel plans, the Sheraton Gateway makes a great choice!

“Love, love, love the London” We've stayed at many hotels in NYC over the years, but the London has by far been the best value for the price. Everything about the hotel is excellent - decor, service, amenities, cleanliness and location. The rooms are HUGE for NYC. From now on, the London is our home in NYC. Gordon Ramsey's restaurant is excellent - as is the breakfasts.

“Mandarin New York , A Great Experience” Just few words to say and rate our great experience at the Mandarin Oriental New York. Have been there for a couple of nights at the end of July 2008. Booked a simply superior room with a main Hudson view. The room was not huge but very nice with a lot of useful tech advantages and features. The bed was very comfortable despite of some really soft pillows. Bathroom perfect in size and very nice. Service absolutely fantastic, very nice view also if it not was not a Central Park room view. Enjoy a wonderful breakast ( also if is the service it was a little bit too slow ) at the Asiate Resturant. Unfortunately did not use the Spa or other services. So , one if the not the best hotel in New York right now , also if it was expensive. I really like new and High Tech hotel and this Mandarin it was in my opinion a true perfect layout . Additional to this , check in and check out were perfect and very quick , as well room service . Bravo Mandarin !

“Good experience” We stayed at The Omni in San Francisco for 3 nights while we went on a wine tour in Sedona. The service was good, the rooms were fine, and it was an overall good experience. I have stayed in nicer hotels, but this was in a good location to sight seeing and shopping. The rooms were quiet and the beds were confortable enough. We did, however eat at the restaurnant downstairs for dinner and breakfast and had some issues. The food was good, but the service was not. Waiters were slightly rude and one night at dinner we had to go find the hostess to be seated. We stood there for over 15 minutes. Across the street there is a stop for the trolley and the bellman was good about helping us hail taxis. One night they even had the hotel car take us to the pier for our alcatraz tour. Overall we had a good experience at this hotel and would recommend it to others.

“A quiet, charming hotel in the best location in town” Location is unbeatable, in the lower east corner of Central Park. It's also a quiet hotel, with friendly personnel at main desk and bar. The rooms are a comfortable, luxurious and fully equipped with large TV, DVD player, Bose player with iPod docking station, complimentary internet access!, etc. Also include several amenities like fruits, bathrobe, slippers, Molton Brown products.... and even though my room was at a lower floor, it was very quiet. I had to use the complimentary 24-hour business center which I found very useful. Not cheap, but definitely recommend it.

“Love this Hotel” We stayed here for two nights after a less than stellar stay at the Westin down the street. We got a good rate that included breakfast, and I signed up for the privilege card which gives you late checkout, and a free drink upon arrival. I didn't take advantage of either of those things, but they were nice if you had the opportunity to use them. All of the staff that we encountered were very helpful. I had reserved a queen bed for myself and my teenage daughter. We arrived before check in time. The front desk clerk said she could give us that room then, or if we could wait until 3 pm, she could give us a room with 2 twin beds. We jumped at that, so they held our bags, and we returned in the afternoon, wiped out from a day of walking and walking to the most comfortable beds we've ever slept in. It was like sleeping in a cloud. The bathroom was large, with huge soft white fluffy towels, and lots of fun extras, such as a candle, and teeth whitening mints. The tub was deep, and nice to soak in before going out for the night. We had so much fun sleeping in on the comfy beds, we didn't partake of the included breakfast. The Red Flame Diner a couple of doors down was great for carryout when returning back to the room from a show. This was my first time staying at a Sofitel, and hopefully not the last.

“A pleasant surprise” We stayed for 2 nights in Dec. 2007. Our party consisted of 2 adults, and 3 young children. I was pleasantly surprised! The hotel staff was very friendly, the room was a nice size and clean, and there were complimentary water bottles and snacks (chocolates and cookies). We didn't hear any of the road/freeway noise, and our room did face the freeway. We were in LA to visit family and some of the attractions, and the hotel was centrally located for all our planned activities. I have to agree with another reviewer that for a "junior suite" it was an average sized hotel room, but we did all fit perfectly. There was even a fridge and a microwave. The hotel has a small indoor pool. Towels are provided at poolside. It's not the greatest pool, but for 3 small kids who love to splash around, it was great to have. Free parking too. I would definitely stay here again and recommended. Great value for the price and location.

“Nice hotel in great location” My wife and I stayed at the Hilton during the US Masters Track and Field National Championships. The hotel's location was close to the University and shopping. The rooms were very nice and the service was wonderful. They have a nice swimming pool, excellent room service, and free parking. I got a great price on Priceline. I would stay here again.

“Oasis in Westwood” We used the Palomar as our home base while visiting colleges, and we're very pleased. As always with Kimpton properties the in- house restaurant was excellent. The service was efficient and pleasant. The hotel is very convenient to the Getty Museum and UCLA. The exercise facility was somewhat disappointing, and smaller than some other Palomar hotels. Overall, I would recommend the L.A. Palomar if your travels bring you to this part of Los Angeles.

“Tolles Hotel mit einiger Lärmbelästigung” Das Hotel befindet sich direkt an der Riesenbaustelle des WTC. Um Verzögerungen zu vermeiden, wird 24 Stunden gebaut, was leider auch im Zimmer zu hören ist. Ein Schreiben der Direktion und beigelegte Ohrstöpsel weisen darauf hin. Zimmer sind groß, gewohnte Bettenqualität. Gute Lage des Hotels, in unmittelbarer Nähe zur Subway, viele Lokale in der Umgebung. Internet nur in der Lobby, hier angeblich gratis. Tolles Hallenbad (mit Blick auf die Baustelle) und Sauna sowie Fitness im 5. Stock. Alle Nebenleistungen dem Szandard entsprechend teuer.

“Couldn't ask for more” We went to Memphis for Thanksgiving and had a great time at Springhill. Perfect location that was 4 and a half steps from the trolley line. We had a total of 14 people so we needed the space, which Springhill provided. Two queen size beds, a pull out couch, two big tvs, and a bar area in the room ;). Our favortie part was the excellent breakfast. Every option you cold think of from waffles and oatmeal, to cereal and fruit. Breakfast was included with the room, which we figured we saved over 100 bucks per day by not going out. We will certainly go back here next time in Memphis, made everything extra perfect!

“No Complaints” Great location and super helpful staff. I would definitely stay there again. The lobby is not that spectacular but the room was perfect and we had a great view. Booked on hotwire and there were no glitches at check in.

“Convenient and comfortable. Worth the price.” This is a very convenient property within Terminal D at the Dallas-Fort Worth airport. I had stayed at this hotel multiple times since it opened, usually for an overnight in transit, but this time I spent two nights there during a business trip to Dallas rather than use another property outside the airport. I was not disappointed. The welcome from the check-in staff was efficient, warm and friendly. The room was the usual excellent Hyatt accommodation with absolutely no aircraft noise even though the airport was its usual busy self. My experience in the restaurant was first class: service, food and ambience. Service throughout my stay was excellent from all staff members. Not only can one not beat the convenience (security is at the bottom of the hotel escalator) but this Grand Hyatt is certainly not the usual in-airport hotel. It's really an airport resort!

“Good for uptown Dallas stay” We stayed at the Hyatt House Dallas/Uptown in order to attend a wedding at the nearby Rosewood Crescent which was too expensive for us and were pleased with our choice. The room was spacious, clean and comfortable and would be great for a much longer stay than a weekend. It's a studio-type configuration with a small, well-equiped kitchen, walk-in closet, and a TV/storage room divider between the bed and living area. The sofa is big enough for stretching out plus is a pull-out bed. Mark was very pleasant and efficient at check-in. No problems with our reservation at all. Parking is $12/day; it's covered and secure. Breakfast was hot, fairly run-of-the-mill. Overall, a good stay. Down side was that floors seemed thin. The heavy footed, night owl guest above us woke us up several times hence the lower sleep quality rating; mattress and bedding were very nice. Go for the top floor.

“what a great weekend in La Jolla!!!!” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Hyatt Regency LaJolla for a long weekend to attend a wedding last week. Overall, it was a terrific stay! The one thing that stood out to me was the impeccable service! Vicky and Emily at the front desk were so friendly and willing to help with recommendations, directions, and neosporin! Waitstaff at the pool, valets and doormen were very friendly and constantly moving to meet the needs of their clientele. The hotel was very clean and we were on the Regency club level. To us, it was definitely worth the upgrade fee for the access to continental breakfast, snacks, and drinks throughout most of the day. The furnishing/decor of the room was a little dated but the room was so quiet and the bed very comfortable. The hotel has a beautiful pool area with a bar and cabanas. The pool is heated which is a bonus. The parking (valet or self park garage) is expensive but there are many places along the street nearby where we were able to park at no charge. The hotel is not in the La Jolla cove area; it is about a 10 minute drive, but the drive is pleasant. I checked that "yes" there is a Fitness Center but it is actually its own entity adjacent that incurs an additional fee for use. We would definitely stay at this hotel again!

“Good Hotel in a Great Location - Excellent Value” Stayed here over the weekend with family, three rooms in all. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. The lounge downstairs was a bit understaffed but the service was extremely friendly and as prompt as one could possibly expect. If I have one minor complaint, the rooms are a bit tight but you're not going to find anything larger on Capitol Hill without spending a LOT more money.

“Avoid at all cost!!!!” Was there from 9/19 to 9/25 on a training conference with 70 others and could not to leave for another hotel in town. All the other attendees had similar complaints to mine. The hotel is in bad need of renovation. The rooms are run down with holes in the wall, paint peeling and appliances not working and that was with the complimentary upgrade to the concierge level! Response to a power cut that lasted from 4am to 3pm was terrible. No electricity, water, phone or elevators functionning for all that time. Many emergency stairs were locked which is a fire violation. Employees could not answer the simplest of questions and guests were left to fend on their own. It is a miracle no one got hurt as far as I know. Hotel manager should be fired for this lack of preparedness planning and for this dismal response to an emergency. Finally the location is TERRIBLE, just 2 blocks from 5 or 6 strip joints including Hustler. Women in our group never went out alone after dark. Even myself, could not walk out at night without getting offers such as "Hi honey, wanna buy my love?" I guess if you like that type of scene....you should check it out. Anyway, I love staying in Radissons in general but would never go back to that one again!

“In line with the chain and value” Staff was really nice but the room was ok despite maybe a renovation? There was an odd odor that was probably new materials but it came off weird. I tried a couple rooms so I don't think it was a cleanliness issue. I slept just fine but didn't personally care for the decor and coloring.

“Great location by O'Hare” I stayed at this property for a conference. At first glance, you can see the property looks a little dated. However, it is so well maintained and clean, that it wasn't an issue. The lobby is large, and there's a Starbucks inside, as well as a bar/restaurant just off the lobby. The staff were always friendly and helpful—helping me with directions, information about their airport shuttle... even giving me a can of shaving cream when I found myself lacking. The room had all the amenities I desire: coffee, nice-sized workstation and internet. The bed was comfortable and had good-quality pillows, and the bathroom worked well. The blinds were perfect for sleeping. Keep in mind this hotel is right by the airport and a major highway, so there will be the roar of airplanes and trucks now and then. Not an issue for me, but it might be for you.

“Pretty darn good.” Pros: * Friendly front desk staff. Some of the best I've come across in the city. Didn't blink twice when I asked for a late check-out. * Comfortable bed and nice flat screen HDTV. A flat screen TV with a huge selection of cable channels and actual HD channels. I hate those hotels that have the flat screen with only analog channels. Why bother? * Great location if you're a fan of Hell's Kitchen. * 25K Priority Club Points per night. An absolute steal for a hotel of this quality in midtown Manhattan. Cons: * Incredibly small bathroom and shower. I could barely fit inside the shower and turn around. * The king size bed takes up the lions share of the bedroom. Don't plan on doing any greco-roman wrestling within these friendly confines. * You're right next to the bus terminal. 'Nuf said.

“Great hotel - just be aware of location” I loved this hotel. Very clean quality rooms. Spacious, comfortable beds, clean renovated bathrooms and tea and coffee making etc. It really had everything and also included breakfast. Probably for about $100 less per night than similar SF hotels. Now you do have to be aware about the area it's in though. As someone who lives in an inner-city area myself I was fine with it. But I can see how a family or an elderly couple who are used to suburban or rural living would find it confronting. However if you are saving $100 per night you can afford to pay for door-to-door cabs to and from the hotel and still come out well in front! So I believe it is definitely worth it - perfect choice for young travellers used to city living. Not ideal location for elderly or families but if you just remember to take cabs you won't even notice you're in a dodgy area!

“Great location, tiny room, big price tag” I'm in my 50s, not my 30s, so staying at some impossibly hip, trendy hotel isn't at the top of my priority list. A client booked me at the Gramercy Park for a nearby meeting. I had to ask for a flashlight to see the sign-in card. When did dark lobbies get so trendy? Remember when Cher sold a line of Goth furniture in the late 80s -early 90s? She must have sold a lot to this hotel. Lots of studded stuff, tapestries, and metal, "updated" with orange and pink. I had to stand on the corner of my bed to open the bathroom door. (The bathroom was just exquisite, don't get me wrong.) I had trouble falling asleep with the orange and pink and could not read by the light of the 20 watt teacup lanterns next to the bed. And I paid a whopping $560 for one night, when all the taxes were included. The location is just as fantastic as everyone says. But give me dowdy over this au courant nonsense every time.

“Pleasant stay” We were here for one night. Our room was on the executive floor at the back of the hotel. The executive lounge was modest and we were only able to use it for the complimentary continental breakfast, which was fine. Unlike some executive lounges we have visited, this one only had views of adjacent residential and commercial buildings.

“Best Hotel Ever!!!” Literally not a bad thing to say about this hotel. The front dest staff is impeccable. They make sure you are VERY well informed. They inform you of the 12.00 parking...which may sound bad BUT it is a monitored lot and thats comforting near the airport. There is a living room area with COMPLIMENTARY water, cheese, candy, chips, ice cream and yogurt. Seriously unreal!! The room itelf is VERY well appointed. Very comfortable bed...plush towels...big flat screen television with a great assortment of channels. This is leaps and bounds far superior to any hotel I have EVER stayed in. While the location isn't ideal...they have a shuttle that can take you to the train that goes downtown. I took a card of their other properties and I only hope they are all as wonderful as this one. Every single employee we encountered was friendly and greeted you. It was just great and kudos to this hotel for hitting a home run with me and my partner!

“problems but good customer service” I cancelled a reward stay at this hotel because I didn't think I would make it in time. At 1 am I arrived into JAX and wanted to try to use reward points to stay here. The night staff said it was too late to do it online but I should call the rewards number. He was very nice and trying to help me out. He could tell I was really tired and just needed a place to sleep till morning. Finally we worked something out but he said he would have to actually assign the room after 4 am (?) He let me into a nice room with more than I needed. A nice little kitchen area. I tried to take a shower to unwind but the shower head was not working. I was in an accessible room (didn't need it) but the hand held showers weren't working. I would deal with it in the am but then I couldn't turn the water off. I just went to sleep and let the water run. In the am. I tried to tell the day time staff who didn't appear interested. Eventually I let Marriott know and received a nice call from the manager at the property. They comp'd my stay. Maintenance issues happen but the customer service is the important part. My experience was very good.
