“Clean but small” This hotel is very clean and the staff is friendly. We checked inn right away. when we got to our room it was very nice but there were a few problums.1. the lamp light baulbs were burnt .2. The bathroom was very small. The hotel staff is very freindly and the gift shop staff will go out of there way to get you what ever you need.The location is great and it is a very nice nebor hood. I would defenitly stay at this hotel again.

“Not your average Hampton Inn” My family of four and my brother stayed at this hotel recently during a short vacation to San Antonio. We booked two rooms which were identical in size and furnishings. This new hotel far exceeds your average Hampton Inn due to the very nice furnishings and modern decor. The employees were friendly and ready to help. I reported that someone (not me!!) had spilled some substance like a smoothie on the floor outside of the 3rd floor evelators. I got a cup of coffee, went back upstairs and an employee was already cleaning up the spill. The bed was very comfortable and inviting with its clean white linens. The vanity area in the bathroom had ample storage area so that the counter didn't have to be cluttered. The breakfast was still your average Hampton Inn breakfast (hot entree, cereals, pastries, fruit, juices, coffee) but they did put out some delicious cookies out in the evenings. The pool is indoors and has a separate hot tub which was relaxing after a long day. The only drawback to this Hampton Inn right now is that there is alot of highway construction going on in the area. The hotel front desk employees were very helpful in explaining another route to get downtown to avoid the construction. Even though it is close to the highways, we didn't hear any highway noise.

“Enjoyed the room, but not the parking.” The hotel is directly located across the street from the SEA-TAC Airport. Got a great deal for the room and loved the comfort of the beds. However, compared to the other hotels on the same strip, the parking costs are outrageous. North of $20 daily for self parking (but you get in/out privileges). It is a quite a generous walk from the self parking garage, though the long meeting room hallways, past the restaurant/bar, through the main lobby, past the front desk, and down another hall to the elevators. They really want to encourage the more expensive valet option (how much you ask? well beyond the self parking daily charge). When I asked if there was anything that could be done to help lower the self parking charges since the competition sitting next door only charged half the Hilton's price, they suggested the airport parking. I would strongly suggest seeking a different hotel in the local vicinity since the Hilton is one of the more expensive properties on the strip facing the airport. Parking costs are the one thing that didn't make the stay worth it for me.

“One night stop in NY” Stopped one night on Manhattan en route on a business trip. Usual small room I have stopped in in previous visits to NY, but smart, clean and comfortable. Location of hotel just off Times Square but far enough away from the bustle. Staff very friendly and courteous, breakfast served next door or as room service.

“Dumpy hotel but good location” I booked this hotel based on location and the price ($199/nite). The location was good - short walk from Times Square, Rockefeller Center, etc. Lots of train lines nearby as well. I have to say, the hotel was quite the dump. Our room was dingy, the rug was ripped up, the TV was terrible (but who watches TV), the bathroom had hair all over the walls (gross), toilet was backed up when we checked in, the vents were filthy and the bed was terrible. I've been to New York many times and stayed at different hotels in different price ranges. I tried to stay out of the room as much as possible here because it skeeved me out. The vents were completely covered in dust, which made me wonder what the hell was I breathing. Don't be fooled, the lobby of the Hotel is beautiful and very modern, but the rooms are run down and not very nice.

“Wouldn't Stay Anywhere Else in NYC” Before I go further into the details of my stay at the Skyline, I feel that it's important to go into detail about my entire trip and who I am.I'm a 24-year-old who has never been on a solo trip before. I didn't even go to sleepover camp (I believe my reasoning was, "everything cool is at home, so why leave?"). I'm also a cheapskate, so the idea of a major trip sent my wallet screaming.After a family member noted that I hadn't gone anywhere in around a decade, I started planning out a trip - Boston, NYC and New Orelans were possibilities, but NYC was the final choice. I would be taking Amtrak from Chicago to NYC (20 hours in Coach, only for the truly hardcore - the train portion of the trip partially inspired by watching too many episodes of the CBS show "Amazing Race"), due to the fact that Amtrak offers rail sale fares on their internet website (in my case, I ended up getting $26.60 each way to NYC and back, which made my cheap side happy.)So, I would leave Chicago at 7pm (ended up being 8, late train) and get to NYC at 1:50pm (ended up more like 3:50pm). That, and I was up the majority of the day before leaving. Once I walked through the hotel doors, I would be going on 36 hours with maybe one or two (tops) hours of sleep.Now, you're probably considering my credibility, given the fact that I have never booked a hotel on my own and had a trip of my own. Personally, I think this makes my review an especially valid one, considering the fact that everything had to go especially right, given the fact that I'd never dealt with any hotel issues (loss of reservation, etc.) That, and the fact that I'd been up for nearly 36 straight hours really made it a necessity that I'd get in my room with a minimum of trouble.I arrived on Sunday evening at 4:30, after walking from Penn Station (which is about 17 blocks/20-25 minutes). Although there were a couple of clerks at the desk (very nice, too and skilled - dealing better than I could ever have with customers on the phone and in front of them at the same time. There were no issues with my reservation and I was in my room within a matter of minutes.This being my first solo trip, I did a massive amount of research into NYC hotels, taking into location, amenities and price (remember, I'm cheap.) The price on hotels for a single room was $109 a night, which is a surprisingly good deal, considering the price of most NYC hotel rooms. While you may find hotels for cheaper in the city, you'll probably end up sharing your bathroom with your neighbors in the hall. While that's popular in Europe apparently, I'd like to go whenever I please.So, I opened up my door on the 5th floor of the main building (the Skyline has two wings, one w/9 floors and one main one w/5) and was rather pleasantly shocked with what I saw. While not massive, the room had quite an above-average amount of space, with plenty of room around the bed, a very nice bathroom and a very nice closet.In the front of the room were four drawers and on top, a very spiffy Sony flatscreen TV that appeared to be around a 20-24 inch. In the closet was an in-room safe and an ironing board and iron. The bathroom had a hair dryer and a nice-sized bathtub/shower (I'm 6ft2, so if I say it's nice-sized, it's pretty nice-sized). 3 fairly large lamps were placed in the room, one that turned on when a switch by the door was flicked. Last, but not least, a comfy chair sat by the door. Everything appeared clean and welcoming; while not sleek and modern, I prefered the warm and comfy approach of the room's appearance.As for other aspects of the hotel:1. The lobby has a well-stocked rack of pamphlets about many NYC attractions. Maps were also available here.2. There is a pool on the Penthouse level of the 9-story wing. While I didn't take a swim (nobody wants to see me in a bathing suit, trust me), the pool is quite beautiful and heated. For those who don't want to swim, stop by here anyway for an almost impossibly beautiful view of the city (there are chairs to take a seat and watch the view), especially during sunset. The pool is only open on some off-hours (evenings generally, it seemed), but it's certainly a bonus, as I really saw few other hotels in NYC with indoor pools when I did my research and I really doubt if any of the other ones have a view like this.3. There is a parking lot where you can store your car (in/out ability costs more) for a small fee.4. The hotel has a very pleasant restaurant/bar on the ground floor, as well as a gift shop.5. There is a concierge in the lobby.6. The hotel TV offers about 30 channels of basic cable/local TV, as well as pay-per-view movies (some surprisingly recent releases - "Pirates of the Caribbean", "American Wedding", "Bruce Almighty" and "The Hulk" were some of the choices as of 10/4/03 - none of which were available yet on video/DVD yet as of that time). The pay-per-view price ranged from $9.99-11.99, which does seem a little steep until you think about the fact that going to the movies in Manhattan costs about $10 and personally, I'd rather watch something in the comfort of the room.The neighborhood is an interesting situation, because you're not in Midtown, yet you're practically in Midtown. The hotel, on 10th (between 49th and 50th) is in a small neighborhood of shops, grocery stores and apartments. Across the street on 10th are a couple of grocery stores and Fat Sal's Pizza, which I became addicted to during my stay (for $12, you get a ridiculously huge pizza that also happens to be quite good.)While this is not an area of skyscrapers and hustle/bustle, Times Square is literally about 5 blocks away. During two of the mornings I was there, I walked over to Times Square at about 6:30 in the morning when the sun was just coming up, which provided both the remarkable experience of seeing the lights in the darkness and also, seeing them with few other people/crowds around. The Intrepid air/space museum (which was certainly one of the main highlights of my trip - it's a real Naval aircraft carrier turned into a museum, accompanied by a destroyer and submarine, all sitting on the Hudson River. It's a must if you go to NYC; while kids will be fascinated by the ability to stand next to fighter jets on the deck of an aircraft carrier, adults will be able to get spectacular views of the city and the river - from the deck of a 40,000 ton aircraft carrier, no less.) was located only a couple of minutes away, on 12th ave. While the neighborhood isn't Central Park West spiffy, I certainly felt safe and enjoyed the atmosphere. For use of a better description, it feels like a real neighborhood. For those of you familiar with Chicago, I'd compare it to some areas of Lincoln Park.The staff of the Skyline were certainly very welcoming and attentive throughout my stay. During my trip, I developed a mild cold (nothing I couldn't fight through to enjoy the trip, but still, it was draining) and didn't really feel like seeking out a place to cash a traveler's check. They were more than willing to do so. When I returned mid-afternoon each afternoon, my room was cleaned to the point where it looked like it did when I got there on the first night. With my cold, it was nice to have a place to come back to at the end of the day where I could really recharge so I'd be able to enjoy the next day and also, so I could feel good enough to deal with the 20+ hour trip home on the train.While the Skyline made my trip a really wonderful one, I do have a couple of veeerrryy minor suggestions/notes.* Perk up the lighting in the halls. While certainly not dim or dark, I felt like maybe having the halls a little brighter would bring a bit more energy. Nothing major. * I had a room nearby the elevator on the top floor of one wing. While there was a little bit of noise outside the door of the elevator coming up, going back down, it certainly wasn't an issue. However, I could see where maybe this same room-next-to-the-elevator on some of the lower floors could hear it pass by more often. As for the elevators, the two elevators were clearly enough to handle the traffic - I never waited long for an elevator. * A couple additional vending machines on floors other than the second floor, which is also where the ice machine is located. Another note for potential visitors is to check the hotel's website (**********). Rates seem to differ ($109-119 seemed to be the norm for a single room, but I've occasionally spotted $99 a night rates. The $109 that I paid for my room was a very satisfactory value (I think I'd be happy with $135 a night for the room I was in), but $99 a night for a room would be a truly fantastic deal.Overall, I couldn't have been happier with my experience at the Skyline. It had to go without a flaw due to the amount of traveling I had to do to get there and my inexperience with travel and it did. Just a great time.

“Look no place else” Let me begin by telling you that I researched hotels in DC for about 6 months before traveling there so it's safe to say I looked into most of the big name hotels. I got a travelers guide from the Visitors Bureau and looked at each and every hotel in their book. The Embassy Suites isn't right for everyone but it fit our needs perfectly and may fit yours as well. We were traveling with our children ages 12 and 15 so we wanted enough room to allow them privacy and have a place for us to unwind after a day of walking so the idea of a suite was a must for us. The Embassy Suites offer a true suite design with a bedroom that is totally seperate from the living room. Some of the "suites" we looked at were actually just a larger room than a normal hotel room and perhaps had a "sitting area" so don't be fooled by what some hotels call a suite. Prices will certainly vary depending on the time of year and the occupancy level but we paid $309 per night and was glad to pay it. Other hotels with similar rooms were almost twice this rate. OUTSIDE APPEARANCE: 3 The outside of the ES is nothing to catch your eye but who cares! There are many eye catching hotels in DC but unless you plan on sitting on the curb and admirring the brick work for hours, the outside isn't that important. The drive was clean and the bellmen were dressed nicely and always helpful. LOBBY: 3 Again...who cares. It's nothing to look at. The Concierge is to your left at a small desk and was VERY helpful and friendly. We were greeted within minutes and were checked in less than 5 . The staff were always smiling and friendly...every day. ATRIUM: 5 Near the elevators is the center atrium and it is very nice. There are small waterfalls and beautiful fish that surround the gift shop area with tables and chairs for relaxing at the Managers Special in the evening. ROOM: 5 Our room was nicely decorated, had a flat screen TV, was full of amenitites and the maid service did a WONDERFUL job cleaning it each day. It was big enough to utilize the pull out sofa AND add a roll-away if you wanted to. We had the King Corner suite and I would recommend getting that for the few extra dollars just because it is off-set in the corner and a bit more secluded and perhaps a bit quieter. The King bed was very comfortable, water pressure was good, never ran out of hot water. I did notice something that another reviewer mentioned: the tap water seems a bit warm at all times but aside from brushing my teeth, I never used the tap water. We bought a case of water at CVS and kept it in the refrigerator. The room was very quiet. We were on the 3rd floor but never noticed any traffic noise or the neighbors. FREE BREAKFAST: 5+ How can you go wrong with this. We ate the free breakfast for 4 days in a row. Never had to wait and the food was great! Juice, coffee, omelets, waffles, becon, fresh fruit.... for a family of 4 each meal would have cost about $30-35 and it would have taken more time out of our day. This was a huge factor in our decision to stay at the ES and it was a BIG pay-off. EVENING MGRS SPECIAL: Can't really rate this because we only did it once. We had some popcorn and a few chips but neither of us drink alcohol so it wasn't a big thing for us. If you do like a cocktail or 2, this is a very neat thing. For 2 hours you are treated to FREE drinks! I noticed several people who seemed to be enjoying this special but for us.... it just wasn't that big of a deal. POOL: 3 Yes...it's true. It's small. If you are looking for a hotel to lay by the pool... look elsewhere. It's indoors, it's small, and it's full of kids. But that didn't stop us from enjoying the hottub. After a day of walking in DC, that hot tub felt pretty good and it's usually a good place to meet some interesting people. LOCATION: 4 There is a CVS pharmacy right around the corner to pick up sodas and snacks and anything you may have forgotten. The guy at the register was stoned out of his mind the first day we were there but at least we got some drinks and snacks. We always used the Foggy Bottom Metro and it's only about 4 blocks away. The walk always felt safe. I looked at many of the other hotels that I researched and considered while I was in DC and I can honestly say that have NO regrets for chosing the Embassy Suites downtown. The manager greeted us daily by name the place was always clean and neat. If you have any questions about traveling to DC...feel free to give me a shout and hopefully I can help.

“Funky noisy hotel. Very disappointing, wouldn't stay again” I was very disappointed with the Royalton and wouldn't stay again. We arrived about 9.00pm and walked to the hotel from teh subway. As I was approaching I saw a group of people standing outside a door smoking, I assumed it was a night club based on teh noise from inside. We walked right past the hotel and back again when a person (may have worked there) asked "are you looking for the Royalton, its in here" which was teh door where the smokers were standing. Went inside and the noise was so loud it was deafening. I had to pretty much yell to the front desk girl to find out if the noise could be heard from the rooms. She explained the noise os only on Tuesday nights and we wouldn't hear it in the rooms. She also advised that she would upgrade us, which i thought was nice of her. We get to the lift an dits the smallest lift I have ever seen, two people and two suitcases and the lift was full. We got to the room and thankfully the girl was right we could not hear the noise. The decor of the roo was cold and had a concrete feel to the room. I know other reviews liked the bed well i found it very average. It was a small double for two adults. The upgrade room was average and I would have hated to seen the other room. Because we were upgraded I didn't get the soaking tub. The bathroom was very large. The next day we left about 10.00am and came back at 5.00pm to find the room had not been cleaned, which was very annoying. Housekeeping knock at the door at 5.30pm wanting to clean the room, which was not a good time as we were getting ready for dinner. We then go out for dinner only to find its nosiy again. So much for only Tuesdays. This is a funky hotel and if you like the nightclub scene then you may like the hotel. I would not stay there again nor would I recommend this hotel due to the noise, small bed and terrible housekeeping.

“Great Stay” Have stayed twice now for business trips to Austin. Fun, Eclectic hotel. Rooms & bathroom are a great size and laid out really well. Staff courteous and very helpful. Great light affordable breakfast options. Great business mingling in the mornings as everyone grabs a bite and heads out. Definatly will stay again.

“Just big enough for one.....” Stayed at the DC Club Quarters for 2 nights earlier this week. First the good. The staff was uniformly warm & friendly.The hotel was clean & secure and the elevators worked well. Now the bad..... As other reviewers have noted the rooms are small.It's tolerable for 1 but there is no way a couple or family should stay here unless they are a REALLY close family. :-) Not just the room was small but the bathroom was very tiny. No vanity room at all.Small closet & no dresser.The free bottled water was empty bottles in the hallway on a rack you filled up from a dispenser...... Overall it was okay for a night or 2 but it's just not among my favorites in the NW DC area...

“Pay for EVERYTHING at Hilton Austin!” My husband and I recently stayed four days at the downtown Hilton location for a conference. We have stayed at similarly ranked hotels with the expectation to pay for additional options, yet thoroughly enjoyed our stay; however, the service made it worth every penny. In our experience, the Hilton Austin did not meet our expectations and every additional cost was insulting because of the treatment we were given. Starting on a positive, we enjoyed the convenient location to 6th Street (one block away), the Capitol, various delicious restaurants, and a terrific barber (The Good Life left of the hotel on 5th, approximately a block - just ask the head conceirge, Steve, he went there too). However, the majority of the service was not courteous. From the front desk to the servers and bartender at the Loft Bar to housekeeping, we began to think one of the prerequisites to work there was pretentiousness. Not all the employees have an arrogance, but it was surprising to get such poor service. Another positive point is that the room was very comfortable! A coffee maker, alarm clock, and iron came with the room...anything else and you must pay. Additionally, only BASIC cable is available. In addition, a refreshment bar/mini fridge is in the room; however, if you want to take out their stuff to cool your personal drinks, you will get charged $25 (they want you to rent a mini fridge and not use the one assigned for their minibar). Other additional costs are internet service ($9.95 per day), parking ($20 per night), and workout facility ($10 per use or $15 per stay per person). If you are interested in spa treatments, they have a wide selection (again, expect the fees to be high)! Another difficulty was the elevator service. Since we were there with hundreds of other conference attendees, it took forever to get up and down the elevators (even though they had 6 available), so don't be in a rush to get to your room and back! Plan to spend a lot of money on additional charges here. However, enjoy the modern and clean facility!

“Friendly and elegant, but expensive and dated” I stayed here for business one evening in August. It is a beautiful hotel, but it felt dated and a little worn around the edges. The staff was very kind, welcoming and upgraded my room without my asking and for no additional charge. The room itself was very spacious and lovely. The hallways felt like an old Ivy League dorm hallway and the workout room seemed to be a tiny afterthought. I also had dinner in the hotel's Oak Room, which has both a dining area and a bar with a display of fresh fish. The bar was friendly and the food pretty good. A little pricey for what you get. I would stay here again, because the room was great and the service excellent, but for the price, I would look around at other options as well, as it's not a terrific value.

“Adorable” We had several rooms booked and I got to see a couple of different room types, from the standard King to a King Suite which has a separate living area. Both are very comfortable and well decorated. It looks newly renovated actually. Our room did not have a number on the door which was a little strange, but we found it through the process of elimination! It was the slowest check in I think I've ever experienced but the man was friendly..... don't try checking in for 4 rooms at once! Chestnut Hill is a really lovely area and it was a great hotel to stay at, very central to lots of quaint shops and close to the train station so you could walk. Beds were very comfortable, breakfast is served downstairs. Would recommend this hotel.

“Excellent nights sleep” We stayed here briefly two weeks ago. We needed a hotel in Boston to crash for a few hours before grabbing a plane and called amex for a recommendation. Due to the crazy weather most hotels were booked as the airport had basically shut down. We arrived here at 3am and had a great nights sleep. The room was nice, the bed was incredibly comfortable. The staff were helpful. I didn't get to use any of the hotel facilities but thought the place was nice and would certainly come back at some point.
“Helt ok” Helt ok hotell men fantastisk lokasjon. Veldig små rom og harde sengenger. God service i resepsjonen. Alt i alt bra, men ikke noe luksus.

“A little too modern for Boston, but quite nice none-the-less” A friend and her husband were stopping in Boston on their way to a New England and Canada tour. She wanted to get together and hoped I'd show her Boston which, I confess, I don't know well. The main reason that I can't figure out which way the roads go... at least not easily. So I suggested I meet her in Boston and we take a Duck Tour (to which I've given a rave review in another post). I'd already suggested she and her hubby find a hotel near Boston Common, which she'd agreed to do, but wasn't forthcoming with the name of the hotel. Thus, I was on my own as far as choices went. I opted for The Revere because the location (and price) were very very good for Boston. I arrived at the hotel via taxi, and was disoriented right away: there are concrete walls and seating areas an no visible front desk from the door I entered. I had to ask where to check in. But check in was fine, despite the lack of warm decor, and the room was great: wonderful view of the city and the bay, big space, comfy bed, all the amenities except a stocked 'fridge. No prob. I met my friends in the lobby as previously agreed, although not sure at all where the "proper" lobby was. I finally found a seat with views of the main doors (there are two I think) and happened to catch a glance of my friends as they entered on of the door (good thing I wasn't reading or I'd have missed them). There's a HUGE cement circle thing in the lobby which block the views and seems incredibly uncomfortable to sit in, so I was outside of "the cage" in a chair I hoped would work. It did. But know this: there are not plants in the lobby, and nothing to make you feel you've arrived at a cozy place. For Boston, it's out of sync: where cozy and old and history are already there as the springboard for interior decor choices. But the designer, in this case, might have been from Afghanistan, although he or she forgot his or her rugs. I WON'T dwell on the miserable lobby any longer. The room was scrumptious. The smell of vomit in the hallways (which I'd read about in other reviews) wasn't on the 23rd floor. Nor did I notice a "wonderful smell" in the lobby. They all smelled about the same. But back to the room: the bed was fabulous. Yes, the shampoo and conditioners are bolted to the wall, so you won't leave with any goodies. Still, it's a nice stay. The restaurant is across a "U" shaped driveway, and serves up very nice food for lunch and breakfast. The hotel itself is right across the street from a Legal Seafoods, which is where we had dinner, and that was perfect. So all it all, it was a good stay. If they'd convert the lobby to something more... well... Boston-like, it'd be all the better.

“Great staff and comfortable beds!” I got a great deal on a room at the Crowne Plaza through Hotwire, and the location was great for me, since I was traveling to and from Indianapolis by train. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. I didn't know until arriving that the hotel is part of a working train station; I had thought it was a separate building right next door. They provide ear plugs, an eye mask, and a relaxation CD, but I didn't need any of those. I could feel a vibration when trains passed through, but not enough to disturb me. My room was very nice. The linens were top of the line, the bed was comfortable, and the bathroom was spacious. The only thing I disliked was that mine was a corner room that faced the main hallway, right across from the gym, and my window looked out into the hallway rather than outside. This made the room feel a bit less private. Overall, the hotel and its staff were great, and I'd stay here again.

“It was just ok...had higher expectations...” I have stayed at a number of other Marriotts and this one just didn't make the cut. I stayed here for a conference (at the convention center) in May. The cruddy weather didn't help either. Here is my review... Hotel/Location: This was one of the plus with this hotel. It is centrally located in the heart of the Inner Harbor. It is connected to a Mall and short walking distance to eateries. It was about a 10 min walk to the convention center. The hotel looks old from the outside, like the rest of Baltimore. The lobby was tastefully decorated and had free Wi-fi (for 1 hr per day). Check in was a breeze Room: It was a typical Marriott room. The king bed was really comfortable. There was an ipod docking station which was nice. Nice big HD tv. I also had a fridge and nice in room safe (big enough for my computer). However, that was about it. According to my other friends that were staying in there, they didn't all have a fridge. There was no stationary. There was no book or folder that explained the hotel amnenities. Housekeeping was nice. There was a bottle of water for $4. In room coffee was typical (horrible tasting). No wine opener. Bathroom was typical and had decent water pressure. Amenities: There was a nice bar (closed kind of early) and restaurant. I was looking forward to taking a swim. However, the pool and all of the 7th floor was closed for remodel. No one informed me this at check in. I found out when I took the stairs to the abandoned 7th floor and got chased away by construction workers. The connected mall was kind of cool. Also free Wi-fi was nice. All in all, this is an average hotel that is located in a nice location. I got a convention rate so that was nice. Don't expect luxury and you should be fine.

“Above Average Downtown DC Hotel” Stayed here for four nights in January on a business trip and was satisfied with the property. The rooms were clean and up to date. The gym and Concierge Lounge at the hotel are some of the best that I have experienced in the Marriott system. The Concierge Lounge was easily twice the size of what you would expect and was open all day until 11pm. This was truly a great benefit. The gym is actually a fitness club that is located in the hotel that the guests can use (in addition to the club's outside members), so the equipment is of top quality and there are windows, etc. A huge improvement over the usual hotel basement gym. I would definitely return to this hotel if business travel brings me back to the area.

“Service with an attitude” I stayed overnight for a business trip. It was my first experience at a W hotel. The room was nice and I was pleased to find a note from the "manager" saying to call him if I needed anything. The following morning I checked out of the hotel but had one of the bell men hold my bag while I was in a business meeting. I tipped him $3 for the one bag. When I came back from my meeting to pick up the bag there was another customer in front of me that was picking up several items of luggage. Once finished, she gave the bell man (a different one this time) some change. She was a bit cheap for all the help he provided her but his reaction was appalling. As soon as she walked away, he slammed the change on the counter and started storming around cussing under his breath. I had to wait for him to calm down so that I could get my own bag at which time I gave him no tip. As I walked away, he slammed his hand down on the counter. I ended up giving his tip to the guy that called the taxi for me. To make matters worse, I decided to call the "manager" about the situation. The "manager" turned out to be a recording where you could leave messages. I left a message and got a very un-heartfelt email apology reply later on from what seemed like an email reply center. I won't be staying there again. There are way too many hotels I've stayed at in NYC with better service.

“A Wonderful Place to Stay” My son and I stayed at The Colonnade in Sept. 2006. We both enjoyed staying there very much. The rooms were spacious, cool and clean. Room service was fast and, while not cheap, was not too expensive. The hotel is in a wonderful location-across from two shopping malls, near public gardens, right on the main subway lines and the stopping point for several trolley tours. However, the main drawing point was the service by the hotel staff. It was excellent. The front desk was extremely accommodating to all our requests. They immediately changed my room when I didn't like the colour of the room. All the staff were very couteous and helpful. We were especially happy with the service we received from the concierge, Peter. He went out of his way to secure tickets to different events for us and he helped to make our stay more enjoyable.If I went to Boston again, I would definitely stay at the Colonnade and I would recommend it to anyone who is visiting in Boston.

“Best Part of Hollywood” We loved Magic Castle Hotel and their staff. We arrived a little after 9a to see about dropping off our bags, and they were super. They gave us our garage card (parking is under the hotel) and offered us to the breakfast. They were able to hold our bags and said they'd call when our room was ready. They had maps and reccomendations and spent the time with us to make sure we were comfortable. When we were able to check in at around 1p, our bags were already in our room and we were offered a glass of a sparkling citrus drink. Take advantage of their extensive snack and dvd list as well. The room was a good size and very quiet. The staff really went out of their way to make our stay amazing and it really was.

“Fun, iconic, good location” During my first visit to the Westin Bonaventure, I found the staff tremendously friendly and helpful, the architecture fascinating, and the location convenient. The Thai Massage at the spa was outstanding.

“Relatively convenient but nothing else” closest big-name chain hotel near airport, but in the middle of no where. No restaurant. No bar. Was clean and comfortable, but I"ve stayed in much nicer Courtyards with more services. Luckily, internet was free.

“Wonderful Location” What a great location directly on the Riverwalk. Lovely hotel with some beautiful decor throughout, but the rooms seemed a little tired, not as clean as one would expect from a Hilton. I found someone elses soap in the shower the first morning I was there and cleaned up some hair off the vanity. Breakfast buffet is $20 and is decent. Not much choice for a less expensive breakfast near the hotel if you are a single female and don't feel comfortable walking in a strange city when it's dark in the early morning. The margaritas at Ibiza, the hotel's restaurant, are very good. I sampled quite a few from many different places while I was there and those were the best. And fairly priced. The rooms have mini fridges for use which is a nice touch and the hotel offers free coffee and tea throughout the day in the lobby. The Original mexican Restaurant down the river was a good dinner choice for a group and the food was outstanding. The river cruise is recommended, but do so during the day so you can plan where you want to visit next.

“5 Star hotel at a great price * amazing location & service !” Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk is truely heaven. Just like a 5 star hotel but without the price! From the moment we checked in to the time we drove off we could not fault the service of all the staff. Everyone was truely amazing and went out of their way to make you feel special. Even with the hotel full everyone was happy and friendly, and wanting to help you and make sure all was ok. The rooms were big, clean, comfortable, and fitted out with the amenities you could want. A very comfortable bed, flat screen tv, and wifi. The free 24/7 coffee and softdrinks and the nightly snacks ( which really are enough for dinner) with included 3 alcoholic drinks were a bonus and with the weather wet outside a welcome way for us to have dinner without getting wet. Also the breakfast was amazing. All the food you could want at a buffet from cereals, to hot food, pastries, fruit and yoghurt. Valet Parking is also available onsite for a fee of $18. All street parking in San Antonio is chargable so to have parking onsite was a real bonus. Overall the hotel is in a perfect location, right in the heart of downtown, and it even has access to the riverwalk and a rooftop pool and spa with a great view of the town. A great place to relax and enjoy all that San Antonio has to offer. ...... at a baragin price. We definatley agree tis hotel is NO 1..... and would recommend it to anyone visiting San Antonio.
“Ah, this is more like it” What a lovely hotel. Everything about this hotel is quietly understated and absolutely wonderful. There are many wonderful hotels in NY but for me this is the one.

“Everything you could possibly you could need for your trip.” I can't say enough how great it was to stay in this hotel. The staff was more than accomodating and they were always eager to help. It started from the time of check in. The guy standing next to the check in machines wouldn't even take a tip after he had been so helpful with us. The hotel couldn't have a better location. You are so close to time square, but still far enough that you don't feel overwhelmed with the crowds. It is connected to grand central station so you can be anywhere you want in the matter of minutes.

“just wonderful -- cannot recommend highly enough” Our experience at this hotel has been great. We arrived around 11 am on a Saturday and were able to check in early. The room was large and clean. (We had two double beds, a table, a large dresser with a flat screen TV inside), a comfortable bathroom with really high ceilings. In the evening, the room was turned down with chocolates placed next to the bed, together with a personal note from housekeeping. We are Select Guest members, so we got free breakfast drinks and newspaper delivered to the room. Everyone we encountered has been nothing but pleasant, helpful, and accommodating. The hotel has fresh fruit and very tasty lemonade in the lobby in the afternoon. One of the nights, when my fiance and I were coming in, the concierge presented me with a beautiful red rose (my fiance did not order one, this is just a completely random, nice gesture -- many thanks to Omni for that!). The lobby is good size and beautifully furnished. The location is convenient. We had a great time and are sad to be leaving tomorrow morning.

“Fantastic Location - Rooms Very Quiet” Just spend 6 days here with my wife and two teenage Goddaughters from the UK, what a wonderful hotel and the location could not be better, one block and you are on Broadway, 3 blocks and you are in the middle of Times Square. Really good restaurant on site, we eat breakfast every morning there before heading out sightseeing. Wait staff in the restaurant are all very attentive especially Marco. The rooms are large for NYC standards and quiet, we had a King Size Bed in ours, and our Goddaughters were upgraded to two Queens Size Beds and moved to the room next to us, thanks to Joanna, Guest Experience Manager. We never heard any “Hall Noise” or anything from rooms on either side of us. Yes, you can hear the fire engines and police when they go down 8th Ave but it did not bother us. The air conditioning is quite and works well, this is always one of my pet peeves (air conditioning noise), I hate air conditioners that turn on and off all night, no such problem in this hotel, you do not hear the compressor turning on/off at all. With three elevators there was very little waiting time, not an issue. Showers are the low water usage type, but not really an issue, just takes an extra few minutes to rinse off. All the hotel staff was very friendly and helpful, always saying hello, always asking if they could help us in anyway or if we needed anything! It is very evident that all the staff have had “Customer Experience Training”, they want to make sure that they exceed normal customer (Guest) expectations and in my opinion they did. In fact my wife and Goddaughters liked the hotel location and staff so much that we cancelled our reservations at a different hotel for our return trip from Washington, DC in two days, and rebooked this hotel for last two nights in NYC. Short $5.00 Taxi ride from Penn Station, if two or more people this is easier/faster than the Subway @ $2.50/each person. We will definitely stay here again on our next trip to NYC.

“A Good Choice at the Right Price” This was our fourth visit to New York City and our first time at the Grand Hyatt. I was well aware of some of the shortcomings of this property from previous reviews, but we managed to obtain a very good rate, so we decided to give it a try. Upon arriving we were impressed with the lobby area and the bank of speedy elevators. Our room was a deluxe king and was sufficient size wise for NYC. With a rollaway it was comfortable enough for the three of us, not large but sufficient. Decor was nice and the room was very clean. The location of the hotel is probably the best thing going for it. Right at Grand Central Terminal for easy access to the metro system and a convenient walk to many midtown locations. Service from the front desk and housekeeping was professional. We received coupons for free coffee from the kisok located in the lobby which was great in the morning Negatives as noted in other reviews are the tiny bathrooms with no counter space, lack of a refrigerator and the noise from adjacent rooms, you can hear just about any conversation next door, ours were from two sides. I think if I were paying rack rate I wouldn't be very happy here, but with our discounted rate it was perfectly fine and I would stay again under the same circumstances.

“Nice location” I stayed here for business several times and the location is great! No need to order room service because the hotel is close to many nice restaurants and the view in the concierge look is really nice. The area around the hotel is clean and there is even a CVS located in the same building. The rooms are standard Marriott rooms but is nice and clean. I would definately stay here if I return.

“Friendly and Elegant” We were here over Christmas and really enjoyed our stay. The hotel is elegant and trendy, but not snobby; the staff are warm and welcoming. The location is fabulous, we loved staying in Soho, its fun to walk around and look at all the shops even when they are closed; the neighborhood is at a much smaller scale than Midtown, there are a ton of great restaurants nearby. We enjoyed the lobby lounge for a drink and snack; it is relaxed, muted, and food & drinks are good. The concierge was very helpful and gracious in getting us a Christmas dinner reservation (we dined at Shorty's 32, which was excellent!) The hotel is several blocks from the subway which was ok as we like to walk. Our room faced the street and it was relatively quiet at night (for NYC) but it was a holiday. We were in a Superior King, but beware that the bed is smaller than a regular King; she said it’s a "European King". The bed was comfortable, the TV worked fine. We had an issue with the heater, and they sent someone up promptly to fix it. The room was clean and comfortable, but quite small and lighting is dim, it would not be great for work if here on business. If we stayed here again, I would book a Corner King on an upper floor to get more room.

“Best value hotel I've ever stayed in !” This is one of the new model SpringHill Suites, opened just three years ago. It is superbly run and very comfortable. Airport pickup is prompt and regular (I only waited 5 minutes at the airport). Front desk is very helpful and nice. The beds are quite comfortable. Breakfast was typical SpringHill Suites, which is substantial and sufficient. Do I wish the scrambled eggs were more like I get in Paris? Yes, of course, but they're edible and nutritious. So I throw some salsa and cheese on them and they're just fine. The oatmeal is made from scratch, and delicious. And the value is great -- I paid $104 for my room. A great bargain! I can't wait to go back to San Antonio and stay at this place again.

“nice hotel, lots of hidden costs” room was very nice, however, $9.95 per day charge for internet, 18.50 for a cheese pizza, and $20 for parking. I will not be coming back to this hotel, based upon all the hidden charges

“Great location, great service!” When I checked in, I upgraded to a suite with a wonderful view. I was also given access to the lounge, which served some great snacks in the evenings. The breakfast there wasn't bad either. My room was very comfortable and had a great view. The staff here are fantastic! This is a very great location for tourists, you can walk to just about anywhere in downtown. I highly recommend staying at this Crowne Plaza for your next visit to Seattle!

“An okay room” The price and lack of amenities make this room hard for me to recommend highly. It is a nice room. It is clean and has a decent amount of room to move about. The sofabed is okay but not that great. The hotel gives out free cookies after lunch. It has wifi but not in the room. If you want it in the room it is 12.00 a day. They don't have a complimentary breakfast but Mcdonalds is two stores down. Around the corner is a little shop that does wonderful breakfast sandwiches fresh. It isn't crowded or expensive. (when coming out of the hotel make a right around the corner and go about 500 yards.) My family loved the breakfasts from there. The hotel's location is excellent and right in the middle of Times Square.

“Super Lage tolles Hotel” In der letzten Woche vor Weihnachten war ich mit meiner Freundin im Sofitel. Komfort, Sauberkeit, Ausstattung und Zimmergröße waren ausgezeichnet. Wir hatten ein Zimmer mit zwei Einzelbetten, jedes Bett war ca. 120 cm breit und ausgesprochen bequem. (Ich habe selten so gut in einem Hotel geschlafen) Im 17. Stock zur Strasse hin zwar wenig Aussicht, aber total ruhig. Tolles Badezimmer mit separater Dusche und Badewanne. Personal ausgesprochen freundlich. Internet im Zimmer, jedoch sehr teuer, in der Lobby nur 3 PCs hier kostenfreies Internet, allerdings mit meistens sehr langen Wartezeiten. Preis-Leistungsverhältnis für das Zimmer für New York völlig ok. Ich würde es immer wieder buchen. Die Getränke in der Minibar im Zimmer sind allerdings sehr teuer, so auch das Frühstück. In der Nähe gibts aber ausreichend Frühstücksmöglichkeiten. Wir waren häufig am Bryant Park im Le Pain Quotidien, hier bekommen Sie ein ausgezeichnetes Frühstück mit sehr gutem Cappuccino.

“New York Charm” We stayed at The Barclay for one night. The room was gorgeous, the hotel is very nice in general. Our bathroom was too small, though, more appropriate for a 2-3 star hotel, and worst of all, gunk was up into the sink, making it utterly disgusting. When I complained to the management about it, they apologized and offered us free buffet breakfast. The location of the hotel is spectacular.

“Fantastic location” You can't beat the location for easy access to subways, tourist attractions, and food -- restaurant dining or food carts. With a hotel full of tourists, the staff at the check-in desk seemed a little stressed, but understandably so. Our room was a little cramped, but the view was fantastic. The windows even opened slightly so we could hear the noise from Times Square. (I should say that this was a free night's stay, from redeeming Hilton Honors points.) We got there too early for check-in but were able to store our baggage (for free). The concierge was extremely helpful mapping out a subway route to Chinatown for us, and we used the mini fridge in the room to store the leftovers for breakfast the next day, using the microwave to heat them up. The ice machine on the floor worked, and the elevators were speedy. A good stay, overall.

“Taxes and $19 a day for parking make this more expensive than you expect” No towels at the small pool, no refrigerator and $19 a day for parking detracted from my experience at this hotel. The beds were very comfortable and the views were nice. Service was good in the restaurant and so was the food.

“Great Hotel in an Excellent Location” I have now stayed here several times on business and find this hotel to be a great hotel to stay at for many good reasons. The hotel restaurants are great especially Sally's for outdoor dinning. The roof top bar also offers spectacular views of San Diego and the bay.The pool and hot tub are located on the 4th floor overlooking the bay area and the Coronado bridge. The hotel is closest hotel to Seaport Village for shopping and more restaurants. The hotel is also within easy walking distance to some of the best downtown restaurants on or near Gaslamp on 5th street. Refer to my San Diego restaurant reviews for some great restaurant reviews. This is a classic hotel. As an alternate I would recommend the Hilton half mile south also on the bay. I will be back!

“Nice location near food entertainment. But could be better” This hotel is a nice standard issue Hilton. Avg/Nice rooms, low water pressure FYI. Check in was pretty quick, and around the counter next to the check in desk is a little store with wide section of drinks and snacks. But this hotel does It have a pool or much of anything going on in the hotel in terms if bar but it's next to Ruth Chris and Capitol Grille. One complaint is that I needed a ride just a few blocks to a resturant and the hotel does not offer any kind of car service.

“Geek Tested and Approved” Four friends and I stayed here for Comic Con, and it was fantastic. The room was beautiful with a kitchen complete with a fridge, freezer AND ice maker (anyone who reads my reviews knows how I am about ice availability at hotels). The location was perfect with restaurants, shops, and the mall in close proximity. And the best part was being on 5th avenue for Comic Con. The convention center is just down the street, and easy walk to and from each day. We were even able to drop off our swag in the afternoon and go back for more! The staff was accommodating, helping us with our massive and awkwardly shaped luggage when we arrived, and storing and then helping us load our geek loot when we left. They were pleasant and made us laugh when they asked us if this was just for us. "Do you have a store?" "No, just for us." Clearly, we had accumulated way too many poster tubes, swag bags, and action figures for just five geek-ettes, but we had a laugh with the valet as he helped us load the TARDIS-like car, all incredulous that it would all make it back to Cucamonga. Again, excellent, fun, terrific staff. The room had a king bed plus a queen-sized convertible couch. We were very comfortable as a few of us didn't even sleep there much and chose to sleep at the Con in line for one of the massive panels in Hall H. I am too old for that, so I can say that the room was very quiet and the beds, even the convertible, were perfect. The bathroom was large, and the shower functional. We had no issues with anything during our stay. If you plan on staying the Gaslamp district for a few days, this is a terrific place to patronize. Horton Plaza is just around the corner for any mall-type needs, and the Ralphs grocery store is down the street. One of the best elements of this hotel was we didn't have to book it through Comic Con. We were able to get it almost a year in advance in anticipation of the Con while all other hotels in the district black-out that weekend and reserve their rooms to be booked through a lottery system via Comic Con. This system is terrible, so the fact that we could get such an amazing place to stay and not have to take the chance of drawing a room in Mission Valley and have to take the shuttle there and back each day, was just another example of what a great place the Wyndham Harbour Lights was. The geeks were thrilled.

“Can't Beat the Price!” You just can't beat the price of Hyatt Place! For what you get it's a steal! I try and stay at a Hyatt Place whenever possible. Always clean and great service, my only complaint is the price of snacks/food from the Gallery which are way over priced.

“Decent hotel outside of city center” This hotel is easy to reach from the freeway and has free parking. It is located at about a 5-10 minutes walk from a subway station. From this subway station you can get to locations in the city center in about 10 minutes. There is a free shuttle bus from the hotel to the subway. The room were basic and clean. The breakfast was not good. When we arrived most of it was already gone, even though we arrived half an hour before breakast was closed. But overall this is a decent hotel, nothing fancy.

“Good location, great staff” The location allows for many travel options. You can walk 15 minutes and catch a Caltrain to San Francisco for $19.00 usd per person per day and it takes a bit over an hour to get there. Santa Cruz and Capitola are about 45 minutes south via car. The hotel has a ton of dining options around it. Arcadia (inside the hotel) has an excellent breakfast. Good drinks at Tancq which is also inside. Lobby is modern and my room (1700) was clean and up to date. My only complaint was the slow elevators. I know this is a convention hotel so there can be a large amount of people moving at the same time but it seems like they could use more elevators (not likely) or a better control system for the managing of the flow of the elevators. Off site parking is $7 usd per day 1 block south versus $26usd per day at the hotel. Would stay here again for sure! Good for business travelers and families on vacation.

“Great Hotel!” I recently stayed at The Fairmont Battery Wharf in Boston & had a great time- the hotel is located near the North End, about a 15 minute walk from the Harbor; a little out of the way if you want to be near Newbury Street shopping, the Boston Commons, etc. The hotel is not the conventional hotel setting, with a main building for everything; instead the hotel is made up of several small buildings which house the rooms. I was in room 4133, which had a comfy bed, an obstructed water view, a great bathroom with a lovely rain shower, nice soaking tub & added amenities such as mouthwash. The room also had a well-stocked mini-bar with a Nespresso Machine. The walls are a bit thin, as I could hear music from the next room, but it wasn't overwhelming. The decor is clean & modern & the room was very comfortable! Chad in Royal Service was outstanding- he was so friendly, kind & when I told him my concern about getting a taxi around 5am, he said he would tell the overnight doorman to have one waiting for me- he indeed did & the taxi was waiting for me! Thanks Chad- you are amazing! Ricky was also very nice in Royal Service & had my In Room Dining order sent right away. These guys seemed very capable of handling anything! I had In Room Dining twice & everything was delicious, especially the Broccoli & Cheese Soup, Boston Cream Pie & the Lobster Roll! I really liked the hotel & thoroughly enjoyed my stay! Best, Patrick Winkler

“Noise is a big problem” Got a $143/night AAA promo rate, which made me want to try the Grand Hyatt. In this case, got what we paid for. Upon check in, we were presented with a piece of paper that claimed there would be noise due to stormy weather. The noise was non stop- it was a creaking that went on all day and all night. After one night of bad sleep, called the front desk and were told that the noise was due to the earthquake retrofitting. The higher floors were particularly problematic. Upon moving to a lower floor, there was an improvement. The room itself was adequately furnished, the bed was comfortable, with soft sheets and lots of pillows. The towels, however, were of a very poor quality, scratchy and thin. The first room did not have a garbage can. The T.V. was ancient with very few channels. No robes, no slippers, minimal toiletries. Valet parking at $55.night was a complete rip-off, On the plus side, the staff was extremely responsive to any problems - lamp wasn't working in second room and maintenance was there in less than five minutes to fix it.

“What a great hotel!” Let's see... Great location Friendly and helpful staff Nice-sized room with comfortable bed and linens with a flat screen TV Clean bathroom with huge tub Reasonable rates Restaurant for breakfast and lunch with the best club sandwich ever What more can you say???

“Unbelievable room in an unbelievable location!” My wife and I were booked into a room at this hotel by our cousin, for one night the Saturday before Christmas. What a room! It was a suite with an incredible view out the window, looking down onto TImes Square. The staff was friendly, efficient and top-notch, which was especially appreciated because we arrived late in the day and the lobby was under construction (in the midst of a huge renovation), conditions that usually lead to a long wait in line and abrupt service. In this case, however, everything was perfect.

“We keep coming back - we've never been disappointed” We've been staying at the Millennium Knickerbocker every time we visit Chicago, over a period of five years. We have never been disappointed. The location is great, the multicultural staff is always friendly, and we have never had a bad room, although we always choose the least expensive option. On our most recent trip we stayed in Room 1218, which has a lovely (if limited) view of Lake Michigan. The rooms are not large, but that doesn't bother us, as we spend most of our time exploring Chicago. Our only complaint on this stay: the wireless access did not work, although I have to admit I never got around to taking this up with the management. Anyway, I would happily recommend this hotel to a friend.

“The Lofts are excellent” For perspective, I spend around 100 nights per year in hotels and Hilton gets just over half that business. The Gaslamp is directly across from the San Diego convention center. It's a two minute walk so if you're in town for a convention the location is ideal. It's also on the right side of harbor drive, in the Gaslamp district, and within just a few blocks of many Zagat rated restaurants as well as nightlife hotspots. I stayed at the Lofts which is next door to the main Hilton. The Lofts are a little weird in terms of getting in/out. From the main lobby you must go up one floor then outdoors across a courtyard then into a second elevator then inside again and down the hall to your room. The Lofts rooms/suites, however, are excellent. Some have a nice outdoor terrace overlooking the courtyard and convention center. The Lofts has the feel of an upscale boutique hotel and it's a quiet respite from a long day conventioneering. My only complaints here are the lack of a gift shop or other place one could purchase water, soda/beer, and sundries. The room rates are also rather high, but in line with other high end hotels in the area.

“great” great location, in a quiet neighborhood but only a short walk to Times Sq, staff very courteous and helpful, were able to meet all our needs all what you would expect from a Kimpton, would stay there again next time in NYC

“Nice hotel, JW Marriott Quality” Stayed at the JW on business for the month of January. Got a nice room on one of the top floors with a nice view. The rooms are big- king size bed with a couch. They provide free internet for platinum members so that was a plus. I don't spend much time in the hotels since I am there for business but I was impressed with this hotel. Overall, had friendly staff, good amenities (restaurant, bar, Starbucks, workout facility, Concierge floor) and a good location. Pros - Friendly staff - Good restaurant - Concierge floor (hot breakfast every morning, snacks in the evening, desserts at night) - Workout facility - Starbucks

“We enjoyed our stay” Driving to the hotel from Interstate 5, there are a couple of confusing turns but the directions we printed from the hotel's website got us there without a problem. Parking is free & we didn't have a problem getting a space. Because we booked late for a special event weekend, we had a king suite, which was bigger than we needed - also more expensive. However, it was nice having the extra room. The sitting area had a large, flat panel TV mounted on the wall but, as far as we could tell, there weren't any HD channels. There was also a TV in the bedroom. The kitchenette area had a microwave, refrigerator, bar sink & 4 sets of dishes & silverware. The vanity/sink was outside the bathroom. The hotel recently opened a new fitness center which was a lot larger than their old one. The continental breakfast was ok but was very crowded. There are lots of restaurant choices at the upscale University Village mall just 2 blocks from the hotel. We thought the food at Atlas Foods was excellen; there was a lot of fresh seafood but other types of food as well. The front desk clerk recommended Speciality's Cafe for lunch; the food was good & the cafe seemed to be very popular.

“The Decline of a Stylish Hotel” What a difference between our stay at The Time in New York two years ago and our stay last week. In 2003, this was a stylish concept hotel. There was a high-energy vibe going with the sleek interiors, the time-oriented decor, and the fun color-centered rooms. The funky and highly functional rooms made one overlook how small they are. We had a great time there. Now The Time is grubby and worn. The fun decor remains, but looks neglected. Our room reeked of mustiness and mildew and we found part of our carpet was soaked from an air conditioner leak. The hotel was sold out so we couldn't change rooms until the next day. Our next room was dry, but the phone didn't work and the shower had barely enough pressure to run. We felt the less time spent in the room, the better. On the good side, the location is great, the staff is helpful, and the rooms offer very useful amenities.

“Highly Recommended!” My wife and I stayed at the Hampton Inn April 7-9. I had prepared myself for a mediocre hotel but we were both delighted with our experience! It is not big, and the rooms, while small, are completly comfortable for two adults. Very clean and quiet. I would stay here again.

“Great Stay” I stayed at the Plamer house with my wife for one night on Feb 17th. After our stay I was a little surprised at some of the negative reviews. The lobby and common areas are beautiful. Yes, the rooms are a little small, but this hotel is in a great location in the middle of the city, so this is to be expected for a reasonably priced hotel. Drinks in the hotel bar are very expensive ($22 for two drinks), but this is not uncommon either, and the lobby/bar area is very comfortable and we enjoyed spending time there. We enjoyed our stay, and wil likely stay again.

“Enjoyed my stay at the Four Seasons” Came here on a business trip with a group. Had not been to Austin iin 30 years or so. This is a nice hotel. They try hard and there are little details like robes and slippers (which I did not nor would I ever use so not sure who does). They offer free coffee in the morning, and the staff seems motivated to help. Beds are a little soft for my tastes but at least they give you plenty of pillows, which I appreciate. They have real wood hangers in the closets and you don't have to wrestle with the "theft proof" type. Nice toiletries in the bathroom,and a really good shower which is always welcome. I liked it. I had a nice view and it's near walking and running paths. I would certainly recommend it.

“Great Location!” I have stayed here twice. The location can't be beat if you like to be in the middle of it all...only one block from Times Square. Rooms are clean, but average. Bathrooms are updated including bathtubs. Very close to multiple food places and lots of shopping. Also very close to many subway stations which makes it very easy to get to/from other parts of the city quickly.

“Nice Vintage Hotel with Modern Amenities” Villa Florence was a nice vintage hotel with modern touches. I was recommended this hotel by a friend of mine who lives in San Fran. Stayed here for a few nights while visiting friends and going to a quick meeting. The hotel was a bit of a cab ride from the airport but centrally located to transportation and downtown. Lobby was nice, had a coffee shop in it that was decent, and their Italian restaurant which was excellent. I checked in and went up the vintage elevator to my room. Staff was always professional and helpful. There was a sitting area in my room with another tellie, I must confess didn't use this room at all. Some storage under the tellie in the bedroom for clothing and a small desk slash minibar by the bed. The bed was big comfy and clean. The bathroom was completely updated and clean. I really liked the photographs around my room and the hotel. For a vintage hotel the carpet was clean and it didn't feel dingy like a lot of vintage style hotels do.

“Gute Lage - Gutes, sauberes Holiday Inn” Hotel in Soho, China Town, in unmittelbarer Nähe zur U-Bahn (Canal Street - auch von JFK zu erreichen) Hotel in einer Seitengasse der Canal Street (Lafayette St.), deshalb auch nicht allzu laut. Zeitweise hört man die U Bahn Fahrenheit (auch im 11. Stock). Zimmer sind relativ klein, aber sauber und offensichtlich renoviert. Restaurant mitt Frühstücksbuffet um 18,95 USD vorhanden. In der Nähe Starbucks und andere Lokale vorhanden. Kleines, aber feines Fitnessstudio vorhanden. Nette Mitarbeiter.

“Great Hotel, Great Room, Great Location” Just got back from a stay at the Beacon. I'll keep it simple. The rooms were well above average (size, quality, decor, comfort), the price was well below average (meaning great prices), and the location was great. We found the hotel to be a great central location to monuments/white house/etc and a good location for restaurants and nightlife. Everything we wanted to do was a close walk or a short cab ride. Would definately stay here again and would definately recommend this hotel to others. The rooms with the kitchenettes were very well appointed and seemed quite roomy.

“Affordable and well located BUT old and stuffy.” Stayed here because we managed to score a really great rate for the room. The price and the hotel's central location was the best part of my stay. Hotel and the rooms were clean and comfortable, decorated in a somewhat stuffy manner that I don't particularly care for but has nothing really wrong with it. Feng Shui is not for everyone after all. Beware of the elevators in you're in rush - they are slowwwwwww. Room were tiny even by New York standards. Moreover, the TV was the size of a computer screen and my window looked directly out to a wall. Seriously, I opened the blinds and got a brick wall instead. Good part of a wall though is that the room was quiet. Finally, I had brunch at the restaurant which was small but good (and as you won't be surprised to read, was in a room with no windows). Only downer there was that whatever money I saved on the room, I wasted on paying for my meal but, hey, it's New York after all...

“più che sufficiente” Notte di passaggio a Phoenix nel 2009. Il prezzo davvero stracciato per una camera enorme con salotto annesso e zona trucco e.... aria condizionata indispensabile! Concordo con chi consiglia di non fermarsi a Phoenix perchè e' una giornata buttata via e non ne vale la pena, soprattutto in estate quando ad agosto si sfiorano i 50° e non si riesce a stare fuori!

“Everything you expect from a Kimpton” Had a great time staying for almost a week at Donovan House. The service was impeccable, the room was spacious, bright and modern, with everything you need. I loved the seashell shape shower, even if it was too week (darn low flow showers and water efficiency!). Food is great also. Would only say it needs a little bit of repair here and there to make it a true 5* boutique. Also, we booked it mainly for the rooftop pool but the hotel is not making best use of it at all - no food or drinks are served up there most of the day and there are no parasols, which in searing DC heat makes it difficult to hang out there. The bar by the pool at night is fun though. Would probably stay again anyway though, though I do love the Palomar too.

“The Only Good Thing This Stay Was the Happy Hour” We have stayed at this hotel many times before since our children were little. This was our last time at this location. If we stick with Hilton Properties next time we will stay at the Embassy in Center City - It was much better. We were unfortunate enough to have my teenage son wake up with bites and sure enough we found bed bugs. Management handled it well, but housekeeping should have noticed them. My son also left his ipod in the room plugged in being charged. We got 20 mins down the road and he realized he had left it. I called the hotel and they could find no trace of it. In other words they have thieves that work in this hotel and I think management should have done more about finding out what happened to it instead of taking a sorry we can't find it attitude. Our first and second room had a moldy smelling room that was not cleaned to our expectations, the pool was filthy and breakfast was not as good this stay. the only positive point was happy hour. They did let us check out early and we moved to Homewood Suites and had a much better experience.

“Decent Hotel Near the Airport and Subway” This property is nice. The rooms are modern and designed like a mini suite with a separate living room and bedroom. The room has a TV – flat screen in living room and old fashion one in the bedroom. The bathrooms are nice with a modern glass shower, but no tub. Room includes a very nice modern desk and ergonomic chair. The restaurant and bar offer good food, which is nice if you’re stuck at this property which is about an hour from downtown Chicago on the subway. Driving at rush hour can take two hours to go fifteen miles to the downtown loop. I’d normally stay at the Renaissance downtown, but decided to stay at this one because I had a meeting in the area. The property has a decent fitness center with modern equipment. If you’re a competitive or recreational swimmer you’d hate the 20 yard lap pool because the water temperature is about 87 degrees. No one can swim laps in 87 degree water temperature. A better name would be a wading pool, which is great for kids. The hotel posted a note in the room that they were doing some minor exterior work on the building during the week day 9 - 5, which I didn't notice because I wasn't at the hotel during that time.

“Great experience: where to stay in Dallas” First, let me say that this is a Ritz: I expect everything to be outstanding (especially given the rack rates) , and this hotel did not disappoint me. The incredibly late check-in (2:30 AM) that went as smoothly as had I been there in the late afternoon, the room was exquisite, the service was outstanding (picking up my shoes to be shined at 3 AM and having them back before 9 was great), and I couldn't recommend a hotel any more than this one. All of that said, I have two very minor complaints: the iron was missing the "cap" that held the water in, so you had to be careful while ironing not to get your shirts wet; and the shower gel in the bathroom doesn't lather well with just a washcloth (they should either give you a real bath sponge or go back to traditional bar soap). The location is very convenient for anything in Downtown or Uptown.

“Lovely hotel gets all the details right” I stayed overnight at the Fairmount for a business meeting and wished I could have moved in! The hotel is beautifully furnished, elegant without being fussy, and well equipped for both business and pleasure visits. Besides the luxe touches that have become almost standard, like comfy beds and robes and abundant desk outlets, the Fairmount includes details that other hotels would do well to add, such as snake-neck reading lamps attached to the bed that cast a cool spotlight right on your page; in-room Keurig coffee makers; and window panels that actually open for some fresh air. Even the coffee service at our meeting included classy touches like flavored syrups, and there were gigantic hot soft pretzels and mustard instead of the usual gluey cookies. One thing I can't comment on is price, because my room was prepaid, but I'll definitely check this place out on my next tourist trip to DC.

“Average if you are on a budget” I met two girlfriends in San Francisco for a four-day stay and was not in charge of reservations this trip. A friend who has not been to SF previously booked the room and I can pretty much roll with most anything so wasn't too worried after reading a few reviews. The property is an older motor lodge on Lombard which carries a heavy amount of traffic most any time of day or night. With a room facing the road you will either need a cocktail before bed or sleep with the tv on. Also, the elevator apparently has been out of service for months so be prepared to carry your bags up a few flights of stairs. Again, realizing the discount not huge issues, just wouldn't be my choice for either. The rooms appear to have been remodeled at some point in the past and the bathroom updated. Carpets were stained but beds were "ok" for comfort and linens. Very limited lighting and electrical plugs so if you have more than a person or two be prepared when it comes to drying your hair, makeup, getting ready in general. Staff was friendly and they do offer coffee, english muffins and bananas/oranges in the AM. Enough to give you a boost to start the day. I would recommend for younger travelers on a budget. Would make a different choice in the future but overall an average accomodation.

“Great hotel for a one night stay” We chose this hotel based on it's proximity to LAX - literally minutes (as well as Randy's Donuts!!). Our room was spacious and clean, we were booked for one night only. The bed was the most comfortable bed that I ever slept on - no joke. The dining options were also very nice. Landings (for a late night drink and snack) was very nice, and the Bistro serves a good cup of coffee. My only complaint was that as guests, we did get "lost in the shuffle" a bit and the staff was a bit short - we had a few questions as to parking and payment, and every time we approached someone behind the desk with a question, the person looked at us like we were crazy. Other than that, the stay was fine and would stay there again.

“Fabulous Location & Comfortable Accommodations” The Doubletree Austin - University Area offers a fabulous location and comfortable accommodations. The property is well maintained and appears to be relatively new. The room provided plenty of room for lounging and the bedding/lines were clean, crisp, and definitely comfortable. Quite frankly the Hilton family of hotels have a superb bedding system that is definitely sleep inducing. The public sitting areas at this property were inviting and well appointed. This property’s swimming pool is uniquely placed on the second floor and the surrounding grounds offer the right balance of sun and shade for outdoor recreation. The Doubletree Austin – University is well situated close to the University of Texas, the Texas State Capital, and the dining and entertainment venues in the downtown Austin area (e.g., Guadalupe, 6th Street, and South Congress). A short drive down South I35 will take you toward Lake Travis area and the opposite direction up North I35 will carry you to the Prime Outlet Shopping Center in near-by Round Rock, TX. A bid on Priceline secured a room on a Friday night for $55. Now that’s truly a bargain!

“Très bien pour un motel” C'est un motel,donc il ne faut pas s'attendre aux prestations d'un hôtel,mais c'est un motel de bonne qualité! Très bien situé,les chambres sont propres et ont une kitchinette. On peut se garer gratuitement devant sa chambre. Piscine,accès wifi,petit déjeuner free dans un espace minuscule et avec le minimum syndical mais correct! Bon rapport qualité prix pour Los Angeles si on veut essayer un motel.

“Has basic amenities but there are nicer Motel 6 buildings” We have almost only stayed in budget motels (often Motel 6 chains) in our trip across the USA and the Motel 6 in El Paso is one of the lowest ranking for us. That said, the rooms were clean, the water was hot, everything worked and the view of the valley in the morning was amazing. The motel is well located near restaurants and shops but it is in need of a spruce-up. The rooms were smaller than most Motel 6 rooms we have stayed in. The blankets were worn and the room in need of a re-paint and light fittings not attached to the wall with a chain might have made it more welcoming. At the time we stayed there was a small flood near the office which did not inconvenience us but added to the run-down atmosphere. We felt safe there and the staff were friendly. I would normally recommend Motel 6 to anyone looking for budget accommodation in the USA but this one needs some investment.

“Very small rooms” I booked this room last minute for a special weekend rate of $179. During the week this same hotel room goes for over $400 a night. This hotel is nice and has all of the original woodwork, which was very nice. But the rooms were one of the smallest I have ever had in NYC. The bathroom was quite large compared to the room. The bed was very comfortable and the room was very quiet for sleeping. Laying on the side of the bed you could reach out and touch the wall with your foot. But since we are not large people, we could deal with the lack of space. For the $179 price I was happy, but I would never pay over $200 for this room.

“Great location, good breakfast.” The rooms are large, they are "suites" after all. The hotel is an older property. The staff is very attentive. No problems there. They have a pool, but sun time is limited due to the fact you are downtown and the buildings are tall. Breakfast was good for a free deal. It has hot waffels and eggs. Very centrally located, Mud island, paddle wheel tours and Beal st are all within walking distance. The trolly runs right by the back door, $1 for a trip.

“Kids loved it...” Join HHonors before you visit...they'll treat you like family! It's nice to be greated by name when you call the desk. The room was clean. Not Hilton-clean...but clean. The suite was quite large. We loved the HiDef widescreen TV in the living room, and the kids loved the video games ($6.95 per hour). The view wasn't much, but no big deal...we were there to sightsee not stare out our hotel window. The free shuttle was fine, just make sure you plan your activites the day before because you need to reserve the shuttle for your destination. Staff very helpful, especially concierge. The warm cookies were yummy, and the kids both received a neat backpack full of activites at check-in. Room service was good, as was both on-site restaurants we sampled. A bit pricey for this middle-income family of four, but nothing unexpected. Sadly, there was no dining choices within walking distance of this hotel that we found. The river borders one side, a large industrial site the other. Walking anywhere was a bit intimidating.
