Parking was convienent other than not being able to access the 2nd floor of the garage directly from the elevators. You have to return to the lobby and either walk up the stairs or board a second elevator. No big deal, I guess. Very close (1 mile) to Cambridge, wish we could have spent more time there. Bottom line: the kids didn't want to leave but the hotel meal $$ was killin' me!

“Perfect location, incredible views, good value” I stayed at this hotel over Labor Day weekend and was very pleased with it. As a devoted Starwood Preferred Guest, I'm pretty picky about my hotels. And this one definitely hit the mark. First off, it's just around the corner from the subway station that serves the A, C and E lines. That means if you flew into JFK, it drops you off almost at the front door for a whopping $7.25 with both the Air Train and Subway fares. Other subway lines are within a few blocks, so you can literally get anywhere in Manhattan very easily and for $2.25 a ride. Add to that, you're right across the street from SoHo, which has shopping and restaurants a-plenty - all very walkable. This is a busy hotel with a fairly small lobby area that made it feel even busier. But that was never an issue for me. I was still able to get an elevator rather easily. The lobby is modern and clean with lots of amenities - a grab-and-go food/drink counter, a small bar with seating area, a restaurant, and an area with several computers . I was lucky to get into a room on an upper floor, so the view was great. Furnishings are comfortable, including the bed. The bathroom isn't huge, but it's well-equipped with a nice stand-up shower and well-lit mirror. The one thing I thought was odd was there were no drawers for unpacking my suitcase. The closet had hangers, but nowhere to really put things that don't hang. Not a huge inconvenience. Staff was very friendly, efficient and helpful. The rooftop deck (which I believe is only accessible to Club floors - Splurge! It's worth it!) has INCREDIBLE 180 degree views of the city, as well as breakfast and evening snacks. This is highly unique for a New York hotel. Yes, so this hotel is directly on Canal Street, which is totally nasty and crowded. But as you walk out the front door, just head left and go around the corner to the parallel street behind Canal. It's quiet, safe, and no one is going to try to sell you a fake Rolex. That's what I did to get to the N, Q, R subway stop. And once you get off of Canal in any direction, your'e right back to charming, movie set-like, downtown New York. Comparing to what NYC hotels are charging these days for a nice, modern, new-ish room, I thought this hotel was a bargain - and I compare all Starwood properties before I make my decision (always check AAA rates and "hotel offers" on the SPG site before you book). This one has often had the lowest price. Request or book an upper floor, or at least one that faces uptown. You won't be disappointed!

“Great Location” Great location and our room was surprisingly quiet even though it was in the center of Midtown. Just a few blocks from Times Square on one side and St Patricks Cathedral on 5th on the other side. Room was smaller than others I've stayed at in NYC but had flat screen TV and coffee maker. The shower in the bathroom was not separated from the rest of the floor so the whole floor was soaked after a shower, which I did not like. Lots of business people in the hotel - not much of a tourist hotel - no concierge to help us plan our time in NYC. Would recommend for location and value ($179 per night when booked and paid for in full in advance).

“Decent for a day or so...” The lobby and bar areas were very nice. I was able to complete a lot of work at the raised tables while my lab was shutdown for the day, coffe/bar area was always manned. The rooms were regular size for a Courtyard but a little cleaning and maintenance might be in order. Housekeeping was nice and efficient. Parking was a bit of a pain with the whole ticket to get in and out of the parking lot. After 3pm or so...Internet (WiFi) was not the best, especially for rooms on the side facing the hill. It was usually dial-up speed and few of the rooms have wired internet. I also had very limited coverage with my cell phones (1 Verizon, 1 Sprint) in a hillside/limited view room. The WiFi and cell coverage was so bad that I actually changed to a room facing the highway. Cell was better but WiFi was still sluggish. I plugged into the wired internet and that was dismal too. Some of the channels on the TV don't display correctly either. Overall, not too bad if you're there for a day or so but I can't stay there again for more than 2 to 3 days again.

“Good Hotel; Decent Price; Far from Many Attractions” It is a newly-redone hotel and was perfectly acceptable. It had a good exercise room and even a small lap pool. The room was very small, even by Manhattan standards, but it was decently appointed, the bed was very comfortable, and the ample windows made it feel bigger. If I strained, I could see a piece of the East River from our room. The staff was very pleasant and helpful, particularly the bell staff. The issue for us was the location - in the lower 90’s on the Upper East Side near First Avenue, in the quiet, predominantly residential area known as Yorkville. If you are driving, you will find the hotel close to FDR Drive, but it is far from any of the usual tourist attractions – Times Square, the Theater District, Greenwich Village, South Street Seaport, etc. A round-trip cab ride to Little Italy for dinner was about $38 with tip. Even the nearest subway station is on the 4, 5, and 6 lines that run up Lexington Avenue, about 10 blocks from the hotel. There are some acceptable restaurants in the area (we liked Café D’Alsace on Second Avenue), but don’t count on anything in the way of shopping or night life. The Metropolitan Museum of Art is probably the closest attraction, and that is about 18 blocks.

“Fine 10 Day Stay” Stayed there for nine nights in August’08. Location of the hotel is good, close to Navy Pier and Magnificent Mile but yet relatively quiet. I (single traveler) had a corner room in 13th floor. No noise from the atrium to this particular room, probably because it is located somewhat further away from atrium than “regular rooms”. Room has certainly large enough for my purposes, big living room and a separate sleeping room. Room was spotless and didn’t have any scratches or other marks from previous usage, so no complains about it. Also other parts of the hotel were in very good shape. Kitchenette consisted of small fridge and a microwave oven. Room had quite nice views towards Chicago river, lake was also well visible as was Sears Tower. LAN access provided with ~10$/day, didn’t notice any WLAN. One very very minor issue though: one of two TVs in the room was not LCD (they advertise two LCDs in a room) but a old-style “tube” TV. Hotel offered free breakfast and a manager’s reception in the evening. Latter offered very little to eat (just some snacks), but plenty to drink (free beer, wine and booze) for two hours. Breakfast was, um, not that well suited for European taste but otherwise offered quite many different options. I never had to wait for an elevator more than 30 seconds or so, thus no problems for me regarding that issue (unlike some other reviewers). Then again, I left the hotel always latest at 8:15am, so avoided the real morning rush hour. Typical customers seemed to be families and there were really lots of them, but didn’t really hear any special noise (no kids running around corridors etc). Obviously there isn’t an Executive Lounge in this hotel, but did receive two water bottles as a Hilton Honors Diamond member. Better than nothing :-) So while this hotel isn’t quite Five Star ûber Luxury hotel, it did its job very well. I cannot really think of anything to complain about. One thing I noticed though (didn’t affect me) was that there was often quite long queues at the check-in desk. Would I return there? Yes, absolutely.

“What A Fantastic Place!” I stayed two nights at the Sheraton Gunter in January. Cab ride from SAT airport will cost you around $25. Although it rained the two days that I was there, I was still able to experience old San Antonio. It is an easy walk (about 4 blocks) to the shopping mall, river walk, and the Alamo. The hotel is so charming...very chic..perfect blend of the old and new. The room service was fabulous I ordered the lamb chops...and it was amazing. I did dine at the restaurant for breakfast and was not pleased with the food nor service. Besides, there are so many fun restaurants around that you should try leaving the hotel for. I'd go back again...I wish I could bring their bed back with me...so comfyt!

“Leider fehlt der Charme” Das Hotel ist schon ein älteres Gebäude, dem leider etwas der Charme fehlt. Wer lediglich ein sauberes, zweckmäßiges Zimmer in guter Lage sucht, in dem er nur übernachten möchte, ist hier gut aufgehoben, sofern er guten Deal gemacht hat (mehr als 100 USD/Nacht würde ich hierfür nicht zahlen). Wer jedoch ein klein wenig Komfort mag, sollte vielleicht eher ein anderes Hotel nehmen. Der Check-in verlief problemlos und die Dame am Empfang war auch sehr nett. Wir hatten ein sehr großes Zimmer im 6. Stock. Das Zimmer verfügte über eine separate Kochnische, einem kleinen Tisch mit zwei Stühlen zum Essen, Fernseher und Sideboard. Das Mobilar ist wie das Hotel schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen, jedoch funktionstüchtig. Von einem der Fenster konnten wir sogar das halbe ESB sehen. Die Küche ist zweckmäßig mit Toaster, Kühlschrank, Gasherd, Kaffeemaschine und Mikrowelle ausgestatte. Das Bad hat eine Badewanne/Dusche, ausreichend Handtücher, Fön (überraschend leistungsstark), Spiegelschrank und eine kleine Ablagefläche rund ums Waschbecken. Seife, Shampoo etc. wird jeden Tag nachgefüllt. Das Hotel hatte wohl mal ein Restaurant neben der Lobby, das scheint aber schon seit längerem geschlossen zu sein. Internet ist kostenpflichtig. Was ich gut fand: + die Lage: Grand Central ist in ein paar Minuten zu Fuß erreichbar. Rund ums Hotel gibt es verschiedene Diner und Restaurants sowie einige Supermärkte. Ansonsten recht ruhig. + die Küche: sehr praktisch, wir haben uns im Supermarkt mit Bagel, Cream Cheese, O-Saft, Jogurth etc. eingedeckt und morgens im Hotelzimmer gefrühstückt. Was mir nicht gefallen hat: - Das Hotel ist schon etwas älter und gerade bei kaltem Wetter zieht es ziemlich durch die Fenster. Vor allem im Bad ist das sehr unangenehm. Gerade, wenn man den ganzen Tag in der Kälte unterwegs war und sich eigentlich auf eine heiße Dusche freut, wird die Freude schnell getrübt. - Die Heizung/Klimaanlage hatte wohl ein Eigenleben. Egal welche Einstellung wir vorgenommen hatten, knackte und kratze es in regelmäßigen Abständen derart laut (sehr gern auch nachts), dass wir manchmal wirklich dachten, da sitzt einer drin und will raus. Wir hatten das Zimmer wirklich sehr günstig gebucht, aber ich persönlich würde nicht noch einmal dieses Hotel wählen - ich mags halt lieber etwas komfortabler.

“Good” Great location to SMU.....about a mile away......an older hotel, but clean and friendly and helpful front desk....free breakfast w/ waffles, fruit, cereal and bagels......a pool that is clean......a middle of the road hotel......would stay here again.

“Perfectly Adequate” Everything about this hotel is perfectly adequate, which means that it is nothing special or memorable, but everything you would generally expect from a mid-range hotel. The rooms were small, but modern and clean. The bed was comfortable. There were enough ammenities, but nothing special. The location is good. You are in close proximity to lots of great shopping and restaurants, but you are not on top of the big tourist draws. I travel to NYC frequently and would stay here again for a quick trip, but probably not for a special occassion. The front desk staff was incredibly friendly particularly for NYC.

“What. A. Dump.” The sad thing is that this could be such a dynamic place. Instead, it's just an old bag that's been around the block too many times. 1) Check in: they'll tell you you have parking...but forget to mention you have to pay for it. 2) You 'll get a nice view....of either another room across the courtyard or to the west, out over the railway tracks. Enjoy the trains-a-rumblin'!! (No doubt these are the rooms for those of us who have paid via Priceline.com.) 3) Water pressure? What's that? 4) How nice: a fire escape out my window. Well, there was no fire, but there were teenagers running up and down it at 3am. 5) Your door slams nice and tight. Too bad all the others do too: nice and LOUDLY. 6) The exercise room is downright creepy. But hey, at least it has (15-year-old) exercise machines. And they work! But wait...what's that? Cigarette fumes floating through the vents. Nice. Like that when I work out. 7) Don't look to close at the moldings and rugs and such: too depressing. 8) Hello and goodbye from the staff that doesn't smile? Not on your life. 9) Wifi? Heck, it's even free at Starbucks. But not here. $10/day, if you can believe it. Caveat emptor. I'm staying tonight at the Red Roof Inn nearby. $30 a night cheaper, just as convenient, much quieter and cleaner and modern.

“Excellent for the Price” For the price I paid on Travelocity, the room was amazing. Actually it was a very large suite (Flat TV, Frig, dishwasher, microwave, dining table). The location is excellent , 8-9 blocks from Georgetown and four from Dupont Circle, basically walking distance to everywhere. The room was clean and room service fantastic. Of course like everywhere else in DC, the staff was NOT Friendly!!!! The view of the room was bad, but that's the price to pay in the City. But overall excellent hotel for the price and location.

“Really enjoyed this hotel” Our suite was a complete apartment with full kitchen, separate living room and separate bedroom. The lavatory and bathe were also in a separate room. The dressing table and sink were off the bedroom. Ample closet space was across from the sink. Plenty of hangars. There is an iron and ironing board and hair dryer also. The bed was very comfortable and had an ample supply of pillows and the european type spread and cover. Two night stands with variable bright lights on two large end tables with three large drawers each. There is a large TV on a three drawer dresser in a corner of the bedroom. Nice big roomy room. Window looked out over the downtown. The living room has a flat screen TV. business desk with executive chair and internet hookups. There is a fold out couch and an overstuffed sitting chair with a side table and a floor lamp. Enjoyed sitting comfortably and reading the paper,which was delivered daily, with a hot,fresh brewed cup of coffee. The kitchen is set up for four persons with all the kitchen needs. The entry is very attractive and all staff are very people friendly. We had two minor repair needs and they were both answered within minutes. Front desk is knowledgeable of the surrounding city. The refrigerator supplys ice so there is no hunting the hallways. Extra coffee and popcorn are available at the front desk. The included breakfast is equivalent to a buffett. There is fresh batter for waffles as well. The eating area is as large and comfortable as any restaurant .There are three large TVs going constanly which is a bit disconcerting since they are on different channels. There are two computers for guest usage. A gas burning fire place with huge overstuffed chair is another place to drink your coffee and read any of the three available papers.

“Good for one night close to LAX” Arriving at LAX 2:45pm after 15 hour flights from Brisbane via Auckland I was pleased to find my room was clean, comfortable, and perfectly adequate for a 1-2 night stopover. I had read some unfavourable reviews of this hotel and my experience was pretty good. The shuttle arrived at LAX some 30 minutes after calling the hotel to request. The return journey the next morning was on time and pleasant. Free Internet was fast and reliable. The breakfast was plentiful although quite basic; had biscuits and gravy for the 1st time in 30 years .. that took me back .... I noticed several people had made use of the pool and small fitness room. Nothing special or memorable about the hotel; but it was good value for money and close to LAX.

“Doesn't keep their promises” I booked a room over a month in advance, through a travel website. When I arrived at the Se to check in, I was handed a letter, and told that I was staying in another hotel quite a distance away. They said that the travel website had overbooked them. I find it very hard to believe that when I made my reservation over a month prior that they had no availability, as my reservation was confirmed. I specifically booked at the Se for the location, on 5th near all entertainment and dining. I had plans to meet friends at a restaurant right down the street for dinner. The hotel I was redirected to did not have any restaurants open at night, and there were not any bars/nightclubs nearby. Basically it was near nothing in the way of dining/entertainment. So, we ended up having to pay for a cab to go out to dinner, when we could have just walked up the street if the Se had honored my reservation. The front desk people could not have been less concerned about the inconvenience that this switch caused me. The Se should not participate with outside booking sites if they do not plan to honor their commitment. Shady business in my opinion.

“Liked the Charlotte Four Points” I think this hotel is recent conversion from another hotel (Morgan?), so it seems fresh and new. The hotel is about half 2 room suites and half rooms, and I was upgraded to a suite. I haven't seen a room, but if the suite isn't much more expensive, I would go with the suite. The suite had a sitting area, desk, refrigerator, microwave and flat screen TV. The bedroom had another flat screen TV and bath area. The staff I dealt with were all friendly and helpful. The hotel has a shuttle to/from the airport every 30 minutes, and it is an easy drive from the airport (about 10-15 minutes on mostly highway). Ample parking. About 5 miles from downtown Charlotte. There is a pool, exercise room, business center, etc., but I didn't use those facilities. When I visit Charlotte again, I will stay here. The hotel is close to the airport, highways, convenient location and probably much cheaper than downtown properties (I paid $88/night for 4 nights).

“Hope Your Experience Will Not Be This Unfortunate” Let me add a cautionary note to the positive reviews others have posted. I booked a one-night stay at this hotel with my partner on a hotel booking website in early March 2010, and received an electronic hotel-issued confirmation number on March 7, four months prior to our arrival. We chose the hotel because of its location across the street from the high-speed Bay State Ferry to Provincetown. Our arrival flight was a red-eye, and on the morning of our flight, I called the hotel, confirmed that we would be arriving that day on the red-eye, and asked that they note in our file that we would be an extremely late arrival and to PLEASE not give away our room. The reservationist assured that this was being added into the file and that they would see us on arriva. We arrived at the hotel at 1245am, only to be told that so sorry, unfortunately, we are in an oversold situation. On the positive side: the hotel had booked us a room at a hotel about 15 mnutes away, and offered a cab voucher there. I appreciated that they arranged a room elsewhere; however, we would have much more appreciated if they had actually honored a reservation we made four months in advance, and that we re-confirmed specifically on the day of our arrival. The hotel also offered a $100 voucher good "on our next stay," which we declined, as that will not happen. Because of our experience, I cannot recommend this hotel to others.

“Great choice if you like a little extra space” My husband and I stayed here for 5 nights in December, and really enjoyed our stay. We didn't find noise to be a problem, even though we had a room that overlooked Times Square on two sides. We loved the extra space the suite gave us. The room was clean and in good repair, although the curtains needed to be washed or replaced. The girl who checked us in was extremely friendly and helpful. The staff was nice in general, but I thought the servers in the breakfast room were too obtrusive. They kept standing directly behind us and it made me uncomfortable. Maybe they were trying to stay occupied because the room wasn't full, but we didn't need a lot of help at a buffet. We've been spending a lot of time in NYC recently, and this was my favorite of the several hotels we tried.

“Among the best, for sure” I do a lot of business traveling and found my recent stay at the Grand Hyatt in downtown Seattle to be among the best experiences in years. The decor is modern and relatively new. My room was spacious and the bathroom had both a deep, clean tub at one end and excellent shower at the other. Wake-up calls are done by staff and you even have the option when making the reservation for more than one wake-up (which one of my sleepy colleagues certainly appreciated). The location, as already mentioned, is great because of all the shops and restaurants within a few blocks. Even getting to and from the airport was a breeze. I had to leave immediately after my conference and the concierge arranged for a cab to be there waiting for me so I could make my flight. For me, the best feature of this place is the outstanding service by the staff. I was in charge of my event and everyone on my staff found the Hyatt personnel to be helpful, cheerful and accommodating. We also all raved about the place and were mad we hadn't left more time to enjoy it. We all did take a soak in that huge tub, though. Granted, it's on the pricey end if you're a budget traveler, but I think you get your money's worth if accommodations and service are important to you. I'll definitely be back.

“Excellent location - north tower with marina view” I could not have been happier with my room in the North Tower on a high floor overlooking the beautiful marina. The weather was perfect while I was there. This was for a conference. It is adjacent to the conference center. It is walkable to many restaurants and sights. I would not hesitate to stay there again. The staff was excellent. Do not miss Cafe 222, a few blocks away for a wonderful breakfast! Also there is a Roy's Restaurant within the hotel which was a pleasant surprise.

“Excellent location, definitely one of the best hotels I've stayed at” The Intercontinental San Francisco is one of the best hotels I've stayed at. I traveled and stayed in hotels over 100 nights in 2009. The location could not have been better, centrally located near shopping, dinning and entertainment. The rooms are large, with high ceilings. We were on the 20th floor. Our room overlooked the entire city. The walls were windows from celing to floor, even in the bathroom. You can see all of San Francisco! Very comfortable and plush rooms. Great bath amenities. The food was amazing! A great experience! Will stay here again!

“clean, convenient, and comfortable in Chicago” Stayed here for 5 nights at end of March. Had a price of $98 a night for the family. Found maid service to be great- even picked up some of my kid's toys/stuffed animals they had laid around. Bought an all day bus/train pass at Jewel Osco across the street and very easy to get around. Also join your local science museum at home and it got us free reciprical access to Museum of Science and Industry, Field Museum, Alder planetarium, and children museum at Navy Pier. Pros- Super location- within walking distance to Mich. avenue, El train line right at corner, bus stop close, grocery store and many restaurants/shopping within one or two blocks. Valet parking was high like most hotels in area but self parking (no in or out) was $29 a day which is cheaper than other hotels nearby. Microwave and refrig in room. Neutragena toiletries. Flat screen tv. Small but adequate pool and hot tub. Business center had free internet access which came in handy. Cons- Suzette at the front desk wasn't the most informative or friendly but she wasn't there everyday either thankfully and 2 out of 3 elevators were broken on the Sunday morning we tried to check out -more than 20 minutes just trying to leave the building but maid was nice enough to let us on the working freight elevator.

“Wonderful for city Hotel.” This place is very nice for a city center hotel, the room are very big, with a bunch of little extras, like free internet, free breakfast, free M-TH drinks and light dinner. I was in a King Studio, with one plamsa TV that would spin to face the sitting area or the bed room. The bathroom was a nice size with the sink outside the shower area. I was please on how clean this place was, and how moden the rooms were. This hotel is very odd, that 1/2 is a Homewood Suites and the other half is a Hilton Garden Inn. The check in counter works both 1/2 and 1/2. Parking is $25.00 per day, and is self in and out parking. The location is in a good area, not right in the middle of the action but a few blocks away. Very please.

“Good Overall Experience but Likely to Get Better” Great location, nice rooms, pleasant environment, good value albeit with lots of little glitches. But look for that to change as hotel was sold this spring and is about to launch complete renovation into a high-tech 4-start property over the next year. Location is pretty unbeatable, immediately adjacent to the Westfield Mall across the The Mint. The front door is literally a few hundred feet from Market so you avoid that traffic but have quick access to the area. Staff were super, super helpful and friendly. But it's also clear that the hotel is presently in a bit of limbo. Front desk is small and check-in wait is long. Antiquated TVs in rooms. Attached restaurant and bar is functional but lots of local clientele creates a different vibe. Renovation plans sound exciting. And it's a really decent hotel to begin with. I suspect next year at this time it will be one of the hottest properties in SOMA.

“Great Location” The location for this hotel cannot be better. It is central to everything. You can walk to Michigan and the Magnificent Mile, and at the same time there is a subway stop on the next block. Stores, resturants, all within two blocks. There is a resturant on this property, Weber Grill, but we did not eat here. Rooms were pretty standard, they include a micro and a small refrig. There was something going on with the smell at the end of the hall. Huge drying fans were drying out whatever it was, we also noticed this on another floor. Front desk was extremely friendly on the morning shift.

“Nice base for a weekend in the city” We were in town for the weekend to see a show and do a little sightseeing with my parents (we gave them a Christmas present of a broadway show and weekend in the city and it took until mid-March before schedules aligned and we could make the trip). The hotel is conveniently located -- just a block away from the Bryant Park subway stop and a short walk over to Times Square -- far enough away to be out of the hustle and bustle, but close enough if you want to walk to a theater in the area. The rooms were clean and comfortable and reasonably sized by NYC standards. Breakfast buffet was good -- but a little overrun on a busy weekend and they ran out of bagels (almost inexcusable in NYC) before we managed to get to breakfast. The hotel held our luggage for us upon arrival early Saturday morning until we came back to check in and again after we checked out on Sunday until we were ready to leave town -- no charge. Room rates were about middle of the road -- I've booked rooms of the same quality for less in the city -- but for some reason room rates this weekend were running high and by the time our weekend arrived, rates for rooms at the same hotel were double what we booked at -- so, something must have been going in the area driving up the rates as everyone knows can happen with NYC hotels. Staff was friendly and accommodating. Definitely going on our short list of places we'll consider when returning to the city in the future.

“Compact & Clean” Great location, close to central park and Museum of Natural History. Room was a bit on the small side (even for New York), but clean and tidy. Service was good, easy check in / out process. Definately recommend for upper west side.

“Good value for a decent hotel in a great location of Chicago” I would rate this hotel a 3 1/2. It is clean and comfortable, but a bit dark. Some features that I found odd were: the closet is behind a curtain, there is a safe in the wall, and the bathtub is a square not fit for a bath. The bathroom is large, but there is not enough counter space for a larger toiletry bag. Internet is about $11 for 24 hours. The hotel has a small fitness center with one bike, several treadmills, and several elliptical machines. There are also weights, mats, and exercise balls. I paid $159 for a weeknight, which is a great deal for this type of room in Chicago. It is conveniently located just a few blocks from the Clark/Lake stop on the Blue line (CTA) from O'Hare, next to the House of Blues, and blocks from many great restaurants.

“Great business hotel” Stayed one night on business. The extras they give you as a Select Guest member are incredible. They make travelling on business easy. For example, you get a free bottle of water, free internet access, free pressing of 2 items, free shoe shine, free morning coffee, paper, etc.. Also, they're express check-in is a breeze. No standing in line, just go up and grab your room card. The location of this hotel is ideal. It is a stone's throw to the business district downtown, and within sight of many popular tourist attractions. The staff was very accomodating, and I really enjoyed the breakfast buffet. The guy working the omelet station went above & beyond to ensure my breakfast was to my liking and that I was able to find everything I needed. The rooms are small but this is Boston, so let's not fault them for that. They're small in NY and Chicago, as well. Toiletries are nice, but they only stock the typical stuff like soap and lotion. If you forget something, like a toothbrush, just ask for it. I only have very small complaints. First, it would be nice if they gave you slippers with the robe. Second, they could have explained how the bed & breakfast package worked. I had to inquire as to where to go for breakfast and what was included. Again, not a big deal, but it should be clearly spelled out for guests when they arrive.

“Picked Hotel Andra from Trip Advisor's recommendation” I picked the Hotel Andra from reviewing the hotels on this web site and I'm glad I did. My husband and I stayed there for 5 nights in mid-July. It offered everything we were looking for - very friendly staff, perfect location, larger than usual room, contemporary feel, daily paper, and fairly priced. Really enjoyed the contemporary look of the room and a very comfortable bed. Staff could not have been friendlier. Since it was our first time in Seattle, we were especially pleased how easy it was to walk to the Market (10 mins), Space Needle (15 mins), Great shopping (5 mins), and even the ball park (about 35 mins). The only things that don't put it in the league of a 5 star is that the bathrooms are nicely updated, but basically older. Also, as mentioned here, the hallway lighting was kind of funky and took a day or two to get used to. We never once smelled any odors from the restaurant. It was noisy from the street several mornings, but I don't know what they could do to help that. Hope you enjoy your stay there as much as us.

“An OK Hotel - at Best” This hotel has a downtown San Francisco location, but is on the edge of a questionable area. I am personally OK with the area, but the service at the hotel is something that leaves a lot to be desired. I had trouble with such minor issues as getting a newspaper delivered to my room. Everyone on the floor got a newspaper but me and this went on for five days. I complained each day all to no avail. The hotel is expensive for breakfast! The best you can do at the hotel for breakfast is $ 20 per person. $ 20 is a lot for a plate of eggs and a few fried potatoes. The service in the restaurant is good, but the prices are expensive. This is NOT the hotel for a business traveller. If you are looking for a business hotel, look elsewhere. For a one time over night stay, this is OK at best. I wouldn't recommend this for any stay more than one night. Even as a Platinum Member of the Holiday Inn program, they offer nothing for the Priority Club Members and ignore you even more if you complain.

“Average hotel, rudest 'front desk' staff on the planet.” I have stayed at this at least five times in the last year or so. I've resisted writing a review because each time I figure, "maybe I've caught them on a bad week." But I was there again last month on business and enough is enough. First of all, while there are some attractions at Penn's Landing, the location isn't the greatest unless you have business in Old City (which I do). If you have business uptown, this is way too far. The hotel itself is alright, nothing special. The hotel restaurant (Keatings) is decent, but expensive. The rooms are average, some with very nice views. My biggest complaint is the staff. I have never met a ruder front desk staff. This last trip, "Louis" checked me. He never greeted me, asked me how my trip in was, never welcomed me back to the hotel even though I am a repeat customer. He simply looked up from what ever he was doing and said "Name?" How charming. Made me feel right at home. He never asked me if I need assistance with my bags, if I needed any help with anything at all. The wait-staff in the restaurant can be just as rude -- until they bring you your check and try to work-in a good tip for themselves. I would say the management at this hotel better check on their staff. Like I said, the hotel is ok, the staff -- YUCK!

“Something missing” Arriving at the J.W. Marriott I was impressed by the entrance and beauty of the building and landscaping. My room was ready and check in was quick and easy. It is a walk to everywhere. The room was smaller than I expected. Is there a special on throw pillows. The bathroom was very appealing. However, a 29 in TV, you're kidding me. This is a resort, I don't even have 29 in tvs at home. There was no DVD player in the room which I would have expected. The rooms were also a little noisy for my taste. The grounds and facilities are stunning with the exception of the health club, which is mediocre. Why is it that Resort and Spas usually have poor health clubs? Maybe the belief is "you're here to be lazy, if you want to sweat, go to Bally's" The equipment was in bad condition and it just wasn't a good facility. The health club requires you to walk outside to get there (bad move). The pools were beautiful with a lazy river and walking path along side. The hotel is pretty isolated, but it is located in a relatively nice area with a huge shopping complex and strip mall within walking distance. We always ate dinner offsite at one of the restaurants, so I didn't have a chance to eat at the Resort. My wife said the Spa was first class and thought the prices were reasonable. There is also a golf course on the grounds (it's Phoenix). I would stay here again, but it probably wouldn't be my first choice in the Phoenix area. I've stayed in much better rooms for less money and better looking places. My wife and I went for a convention and spent a couple of extra days, but as soon we were leaving, another convention was moving in. Maybe that had to do with the coldness of the place. That may be what's missing.

“Not quite worth the money” This isn't a bad hotel. It has it good points and mediocre points but at $225 pn + tax for the four days I stayed, it certainly isn't a great value. I reserved a balcony waterfront view, and the room I got at the end of the hall is probably one of the best standard rooms they've got. I was disappointed that the balcony was almost entirely glassed in, which impaired the view from inside and made the balcony fairly worthless. But there is also a nice view from the window over the desk, so the waterfront request was worth it. The room is pretty small by today's standards and the bathroom positively petite--combo tub shower with curtain, single sink--although the rainfall showerhead was nice. Bed was fairly comfortable, plenty of outlets at the desk, decent lighting for working and reading Time to upgrade the TV to a nice HD flat panel at these prices, Marriott. My biggest gripe is that the internet ethernet connection didn't work for most of my stay, and the wireless connection only worked in a common area on the second floor. This was problematic enough that I cut my trip short. The positive about the hotel is the staff. They were unfailingly efficient, courteous and helpful. Check in took all of about 45 seconds before I had my key, a smile from the clerk and was on my way to the room. When I complained about the internet problem, they removed all charges including the day that it did work before I even inquired. Nor did I get hit with a cancellation fee when I left early. Housekeeping and room service were reliable and prompt. The grounds are nice. I hear a lot of people complaining about the elevator but except for my last night there when hundreds of people checked in at once, I never waited long. Location is convenient for conventions, and a $5 cab ride from the train station which was my mode of transportation from LA. Roy's Hawaiian restaurant was very good food and service, and a prime location with great views from indoors and out. Swimming pool area was pretty small but attractive. To go drinks for the pool area were available from the bar on the Roy's patio, and a telephone outside the gate could be used to order room service food. I can't complain about my stay except for the internet, but this isn't a real resort hotel. It's one of those places that is great for a few nights if you're planning on being on the go all day or you're there for a convention or business. In that light, it is very pleasant.

“location location location” We stayed in the Comfort Inn Manhattan in May of 2006. It was a great location, which was in Herald Square next to Macy’s on 35th and Broadway. Vinny was very helpful by taking our luggage and letting us store it before we checked in and after we checked out. The workers at the hotel were very friendly. The room was small but nice. The shower sometimes got cold but what do you expect with a 100 year old hotel. The hotel was neat because it was older and had character. If you go, check out the old railings in the stairway. The stairs and the old mail slot next to the elevator have a lot of character. There is a nice Irish pub next door and down the way. The 32nd ‘N’ stop is right next to the hotel. The price was very reasonable compare to other hotels in the area. The breakfast was included and it was really good. I would recommend this hotel if you plan on visiting all the sites. We were very close to all the major tourist sites.

“Excellent business hotel with great views” I liked the fact that this hotel borders a lot of different areas, was wonderfully appointed, and a great value. It is really on the border of the financial district and Chinatown, both housing the Chinese Cultural Center and located one block from the Transamerica Building. It's also a short walk to Italian restaurants to the north and 15 minutes to the convention area to the south. I had a nice view and I was only on the 8th floor. The room, while not new, was in excellent condition and tastefully decorated. No washcloths were provided the first day in the bathroom, but a simple note to housekeeping solved that problem. Is that a trend - I've had that happen at other hotels. The fitness center was a good size with both music and TV options. The line at Peet's in tthe lobby was long in the morning, but there's plenty of other options right down the street. I did not go to the lobby restaurant.

“Fantastic Hotel” I visit Philadelphia often & recently stayed at The Le Meridien & had an amazing experience! The building is really beautiful, the lobby restaurant Amuse & Bar were fantastic, & the entire feel of the hotel is clean, simple & modern. Check-in was efficient & I was granted an early arrival around 10am, which was great *& much appreciated!! My room (#1018) was an SPG floor which was lovely & the bed was incredible! The design again was simple & stream-lined, with a great flat panel TV, nice shower head, soft carpeting & was relatively quiet, facing the interior of the hotel. I ordered room service for lunch, & there was a slight error in my order, but the problem was solved quickly; I had breakfast at the restaurant & the food was very good(the Club Sandwich & Fries from room service is insanely good & the Belgian Waffle was really tasty!), as was the service! The location is good, about a 10 min walk or less to Rittenhouse Sq, etc. I really loved the hotel & will continue to stay here....already booked for this week!:) I would like to mention the following staff members I came in contact with who provided exemplary service: the Bellman were all fantastic & quick to greet, Samantha from the Restaurant called me personally about my slight Room Service issue & was very kind & thoughtful; Caroline R. provided lovely breakfast service & was very sweet; Liljana N. from Room Service was great, & Adam at the Front Desk was very friendly!--- I typically stay at The Sofitel or The Four Seasons in Philly, but Le Meridien was flawless & I felt very comfortable staying here! Congrats to a fantastic start! Best, Patrick M. Winkler NYC

“Good hotel, but several flaws” Here for a night on business, so I didn't pay for the say. The hotel is quite clean, ideally situated if one has business on the east side or in Queens, and with excellent personnel. But there were a few niggling issues: -faded carpet in my guest room on the Executive Floor (Hilton Honors Gold) -no food or drink of any kindin the Executive Floor lounge until breakfast time at 7AM (latish for NYC, I think); -one of the two telephones in my room didn't work -I had booked a rate that included parking. But the bill slipped under my door charged that same rate plus $48 for parking. They rectified the bill upon my request; still, it's annoying to have to check on this. Would I stay here again? Yes. Did they exceed my expectations? No.

“I'll be back yet again! =)” My friend & I booked this hotel to be close to Downtown Dallas. After I had booked, I had realized that I had stayed here back in 2003.(BTW-This is a VERY convenient location if you are attending a show at the American Airlines Arena!). So needless to say, it has been upgraded since my last stay. There is a $24 per day charge for parking and it is secure in the connecting parking garage. They processed our requests accordingly- we had asked for extra pillows & a room near the elevator! I booked a King bedroom with sofa sleeper. The room was clean, quite, & comfortable. The only snafu we had was that the corded phone was having issues. We used the cordless phone to call the front desk and a serviceman was sent up. He was efficient and got the phones up and running in no time. The staff was great. When we checked in, we were greeted by Mark. He gave us dinner recommendations for the night. He had a very pleasant and positive attitude-he's an asset to the company. The 2 ladies at check-out were also very friendly! I would come back here again! Thanks for the nice stay! =)

“Unimpressed and Disappointed” We booked our room for two nights in mid-June for a relaxing get-away weekend. When I got into line to check in, I was behind an exasperated family who had been through 3 rooms because of issues. My thought was that it was unfortunate and that they must be too picky...my mistake. It was foreshadowing. Our first room had horrible, dirty stains all over the carpet and the pipes whined when the toilet was flushed. Room two was clean enough but the A/C didn't work. After a 6 hour drive, our third room was decent enough that we were able to rest. The front desk did offer us one free breakfast buffet ticket as compensation for our troubles. I know that room maintenance was not the problem of the front desk, but it is the hotel’s responsibility to keep up the rooms. I am very disappointed and will not book there again.

“Tiny Rooms--TINY TINY” It is obvious this hotel is a relic of the 60's with fresh paint and new linens. While it is very convenient and quite clean, i found the rooms, expecially the bath room to be extraordinarly small. The Courtyard practically across the street is a far, far, far better hotel.

“Great Hotel, great location!” The Marriott East Side is a great hotel in NY and I would definently recommend it. The staff were friendly and so helpful to my whole family. They even managed to get tickets for my parents to see Chicago when it was "sold out". The rooms are a good size and nicely decorated. We had a problem with the blind and window in our room and both were dealt with minutes after we had called reception. The hotel is very close to all the main sights of the city and walking anywhere never takes very long. Grand central station is only a few blocks away as well. Overall great value for money and a great place to stay.

“Great Hotel in a great location” The Sofitel is located in a very pretty part of Washington. Very quiet amongst tree lined streets, but also very close to everything. A walk to the White House and the Mall is easy and interesting and it has two subway stops and a stop for the Circulator within a block, which makes getting around the city very easy. We stayed in a junior suite which was large and elegantly furnished. We felt very comfortable and pampered in the room, although note that these rooms face the internal courtyard which means looking at brick walls. They are also close to the elevators and we seemed to notice the associated noise from about 7am to 10pm. The only other thing to note is that on the weekend there isnt much open close to the hotel in terms of eating. There is a Starbucks a couple of minutes away, but we couldnt find much else close by. But it's worth trying the breakfast in the hotel. The food was great, not overly expensive and in a very comfortable and relaxed setting. The provided basket of pastries never went untouched and while we didnt plan to eat in the hotel, we did every day. This hotel deserves its rating on TA and I think you would be assured of a comfortable stay in a great, convenient location. But if you dont luck out with a street facing room, expect to see nothing.

“A good hotel with attractive prices” During one of my business trips to Austin, I was staying at the Doubletree in the University area. The hotel is in very good shape, the rooms are pretty nice and one has a beautiful view over the skyline of downtown Austin - especially during sunset! The very friendly staff was always helpful and I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel. While the dining options on-site are quite limited, I wouldn't count that as a big minus as Austin has a lot of good places to offer that are all easy to reach. The location on I-35 is pretty convenient for access to almost all areas of the city.

“unbeatable location” Well folks, this W is in the center of action. You are within walking distance to the Smithsonians, the National Mall and the restaurants in Penn Quarter. You are right next to the WH and if you go to the rooftop bar you can get a pretty good view of it. This is the continuation of Hotel Washington and the rooms are freshly renovated and the decor is pleasant. The shower has glass enclosures all around so privacy may be an issue. The rooftop bar generates quite a bit of noise so beware of that as well. The staff is friendly but they do charge $40 if you borrow the umbrella and fail to return it.

“Great location, and value!” We'd highly recommend this hotel! We paid $210/night for the petite room, but were lucky and got upgraded to a suite. The room was nice (they're small in NYC, but it was cool); the hotel in general is very hip. It's a newer hotel and totally redone. Breakfast is good, and its included, as is the free WiFi in your room (they charge you for use of the computer in the lobby). The hotel has a little, but nice (and open 24 hours) hotel pool with swim up bar, steam room, sauna, etc. It looked like a real party scene at night. Hotel staff were super nice. Excellent location in Times Square area (Midtown Manhattan). Cool Irish pub nearby. Not one complaint. Great experience.

“Fantastic view” We stayed in this hotel for 1 night in May. We were immediately assigned a room on check-in at 12 noon and to our surprise, the room was on a high floor with a fabulous view of Central Park! Not bad considering we paid $175 a night thru Priceline! The room was of a good size by NYC standard with modern decor. The bathroom was very nice - unlike some other Trip advisor reviews - with nice amenities. The location is also handy to all the major tourist attractions like 5th Ave, Rockfeller Center and Broadway. All-in all, highly recommended.

“Nice hotel - awkward location” Here were the good things about this hotel. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the room was spacious, they had a free limo shuttle around the city between 7 and 3, the wake-up call was a real person, they delivered free coffee or tea to your room and left it outside the door with no knock (meaning no tip required) at the time you ordered it for, lovely turn down service with chocolates, TV in the dressing area and better than average excercise room. I thought the location was awful... atop very steep hills and you have to really climb or take public transportation. Granted the cable car was right out front, that is not an easy means of transporation if you have to work there. The free limo in the mornings worked well for me. While they do have high speed internet access, it cost $9.95 a day. The desks in the room were tiny and if you had to work, there really was no space. The first room they gave me had a TV in an entertainment center but when you pulled it and even turned it as far as you could, you couldn't see the TV from the bed. They switched rooms for me , and while this TV could be seen from the bed, the tv was along the left hand wall from the bed and the TV had to stick way out into the room and the entertainment center door now blocked the door into the hall. Very awkward set up. If you don't want to eat at this hotel which is very expensive ($20) for breakfast or the neighboring Top of the Mark or Fairmont (also very expensive) you must get down from the hill and then back up the hill. There is nothing else nearby. This location is awkward for business travellers and the room amentities don't cater to such. If I were on vacation, I think something closer to the Wharf or the downtown where walking isn't such a challenge would work better.

“So not in Georgetown” While the hotel is fine, it is not, according to the locals, in Georgetown. Given the walk to get to Georgetown, I'd have to agree. This hotel is situated in the West End, which is between downtown to the east, foggy bottom (George Washington University) to the south, Dupont Circle to the north and Georgetown to the west. It is the west end of the business district, but not, as the owners would have you believe, in Georgetown...which begins once you cross the bridge that separates the west end from Georgetown. Demand truth in advertising. There are three other hotels who are proud of their place in DC - the Park Hyatt, the Ritz and the Fairmount - all who claim to be in the West End.

“巨大モールの目の前” ホテルの目の前に巨大モールがあって、買い物にはとても便利な場所です。徒歩圏内にドラッグストアもあります。その他は、チェーン展開しているホテルですし特に変わったところはありません。アメリカ並みの普通の広さ(つまり日本より広い)で、バスタブつき、キングサイズベッドの部屋に1人で泊まりました。今回は1人だったのでどちらでもいいのですが、洗面所がバスルームの外についていたので、複数人数で泊まる時は1人がバスルームを占拠していても外で他の人が歯磨きなどできて便利だと思いました。

“期待はずれでした。” 仕事で5泊しました。たしかにロビーの豪華な点、ラウンジがとてもすてきな点。夜になるとラウンジでグランドピアノの演奏があったりととても大人な雰囲気の歴史あるホテルだと思います。 ただ、メインビルディング内の客室も、タワーの客室も両方みましたが、非常に古く、感動できませんでした。タワーの客室は景色がいいというポイントのみで、客室が豪華かというと、あまりそうでもありません。それよりアメリカでは仕方がないと思いますが、窓の汚さが目立つという印象でした。 アメニティも5泊の期間中, シャンプー類が置いてあるのみでした。またこのシャンプーはカナダのRoseの香りのオーガニック系のものだったと思いますが、全くほのかな香りもなく、不評でした。アメニティ関係では、スリッパ、綿棒、歯ブラシ、マウスウォッシュ、シェービングキット等、言えば持ってきてくれるという状況でして、英語を話さないお客様には少々ハードルの高い状態です。 また、ホテルにレンタカー(Hertz)のカウンターがあるということで、車を借りたのですが、受付をしてくれた女性の案内&態度が不十分で不安になりました。(一流ホテルにあるカウンターなのだからもう少しまともな対応してほしいなと思います)また、フェアモントでPick Upはできますが、返却は、Union Sqの麓のHertzへ返却しなければいけなかったので、返却後、ホテルまできつい上り坂を歩いて戻るという予想外の展開もありました。 また、朝食付きプランでしたが、あまりセレクションがなく、5泊もしていると 完全に飽きてしまいました。そして、朝食券をうっかり忘れてしまうと、 部屋に取りに戻るよう指示され、部屋番号を伝えればなんとかホテル側で解決していただけるのではないのか?と思うような対応があり首をかしげてしまいました。 お隣のインターコンチや、ルネッサンスよりも、100ドル位高いホテルだったのですが、 正直、ホスピタリティも考慮すると価格に見合わない気がしてしまいました。 ゴージャスなのはエントランスとフロント、ラウンジ、1Fのバンケットルーム等、要するに共有スペースです。

“Solid stay. Nothing special, though.” I flew into Dallas on business and chose the Hilton Garden Inn because it was near the airport. There was nothing bad about my stay, but there was nothing special about it, either. It was average in the most true sense of the word. I was checked in promptly. My room was clean. If you need a place near the airport, this place is fine.

“Small room, nice views, decent price” If you are there on business, and use your room only for sleeping and showering, then it's a good little hotel. Views from the higher floors are downright spectacular. But the room is TINY! No room for anything other than you and your bags. Clean, sparsely appointed, and very spartan in every respect. All business.

“One of my favorite hotels ever!” The minimalist attitude of the hotel design is comfortable and relaxing after a busy day walking the streets of San Francisco. The flat screen tv, eco-friendly amenities and comfortable bed were a great respite in a busy city. Their restaurant has wonderful food all with a sustainable bent. The atmosphere was calm and relaxing at the gates to China Town. The only negative was that I could hear the garbage truck during the night, but I wouldn't have traded me view even with the noise.

“A truly great bargain” This is my second stay at this hotel, though this time my wife joined me, so there were two in our room. I have only good things to say about the Chancellor. This is a hotel that speaks of the caring attitude from top to bottom: ownership, management, employees. Even with two of us in the room, which is on the small side, as anyone reading reviews of this hotel is well aware, we managed without a problem. The room was quiet, clean, newly decorated and the bed was very comfortable. Breakfast was reasonably priced and tasty; service was cheerful and professional. In fact, all of the staff was courteous, knowledgable and helpful (e.g., they take it as a challenge to get you online via their WIFI system, which I am finding is difficult to do with Microsoft's Vista software, but they persisted in helping me -- and succeeded, more than I can say about the other, much more expensive, hotel where we stayed on this trip). In a city like San Francisco, what more does one really need? In fact, many of the more expensive hotels we have been to could learn a lot by observing the efforts that everyone associated with the Chancellor makes to help you enjoy your trip. By the way, if you wish to have a quiet and peaceful room (though without a view), request one in the back.

“Great place to stay” After our long journey from Australia it was lovely to arrive, have a quick check-in and collapse in our very clean, comfy room with nice views. The large Prudential mall is right next door and a number of food shops and delis are in the surrounding streets. Although this hotel is not in the CBD it's only a 15 minute stroll to the Boston Common and there are also two subway train stations nearby. The local streets are fairly quiet so it's easy to get a good rest. It's also an easy walk to local parks and the river and the eclectic Newbury street, just around the corner is full of restaurants and shops. If your coming for a conference at the Convention centre this is the place to stay. we also caught the train from Boston to New York (starting at Back Bay station) and it was excellent

“Good Stay” We had a comfortable stay here; the beds were comfortable, the room was clean and everything worked OK. I don't understand some of the other reviews about breakfast because there was no breakfast here, just coffee in the lobby which is standard for Motel 6. The pool was clean and we had a good swim. One of the bonuses here is the 10% discount for Marlowe's Rib and Burger, with the free pink cadillac which picks you up. The staff were friendly and helpful. We would stay here again.

“Average, Clean Business Hotel” We arrived late in the evening and everyone was really nice, although the front desk person seemed a little annoyed when I asked for a second cookie for my wife. Could have been a long day for her, no harm no foul. GOOD We got a room close to the lobby (but even the porter was telling us how hard it was to get to some rooms). It was clean. We had asked for extra pillows and they were there. NOT SO GOOD The shower's water pressure was pathetic, so was the shower curtain. The bathroom was in disrepair. A little bit of a funky odor (cleared up by opening the window). They advertise that the airport shuttle runs every 15 minutes, but at 6:30A there was no bus there and we were told it would be 20-30 minutes before the next bus. If you were rushed for a flight and depending on them, this would have been stressful. The staff at the coffee stand in the lobby could not have cared about what they were doing less.

“Disappointed in Tribeca” I stayed at the Cosmopolitan Hotel in New York City in June 2005. I have never been so disappointed in a hotel as this one. It is "budget" in price; so you have to take that in to consideration. The good thing about it was the access to the subway-out the door and on the corner. The bad thing(s). The staff was rude, ( I was asking for directions and the day clerk answered the phone; turned her back to me and completely ignored me as I stood there); usually when the shift changes in a hotel; you take a chance -that the new person will be a little more cordial and accomodating. Not so here!! Each one was as arrogant as the last one. They had no time for their guests. The good thing about the room was the bathroom. Even though it was the size of a closet; the sink was clean. The floor had been mopped. I bring my own disinfectant so I did use that on the toilet and shower stall. (no bathtube). The room was so-o small; I had no place to put my luggage- had to put it on top of a free-standing Cabinet that doubled for a closet. Had to cross the bed to get to the window; draperies filthy; window screens did not fit properly; had a fan above the bed which blew dirt all over. I do NOT recommend this hotel; even for the 125.00 budget price; it was not a pleasant place to come back to after a day of sight-seeing. I couldn't wait to get out of there in the morning and hated to come back at night. They have to have your credit card number before they turn on the phone. SKIP THIS ONE!! bJR

“Average Marriott, but beware the highway noise” I stayed one night at this hotel recently. The hotel is an average Marriott, with a soft bed, average-sized room, decent fitness and indoor/outdoor pool, and friendly front-desk staff. The internet was included with my business rate, but based on the prices others were quoting on Tripadvisor, my mid-week $149 fee was too high. However, the hotel is right next to the Dallas Parkway (good for getting on the freeway, but bad for noise at night). I heard the flow of cars the entire time I was awake in my room. I sleep somewhat heavy, so once asleep I did not notice it. The hotel is at least 20 minutes from downtown. Also, even though the hotel is fairly isolated (in an area with tons of parking), they still charge $12 (or something like that) to park overnight. They also have valet covering the entire front lot that could easily be used for all of the guests. The entire valet section had many 7 cars in it. This is just an unfortunate way to make extra money - Marriott should just raise the rates by $10, because every single guest would have to park in the garage (how else would you get to this hotel)?

“great location, busy hotel” this is a big, busy hotel with two huge towers. it's not a place i would choose for an intimate getaway, but the location is great; just over the bridge from michigan ave and a nice stroll to all the stores and restaurants. when we were there (Thanksgiving), there were a bunch of conventions and a big wedding going on. getting our luggage out of luggage storage on saturday afternoon was a zoo. but service was really top notch. we got the hotel through priceline, and saved some $ by parking in the millenium garage, which is a 3 block walk. no in and out privileges, but it was half the price of the onsite parking. there is a also a full service supermarket (bockwinkels), directly behind the hotel so we skipped the overpriced hotel food and just picked up some stuff there for snacks and breakfast.there is free internet available in both lobbies and also in the skybridge that links the two. the weather was really nice the first couple of nights so we walked up michigan ave to eat at the foodlife buffet at the water tower (about 1 mile), which has tasty and healthy food--a huge salad and hot food bar with turkey, stuffing, kale salad, 4 different kinds of soups, etc. the rooms in the hotel are not huge, and i wish the beds were a little more firm. no pool. it was also really overheated for the first couple of days but once the weather cooled down the room was comfortable. concierge, bell service, and the front desk were all top notch. i would return,

“The little hotel that could...kind of. Well, not really.” In a nut shell: If you’re the type of traveler who only uses a hotel room for sleeping and showering, and you don’t mind a broken elevator or a lack of a/c, then you’d probably be o.k. with the Crescent. But if you want modern amenities, good service, and comfortable or luxurious surroundings, then the Crescent is definitely not for you. The hotel has these pros: * A great location -- just a couple of blocks from Union Square and all its shopping/dining. * "Boutique" concept – though the delivery of this concept is suspect. * A reasonable price. The hotel has several cons: * The surly staff (see below for specific examples). * The elevator, which worked only some of the time. * The lack of air conditioning anywhere in the hotel. * The lack of a manager (we never saw one on duty). * The cleanliness. The mini bar in our room was covered with dust, and the tooth-brush holder and shower curtain had visible algae growing on them. * The smoky lobby. People aren't allowed to smoke in the hotel, so they stand right in front of the always-open front door (the only source of cool air in the lobby) -- allowing their smoke to come in with the breeze. More About: Old building with no Air Conditioning The hotel is a boutique property. I don’t know the original use of the building, but I can attest that the floorboards creek and groan when walked upon, the elevator is ancient and unreliable, and the entire property is without air conditioning. Though the San Francisco climate is generally pleasant, we still found ourselves feeling hot and stuffy. The rooms do have ceiling fans, but they only pushed around the stuffy air. We would have opened the windows at night, but they didn't have screens, and we weren't willing to take the chance of bugs or birds coming in while we slept. More About: Shabby Chic Rooms The rooms are decorated in a pleasing and modern/vintage style, but everything in the rooms exudes the bargain-basement prices that the property must have paid for the furnishings. The bed pillows and duvet are stuffed with 100% synthetic, bulky materials, and they were truly uncomfortable. The furniture is (as one of my friends described) “shabby chic.” The mini bar was stocked with a nice assortment of snacks, but several items had expiration dates that had passed by a couple of weeks. Also, certain alcoholic items were listed on the menu, but weren’t stocked in our fridge. During checkout, I was out on the corner hailing a cab (more on this later), so I’m not sure whether the desk staff gave my friend any grief for the missing items when we settled the bill. More About: Bare-Minimum Amenities On our first morning, we went downstairs for the complementary breakfast, which was cheap and, more notably, creepy! The “restaurant” is an empty gray room with hanging florescent lights and no decorations, art, plants, music, or other clues to signal that you’re in a hotel dining room. One employee was walking around clearing tables and depositing the dirty plates on a card table set against one of the walls. And he seemed very unhappy about his job. He was literally slamming things on the table and huffing as he left and entered the room. He never said anything to us nor did he bring us glasses or silverware. We went to the humble buffet of store-bought pastries and juice, grabbed a few things for the road and left. The whole scene was depressing, and we didn’t return to that room for the remainder of our stay. More About: Quirky Elevator As several people have commented, the single elevator at this property is small, old, and often out of service. When we were waiting to check in, we watched guest after guest walk in and head directly for the stairs. At first we thought that these people were off-duty employees or possibly even residents of lower-level apartments. But two days into our stay, we were trained to opt for the stairs unless we saw people coming off of the elevator. The elevator was randomly out of service throughout our stay. The best part about the malfunctioning elevator is that the management never put a sign up or said anything to guests who tried to use the elevator. Because we were on the 9th floor, the stairs got to be nuisance. If I hadn’t been staying with a group of friends, I would have checked out and gone to a hotel with a working elevator. More About: Surly Staff Our interactions with staff were few, but each was completely lack luster. Everyone who works at the Crescent looks to be about 22 years old, and no one seems to take pride in his/her job. We were never greeted when walking into the small lobby. Our check-in was delayed by almost an hour with very little explanation as to why. And on more than one occasion, I watched hapless international visitors (the hotel seemed to have many residents from abroad) make simple requests of staff that were met with heavy sighs and exasperated looks. For us, whether ordering a drink in the lounge or arranging for a cab, the staff were unhelpful and only made the task at hand cumbersome. For example, on our last night, we stopped into the 2nd floor lounge for a drink. The server had very little knowledge of the bar's long (and off beat) liquor selection. As a result, she had to come back twice to tell us that they didn't have what we'd just ordered (and we were requesting common drinks/liquors). The third time was the charm, but by then, we'd waited 20 minutes for a drink in an otherwise empty bar. When we got those drinks, they were so strong that we left them and went back to our room. I appreciate the bartender’s trying to give us value for our $10, but a drink should still be, well, drinkable. My favorite staff interaction was on the morning of our departure. I called the front desk to arrange for a cab. The young lady who answered politely told me that I would have better luck if I just walked down the street to the corner in front of the Hyatt, where cabs came by "every few minutes." She was right. I went to the corner and immediately hailed my own cab, but a staff person could (and should) have done the same thing. Aside from the multiple ways in which the Crescent and its staff fell short, I feel strangely ambivalent about my stay. I’m usually one to immediately communicate any issues to a hotel’s management, but somehow, I had the feeling that doing so would be useless. These people were obviously unable to run the place much less deal with complaints about it, so I just let them be. The Crescent's rate was cheap for San Francisco, but I would have gladly paid more for a consistent, customer-oriented hotel/experience at one the neighborhood’s many trustworthy hotel brands. And the next time, I’ll do just that.

“attentive staff, no odors, clean, fun decor, water temp is highly variable” Stayed there on university business. Found on internet and booked by UWA. Huge improvement over the last time I stayed there a number of years ago (updated). Excellent hotel and very attentive staff. The most attentive staff of any full service business hotel I have stayed at in the last year. They were at my door in 5 minutes when I asked for something at 11:30pm. Convenient and free parking. No odor in room, which was excellent. Not even perfume air freshener. This was one of the high points. Too many feathers, had to request some special pillows and blankets to have a feather-free bed, but they came in about 5 minutes. Had a room on the 15th floor with view of the space needle. Excellent and quiet room. Recently updated. Shower has highly fluctuating temperature. You have to be prepared to jump out of shower periodically as it gets very hot or cold all of a sudden. Comfortable beds. Excellent value for U district. Would stay there again.

“They had me, then they lost me...literally. But still lots of good amenities and terrific location.” My first business trip in a long while, went to Chicago to spend two days working on a project, and chose this from several in the area that my company offered because we had a great corporate rate and location was good. Initially was very impressed. We checked in mid-day and both my colleague and I immediately were able to go to our rooms (early). Trendy vibe the moment you walk through the door. Through some promotion I don't recall, I'm currently Starwood Gold, so was upgraded to a spectacular view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier on the 24th floor and given 4pm checkout on the day of departure, which was nice with a late flight. Room had flat-screen TV, two double beds, well-equipped bathroom with nifty Bliss amenities (and there's a Bliss spa on premises). There is an odd window in the bathroom with shutters that can open and close. I didn't mind it, but can see where it might freak out traditionalists. iPod docking station on the nightstand has become an expected but welcome amenity in this class of hotel. Weird traditional analog bedside clock was very hard to see if you woke up in the middle of the night. Closet space is strange because clothing storage is in drawers undeneath the closet so you have to awkwardly bend down to get your clothes. Not a deal breaker but if I had a bad back, would be annoyed. I missed some small amenities like an in-room coffeemaker and a stand for my suitcase for packing/unpacking. Everything's very design-y and trendy and theme-y. The extra roll of toilet paper in the bathroom had a cover titled "Backup Plan," the newspaper was presented every day in a grey bag titled "News" that hung on the doorknob,even the bathmat had the word "Step" inscribed on it. Little details were fun; guess these are a W signature but I don't stay at a lot of them. Had best intentions of working out so I did visit the pool and gym area, which seemed well equipped. The pool is indoors but there is an outdoor deck which would be fun in the summer months. Loved the treadmills facing the lake. Sadly, business and sleep took priority and I never made it there to actually work out. Had a great ahi tuna sandwich for lunch at the lobby bar and our group even briefly checked out Whiskey Sky, the rooftop bar, which wasn't as exciting as we'd hoped - very small and the view was better from my room. We had the chance to try their Acura "Wherever Whenever" service where their driver will take you anywhere you need to go within 5 miles of the hotel - much more pleasant and fun than a regular taxi cab. Service starts at noon so not great for early morning business meetings, but a really fun perk. So I was feeling great about the place initially, but the love affair ended abruptly when after a grueling 12 hour work day, I came back to my room to find that they'd checked me out. All my things were still there, untouched, but a friend came to visit and texted me to tell me the front desk told her I'd checked out. A half-hour ordeal ensued with a manager (Sasha) who insisted my reservation was only for one night (though I had an itinerary and materials given me at check-in that clearly stated two nights) and suggested that somehow I had made the mistake. "No, there's nothing noted here in the change log, it always was for just one night..." she kept saying over and over again. Wish she'd spent less energy insisting I was wrong and more energy trying to fix it. I was finally checked in again, but the next day the bill slipped under my door was wrong on so many counts that I had to go to the front desk again to fix it. Wound up with two separate bills, one for each night, which should be fun for submitting expenses. Parking was a breathtaking $48, so I was glad I didn't have a rental car, internet access was $40 for 3 days, and they charged me $2.29 access for calling the airline's 800 number. Be aware. Would I stay there again? Sure. But I'd make them print out proof of my check-out date and rate the moment I checked in. I would skip the internet access and stick to the cell phone for all my calls, even 800 numbers. The hotel is a block away from West Egg Cafe, a favorite breakfast spot, and another restaurant recommendation is Graham Elliot (not in the neighborhood but worth seeking out). Pumpernickel crusted sturgeon was amazing.

“We always stay here -- for a feeling of small-town San Diego.” We're frequent visitors to San Diego, and we make a habit of staying at Island Palms. It's often said that San Diego hasn't realized it's a small town that grew into a big city. Staying at this hotel evokes a feeling of San Diego as it used to be. Located on Shelter Island, the hotel is isolated from the rampant development, freeways and mall jams that characterize the more high-profile neighborhoods. Yet it is convenient to all that. But on Shelter Island you're surrounded by shops, restaurants and homes that don't seem to have changed much in the past 20 or 30 years. You're in the middle of the "yachtie" subculture, a different little world. The pace is slower and the view is superb. It's worth the extra price to get a "Bayview Suite" on the 2nd floor facing the harbor (not the marina). Bring binoculars and amuse yourself from your deck, living room or bed with an unobstructed view of the fascinating boat traffic in the channel. You'll see everything from massive U.S. Navy vessels and cruise ships to tourist "duck" boats and fishing boats plus pleasure boats arriving in the U.S. from Mexico. A lovely green park runs alongside the channel -- perfect place for a picnic or a brisk morning walk. Or go to the other side of the hotel, with rows and rows of yachts in the marina, to watch boat crews busily taking care of the rich people's playthings. The suite is comfortable, with ceiling fans, vaulted bedroom ceiling and a kitchen that makes it feel more like home. The rooms were redecorated enough years ago t be a bit dated now. But that wall of windows overlooking the channel can't be beat. We travel a lot and know there are fancier, more exotic places to land. But Island Palms is still one of our favorite destinations.

“Gorgeous hotel - would return” Got a stellar deal on this hotel - $92/night on price line for 4 nights. The room had one double bed and I was told I could upgrade to a room with two double beds for about another $40. The hotel is close (two blocks away) from the train station, however note that there is no elevator in case you have suitcases - wish I had known! The hotel is in sort of boutique upper class area although you wouldn't think it when you get off the train. I was very happy with my stay. The room I got would be a little small if I had another body in there but for one person it was very comfortable. The room included a welcome tray, a TV, aveda toiletries, note only a shower (no bathtub if thats your thing), hardwood floors (nice change from musty carpet), gorgeous decor inside the room right down to the linens. The hotel has noticeably friendly staff and this goes right down to the cleaning ladies. The hotel has a spa which I did not get an oppurtunity to check out, a bar area right in the lobby - great drinks, a nice seating area towards the back of the lobby where there is a mini restaurant offering breakfast - very tasty and good value. I was impressed the most with the cleanliness of the hotel, the customer service - incredible and the location (away from all the madness of tourists). Upon departing the staff made arrangements for transportation to the airport which ended up being a private car service - very luxurious for the same price that we would have paid for an uncomfortable taxi ride. Not sure about parking cost at the hotel but I knew it as a good choice when I saw an entire flight crew checking in one morning. I would definately stay here again and reccomend it to all my friends. The room and the hotel itself looks exactly like the pictures that are available on hotel website.

“Not bad if you don't want Internet Access” The number deal breaker with this place is the Internet, it has issues, it seems to be a re-occurring problem based on other TripAdvisor reviews. Other then internet from time to time the rates on this place drop and can be a real good deal overall. What to expect for the complementary breakfast: Pillow Eggs, Hard Boiled Eggs, Sausage, Cereal, Milk, Juice, Waffles, Assorted Breads, Fruit, oat meal. The pillow eggs are real scary, they are perfect round circles made in a factory somewhere, they taste okay, but I hate to think what kind of additives are in those. Sausages are super greasy, extra cheap and could probably rival the additives in the eggs. The Good: - Suite style room - Sometimes has great rates - Fitness trail right next to the hotel - Close to allot of restaurants (Sweat Tomatoes and Souper Salad are in walking distance in case you are feeling guilty about your artificial breakfast foods) - Comfortable beds - Breakfast while fake offers items you don't normally find at hotels like this - Clean The Bad: - Non-usable Internet - Room layout is such that you will most likely trip over the coffee table coming in or out of your room - Design is a little tired and has a bunch of typical cheap hotel furniture (except the bed). - If you get a room on the far end, it is a hike to the elevator - The remote in my room was for a different brand of TV and was not compatible with my TV.

“Huge, high volume oriented, well located, small rooms” This is an enormous hotel, clearly designed to host large meetings (several at a time), or anything else that brings huge numbers to town.
