The lobby is large, plenty of seating and has a multi station check in desk and three person concierge desk. The staff is polite and helpful, but this is not about personal service. Rooms seem well appointed but small - not Manhattan small, but close. This extends to the bathroom. However, the location is good and the Powell St BART station is a short walk. Just be aware that as you some up from the train with a suitcase, legions of homeless will descend asking if you need directions. On that score, this Hilton has a larger contingent of security officers than I have ever seen in a hotel before. This must be due to size the the number of different ways to enter the building, but it doesn't inspire me to bring my family for a visit. The area around the hotel is okay, not great. Union Square is nearby with a giant Macy's and some great restaurants, but also there are some questionable facilities and hotels nearby. So...it's a very nice hotel in a not wonderful spot, but this isn't the San Francisco it used to be either. For meeting planners, it's great. For individual vacations, not so much. If your business is nearby, then go for it. Good fitness center, serviceable restaurant, Starbucks and so forth. It's a nice property, but is it difficult to separate that experience from the deteriorating urban environment that surrounds it.

“Nothing wrong with this hotel” We were on a road trip and had booked this hotel through Priceline. There is nothing wrong with this establishment and we would recommend it if you are travelling around. The room was large and clean and was like a self contained studio with micro wave, fridge and television. The staff were polite and were helpful in giving directions to the nearest post office. We found that most mid west hotels offered a complimentary breakfast as this one did. The hotel is located about 3 miles from the city centre and around 2 miles from the airport. It has a number of fast food chain restaurants in the area.

“Aging hotel with poor infrastructure saved by good staff” Stayed here for 4 nights last week on business. The hotel is clearly old with things constantly going wrong. The saving grace is the staff who seem to work well to fix the constant problems: Checked in to find no lights working. Managed to call down to reception and an engineer appeared within 2 minutes, and then re appeared minutes later to change the bulbs. The room itself (331) overlooked a roof full of air conditioning units and did not have a proper window. Instead it had a “concrete bunker” style window with only a slit to look out of, which was ridiculous. Apparently all the rooms on the third floor on that side are like that. Complained by phone to front desk and within 5 minutes someone had arrived with a key to a better room. The engineer also made sure the room was better before he left. The strange in-room safe (under the mini bar) malfunctioned twice and failed to open, each time when I needed something from it in a hurry. Both times various engineers showed up, and fixed it but in the end I gave up and stopped using it. The room and decor were functional but rather tired looking and the chair was falling apart. The infrastructure of the hotel itself also looks dated and it could do with a total renovation. The wifi was also not great and quite slow. In summary I would not particularly recommend this hotel, although in an emergency it would do and it is clean. I have to say that without the good will of the staff the hotel would be a complete disaster.

“Beautiful Hotel In Great Downtown Setting” We really enjoyed our stay at this beautiful property. The rooms, furniture, bed, lobby, etc. were absolutely beautiful and immaculate. The only problem I had was paying $28/nite for parking (they only have valet). Dog friendly!

“Schönes Hotel um San Francisco zu entdecken” Das Beresford Arms ist ein gutes Hotel um die Stadt zu erkunden. Drei Blocks vom berühmten Union Square entfernt, findet man ein wirklich angenehmes Ambiente zu einem guten Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis. Die Zimmer sind sauber, auch wenn nicht unbedingt top-modern, aber vollkommen ausreichend. Morgens gibt es ein typisch amerikanische "Frühstück" bestehend aus Kaffee/Tee und etwas süßem Gebäck. Auf jeden Fall ganz nett und man kann schnell etwas snacken wenn man an den kostenlos zur Verfügung stehenden Computern seine E-Mails checkt. Das Personal war sehr nett und hilfsbereit und der Preis hat mich positiv überrascht.

“Only OK” The room rate was a really good price. The room itself is OK, needs updating. The AC couldn't keep the room cool and you couldn't adjust it any lower. There is a charge for internet in the rooms....seriously who charges for internet? Only some guests receive free breakfast and the pool area is nice.

“Bewitched, bewildered, bedazzled” After my trip to NY, Los Angeles was our next stop in the US vacation and I picked Sofitel Los Angeles, just to compare the other Sofitel hotels. After the slight disappointment with the NY branch, my expectations on the LA version was at an all time low. Until I saw the hotel. It was beyond my expectations to see a grander version of Sofitel - from the interior design of the lobby to the concierge, to the restaurant. And the room was large, with rain shower in a large (huge) shower area. Of course, there was no more bath tub, but who needs an itsy bitsy bath tub when it's not going to be used? This was a more practical hotel design and the rates were surprisingly 2/3 the rates of what I paid for in Sofitel New York, considering that I had to pay for parking and internet at their LA hotel. While it may not be at the heart of the Kodak Theater or the heart of wherever you want to be in LA, let me say that for travelers to LA - you will need to rent a car! There is no use going to LA and not driving. Finally, was the service. Unlike the snooty staff in the New York branch of Sofitel, the people in the LA branch were really really nice, especially the staff at the restaurant. They remember you by face, by name, and tell you that you don't have to tip them anymore as it is part of the service bill (surprised!) and that there was that warm smile that would greet you at the beginning of the day. After shopping, partying, and having fun in the city - there was a place to come "home" to.

“Excellent Guest Experience” My wife and I stayed at the Crescent Court on February 1, 2008. The hotel is located in the Uptown Arts District. We had dinner at Nobu, a Japanese restaurant located within the hotel. At Nobu, we recommend the Omasake “chef’s tasting menu”. At $95 per person, we enjoyed 9 courses, each presented with a description on the chef’s preparation. If Japanese cuisine is not to your liking, then located adjacent to the hotel is The Capital Grille. Across the street are Truluck’s Seafood restaurant and Bice, an Italian restaurant. There’s a Starbucks located in the corner of the Crescent Court. Within a mile or so is Rosewood’s famous Mansion on Turtle Creek and the new Ritz-Carlton with Dean Ferring’s signature restaurant, voted best new restaurant of 2007 by Esquire Magazine. We had booked a standard guest room, #445, at $320/night. Parking was additional at $20/night. When we pulled up to the Crescent valets attacked the car, check-in was a snap, and bellman were right there to wisk us up to our guest room. Although a small guest room, it was nicely appointed, similar to The Mansion on Turtle Creek, and as nice as many Four Seasons or Ritz-Carltons. My wife said the spa was great. She had a Swedish massage and a facial and said the therapists were outstanding. LaGina was her massage therapist, and only works on Saturdays. She’s been at the Crescent for 8 years. My wife recommends that you request LaGina if you are there on a Saturday. We live in the area, about 45 minutes away, so we like to get away to Dallas every now and then. We’ve stayed at The Mansion, The Adolphus with dinner in the French Room, and the Crescent Court. We’ve had dinner at Dean Ferring’s, and perhaps we’ll return for a stay at the Ritz-Carlton and another dinner at Ferring’s. I recommend that you compare pricing between the Mansion, Ritz-Carlton and the Crescent Court. They are all very nice. I hope this review is helpful.

“Good Choice for Conferences” I was attending a conference at the hotel and asked to be upgraded to the club level. (Yes, there was an additional charge.) No problem--but the clerk had not disclosed that she had placed me in a room suitable for handicapped individuals, so the bathroom shower had no barrier between it and anything else, making it a bit of a challenge to shower for four days without flooding the floor. I also noted the ceiling above the sink and vanity was in disrepair. I also did not feel the room had been well cleaned, as there were small scraps on the carpet and some kind of human nose product on one of the big pillows on my bed. I should have complained, but I was exhausted and proceeded over the several days to get sick due to the sheer number of sick people staying at the hotel. (Certainly NOT the hotel's problem, but when a guest sneezes in the packed elevator without covering his mouth and you still have 12 floors to go, you just know you're in trouble.) I will say that after that first night, Housekeeping did get my room cleaned each day at the time I requested and did replace all the sheets, including the soiled pillowcases that had greeted me. I will make a pitch for the club level if you are there on a weekday. Monday through Friday morning you have a lovely breakfast with amazing pastries and even smoked fish with accompaniments. Honor bar and lots of appetizers in the afternoon. Sweets in the evening. Note that the evening appetizers and treats cease after Thursday night and the club is locked down after Friday breakfast and over the weekends. Why do Marriott hotels do this? I am accustomed to 24/7 clubs (Starwood, Sofitel, for example) and it is nothing short of annoying not to be able to go have a coffee or lounge on a couch on weekends. Since there was no breakfast in the lounge on Saturday, I went to the restaurant with a colleague. They really pushed the small buffet, which had nothing to recommend it, but we ordered off the menu. Minor screw ups with potatoes instead of fruit with the Denver omelette, and the corned beef and poached eggs were decent, if not too salty from the meat. I'd rate breakfast as average. I had lunch at the bar one day: really amazing garden veggie burger made with beets, if you are a beet person. Mac and cheese excellent. Service at the bar, mediocre. It was more important for the bartender to shovel ice for a long time instead of tend to those of us who sat at the bar. One day we had a banquet-style luncheon. Meh. Some sort of seasoned chicken on lettuce that was supposed to be a Southwestern style salad. As a conference facility, this place is good. I attended sessions in an array of room sizes and the chairs, acoustics, and view of the stage and audiovisual equipment was great. Overall, I stayed here solely because the conference was held here and I did not want to schlep around downtown Denver in the cold. In the past I have stayed at the elegant Hotel Teatro when my conference has been at the Denver Convention Center. Next time, I'll return to that hotel.

“立地良し、清潔 大規模ホテルでサービスはそれなり” 2012年1月にニューヨークへ観光に行ったときに、1泊しました。 立地は、地下鉄E線の7th Ave.駅から歩いて3~4分と便利なところにあり、地下鉄でニューヨーク観光をしようという方には、良い立地です。玄関とフロントは、東側の6th Ave側にあります。 東西はほぼひとブロック分近くあり、低層階には多くのバンケットルームがあり、毎日企業のカンファレンスやセミナーなどが開かれているようで、ロビー周りは朝から午後にかけては、落ち着かない感じがあります。 部屋は、改装されてから余り年月がたっていないと思え、シンプルで清潔感があります。1キングのスタンダードルームでしたが、ニューヨークの多くのホテルと同様、余り広くはありません。バスタブもありませんが、機能的には十分な部屋です。ただ、値段を考えると、コストパフォーマンスは良くありません。高いです。 私たちは、昼時にチェックイン、早朝にチェックアウトだったので、特に気になりませんでしたが、夕方チェックインや朝食後のチェックアウトは、規模が大きいだけに、フロントやロビー周りはごった返すのは容易に想像できます。EXPRESS CHECK OUTなどを有効に使ったほうが良いと思います。 夕方から夜にホテルの53stを挟んだ向かい側に店を出す、”Halal Guys"という、ベンダー(屋台)のチキンオーバーライスはとてもおいしいです。夜中に小腹がすいたときにお勧めです。かなりボリュームがあるので、2人で1皿でちょうど良いかと思います。 歩いて行ける近くには、MOMAがあります。それ以外は主だった観光施設は歩くには少し遠いので、地下鉄を使ってNY観光をしようという人に向いていると思います。

“Overall a good experience” My partner and I visited New York last weekend for a trade show and some theater, so we decided to stay in the Times Square area. Based on good reviews here we chose the Pearl. We paid a pretty steep rate of $500 after realizing there were no bargains to be found in NY for a Saturday night. We were very pleased to be upgraded to a beautiful full suite, and our room was nicely equipped (Keurig coffee maker, iron and board, microwave, and bar sink) with lots of storage, good lighting, and comfortable seating. Everything looked brand new and spotless. I'd call the quality and look "one step up from Ikea" - not bad but certainly not really luxurious. The free breakfast was welcome and serviceable - if you've ever stayed at one of the HK hotels in NY like the Casablanca, Giraffe, Library, or Elysee you would recognize the expanded continental menu. Check-in and check-out were smooth, everything went well. I've got three negatives on my list: 1. The aircon was quite buzzy, surprising for new construction; 2. When I switched to the hand-shower the overhead rainshower would not stop raining on me (I know, it sounds petty); 3. And the big one, the perpetual thorn in every hotel guest's side - the SEVEN DOLLAR bottle of fancy Voss water that sits on the shelf as the only alternative to tap. Please...can't they just put a nice ordinary bottle of water in the room as an amenity? All in all this is a nice upbeat brandy-new hotel in the middle of the Times Square and Broadway action; it's perfectly nice but of course it doesn't set out to compete with The Mark or The Carlyle. It's a good bet especially if you can snag a favorable rate.

“Great stay at the Sofitel” I booked the Sofitel for $113 a night on Hotwire, which is a pretty good deal to begin with. I had called a few weeks prior to arrival to ask for a high floor room and a king bed. When we arrived, they informed us that Hotwire bookings are for "standard" rooms, floors 14 and below. They could not grant our request, but they did give us a room on the 14th floor with a terrific view of the Hancock Tower. I was very pleased with how this was handled. Some hotels (especially upscale ones) will treat you like second-class guests if you book through Hotwire or Priceline. I feel the Sofitel treated our request with respect and did the next best thing to giving us an actual upgrade. This earned major points from me right from the start. The location of the hotel is great, right between Rush and State streets on Chestnut St. This means you are just steps from a great breakfast at Tempo Cafe, great pizza at Pizanos, groceries at the Potash market, bars and restaurants on Rush St, and Michigan Ave shopping. The lobby is not huge, but has a welcoming vibe...a little bit dark and classy feel to it, with fresh flowers all around. The restaurant is on your left when you enter. We didn't dine there, but they do have free coffee and tea at the restaurant bar in the morning. There are 5 elevators, so we never had to wait for one. The room, 1411, was excellent. It is of medium size with a large bathroom. The room has a comfy king bed, a Bose radio with iPhone connection, large windows, soft carpet, and FREE wireless internet. The internet is not blazing fast, but it is free. The bathroom is spacious and very clean, with a separate walk-in shower and bathtub. The L'Occitane bath products are excellent. The housekeeping staff is great. You never even notice them, they are so efficient. I've wanted to stay at the Sofitel for years, and it didn't disappoint. It compares favorably to our stays at the Hilton Conrad and the Westin River North, also in Chicago. We would definitely stay here again, especially with a great price on Hotwire.

“Great location, spacious rooms, pleasant staff” Stayed here for weekend with my three young children. While not the obvious choice as family-friendly (the stylish contemporary bar in the lobby is quite a scene), the rooms are spacious and it is only two blocks from the glorious Reading Terminal Market. We were able to check in early but our room, while large, faced a brick wall (room 837). The kids weren't happy with the view. Later that evening when my youngest was taking a shower, he screamed so I ran into the bathroom. I couldn't really understand what he was screaming about until I saw the huge waterbug crawling up my leg. Yikes!! Housekeeping sent two guys to kill it but I asked to be moved and was, immediately. Room 653 has a great view of the city and my kids were much happier. Our rates were pricier than I would have liked, but unfortunately we chose to come to Philly the same weekend as Penn graduation. Le Meridien is an easy walk from Love park (across the street!), City Hall, Logan Square, The Franklin Institute, Chinatown, and Independence Mall.

“Convenient to Market and Union Square, Balance of Style and Value” I have stayed at several hotels in SF, including others in the Joie de Vivre group. This hotel is more modest - an older property which was spruced up with nice linens, paint, large flat screens, and high-end toiletries. That being said, the walls are thick and the interior rooms are very quiet, affording excellent night sleep. The gym is tiny (essentially one of the smaller guestrooms with one eliptical, one stationary bike, and one treadmill. Staff are very nice. Extremely convenient to BART, Muni and walking through Union Square and to Ferry Building.

“A GREAT CHOICE IN DC” We loved our room at the St Regis. We had a large, comfy bed & a perfectly redone room. All staff was friendly & helpful. Great location, a couple blocks away from the white house. The bathroom was beautiful, we only wish they had a bathtub or jacuzzi. We will stay here again on our next DC trip if we can get another good deal.
“普通・・・” ヒルトンブランドの最高峰ブランド「conrad」にしては 部屋も食事も普通・・・・ barが人気あるみたいだったが、それにしても 何から何まで普通だった。 決して、悪いホテルではないがあくまで 値段通りのサプライズがない普通のホテルだった。

“Light is dim...so don't fall into the lounge area” This is an excellent hotel in a great area of Toddlin' town. Good service, elegant and clean and overlooking the Chicago River in downtown. So now that I have praised this Westin, I'm allowed to quibble. The theme of the hotel is "calm...refresh...sooth...relax in health" etc. I think this theme is a little self-serving. For example, the good-looking woman on the TV tells you to take a deep breath...so I figure maybe they pipe in some Oxygen to the lobby and rooms...but no....she is just telling you that after extensive "research" they have decided that it is healthy if the hotel is non-smoking...like...duh...a non-smoking hotel these days...what a concept. Ok...so then to "soothe" you the lights are very dim in the lobby. Is that in keeping with the "soothe and calm and relax" theme or is it just to save electricity? Whatever, the shiny black tile floors are identical with the shiny tile black stairs leading down into the recessed lounge/bar area. So, bathed in this eerie, dim light, you need to be really careful descending into the lounge area, even long before you've had your first drink. Of course, there are plenty of staff greeters and concierges hanging in the lobby to be at your attention. Though perhaps they are there to just dust you off after you've plunged unceremoniasly into the bar area. The hotel is expensive and so is the braekfast buffet which costs $17 . There are a lot of fruity dishes at the buffet and healthy cereals (Again, I guess, in keeping with the "healthy, soothing theme"), but for that price the only eggs are scrambled and whether they are hot depends on how well the servers replenish those eggs. (one morning they did and one morning they didn't). Anyway, the sausages and bacon are great and the coffee is terrific. As I said, this area of the loop in Chicago is a great place to be with restaurants, bars and shops filled with really nice mid-western people. So, depsite my quibbles, you have fine service, elegance and location. It is hard to beat that!

“Right on the River Walk” The hotel is in a great location right on the river walk, with easy access to the Alamo, shops, restaurants etc. There is a multi-storey car park (self-parking) on site. The reception staff were very friendly and helpful. We arrived early, but they were happy to store bags and called my mobile as soon as a room was available. Initially we were given a room by the elevator. We were not happy with this and reception changed it for us immediately. Our room was comfortable and well equipped. There is a buffet breakfast and a cocktail hour "kick back" with food, which are included in the rate. Service very friendly and efficient. Not keen on the polystyrene plates and plastic cutlery. There is a swimming pool on the roof, with a few sunbeds, tables and chairs. A real bonus for some late afternoon relaxation.
“Comfortable rooms close to airport” Its a fifity years building, however rooms are comfortable, clean and completely refurbished. KIndly staff. Good service of buses to airport.

“THE place to stay in DC!” I just finished my second 4 night stay at Hilton Garden Inn DC - one in July and one this week. I travel fairly frequently to DC and this is the best place to stay for a solo business traveler! The rooms have everything I need to take care of business, including free high speed internet and free printing via a remote link. The staff - every single one of them - are helpful and friendly. Particularly the restaurant folks - they remembered me from my previous stay and knew my preferences for breakfast and room service! The room I had on the 9th floor was next to the elevator but I didn't hear a thing. I had a "view" of an ugly inner courtyard, but it was quiet and I didn't come for a good view - I wanted to sleep after a long day working. Check-in was quick and efficient - I was in my room within 5 minutes of walking in the door. Housekeeping was outstanding - I wrote the housekeeper a note about my allergy to feathers and she removed all feather pillows and replaced with hypoallergenic ones. She also brought extra wash cloths and left plenty of the Neutrogena toiletries. Room service was fast and pick up of tray afterwards was done immediately. The food was great - I had the best turkey burger ever! Breakfast was $2 cheaper if you went before 7 AM - they opened at 6:30 and the selection and quality of food was well worth the $10. Did I mention the staff? Far and above - the entire crew was wonderful. I even received a call from one of the managers asking me if I was pleased with the services and thanking me for being a return customer. I've already got two more stays booked there in next two months! Several have mentioned that there weren't any nearby restaurants and that's just not true. Stroll down 15th or 14th Street towards the National Mall and there are restaurants galore! Yes, you have to walk a few blocks, but a taxi is cheap if you don't feel like walking. And the Metro is right there - what more could you want? You can also get water, sodas and snacks at the CVS two blocks away. The refrigerator and microwave in the room make it easly to stock up. The location is one of the best in DC for business as well as sight-seeing.

“Not a pleasant experience” We've stayed at about a dozen hotels all over Manhattan and never really had a bad experience until we came here. The check-in was long, tedious and unpleasant. The woman that checked us in was just plain rude and seemed to absolutely hate her job. The first room they put us in was an absolute horrible neightmare. The decor was run down, the room was so small, you couldn't even turn around in it, you had to back onto the toilet because the bathroom was so small. Nowhere to put a suitcase or a bag or a cosmetics case. But the worst thing was the horrendous noise from the airconditioning units outside our window. NOT that our aircon even worked!! it was SO hot! We were sweating all night and hardly had any sleep, between the loud noise and heat. The noise was like a big truck running outside the window the entire time. And our view was a big wall with windows and aircon units. You coulnd't even open your window to let some fresh air in, because the other windows were 10cm from ours and people could see inside our room!! no wonder they've had thefts in this hotel, it'd be so easy to climb from one room to another. In the morning, I went and complained as we had been in NYC for almost three weeks and we were about to fly back overseas and we wanted our last night in NYC to be pleasant. So after much trouble, they moved us to a room that was much better and a bit bigger - it faced the outside and we could see lincoln centre. And there was no aircon noise and the room temperature was manageable. There were many other irks with this hotel, like when we had to call and ask for things, it would take between 45min-1hr for someone to bother to come around and bring it to us. For example, we asked for ice, 45min later someone showed up. We asked for an iron and ironing board.. after half an hour we rang to ask for it as we really needed it to iron our clothes before going out to a restaurant that we had a booking for. But it STILL took them another half an hour to bring the iron up. How disappointing. The only good thing about this hotel for us was the location, right across from central park and also a great spot if you want to catch the train to the airport. this was a breeze, we rolled our suitcases to 59th street (i think - at the SW corner of central park) and it has elevators here, so you can go down with ease and catch the train to the airport. Pity our last few nights in NYC were ruined by our experience in this hotel.

“Harbor Court- very nice and relaxed” My girlfriend and I stayed at the Harbor Court on the weekend of december 26-28 for two nights. WIth both of us being kimpton in touch members, we received an email from kimpton with a pretty good promotion. So we booked the room, and then after reading tripadvisor, contacted the manager Jason Stone via email and hw was generous enough to offer us a complimentary room upgrade to a king. Unfortunately Jason wasnt available to personally thank while we stayed at the hotel. Dulce and John at the front were very helpful and friendly. The wine hour is a great kimpton staple and I really enjoyed the living room area of the Harbor court. It was pretty quiet and relaxing even though many guests were enjoying the wine hour. Definitely a difference with the other kimpton hotels union square hotels that seem to have too much traffic. Had dinner accross the street at sinbads and also a couple doors down at mexico df. both highly recommended. Satuday was able to go to the farmers marker right accross the street which was fun. Also the F line streetcar runs very near the hotel, so you can take that to get to fishermans wharf or union square in no time.

“Good Experience, But Not Really a 3.5-Star Property” The Wyndham Garden Hotel would be a winner if it were a 3-star hotel. However, as a 3.5-star hotel, it’s much more average. It is clear that time, money, and effort have been invested in this hotel, though, so I will give it the benefit of the doubt with my rating. I chose the Wyndham for my recent stay in Austin because hotels downtown and along South Congress were simply too expensive for 3 nights. I paid less than half as much to stay at this hotel, and I was able to invest my savings in a good time around town. Hotel staff members were friendly, and the lobby and common areas were clean and nicely decorated in a musical theme. My fourth-floor room had been recently renovated and was well appointed. Highway noise was audible but not overwhelming. The only disappointment was the small bathroom, which noticeably lacked counter space and headroom. The premises are comparable to any number of airport hotels. The pool is pleasant for its size, and the Jacuzzi is attractive and comfortable. Too bad almost no hotel guests utilized them during my stay. The fitness center is large but poorly equipped: While cardio machines and free weights are available, weight machines are completely absent. The surrounding neighborhood is wholly unappealing, but it does not seem unsafe. A rental car is essential when staying at the Wyndham, so do make sure to stay elsewhere if you won’t have one on hand. The hotel offers free parking and free Wi-Fi, and breakfast is available for an additional charge.

“Not Clean” The location of this hotel is good; just eight blocks from Times Square. The lobby is nice, but that's about it. The hallways and rooms are old and need cleaning and/or remodeling. Our room and bathroom were small. The room did not feel clean, and the bathroom wasn't clean (especially the sink and tub, which had mold). The TV had poor reception.

“Two hotels in one” This is really like two different hotels in one. There is the tower part of the hotel which is very typical of any Crowne Plaza (nice), and then there are the "Courtyard Rooms", which I am reviewing. The Courtyard rooms have outside entrances and the inside faces the pool. Nice little balconies on the poolside. Our Corporate Lodging card is only good for the Courtyard rooms, but the price is VERY good. Inside the room was a little ragged around the edges but clean. Front desk was incredibly helpful and responsive. Beds and interior finishings (albeit a little worn) are just like any other Crowne Plaza. Good nights sleep, for the price I'd stay there again.

“Large rooms, great location” I stayed here for 4 nights for a business trip, the location was fantastic. I had a corner room on the 40th floor, very quiet (I could barely hear street noise and I didn't experience noisey hallways). The rooms were quite large & the water pressure in the shower was fantastic. The staff was very friendly - I received two packages while staying there and the staff was sure to alert me. One word of advise - breakfast is quite expensive (they nearly force you to just order the buffet). After making that mistake on the first day, I just walked across the street to Starbucks (though there are a number of restaurants close by since).

“Four Thumbs Down” If you're thinking of staying here...think again! And then RUN!! I've stayed at other Schrager hotels and had a nice experience, although the rooms are usually small. But here, you get to experience the rudest staff on planet Earth, and pay a pretty penny to do so. A smoke detector started beeping the first night we were there (dead battery...great!!); we called the desk before going out to dinner. When we got back, it was still beeping. We called again; "someone would come right up." It beeped all night, so in the morning I went to the desk and complained. Got the same story, which by then was sounding pretty stale. Needless to say, when we checked out after TWO NIGHTS, it had never been taken care of. The hairdryer in our room was broken, and there was a terrifically loud party going on in the outdoor courtyard till the wee hours of the morning. I don't mean just somewhat loud, but so loud that if I hadn't purchased earplugs to drown out the beeping smoke detector, I could not possibly have slept....we were on a high floor and the decibel level was unbelievable. And to top it off, when we went out for dinner and attempted to use the front door of the hotel to come back in, we were rudely intercepted and asked "What are you doing?" (No, we were not dressed like hillbillies or street people.) When we recovered from our stunned state enough to respond that we were GUESTS (remember them?? No, I didn't think so) we were told we'd have to use the side entry, as there was a private party going on. Well, excuse ME! We're only paying guests trying to get to our room and get some sleep! Upon checkout, when I was asked if our stay had been okay, I answered that no, it had not, and explained about the beeping smoke detector, the broken hairdryer, and the noise. There were NO apologies, NO offers of some kind of compensation, and NO chance of my ever darkening their door again. RUN! RUN LIKE THE WIND!

“All form - no function; It's Pottery Barn once you get past the lobby” I'm a Starwood Preferred traveler who ususally books Westins, but we thought, what the heck and booked this W instead for a weekend in Chicago. First - five bell staff standing around joking with each other, each more glamorous than the next, couldn't be bothered to get our bags, but they did spend a lot of time high-fiving attractive metrosexuals who walked by from the neighborhood. Check In - very nice front desk staff, but the clubby music was booming so loud that we couldn't hear her (at all), and she wasn't able to speak up - so we used hand gestures during most of our check-in conversation. Lobby - is truly spectacular deco architecture with interesting gobo's and light shows layered on top of it. First room - was so small we called down to the front desk and told them we thought we were in an Edgar Allen Poe novel. I literally had a panic attack of claustrophobia. What designer in their right mind would paint the walls of a 10 x 10 room brown and black, and the 9' ceiling black? We did NOT book through expedia or a discount broker, we booked through the Starwood.com site, and I expect that when a room is bizarrely small, the square footage should be listed so the customer can make an informed choice. Front desk moved us right away, and charming and cheerful bellman zipped upstairs to help us. We were moved into a much larger room - but still with the hideous dark paint and chic but incompetently designed lighting. Things that worked: amazing bed and linens, fantastic room service staff, high end bath amenities. Wonderful shower heads. Free, nice coffee in the lobby in the a.m. with convenient to-go cups. Things that were just plain stupid: no phone book or reference materials in the room - you have to call the help line for EVERYTHING. Extra toilet paper is in the hall closet - duh, do you think that's a convenient place when you need it? No hook in the chic bathroom so you have to put your robe down on a wet countertop - not so glamorous. NO VENTILATION IN THE BATHROOM - how romantic it is NOT to have bathroom smells wafting through the room. Most of the furniture was Pottery Barn esque painted the oppressive black. Very difficult to manage temperature in the room - the whole system is centralized and there's no individual control. Overall, Kimpton hotels are just as stylish but much more intelligently designed to actually function and not just look good. My advice - if you need to sleep this stylishly, go to a Kimpton. If you love the groovy lobby of this W hotel, stay someplace else and come here for a drink.

“Good location; friendly staff; average on the rest” Silversmith Hotel is an average hotel in a great location with a friendly staff. You are only a five minute walk from the Art Institute and Millennium Park and ten to fifteen minutes from Wacker Drive and the Chicago River. In terms of getting there, you are right next to multiple L routes and a couple of blocks from the blue L line that takes you to O'Hare. I drove my car to the hotel to drop off and pick up my luggage and the valet parkers and busmen were very friendly and allowed us to park our car short term in the valet parking area. Check in and checkout were handled smoothly and other questions were answered by friendly people at the main desk. The room was good-sized with the sleep quarters in a separate room from the bathroom and a pretty small living room. I liked the Arts and Crafts furniture. Bathroom had very good water pressure and was just fine, as were the bath towels. They followed their stated environmental policies and did not wash our linens or towels as requested. So what makes me give this an average rating? Even though we were on the side away from the L, we could still hear it from our bedroom (that doesn't bother me, but it did bother my wife). There were no shades to pull closed so the light came pouring in. The mattress was not very supportive, nor the pillows. The Internet was free and was available both wired and wireless. Unfortunately, the service was kind of poky and spotty. I tried going back and worth between wired and wireless, but had to give up a couple of times because it was taking too long. Business office was pretty sad. There were two pretty old computers that inexplicably used the wireless signal and not wired access. That limited its speed. In addition, only one computer could use the printer at any one time. As cheap as computers are at this point, I couldn't figure out why they didn't just buy some newer computers with better capabilities. The T.V.s in the bedroom and living room were 25" CRTs and the remote didn't really work for one of them. It also turned on at a bracingly high volume. There were no recycling options in the building for paper, plastic bottles, plastic bags, etc. The power went out on Friday morning (utility issue, not their fault) and an elevator got stuck. It was still stuck when we left on Monday. All in all, I would stay at the hotel again, but given it was in the same price range as much nicer conference hotels, I would think twice if I could get into a nicer place.

“Finally - Well-managed Hipness” After so many disastrous stays at various W and Ian Schrager properties, I became skeptical in the "hip hotel experience" - until I stayed at 60 Thompson this past weekend. Interiors (lighting in particular) were chic and took advantage of all the site had to offer. The location was much better than Soho Grand and Tribeca Grand. Service was perhaps the best I've seen in new york boutique hotels thus far - of course, it's nothing like the Peninsula but the staff was cheerful and professional. We stayed at a Deluxe Room and it was as spacious as the generous marble bathroom. I look forward to returning to this well-managed hip hotel.

“Muy buena opción” El hotel pertenece a los hoteles históricos y se siente el glamour desde el ingreso al mismo. Además tienen ahora una camopaña que cuenta sobre las celebridades y los eventos importantes que han sucedido en este hotel desde hace muchos años. Esta situado en una zona envidiable y sin tráfico desde el aeropuerto se hacen menos de veinte minutos. Hay una entrada al metro cerca del hotel. El lobby es agradable, espacioso y con mucho espacio para sentarse y disfrutarlo. EL registro en mi caso fue amable y ágil, aun cuando no ofrecieron hablar en español, pero todo muy bien. El hotel tiene dos áreas: el área principal que se encuentra sobre el lobby y un edificio anexo mas nuevo que queda aproximadamente a 100 metros del lobby dentro del mismo hotel. Las habitaciones (del área nueva) no son demasiado grandes, la calidad del amueblado es buena, tiene inclusive pantallas de lcd de 32 pulgadas, cuentan con cafetera y un pequeño servibar. En mi habitación había dos camas dobles una de ellas tenía el colchón por demás desgastado y era muy incómodo dormir en esa cama, la otra excelente. El baño con tina, muy limpio y sin detalles. Realmente muy bueno, creo que las habitaciones de la zona principal son mejores,

“Nice hotel, excellent location” This is the second time I've stayed at this hotel for business and think this is a great hotel - staff is very professional and the property and rooms are very clean and well kept. The location is excellent - it is just a block away from the Magnificient mile and close to restaurants and sights. With my stay this time, I noticed this hotel has become a totally smoke- free hotel - great for us non smokers. For smokers, there is a dedicated area in outside front of the hotel for smoking. This is also one of the few hotels that actually don't bother you or try to enter your room when you place a "do not disturb" sign on your door. Overall, great hotel for a reasonable price.

“Great location” I stayed at this hotel recently for a couple nights during a business trip. It is a solid choice in a great part of the City. Located between 50th and 51st on Lex Ave, it is easily accessible on the Subway and close to all of Midtown. I was able to reach all of my meetings and other destinations with ease. The hotel is generally quite nice. The lobby area includes a nice restaurant/bar area. Check-in was relatively efficient and the warm Doubletree cookie never hurts. My room was large for NYC standards. The neighborhood is relatively quiet even though it is close to everything. Sleeping was easy from a noise standpoint. Not a lot of hallway traffic or noise. The bed was less comfortable than most Hilton-brand hotels. It was kind of firm and detracted from the sleep experience. The bathroom was functional and nice overall. Room services was prompt and the food was good. Drinks in the bar/restaurant were enjoyable, even at NYC typical prices.

“I just can't escape from this place...” This was my third visit to the Doubletree, though not by choice. I had a rather uninspired visit to this hotel, which I wrote about in a review titled "Look behind the facade - a second stay" that was posted on this site back in July. Recently, a chance opened up to take a short trip to NY February 7th to the 10th of this year. I lept at the chance, but became kind of nervous when I heard that the person arranging the trip had booked me at the Doubletree. I really had no desire to stay there again, as not only did I stay there two times in a row previously, but I found the hotel to be rather cold and impersonal in style and tone with no real character, the larger than normal rooms and location being its only advantages. And anyone who read my earlier review knows that I was more than a little disappointed with the overall service I received. Nonetheless, I could not turn the opportunity down, and prepared myself for another visit to this hotel that I seemingly can't get away from. The hotel itself was pretty much the same as last time. No real style or character that sets itself apart from the hundreds of other hotels in the city, a somewhat impersonal front desk staff that couldn't seem to care less and don't even say "hello" to you when you walk up to check in, and a somewhat bland, yet large and comfortable room waiting for me. I was lucky enough to get a corner room on the 36th floor this time, which was far enough away from street level, so the room was completely quiet. Last time, I was only on the 16th, and could sometimes here muffled street sounds, or people stomping about in the halls outside my room. Maybe the walls were thicker this time around or something, because I heard not a sound from outside my suite. The room seemed to be kept up better as well. There was no mirror smudged with dust and hand prints like the ones on my last visit. Best of all, the housekeeping staff seemed to be more on the ball this time around. Maybe it was the little extra tip I left for them. Whatever the reason, this short visit seemed to go a lot more smoothly than when I visited them just last summer. That's not to say there were no problems. As mentioned earlier, the front desk and even the concierge need to figure out how to smile, or at least make you feel like you're not wasting their time by talking to them. Also, the elevators were perhaps a bit too quick for their own good. While I appreciate the fact that I never had to wait more than 20 seconds for one to come, once I got on, it was another story. The elevator would zoom up and down at speeds so quickly that my ears would often pop. It got quite annoying having to deal with the pain in my ears everytime I got on board. I know I'm not the only one who experienced this, as one or two other people also complained about their ears popping whenever the elevator was in motion. I think they need to somehow adjust the speed a little. I'm still not thoroughly impressed with the Doubletree, but aside from the elevators, there was nothing really to sour the experience. The rooms are still a good size and a good value, the beds are still comfortable, and the location still can't be beat for theatre going as the four shows I saw during my stay (Woman in White, Sweeney Todd, The Color Purple, The Odd Couple) were all in very short walking distance. The big problem this hotel has is that it just has no real distinction of style. The rooms, except for the size, look like something out of my local Holiday Inn, and everything just looks so bland and ordinary. If comfort and size are the only things you're looking for, you'll probably get your money's worth. But, if you're looking for a real New York hotel experience that sets itself above the norm, you won't find it here. I know I won't stay here again, as I've already made reservations at a different hotel for my next visit in October. The Doubletree rates as being strictly average in my book.

“Best Hampton I've stayed at” What an excellent hotel. I stay at many, many Hamptons -- and this is now the best I've been to. My suite was huge, clean, and comfortable. That it was only $99/night (booked through Hampton's own website) is unbelievable. Their beds are super comfortable. Service is top notch and very friendly. The location is good, in that it's away from Fort Worth traffic, but you do occasionally get airplane noise from Alliance. There are a few places to eat across the highway -- mostly fast food, other than very good barbecue at Sonny Bryan's. The hotel serves a typical Hampton breakfast, but this is the only Hampton I've been to that also serves a complimentary light dinner. My only complaint would be their internet service. It's wireless, and you login with a password provided at checkin. I was kicked off several times a day and taken back to the login screen. This is a common problem at Hampton Inns (wireless is restricted by distance -- why even require a login?) Overall, superb hotel -- highly recommended!

“A wonderful experiance!” We booked at another hotel a block away and spent a unhappy night. We walked over to the Talbott and the courtiest staff showed us a room and we booked the rest of our stay. The room was very attractive and well furnished with double sinks in the bathroom. The tub is large and the shower a pleasure. The location was quiet as requested. The staff was always cheerful and very helpful. Tim and Stephanie provide excellent concierge services! The breakfast at the Basil Cafe is a great way to start the day. We travel a lot and appreciate the ambiance of a good hotel. I would highly recommend the Talbott for your stay.

“Go for tea; but stay somewhere else.” I thought the Brown Palace would be the perfect hotel for a mother daughter weekend. I reserved the "executive stateroom" because I believed the two queen beds and sitting area would provide just enough lounging space for my mother and me. The "sitting area" turned out to be a chair next to one of the beds - not at all what I expected based on the room rate I paid and the description provided to me by the hotel's reservations operator. Despite my disappointment with the room, the hotel is worth seeing and high tea is definitely worth experiencing.

“Sun, sea, salt air” The Hendersonville Video team doubled up our per diems to be able to afford this hotel and did so due to the high recommendation of a local. You get what you pay for. The salt air and the view and scent of the ocean made the extra bucks justifiable. Our rooms were somewhat smallish compared to the hotel chain we normally use, but nicely decorated. Staff was top notch. The front desk called us when our car service arrived. A nice touch. The only nit was early morning skateboarders on the walkway along the beach.

“Great value, outstanding breakfast!” My 13 year old daughter and I spent three nights at this newly renovated hotel, sightseeing and relaxing in a king corner suite. The complimentary breakfast spread is amazing but heads up, it gets really crowded. Best to come early and enjoy everything from fresh fruit and yogurt to waffles and bagles to cereals and oatmeal. They even have Jimmy Dean breakfast sandwiches and sausage rolls! The location is terrific for seeing the sites; there is a Metro stop just a couple blocks away, but we walked all over and visited the museums. We even walked back from the Lincoln Memorial -- at 10:30 at night when the DC Tours lady went off and left us. You ought to read that review! Anyway, back to the hotel. Excellent service, spotless room, great location, and comfortable beds. We'll be back, next weekend, in fact!

“A Good Value” My wife and I stayed at the County Inn 2 nights the last week in July 2006. Our room was on the first floor, not far from the indoor pool. The Country Inn looks like a new hotel and it had the amenities many travelers like, including a modern room cooling/heating system, "real" blackout drapes, soundproofing, quality bedding, and high speed wi-fi. The staff were helpful in the business center and at the desk, there was a variety of food at the large breakfast room, and the airport shuttle seemed to always be available. The hotel is located near 7-9 restaurants in a newer area about 10 minutes away from the airport. The only downside is that it is about 25 minutes from the downtown area. But for the price and the quality, we would definitely stay there again.

“Very Enjoyable Week at the JW Marriott” Having stayed previously in the area at the Sheraton Wild Horse Pass and the Westin Kieland, we decided to give the JW Marriott a try. Overall I would give it four stars - nothing blows you away in particular, but it is as advertised, i.e. a resort that caters to business conventions as well as families on vacation. I disliked the $25/night "resort fee" which is a ripoff to me, but more and more hotels seem to be adopting this add-on. I'm not even sure what it covered, and it wasn't even mentioned at check-in though I was aware of it at the time I made my reservation. The only meals we ate the hotel were poolside for lunch, so I can't comment on any of the other restaurants. The poolside service was spotty, despite the area being relatively empty (don't if all the guests were in meetings or whether the 65 degree temperature kept others away from the pool). The pool temperature was great - nicely heated which I find not to be the case at many other resorts. There's also a nice lazy river and water slide for the kids. Plus, the piped in music was unobtrusive in most parts of the pool area except the lazy river. The rooms are nothing special, but they do have flat screen tv's with HD on many channels. The staff was friendly and seemed to be well-trained. Its location is fine - right across the street from the Desert Ridge outdoor mall and right off the 101 Loop which can take you either to other parts of Scottsdale or downtown. Compared to the other two hotels we've stayed at previously, I would put it a notch or two above the Westin Kierland and on par with the Sheraton Wild Horse Pass. If we go back to the area I would consider staying here if the price was right.

“Not for people checking in late!” Despite a call ahead of time ( one day) and a confirmed reservation for a NONSMOKING room, when I arrived at midnight from a West coast afternoon flight, I was given a somewhat nicely decorated room. But the stench from the smoke!!! Arghhh! I marched downstairs, with reservation in hand, and was told, "Sorry, we have NO non-smoking rooms left" As I am allergic to smoke, and can break out in asthma within an hour of being in a room like that I refuesed to stay there. As I was waiting for them to find something for me two other guests showed up, were assigned rooms, and also came marching down to complain of their non-smoking room reservation, and smoking room assignment. They both accepted a rate reduction and a promise to move the next day. As that was not an option for me, after an hour, they located a non-smoking room down the street at the Hilton Garden Inn ( a lesser hotel). Originally they were to 'walk me' for one night only, and I indicated that it was not possible for me to transfer during the day as I had business all day intl the late hours the next day. They agreed to let me stay at the HGI for two nights. MIND YOU THESE HOTELS WERE CHARGING $350/nite + NYC Taxes that brought it to nearly $400 a night. NO WAY JOSE

“Perfect for date night or a girls shopping trip” I love that this hotel is in the middle of it all - restaurants, upscale shopping, and nightlife. We had been to Santana Row in the past and knew if we were ever to return to San Jose that we would most certainly stay at Hotel Valencia. That said, the opportunity did arise and so I booked a room accordingly - for only $140 per night since it was a holiday weekend!!!! Bargain for sure. I love the courtyard, but we went there on a Sunday evening and found that there was no waiter service in the courtyard and also found that the heaters were all out of propane. I stood inside at the bar waiting to order drinks and appetizers for about 15 minutes (the bartenders - 2 of them - were making LOADS of drinks, so they weren't just standing around. . .I guess everyone at the bar arrived at the same time because there weren't that many people in there) and by the time he took my order, he advised me (with a smile) that it was about 1 minute after the expiration of happy hour appetizer prices. . .REALLY???? He saw me standing there for 15 minutes and you'd think he could make a concession to make up for the fact that I was inconvenienced, but NO. That said, we ordered 2 cocktails and 1 soda and took it back up to our room and ordered room service which was just OK at best. Room service staff and front desk staff were awesome. Check in/out was simple. Took my son to the pool Monday morning which was really nice. Beware that the lounge overlooking the mountains overlooks some really noisy air conditioners on a neighboring building - not really relaxing and romantic as they claim it to be. Free breakfast was a treat. While this hotel has the potential to be elegant, it is not quite there - but for the $140 we paid it was definitely worth every penny.

“Good for a sleeping room” We stayed here through a Priceline reservation at $82 plus taxes. We had no complaints whatsoever about the room we were assigned other than the fact we could hear some road noise, as our room faced Century Blvd. We were checked in very quickly, and given a very spacious room with a king sized bed. While the valet parking was very expensive ($26), the service that the valets provided was top notch. We called down just as we were leaving the room, and the car was already in front of the doors. The valets were actually cleaning our car windows as we approached. For what was essentially a sleep and go visit, things went very well, and would be happy to stay here again.

“Our Favorite Place in the Big Expensive City!” We live about two hours outside New York and every once in a while an early business meeting will inspire us to stay overnight. We've tried some other places (like the W Lexington Avenue) but have really come to consider the Westin our "home" hotel. Whether NY small (like London small!) or splurge-worthy corners (our last room, fabulous) the rooms are well appointed, sleek and contemporary without being...over the top...and cozy. The bedding is superb. Our last trip -- last week -- my husband booked a corner room on a high floor (it was about $475, a bit of a splurge) but we loved it! The room had a foyer, and then wrap around windows; the main part of the room was outfitted with flat screen, desk, benches, nice bathroom.... One caveat: we've eaten at the hotel's restaurant -- Don Shula's -- a few times. It's a typical steakhouse (where your sides are separate) and the food is excellent but the prices are a bit breathtaking, particularly for wine. We couldn't find a bottle under $44 (and that one was out of stock) -- and few were under $70. I realize it's NY and it's an expense account restaurant but still.... Service was also totally chaotic (and it wasn't even busy yet) though we did appreciate the gesture, by the maitre'd (she was a woman, not sure what you call her); she'd overheard us say we were celebrating our anniversary and arranged for us to be surprised with a lovely chocolate dessert. What a nice touch! Made up for the early roughness of service. The bar at the Westin is fun -- quite a scene -- and you can order snack food there. We might try that next time. And of course, a whole range of restaurants are nearby. The lobby has free wireless (it's kinda' pricey in the rooms). We asked for a late checkout and the hotel was quite accommodating. All in all -- excellent experience.

“A Wonderful Experience” The Westin is perfect for a New York getaway. We got a great a rate, and had an amazing corner room with a view. At reception, Janice was incredibly friendly, professional and made sure I had a feather free room made up for me. The location is great - it connects indoors to a complex that includes a large movie theater, Starbucks, Chevy's Restaurant, and there is a steakhouse and bar at the hotel. The hotel also contains a fitness center and spa. The room was a comfortable size for NYC, and the bed was very comfortable. Altogether, a fantastic stay!

“Good hotel, expect to pay for it” Recently I spent two nights at the Hilton. Total cost was about $900, not including any meals. The location is great. Rockefeller Center is right nearby, with lots of things in walking distance. They only keep the 6th Avenue entrance open (6th Ave is also called Avenue of The Americas). All of the side doors are locked. So you could be at the hotel, but still have a full block to walk around the corner. Check in was quick. The room was average sized and very clean. The bed was very comfortable. I also liked the night lighting that gets activated along the floor as you walk by. The TV is a 26-inch LCD. Down pillows are standard. I called the front desk for firmer pillows. To my surprise, the shower pressure was good. Space is limited. When using the toilet, your legs will be brushing against the bath towels on the rack. Toiletries were Crabtree & Evelyn. On my first night there were some kids two doors down. All I could hear was constant shrieking and laughing. At 11 PM I called the front desk. I was ready to pound on their door but decided to let the hotel handle it, which they did. Just remember that you can still have noise even at the nicer hotels.

“Nice Corporate Hotel” We stayed here one night during the week, and had a pleasant stay. Our room was of adequate size, and we enjoyed the Westin "heavenly bed". The hotel seemed very busy with training classes, and a large function in the ballroom. It is definitely a large, corporate, business hotel, and not a "get-away" hotel. There is a very large, nice work out room on the third floor, along with a small heated pool surrounded by lounge chairs. There were also two training classes being held at the pool area. I found this odd, and disconcerting wearing wet swimsuits around people in business attire. There is a free parking lot, but we couldn't find it until leaving. We were forced to pay $12 for garage self-parking. I hate this trend in hotels to make paying guests pay to park their cars! The shower had two shower heads, which I have never seen before, and I also liked the leaf shaped soaps, and the Heavenly Spa toiletries in the room. They did smell heavenly. I booked this room through Hotwire for $59 dollars a night under 4 star hotels in Park Central area. I thought this was a great buy!

“Location, Service and Comfort” I stayed at the Embassy Suites Downtown Chicago for 5 nights, and was very happy with the property. The included breakfast/ 6:30-9:30am was excellent (eating before 8am is best, as it gets busy later). There is so many great restaurants (Grand Luxe Cafe is one of my favorites) and stores closeby, and it feels very safe to walk about even after dark. I felt it was a safe hotel for a woman traveling alone. Internet access in the hotel is fast, however not free! $9.95 per day. Even if you only use it for an hour in the evening, after midnight you get a 2nd for the next day's useage. The 2 room suite was well appointed with a large comfortable bed, microwave, safe, coffee maker, sofa table and chairs. 2 TV's one a flat screen in the living area. Because there is no desk, the table is your computer work area, and the chairs at the table are hard and uncomfortable. The living room area furniture was hard as rocks and kind of worn in the suite I occupied. I beleive the sofa in the living room was a fold out bed. Other pluses, a pool and work out area that looked beautiful and clean, Manager's reception at 5pm offered free drinks, and snacks. It looked crowded, and one evening I stopped by at 6pm, and there were no snacks left. It is attractive and has a great front desk staff.

“True Service” I stay with Kimpton as often as possible. The George is another shining example of what good service looks like. We were not happy with our first room and were changed into a great room without any hassle.

“Perfect Location” Great hotel, hip, centrally located within Dallas. Great amenities, descent health club, top restaurants nearby. The hotel is similar to a W type experience. Great pool side area, bar, friendly staff. Top hotel for the Dallas experience.

“Very nice, new(er) hotel” I stayed here for business on two evenings and was very impressed with both the service and the room. In addition to great views of the city, the room was clean and updated. Didn't try the restaurant but the lobby bar was great. Right in the center of downtown, the hotel is close to several restaurants.

“Trendy and Cool Boutique Hotel” Its a small hotel with plenty of charizma. Each floor had cute and different themed lounges with a computer. The beds were small but oh sooo comfy. The hotel is centrally located near great shopping, Theaters and more. The staff was very helpful. This is my hotel of choice when attending a show at the theatre across the street.
“hotel is ok” Rooms are not horrible but not very clean either. Staffs are not very friendly and hotel is not really in a great location.

“Great as long as rundown houses don't intimidate you” I was wavering between a 4-star or 5-star review, but then they did something incredible for service which made me decide on a 5-star review. Pros: -Large spacious suite with clean marble floors and a Westin-quality bed. Great if you need room or for long stays if you want to cook there's a kitchen and fridge. I visited my friends's room at the Renaissance (2 blocks away, the other hotel that's very close to the convention center), and mine was twice the size and much more luxurious. I'm guessing mine was cheaper too. -Close the convention center (if you're here for a conference). -It was raining and they left an umbrella in my room (this made me give it a 5-star). Overall great polite service. Con: -Location. Around the corner there are 3 boarded up buildings. Caveat: I got lost one day, and ended up walking around the block. It's not that bad, it's just those 3 buildings, and the neighborhood wasn't great, but as a single female at 8 pm, I felt relatively safe. I would not be flashing a Louis Vuitton purse here though. If you come from certain directions, the location is fine. But if you come from the north or the east, the neighboring area is slummy. -Cold marble floors. Easily rectified by wearing socks and turning up the heater to a nice toasty 75.

“Best location of all SEA-TAC airport hotels” The Coast Gateway Hotel is just a 5 minute walk (no streets crossed) to/from SEA-TAC airport terminal building. The rooms are quiet and pleasant (including a fridge and microwave and a window that opens); the included buffet continental breakfast offers a good variety of choices from 5am daily; and the staff is friendly. I did not use the business center and do not know about parking for this hotel, but the light rail now serves the airport to/from downtown ($2.50 each way, machines accept credit cards but can be hard to find at downtown stations and the transit police are nasty). The light rail station is in the NE corner of the airport parking structure. The hotel is on International Blvd at the SE corner of the airport. There are several hotels and restaurants nearby (the Doubletree Hotel, which I also like but is not quite as convenient due to its larger size, is across the street). This hotel participates with Pricline.com bidding and can be a great bargain if you know how to bid (see biddingfortravel for pointers).

“Excellent service, good location” The Sofitel is in a good location if you want to be between Hollywood and Beverly Hills. While not as luxurious as some Sofitels, LA's is very nice and a nice alternative to the uber cool hotels like the Mondrain and Standard. It's close enough to walk to Robertson Blvd shopping, and a quick drive to Melrose Ave. shopping. As many others have noted, there is a CVS nearby, which is very convenient. Our breakfasts were included and this was well worth it. The breakfast is excellent and the restaurant staff was super nice. The check in and check out process was easy, valet is a breeze too as there are always at least 4 or 5 valet guys at the ready. The rooms were big and quiet, the bed did not feel like the "heavenly" type found in most hotels of this type but it was fine. As with all Sofitels I've been to, the beds have only a large comforter, appropriate in my opinion for a cabin in Canada in January, but not for LA in the summer. I left a note asking for the bed to be remade with a sheet and light blanket, which was done right away and was perfect. The AC was very easy to operate and worked well. If you are looking for a pool scene this would not be a good choice, as the pool is rather small and there is no view, but I did sit near the pool one morning to read and it was very nice. My only complaint is the lighting near the bed. The switch for the table lamp is on the electrical cord and practically behind the table. There were also "reading" lights on either side of the bed but the switch was not within reaching distance for me and was not really bright enough or in the right position for reading.

“Good quality big-box hotel, no surprises” This is a big hotel, central, and civilized - prime convention territory! But no surprises. Big, comfortable rooms, nice bed (with a futon between the bottom sheet and the mattress - novel - but comfortable), well appointed bathrooms, the food's good, staff are well-trained-polite, if a little try-too-hard friendly (when I told the check-out clerk I was flying to Boston, she said "oh, send me a postcard!". Yes, of course, what was I thinking...). But this hotel is just what you'd expect from a big Hyatt in a big city, and there's nothing wrong with it. I paid about $300 which was a bit expensive for what I got, but not by much. My Hyatt status gets me free internet, tho' I'd guess it 's probably not cheap otherwise, and it worked generally ok. Tea/coffee and ipod player in the room gets plus marks, as does a big bathtub. The negatives weren't life-threatening. The hotel's been well renovated, but it's nevertheless an old big-box hotel, "mutton dressed up as lamb". The one major niggle wouldn't be a problem for most travellers. I checked before I booked that there was a pool, and what the opening hours were (from 5am). I checked again when I got to the hotel, with the front desk. And I checked once more in the hotel services booklet. Jetlag, an early flight, and a training programme, meant I was at the door of the pool at 5:00 sharp in the morning. Locked door. 5:05 still locked. I called reception, who said they'd get someone from security to come, which they did... at 5:30. So my long workout turned into a short workout and I could have stayed in bed another half an hour. And neither the receptionist nor the security guard attempted an apology. So any other lunatic early morning athletes beware. The rest of you... ignore that whinge! But more of you might be unimpressed with the "business centre" that consisted of a room of machines, all self-service with a credit card. No staff in sight and you can't charge faxes, etc, to your room - credit card swipe only. Now THAT's pissy.
“Staying as at home in the middle of the town” Everything was perfect...location of the apartament, fourniture, kitchen, beds, very clean, etc...breakfast included!!

“For the business traveller” Had a good stay here - and only reason I would stay here is if you need to be in this location. It is in a corporate/industrial area - so good if you are working in the area or need to be near the airport. Good clean, comfortable rooms - and very good staff. No restaurant though - but a few decent place just a short walk away.

“We'll Return” My girlfriend and I spent three nights last week at the Hotel Boheme. In San Francisco, its location simply can't be beat. Comprised of the second and third floors above the famous Stella Bakery, Hotel Boheme sits in the heart of North Beach, on Columbus. Just a short walk in any direction will take you other wonderful SF neighborhoods: Chinatown, the Financial District, Union Square, etc. There must not be more than 10 or 12 rooms, all of which are up a narrow flight of stairs leading to a small lobby. The interior is hip and funky, done in tangerine, greens, and black, with walls decorated by fantastic black and white photos of San Francisco in the 50s. The staff was great, particularly Stan, who went out of his way to make sure we were comfortable and knew our way around the city. We arrived before check in, so Stan took our bags, my cell number, and called us as soon as our room was ready. Our room looked out over Columbus Avenue and all of the 24-7 excitement the neighborhood offers. It was small, but clean, comfortable, and probably much like it has been for the past 50 years. The bed was older but still yielded a good night's sleep. If your idea of a great hotel is the typical Hilton/Marriott/Red Lion, Hotel Boheme probably isn't for you. No mini bar, no phone with 60 buttons, no shiny glass doors that slide open in front. If, however, you appreciate accomodations that are unique, fun, and full of character, you'll likely love Hotel Boheme.

“Affinia Shelburne-We will be back:)” We recently had a 4 day stay at the Affinia Shelburne for my daughters 17th b-day. I mentioned this to them when booking my reservations. They were so kind in giving us a early morning check in (we came in on a red eye flight) we were also placed on the 15th floor and had a views of the Empire State Bldg and the Chrysler Bldg. The room was a 2 bed delux, with mini kitchenette. We asked for a coffee maker and they sent one up right away. I also loved the location of this hotel. Close to Grand Central, coffee shops, shopping, everything was central. The staff at the hotel was also incredibly kind and helpful. We will for sure return to the hotel on our next trip. We love NY and the Affinia Shelburne:)!!

“Great location, very good hotel” Don't expect to check in early, but if you ask they will call your cell phone the minute the room is done so you can walk around the area. There are numerous restaurants in the vicinity including less expensive options for breakfast, etc. The hotel is large and somewhat old (the room door is vintage and is not that sound proof) but the hotel is very clean, comfortable, and I experienced no problems with service.

“Not as nice as in the past” I had previously adored staying at the Willard & it's usually my hotel of choice when in the District. But this stay was NOT worth the money. When I went to the Willard before, there was classical music playing when I entered the room, a robe & slippers in the bathroom, & chocolate on the pillow. Plus the room was beautiful & cozy, very colonial. This time I might as well have been at the Hyatt. There was no music, no slippers, no chocolate, and the room had been redone to well, look like a Hyatt. Used to, rooms at the Willard were so great you didn't want to leave. I couldn't wait to get out. In addition, the sleep quality was horrible. I was in a different part of the hotel, so street noise was horrendous. Plus, the mattress was in such poor condition I could feel the boards of the bed frame through it. The Willard is supposed to remember your pillow choice and they had all the wrong kind in there. And the room simply wasn't as impeccably clean as last time. They've also remodeled, so all the beautiful colonial stuff is gone and it seriously looks as generic as a Hyatt. Service this time was also lacking. The valet was impolite when I asked to have the hotel car brought around (an advertised amenity), claiming they didn't have a car, then finally his boss asked where I was going & admitted they did have a car & he guessed I could use it. The front desk clerk when I checked out didn't really seem to care when he asked how my stay was and when I hesitated in answering, then muttered, "Well, it was okay, I guess," he just handed me my bill & didn't ask how they could have made it better or anything. If this Willard is truly this hit or miss, I guess I'm hunting a new hotel for the District. If all I'm going to get is like any other generic hotel, then I will stay at a generic hotel & save the money.

“Good Location, But a Bit Dirty” Positives: Close to the Van Ness metro stop, good neighborhood with lots of restaurants and shops on Conn Ave. The hotel has a parking lot ($15 per night, but they do have parking). Negatives: The hot water is hit-or-miss. Sometimes cold, sometimes scalding. The rooms are a little skanky. They need to be completely refurbished. Furniture and fixtures are a little old and showing signs of wear. The maid did a terrible job, which grossed me out.

“Always enjoy!” I have to travel to Dallas occasionally on business. My office is in downtown Dallas. The Magnolia Hotel is a great hotel that is very close to my office, the tram, and the rest that Dallas has to offer. It is one block from the original Neiman Marcus store. Check in is always easy and the staff is very friendly. The rooms are extremely spacious and nicely decorated. Rooms on higher floors give you better views of the city. This hotel has great amenities that make the stay even better. Full breakfast in the morning is wonderful. I can't believe the selection they provide. From 5:30 to 6:30 they provide a beer and wine happy hour. You are only allowed two glasses of either wine or beer, but that is more than enough for me. The wine is always very good. They only offer one kind of beer though, so you may be unhappy. Then from 8:00 to 10:00 they provide milk and fresh baked cookies before bed. They are wonderful. The fitness center is very large with new, up to date equipment and a hot tub to relax in. Now for the down side. They is a very minor item, but when you are there for business, it can be a problem. The hotel seems to have problems with it's wireless Internet provider. The last time I was there, last year, I had no wireless the whole week I was there. This time, I checked in on Sunday and there was no Internet access. But when I returned from the office on Monday afternoon, it was working. Then on Thursday they had problems again. It can be frustrating, but this time everything worked out OK. I enjoy the historical character of the hotel, the spacioius well appointed rooms, and the amenities this hotel provides.

“Good Stay” Stayed here for three nights. We were given a handicap room so everything in the room was alittle different than a regular room. We didn't have any sink space which was sorta of a pain. We had a roll in shower which would have been great for someone in a wheel chair. The bed was very comfortable though. The staff was very friendly and the Starbucks right downstairs was a plus. Would like to stay again to see what the regular room is like. Did like the location also

“Satisfactory” I stayed here recently on a business trip to East Dallas. The choice of hotel was made based on location to my work. Having flown into Dallas and not having a car, its location does not serve anyimmediate access to tourist sites or downtown, not does it enable access to restaurants / food outlets that might be nearby. Location wise, it is in an urban wasteland, with a rather dreary outlook to vast roadways and nothing much more. However it served its purpose in terms of my business requirements and provided very comfortable accommodation. The hotel is modern, and its welcome lobby is attractive, with the adjoining breakfast room making it quite spacious and inviting. Check-in was efficient and courteous. I had a really spacious room on the 3rd floor - while it faced the highway, it was relatively quiet. The room was very clean and seemed to be well cared for. The stains on the carpet in the hallway need attention. The bed was fantastic, and the assortment of pillows was a treat. I used the small gym twice during my stay - to have this was a surprise and I was pleased to have access to it. I did not use the pool - however, it looked clean and inviting. Breakfast was adequate - this was a summer visit, so having more fresh fruit for the health conscious would be an improvement.

“Ask for a quiet room facing the pool” "We all want a quiet room" said the check in clerk as he gave me a noisy room facing the noisy street (College)--albeit with a pack of ear plugs. After much discussion,they found a quiet room (facing the pool). Why I had to insist when the pool room was available was beyond me.Also,have them remove all the snacks below the TV (including the mini bar stuff) if you are trying to stay on your diet. Otherwise great stay. Helpful staff. Bathrobes in the room a nice touch. And room very clean. Mattresss ok if not a little saggy. Right on canal/RiverWalk.Take the #5 bus from the airport for $1.10. Runs every 30 minutes and takes 30 minutes.

“Beautiful, great location, beware if there is a concert adjacent” Spent a night here a few weeks ago using Marriott Rewards points. The hotel was VERY busy with a conference, but I was able to check in fairly early. I was upgraded to a Corner King room overlooking the Inner Harbor. Very nice room, clean, lots of big windows and an excellent view. My only issue, and it is a big one, was that there was a rock concert (Counting Crows) at the amphitheater adjacent to the hotel and the noise went on until 11 PM. I later found out that they hotel, as a rule, hands out letters to arriving guests on/around days that concerts take place, but nothing was given to me, nor did some staffers know this was going on. I suggested that they get some updated info from the venue as fully half of the rooms would be affected by the noise. The property itself is lovely. Very friendly staff, and they pay attention to details. A large piece of tarp from a nearby construction site blew into the entry driveway and a bellman promptly removed it. I did not drive so I can't comment on the parking. However, the hotel is very well located for seeing the area, including the harbor, Little Italy, Fells Point etc. There is a water taxi stop just outside the hotel. I didn't eat in the restaurant but there is a combination Starbucks/deli/gift shop that looked popular, in addition to the restaurant. There are so many good restaurants in town, there was no reason to eat in the hotel. If you are an elite member of the Marriott Rewards program you will have access to one of the best Concierge Lounges in the company.
