It was open all day with a wide array of beverages (including 2 flavors of fresh brewed iced tea), omeletes and pancakes cooked to order, along with the usual array of Concierge breakfast offerings. Around lunchtime, they had crab/corn chowder as well. The evening offerings included a few kinds of hot appetizers as well as cheese displays, crudite and more. Dessert was the only thing lacking. Nice variety but some of the things tasted like they'd been in the fridge too long. This hotel would be a great choice for a pre or post cruise stay as well. Rates are not cheap, but if you look, you might be able to find a deal (or at least a reasonable price.) I will go back in the future. My one night stay was just too short...though I will make sure there aren't any concerts. (They did offer to move my room, but frankly I didn't stay in Baltimore near the Harbor to NOT see water.....and the noise did stop, as I was informed, just before 11 PM.)

“Good Staff, Good Rooms, Fair Cleanliness” A bunch of Jehovah's Witnesses in town during our stay, I suppose they make for good neighbors but the pool and breakfast buffet was swarmed by these people and despite what I assume were valiant efforts, things were picked through, tables and floor were dirty, and pool water was murky. This last was disappointing as our poor baby daughter was dragged along on a trip and this was the thing we most could have her look forward to, but no thanks on poop water. The rooms are nice and comfortable, however they are a little dirty. They look and smell clean, but the couches need to be scrubbed (that's the beauty of vinyl isn't it), the headboard had all kinds of spooge on it (gross!) and the bathroom had pubes all over the place stuck in the corners and what not. All-in-all decent but not a detail job. The staff is very very friendly and will attempt to accommodate - not "big city" on point, but still quite good and meaning well. At $79 bucks a night I can't really complain so feel bad on the 3 out of 5, but hey I have to be honest, I hate pubes, spooge and butt grease on the couch.

“Not the greatest hotel” I was in Chicago for a conference and stayed at the Palmer House for four nights. Not one night did I get a restful sleep. The hotel has not been soundproofed, so you can hear everything around you from loud televisions to slamming doors. This lack of soundproofing is very evident when the L Train passes by every five minutes. During the time I stayed at the Palmer House, construction was taking place on the floor above mine. The work started around 6AM with a loud jackhammer device shaking the walls. There was also some construction taking place in the lower level of the hotel where one enters from the street. The smell of garbage was strong. I would not recommend this hotel for someone looking for a restful sleep.

“gem-ish” I booked the Silversmith frankly because there were no other options. However, I found the place intriguing. Far from luxurious but rather well-located and with a sense of purpose and history. The National Register Building is quite beautiful, so do take a few moments to appreciate the facade. Our room did not face the L so in that regard we were fortunate. Yes I would stay here again and I would not let the location scare you in the least. My colleagues spent twice as much around the corner at the Palmer House and from what I can see all they got for that was a shmancy-er lobby. Spend some time in the Silversmith Lobby and enjoy quiet and architecture.

“Fabulous Service As Usual” I have stayed at the Crescent Court hotel several times and overall really enjoy the experience. Some of the rooms are really great, but I will review the room from my last stay, in Room 522: King Size comfortable bed with great linens and pillows. Nice flat screen TV and spacious room area, but would have loved to have a coffee maker in the room so I could heat water for tea in the evenings. Bathroom is large and very nice except that water pressure for the shower could be better. The Lady Primrose bath products are ok, not my favorites but nice large sized bottles at least. Loved the dressing/makeup area with cushioned bench, if I could purchase that and take it home I would, the lighting is really perfect and it's nicely designed. Room service was excellent food at an incredibly inflated price. Seriously, crazy expensive, more than I am used to at other high end hotels. Luckily, there is a Starbucks downstairs and an Au Bon Pain across the way in the 200 building, plus many great restaurants nearby for lunch/dinners. Speaking of restaurants, if you love seafood, give Trulucks a try, it's right across the street, excellent martinis and food. Definitely my favorite meal of the trip! Love the gym at this hotel, and love it even more now that there is not a daily fee to use it - lol. Lots of machines, both cardio and strength training and it is always clean. Service level is high at this hotel, from the friendly and helpful front desk and concierge to the maids, everyone is courteous and friendly. While this is not my absolute favorite hotel, I would recommend it to friends......

“Great for budget travel” Recently spent 2 weeks in NYC moving to the Belleclaire for the last 4 days in order to stretch my vacation dollars. Booked a queensize w/shared bath thinking I could switch to a room w/ private bath if necessary. As it turned out, sharing the bathroom with 2 other rooms was fine. I didn't have a travel companion during my stay at the Belleclaire and felt very comfortable and safe at the hotel and in the neighborhood. I would definitely stay here again to enjoy the low rates and explore the neighborhood more.

“Great location!” My daughter and I recently stayed at the Hotel Angeleno while visiting colleges in the Los Angeles area. The location is GREAT--unless you encounter a lot of traffic on the 405--then you SEE the hotel for a long time before you can GET to it!! :) It's located just between Brentwood and Bel-Air, adjacent to the 405 and Sunset Blvd. We were able to zip over to UCLA in minutes and Beverly Hills and Hollywood are also just a short drive down Sunset. Rooms are nicely decorated with a cosmopolitan modern flair, although on the smallish side. We had a flat-screen tv, two phones, a desk, fridge (stocked with mini-bar stuff), coffee pot (with Wolfgang Puck coffee), blowdryer, iron, ironing board and plenty of drawer space. The bathroom was VERY small, but they'd gotten creative with shelving and managed to fit everything in there nicely. Our blowdryer didn't work, but I'd brought my own so that wasn't a problem. The bathtub/shower was on the smallish side and had an almost-attacking shower curtain--the curved rod kept it from being too annoying. Our fridge wouldn't get cold, so we called the front desk and had a replacement fridge (thankfully UNSTOCKED) in very quick time. I also had to ask the front desk several other questions (restaurant hours, pool location and hours, workout room location and hours, internet service options, etc.) because there was no information booklet in the room. The front desk person told me that they were in the process of re-doing those, so many rooms didn't have them. I found that a little frustrating, but I got over it! There was also no notepad, and only one pen (after a thorough search for THAT) in the room, so I don't know if that was part of the same problem. Internet service was free, although the signal was a little weak in our room. The pool area was lovely, with cushioned lounge chairs and a fireplace and very cool lighting, but there was no hot tub. :( The workout room was very cool, with colored lights and a big screen tv. It almost had a nightclub vibe to it! The hotel is circular with small balconies on all rooms. Ours overlooked the freeway, but I didn't notice any freeway noise--probably because the A/C unit was so loud! These units could use replacement, as they're noisy and not very effective. I was way too hot for most of the night, even with it set on the coldest setting. Parking is valet-only and costs $20/night. Typical for L.A., but still pretty steep when you're paying $159 (at the very LOWEST) for a room. The lobby is cool and sets the mood nicely. The elevators are FAST and we never had to wait long for one. We ate breakfast at the top-floor restaurant (The Wave) and it was VERY good, and the view is amazing. I went up at night to check it out and it would be a very nice place for a romantic dinner or drink in the bar with all the lights of L.A. below you. This hotel is nice, and could be even NICER (bordering on lush) if a few more improvements were made. To be fair, it's WAY more affordable than the Hotel Luxe which is just a block away, and the price is very reasonable considering the location. I would recommend it without hesitation.

“My Favorite Hotel on the River Walk” I've visited San Antonio countless of times and have always stayed on the River Walk. This year we pricelined our hotel and got Hotel Contessa. What an AMAZING hotel for the price we paid!! The hotel rooms are pretty big suites giving enough space for a family of 4 adults to relax and sprawl out in. The bathrooms are extremely roomy with modern and elegant touches. I found myself taking a very long shower since it was so relaxing in there. The location can't be beat. Once you walk down to the lobby, you're right on the river ready to go. Even though you are on the river walk, the area still has a calm and quiet atmosphere and does not get too rowdy at night. Service was beyond excellent. Everyone from the valet guys to the front desk to housekeeping were so nice and accomodating. The down size...parking is not free and you have to pay a pretty hefty daily fee to have the valet guys park it across the street in a parking garage. But like all hotels on the river walk, parking is always going to cost you. So this was not much of a surprise for us. I would definitely stay here again and recommend this hotel to future visitors! Thanks Hotel Contessa for great weekend!

“Schön eingerichtetes Satdthotel” Obschon die Zimmer dieses Boutique-Hotels recht klein sind, überzeugen sie doch durch eine sehr komfortable und auch optisch sehr ansprechende Ausstattung. Da sich das Hotel aber an einer der Hauptverkehrsadern Chicagos mitten in der Innenstadt befindet, sind die Zimmer mangels doppelter Verglasung auch einem ständigen Lärmpegel ausgesetzt. Positiv erwähnenswert ist die Weinprobe, die für die Gäste kostenlos an den meisten Abenden in der Hotellobby stattfindet.

“Just o.k.” Stayed at the Millenium Broadway for one night while in New York on business. I got a decent rate on Hotwire, otherwise I probably would not have picked it. It was fine, but I definitely would not chose this hotel given other options. Hotwire rates it 4 stars, but I think it is more like 3 stars. I was given a room on a high floor, which was nice. The room was adequate--bed was comfortable and bathroom was clean.Linens o.k.- But everything was tired, worn and a little banged up. Elevators missing numbers for floors, carpets in halls not that clean. The hotel lobby is sort of cavernous with only small areas for lounging. Not elegant or welcoming. Lots and lots of tourists who really want to be near Times Square. All in all, perfectly fine, but I wouldn't pick it unless the Times Square location is your top priority and I certainly would pick other areas of NY to stay if I was on vacation in the city. I needed to be in midtown so it was reasonably convenient.

“Fine for a Night, Best Value for Close to LAX” I rarely fly in/out of LAX on business, choosing usually one of the other LA-area airports, so I had no familiarity of hotels near LAX. With an early flight out of LAX, I found this one thanks to other Trip Advisor Reviews and for the most part I would recommend it. Only about a mile from LAX, so easy to return a rental car and the hotel has a free shuttle but I didn't use it. Plenty of parking (free). This is a former Howard Johnson (according to a long-term guest) that has been completely refurbed with modern decor into an HI Express. The only thing they didn't do apparently was the elevators which are old, very slow and as of this writing one was still out of order, so expect a potentially long wait to go up and down. I didn't have any issues with airplane noise (none) or street noise (not much, drowned out by a/c and fan) and the room was quiet and I didn't hear other guests. The neighborhood is dodgy but didn't feel unsafe, although I wouldn't go walking around after dark. Hotel was fine, completely safe, lots of families and overseas tourists staying there. 7-11 in front of the hotel if you need supplies and a Sizzler steakhouse also in front. But if you want any nice restaurants or shopping you either need a car or line up the hotel's shuttle. If I was going to fly in/out of LAX again, I would stay here because it's a lot more affordable than the large airport hotels.

“Great Place foir the Price” Excellent location two blocks from Fisherman"s Wharf and walking distance to Ghiradelli Square, cable cars, many restaurants, drug store and the MUNI system. Nice rooms and clean. Free hot breakfast was good but not great. The quality of the food was just satisfactory, good coffee. Very busy hotel so be prepared for a lot of people and lines at breakfast no matter what time you get there. Breakfast served daily 6:30am-9:30am and when it's over, it's over. No coffee after 9:30am is a bit annoying. would stay again considering the great price and location compared to the competition in the area. Regular Holiday Inn is just two blocks away so be sure your transportation/shuttle drops you off at the right hotel. No refrigerator/microwave in room!

“Impeccable Service” I went to DC for the 2011 Suntrust National Marathon and chose the hotel for it's location to the race and easy metro access. My hubby, brother and I could have not been happier! From the moment we stepped out of our 6 hour car drive, the doorman, Ron made us feel welcomed and like Kings. The hotel's lobby is Gorgeous and it was really nice to walk in and know we were staying here. We were greeted with a smile by Annie (hope that is her name) at the front desk. She made sure my brother and I had the same floor and gave me aas quiet room as she could find so I could get sleep. My brother's room didn't have a view and was a little dark but that was fine, he was very happy there. I had a view overlooking the park somewhat and it was REALLY uncomfortable to have the shower the way it was set-up (as everyone has described) they do have to change that! If you stay with a friend or a colleague, there is NO privacy. The room was very small and kinda cramped. The sink is in the actual room near the bed but not that much bothersome that we had an issue but it was strange and maybe I would have changed rooms if I didn't crash and go to sleep. Really Nice bed and my floor was quiet. The SERVICE of the hotel is what STANDS OUT, from Greg (concierge) to the Audi "drive you up the street" service, we did not meet anyone who didn't smile and didn't know I wasn't running the marathon.....I still don't know how half the folks knew!! We celebrated my race at the upstairs club, it was nice and had a great view. Boring but it got better as the night progressed, great place for singles!! Wish they had more seats available to guests though, we had no where to sit and my legs were killing me. Also, I had a really hard time getting a cab the day of the marathon and I had a lovely lady run blocks at 6am trying to get me a cab the morning of the race, the metro access absolutely failed and I was almost in tears! She calmed me down and got me there! I told my hubby when we go back this is the place for us! I cannot wait to go back again for my next race!

“Perfect, though a bit too trendy” The Bryant Park Hotel has the ideal midtown Manhattan location, everyone is friendly and helpful, and the rooms are clean and modern. You can't go wrong when all of the important points are so well covered. Of course, you pay for it. We were there during the 4th of July week and we got what they call a junior suite for $359/night. It was only one big room so I'm not sure why they call it a suite, but it was a bright and clean room. The decor was trendy minimalist. Bare walls, Molton Brown toiletries, a Toto toilet, and a safe, but no coffeemaker. We didn't ask for one and they probably would have sent one up, but it's midtown and there's coffee everywhere. We discovered that if we took the complimentary newspaper with us, we could buy coffee and read the paper across the street in Bryant Park. Maybe it was good that we couldn't make coffee in the room, but it would have been nice to have the option. We never noticed any problem with people going to the bar downstairs, setup for the Friday morning concert (Norah Jones) in the park across the street wasn't silent, but it wasn't bad. We stayed 3 nights and even though security people were making sure that only guests could use the elevators, I'd think that they might have started to recognize us before we checked out. Of course it's very dark by (and in) the elevators, so maybe they just couldn't see us. Anyone who enjoyed the Rocpool Reserve in Inverness would be likely to like this hotel too. Would I go back? Yes, when the price is right. It's not for everyone and I'd actually like a warm and welcoming atmosphere better that the cold trendiness, but I don't think I've stayed anywhere in midtown that I liked better.

“Outside looks bland but interior is fantastic!” I have passed this hotel many times while in Chicago and on the outside it does not look appealing, however on the inside it is fantastic. The staff is excellent and the location was ideal for the clients I was in town seeing. My only complaint is the desk chair is not condusive to sitting for long periods of time doing work. Other than that, no complaints.

“Nice hotel” Stayed one night before catching a 7:30 a.m. flight out. This hotel is great, we dropped off the car at Avis 9 p.m. the night before after dropping our luggage off in the room, the hotel shuttle picked us up at Avis. Great thing. Then had a nice breakfast in the morning 5:30 a.m., they had more stuff than the other Fairfield we stayed at in Cherry Creek. Plusses there. Then we took the shuttle at 6 a.m. to the airport. The shuttle runs 24 hours. Free wireless internet was great. The rooms are small, but fine for one night. The beds were nice and soft with feather pillows. I didn't use the indoor pool or exercise room, so I can't say what it is like. I would stay at this hotel the night before leaving next time.

“Convenient and Comfortable” The Sheraton Fort Worth Hotel and Spa is located in a convenient location for access to the Sundance Entertainment/Restaurant district, Cultural district (e.g., museums), and the Fort Worth Stockyards district. While I wouldn't consider this property to be an "upscale spa" retreat setting the spa and other hotel facilities were comfortable and offered the standard amenities as expected at a Sheraton hotel. I would certainly recommend this property as a good choice for travelers to the downtown Fort Worth area for ease of interstate/highway and entertainment/dining access. Use of the free “Molly the Trolley” public transit stop outside the hotel’s doors was a welcome treat for accessing the various entertainment and dining venues in downtown Fort Worth. The only complaint is the $12 per night parking charge that would have been added to our hotel bill if we would have selected the hotel property parking lot. Instead, we parked next to the hotel parking lot and paid nothing.

“Good, but not Great” I just finished a two night stay at the Cassa hotel, and, as my review title states, I had a good but not great experience. The hotel is located just off 6th Ave on 45 which puts it in a spectacular area for visitors and access to transportation. The building is new and modern in style and as its name suggests, contains both a hotel and condominium. The small, modern lobby sets the tone for the hotel in style and setup. The fixtures are modern, but things are snug. With luggage trolleys and a few guests, it could get crowded quickly. The staff I dealt with all seemed friendly, but the fact they are doing double-duty for the building residents means they have a slightly different vibe than a traditional, dedicated hotel staff. I didn't need much assistance, and my interactions were all good. Up in the rooms, in my case 1403, it was the same situation: modern, snug and just missing a little something I can't put my finger on. The rooms are small. Pretty well-designed in the sleeping area, but the lack of storage is glaring. I had one small overnight bag and I still had some difficulties. I can't imagine what the guests I saw with gigantic rolling suitcases did with them and their contents. The bed was a full-size bed, which was ok for me, but a couple might feel cramped. Bedding was good. The maid does like to come early, so put out the Do Not Disturb sign if you are not an early bird! The bathroom was sleek and clean. It too did not have much in the way of storage. Solo travelers would be fine (unless you were a woman with a lot of makeup you wanted to set out), but again, couples would find it challenging. I liked the spacious glass rainforest shower and modern sink. It was kept immaculately. So, all in all, everything here was good, clean and completely adequate. As long as you are comfortable with the scaled-down design, you will like the room. Staff were also pleasant. But for me, there was something slightly off about the property. I would certainly stay there again, but otherwise didn't have any particularly warm final impressions of the property.

“Nice place, but not worth the price.” We recently stayed here on June 2nd-3rd in a river view room. The room was nice and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was stocked fully and only had one issue. One of the lights in the bathroom only worked some of the time. It would shut off and turn back on when it felt like it. Other than that, nothing stood out in a good or bad way. As for only the average rating, the price is a major factor. We paid close to $300 including all taxes for the room, $30 park, and $40 for two hoagies that we got for room service. That is just way too much money for a run of the mill hotel.

“very nice place but there are some problems” The hotel is a beautiful place with spacious rooms and friendly staff. But beware if you are on the side of the hotel that faces the Alehouse, since you will be subjected to music at very high decibels until the wee hours of the morning. The other problem is that this hotel, even though pricey, allows clients to bring dogs to their rooms -- and there were lots of dogs during our stay. I felt sometimes like I was staying at a kennel.

“Beautiful boutique hotel slightly lacking the Ritz Carlton service level” I stayed here for a trip that involved business and leisure and enjoyed the unusually small size for a Ritz Carlton as well as the location. The rooms were well appointed and large as were the bathrooms. The service touches that are often synonymous with the Ritz Carlton name were not completely there. The check in staff had to do double duty as concierge and they were not as connected and well versed as a normal Ritz concierge would be, however, they were always pleasant to work with despite providing minimal service. I took the house car 3 times will I was there at their suggestion and 2 of the 3 times, the driver was unsure where he was going and slightly lost and erratic with their driving. Additionally, the Fahrenheit restaurant was very average and very overpriced. All in all a very pretty small quiet hotel, but needs some work in the top quality service that is expected.

“Good option” We needed a triple which is exceptionally hard to come by these days. When the hotel advised they did not have any true triples available they offered to put a cot in a standard double for only $10 more a night. Not a bad offer considering the city hotels were jammed due to graduation ceremonies for most of the zillion colleges in the greater Boston area. Overall a solid choice in an area chock full of good hotels.

“Boutique hotel near Gaslamp” A typical boutique hotel just on the edge of the touristy Gaslamp district. The immediate area is actually pretty seedy with lots of homeless and drunks but it was always busy and we never felt menaced. Two blocks away is the start of the Gaslamp area which is a fine location for a family. Lots of transit connections nearby. We also could walk to the harbour. Arrival was complicated by the fact that the room which we'd bought via Hotwire was not configured properly (one bed not the 2 promised) and the desk staff said nothing was available at first, saying it was Hotwire's problem and we could pay for an upgrade and then argue for HW to pay. After a lot of pouting on our part, the manager "found" a 2-bed room and all was well. The room was new, clean and big enough with a decent, but not huge, array of amenities. Like many such hotels, there are those weird quirks like a sliding panel on the bathroom and no door on the shower. No problem for a family or couple, could be awkward if sharing with a friend. Various little touches were missed - lights burned out and not replaced, broken toilet roll holder that took 3 notes to housekeeping to finally get reattached, had to ask for non-plastic glassware for the bar and bathroom. Staff was always pleasant. Concierge helped with a lot of planning and sells zoo tickets at normal price so we avoided the line-up We ordered room service once and everything was truly gross. We never tried the restaurant proper. Pool is small and nice with California style lounges and a bar. Fitness centre was clean and modern, not huge though. Business centre is rudimentary. Generally, they did not over-deliver, but provided reasonable value for the money.

“Great Location” I stayed here for 3 days back in June of 2010. The hotel itself is huge. I believe it is in the 1250 room area, making it quite large... The hotel has tons of meeting rooms, in addition from being just a block away from a large convention center. The location is great. If you are playing tourist like I was, the "hop on, hop off" trolley tour stops directly in front of the hotel. The hotel is attached to a large shopping mall that also has a subway stop (Green line). In addition to being close to public transportation, it is walking distance to Fenway Park (20 minutes or so) and there are tons of great restaurants in Back Bay just a few minutes walk away. When going to Back Bay, I found it quicker to cut through the shopping center that is attached rather than walk all the way around... It will save you about 1/4 a mile of walking. There is a full service Starbucks in the HUGE lobby area... in addition to free-wifi and several computer stations set up to use if you don't have your own computer. You can also print boarding passes etc from there. We were upgraded to a very nice suite on the 26th floor that had incredible views of Back Bay, the harbor and of you even see Fenway park. This place is expensive. I think I paid 230+ a night which is expensive for me.... If you are visiting from out of town, don't wast the money on a rental car. They will charge you 40.00 per night to park a car you will never use. You are better off taking a taxi from the airport rather than renting a car. If in Boston, I would HIGHLY recommend staying here.

“The best located hotel in New York” How I loved the London-- let me count the ways. This may well have been my favorite hotel in New York. Having a 500 square foot suite was wonderful. I had space to spread out, room to move about-- it was divine. The bed was fabulous, very comfortable at the end of a long day. I also thoroughly enjoyed the huge bathroom. There was enough room for two or three people in that shower! Being a woman traveler in my late twenties, I found the hotel to be the perfect combination of luxury, comfort and cool. When I went down for appetizers and drinks, Maze was a buzz of activity. Service was quick and efficient, the food was outstanding, and the drinks were tasty. I liked that the hotel always had a sense of life to it. I never saw the lobby empty, but nor did it feel crowded. It was the ideal mix of action and calm. Also, the location can't be beat. I've heard that the London is known as the best-located hotel in New York, and I can see why. You're minutes away from the theaters, Central Park, shopping, fabulous restaurants-- everything you could possibly want to do in Midtown is only five to ten minutes away! Absolutely loved it.

“Good Enough for the Money” I got this room for $48 plus fees on Hotwire (2* hotel Space Needle zone). After reading the reviews here I was concerned about this place but my fears were largely unfounded. This is a solid 2* hotel with no frills: a small but clean room that was cheaply furnished but the bed was comfortable enough and there was also a microwave and fridge (a nice plus). Plus you get free wifi and a decent complimentary continental breakfast in the morning. They charge $10 for parking (cheesy!!) but for less than $75 total it's a hard to beat price considering you're in the downtown core of the city.

“Fun small hotel” Good 5 night stay at the 70 Park ave. hotel in NYC in July. This is a small boutique type hotel located about 3 blocks south of Grand Central Station on Park Avenue. Location is good for walking anywhere in the city and also close to train or subway. Friendly Door men are very quick at hailing cabs as well. The hotel is very well decorated. Rooms are comfortable and contemporary, we had a plush King size bed with loads of pillows and the large flat screen wall TV was a nice touch, complete with sound system and dvd player. From our window we could see the Empire State Building and that was nice. There was great closet space but the bathroom was tiny. Not really a problem except for the toilet which was pushed up against the bathroom heater. If you are a large person--good luck. But the fixtures were all new and the shower was great, with a nice selection of soaps, etc. In room safe, free coffee in the bar area downstairs. We loved the concierge, John Powell, who went out of his way to help us with several requests. Be sure to talk with him --he has invaluable info about NYC. and can help you get some super dinner reso's in whatever price range you want. The bar area was nice, plus there is a happy hour with free wine in the lobby each evening. Nice touch to relax after a day sightseeing or working. I would recommend this hotel , especially if you can find a good deal because it can get rather pricey --only complaint I had was the toilet and they can use better sound-proofing on their doors--loud bang whenever a door closes close to your room. but other than that the 70 Park Ave. is a really nice hotel in a great part of the city. It's a part of the Kimpton group--so be sure to sign up for their in-touch program.

“Second Visit Here - Would Go Back Again” As good as our previous stay 12 months earlier. Great value for money. The help yourself breakfasts (included in the price) are wonderful (even managing to operate the waffle maker), and the free drinks and snacks in the evening from 5.30 - 7.30pm are really welcome. There's just such a nice atmosphere about the place. Internet stations are free and available for use in reception. A great idea that you have to stand up to use them, so that some people don't take root. Rooms are large (if a little on the dark side). Genuine HD channels on the TVs too. Fridge to keep things cool. Microwave in the main room as well. Given where the hotel is located, don't expect to see any of DC's sights from your window. Top floor 9 is for Hilton Honors guests. Area feels really safe.

“There to make your life easy” Hilton at its best, full of advice on what to see and do. Staff at door keen to park your car, get you a taxi, recommend a restaurant or just pass the time of day with you. When it rained and we were about to sit on a seat outside, they even raced over and dried it off for us! Leaving luggage there for a while on day of departure we were told - "Leave it all to us, go out and enjoy your day!" Staff actually looked happy at their work all the time! Good central position for Sundance Square.

“Intriguing” The Hotel Lobby has history and charm, with a elegant chandelier, grand piano, glamorous carved wood ceiling and intriguing artwork. The front desk staff, concierge, housekeeping staff were kind, friendly and professional. The rooms were cozy, comfortable and extremely clean. The bathroom slightly small but adequate. The shower was awesome, had wonderful water pressure for a nice hot shower. The beds, bedding and pillows were very nice and extremely cozy. Our family of 3 couples enjoyed staying here for 2 nights. We had dinner close by at Fino's, which was fabulous. We had a nice breakfast around the corner at Sears Fine Food, which was also very good. Highly recommend this hotel near Union Square for location, value and charm!

“Great property - but not for tourists” Chose this hotel because of a meeting nearby and had a great stay under a fantastic rate. Excellent service, friendly staff, nice rooms and a full Starbucks basically in the lobby (not just a glorified coffee stand like at some hotels). One of the nicer Renaissance properties I've visited. There is a T stop right down the street - which makes it easy to get to other parts of Boston. Solid (though somewhat limited) dining options just steps away. If, however, you are visiting Boston for the first time as a tourist - unless you are in town for tall ships or something else at the seaport - I'd recommend looking elsewhere as this is more of a business than leisure hotel and you'll wake up every day, walk to the T and want to do things that aren't in the immediate vicinity of this property.

“Great location, friendly staff” We stayed here for one night while in SF for a wedding. The location is great. Easy walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf and other attractions. Very close to a cable car stop. The staff was top notch and very friendly and helpful. The room was very clean, a nice size and the bed was very comfortable. The only negative thing I can say is that you have to pay to park there, but that is typical for the area. We paid for our one night self parking which doesn't expire until 3pm the next day, which was nice since we explored the city the next day before leaving.

“Not great” With so much competition out there these days I certainly would stay elsewhere. The hotel is mediocre,the room we were in was tired, the service varies from excellent to downright rude and the location is far from the city. Staff vary from fantastic to downright rude, but you never know which you'll get at any given time, Management certainly did not respond in any way to our complaint. Give it a miss. Bedbugs abound in new york, I'm not sure about this one.

“Lovely & Close to Everything - But the Terrace Ballroom” I came to the Marriott Downtown for the yearly huge ISTE conference (largest EdTech conference in the world w/18K+people!) at the Philadelphia convention center. Check in was unusually rough. As a member of the ISTE Board of Directors I had a king room reserved near an elevator - it wasn't ready at 1:00pm when I came in all hot & sticky from the Amtrak train, cab, & a 100degree humid June day. It wasn't until after my 9pm meeting (and a temporary dbl room to change & a wasted $20 tip to desk mgr. ) that they finally got me into Rm 1076 - a lovely King near the elevator - on the side of the building that is closest to the 3rd floor bridge to the Convention Center which is key because the hallways are FOOTBALL LENGTH LONG! Whew! Seriously, if you're coming for a conference at the convention center and don't want to add another 10 min walk each way to your room make sure you get a high numbered room! The newly renovated room was gorgeous! 42" LCD LG TV, sleek marble bathroom w/rain shower head, crisp sheet covered feather duvet & a plethora of pillows. It also had a nice view of the rotating guitar of the Hard Rock Cafe. Sadly, the bed hurt my back so I asked for another feather duvet & with judicious doubling up created a feather bed topper. I also asked for a REFRIGERATOR which was not standard for bottles of water, Diet Coke, and fruit. Nice that they delivered it & plugged it in whilst I was at a meeting. The Marriott is a Pepsi hotel but there's a 7-11 out the front door and a Wine & Spirits shop out the back door (across the street from the outdoor cafe) Also close by a Hard Rock Cafe, Melting Pot, & an Italian place where I had a lovely but pricey lunch called Maggiano's. Hotels will generally try and provide items that you need if they are not included. I've also requested table or box fans to put me to sleep and provide air movement - too bad the Marriott didn't have any. Always TIP WELL when you are brought a requested item & thank them with a warm grateful smile! There are 2 lobby bars - one in the middle of the lboby that's round, contemporary, pretty, comfy, but usually full and another Level 13 across the bank of elevators. Handy for meetings as they have a few tables near outlets for laptops - SCORE! Prices for drinks are high - $9.00 for a glass of Chardonnay and $7 for a bottle of Yeuingling. Much has been said on Trip Advisor & Yelp about the rude service but after I got into my room the people were all lovely and accommodating as could be! I had 2 ROOM SERVICE meals that were delivered faster than estimated, piping hot, & tasty with only one hitch. I was disappointed when the cheapest ($40) bottle of Chardonay listed on the menu for an impromptu afternoon wine & cheese party was found to be unavailable with a call back 5 min after I ordered ..OK, let's try next one ($45) .....4 min wait on hold...No? Ok, the next one ($51) 3 min wait on hold...Nope! The cheapest bottle of Chardonnay avail from the room service staff was $65 ...What the heck!? Miffed, I canceled the whole thing and met my friends at the hotel lobby instead where.....the elusive $40 bottle of wine was available. I never did figure that out, but buying the whole bottle for wine and cheese party for 5 was just perfect and saved $10 bucks! The doormen were lovely & hailed cabs quick as a wink but the concierge gave questionable advice when looking for a place to eat steak & seafood. They recommended the Philadelphia Chart House (well known to me because of their sister properties in Annapolis & Baltimore) but the reviews on Yelp for this one were HORRIBLE! We ended up going to the Capital Grille (see my review) that was just amazing. The walk from the hotel to the largest Terrace Ballroom going through the Convention Center is a LONG TREK! Like 5 blocks all inside & lovely but far, far, away! The Reading Terminal Market is also nearby with stalls of food & other delectable just make sure to keep your purse zipped & secured - a friend of mine had her wallet stolen whilst there this week...and that was just a shame! WIRELESS Internet was NOT FREE & had some odd charges but it was fast & reliable. I'm still mystified how the Hampton Inn can a offer free brekkie and free wireless but fancy shmancy places like this can't or....don't. All in all my 7 nights at the Marriott Downtown were great. Clean hotel, nice refurbished rooms, LOVED having HBO for my True Blood & Game of Thrones fix and staff that really - if approached with a warm smile, were gracious & accommodating! Thank you!

“Worth the wait!” This hotel has been on my list to try for a number of years, but I just couldn't get a good rate. When I finally caught a deal, I booked it! Very much worth the wait! Room was not big, but well laid out, never felt cramped. Bathroom was very large by comparison, large sink top with room for all your "stuff", good lighting, swing out make-up mirror, shelf below for more storage, marble shower, and BIG towels! oh, and did I mention wonderful Molton Brown products? a (minor) word of warning - 4 of my 5 nights there, I thought I was hearing a faint coo coo clock and it was driving me crazy! On my last night, I finally traced it to the sound therapy machine set to a very low "rainforest"! The staff was wonderful! Housekeeping, front desk, bell and doormen, they all introduced themselves and asked my name and when I was planning to come back – everyone was genuinely very nice and made me feel welcome. For a hotel known for catering to the hip, fashionista crowd, this was a nice surprise!

“Nice Hotel, but Dreadful Decor!” The hotel is very nice, and is in a convenient location, but the apparendly brand-new decor is dreadful and depressing - especially in the rooms. The walls are completely covered in grey wallpaper, with grey curtains, brown carpet, and black -accented furniture. The designer basically took a gray, rainy day and brought it indoors. While I'm not fond of modern decor style to begin with, I have seen it done well other places (such as the Westin Boston and the Westin in Ottawa), and the color scheme here is really awful. Too bad, because it is otherwise a very nice hotel. The bathroom was nice - reasonably spacious, and with enough white to lift the gloom of the rest of the room. Nice fluffy white towels. The breakfast buffet was good, with only a few hot choices, but lots of fruit, nicely displayed. We did the King Tut package, which came with VIP tickets to the exhibit at the Franklin Institute, allowing us not only to go on a flexible schedule (rather than booking a specific time) but also to bypass a significant line when we arrived at the exhibit. A good way to go. If you really like modern decor, you may love this hotel. If not, be forwarned.

“Much Nicer Than a Typical Convention Center Hotel” We booked our room at this property last minute, using Hotwire. I was pleasantly surprised at what a wonderful hotel our $60 nightly rate got us! Although this hotel is located at the McCormick Place Convention Center, which those visiting the area should know is NOT downtown, it is still easily accessible to the downtown area by Metra train service, just a five minute walk from the hotel lobby. When we arrived, we were greeted warmly and professionally by the hotel front desk staff, which doesn't always happen when they find out you booked the "cheap rate" on Hotwire. The lobby and rooms were immaculate and well decorated. Overall, it was a great stay. I would recommend this hotel and would stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Inconsistant Staff (Some + / Some -) // Lack of attention to detail” We stayed at the Crowne Plaza for two nights on a personal stay. Due to challenges with this hotel during my business travels, this hotel is a reluctant choice as of late. Though some of the staff is great, for example the bellman, executive lounge staff, and some front desk staff were excellent, others are less than stellar. There is one particular staff member at the front desk that is complacent to downright unfriendly and has been this way for quite some time, and nobody on the executive management staff seems concerned, given this keeps going. Overall, the hotel seems to be well kept, but it beginning to get shabby in places, from lack of attention to detail. The lobby area is nice and welcoming. They have a free business center with two computers and printers. All in all, a convenient location, (though not a great neighborhood) Parking is free. The rooms are nice, they are clean and recently remodeled, but rather small, especially the bathrooms. Bathrooms are small but functional. The beds are comfortable, and the rooms are equipped with nice HDTV’s. Climate control works well, and you can leave the blower motor on for white noise. The hotel has a full restaurant, bar, and room service. They give you a cookie on check in as well as a drink coupon. (probably as Priority Club Platinum) Upon check in, the front desk was friendly but the team assigning rooms failed to read my profile, and put us in a room near the elevator that smelled of stale smoke. To the excellent staff members credit, he moved us to a nice suite down the hall upon request. He did forgot to give us the breakfast coupons that were supposed to be provided because the executive lounge was closed over the weekend, but this is a simple omission and was easily fixed...no big issue. The hotel has a small but nice pool and hot tub area (but lots of traffic noise) out back, as well as a small but nice enough workout facility. The pool was supposed to open at 8am but was still locked at 10am. After repeated requests for towels at the pool, which was not followed up on by staff for over an hour we finally got towels, but taking them from a housekeepers cart. The towels were never stocked, till we complained several times near 3pm. (Same dirty towels about all day) The breakfast is rather good and the staff is friendly. Had the breakfast not been included in our rate, there would be a $12 charge per person. Given it includes full breakfast, juice, tea, coffee, etc.....it’s not a bad value. There are several choices for meals around, in the form of chain restaurants. Walking distance to Pappadeaux. Of course the great dining options downtown are only 10 minutes away. When we asked about late check out as a Platinum Member (a benefit of the program) we were met with surly resistance by the same unfriendly front desk staff member referenced above. Later that evening we checked again and the cordial staff member who checked us in the day before said that we would not have any problem with late check out and to remind them in the morning to ensure housekeeping knows. That is a night and day example of poor versus excellent customer service. We prefer to stay downtown, but this is a location is convenient to downtown and our corporate rate led us to try for this personal trip....I don’t see that happening again. Not that we mind staying outside downtown, but rather, this hotel fails to perform. For the regular going rate I would never stay here, and it is a challenge to want to stay here even at our reduced corporate rate.

“A real disappointment” Palomar review We were put in a very small room (Cruise ship cabin size) rm 519. Cheerful staff, but not really helpful. We asked for additional towels, but they never arrived. The front desk did not have any change for tips (no change for a $20). The Fifth Floor lounge is supposed to close at 12:00 on Friday, but was not serving any more after 11:00pm. The in room safe is located in the small closet, need to remove bag stand and any luggage in closet to access room safe. Could be considered an extra level of security. $36-per day parking charge is the highest I have ever paid. take BART then cab it. There are the usual assortment of bums and winos on Market Street, but not in front of the hotel. This place is not worth the money-definitely not a 4 star property in my opinion. The view of Old Navy from our cabin was a new take on window shopping , some interior rooms had a view of a garden with fountain. comfy bed, very sm bath, pocket door, nice furnishings in room. Other rooms seemed a little bigger than ours. We did not have time when we checked in to request another room. I don't know if it would have helped. Newspapers available only if you ask they are not offered or provided with room service breakfast.

“Great Hotel!” The Hotel Carlton is a gem! Decent location, albeit a bit of a walk from the center of town (i.e., Union Square) but only about a block or so away from the main Muni lines. Charming rooms, comfy beds, inviting lobby and the staff were some of the kindest folks we had ever encountered. Willing to go above and beyond! The restaurant on site is excellent. Service was a little off (we had a newbie server) but food is absolutely fantastic! The only complaint was the super thin walls. Otherwise, a great hotel. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great Stay” My wife and I stayed here during the ending of October visiting friends in Denver, Fort Collins, and also attending the Denver Bronco game. This was the last stop of a Chicago, Denver trip. Since we stayed at other Residence Inn's in our past travels, we knew what to expect from the hotel room and the Denver one did not disappoint. Here are some additional information: Checking In: Checking in was no problem, the front desk person was very helpful. Just a side note, there is no bell person so you do have to lug your own luggage to your room. The hotel does have luggage carts for you to use. Room: The room was a typical Residence Inn with a kitchen, sepatate living room and the bedroom. The best part I like is the bathroom sink is outside the shower/toilet room so two people could get ready at the same time. Location: The hotel is located one block away from the 16th Street Mall. There is a free shuttle that goes on 16th Street Mall so that was great. However if you decide to walk the mall, it is not bad. There are several restaurants and stores on 16th street mall. Things to think about: -The hotel has one of those elevators where it is only operated by your room key. Just make sure you have the room card key available when you enter the elevator. -To enter the parking garage, as soon as you enter the driveway, right before you turn up to the garage entrance, there is a place for you to swipe the parking garage card (it's a separate card than your room key). The first time we entered, we could not find it. Once you find it, it's not a problem after that. -Parking is not free, there is a $22 charge per night. Internet and breakfast: Both are included with the hotel charge and both was great during our stay. Overall, this hotel was very good. My wife and I had no complaints, we would definately stay there the next time we are in Denver.

“Good location, Clean hotel, some updating needed” I stayed at the Doubletree because I had to attend a morning seminar at the Supreme Court building across the street. The room was very spacious and appeared very clean and well-maintained. With some new furniture, this room would be perfect. It seemed that the one room that has been updated recently was the bathroom. The parking fee is ridiculous for Columbus, but this seems pretty standard for most hotels, no matter where you stay. The front desk staff was fantastic. I had the honor of staying on the same floor with a bunch of giggling tweens, but the front desk staff, with their walkie-talkies, kept the group in line and I slept well with no distractions. I also had a lot of problems with my key-card, which had to be programmed twice, but on the second try, one of the staff escorted me upstairs and offered to let me into the room if there were further problems. There were some lighting/electrical problems with my livingroom lamps, but all in all, a very pleasant stay. WIth a little updating, this would be a very nice hotel, especially for downtown Columbus.

“Fine place for the price” This property is surrounded by a number of pricier hotels (including the very similarly named Marriott Copley, a different place), but it's fine for the price. My room was a king that was well appointed for the price, including a good bed and simple-to-use alarm clock (as opposed to the more and more common hotel offering that requires a manual and lots of luck just to set the alarm, one of my pet peeves about modern hotels). The Internet (wired and wireless) was free, reliable, and fast, and the room had a quite usable pullout computer table. A few gripes: The room temperature controls took a while to figure out, but worked fine once I did. The hotel breakfast room had a buffet (not included; it ran about $10 for the continental and $15 if you wanted the fuller breakfast), and the selection was a little skimpy; but on the positive side there was a quite capable waitstaff to help you. And there were no washcloths in the room when I arrived, easily fixable but one extra step to get the room in shape for my stay. Despite the minor drawbacks, I would recommend the place. It was a good experience, and I would come back.

“rough night sleep although bed was great” This is a renovated hotel and they did a nice job. Very clean and the bed was VERY good. The internet connection was slow and the complimentary breakfast was ok, nothing special. Upon first impression, I would have rated higher but I probably got about 2 hours sleep because of noise factors....most that are beyond the hotel's control. The only thing that would be within their control was the A/C/heater....it's one of those that turn on and off all night. When it ran, it pretty much drowned out most noises but the minute it stopped, you could hear the planes landing and the airport is obviously active at midnight. But I did pick this hotel because of the close proximity to the airport. But the worst factor was the people, not sure if they were guests or neighborhood hoodlums. About 2 am, a very loud fight broke out in the parking lot outside the window. The police were called and they patrolled the area at least 5 times. On one hand, it was for our safety but on the other hand, having to deal with the bright lights peering through our shades kept us up. And just when it became peaceful again, drunk people were very loud in the hallways. By 5 am, showers were running and you could hear the plumbing noises. So even with such a comfortable bed, we got very little sleep.

“Great Resort Like Property” This property is beautifully maintained! From the outdoor grounds to the club floor, everything was clean and looked fresh. The hotel is broken up into two buildings. The Marina Tower being the "main" tower with restaurants, pools, gym, tennis courts, Starbucks and club lounge. The Bay Tower is about a 5 minute walk along the marina and while not a huge deal it would be a little inconvenient if you were wanting to be close to the action of the hotel. The property sits on the marina and across the street from the airport, BUT this is not a typical airport hotel !! It is somewhere between hotel and resort property probably partly because of the expansive grounds and being on the marina. The rooms in the Marina tower are a tad on the smaller side, but have balconies and in excellent condition. Rooms in the Bay tower are a bit larger. The higher floors have wonderful views no matter which building you are in or which direction you are facing. Even the lower floors I imagine would have nice views as there is nothing around the immediate property but marina or bay. Full Starbucks in the lobby is very convenient for morning nibbles or whatever coffee concoction you like best. There is also a full service restaurant with a very nice breakfast buffet. Equally enjoying is the club lounge on the top floors which is a wonderful place to relax and watch the sunrise over breakfast or the sunset over appetizers and drinks. The front desk agents we encountered were very friendly and helpful, even when we asked to check in at 9am. Although a room wasn't immediately available, it was shortly thereafter and well before the normal afternoon hotel check in time. The restaurant waiter we had was also very attentive and friendly. And I have to give a big thanks to the club lounge waiter who was equally attentive.

“Nice Junior Suite” I stayed in a junior suite at the Sheraton Phoenix.... so my review is based on this room type. The two room suite is very nice. While it is not luxury, it is very nice and comfortable. The bed was very comfortable. The temperature of the room was perfect... I was able to control the temperature. The room had fantastic views of the city. It too has a great gym! I enjoyed my stay and would consider staying here again.

“Comfortable, practical, clean, in the center of Hollywood. Walk to the sights!” Los Angeles is one of the least walkable cities for tourists to come enjoy without the hassle of renting a car. However, this Holiday Inn Express is located just around the corner from the tourist-magnet Hollywood Walk of Fame, Grauman's Chinese Theater and other related points of fun, albeit tacky, tourism about Hollywood and Los Angeles. While small reasonably-priced hotels are everywhere in Los Angeles, many of them are tacky and don't feel very clean. This Holiday Inn was an exception to that, with clean big rooms, soft good linens, functioning air conditioning and a GREAT continental breakfast. (a welcome hallmark of the HI Express chain) Getting going in the morning with breakfast and sightseeing was incredibly easy at this hotel. And getting home late at night from restaurants and nightclubs was equally easy and foolproof. Would stay here again the next time I'm out on the scene in L.A.

“Huge hotel so be prepared to walk.” This large hotel just above Dupont Circle is a convention favorite. It is very large, shaped in a curved V like a pair of wings and has ten floors. That's a whole lot of guests. It is built for crowds. The tenth floor, where I stayed, is reserved for gold and diamond level members of the Honors program. It is accessible by using the room key in the elevator, although the rooms seem pretty much the same as the rest of the hotel. The club offers free soft drinks and snacks, although a glass of non-descript wine at $13 per glass was no bargain. There is a continental breakfast daily, as well. My room was typical and comfortable. Well worn but clean. I will give them credit for the cleanest hotel bathroom I have seen for a big hotel like this one. It was immaculate. I do wish there had been bathrobes .....but that is just something I like. Plenty of towels and amenities came with the room. I really wish that the walk from the elevator to my room at the end of the hall had not almost literally been five minutes, but then again, it was quiet.... except for the roof repairs that made daytime rather noisy. Amazingly, no room wifi, so that made for a full lobby. They really have to make this a priority. While I would not use this as a vacation location (Metro is four blocks away and no real tourist attractions in the area) it is fine for business. It is a big place, impersonal, but I had no problems.

“solid experience, great location” great doormen; older hotel that has been renovated; my room was very small but quiet(2712); no view but preferred the quiet. i told my wife it was about the size of our master bathroom at home. Concierge lounge was a zoo- seemed like everyone in the hotel qualified? Exercise room was fair. However, the location was great for all of my meetings and dinners. starbucks one block south.

“Very good” Convenient location to Metro, breakfast buffet was fabulous! Service was impeccable, various snacks and filtered water at check in. Fresh flowers throughout. No noise in hallway or from neighboring rooms, very quiet. Meeting rooms clean with good service. Bathroom in room could have been better with more amenities given this class of hotel. I did not see or use the pool or fitness area so won't comment on those.

“Perhaps not the Best Option for the Business Traveler.” I am normally the first one to gloss over the "one star" reviews and simply chalk it up to someone who is simply impossible to satisfy. I am perhaps one of the most laid back and easy going travelers you are going to come across. Give me a nice location, a comfortable room, and a decent hotel restaurant (if its too cold to go exploring) and I am a happy camper. We were flying in for a morning meeting and opted to come in the afternoon prior to rest up and be close and well rested for the meeting the next day. The check in at the Lenox was very quick and very straightforward. They were able to check us in quickly, make some suggestions about what to see in the area as well as were to eat if we were looking for something interesting. The hallways on the floors that have rooms are very interesting and very wide, it was nicely done with nice accent lighting which truly offered that "boutique" feeling, however the rooms themselves are small. It doesn't really bother me, as long as you can fit a King sized bed, a TV, and room for my suitcase I am fine, however I couldn't have stayed there for more then a few days without feeling like I was in a cage. The most disappointing thing was the bathroom, I kept looking around for hooks to confirm my fear that they simply converted a closet into a bathroom. I am not a massive man by any stretch but the space around the toilet did not make for comfortable sitting, and I kid you not I almost stepped into the toilet as I came out of the shower. The bed itself; solid. No complaints, I slept well, the alarm worked. However and perhaps this just me, I was a little thrown off that there was no phone on either bed side table. That is annoying for me but perhaps would be a non factor for many travelers who simply do not use the hotel phone anyway. The following morning however was when it all came apart. We had shipped a package to the hotel, which had arrived the day prior to our check in. We asked the front desk if they had received it, and we were told they did not. They insisted that hotel policy required any packages to be delivered immediately to the guest or handed over at check in to the guest. We were told several times that any packages for guests were left at the front desk and if it was not in their hands they had not received it. Originally we assumed it was a FedEx issue; We went to our meeting and apologized that the material had not arrived with the hope that the package would have arrived by mid morning, we called the hotel twice in the morning to see if it had arrived and they very adamant that it had not. We were finally able to reach our logistics department to get a tracking number, and it had been delivered and signed for by the front desk the day prior. Once we called back and explained it had been delivered they found the package within five minutes, I guess they actually took the time to look this time. Aside from embarrassment this caused at our presentation, the main reason why this was so frustrating was because no one took the time to look for the package. Three different employees insisted that hotel policy was to inform the guest immediately on receipt or during check in. They relied so heavily on this policy that no one bothered to even look for the package, which as explained took all of five minutes for them to hunt down once we explained it had been delivered the day prior to the front desk. This is an aesthetically stunning hotel; the curb appeal and the lobby appeal are wonderful. Its in a great neighborhood in the heart of Boston and very convenient if you are seeing the sites. In short; as a tourist this is not a terrible place to stay. However its very clear that the tourist is their niche, and there is nothing wrong with that. From a business travelers stance, this hotel simply lacks the mindset or the interest. We stayed at the Back Bay Hotel during our next stay and they seemed to be far better suited for the basic needs of a business traveler, so its pretty clear a Boutique hotel can be the best of both worlds; just not in the case of the Lenox.

“slooooowwww.” I stayed here on business in November. Arriving on a thursday evening at 7 PM, I waited more than 20 minutes to be checked in because there was only 1 person at the registration desk. Eventually another one came out. Lots of hassles getting the wireless internet to work but I eventually got it to cooperate. At least it was fast - wireless N. the hotel is modern and well appointed but the service leaves much to be desired. The room was large enough and comfortable, but the bathroom is on a par with Japanese business hotels in size.

“Not clean...but flexible check-in times” I requested a room with a fridge which are only accessible by stairs on the second floor; no elevator. The hallway smelled of smoke although it was a non-smoking room and it passed my white sock test (read my other reviews to understand). The bathroom was gross! The floor was caked with a cleaner buildup--think Swiffer wet jet but never using water to remove the residue. The air conditioner was so loud and old! The breakfast was good and very diverse. The check-in times were very flexible, I checked-in early and during breakfast a family checked-in early and were even able to enjoy the breakfast since the hotel employees were late to work. The only downfall was a not so pleasant guest with a sense of entitlements to immediate access to the hotel's computer although I only spent six minutes on it. If she felt entitled, I think she should have paid for a room next door at the Fairfield Suites.

“Brilliant!” Spent 3 nights here in April ( before we found ourselves stranded in NYC) Have no complaints at all. Room was great size, comfy, clean & had fabulous view of Times Square. Only little niggle was that the whoosh of the elevators goes on 24/7 & can be a bit annoying if your room is close to them. This hotel does exactly what it says on the tin...it's big, busy & right in the middle of Times Square and has a brilliant buzz. Good security too. We had booked for 2 shows on Broadway & the hotel was practically next door to both of our venues ( a happy accident). The restaurants nearby are mostly chains & quite pricey. You should walk along to 9th Avenue where there are loads of independently owned restaurants. Giorgio's Country Grill has great pasta. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

“Problems but willing to address and work out” Stay was not ideal and I did have issues but in this instance both the staff involved, the front desk and notably the general manager (Mike Powlen) all willing, available and interested in resolving. I more impressed by the willingness and desire to fix problems than perfection Some rooms are a little tighter than others (see the picture of room layout with some rooms getting squeezed for space) but Hey...its NY

“Very nice place to stay.” We spent two nights here. We wanted to be in the Dupont Circle area and this fit the bill. The hotel room was very large with a balcony -- so nice to open the door and get the fresh air. My only draw back was the size of the bathroom with the shower/tub and toilet -- it couldn't have been any smaller -- I know you don't need to spend much time there but it was tight. Staff were very helpful. You can get to the Dupont Circle metro -- only the 19th street entrance is closed so you have to go to the 20th street one on the northern side of the circle. Foggy Bottom metro is an option as well but a little longer walk. Firefly restaurant is downstairs and a nice restaurant -- however there are lots of options around the area. Bread and Brew was very good for a sandwich and the bagel place across from Hotel Palomar is excellent -- both where the locals eat. I would stay there again. Also wireless internet is free when become a Kimpton member. Only negative was room wasn't ready when we got there and they said they would call when ready, but didn't -- not a big negative but a text would have been nice.

“Bien en apparence... seulement” Habituellement je vais au Boston Harbor Hotel et j'avais envie d'un hôtel plus moderne. A l'arrivée le Nine Zero est moderne jusque ce qu'il faut, joliment décoré, accueil assez sympathique. Déco de la chambre moderne,fonctionnelle et plutôt agréable. En revanche, après 15 minutes dans l'hôtel on est vite déçu : la douche fuit de partout et après la douche, la salle de bain devient une véritable piscine, 4 serviettes pour tout éponger. Quand vous ouvrez le mini bar avec la clef, la porte vous reste dans la main !! On entend tout ce qui se passe dans la chambre voisine. Enfin, je descends 2 minutes faire une course, je remonte ma clef ne fonctionne déjà plus, je redescend à la réception qui m'explique qu'elle ne peut pas me la refaire car je n'ai pas d'ID, même si je lui explique que tout est dans ma chambre !!! Après 10 minutes de négociations, j'ai eu le droit de retourner dans ma chambre. Comme beaucoup de ces hôtels modernes, l'apparence est très positive et ensuite tout se détériore et surtout le service A éviter

“Just OK” This feels like one of those dated Sheratons that I generally try to avoid. The funny part is that I think this hotel recently changed from a Hyatt to Sheraton -- the elevators still say Hyatt on the operating certificate, the in-room TV system still has the Hyatt logo and there were a few other places you can see the Hyatt name. Although Sheraton seems to have taken over the property, I didn't see any signs of renovation. Actually, I take that back. The front desk told me that I was in a newly renovated room, but it certainly didn't feel new to me. It had low ceilings, was dark, and just felt old. It was clean, but the style was out of date. To be fair, we had an incredible view right onto the Ohio state capitol building. And the gym at the top of the hotel was quite good and included an even better view. But the overall property was pretty blah and the room itself was just adequate. Not what I'd expect from a Sheraton, especially at this price point.

“Grand old hotel near the museums and Grant Park” My husband and I went to Chicago this past weekend and stayed at the Chicago Hilton for 3 nights. We got the room off Priceline for $95, which I thought was decent for peak summer season. At check-in I was able to easily and quickly request the type of room I wanted and they also were able to upgrade me to concierge / Executive level for $50 per night. We were there with another couple (shared a room) so that cost was pretty reasonable when you consider the free continental breakfast every morning. The room: Since we got Executive level, it was quite nice. Large, with a pretty corner view of the museum campus and Soldier Field. The only complaint I have about the room is the bathroom was on the small side. The beds were very comfortable, although a bit on the soft side. Since we were up on the 24th floor, we had minimal road noise and it was good for sleeping. The room was always cleaned nicely and there was a turn-down service with good chocolates every night. AC worked great - no complaints here! The Executive Level perks: We were on the 24th floor, which is the same floor that the Executive Lounge was on. The continental breakfast was adequate, although very busy! They had bagels, muffins, cereal, fruit, yogurt, etc. The usual for this type of breakfast. The one perk I did like was the room was open all day for guests to get coffee, water, or pop if you were thirsty. This was very nice since the rooms only had an already-full mini bar for a fridge. As I said earlier, the room was also quite large - which I know was an Executive perk since I had read many reviews of how small some rooms were. Other amenities: We didn't use the parking as I think $43 / night is highway robbery! I did notice some surface lots in the area that were as low as $22 / night though, that seemed quite cheap. The pool and hot tub area were very nice although busy. There were plenty of towels and the outside deck was a nice touch. Overall, I would stay here again if doing a primarily sightseeing trip to Chicago. This hotel is much closer to the museum campus and the Art Institute than it is to the Mag Mile shopping area. We walked a lot and used the "El" system to good advantage - the closest subway stop is only 2 blocks or so from the hotel.

“Great base for a DC visit” This was my second stay here, but the first for leisure. The location is hard to fault especially with the proximity to the Blue/Orange lines of the Metro. We had no difficulty finding an array of dining choices nearby for both dinner and breakfast. Our room which was on the 6th floor was very comfortable, though it was a bit lacking in wardrobe / drawer space. The staff were always helpful and friendly. Bar is good with a really lively evening atmosphere.

“Fine airport option” By wife and I spent one night here. The shuttle was a little slow in arriving at the airport, but I think that was a function of the late hour. The room was clean and comfortable, if a bit strange in layout. We even got an upgrade, but I prefer the vanity bowl in the bathroom, not in the room. There was a fridge and the restaurant/bar appeared to have late hours. We were happy, too, with the very reasonable price we got. (about $125) The bed was comfortable, too. At first, the television did not work. The hand control dry cell seemed to be dead. However, a call to the front desk brought an "engineer" immediately and he quickly solved the problem with a smile- a negative turned into a positive!

“Wow--love this place!” Checked in after a long flight on a hot day. Asked a very pleasant and helpful front desk staff person about an upgrade and for a $30 fee, got a top floor corner room with an ASTOUNDING view of the East River and midtown. The room was very quiet, large, with a very comfortable bed, couch and large desk. The bathroom was sleek and well-appointed. Went downstairs to the Barking Dog for dinner and was delighted to find it one of those "neighborhood" places where I fell right at home as an older solo woman. The location, walking distance from Grand Central, was ideal for me. This is a place I'll return to happily!

“Right on the Cable Car Line...” Very nice hotel with standard Marriott quality touches througout. Prime location in the middle of San Francisco's touristy shopping district. Small intimate lobby lacking thAT impersonal feel of large convention style hotels. The rooms are on the small side especially when comparing square footage to more limited service hotels like Courtyards, Very small bathrooms as already noted by other reviewers, but the quality furnishings and amenties make up for these small nuiansces. Very nice and capable staff. All in all, a great stay.

“the long wait for hot water” This hotel is barely two weeks old, and the interiors certainly reflects that... the staff are friendly and professional, and the location not really that far away from Austin -- it's actually in Anderson Mill, which is about 5 miles out from the Arboretum area ... for some reason, it took more than 5 minutes of running the shower just to get it to luke-warm temperature. When I tried to turn the faucet to hot, it actually came off! Breakfast comes with the stay, with mostly cereals, muffins and bagels, with fruits... and several types of coffee avalable -- hot dishes include sausage and waffles. In-room wired broadband connection also is complimentary, while the lobby has wifi available. Fitness room has one treadmill, a stair-master-type and cycling machine... with a small pool outdoors. For those heading to Austin for a few days' work in the NW part of town, this is not a bad choice... yet certainly not the cheapest -- I paid 109 (before taxes) a night... can't complain except for the hot water problem... also bear in mind Austin traffic is horrible on 183 and just about all major freeways from 4:30pm - 7:30....

“Simple, effective, and did the job - but nothing special” Good location, good enough hotel, clean, and did the job. Sort of similar to one of those hotels you'd stay on I-95 but a bit cleaner and larger. The front desk staff at night were useless and the restaurant was incredibly expensive. Otherwise, cheap and effective hotel.

“Acceptable for One Night” We also won a Hotwire bid for the Crowne Plaza but weren't offered an upgraded room like others. We were tired and only there for a quick sleep but we did notice the very worn condition of the room (marks on the furniture, non-working lamp, etc.). The bed was acceptable but had pretty tacky decorations. The bathroom was huge as it was a wheelchair accessible room and the shower seemed to work fine. There is a restaurant and snack/coffee bar in the lobby. We arrived late so there were no dining options available and the nearest open restaurant was a fairly long walk. I quickly checked out the weight room and again it seemed acceptable but not great. There is a frequent shuttle to the airport shared with another nearby hotel. The hotel is adjacent to LAX but we weren't bothered by flight noise.

“Very Nice, New 4 Points” This hotel was formerly a Comfort Suites and Sheraton 4 Points bought it and totally renovated the hotel from top to bottom. Really nice place for the money (usually under $100). Rooms are well appointed with nice flat screen tv's, etc., a nice gym and pool as well. Just one problem with this hotel. It is located in a very suspect part of town. If I were a thief looking for a parking lot full of cars to break in to, this hotels parking lot would be like Christmas morning to me. It simply is not protected enough. The parking is down both sides of the hotel and not in the front where the staff can keep an eye on things. With the cars parked where they are, it would be VERY EASY for a thief to break in to a car or steal it as there is no one to stop them or even see them. I asked the staff if they had a night guard walking the grounds and they do not. They told me they had never had a problem and did not expect one. But there are at least 20 signs all over this parking lot warning you they they are not responsible. I have enclosed a picture of one and it is not just a warning, it is a very detailed legal entity that relieves the hotel of 100% of the liability in any way concerning your car. If they hotel thought the parking lot was safe, why are the signs every where? I have never seen signs like this anywhere. Other than this, the hotel was perfect.

“Nice amenities, but not worth the high costs” As many other reviewers have stated, this property is a great location for Wall Street, has friendly "hosts", great coffee, wine each evening in the lobby and free mini bar items. What's not too great is the room itself - mine was hot (they hadn't turned on the air for the season so there was no way to cool it down overnight), the lighting is terrible, the TV takes forever to get through all the intro screens, and the bathroom floors/walls are really starting to show the wear and tear. I requested a quiet room away from the lifts so noise wasn't a problem. I would stay here again if the price was right, but next time I suspect I will explore other local hotels that might better represent the four or five star standard.

“Not Quite Finished, but Nice” Bellman were nice and service was excellent. We got there early so we expected that are room might not be ready and it wasn't. Due to their renovations, the lobby is half of its intended size and very crowded. It looks like it will be nice once it is finished, but right now it is barely functional. We went out into the city for a while and came back and our room was ready. The room is new and very nice. The only dissapointing thing about the rooms is that there are no good views of time square because the face of the hotel is covered with signs. It also was dissapointing that there is nowhere to have a drink overlooking Time Square. The lobby has no view. I guess I am spoiled by the Marriott Marquis. Other than that the service was excellent and staff very nice and helpful.

“Great views, location, and friendly staff” The Westin Seattle met all our expectations--convenient downtown location, fine service and modern, clean facilities. We used Priceline and were pleased with the choice. We like a "walking" visit, so the downtown location allowed us to walk to Pacific Place, Pike Place Public Market, and the wharf area easily.
