It's easy to get to favorite foods at Il Fornaio or any of Tom Douglas's restaurants, as well as those of other quirky independents.

“Convenient and modern!” Use the Four Points hotel phone number in the Arrivals area to get put through to this hotel's main desk, so that the 10 minute shuttle can pick you up. The rooms are very modern and trendy, and the view is pretty good (although you're in an industrial airport area, so what can I say). Amazingly quiet, considering that planes are flying overhead. Breakfast buffet is a bit over priced, and the selection is only OK at best.

“Good hotel for MD Anderson” We stayed here while seeing a dear friend in the hospital. No online reservations, so had to call. A patient's name is required to make a reservation; they go it confused and made the reservation under his name. No matter, despite no email confirmation the reservation was there. The room was of adequate size and well-furnished with a comfy bed, desk and recliner. The room and bathroom were spotless. We have a white noise app on the iPad which we use in hotels to block noise which was a good thing as the toilet sounds from other rooms sometimes are noisy. We self-parked for $5; the 4th floor of the parking garage is conveniently on the level of the walkway to the hotel and the hospital. We had dinner in The Oaks Restaurant which is on the floor with the connecting walkways. The food was surprisingly good and fairly priced for the quality--$18.95 for the buffet including dessert. A glass of the rather ordinary house Chardonnay added $10 which was a bit much; coffee was another $3. We went through the buffet, however table service is available for those unable to do so. We saw several people who were obviously patients with menus being served. For breakfast we opted for Cafe Anderson, the cafeteria in MD Anderson, since we weren't terribly hungry. It's cheap and has decent coffee which is about all that recommends it. This is a very convenient hotel for trips which are focused on a visit to the Texas Medical Center.

“Key location to Chinatown, Little Italy, Financial District, Ferry Terminal etc.” This hotel is situated next to Chinatown, North Beach (Little Italy) and the Financial District with the Transamerica Pyramid on the next block. It is also not too far from Fisherman's Wharf, the SFO Ferry Building and Union Square. One would be spoilt for choice of good restaurants within walking distance. It is also one of the stops for the hop-on hop-off tour buses. The hotel lobby is quite small and facilities limited for it's class. One gets the feeling it's more like a boutique type hotel. Our room was not very large by American standard but the beds and pillows were extremely comfortable.

“Perfect for solo business traveler!” I have stayed at The Mosser twice now & find it to be PERFECT for the solo business traveler. They have these single, shared bath rooms (about $100/night -- a steal for SF!) which are quite small but very clean, contemporary & include a robe, closet, large flat-screen TV & sink. Since I've just needed "a place to rest my head" before all-day meetings it's been ideal. Although the "shared bath" thing is not my favorite, the shower is tidy & only shared with 3 other rooms & I've never had to wait. Same with the toilet. Plus, the location is fabulous. I felt totally safe & my room was very quiet. You are steps to Union Square, steps to Market Street, Starbuck's & Peet's Coffee are stumbling distance from the hotel. They even offer simple muffins & coffee complimentary in the morning. A few small cons: valet parking is expensive $30+ & it takes at least 30 minutes to get your car - not fun when you're in a rush! The single elevator that serves the entire hotel can be slow-- again, annoying if you're in a rush. And, finally, the room doors SLAM loudly (Mosser - will you please address this?) so that you can be awakened several times at night if you have inconsiderate "neighbors". But, I would still go back to The Mosser as these small details do not outweigh the good points of this hotel.

“Nice hotel in good location” This hotel is right smack in the middle of the 5th avenue shopping district and close to central park. If that is the purpose of your visit, it is an excellent place to be located. It is larger "boutique" hotel, so the room sizes can vary greatly. This is my corporation's preferred hotel so I tend to stay there a few times a year, and on this particular occasion I was upgraded to a spa suite. It was well sized, and nicely apportioned with a triple head shower (heavenly) and large jetted tub. It had a separate seating area, although the new age couch was not the most comfortable seating. it seemed like it was meant to be flattened to a futon. The large king size bed was very comfortable. This is one of those places that offers you a glass of champagne or water when you walk in, and I always love that when I check in after work. The fitness center is surprisingly large for this type of hotel, although you're so close to the park, its hard to justify using it, unless the weather is really bad. Overall, I like staying here and would do so more often if it was more convenient to my office.

“Unplanned stay, pricy, stay if you have too” Well, I had to stay here because of a tornado cancelled all outgoing flights this evening. Closest to JFK was this one that had vacancy. What a mess. Hotel was fairly old, but well kept. Room service breakfast was very good, but not worth the 50.00 for 2 pieces of french toast, and OJ! If you have money to burn, this may be the place for you, otherwise, I suggest the 4 Points down the road.

“Renovations complete, much nicer hotel than before” This hotel has been through a well-deserved renovation. The staff here is excellent, and was very personable. I'd give this property five stars save for that the restaurant has been replaced with one of the Courtyard line's single-serve cafe style experiences, which comes along with uncomfortable seating and comparatively slow service. (This is not the fault of the staff - it's the layout that makes these slow for customers.) I'm hoping that Marriott is listening...

“Great location, good for groups” Located close to Michigan Avenue, this hotel is a great choice for Chicago. Shopping and restaurants are in close proximity and there are a lot of bars in walking distance, weekends can get a little crazy in this area. It is nice to have the added benefit of a living room (with a sofa bed, so 5 people can comfortably fit in a double room), small refrigerator and microwave. The breakfast was pretty decent with oatmeal, a wide variety of cold cereals, waffles, omelets, muffins, fruit, and juices. Rooms are an adequate size; however the set-up is a bit inconvenient. The sink is located by the beds, so if the light is turned on in the middle of the night, it can wake up other people. There is a range in the feeling of spaciousness of the room, our room felt more comfortable than our friends across the hall (both were double rooms; we were in 1024, they were in 1021) since we had a larger living room. Some of the rooms have nice views, for example, we could see the Chicago Tribune building. A taxi from the airport to the hotel is about $35 (each way).

“Double-trouble- decent spot, noisy, recent renno'ed” So let's start with the positives. Location is great - 51st and Lex - subway across the street, Midtown at your doorstep, Grand Central and all kinds of retail (5th Ave) right there, Times Square about 15 min walk. Place was in v good shape-they must have renno'ed it recently - nice lobby, room small (but hey it's NYC) but well done, clean, nice TV etc. Check in was easy -lady was personable and friendly - we had a good laugh -even got a warm cookie. None of relentless generic interaction that you can find in many places here in the City. Negatives - room noise - from the street (ask for higher floors) but even worse from adjacent rooms and hallway. No credit for Hilton Honors unless you book yourself directly w hotel (which I had never heard of before ) and ridiculous charge for wireless (16/day/device yikes) and as best as I can tell no waivers. C'mon!! Net net good location, decent facilities, friendly staff but a nickle and dime philosophy.

“Average” I stayed at the Westin the night of 3/26. This was a last minute trip, so I was not able to book weeks in advance. All of the online rates started at $199/night. I booked the room online via hotwire.com on 3/24. I selected a 4 star hotel in the Galleria area and this was the one that I ended up purchasing. Of course, I did not know the name of the hotel until I made the non-refundable purchase, but I was okay with any 4 star hotel in the Galleria area for one night. The rate that I paid was $69.00 plus Hotwire.com's fee of approx. $16, brining my total to $85.00. At $85.00 this was a GREAT choice, but I would not pay more than $125 (at most) a night for this hotel. The hotel was definitely nice, but not sure if it is worth $199 a night. PRO: Comfy bed - Starwood properties tend to have SUPER EXTREME FIRM mattresses, but this one was ok PRO: Clean PRO: Great Location PRO: Valet and Self Parking available So-So: Noisy - I was on the 16th floor facing the North Dallas Tollway. I could hear lots of street noise. Not something that the hotel can control - so request an odd numbered room so that you will be on the other side. CON: Only shower stalls in the bathroom, no bath tubs CON: Did not like the “bare” look to the room. Felt kind of cold and empty. CON: Fee for internet I did not make use of the pool (not sure if it is even open) or room service, so I can not comment on those services. I included a picture of the cabinets that contain a safe for your valuables, a stocked fridge ($$$), snacks ($$$), coffee maker, and dresser drawers. I would stay at this Westin again, but only if the rate were below $125 a night.

“micro sized rooms but great location” i was heading out from the hotel and had to stops some friends to come up and see the size of the room. Barely enough space for the king bed and the bathroom had no place to put your toiletries. the location is great but the rooms....well.. and staff majority have an attitude, why i dont know theyre not curing cancer theyre working in a hotel like thousands and thousands of fine people

“OK but can be noisy on weekends” Between the price I paid for the room and the Hilton name I was expecting an outstanding property. It was nice but not anything special. The good: - Large room, with separate sitting area - Good housekeeping - Proximity to hiking trails. The bad: - Room was a bit shabby (scuffed furniture), had no view, and overlooked the parking lot - Not much close by. You really need a car, although there's a Safeway and some shops about a mile north. - 5 pools, none of which are big enough to do laps in - Exercise room (for which a resort fee is charged) is underwhelming, with a limited selection of equipment - Party destination, not a luxury resort, on weekends. I stayed there Thu-Fri-Sat. Thursday night was fine. Friday night the people next door dumped a whole bag of beer bottles off their balcony. Saturday night, the same room was occupied by a different group who were up doing shots and talking and laughing on the balcony. I called the front desk at 1:15 and 2:15 and it took 45 minutes each time before things quietened down. On checkout, front desk staff were relatively unsympathetic (and the ass't front desk manager was borderline rude), saying, "we have no control over who stays in our hotel rooms". True, but you do have control over how you respond to complaints, especially if your guests are paying over $125 night for your rooms. Overall, it's OK. I guess I was expecting this beautiful luxury resort and it's kind of just an ordinary hotel with a few more swimming pools.

“Okay but not memorable” Stayed here one night, reception and concierge were very friendly and helpful. The room was a standard room, clean and tidy. Getting to the room was more of an issue as the lifts are horrendously slow. As we were Priority Club Gold card members we were given 4 free drink vouchers on check in to use at the bar, so we thought that would be a nice start to the evening, but we were made to feel like unwelcome cheapskates by the barman because of the vouchers. The barman's attitude stopped us from then purchasing any further drinks. Breakfast was of a similar ilk, as we also had free vouchers for this as well. The staff were very untrusting of you, watching your every move as the vouchers only included continental. Many of the tables were left dirty. A great location to see all the highlights of Washington. The nearby metro at McPherson square will take you the Ronald Reagan airport for a few dollars.

“Great familiar stay, nice location” Marriott brands are always my favorite because I know what I am getting and the service is great. They were exceptionally friendly at this particular Marriott. The rooms were nice, the same basic courtyard layout. They will give you a double bed at the Marriott even if you book on priceline. Self parking was 15 bucks which is a bit higher than others in the area but the garage is very close and uncrowned. Sometimes you have long walk from your car to your room but not the case here. An interesting note is that there seem to be a lot of popular clubs nearby. I was here on the weekend and saw lots of girls dressed up pretty skimpily and the crowd at thr hotel was pretty young. Only downside that I can think of is that the hotel is kinda hard to find.

“Highly functional, very quiet, a good deal all around” The Pearl NYC is an excellent deal for the leisure traveler. It's new and everything works as it should. The Pearl offers an outstanding location on 49th Street only a few steps from Times Square. The style is crisp and utilitarian but lacking in any real aesthetic rationale. The breakfast is nothing to write home about, but if you like bread stuffs I'm sure you can get filled up before leaving the hotel in the morning. The rooms are large by NYC or European standards, the baths are mostly marble with nice enclosed showers. The bath room amenities are quite good and towels plentiful and quite thick. The windows are sound proofed (some occasional street sounds are unavoidable in NYC I believe) and there is no sound transfer between rooms or from the hallwalls. This is a botique hotel but the services are quite good. We got help with our bags, there is limited room service, a small but modern fitness room, and a free mornning newspaper available from the front desk. My only small complaint was that the room lighting is quite dim and the bed side lamps only have 57 Watt bulbs; probably not strong enough for most readers. We would stay here again, especially for the pittance we paid for our three night stay!

“Filthy and disgusting parking garage.” The filthy and disgusting parking garage was horrible for me to walk through and very scary! The entrance to hotel feels and looks like a service entrance. Once you enter the hotel the first thing you notice is the off track betting lobby which does not give a good impression. Once up the elevator and into the actual hotel everything seems like a normal Embassy Suites Hotel. The room was clean, spacious and well stocked. Make up mirror in the bathroom was a plus! Coffee maker in the room, comfy bed, smaller sized bathroom but there was an extra vanity in the bedroom which was nice. As a female traveller I would not stay there again--the parking garage was too scary and very dirty.

“nice, but not terrific service” The hotel itself is beautiful. The rooms are slightly small, like any older hotel, but they are fairly well-equipped. The service is not excellent, it is okay, and the parking is horrendous - use a nearby lot because the valet is not only ridiculously expensive it is not well-serviced.

“Love the location” We stayed at the Del Mar Marriott for $87 per night on Priceline. I really disagree with the two-star rating that Trip Advisor is giving this hotel - it is at least a three-star hotel. It is much nicer than a Holiday Inn or similar hotel. This is the second time we have stayed here. This time, it was much busier than the last time. There were a lot of group events going on so the bar and restaurant were constantly crowded. That is a sign of the success of the hotel, of course. The restaurant, Arterra, seems to be extremely popular with more than just hotel guests. As far as the rooms are concerned, everything was fine - comfortable bed, rooms cleaned on time, nice amenities in the bathroom. One thing I really like about this hotel is the location. Although it seems unexciting - it is basically in the middle of a business park so is not a good choice if you don't have a car - it is only about a 15-20 minute drive to downtown San Diego and 10-15 minutes' drive to Del Mar, La Jolla and Solana Beach so you have the option to go in either direction for dinner, beach or entertainment. It is also a lot less crowded and much mellower than staying downtown. I definitely prefer staying close to Del Mar when in San Diego, and I am hoping I get this hotel again next time I Priceline a hotel in San Diego.

“Good Location near Gayborhood!” Close to everything you may want to do in Center City. Nice view of Avenue of the Arts also, aka Broad St. The bar was comfortable & convenient. Not the friendliest bartender, but also not rude, just did his job. The restaurant staff was helpful also, & the food was quite good & extremely reasonable price-wise compared to other Hotels. Rooms are spacious & comfortable. We would have liked an in-room mini-fridge, but used ice machine instead. Enjoyable stay!

“Great stay!” Good location for northwest side of LA. Many restaurants/bars within walking distance. Whole Foods as well. Staff very helpful and pleasant. Room- clean, well appointed. Free WiFi. Two bottles of water free in room. Gym- below average. Woud stay again.

“very friendly staff - isolated location” The staff at this particular location was incredibly freindly. From teh guy who drove the shuttle from the airport, to the front desk, even just the staff walking around. My wife and i were walking towards the elevators, and a staff member was coming the other way, turned around, walked back the way she came just to push the button on the elevator for us. Everyone said "hi", just a very friendly staff. Great views of the harbor, but you got the same views from teh lobby or on the elvator ride up, so i am not sure it is worth teh extra money. the guy at the front desk offered the harborside view for the same rate if i took the 2 doubles instead of the king, but I had a 2 year old who much prefered watching the planes at the airport anyway. Very easy to get to from the airport, shuttle was there right away. You dont even need their shuttle if you dont want to wait because the airport shuttles go to the water taxi station/boat dock right next door anyway. The hotel is somewhat isolated for tourists. There is no other food except the hotel and the airport close by, and most of the airport concessions are through security checkpoints. The food a the hotel i found to be very expensive (although i am admittedly a budget traveler), but the breakfast buffet was $25! To get to the city, the water taxi is right outside, but kind of expensive (34$ round trip). The hotel or airport shuttle will take you to the blue line subway, or the silver line picks up at all terminals (terminal A is only a 5 minute walk from the hotel - all sidewalk + safe)

“Stay, Park and Fly” We used this hotel at the beginning of our overseas early morning flight out of LAX. We got a Stay, Park and Fly rate when calling the hotel, could not find one on their website or on the hilton website. But for $169 you got 1 night stay and 7 nights parking in their garage. This included Self or Valet parking. They also run 24 hour shuttles to LAX. It is a very nice hotel and suited for business travelers. The room was very comfortable and we did not find the airport noise distrubing at all. Since we arrived late, we valet parked and then decided to do room service, since we didn't want to get out of sweats to go down to eat or venture out to one of the local resturants. Room service was prompt and delivered on a rolling table. Food was good. Only complaint was that we ordered some plain pasta for a child and they charge the same rate a full meal with Shrimp and veggies. Kind of expected it. Like I said it was a business hotel and not really geared towards families or kids. We had 2 double beds for 3 people. Which they would have had 2 Queens. Down comforters and Plush pillows. Small, clean bathroom with premimum soaps. at 5:30am, 3 shuttles were waiting to take people to the airport. When one left full, the next one was right behind. They were very prompt on getting us to LAX. On our return at 9pm, seemed like it too forever for the shuttle to arrive at our pickup place. We saw several other shuttles come by multiple times for other hotels. (Haciendia hotel came by 3 times,). About 1/2 hour later it came and we quickly got our car from valet. I would recommend, but try to see if you can get a deal on the rate for Park and Fly. Found other hotels Haciendia on their website offered some good deals with Stay, Park and Fly.

“crash pad” I could not find a room in nyc so i went to the Carter. I had a black tie event at the Waldorf, so it was fun to go thru the lobby dressed in formal wear. My room was beat up but not too bad. they should clean better, replace the light 'globe' on the ceiling, regrout the bath, and empty the overflowing hallway trash containers. the cliental was not too bad. $100/nt keeps the real troublemakers out.

“Could of Possibly Done Better in Austin” La Quinta was an ideal stop over hotel for us on the way to Sea World San Antonio. Hotel staff were friendly enough but nothing special, we had to ask about their breakfast hours. Room (we had two Queens) was OK for the price we paid. Everything was clean and comfortable expect the bathroom which did need a good scrub or even re-furb to bring it up to spec of the rest of the room. Breakfast was OK but we felt the entire area needed cleaning once we arrived (1hr before ending). This would have helped with the overall impression of the hotel and your desire to eat breakfast there! There was staff nearby who could see the mess. Pool looked like a good size from what we could see. Location is not ideal if you want explore Austin, but ideal for us to hop straight on to the I35 to San Antonio. There is a I Hop right next door. We would probably seek out another hotel if we were to do the same trip again.

“Great hotel in a great location” So long as Sixth Avenue Inn keeps their prices low, this is an AMAZING value. I don't know what some of you people expect. Your reviews are really off the mark. Some of you people think you can pay $50 for a five star hotel and I don't know why your expectations are so skewered. You get what you pay for. With the Sixth Avenue Inn, you actually get a significant value for $50 a night (what I paid). First, the hotel is situated in a fantastic location, just blocks from Pikes Place Market and shopping centers, close to the freeway (for those with a rental car), and close enough to the action but far enough away from the chaos. The hotel has clearly been renovated and the lobby is quite nice. The outside looks rather shabby but once you walk in, you're greeted to bright lights and a very friendly staff. The staff was fantastic and accommodating, and especially the cleaning staff was lovely. As for the room itself, I had a Queen room and it was a big, cushy room, more than ample. The carpets looked new, as did all of the furnishing. Do you get a mint on your pillow and lots of amenities? No, but hello, you're paying far less for it. I really only needed a room to rest my head as I was out of the hotel for 18 hours of the day. So I was thrilled with my room. I will say that the BIGGEST downside to this hotel is that the walls/floorboards seem to be VERY VERY thin. I could not get much sleep because I could hear the person above me stamping back and forth in their room. I have to assume that all they were doing was walking back and forth but I could hear it very loudly. Initially, I was pretty upset and considered asking to have my room changed. But then I guess I got used to it and ended up just dealing with it. But next time, I will probably change rooms and not be so lazy about it. I am sure that the staff would have changed my room for me. Also, there were really loud, drunk people in my hallway but they didn't wake me up as I got in late myself. They quieted down after a while so I have to assume management took care of them. The bathrooms are a bit small here but it's not a big deal. Wireless Internet access is free and the service was pretty good. They appeared to have two computers in the lobby with Internet service. There is also room service and a restaurant attached but I did not try either. Between the loud floorboards and the thin walls, plus the street noise, this hotel can be a bit noisy and I'd strongly suggest earplugs. But you really cannot beat this deal for downtown Seattle. I found plenty of street parking for my rental car. They do charge $15 for parking. Again, the location is key. Being within walking distance to Pikes Place is a real luxury. Plenty of places to eat, drink, and enjoy Seattle. The area is more than safe and I was walking around at 2 am (I got hungry) and felt fine. I would definitely come here again, despite the loud floorboards. I'll just bring earplugs.

“Great location” Great location in downtown Indy. Parking garage attached but expensive. Updated room very comfortable. Fitness center was small and cramped into basement room with low overhead. Rest of the hotel was "ok". You're getting a great location.

“Always Good” I don't get to NYC often enough, but the last several times I've stayed at The Benjamin and it's always so easy. The staff bend over backwards to be helpful. The concierge got us tickets for The Book of Mormon ahead of time and although expensive, it was nice to have it taken care of so we didn't need to worry about it during our short hectic visit. The location is wonderful and the neighborhood is good. It feels safe and there are a number of decent restaurants near by if you don't want to go too far. It's about a 20 minute walk to the theater district and various museums and shopping are all within that distance. The subway is also very close. We arrived late on a Sunday night, so we ordered a fruit bowl for the next morning. One of the nice things about the Donatello is the little kitchenette, so you can have a simple breakfast in your room if you want to. However, the fruit bowl was expensive and not very good. After that, we bought our own fruit (there's a street vendor during the day right across Lexington). They also charge a lot for WiFi access in your room which always annoys me. My friend and her daughter shared the king sized bed and I used the pull out bed in the sitting room which wasn't real comfortable, but I did manage to find a decent spot on it and the special pillows were nice. This hotel is definitely a fair deal for the cost.
“Decent place for a quick nights rest.” Two and a half to three-star hotel that gives you a decent place to stay for the price, not many frills but clean and fairly comfortable.

“Nice airport hotel” This hotel is extremely convenient to the airport and is easily accessible. The suite was starting to show some age yet was very roomy and clean and I found the service personell to be kind and efficient. The fitness center was well stocked and was never crowded. I was not impressed with the menu at the restaurant so I chose to eat outside of the hotel. I also tend to grumble about having to pay for parking (7.00 per day) and internet (10.00) at these "nicer" hotels when budget hotels tend to include these ammenities. Overall, I would return to this hotel due to it's convenient location, friendly staff and clean comfortable accomodations.

“歴史を感じる古き良き時代のシカゴ” 玄関を入った瞬間に歴史を感じるホテルです。 食事をするにも観光「シカゴ美術館 ミレミアムパーク 等」するにも徒歩で出かけられるチカゴループ地区にあるとても便利なホテルです。 部屋はTWルームなのになぜか浴室が2か所ありました。古い建物なのに清潔感はあります。部屋はとても広く使い勝手はとても好いです。 部屋はインターネットアクセスは有料です。又グランドフロアーにあるスターバックコーヒーのなぜか有用です。気を付けて下さい。ホテルの周りにはスターバックス ダンキンドーナツ等無料のアクセスできる処が沢山あります。 ホテルのスタッフさんから聞いて隣のミラーパブというレストランはシカゴリブ ステーキがよても美味しく又安く食事が出来て夜も遅くまで営業しているのでお勧めです。 ホテルのヴァレー駐車は61$掛かるので注意です。 ホテルスタッフの方は皆さん親切にして頂きました。

“Great Denver hotel close to everything” Awww....we got in trouble in Denver! Not sure how we found our way home from happy hour at Mynnt (amazing Mojitos!) but since the hotel was close to everything, we managed! The hotel is 1 1⁄2 blocks off 16th Street, and about right in the middle making it easy access to anything from the capital to Coor’s Field (Go Rockies!) Our room seemed tighter compared to most Residence Inns, but was comfortable and very, very clean. We had just stayed in an identical room and Tampa that was recently remodeled, but didn’t compare to the Denver Residence Inn simply on the criteria of cleanliness. The hotel has a great (but busy!) breakfast and even dinner and happy hour several nights of the week. The lobby is clean and comfortable – great business center and friendly service. This wasn’t our first stay at this hotel, and it won’t be our last! Denver is a great place to visit – the piano’s on 16th Street was a fantastic idea – we enjoyed many a street musician, or tourist, who just sat down and played. PS -- two or more people? Limo service to the hotel is only $55 -- easier and nicer than the shuttle or a taxi.

“Good!” Though I read quite a number of negative reviews on this hotel, I do find my stay is pleasant and the service is outstanding. Plus: 1. The renovated room and the corridor look very good. I like the blue sky (or sea?) design and the new layout of the room - it makes me feel at home. There are also enough lightings to make the room as bright as possible. 2. The Staff is very friendly - no matter it is for check-in, check-out, and operator/guest services. 3. The fitness center is also excellent with up-to-date cardio equipment, though there are that many weighting equipment. 4. I like the design of the lobby lounge. It's a great place to get-together with friends. Negative: 1. The internet speed is unstable. It is very good for my 3 first days but it starts fluctuating a lot (and even sometimes disconnected) for the last 2 days of visit. I did call the operator (and the service provider) to help but nothing is improved. Surprisingly, I found the Internet speed at the lobby (which is a free Wi-Fi service at the lobby) is much better. Nevertheless, it is the best Sheraton Hotel (North America) I have stayed in the past two years!

“Good Hotel...great location” Location could not be better.Walking distance to Penn Station,Times Square,MSG,Rockefeller Center,etc. We walked even to High line, Chelsea Market and 9/11 Memorial.Many good restaurants close by.Rooms on the small side, but clean.Quiet inside but noisy from the outside ( maybe from the airconditioning of the next buildings). Good value for money considering that is NY and the hotel has free hi-fi and breakfast included. Computer in the lobby available for print.Small reception area, a little bit crowded sometimes. Overall the Hotel serves your purpose but is not remarkable.

“Great hotel in Chicago” Stayed at the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower for 3 nights in early April 2007. Very convenient location just a block from all of the shopping on the Golden Mile. Good restaurant at the hotel serving a la carte breakfast different from the usual fare and with a nice French twist. Dinner at the restaurant was also good. Prices are reasonable. Room is comfortable, only problem was with a card access door lock that usually required several swipes before opening. Excellent service from the bellmen to the concierge and front desk staff. Would definitely stay here again if visiting Chicago. Concierge recommended a small van tour, which was excellent. However early April is too early to visit Chicago as popular activities such as the boat tour of the architecture of Chicago was not operating yet.

“Very stylish” It's clear La Quinta has been taking notes from the higher-end hotels with the renovations to this one. Very stylish, with lots of attractive touches, at a value price. Breakfast was basic but fine. A couple minor check-in/check-out issues, but resolved quickly. If highway noise bothers you, ask for a room on the other side.

“Greeted and treated in style” We booked a park-view junior suite for our 30th anniversary and soon received a personal email from the front desk manager asking about our arrival time and indicating his willingness to assist with whatever requests we might have. Since we were arriving early in the morning, my husband replied that if they could get the room ready early, that would be helpful, and the response was that they would try. We actually arrived before 9 am, and not surprisingly, they had to store our bags for a while, but it was no problem to while away the time relaxing with some coffee across the street in the park. The bottled water the desk clerks gave us came in handy too, as it was in the high 90s that day. When we were taken up to the room, we were blown away by how big it was, especially by New York standards...especially the bathroom! We left our bags and headed out again. When we returned, a bottle of bubbly with a Happy Anniversary note and a helium balloon were waiting for us. Nice! The amenities that are provided are all of very good quality, although one thing you don't get is a coffeemaker. However, there are several excellent coffee options just a short walk away. During the week, guests can go to the complimentary happy hour in the Cellar Bar. (That more than makes up for the coffee in my book.) Classy bathroom amenities, a well-stocked closet of other items, and great chocolates each night at turn-down. They even provided earplugs, which were welcome due to the noise from a concert at the park. Service and housekeeping were professional and top-notch, friendly but unobtrusive. My only suggestion for improvement would be to add sleep masks to the list of amenities provided, as the large window wall let in quite a bit of light around the edges of the blackout shades. (This is obviously only an issue for those who are light-sensitive, as I am.) We had a very nice stay and would recommend.

“Beautiful accommodations, great food, perfect location. Here's a tip for newcomers.” We stayed here for a couple days to do some shopping in Chicago and enjoy the city. The lobby of the hotel seems to stay busy. The room we had was awesome. Not sure if all the rooms are that nice, but I've posted pics of our corner tower room. Here are some tips. 1. This our first stay at this hotel. We were offered to join the frequent traveler/rewards program for free. By doing so, our room was complimentary upgraded during our stay. So if you are not a member of their rewards program, now is the perfect time to join. 2. The car parking is very expensive. I parked for 6 hours and it was $32. Don't drive/park unless you must. 3. Awesome location on Michigan Ave! There is a Starbucks in the lobby, Michael Jordan's Steak House in the hotel, and shopping across the street. This hotel is a the start of most of the Maginificant Mile shopping so once you go out the door, you can walk and walk to all the stores. 4. The gym was nice but there is a charge to use it. The fee was included in our room rate, but they do charge others to use the gym. The pool was closed as well. You had to use the Marriott pool if you wanted to swim. Watch out for that. Enjoy.

“Another Night on the Town - Valentine's Day Style” Top notch hotel, great staff and quality room. Stayed with my wife recently for an early valentine's day celebration and had dinner at Parker's restaurant and went to the Shubert Theatre to see the Adams Family. The building itself is old which the style of the hotel embraces with the decor which makes it all seem elegant and adds to the experience. On this occasion, we had a basic room which is very nice. The room is big enough, the bedding very comfortable, however if an upgrade is availabe, I would recommend the deluxe room as it is much nicer. I think the biggest drawback to the hotel is the location. Although it is in the middle of everywhere you would want to go in Boston, it is located in a dark and dreary area with not much immediately accessible. It does have a nice lounge, the Last Hurrah and the on site restaurant (Parkers) is okay and Ruth Chris Steak House is right across the street, but otherwise it is a dark couple of blocks in either direction to Faneuil Hall or the Boston Common. (at least at night). I also did the online checkin which made checking in a breeze. We walked to the Shubert Theatre, through china town in the theater distict in little more the 15 minutes. All and all a great night starting with dinner at Parker's, the show at Shubert Theater, then back to the hotel for a night cap at the Last Hurrah.

“Conveniently located for a weekend in Boston” The Westin Copley has very modern rooms, updated amenities, and a convenient location in the heart of Boston. Walking distance from many restaurants and stores, I saved on cab fares being able to walk everywhere I needed to go. Check for Starwood and AAA discounts as well. You can also park across the street at the Copley Mall and save a few dollars on parking (the hotel parking lot was sold out when I stayed there).

“Doesn't seem worthy of the Renaissance name...” I stayed at this hotel for a week with a large group from work. It turned out to not be the best choice but we got a big discount, which apparently sealed the deal. Nonetheless, there are several things about this hotel that were less than ideal. The most obvious issue is the location. Why stay at this place, a $20 cab ride from downtown Denver, if you can stay in downtown? The answer is, you don't if you don't have to! The hotel is located right off the expressway in a rather barren, industrial-park type of location. About the only thing within a 10-minute walk of the hotel is a McDonald's, Arby's, and a Panera Bread. Oh yes and a Home Depot. A bit further -- maybe a 15- or 20-minute walk, is a Wal-Mart and some other restaurants. This is simply not the type of hotel designed for walking out the door and visiting shops and good restaurants. As for the hotel itself, they were in the midst of a long-overdue renovation. This meant a lot of noise if you had to go to your room during the day. The hotel has the style of something that was perhaps considered ultra-modern in the late 70's but now seems dated. All the halls open to interior balcony walkways that overlook the lobby. This isn't the best idea because sound from the bar and restaurant carries straight up. As a result, the bar closed each weeknight at 12 a.m., much to the annoyance of many conference guests. The room service food is considerably overpriced for what you get. $10 for an ordinary hamburger with no sides; $34 for a not-so-special filet (and add $5 for mashed potatoes). I suppose way out there, it's either take the hotel's food or take a 15 or 20 minute cab ride to LoDo. The rooms were ordinary. Comfortable beds, typical for Marriott. There were no proper dressers, which was a bit incovenient for storing clothes on a longer stay. Free internet is a plus, but unfortunately it's only wired internet -- not wireless. Overall, this is a place you might stay in a jam or if you get a great deal. But I don't see it having much appeal and I would not choose to stay at this property again.

“the best we had so far in Chicago” It was our fourth visit to Chicago as tourists and our fourth hotel in the city. On previous stays we were at the Ohio House Motel (low on comfort, great on parking), the Wyndham Blake (not up to its marketing), and the Belden-Stratford (very nice place, but not in walking distance to downtown); this time around the Inn of Chicago had a great offer through Skoosh.com, and we are more than happy with what we got for our money! First of all, the location is as good as it gets in a city this big. Next on the list of things you like to experience at a downtown hotel is an efficient and competent service. Big “check” with the Inn of Chicago. As for the corner room we were given, it was not only clean, quiet and spacious, it was tastefully furnished and decorated and very well appointed, too. We stayed for four nights and had a wonderful time at the Inn of Chicago. We will return!

“Comfortable elegance” The Palace is elegant--a great place for business travelers to head after a long work day. And judging by the families, a fun place for kids, too. I was here during the Christmas season, and the lobby featured gingerbread houses and a huge Christmas tree in the restaurant area. And though some upscale hotels have that "air" about them, this one is downright comfortable and welcoming. This place pays attention to details. Even though the hotel feels "historic," the rooms are comfortable, clean, and modern. The amenities were top notch, as was the (pricey) room service. You also get a choice of three newspapers--nice touch. And an indoor pool--really? In San Francisco? Though some reviewers ding it for being old, I have to disagree. I've stayed in "on their last legs" historic hotels, and this is definitely not one of those. The staff was cordial and helpful, the beds quite comfortable, and the elegant lobby is one of the more memorable ones I've seen. My only regret was I was here on business. Next time I'm coming back for some pleasure!

“Great location, comfortable room” Everything was as close to perfect as you can get during my week-long hotel stay at the Gaslamp Marriott. The hotel is next door to Petco Park, making it a great place to stay for ballgames. There are tons of restaurant and bars in walking distance of the hotel. The rooftop lounge is quite nice, though watch out for drunk people in the lobby and elevators attempting to access the lounge. The staff were all very friendly and spot on with answering questions. I was fortunate to be upgraded to a concierge level room that was large, had a great view, and extremely quiet. The concierge lounge had a nice breakfast with plenty of fruit to choose from. Everything was clean. The free wireless provided as a gold member was very fast though you had to log on every day rather than log on once at the start of the week. I ate at the breakfast buffet on the weekend and it was overpriced as expected although tasty enough. Try local restaurants for breakfasts rather than the hotel. I had a great stay and recommend staying here!

“Friendliest Hotel in San Francisco!” My niece and I went to San Francisco for three days as part of our Spring Break. We stayed at the Argonaut and loved it! We pulled up to the hotel in our rented car and were greeted immediately. Check in was flawless. We were told that we had been upgraded from our standard room. That was a nice surprise! The room was larger than most hotel rooms with the usual small (but a bit larger than other hotels') bathroom. Clean, clean, clean! This is the friendliest staff in San Francisco. Everyone greets you with a smile and a hello. I've stayed at a lot of hotels throughout this world but this one takes the prize for catering to its clientele. An evening reception is held from 5:00 to 6:00 PM daily with alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks. The New York TImes is delivered daily. I had a problem with the magnetic key. After replacing the key, I was asked, "Is there anything else we can help you with? DIrections? Places to eat?" These folks really want to help you! This hotel not only caters to humans but to canines as well. We didn't see any pooches on our visit but we heard that they're just as pampered as their "pawrents." The location is prime. The cable cars are within walking distance. Hop on/Hop off buses pass frequently. The Aquatic Park, Fisherman's Wharf, and Pier 39 are within walking distance. We didn't eat at the hotel but we had a wonderful breakfast at the Buena Vista, one block north of the hotel. Their Eggs Bendicts are out of this world. Yum! We didn't try room service or the in-room spa services. The maid service is excellent. We put our "Please clean this room" sign before going to breakfast one morning. We came back an hour later to a room that was clean and ready for us. I highly recommend the Argonaut Hotel!

“Good hotel, typical Marriott” We stayed here for two nights. When we checked in, the AC had been leaking water and the floor was soggy and gross. Called the front desk to be asked to be moved to another room, and within 5 minutes they delivered new keys to us for a room 2 doors down. Great service! Apart from that, it was clean and quiet, though a bit far from downtown (10 minute drive). Definitely nothing within walking distance.

“Enjoyed my stay” Decided to stay here instead of the expensive Hilton down the road where my meeting was being held. Not only saved money but my stay included a great breakfast. I did notice that the rate dropped after I made my reservation, so I complained to night auditor who did adjust my rate. I would recommend checking your reservation a day or two before arrival to see if a lower rate pops up.

“Big Hotel” I stayed in the Hilton New York, during the first week of January while on a business trip. The Hotel is located near Central Park and in walking distance to most of the "tourist" attractions but a cab ride from the business area of Wall Street; however, there is a lot of business on the Avenue of Americas. Hotel is very big and can create problems when checking in. Room was small, but expected for NY, however, it was clean and well furnished. The bathroom was small and cramped, with the shower taking most of the room. Breakfast was manic due to the large number of guests and was a matter of a refuel stop and not a relaxing start for the day. Selection was very good though, but as with most things in NY the price was high, particular with the $/£ exchange rate. Concierge was great for recommending places to eat, and we had three good evening meals on recommendation. The gym is good and well equipped, as previously stated in another review entry is charged. However, if you have a Silver HH membership or above you get in free. Overall experience was good, but that expected from big hotel with respect to service and attention. Rate was reasonable for city hotel of approx $250/night; they also did a good deal on the late check out. Would stay there again, but really prefer smaller hotels?

“Brilliant hotel for San Diego Cruise Ship Terminal access” This hotel is located within walking distance of the Amtrak station and the Cruise Ship terminal. We walked from the Amtrak Station at night and then to the cruise ship terminal in the morning with all of our luggage. The location is brilliant. The front desk staff are the friendliest and warmest staff we have ever dealt with. The hotel should be congratulated for this. The hotel rooms are a bit old and tired but if you are lucky enough to get a front room with a view of the bay, then who cares about the room. Waking up to this view was wonderful. I would fully recommend that you pay for and request a room with a view of the bay. If you are going on a cruise you wont find a better location to stay before boarding your ship.

“Super nice updated room near the pool” I was pleasantly surprised by the location of the hotel given the price we paid per night. We checked in and as we walked back to our room, we thought. . .oh no, this looks like an old motor lodge! Then we walked into our room and couldn't believe how nice and updated and big and clean it was. I would surely stay there again, but would request a poolside room. We had a friend who stayed in a small room in the older tower side and he said that his room was much smaller and looked old and outdated, so I guess the key is to request a poolside room. Again, SUPER convenient, only 1 block from Union Square and from the trolley car. About 30 minutes from the airport in morning traffic.
“Perfectly Good Business Hotel in Wash DC” Perfectly good business hotel in wash dc. Lobby could be less suburban, but other than that, not much to quibble with.

“Sleepless in Seattle.” This is a very nice hotel as far as the rooms and environment; that's why I did not rate it 'terrible'. See other reviews for room details, but there is a glaring, unforgiveable problem: The hotel sits right next to Interstate 5 (which, if you know Seattle is busy almost 24 hours a day) and the road noise is horrendous. I asked to be moved from my room to a quieter one and the desk agent assured me that the room was the quietest in the hotel. This is unforgiveable for modern, very nice hotel to have scrimped on noise insulation when next to a freeway. The rate here was $120, which is not bad for downtown Seattle, but I had to sleep with earplugs and noise cancelling headphones on. No lie. Find a quieter hotel people, you will be much happier.

“Wonderful stay” I've not been one to stay in a Hyatt because I normally find the Hyatt reservation fee a bit high for my budget. Because I had a colleague share a room with me and by getting a AAA discount, I was willing to splurge this time. Let me just say, I really enjoyed my stay. I immediately signed up as a Gold Passport Member to reap benefits. Now that I've tried a Hyatt, I am very interested in staying in one again. I loved all it had to offer! I enjoyed the gym, comfy beds, late check out and delicious breakfast. I like the fact I didn't have to worry about the room being clean and if I'd had to deal with noisy neighbors. The Hyatt is first-class in my opinion and I'm willing to "splurge" again for another good night stay. The only negatives are that parking was a little expensive and the bathroom toilet is not separate from the counter sink and shower stall.

“Average at best” Crowne Plaza Times square... stayed there last week 8th April, 2012. We had requested a Times Square view room, and wow what a view. As I recall the room was 3011 and right opposite the lifts which we thought would be noisy. But not the case. The food around Times Square was ordinary and expensive. The hotel was nice enough. the bar was on level 2 with virtually no view, the Manhattan cocktail was soo strong. The hotel had no safe, well a safe you had to swipe with your credit card... no will not do that, what if you lost your card or it was stolen... Had to have my passport with me all the time, was a pain. No fridge, no safe, was a water heater thingie, but no cups. So did not bother. The shower was the standard bathtub with shower overhead. The bed King size was comfy and clean and I checked for bed bugs, all seemed ok and after sleeping was ok, no itching. I had trouble sleeping 30 floors up, my body kept feeling it was falling, but did it for three nights, and glad to come home. The breakfast was underwhelming and the hotel in general was underwhelming - but expensive. One of our backpacks had been opened during the day, so not sure about the security, but all our electronic equipment was locked in a suitcase while we were out of the room because of the no safe issue. Next time in New York I would love to find an apartment and stay for longer and really look around, perhaps a month and visit other places. NYC is interesting and multi layered place, but a like it a lot

“Обязательный пункт программы в СФ :)” Мы останавливались в этом отеле 3 раза. Невероятное местоположение, захватывающие виды из окон. Не пожалейте, бронируйте номер с видом на Юнион. Отель состоит из двух частей - старой и новой. Не советую брать старую, если вы любитель больших пространств и тишины - достаточно шумно. Новая часть отличается просторными номерами и панорамными лифтами.

“Shotty rooms with confirmed bed bugs” I realize that bed bugs happen. It's kind of par for the course sometimes in budget hotels. At the same time, some of them manage to avoid them or rectify the situation with grace and reason. Not the case here in my opinion. In the first place, the rooms aren't necessarily clean in the first place. Sure, things are wiped down and walkways are vacuumed, but the dust build up and all out dirt along the sides and under the bed suggest cleanliness is not the highest priority. There was also water damage on the ceiling in the bathroom that no one even attempted to fix. The smoke detector was just hanging from the wall by its wire. Still, not too big a deal. It just seems like nobody cares about the place and its showing up in the details. Finally, we found a bed bug in one of our five rooms. We researched it and.confirmed it. After the heebie jeebies were through, we took the bed to the front desk and he confirmed it for us. Although he did move us to a different room, no discount was offered until we spoke to a manager the next day, and that was almost an insult at 25% off from one room, for one night. Aftwr what we will all have to go through (16 of us) to rid ourselves of any potential infestation, that hardly seems compensation. On top of this, we researched further complaints on this hotel and found our exact room numbers, 310 & 312 in other bed bug reports! Someone is dropping the ball here or just does not care about their guests. Avoid the hassle, stay elsewhere!

“Exactly What You Expect” I agree with most of the recent reviews; a very good hotel in a great location. If you have a relatively short lay-over at O'Hare this is definitely the best option. My wife and I stayed twice in one month; both to and from an overseas trip that passed through Chicago. The hotel is connected to the terminal so you don't have to go outside (at least from terminals 1, 2 & 3). The service at the front desk and bell staff was excellent; very friendly and looking to help. The rooms are Hilton airport hotel standard - good quality and functional. For being on site at the airport, both times I don't recall any significant noise in the room. The breakfast was great, as with most Hiltons. For dinner we found it good but not outstanding. Overall, it is not the cheapest option but if you are prepared to pay for convenience it is the only place to stay if you are just passing through.

“Will stay here again” - Super cheap for a major city - Free off-street parking - Large rooms with fridge and microwave - Free coffee and muffins in the lobby in the morning - Excellent location walking distance to Farmer's Market You really can't beat the price for such a great location - the Farmer's Market is my favorite place to visit while I'm in LA. We also walked to Canter's Deli the evening we stayed there - loved that. I wasn't expecting a five-star experience so was not disappointed. I disagree with the other person who posted that said the manager was ill-humored. He was quite pleasant to us - not overtly bubbly but certainly polite and when we asked what the checkout time was he said, "noon or one if you would rather" - very welcomed because it made it easy for us to take our time having a lovely breakfast at Farmer's Market on the day we left without having to move our car. I would stay at Bevonshire again.

“Good value for price” I booked a DDBL room for $149 the first night and $119 additional nights. I called the day before to add my sister's name to the room. She arrived before me and there was no problem. I ended up arriving a day later because of the big snowstorm. I called about parking and was told it was next door. This is false. It's at the beginning of the block, at 32nd and Broadway. It was $28/nite, more if you have an SUV. You drive in, they park it and retrieve it for you. Show your call tag to the front desk to get the hotel rate; they'll put a sticker on it (the parking is handled completely separately). Room was small but adequate, and clean. Free hi-speed was intermittent and unreliable. Breakfast on the 2nd floor was OK--donuts, bagels, yogurt. Also free Red Bulls if you like that. There's a sign up saying don't take food to room, which is ridiculous because the breakfast room is too small. Front desk staff all had thick accents. I think they were south Asian. Not particularly friendly or helpful, but they did their job. Housekeepers were friendly. Location is great. At the end of the block is the 34th St. Subway stop with many different lines. The neighborhood is lousy with restaurants and drugstores, including a 24 hour Walgreen's up on 5th and 33rd. By the way, the hotel is much closer to 5th than to Broadway or 6th. I'd stay here again if I got a similar rate.

“Guys Baseball Trip” Myself and two other friends decided to visit New York to watch a Yankee and Mets baseball game. Since we knew that New York was known for their small hotel rooms, and there was going to be three guys sharing a room, we decided to spend a little more and stay at the Doubletree since we could get a suite. The bonus was the hotel is located on Times Square. After reading the various reviews we booked a room on the Doubletree website and here is some additional information. Checking In: I arrived on a Tuesday afternoon after flying 14 hours from Honolulu. I took the Super Shuttle from Newark and was dropped off right in the front of the hotel. Since there was some construction going on and there was a scaffolding, it took about 30 seconds to find the front door to the hotel. It seemed sort of hidden. But then again maybe I was a little tired from the flight. When you enter the front door from the street, you take an elevator to the second floor to get to the main lobby. Check in was very quick because I was the only person and was assigned a room on the 7th floor. There was an option to pay a little more per night to get a "premium room" on a higher floor, but since the price was already $380 per night, I declined this option. Room: When I entered the room, I was happy to see it was a suite. There was a living room with a sofa bed and a separate bedroom. There was a little sink right outside the bathroom and a dorm size refrigerator. In addition there was two tv (bedroom and living room). The size was perfect for myself and my two other friends. The bedroom had one king size bed, so one person took the bed, another person slept on the sofa bed, and the third person slept on the ground. Again we could have paid extra to get a room with two double beds but this option was also declined. At night, the noise from the street was not bad, even though we was only 7 floors up. We would only hear the sirens when we was up. The curtains would block out the lights from the Times Square signs. Location: As others have mentioned, you cannot beat the Doubletree location. It is right on Times Square. It is about a 10 minute walk to Rockefeller Center and there are several subway stations either across the street or a couple minute walk. In addition, there are several Broadway theaters within a 5-10 minute walk. Yankee Stadium and Citi Field took about 20 minutes on the subway. There is a Starbucks and McDonalds right next to the hotel, but there are also numeorus restaurants nearby. There is also a CVS, Duane Reade, or Walgreens near by. Service: There was nothing to complain about the service. The doorman was very pleasant, the concierge was very helpful, and the front desk people was very nice. We did not use the restaurants so cannot comment on this. Checking Out: Checking out was a breeze, but we did check out at 3:45 am, so there was no one in line. Negatives: The only negative I have is the internet charge. I understand the charge and I am okay with paying for it. I just wish the charge was just a flat fee and not per device. My friend and I both used our computers one night and there was two charges for the internet. The front desk person did credit us back for one of the charges, but watch out especially if you have several devices that need to connect to the internet. Request: One request I have is since there is a charge to use the internet in the room and there is no charge in the lobby area, on occasion the lobby area was very crowded with guests using their computers to access the free internet. My requests is to install more chairs with tables so there will be more room to use the internet. Besides the above item, our stay was excellent. Despite the high rate, we was very happy with the Doubletree Guest Suites. The only reason I would not stay there again is usually I travel with my wife and we would not need the bigger room. However if I was travelling with more people I would definately stay at this hotel again.

“Your average Holiday Inn” Good location. Was in town for Yankee/Red sox game. Made mistake of getting valet parking. The fee was $36.00 for overnight parking. The garage around the corner charges less if you drive in yourself. Room was your average Holiday Inn. Bathrooms were small and needed to be upgraded, but they worked just fine. Pool was OK, nothing to write home about. No noise problems as I have read in other reviews. Construction behind hotel appears to be in final stages. Breakfast in their restaurant was a whopping $32.00 for 2 people. a 10 minute walk to subways and Fanueil Hall area restaurants.

“Wonderful wedding weekend” This hotel exceeded our expectations. My best friend got married here and it was a gorgeous outdoor wedding. The wedding planner there, Gigi, was amazing. She took care of everything for us--parking, awesome rooms on the executive level. The wedding party really received the royal treatment. The bridal suite was also filled with surprises for my best friend. And the lobby had photos of the newlyweds on their TV monitors, congratulating them. The rooms were so nice. Very spacious and a nice view. The beds and pillows are so comfortable. And the hotel restaurant was great too. I can't say enough about our experience there.

“Nice location and rooms but terrible policy about deposit” I had a conference at this hotel and stayed the night of March 12. The conference facilities are generally nice. The room was extremely nice with comfortable beds, high quality sheets and towels, and good toiletries. My room (on the 19th floor in tower 3) was very quiet as well. Most of the staff I dealt with were pleasant. I have one issue with this hotel. When I booked my room in January for a March stay, I was charged a full night's deposit. I have stayed at many hotels around the country, and i've never been charged a full night's deposit when staying at a run of the mill Hilton! The conference website did inform me I would be charged at the time of booking, so I was aware of the policy ahead of time, but I still believe the hotel is not providing good customer service in having such a policy. Because of the conference schedule, I really needed to be at that hotel and could not "shop around" which is why, I'm sure, the Hilton management has this policy in place. But it stinks all the same. I understand a credit card guarantee, and I could even understand having to pay a nominal deposit, but to have to pay the entire night's stay in advance seems a bit ridiculous, and for that reason, I cannot recommend the hotel and would not return here unless I had to. There are plenty of other hotels in San Francisco.

“Great Location, clean room, good service” Location is excellent for the magnificant mile. Near all the shops and 15 minute walk to Grant Park. Rooms were typical Courtyard Inn style. Clean and nice. As most hotels in a major downtown area be careful about room rates. They fluctuate greatly depending upon availablity (especially if there are any major conventions.) Check and double check (especially the day of arrival) for lower rates. I have seen this hotel charge upwards of $300+ a night because of high demand. The hotel is very nice but not that nice. Starbucks inside is a plus.

“Fantastic Spa room, but service had hick-ups” We had heard about the Palomar's King Spa Room from a friend, were very eager to try it out, and now we finally had the chance. I had signed up with their loyalty programme earlier to receive their email offers as well as the perks during the stay (free internet, minibar credt etc). We had only seen the pictures of the hotel, had never walked or driven by, so when we actually arrove with our car at the place, we didn't recognize the location. I saw it while we passed it. No problem, I thought, we'd just go around the corner and come back the 17th Street (a one way street) and do it one more time. Ha, not so easy! It took us actually 45 minutes to return to the same street, and since we had only one night and it was already beyond checking in time, I felt we were missing out. But this was of course our own fault. We stopped in front of the hotel and looked around. Shouldn't we be received by a valet here? I mean, they have no self park option. There were 2 other cars in front of us, but no door man and no valet in sight. But after a while he did show up, maybe he was busy with the other guests in front of us. It was cold, and so I went inside, leaving the rest to Hubby and the valet. Our luggage was then put on a wagon to be carried into the hotel, and Hubby had to ask the valet to also take his coat, as he would need it during the stay. (I am mentioning this because I found it strange that the coat was not taken with the luggage the first time around) OK, but now we were there, and our Spa Weekend was to begin. I am connected with Kimpton through Facebook and Twitter, and I had verified the password of the month ("Cheers") to get the promised surprise (whatever that may be, we had no idea, since this was our first time at any Kimpton property). We were greeted friendly at the front desk, I said "Cheers", and he smiled at me and also said "Cheers", and then continued our check in process. He explained they would offer a complimentary breakfast the next morning, as their regular facility (the bar in the same building) would be closed. I was so excited to be there, and English is not my first language, so I didn't fully understand it all. But Hubby understood it and told me later that he found it confusing, as I had told him before that we would have to go to another hotel for the breakfast. Hmm, good point. Back in time: at my booking in October I was advised by Palomar front desk staff to book a breakfast at LaCroix in the Rittenhouse Hotel, as they would have no breakfast for their guests on Dec 25. I could hardly believe that a hotel of this category would not offer any breakfast at all, so I had called several times to speak to various employees, but they all said the same. There would be no breakfast, and they recommended the restaurant within the Rittenhouse. I then booked that breakfast, and that booking alone required our credit card information, and we were notified that they would charge us a fee if we would either not appear or cancel it too late. Back to Dec 24, when we checked in. I had requested a high floor, foam pillows and a coffee maker for Hubby, and we got all that (floor 18 of 26). We refreshed us at the room and changed clothes, then went down for the wine reception in the lobby. That was very cool! They offered so-called hot toddies (never heard of before), consisting of a shot of Bourbon Whiskey filled up with heated Cidre. Very good!!! My second one got a hat of whipped cream, and that made it even better!! Meanwhile Hubby had shared his thoughts about the complimentary breakfast with me, and I was puzzled, so I went to the front desk and asked again. Indeed, they did offer that breakfast, it would be in the lobby the next morning, and I was now beyond my canceling options with LaCroix. I shared my dissatisfaction with the staff, they apologized and offered to take our valet fees off the bill, which I agreed to. At least they realized this was a bit of a messed up situation. Only a few days before they had sent me an email, asking me if there was anything else they could do to make our stay better, and in my opinion it would have been a good idea to tell me at that point that there would be breakfast. At that point I would have been able to cancel our reservation in The Rittenhouse. But OK, now it was done, and it was resolved fine. Our Spa room was actually a great experience! The views toward the south from the 18th floor were amazing at night, and imagine standing in the shower or sitting in that Fuji tub and looking down on Philly at night! I was so happy!!! I had brought my own Spa products and really took advantage of this facility! Hubby meanwhile went to his midnight mass, and I enjoyed my own spa, then tried on their offered robe (very comfortable and great textile quality!!), went online and watched a bit TV. We have no TV at home, so whenever travelling, I am checking out what is on TV at night. Not much to see this night, Joseph Ratzinger was hosting his show from Rome in full costume that night, mumbling Italian, and some American voice over was translating it for the US audience. Not for me, but there was nothing else on, and of course this was not the hotel's fault. It was pretty late by now and time to sleep anyway. The bed was very firm, which I liked, but the foam pillows were a bit limp. But I would manage, they had 4 of them on the bed. But that sound! What was this houling sound, almost like a faint (far away) fire alarm? I knew it was in the room, but it sounded really like a fire alarm a bit away. I eventually figured out that it was the climate machine at the wall doing that. It was also the heating unit at the same time, and it was coming on and off really every 2 minutes. We couldn't sleep like that, so we ended up switching the whole thing off. Since we had only one outer wall and were surrounded by heated rooms from all other sides, it was not a problem, the room didn't get cold over night. We were still wondering what the surprise might be. You know, that surprise you'll get when you say the "magic word" (or password) at check in. "Cheers" it was during November and December. We had no idea what we might get, and in order to not ruin any upcoming surprise, we hadn't asked. But now it was Sunday morning, and nothing had happened, and nothing was provided to us that we hadn't booked and paid for. We went out for our breakfast at LaCroix in the Rittenhouse, which was actually very nice (read my report on that in a separate review!), and then returned to our room, took a last round in our Spa experience before checking out and driving home. At checking out we notified the staff member of a loose part at the tub (a minor technical thing, no real problem) and then asked what it was about this magic word, and that we hadn't received anything beyond what we had booked. She asked me when I had said the word (as if there were various options), and I replied (of course) that it was at check in. There were 2 other employees now working at the front desk than the day before. She apologized and said it would have been a gift. They took note of the blunder and promised us to make up for it when we'll return. Meanwhile I have received an email from the front desk manager repeating that note. We'll be visiting another Palomar in about 3 weeks in Washington. I have booked the same room there. Let's see how that's gonna work out. Stay tuned, I am going to tell you how it went! I would have given 5 stars to this hotel, because the room really was wonderful (even with that terrible alarm sound going on every 2 min). But with this double blunder at our first visit ever, I feel it is more like a (rather slim!!) 4 than a (full) 5. I wished there were more sub votes in between to choose from. I will return though, this Fuji tub is a dream come true for anybody with a weakness for Spa experiences! I haven't taken pictures this time, as I figured they would only show the same what is already online about the room and the shower and the Fuji tub.

“Location, location, location!” I complimented myself on choosing this downtown Denver Courtyard, right on the 16th Street Mall and thus close to all the restaurants and shops. Very, very friendly and helpful staff, most elegant and stately looking Courtyard lobby I have ever seen, very impressed overall. Rooms are very roomy, comfortable and quiet. Views are another issue, but we didn't come for the views... Courtyards don't offer complimentary breakfast so we went outside to check out the other local offerings. The restaurant (Rialto Cafe) was closed for renovations the evening of our stay, so we went to a restaurant just down the street. There are plenty to choose from so I won't be partial in this review. Convention and performing arts center are also close by. The valet was extremely helpful, probably the best valet I have ever had, going out of his way to give me directions to the various destinations in the area.

“Decent and clean” We were going on a cruise on 1-1-08 out of San Diego and needed a place to stay for one night and park our cars for the time we were on the ship. We booked their park and stay package for $99/night. The rooms were small - but had a decent closet area to pile up our suitcases in for the one night we were there. You cna tell the property is old but they have done their best to work with what they have. I really felt like I should have been skeeved out by the place - it just had that feel to it - but, it was really, really clean - and served our purpose well. You needed to make reservations for the shuttle to take you to the port (wish we had been told this earlier) and we were able to secure the LAST spots on the shuttle that would get us there on time. The shuttle dropped you off right where we needed to be and picked us up within 10 minutes of getting off the boat. I would recommend staying at this property for one-two nights - but no more than that.

“Ottima soluzione per 5 persone” Sono stato all'Embassy suites di Philadelphia a luglio con la mia famiglia di 5 persone. Camera assai ampia, sopratutto l'ingresso con angolo cottura, un divano letto matrimoniale due tavoli e due poltrone; eccellente anche la seconda stanza con un letto assai grande dove dormono comodamente 3 persone. Un solo bagno e due televisore da 42 pollici. L'aspetto esterno non è dei migliori. In sintesi è un palazzone di forma esagonale al centro del quale partono tre ascensori che ti portano ai vari piani. Si mangia discretamente. Appare nelle parti comuni un po' vecchiotto, tant'è che talvolta un ascensore era in riparazione. La posizione è ottimale. Attorno un infinità di soluzioni per mangiare e molti negozi di ogni tipo. A breve distanza si raggiunge il centro della città con il suo minicipio e le varie attrattive. Insomma un ottima soluzione qualità prezzo dal momento che ti danno anche la colazione abbondante.

“Right in LA downtown, hi end, good for the fans” The JW and the Ritz are new additions downturn and they sure are high end. Very nice fittings. Bathrooms are nicely done without being opulent, interestingly the bed was a bit saggy. its a stroll to Staples and the convention center. The place is capcious in scale and you can walk for miles with 100 foot ceilings - its needs to get some character. The room rate at $169 will not last long but they make up for it by fairly expensive food. although breakfast was great. Parking is $25.

“Typical Hyatt but with the greatest location.” This classic Hyatt is a great location for business or family. It is situated across the street from the Ferry Terminal so even though it is rather large with the classic Hyatt inner atrium design, once you leave your decent-sized room and the hotel, you are in a perfect spot for sightseeing, foodie interests and hopping on the Street Car or Cable Car to either Fisherman's Wharf or Nob Hill and the Powell line. I have stayed here more than a few times and I can attest that the security of the hotel has improved. One time, I was awoken by a transgendered lady knocking on my door. Clearly wrong. Great dining is all around you and Chinatown is also up the Cable Car ( get a day pass). The Hyatt San Francisco is a great hotel whose charms exceed its physical structure.

“Nice stopover stay” It's a converted Baymont Inn. Good shape, well-maintained, helpful staff. Had a guard shack at the entrance, manned at night, so I parked my car close by and had no problems. Ceiling fan helped A/C out in keeping the room cool during a hot summer day. Good breakfast in the morning, though selection seemed a bit more limited than other La Quintas, and serving space was small-ish. Clean rooms, with that odd former Baymont configuration of having the lavatory on one side of the entry way and the bathroom on the other (never have figured out why they did that). Excellent rates, good location off I-20 but no traffic noise noticed. Excellent Wi-Fi connectivity. Comy beds. Several restaurants in walking distance. Access a little troublesome, as entry is off of a one-way frontage road, so it takes a little figuring out how to get out. Recommended for a stayover on your way through town. May want something better for a longer stay, but it would do — a matter of budget and personal taste. By the way, other La Quintas in El Paso are very nice, with higher rates to match, but deals can be found.

“Very nice hotel” My daughter and I stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth at the end of May, 2005. We happened to overlap with commencement weekend for Boston U and several other schools, which stressed the check-in desk and also bumped the rates a bit--Be aware of college schedules when you book into Boston! This hotel is really convenient for BU!!! The room was very nice, beds were outstandingly comfortable, bathrooms are spacious, Occitane amenities are great, tub is small and not at the same standard as the rest of the facility. Free bottled water and cookies with turndown service are nice touches. Rooms have DVD players and there is a list of movies available in the hotel. The Barnes and Noble across the street rents videos very reasonably (2nd floor). Access to the MTA subway is incredibly convenient. There is a very nice French restaurant in the next block on Commonwealth: Petit Robert Bistro. The hotel restaurant was also very nice. There is a coffee stand in the hotel--it's well intended, but you get more and more for your money across the street at the Barnes and Noble Starbucks. Do not use the concierge for tickets to Fenway Park--you can do much better on the street, as there are crowds of people selling tickets just on the corner as you walk to the park. We were charged top dollar needlessly. Live and learn. The downside for the hotel is the view (freeway or construction on Commonwealth), and perhaps the dinky tub. Otherwise, it is an excellent value and a comfortable and quite luxurious stop, by hotel standards.

“I love this hotel!” Company business trip. I was upgraded to a "loft" room and this room was absolutely fantastic. Full bar, mini-bar, and loads of snacks. The loft room has a movie room which is a comfortable bed with an LCD projector and Bose stereo CD/DVD system and the hotel has a long list of movies to provide you with for watching or you can bring your own. Staff were great, always accommodating and my only complaint would be that the bar closed too early. Our bar maid staff were extremely busy taking care of all of us and did a great job though, and the drinks were always great too - thanks. Thanks again for such a great time in Chi Town at the James.
