“Awesome location, amazing views” Yes, it's a big hotel with hundreds of hotel rooms. Yes, it's targeted to business travelers. That said, the Westin at Copley Place was still a great place to stay for a leisure trip. We were upgraded to an awesome corner jr. suite that had panoramic views of the Charles River. It's only 4 stars for me because the room decor was fairly non-descript and the amenities average, but I really enjoyed the location of the hotel. It's connected to the posh Copley Place shopping centre, and right around the corner from both the Back Bay and Copley T stations. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great...if you want to be nickled and dimed for EVERYTHING” The most ridiculous hotel that I have ever stayed in!! Parking? $24 A DAY (even if you check in at 4 PM and out at 7 AM) Internet? $12 (even if you check in at 4 PM and out at 7 AM). Also, it is extremely confusing to navigate. From the parking deck you have to get into THREE different elevators!! NOT WORTH IT!! The Crown does not charge all these things nor is it as confusing. However, you can`t sleep a wink there! DENVER - where do I stay?? HELP!!!

“Lived up to it's reputation” This is THE grand old hotel of Memphis and it lived up to it's reputation. The location couldn't be any better just blocks from Beale St. and all the downtown attractions. The service is 1st class. The ducks are the most original thing you will ever see at a hotel. What a neat show. The room was nice but being a typical problem with a grand old hotel, the bathroom was too tiny.

“Sheraton Gateway LAX” Stayed four nights on business/pleasure in Dec. Weekend rates were great...$109/night. They ended up giving me those rates during the week too. Probably because the pool was down and they were rennovating a set of elevators so had to use service elevators...not becoming of a 4 star hotel. They do have a 4 star restaurant...Shula's. Not quite kid friendly or budget friendly but the wait staff was great to look at! They had a breakfast/lunch restaurant on premisis but did not frequent. Requested and got a room close to elevators which is always nice at a hotel this size. Saved my walking for what really counted...Hollywood! Nice clean place, helpful staff. Great for the money! Their shuttle was very timely both to and from airport. Parking expensive and a few blocks from hotel so I just rented a car for one day and returned it that night...to a nearby Enterprise location that is very near this hotel. The Enterprise shuttle actually dropped me off at the hotel because they went past it, which saved me shuttle time from the airport. Probably wouldn't have stayed at this place if the business portion of the trip wasn't held there. I really wanted to stay at Eco Lodge because I heard there were more restaurants over there plus I could get a smoking room, but this worked out.

“Clean and Fabulous Location” I spent two nights in the city @ the Comfort Inn Manhattan/Murray Hill. Location: The location was excellent. Macy's was at one end of the block and the Empire State at the other. There was a subway stop close by as well and Penn Station (Amtrak) was just a 15 minute walk away. Starbucks was a block away as well as was a Duane Read (drugstore). The area was safe and clean. Rooms: The hotel was clean (it appeared that our bathroom had just been redone) but dated. The rooms were ample sized for NYC and had some nice touches such as bed skirts. We did not have any problems with noise levels either from the interior or exterior. The staff at the hotel was most friendly and the lobby offered a bit of a resting spot with free coffee. It was certainly a budget feel but great for the location and price.

“Good room; Great Location. Would stay again” Great that is is a short two blocks from Michigan Avenue; easy access to varied restaurants and entertainment. The staff was prompt and friendly at check-in. Other staff members greeted me as I walked in the halls which was positive. Room contained a sitting area with comfortable desk chair and work station, couch, TV and sitting chair. Had two beds in the room; bed was comfortable and linens clean. Sink area was separate from the the shower and toilet. Room did have a coffee maker. Outside of regular expected city noise, the room allowed for a good nights rest. Off the lobby there is a Starbuck's.

“Location, location, location” Step out of the portico and into Times square! A big plus. Great restaurants just across or down the street and around the corner. Even resturant row is close by. OK, the elevator system is confusing at first but after one time, it is amazingly efficient. My only complaint was the quality of the bath towels. I've had better at a Holiday Inn. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Rooms were comfortable and good size. We were on the 14th floor and noise was minimal. Comp Internet connection available on 8th floor in lobby.

“Like a palace while the royal family is away” My wife, son. and I stayed for one night at ATT Executive Education and Conference Center. We would not have selected it because of its distance from Sixth Street, but it was offered on Hotwire as a downtown hotel for a good discount. We were impressed with what a good deal they offered. Pros. Large rooms, bathroom a bit small but adequate Two people could use facilities at same time because toilet-shower was separated from sink by a sliding door. Free wi-fi for any number of devices, strong signal Lovely palatial building almost empty when there is no convention Good selection of channels on plasma screen TV Extremely helpful and friendly staff. All women at reception were friendly and charming. When they asked how was our stay, I commented that the lettuce in the Caesar salad at Gabriel was bitter, and the lady at reception took the salad off our bill Decent prices at Carrillon for breakfast and Gabriel at lunch. I highly recommend the Turkey BLT at Gabriel. Very convenient neighborhood at MLK Blvd not far from downtown. Interesting restaurants in neighborhood. Lovely view of campus tower from street in front of the building. The few guests at the hotel were quiet, adult Typical clean, like new university campus building Parking for $14 per night with right to come and go as often as you please Very liberal late check out policy when there is no convention. We checked out at 3:30 because we had a late flight It's actually quite easy to find 2 hour parking on East 6th street during the daytime. We were told that it's easier and cheaper to take a taxi to Sixth Street at night. Taxis wait outside the Convention Center Cons. Not within walking distance of Sixth Street. I actually consider this a plus The toilet used compressed air so it was loud when it was flushed Maybe our experience was so positive because there were no crowds staying there. We were very pleasantly surprised to see how convenient and friendly and economical ATT was. All of the reception staff and the waitress named Saba were especially memorable.

“Great Location, Would Stay Again!” My spouse and I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Tribeca for one night in mid-August 2012. We live approximately 1.5 hours from NYC, so we visit often, both for day trips and overnight stays. This was our first stay downtown (we generally stay in midtown) and we really enjoyed the area because it felt more livable and less touristy. The hotel is located a block from Canal Street and fairly close to the Holland Tunnel. The hotel offers valet parking, although there wasn’t anyone stationed at the door to whisk your car away; it would be necessary to park at the curb and come into the hotel to summon someone to park your car. (I think the price for valet was $65 per day, with no in/out privileges.) There are many nearby parking lots and garages with both covered and uncovered parking, some of which are even open on the weekends (many are weekday only) for half that price. There is some very, very limited on-street parking available, which appeared to be allowed only on weekends or evenings but was free. Traffic in front of the hotel was thick at times, but we didn’t hear the noise from our room, even though we had a corner overlooking the car-filled street. The lobby is somewhat small, but features a little grouping of furniture near a gas fireplace. The lobby has an ATM machine, a pantry area where you can purchase drinks and snacks to enjoy in your room, and a small bar area that serves complimentary coffee in the morning (until noon, actually) and cookies in the evening. The AOA Grill is adjacent to the hotel and provides room service in the afternoon and evening. The basement has a business center and fitness center, although I didn’t investigate either one. The rooms are typical HGI style with a refreshment center containing a mini-refrigerator and microwave, desk and ergonomic chair, chair/ottoman, and king-size bed. The king room was large enough (especially for NYC), but would be crowded if it contained two double beds instead. The room had no safe (although the hotel directory says that they can store things for you), and (not surprisingly) no slippers or bathrobes were provided. The bathroom was a nice size, as was the closet (which contained the iron and ironing board). Tiny Bath & Body Works toiletries were provided, and a hairdryer was attached to the wall. The furnishings seemed up-to-date with duvets and flat-screen TVs. The air-conditioning worked really well, even on the sweltering night that we visited. The location was great – there are lots of shops (both trinkets and high-end), delis, bars, cafes, and restaurants nearby. The blue line subway station is right outside the door to the hotel (I think it runs trains A, C, and E), so that method of transportation couldn’t be more convenient. Wi-Fi is free for HHonors members with Gold or Diamond status; I’m not sure of the cost for regular guests. The front desk can store luggage if you arrive early or stay late. The hotel has a little bench around the corner from the main entrance for smokers, and the perimeter of the building is decorated with colorful flowering planters. We would gladly stay here again!

“Very nice place.” This hotel has a fantastic location, amazing rooms and very good staff. My only quibble is that the breakfast buffet is an organized zoo. Although it's good, the lines are way too long. But, I will strongly recommend this place, especially for families.

“Best in Soho, 1/3 the price of Mercer!” I was skeptical, but the staff, service and GREAT beds won me over. I paid $189 on a holiday special, and got upgraded on check-in to a Deluxe King. First of all, let me say that I am young and supposedly hip, that is to say I am Jason Pomeranc (that's Pomerantz)'s key demographic. That settled, Mr. Pomeranc's people know what they are doing. My stay at 60 Thompson kicked off what turned out to be the better part of a long weekend in New York during the transit strike. I stayed at two other hotels, my usual Westin Essex House and the Sheraton New York for the last (emergency) night. I had just spent a week in Canada, so I was a bit weary of hotel-hopping. From the moment I arrived at 60 Thom, I was treated like family. Check in was a breeze, and considering I had a ton of luggage from my week's travels to bring in, the bellman was as cool as could be. I only detected an air of snobbery on one of the bellmen who, thankfully, was pretending to be uninterested in another set of guests. I have a sinking feeling that during a certain time of year, they hire a number of people who can't help having a certain attitude that tends to put off some guests. Moving on... My room, #93 on the ninth floor, faced east toward Soho as all the Deluxe Kings do. The dark hardwood floors and stark furniture give the room a loft feel, especially when you open the windows and let the wind blow the curtains. My first gripe was practical: there isn't enough darn closet space! My closet must have been on a structural column or something because there wasn't one but two areas where it was about 4" deep - barely enough room for a hanging suitcase and clothes and two hotel bathrobes. The king bed was great, just a massive white cloud ready for the magic to happen on its extremely comfortable mattress. The slick 42" plasma screen TV came equipped with a DVD player and separate aiwa CD stereo, and they even gave me a cable to connect my laptop to the TV speakers, so I could play whatever music I wanted. This is something they wouldn't do at any of the other hotels I stayed at this trip. As for the rest...well...the "couch" made a nice luggage bench, and the big leather chair had no desk so it became a clothes hangar. Ah well, the bed made up for either. The bathroom, with its black-marble walls looked nice, but was just a basic shower...although the shampoo by 'fresh' was very good. All in all, the room was beautiful, but I would have added a sexy Aeron chair and a good working desk. I could definitely live full-time in one of these rooms. One evening, when I wanted to dine in my room but not pay room service over-prices, the front desk gladly gave me a laminated menu book of all local restaurants that deliver. In the case that a restaurant didn't deliver, I was gladly told that they would send someone to pick anything up in the neighborhood. Now, that I haven't seen in a hotel before. This place surprised me. The public areas are well designed and well-kept (although I didn not try the bar and restaurant), the rooms are classic SoHo, and the service is r e a l...all these factors make 60 Thompson an ideal bet, especially if you can get a rate under $200. If they charge you over $300-400, I'd really consider splurging ont the Mercer.

“Good, abeit not great, place for race weekends” We stayed there the evening before the Brickyard 400, for $85 per night, plus $5 (per stay) for wireless Internet. The kids slept on the sofa sleeper and liked having their own "room" and TV. They also like the cookies in the lobby. We liked having the refrigerator and freezer to keep drinks cold in between our time at the track. While nothing special, the pool was open until 11 pm and was enjoyed by all. The hotel is also located just across from a mall with a variety of restaurants and being right off of I465, the drive to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway was quick and easy. In contrast to a couple of the other reviewers' experiences, our room was very clean. On the other hand, we requested a non-smoking room, but by the time we checked in they were all gone and the room we got clearly had that smoker's smell. Plus, as far as we could tell, the air conditioner had two settings, ice cold and off. Lastly, as this is an extended stay hotel, they don’t provide shampoo.

“centrale” hotel centrale e collegato con il copley center grande mall per shopping. le camere sono spaziose e con vista città. I servizi sono quelli di uno sheraton. base di partenza e stop del bus cityshgteeing di boston. buoni i piani alti che offrono una bella vista sulla città di boston. nelle vicinanze il filene's basement per acquisti a basso costo di diversi articoli.

“It is greedy to rent rooms to silly customers during building a hotel” Last night we spent in the Holiday Inn LAX. Our sleep stopped exactly at 7.00 a.m.when a crew of skilled housebuilder used all their eqipment at once (drillers, fixing guns, electrical saws) right in front of our room at the11 th floor (the hotel is completely scaffoled). We came from Guam / Hawaii and wished to sleep a little longer (Hawai is 2 hours earlier than LAX). Do not get fooled by the receptionist which will ask you during check-in if you accept the noise which we did. Of course they used this as an argument against me the next morning when I complained about the noise. Frivolous! It is greedy to rent rooms to silly customers while (re-) building a hotel. Furthermore, we got a wake up call which we never booked and the sink of the bathroom was blocked. There a many other hotels around which are not being built.

“Great Location, cool hotel” I had a conference in a nearby hotel and got this via hotwire. It was a total surprise and I liked it a great deal. The room was small, but for me it was just fine. Saturday night got a bit loud -- I think I had folks who'd been to a wedding -- but aside from that it was quite, clean, and great.

“You Could Do Much Better” The warm, nicely appointed lobby doesn't prepare you for what lies upstairs. My first room: cracked and falling plaster, broken glass in the window, busted blinds, furniture in awful shape (badly scuffed with broken draws), carpet had ground in dirt, bathtub mildewed. I asked for a different room and this one was similar but did not smell as bad. There is one small elevator that is very slow. There are no ice machines so prepare for a long wait to have someone bring it up to you (25 minutes). If "quaint" means dirty, unkept and uncomfortable, then this hotel ranks right up there with the quaintest. The location is great and the staff was friendly, and the common areas are classy, but for the money, there are much better places to stay.
“in need of refreshment” I have been staying here 3 times a year for the past 20 yrs. Beautiful Old Dame Hotel, best location in Boston, but in need of some TLC since it was taken over from the Ritz.

“Wished I could have stayed longer” The Fairfax embodies service and elegance. It feels like a boutique hotel but seems a little larger than that. I was in a very large room on the top floor overlooking the lovely rooftops of Massachusetts Ave. It felt like Europe. Perfectly lovely decorations, enormous bath, and attentive service.

“First class all the way” Sofitel is very sophisticated in a modern, European style. I booked through whatahotel.com and got an upgrade, free breakfast, even a nice appetizer, a better deal than Amex Platinum fine hotels. The hotel itself is in perfect location, near Peninsula and Park Hyatt. Architecturally, it is a fascinating structure. Check in was quick and pleasant, and I got a large suite with a great living room, huge bathroom and magnificent bedroom. The only negative is the television set. Oddly enough, they are old and clunky, really a dissapointment in such a plush and luxurious setting. The bed was super comfortable and the suite was enormous. Breakfast was delicious, and the bar on the second floor is active and fun. I don't see how you can go wrong here.

“Charming historic boutique property with great staff” If you like historic hotels or anything that's not a chain, then the Canterbury is an excellent choice. I had several little problems (including accidentally locking myself out of my room), and the front desk staff were always cheerful and helpful. I stopped in the restaurant to request ice for an ice pack - same great service. And the two gentlemen who work the door are fantastic assets. During the rainy weather, loved the skywalk that allowed me to get to my conference hotel while staying dry. The only downside of the skywalk is that it takes you through the mall; too tempting for me. Just one important tip to watch out for. If you ask the doorman or front desk for a cab, they will call a car service instead. Car service is always nice, but also pricier than a cab (airport fare and tip via car service was about $55 versus about $40 for a cab). If you prefer the cheaper option, call your own cab from your room or walk to the corner to hail one. There is no cab stand.

“A perfect stay one block off the Magnificent Mile-Gold Coast” My daughter & I recently visited Chicago for a shopping trip. Marriott offered a a great rate at this property, so we took a chance and booked it. Everything about our stay was perfect! We were upgraded from a studio to a king suite. The room was larger than my first apartment! Everything was extremely clean, well appointed and quiet. We asked for a lower floor to avoid the elevator delays mentioned in other reviews, but never had to wait. The room had a full kitchen and breakfast is included (we slept in and ate out). The entire staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel is one block from the 900 Shops, 2 blocks from Watertower Place Tower shopping and the American Girl store, and a short walk from Oak Street shops. The only slight negatives-parking is $45/night, which is typical for downtown Chicago, but service is fast. Wireless Internet is free, but a bit slow. The rooms have baseboard heating and you can't control the thermostat. We regulated the room temperature by opening a window. We will definitely stay here again.
“Airline crew” Friendly staff for airline crew. They give you $5 to buy from the pantry &the they give you Marriott points.

“A WONDERFUL WELCOME!” We were recently travelling around Texas for three weeks (we are from the UK) and arrived at the Four Points by Sheraton in San Antonio shattered and somwhat stressed. Karina, on reception was excellent. She said we could relax now and let them look after us and as she spoke I could physically feel myself relaxing! They looked after us very well. Nothing was too much trouble - the room was gorgeous - really clean, comfy with everything we could want. We asked for a high floor, and whereas some hotels can be unhelpful with requests, Karina ensured we had exactly what we requested. The room was bright, as well as spacious. We extended our stay for an extra night just because the hotel/people were so nice. The location is brill too; only a few blocks away from The River Walk, Hemisfair Park and all amenities. We were able to go out in the morning and return for a rest when we were exhausted, before going out again! It is certainly worth going up the Americas Tower in Hemis Fair Park to see the views over San Antonio. It is good value for money; included in the price is a 4D film giving an insight into Texas - really funny - esp when the snake "ran over our feet" and the bull spat at us - yuk!!! Also, the entry was good for the whole day so we were able to return once it was dark to see the view at night (they also let us do the film again). We loved San Antonio; although everything we saw on our travels was great, SA was probably the best, enhanced by 4 Points! It did us good to relax and recharge our batteries before continuing with our explorations and travels! We were sorry to leave - and I have to say this was the nicest hotel in the whole of our three weeks.Thanks Karina and Manager. We couldn't fault you! Hope one day we will be able to return.

“Perfect balance: modern comfort, quality service and friendly atmosphere” A little luxury for our last weekend in Boston before moving home to England. Spacious modern room, though in retrospect a city view is probably better than the port side view we asked for. We paid out extra for club room access and that was a bargain - excellent breakfast, and wine and nibbles in the evening. Plus it was a nice place to sit and read a book on a wet afternoon. The staff are really excellent - attentive without being intrusive, polite without being obsequiesce; a really nice balance has been struck at this hotel. It's not cheap - we got a good deal for a 3 day break averaging around $300 a night (but the actual cost of Monday was over $500, which is normal for the hotel. I recently stayed in the Omni Parker House, which was a completely different experience - it's really hard to say which I prefer. Try both.

“Spacious rooms, cool design, great location” I've visited the Ames twice for business, and they did great both times. Nice staff, huge rooms, efficient design, nice amenities, and a great location near my office and shopping. The only note for improvement would be the remote. It's a standard hotel remote, but you have to push the channel button so hard, you fingers start really hurting after flipping channels. If that's the worse thing about the place though, that's saying something. Also- the desserts in the restaurant are intense and huge.

“Just what you'd expect from a DoubleTree...especially the cookie” This hotel is consistently one of the better priced options in Boston. Never one to turn down a free cookie, I'm usually happy here. If you have breakfast at the hotel restaurant, you will be asked if you have a coupon. I never have the coupons of which they speak, nor do I have any idea how to obtain then. The breakfast isn't that good, so given the price point if you have another option I advise you to take it. Having said that the restaurant staff are very kind and generous so my recommendation is no reflection on them. The same holds true for the bar staff. The bar is usually the most happening place at this hotel (all hotels?) and the bartenders allow reasonable flexibility like getting a "roadie" to take to your room if you don't want to finish your beverage at the bar. The DoubleTree will certainly get my business again. If there's any downside (and I attribute this more to Boston than to this hotel) it's that there's no consistency in the rates on a relative or absolute basis.

“Walking distance to the mall” I thought this Hyatt was quite luxurious and had few complaints about the service and the look of the hotel. Maybe it's because I usually stay in mid-range (Comfort Inn, etc.) hotels? You can tell the staff is really trying hard to help out and the location really can't be beat - you can be on the National Mall in less than 10 minutes, Ford's Theater is around the corner, it's connected to the Metro Center metro station, and there are tons of restaurants and cafes around. With all that was wonderful and good, I'm sad that I have to add one important caveat: Beware the rooms with connecting doors (you know, those double sided doors that can turn two individual rooms into a double). When you can hear your neighbors blowing their nose and clearly hear where they are making their dinner plans for the night, it's too thin. I'm not sure if all rooms have this, but if possible I would recommend asking to be put in a room that doesn't have a connecting door. As with all the hotels at this level, you're going to have to pay for any extras including wireless, parking, breakfast, etc. I guess that's life at the top?

“Best Kept Secret in New York” This hotel has to be one of the best hotels in New York. The hotel is located in the Murray Hill area of New York and although not central it is just a short walk to the subway (2 blocks) and buses stop outside the hotel. The room was enormous and had a separate kitchen area, sofa, computer desk and king sized bed. The view from the room was fantastic as I had a view of both the East River and the Chrysler building. The hotel can arrange for a car to take you back to the airport at a reasonable price. I would recommend this option especially if you are leaving mid afternoon for the airport as the traffic can get very busy and a taxi will charge you even when you are waiting in traffic! A couple of points for those visiting New York 1. If you want to visit the Empire State building (which is a 5 minute walk from the hotel) then visit between 6 pm and 7 pm as the queues are at the shortest then. 2. Go on the Circle Line 3 hour cruise as you get to see many places you would not see on other tours.

“Absolutely unbeatable for the price” First off, TripAdvisor needs to immediately correct this hotel's one-star rating as well as its average "$802 per night" rate. Both are skewed on criteria to which I am not aware. I am a former native New Yorker, and I've stayed (both before and following my move) in a variety of the city's best hotels ... as well as a few of its worst. Including this one in its previous incarnation, where I had the displeasure of seeing mice periodically pop their heads through holes in the pink shag carpet. (I only wish I was kidding.) Thankfully shag and mice have long since dispersed. I received a rate of $145/night -- for a queen room, not one of the now-infamous "pods" -- via booking directly through their own Web site. Even considering the nosedive NYC hotel rates take in January and February, that's a total steal. That said, my room was nonetheless very small, and I banged my shins on that infernal platform bed on multiple occasions. I also had some issues with my A/C-heat system, which is the only reason I'm not giving this place five stars. The location next to the Columbus Circle subway stop makes it a perfect juncture for reaching most areas of the city via subway, and although it's too cold to appreciate it this time of year, I'm sure its location practically next door to Central Park will prove a major bonus as well. Blue Ribbon, for those of you unfamiliar with the city, is one of its best "minichains" (with only 4-5 total), and the 6 Columbus location is its first uptown. I ate there and was highly, highly impressed: it's some of the best sushi in a city filled with formidable sushi restaurants, including the infamous Masa across the street. Sadly, it looks like management is already onto the fact that they priced the rooms too low: their winter rates are already up 50% (to $215/night for this upcoming weekend - on their site, not Quikbook).

“Lovely hotel with amazing rooms and such helpful staff” All I can say is this hotel is amazing. The staff were so helpful and even do a free shuttle service. The gym was small but adequate and the rooms were nice with massive comfortable beds. Parking was the only downside as it was expensive with no other alternatives. Would 100% stay here again, it was so clean and modern,

“Fabulous find” Lovely, clean, modern hotel in a great neighbourhood. The staff are wonderful - always friendly and cheerful, and nothing is too much trouble. Our room was a fair size by New York standards, and we could see both Manhattan and Brooklyn Bridges from the window. The bed and pillows were very comfortable, and there was plenty of hot water. Complimentary tea and coffee are available in the lobby from morning till midnight, and there's free WiFi. Breakfast was included in our room rate, they gave us a voucher for a cafe four doors down the street. That's the only thing I would change about my stay, as the cafe was not great (some of the staff were surly, and breakfast was one small hot dish plus EITHER a hot drink OR juice; but - just to be clear - my problem was with the cafe, NOT with the hotel). I loved the area - at the edge of Chinatown where it meets Little Italy. We used the subways around the corner on Canal Street (the 6, N, Q and R, which are all useful lines for moving around the city). The neighbourhood is pretty quiet in the evenings - there are more people about during the day, but it's not overcrowded. The shops and restaurants all seemed to be cheap around there. I'm a fairly frequent visitor to Manhattan, and prefer not to stay near Times Square, as I find it too crowded, noisy and overpriced. Don't be put off by thinking this place is away from midtown - wherever you stay in the city, you're going to be using the subway anyway, and it's only a handful of stops. Plus it's really convenient for exploring places like Soho, the East Village, Greenwich Village etc. not to mention Chinatown and Little Italy. I really recommend this hotel - it's good value by New York standards, and is one of the very best I've come across.

“Good location but there are better hotel choices” I booked the hotel through Hotwire, and was expecting a basic room. I got exactly what I expected--the smallest hotel room in the United States. The room I had (Room 1129) was the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in, and I have stayed in some small rooms in Argentina and Europe. There was very little room between the bed and the desk and the entertainment cabinet. The bathroom was also vert small, with no counter space to put toiletries. I had to keep everything in the travel bag after I used them. The lobby was very nice during the day, but at night it is like walking into a cave, and it doubles as the hotel bar. I could barely see to make it to the elevator it was so dark and so crowded. The front desk people are professional, but they do not present the kind of service one expects in a 4 star hotel. I was offered an upgrade at $77.00 extra a night, which I declined, then the desk clerk said she would give me a room with a queen bed. However, I was only given a room with a double bed, and the W tried to charge me an extra $99.00 a night because they said I had upgraded. The woman at the front desk on Sunday morning was not helpful at all. Another problem I had was getting my car when I was ready to check out. Be warned--if you take a car and park in their parking lot, the charge is $48.00 a night. If you are there on weekends, you can actually park in front of the hotel or on LaSalle Street for free. We tried to call the number we were told to call, and no one would answer. We then called the problem line and the man who answered said we would have to call the valet back, he could not help. We called another number, and this person tells us to come down to the lobby and just go to the parking valet with the claim check. This added an extra 20 minutes to the check out. The W does have some nice features--the bedding was incredible, we had 5 pillows, and the soaps and shampoos were great. We tipped the maid, and she gave us tons of extra towels and soaps. The hotel location was great. We walked to the Oriental Theater to see Wicked--the theater was about 1/2 mile away. We walked to the Art Institute which was about 6 blocks away, and we walked to the Magnificent Mile. The El is a block away from the hotel. My room was across the street from the El, and I never heard it at night. My experience at the W was neither pleasant or unpleasant--I think it is a rather mediocre hotel. There are far better hotels with far better service for the same money, and I would not stay there again.

“Great Location and Overall Nice Hotel” The Grand Hyatt is a huge hotel, perfectly located between downtown San Diego and the harbor area. This is the best thing about the place. You are literally steps away from Seaport Village and a manageable walk from the Gaslamp Quarter and Midway Museum. Pros: Huge, gorgeous lobby. Lots of gift shops, restaurants, and coffee shops. Beautiful view. Nice pool area. Nice bathroom. Easy cab access in front. Awesome location. Cons: Rooms are outdated and have a lot of wear. Outdated TV in room. Overpriced. A bit impersonal due to the size. Self Parking is $22. Charge for internet use. Overall, it's the location that makes this place worthy. The rooms need updating for sure, but I would recommend this hotel at the right price. Try to find it through discount sites (Hotwire, Priceline, etc) before paying full price ($249).

“Awesome!” What a hotel! My family and I stayed here during Tex/Ou weekend and had a blast. The hotel is right in the middle of some great restaurants and bars. There is a CVS across the street if you need anything. The service was top notch at the Joule. EVERYBODY was very friendly and helpful. The pool was incredible. It overlooks the city and has a great vibe to it. Lots of people young and old hanging out and having fun. Only negative about the pool area is the drinks are pricey. My wife and I ordered two vodka sodas and it was $28! We stuck to beer the rest of the time. We ordered room service a couple of times and it was fast and effecient. If you don't mind spending the money you won't be dissapointed at the Joule!

“Clean, Easy, Roomy, Good Value!” I needed to leave the Denver airport early so headed up the day before from Colorado Springs via shuttle and was picked up at the airport by the Hyatt shuttle. Check in on line was easy. I'd asked for a quiet room away from ice machines and elevators and the room they gave me had no shared wall on the bedroom side! I got to the hotel which is located in a fairly open, barren plain about a mile from the airport. There is no restaurant or room service but they have a nice little store where you can buy food one can heat up in the room's microwave OR oven, plus beer, wine, and travel supplies...great selection of ALL. I had an excellent Italian dinner about two blocks away. In the morning, they do provide a FULL breakfast buffet for free...very tasty and starts at 6am. The room was very big with a foyer/FULL-sized kitchen, LARGE couch, ottoman and flatscreen TV area, a desk and biz chair with free internet, and nice big comfy bed, large tiled shower, bath with full size closet. This is a room one could certainly live in as an extended stay option. The room was $109 with AAA discount. Next morning, I took their free shuttle to the airport. All in all, more expensive than some nearby airport hotels, but still a great hotel room value. I highly recommend it!
“You can't go wrong here.” Great location, above average rooms, great service. Hotel in great condition. If you are loyal to the Marriott brand. This is a good choice in SF.

“Old hotel” I stayed there for 2 nights for a conference at the end of Feb. My overall feeling is that the hotel is out dated and looks old. it has 2 sections (plaza and tower) and it is big. Somehow, it is very confusing to get around, and I spent much time trying to find where I was trying to go. The room I had is bigger in comparison to similar hotels. However, bathroom is smaller and very average. The bed is good with soft pillows. Heating, safe had to be fixed to be functional. And it does really heat up the room (I had to leave it on to 81 degree the entire time I stayed and the room was not heating up at all). Toilet stopped flushing the day I was checking out.The main lobby is big and has desks and convenient hook ups for your laptop. Business center conveniently located in the lobby too. I think if this hotel remodel/upgrades, have a easy layout, with its large space, it has the potential of being a great hotel. But for right now, it is not worth what it is charging, and it is too old looking and feel.

“Great Option” I believe the real test of a hotel is how they handle the unexpected. We arrived at the hotel around 1:00 PM. We had called ahead and asked if we could have early check in and they said it would be no problem. After receiving our room key we proceeded to our room. When we opened the door it was clear that the room had not been cleaned. We called the front desk and they apologized and said they would send someone up with a new key to a new room. After about 15 minutes and still no key, we decided to go back down to the front desk. The woman behind the counter apologized profusely and immediately gave us an upgrade to their premium floor, which included free cocktails in the evening and breakfast the next morning. So, they won our loyalty from that moment on. The rest of our stay was fine. Nice quiet, comfortable room with a very comfortable bed. Big bathroom with lots of little extras, like shaving cream, tooth paste,cotton balls etc. A couple of small gripes: we had an older tube-type TV in our room. It seems that a hotel of this caliber ought to, by now, have flat-screen, HD, TV's. Also, they charge $10 a day for wireless for each computer you use in your room. We stayed in a $100 a night Holiday Inn the night before that had free wireless. Otherwise we had a delightful stay.

“Nice extended stay hotel” If you're not familiar with Candlewood Suites, it's an extended stay hotel - this one is a very nice, newly built one in an upcoming north area of town. It's easy to hop on 281 and drive to the River Walk in 20 minutes or so. There are plenty of restaurants and shopping centers nearby, including a Super Target where you can buy groceries. The staff is super friendly! Fitness center machines were fine, albeit a little cheap. My only complaint is the internet. I would definitely stay here again in the San Antonio area.

“Central location, good standards, but don't let them put you in a small room” We had high expectations of this hotel and were disappointed with our first room, which was very small, and was clearly not designed for a queen bed (which it though had - we had booked the queen sized room). We raised this the following morning and were moved without argument at all. Our second room was a much better size - although still not huge, but I get the impression mid-town NYC hotel rooms are generally smaller. Our second room was a decent sized room and good standard. It's a nice, smaller hotel. It's got the right "feel" for a four star place, although it being a city hotel, you're probably not going to be amazed - unless you spring for a suite. The gym was of a reasonable size, and location is fine - really close to everywhere, but that's also a negative for some ... keep in mind it's close to Times Square - which is more than a little touristy (it's not too close though - a few blocks). Final bit of advice: don't drive here ...

“Wish I Had Stayed Longer” Checking-In PROS: PERFECT CONS: N/a Lobby: PROS: Very comfortable and a lot of seating space with separate areas for internet use. CONS: N/a Room PROS: So quiet...loved it!!! The view was awesome as well! CONS: N/a Bathroom PROS: Clean and powerful water pressure CONS: N/a TV PROS: HUGE flat screen TV with a host of great channels to chose from. CONS: N/a Bed PROS: PERFECT for comfort! CONS: N/a Housekeeping PROS: EXCELLENT!!!!! I wanted more conditioner for my hair and she bought me a huge bag of conditioner and shampoo! CONS: N/a Wi-Fi PROS: It's FREE & FAST CONS: N/a Fitness Center PROS: Hubby liked it but I did not get to see it. He only does strength training so if he approves, it must be nice! CONS: N/a. Checking-Out PROS: SMOOTH CONS: N/a They do not have continental breakfast but a breakfast buffet with a lot of food choices. It was a real gem and I hate I could not stay longer. FREE PARKING - yay!

“Out of Order Housekeeping” Our newly renovated room was pleasant enough and the new modern decor certainly takes this old world hotel into the mainstream of hotel room design du jour. The design is simple, very basic white furniture, small desk and a single chair, all white bed linens, white walls and ceiling, no draperies, plastic bedside lamps, a flat screen television and one wall with a splash of color. However, we find it hard to imagine how the new hotel owner is willing to invest so much money renovating this large Manhattan hotel when the most basic common denominator in any hotel, housekeeping, is lacking. We would project all the money the Milford Plaza's new owner is putting into this old hotel is going to go to waste if quality housekeeping cannot be provided. In our room, bed linens were never changed after a multi-night stay, there was hair in our wash basin, tooth paste splatter on the wall tiles around the sink, the glass shelf above the sink was not wiped clean or toothpaste residue, the bath amenity tray was dirty, and the toilet had particulate in it. Mind you the bathroom was so small a housekeeper could possibly clean the toilet and wipe the toothpaste off the wall ... all at the same time! Should not someone check the work of the room housekeepers? We recently saw a news story about a wage study for New York City and we happened to note the total annual compensation for a room attendant is now approaching $90,000, including benefit costs. With that kind of wage rate, we expected our bathroom should have sparkled and surgery might be performed in this room without the fear of getting an infection. Should not a hotel guest expect to have a clean bathroom? It will not take long for customers start to avoid this hotel if it earns the reputation for having dirty rooms. Should such a reputation gain a footing, hotel management will likely have to sell rooms at lower rates to get guests into their beds. The net effect of lower room rates is likely to be reduced cash flow, which in turn, will be insufficient to cover the debt service for the massive renovation project now under way. This is a real shame considering the prime location this hotel has in Manhattan. Based on what we experienced, we believe the housekeepers for our room are being overpaid and we hope such shoddy housekeeping quality does not exist throughout the rest of this hotel. The hotel management should take immediate corrective action to "clean up its act" and, if the hotel has union staff, I would expect the labor organization would assist management in its efforts to remove those employees who are either unwilling or unable to do the work they are being paid to do. But, this is New York City and what is logical ... may really be illogical.

“Comfortable” Given the mixed reviews we didin't know what we'd find at Park 79. We had chosen it for its great location and (for NYC) reasonable prices. Well, we were very happy with what we found. Our room on the first floor at the back was very quiet and comfortable. The decor was simple but elegant, the bathroom, though small, very well appointed and quite adequate, and the bed very comfortable. The staff was helpful. My only complaint is that the cleaning staff was very noisy first thing in the morning, communicating (I think) on two way intercoms. There must be a quieter way to do this! Will stay here again when in New York.

“There are better options in the area” When the best parking option is street parking, you know it's not good, but that doesn't even come close to describing the parking mess you'll find here. There are two parking lots, one is above ground and has about eight spots. It's a dead end lot so while getting in can be doable, getting out is a mess, as you have to manuever the other cars as well as the uncomfortably close walls of the hotel. Once you leave, you have to go out on to a busy street and your view will be blocked on both sides by the lucky guests who were able to find street parking. If you have to park in the underground lot, you have to manuever through other cars, poles, garbage, the ceiling (!), as well as the unsafely steep one way ramp that leads down to the parking structure. If you are entering when someone else is trying to exit, you'll either have to reverse up a narrow hill with walls on both sides or hope the other person will reverse downhill into parked cars. It's going to be an accident either way so just hope for the best. Once you get into the hotel, assuming you even make it that far, you'll probably have to try a few times before you get a clean room (i've stayed here twice and was shown to a dirty room both times). Then you can plug in your computer and if you're lucky enough to get a computer signal (I could on one of the 4 days I was there) it will not be "high-speed." I actually got a faster connection using the phone line. You can try to complain to the front desk but they'll just tell you to call a 1-800 help line that will just tell you that the problem is on the hotel's end. The only nice thing about the hotel is the location, although there is absolutely NOTHING within walking distance or even short driving distance, you can reach all of the LA destinations without having to pay the typical LA prices. There is one guy that works at the hotel that is very nice but most of the workers could really care less about you. Do yourself a favor and stay at the Ramada down the street. It used to be a Holiday Inn Express, it has good parking, and it's cheaper.

“Wonderful hotel in LA” I'm a fan of Kimpton hotels anyway but this one really went over and above what I would expect. The location is great. On a not-too-busy part of Wilshire Blvd, near Westwood and not so far from downtown. What makes it stand apart from others is the way the guests are treated. When I mentioned to the desk clerk that I was leaving too early for the morning tea/coffee, he offered to send up a tea kettle (I bring my own tea bags) to my room! Never happened before. It's a little detail but was really appreciated. The fitness center is larger than I would have expected althought some of the cardio equipment wasn't working very well. The room is typically Kimpton...well appointed and thoughtful for business travel. This is now my hotel when I'm in LA.

“First stay here, won't be my last!” Spacious property, wondefully appointed, rooms renovated and the gym is fantastic! My room had a wonderful view of one of the pools. The staff was so friendly and accommodating. My room was quite large and I loved the sitting room and extra space. It was like an apartment. I don't have kids but this would be ideal for more than 2 people. If I had more time, I would have been able to take advantage of the amazing large pool and waterpark, lazy river. The breakfast I had at Rico's was amazing! It was packed with guests. There was a chef making omelettes to order - mine was incredible. What impressed me: the homemade granola for my yogurt and fresh fruit. This was one of the best granolas i have ever eaten. The manager stopped by everyone's table to ensure everything was going well - how often do you see a manager skulk away from guests? not here - he genuinely wanted to know how everyone's food was. The location is centrally located as well - what a beautiful resort.

“Very average hotel in a terrific location” I've come to this hotel a number of times on business. It's a very average room, and the elevator system takes some extra time. Of course, the location can't be beat. To me this room is OK at $200/night, but not nearly worth the $400 I've seen quoted.

“Great Location!” Stayed at the Hilton Towers 8/5-8/8. This hotel is in a great location, right across from the parks. If you enjoy an evening stroll, this is the place for you! Our room was comfortable, quiet, and clean. Housekeeping had our rooms cleaned by 11 am each day. The hotel was full to capacity. The lobby areas were busy and noisy. However, the rooms were very quiet, and I tend to be sensitive to noise. Public transportation is no problem, several el stations are within walking distance. We walked to the Ogivie Center to take the metra to Glen Ellyn, where our daughter/son-in-law live. The walk was an easy 30 minute walk. We obtained a good rate on the Hilton Website ($152/night). We will definitely stay here again!

“Now that is a pool and bar area.” I recently attended a meeting at the W HOtel which is within walking distance of the UCLA campus. I needed to spend some time working prior to our meeting so I visited the bar area to do some work. Wow, the pool area gives you a feeling of being a celebrity. The audience is a good looking group and the waiters and waitresses are very engaging. If you have a need to visit UCLA or just want to be cool for the day, I would recommend staying at this hotel.

“Expensive, but good location” I chose this hotel due to its location close to where the buses from DC let off, and also because you can walk to Time Square, Broadway, the Empire State Building, and much more from there. I asked for a high room with a view when I made the reservation, and I did get a room on the 15th floor with a view of 7th avenue and Madison Square Garden. I thought I would be high enough to avoid hearing the 24/7 non-stop beeping of horns and wailing of sirens, but every time a horn went off it sounded like it was one foot outside my window. I heard so many sirens I thought New York was under attack. All this noise could be heard even over the very loud window air conditioner. So bring ear plugs and a sound machine if you want to get any sleep. The room itself seemed very small, the bathroom even smaller. For the price I paid I was expecting something bigger. It's pretty bad when Hampton Inns and Radisson's have bigger rooms and bathrooms than this expensive place. Be careful what kind of room you book. Mine was called a "GUEST ROOM 1 BED" and is only 260 sq feet. It had no kitchen, sofa, microwave, etc. The type of room I booked did come with a small fridge, which was good, and a free safe you can use. Also a big flatscreen TV with lots of channels. The bed and pills were so comfortable I slept like a baby (thanks to my earplugs too). I didn't bother with the pillow menu, the pillows already on the bed were great. All the rooms have now been remodeled, so it was a remodeled room, but you think they could update the HVAC system and get rid of the noisy window air conditioners. I had to turn up my TV to like "40" to hear it over the window unit. There were no drawers for my clothes. There are shelves in the closet. I guess you are supposed to use those, but since you can only close one side of the closet your underwear and socks will be in view of any visitors. Not much room in the bathroom for your things. Just a little orange tray already mostly filled with stuff. There is a very narrow shelf below the sink about 3 inches wide, but that won't hold much. Also there's no towel rack in the bathroom, just one in the shower. It's a pain to have to pull back the shower curtain and go in the shower every time you want to dry your hands. Also there were no wash clothes. Internet access should be free for the amount of money they charge for a room, but this wasn't an issue for me as my cell phone can create wifi hotspots. Just a suggestion to the hotel, since most hotels many price levels down from this one give guests free wifi. In my reservation I had requested a bathrobe be delivered at 7pm. When I got back to my room that night none had been delivered and none ever was. Other than that the staff was very good at meeting my needs, even helping me get a ticket to a Broadway show with just a few hours notice. I didn't try the attached restaurant, Niles, as it seemed very overpriced, and being New York you can get quick cheap food everywhere. Go left out the main hotel entrance and there is a deli/grocery store a few steps away. Go right and there are tons of places to eat. Go any direction actually. You'll never go without food in NYC there's so many places to eat. Overall I wouldn't stay here again due to the price, but if you have the money and want a central location within walking distance to a lot of the major attractions, this place should work for you.

“Excellent value in the perfect location!” We booked the Park South Hotel for a long weekend via Priceline, and overall, it's an excellent deal in New York City! I've stayed in quite a few hotels in New York, and this ranks as one of the best for value and location, and I'd definitely stay here again. ROOM: We got a great deal (>$200) via Priceline Negotiator for the Executive Guestroom, which was very large and modern by New York City standards. The bed was large and very comfortable, and the room was quite spacious for two with a small seating area, small desk, and plenty of drawers. The closet was small, but sufficient for a short stay. The bathroom only had space for one, but was very clean and included luxurious towels and toiletries. We kept saying how surprised we were by the size of the room, and didn't feel cramped when getting ready for the day or spending an afternoon relaxing before dinner. LOCATION: The location of this hotel cannot be beat, especially for seasoned New York travelers. You're a two minute walk from a subway station and a 10 minute walk from Gramercy Park. You're a quick cab ride from Penn Station and a pleasant walk to the best shopping and dining, as well as Herald Square and Times Square. The hotel itself is on a street that's not too busy, with a great bagel shop and a Duane Reade nearby. PROPERTY: The hotel itself is a quiet and calm, but modern, boutique hotel. The lobby is small but has inviting seating and candles in the evening. The hotel has a highly rated restaurant, which offers free breakfast as well as cocktails and room service in the evening. We didn't try it, but it seemed inviting. SERVICE: The staff was overall very helpful and friendly, despite a hiccup at the front desk when we needed to book another night when our train was cancelled. (The woman at the desk "couldn't find our reservation," despite showing her the confirmation, and made us wait about 35 minutes when it seemed like all she needed to do was go get a print out from the hotel basement.) Still, we got a great deal on the same type of room, which was equally spacious and nice. OVERALL: Overall, Park South is superb value for New York, providing a great room in a great location. If you don't need a trendy bar or hip decor or a spa, which I usually don't, then Park South is actually quite luxurious and you'll love your stay!

“Excellent location and friendly staff” I stayed at the Intercontinental while in town for business. It offers a great location right on the Magnificient Mile. Room: The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. My room was clean and welcoming with a nice view. It had a desk and sitting area in addition to a quiet comfortable bed. Water and a few free snacks were provided free of charge (fruit, which is a nice healthy change of pace). A daily paper and robe was also provided. There is gym within the hotel complex that requires an extra fee. It offers a few elipticals as well as treadmills and has towel service. A Starbucks is located right next door and a Walgreens across the street.

“on the water, great decor, tasty food, free shuttle” we stayed @ Edgewater many years ago. This time with Priceline.com, we got a nice room for $ 99, but decided for $ 50 a night to upgrade to a huge, water front/with balcony and chairs, room, well worth it. very tasty breakfast with views of all of Puget Sound and mtns. free shuttle took us/and picked up to convention ctr, restaurants. nice staff. great value! great walks to nearby olympic sculpture garden, restaurants, and nearby pikes street market.

“pleasant” Stayed 3 nights and it was very pleasant. The hotel is situated in a better part of downtown and has easy access to major bus routes and metro stations. But at night, the area is really dark and there is barely anyone walking on the streets except for homeless people and beggars. Even though it used to be an office building, the conversion to hotel seems well planned. The people at the front desk were attentive and friendly. The elevators were fast but there is a ping pong table on the ground floor that kind of obstructs the access to the elevators. The room I stayed in was bright and airy. It had a minimalist décor but not high-end stylish furnishings. The flat screen TV sits on a low small plywood stand. There is also only one chair but a long work desk. The platform bed (or just the mattress) was very comfortable but it was covered with a flat sheet that was tucked in a way that exposes a third of the mattress. So when you lay down to sleep, your feet touch the bare mattress. Did not hear noise from the roof or street. I had no problems with the wi-fi. All in all, it was very pleasant.

“Urine Smell and Noise. Everything Else was Great” I checked into this hotel after a 10 hour flight across six time zones and needed sleep. The first night was fine with the exception of the maid staff coming into the room twice to wake me from my sleep in the late afternoon. I concede I did not place the "do not disturb" sign on the door but why two times and for what? The room was cleaned and fully made up when I checked in. Maybe it was "turn down" service but I did not expect that at Hampton Inns. The rooms are nice and the staff were pleasant and helpful. When I returned to my room after the first day at work it smelled of stale urine, much like a men's toilet that has not been cleaned for too long. The smell seemed to be coming from the cooling unit. The front desk assigned me another room, but offered no assistance in moving me to it and required me to downgrade from a King to a Queen bed because they were 100 percent booked. I moved to the new room, took a nap, and went out for dinner. When I returned to the room (11:00 pm on a Wed. night) the music noise from an adjacent bar and restaurant across the parking lot was loud enough that I could hear it in the room. The urine smell from the air conditioning system may have been a fluke but the noise was not. I commented to the desk clerk that he must have had complaints about this before. His response was "You are the first tonight". He was probably honest. If you stay at this hotel do not stay on the side where the Mellow Mushroom is next door (even room numbers). Make sure you get an odd room number. From what I can see there is just another hotel on the odd room number side.

“Stayed the night at the Doubletree” I got to the hotel for a stayover so that I could catch my morning flight out of Houston. When I landed at the airport I placed a call to the hotel to have the shuttle pick me up. Within 15 mins Marcus the shuttle driver scooped me up, grabbed my bags and offered me a bottled water. After I was dropped off I checked into the hotel and was sent on my way to the 6th floor. They currently had an elevator down for repairs, but the hotel was not full so it didn't really matter. The carpeting in the halls could use a cleaning, but overall the room was newly decorated and was clean. I was woke up at 5 in the morning by the alarm clock in the next room which seemed vacant. It lasted for over an hour. If you need to stay over night near the airport this hotel would fit the bill. Reasonable price, lot's of ammenities, etc.

“Nice choice - great location!” This is a great hotel for its location. I took the ferry to work to Sausalito and the hotel is right across the street. It is also near a cable car connection (Embarcadero) and Union Square for shopping. There are so many hotels to choose from in SF so I'm not sure I would recommend this if you are coming for a first time visit. It was still in the pricey range for what you get. Some bonuses: there is a free wine/beer hour in the evenings and the hotel is adjacent to a couple of nice restaurants. Downs: the staff are not terribly helpful or bright. There is no store or place to get juice, etc. other than your mini bar. Another plus - the Embarcadero YMCA is next door and is an awesome gym! The hotel provides $10 day passes. Our room was very quiet however, and we got great sleep.

“Very nice for its class - could not have chosen better” Stayed here after a day of driving and relaxing at the beach, visited San Diego downtown in the evening. The location is rather good - 2 minutes from the interstate and therefore comparably quick to SD as well as the beach. Obviously, the hotel not being either directly at the beach or in SD downtown contributes to the reasonable rate (we paid $65). Finding the hotel is easy, it is surrounded by other hotels, at least one chain restaurant and business centers. Parking s easy, check in might have been the speediest ever. The rooms are of a very good size, nicely appointed and clean. The same goes for the bathroom, which left a very good impression. There was an AC unit outside our window which came to life every once in a while and rustled for a few minutes, but otherwise it was very quiet. The free WiFi worked great. We had a very good night's sleep and woke up to a great breakfast, including several hot dishes and do-it-yourself waffles. Check out was as quick as check in. We had forgotten a laptop charger at the hotel and I called them to days after - I was not actually expecting much of a chance since often hotels are not overly interested in helping in these matters and was very surprised by the positive reactions of the staff - they called me back as promised, found the charger and shipped it. Very nice and unexpected - a big thumbs up! Positive: - Room (esp. bathroom) I would not have expected - they simply lacked the 'cheapishness' often found in non-luxury chain hotels. We felt very comfortable and had none of the "better not touch that" feelings one often encounters. - Breakfast - this was an actual breakfast and a good start in the day. - Staff and Service: Every encounter was very friendly and helpful. - Free parking, Wireless and breakfast. Negative: - Cannot find anything negative that would be worth pointing out - obviously it is not a 5 star property, but a very nice and clean 3 star hotel. Recommendation: This is the best hotel of its class/price range I have seen in a while. I would absolutely recommend it.

“First class hotel -- extremely memorable” Everything was perfect. Elegant, great service, fascinating artwork throughout the hotel, and outdoor dining on the 6th floor terrace, facing Ground Zero. Only afterwards did I realize that the large outdoor screen adjacent to the hotel was part of the hotel. Extremely memorable.

“Just what you need for business” I recently spent one night at the Inn at the Colonnade. It had been many years since I had been there and they have done a very nice upgrade. Rooms - decent-sized, clean, nice toiletries, free internet, comfortable bed Breakfast - the continental buffet isn't all that impressive, but I got the bed and breakfast option and was able to order off the menu. Staff was very attentive and good food came quickly. Location - this is unbeatable if you have business at the Johns Hopkins Homewood campus. Even if you have business elsewhere in Baltimore, it is only about a $15 cab ride to downtown. I recommend this for anyone with business at Hopkins.

“Waterfront Hotel” We stayed here because it is close to the Harpoon Beer Brewery and they were have a biking event. The location for us was perfect. The room is updated and very clean. The bathroom is very nice, but there is no tub only a shower. We had a mini fridge but no microwave. We asked for one but they said they did not have any extra. If we needed a microwave we could bring the item to the kitchen. Parking was $44 a day. I guess that's what they can charge in a big city. I liked that we were not to far from the entrance to the highway. We are also close to the waterfront. There is a great Italian restaurant right around the corner called Salvatores and they had homemade pasta. delicious. They only complaints I had were that the people at the front desk, both checking in and checking out were not that friendly. Not only did they not smile, they did not look up at me. Usually at a first class hotel,when you are checking out they ask if everything was okay. Guess they did not care. The other compliant was that I came downstairs to get my car instead of calling from the room and the guy scolded me for not calling. He pointed right to the receipt and said, "see it says here to call". Well for $44 plus a tip I think they could have been a little more pleasant too. Putting the "no smiles" aside. I would stay here again because of the location and cleanliness. The hotel only lacks in cheeriness.

“Adequate Hotel” I stayed at the Omni for business and it wasn't fantastic but wasn't awful either. My room was fine and the staff was very good, but the hotel is in need of a facelift. It's certainly not up to the standards of Omni hotels I've visited in other cities. The hotel also has a very oddly positioned front entrance that is sometimes hard to navigate with your car. If you want to stay in downtown Jacksonville, this is certainly an OK choice, especially if you can get a good rate. But just lower your expectations a bit. It's not a four-star experience but is certainly deserving of three stars.

“Great Service and Location” The Kimpton Nine Zero hit the spot for a downtown Boston meeting. Front desk was accommodating and professional Room was vintage Kimpton with tiger print bathrobe. Wine reception was great. Room was quiet and well appointed. Only downside was closed restaurant and bar on on Monday night but was not far for other options. Would stay again.

“Not what I expected” The NYC Waldorf Astoria is a historic property in a great location, but my fascination of the property ends with the stunning lobby. The guest rooms are small and exceptionally dated. The windows were covered with plastic rolled shades. Heavy curtains attached to the wall with hooks that had pulled though the wall. Climate control was provided by a loud under window unit that blew air onto guests when trying to get work done at the desk. Wi-fi was $16 per day. The dresser was too small to completely unpack my things. A mini bar had for fee items that guests would instantly incur if moved (magnetic registry). I stayed at the hotel for a business meeting and found it less than ideal. The meeting spaces were crowded. Breakfast and snacks were poor. Starbucks coffee in the lobby was significantly overpriced. Sunday buffet is $100 per person. Save yourself money and stay across the street in luxury.

“Now a Sonesta Hotel and overall very good stay” As I write this review at mid-June, 2012, the Crowne Plaza Hotel at 1800 Market Street has changed names to Sonesta Hotel Philadelphia. This was my first return to the city since leaving here 20+ years ago after working here for just one year before moving on. Now that it’s a plane ride away from home, I took a cab ($35 with tip) from the airport. The rate to downtown is fixed at $28.50 + a fuel surcharge of a varying amount depending on the price of gas. Mine was $1.15 at the time. It is about a 20 minute ride in. Also noteworthy, if you are arriving at Terminal F, (US Airways Express) you’ll need to hoof it to Terminal E via the upper level sky walkway/bridge. Due to construction this summer of 2012, there are no ground transport options from this terminal. It is all of a 5 minute walk to Terminal E. The hotel is situated on Market Street which is one-way eastbound. City Hall looms large in front of you as you approach from the west. The hotel will be on your right despite what some mapping apps may show you. There are no automatic doors and you’ll have to pass through two sets to get to the front desk. If you’re loaded with baggage, get help. There’s garage parking, but dig deep. It’s going to set you back $42 a night, $36 on the weekend. Unless you need a car, cab it or get a car service for about $45. Check-in was quick and straightforward with a well staffed front desk. This is a 445 room property. I was on the 20th floor away from the elevators facing Market Street. Noise was not a problem really. The 4 elevator bank adjacent to the pub and restaurant worked well and we never had to wait more than a minute or two for a car. The lodging room was very cold when I first arrived. I raised the thermostat but soon realized it wasn’t working. After requesting assistance, the engineer came knocking and the problem was resolved as requested, with the repair of a stuck damper. You'll notice the property has some mileage on it but the place isn't falling apart by any stretch of the definition of the phrase. I suspect the new owner will likely put some cash into the place. For Wi-Fi access, use the signals identified as “Sonesta_Functions”. This is the hotel’s Wi-Fi service. Despite what the hotel directory says, it does not require a login. Some people reported that they were unable to use their VPN. Contact the Wi-Fi support people at the number listed in the hotel directory. It is strongly suggested that you DO NOT log into wireless networks that are not part of the hotel. This is not to say the hotel’s wireless is guaranteed safe, but there are many unscrupulous types out there just waiting to snatch passwords and login names from unprotected or under protected PC’s. ‘Nuff said. I had room service on my first night and I had the chicken Caesar. It was very good. It set me back $23 with delivery fee and tip. Delivery was estimated at 30 minutes on a Saturday night. Fifteen minutes later I was noshing on dinner. I had my first breakfast at the regular restaurant on a weekend morning. There is a breakfast buffet on Sunday for about $15 but no eggs are ready-made, so you have to order up with the waiter; kind of negates the purpose of a “self-serve” buffet. Eggs are included with breakfast so you won’t get dinged an additional charge for them. I had breakfast each weekday I was here as a convenience and a couple times for lunch. The food and service is good. Pricing is quite reasonable; about $12 for the “Express Scrambler” which I thought was quite adequate and tasty. You can easily get lunch for $12-$20. Street side seating is also part of the restaurant. “Café Express” is a little place within the hotel where you can get a quick breakfast sandwich or lunch, drink, coffee, yogurt, fruit, etc. I had the turkey on wheat with Swiss and it was very good. They are NOT part of the hotel and they don’t take AMEX; just Visa, MC and cash. There are a few small tables here if you want to sit in the café. There is a bar (pub) just off the elevators, lobby level and was pretty busy each night as I walked past after work. No surprise here. The exercise room is on the 8th floor near the pool. It is well equipped with 4 treadmills, 3 elliptical machines, 3 bikes and a conventional stair master machine as well as some dumbbells and a multipurpose weight machine. It is available 24 x7. Towels provided as well as a water cooler. Bring your ear buds or headphones as the exercise gear is equipped with A/V interfaces to 4 large LCD TV’s. No speakers though, hence the need for your own sound gear. There is soft drink vending on all floors. On floor 8 there is also a snack machine. There is no gift shop but there is a CVS pharmacy around the corner I was told but never stopped in. The hotel is situated smack in the middle of a very vibrant and busy section of town. There are many, many restaurants within easy walking distance. I recommend Devon at 225 18th Street and Serafino, which is also on 18th but about half the distance from the hotel. Both were great. While staying here, I also made use of the meeting rooms and the banquet services. All of the contracted services and specifications were well met and as far as I could tell we had no problems. We rented two large meeting rooms and the Wi-Fi services were no-charge. We also required power be available for attendees and they staff did a great job of putting in temporary power strips and securing them nicely with gaffer’s tape to the floor. Overall the venue was very good and problems, what few were experienced were readily handled by the hotel staff.

“FRESH HIP BOUTIQUE HOTEL ~” Stay here two nights with a baseball road trip tour. 2 blocks from the Space needle . Has a shuttle bus to downtown area. The "Rock" restaurant attaced was fun and reasonably priced. Room had great "extras" i.e. bottled water, frig, microwave, popcorn, and keurig coffee mahine with free coffee. Room was very clean. Very quiet for the most part. Staff was super friendly and helpful. Had afternoon "tea" with free coffee and pastries in the afternoon. Only negative I woud say is that there is nothing nearby for convenience. No stores for convenience like 7-11, a deli or pharmacy. Would definately recommomend this hotel.

“Wonderful Anniversary Trip!” My husband and I stayed here for our Anniversary trip from April 16 - 19, 2012. It was a wonderful experience beginning to end! This was our 4th visit to the Distrikt Hotel, New York City, New York. Starting with the reservation process, Peter was so helpful in making sure the details of our stay were correct, Also, I did a last minute, follow-up email, where Kayte reconfirmed everything was ready for our stay. Their professionalism helped set the tone for our visit! Thank you! Upon checking in at 2:45 p.m., Will, at the front desk was so helpful and professional making sure our room was ready for us. With keys, a complimentary continental breakfast coupon and a $20 coupon for food at the Collage Bistro in hand, we took the elevator to the 30th floor to Room 3001. It was a beautiful King room with a city and river view. Very quiet, super clean! There was a note from Ms. Rota, the General Manager welcoming us with brownies, a welcome note, A Distrikt tote bag and chocolates in a plastic container. WOW! This was wonderful! We went out for a walk to the Chelsea Market and when we returned the turndown service had been completed along with two amazing chocolate cupcakes and a card from the staff welcoming us too! Plus chocolates and a weather card on the bed. Another WOW! The room is beautifully appointed with fresh, clean towels, robe, a wonderful Coffee Maker with coffee and tea (thank you from an early riser!) and a great flat screen television. Our room was wonderfully kept by housekeeping and the turndown staff! We appreciate that greatly. The breakfasts in the Collage Bistro were wonderful and the service from Anthony and Miguel was flawless! A great way to start the day. Peter, again was so helpful with change, a cheerful disposition, welcoming and professional! Ana, was wonderful and checking if we needed anything, Neesha was wonderful and helpful with the printing of our boarding passes. Upon check out, Rachel, was wonderful, super kind and professional! Joseph was great at hailing a cab for our return to JFK airport and loading our suitcases in the trunk of the cab. ALL THE STAFF AT THE DISTRIKT HOTEL ARE THE BEST!! Ms. Jennifer Rota, the General Manager, should be commended for her management skill and leadership of her staff! We are also SO APPRECIATIVE all of her help with our room selection, the warm hospitality and gifts which made our anniversary celebration trip the best ever. We will definitely return to the Distrikt Hotel in the very near future!! Much Appreciation and great Thanks to you all! L.V. Hoffman, Florida

“Worked for us but is getting run down” Okay, I will admit I was torn between a 3 and 4 star rating for this hotel and in other circumstances I might give it a 3. We considered the Homewood Suites - Jacksonville South and came here solely based on price. I brought my family here to keep me company on a business trip and spend a long weekend. It turned out the hotel was about a block from my client which was great, and 3 miles from a very nice indoor mall (Avenues) where they could hang out while I was meeting for a couple of hours. On the upside, the staff has been really great. We paid for a 2-bedroom one night and used points for the other two. They kept us in the same room even though a reward redemption is technically only for a 1-bedroom. Breakfast was good and dinners, while not impressive, were free and free is good. The location is really solid relative to shopping, food, freeway and a lot of businesses. There are driveways both onto the main street and a sidestreet with a traffic light to turn left onto the main street which sounds trivial until you have to spend an hour trying to turn left. Our room could have been cleaner and better maintained, especially the carpets, but overall was fine. Cable channels were great for us. Even though it is on a main street, our room (231) was plenty quiet. I spend over 100 nights/year in hotels so here's my downside critique. I'm disappointed that many of the things people wrote about in reviews 2 years ago are still present. The onsite pond with fountain was completely algaed over. The property itself is in need of a lot of maintenance. I did not think the bed (or any other furnature) was particularly comfortable. Internet is wired rather than wireless and only in the living room. Kitchen does not have an oven (which is only bad because there is a Pepperidge Farm outlet very close and it would have been great to eat turnovers). The grounds are clearly being worked on but could use a lot more. Lots of weeds where there should be plants, mulch missing, plants that should be pruned, etc. As I said, for us this worked well. Since the new Homewood Suites was $70/night more, I would stay here again if paying with my own money. If I was using points or company money, I would probably try the new one.
