“Location Great !” this hotel is on the Mag mile and close to the redline L train that can get you all over the city; the room was small but so was the price I paid to right on the Mag mile ; the beds were comfy and room super clean; close to Hancock tower, great resturants, and shopping; I love staying at this hotel and stay there alot!

“A few snags, but very convenient to Logan” Connected directly to Terminal A via walkway...great as a Continental frequent flier for that early morning flight out. Unfortunately, the executive club was closed on Friday nite. The worst thing was the running toilet. It had a leak in the flapper and would run for a few seconds every few minutes. I called the operator. No one showed up for an hour. I went down to the front desk; they sent up someone who tinkered for a few minutes and said it was fixed. I knew it was a bad flapper, but he didn't fix it. I had to call again in a few minutes; they sent up someone again very quickly who changed out the flapper. The maintenance man then gave me a coupon for a free movie for the inconvenience. I thought that was a great gesture. Unfortunately, it was very pricey...$15 for internet; $17 for a hamburger, and $6.50 for a bottle of beer. They get you for the convenience.

“One of my favorite hotels...EVER!” The Palomar is fantastic...DuPont Circle location, near the subway and great restaurants. Nut aside from all that, the hotel itself is what's so great. I love the dog friendliness and the staff is remarkably friendly and capable. Because of the D.C. Palomar, I'm now addicted to the Kimpton experience! Plus, Eric Dane was at the hotel bar when we were there!!!

“Nice place in the heart of the theatre district” While the rooms here are a bit smaller than the typical Doubletree, finding an all suite hotel at the hub of activity around Times Square makes for a nice stay, especially if you have a younger child or two that won't mind a sleeper sofa for a few nights. Located at the NE corner of Times Square, there are a few rooms on each floor that give you a view of all the neon and people that makes this area so visually appealing. An easy walk to most of the major theatres/shows makes this a great location for the theatre goer. Families with kids who like the comfort of tried and true food chains will also enjoy this as close by are Planet Hollywood, TGI Fridays, Hardrock Cafe and others. For those who like to try smaller, local restaurants it is only a few minutes walk to a large selection of nice places including the collections of Italian restaurants along the periphery of Hell's Kitchen. The hotel itself is clean, with a uncluttered loby that includes a small bar/lounge area, a restaurant with a nice breakfast buffet and a fitness center. The rooms are bigger than your average NY hotel room with a sitting room and a separate bedroom. The bed was extremely comfortable and the bathroom was a bit bigger than other NYC hotels where I've stayed. Overall, this is a great place to stay if you want to be in the middle of the hustle and bustle that is Times Square.

“Mayflower - History is Alive” It breaks my heart to not give a higher rating, but a couple things bothered me on a recent trip for work. First, the lobby is BEAUTIFUL, I love the grand feeling much more than a modern hotel. My room was very large, bed comfortable, etc. A couple things - when I checked in the desk chair had a big stain on it - yuck! There was no paper, no pen in the room and a stain on the wall behind the bed and on the headboard. I left a note and most were corrected the first day but the dirty chair stayed with me all week! Also, the sofa off the elevators on my floor looked like it should be in a frat house, so stained and dirty. That stuff sticks with you. I had room service a few times, food was good. Staff was friendly and welcoming. The place was sure hopping, I guess a few larger groups were there. However, it was quiet at night, not disturbed by other guests. An odd thing, the toilet in my bathroom would just turn on every so many minutes to circulate water or something and it was LOUD. I eventually got used to the sound, but that was weird. The things I didn't like could easily be fixed. The hotel is still beautiful and grand. I enjoyed being there because my Dad told me he attended a ball the night of Pres. Kennedy's inauguration.

“Great value hotel” Stayed here in May. Location could not be better! Generally friendly service, clean rooms, free internet and value for money. Highly recommended if you're looking for a midrange hotel.
“素晴らしい” 建物は古いですが、立地、サービス共にとても素晴らしいです。 ミッドタウンなのに落ち着いていてグランドセントラルにも近く、ビジネスにも便利です。 食事、ルームサービスなどホテルの基本的なサービスはニューヨークでも良いレベルです。

“Aging Residence Inn in a convenient location with outstanding front desk service” Stayed here for one week in hot August. The HVAC worked wonderfully well. The rooms are spacious but showing their age. Comfortable and very functional, like a solid apartment. Not fancy. TVs were upgraded while I was there....a good sign that they are improving the place. Norma and other front desk staff were very friendly and helpful...getting to know guests and offering helpful suggestions and directions. Standard breakfast selections. I will stay there again, due to the staff. Their effort make this four star rating turn to five.

“Clean, comfortable, convenient” We stayed here 1 night to site see San Antonio. Julie at the front desk was very friendly and helpful. It is only a 1/2 block walk to the steps to the River Walk and the Alamo is close also. The room was very comfortable, set up as a suite with a queen sofa bed and twin cot folded and already in the room, if needed. Separating the sitting area and bedroom area is the coffee counter, sink and bath. There is a TV in both the bedroom and sitting area. We used the fitness room and it was very nice. Breakfast is not complimentary, but Julie gave us comp tickets to give to the waitress. I don't know if that is just for SPG members or not. We had a great stay and we were close to the main attractions, which was our goal.

“Good Precruise Stay” Located just off the highway by a mall. Quiet. Clean. We were able to book a two bedroom two bath suite with a kitchen for the five of us. (using Marriot points, bonus!) Good morning breakfast with hot items. Indoor pool with a hottub. Small workout room but they had a small fridge in there with iced towels. (nice touch) About 1 hour and 15 minutes from Galveston. I would stay here again.

“I'd stay here again!” Four Points by Sheraton Midtown's feature is its great location. It's near the train, also walkable from the Bolt Bus and from Times Square. Felt safe going home late at night (although yes, there are a few seedy characters nearby). The room was moderate sized. The bed was comfortable. Free bottle of water. Free high-speed internet. I'd stay here again.

“Pleasant Stay....met my needs!” This hotel met all my needs for a recent visit to Sea World. The room was very clean and I was able to get a parking right in front of the room. The hotel is nothing fancy, but I felt safe. Hotel Circle is indeed a busy area with a lot of businesses and hotels/motels. It's not a scenic area. I felt safe at this hotel and believe it is a good option for families looking for simple/nothing fancy lodgings near Sea World. The front desk staff member on duty when I checked in was very friendly and helpful. I was impressed with his politeness and his help in finding the number to my favorate Pizza place. I enjoyed my stay.

“The cookies are all you don't pay for” Quick and simple: Nice hotel, great location, accommodating staff, good service. And now, the BUT ... the cookies are the only thing you don't get nailed on here. You pay for parking ($10 a night), internet (come on, $13 a day for internet? Haven't we advanced to the point where you don't have to gouge for this anymore?), breakfast ($13 for the buffet and that's the cheap option), $3 for coffee in the lobby IF you're a Hilton GOLD member (alas, I'm but a silver, thank God there's a Starbucks across the street). Also, in regards to the rooms, would it kill Hilton to add a small fridge and/or microwave? Please? I was here for 8 days and it was tres inconvenient. But that would take away from the overpriced food in the downstairs restaurant. I was also fortunate to have a girls soccer team on the same floor and they spent the weekend partying and outdrinking each other. Not Doubletree's fault but it didn't add anything to the experience. Oh well. Nice Hotel. But stop gouging your business partners. My last stay at a Doubletree. Great job, Hilton.

“surprisingly good” So I'm sitting in the hotel right now, using the free internet, so guess that's fixed :) I've stayed here 3 times now over 2yrs, and have seen the place change, a LOT. To me, Sheratons are always a mixed bag within the Starwood chain: you know what to expect from a Westin or a W or even the 4points, but the Sheratons are always undefined. The renovation of the hotel makes it one of the nicer Sheratons I've been in, on a par with the nice one near Heathrow or SanFrancisco airport. Nice lobby, good rooms, free internet in room and lobby (although wireless only works in lobby). The location is pretty crap, as noted in several of these reviews. It's at the intersection of 610 & 290, which is not really very near... anything. It's not near the Galleria district, or downtown, or any restaurants to speak of. However, it's convenient to the highways, and easy/quick to get wherever you want to get. For the dollar, not a bad stay at all.

“Great Airport Hotel w Great amenities” We stayed here on 11/27 and again on 11/29 with a stay in the middle at the Hyatt Regency Cambridge. We arrived very late into Logan and were leaving very early on the 30th so chose to stay at Logan. AGAIN these properties are staffed VERY well!! The service is Great from everyone we encounter. Hyatt trains their staff so well across ALL eight brands!!

“Please with the hotel property and the location, not the internet or food” I stayed at the Courtyard Chicago Downtown/River North for nine nights while at a conference, with a couple of extra days for fun. For the most part I was very pleased and thought about giving it five stars. A few minor irritations prevented me. First, the good: The location was great for nightlife, restaurants, and getting around Chicago. I had no problem walking to various train stations to get around the city, and the hotel is a two minute walk from Michigan Avenue and only slightly further to the Loop. The hotel was immaculate and my room cleaned quite well every day. The front desk staff was helpful and friendly, as were the bellhops and housekeeping staff. Perhaps the best part was the room itself was super quiet; I could not near my neighbors at all, which is rare. I really appreciated that! The bed was also very comfortable! You should sleep very well here. The not so good: The internet is incredibly slow, as other reviewers have stated. There were times it was so slow it was unusable. When I needed to get some work done and answer some emails, I found this very aggravating. Another irritation was I had a daily credit at the State State Bread Company on site. The food there is very average, although there is also a Starbucks. When I checked out, at first the credit had not been applied to my room. It is a good thing I looked closely to make sure they applied it to my bill. None of the front desk clerks were very knowledgeable about the credit. I think they should be taught all the various special rates available online to help them answer questions and make checkout smoother. The people working at the State Street Bread Company all seemed unhappy to be there, and on the weekend they are very slow--don't waste your time there, get out and find something yummier and cheaper (or at least yummier!). The hotel was expensive but in line with other prices in Chicago. I would consider staying here again, but only for a pleasure trip when I do not need the internet very much.

“Recently remodeled and updated” Very nice updates to this Marriott. The restaurant and lobby area is very nice. Lobby can be loud at night with everyone enjoying happy hour. The gym is very nice, but a little tricky to find in the pool area. Concierge lounge is nice, but tiny. Great food and service. We had a meeting here, and they did everything they could to accommodate us and our needs. I asked for a Diet Sierra Mist, and they brought me 4 of them in a bowl with ice, and a glass with ice. My only complaint would be the shuttle ride to and from the airport. Its is long, and makes many stops, including to the Marriott O'Hare Suites. If time is on your side, or you are totally cheap, take the shuttle. However, if you want to get into your bed and be to sleep as soon as possible, take a cab. It runs between $16-$20 bucks.

“BEST HOTEL IN NY....hands down....” Stayed 3 nights starting on 8/28. Found email address for Patrick Armano - Director of Guest Experience via TA and contacted him regarding room checkin. Standard check-in is 3pm and I know its based on availability but was traveling with 8mth pregnant wife and 3 yr old daughter so wanted to see if they could get us in by 1pm. Arrived around 1pm and it was ready. Patrick and his staff including Victor were GREAT! They went above and beyond! Def a WOW!! If I could give them 10 stars I would. I'm not one to give any hotel 5 stars just b/c everything was "good," look at my other reviews, kind of defeats the purpose but W Time Square def deserves 10 stars. Front desk check in staff- Awesome. Ask for Sarah at checkin she is friendly and attentive. Kudos to her as well. Did not encounter one W staff person who was rude, they know how to provide excellent customer service. Location is perfect. You can walk out of the front door of the hotel and within 20 steps you are in the middle of Time Square. Can't beat that! Victor made sure to reach out to us during our stay to see if there was anything they could do for my pregnant wife. I will never forget this! For such a busy hotel to take the time and check in on us was amazing. No attitude like other hotels, asking questions was not perceived as if staff was doing us a favor, they were very accomdating. Other hotels I've stayed at in NYC, Parker Meridian, Roosevelt, W Lexington, Swiss hotel and Holiday Inn express, never will I stay at one of them again. It will always be W Time Square. Thank you again to Victor, Patrick, Sarah and GM Jim!! Other hotels in NYC should look towards you as an example.

“A nice hotel in a great location” Sandwiched between TKTS (discount theater tickets) and M and M World, the Renaissance NY Times Square is a terrific hotel in one of the most desirable locations in America. The check in entrance was deceivingly small. The lobby is actually on the second floor and sits over Broadway. It has a bar and is surprisingly quiet and relaxing. The building has something like 25 floors and the rooms are surprisingly quiet, immaculate, with newly renovated features, comfortable beds and bigger space than many NYC hotel rooms. There is a business center and a fitness room with mostly treadmills and stepping machines. No swimming pool. The restaurant is pricey, but hey, its NYC! The view is terrific and overlooks the heart of Times Square. Walk out the door and the quiet ends and you find yourself smack in the middle of Times Square and all of the hustle and Broadway shows. It is a block from the subway. Room internet costs $17, but the lobby internet is free! We were impressed and would stay here again.

“Rooms - great! Location - not so much.” If this place wasn't located in an industrial area a stone's throw from where all commercial truck traffic passes across the border, we'd be nominating it for a spot of the top 10 motel list. The rooms were spacious and the staff was attentive and helpful. The breakfast was good although as one poster commented, it gets crowded so I wouldn't wait to about 10 to 9 to try and get your breakfast unless you don't mind waiting 15 minutes to get to the waffle maker. There aren't many dining options in the area other than fast food, but it was late when we got in (almost 9) and we called up Bambino's Italian restaurant to see if they were open and the owner decided to stay open for me and my family. He welcomed us to his restaurant and we had an excellent meal. I wouldn't recommend walking across the border here. We decided to avoid Tijuana thinking we might find it easier to shop here. Well, there is almost no shopping to speak of. When you finally walk to the main drag, it is lined with auto part stores and other non-descript offices. We did find a little mini-mart where we bought a liter of vanilla and a small pharmacy. That was about it, although the people were friendly and willing to help. Downtown San Diego is about 25-30 minutes away so if you don't mind driving in and parking and spending the day there, you can save yourself some money and hassle from downtown by staying here.

“Plusses and minuses...mainly minuses” We stayed here for a combination business/leisure trip booked via Priceline. I tend to be a very forgiving reviewer that mostly ends up in the 2 to 3 star category. Here are the plusses and minuses we experienced on our 3-day stay *Plusses Front desk staff was very nice Lobby is nice and comfortable Free High speed Ethernet (not wireless, at least in our room) which is fine beds are comfortable while we didn't eat there, the restaurant looks great. $12 for breakfast buffet nice indoor pool and hot tub convenient access to I-25 Starbucks located adjacent to property King Soopers, Jimmy Johns, Coldstone Creamery across the street *Minuses Can be a long walk to your room...very long, depending on placement Elevators have problems. Doors get stuck, may take a long time, etc Room smelled a bit musty on arrival Room decor and layout is decidedly outdated (as mentioned elsewhere) Adjacent hotel seems to be abandoned hot tub temperature not so hot shower temperature - on HOTTEST setting - still just lukewarm corridors and rooms are very dark and somewhat depressing bathroom is cramped Based on our price, we were satisfied with the hotel and count it average in most respects. But we would definitely not seek this hotel out to return to.

“Excellent!” We are currently staying at the Hotel Vitale and I totally agree with the reviews already posted. The hotel is located very well near Embarcadero and the Ferry building. If you don't like hotel breakfasts (I don't because I generally eat too much), the market hall is a few steps away and provides some excellent places. The design and the amenities are absolutely outstanding, the view even from the 2nd floor on Bay Bridge is amazing. F Streetcar is right at the back of the building for those who don't like to walk too much.

“Nice property but difficult sleeping from the activity across the street” The staff is excellent! Elevators run fast. Has it's own parking garage and valet if you wish (for a charge). The breakfast buffet was good and if you are a priority club member they have a lounge on the 15th floor where you can get snacks late in the afternoon or a simple breakfast. The rooms have been re-modeled and are art-deco. The sink is located outside the bathroom but it presented no problem and I kind of liked it. Internet worked well. As a previous reviewer stated, I was in a room on the 11th floor on the North side of the building and I could hear the music and the DJ loud and clear from the ground below. My advice is you ask for a room on the south side (higher room numbers I believe). I will stay again but this time will be sure to request a special room. Downtown Charlotte is a wonderful, safe area!

“I'd stay again!” The Harrington has a number of benefits outside of the price. You can walk to the National Mall, to Macey's, to Chinatown, and any of 30 or 40 restaurants, The Spy Museum- really worth a visit is 3 blocks away, and Starbucks and Barnes and Noble both a block away. There's always a taxi outside and the metro is 2 minutes walk. So seriously, you couldn't be in a better location. The hotel itself? No problem booking in, and reception helped with brochures and restaurant maps. The room - a king- was comfortable, but furnishings are dated. Lots of TV channels though, and everything is clean. Only complaint was the noise at night- I think it would be better asking for a non street facing room. The aircon was also a bit iffy, but the weather was mild and we didn'r really need it. There are 2 restaurants- we had breakfast twice at Harriets. Order a'la Carte- the buffet was dissapointing. There is a useful kiosk in reception too- candy, newspapers, and little things you may have forgotten like aspirin and toothpaste can be bought there. All in all, I'd stay here again for sure!

“Tradition and lots of formality” Other reviews have given mixed comments about the formal nature of this hotel, but the reality is it's an old men's club that is trying to hold on to its traditions. You expect to see DicK Chaney around every corner, and during my visit there were many formal events going on for the holidays. I thought it was fun to watch, but it's not for everyone. The rooms are (of course) old and not fancy but have all of the expected features. Threre can be noise due to a jazz club across Sansom Street. Ask for a different side of the hotel if that's a concern. I didn't eat in the hotel for dinner, but there is a very nice breakfast buffet that is included in the price of the room. One caution, it doesn't open until 8:00 on Saturday, which was a problem for me. (I guess no one in such traditional places does business on Saturday mornings.) The location in downtown Philadelphia could not be better, so if you are staying downtown, and you don't mind dressing rather properly on the main floors of the hotel, you may consider this an enjoyable trip into the past.

“Eastgate - Thumbs Up!” My wife and I recently spent 5 nights at the Eastgate Tower Hotel (March 1-6) and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We booked a Junior Suite and it felt like we had our own 1-bedroom apartment (kitchenette, spacious sofa area and dining table) - and, above all, at an affordable rate. Important to add that the room was impeccably clean. We were checked in within minutes and given a key to a safety deposit box (upon request). Hotel staff was courteous and efficient. The walk to the the Times Square area is about 15 minutes. We liked being several blocks east of 5th ave. - a noticeable difference in the level of traffic noise at night. Upon our return, we received an e-mail from the hotel inquiring about our stay. A first class operation all the way for budget-minded travellers.

“Love this hotel” I have only stayed in the suites at this hotel and can say that the rooms are wonderful. Very high-tech with the central control for the lights, drapes and phone. The location is amazing - walking distance to Union Sqaure and Moscone. The service is excellent. Everyone is helpful and very courteous. The one thing that I noticed this year is that some of the cabinets in the living room were in need of repair (they were falling off the hinges). And at the price their charging, I feel this small detail shouldn't be overlooked. Otherwise, everything was great.

“really strange place - dark and lots of art - but strange feel and smells” the check in was good - the room smells like mold and everything is really dark. Blacks and tan. The room service menu is really limited, and not what I would consider very healthy. really disappointing. exercise room is nice and open 24 hours, staff is very friendly. So - for the price there are better options. The next issue was the smell of mold and dampness in the hotel - this is April, so wonder what it will be like in August.

“Almost perfect” Overall the hotel is exceptional, with only a couple misses. 1st we ordered rose pedal turndown service due to it being my girlfriends birthday, I confirmed it online for the upgrade request. It did not happen, and of course I assumed it would of happened when we went to dinner at the French Room, by the time we got back around mid-night there really wasnt any reason to call the front desk. 2nd and by far the most important, we had a large suite and the A/C could not handle the room with the Dallas heat, we had it down to 40F, I have never seen a thermostat go that low but we had it there. The room was cool but far from cold. Other than those 2 minor things, the hotel was outstanding. French Room was even better, little hotel bar in the lobby was great, service was fast and the drinks were poured correctly.

“Summer rates and service make this a good Phoenix hotel” Much like its sister property at Tapatio Cliffs, in order to enjoy your stay here you do need to keep things in perspective. The Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak property is comprised of desert style stucco structures, and it sits in the middle of a part of town that is largely small business parks. In terms of appearance, the Westin Kierland it isn't. Still, I think this hotel has a lot of good qualities that make it a good value, particularly in the summer months when rates are low. I was upgraded to a bi-level casita which was more than ample room for me traveling alone. The furnishings and fridge were older but there was nothing in disrepair and the room was clean. The casitas have dedicated parking right there which is handy. I had neighbors but I didn't hear them. My only complaint about the room is that the AC system was loud. But since it was effective in keeping the room at 73 when it was 105 outside it's a little hard to complain about this. The internet service was a bit dodgy and required occasional restarts; not sure why that was, but it was a bit frustrating. I had great service from the staff. Front desk, restaurant bar, poolside bar, all very friendly. I think this is always worth mentioning given how many uptight travelers and stressed out parents these people must have to deal with. I view the location of this hotel as a net neutral. It's pretty central to the overall valley; whether it's good for you depends on what you plan to do, obviously. I played golf in Mesa and Scottsdale and this property is sort of between those two places. There is a Walgreens and a grocery store right down the street which is handy. The main pool area gets much attention in the reviews, and rightfully so, as there is a lot of activity there during the day. As I was there in late July I'm sure I didn't see the type of crowds that others have seen in high season. From what I could see the pools and the "lazy river" were clean; I would defer to reviews from people who stayed in high season on these issues, though. The primary pool area really isn't all that big so I could see it getting very crowded in busy times. I would have liked it if more of this area had been open later, but I understand this is a costs and staffing issue. I didn't eat at the restaurants here. I'll defer to others on that. The restaurant at the front of the property appeared to have a pretty varied menu, though. Overall I think this is a good property, and a good value particularly in summertime. For myself I enjoyed my stay at this property and am planning to return with the kids in tow.

“Good location, expensive parking” Over the years I've stayed here several times. Rooms are nice, but I've never been able to get one with any sort of view. The location is great--walking distance to lots of Boston sights. Mall access is--strangely--attractive. Particularly for reasonably priced foods. There is a grocery within walking distance too. The conference facilities are pretty standard. On this last trip, the AV staff were very attentive. That was unusual compared to previous trips. Don't bother to drive here. Parking is hideously expensive.

“Small rooms, nice lobby.” I stayed for a night, using reward points. The lobby and history of the hotel is fascinating. However, my room was so small I thought I was in New York City. It's a good thing it was only a place to sleep for this stay. The walls were also paper thin, we could here people coming and going.

“Vaisseau de verre.” Design, central, fonctionnel, opérationnel, douillet, francophile, gourmet. Un regret: je ne rends plus à Chicago pour raisons professionnelles. Une remarque: une femme de service est entrée dans ma chambre sans frapper alors que le signe 'ne pas déranger' était sur ma porte. J'y reviendrai...en vacances! ;)

“Frustrating experience” Fine service (friendly and helpful), internet, free breakfast, rooms, pool, and hot tub. Very convenient location. But some extremely annoying frustrations. Card keys constantly stopped working. Had to get new keys 5 times in a 2 night stay. Only 1 very slow elevator for a 7 story hotel (many people give up and use stairs). Fitness center: single recumbent exercise cycle falling apart, with constant shorting out and resetting. Rooms with 2 beds are only full size (not queen), which is very cramped for two people.

“"Great room but . . .” I was in Boston for business. I got the room on Hotwire. I paid $169. The hotel is beautiful and the room was perfect. No complaints about the room. The staff was very nice. My only complaint about the property is that it is a 2-story 150 room property. My room was on the second floor with a view of the harbor. Unfortunately, when I opened the window, I looked directly into a "yacht" where the owner was having breakfast. No privacy. I had to keep my shades closed for most of the time. Also, the only way to get from the Hotel to the Spa is a brief walk outside. Not a problem, except when it is 8 degrees out and you are wearing shorts. The work-out facility was very good. The location of the hotel was well situated for the North End, but not anywhere near where I needed to be. It is essentially in a mixed use residential section of town. A pretty easy and short walk to the North end but, on a cold dark winter night, not the most pleasant walk in the city.

“einfach furchtbar” Für dieses Hotel eine Bewertung abzugeben, fällt schon schwer, es sei denn man zählt all die Mängel auf. Das Hotel ist schmutzig, abgelebt und hat (k)einen lausigen Service. Die Zimmer sind total veraltet mit unhygienischen Oldschool hohen Teppichboden in den Zimmern. Zwar ist das Restaurant im Hotel offiziell bis 22:30 Uh geöffnet, aber wenn man um 22 Uhr hinkommt, heißt es, dass man doch den Room Service in Anpruch nehmen soll!!! Das Frühstück war eine Katastrophe; Die Rühreier hart wie Stein, es gab für das gesamte Restaurant nur einen Toaster. Die Teller waren schmutzig und feucht und um 07:45 gab es keinen Frühstücksspeck mehr. Wer hier bucht sollte genau wissen, was er tut.

“Great for business and fitness travelers” Stayed two nights for business in April, the most outstanding feature is the fitness center available to guests (free for Hilton Honors silver or above). Probably the best fitness center I have ever seen at a hotel. full weights, machines, plenty of cardio, steam room, lockers, showers, etc. There was a yoga class in session when I went down. The rest of the hotel was adequate, typical Hilton amenities. Rooms were clean, nice flat screen tv, nice beds towels, etc. The building is older so has limits of all older buildings (rooms are cut up a little bit funny) but elevators and heating cooling were OK, which is not always the case in older building. they are going through some lobby area renovations, so hopefully along run plus for them. Walkable to the White House. Overall, decent hotel, if you love fitness centers - this is the place for you

“Friendly Staff the best at JW” I arrived with my 7yo daughter in Denver for 3 days of shopping and mother daughter time before flying out of DIA. We have always stayed in downtown Denver and I decided to try Cherry Creek. It was a great decision. Hotel was very easy to find and the minute we arrived the valet was so nice and check-in was a breeze. I especially liked that they came from behind the check-in counter to hand me my keys and information and shake my hand and welcome me. The entire stay they referred me as Mrs. ... and my daughter Miss ... she thought that was cool. Breakfast was good, pretty ordinary buffet but some good choices off the menu. Location terrific! Could walk to all shopping & restaurants. Room was typical upscale room, but bathroom was large with tub and separate shower and large marble vanity. Check-out and retrieving car was the quickest I've EVER had. Just a great hotel, and especially super professional staff.

“Well located, affordable hotel” We stayed for a quick weekend at the Days Inn in Lincoln Park. It is at a busy intersection, but we used the fan in the room and it drowned out all the street noise. The rooms were clean; the beds and pillows very comfortable. The staff was very friendly. The complimentary breakfast was one of the nicest we've seen with a pleasant area to sit. Their coffee is very good! We definitely plan to stay there again.

“This classic is worth a visit...” I had not stayed here in many years, since it was a Westin Property. The rooms are large, well furnished, impeccably clean with large baths and plenty of closet space. I really liked the look of the hotel, and really enjoyed my stay here. The pool area is HUGE, and wonderful. Great place for cocktails on the outside patio or in the main lobby, which is a place to see and be seen. I also LOVED the Regency Club. Great staff...so friendly and accommodating. The breakfast service was standard fair, and very nice. Same with the evening service. Nice appetizers, and a great way to start the evening. The Club also has a self service 'snack' bar where you can get fresh pistachios, M&M's, peanuts, and other snacks. Loved this....but my diet hated it. :) I also love the proximity to Century City Center across the street. Just walk over and catch a movie at the AMC, or explore the shops. The health club at this hotel is HUGE and wonderful. Im glad I had the opportunity to discover this gem once again. I will be back!

“A No Frills Hotel with an Affable Staff” San Francisco is my favorite city in the United States, and when I visit, I don’t require luxurious lodging because I’m never in my room. That’s why the Marriot Marquis hotel, situated on Fourth Street, is a great base. I hope that statement didn’t seem snide; I simply believe the hotel doesn’t offer grand accommodations. Due to its size, you’re not going to have much interaction with the staff at the Marriott Marquis besides housekeeping (who are extremely personable). This hotel was made to host conferences and it feels like it. Everyone walks around with badges on their lapels and meet in the lobby bar to discuss the day’s sessions. My room was located on the 26th floor with an obstructed view of the Bay Bridge. The room, which had a double bed, was clean and spacious. The bathroom was ordinary. The gym, which abuts an uninviting pool, is moderate in size. I ordered room service one evening and it arrived promptly (and hot). This isn’t one my liveliest reviews, simple because the property didn’t offer anything for me to laud. What’s worth mentioning is its location: a block from the Powell St. Bart station and a plethora of shops on Market St.

“Decent but Questionable” When I arrived to check-in, some guy was complaining about how his stuff had been stolen... that led me to ask for a room in the safest part of the hotel (I was quickly offered a second floor room). I personally would not stay on the first floor because it looks like it would be easy to break into. Once I was in the room, it was decent. Small TV but a decent amount of space. Two annoyances that happened while I was there: (1) I was working on my computer and my smoke detector went off randomly. There are some smoking rooms but not on my floor. I think it came up from the first floor, through the bathroom fan vent. I jumped up and tried to get the battery out but I broke the face off instead. Once I had fanned away all the air and gotten it to stop screaming, I went into the hallway to see what was going on, as I still didn't smell smoke. I got a very faint wiff as I was nearing the bathroom/main door and I saw that the fire door released and closed. I explained all this later to the management as the reason for me breaking the smoke detector and he was fine with it (no charge). (2) a very large dog checked into the room beside me one night and the stupid lady proceeded to leave the dog along for a few hours. Of course it barked and barked and barked.... until about 10:30pm when I decided to go downstairs and harass the management. I gave them hell for about 15-20 minutes and I didn't really like the guy's attitude (at one point he was explaining HER rights as a guest to me!!!). Anyway, I asked him to move the woman to a secluded part of the hotel since it wasn't full and I believe he did this. I left for about an hour to get a bite to eat and no barking when I returned. I just felt like the guy should not have been so blase about the whole thing, esp since it was getting to be fairly late. I stayed at this hotel for about 11 nights and I kept staying because my funds were limited and it was $30/night through Priceline. I agree with another reviewer that this should be a 2 star hotel and not a 2.5 star as per Princeline. There are some sketchy people around the hotel so I would not recommend it to women traveling alone. However, it's more than fine for guys looking for a cheap place to stay and probably okay for couples. If I had children I wouldn't bring them here unless I had to. I would, however, bring my dog since its late-night barking would be welcome!

“great hotel” I was really pleased with this hotel from the moment the my luggage was snapped up by the bellperson. I had great service from everyone there. The room was average sized with perhaps a little less room for clothes then some, but I really liked the trendy/modern furniture - it wasn't your typical hotel room. I like natural light and I appreciated that I had a corner room that was very bright as it had four large windows. The king sized bed was very comfortable and the room had a flat screen TV. The bathroom was a tad-bit smaller than some - when you sit on the commode your knees are against the tub/wall, but it was such a nice bathroom that I didn't mind - marble floor, tile walls and deep tub. The sink was pretty cool - it was mounted in this frosted glass shelf and the plumbing was all exposed. Plus there was a 6 inch wide glass shelf that ran the length of the bathroom. As I never have enough room in most hotels for toiletries I liked this. The room was very clean and I didn't hear any outside noise, though this may have been due to the white noise of the heater. I tend to avoid hotel restaurants, but I tried the sushi here and was very pleased. Plus, the happy hour prices on their food are a great deal. I was attending a conference and the location was great - easy walking distance to conference center and lots of downtown attractions. I never did totally figure out the bus system, though. I'd asked the concierge how to get to Pioneer Square and she printed out a sheet with several routes, which bus numbers to catch, where to catch them and the times they were scheduled to arrive. I walked to the stop and it had a map and a listing of the buses scheduled to stop there and the buses I had been given was not listed. One of these buses actually did stop there and I never did ask why it wasn't listed anywhere that I can see. This actually has nothing to do with the hotel other than to say you can trust the info they give you, even if the routes aren't listed at the stop.

“Pleasantly surprised” Spent one weekend night. Great location. Courteous staff. Early chek in. Basic rooms but clean. Nconvenient to everything. Nice weekend Buffett breakfast. Expensive but fast valet. Starbucks on sight needs more staff. Accidentlt left shirt in closet. Called security who kept it for me when I returned.

“A good bargain in midtown” This is a perfect New York Hotel. It was not expensive (booked on priceline). The room was small, yet clean, modern and comfortable. The room was quiet. No frills yet perfect for my short business trip. The location is right next to Times Square yet the lobby was super quiet and you did not feel like you were in Times Square at all. The check in was efficient but not friendly but who cares anyway. I did not have any problems but I just slept in the room. The concierge printed out my boarding pass for me at no charge and also helped me figure out transportation issues. I would definitely stay there again on business if the rate was good.

“Overpriced, but a good hotel” I stayed in NYC for work and pleasure for six days at three hotels, the Intercontinental Times Square, the Hilton Times Square and the W Union Square. The W was a solid hotel, but i frlt overpriced. The location is terrific however for accesss to so many aprts of the city as so many trains go newr Union Square. It also has amgreat walk score,with easy access to so many great parts of the city. The free apples on the front desk was a nice touch as well. Of the 3 hotels i stayed in that trip,the intercontinental was the newest and had the best rate. It's a gorgeous hotel and near Times Square. Great service, nice staff. Hilton wasn't bad, but lobby was on a high floor, but had a large area for sitting, working and hanging out. Main entrance was under construction so one entered on 41st St. W Union Square was nice, but room not as much light as the other two and also didn't have as good views although it was in a great location. the W was normally more expensive, but I had a discount local rate through work. W's bar area is neat, but also sort of small. For the money at hotels normal rates, the Intercontinental was the best value.

“A wonderful European Atmosphere!” I booked this hotel for a weekend layover after attending a conference. My sister flew in to meet me and we spent three nights at the hotel. The lobby and common areas are drop dead gorgeous while the rooms are a little "motelish" and tired. Interestingly, the bathroom was the one spot that was updated and fresh which made a big difference! But that didn't matter in the end. The staff and location more than made up for the lack of luxury. There is a fantastic outdoor patio with stunning views of Broadway-lots of seating and no need to order a thing! We were greeted by name virtually every time we hit the lobby. The bellmen (ALL OF THEM!) could not have been more gallant and friendly. We felt like we were the only americans in the place and that was fine by us. The majority of guests were from France, followed by England, Germany and Italy. It made for a very cool atmosphere and a departure from ordinary. It is the city hotel for Air France and all of the crew members were charming and friendly! LOCATION _ LOCATION_LOCATION!. Turn left out the front door and and there are two theaters and go two blocks and you are in Hell's Kitchen with a stunning array of eclectic cafes. Turn right and you are on Broadway, two blocks from Time Square. Turn right and hike a couple of blocks to Avenue of the Americas (6th), take a left and you are at Central Park in a few blocks. Stop and hook a right before Central Park and you hit 5th Avenue, Madison, etc...SHOPPING. Subways are close and taxis all over the place. What a great place. I will go back. Heck, first night in and there was Omar Sharif in the lobby cafe. He was so friendly and accommodating, meeting "Dr. Zhivago" set the tone for the entire trip! Ian at the front desk was a sweetheart when dealing with the "two sisters from Texas" and I greatly appreciated that. Truly a great bunch of people working at Novotel.

“Reasonable hotel for conference traveler” This hotel has an interesting design. I stayed for 3 nights in April 2012 in room 1901. The room past a full bed bug check of the mattress. Room has refrigerator in the room, which is helpful. Bathroom is slightly small, with sink in the room area without a door. The hotel is large and has many events going on at once. It is very close to a mall with a food court (connected by bridge) and the convention center. Staff is reasonable and friendly.

“Loved the Hilton” Stayed in the Hilton for 2 nights in December. On check in we were given a room on the 44th Floor with a view over the WTC site and on to the river. The rooms were clean and spacious and the staff were helpful and friendly. Although this hotel is in the business / financial district I would not hestitate to stay here again, as everything is so accessible via the Metro. The only slight concern is the lack of restuarants in this area - but if you're prepared to travel - not a problem. We will definitely be back.

“Another great Kimpton (sorry to sound like a broken record)” While I apologize for sounding like a broken record, we have stayed at yet another Kimpton, The Muse. Everything about The Muse was great - staff, rooms, lobby, wine hour and especially location. I was a little concerned because it was right off Times Square but other than normal city noise, you couldn't hear a thing. The room was surprisingly spacious (NYC hotel rooms are not known for their size), it was clean and beautifully decorated. If I had to give a con it would be the bed - way too soft. As in my other reviews, Kimpton is now my favorite chain and I thank them for their gift to my husband who was celebrating his birthday. This is our 5th Kimpton in 12 months. Thanks Kimpton.

“Overall a standard Ritz-Carlton property, with some exceptions...” I stayed at the Ritz-Carlton for five nights recently for a combined business and pleasure trip to San Francisco. Because of the significantly reduced occupancy rate (a cab driver mentioned anecdotely that while fully booked previously, the hotel was experiencing occupancy of only 30% lately), I was able to get a great rate that included daily breakfast for two, valet parking, and internet access, amounting to at least $100 worth of giveaways. The hotel itself occupies a very nice location, midway on Nob Hill facing the skyscrapers of the financial district. The decor could be described on the stuffy side, but everything was incredibly comfortable and well kept. The room itself was reasonably sized, but certainly not large. It had a residential feel, somewhat like that of a wealthy friend's townhouse. Linens were of high quality, and soundproofing was excellent. I don't know if it was because of the light occupancy, but I never heard some much as a peep once inside my room. Overall service was good, but not superb. It lacked the "wow" factor that I've become accustomed to at many high end hotels. One night was a particular example - after arriving back from dinner, I walked back to my room without receiving a single recognition or "good evening" from a staff member, although I passed several along the way. Staying at other Ritz Carlton properties, I often found it impossible to avoid staff member greetings, but this was not the case. It may appear a minor quibble, but that's what give high end properties a certain panache - the high "touch" level. Although the service was very competent, this particular property lacked that "touch". Daily breakfast in the Lobby Lounge was always very good. Service was somewhat disorganized on the first morning, which was an exceptionally busy weekend. Food was of high quality and very well presented. My juice and coffee cups were never empty. Overall it was a good stay, but again, not exactly the best Ritz-Carlton out there. If I had my choice again I would probably try the St. Regis or Four Seasons, but the Ritz-Carlton certainly is a top notch hotel.

“A Small square” The Best Western Pioneer Square Hotel is in a very historic area of Seattle. The location is in close walking distance to the two sports facilities in Seattle and other shopping and eating locations in Seattle. The room that we had was a small room, I am sure there are larger rooms. The staff was good however they do not have a parking facility in the hotel. We arrived after 9PM and they did not have anyone there to help with our luggage but there was someone there in the morning. The parking garage is almost 2 blocks away from the hotel. The hotel is clean and well maintained. Pioneer Square is a great area to walk around during the day but you want to be very careful at night. There are a lot of homeless people in the area, they did not bother me when I walked back to the hotel from the parking garage. There is a small bar next door that only serves beer and wine. This would be a great hotel if you do not want to spend time in your room but want to walk around Seattle.

“The Willard--Friendly Service, Elaborate Furnishings, the Best!” We just returned from a fabulous weekend pleasure stay at the Willard in Washington D.C. Check in at nine in the evening was fast and helpful. The charming employee recommended tour buses, restaurants, and places to visit, as well as checking the weather for our two-day stay in Washington. Room service was equally fast and rather delicious. The concierge was helpful in giving directions to sights, although his hour-long "lunch break" at 6pm made dinner-planning difficult. Our Deluxe Room with two double beds was spacious and comfortable. The housekeeping was excellent, miraculously cleaning our room even if we were out for only a few hours. Turn down service was a nice touch. All staff were very pleasant, friendly, and helpful. Our only caution is that since the Willard caters to the business and political elite, walking around in the hotel in touristy clothes occasionally made us feel a tad awkward. Nevertheless, the Willard's excellent staff and rooms made for a delightful stay. We will certainly return!

“Great Location. Creature Comforts & San Diego” Having been to San Diego for conferences in the past, I was looking forward to attending this business meeting, this hotel helped make it one of the best. Omni Hotels brand is a great customer service focused enterprise. Check in was very welcoming, card-keys waiting. I got a mid-level floor. Every morning had OJ, coffee, and a paper waiting for me. Simple pleasures so far from home. The hotel decor was subtle-chic and staff unobtrusive. Hotel bar food tasty. Lobby bar very expensive, but not to worry, the Gas lamp district is right outside the door. Extra-ordinary selection of restaurants for foodies (also, visit the Palm Steakhouse a few blocks away) Conference Rooms were fine seats were comfortable. Better yet, when interrupted for a phone call, you can walk out on the veranda and speak in 70 degree San Diego sun while the Santa Fe railroad cars slowly coast by. I understand why people love San Diego. Rooms were well appointed, not ostentatious. Toiletries are among the best in the industry. Everything in the city is within walking distance. The convention center is across the street. This is the only place i would stay for another convention.

“Queen bed...NOT!!” The beds are very very small. My husband and I had to take turns turning over. My mother in law thought she could have her 2 nieces in one bed and her and her daughter in another but the doubles are twins. So they have no kings, queens that are doubles and doubles that are twins. The only good thing is that you can walk to restaurants and Walgreens. The rooms are too small...hell the pillows are small. Never again.

“Good Value Hotel, Good Location” Stayed there since the convention hotel nearby was sold out. Comparing to the outrageous price charged at the convention hotel, this is relatively good value in such a downtown area. The hotel is close to shops, restaurants.

“At discount rates, top-notch value for luxurious comfort” This is my favorite Seattle hotel and arguably one of the top three Marriotts I would recommend in the USA. It's a popular stop for tourists transiting the cruise ship terminal across the street as well as business travelers seeking a bit of luxury in a great location. Both colorful Pike Street Market and eclectic Belltown are minutes away by foot. Although I have paid full-freight, the Waterfront Marriott becomes a stupendous value at discounted rates. Check for specials. I recently arrived on a chilly February afternoon, but the Marriott hospitality would soon warm me up. The hotel lobby exudes Seattle charm with generous glass sculptures, dreamy trance and jazz, and well-accented furnishings with outstanding lightning. The valet parking staff and bellmen are universally friendly and efficient. Within a day, they knew my name and helped with a special request. The front desk staff were very accommodating, even indulging me while I snapped photos inside one evening. Room furnishings are quite comfortable with luxurious bedding, although I never have cared much for most Marriott computer work areas. You probably know what I mean. The chair and desk arrangements are often uncomfortable. From the 8th floor, I had a nice view of the container ship Kauai docked at the cruise ship terminal. (Others have noted the same, but I have no surprise at seeing a docked ship in a working port.) I could also watch the passenger ferries cross the sound's waters and discharge near the end of Madison Street. The lobby bar is an excellent place to relax or to meet with friends before a night on the town. Bartenders Chris and Cody can banter with the best and bring a smile to a weary traveler, even if just with a great drink. Food-wise, previous travelers may remember Todd English and should know he and Marriott parted ways at the New Year. His Fish Club restaurant no longer occupies one corner of the building. While the restaurant host told me they serve Sunday brunch in the former FIsh Club, most of the dining is done in the side lobby on the street side of the bar. The setting is a bit dark and dreary. The host -- who may have been the manager -- was hardly forthcoming when I asked questions and was the sole staff member who failed to impress me. The waitress, on the other hand, was friendly and attentive, and she answered all my questions about the food and the operations. It seems the dining area will be re-done in the coming months. Grumpy host and darkness aside, the food was simply outstanding, the center of which was a perfectly medium-rare 16 oz NY steak with baby asparagus and rich, creamy potatoes. WIne selections are reasonably priced for a hotel with a wide variety of quality labels. I enjoyed breakfast in the concierge lounge, which has a limited but adequate range, and evening snacks were pretty good. One night I had a Reuben at the bar, and it delivered on satisfying my hunger. You have a million dining options in Seattle, too. Anthony's Pier 66 is across the street, nearby Ivar's, and many flavors of Belltown are a few blocks away. While taxi fares are not inexpensive in Seattle, no place in the downtown district or China Town is very far. Even the baseball and football stadiums are accessible by a long walk or a short cab ride. Swing by for some dim sum before or after a the big game. If you're driving, you can self-park or take advantage of the valet parking ($34/day). For business travelers with meetings in the downtown area, staying here is a no-brainer if on a discounted rate. Ditto for tourists. Check for package rates, including some sports events, as well as weekend specials, particularly during the cooler months.

“Luxury and Convenience” If you want boutique hotel luxury in the thick of things in San Francisco with convenient local transport, proximity to both Union Square and the Moscone Convention Center AND you don't want generic blah, blah hotel experiences, then you will love this gem of a hotel. I stayed in a sister property in December (see my review of Hotel Palomar, Washington, DC) and fell in love with the service and attention to a guest's needs. If I have learned anything from staying at this hotel, it is their attention to meeting your every need, but the key is that they are not mind-readers and you need to speak up if any single thing is not to your liking. Don't like a meal? They will make it right or comp you. Unhappy with amenities? They will fix things. Really, Palomar goes out of the way to make sure your stay is perfect and that you receive attention from individuals who are decision-makers. It really is like Sax 5th Avenue, not Macys. Arrival: Instantaneous check in with the room available I had requested: Zen garden for quiet. Flavored waters to quench your thirst. Room: Beautifully appointed, spacious. Massive king bed with the feather pillows I had requested. Complimentary Internet with quick log-in because I am an InTouch member. (Join: it's free and there are little perks for members.) Choice of 3 newspapers every day and I could have all three. I had requested a complimentary goldfish "friend" in his own tank, which I had also requested in DC when my children were with me. Food: I did not try room service on this occasion, but did dine at 5th Floor for dinner. Nothing short of spectacular, truly. My server really knew wines and did perfect pairings with my choices. The layers of flavors in the fresh asparagus salad and then in the ravioli were complex and sublime. That said, I strongly suggest the hotel upgrade breakfast service. Very costly for offerings that were mediocre. Overall: On weekdays, there is a wine hour with complimentary white or red. Nice touch, but DC hotel did offer champagne, too. Should have asked! Hotel is pet-friendly but I emphasize that the place has no "doggy" smell nor have I even seen many in 2 stays at 2 different properties. (1 friendly lap pooch on this trip was it. I understand there may be a floor reserved for people with pets, but not certain.) Because I was attending a conference, I think my rate was better than most, but I recommend you watch for their specials or call them directly to see if you can get a better price. In summary, I would return in a heartbeat to this Palomar or any other!

“Excellent value, Comfortable place to stay.” Located on a large chunk of land between the interstate and a Mall, this is an interesting place. It is a little rough around the edges in places but has a lot to like and I would far rather stay here than a chain hotel anytime. The impression I had was of a property that had been allowed to run down and is now being brought back to life. The roughness seems more towards the rear of the property where you will find a lot of chipped paint and dirty looking concrete walkways, but there is also a very- much- in- evidence spruce up program under way. There was nothing objectional - just little things. I was like seeing a well dressed man wearing a pair of run down shoes. On the plus side, it is very reasonably priced and everyone on staff that I met was extremely friendly and helpful. The property has a mixture of accommodation styles ranging from garden cottages to a nine story outside corridor cement block tower that is straight out of the 1970’s Holiday Inn design book. I booked a room in the tower as it was closest to the convention center, and it was ok, clean and well furnished with a balcony overlooking a swimming pool and gardens. One minor discontent is that the curtains were not light blocking and the exterior lighting from the hotel facade was fairly bright going to sleep. They were in the process of renovating a significant number of rooms on my floor and perhaps this will be addressed. Several garden style rooms had open doors as I walked around, and the ones I saw looked to be furnished about the same as my room in the tower. The advantage of the garden rooms is that the gardens are truly spectacular, meandering between the buildings, set with fountains and gazebos and lots of little nooks to rest and read a book. Most of the room blocks in the gardens area have very deep porch style roofs extending well away from the front of the building so you could never describe any of the rooms a sunny, but if you are visiting in the depths of summer that is probably a good thing. It pays to ask a lot of questions about the room you are getting when you make a booking. ‘Without a view’ probably means you have a blank wall a few feet from your window. Some of the garden units face parking areas, while others have a large garden with gazebos and large swatches of lawn. Pool side accommodations may mean minimum privacy as people walk by, or it could bring you a private patio with mature plantings surrounding and great privacy. Ask a lot of questions. The on-site food is good, with Trellises being favored over the Irish pub in my book. There are also several good restaurants in the Fashion Valley Mall, a two minute walk from the back of the property. Parking and internet are separate charges, although they do offer a bundle package that gets you both for $14.95 per night. Also, it is worth checking discount hotel sites if you are planning to stay here. I met several people who had booked rooms through a discounter and were paying up to $50.00 below the convention rate I was booked at. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Friendly hotel, great location” Checking into this Mid-Town on the Eastside your initial impression is that the staff are very friendly. The restaurant suffers from vibrations from the Lexington Avenue below, and I was told that some the rooms on the lower floors also feel the vibrations. I was on an upper floor and did not have this problem. However the television did not work and there were also problems with the shower so maintenance seems to be an issue. The full Irish breakfast in the morning was excellent. Located on Lex and 56th Street the location is really convenient to subway and cross town buses. Room rates when I was staying there were outrageously high, close to USD550 before taxes, but then most other hotels were similarly priced. I could accept that except for the maintenance issues.

“Great Hotel- Normally out of my price range, but lucked out” This is one great hotel- clean, comfortable and in a good downtown location near the Embarcadero and Chinatown. I wouldn't normally stay in a 4 star hotel but lucked out with Hotwire and scored a room for a Sunday night for a great price. Not much to complain about, but I was surprised that the hotel charged for WiFi connectivity (Business Center computers are free). The staff was helpful and friendly, the room and bed were good-sized and there were no loud noises to wake me up. I checked in early and stayed until noon checkout the following day.

“Right in the heart of everthing.” The rooms here are a little small. Make sure you stop in at the Welcome center before you book your room, they have deals on the room that you can't get elsewhere. To book this room online through several sites it was $140 a night, but at the welcome center it was $99.00 a night. The hotel is right on the trolly line so I didn't need to drive for the three nights we were there.Right across the street from the front of the hotel is the Mud Island Trolly. The rooms are clean, the staff were nice, and there is underground parking. I was hoping for queen beds but they only have double beds in the rooms with two beds. The complimentary breakfast in the morning was very nice with lots to choose from. Be sure to get a room on a high floor, the views are worth seeing. There are two rooftop pools on the upper floors with great views of the Memphis Bridge. We would absolutly stay here again.

“Pretty Good Value for the Price, Great Location” We are a family of 4 with 2 early teenage daughters who stayed here as the first leg of our recent US holiday. We like Hilton hotels, as they usually have Queen-Queen options, so for 3 nights, our daughters could share a bed and we didn't need to book a second room. The hotel is very big and busy, but the location was great and very close to the central shopping area of Union Square. The only problem with the location was that if you turned left when leaving the front door of the hotel, you were in the tenderloin area within a block and this can be quite daunting, with scores of homeless on the streets and unemployed youth that looked pretty rough. Otherwise, we couldn't complain for what we paid, the pool looked nice , but it's outdoors(heated) but still too cold to use even in June (12Degrees C outside temperature). There was always a queue to get to the concierge, as it is a very busy hotel. The fitness club is quite well equipped, even thought it appears to be in a basement converted vballroom, with no windows, with new equipmenrt and quite a bit of it, but was also busy and hard to get on a cardio machine at times. We never tried the dining options and whilst there was entry to the starbucks via the hotel lobby, us Aussies don't really like Starbuscks (which is why the closed all of their Australian stores), so we went elsewhere for breakfast. Free wireless internet in the Lobby is a bit slow, probably becuuse there vwere a lot of people using it and I find it ridiculous that Hilton still gouges gusets for the cost of internet in the rooms. For what we wanted the hotel for and what we paid, we enjoyed it and it was exactkly what we needed.

“Good, not great. Needs improvement on the little things . . .” That basically says my feelings. This is the “bargain” hotel of the convention center area and is close to Downtown, Arena District and Short North. So, you've got plenty of restaurants, bars, etc in easy walking distance. I’ve been coming to Columbus about once a year for 10+ years and have stayed here many times (and at least 3 of the other convention center area hotels). In my experience, they have the lowest room rate of the hotels around the convention center and the saving is greater if you're driving; their parking charge is much lower than most of the other options (especially the valet rates at the nearby hotel options). Check-in was smooth as silk as was check-out. That’s about all the interaction I had with the staff (no other reasons). I’ll just add that I can’t imagine how the other reviewer could spend 20 minutes looking for the parking lot, you can literally see it from the front door. (And, if I remember correctly also the big sign which says “Red Roof Inn Parking,” but maybe the sign was added after his/her stay.) The remodel continues, 1st floor (meeting rooms?) were being worked on while I was there, but with one exception, the work didn’t cause any disruption or bothersome noise. The exception was a water outage for the entire hotel. It didn’t cause me a problem as management had posted warnings in the elevators the day before and scheduled it for the middle of the day. The remodeled rooms are definitely nicer than the old ones (can’t say if all are remodeled yet or not), but remember this is still a Red Roof Inn. Yes, you've got a flat screen TV now (at least I did), but it's not a Hilton, Hyatt, Sheraton, etc. I do find it a little strange that for all the time, money & effort going into the remodel that a lot of little things seem to have been overlooked. Some of these could easily have been addressed as part of the remodel, others would just be a matter of allocating the upgrade dollars into things other then the physical plant. To briefly recap: Pros: Close to convention center and (generally/always?) the lowest price. Least expensive parking in the area. Newly remodel rooms (not sure if everything is done yet). Free breakfast (but more on this later). Free wi-fi (but more on this later). In-room fridge, microwave, iron & coffee maker. Cons: Linens/bedding: Bed was so/so to bad (clearly wasn’t part of upgrade or hadn’t happened yet). Had my wife been with me (who likes a cold room for sleeping), I would have froze to death - the blanket & bedspread were the thinnest I’ve ever seen in anything but a Motel 6 - come on guys, I don’t expect a down comforter, but I shouldn’t be comparing your bedding to Motel 6. Clearly lots of money was spent on the remodel, you couldn’t have gotten *new* (and better) showerheads? Nickel & dime charges (you had a separate charge in my room for the safe which I didn’t use?), maybe this was just a breakout charge, but I don’t think so. The wi-fi is now free, but reception can be spotty. It was fine in the lobby area, but I was on the 7th (top) near the elevator. The reception there was never good and occasionally nonexistent. If being "close" to the the lobby area was a plus, I can't imagine the entire 7th floor has wi-fi reception. Yes, breakfast is free, but it’s really just drinks & packaged muffins, etc (not a problem if you know that’s what you’re getting, but if you're not aware that's what it is . . .) As for the bottom line, would I stay here again? Yes. Would I automatically choose the Red Roof Inn when I want to stay in the convention center area? No, I would see what else is available, compare rates & amenities, etc. before deciding on where to stay. hlo

“Really nice staff” I was there for six nights for a conference at the convention center. What a great location - it's catty-cornered from the convention center...couldn't have asked for a better location. And, it's a quick walk over to 16th Street. There's also a church (a Methodist church) fairly close by - a 10 minute walk - if you're interested in making to a worship service on Sundays. When I checked in, the front desk guy, Ari, got me all checked in, and then when I asked about walking around downtown by myself, he assured me I'd be fine. And, then, the next thing you know, he's printing out a map to a grocery store that I'd decided to walk to (so I could get my own breakfast foods). He really did go out of his way to help me figure out which grocery store to get to - and was very helpful in showing me how to get there. The hotel is very nice...nothing extraordinary about it (except Ari). The room (on the seventh floor) had a nice view of the mountains. But, that was really the only thing really special about the room. There was free wi-fi, which is a must for travelers these days. The restaurant (Pi) was fine, room service was quick (20 minutes), the coffee shop was handy (tasty tea!), and the beds were comfy. All in all, it was a nice place to be when you have to be in a hotel for six days. It was quiet - rarely heard anyone else in the hallways and never heard anyone next door.

“Clean hotel seems overpriced for what it is.” The location provides good access to west side but bring your earplugs, The room was clean and free of problems but the furnishings were tired. The bed was comfortable. The bath was clean but in need of updating. The disposable plastic cups were obviously clean but add to a general tone of cheapness that make this hotel forgettable for $320 / night.

“Great Location” Stayed at the Renaissance from 4/5/09 to 4/709. Due to the high volume of guests at the hotel for the Cherry Blossom festivals, our room was not ready when we arrived at check in at 3 p.m. We were told to provide them with a contact number and they would call us when it became available. We were not too happy but sucked it up and went out sightseeing. Within the hour they called to tell us the room was ready. They also provided us with vouchers for free breakfast for two days. The Hotel is very nice. The room was spacious and clean. Since we were at the end of a hallway and faced the interior of the building, we did not hear any noise. The bathroom was smaller than most, but served its purpose. The location was key. About two blocks from the Hotel was the National Portrait Gallery. If you went straight through you would come out and face the Archives and were at the Mall. Near the Hotel there was also several good eateries. i.e. Matchbox. When I return, I will most likely return to this Hotel.

“Good location, friendly staff, strong wifi!” We stayed in the Holiday Inn for 1 night. Staff were very accomodating by allowing us to check in early and also made an excellent recommendation for a diner to eat in the area - Tik Tok diner! The room was small but very clean and was ideally located for Penn Station, MSG and the Empire State building. The wifi connection was excellent, something which is very rare in NYC! We stayed in 7 hotels on our visit, this was the best and it was included in the room rate! Watch out for this, in most hotels the surcharge can range from $10-15! This is a disgrace considering Starbucks will let you use it for free when purchasing a coffee! So don't underestimate the value of free wifi which the Holiday Inn Express provide! Breakfast was very eadible and also included in the price! Overall it is probably a 3.5 out 5 but will give it a 4/5 because it does what it says on the tin! Not flashy, but clean and comfortable, WITH FREE WIFI!

“Excellent” Hotel is attached to the convention centre in South Boston so perfect if you are attending an event there, if you are a tourist then be warned that it is a good 20-30 min walk into the city centre. The staff were excellent and the rooms very modern and light, the pool tiny but gym looked better and changing rooms immaculate. If you are at the "World Trade Centre" convention centre also in South Boston then it is a good 10 min walk, try the Renaissance instead.

“EXCELLENT VALUE” I priced this hotel on their own website, 12 months before the trip, to get ideas for my holiday budget. This year, when booking, the price had come down a lot. We got the spacious 2-bedded room, with full kitchen for $142 a night. An absolute bargain for New York and such a wonderful hotel. I loved the location. It was clean which is a priority for me. The guest laundry was a bonus for us. The staff were friendly, the doorman even remembered our names! I'd definitely stay here again. It was fantastic. We were happy with the restaurant attached as well. Breakfast was a great start the day. The pancakes and fruit was to die for.

“Great service at the Tramont Plaza” My husband and I and our 2 friends spent a great weekend in Baltimore July 8 - 11. The Tremont Plaza is in a terrific location, only 6 blocks from the Inner Harbor and only 1 block off of Charles Street. The rooms at the Tremont Plaza are huge and very comfortable. The bellman also will drive you to and from some of the local attractions. We definitely used their services after closing the Piano Bar at Phillips on the Inner Harbor! The staff at the Tremont was quick to respond to any request. I would definitely stay there again!

“NEAT AND CLEAN BUT NOT THE ATMOSPHERE WE THOUGHT” We stayed a week in Elan in June. Whilst it was very neat and clean, breakfast was good as was the wine and cheese at night, the atmosphere was a little sterile. Staff were very friendly and helpful, rooms were all that you need. So great value for money but missed the mark for me us atmosphere.

“Top Lage - historisches Gebäude” Auf meiner Reise durch Texas hatte ich das Holiday Inn Express gewählt. Die Lage ist wirklich nicht zu schlagen, man kommt fast überall zu Fuß hin. Es liegt aber ruhig in einer Seitenstraße. Das Gebäude war ganz früher ein Gefängnis, was man auch im Zimmer merkt, denn man schaut durch Gitter, aber das hat mich nicht gestört. Das Zimmer war nicht sehr groß, aber ausreichend für eine Person. Das Frühstück hat mir sehr gut geschmeckt.

“Nice rooms and fairly large bathrooms” Great hotel. There are fridges in the rooms as well. The bathroom is much larger than expected, especially for a downtown hotel. The room is also slightly larger than normal hotel rooms. I would stay here again. Very comfortable and clean. 2 restaurants. Starbucks. Parking is on the spendy side.

“Perfekte Lage, guter Service, grosse Zimmer” Das Hotel liegt sehr gut nur wenige Minuten vom Times Square entfernt. In der direkten Umgebung gibt es zahlreiche Restaurants. Das Hotel selbst ist im gewohnten Hampton Inn Stil gehalten. Modern, sauber, schlicht. Die Zimmer sind fuer New York wirklich fast schon geraeumig. Es gibt genug Platz fuer Koffer und Bewegungsraum. Die Baeder dagegen sind sehr klein. Der Service war super. Zimmerpraeferenzen wurde entsprochen. Auf unsere Nachfrage nach einem Korkenzieher brachte man uns einen aufs Zimmer den wir sogar behalten durften. Wirklich top! Fruehstueck ist inklusive und sehr gut. Lediglich der Fruehstuecksbereich ist viel zu klein fuer die groesse des Hotels und es gibt lange Warteschlangen um einen Tisch zu ergattern. Insgesamt sehr zu empfehlen.

“Fabulous Stay on Level Nine of the Dupont Circle Hotel” We spent the first night of our honeymoon at the Dupont Circle Hotel and it was wonderful. We spent two nights in one of the Level Nine suites. Our corner suite with balcony provided beautiful views of Dupont Circle and the surrounding neighborhood and great amenities that are expected at a luxury boutique hotel, (heated towel rack, fully-stocked refrigerator and bar, fresh fruit throughout our stay and assorted cheese platter upon arrival), all complimentary. The Level Nine executive floor offers privacy and the staff is attentive to the guests. We enjoyed our conversation and tour of The Heights with the building engineer and the hotel was very accommodating in allowing us to use The Heights balcony as a backdrop for our wedding photos. Special thanks to the entire staff, but especially Cole Kelly and John Paul Wood for ensuring a stress-free stay on our wedding day and providing extra touches upon our return after a day of wedding activities. The hotel décor is very nice and the Level Nine lobby and its amenities were great. The Dupont is centrally located and offers several things to do within walking distance. Valet parking is offered with 24/7 in-out privileges. A restaurant and bar are located on-site and room service orders for breakfast and dinner were well-prepared and delivered on time. We will definitely return for another stay on Level Nine.

“Huge, Spotelss Suites” I stayed at the London this week while having some renovations done on my apartment and was very pleasantly surprised by the enormous, spotless suites and immaculate common areas. I am rather picky about cleanliness, and could not find one speck of dust or fingerprint anywhere (including the suede walls of the elevators, which were obviously brushed several times per day). It truly felt as though the room, which was larger than most NY apartments, had just been freshly painted and carpeted especially for my arrival. The overall size, decor and cleanliness really made the hotel feel like a well-appointed home. Nice amenities like an iHome, two televisions, two robes, a huge bathroom, plush towels, lovely toiletries and a comfortable mattress only added to this feeling. The fitness center was also very expansive and beautifully designed - feeling more like a library than a gym. Room service was pretty good, as well. While the service was not personalized, it was certainly very responsive, prompt and efficient. In fact, the only negative I can think of is that there were no porters to help with curbside luggage or open the doors. Otherwise, a great value in a great location, especially for a business traveler or someone looking for a long-term stay.

“Good Hotel That Could be Great” Got into Beantown really late after some major delays on a flight outta Chicago. Man was I glad that I had booked a room at the Hilton and didn't have to drive that night. Pick-up was quick after I called. Waited all of maybe 5 minutes for the shuttle. Check in was fast. No rooms available on the executive level even though I'm a HH Gold. Room was great - looked brand new and the bed awesome after a very long day.
