I really appreciated the new LCD (or was it a plasma) TV. That was nice - just like being at home. That was the good..... What I didn't appreciate was the housekeeping staff knocking quite loudly on all of the doors adjacent to my room and announcing "HOUSEKEEPING" way too loud at 7:30 the next morning (5 hours after going to sleep). They were so loud that they woke me up - and they didn't even knock on my door. The icing on the cake was that one of the housekeepers decided to have a chat with one of the maintenance guys right outside my room. Wide awake and mad. I got up, showered and checked out. So much for sleeping in.... I hope that the lady at checkout did speak with the manager about this. This is an easy problem to solve and once they get it solved, it will be an excellent hotel and not just above average.

“Great Value & Location in Chicago” I continue to choose the Doubletree hotel as I travel to Chicago and have stayed here 3 times in the past year. The rooms are all very nice and the service is great. The location is superior. It is very close to Lake Michigan (2-3 blocks) and Navy Pier (0.5 mi) which is ideal for commuting and exercising/relaxing on the beach. This location is also a short walk to Mag MIle and to restaurants and pubs in the area. Beyond the location, the main reason I continue to stay here is the price -- I have paid around $150 whether booking weeks or a day in advance. The parking is $40/night, but overall can't complain for the value.

“A great stay” I had heard of Club Quarters before, but never stayed at one. Needing two nights in downtown Chicago, I found a room at the Club Quarters for an average of $169/night. Compared to other downtown hotels, this was an attractive room rate, so I booked it. I was pleasantly greeted when I entered the lobby. Check-in was fast and easy. Each time I dealt with the desk staff, they were friendly, helpful and very pleasant. There is a space referred to as the living room off the lobby, which has plenty of space to sit and talk, work or watch TV. It really was like having a living room in the lobby. I was told there were two business areas, although I used neither. Free Wi-fi (yes, free at an upscale hotel) is available throughout the building. I used it in my room and it was a strongsignal with good data speed. My room had a single queen bed, a desk, two bedside tables and a side chair. The bathroom had a shower and not a tub, which was fine with me. The room itself is smaller because it has just one bed, but there is plenty of room to move around or even have a couple of guests. The style is contemporary and has a warm feel, and it felt good to return to the room after a long day. Free, chilled and filtered water is available on each floor with plastic bottles to fill and take on the go. I really appreciated that effort. There's a restaurant attached (Elephant and Castle Pub), although being downtown, there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance, including the Berghoff (an established and very good German restaurant). Likewise, there are pharmacies, convenience stores, and just about anythingelse needed for on-the-road travel needs. I also saw a Post Office and UPS store nearby. Being within the Chicago Loop, it was easy to get to a CTA train in several directions. I really liked the Club Quarters Central Loop, and the room rate, compared to other hotels, was affordable, especially when the free amenities are considered. I reserve a full 5 rating for truly outstanding experiences. This Club Quarters hits the mark on all counts. I would gladly stay here again. (CS)
“A dump!” This place is a dump. It's tired, not clean, and just dreary. You'd be much better off staying at the Sheraton Suites across the way. Surprised it's a Hilton. Bad.

“It's age does not show...” Very well located, friendly staff and a nice room, makes this hotel a good choice for staying. It is also very near the AA Center, and the Opera House. It is also four block away from Houston Street and the Conely Park. And if you are in bussiness, the light train station it's just a block away!. The only thing is that room is not so very quiet, may be the fenesteration need to be improved to match the room quality.

“Très bien situé” Hôtel très correct avec service de qualité! Tellement bien localisé : près des Nations Unies, du Rockefeller Center, de Terminal Central, de la 5e! Génial! Chambres correctes, propres! Le bar du lobby est un lieu agréable avec wifi! Ne déjeunez pas au restaurant adjacent : hors de prix : 18$ pour des oeufs... excessif. Seul bémol encore : l'insonorisation des fenêtres : on a l'impression que la fenêtre est ouverte.

“kleine, dunkle Schuhschachtel” Eigentlich erwartet man bei dem Namen Marriot schon eher gehobene Qualität und auch wenn man weiß das Zimmer in new York nicht so groß sind wie i anderen Städten, aber was das Marriot bietet ist eigentlich eine Zumutung. Das Zimmer das hatte war sehr klein, so dass gearde mal ein King-Size Bed hineinpasste, das faktisch den ganzen Raum aus füllte. Noch schlimmer empfand ich aber den Umstand, dass man faktisch keinerlei Tageslicht hatte. Ich ein Zimmer zum Hof, der vollkommen im Schatten lag, so dass praktisch keinerlei Tageslicht in das Zimmer kam. Das könnte man noch akzeptieren, wenn dann wenigstens der Preis sich dann auf einem ähnlich niedrigen Niveau bewegt - aber davon war keine Spur. Das einzig positive an dem Hotel ist die Lage. Es liegr prktisch dierekt am Grand Cebtral Station, so dass man sowohl per Fuss vieles erreichen kann, aber auch hinsichtlich öffentlicher Verkehrsmittel optimal angebunden ist.

“Pfiffiger Hotelturm am Rande des Zentrums” Wir wollten eine bezahlbare Unterkunft in der Nähe der Innenstadt haben und sind nach einer intensiven Suche auf dieses Hotel gestoßen. Interessant ist schon die Bauweise, bisher hatte ich noch nie in einem runden Hotelturm übernachtet, die Bauweise ist jedoch recht pfiffig, nach Verlassen des Aufzuges sind die Zimmer immer sehr schnell erreichbar. Der Service war gut, das Hotelpersonal sehr freundlich, die Zimmer waren recht gut ausgestattet und sauber, das Mobiliar war zwar nicht mehr ganz neu, aber insgesamt waren Zimmer und Bad recht ansprechend. Einen Superblick auf Denver hat man vom Restaurant im obersten Stock, besonders zu empfehlen ist ein Besuch zum Dinner, das Lichtermeer von Denver wirkt absolut bezaubernd. Das Essen ist sowohl qualitativ als auch preislich in Ordnung, es gibt typisch amerikanische Gerichte, für die man etwa 1 - 2 Dollar mehr bezahlt als in einem normalen Familienrestaurant, man zahlt halt etwas mehr für die Lage. Man sollte sich nicht täuschen, die Innenstadt ist vom Hotel aus nicht zu Fuß zu erreichen. Das Hotel bietet jedoch einen Shuttleservice zur Innenstadt an. Ich kann das Hotel empfehlen und würde hier jederzeit wieder übernachten. Ach ja: Die Parkplätze sind kostenlos!

“strong smell of smoke in non-smoking room, road noise” Quite disappointed by smell of smoke in room. There was much road noise with room facing I-10. Noise was drowned out by ac, but there was no fan only setting or switch to keep it on constantly, so it was either too cold or too noisy. The birds in the trees outside my room made it difficult to sleep past 6am. Very much a motel. On the positive side, the hotel was much less expensive that others in the area and it was close to I-10 and 8.

“Good place to stay” Stayed here on Halloween for one night on business. I had the corner executive room which was extremely large and well appointed with a large palsma TV which swiveled so you could watch it from the desk or the bed. Wired internet access worked fine. Valet parking only but service was prompt. Room was very quiet. They had a Halloween party for guests and served very nice hors doerves which actually constituted my dinner. There were a number of hotel staff present and they went out of their way to make everyone feel welcome. The only negative was the breakfast buffet wasn't up to the usual Marriott standards but was acceptable. Bottom line is I recommend this property.

“Very nice hotel” This hotel is a very nice place to stay and a great value. The rooms are well appointed, and the beds are comfy. The hotel is dog friendly which is also nice if you love pups. The location (on Wilshire) means it isn't ideal for walking but you are close enough to Westwood Village where if you wanted to walk there you could. You would need to drive to Beverly Hills or any surrounding areas. It isn't the highest end hotel in Los Angeles, but if you are looking for a quality hotel that isn't going to explode your checkbook then I would suggest The Palomar.

“Quiet hotel in a scenic neighborhood...” Quiet hotel in a scenic neighborhood. Staff friendly and very helpful. More expensive than other HGI locations but I guess it's due to location. Highly recommend.

“Woeful” stayed for two nights over a weekend - first off, i ordered a car through the concierge to collect me - it never turned up - there was some confusion on the dates - then when i was checking in the counter staff had an open discussion on whether I or another couple checking in would get the next available room (this was 12.30pm) - later in the week someone was checking in at 4pm and there were still no rooms ready - when i got to the room it smelled strongly of paint/chemicals - complained about that and they put some sort of air purifier in which solved that - the shower didn't drain properly either - asked them to fix that but never did - asked them to organise a town car to drop me up to colombia university - said minium 2 hours at $90 per hour min 2 hours - managed to organise one myself for $40 - my key card did not work a few times so had to return to reception to get that fixed - the area the hotel is in itself is very loud on weekends - lots of clubs, bars etc nearby - people are queuing in the lobby to get into the club on the top floor until all hours, so mayhem outside the hotel - and there is a big nightclub literally next door with huge crowds of people trying to get in (no queue, just a crowd outside) - room was fine, small tv - air con was poor - blinds let in too much light in the morning - bed comfy - staff generally snooty - location is fine if you want to be in 'hip' area - but a good 10+ mins to mid town and the better shops - overall extremely poor and won' t be returning

“Great location for Statue of Liberty” This was a perfect hotel for our weekend. We stayed on the 30th floor and had a view of the Statue of Liberty. We were celebrating my daughter's 10th birthday, and I asked upon checking for milk and cookies to be sent to room. The hotel obliged and sent up the goods (an a card) as a gift. The room was very clean and a comfortable size for New York, where hotel room can run small. The coffee maker in the room brewed terrible coffee, so we were glad to have the Starbucks in the lobby. Room service was very prompt with breakfast, which was expensive but tasty. There is quite a bit of construction in the area, but we did not hear any noise while in our room. This is a great location if you are visiting the Statue of Liberty, ground zero, TriBeca, Wall Street or South Street Seaport. It was an easy walk to all of these areas (on a sunny day).

“Perfect downtown hotel” Service was helpful and friendly, room was modern, clean and comfortable, room was quiet - liked the fact that there was not much to the hotel, minimal check in, no restaurant (just an affiliated establishment), liked the lounge on the 2nd floor - just what you need in New York

“Only 1 ice machine!!!” The hotel was really cool because it was in a historic building downtown. I stayed heere on New Year's Eve. It is walking distance to everything downtown. There is no ice machine on any floor. The only ice machine is in the basement. However, each floor does have complimentary bottled water (empty water bottles that you fill up your self). But it was a cool look and feel. I love historic buildings so it was cool over all. It got really crowded around check-out time with all the NYE people that stayed there.

“One of the better Marriott properties, especially for a MR member” I spent five nights at this property recently - Saturday through Wednesday. I was there for a conference that was held on-site. The location is great. Close to the downtown shopping and restaurant area, close to the Football Stadium and Baseball Park and City Conference Center. There is a nice State Park a block away where you will find the zoo, museums and walking paths. They also offer Segway rentals. The property itself is well cared for, a few years old but still in good condition. Front desk staff were courteous and helpful. The 18th floor concierge lounge is one of the best I have found at a Marriott. Staff was very attentive and courteous. Very nice selection of choices at breakfast including scrambled eggs and waffles and excellent fresh cut up fruit. In the evening they had heavy snacks and later desserts. Alcoholic drinks were available at a reasonable cost. The biggest plus was that they are open every day! Many Marriott Lounges are not open on the weekends. The rooms were nicely appointed and clean. Bed was comfortable with a nice pillow type selection. Room to room noise could be heard at times but it was not too bad. Parking is a bit pricey ($30+ a night) but typical of a downtown hotel in a large city. We had a conference there of about 500 people and the on-site facilities were fine for that. The hotel fitness center was a little limited, but that is also typical. I found a local YMCA branch about a 15 minute walk away and used that facility which was new and very nice. (Indy YMCA Bike Hub) I did not use the indoor pool or whirlpool at the hotel but both looked clean. I would stay here again.

“Great location, nice hotel!” really liked this hotel. best thing was the location as its only a block from union square. room was on the small side and the bathroom was really tight. i don't care much for service, but liked that the bellboy recto remembered my name (nice touch!)

“Great stop over” My wife and I spent an overnight layover at the Sheraton Gateway. We found the hotel to be great for what we needed before continuing on to San Francisco the following day. The staff members at the front counter were friendly enough although I didn't agree with having to pay for short term parking. If we needed it overnight then fair enough but we only needed parking for 4hrs before having to return our rental car. The room was big and very spacious. We used the gym on the ground floor. There were various weight machines and cardio machines. The pool was closed due to maintenance. The main restaurant was closed due to it being a Sunday so we ate at the bar. The food was good and reasonably priced. There was also an endless supply of non alcoholic drinks. In regards to the internet we used the internet on the ground floor which was located next to the bar. It was complementary so I'm not sure why the other review writers were charged. There is a complementary shuttle service to the airport which runs approximately every 20minutes. Because the Sheraton is the last pickup its a direct trip to LAX which takes about 5-10minutes. Overall the Sheraton is a great stopover/layover and I highly recommend it. The only negative I have which doesn't involve the Sheraton is the poor service provided by United Airlines. All I can say is their service in general sux!! I don't recommend as a preferred airline.

“It was GREAT!! Excellant location!” We stayed at this hotel during the entire first week of June, 2006. It is in a very good location of Manhattan, close to everything, including the main Subway 6 line. Restaurants galore in the area. Lots to do! The free breakfast every morning was GREAT!! Stay here!!!!

“average hotel” Hotel was fine to stay in , not up to Kimpton standard, the decor is dated and wallpaer in collidors is peeling of, we had a family room in the corner at end of corridor with view of backyard.The toilet was blocked and had a smell in the room, though was rectified and were offered another room but smell cleared after a day, but did come back at later days of stay, a problem.Carpet are old and worn.Free wifi- excellant for travellers to keep in touch with friends and business.Concereige was helpfull but had no idea how to book tickets for greyhound over internet, had to sort it out ourselves!

“Busy hotel” We've stayed at this property several times thru the years. It is always a satifactory hotel. It's always busy, tho. The pool is always full of adults & kids. Pool towels & loungers run short. The front staff was nice, no issues. The elevators are hot & always packed. It's great to have a Starbuck's on site! The room was good sized, but the bathroom was tiny. There is a dressing room table with a mirror outside the bathroom where they have the hairdyer.... but it's got a micowave (with coffee maker & supplies on top) and a small fridge under. Really? There is plenty of room in the room itself for these. The bathroom is too small to get ready in, so you need this space for that...but you can't put anything on the desk, as the microwave is there. Here's a gross thing... like I said the bathroom is tiny, the toilet is 8-10 inches from the bathroom counter. This is where they have the ice bucket, drinking glasses & two bottles of water. If you've ever watched shows about germs....you'll know that when a toilet is flushed, the germs fly into the air & can spread out as much as ten feet! Disgusting. When we arrived in our room, we found an empty bottled water on our bathroom counter & dust in the sink. and the room was musty smelling. The next day, after the room was cleaned up, it did smell fresher. But they didn't replace the used drinking glasses (which I washed thoroghly BTW). The bed is a sleep number type bed & it was as hard as a rock. We played with it, but never got it comfortable. We were in room 911 & it was fairly quiet. We were directly over the restaurant & looked down on the roof & AC units. We could see te pool to the right of our room tho...so that was nice. My hubby & I shared a late night snack of nachos one night at the TGI Friday's on site & they weren't very good & we actually both had stomach issues the next day. :-( The valet dept needs some help. Not that they were short staffed, there was only one young man (white sunglasses) that did the job of what I consider a valet staff member should do. He hustled & made sure you had your car in a hurry & was always pleasant. The first day we arrived, the pith helmeted guy, took our keys, put them in the cabinet & stood there. We had to ask for a reciept, he said "Oh! You want to valet your car?" Then the last day, we called down for our car, went to the looby & checked out. We walked outside & waited for our car, waited for our car... the whole time a valet guy was just standing there. After about 5 minutes, he said do you need a ride? We said no, we're waiting on our car! He said oh! yes! I forgot.... (he was the one we talked to when we called down to get it). They just seem like a bunch of Keystone Cops. This hotel is always crowded & lots of families stay here. It's not a quiet, romantic hotel. It's close to the river (you can access the trails right from the property). You can see the Congress St bridge & the bats if you have a "upgraded" riverview room. Which is a possitive. The traffic around the property is very congested. The price was right. Would I stay here again...... maybe, if I can get the discounted rate that we got.

“Great Location, Another updated Holiday Inn” This is an updated Holiday Inn, located very close to the L'Enfant Metro, Air and Space Museum, and National Gallery. I was a bit worried checking in, based on the reviews, but everyone was very friendly. I am a priority pass member, so breakfast was included and they provided some discounts for dinner. I never had time to take advantage of this, but it was nice that it was included. I had a courtyard facing room, which was very quiet. The lobby is very modern, but has been a bit worn because of the large amount of traffic, I suspect. The room is a standard Holiday Inn updated feel. All amenities were there-- expect the basic Holiday Inn experience. The bed includes a pillow menu and I had no issues with water or room temperature. Internet is free. In-room coffee is provided. An added benefit, besides the location, is that a Starbucks is attached to the hotel. In terms of places to eat, I would recommend going to the museums for lunch or early dinner. The National Gallery has an excellent buffet. Air and Space has standard fast food fare. Weekends are very busy-- but it was reasonable during the weekday. CVS Pharmacy is next door. You do not need a rental car if you are staying here. I thought the hotel was a bit expensive-- if you can get <$200/night, I don't think you'll be disappointed. Any more than this, I would look into alternatives.

“Comfortable...with a wanna be boutique vibe.” I have no complaints about the property. Location was good, staff was friendly, the rooms were clean and comfortable, close by parking lot, free wireless(huge bonus) and provided easy access to a small cafe and convenience store on the main floor. I got in late and left early so I don't know if they offer in room dining. I had a room on the street and it stayed relatively quiet in the busy morning hours. It is an old property, which is definitely not a disadvantage, but some of the upgrade attempts left a very odd ambiance. It felt like it didn't know if it was wanted to be a modern boutique property with a mediocre paint job or just be itself as an economical, service oriented property. Again, none of that perspective took away from the actual stay itself.

“nicely remodeled” This Hampton Inn is still in the process of being refurbished - the rooms on the 3rd and 2nd floor have been finished, we stayed on the 3rd floor. Room was very quiet, clean, had a comfortable bed, nice flat screen tv with a fair number of channels - water pressure was not that great. Lots of restaurants in the area and a nice 14 screen Cinemark theater across the street. Was in town for a seminar and would stay here again if I was in the area.

“Check your bill when you leave” I really liked the hotel and found it a great place to stay in Austin... The king bed in my room was awsome and I thought I had found the perfect place to stay whenever I went to Austin. I am a golf pro and I go there once or twice a year to go to Golfsmith, which this hotel is close too... Problem first I checked in and on the sign it said 34.95 a night or 179.95 a week... The night guy was tired on check in (4am) so he said to talk to the guys the next day and confirm the weekly rate... I did the next day and the manager was not happy with me. He argued with me for 15 minutes and finally agreed to let me have the weekly rate and kept telling me I had to stay 7 days... Hey you think he would want me to stay a day and get my money... Anyway I just left the hotel a week later and when my accountant checked the bill the next month I was billed 278 dollars... Man thats alot of tax. I have tried to contact them several times and they are avoiding it... Nice place for the price and I wish I could go there again. Room was a bit and I mean just a bit small but really nice for 35 a night... If that is what they actually charge.. I should have been suspicious because my first day I saw a lady argue with the manager about her bill for 55 dollars and he said she was placed on the nice VIP 3rd floor and had to pay more... Looks like they try and pull a fast one on people.... BEWARE... MY advice raise the price 5 bucks a night and no tricks you have pretty nice rooms. For 2 dollars more then the motel 6 this place is a winner.

“The best hotel I have ever stayed in.” I average about 20 nights a month in hotels, all over the world, and am very picky and critical. I usually never write my review until after I check-out, so I can capture the entire experience. I am currently at night 3 of a 32 night stay at this hotel and already know that it is the best hotel that I have ever stayed in. The location is perfect for what I am here doing. The service is incredible. Every single employee is friendly, courteous, and helpful; and there are a large number of employees assigned to each task. The desk always seems to have 2 or 3 attendants. Breakfast and Dinner service is provided two or three people as well. Senior management is everywhere, from wandering the hallways to asking how things are in the lobby. The meals are great. At many Homewood Suites the evening Manager's reception is a joke. At this one, both Breakfast and Dinner have been world class, all three days. Delicious and healthy. The internet here is very fast. It gets bogged down at some peak times, but over-all is the fastest I've every had in a hotel. Video conferencing with my daughter was better from the hotel than it was in our house testing it out before the trip. Yes, I'm saying that the hotel internet works better than my Comcast Broadband at home (some of the time). I don't watch TV, but there are two huge flat screen sets in my room. I think that they have premium channels beyond the norm as well. I am 100% happy with everything about this hotel. If I had to find flaws, I would say that the rooms could be a little bigger, as the king sized bed in my suite is kind of crammed in. Also, as a HHonors Platinum Customer staying for 32 days, a free upgrade would have been nice. Between the people that work here, the location they built in, and the speed of the internet, I would say that this should be the model for all future Hilton properties.

“Very pleasant hotel, great location” My whole family stayed at this hotel last weekend for my brother's wedding. The neighborhood is great, the hotel is clean, the staff is really nice, and the beds were really comfortable. The only drawbacks were very minor. --Be careful if you're booking a "suite" - my parents got one so that people could get ready in there if necessary, but it was hardly larger than the regular rooms. --When I checked in, I asked the woman at the desk where I could get some lunch. She told me to walk down the street and there were "lots of things there." Technically true but a recommendation would have been nice. --There is no service elevator, so we were constantly getting crowded into the elevator with cleaning carts - oddly, at all times of day. Overall, though, totally nice. I would recommend it.

“Unbeatable ini all ways” Moved here from Intercontinental (which I hated) - should have booked this in the first place, as I had stayed in Palomar in SF which I loved, and this one was perfect. We arrived prior to check in time, so left our bags. When we got back we discovered that we had been upgraded to Presidential Suite - WOW. Everything was absolutely perfect. The staff , without exception, couldn't have been more helpful and the accommodation was great. Even if we hadn't been upgraded, this hotel is wonderful - quirky and unique. We stayed in lots of hotels on this trip, but this was the highlight.

“Great SF find” We have stayed at the Donatello before, and remembered it as a nice, comfortable hotel with great value. Sure enough - it still is. We had recently stayed at the JW Marriott across the street and wondered why for twice the price. The Donatello is a smaller hotel but with nice ammenities, good service, comfortable rooms (nice to have microwave, refrigerator and dishes). It is clean and comfortable. The beds are too hard. But that is the only negative I can come up with. It is in a great location, within easy walking distance of shopping, cable cars & restaurants. We had a nice little terrace too! Don't spend more - this is still a great place to stay.

“Happy with our three day stay at the Hamilton” Positives: - Bed was very comfy + fresh/new linens - Shower/ great water pressure, nice toilleteries - Location location (close to all museums, metro station, bus lines) - Service - Concierge service: very good suggestions on how to get to places and where to go for shopping, etc. - Restaurant Not so goods/negatives: - internet is $13/24 hrs even for Priority Gold - the executive lounge on the 12th floor is nothing to write home about. Closed most of the time, we couldn't even find bottles of water there. Boils down to : I recommend this hotel. Walking distance to all State free museums

“Excellent Hotel” We stayed at Marriott Waterfront Seattle after our cruise to Alaska. This was a top-notch hotel! The staff and especially the valet staff were very friendly and helpful. This hotel is very close to the docks for the cruise ships. We arrived at the hotel about 9:30 am on a Sunday morning just as other passengers for the next cruises were leaving to go get on their boats. This plays out ever time the cruise ships come in and go out on Sunday. There were many people in the lobby, but the lobby was huge and had plenty of seats for everyone. There were 3 beautiful water containers filled with limes, lemons, and ice water to keep us refreshed and there was a Starbucks right next door. Our rooms were not ready which was completely understandable because people were just then leaving. They told us that they would store our luggage and then deliver to our rooms later on, which they did. We went sight-seeing for the rest of the day. When we arrived back that night, the rooms were ready. Our room was very large and spotless. The beds were comfortable and clean. The next morning we ate breakfast in the concierge room. They had a great variety of items such as scrambled eggs, bacon, pastries, oatmeal, fruit, juices, milk, coffee, and soft drinks. This hotel was outstanding in our eyes. We would stay there again and again!

“Grandeur et décadence” Je ne doute pas que cet hôtel ait eu son heure de gloire mais les gérants actuels ont oublié qu'un hotel s'entretient, ils n'ont par ailleurs aucune notion de propreté et de décoration : porte branlante, partie communes sales, bas des portes affreusement crasseux, en bref assez désagréable. Petit déjeuner copieux mais servi dans une salle en décrépitude (dans un coin, il y a même une nouvelle table faite avec 2 plaches d'aggloméré...). On oublie cet hôtel !

“Beautiful hotel” Stayed here 1 night in August 2012 before a conference. Beautifully renovated hotel in great location, very nice rooms. My experience with the staff was that check-in desk clerk was not overly friendly or helpful. Disappointed to be upcharged for a double room, even as clerk indicated plenty of availability. Very comfortable room and nice bathroom. Would stay here again despite staff niggles.

“Great location, good size room,average service” Stayed one night for the location, staff not over all friendly, no view. Room clean bed softer than I prefer. TV responder slow to remote. Would be great for families with small chlidren.

“Amazing location, excellent hotel” The Renaissance hotel is at the north end of Times Square and has phenomenal views of the square, especially from the R Lounge. The hotel feels very new: it's in good condition and is kept clean. The staff were all helpful. Rooms were fairly large compared to most hotel rooms in NYC and well appointed with attractive and functional details. The bed was very comfortable. Some of the little things I greatly appreciated: -outlets at the bed side (in this age of portable electronics, I want to charge devices at the bedside so they're within reach at night). In fact, there were lots of easily accessible outlets around the room. -separate lamps for each bed with easy-to-reach switches -HD TV with actual HD content. Also the HD content worked well. If it was satellite, I couldn't tell (no pixellation). -Shower/tub with a bit of extra room on the wall side in addition to the curve-out shower bar. It made the shower feel quite roomy. Bathroom overall was not cramped. -Bathroom had a volume control and speakers for the TV. And if you bring a patch cable, you can hook up your MP3 player to the connection panel and listen to it through the TV as well. -Desk area swings out. Like many hotels, the desk surface is pushed under a narrow counter that includes the dresser drawers, TV stand, etc. Those desk surfaces aren't always easy to pull out. This one was. The task chair was also pretty comfortable. The lobby is split with arrival and check-in at the street level and everything else (restaurant, bar, shop, concierge) one level up. If check-in backs up, it might be uncomfortable in the small street-level lobby, but I breezed right in after arriving around 6 PM (often a busy time in my experience). More importantly, if you're meeting someone, be specific about where you'll meet them. It's not an inexpensive place (it *is* a Renaissance on Times Square, don't expect a discount hotel). The R Lounge and breakfast are pricey, but not out of line center-city hotels. In-room broadband (wired or wireless) requires payment, but wi-fi in the lobby is free. I asked for a quiet room and was put on the 6th floor. Usually a low floor isn't a good choice, but I think they put me there because there weren't many people on the floor. In the 12 hours I was in the hotel, I only heard one person go in or out (impressive). The downside is that I heard whatever advertising music was playing down below my window. Luckily it didn't play very late (11 or so). I heard a couple of sirens, but in NYC, that's not bad. I didn't hearhonking or people at the street level. In all, it seemed pretty quiet for a hotel on Times Square. If you want something quieter, try a location away from the square. I'm pretty sensitive to noise and I will definitely consider coming back here. The high point of the hotel is the R Lounge. It's a bar with full glass on three sides that puts you right in the Times Square action a couple of stories up. You get the visual stimulation of the Square, but protected from the elements and with a full service bar and quite tasty food. It would be perfect place to spend New Year's Eve. My server, Karen, was very knowledgeable about the food and wine and had good recommendations. The Renaissance is a nice alternative to the Marriott Marquis which has a lot more hustle and bustle. The only reason I didn't give it a "5" is I could not have gone to sleep earlier with the street-level music that played until 11. It might have been better to be on a high floor, but then perhaps there would have been more hallway noise or noise from neighboring rooms.

“Pleasant & 5 Minute to Airport” Stayed at this hotel only for one night and because of the convenience to the airport. They have a free shuttle that runs every 30 minutes. The airport is less than 10 minutes away. The rooms are clean, the bed comfortable. They make good use of space, near the window they put a cushion in case someone wants to sleep in that area. The hotel staff is very in tune to any noise that may disturb guests. They have complimentary breakfast in the morning. All in all, my stay was less than 24 hours but slept great and would recommend.

“Best in New York” Have been coming to New York for the holidays since the 1990's, and have stayed at the Plaza, Carlyle and Ritz Carlton Central Park. The Four Seasons is doing a promotion this time, so have decided to give it a try. Best decision ever! After experiencing the Four Seasons product, I would be more than happy to pay a 20-30% premium over the Ritz Carlton Central Park to stay here for my next visit. The location is, of course, perfect. What impressed me most is the condition of the rooms, as I was originally a bit concerned with the age of the hotel, hence the condition / cleanliness of the rooms. I am however glad to report that they are not a concern at all, as the rooms are spotless. I find the decor much more comfortable than the newly renovated rooms at the Plaza, or the old-school decor at Ritz and Carlyle. The Four Seasons is modern without being too pretentious like the Mercer, and reminds me very much of home. The service is okay, not enough to take points off the overall experience, and one can't expect much from a New York hotel considering that hospitality has never been the strong suit of the country compared to some other international destinations. But this is, by far, the best hotel in New York in my opinion.
“Great business hotel” Massive hotel, ideal for business conferences. Great rooms in terms of size and decoration and wonderful bathrooms. Beautiful grounds, pools and gym. great overall experience.

“Exceeded my expectation” I picked a wrong day to visit the Valley of the Sun, it was May 22, and they issued excessive heat warning for the area. The temp reading was 108 degree at noon, so there went my plans for outdoor activity that day. I landed in PHX in the morning, although the check in time is 3pm, I called the hotel and let them know I have no where to go in this weather except for sitting in a restaurant or shopping mall. Ken was the person I talked to and he let me checked in at noon. Awesome! The room was clean with your typical Radisson decor, although I am not a fan of sleep number bed, that did not bother me at all. The lobby, restaurant, hallways and rooms were nicely appointed as well. Overall this is 3-star Radisson property in my opinion, it was the service that made it a 4-star hotel!

“Great design hotel” I respectfully disagree with the coffee complainers who have posted recently. If you want that, stay at the chain hotels. This place is for people who appreciate good design. It is residential in feeling, and unbelievably comfortable in that dark-wood, cocoon way. I felt very hip staying here! The front desk staff and bellmen were friendly and helpful. Breakfast in the Fifth Floor restaurant was quite good, if a bit expensive. Can't beat the location, either. For dinner, try Annabelle's a couple of doors down. It is very good.

“Great Boutique Hotel, Perfect Location” We were pleasantly surprised by how nice this small hotel was. It is beautifully renovated with a very nice restaurant. We ate breakfast there and I thought for Chicago prices, not too bad. They don't have complimentary coffee in the lobby and you have to pay for it by the cup in the room. I didn't like that, every hotel I have stayed in, if they have a coffee maker in the room it is free. Other than that great location 1/2 block off of Michigan Ave about 3 blocks south of the Water Tower.

“Reasonable Residence Inn” Stayed at the Residence Inn Airport for business travel in July 08. I had no negative issues with the room, it was clean, comfortable and about what I expected from a Residence Inn. The location was convenient and I had no problems with my stay. There was a little bit of airport noise but nothing that disrupted my sleep. Overall I would recommend this for utility stays, such as business travel.

“Fire the Maid Service” This is an old hotel with beautiful architecture, solid walls and large rooms. The door men were wonderful, helpful and friendly. The front desk help was the same. However, the glow was over when we entered the guest room. The room was musty smelling. The bathroom floor has long black hairs and a beer bottle cap on the back of the toilet. What was that about? The headboard, walls and end tables hadn't been dusted in ages and the carpet felt so gurbby I had to wear shoes the entire time I ws there. Old hotels like this should be a jewel. This could be a jewel if only the cleaning crew had pride in their work and the owners cared more.

“Great customer service” I stayed at the MGM Grand during the PGA Tournament. Still believe this property has among the nicest hotel rooms I've ever stayed in. But this review is about customer service. I left my briefcase behind, contacted lost and found and MGM mailed the briefcase to me at my office. The briefcase, nor the contents were valuable, it just contained a bunch of things I needed. So glad to have it back and so glad Shaundra in lost and found took care of me! Thanks MGM!

“Delightfully surprised” I booked this through an on line discount agency at a very good price so my expectations were not as high if I was looking for a full service hotel or resort. This hotel completely met our needs. We needed a central location to visit schools and it was close to everything. It is not in a cultural part of town - just part of a hotel/restaurant strip - but easy access to everything. If you want to be able to walk to places as San Diego is a great pedestrian city - stay downtown. It is very close to Old Town- but not walking accessible. The rooms were clean, spacious and beds comfy. I did think that charging for parking was annoying. Not really a place for a romantic get away - but perfect for families or travellers who want a good hotel at a good price and something centrally located to Sea World, Downtown, Beaches, and have a car and do not mind driving.

“A mixed bag” Usually we can find great deals in DC but this time rooms were running extraordinarily high. We were going to a concert at the Verizon Center so proximity to this location was key. As members of Marriott rewards, we decided to use our points instead of parting with a fistful of cash at another property. We were really disappointed that the full service Marriott got such poor ratings so we chose the Courtyard since it faired better. The locale was outstanding. Some great restaurants around and very close to The Mall. I liked the fact that the building that now housed this hotel used to be a bank. Nice architectural details could be found throughout. Door and desk service were swift and courteous. I was hopeful at this point until I pressed the elevator button. As the doors opened I was scared to step inside. We thought it was a freight elevator since it was draped in big swatches of dirty fabric. With trepidation we entered and pressed our floor number. Well the mystery of the elevator was quickly solved when we walked down the hall to our room dodging a variety of furniture along the way. Ah yes, it was a remodel. Great. The room was very clean, the bed comfortable, but it was small. New York small. We usually get great deals on spacious rooms in DC so we were a bit taken aback on the size. The window looked out into the interior like a courtyard effect, so no view and not a ton of light. The sink was located outside the bathroom, and the tub/shower and toilet were in a minsicule space. All in all not a big deal, as we were there only for the night. However, if we were paying for this room ($250 ballpark) I would have been crushed. Upon leaving, we called in advance to get our car but we must have decided to leave with every other guest, so we waited at least 20 minutes for our car. Not really their fault that there was a stampede but they should consider additional staffing during standard check out hours when the hotel is full. The most annoying thing was the unprofessional way the staff and management handled the redecorating. Stuff was strewn about without any consideration of the guests. While waiting for our car, a truck jammed with new furniture was being unloaded and unwrapped just steps from where we were standing. The worst part was seeing how poorly the workers handled the brand new furnishings. We literally could hear the scrapes as they tried to move the heavy objects. How about a dolly guys? Would not stay again.

“Nice Little Hilton just steps away from the Inner Harbor” This Hilton Hotel shares the same entrance and reception desk with Homestead Suites. I had a “King Evolution Room” with a king-sized bed on the 9th floor and a great eastern view of a huge garden area on the 8th floor (nice trick, eh?). Apparently the roof of the building below was converted into a nice walking/sitting area with grass and stone walkways, etc. The flat-screen TV in the room was great with the HD channels available for “NADA” (free is always good) and the bathroom was large and modern with a roomy glass-door shower. I’m not a fan of the TempurPedic mattress or similar style. Give me a nice over-stuffed coil-spring mattress. There also was a mini-fridge, a microwave and a coffee maker. The hotel has a bar/grill called the Great American Grill and a business room that has 3 free PCs and printers with internet access and a copier and fax machine. This hotel is east of the inner harbor area (Piers 3,4,5 & 6) on the other side of these little walking bridges connected to the various Piers that allow you to cross over by the tip of the pier without going to the top of the pier (E. Pratt St.) and back down. Pier 5 has a hotel and a McCormick & Schmicks along with a small lighthouse. Pier 4 has a Hard Rock, Dick’s Last Resort, Houllihans and more restaurants. The next bridge will take you to the Baltimore Aquarium and Harborplace. The free “Charm City Circulator” orange-line bus stops at the rotary by the Hilton Hotels and goes right by the Inner harbor area before crossing over the Light-Rail transit line tracks that can take you to and from the BWI Airport for $1.60 each way.

“Great value” Boston hotels are very expensive - you'll pay a lot for very little. Keep this in mind when you read some reviews on here which say that this hotel is over-priced, compared to other cities which demand lower hotel room prices some people may think this hotel is too expensive for what it is but for Boston it is excellent value. Shop around online to get the best deal. Great location - right beside the subway station and there is an Avis car rental right next door. Easy walking distance to various popular locations with lots of eating options in the area. The hotel was easy to find. The hotel staff were all pleasant and helpful. I had been worried that they wouldn't be because of some reviews I read on here. Perhaps some attitudes have changed as a result of comments made or perhaps some guests expect an over the top welcome (which you won't get). No problem what-so-ever with key cards as mentioned in other reviews. Lobby area is very nice looking. Our room was as I hoped it would be clean,safe, and a comfy bed. By American standards the room is on the smaller side but there is still plenty of space to walk around the room - we were 2 with 4 large suitcases and didn't have a problem. Room had everything you would need on a city break: hair dryer, toiletries, 'fridge, coffee maker, TV, phone, wardrobe. There was no in room safe which I do prefer to have in a hotel room but I believe they have safety deposit boxes or the option to put it in the hotel safe at reception. The bed was very comfy and I had a great nights sleep on all nights. Other hotel options in Boston are pricey and I don't believe the difference in price would be worth staying somewhere else, especially for us as when we are in a city we are out and about all day so really just need somewhere comfy and clean to sleep. If we come back to Boston we WILL be staying here again.

“Good location but did not measure up to the Hilton brand standard” I was on this trip for business. There were some good things and some not so great things about it. The good things were the location - close to Boston Common and a short cab ride everywhere else, the friendly/accomodating staff and the Starbucks in the bottom of the hotel. Otherwise, the hotel needs a face lift. In all fairness, they did have signs posted saying they were going to remodel in the future (though they didn't say when). My room was plain which was fine but the bed skirt was filthy. The walls had stains/marks on them and the comforters were old and dirty looking. I had two double beds in my room and chose to sleep in one versus the other because the sheets had stains on them. Also, it was VERY difficult to get a cab at this hotel. I am a Hilton Gold member and have stayed in a lot of Hilton properties. This one did not measure up to the brand name standard I am used to.

“Great Hotel” This hotel is located centrally between Pioneer Square and Pike Place Market and is in the free ride bus zone of Seattle. I arrived by train and the hotel is a 5 block walk from the train station. As the train arrived early morning I was not sure if they would have any rooms available so early yet the recptionist gave me a room upgrade into waterfront view room. The room is big and everything in is just a cut above other hotels I have stayed in. The main feature for me was the bath which filled from the ceiling. The only other feature of the hotel that I used was the business centre for internet access. The only thing to be aware of is that the the hotel is quite a distance from attractions such as the Space Needle, EMP and Duck Tours. If you want to get to them then you will need to get the free bus to the Westlake Centre and then either pay on another bus or get the monorail. The hotel is in the middle of the free ride bus zone so getting around to most places is easy and free. If you want to get to the waterfront then the easiset way is to go one block down and use the bridge across to the ferry terminal, this is quicker than trying to cross the other streets to the waterfront.

“Quite Possibly the Best Hotel in the World for Service” Stayed here for my wife's birthday (one ending in a "0"). Each and every staff person wished her a happy birthday, there was a nice welcome presentation and just impeccable manners and service from the staff at every turn. It's hard to describe how much better the service is at this hotel over others. Each staff member "gets it", whether a bellman, housekeeper or maintenance worker - everyone knew how to properly read the situation and make the right move or say the right thing. Amazing. Some asian hotels have service of this caliber and also some of the high end cruise lines, but few hotels. Location, rooms, food service are all of the highest quality, but service is their strongest suit among perfection in all that they do.

“Peaceful oasis, great service” We didn't get to stay long enough to fully take advantage of the wonderful service at this hotel but we very much enjoyed our brief stay. The work area was spacious and light with sufficient outlets nearby. The bed was amazingly comfortable, and the many occasional chairs provided were also comfortable. Our room was in a back corner with a view of next-door buildings, but that was fine for our purposes and we certainly didn't hear any street noise, or noise from the hallway for that matter, from our room. All interactions with the staff, from front desk to housekeeping to room service to checkout were highly professional, friendly and efficient. We really wished we could have relaxed longer at the hotel and will definitely be back. Might I suggest that the hotel consider installing hooks on the back of the bathroom doors? We did have trouble finding places to hang used towels. But that hardly merits consideration in the overall review.

“Nice Place but Pricey” Stayed here only 2 nights out of a planned 7 nights because of rain. The hotel and grounds are absolutely beautiful, but there is NOTHING do to here if it's raining. You will need a car (which costs $$$) to park on-site or prepare to take a taxi into the city ($20+ one way). Staff was very friendly and helpful (found my daughter's stuffed animal that we had left behind) and the food was good, but not exceptional. Everything on site is very expensive because this is a "captive" location. $10 a day for Internet is always an insult. Both of my children asked if we could come back when the weather was nicer.

“Good Location, Good Hotel” Look, when I rate this as good, I'm rating it as good by the standards of relatively upscale hotels in New York City. I would choose to stay here over most other hotels, but it also has some drawbacks that you should be aware of, and which mean that given the choice of the W or other similar upscale hotel, I would go there. We got a junior suite upgrade, which was appreciated, but felt somewhat off-put when they offered us a nicer suite if we would pay for an upgrade. We had two SPG Ambassador Platinum members in a room, which, should have qualified for best available room, so we kind of felt like they were fudging the SPG rules. In our room, there were a couple of glaring issues which the hotel failed to remedy. First, the bathroom sink barely drained, which the cleaning staff had to be aware of, but which was not fixed. Second, the Air Conditioning was not sufficient to actually cool the room - there was cold air coming out of both units but not in sufficient volume to make any difference, which was annoying, and adversely impacted my quality of sleep. Last, the bathrobe hanging in the bathroom had a big stain on it when we got there. I would really think that the cleaning staff would have noticed this and changed it out, but they never did. We left glasses from the bar in our room one night and the cleaning staff placed them outside our door the next morning, but they sat there for almost 24 hours before being collected even as other room service ware nearby was collected. The robe and glassware led me to conclude that the attention to detail that one might expect from such a hotel was somewhat lacking. One other thing to be aware of, especially for business travelers, is that this hotel has far too few elevators for the number of guests and during busy times the wait for the elevator is long (5+ min), elevator rides stop at every floor, and the elevators become uncomfortably packed full of people. The lobby bar is really nice if a bit short on seating, and the restaurant has great breakfast, but make reservations in advance. The hotel has a private gym in the basement that SPG platinum gets free use of, and this is quite possibly one of the best hotel gyms I've ever used. It is a two story gym with lots of cardio equipment and a lot of machines and free weights with ample floor space. All in all, I'd happily stay there again, but didn't have such a great experience that I will go out of my way to do so, which many Meridien hotels have provided me.

“Overall A Wonderful Stay, Incredible Four Seasons Service, But Rooms Need Updating” My wife and I drove up to Philadelphia for an overnight stay to enjoy the city in late December and decided (after staying at the Ritz-Carlton two years ago) to check out the Four Seasons. After reading many reviews online, Trip Advisor, Frommers, etc. we decided to book and we were both excited about enjoying Philly and the Four Seasons experience. Upon arrival we were warmly greeted by the very nice front door staff who never once let us touch the doors to open them. The level of service here is exactly what you know and expect from a Four Seasons: simply the best. The lobby is very stately and inviting and one thing you'll notice at any Four Seasons is how clean they keep the properties (both common areas and the rooms). The housekeepers are some of the best in the business. As we walked through the lobby and over to the front desk to check in early, we were warmly greeted again and told our room was actually ready (we were checking in well before noon). We proceeded to our room and got settled before heading out to walk around. While the rooms are a nice size, with a comfortable bathroom, they are showing their age. Our room was incredibly clean, but lacking in the "up to date" feeling that you expect from a Four Seasons property. The first thing we noticed was how the walls felt somewhat barren and the décor was showing its age. The bathrooms still have standard bath tub showers that were an original part of the hotel and you could tell the woodwork has been painted over and over again in the room. The furniture had definitely been updated as well as the beds, tv, etc. The safe is not even large enough to put a full size camera in (think wallets and jewelry only), let alone a laptop. I believe the closet locks if you ask the desk for a key. It's just the small things that you notice that start to make you realize this hotel was in need of a room renovation. While cosmetics are not important to everyone, when we stay at a Four Seasons property we expect to have the best service and accommodations that meet its high standards. When we are out in the city all day enjoying the sights and come back to our room, we want to feel like we’re truly on a getaway trip and the standard room here just didn’t meet that expectation. All of this is by no means a deal breaker and I would tell anyone going to Philly to stay at this property. The rooms were nice, just not at the level you would expect and that left us disappointed. It is worth noting that I was told the property should be going under a renovation in the next two years. I walked up to the front desk in the early evening and happened to be greeted by the Assistant Director of Rooms, Ekrem Koroglu. Ekrem and I spoke for a few minutes and I told him what I needed. He could not have been more courteous or pleasant. Yet another example of the exemplary service we love at the Four Seasons! Overall, the hotel is a top pick in Philadelphia if you value impeccable service and housekeeping, a great location, including proximity to everything you need downtown and all the things Four Seasons provides! We look forward to seeing updated rooms in the future!

“Great Staff” I love the hotel. The location is perfect to get around NYC and to see everything on the Upper East Side. The only drawback is the size of the rooms. When you regularly book a suite and it is the size of some closets, it is hard to swallow but I guess that is NYC. The hotel itself was great and the room service was fine. The Internet was fast and speedy. The staff was friendly and helped me book some shows I wanted to see. I had a fantastic week there!

“Perfect For Shows At The Fillmore!!!” My wife and I went to see Bloc Party at the Fillmore, and chose this hotel due to its proximity to the venue. Once we checked in, we fell in love. It has a Modern Hostel feel to it...sort of felt like we were europe...or japan. The hotel is located directly in the middle of Japan Town, and there are tons of great noodle restaurants within a stones throw. Not to mention all the Japanese and Korean markets. All-in-all, this was the perfect hotel for our tastes, and any show at the Fillmore.

“Nice hotel across from the galleria.” Stayed here for a conference / business trip. The best part about the hotel is that it is directly across the street from the Galleria mall, which is huge and has all the shopping that anyone could need. The hotel itself is pretty nice. Not sure the cost cause it was included in the conference, but my guess is that it does not run cheap. The restaurant food in the hotel was pretty good. Staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms were not bad but nothing to write home about.

“Nice, but not quite excellent” I have stayed at this JW Marriott twice, for a total of 4 nights. My experience has been pretty consistent. I like hotels in historic and older settings and this is a recently renovated structure, which is a plus. The lobby is large and opulent. The rooms, too, were well-appointed and had a "luxury feel", including LCD tv's, wide molding, granite countertops etc. The sheets on the bed were of a high thread count and very soft. The staff was friendly and attentive. So why not excellent? Well, a couple of things. First, although I paid close to $300 a night after some sort of preferred rate, I still had to pay $15 for wi-fi. Really? I'd pick an internet connection over a TV or many other things in the hotel. It sure as heck doesn't cost them anything close to $15 for a night. If you are a Marriott platinum or some other high level "elite", the internet doesn't cost extra, but I travel all over and, frankly, while it is generally very good, Marriott isn't always the best alternative so I don't have the high elite levels needed for "free" internet access. Second, I thought the prices in the restaurant and the lobby were rather high. The prices for wine by the glass were more than I would pay for an entire bottle at home. They are certainly entitled to a fair profit, and I support their right to one, but $18 a glass for wine that would cost $12 a bottle retail is going a bit too far. Having said that, I had a chocolate martini at lounge bar, an occasional indulgence for me, that was very good (it was $18.50 with tax and tip). In short, they have a beautiful and thoughtfully restored building and an excellent and responsive staff. I was annoyed, however, by the nickel and dime-ing on things like excess charges for internet access and beverages in the lobby. If you are already Marriott elite of a sufficient level, the internet won't be a problem, but you would likely be staying here anyway. If not, however, I would look at the entire package to determine whether the hotel is worth it. I'd leave it up to you.

“Locals like this one.” We are from Columbus, but sometimes we like to stay downtown after a late night event. We have stayed here a few times and have not been disappointed. The rooms are very modern, nicely decorated, and spacious. Front desk staff are very nice. The building was originally a bank, so when you go down for the buffet, you will enter an old safe to get your food!

“In a class by itself!” There are not enough stars on the rating chart to adequately compare this hotel to the others. It is in a class by itself. The service is like nothing you have ever experienced in a hotel anywhere at any price. All of the employees go above and beyond to do whatever they can to make your stay the best it can be. The hotel room we had was huge and beautifully decorated with wonderful bed linens and plenty of fluffy pillows. The bathroom was huge with a shower and a deep soaking tub. We had a walkin closet for our luggage and clothes. We also had a gorgeous view off the balcony. The hotel property is in an idylic setting with magnificent views in every direction. The inside of the hotel is just as breathtaking with plenty of beautiful marble, tile, wood, carpet and drapes. You feel like you are in a very private and special place. The spa is huge and is also beautifully designed with a lovely color scheme and very large treatment rooms. I had a massage, manicure, pedicure, and foot reflexology and they were all oustanding treatments. I highly recommend the spa. We did not rent a car and the hotel car took me to the mall one afternoon. One evening the driver took us to Del Mar to a restaurant. The Business Office made copies of a report for me and faxed it to my office. My husband bought pants in one of the shops and the woman in the shop hemmed them up for him and they were ready in an hour. We ate most of our meals at the hotel. We really loved the breakfast and lunch choices but the dinner choices did not have enough "comfort food" items on the menu for us. However, everything was excellent. The bottom line is you really owe it to yourself to stay at this hotel. Some reviewers said the hotel was expensive but I thought it was quite reasonable for the service and the luxury that is provided.

“The Lap of Luxury” The Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco is fabulous; the rooms and hotel are beautifully decorated. The service is fantastic: room service is 1/2 an hour during peak times (and the food was hot), the turndown service is complete with a bottle of water and soft jazz, the doormen are extremely pleasant and very helpful. I can't say enough about it. We came back from our week there feeling extremely relaxed and pampered. Also made use of the town car several times, it's a wonderful service. Just take note that the town car is available on a first-come, first-served basis, so be down at the bell desk at least 40 minutes before you plan to arrive to your destination so you're not disappointed. The food is excellent in the Seasons Restaurant, don't miss out on the ice tea and the open-faced crab sandwich, also the Chunky chicken soup! Lunch is a better bet as breakfast is very expensive, and the dinner menu seems limited. For lunch, go about 1 pm for a prime window seat that overlooks Market Street. The hotel is in a prime location, you can walk everywhere. The only downside is that the lobby is on the 5th floor, and the bell desk/entrance is on the ground floor, and trying to find your way around can be very confusing at first. Make sure and spring for a view suite; the suite is just a little bit bigger, and if you're spending that much anyway, what's a little bit more. A bottle of champagne (not sparkling wine, good quality champagne) and a plate of chocolates and strawberries were left for us for our anniversary. Definitely worth the splurge for that special occaision. We are trying to think of a "special occaision" to go back next year. This hotel is a 7 star!

“$7 for Parking on Their Lot” Checking-In PROS: The lady who checked me in was nice. CONS: There's a $7 per day parking fee. This is reasonable compared to $20-28 you would pay at a hotel downtown Philly however, as a guest, it should be free. The hotel sits on a parking lot and it's hard to understand why there's a fee associated with "their" parking lot. Lobby: PROS: Very comfortable and a lot of seating space with large separate dining area. CONS: N/a Room PROS: So quiet...loved it!!! CONS: The doors are colored a disgusting color brown that looks like you know what. The hallway carpet is nice but the room doors, kill it. The shade to the room window does not come down. I struggled with it my entire stay. I was real annoyed with daylight creeping in because the shade would not drop. A room with double beds is small. I felt a bit claustrophobic. Bathroom PROS: Very hot water CONS: The tub was not the cleanest and I truly wanted to take a bath. I took a shower instead. TV PROS: HUGE flat screen TV with a great host of channels. CONS: N/a Bed PROS: PERFECT...The bed and pillows are crazy comfortable...OMG!!! CONS: N/a Housekeeping PROS: N/a CONS: Loud and rude. A tap at the door saying, "housekeeping" would have sufficed instead of a very hard knock, several times, yelling, "housekeeping" and after I answered she said nothing but kept going down the hall, to other doors doing the same thing...annoying! Wi-Fi PROS: It's FREE & FAST CONS: N/a Continental Breakfast PROS: N/a CONS: They don't have one but a bar/room service! Checking-Out PROS: Easy and fast CONS: N/a I guess the main reason for a hotel room would be the bed and its comfort. If you are looking for that, this is your place. I cannot say I would recommend this hotel only because it does not offer free continental breakfast and you pay for parking. If I had to choose between them, I'd take a free breakfast at least for having to pay for parking, on a lot, attached to the hotel anyway. Other than that, it just was nothing to really say or compliment the hotel about.

“Great Rate and Location” Finding a good rate for a weekend hotel in D.C. can be a challenge, especially during the summer tourist season, so anything under $100 can prove dicey...if the rate is good, the location is bad, or vice versa. The GW Inn, however, provides both and while you clearly are not staying a a five star hotel, our room was well appointed, clean and quiet. We've stayed several times here and found it to be a reliable choice.

“modern and brilliant - wonderful interiors” Park Hyatt was brilliant!! It truly is in an elite class of hotels. It stands out as soon as you walk thru the front doors - with its minmalistic design front desk etc. The room itself, like the rest of the hotel, is new, and fresh with ample of room. The bathroom, in dark tiles looks straight from a magazine. The restaurant downstairs is also fantastic serving great breakfast and dinner - Obama came here to celebrate his wedding anniversary too (restaurant that is!). 2 slight negatives - the gym/pool, great facilities but so far, far far away - it's an exercise to get there in the first place - but that I guess wont be a problem for those who are already fitness fanatics. Secondly, its location sits in a quiet location in the north west corner from the White House - its walkable but it's a decent walk. Closest metro station is about 10 mins. Other good things - they have bikes for you to u use to get around DC - which is great cos, Washington is pretty much flat - it's a fantastic way to get around all the monuments etc, cos to walk it all will require a decent effort. Great business centre will free printing with top of the range computers. Overall, a very very pleasant stay!

“Good Airport Location” I got a good park/sleep deal here for the 4th of July weekend. I arrived in the afternoon, parking garage is just across the driveway. Check-in was quick and pleasant. My room was clean and everything was in order. While the decor won't likely be published in Architectural Digest, it was fine. Unless you want to drive the only dining choice is the restaurant in the hotel. I did have dinner there and it was just fair and overpriced which is typical of airport hotel dining rooms. The hotel worked out fine for my needs. The airport shuttle bus runs frequently and it was prompt on my departure and arrival. If the price is right, this is an okay choice.

“Nice Business hotel” Stayed here recently for a business trip. Quick check in. Easy to get cabs in front of the hotel. Nice concerige lounge with a rooftop patio. Rooms are typical NYC hotel size but clean. Elevators are a bit slow, especially in the morning. Turn down service at night is nice. Would definately stay here in the future.

“Still Very Good, But Listen Starwood Management” Stayed here again on business in Boston and would recommend, although with advice to Westin/Starwood management. First, this hotel is well maintained- clean, good rooms, comfortable beds, adequate toiletries, and attentive staff. Great location with access to the T, and walkable to the Back Bay and Boston Commons areas. Good for location and for business travelers. Has a nice pool and high end fitness center with lots of variety of equipment. This time the check in staff gave me the top (36th) floor which is a Starwood member floor, with a slightly nicer room than some others in the hotel, and small perks like 2 robes instead of 1, plus a stunning view of Boston and the Charles river. But, Starwood management, listen to what this hotel drawbacks were: hotel "business center" is composed of a couple of iMac computers located in the lobby that one couldn't print boarding passes from, and one couldn't do any other work on. So why are they even there? Another stupid surprise was that the hotel's public restrooms were access key only, so what's the point of that? Where are guests and conference attendees supposed to go, in the adjacent mall? I would stay at the Westin Copley again, but Starwood get your act together about the hotel computers and public bathrooms.

“Great Location - Very Nice Facility” We stayed at the Garden Inn on June 15th - 18th. We were very pleased with the acommodations. The room was large and very clean. The bathroom was of average size and was also clean. The bed was extremely comfortable. We stayed on the 8th floor so there was no outside noise. We had a problem with the door lock that was fixed on a timely basis by a very nice anc courteous maintence person. We arrived at the hotel at 12:30PM and our room was ready with out having to wait. The staff was very courteous and helpful when we asked directions or recommendations. The location is the biggest thing about this hotel. It is within one block of the subway, walking distance to Broadway and Times Square. We could have paid twice the amount and not have stayed at a better facility.

“Pretty good!” When I stay in the Energy Corridor area of Houston, I usually stay at Omni Westside or Embassy Suites. Travelling with othersed to my stay at Hampton Inn. It ended up being a pretty good stay! Friendly front desk workers, holiday decorations all around the lobby and front entrance, decent-sized rooms, coffeemaker, plasma tv's and SUPER comfortable beds and pillows made the stay great. Only issues were small things like poorly working lamp, tv that had technical issues, etc. Small issues that weren't a huge deal. I got a deal on an internet booking site for the room and feel as if it was more than worth the price. I would stay again if the price was right and needed accomodations at a cheaper price.

“Yikes, don't believe the other reviews” I find it hard to believe the other reviews regarding this hotel. My flight was cancelled and they put me up in the Wyndham. The hotel is within walking distance from the airport. True the lobby is nice but the rooms are in desperate need of an update. The furniture would make the Golden Girls blush.The carpet appears old and filthy. The safe in the room did not work nor do most of the light bulbs. The tv's are very old. Even a paint job would help, the wallpaper is peeling and dirty. I am aIso not a fan of popcorn ceilings. I was fortunate to be "upgraded" to a one bedroom suite. It too is very outdated but the room is very big. I also appreciate central a/c instead of those noisy window units. The staff is very warm and welcoming. This hotel does have a lot of potential but I would avoid until an update is done. I previously stayed down the street at the Holiday Inn, the rooms are somewhat updated but have huge flat screen tvs.

“The Hilton Boston Back Bay is a winner.” Our son had a college audition at nearby Berklee College of Music. This hotel provided a great location, a beautiful spacious room, and excellent customer service. The staff provided my son with a space to practice the night before his audition at no extra cost. Everyone was very friendly and trustworthy. I ended up leaving my checkbook in the room. Housekeeping handled this well and it was mailed to us the day after we checked out with nothing missing! The view from our corner room was gorgeous and the beds were heavenly. My son got a good night's sleep and nailed his audition (full scholarship!!!). If he ends up attending Berklee, we will be regular guests here.

“Pas nul, mais décevant après avoir fait celui de Washington” Nous avons séjourné pendant 3 nuits dans cet hôtel du centre de Manhattan. Nous avions fait un étape dans l'établissement de Washington auparavant. Ce fût ici la déception : accueil assez quelconque, chambres très petites, restaurant médiocre et hors de prix...

“Nice Boutique Hotel” My wife and I spent a night at the Galleria Park in early June when we attended the Impressionist exhibition at the DeYoung Museum. Our room was very pleasant; I'd say that the hotel is one of the finer boutique hotels in which I have stayed near Union Square. The hotel was quite convenient to the Ferry Building where the AMTRAK bus brought us and later met us for our ride to the Emerville train station. The lack of Sunday room service is a disappointment as was the Midi restaurant's brunch. I would suggest other eating establishments for breakfast/brunch.

“Very happy, nearly identical to the Conrad & much cheaper!” We stayed here to attend a wedding at the Conrad down the street, so I spent a fair amount of time both at this Hilton and the "flagship" Conrad, and I have to say, there is no discernable difference in quality, luxury or amenities between the Hilton and Conrad. The Hilton Hotel & Suites is extremely nice with a charming lobby, friendly staff, and even nice perks the Conrad was lacking like fruit infused water in the lobby (although the Hilton didn't have a Picasso exhibit in the lobby like the Conrad did, but I digress). We got upgraded to a Junior Suite which was extremely nice of the staff to do, and our room was massive, probably as big as my condo back home. The bed was super comfy, the room nice and quiet, the blackout curtains are always appreciated, and it was also nice to have a separate living room, mini fridge, etc. Overall a great value, great location, and on-par with Conrad and other luxury hotels in the area. I'd definitely stay here again...

“A pleasant surprise” It was a pleasant surprise to have the intimate accommodations that I had at this hotel. The guest room that welcomed me upon check-in was cozy and inviting. It was a nice place to rest a little before venturing the city, and after any full day of walking and sightseeing, the room was a very comfortable destination for relaxation and sleep. I stayed for two nights in a non-smoking room on the fourth floor. It had a microfridge (microwave atop a refrigerator) that I had to plug to make it work. They were fine when I had to use them. The closet stored an iron and board and had plenty of wire hangers.The private bathroom was spacious and clean with very basic amenities (e.g. shampoo, towels) and a built-in hair dryer. I liked the varying water pressures of the shower head especially the pulsing, massage type after a long day. There was plenty of hot water but took a while before it kicked in. The room decor and furnishings were really nice. I especially liked the sturdy yet comfortable bed. There was a television set but the channel selections were very limited. Still, I was able to watch what I wanted. The windows were functional. The curtains also provided privacy. I enjoyed the cool breeze but had to close them at night when it was cold. The radiator heat was turned on at night, and was off during the day. I think it had central control because I didn't make any adjustments. I brought enough warm clothing to keep me comfortable when I needed to. There was a room telephone but was disconnected which I found odd. I attached the phone cord but couldn't make a call. I detached the cord as I found it and just used my own mobile phone. Check-in window service was on the second floor. I buzzed to be let in for the first time and was subsequently given my room key and front door key after registration. Breakfast was available (coffee, hot water, pastries, packaged instant oatmeal, tea bags) across the service window, set on a table where guests can take them to their room. They were adequate to start the morning. The scheduled breakfast was 7 am - 10 am. When I went downstairs one morning at a little past 7 am, nothing was set. An hour and a half or so later when I checked again, there was a full display case of mini pastries, packaged instant oatmeal, pot of coffee and hot water. The breakfast availability was a nice touch, especially if you're there early enough to get some and not be left with just crumbs! :-) I liked the hotel's quiet location on Sutter, between Leavenworth and Hyde. I arrived from the Oakland Airport to BART-Powell station and had a 15-minute walk to the hotel with my rolled luggage and backpack. Going up the street on Powell was quite hectic due to the throng of holiday/shopping crowd. I turned left on Post and followed he route which I used to take when I lodged at the Halcyon Hotel in November. I just walked up one block to Sutter from Post/Jones. That was the only rather steep ascent that I encountered. The hotel's safe location was ideal for me. It's walkable enough to downtown and other areas (Chinatown) yet also far enough from these major tourist areas to be able to enjoy quiet evenings or moments while in the room or when exploring the hotel's immediate vicinity of cafes and eateries. I found another budget hotel through an internet search but its proximity to the hustle and bustle of Union Square made me guess that the evenings could be quite too noisy and distracting. Overall, Mithila Hotel is now something that I am looking forward to staying whenever I visit San Francisco.
