The rates are excellent for a budget traveler like me, and I anticipate relaxing in its intimate and inviting guest room once again.

“Great hotel, good location, nice rooms” Nicely decorated room, comfortable bed, WIFI, nice bar to enjoy a complimentary glass of wine. This was a really nice hotel. Location is great close to Union Square. We had a lovely dinner at Aziza a maroccan restaurant, Slanted door was also great and went for a bike ride to sausalito which was nice and then took the boat back. Many good restaurants in SF. I would definately consider staying at Rex if i go back to San Francisco and recommend it to all my friends.

“Great Hotel! Great Location!” We stayed at the Omni in January for one night as we had tickets for a broadway play. When you turn onto the street for the hotel, if you blink, you might pass it. We had to go back around. Once there, however, the bell captain and valet came right up to us and took our luggage and car. We arrived a bit early, but had no difficulties getting our room right away. The room itself was spacious with 2 beds and a good-size bathroom. The bathroom was very nicely appointed in marble and had plenty of toiletries and extra towels (something I really cherish in a hotel). The hotel had wireless internet and a good number of TV channels. The hotel is located very close to Times Square in the heart of the Theatre District. The concierge was very (very) friendly and directed us to a wonderful restaurant and a nice place for dessert after the play. I had very specific requests and she fulfilled them exactly. If you join their guest program, they have some little perks like getting free beverages delivered to your room in the morning. The hot chocolate was delicious! All in all a very nice stay. Friendly, courteous staff, great location, clean room and nicely stocked bathroom. The wonderful performance of The Lion King topped off a great weekend!

“Can't believe negative reviews” I was very impressed with the stay I had at the HIE Fisherman's Wharf. It is perfectly located, just two blocks from The Bay, and the staff are some of the friendliest I have come across on my trek around North America. The rooms are huge, comfortable and spotless and the breakfast (free) is the best I have come across so far. I can only surmise that those who had problems had actually booked into the non-HIE hotel across the road from the HIE. They are actually two separate hotels as far as I can tell. The fact there is also a Denny's on site which served excellent food was another bonus. The free internet access, available around the clock near the lobby, just confirmed the quality of the hotel. Even a couple of small problems I had with the faucets in my room were dealt with within seconds. Many thanks to the HIE for a fine four night stay!

“The Drake: Fading Beauty” I have stayed at the Drake 5 times in the past 3 years. Typically using Hilton Points, I'm a platinum member. The rooms have varied tremendously, from tiny boxes to beautiful suites overlooking Lake Michigan. This last stay they put me on 2nd Floor "overlooking Michigan Ave". In reality I could hear the traffic from Michigan Ave all night. If you are a light sleeper forget it. ROOM In serious need of upgrading. Old carpeting, small bathrooms, and tiny TV. Desk work area was very small. LOCATION The location at end of Michigan Ave is nice. Easy walk for good shopping and access to run path along the lake. EXTRAS The executive lounge has gone done in terms of food offerings as well as quality of food. On a Saturday morning only two newspapers for room of about 20 guests. No newspaper delivered to room. The fruit bowls they had by elevators on each floor are a thing of the past. Overall, it's a nice hotel, but definitely has seen better days. If money s not an object, then Park Hyatt or Peninsula are much better choices. Using Hilton points consider the Conrad Hotel

“Oh, what it used to be!” If Westin standards are still in force, someone at Corporate needs to visit River North. Time has worn away at the facility that once was so stellar. All I'm looking for is that expected Heavenly Bed and faucets that don't leak. Instead, the bedding is mismatched, bathrooms need work, lighting is dim and depressing. Staff turns out en force when you let them know there's a problem, but who wants room maintenance during a weekend stay? Also, no rooftop pool or spa here. However, if you can deal with the above, ask for a Chicago River View room, and you get the best view of Chicago architecture that money could buy. It's a several block hike from here to the Lake, but you're very much in the center of the entertainment areas of Chicago - the Loop and Michigan Ave and all of River North. Try to book it as a bargain.

“Solidly Fantastic!” The Benjamin has a great location. Period. It was a wonderful oasis in the City. We had a suite which afforded us the luxury of our own wine & water which was great. The service was excellent. Staff attentive & friendly in all aspects of service. The room was good size for NYC & the place was in great shape with nice amenities. We loved the pillow menu! For once we slept great on our pillows like home! We've stayed several places & this one is not smelly or aging or too quirky, while still having the charm of a boutique hotel & not the bland mass-chain vibe. Even the kids loved the place!

“Roomy space close to Philadelphia City Center” This hotel is a bit hard to find among the airport highway exits. Once you get there the rooms are great and luxurious although the bathrooms are a bit small. Seasonal pool is available. Great breakfast included in the room rate. Large ktichen. 3 TV's in a 2 bedroom suite. Good value.

“Fabulous Lobby, but as you go up, it goes downhill” The hotel is excellently situated for visiting The Art Institute or Millennium Park. It is an "old classic" of a hotel, and the main lobby is a must see, but I would not stay there again. The problem with any hotel dating from long ago (the current one was built in 1923-25) is that, even with extensive remodeling (which was done in 2007-2009) it is hard to create spaces that are comparable to what is expected today (in many cases the walls are load bearing so cannot be changed too much). We had a reasonably sized room (king bed and space for a desk and lounge chair) but the bathroom was very small with little space to spread out toiletries. Also, there was no coffee machine in the room - something I have come to expect in virtually all hotels these days. My major complaint about this stay was the Executive Lounge. It is usually worth while to pay the extra for access - in most hotels it is not much more than the cost of two breakfasts and there are usually some hors d'oeuvres in the evening along with a modest wine at a modest price. (Since we are currently at the diamond level in the Hilton Honors program, we get access for free at the Hiltons but I usually upgrade at other chains such as the Hyatt.) At the Palmer Executive Lounge I ordered a couple of glasses of wine (there was a bartender on duty) and was slightly surprised by the cost - $9/glass which came to $21.44 for two with tax and tip - and was even more surprised by the wine. It was about the worst wine I had tasted in many years. I didn't think it was even as good as Trader Joe's cheapest $2.99 wine that I tried a couple of weeks ago. Unfortunately I didn't get a look at the bottle to see what it was (although I did notice that she had to fish it out of the back of a cupboard). I noticed that a couple of groups in the executive lounge had brought their own wine in - and I can understand iot at the prices they were charging. It then occurred to me that the wine had been sitting around open for some time. I checked the room service menu and saw that they offered three red wines by the glass - the same three varietals as at the bar. The cabernet was a William Hill at $10.50/glass from room service. I presume that what I had had at some time been a William Hill that had been left to turn to vinegar. It was slightly more expensive from room service, but I hope that it was in a lot better condition.

“ottimo per visitare Philadelphia!” Ottimo hotel in posizione eccellente! La nostra camera era molto grande e pulita! Come in tutti gli Holiday Inn express era incluso nel prezzo la colazione sempre molto abbondante e per tutti i gusti. L'hotel poi è proprio in posizione centrale vicino al municipio e a tutte le attrazioni della città, tanto che non è stato neanche necessario prendere la metro! E' in ottima posizione anche per la sera dato che è ricco di bar e pub dove poter passare una tranquilla serata! Inoltre è a disposizione degli ospiti una piscina all'aperto. Noi lo consigliamo assolutamente!!

“Good location average room” Not sure if it's worth 4 * rating. The bedroom and bedding is average. The bathroom is updated but quite small. The location is good, connected to 2 malls and right in front of Boston library. Indifferent customer service.

“Enjoyable stay; awesome view!” Just got back from a two night business/pleasure trip and never having stayed at a Loews before, I was very pleasantly surprised. The lobby is sleek and stylish but hardly much to it. The bar/restaurant is also very stylish and occupied the majority of the first floor. Our room location was fantastic. It was really by happenstance but we had a corner room on the 24th floor that had windows on two walls. We had a fantastic view of City Hall to the west and south Philly to the south. So close to City Hall that I thought William Penn was going to reach over and shake my hand. Hmm...but now that I think about it, I hope he closed his eyes at times! =) Anyway, aside from the great view the room was nicely appointed. Some slight signs of wear but overall very comfortable. Bed was great as were the bath products. I agree that the TV was annoying since the satellite would kick out at times nor could you swivel it. Room service was also a bit annoying. The first day they didn't make the room up until late afternoon and the next day they tried to enter the room twice before 10AM. Our room also had some random snacks left from a previous guest and the clock had not be reset for daylight savings. The location of this hotel is fantastic. Brisk walk to the historic area and a short walk to the Avenue of the Arts, shops, and good restaurants. Also pretty much on top of a subway station. Overall a really enjoyable stay. In full disclosure we had a convention rate that was just below $200...and I thought that to be fair. From what I can tell their regular rates can far exceed that. And, should that be the case, I may look elsewhere. But, if you can get a good rate, and lock down one of the rooms with a killer view, two thumbs up for the Loews.

“Small rooms, very nice service, good location.” Tiny room for $404 (with tax). Service was impeccable, except in the restaurant where the waiter kept explaining to me that fish and chips was actually fish and french fries (which I knew, but just smiled and nodded my head). Room looked new and clean. A little poor on the lighting situation. Good location.

“Large rooms and friendly staff” I must have just arrived in a cranky mood the last time I stayed here, because this time everything was great. My room was so spacious and hip, I felt like i was in a one-bedroom bachelorette pad. Everyone was very helpful, friendly, and professional - from the bell staff to the front desk to the restaurant. I spent hours at the huge Galleria mall directly across the street. And my room was quiet -- i slept like a log. Meanwhile, it's about half the price you would pay for all of this elsewhere. So i'm now a fan.

“Luxurious? No. Location? Great. P” If you're looking for a grand club quarters experience, you'll find the understaffed Club Quarters Boston isn't going to make you stay amazing. The location, however, compared to suburbian hotels for just fifty dollars less a night in many cases, will make your stay here worth it! You are literally two blocks away from the Freedom Trail, down in the financial district on a safe Central business district road. Checking in took us some time. We got there on a Friday night. One elavator wasn't working. The card machine for rooms wasn't working well either. The two gentlemen working the front desk were very courtious and apologetic. They were doing the best anyone could do checking in hoards of guests, dealing with grumpy businessmen who could stand having to wait a minute or two for the one working elevator, manning the phones, conceirge requests, etc. They did this all in a very professional manner. The room was small and economical. You get two towels, one wash cloth, one hand towel, two pillows, a comfy bed, small TV, mini fridge, shower (no bath,) coffee machine and that's it. You'll not get anything extra here. So if you're OK with that (my fiance and I were) you'll be fine. If you''re higher maintenence, you'll hate this place. The only reason I rate the Club Quarters with an average score, rather than above average considering their location, was because of our check out experience. A wedding party was staying at the hotel that weekend as well. When we checked out one woman who was cold as ice was "helping" (or not helping) the Mother-of-the-Bride with reservations that had been messed up in their system. For 5-10 minutes this woman went from not being able to help the mother to fixing it once she figured out how. She had a chip on her shoulder, made everyone else in the lobby wait without any awknowledgement, including the Fedex service who had a package for the bride. In front of the mother of the bride, she tried to look the bride's name up in the system and asked the mother (still waiting for the one elevator) if she knew this guest. Yes, it was the bride. After spending that long helping the wedding party, how can she not know? Wouldn't any hotel have the wedding party's name at the front desk? If you're looking for a place to host an event, DO NOT do it here! This woman clearly did not care about service, karma, kindness, people, anything....cold as ice. So that's the impression I left with.
“Excellent location, very clean, great bargain” I got this room on Priceline. it was excellent. Top notch service, very clean, and a location that can't be beat.

“Pleasant surprise.” What a great little hotel and excellent location. We had a suite on the 16th. floor and it was quite spacious and comfortable. The bed was heavenly as were the fluffy pillows. I didn't want to get out of bed every morning! Nice flat screen TV's and workable windows that you can open, which made it nice at night. I'd give it a 5 but there were a few flaws. The front desk staff were a bit stuffy and stiff. Only one robe in our room and no pens or writing paper that we could find. The carpet had burn spots just inside the front door and the bath toiletries were on the tiny size. The soap kept falling through the holder. Overall a nice place. We will stay there again in the future.

“Great Location, Clean Rooms, Good Value!” Stayed here March 5-8 and was pleasantly surprised. The room had 2 double beds, was clean and comfortable. Also, there was no road noise like other hotels I've stayed at in the Fisherman's Wharf area. You can still hear the doors opening and closing from neighboring rooms, but that's normal. The location is right around the corner from Fisherman's Wharf. There is a Burger King one block down if you get hungry and want some fast food. There is also a Safeway and Walgreens two blocks down from the hotel. The breakfast was the same most days - extra extra crispy bacon, sausage, eggs, cereal, muffins, bagels w/ cream cheese, bananas, warm cinnamon rolls, yogurt, milk, coffee, etc. The hotel only offers valet parking at $41/day + tax. So take this into account when reserving your room. Overall, a very nice stay at the Holiday Inn Express and I would definitely stay here again in the future!

“Gut geführtes Sofitel in Washington DC” Das Sofitel Washington DC liegt in direkter Umgebung zum weissen Haus, fußläufig in 3-5 min zu erreichen. Der Empfang ist nett und sehr professionel, man muss sagen das gesamte Personal im Hotel scheint Spass an der Arbeit zu haben. Die Hotelsuite ist schön groß mit einem separaten Wohnzimmer, Schlafzimmer und angrenzenden großen Bad. Die Zimmer sind sauber und modern eingerichtet wie man es von Sofitel gewöhnt ist. In der Umgebung des Hotels befindet sich eine U-bahn Station sowie diverse Geschäfte, direkt gegenüber ein tolles Geschäft für Kaffee Sandwiches Bagels Crossaints etc. Gerne wieder wenn ich in Washington bin

“Blown Away” I had never heard of this hotel, had stayed at the Sheraton DFW and a couple of the Westins in Dallas but went to SPG website and saw this one and while it was 16K points per night, 4x's the rate of the Sheraton Airport the website looked so beautiful I decided to give it a go for a couple of nights when I had to be in Dallas. I was absolutely blown away!! When I first walked in, I thought it was going to be another W which have not impressed me. But, no, this hotel had warmth, the staff were outstanding and the hotel while having a trendy vibe actually seemed to have the service mentality of some of the better Asian hotels I have been at in the past. The rooftop pool and bar lounge area is stunning and the restaurant onsite was incredible unlike so many hotel restaurants, really worth a visit on its own. The friend I was there with was extremely impressed with the wine room. I have a new favorite hotel in Dallas and now am looking forward to my next trip to Texas!

“Getting a bit tired . . .” We had a lovely stay here a few years ago. Re-visiting this weekend was a bit disappointing. The room was nice - roomy, sofa to relax in, wet bar with coffee maker, small bath with walk-in shower, good closet/dressing space, comfortable bed, reasonably quiet. But everything is just a little frayed around the edges, I'd say. The sink in the wet bar only worked for hot water - no cold. The common areas are worn, carpet dirty, etc. People are friendly. In-house restaurant expensive. ($11 for a small bowl of granola? seriously?) No valet to take our car at 10 p.m. on Sunday when we returned from dinner. There were just a lot of little things that seemed to have suffered since our last stay. We could have stayed at the Pan Pacific for the same price. Although it's slightly less convenient, it's miles better in atmosphere and amenities.

“Excellent hotel and location” I stayed here with a group and saw many different rooms. The corner room that I stayed in was huge and it had two double beds. Those are the way to go. The king room I saw was tiny. The corner room was huge compared with the others. This hotel is really nice and the decor is awesome. The lobby is scented and it smells really great. All of the staff I encountered were very helpful and the location is ideal if you need to be near the convention center as I did. It is also walking distance to a ton of great restaurants. There is free wifi in the lobby which includes the restaurant/bar. I would definitely stay here again. Tip: a cab to the airport was a flat rate at $28.50 + extras. But the trains go right to the hotel too.

“Weekend Beer & BBQ” We went with another couple for the weekend, looking for close proximity to Beale Street. Several other hotels were booked, so we ended at the Doubletree. for the most part we were satisfied, we felt fairly good price, great location. Rooms were a little small and dated, but the staff for the most part was friendly.

“The BEST D.C. Hotel...” We stayed at the Westin on our D.C. vacation. The hotel is very clean and well decorated. The staff were beyond courteous (I would run in the morning, and the bell man was nice enough to have a towel AND ice cold bottled water waiting for me). The hotel is nicely situated about a half a mile from the Metro subway, and a 1-2 miles from Lincolm Memorial. The Westin is in a safe neighborhood (we were walking at 1a in the morning with kids with no worries). The next time I am in D.C., I will definitely be staying at this hotel.

“Confortevole e ben posizionato” Ho soggiornato con la mia famiglia di 5 persone nel mese di luglio per due giorni. La sistemazione è assolutamente confortevole. In sintesi un miniappartamento con un bel soggiorno ed angolo cottura, un divano letto matrimoniale, scrivania, poltrona, tavolo con 4 sedie e televisore 42 pollici. L'altra stanza con un letto enorme, comodissimo per due persone con un bambino. Molto curato l'arredamento e la pulizia dei locali. Tutto perfettamente efficiente. La posizione è ottima poichè il quartiere di Georgetown è assai caratteristico e ricco di negozi e locali caratteristici per mangiare. Il centro è vicino e raggiungibile agevolmente anche con i mezzi pubblici. Gran bella esperienza. Colazione compresa nel prezzo assai varia e di ottima qualità.

“Hard Rock, It's Hard to Say Exactly” While there is nothing wrong with this hotel, the location/service/cleanliness/comfort are all very good, the hotel lacks what you'd find at other fine hotels in the same area. The rooms are spacious but the decor is dark and bland, and the lighting in the rooms is dim (to say the least). The carpet in the hallways is old and stained. Furniture appears old. This is not the same as the Hard Rock Hotel at Universal Studios, so for that I was disappointed. But the price was great and the service was great too. I suppose the bar/club is good too but I didn't visit it. I stayed in the Tower at the very top of the hotel. That was interesting because the tower itself is rather narrow. There are only 3 actual hotel rooms on each floor. It was a little creepy. But the view was fantastic. Would I return? It's hard to say!

“Great location” I agree with what many of the other posters have said. Great location, comfy beds, and close to many hot spots in the Gas Lamp district. The only disappointment came from my 9yr old who was sad that the pool was only 3 1/2 feet deep and didn't quite meet his standards. I would definitely stay here again especially if attending a Padre's game. Tip: Try eating breakfast/dinner at the Broken Yolk which is only a 10 min walk.

“New to Marriott so there is still updating but very good” No. 1, you cant beat the downtown location. The service was very good and the rooms were clean and comfortable. They do not yet have a concierge lounge which will be on the top floor when it is finished. That will be spectactular. (breakfast downstairs for Gold & Plat. Members) The Concierge gentleman downstairs is extremely nice and helpfull. Be sure to use him for local knowledge. The hotel sits in a mini-mall that has an ice skating rink (yes, that is correct) and a food court.. It is near the Pearl DART Station and only 4 stops to American Airlines Center.

“A little nightmare” I wish the designer of this hotel would stay in one of the bunk rooms for a week. I did. Going to the bathroom is the main problem (if you're sharing the room), because the door is transparent glass and ours didn't close well—there was a 3 inches gap. With or without the gap, everything you do in there can be seen, heard and smelt by the other person in the room instantly because the room is SO TINY, is like the WC were next to the bed. Believe it or not, the room is narrower than myself with my arms stretched. There's no place for suitcases, they must be on the floor. There's no closet, so you can't unpack. Every morning I sat (or kneeled down) on the carpet and looked inside the suitcase to find new clothes. If you shop anything, there's no place to put it or store it, so the room starts to get flooded with bags and suitcases, and there's no room even to walk! It's exactly like being in jail. Body towels: I thought they were the hand towels, then I realized they were the body towels, they're really really small and thin. There's no place in the bathroom to put anything, only a 2-inch shelf that can't hold anything because it's so small! My toiletry bag was in the room, not in the bathroom, because there was no place to put it! You have to be careful not to hit your head when you wake up, there are sharp metal fixtures by the bed. Bed is OK. I slept well, no noise. Everything seems new but a bit cheap. Lighting & color schemes are nice. WiFi does NOT work. This hotel could be good only if you're traveling on your own and won't do any shopping. Do yourself a favor, pay a bit more and find another hotel. Oh, the terrace is great, you can go there even if you're not a guest. Just take the elevator in the lobby to the last floor and there it is.

“Good hotel for short stay” I stayed 2 nights at this hotel while on business in Houston. It was clean and the hotel staff were friendly. It's a basic hotel with no restaurant on the premises. They have a breakfast buffett but after one morning of that, I had had enough. It just didn't taste fresh. I got sick on my second night there and wasn't able to drive myself to dinner. The front desk staff was very helpful in giving me menus for places that would deliver food. I would definitely stay here again if on business by myself but probably not with my family.

“I adore the Nob Hill!” My family has been staying here for decades. We discovered the Nob Hill in the late eighties and I wouldn't consider staying anywhere else. I lived in the Bay Area for years and visit frequently. The Nob Hill remains an excellent value for the money. The free parking, clean rooms and fridge and microwaves make this a fabulous, comfortable home away from home. Excellent cable TV for those afternoon rest periods and late night jet lag moments. The location is one of the best in the city, close to public transport and in a great, safe neighborhood. Walk to movies, restaurants, shops and Kinkos to check your e-mail. Starbucks is one block away. You could pay twice as much and not have nearly as nice an experience.

“Nice hotel on northside” Stayed a night while visiting family in Austin. I prefer Marriott branded hotels and this was the cheapest in Austin on the night we stayed. Got in late and left early, so didn't experience much of the hotel beyond the room. Check-in was the fastest I've ever had and the front desk was quite pleasant. Room was nice and recently renovated it looked like. Bed wasn't the most comfortable I've experienced; it worked for the night but I've had better nights sleep. Room was pretty quiet - I was expecting much more noise since we were directly off of IH-35. Location was pretty boring with not much directly around at least walking distance. All in all, a nice quiet bed for the night near (but not in) Austin's excitement.

“Adagio is alright” Just returned from a 5 night stay for business at the Adagio. If you are looking for transportation from SFO airport, go through Lorries door to door shuttle service. It was $14 one way for one person and it took less than 30 minutes. The Adagio rooms were nice, but did not have AC. Although the weather is much cooler than most cities it can still get a little warm if you are used to always having the AC on. The rooms do, however, come with high speed fans. Complimentary wired internet is in the rooms and worked very well. The fitness room onsite was decent and open 24hrs. The restaurant, Cortez, in the lobby was not that great. The continental buffet for $14 is not worth it. You are better off walking 1 block to Dotties True Blue Cafe (seriously good food!). There is usually a line in the mornings so get there when it opens at 730am (wed thru mon). You will definitely eat here more than once. If I go back to San Fran I will stay across the street at the Hotel Monaco a Kimpton Hotel. It is much nicer and has a better overall package than the Adagio. Enjoy!

“Nice Location, Nice rooms, would recommend...” I booked this hotel through the website ($189 per night) for a weekend getaway. I had read the reviews and new about the great location. Price: This was one of the best deals that I had found for this weekend. I have seen it as high as $300 per night. I am not sure if I would ever pay that much. Location: Great! We arrived via the BART and got off at Powell St. It was about 2 blocks away and was an easy walk to the hotel. You are 2-3 blocks from Union Square. Lots of restaurants within walking distance. Lots of shopping as well. You are within 1-2 blocks from the Moscone center. Registration: There was no line. However, they got the price wrong. Right before signing, I noticed that they listed the price as $249 per night. I mentioned that I had received a confirmation for the price of $189 (I forgot to print out the confirmation email). They said that I would need to prove it to them. I asked to use their lobby computer and printed out the letter. They finally relented. This was the only problem that I had with the hotel. My friends had a similar issue in that they did not get the promo package that they thought they had signed up for. Hotel/Room: Very nicely decorated throughout. Looks very new. The hotel appears to be set up nicely for business travelors. The room is nice with comfy beds, LCD TV, Coffee maker, and mini bar. The bothroom only had a shower but I didn't mind. The size of the room was adequate. I utilized the pool for one morning. However, it was small and couldn't hold more than 5 people swimming laps. I also loved the free coffee bar set up in the lobby everymorning. All in all, we had a great time at this hotel. We love the location and would probably return.

“pretty good hotel, great location” Hotel is about 20 years old. Needs some freshening up. Didn't feel too fresh, particularly b/c room was smoke filled when we arrived. They didn't have an alternative room,so sprayed freshener and said they would look into a move the next day. We were quite busy,at a meeting, couldn't keep asking about rooms and they did not follow up at all. Concierge was good, not great. There are two other great properties one a very hip boutique hotel a block away and another a much more luxurious newer hotel with a very good chef-driven restaurant. I usually choose Rosewood over both FS and RC chains b/c they tend to be a higher level chain but not this property. This hotel is not up to the standards, particularly of cleanliness and attention to detail of other Rosewood properties I have stayed in. They have a very big gym for a hotel that is well-used by adjacent office bldg. members. Guests and gym members were mostly middle-aged. Location is great, uptown Dallas around the corner from McKinney a street with lots of cafes, bars, etc. Studio suite room was very spacious. Single sink in the bathroom. I might return if price was good, but equally likely to try another property.

“Ask for a harbor view room” I did not get a harbor view room last time and did not know what I was missing. Definitely ask for a harbor view room, which is very relaxing. Bathrooms at this hotel are huge. The rooms are also big and bright. Service is very nice. And if you want some super fresh seafood, ask for directions to the waterfront - about a 10-minute walk out the backdoor of the hotel. The hotel even has a bridge that crosses the road so that you are on the right side of all the seafood stalls selling both cooked and raw items.

“GREAT for the price, book early” The hotel is well located just about 1 mile from the airport. Transport is easy but the vans can fill up during heavy airline traffic times so beware. The rooms are very nice and if you book early the rooms are very reasonable. Comfortable bed and nice layout of the room. They alsso have air purifiers which was a nice touch. Not much close by for food with only one burger place across the street and hotel prices for food a bit steep. For the cheap beer try the liquor store around the corner, it's better than the $6 hotel beer! Service was excellent. They have a pool and workout room. Although it is kinda in the rental car area I would recommend it if you reserve early for less than $200. If ypou like the review mark it! Thanks Berny

“Disappointing stay” I stayed in Chicago doing a doctors' convention and my travel agent booked me at this hotel. The room rate was $500 and the hotel is definitely not worth the money. The room size was nice. However, there was no safe in the room. The TV was over 20 years old and thus was neither a flat screen TV nor was there HDTV. The entire hotel is badly in need of an updating. If the Mariott Corporation wants to charge high rates, they should provide modern comforts. I would recommend the Sofitel, which is a far more modern and better hotel in Chicago.

“Modern hotel and nice stay” This is a modern, green, hotel pretty much in the center of the downtown district. Room was modern and comfortable. We had a great stay. Pluses: Modern good location great pool Negatives: short hours of concierge low shower pressure (this is because it is a green hotel and not a big deal). We had a fine stay!

“Majestic architecture, unsupported by Ritz experience” We stayed to celebrate two birthdays. We traveled from NY & DC. You are greeted with a large, imosing space. The bar area is in the center of the ground floor and the Eric Ripert restaurant is located off to the side. I travel a bit and love Phillie. The history and architecture remain a draw for me. The Ritz is a real cornerstone to the luxury scen there. I didn't feel the same allure to this property. Our room was on the 28th floor and it was small. The furniture was ratty and it didn't feel like a 4 star room at all. The linens and bedding were dated. We went to their mini spa. Nice space and well maintained. I found the staff sort of rough there. The masseuse did his best wasn't at the level that worked for me. We dined on site. Very quiet in the dining area but the 80s music and bae scene spilled over. Inconsistent experiences. The bar was filled with aging gents drinking a lot. Not the acen I would have expected. Check out was fine. Aside from the bellman mispacing the luggage and agruing with us about its location. The front door staff were friendly and attentive. I would give this a miss. Not a super Ritz property. Underwhelming. Do use the gym. It is tucked away but nice equipment

“A very decent business-class hotel” Was in town to watch the Leafs beat the Caps, and stayed at the Ren DC for its location. Overall the hotel is fine. Rooms and public areas are very clean and comfortable. The people we met are courteous (front desk, restaurant, housekeeping). If passing through just for a one-nighter, this would not be a bad choice if the rate is good. There was a conference going on when we stayed. Maybe more than one. Lots of people. But it didn't seem to diminish the level of service. Doorman was apathetic, but well, this is only a Renaissance. But otherwise, everyone else was very nice. We did a self-park, with the entrance just around the corner. It's easy and costs $22 a night (vs $27 + tip for valet). You also get in and out over the 24-hour period. Elevators take you straight to the hotel lobby. Checkin was efficient (despite convention). Our room was ready for us (it was around 4), and the extra towels I requested were in the room. We also got the "away from elevator" request fulfilled. Room was pretty standard-sized. Bathroom smallish but ok. Clean room, though. There's a mini fridge in the room. Coffeemaker. Hispeed internet, both wired and wireless. Standard tube TV, which was a surprise. Standard Lather toiletries. Overall, room was fine. Had breakfast in the restaurant. It was an okay buffet for 17.95. Nothing to complain or to write home about. All in all a decent stay. This would be one of those I'd consider for a quick in and out. Nothing spectacular, but pretty solid.

“There are so many great places to stay in Indy... Stay away from Hyatt” I had the rudest experience the last time I checked in. I left the hotel and stayed elsewhere. Will never stay again. Stay at the JW Marriott they are what service is ALL ABOUT. Very slow wireless internet. Loud construction noise very early in the morning. Elevators Slow and anoying. Hotel very dated and not worth the money. Conciere floor a joke. Well maybe if you think a few pieces of cheese and crackers and gross deserts is a way to reward frequent guests. RUDE staff. Stay AWAY!

“Nel Cuore di Manhattan” Dopo un lungo viaggio di 8 ore per la nostra prima volta a New York abbiamo scelto quest'hotel per la posizione centrale e per i vari commenti lasciati su TripAvisor, che si sono rivelati fedeli. La posizione centrale dell'hotel permette di partire alla scoperta di Manhattan a piedi così come con la subway, di cui c'è una fermata a soli 50 m dall'hotel. L'hotel è inoltre vicinissimo ad una pharmacy dove si può trovare di tutto, dal cibo alle medicine. Inoltre a soli 200 m si trova anche un "utile" Starbucks, se si vuole evitare la colazione dell'hotel. ATM a pochi passi e a soli 5 min dalla 5th street. Al 12° piano durante la giornata si trovano bevande calde a disposizione gratuitamente ed inoltre accessi ad internet con stampanti sempre gratuitamente. La camera: spaziosa, fornita di ferro da stiro e asse, di una piccola cassaforte e soprattutto del wifi, purtroppo non molto veloce, ma utilissimo. Letto confortevole, bagno ampio. L'unico neo è stato il leggero, ma continuo rumore del traffico di Manhattan sebbene fossimo al 21° piano, cosa credo inevitabile nella "città che non dorme mai". Staff a completa disposizione e molto gentile che per il nostro viaggio di nozze ci ha dato una camera di livello superiore.

“Good, Bad, and Indifferent” Oh to be young and decadent. The W LA is a classic example of style over substance. In that regard, it is perfect. The W caters to the hip and beautiful los angelenos with nothing better to do than posture at the poolside. There is enough silicone around that pool to float a battleship. It makes for pleasant "people watching," but try not to stare too much. The hotel itself is OK. Frankly, the decor is getting a little tired if not downright cliche. The room (a "Mega Suite" penthouse) was filthy upon our arrival: the bathroom had lots of detritus from the previous occupants, there was food on the carpet next to the couch, the second bathtub had muddy footprints in it, etc. The service folks are certainly cheerful if not particularly helpful. Their trademark "Anything, Anytime" catchphrase is laughable: the utterly inept valets are either a) too busy checking out the hot women or b) too busy thinking about their screenplay to bother getting your car for you. There are waaaaay better places to stay in LA. Although the location is great, if you need to be on the west side, I would not stay here again- too much money for too little service and too much attitude. For suite accomodations, I would strongly recommend a bungalow at the Fairmont Miramar before I came back to the W.

“treasure island in downtown Detroit” this 4-building property in Detroit's cultural district is a jewel.First the basics - reasonably priced, clean, well-maintained and extremely comfortable. Off-street parking was available, but I took a cab from Detroit Metro. The fare was $36.00 I arrived too early, but was graciously welcomed and offered coffee in the warm parlor where breakfast is served. The inn's shuttle driver delivered me to my afternoon appointment. When I returned, my gorgeous room was ready. It was on the third (top) floor of one of the other buildings and it was stunning. One drawback, because these are converted antique homes, and more B&B than hotel, there are a lot of stairs. One of the other houses did have an elevator tho, so I am assuming that one is accessible. My room was huge, with a couple of special touches, a large leather club chair with ottoman with a reading lamp and a small cd player with a stack of cds. The bathroom was small, but nicely appointed. The pedestal sink with a small shelf above it did not leave room for personal toiletries. In the closet were an ironing board and iron and blowdryer. A wonderful breakfast is served every morning but it is only served in the central house, so you do have to go outside if you are in one of the other buildings. Coffee is served all day long there, too. For dinner, the inn does offer "room service" which you actually order from a nearby restaurant and is delivered to you your room by the inn's staff. The food, from the Union St. Grill was excellent, and arrived promptly and hot! There is also a small business center in the main building with computer & printer available. Oh and the BEST for last, the whole inn has free Wi-Fi access.

“Just as expected: top notch!” Exactly what I expected from Ritz-Carlton: Staff were readily available, always friendly, and very helpful. The room was spacious and comfortable—and it even had a Nespresso coffee maker with a choice of three types of coffee. The Forza health club—easily accessible from the elevator and included in my room rate—was very well equipped. It even included a swimming pool and a basketball court. The hotel is downtown, just a couple blocks from the 16th Street Mall. If you are flying out of the Denver airport, allow plenty of time to get there from downtown. Even without traffic problems, it can take roughly a half-hour to get to the airport exit from I-70, another 10-15 minutes to reach the terminal, and another half-hour or so to get through security.

“Lovely Hotel but not Detail-Oriented” A lovely, charming, traditional hotel with tasteful and welcoming decor. Suites offer a living room and bedroom separated by French doors. My suite had a foyer and a closet-sized room with sink and fridge. The highlight of the decor was the bathroom with magnificent marble and elegant sconces. If the service and facilities had been commensurate with the cultured ambience, I would have been staying at this hotel monthly for business travel for the next two years. The reasons I will not return are as follows: 1) no shampoo present the first night, 2) no local or network channels on the living room tv, 3) sagging mattress, 4) sheets that are 40% polyester, 5) room service Thai noodle dinner filled with grease and served in a tiny covered bowl with no accompaniment save rolls (not very well-balanced!), 6) no ice (requested the first night, but never materialized),and 7) when these issues were reported on a comment card, I was never contacted by any hotel staff.

“Nice hotel, very conveniently located” Visited the Renaissance for 1 night in mid-April with 2 friends. We had a nice 2 queen room, plenty of space for the 3 of us for the night. The hotel is undergoing a lot of renovation, so looks a little construction-y, but should be great when its all done. This hotel is very convenient to everything in the harbor area. We were able to walk to Fells Point, Little Italy, and the Power Plant area. Cabs were also easily obtained in the overhang of the valet area. Our car was valeted & very quickly brought back to us when we turned in our ticket. Overall, it was a nice stay!

“Because I Had To” Ok...this was a no choice hotel made by my company, one I would not wish on anyone...I will start by saying about the only thing this property has going for it is the location. Hard to beat. But it ends there. I guess in fairness the need to charge $42.00 night parking is charged is about what others charge but really...a little much. The lobby is not what would be expected. Looks and feels dirty. Checkin was fine but the king room I had reserved was for whatever reason not available. So, a queen it was. Small, damp feeling and as with the remainder of the hotel a smell that just was not pleasing. Yes the place is said to have been remodeled. But even with a cleaning this place falls short. Dirty carpets and the beds will cause anyone to lose sleep they are so soft and unsupportive. Internet goes in and out so you may not be happy here either. The woman at Starbuck's downstairs said that the normal Internet service they provide was not allowed by the hotel. Only one in DC she went on to say. And at $12.95 per device per day another bad for a service that only costs pennies. So...make your choice wisely and find another property with more to offer in a cleaner setting.

“What you'd expect.....” From a Homewood Suite......It's easy to access (right off the 10) and getting to the frontage roads to find some place to eat was also easy.....It's nothing special, but meets the expectations of a Homewood Suites.....

“Great hotel & location, only minor complaints” The location couldn't be better, if you want a nice, comfortable & quiet room right in the hustle & bustle of Times Square. The room and amenities are fantastic and I would recommend, however, i did have a couple of issues which disappointed me. Firstly, on our first night, one of the bed sheets had a couple of small spots of blood on it. My dad just put up with it and the sheets were changed (without being requested) the following day, my other complaint was the fact that we left our bags with the Porter for 7 hours and returned twice during that time to note that our bags had been left in the very busy passageway, rather than being stored in the baggage store room - not ideal considering the valuables that we had left and the fact that upon returning to collect our bags we waited almost 10 minutes for the porter to appear. Everything was fine, but it was a little worrying that they were left out in a busy reception area like that with no one on duty constantly to look after them. Don't let this put you off though, as the hotel is otherwise, brilliant!

“Nice suites but expensive” Stayed here in February of 2007-08. Got a suite. Big minus: Bathroom was very chilly and unappealing, with only a standup shower. Other minuses: The free breakfast included in room price was not a full buffet, but a relatively light affair with some breads, juice, and coffee. Pay extra if you want more substantial bf. Internet in room was not free. Pluses: The suite itself was very nice, with ample sitting area and separate bedroom. Having stayed in suites at several NYC hotels (incl the Lucerne, On the Ave, and Excelsior), I can say that the Wales suites are comparatively the best of the bunch. Location is in upper east side, on Madison near Mount Sinai School of Medicine. Some interesting boutiques nearby and convenience stores (incl a Duane Reade). Just a short bus ride to the Met Museum and midtown, so hotel was well situated. Quiet nights, good sleeping. Price however, was quite steep (>$350/night). Would recommend other properties closer to midtown if location and pricing are major constraints.

“Great City View Over Christmas Weekend” We stayed here Christmas Eve through Monday checkout. Courteous doormen/valet. Hotel is directly on the water - the Delaware River. The $30 self parking option involves 3 different elevators to arrive at your car, it's a long walk. Valet service is $38. The lobby is impressive in appearance. There are 4 elevators. The hallways are classy looking. The large room was superbly decorated in dark tones with a king size bed with grey leather padded head board, large night stands, an immense armoire, a large 32" LCD screen, a fridge- no minibar, a desk & modern work chair and a large brown leather chair with ottoman. The bed was comfortable with quality linens. The bathroom had a grey/white marble counter top, shower-tub, vanity mirror & Aveda toiletries. Great towels and strong shower pressure. I never saw the pool. I never ate at the restaurant nor the coffee shop. The city view from the sixteenth floor made you breathless. The snow storm we witnessed that weekend was very interesting to see from that viewpoint. The hotel is right on I-95 with easy access to New Jersey & Center City Philadelphia. Minutes south of the hotel by car you'll see a Target, a Walmart, United Artist movie theater and many other national chain stores. Fast food outlets and WAWA are not far away. I would definitely stay here again.

“We are spoiled now!” We got a good deal on a suite at the Sofitel and decided to splurge, and were not disappointed! The hotel location is fantastic -- so nice to walk just 2 blocks and be at Water Tower Place -- and the property itself is great. Our suite was modern and bright and impeccably clean, with great views of the city. Beautiful, fresh orchids in living room and bathroom, and turn down service with a personalized note and chocolates. Roomy bathroom, bedroom, and living room. The safe that's big enough to accomodate a laptop was great -- most are too small. We had two kids with us and when we called to get linens for the sofabed, housekeeping staff came and made the bed and quickly took care of requests for extra pillows, etc. The concierge was great with restaurant recommendations, too, and didn't try to push us into the hotel's spot. Would love to return! One note... it's not the hotel's fault, but parking is pricey. There's an attached but independent garage, and it cost us $34 a day. Ouch. Would be great if Sofitel could work out some sort of validation / discount with them.

“amazing stay” Just returned to Dublin after our five night stay at the Library hotel. Having read the reviews here we decided to book our stay with them and we were not disappointed at all. The hotel is on the corner of Madison and 41st. It's location is amazing, being one block from 5th avenue. Given its location, we walked everywhere. On the rare day when we were going further afield, Grand Central Station is 2 blocks away and you can catch many subways from there. Staff were very friendly and accomodating without being pushy or in your face. Our room wasn't ready on arrival as we got there early so they took our bags for us and we were advised that we can go to the second floor if we liked and have breakfast. There is also a room on the second floor which has two computers and a printer, which was so handy as we could print out directions to different sites and check our emails. The breakfast was substantial with lots of cereals, muffins, fruit, juices, eggs, bagels, cream cheese and different pastries. There was tea and coffee available all day and the champagne, wine, cheese, nuts and crackers were amazing. It was great after being out walking all day to return and have a glass of champagne to relax before heading out for the night. We stayed in a petite double room, which I think is the smallest room that they offer but it was fine for the two of us and we would book it again. It was spotless and we got a room on the 8th floor so it was quiet. Nice amenities left in the bathroom and good water pressure in the shower. Hair dryer in the room also was good. We had also emailed them prior to arriving to advise them that we were celebrating a special occasion while we were there and they left a bottle of champagne in our room and a personalised card wishing their congratulations which was a very nice touch. Will definitely stay here again next time.

“Excellent location for enjoying Chicago” We stay here often, and find this location ideal for enjoying the city. The hotel is located on the river, just across the river from the Magnificent Mile, a few blocks from Millennium Park, a few blocks from Navy Pier, and easy walking distance to the Theater district. The staff is helpful and friendly, the concierge is knowledgeable and eager to help you enjoy this amazing city. I use this hotel for business visits, family visits and just fun weekends with friends.

“Good deal at the airport” This place is not the Hilton but for $70 it was a great deal at Houston's Intercontinental Airport. The night I stayed there most other hotels were sold out due to some large event at Reliant Stadium in Houston. The hotel uses a funky smelling cleaning compound which is not inviting, but my room was clean and I had a good night sleep. Upon check in late that night the lady at the front desk was very nice. The next morning when I checked out and asked for a 'zero balance' invoice, a different staff member rolled her eyes at me. The best about this place was the breakfast. Much better than your regular Hampton Inn breakfast. I probably will stay there again when I am on a low budget.

“Central Location, Clean and Good Service” We recently stayed in a suite for a personal weekend. The property was centrally located to restaurants, shopping and entertainment. Our room and the common areas of the hotel were well-kept, clean, and tastefully decorated. The bed was not as comfortable as we have experienced at other Hyatts of similar category. The fitness center and pool was rather large and well-equipped for a Hyatt. The only downside to the fitness center and pool during my stay was that there were a large number of unsupervised children playing on the gym equipment and in the pool area. I think the high number of children was due to the fact that the city's winter lights festival was going on during my stay. From a liability perspective and to ensure that adult guests weren't bothered, I think management could have done a better job of asking unsupervised children to leave the gym and of enforcing the "adults only" pool hours. The service was good--everyone was friendly, responsive and accommodating. They did a good job of recognizing my Diamond status on check-in. The main criticism I have about their Diamond amenities deals with the breakfast. My partner was sick during our stay and so we asked the front desk staff (who conferred with their managers) if we could order our Diamond breakfast to our room. We were told that we couldn't order the breakfast to the room and that our only option would be the offerings in the Regency lounge. The Regency lounge breakfast was basic with no hot offerings. Management should revisit their policies on how they treat their most loyal customers. Allowing Diamond members to have their breakfast delivered to their rooms would go a long way in making their most loyal customers feel more appreciated. Because the service and property met my base expectations for a Hyatt Regency, I gave them an average rating which I think is quite fair given my experience with various Hyatt properties. Overall, it was a nice stay and we would return, but not on a weekend when the hotel will be overrun with children.

“Wow, a PERFECT stay here” After having stayed in the Edgewater and several other Seattle hotels, this hotel beats them all. I wrote a review with some pictures about this hotel a year ago as well. I had a few minor problems with my stay then, but this time not one bit. I stayed here again this weekend and the hotel is still superb. The entire staff was friendly, the hotel was very clean, and they upgraded me to a beautiful room on the 34th floor overlooking the city. Thank you Westin Seattle! I appreciate this hotel upgrading people to higher floors when they are not sold out! That's what I call good service. The rooms at this hotel are decently large with a very nice TV and superb views of the entire city. The hotel's pool was out of commission but they made up for it by offering free access to either the Sheraton's pool or the Warwick. They also were willing to pay the taxi fare to get to the pool! Wow. Nothing to complain about as this trip was 100% perfect thanks to the Westin Seattle staff!

“Didn't Meet Expectations” We were really looking forward to staying at The Palace and the views are wonderful, location great, the lobby is very nice and concierges are very helpful. It was the other staff that didn't meet expectations. We were rarely if ever spoken to -- no "Have a nice day.", "Welcome back, did you have a nice time." -- nothing, ever! We were there 5 days, do they have don't speak to the guests unless spoken to policy? When we checked in other guests were greeted with hello's and have a nice day. Also in our room there were two lights out in the bathroom -- one very obvious -- that didn't get changed until mentioned. And the rooms are a little dated, but I guess they are starting to renovate them. Turn down service -- for the price of the rooms -- maybe a chocolate?

“Conveniently located to Capitol Hill, Didn't meet my needs” This is a good basic hotel convenient to Capitol Hill. I did not have a good experience and had to move hotels to acommodate my needs. It is clean and nicely decorated; however, when I checked in very late one evening a huge convention was being held at the hotel. It was very croweded and I had to wait 15 minutes to check in just before midnight. I asked the front desk if I could order room service and a drink and they told me that the bar would be open. Apparently, that was incorrect and they closed at midnight. after a long flight without dinner I walked across to the Hyatt without luck and then had to go to the Dubliner ( a local pub) just to get something to eat and drink. The bed was comfortable but rooms are small and the next morning there was absolutely no hot water. I had to check out and go to another hotel . I wouldn't say not to stay here but in DC if you are on a tight work schedule, need to perform and have to get work done you may consider a hotel that is more full-service. It just didnt meet my needs.

“Elegance and Style” I have stayed here several times, usually weekends with my spouse. This place is my favorite in Chicago. Well appointed rooms, impeccable service, fantastic location. While its not the newest of the luxury hotels in Chicago (think trump ) it by far is the best in overall service. My room ws higher up, city view - definite plus if you can get it - try the breakfast with french pressed coffee - wonderful. Close to many decent restaurants, Tavern on Rush, Carmines just to name a few - and excellent shopping. Everything very clean and nice ammenities. Bar is friendly and accomodating, but also more on the elegant side - a great spot to start a special night out.

“Simply the best.” We just returned from stay #4 at the Brown Palace and I've come to the realization that this is my favorite hotel...ever. I've tried to figure out what makes it so amazing and realized that it's really the sum of its parts. Quite simply, the hotel is simple, not ostentatious, perfection. It's the small things that make the Brown so special--the bellman who gave us an impromptu history lesson of the Brown, a single fresh flower in the bathroom, a Keurig coffee machine in the rooms, fluffy pillows on the bed, a stretch out and relax cigar bar, cocktails in the atrium...I could go on and on and on. I'm a rabid fan of all things art deco so we've only stayed on floors 8 and 9--the art deco-themed rooms (floors 2-7 are Victorian). How can you not love a hotel room that comes with a silver water pitcher sitting on a silver tray? This plus the fact that the hotel's water comes straight from its own well makes me a happy customer. I'll add that I'm a stickler for hotel cleanliness and have never had any issues with rooms at the Brown. In fact, I've even taken baths in the wonderful, deep tubs (separate from the shower)--usually I'm a showers-only girl at hotels. This trip we introduced our (adult) children to the joys of Churchill's, the Brown's cigar bar. A cigar and a glass of scotch (champagne for the ladies) was the perfect way to end the evening. Years ago, when my daughter was young, we enjoyed afternoon tea in the hotel's atrium--a treat every mother/daughter should experience at least once. Pricewise, this trip we spent $245 on a 2 queen room on floor 9 with AAA. Not bad at all for a holiday week in downtown Denver. We will return to the Brown Palace as often as possible--I love this place!

“Disappointing second stay” I have used this hotel once before for business trips to Chicago and had been very pleased so I gave it another shot. Second time was quite disappointing. Arrival experience was bad: nobody helping with luggage and reception area crowded with people. There was a long line at the desk, with just a couple of people handling check-in and those in no rush to get more staff or get the customers checked in, it seems. Eventually some more staff came to help but I had to wait over 20mins to check in which is simply unacceptable. Furthermore, when I asked for the comment card so I could complain I was told they had run out - how convenient. Having checked in, my room was then a major disappointment. It was very small compared with the room I had occupied on my previous visit - probably about half the size, was at the very end of a long corridor and felt rather dated in appearance. I emailed reception to complain and then went out. When I returned, there was a message offering me another room which I accepted without viewing because it couldn't really have been any worse than the room they gave me. Someone came to help me move my clothes because I had partly unpacked; the new room was almost identical to the first although marginally larger, with a new bed and on a Club floor. I guess at least they made an effort to address my complaint. One of the reasons I chose this hotel was it has a pool. There were virtually no other people in the pool area when I was there, it was really nice. Also, I had one of the best massages I've ever experienced here. I didn't use any of the restaurants, but the Club breakfast was quite good. So, mixed feelings, still in search of the perfect Chicago hotel I guess.

“Great Location For Chase Field Games” Two friends and I stayed here in late Sept. 2008, mainly to be within walking distance of Chase Field, home of the Arizona Diamondbacks. The hotel is just 3 blocks away from the ball park, an easy walk. It saves time and money not having to deal with the hassle of parking. On the way is a nice pub, the Rose and Crown, which features excellent lunches during the day, and a wide variety of drinks at night. The hotel itself, besides being in a handy location, has many things going for it. The airport shuttle was prompt, just 12 minutes to arrive. The breakfast area is large, and besides the usual cold items, also has hot waffles, eggs, and sausage. The rooms have a desk area, a sofa and chair opposite the desk area, a small wet bar, fridge, and counter, comfortable beds, a separate bathroom sink area, and a good shower, complete with a real mat. The staff were all helpful and friendly. All in all, an excellent hotel at a good rate and location. I'd certainly stay here again when in Phoenix.

“Dirty & in poor condition.” I booked this hotel blind from Hotwire. The area wasn't exactly the best, but the hotel looked decent from the road & it was close to several restaurants (most being fast food). This is where the positives end. The lobby had a run-down & trashy feel to it, & the desk staff was marginal. There was a box @ the front desk where they were giving away cell phone chargers that guests had left behind. I thought that was a great idea...even if I were unfortunate enough to leave mine behind (b/c they can't do anything w/them & by the time you pay to have it shipped, you can just get a new one). The hallways had a odor to them & so did my room. The room itself was also in marginal condition & the internet access wasn't working. I was leary of sleeping in the bed. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone, for any reason. *DISCLAIMER* I stayed @ this Days Inn in August 2007, but haven't written a review until now b/c I didn't feel like taking the time. However, I've since found reviews very valuable in my travels & wanted to return the favor to fellow travellers.

“Very nice hotel and exceptional service” The Hilton San Diego Bayfront is an extremely nice hotel with great views of the city and bay. The service is first class with everyone making sure your stay is comfortable and needs are met. Check in was pleasant as was resteraunt and bar service. The hotel is very clean and rooms are adequate. Great location, across from Petco and short walk to the Gaslamp. The only downside is the Port of San Diego on the south side of the hotel but we had a room on the north side so was our view was perfect! Would highly recommend this Hilton property, as always Hilton is out to satisfy thier customers.

“Chic, tiny, centrally located” A friend and I stayed in the Hudson Hotel for two nights while she was in town for business. As a “native,” I had seen the public spaces in this hotel before, and they are gorgeous – from the ivy-draped lobby check-in area to the chic, floor-lit bar area to the fireplace lounge – very inviting on a cold winter night. We could also see the beautiful outdoor space through the lobby windows – though with temperatures in the 20s, it was a feature we didn’t actually see in person. The actual restaurant in the hotel is currently closed for renovation. The staff, though beautiful and chic as the hotel, are warm, service oriented, polite and accommodating. Joe at the front desk helped us with check-in and gave us a room toward the top of the hotel with a lovely Hudson River view. Everyone we encountered, in fact, from the doormen to the bartender, was polite and helpful. Young, thin, fabulous people straight out of central casting wander the lobby and a few were draped over the leather chairs and sofas, asleep, early on a Monday morning. We stopped in the bar for a nightcap on the first night and got immediate sticker shock from the $15 price tag for top shelf drinks – not specialty drinks or anything, just top shelf liquor – and we are both city people who’ve been around the block a few times. They also offer a $28 breakfast buffet in the bar in the mornings (and complimentary coffee to go for hotel guests). It’s a space worth checking out – just be ready for the price. Now to the rooms. Let’s just say this is not a hotel for your ordinary, generously sized middle aged business person who needs to get some work done and relax in the room between meetings – or anyone with claustrophobia. Though they are well thought-out and designed, the rooms are tiny – and that’s generous. In our queen room, there was approximately 12-18” on either side of the bed, and about the same at the foot of the bed – that is it in terms of floor space in the main area. There's a small hallway to the bathroom with a closet and 3 small hooks on the wall, good for coats, etc. The bathroom is so small that anyone over about 5” 9” would bang their knees on the wall when sitting on the toilet. There is a small desk, a small closet and a tall, thin cabinet that houses a safe (not large enough for a laptop), an older model stereo (I saw no iPod dock in the room though others have mentioned them), one drawer and 3 small shelves. It also looks like it once housed a tiny television. In an ingenious design move, the two walls on either side of the bed are mirrored to give a slightly more open feeling. On one wall, however, the mirror has a cutout that is retrofitted with a flat screen TV on an adjustable arm, which obscures part of the mirror and makes It awkward to walk beside the bed on that side. The platform bed is firm and comfortable – both of us slept pretty well. The bathroom has standard amenities-soap, shampoo, conditioner, lotion, all natural products, and three decent sized shelves for toiletries. For two friends sharing a room, the “open” shower was disconcerting – it has a window with a sheer curtain that faces into the room. It provides light and a more open feeling to the bathroom, but not much in the way of privacy. Also, our room had a shower in a tiny bathtub – but if you want a luxurious bath, this is not the place. There’s no coffee maker (you can get coffee downstairs easily, though), refrigerator or other amenities to keep you in the room. There is an iron and a tiny ironing board. In short, this is a hotel for the young, thin and hip, who plan to spend days sightseeing and nights clubbing. The hotel’s location is ideal for both. It is not a hotel for families (kids would go stir crazy in the teeny rooms), or middle aged business people as I outlined above.

“A great value if you don't mind a little walking” Stayed at the Indigo Riverwalk for two nights on a business trip and as it was my first time in San Antonio, I wanted to be near the Riverwalk area. The hotel is an older property that has been converted into an Indigo. Upon arrival, I was a little concerned about the neighborhood and the hotel exterior which, while freshly painted, couldn't hide the fact that this was an older building. However, once inside, the entire interior has been beautifully transformed with the Indigo touch. Bright colors and contemporary furnishings abound and lots of complimentary ammenities. The room was extremely clean and the bathroom was redecorated, but, strangely, they left some of the old plumbing fixtures in place. The staff was friendly and accommodating. Parking is in a lot across the street from the hotel. The rate was dirt cheap compared to other hotels in the area. My only words of caution are that while the hotel is on the river, it is several blocks beyond the last edges of the populated section of the Riverwalk. It is in a bit of an industrial no-man's land. It is an easy two block walk to get down to the riverfront promenade, but you will have a good half-mile walk before you get to any of the riverwalk restaurants or shops. During the daytime - no problem. Coming back late at night after dinner?? Well, it is a beautiful walk but I am a male that lives in Manhattan and feel comfortable in most situations but I was definitely on high alert while walking back to the hotel. I experienced no problems. However, it is a dark and isolated path with few escape routes and there were a few unsavory characters out and about. I would stay here again.

“Trendy, roomy hotel...nice location” While the Palomar is not bang on Michigan Ave, or just off it like the Penninsula, it's only about 4-5 blocks away. The location however is perfect for foodies- 3 Rick Bayless restaurants a block away, scene-y sushi and a mexican place down the street. The lobby is a bit unassuming and small, however the room we had was a decent corner king, with lovely views. Service is fantastic for a 4 star and as always love the Etro toiletries kimpton offers. Overall, an excellent value for money and great for a quick weekend getaway.

“Creepy” Several years ago, there was a rock n roll photo shoot at this hotel, and suddenly everyone thought it was the cool place to be. It had a great low price, and while the rooms were tiny and not very impressive (with a shared bathroom in the hallway) there was something cool about being there....but that hype has faded, and we're seeing it now for what it is-- a cheap hotel with small rooms and a shared bathroom in the hall. There's an old-school style elevator and the hallways are thin thin thin. A few of the rooms in the front look out at the street, with large brownstone-style windows, and you do get a feeling that you're right there, in NY, and part of it, in an exciting way. The wallpaper in the rooms is funky-- either striped or old-fashioned patterned, and the beds are small (some just single beds) and old and with charming but crappy little blankets. Sink in the room. The prices have gone up, but are still relatively low. The lobby is no more than a vestibule, and the vibe of "we have to be careful of who we let come in the front door" is palpable. The rooms near the bathroom are to be avoided-- the hallway area near the bathrooms do reek of urine and you do hear people coming and going all night and doing what people tend to do in bathrooms. Many of the rooms are very dark and dingy and the windows look DIRECTLY into a brick wall and a tiny air shaft. Most of it is threadbare. Still, a lot of people are charmed by all of this.

“stately comfort” Check-in was easy, quick, friendly. Beautiful lobby, classic, continental, warm, sophisticated. My room in the East wing had a nice if unspectacular view out the front of the hotel onto Calvert St. My king bed room was spacious, with a bath that was not huge or slick but quaint and flawlessly functional (and a deep tub). My Select membership got me free bottled water, free (and quite adequate speed) wifi, and a free morning beverage delivered to my room each morning (I chose fresh orange juice). Other pluses: Nice hi-def tv. Bathroom heat lamp The hotel was not crowded (after Christmas). The elevators were sufficient and my room was made up on time. Good selection of cheap eats as well as the Woodley Park Metro stop just around the corner; Adams-Morgan is a few blocks, an easy walk even in the winter. My one complaint: housekeeping rapped on my door at 8:30 my last morning and continued until I got out of the shower and answered. The woman asked me when she could clean my room. I told her I was checking out that day. She asked me when I was checking out, so I told her 11:00. She came back at 9:30, knocked once, and opened the door with her passkey. This is not a huge deal (and I could have put out the Do Not Disturb sign), but it was quite irritating and there really is no good reason for it. It's why I'm not giving a 5 rating.

“感謝祭パレードに最適!” ニューヨークメイシーズ感謝祭パレードに行ってきました。 お天気はあいにくの雨でしたが、しっかりパレードは行われました。 このノボテルの良いところは、パレード沿いに立地しているところ。しかもホテルの宿泊者はホテルのテラスに入場できるパスを前日に貰えます。予約時には全くアナウンス等がなかったのですが、チェックイン時にもらえたのでとてもよかったです。混雑の中、場所取りも必要ないですし、トイレの心配もないのでお薦めです。

“Great Location, Good Service, Huge Room” Literally outside the East Market station (20 mins from airport by train.) 2 blocks from Market. 4 blocks from City Hall and great restaraunts. Service was OK. Not over the top friendly, but professional. Quiet rooms high up. Big Room $33 for parking for 1 night. Ouch. Would have gotten a 5th star if it had been more like $25

“Bathroom too small, temporary concierge center?” The bathroom was so small I couldn't get out of the shower without touching the toilet. Other than that, and that I believe the concierge lounge was in a temporary location which was also too small (no tables, poor design), the stay was as normal as could be. Good views from the top floor but long elevator waits, even though they are broken into banks that service sections of floors. Check in and out was a breeze, bed was comfy, TV worked great, room was clean.

“Nice hotel in an amazing city...” I was fortunate enough to get a great rate from Starwood for this property during my trip to San Diego for an industry conference. I've always enjoyed the W brand, and this hotel certainly did not dissappoint. The property was a short walk to the convention center and Gas Lamp district. Cabs were readily available, and an abundance of cheap parking lots surrounded the hotel. This saved us the $30+ per night in valet fees for our rental car. The lobby is very modern and chic, but the internet was average at best. Worse still, the rooms only offered wired internet. Why do hotels still insist on charging for internet!?!?!?!?!? I know it is a huge revenue stream, but c'mon, it's robbery! Believe it or not, the wi-fi I stole from the rooftop "Beach" bar was better than anything else I had encountered in the property. It was, however, a nice touch for the managers to roll out the Wii system for happy hour in the lobby. We did breakfast in the restaurant a few times and suffered through very slow service. The food was excellent, and our server tried his best, but the wait killed the experience. On our last night, we came back to the hotel and attended a party hosted by some of our colleagues. The W staff was attentive and entertaining, and they did a great job transforming the venue into a very upscale night club. Overall, the W is a great brand that caters to a young, affluent crowd. I book my stays there knowing that I can expect excellent service in a dynamic and chic setting. I look forward to coming back to this property as soon as I can.

“The trains were wonderful!” I stayed at this hotel during a conference, and I truly loved the hotel! I know some people might worry about the train noise, but I really enjoyed hearing the trains go by! In case you're not interested in listening to trains, the hotel provides a "sleep package" that comes with every room, which includes earplugs, an eye mask, a sleep CD, aromatherapy stuff, etc. The service is friendly and helpful, the pool is nice, the fitness center is clean and all the equipment works, and the location is great, especially if you're planning on being near the convention center. Only 2 down-sides: one is that the jets in the hot tub are too strong, and two is that parking is expensive. (Not more than the other hotels in the area charge, but still, quite expensive for the Indianapolis area.)

“Nice pools but lacking in customer service!” We just spent two nights at this Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs. We're Hilton Gold members and were disappointed not to receive any acknowledgement of this at check-in. Infact we didn't really receive any welcome at all. Check-in agent just gave us keys and a map and told us where to go. Disappointed with room on level two near adult pool - on entering it was very dark and smelt funny. Shower pressure was good however and bed comfy. Woke up after first night with Hilton breakfast coupons under the door with letter acknowledging gold status ... would have been appreciated if we hadn't booked room rate with breakfast included!!!! If you want to relax by the pool then this hotel is okay. The adult pool is next to the hotel's mexican restaurant and you can swim up to the bar and order bar food and drinks. We ate burger and fries and chicken tacos at lunch ... burger was fine but the shredded chicken taco was a bit hit and miss! The best pools are at the falls village. There are two large pools and a slide (fun) and a bar area with food available. The loungers at the adult pool are cushioned and really comfortable whereas the loungers at the falls aren't as comfy! Our biggest complaint with this hotel is the attitude of staff. With the exception of housekeeping who always greeted us with a smile and hello no-else seemed to want to be there. Check-in were just awful, bar staff fairly miserable and our waitress at breakfast was disinterested ... we waited a while for her to reappear when we had finished but she was a no show so in the end we just left our breakfast vouchers and a tip on the table and just left. Other than lunch at the pool we didn't eat at the hotel. There are lots of restaurant choices nearby as well as the Outlet Mall at Anthem if you're interested in shopping!!!!

“Loved it with one complaint” Great location, first class furnishings, great staff - but the kitchen can't fry an egg. Brown crunch all over my over easy's in the dining room - cold potato's and sausage as well. Other than a bad breakfast - no complaints.

“A flower in the middle of Dallas” Stayed at the Magnolia for one night. The staff was amazing! Breakfast buffet was decent. Unfortunately, missed the complimentary cocktail hour and evening cookies...... Hotel has all the amenities one would expect. The only negative is the cost of hotel parking, $25 a night, and extremely slow elevators. Besides these two items, my stay was great. Location is close to the 6th Floor Museum.

“Basic Room at a Reasonable Price - Not Bad” We got to the hotel in the evening and found it easily. It is right off the highway. The area is pretty isolated from the rest of the city being that it's very near the airport. The street that it's on is pretty dark and there are no mini-marts within walking distance. I don't think that it was dangerous, just an isolated street. I certainly wouldn't walk around as there's nothing really close to it that I can remember. Reception was very friendly.
