We got to our room - it was in great shape was neat and clean - didn't look rundown. There was a slight musty smell at the writing desk - probably whatever rag they used to clean it. The rest of the room was okay. The safe was not working so we had to hide any of our electronics when we went out for dinner. This hotel is great if you need a place to stay for one night. It's very close to the airport so if you're arriving late and leaving the next day, it works out well. Parking was not free but only cost $8 for the night. The continental breakfast that was available in the morning was more than what I had expected. I was expecting to just see some cold muffins, some bread and stale coffee that's been standing around. Instead, there is a room with tables and chairs in it where you can sit down to eat. There is a waffle station where you make your own waffles using a special machine complete with a measuring cup for batter, breads, bagels (there's a toaster), danishes, muffins, coffee and tea. You need to drive a small distance to get to some fast food places.

“Average” I agree, its ok if you want a full-service hotel but doesn't have anything that makes it really stand-out. Staff friendly, helpful; the bakery francise is nice; if you like Denny's its next door; parking is free and easy in/out (not a garage); good location especially for the university (although, unless you're more ambitous than most, you will be driving there but won't have to fight I-35). Sorry excuse for an exercise room - more like one I'd expect in a Rodeway or something like that. No microwave or refrig in the room.

“What the yuck Westin?” I have stayed at The Westin La Cantera at least once or twice a year and considered it as a 3-4 star property given the food has always been mediocure, overpriced and the service unstable but the pool and golf course are so nice, it drew us back. However, my mind has changed after this latest visit. It was a regular weekend, not a holiday or peek summer timeframe and the place still felt overrun and overbooked with little staff. This can be overlooked as the did have a wedding or two and I assume many of the guests were in for those. The pool and grounds of the property are very nice, and they have also added many more activities onsite to keep families busy. The problem this visit was our room....it was downright GROSS! STRIKE ONE: We supposedly had a hillside view which I guess equated to a driveway for facility trucks and equipment. STRIKE TWO: Our "Westin heavenly bed" had a huge brown stain on it...I don't even want to think about what it was. Picture attached.......just nasty. STRIKE THREE: The showerhead was ridden with a crusty buildup as well as the shower drain. I made my young son shower in his flip flops as if it was a public locker room. YOU'RE OUT: The AC intake panel was coated with thick dust as if it hadn't been cleaned in 6 months. We had a roll-away in our king room four our son and the only place for it was right next to the nasty AC intake panel. I'm sure we inhaled all kinds of funk over our 3 day stay. And to cap it all off, our room was right across from a staff storage room where housekeeping came in and out of to get supplies, so each morning brought continuous slamming of the doors as different housekeeping associates came and went from this room getting supplies and letting the door slam behind them each time. Thanks for an truly unforgetable weekend which was not only costly, but not worth the minimal points I received at all. I will think twice before ever staying here again or reccomending it to anyone.

“Stylish Convenience” We stayed at this property for an extended date night "staycation" to go dining and shopping at the Domain. It's extremely convenient to walk to restaurants, bars and enjoy yourself in an upscale urban area without downtown hassles of parking and taxis. The hotel is clean, modern and hip. We had a decent size room, which was a little larger because it was a handicapped accessible room. Got a good rate through AAA and we enjoyed ourselves.

“Lovely hotel, close to whatever you may want and to T” The people were friendly and gracious. Moroccan bell man was particularly friendly. Rooms a bit small even in deluxe but not a problem. Great toiletries. My only issues (both slight) were no newspapers and a smell of disinfectant by both entry doors. The people made this hotel above average. Just two short blocks to Berkeley stop on the T which made getting anywhere useful as Boston parking rates are awful.

“Nothing Special Here, Average Business Hotel, Good Location” When one enters thru the front doors you get this feeling that this is just an average hotel. There is really not much of an attempt to make it feel any better than a delux Holiday Inn. The staff seemed nice but did not have the polish and confidence of a well trained staff. The room is nothing special. They only had a double when I checked in. It feels like all Crown Plazas and I am not a fan of their decor. Loud window type air conditioner, the bathroom is so small that you have to close the door to sit on the toilet and the windows allow some outside noise in the room. Street construction out front made traffic a nightmare. The cab driver dropped me off across the street to avoid the very slow moving congestion. Rooms were clean and updated. Decent sized desk, flat screen etc. Perhaps I am a snob. Frankly I believe if the lobby staff and it's appearance we a little more upscale and aside from the small bathroom, this place would have been ok. Good location

“What a beautiful place!” I stayed here for business last week and it is gorgous! My room on the 34th floor was amazing with an incredible bathroom! great view of the navy pier! we had dinner at the plam- highly over rated and $$$$$ as well as drinks and fondue in the lobby bar (also $$$) pricy pool/fitness center and parking- but you are blocks from michigan avenue and the best pizza ever! the staff is super friendly and let me check in at 10 am when my flight from ohare arrived. we ahd a conferance the last 2 days of the week in the ballroom and it was lovely! Stay here!!

“Not what I expected” I stayed here for a night on a business trip. After finding out we were staying in Beverly Hills and I have stayed at several Crown Plaza's before I was excited. Maybe because I was expecting more I was a little let down. Check-in took forever and after a long trip all we wanted was our rooms. When we got to the room it was ok. It served its purpose but some of the decorations could have been updated. The bed was very comfortable and I had a nice view of downtown LA. However, the bathroom was very small and could have used some improvements. We enjoyed the breakfast in the clubroom but after spending 15 minutes to try and print our boarding passes from the computer they offered someone finally came over to tell us the printer wasn't working. With something like that it is important to at least put a sign indicating this or remove the printer paper. The elevators were also run down looking but got us up and down just fine. I would have to say out of all the Crowne Plaza's I have stayed in this was my least favorite. If you are just looking for a place to sleep then I would recommend it but if you are looking for a vacation or a luxury stay then consider other options.

“decent place to stay on business - close to airport” I stayed at this hotel on business because the two Embassy Suites in town were full. This is a well-run hotel, which is reasonably priced ($80 for my room). The location is near to the airport, easy to find and visible off the highway. There’s plenty of free parking, as well as a free shuttle bus to the airport, which I didn’t use. Check-in was problem-free with two people behind the counter. The room was fairly plain as I expected for this hotel chain. The room was clean including the bathroom. No mold was visible which is quite a trick in humid Houston. The AC was a fairly noisy window unit. It cooled very well, and I turned it off or down low at night. The room and hotel were quiet even though the occupancy was quite high. In the lobby, I noticed several flight crews who were staying here. The king size bed in my room was comfortable and I got a good night’s sleep. The bathroom had zero problems – facilities worked well and plenty of hot water was available. The continental breakfast was acceptable for this class of hotel – no hot items but fruit, cereals, drinks, and breads were available. Fruit was also available in the lobby at all times. For an evening meal, there was one OK restaurant nearby, but nothing much else as we roamed the area in our rental car. The hotel had a pool that I didn’t use as well as an exercise room that I didn’t use. Checkout was speedy and problem-free. Overall, this was a good hotel experience and I’d stay here again on a business trip.

“Preiswertes Hotel in Chinatown” Am Eingang zu Chinatown gelegen, etwa fünf Minuten von der Bahnstation der Red Line. Innenstadt daher gut und mit dem Pass der öffentlichen Verkehrsbetriebe preiswert erreichbar. Wir haben dort eine Woche verbracht. Das Hotel ist einfach, recht sauber, die Rezeption bemüht, Englisch-Kenntnisse reichen zur Verständigung durchaus aus. Restaurants und kleine Geschäfte sind in Chinatown reichlich vorhanden. Mitgebrachte Speisen können im Fernsehraum, wo sich auch der Internetzugang befindet, in der Mikrowelle zubereitet werden. Sehr gut gefallen hat uns während unserer Städtetour ein geführter Rundgang mit den Chicago Greeters, die Touren für einzelen Stadtteile anbieten. Insgesamt hat uns diese Woche in der Windy City sehr positiv überrascht, die Stadt kann es mit New York durchaus aufnehmen. Das Chinatown Hotel war uns ein guter Stützpunkt.

“Great staycation spot” We nabbed a $62 special on Priceline for an overnight getaway with our two young boys and this is where they sent us. For that price, it was a fantastic value. The room was very nice, and the bathroom big and roomy (although the tub stopper didn't quite work). We also used the indoor pool and hot tub, and found them very nice as well. Great location in the heart of downtown Indy and walkable to tons of restaurants and attractions. All in all, a great stay.

“cozy hotel in a good location” I think this hotel is a decent choice in NYC depending on your expectations. I book a special rate program through the spg.com website. 50% off the second night but you had to pay a slightly higher rate the first night. Still a good deal. As a spg member I was hoping I might get an upgrade of some sort, but even my request for an upper floor seemed to go unrecognized. I also thought that the fact that I had prepaid my stay might get me a little better service in that regard. But I ended up with a room on the 10th floor. So I could barely see over the building at the back of the hotel. If you are on a floor lower than 10 and on the back of the building you will have zero view. But that is all quibbling. The room itself was compact but efficient. Flat screen hi-def TV seems to be a requirement of most hotels these days. There is free wifi that worked fine. And an electronic safe in the little wardrobe. The bathroom is nice with a small sink/vanity. The shower is large and done in nice black granite tiles. The a/c is noisy and if you run the fan on auto it will kick on, cool the room artically for a couple of minutes and then shut off for a while. Running the fan continuously makes the noise less jarring and seems to keep things at a more constant temperature. I found the bed fine, but the pillows really lacking in support. I did not eat at the hotel. Prices are very high for food as most hotels do. There are tons of places to eat a short walk from the hotel. Two subway stations are nearby. The #1 7th Ave line is less than a block away. The C,E Spring Street station is a few blocks away. So easy access to midtown and beyond. Taxis are not familiar with the hotel. I had to direct my cabbie and he still went right past it. There is a small grocery/deli on 6th Ave, so a short walk away for picking up a couple of things. Film Forum is nearby. The staff were very friendly. All things considered I think this is a decent choice in the Manhattan. In the last couple of years I have been to NYC three times and this was certainly the best of those hotels I stayed in.

“Classic boutique” RECOMMENDED. Tony boutique hotel just behind John Hancock building, prime location. Booked via Hotwire. Checkin uneventful. 12th floor room, quiet, but very small, #xx06, this is not a room to get stuck in with 2 people for an afternoon. Room sizes due vary, assume I got small one because of the Hotwire. Very nice amentities, Bedding extremely comfortable and nice decor. Bathroom hi-tech, well illuminated, but quite small again, Classic boutique and a good overall experience. Didnt eat in hotel, numerous nearby choices for all hours.

“A night in DC” This is a very nice hotel, well maintained and cared for and clean, very friendly staff, and easy check-in. I enjoy it most for its location, and the amenities that four points offer. Skip the hotel restaurant, your in a great location for many other choices, the service is well below standards here, and until i see consistent good reviews on it i will not even stop in for a drink. also elevators are very slow. this hotel is in walking distance to many DC attractions, and cabs are in-expensive in DC compared to most cities.

“Hilton Baltimore” This hotel is honestly very nice. And it has huge assets. 1) if you are going to a game, Camden Yards is right there. By right there - I mean steps away. I've never seen a hotel so close. When I called, they said 2/10 of a mile. I must have misheard. It's literally - right there. We left our room on the 5th floor and were at our seats in 6 minutes. 2) The light rail is right there - next to the hotel's 2nd building. We took the train to the airport - 31 minutes - $6.40 for 4 of us - $30 less than a cab and most importantly, fun fo the kids. The lobby and rooms are very nice - but why the "poor" rating. Well, check in is at 4P - which is late for a hotel. Well I got there at 4:50P, only to be told my room wasn't ready. I was told - they had King rooms but not the two doubles I reserved. Ummmm - check in is 4P. I paid for a room at 4P. I was sent away - my phone # taken - and told I would be called when the room was ready. At 5:32P, I got that call. So what did I do for 42 minutes? I wasn't offered a drink or meal or anything. When I got down there - I expressed my unhappiness. Eventually, I was asked - can I buy you breakfast. Yes, I pushed knowing I'd get something - but it's wrong that my room wasn't ready. Honestly, they should have comped it - because Hilton (at least Hampton) guarantees 100% satisfaction - and they know I can't be satisfied without being in my room. 2nd note - they have a drawer with the hair dryer in it. In that drawer - a pair of women's underwear (think pink was the brand:) Seriously, house keeping doesn't check to see that the hair dryer is there - they'd have seen this. When I told the front desk 20 minutes before we were leaving and I said - just so you know for when you clean tonight - but don't send someone up now - what did they do. Send someone up. My sick wife had to answer the door. So the hotel has some great points - location, location, location - and it's nice. But they are horribly run and don't listen very well. There's a Hampton next door, and Marriott and Holiday Inn across the street. I'd probably try one of them next time. There's clearly ineptitude here.

“Great Times Sq. Location, Value Priced, Comfortable and Clean” I booked here for a last minute business trip through bookit.com. Base rate was $135/night plus taxes and fees for a total of $165/night. For a last minute trip and a Times Square location, that's a good deal if the hotel is decent, and it was. The room was small and efficient as expected for this price. It was a bit dark which made it seem smaller. The bed and pillows were comfortable. The steam heat was pumping out and needed to be turned down, but it's better than freezing! The closet was small, but there was plenty of bureau space. 32" lcd tv worked well, the iHome iPod clock player was a bonus, individual led reading lamps on the head board was a nice touch and the work desk had power in easy reach. There was no view from the rooms unless you were right in the front or right in the rear. The benefit was that it was quiet until the bells on the church next door started to ring at 7:45am. WiFi access was free and there was complimentary breakfast each morning. I didn't partake in the breakfast due to schedule, but I checked it out and they had a good spread of fruits, yogurt, muffins, waffles, etc (continental plus) that would satisfy most people's quick breakfast requirements. If you aren't going to spend a lot of time in your room lounging, then this would be a great hotel to consider.

“Great Family Fun - Will Return” My wife and two kids (1 and 4 years olds) took a road trip to Arizona to see the Grand Canyon and Sedona. Our trip started in Phoenix with two nights at the Arizona Grand. Here are my thoughts: POSITIVES: 1. Room: Our room was large. All of the rooms at this property are two-room suites (similar to Embassy Suites) with a couch, desk, sitting area, TV and wet bar in one room and two queen beds, a small TV, bathroom and a fairly substantial amount of built-ins in the bedroom. The pillowtop bedding was very nice and comfortable. The bathroom was awkward with the sink actually being in the bedroom; however, the shower/bath was large and had great water pressure. Our room was on the ground level and therefore had a small padio with two chairs and a small table. It was nice but was definately not "private" as the hotel's website seemed to indicate. Our patio was shared by three other hotel rooms with only a waist high iron fence seperating each of the "private" patios. The only negative about our room is that it could definately use some touch up (paint, moulding, etc.) but as a family resort these rooms probably get more wear and tear than most. 2. Pools and Waterpark: The waterpark at this resort is great. In addition there are several pools and several jacuzzis spaced throughout the resort including an adult only pool with a bar. For the kids, the waterpark was amazing. It consists of three waterslides, a lazy river, a wave pool, a large pool, a 25 person hot tub and a infant pool. It is open from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and I never thought we could kill a whole day but we did and it was a blast. There are plenty of place to lay out with lots of areas in the shade including first-come, first-serve cabanas. The waterpark seemed VERY safe with lots of lifeguards. Also, there is a grill with burgers, chicken sandwiches, drinks etc. that were not overpriced and the food was decent. A hamburger for example was $5.95 and a chicken sandwich was $6.50. Waitresses come around and take your order so you never even need to leave your lounge chair to order food, drinks, beer, etc. 3. Price: I paid $199 directly through the hotel and I think that the hotel is certainly worth that price. 4. Hotel Grounds: This is an attractive property with nice landscaping and lots of beautiful fountains. This is by no means a 4 or 5 star resort but for being a family resort it is nicely appointed. 5. Service: The front desk person was very friendly but initially said our room was not available but when I told him we had been driving for 10 hours, he immediately put us in another room that was available. The bell desk was extremely nice and helped us find our room and carry our bags. 6. Free WiFi: Always a GREAT PLUS, when the hotel offer free internet and while this Internet is not exactly free (see resort fee section below) I liked having "free" internet access. 7. Spa: My wife got a facial and said the treatment was awesome and the person who gave her the facial was nice and attentive However, the spa was small with only a suana, steamroom and jacuzzi and not very luxurious. NEUTRALS: 1. Lobby: Very plain, with a large timeshare/resort ownership desk that was always trying to hoc people to buy ownership interests in a development currently being built on the property. There is no bar in the lobby and its not really set up to sit around and/or hang out. 2. The layout of the hotel. This place is huge and the rooms are in several 4 story hotelettes spread out all over the property. Therefore, after you check in you often have to drive to you room which can be very far away from the hotel lobby. 3. The sports bar on the 4th floor of a building which contains the spa, gym and Phantom Horse Grill was severly lacking as sports bars go. One plasma tucked in the corner and several very old televisions suspended around the bar. This place could definately use a facelift and some more plasmas. NEGATIVES: 1. I hate resort fees and this hotel charges $20 per room, per night. It says the resort fee covers "the enternce into the water park, the gym, wifi, unlimited local calls, in-suite coffee, parking, faxing and complimentary paper" However, (with the exception of the waterpark) these are things that are normally covered by the price of the room. "Resort Fees" just happen to be one of my biggest pet peaves.

“A little dated.....but so am I...I liked it very much!” I read some reviews here about this place and was skeptical. I have to tell you, the place was great. I think some reviewers listed here want the world but don’t want to pay for it. This is a value hotel; location costs, parking cost in a major city.....if you want to pay $300 and for parking....go to Penn Sq. If you want to pay less than half that...stay here. It’s an older place and is a little dated...but so am I and if it ain’t broke, you don’t need to fix it. I am more traditional...I don’t like the retro look of the newer places like the Hard Rock. Property is in a great location with loads of FREE parking. Good sports bar on the property that locals hang out at; if locals hang out, you know the place is good. Lots of great bars in a nice neighborhood that is safe....just a short walk to the Rocky Movie Steps. Eastern Penn is just up the street if you want to check it out. The room was very clean with a fantastic bed and it had everything ....coffee in room.....adjustable heat....desk with a new ergo chair...hair dryer...iron and board (both new and clean.) Free and fast wireless internet. Nice fast check in....nice lobby......people at the place are very nice. They also provided a veteran and military discount. ......I want to stay here again and will.

“Great view from a great hotel” I stayed here for 5 days...16th floor room overlooking city/seaport. I was there for a convention and the fact this hotel is attached to the convention center makes it worth the cost. So, convenient...clearly the BEST convention hotel (attached to a fabulous convention center) where I have stayed. Couldn't bear to close the drapes since I loved the view. Even with being on the 16th floor at a large convention, there were enough elevators (and they were fast!) so it never felt crowded! Room was large and comfortable. Nicely appointed room and the bed was very comfortable. Room was clean and all of the staff, from desk staff to housekeeping were pleasant. I needed a late checkout and the staff gladly accommodated. Had room service one night...service was excellent, food was merely ok. My ONLY complaint was paying for internet. It was slow and I refused to pay more to upgrade...I thought 12.95 a day was plenty. However, it's free in the lobby...the lobby is a very nice area with a Starbucks, so if you don't need much internet, I'd opt for sitting in the lobby.

“Nice hotel, needs to improve costumer service!” The good things: Good location, coffee, apples, cookies, internet free in the rooms (wired),spacious and nice room. The bad thing: The people at the front desk were not all the time in a good mood, specially a young guy who worked there, didn ́t seem to know about politeness or courtesy. His answers were short and you feel like he wasn ́t liking what he was doing.

“Great visit with my wife on her Birthday” They know how to pamper, we stayed her on Jan 3-4 2012. Concierge Stephanie went over and above providing Restaurant ideas for us and reservations. Along with that a bottle of champagne was also provided to us in our room. We had the City View over looking the Empire State Building, Room was comfy and served its purpose. Free shoe shine is a nice touch. Wine hour was also a great way to unwind after site seeing and city walking. Will stay again!!!

“The Orchard is OK Depending on Your Needs” I went to San Francisco as a single traveler/tourist for a few days, and my goal was to find a hotel that was clean, comfortable, and affordable. I did get what I was looking for. There were a few quirks that made me decide I'd never stay here again though. The acoustics are pretty poor, I could easily hear pipes and sinks running in rooms adjacent to mine, and my toilet made a wheezing, cricket-like noise almost constantly. The carpet looks a bit dated, its obvious that this is an older hotel that was recently renovated. The website promotes wifi, but I had problems getting access and had to get a short ethernet cord from the desk, it defeated the purposed of wireless and left me stuck at the desk. It has an old fashioned style, but clean, spacious rooms and nice staff. If you want to be completely satisfied, pay the extra money and stay at a 4 star hotel, if you need quick comfort, stay here. Its right next to a major stop for the cable cars, and about four blocks away from a BART station. Places to eat are very close by, and Chinatown and Union Square are less than 15 minutes away.

“Conference hotel with good service and location.” Clean, good staff, well equipped rooms with small fridge, large desk, free wireless, etc. Views from our room were poor (overlooking a roof 'garden') but overall a well- run conference hotel.

“Not up to Four Seasons standards but great location and nice enough. Great room service. Other service was lacking” Stayed here for a business meeting and loved the location on the lake and the nice lobby. The service was average and the rooms were very small with old furniture and a very small bathroom. No where near the typical Four Seasons room quality. One highlight was the room service -- fast, efficient, great service and personable order taker and delivery not to mention great food. Valet had long lines and was disorganized although staff seemed to realize they were overwhelmed yet remained friendly and apologetic.

“Hampton Inn Thumbs Up!” We just got back from a week in Chicago, and were very glad we choose the Hampton Inn! The Front Staff was courteous and very helpful (I had forgotten my public transportation directions to the Brookfield Zoo, and they got on the computer to help me out, etc.) The room was clean, spotlessly clean. Spacious! Bathroom clean, plenty of towels, etc. You can't beat the location, for sure! As for the much discussed fire house next door, every now and again you do hear the sirens, but since we're from NYC, we're used to that. I would think that any hotel you stay in downtown, you would hear sirens going off. If that might trouble you, ask for a room away from the fire department. Breakfast room is large and there is plenty to offer. We are single, but clearly families rule at the Hampton. They also cater to groups - we had the gang from Cincy and then St. Louis (wearing their colors) who came in to see their teams vs. the Cubs! Very positive experience and we would certainly stay here again.

“Great experience in SOMA” This Westin lived up to the brand's reputation. The lobby, check-in, room, and luggage desk experiences I had were all excellent. The room wasn't huge, but that's to be expected. However, the layout of the room was sensible, it was well-decorated, and the tall windows offered great light during the day along with the good view. My only 2 VERY SLIGHT quibbles - the housekeeping staff replaced perfectly good towels (no eco-conscious towel program at the Westin) and in the bathroom the toilet was super close to the shower, which was an awkward layout. But these minute quibbles underscore how great my stay was - thanks for a great 4 nights!

“Pleasant Stay” Room looked and smelled great. We could park right outside. Had an excellent meal at the grill. Not much in the way of views though and you'd better be in good shape to get up and down the hills. Would recommend.

“A Study in Opposites in Ballantyne” A while back, I had the decided pleasure of staying at the Ballantyne resort, but recognizing that I would only be spending enough time in a hotel to clean up and sleep, decided to give Starwood's new Aloft product a try. It was a study in opposites to say the least, however, Aloft did not suffer from the comparison. The two properties are simply to different to compare, and as an inexpensive, low-frills property, the Aloft shined. It is a bit off-putting when you first walk in--music is pumping like it's a night club, and the lobby is arranged in the same fashion. But upstairs is quiet, and the rooms very sedate. The room's total square footage is very small, however, they have arranged it in a manner that is both stylistically pleasing and comfortable. The sleeping area is separated from the closet and sink by a modular wall that serves as the headboard on one side and closets/storage on the other. Through the sink/closet area is a small bathroom with a WC and shower. Complimentary products are Bliss, which I rather liked. While compact, the room was both clever and comfortable. The hotel provided minimal services, and that was reflected in the price. I would definitely stay in this or another Aloft again in the future, particularly if I was spending minimal time in my room.

“A Good Airport Hotel” Checked in less than 60 seconds - always a good sign! Was pleasantly surprised with the condition of the room given that airport hotels aren't always very good. Needed to take the shuttle at 445 AM and only had to wait about 5 minutes. Took about 10 minutes to get my terminal.

“Clean, Elegant, Great Location” I spent two nights at the Palmer House Hilton while on business in Chicago. The room was spacious, a two bed, two bath upgrade due to a reservation hiccup, but the bathroom was so small it was hard to turn around and use the facilities, if you know what I mean. Like, really tiny. We were on the 21st floor with a great view of buildings and thankful for the heavy drapes that kept all those twinling lights outside where they belong. We enjoyed the breakfast buffet; it's crowded in the mornings and coffee service is slow, but the spread was fresh and filling, and covered everything from lox and smoked trout to oatmeal and scrambled eggs. Elevators are slow during morning and evening "rush hour" but our longest wait was only 5 minutes. The place is chock full of history. The staff even pointed out some secret escape hatches carefully concealed in the panelling of some rooms, and rumor has it Al Capone and other shady legends used these to disappear and escape to the streets when necessary! The lobby boasts a painted ceiling that one could gaze upon for hours and never take in all the detail. Wow. No charge just for looking! The Palmer House is in a great location, a block or so off Michigan Ave and an easy walk to Millenium Park, uptown, shopping, Marilyn Monroe statue, and tons of museums, restaurants, and other attractions we didn't have time to visit. There are a subway and a mcdonalds right by the hotel, which is a big help for a quick, cheap, meal. Although our room was huge, I did get to peek into some of the ones with just one bed. Wow. I am not sure there is room for luggage in there, so consider asking to see your room before you fork over $250-$300/night. It might be worth the upgrade. The staff was friendly, and the place was sparkling clean. I would stay at the Palmer House again, and I bet it is really decked out during the Holidays! Enjoy your stay in Chicago.

“Our experience was both good and bad.” This is a lovely boutique hotel. However, we were not comfortable with many aspects of our stay. The bed that we had was worn out and we rolled toward the weak center of the mattress each night. The espresso maker in our room was great except that they had no non-decaf pods and the desk clerk shrugged when we asked why. The breakfast in the common area appeared to be gratis but was so not. We were surprised to see a rat in the courtyard of the hotel. Here is our advice: stay here only if you must, and expect nothing but a good bathroom and desk. Even the tv channels were underwhelming.

“No issues here!” This is a nice property with a friendly staff. In terms of the room, they are clean and neat, but they need a bit of updating. I would compare the rooms to a mid level Sheraton property- nothing fancy, but fine for a quick weekend getaway. If we were staying longer or celebrating a special occasion, I would choose one of their flagship or more upscale properties. This trip was just a weekend shopping trip with "tweens", so it suited our needs perfectly. I thought the staff, from the bellman to the front desk personnel, were friendly, helpful, and professional. We enjoyed our stay.

“Great property - mildly substandard amenities/services” I had the opportunity to stay at this hotel during it opening and was quite disappointed so I was apprehensive to stay here again for a conference. The check-in to the hotel was smooth and my initial opinion of the room was positive. The room was average size for San Diego and nicely decorated. Bath was also quite nice. The bed was comfortable and the extra blanket in the room was appreciated. The no so good side were the amenities in the room. The "stylish" and modern trash cans have a tight oval opening and do not accept any type of larger trash. The wash cloths and towels are of extremely poor quality. The first washcloth I used on my face felt like it could have easily been used for exfoliation. And the "free" internet logon was hidden so well that an IT professional would have had problems finding it. I must say that the hotel did correct my billing immediately and pointed me to the obscure field to enter the free internet code into. Room service was good but the server forgot several parts of our order and did not seem to return with them...we did find the missing parts of our dinner in the outside of the hotel room door...not quite sure why she did not even knock to let us know they had been delivered... The hotel location is beautiful and many separate restaurants have been added since the hotel opened. It is very walk-able to the conference center and the San Diego Gaslamp district restaurants and shops. Would I stay here again...probably not.

“Nice Hotel” Stayed overnight at the Hyatt en route to Washington, DC. Overall the hotel was nice and in a good location. Had a view of the river with an oversized bathroom. Eveything was great except wifi is $10 per day and parking is $21 per day.. just something to keep in mind when considering other places.

“Probably not again” I mean, it was a place to sleep, I guess. The hotel was not great. VERY busy and didn't even look like a hotel, more like the Jacob Javits Convention Center. Confusing lobby, always teeming with all kinds of people. The front desk staff was nice, but a bit clinical. Room was not impressive, but the bed was comfortable. For $99 on priceline, I really cant complain too much. Would try to explore other options in the future.

“great location and quiet rooms for business travelers” the St Giles is a go-to hotel for those of us who travel weekly to NY. big rooms, nice bathrooms, quiet rooms in the back, etc -- all the amenities you need. staff is pleasant. i wish there was a coffee pot in all of the rooms, however. that said, the neighborhood is centrally located with great convenience stores, bars, and restaurants. highly recommended.

“Disappointing... watch out for incidentals!” I stayed at the Westin Downtown over the weekend. I picked the hotel because of my Starwood loyalty, and because Westin is usually a nice place to stay. I can't say that the hotel itself had any glaring problems, but overall I was disappointed. The location is good, with many things to do within walking distance. The staff was helpful and friendly too. Our room was clean and everything worked just fine. And, of course, the Westin bed was very comfortable. But, I was very surprised to find that many of the things you expect at Westin were just not there. For example, they have no concienrge lounge, no gift shop/news stand and the restaurant is only open until 11:00 am. Yes, there's a Palm restaurant downstairs, but it's not open until dinner. You are "on your own" for lunch, which I found strange for a full service, downtown hotel. I'll also admt that I was not too happy to have to walk two blocks in the rain to get to a 7-Eleven for bascis that a hotel gift show would offer in most hotels. Also concerning is the incidental costs at this property. For example, overnight parking is $28 per night. I thought it seemed high when we arrived, but assumed this was the typical cost of parking in downtown Denver. Not so, the Chase bank garage (right across the street) is only $19 per day. Why would a hotel be more than an office building? Then, after checking out, I found that minibar charges had been added to my bill. (We never even opened the mini bar.) I have contacted the hotel to get this refunded, but if you were not paying careful attention, the hotel would have just added charges to your bill after you left. For me, even as a loyal Starwood guest, my choice for downtown Denver hotel would be the Hyatt. It's appears to be brand new and is in a very good location. The Westin has just enough shortcomings to knock it off of my list when staying in Denver.

“Was OK, But Nothing Great” My wife and I stayed at the Eastgate Towers May 8-12, 2007. The room was very outdated. The furniture was extremely old. The easy chair's arms were worn away from years of use. The two dressers were from the 70's and were also worn and nicked up. Looked like garage sale material for a college dorm. The bed was comfortable but the blanket was full of cigarette burn holes. The carpet was old and worn away from foot traffic. Even the alarm clock was a decade old and didn't operate properly! The kitchenette was not used so I can't comment. The absolute worst part of the room was the bathroom. There was mold on the caulking all around the tub. The floor was old and worn away and the walls had old peeling wallpaper. You didnt want to walk in there barefoot! As for convenience, the subway is about a ten minute walk that I wouldn't want to make in the winter. Cabs pass by quite regularly and the bell hop was nice and helpful. The cleaning maids need to be retrained as they left gargabe next to the bed from the last guest and it remained throughout my stay (grape stems). Overall, I read alot of great reviews on TripAdvisor-thats why I stayed here. I must have got a bad room or the rest of you are liars!

“Might be the best value in Manhattan” I can't say enough good things about this hotel. If I didn't know Kimpton, I might have been concerned about the price of the hotel, which almost seemed too good to be true, even taking into account the fact that it's a little off the beaten path a few blocks west of Times Square. But it was clear upon arrival what a great place this is, and we really couldn't have been happier. The room was very nice and clean, and unique enough to give it a sort of boutique hotel feel even though you're still in Midtown. Staff are extremely friendly and attentive. On top of all that, there are so many great services that this hotel (and other Kimpton hotels) provide, including complimentary happy hour drinks, coffee, newspapers, and upscale toiletries (including Etro paraben-free soaps), etc, which other hotels are usually too cheap to provide. Those not familiar with NYC might be a little put off by the location since you're not in the thick of tourist attractions, but everything is really within walking distance, and if not, the subway is only a few blocks away. Overall, I can't really picture a better value within Manhattan (short of inconvient locations such as Battery Park or way uptown), and I don't think I'll bother trying -- this is my new go-to spot in NYC.

“clean, comfortable and well located” The hotel was clean, comfortable and well located. The staff was professional and the room was a good size - I was able to conduct business and use the fitness center without any problem.

“Just Okay” I keep wondering what the Renaissance brand really means. In this case, it means a pretty average hotel with some real oddities. In the case, for example, of the Renaissance Mayflower in Washington, D.C., it means something close to perfection. Our room was okay, if non-descript, with a ninth floor view of a parking lot. We searched high and low for electrical outlets and the room itself was dark. On the other hand, the room was very quiet, the bed was wonderful, and we slept like babies. The bar area is thick with smoke and the service is rather eccentric. It had an air of slowly unraveling chaos, but has a great view of the Inner Harbor. The restaurant which we used for breakfast was very nice with wonderful views, even if the staff experienced bouts of amnesia when we ordered exotic items like hot tea. All in all, for a much more impressive Baltimore Marriott, and we do like this chain, try the Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor. Now that should be a Renaissance.

“A room with a view!” Loved this Hilton. The view was absolutely stunning, looking out over the water and the city. Tried the spa, the massage was good, but I have had better. Nice cocktails at the bar. A nice walk over to the gaslamp quarter, or a short cab ride. Not far from a sweet outdoor shopping mall either. Very nice outdoor pools. Good quality internet speed. I would definitely return to this hotel.

“Close to airport and very decent hotel” Other than the dearth of restaurants in the area, this is a pretty decent Courtyard. The staff was very good about MR recognition, which I appreciated. The room was standard CY fare and in good shape. The airport is a whole 5 minutes away and there is a gas station right in front which is perfect for fueling up the rental car on the way back.

“Great Location, Good view, friendly Staff” I've been to New York City many times for business and vacations but never stayed in this hotel. I was headed to Canada on business when American cancelled my flight at the last minute. Frustrating after checking my bags in and then getting the flight cancelled. While waiting for my bags I was looking for a hotel to book at the last minute. Many hotels were full. I saw that this one was available so I booked it. There weren't too many options and I was frustrated as I didn't expect to have to book a hotel in NYC. I just flew in for a quick meeting and then was expecting to head to Montreal on another meeting that day. I called the hotel and they confirmed a suite on a high floor. $400 + tax rate. I took a taxi and promptly checked into the hotel. Everything was quick and easy at the front desk and they had my room waiting. A bit strange since you have to take an elevator from the ground floor up to the lobby and then another set of elevators up to the rooms. I had a room on the 35th floor and it was very spacious with an amazing view. Surprisingly it was quiet even though it faced Times Square. The location couldn't be better as you are in the heart of the action. There is an entrance from Time Square or another entrance on 44th Street as well. There is a bar off the front desk area. Nothing super high end but it was busy when I checked in. The room was comfortable with a King bed that was comfortable, a good sized bathroom, LCD TV and a couch and desk. View was great. Friendly staff with no problems at all. Pay to play internet that was $21 per day and it worked glitch free. There are higher end hotels in NYC but this location is great if you want to be in the heart of the action.

“Sheraton was Fine” The location is the best factor - a few blocks from Navy Pier, Michigan Ave, the park....all great. All staff were wonderful and helpful. The only negative is that the rooms are a bit tired in terms of decor, particularly the bathrooms. 80s/90s style tile and fixtures. An update would be in order. Although clean and fine, I've found other moreupdated hotels at the same price.

“Better the Second Time Around” Once again we made our annual trip to visit family in San Antonio. I checked out several places, thought about trying a new place this year; but decided to try this place again. We had liked it a few years ago when we stayed and all the current reviews raved about it. We had some airline miles to spend so the cost did not bother us too much. We arrived on a Tuesday and was greeted by a mass of friendly folks. The head valet asked if we understood the valet parking cost etc. I had done my research and we had decided that the $30.00 a day would be worth it for us to pay to have a parking place we did not have to hunt for or pay for every time we decided to go some place. We did tip every time we picked up our car. We were greeted at the front desk with a smile and they knew exactly who we were and that we were there for pleasure. Funny thing is I think we may have gotten the same room we had the last time we were there. It was a corner room over looking what used to be the circus museum. It was a very nice room with a good city view and was in a quiet park of the floor. As stated our room was great everything was clean and lovely. There is a safe in the room if needed. The hotel is right on the river, but not on the busy part, which is good. It is within walking distance of all the restaurants and other attractions. But let me tell you the restaurant in the hotel is great. We ate breakfast there every day, and lunch on one occasion.(Be mindful that birds will be a part of any outside meal on the river. Just a heads up.) The bar is good too. If you have breakfast there make sure to find Maria as she will take special care of you. Every time we came back in to the hotel we were greeted with a warm hello or even "Welcome back how was your day?" Or "do you need directions today?" And we were give great info. We even decided to extend our stay by one day. We were given a very good rate and we had no trouble taking care of that at the front desk. As for the valet parking we had no problem with waiting. We were on vacation and not in hurry to catch a plane or needing to be out at a busy time. My husband actually forgot his cell phone in the car when we first arrived and the valet called to see if they could bring it up to our room. And they did within minutes. They also put our navigation system out of sight. Anyone that is coming to San Antonio should try this hotel. We will stay here again. I really don't see the need to explore any others. One thing, our coffee maker never really worked. We told the front desk and they said they would clean it out and they said if that did not work THEN they would replace it. It never worked. It took about 30 minutes to make coffee. We decided to not report it again and it was becoming a "thing" and we were there to avoid "things". Also the clean up crew came kind of early to ask if we needed the mini bar filled up. And one more thing. A grab bar in the bath tub area would come in handy. I am not so tall and stepping out of the shower is a bit of a challenge. Grabbing the slick granite counter is not a good option. Still a great place to stay. Make sure you visit the pool on the roof at night!!!

“WONDERFUL Stay!!!” After reading a mediocre review of this property we were a bit hesitant to stay. We are VERY glad we ignored that single review. Perhaps the writer confused this property with another. We can find no fault with this hotel. The bed was very comfortable, the staff was friendly and helpful, the room was imaculate, the location was praefect for our planned activities in Houston and the layout of the hotel was well planned. We usually stay in upscale properties with suites and this one ranks among the nicest in its class. We will definately stay at this hotel again!

“Another great Hyatt!” We just got back from a girls' weekend in NYC and a great stay at the Hyatt. This hotel is convenient to 5th Ave. shopping (especially Lord & Taylor), good restaurants, and Grand Central Station is right next door! One of the doormen recommended having lunch in Grand Central Station. Great tip! There's actually a food court with dozens of choices, though much more upscale than a typical mall food court. They also have sit down restaurants and some shops...you could spend a few hours there! Check in was quick & easy thanks to Diane, who was superb...very helpful & welcoming! The hotel has recently been renovated and is very sleek & sophisticated. Rooms are modern and chic, yet warm and inviting. I loved the little extra touches like a cozy nap blanket on the bed, extra shelves in the shower for storage, and reading lights on each bed. The bathroom was small (typical in NYC) and could've used a bit more storage & a couple more hooks, but absolutely loved the ultra modern square showerhead..the perfect pressure and amount of water. The closet was a walk in with plenty of storage for bags, shoes, etc. There's a market in the lobby, which not only has drinks, sandwiches, and basics, but hot items, and lots of little extras like Dylan's candy. Very convenient so you don't even have to leave the hotel! Nice trip and will be sure to come back!

“Fantastic location” We stayed at the Hilton for 7 nights at the beginning of May. We did ask for a room on a high floor room if possible, and we were given a huge corner room on the 27th floor overlooking 42nd Street which was lovely (would have liked it a little higher though). We could not fault the cleanliness of the room or bathroom. The views were beautifiul particularly at night. The actual entrance to the hotel is not the best we have seen, and if you arrive by taxi make sure the taxi driver goes to the 41st street entrance (not the 42nd street), or you have to carry your luggage across the road like we did ! Reception staff were very nice - we actually managed to check in at 1pm. The little dealings we had with the concierge was very good. The security was good at the hotel, we had to show our keycard most times to begin with until they got to recognize you. We did not eat or drink in the hotel. Applebees next door is great for breakfast and Paxs foods across the road is brilliant for lunch. There are loads of great irish Bars just off Broadway - particularly the Pig n Whistle on 47th or 48th Street. The location of the hotel was very convenient. It is so close to most things - Bryant Park is only yards away and is beautiful in the sun. The entrance out onto 42nd Street did get a little crazy and busy through at times which is not what you always wanted. We have been to NY several times now, and if you want to stay around Times Square we would certainly recommend this hotel. (Waldorf is great as well if you want to stay somewhere different).

“Overrated? Maybe, but we still enjoyed our stay.” We arrived at the Westin after originally being sort of mislead by a local parking garage that says "Westin" but isn't the actual hotel's parking lot. This lot is cheaper, but even at $36 a night to park at the Westin, it (the Westin's lot) seemed safer. The Westin's parking lot is located behind the building. The woman at the front desk was really nice--the room we were originally given had 2 double beds, but since we only wanted/needed one she gave us a queen size been in a handicapped room. The room itself was spacious, but quite a mess. There were stains ALL OVER the floor--I didn't really want to walk around barefoot on that carpet. There were ugly tangles of cords behind the desk and the table with the coffee maker. The lights also had too many switches that weren't properly synced with the wall switches, and a few of the outlets in the room didn't work. Since we were in a handicapped accessible room our bathroom had a large open shower, which wasn't too bad. Though I was really wishing I'd brought some "shower shoes" because the tile in the bathroom didn't seem very clean. We were on the 42nd floor and had a great view despite a new condo high rise being built across the street. The hotel's location is perfect--in walking distance to Pike's Place Market and the Seattle Center (Space Needle) and to the monorail to the Seattle Center (if you don't want to walk). We actually walked all over Seattle. There is a restaurant across the street, Icon Grill was also good and the service was fantastic. As mentioned before, there is free Wi-Fi in the lobby, which means it's always PACKED with people. Plus, the lobby bar is exactly that--open right to the lobby, so people drinking are basically sprawled out throughout the entire lobby. We actually were having drinks down there one night and there was a loud group of middle-aged people there (for a convention I believe) who were obviously drunk--it made me feel bad for the parents with children who were just checking in. Who wants to check into a hotel with loud drunk people hanging out all over the lobby? Overall our stay was pleasant, the pool area was nice with a little sundeck that overlooks part of the city. We enjoyed the view from our room as well and the staff were helpful and friendly.

“Great Bed!” Just returned from a stay at the Marriott. My stay was wonderful. No complaints at all! The other reviews commented on the distance from other Austin attractions/airport, etc. Since I'm from Texas, I'm used to driving everywhere, so location wasn't an issue. Sixth Street didn't seem very far to me. The hotel staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. My request for a late checkout was honored - no problem. I was there for a convention, and things ran smoothly. The pool area was beautiful - like a little spa. My husband used the workout room and was pleased with the machines and weights. Everything in the hotel was neat, clean, and tidy. My room was good for business with lots of desk space. I liked the in-room safe. The bathroom was on the small side, but was spotless with nice Bath and Bodyworks products. Now about that bed! I honestly think it was the most comfortable hotel bed I've ever slept in! Seriously, after YEARS of hotel travel, this bed wins the comfort prize. If I could have figured out a way to shove the entire bed into my suitcase, I would have!

“Un hotel in posizione centrale e molto confortevole.” Le stanze sono grandi e quindi non sacrificate come al solito negli hotel di NY. Abbiamo trovato un prezzo davvero interessante. La posizione è davvero centrale di fronte Macy's ed è servito da tutti i mezzi di trasporto. Si arriva a Time Square in dieci minuti a piedi. Lo staff della reception è davvero simpatico e disponibile, tranne il personale nelle ore notturne poco gentile e disponibile. Tutto sommato è davvero carino.

“Pretty good!” Sehr gute Lage, Zimmer eher klein - was normal ist für NY - aber ok. Preis/Leistung gut. Schwachpunkt bei unserem Besuch: Concierge/Reception nicht sehr hilfreich beim Fragen zu Touren/Verkehrsmittel oder sonstigen Leistungen. Mit Türen aufhalten alleine ist es noch nicht getan. Empfehlungen im Umkreis New York spricht für sich

“***FOOD POISONING.....ALLEDGEDLY***” My wife & I are seasoned travellers so this is not a claim that I make lightly. The reviews you see regarding the hotel and surrounding areas are true. The Magnolia is a very nice hotel, we stayed there for three nights are for the first two nights we had no complaints at all. Unfortunately on the third night we decided to eat in the hotel's restaurant and my wife ate a meal which made her violently ill, It is our opinion that the steak meal she eat was the cause, alledgedly. Most people have had food poisoning of some degree during their lives and, at the time, you will be able to tell what has caused it. My wife had only drank a fruit smoothie earlier in the day so we know that this meal was the culprit, alledgedly. As a result, my wife & I spent the night in the local medical center with the drunks and down-and-outs on a typical Saturday night in Houston. This was an horiffic experience and my wife was very ill for five hours and as a result had to be hydrated by iv drip. The ER doctor confirmed that her condition was caused by food poisoning and that once she was hydrated, she was ok to return to our hotel. She had to refrain from eating solid food for twenty four hours. Unfortunately, due to our tight schedule we had to leave early on Sunday morning and we were assured by the duty management that the outstanding medical bill, which came to $1400.00 plus prescriptions would be discussed with the general manager. My wife was ill for a further week with fever & stomach cramps and eventually the management of The Magnolia washed their hands of any blame and passed the incident on to their insurance company. To cut a long story short, the insurance company and hotel have both denied any responsibility for my wife's food poisoning and we are left with a hefty bill. So if you decide to stay at The Magnolia Hotel I would definitely think twice about eating their food....just my opinion, and hope to god that nothing bad becomes of you while you stay with them because they will swiftly wash their hands of it. I realise that the claims we make in this review cannot be proven and I'm not sure whether Tripadvisor are prepared to allow this review to be released on their website but we are genuine and honest travellers and we are not in the habit of scamming hotels or leaving negative feedback without good reason. I hope that somebody at upper management level at The Magnolia hotel sees this review and comes to their senses with regard to re-imbursement of our medical expenses but i won't hold my breath.

“Shabby, and not very chic” The main attraction of this hotel was the location, and then the price. I was disappointed to find that the "restaurant" -- a rather grubby looking Chinese place -- was closed for repairs, and that the coffee shop -- very run down -- had limited hours. The room was tiny, rather grungy, and featured an incrediyl dirty window. I doubt, even at the price, I would stay there again.

“What a dump” Pros: 1. Free internet 2. Right next to Belmont Station (red, brown, purple lines) 3. Lots of t.v. channels 4. Decent breakfast selection... not that healthy though. 5. Close to a bunch of lackluster food options 6. Some staff members were nice Cons 1. The hallways smelled of urine and smoke (disgusting!) 2. The rooms and restrooms are small and cramped 3. The street noise and noise from the train is loud, especially at night 4. The area is dangerous at night. Every single shop had a police warning posted, and I saw 9 cruisers pull up to Belmont station and arrest two people. At night, random people holler up and down the street. 5. Elevator is rickety and small I don't recommend this hotel for business travelers. It's a step up from a European youth hostel. It's hard to believe this hotel is in the same chain as the Georgian in Santa Monica! For those with disabilities, many of the stops on the El are not handicapped accessible. The Belmont station is not accessible.

“Best NYC Area Hotel” have to say I absolutely agree with all the other reviews, the Ritz Carlton Battery Park is a great find for a stay in the city. We selected the basic City-View room on the Concierge floor and were not disappointed. We even had a side-view of the Staten Island Ferry’s coming in. Here are some of the highlights: *Rooms are large and spacious for NYC standard. *Rooms are quiet especially on the weekend (no street noise to be heard or minimal compared to mid-town). *They thought of all the little touches when doing the remodel, dimmer switches on all the lights, plenty of closet and drawer space, great working area, flat screen tvs, etc. *The beds are sensational. These days all the hotels have great beds but this one was really exceptional for comfort. *The bathrooms are very spacious, good lighting, separate areas for shower, tub, toilet, vanity, etc. *The Concierge Level service is top-notch. Literally you could not have to eat any meals out if you didn’t want to. Breakfast, while stated as “Continental” included things like hot and cold cereals, smoked locks, fresh meats and chesses, hard boiled eggs, fresh fruit, mimosa’s, etc. Snack service during the day also had salad, sandwiches, cookies, sides, etc. The evening reception offers wine, champagne, fruit, heavy appetizers, etc. Additionally there is use of a laptop and printer and the service on the Concierge Floor is outstanding! They really have great people who work at that property. *Location, a lot of reviewers had concern that is was far from Mid-Town, however it is one block away from a subway/train station that gets you anywhere you want to be in minutes, i.e. Mid-Town, Little Italy, Up-Town, etc. I love NYC public transportations, it’s quick, cheap and as long as you are smart, safe. Cabs are also plentiful. There is also some shopping and restaurants in downtown, albeit quiet on the weekends and some are not open but plenty to do. *Battery Park is right outside your window and you can walk all around. *One more tip, I highly recommend the Carmel Limo and Car Service for transport in the city or airport if you want a private car. Very reasonable in price and consistent, I often use them at least for airport transport. *The gym is definitely decent. It has a view of the water, comes with all the standard cardio equip plus free weights and weight machines. I was definitely able to maintain my workout routine here plus I could run through the park. It did get a little busy at times as it’s not super large (but more than adequate) but I was able to get machines, etc. *There is only one restaurant and two bars on property and we tried them all. I would not necessarily “rave” about it but they were above-average for hotel properties. The 14th floor bar is definitely lively on weekends and hip.

“Excellent and pleasant stay :)” Completely renovated from the old Doubletree Hotel; it's unrecognizable! I was very pleased with my stay here for three nights - from room service to comfort of the room, bed, amenities, and cleanliness of the hotel. Unlike the Doubletree, Hotel Palomar offers shuttle service to nearby destinations. One of the best part is coming back from a long day of meetings to friendly faces offering complimentary wine/beer service upon entering the hotel just few steps from the front door of the lobby was awesome. I had a real pleasant stay and can't wait to come back.

“Another great stay at the St. Francis” Had to write this review, even though it was last December that was my most recent stay, because of all the negative reviews that I am seeing for this hotel. I have stayed three times now at this hotel, and have never had anything but a wonderful experience. I DO ask if I can get an upgrade, and I DO ask for a quiet room, and I think that one must ask, but it has been my experience that they comply with request. I adore the "Clock Bar", the shops, the wonderful location, and the beautiful history and surroundings. Don't be put off by negative reviews, as I have only experienced wonderful times here.

“Nice hotel, small room” I want to give the Onyx a 4.5. It's clean, mostly quiet, and fun in the Kimpton way. There were well-behaved dogs in the lobby and the staff was always happy to do anything they could to make our one night stay pleasant. There were no problems, but I found room 1008 to be really small, I thought the HVAC system was noisy, and parking seemed expensive at $42/night. I liked the Marlowe (another nearby Kimpton property) more and if I could choose between the two, the Marlowe would win. Having said that, the Onyx is convenient to the North End and to the Faneuil Hall area, and it's easy to drive to and from this hotel, so it's a good bet for tourists. The neighborhood is noisy and not Boston's most impressive, but it's not bad either. If you're thinking of coming to Boston as a tourist for a few days, here's how to get the most out of the Onyx: First, join Kimpton's free InTouch program. You'll get email telling you when there's a sale and when there is, make reservations fast because rooms don't last long. And wi-fi is free if you're an InTouch member. Now see if there's anything happening at the nearby Fleet Center (aka TD Garden). You're staying nearby so check it out. If you like Italian food, make reservations for dinner in Boston's North End. We went to Marco and it was amazing. Stay 2 or 3 nights, and let the staff at the Onyx help you decide what to do. As long as you don't mind the small room, you'll love it. Okay, this should be a five-star review, right? If this was a regular hotel, I'd easily say yes. But this is a Kimpton and they've spoiled me over the last 15 years so I expect a lot. By Kimpton standards, the Onyx is actually sort of average. But Kimpton's average is pretty amazing and there was nothing they could have done better, so I'm going to call it excellent.

“Zentrale Lage in San Francisco” Ein sehr gut geführtes und gepflegtes Haus. Gut gelegen. Market Street und Union Square in wenigen Minuten zu Fuß zu erreichen. Direkt vor der Tür ein Bus, der z.B. direkt nach Fisherman's Wharf fährt. Wir hatten eine sehr schöne Suite, die sehr interessant über Eck geschnitten war und einen Blick bis zum Bay gewährte. Im Gegensatz zum vorher besuchten Westin Mission Hills in Palm Springs waren die Klimaanlage (gleiches Fabrikat) problemlos zu bedienen. Auch sonst war - wie in einem St. Regis nicht anders zu erwarten - alles vom Feinsten. Es gab einen Butler-Service und eine sehr freundliche und aufmerksame Reception. Sylvester besuchten wir das hochgelobte Restaurant "Ames". Das sehr schöne Menue war inklusiv der Weine zu jedem Gang und dem "Mitternachts-Champagner" erheblich preiswerter als man in Deutschland für ein gleichwertiges Sylvester-Menue bezahlt hätte. Das Restaurant hat nur wenige Plätze und uns verwundert immer wieder, daß es Leute gibt, die zwar offensichtlich für diesen Anlaß reserviert haben, aber in zerknitterten Freizeit-Hemden über der Hose oder in Achsel-Shirts dort auftauchen.

“Great place to stay in NYC” Spent the weekend of the Ing NY marathon 2011, At this hotel. Big room for NY with a mini kitchen and a pull out a sofa bed. We had 3 adults in the room and found it pretty comfortable. Good beds. Great free breakfast ( a savings of about $10.00 per person per day) and a nice bar to chill out in later in the day. The staff were very attentive to our every need. Bryant Park is across the street and Times Square a block or two the other direction. There is a subway stop a block away.

“very good location and quality, but room and service need improvement” Westin hotels are consistently good quality and the Seattle Westin is no exception. The location is very good, just a block from the Westlake Center and the downtown end of the monorail to the Seattle Center/Space Needle, only a few blocks to Pike Place Market and the waterfront, and just a block from many good restaurants. The rooms are nice but the view depends a lot on the side of the tower. We faced a dozen other skyscrapers and looked directly into the Westin South Tower, so our view was into other hotel rooms and offices. Westin is known for its "Heavenly Bed" and it is a good one, but not the best in the business. Unfortunately, our housekeeper made the bed with the sheets more than a foot from the end of the bed, so the mattress pad was exposed and touching our legs, thus undermining the comfort of the bed. Lackadaisical staff is a problem. We waited more than half an hour for our luggage to be delivered after the bellhop took it out of our car. Finally, we called. It was delivered a few minutes later with no explanation for the delay. Apparently it had just been left unattended and no one was doing anything about it. We could have waited all night for it if we had not called. Some staff are good, such as the concierge and the reception staff. When we checked out a 9am, there was only a single person on duty, not nearly enough. The parking fees ($41/night for self park) are excessive. The hotel a block away charges $30. Westin charges high fees for most extras. The room has a refrigerator but it is a stocked minibar, so there is no place to store any items that need refrigeration. I wish Westin would take a hint from its sister Sheraton chain and provide some empty refrigerator space. The rooms are good size (325 square feet), but because the towers are round, they have shorter interior walls leaving room for only two double beds, not queen beds. Double beds are not really big enough for a family of 3 or 4. The bathroom is nice, and the double showerhead good, but comes only up to the shoulder of a six foot person, not adequate which leads to lots of stooping and bending. Another problem is the almost complete absence of shelf and drawer space. There is a desk and two end tables, but they are very small and have no drawers. The few small drawers are in the closet. The space could be used and furnished much, much better. Overall it is a very good hotel, but it still surprises me how many little things were wrong. It would not take much to make this hotel a five star (excellent) experience, but Westin has to get the details right and to quit charging so much for parking and other services.

“Great location, not so great rooms.” The location of this place can't be beat. It's within walking distance to ons of great places. However, this hotel seems quite old. The rooms were a bit cramped to say the least and it kind of smells like grandmas house. Other than that, the staff was very nice and my overall experience was pretty good.

“Charming, historical” I stayed for five nights in May with a sister and we were generally pleased. The public areas are stunning and the numerous photo displays of historic figures who have stayed at the hotel are fascinating. I was prepared to be disappointed with the sleeping floors, but was quite pleased. The hallways were in great condition and very elegant. Our room looked into the courtyard, with minimal view, but that was okay, as we weren't there much anyway. The room itself was clean and well-kept, albeit aging. We appreciated the in-room safe, iron/ironing board, and flatscreen TV with lots of channels. I was disappointed that we did not have a coffee maker, but I had packed a small water heating pot, Via instant, and my own mugs, so we made do. The room service charges are ludicrous, but there is a Starbucks open limited hours on the Park Avenue side entrance and the hotel is smack in the middle of the city, with endless options for food in all price ranges in the surrounding blocks. A subway stop is right on the corner of Lexington and 50th St, where we bought a $29 pass good for unlimited rides on the city's great bus system. The staff was wonderfully polite, friendly, and professional.

“Modern Sofitel Never Disappoints” We are loyal to the Sofitel Philadelphia and return often because of its terrific location and lovely service. We recently enjoyed a two night stay and took advantage of the proximity of the hotel to shops, restaurants, and historic sites. The hotel lobby bar and restaurant seemed to have gotten a upgrade; the bar was hopping. We didn't use the fitness center, but we peeked in and saw that it was a good size and fully equipped. When we travel with children, we favor the junior suites, which have a small bedroom and a living room. We had a king room this time, which was smaller, but cozy. The bedding was among the most comfortable we've had. The Occitane toiletries were luxurious. The water pressure was great and the hotel was quiet. All in all, I do not see why we would stay elsewhere when in Philadelphia.

“Awesome Customer Service” This hotels customer service was great! We only stayed two days, but left feeling we knew the front desk personally. After checking in we received a phone call in our room from the front-desk manager just checking on us to see if we were happy with our room. The room was nice. The breakfast was great & the lady who ran it was awesome. She offered meal ideas such as adding granola to our yogurt. The breakfast was really good. I did not use the pool, but it looked very small. If I'm in the area again I will likely stay here!

“A great place to stay away from the madness of downtown LA” I travelled to LA for work recently and they put me up here. DJ is the chap who runs the front door/taxis and he was amazingly kind. The check-in staff were a little cool and haughty but efficient all the same. All the dining staff were great. The food is tasty and room service was super-quick. Room was spacious, bathroom was big. Bed was comfy and I had plenty of towels. I couldn't fault the W and felt quite at home during my 4 day stay. I will be back next year!

“Fine.” Not my favorite Residence Inn by far. There are some nice touches; but, the granite and other updates missed this property. Staff very nice and accommodating. Rooms were clean. Overall just "fine." Could I stay here again? YES. Will I likely chose this property on my next trip to Houston? NO.

“Comfort and Convenience” Here's a tip: Ask for a renovated room. That's what we did, and we weren't disappointed. For four nights, my family stayed in a double/double corner room on the 36th floor that afforded us views of Times Square, the Empire State Building and Rockefeller Center. I love the contemporary feel of the renovated room and the new color palette consisting of blues, browns and gray is fresh and calming after a long day of exploring New York. And you've got to try the really comfortable beds and the plush duvet. As for the noise - the room was generally quiet but at times we could hear police sirens from the street down below...no biggie, though. And because the hotel is currently undergoing renovations, we could hear drilling in the daytime - but with the A/C on, it was negligible. I noticed though that the noise was more apparent in the bathroom. But since we were out during the day, we didn't hear much of it, thankfully. We had a 32" LCD TV that had snow issues and which the Crowne Plaza maintenance guys tried to fix. It had a loose cable in the back that made some channels very snowy while other channels were fine. The TV wasn't completely fixed but we managed to live with it anyhow. The room didn't have a coffeemaker or a microwave oven but we requested for a mini fridge and they promptly brought one up. Also, there was a steam iron and an ironing board in the room, a clock radio and a hairdryer. The lamps were fascinating - each one had an extra outlet so we could plug in and charge our cellphones conveniently. The bathroom was clean and bright. I love the faucet! And we had no problems with water pressure or hot water. The shower was great, too. One pet peeve though was the rack for the toiletries. It can be a pain keeping those little toiletry bottles standing up on it. Also, prepare to be annoyed by navigating "two lobbies". The hotel has its main entrance but you can only get to the main lobby by going up one floor via elevator. Then you have to take another elevator to get to your room. It was sort of tedious at times, but I guess the security check by the main entrance was alright for safety and practical reasons. All I can say is the staff was amazing. They were all helpful and accommodating and tried to make sure all our needs were met. We got in really early and checked our bags in and had asked the porter for a good breakfast place that's close by. He recommended Ellen's Stardust Diner where the whole family enjoyed listening to the singing waiters. I also called Guest Services a couple of times to ask about their business center (closed for renovations) or where the vending machines were (unavailable due to renovations) and they always had a few suggestions to offer. Housekeeping was also friendly and efficient. On our last day, the hotel also gladly kept our bags for us after we checked out. For first time NY tourists, I think the Crowne Plaza is an ideal place to stay. My parents were really happy with the location. It was a block away from our tour bus stop and some subway stations. It's a short walk to Times Square itself, and close to restaurants, delis, and a grocery store (I recommend the Food Emporium on 8th and 49th and the Belly Delly Deli next to Duane Reade for cheap, hot meals). I just wish the room was equipped with more amenities like small appliances since we had a relatively long stay at the hotel. However, for the rate we got the room for and its newness and location, we're satisfied and will always remember our stay at Crowne Plaza Manhattan.

“Spectacular panoramic view” I stayed at the Sheraton for four nights while attending a conference in Boston. My room was very clean and nicely laid out. The thing that I remember the most is the wonderful panoramic view looking across the Back Bay area and over the Charles River. I was on a fairly high floor and there were no other tall buildings nearby. Any time I was in the room and not sleeping, the curtains were wide open so I could gaze out the window. I didn't have a computer with me, and was happy to see they had several computers with large monitors in the lobby for guests to use (one had to log in with name and room number to use them). I liked that this hotel is connected to the Prudential Center and a huge bunch of shops. It was also a good thing with somewhat inclement weather. I only used the restaurant once. Was not too impressed with it overall. The service was fine, but the food was not very good. Although usually I was at the conference, I did go to the Gardner museum once, and it was easy to get there on the T trains. Oh, they also had a computer where it was easy to check in for flights and print the boarding pass. That is a trend that more and more hotels seem to be adopting, and was glad to see it here.

“very cool hotel” Arrived there on a Friday night. Couldn't even get to the door b/c of cars and the long line of people waiting to get into the Breslin. Really fast check in. Lobby was like a fancy library/bar. During the night, full of people hanging out. In the morning, full of people on laptops drinking coffee from Stumptown, which makes awesome cups of coffee. I expected it to be good, but they served the best lattes and made images with the milk like hearts and feathers. You need a room key for the elevators to run. My floor had a workspace area with a computer or two. I stayed in the bunk room. It reminded me of a college dorm. The beds were comfortable, but made for shorter people. I'm pretty short and I kept banging my head into lamps and the top bunk. The soap was so cute and hung on a rope off a hook. They provide a shower cap, shoe shine cloth, cotton squares, and mini nail file. The shampoo, conditioner, and body wash are Rudy's barbershop brand--full size, so you can't bring it home, but I think the hotel sells it. In the past, hotel haircare usually makes my hair dry.
