This brand is amazing. It's more of a guy's brand, but as a female, the herbal scent smelled wonderful and my hair looked good after using it, maybe even better than my usual haircare products. Wifi was free, but I had to log in every day and it was a little slow. The A/C was really loud, but I slept well. The bunk room is made for two people, but better for just 1 since it's so small. Not much room to move around, nor put your luggage. Make sure to check your check out bill. I got charged for using the minibar b/c I had snacks lying around that looked like minibar snacks. Maid didn't refill my soap on a rope the second day. Kind of bummed me out. Location is a street over from the subway and a few streets away from Herald Square. Most of the hotel guests were in their 20-40s, no kids. You could get a bigger room/bed for the same price somewhere else, but you won't get the cool lobby full of people and good music, the wonderful Rudy's hair products, delicious coffee from Stumptown, free wifi (many hotels charge a fee), pet friendly (no fee and think the policy is that the dog/cat must be under 25lbs), and stylish decor. The staff was friendly and had the right image, but lacked the customer service found at other hotels, where the bellman greets you and open doors, asks you if you need assistance with luggage. Overall, this hotel met my expectations and I'll probably stay there again next time.

“The staff was courteous and accommodating, but the hotel was definitely in need of a major renovation. t” We picked this hotel because of it's location and the Embassy Suites name. Unfortunately, the place was flat out old and showed it's age. The furnishings in our room were clearly worn and throughout the hotel you could see where multiple coats of paint had been applied over the years, not very appealing. Some of the positives were the professionalism and courtesy displayed by the staff and the quality of the breakfast, it was good.

“Excellent” Stayed for 3 nights. The rate was $199 for a larger corner room when other major downtown hotels were ranging from $260 to $425. The room was spacious, well appointed, very clean, very large desk/table to work at, plasma TV, very comfortable bed and quiet. The only negatives were the coffee maker that makes one cup at a time and doesn't keep it hot and the windows were in dire need of washing-very minor irritants and no reason to even think of not staying here. When I heard the parking was $52 a day I decided to skip a rental car which is very unusual for me. I took BART from the Airport and it stops a block from the hotel at Powell/4th station-cost was $5.35 instead of over $40 for a cab. BART is clean, fast, well run, on schedule, easy to use and makes the CTA in Chicago where I have lived my whole life seem like the armpit it is. San Franciscans do not know how good BART is unless they have taken the CTA. I highly recommend it if you stay at the Marriott. If you do not have a car and want to see Fisherman's Wharf, for $1.50 you can take the F streetcar on Market St. from the hotel. The streetcars are vintage, built in 1948, and were used in other major citiies and have been recently restored. see http://www.streetcar.org/ for info. Very nice nostalgic operation. You can get a transfer for free and use it to ride back in an hour and a half. If you go to Fisherman's Wharf eat at Cioppino's (www.cioppinosf.com) Great Italian/Seafood, large portions and our server was wonderful. It is around the corner from the beginning of the F Market streetcar line We ate at Mel's Diner several times. It is across the street from the Marriott and its motif is from the movie American Graffitti. If you liked the movie you will love Mel's. Breakfasts are good and reasonably priced. Service was quick. Lunch and dinner are fine but we did not like the open face turkey.so stay away from it. Don't eat in the hotel with its high prices when this is across the street

“Absolutely Wonderful!” We stayed one night at this hotel on April 3. I was booked at another hotel that relocated us at the Campton. We were very lucky to stay at such a lovely hotel. The entire staff was wonderful. The doormen were excellent giving great advice on local travel spots. We had a lovely stay. I would stay at this hotel again without any hesitation.

“Nice hotel for a quick business meeting.” Stayed at the Marriott San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf for a quick business meeting. This is a medium sized 4 story hotel that is between the Fisherman's Wharf and North Beach Areas. Small lobby, small bar area and a small sit down restaurant greet you when you check in. Check in was very efficient and quick. They have only two elevators and there is often a wait--catch them going down to go up! Stairs are not available for use between floors for some reason. Once you get up to your room there can be a bit of a walk to your room. Rooms are average sized--separate bathroom with shower-tub combo, bed, desk, table, chair. Minibar in room, no safe was available. Coffee maker available. I was on the third floor facing Columbus Ave. and was worried about the noise, but did not hear anything at night! Rooms were clean, bed was comfortable. Used the small gym which had a couple of flat screen TVs, a couple of treadmills, single elliptical and a single recumbent bike. A few machines and free weight sets were available. There are two laundry machines in the gym area. Fresh fruit and water were available. No one was staffing the room. Meeting rooms were good for our meeting. Rooms are downstairs from the lobby and they had connecting stairs. Food in the restaurant was OK. The food issue is not a big deal, if you are visiting San Francisco, you will always be eating out! Location is good given the proximity to the Fisherman's Wharf area and a few block walk to the Italian North Beach area. Concierge set us up with a local Italian restaurant--very nice place. If you take public transportation, the hotel is nearby bus routes. Valet parking is available--about $40 dollars a day. There is no self parking. Hotel was very busy when we were there--a combination of conventioneers and bus tour groups. The lobby and the elevators were the bottlenecks in the hotel. Would I stay here if I wasn't on a business trip? Probably not, can think of other places I would want to stay. But for a quick business trip it was OK.

“Good but not great!” This is just another typical Hilton in the USA so you get the standard Hilton's bed, its toiletries collection and even a very similar color scheme! Location was great - a block away from all the fabulous shops of Union Square. It is a huge hotel so it is always busy and crowded. Don't come expecting personalized service! Rooms were rather small and some of the furniture could do with some maintenance if not replacement.

“Inland North County homebase” If you want to stay in the North County Inland area of San Diego, this hotel offers a very good home base. We stayed with our teenage daughter in July 2012. We ended up getting a two bedroom unit, as they were sold out of the 1 BR for our last-minute booking. The extra space proved to be worthwhile. The hotel was less than 20 minutes to the SD Zoo Safari Park, and about the same driving time to UCSD. 2 separate bedrooms (with queen beds), 2 full bathrooms, 3 TV's and a small kitchen. Surprisingly quiet considering proximity to the 15, but we had a unit closer to the Gatehouse and further from the freeway. Good A/C and comfy beds. Clean rooms except for a couple of carpet stains. Small fitness room which was rarely crowded during our visit. Free hot breakfast was decent and overall well-stocked, but lacked fruit selection. Free WiFi with relatively (for a hotel) speedy internet. Free parking. Small, but nice pool area with sports court and grill. Very friendly staff. Free USA Today during the week. We did not take advantage of the evening receptions during the week, but many others did. Easy access to I-15. Plenty of nearby restaurants; our favorite was Thaigo in the nearby shopping center.

“location is the only nice thing about this hotel” I stayed at the Best Western PLUS President Hotel at Times Square in September 2011. The good - The hotel is located on W48th Street between Broadway and 8th ave. It is only a block from times square and the theater district. The bad - In the first that we were assigned. the air conditioner did not work. We were then moved to another room where the air conditioner worked, but there was a musty smell in the room. Also, the rooms and the windows are not sound proofed. We would hear traffic throughout the night and woke up to the sound of very loud road construction at 7am. The elevators, hallways, and rooms are all very narrow, so it's hard to navigate if you have big suitcases. The bathrooms are not much better. There is no room to maneuver, and the tub is VERY slippery. Housekeeping were the worst. They left their carts in the hallways all day and night that made the narrow hallways even more narrow. They would also just barge into the room without knocking.

“The city of angels” A Los Angeles da sola con mio figlio di 10 anni, seguo un buon consiglio e scelgo questo Hotel a Beverly Hills. Stanze immense pulite e arredate in puro stile Hollywood, personale gentilissimo e posizione senz'altro privilegiata vicino a Rodeo Drive. Un solo neo e non certo a causa dell'hotel, l'idea iniziale era noleggiare un auto ma genialmente riesco a dimenticare la patente a casa, quindi niente da fare, e la posizione si rivela per me un po meno proficua di quanto pensavo. Cio nulla toglie alla struttura dove ho passato comunque un incantevole soggiorno, consigliato.

“Great hotel - amazing architecture - relaxing rooms.” Received a free night at a Ritz Carlton and the only location available was the Philly location. We were a little apprehensive at first because the mix of reviews but were very pleasantly surprised. Arrived EARLY and was granted checking (Around 11:45am) Valet parking was only option. The hotel was decorate really nice for Christmas. Had a single room (queen) bed facing City Hall. Very quiet relaxing. Nice deep bathtub and robes. My only complaint would be the design of the shower which allows the window curtains to constantly get wet and thus causing mold/mildew

“Great Staff, Central Location” Really enjoyed the family stay here. The staff could not be nicer, from the front desk, to the breakfast crew and cleaning crew. Rooms are clean and typical in size for NYC. Gym is a bit bigger than most for the brand and OK. The neighborhood is great, with easy access to subway routes. Small note of caution is that bar is very expensive outside of happy hour.

“Good jumping off point” Okay hotel. Near mall and other stores, but not near downtown or Scottsdale. Our room was nice as the bed was comfortable and spacious. The problem with the hotel is more on the inside. The hallway was a bit dated and had a musty smell. There was also a McDonald's bag on the floor the evening we checked in and it was still there the morning we checked out. The buffet was good, but there were no pancakes and waffles available. The pool looked nice. We did not use it however. All in all, it is a good hotel, with some shortcomings. We used it as a jumping off point after landing in Phoenix and heading to points north.

“Great property, excellent staff” I visit this hotel twice a month while on business. I am always delighted with the room and the service. The rooms are huge, clean, and well appointed. The workout room is above average and clean. The staff is friendly and very helpful. You cannot miss by staying here!

“Planning to Stay at South Park DoubleTree next time!!” My husband and I just stayed here this past weekend. We had reserved our room about 2 1/2 months ago and were really looking forward to our stay based on reviews on this site. However, we were very disappointed. We had a King non - smoking room which faced the parking lot. The room, including the bathroom, was dirty and definitely dated. Also, the hotel was very noisy -- could hear other pople and children in their rooms as well as people showering,etc. The bar was desolate -- particularly for a Friday night and we waited about 15 minutes for the bartender to come back from a brake before being served. WE would not stay here again.

“Small Rooms, but Service makes up for that” Spent a night in the Four Seasons Houston, and the personalized service was exactly as expected, very responsive with dry cleaning and fax services (if you need a doc printed, don't bother with the business center and the $1 per page printing cost, just email your doc to the front desk and they will print and deliver. Ate at the bar and Quattro for breakfast, very good crab cake at the bar for $5. Breakfast very reasonable from hotel standards if you are ok drinking water. A juice and coffee costs about the same as an entree. Courtesy car was great, Joe and Rashid were both very friendly and responsive, will take you anywhere within downtown quickly. Only complaints I had were the size of the room and the second day my room was not serviced until after 3pm, which of course was when I was at the gym and coming back to shower and finding I could not get in, waiting 20 minutes outside which was slightly annoying, but just unlucky.

“Great location, very good hotel” The Rex is something a bit different as befits San Francisco. Great location, very good hotel, well run and interesting rooms. Very good value. Our only complaint was the lack of Max the pug - he was absent our entire trip.

“Horrible Service!” I stayed here for 3 nights and each morning the housekeeping lady would come and bang on my door loudly at exactly 8AM for housekeeping services. I barely got any sleep in the mornings! The final night, I called downstairs to the main desk and spoke with someone, letting her know that I did not want to be woken up the next morning and wanted to sleep in until at least 10AM. The woman assured me that I would not be woken up and that I should put my "Do not disturb" sign up on the door. I told her that I didnt' have one (I actually did not have one - mine was missing!!). She assured me she would take care of the situation and that I should go to sleep peacefully. The next morning, wonders of wonders, the cleaning lady came before 8AM and knocked loudly. When I refused to respond, she came back at 9AM and banged again. This happened every single hour until I checked out at 11:30AM! I will never stay here again just because of the rudeness of the housekeeping staff. Don't they know not all people like to be woken up every hour of the morning?? Rude is all I can say to describe this place. Also, I went to the front desk to ask about free Internet services and a computer that I could use to check my email for 5 minutes before leaving for the airport. The front desk guy told me to go downstairs to the business services office and get a special code from a guy and then I could use one of their computers for free to check my email. So, I went downstairs only to find that the guy there told me I had to pay to use any computers. He told me the guy upstairs gave me the wrong information and that no computer services were free. Nevertheless, I did not get to check my email. Definitely not worth the money to stay here!!

“2nd time a charm” We visit NYC often and this hotel stands out above all others for many reasons. I was so impressed the first time staying here with my girlfriend that I vowed to bring back my husband one day. It was a special anniversary for my husband and I. I just happened to ask for an upgrade, mentioned the special occasion, and voila, we received a great upgrade for the night. My only regret is not being able to stay a night or two longer. Our suite was spacious, beautifully appointed with antiques, and had a charm that no cookie-cutter hotel can offer. As usual, service was attentive without trying too hard, the breakfast and the late afternoon snacks were a treat. However, the cafe au lait/cappuccino in the a.m. is not good if you know your coffees. Stick with regular coffee. Thanks to everyone at Elysee for another wonderful stay.

“Great Price for Center City” Most of the reviews are accurate for this hotel. It is in a great location and offers an excellent rate considering it's in the heart of a major city. The staff was very friendly and helpful even though the hotel was considered to be at "sold out status." My only complaint, which is not limited to this hotel, is that the sheet would come off the bed throughout the night exposing the mattress (which did appear clean). I don't know why hotels don't use properly fitted sheets. The pool is small but well kept and was full of kids on the Saturday I was there. The lobby area is impressive and there is a 24 hour 7-11 behind the hotel. Behind the hotel is also a multi-level parking garage which is next to Terminal Market which we found to be the best price after getting our ticket validated in the market. It worked out to be about $23 for 24 hours. Be advised that the much cheaper option mentioned in another review below ($7) is closed on Sundays.

“Avoid this Hotel - Poor Management” Residence Inns are typically a reliable chain of business hotels ran by Marriott. Known for their large refrigerators and oversized rooms - a business traveler's best friend can be these types of hotels. This Residence Inn in Los Angeles - right on the border of Beverly Hills - is an old hospital that was converted into a hotel. You will notice that the hot tub is actually an old physical therapy pool and it is two levels underground. While it is open 24 hrs a day, unless you like relaxing in a dungeon type of environment, it is not an ideal set up. There is a gym underground as well. Only one of the elevators actually goes down to the gym and hot tub so you have a guessing game to play because you cannot query the elevator when you want to go down. Parking at the hotel - Don't even bother. Residence Inns are typically known for the complimentary parking - and while this is in LA and it is very difficult to park on the street without getting ticketed. The valet staff will tell you they do not allow self park - which in fact the hotel does if you ask. A separate company runs the valet parking and they are an abrasive group of people. The first week we were at the hotel we parked here but quickly learned it was too much of a hassle to deal with the valet staff. Park across the street at the Crowne Plaza - it is cheaper and the parking attendants are much more friendly. Breakfast at this Residence Inn is very good - excellent help staff and wonderful cooks. In fact if the rest of the employees at the hotel were as good as the maids and breakfast staff, this would be an exceptional hotel even with the awkward hospital layout. Dinners are not near as good as the breakfasts, for the days they serve them and you may as well skip them all together. Finally, we had some minor damage that was done to our rental car by one of the valet staff when we were at the hotel. When we asked to talk to a supervisor, it seemed like he was never available. Finally we were told to fill out a claim form, noting the damage and the incident. The next day after we filed the report - once again asking for the supervisor - one of the valets produced a parking stubb that had written on it the exact damage that we reported in the incident report. He then claimed he saw us do the damage to the car and it was our fault. The time and date he said when he witnessed the incident was a time neither the car or any of us were at the hotel. As a frequent business traveler - this is by far one of the most bizarre and unimaginable situations ever experienced. Appealing to the Residence Inn Manager did no good either. This hotel, due to the unconventional layout and rather coarse management style, is probably the reason the rooms are heavily discounted on deal sites like Priceline. We would recommend avoiding this hotel until both the management and valet company have been removed and replaced with more typical friendly Marriott Residence Inn folks that we're use to dealing with.

“おしゃれなホテル” ユニオンスクエアから近く、観光に便利なホテルです。 部屋は、少し変わっていて、ベッドにストライプの天蓋(のようなもの?)がついていたり、統一感は無いのだけれどもかなり洗練されたおしゃれな雰囲気でした。 フロントの人もベルボーイの人もハウスキーピングの人も、みなさんとても親切で、にこやかに挨拶をしてくれるし、特にベルボーイの人はタクシーがつかまりにくい時などはホテルから少し離れたコーナーまで捕まえに行ってくれたりしてくれました。 アメニティはすべてアヴェダで、こちらもちょっと得したような気がします。またホテルのネット会員になるとフリーのWiFiも使用できるのでとても便利です。

“Comfortable suite hotel” I have stayed at this hotel many times. It happens to be conveniently located near our office in Dallas. The staff is very attentive and the rooms are comfortable. The workout room is quite small but has both aerobic equipment and weights. The hotel is very close to Northpark Mall where you can find several restaurants and shopping.

“Mixed feelings” Washington DC hotels ARE expensive. Windsor Inn is at the cheaper end of the scale. With this in mind the WIndsor is an acceptable place to stay: great location, fine breakfast, friendly and helpful staff. But beware, it is not 'luxurious', it does not exude European luxury, although the website claims it does. It is more like a two star European pension. You may strike lucky and and get an upstairs room; you may luck out and get a 'garden' room (located in a rancid basement lacking ventilation). Three stars for an upstairs room, but barely two stars for a basement room.

“Wonderful service at the Four Seasons” I stayed here for three nights in December with my husband, who was on business. The room was wonderful, the closet space and bathroom enormous and there was nothing I could fault about it apart from the fact that we seemed to be on a housekeeping schedule that left our room until 3.30pm each day. It was really quite annoying to come back from a morning out and find the room still not done. My only other complaint is that the portions of anything from room service were enough for two or three people and it felt like a terrible waste. I expect though that this would be a real plus for a lot of people. Apart from the late housekeeping the service was really quite outstanding. I was treated like a valued, long term client despite it being my first stay and it really made me want to go back again - soon. The main restaurant is a Joel Rebochon which is wonderful at home in Monaco and just as good in New York. I ate there once for lunch and once at dinner - highly recommended! The price tag is high ($1,100 per night) but this is serious value for money.

“Very good hotel at very reasonable price” Very nice hotel located in the historic Mount Vernon neighborhood, about 10 min walk to Inner Harbour, and 15 min walk to Amtrak station. I had read comments that rooms were outdated, but mine had new furniture, very nice. Free wifi, in-room safe, free hot breakfast, very nice staff. Highly recommend.

“Nice value option near Moscone” I usually stay at the Intercontinental when I attend events at Moscone, but due to a big sports event that week, the least expensive room I could get there was $500/night. That's just not in my budget. I stayed at the Mosser on the recommendation of friends. The location is just as good as the Intercontinental, if not a little better. The rooms are small, but clean. The staff is nice. Coffee and muffins in the morning is more than the Intercontinental offers. My only quibble is that there is no good place to work in the room: no desk or table. If it had that, I'd give it 5 stars.

“It Doesn't Get Much Better Than This” The "hardware" -- big, quiet, comfortable rooms. From the over-sized bathroom with separate shower and large bathtub to the over-sized flat-screen TV (and a great selection of channels including full HBO spectrum) to the comfy bed, there wasn't one thing I could fault about the rooms. The restaurant serves breakfast, lunch and dinner and the food I had at each meal was excellent. What really sets this hotel apart are the people. I cannot remember encountering so many sincerely nice, professional and helpful employees (and I met a lot over my 4 night stay). There was nothing that was too much to much to ask of them and more than once they provided service that was beyond exceptional. I have admittedly had a hard time finding a Chicago hotel that I wanted to return to but I have now. And I can't wait.

“Excellent stay” I chose this hotel by default since everything in downtown Seattle was sold out or $500 per night. Stayed 4 nights while here on business. Could not have asked for a better experience. Location was convenient, only 5 miles to the heart of downtown. Free shuttle service available on request. Parking was free and secure. Neighborhood was cool as it's right near the University of Washington. The hotel also loans out bikes at no extra charge which allowed me to explore the area and waterfront which was only a mile away. The rooms had free coffee with Keurig coffee makers and a good selection of coffee and tea. Staff was friendly and helpful. Room was huge as I got a corner room on the 5th floor which felt like home for the entire week. Please give me the same room next time! Overall, a great stay. I'll be back.

“WONDERFUL HOTEL IN A GREAT LOCATION!!!” My husband and I spent six nights at the Prescott Hotel and had a great time. The hotel reminded us of a European hotel, especially the small bathroom. It was exactly what we expected. If we were looking for a hip, glitzy, modern hotel we would not have stayed here. The rooms were impeccable and kept that way daily by housekeeping. All of the staff we dealt with were exceptional and very interested in our having a wonderful stay. The nightly happy hour is a nice amenity. The hotel is very quiet and gives one a very secure feeling. The location is great - a block to the cable car (if you can ever get on one), near public transporation, a couple of blocks from Union Square and numerous fantastic restaurants. All in all this is a great hotel if you are looking for an older, quiet hotel with an ambiance and in a central location. We look forward to returning.

“Dirty Dirty Dirty” Last summer, we had to work in Houston, and there was some absurdly large convention in town, and this was the only conveniently located hotel available. EVERY hotel in Houston was booked. It as insane. So we booked here. I actually stayed here in 2008 when my client managed to bring me into town another time when some absurdly large convention resulted in every other hotel being booked. It wasn't as if a Hilton was $900/night. All rooms were booked at all levels, and the only available hotels were at the airport or the space center or in Sugarland. Again, insane. So, we stayed here both times. In 2008, it was nice enough. No frills, but fine. My 2011 summer stay was atrocious. My colleagues and I had 8 rooms booked. When we checked in at 5 PM, they said seven of the rooms were booked and the last one was "not available." They didn't know when it would be available, because, as I found out, it was drying out. They had just shampooed the rugs. Well, I waited an hour and then took the room which still had soaking wet carpet and reeked of mildew or body fluids or both. It was awful. Their solution? No, don't put me in another room - "all were booked" - spray down the room with chemically air freshener. Enter the headache from the smell. On top of the unexplained reason for soaking the carpet, pulling out the industrial dryer, and then having to cover up that smell with air freshener, I noticed that the room had an overall level of grime that wasn't present in 2008. I guess that's what happens when you don't have daily housekeeping. The room was filthy. Brown grime on the furniture. Sticky bedspread. Mildew in the bathroom. Oh, and the microwave had been ripped off the wall, exposing the original holes in the cabinets. I went into coworkers' rooms, and while generally odor-free, they were still grimy. I got up early the next day and went to work. I got back and five, and the room still smelled terrible. I asked for a new room, and was told "Nope, you should've asked this morning." Again, sold out and the cleaning staff left for the day so i couldn't get a new room and have them pawn this dog off on someone else. On the third day, I was truly fed up. I felt soooo gross in this hotel. Did I mention the nasty, worn out mattress? Oh gosh, this place was bad. On the third day, I spoke up again. They offered me a free night. I said that didn't really matter to me, since work was paying for my trip. And I said I suffered through two disgusting nights with no word from the manager, even though I mentioned this disgusting room multiple times. At that point, they offered both nights for free, but I said I wanted to check out early. I think I paid for one night, which I felt was fair. They did offer me a certificate for a free night, which would be useful, but I was so burned by this experience, that I never want to go to any Extended Stay "Deluxe" again. I recognize my situation was unique. However, even if I hadn't had the room with the mystery problem that had to be hosed down, the fact remains that the rooms were grimy and not undergoing any kind of regular comprehensive cleaning. I'm not sure what happened here. It was fine a few years back. It may be fine in 2012. But I think that the lack of daily housekeeping is part of the problem. Yes, I understand that's how it works at this type of hotel, but boy, the place was grimy. I think what really annoys me about the place being so poorly maintained is that it is next to the hospital and so many people staying here are visiting terminally ill family members and it just seems like this hotel is taking advantage of them. The room rates were decent, but why should they endure such a slipshod place during their troubling times. Ugh. I really hope this place got its act together because it was a major failure for me. Again, I had no problem with the basic accommodations. if it were clean, I'd give the place a much higher rating because it would've provided good value. But it was just soooooo skeevy. You'd think that with such a simple setup, you could keep it clean. You'd be wrong.

“This one's worth a visit” I spent only a short time at the Harbour Court Hotel but it was an incredible experience. From the excellent location just minutes from major San Francisco attractions along the Embarcadero and a major BART train station, to the cozy rooms with swank furnishings, there was much to enjoy. The hotel staff was always friendly and the colorful, plush lobby's a gem. At 5 nightly, there's a free wine party and some evenings there's also cookies and milk to greet guests at 9 p.m. Never got the use the YMCA next door, but heard it was a nice one. I went for long walks along the boardwalk instead. You must check out the food shops across the street in the Ferry Building. A food critic told me you can dine there all day and know you're getting some of the best food in the city. I went alone for business but will definitely be back with my husband for fun!

“Older motel room” The older motel room is what we were given, having used the Entertainment Card discount. Fortunately, it wasn't as noisy as expected, but if you can, opt for the tower rooms, as most everyone recommends. Also, fortunately, this was only a one night stay, and convenient to where we needed to be, but not up to Holiday Inn standards, IMO.

“Great Views, Average Hotel, Inconvenient Location” My best friend and I stayed at this hotel for 5 days last week. The views are beautiful--right on the marina, looking out on the bay. There is a lovely walking path directly in front of it. A great place for biking or watching the fishermen. It is located very close to the airport, which is good if you are only here for a stopover but bad if you want to explore the city of San Diego. To get to any major destination is 15 minutes by car (if traffic is good)--walking is not an option. The shuttle only delivers to downtown 4 times per day. As other reviewers have mentioned, there is charge for nearly everything at this hotel. Parking, Wi-fi, internet access, and local calls all carry a charge. The restaurant and lounge are overpriced; a Cosmo was $12, breakfast $20 for one. The bottled water in the rooms carried a $5 charge. There was no refrigerator or microwave standard. The room itself was average; something I would expect to find in a Hilton hotel. Bed was good, room was quiet. Everything appeared clean. The bathroom tiles and tub were chipped slightly, but nothing excessive. Service was good. Melanie at the front desk was especially friendly and helpful. I tried using the Wi-fi, but gave up because of the shoddy coverage. I did not use the pool or fitness center, so cannot comment on those. All in all, not a bad experience. However, given the price this hotel normally charges, I would rather stay somewhere closer to activities with more value for my dollar.

“Another great Omni property” I'm a big fan of the Omni brand and seem to be doing a national tour of their hotels. This Omni is ideally located near the Galleria area with easy access to everything in the neighborhood. The rooms are spacious and very clean and have the usual ridiculously comfortable beds you find at Omnis everywhere. As usual, don't forget to join the free Select Guest program for free wi-fi and morning drinks. There's also complimentary parking around the corner from the valet if you don't mind a 4-5 minute walk (the front desk can validate your ticket daily). I had an issue with the in-house restaurant that was handled incredibly quickly and definitely exceeded our expectations - I would have no hesitation going back. My only minor gripe is that wish the pool were heated but it's probably fine when the weather starts getting into the 90s!

“Excellent Airport Hotel” This is a great place to stay if you want to be right in the DFW airport--it is as fast "in and out" as you can get. You can walk/take the sky train to the hotel from the gates. The staff are friendly and accommodating. The rooms are really nice--modern, clean, well-decorated.

“Odd layout” I arrived early and my room wasn't ready - this was expected. I was asked to pay $1/bag to leave my bags until my room was ready. That's not a nice way to start the trip, but it's not outrageous either. My room was ready around 1pm and I found it comfortable and nicely arranged. It was a bit difficult to keep the room warm enough and the HVAC system was somewhat loud, banging on and then blowing loudly, with frequent cycling. The bathroom was bright enough and included a smaller shaving/make-up mirror. One problem with the bathroom is the low water pressure, perhaps due to a water restrictor on the shower nozzle. This meant that it took 10 minutes to take a shower instead of 5 because there simply wasn't enough water. I must remember to carry a wrench with me when I travel to remove water restrictors when they're overly restrictive. Another problem with the bath is a permanent nightlight built into the light switch. This is a little bright and lit up the room at night a tad more than I'd have liked. Elevators, conference rooms, dining options, were all very good and above average. When I left, there was noone outside to call a cab. A police car had cut off access to the driveway and I wheeled my suitcase to the top of the drive. Still noone around, so I walked a few minutes to the subway instead of taking a cab. Not too inconvenient - about a five minute walk.

“Great Location. Adequate Rooms but nothing special” Stayed 3 nights for business as this was the conference hotel. Because the hotel was sold out I was initially put in a room that was FAR from the registration desk in one of the older towers. Although I generally take my own luggage, I wasn't offered the assistance of a bellman and the room was far. Once I arrived in the room, it was so old that I felt depressed. When I complained the front desk person offered me a room in the main tower that was a handicap room. The room was one of the more updated rooms and was closer in to the conference activities. That part was good. But there are so many little things that are not attended to at this property. For instance, the tub spout and water diverter in the tub were not properly installed and both moved A LOT when turning on the shower. The bed was a little hard, but the linens were great and I LOVE the bed and bath lotion that you get at the Marriott. The staff were friendly, although I felt they were overwhelmed with the number of conference attendees. The best value, if you don't want to leave the hotel (it snowed one day so I didn't leave, although there are a lot of GREAT restaurants very close to this property) is a bowl of soup at the cafe and it's over-priced but not as bad as other things. I would stay again if the conference is there again, which it probably would be, but it's not a treat in anyway.

“Für Grundbedürfnisse völlig ausreichend und sauber” Das BW-Loyal-Inn liegt etwas nordwestlich von Downtown, zu Fuß sind es maximal 10 Minuten. Empfang in Ordnung und freundlich , Zimmer sind mehr als nur ausreichend groß, LCD-TV, Telefon, Mikrowelle, Kühlschrank. Bad hat Dusche/Badewanne und ist sauber. WLAN ist kostenlos, man kann aber auch das Business-Center nutzen . Frühstück nicht sehr umfangreich und farblos . Im Fitness-Center leider nur 3 Geräte, darunter Laufband und Crosstrainer. Insgesamt jedoch zufriedenstellend, Frühstück könnte mehr Auswahl haben, ansonsten : Weiter so ! Preis-Leistung passt.

“Disappointing for Holiday Inn Express” I was really disappointed by this Holiday Inn Express. I'm usually really happy with the chain, but found this Boston location to be drab and with a mix of good a bad service. The Marriott next door was actually a little cheaper and all around nicer. From when we checked in, we found the attendant to be unhelpful, unfriendly and even stubborn. When we got to our room, we saw how rundown the place was. The doors and furniture were chipped, dirty, sticky and there was a bad odor that was mixed with a cleaning product smell. Breakfast staff was also mopey. We were told about a 'complimentary' shuttle and when we went to use it, found out our room would be charged. That all being said, we did find our other staff encounters to be pleasant and helpful during the remainder of our stay. The walk to the subway is very short, and the hotel is right off of the highway, which makes it rather convenient. The neighborhood setting is nothing too nice, I'm not sure I would be comfortable walking to the subway stop alone as a young woman dressed in business attire.

“Great value for Trendy Hotel” Let me first say we spent only $234 a night and that was a great value for what we got. The lobby is very dark and glamorous.It's actually a bit much.You could use a flashlight to find the elevator.The lobby is dotted with small lights and guests hunched over them squinting to read. We had a great room with a corner view. The theme seemed to be a luxury liner and the rooms were decked out cabins.They were not large but we don't expect that in NYC. The bed was very comfortable;the shower was great. some quibbles- The theme of low lighting continued in the room with inadequate lights for reading. The Trendy iPad for ordering services is more annoying than helpful. I ordered turn down service via IPad .it never happened.The iPad room service is missing half the menu .. As far as room service,try to avoid it.i ordered a cookie and tea and coffee .it was $46! You are in midtown Manhattan-you can get anything steps from the hotel. All in all, i stayed 4 days and I was very comfortable. Highly recommended ,

“Hopefully green is your favorite color...” First of all, when contemplating this property, make sure that you have the correct Holiday Inn. There is also a Holiday Inn Express just a few blocks away. It can get confusing. Also there is a San Jose Airport Garden Hotel on the same street, which is NOT a Holiday Inn property. Just saying, make sure you end up where you think you're going. This is the only hotel I've ever stayed in where the front desk people do not acknowledge their guests when they walk in the door. This is terrible customer service! I walked in and out of the hotel multiple times, and NOT ONCE did any of the front desk people look up and smile or greet me. Every single time they had their heads down looking at their monitors. Usually when you walk past a front desk, someone will look up and say hi or give you a smile. Not here! Secondly, chartreuse green better be your favorite color. Green is my favorite color, but our room was chartreuse green everywhere! WAAAAYYY TOO MUCH! My daughter is an illustrator/color artist, and she said this is not a restful shade of green. As another guest mentioned, the a/c is very noisy. It cycles on and off all night long and unless you're drunk or exhausted, you won't get much sleep. The walls are very thin, and you will have no privacy on the toilet if the person next door is also on the toilet, if you know what I mean. Hopefully you won't be leaving your rooms at the same time. It could be embarrassing! Although the bathroom is not very large, the good thing is that the sink/vanity is not in the bathroom where the bath/shower and toilet are--it's out in the dressing area, so two people can be getting ready in the morning. Also, as in many newer hotels, the lamps next to the bed have plug-ins in the base so you can charge up your cell phone/electronics on your nightstand and have them within easy reach. The lobby is beautiful and modern looking--and not so much green! The lobby would be much more welcoming with smiling personnel though!

“A total trip” Hotel Havana is like nothing else in San Antonio or elsewhere in Texas that i can think of. It is a deliciously restrained renovation of an old hotel or mansion ( not sure which) and there is nothing gimmicky about the period details that abound. You feel somewhat like you are back in the time of the HBO series Boardwalk Empire. The rooms are sparsely but comfortably furnished. Instead of a minibar we had a pale blue/ green Smeg refrigerator beautifully and thoughtfully stocked. I loved the big format toiletries that cut down on plastic waste. The robes are a beautiful red and very light which is great for the hot Texas climate. Rooms are a bit dark lighting wise but again completely enhanced the feeling that you are in another time and place. How often do you travel anywhere and feel really and truly that the hotel isn't interchangeable with one in Boston, or Atlanta, or NYC? Luxury and ammenities are not everything and the Havana proves that. It's plenty cushy but it's oh so much more. The Ocho cafe is in a greenhouse set on the side and it serves fantastic cocktails and light bar fare and breakfast. All excellent (dont be in a rush- hotel is lightly staffed). The decor is sublime, inspired, surprising, comfortable, uplifting. The bar downstairs is so dark it would be a great place to have an affair! Seriously, it is very mysterious and sexy down there and again the bartending is expert. The daiquiris are out of this world. The location is perfect as far as we were concerned. It is right on the riverwalk, but not the garrish touristy part but on the quiet end of it that leads to the art museum and the Pearl center. It is such a pleasure to walk out the hotel and stroll towards the pearl for lunch at the Sandbar. Great stay. Highly recommend.

“Great westin property” Check in was without incident. At the time, I was a gold and the house was booked at 7%, so I got an upgrade to a deluxe room. Deluxe room was in an interesting triangular shape. Moderately sized (by American standards). Larger than normal room sitting area. HUUUGE bathroom with two sinks, separate shower and tub. All you needed and more. Centrally air conditioned, quiet and worked the way I wanted to. Gym was a great facility. Great great great. Medicine balls, free weights, really good machines. Excellent view of the Houston sprawl. Even though it was 105f, the pool area on the 20th(?) floor was cold. Very windy. Hot tub was not hot. Pool was very cold. Friendly attendant said he would warm up the hot tub, never happened during my 4 night stay. Location: if you are looking for real nice inner city Houston, you're not in the right place. It's in Memorial City. WAY west of downtown and galleria. BUT, for a suburban area, it's nice. Walkway to the mall, with a Beck's Prime in it. Along the freeway, there are TONS of GREAT dining options. You can't go wrong in Houston. Area is safe, but dead at night. No real places to go for a good run. I think they charge for parking, but when I stayed here, the parking arms were up and I didn't have to pay. I'll stay here again if business takes me to Memorial City, but I'd rather stay at sheraton suites near Galleria if I want inner city, galleria, good ice houses, etcetcetc.

“Maybe or maybe not” This was our second time staying at this hotel two months it only confirmed what we thought about the first time. We would stay here again if we were in a pinch, but not if other options were available. The hotel staff need some training. They do not pay attention to the needs of the customers and some are just so indifferent that you wonder why even bother to approach them. Add this to the fact that the hotel is dated and need renovations and you have a mix or average at its best. Only plus right for this hotel is the coffee machines in the room.
“Good location” We had a nice stay at the hotel. The room was really well done but the bathroom was a little dated although it was clean. The location is excellent!

“Milk and cookies before bed - how could you miss that?” Good hotel. Had historic touches, but good sized rooms, updated bathrooms, clean, walking distance to anything in downtown Dallas, great rate - good stay! They had free breakfast, HH, and milk and cookies every day, and it was in an upscale atmosphere. I would absolutely stay here again.

“Just So-So” This is not a bad hotel, just a mediocre one. First the positives: The room was nicely furnished and perhaps a tad more spacious than most. The bellman and concierge were friendly and helpful. The breakfast was nice enough, but not remarkable. Now the not so positives: Upon arrival I was told that my room was vacant but not clean (I arrived before check-in time) but that housekeeping was being alerted so that they could give my room priority. I was asked to come back in two hours, which I did, only to be told the room wasn't ready and had not been vacant when I arrived earlier. When I complained that I was being given conflicting stories and that the promise to give my room priority was not being kept, the clerk got a bit snippy as if I had done something wrong. In the end, I got into the room only a few minutes before an appointment I had, so had only a few minutes to freshen up. So all in all, service was not so great. The hotel is in a very good central location, especially if you are going to the Kimmel Center which is just up the street. But for the price I would have expected better service.

“A nice downtown hotel” If you want a great place to hang your hat in New York, the Hilton New York is it. The location is great. The rooms are small, but comfortable. For a large hotel, the rooms are quiet. You are walking distance to everything. You could pay hundreds more, but why?

“Its not the Ritz, but its not bad either...” I almost didnt book the Inn based on reviews here, but I am glad I did. The location alone is worth the cost of the room. It is in the heart of Lower Queen Anne with plenty of choices for food, drink and entertainment all within less than a 5 minute walk. Of course as with any big city, there are street people around and if that bothers you I suggest only staying in the suburbs or staying home. I always felt safe and comfortable. Many families and europeans were staying here during my stay as well as a few retirees. The rooms are rather basic, they could probably be remodeled and it would make a huge difference but for a 100 year old building designed for retired clergy its all ok. The bed was decent, not great, didnt hurt my back. There was a small kitchenette and a large closet. The bathroom was tiny and there was no place to set your toiletries except the toilet. The tv worked and there was a small a/c unit for the three days a year it gets hot in Seattle. You have to pay for parking or park on the street and get up early to feed the meter. All in all I would defininitely stay here again. The hotel is very European in that it is old, small, basic and full of character. If you require sparkling fixtures and everything brand new, you should probably stay elsewhere. If you love the city and everything the urban landscape has to offer, you would be foolish to stay elsewhere.

“Wonderful” Wonderful.Holiday Inn on Ohio State Unversity Campus is lovely.Went to the game and stayed the night and really enjoyed myself.very nice and wonderful people everywhere me and my husband went.And you will not forget anything with this experiment we had it was amazing.Thank You

“Minutes to anywhere in city and felt like a "real" neighborhood” Stayed at the Hotel Indigo Chelsea over the long Labor Day holiday weekend. Location was fantastic, the #1 subway line just at end of street and used that to get anywhere we needed to go via public transportation. A movie was being filmed on the street the hotel was on and I was called the day before my arrival by hotel staff to let me know of this situation. This was great because I was able to tell the car driver he wouldn't be able to drop us off right in front of the hotel, instead of wondering what was going on and why we couldn't get down the street. Staff was very pleasant and accommodating. The room was spotless, the bed very comfortable. Liked the Aveda bath products and the fact there was a walk-in shower, no tub to climb in or out of. Had a room facing the street and was able to sleep with the window open, some general city noise, but nothing that kept us up at night, and couldn't hear anyone in the rooms next to us. Overall, great stay, great location, great room and great staff!

“A great and quiet overnight stay” Service is top-notched. Everyone we came across was courteous and eager to help. We're traveling with a 15-month-old and needed a way to warm up her milk; front desk promptly sent up an electric kettle (the gentleman from housekeeping actually stayed to make sure the electric kettle works in our room). Valet parking is fast. I know others commented that the decor seems to be in need of updating but I'm happy with how our small suite is laid out. Not much of a view outside our window but we were only staying there for one night so that wasn't a concern (my sister's room actually has a pretty decent view of downtown Philly). Bathroom is huge for a hotel situated in a busy city. Also, was expecting a rough night's sleep since there's a convention in town but it was actually very, very quiet. We'd stay here again.

“Beautiful renovation of historic building in Uptown” Beautiful modern renovation. Really cool flat panel TV in the middle of the room that swiveled to view from bed or sitting area. The lobby bar appears to be original to the hotel, and is a great place to meet friends or family when visiting in the Dallas area. Close to downtown and American Airlines Center, the nightlife in Uptown, and a great variety of new restaurants and shops.

“Nice hotel, great staff but need more front doorman to keep from being accosted every time you step out” Wish they had staff out front all the time ...every time I went out someone was asking me for money. One of my fellow travelers got a big blob of white shoe shine spray on his black shoes by a man while he was trying to pay his taxi fare. It is too bad because it is a pretty hotel, beautiful bar and nice staff. Maybe that is just Chicago ...who know ....

“Old hotel in decent shape and a great location” Hotel is old but in good shape. We stayed in one of the two room King suites on the third floor away from the freeway. It was nice to have the extra space of the suite but there was only a couch (pull out) and a desk chair to sit in. Carpet was fairly new, pillows inconsistent. Room had a mini refrigerator but TVs were the old kind, Internet VERY SLOW. I mentioned this to the front desk staff and they told me it was a bandwidth issue. If you need Internet access, I would not choose to stay here, it is way too slow to do much. Air conditioning/heating units separately controlled in each room, they are next to bed and blow on the bed when on. Breakfast area was small. When hotel was busy, it was difficult to get around and seating was very limited. Nice that they had three waffle makers, breakfast staff did a great job hustling around and taking care of everything. The earlier you go, the fewer people. Very easy to get on and off of the 8 freeway and to 805 and 163 north and south. Lots of restaurant and shopping options within a mile. Not sure if I will stay here again but if you need a decent hotel with breakfast, and don't need Internet, you could do worse.

“週末が狙い目かな” ホテル代が高いNY、ここも平日はかなりの料金だが週末は安いレートが出ることが多いので狙ってみれば?8番街でバスの停留所も近くで(北行きだが)、地下鉄の駅にも直ぐで、又セントラルパークやブロードウエーの劇場街にも便利な立地。部屋は決して狭くなく窓からの眺めはたいしたことは無いが居心地は悪くない。 このホテルに泊まればスーパーやデリも近くで困ることは無い。今まで合計4泊ほどしている。スタッフは決して愛想よくは無いがNYではこれが普通か。 室内金庫は無かったように記憶している。フロント横で預けたように思うが定かではない。女性が泊まるのにもそんなに心配するようなホテルではないことは確かだ。 タイムズスクエア周辺、34丁目からセントラルパークまでの範囲、8番街から5番街までならバス、タクシーや地下鉄に乗らなくても徒歩で十分ホテルと往復できる。

“What a find!!!” We wanted to stay at the Comfort Inn based on most of the reviews we read here and we were not disappointed. We booked our 3 night stay through 'hoterls r us' and got a rate of £53/night (approx $106) which is brilliant for a city centre hotel. As our flight had been delayed we phoned from the airport to inform them we would be checking in late and the staff on reception were really friendly, something we found to be true for the duration of our stay. Our room #1667, was a good size room in the corner of the building. The bed was huge and so comfortable, we had windows on 2 sides and a desk wrapping round the corner of the room. The bathroom was a nice size too and the room was spotlessly clean and nicely decorated. We didn't hold out much hope for the free continental breakfast but were very pleasantly surprised. Everyday there was a choice of scrambled eggs, potatoes, bacon or sausage and waffles or pancakes. This was alongside muffins, toast, English muffins, bagels, yoghurt, fruit, juice, tea and coffee. A good start to the day. The location of the hotel is a big plus. You are within 2 minutes of 16th St Mall and its free shuttle bus, 5 minutes of the State Capitol, US Mint and Denver Art Museum. A 10 minute bus ride takes you to Cherry Creek Mall for the best of Denvers shopping. All in all an excellent downtown hotel which offers fantastic value for money. We would definitely stay here again if we returned to Denver.

“Great Thanksgiving week at Doubletree Times Square” Just completed a 5 night stay at Doubletree Times Square. What a great time we had! Hotel is very handy for subway, theater, and lots of things are within walking distance from hotel. We were there to see Thansgiving parade and from our room 1704 which was not a Parade View we were able to see it just fine. Room was spacious and super clean. Staff were very freindly and accomodiating. Breakfast was provided for 2 because I am Hilton Honors Gold. I wouldn't have paid 27.95 each for this but it was a nice treat every morning just to have to tip. Its so nice to have the extra room, fridge, microwave. The hotel also provided lovely thick terry robes. We will definately return to this hotel our next trip to New York. I can't say enough good things about it!

“Average Hotel....Would Not Recommend It.” Stayed at the Renaissance with my husband for one night in September 2011. The hotel is nothing special. The rooms are quite old. The beds were really nice though. The airconditioning in the room was very oud. The hotel provides Aveeda products in the bathroom which I really enjoyed. Overall, our stay was fine; there weren't any major problems. However, I thought the hotel fell short of what I expect from Renaissance Hotels. This hotel is a standard airport property with pretty bland style. The service was fine. The room was OK -- comfortable bed; the rest of the decor was average and seemed a little worn. I wouldn't recommend it..much better hotels in LA. Stayed February 2010, traveled as a couple

“Not the Best Experience” The Hilton Garden Inn is a new hotel that has nice amenities. Unfortunately, our stay there was not as pleasant as we would have hoped. Shortly after checking in, they asked us to change rooms to accommodate another group. The person at the front desk indicated that our new room would be nicer, with views of the mountains. Our new room had views of the mountains, but had not been cleaned properly. It had red stains on the mattress and carpet, a portion of the carpet that was stiff from some kind of substance (perhaps the substance responsible for the red stains). We also found a hair band with someone else's hair in it on the floor. This did not make us very confident about the general cleanliness of our room or the hotel more generally. They offered us free breakfast in exchange for our changing rooms. We had breakfast plans and asked if they would instead give us free parking (they require valet parking, which at $28 a night is a bit on the expensive side). When we went to check out the next morning, they charged us for parking. They did remove the parking charge when we pointed out what had happened, but only because we were able to tell them the name of the person who had agreed to give us free parking. As a result of these experiences, we would probably not return to the Hilton Garden Inn Denver Downtown. The hotel does offer free wireless Internet, which we found worked very well during our stay.

“Great Stay” We just spent a long weekend in San Diego and had a great stay at the Hilton Bayfront. This was our first stay and we loved the hotel. It was very busy but the staff was always nice and friendly. They have a great spa and nice fitness center. The pool looked awesome so in warmer weather that would be great as well. As a Diamond Hilton Honors member we received free breakfast at Starbucks each morning as a perk. The location and view are great and I would recommend to anyone.

“Great Hotel - good location” Hotel has lovely rooms, which are large and have nice furnishings. Rooms were quiet. The concierge provided some decent recommendations, but the restaurant choices were very safe and "usual". I'm not sure I would have found anything new or trendy through the concierge. I was a bit surprised by the fact that the coffee shop in the hotel closes in the early afternoon, as many guests were still wanting to buy water and snacks. The staff at the coffee shop tried to shoo a patron with a service dog (a very clearly marked service dog) out of the coffee shop for having a dog on the premises.

“Perfect Location. Parking a Nightmare” I live in NYC, so I get that big city hotels are expensive. The Westin Copley is no exception. It is a really nice hotel, though, and it's location makes it worth a premium. The room was beautiful, with a great view. The bedding was awesome. Two things annoyed me-- the cost of Internet access and the cost of parking. I tried to do street parking, as it was the weekend, but that is no easy feat. If possible, go to Boston by public transportation, leave your laptop at home, and enjoy the excellent location of the Copley.

“I wish I could love this place like everyone else” I visit New York every year for personal theater trips, and I usually stay at The Michelangelo, which is a wonderful hotel with staff that treat their regular guests almost like family. But, I wanted to try something new on my last trip this past summer, and given the reviews and word of mouth about the Elysee, how could I refuse? I booked the hotel, and was really excited about staying here based on the glowing reviews. Unfortunately, my experience was anything but what I was expecting from a supposedly fine hotel. The problems actually started the moment I walked in the front door. When I reserved my room, I also booked transportation service to pick me up at the airport and take me to the hotel. I was quoted a price for this that seemed quite reasonable. So, the car takes me to the hotel, and when I arrive at the lobby to check in, the guy at the desk quotes me an entirely different and much more expensive price than I was promised over the phone. I brought this up, showed them the price I was quoted, and the guy at the desk simply said he would "look into it". I never heard back on this matter again. Every time I brought it up, I got the same answer that they would "look into it". I experienced a number of problems with the staff during the week that I stayed there. Many of them did not seem interested in helping me, or did not even seem to want to help at all. What follows are some examples of the "service" I received while staying at the Elysee. -The first night, I return from a performance, only to find that there has been no turn down service in my room for the night. The housekeeping staff had completely skipped my room. I call down to the front desk, and they send someone up to do the turn down service. This wouldn't be so bad if it only happened once, but it happened again later on in the week. For some reason, the housekeeping staff kept on skipping my room, even though I had no "do not disturb" signs outside of my door. At one point, I talked to the woman who arrived after I had called down, and asked her why she had not come earlier. I was not confrontational with her. I was polite when I asked. She became very defensive, and lied to my face, saying she had spoken to me earlier, and I supposedly told her I did not want my room cleaned. She seemed angry with me. When I told the front desk about the woman's rude behavior, once again, all I got was "we'll look into it", only to never hear more on the subject. -The first morning I'm there, I go to the area where the free breakfast is served each morning. (Which is quite good, I must admit, and probably the best part of the hotel.) I'm looking at the wide variety of pastries they have on display, and ask the woman behind the counter for help about identifying some of them, since they are not labeled. The woman responded by saying, "I'm sorry, I'm new here", and simply walked away. The least she could have done was find someone who could help me. That same morning, I was handed a bowl by another staff member for my cereal, only to find there was a dead fly inside it. She didn't even look to see if the bowl was clean, she just handed it to me. It's a good thing I wasn't an elderly person with poor eyesight or something, or I would have received some extra protein with my Cheerios. -The overall attitude of the staff in general seemed to be one of indifference. I admit, some were polite and worked well with me, but there were a lot more who just seemed to think I wasn't worth their time. One day, the elevators broke down due to the fact there was a short energy problem in the city. (It was 100 degrees that day, and with everyone in the city blasting their AC units, there was bound to be problems.) I walked down the stairs to the front desk to ask what the problem was, and generally got the run around until I was able to find someone who was actually willing to talk to me and tell me about the situation. The elevator clearly was not the fault of the hotel's, it was the staff's attitude that bothered me. As for the hotel itself, it really is nothing special. I knew going in that it was a very old building, and I admit, was looking forward to it. But, the hotel itself is not just old, it seems very dated, worn, and not that inviting with its dark hallways. The suite they put me in seemed very tired. Nothing really stood out about it, the furnishings looked out of date, and the individual rooms were somewhat small, especially the bathroom. I'm so glad I traveled alone, as there's no way more than one person could use that mini closet they call a bathroom at the same time. So, why am I giving this place a 2 instead of a 1? Well, fortunately, the hotel's manager listened to a lot of my complaints. He had a private meeting with me in a room where he sympathized and agreed with many of the problems I had, was patient and understanding, and ultimately gave me a reduction on my bill due to the number of complaints I had with the staff. He was apologetic, and interested in what I had to say, which is something I had been missing the rest of my stay. I truly do appreciate his time and concern, and I hope it showed when I was speaking to him. I really wanted to love the Elysee. I was so excited to stay here based on the reviews on this site. My greatest wish is that I could be joining the chorus of raves this hotel seems to get. But, I cannot in any good judgment recommend this hotel. I was severely disappointed by the service, the staff, and the hotel itself. There are bright spots to be found, obviously. The free breakfast is wonderful for the most part, and the free Internet is great when it works. During the week I was there, they kept on having problems with the computer. It seemed to be off with the "out of order" sign placed over the monitor more than it was on. Needless to say, I will not be returning. I'll be sticking with The Michelangelo from now on, which not only has a much better location than the Elysee for theater and major attractions, but has a staff that actually makes you feel welcome, and "old hotel" charm without being tired or worn out. The free breakfast may not be as diverse as the one at the Elysee, but considering how superior it is in every other category, there's no question it's the place I belong, and not at the Elysee.
“Bem localizado” É um tipico hotel da cadeia Days Inn. Bem localizado com quartos razoaveis e uma boa relação qualidade/preço. Sem duvida uma boa opção!

“Stay away, not very nice” We booked the Crestwood for two nights through Orbitz. Unfortunately, after just one night we "punted" and "abandoned ship". The bathroom floor was sticky and we could not sleep due to noise from the elevator (if you get Rm 133, ask for another!) Other rooms may be better, but I'd rather you not take the chance.

“A good choice in a loud neighborhood” As a former New Yorker, I tend to dislike Times Square. This place was the best-priced option for me on a recent trip and I was pleased with how it worked out. Despite the location, it was very quiet inside. The guest room floors are all key-card controlled so no nonsense with wayward tourists or revelers. If you walk out the NW exit of the 49th St. N/Q/R subway, you're virtually at the door, so that really helps in terms of getting around. Room was nice, though the shades MUST be drawn tightly at night if you cannot bear light peeking through. The iron in my room almost worked, so that could have been better. It does have the amenities you expect from a Renaissance... nice finishes and products in the room. Great bed. If you are traveling as a tourist, you must eat/drink in the lobby lounge that faces out with a full view of Times Square. You're literally looking at it right down the Pike... a great famous scene.

“Worn Out Hotel with a Five Star Location” A great location near everything that makes Chicago a great city. The hotel, however, needs a complete makeover. The lobby is worn and cramped and hot. Ditto the corridors. The room was just okay, nothing special. The equipment in the fitness room has to be 20 years old and someone removed the tv from the cardio area (but left the fixture that was supposed to be holding it attached to the wall).

“Very good hotel” The Hilton Back Bay is a really nice hotel. Good location in the "Back Bay" area, near the subway station. The room are big enough, the bed and pillow are very confortable. The staff was nice and helpfull. The only "small" problem is the WI-FI : if you want to have internet in your room you have to pay more than 14$ per day! But you can go with your laptop in the buisness center and it's free there. If you don't have a laptop there are 5 computers (with big screens!) in the buisiness center too! The breakfast is expensive but you can have a "starbucks" coffee and some brownies or cookies in the lobby for cheap prices. I'll definitely go there again if I'm in Boston!

“Nice Hotel” Stayed here while visiting family. Nicer than some Fairfield inns I have stayed in. Bed was very comfortable,very clean room. Breakfast was the usual at these types of hotels. We will stay here again!

“Great Find!” Recently had a lovely stay at The New Yorker. I chose this hotel last minute when coming in to the city to see a concert at Madison Square Garden. It is literally one block away from the back/8th avenue entrance to MSG/Penn station. Talk about convienent! I was a little hesitant as the price through hotels.com was much cheaper than any pace Ive stayed in the city & the closeness to Penn station. I was pleasantly suprised how wrong I was! The hotel was very nice. Check in was a breeze, the lady who checked us in was very nice, sorry I cant remember her name but she was very helpful & friendly. The room I had was 3312. It had a great view of the Empire State Building right outside the window & I did NOT pay for a empire view room. The other window looked out on to MSG. The room was very clean & comfortable. Some might say it was a bit small but by NYC standards there was plenty of room. The beds were very comfortable. The bathroom was small but immaculate & bright. The hotel has a diner attached called the Tick Tock. We had a great dinner there, classic diner fare but big portions and tasty. Breakfast was also good, the diner is always packed with people which is a good sign. Overall, a nice suprise and I think a great spot for tourists.

“Worth considering, especially for families” Family just needed a clean place to stay overnight in the San Diego area over the weekend. This place more than fit the bill. Although we reserved a standard two bed room and were using a Marriott voucher, they upgraded us to a suite with a King bed + bath, a separate living area and full kitchen and an upstairs queen bed + second bath in a loft area. Sweet suite! This might have been because the hotel was not particularly crowded and/or because they did not have our reserved room ready when we arrived at around 2:30 or 3 pm. Or, possibly because when we arrived, there was a man who was arguing with one of the clerks very loudly and (it seemed to me) quite unreasonably. After the man left, the clerks apologized but i thought they handled the disgruntled customer very professionally and calmly. I sympathized with them and I think they appreciated that. In any event, we stepped out for a snack and when we returned, they had our suite ready for us. My teenaged daughter loved the idea of having her own loft bed and bathroom. We loved the extra room and used the full fridge to cool sodas and waters, used the microwave to cook up the complimentary bag of popcorn and used the range to heat up some water for a cup-a noodle snack that night. I also used the pool because it was a particularly hot day. the pool was pretty utilitarian but it did the trick to cool me down. The complex is long and narrow with many buildings on either side of a central walkway. The path has some basic but nice plants around it. As all Residence Inns seem to have, there also is a small sports court with a basketball hoop. Residence inns also offer a free breakfast buffet and this one seemed to have enough seating/tables for comfort. The fare is pretty standard: scrambled eggs, potatotes, pastries, oatmeal, cold cereal, waffle maker, yogurt, juice and hot drinks. The hotel is called "central" and it is fairly well located if you have a car. (not much to walk to; next to the freeway). My guess is the pricing is competitive with places on Hotel Circle but you get more than most of those hotels -- a kitchen, seating area and breakfast, in addition to free parking. I believe if you stay during the week, there is a manager's reception with what looked like heavy snacks; you can probably cut down on dinner costs by eating up at the reception. (None during the weekend, though.) And, if you reserve a suite, families ought to be pretty happy.

“Stay on the Freedom Trail” Great location if you want to see Boston. The Omni Parker House is a hostoric site in itself but you can walk out the door and visit the historic sites on the Freedom Trail. The propoerty is an older hotel. The service was excellent and my room was huge. I did see some of the smaller rooms and you want to be sure and verify your room prior to staying. Some of the interior rooms are tiny! The room was everything I needed and then some. The service was very timely. Every morning I received coffee service as requested and the daily papers. Great location! I walked to every site that I wanted to see.

“Nice Hotel, great location” Very nice hotel in a great location. The McPhearson Square metro stop is about a block away. The White House is just around the corner. You can walk to the national mall in about 10 to 15 minutes, and we also walked to China town for dinner. We had a King room, and it was very large, and had big HD TV. Bathroom has a sparate shower and tub. Service was great, I had no complaints and would stay here again with no hesitation.

“Way too loud, stay there to party” We were placed in a room that overlooked the pool which we thought was great, until we realized that meant noise streaming into our top floor room all night long. If you are young and want to party this is a good choice, otherwise look elsewhere. We requested a quieter room and were told that there were none.

“Not Bad” This property is rated 1 or 2 stars depending on which site you use. I noticed when researching this property there weren't too many recent reviews and that is probably because this hotel is primarily used by travellers for flight departures and layovers since it is only 5 minutes form airport (no airplane noise) and that is exactly what we used it for. I booked this hotel using my trip rewards in order to be close for our early flight out the next day. My husband, two sons and I were very happy with our overnight accomodations. The room we stayed in was clean and was just like the pictures represented by their hotel pictures. Even though the rooms have exterior facing doors(motel) we felt safe on the 2nd floor, because you can't enter the 2nd floor up the outside steps w/o a room key, nor can you enter from the steps inside the lobby after 11pm, because the doors are kept locked. The hotel has a pool which we did not use and offers a continental breakfast as early as 6am consisting of bagels, cereal, milk, juice, coffee/hot cocoa and apples. If that doesn't appeal to you there is an IHOP and Krispy Kreme next door. I spoke to two staff members regarding our reservation and both were nice and professional. For an overnight stay at a reasonable price, I believe most would be pleased w/ these accomodations.

“Reasonably-priced location near airport, harbor and downtown San Diego.” i have stayed at this property twice in the past year,and have been pleased each time. The s-x-story hotel offers a free breakfast with waffles, free underground parking, and most rooms have balconies. Even though I am a non-smoker, I requested a smoking room on the top floor so that I wouldn't be disturbed by people above me - there were no problems with smoke odor in the room. Staff is pleasant, and if you have a car, the location is within a ten-minute drive to downtown or to the freeway network. Rooms are pleasant, although a little old. Beds are comfortable, producing a good night's sleep.

“Lusso turistico” Non si puo' certamente dire che il Plaza non sia un hotel di lusso: é il solo hotel al mondo ad avere l'intera rubinetteria in oro, a disposizione degli ospiti c'é un butler personale a disposizione 24/24, la camera viene rifatta su richiesta piu volte al giorno, etc...ma l'ambiente é quello che si potrebbe respirare all'interno di un museo e non di un hotel Naturalmente, essendo un monumento storico, la hall é sempre piena di turisti che fanno foto e si aggirano dappertutto Questo era immaginabile ma non pensavo che la sicurezza potesse essere cosi scarsa : per salire di piano in acsensore non bisogna neanche passare la carta della camera... Lo staff é poco sorridente,... Il tanto decantato butler - che abbiamo incontrato solo quando ci ha accompagnato in camera e quando abbiamo fatto il check out - si lamentava che era faticoso trasportare i vagagli a causa della moquette che rende piu difficile spostare il carrello...e quando gli ho chiesto se l hotel disponeva di piscina mi ha risposto con aria di sufficienza che si tratta di un hotel storico dunque senza piscina (l'equazione hotel storico = no piscina, non ha alcun senso) Check in lento e check out rapidissimo, senza tanti convenevoli Carissimo il parking a 65$ la notte L'unica persona dello staff che invece ho trovato molto simpatico e efficace é stato il concierge Al costo del Plaza potete sicuramente trovare meglio Vi consiglio Peninsula o Four Seasons, che a servizio sono sempre imbattibili

“Aloft Austin--a neon travelodge” You'll know, from my other reviews, that I go to hotels for cocktails and meetings and holidays and all sorts of things but my basic priority is SLEEP! The Aloft is not quiet. It's the sort of place lots of screaming sorority girls reconvene 5 years after graduation for FUN weekends! OH HEY GIRL! SCREEEEAM! It goes like that. This would be ok if the hotel had invested in proper sound insulation and doors that were more than a millimegtre thick. As it was I had to hush people. The doors and wall are so thin I coulkd hear people's alarms going off in the morning. The staff were pleasant enough and v helpful when it came ot getting masses of boring business papers printed out. But the noise is...well, too much. A shame as the basic conept is nice and I applaud their eco efforts.

“Affordable and great location!” I stayed here when it was Jurys and the location was so great, I thought I would give it another try. This time, the rate was amazing (through a third party website) and when I called the hotel to ask if we could come a night earlier and have the same rate honored they agreed and were very pleasant. The room was large, clean and quiet. The pub downstairs is a great place to meet for a drink. The hotel "scene" in Boston isn't that great - the W and Nine Zero are popular but sparse and poor in service. The Fairmont Copley and Park Plaza are from another era. I would definitely recommend staying here to visitors of any nature.

“Decent” This was a decent hotel and I would stay here again. I would not however, come here for an anniversary weekend or anything like that. This hotel is great if you have a conference at the hotel or want to stay in close proximity to the airport. The rooms were clean and I actually liked the view of the runway and sometimes found myself just watching airplanes take off and land. Check-in was not easy as I tried to check-in early – and they had been notified of that. When I first arrived, I asked the young woman behind the counter if I could check in early.
