She then proceeded to explain that check-in hadn’t started yet, etc. I stopped her and said I obviously understood that as I just said I wanted to check-in “early” and that the person who had arranged my accommodations had asked about it and was told that it was a possibility. Well this young woman told me to come back – like 3 – 4 hours later. She made no proactive attempt to help me – she didn’t even check to see if a room was ready. So I suggested that she take down my cell phone number and perhaps think about checking and then calling me if something came available. In the meantime, I went to the restaurant, Andiamo, which is decent, and then came back an hour later. A very helpful woman named Latifah was there this time and as soon as I said,”Can I check in early?,” she checked, found a room and handed me a key. Anyway, this type of service is not surprising at a chain. Also, the restaurant, as I said, was decent. They weren’t good with details – each time I ate at Andiamo, I spotted small irritants – like dirty silverware, crumbs on the table they sat me at, dirty cups, straws in my drinks that were generously decorated with lint and other unknown particles, etc. So I’d have to ask for clean silverware (I like my forks without caked on, dishwasher baked food, thank you very much). Overall, my stay was as to be expected. Would stay there again if necessary but this would not be the place to go for a “special” weekend.

“Perfect in Every Way” Great hotel. Friendly, professional staff. Comfortable room/bed. Room service way better than most and not expensive. Real turkey (real turkey!!) in the club sandwich. All around really good and close to airport/rental card place.

“Sophisticated l'art de vivre at Sofitel” I recently stayed at the Sofitel Lafayette Square, after a superb time at the Water Tower property in Chicago a while ago. Both hotels deserve their ratings and reviews on Tripadvisor without a doubt. I was upgraded to a deluxe corner room, which was spacious, super clean, lovely designed, with the signature marble bathroom, just like the Water Tower. The beds are probably one of the nicest features. No flatscreen TVs as of yet, if you really care about that. Getting to the hotel from Reagan Airport and getting around Washington is a breeze, the McPherson square metro station is just a block away. The concierge can arrange a towncar to take you to Dulles if needed. As most reviewers have said, the most noteworthy asset of this and other Sofitels is their staff - warm, polite, sincere, service-oriented without being overbearing. Internet is available for a charge in the rooms, but there is a business center just off the lobby with complimentary computers, internet, and printer. LeBar is a nice place for a coffee or cocktail, I did not have the opportunity to try the restaurant. Check the Sofitel website for rates that offer great value for what you get. Would recommend it to anyone needing a hotel in DC.

“Wonderful location although a bit expensive” I went to Charlotte for weekend getaway and decided to stay at the Omni. It did not disappoint. The location was incredible- right in the middle of all the action at the Epicenter and the Square. All the sports venues are within walking distance. There's a train station next door. The bar and restaurant in the hotel are great. Didn't use the fitness center but it looks nice. My room needed a makeover but I guess that's 25+ years of usage. So- keeping that all in mind, for two hundred a night I didn't think it was a great value. I would definitely go back if I could find a better rate.

“3rd visit” Excellant as usual...we got same room... Wine hour...lovely coffee...super friendly hotel Recommend Kimpton Hotel chain to everyone Join there Intouch program to get $10 mini bar treat Even have water in Lobby with lemon or lime in... great Bell Captain...always so professional Ive stayed in 4 Kimpton hotels...they are all Excellant

“Good deal, great location” The Holiday Inn Capitol is an excellent hotel in a great location in Washington, D.C. It is one block from the Smithsonian Air and Space Museum and within walking distance of the other museums and the Capitol. Although it is not cheap, it is resonable for Washington. We've stayed here many times and found the rooms always clean, comfortable and quiet. There is a Starbucks connected to the lobby, and McDonald's, Quizno's, a deli and a CVS drugstore within a block. We've tried several hotels in Washington, and this seems to be the best deal.

“Very, very nice new hotel...” Stayed here one night first week of March, 07 while attending a conference. This hotel was originally designed/destined to be an Embassy Suites. Apparently, during construction, ownership and flag changed, and it's now an independent. That didn't stop it from being a first rate hotel. Rooms are a Spanish Mission/Texas design, placed in an Embassy Suites footprint. Solid furnishings and amenities, fast internet (both wifi and wired), and 2 tv sets. Linens (sheets and towels) better than standard, but not exceptional. Employees were very helpful with early check in and late check out. Might suggest that the gift shop carry more newspapers... they sent me next door to the Westin for a WSJ! Location is on the Riverwalk, but away from the central bar/restaurant district (see my Hyatt review). The big Starbucks is two blocks away, but be careful which side of the road you walk on... especially at night/early morning. Would happily stay here again, very nice property. The newness (although it's now 14 months old) is still there, and it is really a good looking hotel. Coupled with excellent staff, it scores well with me.

“Great neighborhood” The neighborhood surrounding the Hotel Madera is lively and a lot of fun - from the folks milling about DuPont circle to the beautiful people sitting outside eating and drinking in the many nearby restaurants. My room was large, clean, and comfortable. The small balcony was nice and offered a great view of the area including the Egyptian embassy is right across the street. A few pluses & minuses: (+) The front desk staff is fantastic. Very friendly and eager to please. (-) Strangely, the valet does not appear to hang around outside much. On several occasions, I had to go inside to find someone to park my car. (-) The bathroom is tiny!!! One has to step next to the stool in order to close the door. (+) The Firefly lounge restaurant makes a great breakfast! (+) The location is great if you are traveling via Metro. If you are driving - not so much. Parking is a nightmare, traffic is a pain. Overall, I had a great stay and will definitely stay here again.

“Best Choice Outside of Downtown” We visited the Westin Domain again after a year's absence, and had a very good experience. Much improved over last year. This is almost certainly the best Austin hotel outside of Downtown. It is a bit isolated, unless you are visiting the Domain itself, or continuing northwest for a camp pickup, as we were. The Domain is one of those New Urban developments that tries to bring together fancy shops, restaurants and a bit of a street scene, all with new construction. The Domain is pleasant, and the shops and restaurants are good. But, it is not near the main attractions of Austin. The Westin is, as mentioned, high quality. The quality of the bed, linens, bath, etc was high; as good as the Westin brand gets. The front desk service was also very good. Never saw the concierge desk occupied, but the the Front Desk folks did everything you needed. The lounge area is comfortable, although a bit spartan. All in all, one of the better hotels in Austin.

“Terrible!!!” I stayed at this hotel in early August for a Tennis tournament & it was absolutely awful. Housekeeping did a terrible job on cleaning our room--never wiped down any surfaces, lousy vacuum job, hairs still in bathtub, etc.... The front desk staff is completely incompetent--I received late wake-up calls each day I was in the hotel & on my last day at the hotel I went down to use their "business center" which consists of a lousy fax machine & 1 computer that everyone at the property is trying to use---they even having a waitlist for the computer----totally unheard of!!!! Nick, Anthony and Roberta at the front desk are extremely rude, including Nick--he obviously hates his job & needs to get a life/job outside of the hotel business. The hotel also has a cricket/bug problem, as they are all over in the lobby dead and in the corridors of the rooms. The floors in the hallways of the room are also dirty & littered with trash. The hotel is grose & poorly maintained--I work in a hotel in New York & this type of business is completely unacceptable!!!! I WILL NEVER STAY AT THIS HOTEL AGAIN!!!!!

“Beautiful Upscale Hotel with Great Service” My company based in Houston has a corporate rate here, recently changed from the Houstonian, and this was my first stay at this or any Omni. I was here for business and I had a great experience. I highly recommend joining their free Select Guest program. I did so before I arrived, and was pleased to find that gave me the ability to pick up my key from a select guest board immediately on arrival, a free beverage tray and paper delivered to me in the mornings, airline miles, etc. The room decor was comfortable and very clean and quiet. I loved the huge bathroom and the bed was as good as the heavenly beds most hotels tout these days. My room overlooked the grounds and pool which are very nice. There is a nice pool with waterfalls and daily chair service and a black swan resides on in a the pond that is near the pool area. I ate dinner one evening in their Cafe on the Green restaurant and enjoyed a perfect 4star quality filet mignon meal and glass of wine for $40 including tip - not a bad deal for a hotel by any means. Most importantly, every single person I encountered at the Omni provided excellent, bend over backwards service with a smile. It was quite impressive! The only potential negative is the parking. The self parking garage is right across from the entrance and is $9/night, which is not terrible. However on my 2nd night here, that garage was full and they directed me to another garage on the property. But after pulling in and seeing how far I would have had to walk in the dark, I decided against i, being a solo female traveler, and instead ponied up for the valet. However on review of my bill today, it does not appear I've been charged for any parking, so it would appear that you also don't have to pay for parking as a Select Guest either. Overall, it was an excellent stay and I look forward to this being my home away from home whenever I head to Houston.

“World's smallest shower” This was a business trip so we loved the location. It was close enough for us to walk to our first meeting. It was nice to be surrounded by so many restaurants and near Boston Commons. I liked being near the prime downtown shopping areas too. But the hotel rooms were unbeliveably small. The room was just large enough for a full sized bed. And the bathroom was really small. I've never seen a shower (no room for a tub) that narrow before! It is an old, elegant historic hotel with a great history. It used to be a Statler Hotel back in the 1920's. It has that old, grand hotel look about it. The room was very clean and nicely decorated (except for the big old TV perched on a wooden stand). A room that small really should have flat screen Tv bolted to the wall. I was afraid I might bump the TV off the narrow stand going to the bathroom. I could also lie in bed and listen to the hum of the subway. It didn't bother me but it did bother my coworker who was one floor higher than me. If you don't care about the size of the room it's an OK place to stay. I give it thumbs up for the location & cleanliness. But it's also a bit pricy and parking is expensive too. There is a parking lot down the street that costs a little bit less. Not many places to park inexpensively downtown.

“Tolles Hotel, tolle Preise” Endlich wieder einmal ein Hotel, das mich restlos überzeugt hat: Die Zimmer zum Central Park raus sind zwar nicht riesig, aber cosy, haben sehr moderne und saubere Bäder, Internet läuft auch gut (obwohl bei 700 USD pro Nacht die 14.95 eingeschlossen sein sollten) und der einzige Schwachpunkt ist die schwache Schallisolation. Denn vor dem Haus geht die Central Park St. durch und ab morgens um 4 machen halt die Strassenreiniger usw. ihren Job mit lärmigen Fahrzeugen. Wer hier unterkommt, sollte unbedingt das Package inklusive Lounge nehmen, die ist der ideale Rückzugsraum nach 1 langen Business-Tag. Spa ist etwas zu aufdringlich von La Prairie gesponsort, aber der (teure) Service ist gut (hier: Schwedische Massage). So oder so - das Haus ist eine gute Alternative für Leute (wie mich), die dem alten Plaza 2 Blocks weiter nachtrauern und das Waldorf-Astoria einfach nur schlecht finden.

“Unimpressive” Was not impressed with this hotel. Average is the best thing I can say for it. The rooms were ok the sheets were not the best and the pillows were poly fiber filled. Might as well say "Generic" on the outside of the building. The only reason I would not recommend this hotel is because there are better choices in that area.

“A Classy Refuge in The Big City” My wife and I spent 4 days in November at the Hotel Bel Air. We arrived around noon and our room was not yet available, we were treated very cordially and we chose to enjoy lunch on the Terrace. This open air restaurant has the same menu as the dining room, but is an oasis of flowering plants and classic California design. The service was beyond compare without being smothering. The first room that we were shown, 135, was on a main walking area, although well laid out we were put off by the proximity to a walkway, in hindsight it would not have mattered as despite a high occupancy we barely ever saw another guest. We were quickly moved to room 115, a premium room with a nice patio with fountain. Not only does this hotel offer a quiet escape from the bustle of the city just a few blocks away, but it also soothes the soul in its gentle charm and the easy service that seems to flow naturally from the outstanding staff. We don't look like a-listers (although we are in our corner of the world!), but we felt that we received the star treatment throughout our stay. No request was too small (like pressing a jacket within 30 minutes of dinner) or town car service to the Getty Museum, discretion was beyond reproach (in fact, noone ever addressed my wife as "Mrs.", they only called her Madame and used my name - I guess in case she was someone other than my wife! I hadn't noticed but she certainly did. There were some stars and influential people staying at the hotel and eating at the restaurant during our time there, but everyone received the same treatment - I can't repeat enough how special you feel being at the Hotel Bel Air - from the valet to the gardener, everyone is in on the star treatment. You notice it even more when you leave the little neighborhood of Bel Air and realize that you are just blocks from the 405 freeway. Don't ask how much it costs. It has a high economic cost, but it delivers excellent value for the dollar. No where else in LA will you feel so welcome. You will be at home in a wealthy friend's estate at the Hotel Bel Air.

“Funky, Fun and Noisy” I stayed here for 2 nights with my girlfriends. Standard room had 2 double beds, see through shower with no door and concrete floors. (Felt a little like a very modern, tricked out dorm room). This was ok for us, but I wouldn't want to stay here with someone I wasn't really comfortable with. The staff here was awesome. Super nice at the front desk, they couldn't be more helpful with dinner and bar recommendations, and getting us taxis. The magic bars at turndown time were also a nice touch. We were here for a weekend of drinking and having fun, so we were not overly bothered by the noise. Like the other reviews say, this hotel is in the middle of all the action -- it is a very very noisy hotel. Lots of noise on the street from the bar scene, and garbage pick up early Sat morning. Ear plugs didn't really help. I would come back again for the same sort of party weekend. I would not stay here if one had expectations of a restful weekend. I would also try to get a suite/room with king beds.

“Great business hotel - probably not the best choice for tourists” I stayed here for one night when working in the area. It is on Lexington around 49th street. The location was perfect for me because I was working nearby, but I ended up changing hotels because my husband was coming in for the weekend and it was kind of a hike to the touristy things. It is about 2 blocks from the subway station and I never had a problem getting a taxi, so it is fairly easy to get anywhere. The hotel was nice and up-to-date and my room was fairly large for a NYC hotel room. I have read other reviews about the noise, but I thought it was very quiet (I did have a room on the back of the building). I would stay here again.

“one of the best moderate hotels” Stayed Nov 2008 with my dog. Rooms are nice and spacious. Staff is excellent...checks id to make sure non-guests and uninvited guests get in. Complimentary breakfast refreshments. Great location, near Times Square...close to Virgin Megastore. Toiletries were L'Occtaine and other brands. Staff is prompt and will fix problems right away. Great decor and lots of furniture, but roomy and comfortable. Will definitely stay there next time I visit NYC.

“Incredibly pleased!” I will admit that I stumbled upon this hotel and sure glad that I did! Hilton created a partnership with the College of Hospitality at the University of Houston and as a result the hotel is both a teaching ground as well as a platform of perfection. The rooms are some of the best appointed that I have come in contact with. The rooms are immaculate. The staff is incredibly attentive and the area is wonderfully quiet. Located just a few exits from downtown the hotel is amazingly easy to access on and off hwy 45. There is not a question that I will be staying at this hotel every visit to Houston I have!
“ロケーション最高” 普通のアメリカのホテル(つまり部屋の広さは十分)なので快適です。街の中心地にあって、徒歩圏内に大きなショッピングセンターやドラッグストア、アパレルショップなどたくさんあります。ビジネスで利用しましたが、ほんの少しの空き時間に休憩がてらフラっと街を散策したりウィンドウショッピングできるというロケーションが気に入りました。

“Lots of Small Extras” I stayed at the Sutton Place for a couple of nights on a business trip. I rarely venture outside of the Hilton chain as I am a Diamond member in that group. The Sutton is much like a Hilton in bed quality. The fabric did not smell like a hotel though....it was like mom washed it and was soothing. The bathroom had a tub with a separate glass shower. Under the bathroom counter was a stool which the ladies in our group enjoyed to apply their makeup. The room also has a DVD player with a small stereo including a few random CDs to listen to (even if I do not care for Lena Horne!). The bell staff and concierge are very good, always opening doors and making you feel very welcome. I found the attached "Whiskey" to be an OK if a little overpriced for drinks. Music was too loud. Breakfast in the Whiskey was pretty good but service was horrible. In the immediate vicinity on Rush Street is Gibson's Steakhouse and the Frog Bar as well as many other places to eat and drink. I would stay here again without a question especially if my Hilton was already booked up!

“fun nyc hotel” got this on priceline....after reading articles abaout how travellers are treated shabby, when they get room via priceline, found the opposite to be true....got a nicer room than after self-check-in failed - quiet room - 2 small problems in the room were taken care of within an hour - clean - food was a disappointment (well except for the s'mores pizza pie) - yeah it's a big hustling bustling hotel, but it's nyc - piano player in lobby made for a nice evening respite after strolling all around the city

“Nice historic downtown Chicago hotel” I recently stayed here one night, and then the next night at the new Radisson Blu. Gold recognition here is good - we got a great view of the lake in a really nice end room. Rooms are nicely appointed. The only reason I'm giving it 4 instead of 5 stars is because of the staff in the club lounge - they are quite aggressive about wanting to close up shop in the morning. I came up for breakfast at 8:45 with very little food left on the counter (they stop serving at 9:00). When I asked for a cereal bowl (there was only one left and we needed two) the lady said she would get one, but for me to remember they were closing in 10 minutes. At 8:55 they started carrying away the unreplenished food items. When I asked why they were closing early, they said they had to because there was no food left for them to put out. Moving away the coffee and orange juice dispenser before we could refill? C'mon, guys.

“Decent, but not great” Got a luxury king room with Park Ave view. The lobby was nice and intimate but the elevators were very dark and unpleasant. Staff, in general, was hospitable, particularly the housekeepers. The room was quite spacious, but i would agree with others that the bathroom was a bit too small for a luxury property. Not a stylish venue, but the location is superb. Generally speaking, average experience and value.

“Keep you shoes on!” The location of this hotel was great for Graceland. Literally across the road. The rooms were a good size and the pool was nice. I think the owners are relying too much on people staying because of the Theme and history of the hotel. It's not cheap at around £70 per room per night. They should try a little harder to keep up to date with the deep cleaning of the rooms. The carpets were so filthy that whenever we walked on them without shoes or socks our feet were black with the dirt. My parents on the ground floor had a cockroach in their room. I would look elsewhere if visiting again.

“Good Value” The suites are big and very good value, but they are a little tired and need a renovation. The beds are really comfortable and the aircon is supremely efficient. The suites are clean, have a good fridge and coffee maker but the bathrooms are small and old, and the furniture was visibly worn. The staff in the bar (particularly Katerina from the Czech Republic) are delightful, and cannot do enough for you. The food is of a high quality and the people here are really what makes this a good place to stay. Thanks so much to the team who turned this from average to nice.

“Great Room and Service” The hotel is really good and the rooms were clean. Being a gold Member with Best western rewards, I was offered a free upgrade to a suite and the room was really nice with the Microwave and refrigerator in it. It was really convenient location being very close to the Time Square. Overall and really nice Best Western plus hotel and affordable and good place to stay. The breakfast offered was really good and the staff was fantastic. I will definitely stay there again.

“Excellent rooms and staff” I booked a room as place to sleep for my wife and I on an overnight layover returning from Barbados via Delta through DFW on May 25 - 26th. I booked directly through the Hyatt website under the advance non-refundable rate - $110 AAA with breakfast. Note: There are two Hyatts at the DFW airport: the Grand Hyatt and a Hyatt. This review is about the Grand Hyatt which is located at Terminal D between gates 22 and 23. It has direct access to Terminal D from the lobby of the hotel. We arrived at 11:30pm, and the DFW terminal connection trains were not operating, so you have to use jump on the terminal link shuttle buses located right outside baggage claim on the DFW terminals second level - easy since they run every 5-6 minutes. You enter and proceed up the escalator or via elevator to the checkin floor. I tried using the kiosk self-checkin but could not access my reservation not a big deal considering the time. Checkin was breeze at the desk and had been booked into a king executive room. I was a little disppointed since my room was right next to the elevator, but amazed once I entered, based on the large size of the room with separate living area, huge bath and bedroom. Positives: Staff available and ready to help even for a midnight arrival. Excellent room - very spacious. Bed was extremely confortable. 6 pillows on bed - nice. Room were quiet to be at an airport. Alarm clock with IPOD docking station. Valet parking available in front of hotel. Hotel has three elevators -appreciated when busy. Bathroom has large seperate shower and oversized bathtub. Hamper in bathroom for towels, wet or dirty, which was nice touch. Plenty of towels on hand. Bedroom and living room each had a HDTV flat panel. Food for breakfast was excellent. (try the Eggs Benedict - 2nd best hollandaise sauce I ever had next to Interconti new orleans). Convenient for overnight stops. Friendly staff and servers including valet people. Lower level has computers and printers for online airline checkin. Elevators can only be operated to room floors with a room key. Hotel has fitness room which is good security measure. Negatives: Charge to park is $16/day; it is airport parking. For overnight stays, you have to park on level 2 & 4 which slightly inconvenient, and could troublesome if you have visitors while there. Self-checkin kiosk was not working which may have been my error or time of night. My Gold Passport number was not linked to my reservation, but staff easily fixed it. No room service available or an open restaurant for late night arrivals. All and all, my wife and I would stay there again in a heartbeat and wished every Hyatt were as great as this one on rooms, breakfast food and friendly staff.

“Very nice property” I had a quick one night stay for a meeting at the end of August. Rooms are very nice. There is a shuttle that picks up from the airport, or one could walk. There is always some confusion because there is also a Grand Hyatt right at DFW. I have stayed at both recently and both are very nice. Convenient to be so close to the airport especially for short meetings. I enjoyed this hotel and will stay again.

“Great Free Breakfast & Happy Hour!” My girlfriends and I stayed here for a "girls shopping weekend" in October. If you're looking for lots of space, a clean room, a free full breakfast and happy hour- this is the place to stay! The hotel is only about a 5-10 minute walk to Michigan Ave and the about the same distance to Navy Pier. The restaurant attached to the hotel, PJ Clarkes- has great food and is open late. The only downside is there is a lot of families with kids- not a hip hotel for a bunch of 26 year old girls. But I would stay here again for all the value added amenities.

“Very nice, euro-style property” Hotel has a European feel to it, naturally. Great location on Wacker Drive with views of the Chicago River, Navy Pier and Lake Michigan beyond. Very clean rooms and bathroom, comfortable beds and great duvet, and very heavily insulated from noise from inside and outside. Had a great rate of $159 per night but this hotel is usually high-$200 to low-$300 range. The Palm restaurant is connected to the hotel in the lobby which is really nice. Overall very good experience. Will come back.

“Good Corporate Hotel” Stayed at the hilton new york once more for a marketing conference. It's a good corporate hotel with corporate amenities. We stayed with 4 guys in one room and asked for the room to be cleaned twice a day. This was no problem. Friendly staff as always. Hallways are noisy, but that's to be expected in a hotel of this size. As a Hilton Diamond member I was a little disappointed that every time I stay at this hotel there's no upgrade available. Decided to stay a few nights extra, and we got the same rate as the **discounted** corporate convention rate. That was appreciated. Would recommend the hotel to add a few extra people at the reception area. Lines are always long.

“Pleasant Memorial Day Weekend Stay” My husband and I stayed at the InterContinental Chicago for five nights over the 2007 Memorial Day weekend. The hotel is well located within walking distance of all the Miracle Mile shopping and dining as well as Millennium and Grant Parks, the Art Institute, and Navy Pier. The room was small, befitting an urban hotel. We were in an end room in the newer tower and the room was extremely quiet. Air conditioning blew all the time, although it did provide white-noise. The king-size bed had very comfortable bedding and superb pillows! The built-in sofa unit was pretty uncomfortable. The shower's water pressure was a little low. There was some minor wear to the room (e.g., wallpaper peeling in bathroom, scratch on mirror), but room was neat and clean. Elevators were speedy and even at busy times came quickly. A newspaper was delivered outside the door every morning except Sunday. A new room service menu was delivered during our stay. The offerings were greatly expanded and upgraded, although pricey ($20 for a small pizza, plus delivery fees). The room had a stocked mini-bar and snack items. I didn't like the non-refrigerated snack items being so blatantly peddled, and looks like there hadn't been any takers in awhile since one of the cans of nuts had a small coating of dust on it. We had limited interactions with the staff, but they were always courteous and efficient.

“Start your day with a walk at the edge of the ocean” This super clean, very comfy and utterly charming historic motor court has a wonderful location a block or so from the walking/biking path along the Great Highway at the edge of the Pacific Ocean. Start your day by joining the lucky locals with a brisk walk along this path --sun or fog it is always bracing and tourist-free. Parking at the Ocean Park is free (versus $45 /night at many popular bay-side hotels), muni is at the door, and the airport is a quick shot down the freeway. If muni is not your thing, a 20 minute drive will get you to the Ferry Building downtown, that is if you take a decently long morning walk and leave the motel after 9 am. Do ask for a quieter room if noise is a bother as muni rattles and screeches around the corner regularly from early morn to late at night.

“This hotel is too big for itself” Let me start by saying the rooms are really nice. The place is new, so everything is clean and in order. Everything else about this hotel is incredibly unorganized though. In order to park there, you have to valet. It took us a total of about an hour to drop off and then pick up our car. There were people waiting even longer than that. There is so much going on at this hotel (conventions, weddings, and other events) that they can't keep up with them. I've never seen anything like it before. There isn't even enough space to put people. We had breakfast before we left and had the food was above average (that's not exactly a compliment), but the service was awful. As I said, the room itself was great, but if we plan a Ft. Worth trip again, we won't be staying here.

“over the top!” I stayed for 2 nights. The one good thing is that the staff is genuinely nice, esp. given the total chaos, noise, long lines, etc. The rooms are fairly big for NYC, but generic. The bad: the elevators are extremely sloooowww! I waited 8 minutes at one point for an elevator to go two floors. Apparently, they are installing new ones, but in the meantime, it's a real problem. The hotel itself was not for me: too big, too many people, too loud, too chaotic. A constant din in the hallways! Many, many tourists, and you have to wait for everything. Good if you like feeling in the center of everthing, esp. if you like being right in Times Square. Otherwise, I'd go elsewhere, esp. for the $$.

“Best Place To Stay in Dallas!” Truly the nicest Ritz I have stayed at the. The staff was amazing. I am still dreaming about the delicious food at Fearing's Restaurant. The spa experience was luxurious and wonderful. House car is a Bentley and mad it very convenient traveling to the convention center and back. I can not say enough about this hotel. Can't wait to go again. They have it all including a happening lobby lounge. Who knew.

“Great Location and positive experience” My boyfriend used some Hilton Rewards points to book two nights here. We had a lovely stay. I love the location (close to many restaurants, shopping, and night life). Our room was very comfortable and quiet. We may not have had immediate neighbors because we didn't hear any of the other guests. The bathroom and tolietries were nice and the bed was comfortable. We had coupons for the complimentary buffet (might have been because my boyfriend has a high status in Hilton Reward Points) and it was very filling. I would defininately stay here again and would recommend it to others.

“BEST HOTEL, CAN'T FAULT IT” I stayed at the US Grant for a week from 1 November 2008. The hotel can only be described as majestic, it is architecturally magnificent. On arriving from the airport in a cab ($10, but the 992 airport bus stops right outside the hotel for $1.25), I was warmly and genuinely greeted by the doorman, he took my bag and somehow without speaking to the staff at reception, passed on my name to them and they subsequently welcomed me by name and informed me that the room was ready for an early check in, they being aware that I was arriving from Australia. I must say at this point that during my week long stay I found all of the staff to be so kind and friendly, I never went unacknowledged, whether I was just passing reception or doormen etc. Just a smile or a hello, nothing irritating like American conversation that never ends! The room was stunning, and overlooked Horton Plaza, the small shopping mall. Housekeeping was mainly of a high standard. The king bed was lovely, air con was great, TV was great with lots of channels to choose from. I must give a big plus to the Grant Grill, the in-hotel restaurant. I would return just for their steaks, words fail me, the best in the world. The staff are subtle but caring, never seeking tips constantly like most American hotel staff. It is unlikely I will visit San Diego again in a long time, but I will always remember the US Grant and highly recommend it.

“Like staying in a college dorm” With big hotels like this you'll get lots of mixed reviews. If you're used to staying in a LaQuinta - this place is fine. If you're used to staying in something better, you'll wish you'd gone somewhere else. My normal standby hotel in mid-town was sold out and the Westin was only two blocks from where I was supposed to go to a meeting. As such, I thought I would try it out - that turned out to be a bad idea. Like most large hotels in mid-town the Westin is more like a college dorm. The rooms are tiny, the ceilings are low, and everything just seems worn and cheap. The hotel had a "modern" look to it that showed signs of wear given the huge numbers of guest who churn through the revolving doors each day. When I checked in the didn't have the type of room I'd reserved, so they downgraded me without downgrading the price. When I asked if they'd lower the rate, they did. However, when I got the final bill they'd only made the change for one night. I called and they were happy to change it for both nights. It wasn't hard to get done, it was just a pain. The Westin beds were quite comfortable and the floor we were on was very quiet. Our maid was nice and thorough. However, she could only work with what she had. The bathroom was very small and had a polished aluminum or stainless steel sink that looked like it was straight out of a prison. The shower was small with terribly weak water pressure. There were plenty of clean towels but the toilet paper seemed cheap. The closet had full length mirrored doors that looked straight out of the 1980s. There was over-priced wifi internet with slow connection speeds. The worst part about the hotel was the premium price for the sub-par hotel. If you're going to mid-town, you can do better than the Westin.

“I prefer to be treated as a guest, not simply a reservation.” We went on a June Saturday night. Two weddings and Pride Weekend meant a lot of people but nothing that they didnt handle routinely. I bet. They couldn't get us in a room until 45 minutes AFTER the check-in time. Put a bad taste in our mouth the rest of the way. Door staff was good. Room was nice but seemed to be putting a hip spin on routine hotel. Exposed concrete ceilings are trendy? Lousy WiFi and TV reception is what people want? I was unimpressed with the hotel and I bet the feeling was mutual. My wife got to the spa early to enjoy the included ammenities. The staff there moved up her appointment and shuffled her out after her treatment without letting her gather thoughts, shower, etc. as so many similar spa setups do. Paying guests should not be made to feel like an imposition.

“Nice view” Stayed on Saturday night in April. Paid $330 a night, and thought it's pricy. If you want to a water front room, it's $30 extra. I gave up that luxualy, however, the view from the room 1512 was facing to river and it was fantastic! Had lunch at their restaurant since this hotel is somewhat isolated on its location. Crabcake sandwitch with tomato soup was soo delicious..Yumm!!! The complains are., the elevator mulfunctions occured several times. Their swimming pool is so shallow.

“Better than typical Hampton Inn” Excellent location, reasonable pricing and very helpful staff. The complimentary pretzels available all day were great! Front desk provided great suggestion for Chinese food nearby. The breakfast was better than the typical Hampton Inn fare. Only minor drawback was size of dining area available, but we were there during car show so probably larger than normal breakfast crowd.

“Friendly service, interior needs a facelift, breakfast extremely average” Just returned from my stay at the Embassy Suites and I am amazed to find that it is currently ranked #6 for hotels in D.C. No way can that be true! The interior of the hotel looks quite rundown. One of the large cascading fountains in the hotel's atrium had no water in it and gave the interior an unkempt appearance. Plant boxes on every floor and underneath every room in the atrium were mostly missing any kind of plants and the few plants that were left remaining looked old and tired. Pluses: Linda at the front desk was very pleasant at check in; the room was comfortable and had all the necessities; the location was convenient and only a few blocks away from the Dupont Circle metro station (I enjoy walking and the weather was beautiful). Minuses: Decor in room looks dated, carpet looks tired and worn, atrium of hotel was in disrepair and looked unappealing, and the breakfast was not very good. More on the breakfast: there were numerous hot items from which to choose and the omelettes were great, but there were no breakfast pastries/bagels, etc. and no fruit. Alongside signs indicating "fresh fruit" there were only small containers of yogurt. I've eaten much better breakfasts at Hampton Inns lately (and I need my fruit!). Oh yes - a word about the fitness center. It was fine but very, very humid. I huffed and puffed through every mile I ran on the treadmill. The temperature really needed to be adjusted but I could find no way to do so. Also, I received not a single amenity related to my Hilton Gold membership. We'll see if I get any extra points but I seriously doubt it. In summary, would I return? My simple answer - not unless I had no other choice. I've stayed at many nicer hotels in D.C., believe me.

“Great location and staff but looking a little well used” This is a nice, no nonsense hotel. Nothing fancy but really good. The Libby is looking a bit worn out and you can see we're the paint has been refinished over time. A little tired looking. Staff is spot on. Whatever you need - you get. Location is good but be ready for hoards of people right outside the hotel's front dior

“Again, we loved it” We've stayed at the Affinia 50 three times. The one bedroom suties are terrific and spacious, with attractive furnishings. If one person wants to stay up late and another doesn't, it's perfect. The kitchen facilities make it great to toast a delicious NY bagel in the morning, make coffee and head out. Stephan, who is at the front desk, is very helpful, as is all the staff.

“Small, but nice” I stayed at the Crowne Plaza Chicago-Allerton on Friday night. It was a great location to all the clubs and bars. We walked about nine blocks to get to Sound-bar, Y, RiNo, Spyclub, etc. FINDING YOUR WAY AROUND: My friend and I took the subway from O'Hare to the Chicago (Red line) stop and walked about 3 blocks to Michigan Ave. Once on Michigan we began out search for the Crowne Plaza to learn that it is NOT on Michigan Ave technically--the enterance is on Huron. The Nine West shoe store shares the same building and its front is on the Mag Mile. When we entered the Hotel, we learned that check-in is on the THIRD floor using the elevator on the right. If you wanted to go to your room, you had to get on another set of elevators on the third floor. To go to Taps or the lounge, you got on the elevator on the first floor to your left. THE ROOM: Very small. We checked in at 5PM and that's the only avalable room they had. My friend saw it and had a fit, but I didn't care because we didn't spend so much time in it. It had a standard bed (full), a small desk, and a TV on a TV stand. The linens and towels were white and clean. The bathroom was quite nice with marble-ish floors and a see through glass shower. On, the floors are very slippery! The room was very clean and stocked with the following: -Shampoo, conditioner, soap, lotion, and shoe polish -Hair dryer and make-up mirror -On the bed was a linen spray and earplugs -Iron, extra blanket and pillow in the closet STAFF: Helpful, if not a bit sarcastic. They at least knew how to get around the city. You can also leave your luggage there after check-out to walk around the city.

“Enjoyed our balcony” We stayed in the Royal Palm Tower for 7 nights. I chose a room in the Royal Palm Tower because most of the negative reviews on Trip Advisor seemed to be about rooms in other parts of the hotel. We stayed at this hotel several years ago so I was prepared this time for the dark, dated rooms. (The walls & carpets are a fairly dark shade of blue.) I'm not sure if the bathroom had been updated but it was bright & cheery. There was a sink in the actual bathroom area & an additional vanity/sink right outside the bathroom - it was handy having 2 sinks. Our room was large & our air conditioning worked fine . All the rooms in the Royal Palm Towers have balconies - most look out at the resort but a few just look at concrete walls. We were on the 2nd floor & enjoyed our balcony a lot because it was shaded by the ground level trees. Parking is definitely a problem but because we never got back in the late evening, we could always find a decent parking space. We ate breakfast & a couple of dinners in the attractive Terrace Cafe - food is ok. The nearby mall (walking distance) has a food court and several popular chain restaurants: California Pizza Kitchen, P.F. Chang's, The Cheesecake Factory & Uno Chicago Grill. It is very convenient to take the Trolley to downtown - we took it to Petco Park. As other reviewers have mentioned, the grounds are very attractive with lots of beautiful plants.

“Nice home base for San Diego trip” Stayed two nights to attend the San Diego Street Scene concerts. Hotel is easily accessed from the freeway and is a quick trip to downtown, Gaslamp, Old Town & Balboa Park. Our room was on the second floor, which lacks an ice machine. Room was nice, updated decor. Bed was comfy for sleeping and lounging in during the day. Front desk could have been friendlier, but did their job fine. Parking lot is large, but spots are tiny. Hotel is nice, typical higher end hotel.

“Great Mother's Day weekend” My sister, mother and 2 nieces spent a spontaneous weekend to celebrate Mother's Day in D.C. We had perfect weather and the Marriott at Metro Center was a great place to stay. Accommodations were very good, clean and suited our needs perfectly. Hotel staff was friendly, courteous and helpful, except for bellman and valet. They were always busy talking with each other and not helpful at all. Check in and out was smooth and easy. The restaurant was nice, the food good and although pricey, had value. There is a Starbucks in the lobby which made our need for coffee fixes very simple. We did not use the gym or the pool. There is a Panera right next door and several restaurants within walking distance. We were able to walk to the Mall and several other historic sites. We picked up the double-decker bus right outside the front door. I would definitely recommend the hotel for visiting.

“Nice getaway weekend” My wife and I spent two nights here and really enjoyed it. The hotel is not perfect, but for the rate ($170 a night, including $50 resort voucher) I was happy with it. Pros: VERY comfortable bed, great pools and hot tubs (8+ to choose from), beautiful landscaping, ample free parking, quiet rooms, nearby hiking trail, tennis courts, exercise center Cons: room had some flaws - broken drawer on a dresser, banged up trim in the bathroom, but nothing major. Coupons for breakfast were not delivered to my room until the night before check out, but staff had already cheerfully provided replacements. To reach the parking areas, we had to navigate narrow roadways, which could have been a challenge if we had a larger car This is a huge, sprawling property, but there are shuttles and everything seems to be within a short walk.

“Very nice hotel” I recently stayed at this hotel for two nights on a business trip. It is about 4.5 blocks from the Foggy Bottom metro stop. It is fairly close to Georgetown and is just north of George Washington Medical Center. The Park Hyatt and a number of restaurants are in the area. The rooms were very nice, clean, well maintained and comfortable. The bathrooms are very nice and are tiled in marble. It has a separate tub and shower. The "heavenly shower" is kind of dumb. It just means that it has two shower heads on a set of parallel pipes. No big woop, and probably violates water use restrictions. Over all, a very nice place to stay.
“Excellent choice for San Francisco” Hotel is immaculate. Everything is new. Beds are comfy - rooms quiet. Best value for upscale hotels in the city.

“Excellent Resort” Let me start of by saying that we've stayed at quite a few of Westin's resorts around the world, and are pretty picky about the caliber of places we stay in while vacationing. I was a bit aprehensive about the resort after reading some of the reviews I read here, but we experiened none of the problems folks here enountered. We arrived on a Saturday afternoon of a very busy weekend, and had 2 rooms booked (vacationing with friends) - not necessarily next to each other. They had one of our rooms in the Casitas, and another in the main hotel - OK, that was a major pain. I checked out the Casitas - and the rooms were not only large, but top notch. However, I would only recommend them if you want A LOT of quiet and are golfing. Otherwise, especially if you have kids, you want to stay at the hotel. So, we took up 2 rooms in the hotel. While for the first day the corridor to the rooms was a bit musty smelling, they addressed the issue by the next morning. The room was a pretty standard Westin room- clean, and smelled clean (unlike many other complaints on this site). The resort facilities were excellent - and the staff was most friendly. In fact even at check in, the woman behind the counter spent an inordinate amount of time explaining things to me and showing me around. Overall, the resort is huge. It's a golfers paradise. But is also excellent for kids - plenty of kids playing areas, and activities for kids. Pools are good - including an adults-only pool. Food is decent - though on the pricey side. While the resort is right next to Six Flags, it would be a waste to stay at this resort and then spend the whole day at Six Flags. We recommend the Omni for that. If you want to go off campus for food, you've got to drive everywhere for that. And parking is a huge pain in the butt - long trek to the parking lot if you're not using valet. This is definitely a resort we will return to.

“No issues” Stayed here on an overnight passing through Dallas, arrived late - 9pm. Short queue at check-in, but encountered a trainee so took a little longer than normal - which was surprising, as the booking was made via the Hyatt Gold Passport frequent stayers program. After check-in we grabbed a couple of drinks at the bar and ordered some food. Unfortuanately the both meals were cold on arrival - faulty microwave? : ) Sent them back, same meals returned 10 minutes later 'nuked' - not stylish - advised that we were still not happy, and the manager took the meals and the two drinks off the bill, and offerered a free take away pizza. The hotel seemed to have reasonable faciilties, but as we were leaving early the following morning did not have time to try out the gym and pool etc. Would probably give here another chance if passing through.

“Really the best hotel in Chicago” I stay in Chicago just about every other month for business. If I can get a good deal, I generally have liked the Trump, followed by the Conrad. But the Elysian blows them both away. I picked it up on hotels.com for $225 a night, which is a steal, as normal rates are $500-$600. The Peninsula doesn't even begin to compare with the Elysian. It's a gorgeous, modern property with amazing rooms. Makes you not want to go home, really. Rooms have a wet bar entry area that goes into a living space with sofa, big screen and a fireplace. How awesome will that be for Chicago in the winter. There's a nice desk and then the sleeping area (super comfy bed and wonderful linens). Full dressing area and then a stellar bathroom. There's so much space it's like a small apartment. That someone cleans for you! The reason this succeeds over, say, regular rooms at the Trump, is that it's all suites and the space is better apportioned. Only beef I would have is that the Trump has lovely little Nespresso machines in each room so you can have a quick coffed in the morning. Elysian could do with having some sort of tony coffee machine in the room. Otherwise, I'd definitely stay here again--especially if I get a cool low rate. One major item: It's in a great neighborhood, but it's not the easiest thing to find. I'm native to Chicago, but took me a minute to figure out where this was. It's basically off the southwest corner of Wabash and Rush. It's actually back behind the 900 North Michigan complex. Cabbies should know, but if you're walking about, just be aware that the entrance is about halfway down Walton from where the Marc Jacobs is on the corner of Rush. There's an entrance for the "residences" a little closer to the corner.

“Average airport hotel” I had to move to this hotel after Hilton Garden Inn nearby was not able to honor the reservation made well in advance. It is an average Hampton Inn ... or maybe slightly below average in terms of room size. Both the room and hotel public areas are clean and everything in the room was in good working condition. The staff is very nice, polite and helpful ... highly above average. They really do care about their guests. It is the staff why my rating is :very good:. Also the breakfast was very good. One does not expect much from airport hotels but this Hampton Inn is at least not disappointing.

“Excellent value and convenience” We stayed at the Coast Gateway as the first step in our trip to Europe. The hotel claims to be the closest to SeaTac. It couldn't be more accurate. From our window we could physically see Terminal A across the street! But it was surprisingly quiet. It took us less than 2 minutes to reach the terminal! Some areas of the hotel look a bit old. The bathroom in our suite was also on the older side but it was clean. The toilette area closes with a sliding door, something I've never seen in any other hotel. Use of Internet in the business center is free and you can check and print your itinerary, boarding pass, driving directions, etc. Breakfast was included and it was actually very decent. The shuttle took us to the terminal on demand (no need to wait for a scheduled shuttle) and the driver was very courteous. The oddest things was the front desk: we arrive to the hotel at 9 pm, then went down to the business center at 11 pm and the we came down for breakfast and checkout around 10 am. The same lonely lady was always there! She was pulling a 12+ hours shift... It was a good experience overall.

“Great Location, Highly Recommend” I stayed at the Hampton Inn Times Square North with my wife and 5-year-old son. We arrived early and checked in around noon. Our room was not ready but we completed the necessary paperwork, and were told to come back around 1 or 2 pm. We went to lunch and returned about 2:30 and our room was available. Check in was quick and hassle free. We had a room on the 5th floor with 2 queen beds. The room faced the rear of the hotel, which was good because there was very little outside noise. ROOM: The room had 2 queen beds, a sitting chair with ottoman, desk with chair, dresser and a small padded table for luggage. There was a flat screen HDTV with PPV and online checkout. There was a safe in the room that used a “big” metal key, rather than a numeric keypad to lock/unlock. The room was a pretty good size for NYC, clean and seemed to be in excellent condition. There was free WIFI access available. BATHROOM: The bathroom was small but functional. The toiletries were Purity brand and consisted of; soap, shampoo, conditioner, moisturizer, body gel, shower gel and a shower cap. The shower was hot and had good water pressure. BREAKFAST: The free breakfast was very good. The breakfast area was rather large, nicely decorated and in excellent condition. Items in the buffet included: scrambled eggs, bacon, “make your own” waffles, bananas, apples, 6 kinds of cereals, yogurt, oatmeal packets, bagels, muffins, and bread. We went early around 6:40 and it was not crowded, although it did appear to get very crowded later in the morning. The hotel even has a sign letting you know the best times to have breakfast (see picture). They also have coffee available all the time outside the breakfast area. OTHER: There is a parking garage right next to the hotel. They offer a discounted rate if you get your ticket stub validated by the hotel. The front desk did not ask me if I had parked a car or mention this validation. I had asked them in the morning if they validated, since this was the case at other Hilton properties in NYC. The elevators were sometimes crowded, but we never had to wait too long. Overall, this is a great NYC hotel and will most likely be my choice for future visits to the city.
“立地はいいです” とくに際立った特徴があるホテルではありませんが、立地はいいです。 お食事もホテルでは取りませんでした。一階?のスタバでコーヒーを何回か買いました。 コプレイの駅まで徒歩5分ぐらいです。

“Great find!” This place is friendly, has more amenities than a typical courtyard and is walkable to a lot of downtown, moscone center, chinatown and union square attractions. Very nice fitness center for a courtyard. Contemporary urban vibe and happy staff. Great value.

“Für den Preis nicht zu schlagen” Ich war für drei Übernachtungen in der Travelodge Hollywood. Ich bezahlte 67.50 $ + Tax pro Nacht, wobei die Rechnung erstmal auf 76.50 $ lautete, der Manager korrigierte das aber sofort. Die Lage ist optimal, man ist überall schnell und die U-Bahn ist auch in zwei Minuten zu erreichen. Das Zimmer ist sehr groß, sauber und hat einen Kühlschrank. Vom Krankenhaus direkt gegenüber habe ich nicht viel gehört. Alles in allem zu empfehlen

“A Different Perspective of New York” We stayed at Ink 48 in March for four days. We paid a bit extra for a room looking out to the Hudson River. It was worth it! Another Kimpton property done to Kimpton's standards and observing the company's quirky design personality. All of the usual Kimpton extras are there: the free wine hour in the lobby; pet friendly; friendly and efficient staff. From the room's side window we could see up to the Upper West Side and from the huge window looking West a complete view of the Hudson River was before us. We were awakened a couple of early mornings by the sound of cruise ship horns as they prepared to dock at the Manhattan Cruise Terminal just a block or so away. This was absolutely no bother to us as it added to the excitement of being in New York City, but for those who book a room with a Hudson view be aware that there might be some interruptions to a late morning sleep-in. Because the hotel is way out on 11th Avenue more cab rides might be required to travel to Midtown or to other sections of the city that are more easily accessible when staying at a downtown location. However we often walked back to the hotel after an evening of theater and/or dinner and we found the streets leading to the property to be safe and well populated during evening hours. Oh yes, I almost forgot - the Ink 48 is also located within a block or so of the Intrepid Aeronautic Museum. We found Ink 48 much to our liking. It is a bit away from the main theater and restaurant districts and is located in what I would call a light industrial area along the Hudson waterfront. We would definately consider this hotel for a return visit.

“Great Location, but the rest of the rooms need to be renovated” I've stayed at the hotel before, but this time something was just off. I was upgraded to a higher floor as an SPG Platinum, but no suite as usual. The hotel itself is pretty nice, but the room this time reminded of the W-New York on Lex before it was renovated. The modern rooms need to be kept up or they just come across as cheesy. Last time I must have been in a newly renovated room, because everything was great. This time I felt like I was in an older room and also felt a little ripped off. I've just come to expect nice bathrooms at every W Hotel I stay at and a bath tub with a shower curtain is a big disappointment. There were some nicks in the paint and a few other things that aren't OK for over $300/night. On the positive side, the staff is always really helpful and the location is perfect for showing around friends that want to see the more touristy side of New York. There's a subway stop right across the street, and plenty of restaurants and broadway shows within a few minutes. Had I not stayed in a newer room the time before, I would have been a little happier about the room, but after staying in so many Ws, the room was a let down and to maintain the prices, they really need to make sure all the rooms are renovated.

“Nice Stay-cation” We stayed in one of the Premier Rooms at the Stoneleigh. It was a lovely, good size, corner room with a nice big bathroom. Our only gripe was the described "sitting area" was a chair in the corner. We just moved it to the open space we thought it should have been in, and we were happier. The renovations of the hotel are beautiful. The chandeliers in the lobby and bar held my attention for a long time. The hotel is described as Beaux-Arts and Art Deco. Truly beautiful. Lots of history. And a good location. We walked to Nick and Sam's for dinner, and had other options within walking distance, too.

“Always Great” We love staying at the Atheneum. Three rooms in a suite, a sitting room with couch, bar and TV, a few steps down to a nice size bedroom, and a large bathroom. With our family of 4 and two queen beds, the extra room allows some to be up later in the evening or earlier in the morning without it being a bother to the rest of us. One note is no pool. Greektown is safe and good food, Fishbones, attached to the hotel has great sushi.

“Beste Lage, sehr gutes Hotel, guter Service!” Sehr nettes Personal, ein Hauch von einem Grand Hotel vergangener Jahre. Zimmer renoviert, komfortabel und sauber. Sehr ruhiges Hotel! Frühstück inklusive (ansonsten rund 40 Dollar pro Person), perfekte Lage, Times Square, Fifth Avenue oder Central Park bequem zu Fuß erreichbar. Grand Central Station in unmittelbarer Nähe (6 Blocks). Wunderschönes Hotel in einer atemberaubenden Stadt!

“I wish Margaret from reservations ran this hotel.” I know my title may sound strange but I really believe if she did, it would truly be a notch above so many other hotels because of her attention to detail and customer service skills. I don't want to give this hotel a negative review, I wanted to like it as much as Margaret in reservations. It is certainly not a bad hotel, but it has the potential to be a wonderful hotel. In defense of the hotel, since I only stayed for one night, maybe I caught it on an "off" day. I was coming to town for a Dr's appt and because I was so sick I needed my mother and her husband to drive me. I had changed my reservation 3 times because my migraine was so bad and Margaret was very accommodating. The day of my arrival I called to add a room to my reservation. The rooms were around $750 and I was eligible for an upgrade because I am an Andrew Harper member. Margaret made the smart suggestion that I upgrade my room for a couple hundred of dollars and then use the upgrade, and add on my parents room making it a two bedroom suite. I thanked her for even thinking that up and was so excited about my stay. The Andrew Harper rewards also entitled us to a bottle of wine, vip fruit basket, free afternoon tea and a continental breakfast. When we arrived, around 3:30, they said the room wasn't ready and I thought, oh perfect we can go for tea, but we were told to wait in the waiting area, which we did. After about 45 minutes we were taken to our room. The living room was great, it was comfortable, newly re-finished, it had a terrace with a really interesting city view, if you hung over the balcony enough, you could even see central park. I took the nicer bedroom, it had the same city view, a gorgeous bathroom with great amenities. The carpet however was wet from being cleaned and had that weird chemical smell, if I didn't have a migraine, it would have been more livable for me. The other bedroom was also nice, city view, but not as good as mine and it had a much smaller bathroom. But again, we were only there for one night. We had room service for dinner and we were told that it would take approximately 45 minutes, it ended up closer to an hr and 45 minutes. I hate confrontation, so does my mother, but my stepfather yelled at room service which embarrassed me greatly, they took care of the bill which I thought was more than generous (maybe it was part, I really stayed out of the whole thing, I hid in my bedroom). The food was amazing, we had this awesome tomato soup, although it would have been better if it came with the gorgonzola crustini it was advertised with. I had the fresh pea ravioli which was delicious. The VIP fruit basket was 3 apples. No tea. There was no breakfast the following morning. We were also charged a price higher than quoted. Oh, and the lady who did the turn down was lovely I guess to some up. Pros: Margaret, Margaret, Margaret.... CIty view suite with terrace room service Cons: Things are just not delivered as promised (I believe this is a customer service issue) We were charged a price higher than we were quoted Honestly, I wouldn't stay here again because I don't know what it would be like, this is my only experience with this hotel. It was overall just more disappointing than anything, it would have been better to expect nothing and be surprised along the way.

“The best of San Diego” Luxurious hotel, beautiful location with harbor view, great pool, excellent service. We had spacious rooms with the view on the harbor and bridge to Coronado. Great service, convenient parking, WiFi in the lobby. Very good breakfast buffet (by American standards), though the restaurant does not have sufficient capacity, so try to get there early to avoid long wait. There is a promenade to gaslamp district, but unfortunately the elevator to go down to the street level is badly vandalized and broken, so you can't get their with disability. Overall, affordable and very pleasant stay.

“Excellent comfort and service every time” My wife and I stay here every time we visit Philadelphia, whether for business or pleasure. The rooms are clean, very nicely appointed, with every comfort and amenity, great beds and pillows, excellent service. Every stay is flawless. It is only a couple of blocks from Rittenhouse square, so there are stores and restaurants all around, and it is a great area to walk, a safe and very central location.

“Great service, excellent value, enjoyable” When my son suggested I book the Sportsman's Lodge (near his apartment in Sherman Oaks) I was prepared for the worst just based on the low price. While I tend to stay at 4 or 5 star hotels, my son is comfortable at a Motel 6, and so I prepared myself for a $129 (cost of room) Los Angeles experience. The lobby was neat, clean and comfy with a round, surround fireplace providing a nice holiday feeling. Service was immediate and I had my room key in about 2 minutes. The room was a bit of a walk past the pool, but not too far to walk with light baggage. The room itself was very comfortable, certainly large enough and the balcony had a nice view of the pool. There was enough room on the balcony for two chairs, though only one was provided. As a cigar smoker, I was disappointed that you could not smoke on the balcony. On the other hand, I am sure this will please some non-smokers. The room had a decent set of amenities and was very clean. The lobby bar was friendly and the drinks very reasonably priced. The bartender (either Joe or Jim ... I forget) has been at the hotel for 29 years and has a few celebrity stories. This hotel (or motel might be more exact) is a favorite of rock bands but it has a quiet and graceful demeanor. Several sports stars stay there as well.The walls are lined with photos of movie stars, mostly from the '40's- '60's. I don't know if they ever stayed there, but I would not be surprised if they did. Checkout was as fast as check in and, as I was leaving, a staff member pointed out that I had not taken advantage of the free continental breakfast (a car was waiting for me). It is that type of personal touch that makes this a very comfortable and enjoyable stay. My only one disappointment turned into a positive experience; the, what would be called in other hotels a "business center" had two computers attached to a cash / credit card machine. In order to use the computers you had to pay. The charge was a minimum $3 but the computer was so slow that it would be easy to consume that time long before you got your passes. Not that $3 is a lot but then to have to wait was frustrating. In the end, the machine would not print and so, after waiting and paying, I still did not have my boarding passes. The front desk apologized, explained that the computer is owned by another company (there is a phone next to the computer with the phone number of that company) and that he could not fix that. On the other hand, he quickly offered to print them out at his station and apologized again for the inconvenience. I would surmise that if you asked them to print out your boarding pass without bothering to use the pay computers, they would. This is that type of place.

“Nice surprise” I used points to book this centrally located hotel having just flown in from London. I was not looking to spend money on my first night since I arrived in the evening. What a great surprise, the hotel is conveniently located for Times Square and Macys, it is very well priced. It appears that many stay here for an extended period in excess of a week. The room is clean and has all amenities including a microwave and little kitchenette with a fridgefreezer. Although I was only there for half a day I really liked it, it feels like the way forward for travellers especially in the USA. You get value - including free WIFI rather than having to spend money on these things at the upmarket chains.There was even a DVD collection for those who want a quiet evening. The hotel has many floors and it seems 6 or 8 rooms to a floor so every room is near a lift. It isn't a problem though if you keep normal times. I would recommend staying here, especially if you have points - in which case due to the conversion rate it is probably the best bargain in NY!

“Outstanding Choice in DC” Stayed here as my second choice because the Willard was ridiculously priced and at $135 per night this hotel was a downright bargain. I received early check in to a nice room with a view - everyone could not have been nicer. The beds were very comfy also. Location was five minute walk to the Metro and 4-5 blocks from the White House and a few nice restaurants - will definitely stay here again.

“Good Hotel, Good Location, Good Price -One Issue” Overall, I would say this hotel was good. The customer service at all the Kimpton Hotels are usually great. The location of this hotel is really good and the rooms are pretty nice and spacious. I did complain about an issue though. The issue was the bed was made with a top sheet and a duvet without a duvet cover. It's pretty odd for a hotel to not have duvet covers on their duvets. The issue was also the duvet was visibly stained. When you go to a hotel, you do not want to see stained bedding! I called housekeeping and they rudely told me that the hotel was out of blankets. What hotel runs out of blankets? When I brought it up at checkout the manager did discount my stay and was very apologetic.

“Great hotel - loved my stay!” We got a great deal via Expedia on this hotel. I loved it! First of all, it's in a great location, just off the Magnificent Mile. Second, the service is cheerful and accommodating. The rooms are nice and there's also a great hotel bar on the roof! Make sure you ask for a room on a high floor; the low rooms can get noisy (we switched and it was no hassle). Also, make sure you go for a drink on the rooftop bar on the outdoor patio - it's very nice.

“The Spa from Heaven” This is for the spa not the hotel itself - Michael is a a massage therapist devine. Had a massage a year ago when visiting and talked of it all year til I returned. Very nice facials - quiet attentive staff. Trail mix stale - very large bowl seemed 1/2 full and thought it might have been there since my visit the year before. Nice waters and juices. Hair salon not as pleasant - both visits staff seems young and inexperienced - noisy - glaring lights. Surprised they do not do nail fills etc. Pricey but Michael is worth it - $100 for 45 minutes. Warning you cannot add tips to your credit card - must have cash for tips.

“Awesome Foyer! Average Room...” I just returned from a trip to Baltimore on 1/11/2005. Upon first arrival, I was extremely impressed with the grand entrance of the hotel. The check-in process was cool. I forgot to pack my toothpaste and they graciously gave me a small travel tube. I anxiousely awaited my room thinking that it would be equally impressive! My room was okay...just okay. I was put on the 19th floor facing Little Italy. Nothing to write home about, but nothing to be fearful of staying. I found a small red wax looking spot on my toilet and then on the floor. After notifying the front desk, they immediately sent housekeeping to clean it up. The bed was very comfortable and I melted in it! The walls are paper thin...so pray that no one will be next door. I did not feel good the first night and went to the concierge at 3am to see if they had a place where I could take my blood pressure. The 3 folks at the desk said "no" and no one bothered to ask me was I "okay" even though it was in the wee hours of the morning. I then proceeded to the front desk to ask the gentleman where the nearest emergency room was, he mentioned that Johns Hopkins was up the street, but never offered to call a cab or ambulance. So I proceeded to sit in the lobby for about 2 hours to call my heart rate down! The only person who talked to me was the guard who wanted to know if I was a visitor or a guest (since I had been sitting in front of the TV for a while). Other than that, the hotel meeting space, catering and wait staff was superb! The food is great and they really cater to your every need. Our food preparation and service in the meeting space was first class! The hotel is in a great location and convenient to a lot of tourist locations. Overall, I had a good stay...since I was on business travel I got a good group rate and can't complain about the nickel/dime ancillary charges.

“Very close to SJC - a typical Fairfield Inn” We arrived SJC at 11:00 at night and I wanted a close hotel that served a free breakfast. I normally like the Marriott properties in order to get Rewards points. This hotel is very close to the airport. We got two rooms for our group of 5. We slept, we ate, we left. Front desk person had 4 people in front of me when I arrived and offered apologies for my delay. She did the best possible and was very polite and professional. Rooms and breakfast were standard Fairfield Inn fare. It would be nice if they had a waffle-maker, but they didn't. Price was ok but no bargain. I'd stay here again under the same circumstances.

“Nice rooms - plumbing has issues and may have bedbugs” The room was big, as were the bathroom and closet. We were happy with the room, but I agree completely with the review about the toilets being VERY loud. I don't think I would have cared much about it except that for as loud as they were and for as long as you have to hold down the handle, I would hope that they would flush all the way - they did not consistently. Also, the plumbing for the showers was spotty so sometimes the water pressure was not that great. As for the bedbugs, we couldn't find any, but my husband has some bites on his back after sleeping one night and we can't think of anywhere else he could have gotten then. The location is nice, but it is HIGH up on a hill so get your walking shoes out.

“Another wonderul stay at the Hotel Elysee” Just got back from a 2 night's stay at the Hotel Elysee. I believe that this was my 5th time staying there. It is my favorite hotel in NYC. It feels like home away from home. The staff is very friendy and very helpful. The rooms are spotless and it is located in a great part of the city. Love the breakfasts and "happy hour" every night. We will be back again soon!

“New York Classic” Whether you like the Carlyle really depends on your taste. If you liked hotels with an old-world charm, this may well be your favorite hotel. The lobby is very tasteful, with a style that appeals to all generations. The "classical influence" really begins at the elevators, which are still manned by elevator operators. Frankly, I find that a bit pretentious and unneccessary. Why demand extra labor when there's no need for it? There's a difference between excellent service and excessive service. And in the context of the Carlyle's elevator operators, this is debatable. With my lowly corporate rate, I had a standard room on the 19th floor. I understand that the hotel prides itself on history, so I won't be overly critical about the wear-and-tear of the furnishings and finishes. My overall impression of the room was warm, tasteful and intimate. It felt like a private residence rather than a hotel. However, rooms are on the small side compared to Four Seasons and Ritz Central Park. You should have realized by now that I'm not a big fan of classical hotels. I didn't like the Plaza (back in the good old days) or Waldorf. But I enjoyed the Carlyle because of its service. I don't know whether it is the fact that 80% of the staff speaks with a French accent or the general professionalism, but I felt that the Carlyle's service is very personal. And that, may I add, is very different from the service you get at chains like Four Seasons and Ritz-Carlton. It makes the hotel a home for its guests. If I were to pay $600 for a standard room, where would I stay? I have to admit that Carlyle would not be on the top of my list. But we all have different tastes. Is it worth a try? Oh, yes.

“Very impressed” I stayed at the Holiday Inn Capitol many years ago, when it was dark, worn out, and far from upscale. I was a bit leery of staying there again, but I was very impressed with all the changes they've made. The hotel is bright and cheery, well decorated, and lively. My room was as nice as any room you'd get in a fancy hotel. I heard no noise from the hallways or other rooms. I loved having the free Internet connection. I was in a rush to get out each morning, so picked up a muffin and coffee in the deli, which is basically a take-out operation with a few tables. The hotel came up with great idea to offer that to guests who don't have a lot of time to eat. The hotel has the deli, Starbucks, and the sit-down restaurant--something for everyone. I would definitely recommend this hotel and look forward to staying there again.

“Best hotel for a getaway with friends - loved everything about it!” I stayed here for several nights in early May with a large group of friends - we occupied almost every room on the "Pool Deck." I can't recommend this hotel enough - great location, great staff, great rooms, great food and drinks, etc. The rooms are large, modern, clean, and extremely comfortable. Rooms on the 2nd floor have sliding glass doors that open directly to the Pool Deck - each room has a small sitting area outside with sheer curtains for privacy, if needed. We spent each day lounging in the chaises overlooking Pacific Beach (awesome people-watching!), went out at night, then returned to sit around the fire pit on the deck late at night. "Room" service was fantastic - we had drinks and food (and more drinks...) delivered up to the deck - and Zack went above and beyond to take care of us (thanks Zack!!). Food from JRDN was excellent and provided a unique alternative to standard hotel room service. Every aspect of my stay far exceeded my expectations, and I can't wait to go back - this is the perfect way to enjoy Pacific Beach!

“Rooms and Hotel need updating - current updates making mess/noise” Agree with previous review - not up to Starwood/Sheraton standards. There are evident rennonvations taking place at this hotel - good, this place needs it. Rooms are tiny, furniture is tiny and out of date. Location is okay, highway is mildly noisy, neighborhood is not the greatest. Internet is fast, though could be due to low occupancy. "Bar"/"Restaurant" staff very unresponsive/unfriendly - left and went north to Carrabba's for dinner.

“+P+E+R+F+E+C+T+” I traveled with my husband and my father in law, so we needed two rooms. Since we rented a car, it didn't matter in which part of the city we stayed. In or around Gaslamp was ridiculous expensive (we stayed three nights starting on a friday), so I checked hotels around the bay. I found out that is would be cheaper to book a 2 bedroom suite, rather than booking two separate rooms. Initially I was looking at The Half Moon Inn, but read the reviews on Homewood suites, and decided to go with Homewood suites. The price on both hotels was similar (on Hotels.com). I payed 500€ in total (around $700) for a 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom suite. About $116 a night per room, if you look at it that way AND you got the nice extra of a small living room, dining area and fully equipped kitchen (not a kitchenette, but a big one!)
