The suite was in an excellent condition, very well kept. One room comes with a queen bed and the other one with a king size. Every room has its own closet. It was very nice that there was free internet, wired and wireless. We didn't have the complimentary breakfast though, we like to go to Café 1134 on Coronado when we are in San Diego. This was actually our best hotel experience ever... It was very, very nice, but absolutely not uptight. We stayed in suites before, but this one gave us a much more comfortable feeling. It's nice to come "home" after a busy day in the city and not in some room with just a bed and a chair. In the evening we just sat in the living room, like we were at home... consider it a home away from home :-) And don't worry about airplane noise...They don't fly at night.

“very good Towne Place by Marriott Northwest San Antonio” New, clean, pleasant, quiet, very convenient, kitchen too. The only less than good was the complimentary breakfast--definitely not as good as a Marriott Residence Inn!

“This Is No Ordinary Courtyard” This has to be the nicest hotel in San Diego. The hotel is located at Liberty Station which is an old Navy base which has been remade into an area of upscale housing, restaurants, parks, and hotels. The hotel sits on an inlet of San Diego Harbor so it is right on the water. It is also very near the airport, although it has great insulation and you never hear the airplanes. I paid a bit extra and asked for a view room on the 4th floor. For my $15 a night I got a sweeping view of the San Diego skyline and views of the harbor and pool. Well worth the money spent. The hotel is about 10-15 min from downtown so you will need a rental car (parking is free). The hotel has all the amenities you would expect, restaurant, airport shuttle, lounge with full bar, coffee shop, and excellent patio for outdoor dining. The pool is beautiful and has great landscaping. Staff is outstanding and helpful. The room was wonderful and clean with an outdoor deck with incredible views. We could even see the fireworks at Petco Field in the evening. The room has a refridgerator and a K cup coffee maker. The wi-fi (free) is a bit of a problem as it ranged from average speed to none at all. Also the elevators at the hotel are mind numbingly slow. However, those minor faults are more than made up for by the beauty of the hotel. This is THE place to stay in San Diego as long as you don't mind the drive to downtown.

“無料駐車場もある便利なホリディイン” サンアントニオのダウンタウンもマーケットスクエアも徒歩で行くことのできる便利なホリディインです。ダウンタウンのほかのホテルは駐車場が有料の場合が多いのですが、ここは駐車場が無料なので泊まることにしました。建物は少々古いのですが、部屋はリノベーションされており快適に過ごすことができます。チェックアウト日は、ホテルに了解を取ったうえで、チェックアウトした後もここの駐車場に車を置いたまま(無料)で、街を観光することができました。リバーウォークからは少々離れていますが、それでもきれいな町並みを徒歩で20分も掛からず、その分値段もリーズナブルで、オススメできるホテルです。

“Muy buen hotel, con habitaciones amplias cerca del Seattle Center” El hotel es muy lindo, con habitaciones cómodas, limpias, estilo boutique,con cafetera, té, etc. Piscina con agua climatizada (tal vez no tanto por lo menos cuando fuimos) Personal muy servicial Cerca del Seattle Center lo que implica cerca de muchas de las atracciones importantes de la ciudad, pero que resulta un inconveniente por la noche ya que es una zona algo desolada si uno no va en automóvil. Hemos aprovechado una promoción de por 3 días de reserva el último es gratis. En resumen un hotel con muchas comodidades, super recomedable, en especial si vas en automóvil .

“Couldn't Fault This Hotel!” To be perfectly honest, if i was to find something wrong with this hotel, i'd be being picky! The rooms are amazing, really nice, a little small for 4 girls but who could complain at that! The location is good, your not too far from a lot of the attractions. If you look it up on google street view or whatever, dont let the view of the street put you off! The staff were fabulous, happy to do anything you ask - luggage, take pictures whatever you wanted. They were really chatty too. If your lucky enough, you could even get a view of the Empire State Building from the rooms at the back of the building - unfortunately, we weren't one of them. No traffic noise either (we were on the 14th floor however!), i would definately stay here again. Free internet, only downside is there is no complimentary breakfast, but as I say i'm just being picky!

“What the Doctor Ordered” My parents have been staying here for many years when coming to MD Anderson. I was able to arrange to stay here on a Saturday night recently and now understand why this is the place to stay when visiting MD Anderson. First of all, guests have to be patients or family members. Therefore, all of the staff is kind and helpful. Everything is geared to making the patient comfortable. There is an extensive reading as well as DVD movie library. There is entertainment several nights a week in the lobby. The restaurant is happy to accomodate special dietary needs. The rooms are extremely comfortable and quiet. Many rooms have kitchenettes. Hotel shuttles are available to take guests to area restaurants and stores. Access to the various clinics and the hosiptal is very easy.

“Great location with great rate” When I received an email alert from a Travel Newsletter regarding a great rate at Swissotel in Chicago, I had to check it out. Booked a two night stay at the rate of $109 per night, which is outstanding in downtown Chicago, in my opinion. We had a huge corner room with a view from the 29th floor out to the lake and downtown. It also happened to be the first weekend for the 2008 Taste of Chicago, so we were a short 3 block walk from Grant Park.

“A fantastic experience from the moment you arrive” The Westin Riverwalk is a beautiful hotel, located at one of the quieter ends of the Riverwalk - however you are less than a 10 minute walk to the Alamo. The building interior and exterior are immaculately maintained. This is one of Starwood's better properties. The friendly service started from the first interaction with valet. Check-in was efficient, helpful and welcoming. Nothing was too much effort for the valet team and JR provided us with some great restaurant tips. We stayed in a King Riverwalk View room. Our room (1209) was at the end of a hallway and very quiet. The room was a great size, tastefully decorated and had a great balcony to take in the views. Housekeeping never missed the mark - and more importantly, you never heard them congregating and chatting outside your room in the early hours!! In terms of hotel amenities, the gym was small (and always busy), but had a good range of cardio equipment that was well maintained and clean. Laundry service was prompt and of a high quality. We dined at Zocca - the food was exceptional, however the service didn't match that of the hotel staff.

“Mediocre at Best” The hotel is in a wonderful location downtown 3 blocks from SoHo. A few of the bad things with the hotel: No parking garage, A little worn out, every 10 minutes or so you can hear the subway and the floor vibrates. It's a do it yourself type of hotel you must go downstairs to the restaurant in order to get ice. The positives of the hotel are: Location, Cleanliness, Big Bathroom, the staff although sparce is friendly. This place will do if you know your way around the city and don't mind doing everything on your own.

“Very Impressive” When entering the lobby area off of State St you're greeted by a modern tasteful lobby area with plenty of pumped in vanilly lavender scent. I agree with a previous reviewer that the scent is quite strong and could be dialed back just a bit. The lobby area is smaller but very tasteful. There is a bar and restaurant located just off the lobby area. I was assigned a room on the 9th floor. The elevators were spotless and quick. A valid keycard was required for guest room floor access. The hallways were very nice. Brand new stylish carpeting, spotlessly clean walls and door and pumped in music at night with cricket and toad sounds included (sounds tacky but was actually very cool). The room was also very nice. A touchscreen phone which gave instant access to things like room service, concierge and wake up calls. The flat screen tv was very nice in size and had actual HD programming. The bathroom was also very updated and stylish with very neat faucets and a bathroom sink like no other one i've ever seen before. The high speed internet access (which i had to purchase due to my VZ Card not being useful from the 9th floor) was very fast but absurdly priced. This HAS to be some kind of record. My high speed internet total for one day was a wallet busting $21. Overall i thoughly enjoyed my stay at the Wit and I definately recommend it.

“Good, clean rooms, friendly staff” Nice hotel, the room was clean the staff at reception, in the restaurant and cleaning staff were al very friendly. Walking distance to little Italy. I had a good stay and would stay here again

“We Were Comfortable at this Place” We stayed at this place for five nights in March, 2008. Don't be fooled by the Robertson Street address--the place is a bit of a shock upon arrival. However, The Carlyle turned out to be a well-managed place (and there is an excellent Thai restaurant directly across the street). We had a junior suite. It wasn't as swanky as the photo on the hotel's web site, but it was comfortable and a lot more spacious than the standard rooms. It was also on the back of the hotel, away from noisy Robertson Street. The breakfast is well above average, with all the usuals, plus scrambled eggs and fresh fruit.

“Very good stay and hotel” The hotel is conveniently located approx. 1 mile from Galleria. The rooms are clean, spacious and well appointed. The check-in personnel is very friendly. A simple continental breakfast was provided.

“FAIRMONT CHICAGO - Great Location, Friendly People” Nestled just off the beaten path and about two blocks from the river the Fairmont Chicago offers an excellent location to operate as home base for your trip to Chicago. The staff were friendly and helpful, arranging many of the sightseeing events we enjoyed while in the city. There are many attractions withiin easy walking distance (The Art Institute is a must see and Millenium Park is a fun visit). The architectural tour by river departs a dock that is very close to the Fairmont and there are lots of restaurants nearby. The rooms were excellent and the club room is worth the extra expense. We would definitely stay here again.

“Expensive, but excellent service and location” Dead-smack in the middle of Times Square, so everything (eats, entertainment, retail, subway, etc) is within a very short walk. Hotel was clean, quiet, staff very helpful, room clean and reasonable size, elevators very fast - nothing but excellent features. Now for the price - given the location, you do pay through the nose. Or in my case, my company paid through their nose. Special convention rate w/all taxes, etc was $292/night, which isn't outrageous for the location and quality. Not sure I could/would afford on my own dime, but that's a matter of economics. If you can afford it, this is a great hotel

“Some nice touches but overall not worth it” Got a breakfast/hill country view/4PM late checkout room for Saturday night that was almost $400 after taxes, etc. Room was 3353 ... breakfast was average (had better hot breakfasts for free at Drury hotels) ... view was partial tennis court, parking lot and hill country ... had to request late checkout and was given 2PM instead of 4PM. Our kids were 5 and 9 ... the five year old likes the shallow part of the pool, but that also happens to be the part that leads from the waterfall pool to the other two pools that were too deep for him. Other kids in his age range also likes that area, so you have a bunch of kids and parents in a narrow area that's already crowded ... then you have traffic that goes through that area from people crossing between pools as well. So it can get pretty crowded. There's a separate kiddie pool but that's primarily for toddlers. Didn't like how the pools are laid out .... I prefer a large zero entry pool area for the small kids. Breakfast buffet was average at best ... poolside food was pretty good though. The smores activity at the pool was nice and very well organized and there was no extra charge. There were other activities scheduled throughout the day that looks appealing to kids as well, but we didn't get a chance to attend. I requested a room near the pool ... it was located at the far end of The room was clean, bed was on the firm side .... wouldn't call it "heavenly" though. Bathroom was clean and nicely appointed. The "heavenly" shower had dual shower heads, which was nice. Saw an ant on the carpet Saturday night after we went to the pool ... saw some more Sunday before we checked out ... not sure if they were in the room or we brought them from the pool. We were in a hurry and didn't notify the front desk about the ants. You may want to keep an eye out for them. We like traveling with our kids and are willing to splurge occasionally to try new places. We've been to many resorts and the Westin La Cantera is decent but not worth almost $400 a night. We're going to try the Hyatt resorts next time.

“Best Find in SF” We travelled to SF for a wedding in June 2007 and decided to travel with our small dog. The Laurel Inn was recommended to us by friends who had seen it on Citysearch as being dog-friendly, which it was. There is no extra charge for yourpet. We have stayed at the W, St. Francis, Fairmont, Hotel Rex, and Orchard Hotel in previous stays and this hotel has become our favorite. There is underground self-parking which is in the hotel building and while it is not free ($15/night), it is very convenient and safe. The rooms are very large and we had great views of the skyline. Linens are comfortable and soft. The bathroom is serviceable without the latest amenities, but certainly fine. The location of the hotel is incredible. It sits at the foot of the Presidio and is close to many trails through the park. There are a number of great restaurants and shops in the nearby pacific heights neighborhood, including a great Cuban coffee house down the street. The staff is very friendly (the desk attendant gave treats to our dog) and helpful. The morning breakfast (rolls/bagels/fruit/hardboiled eggs) is palatable and filling. There are nice touches like afternoon cookies and round the clock coffee. In summary, one could pay double or triple the amount to stay in a hotel with superfine linens, marble baths, etc and then get hit with parking/gym extras, but this hotel is very reasonable. The location and the staff makes this hotel one of those special finds. I didnt even want to write this review because I didnt want the hotel to get more crowded, but my wife forced me too....

“Great Location on the Riverwalk” If you are looking to have a great location on the riverwalk you cannot do better than this location. The hotel was nice even though we just had a regular king size room nothing special. The bathroom was small so if that is a problem for you I would upgrade. The room was clean and we had nightly turn down service also. We did not hang around the hotel that much to talk ith the staff. Our room could have had better lighting. The only problem we had was when we arrived from the airport they took our bags and they were suppose to bring them to our room. We had to call several times for our bags. When the guy came up to our room he thought we needed our bags taken downstairs. It took them a while but they finally got it taken care of. I would stay at this location again if I return to the Riverwalk.

“Pretty Standard” Spent a night here for a work trip. The hotel is in the less desirable downtown LA area, not super close to much, but in an up and coming area that soon enough will probably be full of life. Room was nice, everything is low - bed and TV. Bathroom has a peep through glass wall that would not work if you are sharing the room with anyone other than your significant other. Shower is huge, but has a basic shower head. Was able to check in early, which was a plus on this work trip. Check-in was friendly. Food in hotel lobby restaurant was above average for hotel food. Elevators were slow. Hotel turns into a club after dark, so it could be off putting for some, but I heard no noise. Overall pretty standard stay - would stay again if work was picking up the tab.

“Spacious rooms, Lush beds, and helpful staff” We are not fans of Fisherman's Wharf and always choose Starwood over Marriot, but we completely enjoyed our short stay here. We live an hour out of town, but as my husband was a guest speaker, the sponsoring group booked the hotel. The rooms are spacious, quiet and the amenities (bath and body aromatherapy) are great. The beds aren't as good as the Westin, but if you want to stay in Fisherman's Wharf this is a great option on the almost luxury side. The hotel doesn't have any charachter and it is a shame not to enjoy the great old hotels downtown. It is a standard business hotel. For the money, the St. Francis, the Palace or any of the big old Union Square hotels are more fun and steps to great museums, shopping and restaurants. Also - for tourists, unless you have a car, it is a bother to get to fisherman's wharf. Parking is $35. Amtrak stops a mile away and BART is downtown. If you do have a car, always remember it is easier to get to Fisherman's wharf over the Golden Gate than 101/Bay Bridge.

“The Marvelous Magnolia” I had a very enjoyable three-night stay at the Magnolia. The building itself is marvelous--it dates to the early 1920s. (Look for the Mobil Oil medallions on the elevator doors and the wonderful coffered ceiling on the ground floor.) The room was surprisingly roomy and well-appointed, particularly for an old property. And the hotel supplied me with a list of very good restaurants within a block or two. The highlight of the stay for me may have been my room location--I was on the 15th floor, and my windows faced the top of the next-door Adolphus Hotel, which is a Beaux-Arts fantasy concoction. Ask for a high-floor room that faces the Adolphus. BTW, I was a little apprehensive about staying in downtown Dallas, based on reports I had gotten earlier. But I never felt unsafe, even at night, despite the usual big-city contingent of homeless guys.

“We Enjoyed a Great Stay!” On our way to Europe, we planned a quick one-night stay in Manhattan. We booked through a special on Travel Zoo for $200/night. We arrived about 3pm on Saturday, March 31, 2007. The lobby is impressive and there are doors to both 44th and 45th Streets. The front desk staff promptly greeted us and gave us a corner room on the 45th floor. The décor is contemporary and chic. The bed was pilled with fluffy and down pillows, and made up with good quality sheets and a very soft, warm blanket. The bathroom is updated, had nice shampoo, lotion, etc., and average towels and provided very complete coffee/ tea supplies. We hated to leave the room but also wanted to hit the streets. There are several good Irish Pub/Restaurants on 44th Street; also the Cranberry Deli is a good place to get bagels for breakfast. The hotel is steps from the chaos of Time Square, Half Price TKT Office and most theaters. Our flight on Sunday was not until 9pm, so we asked about late check-out. They offered until 1pm for free and until 5pm for $100. However, they kept our bags and were nice enough to offer the restroom in the gym to freshen up before going to the airport. There was a shower (but no hairdryer). It worked out fine for us and was free of charge. We walked over to the Times Square station to catch the E train to JFK, it costs $7 each and takes about an hour. There must be a better way then the route we took, ask a local for advice because we had to walk at least a mile underground to the E train platform. The Millennium Hotel was a great place to stay during our 24-hour visit to NYC.

“Great Location - Tiny Rooms” I really liked the location of this Marriott Property but the rooms were very small (like a walk in closet). The bathroom was also very small. Everything was scaled down in size. I felt like the rooms were designed for pre-school children sized people. The staff were friendly, the valet parking was good. I also liked the concierge level and service. I would definitely stay at this resort again!!

“What a GREAT time - the BEST all around!” My husband had a meeting in Seattle so we decided to make it a quick family get-away. This trip was for business and for pleasure combined. A friend from Seattle actually recommended the Four Seasons. The chain has been running some great deals lately; Stay longer package deals (stay 2 nights, get one in Houston/Seattle and several other cities), and we have been taking advantage! We stayed for 3 nights over a holiday weekend. So lucky to have PERFECT weather in Seattle and to take in all the great things the city has to offer. Walked and walked. Cant' think of a hotel with a better location to Pike's, etc! Very easy to get anywhere from the Four Seasons. For my taste, the decor was very comfortable, very lovely and soothing. Bathrooms were wonderfully big! They really treat families well, here - at all FS. Delivering pop corn and sodas and fresh made cookies upon check-in. Superb FS service: Late room service (although it did take a LONG time and one of my daughters feel asleep waiting for dinner to arrive) was very helpful to us. Housekeeping even located a lost earring for one of my daughters. The work out facility is really one of the better hotel fitness rooms I have used with the treadmills facing large windows with pool and water views. The pool deck was a nice surprise, got a little crowded on the warm, sunny days. Nice Spa and fire pit, also. The one downside I can think of is the staff could not seem to supply consistent information on whether food could be served pool side- it never was while we were there. The in house restaurant was OK - Four Seasons pricey, very pretty. Oh, and we got an 8am wake-up call one morning we did not request. Thank goodness it wasn't 5am! Staff was apologetic. All in all, the pluses far out weighed the minimal minuses in my opinion and I would not hesitate to stay at the FS if I return to Seattle.

“A nice Boutique Hotel in the Gold Coast” I've stayed at the Talbott in the past and once again on a business trip for 3 nights. This hotel is located in the Gold Coast, just two blocks off Michigan Ave and in the heart of great shopping and restaurants. The lobby is charming with dark woods and comfortable chairs. Off the lobby is the "Restaurant at the Talbott" with a very nice bar area as well. In the summer this restaurant has a nice outdoor eating area which many of the locals take advantage of. I ate breakfast and dinner here, both were very good but not remarkable. Restaurant specializes in Northern Italian cuisine and was the former Bice restaurant. The rooms are where there is some room for improvement. My standard room was nice but could use a good carpet cleaning. There is Apple TV receiver and a flat screen, dual sinks, a normal shower and ample closet space and sitting area. Again, nice but not over 3.5 star quality. A must mention that after two 11 hour days of being on my feet and with an early flight Saturday morning I retired early on Friday night. Just after 9:30 PM a loud and rather obnoxious maid declared "TURN DOWN SERVICE" up and down the hallway. Why she needed to be so loud is beyond me. I would recommend this hotel overall. Especially if you are visiting Chicago as a tourist, this is an ideal location and a pretty good value.One other thing, as others have mentioned the hotel staff is very nice and the doorman is attentive and friendly.

“Excellent location. We WILL be back!!!” Came along with husaband while he was attending business meetings (at another hotel) and my infant daughter and I stayed here. Staff was very friendly. Room was spacious and the bed was comfy. Location was excellent.

“Small room, big fun” I felt like this hotel was inexpensive for a purportedly 4 * hotel in SF. We had a rate of $149 on a weekend. The room was totally adequate and I requested a view of Coit Tower and got it free of charge, even though they said they usually "charge extra" for that view. The room was small, very small compared to other hotels I've stayed at in SF, but the view was amazing. The Tv was old and outdated and not in any sort of armoire. It was sitting on a stand in the corner. The bathroom door was a slider that was on the outside of the room (not a pocket door) with a big gap, allowing virtually NO privacy. Something to be noted depending on who you're traveling with. Despite all that we had a great time. Chinatown and North Beach are within walking distance as is the Embarcadero. The lobby is nice with a great lounge and a decent restaurant. Across the street is a great park for kids with replica Chinatown buildings. It was a fine stay, but NOT fancy at all. Also, $50 parking!! Figure this in when deciding on a hotel. And I really don't think it merits 4*'s: inadequate bathroom door, no robes, no turn down, very small rooms, etc.

“Absolutely horrid!” Well where do I start? This hotel is terrible. Receptionist speaks little English and not very helpful and confused by very simple questions. Our bed linen was dirty upon check in so we asked for some clean sheets that we would have put on ourselves but was told he didn't have access to linen cupboard and gave us two towels to sleep on. Then our room had ants. When trying to speak to the man he wouldn't get off his mobile phone to talk deal with issues. Motel has a pool but I guess your skin may fall off if you use it, its absolutely filthy. As you will see from my other posts I am usually easy to please. Therefore trust me when I say stay away.

“Older Hotel with a bad face-lift” Stayed here for four nights (October 20 - 24,2010) because my national professional organization was having its meeting in the Hyatt's large convention space. The convention area (meeting rooms and exhibit hall) were very good. The lobby is very hip and modern. The valet, waiter service and restaurants (especially the Khyber Pass) were great. I was very disappointed with the rooms, and I was on the Regency Club Floor. We used express check-in and were given a handicapped room. There was only one, quite bizarre love-seat type chair and the bathroom had a sink and counter that was less than 3 feet wide. We thought this was an aberration until we were switched to our non-handicapped room. There was a paucity of dresser drawers, the closet was very small, and the bathroom was no better - incredibly small sink with no counterspace, very small, with small tub-shower. The Regency Club eating area was either too small, or they let too many guests in. Food and drink provided, as well as the service were excellent. All in all, if you are not forced to stay there for the convenience of attending meetings there, I would stay elsewhere.

“Not worthy of Hyatt name -- outside is nice, but rooms are not” Anyone staying here needs to know that there are two sections to this hotel. One is the "towers" with balconies overlooking the pool and/or the bay. The other section, where we were assigned (and probably most Priceline/Hotwire guests are) was the 70's motel-style sections, with outside entrances to the room. The cement floor outside our room was badly stained, as though people had gotten sick there. Our skepticism grew as we opened the door to our room to find filthy carpeting and bad mildew stains in the bathroom. I went back to the front desk to express my disappointment and asked for a room change. They said they were 100% booked and could not switch my room until the next day (it was after midnight when we arrived). Then the next day they apologized that there was no other rooms available either. Hard to believe...could it be because I was a Hotwire guest who paid $124/night? The room was bare bones -- not even an alarm clock!! Had to pay for internet. Upon complaining they gave me a free breakfast coupon for their restaurant and when we went there the next day found it was only for two. Had to pay for the children which made our total with tax & tip come to $40!! That was for a very mediocre-buffet. The grounds are nice but the beach is not easily accessible. Hotwire calls this "oceanfront" which it most definitely is not. The pool are was extremely crowded and the waterslides have limited hours. I have stayed in a lot of Best Westerns that are much nicer. Hyatt should remove their name from this property. By the way, it is the same hotel as the Hyatt Islandia. Even though their website claims it just underwent a huge remodeling project, the money was apparently only put into the pool and ground and probably new bedding...the carpets and bathrooms have obviously not been updated in a LONG time. I would NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. Please note that someone staying in towers might have much better reviews so if you are assigned here please make sure you call to request towers!! BUT...the last night of our stay we were at the Hilton Torrey Pines, which was absolutely INCREDIBLE. Read my review on that for a completely different experience...that place is everything a resort should be!

“Just Okay; Nothing Special” Huge lobby with no real retail. Luckily there is a good mall very adjacent. But don't count on this lobby for anything other than a Subway sandwich, a really bad pizza or Starbucks (mornings only for the Starbucks). Has a 'ghost town' like feel to it, which I really don't like it a hotel. Location is close to EVERYTHING. That's the biggest plus of this hotel. Rooms are comfortable, clean and have a lot of outlets for a Hyatt. Wireless is $9.95 for 24 hours. I bring my own. Paying hotels for it just makes no sense with the prices you are charged for your room. Fast room service, decent food, reasonably priced. 21% gratuity is included on your bill, so don't tip unless you think the service was fantastic. Valet parking is $30. The self park is $22 for the day so you don't really save that much. There are less expensive options - the lowest is about $20 a night, self parking, at the Circle Centre. Flat screen television (not high def), okay channel selection, refrigerator included in room, no tub-just a shower. Bathroom has decent lighting. Tiny work desk. If you plan on doing a lot of work in your room, you might not like it. Very limited surface space. All in all, a decent place. But nothing special. If you're looking for 'special', I'd head to the JW Marriott down the street. Much nicer place.

“Good choice for TS location” Stayed here recently for US Open. Good, clean, comfortable hotel that's not too big. Many of the chain hotels in the NYC/TS area are very large but this hotel is easy to get in and get out of. While it's not in the heart of TS, that's not all bad! It's close enough to the subway to be able to get just about anywhere you need, and for trips to Flushing (US Open, Mets) the 7 train runs from TS. The room was a good size for NYC, bed was comfortable, bathroom was average size, and it's nice to have a small fridge and microwave. I've stayed in many of the mid-upper end hotels (chain and boutique) in the area and would gladly stay here again, whether paying for it, or using HH points. A couple other items you may want to consider in the area: - Becco is a great dinner choice (good food, bustling atmosphere, $25 Italian wine options) nearby to HGI - Starbucks Times Square (47th and Broadway) - Blue Fin (for a drink, TS crowd watching) - walk the High Line park (take Subway to Chelsea)

“Even Better The Second Time Around!” Stayed at the Hilton Times Square Hotel for a second time around this past weekend and once again, was not disappointed. Rooms are clean, comfortable and of good size. Obviously, location is unbeatable - putting you directly in the Times Square area without any street noises penetrating the rooms (all on upper floors). Highly recommend!

“A solid four star property with lovely staff and club lounge” The Hyatt Regency Denver is a big hotel and host of many conferences. Despite the volume of visitors, service levels were excellent, consistent and professional. The concierges were helpful and friendly as were the front desk people. Our room was spacious, clean and quiet with fantastic views of the Rockies. We had access to the Club lounge, which offered a tranquil place to sip a coffee or cocktail. Adrian, the Regency Club Concierge, was extremely polite, friendly and helpful. He made the guests feel special and was an all-round excellent host. Thank you once again! Tip: book a mountain view room with club access. It is well worth it.

“Never Again!” At first glance, I really loved this hotel. I thought the location was great and the accommodations luxurious and the staff friendly. It only took about 30 minutes for that image to be replaced by the harsh reality. The restaurant closed at 10:00pm, but room service offers a limited 24-hour menu. Since I checked in at 10:15pm, and was starving, I had no other option than to order from the limited menu. I ordered a ham & cheese sandwich. After an hour I called the front desk to find out where my sandwich was. I was told they would have room service call me. After 10 minutes I called again and was told that room service would call me. Another 10 minutes passes and I'm about to lose my temper but Patrick, at the front desk, sympathizes with my plight and makes something happen. Room service calls and makes a pitiful excuse for the tardiness and says I'll have my food in 2 minutes. 10-15 minutes pass and Patrick is the one that delivers my food. They didn't charge me for the food - but that didn't help my anger. Over the course of the 2 nights/3 days that I spent there, I found the staff to be rude, misinformed and unhelpful. I've gotten better service at Best Westerns - which actually appreciate my business. I hated this hotel and I'll never stay there again.
“Typical, nice Holiday Inn” Good location for travel: close to O'Hare and right off of 90. It's just after the Chicago tollbooth. It's quiet with typical no frills, but decent decor.

“Typical format, but dirty rooms” Decorated in Hilton standard, it has the familiar surroundings needed after a 12 hour flight, huge rooms Egyptian count bedding, Crabtree & Evelyn amenities. For some reason there were a number of blotched stains on the floor, with a poor attempt to clean the mess. Location was good, just off Union Square,but its the "wrong" side for want of a better phrase, dirtier and more vagrants. Closest BART is Powell. Head to Dottie's True Blue diner, around the corner. Business centre is 40c per min which differs from Hilton's normal block rate. Frankly, this hotel has such a high turnover , its' difficult to be too comfortable, 1 or two nights fine, but there are cheaper and better options
“部屋の広さはありますが格調がなく残念でした” 部屋はエグゼクティブスイートですが ただ広いだけで格調は感じられませんでした。 ソファも色違いで統一性がなく残念でした。 ラウンジの食べ物はかなり良かったと思います。 特に酢豚は肉はかりかりに揚がっていて パイナップルも酸っぱくセロリーも美味しかったです。

“Great Hotel for our meeting!” Stayed at the Crowne Plaza LAX for a 3-day meeting. My guestroom was fantastic! Flat panel TV, great lighting, powerful wireless internet, and the bed was more comfortable than at home. The meeting rooms were very comfortable and the food at all meals and breaks was top notch. The staff was friendly and responsive. I would highly recommend this hotel for any occation!

“Nice rooms, shame about the staff...” Stayed here for a one night trip from New York to see something of Philly. Found the hotel on foot, but the surly receptionist "Gladys" could not check me in cos I was a little early, so I spent some wasted time sitting at reception, whilst her colleague was checking in other families. The rooms are pleasant, much better than Holiday Inn Express rooms in the UK. The room was spacious. The breakfast was basic, but complimentary and the hotel arranged a shared minibus to the airport for me. The location is fairly good, sandwiched between touristy sights, and shops. I had a nice evening meal in the ihop just over the road.

“Average Marriott Decor and Rooms” I travel for business and spend a lot of nights in Marriotts. I have a definite idea of what to expect from a Marriott property and this property meets but does not exceed those standards. However, opinions are subjective as I overheard other travelers raving about the rooms and the breakfast buffet. These were families with children and not adult only travelers. The rooms are very standard small "suites" with basic hotel furnishings and a decent bed. There are two flat screens but the reception was fuzzy. If you need to be in this area the Marriott Suites is a decent choice but for a few dollars more I found the Renaissance across the street to be superior to this property. Overall, a clean average property but nothing to get excited about.

“Courtyard property - with good service” The Courtyard at Washington Convention Center meets the Marriott standard -- well-equipped rooms and well-maintained property. The location is within a former bank-building that retains on the lobby-level vestiges of being a bank (vault, etc). However, the rooms on the upper floors have the usual character of a "chain-hotel" -- standardized but not very interesting. Service is very good -- front desk is helpful with room-assignment and with maps and directions. If satisfied with staying in a standardized Marriott property, this should fit the bill -- but if seeking something distinctive, you may want to go elsewhere.

“Amazing Service” Great room, good location-2 blocks from 16th street mall. Great service. Alexis booked my airport shuttle for me, boarding pass kiosk in the lobby, speedy, friendly check-in. Had extremely early airport pick-up and after the driver called, the man at the front desk greeted me by name and had my receipt ready when I came down. Only complaint is that they charge $10 a day for wi-fi. Went to the Kinko's next door and did my internet business for $3. I would definitely stay here again.

“Nice hotel, good location, friendly staff” The hotel is in a fun location. There are a lot of restaurants and shopping near by. The staff are extremely friendly, internet is free, there's free breakfast, and the beds are comfy. For a NYC hotel it's pretty quiet. The rooms are small and so is the bathroom but that's to be expected in most NYC hotels. I was at the hotel for business so didn't get to explore as much of the neighborhood as I wanted but I'd stay here again. If you stay here check out Eataly a few blocks up on 24th and 3rd maybe? It's a neat market/restaurant but there are different stations in the place - there's espresso/gelato, a pasta/pizza restaurant, a fish bar, a cheese/meat station, and what looked like a restaurant that had entrees like steak and chicken. I'm sure I'm missing all that's in there but it's a neat place to check out.

“great for families” With 2 and 4 year old children, we were very happy at the hotel. It was best to spend time at the pool and lazy river area. There is also a small artificial beach. Although the property is near Sea World, the lack of shade and long lines at Sea World were less fun than just hanging out on the hotel grounds. As far as prices go, the room itself was a great price for its level of quality, but the room service, buffets and restaurants were not inexpensive. The nachos were a good value because they're ample enough for more than one person. Most particularly the service in the hotel was excellent. Everyone working in the hotel was polite and seemed to go out of their way to make our stay pleasant. They refer to you by name and ask if there's anything else they can do for you before leaving any encounter. For children, there were pony rides, the Hyatt camp for kids, even a spa for kids. The hotel can cater to small children or teenagers very well. The kitchens accommodated my son's food allergies reliably. We visited the spa and found it to be fairly good, though not particularly inspiring. The therapists were variable in quality. The hotel facility itself is not very new and is showing signs of wear, though it is a beautiful place. Overall, I was impressed with how good the hotel was for the price. There is a pretty nice bar and amenity for people who are not there for a family visit but it's basically geared toward people with children. I would not hesitate to return but would enjoy hanging out in the pool or going off property to something other than Sea World.

“The Candlewood Concept is Perfect for Us!” We loved our four nights in this hotel. There we did not have to worry about breakfast times and could have our own selection of food at times when we decided it (of course you have to buy the stuff before by yourselves). The Candlewood Suites is excellent when you want to self cater because there is no restaurant / breakfast at all. The room is not very big but big enough for a couple. The ktichen in the room has everything you need for 2 people - even a dishwasher. The staff at the reception was always superfriendly and helpful. The location is excellent - close to the main bus station of Manhattan (but not to close as for example the Staybridge Suites), close to the Lincoln Tunnel and a 8 min walk to Times Square. If you are looking for fabric stores the are a about dozen in the street of the hotel. The only minor thing is that a good supermarket is not very close - the one which is in walking distance is not what you would excpect in this part of town. And the price range is reasonable for New York City. One more thing: There is construction of a new building going on just in front of the hotel. Therefore we asked for a room on the other side of the building and we just heard nothing. On the other hand the construction does not operate during the night anyway. Therefore not really an issue.

“One of Chicago's Best Hotels!!” The Allegro Hotel is one of my favorite hotels in Chicago. I’ve stayed at other hotels in the city, but I wanted to stay at a Kimpton Hotel this time, and the complimentary wine hour surely helped with the decision. The hotel is located a block from the L that goes to O’Hare Airport – get off at the Clark stop and walk a couple of blocks south. The entrance is a bit confusing at first because the check in desk is actually on the second floor. But if you need help with your baggage, there are always proactive bellboys that are willing to help out. Check was pretty quick, and we were lucky there was a room available for early check in. When we went into our room, I was expecting a very tiny room. The size of the room was actually decent. The décor is wonderful, the bed is very comfortable (I remember sinking into the bed and dozing off within five seconds), the television is pretty large, and the bathroom was a decent size. One good thing about this hotel is that you can hook up your iPod to the radio and play your music. I guess the walls are pretty thick because we had the music pretty loud while we were getting ready to go out and no one complained. In fact, we never heard people walking around the hallway at night. There are a lot of restaurants in the area, and State Street shopping, city hall (Daley Plaza), and Michigan Avenue are just a few blocks away. The location is great for the L because the Washington and Clark stops are just a few blocks away. Our favorite part of the hotel was the wine hour. The first night there weren’t a lot of people in the lobby, so they had flatbread pizza to go with the wine. They also had chestnuts and warm apple cider. The second night, there were a lot more people, so they only put out a variety of cheeses. The people serving the wine are very friendly and attentive, and they remembered the type of wines we were drinking – even if there was only one type of red and white. Check out took a while since everyone was checking out at the same time. We left our bags with the bellboy since we weren’t ready to leave Chicago yet. Overall, this hotel is wonderful. I would definitely stay here again because of the price, location, and wine hour.

“Tired and Run Down but ok for budget traveller” We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights during August 2004 whilst on a backpacking trip around the USA and Canada. We booked this hotel online at a reasonably good price for the budget traveller, and was not really surprised at the condition of the property considering the price we paid. The entire outside of the hotel and our room was extremely tired and worn. Our room was clean and tidy, and appeared to have been recently painted ,although it appeared than no pre-painting work had been done, with the fresh coat being straight over the top of the existing surface condition (including the mould covered air vent in the bathroom, now freshly covered in paint!). We found the staff to be cordial without being overly friendly and the housekeeping staff did an acceptable job. While we didn't take advantage of the smorgasboard breakfast of donuts, coffee and juice the hotel had on offer, there is an good diner next door "Lulu's" and a buffet style restaurant "Luby's" across the road. Although the hotel is located next to a busy highway, we found no problems with traffic noise in our room. For the energetic, its about a 25 minute walk to the downtown/riverwalk area, or a 5 minute stroll to the nearby streetcar stop which will take you downtown. All in all, you get what you pay for, and this is pretty standard for the budget chain motels.

“Perfect for business trip” I stayed just one night for a business trip and it was perfect for what I needed. The evening reception and breakfast buffet were both nice. Hotel appears to have been recently renovated and the room was very clean, however it had a somewhat older feel because the ceilings are low and the bathroom is on the small side. But my king suite was large, with a flat screen tv in both the living room and bedroom. I would highly recommend this hotel for a longer-term stay, because of the well-equipped kitchen area. My room faced Harry Hines (a busy street) so the traffic noise was noticeable beginning at about 5:30 am. I will most likely stay here again when returning to Dallas on business, but I would ask for a room that does not face Harry Hines next time, and would suggest that light sleepers do the same.

“Great night at the Carlton!” The lobby was stunning. We arrived after 8pm....there were candles on the lobby steps, the music was nice, the lighting was perfect. The room was very handsome....clean, well decorated, comfortable beds with soft down bedding and lots of pillows. The room was a deluxe double and fairly small. (room 1037). It was an inside room and wonderfully QUIET. We did not hear hallway noise nor street noise. We still had a view of the upper stories of the Empire State Building and enjoyed its lit-up nightime view. I have stayed in much larger rooms at the Waldorf and the Rihga, but the price was good and much more handsome of a hotel.

“Clean, Comfortable and Homey.” Value, Location, Comfort, Helpful staff make Park South a real winner. Its located in a quaint neigborhood with restaurants,bars, the corner store and deli, all walking distance. The subway is also only a skip away. The rooms were small (like most NY hotels I guess) but very clean, cozy and very tastful. The bathroom had nice luxury toiletries, soft towels and comfortable white robe to use. The bed was extremely comfortable with nice quality linens. The furniture was nice as well as the flat screen on wall. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful. The business center was very helpful ( I used it to print off tickets to Musuem of Sex:) The breakfast was oh so delicious. Fresh crossants, bagals, fruit, yogurt, cheeses, pastries, cereal, cold meats (the smoked turkey was devine), juices, coffee and all FREE til 11am (!!) Saturday morning. Park South is definitely my fav hotel in NY now. Just a beautiful stay.

“Needs updating throughout” I stayed in the L'Enfant 15 years ago, and it hasn't changed much, unfortunately. It is very dated and needs to be totally redone. The air conditioning barely worked (runs continuously to keep the room at 75), the TV is fresh out of the early 80's, with a poor selection of channels to boot, the carpet is worn and dated, all the room furniture is scratched and worn. The hotel sits right over a freeway entrance and next to a rail line so there is constant road noise. The only positive thing is that it is conveniently connected to the Metro. The area around the L'Enfant is not good for night life and restaurants, so you need to use the Metro to go to places with restaurants, or take a walk. It is convenient to the National Mall which makes for a nice evening walk.

“A very nice hotel” Myself and two friends stayed at this hotel for 5 nights and we would happily recommend it to anyone. The Hotel is clean the staff are very friendly and informative. Our room had two comfortable double beds and was a nice size. There is a free shuttle bus that runs from the hotel to Universal Studios/City Walk. The staff in the restaurant and the bar were friendly and efficient, and the food was lovely. Overall a very pleasant stay.

“Perfect area, price point and nice people behind the scenes” Travel dates May 21, 2010 for 5 nites. I am a La Quinta Inn follower. I am a member of their hotel program. I go to New York city often and now that I found the La Quinta, just one more nice thing to look forward to. Located in Korea Town (K-town) very close to subway; Macy's literally right there and 34th street retail and Madison Square Garden. Many diverse establishments including grocery, cafes very close with the Empire State Building down the street. The rooms were very nice; I paid 150.00 + taxes of course --per night. Clean rooms, nice bathroom. Nice lobby with FREE continental-type breakfast. Love this. There is a bar/restaurant on the roof-top. Nice touch and views of (Empire state building and more). La Quinta offers room types including AARP, AAA, Military; helps with the price. LOVE THIS PLACE AND WILL RETURN. B Roberts

“Great hotel with everything you need!” Very highly recommended - Clean, comfortable, free internet, kitchen, couch, roomy desk, 2 TVs, separate bedroom, friendly, bigger and better breakfast. Great all-around! We slept great - the separate living room was very nice. I can only add: When we checked in, they asked if we were from the swimming group. When we said no, they put us away from the group, and said they were extending breakfast hours the next morning to make sure there were no traffic jams. What a great idea!

“Clean Clean Clean” We stayed here at the end of December. The hotel was extremely clean, and the room we got was a king suite! It had a bedroom with a TV, a bathroom, a little kitchenette area (fridge, microwave, counter), and a living room area with a TV. (room 210) We parked in a gated area, and although the hotel is located near the airport, it was still close to Graceland, which was our main purpose of visiting Memphis. If you stay here, eat dinner at Marlowe's, which is about a 5 minute drive from the hotel, and also at Four Way Restaurant (good soul food). If I were to ever find myself to be in Memphis again I'd stay here again, hands down.

“As far as Ws go, this one is just average” I do a lot of business travel to Seattle and I like to stay downtown. I also like the Starwood brand because I think they have one of the best rewards programs. So I decided to try the W Seattle. I have stayed at many Ws accross the country and usually I love them. However, this W is just average. POSITIVES: 1. Location. Its right in the heart of downtown. 2. The bed. This is a given in a W which, I believe, all use the "Hevenly Bed." I love this bed, it is pillowed topped and has nice linens and a huge (and heavy) down comforter. It is so confortable. I was so impressed with this bed the first time I stayed at a W in 2002 that I actually bought one. So its nice to have the same bed in the hotel that I enjoy every night at home. NEUTRALS: 1. The room. It was nicely appointed and had a nice window seat with lots of funky pillows. However, the view was of a hotel accross the street and as far as the theme of the room, I felt it was mediocre at best when comparting it to other W rooms I've visited in other states (like San Diego or New Orleans). 2. The staff. They were average at best, nothing out of the ordinary. Not particularly friendly or helpful but definately not rude, pushy or mean. NEGATIVES: 1. The lobby. Its tiny as compared to many Ws I've stayed in and the bar, while nice is TINY and often too crowded to even get a seat. One thing I've always enjoyed about Ws is the club-like feel of their lobbies and the cool bar scene. This W has neither. 2. The elevator and hallways. They are extremely dark!! It is bizzare how dark they are. Maybe its to hide the fact that this hotel is an older hotel that's been renovated to become a W and so they darker down the hallways so that you can't see the age of it. However, I found it a tad unnerving and I'm a guy. 3. Expensive: I paid over $325 for a night at this hotel and when compared against staying at the other Starwood properties in town (or any other hotel for that matter) that can generally be reserved for $200 or less, I think this hotel is a bit over-priced.

“Surprisingly 5 Star” I stayed at the Sofitel in New York a few weeks ago and was blown away by the overall standard of the hotel. Service is phenomenal, the quality of the room and hotel in general are great, and I really enjoyed their bistro. The location is perfect too. Great place, will be back!

“At the Waldorf.... March 24-26” I really wanted to love the Waldorf. I had set my expectations accordingly i.e. low, changed in a few large bills for smaller bills to tip everyone we came across and I had even made sure not to wear blue jeans at the Waldorf=Astoria so I could take in the historic hotel and feel one with my environment. Unfortunately after the front desk, service pretty much went down hill. I remember Lauren checked us in and she was quite nice giving us the option of two rooms to choose from and even supplied us with a map of NYC, complimentary water and a verbal overview of the hotels restaurants. The room (1727) was nice enough, pretty clean and I could find almost no fault with the room, loads of hot water, working quiet heater, no inside or outside noise. The lotion that the staff leaves from FRESH is top-notch. Unfortunately at the Waldorf apparently the doormen are too busy doing other things (standing around looking Waldorf=Astoriaish) to hold open doors. At the Waldorf bell hops are too busy (talking about other guests broken luggage) to take your bags and just leave you standing around feeling foolish in front of the hellhop desk. At the Waldorf cleaning staff never fully make your bed, but instead leave the bedspread and shams folded in the room on the luggage rack for your entire two night stay. At the Waldorf's Bull and Bear Restaurant where one soda, one drink and dessert run $50 the staff is far too busy to provide your table with a table cloth or service of any kind. At the Waldorf you will be left to fight off black town cars sent over by the staff to take you to the airport. The WA even has a sign inside suggesting you only take yellow checker cabs, so why an employee would send a black town car over to it's guests is beyond me. If you want to stay here, you are going to do it no matter what you read. It's not horrible, but I just say make sure you know why you want to stay here and that it's not because you think you're going to have some super four star treatment by the staff of the Waldorf=Astoria.

“Great hotel, good value” I booked the executive suite with breakfast for $ 130 a night. The room huge and has a separate bedroom / living room. The bedroom actually seems a bit empty because it's so big. In the living room is a sink & fridge and the furniture is ok. Free WiFi is a big plus since I was there on business. Every room has a separate airco. The only odd thing I could find was the closet. The one in the bedroom has a weird construction and the one you want to use for your clothes is in the living room. but apart from that it was clean, & comfortable. The hotel is near the galleria shopping mall (it's one block down the street). It's a courtyard so you don't get the full hotel service, but what they offer is ok. Breakfast was good (works with coupons you get at check in) and the reception service was great as well (got me towncar right on time). they have a small internet/print station in the lobby (great for e-tickets) and beware of the warm cookies in the morning at reception I think they are addictive ;-)
“Great hotel in a great location” Excellent hotel right across from Independence Park. Staff were friendly and attentive.

“Short of a Ritz Carlton or Four Seasons, as charming as you'll get” Seaport is simply a splendid hotel: Extremely tasteful without being snobbish, elegant without being cold. Indeed, the staff is remarkably warm and caring - I found this to be true on a business trip in August, and again on vacation in December. Seaport is a modern tower along the waterfront, near the Renaissance and the Westin. Wonderfully convenient to the Silver Line, and in the warm weather it's just a few steps to the wharves & the scenic harborfront. From the Silver line, go UP a level to the concourse & use the lovely plaza-level pedestrian bridge. It brings you in above the lobby, but saves crossing streets and dealing with traffic ... and it brings you in past classical music piped through speakers in the Seaport's little garden area. The front desk staff here is beyond top-notch: Helpful and warm, and well-informed about the city if you have questions. There's also a good concierge. The porters/valets working the door are great, too - equally friendly, professional and well-informed. The good news: There's no "back" side of the hotel facing the industrial zone. Bad news: There's also no front side facing out onto the harbor. Instead, Seaport is set perpendicular to the waterfront (same with the Renaissance) - so views improve a bit if you're on a higher floor closer to the water, but the average rooms have no magnificent water views. The rooms a understated: A slightly nautical theme, perhaps, with light wood tones and light colors. All attractive, new, crisp. Smallish rooms but sensibly laid out with excellent amenities. More importantly, there's there "cozy" feeling that very few business hotels come close to achieving. Enjoy the remarkably sensible doorbells: You use a switch in the room if you wish to illuminate little "service room now" or "please don't disturb" signs. Best of all, the doorbells mean there's none of that hideous keys-on-door rapping in the early morning, followed by the awfully loud "Houskeeeeeeepppping!!" that you hear in so many business hotels. Instead, the maids can use the doorbells - which generate no noise to other rooms. The gym is magnificent - first-rate machines in ridiculous abundance, along with a spa-like locker area (including heated tile floors) with first-rate showers and one of the best steam rooms I've found anywhere. (Don't forget to use the ingenious eucalyptus-water spray bottle; there was one in the men's steamroom that added a lot of sinus-clearing power to the steam. I've heard the women's side doesn't have one -- if not, ask at the desk). The only improvement here would be to make the pretty pedestrian pool more interesting (removing the lap-lane barriers would be a start) ... and surprisingly, there is no hot tub. That's the only serious squawk I've got about Seaport. The restaurant needs a makeover: It has the feel of a Clarion (or an upscale cafeteria at a nursing home) because of the boring design and decor. The overpriced breakfast buffet was just too small and had too few interesting choices. Lunch and dinner might be better. Room service is also mondo expensive. But this is one place where I'd spend the money: Clam chowder, a coke and a pizza is crazy costly, but that 'coziness' factor means a lot. Room service here is more of a treat than a "oh well, I'm too tired to go downstairs" sort of chore. Swing out the flat screen TV and enjoy. Climate control is modern and efficient, amenities are outstanding. Bathrobes and FREE overnight shoe cleaning. Which brings up the nicest feature here: They hit you with a small service charge when you register, but then expect - and accept - no tips. It's not a "tipping isn't necessary" guildeline, but truly a "we kindly request that you not tip" policy. I forgot and offered an extra buck to the cheerful and efficient guy working at the Starbucks - he politely declined, saying that's included already. Free Internet: A very nice extra! Look for special activities here. At Halloween, they did an imaginative game that send kinds to a half-dozen areas of the hotel to gather candy. At Christmas, they had an outstanding $99 a night special - and did up the public areas with plenty of appealing Christmas decorations. Nearby are Legal Seafoods Test Kitchen and several interesting seafood places along the wharves.

“Horrible hotel in a great location” In the weeks before Christmas, New York hotels get busy and with low availabilty, I had to get a room at this hotel for ridiculously high rates, something this hotel certainly does not deserve. The only good things about this hotel are the great location (close to Central Park, Rockefeller Centre and MOMA) and the room size which, for New York, is large. The hotel is horrible in every other way. Poor attitude and low level service all across - whether it is front-office, room service or the restaurant. Lack of room amenities (not even bedroom slippers; no coffee-maker; wifi for a fee) - and one tea served to your room will cost you $17. Breakfast will cost $45. Expensive for this level of hotel - even The Peninsula is cheaper. On most occassions, room service forgot some ingredient; once it was the tea bags itself! The carpet in the room had several stains, the laundry service (outsourced) was not upto the mark. You cannot reach the elevator bank without being confronted by Hilton time share agents luring you to a 'presentation'. I will do my best to avoid this property in the future.

“Schnuckeliges Stadthotel” Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral (5 min von der U-Bahn Station Medical Center entfernt). Die Zimmer sind neu eingerichtet inkl. einem Flat-TV. Der Zimmerservice ist phantastisch. Hab selten in einem Hotel so gut gegessen. Auch eine nette Bar und ein Frühstücksraum hat das Hotel. Sogar ein Schwimmbad ist im Hotel vorhanden. Das Badezimmer war in meinem Zimmer ganz neu.

“2nd great stay, 2nd great experience” Not much more to add here, the title says it all. This was our second time in a year staying here at Nine Zero. Location is great, and we were able to experience more in the area this time around than last year based off of our familiarity with the area. Getting to and from the airport was super quick this time, with not much of a cab ride at all. Didn't need a car; everything we needed to reach was within walking distance or short cab fare distance. The staff was great and helpful as always. The orange and lemon water in the lobby were a staple of our frequent ins and outs of the hotel. Always refreshing after baking in the summer sun. We had a(nother) great time here. This time, we had a room with not that good of a view, and we were on the 15th floor, so it all depends on where you are placed. Our room location was very quiet and we hardly saw and definitely did not hear any other guests. Very comfortable room. Definitely recommended!!! Thanks for providing us with great accomodations for the second time around...

“Terrible service and terrible amenities” We booked this hotel for a family trip to Jacksonville, Florida and were very unhappy with our choice. The hotel is right off the exit but hard to find due to no signage and is located around multiple other "run down" and closed hotels. At check-in the clerks were very rude and unhelpful. They took a long time to deal with customers and were not apologetic. Once in the room, basic amenities such as dish washing detergent, etc. which are common to Residence Inn were not provided. Breakfast was total chaos with poorly stocked breakfast area, lots of mess all over with food all over the serving area, and unfriendly service. We stayed 2 nights and confidently will never return again. A bad experience that I would never recommend to anyone. Stay away!

“Avoid Room 1102” Management certainly knows Room 1102 abuts an air shaft that is so loud it sounds like you're under a flight path or the F train is passing by...continually. Otherwise the hotel is fine.

“Parc 55 Visited 20 months later...last minute deal” My original review was for January 2008... I had wanted to go up to SF for a couple days but was tentative of commiting to the purchase a hotel room due to the threat of a BART STRIKE...Getting into the city would of been VERY problematic. (see parking tip) Now, since my trip was Last minute (No Strike, but I was told many Bay Area people took that monday off because they expected horrible traffic issues) I was having issues making a SF purchase on Priceline with the usual hotels I like. Usually I try to pay between 80-100 = taxes.. I tried the PARC 55 site which has a room for 125ish a night without taxes. I kept clicking around for specials on their site. I found a NON-REFUNDABLE special for the same room for 102 a night (two nights with taxes was 235...PERFECT!!). The hotel is close to the POWELL STATION...I knew it was SAFE, CLEAN and though VERY large doesn't feel so which is why I liked it the last time I visited. My biggest issue my last visit was the lack of consistent Internet...I actually called PARC 55 to ask them if it was more stable. They said they thought so. They also mentioned that the Internet cafe around the corner I mentioned in my last review is closed for 6 months of remodeling ( FYI) The hotel has done a remodel since I visited last. Check in is now in a much more modern area on the second floor. They let me check in early at 12pm which was pleasant since I had been driving from LA and on thr BART for 40 min . The lobby was full of people but not a long wait. Originally they were going to put me in a 13th floor room but I asked my receptionist if they had anything with a view..She upgraded me to the 23th floor which was VERY appreciated by me.Sometimes being pleasant, asking with a smile makes a difference...AlsoTheir new lobby/close by bar area welcomed the NEW York Mets...I heard this is a hotel for a lot of the teams... My room was as I remembered, big bathroom with a cimfy bed, I did like that they no longer used LATHER for products which I though were sucky on my last stay. THE INTERNET was $12.95 a day but WORKED perfectly. they had both wireless and plug in. I was VERY HAPPY! AREA COMPARISION: Since I know the city better this time around I can confidently tell you that this location is WAY better then the Union Hilton and Hotel Nikko. Though they are only a block away sometimes you can feel it in a city such as SF. Plus both those hotels looked SOOO BUSY. **PARKING TIP: Go to the BART SITE, buy an extended parking permit ($5 a day,not 24 hours) Then take the BART into the city. Parking in SF can be 35-50 a day depending on the area. 3 days of parking (15) + a roundtrip from pleasanton (10.55) was = $26 bucks... Also If it is a three day weekend, that Monday parking is free! ***Dining. Hotel is super close to a SUBWAY, WALGREENS (buy water), COLDSTONE, PIZZA PLACE within a block. There is a nearby Chinese Resturant. My fave is PUCCINI & PINETTI off Ellis and Cyril Magnin..GREAT happy hour ($3 champagene but not boozy.

“Decent place, good service, but loud and annoying guests all around, including pool party” I stayed here a few nights during a trade show, and have mixed feelings: The room was clean and comfortable, no problem. Breakfast, not included, was nevertheless reasonably priced and of good quality. Hotel staff were all pleasant to deal with. The free shuttle to the convention center was convenient and appreciated. What was very annoying was the fact that they have a pool party every Sunday afternoon, which means guests can't use the pool unless they pay $20 admission and that there is incessant booming music hitting all the rooms on that side of the hotel, making an afternoon nap impossible. Also annoying were the many guests in town for the A-Kon convention. Scantily clad and completely inappropriate dress is a complete understatement for some of the characters lounging around the lobby, and the continuous running around in the hallways, slamming doors, and loud screaming into the night were completely intolerable. The hotel staff confirmed that they attract a party crowd on weekends, thanks also to the night club downstairs. This is very unfortunate, as it is in complete contradiction with trying to get some sleep and some work done! It is also unfortunate that the hotel seems to tolerate this sort of behavior in the first place.... I'd probably stay somewhere else on a return visit to Dallas.

“Very Nice and Kind of a Bargain” This was our 2nd time here. We aren't crazy about staying in Fisherman's Wharf area as it dies early but the cable car stops right behind the hotel & the streecars go a block to the front. If you buy a one week pass (about $25) you can use it all very cheaply but buying single rides on the cable car is very expensive-we would have spent 5 times that much. The hotel is clean, quiet and well serviced. We spent only about $115/night after taxes (geezer rate). In my opinion there are few places at Fisherman's Wharf worth eating but the cable car gets you close to North Beach & all the way to Union Square. A few blocks walk to the Hyde Street car & it will drop you at the door of Frascati which is wonderful. Also it is a nice long walk mostly along the beach to the Golden Gate. If you are tired of walking take the bus back to Union Square.

“Location excellent, the rest well.....” First off, let me say that I was very pleased with the location of the hotel. The property is in walking distance to Grand Central Terminal which is perfect for catching the subway and reaching all of your sightseeing destinations in and around New York City. There is also a Starbucks and several restaurants within walking distance. One restaurant we really enjoyed was the Fifth Ave. Tavern. Very nice atmosphere and excellent food. Now to the room. The first room we received smelled very badly of cigarette smoke and there was an odd (and still wet) stain on the bed. We immediately asked the front desk for another room. The front desk was very accommodating and provided us with another room. The second room was much, much better. It was fresh smelling and was clean. However, the downside was that the room was very small. Yes, I have heard that rooms are small in New York City; however, I have stayed at other places in NYC and the room was considerably larger. The bed was pushed so close to the wall, that it was difficult to climb into the bed from that side. Not only was the room small, the beds were small. Impossible for two adults to sleep comfortably in one bed. Traveling with a family, size of the room is very important. We felt like we were crammed into the room like sardines. Yes, the good news is there is so much to do in NYC that the room is really just a place to sleep, but when you travel with a family, lack of space means it takes longer to get ready in the morning. Not to mention, relaxing at night is near impossible. We were on top of each other. Not happy at all with that. As far as front desk staff, and the doorman. They were very polite and accommodating. Nothing wrong there. I will not be returning to the Kitano, for one reason and that was the size of the room. Perhaps there suites are much bigger, but I probably wouldn't be able to afford that rate!

“W -- as in, WHY would you stay here?!” Sigh. W's are really hit or miss. Sometimes they work, sometimes not. If you are OK with what this hotel is -- a night club hot spot, more concerned with style than substance, with tiny rooms and impractical furnishings that will simply frustrate you -- then this hotel will be great for you. I stayed here for a one-night business trip two days after a colleague of mine, and we both had the same impressions, although she didn't have to switch rooms several times.... First, it is basically a block from the White House, so location-wise, it has a lot going for it. I checked in around 6 pm on a weekday night; the lobby was crowded (with bar patrons, not hotel guests), but the wait wasn't too long. The staff was somewhat friendly, but efficient (the door and bell staff were, as usual, friendlier than the front desk). When I arrived at my door, I noticed the doorbell and other indications of an accessible room, which I did not want. I looked inside, and the layout confirmed this. So I went down and asked for a non-accessible room. The host explained the rooms were all the same, and gave me a new room. I was surprised to enter the new room and find ... a bed seemingly only inches off the ground, and the rest of the furniture similarly designed for people about 3 feet high. The rooms are tiny, so perhaps they figure low-to-the-ground furniture will help make the room look bigger. It literally took me 5 minutes to figure out how to turn on the main lights; I was relieved to learn my colleague had the same confusion. The bathroom is typical W, modern and sleek, but the sink is a raised bowl with a faucet whose opening is about 3" above the drain. I could not fit two hands underneath it. I'm sorry, but when style comes at the expense of function, it's gone too far. This W goes too far, and falls from hip into the far too frustrating category. When I returned from a late dinner to my top-floor room, I was unhappy to hear a pounding disco above my head. A call to the front desk assured me the noise would stop by 11. A second call some time later assured me the music would stop at midnight. Then the room physically started shaking, as the people above me were obviously jumping up and down in unison. This time I insisted a manager come to the room. She said it was a wedding reception, and would be going on until well after midnight. (Of course, if it hadn't been a reception, it would have been the W's standard night club.) To her credit, she felt the room vibrate and heard the noise and quickly arranged a transfer to a room on a lower floor. Once I figured out how to turn off all the little neon lights, I got a decent sleep, just two hours later than I wanted. I'm an SPG gold member, and have stayed at several Ws around the country. This is one I will not re-visit. But, if you're looking for a night-club atmosphere, this is definitely your spot.

“Great Hotel and Great Location” The hotel is located right in the heart of Center City at 17th & Samson Streets. It's very close to many restaurants, bars, shops and several gyms. The lobby was very inviting. We were able to get a really great rate via hotels.com - $159 prepaid for each night. That was less than half of the list price. I would suggest searching around various internet sites before you settle on a price. The room was not huge, but was large enough to fit a king size bed, several chairs and a desk. There was a city scape view. The room was tastefully decorated and the bed was amazingly comfortable. The bathroom was huge and had a shower stall separate from the bath. The shower felt very great and there were nice toiletries provided. The only downside was that the tv was limited on how many stations it carried. There may have only been about 15 channels. The service by the staff was good and I would definitely return to try the Sofitel again.

“Large hotel, nice view” As to be expected this Sheraton is a good hotel, rooms are large and beds are good. I guess all rooms also have a nice view, we overlooked a "play" fountain and the water next to it. But the only thing Sheraton isn't clear about are the additional costs of ammenities. At this hotel we learned that logging on the paid Wifi from different devices you also have to pay for every device. Beside it really isn't a real customer friendly way of adding cost to the allready high room price you'll have to pay it isn't displayed anywhere. After we found out that every device was charged i went through all the blabla terms for using the WiFi connection. No where was to be seen that logging in from multiple devices also meant multiple charges. They where friendly enough to bring back the charge to only one charge when we commented about this. But still the feeling of being charged multiple times for every devices wasn't good. I really think that $10 for 24 hour Wifi per room really is the limit. Besides this everything was possitive, location was good near shops and restaurants. Hotel had a fullsize Starbucks in the lobby. Downstairs well maintained PC's where available for free and also the printing in black and white was free. Wifi in the lobby also was at no charge. Certainly a hotel to like.

“Change of Management” This hotel use to be great. After stopping in and out over the past three years, the front desk staff was terrific. But now, the regulars are gone and you are afraid to ask the front desk for anything. I came to learn that management had changed and so have i.

“The place to stay for LA Live” I stayed at the hotel for a week during a convention. Prior to my trip, I heard horror stories from colleagues who had events at the LA Convention Center, how it was very dangerous, there were homeless people wandering around, and in general how dirty it was. When I got there ... I was thoroughly and pleasantly surprised. The hotel is fairly new, so it doesn't show the convention wear and tear like others like it do. The front desk staff was exceptionally helpful upon check in, tracking down packages and leaving messages for guests for me. Because I'm a platinum member, I was upgraded to an Executive King, which is basically a corner room with a large hallway. My room faced the Nokia Theatre and Staples Center. The room was large, fresh and very clean. There wasn't a tub, but the walk-in shower was spacious. The sink area had a shelf underneath for storage, which was very nice. Large windows dominated the room and the sunlight could be intense in the morning. The drawback of having a corner room with large windows are the lights from the Nokia Theatre and Staples Center. I had to use paperclips to close my curtains properly so I wouldn't be disturbed by the flashing lights outside. The concierge/executive lounge is one of the best I've ever been to. I enjoyed breakfast there each morning of my stay except Saturday, when the lounge was closed. The variety and quality they had there was outstanding! Because there were several groups in-house, gLAnce bar, the Mixing room, and the ION pool bar were frequently closed for private events, so I wasn't able to experience them. The LA Market restaurant is good although the lunch service was a bit iffy although not terrible. There are several restaurants within walking distance of the hotel, and every time I walked around, I saw security patrols which made me feel very safe. There were events at the Staples Center and Nokia Theatre while I was there, and although my room faced those venues, I wasn't disturbed by the noise.
