Overall, this is a great hotel and I'm looking forward to coming back!

“Worst nights sleep ever.” I am sitting in my hotel bed at the Luxe right now with my iPod headphones on having tried to block out the noises from the people in the room above me for the last two hours. It didn't work. The walls, floor and ceilings in this hotel are literally paper thin. I had to move rooms last night as I was trying to get work done as I am in LA for business. They had originally put me 5 feet from the valet station which also happened to be right ON the ice machine. WONDERFUL right? So I could hear the cars pull up. I could hear the two way conversation between the valet and the guest.... you get the picture I could hear everything. Then lets not forget that I thought it was a major car crash the FIRST time someone got ice. So they moved me. That was nice. Until I could hear the entire two way coversation between the guy in the room next door and the person he had on speaker on his cell phone. I'm not kidding. I the walls are so thin I could tell what they were saying. Then at 5 am this morning when the people upstairs started their day I was jolted from my sleep. I can tell you without joking that it sounds like the entire band of KISS is upstairs with their boots on doing step aerobics. I put on my iPod to try to get some much desperately needed sleep. And as mentioned earlier... it didn't work. I can hear them showering, flushing the toilet, walking, dressing, chatting, watching tv.... I'm almost surprised I can't hear them breathing. Needless to say, I cannot recommend this hotel to anyone who wants a peaceful nights sleep. The main building of the hotel looks pretty but I'm up at the spa building that looks like it was built in 1962. Beds are pretty comfy. TV is tiny tiny tiny. Bathroom is tiny tiny tiny. You can't see what time it is on the alarm clock when the lights are off. I'm just to unimpressed.

“Not great, but not bad either” Had to spend 5 nights in Jacksonville for business. I like Omni's very much. I did have a few small gripes which may seem petty, but not to me. I prefer a firm mattress, this one was one of those pillow-top types, nice enough but just not firm enough for my liking. The real issue I had was with the shower. The water was warm, but I couldn't get it hot. Who doesn't want a hot shower? And more importantly, the shower liner was really mildewy and smelled terrible. Not quite the optimal shower experience. On the positive side, front desk people were incredibly helpful and friendly, the rooms were clean and spacious, and the internet free if you are an Omni member. Not bad, but not great.

“clean & friendly staff” Well the title about says it all. We were there for a few days on business, and this was the closest decent hotel to where we needed to be. As others have mentioned it's in a pretty dull, commercial area of town. No decent restaurants in the nearby area. When we were there the hotel lobby area was undergoing a renovation so it was all torn up, but I'm sure once its complete it will be nice. None of the rooms have been remodeled yet though. I don't know if they will eventually be remodeled or not. Our room was clean, but just old and kind of gungy. It had a musty smell to it. We asked about another room and they offered us another one, but it smelled just the same. The carpets were stained both in our room and in the exterior hallways. We joked every time we returned to our rooms that we had to "take a left at the bleach stain". As do other Radisson hotels, it has the Sleep Number beds, of which I am not a fan, but whatever. At least there were not springs poking in my back. The staff was always very nice and quite helpful when we had any needs or questions. I guess if I had to be in that particular area of LA again for business I would consider staying there because there's not much else around.

“The capital” This was the first time that I have stayed at this property but the ritz never disappoints. The location is not as great as I would have liked but DC is easy to vet around in and cabs are cheap. Room was clean and the club lounge was inviting. It was great having a fitness club next door. Why would anyone stay anywhere but a ritz property. The service is great and the amenities top of the line. Only negative is the wife does not like the shampoo and conditioner. The hotel can even takes care of that problem. Great trip. I would not bring my kids here as there is no pool.

“Okay for a quick stay” Used a big chunk of my Hhonors Hilton points to stay in this hotel for a night, on my drive up the east coast. This property allows dogs, which is what I needed. The hotel is clearly an older property and is not as plush as expected. The rooms are a bit raggedy, but sufficient. The staff was particularly friendly which makes up for any short-comings of the room. Located in a great area of downtown DC -- right by Dupont Circle and GW University, which made for a nice walk w/ my dogs.

“This place is filthy” Having read the other reviews - I was looking forward to staying at this hotel. But please beware - this place is in need of a good clean as a start point and ideally - a complete refurbishment. My bedroom was tired to say the least - the bathroom was nicely equipped but the bedroom was awful. The public areas are frankly awful. The dining room is a collective of broken worn out chairs and the carpet was filthy. At 12.00pm there were still dishes left over from breakfast - just no need for this lack of basic skills. The rest of the hotel is grubby and tired - it really lets down the omni brand name and it has put me off staying at any of thier hotels again. You have been warned

“Didn't feel like a Hampton Inn” I was supposed to stay two nights and after only one night I left. I couldn't wait to get out. While it is fairly clean looking overall and the lot is well it, the hotel looks and feels like it used to be some kind of downscale brand, not a Hampton inn. I felt like I was staying in a prison bordello! Fluorescent lighting abounds. There's no auto entry doors on the lobby. The pool is about as big as a postage stamp. The rooms are cavernous feeling, making furnishings and accoutrements appear tiny, sparse, and cheap. My room had a slightly funky/musty smell. Walls are PAPER THIN. If your neighbor is watching TV you'll know what channel they are watching. If they sneeze, you'll know it. If you said "bless you" they'd hear it! Trust me, I heard my neighbor sneeze. I was just glad I didn't hear other things. My room overlooked a junky looking construction equipment rental yard. They were setting up a "Cash4Gold" thing in a meeting room when I checked out..very sketchy. The best thing I can say about the room is that the bed had a nice featherbed topper. If you are a very, very no-frills person who needs to be in this area and wants a free breakfast with your stay it may be for you, but otherwise I'd head for a comparably priced hotel in nearby Santa Clara.

“Great old Grande Dame of a hotel, with an AMAZING gym facility” Great older property, with a not so great history - while on my business trip, I was frequently reminded by locals that this was the hotel with the Legionnaires' Disease breakout years past. I really enjoyed this hotel. The location was excellent within easy walking distance of City Hall and any number of shops, stores, restaurants, including an entire business focused food court downstairs. The hotel itself was old school Grand Dame - Westin St Francis and The US Grant come to mind. I found the rooms very spacious, good internet, great room service if a little expensive. What put this hotel over the top was the access to the Bellevue Gym. Rated #2 hotel gym in the US last year, it is a 93,000 sq ft facility (not a typo) over 3floors, and access is FREE. At other highly rated hotel gyms, there are fees, such as Meridien Parker in NYC, rated #1 last year, with a $20 daily fee to go. The Bellevue was free access with hotel key, incl the classes. Great downtown location, beautiful old building, great facilities. I will stay here every chance I get.

“Good Overall... made me realize difference between Embassies"” I had a comfortable room for a business trip but I realized Embassies are all a little different. It might be because of the two family weddings and kids sports conference at the hotel but the evening reception fare was nacho chips and salsa served in cardboard trays. Other Embassies I've stayed in really put on a good spread. This, however, wear a weekend. Overall though, comfortable.

“Adequate Hotel” We spent one night at the Sheraton Gunter. In fairness we did not consider this hotel when arranging our rushed trip to San Antonio. We were only there due to our hotel advising us on arrival our room was not available! We arrived tired after a days journey from New Zealand and to top it off we arrived at midnight. The front desk staff (despite the hour) were accomodating and friendly. Our room was certainly not what we would book by choice- it was clean, but dated, tiny and positioned next to the lift shaft (which kept us awake despite our need of sleep!) The Airconditioning unit was also incredibly noisy - so much so we turned it off and put up with the heat in an effort to sleep. There was good coffee in the room which was appreciated. Continental Breakfast was adequate and included. The staff were friendly and again accomodating. This hotel is dated and certainly the room we had was noisy and small. It is however in a good location and the staff seem happy to help even late at night.

“good hotel for a one night business trip” Check in was easy and staff was gracious and friendly (and they gave me two chocolate chip cookies for being a Starwood Gold Member!). Room (2201 north tower) was clean with good work station, but very small. I stubbed my toe twice trying to get between bed and desk chair. Valet parking was easy (which sounds good considering some of the reviews I read about parking lot). I had a great rate and, as always, a wonderful bed.

“Ganz in Ordnung, Top-Lage” Wir haben nur eine Nacht im Powell gewohnt. Unsere beiden Zimmer waren unterschiedlich im Dekor, jedoch schien keines neuer oder älter als das andere zu sein. Die Einrichtung ist neueren Datums in warmen, jedoch eher dunklen Tönen gehalten. Wir hatten ein sehr kleines Zimmer und eines mit weit mehr Platz. Beide hatte die gleiche Rate, so dass man ggf. bei Check-In um ein größeres Zimmer bitten sollte. Das Kleinere von uns war so klein, dass wir Mühe hatten zwei große Reisetaschen so zu postieren, dass wir nicht dauern drüber hüpfen mussten. Es gelang uns nicht so wirklich. Beide Zimmer gingen zu einem sehr kleinen Innenhof, was natürlich nicht viel Licht abgab. Die Zimmer haben keine Klimaanlage. Alternativ gibt es einen Van an der Decke und man kann die Fenster etwas öffnen. Viel Luft war über den Innenhof an dem heißen Septembertag jedoch nicht herein zu bekommen. Leider fiel das Bad deutlich gegenüber dem Schlafbereich ab. Hier wäre eine Renovierung bald einmal nötig. Die Fugen waren verfleckt, die Armaturen veraltet und matt, der Duschvorhang etwas unhygienisch. Die Dusche selbst war in die Wand eingebaut. Wenn man den Vorhang zuzog stand man im Dunkeln! Der Serive am Front Desk war sehr freundlich und arbeitete schnell. Der Gepäckjunge war etwas aufdringlich und das zum Hotel gehörende Deli wurde gerade umgebaut. Absoluter Pluspunkt ist die Lage. Das Hotel liegt direkt an der Ecke zur Marketstreet am Cable Car Turn Point und gegenüber des Nordstorm-Kaufhauses. Perfekter Ausgangspunkt mit div. Restaurants und Cafés in der Nähe. Ebenso positiv war der für diese Lage wirklich gute Preis. Kein Internetangebot war günstiger als das des Hotels selbst. Ich würde das Hotel für einen kürzeren Aufenthalt wieder wählen (jedoch um ein größeres Zimmer bitten). Für Aufenthalte ab 4 Nächten wäre es mir zu dunkel und zu klein.
“WONDERFUL experience - will go back again!” Excellent Location! Wonderful Ambiance! Romantic! Trendy! Great, Comfortable Beds! Valet Parking! LOVELY BOUTIQUE HOTEL!

“You call that room service?” We stayed here for a night in May 2008 to celebrate our anniversary. It was great overall if I discounted the negatives associated with our room service experience. Our corner room (18 tier) had a great Michigan avenue (south) view as well as an incredible (western) sunset view. We live in Chicago and could even see our home from this vantage point. Unfortunately room service failed miserably. When we arrived on Saturday we ordered a late afternoon snack. It came up cold and terribly overcooked. Because we were hungry we ate most of it anyway. We forgot to call for cleanup and later headed to dinner and a show. Much to our suprise when we returned to our room the mess was stil there. It was quite clear that we had finished the food. The turn down service had happened but they chose to ignore the mess. Since it was quite late we decided to put the plates and mess in the hallway. I called down and alerted room service about the new hallway mess. They apologised and told me that someone would be dispatched to pick up the remains immediately. When we awoke on Sunday we noticed that our remains had not been picked up. I assumed that the individual who dropped off our breakfast would take care of it. He also chose not to address this mess. It sat there for another hour. It was quite the Holiday Inn look! I had been reminded at check in that we had a $70 food credit for breakfast. We placed our order on Sunday morning. The food was presented right on schedule. They missed one item but we ignored this small issue. This time the food was prepared much better. Parts were cold but overall it was good. They did not presnet a check with the service. When we checked out later that morning the bill included an overage charge of $16. Apparently our light breakfast was $86. That was way overpriced. My belief is that the Four Seasons Chicago is a great porperty. If you have the chance, book the room! The location, views, and people who work there are great. Christian at the Front Desk and the woman with glasses at the Conciegere desk are two that stand out as trememdous ambassadors of the FS Brand. With competition from the Peninsula, Park Hyatt, and Trump, and demand slowing things will have to sharpen slightly to keep the competitive FS advantage. Good travelling!
“Great Location” We could not have asked for a better location. The staff was very nice and helpful. My only complaint was the tiny bathroom. Otherwise great!

“Ladies of the Night” I stayed at this hotel by default. My flight was cancelled while I was in Dallas and I had to find a hotel to overnight. Expedia gave me a $50 hotel credit so I tried to find a hotel that I did not have to spend much more money, since I had already had to extend my vacation(rental,food, etc). I checked out the BW Conference Center because it had good reviews and the cost for one night stay was only $52. I was skeptical at first but my husband and I figured it was only for one night and they did have good reviews. Well I will just say you get what you pay for. The hotel itself does not look bad it's just that because maybe the rates are so low it attracts another "element" of clientele. When we went to check in the woman at the desk told us we would have to wait because check in was not until an hour or so, as we went to have a seat in the lobby area I noticed they had a conference event going on, this motel must be known for that because the conference goers seemed to be very happy. but then I noticed a woman who was sitting near us having a phone converstaion telling someone to meet her at the hotel, she looked like she was high on something and her heels where even higher she then started talking loudly cursing into the phone and said she will just meet them across the street. When we went over to the desk there was another young woman who was in front of me and she was telling the clerk she needed to get back into the room because she left her shoes in the room she had no luggage and was dressed "sparingly" she looked like she was high and antsy. At this point I was concerned about the rooms and when I talked to the clerk I asked her about the clientele she acted like she did not know what I was talking about and she reassured me that this was a very nice hotel and that we would enjoy our stay she asked if I would like to upgrade to a suite for $30 more I said yes thinking that maybe the suites were more nicer than a regular room. We walked into the"suite" and it had a faint stale smell and the furniture was old and dark my husband refused and said it looks like the "party" room so we went back and got a regular room which was actually alot better it was clean even though it was small for a one night layover it was fine. This motel looks like it was a older motel before and it was spruced up low ceilings in the hallways, dark and very tiny elevators. This is not the kind of place I would stay for more than one night and I definitely would not stay here again. I think the management should look into what kind of businesss there clientele are into and try to discourage this activty in there motel. Sad.

“basic clean rooms, bad location” we stayed here the last 2 nights of our roundtrip through california, nevada, utah and arizona. The rooms are very basic but spacious. A littlebit on the dark side, but clean and comfortable. And very quiet at night! The staff wasn't very friendly. The wifi was terrible (no connection or very slow!) and the 2 computers at the lobby we're not working and when they functioned, the printer didn't function. so don't try to print your boarding passes. For the airport it is a good location, but in the evening it is a bit of an unsafe place to be. For the amount paid it isn't bad value.

“Not a lot not to like” This is my 3rd stay at the Chandler Inn. This time for 5 nights taking in a conference and some other business. I find it hard to understand the negative reviews this hotel gets. Sure, its a budget hotel - but you know that when you book it. With the Marriotts of the world @ circa $300 per night you are not going to get the Ritz for $150 per night in Boston. Regardless of what people have paid that is the 'going' rate. Don't use the hotels own site use one of the others - the rates are better. Yes the rooms are small and the bathroom smaller. I understand the guy who said the rooms remind him of his college dorm - but they are entirely adequate. The location is great (5 minutes to Backbay station or 10 minutes to Boyleston) with cafes around the corner, a CVS across the road and pizza and other food within a few minutes walk. The neighbour pleasant and non threatening and the hotel is clean. I've always found the staff pleasant and helpful. There appear to be some refurbished rooms (last time I stayed on the 8th floor in one) but I prefer the non-refurb room I stayed in the 1st time and this time as it has a desk. The free wifi works well but not, I guess, in all rooms as I've seen a few people sitting in the corridor with their laptops. Lets face it you are not going to stay here if you are on a corporate expense account. But as a budget choice in Boston I don't see much not to like. I'm back in Boston for another conference in June and have already booked my room.

“Nice hotel” The hotel grounds and restaurant were very good and in great condition. The stay included the Ocatilla building. This building location is a problem since there is not an easy way to get to it from any automobile location. It is also hard to find from the signage on site. It offers an area for a continental breakfast, snacks, beer and wine with afternoon hors d'oeuvres and some dessert at 8 to 9. The quality of this is not the greatest and it may not be worth the value unless you partake on the beer/wine. The only major issue is the lack of maid service on a reasonable basis. Turn down was ignored, next day room make up not happened, even after calling it in. This is not a tolerable situation for a hotel that is supposed to be an elite facility. The restaurant is very good and may make up for this issue, maybe. There are better resorts out there- especially the Royal Palms, which is exceptionable for the same fees.

“Good renovation” This is my second review of this hotel. I stayed here exactly a year ago when the renovations were still underway. The wait is worth it and the work has been sensitively carried out. We stayed in the Winthrop suite. Nice view down onto the Freedom trail and some historic buildings. Yes, the rooms are a little tight on space (bathrooms particularly) but more than adequate and are attractively furnished. Staff are very friendly (particularly after coming up from NYC!) and helpful. Some friends from the UK staying in a Back Bay hotel visited and were blown away by the public areas. They were paying the same price for a standard chain hotel. I recommend it - but pick your room carefully if you want space.

“Best bang for a buck!” Have stayed in various hotels in Baltimore. This one is by far the best value for the money. It's location is perfect, the staff is friendly, and the rooms are awesome. The rooms are big and clean. Am a bit confused about some who rated the hotel for noise - how one rates a hotel located in the heart of a downtown and expresses a dislike for noise???? Good breakfast and an ok exercise room. Highly recommend -

“Impressive” This place was very attentive to all hotel details. The room was nice; the towels and shower were good, the kitchenette was very helpful, and the staff was very friendly and accomodating. The bed was a little soft, but not bad. I was part of a group that used the ballroom across the street for a meeting, and the acoustics were extremely poor. It seemed that no adjustment made it possible for everyone in the room to hear at a reasonable level. That detracted from the overall experience. The hotel did a nice job on the buffet, and the waiter service in connection with the buffet was excellent.

“What a great hotel!” Don't believe the unfortunate reviews from August--this hotel is wonderful! My family and I (husband and two daughters) just returned from a weekend getaway to Chicago. The hotel is exactly as advertised--but even nicer (how about that!). We went to New York City for spring break this year, and to Europe in June--but our girls thought this was the nicest hotel we've stayed at! The room had two queen beds and was unbelievably spacious. The bathroom was beautiful--tile and granite, with two sinks and a lighted makeup mirror. Housekeeping does a great job, too--everything was so clean. The staff was very friendly and outgoing--even the doorman and the maids said hello and greeted us with a smile. The staff was very helpful, too--any question or request was promptly addressed. We were even able to get to Sunday Mass with easy directions and a current schedule of Masses. The location is perfect--just a few blocks from Michigan Avenue. We never took a taxi, nor any type of transportation. We walked walked walked all day and evening--and felt very safe and comfortable. Great hotel and great stay. I would highly recommend The Talbott and wouldn't hesitate to stay there again. Thanks for a super weekend!

“Hidden Gem Definately Stay here again!” I absolutely love this hotel. This was our second time staying here in the past 3 months. It is a great hotel that is near I-95. We stay here on our way down to Florida from NC. Everything is perfect with this hotel. The staff is very attentive and friendly. The rooms are large and can accomodate a large family. And you cannot beat the price.

“Delightful” No complaints whatsoever. The location is great. The style and upkeep of the property are first rate. This will be one of if not my only choice for a place to stay in Seattle in the future.

“Very Nice” The staff here make the stay. They are very friendly and genuine. I would not call the rooms deluxe, but they are comfortable. I had a great egg white frittata fir breakfast it was a refreshing healthy choice option and delicious! (also served with a genuine smile)
“Nice Marriott” I stayed one night at this Marriott ,very comfy bed and room was nice,staff were very friendly,not to many eateries nearby but overall enjoyed my stay at this Marriott.

“Great Location, Disappointing Food” Stayed for two nights while in town on business. Great location, just 2 blocks from Reading Terminal Market, a stone's throw to the convention center and a short walk to great restaurants and the major tourist attractions. Room size was good, had an issue with the TV but maintenance solved this in short order. Unfortunately, dinner at the restaurant was very disappointing and so was room service. Next time I stay, I will be sure to eat elsewhere

“Love Love Love This Hotel” Okay..the only place to stay in Midtown Manhattan is the Benjamin Hotel. Service is TOP NOTCH! And everyone is SO NICE! AND HELPFUL! My room was huge..large king bed, with a small kitchen complete with refrigerator and microwave. The bathroom was also a nice size..and with great lighting..and the robes are to die for here. The room is decorated nicely...very clean and professional..but also homey. I had a large desk area which was good, because I did have lots of work to do...even had my own fax machine on the desk. The room faced out over Lexington Avenue, which was nice...I was high enought that I could see what was going on but didn't have to hear all the noise. The bed was really comfortable and had tons of great pillows. Closet was nice size and came complete with iron/ironing board. Room Service was excellent as well.. Everyone from the maid to the front desk to the doorman...could not have been nicer to deal with. I had a really hard time getting a cab one night and the doorman ran down the middle of the street to find me one...such great personal service and everyone had a smile on their face...always. This is a gem of a hotel in a great location..so that you can walk everywhere...I will DEFINATELY return to the Benjamin again!

“A Grand hotel that needs updating” I stay as a platinum member at many Marriott's. Stayed here for 4 nights in the old tower in an executive suite. Grounds nice with a lrge lobby and convention area. Fitness center better than most Marriott's. The room was 884 square feet with a dining room and a living room. Bathroom is large but no counter space, peeling paint in the shower and someelses hair on the shower wall. Towels, linens, blankets and amenities like shampoo all Fairfield quaility. Bed was a double and not bad. Floors creaked when walking and thin walls sonyou can hear your neighbors. Room overlooked the pool which opens early so beware. You must take a cab to get anywhere like Georgetown. Metro will get you to DC attractions. Starbucks is a nice 1/2 mile walk. Conceirge was crowded but adequate. Employees friendly. This hotel should be at least 4 stars but needs some updating.

“Good choice, no doubt about that” I stayed for one night in the Windsor Suites. I opted for this hotel because of the location near the suburban railwaystation. You are really in downtown Philadelphia and I thought it's a perfect location. When I checked in they told me that I had to wait for a non-smoker room so I took a smoker room. The room was really big and spacious and there is everything what you need for a long stay. The bathroom looked somewhat worn but it was clean. There is free wireless internet and even free popcorn! Altough I stayed for just one night I found the fridge very useful. There are some places nearby to buy food and drink such as a seven-eleven. Their business centre is also good, there are 2 computers and printing is free. And don't forget the free breakfast which is awesome. Altough the hotel looks somewhat old and worn (but absolutely not dirty) I would opt for this hotel again on my next visit.

“One of the best” Great hotel, very well appointed and spacious rooms, and very well maintained, excellent service and nice extra little touches, like the pet fish in your room and the free wine hour in the lobby. Great location. Highly recommended!

“Designed by a frequent traveler?!” Everything was well thought out and nicely appointed. The room could be made dark, and was very quiet. The bed, pillows, towels and robes felt luxurious. The shower was set high...good for tall folks. Specific programs and channels could be found easily on the flat screen TV. A Keurig coffee maker made making coffee and tea easy. Free internet access. At $190/night for Gold Coast Chicago, it was a very decent value. Only change I would request--trade out the mini-bar for a mini refrigerator.

“Excellent hotel with great food” I stayed at the Peninsula Chicago for two nights in October 2008 while on business. Had a room on the 15th Floor with views of the Water Works. Everything about this property was wonderful. The lobby and conference areas were beautiful and put together really well to host a large event with multiple meetings. The quality and selection of food made attending meetings a real treat, and room service, salads and burgers at least, were great. Now for the room: it was huge! The bathroom had its own couch! Excellent desk and business set-up with extremely comfortable bed. I don't even think I used every piece of furniture in the room it was so big! Can't beat the location either - you're literally steps away from Michigan Avenue shopping and world famous pizza.

“3 Strikes” I travel to work a fair amount and, as a loyal Hilton Honors member, I have stayed in this particular HGI 4 times with 3 negative experiences. My third bad experience, which happened in June 2012 includes those nasty words that no hotelier likes to hear - bed bug. Checked in, headed to the room and was surprised at the strong chemical smell in the room. I called the front desk about it and was informed the carpets had just been cleaned. They said the smell should dissipate by evening. I headed off for a day of meetings, returned to that same strong chemical smell. I got into my PJs, flipped on the TV and turned down the bed to find a rather healthy 5mm bed bug sitting on the pillow of one of the double beds. Called the front desk after taking a picture and a manager came up to inspect. They took the "suspicious insect" and moved me to a new room with no chemical smell. Upon checking out, I found out that despite their claims that they don't have "that type of insect" that the room I'd been initially assigned had JUST been sprayed for bed bugs that very morning. For me, that was the last straw after two previously negative experiences. Although the managers and concierge are friendly and helpful, I just can't stay somewhere where I need to worry about what I'm taking home with me. Below are my other experiences at the HGI W 35th. My first bad experience was this past January. I stayed for a few days with my fiance while tacking on a few personal days to a work trip. HGI have adjustable mattresses in their rooms (think poor man's Sleep Number bed). Without getting too technical...the mattress is essentially built like an air mattress with compartments. Some of the compartments in our mattress were popped. The result was a crater in the bed. I complained to the manager about it, who assured me that I just didn't know how to use their adjustable mattresses. A maintenance person was sent to "teach" us how to use it, and discovered - SURPRISE - that we had some deflated chambers. We were told the mattress would be fixed, by 10pm that night, it wasn't...and it was time for me to head to bed. That makes 2 days with a large crater in the bed. Believe it or not...my second bad experience is a repeat of my first. I came to the hotel for work, and found myself with a crater on the bed. The explanation is "deflated chambers" in the mattress. I don't know how it happens, but it's pretty hard to tell that it will happen, as you really have to lay on the mattress for a few minutes before you can tell. Between the bed bug and the bad mattresses, I won't be going back to this hotel...ever.

“Good hotel for business travel” I stayed overnight here recently in one of the renovated rooms, which was had the two key ingredients: cleanliness and comfort. The staff was pleasant and courteous, and I'd be happy to stay here again.

“Great Experience” We stayed here for nearly 3 months in one of the suites in the summer of 2009 and had an excellent experience in spite of the hotel going through major renovations. The management and staff could not have been more helpful. We highly recommend this place for an extended stay. The location proofed perfect for us in the Seattle area.

“Great location” Very nice hotel located only one block from Michigan Avenue. My room was large and clean with a nice city view (22nd floor). The decor is sleek modern. Nice pictures frames of Chicago. The bathroom is small. The tub water drain very slow. The front desk staff was helpful and friendly. The roof pool has nice views of the city and the lakes. However, they need to clean the windows. The food at the hotel restaurant is average. For breakfast I recommend the Corner Bakery Cafe just one block from the hotel. Stay away from the hotel parking lot. They charge $48.00 plus taxes per day. You don't need a car in Chicago. Use public transportation or taxis. Overall, this is a good hotel value for downtown Chicago.

“Expected more from the Sheraton brand” My husband and I stayed here for the baseball game, the Orioles vs. Texas Rangers, August 21-23, 2010. This is a great hotel if you are going to Camden Yards. It is a 7 minute walk from the hotel to the ball filed. The hotel lobby was beautiful and smelled wonderful! We did arrive early and the room was not ready. We have never had this issue, so they took our luggage and we waited in the lobby. Now, granted we should have asked for an early check-in, but apparently that was not available at the time. We waited in the lobby for about an hour and a half and an employee, Rena the concierge host, approached us and asked if she could assist us. We told her our dilemma and she left, then 10 minutes later she returned with our room keys and off we went to get ready for the game. Now, we paid for a stadium view, but when we opened up the curtain there was a gorgeous view of the Hyatt. Now, I'm not complaining because we were happy to get a room a little early, but still not what we paid for. The front desk staff in general are unfriendly, but the housekeeping staff were so nice! I would only stay here if I absolutely had to. Rooms seem a litte dated with their seating choices. The bath tub could have used an update, but overall it was an ok room. Happy Traveling!

“The surprise extra charge...” The location, next to a subway and right by Chinatown, was great for us. However: 1. I had called and requested 2 double beds instead of a queen and they said if I arrived early this would be no problem. I arrived at 1 PM, but they insisted on a $30 per night extra charge for a "special request", even though they admitted it was not a premium room. 2. the shelf between the two beds broke when I put some books on it! 3. The heating/ AC fan was so noisy we had to turn it off to sleep. We did not have breakfast here, as it was $18.95! There is a Starbucks and a nice coffee bar called Brew within a block. For lunch, Sun Sai Gai at 220 Canal Street, 2 blocks away is great, and there is a dessert place right next to it

“Okay hotel but would probably try somewhere else.” My husband and I stayed here from 12/31-1/3 for vacation/Winter classic hockey game which was AWESOME! We booked our room through the hotel's website so we could guarantee our room type. We got to the hotel late and unfortunately since it was New Years, the hotel was PACKED! People were everywhere and we could barely park our car in the front to valet it. We wanted to find a parking garage but we were too tired. Valet is 42 dollars and I suggest you dont use it b/c it's crap. Basically when you pick your car up they dont just bring it to you already running and warmed up. You go below the hotel and all the cars are parked one behind the other turned off. You have to go figure out where to get your keys and then if you're parked behind someone that's not there yet or not ready to leave you pretty much have to just sit there and wait. Now we just happened to stumble on a self parking garage attached to the hotel that nobody wanted to tell us about. There is an elevator that takes you from this garage to the 2nd floor. It's 30 something to park there for 24 hrs. The good thing about it is you dont have to pay that flat rate like you do at the hotel. I would suggest taking advantage of this garage if you want to save money and time. Anyway, we go to check in and they tell us we were staying in a room with double beds after we specifically booked a king through them about 5 months in advance. They told us they were booked for the night and possibly could give us a king the next day. I thought this was wrong b/c our reservation did not say that there's a possiblity that we may not get our bed type like travel websites say. IF it had said this then i would have understood but we were tired and just wanted to have a nice vacation without having to change rooms. Basically she couldnt do anything but give us free breakfast coupons. Whoopee. Granted it was for the 25 dollar a head buffet but still we didnt plan on eating at the hotel but there was nothing we could do. Room was adequate. Just a plain old room. The mattresses on the bed are so soft that you actually sink into them. This may sound good for some people but if you need some support on your back and you're used to a more firm bed, you're going to have trouble with these mattresses. There wasn't any noise we could hear through the walls but outside the door from your bed you can hear EVERYTHING. All we heard every night we were there, not just New Years where you expect it to be loud, were doors SLAMMING and people yelling in the halls. I got woken up every single night by the doors slamming. It was awful. Our room we got switched to the next day, which was a king but no upgrade, apology or anything was a view of the "lake" Well we couldnt see the lake b/c all the buildings were covering it. Oh and we also didnt get moved until 6 pm. How caring and concerned they were. Well saturday morning we got woken up by a loud helicopter helping take construction up to the top of a buliding across the street. There is a bunch of construction there so it will be noisy in the mornings. The location of the hotel was convenient though. About a 5 minute drive to Navy pier, we were able to walk there in the 12 degree weather :) on New Years. Right across the street from a movie theatre and bowling alley. About 5 minutes from the museums. For the price it was the cheapest we could find for the location we were looking for. I would try and find something better next time. If we couldn't find a better hotel for around the same price i wouldn't be disgusted staying here again, i would just brace myself that little things could go wrong and it could just be an annoying stay.

“Too Cool for Granny” This hotel is located on N. Clark and Huron which is convenient and quiet. What lured me was the hype about this being a green hotel. Uh, I didn't see it. They did not ask guests whether linens needed to be laundered each day. There were no separate bins to recycle and no instructions about it. Since this is a hip party hotel for the "20 somethings", they rock all night on weekends but the hotel security does ask them to pipe down after 10:30PM. Otherwise, the staff is kind but not terribly helpful. I asked to be placed away from the pop and ice machines. That didn't happen. I had to request an extra blanket three times before I got one. The desk lamps give off a quarter's diameter of light. Literally. I couldn't read at my desk. I was told that this was "green" but it worked like a pen light or flash light. However, it could be that the new generation only uses Kindles, Iphones, Ipads and lap tops. They literally had no traditional desk lamp on the premises. Speaking of Iphones, there were no phone books in the room. Maybe they are now obsolete since younger generations obtain this data from their portable electronic media sources. They did have a business center from which I obtained phone numbers and addresses. Coffee is served in the lobby each morning. So to get data or get awake, I had to leave my room which happened frequently and was not relaxing. Again, I am not sure that relaxation other than partying is the reason folks come to this hotel. The rooms are very small which would have been okay except that the wooden base of the bed is designed to hit the guests in the shins. Guests in the business center were laughing about that as we hobbled to our guest computers. It took me a half-hour to figure out that the dresser drawers were in the bed base. There is not alot of storage space in the room. Bottom line, come here if you want to party and/or tote electronic media sources. Forget it if you need to work and you still use non-electronic media to read and write.

“Bleh...room for improvement” My husband and I stayed at the Ritz Carlton Boston Common for 2 nights because he had a meeting and the room was covered. Good thing someone else was paying because this place is NOT worth the price. The check-in was typical Ritz where they greet you by name after reading it off the luggage tags and radioing in your name to the staff inside the hotel. Check-in occurs at an intimate desk, making me feel like I was opening a bank account. A glass of champagne was offered at check-in--this was a nice touch. The room itself was very average and typical of one you would find in an Omni or a nice Marriott. The bathroom is typical Ritz with marble and a great separate shower and tub. The adjacent Sports Club LA gym is fantastic and is the best gym in Boston. The problem is that unless you're in a Club Level room, there is an extra fee to use the room. Are you kidding? With the price of a room, this should be complimentary! Overall, we had a pleasant stay but if I had been paying for the room, I would have been extremely disappointed.

“One Night Stay Super Close to the Airport” We stayed at this location due to the fact that our flight landed in Philadelphia very late and we needed a place to sleep for one night before heading out the next morning. We chose it because the Hilton brand is one of our favorites and we are always pleased with Hampton Inn. This location was very close the airport so it didn't take too long to get there. The hot breakfast is always a winner with our family. There are muffins, waffles, good coffee, juices, and other great choices. This particular morning there were cheese omelets with maple breakfast sausage. It was delicious! This is a great stop for the traveler. We definitely noticed a lot of guests coming in from the airport and heading to the airport.

“Very Boutique decorated room! Satisfied” First, The location is excellent to Universal studio's! If u don't mind to be a little bit far from the hall of fame take that and drive with your car to any place u need! The rooms are very decorated and seems like they have been refurbished lately! The bathroom was really clean and the bed was so comfortable than any other i've been in my trip! We ask to have a micrwave and the room service brought us one to our room in less than 5 minutes!

“Great hotel” The staff was great and rooms were clean and fresh! Thank you for the great hotel and i think it was worth the money i paid! I love the fitness center and believe it or not the Spa though needs updating I had a great massage!

“It smelled horrible!” I just got back from 3 nights in NYC. I needed a place to stay for 1 night that was cheaper, as I was moving to the Marriott Marquis for my last 2 nights for events I was attending there (their rate for the 1st night was too high, reason for 1 night in another hotel). So, I chose the Edison, always having heard not so bad things about it, before coming to this site and seeing some mixed/bad reviews. It wasn't really dirty, I'll say that much, I can't say much though on housekeeping, as like I said, I was only there one night. The things I noticed right away were upon check-in, the room was ready and we only had carry-ons, they send a bellhop up with you no matter what. OK, not a big deal, but he also wasn't needed. My first complaint was the hallways were 100 degrees and smelled horrid. The room was no better, the smell was horrendous! It was horribly musty smelling, the air conditioning didn't help, it was so bad that I actually had to go to the drug store and buy an air freshener! I have asthma and am surprised I didn't get sick from the stench. The room was small (we had the two twin bed room, for 1 night it was OK), the bathroom was right next to the one bed, which was odd. Their was 2 closets, 1 by the door, a smaller one by the window. The best thing about the room was the armoire was nice and so was the TV! The bed I slept in, in addition to being a really hard mattress, moved everytime you sat on it or whatever, so basically everytime I turned over at night, the whole bed moved in a shaking way. The other bed had a horrible brown stain on the side of the box spring. The staff wasn't overly friendly, they have a "nominal charge" for ice, which is unbelievable. I didn't get any because of that. The best thing about the whole hotel was the cafe, I only had 1 meal there (dinner) and the food was really good and the prices were great. It's in need of remodeling, but it wasn't dirty. The whole hotel could use a complete refurbishment--it's badly needed. I wouldn't stay here again! I couldn't wait to check out and get across the street to the Marriott Marquis!

“Wonderful resort” Beautiful hotel. Beds comfy, service wonderful, food great. Wish the pool scene was better.....but if you have kids it is great. Very expensive but worth it. Far away from everything. $60 cab ride to airport. You need a car if you want to go anywhere. But luxurious, pretty, relaxing, and fun!

“Great hotel in a bad area of town” I have stayed at this hotel twice. Once in Sept. 2010 and once in Feb 2011. I used to hotel pool when I stayed in Sept. Yeah it's still hot in Houston in Sept. The pool is really cool. It is located on the roof of the smaller building. Not crowded at all. A few other people came out from sporadically but there was no more than 1 other person in the pool at any time. The lobby of this hotel is really nice. And the rooms are nice too. Everything about this hotel is pretty good except for the area of town. Greenspoint is a bad area, but the parking lot is being patrolled by a security guard and I have never had any incidents in the area. FREEE PARKING!
“Nothing Special, Decient” Rooms are Ok...all entries are from outside....free parking....neighborhood not the greatest, but I wasn't in fear for my life....

“An Excellent Deal (for some) in the Land of the Overpriced Hotel” A very good deal for those who are satisfied with basic accommodations in a European-type of establishment (sink in room). Clean room, friendly staff. Thin walls however. Clean shared bathrooms. I'd stay here again. If you're very fussy or expect $300+ /night type of accommodations for $150 (or as I paid $115 incl tax), you'd best look elsewhere. At the moment though, one of the best bangs for the buck in MY city even though I've spent the last 30 in Washington DC

“Nice hotel but won't return” The hotel itself is really nice, great rooms with comfortable beds & nice bathroom. The restaurant was good too, we ate breakfast there and had a really gorgeous cocktail in the bar. The only problem we had was that our room was over the bar/restaurant area and on our last night the hotel held a party there which kept us awake all night. Had we have been notified about the party then we would have stayed out later until after the party had finished. We did call down to the reception to complain, I'm not sure if the person that answered the call could even hear us the music was so loud so we just had to wait it out until the party was over. When we checked out the following morning the hotel did offer us a refund of one days valet parking which was fine but I would have prefered to have known about the party in the first place so I could have made other arrangements.

“Very nice stay” I had stayed here when it was a Park Hyatt and it still is a great place to stay in SFO. We had a studio suite with a separate living room separated by an awkwardly placed tv credenza. Clean, sophisticated, and a good deal as well. Will return on the next trip to San Francisco.

“Great Hotel for Business Travelers” The Hotel Nikko is a centrally-located, comfortable, and modern hotel geared to business travelers. It is an excellent option for the business traveler who desires a comfortable, spacious and attractive accommodation with strong business services. Rooms at the Nikko are spacious and well-appointed. My room was decorated in sleek greys with blue accents, and offered excellent Internet access, a spacious desk, and a large, flat-screen television set. The room offered a large dressing and bath area, equipped with a dressing room, countertop sink, a excellent shower and a water closet. The size of the dressing/bath area alone was equivalent to the square footage of rooms in smaller San Francisco establishments. Book the Nikko through a website to enhance affordability. I booked here for three nights on short notice, earlier that day. For the date of my initial checkin, I was forced to book directly with the hotel and paid a hefty $359. For the following two nights, which I booked on a travel site, the rate was $229, and well worth it-- an outstanding value. Dining at the Nikko is pricey, but the cuisine is excellent. The hotel's menu offers both Japanese cuisine and Western offerings. I chose sushi and a California white wine-- both excellent. If you are a sushi afficionardo, do try the sushi here-- but be warned that the prices are steep-- in my case, $18 for 7 generous and flavorful pieces. For those seeking more affordable options, there is ample and excellent dining in the immediate neighborhood. Service at the Nikko is efficient. and capable, if a bit austere The business center is well-equipped and available after hours with one's room key. The clientele is cosmopolitan, with both Asian and Western guests. Bottom line: an excellent value for business travelers, especially if booked through a website.

“Great Value, Great Location, Modest Accommodations” This is one of the best values in New York for the budget conscious. You can't beat the location, and the staff is unusually friendly and helpful. The hotel is very clean, but the rooms are laughably small. The queen size bed took up my entire room. The staff seems to be quite security conscious, which is a good thing in NYC. I regularly travel to New York to see theater, and this is my new favorite hotel.

“a place with history” stayed last week for four days what a grande old lady of hotels all the wow factor as you enter the main reception area ,stayed in the tower wing overlooking the bay very nice large clean room all mod cons ,laurel bar area also very nice and thanks to the brill staff in this area this hotel has history and was a real pleasure to view and stay one i will remember for many years to come congrats to all the staff and keep it like it is alan billington

“Location, Location!” I just got back from an overnight trip at the Showboat to see Daughtry at the Trump Taj Mahal--- Trump was too much money - got a GREAT deal with the Showboat - and did not have to go outside to get to the Trump Arena!!!! Room was very large !!!! View overlooking the ocean!!!! Big bathroom with separate room for toilet!!! Downside - internet was $11.60/day....walls a little thin, but not too noisy. Staff was very helpful -would def stay here again!

“Very nice downtown hotel” Stayed there with my family. The staff was very friendly. The room are huge, great views. Internet was fast and could connect to 3 devices for Same price. Room service expensive but very quick. Club room was closed on weekends but we were give a free breakfast at the restaurant or room service. Only valet parking. Great location.

“very nice” Hotel is part of the Marriott Place complex and is "connected" to everything in downtown Indy. Hotel was great. Service was excellent (front desk offered to go to another Marriott property to retrieve a local paper that they had just run out of). My only qualm is that it is not as connected as the other hotels. In order to get to the skywalk you have to go to the parking garage then up into the JW Marriott. The combined Courtyard/Springhill next door is directly connected to the skywalk.

“Fantastic Location, A Peaceful Rest on Embassy Row” We stayed here from a Thursday to Saturday in March. We got lucky with beautiful, even hot, early Spring weather. We were visiting a nearby school and just sightseeing. The location really is superb -- within a short walk to Dupont Circle and new downtown, and just a bit more to the White House area. Massachusetts Avenue (Embassy Row) and the streets to the north are quite charming. The hotel overlooks charming (if busy) Scott Circle. We changed rooms after our first room had no light as it looked directly onto the next building (a negative for at least one side of the hotel). The room we ended up with looked over the Circle -- a beautiful view. The lobby is spacious and comfortable, with the usual free internet usage. The restaurant in the hotel is actually pretty good (but about par with other Marriott locations). The staff was nice and helpful. The space was clean, and the room was fine if basic. The bathroom was not spacious or well designed -- typical of these types of hotels. However, the bed and furnishings were comfortable enough. The best thing is the location for the price. Also, it is a comfortable base for exploring the nearby areas. I would stay here again.

“Not bad for Times Square” We stayed only one night but it was a very good experience. If you can, choose the deluxe rooms that have been upgraded and something on a higher level. Higher floors tend to be quieter with lots less street noise. This hotel is within walking distance of many attractions and easy transit. It's especially handy for crashing after a long day of shopping then a Broadway show! We had a room with 2 doubles - very comfortable, fair sized bathroom (though showing some wear and tear) and lots of room for luggage and working. Check-in was easy, friendly, and all the staff were pleasant. I prefer quieter parts of town to Times Square but needed to be there those few days and found the Millenium an excellent choice. If the price is right go for it!

“Good hotel, but not 100%” Comfortable medium sized hotel with well-furnished rooms, free breakfast (kinda), free Internet and good workout facilities. Staff are on the whole quite helpful and friendly. The hotel could get five out of five if it wanted to. However, it just doesn't give you that 100% feeling, for the following reasons: 1) Sloppy cleaning - Every day at least one thing wasn't cleaned. Upon closer observation it would appear that the rooms are never checked after cleaning. 2) Elevators - Take hours to arrive. 3) Breakfast - The free continental breakfast is a nice touch. However it really doesn't include that many things, and even doesn’t have toast. Interestingly the paid for breakfast requires the same effort to collect, and also the same effort by the staff, who simply give you the bill. That doesn't stop them asking for a tip. Something important ran out every day too. For example coffee, or bread, or forks. (Forget about telling the staff if you have a dirty fork.) 4) Pool – small and freezing cold. I can still feel it now, two weeks later. Apart from these points it’s a good place to stay and I would go again. A 3.5 really but lets give it a 4.

“Refreshing change from the standard biz experience” My first stay at an Aloft was a little frustrating, but overall a really nice change from bland beige business hotels, kind of a W-lite meets Danish upscale dorm room. Pros: Hyperenergetic staff; food selections in a 24/7 pantry (fresh and good - especially the breakfast sandwiches); free, fast wireless; comfortable bed; cool in-room magazine selections; nice shower and amenities; pool table in the lobby. Cons: Hard to find an AC plug in the lobby lounge (esp strange given their emphasis on tech-savvy travelers); drab rooms (would a piece of art have killed them?) Overall, it was a nice change and I'd welcome the opportunity to stay there again. Non-frequent travelers might find it a bit too spartan and cold.

“Pretty good...Typical Hilton.” This is a typical Hilton hotel. It is pretty good, but not as much as you would expect. I am a Hilton Diamond member, and I am loyal to the Hilton company, but the Hilton brand could use some work to offer more value. One example at this property is that you have to pay for internet use. This seems to be antiquated and shows that Hilton is out of touch with business travelers. This property is no exception. Luckily, on this trip I was traveling for leisure. The parking fee is kind of ridiculous as well. I understand that parking is at a premium, but why not just have a reader at the barrier that reads your room key and raises the barrier if you are a guest? Making guests pay outrageous fees for parking is not the way to show that you are looking out for guests and creating a good relationship. I booked through Priceline, so the parking was ok, but if I had to pay full price I wouldn't book. The rooms are ok. In fact they are pretty nice, with nice beds. Our shower also had pressure that changed many times throughout the course of a shower. The temperature seemed to change in response to the pressure changes. The staff at the front desk was EXCELLENT. This is the biggest and best feature of this hotel. In a way this makes almost any negative forgettable. Hotel managers did you read those last three sentences? Please take note, service is the most important part of any hotel (I should know I spend half a year, each year, in a hotel). This hotel doesn't have the best location, but it is bearable. Unless, you really like Denny's, don't expect to walk to eat out many times. This hotel is a solid choice for the price, if you can get a discount. Even at full price, it is competitive in the region. There are many better hotels on the waterfront, but they are very high priced. This is relatively close to most things, is bearable, has a nice look and a good staff. It is a good choice for those with a car, and who want a basic, but nice hotel.

“Much better than the normal rooms” After having stayed at the Waldorf many times, I think what you get is going to be potluck as far as rooms are concerned. My room in the towers was a roomy queen sized room with a standard hotel bathroom. The bathtub was larger than most bathtubs (though not a garden size tub) and the toiletries were Penhaligon's. I had a foyer that closed off from the bedroom which helped keep my room nice and quiet. My bed was conformtable and I even had a coffee maker in my room (which is not standard for normal Waldorf rooms). The room was decorated in a traditional way and much of the furniture looked antique. I enjoyed my towers stay much more than any of my other stays at the waldorf!

“Great, convenient place to stay!” Consistent quality is one of my favorite things about the Hilton brand, this hotel delivered on that promise. My stay was enjoyable, my room was clean & quiet, the service was good, and the hotel itself had everything I needed from familiar fitness machines to a convenient store that offered healthy snacks to address my late night munchies. A few specifics about this property: they have a free shuttle to/from the airport, a very nice sports bar/pub, a big parking lot and a nice pool.

“Enjoyed the stay” Didn't expect much after reading the reviews but was pleasantly surprised. Had a nicely refurbished room on the 4th floor. Staff was friendly, efficient, and helpful. Beds were comfortable and the location can't be beat if you are needing to be close to USC. One thing was rather odd. The water in the bathroom was either very warm or scolding hot. Our room did not have cold water! Very strange but didn't have time to complain or inquire. I will likely return!

“Good stay but room needs renovations” This former Holiday Inn is well-situated at the edge of the city, but is hard to get in and out of due to the traffic. The room we stayed in for 6 nights was badly in need of a renovation. The furniture was in poor shape as was the carpet and wallpaper. The bedding was fine and the linens were decent. The staff at the hotel was very friendly and helpful. I was surprised to see that so many visitors found them rude. They told me that 4 of the 7 floors have been completely renovated. I hope that I didn't get shown to a "hotwire room" but even if I did, it was good value. We ate breakfast at the Glass Tree restaurant and although a little pricey, it was good. I would stay here again, but would try to ensure I got a renovated room. There is a SuperTarget as well as some chain restaurants (CPK, Chipotle, Pei Wei, TGIFridays, Potbelly Sandwich Works and Starbucks) right in the parking lot.
“Great service, food, ambience and central location” I liked everything about it. More than the Marriott next to it

“Good location in Financial District” We also purchased the Travelzoo deal but were staying over a Monday night so had no problem booking a room. They even advised that we received an upgrade without my asking. We ordered room service for breakfast and the food was wonderfully prepared. Staff were very helpful upon check-in and we needed some extra assist. We loved the location which was close to the 911 memorial, Seaport, Trinity Church and Wall St. Great location for crossing the Brooklyn Bridge and enjoying some of Brooklyn as well as close to multiple subway stops on Fulton St. The room was large by Manhattan standards, bed was comfortable, and bathroom one of the cleanest we had seen in the city. As to someones comment about no top sheet, the comforter was covered with sheets and I found the sheets of good quality which is also becoming harder to find in Manhattan. Our one minor issue was that we were placed in a room on the Platt St. side of the building which is where trash trucks seem to load trash and recycables from a neighboring building for two hours at a time. They actually were loading two trucks at a time with the noise of constant compacting. We were only on the 4th floor so it made it difficult to listen to the TV or each other from 8-10 pm. It was also going on during the daytime but the good news is that it stopped around 10 pm so no problem sleeping. We would return to this hotel but request a room on the opposite side of the hotel.

“Was a bit scared but I LOVED IT!” OK so I am normally staying at Hyatts and Hiltons but due to budget (kid starting college in the fall) I had to watch what I spent in NYC. I have to say I was impressed! I stayed in a single w/ shared bath and I really had a great stay. The room was spotless and yes only room for one. The way they do the shared bath was cool in that there was an indicator above my door that told me when it was occupied. The bathrooms were spotless which impressed me even more and I got to take a great hot showered without no worries. I will be staying there again next month as I get to move my son into college in NYC and this worked out for the price. The location excellent - midtown can't ask for more especially for the price! BTW I am not in my 20's or 30's and this hotel was a great value!

“This hotel should be #1 - GREAT LOCATION!!” We've been to New York several times, and we love this location by far. We got early check-in.....LOVED that....room was HUGE for New York!!...HUGE!!!!....room was clean, well appointed, and lovely decor. Staff were friendly...and efficient. The location is magnificent. ....you can tell from other reviews...it's all about location in New York and this is the best by far!!...but hotel has distinction and character!!...Don't miss the opportunity to try a small boutique hotel!!!

“Great location - Hotel needs rehab” We traveled to Chicago for a wedding and this was the host hotel of the couple. Unfortunately, the couple must have chosen one really busy weekend in Chicago because the hotel was booked solid and no where else in the vicinity had any vacancies. So we booked a room at a whopping $259 a night and couldn't even get a double (two ladies traveling together). Fortunately, we're friends and didn't mind splitting a king sized bed. Overall, our stay wasn't horrible, but I expected soooo much more from a hotel that boasts Presidential stays and such a high nightly rate. First there was no airport shuttle, your on your own, even from Midway. It may be typical for downtown Chicago hotels to not have shuttles but in this day and age you'd like they would spring for a 15 passenger van. When we arrived in the room, it was very apparent that Sheraton had only "upgraded" certain aspects of the room. Newer bedding and television. Same old nasty bathrooms and carpeting. Both looked about 50 years old. The bathroom especially, with moldy tiles. Additionally, there is only one reasonable option for breakfast - a $20 buffet without sufficient seating for the typical crowd of the hotel. Although it was typical breakfast fare, expect to wait in line. Good things - great location, central to all things Chicago - Michigan Ave, Navy Pier, etc. Friendly staff and comfy beds.

“Excellent location, tiny room but decent rates.” If you are looking for the luxurious Manhattan experience, this place is not for you. There is no concierge (the desk clerks claim to "double" as concierge, but I knew more of Manhattan than they did), no fluffy bathrobe, no deluxe restaurant (only a breakfast room), no room service. It was basic accomodation in a really small room. So why did I give it such a high rating? The location is fabulous -- we could walk to just about anything that we wanted to see and do. And the rooms are tiny, but clean and comfortable. The bed was actually really comfortable. The hotel is not very large -- only 92 rooms and is tucked away on a quiet street, so the sleep quality was excellent. And it has a cozy, intimate feeling about it. And for the area of Manhattan, I could not find a better price. There is a free continental breakfast: get to breakfast early. The breakfast room is very small and you could end up standing to eat. Overall, I came away very pleased with the stay.

“Location Location Location” We stayed here as part of a two week road trip between LA, Palm Springs and Vegas. I was travelling with my partner, and two kids aged 13 and 5. Would definitely stay here again How long did we stay? 4 nights Where we booked/how much we paid – via www.lowcostholidays.com £312 total for a room with two double beds. Booked about 4 months before travel., About the place- The hotel is a modern design, painted grey, a tall tower block in a residential/office area. They have valet parking for $20 per day with in/our privileges. The reception is bright airy and welcoming. Lots of modern twists throughout. Outside pool area, quite a small pool max of 30 people I would think. Plenty of sun beds and shade around the pool. Deck 33 restaurant overlooking pool which served lovely food. Locally – Literally 5 min drive from LAX airport. You see this hotel on take-off and landing!!! However the windows are thick and we NEVER were bothered by the airplane noise. Supermarket next door (Ralphs) for any supplies needed. Small selection of restaurants locally including KFC drive-thru, pizza places etc Favourite bits – Room was big, modern and well-equipped Cute toiletries offered Fridge and safe in room Quick checkin, information then emailed such as check out time and invoice. Pool area was nice, relaxing and well equipped Deck 33 restaurant and bar was modern, fun and served lovely food – friendly staff Free wifi with unlimited users per room Bits we disliked/or could be improved – Three lifts however they were super slow. We often waited at least 5 mins to catch a lift down Breakfast buffet could be improved. $12 pp and although it is varied daily they are slow to serve, you must ask for juice which comes in a small plastic cup, slow to replenish foods. The actual food was tasty! On the Saturday afternoon during our stay there was a private pool party. Whilst we were allowed entry to the pool area we had to queue on the street (not appropriate in swimwear!), it was extremely loud music with inappropriate lyrics for kids swimming at 4pm and a general whaft of cannabis! The management were kind and offered us free food during our stay – needless to say we didn’t swim for long!! There had been no warning of this pool party or we wouldn’t have promised the kids a swim!!I have emailed regarding this however received no response 21 days on!! Any tips- Definitely recommend staying here as its just 15 mins to Venice or Santa Monica, 30 mins to Hollywood, and 5 mins to the airport. Our sleep was perfect and the standard was great especially for the price we paid. Maybe just avoid the private pool parties. I would suggest management just put a sign warning guests if they have a party booked! Small diner nearby called KJ’s – do an American selection for breakfast for a better price Web Links www.customhotel.com

“Newly renovated but didn't like the location” Marriott invested in a new lobby and bar area which was sorely needed. We stayed here during a conference. Conference area was very nice as was the staff service. The rooms were small and the air conditioning unit sounded like a Mac truck. It woke me up each time it turned on during the night. The thing I disliked about this hotel is the location away from downtown Indy. It takes about 10-15 mins to drive to a nice restaurant. If you can stay downtown I'd recommend it over this location.

“Perfect Hotel for Exploring Downtown Chicago” I stayed at the Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile on a recent business trip to the city. This high-rise hotel is located in the heart of "Magnificent Mile" and is in walking distance to plenty of great restaurants and shopping. I had read reviews about the hotel being just average, the bathroom being small, not enough outlets, etc. I found the hotel to be quite nice. The room was nicely decorated and had plenty of room. The beds were comfortable, the bathroom wasn't huge but was clean and beautifully furnished. I loved the Bath and Body Works Aromatherapy products! I will admit that some of the amenities were "hidden." For example, the coffee pot was tucked into a cubby in the dresser. The hair dryer was in a cloth bag hanging on a hook in the closet (?). It also seemed that there were no outlets on the desk. My colleague told me to look underneath the desk, and then I spotted the sign that clearly indicated where the outlet was located. There were not, however, easily accessible outlets on the night stand (where I normally charge my cell phone). I had a city view room on the 27th floor. I requested a higher floor, but the only rooms available on high floors were close to the elevator. The woman at the front desk was very patient and carefully researched to find the best room for me. Had I understood her front desk correctly, I probably would have taken her up on a Michigan Avenue view. Being unfamiliar with Chicago, I opted for the city view. I still had a decent view of the skyline, though. The lobby area was beautiful and always buzzing with activity. I didn't at the hotel restaurant, but my colleague had breakfast there one morning and said that it was very good. The next two mornings, we walked a couple of blocks to the Corner Bakery Cafe, which was perfect for us. I was disappointed that they charged for Internet access ($14.95/24 hours) and that it was wired. I think there may be free WiFi in the lobby though. I also understand that parking is very expensive, but since we didn't have a car, that wasn't a concern for us. Overall, I would recommend The Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile to anyone who wanted to explore the beautiful downtown area of Chicago.

“Excellent room and service” - Fantastic location, 2 blocks from the bars of 6th street and easy walking distance to sites - Big rooms, very clean, huge kitchenette, comfy bed - Excellent service from friendly staff at check in to staff in the restaurants - Good breakfast buffet at the restaurant - Lovely touches like free cookies and juice * Expensive valet parking but you can park around the block at a meter or cheaper car park

“Mixed Feelings” The Bellevue Hyatt is centrally located and is within walking disatance of many historic attractions. The hotel is housed in an older building that appears to be undergoing interior renovations. The room that I was assigned had been recently updated and had a modern feel. The in room four seat bar area and balcony were unanticipated and appreciated upgrades. Note... Many of the rooms have not been updated. All remaining members of our group (10 people) were assigned older rooms that I think are intended to have a period look and feel but just simply come across as looking tired rather than elegant. The elevators are slow and during peak periods can take up to 10 minutes to call. If you are a fitness buff. The health club is massive and rivals any hotel facility that I have ever used. I really wanted to like this place based on the location and the room that I was assigned but there were several issues that prevented me from giving this property 2 thumbs up. The first morning the power went out in my room while I was showering. It seemed to be an isolated issue affecting only a handful of rooms but I was unable to use either phone to contact the desk as they required power. I managed to get dressed using the screen from my laptop for lighting. When I notified the front desk of the problem I was told "that's interesting, we have had a couple of other reports of problems". She indicated that engineering would look into the matter. The problem was not resolved before I had to leave for my meeting. I would have appreciated an opportunity to use another room to iron my shirt and finish getting ready. The other concern is linked to a problem a coworker experienced. They had gone to bed for the night and was awakened at 10:30 pm by hotel staff that wanted to inform him that there was a problem with the scan of his credit card. I can't think of a good reason for any hotel staff to be knocking on a door at 10:30 for any reason other than a safety concern. He was unable to get back to sleep after the interruption. His room was comped but what he really wanted was a good nights sleep rather than a free room. This property has promise and if you snag an updated room I'd say its worth giving a try. Otherwise, I'd head up the block to the Ritz Carlton or across town to the Hyatt Penn Landing.

“Great Lodging in DC!” A block of rooms were held for my group and I was very happy with the hotel. I had a 1 bedroom suite non-smoking room on a corner and stayed for 7 nights. The rooms are great -almost a full kitchen with everything except an oven. The kitchen was furnished with place settings for two and about 3 different sized pots with lids. The refrigerator was full-size and the kitchen has a large sink and dishwasher. The maid washed dishes for me most of the days I was there. The kitchen was furnished with a kitchen dish towel- dish and hand, plus paper towels and D/W detergent. The living room was small but has a sofa bed couch and a chair with ottoman. The TV was an average size regular TV - probably a 25 inch. The separate bedroom was huge and had a large closet with wire shelving inside on one side. The bathroom was in the bedroom with the sink outside and the toilet and bathtub shower in a separate room to the side of the sink area. The sink has a large enough counter to lay things on. The bedroom has a desk with the TV on it. There is no light on the desk. There are two bedside table each with a lamp on either side of the King bed. The bed is very comfortable and I am a very picky sleeper and can't stand a very hard mattress. The pillows are overstuffed but I always travel with my own pillow. My sister came to stay with me the last weekend and slept on the couch. It is fairly comfortable, she said. One of the best features of this hotel is that a hot breakfast and hot dinner are provided each weekday. No dinner on Friday night or the weekend. The dinner was surprisingly decent in taste and quantity. I never had to buy breakfast or dinner during the week and saved my company money. There is a CVS Pharmacy close by that I walked to, that I was able to buy water and other items. The hotel also provides a buying service for free. I gave them a list in the morning of about 5 items and they were great, providing all of it. The hotel provides a listing of nearby restaurants. My sister and tried one of the restaurants (I think mediterranean) within 2 blocks and it was very good food. (Service was terrible.) At the hotel, I had a couple of problems such as the coffee pot, DSL Internet cable,and one TV remote didn't work - but the hotel replaced all of them for me and comped one night of my stay for me after I complained of slow service too and two other problems. I had to return to DC in May and tried to stay at this hotel again, but there were no non-smoking rooms available so I had to stay elsewhere. The staff is very friendly and try to make sure your stay is comfortable.

“Better bedding would make this hotel a winner” On the plus side my room on the 49th floor was spacious by New York standards and the bathroom was a very nice size. Check in was quick, the room was quiet, there is a very large flat screen TV and a mini-bar. Personally, I hate being anywhere near Times Square, but the location of this hotel is near my firm's New York office, so it's convenient. To me, what takes a hotel from good to great is the quality of their bedding and towels. I'm especially picky about the bed spreads, which often gross me out. Unfortunately, in pulling back the bedspread there was a 3 inch round stain on the underside. I quickly put the bedspread on the floor and got out the extra blanket from the closet. This blanket should have been thrown away long ago -- I can't even describe the fabric, it was rough and felt like a thin sheet of foam rubber that had perhaps been baked in a oven (or a too-hot dryer). Plus it had fuzz and a small wad of hair stuck on it. Anyway, it makes it hard for me to sleep when the bedding is even a little cruddy. If the Millennium would just improve the bedding, I would give this hotel a great rating, but until then, I'll just give it a good rating.

“Great Location” Stayed at the Hilton Times Square sept 2-3 2005 with my husband and two teenaged sons. The hotel is well located and we would definitely stay there again. We were on the 25th floor facing 41st and found the room to be quiet. Many restaurants, cinemas, shopping steps away.

“The Waldorf, a bit of Old New York glamour” My friend and I checked into the Waldorf, both being Diamond members of Hilton and were treated to a wonderful suite in the Towers.
