The room was like stepping into an english manner, a bit threadbare but chic. To me, that's what gave it the charm. The staff was very helpful and the lobby is truly beautiful. The bed and the linnens are wonderful as were the bath amenities. Do yourself a favor, and enjoy a stay at this great lady.

“Fantastic find - a boutique hotel in Dupont Circle with exceptional service!!” My sister, her pug, and I traveled to the Topaz for our annual sisters weekend. We booked the Topaz because of the great reviews on trip advisor, and the $99 rate we found through their summer sale email they send to Kimpton in touch members (free). We love the special kimpton touches, so staying at a Kimpton is a must. We are friends on Facebook, and learned the secret magic word for August, which got us a free upgrade to a yoga room and valet parking. Raymond helped checked us in, poured us wine at their complimentary happy hour, and even took a picture of Bailey the pug to put on their hotel pet wall. Raymond and the rest of the staff really went above and beyond to make us feel welcome. I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend it!

“コストパフォーマンスは良し” 年末年始は、NYでも一番ホテルが高い時期ですが、ここは、五番街に面しており、比較的安めです。グランドセントラル駅にもほど近いので、エアポートバスを使う方には便利でしょう。ただ、劇場街からは15分くらい歩きます。 また、映画などでも使われた、歴史はあるホテルなので、ロビーなどは格調高いです。 ただ、やはり、部屋の施設には古さが否めません。NYの古いホテルには良くありがちなことですが、特に水回り・・。 サービスにも問題ありです。午前中、ホテルでゆっくりして出かけて、夜帰ってきても、部屋の掃除がされておらず、ハウスキーピングに電話しなければいけないことが二日もありました。一流ホテルのように、一日に何度もドアのノブに掛けられた「掃除して下さい」のカードをチェックするようなことはないようです。 また、窓を開けたところ、建て付けが古いせいか、そこで止まってしまい、どうしても閉じれなくなってしまったのですが、暖房がガンガン効いているため、寒くて眠れないということがなかったのには、ある意味、驚きました。 まあ、場所が良いので、コストパフォーマンスだけは、まずまずでしょうか。

“Average Property” Overall the experience was not bad. The room was standard Holiday Inn with good views if you are lucky enough to score one facing downtown. The Hotel is clean and the bar was very nice with an exceptional view of the city. My issue is more with the Front Desk. I had to talk to them on three occasions and each time they were rude when answering my questions. I wasn't even complaining or asking for anything concerning my room. All three were just not friendly individuals which is a shame because the rest of the employees seemed very nice in my interactions with them. Will choose another of the IHG brands for my next stay in Chicago.

“Quiet room, consistent with the reviews here” Stayed three nights on business. This is a typical Embassy Suites property where the rooms all face into a covered courtyard, in which breakfast is served in the morning. The room was excellent for my needs, with one room for table/work and the other for sleep, fridge and microwave hiding in the closet with a coffee maker. Everything was in good repair, clean, good daily cleaning service. This is a popular hotel with tourists and yes the breakfast does get busy but it wasn't too bad mid week when I was there. Breakfast is OK - nothing special. I did not have time for the made-to-order omellettes which I would imagine are nicer. Otherwise you have a decent assortment of acceptable quality food which is kept well stocked. Well on my last day the scrambled eggs were cold which was a bit sub-par, but otherwise OK. I like the neighborhood. It is quiet, residential, near GWU, a number of small restaurants, But as some point out, unless you're planning on taking cabs (which is silly in a town with such a good metro), the location is not convenient to the tourist sites. But the metro stop isn't too far away (3/4 mile). I will gripe, as I usually do, about hotels that charge > $100/night and still nickle and dime you for internet connectivity. Come on folks.

“Some of the reviews are unfair” I recently had cause to stay in downtown LA for work. The company picked this hotel, probably because the rate is depressed due to all the construction work. The staff was professional, helpful and quick even though they are suffering through the mess of construction with everyone else. I am not particularly familiar with the downtown area and they were quick with directions and suggestions for good food, sights to see and good times to be had. The location is good for business but bad for just about anything else. Downtown LA is pretty dead after 7pm. The 110 is profoundly easy access right off the hotel grounds and you can get to the valley or west LA in 15 minutes or less if its good traffic. The room was small, but the hotel is older and most rooms were smaller back then. It was very clean and the bathroom was fairly modern. Dollar for dollar, I didn't have a bad stay and will probably be back next week.

“Hotel Hell” What a horrible disappointment the Wyndham was. I was very skeptical after reading the reviews on this site. For some reason I didn't check out the hotel here first before booking room. I should have.. Let that be a lesson to you all, be sure and check here FIRST, be-for booking a room if I had I would never have even give them a chance. After reading the reviews here I was worried but decided to sick it out, surely it couldn't be as bad as it was made out to be here..... I was wrong, it was WORSE !!!!!! Far worse....... There were so many things wrong I will just list them in no particular order and address certain ones with a little more detail. * Bad smells in the room and hallways * Mold in the bath room tub and walls as well as on the air conditioner vents *The carpets in the room felt moist all the time * Wasp nest on the balcony the size of a ball. I asked the front desk to come and have maintenance remove it, they never showed up , I gave up after the 4th request. * The toilet after flushing ran continuously * Bath tub leaked * The wall paper was peeling off the wall in several places in my room. I also noticed that the walls were very dirty and so were all the doors, in fact the bath room door appeared to have a fecal stain on it. * Room safe was broken and did not work * Curtains were dirty and looked like they had water stains * The security latch on the door was broken and I could not use it. ( apparently one night when I was there a few Ladies in a different room noticed there latch was broken as well, asked to be moved and denied, later that night the front desk staff checked in two gentleman and gave them the same room as the 2 Ladies had so when the guys walked in to the room (because the safety latch was broken) the 2 ladies woke up to men standing in there room, they were scared to death.) * Several nights we saw coach roaches in our room scurry across the floor * Horrible lighting in the room, they had 3 small lamps that didn't provide good lighting at all. * only working vending machine was by the front desk * Dirty trash cans in the hallways * Dirty elevators and public places * In the restaurant I was served coffee and juice in dirty dishes. * The fax machine in there business center charged me $26.00 to my Visa to send 1 fax, I later found out that the fax never even went through. * The parking was $15.00 dollars a night. ( They had a valet, but when I wanted to leave the hotel he was always in the bar visiting with the bar tender, I could never find the guy to get my car and when I did find him, all I had to do was tell him what room I was in and he would go get my car and hand over the keys to me. I NEVER ONCE had to show any proof I was a guest there. I don't know about you but I find this piratically distressing .....anyone could have gotten access to my car. ) Basically this was the dirtiest Hotel I have ever seen, It was old and run down, all except for the lobby it looked really, really nice but once you leave the lobby it's like you descend in to hell. I was told by one of there staff they had received a grant for a huge amount of money and spent it all on the lobby and nothing on the places that really needed it, like there rooms. I do want to say that they did have a nice staff, especially the front desk girls, Zita she wonderful..... as was another girl I cant remember her name long brown hair, worked in a restaurant at night I think she called it the elephant maybe ?? She worked the day shift Michael in the Saint John's cafe was very nice. In spite of the nice staff my recommendation would be: Avoid this place at all cost. !!!! It is FOUL

“Very nice but take advantage of "upon request" items” We did a "name your own price" for a random Sunday night and were assigned the Hotel Monaco in downtown Seattle. We've stayed at various Kimpton hotels throughout the country and this did not disappoint. The hotel is currently being renovated and we were a bit worried we would get one of the "old" rooms but we did not. Our room was updated, clean, modern and (for the most part) quiet. After looking at the website and reading the reviews on TripAdvisor prior to our arrival, we were expecting a pet goldfish in our room as well as turndown service at night (we've always had turndown service at other Kimptons). We didn't get either and after re-reviewing the website found out that these items are "upon request." That was a little disappointing, especially since it was a quiet Sunday night and the hotel wasn't full by any stretch of the imagination. Another nit-pick: the hotel's website says their wine reception from 5-6 pm offers "worldly and wise" wines. Eh, not so much. They were pouring Columbia Crest Two Vines Cabernet, a bottle of which can be purchased in the grocery store for $6.99. Not so wordly or wise! Oh well. It's free I guess! The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was large with good water pressure in the shower and no shortage of hot water for an older building. We could hear our neighbor early on Monday morning on the phone so it could have been a bit quieter but we understood guests on Monday morning may be conducting early business from their rooms. All in all, no major complaints and for the "name your own price" it was a good deal. Be aware, there is only valet parking and it will run you $40+ dollars a night with tax. Yikes!

“Flying Visit” We needed a hotel for 9 hour layover at Boston on the way to Miami and teh Hilton fitted the bill. Its on the airport and accessible via a (long) walkway from Terminal E. It aws a bit further away than I expected - maybe 10-15 mins walk and the hotel stands alone rather than being part fo teh airport complex but you can't deny its the best placed hotel if you want to cut out any problems with getting to and from when you're tired aftar a long flight. We didn't test any of teh facilities other than teh riooom which was large and comfortable with a big flatscreen TV. Some good views over the airport. Efficient chack in (although it was very late (10pm) when we turned up. Well informed staff helped with transfer information and shuttle times. Check out was fast too - although at 5:30 am there wasn't a queue! The Hilton is further away from other terminals. It's easier to get to them by using the regular shuttle which was running every 15 minutes at 5am and took only 5 mins to get to Terminal B where we caught a connecting American Airways flight the next morning. Check the location of your onward connections in advance. Incoming international flights use E (which is directly connected to the Hilton) but onward domestic connections will be from other terminals depending on which airline you use.

“Basic” Stayed in Hotel Indigo for a couple of nights back in August. What I remember most about the experience is the lack of impression that the hotel made on me. Rooms were incredibly small - even for ny standards. I'm not sure what a 'spa bathroom', as advertised on the hotel website, entails, but I'm pretty sure that I didn't have one. We were hosting a meeting at the hotel, so we got a special rate, which I thought was too much for the accommodations and related facilities. There is no way that I would pay the standard asking rate for this hotel. The small conference room that we used was adequate, but service was a tad haughty. I asked for a little salt and pepper to season the scrambled eggs that were served and the request was met with a look of being 'put out'. Of course, the salt/pepper didn't show up until well after I finished my breakfast (after waiting an appreciable time, while my eggs cooled to an unpalatable state). Pro, location was great, offering access to interesting dining and shopping venues.

“Great new addition to a city with many fine hotels” I stayed here on business three nights in February. This is definitely a fine addition to the list of great downtown hotels in San Antonio. I haven't stayed in this area of downtown before, so it was a very pleasant surprise to see how nice and SAFE Houston Street has become. This hotel is across the street from the post office/US Courthouse, caddy corner from the Alamo (dramatic pause for John Wayne), and walking distance from Rivercenter Mall, the Riverwalk, the Convention center, and some of San Antonio's finest restaurants. The Hotel Indigo is not what I would consider a family hotel, but is fine for business or couples. The view from my room was magnificent. The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating. Pluses: location is great, service is great, ambience is great. Water pressure in the shower was great, valet service was quick and efficient. The bed is probably the most comfortable hotel bed I've slept on. Room design and ambience is very thoughtful. Minuses: it is an OLD building, so you can hear footsteps above you. The A/C is loud. The closet is barely deep enough for your hangers. The ventilation from the kitchen does need some work. When I came back from the convention center, the entry smelled like bacon grease (I like the smell, but others may be more picky). I would love to return with my lovely trophy wife for a romantic weekend and stay here. I did not sample the bar or restaurant. When I come to San Antonio I'm eating at Mi Tierra, Los Barrios, Tomatillos, or Pico de Gallo - I'm not eating hotel food in this town! However, just down Houston Street is The Palm, at Rivercenter there is Morton's Steakhouse, and the many fine restaurants on the Riverwalk.

“A touch of class.” My husband, two daughters (10 and 8) and I stayed at the Palace for 2 nights in early August. We arrived on a busy Friday afternoon at about check-in time. I expected a long wait and possibly a room not ready but we had no wait at all and got right up to our room. We stayed in the Towers section in room 4716. I loved the decor of the entire hotel but was particularly pleased with the Hollywood actors pictures lining the hallway. We happened to be located at the picture of my favorite actor, Cary Grant. I thought this was a good sign. The room was beautiful and spacious for New York city. My girls both received American Girl travel beds, they were very excited. The view from the room was outstanding and free internet was a nice feature - though it was tough to stay on line, I was kicked off every few minutes. I know we were in a special area of the hotel but I don't think we took advantage of all the perks it offered. We had a separate entrance and elevators as well as our own concierge. The lobby was beautiful but did seem to be quite filled with people whenever we were walking through. Not sure if these were other guests or people just visiting but it seemed to be a busy place. The only negatives of the experience was: No ironing board in the room - had to call for one which was received within an hour. The toilet wouldn't flush mid Saturday, not sure why since we hadn't been there all day. A maintenance person came up and fixed it quickly. Lastly, we didn't get to enjoy the outside courtyard feel that I see in the online pictures because there's construction going on all around the entrances. We walked through a lot of scaffolding and blocked views of what looks to be a beautiful building. St Patrick's Cathedral was also under construction so we had blocked views all around. The room was pricey and I kind of expected a bit more for the price but I was very pleased with the accommodations. Watch out for the honor bar though - very expensive small items. My kids quickly learned not to go near it. The location is outstanding, within walking distance or quick cab ride to most everything. The staff we dealt with were all pleasant and personable. We would go back.

“Noisy!!” Just returned from a one night stay at the Algonquin. The history of the hotel makes it worth a visit, but don't expect much more. There is a hotel being built right behind it and the noise from the construction equipment digging all day long is enough to drive you crazy. The rooms are small, but sweetly decorated, The plumbing as you might imagine is very old and the fixtures are meant to give that "old fashioned" look, There is no luxury to the bathroom at all. The bed was super comfortable and the linens were great quality. The elevators were painfully slow and cramped. You must posess patience to stay here. The location however is excellent, close to all. If you catch a great deal and won't be in the room too too much, then try the Algonquin.

“Good for me” I went to San Diego for a conference at the convention center and stayed at this hotel for four nights through hotwire. As a huge fan of public transportation and walking, I tried to walk. It is 3 miles one way and it ook me a full one hour, so I stopped doing this after a day. You can hop in the free airport shuttle and take mts992, which costs only $2.25 and just a few minutes to downtown, although you need to walk additional few blocks to the convention center. Upon the recommendation from this site, I requested a room with a downtown view, and the staff gave me a room at Bay Tower (about 1000 ft from Marina Tower). I found out that I could not see the downtown. The next day, I requested a room to Marina Tower to be near the airport shuttle without any preference to the view, and I was given a room with a beautiful downtown view. From the experience of staying at both towers, the room at Marina Tower was smaller and was okay since I was alone, and I presume that even numbered room at Marina Tower: harbor/airport view odd numbered room at Marina Tower: downtown view even numbered room at Bay Tower: airport view odd numbered room at Bay Tower: harbor view. The staff were very nice. I did not have the privilege of using free wifi in the room, but I saw people with status get it. There are a few computers in the lobby and the connectivity was good. I have no particular complaint against the hotel and I would stay again.

“great new hotel” Stayed at this hotel with a friend to attend a Nascar race and NFL football game.The hotel itself is about a 20 minute drive from the airport and about the same to the U of Phoenix stadium area, not a problem as the road/freeways are very easy to navigate around the Phoenix area.This hotel is fairly new and easy to find in an area that is new(office buldings,stores,restautants,hotels).The room was clean and modern by hotel standards.The staff seemed friendly whenever we crossed paths. I would recommend this hotel to anyone,don't be scared off because its a little further away from everything.

“Great stay at the Hilton Bayfront. Would stay again” Checked into the Hilton Bayfront. Got a great rate for it. Really enjoyed the hotel. Room was on the 29th floor overlooking Petco Park and the Coronado Bridge. Lobby is big and spread out. Can be a little confusing to find stuff especially if there are a lot of people milling about. However, I found that the staff was always willing to help answer questions. Parking in the garage was easy and quick except on game nights. It was a short walk to the Gaslamp but not a straight shot as you had to go around the trolley tracks. They are building a pedestrian bridge which will be great. I got a great rate through work so was very happy with that. I would definitely stay here again but fear that the prices will jump quickly. My only complaints with the hotel were: 1) they had a massive convention going on and it was tough to get an elevator, waited up to 20 minutes at times. Not much the hotel can do but you should be aware of this. 2) All beers at the hotel bar were $8.00 except during Happy Hour. Little too expensive. Also, sodas from the machines were $3.50. 3) Parking was $25 for self parking (Typical for any downtown hotel). Garage is next door to the hotel. However, it is also used for game traffic and can get very busy before games. Just be aware of that, But service at the hotel was very good and enjoyable. I got free buffet coupons for breakfast every morning which worked great.

“Typical aloft: Cool and hip, but a bit noisy” Let me start by saying that I like W Hotels. I love the modern and hipper design. I've always considered aloft to be W-Lite. Perhaps I'm starting to show my age, but I'm starting to think aloft is a bit too hip for me. Checked into the aloft Harlem last Thursday night after my flight was diverted for a couple hours due to thunderstorms that closed all NYC airports. The neighborhood is definitely in Harlem, despite being a few (long) blocks away from Columbia University. At these late night hours (near 11 p.m.), the neighborhood was a bit sketchy (e.g., trash on the streets, streetlights out, vagrants wandering the streets). On the up side, aloft Harlem is located kitty-korner from the local police station. The downstairs bar area was packed with people. It was raucous and loud. I asked for a room on the opposite side of the hotel, and they were quite happy to accommodate me. Service from all hotel points of contact was exceptional, and very friendly. Since I was a Gold member, I was also given two coupons to redeem for two beverages in the self-service area. (I ended up not using them, but it was a nice touch.) I thought the price was a bit much ($199, even on a government rate!), too. The room was typical aloft--comfortable, stylish (similar to W Hotels, but definitely more frugal). Nothing was wrong with the room, and it was indeed very quiet on my end of the hotel (fifth floor, too). I had free wireless Internet in my room, which was a nice plus. However, as a warning, if you're with AT&T (and using an iPhone), Check-out (at 4:30 a.m. on a Saturday) was efficient, and friendly, and they even called a cab for me to Laguardia. I have no real complaints about aloft Harlem except maybe that on the Starwood site, they are trying to minimize the fact they are in Harlem. The neighborhood really wasn't as good as they want you to believe. Yes, granted this is still New York City, but I did feel a bit uncomfortable standing out in front of the hotel at 4:30 a.m. waiting for my cab. However, if you're smart about things (i.e., don't walk around the neighborhood late at night), you should be fine. Since I have no substantive complaints against the hotel itself, I should give it a higher rating. However, maybe I am showing my age, and I'm just not able to tolerate all the loud noises, and perhaps, I'm not as hip as I used to be (or like to think that I am).

“Great find!” i thought I'd stayed in just about every hotel in downtown Chicago, until I found this little gem. I searched solely on location to meetings I was attending over 2 days on North Wacker Drive, and wanted to be able to walk if possible. I found the Holiday Inn - Mart Plaza and was very impressed. It seems like a newer hotel, and I didn't even know it was there until now. It is very clean, Bath and Body Works amenities, awesome Asian/Italian restaurant on-site, which was very convenient and both the restaurant and hotel staff were super friendly. Wi-fi was free, parking with in-out priveleges was $39/day, typical for downtown hotels. The location is a bit off the beaten path, so to speak, but I felt comfortable walking around. It is right on the river across the street from the Loop. I would definitely stay here again.

“I love old hotels, but.....” Where do I start? My husband was in Los Angeles on business and my daughter and I decided to tag along and make it a vacation. The company that he works for, has offices located just two blocks away and has an agreement with this hotel. Therefore, we didn't choose it, nor did we have to pay for it. That being said, entering the hotel lobby is like going back in time. It is spectacular! The entire 1st floor is wonderful. The staff are exceptional and are really the very best part of this hotel. From the car attendant, bartender, check-in staff to the people working room service. All these people were wonderful! The room that we had on the 8th floor, was not! I've heard that they have done renovations on the Club Level floors, but they need to renovate the entire place. Our room was roomy, but there was tape on the walls, holding things in place. The carpet was ratted and frayed. The bathroom was tiny and had holes in the walls, marks on the door and the door would not shut. I had to go to another floor to get to the ice machine, which I didn't mind, but I was the only person in the halls and it reminded me of the hotel in the movie The Shining. It just gave me a creepy feeling. My husband asked the other people there for the conference what they thought of the hotel and they all said the same thing. The lobby area is beautiful, but the rest is creepy and needs to be renovated. I've stayed at many old hotels in large cities and I loved the character and charm they possess. Letting a hotel get rundown, is not adding to it's charm. I liked the area that the hotel was in and we caught the Hop On, Hop Off bus just across the street from the hotel on Grand Avenue in order to tour Hollywood, Santa Monica, L.A., etc... We won't be staying at this hotel again, until I read a review that says that the rooms have been renovated.

“Large Bathroom & Wonderful Bed” Enjoyed our stay at Loews Hollywood in the lovely room and very large bathroom which were very well decorated and clean. The bed and the new linens were wonderful - one of the best I have had in a hotel. Seems like I have been staying in hotels lately with small bathrooms so I really appreciated the space here. The bedroom was a good size too. Great central location for a Hollywood stay, and the added bonus of Starbucks in their lobby. I had a great price with a PricelIne bid, so I'm not sure what the price might have been without this deal, but I certainly will look in to a return stay the next time I am in the area.

“Great Hotel - Great Location - Great Price” I read the reviews on Trip Advisor after making and paying for three nights at the Moderne. Was leery of what we would end up with. But no worries - it is a very small, older hotel - only four rooms per floor - but very clean, quiet and we had no complaints. The bed was very large and comfortable and the room was fine for two adults. The staff were very friendly and accomodating. Great coffee in the morning. And in the middle of everything! Easy walking to everything we wanted to see - which was everything - and around the corner from the subway. Even though there isn't a restaurant on the premises there are numerous places to eat less than a block away. And you can't beat the price for the location. I would definitely consider staying here during my next trip to NYC.

“Uptown” It has been some time since I have stayed in Midtown and now I am ever more sure that I prefer Downtown New York. So my review is biased that I prefer and enjoy being in Soho, Tribeca and the Lower East side. There is nothing wrong with Midtown and since I was there for business it made sense, and also the access to shopping is excellent, though you find most of the higher end shops in Soho as well. Saying all that the New York Palace is a nice place to stay, the rooms are average and the service was good. The rooms could use some updating but my room was clean, spacious and comfortable. The service for my morning breakfast was excellent and the front desk staff at the Towers were helpful. I also have to say they provided the best shoe shine service I have experienced in a hotel and I appreciated the Moltan Brown products in the bathroom. This is a fine hotel that ranks just below the best.

“Andrew Labetti: My Hero!” I have been using Trip Advisor for years and often have wondered if management ever looks at this site to improve their service and get honest (read anonymous) feedback. In reviewing the comments left for the Benjamin in New York I was impressed to see that the management at this hotel DOES read the feedback. I was even more impressed to see the management responses that are consistently left for guests who have posted negative reviews. Whether the reviews are justified or not is irrelevant to me, I was impressed with Mr. Labetti's committment to improving his hotel's image. Needless to say, I was impressed throughout my stay at The Benjamin. Yes, the elevators were a bit of a wait during the "rush" times, but I don't see what the hotel could do to rectify this problem in a cost effective way. I found the staff professional, helpful, and really did go out of their way to serve the guests. The attention to detail such as Easter treats in the lobby on Sunday morning, freshening up the flowers in the lobby each day, and the doorman who really goes out of his way to hail a cab (quite a show indeed). I found our room to be quiet, spacious, and to be honest, larger that my own condo. in Toronto. Both my son and I had an exceptional stay at this hotel and would love to return once again in the future. Thank you Mr. Labetti, you are indeed a hero of the hospitality industry in N.Y.C.

“Historical Building with perfect modern Boutique Hotel inside” In the very, very centre, only a few steps from the subway station Government Center with direct connection to Logan Airport which is only an 8 minutes trip away Carefully renovated historical building with fantastic rooms including impressing bathroom. Very friendly staff, great restaurant. The owners did spend a lot of money to make a deluxe boutique Hotel with all possible comfort including iPod docking station and the biggest offer of a minibar that I have ever seen. They did really put everything in your room you may ever need when traveling including aspirine and world adapter When in Boston I would always stay at the Ames again and can highly recommend it

“Way beyond our expectations for a pet friendly hotel close to downtown - suite surprise!” I originally booked here because we are travelling with our dog and LQ is great about no pet deposits, etc. I did not realize the room was a bonafide suite! It is fabulous! Upscale, with luxe linens, limestone and granite, double-headed shower, many pillows, 2 sinks, *large* mini refrigerator, and beautiful dark wood and earthtone furnishings. Plus free secure parking with elevatot to your floor, free breakfast buffet, and coin laundromat in house. Free Haagen Daz and cookies and of course coffee in the lobby. This will be our new home when making our annual reunion pilgrimage. We loved the Moore Hotel, and it is cheaper, but this is a better value, just not as downtown. And many people with dogs! Dog park across street.

“Sehr empfehlenswert!” Das Hotel liegt sehr zentral im nördlichen Büroviertel von Manhattan. Vor der Haustür befindet sich die U-Bahn, mit der man in den Süden (Südspitze Manhattan) und Norden (Richtung Central Park/Harlem) fahren kann. Die 5th Ave ist in 10 Min. zu Fuß erreichbar. Das Hotelpersonal ist sehr freundlich und zuvorkommend, das Frühstück war sehr gut. Es gab heiße WAffeln, Omelett, frische Früchte. Joghurt, Kuchen - alles, was das Herz begehrt. DAs Zimmer war sehr sauber und gut ausgestattet, die dicken amerik. Matratzen ausgezeichnet. Zum Essen ein Tipp: In unmittelbarer Nähe befindet sich das tgl. bis in den späten Abend geöffnete Selbstbedienungsrestaurant "Azure" (3rd Ave. Ecke 51.) mit einer riesigen Salatbar und einer langen Theke mit unterschiedlichen warmen Gerichten. Da kann man prima zwischendurch essen!

“Liked it Alot” Recently stayed at the Manhattan Club. It was a timeshare exchange through RCI. Check in was quick at the Manhattan Club. We were assigned to an interior view 1 bedroom on the 24th floor. The room was clean and the facilities were in good shape, minus the elevators as others had mentioned. It was slow. It seemed to me the issue was that two out of the four lifts were reserved for the penthouse units/floors. Several times, we used the two freight elevators behind the lobby. The suite was kept nice and cool and noise wasn’t an issue. The 1 bedroom consists of a bedroom separated from the living area via a door. In addition to the one bath in the bedroom, there was a 3⁄4 bath in the living room area. This was nice as there were 3 of us. There was a microwave, however no cooking stove top. There was a mini fridge in the room. It’s NYC anyways... Who cooks? Daily cleaning was provided and the housekeeping staff did an excellent job everyday. All the staff appeared cheerful and we experienced no problems. The were no spas or pools, however there was a good gym on the top floor. There were 3 flat panel TV’s along with all the necessary machines, including free weights to work off all the great meals to be had nearby. I slept on the sofa bed one night and that was enough for me. Did not feel comfortable, but was okay with my little one. Overall, liked it a lot. It was in a great location with the subway a block away. You couldn’t ask for a better location. Tip: at 55th Street and 9th Avenue, there is a laundromat where you can do some laundry if you have to. Also next door on 9th Avenue, there is a bike shop, Liberty Bicycles that rents bicycles for $6 an hour. Looking forward to coming back.

“Great boutique option at LAX” Let me start this by saying I love boutique hotels. Custom Hotel is a cool, quirky option at LAX. The price was fantastic, about $115 for a king room and for another $30 or so I received a late check-out of 8:00 p.m.; perfect for red-eye flights back to the East Coast. Staff members were young but extremely friendly and accommodating. They extended my already late check-out an extra hour. The lounge was equally as friendly, no attitude in this hotel. The lobby, lounge and rooms were great. The corridors could use an upgrade though, they don't do justice to the rest of the building. Room was quiet and cozy, the bed is in the center of the room, unusual but unique. It would be nice to have a stocked mini-bar but there is a grocery store next door. I look forward to staying again.

“Service and location make up for dated rooms.” We booked a one night stay in a two room queen suite. Meredith, who was working the front desk, could not have been nicer or more accommodating. Check-in was a breeze and within minutes we were off to our room The building is older, so everything, including the elevators worked a bit slower, but we did not mind. Our "suite" on the third level was comfortable. The ceilings were quite low, and the bathroom quite small, but it was fine. Again, not a shiny penny, but clean and cozy, with a very welcoming queen bed. Upon registering, we were told of a complimentary happy hour on the top floor of the hotel. We decided to check it out and glad we did. Besides appetizers like fresh fruit, vegetables, dip, salad, and salty snacks, guests also got two free drinks (wine/beer). David, the "bartender", was super friendly and helpful. We enjoyed our cocktails and even chatted with a few other guests. The room served double duty as it also was where breakfast was served in the morning. It is open 24 hrs, so if someone needed to escape his/her room, this was a great place to come to. During breakfast, we could see the harbor from the glass enclosed floor. There was a make your own waffle station, eggs, potatoes, sausage, yogurt, fruit, juices, donuts, toast, bagels and cereal. Plenty of options to fill the tank. And again, service was spot on. Empty serving dishes were immediately filled, and dirty plates removed even though this was a do it your self meal. Of course, if you wanted to be near the Inner Harbor, well you couldn't get a better location. You are but steps to the water, shops and restaurants. We were going to a Bob Seger concert at the 1st Mariner Arena, so Brookshire Suites fullfilled our needs. A couple blocks, and we were at the venue......can't ask for more than that.

“Disappointing” My wife and I normally use this hotel as our base when staying in NYC. We were transiting on this occasion on our way home and we only stayed for one night. We arrived late, at about midnight, and requested a late checkout (both of which we had previously notified). The receptionist was mediocre to say the least. He gave a lot of guff - first 1pm, then maybe 12.30pm, and then maybe 12 pm (ie no late check-out!). When I advised him that we were essentially regulars, checking in late, and just looking for a late checkout at about 1pm, he eventually agreed. On arrival to our room it was very disappointing - it was dull, not very clean, with a seemingly abandoned press, and a poorly functioning tv. Overall poor. We went wandering early the next morning and arrived back about 12 pm after brekkie (at the lovely Pershing Bridge cafe across from Grand Central). On arrival, we found ourselves locked out of our room. Thankfully a kind porter let us into our room, after which we received two phone calls from reception to check that we were actually going to leave while we tried to pack and get ready. To top it off, when we got to reception at about 12.45pm, we had to queue for about 15 mins and were greeted by a rude receptionist and doorman. For all of this, over a 12-hour period, we were charged E220! I think that this hotel has seriously deteriorated since our last stay. The staff are rude and the overall hotel is poorly maintained. I think that they are taking advantage of the Irish contingent that regularly stay there, charging exorbitant prices for the quality offered. We would have considered ourselves regulars, but there are better hotels for a similar price in NYC. We have already advised some family members on their first visit to NYC to pick somewhere else, and we won't be back. Disappointing to see a previously good hotel lose basic standards and not appreciate their customers.

“Loved it!” My daughter and I stayed here for 4 nights and really enjoyed the hotel. The staff was very nice and the hotel beautifully decorated for the holidays. It is an older hotel, but has been nicely redone so that you have every comfort. The 28th Street subway is closeby, which is helpful. We felt safe even coming in late at night. We will go back to this hotel. Coffee in the lobby in the morning would be a nice addition - you have to go the the restraurant or next door to Dunkin Donuts (long line on weekdays) - too much trouble. All in all - a wonderful place to stay. Quiet and beds to die for - I never wanted to leave in the mornings.

“Do they have training for their managers ?” This is one of the nicest hotels you can stay in San Diego - great location, nice views, quiet, great pool area. This hotel definitly deserves an excellent rating if there just wasnt their manager Steve. We checked in and got this nice room with awesome views - we had our luggage brought up to the room and went straight down to the pool. After we returned, we recognized, that this room was used actually right before we checked in - the soap was used and there was trash in both trash cans. We were already settled in, so it wasnt a huge problem for us, but we still wanted to let the management know about this issue so they could prevent this from happening again. At the reception we asked to talk to the manager on duty and he was called. Yes, he got on the phone with us instead of meeting us in person - this could have been anybody!. We explained him the situation and told him that we only want to address this for future prevention. His anwer on the phone was - I am sorry Mr. Scholz, but people make mistakes. Is there anything else I can do for you? At his point we felt like staying at a Motel 6 or Days Inn ( no offense ) and I am sure, that they would have treated us more professional. We did not receive any complimentary compensation. We just let it go so it wouldnt spoil our nite. Next morning we called in again and talk to someone else - at least this time they credited the valet parking this time. The rest of the staff is working very professional and friendly - this hotel deserves an "excellent" if there had not been this manager - so we give this stay an unfortunate "terrible".

“Great Location, but place could have been nicer” The location can't be beat - you come up out of Penn Station on 32nd and it's right in front of you! Room size was also large - rare for an NYC room. Walls are a bit thin, there's a mini bar instead of a fridge, our bathroom wasn't as clean as it should have been - one washcloth had someone's fresh makeup on it and the 2nd day they didn't leave us any washcloths! The elevators are teeny and room smelled a bit musty. A plus is that they do have free wireless internet in the rooms. I give it an A for location, a C for cleanliness/comfort. I have in much nicer hotels for the same price, but they were all the way up by the UN Plaza. I will only stay here again if I cannot get a better price at another hotel.

“Fine hotel near Union Square” For my second stay in San Francisco I looked for a hotel near Union Square. Another requirement was in the room internet. The location of The Donatello is fantastic. One block from Union Square. Diners, shops, public transport, all very close to the hotel. The rooms are pretty good too. Clean, well equipped with TV, coffee machine, and all the usual stuff you expect in a hotel of this class. However, the wireless internet was almost unusable. I was moved to another room after complaining about this. That did help a bit, but not much. Staff was helpful and friendly. I think the hotel is a bit overpriced (I payed over 150 euro/210 dollar a night), but as long as wifi is not that important to you, I can definately recommend this hotel.

“The Hudson Hotel is . . .” We recently spent three nights at the Hudson Hotel. We paid a reasonable price of $140/night from Hotwire for New York. I would say that this is maybe the most unique (strange) hotel we have ever stayed at. For the most part, everything has been said about it in the numerous reviews. I agree the rooms are very small; lobby, rooms, and halls are dark. The hotel is very clean. The staff is very helpful and friendly. The rooms are very cutely appointed and a lot is stuffed into the very small space. We slept quite comfortably and spent very little time in the room. The A/C was working well but I found that if you pushed back the curtain (There are also blinds on the windows), the room was cooler because the curtain did not allow the cool air to go into the room. Would I pick to stay there again? Probably not.

“Bom custo benefício e localização excelente” Bem localizado, dá pra andar até a Fisherman ́s Wharf. Quartos limpos e banheiro enorme. Como o hotel fica na frente da Lombard St., tente ficar nos quartos do lado oposto. Fiquei em um quarto em frente a rua, mas mesmo assim o barulho da rua não me incomodou, pois não tenho sono leve.

“It is all about location.” Don't know how I got such a tremendous rate here, but it was worth every penny. Probably half the cost of other hotels in the area. Right in the middle of everything Times Square. Plus, the Cranberry Deli is a great place for breakfast and snacks, and it only two doors down. For dinner, try the PERFECT PINT, just a couple more doors down towards PLANET HOLLYWOOD. Now, this is not a hotel for those who want luxurious rooms with thick towels, plush carpeting, and a big screen TV. Hair dryers , irons, and ironing boards are available at the front desk. No ice buckets or ice machine. However, it is a good, clean place to sleep with nice sized rooms. (Our group had 3 rooms on the seventh floor; 701 on the smallish side;707 and 714 large by any New York standards) Will definitely try to stay there every time we visit NYC, so that we can spend our $ on other things.

“just average rooms” service varies from a 5 score to 1 score, depends who you meet. Front desk service is almost non exsistence. Bar and resturant has good service, what you expect from a good business hotel. location is great. rooms are very average, need some repair and maintainence. still tube TV's, no flat screens??? needs leadership to wake up and get with the programme.

“Can I live here? WOW!” We bid for this room and thought that even if it was a dump, it would suffice for a single night. We were pleasantly surprised! When I first checked in, the front desk clerk (Ashleigh) was sunshine and professionalism. I asked for two beds, which weren't available (it's becoming a pattern with "bid" rooms). I let her know that we were there for the marathon and one of us *cough* snores. She said they weren't completely full, and that she could upgrade me to a suite with a pull-out couch. Worth whatever upcharge there was going to be. None? Did I hear that right? She said that since they weren't full, she wanted to make sure I enjoyed my stay. I got to the room and it was huge. Small living room, decent sized kitchen, large bathroom, and.... wait for it... a separate full bedroom that felt about the same as the Seattle Renaissance. It was decorated in a tastefully minimalist style, with upscale bedding, flat screens (yes, 2), granite counters, and plush carpeting. We had a view of the water from our window, and it was a gorgeous sunset. Breakfast the next morning was a typical breakfast bar, but hooray for some protein! (scrambled eggs). They have weeknight manager's receptions M-Th. The business center is a single computer and printer, but it's in a nice, secluded room complete with a small library of books. Free Internet throughout the hotel that was pretty quick to load. There's a small store in the lobby with reasonably priced snacks (that, too, was a shock - the reasonable part.) Parking in Seattle SUCKS. There's no way around it -- except that the one block around the hotel has 24 hour free parking. We were lucky enough to find a spot. It was 5 blocks up and 6 blocks over to the start of the Seattle Marathon (the stadium at Seattle Center). Enough of us were there that a shuttle would have been good thinking. I'm really impressed with this hotel. The service was amazing, and every employee we passed acknowledged and/or greeted us. The hotel was spotless and looks new inside. Even at full price, this would be a bargain.

“Excellent location in SoMA !” Stayed 4 nights there, I was expect worst than that actually, quite surprised. Nice hotel, in a perfect location + free wifi, 2 minutes from Powell station (BART/MUNI), 2 minutes from Market Street, 10 minutes from the SFMOMA. Just avoid, the little details like lack of paint in some spots in the room, thin wall, no safe. As well, I think it was a bit pricey, I know it was the World Series in SF but it was 190$ a night. I still will recommend the Pickwick Hotel. PROS: *Location in central SoMa *Free wifi *Confortable bed *Free ''Keurig'' coffee in the room *2 minutes from Powell station *1 minute from Westfield Mall CONS: *Lack of paint in some spots, a renovation will be good for the hotel *thin wall, could hear the people beside my room *when you turn on the hot water, it's make a loud noise *no safe to put your valuables *a bit pricey for what it is

“A charming and comfortable hotel” My husband and I stayed here for a three night Manhattan getaway. The hotel was very attractive, the staff were friendly and helpful and the room was comfortable and quiet. We would recommend the hotel and stay here again. We got our reservations through Priceline -- hotels in Manhattan are never cheap and rarely spacious, but I felt we got good value for what we paid. When we checked in, I asked very politely if we could be upgraded. The front desk clerk upgraded us from a "cozy" room to a "spectacular" room at no extra charge. The room was not large but it was sufficient, and from what I read in other reviews here, it represented a big improvement on the "cozy" choice. Once we closed the door, we heard very little noise from either the hallway or the street. We were on the sixth floor. The bed was very luxurious and we slept well. The bathroom was small (and not very private with the frosted glass door), but well appointed with space to put your stuff. There is a dock for your iPod and wired and wireless internet connections (which I didn't test). There are lots of easily accessible electrical outlets. The concierge answered all our questions and made some great recommendations for sightseeing and getting around the city. There is a spa, but we didn't visit it. We ate breakfast at the hotel restaurant twice. The food was good, if a bit pricey, with plenty of healthy choices. The service was efficient and friendly. Our main purpose in visiting New York is to attend theater, and the hotel was within reasonable walking distance of the Broadway theaters, assuming you are an avid walker. Otherwise, it is a short cab ride. The neighborhood feels very safe and there are lots of stores, restaurants, coffee shops and other amenities. There is a street fair on Lexington in front of the hotel on Sundays. In sum, I would highly recommend this hotel. Enjoy your stay in New York.

“Not their best moment!” I preface this by saying, the employee on duty was flying solo for the first time, after a month of training. She was handling every challenge being thrown at her with a smile. I also want to say I am a "Road Warrior" - (Holiday Inn Gold Member), and have seen a lot of adversity in hotel management. This was handled as good as anyone could have expected. 8PM - Saturday - 7/28/12 - The start of this employees shift! I feel the management and ownership of this property should have taken a closer look at the capacity of this hotel and scheduled more than just 1 employee to be on duty. This was not fair to the employee or the guests. There were rooms which could have been rented that were not cleaned. There were patrons asking for supplies which weren't available (pillows/ iron/ towels were just coming out of a dryer). The retail Pantry was wiped out, and 90+% out of stock. (This happens to be the business I am in, so I take notice of the condition of the Pantrys.) Garbage cans at the entrance were overflowing with garbage. Guests were saying their carpets were soaked with water runover from their A/C unit. The 3 computers at one point had to be rebooted which took the employee off-line until she was able to contact the manager via telephone for the passwords. The location manager handled the situations via phone. I'm not so sure I wouldn't have gone in myself, or called someone to go in and assist. It appeared whomever worked the 1st shift handed off a hotel that was not ready for the night shift person! As it worked out, after waiting nearly 3 hrs. for a room, it was determined the hotel was oversold. To the credit of the management of this location, they sent us up the street to another IHG property, which was just fine. I am sorry to be so critical, as I booked this hotel based on all the "Good" comments left by other patrons. I am sure this was just a bad moment which can be overcome with a little more oversight by ownership and management.

“Excellent experience” A classy establishment from top to bottom. The desk staff was very professional. The room was well-stocked and clean. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom had great toiletries. Join their rewards club for free internet access and a breakfast beverage. I was at a conference in the hotel and the food there was excellent. The hotel is also right next to the baseball park. I enjoyed the ambience of the fans arriving and the smell of hotdogs and french fries. I was on the other side of the hotel from the ballpark and would recommend it to keep the noise down.

“Fabulous, old world hotel!” We are just back from a 5 night stay in the Algonquin hotel in New York. Firstly the bedrooms ARE small, but dont let that put you off. We had a walk in closet, a reasonably sized bathroom ( could have done with better quality towels) with ample space to put our stuff. The bed was immensely comfortable and the room was very clean. Our rate included continental breakfast which was really nice and more than adequete. The lobby area is wonderful, full of standard lamps, cosy nooks and sofas and armchairs, very old world and charming. Drinks are expensive there, 15 dollars before tax and tip for a vodka, though the measures seemed to be generous. Mathilda the cat was on hand greeting everyone, very sweet. We attended the show in the Oak Room on the Saturday night. We paid 360 dollars for two of us, this included dinner, one bottle of wine, the show and a tip. Certainly it was expensive but the show with Mark Nadler and KT Sullivan was wonderful and it was a nice opportunity to get all dressed up. Overall, the staff were most pleasant and attentive and we would certainly stay here again.

“More than adequate” We were accommodated at this hotel as a courtesy when our reservation at another hotel was not honored due to overbooking. The Crowne Plaza is not the same class hotel; however, the staff there is genuinely friendly and accomodating! Our room was clean, bed comfortable, shower excellent, minimal street noise (11th floor), walls between guest rooms not soundproof (TV and voices in next room audible but quieted by 11:00pm); complementary wi-fi; hotel shuttle drove us to the basketball game AND picked us up afterward; Wed. Manager 's reception w/ complementary wine, beer, food; included breakfast buffet not so good - except for coffee, OJ, boxed cereal yogurt (scrambled eggs hard and grainy, grits congealed, biscuits hard and dry); gym equipment minimal. Overall we were satisfied that the hotel gave us their best.

“Needs upkeep but night staff was great!” Overall, motel had good needed amenities (newspaper, flatscreen TV, workstation, shuttle to/from airport, fridge, continental breakfast etc.) Room was too small for all the furniture, stains on walls and bedskirts. Night staff was helpful and welcoming with my delayed flight very late check in-much appreciated!

“My "go-to" place in Boston” I have stayed here several times on business, the last being March 2012. The hotel is in the middle of the action on Boylston, and a couple of blocks over from Newbury. Like most times, I stayed just overnight this last time. The room is large and very new...with auto controls for everything from a touchscreen by the bed. The bathroom is very large with a separate shower and bath tub. I even managed to use the yoga mat to do some surya namaskars before heading out for drinks this last time. The beds are large and very comfortable...makes it hard to get out for meetings in the morning. I have been in the bar a couple of times, when sorta snowed in and the barkeeps are always entertaining and make good drinks. I have had breakfast here in the main resto and the service was good. I have seen the gym a few times, but not been able to use it yet. As mentioned earlier, there are a lot of great bars and restaurants within a short walk, which is a great plus. The doormen are also very helpful and cheerful...always help to get a cab. This is my go to place in Boston...over the Ritz, Taj or the Langham (all very good). I haven't stayed at the Four Seasons in Boston yet...and don't think I will. If anything, the only negative is that I need to go to the Exchange Place area a lot for meetings and it's a 10 min drive at least. Solid 4.5 stars.

“Nice hotel” I was there for a conference and found the accommodations to be very nice. Everything was clean and well maintained. Staff was curteous. There is a lack of food, however. There is one small restaurant, which is more like a coffee shop and it was quite expensive. There are places to walk to but I did not want to do that before an 8:00 meeting. I did best by walking to Panera in the evening and buying something to eat the next morning in my room. Beware of days when there are baseball games as the hotel is acorss the street from the stadium and it creates a lot of activity.

“Highly recommended place to stay near DEN Airport” We stayed here one night by choice because our scheduled flight was due in at night and we didn't want to get our rental car and set off on our road trip until the next morning. We had two adults and a teenage boy in a one-bedroom suite. The teenager used the sofabed in the living room, so he had his own TV, and could use the kitchen sink for brushing his teeth and washing up. He only had to use the bathroom (in the bedroom) for showering, etc. The sink was outside the shower/toilet room, which was convenient. The place was extremely clean and quiet, and the full hot breakfast was wonderful. We also took advantage of the convenience store at the front desk for late night snacks. They have a nice outdoor BBQ grill/picnic area if you're there for longer than one late night! The fitness facilities looked limited - a couple of cardio machines and a small indoor pool. The airport shuttle was free, but only seems to run every 30 minutes - you have to call from the airport to summon it, and make a reservation the night before to use it in the morning. The drivers are extremely courteous and are also helpful with baggage.

“Not a good deal - could have done better.” Drove from Tahoe to San Fran and booked this hotel night before - 3 nights, Friday, Saturday and Sunday $100 per night. Seemed to be reasonable and location was good - Pier 39 20 mins walk. Hotel was just very average - rooms ok, free parking. If you get a good deal, you could do worse, but we didnt and I wish we had looked elsewhere.

“Okay Hotel in the University District of Seattle” My wife and I travel to Seattle four or five times a year. As a couple that enjoys boutique hotels, my wife and I found the Watertown Hotel to be satisfactory, but certainly nothing to get excited about. We usually stay at one of the Kimpton Hotels (there are three in Seattle), but all three Kimpton Hotels were sold out for the July 6 to 8, 2007 weekend due to the Kenny Chesney Flip Flop Summer Tour 2007, so we looked over Seattle hotel reviews on Tripadvisor. The Watertown Hotel was the only top 5 rated hotel in Seattle with a room available (they told me on the telephone it was their last available room), so we booked the room for $185 (plus tax) per night. The Watertown Hotel is located in the University district, about six miles north of downtown Seattle. It is a safe area with plenty of restaurants located within walking distance of the hotel. Our room, like the property itself, was clean and well looked after. The room had a comfortable King bed, basic washroom, tiny fridge and a small television set. Our room was located off the elevator lobby on the fifth floor, so there was a lot of hall noise until well past midnight both nights of our stay. There is free, secured parking, located under the hotel for hotel guests, but the parking stalls are tiny and the ceiling only six feet, six inches high, so larger vehicles may have problems parking. Also, the breakfast selection was not satisfactory (limited items, with no fruit or healthy eating options), so we wandered over to the Farmer's Market (five blocks away) for breakfast one morning and we drove to the 14 Carrot Cafe for beakfast the second day (located a couple miles from the Watertown Hotel at 2305 Eastlake Ave E on the way to downtown Seattle). In summary, we would stay at the Watertown Hotel again, but it will never be our first choice in the Seattle area.

“Grande old hotel in great shape” Fairmont Copley Plaza is a beautiful old hotel that is kept in very good condition. Stunning lobby and the room I was in on Gold floor was great: very large, lovely furnishings, beautiful bathroom.

“Would stay here again” The location of the Chancellor was great, right in Union Square and about 3 - 4 blocks from Market Street and the Bart station. My first impression was that the room was a bit on the small side, but we quickly got used to it. We had a walk-in closet, never heard our neighbors and the staff was very helpful. There's a Starbucks across the street and a Walgreen's on the corner. It's walkable to Fisherman's Wharf (about 30 - 40 minutes) for those interested in walking the city.

“Clean and convenient” I stayed here overnight because of a business meeting nearby. I was a little nervous when checking in because the location didn't look so safe. I was surprised by my room. It was spacious, clean and cool. I walked to a restaurant to have dinner and felt safe. The breakfast buffet in the morning which is included in the price of the room was delicious. The scrambled eggs, sausage and coffee were great. I would stay here again.

“grande dame with small rooms” Came to hotel for a conference. The conference "special" rate ended up being $50 more than the regular website price. The public places are beautiful -the lobby, convention area, etc. Service fairly good, quite good location -7-10 min walk to Copley sq. There many parking lots nearby - avoid the $38/nite valet parking. The rooms are on the budget side - bathroom very small, the heat unit makes a fairly loud sound all night long (turning on and off). Beds and linens are comfortable and soft. Good choice of movies on pay-per-view.

“Average Hotel” The hotel rooms were above average, about what I would expect from a Fairmont property. The lounge service on the night we stayed was absolutely horrible. We have been there (to the lounge) three times before and had great service. On this occasion, we waited for 20 minutes for service, then went up to the bar and asked for someone to be sent over to take our food and drink order. When the cocktail server arrived, she told us, "I'll take your order, but this isn't my section." After very rudely taking our order, I asked to speak to a manager. She said there was not a manager on duty (yeah, right). When we finally received our $11 hamburger, which was listed as coming with french fries, it came without the fries. We were then told by the cocktail server that the kitchen was closed, and we were out of luck. It was now about 12:35 and the menu listed food being served until 1:00am. After a bit of an argument she relented and put in the fry order. When we received the check, she told us, "Don't leave me a tip." Being that it was late at night, and I didn't feel like ruining my evening over french fries and this lousy server, I decided to not pursue a complaint at that time; instead I wrote a letter to management. I have yet to receive a reply. The attitude of this server may have been expected at a low rate diner, but not at a Fairmont hotel!

“Close and quiet” This hotel has real good proximity to OSU and is in a nice neighborhood. The other H.I. Expo (my wife stayed there years ago) is in a less attractive area, but also has close proximitiy. This Olentangy location is much more appropriate if a woman is traveling alone. Other than proximity the room was clean and quiet. Everything else was typical H.I. Express - breakfast room, room layout, etc. The only minor complaint is that there was no card given with the internet access details - I had to call down for the info. Across the street and over is a Bob Evans for those wanting a "real" breakfast.

“Great place at a great price for the city!” We come to Seattle often because my son is in school there. This is the first time we've stayed downtown, because my daughter came along and hadn't seen much of Seattle. The deal was so good (with a free parking perk!) and this hotel was situated in such a perfect spot for exploring. It looked nice on the website, and got good reviews, so we gave it a go. Am I glad we did! What a lovely place. From the moment you enter the warm, inviting lobby, greeted equally warmly by the staff, you feel at home. The room we got was huge--two queens, a gigantic walk-in closet, sitting area, large desk and nice bar area--and comfortable. The beds were comfortable, nicely appointed and clean. The bathroom, although small, was well-stocked with all the essentials. There is a restaurant off of the lobby, with Mediterranean inspired food. It always smelled good, and had a lively bar in the evenings. We could walk everywhere from here, or catch one of the free downtown buses when we were tired. The staff, as I mentioned before, was extremely helpful and friendly. I especially loved the parking valets, who had to RUN back and forth to the parking garage (located above a store kitty-cornered from the hotel) to fetch cars. They were energetic, upbeat and tireless. I would definitely recommend this for those who like a hotel with a bit of character.

“Amazing views from Midtown West... but a little far from the action” I stayed on for a couple of days after doing some business in New York. I chose Ink48 as I was staying at my own expense after the business part of the trip, and I know Kimpton hotels always deliver quality at a price that doesn't break the bank, unlike many other NYC hotels. The hotel is quite new, which is reflected in all the public spaces and rooms - slick modern design, high ceilings, etc. There's a bar on the rooftop with an amazing view back across Manhattan - it's worthwhile going to this bar even if you're not a guest at the hotel. The only downside is it's way on the West side (11th St) - I didn't realise that the E/W blocks were so long, but it took me at least 10 minutes to walk to the subway on 9th, and I walk fast. From Broadway you walk through a residential neighbourhood to get to the 11th, which has nowhere near the volume of people or activity as a few blocks east. All said, if you don't mind a stroll and prefer to be ever-so-slightly removed from the action, it's a great hotel and I'd definitely recommend it.

“Typical for a Hyatt...no surprises.” I was here for a conference and delighted with the Hyatt for the facilities. One problem was that the staff could not direct us to the location of the conference, due to the fact that they had not received the next days schedule (we needed to set-up as the conference started at 0630 the next morning)...in this day and age, this should be something pretty easy to resolve....especially from a hotel that specializes in conferences. Othe rthan this (which was a mild inconvenience) the stay was great.

“A Truly Exceptional Property. They definitely made us feel at home and welcome.” Our family of six stayed three nights in a two bedroom bay view suite in June 2012. We had a perfect stay from check-in to check-out. Every element of the hotel was excellent from service to accommodations to location. I highly recommend this hotel if it's in your budget and would not hesitate to stay here again. The valet was very friendly, professional and efficient at each and every encounter including running down to the car for us to get a couple items we had left. Santiago personified the welcoming nature of the staff and truly made us feel at home. The front desk staff checked us in efficiently and walked us to our room familiarizing us with the hotel layout despite our late night arrival. The complimentary breakfast is more than sufficient to get you up and going for the day. They had a wide variety of pastries, hot filled croissants, breakfast burritos, and breakfast sandwiches, as well as gourmet instant oatmeal and the fixings, at least five types of beautiful fresh fruit and yogurt. Plenty of selection on coffee and teas as well. Our favorite location to dine was the Nursery Terrace (the weather was lovely when we visited) but it can get cool out there. Our room was modern with a well-appointed kitchen. Plenty of room for us and our four children to stretch out. State of the art sound system. The housekeeping staff was excellent. In 8 years of luxury travel, this resident attendant is only the second to leave us a thank you note for the gratuity that we left. Very sweet note, too. :) The location of this hotel was ideal for what we wanted to do. We walked east and enjoyed the Ferry Market Terminal Farmer's Market, Alcatraz Tours, Pier 39, Ghirardelli Square, dim sum at Yank Sing-Rincon Bldg location (MUST TRY) and drove west to the Exploratorium, Chrissy Field, Ocean Beach, and Golden Gate Bridge. Also great for catching the cable car to Union Square though I recommend doing that during off hours as it can still be a wait. This hotel receives my highest recommendation.

“Great value, great location” We really enjoyed our stay at the Chandler Inn. For those who prefer larger hotel rooms, you will likely find Chandler's rooms to be too small, but since I don't usually spend my vacations in my hotel room, I found the space to be more than adequate. Our room came equipped with air conditioning, flat screen tv. Chandler also offers complimentary wifi and a self serve hot beverage station is located in the lobby. The cleaning staff did an amazing job of maintaining the hotel; our room was always spotlessly cleaned when we'd return. The hotel is located in a quiet residential neighbourhood, conveniently above Fritz's bar, a gay sports bar that serves an awesomely strong dirty martini. We went there for a drink, but also returned to try their delicious weekend brunch. Chandler Inn is also within walking distance to good food -- Delux Cafe, a cozy neighbourhood bar on Chandler Street and PICCO on Tremont. There is also a 7 Eleven just around the corner if you ever need snacks at the odd hour. In terms of transit, the closest is Back Bay Station but because Boston is such a walking city, we rarely used the T. If I ever find myself in Boston again, I would definitely book again at the Chandler Inn.

“OK hotel” Stayed here for a conference a few weekends ago; it was an ok hotel. The rooms were large by Boston hotel standards and had a refrigerator, a couch and a desk. It was quiet at night and reasonably clean. The location was not the most convenient and the shuttle service from the hotel was not entirely reliable as a means to get to where you needed to be. The morning breakfast in the lobby was average for this type of hotel.

“They even have outdoor BBQ grills” We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite with 2 Queen beds for the weekend and I must say it was worth every penny. There was so much real estate within the bedroom that we had enough room to stretch our luggage out on the floor and still had room to walk around. It has a full kitchen with pans, cups, plates, gas stove, microwave, and even a refrigerator. What impressed me though was the fact that they actually have 2 outdoor BBQ grills outdoors near the pool area. I don't know how much the hotel would charge for its use, but the fact that they have it as an option was great for families or anyone requiring an extended stay in the area. They serve free breakfast which is included with your stay, and they have hot scrambled eggs, corned beef hash, waffles, juices/coffee/milk, cereal, etc. Pretty good selection in my mind. The area is quiet. It is in the middle of a business park and a gated community accross the street. It might be a little bit difficult to find the place, but worth the hassle for a place like this. I will be back to this place.

“Nice place, the Omni San Fransisco.” We did a 4 week tour of the USA over December/January 2007, with 3 older children (girl, 22, boy, 19 and boy, 18), going to San Francisco [Omni Hotel], Miami (South Beach) [Beacon Hotel], Orlando (Disneyworld, Pop Century Resort), Chicago [Drake Hotel], New York (for Christmas) [Beacon Hotel - unrelated to the Beacon in Miami], Boston [Omni Hotel], New York (again) [Roosevelt Hotel] (including New Year’s Eve at the Renaissance Hotel overlooking Times Square), and a day trip to Niagara Falls. It was sometimes very cosy - sometimes downright stressful - with the kids. Anyway, here are my accommodation reviews. I’ll mention side trips and tours too. Sometimes the accommodation was arranged through a travel agent, but on a couple of occasions I organised it direct. The Omni was arranged through a travel agent in Brisbane, though as usual I had checked with Trip Advisor, and then asked the travel agent to book it when I was satisfied. He got me better rates than going to the hotel direct, too. We were also staying at an Omni in Boston, and as I'd joined the Omni's Select Guest program (free, via the internet), there were advantages to be had. Plus, we'd previously stayed at the Omni in Washington and it was spectacular (my favourite of the 3 Omnis I've stayed in whilst in the USA), so we thought it would be good. We weren't disappointed. Fairly large rooms (we had a double and a triple, though the kids weren't particularly happy at 2 of them having to share a double bed - but then, they're not paying!); interconnecting which was useful. Free internet (I had a laptop) for Select Guest members (if you stay at the Omni, the Select Guest program is recommended - free juice/coffee and newspaper delivered every morning). Very reasonably sized bathroom. In all, very comfortable. It's a grand building with an impressive foyer. We received a lovely sincere welcome from the bell captain on arriving. The hotel is not all the conveniently located, but we were happy to walk and find our way around. Finding cheap restaurants (try feeding 5, including 2 big boys, for 4 weeks straight - you won't be eating at the hotel restaurants very much!) was a bit of a task, but not impossible. Speaking of meals, we fell over Francis Ford Coppola's Italian cafe in Kearney Street on the way back from climbing the Coit tower - it was great. Google it if you are interested. I brought some of the wine back to Australia. We decided to eat there purely on the basis of the menu and the look of the place, then found out who the famous owner was. Recommended purely on the Italian food and the venue, if nothing else. We did a tour of the city (booked through the travel agent), which was absolutely worthwhile. Stopped at good views of the city (from a high lookout), and another spot for views of the Golden Gate Bridge (which the bus drove over). It also included a harbour cruise from Pier 39 at Fisherman's Wharf, which went under the Golden Gate Bridge and circled Alcatraz Island. It's a good way to see the highlights. Our time at the Omni in San Francisco was good - nice rooms and ambience, but not budget accommodation.

“Typical Westin - Great Beds and Comfortable rooms” Typical Westin Hotel, which means great beds and larger, very comfortable rooms. Slept wonderfully in one of those Westin Heavenly beds. Was able to check-in early and check-out a little late, both of which were greatly appreciated. One minor disappointment...when I checked in the front desk asked me if I wanted a Wall Sreet Journal each morning (as is identified in my Starwood Profile). Never did get one, even after re-verifying with the front desk.

“absolutely disgusting, one of the worst hotels in the country.” I travel constantly and I've seen hundreds of hotels from coast to coast. I have to say I believe this in one of my worst hotel experiences every and that's saying a LOT. The staff was rude, the rooms were tiny and outdated. My pillow was flatter than a board. I felt bugs crawling on me at night and had a few bites on me the next morning. Big red ugly welts. I wouldn't let my dog stay in this run down hooker joint. It was really really bad, STAY AWAY, pay more money and get something that is half way decent.

“Average Airport Hotel” Great Beds and Great Location... A little bit of a pain getting in and out thru the airport. The parking is free !! If you are just in the Dallas area for a day or so this hotel has everything. They charge for internet. The front desk checked me in very quickly.

“Convenient location is the biggest asset” Booked with Priceline and got a bargain price. Meets all basic needs, clean room and comfortable bed. Nothing grand or awe-inspiring. Located at the airport although one still needs to ride the shuttle to get to it. Quiet room despite the location.

“Pretty nice!” This hotel was in the process of a renovation during my visit. It seems that they are almost done because the work is being done on the 2nd floor. I was able to get one of the newly remodeled rooms and it was pretty nice. The room was average size with a nice desk for plenty of work space. The bed was pretty comfy. The wireless internet was a little hit and miss my second day there, but there was a nice business center on the first floor that I was able to use. There were several people at the bar each night and looked to be comfortable and having a nice time. The hotel is right across from the basketball arena at UT and not too much further from the football field. This would be a good place to stay for UT sporting events. There is a newly built Denny's in front of the hotel that is open 24 hours. Parking is free as well as the wireless internet. The warm Doubletree chocolate chip cookie is always a plus! I visit Austin quite often and will it's very likely I will stay at this property on a return visit.

“The good and the not so bad” I recently stayed at the Hilton for a convention. The convention was at the Austin Convention Center which is located across the street from the Hilton. You could not possibly stay any closer to the convention center, and this was a real plus for me. There are also convention facilities located in the hotel and a separate convention was going on there. As a result the hotel was fully booked and I was not able to get the king size bed I had reserved. I was able to check in early though, and the double beds were fine for my stay. Also, my floor (15th) and my room were always quiet, and elevator waits were quite reasonable, for such a full hotel. The room was nice enough but is beginning to show wear and tear. They may be undergoing a renovation but it has not reached that floor yet. I used room service and ate in the lobby restaurant and both were fine. I will say that ALL of the employees I came into contact with gave wonderful customer service, and that goes a long way with me in making up for worn out carpet. If you have convention business in Austin and can access a discount rate as a result, I would recommend staying at this Hilton!

“Lovely affordable Art Deco property” When you walk in you are struck by the Art Deco feel of the property. It is inviting. The staff were efficient. My room was very small and would have been too small for 2 people. The towels were also miniature. The rooms were clean. Some ladies who traveled with me had a room with 2 double beds and 2 bathrooms, probably from the renovation reducing the number of rooms. Great option for families or women travelling together. The location is very good although the taxi drivers preferred to drop you at the corner instead of in front of the hotel due to traffic. The Tick Tock Diner is nice and the coffee bar in the lobby is a godsend. I enjoyed it athough it is a no frills type of room But then again, who goes to New York and stays in their room?

“The Roosevelt is a great deal!” Because of work in New York, we stay in the city about a month out of each year. We have stayed in many hotels in midtown as a result. The Roosevelt was a nice find, very close to Grand Central Station and within easy walking distance to the theaters, the mid town business district and Times Square. The lobby is among the best in the city, and the restoration work is near perfect without looking plastic.
