“Decent Stay in a Great City” Silver Cloud had a fantastic front desk staff - very welcoming, friendlly, and humorous. The hotel itself is what you'd expect from a 3 star hotel -- no incredible amenities, but everything was clean and in working order. It was fairly accessible to most Settle sites and provided a good central location for walking points around the city.

“Recently updated with friendly staff and no free breakfast” In what appears to be a trend with Marriott Courtyards, this location was recently updated to a trendy lobby. As I've noticed with other locations, when that update occurs, the free breakfast disappears. The staff was very friendly. The one elevator is slow. The rooms were modern and clean. The location is right next to the freeway so a lot of noise carries into the rooms. If you want an affordable hotel with free breakfast, however, there are many other choices within the immediate vicinity.

“Superb service.” What more can I say. I love great service and from the bartenders, spa employees, to the repair men I was overwhelmed at how each person made a tremendous effort to make sure I was welcome and everything was perfect. I especially liked how gratuity is included so no more carrying around change specifically to tip. The room was spacious, clean, fantastic sheets, comfortable pillows and mattress. Next time I stay in Chicago this will be on the top of my list.

“Average Stay” This hotel is in a great location near the Inner Harbor and Little Italy. There are many restaurants and bars within walking distance and it is adjacent to a Whole Foods store. The property is relatively modern and has a simple restaurant and bar (with a breakfast buffet for an additional fee) in the lobby as well as a limited snack shop typical of Courtyard properties. There is an indoor parking deck with a fee typical of downtown areas. Service at the front desk was cheerful and helpful. The room was medium sized and relatively modern. The bathroom was fine but the walk-in shower appeared somewhat older in appearance than the remainder of the room. The tv was modern and everything was in working order. There is a small balcony for fresh air and to take in the decent views of the harbor and downtown area. I have some complaints about the property. There were some cigarette butts on my balcony and I noticed the same dirty towel two consecutive days in the fitness center. Additionally the weights in the fitness center are worthless and should be replaced or simply discarded. Also, the bread in the breakfast buffet appeared old as if was kept out for consecutive days. Finally, Marriott reward members are given a coupon for up to 25% (depending on status level) off the price of a domestic beer or wine. I feel this is a real cheap "gift" as many hotels offer a free drink and some even have a complimentary wine happy hour. Overall not a bad place to stay for business or leisure but there are a lot of little things that would prevent me from considering this a great property.

“Filthy and unpleasant” What a dump! I have been a follower of this Chain of hotels since the early 80's, and have stayed at this property at least 10 times. In the last year we have stayed twice in San Antonio at this hotel and a new sister hotel on the River Walk in San Antonio. Both stays we're unpleasant. On the River Walk a new Kindle was stolen, on last nights stay the place was so dirty you felt like you had to wash your feet even when wearing flip flops. The linens were thread bare, and the curtains were broken. The elevators were also filthy with spilled drinks, cokes and coffee, seriously! The free morning breakfast was third quality at best with dirty floors and tables in the dining area.. Even the trays were sticky and dirty. Shame on Hilton for allowing their name to be associated with such a dump! Embassy Suites clean up you act. For a stay near the airport in San Antonio there are nicer newer Hilton Properties near by. Don't assume anymore that Embassy Suites is the most comfortable just because of their free happy hour and free breakfasts! CLEAN UP YOUR ACT!!!!

“GREAT HOTEL IN AN EXCELLENT POSITION AND WOULD DEFINITELY STAY THERE AGAIN” ARRIVAL: Taxi from the airport to hotel approximately US$50. Priority Club members will have the normal recognition and greeting. Most staff are excellent and very helpful and check in went without any problems. SECURITY: Anyone can walk into the hotel lobby and take a lift to any floor as you only have to use your key card to open your room door. Very heavy police presence outside the hotel every day with at least two police vehicles parked constantly outside the hotel and at least 4 police officers always on duty. We always felt safe walking around outside the hotel. ROOMS: This is an old hotel but the rooms are what you would expect from an Intercontental Hotel which is very good. The hotel only has 14 floors so don’t expect great views. Windows are double glazed so no problems with traffic noise. In room safes available. POSITION: Great position with restaurants just outside the hotel. TOURS: The Red hop on hop off bus picks up just around the corner from the hotel. Cost is $54 per person for a 48 hour usage. The cost includes all three loop tours plus the night tour so fairly good value - tickets available at the pick up position around the corner from the hotel. Stops include Battery Point where you can take a ferry across to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. There is also a FREE ferry across to Staten Island and return with no ticket required. You need to get off the ferry on arrival and go into the departure lounge to take the return ferry. RESTAURANTS: Try the Longwood Gourmet eatery just over the road from the hotel on the corner of Lexington and 48th - hot and cold self serve dishes with about 30 selections to choose from and all sold at US$7 per lb in weight - ok to eat in as they have their own tables. On the opposite corner there is Raffles which is fully licenced - good size steak with chips and side salad for US$23. Wine by the glass is a little expensive at $10 per glass. They add a 18% service charge which is not mentioned on the menu. There is a liquor store just around the corner from the hotel with most imported wines available from US$8 per 750ml bottle. Try the Australian Yellowtail Merlow, Shiraz or Cabernet Savignon at around US$10 per bottle - excellent wine and good value at this price. INTERNET: Cost is approx about US$13 per day and cable connection is available in room. WiFi is not available in room but is available in other areas of the hotel. Try and get it included with your room package for free. BREAKFAST: Hotel Full Buffett is available at approx. US$35 per person so best if you can have it included as part of your package. Very good selection of hot and cold dishes plus fresh fruits. This price does not include 15% gratuity so much better if you have breakfast included as it works out much cheaper. Breakfast is also available at an eatery just a few doors up from Longwood Gourmet (mentioned above) at very reasonable prices. OVERVIEW: Great hotel in an excellent position and would recommend it and we would definitely stay there again.

“Nothing special, but perfect for what I paid” There is really not much to say about this Hilton. Its pretty unremarkable by every measure, and that isn't necessarily a bad thing for a New York hotel. Pros: -No executive lounge, so breakfast is downstairs at Rare. I've actually decided this is a good thing since the food is good and has a lot of options. Hilton Times Square has the same deal since they don't have an executive lounge either. -Rooms are nice, and the size is fine. People that are saying the rooms are small obviously haven't stayed in a lot of hotels in new york. If you want to see tiny go to a courtyard, hampton inn, element, or any of the really tall narrow hotels. The rooms are probably between 200-300 sq ft which is definitely smaller than the Hilton Times Square, but comparable to Hilton New York, the W and a lot of other hotels in the City. -The location is pretty good. Its a couple blocks from the subway, walking distance to a lot of good food in Chelsea, close to Penn Station. Its definitely a hike to Times Square, Central Park etc but doable if you like to walk. -It was way cheaper than other hotels. I was originally planning to stay elsewhere but it dropped to 109 a night in the winter whereas others were barely under 250. Cons: -Like others mentioned about the elevators, its a lot of floors for a few elevators, it wasn't packed until my last day there and the rooftop bar closed early and there was still a lot of waiting around for a packed elevator. -No executive lounge for those that care Some of the other reviews mentioned issues with the rooms or staff, I had no problems with either. Its hard to pick a favorite New York hotel since I've had good experiences with quite a few over the years. I'll certainly add this hotel to my list of good experiences and will probably be back.

“soulless convention hotel, but great views” typical Hyatt Regency property; standard room was good size, but with slightly unusual set-up in that the vanity unit/sink is in the main bedroom, behind a divider. The toilet and shower are in a separate, very small bathroom. There are a restaurant, a bar, and a coffee shop, all of which have the charme of those you find at airport concourses. Upsides: if you have business at the McCormick Place, this hotel is the obvious place to be as it is virtually a part of the convention centre. If you do get a North-facing room on the upper floors, the views of the Chicago skyline are fantastic. The staff were super-friendly.

“great stay. again.” Another great stay here for a business trip. the hotel staff is friendly, the rooms are spacious, and I LOVE that you get a balcony! great viw this time too.. Excellent. The gym is nice. Breakfast is fine. This hotel is really a great place to stay for being in walking distance of everything and is a great choice for business travel.

“An amazing inn in an amazing location” I only live about 20 minutes from this resort, but my girlfriend and I wanted somewhere to stay for Valentine's day. I found an amazing deal on Hotwire.com, ($149 including taxes), so that was part of the reason I picked it. From the moment we drove in, to the moment we left we were very impressed. The entire resort was beautifully decorated, the rooms were clean and very nice. We dined there for Valentine's day, and I was truly impressed by the food at the Veranda restuarant (both for dinner that evening and breakfast the next morning). I would recommend this hotel to everyone!!!

“Fantastic boutique hotel” A marvelous hotel in every way except location. The lobby has a distinct character that mixes ultra-hip with classic old fashioned charm - featuring a cross between an alpine ski lodge and an ivy league library. Terrific value for the amenities. Only drawback is its location down in the Financial District... but it's really just a short subway ride away from the rest of the city.

“perfect” This is a fantastic hotel - the location is perfect, the staff pretty friendly/professional, rooms are clean, large, comfortable. Breakfast was good - plenty of food and variety - plenty of room to sit down and eat that fantastic breakfast too. Location - also perfect. Valet is pretty steep - but that's pretty typical of the hotels to take advantage of customers to rip them off for parking. You can't go wrong here -- book your room.

“Nice Stay at the W” I stayed at the W Union Square for one night during an extended vacation in New York City. This hotel is in a great location for those who are familiar with the city (especially the subway lines) as it is convenient to the Union Square subway station, but not much else. While Union Square is a nice part of town, those who are interested in doing those touristy things like visiting the Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center, Times Square, Central Park and the other sites of midtown may find it a bit out of the way. The rooms are huge (by New York standards anyway) and very well equipped as can be expected at W hotels. The check-in staff was friendly enough but the girl who checked me in was not remotely interested in going above and beyond the call of duty in any way. Her attitude wasn't negative, but definitely more expected from an economy brand hotel than an upscale hotel like the W. Overall, great stay. The beds are fantastic and they provided a roll-a-way bed free of charge as a one-time courtesy. I'm not sure how much they charge other guests for this.

“Better than last time...” We had two rooms at the Amerisuites Airport this last weekend for a wedding. I have stayed here before and was not that impressed, however this time was different. The hotel is in the process of becoming a Hyatt and I can tell the difference. The staff was cordial, the rooms clean and fresh smelling, the breakfast ok. Drawbacks were the noisy room location (next to the elevators) and the light in the back parking lot went out. This hotel has a reputation of car theft so I was more than a little concerned. The front desk person said it would be fixed in the next few days. That was not reassuring to me. Overall this is a fine location and a acceptable hotel.

“A good convention hotel” The Hyatt is part of the convention centre and a good choice if you are visiting an exhibition. It's a 10 minute taxi ride to the centre of Chicago or 20 minutes with the bus that stops just in front of the hotel. The building is impressive, modern and welcoming. If you have a room on the higher floors you can enjoy great city and lake views. Staff is welcoming, polite, efficient and ready to accommodate any needs you may have. The rooms are typical of a chain hotel, nothing special but nothing missing. The doors do have an inch gap on the side and the bottom, so the noise from other doors opening and closing is disturbing. Breakfast buffet is very nice with a large choice of food but at $20 it does not come cheap. This can also be said from the Wi-fi charge of $10 a day. The Hyatt does have a very well equiped gym with the latest equipment. It is very busy when the hotel is full but outside rush hour offers a great opportunity to exercise. Overall a good choice if you need to visit the McCormick centre but there are better options if visiting down town Chicago.

“would recommend for parties” stayed here as part of a wedding event. the social rooms downstairs are awesome, and the rooms are decently sized. i like the dark fabrics, but the brown carpet color is just...off. you know it's there to hide stains. decor aside, they had three elevators and none appeared to work properly. we had at least a five min wait each time. they did a nice catering service for the wedding post-party and post-wedding brunch. our catered lunch (sandwiches and chips) was overpriced and just blah. the artwork is provacative, to say the least, so Bible-thumpers might not be so comfy here. kudos for the boldness! good location, close to medical center and rice university.

“Loved our stay at the Sheraton Chicago” We stayed at the Sheraton Chicago Towers for 3 nights over Easter weekend. Our room was terrific -- beautiful and very comfortable beds! The pool is complimentary although it costs $12 to use the exercise equipment. Previous posters are correct that everything seems to cost extra but it is well marked; there were no surprises! Even though the weather was really cold, most sights (Art Museum, Michigan Ave shopping, Symphony Center) we wanted to see were within walking distance. There were many, many restaurant choices in the area as well. The rather surly receptionist (the only downpoint of the whole stay) told us that there was only valet parking. When I mentioned that I had called and was told there was self-parking, she admitted there was but to see the bell hop (who said it was full -- which it wasn't). I would definitely stay here again -- especially for the rate slightly over $100/night rate we got on the Sheraton website.

“Good place to stay in Back Bay” Overall a nice place. The rooms are new with new furniture. The bathrooms are spacious. We asked for a room with two beds and a view and got both. The best part is the location. It's connected to the Prudential so when we were hungry we just walked to one of the tons of nearby restaurants. There's a Starbuck's close to the lobby. There's also free internet in the lobby. There's lots of shopping there if you're interested. You can also walk to Newbury Street too. And the Boston Public Gardens aren't too far. It's also close to several T stations which we used a few times. The staff was very nice in helping us find our way around. We saw some guests with dogs in the lobby (a big plus for me since I occasionally travel with my pets). The con was the $42 charge for parking. I think that's everywhere in Boston though. Would definitely stay there again if we got a good rate as we did on Priceline.

“Bathroom design very poor” Great location. Very busy hotel. I had a modernized room but I think the architect had never stayed in a hotel before. The bathroom was disappointing. The hand basin was hidden by a very wide ledge above it. The taps were actually under the ledge and the lever to lower the plug was almost impossible to find. Half the basin was hidden by the protruding ledge and the whole counter top was set 3 inches too low. It was a long way to bend down. My room had motion detector lighting. Very avant garde but if I sat at the desk for 20 minutes working on my computer, the lighting seemed to think the room was empty and closed down. Stand up, walk around and the lighting came on again. Over my 5 day stay, my electronic room key failed three times. Each time the staff were very apologetic but what a pain. And finally, on my last day the steam heating used by the hotel which comes from Grand Central Station was shut down for maintenance from 10pm until 6am so there was no hot water in my room. I was given 12 hours notice of this inconvenience but it was still inconvenient! I used the Executive Lounge on the 16th floor. Nice location. Adequate continental breakfast. Nice staff. My bill had a duplicate charge on it which was reversed without question - but it should not happen

“Working at Javits? Easy Access to Convention Center.” This hotel could be your GEM. This small hotel (39 rooms) is a skip from the Javits Center. This summer room rates in NYC are through the roof. The GEM provided a reasonably priced alternative to the larger westside hotels. Rooms are small ... but honestly, no smaller than many other hipster hotels. The design is clean, contemporary and attractive. Coffee maker in the room. No restaurant in this hotel. All in one shampoo/conditioner and body wash are dispensed from canisters inside the shower. Other toiletries are fine - not too smelly :) Robes in closet if you choose to use them. Hairdryer and Iron also in room. Hotel staff very nice & helpful.

“Not worth the trouble” The San Diego Old Town Courtyard is a great location for restaurants and bars, but the hotel itself is not so traveler-friendly. The parking is very difficult, the elevator is slower than slow and the rooms are just average.

“An adequate hotel with pros and cons” This hotel has some positives and negatives. First, the positives: it is clean, and its rooms are spacious. It's well located, with several chain restaurants, such as Cheesecake Factory and PF Changs, within walking distance, as well as a pleasant outdoor mall. There is also free parking, as well as valet parking (for a charge.) I would stay there again, if I had to. However, there were some negative things that, when put together, would make me look into other hotels in Austin before returning to this one. For one thing--and it's pretty major--the walls between rooms are PAPER THIN. I was able to follow an entire conversation between people in the room next to me, even with my TV on! CRAZY! Also, I ordered room service (which was tasty), but only realized after they left that they did not give me silverware! When I called, it took them over 15 minutes to bring some--insane! And then I realized that they had forgotten some of my food as well! That is ridiculous. Also, the bed has a serious problem--the frame was too small. Although the King bed in my room was very comfortable, the frame it was sitting upon was too small. This meant that, if I sat on the foot of the bed, the entire bed tipped and I began to fall off! If I was not able bodied or a child or elderly person, a serious accident could have happened! Another issue is that the overall design of the hotel has some small, but annoying flaws. For example, there is only one bank of elevators, and the traffic flow is such that there is ALWAYS an annoying crowd to wade through to get to them in the lobby. In short, this is a hotel that is passable, but not nearly as nice as the Marriott chain that runs it normally is. I do love the setting--a grove of trees--and the valley view is nice. However, if you're annoyed by small things that seem large when put together, look elsewhere.

“Very nice” This is a great hotel with optimal views of the water. I was quiet surprised to find out just how close we were to the water - but it literally sits next to it. So, it makes for perfect views. Quiet rooms, very comfy beds. It's within walking distance to prime restaurants. I would stay here again.

“In this price range, there are better places in San Diego” We stayed here two nights as part of a group holding a meeting. The room was pretty good. It was odd that the only chair was a desk chair that was not particularly comfortable for watching tv. For tv, it was mandatory to be on the bed. There was a connecting door to the next unit which, fortunately, was a suite. The second night we could hear people talking but they were not near the door. Of course, this meant they could hear us, too. Both the bathroom and the main room had light switches that were timed to turn the lights off after a set amount of time if there was no movement in the room. The first morning my wife was in the shower when the bathroom light went out. Startled, she yelled for help, thinking there was a power failure or worse. Good thing I hadn't gone for a morning walk. I opened the bathroom door and the light went back on. The hotel has a nice-looking pool area and lobby. Garage parking was included. The restaurant served a nice breakfast. It's the kind of hotel that makes you want to like it, but I am afraid, given other choices, we will not be back.

“Pretty Good for a Large Impersonal Hotel” I am not a fan of big chain hotels but this Hyatt has many nice qualities. First, the bed. It is wonderful with high thread count linens and great pillows. The rooms have all been redone and are very modern with nice flat screen tvs. The bathroom is tiny (at least ours was) and not particularly nice. The food is absolutely amazing and they have a marketplace with everything you could want at reasonable prices. Check in and check out were a breeze. And of course the location is amazing-right on top of Grand Central with many shops and great places to eat! If you don't mind staying in a big business hotel, I would highly recommend this Hyatt.

“Patina Downtown” - eindrucksvolles Hotel downtown - an der einen oder anderen Stelle sieht man, dass dies eines der ältesten Hotels Stadt ist, dass auch schon einige Erdbeben überlebt hat - die Zimmer könnten eine Renovierung gebrauchen - Internetzugang muss bezahlt werden, es sei denn, man hat ein Conference-Package oder ähnliches - sehr schöner Fitness-Bereich und Pool - freundlicher und zuvorkommender Service - absolut überteuertes Valet-Parking (50 Dollar) - sehr teueres Frühstück, aber warum gibt es Starbucks

“Investment needed” Stayed here last month for 4 nights. Sadly, seems that Hyatt have no intertest in maintaining what was once a very well presented hotel. Club rooms are spartan, which is just about acceptable, and poorly cleaned, which is not. Maintenance does not figure high on their priority list.

“Zentral gelegen” Das Westin St. Francis am Union Square ist mitten im Herzen von San Francisco gelegen. Im Hotel sollte man zwischen dem älteren Hauptgebäude und dem sehr modernen Tower unterscheiden. Im Tower sind die größeren und neueren Zimmer, welche absolut zu empfehlen sind! Ebenfalls hat man von hier aus einen tollen Blick über die Stadt und die Bucht von San Francisco. Das Hotel an sich ist sehr alt aber top gepflegt. 100% zu empfehlen.

“Very nice place” I was in town to do some work at Intel and decided to stay at the Holiday Inn Express since they had a good Intel rate and because I would get Priority Club points. The hotel had been undergoing some renovations with more planned in the near future. The exterior of the hotel looked good and my room was large and clean. The wired Internet worked great and the bathroom was nice and clean. Breakfast was not spectacular, but good and even had a few hot items. The exercise room had several aerobic machines (including 2 treadmills) and all appeared to be working order. I did not make use of the pool and jacuzzi, but they looked very inviting. The staff was friendly and helpful. Several restaurants were within a 5-10 minute drive and there was a Cracker Barrel just down the driveway from the hotel. I would stay again if I return to Chandler.
“Muy buena ubicación, muy buena atención.” Muy lindo hotel, bien restaurado, cómodo, bien ubicado, con atención amable. Salones de época, muy lindos.

“Wonderful staff, great location” I stayed at the Riverwalk Plaza Hotel and Suites after my business stay at the Marriott. After the horrible customer service at the Marriott, I was pleasantly surprised at how nice the staff was here. They were very willing to help. The hotel is newly renovated - there's definitely some interesting art to look at. My room overlooked a well-kept pool and courtyard - great place to relax. Also, the location of the hotel was great for all the touristy things I wanted to do. The restaurant downstairs was also great. Fast and attentive service, not to mention good and affordable food. Parking is $12 a day, which is a steal compared to almost $30 at the Marriott. I noticed some reviews complained about the parking lot but $12 a day to not have your car sit in the hot Texan sun, I have nothing to complain.

“good location with small, trendy rooms” Rooms are average to small with some very oddly designed lighting (note to push the on button on the side near the base, but not on the base). As characteristic with some of the other W hotels (Times Square, for example), the lobby is on an upper floor, so that helps getting and out of the hotel (not having to worry about the traffic on the ground level). Note that the hotel is directly facing the Ground Zero construction and visitor sites, so it can be a little messy, crowded and noisy. That said, the hotel is nice and clean with good amenities. I wouldn't recommend the hotel for families, but then that isn't traditionally the market for the W hotel chain.

“Great Stay” A very good choice for my purposes. Good service, standard "suite" set-up with wet bar, microwave, refrigerator and dining area. Bedroom windows looked out on Military Road; living room windows looked out into the Chevy Chase Pavillion. Full breakfast served in a restaurant overlooking the pavilllion's atrium. Self-serve, but they will cook an omelet to order. I didn't take advantage of the free drink in the evening--I think it was in the same place. Nice fitness center on the penthouse with pool, whirlpool, steam room, sauna, locker room (bring your own lock) and fitness equipment. I was impressed with the amount of body space. Although I traveled by myself, I see why other people think it is family-friendly. The space makes is good for people without families in tow to get some peace. Once I got over the initial minor shock that this hotel is really located in an upscale mall, I loved the advantages. Food court, nice shopping, even a Georgette Klinger salon for spa treatments right there. The Friendship Heights station of the Metro is also right there--in the building (good on very hot DC days). If you drive, make sure you understand that this place is located in the middle of a very busy high-end shopping district (Neiman Marcus is across the street). There was no doorman that I could see, so I went into the parking garage immediately next door. It is a tiny, cramped, winding facility, but don't panic. Keep going into the bowels of it where it gets less crowded and make sure you park near the well-marked "Hotel Elevator" which will take you right into the lobby. I got a good rate of $149.00 and thought it was well worth it. I have already recommended it to family and friends and will return myself.

“Comfortable, convenient” While the rooms are a bit tired and could use a renovation, the Hyatt Regency is a decent place to stay. The staff are friendly and the rooms are spacious. The bathroom is definitely not 4 star, but it’s clean. My husband liked the gym very much. The bar in the lobby gets very lively and serves good, albeit pricey wine. The location is fantastic. Right on the river just a few steps down from Michigan Avenue, it’s just a five minute walk to Millennium Mile across the river, or the Loop. Booked through Hotwire we got a killer deal, and would stay here again if we got a good deal. I would not be willing to pay 4 star rates though, unless the rooms were refurbished and the bathroom completely renovated. That said, we enjoyed our stay in Chicago, and slept well.
“Another Great HGI” I thoroughly enjoyed my stay, particularly the upgrade to a suite with a spa. This is a new property, close to all kinds of restaurants and shopping. Great staff.

“Lower your expectations, and you'll like this hotel.” I agree with those who say the hotel is a disappointment. Certainly NOTHiNG like the standard of the London Intercontinental. My mistake was expecting it to be at that level of service and hospitality. The room was a good size and the bed was very comfortable. But the armchairs looked as if they'd been purchased in a garage sale. I thought the pattern color was green and tan..then realized the tan (which was more like brown on the arms and seat of the chair) was actually a silvery white in less used areas of the chairs!! When was the last time the upholstery was cleaned...if ever? This was in contrast to the admirable cleanliness of the lobby, where i saw a supervisor run her finger along a ledge and then check her finger for dust! The lobby is old and beautiful, but dark and busy (not nearly as impressive as the lobby of the Roosevelt, where i stayed earlier on this trip). The Barclay's ambiance lacked a "welcoming" feel, despite staff who were courteous on the surface. For ex, one young lady at the Business Center in the evening was warm, friendly and gracious-- an example of the difference of making the guest feel welcome, vs f mechanical politeness. I got a good room rate, but even with it, i doubt I'd stay again. There is a 24 hour Fed Ex nearby if you need to use the internet without paying a small fortune. Hotel's ;ocation is ok, quite near the Waldorf Astoria. I love Midtown East, but prefer to be a bit closer to Madison or 5th ave.

“Great location, needs a good cleaning!” This was the worst Courtyard property that I've experienced (I've stayed at quite a few). I was there for 2 weeks and in that time period my room was services only twice, and when it was, the sheets were never changed, room wasnt dusted, the floor never vacuummed. As a matter of fact, a few days into my stay I found someone else's makeup right under the bed. I made a few phone calls to the front desk, to no avail. It was skipped at least 4 times while I was there. However, the front desk people were always very courteous, and management did leave a small gift bag for my troubles. But would I stay here again? No.

“So-so” We stayed at the Marriott Canyon Villas for a week as part of a group of several families with young children. Our experience was mixed. Pros: - Very spacious, attractive, well-appointed suites at reasonable rates. We were able to host a dinner for 8 adults and 6 kids in our suite by using all of the tables and chairs provided. - For kids, there is a small playground, a shallow splash pool, and a large 3.5-foot-deep pool at the resort. - Access to the JW Marriott next door (long walk or short drive) with its "lazy river" pool, Roy's restaurant, and very attractive grounds. - Big shopping center across the street has a supermarket, Target, and many other shops and restaurants. - Half an hour drive away from downtown Phoenix and the airport, museums, zoo, Desert Botanical Garden, etc. Cons: - The buildings are very densely packed on the property. The 3300 building, where we stayed, is very close to a busy four-lane road. Most of the time we couldn't hear the noise inside our suite, but when we stepped outside it was very noticeable. As I walked from one building to another or to the pools, I was very aware of the housing development just a few dozen yards away, and of the fairly massive resort buildings packed fairly close together. The net result for me was that it was missing that "away from it all" feeling that I typically get in a high-end resort. - I could not get the climate control to work correctly. I like to keep the fan on to keep the air circulating. In both of our rooms, if the fan was on, so was the AC, and the room kept getting colder. In other words, there was no way to run the fan without also cooling the room. Eventually it would get too cold (much colder than the thermostat was set for, and the only solution was to switch the unit off. - There were bright spots (engineering was super prompt and helpful when we had some minor issues with the rooms), but overall service was mediocre. As one example, two days in a row the supply of towels at the main pool ran out. I can see this happening once, but twice in a row indicates someone's not trained or not doing their job. - The playground and splash pool are far from the main pool. So if you have toddlers on the playground or in the splash pool, and other kids or adults in the main pool, the groups are not going to be interacting.

“Way too noisy/pricey” First, the staff was excellent. Great customer service. That said, I'll likely be staying at a different hotel for my next stay. Rooms were small but clean. A handwritten letter under the door was a nice touch for my welcome. We were on the 10th floor and even that high, the street noise was too loud to sleep well. Breakfast was included in our room for one person and we paid for one person. It was a typical hotel breakfast, nothing fancy and for the price, I'd recommend elsewhere. Valet was $40 a night. So although the staff was nice and the rooms clean, the price point ($400), the extras and the noise level will lead me to change my next few reservations to a different hotel.

“Reasonably priced alternative in Manhattan” Hampton Inns generally provide a good value, wherever they are located, but this Hampton offers a reasonably-priced room, in a very expensive city. Like all Hampton Inns, the services are limited, and the rooms are simple, but the staff are very friendly, and the rooms are clean, as are the common areas of the hotel. The location is also very good, as it is easily walkable to Times Square and Broadway (10 - 15 minutes). All-in-all, if you simply need a place to stay while you explore the city, and you don't plan to spend a lot of time in the hotel (so you don't need all the amenities of a full-service hotel), this may be your best option, and it is priced right.

“Kleine Oase am Riverwalk” Das Hotel liegt direkt am Riverwalk. Ich war zu einer Konferenz in San Antonio und das Convention Center kann in 10min zu Fuß erreicht werden. Das Hotel selbst ist schön im lokalen Stil. Am Freitag spielt eine Mexikanische Band Life am Pool. Der Pool ist klein aber sehr ruhig und angenehm. Das Fitnesscenter, welches im Schwesterhotel gegenüber liegt ist vom Feinsten! Die Concierges sind super für Restaurantbuchungen etc.

“Maybe I'm just too old” Staying in this hotel was a lot of work. From the schlep to the parking garage to the heavy elevator door. The "real" key opens the room door, the key card opens front door, and the parking card-- that's three things to keep up with. My room was cute and funky, but uncomfortable. I left tired.

“Good location, adequate hotel” Location: The location is great. It’s nestled along the Riverwalk and about a 1⁄2 mile from the main tourist area. There is ample free parking and the hotel will provide you with a hanging tag to ensure that you are a guest. The only strange occurrence is that Google maps, as well as my GPS, had me take two streets which could only be described as narrow alley ways to get there. I literally had to cut through the parking lot of a neighboring hotel. It’s about a 15 -20 minute walk to The Alamo. The neighborhood seems somewhat sketchy at night, but safe. Staff: The staff was very friendly and upgraded me to a river view room as a Platinum member. I was given a token when I first arrived for a free drink. I chose a Diet Pepsi and after one swig regretted the decision. It was 10 days past expiration and had a metallic taste...in a plastic bottle. The greeter apologized profusely and offered me another selection. Not a huge deal, but that attention to detail steered me away from the grab and go sandwiches and breakfast the next morning. First impressions. Hotel: What can I say? Park Hyatt is a cookie cutter model so you know what you’re getting when you stay here. The rooms are large and spacious. I had a King room but the bed is more of a Queen size. The “view” is nothing more than a walking trail, a dirty canal and trees. On the street view, you can see the lights change on the Tower of Americas. I don’t know where Hyatt is purchasing their mini fridges from, but they need a new vendor. Every time I want to keep something cool, it’s barely above room temperature. On the flip side, the shower takes several minutes to heat up and offers little pressure. I was in there for a good 7 minutes with the hot water turned on max before I started to get scalded. The TV is large as always and they offer a complimentary HBO pack. I would have liked a few more HD channels. I’m not a fan of the adjoining room concept as a solo traveler, which my room had. My neighbors mistook their door on several occasions. Free Wi-fi in the room. Value: My rate was $116.00. I consider this fair with all things considered. Would I stay here again? Probably. I’m a huge fan of the Hyatt brand. However, I’ll most likely check out a competing property for my next stay. It served its purpose but there was nothing that wowed me.

“New Favorite New York Hotel” This is a really nice hotel - rooms are modern and large (huge by NYC standards) and very well designed. I have stayed in dozens of New York hotels and this is definitely going to be my default hotel going forward. Very good value. Some people traveling for fun might be put off by the location, but good subway access a few blocks away and a Whole Foods around the corner.

“Suite location” Although the room is a little dated, having the kitchenette was nice for our family of 4, and the hotel location couldn't be better. The parking and internet access are included which is a plus. The hotel also has a pool and laundry room. We only stayed 2 nites ($79/nite for jr. suite), but if were staying longer would get a full suite (with full kitchen and microwave). We missed not having a microwave in the kitchenette. It is a good value for a suite in a sweet location and would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Okay, but only okay” I really liked that there was a dressing room with a dressing table and lamps and the room was quite large, but the rooms just felt dirty. I know the building is an older building, but I think the walls need a good scrubbing or to be painted, more/better lighting would also help as it was hard to get any work done (I was traveling for work) with such dim lights. Also, the hotel needs wi-fi. Wired internet was available, but wi-fi would be a major improvement. Lastly, the elevators are up about 6 stairs, which seems inappropriate for today's accessibility standards, but more over it's just awkward to lug suitcases up and down those stairs. I would not

“conference rooms were hot the entire weekend we stayed here.” I Travel and work in lots of hotels and resorts. Check in was fast, hotel beautiful and staff (front desk) were awesome especially catherine and chris (concierge). We worked in the conference rooms and each day someone would have to come in and fix the air conditioner and they always took their time. But they were sweethearts so that made up for it. The rooms were dark, there were smokers in the room across from us (no smoking policy in rooms) they moved our entire two room group opposed to moving them (smoke allergy employee on board) and lastly rooms were extremely dark even with all the lights on. The customer service makes up for all of this though.

“Capitol Hill” I have stayed at this hotel before and it is most noteworthy for its location which is about 3 blocks from the Capitol. The amenities are good, if not great, but considering its proximity to Capitol Hill, it is a good value and a comfortable place to stay. The service is very good and friendly. One thing that irritated me, however, was the internet service. It was $18.98 for two days even for those of us at the Hyatt Gold Passport level. In this day and age when internet service is usually offered at no charge especially to loyalty club members as they do at Hilton, Omni, etc., that would only be a minor irritant but the internet service itself was only slightly faster than dial-up. Hyatt offers and upgraded internet service for more (I think it was $16.95 per day) which I needed to get just to get my work done. It was faster but certainly no faster than the free internet at other hotels. When a business nickel and dimes you (like many airlines do), they should at least offer something good for the money.

“Another great Kimpton property” Was in Denver for one night on business. I stay in Kimpton hotels when I travel to Seattle and San Francisco for business. This was my first stay at the Monaco in Denver and it was great. Typical Kimpton- warm reception, great room with large work space and comfortable bed. Disappointed I did not have a chance to try the restaurant, room service was top notch.

“Return visit” We stayed here in April, and when returning to California decided to spend a couple of nights back here. Again, couldn't fault the hotel in any way. I think what they get so right is that the staff on reception are all so friendly without overdoing it. I enquiried about the make of the body lotion, and on returning to my room discovered five extra bottles of it - nice touch. The rooms are fine and the beds are very comfortable. As always mentioned, the location can't be beaten. After staying here we went to Yosemite, but decided to return to the Chancellor for another night before setting off down the coast - back into the same room (three times in this room - may ask for a different one for a change if we ever go back). It really is a great hotel, but most of all the staff make it what it is. Oh yes, and the cookies are great, especially the cranberry ones!

“Good Hotel” My wife and I have just spent 4 days at the Doubletree Hilton in San Jose. The hotel itself is very nice and easy to find being just off the 101. It’s about a 30min drive from SFO. We were met by friendly staff at the reception area and check in was quick and hassle free. We were in an Executive King room on the 8th floor. The room whilst dated, was large and spacious with a small balcony overlooking the pool area. We had a large king size bed which was soft and comfy. Together with a good selection of pillows and black out curtains, made for a good night sleep. We had a 32in LCD TV with a good selection of channels. The room could do with a few more ceiling and/or wall lights. The lighting at night was adequate. There was no fridge in the room but, I’m guessing one can be ordered if needed. There is a vending machine and ice machine on each floor. The bathroom was a decent size and clean. The shower was over the bath which was fine with us. One good thing was having an extra basin and vanity outside the bathroom. There is a good size gym on the 2nd floor with a good selection of Precor cardio and weight machines and free weights. There is also a heated pool and spa pool on the ground floor. We used these facilities each day. There is also a guest laundry by the pool area, which was useful. We didn’t use the restaurant but, did have breakfast at the Sprigs Café each morning. There is a good selection of hot and cold food. We found the staff to be friendly and helpful. To our surprise breakfast and internet was part of the package, something we weren't aware of or expecting at the time of checking in. I'm not sure what the breakfast costs are but, internet is $12.95 per night. We had a car and parking was $18 per day. We’ve stayed at a number of hotels when visiting the US and this seems to be the standard price so whilst an inconvenient extra cost it didn’t bother us too much. We had access to the Club Level Lounge on the 10th floor which, we used once during our stay. We found this to be a slight let down compared with other lounges we've visited. Overall we really enjoyed our stay at the Doubletree and would happily recommend it to others and stay here again.

“Fantastic location for weekend of shopping with the girls!” We chose the central location of the Double Tree because we were shopping all around the Columbus area. We booked a 2 double bed, 2 room suite with a sofabed. This room was bigger than my first apartment! We had MORE than enough room! The only added benefit to rooms this size, would be to have 2 bathrooms as well! Regardless, the warm cookies at chek-in were delicious and the housekeeping service was prompt and friendly! (Girls can never have enough pillows!). Garage location is a bit tricky, but it's nice to have your car parked close by and easily accessible. Layout of the hotel is a bit odd; it reminded me of how New York hotels are laid out--long, skinny hallways. But our room was at the end, corner and it couldn't have been a better experience!

“Great New Spot in Dallas” The recent renovations at the Stoneleigh put it on par with just about any other top hotel in Dallas. In addition the staff does a very nice job of welcoming guests. I had one of the studio suite rooms. It's one large room divided by a large wooden double sided dresser with a flat panel TV on top. The bed is located on one side and a sofa and chair are on the other. You can adjust the TV to view it on either side. The bathroom is one of the nicest I've seen in Dallas. The marble floor and tile walls had a very clean look. The soaps and shampoos were top-tier. In addition, there were plenty of towels and they were very soft and clean smelling. The bed was very comfortable. It was turned down in the evening when I returned to my room, along with a robe and chocolates left out for me. There was also an ample closet, with an ironing board, starch, etc. The air conditioner in my room was a bit finicky at first, but seemed fine after a while. The hotel also offers your choice of papers in the morning - the WSJ, NYT or DMN. (I suspect they'd find a Star-Telegram for you too, if you asked). The hotel is easy to get to from Love Field, though your only real choice is valet parking. The hotel has a small but active bar in the lobby. In addition, it's fairly close to most of the downtown restaurants, etc. If you're looking to mix things up a bit in your trips to Dallas, this is a great new place to stay downtown.

“BEST HILTON I HAVE EVER STAYED AT...” This is a great hotel. You can’t beat the location, but it is the rooms and amenities that are the real star. The rooms are modern, comfortable and well appointed. They really have a high end feel. Also if you get a high enough room, you will have a great view. The staff was extremely accommodating and the hotel has a lot to offer (multiple restaurants, a large store onsite, shuttle to Universal, great pool, etc.). I really have no idea how some other recent reviews questioned the accommodations. I found them first rate. This is by far the best Hilton I have ever stayed at. Don’t hesitate to book here.

“I really want to write a great review...BUT!!!!!” From the outside this is one impressive hotel. It is rather dominant of the skyline, its HUGE and the lobby is very grand and spotless. I also found MOST of the staff to be very pleasant! However that is where it all seemed to end. I think in a hotel as large as this the devil is in the detail and attention to detail was certainly lacking. The room I had on the 14th floor of the newer tower was very large and spacious. I had a lovely view of the pool area and the other tower as well as Coronado island. It was also bright. The beds were ok although I have had more comfortable at the likes of Hilton, Marriott, Westin, Sheraton etc. The large flat screen TV was brilliant and an empty fridge for my own use was also appreciated. However little things proved irksome such as the noisy AC unit which had to remain on during my visit due to the heatwave and high humidity outside. Also there was a master switch at the entrance to the room. This switch controlled a light above the hallway area of the room which meant you had to switch off the masterswitch if you wanted this light out to sleep at night. However when you switched it off it also cut power to a number of sockets throughout the room. I did not realise this at the time and so when I woke up I realise that niether my phone, ipad or laptop all of which I needed excessively during the day had not charged. I was pretty furious by this. Then there was the housekeeping staff. I was awoken at one stage by an annoying tapping on my front door. Half asleep I was going to just ignore it and hope it went away but no, it continued, it continued for almost 5 minutes until I just stumbled awake, threw on some clothes and ripped the door open to find the housekeeping lady asking if I wanted my room serviced. I politely said no but with a sense of disbelief on my face. Surely a single knock would suffice and when she enters her key she would realise the deadbolt is engaged and therefore there is someone in the room who does not want to be disturbed (BTW, my room had NO Do Not Disturb card available even though I did see them on other doors so again poor attention to detail). I was more amazed the next day when the exact same thing happened again but with a different lady!!!! Then there was the room service....well let me highlight this for you DONT ORDER!!!!! Just put on a nice shirt and go look for food outside the hotel! I rang for room service and was immediately placed on hold. OK, I thought, this is novel, I dont think in my 12 years of travelling 5 times a month I have ever been on hold for my room service order to be taken but I decided to just roll with it. However after 10 minutes of being on hold I began to think that maybe this was a technical glitch. I hung up and rang the front desk only to be told that room service was busy at this time of day (it was 9PM at night ! LOL) and she could put me back in the hold, so back I went....after 20 minutes (now a total of 30 minutes) I totally gave up. If thats how long it takes to take an order can you imagine how slow the delivery of the food must be let alone the mistakes that would probably be made to the order. I found this service to be APPALLING! I have stayed in larger hotels in the likes of Vegas and Dubai and I have never experienced this sort of product shortfall. Fortunately there are plenty of pleasant places to eat around the hotel so I made a point of eating outside of the hotel after this experience and spending my money elsewhere. Another issue I had was with the lifts. I waited almost 5 minutes several occassions for a lift. Each time this happened I then suffered the most excrutiating decent into madness as the lifts stopped at every floor on the way down. There must be something wrong with the programming of the lifts because this was most unusual! Then there was the lady at checkout. She practically accused me of not staying in the hotel because she couldnt find my reservation. She then started to get shirty with me as if I was wasting her time. Transpired when she was trying to find my reservation by room number she was hitting 4 instead of 5 on the keyboard and when she tried to find it by name she hit Y instead of T! I saw her do this 4 times and told her each time but she did the whole "I know what Im doing" thing! She was just rude, its one thing to make an error its another to acknowledge it and laugh about it a little, you dont go and shout at the customer...ever! I was totally appalled by her behaviour! However after the negatives Ill admit the breakfast in the hotel the first morning was lovely (I didnt eat in the hotel after my room service experience however so did not try the breakfast again but instead went to a lovely place just outside the hotel which was cheaper too) and the gym and pool facilities were fantastic. Not to mention the hotels general location right beside the marina making everything very accessible. I love San Diego and I acknowledge that there are a lot of good points to the hotel however I think next time I would prefer to try the Marriott next door until the attention to detail at the Grand Hyatt is brought back!

“Great Convention Hotel” This was my first time staying here and I would definitely recommend this property. Great location, nice and efficient staff, clean clean clean. I even lost a piece of jewerly and the maid found it and laid on the vanity for me! Wow you just don't see that much. Good TV channels, free wifi and a small, but fully equipped gym. There is a 24 hour Fitness across the street if you like a larger facility. The restaurant/bar is great and I really did not need to venture out unless I just wanted to. Stayed on the 11th floor and it was quiet. Very convenient to the convention center but does not get the blaring fire trucks in the middle of the night. If you have ever stayed by this convention center you know what I'm talking about!!

“Cool Place, not sure....” I spent five nights here and felt there were several lacking features. First of all they are understaffed. The bellman/check in guy was trying to do the best he could but it is ridiculous what he is required to do. No one to open the door for you as you drag your bags from the cab to the hotel... and most likely they drop you off around the corner since this place is so new. Rocky was awesome and worked really hard so no negativity to him just that he can't do it all! You have to hail a cab around the corner so this guy worked his butt off to get me a cab. He was the same one who checked me in and delivered my bags to my room. I tried not to notice the sweat dripping off my bags... (just kidding). When I spilled a glass of water all over my bed and asked Rocky for new bedding it was no surprise that I never got anything... least of their concerns. Finally it dawned on me to use the hairdryer... thank goodness they had one of those in the room so I could finally go to bed after waiting for new bedding for over an hour. I love the Lexington Lounge, it was so nice! This is what gives the hotel it's advantage. The people at the hotel lounge were always very friendly! And the lounge was such a fun place to hang out and have coffee/wine and cheese in. Housekeeping does a great job keeping the rooms clean but are very stingy and generous when it comes to the bath products. I used the same empty container of bath gel for days until I remembered to leave a note asking for more at which time I got 3 containers but only had one night left of my five night stay... (I tipped generously every day) Never stayed in a nice hotel and had this situation? Stinks to get into the shower and remember you need more looking around to see nothing...ugh! The bath products were really nice so it made it worse. Normally I would just use my own stuff. Housekeeping should always error on the extra side when you are paying upwards $300 a night! the bathroom was really nice and I loved the drawer under the sink to put my stuff in. The room had a small wardrobe which was way too small for my clothes, could have used more space but alas New York! I loved having the fridge, microwave and sink, very handy! plenty of room for my own stuff in the fridge and the dishwasher was really nice as well. The Iphone station was wonderful! The Premier King does not have pictures on the website and is the same rate or a little higher than the Lexington suite but once you get into it, it is not as nice, so be sure to book the Lexington as the option. I was very disappointed in my room. Of course they had no other options and no upgrades so don't count on that. The entire time I felt like I was in the wrong room as it was not what I expected based on the pictures of the Lexington and I had talked extensively to the reservation person in regards to picking the best option. I might stay there again still not sure... probably only if they got more employees and I saw the picture of the room I am signing up for. Room service was good, expensive but at least tasted good... $7 for a soft drink... hello! Anyways still appreciated having food brought to my room late at night when I am tired and hungry. Thank you! I had written the concierge up front requesting a room that was quiet and of course I was placed next to the service stairs. Another faux pas. All in all I would hesitantly recommend but just know that you don't get a lot of service upon entering and make sure you have the room you want up front. Cheers to Rocky! I got to go home... he is still hailing cabs, carrying bags and checking people in! What a trooper!

“The nicest Westin I've stayed in” I can't believe the negative reviews I'm reading here. I don't travel often, but when I do, I usually stay at Westin hotels, and the Tabor Center is the nicest one I've stayed in. The lobby is beautiful, and the desk clerks were extremely helpful, friendly and sociable. We asked one if he had heard of a certain restaurant, and he immediately pulled out a downtown map and showed us how to get there. The woman who booked our room gave us the choice of a regular or corner room; we chose the corner. The next morning, the same woman asked us if we enjoyed the corner room! Great service! The room was small, but what do you expect for any downtown hotel? The bathroom was perfunctory, but the Heavenly Bed was perfect as usual (the No. 1 reason to stay at Westin). The location is great for walking down the 16th Street Mall, or for Rockies games. Lots of restaurants within walking distance, including several in mall connected to the hotel building (plus Starbucks in the lobby). The pool is amazing - half indoors, half outdoors, and located on an upper floor with an incredible view of downtown, the Six Flags amusement park, the football field, and a grand clock tower looming over the pool. Hot tub, too. I have no unkind words to say about this hotel, and it'll be my first choice if I ever find myself in Denver again.

“Wonderful!” This hotel is fantastic. Enjoyed my 5 night stay and will definitely stay again when i am back in California for business. I stayed in room 1851. The view from the room was very nice. Service was excellent. I had a problem with my internet connection, they sent up a technician and fixed it immediately. I am a hilton platinum member and in addition to the complimentary snack/beverage basket that was delivered to my room upon my arrival, i had access to the lounge on the top floor with all the complimentary foods/fruits and beverages during my entire stay. The lounge was very comfortable and the selection of food/beverages was nice. At dinner, Hilton tried to sell pictures they would take of you with your approval. If you declined, they were respectful and bid you a wonderful evening, but left you a souvenir of a keychain and a instant postcard that were made out of the photo taken. Only negative, the business center needs some work.

“In the middle of everything” Very nice hotel within walking distance of the whie house (one block from the treasury which is beside the white house), and walking distance of Ford's Theater. The hotel is very large and very well maintained but the rooms are pretty small for the price. Great restaurants nearby. They have a unique elevator system, where you type in your floor on the keypad and it tells you what elevator to take, it seemed efficent to me, but others at the conference were griping.

“Good Experience” I am a very frequent business traveller to Manhattan, but this was the first time I had stayed here. I was pleasantly surprised - the toom was fairly large, clean and the bathroom in excellent condition. Everything in the room worked. The bed was very comfortable and there was little or no noise (my room was on the 42nd floor). All in all, a minor miracle, considering where you are - one block from Times Square. And if you don't like the in-house food, there are millions of options within a mile radius. Service - I liked the "one touch service" - you call one number to get access to all services, rather than having to call room service, housekeeping, etc. separately. Some service gripes made me reduce my rating: my in-room dining cart and cutlery was not removed from room for an entire 24-hour period, although multiple housekeeping staff would have seen it. Secondly, as a business traveller I travel with two laptops, but I had to pay twice for Internet access, once for each computer. Central "service express" just told me to put my cart in the hallway and in relation to the Internet issue, said that that was "just the way it was". Really superior customer service would have apologized for rhe first issue and waived the extra Internet fee.

“Excellent value. Loudest AC Unit EVER.” Pros: Newly updated interiors, good service and location. Cons: Crazy loud AC unit. Seriously. Good thing I sleep like a rock. That could have just been my room, but I have no doubts if I wanted to change rooms the staff would be happy to do so.

“Just plain great!” 'Spent a couple of nights here for a girlfriend's getaway. 'Very nice hotel which is centrally located and the windows of the dining room overlook the San Antonio Riverwalk. My list: Large, fluffy towels - spacious bathroom - good water pressure Very large suite with a fully stocked kitchen (full size refrigerator with ice maker, microwave, etc.) Cold a/c and comfortable beds Very good hot breakfast every morning (eggs, bacon one morning; waffles, sausage the other morning) A free dinner is included but we did not partake (stuffed bell peppers one night) Free cocktail hour in the afternoon with beer and wine (we did partake of this) Excellent wifi (it is an AT&T hot spot) The hotel front desk people and cleaning staff were friendly, cheerful, helpful! That makes SUCH a different in a hotel stay! My one bit of disappointment: I know I can gripe about those high valet service parking fees until forever but its not going to change. ($23.00/night) But ... at such high rates I do expect exceptional service. 'Didn't get that here. The valet staff were just kind of mundane. I actually wondered at one point if the hotel had contracted out the service and if these people even worked for the hotel. No one offered to help with our bags on arrival. In three days of coming and going only once did someone open a door for us even though there was someone always there. When we left the last morning I called down for our car to be brought around. When we got downstairs about 15 minutes later the guy acted like he didn't even know we'd requested our car so we had to wait. We were halfway through loading out bags when he called out if we needed any help with our bags (uh...nope... too late now). After we'd already checked in the car we noticed that there is a parking garage across the street from the hotel. 'Might want to check this out for cheaper rates and just take care of your own car and bags.

“New favorite hotel in Dallas” Stayed here for three nights during spring break. Got room 2353, which was on the top floor with a great view of the Dallas skyline on Main Street (see the accompanying pictures). Make sure you join the Omni select program to get free wi-fi, morning juices and newspaper. Also do the online check in and your room keys will be ready to pick up and go. The room was spacious and quiet, beds were comfy and true queen size as described. We all slept well and made for a relaxing trip. Weather was cold and rainy the first night, so we were going to rent an in room movie. But they only have some Starz movie network rental deal and the selection was very limited. I think there was 4 or 5 family movies, and some of those movies we never even heard of. No new/recent movies like we're used to seeing at other hotels. Used the pool with the kids twice. The first time, it was early evening before sunset and there was a staff at the pool to pass out towels. Second time was after dinner, there was no staff at the pool and we didn't know where to get towels. Checked the gym, no pool towels. Had to go back down to the lobby to request towels. Pool area was nice with more great views of downtown. Water was heated warm enough to enjoy even on a cold windy day. Ate at onsite Texas Spice restaurant twice for breakfast and twice for dinner. Breakfast buffet was good but didn't have pancakes. Our waiter had some pancakes made for us and they were delicious. Dinner was ok, I would say it was just average. The flat bread pizza under appetizer was good. The main courses were ok ... nothing to write home about. We did not like the Texas molasses tart but did order the chocolate chip cookies and milk twice. We wanted to try Bob's Chophouse, another onsite restaurant, but they didn't have a kids menu. Service overall was very good and friendly. People make an effort to smile and greet you. Parking was $18 for self parking, just remember to keep one room key so you can exit the garage when you check out. We had a good time in Dallas and at this hotel. I recommend it and would stay here again.

“Bad beginning, but nice stay overall” Hotel Palomar in DC is in a perfect location for Dupont Circle. The rooms are large and clean. Our favorite aspect was the free wine hour which was packed with people and included red and white wines, sangria, olives, and crostini! This is such a nice perk of the hotel and definitely differentiates it from others. My big negative of the weekend was during check-in Friday night. I told the employee checking us in that I was a member of the loyalty program but did not have my number with me, and asked if he could look it up using my e-mail. He stated, "No, you can just enter it when you try to access the internet." I was annoyed at this but there was a long line and figured I would approach the issue later. We then accessed our room which was dark and dingy, and smelled like cigarettes. We soon found out that the room overlooked the employee smoking area and only had half of a window due to its location. I did book the stay through Jetsetter, but never expected the worst room in the hotel. I called to inquire about a different room, and was told it was no problem, and were moved to a much bigger, brighter room. Later that night, I approached the front desk regarding the loyalty member issue, as I was concerned I was not receiving points or the free mini-bar coupon that is included with all stays. The female employee was extremely helpful and apologized, and immediately entered my e-mail to register my loyalty member number. I was really blown away by the fact that the first employee would not take my e-mail address. I have stayed at Kimpton Hotels before, and I have always been treated kindly, and have been told of all the amenities on check-in and been asked specifically whether I am a loyalty member. I was disappointed that this did not occur during this stay. However, I will note that the same employee was working the following night and was extremely pleasant when I asked whether we could enjoy a bottle of wine in the lobby. This helped to make up a bit for the way we were treated on check-in. Despite the initial service, the stay was nice and enjoyable, and I would definitely go back.

“Great for Seattle, a little outside but just do it.” We had to stay in Seattle on business, the cost of downtown was so hight when I trawled through TripAdvisor I found and decided to stay at The Maxwell Hotel and I have to say we were not disappointed at all. The staff was extremely friendly and courteous and given we arrived late and the parking was full they helped us locate street parking. The room was a good distance away from the elevator but they were plenty big, very clean and the bathroom was big enough for two to stay in. The hotel is not in downtown but a short walk to Space Needle brought us on the Monorail to the main shopping district and a short walk further brought us to Pike Place which was just great. They supplied mid afternoon coffee and cake which was a welcome treat after the cold wet walk – the coffee was great. Overall the hotel was worth the risk, the location was great, plenty of restaurants within a short walk and as a previous reviewer stated the fresh creamer in the cooler was also welcoming.

“Great hotel” Everything about this hotel is great except for the size of the bed. We had a room with two double beds that fet more like twins. Definitely get a king room if you stay here. The location is perfect and much better than the W Hotel Times Square. But I wouldn't recommend the sushi bar there.it isn't that great.

“Nice hotel, clean and friendly” Booked this hotel from web site Otel.com. Hotel Nikko was rated a 4 star, and feel it was close, but rooms do need updating. Paid $150.00 a night, but booked this 7 months in advance. I checked rates just prior to leaving and they were going for $339 a night through the same Otel.com. Flew from Columbus Ohio non stop to Oakland. Taxi ride fare from Oakland to Nikko, (in financial district) was $52 with out tip. It was around $55 coming back. PUlled up to hotel and was greeted by bellhop, expressing hellos etcc.. Very nice appeal. You then go up an escalator to the next level to check in. It is a massive open lobby, with all marble ,whites, and massive area to read, sit, and people watch. Check in was a breeze and very polite, all Asian staff, and always smiles. Arrived at 3 pm, so this will probably be why check in was done so fast. Was offered a king, but not yet ready, or a ready queen. Took the queen as we needed to get a shower before we went out for dinner.The elevators are plenty. 6 to be exact, and waiting was never an issue. Our room was on the small side, having a bath/shower, all marble, but the pinkish tile and tub could have used some updating. Our room had a plasma, 2 safes, mini bar, coffee station, raio/cd player, phone in bath. The mini bar is triggeed to charge you by weight, so if you pick out a bottle of Coke, and put it back, you might as well drink it($4). Very well stocked. Used about $20 in room beverages. The bed was very soft, and made up very nicely. Many pillows etc... The air worked fine and heat was not needed. On the thermostat are 2 bottons. 1 for do not distrub, and 1 for making up the room. By pressing your choice, will make a small light turn on outside of your room to be seen by the maid service. Nice touch, and classy compared to paper door hangers. The shower/bath had plenty of hot and high pressured water. Ordered room service Sunday, and in (no kidding) 10 minutes the wife and I had scrabmled eggs, bacon, toast fruit and coffee. Stayed at Four Seasons in Maui in August, and their room service wasn't this fast. WOW! The hotel on Sundays has a quartet playing for the breasfast brunch. we did not partake, as we had to catch flight, but looked very classy. There is a high end sushi in the hotel, but never could find time to enjoy. Reservations highly suggested. There is a gift shop, and also a Starbucks inside the hotel. However when we went there twice the line was out the door....here is what I did, along with others that didn't want to wait. Directly across the street is a small coffee shop, and plenty of rolls , muffins. Like a small mom and pop coffee place. Only 5 people in line here, and all did the same as I, as we didn't want to wait 30 minutesin line at Starbucks. Other than that, valet always whistled for a cab and had no problems. Overall, this is a nice hotel...is it 4 stars???? Close but no cigar. It is a 3.8 one could say. I would for sure stay here again, but to me it is not a Ritz or Four seasons, but was well worth the cost.

“Comfortable” This was a great small hotel. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. The location is close to the Back Bay Amtrak station and easy to walk with a rolling suitcase. We were thrilled with our room. We were on the seveth floor and had a corner room with two windows and a perfect city view. (Must say that we had come from NYC with no view and a room we could barely walk around the bed.) The bed was very comfortable. Great shower. The decor was modern. The room was spotless clean. We liked that we could walk to Tremont Street at night and find lots of places to eat good food. Nice spots nearby for breakfast also. It was an easy walk to the Boston Common area. We also liked that it felt like we were in a neighborhood.

“Shabby, dirty hotel, firmly set in the 1960's” From the moment one walks into the shabby lobby and is greeted by the none-too-friendly Front Desk associates, the sense of impending doom is palpable. There are no surprises, just affirmation of those original thoughts when staying in a room. Clearly, this is the Radisson that both time and head office forgot. Threadbare sheets, graying/off white towels, blood stains on the bathroom floor. Orange 1960's carpeting with a biology labs worth of germs and stains on it. Thin walls, make it virtually impossible to sleep, in fact, it almost becomes stalking, when, it is apparent that every word can be heard from a conversation in the adjoining room. Bathroom is something out of the Smithsonian, and as other reviewers have commented upon, dirty. There is absolutely nothing to recommend this property. If you have to spend a night at an airport hotel, and the other options are sold out, the terminal would be a more preferable choice.

“Room to re-e-e-eally spread out!” If you have to stay in downtown SF, mecca of horrible chain stores and screaming street loonies, the Handlery is an oasis. There are two hotels in one; the motel-looking one with a gorgeous outdoor pool and patio, and the regular one. We had a 5th floor room for 3 and did not bump into each other once! Very pleasant staff, very clean, comfy beds, and very quiet. It's two blocks to Market St, cable cars, tons of restaurants, and a short ride to the Ferry Building and the Embarcadero.

“Excellent, hotel & location” The lobby is huge with plenty of places to sit and even a sushi bar. I had lunch at 13 which is right off the lobby and the crab cakes were wonderful. Hotel is huge and my room was on the 9th floor across the sky bridge And over convention center. Big room, big flat screen tv, updated and modern. Bath and body toiletries, single serve coffee makers, comfy bed and pillows... Not one thing I can complain about. There is a Starbucks off the lobby and a kinko/fed ex. I even had to receive and send a fax and they happily did so and for free! I went across the street to this gigantic food hall and Macy's for a little shopping. Maggianos is across street and plenty of places to shop and eat. Great location and service, can't wait to go back!

“Ouch -- My conscience hurts” I stayed here for a conference, meaning I didn't pay for it (that kind of money belongs in my kids' college account, not a hotel chain). Staff are delightful, from room service to housekeeping to front desk. Really great room: large, super comfortable bed, small but okay bathroom. THANK YOU for covering the unhygenic bedspread with a freshly laundered duvet cover. I wish every 4-star hotel was doing this by now (just stayed at Omni-CNN Atlanta, and they still don't). I appreciated the makeup mirror, but found the hotel toiletries to be too strongly scented for my taste (some of us have fragrance allergies, hello people!). Cute balcony overlooking the bank building across the street, but after five minutes the Santa Anna winds sent me inside with an allergy attack, so not much use to anybody. The real kicker (and my kids really laughed at me later) was that I was starving on arrival and couldn't find a restaurant in my price range in the hotel (there is a mall nearby, I just didn't know about it yet). So I ordered a $19 room service pizza which came with another $10 of taxes, service fees, and other charges. So I ate a $30 pizza. Will never hear the end of it from my kids. And will probably never stay here again, but it was nice while it lasted.

“Excellent stay!” This hotel was perfect for our 3 day stay in the valley. Location was right on Ventura Blvd near Sepulveda, just a (long) block away from the Galleria (shops/restaurants). Our room was very clean, modern and updated. Bedding was very comfortable! There was no room safe which was surprising since most hotels have those now. Shower had great water pressure and consistent hot water! Also, the balcony was not usable as the sliding door only opens 4" wide. We didn't care but someone else might. Staff was one of the friendliest ever. Everyone from the manager Dave who quickly and easily checked us in, to security, housekeeping, lobby bartender and the parking attendants were happy, helpful and always greeted us with a smile. We arrived on the Friday of "Carmageddon" weekend and prior to our stay we even received an email warning of potential delays along with a number to call for further assistance with alternative routes etc. Parking was $15 per day but allowed in/out privileges. You can probably find street parking but it was nice to know the car was in a covered, secure lot. As others mentioned, there are computers and a printer available for use in the lobby - very convenient for printing out plane/train tickets etc. Based on just the hotel and location I would have rated this a 4, but because the customer service was above and beyond at every turn, I rated it a 5! It really made a great impression on us!

“WOW! Unbelievable Service” The best customer service I have ever experienced at any hotel. My husband arranged this trip for my daughter and I to celebrate a birthday and graduation. When told of the event, the front desk manager upgraded our room to a suite, and a giant cupcake was delivered to my daughter on her birthday. The staff who worked the breakfast area got to know us in the few days we were there, and remembered our preferences every day. A special thank you and unlimited praise go to the doorman, Darren.
