He greeted us by name daily, helped with our bags, and even walked us to the subway as we left. We have never been treated as well at any hotel regardless of price. The hotel is new; the rooms are awesome as are the common areas. Prices are still great as the hotel builds its client base, but you better start making reservations early - with this level of service the hotel is sure to become the most popular in the city. Thanks to all the staff for a wonderful stay (and to my husband for choosing this hotel!) We left the Palomar with one thought - "When can we come back?"

“Mein Lieblingshotel in Chicago - da würde ich immer wieder hin” Wunderwunderschönes Hotel. Die wohl tollste Hotellobby, die ich je gesehen habe. War bisher das Le Meridien in Wien mein liebstes Innenstadthotel – nun ist es das W Chicago (Achtung, aufpassen, es gibt zwei Ws in Chicago. Nicht verwechseln!!). Die Zimmer sind qualitativ hochwertig eingerichtet, der übliche W-Standard aber ohne das in manchen Ws nun vorherrschend kitschige bonbonfarbene. War wirklich schön dort. Die Lage ist prima. Und die Empfehlungen des Concierges für eine Blueskneipe haben prima gepasst. Mein absolutes Städelieblingshotel. Wenn wieder in Chicago – dann würde ich dahin wollen (wenn der Preis ok ist).

“Trip Advisor ratings were spot on!” Lovely property, extremely welcoming, great location, comfortable rooms. Would definitely want to stay longer and check in again. I was not able to book a waterfront room (the hotel was too busy), but i loved my room overlooking 1st Avenue. Lively but not noisy, the chairs in the window area were perfect, excellent room and fine room location. As one would hope in Seattle, even the in-room coffee was excellent.

“takes you to another era” For the price it was lovely. Some may feel the older rooms are worn and unimpressive but the point is it feels the way I imagine the hotel must have felt in the 1940's. We were not there to watch TV or have marble counters in the bathroom. Room service breakfast was lovely. Nice big table and huge carafe of deliscious coffee. The bar downstairs is gorgeous. The art work and detailing are from another time and it completes the fantasy. Do not stay here if you are used to chain hotels. This is a one of a kind experience. It is not luxurious, it is charming .

“Large room at reasonable price” Reservation through website. All info correct, just sign the registration and the charge slip. Room is large with some new refurbishing and some old beat up furniture. Bed was good. Stove, microwave and sofa in poor condition. The room on the east side was fine for a Sunday night, as the Harley Dealership next door is closed. Better than average breakfast; some hot items in addition to coffee, juice and cold cereal. Breakfast area can get crowded. Gave up on Wifi, and used 4g cell phone for access. On a previous visit same problem with WiFi (redirect upon opening browser doesn't work) and the front desk was able to get on the phone to the provider and work it out, but it took 30 minutes. Motel is good choice for east bound travelers, depending on the price offerings at the time. Shop around.

“Great little escape near downtown” We stayed here while in town for a Cowboys game. The Market Center area is not that desireable but this hotel was a diamond in the rough! We got a great deal on the room and enjoyed a balcony view of the Dallas skyline! We were able to walk to Denny's for breakfast and enjoyed cocktails both nights out on our patio. The pool and patio area looked nice although we did not use it. There is also an outdoor fire pit. The only complaint I have is that our housekeeper did not come to clean our room until about 5pm. Luckily this did not affect our plans at all but I was suprised that it took so long for them to come. I'd definitely come back again! I do not recommend staying at the Fairfield Inn next door. It needs some work!

“Can't Beat The Location” Stayed at The Omni for 1 night on business to UT campus. The location is very convenient for access to UT and downtown. The room was spacious, clean. The bed was comfortable with nice linens. Parking is $18 daily for self park which is inconvenient but understandable due to the hotel's downtown location. My only complaint is that even though I am an Omni Preferred Guest, they charged me for internet ($9.95/night if you're not enrolled in that program) on my initial bill so I had to head down and clear that up with the front desk before leaving. Overall a pleasant stay, I would definitely stay here again.

“Great New Spot to Stay!” Brand new property on a quiet street near the airport. Great suite rooms with large flat screen TV’s. Pools, hot tub, basketball, and nice seating area in lobby. Bit of noise from the planes but an excellent choice if you want to be close to the airport. Staff was still a bit green and could probably use a bit of training. Make sure you bring the directions as it is not that easy to find. Free Internet, breakfast, and even dinner during the week.

“AWESOME location and style” the hotel was recently renovated on the interior. great location on the riverwalk and in the middle of downtown. near the Alamo and the Rivercenter mall. you can walk to everything. great views. very clean room. price was good for the Fiesta week event.

“Mostly the best of everything” When you arrive, there is no doubt that this is a Luxury property. I had read the glowing reviews on this website and knew that I had to stay here. The lobby is minimalist chic and our room (or should I say suite) was fabulous, large and very comfortable. It had a lovely fireplace which unfortunately, we didn’t need over the Labor Day weekend. There is a flat panel TV in living area and the bedroom and in the bathroom mirror (my favorite). Housekeeping was never seen but our room was spectacularly maintained during our stay. As is not unusual over a long holiday weekend, there were 2 wedding parties staying at the hotel during the weekend of our stay. The first night I heard booming music until the wee hours of the morning. I thought it was from some nearby club, but I was told by the front desk that it must have been the wedding reception. The hotel offered a complimentary breakfast, but since we were otherwise so comfortable in our room, we declined, but thanked them for the gesture. In addition, Bernard’s (that I have read so many nice things about) was closed on the last night of our stay at the hotel (Sunday) so we decided to have a nightcap at Balsan. Big mistake – the service was horrible. It was only semi-crowded but it was like amateur night behind the bar. This hotel can do so much better than that. We like to blend in with the locals when we are out-of-town and this hotel makes that a very easy thing to do since it is away from Michigan Avenue but within close walking distance to all of the high-end shopping and many great restaurants. Even with the problems, I would jump at the chance to stay here again.

“Disgusting” We got this hotel off hotwire, claiming to be 4 stars. RIGHT. It was dirty: peeling, stained carpet, a funky smell, burn marks on the wall...I could go on and on. The location, right across from Water Tower, was good but did not make up for the general nastiness of this joint. AVOID IT!!!!

“Good fit for us” This is a great place and great value if you need to stay for a week. Its sort of basic and it only has one elevator for 4 floors. It is located right across I5 from Northgate Mall. The employees couldn't have been nicer. They changed rooms for us so that we had a suite with a full kitchen with a bedroom on both sides of it. It had plenty of room for the 5 of us for a week. We wouldn't have been able to afford the set up any where else.

“No Hot Water” I was stranded mid-trip in Philadelphia last night. Rather than spending the night in the airport I decided to pay $300 for a room at the airport Marriott. While I didn't have my luggage, my wife told me on the phone "at least you get to take a shower in the morning." She spoke to soon... while I did get a shower, it was ice cold. No hot water at all. And, apparently, the Marriott doesn't have the 100% satisfaction guarantee like the Hampton Inn does. Oh well. Back to Hampton when I have a choice. By the way, there was nothing about the room that was worth $300.

“Interesting Contrast with Sunlovers Report” I too was at the Warwick over Thanksgiving. I paid 'Rack Rate' (a solid $400+ incl. taxes and breakfast) for two queens. In reserving in Sept., I requested a room with a view - at which point the hotel solicited >$100 higher room rate. I passed; I was not upgraded on arrival. Each of the first two nights, I reported that the room thermostat was not functioning (78 degrees all night); this prompted talk of an engineer but no action whatsoever. By necessity, I too discovered a means to open the window (viewing a wall). After the third night, my son and I mistakenly ordered breakfast a la carte over the nice 'vouchered' buffet. Curiously, our a la carte substitutes were lower priced than the buffet, but we were still told that substitution was not possible and 'surcharges' (?) would apply. This finally prompted conversation with the restaurant manager; I advised that the hotel's operating performance (a/c) was subpar and charging structures taken together were not four star. The manager was attentive and apologetic; the a/c was fixed for the last night and no surcharges applied (but must it come to this...?) BTW - there is no in-room television programing whatsoever except in purchased package content - zero! Local news and weather? No. In sum, the hotel is historic, and nicely maintained (generally); ditto - the large rooms. Warwick enjoys an excellent location and staff were not rude. But another poster here mentioned 'nickle and diming' - I concur - and that conditions staff a bit defensively. I felt it or perceived it due to the issues I experienced. In sum, a nice facility and location that did not make the positive impression that it might have. There are other well located hotels in this price bracket in the city that have made better impressions.

“Only if you have to beacuse of early AM flight or cancelled flight” Stayed here with my girlfriend after our flight was cancelled and the airline put us up. I was at the hotel for about 7 hours and it was better than sleeping inside the airport. Still, like most of the reviews, the hotel needs upgrading including room furniture (just old), TV (worst picture ever - is this 1982, get some $200 LCDs in there) and carpet (dirty and disgusting - considered not walking around without shoes).

“Solid 4 Star Hotel, with a great location” The entire downstairs staff is excellent. The doormen regularly did hold the door (rarely happens anymore), valet guy was courteous and allowed me to park for 10 minutes, concierge was helpful and available, and the front desk staff is first class- from Katherine who assisted me prior to arrival to Sasha who checked me in at 11am- into a high floor (as requested), but small room. The furniture was nice, bed comfortable, and there was a nice but small sitting area. It seems like each room has corner windows (due to the building's designs) and I thought that was cool. The curtains were perfect. The bathroom was small, there were too few toiletries (one soap), and the shower head was shooting some water into the ceiling, finally the toilet made a horrible sound when it was flushed. It still was clean but needed a little TLC. I was disappointed that my room didn't have a terrace (as I viewed right into the others around me), but I paid $85 on priceline and was treated like a valued customer. Finally, the location is excellent- walk to Union Square, Chinatown, Ferry Building, Fisherman's Wharf, North Beach... what more can you ask for? It's also close to Bart= airport train. Thanks to the entire staff for making me feel so welcome. I look forward to my next stay here.
“très bien pour visiter Sea World” Vu le prix , très bien . Propre et calme , restaurant a proximité ( joe's bar) . Idéal pour dormir après une journée a Sea World .

“You really CAN'T get there from here” Nice enough place but sooooo frustrating to try to get to. You can see it, but even with a map it is extremely difficult to find. It took us for our five tries (after each wrong turn, back onto expressway, down to next exit, turn around, etc.) and when I finally got there I was really frustrated. Room okay, clean and comfortable, bathroom clean. Business center with two computers. Free coffee and USA Today. Nice pool. Most motels we stay in include breakfast but this one does not and restaurant on site really pricey. We paid $50 for a room via Priceline. I would not stay there again--Austin has many better options.

“The breakfast was the best part of the stay....” In order to attend a conference in the airport area, it was decided that a hotel nearby would be best. The Holiday Inn name is always attractive to us, so the location was the choice. Lots of problems----poor lighting in room, loose headboards that rattle when the bed was sat or laid on, and VERY hard mattresses. Average management and guest assistance. The free breakfast was the best part of the stay. Should have stuck with Marriott nearby!

“Would give it a 3.5 if I could” I arrived late and was greeted by a panhandler - not the best beginning to my stay. I think a better run hotel would have either bribed the panhandler to go elsewhere, or at the very least, had the doorman/porter observant enough to greet me as I exited the taxi, as opposed to after I had checked in. The room was as others have described it - slick and modern - and had just about everything you could ask for. My only issue with the room was that the television reception was pretty fuzzy for a couple of the network stations (NBC and I think CBS). I know this can be an issue in a city, but I would have enjoyed my early morning routine with less static on the TV. Speaking of mornings, one morning there were 2 elevators out of service. After waiting for 20 minutes, and I'm not exagerating, I decided that I would have to walk down, rather than risk being late for my customer meeting. Fortunately, I was only on the 7th floor. I lugged my laptop down a couple of flights, only to be greeted by guests and a hotel employee heading back up. It seems we had all chosen the staircase to no where, and had to get to a floor with the correct access, and then were guided to the basement, and finally to an exit. Kudos for the employee, who did lug my laptop for me. Normally, I wouldn't even mention this last point, but I think it is indicative of the lack of attention paid to details. That was the erratic nature of newpaper delivery. One morning, the Wall Street Journal was outside my door. The next three mornings, no paper at my door, but copies of the San Francisco Chronicle near the elevator. The last morning, USA outside my door. As I say, this was no big deal, but highlights a lack of consistency in the hotel.

“Nice new hotel with excellent staff!” We stayed at the Hilton Suites Phoenix for three nights on business. The front desk personnel was very accomodating and friendly. The hotel layout is very similar to an Embassy Suites. It appears to be very new and well maintained. There's a small gym in the hotel and a much larger and fully equipped gym across the street that hotel guests have access to. There's a small pool and hot tub that we didn't use but seemed clean and inviting. Only two drawbacks to this property; location and lack of an executive lounge. It's not really in the downtown area. Although public transportation is right across the street, you need to drive a couple of miles to get to the downtown area. Other than that, it's a real nice place to stay on business.

“Very, Very, Satisfied” Our family decided on a last minute summer getaway to NYC. Availability of rooms was limited so I explored some options and decided on the Ritz Carlton down at the Battery. This turned out to be an excellent choice. Weekend rates for this Ritz were on a par with lesser hotel chains in Manhattan. The reason for this is location. This property, if you aren't familiar with New York City, is at the far tip of manhattan in the financial district. Personally, I prefer this quieter weekend location and enjoy early morning walks on the waterfront in a beautiful park with views of the Statue of Liberty. The subway is a few blocks away and you can be in midtown rather quickly so I don't see an issue. If you want immediate access to the major museums, theater, central park, etc. you're not going to get that here. Checkin was flawless and my first impression of the lobby and common areas was positive. Service was impeccable as you would expect with everyone being courteous and helpful. Our room was spacious with a generous sized bathroom. Beds were extremely comfortable and the room was spotlessly clean. The impression was one of modern elegance. No complaints at all with the accomodations. Overall, this is a great hotel with a lot to offer the leisure traveler. Take a chance on something a little out of the way and you aren't likely to be disappointed. We definitely weren't and would stay again.

“Great Stay” Stayed here for just one night and had a very pleasant, confortable stay with no problems. I had a beautiful corner room with a fantastic view of the city on one side and Lake Michigan on the other. The style of the hotel and room decor was very unique. Everything was modern and extremely clean. Loved the tv in the bathroom mirror (not all rooms have it though). I thought the location wasn't ideal (not as good as the other Renaissance), but was completely fine for me. Within 10-15 minutes walk there are restaurants. The lounge could get crowded at peak times. If you have two people staying for an extended period of time the room could get a bit cozy, but for me the size was fine. Those were the only negative things I could find about this hotel and I would stay here again. Regrettably I did not get to try the food at Mercat, Iron Chef Jose Garcas'restaurant.

“Just what you want in a hotel and dog friendly” We stayed for a week at the Palomar Hotel in Philadelphia for a week during a thanksgiving trip. This Kimpton hotel is just about everything you would want in a big city hotel. The rooms are nicely decorated, clean, and comfortable plus the entire staff was friendly and helpful. The location was excellent with most downtown attractions within walking distance including the Franklin Institute, City Hall, Kimmel Center for the arts, and the Rittenhouse shopping district. ( Please note that the historic Independance Hall ,the liberty bell, and US Mint are located far away on the east side of the city). Like all Kimpton hotels, the Palomar features a wine and snack reception in the lobby every afternoon at 5pm. Our snack was truffle flavored popcorn. Did I mention dog friendly? My estimate is that 10% of all the guests were accompanied by lovable and polite dogs: not unusual to see one or two canines in the lobby at all times. Be sure to register on-line for the Kimpton rewards program and you will receive free internet plus a $10 certificate to 'raid the minibar'

“quiet budget hotel by freeway, near big shopping center & restaurants” Stayed here for one night while driving with my mom & 2 cats cross country. Needed a place that would take pets -- they do, for no additional fee. Hotel has rooms that are accessed inside/ via indoor hallways -- & also some rooms on the first floor that are accessed from the outside. We picked the latter because we could park right in front of the room & carry the cats & stuff right inside. - hotel is quiet -- despite being on freeway access road. - hotel is on a bit of a rise, so you do have a nice view back across El Paso & into Juarez - room was clean & basic -- not the newest but not too dated either - staff were friendly - located on the east edge of El Paso -- literally -- just 5 min drive further east & you're out of the city. Easy freeway access. - near a big shopping area with lots of stores & lots of restaurants -- so plenty of choices for eating out - yeah, there is a "gentlemens club" (strip club) nearby but it's a non-issue. Just an enclosed box building with its own parking lot. Not a problem. I'd stay here again esp if traveling with pets .

“Old and dirty - service to match” This place is a dump. Service is worse. I'm a Hilton Diamond member. On arrival I waited 15 minutes for someone to appear at check in desk. It got worse from there. No room upgrade. Old smelly room. Next to elevator. No way to get a cold water, soda, or anything else in hotel after 11pm. No working vending machines. Next time in San Antonio stay at motel 6.

“Not a Business Hotel” Good points: - very clean and well furnished - friendly staff - nice beds Problematic for Business Travelers 1) No speaker phone in room. Very annoying if your business is global and requires extensive late night conference calls. Inexcusable for such an expensive Hilton property. 2) Mobbed Breakfast Area. This property clearly markets aggressively to get huge families on vacation from Latin America. Makes the breakfast area hopelessly unusable. 30 minute waits for everything. Even worse, there is no nearby substitute restaurant (a solution I have used at other Embassy Suites) 3) No hot water circulation system. Not a business travel problem, but inexcusable for such a premium property. Have to wait 5-10 min for the hot water to warm up all the pipes between the basement and the top floor before you can take a shower. Premium properties worldwide usually have a system that constantly circulates hot water on each floor to avoid this lag. 4) Inept laundry service. Was 2 hours late. But they also forgot to charge me for it. 5) Expensive and clumsy parking system. Garage is reasonably nice, but they want $17/day for it and they have to fumble around with your room number every time you drive in and out. And they also have trouble keeping track of your charges which requires multiple visits to the front desk to correct their cooridination problems. 6) Slow room cleaning. Rooms still not serviced at 4PM on some days. 7) Sealed Windows. Again, not a business travel problem, but I hate hotels that won't let you get fresh outside air into the room... particularly frustrating when you are near the ocean and can't enjoy the offshore ocean breeze in your room.

“Definately 4-Star” The JW Marriott is a very nice hotel and meets my definition of a four star facility. The room I was in was either new or recently renovated as it was in great shape. The lobby was magnificant and the staff and service are what you would expect at a nicer hotel. While I would certainly recommend this hotel there are a few small negatives I should point out: - The parking garage was always full. And there was no offer from the valet staff to take your vehicle elsewhere. - The room had one of those vending machine refigerators in it, the kind where you take the can of soda and it automatically charges you $5.00 or whatever. There is no room to put your own perishables in it and they post a very tacky warning that you could be charged extra for trying to use it for your own goods. C'mon Marriott, you can do better. I expect a vending machine in the Motel 6. You should spring for a fridge in your flagship hotel. - The elevators were constantly full: children riding up and down, large groups of people getting on at every floor.... It took forever to get to the lobby and then it was not very comfortable being jammed in with 20 people. I was expecting someone with a goat or chicken to get on at any time.... Overall it was a very positive experience and I recommend the hotel.

“Nice location, but small rooms” The location was great and there is free wifi everywhere, but the rooms are tiny and have limited facilities. There's no room service. The staff were very friendly and helpful, but I'm not sure if I would stay there again on a business trip. I found it quite noisy and that made it hard to get good night's sleep.

“Its great to be an Omni Select member” The lobby and bar are relaxing and upscale, and as a select member I got an upgrade to a corner room with a small balcony. I also got the breakfast buffet package, great idea if you like a filling and delicious beakfast. Hot coffee and juice and a USA were at my door at 7am, just as I had requested.

“fantastic hotel & fantastic location” I was travelling with my teenage daughter so we wanted to stay in the heart of NYC. This hotel was an excellent choice. Walking distance to all the theatres, times square, central park and 5th Avenue. The room was excellent. It had a microwave and fridge whch was great as there was a supermarket one block away. The concierge was very knowledgable and helpful. He spent a lot of time with us which was a great help as well as a money and time saver. Would not hesitate to stay there again. Had a great experience.

“Just what we needed at the time” Our flight got cancelled so US Airways gave us a voucher where we received a hotel room for a discounted rate. We are Hilton Honors members and figured due to that, the Embassy Suites would work fine. I would say it served its purpose for this trip. The rooms are older yes, but spacious. The street is sketchy yes, and so are the people lingering around the hotel. I did feel safe once inside the room. The breakfast in the morning which was included was pretty good actually. The shuttle to the airport that was included as well was nice and arrived on time, friendly. The staff at the hotel were friendly as well. If you like 60/70's motif, this hotel is for you and its close to the airport.

“Nice Stay” I stayed here for a seminar. There was construction taking place at the hotel, but it was not noisy or disruptive. One day the tile was being replaced in the lobby and you had to walk around yellow tapes, etc. but it was not a big deal. There were a number of things that were especially good about this property--free wireless was one. I greatly apprerciated the free wireless, but the service was a bit problematic. I had a number of drops while using it but I was still grateful for it. The best t hing about this place is the restaurant. The food was above par--the kitchen here really knows what they are doing. I had multiple meals in the on-site restaurant, room service, as well as meals served for the seminar and all were exceptional. The rooms appear to have been recently upgraded and the style is very modern. The look is attractive though the ceramic bowl sink which sits on the bathroom counter is a bit difficult to use as the faucet sits so close to the bowl. The water pressure was good and the bathroom amenties were crabtree and evelyn. I was able to work easily in the room and appreciated the large desk and the large flatscreen television. The hotel is adjacent to the University Place shopping district and there are places within walking distance to eat and shop. There were some rough looking fellows wandering around this neighborhood which is why I ate most evening meals in the hotel. I did walk to the nearby Talbots outlet one afternoon and I had sushi at the Sushi 101 nearby. There is a rental carcounter in the hotel and I inquired about renting a car there an dropping it at the airport but they tack on a fifty dollar fee for doing that so it was not worth it. I stored my bags when I checked out and went to the shopping center on my last day there. I asked the bellman to call a cab for me but instead he directed me to a limo service. I rode in an SUV to the airport for forty dollars. the cab fare there had ben thirty-five dollars. Next time I will rent a car.

“Excellent Location and Relaxation!” I stayed here Valentine's Day weekend 12-13 and it was perfect! Its right on the bay with an awesome view and walking distance to the Galslamp Quarter with plenty of places to eat and shop! The rail line and trolleys are right in front as well! Now onto the hotel. Check-in was a breeze and we got a room on the 20th floor overlooking the bridge and water. The room was all very new and perfect. Carpet was textured and clean, bed super comfy, TV was a great quality, and bathroom was all marble with Crabtree and Evelyn products. Really folks, it was 5 star all the way. I really loved the onsite Starbucks and Fox Sports grill. There were so many places to sit and watch the water while enjoying a coffee, drink, or meal from ANY of the restaurants and bars. Another thing I loved was there was a small park nearby and a walkway being built for direct access to Petco park. I highly recommend this place for couples, families, and business as it is a stone's throw from the convention center.

“I am still in shock.........and not in a good way” I have stayed in many Ritz Carlton's (laguna niguel, south beach, etc) and I cannot believe how bad this stay was in terms of service. I booked an executive suite harbor view room through the AMEX platinum package. I arrived after 10 PM after a long flight. I was given keys to the room which turned out to be a standard room. I returned to the front desk and they said "sorry, we made a mistake". Next they gave me keys to a city view executive suite (again wrong). I called downstairs and told the front desk about it. They said that they had my reservation as a city view room even though I called AMEX and they said that it should have been a harbor view. The hotel reluctantly "upgraded" me and said that I should feel lucky that a harbor view room was available (even though I paid for it). Near checkout, I inquired about my bill and found that none of my AMEX platinum amenities were included. They told me that they booked me under a "reconnect package" even though AMEX clearly stated that my reservation should include AMEX amenities. I never got my amenities and never got an apology. I told the front desk manager about all of these issues and nothing was done. Finally I was charged 65 dollars per night for overnight parking even though my parking ticket was stamped at 60 dollars. They said that it was because I have an oversized car (I had an SUV). I was so upset at this point that I didnt argue (i just left). The rooms were fine but the service was implorable. This is the worse review that I have given to any ritz carlton that I have stayed in. I noticed several other people complaining. I must say that I think that the hotel treats the wall street business types better than the leisure travellers.

“You could do worse in NY” I've stayed here several times when all other hotels were full. It has some really nice rooms in the front of the hotel, and has some horrible rooms in the back and center of the air shaft rooms that feel and look like a prison cell, only darker. The free breakfast is packed most time so best to get there early to get a seat.

“Average Hotel with Fantastic Staff” The hotel has some of the friendliest staff in the industry. From the valet to the front desk to the telephone operators, everyone was great. the hotel is older...probably build in the early 1900's which means that plumbing was probably added later yielding smaller bathrooms and noisy pipes...but that's not bad for character. The room was clean and comfortable but is was also quite old...looks like they are working on slowly upgrading the rooms...and they could use it. The location is great...convenient to many riverwalk attractions. The Westin, in my opinion, is a nicer hotel, but its surrounding area lacks the character of that of the Gunter. If you can get a rate under $180/nt...go for it. If not, there are probably nicer hotels available at a better value.

“Mixed bag” I got routed here when I missed a plane connection in Houston through no fault of my own. So, the airline foot the bill. Every employee I encountered was cordial and professional. Each went out of way to make me feel like an honored guest- from the shuttle driver, the bellhop, the front desk staff and the restaurant hostess who got me coffee to go. The bed was extremely comfortable and there was no hallway or outside noise to disturb me. Television reception was good and adequate variety of channels. The bathroom grout was moldy in areas and the furnishings like desk, dresser and tv were cheap quality. The business center wanted something like 50 cents a minute to use the computer station. The shower leaked water when I tried to run only bathwater. My room only had decaf coffee at the coffee maker. There is nothing nearby the hotel except for freeway. I did find a Kinko's couple doors down to take care of some work related business. I did not visit the pool, spa or fitness room so cannot comment on those. I would have preferred the Marriott at the airport but decided not to make a drama and insist on that since Continental was very apologetic. Overall this hotel is ok, not excellent but not horrible. A very average Marriott with friendly staff.

“Very decent budget accomodations,” Needed a place to stay on a sunday before my flight out monday afternoon. Found a very decent rate on this motel, I've seen parking in san francisco at 4 star hotels in union square that were more expensive than my nightly rate! Room is pretty basic, but you do get free high speed internet and are located in the south of market region only a 5 minute walk to the location of the event I attended that evening. Good place to park, go out in the city and then get some sleep. You are in San Francisco after all, you should be out enjoying the city!

“Im not a fan. IM an owner, but i prefer better hotel properties in this city” Rooms are contemporary, and nice. Property is clean. Service is average at best, ATTITUDE abounds. I bought into the HIlton Brand here at West 57. I would NOT do it again, and recommend others really think about doing so. THe location is great, and the property is nice. Its not a 5 star property, but probably a 4 star without the service. the 'lounge' for breakfast is better now that they have added seating. Snacks in the evening are nice too... Value can be aggressively debated

“Very Good Hotel But Room Service Breakfast Needs to Improve” I recently spent three nights at the Hyatt for a conference. I was very well treated by the front desk and received a clean and quiet room on a high floor, which was what I had requested. The room was large enough and the bed was comfortable. There was no street noise. I was on a high floor and this may have helped. Housekeeping was very responsive and the concierge was helpful as well. My only complaint is about the lack of options on the room service breakfast menu. In comparison with other hotel chains, the choices for a business traveler were poor. They also don't serve breakfast early enough if a person has a 7 AM meeting. For breakfast for one, I ended up spending nearly $45.00 for a combination of food I really didn't want. I suggest adding a cold cereal and fruit option with toast as an extra add on. Also, they need to have smaller carafes of coffee available. I think I paid $13 for a carafe of coffee that would have been impossible to finish. This makes a big difference to the early morning riser.

“Old but not bad..” Very old hotel, location was ok, 10 minute walk to Westfield shopping centre, tram stop out the front, cheap cab ride to all the main sights. The room was average, comfy bed, clean but very small & basic bathroom. Our room had a connecting door to another room which was locked, made for a fairly noisy night as I could hear our neighbours talking. Starbucks in the lobby is very convenient, the buffet breakfast was nothing worth getting up for. Free wifi was a plus.
“Good Hotel, Good Location” Front desk staff w as excellent. Very good at giving directions. Good business center, large room, comfortable bed. Clean and quiet.

“one of the worst travel hotel experiences....” This was probably one of my worst hotel travel experiences ever, however to start on a bit of a positive note... for the most part, staff were pleasant and tried to be helpful. The room’s outdoor balcony was a nice feature. The Kimpton free internet and wine hour is always a plus. In addition, the Firefly restaurant is very good. That is where the accolades come to a screeching halt. Here’s why you should NOT stay at the Madera: 1. on arrival, three staff were behind the desk, (not busy), but not one to open the door and assist with suitcases - all three could clearly see arrivals attempting to get in 2. upon check in, there was no recognition of Kimpton in touch membership – I had to ask about the credit for the minibar – response = “oh yeah, we do that” 3. after check in, still no assistance with luggage, despite the stairs one had to climb to access elevators to rooms 4. after five hours of the AC on high, it still registered 76 as the temp – one dysfunctional unit cooled the entire space but, since the bathroom is on the far end, must have been at least 90 in there! 5. Requested and received a change in rms – this room was a bit cooler, (albeit a very noisy system), but the bathroom was still HOT with the same dysfunctional type small unit on far end of room 6. showerhead did not function at all (barely a trickle) in 2nd rm – had to be replaced after another call to front desk 7. Both rooms had a strange smell, rugs felt tacky so I stopped walking barefoot 8. Tried to get a taxi from the hotel – told by hotel staff to walk up two blocks to dupont, staff proceeded to walk me out the door and pointed up the street. Was told, “taxis are always full when they get here” 9. Left the “please clean” sign on my door at 9a.m., came back at 2 p.m.and the rm was not touched except for a stack of clean towels in plastic wrapping on the flr – called the desk, after waiting 20 min’s, I finally went down to the desk to request a cleaning with the stack of towels in hand I am leaving out some other issues but this review is getting long. Given these unpleasant experiences, I did appreciate the front desk and general managers, they did appear pleasant, concerned and talked about increasing quality. The Madera is certainly not representative of the Kimpton Hotels’ high quality and consistent personalized service. And, it is certainly not even close to a 4 star which is advertised on the Kimpton website. Cannot recommend staying here at all.

“Nice enough” I thought the JW Marriott was nice enough, we stayed April 5-6 2012. It was busy with lots of kids running around. Had to get our room changed because of children yelling and screaming and showing no consideration for others. I personally though it a bit antsy as a hotel.. trying to be posh yet not. Overpriced for what it was. It was ok, but we moved to the Hilton Garden Inn on 14th, and it was way better. We had a microwave in the room, a fridge, even a laundry and no kids running down the halls and no feeling that it was posh and overrated. I would not go back to the JW Marriott.Breakfast $24.00 for eggs, give me a break. We had no interaction with anybody, except the doormen who were great and helpful, otherwise the place was ordinary at best.

“Don't stay away” I know everyone has their opinions, as it should be but the two recent "bad" reviews had titles that sounded like this place was just horrendous. When you read the summaries they had two complaints: rude staff and stains...two observations that would not make me warn others in capital letters to STAY AWAY. You would think there were rats nesting in the pillows. We had an unbelievable experience here, the suite was a gem and the staff was both accommodating and cheerful. (Loved the cozy pub and the bartender). Three of us stayed there and our hotel experiences combined would rival any world traveler. I, and my companions would without a doubt stay there again.

“OK” I stayed in this hotel recently. It is not a fancy hotel. It's more of a motor inn. Most of the rooms have doors that open to the outside--at least mine did, and there is not an elevator, just stairs up to the second floor rooms. The rooms are pretty worn and the sheets seemed cheap. You know the kind with a low thread count, but they were clean. My room faced the swimming pool area toward the inner courtyard so I didn't feel afraid even though I was by myself. There is a nice lobby, and the people who work there are very accommodating. They really went out of their way to provide good service. They have a nice dining room area. I had the breakfast buffet. It was about $11.00, I think and was good. The bacon was very crispy and delicious. They will make you a waffle or pancakes or an omlet if you like. Although not fancy, it was a good place to stay for one night--on business.

“Not good hotel” In town for the AAN Conference in late April. The rooms were very very tiny. I was also falling over myself in the tiny bathroom - no place to put anything. Went out to a restaurant on Saturday evening and then a local pub and when came back to the hotel it looked like a war zone outside. Literally thousands of drunks lining the streets until late at night - sirens, etc. Also very hard to get cabs on multiple occasions.

“Lovely Hotel - Great Service” I stayed here on my way to NYC from Sydney, to break up the trip. We were planning to stay at another hotel in LA on the return trip home, but enjoyed the Hilton LAX so much, that we stayed here for on the return trip. The service here is very good. All the departments are great, and we particularly were surprised in the landings bar at how good the cocktails, and waitstaff were. The room service waiter was also very exceptional, a pleasant surprise. The hotel is very nice. The lobby is great, and has these massive amethyst and quartz crystal clusters throughout. The rooms were spacious, and very comfortable. My mother had a room that opened onto a courtyard, which she enjoyed very much, and I had a room on an executive floor, that had nice views. The decor is very elegant and understated. The executive lounge views of the runaway were good, though the lounge, as typical in US Hiltons, offered pretty disappointing food etc. The meals we ate in the restaurant and downstairs were very nice, and also from room service in the two times we stayed there. The price of this hotel was very reasonable. There is an airport shuttle that runs every 10-15 mins to and from the hotel. This was very convenient. There are buses that you can take to Venice Beach, and other places, and we also went into LA city quite easily by bus with the directions from the concierge. We both really enjoyed our stays at Hilton LAX, and actually were very pleasantly suprised at this hotel. Really great way to break up the long flight to and from Australia to NYC or the east coast.

“Westin Comfort, But Needs Improvement” At its best, this hotel meets the typical Westin standards. But the hotel lacks in certain ways, and needs improvement. As it is, there are better options in downtown Denver. My room had a nice view of the Rockies, and the furnishings were of typical Westin comfort. The bed was great, the TV was high-quality, the chairs and tables were fine. But certain details were off -- there was no pen or paper, certain outlets didn't work, and the closet doors and front door stuck. The bathroom was quite nice, better than some Starwood properties I've been in. Yet the room gave the feeling that it needed to be tended to more often. Things are no better in the common areas. The halls are basic. The lobby is fine in spots, but has an awkward two-level layout. The restaurant is pretty bad, and felt like a conference room more than an eating spot. There is no gift shop, and the business center feels like an employee closet. The front desks are a bit small -- no room for luggage. The employees were nice, but there didn't seem to be enough of them around. The back of the hotel grounds are overgrown and host some homeless types. Overall, the details of this hotel are just not there. If you are a Starwood stalwart, or need a predictable choice in a convenient location, the Westin is fine. But look around if you want a finer experience. I hope that Starwood invests some money to fix this property.

“Better than I expected” The staff of this hotel, all of whom were friendly and professional, went a long way towards making this a nice stay. The rooms were, indeed, very small but the hotel makes an effort to maximize the use of the space. The location is great. On the con side, the internet connection was extremely spotty and the toiletries could be improved.

“Trendy hotel , only one available in Harlem” Stayed one night for local event, clean basic hotel, with great staff.The view was an alley. The tv was great but obstructed with a wall.No spa , room service etc, but good basic hotel.

“Great value, location, decent staff!” Great (tiny) hotel with an address that is easy to remember. The room was extremely small, but modern, new, and comfy. There was a little noise from the street but that is to be expected. Located near plenty of pubs, restaurants, and a whole foods, I would stay here again to explore the city. The hotel comes with a continental breakfast that was pretty good. Free wifi didn't work at all, but they have a terminal in the breakfast room for free use.

“Wow.” The Fairmont is a gorgeous well maintained property in the ideal location for seeing Boston. Shopping, great restaurants and all the fun of Boston are at your doorstep. What puts this hotel over the top is service, friendly, informed and very polished. Highly recommended.

“Still working out the kinks?” I know this hotel is in the middle of a major renovation, and that may have something to do with the things that bothered me about this stay. Overall the hotel looks nice and has plenty of ammenities to offer. I only spent one night, before flying out of DFW recently. Here are the pros and cons: Pros: The hotel and lobby are beautiful. The hotel looks and feels luxurious, and is decorated well. The lobby has several bars and eateries, and places just to hang out. The staff is friendly and helpful. The concierge was great, reccommended and made us a reservation at a lovely steakhouse. The hotel shuttle is convenient and the driver was really interesting and funny. The rooms are HUGE and brand new. The decorations and furnishing are not the normal drab Hilton stuff, but actually look like a designer was in the room. Our room had two flat screen TVs, and the bedroom was seperated by a half wall where the living room and kitchen were. Bathroom was separate with a walk in dressing area. The bathroom itself was quite small, however. Cons: The biggest con is the sleep quality. The fan in the room made a loud woosh/clicking noise every time it turned on or off, which woke me up about every hour. Then, between 3 and 4 AM, the people in the room next to us were so loud that both my husband and I woke up and couldn't get back to sleep. They were coming and going from the room so we could hear the door slam repeatedly. We could hear everything that was said in the hallway, and we could even hear loud talking through the wall. This is surprising because if you remember how our room was set up, our neighbors were on the far side by the living room, away from the bed, and behind another half wall. It was by far the loudest night I've ever spent in a hotel. When we complained the next morning we were told we were the first people to ever stay in the room and they would look into the air duct noise. We were offered complimentary parking as consolation for the noisy neighbors. The other dissapointment here is the executive lounge. As Hilton Diamond members, I've seen some great perks and lounges in various hotels. The week we stayed the lounge was under going renovation, so was temporarily moved to a small conference room. There was no view, and limited seating. The food that was offered in the evening was good and appreciated. However no free drinks is a bit of a disappointment. We ended up just going to the bar in the lobby for a drink, since the ambiance was much better. You must pay to use the business center. I believe there was free wireless, but since I was travelling without a computer, I had no access without paying. Average: Gym is small but great selection of equipment. It was full, but I was able to use what I wanted. Parking fees are average. Breakfast at the hotel was good, nothing to rave about. Overall, the sleep quality at this hotel made it really miserable for me. But, I do believe this could be a great property once the kinks are worked out.

“Very pleasant - but less radical than I'd expected” The other reviews here are accurate. The decor is very modern in parts (leopardskin robes!) but surprisingly traditional elsewhere, especially the TV cabinets. As its an old building conversion, however, the mix works. I paid $219 for a two-room suite in August and can't complain - you get double the normal space and a jacuzzi bath. All I would say, however, is that this is not a 'design' hotel in the mould of a 'W'. There is no hip-and-trendy bar, no hyper-trendy lobby, no condoms in the mini-bar. Think of it as a traditional hotel with a few funky furnishings and you won't be disappointed. (PS. As with all downtown hotels, the area is not exactly buzzing at night. If you want lots of restaurants, cafes, bars etc you may want to stay in Georgetown and cab it downtown everyday.)

“Good location and a good price” This Courtyard is within walking distance of all the major downtown sites of Seattle including Pike's Place Market, the Space Needle, and the Sculpture Garden. The historic building has been tasefullt renovated, though as one of the shorter buildings in the area, don't expect a great view. While I usually like self-parking, the $26 charge for valet was quite reasonable and the car could be pre-ordered so it was always waiting curbside when I needed it. All in all, this is a standard Courtyard with a great location right downtown. If you're looking for simple, safe, well located, and a good price, this is your hotel in Seattle.

“Nice hotel, friendly staff, convenient to airport” We stayed here before an early flight out of DEN. It's a beautifully appointed hotel and the staff was very friendly. The shuttle to the airport was so convenient and I'm so happy we took it - the traffic was horrible and the shuttle driver knew how to navigate it in order to get us there in time. I'd definitely stay here again.

“Nicely renovated hotel” The good: Service was good, the room was nicely renovated and felt well maintained, separate shower and tub, great location within walking distance to many eateries. The bad: The rooms seemed a little small, due to the layout of the room you could hear everything outside the door when lying in bed.

“Much better than expected - would stay again!” I stayed at this property because I had Wyndham Rewards points to redeem and was a bit skeptical based on some of the reviews. However, this hotel is great!!! The staff is very friendly and accommodating - from the lady working check-in, to the housekeepers, and the breakfast crew/check-out worker, they were all very friendly and kept asking to make sure everything was going well. The room was updated and extraordinarily clean - the linens were luxurious and what you would expect from a hotel like Hilton Garden Inn, etc. There was a new flat-screen HD tv in the room, plush towels, and upgraded features. When we walked into the room, we were very impressed with how nice it was. We had our dog with us and the hotel is pet friendly and there is no fee so that was also a great feature. The pool area looked very nice and clean; we unfortunately didn't have time to use it but next time we're back in the area, we will stay here and certainly use it. Finally, the breakfast was great - much better than the typical free continental breakfast. There was french toast, waffles, hard boiled eggs, cereals, yogurts, pastries, bagels, muffins, fresh fruit, coffee, juices, and milk. I would DEFINITELY stay here again - it's convenient to downtown and Sea World with lots of shopping and restaurants in the area.

“Great location, fine hotel” The location was great, close to restuarants and just enough off of the Miracle Mile that you don't feel under the swarm. Parking is $42 a night, well within the market price for downtown chicago, but an amount that will need to factor into your budget.

“Good Value, Clean, Needs A Few Updates” The staff was friendly here and the property was clean. The rooms are slightly outdated but in good condition. The pool area really needed to be updated, but it was clean. This was a good value for us!

“Great Choice at IAH” My Husband and I stayed here for one night while traveling to Belize. This hotel has a great location and was very convienent for us. All the staff went out of their way to try to make our stay comfortable. The room had the most comfy bed...if it wasn't for catching an early flight I would have loved just to stay in and relax in the comfort of the pillows and cushy comforter. We had no airport noise, which was very unusual as it is located on the airport property. I highly recommend this Marriott!

“Unbelieveable on all fronts!!!!” Of all of the deals I have got on Priceline in the past few years, this has to rank as one of the best. I paid $34.00 last night for a five star room ($189 on their website) Everything in the June 25 review is true, EXCEPT there is no construction. The place is beautiful. I wanted to stay a month. Even at a higher price it would be well worth it. Not included in the previous reviews are a couple of things. First, the breakfast that is free includes cereal, toast, fruit, juice and coffee. If you want hot entrees, there is a menu and the charges are a reasonable $5.50. However, the set-up for the breakfast was top notch; neat, tidy, and first class. Also, the workout room is definitely a step up. Free weights, machines and nice cardio equipment was all evident. The hotel is 100% non-smoking and about three minutes from the airport. The staff is great as well. Jessica checked me in and couldn't have been nicer. She arranged to have the hotel shuttle (which is 24 hours by the way) pick me up at the Avis lot rather then at the airport. This place is a great example of finding a great place on Priceline, but I wouldn't hesitate to pay more in the future to stay there again. Cheers. Marius

“Gutes Preis/Leistungsverhältnis” Das W-Hotel in Boston ist super gelegen und bietet Reisenden eine gute Unterkunft für private und geschäftliche Reisen. Geschäftsviertel und Geschäfte sind in der Nähe - alles zu Fuß erreichbar. Vorallem für den Sommer empfielt sich Boston und dieses Hotel dazu, da man zu dieser Jahreszeit am meißten in der Stadt unternehmen kann.

“a plethora or poor experiences” From lack of internet (both wired and wireless) to overwhelming perfumed scent via fan in lobby to lack of housekeeping to rooms, this was one of the least satisfying hotel experiences. If you can choose otherwise, don't stay here, plenty of other choices in Dallas. If you need consistent internet, check your room as you soon as you get in. Due to lack of internet in reg. room, I was upgraded to "club level suite". The room was no different than the reg. room in which I was originally booked and was never cleaned during the day.

“Would be great for families” Stayed at this hotel for business and it really wasn't set-up as a great business hotel. The rooms come with seriously outdated kitchen's, but the tower rooms have fantastic views of the bay. The property is right on the beach and would be great for people traveling with kids. The rooms were outdated, but if you were seeking a great beach vacation where you could cook and keep costs down, this would be the property for you.

“Extremely Convenient Location” It's an odd place, built in long strips and when inside you spend your time in very long tunnels. However, there are many (locked) doors into the parking lot so you are never far from your car. In some parts the carpet is worn and the hallways need a refresh. If you set aside the dull ambience that is typical of a Fairfield Inn and focus on convenience, then this place begins to shine. It is not only a stone's throw from the San Jose Airport; it's also at the junction of 101 and 880 AND on First Street. You can go anywhere in Silicon Valley quickly from here. There is a small strip of shops in the lot that include a StarBucks and Chiptole Mexican Grill. Also sharing the lot is a gas station. I always like to stay here. Access from 101 is so easy: take Brokaw Road go 1.5 short blocks and it's on the right.

“What a great hotel!” Based on reviews here at TripAdvisor, I booked this hotel initially for a week's stay, and ended up extending my lodging there for three weeks. The cleanliness, the friendly and professional staff, the good food, and the sound sleep every night was tremendously welcome. The exercise room is great, with lots of machines, and neat as a pin. The hotel is located just far enough from I-10 that road noise is not an issue. This will be my preferred place to stay for business on the west side of Houston, for certain!

“Plain vanilla” There is nothing wrong with this hotel, but nothing about it stands out either. It is located downtown, which is good if you have business and the metro is three blocks away. This is obviously an hotel that has been refurbished. Being in the business district, the area has plenty of restaurants to go to during the day, but just about shuts down at night, which would be an issue if you're visiting. The rooms are clean, very plain, but clean is much more mportant to me than decor. Linens were nice. The staff is also very pleasant and helpful. This would not be my choice in the future. One thing I would recommend-check out the food trucks at lunch at the park one block away-they are fabulous.

“Great stay at the Marriott (and more about Boston!) LONG REVIEW” We just returned from four nights at the Marriot Copley. We (it was my husband, my sixteen year old and myself) booked this hotel based on its proximity to BU and Northeastern University, Newbury Street shops, the malls, and historic Boston. We also used three nights of Marriott points and then paid $229 for the fourth night. We chose these dates because of Spring Break in Virginia. We had an excellent stay, and let me say that there was an initial aghast moment when we checked in along with thousands of Anime Conventioneers! Check in was simple (we arrived two hours late due to the tardiness of our flight out of Reagan National), we were given our request of a top floor (room 3045)--this was a corner room and at the very end of the hall which was great since it meant that the only people heading down to our end of the hall would be us! In retrospect, I wish I had asked for an even higher floor, or even tried to get club level or an upgrade, but what I was given was perfect at the time. Before critiquing the hotel too much, I will say that I am a Marriott Timeshare owner, so when I go away for either a night or seven nights, it has usually been in a Springhill Suites-style room, or a timeshare (apartment-like). I haven't stayed in a Marriott Hotel-style room in a very long time, so this took some getting used to (without a sitting area or kitchen, so to speak). There is a chair, small table and lamp against the long wall with the window. The bathroom is small. I didn't love that there wasn't an exhaust fan, the spray of the shower (pressure), the yellow staining on the wallpaper (near the floor and possibly glue coming from behind the paper), or that they turned the water off Sunday night from 12-6am (this would have been okay if our sink water had come back on at six am...instead when we called downstairs at seven to report that there wasn't any water running after an initial try of getting black water, we were told to just keep it on and it "will eventually come on". It didn't, we brushed our teeth using the tub water, and reported it to maintenance (it was on when we returned to the room that afternoon). And there was a letter slipped under our door letting us know the water would be cut off for those six hours (someone else on this post had written about this during his stay as well). There could be much, much better lighting in the bathroom and a better hairdryer (not turbo enough for long hair). But it was clean, enabled two people to stand next to each other and put on makeup ( a bit cramped, but possible), and provided us with the dryer, toiletries, etc I didn't love that I had a full wall of windows plus more once rounding out the corner (about three feet of the next wall), but the bottom half was "foggy". I did love that the top half was BIG enough that the bottom half could be avoided and I got tons of great pictures of the Charles River and beyond. I didn't love the double beds (I would have preferred two queens), but I really do love those Marriott pillows! I didn't love the fee for the Internet for the cost of the room. Yes, it did seem like it took a while for them to clean up the dishes from the halls (a few coffee mugs and wine glasses) like another poster wrote. But the cleaning crew were always working (remember we had a full house of ANIME people...look it up if you don't know what they are...or perhaps you are one of them?). We ate at Champions the first night since we arrived late and wanted to get acclamated to the area. I loved that the malls were attached, and since I left my hairbrush at home (!), I loved that Shaws is across the street (snacks, hairbrush, sodas, EVERYTHING you need). The restaurant was good, but I tried not to go to any other chain while in Boston. We were touring colleges for my daughter (mission accomplished), saw Boston (never been before), took the Trolley Tour (can get tickets right at the Marriott and pick up Trolley there), explored the "T" (very easy--get everyone put on the Charlie Card and it is even easier), tried many great restaurants (listed below) and did a lot of walking! If I didn't have the points to use for a free night stay, I would probably comparison shop and look into the Westin as a possibility. Just for a change. The Marriott has always done right by me. And the fact that this hotel is connected to the malls, the convention center, extremely close to the "T", has a grocery store across the street, the Duck tour boats and Trolleys right at the entrance.....so many pros and very, very few cons. We ate breakfast at Brassiere Jo (three minute quick walk away), Mike's City Diner (fifteen minute even quicker walk away--it was chilly so fast walking was easy for us!), and Thornton's Diner (two more mins past Brassiere Jo's). Had wonderful waffles and you have to order the double hot chocolate at Brass. Jo's. Thorntons had excellent crepes and we liked the home fries/potatoes there the best. And Mike's had phenomenal waffles (cinnamon walnut). Brass. Jo's is french so the waffles tasted a bit different than what you'd expect (wheat?) and the hot choc. was thick and came with small crocks of whipped cream on the side. We ate lunch at Bartleys Burger Cottage (near Harvard)...if you can get past the nasty, rude girl passing out menus outside (and yes, we had a ten minute wait outside on a Saturday at two pm, and we placed our order right there on the street with a man that was taking the orders outside and then having them run inside for a head start!), the people inside are very nice. EXPECT cramped quarters! Small and dark inside. The burgers weren't anything spectacular. They have many choices, a huge menu, and it is the ambience/atmosphere/age that we went for...and Rachael Ray recommending it had me curious. We had Easter Lunch at Upper Crust since many places in Little Italy had special menus or weren't open yet (never made it to Giaccomo's due to timing on our part). I loved Upper Crust's pizza. And we also ate lunch one day in Little Italy at Caffe della Sport (it was very, very good...paninis and pizza and very good). Finally, we ate dinners at The Pourhouse (on Boylston and maybe ten min walk from hotel). It is a pub, and we had good wraps, wings and cheesesteaks. Dark though and the service wasn't great. I would go again, because of the size of the menu and the proximity to the hotel, but it wasn't "all that". Firefly was AWESOME. It is on Dartmouth and literally twenty yards maybe from a mall entrance (so you aren't outside for very long if you walk through the mall). I had Pumpkin Lasagna (!), my daughter had the special (ravioli---very good), and the steak was good as well. I enjoyed that restaurant a lot. Easy to get to, quick, efficient and good service. JP Licks was endured since we walking Newbury Street and just had to stop in for some odd flavored ice creams (we just had to). We had gelato in Quincy Market, and of course we ate many cannoli's in Mike's Pastry. We also gave in to one other chain and had cheesecake in bed from the Cheesecake Factory. I hope this helps a bit...email me with any questions. I have enjoyed reading Trip Advisor and hope to be able to help others, like I have been helped along the way from other reviews!

“It is well-located, friendly staff, but the room was really cold” The hotel is only three minutes walk from the Foggy Bottom metro stop. The lobby is very small, and there was a nice reception from the front desk. The elevator was slow, and the room was a small suite with three little rooms and lots of tight corners. Free warm cookie, bowl of apples at the front desk, free internet as an Honors member... It was spacious compared to most DC hotel rooms, of course, but for a Doubletree Suites it was oddly configured. It had everything you need; 2 TVs, fridge, lightly-equipped kitchen, living room, BR, very small bathroom. The most outstanding feature was how cold it was, though. It was really cold outside, and the room had no heat on when I went in. It never warmed up. The floors and furniture were freezing and stayed that way most of the night. It was as if it had not had heat on for days and had not been rented out... all adding up to getting colder and not heating up well at all. By the time I realized it was not getting warmer it was too late and I just went to bed to keep my feet off the cold floor. I guess this is a situation/weather-dependent issue, but it has really colored my stay. Ask for a pre-heated room!

“Consider for times square location” Close to times square and billed as boutique but still small rooms, small lobby and passageways so not much room to enjoy any public areas. We booked on hot-wire and for one night was ok but for longer you need more room

“Great Overnight Stop, even if driving” I would suppose that most reviews of this hotel are by folks coming to El Paso by way of the airport. I think this was the closest hotel to the airport, and is just a bit off of I-10 if that is your mode of travel. Nevertheless, we sought it out due to the Trip Advisor rating and also its reasonable price. Getting there by car, you are going to go past it and have to make a 180, just count on it. The entrance to the hotel is not in front of the hotel. It is off a backage road behind the hotel that can be accessed at the first traffic light south (east?) away from the airport side of the hotel. It will make more sense in the morning. The hotel was very clean. Our fourth floor hallway even smelled nice and new. The room was generous, having a full couch & coffee table in the suite section, which was separated from the bedroom section by a bar with overhead cabinets. The lower section of the bar has a mini-fridge in it, and the upper cabinet section has the microwave. The TV was a flat screened CRT type TV perched on the top of the armoire (or however you spell furniture piece that you hang clothes in). Clean & functional bathroom was fine. Down in the lobby was a business center that looked to be in very good shape, equipment and furniture-wise. Two airline pilots were using it when we checked in fairly late at night. Next to the single elevator was the breakfast room. Breakfast featured pre-fabbed omlettes, good bacon, pour-your-own waffles, and all the usual Continental cuisine. The wife noted that the juice dispenser also included cranberry as well as orange and apple, but the omlettes could really stand some picante sauce. There was a morning wreck on I-10 that was all over the news, and a doctor who was staying there gave us directions on going over the mountain on Loop 375 to make an end run around the congestion. Good job, doc. We didn't go in the pool or weight room, but they have all that stuff. About the only thing I found wrong was a lack of an ice machine on our floor (the 4th). Some places that you fall in to while making marathon drives across these United States can only be tolerated for a night. Others are nice enough where you would consider staying longer if your business warranted it. This is one of those places.

“Great spot” The hotel was centrally located, and easily visible as I came out of the Grand (Red Line) station, although I don't recommend using this station if you have lots of luggage. The room was spotlessly clean, and the temperature was comfortable despite the incredible heat and humidity outside. The fridge, microwave and coffee maker in the room were handy, and the lap desk made using my laptop in bed comfortable. The breakfast was plentiful, although I didn't try any of the hot options, and would have liked a few more cereal choices. While there were renovations going on, I was never disturbed by the noise or mess. There is a firestation next door, and I did hear sirens during the night (from the 11th floor) but it didn't bother me enough to go ask for the earplugs available from the front desk. My only complaint at all is that, at 8:15 in the morning, I heard what I thought was a knock at the door. As I was walking across the room to check, there was a second knock while the housekeeper was simultaneously opening the door to come in to clean. While I know I could have hung the Do Not Disturb sign, I have never had this experience in the hundred or so hotels I have visited in my lifetime. I wasn't checking out that day, so there was no need for my room to be cleaned that early. Who dispatches housekeepers at 8:00 a.m.? and if they do, surely they recognize that people may be sleeping or in the shower and need more than one quick knock before you let yourself in the room.

“Once Again A Great Hotel” I stayed at this hotel for a week on business. This is the third time I have stayed here and the first time since it changed from a Ramada property. This hotel continues to be an excellent value. The internet (free) works well and the free hot breakfast is very nice. The breakfast is served in an actual restaurant with plenty of room to sit and relax, unlike most hotels were there is never room to sit. The hotel is not in the best area, but then there really is no best area of Hollywood. While I didn't have a problem walking around, some people who are not used to large cities may be uncomfortable. It is in a good location as far as being centrally located and close to the Hollywood freeway. However, if you don't know L.A. be aware the traffic can be terrible; be prepared to spend lots of time in traffic if you have to travel during the rush hours. They do charge $18 a day for parking but have a large secured lot so you don't have to worry about your car. The rooms are nice and room service does a good job. If there is anything to complain about I guess it is slow elevators but that really is not a big deal. I had no problem with the front desk staff as other reviewers have, but then I only dealt with them to check in and check out. If you get a chance check out the Alcove Bakery (1929 Hillhurst). They serve breakfast, lunch and dinner and have wonderful desserts. It is close by (not within walking distance) and has great outdoor heated seating. Overall this is THE place to stay, in less you want to stay at a five star hotel and shell out several hundered dollars a night in Hollywood.

“Some good and some bad.” Checked in without any trouble. Room was ready earlier in the day and the front desk staff was helpful, polite and prompt. They assisted with directions and tips for navigating the area, and their information made getting in and out of the hotel much easier. The problem was the lack of maintenance! The elevators were horribly slow, and one even had a sticker noting a violation. Waited for over 30 minutes to up and down, and there are NO stairs which lead to the main lobby. There was extraordinarily poor lighting, signage and directions to anything within the hotel. The room looked like it had not been thoroughly cleaned, and there was a noticeable smell of mildew everywhere, which even in a swampy climate like Houston was strong enough to be annoying. On top of this, the furniture looked it was picked up in a second hand shop, endured the hurricanes and then sold in a garage sale to the hotel. Unfortunately, the appalling physical condition of the hotel cannot overcome its great staff. This hotel needs to find the balance between offering a good facility with good service--and it has plenty of the latter but little of the former.

“Wonderful hotel!” This hotel is conveniently located along Wacker and is close to a few subway stops. Depending on the room you get (we got 1804), you can get gorgeous views of Lake Michigan. When we arrived at 12pm, staff were friendly and we got our room straight away. There are two elevators that cater the higher levels, so be prepared to wait a while if there is a lot of traffic. The room itself was standard; clean, not particularly spacious, shower only, working TV, toiletries, coffee and free internet. The queen bed was comfortable. For $100, it wasn't a bad deal.

“over night for business” Beautiful property! Front desk staff could be a bit warmer. Love the rooms and how beautifully they are furnished, Clean, quiet, pretty good hotel sleep for NYC. The location is also very convenient, right at the edge of Times Square.

“Typical Stay at the Hilton” I stayed here for 2 nights for a large firm meeting. I have stayed here numerous times in the past. While this hotel is large, with every amenity there, including restaurants, bar, starbucks and alot of meeting space - I just do not like the location. I prefer River North Gold Coast when I am there as opposed to this loop location that is really south on south Michigan. There are far better places to stay that are more in walking distance to things that alot of people want to go, with the exception of Field Museum, Shedds and the Art Institute, you could walk to those places. The rooms are quirky - some are just a very small king bed and bath. Others, double bed, 2 baths and huge - the hotel is very old so all the rooms vary in size and location. Dont be afraid to ask for a different room as they vary alot. Also - this hotel has ALOT of meetings - it is a very large and busy place. If you dont like that - dont stay here. Everything else is what you would expect from a Hilton. They do have self park here for 10 dollars less than valet - very easy with elevators and safe. Runners - you are right across the street from Grant park so that is good - and art enthusiasts can walk to to Art Institute. But Mag Mile shopping, great restaurants, River North/Gold Coast ,even the theatre district - a little too far to walk in heels (or even flats - depending on how much and often you walk). There is a great famous blues bar behind the Hilton - check it out - it wont disappoint if you like blues music. Food there is just ok - Kitty Osheas bar does often have live music - fun

“Affordable, comfortable place to stay on LA's westside.” I've stayed at the Royal Palace in Westwood on 3 occasions (interviews at UCLA Health Center, when looking for places to live, and during a recent apartment renovation). It's located in the Westwood Village, about 2 minutes south (walking) of the UCLA hospital and campus. I've stayed (and put up guests) in places that cost 4x as much in the area (most do) and they have been no-more satisfied that when I put them up here at the Royal Palace. Not sure the name is appropriate -- it's pretty basic with no frills. Still, it's clean, close and affordable (it's hard to find a hotel for less than 200/night on the Westside of LA). The area is pretty safe but petty theft is not uncommon (LA's a big city) -- the university feel of Westwood can be deceiving. I felt safe enough to send my wife here when she came out to interview by herself. I've put my parents up here as well when they visited. Rooms are generally small, but no smaller than business hotels in big cities like Chicago, Beijing, etc. Carpet is old but clean. Beds are not huge or memorably comfortable, but are kept clean. I've had rooms with brand new showers and rooms with older but functional bathrooms. Most rooms have a balcony. Noise is minimal, surprising given the area. Parking is a pain - spaces are tight and many are blocked in (leave keys upfront if you are the blocker). It's a good place if you don't need to move your car around. Breakfast is basic but served early. Cereal, toast, milk, juice, fruit, bagels, coffee, Newspapers, etc. TVs in room along with soap & shampoo. Towels were clean and adequate. Staff is very friendly - especially the guy at night -- gave us several local eating establishments to which we continue to frequent! Upgraded me to a suite at the regular room rate for 6 nights last time - very considerate. Again, it ain't the Ritz or Hilton. Not a honeymoon spot, resort, or place to impress your friends. Just a clean, quiet enough location perfect for UCLA business/interviews at a great price. Sadly, it's about the same that someone would pay in rent (per night) for a 3 bedroom apartment in Westwood. I would return (and have).

“Great if you like inconvenience” First room was not ready for a guest - pillows were strewn about the room without pillow cases. Second room was on 14th floor which is a wind tunnel with excessive noise coming from the a/c units in the hallways which are audible in the rooms. 3rd room had a great view of the roof of the porte cochere. I had to wait forever to get the final room as its very difficult to get anyone to answer the phones. I was not given an apology for the issues with the rooms and no attempts were made to "make it up to me." I was treated like a problem and not a guest. The hotel is poorly run, the rugs are dirty in the common areas. Management is clearly out to lunch. Find another place to stay.

“Lives up to the hype...and more” The architecture and decor throughout the lobby and restaurant/bar are truly excellent. It's not just a modern space, which can often feel cold. This place somehow manages to feel modern and chic yet warm and classic. The white and almost cave-like ceilings in the bar leading to the Pump Room are warmly lit and make for a great place to have drinks. The staff is also very unpretentious and friendly. At the other bar, the high, deep brown ceilings are inviting and a great place to enjoy the scene while the DJ keeps the tempo up. I found a great rate during a week when the rest of the town was booked. As for the basics, service was great, check in was a breeze and they did not give me a hard time when I needed a late check out. The Pump Room is exceptional. Try the tuna tartare, flatbreads, or salmon carpaccio. We tried about 10 items on the menu and they were all great. I really only have good things to say and I will definitely stay again in the near future.
