“Very solid hotel for families” We stayed in the Embassy Suites at the Philadelphia airport for 5 nights. The room was the typical two room Embassy Suite suite, but seemed even larger. There really was a lot of room. There are two new flat screen HDTVs, one in each room, and they get HD channels. Parking was free and the breakfast was great. However, it must be noted that the hotel is very loud. You can hear almost everything going on in the atrium from the living room. It is better in the bedroom. Also, we didn't get housekeeping to clean our room once because we had the do not disturb sign up the first time they came through and we specifically asked housekeeping to come back later and they did not on several occasions. Also, make sure you know that this draws the typical Embassy clientele: families. Overall, I was pleased. Especially with the $99 rate.

“Perfect central location-better than avg hotel” I stayed at this hotel at the end of October and would suggest it to others because of its location and value. We walked everywhere from this hotel and thought it was perfect for its central location. We did not eat at the restaurant but stopped in the bar a few nights which was quite nice with very good bartenders. On the downside, and its been mentioned in other reviews, the elevators are very slow during peak times and the walls are paper thin. The shower in the room next door sounds like its in your room. The room size is very good and the amenities are average. The bay view rooms are beautiful.

“Preisgünstiges Motel Nähe Civic Center” Wenn man einmal von den etwas in die Jahre gekommenen Treppenaufgängen, den altersschwachen Aufzügen und der beengten Rezeption absieht, ist dieses Motel keine schlechte Wahl. Mein Zimmer war geräumig und alles machte einen ordentlichen Eindruck. Es war frisch renoviert und komplett ausgestattet mit Fernseher, Kühlschrank, Mikrowelle, Kaffeemaschine, Bügeleisen und Bügelbrett. Das Frühstück ist minimalistisch. Neben Kaffee und Saft gibt es nur Kuchenteilchen. In etwa 15 Minuten erreicht man zu Fuß Stationen der Muni- und der Bart-Nahverkehrszüge. Meine Bekannten warnten mich allerdings, hier abends oder nachts alleine in den Nebenstraßen herumzulaufen, die belebtere Van Ness sei o.k..

“Elegant and Charming Old Hotel” The suites and rooms are gorgeous, with marble baths and gold fixtures. Beds are wonderfully comfortable, service is impeccable! Tea is served with a Harpist at a great spot above the entrance where tourists and visitors alike display a lovely fashion show un beknownst to them. It is elegant. Peacock Alley has the best Sunday Brunch that flows into the main Lobby. The food is divine, the ambiance fabulous. The beef Wellington superb as are the many other sumptuous choices. This Hotel has it all. Great location too.
“過不足ない設備と温かいサービス” 設備的にもカビなものはなく、けして華やかなホテルとは言えませんが、 清潔でスタッフの対応もフレンドリー。一回のカフェレストランもなかなかちゃんとしていて、 ホテルでゆっくり過ごしたい人にはお勧め。 ミートパッキングエリアまで至近距離ながら、ホテルの周りまではごくごく静かで落ち着けます。 ギャラリー巡りをされる方にも好立地です。

“Our Port in the Storm” The best way I can describe our wonderful experience is to include the contents of a letter I wrote to Bill Marriott, CEO: Dear Mr. Marriott: The purpose of this letter is to sing the praises of your staff at the Courtyard by Marriott on East 92nd Street in New York. When our plans for “Hurricane Irene” weekend changed at the last minute, we found our wonderful port in the storm at this hotel. Not only did we get a lovely room, exactly the size and type we needed, we were also told that normal checkout notices were waived; whenever we got a flight out of town, we were free to check out with no penalties or extra night charges. As we now know, Manhattan was spared the worst of the storm, but prior to that, your staff remained cool, calm, and collected. On Sunday, August 28, when the subways and buses were shut down, we received a notice stating that normal housekeeping would not be available. But I have to say, nothing seemed to skip a beat. We were provided plenty of clean towels and all amenities we needed. The front desk staff members were all courteous and responsive; they even stored my milk in the employee refrigerator and brought it out for me each morning. The restaurant on Saturday night, while slammed with people, kept churning out food and smiles. I know this is exactly the kind of service your brand stands for, and I want you to know that the Upper East Side Courtyard by Marriott did you proud!

“Location, Location, Location” We attended the 2011 Solar Decathlon, September 28-October 2, 2011 and stayed at this property. It is above the Metro station by the same name. When you get off the Metro be sure to look for signs to the hotel or the promenade. It is walking distance to many of the DC tourist sites and government venues. It is also walking distance to the Washington SW Waterfront restaurants, fish markets, marinas, excursion boats, etc. Good deals on breakfast buffet with room. Great breakfast buffet. Wifi did not work very well. It costs $$ extra. Not even free in lobby.
“Loved it” I took my wife and she loved it!! The Intercontinental hotels are always a cut above the rest!!!

“Business Travel and Meetings” Spent a week here for business in late September. Used the meeting rooms and ate all breakfast and lunches here, as well as one formal dinner. Meeting rooms were too cold, but guest rooms were fine. Nice clean rooms, pretty standard Hilton rooms. Staff was pleasant and helpful including food service, front desk and maid service. Food had variety, was appropriate temperature and was ready on time. I agree with previous review that coffee and internet should be available at no additional charge for these room rates. Location is very convenient. Shopping and dining is within walking distance. This was helpful for our large group to go to restaurants for dinner without buses. Overall nice facility and we will be back.

“Non-descript” This hotel is about as plain Jane as it gets. My room, obtained on Priceline, was in the Hilton Honors floor. There was a comfortable, king-sized bed in a large room. A section of Lake Michigan was visible through the window. But there was nothing of interest in the room, and the bathroom was plain. I tried to open a cabinet and the whole door came off. The lobby was also of no interest. Check-in was pleasant, although a woman who could have just walked in off the street interrupted us to ask for cookies. She got three, I only got one!

“I wish I could give this hotel 6 Stars!” I have stayed at the Ritz in DC for the last three years for a conference I attend each spring. I swear, each year is better than the next! The concierge, front desk and all employees learn your name within moments of your check in, and it feels more like you are staying at a friend's home than a large hotel chain! Our room (Standard, king bed, 5th floor) was perfect! Spotless, incredibly clean bathroom, amazingly luxurious bed linens and robes, and well stocked with (free) bottled water! When we needed a cab, there was one within moments, suggestions for lunch? reservations were made immediately. Room service breakfast? DELICIOUS and there exactly on time! I do not have anything but great things to say about this hotel. The location is fabulous, the staff is amazing, the food is wonderful, all in all - it is worth every penny!

“Best hotel/price near Graceland !” Only $34 for this renovated hotel and it worth more .... The reception when you entry is great and you feel immediatly good and say.... waoww ! Deco and new paints on walls are made with good taste, bedrooms are spacious and very clean. The bathroom is correct, no more. just miss a bed cover and the wifi is terrible... but you can use it with patience ! For my price, no breakfast inclused but complementary and we did : $6 / pers and you eat really a great buffet well served ( sauçages, bacon, egg , fruits, ... ) . Just turn left at the lights and you're on the Elvis Presley Bld.... 2 min later in car and you are !!!! Best choice in town !!! Rock & Roll yours.

“First Class Hotel in Times Square” I've stayed in a lot of hotels in NY, and this is among the best. Good sized room, clean, great bed & pillows, well-designed and large bathroom, professional and courteous staff. The decor of the rooms and hotel is modern but warm. It has a hip restaurant run by celebrity chef Todd English, and the food was excellent. The guest rooms come with computers to access the internet or other on-line services. The location is a block from the heart of Times Square. I will definitely return the next time I need to stay in the Times Square area.

“nice enough” This was my second stay at this hotel. Last time, I was in tower 1 where the room and bathroom were spacious. This time, I was in tower 3 where the room was very small. The bathroom was tiny, and didn't even have room for a vanity except for the space above the toilet which was awkward to access...very claustrophobic, and I am a size 0. Also, the bathroom had double doors which had about an inch of space between where the 2 doors met. This didn't allow much privacy, and I was traveling with my teenage son. The bathroom lighting...I know those flourescent bulbs save energy, but I looked like a zombie. Had to do my makeup at the desk which was also difficult because of trying to lean way over in the mirror. Apparently, the hotel was full, or I would have asked for a larger room. Also, what's up with charging for internet access? Be prepared, as the lobby is crowded and noisy. I had a drink at the hotel bar which was nice. However, there are so many beautiful hotels in SF, that I ventured out with a friend to find a bar with more ambience. Try the bar at the Sir Francis Drake for the outstanding architecture. My son is now attending college in SF, so I may stay at this hotel again. Next time I will definitely ask for a larger room when I make my reservation.

“Perfect location, Pet Friendly and Comfortable!” My husband and I stayed at the Onyx for our anniversary. We chose the Onyx because they are pet friendly and the price and location was perfect for us. I booked a Penthouse room for Memorial Weekend and got a great deal (by Boston standards) at $230 a night. When we arrived, there was a cute sign with a bowl and dog biscuits welcoming our dogs. Check in was prompt and to our surprise they offered us 2 rooms for the price of 1! They had some open rooms for the weekend and since we brought our 2 Great Danes with us, they figured we could use the extra space. We were thrilled. The room we reserved was clean and comfortable. The bed was plush and we got a great sleep. Since I had put in my reservation that it was our anniversary, they left us a complimentary bottle of champagne and chocolates which was a nice treat! The second room, which we got complimentary, had a pull out sofa bed (no regular bed). The room was large, with a little seating area, a sink and bathroom. I’m not sure I’d want to stay in this room but it was great for our dogs. The staff was very helpful. They offered us maps and asked if we needed recommendations – we didn’t take them up on these things though since we’re quite familiar with Boston. I also called down to request bowls because we forgot to pack ours and they promptly brought us two. The location is great. We walked the dogs all over the city. The hotel is within 5 minutes of Faneuil Hall, the North End, and Beacon Hill. Any major attraction can be easily reached by the North Station or Haymarket T stops. We would definitely stay here again. Between the great service, perfect location and the fact that it’s pet friendly, it was a great weekend getaway for us.

“LOVED this hotel” This is a really cool, trendy (and pet friendly) hotel in Dupont. In walking distance of plenty of things to do. I booked a suite for my birthday. It wasnt ready when I arrived by the person at the front desk (they have names of celebrities on their name tags and this guy looked like Omar Epps) checked me into another room so that I could rest until mine was ready. Very nice. THEN he brought me a bottle of champagne and wrote a nice note, and came up about an hour later to personally take me and my belongings to my room. You HAVE to get a room with a spa tub. They are so nice. The bathtub in the suite opens up and you can look directly into the bedroom. Room service was not so great. The steak came with no steak knife. TWICE. Pain. We had to call back down and wait for them to bring one. Once, they only brought settings for on person. PAIN. We had to call back down and wait again. The buffalo wings tasted like someone accidentally poured the entire salt container on them. HOWEVER, upon telling the hotel of my experience...They refunded ALL of the room service charges for my entire stay! LOVE LOVE LOVE this hotel.

“Wonderful Thanksgiving Gathering” My husband and I stayed at the Four Seasons along with 18 other family members ranging in age from 9 to 99 literally. Staff was most gracious, lobby bar terrific(try the lemon-basil mojito!), free coffee in the front desk area every morning until about 9 or 930, beds 100% fantastic, location can't be beat. Lovely walking trails along Lady Bird Lake and viewing spots for the bats each dusk March-November. Thanksgiving buffet delicious, but expensive-$75 per adult. No self-parking-overnight valet $16/night. Internet in room $11 per 24 hour period. In no way an inexpensive trip, but the quality and standards for everything was very high. Great stay. Easy walk to PF Chang's, Iron Works BBQ, Shoreline and Moonshine plus many more eateries. Joe's or the Radisson nearby choices for less expensive breakfast options(oatmeal at Four Seasons $11.50)

“Hotel central mais bruyant correspond à un hotel 1 étoile pas plus.” Recommandé par le guide du routard, mais en fait décevant à plusieurs titres, si on vous donne une chambre coté rue c'est l'enfer ! aucune isolation ni double vitrage, chambre plus que sommaire, literie qui à vu du monde avec un sommier troué sur le coté... Bon bref, je ne comprend pas que le guide du routard le recommande, pas de petit dej non plus, l'ascenceur à plus de 3 personnes faut pas le prendre! , acceuil moyen aussi... seul interêt sa situation, mais en cherchant un peu mieux et pour quelques dollards de plus on doit trouver certainement bien mieux.

“Trendy hotel in an excellent location” We stayed here on a two night stop on our way to Hawai'i in January. This hotel was very trendy and clean. We arrived late on a Friday night and departed on Sunday. Our goal was to tour the city for the day and we walked everywhere from the hotel. Pike Place Market is about 7 or 8 blocks from the hotel and the convention center is 1 block away. Check out the crepe stand underneath the convention center overhang right by the hotel - the bananas foster crepe was to die for. We ate at a pizza place highly recommended by friends (and afterwards on the Food Network) called Serious Pie. If you're a pizza lover, check that out. Otherwise, just plan on eating as much seafood as possible at Pike Place, along with Beecher's Flagship mac and cheese right by the market. We fell in love with this city and the hotel was a great place to come back in the evenings and relax. The free breakfast and full kitchenette where we could store our leftovers definitely didn't hurt.

“Good but not great” My friend and I stayed here Dec. 2011 for a weekend. In short, it's just ok. The lobby is very small and you check yourself in and out. They had a guy there to take your luggage but that's about it. Nobody helps you in and out the doors, there's no real concierge, and nobody to help you hail a taxi if you have your hands full. We arrived very early and they kept our bags for free while we went out and about. We could have checked in early for an extra $30. The room itself was very small with a double bed. The bathroom is also very small and the sliding door doesn't connect to anything at the bottom, so you don't get very much privacy in the bathroom. We didn't have an iron in our room and had to ask twice for one to be delivered to our room. The bed was pretty hard but we were so tired that we didn't notice much. There's a desk in the room and free wi-fi, which we didn't use. You have to go to the ice machine on the 2nd floor to get an ice bucket but nobody tells you that. We discovered it on our own. They do offer free bottled water on every other floor. They heavily advertise the Terrace bar and restaurant as a perk for both Club Quarters and the Jewel, which is 2 doors down and a sister hotel. However, on our first night, we were told the bar was closed for a private party. The second night, a Saturday, the bar closed at 10 pm. So, it's not much of an amenity if you just want to have a night cap. The hotel is across the street from Rockefeller Center and on the same block as Radio City, so it's in a convenient spot if that's what you're looking for. Upon checking out, we found that they had charged us $15 a day for an extra person. We booked the room initially for 2 people. We were told when we checked out that the room we booked was for 1 person only. At $279/nt and with an extra person fee and an early check-in charge, this hotel seems to be milking travelers. There are better deals and better hotels to be had in Midtown West. Earlier this year I stayed at the Royalton and loved it. I still recommend it over Club Quarters.

“Great location. Comfortable stay” 1. The bad We had a handicapped room on 3rd floor. The shower would flood most of the bathroom floor after one use. WiFi fee (Apple store is an easy walk for free WiFi) Parking $36/day, No other nearby alternatives. Also with valet only, I tipped every time someone got the car (I guessed this was expected) Wet bar items very expensive 2. The good Beautiful facility with very attractive public spaces Nice pool and health club Nice restaurant and bar Staff was very courteous and helpful Valet parking has in and out priviledges. Our car was available in minutes. Very clean rooms Comfortable rooms with balconies. Very comfortable bed. Room near elevator was quiet. Never heard elevator. One free bottled water supplied daily. Extra bottled water very expensive but labeled with price. Newspapers available in lobby/restaurant Some free coffee and tea in room. Large flat screen TV Excellent location in Century City. Walking distance to mall and restaurants. Bus stops at mall.

“Nice but VERY expensive” I picked this hotel as I was working in the Empire State Building and it was the cheapest (upscale) hotel in the area. I stayed in Room 1202 for 2 nights, a room with 1 King Bed with no view. I requested no view because the room would be much quieter as West 35th is a very busy street. The room was clean and the bathroom was nice and the room was a good size as well. I am a Hilton Gold member so I was able to check-in online which made check-in seamless at the hotel. This was the first Hilton Garden Inn that I had stayed at with the Evolution bed and I was very impressed. Definitely much better than the Sleep Number from Radisson. The location is good but I felt I paid too much. There must have been a special event in New York because I paid $479 but I couldn't find anything cheaper except for the Hampton Inn right next door, but this is nicer. I would rather stay at the Hilton Club next time, as it is a nicer place.

“Good but nowhere near A+” The rooms are larger than average NYC hotel rooms. The bathrooms are industrial chic with good water pressure. There is nowhere to work out, no fitness center. Internet access $9.95 a day one would think it would be included. The restaurant renovations did not make arrival asthetically pleasing. I asked for FOAM pillows three times one to the houskeeper on floor who brought me more feather pillows, maybe didn't understand English? I asked front desk and got no response. The doormen were polite & offered good service. Hotel loaned me an umbrella on two different occaisions. Beds comfortable. The view from the 16th floor observation deck is fantastic, though my room had a view of a brick wall. The location is right on for Upper West side attractions, restaurants and museums. Easy access to public transportation or taxi. This hotel surpasses the Beacon and Belleclaire hotels though I expected more given the star rating, etc..

“Really nice” I had a lovely stay at the Westin. The nicest thing about my room was how quiet it was, and I was able to have a really good sleep. The staff members were very nice, esp. the valet. Two complaints: I always got lost going to my room. Signage could be better. The other was the price of using a computer in the business center. It's outrageous that you have to pay for that. It seems every hotel in America allows you to have free access to a computer so you can check your e-mail. Not this hotel!

“Permission to raid the mini bar - "Yes, please!"” From the moment we checked in, I was reminded why Kimpton is my favorite hotel chain - so much personality and so many personal touches! Being loyalty club members, we received an unexpected perk to raid the mini bar, along with unlimited internet access. The hotel is perfectly located and convenient to all major attractions. With "L" access just around the corner, you can easily get anywhere you want to go. In fact, we even took the train to/from the airport...easy-peasy! A nice respite after a packed day of sightseeing was the daily wine hour from 5-6pm. In addition to offering the usual red and white wine selections and yummy canapés, they are offering a refreshing summer watermelon and basil sangria this summer. They also provide complimentary starbucks coffee & tea in the morning. Every time you return to the hotel, you’re greeted by the doorman and reception with a sincere, ‘Welcome back.” And thanks to the Hotel Monaco’s staff and all of the numerous little touches, I'll keep coming back to Kimpton hotels over and over again.

“a bit too warm” I recently spent seven nights at the Hyatt in Baltimore on business. I arrived at 2:15 in the morning as my flight had been delayed. Lets just say the graveyard front desk staff is there at that hour for a reason. She was not horrible, but she was not friendly, had her shoes off and was chewing gum. There was NO smile on her face the entire time. As for the room... it was nice but the room was warm. The temperature shows that it goes down to 60... it does not. It only goes to 70. I had someone come to my room... and he tried everything he could to get it to work properly... but I am sure the Hyatt has them set not to go below 70 to save money. They want you to think you can set it at 60 but the room will be 70 degrees. The room was also VERY dry. Take some chap stick and lotion! As on the positive side, the rooms were nice. The shower was great. The bed was comfortable. The gym, is one of the best gyms at a hotel that is a chain and not a luxury hotel. It was very close to the convention center. I might stay here again... if the temperature in my room could have been cooler and not so dry I would have enjoyed the hotel... I was just a bit too warm and super dry the entire trip.

“Join Select Guest for Free Internet” If staying at an Omni Hotel, even if you plan no further stays at Omni's, it is to your advantage to go online before your stay to join their Omni Select Guest program. You get free in-room Internet, both wireless and wired if you prefer (saves you $9.95/day). You also get a free 0.5L bottle of Evian water your first night, free morning beverages each morning (if you request coffee, you get a big pitcher full), free clothes pressing, and 500 airline miles per stay. I think I got a better room as well (19th floor view of bay). Things I liked: in-room safe was large enough to hold my laptop computer, room had DVD player on TV and CD player on radio (plus radio had input for my mp3 player), Wolfgang Puck coffee and Earl Grey tea furnished with in-room coffee maker, 2-line cordless phones, outside window actually opens a bit, floor to ceiling windows, electric trolley goes right by hotel, and you can print your airline boarding pass for free in the business center (go up escalator from lobby and turn right - on business center PC's it says there is a charge, but if you look on the very bottom of the screen there is a button to click for free access to airline sites for printing your boarding pass). Things I did not like: in addition to the nice electric trolley cars on the tracks outside your windows there are long freight trains going by - blowing their horns as early as 4AM and as late as 11PM - beware if you are a light sleeper, I requested that towels not be changed and TV not be left on after turn-down service but they did it anyway, and they failed to provide my complementary beverages on my last morning.

“Nice Location, excellente breakfast, so so beds” Ideally located with very attentive staff. Room was fair priced, it included excellent breakfast. Rooms are very spacious, but beds are a bit uncomfortable. Hotel has Airport shuttle, and to other places within a 3 mile radious.

“Downtown style” I loved this hotel. Great location, rooms, and style. I did get it on priceline so I can't comment on the value of normal rates. Hotel also had small indoor pool which I didn't expect at all in a downtown high rise.

“Nice Place...” This is a very nice Westin. The rooms are in good shape and spacious. Hotel's attached to the mall, so there are plenty of eating options without ever going outside. I'll say only two things that were a little disappointing (but probably won't keep me from staying here again): (1) Given that it's not an inexpensive place to stay, I found it odd that they charge a $5.00/box "package receipt" fee when you ship a FedEx box here for an event you're having here... when you're spending several thousand dollars on their ballroom, this really comes across as nickel-and-diming so why risk the ill-will it causes for 5 bucks? (2) The room I had on the 5th floor had a window that looked out over a hallway leading to a meeting room... it's odd not to be able to look out a window, even if you're looking at an air conditioner like a number of Marriott rooms I've been in recently. At least, maybe they shouldn't put their SPG frequent-stayers in such rooms?

“First trip to Los Angeles, CA” My husband and I went to LA to visit his sister and see the city. We got a good deal off of Travelocity. When we first got there we were upset that we booked what we thought was a king executive room and it turned out not to be what we thought we booked. It wasn't Beverly Garland's fault but Travelocity since there was a difference in the wording. The staff at this hotel offered us to stay in the suite we wanted for a good deal (it would have cost us alot more to upgrade). They kept insisting they wanted us to be happy. The room was beautiful and very large. I must say they have very honest housekeeping staff. I put out money for a tip and they didn't touch it. I finally had to put a note that said "Tip" for them to take it. The pool wasn't heated but the whirlpool was nice. They have generous pool hours. This isn't a Holiday in express so no free breakfast. Tula's was a bit expensive but we just went there for coffee and dessert. The dessert and coffee was amazing!! The hotel is located right by the freeway and a block away from Studio City. My sister in law said that is where all the celebrities tend to live or hang out. There is a free shuttle to take you to Universal Studio City Walk. Parking is about $15 a night but the front staff asked if we wanted to sign up for their Holiday Inn reward card and got $3 off of parking a night just for signing up. The beds are comfortable and we had a delightful time staying there. We would stay again the next time we are in LA.

“Amazing Staff, Awesome Location!” This is the funkiest, coolest hotel in NW D.C. as far as I'm concerned. Very 60s mod with a 'strictly kitschy' atmosphere. Dog friendly, perfect location, large rooms, great happy hour, nice outdoor bar area - All good! (I'd heard complaints that the Helix was a noisy party hotel but we saw no indictor of that. We expressed our concern at check-in and Tam - a real customer service pro, as are all staff here - laughed as she put us on the top floor and shared that the hotel has a zero tolerance rule for partiers.) The Helix is in the center of a lovely residential block that is surrounded by the lively activity of P Street and 14th St NW. DuPont Circle is only a few minutes walk away. The huge guestroom windows must be double insulated because there was no street noise even though we could see 14th from our room just a 1/2 block away. FYI, the hotel is a bit worn in spots but it's clean, welcoming and very bright and cheerful. Someone else paid for our week-long stay so I can't speak to the value but I can say that we will absolutely return to the Helix and are already really looking forward to it!

“Very convenient location” Stayed here for 3 nights while attending a conference at the Hynes Convention Center. It is very convenient if you are attending a conference there since they are connected together. You never have to go outside, which was perfect for me since it was very cold when I was there! The best thing about the hotel is its convenience. You are connected to the Hynes Convention Center as well as the Prudential Building and its shops and also Copley Place via a covered walkway. Newbury Street is also only a short walk away with all its shops and restaurants. There is also access to a T (subway) station via the Prudential Building. The hotel room itself was a little tight. I'm only 4'11" and I could barely move around in the bathroom! To top it off, the bathroom floor was slightly raised higher than the floor of the room so I either tripped over that little step or stubbed my toe b/c I forgot about that difference in the floor. Room service was fast and the food was good. There's a Starbucks in the lobby, as well as a bar and a restaurant. In the lobby, they also have several computers with free Internet access and near the Concierge desk there is a computer where you can print out your boarding pass. My only complaint is that there is no soundproofing through the door. You can hear anyone walking down the hallway, especially the loud ones.

“Stylish, Nice Location” We stayed here for one night post-cruise. It's pretty much your typical W with candles in the lobby, dark halls and a bustling bar scene. Interestingly, there also seemed to be a lot of families with members ranging from 5 to 70. I'm noting this because a lot of times the W crowd seems more "adult" and in town for business or pleasure. The rooms were comfortable and large with great views and comfy window seats, bathrooms were very large and I loved the Bliss bath products. Would have liked to stay longer and will probably book another stay next time we're in Seattle if I can get past the fact there's no coffee pot. Pet peeve is hotel rooms with no coffee pots, but that's becoming more the norm (sadly) and The W is following that trend. That being said, I didn't ask for one and it's possible they might have provided one upon request. Overall, it was a very nice hotel.

“Very Nice Hotel” We stayed at the Doubletree for 2 nights while in town to see a Texas Longhorn Football game. It is a very pretty hotel with lots of character. The inner courtyard is beautiful with fountains and tables. There was a small wedding reception going on while we were there. The beds were comfortable and had lots of pillows. We loved the chocolate chip cookies that you get at check-in. The lobby area was very pretty and big with several sitting areas, and a tiny gift shop. We enjoyed our stay and it was convenient to downtown Austin and the stadium. My only complaint was that there was not a mini refrig in the room. I guess we are spoiled since most hotels seem to have them.

“Fun fresh decor” Was looking for a hotel in downtown Dallas, near Baylor, and this hotel looked like an interesting option. The room decor had a very beachy feel in yellow, blue and white colors on the furniture, walls and bedding. There was a separate living room area with two couches and a large work desk, a separate bedroom and a bathroom - the bathroom had a separate vanity area and shower/toilet room, which I liked - I hate having to practically straddle the toilet to get at the bathroom counter or tub faucet in some smaller bathrooms. The room was very comfortable, although somewhat dark since the windows faced the interior of the middle of the buliding and didn't let in much light, but since I'm only in a hotel room in the evening, guess daylight doesn't much matter. The lobby is spacious and bright. They offer valet parking, as well as a shuttle that travels within a 3-mile radius of the hotel - it was great for getting back and forth to Baylor University Medical Center. Would definitely stay here again if visiting the downtown Dallas area.

“Great Hotel in a good location” I stayed here on business for 2 days last week. The reception area is nice and there is a Michael Jordan restaurant, which is always pretty decent. Staff were friendly and the rooms large, with more luxury items than some IC hotels ie bath robes. In room safe/TV/internet. Good beds. Location also good. The hotel is spread out a little, so cant be sure of all rooms. But overall have to say it was good.
“Great location” Great classic hotel in the heart of the Magnificent Mile shopping area. Older style, but clean and would definitely recommend.

“A Windy Long Weekend in San Fran” My wife and I stayed four nights at the Serrano Hotel in San Francisco from January 3 to 7, 2008. We had never stayed at the Serrano Hotel before, but since it is part of the Kimpton boutique hotel chain that my wife and I enjoy, we thought that we'd give it a try. I booked our King Deluxe room via the Kimpton website for $126 per night (plus tax), a rate that I thought was very reasonable for downtown San Francisco. We arrived Thursday night at 10 pm during the worst winter storm of the season (our flight from Canada was delayed 3 hours due to the storm conditions in San Francisco). Unfortunately, after a long trip getting to San Francisco, we did not get the warm Serrano Hotel welcome advertised on many web pages and websites. Don't get me wrong, everyone was decent to us, but there was no offer of a game of 21 to upgrade our room (as mentioned in the bedside book in our room), and the concierge desk person was less than enthusiastic when I asked about any half-decent places to eat on a late Thursday evening in the immediate area (we had missed dinner due to the flight delay). Speaking of the immediate area around the Serrano Hotel, it is less than "upscale." In fact, the neighbourhood, despite being only two blocks from Union Square and kitty-korner to the San Francisco Hilton, is what one might call "Transitional." That is, by day the neighbourhood is okay, but come darkness, the streets are taken over by homeless people and panhandlers. Furthermore, the streets in the area are very dark, lacking sufficient municipal street lighting. Some people may find the idea of walking alone at night too scary to try... As for the Serrano Hotel itself, it is a three star property (based on the five star scale). Some websites refer to it as a four star property, but it is not! The lobby is nice and clean, with a feeling of the roaring 20s. Our room, a King Deluxe, was also clean and contained the blessed Kimpton King Size bed (there are no "Tall Rooms" at the Serrano Hotel). As always, we had excellent sleeps in the Kimpton bed, but our room was extremely small with a very plain and basic bathroom. We can only hope that one-day the Kimpton people will hear about flat screen Plasma and LCD television, and start installing 42 inch sets into their hotel rooms instead of the small 20 year old television sets they currently utilize. Other than our first night when we enquired about a local place to eat, we found the staff to be quite friendly, with many staff members going out of their way to say "hello" to us or to ask if we needed help with anything. The various concierge staff were excellent at arranging dinner reservations and taxis for us, while the cleaning staff did an excellent job of keeping our room clean and tidy. Overall, we rate our Serrano Hotel experience as okay, but not quite what we have come to expect from Kimpton properties. If one "must" stay in the Union Square area, then the Sir Francis Drake, also a Kimpton property, would be a much better choice. But our favorite Kimpton San Francisco area hotel remains The Argonaut Hotel at the corner of Jefferson and Hyde on Fisherman's Wharf. For just a few dollars more, The Argonaut Hotel is in a far superior class to the Serrano Hotel, and at The Argonaut Hotel you get the bonus of staying in an area of town that is fun, safe and filled with excellent tourist and eating options.

“Fast & Efficient” Check in took 10 seconds. Room was spotless overlooking Ground Zero. Pool opens at 5:30am, but closes at 9:45pm. They charge for internet, what a dinosaur thing to do. They should just tweak the room rate and let us get online without a hassle. if you park in the area, due to ongoing construction which have eliminated some outdoor garages in the neighborhood , so other than paying $55 for valet park, try the Battery Park Garage a few blocks south right on West St for $35.

“A lot of room for improvement.” Hi, I normally stay at their other property, the Westin Galleria, but the rates on this one were particular cheaper for the dates we were going and since we were booking 2 rooms for 3 nights, it made sense to give it a try. The bathtub seemed very bad maintained, the enamel or the paint was coming off, not really nice looking for a "white" bathtub. We were in room 1503. We could not find any electricity plugs for our phones to leave them charging on the night stands by the bed. Neither side had them. Probably the Westin Galleria does not have them either because the room furniture seemed the same. And something that perhaps is more personal than anything else, they have not opened the Shuker's sports bar that was by the exit to the galleria shopping center. It has been closed for more than a year or perhaps even longer and when I asked someone from the hotel staff they told us that apparently there were not any plans to have it opened again. Too bad. It made an excellent spot to have a beer and some snacks while waiting for someone to come down from their room or if you are not the shopping kind, wait for the shoppers while watching a game and sipping a cold one. One good thing that I noticed different compared with the Westin Galleria was the new elevator system installed at the Westin Oaks. Never had to wait or got into a crowded elevator with many people inside and making a lot of stops. I do no know if it was because normally the other Westin is more crowded or just the time of year but I think that kind of office like system, helps a lot.

“Great location and illy espresso!” Villa Florence was worth every penny. I really enjoyed my one night stay and wish it could have been longer. The bed alone is worth it. There are some hotels where I really feel like hanging out not leaving, this is one of those hotels. The lobby is abuzz with energy and people. Wonderful illy espresso and bar in the lobby as well as a pretty decent restaurant (I found it overpriced for the quality of food that was offered, I would go someplace else next time). Customer service was stellar. Found this hotel via Rooms Tonight app on the iphone and am so pleased that I went with this option.

“nice hotel, walking distance to Chinatown & Metro” I stayed here recently for work. The hotel room was clean, with a comfortable bed, flat-screen TV, and Aveda toiletries. It would have been preferred to have free wireless internet in the hotel rooms and the conference/meeting rooms, as it was free in the lobby area. The gym was more spacious than normal hotel gyms - lots of cardio and weight equipment. The hotel was within walking distance to Chinatown and the Metro, and lots of shopping and restaurants within a 5-minute walk. The staff were cordial but not overly friendly or willing to go the extra mile for you. I felt like they were going through the motions. I would recommend it again if you were attending a conference nearby, but as for overall Washington D.C. travel, I don't think it's location is near all of the sights.

“Faded glory -- sad!! ” Had stayed at this hotel 20 years ago in it's prime and it was exceptional. Hotel is still ok, but more along the lines of an older Comfort Inn or LaQuinta. Nothing special about it. Service was fine, and lobby was attractive, but the rest of the place (both interior & exterior) in major need of renovations. Rooms are huge, but ceiling stained from leaks and sunlight shines thru holes in drapes. Public areas - pool, elevators, breakfast area -- all in major need of deep cleaning! I'm not saying this is a bad place, and had I paid $79 I would have been happy, but at $119, very disappointed. Fitness center has 1 bike, 1 treadmill and 1 elliptical. This is it for an 8 story hotel. Everything kind of haphazardly plugged in thru use of variety of extension cords. Was an electrical nightmare waiting to happen in the fitness center! Sad thing is, repairs needed are more cosmetic than anything. New paint and a deep cleaning would do wonders for the place. Sad that it's being left to just "fade away".

“Great location, comfortable bed, but a little disappointed” My husband and I stayed here June 3-5, 2009 and were disappointed with several things. The room was much smaller than we anticipated, bathtub/shower had a lot of rust in it, and the furniture was aweful. Now the bed was VERY comfortable and I slept like a baby. We stayed here back in 2001 and we had a fabulous room and it was a great stay. I just think with this being a very busy hotel they are just letting the age of their rooms show. The location is fantastic and the view from our room had a 180 degree view of time square, but I just don't think we would stay here again. The housekeeping was lacking also. Happy Traveling!! :)

“The BEST for Chicago and Michigan Avenue” Once a year a dear friend and I have a long weekend getaway to Chicago. We have stayed here and theredowntown, up north, out in the burbs, but our recent stay at the Sofitel was absolute the best weve had. Guest service is most important, but so is décor, ambience, the little details that travelers remember. For example: the valets new our names by the second day, night saw the lobby illuminated with soft lights and many beautiful burning candles, our bathroom had a fresh flower in it every day (and the bathroom was a palace!), an Ethernet cable was delivered instantly to the room when I needed one for my Mac, and so much more. Get this: there is a speaker in the bathroom so you can here the TV while getting ready. The beds were a dreamsoft sheets, duvets and a feather bed. Do not miss the Sofitel for your trip to downtown Chicago. David and I loved it!!! (i actually spoke to the manager to paraise the staff...)

“Just Great!” This was an amazing place to stay! the location is great, rooms are big and clean, staff was very helpful and it is a pretty cheap option to stay in the middle of Hollywood (two steps away from the Kodak theater). It also has parking. There was nothing bad in the hotel, if i had to point a minus it would be breakfast, cause it really isn't so, it was a little table with croissants and bagels with nothing but Philadelphia chesse to spread on, and plain coffee (no milk or cream). I believe there was also orange juice but we never got to taste it cause there never was any left when we went down. But it is ok to start the day so you go out with empty stomach. Also there is no elevator, we didn’t care but we saw some older couples and solo travelers with bunch of luggage having a bad time (no bellboy of course) I would definitely stay here again!

“Excellent location and Unique Rooms” The Dana has an entrance on street level that takes you into the restaurant. You take an elevator or stairs to the reception area where you are greeted by warm front desk staff. The only strange thing for me was they stay seated at a desk to check you in; it isn't the normal front desk experience. I had a great room overlooking the city on a high floor. The room was spacious with a corner sofa and very comfortable bed. There was a very wide selection of local snacks and drinks in the room. The room I was in had a shower and my little pet peeve is no full door on the shower, but I got over it because there was a waterfall showerhead that more than made up for it and the water was extra hot. There was also a teak bench, and that is always great when you need to prop your foot to shave your legs. The hotel was quiet and the dark hallways were warm without feeling closed in. I stopped for a drink at the bar and found it very well stocked with great wines. It is a few blocks from Michigan Avenue and walking distance to many fantastic Chicago attractions. I didn't have time to visit the spa but heard from other guests it was excellent.

“Too big, too impersonal” It is a very grand hotel but my concerns are the size (way too big) and lack of service. On the size front, the hotel is so large that I literally go lost on three occasions trying to find my room. It's like being in one of those huge Vegas hotels On the service front, let me be clear that I'm not one of those whiny folks that needs to be attended to all the time. From the car valet to getting a few towels at the pool for my kids everything took way long - like 15 minutes. To top it off my kids pancakes arrived at breakfast burned. If you are going to position yourself as a high end resort you have to provide a base level of service.

“Another Kimpton gem” Overall the general appearance of the hotel is not as modern and happening as other Kimpton proerties in New York. It was obviously a make over of an existing hotel. The lobby is small and not as cool as others. However, the rooms are great. Very nicely decorated and rather roomy for New York. The service is what you would expect from Kimpton, professional and always top notch. Was quiet and not bothered by frequent door slamming as occurs in other hotels. The location was pretty decent. Trying to get a cab was a bit more challenging than other hotels stayed at. it was close enought to Grand Central you could walk and catch a subway. I still prefer Ink48 for personal visits as I have more time and not as concerned with the location and having to be on a schedule. For business, i would stay here given its cental location.

“OK choice near the airport” We've stayed in Embassy Suites in a number of different cities, and this one is just OK. Website says the hotel has been recently redone, although the interior was not as nice as in other Embassy Suites we've seen. Rooms were quiet and comfortable, but plumbing and bathroom fixtures were cranky. Front desk personnel were friendly but not very knowledgeable about the vicinity of the hotel and provided inaccurate directions to a nearby attraction. As other reviewers have stated, the pool is small and can get crowded. The eating area for the complimentary breakfast also was smallish, having to share space with the regular restaurant/bar.

“Good Hotel, Fair Price, But a Few Quirks” I found the Palomar by just doing an internet search and comparing prices. I'd never stayed there, and I was a bit nervous booking at a place that was the lowest-priced. But indeed, it is quite a nice facility, new and a stylish. It's got a great location on Dupont Circle, the heart of Washington, so it's easy to get to the metro station and dozens of restaurants, bars, shops, bookstores, etc. The room was on the small side, but quite new and well-furnished. Free wireless internet in every room. On the other hand, I can't give it an A+, because it has a few disappointments: 1. the restaurant is quite good but doesn't serve breakfast. You must either order from room service or go out of the hotel. 2. the front desk staff I dealt with were efficient but stony faced. Not downright unfriendly, but they were reciting their material by rote and never looked me in the eye or gave me a smile. 3. the room service menu is odd. You can get a sandwich from 11am to 5pm and from 11pm to 5am, but not at dinner time. I called down for a sandwich and argued for 10 minutes with a man who insisted that there is a rule against making a sandwich for a guest at 8pm. I guess he wanted me to have something more expensive. He finally had to talk to a manager and the grudgingly sent me a sandwich. Odd. This needs to be fixed. Give the guests what they want, we're paying for it. No hotel staff should have the word "no" in their vocabulary. And they should be especially helpful considering that sandwich and a beer cost me $28 (when you include the $3 "delivery fee", the tax, and the mandatory 19% "gratuity"). Overall, a pretty good hotel, but it needs a few tweaks.

“Good value, Shuttle was very handy” I was in town for business and saw the positive reviews for this hotel on Trip Advisor. While the location was a little out of the way for where my business meeting was downtown, it was very conveniently located to the Galleria as well as some nice restaurants. Since I did not have a car, I found the shuttle to be a very handy way to navigate the local area. I also was quite impressed with the value. The room was nicely appointed and clean. The staff were very helpful and friendly. I would definitely stay at this hotel again the next time I'm in Houston.

“Elegant hotel but awful service.” As a Marriott Gold Elite member, I have grown very fond of the JW Marriott brand. I have also come to expect exceptional service from Marriott's elite brand. The hotel's decor and furnishings are elegant. Indeed, the fixtures in my room reminded me of those I've seen at several Ritz-Carlton hotels. The bed was super-comfortable (as is true at most Marriott properties) and the bathroom was spacious, clean, and elegantly appointed. The gym was bigger than most hotel gyms but nevertheless lacked some basic equipment. The major downside with the hotel was the service. The first incident had to do with having my room cleaned. When I left at 7:30 am one morning I kindly requested to have my room cleaned early. "No problem" I was told. When I returned at 3 pm I found that the room had not been cleaned although it seemed that (most) other rooms on the floor had been! I went downstairs and asked to speak to a manager. The manager was sincerely apologetic and quickly sent a housekeeper to take care of the room. The second (and more disturbing) incident happened two days after my departure. Marriott properties typically email receipts ("portfolios") to elite members a day after checkout. When I didn't receive mine I called the hotel. Usually the hotel will offer to email a copy ASAP. Well, the person who answered my call essentially told me "Too bad" and gave me the brush off. She might have been the rudest person that I've ever encountered at a Marriott property over several decades! I called back and spoke to (another) manager who was again apologetic. I hope that the hotel takes care of this problem because poor service is enough to keep me (and other loyal Marriott customers) from returning.

“Lovely hotel but location is very quiet on weekends...” I stayed here over Martin Luther King weekend having secured an excellent rate on hotelpronto.com. The downtown area is almost dead on a weekend however, with just a couple of cafes open (along with the hotel eateries). However the Disney concert hall is close by, as is the Museum of Modern Art and both have places to eat lunch. Parking is expensive but nearby are large car parks with a reasonably low daily fee; however if you'll be coming and going more than 2 or 3 times then the hvalet . Don't park in the California Plaza car park unless you want to pay over $30 per day! The rooms and hotel are excellent - very big rooms and huge bathroom with walk in shower and bathtub. I don't think I would stay here again largely because of the dead weekend location. However if you're after a dirty weekend away - it's perfect!

“Nice rooms in ok area” I stayed here five nights for a conference. The hotel personel was very nice and helpful. The rooms are large and clean, the bathroom is slightly outdated but still very clean. The food that they served during breakfast and lunch was of very good quality. There are quite a lot of good quality restaurants within walking distance for dinner if you like. The only drawback was that I had a connecting room, which always is a bit more noisy.

“Best Location on the Mag Mile” I have stayed at the PH Chicago several times, but most recently, in June of 2011. The location of this hotel is probably the best in Chicago if you are going up there for shopping. One of my favorite stores/ lunch spots, RL Grill is right across the street! The check in desk ladies were incredibly friendly and helpful in the morning, but the 'night duty' people were down right rude at times! The concierge staff were all very helpful too! The bar is always a great place to meet friends for a quick drink, and for people watching! The spa/gym is beautiful, but gets pretty busy during certain times of the day! We were upgraded to a higher floor level upon check in (always a nice surprise), and the room was lovely! Very clean, bathrooms were brand new, and the bedding/linens were absolutely heavenly!

“大きなショッピングモール内にある穴場ホテル” 南シアトルにある巨大ショッピングモールに隣接するホテルで、空港〜も無料のシャトルバスが利用できます。ダブルツリーは昔から、到着した客に対して、暖かいチョコレートチップが入ったクッキーが無料で配られます。このクッキーとホットコーヒーは本当に美味しいです。部屋は昔ながらのタイプで、プールやジャグジーもあり、ホテル内で食事するよりも、ショッピングモール内で食事できますので、超お薦めです。サウスセンターモールは、市内や郊外から市バスが集まってくるので、タコマやベルビューへも乗換なしで、しかも必ず座って乗車できます。この地区は、ボーイングの工場が2つあるのでホテルが多い地区です。

“A lovely hotel” The SpringHill Suites is a lovely hotel. All of the staff were friendly and helpful. The lobby was very large, with coffee always available. Check-in was quick and efficient. The room was large, with a seperate sofa area and desk. The beds were very comfortable, and the room had a second TV over the beds, with a good selection of digital channels. There was not much of a view, though, although I could see the Ravens stadium in the distance. The hotel is situated only a few blocks from the Inner Harbor. As with anywhere in Baltimore, there were a few people hanging around on the streets a couple of blocks away, but it's fine as long as you are sensible. The breakfast buffet was very good. There was a lot to choose from. Cereal, oatmeal, fruit salad, bagels, hot items, waffle iron, bread. This is a very good hotel.

“Heaven on Earth!” I am a VERY frequent business traveler. Hands down...this is one of the top 3 BEST hotels I have ever stayed at during my business travels (list includes Ritz, Four Seasons & JW Marriott). First-rate accommodations and service: check-in, room, amenities, room design, etc (I can watch The Today Show during my shower thanks to a flat panel in bathroom!). All top shelf!! Apparently, Conrad Hilton wasn't only smart in disinheriting Paris...he knows a thing or two on how to run an immaculate, first rate, top shelf hotel as well (before this, I was wondering why Hilton was still such a big hotel chain). Staff: 1st rate in all respects - clearly they have employed those who take this job very seriously and know how to deliver. First time in Indy (fantastic city!) but I will be seeking out the Conrad brand for future stays in this and other cities (Gold Hilton member but didn't know about Conrad brand of hotels, sadly). Although I know I'm in a hotel, I really feel as if I'm at home, which is a huge plus for the frequent business traveler. Absolutely ZERO complaints (one minor warning - directions on hotel website from airport to hotel are wrong....call for directions). I hate to leave tomorrow. This place has been incredible. Already looking forward to my next say here!!!

“Great New Hotel” Stayed here for one night just before departing San Francisco for the drive down to LA,Booked a Junior Suite and was in room 2020. I was impressed with the corner location,a fabulous comfy King Size bed,the large HD TV ,the size of the room and very good bathroom facilities. Good Views from the corner room over to AT&T park and Bay Bridge and not far to walk to the shops at Union square Used the Club room facility for free Internet use Ate breakfast in the morning at the restaurant and thought my particular waiter was not up to scratch, bill was wrong and service was slow.At this standard of hotel you should not keep having to ask for things.Food was ok but I had eaten a lot better for less money around union square Loved the Room, the lobby staff and door staff were very pleasant and made a great first impression. The Hotel car to the airport was also good value compared to Taxi's. Would stay again at the Hotel if i could get similar good weekend rate

“It's Just Fine!” I stayed at this property for 2 nights in December while in town on business. Due to weather concerns I wanted to stay close to the airport and not mess with a rental car. As it snowed everyday, this was a good call. It took 45 minutes for the hotel shuttle to arrive at the airport, but the shuttle driver claimed that it was traffic related and not typical. I also took the shuttle back to the airport which left timely. Check in was easy, and the front desk called me a cab twice. Actually, the cabs were town cars which were comfortable, but more expensive than a standard cab would have been. An extra $5 bucks or so just isn't a big deal. I paid about $75.00 per night, which was a bargain. The room was nice enough, and it had a good movie system which I took advantage of nightly. The Irish pub was also nice and friendly. One down side is that there is nothing around the hotel so if you need to go to a store, you'll be calling the town car! It's not the Four Seasons, but it was clean, friendly, and $75.00! It's hard to find anything to complain about.

“Lovely lobby, average rooms” The historic lobby and common areas are stunning. Make sure you take some time to look around and up at all the nice details. Workers were carefully cleaning the period ceilings on my visit. But it would be nice if someone did the same for the rooms, which are worn down. Good bed, but furniture and carpets are pretty beaten up. Bathrooms are unexpectedly tiny and lack shelf space, necessitating morning contortions to get ready. Annoying for one person, downright frustrating for two trying to get ready at the same time. Staffers I met were friendly, helpful folks, but there don't seem to be many of them at the ready, which could make things difficult during busy times. Didn't get a chance to try the food or drink there, though the bar looks inviting. I'll stop in next time to enjoy the atmosphere. But I'll look for a different place in downtown LA to sleep.

“A good esperience” Clean, safe, very friendly staff and a good price compared with other hotels in Washington in the same category. The neighborhood is not the best at all, but inside the campus you're safe. Since I always rent a car when in Washington, what happens around the hotel doesn't bother me. They provide a shuttle service to Union Station (metro) and there's another station close to the hotel (NY Avenue-Gallaudet U). There's free parking for the guests, but is a little distant from the hotel what can be a problem in rainy days (or with snow). If you are planning to arrive late, be sure to eat before come back to the hotel, because the restaurant closes at 9:30 pm and after this hour you'll need to eat at the Academic Center where anyone can imagine the quality.

“Acceptable but not three star caliber...” Obtained reservation at Holiday Inn Historic District in Philly via Priceline. Location at 4th and Arch Streets would be convenient if the visitor is interested in sightseeing around the historic area and Olde Town. However, if visitor’s business is at the convention center or University City area, this location will be out of the way. Hotel building itself is bland and boring, no “charm”. Ample lobby area. Front desk staff fast, efficient, informative, helpful, polite, and accommodated a request for a so-called quiet room away from the elevator and ice machine. Reasonably swift elevator service. Window in a sixth floor room provided only a drab view of 4th Street. Room was nicely made up; housekeeper did okay job with one exception (see below re shower curtain). Bedding and furnishings in the room and appointments in bathroom were satisfactory but definitely a notch below some of the other three star Priceline hotels in Philly (Hilton Garden Inn, Crowne Plaza, Wyndham, and Club Quarters). Furniture dark and old, looked about ten years out of style. No mini-fridge or microwave. Heating system functioned well but was noisy. Free internet access in the guest room. Decent cable TV signal/reception and choice of channels. Ice machine on the floor was out of order and a large area of mildew on the shower curtain were minor complaints. Big annoyance was the thin wall between the adjoining guest room - loud boisterous foreign speakers next door made a big racket until after midnight. Overall, the Holiday Inn Historic District was an only average Priceline deal and its three star Priceline rating raises the question of just how much better this typical Holiday Inn could be than the Priceline 2.5 star hotels in Philly (Marriott Courtyard and Hampton Inn)...

“Lovely, excellent service, great "loyalty manager"” Stayed here for five nights on business. Room was nice, not huge but certain sufficient and spotless. Great maid service (they always seemed to find the right time to get in and clean). Loyalty manager helped with a question prior to check in and when there was an issue with my bill after checkout, took care of that immediately as well. Great service, beautiful place. As others have noted, being a Select member is great -- getting free wifi is a real benefit. Omni is an excellent chain.

“Reality check...” I stayed for four nights in this hotel during the two days before Christmas, plus Christmas Eve and Christmas Day -- in order to see friends and visit family in the area. First the merits of the place: Its location just a half mile from Century City along Pico, and at the southern edge of Beverly Hills, makes it easy to get into the Valley via Beverly Glen, or to jump down to the I-10 to go further afield. The rooms are as comfortable as in most Residence Inns (though they're smaller), and the valet parking system is fast and cheerful. Now for the drawbacks: (1) Most rooms face busy streets, and inner "courtyard" facing rooms on lower floors receive noise from HVAC equipment -- only courtyard-facing rooms on high floors are dependably quiet, and that's not many rooms; (2) The breakfast area and service in this Residence Inn is an unmitigated disaster: Horribly mediocre food that runs out if the hotel is near capacity, a tiny dining space for a hotel of this size, and service that has to be reminded to replace the coffee when it's run out. Also, while the reception staff and valet parkers are pleasant, this hotel has a rather detached atmosphere. The only compelling reasons to stay in this hotel are the reasonable rates given its location, and the reasonably comfortable rooms if you get one that's quiet. But generally you will not want to be spending time in this building.

“Absolute luxury and stellar service!” I have had the pleasure of staying at The Michelangelo 4x this past year. The location is fabulous--bustling, great restaurants nearby yet the high quality windows block out almost all external noise. This hotel is truly a gem. I have stayed in many 5-Star properties but the Michelangelo blows them away because of their customer service and thoughtful ammenities. The Doormen are very welcoming. The front desk staff are friendly, efficient, and *every single time* did their best to find me a free upgrade without me even asking. They keep copious records of my room preferences and go out of their way to offer my 'favorite room' when I arrive. The lounge is small but elegant and conveniently located with delicious drinks at a very reasonable NYC price. Room services is very good and fair for NYC prices. The bedding is luxurious and honestly provides me with some of the best nights sleep I've ever gotten. The most impressive thing of all to me may sound trivial, but it's the care that goes into the turn down service. *Without asking*, I return to a room that is playing beautiful classical music at a peaceful, unintrusive volume, a bucket full of ice, a lovely chocolate at my bedside, and a weather forecast so that I can plan my next day accordingly. Individually these may seem like little things but they really meant a lot to me and made me feel very welcome. I'm happy to see that this hotel continues to invest in these little creature comforts because it truly keeps me coming back and recommending this hotel to my colleagues and clients. Well done.

“Nice hotel!” Very clean, good location. Upon check in we requested a quiet room. Our room faced a construction site and when we requested a quieter room we were given an upgrade.The staff was very accommodating. We will definitely return.

“LOVED the Mariott!” I was in Phoenix for a conference that was being held at the Mariott Phoenix Airport and decided for ease to stay there as well...great decision! I was picked up by the free courtesy shuttle within about 20 minutes of landing. Check-in was a breeze. I stayed on the 6th floor and somehow ended up with one of the rooms that had a balcony which was a bonus! The room itself was extremely spacious and comfy. In addition to the super plush bed there was a work station desk and a chair for reading. The bathroom was extremely clean and stocked with shampoo, conditioner, lotion, and mouthwash. During my stay, the front desk provided me with a razor and shaving cream since you can't carry on easily. I ate in the restaurant once each for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Breakfast was yummy with your usual breakfast buffet including omelet station. Lunch was a little overpriced for a limited buffet. Dinner was pricey, but the meal was excellent. I also did room service which is the same menu as the restaurant. Due to a mix-up/miscommunication, my room service was comped which was much appreciated. Check-out was a breeze and I easily caught the shuttle back to the airport. My experience at the Mariott Phoenix was great and I would recommend it to anybody!

“Hotel precioso. Ubicación genial.” Estubimos en este hotel en una escapada relámpago para visitar la ciudad. El hotel es precioso. La habitación amplia, el baño también muy amplio, de estilo antiguo. La cama impresionante de grande y cómoda. El ascensor es una reliquia, pero tampoco supone un gran problema. La ubicación es ideal. Se puede ir andando a Georgetown donde es muy recomendable cenar. También está a un paseo de la Casa Blanca y del Mall. Muy recomendable.

“Good value in a great location.....with reservations.” The price for a "suite" at this hotel is very reasonable. When I stayed there in August on a business trip it was chock full of vacationing families as good evidence that pricing and location were very attractive. But it is also a hotel that tries too hard to do too much. The rooms are all suites but only because a wall was put up to create two very small rooms. The bathroom was adequate but nothing special. The amenities were those you would expect from a chain hotel. There are better choices in the Chicago hotel market.

“Out dated, but a good value” This hotel is located away from the city centre, but only a few minutes away by car. The hotel is dated and looking a bit old, but it has charm. Breakfast is free and provided in a large dining hall, but there's no restaurant at the hotel. The hotel is affordable and the rooms are large, but they look out-dated... Staff are friendly and helpful
“Great Hotel great locaion” Enjoyed our stay there. perfectly located, great Hotel In a perfect location. Clean and rooms were well set up. I would stay there again if going to Seatle.

“Hilton Hotels - Argh!” I have stayed here in the past, prior to reviewing here on Tripadvisor so here is the review of HIlton Memphis. The Good - Locaiton is perfect for me, Target right across the way, Best Buy and Sports Authority being put in there, down the road tons of things to eat, shop or hang. Gym in hotel rocks, fully equipped and modern. The "not so good" - Dated, it was a long time ago and still is, I am being told it is being slated to remodeled. The lobby is nice but rooms are a bit dated and carpets, hallways etc need to be freshened. No club lounge, it was closed and apparently being redone. Staff is a bit rough but I am used to that being from the Northeast :) Food is ok, nothing special. Sleep Quality was poor as I just couldn't get comfy in the bed, pillows are kind of hard and mattress was not to my liking. Summary, would stay in future if it is in fact refreshed.

“Great service” Stayed two nights here. The service was excellent all around (from the doorman to the concierge). The room was very nicely appointed (modern decor, marble bathroom) and fairly large. I requested a quiet room, which they gave me (one at the end of hall). I requested a non-smoking room. I was on a floor labeled "non-smoking," but it still smelled like a smoking floor in the hallway and in the room. It wasn't too bad, though. Not the most posh hotel to stay in D.C., but definitely a very nice and swanky one.

“Nice hotel, a bit busy” I arrived at the hotel around 11AM and despite a top-tiered HHonors member, I was unable to check-in as my room is not ready until 3PM. Later in the day, I came back and a newly furnished room was ready for us. We were given vouchers for continental breakfast at the Market Place restaurant. The Hilton New York is quite a busy hotel with lots of guests check-in. The lobby sometimes feels like a zoo. Although the lifts are separated by levels, they are small and crowded at times. The twins room that we had was surprisingly large and bright. In addition to the bed lamps, we have 2 overhead bed lamps and a LED reading light per bed. The room is completed with a armchair and ottoman. The desk also have place for a 32" Phillips LCD TV with integrated Nintendo 64 game console. The twins bed are comfy if not a bit on the soft side. The bathroom is not huge but is a good size and does not feels claustrophobic like the other NY hotels. The CrabTree & Evelyn amenities are again ever present here. The Market Place restaurant breakfast is a bit pricey at $24 but if you have a Continental voucher, you can upgrade to the full breakfast for $7. If not, there is a Starbucks right inside the property. The location is not as good as the W or Westin Times Square but still it is a short walk to the premise if you like. However, it is a few blocks from Central Park so that you can get a little fresh air or have a picnic lunch. The Hilton is a good hotel if you can score one of the newly furnished room. A much better choice then the Sheraton Hotels and Towers nearby.

“Good Location” The hotel was conveniently located 2 blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. While this was an older hotel, it has been kept up well and the rooms were satisfactory. The morning Starbucks coffee in the lobby was a nice touch. I would not recommend the hotel resaurant. We ate breakfast there one day and were appalled at the slow service, rude waitstaff, and overpriced breakfast food. There are plenty of other places to eat within walking distance of the hotel. Overall, we would stay here again (just avoid the restaurant)!

“Ok stay” I stayed here for one night as I had an early flight the next morning and needed something close to the airport. This property was disappointing for the 4.5 rating it earned on this site. Room 752 was a surprisingly small king room (maybe 3-4 ft between the end of the bed and the entrance door), hairs in the tub and the complimentary shampoo was missing (I had to call housekeeping to get some--the person to whom I spoke seemed bothered that I had called). This maybe ok for a short layover but I do not recommend it for the business traveler or family of 5. As a former hotel G.M. and frequent traveler I expected more out of a 4-star Renaissance. The Hampton Inn in Cypress, CA, was less expensive, much cleaner, more spacious, more accomodating (free wireless and breakfast), and the staff seemed more genuinely interested in making sure my stay was satisfying.

“Diese Bauweise” Das Hotel ist relativ neu und liegt etwas außerhalb von SA. Im Moment finden dort viele Straßenbaumaßnahmen statt. Stau zum Hotel hin ist also möglich. Das HI liegt etwas vom Freeway entfernt. Schräg davor ist noch eine Bar. Daher ein wenig Schallreduzierung. Warum neue Häuser immer noch die Klimaanlage nach außen führen, begreife ich nicht. Dadurch hat man ein Loch in der Außenwand und der Lärm kommt in jedes Zimmer. Bescheuert!. Zudem kann man von dem Nachbarn drüber jeden Schritt hören, da wohl nur OSB Platten als Boden verlegt sind. Da hilft auch kein Teppich. Zum Glück waren die Leute sehr leise. Insgesamt war das Hotel sehr gut besucht und die Zimmer waren kleiner aber sauber.

“Very Pleasant” We stayed at the Warwick on November 6th. The room was quiet, clean, and comfortable, and the desk staff was very nice. We visit New York about nine times a year, and would definitely go back to the Warwick.

“Great Location, Clean Rooms, Friendly and Helpful Staff” After extending our trip to San Francisco by another day with no problem in changing our reservations, we arrived a little ahead of schedule and were accommodated with a room right away. We used the valet parking which was not that much more than the self park and was much cheaper than the San Francisco Hilton valet. The staff were all very professional and seemed very genuine. We received a great offer through the concierge for entrance to Universal Studios for two days for $80/ person which was a great savings and very convenient as it was across the street from the hotel and proved to be a very nice view. Our room was a large corner suite that we added a cot for our teenage daughter. We went out for a while that evening and came back to a welcoming fruit tray with trail mix and creme brule which my daughter enjoyed and was hard pressed to share with the rest of us. There was lots of storage for our belongings and a huge bathroom. We did have a couple of complaints, the first being that one of our neighbours decided to indulge marijuana that could be smelled throughout one whole wing of the floor. I did mention it to the front desk and they sent security to deal with it immediately which impressed me. The other thing that I mentioned as we were leaving was a maintenance issue, the bathtub in our suite had been resurfaced and was chipped around the drain and on the back ledge. It wasn't a huge deal, we just had showers instead of baths, and I'm sure now that they know, it will be fixed. The swimming pool area was very nice, our daughter enjoyed the pool, as we sat beside and relaxed in the cabanas, clean towels were provided on site and depending on what time of the day you were there, they had a snack bar. The concierge(s) were knowledgeable and took care of all our requests, as well as the valet staff. We had supper one evening in the Sierra dining room, the food was really good as well as the service. Housekeeping did a fantastic job, not just our room, but the hallways, elevators and entrances alike. We would definitely recommend this hotel.

“Modern but a bit plain” Our first impression of the hotel was that the building is very stylish with and was in a perfect location. The room was spotless & we liked the oversized bathroom with its rain shower. One concern we had was that the air conditioning was not quite strong enough & had some issues with it. Also, although the room was very modern, it was a little too minimal & lacked some warmth to it.

“Nice but no Four Seaons” I agree with the previous post. This is a beautiful hotel and the views are spectacular. But at this price I would prefer to stay at the Four Seasons. The MO has much smaller rooms and to me is a little too hip. Plus the service is not nearly as good as the Four Seasons. The bar was cool but we had to wait 30 minutes to get in even as a guest of the hotel. I'm gald that we stayed and were able to enjoy a breathtaking view of the city for a night but won't stay there again.

“The centre of it all in Venice, CA” The Hotel Erwin lived up to every review I read, and every good thing I'd heard about it! We were given premium treatment from the moment we pulled up to the front doors, until our departure the next day. The valet service was efficient and affordable, and the staff who greeted us at our car were very polite and helpful. At the front desk we were greeted by a friendly and gregarious gentleman, who invited us to "sing for our room" and gave a heartfelt example of how to do so. Our room was very large, light, comfortable, and beautifully and artfully decorated. Every inch of it was designed to inspire, please and captivate. It fully captured all the spirit and energy of the beach, and was a terrific addition to our visit there. This hotel is literally in the middle of everything! We were very pleased with how easy it was to reach from the highway, and how close it was to the beach, and the famous four corners in Venice. While we didn't have the time to enjoy the pool deck, I did run up to check it out, and it was every bit as lovely as I'd heard it was! On my next visit I will be sure to take full advantage of it. Our stay was part of a very special Birthday celebration, and to this day, we talk about how well this hotel complimented our experience. I would happily plan my next trip to LA around staying at the Erwin.

“ノースステーションから近いホテル” この時期のボストンはなぜかホテルが高く、いつもの出張の金額で評判の高い同じ系列のホテルが取れなかったため、こちらのホテルに5泊しました。 実際のところ、ノースステーションは全く私にとって便利なところでなかったし、周辺の治安も他のダウンタウンやコプリー周辺と比べて若干悪いように感じました。 それでもホテルのサービスは割りとよく、ヨガマットをレンタルできるサービスやフリーのWiFiサービスなどがとても便利なサービスがありました。個人的には、iPodの充電器を忘れてしまったので、iPodが接続できるスピーカーがあったのが助かりました。 ルームサービスを何度か取ったのですが、いわゆるアメリカっぽいものではなく、少しおしゃれな感じのものが出てきて、こちらはこれでまあまあよかったです。 時期が悪かったので、値段はしょうがないと思います。立地以外はとても満足なホテルでした。

“Historic Hotel” Hotel staff was very friendly. The rooms were nice and cozy. The hotel was an old gentlemans club so the decor represents the look and feel of the early 1900's. The old pictures in the room was a bit much. The hotel sits right in the middle of the tourist attractions. You can get to the Pikes Peak Market or the space needle by walking or a short cab ride. There is a great restaurant called Juno connected to the hotel. The breakfast was terrific. Downside, there isnt a indoor pool for children. The workout room is too small and there was only two treadmills, and no spa. The business center was very small as well.

“Budget Hotel, Dirty Rooms but great location” I stayed at Milford plaza for one night, and I was given a room on the 22nd floor in front of the elevators. The room was dirty, there were stains all over the carpet and the 2 single beds were very uncomfortable. I had booked a room with 2 twin beds but was not honored the room as they were full.
