I have stayed at Milford Plaza hotel in the past, and I have noticed that this hotel is increasing degrading in quality. I will reconsider staying at this hotel again in the future. On the plus side, the hotel is located in a great area, close to times square. I would recommend this hotel for people on a budget or if you just need a place to sleep. Remember the rooms can be very small at this hotel. If you need to park your car, avoid the hotel parking as it is very expensive. Try one of the local parking lots of 44th avenue for rates that are half what the hotel charges.

“Well run and dependable Hilton property.” We stayed here due to low rate over Thanksgiving, but the location across from the Mission Valley shopping was a nice plus. This is not a luxuriuous Hilton, and doesn't try to come across as such. I can see why business people stretched for time would stay here as the staff knows what it is doing and there are no surprises. The room was well kept and comfortable, furnished nicely. The lighting was good for reading, the bed was comfortable and the HVAC was quiet and worked well. Bathroom was not huge but it was clean with plenty of hot water. The business center was excellent which is unusual. The web access was speedy and the printers worked. We didnt use any of the recreational facilities. The breakfast buffet was very good and free for Honors members. The parking fee is aggravating but all the hotels in this area charge for it. There is a fancy, full service Doubletree nearby that may be more luxurious, and a Doubletree Club about a mile that is often cheaper. This is the better alternative if you can get the same or lower rate. There is no Honors floor at this hotel.

“Excellent Gem in DC!” Spent a week at the Normandy for a conference and very glad I stayed at the here. This is a nice old school boutique gem of a place right in the heart of the international embassy district. The rooms are small (as you would expect from an older building) but very well appointed. Bathroom very well decorated, marble/glass shower, contemporary sink, black marble tile floor. I checked in too early to get one of the king canopy beds but I was just as pleased with the double bed. Beds were very comfortable, room had sufficient plugs for gadget charging. There was a nice 42" flat screen (though only basic cable channels). Room also had a cuppacino machine and refrigerator. The service was excellent - everyone friendly and genuinely eager to please. As far as location, this property is a short drive from Reagan Airport and a 2-3 block walk from a host of nice restaurants, bistros, and shopping. The only drawbacks about my stay were no fitness center (actually you have complimentary access to the Courtyard Marriott about 1.5 blocks away but even that fitness center is very small with outdated equipment). Also, there is no storage for clothings. It was a good thing I ended up with the double room as I kept my travel bag on the other bed (literally living out of the suitcase). Overall, I'd choose this place again for the service, comfort, and quiet surroundings.

“Great Value/Location/Property” I stayed one night...called from the airport and booked the room. Friendly staff, very clean room, standard room perfect for solo traveler. Noise not a problem...comfortable bed and linens. Staff was prompt in delivering forgotten toiletries/iron, etc. Lobby is adjacent to Starbucks open until midnight. Would definitely return.

“Great for families” Stayed over Massachusetts' April vacation week with my husband and 2 sons (ages 7 and 4). This is the ideal hotel for families. Having a suite is key after the kids go to bed. They also loved the breakfast and evening manager's reception. I would not recommend this hotel for adults without children, though. This hotel is crawling with families--in my opinion, that's a great thing! One down side is that the closest Metro stations are a bit of a hike (Foggy Bottom or Dupont Circle). Otherwise, highly recommended!

“Don't judge the book by its cover, the main phrase here.” "Don't judge the book but its cover", the main focus of this review. When looking at the hotel outside and lobby you right away think it seems like a good place to stay. WRONG. The hotel may have a fancy looking outside, a stylish lobby and a nice website, but the rooms are small and poorly designed. My room was on the 2nd floor. Getting off the elevator (which looks like it was from 30 years ago, with a wooden door after the main metal door) you can turn to the left or right. On the right you see a nicer looking hallway with nice red carpet and doors. If you turn to the left (where my room was) you see a cheap looking hallway with old doors, 2 shared washrooms and maybe 4 or 5 regular hotel doors. (The ugly wooden ones are for the people who live in the building as permanent residents). Going into my room I saw 2 twin beds which had maybe 1 foot between them, maybe even less. A small cramped work desk with nice looking hotel branded papers and a pen (no chair though) and a little armour with a safe and some hangers. No drawers for clothes. The room was the smallest I ever saw. The view from my room was terrible, I looked out to window to see a dirty dindgy building. One of the beds was positioned up against the wall right near the air conditioner. Of course, I had to open the blinds to get the cool air to enter (it's an in-window air conditioner unit) and the air blew across my bed, making it dificult to sleep after waking up at 3am. The next morning I took my stuff and checked into the Novotel on West 52nd street where my friend was going to be staying. I had a great time at the Novotel and will never be returning to th WJ again. The only thing this hotel is good for is for people wanting to stay 1 night, have a little nap and leave. If you want a good hotel around that location, stay at the Novotel on West 52nd or the Sheraton around that area. As I returned to the hotel the first and last night I stayed there, I saw the crew of El Al (Israel Airlines) loading their baggage into a van. Maybe they didn't like it too! Pretty lousy place for a great airline crew of El Al to stay!

“Very nice” The Downtown Westin is a very nice hotel, definitely nicer than others in the area. The location is great, right on the 16th Street mall, at the start of the LoDo area. I ahve stayed in at least two other major, luxury hotels in downtown Denver, and the Westin is much nicer. Rooms are large, with high end amenities. Large, flat screen tvs, free bottled water, a great mini-bar, and comfortable seating areas. Staff was very helpful, and free wifi in the lobby worked with no difficulties. A great selection for business or pleasure trips.

“It's the cheapest hotel you will find - you may want to spend a little more” Are you checking because this is the cheapest Hilton and it seems to be in a good location? Well it is both. It is frequently the best price in the area and it is right off the Mile. So if price and location are your top priorities then stay here. If you are traveling with kids you are likely attracted to exactly those qualities - trust me you will not be alone the hotel is full of kids. I don't mind the kids - but I'd never stay here again. When I booked I reserved a king suite. I did that because I wanted a king and a work area. I'm traveling for business and I needed to work in the room. I check the Hilton zip-in check in box so that I would not be delayed. I arrived to find the hotel was a disaster. The woman at the desk was pitiful.After 10 minutes of typing into her computer she called the manager who pointed out that the system was locked up and her computer needed to be restarted. I asked about the zip in folders which at most hiltons let's you avoid this kind of issue. I was told "we don't do that here." I don't know what that means - this one hotel in the Hilton chain is rebelling against efficiency? (and if that is what they intended they are a raving success). When I finally got a room key and went to the room it was a double. I called the desk and was told the hotel had nothing but doubles. Now if you understand how Hilton's zip in system works you know immediately that this hotel must be managed by middle school dropouts. I was then told that the double room was an upgrade and I was lucky not to be charged more (???). I was later able to talk to a day shift manager who agreed that his night clerk was an idiot and he adjusted my bill. so I guess I should be happy that I didn't have to pay the premium that I had agreed to pay for a king room since I didn't get one. The room itself was a sad little affair. There were 2 double beds (not queens so if you're taller than 5'6" enjoy the dangling feet experience) plus a sofa and a dresser and a desk and a coffee table and another table. Picture a garage sale - that's what the room looked like. The space was way too small for the amount of furniture stuffed in the room. Then there was the fridge. Since they advertise a fridge in the room I guess they figured they better stick one in there. Since the room was a junkyard anyway there wasn't much worry about where to put it. So it's by the door. I mean right by the door - as in when you enter the room be careful not to trip over the fridge. Seriously - this is a pigsty of a hotel. The one bright spot was room service - the food was decent and the service was good (and since there is so much crap int he room there were lots of places to set the tray down. When I left in the morning the day shift seemed pleasant - a lot more competent that the night shift. perhaps mine was an unusual experience - but I'll never stay here again. It's Chicago for goodness sake - there are hundreds of fantastic hotels here - why in the world would you ever take a chance on this place?

“Needs serious upgrades” Let me be clear. I love Marriott properties because they are usually spotlessly clean and this was no exception. Staff attitude was also top notch, typical Marriott. But, this property needs to be upgraded to the new Courtyard standard. The old, CRT type TV was quirky and only 35 channels were offered in the room. The exercise room had a new flat panel on the wall with about 70 channels offered. Huh? Speaking of the exercise room, the TV screen on the eliptical was also quirky - couldn't turn it off or adjust the volume. The HVAC system is louder than the space shuttle launching. The toilet/tub area of the bathroom was smaller than an airplane. There was no sofa or coffee table. The desk was small. Not a fault of Marriott but the location is pretty bad. You really have to navigate the frontage roads to access and leave the hotel. This Courtyard is stuck firmly in the early 1980s in terms of comfort & decor. As I said, it's Marriott clean so that's a major plus putting it way above other choices. But, please guys, spend some capital bucks and upgrade!

“Great Hotel, Great service” Stayed three nights at the MGM Grand Detroit (there for business). My room was fantastic, the service was incredible. The workout room has everything you could need. A top-notch stay. Casino was pretty good, but too smokey (mostly played poker, has a nice poker room but mostly only one game 1-2NL, sometimes 2-5NL).

“Issues....Elite Members STAY AWAY!!!” Nice property location, but experienced several issues and finally had enough: the Concierge Lounge closed with no warning and was told by the hotel staff they did not know when it would reopen, the tub drain was broken and laying on the tub floor, the shower head was broken and was stuck on high pressure with a plastic piece dangling off the shower head, and no clean towels were left on the second day of room service. I had to call twice for clean towels to be delivered after a long day of work...first the room should have been out of service for repair versus in service and second the hotel staff needs customer service training. At the end no way to treat a long time customer and I checked out early...the only bright spot was the hotel restaurant.

“I wish I were still there now” Our whole family loved the new Hotel Monaco Philadelphia. Unfortunately, we could only stay one night before having to move to a thoroughly pedestrian hotel in Philly for a work holiday party; what a difference! Our "park queen queen" room had a totally fab decor and a great view of Independence Hall (and park) and the Liberty Bell. The staff could not be friendlier or more helpful. After 24 hours of being greeted and welcomed every time we entered the hotel, it was a stark contrast to check into a more typical hotel and get a more typically indifferent treatment. The Red Owl Restaurant looked very cool, but our family has never been in Philly together before, so we felt compelled to walk a few blocks to go out to dinner and found a great comfort food restaurant very nearby called Jones. Our kids loved our room,, with cool lamps that respond to touch, bold carpet and wallpaper patterns, and a copy of Alice in Wonderland, of which our daughter read the first few chapters. Special kudos to Rashid, the bellman, who dealt with our unusually copious luggage and tried to track down a package that Fedex failed to deliver. It was only when we (very, very reluctantly) checked out that I learned that the hotel had only been open for two months; it was such a well-oiled machine that i would have never guessed. I know exactly where i will be staying the next time i'm in Philadelphia -- definitely the Hotel Monaco.

“Why doesn't this hotel have a higher rating? It was lovely!” I stayed here about 6 months ago, while I was in Houston for a big family event. I wanted a convenient location with quiet rooms and comfortable beds. When I arrived there I was upgraded to a suite. I really wanted to feel pampered and I was. The room was very quiet (I know others had complained about the trains, but it was dead quiet) and luxurious. I had a great night's sleep. Bath amenities were the highlight - the shower had lots and lots of hot water with good water pressure, and Remede products. Lovely. The service was excellent. Room service was prompt and the food was good. We also ate breakfast in the dining room, which was good. My only complaints probably pertain to Houston in general - it was to hot/humid outside to open the windows and the air conditioning was freezing in the dining room. But I found this to be the case everywhere I went in Houston. The only downer I would concede from other reviewers is the slight slight moldy smell in the hallway, which didn't bother me at all.

“A hidden gem off Michigan” I booked a room at the Palomar, through Hotwire after I could not get a reasonable rate at the conference hotel where I was attending a meeting. The Palomar was a great surprise. A smaller, newer building means fast elevators and quiet heating a cooling, something you don’t find at a lot of older Chicago hotels. The staff was quick, courteous and knowledgeable. Rooms were slightly larger than average, with nice towels and linens, and fairly clean. Floor to ceiling windows give a decent view of Chicago. The hotel is designed for the younger crowd (OK, not me) with cool robes and a staff dressed for fun. A short walk to Michigan Avenue and the Hubbard bar district are also nice for those inclined. Room service was fast, and food was pretty good. The fitness facility was large and had a decent variety of aerobic and weight machines. A good choice in Chicago for business or pleasure

“Great Airport Hotel” It is always a flip of a coin for me when I need a hotel close to the Philly Airport between Sheraton Suites and Aloft. This time Sheraton Suites won the toss and they proved to be a great choice. Early check-in was not a problem. The room was spacious and clean. They now have a functioning restaurant. The shuttle service is timely.

“Great Location, clean rooms, nice staff” I stayed here for 11 days in August and had a pleasant stay. Certainly great value for the location. Large rooms were kept clean & the staff were mostly helpful. Breakfast was ok, the famed warm cinnamon rolls really were delicious. . would have been great if they were available for afternoon tea! Having free wi-fi was a bonus when choosing this hotel, but I found the strength and reliability so bad that I didn't bother to use the internet until I found a computer shop and bought a cheap ethernet cable to plug directly into the phone line. After that internet access was fantastic... fast and reliable. They also only have 1 washing machine and 1 drier, so get in quick :) I would definitely stay there again... value for money hotel in great spot. Close to public transport to get you anywhere you want to go (as a couple of days in the Hollywood Blvd area is quite enough).

“great hotel..but call first to see if all elevators are working” i lived in nyc for 10 years, so i can pinpoint where i want to stay perfectly. this hotel was such a good deal($112 for a double). for me, the location was perfect-we walked to and from grand central. very close to subway(which i didnt need this trip, but good to know) and a little more neighborhood feel than tourist feel. for me thats perfect. the lobby is sleek, the room was great. as far as nyc hotels go, this was def one of the nicer ones. totally updated and clean, great bathroom-not huge but one of the more spacious hotel rooms in nyc that i have been in. flat screen, great night lights, etc. again, centrally located. staff was nice. my only complaint, and its a big one, is that the elevators are being serviced. now, i checked in on a sunday at 10:30. i had to wait 15 min to get an up elevator. we were on the 7th floor(with a yucky view but we would care less). we waited 10 min for an elevator. everytime the 1 elevator and the 1 service elevator would get to our floor, it was completely packed. we had to walk down the stairs. we are both in our 30's and in shape so it was not a big deal(we were a little dizzy). however, if i were in heels or dressed to go out or if had a lot of bags-i would have been livid. we were comfy and casual so it was fine. coming home at night was fine too because most people dont go out on sunday nights, so it wasnt a "rush hour" time. that would be my only reason for not staying there again. it was quiet, clean and nice...just call to check on the elevator. if its working, then stay..if not-stay somewhere else and come back when its fixed.

“Not bad but not best in Chicago” I stayed here recently on business. The hotel is old and historic, and while I think renovations would help (lots of cheap gold fixtures), I was pleasantly surprised. Unlike a lot of reviewers, our room essentially had a view of other hotel rooms although we had a great Sears Tower view if you craned your neck a little. The closet was tiny and we had only one bathroom - the reviewers who refer to two bathrooms had an upgrade compared to my room. But we had plenty of towels, the bed was comfortable, and the room was clean. It was very quiet despite the urban location. There was a computer on the desk for no clear reason but overall the internet at the hotel was expensive, slow and unreliable. The entire hotel was huge and we thought our conference was a little scattered across all the space. The elevators were sometimes slow. The coffee shop in the lobby was often crowded so I usually went to the nearby Dunkin Donuts or Starbucks, both within 2 blocks. The food served at our meetings was average to good. It would also have been nice to be closer to the Magnificent Mile. If that's what you're going for, choose another hotel. This location is OK for the Art Museum and Grant Park. I'd highly recommend eating at Mercat a la Plancha located just across the street (in the Blackstone Hotel) - incredible tapas. Overall this is a fine hotel but I don't think you couldn't do better.

“Excellent hotel” My wife and I stayed at Hotel Monaco over the Canada Day weekend and truly enjoyed our stay. Chicago is a great city, and this hotel has 5* quality. Location is great: close to the subway, 5 minutes away from the Magnificent Mile, and 10 minutes away from the Grant Park. Our room was on the 2nd floor and I was concerned it would be noisy. However, it was very quiet and we both slept soundly. Our room was small but very comfortable and clean. I became a Facebook friend of this hotel and got a few nice freebies thrown in (e.g., continental breakfast and cocktails). Internet is free if you join Kimpton's loyalty program (it's free). Overall, great hotel. I would stay here again.

“Tolels Stadthotel mit super Lage” Wer Chicago zu Fuss erkunden will ist hier richtig. Man kommt problemlos zu allen Sehenswürdigkeiten zu Fuss und auch die Ubahn ist nur 1 Block entfernt. Das Hotel ansich ist ein typischens Courtyard. Nettes Personal, freundlich und zuvorkommend. Die Zimmer sind wie in vielen Großstädten nicht übermäßig groß aber solide ausgestattet. Die Zimmerfenster könnten besser bedämmt sein denn man hört auch in den höheren Stockwerken sehr viel Strassenlärm.

“Ruhiges Hotel in NYC” Das Ritz Carlton Battery Park ist an der Südspitze Manhattens gelegen. Aufgrund der Lage am Battery Park ist das Hotel sehr ruhig und bietet tolle Ausblicke über die Südspitze aufs Wasser. Der Bereich um das WTC, 911 Memorial etc sind in kurzer Zeit erreichbar, wer Richtung Central Park und 5th Avenue möchte sollte etwas mehr Zeit einplanen. Sehr schön sind die Zimmer, vorallem der Ausblick über das Wasser. Je nach Zimmer kann man die Freiheitsstatue sehen. Das Personal war ebenfalls sehr gut geschult und konnte gute Restauranttips geben!

“Good value for a big, loud, boring convenction hotel...” I maintain Silver status with Marriott. This was my first visit to the Wardman Park; for 4 days. The Good Stuff: DC hotels are over priced, at $90.00 per night it's a great deal. Hotel is right on the train system. Hotel public spaces are immaculate and airy. Lots of over stuffed funiture to lounge on; have a drink, chat, people watch, etc. The on-sight gym is one of the best I've ever seen and is free to registered guests. Hotel room was recently updated with Marriotts tech/plug-in package. The room was large and came with a fridge. The bad stuff: When confirming my reservation for a king room on a high floor, i was given a double/double on the 3rd floor. The front desk person was not freindly. Her only excuse for not having a king was they were sold out due to a medical convenction. What ever... Plumbing sucked on the 3rd floor. My toilet never worked properly. 7 minutes for hot water from the shower. Other guests in the elevators complained about the plumbing situation too. Room was too loud to sleep in. Outside my window was the buss loading area. Super thing walls, no sound proofing around doors. Every morning got woke up by maids pounding on my door and/or arguing in the hallway. The "do not disturb" sign nerver worked... TV reception was poor at best. The "on demand" services never worked properly. Pay per view options very limited.

“Loved this hotel” Great hotel. rooms are a bit small, but it worked fine for me. Staff was very courteous and helpful. Ate in the sports bar one time, very expensive. There is a drug store and liquor store close by if you want food, drinks for room. Restaurants within walking distance. I used the workout facilities twice and they are very nice. Clean with lots of up to date equipment. The only drawback is it is a bit of a walk to the Metro and coming back it is up hill. I rode the Metro everywhere & only used a cab one time. Highly recommend Bucca di Beppo restaurant just a block from the hotel. Would stay here again for business, but if I went with family I would stay elsewhere as the rooms are small.

“Good hotel” We stayed here at the beginning of September and were really pleased with the room and facilities. Being really picky, there were no bathrobes provided in our room. The hotel is located at the top of a very steep hill, so not ideal if you're not fit, but taxis are cheap enough (and cheaper than the cable car). We ate in Tonga restaurant in the hotel one night, and were disappointed and would not recommend it. It is a Hawaiian infusion restaurant and the food is very over-priced for what it is (USD25 for a basic stir fry). There are other hotels that are better placed down town or at Fisherman's Wharf if you want to be closer to either of those locations, but I would recommend the Fairmont as it's an iconic hotel - just avoid the restaurant and make the best use of pubic transport/taxis.

“Very happy with my stay” Although the hotel was not my choice because I traveled for business, the hotel was very nice and in a convenient location. The metro was in walking distance and there were many, many local restaurants to choose from in the area. We particularly enjoyed Ruth's Chris and went there for two nights out of our 3 day stay. The hotel pub is also nice. I dined there for lunch and had the chef salad. The hotel room was very comfortable and very quiet. The hotel is very large in size but I was located in the center tower which was not far from the lobby area. I would certainly stay at the hotel again if I am ever in the area again.

“Perfect Location and Great Value!” I was in Chicago last month for a conference and decided to stay a few extra days. I was at Swissotel for the conference, but moved to Homewood Suites for 3 nights and was very impressed with the value and convenient location. Hotel is located right off the "Magnificent Mile" and within walking distance of lots of great restaurants and fabulous stores. If you're on a budget, this is the place to stay. Breakfast is included and Monday - Thursday, a hot dinner and happy hour is provided. It's crowded in the dining room, but if you're traveling with kids, you can't beat this price and location. Service is impressive. All of the staff are very friendly and committed to making your stay enjoyable. Our room had a full kitchen, small sitting area and separate bedroom with a king bed. The sitting area is a bit small, but comfortable. There is a grocery store about 2 blocks away and I walked over to stock up on snacks and drinks. Very, very convenient! There is only one drawback. As others have commented, the elevators get crowded and you can wait quite a while going up and down. This wasn't a big deal to me, but it drove my husband nuts. We had a wonderful time and would definitely recommend this hotel to families or anyone who wants to enjoy all the attractions in Chicago without spending an arm and a leg.

“great except don't ever leave something in the room” I have spoken to 4 employees at this hotel trying to retreive a shoe I left behind. Probably under the bed. Three said they would look and call me right back. They didn't. Now security is telling me 2 days later that as long as there is a guest in the room they can't check. Apparently housekeeping isn't cleaning very well - atleast not under the beds.....I need the shoe!!! Besides this infuriating policy the hotel has great staff and does functions very well. I've been there 10 times and never had a complaint. But I never left something in the room.

“Just found my NY home!” After being to quite a few hotels in NY, I was really happy this Easter to finally find a place that has it all. I chose this place of location and the TA Reviews, and both are right on the mark. This prime Upper East place is close to Saint Patrick's, subway stations, shopping and great restaurants within a max 3 block radius. I got the smallest of rooms facing the street, and to my surprise it was not very noisy (it was weekend though), and definitely not too small, with a separate sitting area with desk. The room was well appointed, spotless clean and tended 2x a day. However, what set this place above the rest is service. All staff was amazingly friendly and helpful, from giving good advice to reserving places and helping you with anything you needed in the hotel. I never made it to the wine receptions or tea, but free breakfast was the real deal, not the pastry and coffee advertised elsewhere. Here you get a full assortment of breads, pastries, fresh fruit, coffees and tea. Though it is mostly self service, there are plenty of smiling attendants ready to prepare you a toast to get you freshly cooked eggs. It was Easter and the hotel was fully booked, and though you could hit the restaurant at rush hour the staff would quickly help to accommodate you. My last great surprise was to come back Saturday evening and find a small pouch with high quality Belgian chocolate eggs. I had no time to buy it myself, so I really appreciated the treat! I should be back in NY soon and will surely come back here or try out one of their sister properties, which are also well appreciated here in TA.

“Outstanding hotel for my layover” I reserved a night at this Courtyard for a very reasonable price, $79, and I couldn't be more pleased with the value of the hotel stay. As stated by many others previously, it is very close by the entrance of the airport. Making it a very quick return to the terminal after my night's stay. Getting to the hotel from the airport is not as efficient, since the shuttle hits the Marriott first, and must negotiate a fair amount of traffic in and around the hotels. I'd say expect a 20 minute trip from the terminals to the hotel versus just 5 minutes... hotel to terminals. I had a top floor room that was attractive, very spacious, with plenty of workspace for my laptop, lots of electric outlets, and a very comfortable bed. The room was very clean. The bath had a tub. I used the downstairs "counter" for a quick bite of dinner and grabbed a few cocktails from there, too. It's a convenient and relatively cheap option for a simple nosh... soups, sandwiches, pizza, rotisserie chicken, etc. Nothing fancy, but perfect for a quick bite on the go. The check-in/out process was very quick and efficient at this very busy hotel. It's an ideal choice for a night's layover at LAX. A word of advice on hotel rates: Marriott guarantees their website's rates. So reserve on their site for your room, and if you happen to find a better rate on another website, fill out the online claim for on Marriott's site and they will match the rate plus give you an additional 25% discount. It's pays to shop around!!!

“This is truly a first class hotel - elegant and comfortable with gracious staff.” I just spent one night here with one of my children and thought it was wonderful. We arrived very late and ordered room service which was excellent. The room was huge, the bed top of the line. The bell staff and front desk went out of their way to be helpful and gracious. We did not try the restaurant as we slept through breakfast. The decor is done in a nice classic/ antique style. I will definitely return if I get the chance. The only downside was that internet access was not included.

“Ups and Downs at the Sheraton” Hotel is clean, modern and centrally located in Dallas. We booked through Priceline for $35 on a Sunday night, paid to upgrade to a Junior Suite when we arrived and we received a room adjacent to the elevator shaft. Since the parking lot was only one-quarter full and we saw only one other guest, we did not think it to be a problem. WRONG. We heard noise from the elevators all night. If we had paid rack rate, then we would have definitely asked to be moved. No parking fee was nice.

“Second time, great stay” Returning for second time. Big shout out to Abiy at the front desk for making me feel welcome and accommodating a couple of special requests. Not much to add over my previous review, this place is great. Quiet, clean, modern style. This is a difference from the Westin St Francis, which is more well known and has its own character. For me the westin market is more my style and the rooms are way bigger. Try La Boulange on Market street for French coffee and pastries, far more interesting then the Starbucks across the street from the hotel - though definitely convenient if you need it.

“simple quality” I rented three rooms at their hotel last weekend to stay there with some friends and family. The rooms were very clean and nicely decorated. They were all very large. The staff really made an effort to take care of the guests. I was very impressed with everyone that I worked with while I was staying there. It is also in a very nice location. We will be staying there again.

“Good stay” My husband and I stayed here for two nights as part of our trip. We got a great rate on quikbook for $229 plus tax per night. Our impressions of the hotel was that it was extremely clean and our room was very large, especially by NY standards. The bed was large and extremely comfortable. Nice bathroom with good size shower. Water pressure was great. The location is brilliant, being so close to Central Station makes it very easy to get to anywhere. The only thing that we were disappointed with is that we didn't find the staff very friendly. Although the girl at check-out was pleasant, only once did a staff member greet us on entering the hotel the remainder of the time. I think part of the reason that we would pick a Fitzpatrick hotel is to have those personal touches which were lacking for us so I don't think we would stay here again.

“Nice place but not top ten in Seattle” Stayed for one night finishing up a week in the PNW. This hotel is fine and I have no complaints. However, I lived around the corner for two years while in grad school so I know the area inside and out. I love the U-District and UW but a casual tourist might be disappointed by the area. There are some good little restaurants but they cater to students so there's not going to be any fine dining close at hand. The nightlife is student oriented as well. That said, the hotel is clean, staff is helpful and friendly and it's not that far from downtown. Our room was big, although it faced the street so it was too loud to open windows. I didn't use their shuttle and it seems a bit limited in hours and destinations. If you're willing to ride a bus, you can get a lot of places pretty easily either from Roosevelt or "The Ave", which what University Way is always referred to. Call it by its real name and locals might be confused. The price was higher than the Mayflower downtown, but we'd booked pretty far in advance. I'm sure things had changed given the recession of the winter but my wife didn't want to try rebooking. Portage Bay cafe is next door and has a great breakfast. Schultzy's Sausage and Big Time Brewery on the Ave are my picks for local spots. So again nice hotel, but it is out of the way for the average tourist, and you might pay less downtown or in Belltown.

“good hotel excellent location” Free indoor parking (but limited space). elevator start from parking , Staff freindly. "Breakfast" (cookies + drink). one free internet station at the reception. Average room. We paid 422 $ for three nights (weekend). Walking distance from fisherman's wharf . 10 minutes driving to golden gate bridge. I would come back.

“Accecptable” Had a two day stay in LA. Hotel is within walking distance of Union Station. Room and bathroom was clean. On the small side but no problem. Heater/ AC worked fine. Inset of building ment you had two windows . Had some what of a view. Staff was great. We got in early morning. [ 8:00 AM ] Walked to the hotel from the station. Desk clerk was very helpful. Of course we were to early to check in. He said come back or call in about a hour..I will try to get a room ready for you. We needed to do some drugstore shopping so off we went. Called about an hour and a half later. He said come on back. [ Side note. there is an underground shopping center about six blocks east of the hotel. The Downtown Mall I think. Hard to find untill you are right on top of it. ] Desk clerk had a room for us. A great help. This hotel is used by many Amtrak passengers. Dont let the neighborhood or the facade fool you this hotel is clean and I made sure. The bathroom is one of the first places I check. This was clean. Lighting was good shower was clean and good pressure. They have a free continental breakfast. This can be a free for all. There is some seating. I got coffee and some danish and took it back to the room. It was well stocked and had a attendant. Check in and out fast. Staff very pleasant and helpful. Two nights 1 king bed $ 219.00 This hotel is on most tour pick up list. Less than a block from Olvera ST.

“Really? Not in a good way....” The hotel name sounds like an elegant old hotel. I found out it is an outdated hotel from the 60s. I was booked into this hotel by a local business that I was visiting. I had a 4:00 meeting scheduled and I arrived at the hotel at 2:50. I later found out that the hotel had doormen, not because there was anyone to open the doors when I came in. There were a group of people hanging out at the front desk some employees and their friends. After seeing me trying to approach they did eventually step aside. The front desk person starting checking lots of things on their computer and after several minutes informed me that check-in time is 3:00. It is now 2:55 ... Really? He said that there should be a room available in 15-20 minutes; I wanted to clean up after my flight and be on time for my meeting. I asked if there were any other options and asked if an upgrade was available. He said that if I paid for an upgrade that he could get me in right now. It wasn’t much, so I agreed to it. He made the comment, “I won’t be disappointed.” He was right, disappointed doesn’t begin to describe my wish to find a new hotel. As I left the front desk I noticed a large pile of newspapers. I asked if that was the Washington Post. The answer was, “yes, but I have to charge you $4.00 for it.” Ok, now I am getting a sense of the place I am staying. The hotel room was a blast from the past. It had a sitting area for the “upgrade” and a full sized stove and refrigerator as well a kitchen set up squeezed into the place. This all explains why the area for the bed was tiny. Speaking of the bed, are hotels still using cheesy polyester bedspreads that never seem to be clean? The cooling system for the room was under powered. I even tried to place the desk lamp close to the thermostat to convince the system to engage. This list could go on for pages... no feather pillows ... you get the idea. I was only staying for one night; I certainly won’t have considered a second.

“Superb views- In dire need of renovation” Checking in I felt like I have arrived at the grand old dame of Chicago. Beautiful old house - located with magnificant views of Grant Park and the Buckingham Fountain and all of Lake Michigan at your feet. However this grand old dame really needs some makeup. The rooms are fading the wall paper peeling off the walls - the beds overly soft after years of use, and the electrical installations eliciting sparks every time you plugs something in. The service is completely impersonal - no one seems to care any more , front desk, bell desk, room service - all of them seem to have lost the spark. Sorry I cant give more than a '2' for this place, I hope someone with money will soon see the potential of this place and have it properly renovated to its former glory.

“Wonderful Hotel in a Great Location” We stayed here the last night of a CA trip with the intention of going to Universal Studios for the day and heading out early the next morning to Burbank airport. The hotel lobby is attractive and the self-parking underground could not have been more convenient. The room we booked was great and had a wonderful view. Of course, the room was rather pricey, also. We were able to check-in mid-morning as our room was ready, which was great. Our plan was to go to Universal for the day, explore City Walk afterwards as well as having dinner and return to the hotel on the last scheduled shuttle at 8 pm. We were, however, told by the front desk staff that since the hotel had few guests the shuttle's last run back to the hotel would be at 4:30pm and we were told by the shuttle driver the same time, except he said it was due to it being a holiday. This was a major disappointment for us and really limited our time at the partk and City Walk. I would not have stayed here had I known that. Walking back up the hill to the hotel at night was not an option. We had been staying at an LA hotel that was just as nice as this one and had a great special. In hindsight, we should have stayed there and driven to Universal Studios. SInce we didn't want to venture out we ate in the hotel restaurant (something I try to avoid except for breakfast). The food was fair, the prices high and the service mediocre..

“Tower rooms are a big improvement - Great Location!” We hadn't stayed in the St. Francis for many years. The renovation and the tower rooms are just wonderful. Service was great and it is one of the best of the Westin properties. We wanted to slip in some shopping between other activities, and Union Square made this really easy. Plus it was pouring and being able to rush back and get out of the rain was really helpful. We had stayed in S.F. Le Meridien in the financial district/embarcadero last month and did notice that the St. Francis wasn't as well equipped or as spacious, but the location is what we needed this weekend. My only complaint about the St. Francis is the parking at $49 a night plus taxes is just ridiculous. Even the expensive hotels in S.F. are less. Guests should get a break on parking. I find I am reconsidering SPG hotels for the high charges for internet access parking which add considerably to costs. Many modern hotels have WIFI .

“Nice place to stay has a very old fashion feel” The hotel was well kept, decorated in a much earlier style (definitely has an old fashion feel) with the large chandeliers and heavy use of wall papers. Beautiful place. I ate breakfast in the restaurant twice, food was good, kind of standard fare for a hotel breakfast, nothing to brag about. Service was good. I found the hotel staff to be friendly. Overall good experience, I think I might choose a slightly smaller hotel next time. I spent two nights here and then three nights at the Topaz hotel and while the Topaz wasn't as fancy I preferred staying there. I found the pillows to be uncomfortable but I'm sure if I really cared enough I could have asked for a different set of pillows. Overall, nice hotel, excellent staff.

“Walk to Graceland” We stayed here for two nights from December 21st to the 23rd. First of all there are NO bars on the windows like the one reviewer stated. We even were able to check in at 10am too. The room was clean and modern. 24 hour Elvis movies and free continental breakfast. The staff was friendly and we never worried once about safety. The property has a metal fence around it with only one entrance and exit in the front of the hotel. No worries. This is a great place to stay for Elvis fans since you can walk across to Graceland and to all the Elvis shops. Downtown to Beale street is only about 10 minutes away.The only downside to saying here is, there aren't many decent places to eat close by and they charge you $1.00 a day for the room safe which I wasn't told about nor did I ever even see a safe in the room. People who expect to be pampered will be better off staying at the Peabody. All other's this place is fine.

“Nice stay - good service and space” Stayed for free thanks to a marriott rewards certificate. Check in and out was a breeze as was valet parking. Breakfast provided is nice, but a bit spotty - the juice was not mixing correctly and there wasn't a great amount of choice. Attached bar is nice and has a good happy hour. Excellent bloody marys. Low levels could be a bit noisy over the bar or on the street sides. Room was nice except for the tiny closet and bathtub, but that's not the end of the world.

“WOW - Staff could not have been more helpful, slept like a baby” I splurged on this hotel for my birthday, and it was a great choice. It's just steps from the subway, but my room, even though it was on the second floor, was completely quiet. The staff could not have been nicer, and were helpful throughout my stay. The room was elegant and very comfortable - the bed was perfect. I enjoyed the TV, the large shower, and only wish I had had some DVDs to use in the player. I would definitely consider going there agian.

“A Favorite in Chicago” The James is a lovely, eco-friendly boutique hotel in the heart of the Magnificent Mile. Service was outstanding and the room was huge in comparison to other boutique hotels nearby. Decor is modern, but not uptight. Very earthy in the heart of the city. The bar is nice and the staff are very friendly and ready to help in every way possible. Highly recommended.

“Spacious, no wireless, possible maintenance issues” During DC's recent cold snap, they put a carafe of hot cocoa at the front desk. It was watery, but it was a welcome gesture, and it speaks to the helpfulness of the staff. My studio room was spacious with a surprisingly high ceiling. Bedding was adequate: triple sheeting around a thin synthetic duvet, with comfortable pillows. Good mattress. Net is free, but is wired only (provided by iBahn). Power outlets at desk height and on the bedside lamps (yay!). Laundry worked fine ($1.50/machine). Valet parking for $20. "Dinner" is served Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, but it wasn't always as tasty or as healthy as we wanted. Alternate Wednesdays are a "Manager's Toast" with a free beer or glass of wine and improved food. Breakfast always included eggs and sausage, but it didn't rival a made-to-order breakfast. Still, it beats most "free" hotel breakfasts. We had some maintenance issues, and the responses were a little worrisome: they fixed the symptoms, but not always the underlying causes, which suggests problems will keep recurring. In one case, the toilet clogged. That wouldn't have been a problem except that the toilet had a habit of running occasionally (a sign of slow leak in the flap valve), and the slow leak led to an overflow. Even worse, the cutoff valve at the wall leaked when it was closed, so one could choose how to flood the room. They quickly unclogged the toilet, but it took multiple reports to get the flap valve properly fixed, and they never fixed the cutoff valve. All told, I'd go back.

“First Class” This is one of Washington DC's "grand dame" hotels. It has been immaculately maintained, and everything about it is first rate. The service, the rooms, and the public spaces are superb. The hotel is located on Connecticut Avenue a few blocks south of DuPont Circle. This places it within easy walking distance of any sort of restaurant you could possibly want, as well as a wide range of shopping. The Mall, Smithsonian, Newseum, etc., are not really within walking distance (for most people), but there is a Metro station on the same block. You don't want to bring a car if you can avoid it, because traffic in this part of DC can be awful, and valet parking at the Mayflower is really expensive. If you have driven to DC, leave the car in long term parking at Reagan Airport and take the Metro to the hotel.

“Great place in downtown Chicago” I was pleasantly surprised. Sometimes the Hard Rock can be a bit cheesy but that is NOT the case here. Great bar, the rooms are nice, the hotel is hip and modern and the front desk service was top notch. It is located near the river in a very convenient area of downtown. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great Place, Good Location” Great price for Boston. Extremely friendly staff. Very clean room and very spacious. Very comfortable bed. Went on leisure trip with sister. Would definately stay there again. Did not take advantage of room service, bar or restaurant.
“Really Nice!” Needed to be in this area for business and stayed here. Looks brand new. What a nice hotel, I was so impressed, the service, the room, really great!!! Highly recommend.

“Just a place to sleep” We spent 3 nights at North Austin Plaza during SXSW. The hotel was just a place to sleep, and we spent literally no time there during the day -- for that purpose, it did the job. It was run down and in need of updates, but was reasonably clean. Some of the power outlets didn't work, had a musty/stale smell, weak water pressure, no safe, etc. Not a high-end hotel by any means. If you're looking for a place to crash, this will do. If you're looking for a nice hotel or will be spending more time in the room, look elsewhere - there are plenty of other options within a half mile.

“Nice for the Price” We stayed here for New Years Eve. It was PACKED, and parking was definitely an issue (even with their own parking lot) - not surprising for the holiday. We got a great deal on priceline.com, and I was pretty satisfied with our stay. The bed and the pillows were amazing! We didn't do much in the hotel (didn't even try the restaurant, but the bar looked hopping - great for happy hour.) I like that there's a beauty bar with a sink outside of the bathroom. The ice machine is by the elevators - far from most of the rooms. Other than that, the room stay was pretty nice.

“Nice hotel and good price” My business has booked me to stay here twice at $69/night. The hotel is clean and is a good option if you are looking for a place by the airport. The free breakfast includes cereal, some pastries that are not that good, waffles, yogurt, either sausage or bacon and egg patties. It's not too bad. I did not mind staying at this hotel.

“Great location in mid-town, excellent hotel value” Found this highly rated hotel through trip advisor and booked several months in advance to take advantage of special. The location was excellent, short walk to shopping (Macy's around the corner) Times Square and Hell's Kitchen restaurants. Easy access to Penn Station with direct connecting trains to EWR Newark Airport Extensive breakfast included for three of us. Highly recommend the hotel

“Nice Stay for First Time in Chicago” My wife and I booked a studio suite at the Affinia through TravelZoo for only $105 a night. Given the great deal, we were impressed with the overall quality of this hotel. The lobby is nice as is the pub down the stairs. It is obvious, however, that the hotel is just a little aged. While our room was spacious and comfortable, the bathroom was too small and there was a little wear on the wallpaper. The carpet was a little thin also. The view was nice and we weren't bothered by the noise from the 23rd floor. We loved the courtesy and efficiency of the staff. The bellman remembered our names throughout our stay and he was quick to offer advice about places to visit. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would recommend it, but the hotel should be much better after the renovations that are planned over the next year. The location was great - next door to Gino's East Pizza and Neiman Marcus - very close to the Mag Mile. We would return only if we found a discount similar to the TravelZoo deal. Otherwise we would probably look elsewhere for a different experience.

“Great Location, Great Hotel” The Orchard Hotel is an excellent choice for someone looking for an above average hotel at a reasonable rate. The location is superb. Located in Union Square, you are within walking distance of the financial district, quality shopping areas, Chinatown, and Little Italy. The Cable Cars stop half a block from the front door of the hotel, providing quick and easy access to Fisherman's Wharf. The hotel rooms are of an average size but are tastefully decorated. The showers are powerful, and it only takes a few seconds for the water to become hot after turning-on the faucets. The breakfast included in the room price is above average, featuring coffee cakes, fruit, toast, hard boiled eggs, ham, cheese, and a selection of juices/coffee/tea. My only complaint with this hotel was the poor quality of the pillows. Other than that, I was very pleased with this hotel and would stay here again without hesitation.

“Very Nice Hotel” I stayed here with my husband last week for one night. We requested a non-smoking room but the first room had definitely been smoked in, probably by a guest who didn't care that it was designated non-smoking. The bellman agreed with us, called down to the front desk and immediately moved us to a new room. We had a standard room, it was very clean, easy wireless internet access (for $10) and not a bad size for New York City. Aesthetically, the decor is modern and very cool, which is great in the sleeping area. I did not particularly enjoy some of the modern design implementations in the bathroom. For example, I personally was not fond of the stainless steel sink with the ball drain stopper in the bathroom - it felt too much like a kitchen sink, but this is a decor preference and did not really affect the nature of my experience. I also wish they had more places to hang towels - the bathroom decor is sparse, and with just two people, I still found it difficult to find a place to hang our wet towels -there is only one hook on the back of the bathroom door, and no place to hang a hand towel. Ladies with makeup bags - be vigilant - the trash can in the bathroom is situated under a hole that is cut out of the sink counter - again, a modern design idea that I think is not practical at all. I had quite a few toiletry and makeup items, and first of all, the hole took up valuable counter space, and secondly, I was a bit concerned that we may accidentally drop something in there and not notice until it was too late to retrieve it. However, these are minor things. The hotel staff is very attentive and wonderful and we ate breakfast and a late snack in the hotel restaurant. Wonderful! Pricey but delicious. Night-owls and bar-hoppers - note that the neighborhood is not much at night - not a lot going on in the area, it is by Canal Street, which does not provide much by way of night life. It is close to the Canal Street subway station, for those of you who don't mind taking the train. Overall, a nice experience at the Tribeca Grand.

“My favorite place to stay while in Austin --” I have a lot of loving family scattered around Austin but I always elect to stay at the San Jose when I'm in town. To me, it's the essence of South Austin -- much classier than it's neighbor, The Austin Motel. Located on a perfect stretch of road on South Congress, it's in walking distance to a lot of the off-beat places one can only experience in South Austin. Across the street from the legendary Continental Club (a good friend, Roger One Night, once owned it,) down the street from my favorite Guero's Taco Bar and right next door to Jo's -- where I always enjoy a late weekend breakfast with excellent coffee outside -- the San Jose is a perfect fit for me.

“Perfect for a family weekend!” My husband and I brought my mom to the Drake in March of '08 to celebrate her 60th birthday. The great thing about The Drake during the winter, is you're able to get fantastic rooms for unbelievably reasonable prices. I believe our two club-level rooms overlooking Lake Michigan were less than $200 a night. The rooms were de rigeur for the Drake - well appointed and ample in size. We love staying at the Drake for the "old Chicago" feel we always get, but are always shocked back into Hilton reality when it comes to service. Most of the Drake employees always seem rather put out, and the biggest example was when the three of us (rather than venture out into the freezing snow) opted to have dinner and drinks in the Palm Court. Our waitress literally had a scowl on her face every time we asked her for something. I'm not a travel snob, but I'm never a fan of servers just being downright rude to people who actually, are quite nice and friendly. The tip we left reflected our dissatisfaction. But, we don't go to the Drake for the service, we go for the history and the fun and the location on Michigan Avenue.

“A jewel of a reno, great staff” I had used TripAdvisor to find an affordable hotel in NYC and found Sohotel, just on the fringe of Little Italy, downtown. it was a great find. The staff was lovely and obliging and very engaged in cleaning! They carry your luggage up the stairs (there are no elevators). the hotel has been re-fitted and, while it doesn't look very exciting on the outside, inside it's all a-glitter with loud colours, exotic prints, pictures and charming, kitschy stuff. My room held a double and a single bed, a dresser and two bed tables with not much room for anything else, but this is NY! I was thrilled! the renos had included lots of lights and good switch control; there was both a/c and an overhead fan; and the very light-and-bright bathroom had everything you could want - all the little bottles of stuff including toothpaste, which is unusual. everything was spotlessly clean. The room had two windows with good coverings - in short, it was great - so much better than other accommodation I have had in the city. and, since it was NYC, after all, there was noise at night from the street but it wasn't so bad and the bed was so cosy comfy that I had a great sleep anyway. A coffee service is provided in the morning and while there is no breakfast room, staff provided a reference and a discount card to a close-by restaurant that served us a lovely breakfast. parking was $28 a day at a nearby parkade, easily walkable, dragging luggage, and that worked out well too. the D train on Grand is the nearest subway station, a couple of blocks. The Sohotel was the most reasonable accommodation I could find in NYC for this visit and it worked out great. I would both recommend it and return myself, when next i visit! (soon, I hope - the city is always so wonderful!)

“Okay Sheraton, nothing special” Very basic Sheraton near times square. For the business traveler, Sheraton towers across the street is much better value. No wireless in the rooms. Seems to cater to groups of kids. Staff is nice. Restaurant in hotel is marginal.

“Loved the Warwick Regis” I stayed at the Warwick Regis for a week on business. The location was terrific- just a short walk to Union Square, and there was a bus stop right out front. The staff was the most professional, helpful staff I have ever encountered. The room was tiny, but it was more than adequate for one person. The decor definately made you feel like you were in a bed and breakfast- extremely charming. I strongly recommend the breakfast that they serve every morning- the food was terrific and the juice was freshly squeezed. I will stay in the Warwick Regis on all of my return trips to SF.

“A Wonderful Stay” We stayed for a night before our cruise to Alaska. Beautiful hotel, great location for access to our cruise ship and for seeing Seattle waterfront area. Just steps away from Pike Place Market and all the sights along the waterfront. Walk or take the free trollys to lots of area sights including the Space Needle. We made reservations months in advance so the price was reasonable (under $300.00 per night for Concierge level which included breakfast, snacks and evening wine and cheese). Wonderful friendly and accomodating service, really yummy apples at the front desk, we enjoyed all the perks of this beautiful hotel. Our room could have had a nicer view but we were gone except to sleep. The train runs along the back of the hotel but the noise was faint. There wasn't enough wrong to keep us from staying again in the future.

“Nice hotel in a GREAT location in midtown” We stayed here for 2 nights over the 4th of July weekend using Marriott Reward points. This hotel is in a fabulous location in midtown on 40th St. at 5th Ave., just 1/2 blk from the NY Public Library, 1 blk from Bryant Park, and a few blocks from the chaos of Times Square. We agree with the other reviews about the small rooms, but of course, this is NYC and small hotel rooms are commonplace. I have stayed at other NYC hotels in the past (Sheraton NYC, Paramount, etc.) where the rooms were actually smaller than at this hotel. Our room had a queen bed which was comfortable. The closet was small but we didn't need to use it. The bathroom was pretty small as well, with minimal counter space, but a decent shower/tub. The A/C unit was loud but that was OK with us as the walls were VERY thin and we could hear doors closing, people in their rooms, and when people got on/off the elevator. The plasma tv was a very nice touch. We had absolutely no problems with the timliness of the elevators. The most we had to wait for an elevator was maybe 1 minute. Staff was great, checking to see how our stay was and if we needed anything. They arranged for the car service to the airport. We did not eat at the hotel, but the "Salmon Grille" restaurant is supposed to be quite good and it has a nice patio which was always crowded in the evenings. We were out and about in NYC, so we really did not spend much time in the room at all, except to sleep. But if we did spend more time in the room, I think we would have become a bit claustrophobic. This hotel was just fine for us and we loved the location!

“評判ほど悪くはない。。” あの悪名高いグランドハイアットNYに二泊しました。とにかくスタッフに愛想がない、部屋は高額な割にショボいと悪評ふんぷんな噂で、ある程度覚悟して宿泊しました。しかし、そのためか、私にはスタッフの態度も部屋もかえって良く感じる位でした。とにかくデカいホテルで場所柄もあり客足が絶えないためか、スタッフが多忙で愛想を振りまく余裕がないだけなのでしょう、こちらが下手に申し出ると何でも要求は聞いてくれました。 部屋の質も値段の割に、というのも分かりますが、とにかくNew York Cityの、あの立地(グランドセントラル駅に隣接)の良さであれば致し方ないでしょう。とにかく、NYCである程度のホテルであればどこも値は張ります。このレベルだったら、また泊まってもいいと感じました。

“Excellent service and amenities” This is a great hotel and would be my choice anytime I need to be in downtown L.A. on business. The hotel makes a good impression as soon as you enter: Efficient, polite check in and delivery of my bags. Fruit-infused ice water and apples available in the lobby – pretty nice on a hot L.A. summer day. Free wireless internet and other perks if you join their rewards program. The room is pretty standard, with your typical hotel furnishings; the bed was very comfortable. The only two off-notes during my stay: usually at this price range you get a flat-screen TV these days, but here the TV was a regular TV, with only ok picture quality. I didn’t watch it much, so it wasn’t a problem for me. As another reviewer mentioned, the room had a bit of a sour smell – it wasn’t overpowering, but I wonder whether it was time to replace the carpet. Other than that though, everything was very clean and well-maintained. I didn’t eat at the restaurant, but a breakfast buffet was included in my room rate. It wasn’t over the top, but they offered a good variety of breads, cereals, fresh fruit, and tasty hot dishes, including made to order eggs. The bar offers a happy hour from 4-6 pm, with discounted bar menu. Even if you don’t order food, the drinks come with complimentary peanuts (regular and wasabi), which were delicious and a nice touch. As with the rest of the hotel staff, the servers were excellent. An extra bonus is the fitness center. I’m used to hotels cramming a few pieces of equipment in a mirrored room and calling it a gym. At the Omni, the fitness room is large enough to fit several machines while still leaving space to walk around. It’s also well-stocked with towels, water, and even headsets for the individual TVs on the equipment. I was not expecting such a nice space. There is an outdoor pool as well. Budget $30/night plus tips for parking (valet), but honestly that seems to be the going rate at downtown hotels. I had no problems getting my car quickly when needed. There were some commercial parking lots nearby, but I preferred the convenience of having the car located on site. Which brings me to the location. Downtown L.A. is ok and has a few cultural attractions to see, but it’s somewhat desolate (especially at night). There is a small shopping center / food court adjacent to the hotel, but it's mainly busy at lunchtime. So you will probably find yourself leaving the area pretty frequently, because much of the sightseeing, shopping and dining is located well outside downtown. There are buses and subway lines within a block or two, and the hotel provides a courtesy car that will take you within 3 miles of the hotel, so it’s not absolutely necessary to have a car. But, as someone who strongly prefers to walk and rely on public transportation, I have reluctantly found it necessary to rent a car for any stays longer than a couple of days in L.A. Most of my trips to L.A. are for business though, so the downtown location was still convenient for me. If I were on vacation for beaches and shopping, I might choose to stay somewhere else, but that’s no knock on the Omni itself, which is an excellent hotel.

“Great location and service” This is a great hotel, especially for the money, location and service. Struck me as more of a business than a leisure hotel (the in-house bar didn't seem anything special), but the location is great for the sites (The Mall, White House are nearby and close to Connecticut Avenue for hopping on a sightseeing bus). Only slight disappointments were that the rooms looked rather tired (although very clean and spacious) and that there was no room service after (I think) 22.00.

“Great experience!” Stayed here for one night with a group. Very welcoming staff, clean rooms, tastefully decorated. Great location. Nicely sized room. Only downside is that I heard the elevator dinging all night, so I recommend asking for a room away from the elevator bay.

“Old and poor breakfast” This hotel feels very old and definitely needs an updating. The rooms are OK, nothing special. The "executive" floor is just a different part of the building that you need key access to get into, the rooms are exactly the same. The executive floor breakfast is poor and has very little selection. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel except for the occasional low prices.

“great location, service and view” Stayed at the Omni for 5 nights in June 2005. After reading other reviews, passed on the 10th floor corner room and instead took the regular room on the 24th floor. Room was nice and comfortable. Giant flat screen TV, soft bed, good service(join the omni hotel program and you get a newspaper and drinks every morning). Location is in the middle of North Michigan and about 4 blocks to the Red Line. I would have rated 5 stars but it was a little expensive to stay here.

“Will definitely be back, best value in the area” Recently traveled with a small group for a short weekend stay. The hotel was more than accommodating for us. We were able to upgrade to two suites for $20/night which was great as it gave us more space. The rooms were not available when we arrived...in fairness that was at noon and check-in time is at 3:00pm. They were ready at check-in time. The rooms were clean and well sized for a city such as Washington. The room had an iHome in the bedroom with an old fashioned tube tv, and in the living room at flat panel television with a stereo system (and pullout couch). There was also a full size kitchen with some furnishings. I especially liked all the touches that made it feel unique such as the basket in the bathroom (don't know why, I just liked it). We chose not to park at the hotel since it was on a weekend, but I can understand some peoples frustrations with the price...but its a city...come one, you should expect it by now. The bar downstairs was terrific. Well priced drinks and very friendly staff. Speaking of staff, we had absolutely nothing but the best courtesy from everyone we encountered from the doorman to the checkout staff. They provided recommendations for places to eat and accommodated our every request. Some improvements/cons: -By this time internet should be free, end of story. -The online reservation system is a little confusing. -The location proximity to the Metro isn't outstanding, but doable. -The standing lane for check-in is somewhat short at a busy intersection. -The suites only had air conditioning in the bedroom, so in other words in order for the living room to cool, the bedroom had to be freezing. All in all I thought the hotel was spectacular. I would probably place it in the 3.5 star category rather than 4, but with some slight improvements the hotel could easily be 4 stars. The value was superb and i will definitely be back!

“I would probably go with another hotel the next time” I checked in at the Carlton after having ended a conference staying at another hotel. I arrived 10 min before three oclock but was not able to check-in before three. I left my luggage at the reception and went for a walk around the hotel which is kind of up the hill from downtown SF. When I returned an hour later I could check-in. The receptionist seemed a little bit puzzled about the room but finally gave me an upgraded room on the 9th floor. The reason he was puzzled was perhaps the reason why a bell-boy an hour later knocked on my room delivering an order of wine for Mr. XX. I explained I was not Mr. XX but he was not quite convinced. I finally convinced him I was not Mr. XX and he went away (with the wine). The room was very spacious and nice looking with a coffemaker, LCD TV, clock-radio/CD player and safe. The safe was paced in a wall-in closet. No aircondition but a big fan in the ceiling. The bathroom was big but not very clean especially the bathtub had a lot of hard soap residues. The amenities ie.e. shampoo, conditioner and soap is placed in large containers over the tub which is good for the environment. Unfortunately it had a bad smell to it so I used my own instead. In general the room could need a make over. The worst thing however was that there was a very thin door into the next room whitout any noise reduction at all. During my stay I overhead all the talk and activities from the next room. Even at night when my light was switched off I could see the light from the next room around the fitting of the door. The staff was in general nice. However when I talked to the receptionist about getting a taxi to the airport I did not get must help except for the advice of using there limousine service. I agreed and he asked at what time I was to be picked up. I actually expected him to know at what time to be at the airport and how long the drive would be. He advice me to be at least 2 hours early at the airport as it was a domestic flight and that the drive would take 20-40 min but hey "you pay and you decide". It turned out that the recommended time to be at the airport was 1 hour before takeoff and I actually had to sit at the airport for 1 1/2 hour as I fortunately did not take his advice on 2 hours but instead went for 1 1/2 hour. At that time in the morning half an hour is sufficient when you do not have luggage. The hotel do have some wine arrangement but I did not attend.

“Excellent Family Hotel” Stayed here during a comic-con convention several years back. This hotel is very nice. Enjoyed the kitchen area sink. Some rooms have a seperate living room with a pull out sofa and then the bedroom seperate. Parking is free at the time when we stayed, dont know if its still the same. They offered a great breakfast in the morning. Its close to some eateries. Would stay here again.

“Across the street from the Academy of Music” We chose the Double Tree because of its location directly across the street from the Academy of Music. I was traveling with my daughter, for her birthday. The hotel was efficient and clean. Standouts were doorman and senior cashier who has worked at the property for many years. Front desk was speedy, gotta love that cookie program, it's cute. Room was high up, on the east side of the city. GREAT VIEWS, clean and tidy bathroom. We had room service for breakfast...traveled with my daughter, kids love room service! Close to the Wilma as well and great Art store nearby. Affordable property, we enjoyed our stay.

“Nitpickers, stay elsewhere” I must say it was quite shocking (even though I was expecting it from reading reviews prior to departure) to see the condition of the rooms here. A complete room redo is obviously way overdue, no doubt about it. I would of expected to have seen such shaby fixtures say at an airport property somewhere off the beaten path, but in downtown Los Angeles? All this said though, I must acknowledge that the room was clean, the bed was comfortable, and the saving grace at this hotel was the great service. The limited F&B options were a bit disappointing ( only one lounge? .. no coffee kiosk ?? ). All in all, we had a nice stay and hope to return as the location for us was perfect. Hopefully our next visit will wow us with new rooms.

“Hotel going under major rennovation” They are doing a nice job on the hotel but the lobby is a bit messy with all the areas under construction. Entry is now on Sutter St. Can be confusing. But the rooms which have been remodeled look great and the updated bathrooms are nice. We had a suite and it was very large and comfortable. No complaints about the room and the furniture comfortable as well. The Club room on the 32nd floor for the diamond gold passport members is terrific. Great foods and service. Stunning views of the water and bay.

“Comfortable at Comfort Suites” I had a king suite which included a 6'counter with sink, refrig, microwave, small table along with a living area with pull out couch, chair and tv. The bedroom also has a tv and two doors, one to the bathroom and the other to the living area. The bathroom was spacious but with only basic amenities. Rooms were clean. Although the hotel is wireless there is a small businness area with computer. Fitness area has only 3 machines and there is a hot tub - no pool, Breakfast starts at 6 but if you leave early there is coffee and danish in the lobby. Down the street are a few other hotel chains and restaurants. If you don't have a car there is a diner next door and they also share a shuttle with 2 other hotels. For the money its fine for a stopover either to or from the airport..

“Excelente opción para viaje familiar” Obtuvimos lo que estabamos esperando. No nos defraudó ni la zona ni el hotel. Las habitaciones son amplias con dos espacios separados lo cual es importante cuando se viaja en familia. Por las noches salíamos caminando para ir a comer, unos días hacia Georgetown y otros hacia Dupont Circle, en ambos distritos hay buenos restaurantes por escoger......... El hotel es bastante grande y estando totalmente lleno no tuvimos problemas de espacio, inclusive a la hora del desayuno siempre había alguna mesa desocupada y limpia. Lo recomiendo para familias.

“Very comfortable A-. Just a few touches to make it an A.” I quite liked this hotel. Pretty comfortable overall. Close to the metro, and lots of fun food and strolling options in Dupont. Also, a nice 20 minute walk to Metro Center on a temperate day. There are a few things though that make it fall just short of an A. First, they either seem to have way too many people standing around the front door doing nothing, or no one at all. I had no one to help me with enormous bag, plus their front door is small, heavy, and awkward to navigate with luggage. Second, as someone else noted below, they ask you for your preference of newspaper. I said Washington Post. Of course, of the four nights I stayed there, two came with USA Today, and two came with no paper at all. You shouldn't ask if you're not going to make an effort to honor the request. Final negative, there's a LOT of hall noise, and you can hear it very clearly. I was near the elevator, and every night, there were a lot of young people going out. Must be close to graduation or something. I was up pretty late working every night, but if I had been trying to sleep, I would have been pretty irritated. All these issues, except for the thin walls, are pretty easy to fix, and I would gladly stay here again.

“Che squallore, sono fuggito!” Posizione ottima, proprio in centro a due passi da Time Square. PUNTO. Finiscono qua tutte i possibili apprezzamenti per questa struttura squallida. Hall desolante e sporca, datata e decadente. Le camere non sono da meno, pulizia inesistente, vecchie e rivoltanti. Le lenzuola macchiate ed i cuscini ormai di una tonalità giallo/marrone sotto le federe hanno fatto si che al mattino dopo decidessi di andare via con 3 giorni di anticipo alla ricerca di una struttura più dignitosa. Tutto questo alla modica cifra di 180$ a notte. Assolutamente da evitare.

“kid friendly” The Catamaran is definitely "kid friendly" and since we were there with a kid, the several days we spent there were OK. It must be a challange to keep a "resort" hotel in satifactory functioning condition when 2 year olds amuse themselves by opening and closing the screen door to the balcony as our grandson did. The staff does seems to stay on top of this effort. The pool and hot tub area was well-maintained, as were the grounds and the beach generally. There are "amusements" for the kids - parrots, swans and ducks. There's a paved walkway along the beach for strollers and joggers. The restaurant welcomed small kids with their Cheerios and the staff was friendly, very courteous and prompt in service. I give them high marks. Our rooms, however, were somewhat worn and dark. The bed cover was very physically heavy, ponderously so. This is not a luxury establishment, a bit shabby not chic. I thought it was rather expensive for the value but since I didn't make the reservation, I didn't compare rates. It was quite satisfactory to be sure.

“Congress Plaza Hotel Chicago” Das Congress Plaza Hotel in Chicago befindet sich nur ein paar 100 Meter vom Ufer des Lake Michigan entfernt. Von dem Hotel aus lässt sich Downtown Chicago zu Fuß aus bestens erkunden. Ca. 15 Gehminuten entfernt liegt der Chicago River. Die Hotelzimmer bieten sehr viel Platz und sind gemütlich eingerichtet. Allerdings muss ich auch sagen, dass die Einrichtung etwas altmodisch wirkt und unser Hotelzimmer etwas dürftig möbiliert war. Aber dies hat mich in keiner Weise gestört und ich würde auch wegen den günstigen Übernachtungspreisen dieses Hotel weiterempfehlen. Einen großen Pluspunkt erhält von mir das Bett. Wie bei amerikanischen Betten typisch, ist die Matratze sehr dick und das Bett wäre groß genug für vier Personen gewesen. Aber da wir nur zu zweit waren, hatten wir mehr als genug Platz.

“Terrific hotel and staff” We had a wonderful weekend getaway here. Our room was furnished and kept in first class condition with top notch accessories and toiletries. Excellent location right on the lake, we walked out one night and watched the bats fly out from under the Congress St bridge. The staff here, especially management, are extraordinary.

“Definitely old, but good” Got a good deal on Priceline here. Had a suite, with a fireplace, sofa, fridge, etc. 4 poster bed was cool, and modern tech- satellite tv, iPod dock. Upholstery was definitely worn and stained, but sheets and towels were fine. Location was in a nice residential area, easy to buses and 10-15 min walk to plenty of food. Liked Fraiche yogurt and Kaka Udon Kitchen. I felt safe walking alone in the evening. Would stay again, but might not be for everyone.

“I couldn't believe this was a Holiday Inn!” I had read about Holiday Inn renovating their hotels but I couldn't believe the difference. Before I would only be caught dead in a Holiday Inn had the title Express after it but I have completely changed my mind. The service was EXCELLENT at the front desk. I came in grumpy after a long drive and I was greeted with fresh baked cookies and a smile. Then, just because we are loyalty program members they upgraded us to a suite. The room was spacious and the bed was comfortable. I was surprised to find that they had room service and a restaurant with an amazing breakfast.
