Plus a pantry for any little items you might have left behind. We didn't get to take advantage of the fitness center or pool which I was hoping to do but I imagine they would have exceeded my expectations as everything else at this hotel did. The best part was that with our AAA discount, our room was only $108! A steal for what we received. We'll definitely consider this hotel again when we are in the area.

“Great hotel for summer!” Stayed at the hotel with my family for a summer weekend. We have family that live in the apartments above and selected based on location - outstanding and would stay again. Super cool lobby, bar, pool, work out facility, outdoor lounge areas. A gem in the middle of the city. Swanky, yet our kids were totally welcome there and felt comfortable. Only issue that between the hotel, apartments, and condos, there are 3 different elevator banks and finding your way around can be confusing. I felt like an idiot the whole weekend trying to find my way to the right one. Small price to pay, however, will be back!

“No WiFi in rooms only wired and I have a MacAir. Room service is awful. I will not return.” I booked my family in here using points left from several years ago. This place reminded me of why I only stay at Marriotts when staying at a full service hotel. Parking 40 bucks a day, room service that was the worst in my 20 years of weekly business travel, WiFi in lobby only, not at all what a Hilton used to be. Waste of points.

“Great Place” I travel on business to Seattle every week and stayed at the W for 2-3 days a week for the past 3 months. It is a great place with a great location and great service. The staff knows me by name and a very detail oriented. I would suggest the restaurant downstairs. The place is always empty during the week nights and I never went there but on a recent night I was too tired to go outside and decided to get a quick bite. The lamb and cheese is great and service is second to none. Needless to say, I will be back.

“Cool theme hotel” Stayed at Hard Rock during convention in June. Looks fancier than it really is and the price was high for what we received. That said it is conveniently located within walking distance of the Merchandise Mart where we were working each day and there were several good restaurants in close proximity.

“Our Oasis in the City ... Affordable Luxury ...” My wife and I like 4-star hotels and the Colonnade fits us in every way. We like to come into the City some weekends to escape our normal life. On this trip we did have a temporary inconvenience when my wife noticed that the rug was not spotless but we have never been moved to a second room so fast in our lives and #2 was indeed spotless. The view ! top floor with wall to wall glass looking straight down a busy street. The bed! so many pillows draw you in, then you find out that it is as comfortable as it looks. The thoughtfulness! Someone quietly slipped a note under our door with extras like free breakfast. The staff! Friendly but not fawning, attentive but not in your face. I can only imagine the full experience in late Spring when the rooftop pool opens. We want to return then to once again restore our souls in this urban oasis.

“Very overrated” I booked this hotel because it had such a high ranking and so many good reviews on Tripadvisor. So I was pretty disappointed to say the least. First the woman at checkin was hardly friendly. Then we went to our room to find it like an oven and with a wonderful view of a brick wall and no natural light. The bedside lamp wasnt working, and (worst of all) there was hair in the bath. Yuk. Moved to another room where it was also very hot (only thing to do was to turn of the heating and wait for it to cool down - couldnt open a window). The smoke alarm went off around midnight (doesnt anyone check the batteries on these things???), dodgy bedside lamp, terrible pillows, and a whole host of other minor but annoying maintenance issues, like power outlets not working etc etc. The TV reception was lousy, the TV remote didnt work properly, the towels were old and thin, and there were no tea/coffee facilities provided. I cannot for the life of me fathom why it has had such good reviews - I certainly wouldnt rush back. Oh and a message for ALL hotels - if you are going to bother providing bathrobes, how about something actually long enough for anyone over 5 ft tall?

“Harbor style” We were here for the inaugural Baltimore Grand Prix. This hotel was located inside the tracks so access to and from was limited between 7am and 7pm. Since this was a very unique situation, I can't hold judgement against Hyatt for the inconvenience. But maybe someone reading this will benefit from my experience if they plan on attending this event the next time. I chose to have a room with a view of the track but had to pay $50 extra. Considering that I was able to book this room on the day the festivities started, I wasn't complaining. So keep that in mind that hotel rooms inside the track do not sell out as fast as you think. I like the lobby and access to the Baltimore Harbor. Parking is pretty expensive but there are cheaper options within a few blocks. The room was decent and the staff was helpful. I did not eat anything the hotel served so I can't comment on that. Especially since there are awesome dining options in the surrounding areas. It's real good on normal operating days but for the Grand Prix, I advise you to plan ahead and don't drive there. Between parking prices and all the streets that were cut-off, it wasn't worth it. But overall, the hotel is nice.

“Wow!” High-end hotel that will leave you satisfied. Luxury and style from rooms to pool/facilities. Turndown attendant service was a nice touch. There isn't a whole lot I can say to improve on here. Fitness Center and Outdoor Pool were as nice as I've seen. Resistance pools in the lower level will give you a good workout. Golf course looked fantastic but the greens were under repair. I'd stay again in a second. Top-shelf!

“OK Hilton but nothing special at all” I stayed one night at the Hilton Houston Southwest for business. I chose this Hilton because it was very convenient to several meetings I had in the area; otherwise, I certainly would not bother to stay here. The hotel was just OK. I arrived early, so my king room wasn't available. I gladly took a double room instead just to get in and settled. The room was spacious but very mundane, even for a Hilton. It felt more like a Hilton Garden Inn, to be honest...perhaps with a slightly nicer bed. The bathroom was small, and the faucet control was ridiculously annoying. It took a number of attempts before I could get the water temperature not too scalding or too cold--it was the most annoying control I'd seen in years. Water pressure wasn't great, either. Otherwise, it was clean and well-located for my purposes. But nothing to write home about. If you have business in the vicinity, it's fine as long as you can get a good rate like I did; otherrwise, it may be worth looking at other nearby hotels. Next time I visit, I am inclined to look elsewhere.

“Enjoyable Stay in the Windy City” I found this hotel on Priceline booking about a week in advance. Everything ran smoothly at check-in and the hotel staff was friendly, helpful and courteous. The concierge gave some really good advice on restaurants and transportation. While this is a historic hotel, the room had a comfortably modern feel, a snazzy bathroom and cozy bed. The location is right on Michigan Avenue in the South Loop, so if you're venturing out into Grant Park, you merely need to cross the street. While this is a good location, you'll still need to get on the subway or walk quite a ways to the River North area. The subway is not very far from the hotel at all and the neighborhood typically has a lot of foot traffic so it feels pretty safe. The hotel has a very trendy restaurant and a smaller bodega for food options; however, I highly recommend exploring the neighborhood. Overall, with the price I paid, this hotel was a great value and highly recommended.

“Excellent Hotel” This is the third time that my wife and I have stayed at this hotel during the last two and a half years and I simply cannot understand some of the more negative reviews that are sometimes directed towards it. As a regular visitor to Manhattan, I think that you would be hard pressed to find many other hotels of a similar rating that can offer the same standards as well as being in the same location. On our previous stays here we have only ever had standard rooms. However, we've always found these rooms to be perfectly okay with excellent bathroom facilities. This time, though, we decided to upgrade to a de luxe room and it was absolutely superb. As far as the hotel staff are concerned, I cannot fault them. And that goes from the reception staff to the cleaners right down to the hotel porters, who are always cheery and willing to assist. And, I would like to take this opportunity to thank all of them for making us feel very welcome during all of our stays.

“center of the centre” Myself my wife and my son stayed there late september and had a wonderful visit. The staff were pleasant and check in was quick. We requested a crib for my son and as they didn't have any available, so the hotel went out and bought a brand new one. The room wasn't the biggest but the location was as centre as it could be. We had a wonderful time here and again trip advisor was spot on with its advice. Considering its position in boston our room was very quiet. The only bad comment is the breakfast, they really could do with a toaster for the bagels.

“Impossible to get a cab” If you stay here without a car, expect to wait at least 20 minutes at the taxi stand for a cab. Unfortunately there are lot of hotels in this area and getting a cab to pass by takes FOREVER! It may be quicker to hop on the F-train down by the Sheraton or a bus. The rooms themselves feel like a Courtyard Marriott...nothing spectacular. This hotel is in a good location and about a 15-minute walk from Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39. You will have to walk to the Wharf to eat...not many restaurants near this hotel.

“Nice place in a busy place” Once again, the wife and I required an overnight stay in Houston to facilitate some medical procedures being done on an outpatient basis. We chose the Crowne Plaza River Oaks because 1) it was close to where we needed to be, 2) the medical rates at our usual haunts more on the south side of the Texas Medical Center were not available, and 3) the wife had recently stayed at this same hotel on business. Notice I didn't say anything about price. Crowne Plaza hotels are not 2 star properties, but with some research this one was had for less than $110 per night during the week. Hint: we had to use Skoosh.com, a UK based hotel reseller. This probably destroyed any hopes of getting this stay credited on our Priority Club loyalty club account. But nevertheless, this Crowne Plaza is a nice property. It is at the Kirby exit off US 59 south in Houston, between downtown and 610. If you are familiar with Houston, you know this is a busy part of town. It is easy to get to, just stay on the access road and make a right at the hotel. You can either valet park or keep right to park yourself in the garage. If you want to save $4 and the bother of waiting for your car to be delivered, use the garage. For your frugality, you will have to ride an elevator down to the ground floor and enter the hotel by the gift shop, walking past the room elevators to get to the front desk. No problem. It doesn't say so, but for your $8 per day you apparently get in & out access in the garage, as we only had the once per day garage charge on our room ticket. The lady on the desk was friendly. I cannot review the restaurant for this trip, as we did not use it. The wife patronized it on her previous business trip and it was fine. However, we did bring in some take-out from a local restaurant during our stay, but I had neglected to check on knife and fork, which of course, had not been included in the take-out. The restaurant desk had picnic sets in their drawer like this had happened before. That was good of them. Our room was fine, very clean. It had a min-fridge, not a mini-bar, which is the way I like it. The soft drinks in the vending machine were cheaper by 20 cents than the exact same soft drink at a Walgreens store nearby. That was a pleasant surprise. And, whoa, the internet access was complimentary. I really don't like paying extras for everything when you stay at more upscale properties while the 2-star down the road can provide all that as part of the room. In that way, this higher level property did not disappoint. Would we stay there again? Sure, didn't see a single reason not to.

“Bargain with a great neighborhood feel” Outwardly, the New Miyako has a strong 80s aesthetic. Inside, the rooms are really clean and comfortable. There was even a bidet and a warmed toilet seat - very Japanese! I came for a Msft show at the LA Convention Center. While it is a bit far too walk, you can easily drive and park there. The fact that your hotel will be much cheaper than something nearby - I paid $109 a nite, during a huge convention, mind you - shows you how much you'll probably save. Also, the hotel is in the midst of Japantown and sandwiched by a gentrifying loft area to the east and a trendy club area rising to the west nearer to downtown. So it's a great location, and very safe. The Japanese ramen place across the street, Daikokuya, is a Mecca for Asian noodle lovers. You'll probably get a ticket for a complimentary continental breakfast at the downstairs cafe, Take 5. Take advantage - while it's a bit carb heavy for my taste (croissant etc.) in the morning, the coffee, filtered using some exotic Japanese technology that leaves fine little bubbles, was delicious.

“Nice place and great deal” We paid $69 for the room through Hotwire and were thrilled with the value. The rooms are very large with a very nice bathroom layout. The bathrooms have granite counterops and are loaded with extra amenities such as facial cleanser. The beds were comfy and the pillows were great. The bar/restuarant was suprisingly good. I went in with low expectations and the restauarant was actually astonishingly good. An earlier review mentioned lack of free wireless internet. This appears to have changed and we did have free wireless. This is the best Doubletree I believe I have stayed in. We were catching a flight out early the next morning at Seatac, and this was a great choice. I would absolutely recommend this hotel and would stay again. Frankly, even if the price doubled this would be a good deal and a great place to stay.

“Massive Hotel in the Heart of Times Square” WIthout a doubt, this has to be one of the largest hotels in the world. It is so massive that the check-in is on the 8th floor. Ok a few things about the property. The hotel is in the best location in New York - right in the middle of Times Square. If you are an elite member, they have an elite check-in on the ground floor, so you don't have to go up to the 8th floor to check in. The hotel itself has about 46 floors. I have stayed at this property two times in December 2011 - 3 nights per stay. If you are a Marriott Elite member, ask for a room with view facing Times Square and you will realize that this is a city that never sleeps; people are out at Times Square at all hours of the night. During my first stay, I was able to get a room with a great view. The second time, they were quite full so I didn't get a room with a good view. If you are Marriott Elite Gold or Platinum, you will get access to the Conceirge Lounge on the 30th floor. Again like the hotel, the lounge has to be the largest Conceirge lounge in the Marriott chain. I only went there for breakfast and also the evening presentation. Both seemed pretty decent. The Lounge faces Times Square with a great view. Rooms have to be some of the largest in the city. They're definitely much bigger then other properties I've stayed in in the city. My room during both my stays had a large King size bed with a sofa sleeper, and desk. I do wish the pillows in the Marriott property were wider. Housekeeping staff also replenishes water daily. If you press 55 on the phone, they will also bring you complementary bottled water. I ordered room service once and was a bit disappointed. I paid almost $50 for a salmon which wasn't that great There are much better dining options steps from the hotel. The one day I requested a late checkout, I was able to checkout at 3p. One word of caution when you checkout. Given the massive size of this hotel, if you call to have your luggage brought down, it will take time. I was waiting for a taxi to go to the airport at the hotel and some guests were complaning that they had waited over 15 minutes to have luggage brought down. Also during peak times, especially after 3p in the afternoon, you should plan 20 minutes to get a taxi. Taxis are hard to come by in the afternoon, especially around the holidays. Overall, this is a solid dependable hotel in the best location in New York. If you stay here, you will not need to rent a car. It's close to everything, and just a few blocks away from the nearest subway station that will take you everywhere. If you prefer a more personable experience that's "boutique like" then I recommend the Marriott Renaissance New York property which is just a block down - near 7th Ave / West 47th Street.

“Ottimo rapporto qualità prezzo, pulito e personale cortese” Ero per lavoro a NY con un cliene e ho soggiornato per 10 giorni in questo hotel. Avevo prenotato solo per una settimana ma poi ho avuto la necessità di estendere il soggiorno per ulteriori 3 giorni. Il personale della reception, molto cortese, mi ha consigliato di fare la prenotazione online (dall'albergo) invece che direttaemtne presso di lui per usufruire della promozione online... direi un ottimo servizio! La camera con un doppio queen si presentava con arredamento di design tutto nuovo. Il bagno curato, pulito. All'ultimo piano dove c'è la sala internet, c'è una incantevole terrazza dalla quale ammirare la città, con belle sdraio in ferro. Complessivamente un ottimo rapporto qualità prezzo. Davvero consigliato.

“Overpriced” My husband and I stayed here the night of our wedding. We paid $300 for the suite with the jetted two-person jacuzzi tub. The hotel has a boutique feel - the rooms are decorated with a lot of stripes and reminded me of Alice in Wonderland. The room we had was huge but had a lot of empty space which was a little strange. The jacuzzi tub was huge and could definitely accommodate two people and was like a hot-tub. The only thing was that the hotel did not provide any bubble bath etc. which would seem normal when offering such a large tub. Parking was outrageous - $40 a night. We previously paid $19/night at the Residence Inn. We ended up parking for free overnight at a meter spot. Room service was fast but the selection was limited and the food was okay, not great. Overall, I didn't have any problems with Hotel Monaco - it just didn't seem worth the high price.

“Perfect Park and Fly Experience” I live about 90 miles from the Philadelphia International Airport. When my flight leaves early in the morning I often stay overnight the day prior to my departure The Hampton Inn provides convenient shuttle service to and from the airport plus secure convenient parking for the duration of my trip. The rooms are spacious and clean, the beds are comfortable. Breakfast is served in the lobby and consists of both hot and cold items. Everything is fresh and tasty. The staff is friendly and cheerful. Ruby Tuesday's Restaurant is adjacent to the property. This is one of those Ruby Tuesday's with good food and service. I highly recommend this hotel for anyone flying out of PHL or to anyone who wants a nice hotel convenient to downtown Philadelphia.

“Class-Act!” I stayed at the James for business, and immediately felt like "family". The staff has the mid-west charm down; all professional, and genuinely eager to go the extra mile. The room was warm modern decor. I love turn-down service and a robe when I travel (it's the small things that help when you travel a lot), and they had both. The location was near everything in the loop, so it makes getting around easy. Looking forward to my next stay with them.

“Very Nice Resort For Family Get-Away” We purchased the Family Fling & Swing Package which includes: $50 Resort Credit daily, Free Golf (certain time restrictions apply; see website), Free internet, Free kids meals 12 and under( at Blue Sage for breakfast/lunch/dinner, and dinner at Tuscany's as long as adult meals are ordered), Free appetizer or dessert, Free self parking, Free Resort Fee, 10% off retail purchases. We stayed two nights, Friday & Saturday, which we thought were going to be very busy and overcrowded. But, thankfully, though it was busy, we didn't feel like we were suffocating. All hotel staff were very friendly and courteous. We were pleased with our hotel room. As mentioned in earlier reviews, the bathroom is massive and comes with a nice deep tub. The water pressure wasn't spectacular and the hot/cold shower knobs were very touchy. To get the "right temperature", we had to "play" with the knobs, so as to not get the water too hot or cold, which was tedious. The rooms give you two double or one king bed. We needed the doubles, which were somewhat comfortable, but the pillows are too small and either too soft or two hard. Next time, we will be bringing our own pillows. We enjoyed using the two comfy cozy bathrobes available to use during our stay. If you plan on using the fridge within the rooms, don't bother! There's absolutely no room! We brought our own ice chest with food for breakfast and lunch then had dinner at the resort. We enjoyed the $50 daily resort credit and used it towards dinners at Blue Sage and Tuscany Restaurants. The kids ate for free both nights, which was included in the package deal. So, for our dinner, we pretty much just paid for the tip. As far as dinner, Blue Sage wasn't very good. Service was extremely slow and not very attentive. Once our food came, we had to send a hamburger back that was cooked only to med. rare and not med well that we had ordered, then it took another 15 minutes to wait for it. With kids, you can only wait for food for so long and coloring gets old. Menu wasn't that great. The next night, dinner at Tuscany's was much better. We didn't have reservations, but didn't have to wait too long. Food was much better and service was more dependable. The pool area was really nice. I am big on cleanliness, and it was exactly what we got. No "dirty ring" around the waterslide, like we saw at the Phoenix Point Hilton Squaw Peak Resort. All the pools were clean as well. Pool staff were working non-stop, keeping the pool area tidy. They also were friendly and courteous. It was such a hot weekend and there were many water stations placed throughout the pool area that had suffiicient ice water pitchers and cups available to use. We never had any trouble finding shady spots to plop our towels and belongings (we only needed 1 chair, as we were always in the water). The kids loved the Lazy river and basketball pool. Near the basketball pool there was a live band...believe it was reggae (?)...sounded very tropical island, which was nice because it really made you feel like you were on vacation. For lunch our last day, we had those tacos at the taco bar that other contributors were talking about. Mmm Mmmm!!! Only $3 per taco and you can chose from chicken or beef, plus they had fresh taco fix'ins. The taco bar also sold hotdogs as well. The grounds are just beautiful. There are some close walking trails, which we didn't take advantage of this time, as it was too hot. But, I am sure there were some nice sights to see on the trails. Beautiful landscaping, waterfalls and flowers. Plenty of very nice outdoor furniture to relax on as well. This was worth paying for as the saying goes "you get what you pay for". This resort was inviting, clean, comfortable, relaxing, fun. We look forward to going back.

“Very nice clean room” My husband and I stayed at Sofitel for 4 nights. We booked a standard room but it was spacious and had a decent sitting area. Room was very clean and comfortable. We appreicated he hotel provided a bottle of water each day. However, first night, we only got one bottle of water then two bottles each night after first night. It is only few minutes away to the White house. We walked to Capitol Hill which was about 30 minutes. We took a circulator bus ($1 each way) to go to Gerogetown. A bus stop was close from the hotel. We had drink at Le Bar. It was a bit expensive but we enjoyed sitting at Patio. Only the negative side was there were not many restaurants around hotel area. There are plenty of choice of restaurants if you dont mind walking about 15 minutes. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay at Sofitel and would like to stay here again.

“Great Stay” The hotel was clean and the staff was tremendously helpful. I am traveling across the country for work and staying at Residence Inns; and this has been the only hotel to date that has CALLED me in advance to ask if they could do anything for me prior to my arrival; AND they had a packet of information waiting for me when I checked in. This packet included information for local attractions, restaurants, etc. SO very kind of them - and also extremely attentive. Will definitely return to this hotel when I am in the area!
“Superb location - rooms, service, food average at best” Five star Beautiful location diminished by average rooms, average food at high resort prices and poor service

“Nice, Central Location” I recently returned from a 2 night stay at The Muse. This was my first time staying at this hotel ( I usually stay at the Omni Berkshire). The hotel is located on 46th St between 6th & 7th Avenues, which is close to the subway, Times Square and Rockefeller Center; it enjoys a location that is very convenient to many things. However, with this proximity to Times Square comes more street noise than I have experienced when staying on the East side at the Omni. My room on the 7th floor #705 faced 46th street and there was lots of people cackling/laughing late into the night (3am). My second night it didn't bother me because I was acclimated to it and was able to ignore it. Check in was fast, friendly and efficient. I had an executive king room which was smaller than the rooms I've had at the Omni in the same price point, but being just one person, this was not a problem or a complaint, just an observation. The bathroom had adequate space as well and had a useful layout, where the toilet did not interfere with closing the door or with the tub, as can be a problem in hotels sometimes. One thing I found odd about the room, is that you really can't see out the window without standing on a chair. The windows are set back in a 2 foot wide ledge which is about 5 feet high, so you really can't see down into the street unless you drag over a chair and stand on it; you are really just looking upward. The room was well maintained and very clean. The furniture was all in very good condition. It appears that the hotel may be in the process of redoing some of the rooms, as there was a furniture delivery truck delivering mattresses and other items. Each evening from 5-6pm they have a wine reception in the lobby. I did not take advantage of this amenity, but saw them setting it up one night. I believe they also said that complimentary coffe and tea is available from 8-10am each morning near the restaurant. I enjoyed my stay at the Muse and will consider it for a future stay-- especially if I go to the theater, as it was extremely convenient walking back afterward.

“Most value for the Dollar-Downtown Chicago” For the price paid this is one of the best values in Downtown Chicago. If you don't need in house Restaurant or bar this a great palce to stay. Newly redone, one of the nicest continental breakfasts around (even has waffle maker), small work out area and rooms but by far the nicest in the low end Marriott properties (nicest Fairfiled I have stayed in). Price and location (right off N. Michigan Ave) can not be beat.

“Expected - typical Marriott” Recently stayed here on a 1 night business trip and felt it was a very standard Marriott. While clean, updated and comfortable, it lacked certain items that separate good from great. While the room on the 29th floor had a nice view and was spacious, there was no vending machine on the floor. And for some reason, you had to badge to this floor - but not to the floors above or below. There is no mini fridge in the room, which was a disappointment. And the door to the bathroom was within a centimeter from hitting the toilet when you opened/closed it. Conference rooms have adequate staff and oversight. Decor is standard. Location here is terrific - really the only memorable feature of the hotel. I didn't venture into the mall, but thought that the fact it was attached to one was cool. Because of the location, would consider staying again.

“Awesome hotel - but the noise !!!!” This Hilton is in an awesome location. I stayed for 6 nights and enjoyed it very much apart from one check-in issue and the noise from the heavy rail line. The hotel is located right at the gateway to the Gas Lamp Quarter restaurant area. A very short walk to Petco Park for Padres baseball and Convention Centre is right out front across the railway and trolley lines. The trolley station is right out front. RAILWAY NOISE: The trolley service (light rail) passes right beside the hotel and is great for getting around and for the most part this is a very quiet service. Unfortunately the heavy rail line also passes alongside the trolley tracks and the train drivers blow their very high pitched air horns numerous times as they pass by the hotel over 2 level crossings. There are numerous late evening and early morning trains that pass the hotel and this is very loud. My room was very good and i enjoyed the western view. Bed was comfortable and windows opened to allow fresh air and a respite from the constant air conditioning. The high speed internet is pretty fast both ethernet and wi-fi available although it is no longer complimentary. I booked the room at the Hilton website six weeks prior to my arrival and i was advised that internet was complimentary. Upon check-in I was advised payment was required for internet. I queried this with the check-in staff and she checked with supervisor and i was still asked to pay. I insisted and she asked supervisor a second time and complimentary internet was finally granted. This was my only hiccup at this hotel.

“Great Staff but the Rest, Not So Good” The Doubletree staff are so pleasant that, if the hotel even half matched that, it would be a great experience. Sadly, not so. Check-in was quick and efficient. Happiness with rooms seems to depend largely on location. Low floors are noisy. Some rooms are near main elevators or service elevator which can be very bad. High floors seem better. My room was a corner (overlooking a bus station) but the curtains didn't close all the way so the sun woke me up early each morning. Room decor is OK but not memorable. They've renovated but have forgotten a few things. Doors look and feel old. Tile around tub hasn't been replaced. Drapes/curtains look old. Beds are comfortable. There is a good-sized desk but it faces away from the TV. The chaise is comfy but you can't sit in it and watch TV. No safe. No minibar. Free water in the room, which is nice. The carpets in the main hallways are disgusting -- stained and torn -- and the hallways are somewhat prison-like. I was told the carpets will soon be replaced. The furniture looks worn. The hotel restaurant is TGI Fridays. Room service is TGI Fridays. The good news is that there are plenty of very good local restaurants within easy walking distance. My stay was marked by a number of problems. The electrical outlet at the desk didn't work meaning I had to unplug the desk lamp to charge my computer. One of the floor lamps presented a safety hazard. A large bug was crawling on the ceiling over my bed. In fairness, each of these was fixed immediately, but I had more issues in one day at this hotel than I usually have in 5 stays at other hotels. On the plus side, internet connection was the easiest I've experienced ever. Wireless and super-easy. Attended a conference at the hotel. At lunch, some tables weren't provided silverware or drinks. Refreshment service (continental breakfast, beverage service) during the meeting was inferior to most conferences I've attended. However, the food at social hour was surprisingly tasty and plentiful. Overall, having stayed at Doubletree Hotels many times, this one was a disappointment. The staff definitely tries really hard but they can't overcome the basic deficiencies. The good news is that the price is right. If you're looking for a basic hotel close to the downtown area (Beale St., etc.), this is ok. However, don't expect anything at all special.

“Had my wedding here and the service was sub-par” I had my wedding here and did not get the attention that was required of an out of town bride. For the wedding rehearsal NO ONE from the hotel was there to help us, the lady Kwanjaii Burgess didn't even bother to show up. We did it all on our own though and everything turned up fine but I was by that point really frustrated. The room was a special suite for honeymooners which was comparable to a room at the Hilton down the street. THEN when we checked out all these sports people were leaving at the same time and it took 45 minutes for our car to be brought from the Valet.

“Lovely stay at LONDON NYC” I just returned from a 2 night stay over Memorial Day weekend at LONDON NYC. Itravel to NYC a couple of times a year for business/leisure. This was my first stay at LONDON, but will not be my last. The suite was huge! I loved the sitting area with its large flat screen TV. (One small complaint...the seating piece in the are is beautiful to look at, but uncomfortable to relax upon.) The bed was comfortable with very high thread count silky soft sheets. It was a nice touch to have a 2nd tv in the sleeping area. The robes were beautiful and comfortable too. The hightlight in my opinion was the double shower. It was beautiful and quite large with 2 separate shower heads on either end. (Rain shower with an additional handheld shower on one end and a traditional showerhead on tthe other end.) The small mosiac tiles in the bathroom were some of the prettiest I've ever seen. A+ to the designer of the bathrooms. Front desk staff were efficient although not incredibaly friendly. Michelle, the front desk manager was fabulous and most accomodating when a small problem arose during our stay. She is to be commended for her outstanding customer service. All in all, a nice place with a "reasonable" price, in a good location. LONDON has worked its way to one of the top places for me to stay while in NYC.

“GREAT, EXCEPT FOR MINOR FLAW” Was there on Sunday night 6/24.12, with family due to home's air condition breaking down. Nice room and amenities, excellent staff, except for locust infestation. Manager changed our room, but by midnight we had killed four in our new room. Aside from this problem, i really liked the room. It had everything a 31/2 star hotel would have. Fridge, microwave, shampoos etc.

“Great stay near the Speedway” My friends and I stayed at the Wingate so we could play golf at the Brickyard Crossing. The hotel is very clean and the breakfast is just what we needed to start our day. The beds are very comfortable. The rooms have a refrigerator to keep your beverages cold and a microwave for warming up snacks. The hotel is a few miles from the speedway but the places closer to the track are rundown.

“First Class Accomodations” I had a business trip to Boston scheduled for mid-October, which is high season for tourists wanting to see the fall leaves. I was very lucky and booked this room at an outstanding price on through one of the airlines. At any price, this is a very nice hotel. The room was extremely modern decor and comfortable. While the location is somewhat isolated and out of the way from most other hotels, it is very close to Hanover Street, where all the good Italian restaurants are located in the North End. It is about an 8 block walk from the hotel to the nearest subway station. It was raining during my stay in the mornings, and I was able to quickly get a taxi on the first day, but not the second. The fitness center is in a nearby building and the spa offers yoga classes (at an extra charge).

“Luxurious, intimate charm” As a frequent vistor to New York City, I am always on the lookout for exceptional hotel values. To be perfectly honest, I had never even heard of The Fitzpatrick Grand Central. When Travelzoo recently offered the unheard of rate of $149 at this property and after I had read the nearly unanimous rave reviews on Tripadvisor I knew that I needed to experience this hotel. I wasn`t disappointed. Let me begin by saying that this is not a glitzy New York hotel with a huge, bustling, noisy lobby with contemporary, flashy decor, endless restaurants and shops and a big city vibe. Upon entering the lobby, I was immediately taken with the intimate, peaceful charm. There are 2 fireplaces, shelves of books and a an immediate feeling of welcoming warmth. Check in with the personable staff was quick and efficient. The biggest and most impressive part of my stay, however, was the room itself. This is hotel luxury that could easily put to shame many of The Fitzpatrick Grand Central`s more famous neighbors. While the room was of average size, thoughtful details and amenities abound. Decor is traditional with beautiful cherrywood furnishings, tasteful lamps, gold framed wall prints, unblemished carpets and walls and luxurious draperies with matching canopy over the bed`s headboard. The pillowtop bed was remarkably comfortable offering the best sleep I`ve had in recent memory. There is a trouser press, small refrigerator (mercifully not the usual minibar with absurdly priced items), iron, ironing board, coffee maker and umbrella. There are 2 phones as well as another in the bath. The marble bathroom is gorgeous, albeit compact. There is no tub, but a huge shower with a glass wall. Tarocco bath products are offered as well as thick towels, terry robes, shaving mirror and hair dryer. Both housekeeping and maintenance are stellar. My room was towards the back of the hotel and I heard virutally no noise from the street or adjacent neighbors. Hallways are somewhat narrow, but brightly lit and nicely decorated. This is a beautiful hotel and the Fitzpatrick management should be commended on running such a tight ship. This isn`t the usual New York City hotel experience. It`s infinitely better than that.

“Residence Inn at Dupont-Great location” Great location, close enough to Metro to get anywhere, right off Dupont Circle yet quiet and comfortable. Staff is very friendly and helpful, very complete breakfast buffet every morning and spacious (we stayed in a studio that was very large) rooms. Good value for the money spent and quite location yet close to everything. Would definitely stay here again.

“Disappointing” Hotel seemed a bit dreary. Seems poetic as the staff seemed just the same (nothing bad mind you). Rooms had a musty odor, however everything looked clean. Bed was standard and nothing was outstanding. Disappointing overall.

“Large room and good service but the wall is very thin” As we travelled back from Vancouver on Amtrak at night, I chose to stay at the regular chain hotel for one night. Instead of two rooms, we got one King-bed suite. The room was large and clean, but we could not find a way to turn one floor lamp on. There were a few long hair left in the bathroom. The front staff was very helpful even at late night. Room service was also good too. There was a view of Space Needle. But the wall was so thin that you could not hear TV when the guests next door happened to be loud talkers. It probably is hard to complete with new stylish hotels, but I think they were trying hard by rennovation and the good service.

“I expected a lot better service” I was at this hotel recently for the CSI Conference. I checked in on a Saturday, dropped off my luggege and then headed down to the tradeshow area to see if my booth had been set up. Later in the evening, I returned to my room and was sitting on the edge of my bed, talking on my cell phone, running my hands along the bedspread when I hit something crusty. There were several thick white stains over the bedspread. It really grossed me out to say the least. I called the service desk to complain and to request clean bedding, and the lady who answered said they'd deal with it ASAP. Over the next hour and a half I waitied for someone to come, spoke numerous times with the service desk before someone showed up. The cleaning lady they send was very rude, and had no idea what the problem was. I showed her the stains, she gave me a dirty look, stipped the cover off the bed and left, saying she's have to fins a clean one. Likely 20 minutes later she returned and didn't speak at all to me, except when she was leaving she asked if she had to trun down my bed for me. She left without saying anything else, even when I said thanks, etc. Over the course of my 5 night stay I made 6 phone calls which lasted less than 1 minute each (checking VM). Minimum charge for long distance calling is $13 and change. I couldn't believe it....over $80 in phone charges for 6 brief phone calls, all under 60 seconds. A friend at the same conference woke up one morning and had no cold water. Someone else's toilet wasn't working properly. It just seemed like there were a lot of little issues. My favorite was the spitefull cleaning lady who I asked to leave while I changed my clother and brushed my hair. I must have left a bit of a mess of hair in the sink, when I came back later she had taken the time to tighly wind it around my bar of soap and put it back in the soap dish. I am not sure what kind of statement she meant to make with that, I just found it to be odd.

“Great historic hotel” What a great location! Right on the Freedom Trail, just around the corner from the Boston Common and pretty much a short walk to most down-town sights. The hotel is beautiful and grand and it is great to see they have not tried to modernise the building as the history of this hotel is fascinating. The check in staff were very pleasant and helpful as were all staff we encountered throughout the hotel. The room (double) was a good size, peaceful, large bathroom and super comfy beds. There is no free wi-fi in the room (there is in the lobby), but if you join their club wi-fi is free so we joined during check in for the free wi-fi. When we booked we picked the package that included the Boston cream pie and a book on the hotel - the pie is great! It is shame though that they only give you one book even though there are two people staying and you get two pies. The only thing that prevented me from giving five stars was that the TV reception was terrible which was frustrating after a long day of sightseeing. The breakfast was also good, but was a bit pricey so we found a really cheap place across the road up the side alley of the old town hall which did a $5 omelette. Overall, I would definitely stay here again.

“A Gem” We booked months ago through a Travel Zoo deal. Weren't too sure of the location, but now would only stay here if we returned. The location was two blocks from Union Square. It felt perfectly safe day and night. There was a doorman at all times, and he was helpful in hailing a cab or assisting with luggage. We actually rode BART from SFO and then walked a couple of blocks to the hotel. We even walked to the Wharf from the hotel one day and used the cable and street cars the other days. The lobby was gorgeous. The check in was fast and easy. There were two small, old elevators with beautiful wood paneling. They were fast in service. The two room suite we had was perfect. The bedroom was a very comfortable king bed with feather pillows and a down comforter. There was a flat screen TV, a mini fridge, and a desk with chair. Wi-fi was free. There were two animal print robes in the closet. There were also extras in the room that could be purchased through use - pj's, cozy socks, and an umbrella. There was a small hallway to connect to the living room. The bathroom was located off the hallway. It was not large, but was nice. Great water pressure. The living room had a pull out sofa, chairs, coffee table, flat screen TV, and ottoman. The TV cabinet was locked and contained food and drink items that could be purchased by use, as well as small toys that could be purchased by use. The views were of the city from three large windows. There was no coffee maker in the room, but complimentary coffee, tea, and hot chocolate were available each morning in the lobby. We did not visit the business center or sauna.

“Great Stay” Great reception staff and location. Bed was too soft.... Shower needs a curtain. Room was clean and being on the 5th floor, it was very quiet. Took advantage of pass to 12th Street Gym - great facility. Hotel is definitely a repeat destination.

“excellent location, very comfortable, good atention” I stayed at the Library for six nights. The location is great: one block from the Public Library and the wonderful Bryant Park, near everything but not noisy. The bus stop is in the corner and the subway station is only two blocks away. It is also very close to Fifth Ave, The hotel is very nice. The staff is very gentle. The breakfast is very good and during all the day you may have something to drink and some snacks for free at the second floor in a very nice reading room, full of books and with good music playing. In that same place, from 5 to 7 they serve wine and cheese, also as a treat for guests. There is wireless internet access for free in all the hotel. The room we had was very nice and comfortable though perhaps little in comparison to the price. I recommend this hotel. I travel constantly to NYC and this is one of the bests hotels I had been in. It is a little expensive but it is worth. You will have a very good time there. The music, the ambiance of the hotel make a great difference.

“Gone WAY downhill” Years ago, The Colonnade was a great hotel. When a conference I was attending included it among its listings, I did not hesitate to book a room here. Just before the trip, I checked TripAdvisor reviews and was alarmed to see a rash of negative reports, mainly citing ongoing construction. I sent an e-mail to the hotel and received reassurance from the director of rooms that I would be assigned a room well-away from the construction zone. Well, I was, but that was all you could say about the room. In contrast to previous stays, it was small, dark and very worn out. The sheets were thin, showing through to a double-sized mattress pad turned sideways on a king-size bed and the thin blanket was totally pilled with its satin lining in shreds. Curtain liners were unraveling.. You get the picture, not anywhere near a 4-star hotel. Guestroom WiFi is contracted out to Guestlinx and is quite expensive - $39.95 for 3-days. It worked the first night, then the entire system went down; I spent a long time dealing with the outsourced automated system before getting to a human being in India or somewhere on a connection so bad he could not hear me and hung up. I had to start over. again, not 4-star service. The shower head was cheesy and water pressure was uneven. Noise from the hallway (near the elevator) came right into the room, worst of all was the last morning at 4 AM I was subjected to loud yelling and swearing in the hall. Although the staff was very nice and breakfast at Brasserie Jo quite nice, I would not consider returning to The Colonnade. There are too many other better options in Boston. Even though I e-mailed the director of rooms my displeasure during my stay, I heard back nothing, and no compensation was offered me when upon checkout I replied in the negative to "was everything OK?" I am sorry to add a negative review, as this was an old sentimental favorite, but there were just too many things wrong to retain my former loyalty. Look elsewhere.

“Decent hotel but call your own taxi....” The good--The hotel and room was clean, which for me, is on the top of my list of must haves and although I did not partake in the breakfast the five other members traveling with me thought it was decent. We are Hilton Honors members so the internet was free. We loved the ceiling fan in our rooms especially after a long hot day. The location was very convenient to the sites and you can easily walk to the White House. The not so good--There was some confusion upon check in regarding the type of rooms we booked but the gentlemen at the desk rectified the issue with no problem. I only write "not so good" because had the hotel been booked or unable fix the issue, my husband and I would have been separated from our party as we would have needed to check into another hotel. When we did get our room and two other members of our party entered their room, the beds had not been completely made. Though the rooms appeared clean, this made me question just how well housekeeping was doing their job. After a phone call down to the desk, personnel were sent up to rectify the situation but I did make them change the sheets. After this initial misstep, we found the room was thoroughly cleaned every day. Also, with temperatures near 100 degrees, I knew we would need extra towels and wash cloths so I left a note and a good tip so they would be there when we arrived back in the afternoon. Upon arrival in the afternoon, nothing extra was left. I had to call and leave a message with housekeeping but to their credit, they did bring them down right away. Our view from the window was bricks from another building. View isn't that important to me on short stays but I mention it for others. The A/C is loud when clicking on and off but as long as our room was cool, it was a small price to pay! The bad--CALL FOR YOUR OWN TAXI. The second day we were there we asked the hotel clerk to call a taxi for us. He called someone in the hotel, who approached us and said I have a cab right outside. As soon as we entered the vehicle, I saw there was no meter. As very experienced travelers, I would have exited the vehicle immediately but we had two elderly relatives with us so I let it go. Of course the cost was ridiculous to take us one mile. We had our GPS and cell phones with us so we knew the distance and direction of every where we went. We could have easily walked to the site if we did not have other members of our party who struggled with the temperature and humidity. We called a cab to take us back to the hotel from the same location and it as $12.50 rather than $20.00 and it was the same route. After that we hailed a cab ourselves or called one if needed. We used three different companies and they were all fantastic and much cheaper than the cab the hotel called for us. Also, we have been to many major cities, domestically and internationally and DC was the easiest place, hands down, to hail a cab.

“Unusual upgrade” We booked online and reserved a double room with an extra roll away bed for $71 per night. When we confirmed the reservation just before the trip the hotel advised that only smoking rooms were available. Upon arrival the front desk offered us the option of moving into the living room/dining room of a non-smoking suite. The catch was that we would be on two sofa beds and a roll away. We agreed to this as it was at no extra charge, it would be a change from the ordinary and the room was non-smoking. The main door opened into a small foyer revealing two separate rooms with key card access. Our room was roughly 40'x25' and even with both sofa beds extended, we still had plenty of room to manuever despite the existence of the roll away, six-chair dining table, armoire, writing desk, end tables and two sitting chairs. The big problem though was the quality of the bedding. No matter how you dress it up, a sofa bed is an uncomfortable night's sleep and mine seemed to have an especially thin mattress. More dissapointing was the bathroom. The tile was old and cracking. The toilet seemed to be an afterthought. It was wedged flush (excuse the pun) with the tub and mere inches from the vanity. It made for some rather awkward positioning when one needed a few minutes of quiet contemplation. As a minor point, the bell captain and the too-numerous-to-count bell hops were more interested in standing around outside than helping people with their bags. On the plus side, the bartenders were genuine in their banter and the whole first floor area had a great old world hotel feel to it. The location to the Arlington T stop is very handy and the faux Irish pub around the corner serves a quality pint of Guinness. If you like chain eateries, there is a Legal Sea Food nearby as well as a couple of other places.

“Good NYC room for a good price” I recently went to the city for a one day shopping trip and found a room here for a great rate, comparable to other hotels in the area. Like most hotels in Manhattan, the room is small, however Holiday Inn maximizes the space as best it can. Check in was smooth, there is a restaurant in the hotel and times square, herald square, madison square gardne adn the empire state building are all within walking distance.

“Even better than expected” Spent a night at the hotel as part of a whirlwhind business trip. Checkin swift but friendly. I *like* the separation of lobby from other functions (lounge, bar, business center, whatever), so others' complaints regarding the minimal lobby are positives for me, as we had two intelligent and affable attendants to ourselves. The lounge (6th floor?) is swanky and comfortable. Restaurant a bit too pricey for my per diem so didn't try it. The room (their smaller, courtyard-view room) was perfect for solo traveler. Great design, clean, etc. Bonus: their contracted limo service to the airport was fabulous and with cost comparable to a cab.

“New Go to Hotel at the Arboretum” I've stayed at several hotels at the Arboretum, but I've now found a new favorite. What a nice surprise. Great welcome, clean property both inside and out, quiet and very easy access on and off Mopac. I recommend this hotel 100%, and will most definately return next time my travels take me to Austin.

“OK for Short Buisness Trip, not for Extended Stay Though” Stayed here for a week in January and December of 2005. This place was clean. The problem is that it used to be a Howard Johnson, and converted to a Fairfield. It definitely looks like an old HoJo, with the updated Marriott trade looking rooms and fixtures. It is convenient to the airport, and there is a shuttle train outside the front of the hotel that takes you downtown. You really do not need a car if you stay here, because of all the convenient public transport. There is no restauraunt here, and the closest thing is a half mile walk to a McDonald's. You could walk across the street and eat at the Hyatt's restaurants though. The continental breakfast is minimal, and does not change from day to day. All in all it is an ok place to stay for a short trip, but not on vacation, or for an extended period of time. There was no HBO, and no FoxNews channel. They did have CNN and MSNBC though...

“WONDERFUL WONDERFUL WONDERFUL” The hotel location its self is just worth it (right across from the famous Carlyle). New York's finest shopping is right at your finger tip along with some wonderful restaurants. Right down stairs and even on the roof, you can enjoy Chef. Boloud's amazing cuisine at Bar Boloud or the roof top terrace. My room was like staying in someone's guest room. Comfy bed with high end Italian linens, great bathroom outfitted with waterworks hardware (the shower was one of the best!), and a great interior design. During my stay I was never once disappointed at all in the quality of the service. The ratings do not lie one bit on trip advisor. I really recommend this hotel for a romantic weekend. Well done Surrey!

“Amazing Service over New Year's Eve” During our trip to Los Angeles the other day, my girlfriend asked me which hotel I've enjoyed the most this past year. Without hesitation I said the Renaissance Harborplace Hotel in Baltimore and she immediately agreed. The front desk concierge was extremely helpful from helping us check-in due to such a busy night (New Year's Eve) to additional amenities. Due to my Marriott Platinum status we were upgraded to a splendid concierge level room overlooking the harbor. The wine and cheese Platinum arrival gift was superb. All in all a perfect stay during such a hectic time of year.

“Overpriced Accomadations.....more bang for the bucks at other Chi Hotels” I personally thought this Hotel was overpriced. The only reason why I stayed here is because the wedding party that I was in chose this hotel. Our room was small; there were charges for internet and the fitness center. These items should be complimentary with the price I paid. I also thought that the bathroom could be a bit cleaner and bigger. Some updating to the decor would be nice too. I did find the bed comfy, the lobby beautiful and the location great. I have stayed at many Chicago hotels and I have paid less and gotten more. I would not stay at this Hotel again.

“Great Value/ Big Comfortable Room” The Quincy was excellent for the money. A big comfortable king size bed and a sectional sofa with coffee table left plenty of spare room. There was a small fridge/microwave and coffee maker for use in the small parlor off of the bathroom. The staff was friendly as was the housekeeping. L street itself is boring although there was some life to be found on 19th st right around the corner. Dupont circle is 2 blocks north and there are many good restaurants close by.

“Great value!” We had a great stay at this Hampton. It was conveniently located near the Interstate, so getting to and from the LA attractions was easy and they were not too far away. Where the hotel is located is not fancy at all, but I felt safe at all times. The hotel itself seemed really new. The hotel owner/manager greeted us at the door and answered our questions about where to park. Check-in was fast and smooth. Our room was very nice, clean and newly decorated. The beds and pillows were very comfortable -- I'm very picky about this. Breakfast was the traditional, abundant Hampton fare. Everything was kept well-stocked and we didn't have a problem finding a table. Our favorite thing about this hotel was the pool! Lucky for us, we had it all to ourselves both nights. I usually don't spend much time in hotel pools as they are usually too cold for me, but this pool was heated nice and warm. ;-) We spent a few hours each night in the pool and the kids loved that! I'd definitely picked this hotel again if we were staying in the area. It truly was a bargain.

“Trendy hotel but beware of the small rooms” Stayed at the hotel for a company meeting. Checking in was easy, as was checking out. Everything in between those two events wasn't exactly unpleasant, but then again it wasn't particularly nice... although the stay was definitely memorable. On first entering the room, I realized that the room was small... so small that it was described by many work associates as claustrophobic. The dark walls are about 2 feet wider than the bed. Note that another interesting feature of the hotel is the clear glass separating the shower from the bedroom. The window can be obscured by a thin curtain pulled from inside the shower. So yes - that brings up the bathroom... you can hardly move. Sitting on the toilet, your knees touch the wall. Interestingly enough, however, the amenities are pretty nice. Which brings me to the other point... once you get over the fact that everything in your room is small, you can have a fun time in the hotel. It is nice, clean, with trendy bars... steps away from the Time Warner center, Columbus Circle, Central Park, and lots of other sites in Midtown West. You can find nice restaurants, places to shop, and things to do. If you are looking for more of a gritty New York City feel (and maybe larger room), I might recommend going farther down into midtown (or lower) - even somewhere around Times Square or Rockefeller Plaza. Otherwise, the Hudson is a decent location in the area if you can deal with some of the down sides.

“My Go-To Lodging in NYC” After all these years, why hadn't I reviewed my NYC crib before now? Have I been selfish of sharing the place where I usually stay in NYC for my business travel? Forgive me for hiding Hampton Chelsea in my silo. I've been staying there practically since it opened, and for good reason: best lodging for the price in the most accessible neighborhood in New York City. It helps that most of my NYC clients are nearby, but given good proximity to the subway you could have a client in Far Rockaway or Staten Island or Hoboken and still stay here. The excellence is in consistent adherence to Hampton standard, even in a crazy/pricey Manhattan environment. Sure, rooms are smaller here (Tip: If you're solo get a queen bed room, you'll appreciate the extra space) but they are cleaned thoroughly, you will get the Hampton amenities (especially in the bathroom) and the free brekkie is up to Hampton standard (unless you all come down at once and the attendant is overwhelmed, it sometimes happens, understandable). HHonors has unfailingly given me a high-floor smoking room, with great views on either side. Jeez, check-in is so easy I'm practically looked at and handed the key card. I would think of staying nowhere else in Chelsea, for business or otherwise. BTW on a leisure trip I really enjoy this part of NYC for good chowish restos, nice cocktail spots (especially Rainbow Lounge) and a more humanly-scaled ambiance than other places in Manhattan. Please consider staying there, but don't all go there at once...keep a room for me!

“Huge and wonderful” Stayed here overnight and I have to say, the room was fantastic. Thank God it is off and away from the busy highway. Room has very dark drapes, so you can sleep in. We had a king-size bed and it was great. It is a big place, so there are lots of rooms, but noise was not a problem. Buffet breakfast was a real plus and very nicely presented. The hotel is close to some mall areas and theaters, but not close to downtown, so don't stay here just because of price. The indoor pool and health facilities are excellent.

“A Zen spot above the hustle of Fifth Ave” My wife & I stayed at the Setai over July 4th weekend in a junior suite. From the moment we walked through the doors at 7am, the service was impeccable but not overbearing. Our room was spacious and featured 2 TVs (+1 in the bathroom), Nespresso machine, a separate tub/shower and WC. Once in the room we had to strain to hear any significant noise other than the occasional ambulance. The closet had ample space for our bags and hanging items. Strangely, there really wasn't any storage in the room itself. The Setai's location on Fifth Ave is convenient to walk to Central Park and the other high-end shops, but it's a hike! The hotel's neighbors are a mix of tourist shops and businesses, it's not the same feeling as walking out of the Mandarin or Plaza. We both succumbed to spa treatments which were delightfully executed, but both therapists gave us the hard sell for Setai's products before leaving. We treated ourselves to one room service breakfast (excellent, but like $80) and ate out the rest of the days.

“Watch out for extra fees and charges.” So, this was a rather dated hotel/resort that rents out the rooms at a pretty good price, at least in the winter when you cannot use the resort facilities. The room was quite large and comfortable. It seems that they make up the difference in price through the extra charges for parking $32 a day(!!) and internet ($15). This is not downtown, so it was not like they are short of space. in fact, the location is away from town, and with little public transport it is a bit inaccessible - the local area is nice enough with parks and beaches (rather sad looking). Staff were OK but not particularly helpful.

“Clean, comfortable and quiet” The room was well laid out, clean, comfortable bed, quiet. Small hotel with not much of a view from many room probably but a good location for Wall St., South Street Seaport and the World Trade Center, Sept. 11th memorial. The front desk staff were friendly. There were 2 computers for guest use in the (tiny) lobby and another type of kiosk. There is a restaurant and room service, neither of which we had time to use. Check in and check out were very easy. Shampoo and soap provided.

“Very Nice Hotel - Good Location” Very nice hotel and the location in D.C. is great. Rooms were very clean and spacious. My one complaint was the toilets looked like they belonged in a public bathroom. I also don't like the atrium where you can see curtain-covered windows to several of the hotel rooms. But those were minor complaints. Overall, a very nice stay and would recommend the hotel.

“pros and cons” Overall it was ok considering the price compared to other hotel/hostel. It was closed in the winter of 2009 as the city fined it for over-crowding but they have changed this now and limit 2 guests per room. Accomodations in New York are expensive so you have to compare what's available the time you go. My friend and I stayed in the 2 bed dorm room. We never stayed in a hostel before. We turned the air conditioner on at night to muffle the noise from doors slamming. Pro's- a)it's on the red subway line-if you get off on 96th you can take lines 1,2,3 (2 and 3 are express) b) there is only 2 guests per room in the dorm c) vanity in room Con's-a) pre-pay up front with cash or travellers cheques...no credit cards (technically you should be able to get a refund if you leave early however some posters complained they could not) b) one slow, small elevator c) kitchen facility is limited if you want to cook. d) there was no hot water to take a shower the first day we checked in at 3pm but the following 2 mornings there was hot water e) mattress is a narrow thin box-spring feel mattress (however it might be common for hostels as no one has mentioned this)

“Adorable Boutique Hotel in Chicago” I wasn't sure I was going to love the Burnham - I'm a huge fan of Kimpton, but knew this was an older hotel. I could not have been more wrong! I spent just one night with my mom and it was fabulous. The hotel is small-ish and has an art-deco feel. The staff, from valet to front desk were absolutely wonderful. The service is fantastic and sincere, without being obtrusive. When you check in, you get regular old keys, which was kind of neat and added to the antique feel of the property. Our room - which had two double beds - was much larger than I expected. The ceilings were quite high, which I think added to the spacious feeling. I loved the decor -- especially the navy blue drapes with gold writing. Beds were very, very comfortable and bathroom was spacious with nice Aveda amenities. The real stand-out at the Burnham is the Atwood Cafe, their onsite restaurant. We had the three course meal for $40.00, which was a fantastic price. The food was simple (we had vegetable soup, cod and a chocolote peanut butter cake for dessert), but so so good. Also, the portions were perfect. Not too big (which I can't stand), so you could really enjoy each course. Service was out of this world. Again, helpful but not too much. The next time I'm in Chicago, I'll definitely be returning to this hotel. Loved it!
“Great Stay” Only great things to say...comfortable bed, clean rooms, and a friendly helpful staff. Special thanks to Karen in the sales department for always taking amazing care of me!

“Fantastic service & nice facility” I stayed here for 2 nights for a conference and was very pleased. Best part: super friendly and helpful staff, from the front desk to housekeeping to room service delivery. Really made the difference in my stay. Other pluses: room service food was excellent; room very clean overall; good soundproofing between rooms. My room was also decent-sized for an urban hotel. No big negatives. It's a few blocks walk to Fisherman's Wharf so convenient, but since it's not right on the Wharf, you're missing views and the ambiance, as well. And to the Hyatt decorating team ... next time you paint, brighten it up a bit! Lots of greys and dark colors make the place awfully drab. Overall, though, definitely recommend.

“A Disappointing Stay” It was my sister's first weekend away from her kids in seven years and I wanted this to be an extra special getaway. I booked a room with two beds, not expecting to find twin beds on arrival... However, that was not the only reason we didn't sleep well - the walls creaked very loudly all night long! According to the staff at the front desk, that is to be expected when staying in the Windy City. (I have never experienced this when staying at other high rise hotels in Chicago.) The creaking stopped after we moved to a lower floor. Another perk to moving was that the second room was less austerely decorated. Service overall was good, but for a hotel of this caliber, our experience was somewhat lacking.

“Best choice for hotel in downtown San Diego” The entire stay was superb with a staff that was so attentive and caring that you would have thought we owned the hotel. Rooms are a delight and if you have the good luck to check in late, Leslie at the front desk will make you feel like you are home.

“Good location/hotel depending on your interests” This hotel is a good value and choice for those who are interested in seeing downtown LA (including Olvera Street, Chinatown, Union Station) and saving money. If you don't have a car and have a short stay focused on the above sites, this hotel is perfect. You can walk to everything (Mexican/Chinese/other restaurants), and the Red Metro Line stops out front and goes to Hollywood. However, if you are not comfortable in urban environments with homeless people on the sidewalks, etc., this is not a good choice. If you have a car, this is still a good choice -- parking is only six dollars a day, and freeway access is excellent. I plan to stay here again. The wi-fi was great, the room clean/safe, and the staff was friendly.

“European splendor” beautiful place with European charm. No complaints, great location, (never like parking in Chicago, though). It was $35 a night next door. Large beautiful lobby, a touch of class. Fantastic location for downtown, Navy Pier, and the great Grant Park(Millenium Park, too)...Loved it.

“Stupid Hotel with Stupid Staff & Amenities” I stayed for 3 nights in Ultra Savvy Suite on 3rd floor, Location-wise its near to Love Field airport-Dallas. Problems: 1.No restaurant in hotel, so even after paying $300+ you have no choice but to go outside 2. No room service, everything need to buy tooth-paste, brush, drinking water etc 3. I paid for 4nights and ask front desk to pre-vacant room after 3 days, I got folio for 3 days when checkout but soon after 2hrs I got bill for 4 nights Which is ridiculous. And when I contact staff they argued that I booked for 4 nights so it will be charged for 4 nights even though I vacant in 3nights, really stupid hotel & staff Shall never stay in Sheraton Hotel ...

“Rock star treatment” We booked a mid-priced room at the W for our anniversary. To our dismay on arrival, they tried to put us in the smallest room they had, even though we paid at least two levels above that price. The smallest room is more comparable to what you get at Aloft, and was a queen bed, not even a king. When we protested, first we were offered free breakfast. Then when that wasn't enough, they proposed a $50 room credit. My husband kept firmly but politely insisting they had to have a better room, which was what we really wanted. Finally, they did some checking and gave us the penthouse suite for the night! Apparently there was some tehcnical reason it was free and not available for renting, so the W wasn't out any money by doing us this huge favor. It was IN-credible. I think it's called the "WOW" Suite or something like that, and Wow is right. We had two bedrooms and two bathrooms plus a living room and breakfast area overlooking a wrap-around view of downtown Austin and the lake. Needless to say, it was like getting an anniversary present and the W turned our frowns upside down. This is a hip part of downtown to explore, and the restaurant downstairs, Trace is a great place for dinner or cocktails. Afterwards we still got an email of apology, and were not charged anything higher for the better room. It made for a very memorable stay and my only regret is that I doubt we'll ever see the inside of that fantastic room again - too pricey! But we partied like rock stars for one night anyway.

“Not Bad!” I've stayed here a few times now...The hotel is slightly dated, and I don't really like outside-access room (where your door opens to the outdoors instead of to a hallway), but with the rooms I've been given here, I can hardly complain...As a Hilton Gold member, I've always been upgraded here to a GIANT 2-story suite...The layout is amazing. I shared the room with a friend from Grad School and we could have gone without seeing each other for days inside this room! Internet worked great, the room was clean (although not the most modern I've had). The included breakfast was good, although it's a bit of a pain getting to your room...The property is several unconnected buildings...If you can't get parking in front of your building, it can be a hike to your door. But I'll come back again and again--hopefully getting the two-story room again!

“Very frendly staff and clean and close” I stayed at this hotel from oct 28th through november 2nd. the staff that waited on me were friendly and helpfull. not once did they complain or anything. they were helpful with my questions and my late arrival. when i had problems with the door key card they were very helpful. When i accidentally checked out early due to me being confused on the time(the alarm clock i had with me is very easy to mess up the time when setting the alarm and when it read 10:40PM i thought it was really 10:40AM and i was panicking thinking i was going to miss my train back to Chicago.) they were very helpful and re-instated my reservation. When i had more problems with the door key(i went up and down in the elevator at least 5 times trying to get the card to work) they did not complain or anything. they ended up putting me in a different room(this was after i checked out by accident) for the rest of the stay. i would highly recommend this place. i did not try the cafe so cannot comment on that.

“Schönes Hotel mit gutem Frühstück” Ich war Ende August im Hotel "The Alex". Der Service war wirklich Klasse. Die Angestellten waren super freundlich. Das Zimmer war groß und sehr sauber. Morgens gab es Frühstück, welches man sich auf einer Karte aussuchen konnte. Die Bedienung war echt super Nett und das Essen hat gut geschmeckt. Immer wieder gern! Habe mich sehr wohlgefühlt und kann dieses Hotel wirklich nur weiterempfehlen

“Great location, good fitness center, great pool = fun stay in NYC” Stayed here 2 nights with friends. Room is definitely New York style, i.e. small. Anything more than two people makes it feel cramped, especially is you have luggage. Room is small but adequate for one person. Room was clean and the view on 7th avenue was nice. I must say the room was a little too hot, even though we tried to control the temperature. We ended up leaving the window open most of the time. Hotel lobby is spacious and offers free internet and printers (albeit those were not working a the time). I really enjoyed the fitness center (although it is rather small and more cardio-oriented) and the swimming pool which is very nicely landscaped (indoor) and of a good size for being in the center on Manhattan. All in all, a good location in a qonderful position.

“Accommodating Accomodations” about a $40 cab ride from Midway. Check in was quick and I never saw a large line at the front desk during my stay. Too bad there are few Swissotels, because it is a good brand. Room was comfortable with a mini fridge. Bathrooms have a glass shower stall as well as a bathtub. Good lighting throughout the room. Gorgeous view overlooking the Navy Pier. Health Club is solid with about 10 cardio machines. A variety of new weight machines provides a good upper and lower body workout. Indoor pool & hot tub. Suana in the locker room. Great hotel for outdoor runners: just accross the street and down the stairs is Chicago's Riverwalk offering traffic-free running along the river and lake.Palm restaurant adjacent to lobby. One floor down is a plain restaurant for breakfast. $26 for full buffet that has someinteresting dishes like Spanish sausage & eggs.This was an overflow hotel for a conference I had at the Hyatt which is 1 block away. The housekeeper volunteered to reheat my deep-dish pizza that I doggie-bagged. Ask the front desk for chocolates. They give you a small bag of Lindt squares. Hotel was spotless and the beds very comfortable. Large flat screen tv (at least 46"). Too bad they don't have a frequent stayer program (or do they?). Terry cloth robes. Another nice touch: umbrella in the closet. A rechargeable flashlight is mounted there too.

“Prisonstyle View and Poor Management” I am writing this review as a concerned Hilton Honors Diamond member. This is not your typical Embassy Suites and I can not agree with the many positive reviews on here. This hotel has many interior rooms facing a bare concrete wall about 6 feet from your window. The front desk is pushing these rooms. We checked in at 3 p.m. and it took us almost 1 hour of arguing with the manager on duty to get moved to a different location. During that 1 hour the manager on duty gave us plenty of attitude and lied to us hoping that we will give up on our request to move. My Hilton Honors Diamond Status did not help. As a matter of fact there is ZERO Hilton Honors recogntion at this property. Your Gold or Diamond status will actually hurt your chances of landing a more desirable room. During our 2 day stay maid service was only provided upon request and the breakfast buffet ran out of certain food items. On a positive note I have to say that the rooms were clean. At least housekeeping does a good job.

“Great getaway” We stayed for a night here as a getaway as a couple. It was hidden behind the great trees near IAH (Bush Airport). The hotel was clean, staff was pleasant, the bedding was nice and room was clean. Lots of good parking and convenient to the airport in a secure area.

“Very accommodating staff” What struck me most about our recent stay at this fine hotel was how accommodating and friendly the staff were. While calling to confirm our reservations and inform the front desk of a late-night check-in, we were offered a complimentary upgrade to an Executive King corner room.
