When we declined the offer for a rollaway bed for our 10 year old, they offered us complimentary parking for 2 nights. When we requested assistance, we were met with prompt and courteous service. The location is great, the property is nicely maintained, and the room was excellent.

“Very nice hotel!” My husband stayed here on business (the Super Bowl) and my kids and I stayed with him. The room was a little crowded but everything was very clean, the rooom service was fast and tasty and the pool and hot tub were very nice. The beach is very close by and it's easy off a major road so it's easy to find your way around.

“Clean hotel that is great value” I stayed at the Comfort Inn Manhattan Bridge for four nights on two separate occasions during a recent holiday in the US. Both rooms allocated to me were clean and fairly spacious for New York. The hotel has just opened so all the furniture and fixtures in the room were new and of good quality. The bed was very high, but comfortable and had great pillows. Breakfast is included in the room price and consisted of tea, coffee, doughnuts, muffins, cereal, fruit juice, eggs and waffles. The breakfast area was a little small, but sharing tables is a good way of meeting people. The staff were very helpful and check in and check out was easy. Chinatown is not the most fashionable area of New York, but it is safe and there are a number of subway stations close to the hotel. The first room I had at the hotel was for three nights on Level 6 and there was a little bit of street noise, which died down later in the night. The second room I had was at the back of the hotel and extremely quiet. I did set of fthe fire alarm when I had a shower, but the staff were quick to resolve this. The hotel has free internet and WIFI. My only complaint is that I wanted to leave a bag at the hotel for two nights while I went up to Toronto. I was staying back at the hotel on my return. The staff initially said that this would be OK, but I was later informed by other staff this was against their policy. Not a big issue.

“Do not stay here at any price” I always wondered about this place as I walked from Penn Station to my destination. Sadly, I wonder no more, as I had the unfortunate opportunity to stay here earlier this week. The high price of $299 per night shows that you definitely don't always get what you pay for! As another person said, the lobby gives you hope, but once in the room, your hopes are dashed. The carpet is stained and uneven, the walls are dirty, the sockets push in, hang out, or are plateless, the beds are in bad shape, and the toilet seat appears not to have been replaced in the last 50 years. The desk wobbles side to side, the clock radio is useless, the light fixtures are in bad shape, it's almost impossible to turn off the water in the sink...and so on. It's hard to sleep, as one is always imagining what critters might be your roommates! Bottom line: don't do it!

“All the Comforts Of Home” Homewood Suites by Hilton, Phoenix Metro Center. I spent three weeks at this nice but slightly out of the way property. Hotel is couched into a corporate park area. My one bedroom suite included separate living room/ kitchenette and bedroom. Very clean and comfortable with nice furniture. Complimentary hot breakfast each morning- eggs/breakfast taco/bacon/fruit-yogurt-oatmeal/coffee/tea/juice. Evening "Managers' Reception," always included beer and wine- with some reheated/microwaved food or snacks. The hospitality and friendliness of the staff, as well as the social nature of the reception outshines the adequate if not gourmet food. Evening menu included either: tacos, pizza, franks, macaroni, eggplant,eggrolls, etc and salad - and chips. It was always a pleasure to grab a beer and a snack before retiring to the room- or going out for a formal dinner. Nice outdoor pool area and inviting great room with fireplace- tv, populated by other happy and conversant guests. Not much in the direct vicinity of the hotel- don't plan on walking from the hotel to any pub or restaurant. Many shops and restaurants within a one mile radius on Peoria Avenue- or adjacent to the freeway. Hotel is close to a small Amusement park called "Castles and Coasters." Altogether a very nice place to call home for a few weeks.

“Second Stay Here!” This was my second stay at the Hotel Monaco. It was absolutely wonderful. Everyone was welcoming and accommodating. Room was well appointed and very quiet. I only have two complaints. We stayed in the hallway without the ice machine. Its a long walk through the hotel lobby and to the other wing that has the ice machine, especially if you're wearing penguin pajamas. Second, my bed was actually broken. The wood on the box springs broke and it was horrible to sleep on. When I mentioned something to the front desk, they had engineering fix it, instead of getting us a new room. Room was a bit small, but that's to be expected in DC. The decor was beautiful. The bed was HORRIBLE to sleep on. I love the Monaco, I really do. I plan to stay again, but I have to say, I was a bit disappointed in my last stay.

“Great hotel, great location, beyond great staff” I spent 4 days at this Hilton and I have to say this was one of the best hotel stays I have ever had. In way of clarification, I am a moderately-frequent traveler with about 6-10 hotel stays/month, coast-to-coast and I was here on business. My great stay started on check-in and I was pleasantly surprised until, and including, my check-out. The biggest differentiator, and the reason I will return whenever in the area, is the staff. Unbelievably friendly and helpful from top to bottom. After a while hotel rooms start to look the same, but a staff like this makes this all the difference.

“Near the Kennedy Center and the Foggy Bottom Metro” This is a good spot. The staff is extremely helpful and the rooms are spacious and clean. I had a good sized living room and bedroom in my suite, complete with a kitchenette stocked with plenty of dishes, pots and pans. Definitely like the hotel. Foggy Bottom location is quiet, though it pays to make sure that you’re not in a room that opens on the alley. Can be noisy with garbage trucks if you’re on a lower floor. Other downsides? There are only a handful of restaurants within immediate walking distance and there is no room service. Getting in late, I ended up grabbing a snack that had to pass for “dinner” from the nearby 7-11! Guess that’s where the kitchen comes in! (Too bad the grocery store nearby had closed....) At least being a Doubletree, they gave me a tasty chocolate chip cookie when I checked in. Also, no high-speed internet and no athletic facilities. When I asked, they said there is a deal where you can use the gym at the nearby Watergate Hotel for a nominal fee.

“Große schöne Zimmer, nicht so gute Lage” Wir übernachteten hier 4 Nächte für je ca. 134 USD inkl. Tax. Das Hotel liegt am Scotts Circle und damit etwas abseits von Sehenswürdigkeiten, Restaurants und Shopping-Bereichen. Hier hätte ich gern eine etwas belebtere Gegend vorgefunden. Das Umfeld ist jedoch nicht als unsicher einzustufen. Hier finden sich hauptsächlich Botschaften und Sitze von Verbänden etc. Das Zimmer war riesig. Nach Öffnung der Zimmertür ging man einen ca 5m langen Gang entlang, der sich dann zum Bad und zum Schlaf-/Wohnbereich gabelte. Letzteres bestand aus einem sehr großen und bequemen Kingsize-Bett sowie einem Sofa, das auch ausgeklappt hätte werden können. Dazu stand ein Schreibtisch mit Stuhl sowie ein großer Flatscreen zur Verfügung. Ein Schrank mit Bügelbrett und eingebautem Safe komplettierten die Ausstattung. Alles war recht neu, in ansprechenden Farben gestaltet und sauber. Wir haben uns während des Aufenthaltes sehr wohl gefühlt. Einzig negativ blieb in Erinnerung, dass das Check-In-Personal uns mit einem empfohlenen Taxi-Limousinenservice neppte. Wir zahlten hier letztlich rund 20$ mehr als ein reguläres Taxi oder der Super Shuttle gekostet hätte. Lassen Sie sich hierauf also nicht ein!

“A great stay, once you figure out where it is.” This hotel is exactly what you'd expect a Hilton Garden Inn to be; clean, quiet, well-maintained, spacious and friendly. The evening cookies are yummy - right by the entrance and the number you take is constrained only by your own discretion and the computers in the business center are fast and come fitted with nice big monitors and a window to look out while you're waiting for your files to load. And, another reason for happiness, Food Network's available on the TV. The hotel's location is both good and bad news - good news because it's tucked away in a sort of low-rise mixed-use office-park-like place that has a lot of empty store fronts - ensuring peaceful surroundings and plenty of parking - and bad news because without a GPS, you may be driving in circles for a long time before find it. So, here's a tip: the hotel is at the end of a winding driveway at the top of a hill. Even without the elevation, you couldn't see the hotel building from the street because there are other buildings in the way. So, instead of looking for the hotel BUILDING, watch for a Hilton Garden Inn SIGN that's been placed parallel the entrance to the driveway at a traffic light. But be advised that the sign is not very large and it's virtually flush with the ground so you'' want to keep a close look out! You'll be glad to know that there's a small grocery-type market down the street (note their diagonal driveway that is a handy cut-through for avoiding the intersection) as well as a gas station conveniently located between you and the expressway that will take you to SAN. (I filled up at that gas station and the tank was still on full when I got to the rental return lot.) I chose this hotel mostly because it was the most reasonably priced HGI in the whole San Diego area. If you're looking for a reasonably priced alternative to the downtown hotels, this would be a good choice. It's about 25 minutes to the downtown area (without traffic, which didn't even appear to be much of a consideration during AM drivetime) and the expressway is only about a half-mile away.

“Great Experience for single female” I stayed here to attend a concert @ American Air Center. Room was very nice, clean, quiet, good quality linens for bed. Although the towels were nice and clean-not very soft. Intended to take Dart to concert and discovered to my delight that they have a shuttle for a 3 mile radius-shuttled to door and picked back up @ same. Staff was all very helpful and pleasant even though they were busy. I enjoy Dallas and attend events several times a year. As a female traveling alone, I can stay here, be safe and use their shuttle service to get around...what's not to love?!

“Basic but clean” This is a new property and as such is in excellent condition, and very clean. As is typical of Candlewood properties, don't expect a free breakfast or a pool - they do not have these here. Very basic services, but excellent for extended stays due to the full kitchen in each room. I had no problems during my stay. The bed was firm but comfortable, there were plenty of HD channels available on the flat screen TV, and the A/C worked well.

“Micro rooms” The russian reception lady was very friendly and deserves a special praise. The 2-bed room was absolutely micro size, the space outside of the beds gave little room for anything. But you get what you pay for, a decent night's sleep for little money 200+ including breakfast. The full "plastic" breakfast was included, but we really do not like it.

“I never wanted to leave” The Surrey is an absolutely fabulous hotel! It's very quiet with a boutique feel when you walk in. The staff was amazing! When I checked in, they walked me up to my room and my luggage was not far behind. The rooms are great, lots of space. The suites have a very large living room area with great views of Central Park. Large flat screen tv, well stocked mini-bar area, and a fantastic window seat to enjoy the view. The desk has plenty of accessible outlets for chargers and laptops. The bed is probably the most comfortable I've ever experienced. It was amazing. I didn't want to ever get up in the morning. In the bedroom, there was another window seat, flat screen tv, very large closet and plenty of drawer space. The bathroom had a large tub and separate shower that was built for two. Great bathroom amenities and plenty of counter space. The lighting could be a little better, but not a deal breaker! The location is a bit off the beaten path, but such a great area. A short walk down Fifth or Madison and you are back in the heart of shopping. I loved walking up and down Madison and peaking in all the little boutique shops. Definitely a recommended hotel for anyone looking for luxury in a quiet, boutique style feel.

“Top of Times Square” I just returned from a lovely "one night" stay at the Times Square Hilton. The location is terrific, less than one block from Times Square. The nearest subway stop is in the same block. I received a lovely room in the corner, so windows on both sides. The room was very large and had a king bed, a chair and ottoman, a desk with two chairs - every thing you needed. The bathroom was very nice and the towels were really very soft and thick - not like some hotel towels. All the staff members were friendly and helpful. The only couple of drawbacks or difficulties, as others have mentioned, it is a bit difficult to find. I really appreciated the tip to "look for the large clock" - because it just does look like a storefront, not a hotel. Also, you need to know that the parking is not on 42nd street, it is on 41st street. You need to go around the block. They will valet it there, but factually, I saw a parking garage directly across the street and I concluded that it would probably be substantially less expensive to "valet it myself" - no parking is inexpensive in NYC - but I didn't pay Hilton's premium.... The only drawback in the hotel itself was that it appeared, although I didn't ask, that the only breakfast option was a buffet. I went to sit down, saw the buffet, and no indication of menus, so I left. This probably saved me a fortune too - so no great loss. All in all, it was a lovely stay and I would recommend it to anyone who wanted a nice, central hotel in Manhattan.

“apartment living for hotel room rate” We just spent a week at the Marmara. It basically is a mid-later twentieth century apartment building converted to hotel. The apartments surprised me. They are attractive, well maintained and very spacious. The full kitchen is large, windowed and well equipped. It's not just a suite, but a well laid out apartment with bath off the hall and not the living room or bed room, so nobody wakes up the other enroute. The service at the front desk is friendly but minimal. One young (looked like) student usually manned the desk and was trying to manage phones, check-in and questions. Don't stay there if you are used to having one of those great concierges staffs, though the desk clerk will do his best to help. There was a friendly security/bellman on duty and visible always. There is a large laundry room and even larger gym in the basement, however the emplyees smoke down there and the air is a little foul. A large grocery is a couple blocks away. The neighborhod is really nice. We had a view of the river. There is 2nd ave subway construction adjacent but much of the work is underground now and the noise didn't bother us. (you might ask for an east oriented room or a high room just in case some above ground work is underway) The area actually seemed less touristy and more residential in feeling than where we usually stay on the west side. The transportation is not as easy as much of the west side, though it sure wasn't bad. The local Lex subway stop is 4 blocks away and here is where you start to notice that all Manhattan is not flat. You have a steep couple of block climb up Carnegie hill to Lexington but a nice coast down when you are coming home. My family will for sure press me to stay at Marmara next trip. They loved it... and it proved a fair cost savings over the my usual west side hotel for much more space. The clientele was international and very nice and friendly - many from Britain and various European countries

“Design trifft Retro Style” sehr schickes und hippes hotel der besonderen art !!! echt mal eine sehr nette und schöne alternative zu den normalo hotels. das ganze hotel ist echt schräg und witzig gestaltet. schon die rezeption und die lobby sind anders als gewohnt. die zimmer sehr großzügig und sehr gut ausgestattet. jedes zimmer hat einen eigenen style bzw. look und einfach mal anders gestaltet. der kleine frühstücksraum ist eher klein und auch ein wenig zu kühl für meinen geschmack. das frühstück allgemein eher mittelmäßig mit geringer auswahl !!! sehr große terrasse mit bbq und chilligen sitz möglichkeiten. ebenso ist das hotel bzw. die bar eine gute adresse und auch bei den amis sehr beliebt die sich zum wochenende gerne in der bar auf einen trink treffen. die lage ist okay, ginge allerdings besser. die nächste metro ist ca. 10 gehminuten enfernt !!! wer einmal ein anderes hotel erleben möchte ist hier sicher sehr gut aufgehoben !!!

“Nice hotel for the money” This is a great location to base a business trip if you need to travel around houston. Wouldn't be my first choice for a vacation ( hit the galleria or woodlands) but the hotel lobby and rooms are fresh and the concierge lounge offers a nice selection for evening app's. I have stayed a couple of times in June mid-week and typically found rates in the $108-$125 range. This is your best choice in the 610/290 area by far!!!!!

“Strike two” This was my second less-than-stellar stay at a W in less than a month. We were there the Sunday night of Memorial Day weekend and attempted to check in at 4 p.m.—an hour after check-in officially begins. After waiting in line for quite a while, we were told that they had to check to see if our room was ready. We were a little perturbed that there was even a question as to whether or not our room was ready an hour after check-in. The gentleman checking us in actually had to go upstairs to check to see if the room was clean because no one answered him on this headset. Luckily it was ready and he was considerate enough to offer us a $30 credit for the wait/hassle. I have to mention the horrible odor in the lobby while we waited. I don’t know what it was, but it was foul—I’ll spare you the description of what it smelled like. I hope for the employees’ sakes it was an anomaly and isn’t always like that. We held our breath when we had to pass through. We were in room 1001 which was generally nice and very W-esque—trendy, modern, minimalist. The bathroom was ridiculously spacious, though almost to a fault. The other side of the room—the bedroom part—was small and cramped. So, while it was nice to have a big bathroom, they probably could have shaved 3’ or so off the bathroom, still had a rather large bathroom, and made the bedroom a little more spacious. Loved the Bliss toiletries. Hated the wifi fee. It was VERY noisy. One would think that we wouldn’t hear much street noise being on the 10th floor. Wrong. We heard the thumping of nearby bars/clubs til probably 2 a.m. or so. On top of that, we heard music blasting from the room next door. I finally just turned on our TV so I could fall asleep to that instead. The location is really great for exploring downtown Austin but bear in mind you’re just a stone’s throw from 6th Street and other nearby bars, so if you’re looking for quiet and relaxation, you should look elsewhere.

“No wireless? What?” I stayed at the Marriott during a conference. The conference was in the hotel - all the conference facilities were nice. They must have mistaken me for someone of some importance and put me on the top floor across from the suites. So, I had a great view! The room was clean, room service was great. But I had one big beef: No wireless access in the rooms. For such a modern hotel and leading hotel chain, I was shocked when I had to pull out their complimentary Ethernet cord. Since this trip was for business, my work grinded to a halt without wireless access. From what I understand, the hotel is undergoing some renovations. Hopefully this includes room upgrades to wireless. I ate at the restaurant twice. Service was really nice, food was good, and I even got to witness the security team in action as they escorted a disruptive guys from the premises. For internet junkies, there's a Marriott Courtyard right across the street that I've stayed at before and has wireless.

“I expected more from the Westin Book Cadillac Detroit” Overall I was very disappointed with the Westin Book Cadillac Detroit. I planned on staying downtown Detroit at the Westin Book Cadillac but checked out after the first night. My biggest disappoint was the room. I received a corner room on the 11th floor. I believe the room was a deluxe king. The room looked like two regulars rooms without the wall. One side was the bed with a large TV and the other side two chairs with a similar TV. I thought it was strange. The bathroom was very nice!! Differently the best shower that you will find in Detroit. When looking out the window you see another abandoned, derelict building. I felt like been looked up in a prison cell while staying at this hotel. The room didn’t feel warm and comforting. I had access to the Westin club lounge but the lounge is located in the 23rd floor. I didn’t go up to the 23rd floor. I would of use the lounge if I had a room on the SPG preferred floor or club floor. I guess as a SPG platinum guest you are not guaranteed a room on the SPG preferred floor. Basically SPG preferred status made no difference during my stay. I also had to pay 5 bucks for the water in the room. The Westin Book Cadillac Detroit reception area and lobby are very nice. The hotel also has a great selection of restaurants, bars and café to eat at. I have eaten at Roast and would highly recommend eating there. Except to pay $25 for valet parking for the night, however the valet service was very good. I saw some parking garages next to the hotel but wasn’t sure if it was safe. Hotel also has a nice coffee shop downstairs. Overall hotel is very nice!! I guess I just expected more been a SPG platinum guest. Next week I will stay at Detroit Westin Metro Airport. I always seem to get a room on the SPG preferred floor or club floor.

“A Tenderloin Experience at a Bargain” I often spend a night or two in the city and have found myself near or in the Tenderloin neighborhood, which is a real educational experience and not for the squeamish. It's LIVING THEATER right outside your window. The neighborhood is notorious for drug addicts, drunks and homeless people wandering around, pan handling and occasionally fighting with each other (as well as their imaginary demons) Saturday nights can be especially rowdy on the streets, but given all that, I am happy to report my experience at The historic Layne Hotel was better than most in this part of the city. The rooms are clean, not too small, the front door is secure (you have to buzzed in) and there is always someone at the front desk 24 hours a day. There is a real charm to this hundred year old hotel. The elevator, in particular, is very old, but it works. You feel you are traveling back in time as you rumble up to your floor. It's very cool. This hotel is very near the corner of Geary Street and only two blocks from The Curran Theater, so it is in a good spot, walking distance to restaurants and transportation options especially when you consider you're often paying half of what the bigger chains charge. Through Booking.com, I was able to get a room with private bathroom for $125.00 (normally 175.00) on a busy festival weekend in a busy month in San Francisco. If you can get beyond the sad and the sordid, you may have a memorable stay in this location.

“Best Beds in Town” This Holiday Inn Expess has the best beds in town. Yes, there are many better hotels in El Paso but the sleep comfort and location is 5 stars all the way. Perfectly located close to I-10 and right in downtown El Paso with many of the downtown attractions located a short walk from the hotel. The area around the hotel is safe. By the way the parking is free.

“Agree with the positive reviews” Agree with the positive reviews. Although this is a typical motel you wouldn't stay at unless you read the reviews, it is clean, bathrooms very modern with fridg and microwave and flat screen tv with a heck of a lot more channels than most upscale hotels. Free wireless Internet worked very nicely. The rate makes this a maximum bang for your buck.

“Great hotel...” Superb decor, extremely comfortable beds and room. Nice little outdoor pool with lounge chairs if you want to catch a few rays and relax. Only two negatives-- one is there is nothing within walking distance of hotel if you want to eat. The hotel does offer sandwiches and salads and a limited menu, but if you prefer to dine out then you are out of luck unless you have a car with you. The other negative is they no longer have individual soap or toiletries in the bathroom, but rather "dispensers" in the shower for shower gel, shampoo, and conditioner. Over all, Hyatt Place does it right, and I would most definitely recommend this hotel. Front desk staff was very courteous, professional, and cheerful.

“NIce full-service Marriott property but common areas were very cold.” We had two rooms reserved and they were side by side but not connecting which was fine. As a MR Plat I was upgraded to the Concierge level. Rooms were nicely appointed. Concierge lounge was a little small and staff had a hard time keeping up especially at breakfast. Evening offerings were a little sparse. Restaurant was good but cold. Lobby and restaurant area was kept at 65 degrees or less. You had to wear a sweater or coat not to be cold. Luggage service was prompt and courteous. Hot tub was way too hot to enjoy. Some of the fitness center equipment was not working properly. Overall a nice stay with courteous staff, but the cold common areas took the luster off our stay.

“Loved this hotel” At over $550 a night room only, a hotel should be good and the Hay Adams was great. I was especially pleased as the hotel was so busy they upgraded me to something called the Federal Suite which had fantastic views of the White House and the skyline generally. But my friends were all pleased with their rooms and the staff were courteous and extremely helpful. The location is great for visiting the Smithsonian and being right opposite the White House it's got nice views and is good for visiting that area. At night there are very few places to eat nearby and our party had set dinners in a nice but dimly lit room so I can't comment on the food at the hotel more generally. There is a wonderful rooftop terrace which we had access to for business receptions. I don't know whether this is usually open to anybody but it's worth asking to go uo their to watch the sunset. that was a highlight of my trip. I stayed at the Mayflower on Conneticut Ave the night before. That was brighter and had a more spacious feel and is handier for Dupont Circle and there are a few eateries open at night nearby. But the Hay Adams has views to die, marvellous terrace & free internet (unlike the Mayflower). It's a hard choice between them. The Mayflower was cheaper, but the HA has a slighlty grander feel to the place & a nice downstairs bar which is cosy & friendly unlike the more open lobby bar in the Mayflower. But in any case, both are highly recommended!

“Nice old hotel, good downtown location” Actually, I give this a rating of 3.5. Stayed for three nights in early May. Although I am only "Preferred" with SPG, I was upgraded to a junior suite. It was a nice, large room with a giant closet. I like this hotel because I get SPG points and you can get to many restaurants and the financial district easily. It has a beautiful interior and offers an afternoon tea service for those into that. Bed was a typical heavenly bed, which are always nice and comfortable beds. Bathroom wasn't huge but certainly suitable for one person. Large flat screen TV with some HD channels. High speed connectivity was $18 per day which I think is ridiculous. Also, no wireless which meant I could only work at the desk and no where else in the room. I wanted to send some emails while laying in bed and couldn't. The walls were thin and so too was the door to the adjoining room. The person next to me left the TV on two nights in a row, and I could hear the broadcast clearly. Overall, this is a nice place to stay for business or pleasure although there might be better places to stay in SF for the $325 per night that I paid.

“Good experience, but not a calm oasis” Based on the good reviews at this site, we stayed here a few weeks ago. This boutique hotel was everything promised, inexpensive, colorfully decorated and conveniently located, but it is not the oasis of calm that it advertises to be, at least not in the lobby. The lobby bar appears to be a popular night spot, and on the Saturday night we checked it it was thumping and smoky and crowded. Luckily, none of this commotion could be heard from our room on the 6th floor, which was huge and extremely quiet. One other warning--if you are the type of traveler who expects a large elegant lobby, fast elevators, and 24x7 bell and conciege services, stay at a Marriott or Hilton instead. The staff was friendly and pleasant, but rarely was there more than one person behind the desk in the small but cute lobby.

“Typical Airport Hotel” I had a one night stopover here after a long-haul transatlantic flight. After battling through immigration in LAX I got the frequent and efficent shuttle bus just outside the arrivals terminal to the hotel. Checkin was simple. Room more than adequate. I updraded to their Executive floor for $40. Wi-fi was good, $12.95 for 24 hours. The Crowne Plaza Lounge was just ok but very nicely staffed by Tony. I jumped on the shuttle bus back to the airport after a good nights sleep in a very comfy bed. All in all good. A typical airport hotel.

“Comfortable place to stay overnight” Stayed here one night after having a late arrival from LAX. Hotel staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Shuttle service from the airport was free and efficient. Rooms are a bit dated, but clean and comfortable. An old motel style with several different buildings. Close to the airport, and for $60 AAA rate, a great place to stay after a long day of flying.

“A little shabby/great location/good price/large rooms” We stayed in a junior suite on the 14th floor. For the price, the size of the room is enormous--actually a bedroom and sitting area. We have friends in the city with smaller apartments. The room was fairly clean, the bathroom could have been cleaner. The fixtures and bathroom are a bit on the shabby side. The front desk is fairly helpful, and you can stash your bags before you check in and after you check out easily. There is not much of a lobby, and there's only one bathroom in the lobby, hidden in the area where luggage is stored. One computer in lobby for checking email. Wicked slow elevators. Really great location for subways and busses, just a few blocks to Central Park. Several wonderful restaurants and grocery stores nearby. The little kitchenette in the room was nice. Microwave, tiny coffee maker, dorm-sized fridge. We paid $215 which is average-to-economical in the area. Overcharge for local calls (.75) and even toll-free and credit-card calls cost. We have stayed at the Excelsior (good rooms, horrible, horrible staff), The Lucerne (wonderful all around but no longer moderately priced) and Comfort Inn Central Park West (room tiny even by Manhattan standards). The Milburn is a good spot if you aren't too fastidious. NY isn't really about the room, anyway, so stay here if you want a great, quiet neighborhood and aren't in need of swanky surroundings.

“Brand New Hilton...Fantastic!” The Hilton Austin is a fabulous property in a great location in downtown Austin. This is a new property and it is a very upscale Hilton. The top 5 floors of the building are going to be luxury condominiums. The building is so new; I don't think anyone has moved in yet. I was given a wonderful room on the top floor of the hotel portion (26th floor - Executive level). The executive lounge on the 25th floor was fantastic with breakfast in the morning and h'ors d’oeuvres in the evening. I had dinner at the sushi bar in the lobby one night and it was very good and not overpriced. The room had a beautiful south view with a huge picture window. The decor of the room was very nice with some great details. The bed was fabulous and I overheard people raving about how comfortable they were. There is a great health club on the 8th floor with steam and sauna in the men's locker room. I considered the nearby Four Seasons but based on TripAdvisor, I decided on the Hilton and I'm glad I did. Please see my attached photos.
“立地最高!!!” タイムズスクエアのど真ん中で立地は最高です。 スタッフも親切で、お部屋もきれいでした。 エキストラベッドを1台入れていただきましたが、狭くて困ることはありませんでした。 次回はガラス越しに見えるジムにも行きたいと思います。

“If your idea of customer service is no to every request, stay here!” I normally don't write a review while still at a hotel, but I have grown so frustrated over the course of my stay that I didn't want to wait until I get home. Thankfully, I am checking out in the morning. My most basic problem is that every request of mine was answered with an abrupt no. I am a seasoned traveler who spends over 50 nights a year on the road so I think I know what a reasonable request is and mine were reasonable. I was here for a conference and upon check-in asked for a room with a king/queen bed as opposed to two doubles - the answer was no. So that's fine, I understand, it is a busy week. Now when I was given a room on the 4th floor I asked for a higher floor, again, the answer was no. I was concerned about traffic noise at night and my concerns were justified as everything from trucks to two-stroke motorcycles roared outside my window each night. I know this could have been accommodated because a colleague who checked in after me (with no elite status either) was asked his preference for a high or low floor. I checked in on a Monday evening, Wednesday afternoon the hotel's digital television stopped working and is still not back up as of Thursday night. All guest rooms were given a notice that it is due to "system upgrades" and a reminder that PPV TV is still available. Now I've never heard of a 36+ hour system upgrade, especially when the hometown Bruins are in the Stanely Cup and unavailable on any analog staion. So I called the front desk and suggested that guests be offered one-free PPV movie to compensate for the trouble, of course, you guessed it, the answer was no!! Those are the big things, but there were also little. I asked the concierge for a dinner recommendation one evening and she obliged, but indicated I may not get a table unless she went ahead and made a reservation for me. I let her make the reservation only to get there and see every table open. She clearly only wanted the tip, which she got, but I felt that was very disingenuous. The rooms are indeed small and the bathrooms smaller, but I knew that going in so could have overlooked it if the service was better. And just tonight my hamburger that was ordered via room-service came undercooked, but I don't care at this point to send it back and ask for a credit because I know the answer - NO!! There were a few positive notes. The location really cannot be beat for either business or sight-seeing in Boston. There are some nice Select Guest Perks, like free beverages in the morning, turndown service in the evening and free wifi. Although the wireless printing does not work and the hotel was no help (had to call 3rd party tech support). So I really hope the Hotel Manager does not respond and only mention the few positive remarks because I was overwhelmingly disappointed and will not be returning to this property. I know my Platinum status at Marriott does get me a certain level of service, and I did not expect that here, but I did expect some common courtesy at the very least.

“Great location” The Renaissance M Street Hotel is located within walking distance of Dupont Circle and Georgetown -- though getting there by car is a bit difficult and parking is horribly expensive. I stated there during a recent business trip to Washington, DC, and left with a so-so impression. Having stayed at other Renaissance hotels, I can say there this isn't as nice as others in the brand. It's really a glorified Holiday Inn or Courtyard by Marriott. With no complimentary internet, I didn't even hook-up my computer. I instead used my BlackBerry because I refuse to pay for hotel internet these days when any decent self-respecting hotel offers it for free. The rooms are small, but nice. The flat-screen TV is nice, the beds and pillows are comfortable and the bathroom is very clean. On the downside, the rooms have a door to the adjoining guestroom which is something you don't expect at this price-point. It also raises privacy issues, as noise is more pronounced in this circumstance. I had a mixed experience with the service. The hotel's maids never cleaned my room on the first day I stayed, which was a major problem. I arrived back at 7 p.m. to freshen up before going out and had no clean towels, no clean face cloths and my bed was totally messed up. I called down to the front desk and the room was cleaned by the time I returned from dinner -- there was even a chocolate on the bedspread. I would avoid the hotel's restaurant, which is ridiculously expensive.. The breakfast buffet is very good, but it's an astonishing $20. You can get something a lot cheaper off-site. As I explained earlier, the hotel's location is good though a Metro (subway) station is about a 10-minute walk, which isn't too fun in the winter time considering all the recent snow has made it difficult to navigate sidewalks in some places. I probably wouldn't stay here again because there are better hotels with better amenities in Washington, DC, that can be had for the same or cheaper on Priceline.

“Surprisingly good business hotel” Booked through Priceline for 2 night business trip. Everything went smoothly @ check in. Room was small, but clean and perfectly adequate. Lobby is gorgeous. Attached restaurant Scala was excellent for lunch and attached Starbucks was a bonus. Union Square location was great.

“Good but some things need work...” The first room we were in was a Jr. Suite which we were told was good for a family of 4. NO WAY! So, we immediately upgraded to a Family Suite. It was on the 1st floor, a little loud on Friday & Saturday nights but ok. There was a leak somewhere in the bathroom near the shower that got all of our towels wet after we used them to dry up the leak. The Continental breakfast was a hit with the kids & the cinnamon buns were yummy. We ordered "room service" one evening & the food was room temp when it arrived & both kid's meals were incorrect - we ordered chicken tenders & fries and grilled cheese & fries & got 2 hamburgers (whatever). We were told a crib would be in our room upon checking in, we had to ask for the crib to be delivered. Hmmm.... all in all- if we went again, we would rent a house instead of staying in a hotel - this or any other for that matter. A week is just too long in a hotel room with 2 kids - even if it is a 2 room suite. The room service was funny too - we came in two times while the turn down service was being performed & the maids were JAMMING to some "Mexican" tunes on the clock radio. They were nice & the room was always very clean, but it was pretty funnny.

“Great hotel, but...” We had never been to Boston and were not sure where to stay in the downtown area. Priceline made the decision for us. The hotel is located in the Tent City area of downtown Boston. There is a fair amount of transient activity in the area. However, it is well located to sightsee all the historical sights, Italian district, the harbor and Faneuil Hall (a great shopping and entertainment area). We were given a room that looked out onto the front of the hotel. Next door to the hotel, was a private Rap party that lasted until 3:00 AM. The noise kept us up all night. As soon as we advised the hotel staff, they moved us immediately and could not apologize enough. The hotel itself is a cute boutique hotel. The rooms are small, but exceptionally clean with an honor bar. They also offer wireless internet. The staff and the service they provide is off the chart. They are exceptionally friendly and make the whole experience a positive one. When I forgot my shaving kit, they had a disposable one to my room within 5 minutes. They have limo service for anywhere in the city. If you don't know where to eat or visit, the concierge provides plenty of ideas with printed directions of the area.
“Excellent” Stayed at this property at a travelzoo rate of $99, which is an incredible value for this property. Overall an excellent hotel, charming modern rooms, would stay again with pleasure.

“Luxury next to the fire station” FIrst, let me start by saying I'm not a Hyatt fan, but I've found Park Hyatt's to be a distinct step above in amenities and luxuries over your typical Hyatt hotels. This property did not disappoint. It has a lot going for it. A great location, terrific rooms with luxury baths, impeccable service (by the doormen and front desk), friendly staff, very clean and beautiful furnishings. Even complimentary internet! I didn't give the hotel 5 stars for a few issues...one that really is just a function of its great location across from Watertower Place. There is a fire station with an ambulance a block away. It must be the busiest station in Chicago because they had a call literally ever 30 to 90 minutes both nights I was there. Although I couldn't hear a sound from any other room, I was woken up continuosly by the sirens wailing by the hotel when I was trying to sleep. Others in the hotel complained of the same problem. I was at the hotel for a business meeting and we had food catered by the hotel for both breakfast and lunch. It was good, but I wouldn't say it was great, given the price. I would venture out of the hotel for dinner. My only other issue was poor service in the hotel bar.....which was annoying given there weren't many guests in the lounge. Our server was very nice, just moved the pace of a snail. Overall, you'll really like it hear provided you're a sound sleeper or there are few fire calls!

“Grander in Theory Than Practice” Eh. This hotel didn't have anything wrong with it per se, but I wasn't a huge fan. The place is grand in theory: a 2-room suite, a big atrium, free breakfast, etc. -- all of the standard Embassy Suites stuff. In practice, however, this property felt old. It had to be one of the earliest Embassy Suites, because it still had that sort of Spanish-architectural style that the earliest properties had. Except that renovations had attempted to mask that Spanish style -- but hadn't masked it completely, which made for sort of an odd feel to the place. My room was acceptable -- clean, functional internet, etc. -- but didn't feel very elevated. The bathroom felt very cramped. The bed was clean, but the linens felt as if they'd seen slightly better days. All of the rooms have French doors as the main door, and windows on either side of those French doors. Since the hotel is an indoor atrium, I didn't feel unsafe with this arrangement, but it's definitely unusual to have your hotel room's main door be a French door! (It did have curtains that totally covered it, so there was privacy, but it also felt weird to pull a curtain over the door to your room.) The hotel's other features were what you'd except -- pretty good breakfast, decent business center (computers were a little slow, but free), fine fitness center. Room service was prompt and, while certainly not gourmet, was hot and tasted fine. Service was fine. Check-in was speedy and welcoming. The room type preferences I have on file with Hilton HHonors were not granted, which I always find irritating as a top-level member of the Hilton program, but to her credit the front desk staffer noted this and apologized for not having a room better suited to my preferences. I appreciated that she noticed, and the room she put me in was just fine. Overall, it was OK, but I wasn't extremely impressed. Next time business brings me back to this part of Austin, this hotel would be on the list of possibilities, but I'd certainly look at other properties in the area, too.

“One of my favorite hotels” I travel a lot and stay in many different hotels. I just returned from Los Angeles the day before yesterday and spent two nights at the Sofitel. (My 10th time there). In reading some of the reviews preceding this, I am amazed at some of the comments. It is certainly enough to make me sure that I would hate to run a hotel! Some people are so hard to please. My room was a standard King room facing the hills. Great view. The room was very clean (what's with all these people finding dirt?) A good size desk (could have brighter lighting for it), comfortable armchair and table, good size closet with iron and ironing board, nice new in-room safe, and a very cosy bed (which a number of people have remarked about). By the way for those who did not like the duvets, there is a blanket in the room and the maids are there to exchange them for the duvets. The bathroom was large, clean and the best-lit bathroom in the business. Nice fluffy towels and plenty of them, white terry-cloth bath robe and soaps and shampoo by Roger & Gallet. Turn down service in the evening with a bottle of water on the bedside table. What's to complain about???? (They used to put a fresh red rose in a bud vase in the bathroom in the evening but no more apparently) The hotel is undergoing major rehab. The reception, bar and restaurant are on second floor and someone had the very bad idea of decorating in black and white in a space with very limited outside light coming in. I saw pictures of the new decor. It is very contemporary (not like the current French provincial look). The lobby and bar area look pretty wild. Not sure how us regulars will like it. The bedrooms will be very pretty if the pictures are accurate. Finally, the staff is exceptional. Very pleasant and no complaints.

“Business Hotel” I stayed here on business and saw many other business travelers on a conference. I would not recommend this hotel for a family vacation spot. It is literally located 5 minutes from the aiport by shuttle, so you will hear the airplanes landing and taking off all day and night. If you stay here ask for a room with a pool and marina view if not you will be facing the main street with a parking lot view - not pretty at all! I would also ask for a renovated room - the pictures on their website are not like the room I stayed in. My room was very outdated, the rugs needed to be change - dirty and stained. The bedding felt old and the room had very bad lighting. This hotel needs a lesson on cleanliness. I found hair on my bedsheets and in the tub. Also, some type of bug was crawling in the bathroom - yuck! This hotel is also about a $12 cab ride to downtown San Diego where all the shops and eateries are.

“Elegant” My husband and I had the pleasure of spending one night at The Peninsula. Our room was on the 10th floor with a view of Michigan Avenue. In style, the room and bathroom reminded me very much of Wynn Las Vegas, with the exception that The Peninsula has more electronic toys, like remote TV from the bathtub and mood dimming lights. Our room was exceptionally well appointed and immaculately clean. The only negative is we could hear a lot of street noise from down below and even on the lowest setting the room remained warmer than we would have preferred. The king bed was very comfortable with probably the most comfortable pillows we have found in any hotel. Looking forward to another stay.

“Used to be a good hotel” We were in NYC on business, for a weekend of events to attend; we're not tourists, and we've stayed here before, years ago, before Barclay was added to Intercontinental. We parked 5 or 6 blocks east, for cheaper parking, and walked to 48th St. and Lexington. We arrived very wet from a torrential rainstorm, and were looking forward to a hot cup of tea, seated comfortably in our room while we dried off. Alas, not to be. The lobby is large, formal and busy. There are lots of people sitting around using laptops because they charge extra for internet in one's room. The check-in went smoothly enough. When we arrived at our room, we were a bit surprised at how tiny it was. There was only room for one chair, at the desk. The bed was too tall for me to sit on. Then we found that the coffee machine was broken. We called "Instant Service", and were told an Engineer would come to look. Forty minutes or so later, he came, pronounced it broken, and went off to find a replacement. While waiting for him, I went into the bathroom and found a wet used bath towel on the towel rack, draped over the unused towels. Yuck. Also noticed a few long dark hairs on floor and sink. So we called "Instant service" again, and were told to not touch the offending towel, and wait for Housekeeping with fresh towels. A man with a stack of towels came 15 minutes later but refused to touch the dirty one ("not my job") so I put it on the vestibule floor, then washed my hands. The Engineer then came back with a non-broken coffeemaker, tried it out, and left, stepping over the towel on the floor. I asked the desk about tea but was informed that they do not have teabags, I would have to call Room Service, at $12 a go. By now we were almost late for our event, anyway, so we went out. Next morning, I was grossed out by a very mildewy shower curtain (photos), and that there was now no coffee (nor tea, of course.) Husband went down to the desk to get a packet, and was told to order room service if he wanted any coffee ($12, as I mentioned.) No one ever did come to pick up the dirty towel on the floor, inherited from the last guest. We just kept stepping over it. Now these are not disastrous things, but irritating, especially at $279 per night (AAA rate). Upon checkout, we complained to the clerk. The front desk supervisor came, and told us that at that "reduced rate", he could not grant us any price reduction, but offered 2 complimentary breakfasts at their buffet ($37 each). We noticed the long line, and opted out in order to make our event on time. The management did not go too hard out of its way to correct what I saw as real lapses in service. This hotel bills itself as luxury, and charges a lot for it. I'd be a lot more understanding if it was a Comfort Inn, and indeed I've had better treatment at Comfort Inn. There are lots of hotels in NYC, and we'll find a better one next time.

“Magnífica experiencia!” Hotel muy bueno. Personal super amable. Muy cerca de la Milla de oro de Chicago y de las principales zonas a visitar. Cerca del río y del parque de la ciudad. Habitaciones cómodas y acogedoras. Wifi gratuito. Restaurante Italoamericano en recepción, buena comida y servicio. Al lado del ascensor, en cada planta, existe una fuente de agua mineral con botellas vacías gratis. Repetiría seguro. Totalmente recomendable.

“Probably my least favorite W thus far” Stayed at the W San Francisco a couple weeks back on a Friday and Saturday evening, ending up 6 days in northern Cali. Compared to other brand properties where I stay regularly, was disappointed. Service via front desk was uneven, with some employees being very helpful and kind and an equal number of others acting indifferent to guests, pick-and-choosing whom to serve regardless of place in line, finding a way to redirect questions, etc. Call this paranoid, but at a couple of times I think I noticed a couple of the hotel goons snarking and sort of snickering at guests. Had to get my key card remagnetized (really? At a W for $250 a night?) I did find my room and view pretty cool, but all things considered including an only-ok location and kind of a dark poseur vibe emanating from almost everyone in the building, I would not stay here again regardless of my Starwood affiliation or points. Too many other good choices in San Fran to try to be cool at a property that is smug and already thinks it's too cool.

“Great Service; Needs a Facelift” This is the Omni off Hwy 10, not the Riverwalk. Booked a great rate $99 - a SAVE rate. Was in town for son's Air Force tech school graduation. Was a bit of a long ride to Lackland. PROS: Wonderful service. Great beds, nice toiletries, free parking, lots of restaurants & shopping nearby, quiet, thick towels. CONS: Needs a facelift; small rooms, smaller old fashioned bathrooms. Slow elevators. For the $99 rate it was a deal.

“Great base for your visit to Chicago” We stayed at the Fitzpatrick at the end of August after reading reviews on Tripadvisor and were not disappointed. Only drawback was the intial room we were allocated on the top floor was subject to a loud droning noise coming from somewhere, we stayed there for one night and asked for a move which was arranged without problems. The room was clean and the bed very comfy. The hotel also provided an emergency razor, toothbrush etc until a missing case was delivered. The bar area was pleasant and all the staff took an interest in doing a good job from the Reception staff to the bell boy and breakfast supervisor. The location is excellent, we were able to travel by CTA train and bus from the airport and found the hotel quite easily, the visitor pass for the public transport is well worth buying, you get to travel around with the locals and see the real Chicago. We found the Fitzpatrick to be a great base to visit the city. (A recommendatin if you are visiting the city do take a trip to Howl at the Moon one night, great musical entertainment). If we went back to Chicago we would stay at the Fitzpatrick again.

“Adequate LAX hotel; nothing special” Stayed a night at the Westin LAX. They've renovated the main common areas, which is quite nice, but there's nothing here that makes this a must-see hotel. The airport shuttle to and from LAX is quick and convenient. The Westin is at the end of the shuttle route, which is also served by a couple of other hotels such as an Holiday Inn and La Quinta. This makes it a bit more challenging if you're late for your flight, or if you have a lot of luggage, but is manageable. The rooms were unremarkable. The bed and bathroom were acceptable, but there is nothing that I can say about the rooms, good or bad. I think that they are getting around renovating their rooms fully to the Westin brand standard. There is still work to be done. My room faced away from Century Boulevard, which actually faces the runways, and is also near a dog pound, with a lot of barking. Parking in the LAX area is expensive. The Westin doesn't help here. If you're with Fox Car rental or Thrifty, you can slightly get around this by picking up your vehicle late and turning it in early in your trip, because their rental locations are just a 60-second walk away. (You can probably pull this off with all the agencies, but it means transferring bus shuttles at LAX. For daytime parking, Fox has a parking lot off Glasgow Place that is much cheaper than the Westin's. Irrespectively, you'll be paying notably for parking if you stay at the Westin LAX. All in all, there are dozens of hotels in the LAX area. The Westin is clean and acceptable, but if it costs more than other properties (and especially if it costs more than the other Starwoods, the Sheraton and the Four Points), then it's not that much worth it. Let your wallet decide among the Starwood properties in LAX.

“Acceptable Only if You Need Accomodations in the Area and Book Cheap with Hotwire” Because I book many hotels on Hotwire for the great prices, this review is based on the low price I paid. Had I paid the hotel's "rack rate" on their website, the review would have been 2 stars. But for $58/nt, it's pretty much the best deal you can find in decently Central/North Dallas for clean accommodations. Frankly, I think Starwood makes a mistake in branding these old, outdated hotels Westins. I remember not too long ago when a Westin meant something special and contemporary; now it seems to be their stodgiest brand, based on several recent stays in different cities. The rooms' decor was rather shockingly 1980's. The curtains, with their dark red floral patterns, were laughable, as was the outdated sink, shower, and bathroom. The windows looking out were filthy; apparently window washing when out the door at some point in the 90's. All of that said, the Starbucks in the room was nice, the staff was friendly, the common areas and parking clean. Didn't use the gym this time, and it's annoying to have to pay $12 for parking in such a parking lot of a city, and $10 for slow internet access is still a rub. But you can tell that they're just trying to get whatever extra fees they can, since they have to offer such low nightly room rates. All in all, it beats the Super 8 or Travelodge experience, but not by much.

“Kimpton Hotel - Excellent Customer Service” Foremost I must say that I will continue to stay in Kimpton Hotels when I can because they really rival any other hotel chain in the quality of their service. I stayed in the Hotel George because they offered a wonderful summer promotional rate for the weekend. When we checked in the staff gave us a $10 minibar coupon for being enrolled in the intouch program. There was water, ice tea, and lemonade waiting for us in the lobby, which was great because it was HOT out. We asked for a later check out time and they were able to accommodate us for an extra hour which was perfect. Upon check in the staff also gave us a map of DC and showed us where the hotel was in relation to several sights. He also gave us directions to a local CVS (ten minute walk) as we forgot several items,. and offered assistance getting items we forgot. The first night we ordered room service and while it was quite pricey it was a delicious meal. It was reallyt one of the best I tasted. Our room was a king deluxe room, the room and bathroom were both spacious and the bed was very comfortable. I will say that I was a bit disappointed by the cleanliness of the room because I have stayed in other kimpton hotels and I must have been spoiled there. There was loose change (a few pennies) on the floor, and a few scraps of paper, leading me to believe that the room was not thoroughly vacuumed. The wallpaper was peeling a little bit in two areas. I could also not get the air-conditioner above 76 degrees despite following the posted directions. Our room faced an office building so we kept the shades closed the entire time. For free internet you just sign into the Intouch Kimpton service. I recommend you do that before your stay so you can benefit from whatever promotional perks they have. I did that and got a wonderful rate for the hotel, the minibar coupon, and a newspaper of my choice delivered every morning. The hotel was in fact an ideal location if you want to see the sites of DC. It was steps away from the capitol building, Union Station (about a 3 minute walk) and a 10 minute walk to the National Portrait Gallery and Chinatown. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who is traveling to DC.

“Great Staff, Good Location” We stayed at the Residence Inn for the Liberty Bowl. Here are some observations: - Great location downtown. Trolley is right outside, and it is a very easy walk to Beale St., restaurants, The Peabody, etc. - The staff is great. Very friendly and helpful. We were traveling with a small child, and they went out of their way to answer questions and make sure we had what we needed. - The room was nice and spacious (studio) and they were very clean. - The free breakfast was a nice added touch, and there was a good selection. Why not 5 stars? - While the staff was awesome, for such a busy weekend we felt that they were a little understaffed and could have used another person or two to help out. - The breakfast was good, however there were not enough places to sit. This may not be a problem during the week or a normal weekend, but with a huge crowd like this it was a problem. - We had one issue with housekeeping. We asked them to come back later in the day which they did. When we arrived back at the room, there was a broken glass on our kitchen counter and our old towels were still on the floor. Hugh (front desk) was quick to come up and clean up the broken glass, but it was a little strange that it happened. Overall, a great hotel and stay!

“Quirky charm and very good value” We booked a regular room but had a corner room with a separate bedroom and sitting area so had plenty of space. The room was very comfortable and the window which opened in the bathroom was great on a sunny day. Location was great and the noise level from the street was tolerable. Breakfast was delicious and conveniently located just in the hall outside the room. Staff was especially helpful and friendly. Little quirks like the unsual to operate elevator added to the charm and the value was great.

“4 Night Stay- Very Pleasant Modern feel hotel” Holiday Inn express, also know as Hotel Cass, underwent a 15 billion dollar refurb thank goodness. I book for 4 nights, got a ridiculously low rate of $40 a night all inclusive as i booked a hotel/flight package with lastminute.com. I was sceptical thinking i would be put in a room reserved for priceline/orbitz bookers but i had a normal hotel room.i even got some extras as im a priority reward club holder. Hotel staff were all nice except one who needed cheering up, doormen helpful ordering cabs and giving out umbrellers when it rained. breakfast was good choice, not many hotels in chaicago offer complimentary brekkie. Location was great, a mile from the lake shore and navy pier but its a nice safe walk. Loads of bars around, hard rock is a 5 minute walk, excalibur nightclub even closer. John hancock tower is a 15 min walk, the mag mile is 2-3 mins away allthough i was dissapointed with the mag mile. Its nothing on 5th avenue in NYC Rooms are small but modern, LCD tv on the wall with 5-6 HD channels and a good range of other channels. Bathroom is modern, no probs whatsoever, choice of soft-hard pillows is a nice touch. Free wifi was useful I would recommend this hotel for the price its great, i cant see a reason to go sheraton or hilton next time im in town. All it lacks is a bar but there are plenty close by. If im really critical id say the cleanleness isnt too great when you walk around the hotel lobby and hallways, in my room where the skirting boards meet the carpet it was full of dust and the coloured carpet really showed it up.

“Would not stay again” I stayed at this Marriott in mid-July for a family reunion. Check-in was not a problem, but the front desk person on this particular day seemed indifferent at best. She could not answer even a basic question about the hotel's events. My room (1623) was very clean, and the beds and pillows were very comfortable---but it goes down hill from there. My particular room did not have a safe or fridge, and the bathroom sink drained very, very slowly. Also, the carpet in my room felt damp and clammy to the bare feet, so please wear socks and/or shoes. I am not sold on the adjoining room concept. The walls are really thin and the noise from the hallway, conversations and other activities travel very easily. There are some things that you just don't want your young children to hear (if you know what I mean). Also, the curious child in the adjoining room next door spent quite a bit of time trying to open our room door which was very annoying. Please avoid room 1623. It is directly across the hall from the ice vending machine room. The machine noisily hums and drains water all night long; as well, there is the constant in and out traffic of people filling up their ice buckets. Unless you are a very sound sleeper, you will get very little sleep in this room. There was also a member of our reunion party who stayed down the hall in room 1610 where the knob lock did not work at all, and the clasp lock did not lock properly. I would avoid that room as well. The parking garage layout is a bit convoluted so watch out for that, too. To offer some balance, I will say that the hotel's breakfast buffet, while pricey at $17.00 per adult, was good with lots of variety including very fresh fruit, although the strawberries were a bit sour. In looking at what I paid for for the value that I received, I would not stay at this hotel again.

“Disappointing for a Hilton ... a 3.5 star experience ... multiple issues” First-timer at the Hilton-Financial District ... disappointed ... GRADE: B- (OK-average) ... it should have been better. On to the review: HOTEL: A large, almost monolithic,concrete (exterior)-looking hotel nestled at the edges of Chinatown, Financial District, adult-entertainment district, and SF version of Little Italy (along Columbus Ave). Very convenient to all of these and with a bit of additional walking, Union Square & Market St. The hotel is a weak representation of Hilton ... probably primarily a business hotel, with a large lobby ... greeted by somewhat disinterested front desk. It was an odd front lobby ... with a large aquarium, giant clocks on the wall, along with a pseudo-combo-bar-concession/souvenir-stand near the front doors, a giant map of SF on opposite side of front desk, and then towards back is the in-house restaurant named Seven-Fifty, which we did not try. The hotel felt a little dated, a little worn & tired, a little run-down..... and we're not that overly picky. The hallway to our room was rather dim, seemed dingy, & grim vs warm, inviting, bright, or colorful. ROOM: Be forewarned: We requested a room on South side of hotel, away from construction going on at North side (new building going up). When we went out for dinner at 6:00, we heard some construction noises & activities still going....so ... ask for the South-facing city view side of hotel. We were situated on a mid-level floor on the 20th floor, and had a view of buildings, as expected, and it was fairly quiet. We could clearly see Chinatown, and the hill-y streets that run through the area. There was a large combo-credenza-desk that ran from wall to wall of the room by the window, with the flat TV on it, built-in A/C-heat unit, and plug-in options for tech-goodies you bring. Seemed ok, though a bit long, and overwhelming. Would have been nicer if not as full-length, and had the extra floor space as well as be able to stand by the window. A nice chaise-style lounge chair made for comfortable viewing of TV. The double-beds were comfortable. The bathroom was an issue.... clean enough, but there were visible cracks in ceiling, peeling paint, and oddly, a rusting towel rack. How do you have a towel rack above the tub, that rusts ?!?! Speaking of the tub, it was elevated ... such that when taking a shower, our heads were above the curtain-rod ... very odd. No, not built for handicapped either. And the towels ... blah.... fairly matted down, somewhat dingy, not very white, and one of them had large holes ..... this is a HILTON ?!?! Paris, would you stay here ??? More oddities: no bathroom cups, no shampoo ... and we asked the cleaning staff in hallway working on another room for these basics, were told they had no more. What ?!?! "No more" ?!?! Wow! Moving on ... the room was warm & musty when we first arrived, so we turned the thermostat on ... nothing happened, and then lowered it to 60 degrees, felt nothing. Additionally, two lamps were not working = bedside and free-standing. Only the small desk lamp was working. 'Engineering' was called = fixed the A/C, fixed one lamp and the other needed a part.... and given we were there just one night, we told him to fix it another day. Sure enough, as the sun set, room was dark even with all the working lights on. TV on helped. Not a huge issue. Lastly, we did have a connecting room, and heard people talking ... but not on that side of the room!!! The voices were coming from the non-connecting side ... thin walls?? SUMMARY: If you're visiting for business and want easy access to nearby Transamerica building, Financial District, Embarcadero, or visiting SF for nearby Chinatown, along with the many restaurants/bars on/near Columbus Ave, this is most convenient. If you're looking for a quaint, romantic, or warm/friendly hotel, this isn't it. For general tourists, there are so many other great hotels at comparable prices and more convenience for sightseeing than this hotel. It is clearly in need of a spruce up, from decor, staff-efforts, and room upgrades. Don't get us wrong ... it is not a dump, but it is not a 4-star hotel either. We recommend this hotel if you get a good rate, or convenience to specific area is essential. Otherwise, so many other great options in this wonderful city. Happy Hotel-ing !!!

“class and courtesy in the heart of the back bay” While on a hybrid business / college evaluation trip I spent one night here, and found everything to be fantastic. The location is ideal, at the heart of things around Kenmore Square. The staff was friendly without being overbearing, the gym was above expectations. I did not eat at the hotel and the Red Sox were not in town so my experience is the room and the staff and the location. All were fantastic, and at least when I stayed, paying less that $200 for a Fenway room, for Boston this was actually decent value as well, considering also that the internet was free. I will return, particularly if I am going to the House of Blues or even Fenway or BU, but even just to walk around Kenmore and then the Back Bay.

“Pretty nice, but a few things you should know” Stayed for 3 days recently for a series of meetings at or near the hotel. Here's the summary: Location: Near airport at interchange of I-35 and Ben White. The grounds are pretty nice, but north side rooms have a front row for the sights and sounds of a typical freeway interchange. Many restaurants, both quick service and sit down, are located within a mile or two. Condition: Showing some age, but generally pretty comfortable. Beds/linens, etc. were comfortable, and I slept better than I usually do in hotels despite the freeway noise. I think they've done a pretty nice job with maintenance. A notable exception was that the water took at least 3 minutes to warm up the first time I used the shower. This was an isolated incident that did not recur, but 2 days later, the water turned cold in the middle of my shower (head fully lathered in shampoo, of course!). It did warm back up after about 30 seconds, without me ever touching the control. Banquet food: About average, nothing memorable or terrible. Onion Creek Grill (hotel restaurant): Terrific cooked to order "pasta buffet" at lunch, which really means you choose all your ingredients and they whip up some fabulous pasta dishes before your eyes. If you aren't counting calories, this is well worth a visit. There's a coffee shop in the lobby and an apparently well stocked lobby bar in the evenings. Leisure: Indoor/outdoor pool is large, clean and comfortable. There's a nice whirlpool and a large dry sauna as well. Fitness center includes Precor equipment (3 treadmills, 2 ellipticals, 2 stationary bikes,) free weights, and 7 or so Cybex pieces for strength training. Headphones, cool towels, water, etc. Half court basketball area adjacent to the pool deck, and even a grassy area with croquet. Under-elevatored at peak times: 14 floors + meeting facilities + 3 elevators = packed elevators and long waits at peak times. If this annoys you, try for a room at or above the 8th floor. I watched many frustrated people on lower floors have to wait for the next elevator as yet another full elevator from above opened without room to get on. Overall, I liked the place and thought the value was fair to good. Here's a tip: Join Omni Select Guest (rewards program -- free, easy to do at check-in if you aren't already a member) and get free WiFi, pressing for a couple of garments, and bottled water.

“A bit overwhelmed by a huge convention” Once the chaotic checkin was over and we finally (after 3) got our room we discovered that we had been upgraded to a suite for no discernible reason. It was huge, immaculate and super comfortable. The bathroom was not luxurious and the amenities basic but all worked well and the shower didn't require an advanced engineering degree. Well located and definitely built for a crowd this a a good convention facility lacking intimacy and charm but efficient and user friendly.

“Very good hotel” The hotel has large confortable rooms. The breakfast is basic but correct. You have to serve the brakfast yourself and you can take it to your room, or if the weather is nice, you can have breakfast next to the pool. There is a large supermarket at 3 min walk and several restaurants (mainly fast food) at walking distance. The hotel has its own parking but sometimes it was full when returning late at night. One plus: the gentleman that was at the front desk during the mornings was very helpful and gave us many useful tips for visiting the city. Besides he speaks spanish.

“My Kinda Hotel ... !” We've stayed here a few times (4 ?). Name has changed since the last but it is the spot we'd always pick first. There are better hotels I guess - but we like this one. We stopped here first many years ago on a trip from Oz. We had a Rt 66 tour starting. Since then we've picked it as our hotel of choice 3 more times. To give you an idea - last time we arrived it was a catastrophe happening. Water broken - and bathrooms unusable. We were told they were fixing but if we wanted they would transport us to another hotel. We said we'd chance it - much to the surprise and thankful reponse of the lady in charge. The water was fixed quickly and things got back to normal very quickly. They are an efficient bunch. We stopped in our normal room - not the swankiest in the hotel - but we like it. Front of the hotel - about 7 floors up. They have an awesome restaurant - where you can feel the atmosphere and almost see the ghosts of old crooners and mobsters of days gone by. Easy walking distance to the Mag Mile, fabulous restaurants, and even Navy Pier. A short block to the lake and an easy walk to the train stop if you want to go to a ball game. Or an early morning walk is lovely - just you and the squirrels. Almost every restaurant style you could want nearby.A wonderful bakery around the corner for brekkie too. When we think Chicago - we think this hotel ! Would love to go back soon.

“How far the mighty have fallen” I stayed at the Wyndham Franklin Plaza for a business meeting. Philly is my home town and I had always considered this a finer hotel. First off, the front desk staff was incredibly nice - its hardly their fault the place is so down at the heels. My room had been slept in already when I opened the door (it was 11 pm local time). I really think that hotel staff was sleeping in this room because they thought nobody was coming to claim it. A tad creepy. That was settled after a phone call including request for soap and shampoo (this was mentioned by another reviewer). The room was huge although I must say the carpet was really in need of a scrub. The place was super quiet and I liked that. There wasn't another hotel room in the city so I stayed there until my relatives would take me at their place.

“July stay - Wit pros and cons” Stayed 4 nights over 4th of July week. HH Gold member. Wife and I on vacation sans kids! pro - clean rooms, good location near Red Line (State and Lake), theaters, and Chicago river, nice view from 17th floor albeit there are a lot of surrounding tall buildings, AM (roosters) and PM (owls) muzak in the halls, big screen TV, large bathroom and amenities, quiet, good floor security (card key access) due to popular club (ROOF) on the 25th floor, good breakfast but only because of HH vouchers, otherwise pricey. Numerous staff in the lobby who were helpful with directions. con - small lobby, 2nd floor Italian restaurant is closed, some AM lobby construction, biz center had internet fee, small gym, no pool, no lobby bar traffic, only the 20ish crowd going up to the roof, some riff-raff outside due to the subway stop. All in all probably a business/chic hotel for young professionals. Not so family friendly. Wife liked the trendy decor while I'm more interested in variety and services. Enjoy.

“Hotel was fine” The hotel was fine and in a fairly good location, i.e., access to Union Square. The rooms were larger than expected. Nothing overly outstanding at the hotel, but it was just a nice place to stay. The negative is that they didn't have their coffee/tea service until the last morning (we stayed 2 nights).

“Nice property but I missed what all the fuss is about.” Let me first stay this is a decent property, in a good location, with very good service. I would definately stay here again. However, in my opinion, going agaist the grain of all the other reviewers, this is definately not even close to the 4th best hotel in Austin. As as matter of fact, it is the 2nd worst Hampton I have ever stayed in. Let me explain. After a pleasant check-in experience, we rode the elevator to our room on the sixth floor. My wife and I joked, "Look the elevator inspection ran out last month, maybe we should not ride the elevator." Unfortunately, another couple had not noticed, this next morning we awoke to trapped people in the elevator unable to get out. 12 hours later, people trapped in the elevator next to the original one. That is problem one. Next while the bathrooms and lobby have been remodeled, the hallways, are dingy 1980's wallpaper. Number 3. While the beds are confomy, even when freshly made they look like someone has been sleeping in them. Upon entering our room my wife exclaimed, we are in the wrong room, someones been laying the beds. Number 4, the breakfast bar was not replinished in a timely manner. Number 5, do not stay in rooms up high with low single digit numbers, they are near the road and you have to run the fan all night to cover up the road noise. Finally, we could not run the heater because the smell was so bad. In summary, decent hotel and a good value but nowhere near one of the top hotels in Austin. I have stayed in at least 5 hotels in Austin, all far superior to this property.

“Great Hotel” We stayed at the Argonaut twice in September while travelling around California. Upon arrive we were told that there was an error with the booking and there was not a room. However, they had found us a room in the Sheraton about 4 blocks away, they paid for our night’s accommodation plus refunded our money for the room and gave us $20 for taxis between the hotel plus a bottle of wine. Following our night in the Sheraton we returned and stayed in a room on 3rd floor with a view of over Hyde Pier and towards the Golden Gate Bridge. The staff was exceptional and willing to offer information about how to get about to various sightseeing attractions. The rooms were well proportioned and stocked with Aveda products.Food in the Blue Mermaid was excellent value for money. We will definitely be staying here again next time we are in San Francisco.
