“A great place to be” Stayed at the Ritz Denver in late-August 2012. The hotel was very nice and I had no problems with the service. In fact I thought the service was top notch. Never had to open a door over my entire stay. I though the rooms were very nice and I love the mirror in the shower. Got room 1004. As nice as the hotel is, the fitness facility is among the best I have ever used. Full size in-door basket ball court, very large rock climbing wall, about 25 treadmills and another 25 elliptical machines. And, if you are looking to exercise with free weights, look no further. I think they had at least three sets of weights going up 100 lbs dumbbells. Overall a very nice stay and would recommend to anyone looking for a great hotel in downtown Denver.
“Very Disappointed” I think I expected some kind of kitchy boutique hotel. No. Just an old hotel. I think a lot of people will like this property. But it wasn't for me.

“Nice hotel, but nothing specials” Our room was clean, updated and comfortable. We have no complaints, but it was nothing special. Although we had a fantastic rate through Hotwire, when we added the cost of parking, we may have been better off staying at a hotel that was just as nice and included breatkfast.
“Great Stay” The lobby was contemporary, comfy, and relaxed. The service was superb, and the Rooms were WOW. Very large and well designed. Great Shower and incredible bed and sleep experience.

“Great home base for a weekend get away” While I am an avid Westin hotel supporter, I was initially concerned about my selection of the Westin Oaks due to the hotel's proximity to the Houston Galleria Mall. I could not have been more wrong. Our room was spacious, clean and quite comfortable. The Oaks, although undergoing a little upgrade construction, was an outstanding home base while my wife and I ventured into the mall for the day, the zoo in the morning and local dining options in the evening. Never once was I sorry I made arrangements to stay for a long weekend. Parking was a breeze as well. Although free parking is available underground, I choose to park just steps from the hotel for 12 dollars a night. If you want to valet, well, that is available as well. Another high point of our stay was the White Oak Kitchen restaurant on the 3rd floor. Their breakfast is fantastic and the happy hour (4-7 pm) is quite popular after a long day shopping! I would suggest this hotel to anyone wishing for ease of access while spending time at the mall or around town. It was a very pleasant trip! Thanks Westin!

“Good choice, but bring more money” Stayed at the Doubletree in February for a birthday treat for my wife to attend the Westminster dog show. The big plus: location, location, location. Close to everything. We even walked to Madison Square Garden twice. Staff was great. Room was oddly shaped, but well-appointed, nice bathroom, and OK for NYC; two-room suites are hard to find elsewhere. I am an Honors member, so we got free breakfast. Good thing. Way too expensive ($20 or so) for a slightly above Hampton Inn buffet. Of course, the room was expensive, like everything in New York, but not more than other hotels, so pretty good value all things considered. Good security, helpful staff. We got snowed in an extra day, and they were very accommodating. Had a billing error after-the-fact, but they cleared it up with no problem. I would go again, but look for a better rate.

“Nice hotel!” Arrived around 7 on a Friday night, just in time for the manager's reception which lasts until 730p. Great drinks and snacks! Can't beat that! Kids loved the huge seating area around the atrium. Ate dinner in the hotel restaurant. Food was very good and not too overpriced. Only downside is that they were not busy at all but the wait for food was very long. That being said, after having a few drinks driving to another restaurant was not an option. Check in was quick and easy. The room was very nice; two queen size beds and a pull out couch. Rooms have refrigerators and a microwave. Coffee maker in room stinks, but it didnt matter because there was plenty of coffee in the morning at breakfast. The living room and bedroom area are separated by a heavy door, which means privacy. Shower was standard with the usual toiletries, nothing special. Breakfast in the morning was fantastic. We stayed because of a gymnastics meet that started early. Usually on Saturdays they open the buffet at 7, but they had it up and running full speed for 6. It is the usual Embassy Suites fare, but there was a lot of food and it was good. My favorite is the made to order omlettes...definately a nice touch. We didn't use the pool, gym or business center. They do have a sundry shop with snacks, drinks of all kinds and other things. The parking is great; a nice garage behind the hotel. They do offer valet parking but you really don't need it because the parking is convenient. All in all, it was a great stay and I would both recommend it and stay there again. Our price was $99 for two adults and two children, booked by calling the hotel.

“Beautiful Hotel with friendly service!” We checked into the Doubletree after scoring a great deal on Priceline.com. We are generally satisfied with our Priceline purchases, however, this hotel is above and beyond all o our expectations. The staff was incredibly friendly and eager to help. The place appears to be well maintained and hey, you cannot beat the Doubletree cookie when you check in! The hotel dining looks exceptional. The rooms are beautiful and very clean and inviting. Definately a property that we would reserve at again!

“Very comfy!” We stayed here for one night at the end of a Disneyland trip to be closer to LAX. The hotel is very attractive and the beds were super. Our only problem was that the first room we were given had a barking dog in the next room. We were quickly switched to another room which was quiet, but not as large and nice as the first room. Since it was only for one night, I did not complain. We had breakfast the next morning in the Breeze dining room. The food and service were very good, but a bit pricey at $75 for 2 adults and 2 children. The location of the hotel is very nice for visiting the Getty Center and Hollywood.
“great hotel in the city” lovely hotel. large room. kitchen area adds a lot of comfort. helpful, pleasant staff. great location. would definitely stay there again.

“Attentive all around” We arrived late Friday, the front desk staff was very friendly and perky which helps after a long drive. They had our keys ready and quickly get us set up so we can go to our room and rest. The space is nice and huge, the fully kitchen does have everything and just having a full size fridge is a great help. The housekeeping was nice and does come back after you ask them to. They made sure we have new towels and soap and shampoo. Plenty of parking spots in well lit area at night, convenient and safe for guests. The down side is, this place is old and the rooms and hallways showed. Keep an eye on the towels, there were couple of times that the towels have stains on them.

“Great Hotel” I was here on business for two nights and it was fantastic. The rooms were huge and very clean. Every single person that works at the hotel was nice and helpful. Very accommodating! Club Level is a must, as the breakfast is solid and free water and coke throughout the day, and free light snacks at night. Workout room can have a little more, but still good! Check out rooftop pool!

“Nostalgic. Great Location.” I stayed here for a quick overnight business trip. As a Hilton Honors member the gym was free. The gym is AMAZING! I think the price to use it is $10-$15. I don't know if I would pay that, but FREE was awesome. The gym is fully equipped and they have nice ice cold face towels infused with basil and herbs. Such a nice touch after a hard day and workout. The hotel rooms are small, but nicely updated. Room service was excellent. Hotel has an older musty smell.....as most old hotels do. If you are a history buff and enjoy old architecture then this hotel would be fun. Room was clean, no view though :( Location is great. Two blocks from the White House. I would stay here again if I needed to, but not my first choice.

“Stylish but noisy” This is a fashionable boutique-style hotel right at the corner of 26th St and Broadway, so close to Fifth Avenue shopping and an easy walk to Penn Station and Times Square. My room wasn't large but was well appointed with contemporary furniture, including electric drapes controlled from a bedside switch. The bathroom had the tech gimmick of a TV built into the mirror (which I had no interest in, and which, when switched off, meant there was a dark rectangle in the mirror when I was shaving). The shower was a highlight: a combination of overhead rain showerhead and front-on body sprays: you could select either or both with the rotating knob. The main problem with the accommodation was that no amount of flashy technology could conceal the underlying dated infrastructure. The heating was crude: every few minutes it came on with a huge whirr and blasted the room with hot air until it began to feel oppressive, then it switched off again and the temperature dropped away until the cycle was repeated. During the night I switched it off to avoid the noise and the big temperature swings while I was under the covers. But at least the room had heat: the bathroom, on the other hand, was distinctly chilly. It seemed that there was no heating there at all, except when you opened the door to let a little drift in from the room. Hotel staff were very friendly but another annoyance was the restaurant/ bar on the ground floor, where at check-in a band was playing so loudly that I asked for a high-floor room. The receptionist chuckled, obviously knowing exactly what I was talking about, having had to work with it all evening. In summary, a great location and nice fitments in the rooms, but with issues caused partly by their own making and partly by the fact that this is a conversion of an old building.

“Westin Quality All the Way” My frist time in San Antonio, and I selected the Westin because of its location and that I am a Platinum SPG member. I only stayed 1 night, and was very pleased with the experience. Check in was smooth. Lobby was marble and woods in a Southwest decor. Everything seemed new. Upgraded to a junior suite which was spacious and modern. Street noise, even on the 7th floor, was unexpetedly disturbing from the buses. Hotel breakfast was right on the river (more like a small canal) which was peaceful and pleasant. Staff were all very friendly and well-mannered and in uniforms. I will definitely stay here again when in San Antonio.

“Good Airport Hotel” Hotel is designed for layovers, with shuttle buses that leave every 20 min on the hour and departure schedule screens in the lobby. The hotel is very close to the airport, approx 5 min shuttle. The rooms are modern and staff is efficient. The bed has a duvet but is a little on the hard side and could be a bit more comfortable for my taste. For dinner I had room service and the sea bass was very good. I have stayed more than once and recommend staying on the side away from the airport.

“Overpriced” My wife, son, and I stayed one night on a weekend getaway using Marriott Rewards Points (30K = too many!). The location is great for spending time on the Riverwalk and Alamo. The hotel lobby/bar/Starbucks/etc. are all excellent, and the underground parking is easy and convenient. The room was fine, but nothing special. A bit disappointing, considering the money/points. The swimming pool is outdoor and located on the 4th floor on a section of roof. The pool is fine, but nothing special, and there is a large deck area for lounging. We did not use the workout room, but it looked nice and had a lot of machines. The only problem we had was that we found hair in the sheets on one of the beds when we pulled the covers back to go to bed. (Gross!) They were apologetic and offered to move us to another room, but we declined and asked for a new set of sheets since we had already unpacked and settled in and it was late. After waiting 40 minutes I had to call again to get them to get them moving. We mentioned this at checkout and were told, apologetically, that there was nothing they could do to compensate. Overall, this is a good place to stay if you want to spend time on the Riverwalk, but as we are not fans of the Riverwalk, we most likely will not return here.

“Nice friendly, helpful staff, rooms were also nice” The hotel is a nice hotel. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Very helpful in giving directions. Hotel is located right next to the Van Nuys Airport, the planes are noisy when outside by the pool, but sound is muffled in the rooms. The rooms are very nice and fairly large. Free wireless internet, also free ethernet cable. Comfortable beds, large sink/counter (which is outside the bathroom w/toilet and shower. The shower head wasn't too great - weird settings, not much water pressure. Not many restaurants or places to see within walking distance. You definitely need a car, but parking is $9.00/day. There are nicer neighborhoods in the Valley but the hotel and staff are very nice. Alot of meeting rooms and big conference center

“Downtown deserves better...” I was somewhat excited about staying at this building full of architectural history, figuring it would make for a unique stay. The room was larger than most in old buildings, as was the bathroom, however it was very noisy. I heard the "neighbors" across the hall with their kids as if they were in my room, and the room door rattled it seemed everytime someone walked by or shut a door across the hall. The hotel staff was not as friendly as I come to expect from Hilton properties. The lobby and free breakfast areas were large (if you have a big group), but was mostly empty during my stay.

“Second time around, things are getting better.” This was my second visit to the Thompson LES this year. The first time I visited (see my review) I was solo, staying in a front facing room for just under a week and it really wasn't what I hoped it be. Upon an invitation to return, let's say the place has picked up in the months since I was last there. This time around I was visiting with family (albeit for the night) and found there had been some decorating in the lobby (a little more ambience). After suffering an abysmal and much delayed none hour flight via American Airlines flight from Dallas (O, I should have known) we were all very keen to get to bed because of the late hour. When we checked in we were assured the requested crib was in the room but no it wasn't and when one of the completely helpful staff turned up with it, he couldn't assemble it. No matter, we had our own portacrib and our son was in bed in minutes. This really was the only blemish on the Thompson's service and friendly staff. The room was of great quality and thankfully to the rear of the building. One thought, perhaps Fellini's La Dolce Vita playing on the elevator screen could be given a rest.

“Historic hotel but the glory has faded” Arrival experience: Arrived early afternoon on a Sunday. Courteous and professional front desk staff. Room (general): the rooms are fairy spacious. The furniture is very worn (see photo of end table) and not high quality. Overall, the paint, drywall, and general quality of the finish out is poor. For example, caulking is smeared near the bathtub, very poor drywall work is obvious throughout, and the carpet was stained. The paint is dark throughout the hotel, possibly in an attempt to conceal very poor finishing. Furthermore, the hotel is dirty. I walked onto an elevator twice hours apart and the floor was covered in dirt. Also, the blinds in my room (1007) were falling apart on one window (see photo). Small LCD TV. Bathroom: Spacious bathroom, but the plumbing is old and makes a ton of noise. Bed: Decent bed but the bedspread was dirty (see photo). Houskeeping: Leave a modest tip to ensure basic service such as changing the liner in the ice bin and replenishing soaps. Restaurants: I did not eat at the restaurant, but the morning breakfast buffet was good. Bar: The free happy hour at the bar was pathetic. The only free options were cheap wine (options of Chardonnay and Cab) and Bud on draft. Grounds: small public area in front of hotel (see photo from room looking down) Pool: none Gym: Medium to small gym with your routine workout machines like exercise bikes, treadmills, etc. The water cooler in the workout room was extremely slow at dispensing water. Parking: Efficient valet staff. At arrival, 2 valets waited at the curb and immediately assisted me. Misc: Other: The first night the smoke detector woke me up beeping; not a fun way to begin an intense work week. I brought this to the attention of the staff, and the problem did not arise again. The free wi-fi was frustrating. The front desk provided code cards for my phone and tablet. One card was invalid immediately. The other stopped working after a couple of days. The elevators are slow and make a creaking noise. The interiors of the elevators have seen better days; they need to be refinished. Overall, I love the history of the building, but history is not enough to generate customer loyalty. I would never stay here again because it’s dirty and worn out. Maybe a chain like Hyatt, Hilton, or Marriott could turn the place around?

“Superb location, historic building, nice rooms, great staff” Stayed here for 4 days on a recent trip to DC. The hotel is very centrally located to most of the big tourist sites, although there are a lot of sights in DC. It is about 1 block from the White House, and is about a 10 minute walk to the National Mall, with the Smithsonians and the major memorials and monuments. Check in was fast and efficient and we were given a corner suite on the 8th floor as a Royal Ambassador. The room was very nice, as it used to be 2 rooms, but had been merged into one large one, with a small hallway linking the two sections. The decor is typical of an old style, historic hotel but is largely functional and useable. The bed was very soft and comfortable and the bathroom was well stocked with shampoos, soaps and other amenities. Housekeeping was efficient and never bothered or disturbed us while we were in the room, which is a nice change from some hotels where they nag you to clean the room. The lobby was very nicely decorated with cherry blossoms, as they were blooming at the time. The only downside was a very subpar room service, where the food took more than double the time we were told and some of it was cold upon arrival. Otherwise, the hotel made an excellent place to stay. Location was excellent and was about a 10 minute was to the Metro.

“Very disappointing” We stayed in this hotel for 4 nights from 8th June. Where do I start. The check-in clerk seemed very confused. There were 5 of us checking in and the person on her own was supposed to have a small room. I think we got the small room. We could hardly negotiate around the bed. The air conditioning system would have to be the most antiquated contraption I have ever seen. It consisted of a metal rod attached to something on the ceiling which had aluminium foil over the outlet. It didn't work anyway and Washington was having a heatwave. We asked for someone to look at it and the maintenance man said air was coming out but we couldn't feel it. We complained again and they supplied us with a fan. The maintenance man was very apologetic and I think a bit embarrassed. We were afraid to plug anything into the wall as the electricity connections seemed very dodgy with loose wires showing. The two restaurants attached to the hotel are not good. We were charged $15 for 2 continental breakfasts which were inadequate and which in other hotels had been included in the price. The next morning we went around the corner to a sandwich shop and got a much better breakfast for the same price. Unfortunately there are not too many eateries open later at night which are near the hotel as it is downtown, at least this was the excuse we heard. The location of the hotel is the only thing going for it. It is about 2 blocks from the White House and within walking distance of museums and the hop-on hop-off bus. The hotel is quite old and in need of some refurbishment. There is a guest laundry and free internet which is some good news. We were given a discount for the air conditioning debacle but that still would not entice me to stay at the Harrington again. Sorry.

“Lovely property recently renovated, like stepping back in time” LOVE, love, love the bungalows and what has been done with this older gem. It's like stepping back in time with the lovely tropical grounds and the old Hollywood glamour in the bungalows. The meeting space is lovely as well, The thing that makes this really special? The employees, people are genuine and hardworking and always available to assist. Loved my time here, wish it had been longer.

“Not a good choice for HH members” I typically stay at the Parc 55 when I am in SF, but decided as a HH diamond member to give this hotel a shot the last weekend in September. As a person with no status with Wyndham, I get better treatment at the Parc 55 down the street then I do at the SF Hilton with no status. One big drawback for HH members is that this property always seems to opt out of the quarterly promos. I realize there was also a conference going on when I stayed there, but the wait to check in was WAY TOO long. They only had one clerk working the HH line and that was open to all HH members. A busy hotel like that should have a line for their higher status loyality members. I was given no upgrade (although I found out another person attending the same event I was that checked in after me on the same rate code was given a lot nicer room with no HH status than I was) and the room I was given was very small. I did like the bathroom products and liked that they had the PTR shower gel in the bathroom (first domestic Hilton I have been at where I had the shower gel when I wasn't on the exec level). The free breakfast was just a voucher was only good for a coffee drink and pastry and piece of fruit at starbucks or the continental breakfast in the restaurant and if you wanted any hot items there was an upcharge:( One nice thing though about the starbucks voucher is that there are plenty of good places in the area to eat breakfast at and you can use it anytime the starbucks is open and I used the voucher later in the day for a coffee and ate the pastry and fruit for a snack. A tip for solo travellers: book the room for two and use one of the vouchers in the restaurant and the other later in the day at starbucks. The internet was decent but they charged me and I had to have the front desk remove the charges at checkout (which they did with no hassle). It is convenient to the Bart and Muni if you are coming from SFO. Near all kinds of shopping and dining, but it borders a very seedy area on the one side and lots of street people in the area at night.

“Your staff are outstanding” Room 1021 - A little worn, but very nice. However your staff make up for that! The lady who checked me in was outstanding and every staff member I came across was a credit to the hotel. Thank you for making my stay so pleasent!

“Cool little place, but no services” This is a nice place. Looks great with lots of exposed brickwork and a cool atrium. Exposed brick in my 5th floor room too. Beds nice, plenty of hot water, linens were middle of the road. There is no restaurant or room service, you have to call out if you want delivery. And no gym or bar either. No coffee in room but plenty in the lobby as well as computers in the lobby too. So if you just need a neat room but not any hotel services this is the place for you.

“Good for the convention center but kind of far from everything else” I was in this hotel for a convention recently and was not disappointed but also not significantly iimpressed either. The hotel is relatively new, so everything is clean and in working order. However, as other people have mentioned, the lobby is very noisy and doesn't provide a good venue to get together to talk. More annoying, however, is that the walls in the rooms are not soundproof, so you can hear quite a bit of what is going on in the rooms next to you. Worse though, is that the sounds from the hall are clearly audible in the rooms. On the plus side, this hotel is very convenient to the convention center but there isn't much else in the immediate vicinity and the area immediately to the north is kind of seedy. You need to go 5 or 6 blocks to get to the Inner Harbor although the circulator bus (which is free) stops right outside the hotel and will take you to the harbor in about 5 minutes.

“Treated reall Well.” There is no check in desk. The Staff greets you in the lobby with laptops and checks you in, while you grab a snack and drink from "The Common Table" free of charge. They make great espresso's to order too, up till midnight I think. The Minibar? It's complimentary for all non alcoholic drinks and snacks as of my stay, and it was wonderful. This hotel was "purpose built" and has a power shade that lowers with a touch of a button, and a huge "rain" style shower stall too. The beds are modern (not too hard or soft) and covered with duvets. This hotel is very clean, I might add. Near the 2,3 & 4 subway trains by Trinity Church made this a no brainer to stay downtown.

“A wonderful example of the Hyatt touch” I had two wonderful stays at this property in January. The hotel exceeded my expectations in every respect. Smooth check-in (the front desk staff noticed that I was exhausted from my trip and offered me a complimentary bottle of Evian) and great Diamond recognition, nice rooms, and great location. However, what really amazed me was the hotel staff's' level of service and dedication. Literally every single person I interacted with had a smile on their face and seemed eager to help. Emad at the restaurant deserves a special recognition. Not only was he a great server, but he remembered my name every morning... even when I unexpectedly returned a week after my first stay. If there is one complaint it would be that the hotel was unable to provide an alternative for the White Ginger shampoo (which I really dislike).

“Lack of Service Trumps Great Location” This is about my 5th or 6th stay at his large, convention hotel in Chicago. I'm always underwhelmed but this stay is the worst. First the positives: Great location on the river and bordering Michigan Ave and the Loop. Easy access to anything in Chicago. Rooms are clean and nicely appointed. Typical very comfortable Sweet Sleeper beds. Good walking/jogging access along the river. The downsides are mostly related to the size. This hotel,is huge and always crowded. You will wait for everything - check-in, cabs, elevators, room at the bar...you name it. I spent 30 minutes in line waiting to check in with no attempt by the hotel to add staff to the counters. Food can be a problem as well. The hotel has a casual place for breakfast and lunch and a hard to find hamburger place on the lower level. Check in later in the evening and your only choices are room service and Shula's Steakhouse. Room service in all city hotels is expensive but more so in this Sheraton. A salad and beer will cost you $35. Shula's is an expensive, fine dining restaurant. Not a place for a light dinner after flying all day. The staff seems resigned to unhappy guests and politely apologizes but always has an excuse for why things weren't better - "we are sold out", "we are very busy tonight", "you need to get that at that other counter"(with another 10 minutes in line). I was unable to opt out of housekeeping without coming downstairs and waiting in another line. If yu are on vacation and have lots of time and just need a nice place to sleep, this hotel may be OK. I will go elsewhere in the future.

“Good Hotel in a Great Location” The Hotel is in a perfect location for exploring San Francisco. Close to bars, shopping, clubs, restaurants and is close to the transport links to see the sights that are slightly further away. The hotel is clean, tidy, stylish, modern and the staff are efficient if a little cold. The room we had (a suite i think) was spacious, with lots of extras. Overall, a good stay and i would return.

“Only a few disappointments” I attended a business conference at the Manchester this past weekend, November 9-12. It was a very large convention, and the very large convention facilities had no difficulty in handling this large group. I had pre-booked a non-smoking king bed, but was told it was unavailable when I arrived. I could take two single beds or upgrade (for $40) to a "panoramic view" room with a king. I chose the upgrade. It was a corner room, with a view of the bay and of the front of the hotel. The lobby is very beautiful, and the staff handling check-in was wonderful. (Staff was wonderful throughout my stay.) The room was a bit of a disappointment, as the carpet is getting old and one of three big windows was blocked by a wall. I had visited the Hyatt website right before the trip and was anticipating the new bed, six pillows, and iPod-ready radio-alarm clock... perhaps a flat screen LCD TV. None of these were present in my room. I ordered room service a few times, which arrived in a timely manner and was appealing. I ordered sausage with my breakfast one morning but got bacon. I called to let Room Service know and they offered to reduce the charge on the tab. When I checked out they had not done that, and no one associated with Room Service has any recollection of that offer. To their credit, they immediately reduced that charge by 25%. In-room internet was wireless, but required a credit card and could not be billed to the room. I wish all hotels offered free internet connections in every room. Charge for this was $9.95 per day. The area surrounding the hotel is great, and fun for exploring. I enjoyed visiting the KC Barbeque restaurant and bar directly across from the hotel, the site of filming the "sleazy bar scene" in Top Gun. It's teeny-tiny. I was on the 17th floor and happy I was not a floor below that. The previous reviews mention noise from the trains and they are LOUD. The trolley trains make a little noise as they come by, but the AMTRAK trains blow their VERY loud horns at each intersection. Because of the convergence of streets right at the hotel, there's at least two intersections the train has to go through right there. Some trains just gave a little blast but some engineers must have enjoyed really leaning on the horn! I will say that I was not disturbed in my sleep, though. Thick curtains? I'd recommend as high a floor as you can get. And if you do, you'll find that the elevator service was spectacular. I never had to wait long for a ride, despite the large crowd in the hotel.

“Bad beginning but got better.” We stayed at the Sheraton Boston last April for 3 nights. I got this hotel through Hotwire. We had a bad start but a good ending. We arrived late to the hotel and were given a double room as I needed. When we arrived to the room it was a little small but nice. After a few minutes I started to realize that our clothes and our bags had animal hair all over. I discovered that there was pet hair, I assume it was dog hair, all over the carpet! I immediately called the front desk but I was told that no more double rooms were available and we are a family of 4. No way I was going to stay in that room. The first option I got was to send someone to vaccum the room. It was 11 pm, my kids were about to sleep, already in their pajamas, and I wasn't going to have someone clean a room that was already supposed to be clean. So then I was told that we could move to the other tower for only one night because that tower was going to be shut down for maintenance and I was going to get another room the next day and a one night credit. So we had to move to the other tower and it was fine and the room was in fact bigger. The next day I was allowed to keep the bags in the same room and I adviced that we weren ́t coming back again until late night. When we returned again there were no double rooms available! I was very upset but finally after some calls we were upgraded to a Club Level double room. So finally we stayed 2 more nights with no problems at all. But other than this problem we had at the beginning, we had a very good stay. The rooms like I said are not very big, but are comfy, clean and well maintained. The location is perfect because it's at Prudential Center and there are stores, restaurants and a metro station right there, so it was very easy to move around the city. I will definitely stay there again.

“okay, but not top choice” We have stayed at both White Swan and Petite Auberge, a sister property, in the past, but not for several years. We were quite disappointed in our recent stay, especially compared to our last stay, when it was still a "4 Sisters Inn." The staff varied from indifferent to excellent. Our room was attractive but very dusty and our bathroom was especially so (corners, towel bars, etc.). We only had turndown service one of our 3 nights there. It was very noisy and our bed sagged in the middle. The morning breakfast was good, but not "like it used to be." Next time we'll stay somewhere else.

“Great value” Stayed with my family in a spacious double room. Got a great deal and breakfast is included. Rooms were basic but clean. Very easy access to subways on 6th and 7th Aves. Staff was helpful in suggestion, giving directions, etc.

“Good location a bit noisy” I stayed in this hotel for a week and while the location was perfect the street noise was quite high. On Two morning I woke at 6am to the noise of the local bin men. The rooms are a little small, but very clean. On saying that, the overall impression of the hotel and the Restaurant / Bar were excellent. The staff were also very helpful. Normally I would stay in the St Regis or Palace hotel, both were fully booked on this occasion, but this is a good 3rd choice. Next time I will ask for a higher room to try and avoid the street noise. It is also worth noting that there is free internet access in the hotel and it actually works.

“Pricier hotels take note, Hampton Inn is just as good if not better.” I love the fact Hampton Inn is opening more and more of these in NY... They have all the stuff you want, and none of the extra nonsense silly stuff. This is a clean, modern hotel with nice people working inside, a great bed, fast free wifi and a great breakfast. This particular Hampton I really like because it's tall and skinny, which means only a few rooms per floor, which = quiet!!! The location is great because it's just off 9th Ave which is packed with some of the best dining options in NY. I also like that they have honest to goodness hi-def programming, and not just a flat panel.

“Miracle on 17th Street” I initially checked into a competitor's hotel but was so discussed by that experience I went to the Westin Philadelphia to see if any rooms were available. I needed both Friday and Saturday night but only Friday night was available. The front desk clerk called two other full service hotels and found me a room, at a special rate for the entire weekend. I believe the desk agents name was Jason, and he went about and beyond the call of duty. I will always stay at the Westin Philadelphia! Thank you

“Great place to stay” Got a great rate through priceline so it's very good for the price. Flew overnight from LA and a front staff checked me in right away! However need to pay more if you want a room with the view so I passed. Room was spacious and comfortable, though on an older side. Location is excellent for tourists as it's right in Times Square. Lobby is on a higher floor so can be a bit confusing. There's no free wifi but you can walk out to TS area to use one. There's a Starbucks right on the ground floor which is convenient. Bellboys were very helpful. Would stay here again if I could get a good rate.

“Quirky but not bad” I booked the Club Quarters at Wacker due to the close proximity to a training session I was attending. CHECK-IN Quick, unremarkable experience. ROOM The room was smaller than I expected and had a 'dorm' feel to it - oddly shaped. Closet was small, only a few hangers. No drawers to unpack - but only staying for two nights so not that big of a deal. Cold outside and hot in the room, so I adjusted the room temp, but it would never come on. Oddly enough, the windows in the room opened (on the 21st floor if I remember correctly), but a sticker on the window said to call the front desk to open the window. Maintenance came within 10 minutes of calling to open the window and that was how I managed the temp. I guess I should have asked him to show me how to work the temp control, but I wanted fresh air once I realized that was an option. The bathroom is small, also found the coffee maker over toilet odd, also only had decaf the first a.m. and was running late so didn't call for regular coffee - but regular coffee was restocked with room service. Bed was comfortable, but coverlet was oddly worn and reminded me of a guest bedroom bedspread instead of hotel linen. Tested the alarm clock to make sure it worked - and it didn't, so I set the alarm on my cell phone instead. I also didn't report the alarm clock didn't work since I had a very easy work-around. LOBBY RESTAURANT Overpriced, but good. Small portions. Drinks a little overpriced. Ate there the first night (it was very cold outside and snowy and you didn't have to go outside to get to the restaurant). Suffice it to say my second night I found a chain restaurant a block away. LOBBY Was on the business trip alone, so preferred not to stray too far from the hotel. Second night, ate at a chain restaurant a block away, and upon returning to the hotel didn't want to be cramped in the small room watching tv, so I decided to check out the lobby. There is a small 'library' sitting area that has a TV, coffee machine, gas or electric fireplace, magazines, and a few books. However, on a night where it was 10 degrees out, I got a glass of wine for the lobby restaurant (they were kind enough to let me take the glass out to the lobby with me) and sit in front of the fire and read. Never before have I 'hung-out' in a hotel lobby before, but really it was cozy in an odd kind-of way! WORK-OUT ROOM Small, several machines, TV, water-cooler, towels. Not bad for a quick work-out. LOUNGE Not sure what to call this - a few PC's available, but quiet and easy to get online for free since I choose to not bring my own laptop. No wireless connections for those that do from what I could tell. CHECK-OUT Quick, didn't look to see if there was automatic on the TV, just stopped at the little desk on the way out and checked out, less than 2 minutes to accomplish. Overall - interesting departure from business travel experiences. Wasn't necessarily a negative experience, just different, and if you aren't stuck on the normal places to stay, might be worth a short stay!

“Nice location to match nice hotel” We stayed at Hotel Monaco around the July 4th holiday. I have stayed at many Kimptons and enjoy my stays. Staff is friendly. Sazerac is a good place to grab drinks and or dinner, try the oysters. It was a holiday weekend and hotel was busy but they seemed to be understaffed in both hotel and restaurant. I have stayed at this location several times. Rooms are mostly nice although we got tucked into a corner room which is smaller than their regular rooms. From what I can tell Premier rooms are just higher floor rooms and do not guarantee better views.

“Cheap convenient stay” Stayed here for 5 nights after flying in from Sydney Australia. I picked this hotel based on price, location close to LAX, free parking and free wi-fi. The room I was in was quite large and had plenty of room for me to get comfortable for the 5 night stay. It was clean enough and I really had no complaints besides the thin walls and the aircraft noise between 6am and midnight but I had noise cancelling earphones which worked wonders whenever I needed to sleep within those hours. There was complimentary breakfast supplied each morning which looked quite basic but I guess it's enough to get going in the morning although there is plenty to eat within short driving distance. Manhattan Beach is 10 minutes away as is El Segundo which also has a Wholefoods supermarket which has plenty of dining options. If you arrive back late at night then parking spaces will be all taken. Just park on the side street of the hotel which seemed safe enough.

“Great value if you want simple accomodation” This hotel is great value, rooms are clean and well kept but very basic (no clock) and may not be for everyone. Staff were helpful, breakfast VERY basic (coffee, Tang, some fruit, donoughts), area around hotel is a bit seedy but I felt safe. Nearby MoDonalds, and several nice restaurants within walking distance. Also easily walked Chase field for a night game. I'd stay again but it is not for everyone.

“Great Location, Great Property” I was in DC for a couple of nights on business, and stayed at the Marriott Wardman Park. The hotel is a mix of old charm and new convenience. I actually stayed in the newer part of the hotel during this visit, but have stayed in the old-historic building in the past. The location is beautiful, convenient, and the amenities are top notch. The Woodley Park Metro Station is just down the hill from the hotel, which makes it convenient to the rest of the District. The staffis great - very friendly and very accommodating. I will definitely stay here when the opportunity arises again.

“Dated but comfortable” The hotel is well located in Midtown. We found it very comfortable although it gives the impression of being run by the Russian mafia! Almost all the staff seem to be Russian or eastern European which seems a little odd for a mainstream Holiday Inn in the heart of New York. The rooms were clean, although the bathrooms were becoming delapidated, with some paper peeling and rough edges around the tiling. There are also some very quirky signs posted around the hotel which look like they were done by an art student on a old Applemac. Quick tip - change these and it could make a difference to the appearance of refinement. Overall though, for a 3-star hotel, we felt it was fine and the fact the rooms were clean and confortable and the staff courteous meant it met our needs for the price and was good value for a Midtown hotel. If you're looking for an up to date hotel, don't choose this one. Otherwise, it's fine.

“Fatal Errors” For all of the good things one can say about this relatively new hotel (eg, incredibly comfortable beds, smart design for such small rooms, friendly staff), there are a couple of major problems that make it impossible to stay here again. First is the air-conditioning. As previous reviewers have noted, when the cool (or hot) air kicked in, the sound was so loud that I was awakened every 5-10 minutes during the night. There is NO option to keep the fan on when the cool or warm air is also desired (which would at least keep the noise at a constant level). How could a new hotel adopt such an antiquated system? And why does using the TV remote turn the a/c off?? Second is the in-room internet. Yes, it is free, but in this case you get what you pay for. The wired option is so slow that doing any work was all but impossible (staff advised that too many people are on the system and suggested that I go down to the business center to work). The connection was non-existent for the wireless option. I stayed for 4 nights and not once was the connection "normal" (much less high-speed, as advertised). I leave this hotel both tired and frustrated.

“Great Hotel, Expensive rooms and parking” This Hotel is very nice and centrally located, it has 15 floors. The rooms are in excellent condition and very well maintained. Close to freeways and walking distance to the airport. Nice restaurant with real good expensive food and nice centrally located Bar. The staff is wonderfull and will do anything to help you out. This hotel is great if money is no object, if you are on a budget there are a few draw backs. 1) Hotel Rooms are very expensive per night during the week day 2) Hotel self Parking is $15 and is a block away 3) Valet parking is $30 per night.

“They really do have bed bugs....” My cousin and I stayed at the Westin LAX from July 28th-30th, 2006. I must say that the hotel's exterior and lobby were beautiful. We booked an Executive room with 2 double beds and paid $104/night. We were given a room on the 10th floor (room 1019). I read one review about the bed bugs, but since there was only 1 review about it, I figured maybe it was just that person. My boyfriend came over one night, and kept complaining that he felt like he was getting bit. Then the next morning me, him, and my cousin had these red bumps all over our arms and legs and we were itching like crazy. I have two more complaints and then I'm done. Parking was $15/day and I knew to expect that, but I didn't expect when my boyfriend came over to visit that he would have to pay that also. Finally, I was charged $15 for a movie that I didn't watch, didn't order, and wasn't in my room to see. If you decide to stay here, make sure that you check the mattress, sheets, and pillows for these little red bugs. And check your receipt to make sure that didn't charge you for something you didn't order.

“Average for the high end. Contemporary Style.” I ended up at this property simply because all the hotels in the area were full. The rate wasn't bad considering the location and quality of the property, but that was only because there was no convention in the attached convention center. I have tried to get into this property when there was a convention and couldn't. So this time, I needed a place, others were full, and I gave it a try. It is VERY Contemporary which isn't really my style. If you like that, you'll like this place. If your tastes go more toward traditional luxury, then this isn't the place. To me, it felt minimalist, spartan, and cold. The breakfast in the status lounge on 18 was excellent. The lobby bar had a well attended live jazz group and the crowd was relatively young to middle aged and attractive. My room had loads of hot water and fast WiFi, so all in all it was fine. For the price and status of this place, it was just average. The Marriott is next door and there are many very nice hotels in the area that claim to be of the same quality, charge similar prices, and are outstanding. Compared to that class of property, this place is only average.

“lasting love” We have stayed at this hotel almost annually for 10 years now and we still love it. The great manager retired last year so we were anxious to see how things were going. Well, all is well and still on track for another 6 star review. We recommend the club level with the free breakfast and happy hour. It is especially great with kids (who doesn't love coffee a few steps from your door that you can go grab in your robe?). Staff is so nice and so helpful. Big smiles! The pool is always lovely. The small water slide still continues to entice my kids. The Wii room keeps them out of the Texas sun for a few hours each visit which we all love. We always celebrate a birthday here and every year they send up something cute/sweet. It drizzled a little this year on the smores' fire so the kitchen made up large trays of them and we just went by the kids' club to pick them up. (Good thinking.) This year we fed the fish in the pond some leftover dinner rolls and they loved it. It might become a new tradition. We highly recommend this hotel.

“Quaint and Sophisticated” Everything about Chatwal is magnificent. From the moment you arrive, until it’s time to leave you will not be disappointed. Upon arrival, the doorman opened the door and whisked our bags up to the lobby. The Lobby is small but classic. Elizabeth at the check in desk was very pleasant as she greeted us with a smile at 6am after our red eye flight arrival from Phoenix. She asked our pillow preference (feather or foam) and introduced us to our butler. We were upgraded to a king room 204 with a beautiful terrace where we relaxed on several occasions with a bottle of wine. The room was phenomenal: high tech lighting, very nice closet and storage space, safe, fully stocked bar with full size bottles of Patron tequila, Jack Daniel’s, Grey Goose vodka, etc. The room is equipped with everything you need; except an iron, BUT you don’t need one, because the butler will press your garments. Both the bed and the sitting chair were extremely comfortable. And the bathroom OMG, luxurious is an understatement: fresh cut flowers, rain shower, bathrobes, Asprey products, and a beday, need I say more....... Our rate included free internet and continental breakfast which was tasty and adequate to start the day. Nightly turn down service included bedside slippers and Fuji Water, The hot tub and pool were a welcoming treat after walking to the Empire State building and spending time in Central Park. The hotel is steps from Time Square and the Theatre district. We also enjoyed drinks in the Lambs lounge. Can’t wait to return to Chatwal!

“Still a great property” We stayed at the Hotel Deca April 3 for two nights. We had stayed at the same property several years ago when I believe it was known as University Tower. The years have been kind to the hotel as the new owner has done a very nice job of remodeling. Although it is an old hotel it still has a nice feel to it and because it is an old hotel, there are concrete walls between units making noise from other units practically non-existent. Plus free parking! The staff- front desk, maids, maintenance, drivers were all consistently courteous, friendly and professional in their duties. We had a problem with our TV, within 1 hour the maintenance guys came in to try and trouble shoot- and then replace the set. The front desk gave great recommendations and directions. If you are visiting the University area this location cannot be beat. easy walking distance to UW. Great restaurants in the Wallingford area, 10 minute drive from the hotel.
“立地、雰囲気は最高。ちょっといかめしい。” 夜、ホテル前のイルミネーションは美しい。クリスマスの時期は特別。 内装、雰囲気もすばらしいが、スタッフはちょっといかめしい感じがしました。

“Convenient location and comfortable stay” Located in the heart of Philadelphia this Starwood property is near Rittenhouse Square close to many of the city’s attractions and business district. Although I was only there briefly, the Westin Philadelphia lived up to its brand reputation for providing professionals a comfortable place to stay. I spent very little time at this property since work brought me to Philadelphia, so I cannot even tell you if one side provides a better view than another, but I can speak to the convenience of the location which is why I will stay here again on my next visit to Philadelphia.

“Some good...Some bad” The Good - Location - Very convenient to Fisherman's Wharf, all the ferries, and cable car lines Evening Wine reception - nice to relax a enjoy a few glasses of wine and appetizers Restaurant - has good food at fairly reasonable prices for the city Suites - plenty of room for families, clean, comfy, nice furnishings Concierge - very friendly and helpful Bartender - very nice The Bad - No microwave in room Windows - the glass was so thin it was like all the windows were open. The amount of street noise was just as loud as if you were on the street. The Strange - toilet paper holder was behind the toilet and EXTREMELY hard to reach In room menu - the lunch and dinner menu in your room was not for the hotel restaurant, but somewhere else, had to go down and get a menu for the hotel The Awful - The valets were by far the WORST we have EVER experienced!!!!!!!!!!!! Unfortunately, our experience with the valets really soured our stay at this hotel. For starters, there aren't enough of them to keep up with the amount of cars. When you arrive you're lucky if you can even get pulled off the street as the loading area is usually full. Then you have to wait for someone to show up, usually 5-10 min. When you finally see a valet they are very unfriendly, and always act like they're confused and flustered. They aren't the least bit helpful. They are EXTREMELY slow to bring up your car. We could usually see our car from the loading area, but couldn't get anyone to get it for us. We always waited at least 15- 20 min. to get our car. Once they even brought us the wrong car. They are more concerned about bringing up cars for people who are not there, and are still not there 20 min. later, than they are about helping the people who are standing there waiting. By the time they bring up all the cars for the people who are still not there they have the driveway blocked and we still can't get out. All of this, and we could see our car, feet from the exit, the entire time. We barely made a couple of tours on time because we were waiting for our car. Upon completing a Best Western survey management assured us that something would be done about the valets. I sincerely hope so.

“Pricey, but you get what you pay for” I spent one night here on a business trip that had me visiting a number of cities in Texas. This is a unique Marriott property in that it is a joint Courtyard/Residence Inn that shares a building and facilities while maintaining a separate check-in for the respective brand. Now I would recommend venturing out in Austin, especially being so close to Sixth Street; however, this hotel has it all if you want to stay in. From the large and well-stocked Champions Sports Bar to the Starbucks both on the lobby level, the hotel can meet all dining needs. At check-in, my Gold Status was acknowledged and i was given a room on a high floor. I would have liked a nicer view, but thats not a big deal. I found the staff to be very friendly and accommodating. Only a few negatives, and largely related to price. The room rates are generally high here - I consider upwards of $200 for a Courtyard to be quite high and pay parking on top of that took the total cost for one night upwards of $225. But as I said, you get what you pay for and here it is location, service and clean accommodations.

“Awesome Hotel - Great Value!!” My boyfriend & I decided to stay here one night when we went to a Dodger game. Found a great deal through their website and was able to utilize their AAA rate. We checked in without any problems, they gave us a room on the 15th floor and it was great. Valet was superb every time and we felt like we were treated like movie stars with the attention that was given to us. I left my phone charger in my room and the hotel sent it back to me without any problems! A great stay in downtown LA and will would recommend to anyone!!

“Stay out of this area!” My friend setup a long stay here- I visited once but would not go back. Location is not good and as an older woman, I did not feel safe when leaving at night. The staff is polite and the room is basically fine, but I'm not sure it is the best choice in a lovely city full of such vast economical hotels and inns. I would map out the area before booking.

“Not as bad as others describe it...” The lobby of this hotel is very nice. It made me think that the hotel might be really nice overall. But once we out of the elevator and to our room, my attitude changed. The hallways were very, very old looking. Lots of stuff in the hotel needs some work. The room we had wasn't that small, but it certainly wasn't great. The bathroom was horrible. Could not get a good temperature of water in the shower for anything. Everything was just really old looking. But, I have seen worse. Now as far as the outside of the building goes, my friend and I were shocked at how safe the streets were because we had read the reviews on this site prior to going. We were in LA for the Pac 10 tourney and we did get a rental car so that we could drive around and do some site seeing in our free time. We ended up walking to Staples Center and back to the hotel on the third and last day of games because we saw nothing threatening about it. And in the walk to the arena and back we were not put in any kind of danger. The streets outside and around the mayfair hotel are unlike any other city streets I've ever been to. Nothing to worry about as long as you be careful.

“Top location for top price” the location 2 min from times square is worth the experience. After long meetings it is astonishing to dive into this place with all the flashing lights, the theatres around.The hotel rooms are well equipped and one has even free WLAN, which is rarely the case in these highprice hotels. the best experience was the quality of the bed. I had very seldom such a good bed and slept accordingly well. The staff was very friendly and the food during the meeting was really good. Whether all this deserves the price I had to pay, has everybody to assess by oneself.

“Excellent choice...great value!” OK..it's not a 5 star hotel...it is more of a budget Hilton...but the staff was extremely pleasant, polite, helpful and accomodating! The location is excellent. Few blocks from FW, trolley, Ghiradelli square, etc. Also, after taking cable car up the hill, you can walk down the crooked street (Lombard & Hyde) and walk back to Hotel! We enjoyed this location as first timers to SFO. Car rental around the corner...drove to Muir woods, Wine country, Sausalito... I would recommend this place, but next time we would stay in another location...but no complaints about the Hilton! We are Hilton Gold members and received complimentary buffet breakfast, and appetizer at the bar. We also requested top floor away from elevators in quiet location...which we received...as well as early check-in! So just make yr requests early! Join Hilton club!

“Great Stay and Location” I recently returned from a short trip to Manhattan and wanted to comment on the Hampton Inn in Manhattan. The hotel and staff were wonderful!. The rooms were nice a big and met my every expectation. Its close to ground zero and one can easily walk to the new site which is open to the public. Its one of the best Hampton Inns I have ever stayed in. Plenty of cabs and shuttles available outside to take you were you need to go.

“Brilliantly situated and big comfortable rooms” Our 3rd stay at the Salisbury and we were not disappointed. The staff were efficient, polite and helpful. I have seen other reviews where guests have had issues with the staff, but we found them fine (and did so in our other visits too). The air con units seem really noisy - but that could be standard, as we come from the UK we are hardly experts on these contraptions! The building work just up the street starts at 7am but is done by 6pm - ask for a room at the back if this would cause you probs. The Salisbury is well situated for subways and buses, delis, diners etc. and feels safe and comfortable. We would recommend it and will use it again next time we are in NYC. Tourist tips: Queens Museum - for the massive 'Panorama' of NYC and the Unisphere The High Line - walk the boardwalk on along the old 'Meatpacking District' train track for city views and a garden above the city streets. Easy access (inc. disabled access) (free). Governors Island - ferry over from Battery Park area (free and frequent). Island can be navigated on foot or you can rent bikes. Food outlets not in abundance, so take picnic.

“Charming Hotel” This is a charming hotel located in a very convenient location that is very close to independence park and to a large variety of restaurants. The building itself is on the historical register and the charm is evident from the moment you walk-in to the hotel. I have never seen ceilings this high in a hotel room ! On the flip-side they do keep the lighting very dim; hence, do not plan on reading after 7PM. Aside from this the room had good modern amenities (internet, AC, bathroom, etc). The continental breakfast was excellent and well organized. They also have evening cookies for the guests. However, plan on spending about $18 for parking at the garage which is located a block away. This is pretty normal given the location. I would strongly recommend the hotel, and would stay here again given the opportunity.

“Glad I stayed here once but probably won't return” My daughter and I spent the weekend at the Waldorf Astoria (NYC) for her 18th bday. A lovely, historic hotel an easy walk (or very short cab ride) away from Times Square, Public Library, Grand Central Station, FAO, Central Park, St. Patrick's Cathedral, Serendipity 3, Dylan's Candy Bar, Rockefeller Center, broadway theatres. A cab is needed to access the Status of Liberty and Ellis Island. A bit of a line at check-in and a delay in room availability but hotel text messaged me when room was available. Our bags were stored while we wait. Room was at a discount rate I found on-line. Comfortable, small (but with two beds), zero view, a bit dated with an old sort of odor/maybe mildew? Felt safe and appreciated the after 10pm need for your room card to access guest floors via elevator. Piano Cole Porter used to compose on is on display in lobby atrim, as well as historic clock and historical overview display cases with memorabiliia in main lobby. Hotel definitely seems to appeal to many international guest. Hotel shop has an adequate selection of items that aren't as pricey as I would have expected. Dining and room service prices, however, are absolutely ridiculous. $30 for a Caeser salad? I'm talking absolutely ridiculous pricing. Glitch at check out with bottled water from the in-room refrig erroneously charged to my account. I believe the price was around $7 a bottle. Hotel removed charges but with a slight bit of hesitation. No safe in the room but there is a blow dryer, ironing board and iron. There is not any late night 'grab a snack' dining in the immediate vicinity of the hotel which was a negative for us returning from shows after 11pm. Staff is aloof but friendly. There is a business center.

“Wonderful staff, Very Nice Room and Great Location” I continue to be a Marriott fan and this hotel signifies the reason. Marriott has the greatest beds, the staff were exceptionally helpful and my room was spacious and spotless. This hotel is in a great location, right on the edge of Dupont, Foggy Bottom and close to Georgetown. My only request to Marriott, please get wireless in the rooms! Charging 12.95 for wired internet is such a negative characteristic!

“Overall a nice hotel” I stayed in this hotel this past weekend, and overall I was happy. The staff at the front desk were some of the friendliest and most helpful I have met on this long trip. For example, I got some horrible Chinese food down the street and they didn't give me any soy sauce. I went to the front desk to see if one of them happened to have any and the staff member actually ran across the street to a restaurant and brought me some back. They were also very helpful with directions and how to use public transit. The restaurant staff was not very friendly at all, but I didn't spend much time there. The room was HUGE. There are two large flatscreen tvs in the room. It was very comfortable, and I like having a fridge and microwave in the room. It seemed very clean. I did not hear anything from other rooms, and there was a party going on 2 doors down. The area around the hotel is very creepy. I am a female travelling alone, and I did walk around alone at night-very stupid, but it's cheap! I did not have any problems, but I was not comfortable. The entrance to the main lobby is in a dark scary tunnel, and there were a lot of loud homeless people outside. If you want to eat food that isn't chinese after 6pm, be prepared to walk a few blocks. The wawa across the street actually has cheap decent sandwiches if you don't feel like making the trek out of chinatown.

“This place makes me happy.” Why can't all hotels that cost $75 or more a night be like this? Free bottled water. Cheap parking. Nice staff. Nice products. Huge, clean room. Nice cozy bed. They even threw in a $10 comp in food! So basically, parking, or the food, was "free". The places I am used to, you have to pay $29+ for parking EACH NIGHT and all you get is a bad parking space. This place charged me $10 and gave me breakfast! Love the look and feel of this hotel. If this room was in California, it would be over $200/night. Huge window that opens to the city. A real shower with a real shower head! Ironing board. Fridge. Coffee. Free WiFi! Huge flat screen TV that pretty much stares at you from the center of the room with a "watch me" look on its face. I did watch it and I normally do not watch TV in hotels. Very quiet other than the outside, city noise. Noise downtown? I like it. Hustle and bustle. A nice area to walk around, across the street. Some sort of buffalo exhibit or something. I decided against crossing the street to check it out, but it LOOKED cool from a distance. Didn't see much else other than a McDonald's nearby. Loved the layout of the room. When I walked in, I thought they had upgraded me to a suite. I was on the 7th floor. Did not use the gym, but I checked it out. It had decent cardio machines. Lighting was fantastic throughout the property. Really young, hip, friendly staff. VERY convenient, no hassle parking. Only had a few problems: I asked for an 8:30am wake-up call, and I received a call at 8:05am. That was odd. I also bought a sandwich from the lobby. An amazing sounding Buffalo Mozzarella and Tomato. Brought it up to the room and it was TOTALLY soggy. The bread was soaked. Couldn't eat it. Nasty. Was in a hurry, so I did not complain about it. Another strange thing. They have these really cool computers where you can print up your boarding pass for your flight. Southwest Airlines is basically a TEXAS, LOVE FIELD Airline. The hotel has all SORTS of airlines available on those computers, even ones I never heard of, but NOT Southwest Airlines. The woman behind the counter had to print mine for me and she could only print ONE leg of my flight. Strange. The other "nice" properties that I found online for Downtown Dallas were all close or above $200/night. They could NOT be better than Aloft. Save yourself $100 and stay at this hotel. Anyways, I had a LOT to work to do so I was "locked up" in the room most of the time. And I liked it. I felt like I was in my own little studio. Brought me back to my college days, minus the drunk girls and dirty dishes. Carpet looks brand spanking new. Bathroom: HUGE.

“Stellar service, beautiful room, friendly staff!” Let me start by saying I'm forgiving the Algonquin a few of things that would have normally made me rank fewer than five stars: 1. the bathroom exhaust vent was dirty - very very dirty. 2. housekeeping left a dirty take-out coffee cup lid and empty sugar packet on the table. 3. our room only had one washcloth when we arrived so I asked for another; the next day, housekeeping only left one washcloth again. Weird. That said, the service and attention we received, the exceptional way the staff made my mother feel welcomed and the way they accommodated her needs, and the superb friendliness of every single person we met MORE than made up for those shortcomings. We were upgraded to a king room, which was spacious for NYC. The bathroom is tiny, yes, but it is beautifully decorated and the shower is excellent. Our room had a bay window overlooking 44th Street - which is great. The City noise is pretty noticeable, but the hotel does provide earplugs. There are blackout shades in addition to decorative light-filtering fabric shades - which are necessary because of the office building across the street. You can see right into their windows, and the opposite is true, so be sure to use those blackout shades! The Round Table Restaurant was outstanding, and we thoroughly enjoyed our meals and the super-attentive service we received. Matilda is beautiful, and is obviously well-loved by all who work there. It was easy to store our bags prior to check-in and after check-out so we could wander the City. Definitely consider staying here. The hotel has recently been completely renovated while maintaining its historic charm. There are two elevators to service the entire 12-floor hotel, so sometimes there is a bit of a wait... Stairs are next to the elevators if you get too impatient. :)

“Quality Experience” Stayed at the Solamar for a conference for work, and overall, they did a great job. Staff were very kind and did their best to be service oriented, but perhaps were a little green, nothing that experience and dedication can not change. Arrived from the east coast early (around 1030am) and a room was not ready, no problem, we were very early! Spent most of my day in our conference room and work room getting ready for our meeting, but staff made it easy to get what we needed. Room was a standard king on the 5th floor- I would recommend a room on the street side, as the bar on the pool deck can get loud at night with party people. Room was nice, maybe a bit dark, as the lights didn't really give a lot of light- the one window did not brighten the room very much at all either. Mini bar is well stocked (join InTouch- their loyalty program for a mini-bar credit -make sure you ask for it as my check-in staff forgot to give me the voucher or mention it- and you get free internet). The Gilchrist and Soames toilitries are great, they are mounted on the wall, which is a great green push, but i wanted to take the body wash home! Where can I buy it? ;-) The worst part of the room was the sink in the bath room. TOTALLY USELESS. Very good looking, but when you washed your hands or tried to shave the water was everywhere and made the bathroom SOAKED. Bed was very nice as well. Convention space is very nice, had a great reception the first night and the appetizers and drinks were great with informative, kind staff. Had a killer ending night party on the pool deck, if you want to host an amazing event use this space! We had a buffet with surf and turf, sushi, and hundreds of other great options! The view is killer and the beautiful SD weather will wow everyone! I would recommend this hotel wholeheartedly!

“This is a great hotel with a great location for sight seeing” We got this place for a steal on priceline ($70 a night). It was very centrally located in the loop and was very close to shops, restaurants and river. It was a VERY large hotel that obviously accommodates to Chicago tourists. We were there during a Cubs home game and the lobby was FILLED with Cubs fans. The facilities were very clean, staff was super nice and the rooms clean (our bed was temperpedic). The down sides were anything extra you need at the hotel (wifi, food, or business center) is very expensive. You would be better suited to stop at the Walgreens or 7-11 a block away to get food and\or drinks. Internet was $7 for 15mins. They did, however, have free plane check in computers. All in all, this was one of our favorite places we have stayed (we travel to Chicago every year to visit family).

“Nice New Holiday Inn Express” I stayed at this hotel for one night after a business meeting ran late and I decided to stay over in San Antonio. Upon driving up to the hotel you could tell it was very new. The inside of the hotel was just as new looking. Lobby was nice and bright. They had a typical small but clean exercise room as well as the typical lobby / breakfast area. My room was a nice King room with microwave and fridge. Very comfortable bed, curtains block out ambient light very well. When I went down to ask for some shaving cream the provided me with two trial size cans cans. Lobby had cookies in the evening. The breakfast was typical Holiday Inn Express fare with cold hard boilde eggs, pastries, toaster french toast, muffins, cereals, juice, milk. As with many other Holiday Inn Expresses, I would like to see a hot option of some kind of egg or meat. They have a small business center downstairs with printer and PC. High Speed Internet connection was nice. Pool was typical for a Holiday Inn Express. I will definately stay here again when the need arises in the area.

“Just Right for New York City!” We stayed one night at this well-rounded hotel and it was surely worth it! Our room had a wonderful view over the New York city streets and made you know that you are in the heart of New York City. The location was amazing with steps away from all of the attractions in Times Square, and the subway is on the same block! All the amentities were prime!

“Honey they shrunk the hotel” The Doubletree is a nice enough hotel - just everything in it is smaller compared to most of the other NYC hotels I have stayed at. Small rooms, hallways and elevators (a total of 3 of which service 46 floors). I go to NYC on weekends about six times a year on average, and often stay downtown at the Millenium Hilton which is supersized compared to the Doubtletree downtown and usually in the same price range. Despite a good location I can't say I will go out of my way to stay there again. In addition to the small room the sink had some major cracks and the door between our room and the next did not fully close or lock, other than the inside latch. I would stay there again if the price was right but there are better options in the Hilton Family.

“Great Hotel in the Middle of the City” *Diamond Member* Stayed here in June for a conference. The hotel was sold out and very busy, but the staff was great. There is a Starbucks in the lobby, but I warn you that the line gets ridiculously long, so you should opt for the location across the street. As a Diamond, you do get a coffee, a piece of fruit and a pastry, which is a pretty good deal. The neighborhood is either cute or sketchy depending on which way you turn out of the hotel. The internet was free, but my wireless card is faster, so I used that. The turndown service was very nice and the room was decent sized, if a little small. I didn't get much of a view. Before you order room service and pay over $20 for a sandwich, google Mango's on your smartphone. It's about 2 blocks away and has great food for a much better price.

“Clean, comfortable hotel” My daughter and I traveled to NYC over spring break and stayed in the Hotel Reserve. I was able to get a rate of $99 per night on bookit.com during one of their 48 hour sales. Room was small, but typical of NY hotel rooms. Bed was extremely comfortable and room and bathroom were clean and modern. Noise level wasn't bad, but you could hear some street traffic noise. We normally stay in Greenwich or midtown which I really prefer because of the location to shopping and the theater. The location is in the financial district, so when coming back from the theater at night, it is pretty desolate down there. We normally take the subway too and from the airport, but the train we needed to take was shut down for repairs. One of the hotel employees called a car for us to take us to the airport on a Saturday afternoon. The employee told us and guaranteed us that the fare would be a flat $65 (tolls included). My only complaint was that when we got to the airport, the driver told us that it was going to cost $75. I don't know if the hotel employee and the driver had a deal together, but I hate getting scammed and this felt like a scam to me. I called the hotel and spoke with a manager to explain to him what had happened. He told me he would call me back and let me know the results of his investigation, but I never heard back. I just feel that if a hotel is guaranteeing the rate of a car/taxi, then that is what one should pay. The next time I do this however, I will definitely make sure that the price is negotiated in front of the hotel employee and the driver.

“Stay away” I totally agree with the negative comments about this hotel and the chain in total. W is just a BAD chain. They can talk the talk but haven't a clue about how to walk the walk. Wahtever Whenever means Whatever W wants and Whenever W wants to do it This property is the worst in the chain Too bad .. so much potential so little delivery If you want a decent hotel experience pick just about any brand except W. If you want horror stories and just pure entertainment about bad W experiences email me. don.brown@brownchild.com

“Very nice, hip hotel” Stayed in room 916, a suite, which was great. Had a decent view over the city rooftops. The room itself was huge with a nice sitting area and a very comfy bed. There was a very large closet in a separate dressing area and a nice large bathroom. I was solo but if one was with family this room would have been more than big enough for 1 if not 2 pull out beds. Room service breakfast was great, service at the hotel overall was prompt and on top of things. Hard to beat the location as well, and the bar downstairs is very cool and has a nice scene going on most nights.

“Great Hotel, Bad Elevators” Hate to do a three-star review, but lack of attention to elevator maintenance on a busy weekend is a recipe for disaster. In fairness, we enjoyed three wonderful days here. The staff was friendly and helpful, the room was spacious and comfortable, the bar had the right energy level, food was decent. But all weekend long, the elevators were a major hassle. On checkout day, we literally waited 30 minutes with only one (packed) down elevator. We ended up schlepping two 70-pound bags down seven flights of stairs. Not cool. Check first. If the elevators are working, this is a great economical hotel with a pretty decent location. TIP: Do note that this is on an I-5 exit ramp. Look for west facing rooms (which we had).

“Varying room qualtiy” I traveled with 2 colleagues so had a chance to see 3 rooms, booked at the same time, at the same rate. One was good, one was teeney, and one was fabulous. With this much room variation, I cannot give this hotel an unqualified endorsement. This historic hotel has an elegant lobby with live music until 8 PM. Downside to the rooms are usual in old hotels -- very small wondows resulting in very little general lighting; varying water temps in the shower; and rather poor temperature control. They charge for internet!

“An Unexpected Gem in Times Square” Walking around in the hustle and bustle of Times Square can be daunting, but as soon as you arrive in the third floor lobby of the Doubletree, it is serenely calm. It is the rooms, however, that really make this an exceptional value in New York. The suites are spacious and have been recently renovated. Mine had two double beds and a flat screen TV in the bedroom. There was a sizable, separate sitting room with sofa, table, chairs and TV. This room also had a wet bar, microwave oven and refrigerator. The sizable bathroom had two sinks and opened into either room. Comfy beds and bedding, too. Another plus -- if you arrive by train or bus to Penn Station, Grand Central Station, or the Port Authority terminal, the Doubletree is a manageable walk if you aren't carrying too much luggage. I would gladly stay here again.

“Solid choice, great location” We just stayed here for a conference I did at the Moscone Center. It was priced similarly to the Hilton (about $220) but this hotel was rated higher on this site. We weren't disappointed.
