The hotel is perfectly located for a lot of things -- easy walk to Moscone, close to shopping on Market St, BART station, streetcar, and the financial district, and also close to our favourite restaurants in the opposite direction. Check in and check out were fast and painless, with no unexpected charges. We were initially offered a room with double beds, and the desk clerk said there were no king beds, but we did get a queen which was fine. The room was on the 20th floor which would not have been our initial choice but it was very nice. The view was fine, and we had a bay window with a little loveseat. You do have to pay 12 or $13 per day for internet acess but the $45 per week is a much better deal if you're staying more than 3 days. The internet connection was tempermental, sometimes fine and sometimes slow. We initially signed in as "wireless", and when that was slow or not working, we had to call IT. They told us to sign in again with a wired connection, pay twice, and he'd get the front desk to reverse the charges. True to word, there was only one charge on the final bill. By the way, the hotel does not charge for 1-800 calls. We seemed to have got one of the "renovated view rooms". The furniture was new enough although the decor was a bit beige. The bathroom was small but nicely finished with tiled walls around the bath enclosure and granite counter. The bath isn't huge but my husband, who is 6'2'', found it fine. The water for the shower is high-pressure and instantly hot at any time of the day. The room size was decent (bigger than the last place we stayed in SF). Our room had a flat screen TV. Strangely, there was no minibar which we usually use for milk or soy milk for coffee, so we had to use the ice bucket to keep it cool. Initially we didn't like the location near the elevators and ice machine, but the soundproofing is so good we didn't notice noise at all. The gym was clean and very well-equipped with good-quality treadmills, ellipticals, free weights and a variety of weight machines. The hotel has a lounge with live music several nights, and there are a couple of other restaurants in the building. Room service menu was pretty standard with average prices. Our only tiny complaints were the lack of minibar/fridge in the room, and the strange little coffee maker which used up a new plastic tray every time (and the paper cups rather than real coffee cups). These certainly didn't wreck our experience. One huge benefit -- the whole hotel is non-smoking, so you won't accidentally get a stinky room. This is not a "luxury" hotel but offers value for money. We'd definitely return, whether for a conference or just for a fun trip.

“Nice hotel with not so great service.” Pros: The room is very large (if you're someone who prefers a large room). It is also clean and comfortable. It is within walking distance of City Hall and the Philadelphia Museum of Art (both things you want to see if you're a tourist!). It is also just two blocks from a subway station. The wireless internet is free and we had a decent connection. Cons: Based on our experience, the housekeeping was poor and the service at the front desk was somewhat awkward. We didn't receive new towels after housekeeping came by our room nor did we receive any toilet paper. We were left with just the one towel that I left on the rack (indicating I would use it again). I know this is a bit nitpicky, but I feel that this is basically the main job of housekeeping. At the very least, there should be enough towels for two people in a room and the guest shouldn't have to ask for two towels. Instead of calling down to the front desk, my boyfriend walked down the hall and found someone who was making up another room to get another towel. She was clearly annoyed that he bothered her. Perhaps we should have called the front desk to ask, but it seemed more convenient for them for us to go straight to the source and get our towels from someone in housekeeping. In regards to the front desk staff: I called down to the front desk three times--our hot water wasn't working when we first got into our hotel, I needed the wireless internet password, and I had a question regarding the toiletries available in the lobby. All three times, the people at the front desk weren't exactly rude, but had poor phone skills and didn't seem like people that should be working the front desk at a hotel. The man I spoke with regarding the password mumbled it so fast that I had to ask him to repeat it three times before I thought I understood it. When I tried it, it was wrong, and I had to call back down to verify it. The other women I spoke with also left me feeling as if they needed to get me off the phone asap. It was actually more bizarre than annoying! I don't consider myself a picky traveler (you can look at my other reviews to see I'm easy to please!). However, my overall experience left me unsatisfied. I'm not saying I wouldn't recommend it, I'm just saying that if you choose to stay here, keep your expectations low. And again, this was my experience. And who knows, maybe the staff members I dealt with were having a bad day!

“Clean, newly-renovated, great location, cool layout.” This place is newly-renovated recently, and overall we had a great stay. The location is terrific, as it is right off I-5 with immediate access to/from the freeway either north/southbound. The main part of Old Town is within a short walk. The hotel offers not only free airport shuttle, but also shuttle to/from Seaworld and SD Zoo. Free shuttle to Seaworld and Zoo has to be pretty rare for any of the area hotels, and it made things real convenient although the caveat is I believe they only offer one set dropoff/pickup times per day. Our room came with a wet bar (sink) and microwave/fridge. Not sure if every room comes with a wet bar, but I think there's microwave/fridge in every room. Of course, the Internet is free. The lobby area has two computers for guest use, as well as a color printer. I will say that the lobby computers were extremely slow. The free breakfast buffet was very good. As with all Fairfield Inn's, it had Jimmy Dean microwaveable sausage muffins. Also had cereals (good selection), fruits (limited selection), muffins/bread, yogurt and packaged cups of grapefruits and pineapples. Although there was no prepared hot food items on offer, I found the breakfast buffet to be still good. Coffee was terrible, though. The dining area in the lobby is modern-looking and nicely done. Very interesting layout. This place is made up of 4 different buildings, each with rooms that are accessed via interior corridor like most highrise hotels. But the buildings are connected via outdoor corridors like at motels, and some of the rooms are actually accessed from the outdoor part of the corridor. So there are some rooms here that have motel-like exterior access setup. The four buildings form an arc that surrounds a courtyard area which has nice tables, sofas to lounge in, as well as pool/spa. Our room was a 1-king facing the courtyard, and it was spacious. Looked like fairly new carpeting. The bed was a little soft, but the bedding was very comfortable. Nice towels, too. Overall the room felt very clean, although I still don't think that the housekeeping did such a great job of cleaning because I saw dust at the edges of the carpet along the wall. When this place is no longer new, the housekeeping will need to do a better job of upkeeping this place to keep it looking clean. One thing that's not free here (although typically free at other Fairfield Inns) is parking. It's $15/night to park underground in their gated garage. There's possible street parking nearby, but street parking near the hotel was completely occupied most nights that I was there. So I suggest you just suck it up and pay in their garage. One important thing to remember, though, is that this place has a very low garage clearance (6 feet).

“a quirky boutique hotel, but pretty nice” i stayed here for a conference being help in the hotel. Overall a nice hotel with some interesting features. The bathooms seem like an after thought, they tend to be small and laid out oddly. My room had had a sink in teh room, a toilet ina glass stall and then a shower after that. The floor was slate and heated which was nice. Room is decorated in reds and browns and very nic, but who ever put white shutters on the windows shouldl be shot. Svereral nice and trendy resturants and bars with both inside adn outside seating and Starbucks across the street.

“Very Good Hotel” Very good hotel. Staff very friendly. Rooms exceptionally clean. Beds great. Bathrooms "spic and span".A few blocks off Broadway. Close to many of the shows. Would stay again next time in NY.Check in and check out quick, friendly and 100% accurate. Stay on top floors and very good breakfast and cocktail hour included in room rate.

“Someone threw up in our room before we arrived.” Someone threw up in our room before we arrived. First of all, I'd like to note that the hallways looked a bit tired & our door looked like it had been kicked in upon arrival, but we got a good deal & were not at all bothered by either fact, to be honest. However, when we walked in the room, immediately, we could tell that someone recently threw up. It clearly had been cleaned but there were red stains all over the carpet & it smelled HORRIBLE/UNBEARABLE. We called downstairs and a) the clerk did not seem at all surprised b) he said there was no way he could possibly move us c) that he would send someone from housecleaning up. Needless to say, no one came, we left the windows wide open for two days, went through a whole bottle of air freshener that we were forced to seek out & still spent most of our long weekend with scarves over our faces. I understand things happen but I can't in good conscience give a good review of our experience or the service at The Radisson. No follow-up from the hotel after our complaint the first day & no extra cleaning. We were completely ignored. Location, however, as noted in other reviews is great.

“The quintessential cheap hotel.” For less than 80 dollars (including tax) you get... a hotel room about a block from the Magnificent Mile for under 80 dollars. You don't get a coffee maker, hair dryer, iron or alarm clock - not even shampoo. (Since my last visit, they've also stopped leaving pens.) Also, I doubt anyone has ever stolen the rather small, rather rough towels. The furnishings of my room seem shabbier than I'd recalled, and this place may have the slowest elevators of any hotel in Chicago. So much for negatives. One doesn't go to Chicago to stay in a hotel room, and I've always had a decent night's sleep here. The cable TV service is actually pretty good and includes at least one station where you can always get a local weather forecast quickly. There's a cheap coffee shop on the main floor where you can get (only) breakfast without paying for a dinner, and a coin laundromat. The desk help does what little it can in terms of info and advice. The original Pizzeria Uno and Due (the first "branch") are within a block, buses and the Red Line El within two. Note: the immediate area can seem deserted and spooky at night. If you demand creature comforts, look elsewhere. If you want a cheap room where you can sleep and keep your stuff, this could be your place.

“Average hotel, good for El Paso” 6 story "cookie cutter" hyatt place. Rooms are exactly what you expect at "HP" which is good vs marriott or spg offerings in the mid-range catagory. location is right off i-10 east of downtown near airport. staff was very nice at check in, the morning staff could use some additional training. Same goes for food, evening dinning was good. Free breakfast ( even though they are advertising the new "skillet" was poor quality). The open face sandwich tasted like they cooked the night before. I say average based on traveling every week west of the MS River, but for El Paso ( grade on a curve) you could go 3.5 stars.

“Can't Beat its location within S.F.” We stayed two night at Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Like other reviewers of this hotel, we find its location very convenient. The California line cable car is just around the corner. We used it to get to the Ferry Building, Chinatown and a couple of restaurants. I took the advice of other reviewers and asked for a room away from the ice machine and the elevator. The room was comfortable, clean and quiet. Parking was expensive but that's true at every hotel in SF. My only complaint is that the front desk was always short-staffed. It took waiting in line 20 minutes to check in on a Friday afternoon at 4pm because there were only 2 people working. When we checked out on Sunday morning, there was only one person working at the front desk so the wait was also long. They also have to answer the phone so that added to the wait time. It's probably due to this economic environment; everyone is cutting back on staff. All in all, it was a nice hotel to stay at and a good value.

“A very good choice” Washington Square Hotel is very well situated in Greenwich Village. There is alot of "ambiance" without the "crowdyness" of Time Square. Around the hotel, there is the beautiful park and many little shops and restaurants. At the hotel, peoples at the front desk are very nice and helpful. You feel in security because there is always a doorman. The rooms are small but that is what we expected. Small is ok because we dont stay in the room when we visit New York. The room are very clean and the bed are comfortable and I think that is the most important. If there is a place they could upgrade, it is for the continental breakfast... it is poor. We got a fruit salad, some bagels and muffin with jam. You can have cheese for your bagel but they don't offer it, we had to ask for it. Maybe we could had something else if we ask for it... Anyway, we really appreciate the place and we will go back for sure.

“great property superb location” The hotel is a landmark property. You get a bit more than you expect. The hotel has style and class. As with any older property there are issues such as the lift service being slow but the views of the park are fantastic. The location is very well placed being close to all the best parts of the city.

“nice hotel on the north side of houston” i attended a modest sizxe conference (200 - 300 people) held here june 22 to 24 2007 - the hotel rooms are ery nice and comfortable - the meeting rroms are excellent - the hotel has a restaurant (the breakfast buffet was excellent) - they also have a bistro bar i would recommend that we use this hotel for the same conference when we have it next year

“A perfect stay” Spent the night at the mag. mile Marriott to take my daughter to see Wicked. The hotel was absolutely perfect. Terrance at the reg desk was a darling. We had an amazing view of downtown and could walk to Volare for dinner and all the shopping we needed. The lobby of this hotel is delightful- plenty of places to sit and chat. The pool was clean and warm. Also a great view here. Most of all, the staff was wonderful. This makes a big difference. I travel a lot for work and have found myself loving the Marriotts. Thank you!

“Es klingt nur so elegant” Das Adante gehört zu diesen kleinen, alten, dunklen Billighotels in SFO. Es ist nur zu empfehlen, wenn der Preis stimmt und der Aufenthalt nicht allzu lang ist. Es reicht also zum Übernachten gerade so aus. Das Frühstück besteht aus Toast und dünnem Kaffee, wenn man Glück hat, gibt ́ auch einen Muffin - gemütlich ist anders. Die Lage ist zwar noch zentral, die Umgebung jedoch nicht sehr einladend.

“Kunst und Service” Das St. Regis Hotel San Francisco liegt im SOMA Bezirk, neben dem Museum der modernen Kunst. Das Hotel selbst beherbergt das Museum der afrikanischen Gemeinde mit einer umfangreichen Sammlung afrikanischer Kunst und Kultur. Alle 260 Zimmer sind mit dezenten Komfort, geschmackvollen Textilien und hochwertigen Möbeln ausgestattet. Das Badezimmer mit Marmorelementen gleicht einem Whirlpool. Technik ist ok und auf dem neuesten Stand. Das Restaurant serviert amerikanische Gerichte der Jahreszeit mit Schwerpunkt auf Meeresfrüchte. Zudem wird eine Sashimi-Bar geboten. Zu loben ist außerdem die Weinauswahl. Ein gut ausgestattetes Business-Center und die Tagungsräume sind ideal für Geschäfte. In der Freizeit kann man im Fitnessraum trainieren oder im Swimmingpool oder Whirlpool entspannen. Das Personal ist überwiegend sehr nett.Bei Preisen über 400 € pro Nacht ist das Hotel sicherlich kein Sonderangebot. Aber die Qualität stimmt und da gebe ich lieber etwas mehr aus.

“Not luxury but good first class” Location is the best in NY. Hotel is very nice first class hotel; Home-away-home -type accommodation. House keeping is keeping the rooms very clean. Bathrooms have old tiles (back to building time?) but new stone floor and counter tops. A lot of high-quality towels which were changed daily. No ventilation in bathroom. Some parts are little dated and need some fresh-up. Room service breakfast is VERY expencive with automatic 21% gratuity. I have styed in many real luxury hotels but never met 21% tips. Is this a record high?

“Missing basic business amenities” I stayed four nights at the City Center Sheraton during a conference: two nights in a suite and two nights in a king room. (The rooms were comped because I was with the convention-staging company.) There were only three differences between the two rooms: (1) the suite included a room with a sofa, second TV, and a round "meeting" table (2) the king room had a shower only, and (3) the suite came with Starbucks coffee for the coffee maker instead of Maxwell House. The beds were comfortable, but the windows offered next to no sound insulation. I heard sirens several times a night and, one night, jackhammering in the street below till after 10. Nothing to be done about that; just be aware. More disappointing was the lack of wifi in the rooms and the absence of an in-room safe. Accessing the Internet (which I had to do for work several hours each afternoon) required paying $10 for an Internet connection that logged me out at 3 (check-in time) each day. I even had to provide my own Ethernet cable. Other, cheaper chains (like Holiday Inn Express) have provided better accommodations for business travelers.

“A good option in Memphis” We chose to stay at this hotel last year because we were regulars at the Hampton Inn Poplar Avenue location, but they were booked up the weekend we were coming, so we tried this hotel. We were not disappointed at all. It just so happened that this hotel was booked up except for the suite accommodations, so we went ahead and splurged. It was very nice! The suite let my growing family spread out a bit and included a separate King bedroom and a living room/kitchenette area in a second room and a very large bathroom suite. It also lived up to the quality in decor and furnishing that I am used to with the Hilton brand. The staff was very friendly and helpful and their complimentary hot breakfast was even better than the Poplar Avenue locations. The location is a quiet one in a good part of town but is not very close to downtown, but not a bad or confusing drive either. I must say that all the Hilton/Hampton brands in Memphis are the right way to go!

“Will Definitely Go Back!” This is a well located hotel. You can take the train from OHare ($2.50. can't beat that) and it stops 2 blocks from the hotel. Walk to many major sites in the city. Great room decor, friendly staff. Only a few negatives as follows: no bathtub, only a shower, not an issue for everyone. Poor sound proofing from the hallway - could hear a lot of noise from hallway but it always died down at night. Dumb flat sinks. They look pretty but they are impractical, sinks have a bowl for a reason, so they can drain! Comfortable beds. We had breakfast at State & Lake on the first floor with good food and service. We also enjoyed the rooftop bar which is a must. If you go after the happy hour crowd and before the late night crowd you can snag a great table and view. I tried to book this hotel for a business trip next month and it was sold out six weeks in advance so it must be good!

“My favorite hotel in entire USA!” I love this place! Great deal on Hotwire. First time, I stayed for a week and ended up getting upgraded to a suite at check in. (Not sure why as I did not pay for it.) Have stayed four more times for business though never got a suite again, but this hotel is definitely something to include in your DC experience! My rooms have always overlooked the courtyard and the White House, which coming from the Midwest, I have found to be a very cool thing! Lobby is fabulous, service stupendous, and the location is convenient as heck to shopping, subway system, fabulous dining and area attractions. And in my humble opinion as a frequent business flyer who has the opportunity to stay in many 4 and 5 star hotels...THE BEST THING ABOUT THIS GLORIOUS PLACE...are the BEDS! They have a feather topper on them, and as someone who never sleeps very well...I could sleep for a week straight. Very comfortable. In fact, this hotel is so comfortable and accomodating, I am going back next month for a little R&R.

“Great service - fair property.” Excellent front desk service. Clean. But - a little scary. Best rate I could find near the Galleria, but I was not comfortable with the location and did not feel 100% safe. I would not recommend to a friend, so I can't reccomend to you. Pay a little more and stay at another proprty nearby.

“perfect stay....” Just had the most wonderful business stay at the Omni Shoreham - no issues at all. Staff were the nicest, all accommodations were perfect! Would really recommend the Omni! I am proudly a platinum member which offers some good perks!

“Outstanding staff even if a little dowdy.” We happened upon this hotel by accident because we had a medical emergency while changing trains in Philadelphia. Our patient was taken from the train by ambulance to U Penn Hospital. We wanted to be nearby and found this hotel on the internet on our phone. They could not have been more accomodating starting from the time we checked in. When they found out about the reason for our stay they gave us a special hotel rate. We had Thanksgiving dinner in the hotel dining room and the food was excellent. It was surprising how many other diners were in there on that holiday night. The next morning we had breakfast in the regular dining room and once again, service was perfect and the food very good. The hotel could use an update on the furnishings but the staff more than made up for that. At every turn they were helpful - even giving us shortcuts on our many walks over to the hospital.

“Solid location, great experience!” This Crowne Plaza was a delight to stay a night. The beds were very comfortable, the pillows were nice and the room was spacious and clean. The front desk staff was efficient and friendly. The biggest advantage to this Crowne Plaza is its location. A five minute bus ride downtown, or a two minute drive to downtown makes it attractive. Also, its proximity to Greektown and the United Center does make it ideal. There often seems to be a deal to stay at this location, I had a groupon, so that helps. That said, the overall experience at the Crowne Plaza-Metro was very positive and would recommend it to anyone staying in Chicago.

“A great find in midtown Manhattan” Located on W. 52nd Street, this hotel is in the perfect location for exploring Manhattan. While my husband was in business meetings (walking distance away), I was able to walk to a Broadway show and enjoy Central Park. Our room was huge and very clean, and the bathroom was contemporary and lovely. The decor in the lobby could use some updating and the front desk staff was a bit off-putting. We enjoyed the bartender as he served us a late night end of day cocktail. I would definitely go back!

“Spotless Hotel” My family of 5 stayed at the Silver Cloud-University for 4 nights in Aug. 2008. We reserved a "Suite" which included a king bed and a pull-out sofa. Unfortunately, it made the room(s) much smaller. The family really liked the 2 large plasma TVs in each "room." Although the room colors seem outdated, we were all impressed as to how CLEAN the room and the bathroom were (it's been a while since a hotel bathroom impressed me). The breakfast buffet had a great selection and was constantly being replenished. I thought the price was a bit high, but breakfast and free wireless internet was included. The hotel also has a nice pool. Our one minor complaint (which was partially our fault) is we believe our son's stuffed animal was accidently put in a trash can (by his brother). I wish the hotel maid would have taken it out or turned it in to the front desk. oh well.

“Acceptable - but nothing to get excited about” I stayed here with my extended family for three nights. Since we had 6 people in our group, I reserved a two bedroom suite. While the lobby and the grounds of the hotel look fairly new and clean, our suite had some obvious signs of wear and tear. The most obvious was the numerous spots and sticky substance (like honey) on the carpet. After using a hotel washcloth to scrub up the sticky spots and some of the most obvious dirt spots, the washcloth was black and I decided not to spend my vacation scrubbing the carpet on my hands and knees. We mentioned the carpet to the front desk the next morning and it was obviously vacuumed thoroughly when we returned in the evening, but the dirt spots still remained. The carpet needs to be thoroughly cleaned which I understand they couldn't do while we were occupying the room. My husband and son tried to go to a movie at the theater in front of the hotel but after seeing the police cars in the parking lot and police officers in the lobby of the theater, plus the numerous questionable-looking teens/young adults just hanging out in the area, they decided it probably wasn't very safe. Two of those type of teens came into the hotel lobby one evening asking us where the water fountain was and then if we knew were the hotel manager was (who wasn't at the front desk at the time). The hotel manager told them there was no water fountain and they left the building but hung out in the hotel parking lot for awhile (we stayed there watching them to make sure nothing happened to our car). These two incidents made us feel that this hotel is probably not in the safest area of town. On a positive note, the furnishings of the hotel were nice, the bed was very comfortable, and the people who worked at the hotel were pleasant and helpful. Overall, this Residence Inn was acceptable but I'll find a different hotel the next time I'm in San Antonio.

“Nice hotel, convenient location, very good restaurant and grounds” We stayed here for its proximity tot he airport. It is located across the street form the airport and light rail station. You could walk to the airport though there is a free shuttle every 20 minutes. For $45 plus taxes and fees (Priceline) it was a bargain. While there were some touches (e.g., no flat screen TVs) that may show the hotel's age, overall it appeared fairly new and in very good condition. We asked for a quiet room on an upper floor and got a room on the Hilton Honors level. I did hear some street noise, though no airplane noise, and ear plugs solved that problem. The inner courtyard, including pool and jacuzzi, were exceptionally nice. Although we drove to a bayside restaurant the first night, on the recommendation of the concierge (whom we told we wanted seafood), the meal we had in the hotel's own restaurant the second night was even better (though with no view to speak of). Not cheap, but excellent wild salmon and the biggest pork chop I've ever had. Bar items rather pricey (e.g., $7.50 for generic brandy). $20 for self parking ($26 for valet) seemed high. WiFi was free in the lobby (and business center) or $12.95 for 24 hrs. in-room. We were there for 2 nights. On the second day, after we'd turned in our rental car, we walked to the light rail station and were in downtown Seattle in about half an hour, for just $2.50 one way.

“Great Hotel - Great Location” This hotel is in an excellent location in Chicago. One can walk just about everywhere on the Gold Coast and Near North Side. The hotel itself is very nice. Our room had an awesome view, was spacious, and the bed was super comfy.

“Nice hotel; bad, bad lighting; very expensive breakfast” Stayed here for a conference at the San Jose Convention Center. It's a perfect location for that, and not a bad location for anything in downtown San Jose. First good stuff: Location, nice work area in the room with lots of plugs and proper height for working on a computer, comfortable bed, quiet (except for a little plane noise - the hotel is in the flight pattern for SJC airport). Bad stuff: Horrible lighting in the room. The lamp on the desk had two, mostly bare, CFL bulbs with the color temperature of industrial lighting. In fact all the lighting in the room were those same awful bulbs. The bathroom was worse - the light was behind the mirror. The TV didn't work when I got there, but that was fixed. Still the channels were junk and no HD. (how can a $99 Fairfield have great HD channels and a $300 Hilton have none?). It also seemed the AC wouldn't cool the room enough. The Breakfast buffet was $20+ (I ate a $10 egg&cheese bagle off the menu that was fair). We should have walked down the street. Food: We ate at Original Joes down the street. It's lost some of its charm, but the food was still good.

“Very nice hotel, wonderful suites, very quiet rooms, luxurious!” I stayed here for 2 nights to see how this hotel fared in comparison with other hotels that I had stayed at on other business trips to New York City (e.g. The Muse, The Soiftel, etc.). I decided to try one of the Suites on the 11th floor. The Suite I had included a hallway, a large living room, and a bedroom that has the most unique photograph over the king sized bed that actually acted as a nightlight--during the day it was illuminated and at night you could lower the lighting to a low level or not at all. The room was quite luxurious; the bed was very comfortable; there was a large walk-in closet with a safe; there were robes (but no slippers); there was a mini-bar (but the ice was on the 2nd floor and you had to ride one of only 2 elevators to get there. It was a very nice stay but there seemed to be some shortfalls. When I arrived by limo there was no doorman to open the doors or to assist with unloading or getting into the hotels. This was automatic at all my previous stays at the other hotels. I had to go inside and ask for assistance. Each time I came and went in and out of the Algonquin over the two days, there was never a door man to open or close the doors. This was automatic at the other hotels. When the bellman took me to my room on check in, he told me about the ice machine on the other floor (2nd floor) and that I could go get ice if I wanted to and that there was a coffee station there as well (which was a nice feature). But in other hotels, the bellman always went and got ice for me. Even at a Courtyard Hotel by Marriott the bellman went and got ice for me. So these were some of the minor blips on the radar that caused me to rate this a 4 instead of a 5 star hotel. Also I felt that the bar prices were over the top. $ 24 for a side car or a martini is a bit excessive even in New York City.

“Very Nice Hotel - On a Side Street” You usually can't go wrong with a Doubletree hotel (chocolate chip cookies!) ... I wasn't familiar with this one - it's new and a bit off the beaten track, but not hard to find, very new, and very nice! It looks like they must have recently torn down an old building, with a fairly small footprint, on this lot, then built this new 27 (+/-) floor hotel. That makes for a very small lobby, but that's not an issue. There is a nice breakfast restaurant behind the lobby. Each floor only has 7 or so rooms on it ... a very vertical hotel! We checked in very early and our room wasn't ready, but the front desk staff was very friendly and helpful ... the front desk clerk called for a bellman, who took our bags very quickly and stored them in the back. We then went out for a short lunch and returned to check into our room. Another bellman showed us to our room ... very professional and very friendly (made us feel very welcomed!) Room was very small (though not bad for NYC), but modern, clean, and comfortable! There is a new underground parking garage (under another hotel) diagonally across 29th street, which has a very reasonable rate for Doubletree guests. Our room on the 21st floor had a view of the Empire State Building. This isn't the heart of the tourist district, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It's a short walk to the Empire State Building, the Macy's main store, Madison Square Garden, Time Square, etc. A good location to see mid-town.

“Excellent” Excellent location, excellent staff. I was a little worried when I booked it because the photos on the site had the rooms looking REALLY outdated, but again for the price and location I could not pass it up. Rooms were excellent and had been updated a bit from what was shown on the website.

“Very convenient” Small rooms (NY standard) but very good position and price for mid Manhattan. The breakfast offered for 12$ has fruits, pastry, bagels and cream cheese, cereals, aso. Rooms equipped with coffee maker and tiny wardrobe.

“Great location, quiet and clean!!” We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights. We booked double bed no view(had a rate at $109 per night AAA). Our philosophy is a room is only to sleep and change in. We like to see and do all we can when on vacation. Room requirement needs to be clean and not feel icky!!! I was pleasantly suprised at the room and loved the large bathroom with a small fridge. Nice suprise perfect for sodas from Vons just up the street!! The hotel was very clean and quiet. Except for the family of ducks and ducklings didn't hear anything. The staff was great and friendly!! So close to everything! If you are looking for lots of extras and pizazz, this hotel isn't for you.

“Horrifying” We booked this hotel for a weekend. The website made it appear charming. Wrong. SCARY!! Photos are completely deceptive. One of the attractions for us was the pet friendly aspect. My dogs would not stay here. NO NO NO. I stayed 30 minutes and paid for one night just to get out of there.

“Gute Location, relativ grosse Zimmer fuer NYC” Der Name des Hotels ist ein wenig Irrefuehrend, es liegt nicht in SoHo sondern eher an der Grenze zu Chinatown und Little Italy. Trotzdem ist die location sehr gut und zentral. Das Hotel selbst ist in sauberem, gutem Zustand. Als PC Platinum gab's ein Upgrade auf den Club Floor in ein (fuer New York) recht grosses Zimmer. Alles war sauber, ordentlich und Holiday Inn Standard. Einziger Negativpunkt war, dass wir einen Late Checkout fuer 2pm bestaetigt hatten und dann um 12pm vom Roomservice geweckt wurden weil wir auschecken sollten (trotz do not distrub Schild an der Tuer).

“Superior Customer Service” Spent one night here while in Dallas on business. I was in a king suite, which was nice and spacious, and had 2 very nice 42" flatscreen LG televisions. The room, as well as the public areas was spotless. Very quiet as well, even with a laarge freeway right out front. My colleague staying in a different room found one of here tv's not working, after reporting the issue it was repaired within 10 minutes! Dinner at the hotel's restaurant was actually very good, in terms of selection and quality. Ordered breakfast from room service via the door card with a requested arrival of 7 to 7:15. They were at my door with breakfast promptly at 7am sharp. Everything I received was exactly as ordered. My only complaints would be that the wine list in the bar was filled with very middling quality wines with prices at least 5x retail. Additionally wireless internet is $12.95 a day. This is starting to be annoying to pay $10+ a day for internet at full service hotels, while their value-brand little sisters usually include this for free. Overall though, I would say that the customer service at this property exceeds expectations. A very pleasant place to stay in the Market Center/Downtown area of Dallas.

“Amazing modern hotel” We booked a last minute trip to New York and as Yotel was coming in at a great price and based on Tripadvisor reviews we booked it. Check in was so easy, we arrived at 1.30pm and our cabin was ready. The rooms are small however so well designed to use the space to best effect. The team at mission control were really helpful when we wanted a late check out. There was a selection of muffins tea and coffee available in the morning. It was really close to Port Authority, Hell's Kitchen and Time Square. We have stayed in a number of hotels in New York and would stay at the Yotel again.

“Nice stay, but....” Staff very friendly and professional. Bellman in the lobby during the day is a credit to the hotel! Location was outstanding. Close to DIA and right off of I-70. Room service was good (no Coors Light in a Denver hotel?!?) Hotel showing its age, however. Could use a fresh coat of paint and some cosmetic upgrades. Probably would stay there again.

“Rooms were tired and so was I” Staff was helpful and the express checkin was perfect for me. I appreciate having a drink delivered for free each morning...all typical Omni stuff. Unfortunately, the king bed wasn't as comfortable as I expected and the pillows were thin and felt cheap. I couldn't quite get a good night sleep as the walls were paper thin and I heard noises of the family next door. The manager was responsive when I mentioned that there was a water stain/mold in the bathroom so i presumed they fixed that after I left.

“Dated and expensive” Like many of the reviews here say, it's definitely not at the standard I expect from a Westin. Although it looks modern on the outside, the inside looks very dated for a supposed 4 star hotel. The definitely need to do some modernization (or at least a little cleaning and a new coat of paint) to make it look at least presentable. Room I had was very small and right next to the elevators. Essentially, I had elevators whizzing by my window (it's one of the open outdoor view elevators) every few minutes, which wasn't ideal, but since it was the only king bed room they had available, I didn't have a choice. The room had old worn carpet, but was relatively clean. Parking is VERY expensive at $42 a day, and internet isn't much better at $13 a day. Ended up paying about $45 for 10 pieces of sushi at one of the restaurants on the hotel (which isn't necessarily the hotel's fault), so I'd suggest eating elsewhere. To add insult to injury they added a mandatory tip to the bill (I was dining alone - the practice makes sense on a large party, but a single diner?). Not exactly impressed with this hotel - there are definitely better places out there than this hotel.

“The Plaza= Excellence” The Plaza is a fabulous property. The service was impeccable. We were treated like royalty by every staff member that we encountered. Even the morning we departed, at 4am, the front desk clerk was alert, friendly and genuinely concerned with how we felt about our stay. The bellman was also at his best at this hour. And if you ever wonder when they could possibly have time to do all of the flower arranging in the lobby, it is at 4am. The amount of flowers everywhere was astounding! The rooms are beautiful and the beds were the most comfortable we have ever slept in. Little things seem to just "appear" in our room while we were out. Chocolates, fruit plates, champagne.........it was wonderful. Room service was prompt and the food equally amazing. Having a butler on hand to see to your every need is more than anyone could ask for. Staying at The Plaza is an "experience" An experience we would recommend to everyone.

“All hat and no cattle” Another shining example of America's race to the bottom. I think that this hotel is seriously mismanaged. Yes, the architecture is lovely but the cold, unwelcoming lobby and lack of signage are missteps. When you finally check-in to your garishly decorated room, you will be overcome by the cloying smell of cheap air-freshener that is inescapable because the windows don't open. The interior designer should be indicted for crimes against humanity. The lighting is terrible, repeat, terrible. Hallways were filthy, hair in the bathtub was a real turn-off and no breakfast before 7 AM is inexcusable. On a positive note, the staff were cheerful and willing to help but seemed afraid or unmotivated to think outside of the box.

“Disturbing, yet fascinating” Have you ever gone exploring in an abandoned house? If you have, you know what it’s like to stay at the Congress Plaza. It’s fascinating to go around and see all the old, forgotten stuff, and yet there’s a sense of unease that permeates the whole experience. As a hotel, the place is adequate, barely. It has hot showers and comfortable beds, but the whole place is dirty, beat up, and tremendously creepy. I like old stuff, and the place still gave me the willies. We were in town for the Rock ‘N Roll Marathon, and Its location across the street from Grant Park was extremely convenient for that. But unless you have a specific reason to be in that exact location and can’t afford to stay at the nearby Hilton or the Blackstone, you’ll find a lot of better places downtown for about the same price. The Congress Plaza may be barely functional as a hotel, but it’s pretty fascinating as a sort of museum of bad remodeling ideas and forgotten antiques. For example, we stayed in the “Buckingham Wing,” a six-story addition to the original hotel that looks like it was tacked on in the 1960s and promptly forgotten. The interior still has all the tacky 1960s touches you can imagine (gold-flecked tile, unnecessary spiral staircases, etc etc), while the exterior is clad in plastic panels that in no way match the rest of the building. I’m sure it seemed like a good idea when they built it. There’s stuff like that all over. The bar has what must be the world’s oldest popcorn machine—it’s made of oak. Just sitting in the corner, forgotten. The basement wall is lined with walk-in wooden iceboxes. The hallways appear to have their original 1890s woodwork, under about 100 coats of peeling paint. And perhaps creepiest of all, the famously haunted 12th floor has a door that’s screwed shut from the outside. All pretty cool to look at. But I wouldn’t want to stay there again.

“Very good experience” A clean, convenient place to stay with friendly staff (except during check-in). Rooms are spacious and comfortable. Great facilities for conferences across the street from the convention center.

“Great location, very clean” I loved the location!!! I liked being in walking distance to soho and the west village! Also the E train station is right across the street that will take you to JFK! I thought the room was very nice!! It was small but that is what you get in NYC! I liked that there was a loofah in the shower with shower gel!! Nice treat! I will defiantly go back!!

“Perfect at every step” I stayed here for a conference and couldn't have been more delighted. This is one of the few times at a hotel where I felt truly taken care of. The room was great - I think about as big as my whole condo! The bathroom was sparkling, with a tub and separate shower. Lovely products. Staff were wonderful. We were given a tour of the kitchen by the chef, and treated to seeing our desserts being made. Brunch at the weekend is unusually expensive, so beware. If staying here as part of the FineHotelsandResorts program the amenity is a $50 discount off dinner, free breakfast, and afternoon treats delivered to your room. Yum! Highly recommended as a signature experience you won't soon forget!

“Diversi punti di forza... qualche punto di debolezza” Posizione L'hotel si trova all'interno di un ampio complesso all'interno del quale si trova uno dei più importanti centri commerciali della città. Il comlesso è a sua volta collegato con un alto grande centro commerciale. Senza uscire si possono visitare centinaia di negozi (Gucci, Loius Vuitton,.. , Sephora). La fermata della metro più vicina si trova davvero a pochi passi dall'hotel. Il centro cittadino è comunque raggiungibile a piedi in una ventina di minuti. Camere Le camere sono carine. Unico limite rilevante: i bagni che sono davvero vecchi e inadeguati per una struttura alberghiera come questa. La copertura wifi è davvero buona e il prezzo ragionevole (circa 10 dollari al giorno). Servizi offerti L'hotel offre una palestra molto buona e un centro benessere (piscina + idromassaggio) davvero valido. La sera venirsi a rilassare qui è davvero un piacere. Un grosso limite è rappresentato dalla mancanza nell'hotel di ristoranti o di luoghi dove poter avere ad esempio un american breakfast adeguato. Unico punto ristorazione disponibile è uno Starbucks che tuttavia non ha pressocchè nulla di salato. Personale Il personale del tutto eterogeneo è un altro punto di debolezza del locale. Abbiamo trovato alla reception persone davvero gentili e preparate (come Paula), ma anche persone del tutto indisponenti e maleducate (come Mario). Andrebbe fatta una migliore selezione del personale. Consigli Se non sapete dove andare a mangiare nei pressi dell'hotel, evitate il pub Champion e preferite il ristorante Legal Sea Food, raggiungibile senza uscire allo scoperto.

“Dated” Second try at the Ritz SF with the same result. Front desk was rather unhelpful. No more pool and fitness room was in the midst of a needed renovation! Bellstaff, concierge, both restaurants fabulous!!! Hotel exudes historic charm BUT rooms really need a facelift. Our room had a courtyard view which offered limited natural light exposure. The room was dusty and there were crumbs on the carpet. The bathroom was sparkling clean thank god but old. FS, Mandarin and St Regis offer a much better value.

“Not worth the price” As Marriott rewards customers, we have stayed at many Marriotts and many Courtyards. This one just wasn't up to snuff in our opinion. Yes, it is convenient to Midway (by shuttle) and to downtown (by El). The lobby is, well, motel-like (it is what it is). The room is okay, clean (except for some mold in the shower) with a comfortable bed and good shower. But there was that mold in the shower, and the air conditioner sounded like a jet engine taking off every time it cycled on. All in all, I think it's way overpriced. If I were to stay at Midway again (a viable option if you're arriving late, since getting into the city the next day is so darn easy on public transportation), I'd find a less expensive option like a Days Inn or Sleep Inn.

“Great example of historic preservation” This hotel property has character which exceeded my expectations. Interior brick walls in the hallways and rooms, along with wooden support beams are very interesting and add a unique feel to this property. Please note that my 4th floor room (there are only 5 floors) faced south into the view of another building; so there is no view and thus very little light. I believe there are a few rooms which face west onto Meridian Street. I have no complaints regarding the room; bed was comfortable, shower water pressure was excellent. Despite the nighttime temperatures dipping near 30F, there was no need to turn on the heating system; the 4th floor location and construction of the building insulated the room very well. I did not hear any outside noise as a few other reviewers noted. However, as also mentioned by another reviewer, I did experience the strange, mechanical noise that seemed to coming from inside the room. It only occurred once; in the morning. Had no problem with the car valet; took only five minutes for my car to arrive. The hotel is close to numerous sports and entertainment venues. Overall, I enjoyed my stay and would recommend this hotel to others.

“Needs some improvement” Stayed 5 nights for a conference and received a room on the top floor. The view from the balcony was nice but even on the top floor I could hear the noise from the nearby freeway. I did enjoy watching the planes on their takeoffs and landings. The bathroom needs better ventilation. I came out from my shower needing another shower just from sweating. There was not a lot of closet space but otherwise the room was nice and the bed very comfortable. The exercise room needs some serious upgrading. The pool area was very nice. Two computers were available in the lobby but were always occupied. The free shuttle to and from the airport was convenient and I did not have a long wait. Like other posters have mentioned, the staff could do better with their customer service skills. With some improvement this hotel has the potential to be really nice.

“Adequate but very small, plain rooms and overpriced for what you get” I stayed here for several nights during this month, which is a very busy time for DC hotels. Most rates were jacked up and this place was no exception. Our small group paid $310/night plus tax, which was the best we could get any of the more reputable groups (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, etc.) during this busy conference season. While the hotel was adequate, it was overpriced. The location itself, which some claim is great, is really not so special. It's way up the Connecticut Ave. hill, in the direction of the Adams Morgan neighborhood. If you have business in the area of the Mall or any government buildings south of K Street, you are definitely not in walking range. Ditto for tourists going to the monuments. Now as far as the ability to walk to Dupont Circle, that's roughly 1/2 mile south so it's perhaps a 7-10 minute walk depending on your exact destination. Not bad. Then again...what's really around Dupont Circle that's so great? Except for Kramer Books and a few other places. Anyway, I would sum up my stay as follows: Pros: Less than 10 min. walk (south) to Dupont Circle area 10 min. walk (west) to Rock Creek/Dumbbarton Oaks Pk Free wired internet connection View from my room, 7th floor - can see Wash. Monument Smaller hotel, not overwhelming or bustling with crowds King bed was comfortable Cons: Expensive for what you get Small, rather ordinary rooms Very small bathroom; sink basin has no counter space Breakfast is expensive, not a good value No wireless internet (only wired) Very small, crammed closet - little luggage space TV is not the high def/flat screen as better hotels now have Closest Metro is Dupont Circle station, 7-10 minute walk

“Overall a good bargin” I was torn between given this a four or five... not that the hotel is "great", but it is very good for what it is: a budget suite hotel. My first thought is that the hotel could use with a throrough renovation, new carpets, a bit brighter atmosphere, etc. However, I am afraid that if they did so, they could command about 50% more per room, which would not serve people like me. That said, the specifics: The suites are pretty good size for a suites hotel (not as big as some, but certainly more spacious than about 75% of the "suites" in whcih I have stayed): We had ample room for five people. The rooms do show their age, particularly the beds are a rather soft. Really nice staff that will try to accomodate your needs. Very good, not great, breakfast (as described by others). They have barbecues for the guests to use. Ample underground parking, but there is a height limit. The kitchens have a good sized stove, full size fridge, and a small microwave, as well as the basics for cooking and eating, but that is about it. If you plan to cook much in the room, recognize that you will have limited cooking implements. To get food, there are three grocery stores within walking distance. On the other hand, there are tons of restaurants of a variety of flavors ranging from inexpensive Mexican (which was good... about a block away), to expensive Japanese. Our kids, like others have mentioned, really liked the Corvette Diner. They also have a social hour, though I do wish they would extend the hours as it is unlikelyt that if you go to the beach, you will be back to the hotel by 6:30. It is rather simple, but it is nice to get a beer and sit outside on their terrace, eating popcorn, cheese and crackers.

“Great hotel!” Stayed for one week in august 2010, got a huge room with a small kitchen. The microwave was missing, but we got one quickly after notifying the staff. Got a room with windows facing the street, but there were not much noise and sleeping was no problem! Breakfast was very good. There were taxis parked right outside at all times, so getting around was very easy! The only thing I find a bit strange is that I got a 5$ charge on my credit card a few days after we left, but the bill stated 0$, and everything was pre-paid. Eddie, the Concierage, was extremely helpful with arranging tours and giving information and directions - Thank you, Eddie! I would recommend this hotel to anyone! And the next time I'm in Beverly Hills, I know where to stay!
“Stunning hotel with spacious rooms and excellent service” I stay in NY twice a month and this is the nicest hotel with the biggest rooms I have stayed at. I will be back.

“Very Nice Four Star Hotel” Stayed here for four nights in September, 2005. Very nice, clean rooms, friendly staff, good sushi. Green tea maker is actually a machine that boils water and dispenses it which is nice because you can make any kind of tea you like. Walk down to 3rd avenue for nice and reasonable restaurants. Room service breakfast was decent and reasonalby priced for a hotel. Prices were the same as the hotel restaurant with no delivery add on other than the tip which is nice. Carpet in the room was stained in one or 2 small places and there was a stain on the bed skirt as well as a dirty rug in the lobby but otherwise the lobby was very nice. I find that to be the difference often between 4 and 5 star hotels....the 4 stars are alittle stained if you look carefully. Room was small but not tiny for NYC.....320 sq feet. I had the Deluxe King and it was very very quiet. Windows they have really are teriffic. you can open them and they also keep the room very quiet. The Deluxe King is the largest King bedded room they have which is odd to me. The suites have double beds. I wish there were a larger room with a king size bed. I travelled alone and believe the room would be tight for 2 although it was fine for 1. The chairs in the room and not traditional arm chairs and are not very comfortable. All in all I will stay here again. Prices are very competitve. Book on their web site. In fact I have made a reservation for December. In my book politeness goes a long long way and they are certainly that. Plus the tea maker is a great touch as well as how clean the rooms were. I believe those minor stains were probably something they did try to get out.

“great stay” We got a room upgrade, picked up from the train station, welcome drink at check in, freebies in the minibar, wristbands for the nightclub. everything was spectacular. Loved the stay. Thanks Mr.Middleton

“Spacious and a good deal” I travel a lot on business, but I stayed at this property when I came to NY for a friend's wedding. The rooms are spacious and a great deal. And the breakfast buffet (included in the room price!) is spectacular. It is such a great benefit, that it makes this hotel a much better value than other hotels in a similar price category, which don't include breakfast. Also, convenient to subway.

“Lots of Room and Lots of Pools” I like Marriotts. They are consistently roomy and comfortable with updated decor. Canyon Villas are no exception. The beds are great, and there was plenty of room for the four of us. There are several pools on property and several more, including a lazy river, across the way. Being August in Phoenix, we spent a lot of time at the pools. We could always find chairs with shade no matter what time of day we went. A few times I even had the quiet pool to myself! Our stay at Canyon Villas was very comfortable and relaxing.

“Best in SFO!” My second stay at the Le Meridien in SFO. It is truly a fantastic property. The location is very convenient if coming into the city via BART (from the airport.) Very easy to walk to the business areas, as well as Union Square, North Beach and the waterfront. The hotel itself is elegant and very clean. Some of the rooms have great views of the bay and the Bay Bridge. Will definitely be returning to the Le Meridien next time in SFO!

“This Hotel is a Gem” My husband I spent chose to spend our 40th anniversary weekend at INK48 - and I can't heap enough praise on Jeffrey Behrens, the Concierge Services Manager, who upgraded us, sent us champagne and chocolate, and was gracious and welcoming. The rest of the staff were equally friendly, as well. I can't tell you how much this matters - but it made the weekend that much more special for me. I noticed that everyone treated well, by the way, which is a mark of a great hotel staff, in my opinion. This sort of treatment keeps me wanting to return again and again. Do I wish I had been in the room with the soaking tub, since my feet were killing me from all the walking we did? Sure! Unfortunately, the rate I nabbed didn't allow for such a luxury. One day... Only one, little complaint - our shower head was so high up that I couldn't reach it to adjust it. I ended up using a hanger! Oops.

“Hip, Clean, Comfortable, Professional Staff” Stayed here for a conference taking place in the hotel. Room was fantastic although my one big complaint is the amount of alcohol that is set-up in the room upon arrival. I realize the "rock star life" type of theme they have going on (drugs and alcohol theme runs strong even in the titles of food items on the menus...) is part of the hotel's marketing, obviously, but I think a little more respect to the customers is in order. Hotel should at least provide a heads-up or a choice to have the mass amounts of alcohol in your room or not. Please be advised if you or someone you are booking hotel with has any issues with or is in recovery of alcohol or drugs...it's entrenched in this hotel. Depending on your family's style and if you are traveling with kids/teens, this hotel may or may not be your scene. Other than that, it's a great hotel. Fun atmosphere and fantastic location!

“Solid Three Stars” I lowered the rating on this hotel due to the following: parking was an expensive add-on at $20+ per day; internet was also an expensive add-on at $25 per day; the king size bed room was extremely small (smallest I've experienced) with the bathroom so small you could stretch out your arms and hit both walls (and I'm a small person). Lastly, the air conditioner could not keep the room at a comfortable temperature (72-75 degrees). Dallas was experiencing temperatures in the 100's but I would think that is normal in the summer and their systems would be built to handle the heat, especially given the room was so small. We finally had to put the thermostat at 65 to get the room even a little comfortable. For the price, I was definitely expecting more. We stayed at the hotel over labor day and something was going on as parking and check-in were chaotic. Overall, the staff handled the volume of people very well. The hotel itself was nicely appointed (recently renovated) and well laid out with a great business center. Our room was clean. Also we had breakfast at the hotel and it was very good (pricey) with great service.

“A good kind of strange!” Just finished a stay at this quirky, strange and endearing little hotel near the Magnificent Mile and am leaving pleasantly surprised by it. Of course, like any hotel, there are a few downsides: -THIRTY-SIX dollars a day for parking!! A staggering amount for putting your car in a spot for a few hours!! -Rooms are very small. Hard to navigate where you plan on placing things in your room. -In my room (610), the curtains couldn't be raised or lowered, as the cords were tangled in a maze that I tried, but could never figure out how to untangle. Among the many positives of this hotel: -Wonderful, tropical feel that's sunny and happy. --Cool colors and furniture selections in rooms, including a very neat espresso-pod machine in each room for a high-quality cup of coffee. -Aveda products are ALWAYS a plus in any hotel! -Very comfortable bedding! -FREE internet connection was an unexpected plus for a city hotel. In fact, it's downright rare! -Quiet halls, nice clock radios, and functional workout room are nice little toppings to round things out. While I have stayed in a hundred fancier hotels with more amenities, this one is simply an offbeat little treat that breaks the monotony of hotel rooms up for a road warrior like me. Definitely worth a try!

“Great hotel - location not so great” I stayed in this lovely little hotel for 4 nights in September. The room was very nice. Not overly spacious but clean and very quite. Had a great nights sleep in there every night. The staff are very nice and helpful. I asked a girl the first day about tours and she spent about 20 mins going through the options. Typical of what they were like for my stay - just lovely. There were a couple of negatives with regard to the hotel. The free continental breakfast was not good at all but there are numerous restauraunts around so it is not a big deal. The only real problem though is the location. It is a 15 minute walk to Union Square or 15-20 mins to the wharf. It is at the top of the tenderloin. I got there at 9.00 at night and the door was locked which it had to be as we had passed several streets with small gangs on the corners. San fransico as a whole is an extremely safe city to walk around but not a good idea around the tenderloin. The walk in to Union Square the following morning highlighted how rough the area looked. However as I say it is at the very top of it so if you head North a couple of blocks it brightens up very quickly. So lovely stay great value just be wary of the location.

“Very nice business hotel” I recently spent a weekend at the Omni on business. This is a very well located hotel right in the heart of the financial district. It is also well located to access Union Square and other tourist locations. The staff seemed very on top of things from check in right to the end of the stay. The entire hotel is designed in a pretty traditional style - think Ritz Carlton, early American revival type furnishings and you've got it. So if you want comfort, quiet and good food, this is your place. If you want a happening scene, you may want to look elsewhere. Over all I was very impressed and would put it up there with the more well known brands in the city. There is evidently a renovation underway which will be a good thing as some of the furniture is looking a little worn. However, this did not detract from the experience.

“Good location, no problems, highly recommend!” This was actually my second stay with the Omni Hotel at Independence Park in Philadelphia. This time we stayed on the 11th floor for 5 nights and have no complaints. The first time here was with my hubby and this time it was a girls' getaway. We used room service at night a couple of times. It came quickly and they set up a table for us - delicious and warm food. We ate in their restaurant for breakfast each morning and had lunch a couple of times. It's kind of odd that they don't serve dinner in the restaurant but you can order it in the bar or via room service. Valet for the car was $37 a night and I believe self park was $27 a night. The room was a nice size with two queen beds, two comfy chairs, a desk, and a flat screen tv. The bathroom was nice but I was disappointed to find a tub/shower combination. Since we were there for sight seeing, it was perfect within walking distance of Independence Hall, Liberty Bell, and so many things. We would stay here again.

“Great property right at the airport” The Hyatt Regency (not to be confused with the Grand Hyatt) is across the parking area from DFW (concourse C). There is a shuttle that can take you from and to the other concourses. I was arriving late to DFW and this was a perfect choice. The Hyatt properties ard typically great and this is no exception. Nice lobby, good restaurant (believe called Mister G's), a coffee bar with Starbucks products and a sports bar. The room was great - clean, comfortable, nice sized HD TV. Some of the staff was disappointing. Our reservation was messed up and it took a while to straighten it out and even the next morning they struggled and were not overly helpful. The wait staff in the coffee bar and restaurant were good. I think the bellman steered us wrong with suggestion a car service over a taxi (it was $65 to downtown Fort Worth area and I think that was more than a cab. Anyway, it is recommended if you don't want to leave the airport. Take note: there is not a sign that I could find for the Hyatt Regency and you either need to walk to concourse C - around gate 21 and take a skybridge over (which was a bit dark and may not be recommended) or leave any concourse and catch a shuttle (better option).

“Business” Nothing unusual. Nice functional place that seems central. As with many business trips I hardly left the hotel. The rooms were fine and the bed was perfect. Minibar had the usual astonishing prices: $5 for a packet of red liquorice. I did notice that some areas that are usually hidden (eg janitorial areas) were more obvious (doors left open etc). The check-in area had an usual configuration. The beginning of the line was across a walkway. No other surprises which is always good. I hate surprises on a trip like this- they are usually not good surprises.

“Great place for a conference” My husband and I recently had a great two night stay at this Hilton for a conference. The beds were very comfortable, and I was especially impressed by the friendly staff. At breakfast on the second morning, the waiter remembered what drinks we wanted, which was impressive. There are sidewalks connecting the hotel to a shopping area that includes a Target, a great casual dining place owned by the same folks that run P.F. Changs (called Pei Wei), and other stores and restaurants.

“Adequate” This is a place to stay if you want to be close to the boardwalk, the action, the beach and the college students. The staff is friendly and the atmosphere is low key. We were kept awake for most of the first night by the homeless people who live right in front of the hotel on the boardwalk, so there is lots of color. This is NOT the place to stay if you want luxury, a big room and some peace and quiet. The pool is not that great and the complimentary breakfast is poor.
“壁が薄い” リッツカールトンホテルとは思えないほど壁が薄く、隣の部屋の声がまる聞こえ。コネクティングルームでもないのにまるで同じ部屋で話しているかのように聞こえる。もう二度と滞在することはないと思う。

“Great rooms, convenient location” Loved this hotel. The room was new, stylish, with a great view of the Coit tower. The bed was very comfortable as well - I probably slept better than I do at home. Had no problem with check-in or check-out. I heard parking was expensive so we parked at the parking lot across the street for $26/night. Breakfast was nice and a notch above your usual hotel fare. Overall, was very pleased with our stay and it was a great deal on Priceline!

“OK and Clean, but LOTS of rough spots” The hotel itself is decent, clean rooms, nice lobby area, restaurant and bar handy, and staff fairly friendly. The problem is with some of the finer points which will not let it get even close to 4 stars: - There is WIFI (internet) in the rooms. However, this costs $13/day PER DEVICE. So, for our family of four, where my children and I each have a laptop and tablet, and my wife a tablet, this is 7 devices. Thus, per day, the cost of using these in our room would be almost $100! What the heck. I brought this to the attention of one of the front desk people, and was told, in his words, that indeed that was the policy "as ridiculous as it is, which I have never seen in any of the other hotels I have worked at". The next day I asked the manager on duty and was also told this was the policy. His solution - use the free wifi in the lobby. OK - sure - I'll send down my two young children to the lobby by themselves while my wife and I are out, or late at night after the old folks go to sleep. CRAZY. Internet should be free these days, just like regular TV. If you need to charge $3/day more per room, do it and stop the nickel and dime antics (don't get me started with Spirit airlines - $3 for a cup of water, how to use the life vest when taking off, but credit card commercials while preparing to land...) - Always WARM! We had out room AC set on maximum (there are no #'s, just a min/max slider), but during the day it was routinely very warm (estimate 76 degrees, even though only 80 outside that week), and never got down to near 70 until about 2am. Several other people I ran into stated the same issue. Big time need for an AC upgrade - have not seen a system like this in 30 years. - There is a CONCIERGE desk, but during the week we were there, never saw anyone there. This left the front desk to answer questions, while the line to check in building up behind me. - They seemed to only have 1 BELLMAN, which took forever checking in and out, and leaving our luggage for a few hours after we checked out. - The restaurant was OK, although the 3 times I went there to eat myself (early am), they kept trying to sit me in the worst table, up against a pylon, despite the fact that the place was 95% empty. - MOVIES on demand: $18 per movie! Instead, we streamed the same movie from amazon on one of our laptops (and watched on the small screen - cozy) for $3.95. Time for hotels to switch away from these pay channels to a real streaming service. - NO POOL or even any outside place to sit to get some sun. Only place to sit was in the lobby, which is subterranean - no windows possible.Ugh. On the plus side, they do have a fair amount of outlets in the room, but could use more than the standard 2 by the bed (my kids fighting for the one open plug for their laptops in bed, while I'm trying to use it for my CPAP machine - but of course, laptops take priority over breathing).

“We love this majestic hotel!” This was our second visit to the Fairmont and it was even better than the first (maybe because we were sans kids this time!) The first thing that attracts your attention is the entrance--with the international flags overhead, the red carpet and the lovely doors. Then you step into the incredible lobby--floor to ceiling marble with columns, exquisite furniture and rugs and, of course, the ornate flower arrangements. The rooms are quite spacious and beautiful, with European linens on the beds, a flat screen television, a marble bath, a huge walk-in closet and of course giant windows, revealing the beauty of San Francisco. We had room service once--it was awesome!-and had a drink at the bar downstairs beside the lobby--beautiful, rich-looking! We frequented Caffe Cento (on the parking level) several times for coffee and breakfast--if you like Illy coffee like I do, you will enjoy this. The concierge was really helpful, pointing us in the direction of some great restaurants within walking distance. The location is very good, too--cable car lines go right by, and there are always cabs available. Plus, since the Fairmont is considered one of the more prominent hotels in town, our tours came right to the hotel and picked us up (some members of our tours had to walk to a pick up location) In our room, I noticed a book on the artwork of the Fairmont, which I enjoyed perusing to check out the art and architecture of this lovely historic hotel--from mirror frames to wallpaper to the gardens--this place is gorgeous. For a romantic getaway, you cannot beat the Fairmont!

“Great Location and a Good Value.” My wife and I stayed in this location for a short business trip. The property is larger than most Residence Inn locations. The grounds are fully appointed and very clean and well maintained. I did have a bit of trouble finding the elevators as it is such a large property and all the halls look the same it made navigation a bit difficult. They do have multiple entries that allow you to park quite close to your room no matter where it is located. The breakfast is typical of this chain but this location I felt was a little above average in cleanliness and presentation. Overall, we had a comfortable stay at a very reasonable price. I would definitely stay here again.

“Try to get as far as you can from a window!!!” Great location, didn't like the restaurant and try not to get a room facing either 8th Av or the 48th. You won't be able to sleep. If you get an upper room or one of the suites, then you are lucky and you will get a great return for what you pay. For some reason, at the time of doing the renovation they forgot to renew all the windows!!!!

“imbattibile il rapporto qualita' prezzo=” hotel senza fronzoli, pulito, comodo, con personale sempre disponibile. stanze a misura d'uomo, le migliori sono quelle con vista su central park. stazione metro a 2 minuti a piedi sulla 103esima camminando verso sud lungo central park. zona tranquilla.

“GREAT HOTEL - CONVENIENT - SERVICE - BREAKFAST!” I stayed at the Elan as a last minute Saturday night in LA (we came a day earlier than we had planned for a week trip). All the other hotels in the area were at least $100 more! We actually booked that morning - they had a couple rooms left. This is a great area - convenient to West Hollywood, La Cienega, and Beverly Center. We arrived at 8pm, and immediately after check in took a cheap cab to the Sunset Strip as it was my first trip to LA. On a nice night you could actually walk to the Strip, but it was cool and getting rainy (plus its an uphill walk). The room was ok. Our 1st floor room had a slider to the side walkway of the hotel - I didnt like being that close to people walking by, but I wasn't at the room very long, and I dont people generally walk out there anyway. As long as you are on a higher floor it wont be an issue. the bathroom was huge and the robes nice. The best part of this place besides location was the breakfast. Wow - I was expecting coffee and a banana when they said continental, but this was great. Selection of coffees, OJ, Lemon Water and some others. Boiled eggs, Bagels (with toaster nearby), jam, oatmeal, yogurt, fruit, pastries and muffins. I think I am leaving out some stuff. Anyway, I was impressed this was included as part of the price of the room. This spread at a diner or coffee shop would have been at least $15pp if they had this selection. Unlimited made it even better! For some this may not be important but I was on a long flight to get here and had lots of things planned so it was nice to get a solid - quick breakfast without having to fork out more money. A few Newspapers were available for free as well! The breakfast area was really nice too - some tables, couch with coffee table and a couple flat screen tv's. Also a few computers were available for use. Overall seemed like a glamourous budget hotel, safe, clean, well situated and staff very motivated to help. No real amenities like a gym or pool but like i said, a great base and good service. We spent the next 3 nights at the Sofitel down the street which was REALLY nice, with pool, gym, spa, and on-site restaurant / nightclub, but you'll pay 20-30% more on any given night. We got a good deal due to it being the week of thanksgiving so it was worth it. If you like to shop, the Beverly Center and Nordstrom's Rack are right there. Melrose Ave is a few blocks north. Robertson St with all the new designers is a 15 min walk, and the Grove about 25 min walk the other way. I'm not big on buses or public transportation, but did take a bus down Melrose Ave one night home from Pink's Hot Dogs (to Melrose at LaCienega) for $1.50 each, because we were sick of paying 10x that for cabs to go just a mile or so down the street. Overall I would stay again, but if I were spending a lot of time at the hotel and got a good deal, I'd upgrade to the Sofitel.

“Great hotel with best location in Fisherman's Warf” This is a beautiful great hotel located one block from the center of Fisherman's Warf in San Francisco. Safe area which allows you to walk to many San Francisco tourist spots. Restaurants everywhere. Trolley line at your doorstep for ease of getting around. We have stayed here before and love this hotel and location. This hotel sits right next to a regular Holiday Inn but this Holiday Inn Express is much newer and looks great from both the inside and out. Here are the only two things to be aware of: First, recheck the hotel website about a week before arrival to see if the rates have been lowered. We saved about $100 per night by doing this. Secondly, the fee for parking your car is $39 per day plus parking tax of $5.46. This is very pricey and is a hidden fee unless you read the fine print. Just be prepared. Overall, a Great experience and would stay here again and again.

“Very Nice for an "On the Road" hotel” This was a very nice hotel for an "on the road" stay. Pros: Free Happy Hour; free breakfast; laundry facilities on site; quiet room even though there were many kids staying there due to a BMX event; free high speed internet. Cons: Slow check-in It is adjacent to a mall with lots of eateries right by. It is easy to find right off I-77.

“Highly recommended, but a few tweaks would make it perfect” I stayed at the W San Diego for three nights in February 2012. From the minute I pulled up to the valet, until I left, the staff and service was nothing but outstanding. I cannot complement them enough. Before arriving I called to ask a couple of questions, and upon arrival there was a personal note from the person I had spoken with along with a lovely fruit tray - outstanding! I needed a late check out, no problem. I needed my luggage in my car a little early, no problem. Room service was great and delivered with a smile and offer of additional help if needed. The rooms themselves were very well appointed. The design was modern and sophisticated, the bed was very comfortable, and the bathroom was very nice. The location is very nice for accessing downtown and the waterfront of San Diego. Many different restaurant options were within walking distance, and I was able to get great recommendations and help from the team working there. The only small tweaks I would recommend to make the W a perfect location are: 1. The carpet and baseboards of the room did show a little wear, perhaps a coat of paint and carpet would take the hotel over the top. 2. The coffee provided with room service was not very good. The food was great, but the coffee tasted like it had been boiled and burned. Overall, I highly recommend the W if you need to stay in downtown San Diego.

“Good - Expensive” Good service and fairly comfortable. But not the top rate experience you would expect from a Four Seasons. For example the rooms and bathrooms are not much better than other downtown hotels. The safe is not large enough for a laptop. There is no coffee machine in the room. The hotel is a bit more expensive than other downtown hotels. However everything else is more expensive as well, e.g. breakfast, parking etc. I would stay there but no more than at other nearby hotels.
