“Very nice stay at the Westin” I stayed here once about 9 years ago and recall it being outdated. I didn't feel it this time. On the 32nd floor next to the elevator, the room was very nice. The noise wasn't an issue from the elevator. I had a king bed and a beautiful view of the Olympic Mountains. Stunning... There are numerous restaurants and even a deli in the hotel. I only had breakfast and the services and food were very good. It is reasonably close to the business district and also many restaurants. I have stayed at the W in Seattle before and also liked that hotel. Different style and location make it a totally different experience. I would recommend the Westin for both business and leisure travel.
“Good choice” For a meeting at MD Anderson this is a good choice. Nice and quite, good location and service, efficient valet parking and shuttle service to the medical center.

“Happy with our stay!” We were upgraded to a spacious clean Executive suite. Our room was located in a quiet back corner of the hotel. This centrally located Courtyard has a nice lobby and tastefully decorated restaurant and bar areas. Gym was well equipped and a decent size pool. We were sorry we were only there one night. It was a crowded July weekend with families and tourists staying in the hotel but we had no complaints about service. Would definitely choose this Courtyard again. We had the bonus bucks rate. Highly recommend the Marathon Grill about 2 blocks down for brunch or any meal. Also, enjoyed the Reading Market Terminal, Betsy Ross House, The Constitution Center and Old City. There are some parking garages behind the hotel.

“My go-to hotel in Chicago” With a wealth of hotels to choose from in the Chi area, I have sampled from the best. Many of them have been quite good, but for the past couple of years, I've opted for the Dana. Location-wise, it's just off the Magnificent Mile in the midst of everything that particular stretch has to offer. Room-wise, it's got everything I need -- they're relatively spacious, have floor to ceiling windows/Juliet balconies that afford you a great view or if it's a balcony, just some fresh air (a great alternative to air conditioning), to-die-for bathrooms situated in the middle of the room (with glass-enclosed showers that let you see out while you shower if you desire, or shades if it's privacy you want), wonderful bath amenities, and -- something I've never had at any other hotel -- hand-made chocolates/candies in their honor bar in lieu of the usual M&Ms etc. Plush bathrobes and slippers too. Room service is good (in terms of offerings and timeliness) and the food is fine. The gym is just OK, unfortunately. Rather small & cramped, there is only 1 workout bench and only a couple of machines. Earlier this week I was there with 4 other (unrelated) guests and we were falling over each other and jealously watching as soon as someone finished his/her reps or workout so we could grab the equipment before anyone else. Dana management -- this is an easy fix -- please expand. The restaurant (Aja, pronounced like the continent) is pretty good too. I've only eaten there once (there are so many choices in this neck of the woods), but when I did, the menu was varied and unusual, and the service good -- even a bit over the top (I lost count of the number of people who checked in with us to make sure everything was OK); I almost expected the chef to be next! Unless my company changes its travel policy, I expect to continue to stay here, esp if they expand the gym.

“Comfortable and Enjoyable Stay” After carefully checking out the reviews, I decided to book this hotel and was not disappointed. The building itself is old but the rooms are renovated and clean. (Soundproofing is so so - several times we hear the neighbors above walking.) The staff is very friendly and helpful. They really strive to make your stay the best it can be. The location is good, there are many restaurants around and it's a short walk to Magnificent Mile. Although we didn't have a car, parking is free here. The staff's recommendations for restaurants in the area well excellent. I would definitely stay here again. A side note: I ran the Chicago marathon and ran from the hotel to the start line as my warm-up( so not too far). Also, my spouse didn't have far to go to come and see me as we ran right by the hotel on LaSalle Street. On the return we were one street over. Something to consider if you're planning on staying here for the marathon. The price was better here as well.

“Not as noisy as the reviews suggest” I found the hotel staff to be friendly and efficient. Room on the 23rd floor was clean and comfortable. Freight trains did pass in the evening, I didn't find that to be a problem. Expect some noise though. Hotel was very busy, seems to be a polular conference venue during the week.

“Can location trump shortfalls?” The Millennium is an attractive, perfectly placed hotel with some warts. In general: - The hotel is fairly good sized for only seven stories so be prepared to walk in maze like, lengthy corridors to get to and from your room. - The lobby is pleasant enough but not very welcoming. - The staff is nice enough but no one will great you by name, not even when answering your calls from the room. - The rooms are very nice - above average for cost. - If you have a view of Quincy Market (it's very nice) be forewarned: it will be loud. You will hear music, bongo's, people leaving bars.... everything. - Valet is $45 a day and a bit slow and congested in getting your car. - Gym has dumbbells and cardio stuff only. - Easy walk to North End, Fanuel Hall area and Downtown Crossing. Ideal location.

“Normally a huge fan of W but slightly disappointed.” My husband often travels to Chicago for work. He has favorite restaurants and hotels but usually stays at the Trump. We are Starwood members so decided to try out the W for my first visit as I as tagging along for the weekend. We arrived at the W to a tiny room but usually size doesn't bother us if the service is excellent and the bed is comfy. This room was clean and minimalist. The common areas and the lobby were fantastic and the location is certainly good for touristy stuff. The Sears tower is across the street, Michigan Avenue is not a far walk and our favorite restaurants were a quick cab ride away. We spent our wedding night at a W in Manhattan (Union Square) and had a fantastic time. We weren't even paying for our room on the wedding night and were treated like royalty. Overall the Chicago CIty Center W seems to not have a clue about service. The front desk told us we could use pts for the weekend nights but upon checkout changed their mind. I ordered yogurt and coffee from room service on Saturday. After 1.5 hours they called to apologize for the delay. I was nice but assumed that since yogurt didn't need to be cooked they would send it up immediately. Another 30 mins went by so I called to cancel as we did not plan spending Saturday in our tiny hotel room. I got in the shower and as I was standing in a towel Room Service arrived with the "cancelled" order 2.5 hours after the order was placed. It was 2.5 hrs. late and they still wanted to charge us $38 for yogurt and coffee. The food was eventually comped but it seemed awfully over complicated for such a simple order. Sunday morning my husband went down to the lobby to obtain 2 cups of the W complimentary coffee that they offer at their lobby until 10:00 a.m. There were no cups so my husband asked a man behind the bar to find some as the complimentary coffee was ending soon. After waiting 10 minutes and asking 2 different people for cups, the original man returned and started cleaning up and dumping the coffee. My husband reminded him of his request for cups and but was shunned. He eventually went back and got cups but not without attitude. By the way there is no wireless and the connection is $30/day for their network. This was annoying. Overall the service was lacking for a W property. We had a decent stay but my expectations were higher and friends who were at other hotels near by for much less money had a better experience. The pros are the location, lobby bartenders, and the gym. Other than that I would not go back to this W location. Perhaps I'll do some reading about the other W property on N. Lakeshore Drive.

“Great Downtown Property” I stayed at the Luxe for a week attending a show at the LA Convention Center. The hotel room was modern and bed amazingly comfortable. Staff went over and above, very friendly. Only downside is the restaurant and bar and under construction so there are no services. There are several restaurants across the street, my favorite being the Farm...great take out. Gym is also under construction but they have comp admission to a local Gold's Gym.

“Close to Airport and Room was Decent” Stayed in this hotel on a Friday night in April. Check-in was early at 2pm with no issues. I did have an issue connecting to internet on 2nd floor which I had experienced about a year ago as well when there. Requested a different room closer to a router and was quickly accomodated by the manager, Beatrice. Beatrice also called the internet provider and asked them to come that week and work on getting better service throughout the hotel as there have evidently been other complaints. I found her to be exceptional in her demeanor and customer service skills! The room I had seemed to be pretty new and was very clean. I know others have reported this hotel to be questionable but I have found it to be OK when staying in area. I think its kind of on the outskirts of town but have found it very convenient to airport and a pretty quick ride to the downtown area.
“great hotel in denver” all the excepted westin qualities. just missing the heavenly shower.. good location. everything was as expected by a westin. rooms are nice and big. Staff was great.

“great girly fun” very feminine hotel with all the touches including nightly turn down service with cookies, bath robes lush bath products, black and white dvd collection. right next to kenmore T and great coffee downstairs too,

“LOVED THIS NO-FRILLS HOTEL!!!” My boyfriend and I spent two nights in July at the Metro Hotel for a cousin's wedding. We had two requirements: inexpensive play to stay and easy access to San Francisco. We found both of those items were covered by the Metro Hotel. The front desk staff was super friendly. We got great recommendations on some good vintage shopping in the Mission. The rooms are absolutely NO FRILLS. Bring your own toiletries as the ones the hotel provides are minimal. We stayed in room 112, which was literally a room with a bed. The bathroom and closet were decent sized, but the room itself was pretty tiny. No worries, the hotel website kept us in the loop about the size of the room so we weren't shocked when we checked in. The bed wasn't super comfortable, but it did the trick. Our favorite part about the hotel was the adorable court yard. After a day of trekking around the city my boyfriend and I enjoyed spending some time in the courtyard with a glass of wine (that we brought ourselves) and some sunshine. I would stay at the Metro again in a heart beat! I would be concerned about staying there during the winter months only because I couldn't locate a heater in the room, but overall we thoroughly enjoyed our say.

“Great place in DC” Our second visit and still one of the best in DC, especially the location just two blocks from Union Station. We arrived early and not only were we sent directly to a room, we were upgraded to King. Comfy bed, great TV, spacious bathroom with shampoo and , conditioner and bodywash dispensers in the shower. The only problem was that the minibar had too little room for us to chill our water bottles overnight; well, we took stuff out so we could. Friendly staff, complementary ice water and tea in the lobby each afternoon and weekday happy hour of wine and sangria. Easy walk to Mall museums, and Metro access at Union Station (also lots of choices for a quick breakfast at the station).

“really outstanding” I stay in a lot of hotels in NY. This one is my new favorite. The greeting when I came in was genuinely friendly, and I was actually brought to my room to be shown how everything worked. Situated across from the library, the location is excellent. I spent my evenings next door on the Bryant Park balcony. Andaz had a nightly wine reception but I never attended. The room was quite spacious and I loved the 10 foot ceilings. Not only was the wifi included in the price but so were non-alcoholic beverages from the mini bar. The price was very reasonable for NY. I stayed in the north tower facing 42nd street. There was a little traffic noise, but definitely not bad by NY standards. The only minor hassle was getting the high tech room key to work. Overall, a very pleasant stay. I look forward to returning.

“One of the best in Charlotte!!” Without a doubt, a great hotel in the middle of downtown-probably the best in the city. Walk across the street to the epicenter for a late movie. Great service. Green hotel. Rooms very clean and well appointed. Can't go wrong here. Hotel less than 2 yrs old.

“Excellent Stay” Cannot say enough nice things about this hotel- from check in until check out. Every one was extremely professional and courteous, even though we had booked through Hotwire. Room was very nice, very clean, and came with a fridge. Did not have time to try the restaurant or pool. Free wifi was nice. Self- parking on garage much less expensive than valet. Would definitely stay here again! Only a block to dart rail train station.

“Not a bad hotel at all” When I got this hotel on Priceline, I was worried based on some of the reviews. I was prepared to write a scathing review! Upon arrival, however, I was pleasantly supprised. The room was huge, spic & span, with little or no road noise, and the bed was comfy. It's true the tub and toilet are in a small separate room, and that the A/C was somewhat noisy, but not overly so. They are renovating the hotel right now, so none of the public areas are open. Since I am rarely in the room, it's OK with me! They had cookies and coffee for free in the afternoon, and everyone on staff was friendly. I agree that this is definately NOT a 4 star hotel. The worst thing I can say about it is that they charge $10 a day for WIFI!
“nice & comfortable, but don't like "extra" charges” $10 extra for high speed internet, around $23 for parking. A hotel of this class should not charge for internet.

“Exciting Marquis Property” This BIG BOX style property is your basic Marriott convention style hotel. Of course, the location is the major draw here. If busy, loud, and crowded is what you're looking for; then this will be right up your alley. The lobby, Atrium, main public areas are all quite spectacular. Our guest room was very nice and it felt extremely spacious but maybe that might of been because the hotel we had been in previously was teeny tiny. Standard Marriott quality bedding made for a very comfortable night's rest. We had an absolutely fabulous Times Square view. Unfortunately, we were only in for one night so didn't really get to use too many of the facilities or F&B outlets, but the staff seemed extremely friendly and helpful.

“Very spacious hotel in the Stockyards” We stayed here with our children and other family on the spur of the moment. The suites are spacious and clean, the furniture/lines are updated, the breakfast options are good and there is gated free parking for hotel guests. The hotel staff is very nice and they accommodated all requests rapidly. We experienced one blip (inebriated partiers) and the manager very graciously addressed my concern. If you are visiting the Stockyards area, this hotel is a great option!

“Overall a good hotel , good value and many conveniences nearby.” I stayed at this hotel while attending a conference in Chicago. The reason I chose this hotel was based on all the positive reviews and a reasonable rate as well as the convenience of having a Supermarket(dominicks), a Walgreens, a Starbucks and a few restaurants all within a block radius. If you are traveling on a budget, getting food at the market is a good place to get food. It is in Greektown, so most of the restaurants nearby are Greek, but there menus are all full of many varieties. Of course the hotel has it's own restaurant, I did not have a chance to eat there, just had drinks. The room was clean and well maintained, each room has a balcony. The rooms are a little small, but for a solo traveler, it's good enough. I would not recommend it for couples or families. The bathroom is a little small as well. They have free wifi and wired interenet. The wifi slowed down at night, so I ended using the wire which was provided in the room. I guess there are too many users. But overall the stay was good. I would definately stay here again on my next trip to Chicago.

“Great value, great location, dont expect any frills” Needed to find an affordable but convenient and comfortable place to stay in San Francisco for a 10 day stay. Five Star hotels out of the question, just way too expensive, and it was Fleet Week so premium pricing all over the place. A friend had recommended Courtyard as viable chain for longer stays and so try it I did. I was not disappointed. This Courtyard is conveniently located just a few blocks off Market, about halfway to CalTrain and the Giants ballpark, did I mention it was conference play-offs as well. I had a 3 block walk to our office, 4 blocks to the Westfield Mall on Market, 4 blocks to the Ferry Building (a must on weekends). So for any business needs in San Francisco its really well located. The hotel itself is what you expect in this category. Check in is efficient if not overly friendly, dont expect help with your bags, better to tip the driver for this. Bell desk was mostly vacant during the times people arrive and leave. The room was very well appointed with a good and very comfortable bed, large sofa, great LCD TV with all sorts of connections for iPad, iPod, movie camera? Who knows. The desk arrangement is a little strange at first, kind of a pull out on wheels effect that you get used to but is weird at first. By the time I left I thought it was something that all hotels want to consider to give more room in the room, which it did, Well done. Lighting was generally good, although more light over the working area might be helpful, perhaps an overhead halogen spot? Airconditioning was perfect, not noisy, although a draft was felt if sitting on one end of the sofa, but changing positions helped, doh! Easy to set to comfortable levels on both hot and cold days. Bathroom was well appointed, shower temperature was perfect, it was all very clean. Toiletries are basic, but this is a 4 star after all so if you want something luxurious bring it yourself, what is supplied is good enough. Internet connection worked perfectly the whole time, no problems to connect and no disruptions in service. Lobby is one of the better features with a great atrium / lounge that serves as the lobby, the overflow from the bar and a place to sit in great comfort waiting for your pickup or friends. Free internet here is awesome. There is also a courtyard open to the air just behind the glass wall, very useful on the fine sunny days, a real feature of this hotel. The food in the hotel is pretty forgetable to be blatantly honest. I ate in the bar/restaurant the first night, should have gone out. Tried the breakfast buffet one morning, should have gone out. The good news is that there is a Starbucks in the lobby and the let you buy there and bring back to the atrium in the lobby or the courtyard to finish your coffee or food from Starbucks, and the free internet means you have ubiquitous connection. There are a dozen or so really excellent restaurants within one block in any direction from the hotel, better to eat at them or call them for delivery, the hotel website lists the closer ones with their telephone numbers etc. Definitely a better option for eating. I will definitely stay here whenever I come to San Francisco in the future. It was the best value for money I have had in this great city and there is nothing to complain about at all apart from the quality of the food, so eat out like everyone else.

“Old Fashioned Rooms with Modern Amenities” This hotel is in an excellent location for business travelers and convenient enough for visitors to the historic sights as well. Despite the recent "modernization", the hotel has maintained its old-fashioned feel; while it no longer feels "dated" it definitely has maintained much of its charm. Room service dinner was not as good as hoped for, so went to McCormicks & Schmicks the next night two blocks away which was much better. Best part of stay was getting to use the sporting club in the same building, free to guests - one of the best gyms ever!

“Have you ever wondered - What if I get real sick on a trip?” I've always wondered what I'd do if I got very sick while staying at a hotel. Well, my wife did. We had just gotten off a cruise ship and my wife didn't feel well. I called this hotel before checking off the ship and asked for early check-in. Got it... at 11am. Wife went straight to bed at at 5pm had trouble breathing. I called front desk and asked if they knew of a doctor I could call. They immediately connected me to a doctors office. This doctor does house calls (I haven't heard of house calls in over 40 years. I did have to pay by cash or credit card, but worth it). He showed up and diagnosed that he thought it was Pneumonia, but needed some tests to confirm. He called the hospital and we took a cab. He was right. 2 nights in hospital and then 2 nights in room resting with antibiotics. Now the positives with this Hilton: 1) I was impressed with their immediate response to get us a doctor and not just dial 911 or tell me to look in a phone book. 2) The front desk, Peter, asked every time I saw him how my wife was doing and was there anything they can do. 3) Kenny at the bell desk was outstanding. He asked if I'd like to have a limo for a flat $40 rather than the hassle of a taxi, it was worth the few extra dollars not to hassle. Plus Kenny picked up our bags from room at the time he told me the day before. We got downstairs and he already had them in the waiting limo. Being a HH gold/diamond member we got free breakfast. Well worth it. Their bar area gets busy. The draw back here is they won't open up tables in the breakfast area and if you want something to eat there really is no restaurant in this hotel other than a limited bar menu. If you want a fun meal go to Ellen's Stardust Diner with the singing waiters/waitress' (broadway talent waiting to be picked up in theatre shows). Don't get room next to elevators, you'll hear the cables and dinging when it stops at floor. The rooms are very nice. The hotel's location is fantastic. Make sure the taxi driver drops you off at the 41st street entrance where the bellman can help. 42nd street entrance is busy and you'll be fighting to get past all the people just to go thru that "back" entrance. When you need a taxi, they get you one immediately at 41st street entrance.

“Adequate for a short stay” We stayed at Hotel 41 for 4 nights, arriving December 25, 2005. The following are what we liked about our room: 1. the bed was comfortable and the sheets were clean; 2. the bathroom was clean; 3. there was a fridge in the room for water, etc.; 4. the bathroom had a dryer, make up mirror, Aveda products, and even a shower cap and Q-tips; 5. there was an iron; 6. the carpet was clean; 7. the staff were friendly; 8. the location was excellent. We did not like the following: 1. the size of the room, which felt cramped and the bed was in an alcove with about a foot on each side to walk in; 2. there were no bed side tables; 3. there was a burn mark on the carpet that appeared to have been made by an iron; 4. there were spots on the bedspread; 5. the walls were dirty; 6. the water took 5 minutes to heat up. On the second day of our stay, there was no hot water all day. We were given a credit of $50.00 but would have preferred the hot water; 7. there was a smell of cigarette smoke coming from somewhere in the evenings; 8. the ironing board was one of those small ones that aren't very handy; 9. the cost of the room was too much for what you got - we paid $189.00 the first two nights and $269.00 the next two nights, not including any taxes; l0. when we were given our bill, there was a space for a "tip". I have never seen this before on a hotel bill; and 11. the view was a brick wall. Generally, we may have expected too much from this hotel, given some of the 4 star plus ratings. We did enjoy our stay in New York and at first we contemplated not sending in this review because our complaints are not major. However, since we use Tripadvisor all the time to check on rooms where we plan to go, we thought we had the obligation to let others know of our experience as well.

“Great staff, location and room” Had a stay at this property last week and found it to be a really good deal with points since rates were in the $300 area during my one night stay. I took the Newark Express bus and it was a pretty easy walk up Lexington avenue to the Hotel. Check in was very professional but the "front desk area" looked more like a bell desk but the people working check in were on top of things and very professional. I booked a standard king and found the room to be bigger than expected after reading some of the reviews. It was not huge but the size was fine especially since I was by myself. Internet was $14.95 for me as I am not Plat or Diamond with Hyatt and although I dont like to pay for internet, it was of good speed when I used it. Got an email fromt the front desk supervisor later in the evening (assume it was automated) and I replied with a comment and to my surprise it was answered that evening as well. Nice touch. The location of this property is great. You have soo many options from this area. I was leaving out of Laguardia the next morning and stayed here instead of the very shabby airport hotels and got to the airport in about 20 minutes. Much better option than staying at Laguardia. I have nothing negative to stay about this property except I would have preferred that the restaurant was open earlier but their opening time of 7AM is normal for NYC in my experience and the restaurant across the street opens earlier.

“Not bad, but close.” The good things were: $35/night rate through Priceline, complimentary water provided in room, close to freeway, gas, food and shopping. The negatives were: Rooms are tiny... the smallest we've every had, the A/C unit made a lot of noise, several lighting fixtures didn't work (or worked off/on... including the bathroom light). It is clean and the staff is pretty good... it would be a good deal if they got things in better working order.

“Nice staying” I benefitted by a good offer for my staying in this hotel so I can stated this hotel was very profitable for me. The deluxe king room was large and clean, the king bed very confortable and the quality of the amenities products very good. The Hotel is well located not so far from Foggy Bottom metro station, 20 minutes walk from the White House and 15 minute walks from George Town attractions. The personnels is nice but a little bit indolent and slow in the reaction. The wireless was working randomly. The Cafè Lombardy breakfast price is expensive and high respect the room rate. On the whole I would suggest this hotel.

“Great location!!” so nice to be able to walk to an entire retail center of great restaurants and shops. New hotel features the new courtyard concept. Very small gym was only negative. great lobby for business discussions. about a 15 minute drive from airport.

“Great location, very clean hotel.” Stayed here for one night in February so that I could attend a two day course in the Microtek building right across the street from the hotel. I got here around 7 a.m. and was going to have them hold my bags but they let me check into a room! Pretty amazing in and of itself. Lobby is large, staff is so nice & accomodating! I felt like they would bend over backwards for me, great service! The room had everything in it you would ever need. Kitchen with full refrigerator, small stove, sink, dishwasher, coffeemaker, microwave, dishes, utensils, pots and pans, wine glasses, wine opener, etc. Small kitchen table that seats two people, work desk, separate living area from the bedroom. Nice large bathroom. I had a rooftop view of the hot tub so no brownie points there, but then again I wasn't in my room except in the evening anyways. This hotel & the rooms are clean clean clean. I always look for "corner dirt" like in the corners of the floor, on the wall etc. And this place was pretty spotless, I was impressed. Very comfortable room. Gym has everything you need for a quick workout. Full, continental breakfast was great. Eggs, sausage, biscuits & gravy, juice, coffee, yogurts, fruit, toast, bagels, milk & cereal...what more could you want/? In the evenings they have free drinks and snacks (changes daily). One night they had bratwurst. Wow. Nice place, kudos. I only rated the value as a 3 because I feel like for the standard person sometimes hotels in downtown Denver are a bit pricey. I got the "microtek rate" of $149 which was quite the steal compared to the rack rate of this place. Within walking distance to shops, restaurants & the 16th street mall.

“Great location and improved facilities” This is probably my fourth stay at this hotel in the last 5-6 years, and I've noted some improvements over that time. While the basic amenities remain pretty much the same, I've noted that some of the rooms have been updated. This time my room on the 20th floor had a slightly more modern feel, a comfortable work desk/chair, and was quite spacious. Unfortunately, the lighting in the bathroom shower is still inadequate -- I get that the sole overhead light can't be moved, so how about a thinner/lighter shade shower curtain so I don't feel like I'm taking a shower in the dark? Other changes include new parking fees in the attached but independently owned garage -- you either pay the going rate by the hour ($41 overnight) or get unlimited in/out privileges with a pass card for $44 (added to your bill in advance). Yes, downtown Chicago parking is expensive and you should just accept that's how it is --no different at any other hotel. This is not the suburbs. That said, at least the internet is complimentary, and worked great :-). Staff is friendly and helpful. Attached restaurant (Viand) can be iffy, depending on the day. I've had great service and poor service there. But it's a good place to have a drink at least. The location of this hotel is very convenient, one block off of Michigan Ave, so it's easy to get to and easy to walk to most gold coast/downtown locations. If you fly in, it will be an expensive cab ride to downtown, or you can take the El, but it's several blocks from the nearest station.

“Perfect for My Down Town Stay” Very friendly front staff and bellman, great room. When you assign up for their membership for free, you will get complimentary wifi in your room and your choice of beverage every morning, plus a bottle of water at the night of arrival. You also get a personally addressed letter to welcome you. The hotel is located in a very dynamic and safe neighborhood. 2 min walk to Gaslamp district, right next to Orange Line Trolley (will become green line starting Sep 2). 5 min walk to the bay front park. Walking further down to the west alone the bay front, embarcadero marina park and seaport village are right there. Can't think of a better place to stay.

“A real mixed bag at this Marriott” I arrived at the Marriott late on a Monday night, tired after a long flight. I asked if I had a "nice room" and the woman at the desk said, yes, a room with a view of the sound. When I got to the room, with the help of a nice bellman, he assisted me with everything in the room and I glance out the window. All I saw was a big staircase and another building. I jokingly said, some waterview. He said it was a waterview if you looked out the window to the right. Ha. It really didn't matter though. I quickly went to bed exhausted and soon heard a ROARING noise. I thought perhaps it was a large truck outside. A few minutes later, I heard it again. And then a later again. I could not imagine what it was. It sounded like an airplane was IN the room - but I knew we had travelled a distance from the airport. Finally, when I heard it AGAIN, I got out of bed and went to my balcony to see a freight train going by right behind the hotel. Honestly, I cannot believe that no one commented on it before. I can only conclude that maybe there was a soundproofing issue in that room but it was unbearable. To their credit, in the morning, I called early and they moved me to another room - where, BTW, I could still slightly hear the train, but I think I was probably very sensitized to it at that point. So that is the "awful" part of the hotel, Another annoying thing was that I got all suited up in my bathing suit, walked down to the pool, only to find it closed. I do understand that sometimes they need to close things for repair or maintenance - but generally, they tell you at check in, or have something in the room telling you what the alternatives are. For the good things, the service was really good and friendly, the room was quite comfortable with a nice desk and chair, a huge tv, and a very comfortable bed. The food and service in the restaurant was terrific. It was reasonably close to Pike Place Market where you had many food choices. I had breakfast and lunch there most days. There was also a lovely seafood restaurant across the street - I think the name was Anthony 66. The hotel itself was really quite nice, but given that you really go to the hotel to sleep, the noise issue was unbearable. I would not be able to recommend this hotel unless the person would totally DEMAND to be on the front side of the hotel so that they would not have the train noise. Its a shame really.

“Great Space and Value” We had a reservation at a different hotel for the weekend, but the day before arriving in New York I saw a rate of $159 for an executive one bedroom king suite at The Buckingham on Quikbook. Although the hotel has fairly mixed reviews on TA, I have always been interested in trying this property because of the space and the musical history of the hotel. I booked this amazing rate and I wasn`t disappointed. We walked into a huge apartment, immaculately kept and nicely decorated. The full kitchen had new appliances including a full refrigerator, cooktop stove and oven, stainless steel dishwasher, microwave, toaster and coffee maker. Also cookware, flatware and dishes. There was a full dining table and chairs, queen sized sofa bed, a large bedroom and plenty of closet space. Also 2 televisions, 2 dvd players, vhs and stereo system with wireless speakers. The spacious bathroom wasn`t contemporary, but charming with crown molding, new fixtures, abundant towels, great water pressure and plenty of hot water. We loved having our own New York pied-a -terre. The front desk staff was talkative and extroverted at check in and check out. This was a great experience and we`ll definitely return.

“Not that impressed......” I stayed at the Arizona Grand for 3 nights on business in April 2012. I am in my early 30s and travel extensively. I arrived quite late from my flight - the check in process was quick but then I had to wait for a golf cart to take me to the building because he didn't want to take just me - there was NO ONE to wait for. After 5 minutes, we left. I was in the Sedona building in a very large room- no complaints, yes TVs are dated but no big deal to me. Now on to the other things: - WIreless works OK- they shouldn't market this as a big part of the $40 resort fee when it is sporadic and somewhat slow. - I had room service two mornings for breakfast. Both times it took a long time for anyone to answer and then 30-40 minutes for food to arrive- i hate to see the wait times when the resort is busy as it was empty this week. They got my order wrong the second time but I didnt' have time for them to fix it. - The hotel bar is pretty bad. - The gym is quite nice - good facilities, clean, good hours. The resort fee is a complete rip off for the corporate traveler and the waterpark does not deserve to be in the company of the other great US hotel parks (Grand Wailea, etc). I will definitely not stay here again.

“I guess it just depends . . .” I stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria in August 2011 while attending a business conference. I get to New York quite often on business, however this was my first stay at this property. Given the large conference at the hotel as well as the many tourists, the hotel was quite busy. Check in went smoothly and the agent was quite helpful, giving me an upgrade to a large corner room as I am a Hilton Honors member. He did notifiy me that there would be men working on my floor replacing carpet in rooms and that mine would be replaced immediately after my stay concluded. I guess that explains the strange, almost urine smell in my room. It was very noticeable each time I entered the room but I became acclimated to it each time within a few minutes and I chose not to ask for another room as my stay was only for two nights. The room was a large, virtually square room located in the corner of the building on the 8th floor which offered two large exterior windows. I enjoy corner rooms as the extra window allows for lots of natural light, ufortunately the windows were covered with what looked to be decades of grime such that you really didn't want to look through them. The bed was extremely comfortable with lots of extra pillows. I slept wonderfully and heard no noise from the hallway or other rooms during my entire stay. The room also featured a bottom-of-the-barrel Phillips television that afforded only passable video quality and abysmal audio. Woodwork in the room had multiple coats of paint built up over the decades as well. The most recent coat looked as if it had been applied by a child using a mop. There comes a time when you just can't put any more paint on woodwork and my room was long past that point. The bathroom was smallish, even by NYC standards. Although it really didn't make a difference or cause any inconvenience, I found it odd that the shower and water controls were located at the front of the shower and the shower head was located at the rear of the shower. The bathroom vanity still had some chrome effects that looked like they might be original and I don't realy mean that in a good way. I'm aware of the hotel's historical significance but when I pay for a hotel room, I'm paying for the here and now. There is a difference between "historic" and just plain old and this hotel crosses that line at times. I was in elevators on numerous occasions where guests would press a botton for their particular floor and it failed to light or stop at their floor. On on occasion, the light was lit for a the floor of a guest in the elevator but failed to stop at his floor, In many ways, this hotel reminded me of the Intercontinental Barclay just around the corner and why I no longer stay there. That being said, I spent some time in a room on the 9th floor that was temporarily converted from a quest room to a meeting room for my conference by removing the bed and replacing it with a conference table. This room was much fresher than my guest room and featured a much larger bathroom with a large, glass shower stall and modern bathroom appointments. This room was very nice in comparison to my guest room. The woodwork in the room was crisp and did not feature multiple layers of poorly applied paint. I did not use room service or the fitness center nor did I eat in any of the restaurants. Food at my large group lunch was a salad that I would describe only as marginally edible. I would have been very dissatistified to have received this salad in a restaurant. This was my first stay at the Waldorf=Astoria and I really don't see myself returning. There are just too many really good alternatives in this part of town.

“Decent location and free drinks!” This is a pretty standard Embassy Suites - clean two room suites with a small refrigerator and a microwave. Nice flat screen TV's in the living room and bed room and a pull out sofa in case your travel companion snores too much. The made-to-order omelets were a nice feature of the free breakfast and my colleagues were big fans of the free drinks each night (5:30 - 7:30). There were also some light refreshments each night (meatballs one night, nachos another, celery/carrot sticks with trail mix another ). I am never a big fan of paying for internet service in the room and one negative was that they do charge $12 a night for that service. Another small drawback, depending on your preferences, is that the nearest metro stop is a 15 minute walk away. It's not too bad, but there are definitely places with closer stops nearby. The neighborhood is pretty nice - only one homeless person sleeping on the sidewalk each night which really isn't bad for D.C. and there is a Wal-Greens and a CVS within easy walking distance. Always a plus. Overall the staff was courteous, the rooms were clean and fairly spacious, the location was okay so it's not a bad selection for the D.C. Metro area.

“WOW Well done!” Cool hotel! Great amenities, Pool, whirlpool, sauna, fitness room, and Fantastic breakfast! WOW the best we have ever had at any hotel with a free breakfast. Excellent and fast check in and out, great location, and parking was a bit tight, but we succeeded! We would definitly stay here again!
“Most personal hotel I've ever stayed in” Amazing personal service, they make you feel right at home

“First Class Renovation for a Child of the 60's” This is my third stay over 11 years and this one was the best. The rooms are updated and the staff were keyed up for what you would expect from a hotel of this caliber. They take care of their elite SPG members and I was happy to be able to check in at 11 AM. There are no club floors at this hotel, but my room was definitely recently updated. The concierge desk is probably the best of any Westin anywhere. If I could ask for ONE THING, it would be to include MSNBC in the selection of tv programming. One thing I think is funny about the hotel restaurant, it changes names/themes every time I stay here! Keep up the good work!

“Great perks for a business traveler” I spent only one night at this hotel, but found it to be very nice. I travel quite often for business and usually stay a certain chain of hotel. This time my first choice wasn't available so I decided to give the Hotel Allegro a shot as I have previously stayed at a Kimpton property and had a good experience. I was glad to hear when I checked in that since I was a KImpton Intouch member that I got a complimentary $10 mini bar check out, in room WIFI, and a continental breakfast next door at 312. I would definitely stay here again as the added perks were great. Location was good also; close to L, restaurants, entertainment.

“nice stay but location is poor for tourists” My overall rating reflects the property and NOT its location. My wife and I just got back after a 3-night stay there so while she attended a conference I enjoyed the hotel. From what we were told, they have only been open 3 mos. so the kinks are still being worked out. Biggest drawback, as other reviews have mentioned, is that this hotel is NOT located for tourists but rather conventions and business as the convention center is adjacent. You will have to either take cabs or public transportation to see any of downtown Boston which was disappointing. As for the cabs, the hotel is situated in such a way that it's in off the main street which makes hailing cabs a problem other than at peak times. We stood and waited for 15 minutes which proved annoying. The other challenge is food. While the hotel has its own restaurant you often need something fast and there is nothing but the gift shop's candy rack, overpriced room service or the lobby's Starbucks. I mentioned this upon leaving and was told the current unoccupied retail space might get a restaurant. Hint: if you exit out the back of the hotel there is a new deli across and down the street in the lobby of one of the new buildings there. It just opened and was really good. Heated indoor pool, hot tub and exercise room were all great as was nice sized flat screen in our room. You are also a 10 minute cab ride from Logan so that makes departures/arrivals easy as well. All in all, for business highly recommended. For sightseers, families, etc. pick an in-town property or learn to take cabs/public transportation.
“One of my Favorite Hilton's” As expected nice rooms ad a very peaceful serene feel tot them Wish they would put the bill undermy door otherwise great

“Nothing Extraordinary but very nice.” My wife and I went to Chicago to celebrate our 10th anniversary. After reading some of the reviews I became a tad nervous. After this weekend, I'd feel comfortable recommending this hotel to anyone. The cost seemed high but since I was redeeming Honors points it was not a concern. Most downtown hotels are expensive anyway. Check in was fast and efficient and as always our Doubletree cookie was great. We were put on the 16th floor and had a decent, not great view of the North side of downtown and a sliver of Lake Michigan. The room was nice, clean and comfortable. The bathroom was above average and clean. Decent room. Location was pretty good, not great. You are two blocks or so off the Magnificient mile, not too far. Would have liked to seen a few more hot spots for late night but there wasn't anything walkable other than Timmy O'tooles pub right across the street. Fun place but way to crowded. We were about 6 blocks from the closest El station. Walkable but I'd have liked to be a little closer. Seemed like this was the case for all attractions. Note: If you are going to a Cubs game (we did and it was great even though the Cardinals lost) get to the El a couple of hours early. The trains are PACKED if you wait until an hour before game time. I don't think I have any complaints. Earlier reviews complained of thin walls. We did experience some noise around 4am (A bachlorette party coming in after drinking all night) but that happens about anywhere on a Sat. night. They could use some updated televisions but not a huge deal as we were out and about most of the weekend. Checkout was fast and easy. It's a 40-50$ cab ride to O'hare so the Conciege informed us of their towncar service. Flat $45 fee in a much nicer vehicle. I'd recommend it. All in all this was a pleasant hotel that was above average, not great. I didn't experience the slow elevators that everyone was complaining about. It's a bit pricey but it's a nice stay. Any complaints I'd have would be very nitpicky and could happen anywhere.

“Utilitarian” The location of the Novotel is excellent and the property is well maintained. It's an OK place to stay, but it is utterly lacking in charm. Our room was austere in decor, sort of French hipster look. That was OK, but the room was not well planned. No bureau or shelves in the closet so you could not empty your suitcase. No shelves in the bathroom for putting your toiletries on. Definitely had the feeling that the Novotel brand is France's equivalent to the "big box" chains here in the US like Holiday Inn. For close to the same amount of money, you could have a much nicer New York experience.

“Pleasant Stop If In Area” A short distance from the highway, the hotel was pleasant and the staff friendly. This hotel is not particularly convenient to anything but a short drive will take you to stores and restaurants. Downtown Columbus was 20-30 minutes. A fairly large hotel with only two elevators there can be a wait at times. Our room was fine although the maintenance was so-so.

“Perfect for one” I echo the previous comments on the size of the rooms (small), the quality of the staff (excellent), and the strength of the air conditioning (arctic.) I would also add that the shower was a good size, and there was an endless supply of hot water. With the heat and the humidity in New York this past weekend I took three showers a day. While the TV didn't work, and I couldn't figure out the ipads for guests on the lobby wall (my fault, not the hotel's) the place was running extraordinarily well for a shakedown cruise. If they can keep the level of staffing while also opening the rooftop bar (I heard later this month) and the Great Room then this will be a wonderful, well located property with very small rooms. I had a queen bed room -- I measured it with footsteps and came up with a 10X10 bedroom and a 4X5 bathroom. Very cleverly organized but I expect it would not be appropriate for larger people, or families, or groups that were not on the most intimate of terms -- while sitting on the toilet you are most visible and audible to anyone on the bed. A major plus of my room (806) was a great view of the Empire State Building -- I fell asleep watching the camera flashes on the observation deck.

“Little gem in the middle of the loop” Don't let the outside of this hotel fool you. It's a small hotel with comfortable quiet rooms. While the view out of our windows was the rooftop of a smaller building, the room made up for it. And yes, because of the decor and the direction our room faced - the room was somewhat dark, but it was ok. Unless you're spending all day in the room, it shouldn't be an issue. The bed was super comfy and the room was clean. Staff was friendly, including the valet downstairs. It's located in the middle of the loop within walking distance to everything.

“Not what we expected, but overall pretty decent” Having business meetings for a couple days in San Antonio last week, I booked my reservation with my company travel agency with the full intention of staying near my meetings at the Marriott Rivercenter. Not reviewing my travel itinerary beforehand (my mistake), I did not notice until the day before my trip that I had instead been reserved a room at the Marriott Northwest. Needless to say, I was extremely disappointed as my son was traveling with me so that we could experience the fabulous riverwalk below the hotel I THOUGHT we had reservations for in the evening hours. Now, we were 20 minutes from that area at this different location. <sigh> Despite my initial disappointment at the distance I had to drive to attend my meetings and go to the riverwalk with my son, this particular hotel was very nice. The room was extremely clean and the hotel staff courteous and accommodating. The beds were comfortable and there were plenty of clean poofy towels for us both. I was beginning to feel more comfortable already. I ordered breakfast the next morning and was surprised at the appearance of my simple eggs and hash browns breakfast tray. There were pretty flowers on both the plate and in a small glass holder. The food was excellent too! My son ordered a pizza at lunch while I was at my meeting and said it was great too. And he's a very picky eater even for a teenager. :) As we were leaving the first evening to go out to dinner nearby, the attached photo shows a black cat happily enjoying the view from on top of our rental car. Many might view this as an eyesore, but being an animal lover, we thought it was cute. There were 2 cats who happily jumped off the car and went about their business. Speaking of the parking lot, there were plenty of spaces and it was free. There was also a security guard walking around which made me feel very secure. The area was not in a bad neighborhood or anything so I believe this to be a nice touch by Marriott to make their guests feel secure and welcome. My initial disappointment went away as my son enjoyed the hotel amenities while I was in my meetings and had no complaints that we weren't downtown in the popular area of site-seeing. My "beef" is not with Marriott, but moreso with my travel agent who did not reserve the hotel I had requested, but if I find myself with meetings in this particular part of town again, I will definitely stay here again. The only complaint I would have is that the A/C took a bit to get cold like I like it and was very loud. We were also charged the $9.95 for internet access twice in one day since we each were on our own laptops. I would have hoped I would have only been charged one fee for the room in general, no matter how many laptops were in use, but I also feel internet usage should be free in hotels anyway. Other than these 2 "complaints," this hotel was above average and I would recommend it for business travelers and families visiting the area. Oh - I forgot to mention that it had a gorgeous atrium like area as you walked in past the check-in too!

“Clean, Fun and Functional...a Perfect 2-Night Vacation Stop!” If quiet, ease, and convenience are top priorities, this hotel will not disappoint! We used the free hotel shuttle, which arrived within minutes of our call. It was a very quick ride to the hotel, which is clean, bright and modern. Check-in was a breeze, although there was only one staff member at the counter. She was pleasant and knowledgeable. The room itself was simple and well-planned. High shelves in the bathroom area enabled us to keep some things out of toddler reach. Instead of table lamps, space-saving built-in sconces smartly lit the room. The shower (no tub) was stocked with high-quality shower gel and shampoo in convenient wall-mounted dispensers- no fumbling with those tiny bottles! Our room was very quiet- we did not hear any others in the hotel, nor did we hear any airplanes. The cube mini-fridge was just enough for keeping drinks and leftovers. The lobby is bright, spacious and airy. The pool table and board games kept our small son engaged; the internet kiosks were a bit slow, but fine for a short e-mail checking session. Although there are two boarding-pass-printing stations, the screens are placed at chest-level; I found those hard to use, so I printed our boarding passes from the internet kiosks instead. The Ruby Tuesday restaurant, just behind the hotel parking lot, was, according to my husband, "surprisingly good!" and I agreed. The Circle K convenience store, next to the hotel, came in handy since we did not rent a car.

“Initial Teething Problems But Great Otherwise” Stayed here for 3 nights and really enjoyed it. On checking in, we were told that, despite booking both rooms at the same time, they wern't going to be near each other although they would be on the same floor. However, when we got to the rooms, the previous guests hadnt checked out of one of them and consequently we ended up on 2 different floors. This was the only issue we had and other than that, the hotel was excellent. Both rooms were really nice with 2 double beds, good size and lovely balconies overlooking the water. Despite the noise of the cruise ships, the road and the airport - which you could see from the balcony, we slept well every night and the noise was not an issue. Excellent Irish pub on site in the hotel which did free breakfasts for kids. It was a 10 minute walk from the hotel to Gaslamp Quarter and Horton Plaza, 20 minute walk to the Convention Centre and 15 minute drive to Sea World. Excellent pool at the hotel as well. Would recommend visiting Star Of India Maritime Museum opposite hotel - great for kids.

“Right place at the right time.” I was booked here by the Broadway League for a business event. After reading the reviews here, I wasn't certain about staying there, but I thought if the League is recommending it, it must be OK. We found it to be delightful! The rooms are small - this is Manhattan and if you want a big room, you're gonna pay huge bucks for it. But, it had everything you needed and some nice perks too. The Bose Wave radio (it's not an Ipod dock as one reviewer expected... it's a radio!) has a great sound. Our room was toward the back of the hotel and overlooked rooftops, so we left the curtains down. A windowbox light made it appear that sunlight was streaming in, even though the drapes were closed. The TV remote has a sensor that is not attached to the TV so if you place things on the desk that block the sensor, the remote won't work. (Another problem cited by a different reviewer.) There is an expensive mini bar - typical. WIFI was iffy, but the in-room ethernet connection worked great. We had a "red" room which felt vaguely "Japanese" to me with clean lines, black furniture and no wasted space. Bathroobes to lounge in were fluffy.The huge shower had plenty of hot water and pressure. Everything was clean. Maids were wonderful about coming in when it was convenient for us. There is a parking garage right across the street. The hotel is about 1/2 block to the very top of Times Square and about 2 blocks to the heart of it. The play "Chicago" is at the theatre right across the street. They were loading out "Spring Awakening" from next door and "Mamma Mia" is just out and around the corner. There is a Food Emporium across the street and 1/2 block down - upstairs is deli food and basement had a grocery store great for families watching their $$. Lots of cool sidewalk vendors on 9th ave, just aroudn the block. Subway, shopping, theatre, it's all within easy walking distance. Everything was clean. The staff was wonderful. The door isn't well marked - look for the yellow signs for Sarafina's - so I'm glad I knew the lobby was on the second floor.

“Not so bad” I actually was booked here by mistake as there was some confusion by the former travel agent in what I required.None the less although initially horrified I found the staff excellent the bellmen went out of his way to assist with my issues and gave some great local advice. Look its not the best place in Denver to stay but the value is enhanced with the people. The food was really quite okay but the people really made the stay. Worth serious consideration

“Good stay” I attended a conference at the Baltimore convention center and priceline assigned me to this hotel. The lobby is quite classic and magnificent in a way. I had no problem with elevators. Although I was traveling alone, the room was large even from the standards of traveling with family. I believe it was not a corner room. The room faces streets so it was somewhat noisy at night, but not anything significant. The sleep number beds were very nice. The staff were very kind. Location was quite convenient, just two or three blocks away from the convention center and very close to the harbor and all other downtown landmarks. Metro was right in front. The only little complaint is that wifi was somewhat weak in the room. It worked at desk and not well at beds. Considering the price I paid, I would definitely stay here again.
“Not the typical Hilton Hotel” Old style , very large hotel. Centrally located, ideal for business but otherwise I would suggest to select a more modern hotel in the same area.

“Pleasant stay” Stayed a night at the Hampton Inn TS North. It was a pretty good experience, the personnel was friendly all around, which sometimes is rare in NYC hotels. The bed was comfortable, the internet free and the breakfast free, so its a good value overall, even though around 300 for a hampton inn room is kinda alarming, but then again you are in NY and the location is in midtown so that's somewhat expected. My only annoyances were that the breakfast is free but its like jam packed with people and kind of messy as a result. Like cereal flakes on the floor and stuff. I'm not sure how to go about addressing that but it is worth mentioning. Secondly, the maid service comes pretty early, was having breakfast in my room and had the maid barge in at like 9am, then again a short while later, then again one more time when i was getting ready to check out. I'm not sure if my room didnt have a do not disturb sign or if they simply dont use them in the hotel but yea that was kind of weird. The maid was apoligetic and polite about it but it did seem a bit excessive to be interrupted on 3 times. Overall, it is good value for its location, i was on the second floor facing the busy 8th ave below and didnt have a disturbed sleep so that was a pleasant surprise. I would probably come back and stay here again.

“Don't miss the restaurant” Enjoyed our stay here - the reception staff was particularly helpful - but what really made a difference was the sensational restaurant, The Saltbox. We had a couple of great breakfasts there - the banana and ricotta pancakes were especially good - and a great lunch. Much better than some of the mediocre restaurants in the Gaslamp Quarter down the street.

“Second Visit and still Excellent in all regards” The service is top notch and I rate this after 40 years of international travel. Exceedingly personal service from the Executive Chef and the Senior Managers. All of the staff are helpful and outgoing. I will be going back when in Washington. The Location, just of Dupont Circle, provides all the support and ammenities one could ask for. All with in a five minute walk

“Good hotel, great staff” We stayed for 3 nights last October and at first we thought that the neighbourhood looked a little run down, but the hotel is very nice and the staff is great. Once we had a look around, we found it's a short walk to Union Square, Chinatown, the financial district etc. Breakfast is really nothing, but there is a great little cafe right at the street car stop a block away. The first night we asked if they had info on NAPA/Sonoma wine tours and within 15 minutes we had our tour booked! The afternoon wine tastings are a lot of fun, meeting fellow travellers from around the globe. We quite enjoyed our stay, but particularly it was the staff that made the visit enjoyable. So, if you want to stay away from the tourist nightmare that is Fisherman's Warf, this is a good location.

“charming but.......” This is an old and charming hotel. It has so much history, however, it's not perfect. Our room and bathroom were pretty small and the sink and bathtub leaked all night..DRIP DRIP DRIP! The onsite dining and bars were VERY expensive but this hotel is within walking distance of many restaurants and the 16th street mall. Fun place to stay!

“Priceline does the trick again!” My boyfriend and I stayed here June 6th... very tricky to find and google maps got it wrong. It's actually on the corner of Columbia and Broadway but the front of the building is on Colombia. We stayed in room 2401 my advice to ask for a high floor and then see if any of the '01' rooms are available even "02" I think have decent views of the city and mainly the harbor. $20.00 extra for a room with a view. Also because the Trolleys run pretty late if you are on lower floors you hear the street noise. Speaking of noise I could hear like someone pipes from MY ROOM??? hmmmm The bummer about staying on a higher floor is that the elevator system is WHACKED! there is only 2 buttons to push for 2 separate elevators - 1 set of elevators reach floors 1-23 only the other set of elevators reach all floors... but the 2 buttons is for ALL elevators so if you keep pressing the button because only the elevator that will reach floors 1-23 is there, you are literally S.O.L. Anyhoo rooms are nice, my first time sleeping on a heavenly bed - it was comfortable (i am biased as I have a double-pillow top with padded mattress pad) linens were fine, I love Gilchrist and Soames http://www.gilchristsoames.com/ toiletries in the bathrooms at this hotel they put the "White Tea" scented items in the rooms. Showers had a neat double-shower head! If you are a Starwood Preferred guest you receive the complimentary bottle waters in the room... if you are not you will be charged. Parking is $32.00 (standard for parking downtown) across the street it was $15.00 but without in-and-out privileges. We went down to the Happy Hour 3pm-6pm it was busy, due to a convention being in town. Had live entertainment a nice young man playing his guitar it was nice the appetizer food was standard Hotel Lobby grub and sadly I was not impressed, our server was new but she smiled a lot and had the ENTIRE Bar area so she was hustling. Would I stay here again... not sure as I am always at the whim of priceline when I go down to San Diego for these little trips... oh yea and the gift shop was highway ROBBERY a 20 caplet box of Advil was $12.00!!! it's only $3.50 tops in the stores GOOD GRIEF CHARLIE BROWN! and there is a 7 Eleven around the corner that isn't to much better but still DANG! Respectfully Reviewed

“Nice all around Westin” Stayed at the Westin Market Street for two nights while visiting SF on vacation. Several nice things about the hotel.. Location - can walk to many of the key areas in SF... all the shops on Market Square and around Union Square... 20 min walk to AT&T Park, walking distance to the Powell street cable car line... We were given a king sized room at the end of the hallway with floor to ceiling windows throughout the entire room facing directly East. Nice views.. Room was a tad on the small side though, but can't complain. Bathroom was a good size with all the goodies, but didnt have the usual heavenly shower I've been accostomed to while staying at Westins. Plenty of pillows.. and comfortable bed - standard for Westins. Staff was friendly throughout our stay and with any questions we had. Were awoken from time to time with door banging and the high pitched "Housekeeping" from the maids, which was odd considering we were at the end of the hallway, and actually went through another door to get to our room. All in all, would recommend staying at this hotel - we did alot of research of the hotels in the area, and for our rate (~$200), cannot complain one bit.

“Good service, clean rooms, nice staff” The Good: Knowledgeable and helpful front desk staff. Rooms were tastefully done, not huge but really nice. The hotel is quiet, the bar was excellent and food good. The position is very good. The not so good: We had a deluxe, ocean-view room, but there was no bath. Not a big deal but for the money would've expected a bath as well as a shower. For a room advertising an ocean view, it was not that great. The room was on a busy road and was a bit noisy at night. Still, this was a classy hotel with first class service, and I would stay again.
“Central location with accommodating staff & clean rooms” Nice rooms. Some traffic noise if you're a light sleeper but comfortable beds. Bath does not have an exhaust fan

“Excellent choice in the Capitol Hill area” My stay at this hotel was great. The staff were cheerful, helpful and attentive to details. The hotel is a short walk from Union Station or the Capitol. I got a great week end rate, too.

“Great location & value, but limited amenities” I stayed at Herald Square Hotel for 3 nights in a "new" queen room while vacationing in NYC. The room size was adequate for me and my wife. Our main complaint about the room was lack of counter space in the bathroom. We didn't have any issues with service, although we did not require much interaction with staff other than for checking in and out. At check-in we were provided a subway map which turned out to be extremely useful. Amenities are definitely limited. The hotel has no restaurant or room service. This was not a problem because there are plenty of restaurants nearby. There's a coffee station on the ground floor, but it's unavailable from 10 am until late afternoon. Free wifi in the room was nice and worked great. A computer and printer are available on the ground floor, probably for a fee. The hotel's central location within midtown was great. It's about a 4-minute walk to the Herald Square subway station, which services 8 lines. We could have easily walked to most of the places we went had it not been so cold and windy while we were there. The value was great compared to other midtown hotels that I researched. I booked the hotel directly via their website. The rate was higher than usual due to heavy tourism on weekends in December. I checked back a month before our arrival and found the nightly rate was about $60 less, so I canceled and re-booked. I'd definitely return to Herald Square Hotel if staying in midtown.

“I should have been warned by the other bad reviews” I saw the other bad reviews and thught, boy are they picky. One one who said this is a rough location was correct. It is located cross from a mall the locals call "Gun-Point" what does that tell you? The road is under construction, so getting in was a mess. Once I walked into a vast lobby area it was hard to miss the 150-200 teenage girls that were there for a cheer/dance competition. Should have left then. They were allowing them to practice in the lobby, it was hard to hear the desk clerk while checking in. Once in the room the first night all was okay. The next morning (6:30am) I went to get ready for my day only to find there was no water. I called to the front desk and was told within 30 minutes all should be okay. Well 1 hour later I finally got the manager, his offer was to come downstairs, take a shuttle to the Marriott 5 blocks away, take a shower and shuttle back to the Hilton. I had no choice. I must say the Marriott front desk people were very helpful. That night I was dropped back off at this Hilton only to find out, you gussed it, no water still. The frontdesk people told e, don't worry in 30 minutes we will have water. I had to press the issue to get them to make other hotel arraingments, you guessed it back to the Marriott. More on his later. Upon checking out there was lady at the desk, she was not in typical Hilton garb and did not have aname tag, that was on of the most rue people I have run across in the service business. Hilton has there 100% satisfaction garrantee, I think running around town qualifies for a free night. She thought diffrent and made sure I knew it. The manage approved the free night. She had me sign the zero balance receipt, when I asked for a copy she refused, being here on business I need a copy of every receipt. She gave me attitude when I asked to see the manager, who finally got a receipt. You know I understand the broken water main is not their fault, but they should be understanding that when you check into a hotel you kind of expect to take a shower in the morning and want to go somewhere else when they don't have water at the end of the day. The bottom line is this STAY AWAY FROM THIS LOCATION. Trust me, I wish i had trusted the other reviewers.

“Centrally Located Beautiful Charmer!!!” Located four blocks north of the White House, near Embassy Row, several blocks north of National Mall Monuments and Smithsonian Museums. Key location. Several eateries nearby. Things close down early in this area of DC. National Geographic Museum is one block away. C.O. Bigelow body products and Keurig Gourmet coffees are available in rooms. Decent wi-fi signal in room. Plush towels and comfortable linens. The hotel and our room had exquisite decor and design...very classy. Standard expensive city parking extra. Lobby bar was a nice place to relax with a drink.

“walking distance to terminal” decent airport hotel within walking distance (10min.) to domestic terminal. this is a great advantage, just cross the street and you're almost there. best choice when you have only carry on luggage. no need to wait for shuttle. rooms average with limited views, as windows have never been cleaned from the outside. no fridge nor safe in room. very friendly and accomodating check in staff = 5points. outdoor pool is large = 5points with plenty of towels available. a real downside was room service and what they call signature pizza. don't waste your money on that one. subways next door. overall a good choice for an airport hotel. would stay here again.

“Competent but not spectacular” Boxy rooms are a tad small and generic compared to more luxe members of the chain. Service was excellent. The location is so-so; a longish walk through a variety of office complexes in order to find the heart of the city. Probably the best in town, but a few shades beneath the finer U.S. Four Seasons hotels.

“Nice little place, very convenient” I stayed here for two night son busines inChicago. While my meetings were downtown, and the Willows is in Lincoln Park area, I stayed because theprice was about $200 less per night. The Hotel is on Surf Street in a quiet residential neighborhood, but is very close to shops and restaurants. Also, it is very easy to take the bus downtown and bck uptown at days end. A two dollar bus ride is far better than a twenty dollar cab ride. Over all the hotel is neat and clean and staff very friendly. Would stay here again

“Great service, thin walls” This is a great place to stay if going to SeaWorld. You are literally a mile away and the hotel provides free shuttles to and from SeaWorld (saving parking costs). We made a reservation in the morning for the shuttle and when we returned, the shuttle was waiting for us in the front (I believe they run each half hour between the 2 different Marriott hotel shuttles). The rooms were clean and had a balcony and fridge. My main gripe was our room was located facing the highway side. The noise from the highway was very audible, especially when motorcycles were revving by in the middle of the night. Also (and no fault of the hotel), the people next to us were so loud and they had their baby playing and running until about 2am -- all which we heard through the thin walls. Service was fantastic and everyone seemed friendly and helpful. I thought it was odd to close the bar at 11pm (pool closes at 10:30), but I guess they don't have much business for that in a family friendly place. If you have kids and going to SeaWorld -- I would highly recommend this place to stay!

“Very Good” A return visit to the hotel, for a one night stay. Check-in was quick and efficient and the cookie excellent! The room, an executive on the 24th Floor was clean and spacious -and just along the corridor from the executive lounge. The lounge itself was good, serving complimentary snacks and soft drinks in the evening and breakfast the following morning. Back to my room, I experienced a noise disturbance from the lifts that were adjacent to it and a lack of ammeneties in the bathroom that I had to request from housekeeping. These items were delivered promptly. I needed to know the location of a city store, the concierge was able to direct me there in a matter of seconds. I would definately return to the hotel - but I would request a room away from the lift shafts!

“Very Enjoyable Stay” Check-in was very easy - I had been at the self-serve terminal just a few moments when someone behind the desk came to great me and help me check in. I didn't really need the help as is was fairly straightforward but it was nice to have someone there. I asked a few questions, got my parking stub and received excellent service. The room was nice and bigger than I expected. Actually, there was plenty of room. It was clean, not brand spanking new but not old old either. The location is excellent. I was in town for the Philly Marathon in November and it was perfect. My girlfriend didn't have to go very far to see me running as the hotel is along the race course - she stood on the sidewalk just outside the hotel. It was close enough to the start/ finish line for me. There are great restaurants and shops around. The hotel restaurant is very good; the food and the service was excellent. The elevators were under renovation and that made for long line-ups. We often took the stairs which is not a problem for us but I could see it being a problem for some. I always bring ear plugs when staying elsewhere, but I'd forgotten to bring some and so I went to the front desk and they handed me a pair. I was really impressed by the quality of service - all of the people who work there that I met/ dealt with were great. The main area/ business center is great - plenty of computers with internet access. There was coffee, tea and water. I'd stay there again.

“Perfect in every way” My 1st stay at XV Beacon . I chose it after reading all the good revievs and boked through Platinum Am Ex. This hotel is 5 star in terms of rooms and service. The customer service is the best of any hotel I have stayed from the Lexus car service to room service. And the front desk manager, Mitchel, was attentive to every need including giving us a very lovely upgrade to a corner suite. We were celebrating our 30th wedding anniversary and had dinner at Moo, which was outstanding. Our only complaint was the lag between courses and the long wait for a simple dinner for two. We regularly stay at the Elliott Hotel, the Four Seasons or the Ritz when in Boston. XV Beacon rivaled all of the above and we gladly will return soon.

“I love this hotel” Came to Charlotte for a wedding at the Westin. I love Westins and this hotel was no exception. The facade is totally impessive, really sharp and sleek. Beautiful lobby and pretty intimate and personal for such a large property. Beautiful, room, very typical westin style, contemporary undertstated furniture. no flat screen though. nice view. pretty good gym, however, you have to sign a check-in form which charges your room $5. Thought that was a rip-off, the gym should be free. Had myself a massage, which was good even though the hotel doesn't really have a proper spa. It was just some massage rooms off of the gym, and the men;s room had a sauna and changing area. Great massage. Had breakfast one morning at Ember Grille. Not your typical hotel buffet breakfast- much smaller but more upscale and gourmet. I liked it. I also liked that the city's trolley service stops right at the hotel, nice touch. Overall great hotel, perfect Westin. Would stay here next time in Charlotte.

“Taste of Chicago” The hotel staff were very friendly and competent . The hotel is clean and our room was fine. The location of the hotel is good, it's about a 2 block walk to the red line subway. Breakfast is served from 6-10AM. The breakfast bar is very popular with families. If you plan to eat after 8AM be prepared to deal with a swarm of children.

“No Sleep for the Moroccan” PROS: - Really hip ambiance. It truly does give you a Moroccan feel. - Patrons seemed diverse and interesting - Parking is only $12 with in and out privileges CONS: - I was not excited to have to make my reservation by sending Uno my credit card number via email as that presents fraud/theft issues, but I was unable to get through by phone. - The sheets were really rough (felt like they had been bleached out one too many times) and the duvet felt like it was made out of canvas. The second my boyfriend and I climbed into the bed we looked at each other and said, "Hmmm...Maybe we should have stayed at a Westin with Heavenly Beds" - The lighting in the rooms is REALLY low. It's probably meant to be low to hide the bad paint job and create ambiance, but it is just one notch TOO low. - No good restaurants in the surrounding area. I guess that's what I get for staying in downtown LA, but I was there for a wedding.

“Absolutely Disgusting!” This place is so creepy! The linens are frail. The hotel was extremely noisy and it is located in a very dangerous area in town.
