I was moving across the country and crashed here. Even as a place to sleep, it was problematic. For example, the tub clogged up and was up to my calves with water (even with a quick shower). The air conditioning gave me a soar throat. I believe that there was either mold in the room or it just was not clean. Lastly, there were definitely roaches. The small German type. I was too exhausted to leave and go to another hotel. I slept 5 hours and woke up to a cockroach on me and that was it. We left immediately and drove to El Paso! DO NOT stay at this horrible place! I still cannot believe I did!

“Comfortable Stay” On occasion the Mr. & I have a need to stay overnight in Fort Worth. We've stayed at the Sheraton Fort Worth Hotel & Spa more than once. Each time we've found our room clean & comfortable. We like the location and it's proximity to the Historic Stockyards, restaurants, and TCU. I'm sure we'll be staying at the Sheraton again in the future!

“Nice hotel, good location, friendly service” We spent a night at the Mayflower Park in August. The service was great and everyone was very attentive and very accommodating. We requested a room upgrade, but the hotel was full. However, the front desk clerk gave us coupons for free drinks and appetizers in the lounge. The lounge was great and so were the free drinks and appetizers. The room was really small and the bathroom was tiny, but this is an older hotel. We didn't have time to use the fitness center, but it looked really good for this range hotel - lots of newer equipment, tvs and magazines to make it less tedious, and the air conditioning worked. We'd definitely consider staying at this hotel again.

“Great for a family celebration” I booked three rooms at this hotel for a birthday celebration for my daughter. We had one King Suite, which connected to a Superior Double, plus one Deluxe Double. The rooms, while smallish, feel larger because of the tall ceilings and large windows. Bathrooms were small but nice. This is a historic old hotel, so don't expect the immense bathrooms of modern hotels. Public spaces and corridors are grand and the beautiful hardwood doors to every guest room really make you feel like you are living in the early part of the 20th century. There is also an enclosed heated pool on the roof deck, which my children used and loved. Service was friendly but mediocre. Our rooms were not ready when we arrived and at one point we were told that we might not have access to the rooms until after 5pm. Obviously, that was not acceptable. Room keys did not work in two of the doors, etc. We ate only one meal (breakfast) in the Garden Court, which was nice as was cocktail hour in Maxwells. Despite the small inconveniences, I would stay here again. The rooms are a great value for the location (just a few blocks off Union Square and tons of shopping, restaurants, etc.).

“Sehr gutes Business-und Stadthotel” in Texas ist man es gewöhnt, von der Autobahn abzufahren und in Downtown und am Hotel zu sein. Aber auch den ruhe suchenden deutschen Touristen kann das nicht abhalten, vorausgesetzt, wie in den USA üblich, er möchte sein Zimmerfenster nicht öffnen. Das Hotel hat einen guten Standard mit einigen Extraannehmlichkeiten auf dem Zimmer wie etwa einem Safe der in USA selbst in der First-Class-Kategorie nicht üblich ist. Ein Kühlschrank fehlt wie überall, aber es gibt auf dem Gang einen Automaten und natürlich Eismaschinen. Der Fitnesbereich mit Schwimmbad ist sehr gut. insgesamt ein Tophotel zu angenehmen Preisen, kostenloser Trolleybus nach Downtown und Stockyards, dennoch nicht zentral, besser mit dem Mietwagen fahren.

“DEpressing!” I travel to NYC on biz very frequently. I happened to hit a very busy hotel week without advance booking ... almost every room in the city was selling for $299 plus a night. Decided to take a chance on the $179 room/ night rate for two nights at this hotel. The best features -- 2-block walk from Penn Station for those arriving from Newark on the airport train, and complimentary wireless access. Everything else was dismal. Arrived to find that they could not find my reservation. Stood at the front desk patiently for 20 minutes (with my online reservation confirmation in hand). Seems like they were encountering a communications breakdown with LaQuinta[-] Finally, the (minimally) English-speaking desk clerk handed me a key to my 5th floor room. The typical NYC small room featured: -windows that would not open (and a view of an old brick wall) -noisy window A/C unit that never cooled the stuffy room -a desk too tiny for anyone to work at -scuzzy old green carpeting (suspect for my sneezing & allergy outbreak) -cheap, thin towels The hotel had two slow elevators and a basement fitness room that smelled of sewage. (There was an odd smell throughout the hotel ... like an unemptied grease trap.) I wasn't brave enough to try the breakfast room. (Starbucks and other options a couple blocks away on 5th Avenue.) There was a crowded rooftop bar which was nice for good weather evenings. Just be sure not to accept a room on the 14th floor where the bar traffic was noisy. The neighborhood? Bleak block featuring many Korean restaurants ... but only two blocks to Herald Square (Macy's!). Overall, a depressing place to sleep in NYC -- unless you just need a (relatively) clean bed to sleep for a few hours near Penn Station.

“Good value, but noise issues” If you are sensitive to noise, this is not the place for you. If you don't mind background noise from traffic, planes, trains, the hum of the mini-fridge, and noise from the AC unit, then this is a good value for San Diego. We had a deluxe king room (#205), which was large, well lit and with pleasant decor. The bed was very comfortable, though it had stiff edges. The pillows were mushy. Our room had a large mini-fridge with freezer and a small microwave. The old-fashioned TV also had a DVD player. We had a small sofa with sagging cushions. The bathroom had a toilet, tub shower, and sink. There was a second sink with lots of counter space outside of that room. The shower head had good flow but was placed very low even for people of average height. I had to turn the knob to the maximum for hot to get barely sufficient hot water for the shower. The towels were thin and scratchy. We had some difficulty with the wifi, but generally it worked okay. The continental breakfast was crowded but the food was decent, including waffle maker, hard-boiled eggs, and fruit, along with the usual fare. It's a short stroll to Old Town and its good Mexican restaurants.

“Trendy stay near Union Square” If you like trendy hotels, you'll probably like the Clift. I don't always stay at places with this trendy of a feel, but it was a nice change of pace. I like the location close to Union Square. The rooms and hallway have a cool, older vibe with typical Ames style decor. The room itself was very simple and I found the bed very comfortable. All the staff were very friendly. I'd likely return.

“Great Hotel in Chi-Town!” My husband and I spent our 9th anniversary at the James Hotel. We stayed in a loft suite. The room was very nice. The bed was comfortable. The ammenities were good. The fitness center was very well equipped. I had a massage on site which is a nice perk. We were across the street from Trader Joes which allowed us to stock up on snacks. One of the best things about the James is the David Burke Prime House restaurant. It is one of the best steakhouses I've ever been too. Great food and great service. They made our anniversary special. We liked our experience so much that I planned a team outing in Chicago and had my entire team stay at the James Hotel. They loved it. I got a great rate. And got to stay in a Loft suite again!

“Comfortable and Convenient” I was very fortunate to land a very nice rate at the Crowne Plaza for three nights over President's Day weekend. The room I was in was terrific - well appointed, very large for NYC, great TV, a chaise lounge and an ample-sized bath with nice amenities. I had no issues with noise at all. Hotel staff was very pleasant and non-intrusive. Only small peeve is that the elevators are fairly slow, even though the two elevators banks are split and the elevators themselves are designed to be express It still takes time, especially during peak hours. Do note that there is a charge for wireless Internet. All in all, however, a really superb stay.

“Good for Shopping” Stayed in this hotel in short notice, close to Jackson CTA, rooms clean and good services as printing boarding passes and free wifi. Pub located in The hotel hast really good food and big selection of beers. Anytime again. Room clean also the bath. Quick self check in, first time i did not have to show my Po.

“Unique accommodation in the best part of Houston” I am a native Houstonian who moved away many years ago. When I go back to visit my family, it's easier to stay in a hotel. While Houston has a lot of hotels (all the major chains are well-represented), they seem to be located either downtown or in the congested Galleria-area or (shudder!) out in the sticks. I found the Modern B&B here on TripAdvisor and I was immediately intrigued both by the modern style and the Expobar espresso machine. I don't typically stay in b&b's because I am allergic to the overly frou-frou'd decor that you tend to find in the average b&b. The Modern B&B, fortunately, is far from typical. My SO and I booked one of the larger rooms with access to a private deck. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The room was much larger than a typical hotel room and had adequate desk space and free Wi-Fi for my boyfriend to work. The bathroom was also very large and had two sinks and a great walk-in shower (with fantastic water pressure). Breakfast was served around 8am each morning and consisted of a hot quiche or frittata along with fresh fruit, cereal, yogurt, juice and coffee. You can make your own cappuccino or espresso. My boyfriend loved the fruit smoothies. We enjoyed talking with Lisa, the owner, and the other guests at breakfast, too. The b&b is in a great part of Houston (IMO), inside the Loop and convenient to the best restaurants and attractions. I was literally no more than 15 minutes from all the places I like to go. Parking is really easy, either in the driveway of the b&b or on the next street. I would heartily recommend the Modern B&B and look forward to my next stay!!

“Great hotel, outstanding service!” Great Kimpton hotel that needs to be ranked higher on Trip Advisor!! It really is a great location as it is one block to neat P street area and a quick walk to both DuPont Circle and convention center area. Lots of great restaurants nearby. Service here is second to none!! Will be back again soon.

“Nice, new hotel” Just stayed in this hotel over Labor Day weekend and was very pleased. As a convention center hotel, it didn't seem very busy as we expected for a holiday weekend. Others have indicated it is off the beaten path, which we didn't find to be a problem since it is a nice stroll or river taxi ride to all the Riverwalk restaurants and shopping. As Diamond Gold Passport members, we were upgraded (without asking) to a "Grand Suite," which consisted of 2 connecting rooms, one of which had a bed, bathroom, lounge chair desk and TV, the other had a large Queen sofa bed, coffee table, full bathroom, desk and TV. Having the extra bathroom and TV worked out nicely traveling with our teenage daughter. Suite was on the 21st floor with nondescript city view. Soundproofing was very good. Our bedroom was adjacent to a mechanical room that was quite noisy in the hall, but we couldn't hear a thing inside our room. The Grand Club on the 23rd floor was very nice and has a great view of the Tower of the Americas. Their coffee machine is the best I've seen at a Hyatt. It is very fast and offers a nice variety of latte, espresso, capuccino coffees. They keep refrigerators stocked with water, soft drinks and juices to help yourself to throughout the day with an honor bar in the evening. Breakfast was a nice assortment of pastries, bagles, and fresh fruit. Huge cookies were offered mid day with cold hors d'ouvres and delicious desserts in the evening. We found the service at the hotel to be excellent. You can find some great offer codes for this and other San Antonio properties at the San Antonio Convention & Visitors Bureau website: visitsanantonio.com.

“Nice and comfy” We lucked out with Priceline and got this hotel for about half the cheapest Hyatt website price. Asked for a nonsmoking king on upper floor and got it! First room had so much "air freshener" sprayed in it that we couldn't handle it. Didn't even unpack. When I called the front desk, they were great and offerred to send a bellman up with the key to another room one floor higher which she thought might not be as perfumey. The second room was great. No perfumey deodorizer, just clean. They need to tell the maids to take it easy with that stuff. Some of us are allergic and those windows do not open! Anyway, after that we loved the room. Every time I called for something they were super nice and always asked what else we needed. Nice! We used the pool area and at first it was nice and quiet until two couples showed up with two 18packs of canned beer and I thought to myself, surely the Hyatt is not going to allow this. But, apparently they did. Kind of tacky letting people bring in giant cases of own beer into the pool area. Reminded me of a frat party or something. Just not what you would expect. Parking is expensive for Phoenix, $15.00 for 24 hours, but since it was the weekend, we lucked out and managed to find parking meters which are free weekends and didn't have to pay. Honestly, though, even if I had payed the Hyatt website price for this hotel, I would not have been dissapointed with the room. I just wish they could monitor the pool a little more. Those people were a little obnoxious. The front desk clerks deserve high praise for being very nice and very helpful... Would stay there again.

“Expected nice but the Bristol was much better” We arrived in early morning and went by hoping to be able to drop off luggage. We were upgraded to a nicer room which was already available. Everything was uphill from there. Staff bent over backwards to be helpful, room was very large for an older hotel and it was so renovated that it was impossible to tell that it was older. Location was perfect as we usually hate to drive on vacation. Location was 1-block from the bus stops, even the bus from the airport which beats renting a car and paying for parking. About a block from the trolley stop and the Transit Store was right on the corner. Buy a 4-day pass for bus & trolley for $15. Service in San Diego is great for a Western City. The Greyhound Station was across the street but almost unnoticeable. There were a few non-aggressive transients around but no more that the rest of downtown. Many fine restaurants within reasonable walking distance-in fact we think this was the best possible downtown location an a great hotel to boot.

“Disappointed. I won't be back.” While the hotel is in a great location the service the hotel provides need drastic improvement. I arrived at the hotel via taxi with an unusual amount of baggage. There was no bellman to assist me from the taxi to check in with my bags. In fact, the doorman at the hotel was ushering others into my taxi before I could even remove all of my personal belongings. I'm a HHonors Gold member and proceeded to the dedicated check in area. I was quickly checked in and told that I had been upgraded and would receive a free "breakfast". After I was checked in the front desk attendant asked if I needed help with my bags. I said I did. He called down to the bell desk and the guy looked around and saw my bags and rolled his eyes. Not what I would consider good service. He reluctantly took my bags to my room. The "upgraded" room had a decent view of the city. However, the room itself needed an overhaul. The space between the door and the floor was so large I had to place the bathrobes to keep sound out and allow a little more privacy. The bath towels were old and tattered. The room itself just seemed "ok". I went to get a snack out of the mini bar and the Pringles I wanted to eat had already been opened by someone before me. The next day I went to Starbucks to redeem my free "breakfast". When I have stayed at other Hilton properties I have always received more than a certificate to redeem at the lobby Starbucks. The hotel did not provide complimentary internet either. I'm loyal to Hilton but will not return to this property.

“Excellent stay!” I came to San Francisco for vacation June 25-29, 2012. We had a great stay at the Palomar and would highly recommend it to others! It is in a great location located close to shopping, food, and transportation (BART, bus line). The hotel staff was also wonderful! They were very approachable, friendly, accommodating, and helpful. We had an early flight from Pittsburgh, and arrived 5 hours prior to check-in. They checked us in with no problem and even recommended a place for lunch.When it came to check out, we had a later flight so they stored our bags for us until we were ready to head to the airport. If you have the time, I would highly recommend participating in the running program they have set up (7 AM Monday through Friday). I participated in it one day, and wish I had done it more than once! I had a great workout and beautiful run along the Embarcadero. Also, each morning they have coffee, tea, and 4 different newspapers on the 5th floor. In the lobby, they have complimentary water and/or iced tea. I absolutely loved this! The pineapple and strawberry flavored waters were my favorite.

“Excellent service and location” We flew into Philadelphia en route to Las Vegas on Sat 19 December, and a scheduled 2 hour layover turned into 2 days - thanks to 22+ inches of snow. As soon as it became clear we were going nowhere on the Saturday afternoon, our search for a hotel started with the airport Marriott. With no rooms available there, we managed to get into the downtown Marriott and after a slow, snowy train journey arrived at Market East station, just a block away from the hotel. Check-in was very efficient (not surprisingly there were a good dozen or more similarly stranded passengers arriving at the same time), and our room clean and comfortable. A refurbisnment is probably due, but no complaints and, as ever, a comfortable Marriott bed. The 24/7 7-eleven right across the street was a godsend as a combination of jetlag and trying to rearrange flights led to an early start (4.30) the next day. With no hope of escape we rebooked for the Sunday, and the hotel proved an excellent location from which to explore dowtown Philadelphia. Food options were somewhat limited, as the blizzard compromised staffing levels at the hotel and elsewhere (many restaurants remained closed). On the Monday morning, breakfast buffet was unavailable for this reason, and we had the cooked breakfast - a good call, and one of the better breakfasts I have had in the US. Facilities were good for a city centre hotel, with a pool (somewhat bizzarely on the 7th floor) and gym. There is an in-hotel sundries shop, adjacent Kinko's and Starbucks, and Macy's is just 100 yards away. With its proximity to the Reading Terminal market and rail station (though we caught a cab back to the airport - flat-rate a reasonable $28.50), I would certainly choose to stay here again if visiting Philadelphia, and we were quite pleased in the end that we had not been able to get in at the airport hotel. Hotel staff were friendly and efficient throughout, and the service much appreciated - I can't imagine their journeys to and from work were much fun that weekend.

“贅沢空間” 一人旅で訪れ、5泊しました。部屋から自由の女神がばっちり見えてこれぞニューヨーク、眺めは完璧でした。ミッドタウンから離れているので、どうしても不便を感じてしまいますが、セントラルパークのリッツカールトンに比べると随分お値段がリーズナブルなので、私は多少キャブ代がかさんでも予算内でこんな豪華な部屋でリラックスできるなら十分に価値があると感じました。とはいえ、地下鉄の駅も歩いてすぐ近くにあるので、便利といえば便利ですね。喧騒から離れて部屋で落ち着いて過ごしたい人には向いていると思います。ただ、ホテル内のレストランはおすすめできないのでお食事は外で済ませたほうがいいと思います。マンハッタン内には朝食から夕食そして深夜食まで、星の数ほどレストランやカフェやダイナーもあるので問題はないのかな、と思います。レイトチェックアウトも快く承諾してくださってさすが世界のリッツカールトンだな、と好印象だらけで大満足です。

“Excellent choix, confortable, très central et économique” Que je ne regrette pas d'avoir choisi cet hôtel!! Je trouve d'ailleurs certaines critiques injustes, tout comme son classement sur ce site (80e sur 248 au jour de cette critique), car vraiment je suis enchanté de mon séjour de 6 nuits, pour lequel j'ai profité d'une promotion sur Hotels.com (moins de 45 € la nuit en chambre simple avec douche et toilettes, petit-déjeuner compris, ce qui pour un pays comme les Etats-Unis où l'hôtellerie est chère, est vraiment une bonne affaire). C'est un hôtel récent, ouvert en 2006, et ça se sent, tout y est neuf, propre et moderne. Ma chambre ne donnait pas sur la rue et était très calme, en plus d'être confortable, j'y ai très bien dormi. Pas très grande, mais j'ai apprécié d'y avoir la douche et les toilettes, tout comme un grand bureau, un frigo, un coffre-fort, pas mal de rangements et une belle télé à écran plasma. C'était par ailleurs très propre. Le personnel d'étage passe deux fois par jour: en fin de matinée et en fin d'après-midi, et vous laisse même deux petits chocolats à la menthe sur votre lit au deuxième passage! Autre attention, on m'a glissé sous ma porte une invitation à un verre de vin et de champagne offert par la maison un soir lors de mon séjour aux clients de l'hôtel. La situation dans San Francisco est excellente, notamment par rapport aux transports en commun (stations de bus, de BART, de métro, de tramway et de cable-car, toutes à moins d'une rue!), on peut aller partout! On est en plein quartier commerçant, on y trouve donc plein d'endroits pour manger ou faire du shopping, vraiment un super quartier, et en 30 minutes direct de l'aéroport avec le BART. A la réception, je ne peux pas dire que j'ai trouvé le personnel particulièrement chaleureux ni même distant, l'accueil y était plutôt fonctionnel. Quant au petit-déjeuner, il est servi dès 7h, mais surtout n'y allez pas aussitôt, car on le trouve dans une minuscule salle au 5e étage et on y est très vite à l'étroit. On y mange pas, il n'y a pas la place, ni même de chaise pour s'asseoir, on vient pour se servir et on rapporte dans sa chambre sur un plateau tout ce qu'on veut. Mais ça part assez vite, et je n'ai pas l'impression que ce qui est parti soit remplacé. D'où une certaine affluence dès 7h. J'ai essayé d'y aller à 7h15, et ça avait l'air une heure idéale: les gens qui sont venus dès 7h sont repartis dans leur chambre, il y a donc de la place pour "circuler", et il reste encore pas mal de choses. Et ce qu'on y trouve est bon, très frais et de qualité. Un bon choix de boissons (café, thé, jus d'orange, jus de pomme et - miracle!- du chocolat chaud), un grand plateau avec de succulents muffins à ne surtout pas rater, plein de toasts et des bagels. Mais les bagels partent très vite, car ils sont bons et il n'y en a pas beaucoup. On peut faire toaster ce qu'on veut, il y a deux grille-pains. Enfin, il y a de la confiture, du beurre et du fromage à tartiner, mais je n'en ai pas trouvé tous les matins. En tout cas, j'étais très content de ces petits-déjeuners, très nourrissants, il faut juste prendre le coup pour y aller à la bonne heure et ramener son repas dans sa chambre. Et d'une façon générale, je suis ravi d'avoir choisi cet hôtel et le conseille à tout le monde!

“Keith made us feel so welcome....excellent hotel” We were greeted on our arrival by Keith, who seemed to be working the front desk most of our stay. He greeted us by name and made us feel so welcome throughout our stay. We are a platinum member and received a room upgrade...nice room. Also many Staybridge hotels we have stayed in have no covered drive through (to check in)...this one did, which was convenient when we check in during a rain storm). We took advantage of the fitness center (nice) and laundry facilties (complimentary). This Staybridge is definately upscale, and we plan on staying here again when we visit Memphis again. Oh, shopping & restaurants were all close by and they provide a complimentary shuttle.
“Beautiful downtown hotel.” Easily accessible location, close to subway, shopping and the magnificent 9/11 memorial.

“Nice location with added extra's makes this property a good choice!” I was booked into this hotel by my client, I had been to DC several times before for assignments but usually stay in Crystal City. This is my first time at this hotel and I must say I'm impressed, upon entering the hotel. Nice lobby and helpful staff for checkin. I was worn out after canceled flights and was happy to see the cafe across from the front desk. I found a good selection of meals burgers, salads and sandwiches and the prices seemed fair. I cant really comment on the room cost as my bill was covered by my client so I have no idea about the value of the rooms but the food at the bar and cafe was inline. The rooms were quite somewhat newly updated and were nice, clean. Rooms were not super large but still nice size for one. Coffee maker in the room and a well designed and useful bathroom with Avada products. I was actually working at the convention center but my agency had a newsroom set-up downstairs (lowest level) and the rooms seemed nice and the service folks downstairs were awesome making sure we always had sodas and ice. While I spent evenings working on the lower level I spent the days at the convention center. I found the walk to the Metro to be easy, while not close its not far either. The walk allowed me to scout places I wanted to eat later on and there;s plenty of cool things to check out. The ride to the Convention Center was not too bad, much closer than from Crystal City. The best thing I found about this hotel was a great breakfast upstairs (healthy options) and I even had a nice hot dinner there one night, this is a reward lounge so check in to that, this came with my stay but for others you need to ask for access to this lounge upstairs. Overall a good stay at a nice location.

“Great 5 star hotel” Stayed over the Xmas new years break. Rate was $79. this is an outstanding hotel with great clean rooms, good tv, good clock, nice bathroom. The fitness center is phenomenal and free. The staff was great. There was an enterprise rental car on site. The staff was great. I thought I would have the hotel all to my own but a youth groupnwas there but all was handled excellently. Hotel was quiet. Can walk to the mall and all the stores and right next store to convention center. This is one good place to stay.

“Nice location, comfortable hotel” I only stayed 1 night while on a business trip. The location is great as it's located right downtown close to the stadium and many nice restaurants. Upon check in I was greeted by a very friendly front desk staff. The room was clean and comfortable. They charged $12.49 for internet access which I still think should be included in the room rate. I did clock the internet speed at 2Mbps down and 0.7Mbps up. I had banana pancakes for breakfast which were kind of pricey, but really good.

“Perfect Location! Super Friendly Staff!” What a great 4 day stay I had in this hotel in a perfect location. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful throughout my stay. Donna from Sales was out every morning at breakfast greeting people and making sure that everything was ok with their accommodations. This location is one of the best in the city--2 blocks away from Michigan Ave. and about 4 blocks away from Rush St. Also right across the street from Rosebud Steak House which is a staple in Chicago. Like most Residence inns, this hotel is extremely convenient. No frills but none needed by me. Fitness room is adequate with pretty good equipment. But if the weather is nice go run on the lake. It's only 2 blocks away as well. I HIGHLY RECCOMMEND!

“First-rate experience” We had a wonderful experience here. My wife and I booked a room on a May weekend for a mere $79 a night, an absolutely fantastic deal given the 4-star amenities and convenient Capitol Hill Location. We arrived on a red-eye flight from the west coast early in the morning and were very thankful to have access to our room a full six hours before the standard check in time; after a blissful nap we were ready to see the city! The rooftop pool was a great bonus after a muggy day of sightseeing.

“Very nice hotel” I stayed at the Hilton for 5 days and was very pleased with the hotel. Received a free room upgrade upon checking in as well as 2 bottles of water. I also given coupons for breakfast based on my Hilton Honors membership. The room was very nice, with a view of the city. Housekeeping staff was extremely efficient. There is a good Japanese restaurant in the hotel which is definitely worth checking out. Plus the hotel is very centrally located, only a couple of blocks from the Powell street station. A couple of days, I came back late in the evening and even though I saw some homeless people on the streets, the neighborhood seemed pretty safe. The only negetive comment is about the Concierge desk. The Citiscape (the restaurant at the topmost floor of the hotel with a breathtaking view of the city) was closed for a private party so I asked the Concierge for suggestions about a dining place. He was not at all helpful and it was a good thing that I knew the neighborhood as he did not give any directions. He was more interested in getting back to his computer. I am going back to the hotel again in July - this time with my husband.

“Great Motor Hotel!” We only stayed for 2 nights but I loved the room. It was very comfortable and centrally located (if you have a car its only 10 minutes away from the main area and the beach) but if you don't have a car don't stay here. The best: ice cream vending

“Disappointing lack of professionalism” I booked this hotel with great expectations. I had family visiting from outside the country and wanted them to have a good experience in Chicago. Upon arriving to the hotel (at the exact time I indicated in my reservation) I was told I’ve been “downgraded” to a lesser quality room. I travel very often and never had this before. Moreover, I did not hear a single “I’m sorry”, it was like usual business. What bothered me the most was that the receptionist kept telling me “I will decrease the rate for you” “what do you think, nice eh?” like he was doing me a favor!!!! They decreased the rate to that of the rooms they gave us of course (which is the legal thing to do, since I am sure is illegal to charge me for one room and give me a lesser value one for the same money). They did not care that I wanted higher level room independent of value. I did not know what to say, since this never happened to me before, also with family present did not want to start arguing. The rooms were nice (not as nice as I thought) and location is good, however be aware that they might not honor your reservation and not even apologize for this. That is enough for me not to go back again.

“Nice rooms” We chose the hotel due to its proxinity to the convention center, and its prices (it cost less than the conference's official hotel, the Hilton, even with the conference's special rate). We were "upgraded" to a small suite, which was nice, though it also put us on the second floor, closer to the noise (especially the piped 40 and 50s era music which can be loud at times) in the enclosec courtyard/atrium area where the registration desk, bar and restaurant are located. Also, our view was of the back of the hotel's main sign; we did have a partial view of nearby Minute Maid park. The room was comfortalbe, with wood paneling, and the bathroom modern and spacious, with separate shower and shower/bathtub facilities. TV in the room was large. Bed comfortable. We did not need parking; it costs a little over $20 a day. As noted, there are not many restaurants within easy walking distance, though we walked and used the hotel's shuttle to get to some stores and a restaurant. Prices in the hotel's restaurant and bar were high, as you would expect in a hotel, though the tomato soup with garlic bread was a good deal at $6. We never did get around to eating at the high-priced steak house (also had fish) next to the hotel. There was one PC for customer use in the lobby area. The "concierge" area was the front desk. Service there was uneven. In some cases, especially with seemingly more experienced personnel, there was a wiligness to quickly get you any info you needed, while in a couple of cases a request for info, such as regarding busses or airport shuttles, was met with a quizzical look and a suggestion they could get me a phone number to call myself. There was no game on at Minute Maid Park during our stay but I took the $9 guided tour, given 3 times a day, and enjoyed it more than I expected. There is not much in the way of attractions in the area, other than the park (and the convention center). To get to/from the airport, your options are taxis or shuttle services (though, as noted, it can be difficult to get info about the shuttles, which are not always cheaper than taxis for more than one person, anyway). You can catch a city bus, or light rail, within a 5-10 minute walk from the hotel. We took a bus down to the space center (an hour each way). The area around the hotel did seem safe, even at night.

“Excellent” Very impressed! Recently renovated corner room #712 was very spacious and had excellent views north and west over the Fox backlot all the way to the Pacific. Everything was very well maintained and very clean. Service throught was refined, prompt and professional. Relatively convenient location (as long as you have a car or can use the hotel's compimentary car) is close to Beverly Hills & West Hollywood. We chose this area over Hollywood and after seeing Hollywood Blvd., we were very happy that we chose this location. Hollywood Blvd. still has a long way to go and is very touristy and still seedy. Hotel has complimentary Town Car drop off/pick up within 1.5 mile radius up until 10:00 PM. Spa area was great. Hotel is within walking distance of Westfield Century City mall, which was much nicer than the Beverly Center. Great selection of shops and nice restaurants in a pleasant outdoor setting. We did not eat at the hotel but had excellent dinners at Angelini Osteria, Angeli Caffe & Mastro's Steakhouse. I'm extremely fussy and I would not hesitate to stay here again for the right price.

“Good hotel, good location.” I stayed here at the end of March for the weekend. I got a great rate of $60/night on Priceline. For the price it was excellent. The location was perfect for me. It’s only a few blocks from Bart so I took Bart to the hotel from the airport. It’s right next to the gorgeous Ferry Building that has an awesome farmer’s market on weekends. Don’t miss it. It is walking distance to Union Square and I even walked to Fisherman’s Warf and the Haight from there (well I like walking). The room was pretty small, but it was fine for one person. Two people with two large suit cases would have been a little cramped. I didn’t have much of a view because I had a cheap Priceline room, but I didn’t care because I was gone all day long. The bed was comfy and the bathroom was nice. Had to wait almost 2 hours for my room to be ready but I came early and it was ready by their official check-in time. However, they didn’t seem to do much to hurry and get it made up for me since I was waiting. This was a little annoying but , oh well. I asked the front desk people if I had the smallest room and they said no, they had smaller ones. Room was relatively clean and when I asked for more towels, service was prompt. Didn’t use the YMCA, but heard it was really nice. Overall, a nice hotel with small rooms. I would stay there again especially at $60/night!

“Great location! Overall, a nice place.” I stayed here while traveling for business. Location was right downtown in “the loop”. Cost of standard room w/taxes was about $230 per night + an addtl $40 per day for parking. You can go in and out as many times as you want to but you have to get your parking pass validated by the hotel. I stayed 2 nights. The 1st night I tried to exit and my ticket was “invalid” so I had to call attendant who let me out, told me to have hotel revalidate a new ticket which I did. The next day, I tried to exit with my new ticket and once again, couldn’t. Not sure what the problem was but was frustrating. Rooms were clean for the most part with the exception of a few stray blacks hairs matted against outside of shower stall. Shower itself was clean and spacious. Counters had ample space. Their bath towels were the nicest, newest, thickest towels I’ve ever seen in a hotel. I disliked the lack of accessible plugs for laptop and phone. All plugs were under tables and behind things. Also, no bags in any of the trash cans was kind of weird. Those are small things though. Overall, this hotel was nice and is in a great location.

“Amazing Views” First of all, there are 2 Marriots in downtown and we showed up at the one in the gas lamp and tried to check in, ophs, happens alot I think, This part of San Deigo is a bit sleepier, not as many resturaunts around, its close to the harbor which if you want to walk or run, is a perfect place. Our room was very nice, clean and modern and ofcourse the view was killer. Our big disappointment was that the pool we closed for renovation, darn!

“Great Place to Stay Downtown” We had a great stay at the Courtyard, Downtown Indianapolis in October 2007. The location was perfect for our desire to explore downtown on foot. The capitol building was gorgeous! The walk on the canal is beautiful and relaxing. Our room was spacious, clean, comfortable, and attractive. The wonderful bed and pillows provided a great night's sleep! The public areas are clean and well-maintained. The parking was $12 a day. The only thing free in the morning was the coffee and a piece of fruit. I generally like to stay where a free breakfast is provided but didn't think that would be an issue for a city the size of Indianapolis; however, we did not find many places to have breakfast nearby, and what we found was as pricey as the Courtyard's buffet. Next time, we will either pay for the buffet or price compare with the Residence Inn across the parking lot which charges more for a room but does provide a free breakfast. All in all, the Couryard is a great find. Many of the other downtown hotels charge much more, and comparatively speaking, we received good value for our money. We will probably return.

“A Rose in A Dung Heap” Houston has no luxury hotels which is a real shame. The Four Seasons downtown was built at a time when bathrooms were small and ceilings were low, so no matter what they try to do to update the property, it just does not work. Other hotels have a traget market that does not encourage luxury. Indeed, Houston is not much of a vacation destination and its convention business tends toward the less affluent travelers who attend the gun shows, religious conventions, and oil industry events that predominate Houston's convention calendar. In year's past, there have been rumors of a Ritz Carlton coming to downtown Houston, but that has not happened. Instead, some boutqiue hotels have opened that are trendy, but lacking in service and business amenities. The best of the worse in this city is the St. Regis Hotel which was once a Ritz Carlton. The rooms have been updated and they are very nice and suprerb butler service is available in the suites. Rooms are comofrtable with large furniiture, flat screens, and nice mini bars. The food is reliable and room service is prompt and courteous. The bar is infamous. It is beautiful with dark wood and nice furniture and there are plenty of seats at the bar. The barman has been at the property for years and he is one of the best in Houston. The bar is an excellent place to make a new friend for the evening and there is live music on the weekends when you can meet new friends who can dance. There is tea in the lobby if you go in for that sort of thing. Do not expect to see any of the ladies from the bar at tea. Afternoon tea has a different audience. The bellmen and valets are excellent. They recall your name and they are quick to retrieve your car even if you misplace your ticket. The pool is very nice but the fintess center needs work. In fact, it is not really a fitness center at all. Instead, they have a couple of treadmills and a couple of elipticals and a bike overlooking the pool. They would do well to build a real fitness center some day. The location is very good--just inside the loop in the Galleria area. But, the property is located near an active railroad track, so make sure to ask for a room on the front side of the hotel if you are a light sleeper. The St. Regis Houston makes up fro its shortcomings with top notch service. The people who work there genuinely seem to care about your comfort and they act as if they want your business.

“Nice Small Bouquet hotel” This was a nice little hotel in a nice little area of Chicago. The rooms are nice and a good size and the beds are great. Nice bedding and really well done. Great sleep. It's not noisy though the room right next the the elevator can hear the constant ring of the elevator all night. The buffet for breakfast is a little small and there isn't a real restaurant but there is a great breakfast place just down the street. The staff were nice and accommodating.

“Not our favorite by any means” We only paid $85 a night because we bought the room through an 'on-line auction site' so we really can't complain at that price. But, had we paid full price (around $250 a night) we would have been VERY disappointed. I believe that every hotel room should have two chairs. Who wants to sit on the edge of a bed to have a conversation? That is what you have to do at the Allegro because there is only one desk chair in the whole room - even though there is room for another one. We thought the decor was cold and unwelcoming, there wasn't enough surface space to put 'things', leaving guests to totally live out of their opened suitcases, which had to lay on the floor because there was no other place to put them. The bathroom was very small with no counterspace. There was no coffee maker and we never found any drinking glasses. In the closet was a leopard print number that you could purchase for about $50. Never saw anything like that before. We had a horrible view of crumbled buildings and we noticed that there were hardly any guests to be seen in the common areas. On the plus side - we arrived at 7:30 a.m. and they let us have access to our room at that time. We figured that we would have to store our luggage until 1:00 pm but, luckily, that wasn't the case. Also, the internet service is free. Generally, the Allegro is trying to be artsy-fartsy, hip and unique but we thought it mostly just looked a little bit tacky.

“For the price ($140), an excellent value” My husband and I stayed here from 5/13 to 5/16 for a long weekend. We got the room from bidding on Priceline. All the rooms have great views, and for a New York hotel room it is extremely spacious. Our room had a king-sized bed, a sofa, a writing desk, and plenty of room to walk around, with a great view of the Chrysler building. The staff was extremely friendly, despite our many requests at check-in. Only some rooms have high-speed internet access, so check ahead if this is important to you. Although this is ranked as a four-star hotel on Priceline, it is certainly not the Ritz; the bathroom, though clean, was a little shabby. However, for the price we got, this was a great value, and the hotel is really very nice. The location is also not bad. It is far east side of midtown, but we took cabs many places, and it is not that expensive. We'd definitely stay here again.

“Pretty good...had a nice stay” I can't say I had a lot of complaints about this hotel. After staying at the Crescent for a week (business mixed with pleasure) I have looked at previous reviews and I find them to be a little too harsh. I will break it down by good and bad: Good - Lobby and grounds are pretty and well kept. If you drive you will find they have ample free parking. The pool area is relaxing and quiet, and there are several benches and shaded areas to sit. Tennis courts and workout facilities are nice. Everything is clean and the landscaping is pretty. The conference rooms where we had our meetings were spacious and kept at a comfortable temperature. They did a good job of having coffee and snacks available at all times. The rooms-comfortable and large enough to suit me. I did not think the decor was "dated" as so many stated. The balcony is too small to sit out on. The beds were great. The wireless worked fine. The room was clean enough but I have seen cleaner. Don't get me wrong- it was fine. I wished they would have vacumed but not a huge deal. They cleaned the bathroom well each day. I did not think the bathroom tile looked dated...I thought it was fine and I have seen much worse. Room service was prompt. The staff was friendly enough but I barely interacted with them. Bad - Very little negative to say. I would stay here again. My biggest complaint is beyond the control of the hotel--I just didn't care for the location. I would have liked to have been closer to Scottsdale and it is quite a hike. Other than that, you are right by 17 which will take you anywhere. Traffic can be congested near this hotel. I also thought the hotel cafe was kind of bland considering the high prices they charge but that is very typical of many hotels. I would not spend $17 for their breakfast. A real balcony with room to sit would have been appreciated. Other than that, this is a very nice hotel.

“Great location, Not so great room/ hotel ....” Cannot fault the location of this hotel - within 2 mins walking you are in Times Square. So perfect if you are not going to be using the hotel room very often. The hotel reception is a bit deceiving to the rest of the hotel. The Reception looks new and modern.... But the hotel rooms are far from that. The pictures on websites really are deceiving. There was one lift in operation whilst we was there, which was slow and we waited ages for it each time we wanted to get to our room. We were awoken most nights by the loud traffic passing outside our room. The room was clean..... But ODD! Cant seem to describe what it was, but definetly not what i expected at all. The shower didnt work... each time we used it, it flooded the entire bathroom. The sink taps wouldnt turn completely off. This hotel is ideal, if you just wish to use it for basics!!

“I thought it was great!” This hotel has to be the bargain of the century! You have to monitor the website as they are constantly relooking their rates and offer ongoing specials. We ended up with great king rooms for around $75 a night. Check-in was easy and the service great. We were hours early but they made a plan to find us a room. The room wasn’t huge, but was well appointed. Honour Bar, bathrobe, upmarket toiletries and generous wine tastings in the evening were really nice touches. Plus the reception organised early morning airport cabs that actually arrived on time! Location is great, a block from the cable car stop, a block or two from Union Square shopping, and walking distance to many restaurants, shops and all services you’d need. Negatives? Agree with other reviewers: Spotty internet, the 5am garbage pick-up, and a little worn round the edges. But on the whole, a big thumbs up from us!

“Best location for airport travel” Clean, spacious hotel rooms. Very convenient to airport for early morning flights. Shuttle service only stops at 2 other hotels, rather than the larger routes most other hotels use. We upgraded to the parking package so that we could leave our car for 14 days. Shuttle service from airport to hotel runs every 30 minutes. We had no trouble getting back. There was no one at the front desk when we arrived, and we had to wait for ~20 minutes. Clean hotel. Breakfast "buffet" in the morning. Weill stay again.

“Posizione centrale” abbiamo soggiornato tre notti. l'hotel è una struttura un pò vecchiotta ma complessivamente ben tenuta. siamo arrivati dopo alcune ore di un nubifragio e, forse impegnati nell'allagamento della fitness room, all'arrivo non hanno praticamente dato retta alla nostra auto. ci siamo così arrangiati... ho portato l'auto al parcherggio del prudential center a 50 metri sfruttando un coupon stampato da casa e risparmiando più del 50 % sull'esoso costo del parcheggio.. il collegamento ad internet, forse perchè eravamo l'ultima camera al fondo di un corridoio, non ha mai funzionato con regolarità. la stanza è sufficientemente grande e l'hotel è situato in ottima posizione nell'esclusivo quartiere di back bay, comodo alla copley sq e alla metropolitana, la zona è molto sicura e comoda è anche la vicinanza del prudential

“Absolute Luxury” It was our 10th wedding Anniversary and I wanted to do something special for my beautiful wife so I booked a room at the St. Regis for one night on the Friday of Memorial Day weekend. I booked the Astor Suite for our stay. I also booked a custom massage for my wife and myself. The Concierge was able to get us a dinner reservation at Daniel and everything was in place for a wonderful trip. We drove in from Connecticut and arrived at the St. Regis at 12:15 p.m.. We took advantage of the valet parking and our bags were taken care of smartly by the very professional doormen working the sidewalk. We we're greeted very warmly and we followed the porter inside to the magnificent lobby. We proceeded to guest registration to check-in. I was greeted warmly by the woman checking us in and she told us because of our early arrival, our room was still occupied. However, she said she had a very nice room for us, a very, very, nice room. She handed me the key cards to our room and we were shown around the hotel by a very charming young woman. We were then taken to the elevator and we proceeded to the 18th floor. We got off the elevator went through the french doors, turned left and proceeded to the end of the hall and there was our room. Room 1803 is also known as the Imperial Suite and we were led inside by our butler. The Imperial Suite was gorgeous. You walk into a marble floored foyer with fresh flowers in a vase on the table. We turned left and proceeded to a beautiful bedroom with french antiques and crystal chandalier over the bed. The marble master bathroom was exquisite and spacious. On the other side of the foyer was the living room with two large circular windows. The oval window looked out to the west on 5th Avenue and the Peninsula Hotel across the Avenue. The other round window faced north with a breathtaking view up 5th Avenue with the trees of Central Park verdant in the distance. Next to the living room was an elegant dining room with a six foot round mahogany table surrounded by six elegant chairs. Off the dining room was a full kitchen with granite countertops. Beyond the dining room was a rich paneled study in the most handsome, masculine wood with a beautiful wood desk and chair. The Imperial Suite also had a total of two and one half baths, four flat screen TVs, crystal chandaliers in every room and luxurious empire furniture. I kidded my wife that I felt like french royalty in this fabulous suite. I could have sat on the padded window seat looking out over Central Park for hours. We left and walked over to MoMA. After about three hours at MoMA, we returned and dressed in only our slippers and robes went down to the Spa and were treated royally with our massages. My masseuse was wonderful. My wife reported that her masseur was also fantastic. We returned to our suite and I decided to take a bath. It was a perfect compliment to the massage. I was totally relaxed. We got dressed for dinner and the doorman hailed us a cab and we were whisked away to Daniel for dinner. What a fabulous restaurant. The food, the presentation and the service were all incredible. After dinner, we decided to walk back to the hotel since it wasn't that far and it was a beautiful spring evening in the city. We returned to the St. Regis and walked into the King Cole Bar for a drink. After a round of Red Snappers and catching up with my cousin the artist and musician who met us there, I told my cousin that he had to see our room. He had been to many 5 star hotels throughout Europe and he said he had never seen such a great suite. After he left, my wife and I sat on the padded window seat and took in the city from our big round window. The bed was like sleeping on a cloud and our bedroom was quiet and peaceful. We awoke the next morning and unfortunately had to check out. What a fabulous experience. We will never forget our stay at the St. Regis

“My New Place in the D” Now I can say I will stay here again, We had a king size room and we had plenty of room to spread out. The bathroom was nice size also with a two shower head. The location was great one block from the people mover so this helped us get around. Staff was friendly and I called the front desk the morning of checkout and I asked for a later checkout and they granted me another hour. Parking was $25.00 with end and out privileges. A well put together hotel in Detroit.

“Go Somewhere Else” I stayed 3 or 4 nights at this hotel in September 2003 for a convention and it was dissappointing. The pictures on the web-site are taken only from the very best angles -- if the camera moved a little to the left or the right, you would see that the overall location is not very nice. The area is very crowded. The front of the hotel overlooks a Navy base across the bay - - very unattractive. Our room at first glance was well appointed and tastefully decorated. However, there was a strong musty/moldy smell and I have a terrible sense of smell due to allergies and usually don't detect odors that other people do. The room was also cramped for two people. Our room was on the back side of the hotel and had a small patio but it was right next to a walk way so there was no privacy and we had to keep the curtains drawn whenever we were in the room. The view on this side of the hotel was not very attractive either. The service was definitely a notch below many other hotels I have stayed at. Staff were not particularly professional or friendly. I believe my rate was about $130.00 or so per night. While this is reasonable for San Diego, I cannot recommend this hotel.

“Classy and Comfy!” I could not have picked a better hotel for my first time in Boston. Upon arrival the staff was incredible. From the receptionist to the concierge, everyone was helpful, whether it pertained to information or assistance regarding my room, or pointing out places to eat and sightsee. The lobby floor has a restaurant called City Bar and also a starbucks (very helpul for New Yorkers!) There is also a souvenir store right next to the starbucks. I stayed in a double bed room with friends and it could comfortably fit three or even four people. The rooms are incredibly clean and the beds are amazing! This hotel also offers late night in room dining. This hotel charges for parking (the only downside). Taxis are the easiest way to get around and super easy to get one outside the hotel. Average ride to points of interest like Fanueil Hall was around 10 minutes. Bottom Line: Great Hotel, I loved it!

“Of similar type hotels- you can do better than this one-its tired” Almost a week in this hotel...sigh, I knew it wasn’t the best hotel option based on prior reviews but it was where my meetings were. I suggest that if folks have an option with a similar price, to pass on this hotel. But its not bad, just not the first choice. My room was kind of shabby around the edges- chipped paint here and there, some torn wallpaper. It was also incredibly stuffy. I called and maintenance reported the AC but they just gave me a fan (which helped.) The lobby has free internet, but the lobby is below ground level, small and busy-not a place to catch up on work. They have a few computers for guests to use, but two of the key boards were so well used the letters were worn off-not easy for poor typists or Europeans. I was also annoyed all week because I had to PAY to have a refrigerator in my room. Geez. On the plus side, the staff were all genuinely nice, and high energy. They made this property tolerable. And-coming from the east coast I woke at 4am hungry- and was saved by the Famima across the street. It’s a chain which actually stays open all night and has good sandwiches and coffee.

“Good stay on business” I stayed for 3 nights for a convention, so my comments do not include information about tourist activities. The hotel was clean and comfortable, the staff friendly and helpful. Check-in was efficient and the room was very pleasant. It had a large wood-floored entry way, with the bedroom beyond. The bed was terrific, with loads of soft pillows and a down mattress topper. I slept really well on it. Breakfast was room service, which came promptly and was good value - $17 for eggs, sausage, toast, tea, juice. The food was hot and well-cooked, not at all greasy. One nice touch is that, if they are late delivering it, you get it for free. I've stayed lots of places where they turn up late without even an apology, which is not funny when you're trying to get to an early meeting. The bathroom was large and bright. The only sign of wear was the shower curtain which was grubby, and the towels were hard and scratchy, but I wasn't bothered by this. The only real criticism I have of this hotel is one that many other people have made: the stupid elevators. They are impossibly slow, and people were complaining loudly about them every day. I thought, as my room was only on the second floor, I could just take the stairs, but no. There is no stair access from the lobby. I find it incredible that the management has allowed this situation to contiue for so long. This factor aside, however, I'd recommend the hotel to anyone in central DC for business.

“Alamo Bowl trip, best pick!” The Marriott Plaza in San Antonio is one of 3 Marriott hotels within a 3 (or so) block radius and this is the one you should pick. The hotel is a smaller, boutique-style hotel and in a great location. It is only 2 block from the Riverwalk and 15 minute walk to the Alamodome. We were there for the Alamo Bowl and were very pleased with the hotel. Our room (548) had 2 Double Beds that were comfortable and the room was clean and was pleasing to the eye. We had a view of the Hemisfair Tower and the Alamodome with a furnished balcony. The food at the hotel was good, we ate both dinner and breakfast at the hotel and the food was good and reasonably priced. My only complaint for the hotel is that parking is $30 for valet and I understand a charge for parking in a downtown area, but that is almost too excessive especially not being directly on the Riverwalk like the other Marriotts that charge the same. I would definitely stay here again! Our room was $209 for that night but I would not pay that unless it was a night like the night where the Alamo Bowl was being paid, otherwisem I would pay $150 max. Also, check-in took almost 15 minutes because she had to find a room for us.

“Decent conference hotel. small room and limited amenities. a little bit overpriced.” was there for 3 nights for an on-site meeting with 15 other people. Paid over $250/night for a relative small room with limited amenities. similar to what others have said, there is absolutely now view/sunlight so might as well keep the curtains closed all day. For the price we paid I expect higher level of service...but housekeeping was only so-so...(did not refill teabags / bottled water / shampoos/etc). as a meeting location the catering was pretty decent. hot lunches with fancy salads and a good variety of healthy snacks...but we also paid some good $ for that so it was kinda of expected.

“Great place to stay. Good location, good price, nice and neat.” Motel 6's are usually all the same but this one was a little better. Its in a great location very close to Houston Hobby Airport and is near the highway also for easy access to anywhere you need to go. There are alot of places to eat around the area and gas stations are close by also. Now, the motel itself was great. Really nice staff and a nice and clean building inside and out. Lots of well lit parking spaces in a huge, somewhat enclosed parking lot so it felt safe. There is a small pool outside that was closed at the time I was there (fall, out of season) but it was still clean and the area looked like a good place to lounge around in. The room I got was HUGE! I got the standard king size bed and it looked like they had once used double beds in the room because I had so much extra space. Ive been to Motel 6's where it looks like they crammed a king size bed into a room the size of a large walk in closet (South Padre Island) so this was great. The room was spotless clean with fresh everything. Huge comfortable king size bed, wood flooring throughout, flatscreen tv, alarm clock radio with audio input for an mp3 player or phone, optional wifi, small desk and lounge area in one corner of the room, coat rack with hangers and a shelf near the door. Clean larger bathroom with curved shower curtain for more room while showering. Overall a nice and big clean room that slept well for a cheap price. You cant beat Motel 6's prices anywhere.If they threw in free WiFi they would be untouchable. Stay here if you need a place to crash while on business in Houston or the vicinity. The location is kind of middle ground to the area so i was able to visit downtown Houston, North Houston, over near NASA, and even Galveston during my stay. 2 thumbs up.

“Historic? No, dated” We stayed for a night to sightsee and shop. This is a grand old building with a great location. Aside from the bellmen and the extremely miserable people who work in the Starbucks outlet in the lobby, the welcome was consistently warm and friendly. We were allocated a very small room on the 15th floor. This was reasonably well-fitted in a very old-fashioned style but was also quite worn in parts. While we could cope with the small bedroom, the boxlike size of the bathroom was much more of a challenge. There really was no room in there at all and, for this standard of property,and given our gold Hilton Hhonors status, we'd have hoped for much better. This hotel trades on its name and its history but for the most part the place just felt dated and in need of a refresh. We moved on to the Conrad at Battery Park which, for the same price, provided a far better experience and a real taste of luxury. Waldorf Astoria next time? No thanks.

“Excellent Overall” The Washington Hilton is becoming my accommodation of choice in DC. I stayed here for 2 nights with a friend in late Feb 2012 and the service was terrific. I am a Hilton Gold member and was upgraded to the Exec floor, where even on weekends they served breakfast and early evening snacks (including hot food like chicken wings). The location is just a few blocks (walking distance) to Dupont Circle. I know the hotel doesn't have wireless in it's guest rooms (it has corded high speed internet)...but our room was right near the lounge so we were able to pick up wireless from the lounge. My only gripe is it looks like they raised the parking fees recently. It is very expensive to park here and given it's further away from downtown I would hope they would consider making their rates more reasonable. We ending up valeting and a few nights it was really busy and took over 20 mins to get the car, but this was my only gripe. I'll be back again to this historic hotel.

“What's Not To Like?” I could not fault this hotel in any way. Every element came together. Light, bright room, fluffy duvet and comfortable beds, brilliant aesthetic, and amazing bathroom - especially that giant shower. I love that they comp the drinks/snacks - we probably had 2 things in a 3-night stay but it's the gesture that's meaningful. Staff seemed nice, though I can't say we called on them much to test out the services. It might be nice to be in an instant "neighborhood" like SoHo depending on what you're in New York for, but it was quite handy and central for most of our needs. Lots of value here. I've stayed at many places in the city but unless I'm splashing out at the Crosby Street or similar, this will be my new go-to spot in New York.

“Great staff, clean modern rooms - recommend this hotel” We stayed here after a driving vacation to see colleges in Boston before flying home. The location is right next to the UMass stadium & near the JFK Library, a few minutes from downtown. Easy to get to but we definitely needed the GPS to navigate Boston's exits getting here. The lobby is large and modern with many cozy seating areas, free wireless access, a bar, and a deli located right off the lobby. The staff was friendly, professional and provided clear direct answers to questions. I love Doubletree's custom of their warm cookie check-in greeting! Overnight parking was in a gated lot behind the hotel. Our room was on a higher floor overlooking the parking lot, the bay and Logan airport. There was very little noise from the planes in the room. Our room had 2 doubles, which was roomy enough for our family of 4. It had a desk with internet access, a small fridge & double cup coffee maker. The bathroom had a tub/shower & the standard amenities. The shuttle driver took us to a nearby restaurant which was convenient. One tip: The business center computers were 1970s slow due to video gamers gumming up the servers. Let the staff know. Once they were alerted to the issue, they dealt with it right away & offered their personal computers so that I could check-in for our flights while the servers rebooted. Kudos for making sure customers needs were met efficiently. Recommend staying here. Very nice hotel with a good location to get around Boston either by car or mass transit, & great helpful staff. Also very economical when comparing prices compare total costs including coffee, parking, internet access. We saved lots by staying here!

“Great Airport Hotel” We spent one night there after a very late flight arriving at LAX. Staff was helpful and very nice. the room was nice and quiet. We particularly appreciated how quick our room service order was delivered. Great Airport hotel !

“Decent deal, good location” This is a very typical hotel but the rooms are nicely renovated and we were surprised at the large size, unusual for Manhattan. They don't offer many extras (like no room service or mini-bar), and the doorman was on the take with the airport car service, but with the subway steps away, a 24hr drug store next door and an easy walk to some of the best attractions, we would recommend this hotel for tourists who want location.

“Good and convenient to downtown” RECOMMENDED. The hotel sits just off the I-880 freeway and is directly on the light rail station to downtown (Gish). Hotel is not in an OK part of town (bail bondsman and dive bar nearby), but didn't see any serious crime problem, just don't figure you'll walk to dinner. Plenty of free parking. Hotel staff was efficient and friendly. Hotel is clearly older, but in good condition and has been renovated. Rooms are not huge, but nice sized, bedding very comfortable. Bathrooms well illuminated, a bit on the small side. As previously noted, heavy use of tile in public areas make 1st floor rooms subject to noise (note: they generally fill these rooms last). No experience with restaurant. Light rail is direct 10 minutes to convention center. Would stay again.

“Speaking from experience” I have had the pleasure of staying in the Park South over 20 times in the past 4 years and for me it's a home from home. Helpful and friendly staff, clean, bright rooms and a good value breakfast. The area is full of great, cheap restaurants and the store on the corner is open 24 hours and is full of great snacks, beer etc. The Black Duck food is excellent and it is all round a great hotel for the cost (Cheap for NY prices). Admittedly the rooms are not huge but this is New York..space is at a premium and if you want a football pitch, you pay. And anyway, if you are in NYC..You should be spending 20 hours of your day enjoying the greatest city on earth. And for the person below who suggests the subway 3 seconds walk away isn't convenient..get a cab!

“This is a very nice place and it will get nicer...” Reading the previous review by Cyclismo 74 and being a lowly "regular" Ambassador as opposed to the Royal Ambassador, I guess I am easier to please... I stayed for the weekend with a $273/night rate and was upgraded to a Sky View room on the 32nd floor (very nice with unobstructed views of the West Side and the Hudson River). The rooms are large by NYC standards, and the demeanor of every staff member I encountered was excellent. Rooms are very quiet (I have stayed in NYC hotels at similar floor levels and could hear traffic and sirens throughout the night). Also, the location just can't be beat--you are close enough to Times Square and Broadway but are not directly in the massive crowds that jam this area. This is a soft opening (only a third of the planned rooms are available), and they will need to determine the traffic flow patterns as the business develops. There were some details that need attending, e.g. more staff at check-in (took nearly 10 minutes which is why I docked the review by 1 star), placing a sign on each floor to direct the room number. The staff was apologetic and I am sure that they will take the necessary steps to improve. Cyclismo74--you need to chill!! Having stayed in many NYC hotels through the years, this is already one of the better ones, and the Intercontinental brand will continue to improve on it. There are plenty of places in this city with dismal rooms, bathrooms where even one person cannot fit, and/or obnoxious staff--all for the price that is much more than what I paid.

“A great view in a comfortable hotel. Good for families with young kids.” We went to NYC for a long weekend with our kids, ages 2 and 4. From experience, we've realized that "suites" hotels work best for us because we can put the kids to bed early in the bedroom, close the door, and watch TV or read in the "living room." The hotel worked perfectly for our stay. Times Square is mayhem and it was fun to be in the middle of it. The hotel staff was friendly and the concierge answered our questions about how to get tickets for Broadway shows. The hotel restaurant was empty when we got there but we ate at 6pm with the kids, so perhaps that's no surprise. The food was good and the waiter accommodated our picky eaters.

“En el centro de Memphis..” Este hotel está en el corazón de Memphis. A un paso de Beale street y casi todas las atracciones turísticas de la ciudad, exceptuando Graceland. Este hotel es famoso por muchos motivos,pero uno de los más grandes son...sus patos!! Todos los días, 2 veces al día, los patos recorren la recepción del hotel.Por la mañana a las 11 para salir hasta la fuente, y por la tarde a las 5 para volver a sus "aposentos"... Las habitaciones bien, aquí me esperaba más,porque el hotel no es precisamente muy barato..pero teniendo en cuanto que no paras en el hotel y que está en el centro...y los patos...pues Ok!

“Goof midtown hotel” I have stayed at this hotel on several occasions for business and pleasure. It is in a good location right on 42nd and second but a bit off beaten track so that it is not too busy. Right near UN and Grand Central. Service is good and the room are well maintained. Ever since Hilton took over a few years ago things have improved significantly.

“A safe bet in San Fran” Stayed at the Hotel Carlton for 3 nights in early May 2010 and as you would expect, being in San Francisco, the hotel was old and charming. Sound insulation is obviously its major problem. The wind just howls through the place and we heard our neighbour snoring all night as if he was in the same room as us. I didn’t really mind, we just accepted it for what it was, an older, character-filled place to stay. The décor was really comfy, exotic and inviting. It was a bit of a hike to get to the central areas of the city from the hotel, but we’re not afraid of pounding the pavement and caught the trolley a couple of times to get to where we needed to go. The rate of $126US was for the room only. For breakfast I would recommend Golden Coffee Shop, the prawn omelette and pancakes were yum. And for lunch or a snack I would strongly recommend Swan Oyster Depot on Polk St, and Chutney on Jones St for a cheap Indian feast, all within walking distance from the hotel. I would not recommend this hotel for anyone looking for a quiet, private stay. But if you’re looking for a reasonably priced, clean and inviting hotel and you don’t mind strolling the streets, then go for this hotel.

“Of mice and things that thump in the night...” You can't say the Hotel Helix is dull. From the 60's retro modern decor, classic candy in the mini bar to the furry bedspread, the Helix is not your typical lodging establishment....and therein lies part of the problem. The staff were friendly, efficient and knowledgable...when you could find them. At times, I had to go a-searchin' for a valet to take the car off my hands. Lobby is very small and during peak hours very crowded. Hotel location is a bit of a hike from the nearest Metro station, not a horrible walk in nice weather, wouldn't care to make the trek in winter. Our room on the fourth floor overlooked the outside area of the Hotel Helix club...which you could hear quite plainly, you could even hear the scrape of the club chairs on the patio concrete, until 11 pm when the outside portion closed. Our king room was comfortably large and seemed clean, but needed some upkeep, like a chipped tile in the bath/shower that I'm sure will result in some type of water damage or mold problem in the near future. A couple traveling with us were awakened to a hungry mouse in their room on the first night, they were relocated to a suite, with a leaky bathroom sink that pooled water on the bathroom floor. Elevators are small and at times slow. Restuarant and room service hours are very limited. Bottom line, the Hotel Helix is visually interesting, but it's location and limited amenities probably would preclude me from recommending this hotel.

“Not that horrible, 25 dollars PLN hotel” I agree with most of poster here. This extended stay hotel is dumpster. But that is what extended stay hotel is. Do not reserve this hotel in their website by paying 50 dollars or more. You can go priceline.com and bid just 20~25, 26 dollars. This hotel is better than other extended stay hotels nearby area. The hotel itself resides in small business park - bank, wingate hotel so area has nothing at night. Please pack your own linen and maybe some protective sheet to remodel the room for your sanitation. The Internet is working fine.(4.9?? dollars for your stay)

“Clean and comfortable hotel in heart of Financial District” If you don't mind being in this part of Manhattan, this is a great hotel. Easy walking distance to a lot of great things and transportation is easy to find as well. Hotel restaurant is great; the breakfast is delicious and the croissants are top notch! Very clean with nice showers. It's small but that's to be expected for NYC. Staff is very helpful and friendly.

“Not bad, but forgettable” I've stayed at more than my fair share of hotels in Baltimore, and while this one is fine, it ranks the lowest of the several Baltimore hotels I stayed at. There's nothing terribly wrong with it. My TV didn't work on my last two stays, and was easily fixed when I called. And I noted that there was an assortment of screws used throughout the room. For instance, the towel rack was hung on four screws, and each was different. Again, there is nothing wrong with this hotel, but there are just signs that it's not on-top of it's game, as you see elsewhere in the city.

“Great Value -and Wonderful Hotel” The location just off Union Square is fantastic. Walk from BART. The lobby is a little small and has lots of activity. The room is nicely updated, and the bed is super comfortable. The windows open so real air is possible. The bathroom is not big but it has the deepest tub I've seen short of a hot tub. I would definitely be happy with the room at almost twice what we're paying. Besides the desk said that it's expected that the guests will take the rubber ducky. Now that's a real nice touch. The room is very clean and has no smell at all.

“Exceeded Expectations” I booked this direct for business travel and was pleasantly surprised at how clean and smooth the whole experience was. The staff was efficient and knowledgeable, and the room although Manhattan-sized was impeccably clean. And less than 5 minute walk from Penn Station mid-town. $ 169 before taxes and fees incl free wifi. All I needed. Overall exceeding expectations.

“nice location rooms are small” The location is great. Very close to the airport and right across from Quincy market. The rooms and buildings lay out in a maze and it can be hard to navigate thru the hotel and find your room. Rooms are small even by Boston standards but clean and updated. There was some sort of drunk domestic issue right in the hall outside my room at 1am when a couple could not find their room- security actually had to remove them- very odd experience and due to that not sure as a woman traveling alone I would stay at this hotel again (for sure not if I am alone!)

“Average, moderate hotel” Rate: $249 night during the week (Corporate rate). Competitor rates were in the $400-$500 per night range. Liked: Location - distance from airport was great (cab ride was $15 from DCA). Restaurants within walking distance. Room was adequate but definitely dinky. Liked the small amenity bag with linen spray, ear plugs and a sleep mask that was left on the bed. Nice touch. Starbucks within the hotel and was a definite hot spot in the morning for both walking patrons from the street and hotel guests. Gal at the check in desk was friendly and accomodating as she allowed me to check in early (1:30 PM) AND gave me a nice-ish room with a view that overlooked a park and a distant view of the Washington Monument. The room, while small, was comfortable. Bed was nice. Air conditioner/heating unit was a bit loud when it kicked on (it woke me up once during the night - not a biggie) and somewhat temperamental, but worked well enough for one night. Had a cocktail at the hotel bar, called 14K, and the bartender, Meriam, was delightful and was quick to recommend places for us to venture out to during the evening if we didn't want to stay at the hotel. She was a gem and nice to have wait on us! Disliked/Needs improvement: Room size was dinky, but really, that's about it. Hotel was a bit dated but not enough for me to complain or write poorly about it. I would definitely stay there again for business or pleasure.

“Nice, modern hotel, but lousy neighborhood” The hotel is your standard Manhattan boutique hotel: the whole place, including the lobby and rooms, are munchkin-sized. But the place was clean (even sleek), the bed was comfy, and the staff members were friendly and helpful.
