The downside is that the far-west, Midtown location is just plain lousy: it's somewhat grimy, it's near a busy tunnel, and it's a substantial walk to almost anything of interest in Manhattan.

“Great location” Stayed at the Lennox through SkyAuction. It was a terrific choice. Pluses - super, central location in Copley Square area (next door to Lord & Taylors, block to Prudential Center and a block to Newbury St, a block to Copley Square Plaza, great restaurants right across the street, near the subway, etc.). Fast check-in once the room was ready at 2pm (arrived before 11am, a room was available but not the king bed we wanted). Room reminded us of a NYC hotel room in size with the bathroom being the smallest we've ever seen. But everything was fine, clean, etc. Wi-Fi was complimentary (and fast) and there were two bottles of complimentary water. One disappointment was an unfinished repair near the tub in the bathroom (needed to be sanded and painted). Negatives - not really any (elevators were a bit slow maybe). We would definitely go back for another visit.

“Loved it!” I normally do not rave about hotels - but this place was great. It is located in the center of Times Square, the inside is gorgeous, rooms are a good size and they even have a great gym. The only part of this hotel I don't like is the price - but it is in the middle of NYC, so I guess I can't complain too much.

“Knowing the floorplan is the key” The Monaco is perfectly situated in the Penn Quarter of Washington D.C. It is within walking distance of almost all the major sites, and Metro distance of all the others (Gallery Place Chinatown Metro entrance is directly across the street.) My experience with service was excellent at the front desk, especially the concierge who successfully steered us to two excellent restaurants (Zaytinya and Ceiba). My room was quite large, tall and very pretty. The bathrooms are a bit small. My business companion upgraded to one of the suites and the thing was enormous. Key here: if you do not like your room, ask to change. He did and was very happy. One curious thing was the bizarro toilet flushers they have. Very loud and not too effective. We asked them to fix it several times. They snaked the heck out of it (scarring the bowl), but never really fixed it. Eat at Poste (restaurant in the hotel; rabbit is divine.) Reference a previous writeup, not sure I understand why you wouldn't be able to have al fresco dining in the spring here, but you certainly do not want to eat outside in July in DC (it was 100 degrees for several days). Dress accordingly. Any of these restaurants are nice slacks and collared shirt type places for men. Enjoy the Monaco and the Penn Quarter.

“Quiet and Clean” The Hilton Austin Airport is a great hotel for business travelers and large groups. Perfect hotel for a one-night layover from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, especially since they offer complimentary shuttle service. Clean - from the parking lot outside, to the room inside and everywhere in between. This hotel was almost too quiet. It could benefit from subtle music in the atrium area. Because of its location, the hotel is removed from the charm of "keep Austin weird," but it's only a short drive to Congress and Sixth Streets. Hotel was booked through Priceline.com at $45 and was a steal, even with the added parking. Just my luck, the attendent was working.

“An instant classic” Somehow, I was under the impression that the Joie de vivre chain was solely dedicated to restoring once elegant properties back to their original glory, and thus, came to the Moorpark with that expectation. My reaction to that was "Wow - they did a fabulous job restoring THIS property," until a friend told me, "Oh no - this is new construction." Even so, it still has a nice 'historic feel.' Lots of wood. Leather chairs. Elegantly appointed rooms, and a lovely pool area with canopies over the lounges for that quasi Hollywood in the 30s feel. Way more personality than your average Hilton or Hyatt, beginning with the fire in the fireplace as you walk in the front door. Our room was spacious and well appointed. The desk staff was friendly and helpful, and the buffet breakfast (not included) was nicely presented with excellent seasoning in the eggs and sausage. The location is just a jump off of I-280, so providing you have a car, it's well situated to doing business in downtown San Jose. Why not five stars? We'll... not quite a put on the dog all out vacation destination, but a very comfortable stay for an appropriate price, I think. In fact, I would go back in a heartbeat, opting to stay here over any number of 'big chain' hotels. In a couple of words - lovely and comfortable!

“Excellent hotel and location, excellent value” The other reviews give a good picture of the place. I was confused by one common remark, that the hotel is far from "downtown". Boston doesn't really have a single downtown. There's the financial district, but tourists wouldn't particularly want to go there, except maybe on the way to Quincy Market. The Boston Common area would probably be best for sightseers. But the Copley/Back Bay area is probably best for shopping, and certainly for going to Fenway. Here's something nobody's mentioned about the location. You can cross the street and enter the Sheraton, and from there you have indoor access to the Prudential Center (and the Hynes Center if you have an event there), from there the Bridge Mall, from there the Marriott, from there Copley Place, from there the Westin... and you can even walk into Back Bay Station without going outside. I thought that was important since the weather was pretty intimidating while I was staying there! A few things about the hotel itself: o I happily took my laptop to the lobby, rather than pay for internet. o I got a king corner room, on the 22nd floor, for a very good price (others at my business event stayed at the Marriott, Sheraton, Westin, for much more money). The room was huge and the view amazing (the river and Cambridge, the famous Citgo sign, Fenway park). o The bathroom was on the small side. o I liked the staff, but I didn't need much service. o The breakfast at 40 Dalton was overpriced.

“With old world charm, this place is a gem.” Having been to Europe as a student, where I learned to love pensiones as they enabled me to see the world on a student's budget, I was ready to try an American hotel that was not "ensuite". I was at a conference next door at the Marriott, where the rooms were specially priced for our group at three times what I paid at the Mosser. I am glad I stayed here. I never had to wait for the facilities, and had a terrific little room with everything I needed except the internet. That was changing as I was there, and free internet should be available for future guests. Our American hotel tradition is just like Europe's, we just tend to discard our past sooner. Fortunately, this Victorian hotel was not discarded. I hope to go back.

“SUPER, SUPER, SUPER” The hotel was outstanding. It is in a GREAT location and the free breakfast each morning is the best spread of food I have ever seen at a hotel. This is the only place I will stay at in New York City.

“Comfortable Hotel in nice Dupont Circle area” Attended a conference and found the staff to be friendly. The hotel lobby while cute was comfortable and with wireless connection. Because the weather was cold, the outdoor pool was not available for use. Food served in the restaurant was good and overall experience was positive. Will be back.

“Comfortable Little Gem” Very beautiful building and comfortable rooms. The hotel staff is remarkably friendly and helpful. Perfectly located in the heart of Back Bay/Copely Square area. The only thing I didn't like is that there are no coffee makers in the rooms - but there is complimentary coffee in the morning at the bottom of the elevator. The hotel is nice enough that the coffeemaker wasn't a signficiant drawback (and I'm a big coffee drinker). I love the free internet. I'd stay here again in a minute - it was one of the highlights of a multiweek, multicity trip.

“GUT!” four points: gute lage, nicht direkt downtown, da geht aber mit monorail in fünf minuten hin der die sation direkt neben dem space needle hat, welches wiederum auch nur wenige minuten vom hotel entfernt liegt, vom flughafen ca 30 min. mit dem taxi um ca 50 $ tip incl. 2 supermärkte in der näheren umgebungung die auch tw. 24 h geöffnet sind, sowie einige lokale mit thailändischer und vietnamesischer küche.umgebung ist relativ ruhig und sicher. hotel auf 4 etagen, war im 3.stock, keine lärmbelästigung durch aufzug, ac ode strasse. zimmer mit kingsize bett sind schon recht klein und eher für single reisende mit wirklich wenig gepäck gedact.betten und matratzten sehr gut, 42" flatscreen, safe, kein kühschrank, coffeemaker mit cafe von sehr schwacher qualität, eismaschine und automat für sweets und soft drinks auf jeden floor. bad mit grosser dusche, druck ausreichend und armaturen in neuwertigen und sehr guten zustand, auch sauber. gym für cardio und auch etwas krafttraining ist 24/7 möglich. kleine lobby, gepäck wurde vom taxifahrer auf den trolly verfrachtet und von mir nach quick check in aufs zimmer gefahren... in der lobby befindet sich ein businesscenter und eine bar mit happy hour und frühstücksraum..frühstücken war ich nicht, kostet angeblich 16 $ und soll sehr spärlich sein... n der lobby vorm check inn ist eine sitzgelegenheit mit einem künstlichen kamin, wo man zeitung lesen oder warten kann..

“Exactly what I expected” This is a clean, basic motel that is exactly what I expected at this price point. On the plus side, the staff is very friendly and helpful. We left some pillows in our room and the General Manager offered to box them up and mail them back to us. The rooms were clean, with a nice flat-screen TV, refrigerator and microwave, and the bed was very comfortable. The showers were good and hot with ample water pressure. The swimming pool was tiny but clean and the hot tub worked great. Breakfast was OK, although the breakfast room will really only accommodate about 10 people at a time. There is quite a bit of traffic noise from the adjacent highways, although when we put the air conditioner on fan it drowned it out. The neighborhood is not exactly beautiful but I felt perfectly safe walking around. We never had any trouble finding a parking space even though the motel was full. My rating of this motel is not based on it being a 4 star hotel but rather on its value.
“Decent Place” It certainly isn't a fancy hotel, but it's a great place to stay. The staff was polite and the location can't be beat.

“Fine Overnight Hotel for Business” I have stayed at the Sheraton Suites multiple times for business while in the Philadelphia area as well as when needing an overnight for international flights. First off, as far as Sheraton Suites go - it is a fine hotel. Its an older property that has been converted to an all Suite Hotel. It definitely looks dated from the glass enclosed elevators to the carpeting down the hall ways and the wall paper both in public spaces and the rooms. Front Desk and Public Spaces The front desk area has been renovated, with marble tile floors, granite counter tops and dark, rich woods. The staff was ok, the first time my room wasn't ready even though I had requested early check-in so they did offer to hold my luggage for me while I went to my meetings. I wasn't overly impressed with the front desk staff, but they were ok in their service level. There is a business center type area on the main floor that is very hip and functionable just somewhat loud as it is near the bar and restaurant area. The Burger Bar was always awesome for both lunch and dinner. The bar area was very open air, with televisions, ample seating spaces and great service. The lady that waited on my had like 20 years of experience with the company! Food was also very good. I never utilized the pool or fitness areas so I cannot comment on those. Rooms The rooms are HUGE and great for me as I need lots of space to spread out my work items. The main living room area has a nice size couch, coffee table, chair, desk area with television. Plenty of light - my only downside was I didn't think there was enough outlets near the desk. I'm not sure on the cost for the internet as I have a wifi card that I use when traveling for work. There is a small wet bar type area with a counter, refrigerator (would suggest a mini bar) and coffee maker. The bathroom was just your standard, typical hotel bathroom with toilet, tub/shower combo, and counter with sink, mirror, etc. There were plenty of towels. The bedroom was very large too. My room looked out at the airport and it was very quiet. The bed was very, very comfy and loved being able to shut the door to the living. Room Service and Housekeeping Room service usually fairly prompt in their delivery, but I felt as though I had a lot of hold time waiting for someone to answer the phone. They also took a while in clearing away old dishes. Housekeeping seemed to offer pretty decent service and I had no complaints with them. Shuttle Service The hotel does offer a shuttle service that I have used numerous times. The drivers are always courteous and offer to help with your luggage. My only concern is that in the mornings, the Sheraton is located in the same area as the Aloft and one other Starwood property so the shuttle back to the airport can be VERY full. Also make sure to tell the driver which terminal you are going to so he knows where to stop. I would and plan to definitely stay here again for work because its convenient for me. Just remember its a Sheraton Suites, not a Marriott, not a Hyatt, etc.

“Nice Hotel for Girls' weekend” My best friend and I decided to stay here for a girls’ weekend in Chicago and absolutely loved the hotel. We got a good rate for a Superior room off there site approx. $129/night. The room was super clean and comfortable for the both of us. The bathroom was huge with Jacuzzi tub and separate shower. The location was perfect too and we were able to walk every where. Two blocks from Magnificent Mile and 4 from the John Hancock building where you can pick up the double decker bus. Concierge was friendly and helped us with the purchase of our Sears Towers tickets and bus tour. We ended our nights with a nightcap at the hotel bar. Martinis were a little pricey but the bar atmosphere had a good vibe. There an old school diner right next door for breakfast...the omelets were delicious. Overall, if I were to return to Chicago, I would stay here again and highly recommend.

“The best hotel in New York I've ever stayed at.” I've stayed at many hotels in New York and this has to be the best so far. Given the $275 price through Quikbook and the size and quality of the room this would be the first hotel I would look to rebook again when I come back to New York. Overall, attention to detail, the quality of finishings, friendliness of staff, bathroom accessories (though what is it with American towels..they are almost never large, soft or fluffy) and a lovely view over a small park made this a great stay. The location is not so seedy as people make out and it's a quick walk to Soho and close to other downtown hotspots . There's even a Wholefoods a block away and check out the small restaurants in and around nearby Bond St.

“Nice Hotel, Large updated rooms, nice pool, lots of families, $25/day parking” My wife and I stayed here for an extended holiday visit to my family and we had an enjoyable stay. The room was comfortable and the pool area was great. The hotel also has a small gym, which was nice. Although the hotel is not convenient if you want to go out downtown (or anywhere, really, without a car), it's a nice place to stay. Parking is a joke at $25 a day - but San Diego thinks it's a big city and most hotels these days charge outrageous parking fees. The city colludes with the hotel by not allowing parking on the bay between the hours and 2 and 4 am. Aside from the parking and somewhat isolated hotel (if you're accustomed to city living and public transportation), we had no complaints. The hotel even has a really good happy hour. The pool area can be loud with children, and we never found a quiet place to escape the playing.

“Comfy boutique hotel” I had a nice stay here. You can't beat the location, right in the heart of the city, near all sorts of great restaurants and dive bars. As with many hotels in the city, the rooms can be a bit small, but ours was clean and well appointed. The staff were friendly and helpful and the free wine reception in the lobby was a nice touch. I think it was a little pricey, but I'd stay again.

“Ok Hotel But Not In Great Shape” Not a bad place to stay but most certainly not great. Looks like another typical hotel that was already in business, then bought by Sheraton Group and remodeled into a 4 Points. Modest in every way without any perks to speak of. Elevators are either ancient or not well maintained. Entire hotel not well maintained. But it does have Sheraton Sleeper Beds and that is a plus. Location is pretty good right across the street from a large shopping center with lots of places to eat. Small parking lot and not patrolled. Really a big deal to me as I had so many things stored in my vehicle that I could not take inside. Make sure you park near the front door where there is light and a resemblance of security. Memphis is not the safest city in the USA for theft.

“Decent, but would I stay again?” We stayed here for a weekend trip to just hang downtown. My husband and two young sons...for the prices this place charges don't know that I would stay here again. Yes, its right on PCH, but we had a view of the parking lot. ( maybe if you ask for a view you'd get one??) We are seasoned travelers and often come to San Diego since we live in Orange County, but I think this hotel's website photos make this place look nicer than it actually is. Rooms are a tad run down and definitely could use a remodel. One plus is the breakfast in the mornings...nothing special, but great if you have young ones. Again don't think I would stay here again unless I got a deal.

“Yet another top rating!” After an initial hiccup that was dealt with in an exemplary way, we had a great stay at the Magic Castle Hotel. We are a couple in our sixties and the location and accommodation suited us perfectly. There were a few families staying at the time but a general mix of all ages. The Room we were allocated, 207, was excellent and recently refurbished. It had a spacious bedroom with very comfortable king sized bed and lots of storage, a pleasant bathroom and very spacious separate living area with integral kitchen. The balcony which again was generous in size and had a table and two chairs overlooked the swimming pool. I don't know how they do it but the Reception staff are all outstanding and everything other people have said in reviews is absolutely true. We didn't really partake too much of the free snacks but they were there if you wanted them and for a visiting family with children this would be a great bonus. Breakfast was adequate and could be taken near Reception or to your room. There are good laundry facilities which cost 1 dollar 25 cents for the wash and a similar amount for the drier - excellent if you are on a long road trip as we were. The location of the hotel couldn't be better being just around the corner from the main Hollywood action - a five minutes walk which, at all times, always felt safe. To get to Universal Studios, the metro is only one stop North and costs 1 dollar 50 cents, the hotel will lend you a tap card that you can add the return metro fare on to ensure it is effortless. The machines at the metro station near the Chinese Theatre accept dollar notes and give change. If doing Universal, try to splash out for the VIP experience (not really recommended for children however), it is costly but worth every penny. The Magic Castle itself is also worth a visit and the hotel can arrange this. We ate one of the best fillet steaks we have ever tasted there at dinner on a busy Saturday night. There is so much to take in and we spent 5 great nights really getting to know the main features of this sprawling city. The 2 day Hop On Hop Off bus helped us do this as I didn't want to drive too much in the city and the 3 routes offered give a comprehensive oversight. The Magic Castle Hotel is perfectly situated to enable you to take advantage of most of what is on offer. To sum up, exceptional customer service, great location, superb value for money and a great Los Angeles experience - the Magic Castle Hotel was comfortable, not luxurious; perfectly located but not in the noise of Hollywood; and very good value for money, particularly if travelling as a family. What a great product - I am really pleased we experienced it!

“Average hotel. Good location.” I stayed for one night for business. Very good location right in the heart of downtown. The lobby area is nice. There is a little cafe that serves Starbucks coffee. In the morning you can buy muffins, breakfast sandwiches, etc. There is an area to sit and eat which is a bar in the evening. Internet is free. The room is average and the bathroom is very average. As a woman traveling on business, I found the hair dryer in the room horrible - make sure to bring your own. Parking is expensive at $38/night and the drive way to valet in is narrow and right off a busy street. Also, it took the valet over 20 minutes to bring the car around - make sure you call ahead.

“Awesome site for corporate retreat and destination wedding.” I recently attended a business retreat at the Hayes Mansion. Thee site is awesome, the food is excellent (two great restaurants on site). Accommodations are very nice and quiet. Tremendous amount of San Jose history surround you. Excellent remodeling, keeping the historical character of the site. The staff is very accommodating and friendly. Lots of area surrounding with hiking trails. The only drawback, which could be a positive, is that it's a way out of the San Jose downtown and nightlife. Yet the site provides lots of after work relaxation. The plaza bar is nice with a comfortable outside area for casual dining or after meeting conversation. I'd return for a get away weekend or another business meeting.

“Nice "Place" You've Got There” Stayed there with several in a wedding party, $110 a night. This is a really nice, immaculate hotel. Large room with nice sitting area, desk and office chair, fridge, small microwave. Comfortable, clean, quiet. Great staff who unlike the losers at the Faust Hotel in New Braunfels let me have 2 p.m. check out since the wedding was not until 5 and I had nowhere to go. Nice breakfast....not elaborate, but good. I was intrigued to see some wall plugs beneath the TV. Turns out you can plug in your laptop, tablet, DVD, probably even iPod. Never seen that before anywhere. TV was 42 inch with swivel so you can watch from sitting area or bed. This Hyatt Place is a great place to say. I hated to leave because it was such a comfortable stay.

“The Omni...beautiful and convenient” The Omni suited my family of four. The room and hotel were beautiful. The level of service given by every employee was unsurpassed. We found the location to be very convenient. Many restaurants were in the area including the resaurants in the foot -traffic -only alley a couple of blocks away. Union Square was within easy walking distance for my husband, me, and daughters, 18 and 20. We took the Powell cable car to Fisherman's Wharf. We took a bus to the Japanese tea garden from Union Square.. We also visited Haight-Asbury from the same location. The Market, Montgomery St. BART station is a few blocks from the hotel and is very convenient for getting to and from the airport. It may be a bit more difficult to get around from this location with small children in tow, but for us, it was perfect!

“Very tiny room, but very clean and in a nice neighborhood.” This hotel has very small rooms (we are talking 9 ft x 8 ft with normal size bathroom) but they are clean, which is my #1. I am sure they are average size for NYC. On a very quiet street in Chelsea, walking distance (3 blocks) to subway or short cab ride to many destinations. Neighborhood has many good restaurants. If you are in the neighborhood for an appointment at Kleinfeld (as I was for my wedding dress), it is only a few blocks walk. Overall, its pricey for the size, but definately clean and comfortable enough for the amount of time you would actually spend in a hotel room while seeing NYC. Definately quieter than hotels nearer to tourist locations. Staff is average. They will store your bag for you before/after you check out for no additional cost but charge you some dumb $2/night fee for some arbitrary safety something or another.

“Comfortable” I stayed a weekend here for fun and found the hotel to be very comfortable - even on a very busy weekend. Check in and check out were easy, the elevators were fast, the room was spacious and quiet and there was a good amount of shaded parking. I enjoyed the location because it put us walking distance from downtown as well as SoCo and the bat bridge (which I'm glad that I checked out). Good stay, thank you!

“Great value at $50, very satisfied” The only explanation I can find for the previous negative reviews are that the motel has been refurbished and they rated it before that happened,. Or possibly that the reviewers are confused, or they are malicious idiots. One reviewer said "good for the price" and then gave them a 3-star rating?!? Yes, it has to be cleam, no matter what you pay, but beyond that you HAVE to take price into consideration when you rate. I literally moved out of 3 nights in a $475 executive suite at the Catamaran on Mission Bay into this Motel 6. I loved the Catamaran, but I cannot expect to get the same at the Motel 6 for $50. I stayed in the motel room closest to the office, right by the pool. It was clean, looked like it had been recently renovated. I slept well (because I always use earplugs), so I guess the bed was OK. The shower was fine, the carpet was fine, internet access at 3 bucks a day worked fine. And then you have a pool and free coffee in the morning. That is great value if you ask me. I'll be curious to see what future reviewers have to say, because I will likely use this motel again and again. I also note that Tripadvisor under 'describe this hotel's style" does not have a checkbox for "value". This is the best Motel 6 I have every stayed in. I live in Florida, and there are tons of bad Motel ^'s south of the Mason-Dixon line.

“So-So Paradise” My husband & I went down for the weekend and checked in and were taken to a very bleak room, with a view of the parking lot, we had requested a garden view or bay view room. I called reception and they told us they could move us to a bay view room for $75 more, we decided to move after being tempted by water....The room was very nicely appointed, but there were some issues with smell and must as well. Room service is a disaster in the mornings. Trying to get through is a joke, and after finally getting through being told rudely that the wait would be "90 minutes." The wait on both days for breakfast orering at 8:15 am on both days, was two hours. The food was cold, order was completely wrong on the second day. Thank heavens for the microwave in the room. We rented a hobie catamaran on Saturday morning which was very nice, the staff was very helpful. For the price, we would rather stay at the Coronodo. The grounds at Paradise is gorgeous, just be very specefic when making reservations as to what exactly a garden view room means.

“Forget the bad reviews, great experience!” The reviews made a bit nervous, I was disapoointed after booking on priceline and seeing that our bid was accepted with the Allerton. Boy was I wrong, the Allerton was in a great location and everything was wonderful from the price of our room to the staff. Our room was huge, we upgraded to suite and it was on the 22nd floor and over looked Michigan Ave! We had a huge sitting area with a couch that pulled out into a single sleeper with tons of window and TV, there was a sperate large bedroom area with two queen beds, a big TV and a ton more windows. The bathroom was huge with a big walk in shower. The staff was more then accomadating and very friendly. I will say that the elevators are small, but there are five of them. In prior reviews people said that they waited long amounts of time for the elevators, I can't say that we had this problem once and we were in and out of our room a lot. Also, there is a starbucks right acorss the street, another added bonus. I would definately stay here again.

“Great location and good value” This small boutique hotel located on the outskirts of thwe Broadway district, provided a comfortable night's stay during a huge snowstorm. The staff was very friendly and the lobby quaint and clean. There was only one elevator and most of the time it was quicker to walk the 4 flights to my room rather than wait. The room was pretty small and plain but it was clean with a nicely stocked bathroom. I booked this Hoter on Hotwire for about $100, and for a NYC hotel with prime location, it was a great value.

“Wow - impressed” Was in Dallas for business and stayed at the Omni. This hotel really stands out. The hotel opened in November 2011 and the design was really well thought out. The entire hotel is very stylish and modern. Staff is very well trainned and provided exceptional service. For example, I arrived about alittle prior to my room being ready (was listed cleaned - but not inspected) - the registration staff offered me a complimentary drink in the lobby area bar. About 1/2 hr later, he called me and brought my key to me. Staff throughout our meeting was really attentive. My room was exceptionally decorated and comfortable. Clean modern lines and artwork. Bathroom came with a hidden TV in the mirror. Bathrobe was very complimentary. The rooms are also green - you need your room key to turn on lights and most electrial outlets. The workout facility well equipped with treadmills, ellipiticals (two types of Precor), free weights and weight machines. There is an infinity pool - weather was really cold when I was there and didn't go outside much. Food was really-really good. Ate at Texas Spice - food and drink was great. We had conference buffet style food for the rest of the meeting - all was surprisingly good. Overall, I'm a fan of Omni hotels because of their expectional service. This one stands out among the many other Omni's that I've stayed at (including SF, NYC) and among other top flight facilites like the Four Seasons and Fairmount

“Quite the Surprise” After reading some of these reviews, I was expecting the Bates Motel, but was very pleasantly surprised by things. I booked blindly on Priceline, so I wasn't expecting the Ritz. I admit I wasn't entirely pleased with the $18/day for parking and $10/day for wifi, but the room itself was clean and comfortable and what I'd expect for what I was paying. The carpet was a little stained in a couple of places, but not to the point of grossness, and the remote control was spotty on the TV, but that was it as far as the room goes. There was an oddity in that, on the second night of my stay, I noticed that the carpet between the bathroom and the closet was really wet, as though someone had spilled a lot of water. I don't think the toilet had overflowed, as there was no other indication of that. It had mostly dried out by the morning, but when I returned that afternoon, it was wet again -- really wet -- and there were marks in the carpet as though housekeeping had tried to vaccuum or suck it up. I mentioned it to the desk staff on my way out and they immediately responded by moving me to another room and apologizing. The next morning, one of the two shower heads in the new room wasn't working, When I mentioned it to the desk clerk upon checking out, she refunded three days of my wifi service, so I can't complain about that price. That shower is a highlight for me. I so rarely find a powerful shower in a hotel room that it's a delight when there is one. Overall, a pretty good stay and a very friendly and helpful staff.

“Nice place, great staff, a few snafus.” We were coming in to set up an apartment in NY for the time we spend there. We booked a large room with a king bed and notified them we were traveling with a cat. We were assured litter and a box would be in the room upon arrival. It wasn't. Granted, it is NY and you should be able to find anything at any time... with the exception of cat litter. we ripped up some old newspaper and used a cardboard box in case it was needed. We kept her in the bathroom so she wouldn't mess up the carpet or furniture for the two nights we were there. She decided the shower was her best choice but who could blame her after 8 hours in a carrier. The next day we had litter and an apology at the door and things were fine from that point on. The room was extremely clean and posh and the staff remembered our names up until our departure. Location is a bit off the beaten trail but not all that bad. If you get a good rate... grab it!

“Okay Experience” I stayed at this hotel on business. The hotel could not combine my reservations into one (as a third party entity had paid for my stay for one night and I paid for the others) and I had to unfortunately check in and check out each and every day. The check in time was unusually late -- I was told that I could check in at 4PM (this was on the same day as the St. Patrick's Day parade). The hotel is located in Center City. In theory, it is very convenient and the Reading Terminal Market, drug store, Macy's, and other things are nearby. However, I made a point not to wander too far as crime is not unusual for this area. The restaurant, Sole Food, has okay food. I did not find it very delicious, though. I also found that I had to tell them to apply the "Tasty Credits" (apparently, you have a discount on food if you eat in this restaurant which is inside the hotel). I also ordered room service. They did a pretty nice job with the food and delivery. The room service people were very cordial. The hotel is very big. Initially, I had a hotel room near the elevator and I had to change rooms because my neighbors next door were making a lot of noise and because of the noise from the elevator. The front desk had switched me to another room (and I requested that it should be away from the elevator). The new room was nice and quiet. The bed was also very comfortable. I had no problem getting a good night's sleep. Taxis are generally available outside of the hotel. Maggiano's is located close to the restaurant (about a block away) and McCormick and Schmick's is a few blocks away too (albeit in the opposite direction). The hotel is located across from the Pennsylvania Convention Center, which made it convenient in terms of attending my conference. There is a Fed Ex location across from the hotel and also within the Pennsylvania Convention Center itself. The hotel has a computer which is near the front desk in the lobby. It also has a printer attached to it. Use of the computer and printer was free. (However, the front desk people told me that use of the business center's computer would cost a lot and therefore was not free.)

“Very Satisfied” We stayed at the Beresford Arms Monday, March 17, through Wednesday, March 19th. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. We got into the city around 9 am and they held our bags so we could start exploring. The breakfast was great compared to other continental breakfasts we have had. There was a lot of fresh fruit and muffins. And the wine and cheese social hour was a great little treat before heading out for the evening. The room was clean and the shower had great pressure. We stayed in room 702 which is facing the Post Street side. The only complaint that I could give is the same as a few of the others in that the street noise is kind of loud. The garbage trucks came about 6:00 a.m. on Wednesday. But it really didn't bother us too much. The location was great, we were able to walk about everywhere we wanted to go. And we were close to the Powell Bart that took straight to the airport.

“Being pissed off starts at check in...” ... When, at 3.30pm, they tell me I can't actually get into my room because it's being cleaned. So they make me sit in reception like a lemon for thirty minutes. Way to start a business trip, guys! That pretty much sums this place up: grotty, sloppy service, unenjoyable to visit. Oh, and despite it's name it's actually about two miles from downtown. rooms were pretty basic, too. So basically don't bother

“Great Hotel-Wonderful Location” Stayed here New Year's Eve and rented the penthouse and adjoining double room. Kimpton hotels are usually pretty good but this one was wonderful. Embarcadero location is great, hotel ambience & decor is very nice, rooms & hallways were spotless, service was very good (tough test on NYE weekend) but having the top room and fantastic SF Bay views was the reason we stayed here for NYE. Watching the fireworks on the Bay, felt like we were in the middle of the show and was spectacular. Prices are usually reasonable (for SF). Be warned though, the rooms are small, even the Penthouse was not huge, but all in all, a good hotel & if you get a view room - wonderful.

“Love the space” I just got back from another work related trip. This time I was lucky enough to get into the AKA White House which is right by where we meet. It's just like being in a furnished 1 or 2 bedroom apartment ! All the conveniences of home are there. The staff is great & always make you feel welcome. It's very centrally located 2 blocks from the White House.Traffic noise which is an issue in most DC hotels isn't here because the living room not the bedroom gets that. Plus you get high speed wireless internet to boot! Parking if you need it is pricey but that's the case ANYWHERE in DC. This is always the first place I check when we have meetings at our national office. I recommend the AKA VERY highly if you need to stay in DC for business or pleasure

“Good for a short stay” I am one of the very few tripadvisor users reviewing this hotel while not going for a cruise trip. I booked this hotel through Priority Club's point break promotion for merely 5k points, which is a good deal and I believe the right price I would pay for this hotel is around $100-120 per night. The hotel is located near some restaurants, but there is no sightseeing spots within walking distance. So either drive your own car, rent a car, or use the hotel shuttle. I believe they offer free ride in 5-mile range (I didn't try it, but this is according to the hotel guidebook). There is a huge pier, and a nice park with Korean pavillions in a few miles. Except that there is not too much to see. From my observation in the car, the neighborhood might not be dangerous, but also not 100 percent safe. The hotel room is huge and spotless, well equipped with all kinds of accessories. The TV is one of those outdated CRTs, and the variety of programs is limited. I stopped by the fitness room, it's small and like other hotels there is no free-weights. The swimming pool next to it is small but looks decent, I haven't tried it though. One negative thing about this hotel is that as a platinum member, I wasn't greeted or offered room upgrade when I checked in, the only thing the staff has done was changing the normal envelope holding the door card for a more fancy one designed for gold and platinums. They reluctantly gave more two breakfast vouchers after I ask. Even though I understand for point break bookings, elite benefit are not guaranteed, I was still slightly annoyed by their cold attitude toward customers.

“Convienient ~ but not up to date” In May I traveled to Indianapolis to give a presentation, I chose the Indianapolis Marriott East because I wanted to have some quiet in the suburbs and it was convienet to thelocation of my meeting. The hotel's lobby seemed nice, but upon further inspection I found that the entire property was in need of updating. Meaning the lobby felt a bit run down, as did the gym, and the restuarant. The restuarant although clean was really a throw back to 1985 ~ I was disapointed because it has been my expereince that the Marriott brand hotels are ussually very comfortable and near trendy. I got in late due to a weather delay and as a result when I checked in at 1am. When I got to my room it smelled of bug spray, in fact the whole floor did. I was too exhausted to do more than think about having a different room and also needed to be up early to review my presentation. The room was spacious and had the new mattress and linens that are now standard at all Marriott properies (at least in my experience). I stayed on the concierge level. The coffee was really instant coffee -made by a novel -robot type machine.... Although mildly entertaining I would've prefered real brewed coffee. In a word that coffee was awful. The assortment of breakfast pastry was limited and there was no milk for my cereal, until I started hunting for the attendant... She was pleasant. The staff was great but all in all I did not feel I got what I paid for and really wish that I would've stayed elsewhere. I will not be back to the property if I can help it.

“Not good.” Unfortunately I found this La Quinta in a state of disrepair. Everything needs updating from the carpet to theTV to the paint. The check in staff was excellent, but our room was not cleaned. This hotel is in a decent location but I probably wont try to stay here again. The rate was good $84.00, I guess you get what you pay for. The bed was sub par as well, with a hole in the sheet to boot.

“On the Fence” My room was on the function room floor, it was strange to walk out of my guestroom to see a buffet station set near my door. Bathroom was beautiful, the bath tub was a nice size and at first the water pouring from the ceiling was fun but it splashed all over the glass wall. It's more of a conversation piece but impractical. The Molten Brown shampoos were mounted on the wall in the shower instead of those environmentally unfriendly miniature bottles. Somehow the germaphobe side of me was grossed out by the thought of someone else using products from the same bottle. For a dark rainy city the decor was a little too gloomy. It's a chic colour scheme but walking in at night after dinner I was left with a lonely feeling. Staff were unimpressionable, neither great nor bad. The gym didn't have windows, I prefer to see natural light when I workout.

“Pool not warm and too crowded breakfast” The breakfast was like fighting everyone for the same waffles or toast, way to stressful! And not enough seats, so people would watch you until you stood up to leave to snag your table. Nice it is a free breakfast but too chaotic!! The pool was freezing. Mind you, I am just getting around to this review from June. But keep this in mind if you aren't traveling in August or September where the nights will be very cool. The room was clean and suited our needs. We messed up and brought a frozen pizza and then we realized no stove! Haha. Only stove top and microwave. Decent location but pretty far from any restaurants!

“Classy, elegant and central!” One can appreciate this hotel more after reading up it's history; fascinating stories which make you appreciate this place even more. Omni Hotels online booking was seamless including online check-in which then allows you to bypass the front desk check-in line as an envelope with your room key will be waiting at the desk. The room we had was well appointed, 2 big double beds, triple sheeted, double glazed window and with a well stocked bathroom including terry cloth bath robes. I found the mattress too soft but that is a personal preference! WiFi at no cost for 'Select Guest' members in addition to a complimentary bottle of water delivered to the room when beds were turned down and a very welcome complimentary early morning small thermos bottle with coffee delivered to the door. The room service card to request this service has an option to 'deliver in room' or ' knock and leave at door' if you don't want to be disturbed; very thoughtful! The location in Downtown Boston is the best, walk to the Commons and the Theatre district. Valet parking is available but there are less costly self-park garages in walking distance too. Overall, I really enjoyed the whole experience and will certainly return to this great hotel.

“OK for a Night” We were traveling to Georgia but flew into the nearest airport, Jacksonville. We stayed here the night before we flew out. Sam at the front desk was great - wonderful personality. The room was spacious, but just OK. It smelled and not all of the lights worked. The price is right for only needed somewhere to sleep overnight.

“Owwwwww! Really great stay.” Great hotel. Modern and classic-chic. Very good location just one block from the waterfront and great restaurants. Really nice and big room with super confort bed. Room with lots of amenities. Nice bathroom. I had a great view from my room. They also let me check in at 8am. They have a great restaurant inside, a Starbucks and a guy in the lobby that can help with maps and info about the area. Really close from South Station and the Silverline stop right in front the hotel. I ordered room service (food) and the only complaint is the 4$ they charge for delivery (which is not great cause the restaurant is inside the hotel). Maybe a 10 min drive to the airport.

“Nice Hotel, Nice Location, A Little Dated” Stayed here for two nights in February. Was a nice hotel, with great views, but the rooms felt small and older. I'd suggest requesting the newer tower (there are two towers to the hotel) when booking. Overall, a nice property, but not worth more than $160ish per night in my opinion. I'd look around and see what else is out there, if the rate is exceeding $160ish.
“Good location, not great cottages” Great location but cottages were a bit shabby. Had ants in the bathroom. Great place to stay cos you can walk down to OB, OB is excellent

“Bright Lights, Big City” If your primary NYC interests are Times Square and the theatre district, the Marriott Marquis is a good choice. Like the neighborhood around it, it is filled with activity. It operates very efficiently for a big hotel, with easy checkin and checkout. Its lobby cafe offers a great breadkfast buffet (although at NYC prices). The revolving bar on top, The View, has superb views of the city's skyline (again NYC prices for drinks). The rooms are typical Marriott, adequate but not luxurious (no refrigerator or mini-bar). I was surprised and pleased at how quiet the rooms were, given all the hub-bub on the streets below. I did not try the fitness center, but a colleague did and reported it well equipped. One pet peeve: Marriott charges for the in-room WiFi. On the other hand, if your business or pleasure in NYC is going to take you primarily out of the theatre district, I would stay elsewhere, as it too hard to get in and out of there in a cab (on foot is better) with all the traffic in Times Square and the theatre district.

“Comfortable well located property” This is an ideal property for business travellers, close to the city approximately 35 minutes on the light railway and minutes (walk) from the airport. Good Breakfast, prompt check in and out, professional and efficient concierge. Room was large and comfortable. Good wifi access in the lobby. Bar food a little expensive but quality of the food was good. Staff in general were very pleasant.

“Adequate Westin” As a Starwood preferred guest, I've stayed at many Westins. This one was merely adequate. As others have noted, the location is really poor -- completely out of the way, although you can walk to the North End in about 25 minutes. The room had a good view -- floor-to-ceiling windows and the heavenly bed, which was good. But otherwise, just a standard room, although clean. The lobby was cavernous and lacking any charm and there was always a long line for the desks. They don't appear to have enough staff. Valet parking was over $40! We never ate at the hotel, but did enjoy having the STarbucks in the lobby. The gym and pool were nice. All in all, it was fine, but I wouldn't choose to stay there again,given all the great hotels in Boston more centrally located and it certainly wasn't inexpensive.

“Great base to tour city” Stayed here for 4 nights in December. Our room over looked Beach street and like another reviewer mentioned was noisy with the sound of street car as not double glassed. However when in San Francisco you expect to hear that noise. It reminded where I was. We booked the hotel through our travel agent as part of a package deal on a cheap airfare to New York with a stop over in San Francisco which I had always wanted to visit. The hotel wasn't the cheapest of those given to choose from but had better reviews than others and based in Fisherman wharf area. Check in was easy and staff very friendly. The room was fine and clean which was what we wanted. The bed was big and one of those number beds. The area is easy to catch cable car, pier 39 close by and easy sight seeing. I hop next to hotel for breakfast which we went to once. Would stay here again if I needed to be in the area.

“Wonderful staff and a great location” This is our second time at the Marriott Liberty station. Great location - quite, pretty neighborhood, park behind the hotel with views of downtown. Nice restaurants in walking distance and an easy drive to all major attractions. Downtown is a 10 min drive away. Three minutes from the airport. Free internet, free coffee throughout the day, free airport shuttle. Opt for the breakfast package - well worth the money. Staff extremely friendly and accommodating. Only issue is for those who are sensitive to noise - if you're not on the top floor, you could be disturbed by the walking above you. They moved us the second night to a top floor upon our request.

“Fantastic!” A fantastic hotel. We arrived early for check in and our room was not available but the hotel staff arranged for us to have access to the pool area whilst they prepared the room. The pool area is not large however it was not crowded and we had a pleasant hour or so relaxing on the double loungers. Unlike other reviewers I liked the fact that you could hear the hustle and bustle of the trains running past at street level below. My partner arranged for us to stay in a loft room in the enclave tower part of the hotel. It was well worth the price! Immediately on entering the room I LOVED it!. The room had a stylish decor and great furnishings. The bed was extremely comfortable. The bathroom was amazing with a large jacuzzi bath (big enough for two) and a large separate shower. I particularly liked the fact that the bathroom had a large hatch area opening onto the bedroom area - great for watching tv whilst relaxing in the bubbles. The hotel is in a great location for the Gaslamp District and all it has to offer.

“Very Nice Hotel” I spent this past New Year's Eve here with a friend. Unfortunately, we never made it to the hip bar at the hotel but we did eat at the restaurant Heartbeat, which was excellent! The staff at the hotel was excellent! The rooms at this location are a small, but clean. The beds, as always, were comfortable. The location was nice, although my cab driver couldnt seem to find it. The atmosphere is fantastic! Very chic, and laid back. If you want a lot of space in your hotel room, you are probably going to have a problem here, but if you dont mind a small room, then I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Shiny New and Nice” Never been to Columbus before, but the hotel appears to be fairly new and in a relatively new shopping area of town. Cab from the airport was about $35-$40, but Hilton has a free shuttle van to businesses nearby and that worked well. They even took us to the airport after we checked out (for a fee of course), but it's not a regularly scheduled service -- you have to ask. The room was spacious and nicely appointed, with a really comfortable bed and a coffeemaker. There is a monitor in the lobby where you can print your boarding pass at no charge (wish I'd seen that prior to paying for access to the business center). There is a good restaurant right across the parking lot (Eddie Merlot). Overall I'd stay here again if I needed to travel to this area.

“Great Location, fancy hotel, luxury rooms for a reasonable price” Unique architecture from the outside. My room was a deluxe which had a view of the Hancock tower (the best view of Chicago by the way is from the bar at the top of this building). The Hotel is in the heart of the action and next to designer shops and restaurants. The rooms are large,clean, fancy and modern. Bathroom comes with all the extras (slippers, TV) great bed and desk. Staff is very good and even says "bonjour " in French to keep the Sofitel theme although no one really speaks french. Bottom line, this hotel has a very expensive feel to it at a reasonable price.

“Small rooms, nice hotel” Had stayed here before, both times on priceline/hotwire hidden deals, and both times have been left with the same impression: it's a nice hotel but wow, are the rooms small. I actually banged my leg on the bed trying to walk around it because there was so little space between it and the wall. Other than that, everything was fine: nicely decorated, comfortable bed, pretty good restaurant, great service. A little annoyed that we had to pay $3 for wine glasses and a corkscrew from room service, but at least they came quickly. If you don't mind extra small, "boutique" style room (ie plan on going out more than staying in and working), the amenities are nice and the location, while not on Michigan Ave itself, is great.

“This is a cute hotel with dvd players...” This is a cute hotel with dvd players & little kitchenettes in the room. It's a close walk to the space needle & you can easily catch the monorail or bus downtown, but if you want to walk it's about 1-2 miles to the market. The staff was very helpful & polite, Barbara was awesome. There are lots of cool places by to eat, try the mecca for a good breakfast. The were renovating on our floor but it was still clean & nice. The rooftop deck offers a great view.

“Washington DC's best hotel” Arriving during 102F weather, the cool a/c enviroment in the Sofitel was a nice break. I give highest mark for the front desk staff as well the comfortable bar area off the lobby and the comfortable room with very comfortable bed. The hotel is located just two blocks from the White House and only one block from the metro stop so it is within a short walk to many places to visit if the weather cooporates. The only negative aspect is internet which very expensive if accessed in your room however they do offer free access to three computers in the lobby. The one down side is dining due to the hotel's central location. Unless they are frequented by visitors, most cafes are closed on the weekend as they cater to the office staff. Having stayed in Sofitel hotels in different parts of the world, I am struck by the uniform high quality of their hotels and staff.

“ESPERIENZA POSITIVA” Hotel curato, non proprio in posizione centrale ma con servizi pubblici nelle immediate vicinanze per raggiungere il centro in 5 minuti. Personale accogliente e preparato. Ottima la possibilità di parcheggio gratuito per i clienti. Camere ampie e con buon livello di pulizia. Unica pecca l'impossibilità di fare colazione in hotel, ma per il resto tutto veramente ok.

“Good choice for airport travel” If you are looking for a place to stay near the airport this is a good choice. I can't complain about the room, it was clean & comfortable and actually had a very nice view of the skyline. Service was excellent and I was easily able to print a boarding pass in the business center. The free breakfast was good & they had Sunday papers available. The hotel is a 5 minute drive down Bartram Ave. to the airport. I would definitely stay here again.

“They don't seem to have their act together” Our stay at the Marriot Courtyard in Denver was very strange, very strange indeed! Yes, the staff is wonderful, the rooms are very clean, and it’s a great location, but this hotel needs some serious logistics work. We booked this hotel, highly rated in the TA, using the Denver Mile High Holidays deal which gave us an amazing price, but there were many small problems that really brought the irritation levels up throughout our 7 day stay. I hope these problems were not the result of the great price and just bad planning. We first arrived to the hotel early, about 11:00, and took the chance that we would be able to check in. Our room was not ready (they seem to assign rooms as they take the reservations), and we were told that we should try about 4:00. Seemed a bit late, but we were with our son, and could keep ourselves busy for the afternoon. They allowed us to store our bags, so it was not a big deal. When we came back at 4:00 the room was still not ready, and we waited again and finally checked in about 4:30pm. Our daughter joined us on the third day and we checked her into her own room. It was about 3:00pm and her room was not ready, again, until about 4:30 or so. They put her in a room two floors below us because they were going to start renovation on our floor the next day. We had three more nights at the hotel so I asked if this renovation would impact our room. They were surprised that we were booked on that floor in the first place, and offered to move us the next morning. Again they were very accommodating and left the choice up to us... we moved the next day. The new room was smaller, and we were comfortable at first. Our daughter’s room had a malfunctioning thermostat in her room which resulted in no heat. She called down around 1:30 a.m and they sent a man to look at it, he adjusted the thermostat, and then sat down on her bed to wait about 30 minutes to see if it was, in fact, corrected. It was late and she was a bit uncomfortable with this so she told him it was fine. He did offer to bring up blankets however. The heater never did work so she rolled up cocoon style to stay as warm as she could, not getting any sleep at all. They moved her to another room the next day. This second room also needed attention to the bathroom light which she “jiggled” to get the light to work, and left the light on the rest of her stay. Our second room was next to hers - it had TV reception problems; the engineer they sent up had to adjust the cable, and it worked well for a day or two. We did our best to play with the cable to get it to work again. We were comfortable until our final day. Denver temperatures were in the 20’s that day, and our room was very cold. We contacted the desk and they said that they would reset the thermostat and also have an engineer look into the problem. When we returned from our day in the city, the room was freezing. I called the desk and they told me they had to replace the heat pump and it should warm shortly. I did see the engineers in the hallway, and they said the the broken heat pump caused heating problems for many rooms in the hotel. The room did warm up for our last night. The hotel staff did give us post cards and phone calls apologizing for the heating problems. After reviewing our bills for both rooms, we started to realize how inconvenient our stay had been for us and for our daughter. We talked to the desk and asked if there would be any compensation for all the trouble we had to endure, especially my daughter’s first night where she had no heat at all. The desk attendant checked with her manager, and they said that they would give us an additional 500 points to our rewards program, only to find that they were never added when we checked our account nearly a week after we left the hotel. A call to the Marriott Rewards contact corrected this, though it shouldn't have been necessary. To top it all off, they charged us an additional $3.50 on the credit card which was different from the bill they slipped under our door. Apparently we were charged additional for a bottle of water that we did not drink. The rooms are nice, clean and staff is friendly. It feels like a hotel that is in transition, and it’s renovation seems to really have the staff confused at the expense of the guests. Frankly, we are surprised with our visit to this Courtyard. We have stayed in Marriott hotels before -- in Denver and other cities -- using the TA recommendations. Very rarely are we disappointed, and this trip to Denver was definitely one of those rare occasions.

“Nice hotel, small rooms but good design” Hi, We booked this hotel through Priceline using the "Name your own price" feature. Bid won at $75. After having checked the review in this website, I thought it would have been a crappy hotel. Not at all. Even though the rooms are small, the staff is friendly, and the decor is really nice. Comfy beds and nice bathroom. Definitely worth the price.

“Family Enjoyed Stay!” We like to stay at a Marriott Hotels and Fairfield is usually our pick.Although my husband liked other ones better I thought it served us well.At the start at check in we were selected as family of the day and was upgraded to a suite room and grandson got to watch a free movie that night (RIO).Also at check in they have freshed baked cookies (yummie) and cold water with lemons to cool you from the heat.A very nice idea. The staff was extremely nice where as all the staff members had something to say to you!First hotel I"ve stayed in where they ALL made you feel welcomed.It makes your stay more enjoyable because of the staff. This hotel includes breakfast which we didnt get to eat i (took it to our room) because it was so crowded.They did have a good selection along with Texas shaped waffles. My grandson wanted to go swimming.On the website they mentioned an outdoor pool which is actually at the Residence Inn next door which you are welcomed to use.We took a short walk over and liked the outdoor pool.There was a hot tub there but I use the word "hot" loosely.Not very.Then we stopped at the pool at the Fairfield on the way back.This one was indoors and we stayed a short time because it was cold and my grandson slipped on tile flooring.I saw another child slip as well.The tile was very wet and hard to walk on then my grandson got out of the pool and went to walk to other side and slipped -we then left after that.He had a hard time walking to his towel because it was so slippery.Think they need to make it a little more safer with taking out the tile and just having cement for more leverage like other pools we have used. We were able to walk to Market Square and then around San Antonio.Was easy to get a taxi to take us back. No problem with parking,which is free.Some hotels there will charge you to park.

“Stunning/Newly renovated” My husband and I stayed here over 4th of July weekend with another couple. The location is excellent as it is next to Horton Plaza and the gaslamp Quarter. It has recently undergone a 2 year renovation and is absolutely beautiful. A fantasy art deco bar in the lobby/marbled floor entry/ chocolate brown and blue billy haines era furnishings /incredible chandaliers are all part of its charm. The rooms are upscale and tasteful with every amenity- bowl sinks/glass showers/travertine floors/bose radios etc.

“convenient and comfortable” Stayed for one night while on business at UPenn. Check-in was easy-- I arrived in the morning and was disappointed to learn that early check-in has a fee. However, they held my bags for free while I went out to a series of meetings downtown. Very convenient location for all museums and downtown businesses and restaurants. Multiple drugstores nearby with late hours for purchasing snacks (good, since many of the downtown fast-food places aren't open after 10pm). The room was small but very comfortable. I had no trouble using the free internet connection, and I also used the gym, which was quite nice (though small). I enjoyed the free water coolers in the hallways. View was nothing special-- side of other ugly buildings-- but my room had high ceilings, which I liked. Sleep was comfortable, no noise issues. Very easy working with the staff for all my needs. Used their computers in the lobby to print a presentation, and the staff helped me when the computer stopped responding. Very friendly! Overall, thoroughly pleased! I didn't pay for this room, so I can't comment on the price or value.

“pretty good but” The staff in the hotel were friendly, the room was a good size and clean. Bed was comfortable. However, this hotel is not in a location where it is easy to walk around because it is on the side of a freeway. Despite there being no grocery store or 7/11 in walking distance, the hotel had minimal food available outside of one or two vending machines. That's not such a big deal I guess but we were annoyed at the hotel staff for organising local limo drivers who had set prices for their services. Three times we requested at taxi and three times hotel staff organized limo drivers who they seemed to know very well. These drivers did not have vehicles with meters and therefore just named their price. The drivers were not cheap by any means however they were punctual. On the whole though, we were dissatisfied with this element of our stay because we felt like we paid more for drivers than we would have paid for a taxi. For example, a ride to the local shopping mall which was literally 3 1/2 minutes away cost $10 and the driver waited for a tip. Someone should check on him cause he's probably still standing there waiting! Hotel was ok, breakfast was really good, location was better for people with a car but hooking us up with over priced local car services was unappreciated to say the least.

“Great location, nice hotel” I stayed here one night, checked out the next. Learned my flight out was cancelled (east coast/Hurricane Irene storms?) and happily checked back in! I was able to walk everywhere I wanted and needed to go. My meetings were about 4 blocks away. Macy's is across the street. Reading Terminal market out another door. The bars and restaurants in Rittenhouse Square were a nice 10-15 min walk. Restaurants on South 13th were even closer! Both rooms I had were a very nice size and clean. Staff was very friendly. I am lucky this is on my company's approved list.

“Very good experience” I just came from NYC and I had a very good experience in this hotel. I stayed there for 15 days with my wife and my three-month baby. I got there at 9:30am and check in time was 3pm. At 10:30am, as soon as maid cleaned up an available room they allowed us to live in. So We could enjoy NYC. Staff was very friendly and helpful. They arranged a crib as soon we asked for. Room are modern, well furnished and clean. I think that hotel was open two or three years ago. It has a good matress, a 2-door wardrobe with a safe where fit a laptop, coffee facilities, desk, wi-fi internet, flat panel TV. Bathroom is great. At front desk there are two complimentary computers and printer. They serve a basic breakfast. It ́s not that breakfast but enough to hold untill lunch time. And it ́s complimentary! Breakfast was apple, bagels, waffle, oatmeal, corn flakes, muffins, pastries, sliced bread, hamburger, sausage, yogurt, coffe, milk, tea, boiled eggs, cream cheese, butter, maple honey, orange and apple juice. Hotel is located in Chinatown. It ́s closed to Grand Station (one block) and Bowery Station (three blocks). Within a walking distance from Soho, East Village, Ground Zero. About 10 minuntes. Canal Street is right there. I recommend car service to airport. I paid $ 65 for a Lincoln, with tax, to Newark. Almost the same price of a yellow cab but more convenient. I would stay there again.

“Excellent Hotel and Great Location” My daughter and I spent three days at the Holiday Inn. I think it is the best Holiday Inn I have ever stayed at. We stayed in the annex which is in the same building as Denny's. The beds were wonderful, rooms clean and quiet. We were within 2 blocks of In-N-Out Burgers which I would highly recommend. We took the Alcatraz tour at Pier 33 was half mile away. From our hotel which is at 1300 Columbus Avenue, we walked 1.5 miles to Union Square. Another option would be to take the #30 bus for $2. The bus stop is across the street at the Marriott. To return to Fisherman's Wharf, bus 30 bus stop is right before the tunnel on Stockton. It is where Stockton St. becomes a two way street. We were within a few blocks of Lombard St. This hotel is in a safe neighborhood and great for families as well. I would definitely return for the excellent price and quality of hotel.

“Great location, but a few things to keep in mind” Yes, great location to the attractions. It would be classified as a "motel" with outside walk ways. The room was clean, but dated. Parking is rather tight and extremely limited. If you are booking this room through a non-Best Western search engine, you may want to see how the parking is categorized - is it free or is there a charge? I had this debate at the front desk and I showed my printouts. Not the nicest conversation to have when you are checking in. If I had to say a negative is trying to pull in/out of the property with a car during rush hour. The hotel is close to 101 and you must have a ton of patience and the skill to pull out/in timely when your opportunity arises.

“Loved it” I stayed here while attending a conference at the Marriott across the street. This was cheaper and more comfortable. As other reviewers have noted, this is a gem of a hotel. It's a true suite, with living room, full kitchen, and bedroom. The living room has a sofabed, sitting chair, coffee table and 32" LCD TV. There is a small dining table/desk next to the kitchen. The kitchen has microwave, two burner oven, dishwasher, coffee maker, fridge. Also plates, pots/pans and silverware. The room was clean and comfortable with no obvious signs of wear. The king size bed was also comfy, though not as high end as you would find in a nicer hotel. There is a regular tube TV in the bedroom. The free buffet breakfast had scrambled eggs, meats, cereal, make your own waffles, etc. There is also a dinner with a different menu Mon-Thurs but I did not have that. There is a gym inhouse, but you can use the Crunch gym next door (same building) that is much bigger and has everything. The entrance is not much to look at; just an elevator to the sixth floor where reception is. But the bellman was friendly and the reception desk was efficient and very friendly. It does cost a lot to park here (I think $42/night so don't bring a car). There is a small store next to reception, open 24/7. Free wired and wireless internet in the room. Only minor complaint is that the walls are somewhat thin so if the neighbor raises his voice I can hear it. Also, I can hear water running next door. But all in all I would definitely stay here again. It's much more comfortable and better value than the big hotels nearby.

“Great Stay” The hotel is in a fabulous location and is on an upscale tier. Most of the museums and monuments are within walking distance even with young children. We were able to check in early and were granted a late check out. We stayed on the 6th floor and did not find the room to be too small (even with 2 kids) and other rooms on six appeared comparable - - the size is no different than a Courtyard or other chain hotels (ditto re: pool). We paid less than $140 a night (Thurs-Sun) but would be willing to pay up to $199 if we visited DC again. Be sure to go to the "Deals at this Hotel" tab on the hotel's website for the best rate. In response to the hotel's confirmation e-mail I requested a room with a view and asked again upon check-in. What we got couldn’t have been better - - a view of the plaza below and the Washington Monument, truly spectacular. When I wasn't staring out the window, I was watching the 32" flat screen HDTV. I've never grasped the concept of valet parking, which is the subject of many complains throughout TripAdvisor. Why surrender your keys to a stranger, pay a premium rate, and be required to wait 15 minutes for your car when you can walk 5 minutes and fetch your own car? There are several self park garages in the vicinity; pmi-parking.net is a good resource. I parked on 12th b/w E&F for $20 per 24hrs and it’s open on Sundays. I even emailed the night manager of PMI parking in advance to confirm rates and times and received an almost immediate, and courteous, response. The only negatives I can think of are (1) that food after 7 or 8 PM is hard to come by unless you want to eat in the hotel or are looking for an upscale restaurant, and (2) after sightseeing for 5 hours we would return to the room around 2PM to find that it had not been cleaned (housekeeping works until 5:30). As for food alternatives, there is a pizza place on F b/w 12th and 13th which is open until 10PM weekdays and 8:45 on Saturday which was good. Also a McD's near the Metro Center station. Starbucks and Corner Bakery are convenient for breakfast.

“A little off the edge of downtown but nice place to stay” The lobby was clean, staff was friendly, nice room. Closer to the sports venues. You can cut down your cab fare by staying there instead of downtown. However, if downtown is your destination, then you might want to stay some place closer to it. Everything a Courtyard should be. Coffee and computers in the lobby. They have a bar - beers were $3. Room was great, had a pull out sofa bed.
“立地はよいです ” ちょうど、日航ホテルのまん前にあって立地は良いです。室内プールがあるのもGOOD。ヒルトン自体個人的には、あまり’好みではないのですが、まあ、この値段だったらこんなもんかなって感じです。

“Nothing too special about this hotel” I booked 3 nights at 89 USD per night plus tax, and rang through to ask for an upgrade using my marriott gold card. I was told this wouldnt be a problem. At check-in, no upgrade was available, although give Igor his due he arranged it for my final two nights - so I stayed in a king suite. Whilst the hotel is centrally located (and the fire station really isnt right next door) I was pleased not to hear as much noise as people had described. So, what I didn't like about the hotel - the pool area didn't have proper changing rooms and was starting to look shabby, tiles coming off the walls etc. The soda machines were out of order on almost every floor. The hotel doesnt really have a proper restaurant, so watch out if you like your roomservice or dining in. On the positive side, it was reasonably priced and very central, the rooms were clean (apart from a comments card which had already been completed by another guest). I'd imagine there would be nicer places to stay for not too much more money.

“Great location, great room with view” I liked it! Beautifully updated room with a nice view of the city. Very close to Times Square, I walked everywhere, MOMA, Central Park, restaurants, shopping... I would stay here again. One of the more reasonably priced hotels in the city. I would have given it a higher rating but the room was too warm no matter how much we fiddled with the thermostat and room service was slow (1 hour wait for breakfast).

“Gutes Hotel mit toller Aussicht” Die Aussicht ist das Highlight des Hotels, aber auch die Zimmer sind groß und gut ausgestattet. Nur bei der Sauberkeit wird etwas gespart. In der Nähe befindet sich eine Buslinie mit der man auf der 42nd Street zum Times Square fahren kann und 10 min Fußweg die Grand Central Station. Gleich um die Ecke kann man frühstücken oder im Deli was besorgen.....

“Great value for the price” Got a room for 130$ using Priceline. Spacious, clean, recent, great view, I am short of superlatives regarding the room itself. Water pressure was great in the shower, Internet access worked great (wired) and it had a lot of space. The bathroom was superb (with marble and a sliding door!). Went to the Altitude bar on the 22nd floor right before the game, the drinks were good and the price was ok. Couldn't sleep with the windows open because of the noise, but soundproof windows and A/C did the trick. Had breakfast delivered at 6:00 AM (the earliest). It was a tad on the cold side.

“An Affordable Hotel for a Family looking for Adventure in NYC on a Budget” I am a faithful tripadvisor user and trusted the reviews on this site and, boy, they did not let me down. The Herald Square Hotel was an affordable option for a single mom and her children. Not only did we save money, but we did so in comfort, cleanliness, and with a great location. As mentioned before, the beds are pure heaven and we all got five great nights of well-needed sleep. Our room faced the street and there was never any distruptive nights due to the noise from the street. The bedding and linens were equally nice and VERY clean. I was shocked when I got there and found that each bed had FOUR fluffy, comfortable pillows. I am a person who sleeps with at least two pillows and was estatic to see I would have two pillows without having to call down to the front desk. The room itself was a spacious double room that was well-maintained and cleaned daily. My kids had plenty of room to move around and I felt comfortable with them playing on the carpet with their toys. I was in one of the rooms that had not been refurbished, but the bathroom was fine. It was clean, had plenty of hot water, and fabulous fluffy white towels. One day we left the room early and came back for a mini rest pretty early in the day. By 9:00 am our room was already cleaned. That was a nice surprise, too. The hotel is located at 31st and 5th and has two convenient subway stops that are easily walked to. For eating, there are Speedy's, Dunkin Donuts, and Empire Pizza, all for a quick bite to eat. There are even two pharmacy stores (CVS and Duane Reade's) close by. With two kids, it seemed I had to pop into a pharmacy at least once a day...allergy medicine, snacks, etc. I also have to say that the staff was really friendly. The staff always greeted us and asked how our day was and what we planned/had done for the day. I was impressed because they always greeted my children. We enjoyed the complimentary coffee, hot chocolate, and biscotti. I highly recommend the Herald Square and plan to stay there again if I am lucky enough to visit the Big Apple again. This was a very FAMILY FRIENDLY hotel. love the NYC and the Herald Square.

“Outstanding Stay in a Convenient Location!” We stayed at the Westin Times Square November 22-24 while in NYC to see the 2005 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade; I found a great deal on an Executive Club Level room through Expedia. The location was outstanding! I've stayed at many hotels in NYC & this was probably the best stay I've had. The hotel is located right in the heart of Times Square, 2 subway stops are less then half a block away which is very convenient. The staff that we encountered were all very professional & pleasant (no one hinted at being tipped as mentioned in some of the other reviews. However I recently noticed that an unauthorized $10 "tip" was charged to my credit card which I plan to look into.) Since it was Thanksgiving week, at check-in we were given a packet of information about the Macy's parade, other events in the area & some of the big stores' holiday hours which was nice. The hotel elevators were very fast, we never had to wait for one.
