Our room was very spacious, comfortable & clean, with modern decor & a live plant on the desk, a Bose radio/CD player on the night stand & a bathrobe; 2 bottles of imported water, Starbucks in-room coffee & a morning newspaper were provided complementary each day. One nice room feature was the windows in our room could be opened a bit if you'd like some outside air or want to bask in the sounds of NYC for a moment without leaving your room. The Heavenly bed was just that, VERY heavenly! The Heavenly shower was also nice with extra room, dual shower heads & deluxe cotton towels. The evening turn down service was a nice touch complete with chocolates on the pillow & a little card stating the next day's weather forecast. The complimentary breakfast was fine, it consisted of the usual coffee, juice, bagels, Danish & cereal. We didn't get a chance to take advantage for the complimentary hors d'oeuvres in the evening because we were out & about. There is an AMC theatre, Starbucks & a few restaurants connected to the hotel, you can reach them all without stepping outside which was convenient. The Westin tends to be quite pricey for obvious reasons but if you can get a good deal (esp on the Club Level) go for it! I would stay here again & recommend it to others. For a casual lunch or dinner try Viva Pancho @ W. 44th, a good, moderately priced Mexican restaurant that's close by. A good place to catch a bite after the theatre is John's Pizzeria also @ W. 44th. I would also recommend getting tickets to see Avenue Q, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels or Spamalot, we thoroughly enjoyed all of these shows. The TKTS booth is a great (safe/legit) place to get good seats at a discount (they accept cash only); for shows that are sold out try the theatre box office, most of the time a limited amount of SRO seats can be purchased for a fraction of the price as soon as the box office opens but be prepared to stand after walking around the city all day! Have a good stay in NYC!

“Seattle Secret” One of my best friends turned me on to the Inn at El Gaucho. The Inn is above the ever-popular Steak House. The hotel is small, well appointed with high quality furniture, flat-screens, and crisp sheets. The staff is helpful and caring. My corner suite overlooked the bay. This is a great place to stay on a business trip if you do not need all the features of a full service property.

“Fine property; service needs work” I stayed at the Denver Ritz Carlton for a weekend in March. I was very excited about the stay, as it had been a long time since I had been to a RC property, and this one is new. I got a decent weekend rate for a room on the club floor. First impressions matter. I walked up to the hotel with a suitcase and backpack, and no one offered to help me, or even open the door. The front desk staff were efficient, but not very friendly. No one accompanied me up to my room to show me how the gadgets worked. I loved the room, and it was spotlessly clean. Just what you'd expect int terms of a super comfy bed with silky sheets, a marvelous bathtub with thirsty towels, a deep soaking tub, and cushy robes. What I did not like was that the cable to the TV was unplugged and it took me a while to understand that it was not the remote that was faulty. A call to maintenance had someone up quickly to locate the problem and fix it. That evening I was baffled by both bedside lamps not working; I tried switching lightbulbs, and determined that they were burned out. Why these were not replaced after previous guests had stayed there is beyond me. Again, a call to maintenance had someone up to replace them right away. The one exception to the staff issues were the helpful people in the club lounge. They went above and beyond in responding to my needs, remembering my drink preferences, and generally being friendly. The club lounge is a beautiful space, but I was disappointed with the scanty food selection, and was concerned that food items (such as cottage cheese, yogurt, meat sandwiches, etc.) were set out and left unrefrigerated for hours. When items ran out at breakfast, they were not automatically replaced. We had to ask for more bread, more butter, etc. I attempted to eat at Elway's for lunch, but did not succeed. Even though the place was about half full, the staff was inattentive, and when they did take my order, what came out (after about 15 minutes) was not what I had ordered. I did not have time to wait for the correct dish, so I left hungry. I was grateful not to be charged for the potato chips I ate while waiting. I had one service in the spa, which is also a breathtaking space. The facial was superb, but the esthetician talked the whole time and it wasn't very relaxing. All in all, I believe the Ritz Carlton deserves a four rating -- five for the rooms and physical property, but only two-three for the service. That latter can certainly be improved. It's interesting that I wrote a detailed comment card before checkout and responded to an online questionnaire about my experience; it has been a month and no response from the hotel. Stay here with confidence, but don't be surprised by the amateur service the hotel is currently providing.

“Extremely Poor Service at the Champagne Bar” We recently stopped in for a bottle of champagne and cheese plate. Both were excellent. They were not overly busy, but steady. We had a $140 bottle of champagne - the waiter poured the first glass and we never saw him again - the champagne a little bit away from the table in a cooler/urn - my husband finally got up, retrieved the bottle and refilled out glasses. Atmosphere was festive. Plenty of staff standing around chatting - but not attending to customers - many people commented to us as they had similar experiences. A few couples walked out.

“What a great hidden Treasure” I tend to stay at alot of hotels in SF, and I had always seen this hotel, and 1 day, decided to try it. The staff knocks you out......Very Friendly, wanting to make sure that you enjoyed your stay, and if there is anything they forgot. Rooms are nice, and a flat screen tv. I think what they have done with the TV's in the bathroom is a terrific idea. How nice to lay in a tub after a hard day and enjoy the tv. The resturant for lunch was nice. It's not a bad walk to the financial district, it took me 10 minutes and I sort of shopped on the way down.

“Elegant, stately” We recently stayed at the Melrose for one night. This hotel is so elegant and stately. It was built in the 1920's and has undergone a complete renovation in recent years. We stayed in a corner room/suite with a king size bed. The room was HUGE... full sitting area, desk and bed were in one very large room. The bathroom, closet area is in a separate room and again the bathroom was HUGE. 'Just absolutely gorgeous. Luxurious bedding - glassware (including wine glasses) - a coffee table with top tier local magazines - floor to ceiling drapes. The staff were friendly and offered excellent service. 100% no smoking. 'Only valet parking and they charge $24.00/per night! Even though the neighborhood is probably not one in which you would want to park on the street, this exclusive/expensive parking policy always takes me back a bit. But what does one do? The Melrose is not doing anything that other downtown hotels in other cities do but it still seems like a rip-off.
“EXCELLENT!” This property is new and immaculate. Very much enjoyed the stay and would recommend for individuals, families, business or pleasure. Great location - great amenities - overal - GREAT!

“Better-than-average business-class hotel” What stands out here, as other reviewers have noted, is the comfort of the rooms. A huge bed, with high-quality bedding, and a large flat-screen TV were very welcome. The staff are friendly and knowledgeable too. I was here for a conference, but would happily stay here again with my own money. Only niggles: why can't you open the windows in large American hotels? This is infuriating (and the Nikko certainly isn't alone here). Aircon shouldn't be necessary in San Francisco in winter, yet with sealed windows it is. Some of the rooms have very uninspiring views, but I guess this is standard in downtown.

“nur im notfall” haben an einem messewochenende 74$ pro nacht gezahlt. frühstück okay. streetparking. geht kostenlos am we, sonst problematisch. zimmer alt und abgewohnt, fenster sehr dünn, teppich fleckig. infrarotlicht im bad es war okay aber ganz bestimmt nich meine erste wahl!!!

“A it disappointing for a Residence Inn” I am a Marriott Platinum member so I have a good bit of background for comparison purposes. We are a family of 5 so we often stay at the Residence Inn's We travel on vacation. This one needs some work. They are beginning a remodeling, which is good. The staff attitude is average. The room we reserved was not available and they did accomodate us to our satisfaction but not without a lot of pushing from me. The hotel is a bit noisy - walls are probably too thin. The location is very good for anything you want to do in San Diego. You will need to drive to all of the attractions but most are within 5 miles. The breakfast was good. Parking is $10/night which isn't bad but I think a lot of the adjacent hotels are free. I probably wouldn't stay here again but its not the worst place in the world. Value for what we paid was reasonable, but there are better choices.

“Wow- Great hotel, awesome value, very good service"” Don't believe all the negative reviews. I am always careful about staying at boutique hotel. This hotel had a great front desk staff, courteous restaurant staff, and overall great experience. My room was very clean and view of the Space Needle was a bonus. Great rate compared to other downtown hotels

“10 Nights Here...Nothing Special...OK” The hotel is in a GREAT location! You are blocks away from Time Square and 5th ave and Broadway shopping as well as Chelsea. Loved being "home based" here. The hotel itself is clean, decor is OK, breakfast is OK, customer service is OK. Nothing incredibly great or horrible about this hotel. My 2 complaints are a flashing light in my room made it a little hard to sleep sometimes. Second, some water pressure deal made my toilet make a weird noise every 10 minutes...which also made it hard to sleep. I turned off the water and faced away from the flashing lights at night which made it bareable.
“Too pricey” This hotel could use some freshening up. My husband felt it certainly needs new sheets. Work out equipment just adequate. Felt it was very pricey for what you get.

“Very Central Indeed” Booked this hotel as part of a package deal flying out of Madrid. Booked 3 rooms for 5 people (parents, 2 brothers and myself). We got given 3 rooms together which was a start. The hotel is right by Times Square which is brilliantly central for Manhattan. It is wedged between a bunch of Irish bars. My only issue with the location - and this is completely down to personal preference - is that it is way too touristy and if you come back in the evening from a long day walking, shopping and sight-seeing, you dont really want to go too far for a beer and some food but here you are limited to the option of an $8 beer and a $15 burger which isn't so great when there are 5 hungry people staying there for a week. Looking at the hotel website this is a spanish hotel chain - all the staff are spanish speaking (apart from the cleaning staff who are all Thai I think). Rooms are nice and all different. They're not as small as people mentioned though I was told we had been upgraded (aren't we always). TVs were quite small. Shower water pressure not great. The pool is in the lobby and is tiny -never used it or the sauna as didn't have time. There would occasionally be people in there posing. Downside to pool is that the lobby and the breakfast room stink of chlorine. Despite there being no hot options available, the choice of breakfast was extensive and delicious (bagels, donuts, fruit, jam, boiled eggs, ham). Would stay again but there are nicer hotels out there and I would stay in a funkier part of town.
“Beautiful hotel” Even though under renovation, I had a lovely room which had a comfortable bed, delightfully quiet environment and exceptionally helpful staff. Town is adorable. loved it.

“Good but isolated if you do not have a car” An attractive hotel. Nice rooms. Marina views were enjoyable. All staff - top notch. However, if you are in for a cruise and without a car it is difficult to enjoy the restaurants, museums and shopping of the San Pedro waterfront. There are hotels close to these features. The Doubletree offers complementary van transport to close-by attractions but during my stay there was only one driver and the van was often busy. Buffet breakfast was very good but a little high in price. A light breakfast eater would not be pleased. Again, I would like to complement the management for putting together a great staff.

“A stylish boutique hotel” I agree with other reviewers that travelers should consider what they want out of their trip to NYC before booking at the Rivington. If you want to spend most of your time seeing Broadway shows and visiting museums, you might be better off in midtown or uptown. But if you would like to be near the Village and Soho, the Rivington is a stylish choice. My husband and I stayed here three nights over a long weekend in July. We had room 113 on the 11th floor, which was a king room. It is a corner unit, with wall to ceiling glass windows on two sides. The bathroom has both a shower (with frosted glass windows, so you get the feeling of showering in front of an open window in the city), and a soaking tub. Toiletries are nice and replenished daily. The design of the hotel is funky and cool. The room is by no means large, but it is well-designed and perfectly fine (hotel rooms in NYC are definitely smaller than average). The continental breakfast is pretty good. There is coffee, whole pieces of fruit, cereal, pastries, and bagels. The bagels and pastries are from a bakery. The downsides – no juice, tea, or water. I suppose these could have been tracked down if we had gotten a waiter to help, which we didn’t do. I gave the hotel four rather than five stars because (1) there is no music in the hotel – you have to pay $10 to play a “jukebox” on the TV for 120 minutes – a total ripoff, I think. A CD player is standard in this kind of place; (2) the NY Times was not delivered to the door; (3) ice was quite difficult to track down (no ice bucket in room, I was put on hold when I called for it, and finally went to lobby restaurant and got some); (4) no tea/water at breakfast. I found service good. Upon check-in, there was no bellman to help with my bags (my husband was parking). The man behind the desk helped me instead. When I looked for ice, the hostess helped me track it down, even though the restaurant was quite busy. The club is hopping on Friday and Saturday nights. We did not hear a thing in our room, but I can imagine that rooms on the lower floors might be quite noisy. I would watch out for this if booking a less expensive room. We didn’t order from room service, but it looked to be quite inexpensive, which was a good thing. The minibar was also well stocked and quite inexpensive (in other NYC hotels, I have seen water being sold for $10!) I did not feel a bit unsafe in this neighborhood at any point. There were plenty of normal looking people out on the street barhopping and clubbing, and I never felt that weird “we’re the only ones on an empty street with only a strange-looking man across from us” feeling. The LES is one of the more interesting sections of NYC these days, and if you are looking for a stylish place to stay, the Rivington is a solid choice.

“A Scene” The hotel is newly built and is clean, but the rooms are cool to the point of being cold, they are taking a certain aesthetic too far. The staff is very kind and helpful. The pool is lovely. FYI , this place is a total scene and that is not always a good thing. if you're going for a bachelor / bachelorette party weekend, this is a great choice. For any other reason, skip it. It is a total mob scene down in the lobby every night with totally gross people who are obsessed with trying to be cool. They are often really drunk and rowdy. I love going out and used to live in NYC and this is the type of scene that a lot of Manhattan and Brooklyn folks avoid.

“Great location!” I gave the hotel an above average rating mainly because of the location and the price. It truly can not be beat. The rooms were spacious, two queen beds and a separated living room area. The beds were comfy and the room had a fridge in it so you can stock it with water etc for your stay. The downfall would be the service, ie. valet parking, check in, check out etc. You are instructed to call 20min in advance for your car because they have to retrieve your car from another lot, which is fine and maybe they were having an off day, but we waited almost an hour. And there was never any one around for us to even complain to. Also, check in is at three, and we were not given a room until almost 4:45PM! The lobby is nice, but small, so sitting there with all the luggage and kids for almost two hours did not start the weekend off with a bang. But all in all, I would still stay there again.

“quiet, old-world Upper East Side hotel” We enjoyed a very quick 2-day, 1-night stay here over the July 4 weekend. Since we would be spending most of our time at the Met Museum (Alexander McQueen exhibit) on the Upper East Side, I first booked at the Surrey, where we stayed last year, which is a short walk from the Met. When the Plaza Athenee (PA) came up on a private sale website, I reserved here, even though it's 12 blocks further from the Met. Much to my chagrin, the Surrey came up on the same website a short while afterward, but the website has a no refund policy. Although we were "stuck" staying at the PA, we were by no means disappointed. The stay was quite pleasurable, and although the hotel was slightly more inconveniently located for the purpose of our trip, it is very well located for visits to Midtown shopping and to Central Park. The New York PA is a more intimate hotel than the Paris PA, tucked away on residential East 64th St. (as opposed to busy Ave. Montaigne) in the chichi Upper East Side. The elegant lobby walls are painted with trompe l'oeil murals, you are seated at a desk for check-in. Much to our surprise and delight, we were upgraded from a Classic room (lower floor, interior view) to a Deluxe room with a terrace to boot! This is the first time this has happened using this particular website. The room, on the 15th floor out of 17, was large, especially by New York standards, and recently renovated but classically appointed. I would not say the room was technologically advanced. There is a charge for Wifi in the room, but not in the lobby or bar. There was a wet bar with a sink, mini-fridge and cook-top, but no utensils or dishes. The minibar was in another fridge. The bathroom was quite small, with a combo shower-tub and limited counter space by the sink. The terrace was lovely, south-facing, spanning the length of the room, with potted plants and a wooden table and 2 cushioned chairs. A small glimpse of Central Park could be seen to the west. The hotel's public spaces include a bar, restaurant and business center (complimentary) on the first floor, and a spa, fitness center and meeting rooms on the second floor. We had breakfast at the restaurant after plans to dine on our terrace were foiled by rain and thunderstorms; the American breakfast is pricey ($38) but of good quality and convenient. As a fan of the series "Sex and the City", I was aware that a 2 scenes from the series finale that were supposed to take place at the Paris PA were actually filmed here, in the bar and restaurant. Front desk service was excellent on check-in and check-out. The doorman was a tad surly, the bellmen friendly but not always at the ready (but we didn't require their services). The hotel seems to have a large international clientele. I would say this hotel is for the upscale traveler looking for a quiet, intimate, old-world, service-oriented hotel. While my first choices along these lines would be the nearby St. Regis or Peninsula, I would certainly visit the PA again.

“I agree, just OK” I agree with the recent reviews that 70 Park Avenue is OK, but not great. I arrived Friday afternoon and was assigned room 1709. I liked the idea of being on the top floor. One elevator was out of order leaving 1 passenger elevator and the freight elevator. However I did not experience any especially long waits. My room was at the back of the hotel. The view was nothing special, but I suppose it was relatively quiet with regard to outside noise. Upon entering my room I was immediately hit with the smell of mold and Lysol. Not very pleasant. The a/c unit was very dirty and there was a black substnace on the louvers that I assumed was the mold. I wiped as much of it off as I could, but I could see inside the unit that it was filthy. I opened the window to let a little fresh air in which helped a little bit. When I went out for the evening I brought the mold smell to the attention of the front desk. On my return it just smelled like more Lysol, not very pleasant. The room was OK sized for NYC, but nothing to write home about. The plasma TV is a nice touch since it takes up less space, but the incoming signals were nothing special. I tried to use the DVD player to play an audio CD, but couldn't get any sound out of it even after following the directions. Wireless internet is an extra $10.95 a day, which I think is ridiculous. But they do have two computers publicly available downstairs for free. There was a lot of hall noise at night and if you want to sleep in late in the morning forget about it because housekeeping is up early making noise in the hallway. They happened to set up their trash collection point right outside my room so it was quite noisy. The bathroom is a decent size. My bathtub drain wasn't working properly as there seemed to be a partial clog. I also told the front desk about that and they did have some one fix that issue. Overall for what I paid with a special rate I thought it was an OK value for NYC, but I am sure there are other, nicer properties in the same price range.

“Awful hotel” Stayed as part of a 2010 roadtrip, booked online. The front office didn't have our booking and didn't do much to help us out. Room was disgusting and unkempt, and the TV didn't work. The parking lot outside was home a hangout for a number of beer-drinking young men and women throwing beer cans about. Overall, the hotel is so bad that it somehow manages to bring the down-at-the-heels strip club across the street into disrepute.

“Affordable, comfortable mid-town hotel” Just returned from an overnight girls' overnight to NYC. We stayed one night (Saturday) at the Courtyard New York Manhattan/Times Square South. The good: * Location is fantastic - 39th near Broadway -- and is just one block south of all of the Times Square action. * Very quick, no-hassle check in and out. * The beds are out of this world comfortable. I didn't want to leave. * Rainshower and new/clean bathroom fixtures. * Over look and comfort -- new, bright, clean and fresh were adjectives we used to describe the room. The okay (nothing was bad): * The price wasn't bad, especially because we needed to sleep 3 adults (I found cheaper deals on higher level area hotels, but only offering 1 bed). * The view -- really, there isn't one at all, but I wasn't expecting much. * Room size isn't very big, but again, we didn't expect very specious accommodations for NYC. I recommend this hotel for anyone wanting to do tourist activities in the Times Square/Theatre District.

“Fantastic Service and Wonderful Rooms” This is a beautiful hotel very close to the Convention Center. The rates in December were fantastic- under 100 dollars per night. The service and the hotel were fantastic. The only complaint I had was the cost of parking per night - we had two vehicles and it cost 42 dollars per night to park them ---- ouch!

“Disappointed in the hotel, what a let down.” So disappointed, and I'm a huge Marriott fan. Tiny rooms that really are the same as Fairfield Inn Marriott, towels feel like sandpaper, food trey left in hall from 5 pm until next morning around 8 am with half eaten food on it. There is nothing special about this JW, the standard Marriott in Louisville KY is far better than this JW. The staff could have cared less that my smoke alarm started beeping at 2 am, not even I'm sorry that happened, over all just a big let down,Next time in DC I will stay at a Marriott Courtyard and save my money.

“Excellent Service. Great location.” This past weekend we stayed at the Hilton because we were talking my daughter to see Wicked for her birthday and I had enough points to get one of our rooms free. From the moment we arrive to the moment we left the staff was excellent. As we were checking in, the staff found out that we were celebrating my daughter's birthday so they gave her a free movie. Our free room was a corner room that was very large and has an excellent view. The bed was very comfortable. The location was great; we walked to Quincy Market and the North End. Our waiter for breakfast was excellent; he ensured we all had fresh, hot food from the buffet. My only complaint is paying $38 for valet parking and $12 for Internet access but I would definitely stay here again.

“A bit dated, but the view makes up for it.” Stayed in the Seattle Westin for a business meeting, and especially given the convention rate, I was not disappointed. A large cylindrical structure, all the rooms have a slightly skewed shape with one wall completely of glass that created the illusion that Seattle in November is actually a bit brighter than it actually is. I was particularly fond of working at the desk facing the window, gazing upon the streets below. Lovely king size bed with lots of pillows and crisp linens, and robes for him and her in case you needed to make the trek to the spa – though apparently you could have a massage delivered right to your room if you so fancied. I also enjoyed the Italian restaurant right across the street - good food, nice ambiance! The location was excellent, essentially at the base of the southern monorail terminus and located next to a couple of excellent shopping malls that heralded a wide array of restaurants, food courts, and even a multiplex movie theater (which came in surprisingly handy!) I retraced my childhood steps (or should I say tracks) to the base of the Space Needle, only to find that a round trip to the top of the tower would set me back about sixteen bucks. Seemed like too much even for a view of the autumn cityscape at twilight, so I took a pass on that one. The Westin is also one of the stops on the Grayline airport shuttle, which I would have to say constitutes about the ONLY airport shuttle experience I have had that didn’t turn out to be a total disaster. (I shudder with memories of nearly missing a flight at New York’s JFK as we spent hours winding around mid-town Manhattan.) All in all, it was an excellent hotel, and I would stay there again on a subsequent visit to Seattle. Not the best ever, but a very comfortable place to sleep.

“Great Nights Stay at Hollywood & Vine” We ended up in California a head of schedule for our nephews graduation from the Marines in San Diego so since we had an extra day, we decided to spend the night in LA - I had seen the hotel on line and read the reviews and plugged the address into our GPS and we ended up staying there. The staff was extremely friendly, Jeff who checked us in helped us to see the Hollywood sign and gave us directions to Rodeo Drive. The room was very nice and a step back in time - they had a record player in the room with albums to play. The sleeper sofa was comfortable for our teen and the master bed was very comfy to sleep in. The room also had a washer/dryer combo unit - it is all in one you wash and then dry without having to switch loads so we got caught up on our laundry. I will certainly come back again. We did dine at Cleo their restaurant downstairs - some of it was excellent some missed but I know they are improving and I will give them a try again. We also could walk and see the hollywood stars of fame which were around the hotel and hollywood blvd. It is a small hotel, but we will definitely return.

“Great attention to detail” After experiencing travel delays gettign to Houston it was a very nice surprise to get into the Hotel. It felt like going back into time where Hotels were about personalized service. Even though this hotel is part of the Marriott brand, you are in something completely different. The lobby and restaurant have truly unique look and feel to them. I will always remember the great antique safe behind the reception area. The room was super quiet and the bed was very comfortable..I will definitely stay at Hotel Icon again when visiting downtown Houston.

“A respectable choice for long term stays” My husband and I are in our mid-40's and were visiting professors in San Francisco for two weeks in Jan, 06. We were looking for a place with a kitchen which was not in Union Square, had wireless internet access and allowed bookings for <1month but >1week. This severely limited our choices; however, the Steinhart was ultimately a rather good one. It is on the edge of Nob Hill and the Panhandle neighborhoods. It is quite safe and allowed us ready access to Union Square and Nob Hill for multiple dining options. While the decor is akin to a college apartment, the apartments are surprisingly large and very reasonably priced. The building itself is architecturally quite interesting and if a bit more money was invested in furnishings etc., it really could be spectactular. Carlos, the manager, was professional and helpful. The Steinhart was not noisy at all while we were there. It is not the Four Seasons; however, it does not pretend to be and really is a great alternative to the myriad boutique hotels where one is forced to eat outself the hotel every meal. Great for a stay longer than one week and would likely work well for a family.

“Mediocre Hotel in Great Location” The hotel is in need of renovation. The fitness center is far too small for the size of the property but you can get a $10 pass for the excellent independent fitness center nearby. May very good restaurants within walking distance - all better choices than the hotel's outlets.

“Correct” Les prestations de cet hôtel sont tout à fait convenables. Les chambres sont spacieuses et bien équipées. Il dispose d'un parking payant... et le petit déjeuner continental est inclu. Il vaut mieux insister pour ne pas avoir une chambre sur la rue car c'est assez bruyant. Le seul bémol reste le quartier qui semble assez mal fréquenté le soir et il est difficile de trouver de quoi se restaurer correctement à proximité. Il faut reprendre la voiture et se rendre quelques "blocks" plus loin. Universal Studios n'est pas non plus à la porte de l'hôtel contrairement à ce qui est dit dans l'adresse !

“Stay somewhere else” We almost always stay at a Hampton Inn or Embassy Suites and are use to receiving a clean room. However this hotel is dirty. Stained carpet, hair on bathroom floor, weevil in cereal, smelly towels, old mushy beds. Staff was good. Will never stay here again.

“Quirky,Clean,Friendly and Location!!” We stayed at the Curtis for a long weekend for the Bengals/Broncos game. Had a room on the 13th floor (Dun,dun Dunnnn!). This was the scary themed floor. Cool quirky concept and it works. The room cards say open sesame! Sunday brunch is a disco theme. The hotel is four blocks from Larimer square and two blocks from the 16th street open air mall. Our room was a corner king. Clean. Fridge is hidden drawers. Ipod docking station. Free WiFI. Also good business center on 2nd floor. Nice 42inch flat screens. The only complaint was the Sunday brunch. Overpriced and very limited. We opted for Sams NO. #3 on the block up. It was Featured on Dives,Diners and Drive-ins. Good eats, Friendly service and great prices.

“Who's been staying in my hotel room? Room cleaning breakdown” This doesn't happen often: you unpack, get settled in and then notice in the bathroom that there is debris in the trash can. And then, as you study the situation, you see debris from a shower -- the hotel shampoo bottle, the wrapper from the soap bar, etc. And then, still taking the bathroom in like a first time trip to a crime scene, you notice a used bar of soap in the bathtub. YUCKK. If it hadn't been the middle of the night, I would have rejected the room, but I was too exhausted to think and simply went to bed. I had a second breakdown in the one meal I sought: dessert. I ordered two items. Only one came, and after a wait, I prodded the staff into action. The workout room was a B- at best: About 12 pieces of equipment. I was able to get a treadmill. But the ICH charges $12 for the privilege of a workout. Memo to ICH: this is a problem at 530am when I don't have cash -- now I have to choose between exercise and the additional charge on my bill which I will have to break down when I get home as a personal charge. Thanks a lot -- I don't generally take cash to a nice hotel workout joint. The hotel room I was given was not for a second honeymoon. I opened the prison-like window drapes only to find a sticker that read something like: "Do not open window swarms of bugs outside" Nice. I do not believe, based on my stay that this is a five star hotel. I am at 3.5 stars at best. This great chain is really coasting on it in Chicago. Michigan Ave address isn't worth this. I will keep looking in Chicago.

“Great location. Nice hotel.” Not having stayed here for a few years, I was worried about some of the recent reviews on this hotel and talk of upcoming renovations. I can report I had a great stay. Large room, very clean, pleasant housekeeping staff/ doormen. Can't beat the location for the room rate. Select Guest members get 2 free drinks in the morning. Great deal. Two downsides: The room thermostat didn't seem to work and the temperature was whatever it was elsewhere in the hotel. And I wish the room had a tea pot. Coffee/tea was $7 from room service.

“Great choice if you have kids.” Stayed here for two nights with my kids. The two-room layout with the sofabed makes that effort a bit less of a challenge. The staff was outstanding, from the desk clerks to the breakfast attendants to the shuttle drivers. However, the hotel considers itself to be an airport property, and since they offer a shuttle then that's an acceptable idea. However, if you are driving, know that the hotel is quite a bit off the beaten path to/from SeaTac, and that there is substantial road construction in the area of Southcenter Mall. We did ultimately find it - and liked the property. A couple of things bothered me; ostensibly we were in a nonsmoking room, but it REEKED of smoke. Housekeeping should have notified management, the TV in the bedroom had horrible reception - that should have been taken care of by someone prior to check-in (although we did figure out that it was just a loose cable in the back of the set). Parking seems limited and quite a way from the front door. These issues were minor and I would quite readily return. While there is nothing outstanding about the hotel, it offers a pleasant atmosphere, and great staff.

“Great combination of location and price” My husband and I stayed at the Hotel George for a four-day weekend in mid-April and happened to hit spectacular weather and flowers. I chose the Hotel George for its combination of location (just a couple blocks from Union Station, which means you don't need a car if you fly into National), reasonable (for DC) price (booked on the web from the hotel's site), and because we have stayed at a couple of other Kimpton hotels and liked them. I asked for a quiet room, and we got one on the interior, which meant no view, but who cares when you've been out seeing the sights all day? The room was indeed quiet (I'm a light sleeper), comfortable, and clean. We didn't use any of the hotel services other than having one dinner at the hotel restaurant (Bistro Bis) because it was convenient for a preconcert dinner. The meal was lovely--excellent service, good wine recommendation, and very flavorful preparations (fish and lamb).

“Looks good, lacks finer points.” Hotel Valencia is a nice hotel in a great location, but in the end I would probably choose a different hotel the next time I'm in San Antonio. The good: -The rooms and common areas are decorated very nicely and exude cool sophistication. -Service from room service was very quick and very friendly when was called to ask for a cork screw and some wine glasses. The bad: -The valet parking situation is really bad. I would go so far as to call it incompetent. When we first arrived, the drive was full of cars so we could not pull in. We had to sit on the street blocking traffic while we watched two valets standing around sipping Red Bulls. There is absolutely no hussle from the valet staff to get cars moved . There appeared to be plenty of staff, but there was always a lot of standing around without much sense of urgency. For $29/night, the valet staff really needs to be better. -Bathrooms are small and the shower in our room drained very slowly leading you to stand in several inches of water while showering. -While I understand the dark corridors and lighting are part of the atmosphere of the hotel, it would be nice to be able to get more light in your room if you so desire. The rooms are pretty dark, even with the window shades fully open. -The service in the lounge was pretty poor. We went in and sat for over 20 minutes without a cocktail server coming by to take our order. I finally went to the bar and asked one of the bartenders if there was a server for our area and she said there was, but that she was in over her head (she actually used a different word to describe her, but I'll leave that out). To the credit of the bartender, she took our order and brought drinks out to us. Like I said in the beginning, I don't think I would stay here again on a return trip to San Antonio. On the surface, Hotel Valencia looks like a really nice hotel, but there are enough flaws that knock it down a few notches.

“Hilton Times Square” great location, you're already in the middle of everything. cool hotel with the lobby on the 21th floor. amazing view and great great staff! the italian guy in the little "info desk" was funny and very helpful. The room was big and clean. big bathrooom with fresh shower. beds were very comfortable and the view was great! we only slept one night and were really happy with everything! I can really recommend this.

“Awesome Stay at the Conrad” We recently stayed at the Conrad to celebrate our one year engagement anniversary and a birthday, the Conrad made this one of the best celebrations ever! We had an executive suite facing Michigan Ave that was spectacular-the room was just perfect! I had called in the day before and ordered some champagne and chocolate strawberries as a surprise to my fiance to be delivered right at 4:30 and they were right on time, it made the surprise perfect! Overall, the hotel is very nice and is a perfect location for just about anything you want to do in the city. You walk out the front door and you can shop, eat or go see just about any attraction you want to see in Chicago. In addition to that, the staff is top notch and they really go out of their way to make your stay perfect! We will definitally return to the Conrad and if you are looking for a great hotel-this is it!

“Nice Hotel, Great Location” We had such a nice stay at the Fairfield Inn... We will be sure to visit again! My husband and I traveled to Chicago for an exhibit at the Field museum and a Cubbies game, and decided to stay at the Fairfield Inn, as we could not get a room at a Westin, W, or Marriott property. We typically like to stay a full-service hotels, so we were not expecting too much, but the Fairfield was really nice! What makes it so nice? Staff - This hotel has about the FRIENDLIEST staff in Chicago. Everyone, from the front desk agents to the maid to the people working in the breakfast room were warm and friendly. They all gave you the feeling that they were happy that you were there. The room - It was not elaborate, but very nice and SPOTLESS. The bed was comfortable, and there was plenty of room to move around. And quiet! I know we had neighbors, as we could hear them when we were in the hall, but once we were in our room, it was quiet! The breakfast - It was terrific! We had fresh waffles for breakfast - it was such a treat. They also had cereals, bacon, egg, and cheese sandwiches, donuts, bagels, and oatmeal. The only thing I would improve was the coffee (but there is a Starbuck's at the Courtyard diagonally across Ontario!) The location - Really great - about 2 blocks off of Michigan Ave., it is REALLY easy to walk to the best shopping areas, and to some great restaurants (Capital Grill is next door, and Cafe Coco Pazzo is just across the street). You are also not too far from Navy Pier and from the Museum of Contemporary Art, as well as the beack (Ohio Street beach). I would recommend the hotel to anyone, and we will likely stay again.

“Good Choice for an LAX lay over” It's hard to review an airport hotel. I don't expect much. I want a comfy bed, good transportation and a place to get a tasty bite. I am not looking for much more. The Hilton at LAX fits this bill. It's a few minutes away from the airport and runs quick and frequent transportation. The hotel is large. Check-in was fast and painless. The rooms are nice sized and clean. Some of fun views of the airport and runways. If you are a Hilton Honors member you can upgrade for a small upgrade fee on the day of arrival. We once upgraded to the Executive Floor which was nice. The offer a small cocktail hour in the evening and it was a nice relaxing touch. Another time we upgraded to the Presidental suite which was simply outrageous. Huge, spacious with a world class view. The suite was massive with a huge dining table and living area. It was fun to order room service and eat at the big table. If you are staying at LAX for an early morning flight or a stuck with a missed connection I would have no problem suggesting this hotel. It is just what a good airport hotel should be!

“Would expect more from a Four Seasons” When staying at a Four Seasons you expect to have, bar-none, the best service and accommodations. First off, the hotel is conveniently located. The lobby is very nice, but the rooms fall a little short. It almost feels like a Hyatt. We also had difficulty with the AC maintaining a cool temperature at night and it actually felt a bit warm. On to service.... they have a courtesy car which came in handy for rides in the downtown area. Very nice. Check - in was a breeze. I had to call down twice to get a full menu (offered) for the hotel restaurant because it wasn't delivered after 45 minutes. I had to call down twice to have our breakfast table removed because it wasn't pick up after an hour. Lastly, we needed a rental car and the concierge offered to call Hertz and get us a quote. I'm at home now and I'm still waiting for that phone call with the quote. These are just small nuances that you wouldn't expect from a Four Seasons. They do, however, offer a very nice package of "buy 2 nights get a 3rd" free which, after staying 6 nights there brings the nightly rate to $250 per night which is nice. Linens and beds are very comfortable. Drinks and food from bar/restaurant downstairs were exceptional and bartender was very nice.

“Incredible stay!” I've stayed at Kimpton hotel in the past but this experience was exceptional. From Lane at the front desk to Louis at the concierge desk the staff bent over backwards to help us. The rooms were clean and well appointed. The location is centrally located and the food and drinks were all top notch! I will stay here again without hesitation and recommend it to anyone traveling to Seattle.

“Do Not Stay On Freeway Side Else Noise Won't Let You Sleep” Typical Hyatt Place; good accomodations and amenities but beware; DO NOT STAY ON THE FREEWAY SIDE ELSE NOISE WILL NOT LET YOU SLEEP. Be sure to ask for a room on the side opposite the freeway. free breakfast not very good; choice limited to juice, bread, a few fruits, etc. very limited hot choices for extra charge. large HDTV in room

“Nice Stay Great Location” Okay, my bathroom was little tight #206. Got the bad news out of the way. If you are going to DC to hang out in a hotel bathroom this probably is not the place for you and you may have other issues to deal with. Bathroom was well appointed with granite, citron soaps, curved shower rod and great water pressure for the speakman showerhead. Room was very clean and in great shape. Large LCD Flat screen, nice desk area, in room coffee, room safe, large closet, extra lounge chair with ottoman. The stafff was very pleasant and knowledgeable. Just a few blocks from DuPont Circle where there are a variety of shops and restaurants. Very safe neighborhood. Nice walk to the Whitehouse and then on to the Mall area where many of the monuments and war memorials are located. I had one minor issue with my room and it was fixed in a flash (iron). I would not hesitate to stay here again. (nice warm cookie at check-in). Safe travels!

“I always try to book Kimpton Hotels” I've enjoyed staying at Kimpton hotels over the years because of their boutique feel and welcoming atmosphere. I also appreciate the wine hours and the coffee in the lobby in the morning. I often eat in the attached restaurants which the chain makes an effort to create a destination restaurant. The Hotel Vintage Park did not disappoint. The location is good and the front desk staff are very helpful. The room was comfortable and I appreciate the ability to get different pillows easily. Having a bathrobe in the room is wonderful, especially for women traveling for business and trying to keep baggage light. Housekeeping did a good job and the room was clean and fully stocked with amenities. The Il Tulio Restaurant was also good for dinner.

“Bring your swim suit.” I stayed 2 nights in this downtown hotel in mid-march and enjoyed every aspect of my stay: the price was super; the service and staff were helpful and pleasant; the room was large, clean and well decorated; the bed was big and very comfortable; and the location, though a couple of blocks off the beaten trail was fine. But the best suprise was the rooftop heated pool which even in late winter was heated to 80 degrees and which gave a brilliant view of the city at night. The excercise room also offers the same great views in a spotless facility so bring your sneakers. There is plenty of parking all around on the street so you need not pay extra at a lot.

“Convenience Central in Midtown Manhattan” Conveniently located across from Madison Square Garden, a welcome and conveniently located refuge across from the train station, near everything. Recently desinger-renovated spacious rooms, nice views of the city on the upper levels, and very friendly and accomodating staff who take seriously the idea of making your stay as pleasant as possible. For the kids, King Kong stuffed animals greet them in every room.

“Old hotels have theircharm” Staying at the Waldorf Astoria for a conference was not the best way to enjoy this old hotel, but it made the conference elegant and fun. The hotel retains much of its character and does go the extra mile to give guests a great experience. The building's age does show through with inconveniences like no water for a morning due to a plumbing mishap, uneven heat and cooling, or difficulty with wireless internet. The situations were resolved fairly quickly and to my satisfaction. The meeting rooms were elegant and the conference food was very good. I do suggest the hotel work with both the coffee shop and Oscars to expand capacity in the coffee shop and hours at Oscars.

“Great Friendly Helpful Staff” The lobby areas were lovely and and enormous. Rooms were large and nice too. The best about this hotel is the great staff, so friendly and helpful and pleasant! Large pool w. Palms. Loved the folks who worked here!

“Concerts attract noisy and thoughtless guests” We stayed here for 4 nights. What would have been a fantastic hotel was spoilt by the noisy concert-goers who shouted and laughed at the top of their voices till about 1 or 2 a.m. without a thought for anyone who might just be trying to sleep! As another reviewer remarked, the door left a gap between it and the frame and you never felt particularly safe in the downstairs rooms facing the car park. (Ask for a room at the back if you can get one.) The rooms themselves are spacious and the cabins make a change from an ordinary hotel room. The gardens, pool area and lobby are all very pleasant and the hotel has its own laundry, though it closes at 4..pm. on concert days!(Not much use to us!). Would probably not stay here again unless we can be assured of a quieter room facing the pool or harbour .

“Great Value / Tiny Rooms” There is no other way to put it but the rooms are tiny. The running joke between myself and my group was "I have to go outside to change my mind". I stayed in a room with two double beds, which had no closet and a very small dresser, but it was very clean and had a quite comfortable bed. Staff was friendly and helpful in giving directions to local places. Continental Breakfast of coffee, assorted teas, waffles, bagels, fruit & cereals was good as well. The location is great, two blocks from orange line subway & a block and a half from the Rock Bottom Brewery (highly recommend “Good Beer & Food”). Overall, I have stayed in much nicer and much worse; I would defiantly stay here again.

“You get what you pay for” I was in town for only one night to watch Atlanta destroy the Phillies and booked last minute. I wanted a hotel with an outdoor pool. On SPG's website, Sheraton Suites is listed as having an outdoor pool when in reality the outdoor pool is across the parking lot at the Four Points. Sheraton Suites, Four Points and Aloft are all in the same parking lot and seem to have reciprocity between them. If I had known this, I would've booked the Aloft because it's newer and maybe a touch a nicer. The printer at the Sheraton Suites was down and so the front desk advised me to print my tickets for the game at the Aloft. The Aloft attendant was very polite and accomodating...as if they're used to guests going between all three properties. I think the only upgraded option for this hotel is one presidential suite. It was occupied during my stay. All of the rooms are suites. My room had a couch and tv in the living room, bathroom in the middle and a king sized bed and tv beyond that. Nothing super special. The room was very clean. I didn't pay a lot for the room...$80 or $90. It was only a 10 minute drive to the sports stadiums/arena area. Definitely an option for airport customers or people on a budget.

“Beautiful View, Good Stay” I booked this reservation directly with the hotel website. It was a mixed reward rate - 4,000 spg points and $60 a night. It turned out to be a great deal for us. I contacted the hotel prior to our arrival after reading some mixed reviews. They advised me all of the rooms had been rennovated about 3 years ago, and this Westin was actually the very first Westin in the chain. We decided to go ahead with the reservation, and I was glad we did. Our room was on the 34th floor and the view was spectacular during the day but even more beautiful at night. Our room was clean and comfy and fit our family of four with no problems. The Concierges were very helpful and assisted us with making our plans. Since we wanted to go to the Space Needle, they recommended we eat lunch there and then we would not have to pay the entrance fee to go to the top. We agreed this would be a good option, and they made the lunch reservation for us. I'm glad they did because when we arrived, I overheard the hostess at the Space Needle advise someone they were full and could only accomodate those with lunch reservations. I was about to order Crab Cakes for lunch, when our waiter informed us that the Concierge from our hotel was treating us to Crab Cakes as an appetizer. What a nice surprise! The onsite parking was very expensive ($35 a day), but on check in I asked if there were alternative parking options. The front desk rep told me we could use the parking garage right next door even though they had no affiliation with the hotel for $18 per day. This parking garage was even connected to the Westin with a sky walkway. The location couldn't have been better. Within walking distance to just about everything. The Monorail picks up right near the hotel also.

“Location, Location, Location” If you need a hotel in the Hillcrest area, this is pretty much the ONLY hotel there is! Here's the good reasons to stay here: 1. GREAT location. There is soooooooo much to can walk to - restaurants, bars, clubs, grocery stores, stores. It's in a great spot! Although downtown is about 3 miles, on a nice day (which most are in San Diego) it would be a really easy walk! There is plenty of public transportation (bus) as well. 2. Physical property. It's a cool set up - in a U shape with a nice pool/spa/patio area in the middle. It makes it easy to enjoy the great SD weather. 3. Room size. The rooms are all suites with a full kitchen and a sep. bedrroom. Very spacious! It appears all rooms have a patio with furniture - which is awesome! 4. Very clean! 5. Free Wifi that worked very well! The negatives: 1. Although I loved the location and physical layout, the hotel is a bit outdated. Certain things are fairly up-to-date (like the bedding) but other things (like the kitchen) could use a little modernism. In any case, it's all comfortable and worked for us.. 2. The bathroom shower was probably the worst hotel shower head I've had in a while. Maybe it was just bad luck in this room?! It was a cheap fiberglass tub and a THIN shower curtain and didn't hold the water back. 3. At check-in, the clerk was a little surly. However, the other staff I ineracted with seemed a bit friendlier. 4. They charge $6/day for parking, which I thought was a bit ridiculous. 5 There is no workout room! I would stay here again in a heartbeat. I would be great if they updated the furnishings...but then again the rates would probably go up?!

“It's the View” Stayed here with my daughter for a combined business/personal getaway. Rates were hight due to Chicago airshow but we selected hotel for its view rooms. This hotel has a very convenient location to just about everything... it's not only connected to the Merchandise Mart and the Brown line train station, it's an easy walk across the river to the Clark/Lake transit point and there is always a taxi stand in front of the hotel... or you can walk which my family always enjoys in Chicago. Arrving in Chicago you can walk from the Amtrak station, take a taxi or from the airports take the L train to Clark/Lake and walk over from there, or transfer to the Brown line and do hardly any walking at all. In inclement weather this is a nice option. Now on to the hotel itself. The hotel occupies the higher floors of the MM so once there, take the lobby elevators to the 15th floor for checkin. Employees at front desk have always seemed friendly and professional to me. The view: I do have an issue with the random treatment when it comes to booking a "room with a view." I have received nicer views when booking through an opaque site than when booking the hotel direct; I guess it all depends on availability. But it can be frustrating if you select this hotel for the view. The rooms are clean and comfortable, with the upgraded HI bedding you will get a very restful night's sleep before your big day, whatever that might involve. Internet at the business center starts at 5$ for 15 minutes; did not try the wireless. Pool and gym area are nicely maintained and the pool was especially refreshing on a hot summer day. The onsite restaruant has excellent food, ambience and service, with a "kids eat free" bonus but you have to remember to stop at the checkin desk before (or after) the meal to get the coupon. Not sure why they don't just offer this at checkin. The hotel is connected via walkway to the Merchandise Mart which has a food court including Dunkin Donuts, McD's, Arbys, and other chains that can be helpful for getting a quick and inexpensive meal so you can splurge on another meal at the hotel or elsewhere in the Windy City. also a Starbucks. But there are so many dining and shopping options within walking distance it will be your typical Chicago getaway, just trying to decide where to go. All in all this was a nice hotel to come back to in the evening, especially when my daughter saw lighting strikes over the Chicago river. We ducked inside the entrance of the MM and walked all the way inside to get back to the hotel, then watched the storm and heavy rains all evening from the comfort of our room. I am sure we will be back.

“AVOID - subpar hotel” This looks like a 1950's construction that used to be some other brand of hotel before it converted to a Raddisson. Here were the problems - The deadlock on the door did not work. It just swung back and forth. Smallest bathroom I have ever seen. Forget about shutting the door. SLICK bathtub. Like it had a layer of slime on it. Carpet is worn out. Short list of TV channels No plug in for your computer Room did not look clean Pillow cases ten inches too short for the pillows The sheets on the beds do not fit. They pop right off. The sheets were stained and worn. Very small bath towels. My recommendation is to avoid this hotel.

“Dated, spacious, crowded but convenient” First of all Broadway on 47th is closed so if you have new taxi driver as I did you end up going around in circles to go to 7th Av. The exterior is congested with scaffolding at present and the door staff were too busy doing deals with taxi drivers to help me with my luggage. The entrance is poor.. the reception is on the 3rd floor but has no signage.. you have to walk in and get a lift to the lobby.. then a different lift to the rooms. They need more front of house presence and to assist and meet and greet guests.. I had to ask a member of staff of hold the door for me as I struggled to get my case in.. Staff services are basic..I felt as if I was more in a Travelodge. The left luggage is poor.. there is not enough room and luggage is sometimes left out on the lobby at times unattended piled up. Not a good impression as soon as you get out of the lift. Atmosphere is more cattle like. It can be noisy with large families and groups of friends. I did have to complain and it was dealt with, lack of enthusiasm from the staff and unhelpfulness was consistent when I arrived. I had breakfast included which was OK.. nothing special but an omlette/waffle station was good. The rooms are dated.. locks don't work.. sofas sink.. bathrooms fairly plastic.. my work chair was not steady.. Plus side.. lots of lifts so I never had to wait too long. A very impersonal hotel and the chocolate chip cookie is on arrival is a bit of a waste of time as I would rather just have a bottle of water..

“Consistently Excellent Quality” Have come to place a higher value on quality and consistency, given the travel that I've done over the years. Cannot beat the value of the Embassy Suites brand. - Ease of check in - Layout makes sense - Suite-type setup with a separate bedroom is more comfy than a standard one-room hotel - Amenities are always top notch - Curved shower feels like it's bigger than it really is - Separate sinks allow for sharing - Bar-type sink is useful for coffee/beverage prep - in-room microwave/fridge is SO handy - two TVs work well for those with families or with different TV tastes (though it's beyond me why anyone would go to a hotel to visit an area and then spend the night in front of the tube) - Nice indoor pool - small but functional business area - Go early for breakfast! - Enjoy the manager's reception - standard - each night Do NOT - NOT - go eat at Kansas City BBQ! Yes, they filmed Top Gun. It's a cute photo spot. But ... be warned ... not only is the food inconsistent, it's also sometimes painful to your intestinal tract (having experienced this first-hand!)

“get a corner room” The hotel is right on the river and because of the triangular shape of the building corner rooms have a great panoramic view from the Wrigley building to Navy pier. I didn't experience the slow elevators or the bad TV reception noted in other reviews. Thanks to some of those same reviews I didn't touch the minibar so no undue charges appeared on my bill. I do share the complaint of others that charging for an internet connection in this day and age is enough to make me seek alternative lodging options the next time I'm in Chicago.

“Would never stay here again” As an elite Marriott rewards member, I expect a certain quality when I check in. This hotel, at $300 a night, failed to meet any of my expectations: air conditioning didn't work when I checked in and double glass doors that open to the street were stuck in the open position. The humidity was so high my glasses steamed up upon entering. Sheets looked old, were not smooth, nor very white. Pillows flat and looked used. Toilet flusher was so loud I felt like I was shot in the rear every time I used it. Really ridiculous when you are sharing a room so you inevitably wake up your roommate if you use the bowl. Fire alarm went off and was inaudible in our room as was the announcement. Towels reek of chlorine. Just not up to any Marriott standard. Wireless didn't work, either. TV had limited channels, no PBS!

“Great Old Classic!” The Oxford Hotel is an old school gem located right in the heart of LoDo in downtown Denver. The staff are truly fantastic. The building is a treasure. The location is perfect. You are 3 blocks from Coors field. A block or two in any direction from numerous bars and restaurants. One block from Union Station. Mere blocks from the Pepsi Center and Mile High. Great place for a Denver getaway. Don't miss the classic Cruise Room off the lobby for a martini. A must. Repeat visitor. Would not stay anywhere else in Denver.

“It's as good as the best reviews” I must have read all the reviews placed here for the last 6 months, and I can say that The Michelangelo Hotel in Midtown Manhattan is as good as the best reviews. Our room had a marble foyer, and an all-marble deepbathroom and dressing room. The shower/bathtub was deep...up to my knees, and I'm 5'9". Every night, they came in for turn-down service, and pulled-down BOTH sets of window shades, and emptied the trash. This felt like a 4 star hotel, but we paid like a 2 star hotel, considering that it was summer vacation in New York City. I would stay there again.

“Oprah's Guests SHOULD Stay Here!” Three friends and I stayed at the Omni on August 31, 2004 when we flew to Chicago to go the Oprah Winfrey Show. Everyone wanted to stay in this hotel because Oprah's guests stay there. I was a little concerned about some of the negative reviews, but this is actually a WONDERFUL place to stay...especially for shopping on North Michigan Avenue!! Great views of Chicago and a perfect location! The suite is very nice. The decor is much better than at many hotels...wingback chairs, bookcases with real books. The bathroom is larger than average with a hair dryer and plenty of shampoos, soap, lotions etc. There is an expensive but well-stocked basket of goodies (we didn't eat any!). We realized in the morning that we didn't have a coffee maker, and one was brought up as soon as we requested it. The people at the front desk were pleasant. The beds are comfortable, and there is an iron and ironing board in the closet. You DO have to take two elevators, but that really isn't such a big deal. You have to enter the suite through a short hallway that seems to be wasted space, but there was virtually no noise ever in our suite. We did not try the restaurant or room service so can't vouch for the food. There are TONS of fabulous places to eat in Chicago (including a Starbucks right around the corner for breakfast), so I wouldn't have wanted to eat at the hotel anyway. We had a AAA rate of about $170 per night which I thought was a very good value for the large suite. I DEFINITELY would stay there again. We have been in Chicago many times before, and there just isn't a better location than the Omni!

“Great spot - skip the car and explore by foot” I stayed here for one night as part of a quick trip to the area. The immediate area is a little on the quiet side, but the Gaslamp District and Petco Park are a very easy walk of 10 to 15 minutes. If you are going to a Padres game and/or spending the day in the city, there is no need for a car - I picked up a car the next day, cutting a lot off of the cost of car rental and parking. Tons of spots for food and drink in the area - good happy hours, primarily 4 to 7 or so, but keep a lookout for earlier starts and some late-night specials. Hotel is clean, comfortable, and well-furnished. Wifi is an added cost ($11 or so). Restaurant/lounge in lobby has a Happy Hour - but it was only from 4 to 6, so I'd go elsewhere. The area seemed very safe, though as others have noted there were a few homeless folks around (they did not bother me). Trolley system is close by ($5 gets you unlimited rides for the day). Overall, a very good spot and a good value with terrific employees.

“Nice hotel, great architecture details...” Nice hotel with distinctive architecture you are not going encounter these days. The staff was great. Very welcoming. Rooms were large and comfortable with flat screen TV's. Would stay here again. A little noise creep but not bad.

“No Frills/Good Value” This is not the upscale, pretty part of Lincoln Park area (you need to be S. of Armitage for that) but it's not dangerous and this is a good location for getting around via the bus ($2.25 per ride), either the #22 Clark or the Broadway bus. Room was small but ok...very clean if you overlook the used bandaid I found on the back of the black plastic-covered guide to the hotel book. The A/C wasn't noisy, so I didn't have to use the earplugs that come with the room. No view; but, given the location, I didn't expect a view. Pillow cases were a little scratchy. Room was quiet even though it was near the 1 elevator that serves the whole hotel...no long waits for the elevator either...amazing. Breakfast is 6:30am to 11am and I always got there early when the selection of cheese danish was still there...fresh oj was nice...some protein or yogurt would have been nice. The staff was helpful and friendly but they might need more maids as I couldn't check in early...but, they held my luggage for free. There was a huge convention in town, so I stayed further north than I normally would...but, I would consider this hotel a pretty good value (via Priceline). They will put $60 charge on your card to cover any mini-bar (which is basically micro-wave popcorn & a granola bar) or damage charges. But, they take it off within a few days. There are vending machines with chips, water, soft drinks (all reasonably priced!!) on the 1st floor and there's one washer & dryer too...which is a big plus when I travel light!

“Low-key and comfortable” This hotel is different than most I've seen lately because of the way the entrance is tucked away between a restaurant and office building. There is small hallway from front door to check-in to elevator. It has a European feel and in fact many European tourist were staying there. The room was nice and very comfortable. The walls seem to be thinner than most and hall noise was noticeable. The most impressive is the housekeeping. It is excellent. They really deserve a mention of this because it is really a cut-above the norm.

“Cheap place to stay at the airport” Without a doubt, one of the ugliest hotels I’ve ever seen and does not look anything like their web page advertises, however ugly doesn’t keep you from sleeping at night. This is a good place to go if you want a cheap, mostly clean but dated room to stay in right at the Seattle airport. There was a little mold in the shower stall grout and a few mystery stains throughout the room, but I’m practically a germophobe and slept comfortably at night. The rooms were quiet but then again I think the hotel was mostly empty. Shuttle service was FAST, and the entire staff was friendly. The restaurant was one of the strangest looking places I’ve ever paid to eat in, but the food was surprisingly good and so was the value (for a hotel restaurant). The in-room heater was a little unusual (Setting 1 is highest heat, 10 is lowest heat, makes sense if set as an air conditioner though). The room didn’t smell at all and neither did the heater. I would stay here again if I needed a cheap room near the airport. A lot of the other people commented that the hotel needs a major facelift, but they’re probably not factoring in that would probably increase the room rates too. If you need a pretty place to stay, there is a Hilton right next door for a lot more money. When I booked the Clarion had lots of rooms in the $70-$80 range.

“Good value” As long as you get a good rate, this place is a great value. Don't expect a ton of extras, but the place is clean and the staff is friendly. The room was huge; the decor reminds me a bit of a guest bedroom, complete with wicker. It's close to everything and has on-site parking.

“Perfect location and price!” The hotel perfectly fit our needs. The rooms were a good size (a little small, but still great), bathrooms were great and we even had a small walk-in closet. The staff was friendly and very helpful and the continental type breakfast was good. Easy access to everything especially when a subway station was at the end of the block! Would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in NYC. The elevators were a little small and slow, but the hotel is older which means it has tons of character (and I mean that in a good way). And if you have a street view, it can be a bit noisy sometimes. Those were the only negatives we could find.

“Clean and comfortable but a bit overpriced” Why oh why do the upscale hotels charge for Internet service when a low priced hotel offers it for free? Otherwise, I can't complain too much. The room was spacious, clean and the bed comfortable. The common areas are well maintained. Parking at the hotel and the room itself are overpriced. Location is great - you are close to restaurants, the convention center, Back Bay shopping, the South End and Copley Square. I tried the fitnesss center and pool and found both to be worthwhile plus no extra charge.

“Great location, helpful staff” One night stay for business. Close to the White House, K street, and both the red and blue (DCA) metra lines. Concierge helped me order in good Chinese food. Watched a motorcade zip by. Will definitely stay again.

“Great Value, Clean and Convenient” We stayed a week at the Holiday Inn Express, Wall Street using our accumulated hotel points. Check in was fine and we were given a room immediately at 12 Noon, much ahead of the check in time posted (4:00 pm). When we got to our room on the 7th floor we immediately noticed the carpeted floor directly in front of the bathroom was wet. So we notified the front desk and we were sent to a better room higher up in the building. I met with the housekeeping staff about the "wet floor room" and found out that because the building was so new the staff had maintenance issues with a number of the rooms. Most notably the ceramic soap holders in the tile showers were falling off! Even in our "better room" the soap holder was no longer in the shower. But, these are all small issues and the real value in this hotel is that it is clean and new. The breakfast offered is the same old Holiday Inn Express fare that a traveler finds in every single Holiday Inn Express. The staff at this hotel tries very hard to be helpful and they are sincere. If possible, get a room away from Water Street. The road and construction noise could be heard all night long. I am used to very busy street noise but some travelers would find this unacceptable. I will stay at this hotel again and loved the convenience to the subways. Also, the neighborhood is safe and there are enough conveniences nearby to make this a fairly good spot for an extended, moderately priced hotel stay.

“Better than expected” The hotel appears to be a conversion of an Embassy Suites with its vertical atrium and actual two room suite layout. The rooms are roomy and nice. The hotel common areas were a bit better than expected, and the hotel has one of the best Jaz Clubs we have seen. Big names are booked in all the time. With the property's proximity to Harvard and MIT, it was clear they have quite a few related events, thus the quality of the common and group areas appears higher than most Double Tree hotels we have experienced. We were disappointed with the cleanliness of our bathroom. Too much dirt and dust and foreign hairs for our taste, but we always examine the bathrooms very closely when we evaluate a room. Another slight disappointment was the parking fee. We understand they need to pay for the nice garage structure, but we thought $25/day was a little high for a hotel that is not in town. It would certainly be even more at a downtown hotel, but $15/night would have been okay with us. While it may be possible to get a view that isn't great, our view of the river and MIT was outstanding. There were rowers every day, and that added to the feeling of the area. Given the property is a bit removed from downtown Boston and Harvard Square, the shuttle is a very nice service. It is regular, on demand and costs nothing. Many people may view the distance to downtown a real negative, but we found the property to be more quiet and peaceful than an urban hotel, and shuttle transportation offset the distance.

“Excellent Value self contained suite” Under $100 per night via Expedia, in the middle of the Biotech area outside San Diego, $50 cab ride from the airport. Staff are great really helpful and friendly, suites are big, well looked after and kept clean, most seem to have a balcony too

“Not much good at PHL Airport” The reception area is quite run down and untidy. Rooms much better. Cleanliness ok, good beds, although narrow Queens. Could become a problem if they put you up with two adults and one child in such a room, as they did in our case. Airconditioning unit much too noisy to sleep, definitely have to switch it off at night. Other than that, quite thin walls, so you hear a lot from your neighbors. Also, very noisy water lines, alive all night... Nothing at all in the surroundings (even the immigration officer at the airport warned about that..). Except a so-and-so Ruby Tuesday Restaurant next door. Small outside pool is clean and ok. All in all, hotel seems to be one of the more acceptable ones at PHL Airport. However: If you have the choice timewise, definitely go downtown! (We hadn ́t, because our flight left at 7:30 next morning.) Enjoyed the free hotel airport shuttle though which runs every 30 minutes and takes 10 minutes.

“Great Top to Bottom!” We stayed here for three nights and loved it. Staff, cleanliness of rooms and location are highlights. Just steps from a subway. Very friendly staff, every one of them. Unfortunately we didn't have a room that faced the front but were still very happy with our room. The rooms are a little small but it's New York City so I expected that. However, the rooms are very clean and up-to-date. Area was safe and you could walk to Times Square, Empire State Building and Rockefeller Center. You could also take a short subway ride there as well (except Empire State). If you need some quick food there are a couple good mom & pop Italian places right next to the hotel. I recommend the one (can't remember the name) that is about 100 feet to the east of the hotel (take a left when you walk out the door. Breakfast was standard continental and was fine. Nothing fancy but got the job done. I couldn't believe the rate I got. I just hope whoever manages this hotel keeps up the good work. I'll definitely stay there again when I come back. Free WiFi is a definite plus.

“Pleasantly surprised - great stay” My wife and I just completed a two night stay over Memorial day 2010. Check-in was very efficient, and we proceeded to our room. The room was still being cleaned, so my wife and I just waited in the hallway for them to finish - we didn't grumble one bit. Now perhaps all of this happened because of my Hilton status (Diamond Member) - I can't be sure. But within minutes a crew of cleaning ladies came to aid the one woman finish cleaning the room. About the same time, the lady who checked us in handed me a $50 food voucher for the restaurant downstairs and offered to change our room (which we accepted as we got a street view room - which was much nicer). In all of my many years of staying (generally only) at Hilton-brand hotels, I have never received such great service. I was amazed. The room was nice - a standard Hilton Garden Inn room. The breakfast (which there was some discrepancy if I should receive it for free - which I am used to as a Diamond member) was very good and it is located in the restaurant downstairs. The subway is right outside the door - which is very handy (A,C,E line). Wifi is free. Looking at other reviews, I have the following comments: I had a dresser to store clothes. The flat screen TV was on top of this dresser. I also had a refrigerator (which worked great and was empty - just waiting for me to use). For NYC Standards - these rooms are on the larger size. I stayed in room #314 - it was a nice room/location/view. We paid $200/night, though we booked months in advance. Lastly, when we used the free food voucher in the restaurant downstairs, we had EXCELLENT service and the food was very tasty (though a little on the pricey side). The service for the buffet breakfast was not as great, but I guess that is to be expected. Note: Weekend parking seems very plentiful (and free on street - just be sure to move it Monday - Friday

“New, modern, comfortable conference hotel” I stayed here with my husband for a conference. I found out this enormous hotel is new, only 3 years old. The rooms and bathrooms are modern, immaculate and bright with floor to ceiling windows. The beds are extremely comfortable; we slept so well. There was no minibar in the room which was fine for us and there were many places to get food just outside the hotel in the Gaslamp area. There is a Starbucks and yogurt store onsite but they can only be accessed by going outside which is a bit inconvenient. As with previous reviewers' mention, it is a little sterile and impersonal. The lobby is open and there was always people milling about. The concierge was a bit snobby, not even attempting to call one restaurant for a reservation as she was sure it would be fully booked. We used the hottub which was nice. Regarding conference areas, these were plentiful but the wifi access was terrible and not available in the rooms.
