With conference booking, we got free wifi which was a super perk (they left a message on the phone with the password) and wifi worked seemlessly in the hotel bedrooms, thank goodness. My husband and colleagues were appalled that the waitstaff were clanging dishes and serving etc during a lunch session when speakers were presenting. We hope that the hotel can communicate better with conference organizers to prevent this rudeness by organizing time/breaks when there is no food service and disruption to speakers. The main onsite restaurant Vela was terrible - they messed up our order twice (bringing the wrong dish to our table and then the dish had the wrong side dish) and the total time between sitting down and finally getting our meal was 45 minutes. It was not busy and there was no compensation. I would not eat there unless you absolutely felt lazy and don't want to leave the hotel. Maybe try the Sports Bar. Location is good, right next to the Convention Centre and 5 minutes walk to Petco Park and 5th Ave/Gaslamp Area. Horton Plaza shopping was disappointing. We had dinner at the Hotel Del Coronado one night. It's worth visiting that historic hotel across the Coronado bridge. There is some strange thing about which kind of taxis and can you between San Diego and Coronado though. Nobu in the Hard Rock Hotel across the street was excellent. I was also displeased to find out that packages I sent to this hotel required at least a $6 fee per package for handling as all their mail is processed through the UPS store. No other hotels at which I've stayed had this policy but I think because this hotel is so large, it requires this service. You can check-in for your flight and print your boarding pass for free in the UPS Store/Business Centre. I still give this hotel a 5 points because it was comfortable and new. We paid conference price for this hotel, which was still about $250 per night. I would only consider it again if it was quite discounted. We did however, make good use of Hilton HHonor's current bonus points deal.

“Great staff, good location, not so great rooms” As the title says- they have a great staff. Very friendly and helpful people and they must have said hello to me at least once an hour. The hotel is right beside the airport so it's perfect for an overnight stay when traveling. Conference facilities are excellent. My room looked and smelled a little dated but I guess the hotel has been there for more than 20 years. So overall it was nice and I'd go back.

“sauber und preisgünstig” Das Ramada hat eher Motelcharakter, aber die Lage ist ruhig, die Mitarbeiter freundlich und hilfsbereit, das Zimmer war sauber. Das Hotel war sehr hellhörig, man hörte selbst, wenn jemand leise am Zimmer vorbeigeht. Ich hatte ein ruhiges Zimmer verlangt und zwar eines bekommen, bei dem die Nachbarzimmer nicht belegt waren, aber leider direkt unterhalb der Klimaanlage auf dem Dach, die nachts alle 30 Minuten lautstark regelte - absolutes No-Go, insbesondere, wenn ein Hotel nicht ausgebucht ist. Es gibt definitiv Hotels in Canoga Park, die ein besseres Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis bieten.

“Great Stay in the Loop!” Shared Thanksgiving weekend with family at The Silversmith! Helpful staff, top-quality rooms and convenient to the L. Safe and a great base for shopping, exploring architecture - and if you're a foody!

“Very high end, but left me cold” I stayed at the Fairmont for business in March. It is a beautiful hotel, impeccably maintained. The outdoor patio garden is beautiful at night, lit with thousands of tiny lights, and is a beautiful, romantic place to dine in nice weather. The rooms are very nice and clean, bed was very comfortable. Location is 10 minute walk to the Foggy Bottom metro, which was convenient. However, as nice as the hotel is, and I don't want anyone to think that this is not a four-star hotel, my experience left me cold, and I would stay elsewhere next time. You have to pay extra to use the gym and pool, which seems ridiculous considering the prices they are charging. The staff was very courteous, but distant. I arranged for a wake-up call which I did not receive, which caused me to be late to the first day of my meetings, which was extremely upsetting. When I went to the concierge's desk to get some directions, I had to wait until the two people at the desk were done talking to each other. There are hardly any restaurants in the area. I did eat dinner at the hotel, and it was very good, particulary the prix fixe menu. Maybe I just had an off experience, but the Fairmont would not be my choice next time.

“Great Location... but subpar treatment of Gold members and so-so rooms!” I checked in at the Embassy Suites downtown Houston yesterday afternoon. I've stayed at a number of ES properties and tend to prefer them, especially if I'm sharing the room with another person. It's always nice to have the extra space, or at least the separation of space. This particular ES property is in a phenomenal location if you want to be downtown. Having said that, it's not the typical ES. It's not set up in the typical atrium fashion, which is either positive or negative depending on how you feel about the atrium set up. Instead, it's set up like every other normal hotel. Oh well. The room itself is very small for an ES property. I booked here rather than across the street at the Hilton because I wanted the extra space. But, I'd bet that the Hilton rooms are just as big as these, if not bigger. My other room-related qualm is with the bathrooms. We don't have a bathroom door. Instead, we have a sliding divider than partitions the bathroom from the rest of the room. It does not, however, give you very much privacy. Very strange set up, to say the least. My biggest issue is with their treatment of HHonors gold members. I have been staying almost exclusively at Hilton brand properties for the last few months in an attempt to gain more loyalty points. I have been very impressed by the service of the vast majority. From free upgrades to complimentary breakfasts, I was really starting to believe that it paid to be loyal to a hotel brand. My check-in at this hotel has proved otherwise, unfortunately. My Gold member profile shows a request for a high floor room. I booked this room three months ago. On a 19 floor hotel, where did they put me? On the 6th floor overlooking the parking lot. Wow! No recognition of my gold status or any special benefits. Just a standard check in and thorough disappointment when I got to the room. Oh well, stuff happens, right? I would be unlikely to stay at this property again in the future. While the location is excellent, there are other hotels in the same area that might have better service etiquette. The Hilton is located directly across the street. The Four Seasons is right around the corner as well. I'd recommend staying elsewhere, but maybe I just hit this hotel on a bad weekend.

“Great staff but needs renovating” I've stayed at this hotel twice in the last few months for a total of 9 nights. The front desk staff is top notch. They are friendly, helpful and go beyond the call of duty. When I lost my phone charger, they searched the hotel for another. One of the staff offered to let me use his until he went off duty. However, the hotel needs (and is scheduled for) renovations. My shower leaked terribly. I even called the manager up to show her the tub was 1/2 full from drips during the day. She was very appreciative that I'd called it to her attention. This hotel is very close to the airport, shops and restaurants.
“Nice hotel...good service...met expectations” Standard stay at a place like this. Staff was nice. No noise or cleanliness problems. No issues and close to TCU stff and Ft Worth zoo.

“Renaissance Marriott Times Square-Loved It!” My family and I were very pleased with this hotel.The employees treated us very well including the maid who was able to tend to our requests.They were all very pleasant. The room was very spacious and beds were very comfortable!Also the rooms were very clean.This was the first time we had a great view of Times Square (At many hotels we looked at walls!)And being in the middle of Times Square it was a great location. We had breakfast at Foley's and although a little expensive it is worth it for the view.Great service! When booking this trip I searched many vacation package sites.I actually found a better package (hotel & airfare) on the Marriott site itself.It sometimes changes prices from day to day so keep checking back for the best deal and flights. We plan on returning in the near future and hope to return to this hotel.We will plan on going to Foley's at night this time but will remember to make reservations because they were booked when we tried to go in the evening. All in all a great hotel!

“Good location, hotel not so great” The location on this hotel is great, just minutes from LAX. The shuttle runs 24 hours, every 15/20 min. The shuttle ride was only about 10 minutes to the airport. The service was great, and there are free drinks and snacks in the lobby every night. The rooms were spacious, with a balcony, but mine was somewhat musty smelling. The onsite restaurant was kind of disapointing, with limited choices. Overall, for the price ($200) it was ok, but not great. Also, the internet was a 9.95 per day charge.

“Good hotel, lost a star because of the noisy heater and non-working pool” The hotel location was perfect, right in the center of town and just a few blocks to the convention center. I walked from here to Pike's Place market for breakfast, then on to the convention center each day of the convention and found it all very convenient. (Try the Crumpet Shop for breakfast, delicious crumpets, and cheap lattes before 8:30am every day!) The hotel room was clean and everyone who worked here was helpful and perfectly friendly. The bed was too comfortable :). The first night I had trouble sleeping though, because the heater would wake me up every couple of hours. By the second night, I learned to tune it out. There is a coffee maker in the room, by the way (I had read somewhere that there was only coffee in the lobby, and this is not true.) There is also a nice little fridge where I stored away spring water for my week. I had a view of the Space Needle without even asking - very nice. Unfortunately, they were working on the pool during my one-week stay, and that was kind of annoying because I had chosen the hotel for their pool. I did get to swim the first night, and it was a nice smallish pool. There was a lukewarm hot tub attached. All in all, though, nice amenities. Would stay again, would recommend for the rates, the location and the comfy rooms.

“Lovely Hotel - Great Location!” The Affinia lived up to the Tripadvisor reviews. Hotel was in a great location, just of the Magnificent Mile, and will easy transport links, just one block to the bus routes and a couple of blocks to the subway. Rooms were spacious, the split level layout made them feel even more roomy. I also loved the pink shiny bathroom! People have mentioned in previous reviews about the street noise, but we slept soundly, but we were on a high floor. Perhaps worth requesting a higher floor if you are noise sensitive. Roof bar had amazing views, but was pretty busy when we went up - however service was good and we enjoyed it - worth a trip up even just to look at the views at sunset. Facilities at the hotel were great, we had a walking tour delivered to our rooms for no extra charge which was a nice touch, it had an iPod, pedometer and guide books. Really enjoyed our stay at this hotel and would definitely stay here again if our travels take us back to Chicago.

“Wonderful for a Business Stay!” I am in this neighborhood for work often. I have tried the Four Points (eh), the DoubleTree (not bad), and the Affinia (steer clear) - but I am going to be staying at the Eventi going forward - no question. PROS: great location (near Penn Station) 630am (free!) morning pilates class - sign up the night before, they give you a wake up/reminder call free internet - if you sign up for Kimpton rewards program, no big deal quiet - I had a room on the 21st floor, no street noise great view wonderful, clean, brand new gym big and beautiful bathroom security - they check to make sure you are a guest before letting you go up the elevator in the evening CONS: bedroom was small - but it's NYC, so what can you do? (There is a full service spa on site, I did not try. Nor did I try the restaurant or room service.) There is a very fun outdoor seating area connected with their "food court" - aka FoodParc - which is a perfect place for a quick snack, or night time frozen yogurt.

“Nice hotel in downtown” We stayed here one night before heading out to lake country... The hotel was very clean with several restaurants within walking distance. Our room was spacious and clean. (Aside from the windows which needed a good cleaning on the outside). Although Detroit can seem a little intimidating to walk around, we had no problems walking from the hotel to areas near the Fox Theater, Greektown Casino, etc. even in the evening. I would stay here again if I needed to be downtown. The only possible negatives I might add are: - parking is about $25, valet only - downtown Detroit is pretty depressed and obviously so with the many abondoned buildings surrounding the hotel - though the hotel is clean and modern, it's not much more interesting than that - the building exterior needs a deep cleaning - the rooms are a bit overpriced

“Basic but comfortable” I booked this room for a night before an interview at UCSD. Arriving late at night, the room was not clearly marked on the outside, so a little searching was required. Once I found the room, it was basic with a king size bed, small table, and a desk. There was a fridge in the room which was nice. The towels smelled like smoke, but they appeared clean. The room overall was clean (which was not the case on many of the subsequent hotels I stayed at during this trip). Check-in and check-out was quick with no problems. I would stay at this motel again, but this is more of a place for budget minded customers and business.

“Helpful and Accommodating” When we checked in, the room was not really acceptable. I'll spare the details (it involved some limited mobility issues we had at the time) but when we went back to the desk, they were more than accommodating. It may have helped that I am a Diamond status with Hilton but they quickly found us a very nice room and offered to help us move our things. The executive lounge is nice but nothing to write home about. A good place to step out of the hurly burly, however, and a pleasant place to sit a while at those times when you really want to get out of your room. Our conference amenities were well handled and even though some construction was underway they managed to keep things flowing well. And, of course, the location is great as most reviews note (except when the President decides to dine across the street, as he did during our visit, and the whole area of blocked and congested!) So for a pretty much standard Hilton experience with a helpful service attitude, the Capital Hilton is a fine choice.

“For the price this is disappointing” What I didn't like: 1. Bed is not triple sheeted - I hate touching the blanket that a naked person sat on hours ago. 2. Starbucks closed at 7:15 am 3. Room not made up at 4:30 pm - I had to call 4. Despite what was written in the reviews here, there was no transportation to the sports complex 5. Security gate to parking lot did not work on two different attempts 6. Indifferent staff (except for one housekeeping supervisor); blue jeans are the new restaurant uniform? 7. Bathroom needed attention 8. Asked for an extra towel - did not receive it 9. First room - lamp broken and hanging over - how did the housekeeping staff miss this? 10. Signage poor coming from 95 S I am a frequent traveler to Philly. There were no rooms available in town because of a convention. I would not return here unless I had no choice. Good luck.

“buona solo la posizione” Ho soggiornato due notti presso l'hotel BW President di NY. La posizione è ottima, proprio ad un passo da Times Square, mentre l'hotel non è un gran che. La sala colazione è piccolissima e praticamente nella lobby, il cibo passabile, ma con poca scelta. La prima camera che mi hanno assegnato doveva essere non fumatori e c'era dentro una puzza di fumo terribile. Quindi ho cambiato con una apparentmente migliore, anche se sempre molto piccola. La sera poi ho dovuto fare i conti con le tubature dell'acqua che andavano in risonanza quando i vicini facevano la doccia oppure io aprivo l'acqua calda. Neppure l'idraulico ha potuto farci niente ed ogni volta dovevo chiudere il rubinetto generale dell'acqua. Per non parlare del rumore... le finestre sono quelle americane vecchio stile e ad ogni ora del giorno e della notte sembrava di essere in strada e NY non è silenziosa neppure di notte.. non lo consiglio e non ci tornerei.

“Not Too Shabby!!” Stayed here for a weekend getaway on the Stay 3 Nights and get the third night free. This in itself was a great deal, and sold the hotel for us. We brought our dog along because it was dog friendly, and the website promised welcome amenities for the dog when we got there, we never got anything. This wasn't a huge deal, and our dog didn't care so that was ok. The pools were awesome with a relazing lazy river. Unfortunately, there was a nerd convention in town, and there was a bunch of teenage geeks running around in costumes making a lot of noise. This almost ruined the whole weekend. But when you look at things that the hotel can control, they didn't really do any wrong. There was no above and beyond service, but it wasnt bad by any means. We liked the spacious rooms and the pools, and was in a nice location We will probably be staying here again!

“Great stay but could use some improvement” I think the first thing we were all surprised with was the location of the hotel. We took the subway from JFK to get here and got off on 28th St. It didn't look like much but once we got to the hotel and headed towards 23rd, you see the beautiful Madison Square Park and Flatiron Building! The Flatiron is really a beautiful building and truly unique! Around that area is also the popular Shake Shack right inside the park, as well as Mario Batali's Eataly! There's no restaurant in the hotel itself so at least there are a couple of legit options around. We had the Madison Double and it turned out to be one of the biggest hotel room I've ever stayed in for NYC. NYC is known for the tiny rooms, even with doubles, but this room was fairly spacious with two full size beds rather than the "queen" size bed that it states. Flat screen TV and a remote controls the curtains. The temperature can be set easily also. Beds were very comfy as we all got a good night's sleep. The room also comes with one of those iHome iPod/iPhone controls. The only thing about the room is the layout of the bathroom. Our room's wash stand was right in front of the toilet with little room to spare. Had to make sure we didn't touch the bowl when we were brushing our teeth :P However, the showers were awesome. Swiss rain fall coupled with a few shower heads that shoots right at your body. The knob did fall off but I blame it on the Moen shower controls they use since I literally fumbled with everything until I found the right one. Took me awhile to figure out where the control was and how to turn the shower on. TV in the mirror is a nice touch! Free wi-fi which should be great, but it is PAINFULLY slow. It got to the point where we all gave up on using the wi-fi for our phones and switched back to 3G. Staff was very helpful!

“Stay Elsewhere” Stayed at the W on the same trip to Austin, so comparing my experience there to here. Room was incredibly small and worn out. Internet did not work well. AC unit was noisey. No real desk area to do any work. Had an issue with the room rate (booked with Amex FHR, show up and it's another rate at the Driskill). Had to call twice to the front desk to get this issue fixed, and it prolonged check-in to a 10 minute process, which is not the greatest thing when all you want to do is get into the room and take a nap. The bar is great, but I would rather stay at the (better service, value, gym, etc) W or (save your money) the Sheraton down the street.

“Good Spot” I have mixed feelings about this hotel. The location was superb for us, walking distance to our first visit to Fenway. Check in was a bit rough though. When we arrived they told us our room would be ready in an hour to an hour and half (3pm-3:30pm), no big deal. When we came back we we were told that it would be another half hour. So we got our bags and went up to work out. It was the day after the 4th and I am sure there were a lot of late check outs and maybe the hotel was short handed with staff. Just a minor annoyance being a gold member. The fitness center was nice, although I prefer Life Fitness ellipticals over the Precor ones that make you feel constricted. The corner room we had was very spacious. However, the bathroom in the room was rather small. The sink was like 2.5 feet tall. I am 5'11, so not tall by no means, so I could see how it would be very uncomforatble for tall people. I think the shower would pose some problems for taller people as well. Oh well, maybe the room was made in revolutionary times.:) The bed was very comfortable and the noise level was pretty good for a city hotel, but maybe that was because we had corner room. Unfortunately after the first night, we noticed the sheet had a stain, that appeared to be a small blood stain, on it. The manager at the front desk did make sure that the sheet was gone that day while the room was cleaned. Finally, the free breakfast vouchers we received were a big disappointment. They had a little room reserved for the "Continental Breakfast" people with limited selection of cereal, fruit, cheap breads, and eggs that look like they were sitting out there for hours. The restaurant next to that little room would be more appropriate place to have breakfast. Needless to say, we didn't use the vouchers the next two days. Instead, one of the days we made it to Stephanie's on Newbury within walking distance for a great brunch! If going to Fenway, we would be back. If going elsewhere in Boston we would look elsewhere before booking here. And after originally ranking this thee stars, after writing the entire review I felt compelled to go back to make it two stars, based on the # of negatives in a 3 night stay.

“Desperately Needs Updating” This is a Courtyard that is overdue for the major renovation that all the other Courtyards have been getting recently. The lobby and rooms are kinda shabby and dated and my bed was way too soft. I was told the big remodel is happening in January, so this will soon be a great hotel. The counter people are among the friendliest I have encountered in this level of hotel. They will drive you anywhere within two miles -- which is great, as there isn't much a person can walk to near the hotel. They took my travel companion and I to a great Mexican restaurant about two miles away for dinner. And, they offered to take me to a Starbucks for coffee the next morning. If I return after the remodel, I bet I will give this one over 4 stars.

“almost perfect...just a few tweaks would do it!” will start with the staff...loved them! from check in, to restaurant, cleaners wishing me good luck, and the bellman who found me a ride to the airport (great value) around the parade, the staff made our stay wonderful. the room is not big, but you can have a party in the bathroom...huge!!! loved tub and shower being separate, and the modern, high sink and counter space. furniture (desk chair, chair and ottoman, dresser, etc) were functional and that was much appreciated...so cool to have a recycling bin! safe was big enough for my 17" mac...which is not always the case at hotels. everything was clean, except a couple of spots on carpet and bed skirt...what would i do differently? a trash can in the room (along with recycle one), a make up mirror in bathroom, and if not too much to ask, a harder bed? bed was "ok" but both hubby and i thought it was sinking in the middle. finally, i would have loved some better choices of tv channels...yes, i know one does not travel to watch tv but lodgenet is definitely "male skewed"...every channel was sports or news. missed having some other options like lifetime, a+e, bravo etc. maybe it is a ploy to get you to buy movies? liked the choices of movies but sometimes a little tv is very comforting. overall would not hesitate to stay there again...enjoy!!!

“Great location but not impressed for the price.” I stayed here for 2 nights on business. The good: The rooms are huge, clean, great views, easy access to anywhere in the city. T or Amtrak. The not so good. The cord to the plugs on the desk could not reach the wall outlet. I didn't understand how this done. I had to unplug the TV and light to use my laptop and there electronics. My first day I could not find the toilet paper dispenser. I looked all over the bathroom and just figured you used the spare roll. Only after taking a shower my first morning did I notice it was affixed way under the sink!

“Less than stellar Hyatt Place experience” I typically love Hyatt Place, and thought I would love this one as well. We stayed for two nights last weekend, and although the hotel itself is fine, the service was lacking. Every customer touch point was missing something. So, no love here. For example, I was able to book through Hyatt Gold Passport, two nights free using my points, smooth, easy, great service,No problems. A few days later, I called to the hotel to confirm our reservation, checking to make sure they gave us the same room for both evenings. The hotel did not secure the same room for us for both evenings. I had to really insist that yes, we really did want to stay in the same room for both evenings. once we got to the hotel, there were other little issues ( that add up to a less than stellar experience). for example, the bedding on the pull out sofa had blood stains on them, very unappealing in a blanket for my daughter. Or the number of towels in the room... They knew there were three of us, they should have supplied sufficient number of towels. The free breakfast area... So many people showing up for the free breakfast, yet not enough places to sit for everyone. The elevators... We had to wait ten minutes for boatloads of people to come and go, with only two small elevators for 6 floors of people. Or, the lack of bottled water in the room, even for a fee. The lack of a newspaper. Or the lack of body lotion with the bath amenities. Poor cable connection for the TV ( a sin during the Olympics).

“Great place for early flights” I am Diamond HH member and stayed one night on business trip. Had an early flight and decided to stay there night before, Checked in late that night and room was waiting for me. Hotel was sold out so glad I was able to even get in. Hotel was very clean, looks new. Front desk staff were very friendly and quick with checkin. Room was pretty standard for Hampton. Newer furniture and large bathrooms. Flat screen TV with Hidef stations. AC is window unit which is typical for Hampton. Those can be a bit noisy. Bed was comfortable. Nice towels in the bathroom. Wifi was strong but a bit slow. Took shuttle to airport the next morning. Very friendly driver and right on time! Great place to stay if you have to catch a flight early in the morning.

“Very Nice, Clean Hotel” My friend and I stayed for just one night, and loved the hotel. It had an awesome water feature in the hotel, and great large bar. Like all Hyatts it had a very comfortable bed, lot's of pillows, and large bathroom.

“Excellent location and overall good hotel for NYC” My husband and I stayed in this hotel for three nights. We were upgraded because my husband is a platinum member and therefore we had access to the concierge lounge. I haven't given this hotel 5 stars as we have stayed in more impressive Marriotts however this hotel is good for New York standards. A couple of things that could have been better.....the concierge lounge is not open on the weekend and no provision is made for breakfast on those mornings. This has not been the case for other Marriotts we have stayed. The breakfast (on Weekdays) and the hors d'oeuvres are pretty ordinary and we have seen better. Having said the above, the location is great and the rooms are very nice (as with all Marriotts). I would stay at this hotel again.

“Beautiful historic hotel ... pity about the folk out on the street!” I loved the historic beauty of Hotel Whitcomb. Stayed for 2 nights mid August before flying back home to Australia and I enjoyed my stay. The lobby was very elegant and I came back down after the quick check-in to admire it. The elevators are slow but then again it is an old building. I took the stairs a few times when I wasn't willing to wait. The hotel appears to be popular with tour groups and there were numerous full coaches dropping off and picking up folk in the few days I was there. My room was a little smaller than expected but manageable, the bathroom was cramped and there was nowhere to even put a toiletry bag which I ended up hanging off a clothes hook on the back of the door. Despite this, the shower was great as it had a new massage shower head which gave excellent water pressure, a good comfort after a day wondering around in the cold of SF's strange summer. There was free wi-fi which worked pretty well and a business center downstairs if you don't have your own computer. I think it was $5 for 20minutes which isn't bad value. Much has been said about the homeless and druggos around this end of Market street and I was surprised just by the sheer number of them all over SF, not just near Hotel Whitcomb. They didn't give me any trouble, even walking home at 2am after a big night. I found it fascinating that homeless co-exist with theatre goers and high end shoppers around the whole Union Square/Civic Centre area. The girl at the airport shutter booking desk was very helpful - forget her name but definitely good value. For the price and location, I recommend Hotel Whitcomb for its value and experience of staying in a historical building.

“fantastic service + rooms” From the valet to the front desk, I am extremely impressed with the level of service this Hyatt provides. The employees were genuine, helpful, prompt and kind. We had a beautiful mountain view room and found it comfortable and well appointed.

“sexy hotel” I highly enjoyed my stay at this hotel on a Saturday night. Though the hotel was full and the elevators were slow everyone was so nice and friendly. Having read the reviews here I knew what to expect and I was pleasantly surprised how nice the room was, not run down at all. First thing I did was start playing the CD they provided and mixing cocktails. Then off to the pool which is just OK but I do like the chaise lounges, nearly fell asleep in them. Then back to the room to use that awesome shower while looking out on the lake. Dressed and went to Whiskey Sky for cocktails, woops it was closed for a private party. Only disappointment of my stay. Went to Navy Pier for dinner at Riva's which was excellent then to the Shakespeare Theater for Second Cities Romeo and Juliet. What a hoot! Back to the hotel to watch the fireworks from our room. (See photo). Great bed. Good breakfast at Wave. Quick valet.

“Not bad but nothing special” Not quite Tribeca but location on Canal St between TriBeCa and Chinatown would be a good fit for business and leisure travelers wanting to be off the beaten path a little bit - the neighborhood just seemed to be a bit more quiet, a bit less crowded which I liked. Since I traveled for work and the office was in close proximity, I felt the location was very good. Hotel lobby is modern and brightly lit, and visitors seemed to make good use of the bar and computer workstations nearby. Room was OK - for the most part clean though I noticed a lot of smudges and scratches on the walls that probably could be addressed in a more thorough cleaning session. The outdoor patio was nice though - I think there are only three rooms that have this feature so request it if you can. These rooms are on the second floor only. Fitness center is just a room converted into a workout room with some various cardio and exercise machines. I'd recommend to anyone needing to travel for work in the SoHo area or anywhere south of there, but that's about it.

“A True Great Hotel” Recently stayed for 4 nights. Hotel is a local institution - Grand entrance lobby fantastic detail in the historic building but the rooms are modern and stylish. I had a corner room with city views (and a view of the lake -just). As with a Marriott spotlessly clean with a great bed. Bathroom was large with a walk in double shower. Staff were friendly and efficient. Only minor niggle is the excutive lounge is locked at 10pm - so no ability to get a bottle of water late at night. Location is great as well opposite Millenium Park/Grant Park. Eay walking to shopping and restaurants or a $10 will get you almost anywhere in the center. definitely high on my list of Marriotts to stay at.

“Wonderful wonderful” I stayed here for two nights in July. It is a very nice hotel, located within walking distance to the water Pikes Place Market, Pioneer Square and some shopping centers. Its a nicely appointed, beautiful boutique hotel. Staff was great; service was excellent. Free wireless if you are a Kimpton member. They also gave me $10 free from the minibar for being a member! Wine hour was a nice way to relax at the end of the day. I turned down the complimentary pet goldfish. Unfortunately I missed the fortune teller and massage. Pros: Location, great staff, beautiful hotel, wonderful service Cons: can't think of any aside from not being able to get a late checkout Summary: Loved this hotel. I'd definitely stay there again and recommend it to others.

“Overall very nice. A few nit-picky details...” This is a nice place to stay, and the valet staff are very friendly. The room is quite nice, as you would expect at an Embassy Suites. This is a very good location for downtown access, although our room view was of the top of Bubba Gumps restaurant below. There were a few nit-picky details that kept this from being a 5 star review. The tv picture was quite dark, and despite multiple attempts to remedy it, it remained so. It was that way on both tvs, although worse in the bedroom. They do NOT offer free wifi - strange in a hotel these days. The shower pressure was low-average, and that is quite disappointing to me in a nice hotel. The breakfast is overall an amazing hotel breakfast, although I was surprised that they did not offer flavored creamers for the coffee. At breakfast, they do ask you how your stay has been, and when we responded positively, we were handed a card asking us to review them on TripAdvisor. I believe this is likely why they are ranked #1, as I'm not really sure that this is the very nicest hotel in Denver, but overall, it is truly very good, and we did enjoy our stay. One additional note - I had purchased a room with valet package, and the checkout receipt had an additional valet charge. When I brought this to the desk clerks attention, she did fix it right away, but I don't know if they would have removed the charge, had I not caught it.

“Well-located, SO-SO Hotel...” I stayed here with a friend last summer and forgot to post a review. Copley is a great area to stay in but I don't think that the Westin is worth the price that it charges. The Marriott would be better for sure as it is connected to the Prudential Center. With that said, this year, I stayed in the TAJ and that was above and beyond ANYTHING compared to the WESTIN Copley. The Westin must attract conventions so it has a zoo-like atmosphere in the lobby, in front of the elevators and on the elevators. It was always crowded and noisy. The rooms were average and the bathrooms were not as clean as I like to see. I usually like the Westin Hotels so this one was not up to par as far as I have seen in other parts of the world. It was not worth the cost.

“A suite for $200 plus tax - unheard of!” I absolutely LOVE The Lombardy - if nothing else but for the fact that I booked a luxury room on one of those Web booking sites and was upgraded to a suite when I got to the hotel! Huge suite - livingroom, kitchen with small breakfast nook, a view over DC (suite was on the 11th floor), comfortable bed, great bathroom, flat-screen TV in both bedroom and dining room - great toiletries, functioning coffee maker, easy thermostat, ceiling fan - OMG, I really loved the whole setup. Free Ethernet connection on the desk in the livingroom, very fast and very reliable. Nicely stocked minibar, not too overpriced. They were renovating the elevators, so I assume that the hand cranking elevator staff will be gone. Otherwise, the hotel is lovingly restored to its 100 year old glory and gorgeous everywhere you look. Water pressure was a little dicey in the shower, but I tend to overlook such things when everything is so historic about the building. Had dinner in the restaurant - good food without too many complications. Had drinks in the bar which is super cozy and quite romantic (for those not traveling solo). Only drawback was that I asked for a wakeup call in the middle of the day, and they forgot. Otherwise I can't fault them for anything. Will stay there if I return to DC again.

“Will Come again and again” The location is great. The rooms are nice, the bathroom had a great tub and it had a very interesting mini bar. Yes, it has a mini bar that has "adult" items. If you are reading 50 shades of grey and want to give it a go all you have to do is open your mini bar. I would not want to bring children here as explaining the items would be very difficult. A fun stay nonetheless. A very nice staff also. The food in the mini bar was also pretty darn good

“My new favourite San Francisco hotel” I had the pleasure of staying at the St. Regis for 4 nights while attending a convention at the adjacent Moscone Center. The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is next door. Union Square, Market St. and the Ferry Building/Farmer's Market are within walking distance. The hotel deserves high praise for its location, design, style, technology, amenities and especially its service. The St. Regis and Luxury Collection are the Starwood group's high end chains. Having stayed 3 times at the wonderful St. Regis New York and having visited the St. Regis Monarch Beach CA and Washington DC, I was looking forward to my stay here, and at a convention group rate to boot. The hotel is about 2 years old and located on the corner of Mission and 3rd. Directly on the corner, the facade of a historic 8 story building was preserved and a high rise tower was integrated behind, beside and above it, on what once was a parking lot. The hotel occupies the first 20 floors of the tower; the top 20 or so floors are St. Regis residences. Within the older building are the hotel's 2 restaurants--Ame (dinner) on the first floor and Vitrine (breakfast and lunch) on the 4th--as well as the 2 level spa and offices. There is a landscaped terrace on the roof and another larger terrace on the 4th floor which was tented for an outdoor dinner party when I was there. The lobby in the newer building is compact but stylish and well-designed. A design feature of rose petals is echoed throughout the public areas. Our convention rate was for the superior room category on the lower floors (5-8), so I was pleasantly surprised when I was upgraded to a deluxe room--same size but on a higher floor (15). I also was able to check in early. My room looked similar to the photos posted on 1/1/06 by a TripAdvisor member from Sunnyvale CA. My room faced west with a view of Yerba Buena Gardens, Moscone and points beyond. The east facing rooms face the Bay, but several employees told me the views are often obstructed by the high rise office buildings of the Financial District. The room itself was not too large but contemporary and sleek. The entry foyer had a table, wooden floor sculpture and leather walls. There was another wood wall hanging in the bedroom. The bedside table held the St. Regis signature phone/computer that can control the thermostat, lights, window shades, alarm clock, etc. via a touch screen. There were 2 desk chairs and an easy chair, but no chaise lounge or "fainting chair" as seen on the hotel web site. There was a large marble window ledge--great for counter space. One wall held the 42" flat screen TV (which did not swivel) and 3 recessed doors--one was a too small closet (only about 2 feet of space), another held a safe, fax machine (out of ink) and 3 drawers, the third held the minibar and fridge and DVD/CD player. The spacious bath had an enclosed WC, a tub that opened onto the bedroom, a separate shower stall with marble bench, rain head plus hand-held head. There was a 2nd flat screen TV, but only one sink. In the room and bath, there were not enough places to hang clothes or towels. Technological glitches included: 2 remotes did not work but were quickly repaired (batteries?). With the phone/computer, the party I was speaking to occasionally could not hear me, though I could hear them. The hotel turned this glitch into an example of great service when I requested a wake-up call and the operator called twice but could not hear me, so she sent someone up immediately to give me a personal wake up call at the door. Alas, the phone still was acting up on check out day. Overall service was top notch--quick, courteous and professional--especially the front desk and housekeeping. The problem of a constantly barking dog in the next room was handled well and with many apologies. The doormen were not so attentive--often talking with the valets. No one helped me when I walked up with my luggage when first checking in. Some of the concierge staff, while helpful, were a bit aloof. I believe all the St. Regis' offer Butler Service. In New York this is quite formal, but seems less so here. One Butler I spoke to on the phone was rather unprofessional--when she couldn't answer my question, she yelled/asked another employee without putting me on hold, so I could hear every thing. The public facilities include a medium sized fitness center open 24 hours with the friendliest staff, and a wonderful indoor infinity lap pool, also open 24 hours. The whirlpool, steam room and sauna are within the spa--all are on the small side. The "Business Center" consists of 2 computers and one printer squeezed into a 3rd floor alcove by the elevators. This may be a temporary location. Regarding the sound of sirens mentioned in other reviews--yes you can hear them, but I imagine the other nearby hotels--W, Four Seasons, Westin, Marriott--can as well. I have stayed at a few other high-end hotels here--the Ritz Carlton, Campton Place, the Palace. I would like to one day try the Four Seasons and the Mandarin Oriental, but for now the St. Regis is my favourite San Francisco hotel.

“Good downtown Seattle hotel” My family and I stayed there for three nights during a vacation stay to Seattle and Vancouver this month. At a price in the low-$200s, we thought it was good value. It's an easy walk of several blocks to the Pike Place Market and everything else downtown. (Beware, part of this walk is uphill going or coming back. Choose your poison if you're sort of out of shape.) Numerous top-shelf restuarants are nearby, including the incredible Wild Ginger, which is just a block and a half away. The rooms have a clean contemporary feel. Our rooms (we stayed there before and after going to Vancouver) were outfitted with high-def televisions, mini bars, and safes. The rooms start on the 14th floor and go up from there (the garage is below) and offered great views. The hotel's business center is open 24 hours daily, and Internet is available there for a nominal fee. The Top of the Hilton restaurant offers great views of the city. We tried the breakfast buffet one day, and it had decent, but limited standard fare (sausage, but no bacon! was my 6-year-old daughter's complaint) for the money. Some of my party ordered off the menu for breakfast and loved the food. The Top of the Hilton is also open for lunch and dinner and has a small bar, but we didn't go up there for anything but breakfast. The lobby bar and lounge is comfortable and is laid out in vignettes that feel like your living room. The staff is very, very chatty and friendly and the concierges are very knowledgeable about local restaurants and attractions. The manager personally greets people as they check in, and thanks them for their business. Very nice, genuine touch. Nice hotel, whether you're in town for business or pleasure.

“Beautiful Hotel in a Great Location” We stayed at this hotel for two nights with our sons, ages 16 and 8. Our room had a wonderful view of the beautiful City Hall. The front desk and bell staff was so friendly and helpful, we felt welcome from the first moment we walked in. The location is perfect for us as it provided quick and easy access to the subway and a trolley stop. This was our first trip to Philadelphia so we were in awe of all of the wonderful history and architecture right outside the door. The little indoor pool area is small and only three feet deep, but is very charming looking, has a nice view and comfortable chairs,and was a perfectly fine place for us to relax and for the kids to unwind a little. The hotel seemed to have mostly business travelers and seemed to be very business-friendly. Since we were only there for a couple of days and were out and about most of the time, the fact that most everything there was geared more for business than family didn't bother us at all. If we were there for longer, I might have selected a hotel that had things for the kids to do and a bigger pool area. All in all, this was a really nice little hotel and we were very satisfied with everything about our stay there.

“Good with the bad” Everything in life is a trade-off. I was there four nights. The staff was very accommodating with a complex reservation and actually changed some things for my convenience. Good room rate. Location is convenient to Metro (not even a block if you walk in the right direction!), beautiful neighborhood (GWU). Grocery and pharmacy nearby. Hotel was very quiet. Refrigerator and stove were great conveniences. Cooked and ate in the room a lot. My room was well-cleaned each day. Any good restaurants are quite a hike, as are all of the tourist sights, if walking. Rented a car on the weekend. Parking is non-existent in area. Either park illegally, troll for 20 minutes, or pay high off-site valet prices. VERY small lobby. No business center. The hotel TV touted renovation with plush beds, but they hadn't made it to my room yet, apparently. Old worn furniture and bedding; linens were worn out. Room decor dated (gold, green, brown). I picked it due to personal convenience and Hilton points. All in all, would stay again, but things could be better.

“Quiet, competent, quality” Stayed at the Intercontinental for a conference, on the Concierge floor. All as expected in the clean, comfortable room. Pillow-top mattress and plenty of pillows as expected in a hotel of this quality. Room was clean, housekeeping came promptly every day. The housekeeping staff did one thing that is a pet peeve of mine - they changed the radio station from the public radio station I'd selected (which is hard to find on the dial) back to the classical music station they use for turndown service. This is so vexing, but obviously they've been trained to do it. Nice bath amenities. Shower curtain rod curved out - yay!Fresh orchid in the bathroom. Plenty of service staff in all public areas, restaurant, bar - food and beverage very solid. I ordered room service breakfast and asked for a couple of special things (eg: 2 egg omlette instead of 3, skim milk, salsa on the side) which usually most hotels mess up in some way, but it came within 20 minutes exactly as ordered. The cost was extremely reasonable for room service in a hotel of this quality. Also, many, many great restaurants within walking distance plus the Dallas Galleria shopping mall across the street. Business center was outsourced but the costs were not outrageous as they are in some hotels - $2.99 access fee and 60 cents a minute (it's much worse other places). Service was uniformly cheerful and efficient.

“Great value in NYC” I absolutely loved staying here. Nice room for a very nice price in Manhattan. Friendly staff, fresh baked cookies in the afternoon, and everything you need in NYC within walking distance. The rooms are actually fairly big for NYC standards. I highly recommend this hotel--no frills, but just what you need for a very pleasant stay in NYC!

“Perfect for families - Great location, large rooms, free breakfast!” We paid $89.00 a night for a king deluxe suite with a bedroom separated by French doors. The den was large with a full size sofa bed. The kitchen included a full size fridge, a stovetop, microwave, and a dishwasher. Also, a washer and dryer are onsite. Our first floor room had a 1/2 bay window in the bedroom and a huge window in the den that both overlooked the beautiful landscaping outside. All areas were clean and nicely decorated. I35 and other main highways are 1 minute away and downtown is very easliy accessible in 5-10 minutes. The free breakfast was hearty, and weeknights include a free dinner. Our family of 5 was perfectly comfortable!

“expectations were exceeded” i've always known hotel monacos' in various cities to have a certain style and level of service. The seattle hotel monaco blew them out of the water! my group and i were so impressed with our large, hip stylishly appointed rooms. I'd like to duplicate some of the fun touches in my own home! check in staff extremely friendly and nice. very comfortable bed/bedding--slept very well. good location to base your seattle trip. will definetely stay here again!

“Ideal Location” This is an ideal base for taking advantage of all the tourist sights and activities. Likes: - location - easy access to the Metro (no need to step outside) - clean comfortable rooms - close proximity to 7th street where there are plenty of restaurants. - easy walk to the White House and area. - concierge desk very helpful and good suggestions - toothpaste in addition to shampoo etc in the washroom - well organized; we were a large group and when we arrived all our room cards were made and placed in envelopes with our names. - there are several places to eat in the lobby including a Starbucks (but no free wifi there - unusual as all Starbucks have free wifi - see below) Dislikes: - high daily prices for wifi (it should be free - most hotels hi and low end have free wifi) - once I called the front desk to ask if local calls were free, I was told that they were but that there was a fee just for dialing out of the hotel (?). Ok so they're not free. I asked if I could go downstairs and make one local call from the concierge desk - the person at the front desk was not receptive to that at all and told me that there was no one there anyway. I could see from my room window into the lobby that there were in fact 2 employees at the concierge desk. I went down to the concierge desk to make my call without any problems (was helping some people get back home before hurricane Sandy was about to hit.) I had a good experience here and would consider returning if the price is right (if I could get a good deal).

“Still a great hotel, super location and wonderful staff” Booked this hotel at a pretty good discount about four months prior to my stay after having stayed here 15 years ago. The staff is the best thing about this place; my room had a terrible view but was comfortable and quiet and housekeeping was attentive. The bed was comfortable, the blackout drapes were effective and the air conditioning worked well for the surprisingly warm November weather. The wait for elevators was pretty short and the room was ready on time. The hallways were hot and dark but the woodwork and architecture throughout is charming. The front desk and bell captains were excellent and the location was very good for Union Square shopping. It is a quick walk to the Moscone Ctr or a brief cab ride. Coffee, cookies and wine in the lobby were a nice touch, too. Since I did not stay on the upper levels I cannot comment on the Concierge perks but this is a good choice for a business meal as the restaurant is really good. Would stay here again (perhaps sooner than another 15 years!) if I could get a repeat rate as good. This is a great example of a well-run boutique hotel.

“My New Favorite Hotel” My friend and I selected the Hotel Beacon because it was next to the Beacon Theater. We had tickets for Leonard Cohen and the hotel location was convenient. We were pleasantly surprised with a great room. There were 3 closets; important if you travel with kids. The bedroom had 2 double beds and a TV. The living room/kitchenette contained a loveseat size sofa bed, a chair and ottoman, bistro table with 2 chairs, coffee table, TV on top of a bureau, fridge, sink, stove and oven, and cabinets. The bathroom was small but looked newly tiled in marble and was fine for us. The room was clean and the furnishings appeared to be on the newer side. Close by are plenty of places to eat in a variety of price ranges and the Fairway market across the street was an experience in itself. I will definitely stay here again even if I attending an event in mid-town.

“Good airport hotel” Arriving from Asia after a long flight, I was looking for some needed sleep in the Westin Heavenly Bed. The free shuttle bus pick me up from the airport, it is shared with several other hotels around the area but the Westin is the first drop-off point from the airport. The lobby is a nice open space and quite busy at the time when I arrived. There was a long line at the check-in counter and as I was ready to line up, an employee came around and ask if there is any SPG Gold and Platinum members. There is a special check-in counters for these members on the right that I did not see. It was good to know that I was upgraded to a deluxe room, not sure what that is as I only want a room to rest before my transcontinental flight next morning. The room was a good size and look remarkably like the Westin Horton Plaza in San Diego. The Heavenly Bed is of course as great as usual. The bathroom is stock with the usual Heavenly Bath products that always a good choice in waking me up after a night of rest. The location of the Westin is pretty drab, there are nothing within a walking distance in terms of nice restaurant. So I just stopped by the McDonald and get something to eat. There was no one manning the front-desk the next morning around 5:30AM but the doorman was there to help me and a few other guess to either get a cab or the free shuttle to the airport. With a price of $120/night that I got, this is a pretty good for an airport hotel as good as this.

“Wonderful spa” I didn't stay here, but spent two glorious hours in the Spa. The facilities are brand-new and beautiful. The women's locker room is carpeted and furnished with full-length wooden lockers with digital locks--no key to keep track of, and you set your own combination so you'll actually remember it! There's an area with hair dryers, curling irons, complimentary hairspray and other toiletries; the immaculate showers are stocked with excellent shower gel, shampoo, etc. Oh, and the steam room! Gleaming porcelain and eucalyptus-scented steam...The only thing missing was robe hooks outside the steam room. Did I mention that the robes are thick and sweet smelling? I had a massage and a facial. Both were perfect and the providers most proficient. Even the obligatory new-age music was less annoying than usual (much of it was based on classical themes instead of endless appeggios). Altogether, a most highly recommended spa.

“Great stay” Although I'm typically a Starwood person, I have to admit this property is pretty nice. It's about a 15-20 drive from downtown Denver but it's close to Cherry Creek which is another nice area outside downtown. There were a lot of great bonus features: excellent fitness center, free parking, if you join the free Lowes membership you'll get free internet and the coffee in-room is generous. Rooms are spacious and clean & the bed was comfortable. Nice linens and bathroom amenities are also included. Staff is extrememly friendly and helpful and the bar/restaurant are cozy. Overall, I would recommend this hotel and the price point is typically much better than staying in downtown (LoDo) Denver. if you have a rental car or don't mind using a taxi - this is a great option. I should also add - it's a pet friendly hotel which we love!

“Good hotel - great location!” I didn't experience any of the negative things that other recent reviewers have commented about. My stay was only for an evening, but was quite nice. Likewise, the bartender at the bar on the top floor was also nice. The front desk staff, upon both check-in and check-out couldn't have been nicer. The room has a quirky and campy feel that perhaps some people don't get. The "window" between the room and bathroom was indeed odd, but it did manage to open the room up and closing it for privacy wasn't a problem. The wood panel-type walls behind the beds are different if nothing else. The park-like shades on all of the lights are unique. The usual Bliss toiletries found in all W Hotels are awesome. The beds were comfortable and was well furnished. The wood-like blinds on the windows were cool, and appropriately supplemented with a giant solid blind behind them in order to make the room truly dark. My only complaints about the room was the $14.95/day Internet charge (archaic in today's world where it's expected as a utility) and a couple of battle scars including a part of the desk where the varnish was coming off (see picture) and a big chip in the bathtub (see picture). The outside-facing wall unit HVAC unit was also odd for such a big inner-city tower hotel, as others pointed out. I'd much prefer central HVAC in any situation, but especially for such a big city hotel. The location is spectacular. It has a view of Lake Michigan and is right next to Navy Pier and beaches, and just a couple of blocks from North Michigan Avenue and the rest of the River North area were lots of great restaurants and bars can be found.

“In the heart of Midtown” A perfect location in Times Square. This hotel is in the heart of Midtown. Easy walk to theaters, restaurants and shopping. Large, clean suites with very comfortable bedding. We opted for a Times Square view. A great view indeed. Higher floors will be a bit quiter from the hustle and bustle of Times Square below. Front desk staff was very polite and professional.

“disapointing, from a hilton honors gold member, who knows hiltons” So, the hotel is what you expect from a monster size hotel connected to a convention center with a great location in Austin. Huge Lobby, built in Finn & Porter steak and sushi restaurant, Java on 5th that serves starbucks, all great and convenient. Why do I always get disappointed in a full service high-end hilton? Maybe I just expect too much. 1st annoying interaction, the parking lot was full when I came back from dinner. I was asked to park across the street in a surface lot at night, walk back and then go stand in a huge long line at the desk, complain and ask for a refund on the $20 they charge for parking. No apology, no sympathy. I hate the extra charges for internet. No water or coffee in the room. The walls seem to be thin, the hotel is a loud party hotel. The maid service never refilled my soap. I definitely get better service at the lower end properties in Austin. Personally, I'll go low key on my next trip.

“Location is great” We had a partial ocean view room that was about 6 rooms back from ocean front and you could hear the waves. We saw dolphins one of the mornings while sitting on the lounge chairs. The front building with the pool is just as pictured on the website. However, the standard rooms are in a completely different building. I would advise booking at least a partial view because the standard rooms are in a separate building behind the main building. The main building has the partial view rooms, full view rooms and pool. They don’t even show that other building on their site. It is nice having the refrigerator and microwave in the room. We went to Ralph’s and stocked up on drinks and snacks. We loved to be able to sit on the pool lounge chairs in front with a view of ocean and relax. We just took our cooler with drinks down and enjoyed ourselves. There are many restaurants/bars near. We ate at Kono’s for breakfast and, of course, it was great. Our friends that were with us had never been there and it was one of their favorites on PB. I would recommend this hotel for the beach front location.

“Performed well under stress” We stayed in this hotel for a football game, so needless to say the hotel was packed. Despite the crowds of people, the service was efficient and friendly, our room was nice and quiet, and it was a great location for an event at Bank of America stadium. It was a quick (maybe 4 block) walk to the stadium. We also enjoyed the downtown location for walking to nearby bars and restaurants, and it was easy on/off the interstate. Our room was comfortable with all the required amenities. Even with a lot of people staying at the hotel, the parking and front desk were efficient, and the staff kept people moving with speedy elevators and attendants.

“It's okay., for my Grandparents.” Stayed there last week for a business meeting. The staff from the start was horrible. I was told because they were so busy that I would have to wait for a room. I asked for the manager and while waiting for her two others in my party were given room keys. The manager said she was sorry and all of a sudden a room was available. Not sure what the problems is there. The room was small and old. The lobby, meeting, and ballrooms were incredible. The construction was minor. If I were wanting to relive the Roaring 20's or searching for Al Capone's loot this is the place. Otherwise there are a lot of great hotels in Chicago. This is not one of them.

“Nice hotel with minor annoyances” Why do the most expensive hotels charge for internet access - and in this case, access that worked sporatically. I had to end up replacing not only the wire (since wireless and wired are billed seperately, you must choose one or the other or pay twice!!!!) provided in my room, but also the in-room modem before getting any consistant service. It should be noted that the maintenance man that brought the equipment was very helpful and concerned. Otherwise, a good hotel with the typically overpriced amenities and F&B.

“Not Bad” Booked this place for 4 nights when it was still the Crowne Plaza and was hoping i wouldnt have any problems with check in due to the fact it's now the Tudor. Fortunately i had no problems other than turning up an hour before check in to be told i had to "Wait" for my room by a woman who wasnt the friendliest person i've met. I dropped my bag at the Bell Desk and they were happy to hold onto my bags for an hour. Came back an hour later again to get a guy with a bit of attitude but he issued me a room on the 2nd floor and i proceeded to my room. It was huge and to their credit actually quite a decent room. Bathroom was large as well and had a very generous serve of tolietries! Beds were clean and the TV was a decent size. As i was visiting friends i rarely spent time in my room but i did find it a little strange that my room had no "Guest Services Directory" in it. I'm not sure if it was just my room or if it applied to all rooms. I never did get a chance to ask them. Fitness Centre was nice and on the 2nd floor and whilst i never used the restaurant/bar it was always full of business people and seemed decent. One day i needed to find a post office, I asked for directions at the Concierge and they gave me the wrong directions!!!! It's about a 15 min walk to Times Square and about 5 mins to the Empire State Building. As someone said before i think the problem with this place is bad management and low staff morale. Overall i'd rate my stay as average but found the place a little too far away from everything!

“People and room choice made up for the decor” We stayed here for one night to let some of our party, who had never been see the city. Having read the reviews we had low expectations re the decor. We stayed in 14G, a two bedroomed apartment style suite. One room had 2 Queens and the other had a King. Both rooms had plenty space and the communal areas were very spacioius. However the bathrooms were tiny but as it was one night and we were all family it did us fine. We did not use the sofa bed as the 3 beds were enough and to be honest the sofa bed did not feel very comfortable. The room was very clean and the staff at the desk and door were very helpful. We left our bags at the hotel till we went to the airport. The front desk allowed us to use the fitness room washroom before we headed off, which was very convenient. The porter had arranged a great car for all 6 of us. The Internet charge is $13.95 + tax per day so we did not use it as we only had limited time to use it. I did notice a PC and printer at reception and a guest using it but I was not informed that this was available and the information pack in the room did not mention it nor the lady I spoke to re the internet connection. The location is slightly out of the main drag but was fine as we managed to walk up to TOTR and Times Square and also caught the bus across 42nd St for the water taxi tour to 9/11 Memorial. I would recommend this place for a larger group wanting to stay together.

“worn” I had read the posted reviews so I was not expecting too much. Most of the reviews are right on. The hotel common areas are very worn. There was a note in the room stating that the carpets are going to be replaced. No time frame was indicated. The halls smell nasty. The smell does not carry over into the room. Most disapointing was the location. In my opinion this is not a downtown location. There is a shuttle service and we were able to use it to get us to the 6th street entertainment area. A cab ride back was $5 - $7. There are several vendors operating out of the hotel parking lot - bike, boat - just a weird setup. I obtained this hotel on Hotwire. It is easy to spot as it is the only 3 star with a shutte icon. I would not pay more than $90.00 for this property.

“Would Try Again, But Not Impressed” To be fair, the hotel was under construction when I stayed. I was NOT expecting this when I arrived. I needed a place to stay on a Saturday night as I had a quick trip into the city. Saturday night rate was good....I should have known that construction would be the reason. Room is small, and bathroom was updated with fixtures, but tile and shower were very old. The tile in the shower was separating from the wall. Not impressed. However, the room and bathroom were clean, but housekeeping forgot to put a trash bag in the bathroom trashcan. I flew in LGA about 11:30pm so I was really excited to hit the bed. About 15 min into my sleep, my neighbors heating unit came on and rattled through the walls the entire night. I had to sleep with a pillow over my ears. Very thin walls. When morning came around, I checked out as fast as I could and grabbed breakfast at a nearby restaurant. Since the hotel was under construction their kitchen was closed. They attempted to make a temporary eating room out of another hotel room....but I was so annoyed with the lack of sleep, I did not even want to bother to see what was being offered or how it was set up. If the circumstances were different, my experience may have been better. The location was nice and once construction is complete, I may return to really see how this hotel really operates.

“Huge rooms!” It's a very busy hotel in the heart of times square but theres nothing like it. Its the amusement park of all hotels.certain Floors have restaurants, bars, gym is huge! All and all the rooms are clean and huge! The beds of course are phenomenal enjoy your stay! I know I did!
“Great stay in Soho” Extremely friendly staff is the first impression. After that - clean, modern rooms (albiet NY sized), fantastic location.

“It's not that bad!” I booked a room at this hotel through Hotwire and was very apprehensive after reading the reviews on this site. Well, the hotel really isn't that bad! I didn't have any of the problems that people have listed here. First of all, the staff had absolutely no difficulty with checking in someone who had prepaid. I was in my room within minutes. The room was at least average, possibily even above average. The size was nice, with an efficiency kitchen (including a full refrigerator). The room was quite clean and had no odor whatsoever. And there were no stains on the carpet. Everything looked reasonably new. Look, if I were judging this as a five-star hotel, I might have to raise some complaints. There were little cracks in the sink by the drain. There was a small area of chipped paint on the wall in the bathroom. The TV is small, maybe about 21 inches. But that's all I'd have to gripe about. This place doesn't pretend to be a five-star hotel (and doesn't charge like one, either). For what it is, it's at least acceptable. I'd have no problems staying here again.

“A very interesting experience.” Paid 80 dollars for this room through Priceline, and it sounds as if that's a steal in SF. If we couldn't have gotten this deal, we probably would have ended up staying at the airport. Anyhow....a few things: - Yes, the bad part of town is nearby. Here's my tip: Don't go southwest of the hotel. That's the Tenderloin district and it isn't very pretty. if you stick to going east (shopping and theater) and north (Wharf, touristy areas, etc), you'll be fine. The neighborhood the actual hotel was in seemed fine to me. - The beds are indeed pretty hard. My fiancee and I woke up both mornings with big time back pain. Let's just say we're more thankful for our bed at home now. - The decorations are very beautiful...it's a departure from your "typical" hotel...which I guess is what defines a boutique. - The room wasn't as small as some people made it out to be. If you want a Hyatt sized room...well...stay at a Hyatt. - This isn't close to the Wharf really...so that was a letdown. It was quite a hike to the coast! All in all..worth the money though.

“Not a fan before, and even less of a fan now!” I'll preface this review by saying I have never been a fan of this hotel and only stayed because the event I was attending in NYC had a complimentary room block. Suffice it to say, I won't even accept a complimentary room here again. My previous problems largely were due to the sheer size and inability of the hotel (particularly the elevators) to accommodate the numbers of guests and/or convention visitors. My complaints now encompass much more. Upon entering my first (of three) guest rooms, I could not believe I was in a Hilton versus a 1-star motel on the outskirts of town. I was given a non-renovated room which had carpet so dirty it turned my white socks black. The window curtains were stained. The walls were chipped as was the furniture. The stopper in the tub was pulled out with its rubber tubing attached and a puddle of yellow water in the tub. One of the light fixtures in the bathroom was missing its housing so the bulbs and wires were completely exposed. A call to the front desk informed me that none of the upgraded (deluxe) rooms were available that night so the soonest they could move me would be the following day, but maintenance would come take care of the other issues. The tub was fixed, but there were no replacement housing for the light fixture so it would stay. I switched rooms the following morning and the difference was as great as night and day. The room felt like a Hilton in an upscale business hotel - everything about it was 10x better. So the problem arose when I do my routine mattress inspection. I have been bitten by bedbugs before at an upscale hotel and it was not a pleasant experience so I am quite OCD about this. And sure enough, along the seams of one of the mattresses is a live bed bug, which I catch, and call the front desk to let them know. They immediately send security up to my room and the fellow could not have been friendlier, but I think part of it was that I actually had the little bugger so there was no denying it was there (at one point it felt like they tried to pin it on me for bringing the bedbug in the room, but as a frequent traveler who understand how to protect their belongings - I know I did not). So upon entering the room that the front desk manager had him move me to, he takes one look at me after smelling the stench of smoke and knows it is not acceptable. Beyond the obvious smoker who previously stayed, it was one of the older rooms again. At this point I was beyond angry, to downgrade me back to a basic room after finding a bedbug in the upgraded room was dumbfounding. The front desk manager informed me that all deluxe rooms were again full and there was nothing she could do. I told her thanks, but I would be checking out at this time. She finally offered to put me in a king room on the executive floor and give me access to the executive lounge the remainder of the stay. So that I would not have to leave hotels at 11pm, I agreed so long as the room was clean. Again though, this was an older room (why the executive rooms were not the first to be renovated is beyond me). So I entered my fourth room, thoroughly inspected it and agreed to stay. Suffice it to stay, I did not get under the sheets and barely slept the remaining two nights. At checkout, when asked how my stay was, I decided to be honest instead of delivering the obligatory - "Fine." The front desk agent was incredibly friendly and could not believe I had not been offered compensation beyond the pseudo-upgraded room and executive lounge access so she promised me that somebody would be in touch about additional compensation. I did receive a friendly e-mail from one of the assistant managers apologizing again and offering me a sizable number of HHonors points. At the end of the day I was hesitant to write such a critical review because I believe that eventually the customer service really tried to compensate me for the problems, but in 7+ years of extensive business travel I have never had such an awful experience, been in such an out-of-date and dirty room at an upscale business hotel or switched rooms more than once so I felt compelled to share. I believe my experience probably was one of the extreme's, but it happened and as I said before I had never been a big fan of this hotel during previous stays. On the plus side, the location is excellent being steps from Rockefeller Center and blocks from Central Park. The Halal Guys food cart right across the street is deserving of the long lines and worth a try. So I may try a different Hilton property next time in NYC, but can't say I would return here.

“Isolated property, inconvenient location, average.” Situated just off i93 South, and adjacent to two massive car parks, this location is not pedestrian friendly. Rooms are on the small side, also, the location is under the flight path to Logan airport, so factor in noise. Speaking of noise, the A/C units are the old type units, wall mounted under the window and very loud. The Market Place cafe, is self described as a 'limited service dining experience'. It is very, very basic and frustratingly disorganized. On two occasions, the wait exceeded 15 minutes for basic coffee and cereal. Most of the food is pre-prepped and not that appealing. Gym is small, on the 2nd floor. Max weights are 30lbs, with 2 running machines. Overall, if the main City hotels are sold out, then this hotel is a distant option.

“Average Stay” The hotel is in downtown El Paso. The shuttle picked us up from the Amtrak station promptly. The room was clean and comfortable. One thing was that the toilet was hooked up to the hot water supply. So when you flushed the tank would fill with hot water. We were on the top floor of the hotel facing traffic and you could hear the traffic from our room. The person who checked us in was nice and the shuttle drivers were very nice. The evening desk clerk was not so friendly. I would stay here again. The elevators are slow.

“Pleasant surprise near Columbus” Stayed for two nights at the Staybridge Suites for a conference on the outskirts of Columbus. Overall, I was very impressed with the hotel and the services it offered. I had the one bed "suite" which was actually one big room. The room was very big and included a couch, small kitchen area, in addition to the bed. It was clean for the most part except for a couple stains on the carpet and a couple of hairs on the bathroom counter. The tv swivels between the sitting area and the bed, which is a nice touch, and it had a lot of channels. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom area offered plenty of room, which was appreciated. The location was great if you are going to the airport or to Easton, which is about 5 minutes away. The hotel offers a shuttle, which is good since fast food is the only option within walking distance. The hotel offered a variety of services for the longer stay. The breakfast, which was included, was good although it offered limited choices. The evening reception, with beer, wine, and a light dinner was excellent and greatly appreciated. Overall, I was impressed with my stay and would stay again.

“nice stay at the hilton garden inn chelsea” The room in HGI Chelsea was a good size, with a very comfortable king size bed, newish furniture with plenty of storage space and modern deco. My room was on the very top floor and the view is not fantastic, but the location is relatively quiet for Manhattan. Even though the street the hotel is on is not exactly pretty and kind of deserted at night, it's such a short walk from the subways that I felt safe walking back at night. I had a problem of the bath water running yellow, although not with the shower. The mini refrigerator was a little noisy so I turned it off at night. Other than that, the crisp linens, DirecTV, free Wi-Fi, the coffee machine, microwave, morning paper all added to a very nice and memorable stay. I would definitely recommend this hotel, and will consider returning to in the future.

“Not bad, but other places are just as good for price” My wife took me to NY for my birthday and we stayed here for the weekend. Not a bad place, but I have stayed in better for the whopping price she paid. The room was very small but decorated very nice and the bathroom was very nice as well. The hotel lobby is a very big focal point of the this hotel. You couldnt beat the location!! Its central to the entire city. I would recommend it, but seeing she paid almost the same price as the Waldorf, I would have opted for that place much more!! Try to get a cheaper deal at the Holiday Inn midtown if you can!
