“Better than expected!!!!” The Milburn Hotel does not seem to be a favorite of the local NYC TA experts. I booked it despite their suggestion to book elsewhere. I was extremely happy with my choice!! I had ,what they call a studio room-kingsize bed +small alcove with fridge,microwave and coffeepot. The price was $185 +tax. It faced asmall courtyard and so was very quiet. The room was a good size,furniture modern and bed comfy. The bathroom was tiny but the water pressure in the shower was super! Housekeeping was eager to be helpful. When I didn't want service one day they called to make sure I was OK and to ask if I needed anything. Coffee,tea and Famous Amos choc chip cookies were provided. The hotel doesn't have a restaurant on site ,but provides room service from the 24hr diner across the street. There are 3 computers you can use ,a small exercies room, and an arrangement with the community center down the street to use the pool. I love staying in a real neighborhood where you can make believe you actually live in NY and are not just visiting. I will definitely stay here again and will tell my friends about it as well.

“Great location!” The Bostonian was in an excellent location to see Fanueil Hall, Quincy Market, the North End, and the Freedom Trail. Our room was quiet and slightly smaller than what we're used to, but fit our needs fine. The lobby area was nice, and there was a wonderful bar and restaurant. We didn't eat at the restaurant due to budget constraints, but it is great to have that convenience if needed. McDonalds was on the corner, as well as the Union Oyster Co., and several other eateries/bars. The staff were very helpful. We did miss having an ice machine at our convenience and had to call and ask for it when desired. There was also a nice mini bar in the room, however, again not necessary as it was out of our budget. I would recommend for anyone desiring a convenient and comfortable hotel in downtown Boston.

“Very good experience” This is a seemingly brand new property located just minutes away from downtown Columbus, OSU, and the Arena District. The staff is friendly and helpful, and the rooms are spacious. The rooms were generally clean, however one pillow had a few small hairs on it. However, after tossing this pillow aside, there was nothing else wrong with the beds. The air conditioner was rather noisy, and took some getting used to when it came time to sleep. All things considered - a good stay. Nothing too special about this property, however there wasn't much to complain about either.

“More service; less buzz” Things I love about the Mercer: 1. The location -- right in the heart of Soho, with lots of restaurants and shopping right outside your door. 2. Service -- warm and very friendly, which shows that this hotel has settled into a comfortable, luxurious middle age. When the hotel was fairly new, I felt that the emphasis was on "cool" service, in all its various meanings. Now the staff rushes over with a smile. 3. The little luxuries -- an iPod player in your room, for example. Generous supplies of shampoo, etc. Plus a very comfortable bed and a wonderful shower. 4. An inviting lobby -- a comfortable place for breakfast or a drink. Pleasant alcove with a computer for checking your e-mail. Things you may not love about the Mercer: 1. The location -- you're right on a busy corner, with crowds outside day and night. The rooms are well soundproofed, but forget about opening your window (unless you have a courtyard room). 2. The rooms -- the epitome of industrial chic when they were first done. Now they just look industrial: long and narrow (like a galley kitchen) with white walls and venetian blinds on the windows. Maybe time for an update? (N.B. I had a standard room) 3. The shampoo, etc. -- the Mercer has been using the same brand for as long as I can remember. Time for a change? I'm sure I'll be back, though I wouldn't be disappointed to hear that they're making some changes around the edges.

“Perfect setting!” We stayed four nights at Humphrey's for the San Diego Rock & Roll marathon. We did not care for the first junior suite they gave us (too close to the restaurant dumpster and overlooking the parking lot), but they graciously upgraded us to a full suite at no additional charge. We had a beautiful room overlooking the marina. The bed and pillows were comfy and, of course, the grounds are beautiful, although it was a bit cold when we were there to really enjoy the pool. They even gave us late check out. And since I am such a slow runner that it took me past the noon check out time to even finish the race, it was a bonus to be able to come back and shower before our flight home. The only complaints I have are that, like others, I found the carpet to be very dirty. I didn't really see the dirt until I looked at the white slipper socks I had been wearing and they were almost black on the bottoms. I had to throw them away. The only other thing was that the walls were VERY thin. We could hear coughing and snoring. etc. from the room next door. This wouldn't have been as much of an issue if I didn't have to get up at 4:00 AM on Sunday. But I would absolutely recommend Humphrey's if you want a place to relax and get away from it all.

“Tripadvisor is right, Hotwire is wrong” I booked this hotel on Hotwire: a 3.5 star hotel near the airport for$75, and a "customer favorite". It is near the airport. It is a multi-building hotel, rather like those 1980s two-floor all-wood condos. I didn't hear any other-guest noise like the other reviewers, but I may have been just lucky. There is no elevator, not a big deal, but annoying. The room was OK -- usual Holiday Inn, always something broken, but not bad -- and the bed was very nice. The TV was in a hole in the wall way off to the side of the bed. OK, I know that's a whine, but it's really hard to see. Another whine from me is the parking lot: it is a strange labyrinth, with arrows pointing in weird ways and, I think, some blind alleys with no "legal" means of exit. I guess $75 is not too bad. But it is a 2.5 star hotel. I've reviewed it for Hotwire, and I hope their "customer favorite" gets erased.

“Delightful and deliciious!” I love this hotel. I stayed here for 2 days, and was totally spoiled by the fabulous room and the great staff. Amy checked us in and she made that a flawless pleasure. The room rocked: bed was killer, the bathrobe was so comfortable; I enjoyed the Bilss sink amenites, the Asian inspired shower and bath, and lovely lake view. I indulged in the BIlss spa which was great (as always) and highly recommend Gina and Serena for all spa needs (you girls rock!!). I had breakfast at Wave, which was pretty good-Phillip was the server and he's so great. I did prefer the room service menu as it has better food, more choices and the desserts rule (I recommend the brownie-it is so good). DIdn't go to the bar but checked out the pool and gym and both are pretty good. Everyone was helfpful, friendly and great, esp Christopher R. from Whatever/Whenever service (which we used a couple times)-this guy is the best! Angela is also great -they will go out of the way to make you happy. I can't wait to stay here again; this is my favorite hotel right now.

“Great Value on Union Square” Stayed for 4 nights in two rooms over Christmas. Worked out really well for us. The bed was super comfy. The shower had plenty of hot water. The room was quiet for us. The room isn't large but has a couple of chairs and a desk. Free wireless internet too. San Francisco is one of those cities were if you are spending lots of time in your room, you just ain't doing the city right. Our 3rd floor room faced Powell street which is where the cable car runs and they start at 6:30am. This didn't bother us but we also don't sleep late. I'm guessing if you are a light sleeper who wants to sleep in you should ask for a room either higher up or not facing Powell. BTW, our 19 year old teenagers had no problem sleeping late! (Based on my other reviews I seem to be a little more sensitive to noise than others.) The front desk was very helpful in recommending places to eat. Only complaint (and the GM seems to read these comments) -- more chocolate chip cookies and fewer cinnamon raisin! Wow, that should be the complaint about all hotels right? We rented a car for a few days to go north along the coast. We self-parked which is no big hassle -- just around the block. We really liked the hotel's restaurant for breakfast. We ate there two days and service was fast and friendly. My coffee was refilled so quickly one day that I lost track of how much I drank and spent the day wired! The "Sears Fine Food" place next door gets lots of hype and a line of people standing out in the COLD for maybe 30 minutes to get in. It was good but not that good. The french toast at Sears is in my opinion better but the eggs were better at the hotel. We took BART from the airport and walked up Powell to the hotel. That was exactly 1 hour from the domestic terminal to the hotel's door.

“Great choice near the lake” We spent two days on Lake Travis and stayed at this hotel for the night. We were celebrating our son's 17th birthday, so we had four teenage boys with us. The hotel was perfect for our needs: close to the lake, great pool and hot tub, clean, good beds, and free breakfast the next day. The desk staff was helpful, too. They suggested a pizza place that delivered and we ate pizza out by the pool. We would definately return!

“Well worth the confusing I-30 exit arrangement” I found the Hampton Inn Fort Worth to be above average during my stay; I would definitely stay at this property again. The mid-rise hotel with interior room entrances is located in a low-rise commercial area and was literally right off an I-30 exit ramp with easy access from the main road. A couple of notes on entering, exiting the hotel: A) the hotel exit off I-30 appears more like a service road with several other intersecting roadways between leaving the interstate and reaching the hotel, be aware, and B) exiting the hotel to the left from the front enterance was difficult during periods of heavy traffic, consider using the side enterance off Calmont Avenue and then making a left turn onto Green Oaks Road at the traffic signal to return to I-30. The area appeared to be generally safe, I had no concerns whatsoever. There is a Putt-putt course for the kids and a real municipal golf course for the grown-ups right across Calmont Ave from the hotel. The hotel has restaurants and convenience stores within the immediate driving area. There is an Applebee’s just across the interstate and to the east. Check-in was quick and the front desk staff was friendly and pleasant. The property is very new, not more than a couple of years old. The room was spotless upon entering. Décor was modern and the room items were in good condition. The bed was firm. The shower head was located high on the wall; hot water and water pressure were satisfactory. I did not have any safety concerns in the hotel or in my room. The room contained a coffee pot, flat screen TV, microwave, and refrigerator as well as the typical Hampton amenities. I did not have problems with noise from inside the room, neighboring rooms, or outside the hotel (i.e. I-30). The breakfast was included in the room price, offerings included a continental breakfast with cereals, pastries, eggs, etc.; the food overall was very good and was more than filling. Notably, the breakfast area hostess was the nicest and most welcoming I’ve ever encountered at a Hampton property, even bringing me refills of orange juice to my table which I’ve never seen before. I would definitely stay here during my next visit to Fort Worth.

“Very Nice Boutique Hotel” Close to everything within walking distance in the Gaslamp District and the convention center. Hip decor. Oustanding service! We stayed there in late December and they even had complimentary hot chocolate in the lobby in the morning. The restaurant was also great- too bad, no breakfast buffet.:-) Pet-friendly. I had problems with internet charges but they immediately resolved it.

“Excellent!!” Stayed there for 3 nights. Great hotel with a convenient location. Awesome views of TImes Square. Friendly staff. Rooms are generously sized, clean and updated. Two Starbucks onsite. Well equipped fitness facility - with a view of Times Square from the treadmills. Flawless billing and check-in.

“Well, They Tried . . .” This was the second time I'd stayed at the Radisson. My first trip is unmemorable to me now, but it must have been good enough that I decided to try it again. It's not a bad hotel by any means; rooms are very clean and generally comfortable, but on coming into the room, I noticed it was a little warm. I went over to the thermostat -- which was literally disattached from the wall -- and tried to cool things down from the 75 on the readout to a more comfortable 68 or so. The thermostat itself is very similar to the one in my home, so I knew how to adjust the settings, and no matter what I tried, there was no indication that it was working. I left for the evening, hoping it would have kicked in in the interim. When I returned, the room was still in the mid-70s, so I went down to the desk to request either a new room or a repair. After waiting in line (at 11:45 pm! The desk invariably had a line), the clerk assured me that they'd send a maintenance man up to look at it. I went back upstairs, and sure enough, within a few minutes, the maintenance guy appeared. I pointed out the unattached thermostat, which he re-screwed to the wall, then he climbed a ladder to look at the air conditioning's innards. After a few moments examination, he assured me it was broken (I had gotten that much myself) and that they would have to tear it apart to repair it right. He suggested I tell this to the desk and get a new room in the morning. Aftter he left, I did indeed to back to the desk (another line!) and was finally told by the same clerk that they were fully booked (given the crowds in the lobby at that time of night, I believed him), so the room-switch was out. He immediately asked what he could do as a make-good. I said I didn't know, so he offered me a free breakfast. Not a lot, but he was trying; I'll give him that. I went back up to the room, and while it was still about 73. it wasn't awful, and I was able to sleep soundly. The next morning, I told another desk clerk that I wouldn't be needing the breakfast, but that I hoped the room would be repaired. When I returned late that evening, the situation was the same, but again, not to the point where sleep was difficult. Other than that, I have few complaints. The shower is terrible, but I've come to expect that in hotels nowadays. The room was clean and generally well-maintained (air conditioning aside), and all things considered, I'd probably stay there again -- just wary.

“I quite enjoyed it...” Despite some shaky reviews here, I booked the Hollywood Roosevelt because I wanted something fun for a quick 1-night stay and didn't want to spend $400 on one of the 5-star hotels. It definitely served its purpose well. The location is excellent, though quite the mobbed tourist scene on a summer weekend (as expected). The lobby area might be dark, but it has been very attractively renovated and captures the older feel of the building with a contemporary twist. The service throughout was friendly enough, never rude or snobby, though not of Four Seasons caliber. My room was as expected --- small, rather dark, though clean and nicely renovated. The bathroom was absolutely tiny, which is often the case with hotels in older buildings, and water leaked from a gap between the glass partition at top of the tub and flooded the floor after a brief shower. I had plans all evening and wasn't around to spend time at the Tropicana bar, pool ,or restaurants, though they all looked like a lot of fun. The Roosevelt isn't the best hotel in L.A., but for the $179 I spent, I thought it represented a relatively good value compared to other options on the Westside. I'd definitely go back.

“Convenient and Comfortable” Stayed at the Wyndham for a long weekend while visiting SMU. The rooms are nice, large and appear to have been recently updated. My only complaint is that the comforters are too hot for the climate in Dallas, the bed would have been perfect with a lighter weight cover. The bathrooms are larger than those of other area hotels that I have stayed at and I loved the shower. They provide very nice toiletries. The room was clean but dusty, I know that this sounds like a contradiction but the bathroom was very clean while the furniture in the room had a coating of dust. The location is perfect for flying in and out of DAL and the shuttle service to and from the university was very convenient. I had considered staying at this hotel in the past but had found that their rates were higher plus they used to charge additional fees for parking and internet service and that had kept me away. They now have free parking and free high speed internet so I will consider this as my first choice for future trips.

“do not deserve the Hilton name” we stayed there from june22tojune30, 2011 the Front Desk's people are unpolite and rude, the room was small, noisy,and a non smoking room smelled cigarrette, the bathroom with the shower that did not have a regular hot water. The Hilton had to change a lot of things

“First Class Luxury” Spent 4 days at the renovated Jumeirah Essex House hotel in NYC. The location is as good as it gets with a suite overlooking Central Park. The room was spacious, bed comfy and service top notch. Midtown is a perfect location for taking in all of New York. You are close to the theater district and museums, and the park is across the street. It is not cheap, but it was less expensive than other hotels on Central Park South. The lobby and rooms still have the charm of 1931, but the flat screen TV's, fresh bathroom fixtures and luxurious linens remind you that you are in the 21st Century. I have stayed at other hotels on this street, and this was the best to date.

“Terrific Hotel” I don't normally stay at Hyatt Hotels but I have to say my experience at this hotel might make me reconsider that. The complex is very clean, well-maintained--it feels new. What's exceptional about this hotel is the professionalism and attentiveness of the staff. They are very accommodating. I called down for extra hangers and someone knocked at my door no less than 5 minutes later. The rooms have new interior design with clean, sleek lines. I was uber impressed with the fact they have IHome clock radios (the ones that allow you to dock and play your Ipod...love that). A nice stay. I would definitely stay here again.

“Nice size room” The room size was more than generous with very comfortable beds (with a very small but very clean bathroom). Having a variety of pillows to choose from was also a treat. The location of the hotel was great, close to just about everything. The bellmen were very accomodating and friendly. The cost of the room was resonable. Our room faced 7th Avenue and was considerably noisy at night, even with the window AC turned on. My two complaints with the hotel are (1) No free internet in the lobby. There is actually a $5.00 minumum for use of the computer. The printer was not working when I was there and I was not able to print out my boarding pass (therfore a waste of money), and (2) There was horrible odor when coming off the elevator or entering the hallway from our room on the 8th floor that resembled a musty/body odor that was very foul. I may consider this hotel again, predominanatly because of location and size of rooms.

“Amazing Hotel but even more Amazing Staff !” So first, this is the hotel I turn to when I need a great place to stay in the loop. Usually they have good food and a nice front desk staff, but on my recent visit it was even better. My wife and I had come in late from a meeting and Mr. Jason Jones at the front desk saw how tired we were and was super fast in getting us setup but beyond that was a kind and smart gentleman. He was just super fast and hard working that late at night. If you stay try the Chicken Soup , there is nothing like it anywhere.

“Very friendly staff, but I expected more from this Hilton” I booked this hotel due to the fact that if offered an airport shuttle. I had booked an overnight connection through SAN and needed a nice hotel by the airport for one night. When I called the hotel at 12:05 AM, for the shuttle, I was told that the shuttle ended at midnight. After a little hesitation, I was told that I should take a cab and that the hotel would pay for the cab, but I felt like this was all my fault for not know this..... I did take a cab and since I felt that I had been a bit abrasive with the front desk agent, I chose not to accept the offer for the cab fare. It was only $6.... The check in was quick and convenient. The room seemed nice, but pretty basic. the room was pretty large and had the basics in furnishings. My big surprise came in the morning when i woke up to a sink full of sludge. I was less than impressed with this as I was in a bit of hurry to get ready, have breakfast, and get to the airport. I chose to take a shower and just brush my teeth using the tub faucet. At some point during my shower, the watery sludge in the sink decided to begin draining. The problem is that it decided to drain all over the floor, leaving dried sandy sludge in the sink. Being in a slight bit of a hurry. I did not have time to deal with maintenance and all. I informed the front desk and then proceeded to the restaurant for breakfast. The staff was friendly. I had a continental breakfast coupon due to status, but chose to upgrade this to the full buffet. The buffet was average at best in comparison to other full service Hilton Hotels, however, the food they had was very good. I was not offered a menu, so I assume there was no menu / a la carte option. Check out was quick with no compensation offered, and the shuttle promptly took me to the airport. The pros of this hotel are its convenience to the airport and the friendliness of the staff. Also the view from my room was great. The cons are that the shuttle does not run for the last arriving flights, the rooms are average (kind of plain, though I like the colors.), and you might have a surprise in your sink in the morning.

“Marcel is a good NYC Option for liesure travel - Go with an open mind” My mom and I stayed at the Marcel two nights on November 5-6. The first night my mom and I arrived about 10:30p. We were greeted by a pleasant staff at the front desk and given a room with two double beds on the 2nd floor. As we get off the elevator, there is a weird smell. We find our room. The room is a modern decor and plenty of space - this is NY, the rooms are small here - expect it and if you get a big room then you will be all the more pleased. At any rate, as I am walking about the room, I hear a very loud noise coming from outside the window. I open the curtains and see nothing but metal and pipes - apparently it was the heating/air conditioning system consuming the entire view and making very loud noises. As I go to sit down on one of the beds, I am like Mom, does it smell funny in here? Yes, it does and I see an ash tray on the mini bar area. I call down to the front desk and say...is this a smoking room? Smoking is optional on the 2nd floor. Well this explains the awful smell on the 2nd floor. I ask for another room, I can't sleep in that odor. She says so sorry I have nothing else for you. Tomorrow you can move. I am frustrated and state that I can't sleep in this odor. She says the only thing I have is a room with a queen size bed. So my mom and I have no choice but to move to this room if we want to get any sleep (both from the odor and the mechanical noise outside our window). We are moved to the 6th floor. This is a small room with a queen size bed. The room faces the 24th street. Now for the good things... we slept just fine other than being snuggled up in a queen bed for two nights. I have stayed in other NYC hotels around town and found that this one was quite despite what a few others have said. The room was very clean and the location was good. We were able to walk up to Times Square and Chelsea easily and caught the subway to go other places around town without issue. There is a Starbucks a block away as well as drug store, restaurants, bakeries, and bars. Pretty much anything you could need is close by. We booked our room online for 241.00 per night which after much research I think is a very reasonable price for this hotel considering you are in NYC. My only complaint is the fact that they did not accommodate our room choice - two adults (and not a couple) were basically forced to sleep in a queen bed when we had requested two beds. I would stay here again but would stress my concerns about room preferences at time of reservation.

“Average Hotel.” I booked this hotel for two reasons, the brilliant reviews on TA and the fact it stated the rooms were extremely spacious. We found this hotel to be very ordinary and totally overpriced. However, we did notice that they offered a “free” evening buffet dinner and breakfast which was simple but adequate if one didn’t want to dine out. Location – In a acceptable location within a easy five minute walk into the city 16th Street Mall. The best located hotels are the Sheraton and the traditional Brown Palace Hotel. Check-in – No assistance with luggage and we were told to move our car before checking into our room. Room – We were disappointed as we thought it was supposed to be an apartment. Basically, our room 1932 consisted of a large room with a couch / bed / working desk with fully self contained kitchen attached with NO separate room division or doors.. The bathroom was clean and basic. Overall : We didn’t have a problem we just thought the hotel to be totally over rated and over priced. It would however suit many travellers who are looking for an “all in one package” with dinner and breakfast included. Sorry, but it just wasn’t for us.

“needs to be renovated” i lived in nyc for 10 years and recently moved but i still have business in nyc and travel back once a month. last week I stayed here for 3 nights - it is a company choosen hotel. it's a great location right next to grand central so it's perfect for my work or for tourists. i've stayed here 3 times this year - each time in a different room. this room was the worst of the bunch (I wasn't impressed with any room yet). all rooms that i've stayed in were older with a few cosmetic updates such as new bedding, a decent tv and a new sink. all rooms tend to be dark with poor lighting and uncomfrtable pillows in my opinion. last week i got stuck with room 2254. the room was basically the same as before with a decent view looking west. the room is older and had a musty smell. the carpet was OLD. it was held down, near the bathroom, with electrical tape. shocking, in my opinion. Not sure why they don't replace it instad of using tape to hold the frayed edges down. then the 1st morning I got a shower/ the shower is old & doesn't drain so i was stuck standing in dirty water. on my way out to meetings - i asked someone at the front desk to have the tub fixed and was assured that they would. the next morning - it was somewhat better but after 10 minutes the water filled up again. on top of that - the drain plug wasn't even attached to the tub but placed on the side of the tub. again, i asked for this to be fixed. the final morning - another shower, the plug still sitting on the side and the tub filled up yet again. i'm not sure how many times you have to ask for something to be fixed but for the price I (or my company) paid, once should have been enough. overall, i think the hotel is in need of serious renovation, not just a cosmetic one. next month when i am in town - i am staying at a different company preferred hotel. it just isn't worth the price to me.

“Ok, a bit strange though.” Great value and modern hotel. Not in walking distance to Austin though. Problem was it seemed to have a confused identity. I think it was trying to run with a far eastern theme but it was all a bit out of place. Reception were pretty awful, not interested in guests and generally half asleep.

“Private Funky Oasis” If you want something out of the ordinary, hip, with a touch of romance, then stay at The Royalton. The outside looks old and proper. However, going through the double doors transforms you to another world. The hotel's location is easy to navigate Manhattan and Grand Central subway station is an easy walk away. I personally loved the soaking tub, candles and THE BED. The only noise I experienced was in the morning when other guests were exiting their rooms and hearing their doors close. I stayed three nights in NYC and each night I stayed at a different hotel (I felt adventurous!). This hotel was booked through Priceline at $100/night and was my least expensive and most favorite. I look forward to coming back with my husband, even if I have to pay full price.
“great time!!!” Good old fashioned Colorado hospitality. Super friendly staff, esp in the Sports Bar. Clean, fun and comfortable, what a great time!!!! Great deal!

“Excellent service, great atmosphere” Traveled with our Bulldog for a total of 3 nights. Only down side was that it is about 4 blocks to Millennium Park to walk the dog, which sadly is a big down side for us. Looking past that, it was very,very nice. Stayed in a king bed suite, the second part of our stay the room was spectacular. Bedroom was off of living area, split by french doors, overlooking Washington and State streets. Hotel is very historic feeling, floors only have about a dozen rooms each. Bathroom was on smaller side, but that's to be expected. The front desk, doorman, and bellman were excellent and went above and beyond making us feel welcomed. Can't say enough on how great the service is here. I give it a 99.99999 out of 100, with only location for our dog, being the downside. Despite being in town for the NATO Summit, they made us feel safe.

“The View is About the Only thing Going for it” we'd read the reviews, and we learned that there had been major remodeling done to part of the hotel, so we asked to stay on that side. They wanted an additional $45 per night/per room (we had 2) so we decided not to. They wanted this extra fee Despite the fact that the weather was Cold and the hotel had very few guests. We should have demanded a free upgrade; the "old" rooms were terrible. Noisy, thin walls, Horrible Shower that leaked all over the floor > into the carpeting...(except 1/2 the water came out of the Tub Faucet and wouldn't get up to the Shower Faucet). Service: I called the front desk so many times I lost track! Asked for a hair dryer-Never got it. Asked for an iron (there was an ironing board) Never got it. Room Keys stopped working almost every day we were there, and had to have someone come and "re-set" them. Fuse Blew: twice. I sat in the dark till a maintenance man came. Housekeeping didn't show up to clean my room 'til 4:30 in the afternoon. They charge extra for everything; parking, shuttle, internet access, "fees" etc. The location is beautiful, but I've stayed in several places in San Diego and considering the cost, condition of the place and the poor service, there are many other places I'd recommend before sending friends here.

“A place to stay” Friendly and helpful staff. Older, tired property, but nt awful. Rooms were clean. Very busy and somewhat noisy. Close to mall and lots of shopping and food choices. Stayed here three times for business. Rates are okay. See other review for nearby option that is quite a bit nicer.

“This hotel is very comfortable and a great way to begin or end a flight at Logan” I have stayed here a few times over the last few months, either before a flight or after a flight from Europe. The hotel is located within the airport grounds and is easily reached by a free shuttle. The staff are very friendly and helpful. The hotel is very clean and each of my rooms has been very comfortable and well appointed. The windows appear to be soundproofed because you do not hear any of the planes. The included breakfast buffet is amazing, with a wide choice of both hot and cold foods, although it can get a bit crowded at peak times. I definitely recommend this hotel for anyone at the beginning or end of a journey at Logan. In particular, I definitely prefer it to the Logan Hilton (which is good, but not as good as the Embassy Suites). My only complaint (and this had nothing to do with the hotel) is that GPS may take you into East Boston to get there. You end up being on a street next to the hotel, but which cannot access the hotel. The hotel told me that this was a problem with a lot of GPS systems. Instead, head into Logan and follow the signs for the airport hotels.

“Definitely going back!” Finally! A great place to stay in Downtown Chicago that is affordable, clean, in a great location and with a superior staff! I couldn't believe the state rate was such a bargain, and even though the valet parking wasn't cheap, the service provided made it a good value. The front desk staff on check-in was exceptional. Very polite, professional and friendly. We asked for directions and recommendations several times for restaurants, the lakefront, museums, and a local bar - all of their assistance was spot on. The guys at the valet stand were so helpful. We decided to go around the corner to get a bite to eat and asked them to keep the car close by so that we could use it afterward. They made the arrangements and did it all without skipping a beat. Though I would allow 15-20 minutes lead time when you call for the car from the garage. As a Hilton Honors gold member, they upgraded me to a spacious suite with a king size bed in the bedroom, a full living room, and a kitchenette with a mini-fridge and microwave. The decor looked new and everything in the room worked great and was spotless. I loved the cabinetry they used (looked custom) and the granite countertops throughout. The breakfast service was one of the best I've had at a Hampton. Lots of choices, including different selections for fresh fruit, and good hot entrees. Plus it's located on the second floor with great views of the street below. They had breakfast attendants who were responsive and helpful. The doors to the rooms are not sound-proof however. But since I had a suite, the noise didn't make it through to the bedroom. All in all, one of the best Hamptons I have visited.

“Quiet” This is not the flashiest on the South Charlotte Residence Inns but it's the only one not located by a motorway. Which is why I like it most. It's a bit run.down but clean. Residence Inn red-standard, thougthful room design and well-equipped kitchen. In my first week they gave me first floor which was dark the whole day (lower than street level), smelly, the window did not open and around me where dogs in the rooms and the hall smelled of wet dog all the time. I came back only because of the quiteness and got 8th floor the second time which had windows that open, was clean, smelled fresh and nothing to complain. One of the few hotels I have been in the area where they are really keen and skilled to get my invoice address straight. Some days they have a problem with the internet for a day (seems to happen on Thur/Frid only but every Thu/Fri). The gym area I do not like, it's even further below the street, very lonely, only pool on the same level and I am a bit afraid to go there. Parking is not so plenty and the spaces are not big (and there are too many people not considering others and taking two spaces) but around the hotel are more spaces, at least in the evening.

“Awesome Accommodation” I stayed at the Mark Hopkins Hotel for 7 days last July and I had a wonderful time. The service was excellent, room service was great and the food was so good. My Mom always say "You get what you pay for." That's exactly what you'll get at Mark Hopkins. You pay a higher price for an excellent hotel stay. You will not be disappointed. In fact, I have made another reservation to stay at this hotel while I am in San Francisco for business. I don't think I can ever stay elsewhere. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Service was great, but room just ok” We stayed here for a night while visiting friends and family. The staff couldn't have been nicer- from the glass of limonada when we arrived to great directions on our way out to dinner and complimentary scones, fruit, and juice for breakfast. We really felt like we were at a small 5 star hotel! The room, though, wasn't up to par. It was really small- barely enough room for the bed, end table, desk, and tv/stand, and the furniture reminded me of the stuff we had in college. The mattress was flabby, sinking in the middle. The tv also had a big purple spot on the lower right screen. The bathroom pretty much matched the bedroom: there was some paint/baseboard issues, and there were no turkish bathrobes as the website advertised. Turndown service was a nice touch, though, and the pillows were really plushy. For us, the location, $8 parking, and service stood out above everything else, and if you're looking for some charm in Hollywood, this is the place to go.

“Great Choice when Flying Into or Out of Indy” I am giving this Hampton an excellent rating because of the staff, the facility, and the rooms. The staff were friendly and accomodating, facility is bright and cheerful and the rooms are clean and love the fresh duvets and sheets. I would stay here again, I have stayed at the HGI across the parking lot and the attitude of the staff isn't worth the hassle, and I will stay at the Hampton next time I'm in Indy.

“Outstanding” This is a great Ritz Carlton property. The room was great and the staff was outstanding. I arrived early and they ensured I had a place to work, charge my Blackberry, etc. Absolutely flawless delivery of service. The location is not the most convenient to downtown activities, but if the location is not an issue for you, this is the place to stay.

“Living in Luxury” We arrived at Trump Towers for a two night stay in an executive city suite. From the moment we arrived to the moment we left we received seamless excellent service. The room was beautiful, the whirlpool bath perfect after a long walk in Central Park. The location is perfect; within walking distance to a lot of exciting places. Whenever we called the front desk with a request it was handled in the shortest time I've ever experienced in a hotel. The rooms were nice sized, the ceilings high, and the walls well insulated. We felt at home, not like we were in a touristy hotel. (There is even a doorbell to the room.) The nightly turn down service with chocolates was great, as well as the ice bucket filled each night by staff. The bath products were top notch. Mr. Trump and his staff have an eye to detail and service. We were living in luxury.

“Fair hotel but great location” The only thing this hotel has going for it is the location to the National Mall and the Metro below the hotel. - The restaurants were fair (expensive) but expected since it is a hotel. - Rooms were very outdated and bathrooms were a bit scary. The last night we were here, there was a lot of police commotion going on, not sure what was going on there. The rooms are run down

“Clean - large rooms - comfortable beds.” Stayed here with wife and two boys. Rooms huge by new York standards - think of an embassy suites type room with upgraded finishes. Room had kitchenette with mini frig and microwave. Two TVs, two large closets, nice bathroom. View was of building next door. Smallish common areas include a nice computer lodge, nice but smallish lobby, and a breakfast room where the continental breakfast is served. Breakfast has cereals, yogurts, pastries. Great midtown location within short walk of lots of attractions. Subway station one block north. Get the one week metro pass and you can travel all over thes city for the cost of one round trio cab ride. Overall, a great base to explore and a good value compared to other NYC hotels.

“Superior service throughout the Hotel” Stayed in a Club Level Suite over the Easter weekend. Service was excellent from the moment we stepped out of the cab. Check-in was fast and efficient; warm towels at reception to refresh ourselves after the flight, little toys for our children, hot chocolate and cookies in the lobby. Thoughtful and welcoming. The suite was comfortable and spacious but not particularly remarkable. ALL of the Club Lounge staff were friendly,courteous and attentive and the food offerings were varied and delicious. This Hotel must be commended for its Staff, from the Greeters and the Bellmen, to the Club Lounge staff and Reception. All requests accommodated, "with pleasure". Travelling with young children is not always easy but if you can stay at a Hotel like this, dedicated to offering a high level of service to ALL of its guests, you can really relax and enjoy yourself...And we did! Terrific!

“Gutes Flughafenhotel zu vernünftigem Preis” Das Hotel befindet sich unmittelbar in Flughafennähe und ca. fuenf Minuten Fahrzeit vom DEN Rental Car Center entfernt, und ist umgeben von weiteren Hotels, die zur Marriot-Kette gehören. Leider gibt es kein kostenloses Frühstück und das macht es eigentlich uniteressanter im Gegensatz zum daneben befindlichen Fairfield Inn. Zimmer und Lobby sind sauber und gut eingerichtet und das Personal ist freundlich. Die Klimaanlage im Frühstücksraum ist wie so oft, zu kalt eingestellt, so dass ein längeres Verweilen dort nicht möglich ist. Für eine Nacht, vor oder nach einem Flug, bestens geeignet.
“比較的安価な高級ホテル” 金曜、土曜に宿泊したこともあり、比較的安価で、すぐれたサービスを楽しむことができました。無料の朝食はバラエティに富んでおり、部屋も十分な広さがあり、幹線道路沿いであるにも関わらず、敷地内の少し奥まったところにあるために、とても静かでした。はじめテレビの調子がやや悪かったのですが、迅速に対応してくださいました。機会があれば再び滞在したいと思います。

“Not the best” This hotel is not the best you can find. It is old and shows a lot of wear. We were there for the Houston Stockshow and Rodeo. It is real handy to Reliant Park. The price was higher than the value. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Pieces of the ceiling were flaking off and cracked. If it had been cheaper than it was, I probably wouldn't worry about it at all, but it was as expensive as a really nice hotel.

“Great Value, A little out of the way” The hotel was a little older, but still clean. They offer coffee and some pastries in the morning. Its about a 5 min walk to the bus which takes about 15 min to get into the city. I had a bicycle with me and made the bike ride from the hotel towards the city which took about 20 or so minutes. If you don't mind taking the bus into the city its a great hotel for the price, if you want to be right in the city I wouldn't stay here.

“Does not live up to hilton name - bad service” Typically, I think of hilton having good customer service. Not at this location. First off, I dropped my wife, kids, and luggage off at the front since I wanted to go park on my own and save $20 a night. (btw....if you park behind the hilton, it's $25 bucks a day versus $45 in the Hilton). I asked my wife to check in for us. She waited in line for 10 minutes, and then I received a call. She told me they would not check her in since it's under my name. I asked her to put them on the pnone, and she said they would not talk with me. 3 minutes later, I walked in and by then they had already moved on to the next customer. Of course, I was mad, but I figured I could handle waiting in line for a few minutes. Then, another line started to form as many people began to arrive at once. I realized we were all standing in the Hilton Honors line, and others were entering on the main line. So of course, the clerks started helping those people just arriving in the other line (not the Hilton honors line) before us! Why are there two lines and if so, shouldn't they be helping us in hilton honors line first regardless (i'm not sure most people noticed the difference in lines and no one was helping funnel traffic). So there were 3 desk clerks to help the 20 people in line. I thought they were short staffed for such a nice hotel. Of course, there were 7 bellmen waiting to grab our luggage! Maybe they should switch up their staffing and prioritze what guests really want? fast, speedy check ins after long drives in traffic. When I got to the clerk, I told her it was rediculous that my wife couldn't check us in? She never even asked for ID to see if the same address and last name? Also, I put a sign on some pizza boxes to throw away each day, and they never threw them away. the bar (not the irish place) has sllow service too! Overall, a nice looking hotel with horrible service.

“Good hotel and location” Stayed at this hotel for 5 nights on the last part of a trip to San Francisco, Las Vegas and LA. We arrived at about 4pm after a trip from LAX which cost $50 in a taxi on the way back to the airport we left in rush hour and the hotel provided us with a private car for $50 so we didn't have to rely on the taxi meter to get us there which was helpful. Staff were good and check in was smooth we were given a room on the 10th floor with a view of the pool and front street of the hotel. Rooms were a good size and clean as was the bathroom but furnishings could have been a bit newer except the tv it was a 37inch flat screen! Hotel was a lovely location in Beverly Hills with Rodeo drive a ten minute walk away. There is plenty to see and do around the hotel but I do recommend a car for LA as last year it was much easier to get around the city.

“Never Let Down at Four Seasons” It is a Four Season Hotel so the expectations are high, and once again this hotel didn't disappoint. The lobby is understated and classy, reeks of class and money, but at the same time is inviting. This is a rare combination that makes you feel immediately at home. The front check in staff is world class. I found them to be kind and caring and genuinely interested that I have a positive stay. The only way that I can put it is that seemed personally invested in my happiness and comfort. Great first impression. The rooms, though on the smaller side, are gorgeous. The design is elegant, not terribly modern but much like the living room of an extraordinarily rich aunt. Classic. The beds are simply divine and encourage loungy mornings after drinking too much wine at the Bristol Lounge. Though not the same since Aujourd Hui left, it is still in a prime location in Boston...near both the business centers of the city and (if you're a tourist) near the "sights" Highly recommended

“Great deal, location, and pool” Great hotel. If you are at the pool, you'll swear your in a 1960s hotel in Fort Lauderdale. Rooms were big and clean. Great location and close two multiple T stops. Friendly and helpful staff. I would definitely stay here again when in Boston.

“My new favorite hotel in NYC” Trendy, but unlike other trendy hotels in NY (Hudson, Paramount) where it's just smoke and mirrors, this hotel follows through. Rooms are modern and ultra comfortable. Service was wonderfully professional, yet friendly. Location across from Bryant Park an added bonus.

“True luxury on Fifth Avenue” A wonderful hotel; great service. It is located right on 5th Avenue a couple of blocks from Central Park. Fifth Avenue Shopping, the iconic Apple Store, Rockefeller Center and MOMA are all right there. The room design is unfortunate because although the room I got was luxurious and of a good size, it was divided inefficiently and felt smaller than it was. Very nice four-fixture bathroom with a separate shower in addition to a bathtub and high quality toiletries. Good efficient service from In-room dining, laundry, bell desk, concierge, front- desk and in the restaurant. The ancient enclosed television set in the bathtub was laughable, though! High speed wifi was free. No coffee maker, although tea/coffee from In-Room Dining was not prohibitely priced. The popular rooftop bar is always busy and has great views. Pre-Christmas decorations both outside and inside the hotel were very nice. True luxury.

“Beautiful Hotel, great staff, will stay again” Was here last week on business with a few colleagues. We needed a nice hotel close to downtown area. It was a bit pricey but we went on priceline website and got a better rate. We checked in early (which was very great) My standard Room was very large with a king bed. Bathroom was nice. (See attached photos of the room). It was chilly in Denver and there was snow on the ground when we arrived but it melted. Room heater was great. Bed was very comfortable and I appreciated all the nice firm pillows on the bed. The shower was too powerful even though you can adjust the type of water pressure as the regular pressure was too powerful. No conditioner in the bathroom. Please add conditioner to your amendities as this is important to a frequent business traveler. We ate at Randolph's restaurant downstairs and it was very good. Staff is WONDERFUL and friendly as well in the restaurant. They allowed us to sit in the restaurant in the afternoon to work on our presentations. Will stay here again!

“Great Roma, recently redecorated” Amazing, heavy hallway doors block any noise. Entire hotel has been recently redecorated, very pleasant. Granite counters in the bathrooms. Breakfast included was below average, butbtehvalue overall was very good.

“Great Hotel, Great Neighborhood” We have stayed twice at Lyden Gardens. We love the neighborhood and the roomy suites - a nice to place to relax in between NYC activities! Not the most luxurious of hotels, but a great value and wonderful location. Staff is very helpful with restaurant recommendations, arranging car service, etc. Will definitely go back.

“Much better than expected!! Great Hotel!” I was a bit concerned after reading some reviews and of the location, but to my surprise, it was a great 2 night experience!!! I would definitely stay here again!! Parking is secured and easy-even reserved spots for Priority Club Members-never have seen this before. The hotel is almost done with a renovation and it is very nice! The hotel is definitely an older property, but again, it is up to par with the "new" holiday inn look after this renovation. The rooms are large (except for bathroom) and spacious and come with all the modern Holiday Inn (IHG) amentities. Very Very Clean hotel!!! Great AC, very comfy beds, and VERY VERY good strong water pressure. The staff is very friendly and willing to help in any way they can. From the service stand point, it is that of a four star hotel. Finally, the breakfast buffet is better than average-a full buffet. If you are in the Valley, this is the perfect place as it is in the center of it all. Save your time from searching and stay here, even though it is a bit more than other properties in the area.

“Usual HGI quality in great area!” I frequently stay at Hilton Garden Inns when I travel, so when we were planning our New York vacation this year I was pleased to find the HGI in Tribeca offering a stupidly low price--$158/night, which is almost unheard of for ANY chain in New York. The location is fantastic, literally steps away from the A/C/E trains on Canal Street. We flew in through Newark and took the Airtrain into Penn Station, then hopped the A train down to the hotel (little trick since there's so many exits at Canal--look for the one marked Beach Street. Go up the stairs, hang a left once you're outside and there's the hotel). We got a nice view of the neighborhood from our fifth floor room--I suspect those are the HHonors rooms--and as per usual HGI operations the staff was pleasant and helpful. A special shout-out to Felipe, who helped out when I somehow screwed up the TV! Beds were comfortable, room was spotless and decent-sized by New York standards. If there was any nitpick it was the business center--there's two computers but only one is hooked up to the printer, and invariably said printer-compatible computer was being hogged by a teenager on Facebook. The staff will let you use their printer though, but still. If you want a little night life Bar Artisanal, attached to the hotel, seems to be a pretty popular spot. Tribeca isn't cheap foodwise, but you can always walk a few blocks to the Village for lots of cheap eats. Also check out Kitchenette, a funky little place on Chambers Street that serves great and (for the area) cheap breakfasts. I don't know if we'll ever luck out and get a rate this low again, but if you get the opportunity to stay here do so, it's a great hotel.

“Some one is joking” If you like the bottom of the Days Inn barrel or are satisified with uncomfortable beds and floors that look to grimey to walk on barefooted and showers with shower heads so clogged that the water trickles and very well worn 50's furniture and desk clerks with unintelligble accents than this is a place for you. Seedy is a kind word. Yes you are only feet from Hollywood Blvd and Kodak Center and The Star walk and Mann Chinese Theater and all the souvenier shops in LA but the street the hotel is on has numerous run down hotels that make you feel you want to be securely inside your room at sundown. Stay away. I have no idea what criteria the people that wrote 5 star reviews of this place use to judge hotels but they surely blew it on this one. I know I must surely have stayed in worse but I can't remember a place as worn out as this one andI am pretty sure they were less than single star bad dreams in scary parts of Europe. The room I had was a king for $99 .. a fair price would have been $39. don.brown@brownchild.com

“Service was outstanding...dont let decor get in the way.” Like everyone has posted, the physical structure and dated looks of the building inside and out is very obvious. That said, the staff was one of the most outstanding crew I have ever encountered in a hotel. Wonderful service all around. Super nice caring people...Four Seasons all the way. Very low key hotel. The outside pool and bar area is very nice. Great service here too. Check in and out was a breeze. Valet guys exceptional. Housekeeping fantastic, breakfast was excellent. The hotel is close to many things in downtown and wonderful hidden gems of the locals. The spa was booked but they sent me to the Hilton 2 blocks away and I had a great massage. The Hilton is gorgeous inside, brand new...I do not know if their service was as top notch as the Four Seasons but their Spa staff was great. Do not let the outdated looks of the hotel stop you from staying here. I am sure they will update soon. This was our first time in Houston and both my husband and I agreed that this city has the nicest people we have ever met. We will be back.

“Good size suite, but tired & outdated with lumpy sofabed” Really liked the staff at the Kimberly and was impressed with the room size, but couldn't escape the fact the the room was musty and in urgent need of updating. The sofabed my poor son had to sleep on was tough and lumpy, though our bed was beautifully soft! The bathroom was fine though and the roof top bar and deck were a bonus. The price for a 2 room suite is definately one of the cheapest in a central location, but ultimately, you get what you pay for; in this case, an old fashioned room.

“Stunning hotel, unfortunate experience” I am checking out of this hotel today, after arriving on Monday. The hotel is lovely and for the most part, so is the staff. The president of South Korea happened to be staying here on Monday. I was not aware of this at check-in. I went out to dinner with colleagues and when we returned at 9:45 p.m., we were not allowed to enter the hotel for at least 45 minutes while the president was arriving. This was disappointing to our group as we all had traveled from the east coast that morning. 9:45 PDT was 12:45 EDT. We got no apologies or any explanations from the hotel. Throughout the day on Tuesday, elevators were intermittently shut down while the president was moving around the hotel. We were even locked in a meeting room while the president moved through nearby hallways. I understand this is largely out of the hotel's control, but a note under the door explaining the circumstances would have been helpful. The fitness center is standard for a hotel, yet there was a $15 daily charge. Disappointing. A silly gripe, but there were no laundry bags in the room. I don't like to pack my sweaty gym clothes with my clean laundry, but that's my only option today. Not sure why this standard feature wouldn't be included here. I requested a 1pm checkout for today as I'm taking a red eye back to the east coast tonight (want to change into casual clothes after meetings end at noon) and was told this would not be permitted. One hour, after all of my inconveniences? The answer was no. After I again reiterated my inconveniences over the past few days, I was granted an extra hour. I'm soured on this hotel and while the property is beautiful, I won't recommend this hotel, nor will I stay here again.

“Overpriced” We stayed two nights here when we were stranded by Hurricane Sandy and it was the only hotel with availability. It was very expensive $990 for two nights! so our expectations were high! It started off well with a welcome cookie but the room was disappointing. It was small and though comfortable the bed was very high. It was clean and comfortable but for the price I expected a little bit more, we had to chase up the room maid for tea and coffee and there was no free wifi in the rooms. Wifi was available in the lobby which was very brightly lit but not very comfortable to sit in. The staff were very nice and friendly but there was just something missing, I would return but it would have to be at a much lower rate.

“Kitch, Glamour and Cheerfulness” The Hotel Helix is a fun place to stay at full price; however, if you can catch one of their special deals, this becomes a "must stay" location. The hotel is clearly in an older building which has been renovated. The furnishings are not high-end, but they make up for their price tags with fun, humor and kitsch. In the room itself, the bed, chairs, tables and lighting are ample and in good condition; however, the amenities are the stars of the show. The mini-bar was stocked with standbys like water, soda and alcohol, but there were also little surprises like pop rocks, wax lips and a tempting bar of high-end chocolate. The closet held not only extra pillows, but two plush animal-print robes for use or purchase, fuzzy slipper socks and an umbrella. The staff service was on par with a swanky five-star establishment. As I descended the steps to check out in the morning, one staff member cheerily helped with my luggage while another checked me out and a third hailed me a cab. Everything was quickly and easily taken care of. I had dinner in the lounge one night and there were several weekday specials. I was able to order a strong mixed drink and a burger with fries for around $10. The atmosphere was festive, but subdued enough that our group was able to converse easily. Our server was also unfailingly chipper and didn't seem to mind our talkative table, who lingered for hours after eating. The hotel is in an up-and-coming neighborhood which felt safe enough for a female traveler alone at night. The nearest Metro stop is a walkable distance. Nearby is a convenience store, a drugstore and a lovely Whole Foods grocery, not to mention various coffee shops, bars and casual restaurants.

“Nice location, decent service at this hotel” I seemed to run into quite a few issues on my business trip to NYC, two of them relating to the hotel. However, Kimpton hotels are known for their friendly service, and this hotel is no exception. I just wish that I wouldn't have had the problems in the first place! First, my co-worker and I arrived at the hotel and they had lost her reservation. She had a confirmation number and everything, but there was nothing they could do because the hotel was at 100% occupancy that night. She ended up staying on the pull-out sofa in my room, and the hotel generously waived the charge for that night. Second, my office shipped several boxes for an event that we were holding on the hotel's terrace, and one of our boxes was lost. It was a huge ordeal to prove to the hotel that we had shipped to the correct location, they signed for the package, and then it was misplaced. It was a big waste of time, but they ended up replacing what we lost in the box. On to the other aspects of the hotel: -The rooms are lovely and the bathrooms are very spacious. The quality of their bath products was appreciated. -If you sign up to be a Kimpton member, you can receive free wifi and $10 free to the mini bar -The downstairs restaurant had a fun wine sampling bar - pay by the ounce instead of glass -Room service was very slow

“Lots of Room - Loved it!” We stayed at the Affinia 50 on April 13 - 15, 2007. We booked the Amercian Girl Package. Originally we reserved a Studio, but were pleasantly surprised when they upgraded us at no extra charge to a Jr. Suite. I have stayed in NYC a lot for business and usually stay at the Crowne Plaza in Times Square, but this time we had two children along and couldn't have been happier with the room and hotel. We had a living area w/pull-out, two large, comfortable beds, a full kitchen (bring utensils if you plan to use) and bathroom. There was plenty of storage and the pillow menu was great. The pillow that plugs into an IPOD was a big hit with my 10 year old. The Club Floor was spacious and bright and the free coffee was good. The location was super. The diner up on 50th and 3rd, Morning Star Cafe had good breakfast at reasonable prices. Only Negatives - the safe in our room didn't work, but we did not call about it. The bathrobe was missing upon check-in, but the front desk brought a new unopened one to us when we called. The temperature control wasn't the best. Tried to run just the fan for outside noise reduction, but it poured out heat no matter how it was set. We were on the 8th floor facing 50th - so we had some street noise. It wasn't excessive though - we live in the mountains with NO noise - so we notice any noise. All and all - loved the place - and will go back ! BTW - if you are a baseball fan - try the Yankee Stadium Tour (when there isn't a game) for a reasonable, memorable tour. If you plan to go to Liberty Park - plan ahead - they give out a limited number of passes online and the day of - to get "inside" the Statue of Liberty. We missed out on this, but walked around the outside and got fabulous pictures. If you have kids -try Ruby Foos (Pan-Asian) on 49th and Broadway - good food, loud, and roomy - has a kid's menu too.

“Donatello Hotel” This hotel is a bargain. I would definitelygo back. The staff, decor, amenities, room, cleanliness and facities were on par with any of the 4-5 star hotels I have stayed in on many trips to this city. The location is near Union Square.

“Nice hotel, great service” The location of the Ritz-Carlton Chicago is really terrific, near great shopping and restaurants, it is perfect for vacation or business travel. The rooms at the hotel are very nicely appointed, but the rooms on some sides can be louder than others. When the wind was high my room would creak a bit, but not as bad as some others who were attending the same event, some of whom had windows blow open or had loud wind or street noise. Chicago is a typical big city with city noise, so if you are sensitive ask for a room on a higher floor. The service at the hotel was great, just what you would expect from a Ritz-Carlton/Four Seasons location. I was attending a conference, and without fail the service and food were both excellent. If you want a reasonably priced meal or bottle of water, there is a mall in the lower levels of the building that offers a food court with several quick service options. There also is a Starbucks and drug store within a very short walking distance.

“Line & Lariat Restaurant at Hotel Icon” I wasn't able to find a listing for this restaurant so decided to post here. I highly recommend this location for an excellent fine dining experience! Both the service and food were top notch! Menu had good variety in main course (steaks, seafood, and other rarer meats like boar and venison) and mixed drink menu was amazing! For appetizer I had crab cake, and for main meal I had the Filet Mignon (perfectly cooked), with melt in your mouth mashed potatoes and sweet carmelized carrots. Then for dessert, I had the flour less chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream. The restaurant is in the lobby area and has amazing trendy and modern Texas decor (cow stools, Texas state flag upholstery, but also grand pillars and large chandeliers). I would recommend this hotel's restaurant for a romantic meal or a classy business-entertaining venue!

“Best place to stay in San Francisco!” If you are going to San Francisco for vacation, this is the place to stay. For the price (paid $600 for 4 nights) and location, not to mention FREE PARKING, it's a no brainer. The staff were very helpful (fixed our broken desk lamp as soon as it was reported). The room was a bit small but still contained a semi walk in closet and a good sized bathroom. The room was clean and semi secured since you needed your room key to access the elevator. The location is IDEAL. Pier 39 / Alcatraz ferries were about a block away and the wharf area (Embarcadero) was a half block walk from the hotel. 7-11 is right across the street and IHOP is one block down. There are many places to eat within close proximity of the hotel. The cable car turnarounds are also close by (Mason / Powell about three blocks away, Mason / Hyde about five blocks away). Lombard Street, Coit Tower, and Ghirardelli Square are also within a mile or so distance from the hotel.

“Great service, but suites really need update” The service is wonderful. Everyone whom I encountered here was incredibly helpful. The location is good; residential area with free parking in a deck, and close to a lot of attractions. Kitchen has oven, fridge, coffee maker, toaster, microwave, and utensils incl. glasses, some plates, coffee mugs. You can ask for additional utensils or pots to cook. I like that it seemed like an apartment (which indeed it originally was). I liked the shampoo and soap amenities too. Shower head gave a great flow of water. Nice flat-screen tvs. Coffee replenished daily. I am sure it was beautiful when it was new, but the suites really need some updating. We had a suite on the 11th floor which needs new carpet, new paint in a color other than taupe, replace the old metal switchplates (one had a missing screw and there was tissue stuffed in the hole!) and some new furniture. Kitchen cabinets could use refurbishment too or a good wipe-down. Carpet in kitchen was stained and gross—why is there tan carpet in the kitchen? A down comforter on the bed would be much better than the sheet and blanket provided which are just not enough when it is seven degrees outside. The suites could be really beautiful and it would be a perfect place to stay if renovated and updated; it would then easily deserve 4 or 5 stars. But as it is right now, even 3 is generous. If I did recommend it to anyone, it would be with the awareness of the above. Since so many people have said the same thing on this and other review boards, I hope the hotel management takes this seriously and will take some action and update the place.

“Better for baseball fans than for business trips” If you're in San Diego to see the Padres, this Marriott is where you want to stay. If you're here for a convention at the convention center, it's a short and pleasant walk. Beyond that, the hotel has its good and bad points. First, the good points: this hotel is at the edge of the Gaslamp district. There are endless restaurants, bars, shopping, or whatever touristy diversion you could want. Second, there's Colleen (hope I remember that right) at the front desk. If you have a problem, she'll fix it. It's also a very quiet hotel unless you have noisy neighbors like I did on 1 of 3 nights. Unlike the Hyatt, you'll never hear the trolley because it doesn't run next to the hotel and that's a good thing unless you plan on using it. There's a coffee maker, a hair dryer, and all of the usual toiletries. Hot water came up pretty fast except on the day when I got up at 4AM to catch an early flight. Then it took a few minutes for the shower to get up to temperature. Not everything was perfect and I found more problems than I would have expected in a hotel that's so highly rated here. First, realize that all of the hotel's rooms were not created equal. The first room they gave me was on the 9th floor. It looked like a basement apartment because the windows started halfway up the wall, and the glass was frosted so you couldn't see out of the room. Fortunately the windows opened far enough for me to see what they were hiding and it was a roof with some kind of equipment on it. Maybe they weren't noisy air conditioning compressors that I saw, but I didn't want to find out. I went back to the lobby and got switched to room 1701 with a view of Petco park that was just like the ones in the traveler photos here. Another problem is that you can't get to your room without using your key card in the elevator to allow access to the guest floors. It's a nice security feature but when you get into the elevator with both hands full of luggage, it's a bit silly. There's a bar on the roof that's open to the public and at night they block off one of the four elevators for roof access only. There's always a crowd in the way, the three other elevators become busier and slower than ever, etc. And this is when it's not baseball season. The roof bar looks down on the stadium so during a game this elevator situation can't be fun for guests in the lobby. I think the roof bar is probably a good reason to avoid staying on the top floor, but that's just a guess. Finally there's the high speed internet access. First you have to call downstairs. Then you have to tell them if you want wireless or an ethernet connection. After you say "Wireless", they tell you that you'll need to give your credit card number to some company that you've never heard of. And if you want to use a cable to connect, the charge can go on your bill. Once you try to use it, you go through a screen that basically says "Your only choice is 24 hours of broadband. What would you like to choose?" You have to do this every 24 hours or you can skip a day if you'd like. Upon checkout you'll discover that after you pick the 24 hour "option", you get billed for this automatically every day until you check out. One good thing is that along with the internet, you also get free domestic calls, local or long distance. I'm not sure how much people actually use the phone in their room for long distance calls, but it seems like a reasonable way to call home once you realize it's free. The system doesn't seem to be well thought out. I think they'd make more money if the rooms were $3/night more and there was free wifi, but I'm not in the hotel business. I just stay in hotels. Overall, I had a good time at the Marriott. It wasn't as nice of a hotel at the Hyatt and there were ar too many small problems, but this would be my number one pick if I was in town to see the Padres.

“Convenient and clean” Although I work in NYC, my wife and I attended a wine dinner and I didn't want to drive home. The hotel was within walking distance of the restuarant, so it was perfect. The check-in process was quick, but the elevators slow (although they say they are working on upgrading them). The room was spacious and included a small, full-service kitchen (wonder if this was an apartment building in a past life?). My biggest peeve was that I took a bottle of Sierra Nevava from the fridge and found it stale. I then noticed that it was a screw off top, which Sierra hasn't made in years. Altohugh they said they would remove it, that fact that they would put this out is embarrassing. Either it has been laying around for years or their supplier is swindling them. Either way its not good. I would however stay here again.

“It was a Super 8 and it still feels like one” It recently changed ownership and went from Super 8 to Ramada. It's a blight on the Ramada chain. What made me the most upset is that the picture they show makes it look like a nice hotel from the front. They have the word "HOTEL" really big on top. What they don't show is that the majority of the rooms are MOTEL style and not hotel. We were in the way back in a building on a slope. Second floor with no elevator and many steps. No offer to help with luggage. No offer to help with anything, really. It looked like they slapped a coat of paint on it and maybe bought new (very hard) beds. The blanket (inadequate) was stained. The windows don't have screens so I wasn't comfortable opening it to air out the room. The ice machine, as listed on their ammenities flyer, was not to be found at all in my group of buildings and you had to walk down a sloping parking lot to the main building. The fitness room had 5 machines and the bike didn't work. They advertise a shuttle service but never mentioned one and when I asked, they said to get downtown was by taxi or local bus. There's a nice espresso bar/cafe across the street but when I asked about any local restaurants they said the only thing is their own restaurant yet their website lists over a dozen restaurants. It was very misleading and since I didn't have a car, I was stuck there after returning from my business downtown. My advise is to stay away unless you want to stay at a newly painted Super 8 Motel.

“Good Choice” Recently stayed four nights at the New York Palace. Location is faultless. Check in was quick and efficient although charmless. Receptionists face might have cracked if she'd smiled! Was given a room with the iconic view over St. Patrick's Cathedral so all was forgiven! Room was palatial and very comfortable. Exceptional beds with premium linens and plenty of closet space, large flat screen TV and good quality toiletries in the bathroom. Bathroom was not as palatial or luxurious as room which was a little disappointing but it all worked very well and nothing was lacking, plenty of towels too, if a little thin. They don't seem too bothered by the environment here though as they changed towels (and bedding) every day whether needed or not. Turn down service was very professional. Avoided breakfasts having read previous reviews but the astronomical cost was off putting anyway. This seemed not a problem to a lot of people as there were lengthy queues for breakfast each morning. We used the numerous delis surrounding the hotel to get a take away breakfast to eat in the room - sounds tacky but we were by no means not alone in doing this either! Public space is limited and rather gloomy being in the original mansion but still very impressive. It frequently got very crowded and uncomfortable. We had dinner in Gilt, the hotel's 'signature' restaurant also located in the mansion part of the hotel. There were seven of us and the service was attentive, presentation very good and there was an astronomical bill at the end and I thought quite frankly not worth it. However, enjoyed the stay and would recommend without hesitation.

“Hit all the right notes!” My young adult daughter and I just returned from our latest NYC trip where we stayed here. We try to go at least once a year for a weekend, and squeeze in as many shows as we can, so I look for something affordable, and in the Times Square area, so we can easily walk to shows. The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square was perfect! We arrived earlier than stated check in time after a long and crowded bus ride, and were allowed to check in early. We also received a goody bag with some nice surprises. I reserved a King corner room, and it was nice and spacious, with a cute futon style sofa/sofabed. We really appreciated having the microwave and mini fridge. We were not more than a quick walk to all our shows, and I walk slowly! Loads of delis around to grab a bite to eat, and I really like picking up some things at the Food Emporium grocery store, the prices are high there though! My daughter usually has no opinion on where we stay, as long as it's clean. We have stayed at classes of hotels ranging from The Hotel at Times Square to the Sofitel. She has said that the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square is her favorite of all of them. Hope to bring my mother back one day for her first trip to NYC (had the trip already planned and paid for several years ago, and she had a heart attack a month before and couldn't go), and she is already looking forward to her stay here. Thank you all for a wonderful trip!

“Almost like a home away from home” This is my fifth visit to this great gem of a hotel in downtown NYC. I just love the hotel and the location. This time, my wife and I were here with our college daughter and two of her friends. We had two rooms. They made arrangements to set the two rooms up with a foyer between the two. Very nice arrangement for our situation and one that was much nicer than my expectations. Even the smaller of our two rooms was quite spacious and our suite was like a small home in Manhattan. Kyle took great care of us when we checked in and came up with us to our room to make sure we knew how everything worked. The breakfasts there are especially delightful and amongst the best we have had at any hotel. My daughter rates it #1 anywhere. Finally, it's nice being in a quieter part of Manhattan during this very busy time. You can "parachute" into the midtown area and come back to your hotel with a 15 minute Subway ride. Very nice indeed.

“Good Value” I have been going to Indianapolis for NASCAR races since 1996 and have stayed at many, many hotels, most of them not very rememberable. I chose to stay in a different part of the city this time, and what a difference. I stayed in every hotel on the east side of indianapolis. Going to the southern part of town proved a smart move. This red roof inn was older, but the staff was excellent and the neighborhood, while it being in a commerical district, was very quiet. This is a perfect place to stay if you need to get a good nights sleep in a convenient location.
