“clean, basic accomodation w/microwave & fridge” best western diamond elite member; paid $64+tax in december-2011 which is good rate for value received; appreciate upgrade to family suite with kitchen with utensils and separate bedroom and living room; ralphs and vons grocery stores, walgreens,, cvs near by; some restaurants near by but did not try them clean, comfortable basic accommodation; chose for high traveladvisor rating and not disappointed except for minor irritants as detailed below; helpful, courteous staff; older property but well maintained; nice firm comfortable beds; plenty of clean towels bulbs above sink outside bathroom burnt out but not replaced for two days despite request; at arrival, room very clean but housekeeping didn't clean interior of microwave where previous guest left spilled coffee & half full coffee cup but i didn't report instead cleaned myself; flat screen tv in bedroom goes blank for 30 seconds each time channel changed [most annoying] so instead watched CRT tv in living room; stayed 3 nights but housekeeping never left fresh paper coffee mugs or condiments packet until i left note asking for them; very clean room and well maintained property; realize breakfast under reconstruction but general quality & variety of breakfast items poorer than comparable hotels; provided soap, shampoo and lotion but no conditioner would definitely stay here again & would recommend to others

“Clean, relaxing, ideal location” Friendly staff, clean, spacious rooms. A stones throwaway from beale street. Perfect in every way apart from a few of the locals who tend to spot tourists and rudely beg for money when they clearly have plenty/money for themselves, be on the whereabouts (although the police presence at the weekends in the evenings is relieving).

“Marvellous” The Westin Philadelphia was wonderful, the staff were over and above the usual, the hotel is truly stunning, and room was slightly bigger than the usual, room service was great but it was the staff that really made us so welcome. On the second day we went to give our concerige a tip and discovered to our horror we had no smaller notes, we apologised and said we will catch you later, the staff were "no problems" don't worry you tipped yesterday etc., and it was geninue. A truly wonderful stay, wish we could have stayed longer!

“Great Addition to the Chicago High-End Hotel Portfolio” The Elysian is all that it is cracked up to be. Great service, great location, great decor, great rooms, great beds. Chicago has some great boutique hotels and the Elysian is another on the list (probably the best on the list). The rooms are exquisite -- fireplace, luxurious bathroom (with tv in the mirror), separate shower and tub, elaborate tile work. Had drinks at the bar which is small but quaint. I was looking for a particular type of scotch (oban) which was not displayed. I asked the waiter if that was everything they had. He asked what I wanted. I told him, and he said they'd get it. I don't know where they went, but about five minutes later, a staff member walked in with a brand new bottle of Oban. That's great service. And though it's expensive, it was completely in line with any other bar of that caliber ($15 for scotch, $10 for cocktails). The technology in the room is great. Free wireless throughout the hotel. We only hit the gym (which was nice) but the Spa is apparently very happening. Didn't eat at any of the restaurants this time though Ria gets two Michelin stars so must be outstanding. Will definitely return.

“Loved It” Awesome Big Rooms, Luxury and comfort, Great Staff. Went for a business trip , they do have large conference rooms, no pool but a indoor ice rink . Hotel was not really located in an area where i could shop, but it was a very nice hotel. Great Cusine food!

“Nice, elegant hotel” We booked this room via P-line just one day before arriving for a short get-away night in the City. Location is at the tippy top of Nob Hll, which means a serious downhill walk to Union Square or China Town (or anywhere) and an even more serious walk back up the hill. However, the rooms have great views. Our 6th floor room had a comfortable feather top bed, large bathroom, nice TV, desk, etc. Internet is $12.00 per day (c'mon!) The staff was friendly. Room very clean. You can open the windows about 6 inches to let in wonderful fresh air. If you sleep with them open, be ready for the sound of the city, which in San Francisco means at least two sirens per hour...all night. I could also hear the taxi whistle of the busman late into the night and first thing in the morning. The taxi whistle isn't so bad, but the sirens will wake even the most heavy sleeper. The room has a coffee maker, but there is also free coffee near the elevator in the lobby if you get up early enough. The bathroom is large, and has a tub for one. There is a lack of counter space, which is surprising because you can almost fit another bed in the bathroom with the extra space. A small table in the bathroom would be helpful and keep you from having to place your "stuff" on the floor. The bar at the top of the hill is an "experience." 100 different types of martini's all priced at $12.00. A beer is $6.00. Service is excellent and the view breathtaking. We arrived at 9:30 and there was a 15 minute wait. We were seated next to a window and had a drink. Thirty minutes later the wait was over 45 minutes. Parking anywhere in the City is pricey. We looked for spots on the street and found one just across from the hotel, but beware of when the streets are cleaned. Like most times using P-line, I was very happy with the hotel. At full price, which was quoted at $189.00 before taxes/fees, it is still a very nice place to stay.

“Well it seems like it almost has it together” We had a room booked at the Intercontenial down the street but switched since this had such high ratings on Tripadvisor. We stayed two nights Friday the 10th to the 12th, when we checked in the lobby was nice. I was using my points from Priority Club, I am at the Plat level, the girl checking us in wasnt that cheerful until she saw my profile on the reservation then changed her greating after that. We we given room #315 which is a corner two room suite. When we get to the room the first thing I always do it turn down the A/C. My wife and I leave to go to an Astros game come back and get to the room and it is still not cold. Mind you that there are two ac units in the room. Well the thermostat thats on the wall still shows 76 in both rooms. I make sure to turn it on again, still an hour and a half later is still 75 on the wall, my clock I have shows 79 this is at 1 am at this point. We call and see if there is a fan, they say no they can switch us rooms. So we did at 2 am switch rooms, at this point I didnt even want a suite so we just got a reg room which turned out to be fine. I did notice in the rooms, the tile grout needs to be re-done, the showers dont drain good. But the setup of the rooms are nice, nice bedding, nice work area, nice to have a wet bar, the rooms are quite I didnt even hear people in the hall. The rooms are very bright they do not have darking curtins, even in the suites there are windows with no shades on them at all. We ate dinner one night there and the flat bread pizza is very good.

“Clean Hotel w/Friendly Staff in an OK Location” We stayed here on a business trip and found the room to be clean, modernly decorated, and in a decent location close to little Italy (about 2 blocks away) and 10 minute drive from Gaslamp Quarter. For a Doubletree, we were expecting a little bit more, but there was nothing really special about it. We were surprised that the TV was a 27" tube TV. The front desk staff was friendly and courteous; they provided good recommendations of places to eat and things to do. They also provided us with their heavenly signature chocolate cookies, the best ever! Self parking ran $20 which I think is a bit much for doing it yourself, but looking at other hotels close by, this was about the average running price. You definitely need a car to explore some of the highlights of San Diego which is why I would recommend a hotel closer to the desired attraction.

“Outdated rooms, but good location” Hotel Front desk competency is excellent and friendly. Lobby is fine. Breakfast is excellent, although the 7:30 am start on the weekends is late for people that need to get going. Rooms were outdated and average in cleanliness. Beds were VERY comfortable. Room was very big. Sign on mirror and key card envelope said we had to request "light cleaning service" on weekends, so we did and the front desk said, yes, no problem. So our beds were made and bath towels were replaced, but not washcloths and not shampoo. Not earth shattering, but annoying. Room has kitchenette and refrigerator. Location is about 2 blocks from Alamo, Riverwalk and across the parking lot from the Alamodome. Fitness room was fine, but tv was very small. Nice perk if you're staying a few days is that guest laundry room is free.

“Okay for the price” The comfortable bed and hot shower were the highlights of our room, which was extremely small. The front desk staff are like robots. When checking in, there was a line so I was able to observe the bored, canned responses that they continued to give with no sincerity. Whatever, you're not coming to Chicago to spend time at the front desk. The hotel was clean and quiet, and the bartenders in the lounge were very nice. There is a convenient store across the street and you can get your morning coffee at the 24 hour Dunkin Doughnuts, also across the street. Overall, not bad but nothing great.

“What a surprise. Nice stay.” A pet goldifsh in your room? A shih tzu in the lobby to greet you? Free overnight shoe shine? Choice of four bubble baths (for a paltry $40)? Both nightwear (yes, several sizes) and robes available for you to purchase right from the closet? Vegetable soap bars? Did I just overshoot Denver and end up in San Francisco? It's a really ritzy little boutique hotel called the Hotel Monaco in Downtown Denver. One block from the 16th Street Mall, the Monaco surprised me with both opulence and gimmickry. The rooms are nice... tall ceilings and appointed well, despite their compact size. The hotel is an older one, meaning that most of the rooms have a great view of a wall or a parking garage. Just leave the blinds drawn and enjoy the comfort. There is a great bed... lots of pillows for your selection... some really expensive stuff in the frig and on the snack tray. (Walgreens is two blocks away and has all that stuff at a fraction of the cost.) And the people are kind and accommodating. What really blew me away was when I dined in their Italian restaurant downstairs. The place is called Panzano and features the creations of Chef Elise Wiggins. I had the most wonderful veal of my life. I proposed to the chef, but I didn't have a ring on me at the time, and she wanted one really badly. Thanks for great food in a very attentive atmosphere, Elise. Pricey? What isn't in the downtown of a major city? But yes, it was a little more than I would have liked to have afforded, but there were few choices because of some convention in town that week. I did not find a problem with noise in the hotel, though they do have a funny way of putting ice machines on only the odd-numbered floors.

“Great property, service and location in Washington DC” This is a great hotel to stay at for business or pleasure while in Washington DC. The property is an older building converted to hotel many years ago. Rooms are unusually large and this is one of very few central DC hotels with outside pool. I had only one request - quiet room - and they put me on back side on 9th floor and my room was very quiet. This is good location, lots of shops and restaurants within easy walk and about three easy blocks to DC Metro system. Staff friendly and helpful and my request for late checkout was accommodated. The M-F managers wine tasting is nice touch.

“Good hotel, difficult to find” Hard not be jaundiced by the difficulty of finding this place. If you reserve online and click on the link in the confirmation e-mail, you are taken to someplace completely different than where the hotel is actually located. When I called to get directions from the incorrect location, I was put on hold for several minutes while I stewed in a gas station. Eventually, I made the desk clerk guide me to one of the several bits of S. 48th Street in the area. Once there, the people were very nice. The bartender lent me her bottle opener so I could open the beer I had in my room. The hotel is clean and bright. The room was good-sized and had pillows labeled as firm or soft. The firm pillows were very firm. The bed was reasonably comfortable. The only real problem was the noise, and not from airplanes. This is one of those hotels where the doors slam closed unless you're careful. This woke both my daughter and me on several occasions. Also, while it's nice to have microwaves in the room, they are perhaps the loudest, beepingest microwaves I've seen. You can easily hear them in the next room. The hotel has a small fitness center that I saw other guests using. If you know where you're going it's very convenient to the airport, so I would certainly stay here again if I needed that kind of accommodations.

“Very Nice Hotel” I stayed at this hotel on the way home from Disney. I found it to be a very nice, clean hotel. The beds were comfy and everything was very modern. The hotel had free wireless internet, an in room refridgerator, and many nice features. The handle to the bathroom door was loose and that would be my only complaint (and really thats just being knit picky)

“Decent location, poor service” Stayed one night at the Doubletree in Boston. The location is central and perfect. Those who say it is shady or dangerous have not been to many shady or dangerous places. It's right near the Theater District, Chinatown and New England Medical Center. The parking there is ridiculous, $35 a day as I recall, so park in any one of the 100 garages nearby. I paid extra for a high room, and took the free upgrade for the larger room with a city view from the website as a Gold member. My room was small, with a tube TV, No welcome to the hotel. No recognition of Hilton Honors status. I would say this was an average hotel, but not for what's supposed to be a full-service property. The guy even forgot to give me my cookie. I should have known from reading the reviews here. Boston is a great place. This hotel not so much.

“泥棒がいます” 残念ながら絶対にオススメできません。事実なので堂々と以下に真実の有様をそのまま書きます。 スイートに泊まりましたが、初日に荷物を荒らされた形跡があり、おかしいなと思っていましたが、結局いくつかのもの(金額的にはたいしたことないですが・・・)がなくなり、また機内用のBOSEヘッドフォン(QC3)を壊されました。QC3は物色された際に、ケースに上下反対に無理矢理詰め込まれたための破損です。 ちなみにホテルにクレームを入れたら、丁寧に入れたのですが謝罪もなく、マネージャーは話をしたいから部屋にくる許可を聞いてきたと思ったら、30分待たせたあげくに複数の警備員を連れて、はじめから「飛行機で来たのだろう。飛行機乗ってたらヘッドフォンぐらい壊れるだろ!」と大声で恫喝する有様。このクラスのホテルでこの対応はありえない、と思いました。 掃除も行き届いておらず埃だらけで、アメニティの補充もいい加減。シャンプーの小瓶のみ並んでた日もあり・・・、全く無かった日もあり・・・、みるからに汚い清掃道具が置きっぱなしの日もあり・・・。タオルも薄汚れた感じでした。

“great breakfast” Nice, elegant building, good location to the shopping streets. Large room, comfortable bathroom. The bed was too soft. Although I had big screen TV, no wide range of radio, TV channels, no DVD or CD library. Excellent breakfast, the berries were amazing! Service was average. Swimming pool was great, the gym part too.

“Great service and location, rooms a touch dated but still a favorite” While there are newer and more up-to-date options in the area, the Four Seasons remains my favorite. Service is top-notch. The staff has helped me with everything from reservations to organizing birthday surprises and taking deliveries prior to my arrival. Always welcoming. The rooms are very nice, if a touch dated. The larger rooms (I forget their exact name, but the largest room before getting to suite level) and the lower level suites are roomy and very comfortable. Nice bar as well. Recommended.

“colts/steelers game” My Wife and I go to Indy 2-3 times a year for games. We have always stayed right downtown around the circle center. We decided to try this place out. First of all, we saved a minimum of $60-$70 on the cost here vs. downtown. It was a 15-20 minute walk to the center of town. Not bad if the weathers nice. It rained the entire time we were there. But we were prepared for that. Yes the elevators are very small. But they worked better than most of the hotels we have stayed at in Indy. Parking was very convienent and somewhat covered. We slept in Monday, so we missed the breakfast. The room was spacious and clean. Bed very comfortable. Shower nice, but could use more pressure. We didn't notice any excess noises from other rooms, or hallway. Although the doors do tend to slam, because they are very heavy. All in all, we would stay here again, as long as the weather is decent.

“Good location and a reasonable price” I had stayed at this property back in 2000. Not much has changed since then as it is dated. The beds are comfortable. There is a microwave and fridge as well as a decent breakfast. On the last day as I was checking to see if I left anything behind I found an item left over by the previous guest. I should have reported it on check-out but was too busy thinking about my day. Just to make sure it was taken care of I called the hotel today. I choose this hotel as it was close to the Seattle attractions, clean (until the last day) and offered a good rate. Like previous reviews, Samantha stands out in her hospitality.

“Good choice” We stayed at this hotel for two nights in a room with two double beds on the 32nd floor. We enjoyed the view from way up there! The room itself was a bit small for 4 people, but it was very comfortable and everything was new. We loved the full sized refrigerator and kitchen area which was nice for preparing small meals. The bathroom was also very nice and big. However, the glass in the bathroom door can be seen through when someone is laying in the bed! We taped paper towels over the door as I was not happy about my teenage sons being able to see me undressed. Yikes! The breakfast was good and you do want to get there very early. That was fine with us since we had things to do and wanted an early start. The area around the hotel is not the best. It is a very active area and you need to be watchful in the nighttime hours. Would also advise anyone wanting to walk to Times Square at night to avoid 42nd Street by the wax museum. It was very scary with a big police presence and many young men looking for trouble. I was never so glad as to get off that block!!! If you walk up to 44th Street and cross over from there, the area is much different and there are plenty of normal tourists around. It is difficult to find room in front of the hotel to pull over when picking up or dropping off people/luggage. And you don't want to have to circle the block as the traffic is quite heavy in this area. I was happy with my choice in staying at this hotel. I am a Priority Club member and I was able to get a great AAA rate for the two nights. I don't think this would be my first choice of hotel, mostly because of the area, but it was a good hotel and it worked out fine for our family.

“Hotel That Delivers!” My wife and I spent a week at the Hotel Palomar in early March. Conveniently located in downtown Chicago in the River North area - minutes away from the Magnificent Mile and major attractions. Hotel staff is courteous and welcoming. Rooms are spacious, impeccably clean and the daily wine reception from 5-6 pm (including pizza appetizers) in the lobby area is a real treat! For light sleepers, the surrounding area can get a little rowdy on Friday/Saturday nights - lots of clubs and bars bringing in a college crowd. This hotel deserves all the accolades it receives!

“Simply the best hotel in the area” There are at least ten hotels/motels in the general area and I've stayed at most of them over the years, until now preferring the Marriott Courtyard near I-270. However, this brand new Holiday Inn has won me over. Lovely rooms and attentive staff. Nice lobby bar with a lively crowd. Close to I-70. This is the best business travel hotel in the immediate area, without a doubt. You can walk (about 1/4 mile) to an independent Italian restaurant named Salvi's Bistro, which offers fare other than the chain restaurants that predominate the area.

“bello moderno e strategico” Abbiamo dormito sabato scorso all Hyatt di seattle. il personale alla ricezione molto molto gentile e disponibile. le camere non enormi ma accoglienti e proviste di ogni comfort con trattamento RESPIRE, che devo dire non trovi ovunque. il bagno abbastanza grande e con prodotti per l igiene di qualita, letto molto confortevole e stanza luminosa. ho trovato anche una spa (compresa nel prezzo) il che non e male molto pulita e curata ottima anche la piscina. la posizione e veramente ottima perche molto centrale e comoda a tutto. sono stata veramente bene. avendo il volo nel pomeriggio ci hanno anche permesso di tenere la stanza piu del dovuto. da raccomandare.

“Outstanding Boutique Hotel” Great location, quiet hotel. Have stayed here twice and the hotel is wonderful. Very reasonably priced. I have been upgraded both times, one times into a huge suite with a piano. Made a reservation online at spg.com just 15 mins before I arrived and they had upgraded room all ready.

“It doesn't get more convenient than this” I have stayed at this hotel more nights than I care to admit - most recently last night. The staff provides consistently good service, the fitness center is excellent, the restaurants are great and you can't beat the convenience of just walking through the tunnel from the O'Hare terminal. You pay for the convenience through the room rate and extras for meeting rooms but overall, it is probably one of the easiest places in America to have a one day fly-in meeting.

“Clean and convenient to the Inner Harbor and Camden Yards” The Hilton is a good choice for downtown Baltimore. My room overlooked Camden Yards and it was a short walk to the Inner Harbor area. The staff was pleasant, rooms were immaculate, and the overall facility was great. My only reservation is that hotel was almost too sterile. The large lobby area felt functional and not comfortable or inviting, and there were not the little touches like ice water or coffee available in the lobby. There is a small bar there, but it felt exposed and the restaurant was in a different building. These comments at be a little harsh, but it just had a very corporate feel and lacked personality like some of the best Hiltons. You will definitely enjoy your stay here.

“Hotel tendance a Soho” Bel hotel en plein coeur de Soho avec restaurants et boutiques de luxe tout pres. Les chambres sont design, papier peint funky dans la salle de bain, mobilier sympa et dressing "walk-in". Le petit dejeuner est servi dans le lounge sur des canapes et a la fois l'ambiance et les clients sont plutot trendy.

“Nice rooms, quiet, close to Convention Center” I was here for business and the rooms were a good size and clean. We didn't have a view so that would probably have been nicer but being there for a convention we weren't in the room much anyway. We did the breakfast buffet once and it was pricey (as are most breakfast buffets) but it was very good. Can't beat the location by the convention center & the Gas Lamp area both 5 minutes walk from the room. I would stay here again for business.

“great midtown spot” Do not hestiate staying here if you want a great room at a great location. We have stayed here several times. Once again, staff was excellent. Upon arriving early, they upgraded us to a executive room and offered to set up roll away for daughter. You will find rooms a little larger than most NYC hotel rooms. The size would compare well to the higher end hotels like Plaza, Ritz and Waldorf.

“Too expensive for what it really is” We payed too much for a small renovated room.We asked for a rollabed, they said there wasn't enough space for one but we had a convertible sofa in the room. When we opened it up it was filthy, there was a kid's note from two years ago and it was so uncomfortable we could feel all the springs! The hotel is very well situated and we loved having breakfast at the starbucks in the lobby.

“Badly in need or renovation” Very spacious. That's about the only thing there is positive to say. Appliances are nearing antique status, bathroom is in sore need of renovation and re-appointment (missing shower curtain hooks, grout is black, toilet runs constantly...). Entire room is not particularly clean, and from the outside the separate hotel buildings look awful. Very cheap through some discount travel sites, but I would stay away.

“Good location” Needed one night accomodation in the city and wanted something centrally located. Also wanted to earn double honors points! Location of hotel is great. Staff was very friendly. When we got to our room we immediately noticed the very noisy elevator on the other side of our wall. We asked for a different room but they were sold out. The noise through the night was awful and in the morning we brought it to the attention of the manager. They were very apologetic and immediately offered to give us the night for free. I told them that everything else about the hotel was great and that a 50% discount was quite acceptable. Breakfast was typical of most Hamptons. They didn't have a business center but offered to let me use their office computer to look up the location of a local festival that was in the city. Parking was right next door and staff there was also very friendly. We left our bags with the bellman for the day and he quickly retrieved them for us when we returned at 3pm. I would pick this hotel again but request a room away from the elevator just in case they aren't able to resolve the noise issue.

“Great Property for $1! :-D” Back in January, I lucked out and was able to book 2 consecutive nights at the Public Chicago during their $1 sale. The 270 $1 rooms sold out in minutes, and many have argued that the sale was a marketing hoax/publicity stunt on behalf of the hotel. The good news is, I’m living proof that it was a real deal, and frankly, my entire decision to take a trip to Chicago with my girlfriends was influenced by this sale. In fact, we were thrilled that we were able to make this trip possible for under $100 each including round trip airfare. Overall, we had a great 2-night stay for a grand total of $2.34 including all taxes. The chic boutique hotel is conveniently located in downtown Chicago, a few blocks from the famous Michigan Ave (The Magnificent Mile). A cab ride from ORD is about 20-25 minutes depending on traffic and will cost roughly $35; luckily there were three of us to split the cost. As you can see from the website, the Public Chicago is a new addition to Chicago, with its grand opening in October of 2011. The Public is a very sophisticated luxury hotel conceived by Ian Schrager (creator of Studio 54). Inside the Public is the Pump Room restaurant, bar, and lounge. We did not dine at the Pump Room during our stay, but we did have a drink during happy hour (5-7 pm). The crowd was a bit older (45 ish), and very upscale. As far as drink prices, they certainly were very expensive for Chicago. I ordered a mojito, and it was $15; let’s just say that I was sure to sip that drink for a very long time. The staff were friendly and accommodating overall. Since we arrived to the hotel before check-in, they allowed us to leave our bags with them so we could explore Chicago for a bit. We had lunch nearby at Gibson’s on Rush Street, which was only about 3 blocks away from the property. During lunch, the front desk called us to inform us that our room was ready. The lobby, common areas, and rooms were absolutely stunning, modern, and artistic. We were certainly impressed, and most importantly, we enjoyed some much-needed quality “girl time” away! If you missed out on the deal the first time around, don’t fret. They’ll be another chance of scoring a room of your own for $1. The Public Chicago will soon be announcing another round of 270 rooms available for $1. You must register your email address to be notified of the sale, and act quickly! The lobby of The Public Chicago was definitely chic, modern, and stunning. We were given a standard king room. I'm surprised all three of us were able to comfortably share this bed. Flat screen TV and decorative artwork I loved this modern desk and faux-fur throw. The mini bar and menu (caution: very steep prices). Fully stocked mini fridge. Again, very steep prices. In-room snacks and gift memorabilia. The Public candle costs $65. Ouch. The bathroom was stocked with The Public's own line of bath products (shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, and bar soap). The sink was modern and had plenty of hand towels. The shower was new, immaculately clean, and had the best water pressure I've ever experienced at a hotel. For my complete review inlcuding pictures, please visit: http://boardingarea.com/blogs/justanotherpointstraveler/2012/03/03/hotel-review-public-chicago-1-sale-success/

“Beautiful Reno - a few bumps” First let me say that I stayed at the Madison years ago and I couldn't believe the beautiful renovation job. The hotel looks gorgeous. Unfortunately, they checked me in to a room that was already occupied. Imagine my surprise when I came to the door and it opened to reveal a family inside. I returned to the front desk and received a new room but no apology. My new room was tiny but nicely appointed except for the missing shampoo which was delivered promptly when I called. I'd definitely stay here again but they need to smooth out a few wrinkles.

“Great location if you are downtown” This hotel is a great location if you are attending events downtown. I attended the fireworks show and it was a quick 10 minute walk from the hotel down to Hart Plaza. The front desk staff and bell desk staff were excellent especially parking my car and dealing with all the cases and boxes I had for this trip. Cookies were in my room when I arrived (unexpected surprise). Rate for one night (06/27/06) was $141.45 and parking $17.00. Highly recommended if you are in the downtown Detroit area.

“Hard to beat” In town to see a ballet and Zarkana for the weekend and picked this hotel based on TripAdvisor reviews, once again TA did not steer me wrong. This is a great little boutique hotel very near Times Square and the Theatre district, half a block from a metro stop for the ABC lines, and a block from countless restaurants and bars in the Hells Kitchen district. You can get here direct from the airport via the AirTrain and Line A or Line E for $7.25. The rooms are small but pretty and comfortable and extremely well maintained. The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful, the best I've encountered in Manhattan hotels. Free wireless throughout and there are 3 new Mac computers for use by guests in the lobby to look up things to do or print boarding passes. It's not the most savory view out the front door (directly across from the port authority) but the location otherwise is really quite excellent. Highly recommended.

“Nice Rooms, Good Location” We came here for a convention and it was great. The staff was very friendly, rooms were very clean, and hotel was nice. Had a dinner reception in the ballroom, and the food was delicious. The room was beautiful and we had a great view on the 35th floor of the city and Rockies. My only wish is that the rooms had refrigerators and microwaves.

“Argonaut - clean, refreshing, worth the money” Stayed at the Argonaut April 14-18, 2007. Had stayed at another Kimpton hotel in Chicago, so we knew the standards were high and Trip Advisor had good reviews. It was our first trip to San Francisco. When we arrived on a Saturday afternoon, we were somewhat taken aback by the crowds at Fisherman's Wharf and not sure if we made the right choice, but the hotel is a couple blocks from the heavy traffic areas of the Wharf and the crowds lessened during the week. Our room was a double with views of the bay - Alcratraz and Golden Gate Bridge, if you stretched your neck. The room was very comfortable and spotless!! The beds are heavenly! The bathroom is nice size with L'Occitane toiletries, whch have a refreshing scent and we thought the entire hotel smelled like them. The bellboy was quite helpful when we checked in and made sure we were happy with our room before leaving. The doorman on duty was always friendly and helpful. The lobby is very comfortable and the hotel's nautical theme is suited well to the area. The cable car stop is just a block up. A one-way trip is $5, so it pays to purchase the all-day pass for $11 which gives you access to all modes of transportation. We rode the cable cars up to Union Square, then hopped a street car or bus to our other destinations -- Golden Gate Bridge, Haight-Ashbury, Alamo Square. China Town is a stop along the way to Union Square. Most of the cable car operators we encountered were fun and enjoyed interacting with tourists. Hertz and Avis are located a couple blocks from the hotel, so it's convenient to rent a car and drive to Sausalito and on up to Napa Valley. We used Hertz and the girl behind the counter was very helpful and patient, even with several people on hold. There's a Ben and Jerry's next door, but we would suggest Norman's Ice Cream which is located in patio of The Cannery, next door to the hotel. The ice cream is good, and the owners were very friendly and appreciative of our business.

“Good place to stay” We stayed here for two nights during Austin City Limits. The hotel is only 10 or 15 minutes drive from downtown Austin and despite being located by I-35 it seemed quite quiet. The room was a good size, clean and comfortable. The staff were friendly and helpful. If you can't find anything downtown then this is a perfectly good alternative.

“Maybe about time to invest in a refurb Mr. Humphrey, and what about those ducks!” Final stop on our tour of California, which started two weeks earlier in San Francisco! Checked in and full credit to the front desk staff who acknowledged my request for a water view and prompty delivered with a room in the M building. No balcony to sit out at, but at least we could watch the boats in the marina. The room itself was showing it's age and despite being thoroughly clean is about ready for a refurb. There was a concert taking place on our first night of three, but this didn't bother us at all. In fact it adds a nice feel to the evening. There is one BIG health and hygiene issue that the property should take urgent action on. That is the resident duck population that treat the pool and pool area as their personal toilet. I'm not kidding here folks, excrement was floating in the pool and around the steps in and out. A bit scary when travelling with young children and the international spectre of H5N1 bird flu. That aside, the pool area was nice and relaxing, the bar service fine with a good choice of cocktails. I would recommend taking the 10 minute trip into the Old Town and dining at the Old Town Mexican Cafe. A great experience, with good quality Mexican food at great prices. Another recommended option just a 10 min walk from the hotel is Miguels Cocina - great option if eating with kids, the staff there were great and so were the Margaritas :) We enjoyed our stay in the San Diego area, as we did our overall journey down the pacific coastal highway. If we ever return to SD, I would probably try somewhere different, but wouldn't rule out a return to Humphreys for it's laid back, tropical feel and decent staff.

“Just wonderful!” My husband and I were looking for a quick getaway for our anniversary last month. We have stayed at the Hotel 1000 and loved it, but it was booked. We decided to book a suite at the Grand Hyatt and it was a great decision. The room was huge! On the 26th floor, with glorious views of the Sound and Lake Union. We had 2 bathrooms! I am very particular about hotels and the Grand Hyatt was definitely up to my standards. The front desk staff wasn't very helpful and the parking is expensive, but the room and amenities more than make up for it. Planning a Christmas shopping getaway that includes the Grand Hyatt!

“Great Indy Stopover - Lots of Room and Great Service” Traveling through Indiana, and had a morning flight out of IND, so picked this particular property to stay the night. It was - while not really close to the airport - on the way to the airport, and based on the hotel's website, only about 15 - 20 minutes away, all freeway. Plus the midweek rate was pretty good - $98, and that includes breakfast and dinner (only M - Th for dinner). The hotel itself was in pretty good condition - it's right on the corner of the beltway (465) and another busy street, but it was behind another hotel property and the Cracker Barrel next door, so it seemed relatively quiet. Definitely no noise issues. It seemed fairly new, not sure when it was built, but the rooms, hallways, common areas, etc. showed no signs of wear, and things were kept relatively clean throughout the property. One exception was the dining area - it wasn't "dirty" per se, but could have used a bit more attention during the busy eating times - dinner and breakfast. I think they keep it staffed fairly tightly - one or two people running it all, and they did a fantastic job at keeping the food and drink areas well stocked, rotated, and replenished. The table cleanliness is just a nit, didn't detract from the mealtime at all. The breakfast spread was great - plenty of hot and cold items, much much more than typical continental type breakfast spreads. Also nice is the "manager's reception" on M - Th evenings - it's really dinner, but they just have one choice...it's not a buffet. The night I was there, they had hot dogs, macaroni/cheese, and salad, plus free wine/beer if you want. Limited selection notwithstanding, it's a really nice feature - especially if you ever travel with a family. The room was great - typical to Homewood Suites properties, had the bedroom, bathroom, living area, and kitchen with oven, full refrigerator, sink, etc. That's really nice if you are staying for one night or a long time. You can get food at the grocery store, and store it for cooking later. That was really nice, and they have a dishwasher to use, plus the plates and silverware you would need. That's also a great feature. They have the standard hotel fitness center and pool/hot tub areas. The fitness center was pretty small - one treadmill, one bike, one stairstepper, and some free weights. The indoor pool/hot tub area was pretty big - a lot of seating area. Maybe could have made the fitness room a bit bigger, but it definitely served its purpose. I didn't use the business center, but it was the standard one, looked like it had everything you'd need. Something nice was that the hotel had free internet - it's good to see that all properties are moving this way; it used to be just the Hampton Inns that had the free internet, now it seems like most Hilton properties do. The area surrounding the hotel was ok - fairly busy, but consequently there were a ton of restaurants, shopping, grocery, Walgreen's, etc. So I would rate the location as decent for that reason. I'll definitely be back if in the area under similar circumstances (flying out of IND), or if I have meetings in the city. The rate was the clincher - better than most other properties of similar size.

“Great Location, Okay Hotel” Just got back from DC and stayed at the Residence Inn. A very nice hotel with a good breakfast and spacious suites. It was kind of strange seeing a place like this in DC, but the all suites idea is a good concept for a large city hotel. A good place to stay when on a budget as compared to it's upscale neighbors in the DuPont Cirlce area. Don't expect lavish accomodations, but just a simple and clean hotel with a friendly staff.

“Large comfy rooms” We stayed at the Indianapolis downtown Hilton over New Year's weekend to celebrate our anniversary. This Hilton is know for having some of the most spacious hotel rooms in Indy. Not only are they large, but they are very comfortable. It was a busy weekend in the hotel, but the staff was courteous. This hotel also has a couple of great restaurants including a very good McCormick & Schmicks. It is also within walking distance to many other restaurants and shopping.

“Great all the way around” My girlfriend and I went to New York City to see a play. I chose the Doubletree, first, for its proximity to the theater, and second, it received overall good reviews on Trip Advisor. We flew in to La Guardia $35 cab ride to the hotel. We had "carry on" size luggage so the bellman never even approached us - I prefer to deal with my own luggage. This trip was a rewards certificate from Hitlon Honors 80,000 points for two nights. Kathy M at the front desk was super nice and honored my request of a high floor (#1604). I'm just a traveling country boy so I thought the lobby looked nice, never crowded but it was Super Bowl Sunday. The Hotel Bar "The Met" was bad on so many levels. I went in one night and Abdul the bartender was so engrossed in TV he didn't notice me for several minutes. A Guinness and another beer was $13 + tip.. The decor in the bar was a hodge podge of a 70's flea market.. It seemed dirty lots of food crumbs on the floor and hardly any customers. The Staff from the maid to an Assistant Manager were friendly - I was shocked that the maids in the hall went out of their way to greet you. My one issue was in my opinion being lied to or at least misled by a female Concierge. Upon arrival we asked about going to the Statue of Liberty she tried to dissuade me by saying it would be too crowded on the normal ferries. She was much too quick in whipping out a private cruise boat and trying to get me on their cruise. I opted to go to Battery Park and check it out for myself -no lines quick to get tickets, quick to get on the ferry and off we went. The rooms are small but functional, the beds were great and did not get too much street noise. theres is no coffee service in the room. As Hilton Honor members we got a certificate to go to the 17th floor for breakfast. It was nice mainly carbohydrate type breakfast, muffins, fruit, cereals, etc. Sunday morning that was closed and the front desk gave us vouchers to eat in the restaurant. Those guys were amazing the way they moved people around all with a good sense of humor - it was a complete hot breakfast. Pros: Nice location, friendly staff, great beds Cons: Concierge misleading us; hotel bar is nasty I'd stay here again

“Beautiful hotel located in a perfect area” Had the pleasure of booking this hotel directly through the Starwood web page, which linked me to this hotel. I was quoted 199.00 per night, and thought that this was a very reasonable deal. After reading some comments, I took some with a grain of salt. I have stayed at the Palace in Madrid Spain, and thought if this was anywhere near that ,I would be happy. Location is about 40 minutes to SFO. I hired a cab take myself and my date, the cost one way is 45.00. Upon leaving the hotel after our 2 night stay, I was offered by the doorman a black Town car to return to SFO for about $50, plus I tipped 10. They staff was very friendly and served you with smiles. The concierge was a life saver. They ordered a strech limo for me and my guest to go out for dinner and club hopping. Cost was billed to the room for $210 including tip. The moment you walk in , it will take you a while to absorb the architecture of this building. It was very ornate, simular what you might find in Venice or Rome. All avenues were spotless. Rooms were small, but had marble, shower,tubs, all necessities one would need, including free bottleds water. The only down side is that there is a refrid. in the room, but no mini bar.Wonderfully done bed, and very comfortable. I had scheduled a romantic lunch at The Gardens. Very opulant and grand. Lunch was around $100. They even sprinkleed our table with rose pedals,something I had not asked for, but made me look like a hero...Thanks!!!!! Went to the sushi rest. adjoining the hotel. Had wonder dinner, sushi etc for about $150. Mornings, I went to a Starbucks no more than 150 feet from hotel. I would absolutly stay here again. There was some signs of age, but I would rate this hotel a 4 out of 5. The Wharf is a 11 dollar taxi ride. Enjoy...I did.

“Good location” We stayed here to visit Boston University; the T line out to Boston U. is very convenient to the hotel. This is an old and grand hotel, a little dated maybe. We found our room (2 double beds) to be very clean. The bathroom was small but also very clean. Our room was quite large and was on a high floor facing the street. We came in on the eve of the first snowstorm! Because of the weather, we were glad to be able to have both dinner and the following morning's breakfast in the lobby (at a little stand that sells rolls and coffee). The beds were comfortable and we didn't find it too noisy. What was a shame was that there was no hot water in the morning. I don't know whether this is a common occurrence or not, but no hot water is not acceptable! Otherwise we had a fine stay.

“Nice hotel, a little pricey” I had no problem with this hotel, however it seemed more like an upscale vertical motel than a full service faciltiy (which I expected in a Doubletree.). The friendliness at the front desk was spotty. Some were excellent, but one woman acted like she couldn't be bothered by my request. Overall, the service was very good. The garage is very difficult, as others have pointed out. The hotel was very crowded this weekend, so that might have affected things. I really have no complaints: I was just expecting a little better from Doubletree

“A small, functional yet well designed hotel” Let me start by saying this hotel has probably one of the smallest rooms I have ever seen in the U.S., yet, everything worked out nicely. The room (I had a double room with private bath) looks exactly like what the hotel photos showed so I arrived with absolutely no surprise. Space inside the room is TINY - no more than 90 sq. ft. including the toilet/bath area (so you can imagine how small the actual room is). But everything works in its own way: from the airplane looking stainless sink, sleek see through stand-up shower, functional bed with storage drawers underneath and the practical desk area (a phone and an iPod sound system). My favorite part is the stand-up shower/toilet area, very modern lookig with a tiny bit of desinger's touch. Bed is comfortable and clean with bedding sheet changed daily. Location. This hotel sits on E51 between 3rd and 2nd St. on Upper Midtown East. Subway Line 6 is about one and a half block away and Subway Line E & V are about 2 blocks away so it is quite convenient. There is no restaurant inside the hotel but tons of dining options are available in the immediate area: check out PAX (sandwich/salad haven), Azure (self serve buffet market) and a number of ethnic restaurants nearby (E51 as well as 2nd). There are even a bar and a chic lookig restaurant outside the hotel on either side of the street. Hotel premise. The buidling has obviously gone through a mjaor overhaul and was turned into a boutique style hotel. The lobby is spacious and decorated with IKEA style furniture - mordern yet somewhat cheap looking. During my 4-day stay, I had seen tons of young hotel guests gathering in the lobby. I never used the area myself but can imagine it would be a great meeting point. Amenities and service. Basic bathroom cleaning supplies is pretty much what you get. There is not even an ice machine in the hotel. But all rooms come with a LCD TV and free wireless internet, which is definitely a big plus. You can pick up log in and password information when you check in but do not expect fast internet as the service was very sporadic and tempermental. I was able to check emails okay but could not go too much beyond that. I could imagine how frustrated heavy web surfers can become. There are two elevators on premise, unfortunately as some of the reviews pointed out previously, they are EXTEMELY SLOW. A couple times I had to wait about 5 minutes to get into the lift so be prepared to have some patience if your room is at the higher floor. The other issue that could possibly distrub people is the noise level but this is probably due to the hallway is so narrow and the thin wall as well as small room space make the noise sound even worse. If someone slams the door (which happened a lot), then you definitely hear it. If you were a light sleeper, make sure to bring your ear-plugs. I brought mine and they were extemely helpful for sleeping at night. Overall, this is a pretty good no thrill hotel designed for budget conscious travelers. If you don't mind the bunker beds and shared bathrooms (which are very clean), this is absolutely a much better option than those youth hotels such as YMCA. But even for people who want an upgraded room, you only need to pay a little more to get your own private bath/shower facility. For a city like New York where hotel price is skyrocketed, Pod is a great alternative and provides exceptional value. This place definitely goes on my NYC hotel list of stay.

“ghosts with your stay? very possible” there are pros and cons...the pros=huge apartment sized "room" you could host a family easily with the separate bedroom, full kitchen etc. very quiet, and great staff even at 2 am...cool architecture and an elevator door that is from the old days! clean but very dingy!!! this is a place that has seen history go by and never pulled ahead of it. the cons? squeaky doors, weird music and smells, hole in the sheet (small), incorrect channel list , dust under the bed, lumpy pillows, very old, dirty phone, no extra pillows or towels (they were full so no blankets for pull out bed either) so very austere. very old tv's in both rooms and furniture from two centuries ago. internet access sorely lacking as well. lots of atmosphere but not sure the atmosphere you like unless you are a ghost buster...

“Great Location, Great Price, Tiny Room” We went to NYC for a long weekend and because of the time of year, the hotels were booked solid, so we tried here in order to get a price we could afford. The staff was friendly and efficient, the room was clean, the bed was comfortable. However, the room, even by NYC standards was TINY! There was litterally one foot (12 inches) between the bed and two of the walls. Trying to get out of bed to the bathroom was extremely difficult. The bathtub was not full size, so I'm not sure how an adult was supposed to take a bath. If you are a single, the rooms would be fine, but for two or more people, they are VERY cramped.
“Great hotel for business meetings or for vacation in DC.” Location is great and dining on site is wonderful. Staff is very helpful. Very nice experience.

“Needed a break” After relocating to Charlotte a few weeks ago I have been living in different hotels. After a very hectic week at work and hearing my co-workers talk about this hotel in such glowing terms I booked a room for 2 nights. Was greeted immediately when I drove up to the hotel. Luggage was taken and I made my way to the front desk. After this weekend I will meet the 50 night criteria for this year which will not only give me Platinum through 2013 but also lifetime platinum. I have a room that faces the golf course. I then went to the spa since when I tried to book via the website it returned a website error. The woman at the spa was very nice and found a slot for my facial. I then went to the bar. Reasonable prices, nice selection. I ordered a burger at the bar. I would say it was fair at best (left 3/4 of it uneaten). Not all that impressed with the food but the bartender was very nice and service was great. Beautiful fresh flowers in the main lobby. This is definitely in the suburbs of Charlotte (new buildings everywhere around here) but there are many choices in terms of restaurants around here. The pool is nice as is the fitness center and the grounds in the back. The hotel isn't that big. The upgraded room is nice but definitely not anything to post about - it's a room facing the golf course. It is very relaxing here. DAY TWO Had asked the concierge to make me reservations for brunch (Saturday). She told me I was in and gave me directions. I arrived at the brunch place - Terrace Cafe. Explained that I had a reservation made by the concierge at the resort. The hostess with the MOSTESS attitude told me they don't accepet reservations and I should go back to the resort and tell the concierge I wanted the printed out email showing the reservation. Anyway. . .after I finally ate there it was OK but wouldn't recommend it like so many other people have who live here. Walked around the Ballantyne village shops. There are very few but cute shops. Bakery, stationery store, local craftspeople jewelry store, wine bar, theatre, chocolate/ice cream shop, and pizza shop. None of the places are "standard" e.g., Hallmark, Baskin Robbins, etc. which was nice. Then walked back to the resort to try and get in for a 25 minute massage. They had an opening. Spa is nice. There is a sauna and a steam room (men and women locker rooms are separated and each have their own steam/sauna). Lockers are given so you can put your stuff in it and not worry about it. Robes and sandals are provided. Flavored waters, coffee, and trail mix snacks are offered. Relaxing lounge is provided with lots of magazines. Private showers are also offered. I had an amazing massage and my body feels brand new. At the end they gave me a rose as a thank you. The outdoor pool is not opening until the end of March as it turns out and the golf shop was closed at 5 PM today as well so I couldn't go to the driving range. I did have some bar food. The wedge salad was very well done and fresh as well as the guacamole.

“Great non-chain choice in heart of Seattle” I try to avoid chain hotels b/c they are so cookie cutter. Nobody would ever call Hotel Max a cookie cutter hotel. The hotel's best parts spring form its decorative elements. I really appreciated the art throughout the hotel, but the vertical format images that cover all of the doors were a touch of brilliance. They are all different, stunning, and make it impossible to forget what room you are in. I also enjoyed the finishes in the rooms, with flat screens, high concept bathroom fixtures, and the (somewhat) overrated pillow menu. The lobby was nice with smart counter people (all their recommendations were spot on), interesting coffee table books (I know it sounds stupid, but I was traveling in a group and we spent a lot of time chilling in the lobby), and a super business center with two computers with broadband connections hooked up to a printer (leave your laptop at home). The only problem with the hotel is a typical problem in downtown hotels -- the rooms were super small, particularly in the two bed rooms. If you can live with that, then you should stay at Hotel Max. I don't recommend the hotel restaurant for breakfast, but a couple blocks away are Lola (sit down) and Hot Pot (gourmet donuts). So, don't be afraid to take a stroll.

“Only stay here if you have to” Basically a dark, dingy motel - so if that's what you want, fine. However it's hardly cheap, and I just can't understand why so many travel companies feature it. Unless you're desperate, pay more and stay elsewhere. (Staff were great, though - so don't take out your disappointment on them.)

“Decent value, but small rooms” The Renaissance M Street is a good upscale hotel. The staff was friendly and helpful. As a business traveler the location was fine, but not very convenient to monuments, museums and other attractions. The rooms were clean, but small. Overall, a decent value for the price I paid through Priceline.

“Not impressed” I stayed here with an old friend for a girls weekend. I love modern hotels like the Standard, W, etc. but, we got a good deal here and thought the location would be good & willing to try something different. The room was SO hot when we got there & we couldn't figure out how to turn it down. Waited and waited for someone to help but, got impatient and went out to shop & eat. We came back hours later to find all they did to fix it was crack the window open. The room was ok size. The bathroom was ok. No hairdryer. We weren't in the room that much anyway. Decor was stuffy & old fashioned but, we expected that. Totally unimpressed with the dated lobby. We asked the concierge for lunch suggestions and they sent us to a closed restaurant. The next day we asked for a reasonably priced brunch recommendation. They suggested Oscars (the hotel restaurant). We had the buffet - it was gross. Watery eggs, burnt coffee, a bagel & potatoes - $100 for 2 w/ tip. INSANE!!!!!!!

“Staff is great, but hotel needs some updating” I have stayed at the Sheraton Philadelphia a few times in the last few months for business. This hotel consistently has great room rates, and staff is very helpful. It is a large hotel conveniently located by Ben Franklin Parkway, which is home to the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the new Barnes Art Museum, Free Library and Franklin Institute. As others have mentioned in their reviews, the hotel is a bit dated and the rooms could probably use some refurbishments.

“A lovely hotel” My husband and I stayed here for a couple of days. It's location is great with easy access to the metro and surrounded by places to eat. We didn't try the hotels own restaurant as we didn't have time so we can't comment on that. Our room was huge as was the bathroom and everything was very clean. We thought it was absolutely great. Hotels in Washington are expensive in comparison to elsewhere, however, we thought this hotel was excellent value for money and a nice treat. We choose all our hotels using Tripadvisor as a guide, as do many other people, so it is great to see that the Manager takes the trouble to read the comments and add some of his/ her own. Some reviews have commented on the reception aspect of the hotel and this would be my one adverse comment. The staff are great in that they get everything done efficiently and help when asked. Some do, however, seem ever so slightly frosty. I don't advocate an effusive reception but it would be nice to receive a genuine welcome when you arrive travel worn and tired, it's first contact and has a marked effect.

“A nice stay for a fun weekend” I was going to Philadelphia for the King Tut exhibit and got the Westin for $112 a night through Hotwire. Silly me thought it would be a short walk to the hotel from 30th Street station and it was a hot day. But once I was warmly greeted at the front desk I knew it was going to be a great stay. The room was everything you would expect from a Westin, including that Heavenly Bed! Onr complaint I have is the charge for internet service; $9.95 a day or $4.95 for 30 minutes. Why can't it be free? All the staff was friendly; the concierge was particularly helpful in giving me info on how to get around. The bar was nice but not what I would expect from a Westin. I still remember the Library bar in Providence. Anyway, the service here was slow, which confused me because there were very few people in the bar. Checkout was friendly and I received a complimentary Sunday paper. How nice! This hotel is not the most convenient if you are visiting the historic sites, but it's worth the extra distance. Just go there!

“Tired Old Hotel” We stayed here for 3 nts Mar 1, 2, 3, 2012. GREAT Times Square location, looks great from the street, lobby looks beautiful. Super nice front staff. We were upgraded to the 8th floor (large corner room) - NW CORNER - facing Broadway out one window & Times Sqaure out the other window. AWESOME VIEWS! Once at the 8th floor, we noticed the halls walls, carpet & paint was worn, dingy & just plain tired looking. Our room looked the same, wall paper was yellowed & bubbling, sink was off color, our sink stopper was out, laying on the counter - later in our stay the sink backed up - we called & they sent someone to fix it, it helped for a while, but it was draining slow when we left. The bathroom was tiny... I banged my foot on the toilet getting into the shower. The bed was great, slept like a log every night. The subway runs right under the sidewallk below the room & about every thirty seconds you hear it. (It didn't bother us tho). Our TV was a large flatscreen, that we couldn't get to come on half the time without going to it & turning it off & back on (to reboot it).The picture was fuzzy & had lines all thru it. Not terrible, but not clear. There is no fridge in the room, so we used our bathroom wastebasket lined with a plasic liner filled with ice to keep our wine & beer cool. Plastic cups, cheap (vegetable) bath soaps...really? Gees. You have to pay for internet service in the room (I used my 3g phone & MIFI for my laptop for free)...however the connections were S L O W... They have free internet in the lobby & several computers & printers. The hotel has a nice restaurant that is only open for breakfast. No Bar. Strange to us. People are up, milling around at all hours of the night, we sure would have liked to have had a drink in the hotel bar.... if there had been one. Would I stay here again??? Maybe. Only if the price was right (as it was this time - they offer a government rate). To pay their regular price, I'd stay at several of the MANY other hotels in the area with the same price range. The Park Central is just steps away, as is the Sheraton (both in the same price range). I've actually stayed in nicer Holiday Inn Express' & Hilton Garden Inn's. Starwood needs to upgrade this hotel...it desperately needs a refurb, desperately. And a full time restaurant with a BAR! Hope they are listening.

“good budget lodging” I am a budget minded traveler and dont like to over spend for my hotels, since i dont spend much time in the room, so take my review in that context. i stayed there in october 2006, for the running of the detriot marathon. The motel is on the edge of downtown. I felt safe walking to downtown and did not encounter any unusual vagrants or shady characters. Not the prettiest of locations, but not too ugly, as other parts of the city can be. Easy walk to downtown, Greektown casino, etc... The staff was very friendly, even offered to come to my room to help set up a baby crib and offered extra linens without me asking. Restaraunt is awesome. Great food, large portions, and cheap. A true find. teh rooms show their age some and are pretty simple, but were clean and bed was comfortable. I did not experience any of the problems with noise at the hotel as other posts had mentioned, although with the large glass windows, you can hear people outside talking and walking up/down the stairs. all-in-all a good value

“Comfortable rooms...” We stayed at the Sofitel from 6-8 April as we were anxious to see what it was like after the rennovations! I must say the place looked sensational, the staff were sensational (as they always were) and the rooms were still as comfortable as ever! Check-in was a breeze and the front desk staff were very friendly! The bell boy came up to the room with us and explained the room in detail and also gave us some tips on the area as well as ways to get to the ice hockey which was a nice touch! The new bathrooms are sensational and the rain water showers are awesome! I could have stood under that thing for hours!!! The gym facilities were great! TV's on each of the cardio equipment, headphones to borrow, fresh towels, wet refrigerated Eucalyptus towels, bottles of Evian, brownies on one of the days and free internet access - what more could we ask for?! Fantastic!!! The free slippers were great!!!! The amenities were awesome and the rooms were always fresh and clean!!! Turndown service every night and it was great to receive a bottle of Evian instead of chocolates that's for sure! Check out was a breeze as was valet, the staff were fantastic! Love the black outfits and berrets!!! We will definately be back (if the price is right!) :) Enjoy!!!

“Beautiful restored lobby and convenient location” If you haven't noticed - I am a big Kimpton fan and San Francisco has many properties to chose from. The Serrano is a rehab of an older building and they do their best to make it Kimpton worthy - including Kimptonized bathrooms. I was able to upgrade to a corner suite for my stay and the extra sitting space was nice. The building is Spanish revival and the lobby is beautifully restored and the entrance doors are impressive. The building is older but again they do all the things right - free wiFi, coffee and wine. The staff were all friendly and helpful. The elevators are a bit tiny more like Europe but overall it was a pleasant stay. I was not overly impressed with the restaurant associated with the property - Jaspers is more like a bar, they are known for what is on tap and not being a big beer drinker it is not a place I would hang out in much but the burger was fantastic and the omelette in the morning was terrific.

“Won't stay here again” I should have listened to the reviews on this place. When I booked via phone, I was informed that there were some rooms that were updated, some weren't. The $57 internet rate was for old rooms, while the $83 rates were for the updated rooms. I bit on the $83 rate, deciding that maybe that's where others had gone wrong. We checked in early, only to be given an older room. When confiring with the front desk help, they had no record of my having a nicer room, but said that if I came back in an hour, their supervisor would okay it. An hour later we were in our new room. (4th & 5th floors are updated, the rest not.) The room was okay, cleaner than downstairs, but not terribly special. I had some problems with the shower and there was no fan to vent the steam. Mold is sure to follow soon. We were on the odd-numbered room side, which faces the highway and train tracks. Very loud road noise to be heard, and the 100+ car trains that rumbled through were very loud. Definiately not the pleasant whistle of a passing train. There were a lot of shops & restaurants nearby, but downtown was a trip. It sufficed, but I woudn't stay there again.

“Nice hotel - great service, but as most urban hotel chains - very pricey amenities” I stayed here for 3 weeknights in March 2011. At that time the hotel was undergoing renovations in places. I was given the choice of a renovated room or a room with a great view. I took the view (30th floor of 36). The room did indeed have a great view toward the bay and financial district but it did need some modernization. Tube TV, dated curtains, worn dressers/doors, straight shower curtain bar, and worn carpeting were some of the items needing an update. However, everything worked, the bed was comfortable, the shower had great pressure and plenty of hot water, and the room was quiet. So for this yet-to-be-renovated room the pluses outweighed the minuses. I had a car and parked it in a garage around the corner from the hotel for $35/day which is high but not as much as the hotel valet service. That garage by the way, is clean and the attendants are courteous and professional. The restaurant on the top floor has fantastic views of the city and beyond. The service was top notch and not rushed if you didn't want to be rushed. The full breakfast buffet with gratuity was $22-$24 which was about the same price as a late evening burger, beer, and gratuity. Lots of dining of all types within a five minute walk - Starbucks across the street, cafes on Union Square 1/2 block away, Lori's Diner (50s theme) is a block or so away, and many others. Overall a very nice hotel and I'd recommend it to anyone.

“Best Value, Great Vacation” Stayed here for 9 nights and had a great experience. Paid $99/night which is a steal for Manhattan. The hotel is at the foot of the empire state building on a street with mostly Korean restaurants and markets. Subway station was less than a block away. Felt very safe walking around the area at night and tried a couple of the restaurants around the hotel which were pretty good. 15-20 minute walk to Times Square. Complimentary continental breakfast was a great way to start the morning. The breakfast room was kind of small and difficult to get a seat, but we made do. The hotel has a work out room which was great. Building is kind of old and we did get stuck in the elevator one night, but the staff responded quickly and got us out within 5 minutes.

“Classic service, nice accomodations” I stayed at the Waldorf twice in the last year. The most recent stay was the nights of 1/23 and 1/24/2012. As a Hilton Honors member I was upgraded to a superior corner room on the 10th floor. The famous Waldorf Towers have the top floors of the hotel. I don't know how many they have, but most floors are the regular hotel. I saw the beautiful Grand Ballroom - make sure you check it out if you're in the neighborhood. It kind of looks like Carnegie Hall! The service is outstanding at this hotel, but my room wasn't real special. The furnishings are a bit old and the heating/ac system also is a bit dated. The room was comfortable - but you are not paying top prices here - the regular base Waldorf does not have high prices by NYC standards. The Towers is pricey - and I don't know what the rooms are like up there. The location of the hotel is ideal. Lots of history there. I hear the base rooms are small - so always go for an upgrade.

“Very nice yet not at all stuffy” Stayed here for a conference and was pleasantly surprised. In general, I find "luxury" hotels to be forgettable or uptight, and this was neither. Besides the great location, the staff were courteous - particularly the housekeeping staff, whose nice touches (wrapping cords, leaving bookmarks, folding and tidying) were appreciated. Concierge, front desk, amd bell staff were also quite helpful. And the giant bathroom and bathtub were definitely a plus. Other only reason I can't go quite to five stars? The bed. While dressed nicely in a down comforter and plenty of pillows, the mattress clearly was well-used on one side. Call me weird, but having a really comfortable bed seems like the first thing on a luxury hotel must-have list. But that said, I definitely would stay here again as it has risen to the top of the list for best hotel in Chicago.

“prime lodging for Camden Yards” Stayed at Hampton Inn Camden Yards for the opening day Orioles/Yankees game earlier this month. I had gotten an email in advance with special directions/parking information in light of street closures in connection with the game, which was a big help. As we got closer to the hotel from the highway, it looked like there would be no way to get through, but, just as the directions said, we were able to get past the barriers and throngs of fans there for the game and pull right up to the hotel. The staff of the hotel was most helpful in allowing us in and then parking the car to let us check in. The hotel is right across from the ballpark and our room overlooked the stadium, though the building is not high enough to see the field (which the Hilton Inn next door would be able to do). Even though the room was that close to the crowds below, the noise level was not a problem. The hotel still looks new, and the room was clean and good sized, with comfortable beds and especially good pillows. Free breakfast the next morning was great, fresh food and even with a self-service waffle maker. The ability to get to/from I-95 is a plus, as the hotel is only 2 blocks from the entrance/exit ramp and easy to access. Walking to the Inner Harbor is a bit far, especially in cold or rainy weather, but probably a pleasant (15 minute or so) walk when it is nice out. Given reasonable room rates, this hotel is a keeper.

“Excellent location” We were in town for an event at the Toyota Center, so the location couldn't have been more convenient. Easy walk to the facility. Also would have been a great spot if going to a game at Minute Maid Park. What little time we did spend at the hotel was just fine. The room was clean and functioned as expected. Front desk staff seemed a bit detached, but did their jobs fine. Breakfast was quite nice, relative to other Holiday Inn Express locations. Everything was stocked well, hot and good. The only annoyance was the computer they have available for internet access off the main lobby. I was never able to get it to work and only saw one guest who did during our two days there.

“Great Marriott Service and Location but Rooms need Redecoration” I am a frequent Marriott traveler. Like most Marriotts, this hotel had good service and nice public spaces. It is in an excellent location. The hallways are tired and need refresh, with some of the loudest icemakers I have ever heard. The rooms feature typical comfortable Marriott bedding, but the TV is old style, the work desk is quite small, and the chairs are uncomfortable. The bathrooms are okay. Rooms are clean but need to be updated. Ok if you get a reasonable price.

“Watch your stuff” I stayed at the Boston Park Plaza Hotel the weekend of June 12th with a few friends and I wasn't absolutely in love with the hotel and its services. To start off, the hotel itself is beautiful, high ceilings, and tons of character. The rooms also are kept up nicely. I had issues with the hotels services. When my friends and I went to check-in, it took about 40 minutes of waiting online at the front desk, then we finally get to the room and some keys did not work so we had to go back down and wait on the long line once again. My biggest problem with them though, is that I checked my luggage at the bellhop to get brunch that final morning and when I got home I noticed items were missing from my bag. The front zipper of my luggage was completely opened and I am missing two pieces of jewelry. It was only expensive costume jewelry so I didn't deem it necessary to remove from my bag before checking it. I usually know not to leave a passport or anything of importance in my luggage when its being checked at a hotel. However, I also thought my luggage was being watched. I contacted the hotel about this matter, they didn't seem very concerned and said they would call me back to file a claim, never heard from them. So just make sure in the rooms and if you check your bag to take anything of importance with you!

“Location price restaurant” Frist off this was our 2 nd. visit. Location is great. Walking About three blocks to the Mono Rail for the short trip to the Seattle Center. Mono Rail stop is in the Westlake Shopping Center. Walk to the Market is a little longer but doable. Many shops and coffeee shops along the way.Staff is always helpful and frendly. You have only to ask. Cookies at the desk is a nice touch. The only thing [ If it is a bother to you. ] a lot of young people stay here. So it can be noisy at times. late comings and goings. However we had no problem with noise. Room was clean. Bathroom was clean. The bathroom floor is one thing I always check. To me the bathroom is an indicatior of the kind of care that the rest of the room gets. The heater worked fine. The bed was OK. To bad this hotel will not be around much longer. I will miss it. The service is good, the location was good and the price was right.

“Great location and nice hotel” I was in Denver for a conference and chose the Grand Hyatt, based on its proximity to the Colorado Convention Center. It's in a good location--I could walk to just about everything. The hotel is quite large, rooms nicely sized and apportioned. The housekeeping staff must be stretched pretty thin these days--my room often wasn't serviced until well into the afternoon. I had to dig around for a wall outlet to recharge my phone. Fortunately I had internet for my computer--really don't understand why Hyatt charges for this. Room service was ok, food at appropriate temperatures and it was very prompt. Don't think that I'd stay here again--there were some other spots that looked quite nice.

“Not Bad for the Price” We booked same day through Orbitz. Checked in fine. Had to wait about 10 minutes, since Orbitz hadn't faxed in our reservation. Not a big deal. Yes, the hotel is old and needs to be remodeled, but we only paid $89 for one night and I thought this was a great deal to include breakfast. We checked in around 3 pm and spent one night. We were in room 328 and overlooked the road. The bed and room were clean. Large room. Shower initially was cold and was told the water heater broken earlier. Morning shower was nice and warm. Breakfast was fine, waffles, fruit, bagels, cereal, coffee, teas and juices. Check out was speedy. Parking was free and was easily accessible. I would stay here again for the same price.

“Great hotel on the grounds of Georgetown University” What a pleasant surprise - a very respectable hotel nestled inside the campus of Georgetown University. It's up-to-date, very clean, well-trained staff. . .and, very convenient to the Georgetown area. The rooms are well-appointed and the surroundings - a campus and residential area - are wonderful. Plus, just a couple blocks away is one of the best restaurants in DC - 1789. There is a restaurant in the hotel that's open for breakfast and lunch. You have to go elsewhere for dinner. As the hotel is connected to student eating areas, there are plenty of easy choices. Subway, Cosi, Starbucks, and many others are adjacent.

“great location, good service, good location - but needs soundproofing” Stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in April 06 on a timeshare exchange and it is our 3rd return visit. Location is excellent - 2 mins from union square and the cable cars/buses/shops. Rooms and facilites are excellent, lovely king beds, good lines and bathroom freebies, nice marble bathroom and high quality fuurnishings. Rooms are huge and generall feature an oversize sofa which is very welcome after a day walking around SF However they do need to soundproof the rooms as like other reviewers we were kept awake at night by the noise - however we moved rooms and that helped a lot. After staying at the Donattello we now know that there is a quiet and a noisy side - we moved to room 1415 which was fine. We found the customer service standard to be very high and the concerige in the club lounge was super and very helpful. We did go to the bar one night but found it very expensive. I would visit again as the location is fantastic and the quality excellent, but next time I would buy ear plugs - however if you stay in the middle of a big city it will be noisy!

“For a convention hotel, this one is good!” Arrival experience: Great! Walked from the train's Grand Station, arriving at the automobile court. Several bellhops immediately inquired if I needed assistance with my two bags (one on wheels, the other tethered to it). Lots of smiles and a warm welcome, with specific instructions on where to find the reception desk. Checkin experience: Neva was so cordial and friendly! She upgraded my room on the spot when I requested it. Room: Typical of large-city hotels, the room was rather small, but more than adequate for my needs. I had a king room on the 37th floor, with a west view. Floor-to-ceiling windows added to the breathtaking view! The bed was incredibly comfortable and loaded with extra pillows. The linens were in excellent condition and spotlessly clean.
