The desk was a bit worn, and the room safe took a while to locate... it's in what used to be the bottom drawer of the nightstand: the drawer has been turned into a door. :) Bathroom: Perfectly clean, but tiny. And I mean tiny. The door barely clears the front of the toilet seat. Single sink vanity with lots of counter space. The tub seemed a bit old, but it was spotless. Curved shower rod with updated shower curtain. Public areas: Clean clean clean! Elevators are "divided" into low-rise and high-rise. Conference center: Confusing! There is an extreme lack of signage and wayfinding - to the point that Marriott employees were actually always on-hand to guide people to the correct rooms/floors. Seems to be a waste of human resources, when appropriate and adequate signs could provide that service! Escalators in the conference area totally skip the 6th floor - and I never found the stairs so getting an elevator was sometimes a challenge, especially during busy times. Lobby bar: Great service, even when it was packed with conventioneers! I highly recommend the chips-n-fondue and the mini Chicago-style hotdogs. Be sure to try their site-made honey beer (there are 100,000 bees on the roof of the hotel). Harvest: Second-floor restaurant. Great food - superb service. Chef's salad was a bit of a disappointment, though - I was expecting something other than iceberg lettuce. The chicken & mushroom sandwich is very tasty. I had the house-made potato chips, but my traveling companions had the garlic cheese fries and said they were quite good as well. Checkout: I requested a late checkout of 1:00 (normal checkout is noon) and was immediately accommodated. When I realized 1:00 would really be pushing it, with my conference schedule, I called to see if I could back it off until 2:00 and was denied. I checked out with three minutes to spare, and stored my bags at the bellstand - as much as that goes against my grain. Departure: Bellhop hailed a cab the instant we walked out the door, telling the driver which airport we wanted, and double-checking that he took credit cards. All-in-all, I'd definitely stay here again. As always, the biggest downside of staying at a Marriott is the ridiculous daily charge for Internet service (here, it's $14.95 for noon-to-noon service).

“Lots of room for improvement” This is a doubletree hotel, but don't expect any cookies, I never saw any.Great bar on the roof, if only they knew how to make a drink. There are bar snacks but be prepared to pay, $9 for french fries? Breakfast is adequate but service is lacking, and the coffee is weak dishwater. Soundproofing in room kept the el sounds to a minimum, but sirens come through loud and clear, as does the slamming of the heavy room doors. Barely adequate hot water in your bathroom. Gigantic sink in that bathroom begs the question, why? For all the raves this place gets there's lots of room for improvemnt.

“Worst Residence Inn Ever” I stay at Marriott Properties all over the country. I've stayed at every type of property as well and never had as bad an experience as I did at this property. The property is old and in serious need of a remodel. As I entered the room, it had a pungent smell. I was only there one night so I decided to just open the windows, turn on the air and get going....I was pressed for time and didn't have the opportunity to deal with room changes. I immediately left for a meeting and returned that evening. After further review, I noticed the carpeting was filthy and had several stains. The kitchen counter was also filthy as was the stove. When I attempted to shower....there was NO HOT WATER. I called the front desk to find out they were aware of the issue, were awaiting parts and did not offer any solution. They also failed to tell me this upon check-in which while wouldn't have solved the problem, I would have had an option to do something about it. While in the cold shower, I noticed mold on the ceilings and on the wallpaper in the bathroom. In general, I would say the property was filthy, the PC in the lobby was slower than my cell phone for pulling my airline web page, the dinner/evening snack is only served 3 days per week....this night had "deli sandwiches.". One of the worst experiences in a Residence Inn I've ever had. I will never stay here again.

“Westin Charlotte - excellent” This is a very nice hotel located in downtown Charlotte. Restaurants and bars are all within three blocks. My room was clean, fresh and the bed was so comfortable. The fitness room is incredible for a hotel - 6 treadmills 5 ellipitcals weights, etc... The only negative is that parking is a bit expensive, but but it is in the same facility.

“Nice,reasonably priced place to stay” This is definitley not a resort, and isn't near anything, so if you stay here make sure you have a car. We checked in late and left early, and this hotel met our needs nicely. It's reasonably priced, and the room was large and clean. The pool and fitness room were adequate. I would stay here again.

“Nothing Special” I stayed here for two nights in late May 2004 while attending a convention. This would really be the only reason you would want to stay here. The location leaves a lot to be desired. It's not really at the airport (as the name suggests), and quite a ways from downtown. Located just off the highway so it can be a bit noisy. Overall, the staff was friendly, and the hotel and rooms were fine. Just another Marriott hotel ploped down on some land as far as I'm concerned. The lobby was very nice, but once again nothing special. But what can you expect from a Marriott? I probably wouldn't stay here again due to the location. There are hotels with more character in better locations in Austin.

“Great Hotel in the District” We recently had a two night stay at the Topaz. This was our first time at this Kimpton property and we were very pleased with both the hotel and the central location near Dupont Circle. The staff are extremely friendly and professional. Rick will take great care of you at happy hour and Donte makes sure everything runs perfectly. The hotel retains its old style charm but has been completely renovated and updated. We had a huge room with plenty of space to spread out. As another review mentioned the separate vanity area was a real plus. The hotel is in a mixed residential/business neighborhood so there is no traffic noise and even though you are very close to the heart of the Dupont Circle shopping area you really feel like you are away from the hustle and bustle. We will definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Good hotel, great location, reasonable price” We stayed here on a two night trip. We came to see a show and do a couple of quick sight seeing things. We could not have been happier with this hotel. It was located right next to the bus terminal where we arrived and you could walk out the side door and cross the street to the hotel. Yes the hotel is next to the probation office and there are a couple of adult stores, but this was never an issue. The staff was very good and we didn't have any of the issues mentioned before about check in or anything. We did stay on the 3rd floor which did make it so we heard the traffic a little, mainly when busses or trucks honked, but if we turned the a/c on we couldn't hear it. If we are ever back I would ask for an upper floor. The rooms aren't huge, but they are prefectly fine. Every amenity that you need, might be tight for 4 people, but for the two of us it was perfect. We ate in the Gotham Bistro for dinner one night due to the heavy rain that evening, though there are a thousand great places to eat within walking distance I was impressed with the quality of food. It was actually pretty good, I was nervous that I would regret not venturing into the rain again. It was nice for a quick, casual dinner. The location of this hotel is perfect, plenty of subway options nearby, more places to eat than you can imagine, theatres are all within walking distance. If I am in NYC again I would stay here, especially if you are coming in by bus, you cannot beat the location.

“nice hotel...expensive garage!” We stayed at the hotel last week for 2 nights, and for 4 people (2 adults, 2 kids) the room was a bit small, and the bathroom was tiny. We did get a nice quiet room up on the 25th floor, which was nice. But be warned - parking is $37 a day! And 4 pm ends the day, so if you stay later than that, you get charged more. Location is near the T, Fenway Park (20 minutes), the Art Museum (20 minutes), Faneuil Hall (short T ride) - and of course the Prudential Center mall is great. Amazingly, they do not show Red Sox games on the tvs in the rooms - you have to go down to the Hotel's Bar (Champions) to see the game. Very nice pool, and the breakfast buffet at $15 per person seemed a good value.

“Everything we were looking for” My family had a very good experience at the Embassy Suites LAX North. It had everything we were looking for: an indoor pool, complimentary breakfast, large suites, a shuttle to LAX and was near the car rental companies. I also requested and received WIFI as part of my rate b/c many other hotels at LAX inc. free WIFI. The hotel has 8 floors and all the rooms are situated around the huge Atrium (see pic). On the main floor of the atrium is where they host Happy Hour and breakfast so every sound carries up to the rooms. However, you would only hear that if you were sleeping on the sofa bed (luckily, my daughter is a heavy sleeper). The king beds have a door to the room so we slept very comfortably. The suites are all renovated, spacious and gorgeous.The bathroom was heavenly. The one annoyance I have with all the hotels (not just this one) is that when I book a room for 3 ppl and that is clearly stated on the reservation, the room only has 2 towels or 2 pillows. This was the case at Embassy also where there were no blankets or pillows for the sofa bed.

“Great Value for Money.” Stayed at this small property last week while I was in New York on Business. I had quickly booked the hotel through HotelTonight 5 minutes before arriving at the property and they hadn't received my data yet. They called HotelTonight and it was all sorted out quickly. Rooms are small but average for New York. The Bathroom is nice, clean and modern. Bed was very comfortable and the room was quiet. Was very surprised by this hotel and will definitely stay here again. The receptionist also gave me a late checkout at no extra charge cause I needed to switch hotels at a later time then default checkout.

“Perfect for the zoo and downtown” We were in town visiting family and the usual tourist attractions. After a night on Penn. Ave. we decided to see the zoo and try out this massive property. Everybody was very friendly and the rooms were standard Marriott (although I turned down an upgrade to stay near my sister and her family). Service in Harry's Bar and Stones Throw were great and the breakfast in the latter hit the spot with the omelette bar and lox and capers. We had a package that included parking otherwise I'd have remained downtown. The National Zoo is a short walk from the hotel as are a number of restaurants on Conn. Ave. We had dinner at Rajaji at the recommendation of the concierge and we were not disappointed - very attentive service and delicious food. Also, you can leave your car in the garage until 5 p.m. after checking out making this perfect for a day at the Zoo. Finally, the Metro red line station is just down the hill from the hotel so the Mall and other attractions are a short subway ride away. I visit the D.C. area every year and I will return to this wonderful property.
“Great rooms and location” Stayed for 3 nights on business and was fortunate to have been upgraded to a 1br suite. Room was great. Very quiet and clean.

“Perfect hotel and perfect stay - it will be our spot in San Diego every time” We stayed here from April 8-13th and I must say this was the perfect place for us. Please note - we had a rental car. Overall - If anyone is looking for a luxury, full service hotel, this is not it. But it is a beautiful motel with pristine rooms, great beds/pillows, clean bathrooms, superb water pressure and a nice pool area. Rooms - Rooms were very clean and a good size and we never felt cramped at all (we had the dual Queen room). The bathroom was exceptionally clean. The tub and tiles were gleaming ! Let me take a quick second to address the supposed thinness of the walls. We had zero problems with noise from neighboring rooms, outside cars, pool noise or TV's. The Lamplighter Inn should be your absolute top choice for a stay in San Diego. Plus the rooms were under $100/night. A++ value ! Staff - Vanessa and the rest of the staff at the hotel were very friendly and helpful. High Speed Internet - Was ok. Slow in the early evening hours when perhaps many other guests were sharing the wireless link. Laundry - Was very convenient to have on premise laundry. We took full advantage of this. Breakfast was great - choice of multiple breads/bagels, muffins, cereals, toast, waffle maker, boiled eggs, juices, milk, coffee and tea. Yes - no yogurt. The neighborhood around the hotel was good - we felt safe but its not anything fancy. Rite Aid and CVS are one block away. Starbucks is close by as are Ralphs and Vons (grocery stores). There are also lots of great ethnic restaurants around the University Area - we recommend the food at Best Thai in particular. Distance to Attractions - Perfect location for rental car. 15 -20mins from Sea World, Zoo and Old Town. About 30-45 minutes from Legoland and the Wildlife Park. 20-25 minutes from La Jolla and Coronado.

“Good location” Stayed here a few times, last time in March 2012. I seem to always get the same room, overlooking 14th St. It's a good room as well. Very large and absolutely packed with anything one needs. I like the Nespresso machine. The hotel is near a large number of restaurants and bars, so it's easy to step out after a day of meetings. Also, near most of the businesses in the downtown area. Staff are usually very cheerful and glad to help with anything. This is my go to place in Denver.

“Nice hotel for a night or two, great location” This hotel is next to my office in DC so I decided to stay there for some overnight business. Its a great location for business travel as it is in the heart of the NW business district, and also a good tourist hotel because its near the whitehouse, washington monument, et.cet. I thought it was expensive, but most decent hotels in DC are expensive. However, what helped defray some of the expense was the complimentary evening snack (which for most would be dinner) and a great morning buffett breakfast. This is not high end luxary food, but certainly sufficient. There is no hotel restaurant or bar which is a minus, but within a block or two there are dozens to choose from. There is also also a 24 hour CVS store right next door which is convenient. The room was HUGE and included a full kitchen. Not sure if I was upgraded, but I suspect I was. Overall, a nice experience.

“Great choice in the Upper West” Stayed at this hotel in a weekend last June. I was specifically looking for a place in the Upper West and it took a lot of online searches to find this one! I must say I was very pleased with my choice. I got a Superior Room with a view directly from the hotel website - there are good discounts for early booking. I got a room in one of the top floors, and was really surprised with the large balcony with table and chairs! And yes, there was a good view of the surroundings. The room itself had a very decent size for NYC standards, was rather clean and comfortable. The bathroom was also of good size and had a great walk-in power shower. Unfortunately, there was no private safe in the roo. The only negative point was that (at least that specific Saturday I arived) they were really late in releasing some rooms. Though check-in was supposed to be at 3 p.m., I only got my room after 4. There were other guests in the same situation. As a cpensation, they offered me free breakfast during my stay. The location is just perfect, two blocks away from the tube (79th & Broadway), there's an excellent mini market across the street with top choice of groceries, and plenty of great eateries nearby. The everyday brunches at Cafe Lalo are a must go! I would definitely recommend this hotel and would come back here in my next trip to New York. There aren't many tourists in this area, so you really get a feel of true NY here.

“Clean borning hotel on the edge of downtown” My husband and I landed at this hotel through a Priceline deal. Price was about $200 and it was clean, but very boring hotel. Even the work-out area was fine, but nothing special. Rooms were large (had to pay for wi-fi). Bar had a scene during certain hours of the day but we didn't eat or drink in the hotel and lobby wasn't conducive to hanging out. The hotel was on the edge of a rough area and it was often deserted walking back at night. Wish we'd stay in a boutique hotel that added more San Fran charm to our trip.

“Graduation Celebration in San Diego” My daughter graduated from the New School of Architecture and Design in San Diego, so we traveled from Florida to San Diego and stayed at the Ocean Park Inn for 3 nights. We had a lovely room with a balcony overlooking the ocean and pier. We enjoyed the fabulous location within walking distance to many restaurants, pubs and stores. We enjoyed the beautiful pool and hot tub with view of the ocean. Complimentary continental breakfast was very nice with bagels, waffles, cereals, pastries, fruit, coffee and juices. Free Wifi was a very nice addition to the hotel amenities. I loved the PB Shore Club just a block away for great Tacos, Cocktails and ocean view, we ate there twice! I would highly recommend this hotel. The front desk staff were always helpful and very friendly, it's nice to come into the lobby and always being greeted by a friendly face. The lobby has a large awesome Aquarium full of beautiful saltwater fish, I loved watching the clown fish swimming around the coral and sea foliage. Our stay at the Ocean Park Inn was just perfect.

“Less than remarkable, better than basic.” With the Hyatt name on this property, I expected more. The Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Center is in a somewhat remote area, surrounded by office buildings with a number of restaurants blocks from the hotel, but very little shopping and/or nightlife. Our rather small hotel room was seriously outdated (with what appeared to be tacky "faux bamboo adhesive paper" decorating the bathroom vanity, the nightstand wall and the dresser drawers); upon walking in the room for the first, it looked much more like a budget motel than a Hyatt. We purchased the "Perks" package, which afforded us a daily $20 allowance in the hotel restaurant/bar, and a choice of a daily snack, bottle of wine or wifi or parking, which was nice. But the restaurant was horribly overpriced, with painfully slow service-- and it wasn't even open for dinner on Saturday night. The conference facilities for this property are appealing, but the cabfare to and from the airport is hefty and the hotel amenities did not compensate in any way. The concierge staff was helpful (especially Calvin!) and the shuttle service (free within 5 miles) was appreciated, however.

“Average Room in Large Conference Facility” This hotel is huge and much more of a conference facility than a standard hotel. We stayed on 10TH floor (concierge level) in the new(er) building. The room was at the very end of the corridor. As soon as we opened the door to our room we were struck by a very strong odor that smelled like car exhaust. We contacted the front desk and they immediately assigned us a new room. The second room seemed fine, if a bit small. However on our first night the smoke alarm directly over the bed went off at 4 am. After being shocked awake, we had to clamor around to locate, reach, and finally remove the alarm to get it to stop. We didn’t report it right away as we didn’t want repair people in the room at that hour. After trying unsuccessfully to fall back to sleep we decided to turn on TV to watch early morning news. The TV did not work! Getting more frustrated by the minute, we picked up the phone by the bed to report the problems, and the phone did not work!! Not a good start to our stay. I will say that once we spoke with someone at the desk they were very responsive and an engineer came to the room very quickly and fixed the fire alarm & TV. They thought they fixed the phone, but it never did work. That wasn’t a problem, since there was another phone in the room. Overall the overnight rooms are a bit tired but clean. The bath is small. There was some mold on shower curtain, but I left a note and housekeeping replaced it. The bath towels were pretty thin, but they did leave a sufficient supply of bath linens each day. Since this is a very large conference hotel, I am surprised there was no makeup mirror. Wireless was OK, but I did have to sign on several times even though we had signed up to have wireless for our whole stay. Now for the good. The bed was comfortable and double sheeted (although blanket was extremely thin). Room also had a small refrigerator. The breakfast in the concierge lounge was excellent with lots of healthy options including fresh fruit (with various types of berries, melon, oranges, etc), cold cereals, yogurt, oatmeal, hot dish was scrambled eggs. Was very happy one morning to see smoked salmon complete with capers, chopped onions and tomatoes. Cookies and cold drinks were available all day. Appreciated that evening snack was also fresh and healthy: veggies, hummus, tzatziki dip, edamame bean salad, and lentil salad. Concierge lounge has computer & printer that we used (free) for boarding passes; I understand the business center in the lobby charges even to print boarding passes. Housekeeping did a good job and both housekeeping and concierge lounge staff were unfailingly cordial and polite. The food in the bar/lounge off the lobby was surprisingly good and very reasonably priced. We ate there twice for lunch and it was excellent. Another positive was that although the hotel is huge, we never waited more than a minute or two for the elevator. Overall, the rooms are average, and a bit smaller than most Marriotts at which we’ve stayed. Both the service and the location are excellent. The hotel is very close to zoo, abuts a nice residential area and is within walking distance of restaurants and parks. The metro stop is right in front of the hotel and the metro system is very easy to navigate. The hotel is so large that there are always taxi cabs available right at the hotel entrance. I would probably stay again, but only if I was attending a conference at the hotel, and could stay again on concierge floor.

“A great value!” I just stayed here one night on business. I found the staff to be very friendly and helpful. The room decor was different, but attractive, and the bed was very comfortable. The elevators required a key for access to the floors, so that bit of security was nice. The only drawback was that the exercise room was extremely small. Get there on an off-peak time or you won't get a machine. The good news is that it is open 24 hours.

“Great location - expensive parking!” Stayed at the Doubletree one night before an early flight. The hotel property is large with a tower plus several smaller buildings. The public spaces are nicely decorated & very comfortable. I stayed in the tower --- a room with two queen beds & a balcony. Room was very clean, bed was comfortable and I loved that it was quiet! Parking is expensive $16/night for self parking (valet $20) plus internet was $14.95. Two well equipped fitness centers plus a large outdoor pool. Hotel has great restaurants & a bar. Plus several restaurants/fast food in walking distance (Subway/Jack in the Box/Taco Bell/Thai Food)

“Can't swing a hamster” New York's Hudson Hotel on West 58th Street is part of Ian Shrager's hotel empire -- very trendy, very lively crowd of guests and visitors to the bar -- but it is not all peaches and cream. Everything in the hotel is dark -- the public areas, the corridors on guest floors, and the walls of guest rooms. Perhaps the word 'room' is not accurate -- chamber is more descriptive. Guest chambers are not large enough to swing the proverbial cat; in fact swinging a hamster might be a challenge. There's a chair and a desk/table and micro tables beside the bed -- but no other furniture (there's no space), no carpeting, no place for storing clothes, barely space for luggage in the one closet per room (whoops! -- chamber). The bathroom is so tight that when a person washes their hands, the toilet paper roll gets wet. The bed is very good, linens and all -- especially for people less than 5 ft. 9 inches tall. Moving from the bed to anyplace else means a careful walk in the very narrow space between the bed and the wall. One gets the feeling the hotel was not designed for overnight guests, but rather for folks who rent rooms by the hour.

“Good Hampton” Stayed here one night on business. This is an older Hampton - I have stayed here a few times before over the years. It is okay, the rooms are a little smaller than the newer Hamptons, but everything was clean and worked well. The Internet is hardwired, but works fine. Breakfast is typical Hampton - so no surprises. This one is a little hard to get to while IH 410 is under construction. If driving east on 410, exit Callahan, turn left on Callahan, then right on Manitou - it's a little ways down. This is a lot easier and quicker than going down to the next intersection and making the turnaround and coming back.

“Pretty good for a motel” This is more of a motel I guess since the rooms face outward. The rooms are pretty nice though: separate sitting area with couch and chair, kitchen and king bed. Initial customer service impression was extremely bad. The woman at the front desk looked very annoyed when I seemed to interrupt her from looking for something in the phone book. Not a friendly or courteous greeting. Then, when she saw I booked through priceline, it got even worse. She charged me a $20 early check in fee only reserved for third party bookings. Check in was 3:00pm and I checked in at 1:15pm. Parking lot remained less than half full my entire stay so I doubt anyone was inconvenienced. Anyways, a gentleman with a pony tail working the front desk on other days more than made up for her. If you are staying in town for an extended period this would be a good motel. Complimentary "continental" breakfast.

“Some positives, some negatives” Positives: -- really good AAA rate for downtown -- excellent location, right next to red line train and close to restaurants, bars, N. Michigan Ave. -- very friendly, helpful staff -- nice rooms with comfortable beds Negatives; -- be careful with reservations, our rate did not have a guarantee on # beds or rooms. Desk said only king beds initially but fortunately was able to get 2 beds -- Some floors have both smoking and non-smoking rooms. Hallway smelled like smoke. -- Elevators were backed up at times -- Lobby, elevators and hallways were warm and humid -- Internet connections never worked

“in pieno centro - consiglio” sicuramente ottimo per la sua posizione centralissima in San Francisco da dove si puo girare a piedi gran parte della città. camere molto spaziose e tranquille - pulizia approssimativa (purtroppo un leitmotiv negli westin negli stati uniti). tanta confusione nella hall e nel bar. personale molto disponibile. garage molto comodo con servizio valet

“Always chic and hip with great service (except in lounge bar)” Stayed here many times and it is definitely the hipster spot in NYC. Views from rooms are incredible given over all the bright lights big city in Times Square. They cool lounge with great ambient lighting on the 7th floor, the entrance on ground level with the water coursing through the floor and ceiling, Blue Fin restaurant, Whiskey Bar....place is always rocking. Rooms are nice and crisp with trendy furnishings. I am Platinum SPG so can't comment what the room size is for standard since they always seem to give me some sort of upgrade so the rooms are not huge but good size for NY. Service is great except in lounge bar they are always non-observant and kind of float around expecting a decent tip b/c the price of the cocktails is staggering. Don't expect to be quickly served and you will go thirsty. Cocktail waitresses are useless if you are not a big party.

“Old Style New York” We stayed at the Carlyle because we were tired of the hustle and bustle of Midtown and were looking for something a bit quieter. The Carlyle certainly fit that bill. It was nice to return from a Broadway show or dinner and get away from the mobs of people. The residential streets of the Upper East Side were also a welcome change. Speaking of residential, the Carlyle itself is full of residents (perhaps 20 – 25% of the rooms are permanent residents). This fact makes the hotel feel more like a residence than a hotel. However, don’t be surprised when the elevator opens and a dog or two walks out! Speaking of the elevators, they are run by friendly white gloved operators. Stop by the lounge area after a show and be sure and try out the 20 layer crepe cake!

“No surprises!” Love this hotel. No surprises. Important while in NYC to be able to come "home" to the Courtyard Marriott and know what to expect each evening. Rooms are large for NYC; excellent location with EVERYTHING near by. Staff wonderful. Clean, clean, clean. Breakfast buffet was very good with a great staff. Very pleasant concierge. Next door is a drugstore. Houston's and PJ Clarke's nearby for food. Great for a business stay....free internet and wifi in loung area on 14.

“600 bucks a night...” ... And they stil want you to pay $14.99 for 24 hours of Internet? This smacks of cheapness and just gives the impression that you're being ripped off. It costs fifty bucks A MONTH to get it in my home. That's a 900 percent markup. Aside from that, it's a jolly nice hotel and I'd reccomend it to anyone with a company credit card or money to burn

“Overall--a nice experience” We booked the Hilton Times Square in large part due to the positive reviews on TA, plus we are also Hilton Honors members. I called the hotel directly to make the reservation and requested a room on a high floor and also booked a standard room. After all, the deluxe room is only 20 square feet larger and cost about $20/night extra. When we arrived at the hotel, there was a long line to check in and only 2 clerks working at the desk, so we waited 30 minutes. Upon check-in, we learned that we had been upgraded to a deluxe room and that our request for a high floor was honored. We got a room on the 37th floor that had a great view of the Empire State Building. Overall, the hotel rooms are nicely decorated with blond wood furnishings. Positive things about this hotel -- every night we had turn down service. Not only were the bedcovers turned down but the maid left two bottles of water and two pieces of chocolate. The rooms were kept very clean. All the staff we encountered, were friendly and helpful. During the week, you get a complimentary copy of "USA Today". The closet was surprisingly spacious. The downside---there is only one very small trash can in the room, in the bathroom. By small, I mean that once you throw out those two empty water bottles, there is little room for anything else. As for trash removal--sometimes the maid was a bit over zealous. One day, we left our copy of "USA Today" on the desk and the maid threw it out. Other days, the maid wouldn't take old newspapers we left next to the trash can--go figure! The shower pressure wasn't the best but that is often the case in hotels anyway. The hotel lobby is on the 21st floor. You enter at street level on either 41st or 42nd Street and then take an elevator to the lobby. Once in the lobby, you take yet another elevator to your room. Just note that it is easy to miss the entrance on 42nd Street due to the fact that the street is cluttered with large, bright signs, thus it is easy to bypass the entrance. Overall, we would stay here again. I think the positives outweigh the negatives.

“LOVE TIME” I have stayed at the Time on various occations. I love the themed rooms and probably have stayed in all colors. Each time, that I have visited, the staff has been amazing. On one or two occasions I have brought my son. He was only a few months old less than (6) when we first visited. The staff was very accomadating. I moved some items in the mini bar to Jam bottles in and the front desk immediately took the charges off of my bill when I explained. I love the location and the high priced bar and rest inside. The rooms are small but many rooms in NYC are and quite honestly the hotel room is as big as some city apartments that are $1200 a month. If people think this room is extreme and small you should see LOEWS Universal Studios. I love this place and would stay here again and again.

“very nice hotel” The Millenium Bostonian is a very nice hotel. Very nicely located by Queen's market, car rentals aren't far away. Lots of restaurants and shops in the area. The room was nice and big, so was the bathroom. Big windows. Very friendly staff. The only thing i didn't really enjoy was the lack of a traditional breakfast, everything was a la carte and the waiting time was rather long. I would have liked to have some traditional waffles/pancakes etc on the breakfast menu.

“Great location and staff” Just visited for 4 nights. I must brag a little on this hotel. Great location, great staff, and great perks. 9 out of 10 staff members were excellent and really tried to make you feel like you were at a top notch hotel. (we won't talk about the 10th since no hotel can be perfect.) The hotel is in the perfect location to walk to Mag mile, restaurants, all of the theaters, and Navy Pier. The breakfast was just enough to carry us over until lunch. The only tiny and I do mean tiny thing that I will mention (which is no reflection on the hotel) the alley directly behind the hotel is filled with dumpsters (30-I counted) and for some reason they choose 5:30am to dump them so you will wake up early if you are a light sleeper but I would stay here again in a heartbeat. Well done!

“Charming!” This is an Art Deco boutique hotel surrounded by Embassies in the DuPont Circle area. I walked easily from Metro with my suitcase. The lobby is a spectacular marble mosaic. There is a bright breakfast restaurant and food is also served in the bar / grill off the lobby. The rooms are a mix of modern conveniences and vintage details - my small room had a desk fridge, Keurig, microwave, and a high top table and stools with a beautiful view of New Hampshire Ave. One of my bugaboos, the room had plenty of lighting and electrical outlets and free internet. The bath was tiny, with little counter top space, but a generous shower. I was with a group and the rooms were quite varied, some very large with seating areas and kitchen alcoves. The staff were great – very attentive. My single bed room was a double bed, fine for just me. The hotel has an arrangement with the Washington Athletic Club, so no fitness room in the building, but walks viewing the architecture and gardens in the neighborhood are stunning. I could only find one vending machine and it was in the basement. This was a great respite from cookie cutter hotels.

“Hotel in need of attention” Located in Midtown - I stayed at the Flatotel for one night and although the hotel has the basics covered; good location, nicely apportioned rooms and bathrooms, and helpful staff. The property left me wanting. The hotel rooms had a musty smell. Initially I thought it might be just my room, but nearly everyone on my team mentioned the same thing at dinner and a couple of my colleagues actually mentioned the smell gave them headaches. The hotel has a trendy appeal in the lobby but the design (if you care about that sort of thing) falls flat in their fairly spacious guest rooms. White walls meant to appear minimialist instead seemed institutional. The bulky television circa late 90s was an anachronism in what was meant to be a hip, modern room. Adding to my frustrations was a sketchy internet connection that seemed to move at the speed of dial-up. However, probably the most frustrating part of my stay was spent waiting for elevators to take me to the hotel lobby. I was on a very high floor and it regularly took me about 10 minutes waiting for the elevator. If I'd been on a lower floor I would have simply opted for the stairs, but walking down 20+ flights was not an viable option.

“Grandpa and Grandma and 6 year old grand daughter” We have stayed at this Fairfield Inn when it was new several years ago and a couple of times since. It has been updated and well maintained. It is an easy on and off the Interstate to get to the attractions downtown etc. one of the reasons we stay here. The room was always clean. We were there during the week not a weekend. It was being used but several junior girls’ softball teams for a tournament. Breakfast was always a questionable situation. Even with the large area we ended up taking our breakfast to our room. The breakfast hour was under staffed. The person running the front desk was also taking care of the breakfast area. In fact the front desk always seemed under staffed but always helpful. The pool is a typical small Fairfield Inn inside pool. We tried to use it several times but as soon as the girls return from their games we gave up. We will more than likely come back here again if it meets our needs for location.

“Worked for me” Upon entering the hotel, I was promptly greeted. The lobby area was clean, and there were fresh cookies for guests. When I got to my room, I received a phone call making sure everything was okay and letting me know to contact the front desk if I needed anything. The room was clean, but the towels were a little dingy. I thought one was dirty, but it was just stained. The air conditioning was also very loud, but I was pretty tired every night, so it didn’t bother me too much. They did have breakfast every morning, which I did not get to try, but I heard it was pretty good. There’s also a Wendy’s right next door. About 5-10 minutes away, there’s a shopping center with tons of good restaurants. Overall, my stay was pleasant.

“Hyatt Olive 8 did not disappoint!!” Lets begin by stating this was a 4 day trip to the Pacific Northwest and a well thought out stay. Location is 3 blocks from the Westlake light rail exit at 5th and Pine thus just a 3 block stroll to the hotel. The building exterior is new and hip and the building itself is huge, though only the lower floors of the building are the hotel as the higher floors are residential condominiums. Check in was painless and initially we were given a Deluxe King room with a terrible view on the 17th floor. Again this was not the staff's fault as I checked in early and nothing was clean at the time. I immediately went downstairs and spoke to a gentleman by the name of Chris who helped us and gave us an option to be upgraded to a Luxury King suite later in the day. Chris handled all the baggage delivery and key delivery for us prior to our return from a day out in the city. When we walked into our suite later in the day we were definitely floored as the amount of windows allowing natural light as well as the city lights was amazing. Bedroom had a king size bed as well as two chairs and two separate closets. The room was separated from the living area by a frosted glass sliding door with separate temperature controls between rooms. Bathrooms had a rainfall shower head and allowed easy use of the water temperature controls from the outside of the closed shower. Great design as a lot of hotels make you get in the shower to set your controls. The living room along with it's sofa and chair were a great place to relax and sit back and see the city. The work desk was perfect as it allowed you to setup shop for the 4 days and forget about your computer being out. The internet was fast and very easy to connect. Urbane was not as great as expected but it may have been due to the steak being very much undercooked when medium well was requested. It was corrected immediately but it kind of ruined the mood. Drinks at the bar were wonderful and great tasting. All in all I can definitely recommend this hotel with the highest of grades due to the room experience, location, decor and great customer service by the bellman Chris. One last note, we had 4 days of sunshine and wonderfully crisp weather.

“Great place to stay” I recently stayed at this hotel for a conference that was taking place at the Moscone Center and surrounding hotels. This property was centrally located to the center and other venues. I was worried because I did not rent a car and thought I might have difficulty accessing the city. I did not find this the case at all. The hotel's location really is central and it was easy to walk to most places. If not a quick cab ride was in order with no hassles. The hotel itself is well kept and the customer service excellent. I found all the employees to be pleasant and I enjoyed the rooms immensely. They were outside of the standard Marriott/Hyatt/Hilton decor and provided a different feel to it. The rooms were clean and well maintained. I have no complaints at all and really felt welcome at this property. Highly recommend a stay here whether for a business trip, family, or couples vacation.

“Nothing but great things to say!” My husband and I stayed for my birthday this past weekend and loved everything about our stay! The hotel itself is beautiful as always, nice clean rooms, and an amazing hotel staff. Our bell boy Joe F. was fantastic. He was not only helpful but did a wonderful job at making us feel very welcomed and we genuinely enjoyed our interaction with him! The concierge representatives Gino and Sandra were outstanding. They went above and beyond to work with my husband to make my b-day extra special. I walked into the room with flowers, balloons, wine, and chocolate covered strawberries waiting for me! I was surprised and really made a great stay turn into the best stay I've ever had at a hotel! Thank you Joe F., Gino, and Sandra for taking the time to make our stay a memorable one! Overall everyone a the hotel was very nice and helpful. Can't wait until our next visit!

“so-so location” The location is not that great. Most people think that just because it is located near some historic sites makes this hotel an ideal place to stay. I must warn people that this hotel is located across from a fire station. So be prepare to hear sirens in the middle of the night if you have a room facing the street. To avoid such noise disturbances, get a room facing inward. It wouldn’t matter if it was facing the street or inwards because it is a low rise building with no views from all sides. Though rooms facing the street has more sunlight which is of no benefit if you just need a bed to sleep. The historic sites nearby closes by 4 or 5pm so there is nothing nearby to do at night. There are not that many good restaurants nearby either and the area is deserted at night. The rooms and furnishing are the same as other Holiday Inns so there is not much to comment on. The hotel did go through a renovation but not everything was renovated. The sink is new but the bathtub is old. The TV is not flat screen but the wi-fi is free. Be prepare to wait to check in and out. The women at the reception desk needs more training but the men seems to know what they are doing.

“Great Location and typical Hampton standards” After reading a very lengthy review about this hotel, we booked it anyway. Why? Because experience with the Hilton chain of hotels has taught me that when there is a problem and I have an unsatisfactory stay and report the stay, I get my money back for that night. This Hampton is well located for conventions, sports events, and trendy night spots. We were there for our son's 35th birthday party at a nearby nightspot. The property was clean. The staff were friendly. The room was typical Hampton with the comfortable beds and neutral decor. I expect no less with the Hampton chain. Breakfast was also typical and I did find that I could stay on my WW points easily with the selection. If you don't like what's being served at a free buffet in a hotel you can go elsewhere and pay. The valet parking was $21 with in and out access. Cheaper than most of the hotels in the area. We were on the top floor and there were no issues with noise. Granted, the 2nd floor to this Hampton is unusual with all the amenities grouped onto this floor; pool, breakfast area, business center, fireplace lounge, etc. But, as I will repeat again, Hampton has a 100% refund policy that I have taken advantage of a few times in the last 10 years.

“Eine echte Überraschung” war eigentlich von den holiday inn hotels nie wirklich überzeugt bzw. hatte schon einige male schlechte erfahrungen gemacht. dies hat sich bei diesem hotel allerdings wirklich geändert. schon der check in war sehr rasch und das personal extrem lustig und scherzte mit uns auf eine wirklich witzige weise. wir bekamen auch ein welcome geschenk vom hotel. die zimmer sind zwar etwas in die jahre gekommen allerdings sehr groß und sauber gehalten. man kann für dieses preis/leistungsverhältnis wirklich nichts beanstanden. die lage perfekt und sicher (gleich im angrenzenden gay village) und mit vielen netten lokalen und restaurants umgeben. die stadt lässt sich von diesem hotel wirklich perfekt erkunden. das parken ist eine wirklich spanende erfahrung - aber ging alles gut !!! das hotel ist auch bei gruppen sehr beliebt. das frühstück war den doch wieder holiday inn standard aber ganz okay. für einen kurzen aufenthalt in der stadt kann mann diese hotel ohne weiteres buchen !!!

“Great place to stay; but watch cost of reservation changes” Great place to stay. Reports of highway noise in other reviews are exaggerated. I am sensitive to such things and it was simply not an issue. We walked practically everywhere from this great location. Don't let the proximity to interstate 5 throw you. Pedestrian traffic is beautifully accommodated, and protected, in Seattle and there is a walkway/sidewalk straight down Pike. Coming back will be mostly uphill so it is a little harder if you aren't in shape. The only problem we had was a need to leave, unexpectedly, a day early. Our room rate for our entire stay was impacted. Never had a Hilton brand do this to me before. :( Overall though good suite hotel. Clean. Can't beat location.

“Excellent location” Opted for an overnight at the Hyatt during a business trip to DC. Regular rates are very expensive but I landed a fair price on a last minute hotels.com offer. Rooms facing the street on lower floors (6 for me) were indeed noisy, but the rate was such a good value I did not mind. Tried the "Cure" lounge while meeting with 2 colleagues. We ordered coffee and it was sooo cold it had to be sent back. Lots of dining options in the area, so we did not try other hotel facilities.

“Perfectly Priced, Located, and Fab Service” My husband and I and our teenaged daughter spent the weekend for my son's SD university Parents' Weekend. We ended up spending more time at this fun boutique hotel than on campus, and my son opted to stay with us in our hotel. The hotel is chic, the service wonderful, the food from both room service and the restaurant was first rate, and the location right next to Petco Park and one block from the main drag was perfect. The 4th floor rooftop pool was so nice - away from the noise of the street, but enough going on (there's also full screen TVs in the rooftop bar to watch the Giants win the pennant) Our room actually faced the bar/pool which made me a tad anxious as to noise, but we heard nothing whatsoever. We walked everywhere, and had rented a Prius, so the overnight parking fee was cut in half (take note if you're staying - the parking rate is $35 which seems like a lot but all the downtown hotels charge the same - there is a public lot across the street for $20, but with the hybrid car rate of $17.50 we had somewhat of a bargain) Also to note: dogs are welcome - there were 5 or 6 staying, but we rarely saw them, and were glad when we did. (Heard no barking.) Something else to note about downtown San Diego in general: LOTS of homeless around (and I'm from San Francisco!) but it seems they mainly hang out down near Broadway - very sad.

“Decent location, just not a decent part of town. Huge Loud Gay Bar next door.” Good price, average room and friendly staff. Nice firm soft bed and was happy with good air conditioning. Internet was very slow. The location is decent but I wouldn't walk outside at night. Too many homeless and beggars everywhere. The Gar Bar next door was too loud. Few restaurants a few doors down and a store. I'm not sure if I would stay here again.

“Luxury With a Low-Key Feel” My husband and I just spent a weekend at The Peninsula after wanting to stay there for some time, and we were very favorably impressed. Having stayed at most of the top NYC hotels, we liked the Peninsula's elegance without glitz and its genuinely friendly staff. Some other hotels seem to have the philosophy that a snobbish attitude on the part of the staff lends an air of exclusivity; that just puts us off. Every single employee we encountered during our stay had a smile and a pleasant greeting, whether a maitre d' or a housekeeper. We always felt welcome and appreciated. The public areas were elegant, but a little bit dim due to the dark wood and olive green carpeting. Because the lobby areas are on multiple levels and the ceilings are somewhat low in some spots, the feel was intimate rather than awe-inspiring. It almost felt more like a private club than a hotel, with different places to sit and relax. Our room was upgraded to a junior suite which was lovely and very quiet despite facing onto Fifth Avenue. We had a drink in the rooftop terrace bar but didn't have a chance to enjoy the outdoor lounge area as it started to rain as soon as we arrived. Service was quick and polite, which we were glad of as we were in a hurry to get to our restaurant for dinner. Breakfast was very nice, though with the incredibly high prices that seem to be the norm in New York these days despite the economy. A guest at a neighboring table actually had her unfinished bagel and lox packaged to go, and at $32 or so, I don't blame her. In all, we were very happy with the Peninsula and look forward to staying here again.

“Some Issues but a Beautiful Facility” I have been staying at The Drake for right at 20 years and always rated it well. The hotel is just an elegant gem that continues to hold its' own after all of the years. Even though it is not convenient to the business area I continue to stay here. Two issues: The internet is simply awful. For a business hotel charging $13 a night for slower than dial-up internet it is a crime. I gave up trying to download business documents. Second issue...they lost my FedEx package. I was not notified of the arrival and 6 hour later I went down looking for it. It took them almost an hour to find the package. The day manager was polite and professional but she needs to whip her front desk and receiving staff in line. One sad note. The wonderful Cape Cod Restaurant (where i first ate nearly 50 years ago) was just empty. It is clearly struggling in this economy. The food was great but in the two hours I was in the restaurant during prime dinner time they served just two tables.

“Great location-don't spend money on upgraded corner room.” We made the mistake of booking our trip during UN and Fashion week so all of the hotels were charging 200% more than the average rates, which was frustrating but i guess that is the name of the game. At any rate, we paid a bit more for a corner room to overlook Times Square. Looking back, probably not worth it. Its a small window in the corner of the room so its not like you can wake up and pull back the curtains to the extraordinary view. but the corner rooms do offer a bit more walking space with separate wardrobe, mini bar, etc. room in addition to the bed and bath rooms. If you are going to see plays, shop, etc. its perfect! just step outside and go! Particularly, if you are wanting discounted Broadway tix-the TIX booth is underneath the hotel. We really enjoyed being so close, especially after a good meal or late show and you want to walk and see the lights but not so far!! An extra recommendation-you mut get a drink or pre-show appetizers at the famed "The View" which is a revolving roof top bar/restaurant. very romantic!!

“What a great property” Stayed in the "5th Avenue Loft Building", which was adjacent to the main building through the Terrace level. Although it took a while to find the room through the many passageways, the signage was adequate. The loft building features many unique room shapes, which are accessed through a sigle elevator off of the "The Terrace" which is a large outdoor seating patio area. The rooms from the loft buildings are accessed through partially outdoor hallways which then lead to indoor hallways for the remainder of the long walk to the room. The room was loft like, with large windows and very high ceilings, I would say around 14 feet or so. My room overlooked the Hard Rock hotel and the main entry arch for the Gas Lamp District. The convention center is across the street and the light rail (Orange Line) is directly in front of the hotel. I had no issues with noise or train horns blowing as other readers have commented on. The room was attractive. There was one king berd, a chair, desk, and avery large flat screen television. What was a shock was the FREE in-room Internet. Now we're talking. It's about time large chains started offering what small chains have been doing for years, although I feel this property is unique within the Hilton brand. The lighting in the room was pleasant and offered many choices, including pot lights on a dimmer above the bed. The bathroom also featured pot lights that were controlled by a dimmer. The bathroom was larger than any other I have seen in a standard hotel room. This would appear to be the trend moving forward as clients are demanding larger and larger bathrooms than in the past. This place delivers to those who demand large washrooms. The floor, although tiled, was never cold. The lights and heating system are controlled by motion sensor. This means taht the heat/air conditioning will not work unless movement is sensed. The room may be a little warm upon entry, but will cool down quick once the system senses movement. The bathroom lights were the same, but if this is conserve energy, it was frustrating that the vanity lights could not be shut off manually. This seemed to waste more energy than it saves. The in-room coffee system was impressive at first glance, but delivered a regular average cup of coffee. The bed was comfortable. There is a window that opens. A robe (black) is provided in the front cupboard, which also had an small safe. The Crabtree and Evelyn bath products included mouthwash and body gel. The towels were plush and plentiful. Overall the property was beautiful, modern and stylish. Would stay again.

“Good location - nice hotel” Hotel has great location - close to mall and restaurants. The steakhouse onsite was actually pretty good. Service was a little slow, but food was delicious. The room I had was non-smoking but it smelled like an ashtray. Another person who traveled with me had same problem. I could have switched rooms but was only there for a night so I put up with it. Bed was comfy - room was clean. Bathrooms are kind of small for the size of the suites. Free cocktails are nice, as is free breakfast. But they don't offer free wireless, which is odd these days. Overall was a fine stay.

“Exceptional Service + Uncomfortable Room = Average” I had a job interview scheduled near the area that is why I reserved a room at the Courtyard (I don't live in the area). I was hesitatnt to reserve a room at first as it was a bit pricey $259 for one night + $45 parking, plus I knew I would be arriving late (11 p.m.) with a checkout time at noon. So I didn't know if it was worth it or not. Still, I didn't want to be pressured going to the interview so I still made the reservation. Plus, I was hoping they would let me have a late checkout. Upon arrival I drove my car towards the entrance and there was only one person doing the parking. There were two cars ahead of me. He was prompt and courteous though. Upon entering I was assisted by a very nice clerk who checked me in. I requested if I can have a later checkout but he said the hotel was fully booked the next day that is why they can't do that. However, to call in the morning to check. I did call in the morning and the clerk, Maria, said that the latest I can checkout is at 2 p.m. I was surprised they granted it considering they said no twice previously. So that was good. My interview was at 4 p.m. so I wanted to checkout at 3:30 p.m. Instead, I had to wait in the lobby area for an hour and a half. However, when it came to parking they charged $10 for every three hours over the expiration of the one day parking. I started feeling I was being drained of funds for this "darn" stay. Yes, I was feeling frustrated (due to cost) and nervous (due to the interview) the whole time I was there. Now the room - the room was very nice, clean, and well-decorated. However, the air conditioner was awful! I sleep with the a/c on. This a/c turned on and made a subtle sound but no adequate air/circulation came out. I tried opening the window but it was glued shut. Unfortunately, I did not have a good night's sleep (the night before my interview). I kept waking up in the middle of the night hoping the a/c would kick in. Unfortunately, I didn't report this to the hotel services. I also didn't like the fact that the bed was a bit uncomfortable. The next morning I went downstairs for their breakfast buffet. I was pleasantly surprised how nice it really was. The food selection (yes, you can have your eggs cooked the way you want - even egg whites) was awesome! The waitress, Regina, was so friendly and helpful that it made my stay there worth while. After that I went to the exercise room and worked out for a good hour using their treadmill, bike and weights. It was nice. It's right next to the pool on the second floor. I also used their computer (you are limited for 15 minutes). It was somewhat slow and you can't open more than one window it seems. Overall, my stay was an "average" one. The staff was phenomenal, but the comfort, price, and the fact I didn't have the late checkout I wanted made my rating at average. Would I stay here again? Perhaps if the room rates go down and if I get a room where the a/c is working appropriately. We'll see.

“Run Down in a short time” We stayed here twice before and were very pleased with this hotel and recommended it to everyone. The staff at this hotel is the best one could ask for, but the owners have really let things slide. Parking is creepy even though it is gated. Elevators are scary. Don't even think about going downstairs during late evening. Creepy people and filthy floors greeted me. Didn't feel safe at all. This will be our last stay at this location.

“Only stay here if you HAVE to be downtown” The hotel is located a few blocks away from Skid Row in downtown LA. The hotel itself tries to be very 'LA hip'. There is a salon, a bar, a restaurant, a rooftop pool. It might be a nice place to stay if you want to take someone for an authentic "LA hipster night out". I would recommend this hotel to someone IF they HAD to be downtown for some reason or they wanted a hotel where they could party with wanna be socialites. The beds are super comfy, the TV works and the bathrooms and big and clean. But the decor is kinda gross and it has an IKEA feel to it. PROS: - Comfy beds - Good food at the restaurant - Nightlife hot spot for LA Hipsters CONS: - Location is horrible - You have to valet your car - Room decor needs an upgrade - Expensive

“Just OK in the Back Bay” I've stayed at most of the hotels in Boston's back bay for business: the Westin (a total dump), the Marriott (poor quality), Copley Square Hotel (OK), Fairmont Copley Plaza (faded glory) and the CharlesMark (nice but very small rooms). This place, like its neighbors, is just OK. The rooms are clean and perfectly acceptable for a business trip, though nothing special. The service was a complete mixed bag from friendly to gruff, prompt to totally unreliable (i.e. I asked room service to read my order back to me when I was sure they had it wrong, they read it back correctly and still got the order wrong and 45 min. later). The heat in my room was malfunctioning and so I had to keep the window open otherwise it would have been 80 degrees in the room. If you have business in the area this is probably about as nice an option as you'll get, definitely much better than the Marriott or the Westin but nothing to write home about. If you're looking for something special near here, try the Taj, the Liberty or especially XV Beacon.

“Comfortable Stay” Overall I was impressed with my stay at Inn at the Ballpark. Room was decent size, comfortable, and public areas were clean. I booked via priceline the day off and my rate of $58 +taxes was accepted for a Sat nite. This was half the price of their lowest web rate for the night. Location wise, the hotel is directly across the street from Minute Maid Park.. Other than that, there were not a whole lot of other things that were extremely close, with the exception of the Vic and Anthony's steakhouse which was next door and a great place for prime steaks. If looking for other downtown hotels that might be closer to some things, the Hilton Americas and Four Seasons would come to mind being walking distance to the Houston Pavillions. I valeted my car and service was quick and friendly both when coming and leaving. Check in was friendly and quick and 2 or 3 times I was offered assistance on taking luggage to my room. There were 3 elevators to service the 12 floors and I found them to be fairly quick. All of the public areas were clean and had an upscale feel to it. The hallways were dark due to the dim lighting and dark walls. Room size was pretty good for a boutique downtown hotel. I had an 8th floor room facing north. The high ceilings and tall windows definetly helped in making the room spacious. The rooms lack an IHome clock/radio, but have a more basic one that accepted an auxiliary input. 42" LCD screen, coffee maker in the room, and a nice sized desk to work on. The bathroom was decent sized and sort of L shaped. Wood type flooring for the entry and in the bathroom with a marble counter. Bathroom had a tub/shower combo and good quality thick and soft towels. The room had a ceiling fan and the only thing I wasn't crazy about in the room was the temperature. As one who likes to sleep in a colder room, i was not able to lower the thermostat setting lower than 72 degrees. Not sure if it was only my room, or if the hotel set that as the lowest possible setting. The room had the usual assortment of Houston literature for travelers as well as a postcard, envelope, and stationary to write on. PPV options were available on the TV and guest checkout could be done on the TV. Room service selections were varied and fairly priced considering the hotel and location. Room service from Vic and Anthony's was also available which is a plus for someone wanting a quality meal in room. Unfortunatly I didn't dine or eat anywhere on the property or utilize any services of the hotel other than valet so I can't offer any additional comments. Because of the location, this hotel would be a great stay for a baseball game or any events at Minute Maid Park.

“Mai più” ...arrivati in questo hotel si viene accolti da bella e grande hall. Il via vai è continuo e non si capisce chi è dell'hotel e chi forse è lì di passaggio. Fatto il check-in,ci dirigiamo verso la nostra camera. Appena le porte dell'ascensore si aprono lo scenario è da INCUBO. Il piano della nostra camera è fatiscente e c'è odore di "vecchio". La vera sorpresa la abbiamo non appena apriamo la porta della camera. Piccola, buia, e NON pulita. Evito la descrizione del bagno. Presa da un attacco di rabbia, torno giù e mi lamento col personale. A questo punto mi viene data un altra camera. Appena le porte dell'ascensore si aprono lo scenario è differente. Il piano si vede che è stato appena ristrutturato. Purtroppo la camera no,anche se migliore della prima, siamo ben lontani da definirla comunque CAMERA DA HOTEL. In definitiva sconsiglio questo hotel che a mio parere essendo troppo grande viene gestito in maniera superficiale. Un incubo!

“Charming and Affordable Alternative in Boston” I have stayed at the NGH many times in the past, but had not visited in several years until this October (2012), when I was there for three nights. What a change! Gone are the breakfast room in the basement, the hardwood floors in the guest rooms and the aged bathrooms. In their places are: A restaurant off the lobby that offers a free breakfast daily (the quality and variety of the breakfast is the only change for the worst from my last visits--and I am inclined to think that might be the result of the inattentive wait staff watching over the buffet). The rooms (well, my room!) now have carpeting, a modern decor in soothing neutral colors, a small but full bathroom, and a big flat-screen tv with a gazillion channels. There's no one to help with luggage, the elevator is small and slow, but the location is superb--you can pretend to be a Bostonian--and single travelers can feel very safe. There is limited outdoor parking at an incredibly ($20) low price. And, just down the street is a small gourmet-ish grocery store that makes fabulous sandwiches for not very much money. This a great base to experience Boston. Closest T stop is Exeter Street/Copley--a couple of blocks, but not unmanageable with luggage. Guests in wheel chairs, or burdened with luggage should enter the NGH from its rear (in a public alley): no steps, and the elevator is close at hand. Otherwise, you will have to negotiate a steep set of stairs if you enter on Newbury St.

“Trying too hard and forgets the basics” TheWit is trying to be a trendy, hip hotel, but has forgotten the basics that guests are looking for--comfort & service. The rooms are uncomfortable--small, odd furniture, the bathroom sink is strangely shaped and so tiny that it fails to drain water. The bathroom door slides open, which was annoying and leaves for very little privacy. The service is spotty. We had requested items from housekeeping and had to call multiple times. In the interim, we received a rubix cube and jelly apple--fun touches, but would much rather have received the towels that were needed. I can't imagine staying at this hotel on a business trip. The internet is not free and overall the hotel room is hard to function in, given the size and odd design of the bathroom. The hotel gym and rooftop bar were top notch, but not a reason to stay at the hotel or recommend it. Go elsewhere for a more polished and relaxing stay.

“Great location but hiccups galore on this visit” I know my last review of this hotel just a few months ago raved about the place and I must admit I still love this hotel compared to some of the other places iv stayed but to be balanced I must admit this most recent stay was less then ideal! Upon arrival into a very congested lobby and waiting some time to be served I found myself without a room for a further 40 minutes as "housekeeping have yet to service your room"! I arrived around 6 pm so this seemed unusual. No apology given. When I finally got to my room which was perfectly clean, comfortable and acceptable I discovered that the air conditioning in the room was totally ineffective at cooling the room. Also whenever water was running be it the sink, shower or toilet it sounded like someone was banging away with a jack hammer behind the bathroom wall! On the second day of my visit despite being out of the room without the "do not disturb" sign on the door my room was never serviced! I had to ring down for fresh towels in the end. On check out I waited TWENTY MINUTES before I was seen to despite there only being one couple ahead of me in the line. 3 staff at the desk and plenty more passing through chatting to one another. I began to get very frustrated. I then had an issue with my bill where a charge of over $90 was placed for drinks and a meal I never had at one of the bars. The receptionist insisted in making me check receipts! Turned out it was from the previous guest in my room but in total took almost 35 minutes from leaving my room to actually getting out of the hotel! But there are positives! The location....WOW! The beds...AMAZING and most of the staff I dealt with where lovely! The fitness club and spa area are also top notch! On this occasion I'll put this one down to a bad experience but I shall be back I'm sure!!!!!

“Tolle Lage - sehr schöne Zimmer” War gleich 2x im W diesen Mai. Die Lage ist sehr gut, ein Block off Market Street und zwei vom Union Square. Die Lobby ist jetzt fertig renoviert und wer modernes Design mag ist sehr gut aufgehoben hier. Zimmer sind grosszügig und bieten tolle Aussichen auf San Francisco. Viele Lokale in der Umgebung für Frühstück und Abendessen

“Great Place to Stay” My wife and I stayed two nights at the Talbott at the end of February. This little hotel was the perfect place for us. The lobby is very small but also cozy, and with both fireplaces going it was a welcoming atmosphere coming in from the cold. The staff was very friendly and efficient. The room was pretty spacious, and the king bed was extremely comfortable. We had a seventh floor room facing delaware st, so there was really no view. The bathroom was a good size, including two sinks and a spacious tub/shower. There was also free wireless internet...a big plus for us. Perhaps the best thing about the Talbott is the location. We were only a few steps from State, Rush, and North Michigan. Tons of shopping, bars, and good food are easily within walking distance. This makes the Talbott a great place for tourists who want to walk around and take everything in. We highly recommend the Talbott, and will gladly stay again on return trips.

“Made our vacation!!” Got a good rate through Priceline. Stayed with my husband and two daughters for a 4-day San Diego get-away. The hotel was a quick 5-10 minute drive to the beach, museums & Hillcrest. The room was very clean, the furniture looked new or well maintained. Bed was comfy with a fluffy comforter and lots of pillows. Kids slept fine on the hideaway bed. Internet connection worked great. The kids enjoyed the microwave popcorn provided. Maid read my note and provided exactly the service requested. Kitchen and fridge were handy for storing snacks and drinks. Breakfast buffet was more comprehensive than I expected - make-your-own waffles, eggs, sausage, bacon, OJ, yogurt, cereal, fresh fruit, etc. Staff was friendly and efficient. Contributed to a great family vacation.

“Very nice hotel...” Hotel looks new, sign up that said grand opening. Met my expectations for a hotel, no complaints. Rooms were nice. Comes with everything you would expect from a hotel room. Good breakfast area with nice selection of foods, some hot. Would recommend and would stay again.

“Great stay” Stayed here for a local wedding and we enjoyed it. Rooms are nice, clean and a good size. Location is convenient to historic sites, eating, bars/night clubs and other hotels. There isn't fee wifi, but there is a hotel business center in the lobby. Also, if you you are looking for a place to book a wedding or an event, they have nice ballrooms. I noticed several weddings going on at this location throughout the weekend so, I popped my head in the doors to sneak a peak. The front desk staff was very accomodating from providing umbrellas for the rain to ensuring our friends had the adjoinging room next ours. Someone did get stuck in the elevator while we were there which made us take the stairs, but overall it's a great place and I would return.

“Even more enjoyable the second time around” I reviewed this hotel on my site visit and chose it to host our annual retreat. And I sure wasn't disappointed. Will try to give you new insights (see previous review for basic info). Planning: Once we decided on this resort, the planning process was awesome. They plugged me into many different people who took care of all aspects of the resort (ie. spa, golf, kids club, AV equipment, rooms, etc.). I can't say enough about Lynette (rooms) and Lauren (spa). I must have emailed them with changes 20 times a day. They were always prompt to respond and very professional. That is a reoccurring theme to this hotel, awesome service! Checking in: They had everything in order and check-in was a breeze. The valet people made sure to call you by your proper title (Dr. in this case) and always offered bottled water. Bellboy actually beat us to our room Rooms: immaculate (see prev review). I had mentioned that I needed a crib, and it was there waiting for me. I asked for a hot water kettle and that came within minutes. I was able to clear out the fridge and used it for our own personal use. Restaurant: Great service. We made it in time for Restaurant week and enjoyed that. Some of our VIPs made it in late and didn't have dinner reservations. The captain (for our cocktail reception) went out of his way to get a party of 9 squeezed in prior to the kitchen closing at Amaya. The party ate and drank away and they kept the restaurant open til close to midnight for them. Pool/Spa: My wife still raves about her treatment from the prior trip. This time did not disappoint as well. All of the other guests also mentioned that it was a fabulous experience. The pools were nice. We didn't use it last time. The moment you walk in, pool attendants will find you and set up a lounge chair for you. They will bring you water and even water in a kids cup (with a lid) for the little ones. The underwater speakers were a hit with our kids. We also rented a cabana for a day and that was nice. Catering/Banquet: As you can imagine, there are a number of events that go on simultaneously, however, they juggled it really nicely. They even had a Mitt Romney fund raiser in the adjacent ballroom, and aside from the noisy band, every thing went smoothly. The staff was once again very professional. From the waiters to the captain, everyone was there to make sure our event went off without a hitch. When we had more than the expected count, they were able to provide the extra food within a timely matter. Bar/Club: They have a really nice lobby bar with jazzy entertainment on the weekend. Even though we had a large party, the servers did their best to accommodate us. We even tried Club M one evening. I was very leery about what Club M had to offer, however, it was pretty happening for a resort club. Apparently locals come there to party as well. They had a DJ spinning and it provided a nice atmosphere. All in all, this resort truly lives up to being a 5 diamond resort. I can not imagine having this retreat at any other place.

“Excellent location, very comfortable hotel” I was on business when I stayed at the hotel in January, 2011. The hotel is in a great location, just one block from the Gaslamp Quarter where there are lots of shops and restaurants. The staff were very welcoming and when one of my colleagues experienced a flight cancellation after checking out, the staff member put her back in her room and even ended up extending her stay at the conference rate. The Business Center also offered free computer use and printing which was nice for printing boarding passes. I had breakfasts and a few lunches in the hotel restaurant and it was very good. I also thoroughly enjoyed the rooftop bar! The room itself was fine with a working area although the chair really needed to be replaced as it was about shot.

“Location, Location, Location!” Great location and believe it or not, a very quiet hotel in NYC! Excellent stay and would have given it perfect stay if we didn't have a lousy breakfast the first morning we were there. Everything else was great! The hotel was in a great location for Broadway plays, we were there to see Wicked which we could just about see from our window! The room was clean, a normal size, bathroom a bit small but bigger than most in Manhattan! Everything worked, check in was a breeze, hotel parking was a bargain for the city at $26.00 a day and there were cookies there every afternoon, coffee, tea, and hot chocolate 24 hours a day. I was so surprised at how quiet it was, we hardly heard anything, maybe once and a while a siren or a horn but when you stepped outside it was loud. I guess they don't build them like they used to. We've been at many Hampton Inns and they were not quiet at all. The hotel was busy and there was a very long line for breakfast, the first day they were out of bagels! Imagine, out of bagels in NYC, but they had grits? We opted to eat breakfast down the street the 2nd day and then saw people getting on the elevator with tons of breakfast way past the breakfast hours? Other than the breakfast which to me is always Hampton Inns weakness, a Great stay, no problems at all!

“Where's the Water” Stayed one night while in Houston on business. Front desk attendants who helped me check in and out were in training, but very courteous and efficient. I was told that I was upgraded, but seems it just meant I was on top floor (30th) with more of a view. The room was large and clean. Much of the room is updated, but some aspects seem not so much. Temperature controls were good, room was quiet, and bed quite comfortable. After waking up, turned on hot water in sink to shave, and got air. Hot water finally came on, and it was green with silt particles. Had to run the sink and shower for some period of ti,e till the water cleared up. Heard nothing from the hotel to warn me about problems with water, and what was being done to fix the situation, and when. Found that annoying. Otherwise a good stay at hotel. If your business is downtown, then OK. If not, better to stay in Galleria area. Not much downtown.

“Bargain boutique hotel stay” Chicago has a lot of hotel choices with reasonable prices. We prefer boutique hotels and Chicago has a lot of them as well. We picked Affinia because of its location near the lakeshore where we wanted to go for morning runs and the price was unbeatable. About six weeks before our trip, the hotel website was offering a special rate. We booked and prepaid for a junior suite averaging $186 per night. The hotel is located just off the Magnificent Mile so was a great location for shopping. A short walk south on Michigan Avenue will take you across the Chicago River to Millennium and Grant Park where we also wanted to go. And with the proximity to the lakeshore pathway, the location for us was ideal. The hotel has a number of extra amenities including C Restaurant, a 29th floor roof top bar, in room spa services and a fitness center. We had a lunch and a breakfast at the restaurant and enjoyed a nice meal and pleasant service each time.
