The roof top bar on the 29th floor provided a good view all the way to Millennium Park and over the rooftops of nearby buildings on Michigan Avenue while sipping on a drink and soaking in a bit of sunshine. We did not try out the spa services or fitness center. The room itself was very comfortable. Lots of room with a spacious sitting area and a flat screen tv which could be swung around to face either the bed or the sitting areas. The bathroom, like most boutique hotels, was stylish but small. A vanity area helped ease bathroom congestion. The hotel offers a pillow menu of six different types of pillows. I tried the Swedish memory pillow which offered extra neck support and supposedly eased tension. Hard to tell since I was on vacation and tension was not a concern. The hotel also offers experience kits. I took the stay fit one with a yoga mat, work out DVDs, etc. but did not use it much since we were running each morning. They also offer a walking tour kit and a picnic kit. The room has a coffee maker and coffee free of charge. We did not sample from the mini bar nor use room service dining. We wanted ice and wine glasses had to request that each afternoon but delivery was very prompt. Housekeeping kept the room clean. We found all the staff to be very friendly and helpful and could not fault the service at all. When we arrived, they gave us city maps and directions. They printed out our board passing at the front desk the day before we were to leave. The doormen were always very welcoming. The one negative aspect was the noise from building construction next door. The single pane windows did not reduce the noise level by much, so it was noticeable each morning. If you want to sleep in late, which we did not, you may not want to stay at this hotel. Another minor annoyance was the elevator. One of the two elevators servicing floors 8 - 29 was being repaired leaving only one elevator and often some rather tedious waiting and then getting on a crowded elevator car. The other elevator is supposed to be repaired by the end of June 2009.

“Dated, but Clean and Good Location” We stayed here for one night before heading to the airport. As a Starwood Platinum member we were upgraded to the Presidential Suite, which had beautiful views of the city, three bathrooms and a sauna. The Suite was definitely dated but we understand that it is to be remodeled soon. The front desk staff was extremely helpful and friendly, as was the valet. If you are budget-conscious, don't pay to park at the hotel. There are several parking lots/structures within a block or two that are much cheaper and street parking is available on the weekends. The only real drawback was that we stayed here on a Sunday evening and there was nowhere in the hotel or close by (that we could see) to get a few bottles of water or snacks as everything was closed.

“Good Location & Nice Room” We booked with a group and the rate was high but the hotel had great beds and sheets. It was also a block or two from Little Toyko and withing walking distance to other sites. Comfortable stay with refrigerator and desk in room. Stayed a week and staff was helpful. The hotel is lacking a pool but the Japanese garden is very pretty. Also, it was undergoing renovations into a Doubletree at the end of our stay which created quite a bit of noise.

“Fantastic Choice for Location and Overall Stay Comfort” It's experiences such as these that remind you why your loyal to a Hotel chain. I was participating in the Rock and Roll Half Marathon in San Jose and the obvious choice was this property, located near to the start line in downtown SJ. Locating the Hilton San Jose was easy, being close to the 101 and the 87, as I drove from San Francisco. The property was not only 3 blocks from the race start line, but within walking distance of many restaurants and convenience shops. I found many things to like and none to hate about the hotel location. As the hotel was attached to the Convention Center, the parking was underneath both, and convenient to walk from your car to the lobby. The Convention center was also the location of the Health and Sports Expo for the race. The convenience of walking from your hotel elevator to the sports expo in less than 5 minutes with a full "swag bag" cannot be understated! The hotel check in was painless, and I was upgraded as a Diamond member to the Executive floor. The room was very nicely sized, and had a superb comfy bed. A testament to how comfortable it was is that I didn't care for once that they did not have a king bed available and had to provide a room with 2 double beds. Alas, the bathroom was a tub/shower combo, not the shower stall as some upgraded Hilton's have. Overall tho, the bathroom was roomy enough and the sink fixtures modern. The shower head had good water pressure but tended to spray the water outside the tub around the edges of the curtain. The view from my 18th story window was also superb, with visuals of the valley and nearby mountains. The Executive Club was good but small. In the mornings and evenings at peak hours, they ran out of chairs :-( Another sad note is the "Honor Bar" where they charge for alcohol. Having traveled to many international Hilton destinations where they still do NOT try to rake in every penny, I continue to be disappointed with this US Hilton implementation. The stay convenience of location came together as I woke up at 5am for the 8am race start gun and only had to walk 3 blocks away...No cars, no travel pressure, and a convenient race breakfast as the Hilton restaurant opened also at 5am. It was interesting and curious to see that although the Hilton was a sponsor of the race, no special amenities were prepared for runners staying there or recognition of the event in any way. I have stayed at other Hilton properties that took these recognition steps and would highly recommend that the San Jose Hilton do the same. For an example of another Hilton property, they can contact the Hilton Bonnet Creek in Orlando, FL, where special packages are prepared for the Disney Marathon Weekend, or the Embassy Suites in Philadelphia, PA for the Philadelphia Marathon. It's a touch of class and sophistication that appeals beyond words As I signed up for the race next year, I will be back to this property without a hesitation and will be sure to reserve early!

“An "okay" 1-night stopover” Stopped at The Dolphin for 1 night - prebooked it ahead of our visit direct after reading reviews on Tripadvisor. The motel itself is well positioned, on the front and in a residential district. It's a no-frills establishment and our room (#32) was very basic. For a 1-night stay it's ok but we couldn't have stopped another night here if we had to. The staff were very helpful and friendly though and pointed us in the right direction for a good mexican meal in the evening! Breakfast was very basic - coffee and muffins. In summary - ok for 1 night but I probably wouldn't stay again if visiting San Diego.

“Best Hotel Experience Available in Dallas” Elegant, romantic, historical, impeccable service, best restaurant experience of our lives at The French Room, extremely relaxing, within walking distance of many types of adventures, spacious rooms, and good quality wi-fi (for the price: free) are descriptions off the top of my head. The staff would certainly be entitled to being snooty in such a grand hotel but it's remarkable how helpful and down-to-earth everyone is without exception. I left my bags with a bellman and then parked in Thanksgiving Tower for $5 for the entire weekend. It's only a few blocks walk past some good restaurants and nightlife - great places to try if you care to venture outside the hotel. The Adolphus will be our regular staycation address when we need a long weekend to decompress or to celebrate a special occasion. You truly are transported to a far more magical place and the rest you get in the comfy beds makes you feel like you've gotten away without all the hassles of travel.

“Good location, nice room - expensive parking” Our family of 4 stayed in a Family Suite for 3 nights. Although not technically a 'suite' (it was all in one room), the room was huge and would easily accommodate 5 or 6. It was clean and comfortable. It had a microwave oven and small fridge (though no crockery and cutlery) Breakfast was adequate - it gets very busy and is not a relaxing experience! The hotel is ideally located for FIshermans Wharf, Alcatraz and the Cable Cars. This was the 7th and last hotel we used during a tour of California and it seemed expensive. It cost more than any of the others and gave us less. (5 of the others were suites - i.e. seperate bedroom and living room - , all 6 had full kitchen facilities, 5 had swimming pools, 5 had free parking, 3 had cheese/wine or other free 'goodies'. Perhaps this is a reflection of San Francisco, rather than this particular hotel. Parking is very expensive (about 40 dollars a night, from memory), but the service is very efficient. In summary, this hotel delivers the basics very well but has no 'extras'. I would stay there again.

“3rd time here and always perfect” Though I am in Houston often for business, this beautiful hotel is not usually in budget. However there is a yearly business event I attend at the Houstonian. This is a wonderful, luxury, perfectly staffed hotel. Rooms are terrific, I suggest to pay extra for the concierge level as it is truly a catered and staffed lounge. This is the event, even in the heat of summer in Houston I look forward too, mostly because of the Houstonian experience.

“Clean, comfortable and well priced” Stayed at the Sportsmen's Lodge for work for 3 nights. The hotel feels somewhat like it has been stuck in 1962, complete with kitschy astroturf ringing the pool. The room that I had was on the 3rd floor and faced the pool. This only presents a problem if you want to get to sleep early as the pool is frequented until about 11pm. Room and furnishings appear to have been updated within the last few years and were quite clean and well kept. Hallways and lobby are beginning to show their age but are quite clean. The hotel restaurant was under renovation during my stay so a temporary dining room had been set up in one of the hotel's conference rooms. The wait staff still appeared to be ironing out the details of this change. As I only had breakfast (cereal and fruit) at the hotel I can't comment on the quality of the food though the selection looked decent for all meals. Staff at reception were quite friendly and happily made taxi reservations to the airport, etc. Overall the hotel is comfortable, clean and offers a decent value for LA area.

“Liked it” Stayed at the Alexander Inn for a weekend in November. As I frequently do, I used TripAdvisor reviews to find a property that met my criteria of good location in the city (to me that means you can get around easily either on foot or by public transportation) and reasonable price. The Alexander met both of those requirements perfectly. I came in from the airport on the train and it was a short walk (maybe half a mile) from the train station to the Hotel. It was a even shorter little walk to the Kimmel Center where we went 2 nights, once to see the Philadelphia Orchestra, once to see PhilaDanco dance company. The breakfasts we above average for a continental breakfast bar and there was a very nice man who staffed the breakfast area and he was a great source of local entertainment info and options. We had the smaller of the queen rooms and it was rather small for 2 people but we were there to see the city, not the hotel room, so that was fine. I would definitely stay here again.

“Amazing Kimpton Experience” This was our second visit to a Kimpton Hotel and both stays have been literally perfect! The Muse is a fun hotel in a great location with truly outstanding customer service. Every single staff encounter we had was positive. And some were downright unbelievable. I had forgotten to add my InTouch number to the reservation, but the hotel staff spotted it in advance and had me all set. We had a superior king, which was just a bit more than a standard room. It was huge for New York and completely spotless. What was especially nice was getting a totally quiet room, that actually had a view and was as close as we were to Times Square and Rockefeller Center. We're sold on Kimptons!

“New and clean -- very friendly staff” Stayed one night before an early AM flight out of DEN. Property looks and feels quite new. Unique furnishings and layout to a king two room suite are very contemporary but a bit cluttered. What I mean is that there is an open room divider/shelving unit between a large multi-sectional couch and the king bed, leaving very little floor space. Nice work desk, great bedding, and a large bathroom with walk-in shower balance things out. Kitchen would be helpful if staying longer. Windows open, which is a blessing because the AC blows straight down on the bed. Breakfast buffet was limited in selection but well-prepared. Shuttle bus to airport leaves promptly on the 1/2 hour - reserve it when you check in so you are assured a spot. All in all, a very nice property, less than 10 minutes from airport, but a good 20-30 minutes from the sites in Denver, depending on traffic and a car is a must.

“Comfortable and clean yet not outstanding. Trying to be trendy but just a bit dull.” Ok location, however the overall hotel is a rather dark (rooms included) and really lacking a cozy and welcoming look&feel. Trying to be trendy but not achieving it really. Not a bad hotel at all, but without any specific charm or appeal, would not recommend if you're a picky hotel user. A bit pricey for what it has to offer.

“Nice hotel Great bed !” It's dc type of hotel . It's not high as the area will not allow it. We had a bit of a problem with the front desk girl on sat night the 7th of July . We were due to have free Internet . She was not nice and then when I show her , my confirmation she said "we will give it to you even if we don't give free Internet to 3rd party " well, didn't like her much. Smiling . Great area ! 40 dollars for parking !!!watch it . Nice apple basket touch in the lobby .

“Great location” I liked this Hilton Garden Inn very much. The staff (especially housekeeping) really helped to make me feel welcome. I stayed for 5 nights to experience NYC. The location is great, as the hotel is located above the Canal St. subway stop. Buying an unlimited 7 day transit (subway & bus) pass is well worth the $27 cost. My room was right on 6th St. on the second floor above the restaurant. I heard no noise from the restaurant & minimal street noise. The little noise/vibration that there was came from the train, but even this was minimal. Housekeeping was excellent each day. Towels & toiletries were refreshed & the room was always cleaned. The front desk staff was very accommodating and pleasant. I've heard quite a bit about NYC hotel rooms being tiny. This was just the opposite. My king bed room was about the same size as other Hilton Garden Inn's I've stayed at in the past. Plenty of room for two people. Only complaint is that the bathroom is pretty small (but functional). There are many good restaurants within a 5 to 10 minute walk. Greenwich Village and SoHo are both within 15-20 minutes away by foot. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to stay in a locale that isn't right in the heart of Manhattan (but is very convenient to public transportation).

“Nice, safe option for Midtown” A group of friends were coming to NYC for a Yankees game and we wanted to stay in Midtown for good proximity to the game and to nightlife -- in the other direction. This place is well located about half a mile walk from Time Square. Getting to the game and Greenwich Village via subway were both pretty easy. The hotel has little local flavor (though the hotel bar isn't bad), but clean and has nice appointments (TV, shower, bed) and the price is not crazy high.

“Atmosphere and decor are great; the ducks, not such a big deal” First of all, the ducks: crowds gather early to see the attendant march the ducks to the fountain (late morning) and back to the elevator (late afternoon). The "action" lasts for a couple of minutes. The ducks walk and the attendant talks a lot. You can get a good view of the ducks in the fountain throughout the day, without the crowds, or in their hutch on the roof, afterwards (nice view of Memphis from there, as well). The rooms are not large, but are comfortable. The lobby is comfortable, historic and surprisingly active at nearly all hours of the day and evening. Breakfast is not included and we found the cafe, with its buffet, expensive. Even more expensive is the French-style restaurant off the lobby. We found quite good, far less expensive, alternatives nearby, ranging from the Flying Fish to the Majestic and, for beer, the Flying Saucer. We paid about $169 plus tax as a special conference rate. Not sure I'd stay at the regular rate, but I imagine deals can be found. It's an easy walk to Beale Street. There is a street car line on Main Street to some places, but otherwise you need a car to get to anywhere of interest (some areas a few blocks from the hotel I wouldn't walk through at night). As noted, parking is expensive. If you don't need to have a car for your entire stay, there are car rental franchises (we used Avis on Madison) a few blocks away. My wife used the pool in the "basement" and said it was nice.

“Wow! You could not ask for a more service oriented staff...” I take my hat off to the management of this hotel. As a very frequent business traveller who stays at 4 and 5 star properties throughout the world, I was totally and completely impressed by this property. Rooms were very comfortable and decently spacious, the staff catered to our every need and the experience was a real treat. Bravo!

“改装されてモダンなブティック風ホテルに様変わり” 実は、自分はこのホテル、以前から地の利の良さには魅力を感じていたものの、あまりに古そうで(以前、ルーズベルトホテルで痛い思いをしているので)、ずっと避けてきた。それが、この度、改装を行い、「The Milford」として新装オープンをしたので、試しに泊まってみた次第。 結論を言えば、夜は観劇三昧で過ごす自分には最高の立地で、且つ、さすがに改装されたばかりの部屋も清潔でモダン、それでいて料金が以前並みに抑えられているので、大正解だった。 場所はエアポートバスの終着地点であるPort Authorityから2ブロック、8th Ave.に面して入口がある。このホテルで特筆すべきが、独特なシステムのエレベータ。乗り場に10キーみたいなものがあって、宿泊客は、自分のフロアを入力すると、どのエレベータに乗るのか表示されるというもの。よって、エレベータの箱内部には階数を押せるボタンが無い!慣れると、それほど不便を感じないが、何で、こんなシステムをとったのか、とっても不思議。 肝心の客室は、広くは無いものの明るい色調で清潔。部屋の広さの割りには十分大きな薄型テレビが装備。何が嬉しいって、水回りが一新されているので、バスルームも清潔で、お湯の出も十分。バスタブも深めで日本人向き。アメニティも、シャンプー、コンディショナー、ボディソープ、フェイスソープと一通り揃う。狭めながらもクローゼット、引き出し、セーフティボックスも装備。難点を挙げるとすると、冷蔵庫が無いことと、空調の音がとてもうるさいことぐらい。それでも、この立地で一泊2万円前後で泊まれるのなら、下手なミッドタウンのブティックホテルを選ぶより、よほどコストパフォーマンスが高いと思う。

“Really like the Kitano” I often work in the 40th and Park area,. i have stayed at numerous hotels within a mile of the Kitano, but that hotel is easily the best. i got upgraded to a suite this time. Room was very quiet--soundproofed windows worked! Staff generally very good. The one very annoying thing--$17.76 charge for one small bottle of Jack Daniels from the mini bar. I didn't see a price list any where. Discovering the cost at check out left me with a bad last impression, which was unnecessary and a shame.

“Nice stay in downtown Baltimore” Was able to get a decent rate for Fri/Sat stay in the Baltimore downtown. Only a couple blocks to the Inner Harbor, so very nice walk in good weather or a cheap (under $5) cab ride. Check in was quick, and the front desk clerks seemed friendly. It's an older hotel, but in really good shape. The room itself was clean with a decent layout and plenty of room. The bathroom has definately been modernized not too long ago. There was some street noise from traffic, but we were able to sleep well. There is a business area off the lobby with 3 PCs you can use for free. And they have free continental breakfast. I will definately look here again when coming back to Baltimore. Great location, and good price for a decent room.

“Clean, quiet, bland, and cheap” This hotel is close to the River Walk, about a 5-10 trek, but the rooms are about one-half the cost. Recently given a cosmetic facelift, the rooms are clean and quiet....except for the trains, for which the helpful clerks will give you earplugs, if you ask. We paid $99 a night during the final four, which we thought was a bargain.

“Almost Perfect” We were treated with kindness and generosity during our stays here in September. The Jr. Suites are huge... more like a true 1 bedroom suite but without a bedroom door. The common areas are newly redone as well as the room furnishings so little to dislike. Mattress is adjustable,WiFi fast, AC controllable, spotless maid service, and the most friendly staff you will ever meet. Free self laundry as well as soap/ fabric softener, free shoe shine, above average breakfast with eager chefs willing to personalize your breakfast order. How can an entire waitstaff be so cheerful at 6am ? We slept well and relaxed at night after our long daily visits to the rehab hospital. Numerous dining/shopping choices within walking distance of the hotel. We had a few blips with the toilet and shower nozzle but quickly fixed and yes, the fridge was a little noisy. IMO... $150/n charge is excessive for a regular room but well priced if you can snag a Jr. Suite. Unfortunately, this is almost impossible to accomplish M-Thur because the repeat businessmen have prebooked these rooms for weeks in advance. In closing, a special thank you to Antionette and Cindy for making my difficult family crisis easier to deal with. I will always remember your special consideration to us.

“Awesome Boutique Experience” I have stayed at a number of hotels in Boston and the Lenox is at the top of my list right now. The staff is exceptional and will go out of their way to help. Though small, the hotel is in an exceptional location with lots of shoppring and sites nearby. There is a great bar, a fun restaurant and an Irish pub all on premises. The fireplace in the lobby was blazing and the hotel was just a very inviging place to hang out. This is a top choice is you are looking for an exceptional boutique experience with the best staff out there.

“Great!” Lives this hotel and extremely comfortable for the business traveller Great bartenders downstairs and a very welcoming front desk staff Will definitely be back! Definitely a must stay if you don't need to be in downtown houston

“Check the $$ room rates very carefully before chekout when booking through travel websites” This hotel boasts a "Save 30%" on Expedia.ca, but what is not obvious (and certainly unexpected) is that the rate is for only one person!! So you think you're getting a good deal, but they add on an extra person fee (at the checkout - it is not noted in the actual "price" - so right away, your 30% off is now less than 20% off!) Check your rates carefully - as what sounds like a deal is not!!! What is the point of advertising "Deluxe 2 Queen" rooms at 30% off, but I have to pay extra for because 2 people stay in the room? I have stayed at this hotel several other times - paying regular price - and it was always for double occupancy. This method of advertising is misleading. Having said that - I would still stay again - even if it is "single occupancy" rates, just more aware...

“Water and airconditioning problems” We were booked in at this hotel for 4 nights for our stay to watch the Preakness. When we arrived we were told we'd have to stay at a different hotel for the first 3 nights as they had water and airconditioning problems and the Preakness tickets we'd sent to them hadn't arrived [turns out they'd been stolen either from the hotel or in the mail]. So we ended up staying out of the main part of Baltimore which was inconvenient as there was no shops or restaurants there apart from the one at the hotel we were staying at. The Brookshire paid for the accomodation but not the breakfast which was in the original price so ended up costing us more. We ended up back at the Brookshire for the last night and it was okay but could do with an update. All in all would not stay there again or recommend.

“Great location!” This hotel is under rennovation. The check in process was slow, and my room was adjacent to a work/service area on one of the lower floors. The room was a surprise, though, as it had a living room, a bedroom, a couple of small alcoves, and a separate bathroom. It was quite in the bedroom, but the living room area loud due to the service area across the hall and what sounded like kids next door. This hotel is in a great walking distance to the White House and some wonderful restaurants. I would definitely stay here again.

“Happy Repeat Customer” I first stayed at the Belvedere in September 2004, and I was very happy with the room and the service, so I decided to take advantage of a "stay 3 nights, get one free" deal with hotels.com for a visit to New York with my daughter. We booked a King Executive room, and the hotel website stated that all the King Executive rooms had been renovated. We arrived too early to check-in, but got a call while we were at lunch offering us a queen room that was available immediately. I declined the offer and agreed to wait until a king was available. We arrived back at the hotel at 3:30 and were given a room on the 15th floor facing 48th St. We were very impressed with the renovations; the room looked, and even smelled, brand new. The entryway and bathroom were done in a beautiful brown marble, and the kitchenette area also had a marble countertop. The small fridge was hidden under the sink area, and there was a microwave and coffee maker, but no utensils. The bed had a pillowtop mattress and was very comfortable, and there was a small flat-screen TV on the dresser. There was a large closet with an iron and ironing board, a safe, and a hairdryer in it. Housekeeping did a great job of cleaning the room every day, and we had plenty of Penhaligon products. I guess if I had one complaint, it would be that the towels weren't very soft, but that is minor! The front desk staff and the bellmen were very nice, and there was always someone there to open the door and greet us. They also stored our luggage and hailed a cab for us when we needed one. The location is great - it's close to several subway lines and near Times Square, but the street itself is very quiet. There is a fire station on the corner, but I live near a fire station at home, so I wasn't bothered by sirens at all. There is a 24-hour grocery store on the corner of 48th and 8th where you can buy snacks, drinks, sandwiches, etc. 9th St. has a lot of great restaurants; I recommend Vynl and Eatery, both within a few blocks of the Belvedere. My daughter and I both enjoyed our stay at the Belvedere, and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to others.

“Opera -and A Bed and Breakfast” This hotel is sooo very close to the Opera House. You can catch a cab to anywhere-they are always going by. There are plenty of places to eat that are with in walking distance - with many being local. Delish! The breakfast that comes with your stay here is good. At breakfast we met others who had attended the Opera...then who should appear for breakfast but the director of the opera. It was fun to hear the director's take of how the opera was interpreted....a bonus. There is parking! Off street! Security. An elevator- which we used. Help with your luggage -if needed. TV in the rooms. We asked for 2 double beds ... they have rooms with 2 doubles. This place is MUCH larger than expected. And we drove to the airport in 15 minutes.

“Lake view but oh the sirens!” This Marriott has a great location where we were able to walk to everything we needed. Hip lobby with two entrances but always packed full of people. Our room was located on the 44th floor with a magnificient view of Lake Michigan which thrilled us. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. However, be sure you bring your earplugs. No wait, I tried ear plugs which were not enough. Perhaps the Bose noise reducing ear phones would block out the almost constant noise of ambulance and police sirens. We found out that a hospital was a few blocks down but holy cow, the sirens were never ending. We were stunned at the noise. I hardly slept the first night even with ear plugs. I must also note that only 2 out of the 6 high rise elevators seemed to be working. There was almost always a wait in the lobby for an elevator. Once a 3rd elevator opened on the 44th floor for us to take down, the doors closed, we thought we were moving but it shuddered and vibrated several times over a minute, then the doors opened on the 44th floor. Yeah, we got out and took a different elevator.

“Front desk staff should learn about customer service from the restaurant” Room service was prompt and extra-courteous; food was fresh, excellent, and prepared exactly as ordered. A wonderful experience. Condition and appearance of room and public areas was fine, with the exception that the a/c unit is programmed so that the blower CANNOT be left on to provide a constant white noise. At the front desk, I explained my desire for white noise in order to assure good sleep quality, and asked whether a portable fan was available that I could use. They checked with housekeeping and engineering, and very cheerfully told me that I was out of luck - basically that they had no interest at all in fulfilling this simple request for a Gold Holiday Inn member paying $700 for a several-night stay.

“Dirty Room & Surly Staff” I stayed at the Sheraton Philadelphia Downtown Hotel for 4 nights in May 2012 and will not return. Upon entry to my room, I noticed that the carpet was quite dirty. That's understandable, considering it is a beige carpet that I am sure gets plenty of traffic. What is not understandable is how dirty the bathroom floor and walls were. I immediately noticed black dirt marks all over the floor. The next morning, I noticed the same black dirt marks while I was in the shower. I notified the front desk in person of the dirty bathroom and asked that the floors and walls be cleaned. I also left a monetary tip for the maid each day. Despite numerous requests, the bathroom floor and walls were never cleaned during my stay. Very disgusting. Most (not all) of the front desk staff were also rude and surly during my interactions with them. The hotel AC (and heater) is a wall unit that you typically see in a motel. It is very noisy and blows the dirt and dust in the room around. The hairdryer was also coated in dirt and dust. I will mention the few positives: the bed was very comfortable, the shower had great water pressure and the tv was great. Had the entire city of Philadelphia not been sold out during the week of my stay, I would have switched hotels after my first night. Management gives canned responses to complaints: "Thank you for your comments. It's how we can improve." Obviously there is no intent to improve if the majority of guests provide the same comments. Oh, and I am a loyal SPGer who won't be loyal to this property.

“Good Stay” I was only in the hotel one night, but it was clean, comfortable, and well maintained. Several restaurants nearby and easy access to the freeway. Will stay here again when I am in the area.

“Location, location, location...” This is the only hotel on JAX Airport proper. Clean rooms, good service and the soundproofing is very good. You really can't hear planes from your room. The complementary breakfast buffet was tasty and well presented. Best of all, free parking for hotel guests!

“It was OK - not stellar, not horrible” Stayed at the Hyatt Regency Washington DC when my business facilitated a meeting for about 200 people. We organized everything and negotiated prices, etc. (this is important in explaining things below). The room was as expected. Good size for DC, flat screen TV was nice, bathtub with shower and good water pressure, great iHome clock radio. It may just be me -- but all three nights the bedding (bottom sheet and mattress pad) did not stay in place and i kept waking up with my body on the actual mattress. I've never had that happen before, but it may just be me. Fitness room is quite large and has everything and everything is clean and in good working order. It is combined with the pool area. Locker room for men had a private dry sauna. I am assuming the same was true for the women's locker room. The meeting room space was just so-so. We reserved numerous rooms for break-out space, and we got shuffled a little bit. I don't know the back-story on that, so I can't explain why (it may have not been the hotel's fault). My biggest issue with the hotel was with the catered lunch. We had to have working lunches with our meeting, and our business will not allow us to pay for the lunches of the participants. The participants had to buy the bagged lunches catered by the hotel. Our business negotiated the cost of the lunches and did the best we could. Bagged lunches were $18 and included a turkey sandwich or a small salad or a veggie wrap. Each came with an apple and a bottle of water. Yes -- a turkey sandwich, an apple, and a bottle of water for $18. I complained, and told the catering that no one minds paying $18 for lunch (we were all getting reimbursements or per diem), and no one minds a sandwich with an apple and water for lunch, but paying $18 for such a small meal is nothing short of highway robbery. (I believe I told the woman in charge of catering that I questioned how she could sleep at night knowing she was charging such amounts for so little food). The following day they added a bag of chips and a cookie to the $18 meals, but not sure if our contracted meeting organizers had to pay for that extra food. I took pictures of the lunch and promised to post on trip advisor, so I encourage you to take a look at what I posted. Other than that, all was fine. Great location, and courteous staff. I never got my newspaper at my door, as I had requested. Not sure what was up with that. I asked all three days to no avail -- one front desk clerk said it had to do with the way the reservation block of rooms was made. BTW: if you are in a wheelchair you may want to check with the hotel about access. I am sure they are ADA compliant, but immediately after walking in the front door are stairs and escalator going down (no elevator). Not sure where access is for people in a wheelchair, so you may want to check.

“An Oasis in the Heart of the Fasion District” We spent one night, November 27, 2011, at this great boutique hotel. When we arrived early in the afternoon, we remarked to the staff that it looked strikingly reminiscent of a hotel by the name of Fashion 26 where we stayed several times months ago. And the staff told us smilingly that it's the same hotel, and Fashion 26 was the previous incarnation prior to Hilton took over in Feb 2011. It was obviously a stressful day, but the staff, especially Christine, who pleasantly went way beyond the calls of duty to find us a beautiful room with luminous view of the Empire State building. The room was not ready when we checked in, but as soon as it was, Christine called us informing us so we could settle ourselves at our earliest conveniences. Another staff, Zoribel, went out of her way to make sure our luggage would arrive at our room in a timely fashion. Stunning view from the roof-top bar, but unfortunately it was closing a little early since it was Thanksgiving Sunday. Very comfortable bed, spacious bedroom and bathroom (great shower but no bathtub) and, in between, there is this lighted area that contained the mini-fridge and the coffee machine (it looks like a small open curio cabinet) was set up in a very aesthetically pleasing way. One slight disappointment: there is no ice machine on any floor, and we had to call room service for ice. I sustained a black eye earlier in the afternoon from an incident at a friend's place, so the difficulty of obtaining ice that evening was a little inconvenient. In the morning, another very competent and friendly staff, Caroline, checked us out. Also, the bell captain (I believe his name was Allen) was very helpful, as was everyone else.

“Tough Reviewer, worth every cent.” We are tough reviewers from Perth, (two Adults and one 9 yo girl) from Western Australia on hotel stays, and we found the Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn value for money and provided everything we needed. We stayed from the 16th to the 19th of December 2010. I chose the location to visit Universal Studios and the Hollywood area. The hotel provides a free regular shuttle service to Universal studios and when needed a drop off and pickup at the North Hollywood Metro station. The room had two comfortable queen beds, provided laundry rooms and a pool and spa. The staff were very friendly and helpful, the hotel is ideally located to explore the area via car (which we didn't) or public transport. For our needs, the Beverly Garland ticked all the boxes. We highly recommend this hotel.

“Echoes of the Japanese bubble economy” The Kitano Hotel is Japanese hotel that is reminiscent of the elegance of the Japanese bubble economy of the 1980s. It reminds of me very much of a slightly scaled down version of the Hotel Okura in Akasaka, Tokyo. The hotel was clearly built in a grander time with lots of marble and plushness. Surprisingly, time has treated it well. In particular, I really thought the rooms were excellent. My room was exceptionally clean and well appointed. Personally, I appreciated the hot water pot with Japanese tea bags and china cups. More importantly, the bathroom is huge, especially by New York standards. The bathtub was clean and nice for soaking. The bed was nothing spectacular (not a pillowtop) but was comfortable, all the same. The room size was about average for New York. The location is okay. It is 3 or 4 blocks from Grand Central station and a slightly longer walk to Times Square. There are several other hotels in the area that have slightly closer subway access and more restaurants, coffee shops and pharmacies nearby.

“A little Oasis Downtown” I really liked this place. Like all hotels It has it's pro's and con's which I'll try to list, but I think this was a great choice. Pro's 3 to 5 blocks to the heart of Downtown. Great alternative hotle for those meetings at the Sheraton or Hyatt. Nice Pool and Jacuzzi area. Rooms are clean and have plenty of room. Fridge and Microwave in each room. Decent free breakfast. The regular HIE fare, but the hostess keeps it freah and clean. Convenient to Ceiy Center Mall area. Several good restaurants in City Center. A few neat/unique place north of the Hotel too. Cons The hotel is over priced for what you get. The hotel keeps prices close to the Hyatt, Sheraton, Hilton $$ range. They get it because they keep the place neat, tidy and supply a free breakfast and have free parking. No managers welcome package. No beer/wine available at the hotel or take-out nearby. I usually stay at an HIE or Staybridge so I can have a glass of wine and cigar at the pool in the evenings.

“Great hotel, no so great neighborhood” Booked the Holiday Inn Topicana via Hotwire for $58 a night. I'll admit I didn't expect much from the Holiday Inn but I've been extremely surprised. The hotel is older but has been completely remodeled to be reminiscent of the 50's style hotel on Miami Beach. Although the rooms are on the smaller side the beds are very comfortable. My room was immaculate and the bathrooms are modern. Although most of the rooms have older wood furniture my room was decorated in new leather furniture. The rooms have flat screen TV's with a good choice of stations. Make sure to request a room facing the pool they are quite. The hotel has a 3000 sq. foot gym which is amazing. The only drawback to the hotel is the location. It is about a 15 minute walk to the riverwalk via a sketchy neigborhood. I would avoid walking this alone at night. There is nothing on the riverwalk at this location. The free internet was a nice added touch. Parking is $13 for in and out privileges. By the way the staff is excellent and very attentive. Enjoy.

“great place to stay” We stayed there for the July 4th long weekend this year. Very nice and clean hotel. Well positioned in NY with easy access to everything and within walking distance of Times Square. A very cool lounge area where you can relax or eat food and watch whatever you want on several flat screen TVs located in different areas. Friendly staff. The only negative was that the rooms were smaller than usual but that was not a major issue. Recommend getting a higher floor to avoid street noise. Would definitely stay there again.

“Thumbs up!” A great value. We (a group of four) were upgraded to a Superior Double Double, which was roomy by NY standards and had an actual view of the street. (Standard rooms are typically small, but otherwise fine.) The room was quiet and clean, beds extremely comfortable, bathroom immaculate. Rooms are furnished in a simple modern style. The free breakfast buffet is a handy feature, with pastries, cereal, yogurt, hard boiled eggs and cold cuts served in the pleasant adjoining restaurant. (If you're particular about your coffee, though, you might want to get it elsewhere.) The location is very convenient, walkable to lots of places and half a block from east side subway. There are good neighborhood Indian restaurants within a few block radius and a great little Indian gourmet store, Kalustyan's, around the corner on Lexington.

“Nice getaway spot” We stayed at the Sorella one night for a little b-day getaway on the recommendation of a good friend. I love the interior of the hotel and the decor, very pretty. Check in was fast and the desk attendant was very polite. The room was very roomy with modern decor. We decided to walk around the City Center area for a bit that afternoon...I guess I didn't realize how new the whole area is, but there are still very few retail stores occupying the spaces, however there are several restraunts, and there is still construction going on around the area. We decided to have a cupcake at Sweet and then a drink at Yard House. Later in the evening we walked over to Brio for dinner. The general area around the hotel outside was just swarming with people...and was still equally packed when we came back over 2 hours later after dinner...lots of kids running around too which I thought was strange since it was after 10pm and it doesn't strike me as a kid or family oriented area. After dinner we decided to go up the the hotel bar, the Monnalisa, for drinks and some live music. The music and drinks were great...but unfortunately we didn't stay too long because it was absolutely packed in there and there was no seating available by the time we got there...very little offered to begin with. We would have been ok to stand for a while and enjoy the music, but for some reason there is a large fire pit in the center of the room. While it looks really cool, it's still fire and it really heated the place up! That heat combined with the muggy and hot Houston air flowing in and out as people walked out onto the patio just made it uncomfortable in there. Next time I'll make sure we get there early so we can get a table...far away from the fire! We weren't ready to turn in for the night so decided to go over to the large lounge area near the lobby...there was ample seating there inside as well as outside and only a few people over there. We ended up sitting for a while on the patio (2nd floor) and people watched below. When we returned to our room we found a bottle of champagne waiting for us on ice! Neither one of us ordered it and there wasn't a note (and we weren't charged for it) so I'm assuming it was just a gift from the hotel...Nice :) I do have to say that the walls are paper thin. I was unfortunately kept up several hours throughout the night because of some drunken fools banging and screaming. From what I could hear, I believe they were asked to keep it down several times either by hotel staff or other guests, but that seemed to only fuel their behavior. So, while the bad behavior of others certainly isn't the hotel's fault, the walls provided VERY little noise buffer! I booked the room package that included sunday brunch at the hotel restaurant, Bistro Alex. The food and service here are great. I highly recommend this package for the value. The brunch included in the package is not buffet, but on a normal menu and you can just order to your content as many courses as you like...even dessert! One adult beverage per person is included too. I recommend the steak migas...soooo good! There were also musicians playing jazz music throughout brunch with was great! Also, we did not use the pool, but walked by it several times and were surprised at how super-tiny it is! the lounges by the pool look really nice, but I was just really surprised at how small the area is as well as the pool itself. If you are planning on some pool time during your stay, I'd get down there early to claim a spot! All in all, we had a good expreience, minus the noisy drunk idiots of course, and will definitely consider this hotel again.

“Lots of good things, a few bad things” We really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. We have previously stayed at the Marriott across the street, but preferred the Doubletree. Pros: Yummy cookies at check-in Extraordinarily friendly and helpful staff No parking fees No business center fees No resort fees Nice room with flat screen hotel We had a view of the pool and tropical garden instead of the air con system like we do when we stay at the Marriott Reasonably priced room service Cons: Don't care for the sliding bathroom door - hard to maneuver, especially late at night Took forever to pick up room service dishes that were left outside rooms - hours and hours - even after we called. Seems like it would attract insects or even rodents. This was pretty disgusting. How hard is it for the housekeeper or someone to make rounds a few times a day to pick up the trays? The location is in a business park and you really need a car if you stay here. It isn't far from either downtown San Diego (maybe 20 minutes driving) or the beaches up north. Aside from the few negative points above, we really enjoyed our stay and would definitely return.

“サービス、ロケーションとも優れ、日本人には安心のホテル” 妻と2月に2泊利用しました。マンハッタンはいつもどこに宿泊するかで悩むのですが、このホテルはどこかのスポットに特別近いということはありませんが、逆に5th Ave.、ロックフェラーセンター、ブロードウェイ、ユニオンスクエア、国連本部など全て徒歩圏内で、どこに出るのもそう遠くなく便利かと思います。建物はちょっと年季が入っていますが、豪華で格式を感じさせます。ホテルマンの教育も行き届いている方です。 もう一点コメントしたいのが空港とのアクセスです。ラガーディアにしろJFKにしろ、マンハッタンとの行き来は本当に不便でストレスに感じますが、NYASのシャトルサービスは現在43rd St. & 3rd Ave.のTD BANK前が停留所となっており、ホテルと徒歩で5分程度です。 NYで人気のうどん店「温や」や焼肉の「牛角」もすぐ近くにあり、NYの日本グルメを試したい方にもお勧めのロケーションです。
“Average basic stay” Good location, I enjoyed the touristy wharf area. Could walk to great bars, and eaterys nearby.

“Ok property, road construction a mess” I've stayed here quite a bit. The lobby has been updated, which is great, but the room still feels like an old Courtyard. Why do hotel chains insist on updating the lobby, only to disappoint when you open the door to your hotel room? There is a big disconnect here. The freeway construction is out of their control, and I'm sure it negatively affects their business, but the rooms need a facelift, especially at this price point in Houston. May return if I can't find other close options but not in a hurry to return.

“Crowne Jewel in Philly” Stayed one Saturday night at the Crowne and the hotel itself was perfect! First and most important tip: If you are driving, DO NOT park in the lot connected to the hotel. They charge $31 (per 24 hours) which is almost criminal. If you go half a block down, there is another lot at 1700 Market that is $11 per day on weekends. It's not attended so you pull up to a brown metal closed door and it automatically opens & gives you a ticket. You can park it yourself and there are oodles of spaces. Besides a decent price, it's nice to have access to your car when you want it. The lot at the hotel is attendant-parked so you can't get to your car. The Crowne is a nice hotel in a good location. Close to shops & restaurants within a few short blocks. The room (king) we had was spacious and very clean. Bathroom was small - toilet and tub took up most of room and the sink was just outside the door. The linens, pillows, etc. were top-notch. All the staff were outstanding - especially the concierge. Gave us great recommendations for local restaurants. Did not eat in the hotel restaurant as it had so many bad reviews. (If you are looking for a great meal at bargain prices, go down the block to the Midtown III restaurant - Huge breakfasts for two people and total tab was $11!!!) The hotel had a very nice outdoor pool area on the 8th floor. Plenty of loungers, chairs and lots of towels. Pool was very clean but water was quite chilly. I did like the fact that there were ice and vending machines on every floor - made it very convenient. We were on the 24th floor but could still hear traffic noise. Didn't bother us though. What did pose a problem were a couple of drunks staying across the hall. Yelling and stumbling around at 3 a.m. Security was quick to come up and set it straight fairly quickly at first. But the drunks rebounded a short while later and one of them was actually parading outside his room in his skiivies! What a sight! The security guy came back quckly and told him he would call the cops so they finally quieted down. Hotel staff did leave notes under the doors of the adjoining rooms, probably notes of apology. (We didnt' get one, though.) Can't fault the hotel for these drunk dumbos. It could happen anywhere. I'd definitely stay at the Crowne again.

“Good hotel but...” Even Fells Point, now a most touristy part of Baltimore, is sullied by small groups of merry but sadly filthy -e.g., poopy pants-drug addicts hanging out right outside the hotel, visibly intoxicated or high beyond most human endurance and still seeking interactions with tourists in the hope of getting money for a next fix. The hotel itself is lovely, proud of its history; rooms are comfortable and 18th century (lovers of contemporary architecture, modern art....stay away). No fitness center on site. No free internet. Free parking in the street from 8 pm to 10 am (but you worry about the car).

“Nice Stay in Austin, Texas” I love these hotels in general and this one is no exception. Great rooms, and very friendly people. The breakfast is better than you get at similar hotels for the same price. Overall, I have no complaints. Located well... just about 5 minutes from downtown and the convention center. I stayed here insted of my downtown convention hotel. Saved some money and got a great room. Also, just another random comment... Country Inn & Suites have one of the better guest frequent stay programs. Lots of earning and redemption opportunities. Stay at the Country Inn, you'll be glad you did.

“Decent hotel, located right at the studio” I stay here for business travel. It's a pretty good hotel. The rooms are larger than normal and the beds comfortable. The pillows are especially good. The bathrooms are large, modern, and better than the ones at the nearby Sheraton (which hsa slightly better bedrooms but is more expensive and lacks the great views.). The buffets here are good but expensive; it's worthwhile to walk across the street to the Citywalk (sp?), which boasts a large number of eateries. Avoid the coffee bar here, which serves substandard brew. The hotel's best feature is its staff; everyone I interacted with was surprisingly friendly and helpful.

“Hyatt meets the W......” This is a recently opened hotel (they told me it was only a couple months since they opened it) and that's one of the good things about it. Apparently, it was an old Barclays Bank office building that has been converted into hotel rooms (W Montreal anyone??) on the one side and luxury residences on the other side. Unfortunately, the entrance to each is not clearly marked and in fact, if you walk through the door marked 75 Wall Street (hotel address) you'll probably enter the residential side. I stayed over a Saturday night and the area is very quiet during that time (a positive if you don't want all of the hustle and bustle of NYC). I was greeted at the door by 2 women who obviously were not used to leisure travelers staying here (or at least very casually dressed ones) as I seemed to have gotten a weird look when first entering. No worries, as I was promptly asked to take a seat and asked if I wanted something to drink. One girl promptly got me a glass of wine while the other proceeded to check me in and then took me directly to my room. I was lucky enough to get a Deluxe King room which is the one with the spinning wardrobe but the bigger draw is the spaciousness of the room---one of the largest standard rooms I've encountered in NYC. Everything was tastefully decorated with low mood lighting and a central panel to control lights and drapes at your bedside. The shower and tub room (as I call it) was huge and very relaxing with a wonderful rainshower head and ample sized bathtub (not super huge but it works just fine). As others have said, the draws here are the complimentary non-alcoholic drinks and snacks in your room----a great selection with about 4 bottles of Voss water, 4 or 5 soft drinks and some OJ and iced tea among the selections. Also, there is complimentary wine at night (until about 10 or 11pm) and coffee (espresso based only) in the morning with some light snacks. You can also purchase other snacks during those times but I didn't see anyone do so while I was there. Free local phone calls and free WiFi are other nice pluses although I had to log in every single time I used the internet which was a bit annoying. There is a nice restaurant on the 2nd level overlooking Water Street and an "unstructured" bar on the mezzanine (basically a bar without a physical bar---intended to resemble your living room). A good sized and outfitted gym on the lower level that is available 24 hrs a day was another plus for me. This is a very nice property and has a lot of touches found in the W hotel chain (low lighting, lounge-y atmosphere, nice bar, great beds, etc) and it's a great location if you need to be in the Financial District for work or want to be in quieter part of New York (definitely on the weekends). There isn't much in the way of eating establishments or bars nearby so if this is your first visit to NYC or you want more nightlife you'd need to take the subway or cabs for that. I was impressed and would like to return but not necessarily at those rates. I also noticed that the renovation wasn't done that great as the fake wood flooring in the bathroom seemed to "pop-up" every time I stepped off it. Somehow I can see the rooms getting a little "tired" and worn-out in a year or two because of that and that's partly why I'm apprehensive. All in all though, it's nice to see one more Hyatt property in the city and I'd like to see what the one on 5th Avenue will look like when it opens soon.

“Decent Hotel” I'm not quite as enamored with this hotel as I had hoped to be, but I really can't find any complaints. It's a very nice hotel. For NYC, the size of my room is great. Some of the design details are great. i LOVE the sinks and design of the sink and shower. Very modern and fun. I agree with a couple of reviewers about a few details being very slighly worn, like the desk and dresser, but it's no big deal. The white noise machine that's built into the wall is great. I haven't had any noise problems at all. Good room service, not obscenely pricey. My only suggestion to the hotel would be better water pressure in the shower and more clerks at the front desk.

“5th SPG property in the City” I stayed downtown this trip as a result of having a meeting in the area. A word about the area - it is uneventful really. Another reviewed called it "soulless" and while I wouldn't go that far, I would say that there are better neighborhoods to stay in. For the hotel, I think this hotel was nicely done. I have an issue with the lobby check in simply because it's small and if there are a lot of people trying to check, it could be crowded. I really enjoyed the decor (even if modern / trendy isn't my personal taste). My room was clean and comfortable. Like many other W's, there was alot of snacks and other items taking up space on the desk. Speaking of the desk, it was slightly small for my business needs. I'm sure a larger room wouldn't have this issue. I absolutely loved the window seat they had. I sat there while preparing for a meeting instead of the desk. Bed was of course, very comfortable. I agree with another reviewer who said it would have been nice to have towel hooks. The counter space was also small. Shower was great though. I used the gym once and preferred the gym at The Westin, mainly for the equipment and space. However, the gym was still good and really my only complaint is having to walk through the lobby to get to the second set of elevators to use the gym. I found the staff to be very friendly here too - not annoying friendly but just enough. BLT restaurant was cute and I really enjoyed my lunch. If I don't stay here again, it would only be because of the location. Otherwise, a great option!

“Good but not Great” Stayed for 4 nights while two conventions were going on. Arrived at 11 pm on a dark, rainy night and had great difficulty figuring out how to get into the hotel (you can do a legal U-turn if coming from the direction we were.) This is not their fault, but just be aware that it's the situation. Our room had been booked through our local fencing club (my son was in a tournament) and I asked at check-in to have it transferred to my credit card and also to our Hyatt Gold number, and I gave the clerk a piece of paper with the number written on it to do so. When the bill was put under the door for checkout, the number wasn't on it, so I had to go get it added. No big deal, but it should already have been done. Neither did this bill have the valet parking charge on it, necessitating another question at the desk. Apparently the checkin clerk should have stamped our valet ticket, we learned. This was the pattern...no major problems, but a few things that should not happen in a hotel of this nature. Other minor problems: housekeeping forgot to clean the coffee pot one day (but didn't forget to leave a new package of coffee); service at the Market Cafe was very slow (it took my sister-in-law over 5 minutes to get a cup of coffee to go even though there was only one other person there; we couldn't even get seated at the hotel restaurant the first day, although there seemed to be quite a few empty tables (we gave up waiting for the host to get off the phone and ate across the street). The heating system seemed very erratic; our room was 77 degrees when we got in, so we cooled it off, but I thought it was odd it had been left set so hot. The hallway the next morning was freezing, and the following morning was baking hot. Again, no big deal, but go figure. On the plus side, the staff was uniformly pleasant and professional, as I have generally found to be the case at Hyatts. The room was very clean and nicely appointed, although clearly "of a certain age." A good selection of toiletries was provided. I personally didn't care for the "ginger" scent they had, but it was something out of the ordinary. No refrigerator. My son realized when we were ready to leave the tournament that he had lost his winter jacket. He thought he must have left it either at the restaurant or in his room. We checked with Lost & Found, but they didn't have it. The front desk said the room hadn't been cleaned yet and he could still use his keycard to go see if it was there. When he got upstairs, he found it HAD been cleaned, so all we could do was fill out a Lost & Found report with its description and our contact information. This was on Monday; on Wednesday morning, I got a call at home that they had found the jacket and would send it to me via DHL if I provided my credit card number. I was very pleased! I didn't request overnight service, but did expect it would go out that day. When we didn't receive it by today (Monday a week after we checked out), and there was still no charge from DHL on my credit card, I called the manager at the number provided on the receipt to follow up. He was most courteous and called me back to let me know it went out today. No explanation of why there was a holdup in sending it, though. Valet parking was another $21/night; if we hadn't arrived so late and had been able to figure out how to get to the Chestnut St. garage, we would have parked there for $12/night, also billable to the room. Valet service was prompt both times we requested the car. Certainly an excellent choice if you have a function at the Convention Center. Plenty of dining within walking distance, and walkable to Short North shopping. We had a convention rate of $115, and had it not been for the minor hiccups, I would have rated it Excellent at this rate.

“Without a Doubt, Best Hotel in Chicago!” I often travel to Chicago from NYC for business and without a doubt, my hotel of choice is the Peninsula. I've tried several other comparable hotels such as the Trump Hotel and I still find myself going back to the Peninsula. Service is fantastic, exactly what you would expect from a Peninsula. Rooms are great, and I often get upgraded now to very large suites which are fantastic. Location is convenient. Nothing to complain about at all. The fact that the Peninsula is not ranked #1 on this list is a crime!

“New Hotel in the Middle of the City” Nice stay. New property in a great location. Rooms were nice - limited availability of bathtubs (we were traveling with young children) but the hotel did their best to accomodate us.

“Lovely Hotel, Great Front Desk Service” This is a lovely hotel, right in the heart of Broadway, close to all the action, near the theater district, close to restaurants, subways, and more! The rooms are superbly decorated and well appointed. The bathrooms are very spacious and well done with comfortable showers and tubs and marble sinks and countertops. The lighting and sound systems in the rooms are very nicely done. Ask for a higher level floor to avoid noise from the street level below. We checked into our room and found the sit down at a desk check in system to be personal and friendly. While we were staying there we needed to do several business items of a personal nature and the front desk staff helped us arrange each of these trips individually. They sat down with us "at the desk" and looked up the information, helping us book cars, drivers, or public transport, making reservations for us, getting information and all sorts of other 'hand on' tasks that went well beyond the normal service you would receive at other 'big' hotels. Our only complaint is that the housekeeping staff never seemed to arrive at a timely hour. We would often wait until well after 2 p.m. for our maid to come to the room. We would go out and come back several times during the morning, only to return to find the room unmade and the maid no where to be found. We complained several times over the course of several days to the front desk. They would try to be helpful and hurry the maid along but it didn't seem to help expedite our particular maid on our particular floor. Otherwise, it is a great hotel.

“Very urban feel, loved it” I stayed here Feb 24-26 for a business meeting which was just around the corner from the hotel. Pros: My room was fully stocked (and I always like Aveda bath products), there was a comfy zebra stripe robe to wear, the shower water pressure was really good, the minibar contained a wide variety of items, and the bed was very comfortable. The doorman was friendly and hailed cabs for us in the rain, the lobby was inviting, and the pleasant front desk staff gave me a travel size hairspray since I forgot mine. I didn't eat at the restaurant but had room service one night which was good. I didn't hear any noise from neighbors at all. Very slight cons: The free wi-fi worked fine in the evenings but I couldn't get a connection in the mornings (maybe everyone was trying to connect at that time). They generously provided 4 towels, so I followed the "green" instructions to hang your towel up and therefore not have it needlessly replaced, but they replaced it anyway. Overall a great stay.

“Lives up to expectations and more!” We recently stayed at the Bryant Park Hotel and found it very relaxing and aesthetically very appealing. It is modern and pared down but the rooms although on the smaller side are efficiently laid out. We stayed in a deluxe queen. The bed was fantastically comfy, solid mattress that felt somewhat like a futon but did seem a bit smaller than our queen bed at home. The bathroom was spacious and had both a tub and shower. The shower had excellent water volume and good temperature control. We did not have much of a view as we were in the back of the hotel but it was very quiet and that was a plus. The metro is at the end of the block and the location was desirable. They are currently putting in the ice skating rink so that was a little disruptive and but the park was still relaxing to hang out in. I would definitely return here.

“Above and Beyond Wonderful” Hotel website offers $150 to $250 credit to room or hotel credit for spa etc. Wonderful hotel. We upgraded to a suite and had a beautiful view of Michigan Ave. The spa type bathroom was unbelievable. Our room had a jet tub and separate shower. The hotel felt very new. Our room had 2 flat screen tvs and dvd player. I had a massage at the hotel spa and it was wonderful as well. We would definately stay here again. The hotel is located inside the 900 shops which has Bloomingdales, Mark Shale, and many other stores. It is a great location right on Michigan Ave. We asked the concierge how we could get impossible tickets to see OPRAH. They made no promises, but that next day my husband and I were at the OPRAH show! What they do is call the Oprah show and ask for tickets. If there are standby tickets available they will put you on a standby waitlist. You have to be on the list, you can't just go to Harpo to possbily get in. There was room on the wait list so we got on the list and there was seat availability and we got in!!

“A relaxing weekend” A really great place to kick-back in San Francisco. I like to stay here when I want to play in the city. Reasonable rates, clean, bright rooms. Great service - wine in the lobby n the evening.

“Great Location---Bad Service” Can't bet the location, central to everything. However, the customer service is the worst. Front desk staff seemed to be bothered whenever you asked them any questions. For example, once we approached the desk and the man looked up at us and had this annoyed look on his face and then went back to his work and ignored us. The doorman was the worst, whenever we asked for a taxi, he told us to go to Broadway and get it ourself! But if your willing to put up with a staff that doesn't care, it's still a great value for the location.

“Lazy on the Lazy River” My family of four, including 10 year old twins, stayed here for vacation for six days during a stretch of record-breaking heat in the summer of 2011. Each day's temperatures were anywhere from 105-110 degrees. Despite this, we found the Hyatt Regency's Hill Country Resort a wonderful, relaxing oasis. My husband had attended a conference here years before, and this time he wanted to bring the family. We used Hyatt Rewards Points to upgrade from a regular room to a Hill Country Suite. The suite was the perfect size. There was a bedroom with king-size bed, living room with pull-out sofa, dining table and chairs, and refrigerator, and bathroom. The closet held an iron/ironing board and bathrobes. There was a coffee maker in the suite. There was also access to an outside terrace (although we found it too hot to sit out there). Everything was very clean. My only complaints were that the bathroom was just a tad small (it was too bad there wasn't a "door" to the toilet, so that someone else could be at the sink), and the walls were somewhat thin. We could hear neighboring rooms at night, and I see others were disrupted by some hallway noise. The resort itself came with an activity guide, put out weekly. There are many activities for children, including free s'mores by the fire pit at night and a nightly movie on the lawn. My "tweens" didn't utilize Camp Hyatt, but for a price it looked to provide nice entertainment and a meal for children while parents spent some alone time. The spa had numerous services, its own pool, and a gift shop. We also didn't utilize the bikes, nature trail, golf course or tennis, again because of the heat. But we spent plenty of time on the Lazy River (called the Rambling River)! There was some "wildlife" around - including birds and squirrels, and some racoons one night - but lots of shade on the river. The activity pool also had volleyball and basketball. I also used the Health Club, and the kids checked out the arcade. A free laundry room was very convenient. On site dining, unfortunately, provided limited options if you're here for several days. Springhouse Cafe was convenient for breakfasts and an occasional dinner; it offered buffets on certain days. We also bought breakfasts (and pizza) at the General Store, and brought back to the room. It was too bad the store closed early (8:00) during the week; it would have been nice for it to be open a couple of more hours. We never ate at Antler's Lodge, as it looked a bit too pricey and dressy for the kids. We found nearby BBQ at Rudy's - an experience unto itself! And there were some chain restaurants, and a nice Tex-Mex, a short drive away. While in San Antonio, we spent one day downtown at River Walk and saw the Alamo. This was maybe a half-hour drive from the resort. SeaWorld is literally down the road, maybe 5 min. We also visited Schlitterbahn, voted best water park in the country. I'll write separately about that. This was about 50-60 min away by car, but made for a much cooler day spent in the water. Overall, this was such a nice time. I am already missing laying in my inner-tube on the Lazy River!

“Elegance,Style Comfort and more” We spent two nights here in July. Having phoned prior,the concierge had confirmation of restaurant bookings waiting in our room. We had a butler and she was amazing.I needed my suit pressed in a hurry after a long day travelling and she had it back to me in 30 minutes! The rooms are Grand in a European (think Paris) style and just so neat. The room daily service was great as was turn down with plenty of water left out and fresh fruit. I highly recommend their special recipe french toast for breakfast , it's unusual and very very tasty!

“Ok place to stay in SF. Nice view.” Stayed at the Holiday Inn for three nights while on vacation in San Francisco. The hotel room is small, but it was nice. We were two persons in the room, and a queen bed felt a bit small. The bathroom was also small, and cold. The room was on the 25th floor, and the view was great. As a tourist, the hotel is a bit far away from everything. It is 30 min+ of walking time down do Fisherman's Wharf, it is however possible to take a buss. Taxi ride down to Fisherman's Wharf costs around $10. The hotel is however at the end of the California street Cable Car, this can be used to get around. Had breakfast at the hotel all three days. The buffet was nice, and a ok price. The people in the front desk was also friendly, and Internet was free, There ware some minor problems: Using the business center (printer and computer) was expensive, and the people working in the gift shop was not very friendly.

“Ft. Worth” My stay here was quite pleasant. I was here for a conference so I didn't get to experience much of the locale beyond eating at a few nearby restaurants. The hotel itself was quite nice, though it was clear it was an older hotel. The hallway on my floor could use a renovation, but the rooms were spacious and my view of downtown from an upper floor was outstanding. Bed was quite comfortable and room was relatively quiet. The hosts and conceierge were quite helpful. Didn't use the fitness facilities but they looked outstanding.

“Ok hotel in a good location” I'm super loyal to Marriott as a Platinum Premier ... Its in a good location - between Market and Mission Sts on Fourth. As for the actual hotel, its a convention/meeting type hotel. Very busy lobby. All the time. Rooms are small but do the trick. Even with my status, no upgrade to even the Concierge level. Bonus that the Concierge lounge is open 7 days a week. Friday morning quiet, Saturday morning PACKED. Gym is ok. Has all the regular equipment. Some have tv's that work. Biggest issue with the hotel was the cab line. The doorman was more interested in getting people to take the sedan service than trying to wave down taxis. I get that taxis are sometimes tough to come by - but we waited 40 minutes (when we got there we were fourth in line....). Watched the doorman count his wad of cash tips four times openly. That's a bit tacky. I would come back but we've enjoyed the JW Marriott near Union Square a bit more.

“Strong Recommend....could be top tier with a few minor tweaks” We spent three nights at the Westin Galleria with our two young children and had a wonderful stay. Our room was standard with two double beds but was recently renovated and beautiful. The windows were spectacular and were nearly floor to ceiling. Our kids loved sitting, reading and drawing on the built in bench with cushions by the window. Nice LG Flat screen and typical lovely Westin beds/bedding. Our bathroom did not have one of the newly renovated full-size showers with frameless glass door, but rather a standard tub-shower combo. Because our kids take baths, this did not matter. Maid service, turn-down requests, bellman requests were all prompt. We had access to the spectacular concierge lounge on the 21st floor: great continental breakfast with smoked salmon and Starbucks and nice evening appetizer presentations (two hot foods such as eggrolls, chicken fingers, cheese selection and beer/wine). The women who worked in the 21st floor lounge were exceptionally helpful and gracious and especially kind to our children. Sometimes it's not worth upgrading to a club level but here it was definitely worth the price. The gym was exceptional with all top-of-the line Lifecycle Fitness equipment and machines. The connection to the Galleria mall was perfect for our kids and keeping them occupied with diversions to the ice rink, shopping, etc. The few issues we had were as follows: (1) the $10 charge for WIFI per day was absurd at a hotel of this caliber. Is Westin really making that much money on this charge to leave customers feeling nickel and dimed on what is an essential service to the modern traveler? Especially for SPG members or those paying extra for club level access, it's time to bag this silly incidental. (2) the pool area was lovely with great cabanas and nice fluffy towels. However, as echoed by previous comments, the water was unheated and nearly unswimmable. A little heating would go a long way. One other minor point: I had a great meal at the Second Floor restaurant but the service during the day was mediocre: it took almost an hour to get a sandwich and a bowl of soup. All told, these are minor issues (other than WIFI) compared to the positive aspects of this hotel. A strong recommend.

“Near Perfection” I booked before it opened with a little trepidation, but the rate was too good to pass up. Any concerns were immediately put at ease when I walked into the lobby. It is a beautiful inner city hotel with a highly attentive staff. Location is closer to the business district, but walkable to the harbor and a variety of good restaurants. However, the hotel restaurant was outstanding. Great food and even better service! The only disappointment was that the room was a little on the small side, but very comfortable and an amazing view.

“Günstig für New York und gute Lage” wir waren 3 nächte in diesem hotel. es liegt in der 6th ave unweit des times square, ca 15 minuten zu fuss. der empfang war freundlich aber es wurde unsere buchung nicht gefunden. das hotel hat eher eine kleine empfangshalle und nur 2 lifte, was bei ab und anreise mit gruppen zu wartezeiten führen kann. die zimmer sind sehr klein. typisch für die usa überall teppichboden, welcher nicht grad rein sein kann. es gab einen flat TV, keine mini bar oder kühlschrank, kein duschgel und keine klimaanlage. wir waren in einem höheren stockwerk, jedoch war lauter strassenlärm zu hören. es gab ein restaurant. zimmer war ohne frühstück. Free W-Lan ! hotel war trotzdem, wenn man nicht unmengen an kohle ausgeben will, für NYC ok.

“Noisy and understaffed” I stayed at the W New York for one night last August. Having waited in line at immigration at JFK for two hours, I was ready to collapse into bed upon arrival at the hotel. On arriving at the hotel, I was practically thrown out of the cab by the waiting hordes outside. I looked in vain for someone to help me with my suitcase (it was heavy!) and in the end a passer-by took pity on me and helped me inside the hotel. I left my suitcase at reception to be brought up, but waited almost an hour in my room for it, before going back to reception to fetch it myself. The receptionist promised me a free breakfast as compensation for the poor service, but after I checked out I noticed I had paid for my breakfast. The room was nicely furnished but tiny - any longer than one night would have been claustrophobic. The lobby was more like a nightclub than a hotel. Bliss toiletries in the bathroom were a nice touch. The guys in the room next door decided to party all night, and the walls were too thin to block out the noise. I couldn't wait to check out and won't be coming back. I emailed the manager afterwards with my complaint and never heard back.

“Beautiful Room and Fantastic Breakfast” This property has a great modern feel. There is a Starbucks right there. The rooms were beautiful with stunning views of the water. The robes in the room were amazing. The bathrooms were huge. The staff was average to great. Check-in staff was snooty and we seemed to be interrupting a very serious conversation between two employees. The breakfast buffet was the second best breakfast I have ever had at a Marriott property (THE best is JW Cancun); my husband and I said that we would return just for the breakfast! We had to park our vehicle several blocks from the property at a meter so that was a bit of an inconvenience though it was very cheap.

“Underpar service for busy business traveller, very limited room service” I have stayed in this hotel several times and most recently in March, 2010; I love the location. but I would not stay here again---there is absolutely no room service in the wee hours, and I am a business traveller that is ready for my coffee at 5am. I am a woman who does not want to traipse the streets at that hour. I spoke with the front desk and eamailed cusotmer service but for two months my comments have been ignored. I was with male colleagues who also wanted late night food, and were equally dis-ssatisfied. If this hotel wants to attract busy business travellers, they need to modify its in room- dining to 24/7 like all other top notch hotel programs.

“Upscale, convenient & very reasonable!” I travel quite often, and I really enjoyed this hotel. The property is close to Love Field and in great shape and surprisingly inexpensive.
