From the Navigator who greets incoming guests to the housekeeping staff to the Concierge hostesses, all employees were enthusiastic and attentive. The room was modern and attractive with a very comfortable bed, large flat screen TV with AV inputs, a safe and a small refrigerator. Parking was thin the first night but easier the second night.

“A Very Good Stay” We stayed at the Fairmont recently and I was pleasantly surprised. As many prior reviews have stated, the service is incredible. The location was great too since we needed to be at the Convention Center. Rooms were quiet and we slept well. The hotel was not near as dated as some reviews state. It is not sleek & modern but it didn't look quite as worn or in need of a renovation as some had posted. My only complaint was the Starbucks closes really early - but hey - they at least had a Starbucks! We come here every February for NCA Nationals (this was our 6th year) and this hotel & the Ritz are my two favorites in Dallas when I look at everything - service, location, quiet at night, etc. Oh - And I guess I would prefer Queen beds as opposed to double beds - but that was the only other thing I would change.

“A Park Avenue Standout” We stayed at 70 Park the weekend of May 19-20. I was in Manhattan to take place in the Gran Fondo NYC. From the moment we walked in the staff was very friendly and accommodating. They not only helped us with all our bags and bike, but had treats waiting for our dog. We were in a King Premier room (#315). While the elevator and hallways were tight the room was spacious. Large enough for two people, a dog and a race bike tucked in the corner. The bathroom was a very nice size and had a hot tube built into the shower (a nice feature for after a long ride or day in NYC). The bed was very comfortable. The room had a closet plus an armoire style standing closet with a safe inside. It also had a very nice velvet couch that our dog took over and made her own. What was really nice was that the room was very quiet, even though we were only on the third floor we barely heard any street noise. The staff was very accommodating with our dog, besides the treats they brought up a huge dog bed and bowls. One of the staff even played with her as the maid cleaned up our room. The location is great, only a few blocks from 5th ave, 42nd street and a short cab ride to most places. The hotel wine happy hour was very popular. Being that the lobby is small and the happy hour was packed we barely had a place to stand. But it's a nice touch after a long day. I would highly recommend staying here and will be back the next time we visit NYC.

“Excellent Location & Staff” This hotel is excellent value at Christmas time. The staff are lovely and very helpful, the rooms were clean and very comfortable and the breakfast was first class. The made-to-order omletes at breakfast are a must. I would definitely stay here again. My one little complaint is that the pool was cold, the jacuzzi was too hot, minor irritants which can be easily fixed. My teenage daughter enjoyed the internet facilities available in the lobby. Washington DC is a fantastic holiday venue!

“Excellent Little Place” I stayed at this hotel for six nights having booked it via Hotwire for $59 per night. All I can say is, wow what a value!! The hotel itself has small but adequate rooms. My room also had a small wet bar with microwave, refridgerator and coffee maker. Each morning they serve a very good continetial breakfast in their nice restaurant. A moring newspaper is also complimentary. The breakfast alone is a huge money and time saver. The hotel was nicely decorated and seems updated. The staff was very friendly and quite helpful. It is not near the touristy Union Square area, but I found that to be more relaxing as it was very quiet without the constant siren and cable car noises. The Muni (subway) is about a five block walk and you can get anywhere from there. There are many very nice restaurants within a two blocks in the Hayes Valley area. Overall a great place to stay, unless you are traveling with younger kids, then it could be challenging if you are trying to do the tourist thing due to the location.

“A liitle tired but value for money for downtown San Francisco” My company has a $200 per night (plus taxes) rate for this place. As you enter it looks very grand and is enormous for a hotel in the center of downtown San Francisco. The rooms are not quite up to the standard of a Westin but then it's not bad for the rate, especially when other hotels in the area are between 50% and 100% more expensive. Rooms are big and the beds are very comfortable. The climate control was noisy and clunky. The disappointing aspect was the bathroom, with a ridiculously low shower rail. I did wonder if I'd been put in a room for disabled people. There were a lot of extra handrails, but the toilet wasn't raised and the basin wasn't lowered, so it was useless for able and disabled people. I took room service as I arrived late. It was very efficient and had a good selection of healthy items on the menu. As room service goes it was above average. The same could not be said for breakfast. I did drive to the hotel and self parked in the Union Square parking, which a half the price of valet parking.

“Nice Hotel in Great Location” This is one of the better Marriott brand hotels I've stayed in (not including JW Marriotts, etc). The staff is friendly, the rooms are comfortable etc. Best of all, the location is terrific. The hotel is adjacent to the light rail line, and only a block away from the Sixteenth Street Mall. The Sixteenth Street Mall essentially runs the length of downtown Denver, from the state capitol building to within four blocks or so of Coors Field. It is closed to traffic other than free shuttle buses which run its length. The buses are clean and run almost continuously. I never had to wait more than a couple of minutes for one. This puts the Marriott essentially within a one block walk of the capitol, Coors Field, and a huge variety of restaurants, shops, and entertainment.

“Lovely Hotel” The Michelangelo is a lovely boutique hotel close to Times Square. The lobby is beautiful with European art and a very nice bar area. The staff was courteous and helpful during our stay. The rooms are quite large for NYC and the bed was very comfortable. Very nice furnishings in the rooms. We will definitely stay here again.

“Exceeded my expectations” Stayed for one night on a business trip to a site near the Medical Center. I was really surprised at the nice layout of the guest rooms - sitting room and work desk separated by a partial wall from the bedroom/bath/sink area. Very functional. The lobby staff remembered my name and were very helpful in booking the free shuttle to our work site for the following morning. The breakfast was better than expected as well: egg sandwiches with a nice green spicy salsa, oatmeal, fruit, cold cereal, and the usual pastries and waffles. A small bar/coffee area in the lobby was also a plus. The hotel is pretty close to the airport, but relatively far from Riverwalk - but a perfect location for me on a business trip.

“Man, I love Loews” Loews Cherry Creek is a great hotel with a great location. The hotel has a number of nice touches, and their staff retention makes this property a cut above. With a doorman/bellman and a concierge, this is an upscale hotel. The front desk personnel are the same each time I've been there, and the same is true for restaurant staff. The driver (Loews will take you downtown via SUV) has been there 7 years! The parking is free and close, and the hotel appears to have a contract with a taxi company, as there is always a taxi standing by in the parking lot. Out of more than a dozen visits, I've not seen a taxi there once - amazing. Although the rooms show some wear, the comforter for the bed and the furniture are great, and the comfort of the bed rivals the Westin's. The exercise room seems to be an afterthought, and the hotel lacks a pool. For business travel, this is not an issue. The Loews chain does advertise they love kids, but the lack of pool and the room layout are more geared for business. Internet service is lacking. It is highly latent, and has terrible upload speed. It makes it hard to do business. There are times I have booked other properties, knowing I have a heavy workload to address at night. If they resolved this, they would have a customer for life. * cleanliness above average * beds are great (wonderful sheets, comforter) * staff are great (consistent, well-trained, friendly) * Internet below average (hard to use for VPN due to upload) * room controls are great (digital) * price above average (rate matches hotel quality) * location above average (Cherry Creek is central to Denver)

“Terrific rennovation job! Great centrally located hotel.” This is a great hotel in the heart of downtown San Jose. The recently rennovated hotel looks very plain from the outside but the inside is a completely different story. Stylish decor with the kind of in room amenities you'd expect from a far pricer boutique hotel. Computer desk with comfy adjustable leather chair, expresso maker, iHome system, etc. Parking is moderately priced for a downtown location and is right next to the hotel. Location is very convenient if you're going to the Tech Musuem or Performing Arts Center and just a short walk to the SJSU campus. I highly recommend this property.

“Outstanding service; incredible location” We stayed at the Taj for a week in October and had a fantastic experience. Since we were staying for several days, we paid for the Club level upgrade and it was completely worth it. The food and drinks in the Club room were fantastic and the service was outstanding. Overall, the service at every level of the hotel was fantastic - from the front desk, to the concierge, to housekeeping - service was never overlooked. The bed was comfortable. The bathroom was small, but the tub was very deep so it was easy to take a very luxurious bath. Housekeeping was thorough and the room was always clean. The business center is small (two computers), so if you don't have your laptop, you may have to wait for a computer. Depending on your schedule, this may or may not be a big deal. The location is fantastic. Since it's at the top of Newbury, we had our pick of really nice restaurants in the area or a short T-ride to the North end. So, I don't know what the hotel restaurant is like. However, we did order late night room service once, and it was solid. Hard to complain about 24 hr room service, since it's getting harder and harder to come by. The mini-bar could have been stocked with more boutique snacks and liquor, but that's pretty minor. A $3.75 Sam Adams is a pretty good deal at nearly any bar, and especially a hotel mini-bar.

“Nice Stay, rooms are on the small side” If I could give the hotel 3.5 stars I would. I had higher expectations and they were not met. The Alex is part of the "Leading Hotels of the World." I joined their organization (LHW) in order to receive additional amenities. I am not sure that money was well spent. I booked a two bedroom suite for my daughter's graduation from grad school. There were three people in the suite including myself, my husband and step-mother. We stayed for three nights. I called ahead of time and spoke with the Manager, Mary Lou Pollock, who assured me that we would receive excellent service. She did not follow up, nor did she make us feel welcome. At the outset, I was told that breakfast was only for two people (in our two bedroom suite with two king beds). If I had booked two separate rooms which would have cost less, I would have had breakfast for four. They did agree to include breakfast for three. There was also an issue because they wanted to charge an additional fee for the third person in the two bedroom suite. This also did not make sense to me because we had two king bedrooms. The suite was pretty stark and very small. The furniture in the living room area i was very low to the ground, not too comfortable. The beds were comfortable. The elevator system was very quirky. I found the front desk to be very snotty. They were not particularly welcoming or helpful. We were sent a lovely welcome note addressed to some other guests who were attending a VIP wedding ...which as a result all other hotel guests were ignored. The hotel services and amenities were very disappointing. There are too many hotels in NYC to bother with this hotel a second time. They do not deserve repeat business due to their lack of customer service and follow through. The upside: I thought the food at Riingo was surprisingly delicious.I also thought the service at Riingo was top notch.

“Great location, wonderful desk staff, yucky rooms.” I recently stayed at the double tree with my family (kids) fo a little mini break in the city. The location was great as my teenager wanted some quality time at the Galleria for shopping. The front desk was so friendly and helpful. Housekeeping also very quick to help. However, the rooms are so out of date. The property needs a big renovation. It was clean enough, but the air conditioning unit was old and made noise. Windows were very dirty. Everything just very old. I bought this room with a Living Social coupon that stated that the property was newly renovated. They either have another section that has been updated, or else LS considers 1993 as recent.

“Good but not great !” The screened off drinks terrace gives the exterior a bit of an unfinished look.Thats the front wall.Our room on the back had the hills view and that Hollwood sign in the distance,and the unfortunate school yard below.To compensate the noise double glazing should be in place of the strange opening "french doors" windows. The staff are good,but an upgrade was denied against my expensive "Accor Favorite Guest "loyalty card.Thats OK,except that the two of us and four bags and a room service trolley were more than our little triangular room space could hold.The shower was large but we chose not to eat in there.Exceptionally good air condition unit.LED bed lights,and some other toys,but where's the space and quiet? The bar and restaurant are fab designs,the locals know how to party,dont go looking for any quiet corners here.You pay for the style too. I did not see any good near by restaurants , I should have asked the friendly concierge. The fastest check out in the West. I would stay in another district , if I return .

“Would have given it 5 stars but...” This is an excellent place to stay when arriving or departing from LAX. I have to give the staff 5 stars - not just one of them but all of them were extremely sweet, helpful and friendly. The rooms were up to Hilton property quality, beautiful and clean. We stayed here recently when we arrived and then again when we were departing LAX. The first night we had a room that was near the elevator - which incidentally I don't usually like and have listed on my Hilton profile as something I don't want as in "please put me in a room far away from the elevator." However, in this particular property the rooms nearest the elevator are furthest away from the airport runways and accompanying noise. On our last night, we were in a room on the far opposite side of the property from the elevator and noise woke up us at 6 AM. So..ask for a room near the elevator. It would have been smart when designing the hotel to reverse the layouts of these particular rooms and put the main bedroom near the front door! Anyway, the shuttle from the airport is free and very convenient at LAX. And then, if you have time, you can take the Manhattan Beach trolley for $5 from the hotel over to the beach area for sightseeing, clubs and restaurants. This hotel is incredibly convenient and the staff wonderful - wish I could give it a 5 star rating but the noise!!! We will know better next time.

“Lovely and well loved Victorian” We arrived for a two night stay and were greeted with a warm welcome. Our suite was spacious, well furnished, and very comfortable. This is an older hotel with all the quirks that come with an older building, small elevator, slightly dated decor, tight odd hallways, but all very well cared for and recently painted with new carpeting. There is not an in house restaurant, but Sarabeth's next door provides room service and is literally two steps out the front door. The neighborhood is charming with nice restaurants - Island, Table d'Hote, and Paola's all on the same block. The only smear on an otherwise lovely stay was the hot water system failed sometime in the night and we were hot water the morning of our departure. The only concession offered - and it was now 10AM - was to comp the internet charge. Too bad...breakfast at least would have been nice. There is construction going on in the neighborhood at the moment, so don't plan to sleep in.

“Not a bad place, but not exactly great.” My family and I just stayed there a couple of weeks ago due to its proximity to our house which was being worked on. We stayed 4 nights, and it was not too bad. Although we pretty much just slept there, we found the room to be spacious, fairly clean, albeit dark and stuffy. The bathroom was clean but very very small - no counter space! And the shower was just plain weird (no tub) but clean. The bedspreads (we had 2 beds) did not look that clean, so I examined the blankets and sheets closely. Found a few gray hair in the blankets! Yup. Sure did. I quickly asked for clean flat sheets to cover our blankets. Oh, and I pulled off the bedspreads entirely. The next day and went home and took our beddings with us. I know this is not an option for most people, but because I could, therefore I did. The breakfast was buffet style and consisted of bread and bagels which you can toast yourself, pasties, hard boiled eggs, juice, coffee & tea. Although it wasn't the greatest, it was good to have. In the evening they serve fresh baked Otis Spunkmeyer cookies, and we enjoyed them, of course. The parking was not too bad, but the spaces are small and narrow. The hotel was not full that week so we always found a space, but it would be hard if it were full. The pool was very small and didn't look that clean so we never used it. The evening clerk was extremely nice and responsive. Had a problem with the remote and the repairman came very quickly. The day staff was so so. Housekeeping was okay. Don't know if they change the blankets and bedspreads with each guest, and don't know if the hair simply got stuck to the blankets even after washing (which happen sometimes). Since I brought our own beddings, I didn't want anyone to mess with our beds so I asked them to only remove the trash and replace the towels, and they were happy to oblige. Would I stay there again? Probably if we had work done on the house again, but I'll remember to bring my own comforter.

“Park Central, NYC. Good location-Mediocre experience” We just got back from New York after a family reunion weekend. My folks booked rooms for us at this hotel, and since they were paying, there was not much choice in the matter. Truthfully, the location was ideal. Close to the theatre district, close to Times Square, right next to a major subway line, and very easy access to taxis. Our first impression was good. The doorman took care of our luggage and whisked us to the front desk. We were greeted with a smile and checked in quickly. We had asked for two adjoining rooms, which they did not accomodate, but we were only 3 doors away. The Bellman escorted us to our rooms. Neither room had card keys that worked, so the Bellman let us in with his Master key and went back down to get us proper key cards. The rooms were OK. Reasonably spacious for New York, with two double beds (we asked for that), a view of the street, decent bathroom, decent closet with a safe and a flat screen TV. The decor was tired, and there were some stains and marks on walls and in the bathroom. But no real big problem. Other issues: One of the elevator banks was under repair, so it took a while to get an elevator. My in-room phone's handset was broken, so I had to communicate exclusively by speaker-phone. The room rate was $250 which I gather is cheap by NYC standards, so I suppose you get roughly what you pay for. The lobby was nice, although constantly busy, and on our departure day, they charged us $3 per stored bag until we had to leave for our flight home. We had a nice weekend and did not spend much time in the room, so it was not a hardship, and the location was really ideal. PS: Had the worst brunch/meal I've ever had in my entire life at a place called Frederick's on Lexington near 28th St. Avoid it like the plague!

“Great location, spacious rooms, good amenities!” We stayed here for three nights over a weekend in mid-July. The location of the hotel was excellent; it was about three blocks to Navy Pier, the Ohio Street Beach, and Lake Michigan, and about two blocks to the Chicago River. There is a grocery/store pharmacy called Dominick's across the street, so it's easy to buy drinks and snacks for your room, although that is almost unnecessary with the free hot breakfast served every morning and the nightly manager's cocktail party (even on weekends). Because my spouse has priority with Hilton, we were upgraded to a corner suite on the 17th floor (the highest floor), with excellent views of the river. The standard suites weren't quite as large as the corner suites (there's an odd window from their living area to the hotel atrium, so one could see in), but were still a great size, with a separate bedroom, bathroom, wet bar/microwave/fridge area, and living room with sofa bed and desk (the corner suites also had two chairs as part of the sofa grouping). There is an indoor pool and fitness center, as well as a gift shop, bar, and large lobby lounge area. There is no outdoor space at this hotel, which was the only drawback for me. A little sundeck, or other outdoor relaxation area (no matter how small) would have been welcome. The hotel spans an entire block, so it is possible to enter from multiple locations. There is an AMC movie theatre right next door, along with a bowling alley, PJ Clarke's restaurant, a Japanese restaurant, and a Walgreens pharmacy. There aren't many non-chain, unique restaurants in the immediate two block area, which was another slight drawback, but it was a quick walk to more cuisine-friendly streets. It is necessary to take two sets of elevators to reach the guest rooms. One set of elevators only travels three floors, from the street to the mezzanine (meeting) level to the sky (lobby) level. Then you must get off and walk to the other side of the hotel to catch another set of elevators that goes from floors 5 to 17. I understand that this set-up discourages non-guests from hanging out in the lobby and using the restrooms, but it is slightly inconvenient. I must say, though, that this hotel has the fastest elevators that I've seen in a long time! If you hesitated the slightest bit before trying to board, the doors closed and the elevator whisked away. (But that's probably why we almost never waited for an elevator, even being on the 17th floor during a busy summer weekend.) I would definitely stay here again, even considering all the other hotel options nearby.

“Nice Hotel” I had the pleasure of staying at this hotel for one night. The staff was friendly. The rooms were small, but clean. The hotel offered free continental breakfast. For parking, it is best to go to the adjacent mall and park there.

“Good Location, rather dated hotel” I have just returned from a two night stay in The Menger Hotel. The beds were on the small size although the room was large. We had a very damp room, which was felt in the sheets and soft furnishings. Also our clothes and personal belongings. It was noticable as a damp feel and smell. We stayed with family and we had joining rooms, which were both the same (DAMP) My cousin was in a different room, but asked to move so we could link rooms. Their original room was also damp. The pool was nice and staff seemed friendly. (We asked them to clean mould off the joining doors so the kids did not get bad stomachs. ) You come to San Antonio to see the Alamo and it was just across the street so location wise it is fantastic. The Riverside is just yards away so it is good but check to see if your room is ok first.

“très bien” personnel accueillant, hotel propre, chambre spacieuse... jacuzzi, piscine(un peu petite), sale de fitness, ordinateur a la disposition de ceux qui n'aurait pas de pc portable, petit dej très bon... très bien!

“Absolut nix besonderes - in keinerlei Hinsicht” Das Westin Charlotte ist so wie man es erwartet - nettes und absolut unspektakuläres Zimmer, nette und absolut unspannende Lobby, und so könnte ich eigentlich beliebig weiter machen. Ich denke das Hotel lebt von seiner Nähe zum Kongresszentrum, von der ich ebenfalls profitiert habe - es sind keine 100m Luftlinie. Das ist vermutlich auch der einzige Grund warum man hier absteigen sollte (und in Charlotte). Da das Hotel für die Konferenz gebucht war, konnte ich nicht das Starwood Platinum Upgrade in Anspruch nehmen und hatte ein ganz normales Zimmer. Das war (bis auf die Gebrauchsspuren) in der kleinen Badewanne absolut in Ordnung. Was kann ich mehr sagen - in der Form absolut ausreichend aber keinerlei Grund für Begeisterung ...

“A Comfortable Sleep But You Might Eat Breakfast Elsewhere” On a trip south, I spent the night in Charlotte NC area in order to see old friends. This was my first stay the this location. There are five SpringHill Suites around Charlotte and this one had the lowest price and was near enough to where I wanted to be and far enough away from Charlotte traffic. Positives? Nice staff; comfortable sleep; good air conditioner; nice selection of TV; comfortable couch (although room was smaler than some other SpringHill locations that I have stayed;) overall, quiet (except for al the kids staying there for soccer games.) Negatives? Hallways incredibly hot; breakfast area for "getting food" is small and cramped; not a lof breakfast selections to be seen; business area is in "middle" of dining area; walls/doors allowed noise in (perhaps it was the kids on cell phones outside my door talking loudly?); and, lack of ice and/or freezer in rooms. The hotel also needs some maintenance. Shower head for instance. See photo. Hotel is convenient to Tanger Outlets and Charlotte Speedway as well as all that is Charlotte but beware of interstate construction.

“Large pleasant rooms and a good location” I have stayed at the Rittenhouse and have had good experiences each time. The service personnel from front desk, concierge and door staff are excellent and very pleasant. The rooms are large, if a little old fashioned, mini bar, separate dressing area, large comfortable bathroom with good amenities, fluffy towels and good water pressure. Good bed and lighting and good wifi reception in rooms. A very good location to use as a base on Rittenhouse Sq, walking distance to restaurants, shops and the historical sights. The price is creeping up which is making the Rittenhouse less of a good value for what is in essence a dependable, comfortable luxury level stay

“Clean, Reliable, Friendly” Given the audience for a Hilton Garden Inn, the competition should take note of this particular hotel. I've stayed here at least a half dozen times over the past year and the staff is consistently friendly and helpful, the rooms are always clean and comfortable, the furniture and bathrooms are all up to date and the hotel is in a great location to hit up some great casinos or the ballparks in downtown Detroit. My only complaints are that the "health club" is pretty anemic (only 3 machines and a small rack of free weights) and the breakfast buffet could offer some more healthy offerings. However, there's nothing about this location that makes me think twice or hesitate to stay here. It's a solid choice if you have to stay in Detroit.

“Great Stay! Great Customer Service!” A taste of the great customer service started before we ever landed in DC. In addition to the "standard" "Welcome on your upcoming trip" email from WEstin, we received a customized "Welcome" email from Sloane Aureli, the "Stay Relations Manager" thanking me for my loyalty as a Starwood Gold member. We emailed back saying thanks, informing her that we would be arriving early and would really love it if our one king bed could be changed to two doubles--not available when we booked and what my teenage daughter really wanted on this trip to drop her off for a summer program at Georgetown. We arrived at hotel and although no early check in was available (which was fine--we stored our bags and went and saw family members) Sloane had worked her magic with the front desk and we had two double beds-meaning I did not have to suffer through whiny teenage daughter (or get kicked by her in bed at night!). The rooms were spotless. Bathroom huge with separate WC, stall shower and sunken tub. Easy walk to everything we needed to stock the room with Diet Coke, Water, etc. from CVS and Walgreens. Doormen were about the friendliest I have ever met and very helpful in getting cabs, etc. Easy walk to restaurants (great lunch at casual Devon & Blakely) and to Whole Foods where we picked up pastries for cousins who treated us to brunch at their home. I've lived in DC and visit often--We will definitely be back to this property. Thanks All who made the stay so pleasant.

“Gutes amerikanisches Hotel, schlechtes Hyatt” Ganz okay, aber nicht mehr. Liegt relativ zentral, im Financial District / Chinatown. U-Bahn in Laufnähe. Service und Standart, sowie Einrichtung sind nicht wirklich Hyatt. Etwas einfach und nichts besonderes. Rezeption ist etwas umständlich zunächst über Treppen und dann noch mit Fahrstuhl zu erreichen. Peronal ist hilfsbereit, aber die Wartezeiten an der Rezeption sind oft inakzeptabel!

“Hot Hell Hole” Last year I fled from this awful hotel after 1 night. The antiquated Heating/AC system can only supply heat to the whole hotel or A/C to the whole hotel. My room was like a sauna but no A/C was available. Even a Red Roof inn will provide A/C on demand but not this place. The stated "Panoramic Manhattan Skyline View" was of a balcony on the tower across the street. One could die waiting for the elevator to arrive. The Front desk was unconcerned that I was not happy with my room. I would describe their attitude as snotty. The rooms are worn with nicked furniture. Modern Design requires good care to remain attractive. My room looked cheap from wear. Even the windows were caked with filth, the seals between the double pane glass had failed; allowing water and dirt to be trapped inside. Again no upkeep. An unusually large minority of the guests smoked constantly and just the elevator door opening on the smoking floors was enough to choke a non-smoking guest. I checked out a day early and moved to the infinitly better W Times Square. Avoid this creaking pile like the plague.

“Beautiful hotel with a terrible bed” I am really torn about my stay at the Ace Hotel. The lobby is spectacular, the service was courteous, the location convenient. The room itself was a nice size, the shower was outstanding and I really liked the bathroom products (shampoo, body wash). The room's decor was inviting and interesting; there was always something new to discover. It was an absolute pleasure in every way until bedtime. My husband and I stayed in room 523 and we had the most terrible night sleep. The mattress was the hardest, most unforgiving bed I have ever slept in. We both ended up sleeping about two hours solid because we were tossing and turning so much. As we were in the city for work the next morning, it was extremely frustrating laying awake knowing that we were going to exhausted the next day. I am aware that the firmness of a mattress is a subjective thing, but I can't imagine that the average person would enjoying sleeping on a bed that hard. It seems as though the Ace Hotel spent too much time developing the aesthetic and brand of their establishment and forgot their most basic purpose: to provide a comfortable place for people to sleep. I would love to go back to the Ace Hotel, but I'm not sure that I would because of my poor night sleep.

“Rooms are small but great nonetheless” I booked a Deluxe Room but was upgraded to a Sky View Corner Room as a Platinum member even though I am not an Ambassador. I think this is unusual and likely it was because the hotel was very full on a holiday weekend, but it was certainly very nice. We had a great view of the Hudson and a decent view of downtown from the 34th floor. We ended up spending one evening sipping on drinks by the window, and although they didn't really have coffee tables, the windowsill was perfect for holding our drinks and snacks. Much more private and quiet than going to a roof top bar with just as nice of a view! The room, although small, was nice. The bed is comfortable and the shower has both a "regular" shower and a rain shower. One downer for a place as nice as this is that there were no bath tubs! I know space in NYC is precious, but how can you not have a bath tub??? Otherwise, the room was nicely decorated and supplied. The bed was comfortable and there was a large TV and even a computer in the room. The location by Times Square is great if that's what you like, but it's also a block removed from the noise on Broadway, so it's quieter. There's also a Shack Shack downstairs although we opted to go with other food options.

“Great for kids, but can get crowded” Took our daughter here to meet the grandparents, et al. for a mini-family reunion and to escape the heat and crime of Laredo. This was last weekend in August before school started, and the place was packed with families. I really couldn't complain, as we were here for the kids. I guess everyone else had the same idea we did. The rooms were fine, and decorated in Hill Country fashion. The pool and river were fabulous, though they got crowded late in the day. Thankfully, they had several pools, with one for kiddos and one exclusively for adults. We ate at the grill by the pool, and the food was palatable. Not offensive, but just slightly above every other poolside grill I've been to. The casual place inside was OK as well. They also have a nice little mini-mart onsite where you can get coffee, hot dogs, etc... They also do a booming business in beer. You can buy 6-packs for the pool/river for an only slightly exorbitant prices. It is, however, cheaper than buying 6 beers from the bar. The big bar inside is quite nice, though curiously empty considering how crowded the place was. Good selection of bourbon and tequila. Overall, the place is pretty cool for families, but it isn't cheap.

“Decent Hotel, but a few too many problems” My spouse and I arrived at the San Carlos on a Wed night for a 2-night stay. We checked in and were told we "were upgraded to a better room", whatever that meant - but we were pleased. We arrived on the 4th floor and immediately all you could smell was stale smoke. We overlooked this assuming our room would be fine, but it too also smelled badly of stale smoke. I thought rooms in NYC were non-smoking, but apparently I was wrong given the air purifier functioning in our room, as well as an ashtray in the top drawer of the nightsand. After trying to deal with it for about an hour, we finally we down and asked for a new room. We were told the bell captain would be right up to move us. After 20 minutes of packing, and still no bell captain, I finally went downstairs asked for our keys to our new room, and headed back up sans the bell captain to help us. My spouse and I relocated to what was promised to be a "comparable room" on the 6th floor. Unfortunately we got downgraded from a King to a Queen, and also had a handicapped room with a disgusting tile bathroom floor with visible dirt in the cracks. To make matters worse, I opened the toilet and found someone else's waste there - unflushed! I flushed once, and quickly realized the issue, it was clogged. Immediately water started running over the top and on to the floor - so we called the front desk. Staff showed up with a wet/dry vac and got rid of the water, but not the feeling in the back of our head that we would now be using a bathroom where fecies had spilled over and on to the floor. One of the perks was that after about 10 minutes after this fiasco we did receive a platter of wine and other snacks as an apology from the hotel. Other positive notes of the hotel included the location, free wireless, and a second floor business center/lounge area with 6 working computers. In hotels much larger than the San Carlos, I have seen just one or two computers that the hotel expects all guests to share. It wa a welcome sight to see the 6 options available. In short, we had a bad experience that kept our stay from being really enjoyable. I hope it was a one time issue and just bad luck.

“Wow...relaxed environment and wake up refreshed and renewed....breathe deep!” Upon arrival, my allergies were alleviated due to the clean smell of white tea and somehow the pollen from outside was alleviated. The normal rooms are small but tastefully redecorated from when it was a Wyndham. Thedouble shower head was awesome and water pressure made the neck massage a great wakeup call. The elevators were fast and are made of glass. I recommend you definately eat at 400 West. Awesome menu to refuel eier in the morning, afternoon or evening. To belike a native and not what locals call "zonies" (people from the neiboring state of Arizona) ask for Kelly or Lindsay to be your server. Both are excellent and will be so attentive to you. The hostess is Zulema Lopez and looks like Jennifer Lopez and has the same hourglass figure. She is extremely personable and a local and can give you good pointers on where to go and see in San Diego. If you cannot find the concierge, remember Zulema has the know on where to go. If you visit San Diego and stay at the Westin, you have to experience the 5 star breakfast buffet and meet Kelly, Lindsay, and Zulema. The experience will leave you refreshed, renewed and refueled. If you can not find them,ask for Randy and he willgiveyou theVIP treatment and ensure you are well taken care of.

“Convenient location ...” The location is perfect ... it's next to 5th ave and about 10 minute walk to Broadway / Time Square. Although I think the front desk staff needs a little improvement. Upon arrival I saw how one of them was talking with an attitude to a guest. I'm assuming the guest had some issues . Just the tone wasn't very pleasing to see especially since it was quite busy. The AC is still old fashion because it's an old building. You can't control it. The engr. staff had to open a window to cool my room and once it cooled down I couldn't close the window so I had to cover it with stuff to keep the room warm. They use Styrofoam cups in the gym. This is something they should consider changing for the environment. Overall, Location and the room was great. Big and spacious. The bathroom is a little bit small but I guess most New York Hotels are the same. I paid 299 a night . It's a little bit pricey ( because of the temperature/ ac issues ) otherwise it's perfect.

“Solid, convenient property with room for growth” I stayed here while visiting the University of Texas and came away impressed. The hotel is a convenient drive or walk to the Erwin Center, football stadium and points on the northeast side of campus. Walkers should use extra caution since you must cross a highway overpass to get to campus. As the hotel is close to the highway, it is relatively easy and inexpensive to get to and from the airport - $20 in both directions by cab Renovations are well underway and have already occurred on the 6th floor, where most guests appear to be staying right now. These renovations are likely reflected in the desk furniture and bathrooms, which appeared to be fairly new. The paint job in the room also seemed recent. The management would be well advised to update the elevators, which appeared to be too slow and too few in number to handle the hotel. Times are slow, but they could also benefit from having another waiter or waitress in the evening to handle bar traffic and dinner menu service. Using a lighter color tile in the shower might also inspire more confidence in its overall cleanliness. Upgrading the restaurant quality would also push this hotel closer to 4 stars, when it is a solid 3 1/4 stars without it. All are minor complaints that do not detract significantly from my overall experience and evaluation. Free high-speed internet - Ethernet and wireless - is a major plus at this property. The traditional Doubletree cookies at check-in are pleasant and a unique touch for this brand. Whoever thought of that is a genius. I stayed in a room facing the highway and did not have any issues with the noise. I kept the air system running, which helped to mitigate the noise, but, truth be told, the windows are thick.

“Best (and newest) Marriott property I have stayed at in Boston othern than RC” I am in Boston once or twice a month for work. Since I always stay at Marriott's, I have pretty much stayed at all of the Marriott prop's (full service and CY's) around downtown. I had not stayed at the Renaissance so far since it's further away from the Beacon Hill area where my project is. However, I decided to give it a go last week and was glad I did. Compared to Copley or Longwharf, it is a much newer and sleeker property. Much larger modern bathroom and good work area. I had booked my reservation last minute but as a Platinum premier was a bit surprised to be on the 14th floor when conceirge was on the 20th but not a problem. Platinum arrival gift - the cheese plate - was pretty basic - interesting that some properties to try to make this a bit nicer with fruit on the plate as well. Conceirge lounge is nice size and hots were pleasant. So overall recommend if you don't mind being outstide of the core tourist area.

“Not A Comfy Place At All” Got this on Hotwire at a good rate. Listed as a 3 star hotel by Hotwire. I personally think that this is a glorified Motel 6! Away from most everything. Difficult to obtain a cab here. Plain barren rooms. A nice flat screen TV though. No restaurant on premises. No room service. No wireless internet, but they do have hard wired internet. I ordered pizza and had to go to the lobby to get it. That is not a nice touch when you cannot even provide me with a restaurant. The bed was very hard. I nice pillow top would be nice. The hallways were cold. I would not stay here again if I have a choice. This should be listed as a 2 star max.

“Superb Location” I stayed at the Hilton Times Square for one night on business. Check-in was quick and easy. The room was very clean and large by New York standards. Staff was friendly and helpful with directions. The bellman are the best. They retreived cabs and provided directions as well and were always smiling and friendly. The location is fantastic - a few minutes walk to the fashion district, theater district, and Times Square. Note that the 42nd street entrance is closed due to remodeling, so you have to use the 41st street entrance (which looks nothing like the entrance shown in the photographs....those photos are of the 42nd street entrance). I did not eat at the hotel as the breakfast buffet was $25. It only took me 3 minutes to walk to the Dunkin Donuts for an egg sandwich and hashbrowns and that was only $4! My only complaint about the hotel is that they charge $13 per day for wireless internet, which I feel is a complete rip off. Luckily I did not need to get on my lap top while at the hotel. I would definitely stay here again.

“Double, Triple, Quadruple Stays at Doubletree” The Doubletree Seatac is my go-to SEA aiport hotel. I've probably stayed there 15 times. I've stayed at a handful of other hotels in the area and the Doubletree is probably the nicest and most consistent. I always book it via priceline. I bid $51 for seattle airport area, and 90% of the time I get the Doubletree. Location It is literally a 3-min shuttle ride from the airport. Shuttles leave every 15 mins. Rooms All rooms are fairly spacious and consistent in their offering. I love the Neutrogena face and body amenities they provide, particularly the spf 45 sunscreen/face cream. Although you're in an airport town, some rooms actually have a lovely view of a little lake beside the hotel. Service I've never once had a bad experience at this hotel. My rooms have always been clean, front desk staff always nice, concierge always helpful. Hints - the cookies you get a check-in are good - the coffee shop/lounge in the lobby has free wireless - if you are coming home from a flight, staying at the doubletree that night and need to get your car from an external lot, wait to get your car until the next morning because the doubletree charges for parking nightly - bring slippers, the tile floors in the bathrooms aren't heated and in winter they are COLD - you can print your boarding pass in the lobby (unless you originally booked your US flight from Canada) - the on-site restaurant is decent but in general I prefer to eat prior to arriving in the hotel area of seatac - many airlines put up their flight crews at the Doubletree

“Great Location!” Hotel is in a great location. Time Square was right at the end of the street and parking was directly across the road. The hotel is an Older style building but had been renovated inside. Our room was clean and furniture and bathroom seemed new. Staff were friendly and helpful. We would stay here again.

“Great hotel - a true gem” I stayed at the Drake for one night and I was pleasantly surprised to see a wonderful hotel - a bit dated, but still quite beautiful and comfortable. There was an elegance to the rooms and furnishings and everything worked well, especially the great fitness center.

“The Jetsons meet Lucille Ball” The guy who checked me in insisted on telling me about the amenities I'd missed, such as free wine in the lobby. "I'm your new best friend Rick," he said several times to me, a stranger. Speaking of "stranger," that described the decor as compared with, oh, any other hotel. The room was big with a lot of empty floor space. A rock-hard, low, multicolored sofa was angled into the room. The "desk" was an inefficient small triangle. The TV and a lamp rotated on a sort of stripper's pole. Chiffon curtains and other, mid-century-fabricked curtains comprised the closet door, the drapes, and a divider between the nearly-empty sofa room and the bed.(Since the latter were semi sheer, their purpose was unclear.) The minibar and drawer unit looked like a chartreuse icebox from the 1950s. The artwork: Photos of Barbie and Ken. As a fiftyish business traveler, I was clearly not the target demographic. They are remodeling in 2013. I won't be back.

“Really? Not like other Hyatts...” This place is beautiful to look at. And the service is excellent, literally every person we ran into was amazing, especially Chris the Bellman. But beyond looks.... let's see. The bed is uncomfortable, and there are not enough outlets (we had a suite). The room is dim, and boy is the lounge/bar dim - no reading in there! The bathroom in the suite had a walk in shower which I've enjoyed in many other hotels but it was SO open, its like you're showering in a great big empty room. Except the tub, the sink, the toilet and the CLOSET are right there. Very noisy in the morning. Light switches hard to figure out - we had a lamp that was positioned with the globe just directly on the floor, and you had to turn it off seperately - no switch turned it off. The worst part is the price of food/beverage. The bar has a very limited menu. So how about this: $30 (not including tip) for a cup of coffee and a bagel. Then $65 (not including tip) for a chicken caesar, glass of white wine and a diet coke delivered via room service. And a tea room? Please... give me a Starbucks or some kind of coffee shop any day. I just... don't think there's much value here. Even considering I expected it to be a high end hotel. Oh - and 2 nights in a row an unexpected knock on the door in the evening when I was already laying down. First - someone to scan the mini bar. Second night - someone to get my room service tray without calling ahead. So - the people were outstanding but I dind't much care for the rest. Have travelled quite a bit, and stayed in many Hyatts. This one is not for me.

“Nice Stay” Stayed at the Courtyard for one night. Upon check-in I was given a room that had been cleaned but looked as if someone had gone back in and used it (soap and washcloth used, remote on the sofa). Being a female traveller on my own, that is disconcerting, so I asked for a new room. The gentleman at the front desk was very kind and helpful and I was promptly moved. The rooms look as if they have been recently updated. There was a large flat screen TV and the WIFI connection was good. The bathroom was large with a corner-round whirlpool tub (odd as standard). The next morning I was given a free breakfast to make-up for the room the night before, which was a nice touch. I would stay here again.

“My New Place to Stay in Chicago!!!” Stayed at the Blackstone for a week on business and was really impressed with everything about the hotel! First, let me say that I'm a Chicago native and a frequent Marriott patron. The Blackstone is a historical landmark in Chicago and i appreciate the historic French look in the lobby area but the chic style of the rooms. The bellmen, desk service, and housekeeping staff were all very attentive and quick to respond. I was first placed in a room on the 19th floor very close to the elevators - in fact, you could hear the pulleys and occassional bumps immediately. I didn't even unpack, but instead called the front desk who immediately moved me to a different room (Michigan Ave View) and had a bellman bring me a new key. There's a Tapas bar in the hotel that's very good (forget the name but it was rated one of the top tapas bars in the city). I was especially happy with the fitness center b/c the equipment is top notch and ceilings high (a stickler for me since I jump rope as part of my routine). Fitness center also offers warmed towels and 2 water dispensers with sliced lemons. Flat screens and view of Michigan ave also nice touch. The room itself was adequately spacious and well appointed. Bose sound system was great, flat screen TV, and wet bar which I didn't use (automatically charges the minute you remove item), and wireless internet for a fee. The bathroom was also spacious with TV embedded steamless mirror and sliding smoked-glass door. The business center was being remodeled so they had two desktops in a small room off to the side of check-in and Concierge desk. Hotel is on S. Michigan Ave which takes you away from the major crowds - but a brisk walk to N. Michigan Ave. with all the high-end shopping. Cabs are all over the place if you need to get anywhere. Overall, an excellent experience and will definitely be the place for me on future trips to Chicago.

“Lovely Property, Great Location!” Spent two nights at this hotel the weekend after Thanksgiving. The doorman was friendly and helpful. Front desk staff was aloof when checking in and later gave us incorrect information regarding charges for using the phone and internet. I hate that this hotel charges you $14 to use the internet! Location is great. We were able to walk just a couple blocks to Faneuil Hall Marketplace which was beautifully decorated for the holidays. I would like to visit again sometime in the spring or summer since the hotel is right on the waterfront.

“Good place to stay for seeing the museums” Courtyard upper east side made my stay in my favorite city all that more enjoyable. For once I was not traveling for business and I picked this location purely because of it's proximity to museum mile. The courtyard is nestled on the northern end of the upper east side by east Harlem. It is a short distance from Central Park and from museum mile. It is also a reasonable cab fare from the airports; in my case LGA. The lobby was nice, nothing special. The staff was friendly. The rooms are small by North American standards, regular sized for NYC. Everything was very clean. The bathroom was good sized and had minimal toiletries. The bed was very comfortable. The view was fair. There is a weighted mini bar with snacks and drinks. No refrigerator or microwave. The desk included a free wired internet hook up with a cord that doesn't reach beyond the desk. The safe in the closet isn't big enough for regular sized laptops. In New York it's all about location and for me it was perfect and the price was fair for a major chain. If you are going to the common tourist attractions that are in lower Manhattan this hotel is quite a bit north for those activities. It was an average hotel for an average price so I gave it an average rating.

“Another great Kimpton Hotel!” Loved this hotel! It is my favorite Kimpton thus far. The rooms are a bit small but that's to be expected in a historic property. The building is beautiful and the decor gorgeous. As always, the Kimpton bed is soooo comfortable. The hotel only has three floors but I was amazed at how quiet the rooms are. Really nice Penn Quarter location with the National Portrait Gallery and Gallery of American Art directly across the street.

“Best breakfast” Had high expectations from 4 star rating, but was a little disappointed with room- in particular a very low pressure shower that would change temperatures during shower, no heating in room ( but was bought a bar heater when we asked) and a running toilet. But the breakfast buffet was amazing- the best i have ever had, and there were other good services such as business centre and shuttle ( which was a necessity as there is nothing at all around the motel)

“Quaint Hotel for Quick In & Out” Boston The Charles Mark Hotel Copley Square The location is approximately a $32.00 cab ride from Boston Logan Airport. It is in a fantastic location amongst several café’s and upscale shopping. There is a Thai restaurant right next door that they use for room service. They have an outdoor seating area attached to the bar that plays loud dance music (at least when I arrived on Sunday evening around 10pm). You might miss the hotel the sign is small & there is no door man standing outside. It is a very small boutique style hotel that I found online because I was stuck at the airport. My rate was $119. Before taxes. The room very small #103. The walk there was as unique as the room itself. Pleasantly surprised, when I walked in the had classical music playing on their sound system and the lights dimly lit. I called ahead so they knew I was coming & thought this was a really personalized touch. There is no view in this room but I didn’t care, the room was cozy, the bed comfortable, the bathroom small but has the best showerhead ever!! There are many lighting options in the room 2 end tables, a very large mirror on one wall a leather chair and a love seat as well as a desk area. No food after 10pm but plenty of cafes around. If you love chocolate there is Mark Brennar’s around the corner where they specialize in everything chocolate. Nice indoor outdoor seating and wifi. Try the mac and cheese it’s unique but don’t mix it with their chocolate martinis...they just don’t go together. They have complimentary breakfast in the am at the hotel and two computers in the sitting area of the hotel. You can print your boarding passes out here. Affordable not sure I would choose this as a first option next time in the area but, it’s a good go to place if the price is right. I had no problems getting a cab back to the airport at 5:45am.

“Wonderful Valentine's Day getaway” We had a wonderful stay here over Valentine's Day weekend. Our room was spacious and comfortable, and we heard almost no outside noise. The turndown service was wonderful, including the special Valentine's Day treat. The staff was wonderful, too. They have an excellent collection of DVDs that you can get for free to watch in your room, which we took advantage of during our stay. The location is also excellent, as it's right next to a "T" stop if you want to use mass transit to get around Boston. It's also within walking distance of many of the top sights in the city. As a newspaper lover, it was great being able to pick up a free London Times, NY Times or Boston Globe at the front desk, even on a Sunday! Even though we didn't have a laptop with us, it was nice to see that there is free Internet access in the guest rooms, which isn't always the case at the pricier hotels. A friend who lives in Boston told us the restaurant located in the hotel was excellent, although we never got a chance to sample the cuisine. If I got a good rate, I would definitely come back. I'm afraid this place is out of my price range with its normal rates.

“An amazing location, rooms need an upgrade” Typically when I travel for business, I find myself to be quite lazy at night time after a full day of working. This is especially true when I work in a booth; selling all day long. My requirements are simple - comfortable bed, clean room, inability to hear my neighbors at 5AM, great internet connection, close proximity to restaurants so I do not have to go far for dinner. Maybe I got unlucky with my room in the south tower- 2360, which look weathered and definitely was in need of a facelift. I travel at least 8-10 times a year and have developed certain expectations of the workspace of a hotel room since I do find myself working at night to catch up on my e-mails. My room's workspace was average at best and the chair at the desk had a piece missing from the arm. Also I felt very closed in while working in my room and actually found the room size to be small. I was also not impressed with the bathroom. OK, enough of the bad. The great was the hotel lobby, restaurants, pool, meeting facilities and LOCATION. Roys, the restaurant attached to the hotel was amazing!!! I ate at the outside bar 2 nights in a row and watched football. Also I took a walk along the water every morning before I started my day. There is also a village full of shops and other restaurants within a 5 minute walk along the water from the hotel. The pool area is fantastic. It created this whol tropical feel. After working all day I would go to the pool area to just decompose with a drink; and twice for a cigar. If you ask me if I would recommend this hotel for play and business, I would 100% say yes, even with the issues I found with the room.

“Nice Hotel but it is Far Away from the Action” The hotel is comfortable, clean, and relatively inexpensive for a supposed 4 star hotel. It is far from Beale Street and the party part of town. You will need to take a cab to get to the action. Cab far plus tip is in the $8-9 range each way to Beale Street. There are several hotels closer to the action where a cab is not necessary like The Peabody and Hampton Inn. Also be prepared to pay $12 per day parking at the parking Marriot parking garage. While this seems like a good deal if you are from NYC, it is not a good deal in Memphis. In Memphis we found parking for $3 per day in the heart of downtown by Beale Street. If you bid on Priceline, be prepared to win this hotel if you bid for a downtown location. It cost us about $95 per night (after all taxes and fees) for a Thursday to Sunday stay in April.

“Convient, Clean and Comfortable” Stayed at the Embassy Suites Arboretum for two nights. The front desk personnel were friendly and efficient. Check in was a breeze. Stayed on the 6th (top) floor. Our room was comfortable with a great bed, good air conditioner and plenty of hot water for the shower. Televisions were large flat-screen LCD's with lots of channel selections. Housekeeping was timely and did a good job. Breakfast each morning was good - with omlets, eggs, pancakes that were cooked to order. Breakfast meats and hash browns are also offered. There was a large selection of breads, cereals, etc. Coffee and juice was also provided. The manager's reception from 5:30 - 7:30 pm was nice with free drinks (beer, wine and hard liquor available). Chips, salsa, popcorn and veggie sticks were also available at no charge. There is also a "happy hour" for appetizers during this time. We had dinner in the hotel restaurant the first night. The blackened talapia and the blackened rib eye was excellent with prompt and friendly service. I had a sandwich the next evening that was also excellent. There are quite a few restaurant choices near the hotel; along with shopping. Good area of Austin. I would certainly recommend this hotel and will definitely stay here on a future trip to Austin.

“Great for accrss to trade shows” Front desl staff are friendly, rooms are ok but getting old. Bar really rocks on Tuesday night kareoke night if that is your thing. No breakfast except a little sandwich place and don"y bother.

“another good Marriott” This busy urban Marriott feels like a small boutique hotel, with a friendly staff and modern, well-designed interiors. It's right next to the 405 freeway, which is both convenient and noisy. However, the double glazing on the large windows keeps the highway noise down to a minimum. It's a pleasure to come into such a clean and comfortable room. The pure white cotton bedding that's now standard Marriott issue is great. Marriott made a good move when they went non-smoking chainwide. The breakfast (not included in the price) was good, and healthy options were there. The parking was a bit steep ($14 per night) but it was secure, and street parking seemed impossible.

“Absolutely one of the finest business hotels I've ever stayed at!” This is a beautiful hotel right on the waterfront across the street from the convention center. The hotel is only 2.5 years old and is extremely modern and very comfortable. The views are fantastic, either bay/city or Coronado. The rooms are excellent as well as I said one of the PURE allergy-friendly rooms with a HEPA air filtration system. The hotel lobby has a wonderful airy feel, almost tropical. There are a number of restaurants, a Starbucks and a Sweet Things yogurt parlour (very good). It is also a very short walk to the convention center, Gaslamp district, Petco Park and downtown. I can't comment on the additional costs like parking, internet access, etc. but they seemed fairly typical for a high quality downtown hotel. This would absolutely be my first choice for my next stay in San Diego!

“Five stars, but . . .” You'd expect anything with the name of Trump on it to angle for five stars, and believe me the Trump name is on everything here (from suit bags to laundry slips to stationery), and while the property gets a five star rating, it needs to work a bit to hold on to it. Here's our experience. Our first room (yes,"first room") was a deluxe king on the 24th floor, overlooking parts of SoHo and a car wash. It didn't take long for us to notice, however, a rather pungent smell of cooking (steak, actually), overtaking the hallway and room. Curious about whether there was a kitchen on our floor we called the front desk, and the first reply was "Engineering will look into this. This is the first we've heard of a problem like that." Really? The second call to the front desk a bit later (and by that point I was pretty much committed to having a steak for dinner . . .somewhere) elicited a snippy comment that the hotel was full . . .and that engineering was "on it." Really? Shortly thereafter someone from engineering called. He apologized for any inconvenience the smell was causing, and offered that this was a "chronic design problem" in the architecture of the building, effecting 3-4 mid-level floors, and that they have known about for some time. I thanked him for his candor, and he set about to get us a new room in an otherwise booked hotel. Really? Really. Within a few moments we were offered a suite on a higher floor, away from the smell. Good timing. I was just about to call the Ritz-Carlton Battery Park for a room. Not to make too fine a point on all of this, but (a) the venting problem has been known for some time, notwithstanding comments from the front desk; and (b) candor at any juncture in a hotel visit is a welcomed moment. The front desk might just learn something from engineering. Go figure. The suite (see bedroom picture) was quite nice, overlooking both the Freedom Tower and the Hudson River, so they do indeed know how to do it right, if pestered. And the smell was gone. As for dinner; we ate at "The Dutch" a few blocks away, upon the advice of one of the bellmen.. And the bone-in sirlion was great.

“Fantastic Service” All the staff that I encountered at this property made my stay fantastic! From the time I checked in to the hotel until the time I departed every staff member offered impeccable service! The rooms are clean, but feel like it’s time for a renovation. The location is also great for walking around downtown.

“I Love This Hotel” It is shocking to me how this hotel ranks only 150 of Hotels in San Antonio. This is an absolutely beautiful, historic hotel. When I say beautiful, I don't mean Beverly Hills or Four Seasons beautiful. I mean truly old school beauty. I am in my 40's and I think that most people in America these days simply do not appreciate classic beauty or architecture. I was originally checked into a different, major hotel chain. The first full day of my trip I did some sightseeing and wandered into the hotel. The minute I stepped in the front door I fell in love. I walked into the courtyard and almost cried it was so beautiful. I hustled back to my large hotel chain, checked out and moved into the Menger. I'll be the first to admit that this place has it's quirks. One reviewer said that the water temperature varies between "scalding hot and freezing cold.". You definitely need to be on your toes and pay attention when you take a shower - the water does get hot(ter) and cold(er), but scalding and freezing is an extreme exaggeration. One day the housekeeper took my dirty towels and did t leave clean ones. I simply found the housekeeping supervisor and asked her to take care of it. She apologized, politely called me ma'am and it was taken care of. I don't understand why people have to lie and make things seem worse than they are. Anyway, anyone who appreciates a truly beautiful old hotel with fabulous architecture and loads of personality and character will love this place.
“like going back in time.” was exactly as I remembered it from several years earlier. simply a timeless classic in one of my favorite cities in the US. the place oozes charm.

“Incredible location and service” I stayed at the Omni Chicago in March for business. The hotel staff is incredibly friendly and helpful. I had to arrive early and they accomodated me without any fuss. The hotel is located on Michigan Avenue close to Northwestern and the major shopping centers. The hotel is clean and modern with soft comforting touches. My room was very big, as was the bathroom (also appreciated was the high placement of the showerhead). The views from the room were inspiring and the bed was one of the more comfortable ones that I have slept on. I didnt use the gym or any of the restaurants. While there are literally a million hotel rooms in Chicago, the Omni stands out because the quality of the room and the friendliness of the staff come at a price that is very affordable. The Omni offers free high speed internet connection if you join their promotional program, another nice touch.

“Great stay” My husband and I stayed at the Hilton for one night. We booked through hotwire for $65.00 per night. Be advised, the hotel charges $13.00 for parking. The front desk help was excellent and the lobby was very nice looking. The room was large and the bed was beautiful. It had a white down comforter, white sheets and lots of white pillows. The bathroom was very small and we had trouble with the water temperature in the shower. (It literally took 2 minutes for the water temperature to change once you made an adjustment.) Overall, the hotel was nice for a short stay.

“Good but not worthy of 4 stars” Second stay at the Knickerbocker. Happened to go on one of the busiest weekends of the summer. Tall Ships, Lolapolluza, Art Festival, Cubs and White Sox all going on. The room we stayed in was clean and nice. The only downfall is the fact that we had to sleep in a Murphy bed. No 4 star hotel should have a murphy bed. Beyond that, the staff was very helpfull and made the stay enjoyable.

“The King Jacuzzi Suite is one of the sexiest Seattle hotel rooms I've found!” I was blown away by the level of service, quality of facilities and special details at this alleged 3 star hotel. Everything is nice and new, clean and the amenities are ample and varied in a very boutique manner. Favorite things: -the friendly front desk staff (even when I made it down to check out at 3pm) -the rooftop outdoor pool and hot tub -the en suite 2 person jacuzzi tub I got in my room for just $50 extra -the counter, sink, fridge and microwave -really tasty coffee -the security of the hotel (they call to verify guests, etc) Less ideal: -weird hours for all the amenities (not even consistent from one to another) -unless you're in town for an expo or game the location is weird and possibly a bit scary -the staff at times provided inconsistent answers to inquiries and could possibly communicate among themselves better so as to avoid confusion Overall it was a ton of fun and I will definitely stay there again some time!

“Good, but not great” Overall this place is a nice option because of its size, it is quiet, close to many walk able places, and works for a business or leisure traveler. But The Orchard needs some updating. Time to get rid of the outdated TV, update the linens, carpet, decor in general. Felt a little dowdy for a reason I could not quite put my finger on.

“Great for a short stay” We stayed here last year for a business dinner. All hotels were around the same price in the downtown area and we decided to go with this one since we've had good experiences with Westin in the past. I have to say it was a great stay! Excellent location, just 2 blocks away from where we had our dinner so it was very convenient for us. Plus, it's connected to a mall and the shops were decent, I'm sure good for some. I would have preferred more variety but just outside there are plenty of other stores to choose from. The room was large, clean and well furnished. Bathroom was your standard, nothing special. The bed was comfortable and pillows were nice and fluffy. Checkin was a breeze and all staff were courteous, but not over friendly. I think they had gym access to a sports club but not sure. All in all, a safe and solid choice for the city. Just booked a night for the Loews for this weekend, so I'll be able to compare more when I write that review. I would definitely recommend staying here!

“Nice place to stay downtown” Pretty consistent with service expected from Doubletree brand. Nice rooms, good service. Had a large well equipped fitness room. We chose for its proximity to event attending in Little Tokyo. Liked the fact there was a shopping center next door to hotel with several great asian restaurants. Could enter directly from hotel. Parking is pricey @ $34/ night, but common for downtown. Would definitely stay here again

“Surprisingly nice” A chain hotel on Canal Street would not ordinarily be my first choice in NYC,but this was a very nice surprise. Clean and recently upgraded, the rooms were spacious and comfortable. I was very surprised how quiet they were. The bed was very comfortable and clean, the armoire had just enough room for my hanging items and the must-have safe big enough for a laptop. There is even a robe, which is a excellent touch. The bathroom was not terrific. Better lighting around the sink and more room for toiletries would be my suggestion. I had just a shower with no tub and it looked to be ada-compliant even tho the rest of the room wasn't. The bathroom also had an automatic fan with the light that made it impossible to be in there and hold a conversation or hear the tv. The location is excellent if you want to be downtown. Right on the subway, plenty of markets and amenities nearby, and easy walks to TriBeCa and Soho as well as financial district. For the great rate I got, I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Nice Hotel” We bid and won this hotel on priceline for $45 a night. We stayed here to be close to the airport. It is a 10 mile or so drive to the airport but that is about as close as your going to get to the Denver airport. If you pay full price for the room they have a complimentary shuttle to the airport and you can park your car in their lot for free. Since we got our room through Priceline there was a $8.00 per day charge for this service. The hotel is going through a renovation but the interior looks like it is finished and they are working on the outside. Our room was nearest the Interstate but we couldn't hear any road noise. The only complaint (if you could call it that) was that the furnace/airconditioner in the room was not updated in the remodel and looked really shabby, as they had just painted over it. Overall a nice hotel!

“Nice hotel, Pricey Internet” Okay, it's a strange rating. But after paying $26 per day for valet parking (no other kind is offered), I am very annoyed at having to pay $14 per day for internet access. This is 2009, not 1999. It's time to get rid of those internet charges. Even the little cheap motels give free wifi. Other than that, it's a nice hotel. I'm here for a convention. The rooms are big, the decor soothing, and the staff helpful. But these days, everyone lives on the net. I don't pay a special charge for water or power in the room. Why am I paying for internet? If I add $40 per day to my room rate (internet plus parking) it's not much of a bargain.

“Nichts besonderes” Das La Quinta Inn ist eine Massenhotelkette und so sieht es dort auch aus. Nichts individuelles. Der Pool ist recht schön, die Lage direkt an der Interstate einfach nur praktisch. Zu den stockyards in Fort Worth ist es nicht weit. Die Zimmer sind modern und zweckmäßig eingerichtet, aber es fehlt ein Zimmersafe. Dafür gibt es safety deposit boxes kostenfrei an der Rezeption. Das sollte dann aber bitteschön funktionieren ! Als ich bei Abreise die box leeren wollte, wurde klar, dass man mir einen falschen Schlüssel ausgehändigt hat. Meine Wertsachen lagen in Box 7 und man hatte mir Schlüssel für Box 8 ausgehändigt. Die Dame am front desk wirkte etwas überfordert, musste eine Kollegin anrufen und es stellte sich heraus, dass im Zweifelsfall beide keine Ahnung gehabt hätten, wo sich der master-key befindet. DAS hätte bei Zeitnot ins Auge gehen können. Und sowieso, wenn jemand anders den Schlüssel für meine Box ausgehändigt bekommen hätte. Ein riesiger Fehler, unentschuldbar.

“These people get it” First, this is not a brand new facility. As a matter of fact it is quite old. But, they understand customer service. They track the ratings that people give them on tripadvisor ... and they are doing everything in their power to drive those ratings. The place is clean - but its old. The people literally bend over backwards to help you. I arrived late in the evening and needed to drop off a rental car - so I didnt need to mess with it in the morning. They arranged for their driver to pick me up. And in the morning, they arranged for two wake-up calls to make sure I got out on time. And, they are just minutes from the airport...

“Stilvolles Hotel im Hafenviertel Fisherman's Wharf von San Francisco” Originell ausgestattetes Hotel der Kimpton Kette direkt in Fisherman' Wharf gelegen mit Kimpton-typischer Themenausstattung des Hotels und der Zimmer. Thema hier: Seefahrt. In den Zimmer sind Utensilien aus alten Seefahrtstagen liebevoll in die Zimmerausstattung integriert, jedes Zimmer hat daher eine etwas andere Ausstattung. Damit nicht so steriler Look wie in anderen Kettenhotels, das brachte Wohlfühlatmosphäre! Mein Zimmer (Basiskategorie) war nicht riesig, aber ausreichend groß, Blick nach hinten. damit ruhig. Die Zimmer zur Strasse hinaus haben zwar einen besseren Blick, sind aber nicht ganz so ruhig. Man hatte mich darauf beim Einchecken hingewiesen (fand ich fair!) so daß ich mich für mehr Ruhe entschied. Wie ich leider etwas zu spät entdeckte, ist das WLAN für Teilnehmer am Kimpton Loyality Programm gratis, also sollte man sich davor dort anmelden. Nett war das allabendliche >complimentary wine tasting< also Wein und kleine Snacks auf Kosten des Hauses in der Lobby, ich glaube es war zwischen 17 und 19 Uhr. Da fanden sich alle Nicht-Abstinenzler unter den Gästen zusammen und prüften ihre Trinkfestigkeit. So kam man nett ins Gespräch und konnte den einen oder anderen Tip bzgl. Sehenswürdigkeiten der Stadt und Umgebung, der nicht im Reiseführer stand, aufschnappen. Durchaus hilfreiche Veranstaltung, soll es in anderem Kimpton-Hotels so auch geben. Ein Schwachpunkt war das Hotelfrühstück, es wurde im angeschlossenen Restaurant serviert. Habe ich mir nur ein Mal angetan, denn das war doch eher Magerkost. Das Hotelpersonal war sehr aufmerksam und entspannt, eher unaufdringlich. Das Hotel liegt in einer typischen Touristengegend, Fishermans Wharf ist schön zum Flanieren am Abend (tagsüber zu voll), auch die legendären Seelöwen am Pier 39 sind nur wenige Schritte entfernt. Die Alcatraz-Fähre ist in naher Laufentfernung. in der nächsten Querstrasse rechts neben dem Hotel ist einer der Wendepunkte der Cable-Car, mit der man quer über die hügligen Straßen bis zur Market Stret kommt, sozusagen ein Punkt des Pflichtprogramms in SFO. Also ein guter Ausgangspunkt für touristische Zwecke. Empfehlenswert!

“Nice hotel easy access to Love Field” I stayed at this Embassy when all of my business was going to be conducted at the hotel. Nice shuttle service to pick you up and return to Love Field. The rooms were fine - standard Embassy Suite quality. I ate at the hotel restaurant a few times and the food was very good. As always, the breakfast was great. Staff was super friendly and went out of their way to accommodate.

“Love San Diego” Westin Gaslamp Quarter was a last minute booking and it was definitely a good choice! Only stayed for one night but it was great all arond. Service was very good from the check in to the concierge and valet was also very smooth. The location was superb and many restaurants and bars are close by. We also saw a San Diego Padres game and that was a great experience for just relaxing and taking in the city. The hotel is modern and rooms were great - had a nice view of the city and looked as though it was newly renovated. Parking was not cheap but for valet service it is pretty much the going rate these days. You pay for what you get and the Westin is in my opinion a quality brand and paying a bit more doesnt bother me if the experience is worth it. All in all a smooth and positibe stay at the Westin Gaslamp Quarter in San Diego, cant wait to come back - love the city.

“Nice staff, very clean, one of the best FFIs” I have stayed at this hotel on 3 occasions in the last several weeks. The staff here are all excellent. Check in is always speedy, as is airport pick up.
