There are 6 or 7 hotels on this property: The FFI, A Courtyard and a Full-Service Marriott, a Hilton Garden Inn, Hampton, Slle Inn and A Holiday Inn Express. They all share a shuttle to and from the airport. There is also a TGIFridays in the Courtyard. The nice thing is that Fridays will do room service, take out AND you can charge to your room if you are a guest in any of the hotels. They have a good happy hour too! The Marriott also has a full service restaurant but I have not tried it. Prices seem average for a Marriott restaurant. As for the FFI, the rooms are decent sizes. All are nonsmoking and have the new Marriott beds. LOTS of TV channels if this is important, free internet,etc The free breakfast in the AM features cereals, Jimmy Dean egg sandwiches, waffles, breads and danish. Honestly, my only complaint is that they need to get some better pastries...maybe muffins or donuts or something. They do offer a park-n-fly and you can get some decent rates if you are a Marriott rewards member. Rates aren't bad anyway. AIrport noise isn't bad and the hotel is less noisy than many in which I have stayed. Rooms are clean, staff is attentive and welcoming and you can take the shuttle to the airport and hop on the Orange line to downtown (about 45 minutes to Chicago give or take). There are a few other places around to eat that are walkable...Giordano's, McDs, BK, White Castle and a few others. Many flight crews stay in these hotels and they were talking about some local bars nearby. The PACE bus stops right at the edge of the property and it is a short ride to a mall, Target, Wal-Mart and a couple other places. Overall, a decent place to sllep for an early flight or to visit Chicago if you want to save some money!

“Very nice hotel, great location” I was in Baltimore for the marathon and got a fantastic deal on Priceline for the Marriott Waterfront. The location was perfect, very close to the inner harbor and all the stadiums, but pretty quiet right outside the hotel. Our room was very nice and clean with extremely comfortable beds. The front desk was very helpful and sent up a roll-a-way bed just a few minutes after I asked for it. All in all, it was a perfect hotel for our weekend. I am amazed I was able to get a good deal on it the weekend of a Ravens game and the marathon. I would definitely stay here again and would recommend it to friends.

“Great location, nice rooms but some issues” I'll start with the bad. As other posters have noted the hall noise is pretty bad. Don't expect to sleep beyond 6AM. The doors slam shut with a VERY loud metallic click, so when your neighbor goes for breakfast, you'll know it immediately. To a point where the wall actually shakes if the person next to you closes their door. Second bad, the heat/ac unit. It is a motel type unit on a thermostat. The vents are not adjustable and the low fan isn't very low. The rooms are kind of small so when it starts up you get a gale force wind blowing right over the bed. And it is loud. We have had to leave it off at night. The medium. The rooms are kind of small but not at all bad for New York City. A single queen bed would have been more suitable for the space. The good. The room is VERY clean and fresh. Bathroom is good, bed great, staff helpful. My wife says the breakfast is quite good. We are on the top floor so I can't say if you'd get any noise from above but the sound deadening between the room (except for the doors) is great. Outside noise for New York City is good. We have a nice city view. The great. Location. We took the train to Penn Station and it was about a 10 minute walk here. Times Square is close, the Empire State Building is practically next door. One other thing we have noticed were VERY large crowds in the lobby at certain times of the day. Don't know what they were doing, sort of milling around with tons of baggage. Maybe tour groups getting checked in. Check in could be tedious if you hit the wrong time. My wife also said breakfast can get very busy. Overall a I am satisfied, expensive (but this is NYC) and the door issue was pretty annoying.

“A solid stay at a Grande Dame... mind the renovations, though.” Stayed here for a three night stay with Mrs. Gardiner and Kiddo. Upgraded to a very, very nice suite. We’d stayed here (all 3 of us) in 2005 for a large conference, and they needed a renovation then... Well, renovation now partially completed. (More on that later) Our room was terrific, well appointed and clean. Beds were comfy, and flat screen tvs were nice. That said, there were touch screen computers on the desks, and access to anything of value was behind a firewall. At check-in, I was given instructions for wifi (which worked great), but the desk computers are clearly designed to be little profit centres. Please, don’t throw fancy tech at me and then give me a choice between my tech for free or your tech for cost... you’re going to lose. I used the USBs for charging ports, but nothing more. Couldn’t even get weather on them... which I CAN get at a Courtyard... Also, I was disappointed that in a 2-room suite there was NOT an in-room safe. You got two mini-bars and a dorm fridge in there, but no in-room safe. Big omission for a property of this caliber. Then (and I write this first half of Dec 2011) they had only ONE restaurant open, and that was Kitty’s Pub... Either they have spent enormous amounts of money to hire Disney to engineer and recreate an authentic, dark, grungy, dirty, well worn Irish pub, or they have a dark, grungy, dirty, well worn pub that badly needs to be renovated. We ate there one evening, and certainly never went back... Kiddo had dinosaur chicken fingers and mashed potatoes... they didn’t even get those right. There were four adults and one Kiddo for dinner, and NONE of us finished our dinner. Jeepers. So, until they have other food options, be aware of this. (Nice looking restaurant reno across from Front Desk, but that’s only open for Breakfast, so you’re at their mercy for lunch/dinner) In short, a dire lack of in-house dining. Nearby, I can verify that Eleven Deli (Wabash at 11th) was quite good, as was Tamarind (Asian, on Wabash, 200 feet from Hilton’s porte cochere ). Both are a short walk from the Hilton. (Of course, short walk is a relative term in Chicago in the winter...) Concierge Lounge was reasonably nice. Evenings had two hot dishes and a full selection of soft drinks and coffees. Wine and Beer selections were available, although they never tell you precisely what wine they served. Also, $8.50 for a glass of unidentified Pinot Grigio was a bit steep when a very nice Kiwi Sauv Blanc was available in the lobby for $9. GM, please help me out here... make me feel like you and Hilton want me back. Breakfast was Continental, with NO hots, no chafing dishes. Big bagel selection, variety of pastries and cereals... Fully acceptable, and the staff was friendly and helpful. I did use the Parcel Shipping Center, and the gentleman there happily taped together two boxes for me, and wouldn’t charge me. Nice. Very nice. So, this was our second visit to this Hilton property. Looks much nicer now, but the lack of restaurants is a serious drawback at this time... If eating in will be important to you, check what is open/finished there. Would I return? Probably so. I’ve stayed at the Hyatt Regency, the Hyatt McCormick, the Sheraton, the Marriott, the Allerton, and so on. It depends on what I am doing and where I need to be. Yes, I’d go back, but if location was not an issue, I’d probably choose further North in the city. It was a good stay, not great... Maybe if F&B had been better, I could've gone with four stars.

“Not impressed; well below average” I travel for business a lot and usually always priceline my hotels, and got this one via priceline for $60. It was the Sunday before Memorial Day, I had to travel on Memorial Day out of Baltimore Airport, so I'd figure I drive in a day early and have fun in the city. What a below average experience: 1) Parking was a nightmare. The selfpark garage for the Sheraton only allows SUVs to park on the first level. Meaning if there are no spots you cannot go down lower levels, however you ONLY find that out after you are down there and there are cars behind you looking to park. Thankfully, a Valet guy was walking buy and was able to hop in and back my SUV up through the narrowest of alleys and garner me a spot that Houdini would have had difficulty finding. Unreal. I tipped him a few bucks for his effort. I have never seen a more dysfunctional parking garage, especially for $24 a day 2) The rooms are beat up. Old furniture, shower had plenty of mildew and ancient wallpaper in the bathroom. And it was clear the toilet had not been cleaned if you get my drift. Also the rooms were cramped. Could not see how two people could fit with any comfort. Oh, and there was a hole in my window, not a crack but a physical hole. Yes, a hole the size of a thumb at the base. It looked like it has been there for a while. Have some pride and fix that management 3) Elevators. LOL. Be prepapred for a 5-10 minute wait and I am not kidding. I was on the top floor and it was frustrating waiting 5-10 minutes just to get to your room 4) Margarita at the hotel bar was $9. LOL. Those are NYC prices The crowd in the hotel that night was painfully obnoxious, though I do not blame the hotel for that. There was a Heavy Metal concert in Baltimore which attracted some of the most bizarre people I have ever seen. Not sure why 25 years olds cover themselves with tatoos. You realize one day you will be 40 and will look even more stupid? Lots of heavy metal people loitering around in black tee shirts with dyed black hair The Lacross championships were also in town, so there were a lot of drunk college kids in the hotel, but oh well. That actually brought back memories being drunk in college. I am sure I annoyed plenty of 40 year sold business men in my college days. LOL. I walked down to HarborBay which is a few blocks away. That was a good time, though the seafood I had was terrible down there. You'd think on the water they could learn how to cook shrimp. Just a lousy experience. I just did not like this hotel and if you look at my many reviews, I am certain not particular. But this place was weak.

“Clean and comfortable, well maintained Hilton in DC” Stayed one night for a function in the hotel. Unfortunately due to the event, we arrived too late for valet parking, but registration easily removed the charge (as it was included in the rate). Quick and efficient check in, friendly staff. Again, clean and comfortable room. For the number of rooms in the hotel, the service was amazing. One complaint was the adjoining room feature appears that the gap at the bottom of the door allowed for a lot of our neighbors noise to come through/under the door. And unfortunately they we loud talkers - stuck and extra pillow and blanket at the door jamb - and it helped a little -but still a nuisance. Overall, very nice experience, great room, super friendly wait staff for AM breakfast in the dining area - good food and coffee too. Definitely would recommend, as well as would stay here again.

“Treated properly at the Hyatt NYC” I stayed at the Hyatt NYC during marathon weekend and I was extremely impressed. I had booked a cheap deal via a travel website and being a single person, expected the normal treatment, which is to say I thought I'd be shunted into a back room with little or no natural light. Not so with the Hyatt - my room was enormous, tastefully decorated, warm, comfy and quiet. I ordered room service twice and both times were prompt and the food was delicious. I found all of the staff - from the cleaners to the security people - to be courteous and efficient. I really enjoyed the "big hotel" feeling, despite it being very busy. Most evenings I would return to the hotel well after midnight and I personally found it reassuring that I was asked for my hotel card as identity before being allowed to pass into the lobby. This was my fifth trip as a single person to NYC, and by far the best comfort, service and value I have received by far. Merry Christmas.

“Warning: All of their beds are *extremely* firm” When I got into my room, I laid on the bed and it was of the "extra firm" variety. I have shopped at Sealy/Beautyrest mattress warehouses and have laid on many beds... this bed would certainly qualify on the extreme end of firmness. I called the hotel management to ask them if this was somehow a special bed and they said no, all beds are the same... even so, they showed me another room and the mattress was the same. If you don't like sleeping on an extremely firm mattress you will not sleep well at this hotel.

“funky smell in room - fantastic breakfast - close to airport” room had an old time motel smell - but seemed clean - could use a thorough cleaning behind night stand and in the bathroom - bed should be replaced...we rolled to the middle :{ Breakfast was incredible - friendly staff and real plates and silverware. a small bar for an evening drink if you get in before 10:00 p.m. A good place to stay for a night after traveling. good price when you include the good breakfast menu

“What an Improvement” We last stayed at the Palmer House Hilton in September 2001. Then we experienced offhand treatment from most of the staff we encountered, had a tiny room not much bigger than a closet and a view of absolutely nothing. We did not feel welcome. Also, the area seemed to be going down hill and, last straw, Marshall Fields, the landmark Chicago department store, was about to be taken over by Macy's. This time? Wow, what a difference. It was a busy weekend being Memorial Day on the Monday but we checked in rapidly (thanks to Hhonors Priority line) got an upgraded room on the "Executive Floor" (not many executives in evidence, though) and had a view, sort-of. The room made up for it. It was splendid. Throughout our stay, every single member of staff we encountered were friendly and helpful. And the area is on the up too. And Macy's has preserved some of the original elements of Marshall Fields including the wonderful top floor restaurant. Millennium Park and the The Arts Institute are nearby and, if you must, "Miracle Mile" is a short walk or 'El' ride away. We really enjoyed our time here. Well done Palmer House Hilton.

“Average hotel” Hotel was average; it is an older Holiday Inn Express but it was clean. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The hotel is very convenient if you are going to Methodist Hospital ; it is located a block from the Methodist Hospital. There isn't much within walking distance, but restaurants are close by.

“Very Good for a Marriott!!!” I am far from a fan of most Marriott hotels (I think they are dated, ugly, inconsistent), but enjoy staying at a JW from time to time. The LA Live property is quite good and worth a return visit. I was given a 12th floor "City View", which consisted of a view of the LA Live facility, which was perfect for me. Room was very clean; I requested a quiet room and definitely got that--at the end of a hallway next to what appeared to be an occupied corner room/suite. The only drawbacks I could find was the price of internet, no free newspaper (important for me when I travel for business or pleasure) and no express checkout. Overall, a great stay in a great location if you are looking to hang in your room and just go out to eat or have a beer.

“Nice hotel; great location” Stayed here for 3-day weekend. Great location. Lots of attractions in walking distance. Beds were wonderful and room in historic tower was very nice. Great views and the windows open which was great for some fresh air. Changed from 31st floor due to banging we kept hearing for 24 hours (sounded like someone jumping on the floor above us). Hotel was gracious in moving us to 37th floor, but had breakdown in communication as to why we were moving. In the morning, told us to leave our stuff and bellman would move it; just pick up key when returning at day's end. When we came back at 5pm to pick up our new key, they then asked all sorts of questions which should have been noted already. So it was annoying to reiterate the whole banging noise, engineer you sent up heard it, never got back to us, etc. Both rooms we had were very nice. Bathrooms have a lot of marble, nice tub and separate shower. Nice toiletries too that smelled great! Amazing lap pool--one that must've been shown in movies. Interesting how you must shower first--you have to walk past the attendant to get to the pool from the showers; this rule is apparently enforced. Pool does not smell like chlorine which was great. Didn't eat there so can't comment on food. Check on internet access--some get billed and some don't. There's a Starbuck's on the ground floor too. Took doubledecker bus tour first thing and saw the whole city. Next day went to Space & Invention museum (taxi cost $20) and then to Millennium Park. Walked around the City and shops, etc. Hancock Tower was cool at night. Fox & Obel store near hotel was great. Lobster club sandwich was so good I went back next day and got one to go for the plane ride back to NJ (United serves/sells NO food in flts < 3 hours). I'm sure the cupcake we ate on the plane was the envy of passengers around us. Nice upscale store with a great "to-go" selection too. Ditka's had good food for dinner. All within walking distance of the hotel. Hotel staff was very courteous. Used Continental Van service from/to airport. Paid r/t at airport but next time would taxi back as the p/u was late and driver had attitude toward everyone. A LOT of traffic to and from airport. Leave about an hour to get there. Overall a good experience.

“Truly a Luxury Boutique Hotel” I stayed here many years ago and don't remember anything nearly as nice as what we found this trip. It's truly a luxury boutique hotel now... the front desk clerk said the interior was renovated about three years ago. We had a King Deluxe room which was plenty large enough for two. The room comes with a comfortable king size bed, sofa and matching chair, desk space, flat screen TV, rain shower stall and separate bathtub, and large bathroom with two sinks. Very nice, modern decor with a theatre motif (the hotel is right beside the theatre district). Staff were all unfailingly polite and friendly... very competent. Concierge gave us some good advice re: Golden, CO, restaurants. A minor maintenance problem that we reported was attended to at the requested time and fixed. There are no ice makers for guests, so you have to call and request a bucket - but they do have in-room coffee makers. We splurged and ate at Kevin Taylor one night. The food was good, but, as you can tell from looking at the menu, it's pretty fancy (and pricy, of course). Service at the restaurant was very good. We were tempted to try room service for breakfast... the choices looked really good... but just couldn't bring ourselves to spend that kind of money with a Starbucks a block or two away on Larimer Street. Speaking of which - Larimer Street near the hotel is a neat place to have dinner and take a short walk... all lit up and decorated. We ate at Osteria Marco... had the pizza and salad. Delicious. Very nice - I would not hesitate to stay here again when in downtown Denver. A Four Seasons opened about a year ago across the street from the Hotel Teatro - I hope that's not a problem since I suspect both hotels cater to the same clientele.

“Bit Pricey for Average Hotel” A magnificent old building - originally called The Bradford I believe - The Courtyard is ideally placed in the centre of Boston with the public gardens and Boston Common only a short walk away, making it a perfect location for history buffs. It is also in the heart of the Theatre District close to Chinatown. Unfortunately, however, like most older buildings, space is a problem here too and ours was one of the smaller hotel rooms that you can expect to find anywhere. That said, it was perfectly adequate for our needs and the kingsized bed was very comfortable indeed. I was also quite impressed with the bathroom facilities and the view from our room of the Back Bay area was also quite impressive. Wasn't too impressed with what passed as the hotel restaurant, though, and the breakfasts weren't up to much either. On one occasion, I got charged onto my room account even after paying cash with gratuity for a breakfast. During our seven night stay, we were disturbed twice during the night by fire alarm actuations, which I am led to believe were caused by break-glass points being activated by late night revellers in one of the adjoining nightclubs. When this did happen, evacuation of the building was a bit too slow for my liking, especially as the fire department was already in attendence by the time that we hit the ground floor. Furthermore, on the morning that we were due to check-out, I received a bill for car parking and valetting, which I did find rather odd considering the fact that I didn't have a car. However, in spite of these small inconveniences, we did enjoy our stay. The hotel Manager was very helpful and so was the reception staff. And the small touches were nice too. Like when we were given complimentary toothbrushes, toothpaste and deodorants after my wife's suitcase had been left at the airport in New Jersey. All in all, a fair to middling hotel with a very grand interior, but a bit on the expensive side.

“Overall... fair” stayed here via priceline ($105/night) for a midweek stay and it suited all our needs. Rooms are very small but clean. It did have an overpowering chemical orange smell that almost made me gag when i walked in but i guess i would prefer that smell over Body Odor or worse. although in a decent location, i definitely would recommend asking for a room not on the ground floor. There is a car repair garage open 24 hours across the street which provides for some seedy people hanging out on the street and knowing there was only a brick wall dividing us was somewhat unsettling.. this also made it for no real view out the window (not that i would want to see the garage, but you get my point). so, ask for a higher room if you can. i think this place is fine for the price but if i was traveling with girlfriends only or if parents are letting their kids travel alone, i feel like it is a tad too stetchy of an area to stay here esp if they will be coming in late with that car repair shop always having people lingering. i didn't interact with the staff too much but the person that holds bags was nice.

“Fantastic location and friendly staff.” So, this property is a pretty nice property though maybe a little cookie cutter. I've stayed at one of the Loews properties in Orlando and that was far nicer than this one. But, I can't complain about anything, really. The room was clean and the bed was super comfortable. The room was a good size for a big city, clean, and modern. Nothing extremely fabulous, but would get an above average grade. However, the property definitely gets a four bubbles for the location (1 block from Reading Terminal Market, 1/2 mile from the historic area, and in a very walkable neighborhood.) The staff was also extremely friendly from the late-late night check-in (friendly and quick) and the awesome doorman that gave my husband and I a tip about umbrella loaners at the front desk as we were about take our chances walking to Reading Terminal Market in the pouring (and I mean pouring!) rain. I'd certainly stay here again if I were visiting Philly again.

“Some good, mostly bad” The first two are particularly bad because some of the other problems are things that could be improved upon with staff changes. But overall, would not stay here again (even for one night)! The good first: 1) Room seemed relatively clean, furniture not as scuffed up as previous reports seemed to indicate (though one night I did see a rather large rat entering a building adjacent to the hotel). 2) Concierge lounge is fairly decent (if you have access) with friendly staff. Real pastries in PM, and continental breakfast (average) in AM The bad: 1) Location: some distance from Convention Center, downtown shops. Especially at night walking in near vicinity as young/non-body builder female, didn't feel entirely "safe." I've stayed in Philly many times before (convention center area, Rittenhouse Squate, Upenn area), and not felt as unsafe in the neighborhood such as around this hotel. 2) Paper thin walls. Someone coughing in room next to mine, and it literally sounded like he was in the same room. And given problem #2, especially bad. 3) Housekeeping: yelling (yes, yelling) at one another up and down the hall at 8:30 A.M. Particularly bad given problem #2) 4) Front Desk Staff: 12:30 AM, awakened from a deep sleep by security knocking loudly on my door: "SECURITY!" Fortunately, I had put the door latch on (always a good thing in any circumstance), because the security guard tried to open the door (and failed). Startled, I leap out of bed and say "Excuse me?" The guard says "Oh, there's someone in there." Incredulous at this astute observation, I say "Yes, apparently there is someone in here, how can I help you?" The guard leaves without replying. The next day, I try to reenter my room after getting breakfast, and the key doesn't work. Go downstairs to the front desk, and mention the incident from the prior need. Amazingly, front desk staff does not immediately apologize, and offer to make amends, but asks "When are you checking out?" Finally manager comes over and (after some prompting on my part) offers an apology for the early wake up call, and offers amends. Check-in front desk staff was very pleasant, but apparently not very competent as she didn't actually check me into my room, so the incident was entirely hotel staff's fault. Question: Why is it so hard for them to admit that they made a mistake and offer an apology? Craziness..not the way to keep customers coming back!

“Not exactly Paradise” I had really high hopes for my stay at Paradise Point. The reason I rated it average was if we had paid $100-$125 a night, I probably wouldn't have been as unhappy as I was. It's an older, average place. We went for my cousin's birthday, and the first night there were three couples that had rooms there, the second night there were 5 couples that had rooms. My cousin got a bayside room, opening out onto the beach, and the rest of us booked garden rooms. My experience started off on the wrong note. I checked in 5 minutes before our friends, who booked their room on the same website as me and paid the same rate. They were across the driveway from us. Well, our room was in the middle of the building, had no dresser, no walk in closet, and virtually no patio. The website promises private patio with Adirondack chairs. It was private all right. There was a large hedge separating the 3 ft of patio space from the driveway. Their website states that every room comes with "Views of the bay, garden or lagoon" I had a view of a big hedge and the driveway. Our friends, paying the same rate and checking in after us, had an end unit, with a huge walk through closet, a dresser for their clothes, a huge vanity top, and a very large patio that actually opened up into the gardens. Right after we checked in we had to leave for dinner in Old Town and a Padres game, so I really didn't get much of an impression of my room other than the fact that I had no dresser to put my clothes in other than a nightstand, a 3 ft vanity top which made it necessary to store our toiletries on the shelf above our clothes in the closet, and a patio that was smaller than the inside of my car. Well, the next morning when I got a good look at my surroundings I was not very happy. Mind you even though we booked through a discount travel site, we were paying over $300 a night. Add in the $17 resort fee and the $32 a night parking, and we were over $350. The paint on my bathroom wall was peeling, the paint on the wall next to our table and chairs was bubbling and peeling, the hot water handle in the bathroom was loose, the bathroom door had black scuff marks on it, the tub didn't drain when we showered, so we ended up standing in soapy scummy water while showering. The area rug in front of the sofa needed a shampoo. When they cleaned our room after the first night, they left a dirty glass on the coffee table, and didn't leave us a fresh glass on the vanity. Strange. When we were ready to leave on Sunday, i attempted to check out on our television. They do not offer it. We had to drive up to the lobby, and physically go in to check out. Huge inconvenience. So after standing in line to check out, the gentleman at the desk asked me how my stay was. I told him about my issues, and he was very apologetic. He waived our resort fee and parking, which was terrific, saving us $102.00. Then as I was speaking to him I noticed a placard to the side advertising their loyalty club, Destination Delivers. I had actually signed up for this when I booked my room. The placard stated that members would receive an upgrade at check in, and also late check out. I pointed out to him that I had received neither, and he immediately offered to give us late check out. I thanked him but told him that we were already packed any my husband was waiting in the car. I will say that my cousin's room on the bay was very nice, it had all of the features our friends across the driveway had, in addition to opening up onto the beach. Overall I was totally disappointed in the quality of our room for the price we paid. in my opinion $32 a day for parking is ridiculous, as they have a parking space in front of your room that is reserved, and the resort is so huge that it would be tough to get your stuff to your room if you don't park there. If you don't use it, nobody else can, so I am not sure how they justify charging you an additional fee to use that space. For $350 a night I can find much more luxurious accomodations.

“Nice location for a hotel in desparate need of a makeover” The hotel is located at the Potomac River only 10 min walk away from the Waterfront Metro station. Some of the rooms overlooks the river. Right across the street is an Arena of some sort. The neighborhood seems ok - I did not experience any problems walking back and forth from the metro station. At the metro station there is a nice safeway and some fastfood restaurants. I checked in late afternoon and the receptionist asked about my name. She found my reservation, asked me to fill in address on a card and gave me the key. No verification about my identity or anything. The lobby seems nice but the minute you enter the elevator you notice the worn down carpet and just how worn down the interior of the elevator is. My room was on the second floor but when I came to the room (4:15 o'clock) the maid was still in the room (checkin time was 3 o'clock and the receptionist did not mention that the room was not ready). I waited for the maid to be done and noticed afterward that there was no towels. The maid told me that the towel would arrive later which kind of annoyed me as I was desperate in need of a shower after having travelled from New York. The room itself was nice size but was very much in need of a makeover. There was a cabinet with a 20" CRT television but when opening the doors to the cabinet the doors almost fell apart. The channels on the TV was great however the reception and size of the CRT was not that great.The bed was nice and right next to the bed was a small couch and table. There was a balcony with a view over a playground and in the distance the Washington monument. There was not information inside the room about the hotel and the receptionist did not inform me of anything. One thing that worried me a bit was the lack of information in case of a fire or an emergency (see picture). The maids start each morning at 8 o'clock. They start by knocking on every door to ensure that all will be awake. I did not ask for that 'service' but I think you cannot avoid it. It does not matter if you put out a 'do not disturb' sign - the doors are so poorly isolated that you can hear the maids knocking on the doors down the hall. However they do a great job and the room was very clean during my stay. They also had complimentary Wi-Fi which basically is useless (when it works). When I realised it was not working I told the receptionist. It was an elderly couple and the man just responded 'yes we know'. For the 5 days I stayed at the hotel it worked maybe all in all for 2 days and it was very slow. There is a bar and restaurant at the hotel, however I did not use them. Also the bar seems to have a band on occasion. They play very loud and I was glad my room was no the second floor. I did not interact with the staff that much but they seemed to be nice.

“heaven on the beach” we stayed at this lovely little hotel for 5 nights and found this a great place to stay. the rooms are not huge but who stays in their room when in LA. the bathroom is also small but with a large shower. there is also a fridge and micowave. greg the manager was friendly and ready with any advice that you need if you havnt visited the area before. there is small free breakfast available on the landing which is great for taking the munchies away. on the same landing is a computer that is free to use for the guests. the hotel is in an excellant location, the only hotel with a terrace area with comfy chairs looking out on to the beach. venice beach is about a 10 min walk away, with some bars and restaurants just 2 mins away. santa monica pier is walking distance but a long walk. but cycle hire is available 2 mins away. for the money this hotel offers excellant value for money and a superb location its not a 5 star hotel but doesn't pretend to be.i would give it an excellant 3 star

“Very nice, but very small” I thought the hotel was beautiful and elegant. Our room appeared to have been recently renovated and was very nice. A plate of freshly baked cookies were available at the front desk, which was a nice treat on check in. The location is excellent but in a very expensive area of Manhattan. The subway is close, and I even took the subway/train to and from the airport with no problems. The Waldorf is right across the street (stayed there last time I was in town). I have one negative comment concerning our room. It was way too small to include a desk chair. The desk chair stuck out and was practically touching the bed. It was difficult to get by this - especially in the early hours of the morning on the way to the bathroom.

“This place is a joke” I don't even know where to start. This was the most strangest hotel I have ever been in (even in Europe). NYC is filled with trendy niche hotels but this one is just plain bizarre to the extreme! I stayed here one night because I had to move hotels and NYC was filled everywhere and PriceLine put me here - ugh. The Cons: Take a building make it as dark as you can from the lobby to the halls to the rooms. Add the strangest furniture combinations (not even contemporary). The rooms are smaller than a walk in closest. NO ... I AM REALLY SERIOUS! Read all of my travel reviews... I am not some untraveled one timer that complains on tripadvisor - these are THE smallest rooms in America - I would be willing to bet that statement! It is insane. It is beyond NYC small rooms - it is smaller than a dorm room! I cannot even express how SMALL and cramped you are. The bed is so low to the ground and on plywood - futons are more comfy. There are two metal end "tables" - the lights are strange backlite colored creepy lights on the side of the bed. That is IT - nothing else can fit. If you have any luggage you have one little "indent" in the wall upon entry to store a duffle bag. The windows and AC are behind the bed - but the bed is so low and hard you cannot see out the window anyway. It is so dark! The paneling on the walls and the wood floors in the room are dark walnut color as well. NOW, you think that is crazy... the bathroom is not enclosed for privacy. The shower (no tub) has a glass wall looking at the bed on one side and if you sit on the toilet you will hit your knees on the wall in front of you. You could shave, use the comode and shower all at once. There is literally NO PRIVACY - it is part of the small room. It is insane! Mostly Europeans staying here or college kids - which is fine - but not because it is cheaper - just because they don't care. I have never seen a hotel so far fetched and creepy. There is no insulation between rooms or hall - and since hard wood floors - you hear everything next door, in hall and above you like there is a speaker in your room. DO NOT STAY HERE FOR ANY REASON - you will be sorry and you will think of this review right away! The whole time I was thinking "are they serious".

“Nothing fancy, but decent place close to Universal” We stayed here for 3 nights while we visited Universal Studios and Magic Mountain. The hotel is very clean and new feeling. The service was fine and the free breakfasts were decent-each morning there was your standard donuts, bagels, toast, dry cereal, coffee and juice. In addition to that, each day there was a hot egg dish (one day scrambled eggs and twice "omelet things") and meat (bacon twice and sausage once). There is also a waffle maker which we enjoyed. The breakfast area was clean and they did a good job of keeping it stocked. Our beds were comfortable and the room was a nice size. We didn't have any problems with loud neighbors- we were on the 3rd floor, so no one above us helped. There is a small, bare bones pool that our kids swam in once. Not fancy, but clean. Free Wifi and free garage parking was also a plus. This certainly isn't a fancy place, but if you are looking for decent place to stay while visiting the area, I'd recommend it.

“Nice Hotel especially if you will be at the Convention Center” I stayed at this hotel for a conference, and it was the perfect location. It is across the street from the convention center and just about two blocks from the 16th Street Mall. I arrived a little earlier than check-in so I was told to check back in about half an hour. I did, but my room was still not ready (even though it was now check in time). They then put a rush on my room and called my cell just a short time later to notify me that it was ready. And while I was there, I had a change of plans to come up which meant checking out a day early, and they were very nice about it and did not charge me a fee. The room was clean, the bed was comfortable, and even though there was another conference going on with what seemed like hundreds of high school students, the only time it was extra loud was in the morning when they would let their doors slam on the way out. I did not eat at the hotel, and with so many restaurants being so close you definitely don't have to. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in downtown Denver especially on business.

“Do NOT stay here!” Do NOT stay here. Everything was wrong: drawer missing from dresser, bath vanity broken, door lock damaged, no toilet paper, high noise of trains right next to room, hostile staff. I stay often with Marriott and they should not have their name on this place. It is a dump. Do NOT stay here.

“One block from Macy's at Herald Square” Very conviently located close to Macy's, Madison Square Garden, and several subway lines. Furnishings are a little outdated and showing wear. New sleep number mattress is a great feature but not really explained at check-in.

“Nice location and nice staff” Overall nice place to stay. The beds were very comfortable and they had an excellent breakfast. Wish we would have had more time to enjoy the place. Pool was very nice but the hottub had been boarded over so that was disappointing. Did have an issue with a guy talking to my kids and following them around the pool then he followed one of them into the weightroom and the staff and security handled it very well, probably better than me. I recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

“Brilliant hotel” Brilliant hotel. – stayed 3 nights from 4th August. Very friendly with a homely feel. Gardens & pool lovely Bar pleasant and relaying - kids could sit with us and drink sodas I booked 2 rooms and requested they be near each other but when we arrived on was on the 3rd floor the other on the 4th. I was worried at first leaving our teenagers on their own, but this was not a problem due to the feel of the hotel. One room had king and was quite small however it directly over looked the Alamo which was wonderful and was the main reason for visiting San Antonio so the size of the room did not bother us. Our teenagers room was very large with 2 queen beds and looked over to pool. Both bathrooms were very clean Complementary coffee at breakfast time in the lobby you can take back to your room. Very convenient hotel – just across the road to the river walk, next to the shopping mall, on the corner you can pick a local bus that took us to the Fiesta Six Flags theme park and the North Star mall I would recommend the hotel and will return next time I come to San Antonio

“Average Marriott-Not too bad, not great” I will begin by saying that the front desk, and lobby staff are exceptionally friendly. Each staff member greets you throughout your stay. Check in process was efficient and friendly as well. Rooms are a bit dated, but spacious, clean and comfortable with Bath and Body Works toiletries. The housekeeping service is pretty basic they just changed my sheets, emptied the wastebasket and replaced used toiletries. There was no straightening at all, or effort put into tidying the room despite a generous daily tip. The wireless internet is really very bad, last night it was down completely, this happened on a previous trip as well. In general it is so slow that it is not possible to use Facetime, watch a video online or even surf the net. It was painful to even check my business email. For the television, there is no channel guide in your room or a Guide of channels or programming available on the TV. I called to ask if maybe I had missed the location of one in the room and was told someone would bring one up to me, it never arrived. There are no premium channels (HBO, Showtime, Cinemax) and a limited lineup of other channels. The concierge lounge staff was very friendly, and the selection of breakfast food is fine, scrambled eggs, oatmeal, fresh fruit and pastries etc. Basic alcohol offerings at cocktail time, I didn't have any of the appetizers or drinks. Parking is free, there is plenty of it and the hotel location is convenient to the Fashion Mall and Castleton areas.

“very dood for manhattan” after arriveing with amtrak from phili walking only 10 min with the luggage around the crowded streets of NY ( we arrived saturday ) at it was hard to find the plase...we reachec the enterance in 33st ( korea way ) but after we enterd all the suspicious about the place dissolved very nice service sent us quickly to our room 704... the bes is nice and comfy the bathroom was cool and nice no terrible noise or stange things ( see review of WOLCOTT at 32 st ) we had what was called continental breakfat that included the following : fruits : apples, pairs and bananas coffee, tea hard bioled egges orange/apple juice yogurts all kind of breads for toast and last but not least Doughnut WOW for continental breakfat the only drawback that comes with every hotel in NY is the price :(

“Not well staffed and a bit past it's prime” Not only is Valet parking $52/night it is horribly slow and disorganized the only part worse is the rest of the service. I tried repeatedly to call the front desk on speaker phone since the handset didn't work but they were too busy to pick up the phone. Apparently they like keeping the wireless password super secret so I can't tell you if it was good or not. The location is great for Chinatown but I won't return to this location. The Hyatt embrace deep , Sheraton Fisherman's wharf or the Hopkins are all much better for similar prices.

“Exceeded Expectations on Service, Great Location” My stay at the Hilton was my best hotel stay in the last year. The staff, from bellman to the wait staff at the Top of the Hilton were the most helpful, courteous and attentive I have experienced. Room had a nice few of the city and partial few of the waterfront. The room was clean, adequate in size, had a flat screen TV, and a very comfortable bed. Comfortable work station and the Internet service worked great. Added bonus was the free printing from your room to the office center. Free snacks at the Top of the Hilton in the evening, also a good breakfast buffet. Location right downtown, easy walk to popular spots, convention center, and cabs are readily available for the longer trek. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

“Great party location and great staff, parking weak” I would recommend this hotel if you have activities downtown. . We visited Austin to see family and a night out. The location was great, walking distance to food and fun. The staff was very helpful and friendly. Rooms were ok and I was able to get a room on the 23 floor,, good view looking east. I did later find out they offered a free breakfast but only after we had already check out, wish that had been relayed at check in (no big deal). Beware of the parking. The valet service told me their area was full and I need to self park in the area below the hotel. After driving around the 5 floor garage, found this full as well. I located a spot on the street and on my walk back to the hotel noticed the valet parking still cars,,, guess Mercedes trumps Dodge trucks. Well the street parking was free on the weekend.

“Great value, great location” We've stayed here many times mostly because among very nice midtown hotels this one is almost always the least expensive. Very easy to book connecting rooms. Views are great, especially looking west over St. Patrick's Cathedral. We used the concierge for the first time on this trip and they were terrific. The only negatives I'd mention are that some of the room fixtures (including the lighting and temperature control system) are getting very dated and the wifi was virtually unusable (at least from our corner rooms). Also, be warned that cell service is iffy on the high floors. Hotel seems to always be very booked especially with international guests.

“Amazing Rate for an Amazing Hotel” We bid for two nights at the Hilton Inn at Penn for a local reunion. The rate was extremely low, which made the weekend a terrific value. Everything about this hotel was great. The location is perfect for UPenn. It's practically on the campus. And it's within walking distance from new stores and restaurants. The hotel itself is connected to restaurants, the UPenn bookstore, and other stores. But you can only get to certain stores by going outside first. The Inn is charming and old-fashioned with a modern twist. It is very clean, and sleeping rooms are nicely sized. Ours was on the sixth floor facing the UPenn campus. Almost no street noise. A common living room near the lobby is comfortable to sit in, read, and have a drink from the small bar. Although we didn't use their services, we found the valet parking attendants and lower lobby greeters to be very friendly. The registration desk is set back quite a bit from the main hallway of the upper lobby, so when you pass by, the staff might not see you fast enough to say hello, which I think is a design flaw of the registration desk. No big deal. As far as conducting business at the desk, they made check-in and check-out faster that most hotels I've stayed in recently. Most importantly, we felt safe and comfortable at the Inn, and it ould've been worth a higher nightly rate.

“Location, check. Renovation, check. Service, disaster.” I arrived for a 3-night stay, excited to be staying in a wonderful NYC location. The property is close to everthing! Whether you need to get around the city (Grand Central Station is next door), want to grab a great breakfast (Pershing Square across street or choose Dishes in Grand Central to grab and go), or want to venture to theatre a few blocks up, you can't beat this spot. Upon arrival, I was given a hand by the bellman, was asked if I needed help with my bag, and was ushered to the front desk. I had a small wait and was checked into my room on the 25 floor. Hey, it's NYC, but I was pleasantly surprised at the size, cleanliness and appointments of the room. King size bed with 2 night stands, large armoire (with safe), love seat and table with chair. I personally would have preferred to have a desk and good lighting rather than table and loveseat to do work. Strangely, there was a college-like refrigerator completely out of place in the room. Because I was staying for a few days, I unpacked into the armoire, but couldn't get far as there were only 2 hangers. A call to housekeeping remedied it. I then went to the bathroom to freshen up and there was one facecloth. So again, called to housekeeping and they explained there was a problem with towels and they would bring some up, which they finally did. The bathroom was NYC small, a sink, toilet and shower/bath with the extension rod for the curtain. No robes provided. At the end of the night (11:30pm), I went to shower and the tub filled up and wouldn't not drain. A call to maintenance had someone in the room 30 mins later. It took 15 minutes to fix the problem and then I had to wait another 15 minutes for whatever he had to spray down the drain. Ridiculous. A conversation with the night manager to share my experience was pointless. But the real kicker was that I needed to add another night onto the room at the end of the trip. A call to the front desk shared that the hotel was sold out and to try back later. Calling back later they told me I could have a room for $580/night. A call to American Express travel agent got me a room at hundreds of dollars less. In general this is an outstanding location, great room, but lousy service - by which I took off 2 stars.

“Nice Hotel, but the A/C wasn't working properly.” Stayed two nights on a recent business trip. As previous entries stated, make sure to join the Kimpton Hotel rewards club. I was able to get free wi-fi, breakfast, and $10 to use towards the mini bar. The room decor was very nice and they have Aveda products, which I absolutely love! The staff were very nice. The only issue is that I was staying there when the heat was 95 plus degrees. When I arrived, my room was set at the normal 70 degrees. I lowered it, but it didn't seem to cool off. I mentioned this to the front desk the following morning and was told that they would have engineering take a look. Well, that never happened! The next night was even worse! It was cooler in the hallway than it was in my room. I couldn't wait to leave the room to check out. While I'm sure this is not the norm, it needs to be addressed. While I would recommend the hotel, I would check the weather and call ahead to make sure the air conditioning is working properly. Oh, great happy hour reception for guests that's free!

“My favorite Embassy Suites” Hands down, this is my favorite Embassy Suites hotel, to date. The exterior architecture is unique and quite pleasing. Front staff personnel were friendly and helpful; check-in process was uneventful (as it should be!). Not sure how old the hotel is; however, it had the appearance of a newer property or at least one that is maintained very well. The condition of my room was excellent; I couldn't find a blemish. The beds and pillows were extremely comfortable; bathroom was clean; shower water pressure is strong. I like how you can open a french door to a small exterior balcony. It was very warm the day I stayed, and it was very nice to be able to open the door and enjoy the balmy breezes blow into the room. For a moment it didn't feel as if I were in Indianapolis. Granted, the view from my third floor suite was nothing special and brought things back to reality. Access to I-465 or 86th Street is very easy. I did not avail myself to the other amenities, including breakfast, on the property. I can not pass up a Cracker Barrel breakfast (located just around the corner!); otherwise, I would have had the good breakfast at the hotel. Overall, an excellent choice for accommodations on the north side of town.

“Fun Location, Teensy Room” We chose this hotel because of a special bargain rate. Our room was one of the smallest I've seen in Manhattan. We really did smash into the furniture and the wall column in the middle of the night. The front desk staff was confused, to say the least. We were given the wrong person's receipt at check-out. We stayed here with family members, and each room requested a 4:45 AM wakeup call for an early flight. Thank goodness we used our phones as backup alarm clocks. Neither room got a call, and when we mentioned this to the desk clerk, he began to argue that we hadn't requested calls, rather than finding out what is wrong with their system and apologizing to us. There was quite a bit of street noise, including drunken revelers and garbage trucks. However, it was a nicely-decorated, clean room with comfy beds in a fantastic neighborhood. Since it is near the fabulous High-Line and lots of great restaurants, you may want to try it.

“Cute Boutique Hotel with Large Rooms” I loved this hotel from the second I walked in. The staff was very pleasant and always greeted you with a smile when youwalked in anad out of the hotel. This is a Kimpton Hotel, and stands up to the name which are boutique hotels with personal charm. There is a manager's reception in the eve with wine pouring for everyone in a a nice setting. This one also had someone doing chair massages - what more can you ask! I was in RM 1107 (king) and the images online matched the room and I was pleased to finally find a website that has accurtae pictures of the propert. The room was huge for a boutique hotel and any other for that matter. The mini-bar wasn't outrageously priced and I feel I got a better deal for my money than other places I have stayed in Seattle (see my other Seattle reviews). Next time I am in Seattle - I will stay at this hotel. Perfect

“adequate” Small bed and uncomfortable mattress, TV from the last century. Room clean and decently appointed. Public areas very nice. Decent comp breakfast in the AM, I've stayed here several times and sometimes get a good bed and sometimes an uncomfortable one, (luck of the draw). Priceline rates this a 3 star, it is not. I've tried telling Priceline this but they stick to their guns, bet they've never stayed here. For $50 it's OK but pales in comparison with the other 3 stars in the area. Airport pickup and dropoff was reasonalbly prompt, staff was courteous and helpful. This is a six floor building with one working ice machine, that's not 3 star. It's about the closest hotel to the airport, that said there is no problem with airplane noise. On a nice day a 10 minute walk to the airport. The restaurant is across the parking lot and you'd better like bar-b-que because that's all they serve. On my last trip I noticed a Subway half a block down, step in the right direction.

“Great view and lounge” We stayed here on way to San Antonio. It was a great relaxing stay. The lounge is a nice touch with 2 hot appetizers cheese plate and veggies in the evening. They have a stocked refrigerator with juice, soda, and water. There was enough so we didn't need to go out to dinner. The breakfast the next morning also had ham and cheese roll ups and wrapped sausage (hot). The guest services where wonderful and they even remembered my birthday with a great gift and a upgrade. Thanks again.

“Perfect for my needs- Clean, reasonable, free parking” Met all standards and then some. Location is convenient to all locations I need to get to while in Houston, Hotel is friendly, clean, free dinner and breakfast, parking. Rooms are good. No complaints and a terrific value for less than $150 per night!

“Very nice, Very convenient” The PHL airport Marriott is a very nice hotel with a very convenient location. I walked to the hotel from my arriving flight without going outside...so the hotel is actually IN the airport, but outside of security. This place wasn't that inexpensive, but the rooms are very nice and very quiet.

“Location ...but nothing else” Stayed here for 6 nights in March - in a premium room (means larger but just as spartan). What was good ? As everybody else says, location What was bad ? Room reminded me of Belgrade early 80s. VERY basic. Not that large: rather very high ceiling. Very noisy. All premium rooms are in first 6 floors so street noise (and from Cowboy-themed restaurant next door) is unbearable at times. The Terrace might be a great spot in the Summer: just tired and sad when I went. Altogether, poor value for money: there is much better for $300 in low season.

“Good Value for Business Trip” Stayed from a Saturday until Monday for a recent business trip. Compared prices to other nearby hotels and this place offered a better deal. The room was clean and spacious enough to get around in. They had an ample buffet breakfast Sunday morning. The staff was friendly and would help when needed. There is a steak house restaurant 100 feet in front of the hotel and there is a Kinko's a few blocks down the street. The hotel is located on the service road along the I-10, allowing for easy access to the freeway. Overall, if your looking to spend a few nights on a business trip and don't expect anything fancy, this place is a great value for the money

“Not recommended” This is no more than a 1 star property. Check-in was quick and staff friendly. The bathroom was clean. The rest of the room could have used a little more care. The bed was not nice. Mattress pad covered only about one third of it, and the bed was thrown together. Before I could sleep in it, I had to strip the other bed so that I could have two mattress pads that covered the mattress and then remake the bed. The sheets were terribly wrinkled and the bottom sheet was not form fitting. The furniture had an inch of smeared wax on it and was sticky to the touch. The TV also had a smear of wax on it as the same cloth that was used to clean the funiture was also used to clean the TV screen. I would not stay here again.

“Location superb” Loved the location right on mag mile. Can walk just about anywhere. Good concierge restaurant recommendations. Attached by a bridge to some fabulous shopping too. Breakfast typical of hotels.

“You are kidding right” This place is a joke right? The front desk staff is ridiculous. They are clueless and rude.The room: where to start, a bed on the floor and a bean bag chair? thats about it. The wort hotel room I have ever seen. Silly, uncomfortable is an understatement. The bar upstairs is super, of course ruined by the awful service. NYC has so many options for cool. hip spots, Do yourself a favor and GO SOMEWHERE ELSE.

“Nice but needs renovation” In the winter time Grand Hyatt is great to stay at since it has a direct passage that links it to Grand Central. That way you never have to go outside to get to the subway or trains. But the rooms are getting a little old and dirty. our last stay here we had to keep the bathroom door closed because to the mildew odor coming from it. We called and complained but were told that there were no more rooms available. Isn't that always the excuse? But the location of the hotel is excellent. In the summer time the restaurant "Pershing Square" (i think it is the name) across the street and in front of Grand Central's main entrance has outside street tables set up which is really nice. So, I would probably stay here again since after last time we complained with a letter and actually got hotel management to call and advise us that when we return to ask for him and he would make sure everything was great. Overall it is a nice hotel, in a great location, a little bit pricey (but everything in NY is getting that way) just in need of a little spring cleaning and sprucing up.

“My new favourite hotel in New York” The Sofitel in New York is my new hotel of choice in New York City. The hotel was everything I had hoped. Its located in the very heart of Mid Town, two blocks from the Theater District and Times Square. But for all that its incredibly quiet. The lobby area is very nice, very European and very comfortable. Check in was quick and friendly, in that French way. The concierge was also quick and efficient with our bags, they were in our room within 5 minutes of getting our keys. Bellman happily helped me get some ice immediately and arranged our heavy cases for us so they were in the right places. And I mean happily. Room service was quick, very tasty and good sized serves. Ok, its expensive, but the quality was certainly there and with the added extras one expects from Sofitel, bread basket, yummy butter and plenty of chilled water. Again all done with a smile. Needed a cup of tea after dinner and a whole day of travel. No kettle or coffee maker in the room. Called down, was told that there were none available until morning but that they would send up hot water and cups immediately, at no cost. Very impressive service for midnight. Had some minor issues with television and internet not working. Maintenance were there in minutes and everything was fixed within 10 minutes. The bed was heavenly. Nothing more needs to be said. The room was extremely quiet, a blessing given the usual New York Symphony of fire trucks, ambulances, police cars and garbage trucks one usually has to put up with. We were on the 20th floor but even so it was so silent we both had our best nights sleep in a long long time. The room was also very clean, as was the bathroom. The bathroom was very well appointed and there was gallons of hot hot water. There are two options here for the internet. The wired internet service is $10 but cuts out at 1200hrs regardless of what time you purchased your 1 x day. The other is a T-Mobile Hotspot, that also works out to about $10 but it does not cut out, gives you a full 24 hours. I found little difference in speed between the two and the T-Mobile one could be used in the lobby, so that was an advantage. We asked for a late check out, which is always tricky in a big city, the hotel accommodated us for a reasonable compromise, gave us an extra couple of hours. Returned later in the day ahead of a midnight flight and relaxed in their very cosy lobby. All in all, one of the most pleasant hotel experiences I have had in New York. I will stay there next time for sure and certainly recommend for others.

“Great location and nice rooms but be aware of nearby construction” Location is close to many things and to subway stops. Just a few blocks to Central Park. Construction is going on nearby. Beginning at midnight on a Friday night in February there was heavy work going on. The front desk said they weren't aware it was going to happen that night and offered to move me if it was continuing the next night. They said they would call me to let me know the status of the construction, but they never did and would not answer calls to the front desk. Luckily there was no more construction during the weekend.

“Very clean with great service” Our family stayed here the night before Thanksgiving to see the parade the next morning. Check-in was literally less than 60 seconds. Rooms with 2 double beds are on the 5th and 6th floors (out of 15) but we still had a decent view. The lobby, elevator, corridors, guest room, and bathroom were clean beyond expectations - I mean I looked for dust, mold, stains - none at all. Beds were comfortable. Flat screen TV had a good choice of channels. Temperature controls worked and responded quickly. Shower had 2 heads and the bathroom was brightly lit. We didn't hear anyone in neighboring rooms and any noise in the hall seemed distant even though people were nearby. Only negatives were 1) the automated wake up call didn't work (as a backup use an app or old-school travel alarm) and 2) the internet service was not complimentary unless you were in the lobby. In 2011 when the Motel 6 on the interstate can give free wireless internet, the $13+ tax per day rate in upscale urban hotels is ridiculous. Gold or Platinum Starwood Preferred customers DO get free internet service however. We asked for a late checkout and had no problem getting ours bumped up to 1:30. Self parking is available for $35/day or valet service is available for $47/day. Overall, the staff were genuinely friendly and the facility was quite clean and comfortable.

“Good access to transit from here, bit scary location” This hotel is cheap and only 2 blocks fro L.A. Union Station, so that's why I ended up here on a long distance train trip once. The place was real busy, seeming to cater to groups of foreign students and the like when I was there. The place is not real fancy and not real clean, with slow elevators and grubby hallways leading to average motel rooms. The windows in my room overlooked other guest rooms, so that was uncomfortable. The area around the hotel is gentrifying a bit but still has a long way to go. The people in the lobby were mostly polite and the staff did their best to keep up with what appeared to be inadequate technology to deal with checking in and checking out. Not a lot of great options for dining nearby, couple of mediocre taco restaurants.

“Bin ich von W anderes gewöhnt...” OK, das Hotel ist in New York und da muss man Abstriche machen. Aber Preis/Leistung waren nicht einfach und besonders klasse finde ich DIESES W nicht. Es ist zum Glück nicht so bonbonmäßig renoviert wie das in San Francisco aber steht doch den meisten anderen Ws weit, weit zurück. Die Zimmer sind winzig (selbst die upgrades) und irgendwie kommt es mir ziemlich verwohnt vor. Die Lage ist klasse, ganz nah am Central Park und für die Shopper-Freunde nahe an Bloomingdales. Dennoch würde ich bei gleichen Preis andere Hotels in NY vorziehen.

“Great Stay” Compared with some tredy hotels it lacks the sophistication but the room was clean, people were nice. The food in their resturant was quite good and seemingly close to everything. Room was quiet although needed a little attention. Big Flat screen, free wireless. Great rate. Will definietly stay there again. The business center charged a bit much for copies etc. but what hotel doesn't these days.

“Has the potential to be very good - not there yet.” This hotel is 4 blocks from Port Authority or 6 blocks from Times Square. It's in the up-and-coming Fashion District outskirts, and felt safe. The Candlewood Suites sit between the Holiday Inn Express and the Hampton Inn. 32 stories with only 6 rooms to a floor. Pros: * The rooms themselves are lovely. They are little studio suites with a mini-kitchen (full sized fridge). The decor is cozy and beautiful. * Nice workout room. It's in the basement, but fully equipped. * Free laundry room. Great touch! Provide your own soap, but the new washers and dryers are without charge. * Very quiet rooms. We didn't hear a peep from other guests the whole time. * Fast elevators. Two elevators that go from 1st to 32nd floor in about 10 seconds. * Price. For the area, this is pretty reasonable. Cons: * The staff - With the exceptions of Jamie and Kenyetta who were wonderfully attentive and helpful, the staff seemed mostly annoyed with the requests of the hotel guests. Night staff was considerably better than the day crew, but I can only surmise that this is the "trainer" hotel for the other two. It's not the place to go if you're looking for top-notch service (the HIE next door, however, has amazing staff!). * No business center - It's advertised on their site as having one, but there isn't any. You can go next door and use theirs, but it's only 2 and there is always a line. * No breakfast - Again, you can go next door to their buffet (sensing a pattern here?). * The common areas - Simply put, they lack any semblance of luxury. This feels much more like an apartment lobby than a hotel. The staff's work area is open to view, the carpets in the halls look old, and the lobby lacks any sense of warmth. * Hot water - At night, it takes about ten minutes for the shower water to heat up. We didn't seem to have that problem in the morning, though. Overall, if price is your main concern, this is a decent hotel for the location and the money. If you can afford the extra few dollars, I'd stay at the Holiday Inn Express next door. If money is no object, you can't beat the Marriott Marquis for Times Square. Great little Mexican take-out across the street (Fresco Tacos)

“Nickle and Diming to the extreme” Let me start by saying that I did not have a choice but to stay here and that as a Hilton Silver member I had some expectation of a reasonably good reception. My 3 day business meeting was in the hotel and it would have been a hassle to stay elsewhere. Retrospectively I wish I had. Silver membership be damned. First warning should have been enough. Upon checking in at 12:15 pm, I was told that yes, rooms were available but that the hotel policy was to charge $25 for check in before 1 pm. That was a new one for me and I do travel around the county about 2 months of the year. I politely declined even though I felt like by responding with a few choice words. While I was patiently waiting for the 45mns to elapse in the lobby, I had to fend off 3 different bell boys who kindly offered to put my carry on in storage for a fee of course. Checking in at 1.01pm I was informed that a king size bedroom was not available. Hmm, I guess all the other guests either paid way more than I did or had a least a gold or platinum club level. Room was passably clean, spacious enough, view on a brick wall. No coffee maker ! Even the seediest motel provide those nowadays. Gym was only accessible through the spa at a hefty fee. Pool was closed although it was already warm enough but I suspect access would have been for a fee. Self park was $35 a day, $51 valet. Good job I did not bring a car! Of course, wireless internet or LAN for a fee. If you request directions to the business center you will be directed to the one on the street level which is very pricey. No one will tell you about the self serve business center on the 7th floor which although far from free will allow you to save around 75% on what you want to do. Phone charges were outrageous. Thank god for cell phones but usually you are allowed to call local numbers or 1800 numbers for free at least for a short period of time. Not here! $1.50 connection fee then 10c a minute after 60 mns Also, strangely enough the hotel Starbucks was about 15% more expensive than the one down the street Location is NOT great by the way, hotel is pretty far from everything except for the Bank of America theater. It is not even on North Michigan Avenue. If you can, save yourself the aggravation and stay somewhere else eg: at the Embassy Suites a few blocks down the road and enjoy a much better location and many more free amenities and perks. Vote with your feet and those hotels will stop treating us like cash cows.

“Average Hotel with Above-Average Staff & Location” I used my SPG points to book a free room. I arrived on the redeye at the crack of dawn, exhausted and desperate for an early check in. Valerie Alverio at reception pulled a miracle and got a room for me not long after I arrived. Beyond that, she was cheerful, courteous and had a great smile. I can say the same for the rest of the staff I encountered. The location is excellent--you can walk to the theaters, the park or one of any number of subway entrances. The room itself was well-sized for New York and suitably clean. The room was showing it's age, however, looking a little tired and worse for the wear, much as I looked upon arrival. Overall, if you're looking for a good location and friendly people, you'll be happy resting your head here.

“Good value” I stayed here a couple of weeks ago and was very pleased with the value for money (especially on the UK exchange rate). I had a good, well airconditioned room with plenty of towels, good toiletries, space and all the facilities working - not always the case in chains. It was very clean and as a non smoking room was smoke free - definitely not always the case. There was also a dressing room area with a separate wash basin outisde the bathroom. Also a microwave and full size fridge should I have needed it. The staff were very cheerful and helpful. The inclusive breakfast was OK if not totally stunning- my colleagues thought the OJ was watered down, but I enjoyed the fresh bagels, eggs, good yoghurt and fruit. The downsides were that the towel rail was located so you cracked your head regularly and the swipe cards for the doors were temperamental. Overall, it is very much better than it looks on arrival. It has an Elephant Bar next door, which again is a chain, but also has friendly staff and a lot of good fresh choices if you choose wisely, aswell as pleasant indoors and outdoors sitting areas.

“BEAUTIFUL, BEAUTIFUL” What can I say, the Mondrian Soho is absolutely gorgeous. I stayed here for my wedding and it was a fairytale hotel, just fantastic. The problem is the staff at this hotel, they are rude and very unhelpful. Twice I called the concierge to schedule a limo for my wedding and both times they never got back to me. I had to book my own limo for my wedding, which was fine but irritating for such a fancy hotel. My reservations were under my first name and not my last so they couldn't find it and I was panicked as the front desk people tried to not look worried. When we asked what came with the room the desk person said a mini bar. We were never told about the safe, restaurants, internet or laundry service. My husband could not get over how unprofessional the front desk staff was. There was a bottle of wine in our room with a note for a different person---attention to detail, not so good. We had asked the person who booked my room many times about photos on our wedding day and I was assured it would not be a problem. 5 minutes into photos I was told the manager was upset and wanted to know who gave us permission for photos. I WAS LIVID. We were running late anyway for our wedding and then had to deal with this after I asked so many times if it would be okay. It started my wedding day off really bad. We asked the restaurant attendant how we went about getting some food and she snapped at us and said to ask the front desk she didn't know how it worked, we has to sign up in advance. She was so awful. For such an expensive hotel, you have to pay for internet! They do have ipads in the room that you can get on for free but it was set up to be quite a bother. We were also told that we would be able to use a steamer for our wedding clothes when we booked the room only to find out we couldn't and if we did we would have a huge charge. After talking with the manager we miraculously had a steamer in our room after being told by the front desk person that they weren't portable. On the up side, the room itself was INCREDIBLE, clean and like nothing I have ever seen, blue carpet and crisp white walls. Floor to ceiling windows with views of the city, perfect lighting for the make up artist and photos, an amazing bathroom and just over all outstanding and dreamy. I would stay here again just because it is that beautiful and it was perfect for a wedding. Hope the staff can try to smile and be a bit more friendly next time. They also let us stay an extra hour after check out time which I thought was very, very nice.

“Charged for a cancelled reservation” I made a reservation and timely cancelled it in writing. The hotel still charged my card, and passed me around when I called about it. No one could help? Then, knowing full well they were wrong, they fought me when I contested the credit card charge. What a dump! Scum! Don't stay with these rip-off artists dirt bags!

“Most improved.” I stayed here in 2010 and in two years this hotel has improved drastically. Great staff. Newly updated rooms. Excellent location. Huge room by Ny standards. It is a huge hotel, so expect throngs in the lobby. Friendly staff and comfort galore. Well-priced for the broadway adjacent location

“Way Downtown But Great Nonetheless!” A wonderful hotel with comfortable beds and wide screen TV. It's right opposite Ground Zero so those who lost folks may want to find somewhere else to stay. Right near Chambers Street subway stop. All around great experience and paid only about $218 through Hotwire!! One caveat - the mini-bar is rigged with some sensor so even if you just LIFT an item to look it, it'll be recorded as a taken item.

“A solid four star hotel in a four-star location” I stayed at this hotel for one day and found it to be a solid four-star hotel in all respects. They upgraded me to a corner suite which had a balcony with a spectacular view. Everything lived up to the four-star level except possibly the pool which was not a scene and had a small pool area. But it was very acceptable. My room was fine, quiet and nicely furnished. They do charge for Internet in addition to parking. They have a town car that will take you to places within one and a half miles but I was not able to use it. It cannot be reserved but utilized on a first-come first-served basis. I would say this hotel is comparable to the Century City Hyatt which is about a half a mile down the same street. The one reason the Hyatt would be preferable is that it is immediately adjacent to the Century City shopping mall and walk able from the hotel. The Intercontinental is too far from the mall to walk. Bottom line is the hotel is fine and I would highly recommend and stay there again myself in an instant.

“My first choice in Fort Worth” My conservative estimate is that I have spent 50 nights in Fort Worth hotels. After bouncing around several locations, this has become my #1 choice in Fort Worth; both business and family trips. The facilities are outstanding; different than your traditional Embassy Suites open-air atrium set-up but I like the feel. Perfect location for walking anywhere in downtown.The big winner here is the staff. Just walking to your room I bet 3 different folks welcome you warmly. If you're trying to decide, this is where you should stay.

“立地は最高だけど・・・” タイムズスクエアのtktsとは目と鼻の先で、とにかく場所が良いことに尽きます。スタッフは可もなく不可もなくといったところです。荷物を預けた際も、引換証と交換でスムースに預け&受取ができました。 ホテル自体も非常にスタイリッシュです。部屋からタイムズスクエアを見下ろすと、N.Y.のど真ん中にいるなぁと感じます。部屋はタイプにもよるのでしょうが、それほど窮屈には感じませんでした。 ただし、夜はロビーがバーになるため人が溢れかえっています。部屋へのエレベーターは、ルームキーを持っている人しか乗れなくなっているため特に危険なことはないと思いますが、あれだけ宿泊客ではない人がロビーにいるのを見るとやや不安は残るところです。

“The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly” I'll start with the good. The grounds of this resort are beautiful. Very well maintained, exotic, and lively with parrots, massive koi (coy) fish, and a duck sanctuary. The beach is well maintained and there are decent water activities if you're so inclined. The staff was also very friendly outside of the maid staff that pretend you're not even there. Great location, too. A block away from Mission Beach and right on the bay. This is where the compliments end though. If this place spent half as much time maintaining their rooms as they do their grounds, this would be a much better place to stay. Unfortunately though, they don't. The decor of this place has an 80's look and feel (because I'm sure it's the last time any of it has been updated). Rather than repair the damaged drywall around our sliding glass door, they used what appeared to be packing tape.
