When we finally made it onto the balcony, it had more spiders and webs than we saw at the zoo. Anything that could leak water, did. Our air conditioner leaked so much, the carpet was soaked all around it. I took a closer look at it on our last day and found mold all over the interior of the A/C unit. Unfortunately, I didn't see that until our check-out day. Who knows what we were breathing in while we were there. The pool is way too small for a resort this size. If you're there while it's busy, good luck getting a seat. All in all, I wouldn't recommend this place. We weren't in San Diego to spend our time in the room, but when we did, it was musty, wet, and moldy.

“Small rooms, Good location” Stayed here the first week of February on business. The best aspects of this hotel: 1.) Location 2.) Common Areas. There is a great lobby and a couple of happening hotel bars. The hotel is situated near the Columbus Circle Mall, as well as several restaurants, starbucks, little markets and pharmacies. The staff was also very friendly. The rooms are small. If you've got a queen size bed, the width of your room will be the width of the bed plus one foot on either side (I had the 150 sq. ft. room). My colleagues complained that when they sat on the toilet, their knees touched the wall (they're about 6 ft tall). As I'm only 5'5", I didn't have this problem. If you are looking to relax in your hotel room, this may not be the place for you. The room is small and the t.v is about 9" and shoved into the closet. If all you want is a place to sleep, then this hotel should be just fine.

“No pretty view, but comfortable, roomy, and good service.” My hosts for a business trip had reserved me a room here recently. As they covered the charges, I can't comment on value - I never saw the bill. My room was on a low floor, and overlooked the top of the entry roof, so no view! But it was very spacious and comfortable. I enjoyed the cozy robe at the end of a long day. Staff members very helpful and friendly. I ordered breakfast from the hang tag one AM, and it arrived right on time and was tasty. One minor suggestion for improvements: Replace those awful fluorescent bathroom lights.
“便利かつおしゃれ” ビジネスで使いましたが、こじんまりしてしゃれた雰囲気です。 ユニオンスクエアにも近く、すぐ近くをケーブルカーの駅もあります。 スタッフも感じがよく、アメニティがロクシタンなのも好感が持てました。 ただビジネス仕様での機能性には欠ける気がしました。

“un bijou” abbiamo trascorso due notti in questa strtuttura molto carina e soprattutto particolare. nella hall è presente una piccola sala cinema dove ogni sera viene proiettato un film. le camere sono molto carine, ben arredate e soprattutto pulite. ogni camera ha un nome differente e richiamano tutti film girati a san francisco l'albergo, anche se si trova in pieno centro, è attaccato ad una via piena di barboni. non sono pericolosi, ma cmq è meglio evitarla del tutto. di fianco all'albergo c'è un pub, molto rumoroso ed aperto fino a tarda notte.

“A Sheraton with a bit of a motel feel” I stayed here for two weekend nights. I couldn't help but feel that it was a little motel-like. Not that it's a bad thing, just different for a modern Sheraton. The Fisherman's Wharf location is convenient if you'll be spending time at the Wharf or seeing Alcatraz since the ferries are down there. Otherwise, I find the Wharf to be a bit distant from the other attractions in SF. The good: nice lobby; fire pits in a few seating areas outside; bed was comfortable; friendly staff The ok: I stayed on the first floor and there was a long walk to the room and I had to open a door to get into the hallway where the rooms were located - a bit of a pain when carrying bags; The room decor was ok but the room with the tub and toilet was a bit dissapointing as it was small and dark (the vanity is located next to this room). The bad: nothing

“Well-located, nice rooms, good service” My stay here was six nights. The first three were business-related, and I stayed in a room with two queen beds. The second part of the trip was for fun, with a friend joining me in Chicago. We booked a one-bedroom suite for those three nights. This is an incredible location. On the corner of State Street, you are just a short walk to the bridge and the heart of downtown. If you like walking (and the weather obliges), you can get most places near downtown. The subway and El are also nearby. I was really happy with the location. The rooms are nicely done and a decent size. The suite was quite nice for two of us old friends to spend time hanging out. The layout is a bit odd (one tiny closet, bathroom off the living room rather than the bedroom). I was on the third floor, then the second. There are only six floors in the building, so there is not going to be much of a view regardless. The only thing that might induce me to try another hotel in Chicago is the quest for a great view. Chicago is so stunning, architecturally, and it would be nice to see that from your room. Amalfi is guilty of one of my pet peeves (the $7 bottle of water), but not the other (the minibar fridge could be used to store an item or two, rather than being electronically monitored like some hotels). But they do have a decent continental breakfast available right on your floor, which is a great perk. The Aveda soap, lotion, shampoo etc. was a nice touch. The service was great. One little thing they could do to improve: add more electrical outlets. I generally have 3-4 gadgets, and there was a dearth of convenient places to plug them in.

“Back Again!” We stayed at this property in July and really liked it. It was convenient, clean and fun. We received a promotion for a $169 rate for Labor Day weekend and decided to stay for my wife’s birthday. When we arrived my wife informed them that it was her birthday and they upgraded us (and the other couple with us) to a small suite. It was a great room. Other reviews have talked about some issues: 1. Small rooms: I have been in smaller rooms in NYC. The W New York has much smaller rooms. These rooms are on the small size but well appointed and outfitted. 2. The basket of goodies: In our first room I found this to be in the way, so when I arrived I put on top of the wardrobe (closet). Also I thought some of the prices for the items in the mini-bar were reasonable, such as $2 for a soda, many of the items were over priced but you don’t take them and go across 6th Avenue and get what you want at a Duane Reed. 3. Amenities: It doesn’t have a concierge or a large staff but it does have room service and I found the front desk to be very accommodating and helpful. The bellboys were always asking us if we need anything. I have stayed in at least 10 different hotels in Manhattan and I would put the Hotel Mela at the top for the price. It is in a great location (particularly for first time visitors), it has great beds and its fun. That’s all you need.

“A Genuine Suite” Unlike many other "suites" this one was the real deal. You enter an area with a couch, desk, TV and fridge, and then there is a door to the bedroom. So if you're in the front of the room watching one of the many TV channel, you won't bother someone in the bedroom (where there's another TV). Room was very clean. Used the wired Internet which was free and fast. Front desk folks all very nice. Plenty of free parking, but be sure you're in the correct lot. Free business center in the lobby with 2 PCs and 2 printers. University is across the street, but that's it for walking distance. Need a car to go anywhere else. Wouldn't hesitate to return.

“The lobby is grand but the rooms? Not so much...” We stayed at this property once before, when the new lobby and tower were under construction (2003)--it is as though the rooms in the Seaport Tower have not been renovated since that time as ours appeared worn and tired, particularly the bathroom. The location is terrific and once again we had a fabulous view of the bay and surrounding area. Not sure what is so Grand about this Hyatt, however, other than the public areas which are very nice as is the pool. Oh, and the price--they must have the market cornered to charge the fees they do for such an average room--thank goodness for the views! If ever we find ourselves in San Diego purely for pleasure I would not stay here and only did so because of husband's business meeting.

“Great for a girls' trip” This was my first visit to this hotel. I found the hotel on Quikbook and called hotel directly to reserve my room; great rate and the fact that it's brand new are what made my decision to go with the place. I visited with my mom and her 2 sisters. All 4 of us fit comfortably in our dbl/dbl room (rm 404). The shower was great (nice water pressure and very hot each time) and the decor was modern and clean. We did not make use of the breakfast room though we did visit it for ice/vending machine. No problems with check-in and check-out and I love the non-smoking policy. I'd recommend this hotel and stay here again.

“Fantastic Everything!” Just got back from this property and I was exceedingly happy with the experience. The service was amazing across all levels. Room was clean and spacious. The bedding package was amazing. And, the location is unparalleled. Whether in Boston for business or pleasure, you can't beat this hotel. It is walking distance from most anything you could want to do. Combine a premium location with staff that genuinely seems to care and it's a combo that you can't beat.

“Loved the Warwick” My husband and I spent three nights at the Warwick, arriving on November 29. We got a great rate on Priceline, which may account for the fact that our room faced the interior (9th floor) and the sound of the building's outside heating units could be heard slightly. When asked about an outside view, the front desk responded it would be $50 per night extra. We opted not to change room. Other than the no view room, we loved the Warwick, the rooms are clean, well appointed, and comfortable. Yes as others said the room was a bit warm but again not a big deal for a short stay. The lobby is beautiful and I loved the ambience of the entire hotel. I definitely would stay here again as it's steps from MOMA, close to subway, and near great places to eat and shop.

“Grand Dame of Downtown Hotels” The Biltmore is a classic old hotel with two distinct parts, the old section and the new tower. I usually book them online using pricing tools like hotels.com or expedia and get great rates, but they are always in the old section, which is fine by me. I am in and out for business so the room works. If I were staying here for several days, I might want to be sure I was in the new tower. The two best parts of the hotel are the health club and the old lobby. The old lobby has been in a ton of movies, it is just a great place to hang out and read and get served cocktails. The health club has a pool that is reminiscent of a pool on a 1930's ocean liner. The Gallery Bar is also great, but I do miss the Grand Ave Saloon and Bernard's.
“They do no wrong in the area of service” From pick up to check in I am having a wonderful stay. I feel cared for in factual experience and not just in corporate self promotionam

“Great 3-Star Hotwire Hotel - Highly Recommended for Downtown Dallas"” Pros: - Very close to downtown - Very personable staff - A mile from American Airlines Arena - Free parking - Across the street from Denny's - Flat screen TVs with all the channels - Clean throughout - Outdoor pool - Very hot water w/ high water pressure - Plenty of space (two bed room) - Great hotwire rate ($44) - Doorman - Free cookie at checkin w/ fresh fruit at front desk - Restaurant - Free and fast internet connectivity - Free USA Today - Fast elevators that stay open on the ground floor for easy entry (major plus!) - Less than 2 miles from Kroger grocery store Cons: - No complimentary breakfast (Buffet for $12 per person) - No micro-fridge Overall: - Fantastic place to stay near downtown/central dallas with a hint of elegance

“Showing its age” I recently stayed at this hotel for a meeting. It is convenient to Love Field (not DFW). This is an aging facility that is showing its years. It's been updated but the quality of work is lacking. For instance, there are no soap dishes in the showers and caulk was used liberally to hide large gaps in bathroom tile. The A/C never got the room very cool. Elevators are very old and tend to malfunction. My room, however, had a comfortable bed and updated TV. The staff were very nice and were always accomodating. Food in the hotel is average but there's a nice diner next door that was very good. Not much else in the immediate area.

“good location, but very expensive parking fee” great location, walking distance to lots of things, nothing can beat that...although parking for $30 is really expensive, there is a parking lot for $5 a day behind PETCO park...another option good breakfast, included with your rate, comfortable beds bizarre thing about a room, we had a studio suite, and all residence inns i stayed at (and i stay at many) all have pull out sofas in studios with one bed...this one did not; we were travelling with friends, so some of us had to sleep on the floor...just something to consider if there are a few people staying in the room

“A Short Walk To Old Town” Padre Trail Inn is a pleasant and quaint motel with a 1960 fee to it. Located close to the Old Town Transit Center, a major hub for train, bus and trolley, this reasonably priced accomodation is a great finf for anyone wishing to spend a lot of time in expensive San Diego without spending a lot of money. It;s prime location, adjacent to San Diego's Historic Old Town is a major plus. Energenic guests can also hike up the hill to the Presido Hill overlooking it all. There is a complimentary breakfast of pastry, cereal and coffee available in the retro restaurant for guests.

“I felt very welcomed” I was greeted at Zip Check in with Room 602, high floor king, no connecting door, away from the elevator. Perfect. Very energetic and helpful staff. Ate dinner at another site, but the breakfast the next morning was quick and appetizing. This is a very good hotel for business travelers and provides good value. Clean rooms, large comfortable bed.

“Excellent!” My husband and I accidently end up here. I was very sure I've booked Best Western River north (through Midashotels), location was interesting and the free parking as well. When we arrived there, we were told that we booked at the Inn of Chicago, which was a Best western in the past. There was no free parking, so I was very disappointed, but that only lasted until I saw the room. It was very nice, very clean and large enough. Location was even better then the best western I booked. We were just steps of Michigan Av and much closer to the lake. It was our beginning of our Route 66 journey, but spend an entire day in Chicago. We walked from the hotel to Lou Mitchell's via Michigan Av. From there we headed toward the lake and stopped at the Sears Tower on our way to the lake. We walk all the way up to the Navy Pear and then headed back to the hotel. In the evening we went to the Hard Rock Cafe, which is in a walking distance and had dinner at the thai restaurant, I don't remember the name, not far from the hotel. We both loved chicago very much, so there's a good chance that we will go back and see a little more of the city. We will absolutely stay in the Inn of Chicago again, even if we have to pay 35$ a day to park our car.

“Beautiful Hotel, Excellent Service” I stayed here with my mum in the Spring for a girly city break and we weren't disappointed. The hotel staff are attentive and professional and can't do enough for you. It's definitely a business hotel, as you can expect in the capital of the US, so i think we got extra attention being the only people there who clearly weren't putting the trip on expenses. We had a bit of confusion when booking in, as we had booked a room with 2 double beds and had been booked into a room with 1 king bed. I have a feeling they thought we were a same-sex couple on paper, as my married name is double-barrel with my maiden name and we were both Mrs. This was resolved quickly though and they were very apologetic. The doormen are very friendly and professional and even helped my mum put some extra shopping in her suitcase in the lobby before we left for the airport. The room was clean, spacious and quiet, with the most amazing pillow top mattresses! I'd had a stiff neck for a week before going away and it had gone by the end of our stay. The service does go above and beyond, but sometimes you do just want to be left alone - especially if you want an afternoon nap! Georgetown is a great location for shopping and just wandering around. It's a really pretty area with a lot of history, but is a cab ride away from the main tourist area. We would get a cab to the museums in the morning, then come back and get cupcakes from Georgetown Cupcakes (as seen on tv), which is a couple of blocks away from the hotel. The best museums we visited were the Crime museum, Museum of American history and the Native American museum (which does amazing vegetarian food!). Our only let down in DC was that the reflecting pool is being renovated, so is empty and surrounded by wire fencing. This was a bit of a disappointment as it ruined the view from the Abe Lincoln memorial. It is an exceptionally clean city though and you can walk just about anywhere once you're in the main drag. We ate near the hotel in the evenings and there's plenty of places to get food. Our favourite was a place called "Clyde's", which is a pub/restaurant which has that "St. Elmo's Fire" feel about it, as do a few of the restaurants in Georgetown. Nice food at a decent price, with a great atmosphere. All in all it was a great trip at a lovely hotel and my mum can't wait to go back again with my dad.
“What you would expect from NYC” This is what New York is supposed to be like!!! Very plush and elegant just what New York is known for!

“Good Value for a Hollywood Bowl Event” Having requested non-smoking, we were pretty upset when we first opened the door of our room. The smell of smoke was overwhelming, and the room was not very clean in appearance. As soon as we contacted the front desk, we received an apology, and a key to a clean & tidy room. Everything was fine from that point on. Hollywood Bowl is close enough to walk, and parking is a breeze - especially compared to the area's "stacked" parking.

“Average” Holiday Inn's lack some consistency and this property is no exception. Overall a good property but not without some problems. No special amenities for Priority Club members. Lobby was like 90 degrees. Room was fine once I was able to crank up the air and drop the temp. Room was in ok shape and clean. Bed was comfortable and wireless worked fine. I had one major problem when I went to jump into the shower in the morning and found the tub filled with coffee grounds. Nice. Overall the stay was ok. Would I stay there again? Probably not.

“Heaven and Hell at the same place!!!” Great location and a great ambiance. Service is ok as long as you do not have any store delivering at the hotel... they are not so good with handling that. The key here is space, if you are looking to comfortable and spacious bedroom; this is clearly not your option! For a couple of days in the city without major shopping, this is the place to be.

“ottimo rapporto qualita' prezzo” l'hotel e' a tribeca. comodissimo alla metropolitana. pregi: rifiniture delle camere, personale, letti, internet gratis. difetti: stanze ai piani bassi non insonorizzate, un solo ascensore. consiglio per la colazione il locale uscendo dalla porta principale a destra. se vi hanno smarrito il bagaglio c'e' un minimarket aperto fino alle 2 di notte.

“This is a LARGE downtown business hotel, but does a great job of it.” Having seen the Westin Bonaventure used in movies for years (True Lies, In the Line of Fire, etc), I stayed here for a business meeting being held at the JW Marriott down the street. For a large, downtown I was extremely pleasantly surprised. The rooms have very recently been refurbished (new carpet, furniture, wall covering). My room was a 31st floor suite (thank you SPG platinum), with a very comfortable bed, great furnishings, and incredibly spacious. Views were unbelievable, and I got to make fun of my colleague who could not face the windows in the elevator (cowered against the door due to fear of heights). Breakfast in the restaurant was very well done, albeit at large downtown business hotel prices. Staff in the restaurant, front desk, bell desk, and doorman were great. My only critical comment would be a softball I threw to the concierge. I asked if he could have a bottle of champagne couriered to a business associate who is taking a new job. The request befuddled him, offering room service on the telephone. I know I was looking for a creative solution (the Ritz or the St Regis would take an address, and charge me out the wazoo to do it, but they'd do it). Instead I had to make other arrangements. No big deal. I recommend this hotel and will return if given the need to return to LA.

“I'll try to stay here every time.” For the same price as nearby hotels, I got a 2-room suite. Bedroom with king bed, bathroom with toilet and shower separated by a door from the sink and closet. Also a big kitchen/living room and desk. Free wireless didn't work in my room but did work in the lobby. Staff was VERY helpful and offered to have me move rooms but the wired internet worked so I stayed in my original room and it worked great. Kitchen had everything you would need for an extended stay. Great location by restaurants, shopping and bars. FULL breakfast is free in the morning, as well as FULL dinner every evening. I'm going to try to stay here every possible time I visit Chicago.
“Top-Notch hotel!” Clean, visually pleasing room, and helpful staff. The valet staff especially were friendly and courteous. Can't beat the location!

“Lovely hotel in perfect central location” This is a very clean and crisp good quality hotel in the heart of central San Fancisco. The hotel is close to everything including good shopping, public transport and Union Square. The rooms are clean and modern and the bed is very comfortable with quality linen. The shower head was powerful, and the room had a shower and bath. My roomed looked out into a central courtyard and to other rooms, but some rooms would have a street view which might be noisey. I have stayed in San Fran several times before and have often found hotel rooms to be noisey with street noise but this room was very quiet which was great. The rooms dont have a jug or cups which means you cant make a coffee when you want. The wine hour is a nice touch and I enjoyed the odd hot chocolate during the afternoon coffee hour. which they also host. I found the hotel staff to be very friendly and helpful and genuine in their attempts to help. I would strongly recommend this hotel as a great base to explore San Francisco

“Great Gold Coast Location” I stayed at the Sutton Place for two nights while in town for my bachelor party. Our group had three rooms at the hotel, and all were quite spacious. The bathrooms are particularly large and appointed with high quality towels, soaps, shampoo, etc. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful from the moment we walked into the lobby up until we checked out. The location of this hotel is amazing. It is located right in the heart of the Gold Coast neighborhood and steps from some of the best restaurants in Chicago. The Whiskey Bar, located on the ground floor of the hotel, was an ideal rendezvous point for my group throughout the trip. The food and drinks here are quite good, not to mention the great ambience. The location is also a short walk to the Oak Street beach on Lake Shore Drive, and all of the shopping on Michigan Avenue and Rush Street. The doormen can hail a cab in seconds or you can walk north to the red line stop at Clark/Division or a few blocks south to the red line stop at Chicago. All in all, you cannot ask for a more central location. The only negative that I might mention is that the rooms, while nice and clean, do not appear to have been too recently renovated. I can't quite put my finger on the vibe of the decor, but it seems like it could stand to have a bit of an update. This, however, would absolutely not deter me from staying at this hotel again. I can't say enough about the staff at every level!! Overall it was a great stay!

“Lovely Hotel in a location that works” Stayed at the hotel arriving December 24th for six nights. I will not repeat the rave reviews for this hotel only confirm that they are all true. I love the location of this hotel for ease of walking either north or south to great neighborhoods, sights and restaurants. We booked an Avenue apartment and if you have spent anytime in hotels in Manhattan you are going to be blown away by the finishes and size......I have friends who live in Manhattan and this accomodation was larger than any other homes. Great hotel and staff and will definitely return.

“Who Trains Your Staff???? Wow!!” It started in the middle of the street as I maneuvered to pull over for the very busy valet parking. The staff assured me everything was ok and helped me to a spot. How refreshing to have door staff that actually gets the door for you. More than once, they came running to do it! There was a little line to get my key and two of the reception workers gave me good eye contact and a nod to let me know that it would just be a moment. Even the bellman gave a nod and said, "It will just be a moment." A bit of chit-chat each time I walked through the lobby. This is just the best-trained staff I have encountered in a long time. Guess what?? It makes a difference!! The room had no view, but had a roomy feel, as did the bathroom. Bed was super comfy. No noise at all from surrounding rooms or hallway. This was a great stay. It's nice to see that some hotels still care enough to make sure their staff is well trained and makes the customer feel as if they matter. Will definitely stay again.

“Very ordinary hotel” This hotel was a disappointment. The rooms need upgrading; the wallpaper was coming off the walls in mine. No minibar, no tea/coffee making facilities, severely over-priced buffet breakfast. The only two positives which I will remember are the location, which is excellent, and the beds, which are extremely comfortable. The freshly-baked cookie that you get at check-in is a nice touch, but I will certainly not stay here again.

“CLOSE to the Airport, but a good night's sleep and stay” I had to fly out of CMH after several days of meetings, so stayed here on my last night so I would be close to the airport. When they say it's close, they mean it's CLOSE. You are literally in the airport circle drive, just a stone's throw from the control tower. But, interestingly enough, noise wasn't an issue at all, and it was a very restful stay. If you have an early morning outbound or late evening inbound flight, this would be a great place to stay. You are inside the airport grounds so there are no "neighborhood" issues to deal with (which can sometimes be an issue with hotels located near airports); it's kind of like a little village with several hotels and a McDonald's all clustered together. You can drop off your rental car and rely on the HGI shuttle to get you to/from the terminal - but if you do so, there's nowhere else to go to eat except the HGI restaurant (which wasn't half bad) or the McDonald's across the street. The front desk and cleaning staff were great - very friendly and helpful, and made you feel welcome and not at all rushed. I had a dinner and breakfast at the hotel restaurant - service was OK, food was pretty decent and priced fair for a hotel. The hotel itself was very clean - all common areas and especially my room, that also made the stay very pleasant. They had a pool and fitness center - nothing huge, but adequate for a hotel of this type. The fitness center only had a few items, one treadmill, but there wasn't a crowd when I went in there. Could be an issue if it was a peak time when several people wanted to use it. Everything else was pretty much standard HGI; but the rate was very good (~$100 midweek) the staff were pleasant, the hotel was very clean, and the room was a decent size (see pictures). Would definitely stay here again if in the area, especially the day of arrival or the evening before I leave the next morning.

“Great Place to Stay with Kids” Wife, toddler and some other extended family members stayed here for 4 nights in October 2012. Atrium style hotel was great for kids to run around, look at the fish in the indoor ponds etc. Breakfast and happy hour were both complimentary. WiFi was expensive at ~ $16/day. Suite style room had a living room (TV, pullout sofa, wet bar, refrigerator) and very large bedroom including bathroom and 2nd vanity in the bedroom area. Room was clean, hotel was mostly quiet etc. Outdoor pool was nice, a lot of shade. Great location in Biltmore area. Walk ~ 1/2 block to the outdoor Biltmore shopping center.

“Perfect from check in to check out” We stayed here for 4 days and it was like a home away from home. The staff were super helpful from check in and made sure we were comfortable. We had left NY in the aftermath of Superstorm Sandy and needed a place to stay. We originally booked 2 nights but the hotel was great and extended our stay for another 2 days - this was really great in light of our circumstances. The rooms were very large and comfortable. The beds were great. There was a swimming pool that the kids liked. This is in a great location and we were able to walk to many of the sights like Quincy market and the Aquarium.. We really enjoyed the Boston Tea Party museum right behind the hotel. We will definitely use this hotel on our next trip to Boston.

“Nice Hotel, Lovely City” I stayed here for one night while on business. The location is near the 19th & Market SEPTA station and close to downtown restaurants and shopping. The room was heaven! Quiet, comfortable, clean. It was everything I needed after a day spent traveling. The hotel's staff was very fun and pleasant, too. I would stay at this hotel again and recommend highly to everyone.

“Nice historic hotel” I stayed for two nights in the 1920s section of the Driskill. I like historic hotels and this one is in excellent shape. The rooms are nicely done and everything is kept up. The building and common areas are beautiful. The location is right downtown, within easy walking distance of many or the music and dining spots. The front desk is efficient. It is an older building so the rooms are smaller then new hotels, but they are nicely furnished. My bed was very comfortable. However, I could not sleep well since the central air is really loud. It is hot & humid even at night so keeping the air on was a necessity. It worked great, but I could not sleep. As other reviewers have noted, coffee is available in the lobby, not in the rooms. Parking is valet and expensive. I don't really mind the cost on a business trip, but I do mind the excessive amount of time it took to get my car. I waited half an hour - and this was after calling down before I left my room. The valets were all very nice, but rather disorganized. I parked in a public garage a block away the second night - cost less then the hotel & quicker. The Driskill does have the best hotel bar ever - worth a visit even if you are not staying. I loved the idea of being able to take the elevator down from my room into the bar and having a bite to eat there, then zipping back up to bed. Unfortunately, the restaurant is closed Sun & Mon eves, and that kitchen also serves the bar. I’m glad I tried the Driskill, but would not stay again unless it was a Tues-Sat eve and in the winter (or whenever it cools down in Austin).

“What a lovely surprise - one of the best in NYC” The NYC East side Marriott was a fantastic surprise for us. We must have been in a newly renovated room because it is very hard for me to imagine that all the rooms can be this nice, and I am rather picky – you can look at my other reviews for NYC rooms and you will find this ranks higher than most. The room furniture seemed brand new and very tasteful. The beds were better than the most of the luxury chains, with 300+ thread count sheets, full down comforters (and an extra one in closet too), partial down pillows AND regular pillows, lovely soft chenille throws on each bed -all so clean and new. The mattresses were the highest quality. The toiletries in the immaculate marble and granite bathroom were quite nice higher end products in great packaging and a perfectly clean double shower curtain and plush towels were also very pleasing. The bathroom was quite luxurious compared to your average NYC 4* hotel, and better than any of the 4* hotels in NY I’ve been at in last few years. The plasma TV had many channels including HBO. The staff were friendly and courteous and efficient – checking in took 2 minutes. The hotel is opposite the Intercontinental and “W” hotels and a block from the Waldorf Astoria. It’s location is fantastic and there is a subway line right there, not to mention easy access to the better restaurants on 2nd Ave. The room we got was absolutely spotless, as were all the public areas and hallways leading to it - a stark contrast to some of the ghetto 4* hotels we have stayed at in NY before. The lobby area is quite small and not fancy, but very clean and much more appealing than the lobbies at other NY establishment – highly polished stone, nice furniture, clean carpets. The only “older” spot was the elevators which were a bit small and cramped and showed a bit of age. There is a small gym on the very top floor which you need to take two separate elevators to get to, no matter which floor you are on. It’s a bit cramped, but has gorgeous views of the city, and was very clean, with stacks of fresh towels ready to go. The only negative I can state about this hotel was that the noise level from the street was quite high, so the windows didn’t have enough sound protection for my taste, perhaps an issue on lower floors, as indicated by other reviews. I used ear plugs and all was fine. I highly recommend this hotel, but you may want to be sure you end up on a renovated higher floor, in case the other reviews are indicative of other floors or rooms that were not similar to ours.

“The Ritz!” I stayed here as part of a business trip and overall I enjoyed my stay. The rooms are well appointed but that is to be expected at this level. The customer service is very good but not the best I've experienced (that would go to the Park Hyatt in Tokyo). I say this because I started my stay at the adjacent JW Marriott and then transferred to the Ritz during my stay (they didn't have rooms at the Ritz for the first few nights of my visit). When I went to the front desk of the Ritz to check in, I asked if they could help me move my stuff from the JW. The front desk staff said that the bell man was out on a call and that I could ask the JW staff to assist. My request was actually a test (of course I can move my own stuff) and the Ritz failed. The response I expected would have been, "let me call the JW and have that arranged for you". This is the Ritz, right? What the others have said about the lobby is true - it's very small. I didn't have a problem with it but I can imagine check-in could be an issue. I did use the spa and it is great. The staff is very professional and the massage was one of the best I've ever had! I will definitely return.

“So-so location but a good deal overall” Stayed here with a friend for three nights. At a little under $100 a night, the room was a bargain, at least by San Francisco standards. It was not exactly luxurious, obviously a bottom-of-the-barrel place that has been given a face-lift. But it was decent sized, clean, comfortable, in good shape, and it had some stylish touches that were nice. It was also nice to have wifi, real mugs and glasses, and a coffee maker. The iPod dock did not work, we called the front desk and told them but no one ever came and fixed it. Not the end of the world. The neighborhood was not terrible but not great. Our friends in San Francisco reacted with varying degrees of horror when we told them where we were staying but I didn't feel unsafe. There are a lot of homeless people around, even for San Francisco. If this bothers you, you might consider looking elsewhere. Not a huge concern to me. There was also a lot of traffic noise from the street, pretty common in a big city, but if you are picky about this it's something to keep in mind. If you can put up with the noise and the so-so location, the Good Hotel is a good choice.

“Zentrale Lage, renoviert, mit der richtigen Zimmerwahl gut” Der große Vorteil des Hotels ist die Lage. Gegenüber dem Waldorf Astoria und direkt neben dem neuen Hyatt 48 Lex gelegen, befindet sich das Hotel an der Lexington Av. und der 49Str. Der Service ist, wie Marriott üblich, freundlich und ordentlich. Die Preise sind NY angemessen, die Zimmer auch. Bei der Zimmerwahl und der Buchung unbedingt ein EXEC Zimmer buchen und als Wunsch "möglichst weit oben" angeben. Ich hatte das Zimmer 3006 auf der 30. Etage, welches neben einem Bett auch noch eine Sitzecke, einen Schreibtisch und somit eine angemessenen Größe hat. Durch den Bau "über eck" war das Zimmer größer als die andreen, ggf. beim CheckIn nach einem CornerRoom fragen. Die Zimmer wurden in den letzten Jahren renoviert. Es sind unzählige Steckdosen vorhanden, was ich als Geschäftsreisender sehr begrüße. Die nächste U-Bahn ist nur eine Strasse entfernt, ebenfalls ein großes Kriterium. Wer Urlaub machen will, der sollte sich alternativ auch das 48Lex von Hyatt anschauen, gerade in 2011 neu eröffnet. Dazu mal in meinem Blog unter svenblogt.de schauen und 48 Lex in das Suchfeld eintippen.

“Decent hotel, good location to airport” I stayed one night at this hotel at the end of April. The airport shuttle runs every 20 minutes and drops off to a few other hotels, but it's not a bad wait. The hotel is big and has a nice large lobby with all kinds of amenities like a coffee bar, gift shop, restaurant, etc. The restaurant was pricey and we opted not to use it. We actually crossed the busy street at the crosswalk and walked down several blocks to the Denny's. There were some other fast food places so that is an option if you don't mind walking a bit. We did get asked for money and politely declined. The hotel itself was all right. It is a bit tired and could use some updating, especially in the hallways and rooms. Ours was very clean and comfortable, so we had no complaints, but I would say it is a 3 star, not 4 star quality. We used the pool and hot tub area, the kids enjoyed it and we enjoyed the large hot tub. We also took advantage of the weight room, they have an excellent weight room with everything. We didn't have any noise issues while in our room. If I were to pay full rate I would say it wasn't worth it, but for the great priceline rate I got, definitely.

“very helpful staff, good overnight stop” We spent a night here back at the start of March, overnighting on our way up to North East Arizona. The property was in a slightly confusing location when trying to find it from the freeway. The check-in person was extremely helpful and friendly and we loved the room, which had a nice southwestern decor and was very clean and spacious. As we were there for one night only I can't comment on how good it would be for an extended stay, but having the small kitchen and living area separate from the bedroom made it very comfortable for the short stay. Breakfast, which was included, was okay - nothing to rave about, but also nothing wrong with it.

“Older, But Very Nice” I've stayed at the Palace on a number of occasions. Service has been well above average every time. Rooms have been very nice. Always clean. Public areas are attractive and well maintained.

“Terrific Hotel close to Airport” We stayed at this Hampton Inn on the 1st and last nights (2 nights total) of our week long trip to Big Bend National Park. The staff is super friendly. Rooms are very clean. There are 4 terminals with high speed internet available in the lobby. The shuttle service was quick and safe. We even had the shuttle ferry us to a recommended spot for dinner the 1st night. The price (with AAA discount) was a deal. The hotel was fairly full both nights but remained nice and quiet!

“Great location, excellent staff” Within walking distance to Camden Yards, Little Italy and Fells Point, this hotel is in the perfect spot for Inner Harbor touring. A very well-kept property, it is supported by a very friendly and accommodating staff who fulfilled our every need. Our request for special sleep accommodations was handled with prompt, friendly attention. Complimentary breakfast is good, but just below the average hot breakfast buffet found at similar hotels, as they were somewhat lacking in variety and visual appeal.

“Pretty Decent” Nice Place. Was here to meet a friend and hang out for the weekend. Also stayed at a Kimpton in Chicago but hated that one (had bed bugs so ran the wind outta there). This location wasn't bad and I actually had a good experience. It was average, nothing spectacular but I did sleep well although the rooms were small. Would stay again if it was a great rate and a short stay.

“Good deal” Got an amazing deal... stopped at the Florida Welcome Center on I-95 right before we entered Jacksonville. Found a coupon book advertising Comfort Suites Airport for $58. Got a CLEAN suite at a clean and new hotel for six people for 58 bucks, with free waffles and warm express breakfast setup. You can't beat that.

“Average hotel at best” Very average hotel at best. Rooms need serious updating. Housekeeping staff constantly knocking on door. Disappointed that, while the club lounge is down, they did not take care of their frequent starwood guests. Typically they would offer a free breakfast in their restaurant, at other starwood properties. Not so at this location. The food at the hotel is a plus though. Perfect location to the universities...Staff and management could be a bit more professional.

“Great location; comfy clean building” I've stayed twice, most recently in April, 2011. You can't beat the location in a terrific neighborhood right by Lincoln Center and the Subway. I stayed in a one-bedroom, which had more than generous space. There is a full kitchen, which helps save a bundle on food expenses in NYC, since you can eat breakfast and other meals in the apartment (there is a Food Emporium supermarket across the street and uptown a block or so and a gourmet deli next door). There is a coffee pot in the room - and a bag of ground coffee, which I thought was a nice touch. The staff was attentive. I stayed here on another occasion with my children and had a very pleasant stay. Guests have gym privileges at Club Reebok, across the street. I didn't have time to go, but heard it's nice. The Phillips Club subway stop (66th / Lincoln Center) is a few stops north of the theater district and Penn Station.

“The reason I choose Marriott” Excellent and friendly staff made this a welcoming, relaxing overnight stay. Was pleased in the size of the room and that it was perfectly clean and comfortable, as I've come to expect from Marriott. This is one of the better Marriott's I've visited recently, service was far better than the Marriott in downtown Chicago. Concierge lounge was average with an acceptable food and drink variety and welcoming staff. Will return for future travels.

“The Adolphus lives up to its name” The lobbies were beautiful. The room was pretty and comfortable. I could get used to to an all-marble bathroom. The magnifying mirror is nice. The TV was topnotch with good channel selection. The bed was supremely comfortable. The room has plenty of space and comes equipped with a safe and two luggage stands and plenty of drawers for those staying longer. Unusual for a downtown 4 star: in room wireless internet is free! While waiting for the valet to bring your car, if you stand around the corner of the lobby driveway, you can see the ramp into the parking lot and see an old-fashioned, continuously-moving open 'person-lift' that the valet drivers jump onto in order to ascend to the upper levels The criticisms are minor, to be sure. If you arrive at check-in 'rush hour', you may find yourself in a traffic queue on Commerce Street; the circular driveway is ample at most times but a little small for peak periods. The beds are not heavy, but move a little bit. This allowed the bed next door to knock against the wall just a little bit, not bad. At the time of this writing, parking was $26/day, pretty standard for a downtown hotel; their valet service was quick.

“Bonne situation mais hotel vieillissant” Je suis resté 3 jours dans cet hôtel qui n'est pas à la hauteur (ou plus à la hauteur) de la qualité attendue. L'emplacement en revanche est idéal pour visiter San Francisco : proximlité des magasins, de la baie, d'un marché extraordinaire ! En revanche l'hôtel en lui même est vieillissant. Au delà de l'absence totae de charme dans cet immense bâtiment de beton, les peintures sont vieilles (couloirs et chambre), les salles de bain sont dignes d'un hôtel 1 étoile (vieille, pas pratique, pas très propres). Il n'y a pas de mini bar, même pas une bouteille d'eau !! Ma clef de porte a du m'être changé 4 fois en 3 jours car elle ne fonctionnait pas... Je précise que j'étais au 16e etage avec un balcon qui avait en revanche une assez jolie vue sur la baie. Il y a vraiment mieux à San Francisco pour ce prix ! Le lobby qui est très beau

“Wonderful Hotel” Booking: I contacted the hotel directed to make reservations. It turned out to be less than any website. We paid $112 for each room a night, however, it was on weekdays. Checking In: We arrived an hour early and to my surprise they had our rooms ready immediately, which was nice since we had been traveling all day. Interior: I loved the Japanese theme of the hotel yet it still remained western enough to not feel like it was over board. Simple and elegant. Rooms King Room: Nice and clean. The only thing is that it is a bit small to have any visitors, but its perfectly fine for just two people. Deluxe Double Room: Once again very nice and clean. We love the little sitting area. Since there were 7 people traveling (only 4 stay at the hotels), we used this room as a hang out place at times. Service: The front desk was very accommodating and answered any questions that we had. Housekeeping always did a wonderful job with the rooms. Valet however was not always available but parking was easy. Amenities and Dining: Since we were not in the hotel during the day very often, I cannot review on the amenities or the restaurant . We wish we could have taken advantage of what the hotel had to offer but there is so much to do in SF. We love the little mini mall that is attach to the hotel especially Ichiban USA. It is a wonderful place to buy little snacks and souvenirs for friends and family. So inexpensive and fun. Places to go in SF: -Check out Coit Tower at night and during the day if you have time. -We had dinner in North Beach one night, which is highly recommended. -One of our favorite activities was taking a small road trip to Stinson Beach. From San Francisco after crossing the Golden Gate Bridge, take Hwy. 101 North approximately three miles to the "Hwy. One, Stinson Beach" exit. Follow the signs and enjoy your drive down one of the most scenic highways in the nation. Stinson Beach is approximately 20 miles from San Francisco. Make sure you stop at Muir Beach Outlook, you won't be disappointed.

“Thin walls” Went to check out Georgetown University for college bound daughter. Looked a number of hotels in Georgetown and decided on Holiday Inn. The hotel is a bit far from the shool as well as restaurants and is not accessible to the metro. There is a van but it became a problem each day getting back from the sites once we got there. The rooms were ok except for the very thin walls. If you want to know everything the guy in the next room said or watched on TV ask me; I heard every word. We ran the AC all night to block out the noice that went on until after 2AM resulting in a room we could freeze meat in. The really nice thing about the hotel was the staff which seemed competely overwhelmed with work but really tried hard to be nice. With some may hotels in DC, you might do better.

“Extremely Nice Hotel - Convenient Location” I stayed at this hotel in June 2009 due to it's close location to the airport. The Hampton Inn - Jacksonville Airport is consistent with all of the Hampton Inn's that I have stayed at. I was very surprised at how large the rooms were in comparison to other Hampton hotels! The Good - Large Rooms - Comfortable Bedding (consistent with all Hampton Hotels) - Quality Furnishing(s) and Room Decor - Clean\Nice Outdoor Pool and Hot Tub - Close to Airport - Friendly\Helpful Staff The Neutral - Breakfast was just "OK" in comparison to other hotels in this chain The Bad - Absolutely Nothing! You can never go wrong in staying at a Hampton as their quality is consistent across the board. I will definitely stay at this hotel in the future.

“Lukewarm experience, expensive overnight parking” This hotel really failed to “wow” me, but it gets the job done for the busy road warrior. A few pros: • Surprisingly quiet, despite the fact that I overheard the desk clerk telling another guest the hotel was full the nights of my stay • My third floor room had a very spacious bath • The bedding is very comfortable, complete with feather pillows and down comforter • The entry is stylish and inviting; the air conditioning was nice and cool and the décor handsome and sophisticated in a central Texas fashion A few cons: • The hotel has only three elevators for a 16 story facility, meaning lengthy waits during high traffic times • The bath towels are rough and harsh, in line with the “John Wayne toilet paper” provided • In-room hotel coffee is never “the greatest,” but this coffee is especially bad. Even after several potsm the drink reminded me merely of coffee-flavored water Now the ultimate negative and the one that will prevent me from returning to this hotel in the future: The hotel parking garage is valet only, and this privilege comes at a hefty rate of $23.00 per night. Taking a cab to and from the hotel, of course, eliminates this concern, but when I am in Austin for business, I simply need a car to get to/from meetings and client/colleague meals, no ifs, ands or buts. As a result of having to expense nearly $50 simply for parking my rental car for two nights, I will need to continue looking elsewhere for Austin lodging.

“Love this Hotel !!!” The rooms are cozy and comfy, the staff is courteous, kind and thoughtful and the location is ideal. The only problem I have ever had here is some parking issues, but they were always addressed immediately and resolved on the spot. I will come back again and again and again. PS. - the bar is great and food is good.

“Total RIP-Of!!! $20 Resort fee at the Check in” This hotel charge " $20 Resort fee " per night! at the check in; that incluid internet, pool, parking and you can chose 1 snack per day from a list of snaks they have at the front desk 50cents snacks, and incluid locals calls and the pool towels ah! and the gym is incluid! It is The same size that a regular room with 4 old fashion treadmills no machines at all!. So if u don't need Internet or snaks or parking you still have to pay the $20 DOLLARS RESORT FEE! The only windows the rooms have are facing the pool, NO PRIVACY! I didn't like the hotel at all. I felt upset since the moment I saw they were charging hidden fees like the RESORT FEE!

“Home away from home” I started a new job in San Antonio, and stayed at this hotel as my temporary home until I found a San Antonio apartment. It's very easy to feel at home here. The rooms are semi-suite style with a sofa, big screen TV (which I can connect my laptop to), and fridge. There is also a microwave in the eating area. Continental breakfast is also provided. Internet is free but a bit slow. Staff are very helpful and pleasant. The only cons are: no weight equipment in the fitness center and getting on the I-10 access road can be a challenge during rush hour.

“Some major disappointing mistakes” Though this was a rather pretty hotel, with plush beds and modern baths, there was serious oversight with the staff. When I checked in I was given a key to a room that was still occupied. I do not mean that house keeping had yet to come, I mean that the previous guest had yet to vacate. I do not understand how this happened, and my questions through the hotel's website go unanswered. I was honestly uneasy staying there. If they could so easily issue me a key to another guest's room what was stopping them from giving the key to my room away. I expect such antics from a hostel, not from a well appointed hotel. I also expect management to respond to such serious issues.

“日本語が通じるけど・・・” NY出張でこのホテルを利用したのは2回目です。すぐ近くにスタバがあり、立地は良いです。今回残念だったのは部屋に蚊がいたこと。あいにく満室だったため部屋を替えてもらうこともできず、ベープを入れてもらいましたが退治には至らず、悩まされました。日本語が通じるのでこうした交渉も楽でしたし、真摯に対応して頂きましたが、そもそも蚊がいなければそれも必要なかったわけで、まさに「痛し痒し」。たまたまだとは思いますが、安いホテルではないですし・・・

“Loved this resort!” Just returned from a trip to San Antonio. We stayed two nights at the Marriott River Walk and two nights for R & R at the JW Marriott Hill Country Resort. I am glad we stayed at the two different locations as it is not a quick trip to the River Walk. That being said, we loved the Hill Country Resort. We were able to totally unwind at the resort enjoying both the adult pool in the pool complex and the separate spa pool at the spa, free if you book a service. The hotel and grounds are absolutely luxurious. This hotel complex ranks at the top of the many places we have stayed in our travels. It totally met our needs for relaxation. We felt rejuvenated when we left. It would be important to note that we stayed midweek in October. I am not sure the relaxation effect would be the same in the middle of the summer when family activity would be present. We will definitely return if we are ever in the San Antonio area. Wonderful stay!

“Great Location/Standard Holiday Inn” The location is the Best! It is right across the street from the Cruise Ships stand, Ferries, Tours and other attractions on the Bay. You can take the Ferry to Coronado Island cost is $6.00 round trip and then take the free shuttle to the Coronado Hotel to visit. .....Near the HI on the Bay on the corner maybe about half block away is a visitor’s center with lots of good information. If you like to walk early in the morning; Walking along the pier is great. Around the hotel are many restraints, Ruth Chris Steak House, Seafood Restaurant and other small eating places. You can walk to see the USS Midway and on to the Seaport Village with cute shop and restaurants. The hotel also offers free shuttle to many of these places, check with the concierge. The hotel also has a shuttle to and from the airport every 30 minutes (I think) The HI at the Bay is a standard Holiday Inn. Our room was cleaned but you could see the wear and tear on it .Our room on the 8th floor looked over the Bay. Many rooms have a balcony with 2 chairs and table for sitting. That along made the hotel alright for me. The view of the sun setting on the Bay was wonderful. I understand that there is renovation going on at the hotel........ The hotel staff was friendly and helpful,. all questions were answered courteously. There is free internet service at the hotel. It is located at the concierge’s desk, which is a good idea to me. You have to stand to use it. Therefore you don’t stay as long as if you were sitting. Others don’t have to wait as long to use computer. The lobby area was a little dark but a pleasant sitting area. This is family hotel also; because of the children eat free breakfast in the restaurant. We had a great time! I would stay here again

“Surprisingly nice for a Marriott” We were pleasantly surprised with this hotel. Normally we aren't huge fans of Marriott branded properties but this one was nice! The room was clean. Bathroom was nice, and spacious. Beds were really comfortable. The paintings that were behind the beds in place of headboards were a bit "loud" but that's okay. My only gripe was that we paid $56 via Priceline for the hotel, but had to pay $28 to valet the car (plus tip). The valets were great, one even walked my husband to the car when he forgot his cellphone charger in it. But yeah, $28?! Self-parking was full due to an event downtown at one of the stadiums. Every other garage in the area was full too due to the event (not sure what it was). It just kind of irritated me that the hotel wasn't full, but the parking garage was because non-guests can park in it and fill it up. Not cool. Essentially the only way out of the valet parking was to leave downtown for dinner and come back later after the event goers had left downtown. Didn't want to bother. There were quite a few people milling around the lobby the whole time. But I've noticed this quite often in downtown Indy. This hotel was a bit further out than some other locations we've stayed downtown. In the super cold January temps the walk toward Circle Center and restaurants just beyond there wasn't the greatest. I'd stay again though!

“Excellent Hotel All Around” Travelled on Business - would stay here for pleasure. Location is nice - near good restaurants (mainly chains - but some others, too), right on the water (get em in the water!), and easily accessible to a variety of businesses. I expect good service at the full Marriotts and this met that expectation. The room is updated with a flatscreen, clean bathroom, and reasonably zippy internet. Views as you can read below are great. I won't repeat it, but it's true. Staff is helpful and courteous without being over the top. The kicker at this Marriott is the lounge. Should you be (un) fortunate enough to travel a lot and maintain status to get you to the lounge, it is as well-appointed as they come. I counted 4 folks working the lounge one night from serving drinks, to making sure food was full (more on that coming) to cleaning up those impossibly small plates they insist you use. Breakfast had an omelette bar... not eggs in a chafing pan... an actual made to order omelette. "Snack" options included wings, nachos and soft pretzels one night with sliders and associated accompaniments. The next night (much to my surprise but seafood not-eating chagrin) was bacon wrapped scallops and oysters in the half-shell. They stick to the schedule, though, so be punctual or be left eating chocolate dipped strawberries for dessert. People will wine about parking, but they always do. You are downtown in a major US metropolitan area. Parking costs money. Marriott waterfront is no different. Cabs seemed plentiful if you are a cab rider. Seems to host a lot of events as I often see people with lanyards enjoying the lobby. It does seem to get a lot of business traffic and I did notice some cab lines in the evenings a couple of nights. It is right next door to an outdoor concert venue and spitting distance from the aquarium if you like penguins and other aquatic life. I could see the Ravens stadium and it wasn't too many blocks from where the Orioles allegedly play baseball. I've stayed at a few of the properties in Baltimore including other Marriotts and this has been the best stay I've had. One of my favorite full service marriott's in the country.

“Another Great Stay” Just can't get over the consistency of this hotel. It is comfortable, breakfast is good, relaxed atmosphere, clean, upscale, and all round convenient to everything great in Philly! Avenue of the Arts is only 3 blocks away. Historic District is 5 blocks away. Shopping downtown is at the doorstep. Nationally known Reading Terminal Market is 4 blocks away. This is the first time that we had our car with us, so we parked it at the garage that the hotel has arrangements with and never got it out once for our 48 hours in the city. Parking is cheap compared to the $48 that the other downtown hotels are now charging. There is a 20 minute loading zone directly in front of the hotel. Staff is knowledgeable and will help in any way they can. The guests at the Alexander Inn seem to be more and more international, so the word is out about this place. Anytime we are in Philly, this is where we will stay.

“A Great Bargain & A Great Hotel” Spent 3 nights with a family of 2 adults and 3 kids in one double bedded room. Paid $179.00/night thru the Holiday Inn Express website. Fantastic rate for this hotel and location. 2 blocks from Rockefeller Center, St. Patricks Cathedral, Times Square. Much shopping and many dining choices all around. Super service. Everyone at the hotel were friendly and very helpful. CLEAN - CLEAN - CLEAN. Hotel is brand new so nothing to complain about at all. Felt very safe and very comfortable. If there is a negative it is the size of the rooms. Cramped, but average for NYC. Front desk reception aisle is literally an aisle way, seperated from the breakfast area by the buffet bar. Sometimes difficult to maneuver in or out of hotel on either side as it's so narrow. 5-10 peoople in the lobby area and it's a crowd! Forget it though -- go and enjoy!

“LOVED IT!!!!!” Wow, the lower east side has really changed since the last itme i was there. it is the hippest part of town. i almost didn't know we were at the hotel when we pulled up. we had king studio suite and it was huge, in comparison to other nyc hotels. clean and cool furnishings. floor to ceiling windows, modern and large bathrooms with rainshower (light water pressure was a bummer). the platform bed was not the most comfortable but the sheets & pillows were, so it evened out. i am definitately staying here next trip.

“Great Time in Hollywood” Hotel: Very nice. Room was great. Shower was huge! Stayed in room 821 I want to say and would go back in a heartbeat. Pool: Place to be. Very nice. Spent all day here. Shopping: Walked over to Melrose and found great shops. Shopping off Hollywood Blvd too. Nightlife: Les Deux right off Las Palmas, Area in west Hollywood. Tons of other places too. Dining: Ate at Blowfish (great food) and Dolce (good as well) Did room service in the hotel one night too. Car: I wasn't traveling all through L.A. no car was needed. I wouldn't recommend it. Plenty to do within the area.

“Loved this hotel” I paid about $670 for 2 nights at this hotel on priceline as a named hotel and I thought it was very nice. It's on Conneticut Ave which is busy during the day but fairly quiet at night. The location is reasonably handy for visiting Dupont Circle and not too far from the White House and environs. I ate in the restaurant and got good service and the place had a nice atmosphere & reasonable prices for this standard of hotel. I arrived quite late at night and just wanted a sandwich so they made me one rather than insisting I order a big meal from the dinner menu which was good of them - especially as there are not many places to eat nearby at night. I stayed at the Hay Adams hotel the following night which was also lovely, but more expensive. The lobby of the Hay Adams is fairly small though whereas the Mayflower has a lovely spacious lobby with a wide bright corridor leading from the front of the hotel to the back (entrances on both sides) so that although there's a lot going on there with business events etc (the Ugandan President was there 1 of the days I was staying there) it doesn't feel as cramped as the lobby of the Hay Adams. And despite the activity on the ground floor of the Mayflower, the rooms are peaceful and comfortable. On the other hand, the Hay Adams has views to die, marvellous roof top terrace & free internet (unlike the Mayflower). It's a hard choice between them. The Mayflower was cheaper, but the HA has a slighlty grander feel to the place & a nice downstairs bar which is cosy & friendly unlike the more open lobby bar in the Mayflower. But in any case, both are highly recommended!

“Great visit” Been travelling a ton for business and we were booked in the Cliffs for a two night stay. I was put in an end suite that was tremendous, beautiful living room, bar, 2 bathrooms and a beautiful bedroom w/ small porch overlooking the valley. Had room service the first night and food was great. pools were beautiful and clean, check in was flawless and service wa terrific w/ them driving me to my room in a van. wish the wife and kids were w/ me.
“Good hotel, but very far from LA” It is a standard HoJo Inn, good bed and quiet hotel, but it is really far from main attractions at LA.

“had reservation unilaterally cancelled” I booked at 2 night stay through otel.com; it was at a low price (roughly $148/night) so i expected to be in one of the small rooms at the Nikko commented on in prior reviews. I received an email from otel.com yesterday (Monday) stating that due to "extreme and unusual circumstances they [Hotel Nikko] are no longer able to honour this booking". I was offered a choice of going to a rather poorly reviewed hotel in the area and receiving a 10% credit or getting a refund of the amount I paid (I had to pay in advance for the pleasure of this treatment). This all occurred on a Monday prior to my upcoming visit (arriving Friday). I emailed otel.com back, asking for an explanation but received no answer until today (Tuesday). otel.com is based in Turkey.... and responds to emails on local time. I informed otel.com that this cancellation is unacceptable and that I assume the cancellation occurred because they found some other folks to pay more for the room. It does call into question the meaning of a reservation if it can be terminated unilaterally (maybe it should be called a "potential reservation"). I have not received a coherent answer. I also told otel.com that i would never use their service again and that I would tell my friends not to as well. So, friends--- be forewarned--- the price may seem right but there is no accountability here; I would avoid otel.com and I'm not sure that the Nikko doesn't bear some responsibility as well. (I'm lucky I was able to find a place in a decent hotel for not a huge amount more--- $209/night--- so not the end of the world but highly annoying and surely not worth the effort.)

“Location, location, location!” We stayed here for a wedding weekend, and the first and best thing I have to say about this hotel is that the location is AWESOME, especially for a wedding weekend. There's tons of shopping, restaurants, etc. It's a pretty good trek from the airport though, so you'll want to take that into account. That being said, let's talk about the hotel. The pros: -Staff is incredible and very friendly. We had a really late arrival, and they let us take beverages from the mini-mart downstairs at no charge. (It's the little things.) -Housekeeping was incredibly understanding and helpful when we needed our room cleaned later due to the wedding festivities. They were kind, patient, and friendly whenever we ran into them. -The rooms are large, comfortable, and the beds were soft. It was like sinking into a cloud. -The pool/workout area offers water. -Free parking at a full-service property!! -We rarely heard our neighbors, if at all. The "eh": -The rooms are dated and even though the rooms have been renovated, they still seem dated, and I could see a lot of water damage on our room. -Our toilet didn't seem to have enough water pressure to flush correctly, and we had to hold it down multiple times. The shower water pressure wasn't that great either, and we were on a lower floor. -Our door didn't shut completely. Several times we thought we had pulled it closed, and we would come back to find it ajar. Not sure if it was our error, housekeeping, or a combination, but it was a little alarming, to say the least. -CNN didn't seem to work or be included with the cable package - it was a constant car commercial. The rooms overlooking the lake were really peaceful, and we would have liked to have one. :) Overall, at a lower rate, I think this hotel is a great value. It's not as nice as some full-service properties, but it is a lot nicer than older Courtyards or Fairfield Inns, and the rate was pretty comparable. I'd go back based on the location and the lake if I had business in the area.

“Not what I expected. A letdown” Booked this as there was a conference in Chicago and nothing else was available. Paid over $200/night and really not worth it. The hotel is in a URGENT need of renovation. Its old and dated. Really will not be back. There is a restaurant linked to the lobby, not the best food but the lady there (Barbara) is really nice so she makes it worthwile.

“some good, some bad” the hotel lobby is very nice - minimalistic chic, sophisticated and trendy. there were nicely dressed people in the bar at all times, but on the 14th floor where we stayed it was quiet. after 12mn, a bouncer is at bay by the elevators checking room keys for access. (doesn't mean though that this is foolproof as one could have already checked out the hotel but still have the room key). the checkin was fast and efficient; the staff was not snobbish at all. the apples and wipes were a nice touch. there were multiple elevators, tiny but efficient. the hallways were indeed dim but still nicely decorated but showed signs of wear. we were given a room with wheelchair access, which was slightly larger than the usual room. a true disabled person needing a wheelchair will find it impossible to navigate as there is simply no room. the queen bed was just the right fimness, and the sheets were adequately clean. however, the whole room was so dimly lighted. there was a small window but the view was just a side of a building mostly. the closet was small and there was a canvas shoe holder that was supposed to replace shelves, i think? there was a small loveseat, a small work table. a small tv was resting on an equally small tv stand. everything was again simple decor but they looked worn down. there was a keyboard for internet access, costing $9.99 to access a day. the bathroom was a little bigger, again because it was wheelchair accessible. counterspace was just a small ledge by the top of the sink and toilet. the hairdryer did not have its own charging area and occupied some of this precious shelf space. there was a thin bar to keep things in place but alas, 2 of my makeup fell off into the toilet!! additional space for towels and extra toiletries was provided by a modular ikea- like coffee table in the bathroom. the floor tiles were relatively clean but the grout was very dark. in line with the w style, i guess, everything had an industrial feel. no granite, no marble/limestone anywhere! the sink was rectangular porcelain, the showerhead had adequate pressure but can only be adjusted up and down, but not side to side, showering here made me feel like i was in a gym! thankfully the bliss toiletries smelled divine. we got this hotel through priceline, and felt it was ok value for money, but if we paid retail, there are a lot better choices out there!

“Location, location, location” The location right on the riverwalk is the best. The property is a little dated and could use a general overhaul. It is typical Hyatt which isn't bad but is a bit of a cold environment that is very 60ish. I had a very ordinary room, but comfortable. Hallway sound easily filtrated into the room. There was some inconsistancy on the part of service provided by the staff. The British Pub onsite was very unfriendly and seemed very uninterested in service. I was told it was seperate from the hotel, in which case, I will not hold the hotel accountable. I have made several businesstrips to San Antonio and have found it to be rather over hyped. The riverwalk is really not a big deal and I would hardly call it a river. But, if you feel the need to be on the "river". The Hyatt is the place to stay and you should find it comfortable and well served.

“Great Downtown Hotel” Came for a seminar at the Convention Center (across the street). The hotel was great but a bit odd. They have a bellman (not typical for this chain). The lobby and business center are on the first floor, the rooms are floors 7-10, with the restaurant, bar and meeting rooms on the 10th floor. Floors 2-6 are a parking garage. Everything (shopping, drug store, some excellent Asian restaurants) are within walking distance (2-3 blocks), as well as Reading Terminal. The rooms were spacious and very clean, with new LCD-HD televisions. The restaurant was above average for HGI. My biggest complaint was that they did not use real half and half for their coffee or in the rooms. I would definitely stay here again.

“Nice Location” We stopped at this hotel on the way back from Louisiana. It is very hard to find. GPS and all maps tell you to drive on the trolley tracks to get to this hotel, which is illegal. Eventually we figured out a way around, but at 11:30p.m. after driving all day, we were frustrated. This hotel has a self-park option with in/out privileges ($10), which is nice. We stayed in the historical part of this hotel. Our room was very nice on the 5th floor. Small wet bar, living room, dressing area, bedroom and bath. It was what I expected. You can hear the trolley early in the morning. It woke me up, but I was able to fall back asleep. The location of this hotel is excellent. Right in the middle of downtown by the river. When we return to Memphis I will stay here again.

“I really wanted to love this place...” When I checked into the Park Plaza, I was blown away how beautiful the lobby was. It's an old hotel, built in the 1920's, and they've done a great job keeping try to its original architecture. But problems (though minor) started in the room. First, the safe was not working and a call to the front desk got security to my room to fix it...after an hour and a repeat phone call. The bathtub/shower is molded plastic that would bend when I took a shower. There were also other little things that kind of disappointed me...lack a total lack of available sockets to charge electronics, and one group of those sockets had no plate on it. (see photo) Then, on the first morning, a housekeeper with her colleague began cleaning the room next door at 6:30am, chatting quite loud to each other. (I'm an early riser so it didn't bother me, but I can't speak for the room on the other side.) Oh yes, when they were vacuuming, they blew a fuse/circuit breaker, which took down the AC and lights in my room. Bottom line is that the rooms need a major facelift. On the other hand, the breakfast food is very good and the staff's attitude is excellent.

“Lovely surprise” An amazing and clean hotel amidst the chaos of Chinatown. Rooms had all the mod cons and the bed was incredibly comfortable. Staff were very helpful and friendly. The location isn't bad. It's downtown, very close to SoHo and about an hour's stroll to Times Square. If the craziness of Chinatown becomes overwhelming, it's very easy to walk/subway to other parts of Manhattan. The fitness centre is limited; a treadmill, a bike; and a cross-trainer. Breakfast was a bit like school camp, but it sufficed.

“No frills and tired” Very basic hotel. Lacks character and ambiance. Restaurant and bar are flat out boring. Location is great for getting on highway to see all of San Diego. Negative is you hear that highway. Be sure and ask for room facing the hillside versus the highway as it will be quieter. The top 14th floor has vaulted ceilings that are really nice.

“Great for activities at the UW!” I stayed here for a UW Husky football game in October 2011. I arrived at the hotel at about 9 AM, and inquired I could check in. The game was at 12:30 PM, but I was able to park my car at the hotel and check in after the game. :) The clerk even offered that I have breakfast at the hotel before I went to the game, but I was too anxious to get to the tailgate. :) The hotel is about a 5-10 minute walk from the stadium parking lot as well as the UW campus. Having stayed at other Silver Cloud Inn properties in Seattle and having been impressed, I will once again say that I was impressed. The rooms are large and comfortable...flat screen TV, easy chair and ottoman, nice work desk and chair, mini-fridge, microwave, and wet bar. Free Wi-Fi, free hot breakfast, and free parking! Being close to University Village shopping center, there are numerous shops, bars, and restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. I have booked a room here for a Husky basketball at the end of December, and I hope my experience then will be as good as it was in October.

“Excellent Value” Stayed here for three nights in early December 2010. The location is perfect, very close to the subway system, Macys, and the Empire State Building. The check-in was fast, and the elevators were efficient even during the busy period. Room was very compact in the typical New York manner but was clean and functional, nice comfortable bed, adequate lighting, with a work desk, flat screen TV, and nice bathroom with adequate lighting. Beware of noise from the street late at night due to garbage pick up; rooms on the backside of the hotel would likely be quieter. My room had an incredible view of the Empire State Building, and it was worth it being on the street side, but I do wear earplugs at night when I travel to busy cities. The maid service was not up to par as the shampoo, and coffee packets, cups, and cream and sugar were not replinished satisfactorily. The breakfast buffet was excellent with several hot items and some healthy fruit and cereal options. I would definitely stay here again without question.

“Not bad, but not great.” My partner had a meeting in this hotel so that's why we chose it. It is right next to the Space Needle but not much more. There's a club right next to it but only 1 night we had some noise from it when it closed. We had a room overlooking the Space Needle so the view was nice, to get into downtown we rode the Monorail, the station is also next to the space needle. The room itself was big, the bathroom kind of small but served its purpose. The restaurant was ok ( one of the very few restaurants that has a Montecristo sandwich!) and room service was prompt. I'll pobably will not stay on it again but in downtown proper unless you are really crazy about the Space Needle, then it's in the perfect location. There's also a McDonald's next to it.

“Great Amenities, Great Price!” We stayed at this Hilton property for one night on our way out of Arizona after a wedding. We picked the location because they offer a free airport shuttle and were close by (we had a super early flight out the day after check-in). The staff were very friendly, they were able to accommodate a last minute request for a room with 2 beds, versus the 1 king bed we had booked with no issues. The price was excellent, just over $100 for the room after tax, and the concierge level floor was very good, they had great appetizers, happy hour priced drinks and free softdrinks. The room we had was very clean, and was a fine size. The bathroom was a bit small but also very clean with good amenities. It wasn't anything extraordinary however for the price I was very pleased. The restaurant on site was good, fairly quick service decent prices and good food.
