The pool area was very well kept, pool towels were well stocked and the ground are large enough that its not crowded. If a person was staying here as a tourist to see the area, I don't know if it would be the best location just for getting around, but if you had a car it would be fine! For the price and the location as well as the services, I was very impressed. I would definitely stay here again!

“All-right hotel if you want to directly at Union Square” We stayed at this hotel with a baby as an award stay. Otherwise it would not have been affordable. After I saw what the price would have been I expected a high quality 5 star hotel. It is not. Accessing it with wheelchairs or babys is difficult and you have to change elevators. Lobby is fine and up to date. The room was a bit dissapointing, but maybe only because I expected a bit luxury due to above mentioned expectations. The window didn't close properly on the 27th floor which resultet in quite chilly and not quiet nights, which was not ideal for the baby. The bath was alright, the cleanliness acceptable but not great. The whole furniture should have been maintained better or exchanged. The room itself was very dark.

“Clean, comfortable hotel” This is a good choice of budget hotel. It is located on the busy Montana Avenue which is one of the main roads in El Paso and on which there are numerous restaurants, stores, bars and other hotels. As such, it is a convenient location. The rooms are spacious and spotlessly clean, as is the bathroom. There is a television, fridge and micro-wave oven in the room. I found reception staff quite helpful. There was a photo on the reception desk showing customers that the Motel will soon be renovated in which case the rooms should be even better. The only downside is that there is no breakfast, so you leave in the morning on an empty stomach, and it is quite expensive if you take this into account. Yes there are cheaper hotels in El Paso, but some of them are filthy dumps.

“A great stay in a great location!” Upon arrival the door staff was friendly and the front desk attendant was professional and helpful. The rooms are relatively small, somewhat typical for a downtown convention hotel, but were nicely furnished with a great work desk, plenty of electrical outlets, 36" flat screen television and a very comfy bed with lots of pillows and soft linens. Despite the immense size of the hotel, the elevators were speedy and there was never much of a wait for one to arrive. I'm a bit stunned that this is only a 3.5 start hotel on Priceline. I've been in 4-star Priceline-rated hotels that are inferior. For full disclosure though, I had a remodeled room, and apparently not all room are remodeled...at least not yet. I can't imagine that any rooms are too bad of shape at a full service Marriott property though. The location in downtown is great with the Reading Terminal Market just across the street and plenty of restaurants and bars within a few blocks walk toward Walnut and Spruce Streets. My only complaint is the price of parking, which has more to do with Philadelphia than the hotel itself. Valet is advertised at $38/day with in out privileges, but I was told comes to $45.50 with tax. I opted to save the gratuity and higher fee and self park across the street, which isn't something that the hotel staff will present as an option., The garage seems safe and secure and is just across Filbert Street, which is the side of the hotel with the main door and arrival area. It's $37 for up to 24 hours with hourly rates for less than 12 hour parks. You can save $2 by having your ticket validated with a $10 purchase, which is easy to do with the purchase of a quick breakfast or lunch, or lots of other great goodies to take home.

“Great location, cool bar, but lousy overall experience” I picked the hotel because of its location and appearance from the outside. I previously stayed at the Gansevoort hotel nearby, and thought that this would be a better alternative. The lobby is cool, and checkin was quick and friendly (not as pretentious like the average W hotel). The rooms are very small, but this isn't a problem due to a clever layout, big windows, lighting, and mirrors. The design reminds me a bit of a youth hostel, however if you have enough of over designed hotels, then it's is refreshingly simple and functional. The first room (1509) had a very loud ventilation, however the second room (1701) was even worse. Since it was windy outside, somehow some flaps in the ventilation system made a loud hammering noise that prevented me from sleeping. Was too tired to change it again. I had dinner at the Standard Grill (my second visit, just ok as they barbecued the scallops without any spices or seasoning, the worst scallops in a long time, and the most expensive, too). The bar at the 18th floor is phantastic, cool design, good crowd, great view. Since I left at 6:00 am next morning I placed an order for room service breakfast at 5:00. I was informed that room service won't start until 6:00, despite being told at checkin that they have 24 hour room service. They finally agreed that they could only do an omelette with a filling different to what I ordered (god knows why), however finally delivered the omelette I had originally ordered. The coffee was on the house for the trouble caused (however without spoon to stir the sugar). Still better choice than the Gansevoort, but wouldn't return.

“Excellent hotel!” I stayed at the Bulfinch Hotel during a recent business trip to Boston, and the hotel certainly lived up to every single one of the excellent reviews it has received on Tripadvisor. The hotel rooms are spotless, there is free internet service in every room, and the staff was very helpful. I will definitely stay here again the next time I'm in Boston.

“Both good and bad at Comfort Inn” A mixed one-night stay here at the Comfort Inn. Check-in clerk was very friendly (although next day's clerk not so much). Room was pretty large, and relatively clean. Good internet service, and breakfast had quite a few offerings. The bad thing is the location. I did not choose this hotel (I was visiting on business and hotel was chosen for me). The neighborhood is sketchy. We had to drive several miles to the nearby shopping mall to find restaurants and good options. Other people with whom I was traveling had issues with cleanliness of rooms (mine was OK).

“close to everywhere” If you are a light sleeper, don't forget to ask "not facing Ellis St. " Anyway, ear plugs and eye mask were set in the room... The staffs were helpful when I asked to have my room change due to the street noise. Unfortunately, very close to the elevator sometimes annoyed me... the walls are not thick enough to cut the people talking at the midnight, seemed the next door had a party with music. Location, location, location! This property is convenient to BART, muni, F-line to fisherman's wharf, of course cable cars and for shopping. 1 king room felt a bit smaller than I thought. not so much space to open the suit case. Free wi-fi is weak (stressful...) Room was classic as other traditional hotels in SF. shower booth was clean with Loccitane bath amenities. If you stay weekend, visit Glide church on sunday either at 9a.m. or 11a.m. for Sunday celebration (famous for Gospel music) located on Ellis and Taylor St. (just 2 blocks away) Fabulous!

“Great location, good value” I've stayed here twice now; once on business last summer, and over the July 4th weekend this year with my wife and 20-month-old daughter. I chose it over the Union Square boutique hotels I usually frequent for a couple of reasons -- the location (closer to to Yerba Buena Gardens and the carousel, half-block from Market for convenience to the street cars, etc.), the size of the rooms and the potential for a decent view, and the fact that they were offering a decent holiday weekend special rate. Despite booking via hotels, we had no trouble getting a 23rd floor room. It was a bit close to the elevator, but we had no complaints about elevator or hall noise. The room, as I expected from my previous stay, was larger than those in most of the affordable Union Square hotels -- an important consideration with a toddler in tow. Our floor-to-ceiling window afforded a nice, if unspectacular, view of Yerba Buena Gardens, SBC Park, and the bay beyond. We elected to skip the crowds of the Pier 39 fireworks on the Fourth, but got to see at least five different fireworks displays from different areas around town from our window -- a pleasant surprise. The room appointments were perfectly acceptable and clean; the fabrics on the chairs showed a little wear if you looked carefully, but were clean and stylish. The in-room safe provided a convenient place for my wife to park her purse and some of the small but expensive items she purchased while there. I've never had occasion to try the onsite restaurant , Jesters-- it's pricey, and didn't seem like someplace that would deal very well with a toddler. There are plenty of other places to eat nearby, and we were there to see SF, not hole up in the hotel all day and night. In-room internet access is $14.95/day, which is the highest I've seen anywhere in the country (including several Manhattan, Boston, and Chicago hotels). In a way, that was a good thing, since I decided it wasn't worth it and had a good excuse to ignore my e-mail for the duration. Phone charges can also be exorbitant, as I discovered on my first stay there -- my cell phone battery died and I'd forgotten my charger, so I had to use the room phone for a couple of local calls and a toll-free conference call, which altogether cost me nearly $100. Didn't make that mistake this time. Since I've been to SF at least two dozen times, often for a week at a time, over the last 15 years, I know my way around and know what there is to do. Given that, and since we weren't trying to do shows and such, I only had occasion to consult the concierge once -- to find out whether the cable car schedule was different on the Fourth of July holiday. Didn't know, and was distracted and not particularly friendly; otherwise, the staff was at least cordial and in some cases friendly. If your usual accomodations are the Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, Hotel Nikko, Pan Pacific, or the like, you'll probably find the Argent a bit of a come-down. It doesn't have the character of the Prescott, or the affordability of the Andrews. But if room size and location are among your prime criteria, you should definitely give it some consideration.

“My usual spot when in Chicago” I'm a Marriott guy and this is my go to hotel when I'm in Chicago for business. Its easy to get to from O'Hare on the blue line which is great. Blue line is air conditioned, cheap, and takes about 45-50 minutes door to door, which is better than a $45 taxi in traffic with no AC! The hotel itself is nice. Solid gym, tiny indoor pool for bouncing around, but acceptable, and the rooms are clean and modern. If you are Elite member, the concierge club room is great for breakfast, etc. You are on Wacker with walking distance to all kinds of restaurants and attractions. If you are heading to the convention center, you're looking at about a $12 cab ride. All in all a great hotel with plenty of food options nearby.

“Cute hotel.......nice staff” Rooms are small, barely any phone service in my room, and view of another person room. Maybe my cell service wasn't working because I had an inside room. Bathrooms are cute, bed was comfy, room was clean, great location, nice wine selection, etc. This place doesn't blow me away, but I do like the Empire. Rooftop is always a good time. Loccatane beauty products in the bathroom are a nice touch. Walls must be made out of steel or maybe no one was staying on my floor because it was super quit which I appreciated. As a single girl traveling this place is perfect. I don't know if the Empire is good for a family trip. I'll be back to stay here during Fashion Week.

“It is the standard for Excellence!” The Burnham is an exceptional hotel experience. From the moment you see it, you know the place is unique, warm and welcoming. The location can't be beat, the rooms are spacious and well appointed; you could easily stay inside your entire trip. The Atwood Cafe gets better each time you go there. The complimentary wine hour is a very nice way to get to know other guests. The real key to the Burnham however, is the outstanding team of people working there. On this trip, I got to spend time with Emil, Darnell, Kelsey, Terrell and Vane. Each of them are extremely professional, gracious, and clearly proud to be part of Team Burnham!

“Good, clean & comfortable” Stayed here for 2 weeks. The room was very clean, though slightly worn in spots. The staff was excellent. The free breakfast was excellent, with a friendly staff. Right off the highway, so not a scenic spot, but convenient to most areas around Dallas. One thing I didn't like was in my room/suite, the TV could not be seen from the bed.

“Nice stay in Dallas” My wife and I stayed at this hotel for a conference. The conference center is about a five to ten minute walk away, so it was very convenient. The staff were always friendly whenever assistance was needed and rarely did you walk by a staff person who didn't look up and say hello. We had a suite that was very nice. It worked well because my wife and I were both participating at the conference, but had very different schedules on some days and were able to get ready to go in the morning without distubring the other one. The suite had a kitchen, including a full-sized fridge, but we didn't use it. Wireless was free in our room which we liked. There were some issues with the signal coming and going, but rarely did the signal completely disappear, it was typically a matter of re-connecting. Hotel had the standard hang-up-the-towel and it won't be washed deal, but I didn't see the same option for the bed sheets and there were no recycling bins in the room or anywhere on the floors, including the lobby. I finally just dropped off the paper and plastic bottles at the registration desk; seems kind of silly in this day and age to not provide recycling options, in the lobby, at the very least. Second floor has a bar and offered free breakfast, but I never used it, so I can't comment on its quality. Did enjoy the free cookies and milk that was offered in the late afternoon/early evenings. The only thing that I specifically remember is how the TVs were such a pain to use. The remotes didn't really work well in either the bedroom or the sitting room. Not surprisngly, the TVs started on the pay-per-view screen, but we often had a bear of a time actually getting past that screen, to watch normal cable television. The default audio level was also ear-splittingly loud. I paid a reasonable conference rate, but would never pay the normal rate noted on the sign on the door. I realize that rate is often the maximum that can be charged, but I can't imagine paying anywhere near that much.

“Nice hotel - great renovations” The hotel is still in the process of being remodeled. When I checked in, all the rooms are done however there is some furniture missing (a few end tables), artwork, etc. from the room but nothing you would need to stay there. A letter on the desk states that these items are on the way from overseas. The rooms are beautiful. New carpets, drapes, fixtures, granite top countertops in bar area and bathroom. Good neutral colors - contemporary earth tones. The cooling system is great. NO wall unit and that counts a lot for me. The air comes through vents near the ceiling. As the other reviews have suggested, there are 2 flat screen TV's that are literally across the wall from each other. one in the bedroom and one in the main part of the suite. There is a small refrig. in my room. The beds are nice - very comfortable. The bedroom is small, but not impossible to get around in. I'm a big guy, 6'4" and 300 lbs, and I didn't have a problem so that puts most others "under me" in being able to get around in a small space. Bathroom is very modern and fairly spacious. For the negatives - you pay $7.95 a night for parking. WHY? I don't get it... there is a sign at the front desk that states don't leave valuables in the car, which is something you should never do. It also says there have been break-ins "in the immediate area". If you pay for parking, and this is not a garage with a monitored gate...then what is the parking fee for if there is no security? What does the customer get for their money here? Also, you must pay $10 a night for Internet service. Come on...most places offer it for free. Its Wayport so you know you don't have trouble connecting which is a good thing since some places (many in fact) offer free Internet that a lot of the times is DOWN. I don't like the nickel and diming...but if its for a good reason such as security to park your car, I really don't mind paying for parking. Enjoy your stay here, its going to be a nice place in 3 months or so. I got a rate here for $50 a night on Priceline but that may not last for too much longer when the hotel is completely done.

“Good hotel, great internet, preferred choice for future stays” The hotel was renovating rooms while I was there. I was able to stay in an already completed room. Essentially all new furniture and fixtures. The ceiling probably had a new coat of paint, but seriously could have stood to have been replaced completed as it's a bit outdated. However, that's just a personal item. Excellent internet, no problems, strong and reliable signal. The fitness center is ok, and certainly big enough to get the job done. Excellent staff and lobby is a great meeting spot. Right in the middle of the Mall, so there are many restaurants and shopping choices very close. The available mini-fridge was excellent to go to the c-stores on the mall and stock up on beverages and snacks for the late night indulgence. Good choice if you are doing business near the Mall.

“Suite hotel in El Paso” We paid a $99 internet rate on the hotel chain's web site to stay one Friday night in a suite that had a queen bed and a pullout sofa separated by a waist-high barrier, but basically in the same room. Each area had its own TV, though you could hear each other's TV. It was nicely appointed, clean and had a well-equipped kitchen that might make this appealing to folks who like to eat in. There's an outdoor pool and a hot tub that we didn't see until the next morning when we were checking out; we didn't see anything in the room's literature that mentioned this, but maybe we missed it. Breakfast was included, and it was pretty much a minimal continental type in an attractive room that was part of the lobby. There was one public computer available, and it was so heavily used in the morning that we never could get on it. The units are clustered in several separate buildings, so if you wanted a soda from the vending machine you needed to walk outside and over to the office to get one (unlike a regular hotel where you'd just walk down the hall). The staff was efficient and quickly brought us extra pillows when we asked for them. A bonus: nice big cookies for everybody when you check in. Good location for the airport.

“Fantastic hotel in the heart of Chicago” First time visit to the Ritz Carlton Chicago, travel with wife and 3 kids. We had 2 deluxe adjoing rooms, very confortable beds (Four Seasons Bed), good size rooms, ample bathroom with premium amenities. Service at the highest standard - Four Seasons - always with a smile and ready to help. The lobby area has a beautiful water fountain that provides serenity and peace while having breakfast nearby or enjoying a drink in the bar, also next to the fountain. The hotel is on top of a mall with 100+ stores, with a few restaurants and deli's in the base floor. Everything is close to the hotel, restaurants, BestBuy, American Girl store. Its like being in 5th Ave N.Y., without the noise and hasle of N.Y., very quiet city with nice and respectful people. We enjoyed the Ritz Carlton and would recommend to friends and family.

“Great Value” This hotel has a great location when visiting Chicago as it is close to Navy Pier, Mag Mile, and doable walks to the Loop and River North. The price of the hotel includes a reception in the evening that includes light snacks and alcholic drinks. In addition, a full cook to order breakfast with many extras is also included. I would suggest that you buy the package that includes valet parking. It adds about $30 which is a fair price for Chicago. Prices at other hotels can run $5 to $15 more each night. Public parking is also almost as much, and for about $5 more, I would choose the hotel parking The room is a suite with two rooms and includes a microwave and refrigerator. A large grocery store is located right across the street. The workout room has everything needed for a good workout, and the pool area is nice and includes a hot tub. This is a good and economical choice when visiting Chicago.

“You Won't Find Better” This is a real sleeper. Everything is great. The employees can't do enough for you. Great location. You name it. You can't go wrong here. I noticed a remark about some small bathrooms. True, but it won't spoil your trip. It is really a sensational hotel. I've stayed in many. This is a keeper.

“Skanky and miserable.” We arrived in town last minute and didn't have time to waste searching for a room so checked in. Location was okay, just a five minute walk to the main attractions. Receptionist grumpy, just didn't wan to be there. Room was grim and we had to request that they remake the beds with clean linen as they appeared to be the same ones that previous guests had used. Luckily we had a few drinks out that night so managed to sleep okay on the below par / ancient beds. Had no intention of trying out the breakfast so can't comment on that. Try somewhere else!! Travelodge - the prison cell rooms in this dump seriously lets your brand down.

“Not Starwood Friendly” I didn't have such a great visit here. Prior to arrival I feared that this would be a typical "popcorn on the ceiling" type of place. Rather than rely on my platinum status I bumped up our room to an executive level. The room was old and the club room wasn't even open. Judging from the other reviews, some floors or wings must be better than others. Unfortunately my experience didn't live up to my expectations.

“Here for a convention” Nice hotel, well located. The catered food we had as part of the convention was sub-par. Hard boiled eggs for a continental breakfast? Rooms clean, average size, Great view. There is an adult pool near the spa. My wife loved being able to enjoy that Marco Polo free zone. Had one lunch at Sally's and ordered the Baja Cobb salad. Nothing Baja or Cobb about it, but it was delicious. We understand the rooms will be fully renovated this year. The gym was well equipped but given the size of this massive hotel, too small.

“Disappointed” We chose this hotel because the last time our convention was in Philadephia this hotel was so incredible - staff and facilities. This stay was the polar opposite. We were at the hotel for a week and had some good experiences and mostly adequate to bad experiences. On Saturday I was gone all day to a meeting but my roommate stayed away from the room so the maid could clean the room. She might as well stayed in the room and done her work. When I arrived back in the room at 3p the room had not been cleaned. Not knowing the maid's cart was on the floor most of the day I went down to the business center to check email. Getting back up to the room at 4p my roommate called down to the desk to find out when they were going to clean the room and was told that the maids were leaving for the day but that they would get one to clean our room. At 5p I called to find out whether they were going to clean the room since I had a 6:30p dinner. The maid finally showed up at 5:15p but did a lousy job including wiping glasses with a dirty rag. The front desk called at 6p to find out whether our room had been cleaned. They apologized by saying that the hotel had been full. The hotel was full but not with unexpected guests; they knew they were going to be full but did not have adequate staffing. I could have put this off to poor planning if this had been the only bad experience. The front desk staff were rude to my roommate when she checked in and were unhelpful several times when I asked a question. On our last night we asked a bellhop to pick up boxes for shipping. After 2 hours and calling several times to find out how long till someone would be up, we wanted to go to bed. My roommate went down and got a cart and we took them down ourself. The bellhop told us that they were never told of our request; he said if he had that he would have been right up.

“Fine Place to Stay” My husband and I spent 5 nights here in September. It was a great stay. The hotel is located in the Loop, within easy walking distance of Millennium Park, the Art Institute, the El, shopping, restaurants, etc. The hotel is very comfortable, and exceeds the usual high standards of Hampton Inns. The room was large and comfortable (although it did lack a mirror with decent lighting to apply makeup), the staff was amazingly responsive and cheerful. Breakfast was very good and there were computers in the lobby which you could use for free. We found this to be an excellent place to stay to explore the fabulous city of Chicago.

“Very average downtown LA hotel.” This hotel was, in my opinion, very average. Room service arrived cold (though the staff was very friendly). The hotel’s restaurants kept odd hours, so we would have to step out for lunch (it simply wasn’t served). There was an odd “Being John Malkovich” type small cutout door in the bathroom ... not exactly sure what it was for?? The hotel layout is a bit annoying: you have to go up a level to catch the elevators, but you can take the elevators down to the ground level (not having the ability to do both is annoying – if security is an issue, perhaps other measures should be taken as well). Cabs were abundant, and I believe there was mass transit nearby. I was in town for a convention at the LACC, which was within walking distance (so the Staples Center is just as close). There are plenty of decent bars and restaurants in the area, so you won’t feel like you’re missing out at the hotel. Regarding the view ... it’s downtown, so there isn’t one. All in all, just an average hotel - nothing spectacular
“Nice” Quick stay, less than 10 hours. Friendly front desk.Free parking, HUGE bottle of water, good room, great value.Rooms near interstate noisy

“Very stylish” My husband and I spent two night at the London having seen a review in a UK magazine. We were not disappointed, We loved the space with a proper door between the bedroom and sitting room. The bed was very comfortable and the shower room was very chic with mosaic marble tiles on the floor. (I'm not sure it's such a good idea to eliminate baths completely but we did enjoy the double shower). Unlike many hotels, the WIFI worked and was not charged as an extra. The bar had a good ambience for a pre dinner drink and the Ramsay restaurant was surprisingly OK given the hype. The only thing my trendy New Yorker friend did not like was the colour of the sofa- I could live with it for two days and will definitely consider returning to this excellently located hotel.

“Good hotel, great location” We stayed for 2 nights at the end of a trip round the North East. The hotel is well located within walking distance of Penn Station. Staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was small but well appointed and clean. Bathroom has a Good shower. Great choice of breakfast in the lobby with plenty space to sit and eat. There is also a little outside area with 2 small tables. Complementary coffee is available in the room and in the lobby all day and also cookies in the evening (of course all this is reflected in the room rate which is higher than similar hotels who do not offer 'complementary' breakfast). Overall a good hotel and would recommend it.

“Still A Classy Hotel” We had not stayed at the Fairmont for about 10 years and were pleasantly surprised at how nice it still is. The lobby is elegant, not old, and the service was impeccable. Everybody, from the maids on up were smiling and said hello. We wanted a hot fudge sundae (which apparently is not on the menu) and the restaurant manager (Max, we made sure to note his name) want back and asked the chef to do it special. Talk about going the extra mile! The room was nothing special but it was very clean and quiet. The towels were better then most but still not plush, and, surprisingly, there was no bathrobe. These are not complaints, just observations for comparison to other 5 star hotels. Clearly what separates this from the other was the level of genuine caring of the staff. While staying here can be a bit pricy, if you can score an internet special it would be difficult to do better.

“A treat for the kids” Overall we enjoyed our stay here. The pools made the whole trip worth it, since it was 115 degrees and we had no desire to leave the hotel area. The rooms (in the casitas) were large but the furnishings a little drab and we did find a couple of roaches in the kitchen. A few items would have helped -- like a toaster and maybe a kitchen trash can that could hold more than a cereal box. It would have been nice if the pools had been open a little later than 8 on such hot nights though, and the little pools around the casitas were mobbed, and hot and felt oily. It was nice to have laundry facilities right near the rooms, and the shops were convenient for buying small items. The fitness center was well equipped but the employees were so snooty toward the paying hotel guests that they made us feel very unwelcome. Apparently it is a fitness club for local residents too. We're not terribly fussy, but I think that the rooms could be updated and a little cleaner. The pools also showed signs of wear (chipping tiles) all around the shallow end. On one hot afternoon the whole pool had to be closed (for the night)because a child had gone to the bathroom, so that was a huge disappointment. But generally, our 4 kids had a great time--ages 10-17-- and it was relaxing to sit around the pool and see them easily entertained through most of the 3 days we were there.

“New room renovation is GRRReat!” My wife and I needed a night in city this past weekend and the Sir Francis Drake was a perfect getaway. Located 1/2 block from Union Square the SFD is in the middle of SF's best restaurant and shopping. Check-in was a breeze and within 5 minutes we were in the room. With limited availability the only room remaining was a deluxe queen, which normally could dissappoint, but with new bedding, plasma TV and a view of Union Square it was tough to keep the smile off our faces. The bed was excellent, room was clean and offered plenty of space. I'd recommend any travelers looking to stay in the heart of the action to stay here. We will be back. Tip: Starlight Room is a great bar at the hotel but could be loud if you are staying on 20th floor. If staying on a weekend be sure to finish out the night dancing at the Starlight room or request a room on a lower floor if going to bed early.

“Excellent hotel with flair and location!” What a delightful surprise this newly renovated Chicago hotel was. We chose it for it's next door location to the Palace Theater, and got style, class and great service! This "pet friendly" hotel is immaculate! From the rooms, which we saw got deep cleaning (after every guest stay) to the public lobbies (yes there are no less than 4 really chic lobby areas) to the public toilets. Clean, clean clean! The beds were very comfortable, and the rooms very spacious. They have a Kimpton Frequest stay club, and I suggest you sign up before you book. It gets you some special ammenities like upgrades and chcolates. There is even a complimentary wine reception in the lobby each evening, and FREE wireless internet in every room, or free use of the computers next to the check in desk. The only one problem we had was that our check out bill showed a $10.50 room service charge, which was very quickly adjusted once we brought it to the front desk that we had not ordered room service. Kimpton has done a beautiful job of renovation this old building. We will certainly go back.

“The problem is, it's just good” It's not great and for $300+ per night for a regular room, you can and should expect more. At the end of it I probably spend $500 per night after all the add on's like parking, any food you eat, taxes etc. The people are pretty nice, Ryan at check in is great. The location is good, easy walk to work. Century City has some good food at the mall and BH is right down the road. For the same price, I stay at the Beverly Hilton, unless there are no rooms available. Like the title said, it's not bad, just not a very good value for a business traveler.

“Stay on a non-convention weekend for a great deal” Don't make any mistake, this hotel was built to serve the Convention Center next door. But, as we've found with most luxury hotels in large cities that cater to business traffic, you can get a great deal on a wonderful room when the business traffic is scarce. We stayed a Fri-Sun night over Easter weekend (family of four) and were very pleased with the value. We booked our room at the Hilton web site and it was cheaper than the usual travel web sites (Travelocity, etc.). (I can't comment on Priceline because I don't use them - I'm funny about wanting to know EXACTLY which hotel I'm getting.) The hotel is immaculately clean, as it has only been open since Dec. 3, 2008 (we asked). I had to ask Housekeeping for two items and they were both waiting in my room when I returned. The staff was very friendly and helpful. To address some points in other reviews, yes, it is really annoying that there is no gift shop open yet and no other "quick mart" in walking distance. My husband had to pay $5 for two AA batteries at the front desk. Ridiculous. Self-parking is $21 a day, which in my experience is very reasonable for a downtown spot in a major city. We paid $40-$50 in NY and over $30 in San Francisco. Yes, you do have to walk outside to get to the parking garage...about 100 feet, on a ramp that goes directly from the front door of the hotel into the 3rd floor of the garage. Not a big deal, IMO. If it really bothers you, you can valet your car for $10 more per day that the self parking. My husband and son walked to Petco Park from the hotel and didn't think it was far, at all. You could actually see into the stands of Petco Park from our room. We did pay a bit extra to have our view upgraded, an offer that is made at the time of booking (sort of a standby arrangement - you agree you'll pay the extra when you check in if the upgraded room is available). One thing about the view that is misleading...this hotel *is* on the bayfront. There is a wonderful photo of the pool on the hotel web site, which is lovely. HOWEVER, the photo is misleading in that the pool DOES sit on the bay, however about half the pool also faces the pier where Dole bananas are unloaded. While we were there, there was a freighter tied up and you know what freighters look like. However, I have to say that the hotel (or someone) has obviously tried to make the best of this situation by putting up a kiosk on the boardwalk that tells all about the Dole pier, the capacity of the ships, their voyage, etc. So, your kids just might find this interesting. I did, but I couldn't see the freighter from my hotel window, so maybe that made a difference. :) The Gaslamp district is technically in walking distance, but if you want to venture past the first few blocks, I'd suggest taking your car. The restaurants we ate at were not within walking distance. Downtown garage parking was ridiculous...$2 per 15 minutes...and street parking was hard to come by, especially if there's a ball game. One night (no game) we found a space, on the other, we should have used the valet at the restaurant. At $15 it was cheaper than what we paid at the garage. We did have the breakfast buffet at the restaurant one morning and it was wonderful, BUT we didn't pay for it. My husband had trouble with the tickets he got from the concierge, so they comped our whole family with breakfast. I don't know if I would have paid $25 per person, but the food included an omlette station, smoked salmon, homemade pastries, and some other unusual items along with the breakfast regulars. What it's like when full, I can't say, but all in all, we really enjoyed our stay and would definitely stay here again.

“Meh . . .” The Hyatt is an enormous convention hotel a block from the heart of downtown Chicago (Wacker and Michigan). Neither impressing nor offending, it was somewhere between Something and Nothing . . . $200+ per night of impersonal white-noise specially designed for the hollowed-out corporate drone or hapless conference attendee (like me). Check-in offers self-serve kiosks (similar to airport check-in). The room was equipped with the typical stuff, plus a coffee machine good for one cup of bad swill per day, iPod dock (good!), ironing board/iron, and safe. The bathroom had toothpaste, which was unusual. The bed was comfortable and climate control was great. Some kvetching . . . Housekeeping was inconsistent. I could have made a wig out of the hair left in the tub by the previous occupants. My guest room was clean everywhere but the corners and edges, which were grungy and dusty. The bath mat was taken and not replaced. Shampoo was not replenished (fortunately I had some of my own). If there were any drinking glasses, I didn’t see them. The water pressure in the shower was pitiful. Still more kvetching . . . Despite the in-room coffee/condiments being packaging-waste overkill, Hyatt declares its dedication to the environment by changing towels and linens only on request, which we all know really means “reduce services to maximize profit but tell the gullible customers it’s for the good of all creatures great and small.” The whole industry does this but Hyatt is the first I have seen where they refresh nothing unless you call the operator and make special arrangements. Maybe it’s just me, but I really don’t want to hunt someone down for a fresh towel. Now let’s do some math! Absurd minibar prices are always amusing. In the case of the Hyatt, a 12 oz. can of Pepsi is a mere $4.25 . . . but wait there’s more! An 18% service charge ($.77), 11.5% sales tax ($.49), and – my favorite – a 3% “carbonated beverage tax” ($.13) brings the grand total to $5.64, or $.47 cents per ounce. Oh yeah, and remember, if you pick it up to look at it, you bought it. I woulda splurged on the Pepsi, but I spent all my money on the $52 per night parking fee and $9.95 per night internet fee. (That was for slow speed; medium speed was $14.95 and fast was $39.95.) By all means, have an expensive un-experience at the Hyatt. Hope this helps. .

“Fall Break In the NYC!” This hotel is in an excellent location. I felt fine letting my teens walk in Times Square alone. They enjoyed the shops and numerous eating locations. McDonald's is right next to the hotel which was great for a quick breakfast before heading down the street to Good Morning America! The bellman were awesome! The front desk staff were great. They gave my children cookies everyday. Our cleaning service wasn't that good over the weekend. We were also stopped every time we left the hotel by a Hilton rep selling timeshares. Other than that we had no problem with this hotel.

“Convenient for downtown, but evening is boring” This hotel is a remodelled old business building. It is shared with the Marriott Residence Inn. They did a great job in remodeling, and this is one of the best Marriott Courtyard I have stayed in. The room is pretty good size, although the view of my room window is only into a very small concrete courtyard. Good items: (1) Tall ceiling in rooms, nice! (2) Very convenieny if you need a place to stay for business meetings downtown. Mine is only 5 minutes walk away. (3) Front desk is outstanding, and they provided service with a smile. (4) The restaurant food was outstandingly good for a hotel. Compliment to the chef. (5) I got free internet from my room (using my own laptop). (6) During daytime, there is Macy's across the street, and a lot of shops and restaurants in the downtown tunnel right there. (7) Hotel provides free shuttle to the downtown area during day time. (8) There is a light-rail service within a block to travel to other parts of town. (9) The outdoor pool and gym were adequate. Bad items: (1) The neighborhood is totally dead in the evenings. Many restaurants are closed at 3 p.m., even McDonald's was closed by 7 p.m. The tunnel is closed around 6 p.m. No bar, besides the hotel bar, anywhere is sight. Good news is that a "mall" is being built across the street. Maybe the situation will improve by later this year. (2) Hotels charges for parking. (3) One of the waitress in the hotel restaurant is super-forgetful. Everytime I ordered something, even as simple as a cup of tea, she has to come back two times asking before getting it right! I am glad she is the only one forgetful, the other waitress did an adequate job. Not super, just adequate. (4) There are homeless people in the neighborhood in the evenings. I will come back for downtown meetings because it is convenient for me. However, if I need to be in town for more than four days, I will need to rent a car sometimes so I can drive to other places, just to keep my sanity. Scoped up in the hotel room every night can get old very fast.

“Very nice, but not worth rack rate” We got our deal for $170 via TravelZoo. Morgan's is nice enough but dissappointing upon arrival. Curiously there is no signage anywhere to indicate that this place is a hotel. The lobby is very small with just one person behind a very small kiosk. The bellman was busy when we arrived, so we nearly missed the place. But once we got our bearings the bell staff and the front desk people are exceptionally nice. The front desk staff also serves as the concierge so you really can have a long wait as various guests are sorted out in various languages with seemingly complex negotiations. There is no furniture in the lobby, but if you want to hang out there is a living room on the fourth floor with a TV and coffee and tea fixings. The room is small and minimistic. Very comfy beds. Quiet. Nice black out curtains and sheers for filtered sunlight. Our room on the 16th floor was quite pleasant and sunny - it was small but we were told it was a free upgrade. Upscale bath appointments. Ask the bellman how to turn on the various lights as they are quite hidden. Our bedroom clock was off by an hour, thank goodness we did not rely on it. Very upscale mini-bar. Beware the midnight munchies, it will really hurt your wallet!!I know this from dire experience. There is no price list or indication that the mini=bar food/drinks are not complimentary, so make sure that all guests understand not to have their way with the contents.

“Welcome to the South's Grand Hotel” "Welcome to the South's Grand Hotel" is the line delivered by the Peabody Duckmaster before the start of the daily walking of the Peabody Ducks to spend their day in the lobby fountain. This is truly a Five Star Hotel. It is simply the nicest hotel at which I have ever stayed and would recommend it to anyone. The rooms are beautiful, bed and linens perfect. The lobby is a beautiful, grand old hotel. The service is absolutely incredible. Rooms are relatively expensive (about $300 when taxes and parking in the adjacent garage are factored in) but you still are receiving value for your money. The hotel is the heart of downtown Memphis and the Redbirds AAA baseball team is across the street. Beale Street is a two block walk. The Rendevous BBQ joint is also across the street. The Ducks arrive daily at 11:00am and return to their rooftop habitat at 5:00pm after spending the day in the fountain of the lobby bar. A couple hundred spectators show up to see the ceremonial duck walks and you'll need to get there at least 30 minutes ahead to get a good spot. Don't miss the Peabody.

“Location excellent, just what we needed in NYC” I took my wife who had never been to New York City before to visit the city for Memorial Day Weekend. We had a jam-packed weekend planned and hadn't planned to spend a lot of time in a hotel room, yet we didn't want to stay somewhere that wasn't centrally located nor somewhere particularly grimy. We obtained a great rate of less than $120 per night on Hotwire.com (it was rated as a 3 1/2 star boutique hotel in mid-town west, if i remember correctly). Turned out to be a great choice. Our flight arrived at LaGuardia early and we were at the hotel just after noon. They were kind enough to allow us to check-in early, which allowed us to drop off our bags in the room and head out and start exploring. The hotel is right across the street from Rockefeller Center and within walking distance of two subway stops, making it fairly easy to access nearly ever portion of the boroughs with a max of one change on the subway. If you're in NYC for a few days, I reccommend getting a subway pass so you don't have to worry about how much/how often you use it. The hotel offered a couple of nice amenities - the fitness center I only used once but it was adequate and very clean. They offered a discount at the hotel restaurant at the Club Quarters next door and they had a nice buffet breakfast on Sunday, and my wife appreciated the purified bottled water. The rooms obviously were small as is typical in Manhattan but the beds were very comfy and the shower was nice as well. The cleanliness was the thing I appreciated the most about The Jewel. They also let us check out late at 3 PM on our last day as we had a 6:00 flight. That cost us $35 plus tax, but we figured it was worth the price. We'd definately be open to staying there again if in NYC.

“Great Stop-Over Hotel” My wife and I stayed here a couple of nights before leaving for Singapore in early April '08. It is situated just shy of being in a flight-path for LAX. The surrounding area is pretty much a rental-car wasteland. Nothing of significance is within close, walking distance. The only two dining options within walking distance are the hotel's offerings or a Burger King directly across the street. We ate dinner at one of the small number of tables included in the "bar". Drinks were a bit on the pricey side for us (what's up with wine prices these days??), and the food itself a bit less so, but the staff were very friendly, and the food was pretty tasty and creatively presented. In spite of our proximity to a flight path, our room was surprisingly quiet. It was also small, but clean, modern and comfortable. I can't remember offhand how much we paid, but I booked it through Hotwire and remember thinking that it was a very good deal for the money. I would give it a definite thumbs-up for a stop-over hotel.

“Good hotel in a good location, but possibly a bit overpriced” I spent two nights at One Washington Circle. The location was very good, within walking distance of Georgetown and downtown (20 min). My room was quite spacious, and adequately furnished. Staff was fine, but not particularly friendly and the breakfast was fine. For what it offers, the hotel is a bit overpriced, but not outrageously so.

“Very nice. Would stay again.” Great location. Had a room on upper floor in old tower, which was quite nice. Room was large and quite comfortable. Work was being done on elevators in new tower and some colleagues waited 20+ minutes for elevator. Meeting rooms were OK - but either too hot or too cold. Staff very helpful - except for gym. Would have appreciated being told about the weekly rate. Check out line quite long until I called the hotel from the line and suggested they staff up - presto! Drinks in lobby bar expensive. Lunch in Oak Room enjoyable. Business center OUTRAGEOUSLY expensive - $64 to print about 20 pages.

“Comfortable and luxurious hotel.” Having had to check out of a previous hotel early, we walked into this one and felt instantly happier and pleased that we were going to be staying here. The lobby is plush and comfortable. Check in desk is hidden away to the left. The desk staff were very friendly (and remained so throughout our 8 night stay) and we were in our room after a few minutes. The rooms are not big but they more than make up for it terms of comfort and ambience. The furnishings were pleasant and comfortable. The bed and pillows were comfortable although ours squeaked a little bit, but not enough to cause us any problems. I am sure if we'd wanted to do something about it, it would have been no problem. On the 11th floor we had a very nice view of the pool area and the hotel grounds. The ability to open a big window was also a very nice feature. The tv is an old style set but it's no big shakes to me. The bathroom was small but immaculate throughtout our stay. The shower was fine, which was a blessing after our previous hotel. The products were generally good too, although I found the soap dried my skin too much so had to stop using it. The only complaint in this area was that the towels were a little scratchy and could use replacing. The hotel has a small coffee bar that is open til 11am which serves tea, coffee and pastries. This is a blessing since the buffet breakfast is a little on the expensive side. I also used the outdoor heated swimming pool a couple of times. Although I am sure there was somewhere to change, I couldn't find it so used the mens room. It's a nice facility to have and that it's heated makes a difference especially in december when I was there. Parking is also a little expensive and this is certainly a deterrent from using it at $16 a day. As is the distance from the car park to the hotel itself, vast areas are sectioned off for valet parking which means self parking is relegated to the distant spots. We gave up on it the first day we were there and parked on the street for free and usually closer to the hotel entrances. For a decent breakfast outside the hotel I recomend Le Peep, it's a few minutes drive to Towne Centre Drive, located in the shopping plaza. It's not the big Westfield UTC mall, but a smaller plaza a couple of hundred yards further along the road. Be aware it shuts at 2pm. Nearby shopping at UTC is excellent, one of the best malls in San Diego IMO. There's also a smaller mall and AMC movie theatre across the I5 freeway, visible from the hotel, you can use Nobel Rd to get there easily. Overall, this is my second favourite hotel in San Diego, (after the Omni), it's convienient for most of the city, it's comfortable and the staff are excellent. We didn't leave our room until 4pm one day and upon our return our room was still made up even though we weren't expecting it. In my mind, this going the extra mile makes a difference and I would be happy to stay here again.

“perfectly imperfect” A comfortable room, great bed, friendly people, wonderful location, fully equipped gym. A cookie-cutter experience -- but then, I wasn't looking for anything more. Perfectly unmemorable, but in a good way. Two things: They charge for wifi. Incredible in this day and age. There are free computers in the lobby, though. (Be warned that these will be occupied by children whose parents want technology to babysit their young children -- no parents around. The hotel should restrict access to 18 and over.) Second, you cannot control your A/C. Pleasant staff, though the front desk appeared to be understaffed.

“Great Service, Location” This was our first time at the InterContinental having stayed at several other downtown Chicago hotels. We booked through Hotwire and got a fantastic rate of $100 per night. Upon arrival, we upgraded to a "suite" for $50 more per night. So, at a price still far less than what we would have paid for a small hotel room with two beds, we got a room with a living area with pull-out couch, king bed in a separate bedroom, and a view of the lake (albeit partial). Not to mention the fact that you walk out right onto Michigan Avenue - we'd do it again in a heartbeart. Upon arrival, valets were gracious and attentive with baggage. The front desk met our requests without skipping a beat. (The lobby was beautiful at Christmastime with a huge decorated tree.) We didn't use the lounge or the restaurant - too busy sightseeing and shopping - but our room was nice to come back to at night or for a rest during the day. Housekeeping exceeded our request for extra coffee in the room, and even had nice music and dim lighting waiting for us when we returned. I did notice that the armoir in the living area was beaten up a bit around the bottom, and that the sofa had at one point seen better days, but despite the nitpicking thought it was a great hotel room. And for 150 bucks a night in downtown Chicago, who could complain?

“Good experience, would stay again” Stayed in a king city view suite for two nights during a business trip. Check-in went quickly and staff were professional. I stayed on a higher level, so I didn't notice the noise from the atrium as others have mentioned. Furnishings were dated, but in good condition. Bed was very comfortable, and complimentary breakfast was great.

“A room with a view” I love pleasant surprises and the Savoy Suites was full of them. First: a city hotel with a country view? I had a lovely oversized well-appointed room with a view of the woods, a lovely church steeple and off in the distance the US Naval Observatory. Room: #308. Second: Free parking. Yes free secured garage parking in the city. Third: the outdoor deck was great, a lovely setting in the middle of the city. Fourth: the neighborhood of Glover Park was spectacular: safe, clean and walking distance to several bars and restaurants, a Starbucks, CVS and a Whole Foods Market. Fifth: excellent staff always ready to assist and greet you. I would have no hesitation of staying here again and love when I feel that I have stumbled on a "find."

“Sadly disappointing! No AC, bad smelling, malfunctioning light” I was really looking forward to this one night stay, which was a layover for my daughter and I for a one night on our way back from 2 weeks in Europe. The photos and website showed a hotel I would like. Unfortunately for us it was not so great. When we checked in around midnight, we were given a king room which majorly reeked of cigarette smoke (the whole 2nd floor did). So I went down and asked for a non-smoking room. The nonchalant English desk clerk said he may have one other room available and then brought us the key to a 5th floor double room, which was fine with us. Upon our entry we thought the room was a bit muggy and the thermostat, which was set at 72 read 76 room temp. But we stayed thinking this was better than the smoky room and reset the thermo to 65 hoping it would get cooler overnight - and we were really tired by this time (plus apparently we had the last available room). In the night the hall light would come on and go off arbitrarily (this was something I had read as a complaint on other reviews on booking.com and was surprised that it was still a problem). And worse, the temp continued to rise in the room. It was hot, damp (it had recently rained) and had no air movement at all. It was impossible to sleep and the room smelled so musty and gross. By morning it was 78 degrees. I went to the desk at 6am to tell them and the desk clerk only offered me a late check out and to send an engineer (why do we want an engineer when we are checking out?). While I loved the decor of the hotel and the soft beds, these problems and the lack of any offering of reduction for the price we paid for the room was too much to be able to give this hotel anything better than a bad rating. The hotel sent me a survey which I completed referencing this problem and also asked for a response, and I separately sent the hotel corporate office an email. I have not had a communication from either. I think if my AC had been operational my review would have been really good, but that was not the case. I would have been better off at the airport Holiday Inn Express...

“Frustrating Experience” The hotel was ok for the money. Definitely less than I'm used to, but I'm also not comparing it to the Four Seasons. Upon arriving to NY around 4pm, I had my assistant call the hotel to confirm that my room would still be available if I didn't check in until after 6pm that night. They confirmed that it was available as expected. When I arrived at the hotel - about 7pm - they announced they had "upgraded" me to a double room. I had booked a king. I explained to the front desk person that in no place on earth was two double beds an upgrade from a king, but he said they were already sold out of the king rooms and that they could move me the next day. I agreed to this, but let him know I was dissatisfied. The room was ok, but it had more than a few things that I either didn't like or was ambivalent about. The Pros: Good sized room - especially for NY Comfortable bed (although the double was small) Clean linens - sheets with a minimum of stains, towels fluffy Nice size desk area - although I didn't use it, I always book a king bed so I can spread out on it - obviously not possible on a double bed Relatively clean room, although I found some hair and dust on the floor when I dropped a pantyliner sticky-side down - yuck. Shower pressure was good The Cons: Gray grout in bathroom makes the whole thing look dirty Only one trashcan in the whole room - in the bathroom Remote control wasn't strong enough to reach the TV in the double room (although this was better in the king room) Weird bathroom layout (in the double room, I had to close the door to use the sink) Ugly light fixture in the center of the room. Really ugly - they could have spent 5 dollars more and made it better Inadequate lighting - I had to rearrange the lamps to get enough light to even read Toiletries in the bathroom were obviously not fresh - yuck. Lousy TV selection - no TBS, Food Network, Discovery channel, TLC...? No washcloths - is this a European thing? This has happened to me several times lately... Hallways look like what you'd find in a hostel My opinion of the hotel might be different if they had offered anything for my inconvenience of switching rooms... but all they did was switch me. I think they should have refunded my first room night, or at the very least offered me a discount on a future stay. But nothing. I never heard from them again, not even to check in and see how the new room was working out. Sigh. I probably won't stay there again - another NY hotel on my "Don't stay there" list.

“So-So Hotel” W’s renovation of the Washington Hotel, and its great rooftop terrace, is a mixed bag. It’s not that they do a bad job, but it’s not for everyone. If you’re visiting with kids, you won’t want to do more than pop up and look at the view for five minutes (which is worth doing). But if you want to have a drink or two in a unique setting, you could do worse. We only saw the public spaces, not the rooms or the spa. The lobby they call a Living Room, so there’s a large TV showing a fire in a fireplace near the side entrance. I know the designer thought it was clever, but it comes across as cheesy and out of place. Lots of marble on the floors and lots of shiny things dangling from the 40-foot ceilings—like they can’t decide if they want to be old world classy or bordello tacky. Then it all veers toward Eurotrash with the blaring synth-pop that makes conversation all but impossible. They seem to want people to lounge around with headphones and their laptops, since that’s what most other people I saw were doing. They were beaming the word “Welcome” onto the wall in light; like the Bat signal, but dopier. We went to check out the rooftop bar, which was the only reason to visit the old hotel. Elevators are staffed, and tiny, so there can be a wait while they shuttle people up and down four at a time. Once on the roof, you have two choices—the lounge or the terrace. The lounge is new, very dark, sleek and cool. Great view of the Washington Monument out one wall of windows. You can sit at the bar without a reservation, but if you want a table, need to book in advance. If you have five people or fewer you can reserve on Open Table, more than that give them a call. The terrace is pretty much the same as it was under the old management, and still has the same great views—and the views are still the only reason to go. The small tables also have to be reserved, and they’ll expect you to order food as well. Otherwise you can stand around the bar or wander (in winter you will probably want to huddle around the space heaters, as the plastic they’ve set up doesn’t do a lot to ward off the chill). The walls are plain white painted brick, the floor is concrete tile, there is Astroturf (!) on the side of the bar. Clearly this is not where they put their money. If you don’t have a reservation, your best bet is to get your drink and then walk between the view of the White House and the other end of the room to see the monuments. If you do get a table or couch, they’ll give you a blanket, which is a nice touch in winter. In summer the ceiling fans probably keep it comfortable; but if it’s raining they will drop the plastic walls and it would get unbearably stuffy really fast. Even without a reservation it looks like you can sit at the tables, but they may make you leave if someone with a reservation shows up—probably safer on a Tuesday than on a Friday. Drinks are expensive versus comparable places downtown—$14 for a glass of pinot noir—and the cocktails are standard fare, with stingy pours on the alcohol. We looked at the menu and it’s clearly trying to be fancier than the calamari rings and poppers they used to offer, but nothing tempted us to order. Valet parking (on the F St. side entrance) is $20, which is normal for hotels in the area, but very high for restaurants. If you’re just stopping for a couple of hours, you can do better at the garage next door or by going a block further up and using the valet at Old Ebbitt Grill (for $8). So, bottom line: They spent a lot on the renovation and gave the designer too free a hand to do whatever he wanted—some ideas work better than others, but taken together it’s not quite right and shamelessly pretentious. It’s a W, so they have a lot of solid ideas about providing great service. It’s D.C., so the staff doesn’t quite deliver that service. They’ve made a conscious decision to go after a young and hip crowd (or people who want to think of themselves as one or the other); so if that’s not you, you’ll be more comfortable elsewhere.

“Excellent hotel in La Jolla” Stayed at the Hyatt Regency La Jolla for a business trip to UCSD. Arrived the hotel with car, and used the valet parking. The people working in the checkin was very friendly. I had a room in the Regency Club floor, and both the room and bathroom was clean. for breakfast I used the Regency Club in the hotel, which has a continental breakfast. The hotel also has a swimming pool and a fitness center in the back. Overall, the hotel is very good, and I will return here next time I am in the San Diego area.

“Great location, but be careful which room to choose!” This hotel is part of the Personality Hotels group and I stayed at other hotels before, always having been very satisfied. This time I was a bit disappointed, as the room was tiny without window and got very hot, as there was no aircon, either. I was expecting a small room, as it was explained on the hotel's website, but not that small, as the price was actually not that cheap in comparison to standard sized rooms in other hotels in the Union Square area. Apart from that, the location is excellent just 200m away from the Powell St cable car stop and around the corner from Union Square, also very conveniently located to Powell St BART station and transportation to the airport. The design is also very modern and very nice. They served coffee every morning and wine every afternoon in the hotel lobby, which is a nice touch. I wish I had stayed in one of the other room types. I probably would have been more satisfied, but I cannot recommend the economy class room category at all.

“Standard Ritz Experience” We got off to a very good start at this hotel. Amy at the front desk was welcoming, pleasant, efficient, and best of all, explained the details of our package thoroughly. So off we went to our room. Our first impression was that we would be happy in our room partly because it did not have the standard hotel room layout. This room was longer at the window wall, instead of the window wall being the short end of the room. The room was still standard Ritz size with the same amount of furniture, just in different places, and with an extra window which is a nice bonus. The blue and gold color scheme was attractive, and the room had a nice luxurious look to it. The bathroom was spacious with separate shower, tub, and water closet. The sand colored marble was particularly beautiful. Once we settled in we noticed the room had some functional issues. The closet was just about the smallest we have ever encountered at a hotel. We were on a short trip so we did not have much luggage, but if we did, most of it would have been on display in the room, which is something we do not like. There was however, decent drawer space. The door into the water closet was extremely tight when exiting, even for average sized people. We are not sure these problems exist in other rooms since this was our first stay at this hotel. Later we noticed that the two chairs at the desk were very marked up at the legs with what looked like paint. We thought we could solve having to look at these marks by reversing the chairs, but the backsides were just as marked up. Finally, there was no decorative pillow or throw on the bed, which can be seen in some of the pictures on the hotel web site. All kind of minor issues on their own, but when you add them up it changes your impression in a negative way. If we were there for a longer stay I think we would have asked to see another room. The staff at this hotel was especially friendly and really tried to go the extra mile to make our stay pleasant. At breakfast, I looked over the paper selection and walked away empty handed because the WSJ was not published on that day, President’s Day. A staff member, Edward, noticed and asked what I was looking for and tried to find the weekend WSJ that I had missed out on and was hoping was still available. He could not find a copy for me, but I was very impressed that he tried. A valet staff member went over directions with me in great detail to make sure I understood them. The easily accessed Sports Club/LA is the hotel gym. It is a very nice mega gym that even includes sports court activities and a light restaurant/snack area. The pool, however, was not super sized and only had four lanes that were occupied during my visit, so I was unable to swim my laps. Since the gym is so large, the hotel feels it can charge fifteen dollars for a visit. For most people this gym would be overkill and the gyms and pools at most Ritz hotels are good enough and free, so I wish the hotel did not have this charge. It could be a deterrent to using the gym or staying here if you really want to workout. The hotel seems small with an elegant clublike feel. The location is central and easily walkable to many sites including wonderful Georgetown, and just blocks away from the metro. There is not much going on in the immediate neighborhood. Overall, a stay here is a good choice, but there are many good options in Washington DC.

“Too Small and Bad Practices” The lobby and bar are the only benefits to staying at this hotel. The rooms are too small for any reasonable size adult person and the service is marginal. But beware of questionable practices...the hotel group that owns the Hudson initially authorizes your credit card for four times the room rate and then takes their time correcting the charges. If you like small rooms and floating cash to a business, then the Hudson is for you. Timalyn Franklin

“Excellent stay - we couldn't believe what good value it was!” Stayed here at the start and end of our trip to the States. Using satnav it was very easy to find and a convenient drive to and from the airport. We liked this hotel very much. It was incredibly good value, the staff were all very pleasant and welcoming and the accomodation very good. There are free snacks and drinks between 5.30 and 7pm every evening and also breakfast is included in the price. Although this was not the best breakfast that we had during our trip, it was adequate and we felt that it was excellent for the price that we had paid. It is also adjacent to a mall - I could walk across to Macy's while my husband sat at the pool! It is a lovely mall with lots of shops, eating places and cinemas so we were very happy with its location. The hotel also had free wireless internet and parking. If I flew into Charlotte again I would not consider staying anywhere else.

“Great staff” My family of 4 stayed here during the weekend festivities of my nephew's wedding. Most of the family and friends stayed at the Canterbury Hotel but since that hotel would not let more than 2 people stay in a room; I looked around for a close hotel that served breakfast. I am a Marriott Rewards Silver member and have stayed in many, many Marriott hotels. This hotel is new, cleverly decorated and in the same area as the new JW Marriott and Springhill Suites. The hotel staff was very pleasant, courteous and on the ball. I like when the hotel staff reply "my pleasure" after the guest requests something (extra hangers, where the closest ATM is, etc.) Hotel underground parking is shared wtih the other 2 hotels above and the nice thing is that you can walk all the way to the City Center Mall (approx 4 blocks away) without going outside. Very nice-especially if you have a tween girl who just got her hair fixed for her cousin's wedding. Only thing I could possibly find fault in was that the rate was high (a conference was in town) and there was no convenience store easily accessible. Good location (right next to Lucas Oil Stadium) and excellent customer service. Only thing

“Excellent Hotel” For the last four years we stayed at the Michelangelo Hotel. This time we thought of trying to save money, earn points with Marriott, but still be close to subway lines in Times Square. The Fairfield Inn was an excellent choice. The staff is very friendly and willing to please. The rooms are clean, the complimentary breakfast adequate (don't expect bacon, steak, and eggs), and located within easy walking distance to 4 subway lines. It is a safe area to walk and close to all types of restaurants that are more than adequate. Also, no history to date of bed bugs. The theater district is within a few blocks.

“Clean, Comfortable and in a safe area” I stayed at the Courtyard Sept 27-30 for a business trip. It was the weekend of the ADA Convention so the room was $354 a night! The room was typical Courtyard style with not much frills. The pictures on the web showed flat screen tv's and modern furniture...I had two different rooms and neither looked like the pictures. Both rooms had regular tv's and plain looking furniture. Although I must say both rooms were spotless and very quiet. The hotel is in a pretty good location, several blocks from good shopping (Westfield mall) and about 4 blocks to Moscone. If you are going to SanFran for a convention at Moscone I reccomend the W, the Westin Market St, or the Marriott. All are MUCH closer to Moscone......I tried to get in these places but all were booked. If you can get a good rate and have great walking shoes, I would recommend this hotel. But it wasn't worth $350 a night when they are plenty of other great hotels in the city.

“Muy buen hotel en una ciudad compleja” No entiendo como hay gente que dice que el personal de este hotel no es bueno.- Nosotros fuimos atendidos de forma excelente y el hotel es MUY bueno y recomendable.

“Centrally located - Good value” This was definitely one of the more interesting hotels I've stayed at for business. Four towers with different colour names go to different "wings" of the hotel. First the lobby - very big and basically goes around in a large circle which made it a little challenging to meet with business associates but I managed. Plenty of seating which was good. Room - It was fine, clean, bed was comfortable however the room itself was quite small which doesn't tend to bother me except that there was a door to an adjoining room hence it felt a little intimate being able to hear someone russling about on the other side. I was however annoyed about the card swipe into the room (which is amusing seeing someone else comment on this.) After checking in, I had to return to the reception as my cards didn't work to get into the room and to get them re-magnetized..... lo and behold, they still didn't work when I returned and after trying them again and again, finally managed to get the door open. Every time I returned I would have to swipe 15-20 times to get the card to register (and I stay at hotels regularly hence am not unfamiliar with how these work!) They need to look at fixing this as it's frustrating. One very positive note, after finally going to get some dinner at around 9pm I decided to eat in the lobby bar and had an amazing prawn fajita....great value too.

“overrated on this website” I do not see why this hotel has been #1 on TA for so long. I was disappointed. The rooms/carpets are dirty, The pool and health club have a nasty odor.The housekeeping is really sloppy= they dont wipe the bathroom counters, vacuum rugs etc... The reception staff is ok but not overly helpful. We had three rooms for three days and were celebrating my mother's 70th birthday and the hotel did nothing. Some Chocolates, cookies something small might have been nice. When we asked to be together - they got us on the same floor- but not together. We did get the requested early check in. The hotel sticks to its formula with the big breakfasts and happy hours but at the price point is pretty unremarkable and certainly not deserving of its high ranking on TA. I'll stay elsewhere next time and will not return.

“Pleasant downtown hotel experience” It was our first stay at this Hampton Inn. Great location near the downtown attractions. Staff were friendly, bed was extremely comfortable and room amenities were nice. Pool was indeed small and not very clean. We had to try out the AC in three differentrooms before we found one that cooled adequately. In fact, the maintenance man finally just put a new AC unit in our room which did the job and helped us beat the 100 degree heat outside . Breakfast was good but space limited making it a bit hectic at times. Always love the fresh waffles

“Great Central location in San Francisco” We stayed in Room 2009 for two nights: November 22 and 23 (Thanksgiving night and the night after). We arrived via BART and a half mile plus hike from the airport about 2:30 pm, and the room was ready. When I checked in on line the day before, I was assigned a room on the 21st floor so I’m not sure why we didn’t get that one, but I have no complaints. We had a view of Telegraph Hill and Coit Tower. The room had a nice work area by the window, and the free wifi worked perfectly. The television was good also. The bathroom had one of those frosted doors, but you couldn’t see through it. We had a bathtub/shower combo with sink area and toilet. Many amenities were provided. The ice machine was down the floor just near the elevator. The beds were comfortable. There was no available outlet between the beds so they provided a power strip. The executive lounge was available 24 hours a day with snacks and soft drinks. Alcohol was extra even at happy hour. Everyday at 5 they had hors d’oeuvres. The first night they had chicken wings, crab cakes, and one more. They also had 3 choices on Friday, but I forget exactly what. Service was good, and you could make a meal out of it. I did eat too many wings so even though I didn’t have dinner until 7 pm, I wasn’t very hungry and only ate my fish and not the veggies and potato. It would have been nice to have a small refrigerator in the room because I couldn’t take leftovers back after my meals. There was a safe in the closet which was a nice extra. One complaint was the breakfast in the executive lounge. They had boiled eggs but nothing else hot. Lots of pastries and some fruit. It would have been nice to have scrambled eggs, even if fake, and definitely a meat selection. The Hilton in Tampa had meat in their executive lounge. That was about my only complaint except for the people who would stand outside the executive lounge and then enter when someone left. The hotel needs to monitor better. The lobby was pretty, but we didn’t spend any time at the bar area. When I stopped to asked the valet how to get to Pier 2, he was speaking French to someone so when they finished, I spoke in French and then switched to English. I thought that was good that they catered to many people in many languages. The hotel was about .6 mile from the Esplanade. Fisherman’s Wharf was a bit further, especially if you took a flat route. We walked up Telegraph Hill and went up Coit Tower before zigzagging down the hill to Butterfly for lunch. We had a good dinner Thursday night at Sinbads as well. We had one bad meal at a Hunan restaurant on the street that runs diagonally from Kearny to Ghirardelli’s. We walked a lot and enjoyed the central location of the hotel. I would definitely stay there again. Next time, I won’t make my dinner reservations until I have checked out the lounge offering. They do need to improve the breakfast for the executive lounge and monitor those who enter. We will return in the next few years. Thanks for a good Thanksgiving weekend experience.

“Boa localização,tranquilo e pratico” O pessoal do front desk e muito atencioso e eficiente.Na chegada meus filhos ganharam um lápis gigante com os pontos turísticos da cidade,foi atenciosa a recepção .Todas as solicitações feitas na reserva foram consideradas e atendidas.Há Starbucks no piso do Lobby e o restaurante no andar de baixo tem um bom buffet de café da manha.O quarto econforravel,cabe ate uma cama extra alem das duas de casal,se for preciso.O secador e muito bom,não e daqueles de parede que demoram para secar.

“A comfortable overnighter courtesy of airline” American Airlines provided 2 nights’ accommodation and meal vouchers as compensation for the delayed arrival from Chicago and my missing the late night connection to Sydney. I was greeted by an impressive lobby and efficient, albeit robotic front desk staff. The room with all the wear and tear of an airport hotel showed signs of age, including the polished dark wood decor, but had comfortable facilities and the North facing view from the seventh floor from Century City, with the Hollywood Hills behind, to downtown in the distance is great. Housekeeping was very efficient and I had a bathrobe within 3 minutes of request.
