An excellent breakfast in the Daily Grill and take out meal in the evening was marred only by a slight memory/attention problem by the kitchen staff who responded promptly when reminded. As on a previous LAX stays I opted to go to Manhattan Beach Village on the $5 return trolley bus that stops across the road rather than other options of venturing to Marina del Rey, Westwood, Santa Monica or Beverly Hills or downtown. That is much less stressful than renting a car and has all the shopping, including department and Apple stores and quality shops and even a movie theatre if people want to pass more hours, there is not much more needed for a lay over. Rather than purchasing a bottle of water for $4 from the mini-bar I threw $1.50 into the vending machine next to the ice maker and had several beverage choices. I thought the lobby shop closed a little early and with the Daily Grill the only in-house food outlet the services are limited for late night arrivals. For my LAX over nighter I don’t think I would choose Westin over Hilton, Sheraton or Marriott but if it is the airline paying I’ll take it again with pleasure!

“Great view, ordinary hotel” The hotel is located on the river and offers splendid views, especially at night. I was there during a major thunderstorm and it was a spectacular light show! The hotel itself is a pretty generic convention hotel. The rooms are comfortably sized but the bed and linens were very ordinary and not particularly comfortable. The hotel is reasonably quiet despite the fact that it is very busy.

“Couldn't be more convenient, great staff, average rooms” The hotel is connected to Terminal B at the Airport by a walkway. This makes it incredibly convenient for meetings, or just for an overnight stay. You can also walk to the SEPTA train, which gets you to downtown for $7. Buy an "Independence Pass" which gives you unlimited use for a day for $11. The meeting facilities are good, and comfortable. Had a very nice group dinner, white glove service. The public areas are very nice, the room is the standard marriott room.....club chair with ottoman, desk, dresser, no minibar, and a comfortable king bed. The shower was hot and powerful. My main complaint (and suggestion) is that they get WIRELESS INTERNET! This is pretty much the first Marriott (other than Fairfield, etc.) that only had wired internet. Not much help for a tablet user. Given that I am sure they cater to business travelers, this is really expected in a hotel these days. By the way, if unable to walk from the airport, they offer a shuttle to and from. It clearly meets the need, and then some.

“Trump Luxus Downtown” Spektakuläres neues Hotel von Donald Trump in SoHo. Sehr moderner Glasbau mit atemberaubendem Ausblick auf Manhattan von den High Floor Zimmern. Sehr komfortable, großzügige Zimmer mit bodentiefen Fenstern, sehr moderne, schlicht designte Ausstattung, schöne große Marmorbäder, Nespresso Maschine mit complimentary pads. Unbedingt high floor buchen. Ein Highlight ist sicher auch der Pool im 7. Stock, zwar nicht groß, aber es liegt sich sehr gut, nette Bar. Eine Oase in Manhattan im Sommer. Tolle Lage, nur ein paar Schritte vom quirligen Soho entfernt.

“Great property, great location, you really can't go wrong here....” I am going to be relatively short and sweet with this review. Met up with a friend for a Yankees game and we decided beforehand to stay overnight because that is what mature adults do when planning to responsibly consume several (ok, multiple) $11 beers at Yankee Stadium and want to take driving out of the equation. The Yankees won the game in the bottom of the 10th with a walk off, so our lodging expectations were high... Anyway, I am on the road for around 60 days a year for both business and pleasure so I know a decent hotel property when I see one; often within 30 seconds of walking in the front door. I am not going to waste your time with a review of the size of the room, how fluffy the pillows were or my opinion on the color of the grout in the bathroom. I have no complaints. Bottom line, this joint is just plain nice...period; and the location is even better. You are within a 10 minute walk of Times Square and Central Park and several subway lines located out front. MSG is a 15 minute walk away. You are basically in the heart of Manhattan. The “D” train (7th Ave Station) to Yankee Stadium is right out front. I can’t see how any leisure or business traveler would be disappointed staying here. I would certainly stay here again and for someone who travels quite a bit....enough said... If you want the Ritz, go stay at the Ritz and you will drop $700 a night and you will feel like a king. But for way less than half the cost, this property delivers a fantastic stay; modern and clean and for what I would consider a great value. Even for NYC. Go Yankees! I will be back....

“Showing its age” This is one of those hotels that survives by being adjacent to buildings housing large companies. There is nothing wrong with the hotel, but there is not a whole lot positive to say about it either. The room service menu is extremely limited and the food isn't that good. The rooms are clean and comfortable, except that the old-fashioned air conditioner is noisy enough to justify the earplugs supplied by the hotel. The staff is very pleasant. The wine list at the bar is actually pretty good. For guests who register with their awards program, the hotel provides free drinks and appetizers each evening. That's definitely a plus. Ask for your coupons.

“Good location, facility, rooms. Service?” Enjoyed several nights in a spacious, nicely-designed modern room. Great views, huge bathroom with luxurious shower. Nice front desk staff. The bar scene can be VERY loud to obnoxious, so you might opt to sit outside and have wait service. I left instructions for the maid with my tips, while the room was serviced, the instructions AND the tip were both ignored! Perhaps a language barrier? Upon checkout, I mentioned the incredibly slow speed of the internet and they said they'd share the concern with the IT dept. This is one of the better hotels I've enjoyed in Phoenix.

“Perfectly located for a theater vacation” My husband and I stayed here last week on a one night getaway to Manhattan. We got the room at a very attractive rate on Hotwire. We were in town for less than 36 hours and hoped to see two plays. We could not have been more pleased with the location, with handy access to the theater district. We found the hotel to be a good value for the price we paid. When we checked in, we asked if we could upgrade to a queen or king size bed and were given a Deluxe room with a king bed. The room was average sized by Manhattan standards (small by any other standards) but very comfortable, attractively decorated and clean. It featured the usual amenities, including cable TV, room service, mini bar, upscale toiletries, etc. The bed was very comfortable with lots of pillows. Note, the room was only suitable for one or two people, as I don't know how you could squeeze in even a small child. Our room was on the second floor and I could hear the trash trucks at 1 a.m. as well as street noise beginning around 6 a.m. However, we had shut off the air conditioning/fan before retiring. Had I to do it again, I would leave that on all night to block out the noise because we really couldn't hear much from outside with that on. The view was not great in the traditional sense, although we could gaze upon the Belasco Theater. We found the staff very friendly and efficient. They accommodated our request to place our luggage in the storage room after we checked out and handled the retrieval in a jiffy. We ate a post-theater dinner at the restaurant and were very pleased with both the service and cuisine. The only off-note was when we requested a restaurant recommendation for lunch -- the front desk employee really couldn't come up with any suggestions. Overall, the hotel is very comfortable and an excellent value at Hotwire prices. Its best feature, however, is the great location in the heart of the theater district. The hotel is in easy walking distance of many theaters as well as the TKTS booth -- to say nothing of the other Times Square tourist attractions (get your photo on a Hershey bar at the Hershey store!). Highly recommended.

“Affordable, Nice Location, Pleasant” Was here for three nights during the week in mid December for business. Overall, very nice play to stay. Right in the Chelsea area. Rooms are small (they are small everywhere in NYC) but nicely appointed. Bathroom functional and nice, beds great, elevator is a bit slow at times but nothing major. Great breakfast places right around the corner for coffee, breakfast sandwiches, etc. as noted in below reviews. If you like cigars, there's a great cigar spot on same block just across the street, Martinez Cigars, where they've been making good cigars for 30 years. All in all, I'd recommend highly. I paid $199 per night booking through the hotel's website. Pretty good deal two weeks before Christmas.

“Like a 1980s retirement community” I stayed here for a convention and left early. If you've read other reviews then you know that this Hotel is very old and needs updating. The best way I can think of describing it is to say: "Think of staying at a 1980s retirement community." The grounds are nice and there are people driving around in golf carts (because the place is so spread out) but the furniture is old and looks like grandma has been using the same bedspread that your mom grew up with. You check in at the lobby then walk or get a golf cart escort to your room. I had reserved a King room but was given a double (not a big deal). The rooms have very old decoration, old TVs (cathode ray tube), fuzzy reception on several channels but are otherwise very clean. The mattress on the bed felt old and stiff. I could feel individual springs through the sheets. Internet is provided by ATT-wifi (daily fee) and is spotty at best (can check an email or two before signal is lost). I called to ask where the best place in the complex was for a good signal and was told "outside." While this may be accurate I don't feel that it's an acceptable answer. The conference facilities have been fine so far and I think that's why this place still operates. I ran into several other conference attendees who were also a little surprised by the hotel rooms as well. I'm not really a hotel snob but if I'm paying upwards of $150 per night for a hotel I expect something better than what Motel 6 offers. If you're old this place will probably remind bring back memories. If you're under age 65 I would recommend looking elsewhere. I was able to check out early. They were nice enough to waive the $50 per night fee it would have been to check out prior to my scheduled stay. I haven't seen this policy at other hotels so it leads me to believe that the situation has come up more than once at this place. I had some pretty bad experiences with the parking lot attendant and security guard which are likely isolated incidents related to personalities and led to me leaving the hotel early so that's why they waived the fee. Pros: Clean Landscaping with lots of flowers and trees Several restaurants on site Good for old people Friendly front desk staff Cons: OLD OLD OLD beds and decoration Very hard old mattress Old cathode ray tube TV with fuzzy channels on 1/2 of my stations Spread out - everything is a walk from your room. Wi-Fi internet - poor signals throughout, unreliable, not for business traveler Beware of angry security guy and parking lot attendant. Let's say you book for a week but need to leave early, you are charged $50 per day for the remaining days on the reservations that you didn't stay. Not good for young travelers. If you have to attend a conference at this hotel I would recommend booking at the Courtyard Marriott (where I fled to) across the Interstate (about 1 min drive) or one of the others next to it.

“Way too small for a four star hotel” I stayed here for two nights and I was surprised that this hotel is a four star hotel. The lobby is very tiny and so was the room. The bathroom was pretty decent size and I liked it. The service was fine. I didn't feel it's a special place at all. Surprisingly they had a gov rate so I stayed there for $108/day (and I needed to stay in downtown) otherwise I wouldn't have stayed.

“Rooms suited for miniatures” For a price of $110 I expected a little more. The "suite" was the size of a couple of desks. VERY small room for the price. Not exactly a "suite" in the sense that I've experienced hotel suites over the years. No more than two to a romm is what I'd recommend! Walls as thin as paper kept us up all night with the sounds of our neighbors... NOT a restful sleep at all. Stinky room as well. I'm looking for something positive to say and I guess that would be the accomodating and friendly staff at the front desk. Very helpful and friendly. Nice continental breakfast as well. Recommend taking your coffee tray down from your room to carry back items to your room. Benihana is just a short three minute walk up the hill and a fabulous dinner there, but rather depressing to come back to our little hole of a stinky room. Very bad value for the price. Had I paid around $50 as some other reviewers had paid, I'd be a little more gentle with my review, but with the price I paid of over $120 after taxes added, it's a poor value and stay overall. Will not stay again.

“Fabulous NYC Experience” I was a little concerned about booking this hotel because of the location, but am so glad I chose it. The Bowery is located in the middle of some great neighbourhoods, all walkable. You can get to East Village, Chelsea, Soho, etc. on foot. Plus, there are a ton of great restaurants within a 20 minute walk. The Bowery itself has some really great restaurants, cute shops and even a Whole Foods. But it is not totally gentrified, which give the area an interesting urban feel to it. The Bowery Hotel has really amazing decor The design team did a fabulous job creating a cool gritty/luxury NYC feel of the 1930s. It is quirky (dark lobby, no concierge desk, small wood paneled elevators, a bar that looks like something from the shining or Barton Fink) but that is what really makes the experience great. Plus, they have an outdoor lounge area which I really value when spending time in New York. The decor of the rooms is eclectic too and are fortunately very bright. Luxurious sheets, wood floors, grey marble bath (very retro NYC) all make for a great experience. Plus a great view of the Bowary below, NYC buildings ( with water towers) and even the empire state building in the background. The neighborhood was great. At night there are tons of people walking around until all hours and during the day, it was very quiet. The street noise could be heard in the room, but just barely, just enough to remind you that you are in NYC but not disturb sleep. Some of the staff at the front were really great and others a bit distracted. I think it would be easier for everyone if there was a separate concierge desk, with people who just specialized in that. One person at the front desk seemed a bit put out by my questions, others were great. We ate dinner and breakfast at Gemmas. Dinner was really outstanding. Great fresh food and perfect service at a decent price. It is really an amazing place, looks straight out of some Northern Italian village. Plus, it is very fun to eat outside and people watch. Breakfast was not as good, slow service and boring food. But we discovered Think Coffee and Peels. Peels serves fabulous fun food with incredibly nice service, so we ate there constantly. There are hotels that offer a more luxurious feel, but can't offer this amount of personality and great location at this price point.

“Small, but Great” I'll start off with a warning: when booking, check to see if you're getting a room with a private bathroom. The rooms were really small, but it was cozy and conveniently located. When I first got into the room, i was shocked to see that it didn't have a bathroom. Apparently there are rooms that don't have bathrooms and toilets so you have to use the shared toilet and shower down the hall. For $10 more, i was able to get bumped up to a room with its own bathroom.

“Good location. Great for a long term stay.” I was here for ten days, mostly on business that was spread out around the city. This is one of the smallest Residence Inn rooms I have been in, but it is large for a NY hotel room. My room on the 11th floor had a great view of the Empire State Building, but not all rooms would have that. The positives: 2 minute walk to Bryant Park/42nd street station, about five minutes to Times Square station, Good breakfast, Full sized frig, safe big enough for your laptop, comfy bed. Negatives: the curved rod on the shower made the bathroom even more crowded when the door was opened, during busy tmes you could wait up to 10-15 minutes for elevator, and the night snacks were minimal (had much more of a spread at other Residence Inns), and would have loved a small desk for my laptop instead of the kitchen bar. I stayed on a discounted promo, so I am not sure that I would pay full price for the room; however, I would stay here again if I could have that same rate. The concierge (Judy) was helpful with directions and arranging car pickups. There is a Pret a Manger on the corner across from the hotel for sandwiches and a small market next to the hotel on that side as well. Bryant Park is a great place for a little sunshine (when it is not raining) and it is about a half of a mile to Penn Station and to Grand Central as well.

“Thin walls.” Good breakfast, fair price, nice room - seems clean. But the the walls were very thin. You should not hear someone in the next room going to the bathroom. I've been in numerous hotels where I couldn't hear sounds from my own bathroom. Just gross. There are several other hotels right next door, at least two of which look a lot newer. I'd try one of those if in the area again.

“Best hotel in Philadelphia” This was my second stay at this hotel. My first stay was in July 2005. I don't know if it was coincidence on not, but they gave me the same room both times, which was fine because the room was a huge corner room and very nice. Philadelphia is my home town, and I come back here a few times a year and have stayed in almost all the major hotels here, with the exception of the Four Seasons. The Sofitel is far and beyond the best hotel in the city that I've stayed in. The beds are extremely comfortable, the bathrooms very big with a tub and shower, with nice soaps and shampoos. I wouldn't stay anywhere else now.

“Noisy!!!” The hotel is in a great location if you are in Austin to party on 6th street. We had a room that faced 7th street and it was impossible to get any sleep until about 4:00 am. Between the people on the street and traffic noise it was very loud. We were on the 4th floor, maybe a room on the opposite side or higher up would have been better.

“A Nice Stay for NYC!” This hotel is a nice stay for NYC because the rooms are very clean, hotel is very comfortable, and it's in a great location. A few blocks from Herald Square, 34th street shopping, Madison Square Gardens, Penn Station...everything! The staff was very nice and always accommodating. The hotel also has a great view of the Empire State Building in rooms facing 6th Ave. Very cool pic to have if you get lucky! I was extremely satisfied with the my two night's stay and would stay again.

“Outstanding hotel in San Francisco” The Intercontinental is a teriffic hotel. We just spent four nights there and could not have been happier. The rooms are large, spotless, and well-furnished. The location is very convenient to sights, shops, and restaurants. The service was outstanding. Altogether a perfect stay.

“Clean and convenient LAX hotel” Hotel is close to LAX; we were able to return our rental car and walk back easily to the hotel. There is a shuttle that serves this and another hotel that runs every 20-30 minutes. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. Service was top notch; the front desk clerk gave us a room that was quiet but had a view for the little ones and also sent up complimentary milk and cookies for them. The bell man was very helpful with tips and also got us extra towels for the kids, unasked. Very friendly, clean and comfortable with clean, modern decor. I would highly recommend this as a great airport hotel.

“Terrific hotel, small, but excellent for the price” I can't list any complaints about the Belnord Hotel. For those who lament its small size, what in the world are you in NYC for? It's all about being outside of the hotel, exploring and enjoying the City's sites. Sure, the rooms are small. Our room had a full-size bed that my 6'4" husband had a bit of trouble keeping his feet on. But it wasn't a nuisance, and there was a good-size flat-screen TV and a small, compact closet to store our stuffs in. The bathroom was teeny-tiny but good enough for our needs. Overall, the hotel was easy to find, clean, efficient, and offered a great price. The one complaint I had was about the luggage storage room. They don't check to see if you're even staying in the hotel before they give you the key to it. All of our stuff stayed secure enough, though, so I suppose I should give them the benefit of the doubt. This is a great place just to crash, and just one block from the subway. Excellent location for families, especially if you're hopping on over to Central Park or the local museums.

“Good Property” I have stayed at this property many times and plan on coming back. It is not the Anatole next door, but is consistently a good business traveler property for $139.00. Location is good to downtown and market district. Nothing within walking distance to property, including restaurants. Overall, staff has been very good and always very helpful. Property is older, but everything has been remodeled and very nice.

“Avoid the lower floors” Reviews calling this a slightly faded beauty are correct. Dull but safe uptown location, big rooms, HD TVs, friendly staff, near lots of attractions and subway and a short walk to the park. Big warning: the lower floors are used for movie interview sessions where thousands of cigarettes are smoked. The result was my 3rd floor room absolutely stunk like a thousand dirty ashtrays. The industrial air purifier in each room seems like a perk until you realize that it is fighting a losing battle to the stench. Even smokers will want to insist on a higher floor or a non smoking room and step outside.

“Discreto” Un hôtel come tanti altri. Per quanto mi riguarda hi avuto una spiacevole esperienza. Nonostante fosse prevista la possibilità di avere sistemazioni in una quadrupla con letto aggiunto, ho dovuto far dormire tre figlie insieme in un queen bed. E' infatti successo che dopo avermi assegnato la camera, contrariamente a quanto mi era stato detto alla recepito, si sono rifiutati di portarmi un letto aggiuntivo per problemi legge incendio. Insomma, in quella camera proprio non era possibile. Dopo molta insistenza mi hanno portato delle lenzuola e dei cuscini che sarebbero, secondo loro, dovuti fungere da materasso per far dormire sul pavimento una delle mie figlie!! A quel punto ho perso la pazienza e il massimo che ho ottenuto è stato di avere il garage gratis... Insomma un hotel serio non si comporta così...

“OK - 2 nights, 2 rooms. 12/2011” We were in for a wedding and spent Saturday and Sunday nights at the Four Points. This place is clean but showing signs of age. Rooms appeared to be heavily used with many scratches and dents. Chrome trim on many of the light fixtures were missing leaving just the residual glue. The gym was nice, clean and up to date. There is a good sports bar next door. Please, if your staying for more than one night or intend to go in and out a lot - learn how to use the back entrance onto Grant Av. Otherwise, you'll be going out on the Boulevard which unless you grew up in NE Phila will drive you crazy - I will wager that any out of towner who attemts to navigate the Boulevard will make at least 2 wrong turns on this ancient, never been used anywhere else highway design .

“One of my new favorite hotels!” I had a wonderful stay at the Palmer House--truly one of my favorite hotels that I've ever stayed at. The staff were friendly and accommodating. The lobby is spectacular and a wonderful place to relax or get a drink. The guest rooms were equally appealing. I appreciated the mixture of the historical/luxurious old world charm mixed with modern amenities. A lot of times historic hotels also feel a little old and run-down, but this was not the case at the Palmer House. It was impeccably renovated and clean. The hotel was also in a great location--close to the L & all the downtown Chicago attractions (museums, Millennium Park, Michigan Ave, etc.) but was still very quiet--I rarely heard traffic or noise from the L. Can’t wait to go back!

“Lovely historic hotel!” My husband often stays at the Adolphus ob business; the Federal Courthouse is steps away. The hotel is one of those beautiful old Grand Dames, at once elegant and classy. But the hotel is also a perfect weekend or vacation choice for Dallas. We stayed there recently for a Rangers game and took in a Mavericks game last season. You can leave the hotel and quickly acces the freeway that will take you all over the Metroplex. There is valet parking, but with a weekend rate of $99, it's a real treat to stay in such a nice hotel. The rooms are very large, and they are super quiet, with large bathrooms and comfy chairs or a sofa with a big flatscreen...we'll what's not to love? There is a great restaurant in the hotel, but there are other options within walking distance. One could walk to the Kennedy site at Dealy Plaza and catch the Dart Train to the fabulous art museum or new fine arts area. We are loyal members of a national chain, but we spice up our travels with stay in unique, lovely hotels or bed and breakfasts. The Adolphus is a choice we return to again and again.

“Nice option in Harlem!” Stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in January, and had a great experience. Definitely a trendy feel to the lobby and rooms, but not off-putting for someone middle aged. In a NY hotel I mainly look for a good location (meaning ability to walk/subway easily around town), cleanliness, and price. Aloft met my standards and then some. I got a good deal, and was in a location that made it easy to walk around and see the sights. I love what Harlem has to offer, so didn't partake of the gym or bar offerings - too many places to go and see around the area. But the room was large by NYC standards - I had a 2 bed, and my favorite thing was the HUGE shower - and even though the storage was odd (no bureau, nothing with drawers, but lots of spaces for piling things as well as a place to hand clothes) I would stay there again. A great staff is important to me, even though I enjoy getting out there and planning my time and routes myself, and the staff was friendly and helpful whenever I needed something. I appreciated that the housekeeping did those little things that I expect when I'm on vacation, including meeting my request for massive coffee supplies ...lol!

“Good Business Hotel” The JW Marriott is only a couple of blocks from Union Square. That makes it convenient to a number of great restaurants, shopping, etc., but a fair distance from the tourist areas around Fishermans Wharf etc. The set up was nice for business travelers, with a decent work space and good internet access. The club level lounge was large, had great views of the city, and featured a hot breakfast and the usual snacks etc in the evening. The room was large especially by SF standards, and the bathroom was particularly well appointed. The room looked like it had recently been renovated but I am not sure. Overall a nice choice, but not heads and shoulders better than the many other competitors in its price tier (i.e., it is about the same as the SF Hyatt Regency on Market Street, but the SF Ritz Carlton is lightyears better).

“For DC This was a great choice” We decided to stop here for a few days on our trip across the us. We ended up staying 4 nights. The accommodations were great, we were upgraded, and the staff from doormen to bellmen to check in staff to concierge were helpful with all of our questions and recommendations. the room was clean, the sheets crisp, the room service fast and right on the money. I really am picky, and can't think of a thing I didn't care for or that was off

“Pretty good with a few quirks” This was a tough review. I wavered between a score of 3 and 4. Had I paid full price for this 4-star hotel, I would have expected more pizazz. But because I got a tremendous deal through Priceline, I was quite delighted with what we got. My wife, myself, and our friend staying with us noted these highlights: Helpful, friendly, and cheerful staff, including easy check-in, helpful bellman, cheerful coffee counter workers and other randomly-encountered workers. Excellent location, especially if you enjoy walking in the city (central to Michigan Ave, River walks, Navy Pier, and Loop). I suspect all rooms have views ranging from very good (ours from room 2836 was of skyline to the north), to stunning. Nice new large, hi-rez, flat TV. Nice Bliss bath products. The comfy, luxurious beds tempted us to linger. All other functional features were in good order (water pressure, heating/cooling, etc.) Coffeemaker in room w/Starbucks. Now for just a few little quirks: Surfaces in the room were a bit dusty (but not badly so). One floor lamp could not be turned off and had to be unplugged (we all tried). Bathroom had no fan or other ventilation. I believe they still charge $12 a day for fitness center, but we didn't have time to try. Parking is $42 for valet, $34 for self park. I paid $32 at lot 1 block north under AMC theaters; probably could have found cheaper, but we were tired. Bought 3 pastries and an OJ at coffee counter for just under $20. I wished we could have stayed longer and tried the pool. This hotel would make a great "home base" for exploring the city.

“Downhill Fast” This is the last time I will stay at La Cantera. I have previously lived in SA when the hotel first opened. I have stayed there 4 times in the past 4 months and every experience has gotten worse. We had torn sheets, plastic cups in the bathroom, a clogged sink, a leaky shower that did not drain well. No AM paper available. We had no key to our mini-bar. TV sets are old. In all, what a joke. To give you a contrast, my wife and I stayed the previous week at the Four Seasons in Dallas. And while dated in some respects, it was a far better experience than La Cantera. As people have mentioned, the place has really gone down hill. For a gift to our close friends, we put them up at the Casitas and like several other guests have mentioned they had a horrible experience. At $500 a night they deserved better and actually got the room for free---but their laundry list of complaints sounded like what one would find at a "roach motel" not a 5 star property. Shame on Westin! Shame, Shame, Shame! We have spoken with other friends who still live in San Antonio and they have shared similar experiences to the point where they no longer recommend the Westin to anyone. Is there a common thesis here. You bet! Management better get a wake up call and address these remedies. Don't be on the losing end and waste your money....you will be most disappointed. This is coming from a preferred StarWood guest who typically has a pretty understanding point of view of what can go wrong in a hotel experience but we have seen a pattern of behavior that has led us to look elsewhere next time we hit San Antonio.

“Hilton Americas is great.” Really nice hotel. I was there for a convention with over 2,300 people. They handled everything with ease. The staff was always courteous, smiling and willing to help even though I know it must have been a very hectic time for them. The food was delicious and the it just seemed that they went over and beyond to make sure that all of our events were up to or requests. I would recommend this hotel to others for their events or even just to stay while in Houston.

“Cannot say enough good things about Casablanca” Whenever I can, and the rates are right, I try to stay at the Casablanca in Times Square. Every visit I have done has been positive, with some of them being the best hotel stays I've had in NYC. The reason is mostly the friendly positive service, but I also enjoy the free breakfast (excellent bagels and juices always), the free wine and cheese in the evening (the Proseco is always nice), the sweet-smelling orange-scented bathroom products, and the prime location. Now, some of the rooms are definitely on the small side, and in some cases the wi-fi has some weak spots. But those are pretty minor, and the benefits of such a great property (in a city where a friendly staff and reliable amenities are rare) will always trump.

“Another terrific Four Seasons stay” Our one-night stay at the Four Seasons New York was our sixteenth Four Seasons property. We had been looking forward to staying here for years and were pleased to finally be able to add this lovely property to our list of Four Seasons stays (full disclosure: this is our favorite hotel brand, so we're likely a bit biased). The soaring lobby in the I.M. Pei-designed building creates a larger, more public space than we're used to in a Four Seasons (and makes the bar area feel a little less clubby and secluded), but it is pretty and interesting architecturally. With only a few rooms on each floor, the feeling you get is of quiet, calm and luxury from the moment you step off the elevator. Our room - a deluxe king on a high floor - had a typical New York view with vistas of buildings all around. The room itself was beautiful, with typical Four Seasons furniture and a wonderful king bed that was oh-so-comfortable. The room was large by New York standards and very comfortable for two people with a desk, sofa and coffee table. The bathroom and dressing area were also large and very well thought-out with plenty of space for bathing and dressing. The bathroom was gorgeous, made all the more so by the fantastic Bulgari toiletries. We had coffee delivered to our room in the morning and enjoyed the typically-excellent Four Seasons service. With more time (and without brunch plans), we would have tried breakfast as we generally like eating at least one meal at a FS property when we stay. We agree that prices here are high, but we also recognize that most hotels of this caliber in New York are similarly priced. We generally visit NY at least once a year and we're looking forward to making a return visit to the Four Seasons New York - highly recommended.

“Nice place for the money.” We great a great rate, nice corner room, quick and easy check in, no complaints. Our room was ready, clean; we dropped our bags and headed out in NYC! The hotel is in a great location, walking distance to just about everything. There was a bit of street news in the morning but you are just about in the center of town. The only drawback was no room service for breakfast. They did offer a breakfast buffet but nothing in the room in the morning. Otherwise, they had everything else and the fridge and microwave were a plus. The staff was very pleasant.

“Very nice property on the Riverwalk” Stayed here for a quick weekend getaway to San Antonio. As others have said, this is a great choice if you wish to be in the center of the Riverwalk action. All of the staff I encountered were extremely courteous. Was given a very nice welcome upon arrival at the front desk, and was provided with a nice king room on the top floor that looked out over the Riverwalk. Despite facing the river, it was very quiet at night! The rooftop pool, though a bit small, is a great place to wind down and relax. We were also provided with complimentary breakfasts at the hotel, and the buffet had everything you could wish for, including an omelet station, and chilling drawers for the fresh fruit. Great experience, nicely remodeled. Would stay here again anytime!

“One Of The Very Best Hyatt Hotels” We had a one night stay recently. As a Hyatt Diamond member, we were upgraded to an Executive Suite, which consisted of a separate bedroom and living room. This is one of the very finest hotels we have stayed at. Everything about it is clean and contemporary. Despite being in the center of a busy airport, we never heard a sound. The room was beautiful and had interesting electronic shades; when we left the room, they automatically closed to keep out heat and when we returned they automatically opened-- very cool ! The front desk area is beautifully done and makes you feel like you're at a very luxury, guest focused hotel- which it is ! The well staffed concierge desk is adjoining and they personally print out your boarding passes. If you're flying on AA, this is the place to be. Just press "terminal" on the elevator keypad, get out and turn left and walk less than 2 minutes and you are at American Airlines terminal D check-in counters. No matter what terminal you are departing from, you can check in your bags at those desks. We did so and then returned to our room for another hour. But if you want to get to your gate, just go through the adjacent security checkpoint and if your flight is at another terminal, just hop on the Skylink which is right past security and you'll be close to your gate within a few minutes. As this Grand Hyatt doesn't have a Grand/Regency Club, we received complimentary breakfast in the restaurant. The restaurant was beautiful and the service impeccable. The breakfast selections were just outstanding. I can't recommend this hotel more highly. While their rates are somewhat higher than other hotels off-airport, the location, quality, and ease of this hotel make it well worthwhile.

“Very Nice Stay” Beautiful hotel, wonderful location. Really enjoyed it. The room was huge. They let me stay late. I would definitely stay here again. One star less than perfect because of the small drain flies in the shower.

“Great Room Second Time Around” My family and I had stayed at the Doubletree a few years ago when we took the Ohio Bar Exam. The room was very spacious which was great because my in-laws met us to watch our daughter while my husband and I took the Bar. Last year while we were in Columbus for an event we stayed at the Hilton and I really wasn't that impressed with the room so when we had to return back to Columbus in December '04 I decided to try the Doubletree again because the Hilton was so expensive. The room was still great (my in-laws met us again to watch two kids while we were gone). The only drawback is that there is no pool. If you want to use a pool you have to pay for a one-day pass to an athletic club. I would have considered taking my kids there but I don't think the club was even open on Saturday. This was disappointing to the kids but there are two TVs in the room so they were satisfied to hang out and watch TV in the bedroom while the rest of us hung out in the living area.

“Excellent Hotel” I stayed for one night. I was upgraded to a very nice suite. The hotel has a free happy hour from 4-6 pm (unusual for Hilton) The location is great, nice outdoor firepiits/pool. Staff was all great. I was very impressed, especially for the price. Check my other reviews, I rarely give a 5.

“Both sides are right” My wife and I had business in Manhatten and I picked the 70 Park Avenue because of its great location and the many positive reviews on Tripadvisor. I did notice the negative reviews, and had some reservations, but went for it. My experience during May 2005 was that both the postive and the negative comments were right. The good news: the staff is very courteous, knowledgeable and helpful. Ask for something and it happens right now. Even the bellman gave us a great recommendation for dinner. The rooms are appointed tastefully, with feather beds, Villeroy and Boch sinks, glass tiled showers and hugh flat-panel TVs with sound systems. The bad news: the rooms are small and noisy. The latter is common in Manhatten because of traffic noise in the concrete canyons. But, at 39th and Park Ave. it is very noisy indeed because of some sort of road excavation that the city has covered with huge metal plates. CLANG every time a bus or truck goes by. Room 1005, our first, was a corner room in which this was unbearable. In addition, that room was so small as to be unmanageable for two. The closet, for example, consisted of an 18 inch wide opening. The bath room was so small that the toilet was flush against a wall heater so that one had to sit sideways on it. Not sure how that would work with the heater on. We requested a room change which was accomplished while we were out. Room 1216, two and one-half floors up (yes), was bigger, had an adequate armoire and a bathroom which, while not spacious, was big enough for use. Although quieter, we still heard the CLANG in the night. I like the Kimpton chain, but as I have said in other Tripadvisor reviews, not all Kimptons are created equal. We won't go back the the 70 Park Avenue. But, after New York, we went the Washington and stayed at the Monaco which was about as good as it gets.

“Great hotel, super location” Was in New York for the 5 Boro bike ride and to see a few Broadway shows. The location was awesome, overlooked Time square, walking distance to everything. The guest room were very comfortable and normal size vs. some New York hotels with small rooms. Other than a few people in the lounge, staff was great. Would highly recommend this hotel.

“Fine But Not Outstanding” Room was fine, club lounge (including breakfast) was fine, service was fine, everything was fine--just nothing outstanding. Note that I am a Gold member, and the hotel wasn't very crowded, but I was given what seemed to me a very standard room.

“Stuck in Detroit from missed connection, great place to stay at moments notice!” Missed a connecting flight, had to spend night in Detroit. Was concerned the hotel may be loud from aircraft. I did not hear one jet while there. Room was nice, clean, comfy, and quiet. Had room service dinner and breakfast, all was incredible. :) Hotel is what you can expect from a nice Westin. Also, they have a security gate after 7am, you can use if you have your boarding pass already, and do not have to check luggage, which can help speed things up a bit.

“Will be great hotel when they have more experience” The Omni Dallas (at the convention center) is a gorgeous hotel both inside and out. I understand that I was part of the first convention group that has used this hotel so they're still doing their "shake down" cruise. However, they need to ramp it all up more quickly than it is now. Good points: Great customer service lovely lobby TV in bathroom mirror (!) quiet rooms fast elevators great ambience good business center Points that REALLY need to be worked on: Lighting in hotel room is abysmal. I know it's a green hotel but very hard to work in or even navigate the hotel room with the lighting. I heard many, MANY people talk about this on the elevator. ... Speaking of the elevator, if I had to hear that cheery elevator quasi british/australian voice say "going up" or "going down" one more time, I was going to go postal. I would have gladly had the elevator plummet to the ground rather than hear that voice one more time. I wasn't the only one complaining, it was THE talk of whomever was in the elevator at any given time Only 2 little towel hooks in the bathroom-no towel bars. If you REALLY want to follow green guidelines, you need someplace to hang your towels up so they don't get washed daily. This is especially important if you are sharing the room with a non-family member. The hooks couldn't hold a wash cloth without it falling off. The water in the shower was never CLOSE to being as hot as the bathroom faucet. I complained about this 3 times and the water only got marginally better. Nowhere near the heat of the faucet. I think this could be solved by taking off the shower faceplate and moving the heat off the safety setting. The customer service was great in both the hotel and restaurants, but the timeliness of getting food ordered, receiving it, getting a bill, having the bill picked up etc. etc was frankly lousy. MAJOR training needs to occur for the food servers, busser's etc. The hotel employees also need to know the hotel better. I was waiting for a friend who said they were in the bar. When I went into the sports bar and didn't see them, the hostess told me they were the only bar in the hotel. WRONG, there are 4. Took me another 10 minutes of wondering and several texts until I found my friends. The housekeeper didn't know where the fitness room was, the business center employee didn't know you could pay and print off usps labels in the business center and then just take the mail down to the front desk to be sent out via usps NO SIDEWALKS! You either walk on the very busy driveways or you walk thru grass

“Historical - yes; Luxury - no” We stayed two nights over the 4th of July holiday weekend at this hotel. One of the shortcomings of this property was obvious when we pulled up to the curb to check in – the valet parking situation is lousy for this grade of hotel. The interior driveway is closed and since the crew was not prepared for the rush of Friday arrivals, we had to wait in a line amongst the street traffic for our turn. There was no one to help us with our bags but once inside, check-in was professional and prompt. However, in spite of my SPG status and because I had negotiated their lowest rate, we were assigned a NS King on the somewhat shabby lowest level. The room was very small and even thought the hotel has been updated recently, it already appears dated and worn. The bathroom had limited counter space and has a modern bowl sink which seems out of place in this historic setting. We had to run the AC unit on the noisy high setting to get the room moderately cool. I understand that this hotel is used for high profile special event dinners and receptions, but I am at a loss as to why. One of my main complaints about this property is that the hotel lobby environment is not conducive to hanging out and the receception/concierge desks are back in the corners so there is no interaction with the desk staff as the guests enter and leave the hotel. On a positive note, housekeeping was thorough and offered a nice turn down service. As far as location, the hotel is conveniently located on the edge of the Gaslamp District, but it is surrounded by dilapidated and abandoned buildings. Every one that we came into contact with was pleasant and helpful, but there are too many negatives to ignore. Considering all aspects of my disappointment with this hotel, next time I visit San Diego, I would choose the Omni, Marriott or Hilton by the Convention Center or even stay at one of the beach communities like La Jolla.

“very good” What you expect from a Hampton Inn Pretty good overall, standard breakfast with omelettes etc... Bus route direct to downtown stops by the hotel Nearby QFC grocery store and restaurants in the area. Walking distance (5 minutes) from the Space needle park. Difficult to walk in the area as roads are blocked for construction The room was good, as what you typically find at Hamptons Friendly front desk staff Good concierge service – they kept our luggage for more than 12 hours prior our trip to the airport (tip: use bus and transit train for a few $)

“Perfect Location” Stayed 3 nights between Christmas & New Years. Nice hotel, best location on Riverwalk. Jim Cullum's band (from Live on the Riverwalk on NPR) plays here - highly recommend. First time in San Antonio and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Lots of nice restaurants to choose from on Riverwalk. Be sure to visit El Mercado (Mexican Market) within walking distance.

“Great rate, great location, great service.” Stayed a night at this hotel. We came to San Antonio without reservation, This was the best place we could find that was not sold out. What a pleasant surprise. Great location, service, rates and room. Would stay here again.

“Francisco Bay Inn - a good value” If all you need is a clean room in a great location, this is the place for you. The room comes with a small fridge and a microwave and there are little markets nearby. The bus stop is about 2 blocks away and can take you to most of the tourist sights. Fisherman's Wharf is about a 20 minute walk away. The rooms here are on the small side but if you're not spending much time there, does it really matter? There is a small Italian restaurant nearby called the Cafe Lombard and the food is very good. Also, my daughter and I felt safe in this area. I would stay here again. I booked directly with the hotel and paid $114 per night USD in July 2005. Parking is free, a BIG plus.

“Horrible hotel- avoid at all costs” I stayed here for one night on business in October 2007 and have advised my company's travel agent never to book anyone here again. First, the room (like many in NYC these days) was $400! It was old, musty, and very small. The comforter was ripped in several places and the carpet was stained throughout the room. Service at the front desk was mediocre and the waitstaff at breakfast was rude. The breakfast itself was basic continental. I have stayed at many hotels in NYC so I know not to expect a view or much space, but for $400 this was a complete joke. Stay elsewhere!

“Meh” I had to book at this property because the hotel in which my conference was held was sold out. Location/Check-in First, be very careful and ensure you want to stay at this hotel. Their cancellation policy is a 24 hour one, not a day of, like most Hilton properties I've stayed. I tried to cancel same day, and they weren't having that. The hotel is a bit far out for my tastes. Is a good 15 minute hike to the nearest Metro (Dupont) and some of the streets are a bit isolated at night, which I don't love. There is a Hopkins University branch very close by so there were a decent amount of students on the streets, which made me feel a little safer. Lots of restaurants on Mass or New Hampshire, so definitely can walk to eat. Check-in was fine and they accommodated my room requests. Even got a free upgrade, which was nice. Free hot cookie at check-in and staff was pretty friendly. There is a restaurant on site, however I didn't eat any meals there so wouldn't be comfortable rating it. Wasn't able to check out the fitness center or business center. Room The hotel does show some age. From the elevator to the hallway to the room itself. Needed a little sprucing up. Because I had a suite, I can only rate the suite, I'm not sure how their standard rooms are. The suite had a nice area to store beverages, drinks and a coffee maker. They gave me two free bottles of water and some snacks as well. The living room had a sofa, ottoman and desk and there was a table and chairs as well. The TV was decent, had closed captioning and good amount of channels. Bed was very comfortable and they offered different types of pillows, however the linens could have been much cleaner. Alarm clock was fine, however this is the 2nd time in a row that my alarm clock at a Hilton Property had no back-light on the alarm clock so in the dark you have no idea what time it is. Bed was firm enough and slept fine. Wake up call was right on time. The bathroom was absolutely huge. Almost oddly huge. There was a regular toilet (that seemed to have some power issues, barely flushed) and the bathroom also featured a bidet, which I was scared to use because it didn't look all the clean/new. Never used one before and was at least interesting. Shower had decent water pressure and towels were decently clean. Iron and iron board were fine, nothing super impressive. A lot of the light switches were nasty dirty, which is a really basic housekeeping issue, need some magic erasers or something. Overall, the one-room suite was very large and was definitely big enough for more than one person. Enjoyed the free beverages and snacks, however housekeeping left a bit to the imagination.

“Excellent location and nice hotel” Right near the 16th St mall with plenty of shopping and walking to do during the day and then a vibrant nightlife takes over at night, with tons of pedestrians and merry makers. The location can't be beat. The hotel itself is nice and compact. I enjoyed having business meetings that took five minutes to get to a few floors down from my room, instead of wandering through endless corridors searching for a meeting room like in some other hotels. The room is a good size, comfortable, and it is nice to be able to open the window a little to get some air. The light-blocking curtains are very effective! The fitness center is bare bones but they give out free magazines to read and wow, it has an indoor basketball court! I don't think I've seen that at a hotel before. The pool, although I didn't use it, looked amazing, with partial indoor and outdoor sections. It's on a roof which makes it special. A nice touch with the live piano every happy hour and evening. It can get a little loud when trying to deal with the front desk which is nearby, but otherwise nice. All in all a good stay, no complaints.

“Great hotel” This is one of a number of Club Quarters hotels in NYC. I have stayed at several of these, and there is consistency of service and facilities. It well serves the business community that surrounds Wall Street. It is very quiet at night, and the immediate subway access still gives it wonderful access to all the Manhattan offers. The rooms are not large, but by no means claustrophobic. They are furnished very comfortably, and there is a great working desk and space. The rooms have a very nice modern ambiance, and provide a nice retreat after a busy day. The free, refillable bottles of water are a plus; there is a guest closet cupboard on the floor where guest can get additional stuff they need in the room. WiFi access is free, connects quickly and works well. I like the automatic checkin, yet front desk staff are always so polite and pleasant when you interact with them. A little noise appears to travel between walls, but this was not a problem. The old airconditioning unit was a little noisy. I would certainly stay here again

“Great hotel - good location - problems with breakfast” Great hotel - nice, comfortable, large, clean rooms. Location is great - good in the business area and restaurants and shopping within walking distance. The only downfall I have is the breakfast line in the mornings. It is not set-up well and I had to stand in line for 30 minutes to get the buffet-type, ready to eat food. The reason the line was so long was because it's only one line for ready to eat and cook to order food. So you had to wait in line for cook to order, even if you did not want it. It was ridiculous. Other than that, super nice hotel and highly recommended!

“The best so far” I selected this hotel based on the reviews and I am glad that I did so. The location is very good, with access to public transport and taxi any time. The desk and bell staff are extremely polite and gentle compared to many hotels I have been to in the US. The rooms are sufficiently spacious and greatly decorated. Everything looked new as of early 2012. The lobby is clean and shiny, and guests receive a personal attention. The room keeping staff would leave you hand written messages of greetings everyday, which is an excellent idea to make you feel at home.I didn't have a chance to eat at the restaurant but I think I wish there were more restaurants inside the hotel. Of course many bars and restaurants are within walking distance.Overall I had a pleasing experience.

“Its a decent hotel - but not as good as other Kimptons” I was slightly dissapiointed with the hotel against other Kimptons I have stayed at in the past, it just didnt have that real luxury feel and refinement, that said, it is a very good hotel in a decent location for the main points around Fishermans Wharf. The service was ok but not overwhelming, the rooms were nicely appointed but didnt really make the most of the original features, it did feel like square boxes and its the first hotel I've stayed at where the bedroom door only open outwards (bit like Alcatraz!) However, for Fishermans Wharf and access to the Cable Car at Hyde Street, you can not fault it.

“Centralized location and everything I needed” OK, I'm a bit biased, as I am a Marriott Rewards holder and specifically love the Residence Inn brand. What can I say? I like free breakfast and having my own kitchen regardless of whether I end up using it or not. I used my rewards points for my stay, but also checked the online pricing, which was overall reasonable. Be advised that parking is $10 per night with in/out privileges. This isn't overall too bad price-wise as compared to staying in the Gaslamp Quarter, but if you were to stay a few miles down the 8, up the 5 or up the 163 parking would be free. I had a few complaints about this particular hotel: 1. My front stove burner did not work and a coffee carafe was slightly broken 2. The layout of the hotel is slightly confusing 3. There was only wired internet and no wifi. 4. I had to pay for parking As usual with Residence Inns, there is a business center and a workout room, as well as a basketball and a BBQ area. This hotel did have a larger pool area than usual with one large pool and two smaller pools. There is also a pantry area where you can buy some more groceries if you need to. This hotel seemed very family friendly (probably because its in Hotel Circle where most of the families go). There was a hotel reception (with free beer/wine) in the evenings, however, the snacks were all gone when I got there and there was a good 15 more minutes. Breakfast was good for a free breakfast with more than average hot items. There were biscuits and gravy, french toast, 4 do it yourself waffle stations, sausages, 2 types of scrambled eggs, oatmeal, yogurt, sliced melon, grapefruit, cottage cheese, bagels/pastries/toast, and lots of beverage options (juice, coffee, hot cocoa, tea, soda and including the more unusual horchata and orange bang fountain drinks). The breakfast area was very crowded and the staff was on-task keeping the food replenished. I will say that it was quite a zoo even though the dining area was sufficiently large. The hotel was smart enough to be situated a bit closer to the hill and thus away from the freeway, so there was no noise. The room was nice and the bed firm and unmemorable (which is a good thing). Location-wise it can't be beat: close to downtown, balboa park, the zoo, gaslamp, sea world and Mission Bay. It is also very close to shopping at Fashion Valley and Mission Valley. The staff was nice, but did not allow me to extend my checkout time (which knocks them down one rating). I would definitely stay at this hotel again and would suggest it to others.
“Good business hotel” I haved stayed here several times before. It is a great easy to access location off of 101 south First Street exit. It is great for conferences or other business.

“Great location, accommodations, service” My husband and I moved to the Omni at the last minute after checking into a different property the same day of our arrival and being quite dissatisfied. We called over to the Omni and they were perfectly helpful in arranging our move to their hotel. We had a speedy check in and were pleased with customer service from start to finish. The valet is pricey, but the valet staff always had our car waiting for us when we arrived downstairs and they always left little bottles of water for us. The location of the Omni is perfect for exploring the Gaslamp Quarter. We were on the 17th floor, so whatever noise issues other reviewers have complained about never bothered us. We ordered room service a few times (I highly recommend the apple pie) and it was always prompt and correct to our order. I have a hard time enjoying hotel stays anymore since we purchased a TempurPedic for our home, but I loved the bed and linens at the Omni! We had a fantastic view of downtown. The hotel pool is heated and small for the number of people that frequent it, but its still a nice place to hang out and get a drink. My husband and I moved hotels because our original hotel was crowded and busy. The Omni was still busy, but had a more adult feel and we are eternally glad we moved. I would recommend the Omni time and again--it was a great "home station" from which we explored San Diego.

“Respectable value for a midtown hotel” Our visit to midtown/theater district was centered around seeing Broadway shows and dining at Patsy's & at the Oyster Bar in Grand Central Station. The Hotel Mela was a convenient home base for the trip. It is walking distance to the theater district and to Grand Central. While our room was small, we've stayed in smaller places in Manhattan that were not as well kept, and we experienced excellent service from the hotel. We booked through a link on travelzoo, which gave us a $200/night rate & included a welcome gift. Check-in/out was a breeze with their polite and efficient staff. There were no issues with the cleanliness of the hotel, noise from the surrounding area or inside the hotel. The small rooms are attractively furnished, with comfortable bedding. You can get a good night's sleep in this hotel. While certainly not a luxury hotel, the Mela is a fine option for the frugal visitor to Manhattan. Centrally located, it's a stylish "middle class" hotel. For those who come to midtown with a car, there is a Hippodrome garage just a block east of the Mela that gives you 12 hours overnight for $12. A much better value than the $40+ a night for the garage adjacent to the hotel entrance... FYI

“Adequate, Good Price” I stayed at the Jurys Normandy for three nights because it was less expensive than virtually all of the other hotels anywhere near DuPont Circle during the time of my stay. I had had some hesitation because a review had mentioned construction noise, and there is indeed construction on the adjacent building, but I heard nothing during the mornings and nights I spent there; can't say about the rest of the day. The rooms (I was in two during the course of my stay, although not because of any problem with the first one) were perfectly adequate, although unspectacular; I'd say they were on a par with the many other mid-priced hotel rooms I've stayed in around the country. The beds were fine, the TV and everything else worked, the shower was good, and everything was clean. The front desk was helpful. My only hesitations about staying there again: (1) it's a 15 minute walk to DuPont Circle, downhill going and uphill returning, and this isn't really a problem but all other things being equal I might stay a little closer, since I don't like to take cabs if I can avoid it; and (2) the hotel has virtually no facilities other than the room. No pool, no health club, no restaurant. They do serve a continental breakfast, for which they charge about $6.00 -- not exorbitant, but seems a little chintzy when you're spending hundreds of dollars at the place. Although there are restaurants not too far away, it would be nice to be able to get something to eat at your hotel after checking in at 8 or 9 pm without going on an expedition. But again, no real problems.

“Amazing location and value” What a great experience. The hotel is a short walk from Universal Studios (or take the free van) and 15 minutes from Burbank Airport. If you are going to the Studios or having a company meeting or incentive this is the place. The facilites are tops. I am a Hilton Diamond member and was treated very well. However, if you do not have HHonors status you will still be treated like a king. The hotel has one of the best buffet breakfest I have every had for under $20.00. They also have a $15.00 meal deal from 4pm to 6pm midweek. I had Seafood Soup loaded with seafood, Prime rib with veggies and potatoes, and Cheesecake for only $15.00. I have to say...I love this hotel.

“Great location and staff, needs an update” I recently stayed one night at the Sutton Place for business. I chose Sutton Place for it's location - walking distance to my dinner meeting. The location is perfect, and the staff was very friendly. The rooms were clean and nice-sized. However - the rooms (especially the bathrooms) were so outdated it was almost comical! White Formica cabinetry and counter top, white porcelain fixtures, black and grey tile... the Sutton Place either needs to embrace their kitschy look, call themselves "retro" and up-charge, or they need an update.

“Best NYC Hotel experience in a LONG time” I travel to NYC 5-6 times a year on business. I usually stay towards midtown in the Royalton, Algonquin or the Iroquois to be close tot the office. This time I was looking for a change, and a good deal. I had heard some good things about the Standard, and though I had a poor experience in the Los Angeles Standard I decided to check the new NYC location our none-the-less. The room was perfectly appointed. Great bathroom complete with a shower featuring a natuaral rain style shower head - nice! The floor to ceiling window along one entire wall was amazing, provided great views, and made the room feel a little more spacious. The bed was top notch comfort - great linens and pillows. My room featured a small couch and table that were perfect for working. Its rare to stay in a hotel room that feels like home. I loved this room - to the point that I was actually a little sad to check out. I love the little diner in the front of the hotel - perfect place to grab a great breakfast before starting your day. Try the steel cut oatmeal with raisins - awesome on a cold NY morning. The only tricky part is the locations, while its quite beautiful with the highline and the river right there, it is a ways from the subway, meaning more cabs than I usually like. But in the end the hotel was so perfect Iplan to stay ythre every chance i get...
“Very nice place in the best part of town” Still a very nice place to stay. Good rooms and very good bathrooms. Friendly staff. Great restaurant. Super location. Only problem - the closets are tiny!!

“Great location for neighborhood vibe” We have stayed in this property many times and on two occasions this summer. The location is downtown and the bike and walking paths with river views run for miles along the Hudson and begin in this area. It is a perfect spot to bond with the Statue of Liberty! We like the downtown area because it is quite and has a neighborhood feel. The hotel is close to Tribeca, the Meat Packing district and Soho. There is a large movie theatre just blocks away and many wonderful restaurants and the rest of NYC is only a cab ride or a subway ride away. The hotel has come a long way since it began it's renovation. The rooms are fully up to speed, but the elevators are a different story. They are being refurbished and in the mean time are extremely slow. The concierge was okay at best ( we live in Northern New Jersey and are in the city all the time, so for us it did not matter much). Hotel staff were just going through the motions and security did not seem to be around ( which on our last stay over a year ago very much was). The concierge lounge was very nice and breakfast was fine there. It was nice having a Starbucks inthe lobby. We would stay here again for the views and because we like the general area, but would like to see hotel management instill a "can-do" attitude with it's employees. We will wait until the elevator refurbishment is complete!

“Big Rooms, Convenient Location” I stay at this hotel on most visits to Houston, usually because I can get a decent rate on Hotwire, plus the free Internet. The rooms are large, with a small bar area with refrigerator. The entire hotel is no non-smoking, which is nice (for a non-smoker). It is located within walking distance to the Galleria, but getting in and out with a car can be time-consuming because you have to access from the service road, right at the off-ramp from the freeway to Westheimer - one of the most congested areas of Houston. The parking garage can get full, and there are no other places to park in the area if you can't get a space there. The hotel is beginning to show its age, so don't expect too much. And whenever you deal with desk staff, make a note of names, because they may tell you something that isn't policy. I booked a room for two nights but was unable to make it the first night. I called to let them know, and the desk person said "No problem". But when I arrived on the second day they had deleted the entire reservation. Luckily, they had a room available, but told me I should have called. I told them I did , and they were very nice about it. But I believe if their had been no rooms available, things could have gotten ugly. Overall, I like this hotel, but it's not as nice as other Sheraton Suites I have stayed in.

“Good, convenient, if undifferentiated large hotel” This is a large, relatively undifferentiated hotel, well located in the heart of downtown on the main shopping street. It is quite acceptable and comfortable, if unmemorable. It is particularly convenient for events in the conference centre to which it is attached. By the way, it's no fault of the hotel, but the conference center itself is a confusing rabbit-warren. Get clear directions from the concierge if that's your destination!

“tiny rooms” I accompanied my husband on a business trip to Houston and we stayed at the Club Quarters. He was booked there by his corporate travel department. This would not have been our choice. The rooms were modern and clean, but extremely tiny. It reminded me of a European hotel. The rooms were not even big enough for any of them to have king-sized beds. It is very definitely designed as a business hotel only. The rooms have only enough towels, etc. for one person. As other posters mentioned, the hotel has only showers and not even a dresser in the room. There is not even anywhere to put a suitcase, except on the floor at the end of the bed. The desk clerk looked at us like we were from Mars when my husband requested 2 keys, and she realized I was not another person checking in alone, but rather with him. In addition, our room had a lovely view of a brick wall. I will say that the staff was all very helpful and friendly. This hotel would be good for a person traveling alone for business, as it has a decent downtown location, but it definitely not for anyone else.

“An older proprety, showing its age” The range of room types and services at Hampton Inns is narrow and this property is at the low end of that continuum. The rooms are dated and the property a bit claustrophobic. It does have the advantage of convenience to the airport (and I-10 for people just passing through). This property needs a renovation/modernization. Otherwise, it competes against the non-chain motels in the area and not the chains.

“i liked this hotel” I stay in NY a lot for work - in fact, last week i stayed a block away at the W. While the W is hip, my room was a closet. Not here at the Hyatt. My family was upgraded to a suite (for no charge) and we had a beautiful view of the local area. I thought the personality of the hotel was great. They have a nice lounge with complimentary beverages and an easy, laid back attitude. i will definitely consider staying here for work even though i am Gold at Starwoods. That should say something....

“Nice hotel in NYC” I was at this hotel w/ 3 other girlfriends on a whirlwind trip. It was our 1st time here & we came in during the heatwave that NYC was having at that time. The hotel made our stay nice & bearable. Every1 was nice- from the front desk ladies to the bellhops. The lobby is on the 2nd floor. You can see a photo of the lobby w/a ivy covered glass roof in the professional photos provided here. It was nice. We didn't get to go to their restaurant but hopefully next time we will. We had a double double room and it suited our needs. I liked the hard wood floors and solid white bathroom. Loved the bowl sink but the common pull handle toilet-not so much. When we were checking out, the front desk associate encouraged us to visit the rooftop terrace. It was nice and had an ok view. No big sights to see from there. There's some places to eat in the area, there's a CVS on the adjacent corner, and Columbus Circle is just around the corner. The only issues was that the hallways were dreary & humid. They need a brighter color of paint on the walls as gray made it dreary and drab looking. There is some renovations going on currently. You will know with all of the scaffolding on the outside of the building. The hotel name is not too visible- there's only 'H's on some of the scaffolding banners. We didn't hear any construction noises from our room thankfully. In all, this was a nice hotel and my friends and I might come back here again when we head back to NYC.

“Reliable conference hotel” Attended a conference at the hotel that included visits to Capitol Hill so the location was convenient. There aren't many restaurants in this area however. The property is well maintained and my room was clean and comfortable. The rooms are small and the bathroom, while adequate for one would have been crowded with two people. I rate it average in that there wasn't anything that really stood out as above the norm for DC chain hotels.

“Good, but unfortunately, not great” We got the room on Priceline as part of a romantic getaway weekend, and was happy we got the Drake, but were weary that the hotel may have been past its prime. It may be. We were given a room facing the HVAC system, and which featured a size "full" bed, or something smaller than our bedroom at home. We think the room could have fita king size. The room was clean and the bathroom was well appointed, though the shower head hit we at the shoulders (I am 6'3"), and was difficult to manipulate. The room did seem stuffy, and the thermostat never seemed to get to the temperature we were set at. The service we encountered was all good, and the common areas are beautiful. Room service, though pricey, was quick, and when they brought the wrong thing, corrected their mistake even quicker.

“Overall O.K. with Areas that need Improvement” I just returned from a two night stay at the Herald Square Hotel. I was housed in room 500 which faces 31st Street. While my stay overall was satisfactory I would be negligent if I failed to mention some significant observations. My room had not yet been renovated. It was quite small, as expected, but would not accomodate more than one comfortably. The "surface' was quite clean but with no effort observed hair on the toilet paper dispenser, dirt and debris on the bed skirt and laundered stains on the comforter cover. The mattress does have a completely insulated mattress which is positive if one wants to avoid bed bugs. What became annoying was the void of any electrical outlets anywhere near the bed. The alarm clock sits on the desk...5 steps from the bed. The lights above the bed are on a dimmer but you must stretch completely accross the bed or physically get out of bed to adjust it. The t.v. is on top of the hutch making the bed the only place to watch it. The a/c temperature is "regulated" or "not cold enough" as I prefer to say. The a/c was just loud enough to drown out the street noise but not quite loud enough to eliminate the fire truck siren blasting from the fire house a couple hundred feet away. Even with ear plugs it was VERY noisy. The shower was satisfactory but a complete crap shoot as to water temperature which changes with each flush, shower and sink use. The hotel does provide some very nice soap and shampoo. While the staff was very friendly and helpful the setting is not warm or welcoming. You get buzzed in from people who sit behind a plastic cage. The entire lobby area is reminicint of an icky 1970's pay by the day or week hotel, which it may have been back in the day. They are clearly trying to remedy this situation but haven't quite succeeded. The history of the hotel is very cool. Very close to the subway and restaurants. I paid $179.00 plus tax per night. It was closer to a $120.00 a night room. I can't say that in a pinch I wouldn't stay there again but maybe in an updated room.

“Tolles, modernes Hotel in zentraler Lage” Das Hotel wirkt wie frisch renoviert oder sogar erst gebaut. Die Zimmer sind super modern und sauber und haben sogar Parkett Boden. Im obersten Stockwerk gibt es eine Rooftop Bar, die Aussicht ist allerdings nichts besonderes. Da wuerde ich eher das 230Fifth empfehlen. Die Preise koennen es zwar in sich haben, aber das Hotel ist auf jeden Fall mein Favori in der Ecke.
“Really nice hotel with comfortable beds...” Really nice hotel with comfortable beds. I was happy with everything.

“perfectly fine.” Did not have any problems at this hotel, but the bathroom is tiny and the room is a little small-ish and bland. Excellent location (although there really isn't an easy Metro station near it -- you'll walk quite a few blocks to a station, but it is still doable), great restaurants all around, and DC is at your doorstep. Staff were friendly and helpful. The lobby felt cramped but not a problem. Overall, you should feel satisfied with a stay at this Doubletree.

“Great location but average service.” Stayed here a week ago for 5 nights, booked through Trailfinders, the location is excellent on 6th Avenue and only 4 blocks from Central Park, 10 blocks from Times Square(1/2 mile). Check in was quick but unfortunately given the wrong room with only 1 bed, this was corrected to a room on 23rd floor at the far end of floor. Room was surprisingly big and clean, bathroom was bijou, no noise from the streets, but could hear chat from neighbouring rooms. Didn't use the Restaurants as breakfast was $35, very busy for breakfast but quiet at dinner. There are better options for food close to the hotel, such as 7th Avenue, though it is pricey as this is Manhattan. Tip for cheaper food go to Chinatown at Canal Street or Flushing Main Street where breakfast for 2 cost less than $10 and dinner for 2 for $20. Had to use the hotel gym once when there was bad weather, it costs $15, don't be fooled by the photos, it is small so not enough equipment, a better gym option was the YMCA at Central Park West, 10mins walk away. The staff didn't smile much, you get the feeling you were just a number, typical of big chains, also opportunity to nickle and dime you, such as leaving your bags for storage, it is $3:50 per item. Surely this should be free, is it an American thing, Asian hotles look after your bags for free as standard. Big tip for travelling around is to use the Subway and buy a weekly card for $28, excellent value.

“amazing stay” Stayed here for one night for my husband's birthday. We were upgraded to a fabulous suite - probably the nicest hotel room I have ever stayed in. Huge windows that overlooked the harbor and Statue of Liberty. Our room (#317) was spotless, tastefully decorated, and like I said had many huge windows that showcased this spectacular view.
