We received not one but two bottles of complimentary champagne (one was from our sweet housekeeper Digna). I found the staff to be so nice and attentive, and they all seemed very genuine about it. The fitness center was a good size, open 24 hrs. Drinks at the bar Rise were great and the view from the 14th floor of the sunset was very special. We had no problem getting a cab in the evening and the next morning there were plenty of cabs lined up just wating for guests. We walked a pleasant 25 minutes or so home from dinner in Tribeca on Friday night, so that is not a bad option either. Overall I think this hotel is great and for $370 a good deal for NYC. I loved the area - it is totally different than midtown and that is what we were looking for.

“World’s Best View (if you don’t mind hammering at 6:30 AM)” It’s almost unfair to be writing a review of a hotel in the middle of construction, but insofar as the Millennium Bostonian is in the game of renting their rooms out to the public, I suppose that my experience counts. Here’s what I can say about the Millennium Bostonian. For the leisure traveler who wants to be in the heart of Boston, I can’t think of a better hotel to be in. After seeing all of the lousy economic news and knowing that it meant that hoteliers would start discounting like crazy, I waited until the last minute to book a midweek room. When my 50% off rate at the Westin Waterfront still ended up being $225, I went for the Millennium, knowing from the Tripadvisor reviews that it was under construction. My $200 rate would be discounted to $150 if I made my reservation non-refundable, which I was willing to gamble on. However, I did splurge and spend an extra $30 to be on the better side of the building, and I sent a little note asking if I could get a good view of Fanueil Hall. All of this for what I presumed would be a $400/night room once the renovation was complete, and I was again willing to take a chance on the noise. That extra $30 was the best money that I spent during my trip to Boston. The room was absolutely outstanding. I was in a corner room on the 6th floor with a balcony (which was equipped with a lovely flower box) overlooking Fanueil Hall and Quincy Market, and we could see the Custom House and the Old State House as well. For my 10 year old, this couldn’t have been better. Now the noise which didn’t bother me was the music, drum circles and general hubbub from the streets below, and that pretty much died out by 10 pm. The location was ideal in another way because you are so centrally located to everything in Boston, particularly because you can walk to any of three different subway lines. We were also in one of the newly renovated rooms which were very nice. I would describe them as boutique hotel contemporary. Not way out there, but tasteful and refined. What I liked were the bigger-than-it-had-to-be-but-I’m-not-complaining flat screen TV, the comfortable bed and sheets and the seating furniture in general. The clock radio had an i-pod hook-up as well. One disappointment was the $9.95 that they wanted for wi-fi access. The highlight of the room, however, was the bathroom. I give the shower an A+; it’s one of the nicest I’ve used anywhere. My son who rarely takes showers actually took two in eight hours. The limestone tile and oversized shower area gave it a luxe feel, but the kicker was the Grohe hardware – a combination raintree showerhead with a separate hand washer. It took a little while for the water to heat up, but that’s probably because of the low occupancy. Other than the shower, the bathroom was a bit small, and they could’ve actually claimed some room where they have a closet so that there would be a place to put my toiletries down. As it stood, the sink was the width of the room so my bag went onto the floor. Another amusing part of the room was the toilet which had a suction so violently strong that it could probably take off a limb. Finally, they had these frosted glass sliding doors separating the bathroom from the bedroom, probably to make the bathroom seem bigger, but they’re tough to keep clean so you see all the spots. I didn’t mind the lack of a lobby or the fourth floor check-in. The areas which are being redone certainly needed it to get rid of the last vestiges of the motor lodge/rounded-high gloss-dorm room wood aesthetic. We didn’t try the restaurant since there were so many better options around. I didn’t really ask much of the hotel since that’s not why I was in Boston, but the service level seemed serviceable enough. Which takes me to the noise. I knew there would be noise, I’m someone who prefers a fan when they sleep because the noise puts me to sleep, but I have to say that I know of many other hotels that tell their contractors to not start until 8 AM when many guests could be sleeping, particularly those from the west coast who can’t fall asleep until 2 AM. I wouldn’t complain if the contractors worked until 8 or 9 PM because most people are out enjoying the city, but starting the hammering at 6:30 AM seems pretty ridiculous. So I was awakened by this huge vibration vaguely reminiscent of the 5.4 earthquake that we just had in Los Angeles, followed by incessant hammering, and not the loud whacks that my next door neighbor’s contractor back home uses at 7 AM to frame their McMansion. No, this was more of a “tap tap tap tap tap tap” with a 10 second to 2 minute delay, then more of the same, ad nauseum. Then housingkeeping came by at 8:13 AM, by which time the hammering was perfectly acceptable, in my book, other than the fact that my son was still asleep, but fortunately the paper thin doors tipped me off and I opened the door just before the housekeeper knocked. What kind of housekeeping person comes by that early? In any event, it allowed me to see that the contractor had ripped open the ceiling a few feet outside our room. I said “Good Morning” to the tapper, and he tapped right back at me. In the end, tapping or no tapping, I would definitely stay at the Millennium again because the positives definitely outweigh the negatives. What I will say is that that I wouldn’t take my wife during construction because I know she would be furious based on how she feels when the contractor next door gets a little over eager at 6:53. Also, I wonder what happens to the Millennium when the new Ames hotel which I can also see from my window opens up (Ames, of the Hudson/NY, Mondrian/LA uber-swank fame). But for me to be in the heart of Boston with everything at my fingertips, the Millennium is near perfect.

“Big rooms, convenient location, it works!” Recommended. This convenient mid-town location is an easy shot to Times Square and 5th Avenue mainstream areas. Check-in was swift and uneventful. The lobby area is smallish and clearly not a hangout. Rooms appeared to be generally large, floors are small with only ~ 10 rooms per floor. My corner room was exceptional in size. Bedding was comfortable and bath area in modern condition and OK illuminated. Considering mid-town location, rooms were fairly quiet (I was on 17), always ask for higher! Nice amentities. Each floor had only a handful of rooms and with 39 floors serviced by only 2 elevators, the wait time to go up/down can be lengthy. General condition of the property was only OK. Some signs of disrepair and various shades of gray in the décor didn’t help the atmosphere. Food for our conference and in the restaurants was very good as was the service. All in all – nothing not to recommend, depending upon your lodging price – either an exceptional value or over priced.

“Gut für eine Nacht” Nach einem langen Flug aus Europa an die Westküste finde ich es am angenehmsten, immer gleich in der Nähe des Flughafens zu schlafen, um so den Jet-Lag entgegenzuwirken. Das Holiday Inn war schon mehrmals meine Wahl, da es sehr leicht zu erreichen ist. Für diesen Zweck ist das Hotel auch mehr als ausreichend ausgestattet, einen längeren Aufenthalt würde ich aber nicht empfehlen. Die Zimmer sind geräumig und funktioniell, die Einrichtung aber sicherlich nicht die neuerste. Auch das Frühstück ist durchaus in Ordnung. Parkplätze gibt es ausreichend, und das Hotel ist leicht zu erreichen.

“Always comfortable” Still a comfortable hotel to stay at. Rooms are decent and resembles a typical Hyatt recent renovation property. The location is fantastic to the mall. Breakfast is a little expensive but you may find it is so filling you won't need lunch. I got my room + breakfast buffet for $140, a great value (Hyatt site, AAA rate).

“Not Recommended” Not the usual standard of Best Western. We paid £40 per room per night but it didn't meet my expectations after staying at other hotels in the same price range. It was conveniently located for Sunland Park Racetrack and Casino. The rooms were clean but the hallways could do with some attention. A lick of paint and new carpets would brighten the place up. The desk clerk was unattentive but the facilities, pool etc were adequate for a one night stay. I would try somewhere else if going to El Paso again.

“Fine for a night” The shuttle to & from the airport runs very regularly. This hotel does seem more reasonably priced than others serving LAX. The rooms include TV, clock/radio, iron/board, hairdryer, coffeemaker & a sofa/footstool. One slight aggravation is that there were enough coffee for four mugs, but only enough sugar/creamer for one mug. The area is not great with mainly offices/parking associated with the airport & lots of fast food outlets-Macdonalds, Denny's, Taco Bell, etc. I understand that there is a shuttle bus to the beach & a shopping centre but I found no sign of it during my visit. The hotel does serve bar meals & snacks. I did not eat there, but the prices seemed OK. The complmenatary breakfast is adequate, but they stop serving at 9.00. I would have thought it better to serve it later & allow guests to have a lie in before flights. There is a pool on the fourth floor where you can swim or just chill.

“A good choice.” Great staff, clean rooms, and a quiet location. You're just off the West end of the airport, but airplane noise is not an issue. The staff is friendly and helpful and rooms are clean. The only drawback: the internet, whether WiFi or wired, is HORRIBLE. All three of us in my group (different rooms scattered around the hotel) had the same experience. Bring your own air card.

“Confortável, mas longe de tudo.” Camas confortáveis, máquina de bebidas nos corredores e café da manhã americano. Atendimento razoável. Estacionamento e internet gratuitos. É possível sair do hotel e caminhar até o metrô durante uns 30min, mas é longe e passamos por locais bem esquisitos. Se você está de carro, tranquilo, pois à pé, anda-se muito e á noite, não recomendo sair do hotel andando. Local escuro e sem ninguém. Whashinton tem problema com estacionamento. Quando há, é muito caro.

“Good hotel. Could hear next room through the doors” It WAS a nice hotel. Couldn't ask for a better location. Across the street from the Architectural River tours, down one block from Millennium Park, down two blocks and across the bridge to the Magnificent Mile. Perfect location and great hotel did equal full of conference goers, weddings and families on vacation. If the people in the next room were close to the adjoining doors you could hear them talking, but since it isn't a party hotel it wasn't bad and all was quiet at night. But room felt new and very clean. Bed was very nice and comfortable. I was there for a conference in the same hotel. The basement conference rooms had huge pillars that obstructed the sight lines during some of the talks. Workout room was small and had barely any empty floor space for mats. For the price it should have had a pool. But otherwise it was a very good hotel.

“Excellent place, outstanding value” Very quiet, understated, elegant boutique hotel. Our queen room was small but well-appointed. Housekeeping was superb - as good as any property we've ever stayed at (which means that every time you leave the room for a while you return to find everything made up and every used item replaced). All staff were extremely friendly and helpful. We're big breakfast fans, and thought this hotel's breakfast was elegant, personalized, and fairly priced. All in all, a very pleasant place and a tremendous value, especially if you want to be in this part of town.

“Stay away, far away” When you first arrive at the Hudson and go up the escalator to the main lobby, you will likely be impressed by the decor. It is striking, even though the music from the hip bar area might invade the lobby a bit much. I learned that New Yorkers love the Hudson bar scene, and it is something. But I think you'll also learn that no New Yorker in his right mind would stay at the hotel. We got our first negative vibe at the front desk where the girl checking us into our room could not have been any less friendly -- a single smile would have been alright. Then came the rooms. During my stay of 5 nights, we (a friend and I) had two rooms -- one with a single queen bed and a deluxe room with 2 double beds. (We couldn't get the deluxe room until our 2nd night). The room with the single queen bed was disgraceful. The floors themselves are nice wood floors and the bed is comfortable with nice linens. However, there is no dresser or anywhere else to put clothes, other than a shelf-less closet for shirts and pants. The television is tiny. Also, there was only about 1-2 feet on each side of the bed and only a few feet in front of the bed -- it was like living in a closet. If you want a room for anything BUT sleep, you are going to pull your hair out in this place. The room with two beds (a deluxe room that was much more expensive) was considerably larger, yet small even by New York standards. The amenities were the same -- no dresser. Where do they expect you to put your clothes? In both rooms, the bathrooms are incredibly small. Worse yet, on the Saturday morning of our stay, the entire hotel had no hot water until early afternoon. The water was ice cold making for one great shower. I was also disappointed with the staff -- you'll pass them in the hall or elsewhere and you'll never get a "hello." I also noticed that they have no problem entering an elevator before guests, which I have never seen happen at other hotels. Of course, we also found it very difficult to get onto an elevator. Even though there are several elevators, it seemed as if few were working, you'd always wait several minutes for one, and when it finally arrived, it was already full. After a couple occasions of watching 2-3 full down-elevators pass us by, we finally took to riding the elevator up just to ensure getting a ride down -- some stay! Waiting minutes for elevators happened every single day. Overall, I was very disappointed with this hotel and would not stay there again. The hotel is all appearance over substance, and the appearance did not even hold up entirely given the water stains on the ceilings in the bathrooms of both of our rooms. If you do stay, you better make sure you are in a deluxe room because the 150 square feet (room and bathroom) of the standard room is unacceptable.

“Gone downhill and spiraling” I have stayed at the Days Hotel six times now. Count 'em, SIX times. You can scroll down for my initial review, which I posted after my first two times. Since then, every experience has taken a nosedive and I can no longer positively recommend this hotel. It is STILL a "value" for NYC. I won't get into what a ripoff NYC hotels are, and how awful they all are and how much they overcharge. It's terrible, and as much as I like NYC, it is not worth what hotels overcharge. Given that Days Hotel averages about $150 a night, it's considered a "bargain." But it's still a craphole. Yup, a craphole. Since I've been staying there, the wear and tear on the motel is just getting worse. A lot of it has to do with the fact that, because it costs less than most hotels in Manhattan, you get a large crowd of big families or tourist groups. The hotel is just not doing its part keeping up with the amount of people who stream through here. The biggest issue is that the rooms are so hit and miss. On my last stay here, I had a big, spacious room but I got NO cell phone or Internet reception (I don't mean their WiFi, which is a joke because you'll never find a signal; I had my own broadband card). I couldn't get a 4G signal, which had never happened before. So I asked to move to a room where I could get better signal. They moved me to a room that is facing the street. So I did find out that the rooms that face the street (Broadway) get some Internet reception. The rooms that face the back do not. However, the street-facing rooms are incredibly small. The size of a closet. And the heaters that they attach to these particular units are so loud and constantly banging throughout the night. So in the end, you have to choose between Internet reception or a bigger room that doesn't have banging pipes. That they can't figure out a happy medium between these two is the Days Hotel's downfall. If you're a business traveler, you'll have to suck it up and shell out the bigger bucks at a better hotel. It stinks but you won't get any work done at this place. Their receptions are not friendly at all and the lack of good customer service is another ding for this place.

“It IS the Location...” Spent two weekend nights there in early February 2012. Clean, good sleep, nice views adequate room size and friendly enough staff. All very important features, but you stay here for the location.

“Great place!” This is another great Holiday Inn and it is in a very good location. It is about 14 miles from downtown but close to the airport with shuttle service, right across the street from the local commute train service (30 minutes to downtown) and it sits in a small town area with great restaurants and friendly people. Oh, and they are motorcycle friendly!

“Stellar Stay” Fantastic staff made the stay very pleasurable. The rooms were well decorated and large. Room service was alway responsive and hot. The happy hour wine tasting from 5-6 was a nice departure from other hotels. We highly recommend this hotel.

“Loved the Jury's” Thanks Tripadvisor, the Jury's has another satisfied customer due to the postings here. We were not disatisfied with our choice......... & this from former Boston residents. The hotel is centrally located (halfway between the Copley & Arlington T stops, walking distance to Copley, Pru Center, Boston Commons, Newberry Street Shops, Boylston Theater district & the Starbucks or Au Bon Pain that we frequented when we did not want the delicious but pricey hotel restaurant for breakfast). The rooms and all appointments are new and the whole hotel is tastefully decorated. Staff was helpful and courteous. We went for 2 rooms for our family with 3 kids and we had 2 rooms at the end of a hall across from each other. The plus for us (& I'm sure our neighbors) was that there was an additional door that cordoned off our end of the hallway which made our space more like a suite. I noticed that each floor had 2 sets of these so it's worth requesting for a family. It was sure a plus! Our rates were quite reasonable for a downtown city hotel too. I'm sold on this chain of boutique hotels. I hope they'll bring more to the States from Ireland.

“Hôtel central à Chicago, mais chambres avec peu d'intérêt” Nous avons séjourné en mars dans cet hôtel du centre de Chicago, situé dans "Le Loop". Accueil assez standard. Chambre spacieuse mais sans grand intérêt. Petit déjeuner en chambre quelconque et cher.

“Glorious...” The Bowery Hotel My new favorite New York hotel. The idea was to evoke a classic New York pre-war apartment...and it really works, right down to the doilies and key-in-keyhole bathroom door lock. This place is almost like magic, it suits my taste so! Huge windows look out over lower Manhattan in a most contemporary way and the nostalgia isn’t twee at all. Honestly, it’s been a few months since we were there and I can’t remember every detail but I’ve stayed in several other new NYC hotels since and this one remains my hands down favorite, even when compared to ones like the Crosby Street Hotel. (It’s gotta be those doilies!) The bar is also gorgeousness itself in a tastefully overdone way. It would be a great place to meet someone for a drink though it does get crowded in the late afternoon and evenings. The location might not be for everyone, but it’s just up from the new Museum of Contemporary Art and the neighborhood is very cool. I’m looking forward to another stay soon!

“Great Downtown location” This is a old style athletic club and you get to use all the facilities for free. No resort fee scam. The parking is only $12 a day with in and out and you can stay parked after check out time. Breakfast is included. A fruit plate is delivered to your room. The rooms are only on the top few floors so it is very quiet. The rooms are very cool; designed in dark colors with nice amenities and comfy beds. And the wifi is free too. The extras are what really made this place. Our son lives a few blocks away and it was great for us.

“Great Location, Nice Rooms, No Complaints” Nice location, right on the Magnificent Mile in the midst of all the stores and action. Walking distance to the Navy Pier (about 15 minute walk). Down the street from Millenium Park and the Art Institude. Right outside the door is the trolley and bus stops to get anywhere you desire. Couple blocks from Grant Park and river cruises. Lots of restaurants and shops all around. The room was very clean, beds were comfortable, great view from our room. Service was great, fast check in and easy checkout. They charge for a late checkout, but will also hold your bags if needed at no cost. I would stay again without any hesitation. We loved our stay and I recommend to all my friends and family. You won't be disappointed with the location.

“Quality Hotel - bit pricey in some areas” This was our third trip to LA and each time we have stayed in a different area. This hotel was well located near Beverly Hills although it seemed a bit limited at night. We chose not to eat in the hotel as it was quite expensive and instead went to the nearby Chinese Restaurant which was very popular, very tasty and very reasonbly priced. We also had a very good breakfast at the local Jerry's Deli. We felt that the drinks in the Hotel were also over-priced, a good glass of Merlot at the Chinese was $7 whereas it was $14 in the hotel. Friday night appeared to be singles night so it was great fun watching who paired off with who. The room was comfortable and clean but not as big as others we have stayed in. There was no tea/coffee making facilities so we had to use room service but this was always prompt and I am pleased to say that the gratuity was included in the price. We like walking in LA and the Farmers Market/Grove was only 30 mins away, the Walk of Fame and Chinese Theatre took us about 1 hour. Buses are easy to use in LA although a bit busy and it took us over an hour to get to Santa Monica beach but it was worth it although it could have been a bit warmer. The staff were always courteous although the Concierge was not aware of the Universal/Sea World Flexi ticket even though it was on the information she gave us. She seemed more keen on booking us a taxi and a single ticket rather than trying to save us money by giving us the options. Overall the hotel was a good place to start our two week stay in the US and I would cautiously recommend it.

“Loved it” I was staying at the Residence inn for 3 nights in October for the Amigo Airsho. I had a very spacious studio suite on the second floor. It was clean and had all amenities like kingsize bed, kitchen, sitting area, working area and flat-tv. I also had a great view all over El Paso that was amazing at night. The check-in was also quick and friendly. I would always stay again.

“Great location, but the hotel is just OK.” As the name implies, the Marriott at Metro Center is just a few steps from the biggest subway station in Washington, which means guests can get just about everywhere in a few minutes. It's also within ten to fifteen minutes' walk of the White House, the Mall, the Smithsonian, the National Gallery of Art, and any number of downtown stores and restaurants. Unfortunately, the hotel itself is nothing special. The rooms are of reasonable size, the beds are comfortable, and most of the staff are friendly, but the hotel lacks most of the nice touches found in many other Marriotts. Our room had no mini-bar (not that we care) and no safe (a much more important defect). And of course there were no robes, no slippers, no chocolates on the pillows. The in-room wireless took a while to make an impression on our computer and then kept going on and off, so we switched to the wired internet connection, which worked better. And the room was never made up until mid-afternoon. There is no fine dining restaurant, but the "Fire and Sage" has a menu much like the coffee shops in many nice hotels (with a pretty good breakfast buffet for $20 as well as sandwiches, pasta, etc. for lunch and dinner) and there is also a Starbucks in the lobby. The Fitness Center was a pleasant surprise -- hardly top-end, but bigger and more inviting than the "exercise rooms" at some downtown hotels -- and the indoor pool looked swimmable except that it was always crowded. The biggest problem we encountered was noise. The walls seem to be thin, and there were a number of boisterous guests on our floor. The Marriott Metro Center seems to do a lot of its business with large groups -- conventions, family reunions, school field trips, etc. -- and must offer rates for these groups that are far lower than those paid by business travelers and tourists. A lot of the guests we encountered seemed as though they did not have much experience staying in a hotel, and some of them clearly didn't know how to behave there. We were awakened one night at 1 a.m. by a large group of young men and women literally shouting down the hall to each other as they made their way from the elevator to their rooms. Then there seemed to be parties going on in several of the rooms for the next few hours. That night was the worst, but it was always pretty noisy.

“book this hotel.... its really nice” I had an incredible stay at On the Avenue.... its right near 2 subway stations and its in a really fun safe area of New york City. If you've never been to New York, I'd come here. It's walkable to all your major attractions but far enough away so you're not surrounded by the tourist trap crowds and restaurants. Being on 77th and Bway will give you a taste of being a local and you'll love it. Check out the restaurants on Amsterdam Ave... a block away.... Some great Italian ones between 72nd and 77th.. My room was very comfortable and modern and the staff went out of their way for me the moment i walked in. Very friendly. There is some construction going on across the street, but in all honesty, it wasn't loud at all. If you call On The Ave and you're not liking the rates.... Try calling again because their rates change a lot. STAY HERE GUYS.... No negatives.

“Great hotel!” Upon entering the hotel, we were greeted with great customer service from the employee at the front desk. The room itself was bigger than expected and very clean. We had a poolside room. In the off season, it wasn't too bad. However, I could see it being a little noisy during the day during a busier season. There was an Applebee's located right next door -- only a short walk across the parking lot. The hotel was only a few miles from the Winchester Mystery House. Also, they had free wifi, which is definitely a plus. Would stay here again, if in the area. Definitely recommend.

“The dream lives on!” I chose the hotel based on great reviews. They were right on. Clean, newer (no flatscreens though), good service, and decent breakfasts. The location is actually very good. (It's the burbs, but good burbs.) We were tourists seeing the zoo, Seaworld, Pacific Beach and were brief freeway drives from each. One pointer- they should stock Cascade for the dishwasher in the room. They had a limited supply in their little store/pantry. Soft towels, responsive housekeeping, good shower pressure, and good heat/AC control are my minimum requirements that aren't met often as I'm a road warrior. This hotel met them all with flying colors.

“A very pleasant surprise” After reading positive reviews on TripAdvisor, we decided to give this a try on our trip north from Florida. I am usually hesitant to go away from the major chains, especially when some of those are nearby. But with the nice reviews and by far the best rate, I couldn't pass it up. We arrived and were checked in quickly by the friendly an efficient person at the desk. Our room was small, but certainly good enough for a night. Everything was clean and the front desk called to make sure all was well about 15 minutes after checkin. I had to call back to get a password for the wireless Internet, and that worked well once I was able to connect. I did need to put the water all the way on the hot setting in the morning, but never did the temperature become uncomfortable. The towels were bigger and softer than those found in many hotels where I've paid twice as much or more. In the morning, checkout was easy and the breakfast selection wasn't bad. We'll definitely stay again if and when we have a stopover in Jacksonville.

“Always pleasant to go and great service” We were recently at the Biltmore for a night and for a special birthday dinner for a relative. the biltmore has beautiful grounds, is wonderfully kept up and is exceptionally pleasant and relaxing-even in the heat of August. When my bag did not quite make it to Phoenix with me, the staff made a very special trip to get the bag at the airport so i would have it before the dinner that night. It was above and beyond the call of duty but was also done with true helpfulness. The food and the service at the dinner that night (for 14) were very special, exceptionally good, and very nicely served with consideration of the pacing of the function. We have done this before at the hotel and the biltmore has never disappointd.

“Great Location..Excellant Staff...Clean and Spacious Rooms” If you are walking on Madison Ave you may not realize the hotel exists as there is no large sign or flags to tell you so. In the vicinity of the hotel there is a deli, laundromat, convenience store among other things. Check-In The check-in was smooth and fast. The lobby is relatively small but it feels warm. The front desk was very friendly. The bell man was ready to assist with my carry on bag. Room I had a suite which had a large living room and the furniture is very comfortable and makes you feel you are in your own home. The down comforter which they have was great. The mattress is a bit soft for me since at home I sleep on a Tempur-Pedic but it was still a good night sleep. Beware: I am travel alot and generally use the laundry bags in the closets to put clothes I need washed. Morgans will charge you 25$ if you take their laundry bag so watch out. View- We had a beautiful view looking Madison ave and to the left you could see the Empire state building. Bathroom- Was a bit small but the shower was great. More importantly everything was clean. Electronics- Everything worked from the TVs, the IPod dock, Telephones, etc. Suggestion: Ask for a room above the 13th Floor.

“Great hotel in walkable location - in the heart of Beverly Hills” I was very impressed with this hotel! I stayed here with my mother for a few days in July and we had wonderful time. This hotel was recently renovated - a big plus! Our room and bathroom were new, modern, VERY clean -- and the beds were extremely comfortable. The staff at the front desk were incredibly helpful and genuinely friendly to us. The hotel has a small, updated fitness center if you want to workout. We especially loved the rooftop pool as it a was a perfect spot for a quick dip in the afternoon before heading out to the many happy hours nearby. Regarding location...in my opinion, it's the best in the city. I've been traveling to Los Angeles several times a year for over 15 years and finally found an ideal spot to stay. You don't even need your car if you plan to stay in the neighborhood. West Third street is bustling with new boutiques, shops and many, many excellent restaurants. We found most cafes and restaurants open early for breakfast and stay open late at night as well. In addition to restaurants, you can easily walk to the Beverly center (my favorite LA mall) and the Grove & farmer's market -- at the opposite end. A few of our favorite local restaurants include Doughboys, Toast, The Little Door and the hotel has an excellent restaurant as well, The Churchill. We had lunch and dinner there during our stay. Oh, the famous Magnolia Bakery is directly across the street if you are craving a cupcake....who can ask for more? We will definitely stay here again!!

“Slept like a Baby” Hotel was okay. Needs renovation. Not terrible, but dated. Room was spacious. Bed was comfortable. Sleep was peaceful. Stayed for two nights on floor 19. Very quiet. Loved the fridge. Would stay again. God willing.

“Unlike any other Doubletree” My first reaction when I walked into the lobby was a pleasant surprise. Unlike most Doubletree's that I've stayed at, theWit is trendy, clean, fresh and kind of has a bit of a W-esque vibe (be ready for this). Rooms: My husband and I were upgraded to a suite. The room was huge! It was actually 2 rooms, living space/kitchen and then the bedroom. The rooms were incredibly clean and hip. Every night at turn down, they left you a little fun quote with a trinket to match the quote. Our bathroom was huge with a soaking tub that for $25 you could have the spa staff draw you a bath with special bath soaps, suds and oils. Service: The staff was great. Very accommodating, knowledgeable about the area and friendly. The attention detail is excellent. Location: It's at State and Lake, which if you know Chicago, is in a heavy business district and right on the brown line. It may not be the best location for a tourist new to Chicago, but it is a GREAT location for business travel and if you don't mind walking 8-10 minutes to Michigan Ave. And of course since this is a Doubletree property you always get your unlimited supply of warm chocolate cookies. : ) The hotel has a great restaurant attached to it. Great food- we ate breakfast and lunch one of the days there. There is also a great bar on the top floor- very cool, hip vibe. Nice spot for a drink. Overall, great property, we will return.

“You Can Do Better in Rittenhouse Square” This hotel is located in a lovely part of Philadelphia but there have to be better hotels than this one. On the plus side: the bell staff is great, the restaurant is well-staffed and very nice, and Justin at the front desk was helpful. That's it. We asked for adjoining, non-smoking, rooms, one with a king-sized bed, one with double beds. I called twice to confirm this. When we arrived, we were given adjoining rooms with double beds. Also, one of the rooms was labeled as "non-smoking" but reeked of cigarette smoke. As a result, we had to move to other rooms. There were patches on the ceiling from water damage, instead of re-painting the whole ceiling to cover the patches. None of the staff, save for Justin at the front desk or the guys at the front door, ever smiled or said hello. The hotel is old and felt old. You can do better.

“Great Location” Right in the heart of Georgetown and shopping. The rooms are nice with comfortable beds and linens. My bathroom was kinda small but for DC, nothing to complain about. The bar on the 1st floor was fun too. I'd ask for a high floor so you can be away from the street/bar traffic below.

“Convenient , low cost, quiet!” I wawsn't expecting much. We'd stayed here many years ago when it was a Howard Johnson and I was expecting something run down for the money. However, I was pleasantly surprised. The reception and teh rooms have a fresh and contemporary feeel. Desk staff were efficient. Breakfast was good with the usual HIX plus hot items. Rooms weer also quiet. Ours overlooked teh runway but I coudl not hear a thing through the single soundproof pane of glass. It seemed like a miracle to me. We drove here from teh Dollar rental plaza on Air[port Blvd in about 3 mins so its every convenient if you want to collect a car and then sleep overnight. The area is definately dodgy so you probably needa car to get about but teh 7.11 store right next door is bright and modern with agood selection of sandwiches, drinks and snacks. There are also a few restaurants including a Sizzler that you could walk to safely. All in all a good deal. Low cost and comfortable, quieta nd a nice breakfast. A perfect airport hotel.

“It is the staff that truely make this a great hotel” It did not help that due to a mix up we needed to squeeze a family of four into a King Room, the sofa was hastily made up (no doona or blanket for warmth) and breakfast offered for the mistake(which ended up costing us, as the full price of breakfast was debited to our travel card, and then removed in a subsequent transaction costing us in fees and exchange rates). The rooms are ageing and a number of mild imperfections cautioned us about the room, such as dirty sink, yellow stains on shower base, dirty underblanket on bed. Our next major disappointment came with room service, we were told at the restaurant to order room service, but only 1/2 our meal arrived, when questioned about this we were told the kitchen was closed leaving 3 hungry people to devour 1 burger, this was the only time that staff did not work hard at helping our requests, in fact there were times when I almost felt the staff were reading my mind. A big thanks to Edgar Padilla and the others that assisted us, their local advice about Washington made our trip.

“The Purple People Sleeper” This is a really fun hotel. Brand spankin' new and shiny it welcomes guests to the future. A future where everything is purple. Rooms are uber modern, brightly lit and very small. It feels like a cross between a space capsule and the Big Brother house. Given that most New York hotels have small rooms, the way Yotel has utilised the space is clever. And why would you stay in your hotel room all day when you have New York to explore? Beware though, that the bathroom area is divided from the bedroom space with only a curtain. If you are travelling with a companion ensure you have close comfortable relationship. The room is very clean and noise from the city is minimal. (It's New York so some noise is to be expected.) The noise from the corridor was bothersome at times. Doors slamming every morning from the cleaners (Cabin Crew) and guests can get to be a nuisance. A muffin breakfast was provided and enjoyed in the restaurant/lounge Level 4 area. The elevators were one of our favourite features, the funky music and dim lighting made you dance for every ride. It is difficult not to stop when the doors open. All the DJ music throughout the hotel was great and put you in a positive mood for your New York adventures. Location is brilliant. Times Square - safe, easy to walk to Broadway shows and close to the subway station. The hotel is great value for money, and I would recommend it to couples, single travellers, and trendy young things. Given the confined space of the rooms it is not suited to families. As the Level 4 space also becomes a Night Club/Lounge in the evenings, it's not a hotel with kids in mind. But grown ups like to have fun too and it's nice to have a hotel designed just for us. I really enjoyed the "Space Theme" throughout the stay. If you are looking for something warm and traditional - this is not the place. But if you're ready to fly to the future, then don your moon boots and give the purple planet of Yotel a try.

“What a great place!” This is a wonderful little hotel close to all of the major Hollywood attractions. It is dated, but has a certain charm to it that you'll never find at chain hotels. Our room was average in size, with 2 queen (or maybe double) beds, a small dining area with a mini-fridge and microwave, full bath and dressing area. It was cleaner than a Radisson I stayed at just before this visit. However, my boyfriend saw a bug in the shower our last day there. He swears it was a cockroach, but I'm not sure. Our room overlooked the courtyard of a neighboring apartment building. We had no street noise and hardly any noise from the neighbors. As mentioned, parking is free - a HUGE plus - but can be challenging. The staff had me double-park in the lot when we checked in around 9 p.m., but also had me give them the keys so others could get in and out. By morning, our car was in a regular space. The continental breakfast was enough to get us started each day. Free internet access was a nice touch. The staff was very friendly. For $89/night I can't recommend the Hollywood Celebrity Hotel enough!

“Nice Hotel / Welcoming Staff” This is a nice facility, conveniently located just a couple of miles from the Columbus airport (they run a shuttle). The staff was friendly and welcoming - from the bellman driving the van to the front-desk check-in personnel. Lobby is spacious and inviting. The walk from the lobby to the room elevators is a bit long if you're dealing with a lot of luggage (however, if you've got a car, you can park closer). Same floorplan as the Cincinnati North Marriott which, it seems, is owned by the same folks. Overall, a pleasant stay at a reasonable rate.

“A very pleasant experience for the weekend.” From the moment we were greeted by the person who checked us in, our experience at the Hampton Inn & Suites couldn't have been nicer. The beds were very comfortable, there were free snacks and water in the room upon our check-in and the breakfast was more than ample. My one complaint is that we could hear a lot of noice in the hallway when people were walking by and talking. Overall, a very good experience.

“Fantastic Southwestern Resort!” I visited this hotel for a conference. The rooms are spacious, clean and well appointed. The staff is friendly and very helpful. The meeting facilities are roomy and comfortable. There is a beautiful golf course, several nice pools, and idyllic grounds. The hotel is about 15-20 mins away from the San Antonio Riverwalk and other attractions. This hotel provides a great combination of upscale amenities and comfortable, friendly atmosphere that is very relaxing. I highly recommend.

“Great location, but rooms have seen better days” I booked this hotel with a last minute deal from Priceline. I would argue that there is NO way this hotel is four stars, but we weren't in the room often during the one night stay. The location is great and we really loved the cocktails and appetizers at the hotel bar. Beds were comfortable, but small (two twin beds). Parking was WAY overpriced! If we stay here again, I would park in the O'Farrell garage and walk. $50+ for less then 24 hours of parking is highway robbery. Overall, I would stay here again for a quick trip to San Francisco. I certainly wouldn't stay here for an extended period of time. There are better Union Square hotels for the money.

“Nice clean motel-in process of upgrading” Motel was in good location and antiseptically clean. Desk clerk worked an 18-hour shift and was very bubbly and friendly. Very attentive to our needs. The landscaping around the motel was well-kept with palm trees along the east side. Motel is in process of upgrading with new carpeting and furniture. New earth-toned carpeting already in hallways. Clerk informed us that rooms are next and will also get new furnishings. Our room was very clean but bland. Could use some more paintings or something. New furniture will be nice when installed. Bathroom was immaculate. Very nice shower head with curved shower curtain. Breakfast was adequate. Breakfast area was very small and easily became congested. Overall, very nice for the price. We'll be back in March 2006.

“Nice suite hotel, swans in the lobby are nice touch” Simillar to other dozens or so embassy suite stayed in terms of room, settings, location, price. Breakfast did not have as many selections as expected. The swans in the lobby are beautiful.

“Not bad but not great” Here are the good things - great location, very comfy bed, friendly staff. Clean. I actually like the toiletries in dispensers - much greener that way. Coffee in the lobby this morning was good. On the down side, the furniture in my room was banged up and there was peeling paint around the windows - only one elevator to the fitness room -- there is a reason there is no picture on the website. Not the worst sweatbox but not great - there was a wait for equipment.

“Great hotel, great service!” We spent our first night in San Francisco at the Argonaut and from the time we pulled up to the front of the hotel, we were treated like royalty. They opened our doors for us, took our luggage inside, took the car for valet parking and brought us drinks from their manager's welcome, while we were checking in. It is a great location on Fisherman's Wharf and there are a few different breakfast places that are located a block behind the hotel, which were reasonably priced. The only negative is that my daughter wanted a pool, but we were so busy that day, that I don't think she even missed it. My only regret is that we didn't stay there for more nights, but we went to Napa and Sonoma valley the next day. Also, we didn't have a view, but it was late by the time we got back to the hotel, so it didn't really matter. We would definitely stay at the Argonaut again. ***If you are taking children and are not from a city that has homeless people on the streets, I would definitely have a talk with the children about it, before you arrive, because you will see homeless people on Fisherman's Wharf and other areas of San Francisco. We always felt safe, so we didn't consider it a problem, just a sad sight to see, especially for young eyes.

“Not worth the high price” Stayed here for 2 nights. Paid extra to stay on the concierge level and was sorely disappointed. Hoped to avoid the usual 'cattle call' of continental breakfast at other hotels but this was actually worse. Concierge room was way too small for the amount of people who had access (which I think was half of the hotel- people were coming from other floors) and the offerings were meager. On both mornings the coffee urn was empty (although it was refilled promptly after asking) and there were not enough seats. The room was adequate and clean and did have a very nice view. The location is great for sightseeing. I probably would noot choose to stay here again though because the general vibe was a bit too crowded and hectic. Didn't feel as though I were staying in the level of hotel I was paying the price for!

“First Class - Down Town Charolotte” I traveled to Charolotte to watch Miami vs Carolina and spent two great days at this hotel. It is located right in the heart of the city, almost everything was in walking distance. The staff and appearance of this place is outstanding. If you are going to visit Charlotte, I highly recommend this hotel. In my opinion 5 stars.

“Oasis in DTW” First of all, I had no idea such a tranquil place existed smack in the middle of the very busy airport. I really had never intended to stay at an airport hotel, however the only other option was to sleep in the terminal on this trip. The rooms and bathroom are huge, I was actually wondering why they were so huge, since I figure most people are just staying over night between flights... Anyways this place total reinvigorated me before I had to wake up and hit the air for another flight - work - flight day. Like the another reviewer said, there is a hum in part of the room, but lets be real. We are at an airport with jet engines producing 180 decibels of noise just on the other side of the glass window. Oh, almost forgot. Private TSA entrance directly into the terminal. So lobby to Gate in 5 mins.

“Nice hotel close to campus” The highlight of this stay was the friendly staff. Everyone I dealt with was responsive and helpful. The rooms were average although clean and quiet. The hallways were a bit dingy on the 11th floor where my room was located. If you are going to visit OSU I don't believe there is a better place to stay. It is directly across the street and I could see the stadium from the room window. I did not eat at the restaurant but I heard good comments about it from others. Overall this is a good place to stay. and I would recommend to anyone.

“noisy” This is a low budget well located hotel, its access to the main freeways are only a couple of blocks away, there is a target store at 2 blocks walking distance, an Ihop jut 3 blocks away and accross the street a Starbucks. Inside the room you have the basics for a family trip such as microwave, fridge, and a small table. The area to improve is that the hotel is to noisy and you can hear the people below and besides your room. the breakfast that is included is poor, as there is only 2 cereals, apples, sometimes oranges and only 2 tosters for the whole area, for $5 usd you can obtain a plate with scrambled eggs and pancakes that looked ok. all the phone calls have a cost, and even at the reception if you request the phone for a quick local call it will be denied. Next trip to San Diego I will pay a little more to obtain a quiet sleep and a better breakfast.

“Grand, not great” A rather boring exterior with no real proper "grand" entrance. When the taxi dropped my off it was like you where going in the back door. The lobby is just great old pompous grandeur and checkin was quick and efficient. I did not know about the ducks, so that was a great and positive surprise. The room I got was smallish and a very small bathroom. Being used to small European apartments, it was OK... barely. More importantly, while the room (and the hotel) was very clean, it was worn. The sink was cracked, the toilet seat loose, wallpaper pealing and paint peeling. But, the service was friendly and quick and overall, the experience was good. A refresh of the rooms would take this hotel back to the "Grand" category!

“I only stay here in SF” This is truly my home away from home. The apartments (they are not rooms) are spacious, well appointed and sumptous. THe only problem is that everyone else has discovered this place. The views from the bay side rooms are incredible. You see the Golden Gate bridge as well as Alcatraz. The only drawback is that there is no room service. There is no restaurant attached to the hotel. THey offer a generous complimentary breakfast and wine at 5 o'clock but if you get hungry after dinner you are out of luck. Isn't a great place for small children either and the gym is still years away.

“Great place to stay in Hollywood” We had a 2 queen room which was spacious for our family. The included breakfast was great. Gets very crowded at peak time but we were fine as we came down before the peak & always had a free table. We chose this hotel as it's close to the freeway & away fm the crowds in the main Hollywood drag yet a short walk down. My only gripe is the relatively high overnight parking fee but this is Los Angeles so it's to be expected. There's off street parking in the residential area a few streets up the road but we didn't feel so safe leaving our car out at night so we parked in the hotel carpark.

“OK Boutique Hotel...but terrible odor!” I stayed at the Orlando for one night in May. The hotel is in an OK location on 3rd, near the Beverly Center. The hotel is OK, though sort of souless. The room was fine, though forgetable. The biggest issue for me: there was a terrible odor on my floor. I have no idea what it was, it wasn't exactly strong, but enough that I felt nauseous when I woke up. Half of the hotel was being renovated during my stay - the odor could have been from the renovation. There's too many great places to stay in LA. I'd rather stay elsewhere on future visits.

“Recommended” Pros: Still feels like a newly built property; clean lobby and largish rooms. Walking distance to LA Live, Staples Center, Convention Center, etc. Just off the freeway, so no long drives down surface streets. Cab ride from airport is about $50, but colleagues said it only took about 30 minutes in fairly heavy traffic. Not far from historic districts of downtown - about a mile to Broadway with all its interesting old buildings. Great coffee at illy in lobby; Starbucks also available just outside hotel. Decent choice of so-so restaurants outside hotel - not the best food LA has to offer, but at least you have a selection. Cons: Close to LA Live, Staples Center, etc ... so if you're not there for events at those places traffic around the hotel can be heavy, nearby bars and restaurants can be loud and obnoxious. North-facing rooms have noise from construction site across the street starting at 6:30am - woke me up before my alarm went off each morning, and I was sleeping with ear plugs. Stupidly expensive $40/night parking ($32 if you're driving a hybrid). No self-parking; valet only. (That said, the valet service was very fast, very efficient, both for drop off and pick up.) Neighborhood immediately around hotel doesn't have much in the way of character - generic chain restaurants. Tips: Ask for north-facing room for nice few of downtown LA ... with the downside of aforementioned construction noise.

“Can't Wait to Go Back!” I was a little apprehensive about the financial district location on the weekend, but after visiting the Union Square area for shopping, I was thankful to have such a peaceful place to return to. The hotel was the best I've stayed at in SF. I rarely say this, but the staff were incredible. Everyone aknowledged you coming and going, the concierge was friendly and helpful, they pressed the elevator button for you if they saw you coming loaded with packages, etc. In the morning, coffee was available in the lobby and in mid-morning, hot cider and tea cakes. (I learned later that you could request an in-room coffee pot.) The room was huge, and with SPG Gold, I got a bay view room for $139. The bed was incredible. I don't understand the previous comment about the sliding bathroom door. In my mind, it gets the door completely out of the way. I would go out of my way to stay here in SF. I didn't want to leave, and I can't wait to go back.

“Pleasantly Surprised” I don't know if I got lucked out with a newly renovated room, or if the bad reviews were a case of bad luck, but my stay was quite nice. My room was very clean decorated with modern furniture and a flat screen tv. Noise level wasn't a problem either so I was able to get a good night sleep. Parking lot is spacious and free. The only knock is the location. It's right off the freeway on a one way road so it's kind of difficult going in and out. There is a back road but it's kind of hard to find. Overall nice place.

“I really liked it!” I was pleasantly surprised with this hotel. The room was very clean and nicely decorated, the bed was really well made and clean, and the furniture was very nice. The bathroom was nice, although a tad small. I loved the breakfast room; it was different from all the breakfast rooms I had seen before because it had a nice architecture and several sitting areas. Breakfast was good and had plenty of options. I really liked this hotel! I wish we would have stayed longer!

“OK place for the money” Pluses: Clean rooms, fairly quiet (could hear some street noise on highway side and some activity in other rooms and hall) but slept ok. Has a business center with free internet, computer and printer stocked with basic office supplies. Clean pool (outdoor). VERY Convenient to airport and even downtown sites with just a little driving (time the traffic to avoid rush hours though). Free cocktail hour and good cold breakfast bar (cereal, muffins, fruit, etc). Have secure parking garage attached. Not many minuses: I saw no advantage to being a Priority Club Member and staying here except for points. No complimentary USA today at your door, etc. Good budget stay place.

“business traveler friendly” Channel 70 Productions had a project only a few blocks from the Hyatt, our reason for staying there. Upon arrival, the lobby was full of kids and families, so we left and found Embassy Suites around the corner. Much more peaceful, so that was our base of operations for two days. And, it was easy to park our equipment truck out front. I love hotels with lots of close in parking. Gardens and landscaping are nice, but when hauling luggage and equipment, I'll take big and handy parking lots every time. We make a lot of demands on hotel staff (faxing, receiving packages, local information, directions, etc) because our rooms act as our offices when on the road. The staff here was always instantly available in person or via the phone. Good breakfast, but we worked through both day's happy hours, so missed those. Darn it. One bad: wi-fi fees. Sure, it's free downstairs, but our rooms were upstairs. Next time in the north Dallas area, this will be our first choice.

“Pool Under Construction” The Four Seasons is a extremely quiet hotel and the staff goes the extra mile to help you. We has no problems with valet, our room or service. They seem to have the quickest elevators I have ever seen and even gave us a ride to Minute-Maid Field for it was pouring rain. Unfortunately, one of the reasons we were staying here was to relax by the pool, but it was closed for renovations. Otherwise we would have stayed somewhere else. But this hotel does have enclosed access to a small mall next door. We will return back when all the construction is completed.

“What staying at the Ritz should be!” I stayed at the Ritz for one night of a recent business trip. At the last minute, my husband joined me and so I experienced the hotel both as a business traveler and as a romantic getaway. The Ritz scored well on both counts. As a business hotel, it is conveniently located near the financial district. The business center servies (though pricey) are vast, so you can quickly get what you need. The wireless connected quickly and was stable - though only one computer could be connected to the internet at once. As a more romantic getaway, the Ritz was nice. I was working through my birthday, and the hotel staff helped my husband surprise me with some of the best chocolate-covered strawberries I've ever had along with champagne. We also had a delicious dinner in our room, and the bed was extremely comfortable. The service was excellent on all fronts as well. Honestly, I was a little too relaxed for a business trip! Sometimes you stay at higher-end properties and it is overrated...the Ritz, however, earned its name during our one-night stay.

“Not so bad at all...thought it was a good deal actually” OK, I'm going to depart from the pack here a little...yes, this hotel is dated, and yes, it's got some issues with carpet needing cleaning and the like. However, it also gets extra points for a few amenities you often don't find in hotels with price tags twice this high. I stayed here twice - on both ends of a scuba diving liveaboard trip out to see some great white sharks, long story - and my review applies to both rooms. As I've mentioned in other reviews, certain things usually score extra credit points from me: good ventilation and water pressure, a comfy bed, a quiet room, and access to snacks and soft drinks. This place scored high on all those counts, honestly. Air conditioning worked great, the rooms were comfortable, the bathrooms had recently been remodeled and were quite spacious. One room was just average size, but one was huge! This place actually is something of a flophouse for several companies that run trips out to see the sharks, and some outfits that do sportfishing, so you may want to call ahead to double check room availability. I screwed up my travel plans, then called at 8 AM to book a room for an extra night and it turned out to have been a great thing...I heard later the place filled up shortly thereafter. A couple of real extra credit points to this hotel: There was a fridge and a microwave in each room; the drink and snack machines were amply stocked, not broken, and conveniently located in the lobby - and, oh joy! A change machine! Best of all, this hotel was silent as the grave. I stayed up super late one night and was not awakened early the next morning by loud talking, slamming doors, any of that nonsense. Also, there's plenty of parking, and the hotel is located very near some really wonderful restaurants (we liked the Fish Grotto and, aw heck, another one the name of which escapes me right now...but seriously, there are several outstanding joints within easy walking distance. There's also a Denny's a block away and I had no trouble ordering a pizza late one night.) The neighborhood was just fine, not frightening, and you're within sight of the incredibly beautiful harbor. You're also right on top of the airport, and yet somehow not within the flight path...I didn't hear much jet noise. The Internet worked great!! This one gets REAL points from me...I've stayed in "luxury" hotels where the wireless signal was terrible, or they charged $30 per night or something absurd. At the Ramada, I got a strong, clear signal, no trouble logging on, and no need for a "bridge" for rent from the front desk or similar foolishness. I'd stay here again in a hot second. I think the value is actually pretty good for the price paid. My only real complaint was with the tiny elevator - I had to rearrange my bags a few times to get them onto the cart so it all would fit...

“Posh elegance at the Wharf” My husband and I stayed here for a wedding in late Sept. this year and really enjoyed our spot at the Fairmont. We got a great rate because of the block of rooms was reserved for wedding guests, and felt it was well worth it! The rooms are beautiful, very comfortable, spacious and well equipped with modern ammenities. There is a very lovely and fancy espresso maker that was great in the mornings. One complaint I had was we could not get our DVD player to work and called the front desk several times and several times they said they would send someone up to assist us, however no one came, and this was irritating. Other than that the service was impeccable, from checkin when we were escorted to our room so we did not get lost, to the bellhop flagging a cab for us. The housekeeping did come rather late in the day (after 4pm), which was odd to me, but did a great job. It is located in a great spot, easy access to all parts of the city and right in the heart of LIttle Italy. We were able to walk almost everywhere and those parts we couldn't get to by foot we easily found a cab. I would definitely recommend this spot if it's in your price-range. Thanks for putting the cherry on the top of a lovely elegant weekend in Boston Fairmont!

“Location = Wonderful Convenience” O'Hare Hilton, Chicago. First visit, and we love this place. Rooms are clean and nicely furnished. Comfortable recliner conducive to relaxation. Public spaces are exactly as depicted on their website. Indoor pool- suitable for a dip, laps, as well as jacuzzi. Large gym on premises- subject to daily fee. WALK to hotel from any terminal through the underground walkway or take the terminal connector shuttle to Terminal 2. WALK to CTA BLUE LINE subway. 40 minutes to the Loop. Breakfast buffet is nothing short of spectacular. We enjoyed the hospitality of the GASLIGHT CLUB, on lobby level. Great steaks, food, and ATMOSPHERE. Talented piano player - welcomes sing alongs. Restaurant is richly decorated with red velvet wallpaper- dramatic chandeliers- in a turn of the century San Francisco Barbary Coast motif. At the conclusion of our stay, wewalked from the room to our gate! NO SHUTTLES- AND WE DID NOT EVEN HAVE TO GO OUTSIDE. There is only one hotel in our future for Chicago- the O'Hare Hiltom.

“A gem on the riverwalk” I stayed with my wife during our recent trip to Texas, upon recommendation from a friend. This is a real gem! It is very conveniently located on a quiet part of the riverwalk. It will take you approx 10 minutes walking to get to all restaurants & bars - a very nice walk. It has its own bar & restaurant. Restaurant (called Ocho) doesn't have a lot of choice, but the food was pretty good. The room was very charming, very nicely decorated, equipped with both a fan and air conditionning, and with a little view on the riverwalk. You also find a basket full of anything you could need (and more!) in the room. The girl at front door was very nice, polite each time we spoke with her. We really enjoyed our two nights there. In order to give the fifth star, I would have enjoyed to find breakfast and / or parking included in the price - overall, it becomes a bit pricy. And, the giant television antenna across the riverwalk is kind of an eyesore. But this wouldn't prevent me from recommending this hotel to anyone visiting San Antonio! I'm not sure we could have found better.

“Really liked it...” Ok, well the $42 per day valet is steep, but the hotel itself is nice. I liked the fact that there are plenty of places to eat right inside the hotel. The rooms are small, but cozy with decent views. Very clean and a wonderful lobby. You will have to call for your paper, this is true, but all in all the deal I got on hotwire made it all the worthwhile!

“besseres ist möglich” Das Hotel ist etwas in die Jahr gekommen und liegt auch nicht super zentral. In nächster Nähe gibt es wenig, um Essen oder in eine Bar zu gehen. Das Servicepersonal beim Check-in und Check out war sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit. Die Hotelbar hingegen war "merkwürdig" besetzt und es hat keinen Spaß gemacht, dort noch einen Absacker zu nehmen. Es gibt Getränkeautomaten auf jedem 2. Flur ! und auf jedem anderen gibt es Eismaschinen - macht auch keinen wirklichen Sinn ständig für Eis oder Getränke mit den Fahrstuhl fahren zu müssen. Warmes Flaschenwasser auf dem Zimmer für 5 USD ist unverschämt. Insgesamt würde ich das Hotel bei einem nächsten Besuch nicht mehr wählen.

“Great Value-Interesting Location” Lets start off with what this hotel is-and what it isn't It is, a really good value and offers a great product for the price. In a week where everything in DC was $350-$550 this place was $200. The rooms were very nice and my standard room had a great bathroom and was a well sized room. In addition, I had probably the best priced room service meal-in years. On the downside if you are visiting DC, nothing other than campus is in walking distance, not even the bars of Gtown. So its a taxi ride of $20 for everything, And the cabs don't sue here so you must ring them up. Staying on campus was interesting, I was in DC-but I felt like I wasn't.

“Bad location if you're going downtown.” My husband and I stayed here for one night, and weren't impressed at all. The beds are extremely hard - not just "firm". We were given a room next to the elevator, the only one they had available despite being Marriott Rewards members, and we could hear the elevator going all night. The walls are quite thin, so when our neighbors cell started ringing at 6am, it was like an alarm clock you just couldn't find. The curtains didn't close all the way, so the streetlamp that was our view was blaring into the room all night, just another thing to keep you awake if the bed wasn't enough. Other than that, the property is clean, and the staff is helpful and polite. The location is not in the downtown area, which we didn't realize when we booked. We called Marriott and asked for "downtown" and this is what they gave us. If you're going out at night and want to take a taxi to the 6th Street area, it's about $13 each way.

“Beautiful Hotel” I stayed here just for a night while attending a meeting. Had stayed here before a few years ago with my family. Upon arrival several attendants approached my car and asked if they could help with luggage and the valet was quick with a ticket. Check-in was smooth, if not overly friendly. My request for a high floor was met with a room on the top floor. I stopped at the bar for a cocktail to take to the room and the bartender was so nice and even offered a small glass of nuts to take with me. Nice touch. The room was nice and probably a typical newer Hyatt room; nicely decorated but not super comfy or plush. My only complaint is that the noise from the hallway was easily heard in the room at night so I needed to turn on the tv to drown out the noise (and I wasn't near an elevator.) The mattress and linens were very comfortable. This is a large convention hotel and the lobby bar is huge with large communal tables and a bar. It has a cool vibe with the tables being lit underneath. My friend and I stopped by late after dinner and it was very busy. Our server could not have been more unfriendly or rude -- she really couldn't. I'm guessing it was busy and maybe she had had a bad night, but she was unpleasant to everyone around us, too. Luckily, she was the only person at the Hyatt with a bad attitude. While waiting for my car by the check-out desk with full hands a bellman come up and asked if he could help with my luggage and what type of car I had -- he had it loaded in my car when I got there. This may not seem like a big deal but I wasn't standing close to the door so he was looking for people who might need help, which was nice, instead of having to track someone down closer to front doors.

“location is best part” We arrived without a booking after a long drive and they welcomed us with open arms, so we were very grateful. Parking was no problem, right inside the hotel basically. It's just a bit tired but given the numbers of visitors no wonder it's wearing out. Probably due for a renovation but location and value are excellent. An easy stroll around the corner to Beale St and across the road to look at the ducks at the Peabody. We had a corner room but it was not too noisy on the higher floor.

“Great as a base camp” Stayed here on a 1-day trip through NYC. Check-in was slow, but the bellmen were great - we were two people with six suitcases! - and the room was clean and quiet. This hotel was very trendy during the 1990s, but it has been well-maintained and updated. The only clue to its age is the lack of outlets in the room for recharging today's iPhones, iPads, etc. - the only one we could find was in the bathroom! Also, wireless in the room costs $14 bucks a day, which is silly. It's free in the lobby. The Paramount is a great choice for young, hip tourists who want to use it as a base camp while exploring NYC. The rooms are small, but they work fine if all you want to do is sleep, shower, and get dressed for the next nightclub tour.

“Perfect hotel” Stayed here 4 nights. The only complaint I had was my room wasn't ready when I arrived at 16:30. This was due to a late checkout of a previous occupant and it was currently being cleaned. I'd been upgraded to a suite from a club room, so went and sat in the lounge for a bit until it was ready. Very impressed with the room when I got into it about 30 mins later. The hotel is a short walk from Powell St BART station, so if coming in from SFO, it's very easy to get to, and no hills to pull your luggage up. Every member of staff I met was friendly and seemed happy to be there. The club lounge was perfect for breakfast, and snacks throughout the day. There is also a nice outside terrace. Great view from the room of San Francisco and a lovely comfy bed. When I return to San Fran I'll stay here again.

“My first stay in a haunted hotel room” I stayed in room 304 four days before Halloween and I won't be doing it again. That said, the place does has a few excellent features. The lower Queen Anne location is great, near the Seattle Center and within a block of numerous places to eat, a grocery store and a drug store. The hill immediately to the North is a fun place to walk, with lots of old staircases and stately mansions. Second, the rooms are huge compared to other Seattle hotels. Mine was the smallest in the hotel, and it was nearly identical to a 450 square foot studio apartment I once lived in. Apparently the hotel was built as part of the Seattle Engineering School in 1918. Back then it housed young engineers who moved to the city to work in the auto industry (the building also housed a mechanics training school). The decor is appropriate for the hotel: American Colonial furnishings accented by framed paintings of roses and such all over the walls. The room had a full kitchen, complete with dishes, glasses, silverware and a breakfast nook with a table for eating. The kitchen did not have a stove but made up for it with a ridiculous amount of built in storage. I slept horribly. The bed clothes and bed were old and uncomfortable and the walls were so thin I might as well have been in attendance at the raucous party next door. When I did manage to fall asleep I had this awful dream over and over where I would get pushed into a pit by some woman. I woke up quite out of sorts. So, yeah, it could have ben something I ate or maybe the neighbors noise, but it definitely felt to me like the place was haunted. I asked about it at check out and they said they'd never heard anything like that about the room before, so who knows!

“Triplets' first trip to NYC” Just spent 4 days during Christmas week with the fine folks at the Hilton. I took my triplet 14yr old nieces for their first trip to NYC. I have stayed at this hotel many times and chose it for the location to everything we wanted to do for Christmas. I booked 2 rooms due to having 7 people and the front desk was able to put us 3 rooms apart, which made it very convienent. We had a deluxe double room and it honestly looked as if they had just remodeled it. We were on the 14th floor and had no problems with the elevators. There was a line for check-in but that has been the case every time I have stayed here, no matter what time of year. The bathrooms were great, the tub drained and the lighting was fantastic. The room was also very clean and we slept great in those beds. The rooms were a great deal as I had paid $189.00 per night. This was a prepaid special and I always look for these. Please don't overlook this place. The location is the best and the hotel was great.

“Pleasant Stay” We had a pleasant stay. The hotel is nice and clean with renovated rooms. It is more in Chinatown than in the financial district but that is not a problem as a two or three block walk will put you in the action of Union Square. i am not giving the hotel a better rating because I paid for an executive room that included continental breakfast and hors d'oeuvres and soft drinks in the evening. Upon my arrival to the executive lounge there was a sign that they closed on Fridays and Saturday evenings. The front desk was not sympathetic at all.

“excellent accommodation” What great value for money. The suite is huge and very comfortable. Bedding was excellent including the sofa bed. Breakfast was one of the best we have had in the terms of quality, not selection(only basic, but very tasty). The service was fast and efficient. Check in at noon and we were given a room, no waiting. The shuttle was quick and reliable. Great location to airport and even tourist attractions. After checking in we walked up the road(2 minutes) to Avis and collected our car. Budget is right next door to the hotel. There is a $9.90 fee for the internet. I could not fault this hotel in any way, and will certainly return in the future

“Great Choice for Chicago!” Clean, best breakfast, extremely friendly place. Especially Connie at breakfast. She was one of the best smiling people I ever met. Breakfast was great, too, by the way. Fresh big blackberries and blueberries. This is a short review, because we are just passing through. But we loved the hotel, location, and the staff ( especially Connie).

“Pleasant Environment/Food and Temperature Needs Improvement” I recently stayed at this hotel for a business conference. The conference rooms were easy to access. The cafe shop was well stocked. The hotel location was excellent. My room was a good size, well cleaned and most comfortable. The hotel food was not good at all. The room where the conference was held was extremely cold for two days and distracting from the content of the conference.The front desk personnel and bell men were friendly and helpful. Please eat at Cool River rather than the hotel. You will truly enjoy the experience. The hotel food was more expensive than the great food at Cool River.

“Very good stay and would stay there again” The value at this hotel was excellent. It is hard to get a decent rate at a hotel near any airport. This place was not only an exceptional value, the hotel staff was also great. I accidentally left a valuable item in my room and the staff found it and then held it. Room and bathroom were both clean. Hotel is near many restaurants that are accessible by walking. The breakfast room staff was very nice. I highly recommend staying at this hotel

“Some booking issues thru hotel, but GREAT service upon arrival, highly recommend!” We stayed at this hotel because we were attending a wedding at the hotel and it was more convenient as we took our 1 year old with us. We had a nightmare trying to book the room under the wedding rate and difficult time dealing with people on the phone (central reservation line) however once I spoke with hotel directly and after arrival, we experienced great service from very friendly/ attentive staff. From the check-in, valet, bellhop, room service, waitstaff -- everyone was great! We had a room w 2 doubles and had room to set up the pack n play. Hotel offers pack n plays but we had arranged rental of a stroller, pack n play and bucket of toys from Russell @ LA baby gear rental so we wouldn't have to lug it all from the East coast. Would also rec'd Russell's services! Very nice plate of fruit, nuts, water and snacks was in our room upon arrival and refreshed a few days into our stay. Nice touch from the hotel. Location is great if planning on a visit to Universal Studios/ City Walk. Within walking distance which was great. During our stay, we had a rental car and visited local sites - Hollywood sign, Hollywood, Rodeo Drive/ Bev Hlls, UCLA, Mulholland Dr and Santa Monica Beach & Pier. All within an easy drive. Pool is very nice at the hotel, location on the grounds is not the best, but nice none the less. pool bar and cabanas and plenty of chairs. Was not crowded at all during our stay but the weather was in low 70's. The hotel is about 30 minutes from LAX so keep that in mind if flying out of LAX and traffic times. If your flight is anywhere near rush hour, you may want to reconsider staying and driving from this location.

“Clean, roomy and safe location” Nice, clean, good location, roomy and in a safe area. Right off I-10. The rooms were quiet and the beds were good and comfortable. You have to pay a fee for breakfast and/or dinner, however, we were not able to partake in either one. This was a one night stop and it met all of our requirements.

“Perfectly fine hotel” This hotel is well located and more than adequate for a Boston visitor. Hotel is within easy walking distance to downtown and the South End and is next door to the NE Medical Center T Station (Orange Line).
