Staff at the reception are very pleasant and the rooms are clean, modern and comfortable. Note that Tuft's hospital is just across the street so if you get a room facing Washington St. you may here ambulances from time to time. Buffet breakfast at the Wisteria restaurant was good and the male host and female omelet chef were very nice. The other so-called waitresses walked around like unmotivated zombies; perhaps they didn't get enough sleep the night before! All in all, however, if you're looking for a centrally located clean and safe place to stay, this Doubletree is a good choice.

“Impressed” Possibly the best hotel I have ever stayed in. Hotel is very luxurious and perfectly clean. Georgetown is within walking distance. The in house swimming pool isn’t huge but fine. Breakfast is not complementary and a bit pricey but one of the best breakfasts I ever had. Parking for the hotel is not free which was not explained to us checking in.

“Good choice” Perfect location arriving at Houston George Bush International and thinking to move from Houston using the highways. Good rooms, nice free wifi also in the room and very good breakfast. Free parking also. Very positive experience. Recommended for business needs.

“Great stay at the beautiful Indy Marriot...” We stayed at the downtown Marriot in Indianapolis for a wedding in July of 2009. The first impression when you walk in is that this is a beautiful, modern, updated hotel. The lobby is comfortable and beautiful, with fruit flavored water for you to enjoy when you come in from that Indiana humidity! The staff was very friendly, and when we checked in we were the V.I.P. of the day, which entitled us to free appetizers at the in-hotel restaurant, Champions. The rooms were clean, updated and comfortable. There was a flat-screen HDTV (with only a couple HD channels), down pillows and comfortable beds. The bathroom was very roomy and featured Bath & Body Works toiletries, which was awesome. Usually you get some grandma-smelling lotions made in God knows where. The fitness room and the pool were top-notch. The fitness room was high quality, and you can actually get a good workout done there. The pool was an infinity pool, with a metal bottom, which has an interesting feel on your toes. The hot tub is also very nice and hot. There is also a guest laundry that we were able to use to get all of our clothes clean for like $6, a fraction of the cost it would cost to send them out. The restaurant, Champions, is a sports bar, with good beer and good bar food to eat. The atmosphere is nice in there and the staff is very friendly. We attended a wedding for my cousin there, and the banquet facilities were very nice, the food was great and the service was friendly and great. There is an urban mall that is essentially across the street, with all of your standard mall retailers, great dining and a food court. Nice place to get out of the heat. Basically, this Marriott, like most Marriotts I have stayed at, was a slam dunk. Outstanding stay, great food and amenities, and friendly staff.

“Got stuck in a tiny closet of a room” I chose this hotel based on past stays at Homewood Suites. I stayed here for a night before a cruise. The room i received was nothing like the room described on teh website or what i have at other Homewood Suites. I travel about 300 days a year and I know my hotels. The room was tiny! My 2nd bedroom in my cruise ship cabin was larger! The room was so small that i had to have the dresser removed so we could move around the room. We had 6 pieces of luggage, plus carry on bags and there was no room to move. I choose Homewood because I have special dietary needs and like to make my own breakfast in the room. This room had nothing, no fridge, no microwave, no stove (but they did give us a package of micowave popcorn, too bad there was no microwave to pop it in) NOT WHAT I PAID FOR! THIS CLOSET OF A ROOM WAS THE SAME PRICE AS A FULL SUITE. I complained to the front desk staff many times. They said the hotel was full. I wasn"t even offered a discount or additional Hilton points. As a GOLD level Hilton guest i should have been up graded to a better room, like they did at the Hampton Inn Istayed at in Vancouver. ALso, we did not have a private balcony so i could leave the door open as i slept. I didn't get any of my gold level freebies (water, cookies or whatever) and I was not greeted as a Gold Hilton honors guest like I should have been. I plan on writing letters to Hilton, the GM at the Hotel as well the corporate owners of the property, Chesapeake Lodging Trust.

“Pretty Good, But Rooms Need Updating” Like many of the other reviewers, I was very pleased with the location of this hotel – it’s easy walking distance to downtown attractions such as Pike Place Market, as well as shops (across the street from Nordstrom and Westlake Center), restaurants, and public transportation. The lobby area is spacious and feels modern, well-appointed with plenty of couches and tables. It’s also really active with people checking in and out, meeting up, using their laptops (free wifi in the lobby, but not in the rooms), and hanging out at the bar. It could get pretty loud, but I thought it was nice lively atmosphere. As others have mentioned, there can be a long wait for the elevators, but most of the time I wasn’t in a rush to get anywhere, so it didn’t bother me. The fitness center was pretty good too , consisting of two rooms, one with cardio and weight machines, and another (smaller) room with a few recumbent bikes. There are locker rooms for changing. The pool is small, adequate for splashing around, but not for real exercise. I didn’t try the hotel restaurant, but there is a small café in the lobby that serves breakfast and light lunches; it looked very popular and the breakfasts I saw looked (and smelled) great. Note, however, that a great donut shop, Top Pot, is only a couple of blocks from the hotel! It appears they have made efforts to update the common areas of the hotel, but unfortunately, the room itself looked straight from the ‘80s. The carpet was stained. The bathroom seemed clean enough but smelled sour – almost like there was a leak somewhere. The bed was comfortable though. Despite the room being less than optimal, for the right price I would stay here again. I paid $100 per night through Priceline, which was still a very good deal for a conveniently-located, decently-appointed hotel.

“Great Price bidding Priceline..HoHum older Marriott CourtYard in East Dallas” Picked this up bidding priceline.com $30 worth about that.Nice enough good beds food nearby.Staff indifferent breakfast expensive but good food within walking distance although neighborhood was dodgy.Everything except the bed seemed VERY old.OK for an overnite stop but needs much work to be once again ready for prime time.

“Perfect Mother & Son weekend” Having been to NYC a handful of times and stayed at more botique hotels, this hotel was great for being a large chain. I booked a weekend trip with my Mother to New York and elected to stay at the InterContinental Barclay. I didn't see a need to get two rooms but we did need 2 beds and this can be a premium in Manhattan. The hotel was great from the second we entered and loved the location. We had multiple places to go, and being close to Grand Central Terminal made it very easy to get where we wanted to (I'm not a huge fan of public transit but it beats traffic and the horrible NYC cab drives). It was a short walk to Times Square, or a quick cab ($7) for when we didn't want to walk. Most restaurants we wanted to try were about 20 Blocks south, but overall this hotel is very centrally located if you're looking to spend time a little time everywhere in the City, this is the spot. It was raining lightly on Sunday, and they provided us with umbrellas (no charge, if returned) The Room was nice with a good/great bed and great linens. Bathroom was a little small but you don't go to NYC to be in your bedroom. Also, we were on the top floor and there was not a problem with road noise.

“Good location, nice staff, clean room, great breakfast” I recently stayed at this hotel because we were in town for a wedding. The wedding was at St. Patrick's cathedral and the location was perfect for that (a few minutes away only). The staff in the hotel was really nice and we enjoyed the free wireless in the hotel. I was really impressed with the free breakfast too since they offered quite a few options... and the good part was that everything was continuously being refilled up until the moment the breakfast closed - not at like some other places where all the good stuff is gone if you don't rush there before 7am. While there was nothing to do right around the hotel, everything was accessible by car. I liked that they have a big parking lot right in front of the main entrance.

“esperienza perfetta” Per la mia prima visita a Chicago, avevo scelto il Conrad su base delle recessioni di tripadvisor e sono rimasto più che soddisfatto. L'albergo è proprio nel cuore di Chicago, all'inizio del magnificent mile ma anche vicino alla parte sud della città. E' il primo Conrad che frequento. Camere e bagni spaziosi e puliti. Letti stra-comodi. Ho scelto una tariffa con prima colazione americana inclusa (prima colazione con ampia scelta e abbondante....). Personale stra-cortese e disponibile. Non posso che consigliare questo albergo (come consiglio Chicago come meta turistica)

“Not worth it” Overpriced hotel in trendy old town area of San Diego. Rooms are comfortable. Restaurants are limited. Room service food selections very limited, and they charge 20% service plus delivery fee. Parking charge is $26 per day. Wireless internet connection in room is very unstable, frequently breaking off. Service is friendly in a formal, phony way. Not worth $300+ per day. Do yourself a favor, you can get much better value in San Diego than this.

“This is the Place” Don't bother looking elsewhere - this is it. Incredible location (walk out your door almost right onto Beale St); very nice lobby, clean rooms. Parking is $17, but worth it for this location. A sign at check-in does note that this is not the place to stay if noise bothers you (that would be the noise from Beale St below). Make your own waffle for breakfast was nice. Great hotel - this is the only place I would stay if I return to Memphis. Oh yeah - Tunica, MS is 1/2 hour south - great gambling. If you are going to spend a night down there, I recommend the Gold Strike.

“Different from the rest” We make a trip once a year to San Antonio to visit family. We try to stay some place new and fun each time. I had read an article in the Southern Living about this new little boutique hotel in down town SA. I researched it and we decided to give it a try. Here are my thoughts and travel suggestions. 1. This is not a place to take children. 2.If you have trouble getting around yes the beds are very high and you may have trouble getting in and out. 3. It is an old building and if you are looking for a slick modern hotel this is NOT your place. Ok that being said. We enjoyed our stay very much. We loved that is was off the beaten path but still within walking distance of all the activities on the River. We loved that the floors creaked and that it was dark. We wished that we had had a better view, but we did not go to stay in our room and look out the window. True there are no closets in the rooms, but there are hooks and hangers in the drawers. And who really needs a closet. If you are staying in town long term maybe another place will suit you better. The fridge is cute, and stocked with fun things. We did not partake but the prices are not bad. (the monkey in the basket was a bit pricey and I would have liked to have taken him home) The bathroom is small and functional. The lotions etc are in bottle in the shower. I would have liked a sample to take home. They were offered for sale, but at "very well thought of " price. Parking is limited, but we had no problem finding a space and it is just $10.00 for the whole day. Much better than the bigger hotels. Suggestions to the personnel pay a little more attention to the front desk. We had to hunt down someone to check out. And I do think it would be nice to offer breakfast in the lobby, free. Or in that wonderful sun room we could only see from outside. We did not partake of anything in the bar, but did travel down to see. And yes it is dark. All in all it was a good stay. Try it out if you are headed that way. It will be fun.
“Fabulous historic hotel” The rooms were updated recently, the hotel has a great location, the service was great. It was a real treat to stay there.

“Clean, well located, average...” As said below by many reviewers, very clean, well priced and great location (basically on Times Square). On the minus side: AC unit in my room was way too noisy and breakfast (not included in price of the room) not worth the additional 14+ dollars.. Saved quite a bit by using an online booking site via TripAdvisor.

“Superb” I was tired when I reached this hotel after an arrival on the Victoria Clipper. Check-in was easy and fast. The receptionist was warm and friendly. She told me about dining options in the hotel and in the area and told me that they would be happy to help me during my stay and seemed to genuinely mean it. I was very pleased with my room which had a view of the harbor. It took me a long time to locate the switch for the room darkening shades. They are electronic and the book in the room simply says the switch is on the wall--but what wall? The switch was behind the lamp on the bedside table with the radio.........after leaving my bags I walked downstairs to find something to eat. There is a Ruth Chris steak house that appeared to still be serving but the NY Deli was closing up. I walked across the street to the mall and had dinner at an Italian place there. It was very good but I do not recall name--il Fornio? The room was clean, nice TV, free internet to Passport members, nice amenities in the bathroom with deep soaking tub and separate shower, No complaints. There were magazines in the room to read which I appreciated. Breakfast in the Club Lounge the next morning was disappointing. I had eaten breakfast in Marriott concierge lounges most every morning the week before and had been pleased. Breakfast here was very skimpy--three or four choices of cold cereal, some pastries, smoked salmon, cheese and capers. Nothing hot except coffee. There were two choices of Greek yogurt--honey or pomegranate. Check-out was easy. I used award points for the stay so can't say much about value. I prefer this property to the Hyatt on Olive and 8.

“Decent Riverwalk hotel” We booked this hotel through their Summer Promo special - $99 per night with free self-parking. The parking clinched the deal since it can be expensive to park near the Riverwalk. The garage is across the street, but connected through an underground passageway to the hotel. It's a nice touch since the surrounding area can look a little dicey at night if you're not used to San Antonio. The hotel is located a bit northwest of the main Riverwalk action. The hotel is an old Adam's Mark. The lobby is very nice, dark woods. The check-in staff was OK and provided us with some restaurant recommendations. (We like to ask the staff where they like to go. It's usually less touristy.) The halls leading to the rooms definitely need to be freshened up a bit. Very pinky, textured wallpaper and funky carpet. It was clean though. The room is also a bit dated. Our room overlooked the north area with a view of the Riverwalk and pool. That section of the Riverwalk is a quieter section, and it's nice that it's not situated smack in the middle of the action. The only caveat is that the bath opens directly next to the bed. It's a strange set-up and with no bath fan, it is a bit awkward if the Mexican food gets to your stomach. The room was clean and I did not see any bugs. The only issue that I had was that the noise was a bit loud from the hallway and the adjacent room. Most hotels have this problem, particularly if the person in the room next door is deaf and plays the TV very loudly. The doors needed to be pulled shut and it caused everyone to slam their doors. The hotel has its own entrance to the Riverwalk which is nice. The main action is about a five minute walk away. Make sure to pick up a map of the Riverwalk so you know where you're going. Also, when you return to the hotel on the Riverwalk, you need to get on the correct side as you're leaving the main area. Otherwise, there are very few crossovers and entrance/exits down where the hotel is. We got caught on the other side and had to walk another two blocks to get up to street level and walk on the street level to get to the hotel. As I had had some margaritas and was not feeling well, this extra walk was not welcomed! Other points - the fitness room is decent with treadmills and ellipticals. There's a nautius machine too. The pool was partially closed while we were there and we didn't get a chance to swim. The Pecan Street Pub is a nice, cozy bar with good service. We would return if we managed to get another deal like the one that we got this time.

“Tolle Lage, nettes Hotel” Das Hotel liegt direkt am Yachthafen, nicht weit entfernt vom Gaslamp Quarter und den anderen Bayfront Hotels (Marriott und Hyatt). Die Zimmer sind Hilton typisch, relativ modern, sauber und geraeumig. Wir hatten eine Rate fuer $99 pro Nacht die ein super Deal fuer San Diego ist. Man erreicht die vielen Restaurants und Bars des Gaslamp Quarter in wenigen Minuten zu Fuss. Sehr zu empfehlen!
“super hotel tres bon rapport qualite/prix” hôtel a recommander! nous avions une chambre + salle de bain. c'etait tres spacieux, calme (nous étions cote cour). hotel impeccable bien situe.

“Pleasant Surprise - Nice, new large rooms” Great hotel. Large room and bathroom. Perfect for a family of four. Housekeeping could use a little help. Overall, staff was very helpful and accomodating. I would definitely recommend this property.

“Do yourself a favour.” We booked this hotel because it was rated #1 on TA and we were not disappointed..I booked a limo pick up at the airport through the hotel webiste and it all went smoothly. After 29 hours home to hotel it was nice to have someone waiting for us where we didn't have to make any decisions and we felt it was well worth the money. We stayed for 4 nights at the end of June in a deluxe King room. Could not have been happier, the other reviewers have it all covered, it was clean, comfortable, quiet, convenient and we could not fault anything. The staff were helpful and friendly, we were comfortable chatting to the other guests when we stayed for wine & cheese one evening, breaksfast was appreciated and quite a cost saving not needing to go out and buy it. We are not really coffee drinkers and it was the one hotel in the US that we stayed in (7 in total) that had a good selection of teas. Thank you Casablanca for catering to your international guests. If we are ever back in NY we would definitely stay at this hotel again. If you are looking for a flashy 5 star place this is not for you - but if you want a home away from home do yourself a favour and stay here.

“Best value for the money” We have stayed here a half a dozen times, and were pleased with the cleanliness of our room, the bathroom was clean and well stocked. The breakfast buffet was very good, offered a great selection of muffins, breads, fruit as well as the eggs, hashbrowns and waffles. Very convenient location with easy access to restaurants and grocery stores. For the money I recommend staying at the Ramada inn.

“Shabby rooms, good staff” This W really is not up to snuff. Rooms and baths are small, which is expected in NYC, but also shabby and outdated. It's as though all the attention has been lavished upon making a cool lobby and bar. The staff is very helpful, however--it's just that a renovation is desperately needed.

“Nice Hotel at a good Deal” Reserved on ihg.com and got a great deal that included parking, drink coupons and breakfast. Although the evening clerk said that I didn't he upgraded me to a suite since I was a platinum rewards member. The next morning I discussed it with the guest service agent and he made it all right!

“Worked out just great!” I landed this hotel via Hotwire ($69), having a good idea that where Hotwire would place me in Streeterville would quite possibly be here. It totally suited my purposes and comfort as I was in the area for a few days for a friend's wedding in this area. It was lovely to be able to walk to the various locations (Ivy Room, Conrad Hillton, etc) we were to be at - and pay the rate I was able to secure for the quality of accommodations. The bellman who greeted me at the door and was on duty several times in the 3 days/2 nights I was there was cheery and helpful. Loved having Einstein's Bagels on the ground floor area for on the go lunch or breakfast option. Totally pleased with the 2 double bed room. Would stay there again.

“Perfect” I am not sure if it was the exhaustion from the red eye but the bed at the Willard was by far the most comfortable one I have ever slept in, even my own. The pillows, the feather bed, the down comforter were perfect. The hotel itself is elegant, a bit stuffy but really feels like you are in Washington DC. When I was there the lobby was filled with cherry blossoms and it was really breathtaking. My room was large, beautifully appointed and very quiet. The location of the hotel is within great walking distance of great restaurants, monuments and shops. When I go to DC again I will always stay at the Willard.

“Hyatt Disappoints This Time” This was my third stay at the Hyatt in the last year, and while I like the hotel , it disappointed me this time. It is extremely convenient to my firm's LA office which is why I've stayed there, but I think this time was the last. As has been mentioned before, the rooms are very nice: the finishes are high-end, with granite countertops and gorgeous flat screen TVs. The rooms have very nice balconies and no matter which way your room faces, it's nice to be able to sit outside. The beds are also very comfortable. However, all this is negated by bad housekeeping. My bathroom floor this time was covered in hair. Not just little stray hairs, but lots of long, black hair which was impossible to miss. I did not arrive until really late, so I just took a towel and wiped them up myself, which I immediately regretting doing. When I lifted the towel, it was clear that the floor had not been washed in a while. UGH. The next morning, as I was getting ready to take my shower, I looked for the first time at the towel rack in the tub area, and realized that both towels there were used. DOUBLE UGH. I called housekeeping and while they were up in a flash with clean towels, I was disgusted beyond belief. As I left for the day, I reported all of this to the front desk, and when I got back, there was a message from housekeeping apologizing - sort of. It said they were sorry *if* their housekeeping did not meet my standards. I am pretty sure this doesn't meet anyone's standards, and the "if" in the apology sounded hedgey to me. Anyway, I was leaving at 5 the next morning and did not have the time or inclination to pursue it further. Unfortunately, the worst was yet to come, when at 4:30 that next morning I tried to take a shower only to find that there was no hot water. I got a tepid shower, but my colleague could not even get tepid water on her floor. She reported it and the hotel accomodated her with a credit, but still - it was a lousy way to start a long travel day. In any case, the long and short of it is that I've had 2 nice stays at this hotel and 1 pretty bad one, so I am giving it an Average rating. Any hotel can be "off" on occasion, but the cleanliness issue probably pushes me to try the Intercontintal up the street next time.

“Platinum member review” The platinum spg member upgraded room was nice. They have very good service and the employees did a great job. The hotel is in a nice location for a convention. The room was loud with street noise, guess just part of the deal in San Francisco.

“not for a special occasion” Just returned after 2 nights for our 35th wedding anniversary. We are Starwood Owners and we were assured of an upgrade. When we arrived we were told we were on the 6th floor so we asked and were granted the upgrade to the Starwood floor (shouldn't have had to ask). Called 3 times to ask for a 2nd robe which was only brought up when we said we had to leave for dinner reservations . It was brought up by a giggling man who handed it to me only to discover no belt. Real funny. My sister and her husband sent us a bottle of very good champagne which was deliverd by a girl who stated she "forgot the glasses and would be right back" , never saw her, called down 2 more times for the glasses, no one came. They also sent a beautiful bouquet of flowers that never got sent to the room and when she called to inquire, they were sitting on the concierge desk the whole time. I hope they were enjoying them. Then upon checkout, we were charged an $85 a day charge,(we used our points to stay) and they also charged us for the champagne my sister had already paid for. I will say the young man at the front desk was very nice and adjusted the charges. I found the room small and dark. The bathrooms had very little ammenities. I didn't find any of the staff very friendly at all. They could have cared less that we were celebrating a big anniversary. Have always loved the Westin, but do not love this one and would never stay there again.

“Pretty good place to stay” This seems to be an older property but the lobby has been updated to the 'new' style of Courtyards, complete with a touch-screen "navigation" in the lobby. The lobby bar/cafe is spacious and even has personal TVs in the booths! Weekdays are happy hour in the bar from 5 to 7. I got a 10% off coupon for the cafe, but was told it didn't apply to alcoholic drinks (even though there was no limitation of that on the coupon.) Nonetheless, the service was good although I didn't eat there. The front desk staff was very nice, especially Thomas. The fitness room was one of the better ones I've seen in Courtyards: 2 Lifefitness treadmills and 2 bikes, all with TV and free earbduds (and great air-conditioner). My room had a coffee maker and mini-fridge, but no complimentary water. There were plenty of TV channels, but 6 of them were ESPNS! There is an outdoor pool with access from the first floor rooms and balconys overlooking the pool. The hotel is across the street from Karl Strauss brewery/restaurant (but it's closed on Saturdays). There's also a small strip mall with a Starbucks, Quiznos and McDonalds in walking distance. Overall, it was a nice place, but it was a little pricy for a courtyard property.

“Very nice European style hotel, decent breakfast, great location” Stayed here for 4 nights last month. Very convenient location to lots of places on the riverwalk and other parts of downtown. My room was on the upper floor facing the main street. Street noise can be an issue, but I the room air conditioner was able to be set on "continuous fan" which is HUGE for me...I need white noise to sleep and drown out the street noise. My room was SMALL, but very well appointed. Good desk for working, full sized refrigerator. I did NOT park a car here based on other reviews and I didnt miss having a vehicle.

“Excellent service at the Alexander Inn” We just returned from our vacation in Philadelphia. Based on the great reviews, we decided to stay at the Alexander Inn. The Alexander Inn proved to be a fantastic hotel! For the price, we had a hard time believing that there was a continental breakfast, a fitness area, two PC's with broadband access. Best of all, the friendly folks at the front desk provided us with good directions each day. Yes, the bathrooms are small, but how much time do you spend there? The hotel is very close to the Society Hill section of town and it's a great place to walk. We were happy that we did not have to take a cab to any of our destinations. We will definitely stay at the Alexander Inn again!

“If you cant stay at Graceland, then stay at the Days Inn Graceland” This motel is exceptional value ( we got our room on Easyclick.com for $37 per night- after some booking issues- websites fault, not Days Inn). My wife and I are on a 7 week holiday around the southern states and needed affordable accommodation in locations that allowed us to get around without a car. The motel is steps away from Graceland, where you can also catch the Sun Studios free shuttle to downtown attractions, and a taxi back from downtown is $23, and local buses leave from out the front of the motel. There are plenty of restaurants/fast food and grocery stores within 1 mile of the motel, the service was great and the free breakfast included waffles, fruit, toast, cereal etc. Yes, our mattresses were a little hard, but when you get all of this, plus a micro/.fridge for $35 you cant really complain. The motel even cleaned up the snow on their premises better than Graceland did. Our only request would be for you to have a laundry ( but the receptionist pointed us to once about .5 miles away).

“Excellent Hotel, Excellent Service” I stayed here from January 10-13 and found the hotel to be top notch. The lobby was inviting and check in was easy. The staff was polite and helpful. My room was clean and well appointed but unlike concierge level rooms at most other Marriott properties there was no complimentary water in the room. The concierge lounge was well appointed and offered some of the best food of any Marriott property. It's 14th floor view was great and looked out over the Washington Monument. While the lounge often put out 100 bottles or more of water it seemed to go very quickly. This was one of the most crowded lounges I have been to. The health club was small but clean and not crowded most times. The equipment was well taken care of. The valet service was timely for the most part but parking is limited. If the valet has no room you will be directed to one of three other garages within a couple of blocks of the hotel. This hotel is across the street from the Ronald Reagan Building and is within walking distance to the Washington Monument, The White House, and several area museums. All in all this JW Marriott is top notch, you will not be disappointed.

“Solid experience at the Westin” I staid at the Westin for an event and had a great time there. It was all you can expect from a Westin: nice atmosphere, contemporary decor and good service. The rooms were huge and mine had a great view (23rd floor, overlooking the Charles and Cambridge). The bed was excellent as in any other Westin I've slept in. The bathroom was very spacious and confortable and everything was perfectly clean. The whole hotel feels new; there's a nice bar at the lobby level and the property is connected to a series of malls in the Copley Place areas, which is very convenient in the winter. Location is great, just steps from Boylston and Newbury streets. I'd definitely stay there again!

“Value and Location” Making the "college" move in Boston is never fun. Out on 8/31 not into the new until 9/1. So - where to overnight with parking for a van, a good meal, and a restful night...this is the spot. Convenient to everywhere, exceedingly cordial staff, comfortable beds, and from the 20th floor a great view. Will stay again.

“A Low Quality Springhill Suites” Some Springhill Suites are brand new, state of the art, and in a higher quality then the price you pay for them. This is not one of them. This one is old. The rooms feel ancient and outdated. The tv is old. The parking is expensive and only valet is offered. The office staff was pretty nice during my stay here and the location makes it the only real major chain hotel in the west end district. It is a great location literally next to the food/store offerings the west end has.

“Good hotel for price.” We stayed here for 3 nights and had a nice stay, overall. There were a couple minor problem that were quickly addressed by the staff. Our King suite was clean and fairly large. The living room w/ sofa bed and bedroom were in separate rooms, entirely. What puts this hotel over the top was the rate. $70 a night!!! Great bargain. We will stay here again.

“Superb location” I have stayed at this hotel many times when in boston. For me the location is great, just a short walk from newbury street and down to the park and common. Also within walking distance from fenway and other good spots in the city. The hotel itself is fine. Very typical big city marriott. The lobby houses an entrance to the mall, has a good very big sports bar and the gym and leisure facilities are good. The rooms are quite large and nicely decorated. The bathrooms are pretty old and need modernisation. All in all a good solid place to stay when you are in boston.

“The cutest little hotel on the Gold Coast” This was my third time staying at the Indigo. I always use the Priceline "Name Your Own Price" option and I know that I always get the hotel WAY under market value. But, I always feel that I am being a little bit shunned because I booked through a discounter. If the Indigo doesn't like third party bookers, they shouldn't partner with them. Anyway, when we checked in the room wasn't ready. We asked how much it would cost to upgrade from a room with a Queen bed to a room with a King. She said the cost would be $30. We put our suitcases in the storage room and left for four hours. When we returned and checked-in, the cost to upgrade to a room with a King bed suddenly shot up to $75. I guess this is the only thing I don't like about the Indigo. I have the feeling if the entire hotel was empty and the guest booked through a third party, you would be assigned to the most undesirable room they have. ( That's my opinion, for what it's worth.) We LOVE the location of this hotel and the entire place is visually VERY unique and attractive. There is a Keurig coffee maker in the room and NO CARPET! A hotel room feels so much cleaner without carpet. And, it also feels a little European, too! We loved the free internet, also.

“I'm not sure it could have been any better.....” My partner and I booked a Terrace Room at the Chicago Park Hyatt for the weekend of Feb 2-4 to celebrate our birthdays. I know it was a little silly to book the Terrace Room on a weekend where the high was around 3 degrees, but I wanted a special room, and we were not disappointed! First of all, the check in was seamless...everything about our reservation was in perfect order, and the desk clerk escorted us to the elevator. The Terrace Rooms are on the 3rd floor...a quick ride up the elevator. After entering the room, you are in a small "foyer." The bedroom portion of the room is large, with a king bed, leather chair, large desk, and TV/storage unit. Then there is a large set of sliding french doors that open out onto the terrace. Now, the terrace is not what you usually expect from a hotel. Usually, a hotel balcony or terrace is large enough for 2 small chairs and a little table to put a drink on. This was HUGE! Since it was winter, there was no furniture available, but it was big enough for a cocktail party for 30 people! There may have been more square feet than the actual room/bathroom...which was 550 sq ft. AND THE VIEW! You looked out right onto the historic water tower and Michigan Avenue. Since you are on the 3rd floor, you don't get much of a lake view, but with everything else there is to look at, it is not missed. Now, back to the room.....actually, the bathroom. in the hallway leading to the bathroom, there is a small bar and the closet. The closet isn't large, but has an ironing board, iron, hair dryer, safe, various hangars, and shoe polisher. Then the bathroom! When you walk in, you see a glass shower door...through that door is the shower and bathtub....all in one room, with a window looking out onto the terrace and the Water Tower. The tub is huge, probably big enough for 2, and the shower has 2 heads....one stationary, and one hand held. They don't work at the same time, but the water pressure is great. Then back into the bathroom there is a large vanity with double sinks...and a small wall mounted TV with a remote control. Next to that, there is a small vanity with a bench for putting on make up and such. And the toilet is in a seprarate water closet. There is also a closet door that opens into the other side of the closet in the hallway, which is very convenient. The room decor is simple. Black and white photos, and taupe carpet. The bedding is all white, and the furniture is contemporary medium stained wood. Besides lamps, there is recessed lighting over the bed, in the hallways, and in the bathroom. Service for the room was provided twice a day. Our cost for the room with the AAA discount was $400 a night, which included breakfast for 2 both mornings at NoMI, the hotel restaurant....more about that in the restaurant section. As many have noted before, the location couldn't be better. Since we are familiar with Chicago, we use public transportation, but cabs are readily available all around. We can't stay here everytime we stay in Chicago due to the cost, but we'd sure like to. We're definitely planning on staying here again for a special occasion.

“Trendy hotel in great spot in DC” The W hotel is next to the Willard hotel and couldn't be in a better spot for seeing DC. Both hop-on, hop-off buses have a stop outside on the loop for the major monuments and museums. It's very trendy and modern. The roof-top bar is fabulous to give a view of many of the well-known sites and our under-21 year olds were welcome until 5pm.

“Started the New Year with the bang” I had an amazing stay at Grand Hyatt San Francisco earlier this week. After a busy week at work I just wanted to get a way and relax and enjoy the city. I went to the hotel with my dog and I had a fabulous time. Everything about the hotel was perfect from the time I arrived at the front drive until I checked out of the hotel. Customer service at this hotel is exceptional. Mylene and Ron at the front desk are awesome. They went out of their way to make sure my pet and I had a perfect stay. My dog was so excited when she entered the room, there were doggie treats and doggie bowls and very nice comfortable bed for her. Housekeeping staff did a fantastic job taking care of the room and my stay was perfect. I will make sure to tell all my friends Grand Hyatt San Francisco.

“Poor Location; OK Hotel” My rating of "okay, but some problems" is mainly due to the location of this hotel. Marriott's tagged it as an "airport" hotel, but it's really a full seven miles or so from the airport and also about seven miles from downtown Austin (6th Street, etc.). Thus, it is not a very conveniently located hotel. In fact, it's in an unattractive part of south Austin and all of the views are of an industrial area and a highway. Having said that, the property itself is well-run and comfortable. The staff is very friendly and the menu in the hotel's restaurant includes a number of locally themed options. All in all, I'd have to give the property itself decent marks, but the location brings its rating down significantly. I wouldn't stay again.

“Nice 2-star hotel: old loud rooms, great location. If cheap, a fine stay.” We got a great rate for our stay, so this is a positive review based on this value. However, had I paid the normal rates I see online ($100 and more), I would have regretted not upgrading to a different 3-star hotel for similar money. Why? The rooms are 2-star. They are loud, thin walls and old windows, the faucets and shower hardware is old and needs replacing, there is paint chipping all over and cracks everywhere, chips all over the porcelain in the sink, the toilet and the shower, that sort of stuff. Nothing unlivable, but sort of shocking they spend so much effort on the Hollywood theme and completely ignore glaring bathroom discrepencies. The toilet seat was barely attached it was so old. (And bring your own toilet paper unless you enjoy sandpaper) The good: The location is literally a block from the Cable Cars, or BART, or any of the countless Muni choices, 2 blocks from Union Square, and very close to all sorts of rental car choices (we went with Enterprise located a block away at the Nikko Hotel). More good: there is free simple breakfast offered, including bagels and muffins, coffee, tea and juice, and cereal. Don't be fooled by the websites - there is no free wifi. Even the guest computer in the lobby costs per-minute rates to use. So, all in all, for $69 a night we have little to complain about. But I wouldn't pay much more than that unless I were out of options. (And with TripAdvisor, you're NEVER out of options!)

“Maybe I was wrong....” Last December my visit to the Mark was marked by a few service slips that seemed inappropriate for a hotel of this caliber, and I downgraded my review on tripadvisor accordingly. The Mark's management invited me to contact them and when I did so, I found the manager to be very interested in my experience and eager to improve their product. When I revisited the hotel a couple of months later, my partner and I were upgraded to magnificent suite, which I believe was a sincere gesture on the part of the hotel, not a bow to the pressure of the social media and tripadvisor. Needless to say our experience was perfect, as have been two subsequent visits. So after these several stays I can only conclude that my first impressions may have been unfortunate but overall the Mark is a wonderful combination of great location, perfect facilities, good systems, and a caring staff. Highly recommended.

“どうしてもヒルトン” どうしてもヒルトンじゃなくては、という「ヒルトンしばり」がある人向けホテルでしょう。 例えばHオーナーズの上級会員の人とか。 LAX周辺はエアポートホテルが乱立していて、正直五十歩百歩のような気がします。 ヒルトンだからシャトルがガンガン来るというわけでもないし、部屋が超豪華というわけでもないし。 上級会員で、朝食が無料とか、部屋をアップグレードしてもらえる、という人にはいいでしょうけど、 そうでない人はちょっと割高感のあるホテルかも(レート次第だけど)。

“Decent location, cool concept, worn out” I stayed here on business and my colleagues selected the hotel. As far as downtown San Diego hotels go, the Couryard is in a decent location. But there are homeless people hanging out around the hotel and you literally have to watch your step to avoid tripping over them. As far as the hotel goes - the lobby is nicely converted from the old bank and my room was fairly large. The valets were friendly and the front desk staff were professional. The bed was fine, not great, and the bathroom was large (if you need a large bathroom?). Unfortunately, the complements stop there - I stayed for 4 nights but only allowed my room to be serviced once because on the first day of service the staff who cleaned my room ate some of my food, spilled it on the floor of my room, and failed to clean it up after their feast. I was a bit disgusted and could not eat the remainder of my snacks I had purchased and kept in my room, but I immediately opted out of cleaning service to avoid any additional intrusions into the privacy of my room. While I informed the front desk of the hotel, they said they would note the issue both after my first day in the hotel and upon check-out. Also, paying $30 a day for parking in San Diego is absurd. There is a parking lot on every 4th corner, but since so few people use that parking they allow homeless people tent cities to flourish and then they charge outrageous prices for those unfortunate suckers (like myself) who require overnight parking and convenience. The least you would expect is breakfast included for a Courtyard, but even that was not offered at this hotel.

“Absolutley superb room and service” A superb hotel with an excellent room with outstanding views (32nd floor). Staff were very helpful and polite, room was superb. The only thing that would deter me from staying here again is it's location - if you want to be near Times Square it is a fair walk, and most things close around 10.30 in this area. However the hotel room more than makes up for that.

“Small Wedding Reception in a Suite!” I booked this knowing it was fairly convenient to DC Superior Court, where my sister and her partner were married. The suite on the 10th Floor was perfect size for our small party (10 people) that followed the ceremony and for the newlyweds to stay in for two nights. The staff could not have been more helpful, more friendly! Thank you, Helix! For giving us and extra table and providing us with extra glasses! Everything turned out wonderfully and it was the perfect space! The couple loved staying there. Also, great neighborhood... parking at the hotel was expensive, but worth it for the convenience.

“La Quinta Inn with a Holiday Inn feel. Some loose ends to tie up.” Positives. I really liked the room. It was tastefully decorated. It looked new. The wooden tiles in the bathroom and in the foyer made it look modern and the carpets are a good look too. There was also a lovely lcd tv. The bed was very comfortable (I think its the beds from Holiday Inn) and the sheets and blankets they used felt great (again I think its Holiday Inn's). The staff were friendly which was nice. Shower head had good pressure and spread. Negatives. The towels were still the same towels from Holiday Inn (they had the tag!), the phone still had the Holiday Inn logo on it, wiring was exposed and some of the wall tiles were not connected properly exposing what was underneath it. Its clear that they've rushed to open. Overall, I feel that this La Quinta has benefited from taking over a Holiday Inn. It has a Holiday Inn feel about it from the beds to the shower head. I enjoyed my stay nonetheless and if I ever return to San Diego I would definately stay here if the price is right.

“Awesome location but the rooms were not so hot” I stayed at this hotel for a weekend out downtown. I bought the room on Priceline and was really excited to see a Hyatt. The lobby area was really nice and the room seemed great at checkin. However, when we came back to sleep later I noticed that the comforter didn't look very clean. When I turned it down there was what appeared to be a bloodstain on the top. I switched it for the blanket in the closet and we fell asleep. But we were awoken shortly by people in the hall and then we could hear them once they went into the room next door. We turned a movie on to drown them out and fell back asleep. The breakfast the next morning was delicious. In sum I'd have to say this hotel isn't what you'd expect from a hyatt

“Flunks on cleanliness, great on everything else.” Our hotel room and bathroom were among the filthiest I've ever experienced. There were crumbs and a chocolate stain on our sheets, revealing they hadn't changed the sheets after the previous occupant! Yuck. Given that we didn't discover this until late at night after we were all settled in, we asked for new sheets and pillow cases, and made the bed ourselves. In addition, the bathroom floor had dirt caked on it and was in serious need of mopping. Normally, I would never even consider staying in such a place again, however, this hotel excelled in many other areas, listed below. Thus I would pull up again and examine a room prior to checking in. I'm hoping the filthy room was the aberration of one neglectful housekeeper and not refective of the hotel. Here's what we liked: * Very reasonable cost for a major metropolitan area: $119 special price, which included free parking. * Very helpful, friendly staff. * New, very comfortable pillowtop bed. * Very quiet room, even though the hotel is right off the freeway. * Refrigerator (next size up from the smallest) and microwave in every room. * Thermostat where you can set the temperature, as opposed to just cool or warm. * Shower temperature easy to regulate + massaging showerhead. * Nice, unclutter layout where my partner had room to practice his tai chi. * Elliptical trainer in fitness room.

“Nice location, OK styling, rooms need updating” 4 Stars for: Fitness Facility, Location, Business Office, and lobby area. 3 Stars for the rooms. They are the old style Marriott and need updating as far as design. 2 Stars for Concierge Lounge. The staff up there was not friendly. As a frequent Marriott user, you do get used to the friendly concierge lounge staff. This is first time I did not leave a tip for them. Disappointing. Hotel staff is generally very friendly. Easy to help with luggage, hailing cabs, etc. Location is everything with this hotel. I loved it.

“Sehr schönes Hotel direkt am Riverwalk” Das Westin Riverwalk liegt zentral am Riverwalk in San Antonio, alle Sehenwürdigkeiten der Stadt sind sehr leicht zu Fuss zu erreichen. Auch das Konferenz Zentrum liegt nur ca. 10 Minuten entfernt. Das Westin ist sehr geräumig, die Zimmer sind gross und gut ausgestattet, ebenso die Bäder. Besonders angenehm ist der Pool auf der Dachterasse mit Ausblick über die Stadt. Auch das Restaurant direkt am Riverwalk ist sehr schön und bietet angemessene Küche. Der Service war Westin typisch sehr aufmerksam und freundlich. Alles in allem bietet das Hotel alles was man für einen Urlaub oder eine Geschäftreise in San Antonio benötigt. Es setzt sich aber auch nicht von den anderen Hotels der selben Kategorie am Riverwalk ab.

“A Let Down From the Marriott” If you have not stayed at other premium Marriott and similar hotels, this property will impress. However, As a Marriott Gold Member and frequent business traveler, I was quite dissappointed in this property (sorry if that sounds snobby - not meant that way). The decor is a bit dated, the hallways dirty (for a Marriott hotel), and the hotel has some bizarre quirks (such as the elevator system - choose your floor before you get on the car). Don't bring a car here as the valet service averages a 20 minute retrieval time and I had to wait as long as 45 minutes - all for the bargain basement rate of $40/night. In fact, I'm willing to bet more is made on parking than on the rooms per square foot of space. Rooms are a little smaller than most of the standard full service Marriott's I stay with, but mine was nicely appointed and clean, albeit the fire sprinkler was missing part of its assembly, the wood floor in the entry scratched, and oddly - I had a cheap plastic seat on the toilet. So why stay here? Location, location, location. Easy walking distance to the National Mall, the White House, the Metro and some solid restaurants. If you can get a good deal on Hotwire or through a similar system (less than $200/night) give it a shot. Otherwise at the normal rates, look elsewhere.

“W une valeur sure : service, accueil, modernité et gout” Je n'ai séjourné qu'une nuit dans cet hôtel lors d'un voyage professionnel. Comme toujours, l'accueil et le service était charmant, rapide, efficace. Les chambres sont modernes, décorrées avec goût, finesse et "humour". L'hôtel est calme, le lobby est agréable (dommage leur fameux bar sur la plage était fermé). Pour l'emplacement, il est à 10 minutes à pied du centre. TOut ce qu'on attend d'un hôtel moderne

“Location, location, location!!!” Stayed here for 1 night in October 09 -- wonderful staff - very friendly and helpful!! Nice rooms, decent size and nice size bathroom - clean, comfy beds. Only 1.5 blocks away from MSG, Penn Station -- wonderful location!!!! Will definitely stay here again!

“Location and staff are redeeming qualities” I was surprised when I entered the hotel based upon the reviews on TripAdvisor. The lobby is tiny and was somewhat unclean. When I returned later in the evening, there was a drunk couple arguing by the check-in desk. I was not acknowledged as a Platinum Ambassador member upon check-in, nor was there any extra amenity provided. Dennis at the front desk as very nice. There is a business center, but no gym in the hotel, which is a major negative. You have to pay $15 to use a NYSC location a block away. Parking is on the other side of the block for $35 with hotel voucher, so if you have a lot of luggage, plan accordingly. What was most upsetting was that they seemed to use my floor as a staging area for equipment. When I got off the elevator after checking in, there was a large luggage trolley impeding access to my room. With a handful of luggage, it was not easy to maneuver. The following day upon checkout, there was a large mattress and the housekeeping trolley right outside my door, which I again had to move. Not very professional. The rooms are tiny, as expected and don't really have great views, even on the higher floors. the elevator was rather slow. I think this hotel needs a major overhaul and I don't felt like I got value for the money paid.

“Very Nice Courtyard Get A Room That Faces it” Although this is clearly an older hotel it is very nice if you have a flight out, or want to schedule a conference. Of course, there are hotels downtown near the Riverwalk, but probably not at this price. There is a great deal of convienent shopping and some very good retaurants nearby. We did have a problem with the plumbing in our room, which we called on several times and they did not fix although we were there two weeks. The carpet was soaked and it may well still be. They also need to install lights in the parking lot, as someone did a smash and grab on one of our party's rental car. All in all, though it was a great place to attend a conference.

“Friendliest place to be!” This review is overdue (sorry!) but what more could we add to all the stellar reviews Chelsea Pines Inn has received?! Stayed here for 8 nights in July. We were a bit on a budget, so opted for the smaller room on a higher floor. Service was fantastic. We were always greeted with a friendly smile from whomever happened to be at the front desk, kitchen, or on any of the floors. Upon check-in, they helped us lug our luggage up to our room, and supplied us with maps and recommendations. Other times they printed out suggestions re: jazz clubs, eats, theatre shows, etc. in whatever area we happened to be that day. A lovely personal note and flowers were a nice touch to make us feel welcomed. There aren't any elevators, and the rooms are a little worn, but it all adds to the charm and preservation of the place. It's clearly marked on their website as well the same. Loved the idea of that all the rooms are named after stars, with posters plastered on the walls. The air con worked fine, and kept our room cool. We thought we'd get a tiny room like previous stays at other NYC hotels, but were pleasantly surprised at the size of the room and bathroom. We even had a view of the courtyard that added to the charm. At times it was hard work climbing those stairs after a long day exploring on our feet, but we just thought of all the pounds we were shedding post eating fest. The complimentary little touches also added up: daily breakfast, fruits, cookies, water, juices, and Nespresso machine available all day, and business center with internet, computers, and printer, and a morning newsletter telling guests about the day's weather and suggested itinerary. Location was fantastic! We enjoyed this area much more than being in Times Square or Central Park. Chelsea/Meatpacking District/Greenwich area was great, so many little eateries, stores, and hidden gems to discover. It made us feel far less "touristy" and more like a local. And when we wanted to visit all the big stops, we were close to 2 subway stations (ACEL line or 123 lines). There were some minor details: wifi wasn't great in our room, but we just hung out in the breakfast/patio area to check our emails. The TV was grainy and not working at one point (but that was quickly fixed).. and we hardly used it anyway. Breakfast was repetitive, but filling enough to give us a good start to our day (great bagels!). If you aren't able bodied, lack of elevator will be an issue. Also if you're allergic to animals, they do have a cat on the premise, but he knows when to be there and when to not be a bother (and he's adorable with his 'stauche!) Highly recommend! We won't be jumping to another hotel when we're back in NYC.. hopefully there'll be a room for us! :)

“Great location” We took the kids to New York and figured this hotel will be perfect for them (hotel is close to Times Square, many water fountains nearby and other attractions). People are welcoming and rooms are big for New York standards. My only complain is that elevators almost take forever to arrive, which could be problematic when you are with kids. Hotel has the same lobby feeling most NYC hotels do. Although it offers a good value for your money.

“Okay, but my British friends would have a problem” We got this reservation on Hotwire, so I won't complain about the small room tucked away in nowehereswville. It was clean, orderly, and comfortable. Staff was polite enough. In short, no major problems. Minor problems? Yeah, sure... Kind of thin walls - heard noise from adjoining room for awhile. I find it annoying when the coffee service in the room doesn't provide tea. This is the second hotel I've been at this year where no tea was available and where the staff would not provide it. I do not drink coffee, but I really enjoy a cup of tea or two or three, as would my friends from Lancashire. We were told here to order it from room service (btw, what is it about NYC room service that puts the prices so stratopherically high that it seems they are trying to discourage it? $50. for breakfast once the various fees and taxes are added? Needless to say, we ate out). You couldn't even buy a box of bags at the nearest Duane Reade as the coffeemaker used Keurig pods. Come on, hotels, get a clue. Some people like tea. And, please, more than two bath towels for two people for two days. I used a hand towel for a bath towel when I took a shower in the morning, since the one other one was used by my partner in crime and one was wrapped around my wet hair. Seems hotels either give you two or two hundred. Positive Perks? Great location if you are coming or going from GCT. Early check-in no problem. Arrived at 12:30 and had a room during the busy holiday season on a Saturday. And, minor but clever, the shower cap for the first time came with one of those mini-scrunchies. I often do use a shower cap and try putting long hair into one without a scrunchie, which I try to have with me but often forget. I found this a thoughtful little thing. Kind of made up for the tea withdrawal.

“Great value on Nob Hill. New hotel.” In my business life I am a Marriott guy. However, I usually like to try something different when I travel on my own dime. I can say that every time I come back to San Francisco (which is every August for the OutsideLands Music Festival) I will stay here. Nicely remodeled rooms and great service. I got a suite overlooking the Bay Bridge and it was fantastic. Perfect location if you are looking for a quiet neighborhood but close to all of the action of Union Sq. I would say this is the best value I have found in SF and I would highly recommend it to anyone.

“Very convenient San Jose airport hotel” My wife, 10-year-old daughter and I stayed here during a one-night layover from a trip to China this month. Our room was very clean and updated, it had a couch and a sitting area, and the two queen beds felt huge, returning from Asia. The bathroom was also clean and updated, with a fullsize tub and shower. The air conditioning was very effective. We checked in late, and the staff was friendly, arranging a cab ride and wakeup call for our return trip to the airport the following morning. The hotel paid for the shuttle ride to the airport. We paid for the cab ride to the hotel, which was within the $15 minimum cab fare from the San Jose airport. Free, fast password-protected Wifi in the room and lobby. The hotel is a short walk from a Denny's restaurant and a Chinese buffet. It's also two blocks from a 7-Eleven store. We had to walk to the 7-Eleven about midnight for toiletries, and there was an oddball mix of characters in the store, but we felt otherwise safe walking in the area within our group. The hotel had a free breakfast starting at 6:30 a.m., but we had to check out before then. We also noticed the hotel had a coin-operated laundry.

“Location,Heavenly Bed, Service WO W !!!” Location, Heavenly Bed and service, Westin knows how to do it and has raised the bar. On a get a way weekend, one thing I look forward to is to going to bed...who can say that at a hotel !! ...Heavenly Bed that is ..hehehe.. that is why I can say that !!!Location was excellent, next to Lord and Taylor, Sax Fifth Avenue, and Nemon Marcus. All in an indoor skyway walk. Also Legal Seafood, which was AWESOME !! Cheesecake Factory and other resteraunts where in the same area. If this is to pricey a block away behind the beautiful and architecturally significant Trinity Church, across from the beautiful Boston Library is Filenes Basement and Marshall, all on the beautiful Newbury street, perhaps better then Chicago's Magnificent Mile ???!?!?!? A few blocks in the opposite direction is the always hip and cheaper H and M store. Westins excellent staff, service, and top notch workout facility made this hotel wonderful. A bar in the hotel, I believed called 10 was great and how convenient !!!! Even the valets went the extra mile for great service. Great weekend get away and great first time trip to Boston !!!

“Great Location, Value” I've stayed here a number of times, and there's no better value for a downtown Chicago hotel. I don't think this is your spot for a romantic getaway, but if you're traveling on business or on a budget, this puts you in the middle of the loop for a reasonable rate. The location is tough to beat, as you're right on the river and within walking distance of both Millennium Park/Grant Park and the Mag Mile. This would be a perfect spot for Lollapalooza attendees. The staff is absolutely over the top in their efforts to be accommodating and welcoming. Other than the location it's the hotel's greatest asset. The rooms have a full kitchen, which again for a budget traveler is a huge benefit. (But less of a value if you're vacationing and plan to eat out a lot) The room layouts are unusual in some cases, but roomy and comfortable. The hotel is probably at the point where it needs a facelift, and in some areas the "wrinkles" are starting to show. Always clean, just well used. The furniture is clean and in good condition. They have a standard free breakfast every morning, which (again) for a dollar-conscious traveler is a huge plus. They have a small business area, though it's best for simply printing off boarding passes. There's free wi-fi that's acceptably fast. So, clean, comfortable, and convenient, just not sexy in any way. HOWEVER, if you're willing to pay for the upgrade, the top-level suites have open air balconies that are awesome.

“Underneath the cool vibe is an excellent hotel” I wasn't sure what to expect, based on website and various online reviews. I was expecting a hyper version of a "W" -- and I try to avoid those. But the Fairmont was booked, and my meeting was in Uptown, so I went for it. I am glad I did. From taxi drop off to taxi pick up, everything was high-touch and great. Friendly service. Big room. Excellent bed and bedding. Little welcome snacks in room. Nicely done minibar. Nice bathroom with good lighting, nice towels, and appealing shampoo, etc. Restaurant was a tiny bit over-priced, mostly on the wine. Food was excellent, and noise level was fun but not chaos. Other than the auto-close slam of doors, endemic in this land, quiet rooms. Sure, the silent screening of "The Matrix" on a wall in the lobby and the very dim lights in the halls at night give it that "look, this is us being edgy" vibe, but it is like the honors student who thinks she/he is being rebellious by getting two earring piercings. This is my new place to stay in Dallas.

“No complaints” A basic highway motel at a good price. Nothing luxurious but no problems either. The front desk was friendly, the room was clean and reasonably quiet, the bed was comfortable, the water was hot, the breakfast was adequate. When they call it a "hot" breakfast that's a bit of an exaggeration. The only "hot" part was some slices of ham and the do-it-yourself waffles. The eggs were hard-boiled. But there was yogurt, fruit, juice, cereal, and coffee so they had the basics covered. For those of us who don't need luxury and aren't willing to pay an arm and a leg, a fine choice.

“A comfortable stay at the Comfort Suites” I was in Charlotte during a NASCAR race weekend. Although I wasn't attending the races, hotels were pretty full and many at the Comfort Suites were obviously race fans (apparel, logos on vehicles, etc.). There were many families with children but I did not hear any disturbances at night. The free breakfast buffet was adequate (not anything to rave about). The room was clean, bedding in good condition, refrigerator working well, etc. I was impressed by the desk clerks and the way one handled a problem with a customer. They were also quick to offer maps and directions to those unfamiliar with the area. The clerks were both friendly and competent--a good combination. I also liked the location, near Interstate 85 exit and just off Billy Graham Parkway but still not noisy traffic. As I said when checking out, I will probably stay there again.

“Doubletree was great!” Traveled with my three teens to NYC for 5 days and 4 nights...and found the Doubletree to be a perfect choice! We were dropped off right in front of the hotel and bellman was ready to take our bags. The security that everyone mentions was consistent....gave you a sense that they were always careful when someone would approach the entryway. Check in was quick and the cookies were good...(however, would have been great if they offered cookies with and without nuts...one son is allergic.) Found the suite to be quite roomy for our needs...and it obviously had been updated...impressed with all the amenities. Our view was a partial one of Times Square...which was good...because the bright lights were great, but not when you're trying to sleep:) Love those "Sweet Dreams" beds...have stayed at the Westin with its' Heavenly beds...and these are a very close second! The only slight negative was that of the Concierge team... Only one went above and beyond the call of duty....Marko. He was very personable...and gave us great advice concerning ballgames...and activities my teens might find enjoyable. The others just seemed to give out only what you asked for...never made suggestions...almost seemed as if you were bothering them. But the very best part of staying at the Doubletree...was it's location! As soon as you stepped outside, you were right in the middle of things...with TKTS directly across the street...and the Grey Line tours only two blocks away...and all of the theates and deli's you could ask for just steps away... It felt very safe...even allowed my kids to go to McDonalds(in the same block as the Doubletree) and Virgin Records...(a couple of blocks down) by themselves. Without a doubt, the next time I come to New York...I'll be staying at the Doubletree.

“Pretty good” I had mixed feelings about this hotel on arrival. Indianapolis appears to be a city with many hotels, and of the Downtown hotels, this seems to be the furthest out of Downtown. It's still a short walk - only 5 minutes to the mall, the Lucas Oil Stadium, etc, though. Parking was good, though it's usually valet - the self park was full 3 out of our 4 nights there. The valets are friendly, and quick - there was both a Colts game and the MotoGP at the speedway while we were there and still no delays. It's only an extra $4 for valet over self-park too. There are boardgames, coffee, a shop, gym, pool and internet in the lobby area - everything felt very close. It's part of a complex of four hotels (with the JW Mariott, the Courtyard and a bridge over to the regular Mariott) and a TGI Fridays (which does room service, which I thought was excellent...). The guy who checked us in was a bit useless though. We asked him for a corkscrew two nights in a row and he couldnt find one. The first time we saw a different guy at the desk we asked him and he immediately handed us one - definitely a mix of quality in the staff - some very useful, some very dopey. Breakfast is great - lots of fresh muffins, bagels, cereal, etc etc. The eating area's big but it's a busy hotel so we still had to eat in our rooms most mornings. It was disappointing that our suite was big, but only had a shower when it could've had a bath. Otherwise though the room was pretty big and well decorated - you can tell its a fairly new hotel. Wireless internet is free and pretty fast (on the 4th floor at least).

“広くて、映画館やショッピングにも最適” ホリデイイン系列のホテルです。 朝食は無料でブッフェスタイルです。 お持ち帰りもOK! コーヒーの紙コップなども用意してくれています。 部屋はとてもきれいで広く、なんといっても放っておいてくれるところが好きです。 部屋にちゃんとしたキッチンもついています。 間食用にポップコーンがついていて、レンジで作れるように なっています。 毎週、フリーディナーもおこなっているようです。 プールやバスケットボールコートもあります。 近くにレストランや、スーパーマーケット(Whole Foods)などもあり大変便利です。 バス停も徒歩圏内に2カ所あり、まもなく近くにターゲットもオープンするようです。 ホリデイインのポイントもたまります。

“Modern, Upscale, Attractive and Good Value for Boston” I stayed here March 15-18 2005 (business trip). Business travelers usually have to stay in large, impersonal hotels in Boston which are devoid of character and have small and worn rooms and so-so service at not so low prices. Sure enough, my company was going to put me up at the Sheraton Boston (corporate rate of $155). Based on TripAdvisor reviews I knew that my experience there would have been mediocre or, at best, fair. So I shopped around for a comparable rate at a better hotel. I had previously stayed at the Topaz in DC, another Kimpton hotel. That is a fantastic hotel. I figured that if the Onyx was half as good, it would still be a very good experience. I shopped around on the web and found the Onyx for $169 on a discounter's web site; called Kimpton and got a rate match. $169 is a very good value for a mid-week stay at this Boston hotel! I was not disappointed with the Onyx. It had a distinctly upscale feel to it. My room was relatively large by Boston Standards. The decor was bright, contemporary and tasteful. The beds plush and comfortable. CD player and large TV (and lots of satellite channels --but no HBO or Showtime). Gourmet coffee in-room. The room was spotlessly clean. The gleaming black marble bathroom was very stylish (the marble's pretty cold to walk on though!) No sign of wear and tear in the rooms at all (the hotel is very new). It was a treat to return to the room after a full day of work. There was not much else to the hotel...there is a small but very stylish lounge (I did not take advantage of the free happy hour). I'm sure it would be fun to have a drink there. There's not much to the lobby; although it is stylishly decorated, it is little more than a hallway! The front-desk service was impeccable and the staff eager to please. The hotel is a 10 minute walk from Faneuil Hall. 2 minutes from the fleet center. 5 minute walk to the North station to catch the T. It's easy to get to all the interesting places in Boston from the Onyx. Tons of eating choices very close by. The cons: the only thing I can think of is that the street the Onyx is on and the nearby Fleet center area are somewhat run-down (vacant office buildings, trash on the street --probably thanks to the clientele of the numerous pubs and fast-food joints, lots of people standing around smoking outside the pubs, several panhandlers near the Fleet center). None of this would deter me at all from staying at the Onyx again though. I wish there was a 4.5 star option...that's what I would give to the Onyx. Stay here if you want a really nice place to stay with good service and well-maintained upscale rooms that have lots of character at not-so-high prices (for Boston).

“Fantastic location for shopping in San Francisco” Two of us stayed at the Westin St Francis for 2 nights. We stayed in the older part of the hotel. The room was big but the condition of the room was average. Wallpaper was peeling off the walls. What we liked about the hotel was the location. We wanted to do lots of shopping and found the location to be fantastic for both shopping and eating. Macy's is just across the road from the hotel. We loved San Francisco and would consider this hotel again despite it not being perfect.

“Wonderful Stay!” Wonderful, warm service and a unique hotel. The views were incredible! Located in the heart of everything. We had a wonderful romantic weekend, - everything we did - great restaurants, shopping and a concert at the Kimmel Center were within walking distance or a short cab ride. The only downside was that the room service took longer than expected once, and the meal was comped because of the delay anyway.

“Good Stay” We had a nice 4-night stay at this hotel for a mini vacation during the last week of August. The location was convenient and we walked to many things. The room was fairly spacious, clean, everything was in good shape and we had an ok view. It was fairly well equipped with a refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker, iron, internet service, etc. One thing I forgot to check for when booking was an in-room safe, which they did not have. They did have safe deposit boxes at the front desk and that worked fine for us. We requested a high floor and they followed through by putting us on the top floor. The staff was wonderful. Over all we enjoyed our stay and would return. Our Sun-Wed stay got us a free night, so it was a great deal for this class hotel.

“Great business hotel” The Grand Hyatt Washington is in a great location and its staff are very service oriented. I had several special requests that were easily accomodated by the staff. Rooms were spacious and comfortable. I have absolutely no complains and would recommend this property to other business travelers.

“Sehr zentral gelegen” Das Hotel liegt sehr nah am Fisherman's Wharf Pier 39. Wer das abends ausgehen möchte, ist mit dem Hotel gut beraten. Muni-Bahn ist in der Nähe, auch zum Cable Car kann man laufen. Die Fähre nach Alcatraz ist auch bequem zu Fuss zu erreichen. Nachteil am Hotel ist, dass es über kein Restaurant verfügt. Fürs Früstück gibt es einen kleinen Stand in der Lobby, an dem man das nötigste fürs Frühstück kaufen kann (Hat nur vormittags geöffnet, ab Mittag muss man sich auch Wasser ausserhalb besorgen). Zimmer haben einen kleinen Balkon, das ich in USA bis jetzt selten hatte. Über Parkmöglichkeiten kann ich nichts sagen, da ich kein Mietauto hatte. Ich habe mich mit AirportExpressSF vom und zum Flughafen bringen lassen und habe den Rest zu Fuss oder mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln zurückgelegt. (Ich war nur zwei Nächte im Hotel)

“Nice Hampton Inn - Spacious Suite” This is a nice hotel. I found the staff to be very friendly and welcoming. I am a gold member with Hilton and was upgraded to a suite without asking. The suite was big with three rooms. Normal sized bathroom, very large living room with a pullout couch bed, desk, chair, refrigerator and microwave and a normal sized bed room with a very comfortable bed. The living room was so big in fact, that it seemed to be lacking furniture compared to the room size. The room was clean. The hotel has wireless internet which worked well. I opted for valet parking for $35 (kind of pricey but it is the city...) as self parking was $25 and across the street in a lot. Close access to getting on the highway too if you're driving. I did have to call down a half hour in advance to pick up my car. Breakfast buffet in the morning had lots of waffle makers so there was no wait along with all of the other standards. Lots of seating. The hotel is right beside the conference center. This Hampton Inn exceeded my expectations!

“Superb Hotel,Staff and Location” We arrived here on the 20th of January for 4 nights got a fabulous suite top floors and smoking as requested. First impression was great it is like walking into yesteryears in a modern way,if that makes sense. They really have taken a once glorious and rich bank and its settings and turned it to a really cool hotel without losing any of its spirit. The staff were exceptionally pleasant and helpful and we on our way to our room with our maps, invitation to complimentary evening reception and all we needed to know in less than 5 minutes. We had a fab suite,separate sitting room and large bathroom spotlessly clean and well stocked. Big comfy bedroom lots of windows so bright and cheerful and relaxing. Loads of in room extras free internet connection, free calls usa in the evening for a certain time and the fridge which was discreetly hidden was very handy. The evening reception was a very casual and relaxed affair with drinks and dips and it was pleasant after a long day out. The location is superb the hotel is on one end of the riverwalk but only a minutes walk to the thick of the action,you are surrounded by a great choice of bars and restaurants and shops.Everything you need is 2/3 minutes stroll away. The rooftop pool is class i did'nt try it but the peace and scenery high above the city is very calming. This hotel is like a home away from home you do as you please with a helping hand and smiling face (and it was never false) right there whenever you wanted. Thanks to all at Drury Plaza

“Luxury Hotel located in great area” This is a very luxurious hotel located in San Diego's Gas Lamp district. There are tons of shops and restaurants within a couple of minutes walking distance of the hotel. All the other reviews are quite right about this place. There is a resort $15 fee which gives you free internet ... I found the $32 Valet parking a bit high, but the service made it worth while. Don't bother looking for cheaper over night parking as you are most likely not going to have much luck. I looked for a self serve 24 hour parking for about 30 minutes and gave up and valet parked the car. Overall this is a very nice hotel if you are willing to spend $250+ per night. I would compare this to a Fairmount hotel in Canada.

“Would definitely book again” Initially, I had mixed feelings about booking this property, as I saw this property was ranked around #100 in NYC on Trip Advisor. But my employer has strict policies that dictate we can't spend more than $300 a night for a room, even in NYC, and the Marriott's price was right for me (and a lot of my regular go-to hotels were sold out). So I decided to give it a shot. After a very efficient check-in, I was pleasantly surprised how nice my $295-a-night room there was. It was much larger than I expected, and it was spotless. There was even a small area for relaxing by a window overlooking Manhattan, with an armchair and table. The decor was unremarkable (i.e., basic) but certainly not worn out or outdated. The bed was extremely comfortable. I did hear some noise from the neighboring room and from the hallway, but the white noise app on my phone did its thing and I slept well. Water pressure in the shower was excellent in spite of my high floor (24?). The concierge staff led me to great choices for sushi (Sushi of Gari, I think it was called) and for bagels (Times Square Bagels, a great takeout option for breakfast that was really reasonably priced). I was just there one night (and was there in NYC less than 24 hours, total), but I would definitely return and stay there again. Great value for such a large, clean room.
