“like the renovated guestrooms!” We have stayed in this La Quinta location a few times in the past years, we skipped a year to stay eleswheree in NYC,. Decided to try LQ again or 2 nights, very happy to experience the updated accomodations! Clean and comfortable and service very friendly and efficient! The only thing missing is the hard boiled eggs( needed the protein and less of the sugary carbs) and packages of oatmeal in the breakfast buffet. Good for a quick stop for a piece of fruit and a hot beverage before hitting the BIG CITY!.I agree with other reviewers, LQ is in a great location! Cabs pick you up right outside this busy area if needed..

“Treated as if we were the only guests there” I can't say enough good things about this hotel. Everyone is so very friendly and helpful, as well as being professional. The head concierge had our room set up with the wine we ordered our step mom and threw in a cheese, cracker and fruit tray. We can't say enough about the other concierge, Jason! He was fabulous! He did everything he could to make our stay exceed any of our expectations. The rooms are clean and spacious and the city view was nice. If there had to by any complaint, it would be that we had no coffee maker in our room -- really not a complaint, just an extra we would have liked. But they offer complimentary coffee in the lobby, as well as fresh lemonade in the afternoon. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone. It is in the back bay district.

“Great hotel in Times Square” We state here for the US Open. It was easy to maneuver from times square to the subway to flushing meadows. The hotel rooms were huge considering you're sitting on times square. The hotel staff was awesome everywhere...except the restaurant. The service was slow even though it was completely empty. I'd still say again, just wouldn't waste my money at the restaurant even in a pinch.

“Good Hotel. Staff is friendly. Beds are comfy.” Good location. Right near airport. Had shuttles running constantly between airport and hotel. Staff is friendly, though they can be a bit rushed when lots of people are checking in. Beds are comfy. Room was large, but appears somewhat dated. Hotel is HUGE (800+ rooms)... so some rooms are fairly out of the way and a hike from the front desk. I was traveling with my sister and her family, so we got a family room. Very nice layout that I haven't seen elsewhere. Basically, 2 rooms connected with 1 bathroom. Had King in one bedroom and 2 queens in the other bedroom. Gave us all the space we needed. No executive lounge here for HHonors members, but I am a Diamond member, so they sent a small fruit and cheese plate to my room. Nice touch. Also had $10 vouchers for breakfast at the restaurant or coffee stand (had breakfast sandwiches, yogurt, etc.) for diamond members.

“Wish the rooms were more soundproof” This is a very nice clean hotel, however, do not get a room near the stairs because the door to the stairs is noisy when it is opened and closed. You can also hear the doors to the adjacent rooms opening and closing and the showers being used in the adjacent rooms. My room had a bathroom with a new walk in shower and a pocket door to the bathroom that you pull out for privacy. The sink was outside the bathroom. The room had a small clean refrigerator and clean microwave but no table for dining so I ate at the desk area. The light around the bed is an overhead florescent tube fixture and there are no table lamps on the bedside. There was a convenient electrical outlet near the bed for computer use and the internet was fast and I could stream netflix movies. The room is small but adequate.

“Great service & experience for the whole family” We stayed here from a Friday night through Sunday afternoon in February. I got a super deal on a room through Hotwire, at $102 per night (which I thought was great.) We had 2 double beds for 2 adults & 2 teens which was plenty. Great view of the harbor and World Trade Center Boston building across the street. We walked just over 1 mile to the New England Aquarium & Legal Seafood Restaurant. The concierge was excellent & saved us tons of time from waiting in line at the aquarium by purchasing a pass before leaving the hotel. Hotel was indeed family friendly as there were lots of families there (many with kids much younger than ours) Clean & serene! Would stay again. The self parking is great, it gets you unlimited in & out access from the underground parking garage for the duration of your stay. Can't say enough great things about this place.

“空港至近、トランジット向けホテル” ロサンゼルス空港近くのインターナショナル・チェーンのホテル。 24時間運行しているホテル専用空港送迎バスにて10分程に位置する。 ホテルの存在目的それ自体が空港利用者客向けであり、 トランジット利用と割り切れば、十分に目的を達しているホテルである。 ホテル周辺の徒歩圏には、 大通り沿いにチェーン系列のファーストフード、ファミリーレストラン等が数軒あるので、 気分晴らしに外食することも可能である。

“Great location and reasonably priced” Stayed for 5 nights in a superior king room. The location is excellent at the Gates to Chinatown and a couple of blocks from Union Square. There are lots of dining options nearby and a good french cafe opposite. Had breakfast in the hotel almost every morning - delicious and good value. Service from staff is OK or below average but most of the time we tend to call our own cabs and bags. The wifi is free but very slow. The room itself was quiet, spacious and clean. We were on the 10th floor overlooking into Chinatown (Grant Ave). Definitely would recommend this hotel purely due to location and good sized rooms.

“Pretty Good!” My partner and I stayed at the Sheraton during the middle of the week while a major conference was going on at the hotel. Our room was on the tenth floor of the East Wing looking over the Marina towards downtown. Pluses: 1) Spectacular view of the San Diego skyline and wonderful location along the marina! 2) Very comfortable beds. 3) The lobby is very nicely designed with a feature called Yahoo Link. PC workstations are clustered in groups around comfortable chairs and tables. High speed broadband service is free along with wireless access if you bring your laptop. Yahoo Link adjoins the Aroma Cafe where snacks and beverages are available. The idea is to create a place to "meet and greet" and hangout. 4) The fitness center is equipped with all new Lifecycle treadmills, bicycles, etc. The facility is spotless and well air conditioned. 5) The lagoon style meandering pool is very nice and in certain places very compatible with lap swimming. Minuses: 1) Room decor in the East Wing needs to be updated. Furniture isn't bad, but the table and floor lamps look like something out of the Victorian past. Previous reviews refer to a nautical theme in the West Wing--hardly the case here. 2) High speed access is $11.95 in the guest rooms--it's still a mystery why upper scale hotels charge for internet access and value hotels don't. 3) Parking is expensive everywhere and no less so at the Sheraton. Overall, I would definitely stay again!

“Excellent value” I don't give five-star ratings very often, but this hotel really delivered. Including taxes, we paid about $250 a night for a two-night stay in June '07. The location is just as many others have described- easy access to the theatres and the rest of Times Square. We've only stayed in NYC one other time- at the Westin- and we were very pleased with the size of the Hampton rooms. Noise was a complete non-issue (we did as another suggested and requested a room away from the elevators). Breakfast was as it always is at a Hampton. If there's anything I'd critique, it'd probably be the concierge. The men on duty during my stay were perfectly pleasant, but didn't seem as knowledgable about NYC as the staff was when we stayed at the Westin. All in all, though, just an excellent property. We'd go back in a heartbeat.

“GORGOUS Hotel in Charlotte!” We stayed here on an overnight while driving from NY to Athens Georgia to get our girl off to grad school. It is directly off the highway and check in was a breeze. We stayed in a 2 room King suite that also had a pull out couch. The room was gorgous, the bathroom large and well stocked-the Bed was super comfy (sofa bed less so-but what do you expect) The free parking lot accomodated our HUGE moving truck and we walked across the street to TGIF for dinner (we were too late for the free evening goodies...darn it!) The free breakfast was pretty good and did I mention it was free! Eggs and meats, waffle maker, cereals, yogart and fruit. Good coffee and juice as well. They are pet friendly as well! I highly recommend this place!

“Need of renovation !” Need of renovation! Indeed, worn carpet and furniture, bathroom sad and gloomy. Good beds. Small room but with a beautiful view of the bay floor 31. Quality service and welcoming lobby.

“Great Property, Friendly staff, excellent location” I arrived around 8:30 pm local time and was greeted by a very polite valet person. He was friendly and directed my inside. The lobby is a bit odd and is set-up in the new fashion without a counter, just a table at check in. The guy working check in was even better than the valet, was incredibly friendly, let me know my room was indeed quite and was in fact upgraded to a suite. Please see my blog at http://talesfromtheroad-mwalno.blogspot.com/ The room is awesome, and the thing that surprises me is how quite it really is...... I walked into the restaurant/bar and there were quite a few people there, it look nice with several big screens, and a lively atmosphere. It is located 3 blocks from the warf and I recommend Scomas for dinner there. I can't stand the Grand Hyatt here, and this really is a great property, I will stay here every time I come to town!!!!

“Great stay!” Hubby and I stayed here for a weekend getaway. We could not have been more pleased with the hotel. It was very clean, rooms were made up very nicely. The front desk staff were very pleasant to do business with. They had a manager's special that evening, and served sodas, wine, and beer, and some snacks. We ate breakfast there the next morning, and the food was good, and hot. We will stay here again on our next trip to San Antonio.

“The location and price were impossible to beat” I guess we got lucky-no noise from teenage drunks or elevators. Location was great. I hate valet parking but there is little choice in downtown Denver and the car retrieval times were actually prompt, not the usual eternity which makes you wonder what the $20 was for. Breakfast was good, not the usual bun passed off as a "continental" breakfast. The room and bath were small but comfortable. My only complaint (which generally applies to Choice Hotels) is that despite Choice Hotels statement that airline milage is available if you ask, the hotel refuses to give it. Most Choice Hotels have a line that they don't know how to enter it in the computer. This hotel just tells you that they won't do it. Choice points are pretty worthless to me and calling to argue with the Choice people is more trouble than it is worth. As an incentive their rewards system is a negative in my book so they have to beat the competition's price badly to get my business. I wish they would drop the whole program and stop bombarding me with spam about the wonders of their program I know I am paying for it.

“Attractive Small Hotel in a Great Location” This small hotel is located on the edge of Washington’s beautiful Embassy Quarter and a twenty-minute walk will take one to the White House and Mall areas. The first impression was not good – the lobby is somewhat Spartan and there are four steps to be surmounted with baggage to reach the corridor leading to the lifts. No assistance appears to be available and this, and the steps, would rule this hotel out for older travellers or any who are wheel-chair dependent. I was however very pleasantly surprised by my room, which turned out to be large and well furnished, as well as immaculately clean and well cared for. A simple breakfast is served in the morning (coffee, juice, pastries and cereal). There is no restaurant attached but Washington, as a city, is not deficient in this respect and so it is not a drawback. I know Washington well, both as a tourist and for business reasons, and were I making an extended visit I would certainly consider making this hotel my base.

“I do not care HOW close this place is to the airport...” My room was a dump. In my opinion, this hotel has GIVEN UP. First thing I saw when I opened the door: A HOLE IN THE CARPET! A dirty, nasty looking hole in the carpet, right by the door. How could they not fix this before selling the room! There is NO WAY that the hotel did not notice this hole, it was THAT bad. This room, with a nasty hole in the carpet and paint and or wall paper peeling right off the walls should NOT be sold as anything other than a 1 star. The faucet in the bathroom was crooked and off center. Strange. There was no working clock in the room. The TV was straight out of the 80's. Weird smell in the room. The closet doors would NOT open. The walls are THIN. Do yourself a favor and do NOT worry about the airplane noises. Worry more about the noise from the hallway and the rooms next door! (There is a good inch between the floor and the actual bottom of the door.) When I called for a wake up call, the person at the front desk did not even know my room number. Normally, when I call the desk, the know right away who is calling. That made me nervous, so I set my iPhone to wake me. The ceiling had patched areas. Not sure what happened, but for some reason, they had to patch the ceiling. Bathroom: SMALL. When you open the bathroom door, you practically hit the toilet with the door. THAT is small. Scuff marks all over the walls as well. This room was just not good. I am a nice guy. Super cordial to the front desk. No attitude and VERY polite. Why did the front desk guy do this to me? What did I do to deserve this room? Are all the rooms this bad or was I just being punished? Did I remind the front desk guy of someone who stole his girlfriend in High School? He seemed nice enough, or are all the rooms this bad? If all the rooms are this bad, I am shocked they are still in business. If all the rooms are NOT this bad, then I was ripped off. The lobby actually looked nice so I was very surprised to be put into a 1 star room. Oh, but they have free WIFI! This is the first time I have added pictures. These pictures were taken very late at night. Sorry about the quality. Trust me when I say the photos make it look better than it actually was....

“Nettes Hotel für jüngeres Publikum” Hippes, trendiges Hotel, das sehr schöne Corner Rooms hat. Die Einrichtung ist nett gemacht und setzt sich von normalen Starwood Hotels ab. Nette Fensterbänke, die als Sofa genutzt werden können. Nette erwerbbare Goodies auf dem Zimmer. Das Zimmer war sehr groß und auch sauber. Allerdings sind auch Dogs Welcome, daher ist bei manchen Zimmern Vorsicht geboten. Das W bietet gegen Gebühr auch einen TownCar Service an. Der Pool und Partybereich im ersten Stock ist sehr nett gemacht, nur kann es des Nächtens auch sehr laut werden. Das Gaslamp Quarter ist in ca. 10-15 min zu Fuss zu erreichen. Das Hotel liegt direkt neben einem offenen Parkplatzgelände, aber es ist nicht unsicher.

“Wow!!!” I can't imagine how I could add anything further to the already-glowing reviews of this place. We had a fabulous experience here! Actually, we had a pretty awful experience at another D.C. hotel and, after 2 nights at that other hotel, we decided to look for another place to stay. We ended up booking 1 night here and, let me just say, it was a breath of fresh air. The hotel was elegant, immaculately clean and beautifully furnished. Our room had a bit of a Hollywood glamour-ish style going on, and my husband and I opted out of going out that night to instead just put on the plush robes, sink into the comfortable beds, and relax. The valet was fabulous and, with in-and-out service, they always had our car ready within minutes of us requested it. Overall, would I stay here again? Absolutely. If I go to D.C. again, I won't even consider staying elsewhere! Bravo, Hotel Palomar. We are avid travelers and have had the opportunity to stay in many elegant hotels abroad, but you have found repeat customers in us.

“Nice hotel, VERY friendly staff” What I noticed most during my stay here was how polite, friendly and accommodating the staff was. From first check in until we left, the staff was great--always called me by name, smiled, and acted like they really enjoyed working there. They moved me to a different room because I ended up into one of the smallest. The funny thing was the move ended up being a few square feet bigger, but it was fine. The rooms here for the most part (unless you get a suite) are pretty small. I didn't even have the smallest room and was surprised at how small it was. Despite that, the room was very clean, as was the bathroom. The showers had awesome water pressure and I liked the toiletries. The hotel is in a decent location. A short walk to Union Square and to the BART. I would definitely stay here again.

“Comfortable and swanky hotel in beantown” Stayed in a Wonderful King - nice size room and comfortable. Bed was amazing, as all W's seem to be. Only set back was the location. The hotel borders a sketch area, especially at night. One block you're from the Commons, but one block in the other direction and you're holding onto your purse. I was suprised the W picked this location, but I suppose the area is "up and coming" so maybe it won't be like this for much longer. Room was fairly cleaned, but found plastic bags from previous guest and a wash cloth in between the wall and dresser. Both those things were there the entire visit, along with the iron board and iron that I had used Friday night. I am a clean freak, I'll freely admit, but I don't think it's much to expect a thoroughly cleaned room. I booked an in-room massage with Bliss for when I arrived and it was excellent. Probably one of the best massages I've ever had. I also booked services at Bliss and they were outstanding. Definitely highly recommend that spa/in-room services. HD TV in room was nice, but all movies, "just missed tv," and music all had to be paid for. Was a bit annoying, but you don't go away to watch tv right? Unless you're entertaining kids... Bouncer-like concierge guarding the hotel at night is annoying. I'm not sure why people stand on line to hang out at the hotel lobby bar, I don't see it as being such a hip/swanky place, but maybe it is for Boston. There should be a separate entrance for guests so you don't need to get death stares when you're walking to the head of the line trying to get into your hotel for the nigh. Overall, nice, relaxing, and pleasant stay so all the borderline issues were easily erased from memory. Would recommend for singles/young couples/girls/guys weekend away. Not a family place or an older persons retreat by any means.

“Convenient to Airport!” Stayed here for one night, as we were coming in from out of town and flying home out of DFW early the next AM. Rooms very spacious and clean. Beds were very comfortable. Bathroom was clean and well appointed. I did have a chance to use the fitness center and it was very clean, had good amount of equipment and plenty of clean towels. We had dinner and drinks in the lounge one night and the food was ok, typical bar food. BUT we had breakfast in the cafe in the AM, did the Breakfast buffett, and it was very good. Lot's of variety and good quality food w/ omelettes to order! Went out on the town that night and the concierge hooked us up with some ideas and free passes and got us a cab there and back. Even though this place is right at the airport, you do not hear any of the jets landing or taking off. I was very impressed with the sound proofing and it made for a great nights sleep! I would recommend this to anyone in town on business or pleasure and wanting a place to stay, very convenient to the airport and needing to fly out on American. If you are flying in or our on another airline, they will give you a free shuttle ride to those terminals, but they are not walking distance.

“Dirty” I stayed at the Red Roof once last month in Chicago for $99 a night, and my room had recently been renovated, was clean with a desk and ample outlets. The location is terrific. Based on those benefits, I decided to stay there again a few days ago. Bad idea. This time I was in a smelly room on the 6th floor that was dirty and dusty. The radiator was very loud and didn't make the room warm, so I finally gave up and turned it off. Plus my room rate was $140. I twice had difficulty getting into the room because my key didn't work. The hallways were narrow and dim, with streaks and scratch marks from people's luggage rubbing everywhere. The people at the front desk asnwer your questions, but do so with reluctance. So, if you decide to stay at the Red Roof, make sure you at least ask for a renovated room!

“Fantastic stay and great location!” We stayed at the Taj in Boston for my birthday celebration and also because we have stayed in Taj hotels in India. This is the original Ritz Carlton hotel in Boston. It is right on the Boston Commons. Newbury street--the Rodeo Drive of Boston is one of the entrances to the hotel. We booked a "junior" suite---it was about 550 square feet with a separate living room with a working fireplace and a separate bedroom. The marble tiled bathroom was small (probably due to the age of the building) but it was well stocked with large sizes of Moulton Brown shampoo, conditioner and bath gel products. We had access to the Taj Club. It was well worth it! It seemed the Club was serving food all day long. Not just snacks but enough food that you could make a meal, especially at dinner time! Everyone in the Club was extremely helpful. It is a dignified, classy hotel. I would definitely stay there again. Also note that at the resturaunt that they served very delicious Indian food. Not an inexpensive place but worth every dollar!

“Rundown and smelling of curry” I stayed here for business due to it's location and price and could not have been more disappointed. Check in took 20 min and we were the only guests there. While checking in, guests came by to complain of leaking water pipes, out of service toilets, etc. A thick, recent coat of paint haphazardly covers all services and the hotel smells bad. Spend $15 more and stay elsewhere.

“Embassy at Convention Center” Just a few blocks from Metro Center and Gallery Place/Chinatown, this hotel is in a good spot. The suite was large and had a nice sized bathroom, too. It was clean and quiet, plus a good, hearty breakfast buffet.

“Top Hotel... aber nicht billig” Das Hotel ist riesig aber ausgezeichnet gepflegt. Es war (wie immer bei Hyatt) ein toller Aufenthalt. Man kann auch alles im Hotel finden - kleine Geschäfte, viele Restaurants & Bars.... Ich würde auch ein Regency Club Zimmer empfehlen - erstens der Blick auf Chicago River war unvergesslich und auch das Continental Breakfast und Cocktails & kleinigkeiten zum Essen am Abend sind mehr als genug für einen Tag. Man bekommt dort auch alkoholfreie Getränke fast rund um die Uhr. Das Personal was toll - auch einige deutschsprachige Mitarbeiter getroffen was eigentlich für die USA sehr selten ist. Wenn sie parken vollen - besser ein Parkplatz/Parkhaus ausserhalb des Hotels suchen sonst wird es echt teuer - mindestens 50 Dollar pro 24 Stunden rechnen. Ja, alles toll... aber die Preise sind entsprechend hoch für eine Privatreise

“Price was right!” Stayed here for two days in early september. Room was small, but for the price, the value was unbeatable (for san francisco atleast). Free parking was a huge plus. There is no AC, but in SF you rarely need it. Request an inner room, due to noise on street. Very close to bus to Wharf area. Would stay again.

“Great location and beautiful foyer” Located a short walk from the White House, DC Mall and Smithsonian Museums, the JW is perfectly situated to experience DC's biggest attractions. The foyer and entryway is gorgeous as guests are greeted by a friendly a professional staff. The restaurant/lounge is trendily decorated and has an energetic buzz about it. The rooms are well appointed, but not much different from the recently renovated Marriott properties - a disappointment when you consider the premium rates demanded by JW. The pool is average at best, while the gym is more than adequate for a good away from home workout. Overall, the JW is an excellent option for anyone looking for a comfortable and well appointed hotel in the heart of DC.

“Great New Hotel” We stayed only 1 night and were really impressed. The room was spacious, beds very comfortable, free internet in the room worked great. There is a small indoor pool, & a great Sports Bar/Grill where we had a nice meal reasonably priced. The business Centre with free internet & printer worked great & was open 24 hours... We did not intend to go to S?eaworld; just could not resist a great new hotel reasonably priced...

“Almost Perfect” Gorgeous hotel, gorgeous room, and very convenient location. The bed is very comfortable with lovely pillows. The bathroom is very nice and the toiletries provided are amazing! The staff is also very courteous and welcoming. The only issue I had was that housekeeping did not make up my room at all during my two-day stay. Otherwise, I highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting D.C.!

“quite satisfied again with the aloft brand” This was my second stay at an aloft hotel and the design and amenities are all pretty much the same since they are all new hotels. The check-in person was very nice as were the parking attendents. It cost $6 for daily parking right outside. Everything was very clean and the rooms were all nicely furnished. The location was very convenient to most major historical attractions. Will definately stay here again during future visits. There are 2 other spg properties in this same location for those that might be interested. Pool was small, but fine for my young kids, workout room was nice as well.

“Impressed” This was my first time at a Home2. As a Hilton Diamond member, I tend to expect a lot. This place was nice. The colors and atmosphere was bright and warm, similar to aLoft in style. The only complaints were the layout of the breakfast area was very poor and the iron in the room was very cheap. I actually had to go to Walgreens accross the street to get starch to iron my shirt.

“Nothing exceptional” This hotel is not as impressive as I expected, especially for the price. Self parking is $17 per day. The rooms are clean, but small. The bathroom is very small. The concierge lounge, open to Gold Elite members and up, was just so-so. The decaf coffee was lukewarm two evenings when I went for dessert at the concierge lounge. The best thing about this hotel is the location - lots of shopping and restaurants nearby. Also, good selection of TV channels to watch. Overall, this hotel is OK as long as your expectations are not too high.

“The roof top bar is awesome” What a great little gem. We enjoyed the bar so much. Great music, nice crowd and great drinks. The view of the city is spectacular. Truly a perfect ending to a wondeful night in NYC!

“It's Why We Stay at a Marriott” In town for a conference. $45 cab ride from airport. lobby is on same level as car port. registration was fairly quick, although I did see a line later in the day. Have to give props to Alan who set us up with a fantastic corner room on a high floor, overlooking St. Patrick church. Windows wrapped around the entire length of the room. Great comfortable bed. enough drawers for a couple's week worth of clothes. Work area a little cramped, only one easy chair. Adequate bathroom, Bed & Bath brand toiletries. Plenty of restuarants on premis. Great part of the city. Concierge level did a good job of replenishing for what was a highly active dinning area.4th Street Grill, sports pub, is accross the car port. Not marked very well. If you're in with a big group, beware: all 25 cardio machines were in use by the time I arrived just before 6 am. All the east coaster are up early! if you can, go on your lunch break- wide open. Good hotel.
“As good as good can get!” High high end boutique hotel. Elegant in heart of City. Great value.

“An excellent choice outside of Union Square” Don't park at the hotel, use the Mission Street Garage behind the hotel. It will save you 20-30 dollars per day. It is perfectly within walking distance from Market Street/Union Square. And if the distance is still too far, there are plenty of shopping to do in between. The corner junior suite is big, and the wrap around floor to ceiling windows allow you to watch the fog roll in and out of the city. The lobby can get crowded and noisy at night (bar/restaurant). We walked around town, visited the museum of modern art, and ate at the restaurants along SOMA. The area is relatively safe at night, provided you don't wander West or South of the hotel. Overall, you will get a bigger room for the price when compared to the hotels located immediately around Union Square.
“綺麗なヘアでゆったりと” 毎回ジュニアスイートに宿泊致しました。 寝室と居間があるのでそれなりに広さを感じます。 多分部屋の広さは50~60m2弱ではないでしょうか。 ソファーも通常のソファーと窓越しに固定設定されたソファーがあり ソファーが多く、ゆったりできます。

“Excellent Staff - Extremely Quiet” The staff was friendly and efficient at all hours. When I arrived I needed to obtain a joke gift. The front desk clerk had a phone number for me to call. Thursday night I needed to secure chair rentals and an other clerk help me locate a convenient rental company. Housekeeping were like ghosts. The professionalism of the staff was superior. Pickings were slim during the Democratic Convention, but I was in Austin for a wedding. The hotel was packed, but the room was cool and quiet. The air conditioning was quiet also. A family was staying in the suite next to me and I didn't hear a thing. The hotel is older and starting to get the musty smell. If you have allergies or require a renovation within 2 years, this is not the hotel for you. The hotel is convenient to I 35, Wal-mart, Sams, the airport, and a business park. There is a walking path through the business park. I felt safe and comfortable. I made it to First Thursday in SoCo. www.firstthursday.info Music and people watching were great. It's only a five minute drive to South Congress & Mary St.

“Top Notch for this hotel brand” This hotel strives to be the best. Upon arrival, you see the table full of awards they have acquired. Check in was effortless, and if you are a Priority Club member, you also get a welcome bag of snacks and water. The double bed room was spacious, and the alarm clock has a dock for your iPod or iPhone. I'm used to there being electrical outlets on the lamp base, however, there were none here. There were more tv channels here than i have ever seen at a hotel, and surprisingly, FOUR premium channels-two HBO and two Showtime channels.

“Never again” I am a real Marriott fan and I have stayed at this hotel several times before without incident but this time was a disaster. There were dirty room service dishes (not mine) in the hallway for days, even after I complained several time. My room was not serviced ("The housekeeper for this room is new and must have forgotten" was the response I got). My car was not brought up when I called the valet (he said no one "told him" to bring it up). And when I asked the front desk attendant for the name of the GM, he said he didn't know who the GM was. Really??? You don't know your boss' name? Although they were ALL very apologetic, this was just a service nightmare. In all fairness, I have written the GM but have not heard back yet as it is too soon. But there were just too many problems and I expect more from a Marriott.

“Very Nice Boutique Hotel” This hotel is not even near Times Square, so not sure where the name came from. But it is very conveniant to 5th and Madison Avenues and worked perfectly for the business meeting I had in that area. Nice rooms, nice ammenities, and reasonable price for mid-town Manhatten. Very helpful and friendly staff. I would definitely stay at this hotel again, but if you are looking for walking proximity to the theatre district this may not be the place for you.

“The Best” This is a review I've hesitated to write, because I didn't want to share this gem with anyone else. I've stayed in a great many wonderful hotels, and the Pacific Terrace ranks among the very best. It is, I dare say, my favorite hotel in North America. The views are absolutely sublime, and the rooms themselves are beyond comfortable. The friendly service is second to none. From the moment you arrive, you slow down. It is not a super-swift or efficient check-in process, but you very quickly discover that you don't WANT it to be. This is a place where everything is personal - at reception, you are instantly treated as a friend who deserves personalized service. It is, after all, a beautiful hotel on the beach, so why would you want to continue rushing? The hotel does not have an actual restaurant on the premises, but they have arranged room service with several of the local restaurants. In addition, a brief stroll down the beach takes you to Jordan's restaurant, where the food and service are MAGNIFICENT, and you can conveniently charge your meal to your room... I've now stayed there on numerous occasions, in 3 different style rooms. Yes, if they aren't full, you get an upgrade you will never forget, but even in the most basic room, you are bathed in the sound of the surf, while you sip cocktails on your private balcony. Would I return? Oh yes. I have, and will continue to do so.

“Loved it” We booked a two bedroom suite, that had three bathrooms, kitchen and full living room. We stayed one week and were very pleased with our stay. There were 5 adults. Each bedroom had its own bathroom, with another bathroom off the living room. The kitchen had a coffemaker with a full size fridge. We used the fridge for leftovers, soda and water. Made coffee almost every morning unless we visited Dunkin Donuts right downstairs. (yum, great coffee). We booked our room far in advance so we got a great rate. I have stayed at the Grand Central Hyatt and have paid the same price for their little crackerbox room as we paid for this big suite. This was great. We never at anytime felt cramped because the room was sooo big. Used the internet which they do charge for. They even have washers and dryers downstairs available for guests. $2.00 to wash & $2.00 to dry. Concierge was a great help. Even purchased tour tickets from them. The housekeeping staff accidently threw away a couple of Metro passes and the hotel immediately replaced them. There is a little market right next door for soda, water or snacks. Penn Station right across the street. Never really bothered by any sirens as others have said. Also, our living room and one bathroom backed right up to the elavator. Never heard a sound. This is a very beautiful old building with alot of character. Love the Affinia hotels. This is the 2nd one I stayed at in New York. Next time we'll try another Affinia. The staff is the best!!!!!!!!!!!!

“good, not great.” My husband and I were traveling with our 2 and 4 year old first off (yikes) for a two night stay in San Diego. We asked for two queen beds which we were given. Upon arrival we asked if we could upgrade to a suite so that the little girls could have their own space, but the hotel did not have upgrades (this was fine, it was a weekend and we understand). The room itself was "ok", with pretty decor. Very cramped for a family of four, but woud have been fine for two people. We had a pool view which was nice and the patio is spacious (we were on the 5th floor). We did not use the pool, but it looked well kept and pretty. The bathrooms need a remodel (tub was cracked, floor was very tired looking, tiny). Here is the good: 1) It is in "hotel circle", which means that you are in a cricle with dozens of hotels and close to all of the attractions (Seaworld, etc). You are also right off the freeway, so it is noisy and bustling. The hotel provides you with several amenities for this reason (CD to help you sleep, sleeping linen spray, eye covers, etc). 2) I thought the food room service was excellent. We ordered it twice and both times, the food was really good and the service was speedy(what a plus for two little kids) 3) The black out curtains are awesome and it stays so dark in that room that my kids actually slept in b/c of that until 8am (unheard of). 4) There are lots of movie channels and movies on demand which we like for us and the kids. Here is the bad (which was really bad for me): 1)Cleaning room service never came. We stayed for two nights. After ordering food room service, giving two little kids baths, etc our room and bathroom was in desparate need of housecleaning (especially with how small the rooms are). I was beyond disappointed when i came back to the hotel at 4pm to find a messy room (after being with two little kids at Legoland all day). We had been gone since 9 am! We called down to front and the manager said that housecleaning was gone for the day and they had not gotten around to cleaning our room. My husband said this was unacceptable and that we have small children and that we need a clean room (not to mention towels). The manager said that he would find someone to clean it within 2 hours. So, we left (again after a full day at Legoland already) and came back in two hours to find a room that was cleaned to about 80% cleanliness (we took what we could get) 2) The bedding linens and bathroom towels are unacceptable in my opinion (gosh- Crowne Plaza spring for some nice linens). I have never, ever felt such rough and cheap bedding(even in 1 star hotels). I thought maybe it was me, but my husband and 4 year old complained the next morning as well and said that the bedding felt like "sleeping on towels". He was so right! We actually went to a local Target and bought some blankets to use for our second night! Talk about desparate, huh. I do not think that i will stay here again and with all of the choices that you have on hotel circle, you can probably pick a better one. Again, there were some positives which may outweigh my negatives for you?

“Much better than ratings suggest” We bid for this hotel on Priceline and were not expecting much after reading some of the TripAdvisor reviews for our purchase. We were very pleasantly surprised. The rooms were clean and fresh (renovation couldn't have been that long ago). The room was not large by American standards, but was quite adequate. It has a very large uncluttered desk with a flat panel television. They even addressed two of my pet peeves suggesting that someone might have read my previous reviews: The bed was made without the top sheet and bedding tucked in--allowing one to get into bed without pulling the under-sheet loose. The labels on the shampoo and other bottles were huge so that those of us requiring glasses need not fear the inadvertent application of hand lotion to the hair. Some reviews made note of a dangerous neighborhood. This was not our experience at all. We walked several blocks immediately after dark one evening and felt safe--even the Deadheads outside the adjacent arena were more happy than threatening. If you do not want to pay the hotel's parking charge, a public parking directly across from the hotel entrance charges only $7.75 overnight.

“Convenient - Clean - Good Lobby” The shuttle service is good running every 20 minutes. I arrived early and no lunch is served at this hotel, you have to walk over to the Sheraton Suites. I had to wait for an hour to get a room - but, I was early. The lobby is nice with a few tvs and a good bar area. The roofs have free wired internet- but it worked well. there was a good desk area to work. The Four Points was the lowest priced in the three SPG properties. It works well for an airport hotel. Do not hesitate to stay here for airport convenience.

“Location was good, but room was filthy” I can say for a fact that I've never been given a hotel room this dirty before. Since the hotel was "sold out", there was nothing they could do to offer me a better room apparently. The bathtub was dirty and I refused to take a shower, so I really am glad I was only here for a short time. And $40/night for parking was totally ridiculous! This hotel is overpriced. I usually stay at the Courtyard Marriott when I'm in Boston, but this hotel was a bit cheaper so I tried it...let's just say I'll never stay here again. The only plus for me was the location - it's walking distance to many restaurants and shops (but, then again, so are lots of other hotels.)

“Overpriced and disappointing” As a frequent traveler to Chicago, I always welcome the opportunity to come back to a city that has some of the best hotels in the US. Usually I stay at the Park Hyatt or the Peninsula, but our conference was at the Marriott so I stayed there out of convenience- what a mistake! For over $300, you get a room smaller than some closets, with virtually no amenities. The Michigan ave location is good, but for another $150, the Park Hyatt is sure to delight you!

“Before You Stay Here...Think Again!!!” I recently took my mother-in-law to the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville and made the mistake of staying at The Inn at the Mayo Clinic Managed by Marriott...and I even called and talked with a night manager before making the decision to stay at this hotel. The advantages of this Marriott hotel are the location with direct indoor access to the Mayo Clinic, wheelchairs for use in the hotel and at the Mayo Clinic, and kitchenettes in every room. The disadvantages of this Marriott hotel are the malfunctioning mechanical systems, poor maintenance, and inadequate management response...more of what I would expect from a Holiday Inn or Red Roof Inn rather than a Marriott hotel...and also don’t expect to sleep in this Marriott hotel! The first night I went to bed early but was then awoken by three fire alarms at approximately 9:00 PM, 10:00 PM, and 11:00 PM...after the first fire alarm I was went to the Lobby and let the firefighters into the building since the night manager could not be found...and after the last fire alarm the alarm system was “shut off” for the night but restarted again with another fire alarm at 7:00 AM (I only got three hours sleep). The second night I went to bed early again but was then awoken by a woman arguing on a cell phone in the courtyard between our room and the Lobby...and when I went to the Lobby to report the problem the night manager did nothing to address this situation. However, this was the night that we also realized that there was a significant problem air conditioner in the closet of the one bedroom suite...basically the air conditioner was “oversized” and very loud...and it would continuously cycle on and off if you closed the bedroom door...and also maintained the temperature at 66F regardless of the thermostat...eventually to sleep we had to turn off the air conditioner and awoke early in the morning when the room became very warm (I only got six hours sleep). The third night I went to bed early again but was awoken by a problem with the refrigerator which was making a very loud noise which only stopped when I unplugged the refrigerator so I could get some sleep (finally got eight hours sleep)...I reported these problems to maintenance in the morning and was told, “We get a lot of complaints on the air conditioners.” Lastly, I chose this Marriott hotel because of the location and the complimentary breakfast...but although the complimentary breakfast looked great it was basically made with cheap generic food that had no taste...the only thing I would recommend eating would be the donuts, hard boiled eggs, bananas, apples, yogurt, and milk...and don’t try the waffles, oatmeal, bread, bagels, grits, and coffee. In conclusion, if you have to stay at this Marriot hotel I recommend that you request a studio room to minimize the problem with the air conditioner, bring your own breakfast foods to supplement the complimentary breakfast, and call Marriot Customer Service at --- if you have any problems...and if you don’t believe my review is accurate please request Suite 123 and see if you have a better experience...definitely not what I expected for $190/Night.

“Nicest Hotel, for the entire Roadtrip” This was probably was of the nicest hotels, we had stayed at for our entire 5 week roadtrip, the only problem was the bathroom and slow valet pick up. We stayed here 4 nights, the room was the smallest we had, had but this is downtown. The room was nicely decorated, double beds, the issue was the bathroom, was werid slide along door, that like to come out of it's hinges, and shower that liked to flood the bathroom floor, housekeeping always lined the shower edge with towels, the shower needed to be dipped into the floor. We had a car, valet was $26 a day, but this was the cheapest decent hotel I found in San Diego including valet, though you could have a wait alittle while in the morning to get your car. Good location, tourist attractions are quite close in SD, we never got stucked in traffic. Room could get nosiy though, we faced the Greyhound bus Station, and would hear alot of beeping, and sirens all through the day and night. I have never heard so many emergency vehicles sirens before, and I though San Diego was one of the safest cities. Would stay again.

“Nice location and room but very noisy” This hotel is very well placed for visiting San Antonio. The hotel is very nice and our room was spacious and comfortable with a great shower. I thought the valet parking as USD39.00 per night was a little steep. One downside was, we were on the city side of the hotel, and it was very noisy with traffic noise, trains etc all night so we did not sleep that well. Even though the staff were great and the room was good and it was good value for money, because of the noise I am not sure we would stay here again.

“Not the handiest base for sightseeing.” We stayed here for three nights. Our room was on the tenth floor at the front overlooking the street. The windows were not double-glazed and it was a bit noisy. Also the bedding was very warm which didn’t help when it came to sleeping. Apart from this the room was clean and comfortable and the aircon unit was good. We ate dinner one night in the hotel’s Interlude Bar and Grill and found the food and service to be good and the prices reasonable. The service and choice at breakfast was good too. The position of the hotel is not the greatest when it comes to sightseeing and the area around the hotel is a bit run down.

“Closest to the new terminal great value.” We needed to stay close to the airport due to bad weather and an early flight. They have a very nice stay park and fly program. I was able to negotiate an excellent rate for a family of five. They offered us a handicap room and a roll away bed. This worked great for us. The hotel is three years old and still feels new. Breakfast saved us at least $30 since we didn't need to eat at the airport. I highly recommend this hotel. The only downside is the lack of restaurants for dinner due to its location in a newly developed area. However with proper planning that issue can be avoided by stopping prior to your check-in.

“Best hotel we stayed at the end of our trip to Colorado and Wyoming” great hotel, friendly staff at the front desk. large clean modern room. great biscuits at front desk. staff upgraded us after checking loyaly card. brilliant. totally recommend this and will return.

“Does not deserve 'Grand' status” We have stayed at other Grand Hyatts (Kauai and Indian Wells) and they lived up to the Grand status that Hyatt gives their premier properties. However, Hyatt should reconsider giving this property the Grand status. We stayed at this hotel from December 2-4 and found that hotel to be just average. Positives: (1) Location: Easy walk to Times Square and Rockafellar Center. The 4,5,6 subway in the adjacent Grand Central station. (2) Check in: Fast and friendly Negatives: (1) Room: Bathroom was no larger than 30sf. Very small and was not condusive for two people to prepare for a night out at the same time. The toilet had a handle (like a public restroom) would leak if it were not returned to its horizontal position. Don't think housekeeping does detailed cleaning between guest. Dust on the phones and hair in the corner of the bathrooms. (2)Cost: We are Gold passport members and used points for one night and were charged $650.00 for the Saturday night + $2.00 per bag to have them stored at the bell desk after check out. If you can book this hotel at $200.00 per night, do it. But do not spend more than that for this average hotel. There far superior hotels in the city for the $650.00. Sorry Hyatt, but we will not be staying at this property again. We will take our money and spend it at truley "Grand" facilities such as the Ritz Carlton Battery Park for a few hundred dollars less per night.

“Just another Courtyard on the inside” Let me start by saying that I stayed here using Marriott Rewards Points from July 20 to July 23, 2006. So I cannot judge the value of my stay. If you have seen one Courtyard hotel room, you have seen them all. Furnishings were fairly new but uninspiring. Bathroom was basic. Sink area was too small for two people. Typical Courtyard with basic features. Nothing new to report about this Courtyard. The property itself is kept very clean. Check-in was a breeze. Although, I did request to be upgraded to a suite but the front desk clerk informed me that they were completely booked. I did not challenge the clerk, but I logged on the Marriott website before arriving and it showed availability for suites during my stay. I am an elite member and they choose to ignore my request. We had a nice City View with a view of they "pyramid" building on the 14th floor. Soap and shampoo were no name brands unlike other Marriott properties which use Bath and Body Works products. If you are picky about hair products like I am, be sure to bring your own. The Courtyard is in easy walking distance to AT&T Park and the Muni/BART Station (15 to 20 minutes). If you are walking from the Muni/BART Station, I recommend walking on the north side of 2nd Street. For some reason, this side is more developed and nicer. The homeless tend to stay on the southside during the evenings. Union Square is one Muni/BART station away. We found a great Thai restuarant on 2nd street a couple blocks away called Osha. Roys is also a couple blocks away also. Starbuck in lobby is convenient but hours limited. You can charge your drinks and food to your room. To summarize, a typical Courtyard. Room very clean and comfortable. Free wired internet in the rooms.

“Second visit this year, Quality, Friendly, Service!” In the first week in August, 2010, I returned for a couple of nights at the Ritz Carlton Philadelphia. I am impressed with the upbeat and positive demeanor of the employees who work at this hotel. The location is great. The ambiance exceptional. The food is very, very good. Two employees recognized me from an April stay and greeted me. I have recommended this hotel to many friends and associates. I stayed in a spacious corner room near the top and with a panoramic view of Broad Street.

“Pleasant and very comfortable, and a fantastic price for quality and location!” This hotel is among the nicest we've ever stayed, starting with the lovely people - friendly and helpful. Our twin room was (contrary to popular belief) actually very spacious for new york, and we had great sleeps with little to no road noise. Beds were very comfortable and bathroom was nice too. The best thing about our room was that however much we looked carefully, we found no, I repeat not a single bed bug! The location of this hotel was wonderful, right across from the belasco theatre and right beside the lovely saju bistro which we ate at every night. This hotel is so worth the reasonable prices, so stop reading other reviewers' complaints about small rooms and unfriendly staff (neither of which are true) and book accomadation at this wonderful boutique hotel in the perfect location! You wont regret it!

“Gracious, yet unpretentious” I stayed at the RBI for two nights and it was one of the nicer places I've stayed ever. The staff is friendly and accommodating, the grounds are lovely, and the rooms are spacious and comfortable. The property is in a residential neighborhood and is surrounded by golf course, so it's quiet and tranquil. The place is laid out so that you never feel like you're in a big resort -- there are plenty of private places throughout the grounds so you can sit by a fire or a fountain or on your own balcony or patio. It's perfect if you're looking for some peace and quiet. The Veranda restaurant is a nice outdoor space for breakfast, lunch, or a sunset dinner, and the sports bar inside is comfortable and good for a happy hour cocktail or beer. My room had a king bed and a large soaking tub with a separate shower, as well as his and hers sinks. It also had a Keurig coffee maker and small refrigerator. The spa was great -- I had a really good Swedish massage and spent some time by the adults-only saline pool. The place was really busy -- several weddings during my weekend stay -- but it never felt hectic or crowded. Even though I was there on business, I came away feeling relaxed and rejuvenated. I can't think of a single thing that wasn't close to perfect. If you're looking for endless beach action or a wild nightlife, this isn't your place because it's about a half hour from downtown San Diego, but if you want a retreat from the world, this is it.

“Won't Return” I arrived rather late in the evening to this hotel (after 10:30 PM or so) and one could guess given the fact that I was at a hotel, that I was a very tired traveler. I’m sure I looked tired. So I was somewhat annoyed when the woman checking me in kept trying to get me to sign up for some reward program. Why would you hassle someone about signing up for something when they are clearly just arriving into town, checking in, and probably just wanting to go to bed? All I wanted was the key to my room. The room appeared clean when I first arrived. The bathroom looked clean. However, when I pulled back the sheets on one bed, it appeared as though someone had been eating chips between the sheets. There were crumbs in the bed. So I made my way over to the next bed, and while the sheets appeared clean, the pillow case did not. It had makeup smeared on it. Next time I am in Houston, I’ll find someplace else to stay where I won’t be expected to climb into bed with old potato chips and rest my head on a pillow stained with makeup. The best part about my stay here was the very good Mexican restaurant across the street - Juanita's.

“Professional and Comfortable” This was to be a quick turnaround trip: 1 night in DC for a business function so I wasn't too picky about where I stayed. I choose the Holiday Inn because it was close the function. I'm traveling with a cane because of recent foot surgery. I was quite surprised when, as the taxi pulled in, a friendly man was immediately aside my taxi to assist me. He brought me and my overnight bag to the front desk. There, Shannon, welcomed me and checked me into room 823. She was most helpful and the most polite person I have ever dealt with in hospitality. Shannon called me by name, welcomed me as a Priority Member and answered all questions promptly. Mohammed, who had helped from the taxi, assisted me directly to my room showing me the coffee lounge area, etc. along the way. The room was comfortable, clean and everything was in working order. I was most please with a big desk on which to work (and with the free wi-fi). Since I had a few hours to waste, I brought my mint tea bags and a book back downstairs to enjoy the lounge. If first impressions are what count the most, The Holiday inn Central/White House has no worries. These employees are the face of the hotel and, even possibly, the chain. They represent you well! I had a most pleasant stay, will tell others and will return when I have need for accommodations in the DC area. Thank you!

“The best feature of the hotel is its location” We were attending an event at this hotel, so it seemed like the most convenient location. And the location is VERY good for downtown Boston -- at least if you don't have to park a car at nosebleed prices. A free airport shuttle bus, then two stops on the "T" subway train and you can get from terminal to hotel in less than 30 minutes for $1.70 with a "Charlie" card. But that's probably the only good deal about this hotel. By any objective standard, you pay a lot for, well, not very much. Hotel prices in Boston are just very expensive, so don't expect good value. The worst feature about the hotel is its atrium design, as noise can be a big problem. If you're sensitive to noise, beg for a room off the atrium. With a lower floor room on the atrium, some idiot (or a party) WILL wake you up in the middle of the night. Not so great if you're paying $300/night to stay here. In addition to easy airport access, you are right on the waterfront, next to the (expensive) aquarium, and very convenient and highly walkable to Boston's historic sights. Prices for everything in the area are expensive, except for the Haymarket fruit market, which sets up a couple blocks from the hotel on Fridays and Saturdays. A must see for local color and very cheap fruit/veggies. And even if the market is not running, I'd recommend the pizza shop on that street. $1.25 a slice, instead of the $4 you'll pay in Quincy Market, for very good pizza. As noted, the hotel is currently undergoing renovations, and the main restaurant was closed during our stay (they fed us breakfast in a ballroom). Food and beverage in the hotel are fine, but not exceptional. Better if you're paying with somebody else's money. Architecture and public spaces are a bit outdated and not stylish. Rooms were small for the price paid, but reasonably comfortable (small bathrooms without real doors a bit annoying). The staff -- like most folks in Boston -- were friendly. Bottomline is that this is an expensive, mediocre hotel. I'd recommend looking for something better for the price.

“Very honest Maid!” In general, we enjoyed our stay at the JW Marriott, and I have to start with a reminder of the extraordinary trust we place in the people who make a pittance and leave all of our valuables alone- the hotel maids. On this trip, I lost a ring in the room and searched all over for it. It was a small diamond set in stainless steel- not priceless but not cheap, either. The maid found it and left it on the desk for me. (And I did leave her a nice tip and a note of thanks.) As Gold Elites were were give a room with a view of the city but other than that did not feel like they did anything to make our visit "extra special" as the note accompanying the key card promised. Wi-Fi is still $12.95/day. I avoided it till the last day when I wanted to download podcasts. It took me half an hour to figure out that it was stopping but if I restarted again it would pick up the download where it left off. I've used this iPod and Wi-Fi to download many times before and it's never been that flaky. We were going to get room service the first night we arrived- the prices were crazy so we went to a nearby restaurant instead. The minibar was worse, although you had to squint to read the prices on the menu pasted on the refrigerator. Want a nice mini-bottle of vodka? That will be $10, please. Our room was comfortable, with immaculate white linens. Pool was a generous size with a view of the courtyard. Location, as others have said, was perfect. I was with a convention and noticed that they did an admirable job of getting the catered lunch out to a room of about 700 people at once. My vegetarian meal was very good. I had hoped that the computer-controlled elevators would have worked better when all of us were going to or coming from sessions at the same time- alas, they didn't seem to work much better than the average elevators. If you were using one in the off-hours, however, they did seem to arrive faster and stop at fewer floors. Overall we liked this hotel but at $300/night all-in we would have preferred that they not try and rake in extra bucks by overcharging for room service and not including Wi-Fi in the room rates.

“OK stay” Stayed here the night before a morning flight out. Booked a AAA rate of $69 a night. Dropped my rental car off at Thrifty and the Pear Tree shuttle came to the car rental location and picked me up which was nice. TIP - while construction continues at SAT - do not rent from Thrifty - they are off property and IMPOSSIBLE to find - and slow- both picking up and dropping off - and gave me a car with no gas...I could go on and on. The Pear Tree was ok for the price - older, not very comfortable beds, thin thin towels. Did have a computer in the lobby free to use to print out boarding passes. Also has a.m. breakfast but I took off too early to have any. Quick morning shuttle to the airport.

“Second Stay Wasn't (as much) of a Charm” Now granted, I had just come straight off a bodacious stay at the Hotel Hershey, so it'd be unfair to compare this very serviceable hotel to that, but the odd-smelling cleaner used in the rooms threw me off a little. The price didn't: $111 a night. After waiting over an hour at the airport with no shuttle in sight, we gave up and called a friend to pick us up. The 5:05AM shuttle to the airport the following day was a much better experience -- the driver was helpful and even helped check us out of the hotel. The complimentary breakfast was in its beginning stages at that early hour, so I can't really comment on it too much, but the ever-present coffee was robust and strong. I would have liked to partake in the outdoor pool which looked cozy and inviting. I would like to throttle the loud man having a MIDNIGHT conference call in the adjoining room. Perhaps the way entranceway to the room is designed made for bad acoustics, but someone needed to have that man pipe down. A housekeeping supervisor kindly directed us to our rooms, and I enjoyed the free USA Today waiting for us in the morning. This is probably my top choice near the Philadelphia airport.

“It is all about Location” This hotel is all about having a great location a block off Beale Street. It is a decent hotel, but there is nothing special about the place. At $300 per night and $20 for valet parking, you expect something special. I had a wonderful view of a trash filled alley behind Beale Street - not what I expected for the price paid. I had an executive suite, but there was no lounge and the suite was a little larger than your standard Holiday Inn - all crammed into one room. It is expensive for what you get. If cost is an issue, there are a number of other comfortable hotels in the area that cost a lot less.

“Great Service” I have stayed here before; in fact for the same convention every other year. The service is always top notch. For me it's the little things, like using my name when I check in, thanking me for my HHonors loyalty...etc etc. This hotel has top notch people. My room was on a high level floor, beautiful view of the city. I love the gym in this hotel, nice equipment, spacious and overall it felt like a real gym. I did not eat in the restaurant but I did sit at the bar for a few drinks; overall great impression there. I recommend not using anything from the mini bar. You can walk to a convenience store just minutes away and pay substantialy less. I would stay here again. Great location for conventions at McCormick Place!

“Great Location” Pros: * Very friendly staff * Room large and clean. Comfortable bed and pillows, and a separate table and chairs. Also small fridge. * Great location. * Decent breakfast with hard-boiled eggs, salad and soft cheese, fruit, instant oatmeal, so-so muffins * Two sinks: one inside the separate shower area and one in the room. * Very dependable free wireless. * Parking pass for neighborhood street parking. * Large homey lobby with comfortable sofas. Cons: * They take a deposit on your credit card over the cost of the room when you check in. * Shower: Clean, but loose knob made it difficult to turn on the water, and the shower head was very, very low - I'm 5'7" and I was eye level with the top of the shower nozzle. Also, the only soap dish was below my knee. Not only was the soap dish rusty and pitted, but it wasn't even deep enough for the soap!

“Great hotel and well located for shopping...” As other reviewers have said, the staff at the Kimpton are very welcoming and go out of their way to help. The lady on the front desk arranged directly with our car hire company to drop off at a location across the street which was great. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. Had a slight issue that our door was stiff and heavy and the key didn't always work but not enough to make a complaint. The bathroom door is a sliding door so again a little heavy but we got used to that. Lots of coffee available in the mornings. As Kimpton in touch members we got a $10 raid on the minibar which is a nice touch. Only downside is the bar area which doesn't take full advantage of the location as it has no view. The lobby area on the 5th floor was a little impersonal which was a shame as thats where they held the drinks reception each evening. Other than that, it's a great hotel and located in Market street in the same block as the Nordstrom shopping mall, and about 5 mins from Union square.

“Very slow service.” I am staying at Hilton after about a year though this is my first time at Capital Hilton. I didn't remember Hilton's service being slow and the rooms feeling so bare. My impression was they are cutting costs in many places. On the first night there were no soap and bath mat. I called and waited for about an hour for soaps to be delivered. Next day the plug in the bath tab was broken. A handy man arrived in about 45 minutes but fixed it quickly. Then the hair dryer was broken. I called and waited for 30 minutes but I had to leave the room before it arrived. I called the room service at about 8pm to order a sandwich and was told it would take 35-45 minutes. I don't recall having so many issues and slow response from any chain hotel of this class. Also there's a loud noise that sounds like a construction or loud ventilation coming from somewhere as I write this at 12:15am...

“Stains and Smells!” I am a Diamond member with Hilton so have stayed in a lot of Hilton brands and have to say this hotel made the bottom of the good hotel list. Unexplained stains on bathroom wall, crumbs/hairs on the blanket covering the bed, horrific moldy smell and dirty floors. The area the hotel is in also appears to be kind of shady. I only choose this hotel because I had to book a last minute trip and the Hilton I stay at closer to the city was booked. I would have rather camped out in a tent. This hotel should be around 70 a night, not 160.

“Met expectations” We selected this hotel because we were attending the annual Bumbershoot Arts Festival. It is within a few blocks of the Seattle Centre which was perfect. We had a one bedroom suite with a full kitchen for $200 per night. I thought is was OK value. It includes breakfast every morning. I was dissapointed by the amount of styrofoam used for plates and so on. I would have assumed that hotels were a bit more environmentally consious these days. The breakfast was greasy average. As an alternative there is a QFC grocery store within a block of the hotel. If you were staying longer it would be easy to do all your own meals. The negative about the location is that it is quite a ways away from the rest of downtown seattle. Not the place to be if you are headed to a Mariners or Seahawks game. Rooms were clean and well appointed. The free wired internet was a nice surprise.

“You Can Do Better” As we booked late, and there were several events in Austin, hotel options were limited. We chose this hotel due to proximity to the city and other attractions. I would opt to stay outside the city rather than this property if given the chance again. Pros: free shuttle service from airport and town; rooftop pool. Cons: Old, musty decor and interior; big bugs; rooms face the highway/noise; mediocre-poor service; price for what you're getting. If you must stay here, ask for a refurbished room on a higher floor and not facing the highway. But overall, you're better off staying outside of town and cabbing/walking for this price.

“One of the nicest hotels I've been to!” This is one of the nicest hotels I’ve been to. The building used to be a bank, and has been amazingly renovated. The lobby is beautiful, maintaining the teller stations and has a beautifully decorated high ceiling. They have all the old time charm (wood paneling, nice elevators, etc.), but very nicely renovated. They even still have the vault downstairs, which serves as a meeting room, and old fashioned wooden telephone booths. The rooms are fine, typical Courtyard: good sized, you can get a fridge if you ask for one, nice bathroom, tv, etc. Everyone is extremely friendly and helpful. Considering I got there half an hour before the San Diego power outage, and having been there under exceptional hard times, I have nothing but praises for the staff, both in the good times and the bad!!! Only minus: though you have free access to internet in rooms via cable), there is only wifi access in the public areas, which is not to convenient if you've got an iPad or tablet. Excellent location, great breakfast buffet, nice bar.

“fantastic stay” make sure you book an executive suite which is a two room suite separated by french doors...elegant older furnishings...hotel staff is quite friendly and accomodating. perfect views of puget sound from upper floors. nice bar but pricey. would be nice if they added a fairmont gold club floor at this location. love the complimentary shoe shine service and free internet for presidents club members

“good location,price and staff - small rooms” 100yds off times square, easy access from the Newark bus - Bryant Park. Good friendly staff, bars and restaurants nearby. Quiet air con. Good state of bathrooms.

“Great hotel near Times Square” This was our second stay at the Blakely and we were not disapointed. We had a two bed suite which turns out to be a great deal, large bedroom with two large, very comfortable beds (they seemed like Queens, not doubles), reading chair and TV. The second room has a large day bed, two chairs, TV, closet and access to a large, clean bathroom. For the money and the location, I haven't found a situation like this in New York (and we come twice a year and have tried many places). We usually do not use the breakfast as we have found, like other reviewers, the service is not friendly and we prefer to cross the street and have a quick bite there with great coffee and variety of food. The subway stop is seconds away, times square is right around the corner, Rockerfeller Center is 10 minute walk. The only complaint we had was that only one (tiny) elevator was working while we were there, luckily we were on the 5th floor so could take the stairs. I'm assuming this isn't a regular occurance, best to ask as it would be an inconvenience to anyone with mobility issues. We were not on the street side so didn't have a view but it was very quiet for NYC (except we could hear the girls screaming for One Direction at The Today Show one morning!!) We have recommended to many friends, it is great for a family or group of friends.

“Nice change of pace to stay at an "urban beach house"” This was my 2nd time staying at this hotel - and I've enjoyed it both times! It's really hard to believe this place is related to Holiday Inn!! LOCATION- Awesome. In the fairly quiet section of Gold Coast. Plenty of restaurants, stores, etc, just around the corner. The Red line subway is very close as well. In a very walkable area!!! SERVICE- I agree with a couple other reviews. The staff can be slightly aloof, but for the most part nice and helpful. But that's really what you would expect from a boutique-type property, right? ROOMS- Unique. Pretty hard to describe the vibe if you haven't been there. It feels sort of like an urban beach house with a whimsical edge. Different than any hotel you have stayed with before, trust me!!! I like it. Tiny rooms (think NYC), but some unexpected touches. The bathrooms and cool (a bit minimalistic) with a stand-up shower. Great bedding and pillows! NOISE- It was out of hand this time. I was at the end of the hallway (room 913) and the noise from the maids was awful. Woke me up before 0700 and it never really stopped. I blasted the A/C for some white noise and was able to get a little more sleep. You might want to request a room AWAY from the maid closet!!! GYM- Very nice for such a small property. Pretty much anything you might need, although it's a LITTLE outdated. Hard to complain though - most boutique hotels don't have any gym. You really should try this place. It's not for everyone. However, it's nice to steer away from predictable hotel rooms for a change!! FYI-They have larger rooms available in case you have a larger group or family. I actually think this would be a good place to stay with kids, too!

“Nice 'Modern' Hotel” The Hotel Palomar is the latest location in the Kimpton Group's chain of boutique hotels. All of the distinctive Kimpton touches are there - evening wine reception, premium morning coffee, very comfortable bed, L'Occitane toiletries, great upscale restaurant on-site. The Westwood-area hotel is easily accessed on Wilshire Blvd., which is good, since most area restaurants and shops will require a drive (or at least a very long walk). Everything looked new, which makes sense as the hotel was extensively renovated and has only been open as a Palomar for three months. The staff seemed friendly and eager, but unpolished (I generally don't expect to hear the terms 'cool' and 'awesome' being used by the staff during check-in). The rooms seemed somewhat smaller than usual, but were clean, and included both very nice details (42" flat panel television, chaise lounge, ample lighting with touch controls) and disappointing shortcuts (no HD on the TV, cheapish furniture). During my stay I was able to enjoy a dinner at BLVD 16, the combination restaurant/lounge just off the lobby. The food was good, the service was very attentive and the atmosphere was festive--the restaurant was still quite busy at 10 at night. Overall, I enjoyed my stay and recommend the Palomar, particularly if you like your hotel with lots of 'attitude'.

“Nice location, but outdated” I stayed here during the Chicago Marathon and it was a great option. Pros: The hotel is very close to Grant Park and a central location in the city. The staff was very helpful and the hotel was quiet. Cons: The hotel is a outdated and if you're looking for a view from your room, this is not your place.

“Perfect for living the Upper East Side - be careful you don't lock yourself into the bathroom!” This is a landmark hotel that has been transformed recently.The bedroom was very large and full of technology. The bathroom was beautiful, i.e. the best I have ever experienced in terms of style and set up. Except for the sliding door which we could not lock. However one evening my wife slid the door closed and the lock engaged by itself - but would not disengage! However a quick call to reception at one in the morning and a workman was on hand to release my wife. Apart from the workman apologising, a quick "sorry about the incarceration" would have been in order upon checkout with perhaps a free drink. Other guests might not have seen the funny side, say someone with claustrophobia! The door was not repaired during our stay. All in all however I have no complaints and would stay there again. The front of house and concierge were excellent with the concierge managing to get me a reservation at a restaurant I wanted to visit but had been unable to book a table.

“Great price” I agree with the previous poster who said it is a hit or miss place. On the plus side - great location. Great price for the location. The room was clean. Beds comfortable. Free parking. We felt safe. Nice that there is a refrigerator and microwave in the room. On the negative side, everything seemed a little worn. It looked like the rooms may have been redone - with new bedding, for example - but there were still water stains on the ceiling. The bedside lights did not work. The bathtub and sink drains both backed up. We were not impressed with any of the employees. Breakfast was basically carbohydrates and nothing was restocked. Even with all that being said, we will stay here again if we can continue to get a good rate. If you choose to stay here, keep in mind it is a La Quinta and not one of the nicer ones but your basic needs will be met.

“Nice hotel in a good location” We stayed for 2 weekend nights over Thanksgiving weekend, booked through Priceline at a rate of $135 a night. The hotel has 2 towers -- East tower is where most of the amenities are and the West Tower, where we stayed, is across the street, connected by an interior walkway. Overall, we enjoyed our stay a lot. The room wasn't huge, but was comfortable enough (the bed was very comfortable!) OK assortment of TV channels -- but I really wish that hotels would consider that women might prefer a channel mix not so dominated by ESPN and 24 hour news channels. They could use more counter space in the bathroom. Loved the free in-room internet and the snack shop in the lobby. While the room was nice and clean, the lobby furniture could use a good steam clean -- the sofas all looked a bit dingy. A tip to future travelers -- we were staying in the city for 2 nights then moving to another location where we'd need a car. Rather than rent a car at the airport and then pay for parking, we found that it was more economical to rent at the hotel's on-site Hertz location and return the car to the airport (no additional charge for dropping the car off at O'Hare).

“Loved the NY Palace” We spent two nights at the NY Palace and it was fabulous. I pre-booked (and paid extra for) rooms with a view of St Pats – I have to say I’m so glad I did, as I would have been disappointed to get there and not have ‘that view’ – even though we didn’t spend a great deal of time in the rooms it was worth it (so I would recommend doing this for $35 extra per night). From the moment we arrived to the moment we left the whole experience was special & we were made to feel that way. Check in was speedy and we were taken to our rooms on the 29th Floor – wow. The rooms were perfect – but I guess you expect that for what you pay. They were spacious and spotless with very comfortable beds. The location of the hotel is excellent too, you’re close to everything, but feel like you’re a little bit out of the hustle behind the courtyard. All of the staff we dealt with were genuinely helpful – although if there is a downside it was that you felt that you had to tip EVERYONE – now I know that’s quite normal in the US, but I felt a bit tired of it when one guy gets you bags from the car to reception, then another guy takes them from reception to the room – this could cost a fortune in tips ; ) We didn’t eat in the hotel as we were out and about all the time – we also declined the $37 breakfast in favour of a local diner for $7 – ummm ..... but each to their own, we quite enjoyed having breakfast with the locals.
