Anyhow, we loved it and would definitely stay here again.

“Ideal location, lovely staff” I recently stayed at this hotel for 3 nights while in Seattle on business. Others have mentioned it, but the location really is exceptional. It's such a treat to be only steps away from any number of great foods, restaurants, coffee, wine, etc. in the market, but still within easy walking distance to the conference center and downtown shopping. The hotel has a great rooftop deck, with glorious views across the harbour. The staff I encountered were without exception friendly and helpful. My room was just fine - a standard hotel room with everything I needed. The bathroom was huge, and the bed very comfortable. It's also nice that the windows open. Overall, my impression is that the interior of the hotel is perfectly pleasant, but pretty standard - it's the location, the lovely staff and the rooftop patio that make a stay here so enjoyable.

“Decent stay. Everything you need.” Cheers: ------------------- - Kitchenette – D/W, frig (w/ ice maker), microwave - Quite AC unit - The room was cool when I arrived - Free Internet service with good speed - Nice comfortable bed with soft sheets - 24 hour convenience store - 2 phones – 1 by the bed and 1 on the desk. - A nice work area with power outlets above the desk. - Easy access open power outlets by the bed and desk - DVD player and VCR combo - Movies at the front desk - TV swivels to watch as you work - Decent office chair Jeers: ------------------- - No automatic door as you enter the hotel with your hands full - No on-site central ice machine. Just the in room ice maker - The overall décor and furnishings were the bare minimum - The room darkening shades did not do a good job on keeping out the light if you need to rest during the day - Needs a shower head upgrade...C'MON MAN! - The alarm clock/CD player seemed overly complicated to set the alarm (why 14 buttons???)

“Good & Bad” We stayed here 1 night both before and after a flight to Florida. The bad..... On the first stay, a Friday night, there wasn't any bottled water waiting in the room. This has always been supplied due to my Hilton Honors Silver level. We also called Housekeeping to request an additional blanket, but it never came. The shower head was coming off the tile wall and didn't supply much pressure. In the dining room, they still use the old credit card machine with carbon. At 5 AM on the morning of check out, the toilet overflowed in the bathroom. We shut the water off and I immediately called the front desk to request help. The response was "we can move you to a different room. There is not anyone to send up. I am alone at the front desk". We were leaving on the 6 AM shuttle, so we put towels down to soak up what water we could and tried to finish dressing in the other room. A hotel of this size and quality, should have more than 1 person on duty. Upon check out we were informed that we should have called the front desk directly for the blanket. Also, there was no apology for the inconvenience. And there were several people standing around behind the desk when we left. The good.... On the return stay, a Tuesday night, we were moved to a room with a view and the desk clerk immediately informed me that the bottled water was waiting in another room and would immediately be delivered, which it was. Also, we asked for the blankets up front, and they too were delivered right away. The shower worked great. Upon check out we asked the shuttle driver if he could take us to Hertz a few blocks away, which he kindly did. I think we just had one of those bad travel experiences that happen occasionally, but management needs to look into providing additional help or better training their staff to handle problems. And please upgrade the credit card machine in the dining room. Also, if you attend the free beverage reception, stay with beer or wine. The mixed drinks were very weak, if they had anything in them at all.

“Very comfortable boutique hotel near Times Square” The Muse in New York City is the third hotel in the Kimpton chain I have stayed at and they have all demonstrated high quality standards. The Muse is very convenient to Times Square and I stayed there for two nights while I had business there. The room was not large but made good use of its space. It was tastefully decorated and all supplies (bedding. toiletries, etc.) were of first quality. The staff were all professional without being unfriendly. It was expensive but that is what you have to pay in this location. I will definitely stay here again when visiting New York City.

“Clean, Safe Convenient and Recently Renovated Uptown Hotel” I enjoyed a 2-night stay at the Omni Charlotte in Mid-September. I was in town for a conference and traveling by myself. I actually got the room through Priceline because the hotel block for my conference were already booked (another hotel). I would recommend the Omni Charlotte for anyone in town for a short stay in the Uptown area, but it would be best-suited for business travel. It was a quick and safe walk a few blocks up to quite a few restaurants and night-spots. It is also about a 7-10 minute walk south to the Convention Center (4 blocks I think). My main complaint is that there was a "stale cigarette" smell in my room. I could not figure out if my room was smoking or non-smoking- there was not a sign on the door, but there were not any ash trays in the room, either. I did not call Housekeeping because I did not want to breathe some flowery air freshener, but the smell was annoying until I got used to it. Also the only plug I could find for the iron was on the strip on the desk, so I lugged the board across the room to use the iron. Not a big deal, just an observation. The hotel is an older property, so the rooms are standard-issue and the bathrooms are small (sink outside, with toilet and tub in a small room). However, the very recent renovations made the room very attractive and I found the beds to be very comfortable. Beds are done in white duvets with plenty of pillows and the overall color scheme is gold/brown. There were also plenty of towels and 2 robes in the closet. I valet-parked my car after reading a comment about the sketchiness of the parking garage. $24/night during the week. The fitness center is small- 4 machines and a small weight bench, but I really appreciated the abundant towels, cold bottled water and fresh fruit that were available there. I had the place to myself at 4 in the afternoon. The lobby is open down to an atrium area that connects to Charlotte's Overstreet Mall complex. There was a Starbucks, Einstein bagels, and several other sundry-type stores right at the bottom of the escalator. I would stay here again, especially at a nice Priceline rate.

“Excellendt stay for Astros game- would do it again” I was looking for a downtown hotel for a one night stay and got this for $75 on priceline. Some of the reviews were a bit off-putting but I have mostly found to take reviews with a grain of salt. Our stay was a great, positive surprise. The valet, desk staff and bell service were all professional, courteous and efficient. We were not surprised by the cost of valet- I always look when staying in a dowtown area- and found it competitive for the area. Our bellman was quite congenial, joking and informative. The king room itself was very comfortable and clean with a nice size bathroom. The bed was so comfortable with nice linens and pillows. I like the way Hyatt is designing their rooms with simple sleek lines now days. The room was very quiet despite all rooms facing out toward the tower atrium. We had a couple of beers in the bar before hiking over to Minute Maid ballpark for an Astros-Dodgers game. Typical hotel prices, nice bar mix for snack and some little happy hour food at 6 pm. Service was quick and professional. Location of the hotel is good- easy access to the metro rail line and several good bars and restaurants within walking distance- not the closest to the ballpark but we always felt safe. There's a lot more to do downtown than our last visit 10 years ago. It isn't a New York city kind of lively but plenty to eat and drink while walking to the ballgame.

“Nicely renovated” When I won this hotel as an Expedia Unpublished Rate hotel, I felt disappointed, because I had stayed here some years ago, and found it shabby and worn. Well, I needn't have worried, because the hotel has since been renovated, and my room seemed brand-new. Even though I had a deeply discounted, prepaid rate, I was able to get a top (29th) floor room. The receptionist did warn me that the room was next to the elevators and would be noisy. This didn't bother me, as I had earplugs, so I slept like a lamb. Without earplugs, though, the elevators would make quite a racket. My bedroom was spacious and well decorated. The only things missing that would have made it perfect were a safe and a mini-fridge. The bathroom was very small but sparkling clean and perfectly functioning. No free wi-fi in the room, but it worked great in the lobby. Great location, very safe and convenient. Overall, a very pleasant weekend stay.

“Chose this hotel for value in center of city” This is an older hotel that has been fully renovated and provides excellent quality of food, service and value in the center of Chicago. However, being an older building, it is not very soundproof and not recommended for light sleepers. On the lower floors with windows facing Michigan Avenue, the noise is unbearable. It seems there is an ambulance station nearby and they run with sirens blasting at all hours of the night. After we requested a change of room from 7th floor to 17th floor and from front of building to the back of the building, this problem was solved. But, there are many utility rooms and stairways that have very loud metal doors...we looked around and it looks like there is no guest room that is not near one of these doors. In both rooms we had, staff started slamming doors very early in the morning, frequently going in and out of these stairways and utility rooms. Given the property handicap of the type of doors, one would think the staff would be more sensitive to travel gently during the wee hours of the night and morning. All in all, we felt that for the price, this hotel is of excellent quality and value...just not for light sleepers.

“A good offering in Downtown Seattle” Lots of good things to say about this Homewood Suites. First, as a Hilton Diamond member, I was extremely well treated and staff was friendly and helpful. Upon arrival, I was accomodated for an early check-in and my room was prepared as requested (free of allergens such as feather pillows and duvet). The room provided was very weel-maintained, although you could tell that it wasn't brand new either. This property (so far) is aging well, but as it is the case with the value offering within a hotel chain, these are the properties that often requires massive upgrades down the road. The good news is that this does not appear to be a problem there! This hotel features the standard Homewood breakfast, as well as the evening reception which includes complimentary food (burgers the night I was there, but sometimes, they have entree-like options such as teriyaki chicken!). Although marginally better than Hampton Inn breakfast, the Homewood brekfast is quite average when compared to other properties within the Hilton group. Food quality and variety was adequate, but nothing to write home about. The suite provided was of a nice size with separate living and sleepîng areas. Everything was well-maintained and in working order. The view from the room was courtyard-style. Fully equipped kitchen. Complimentary wifi worked fine. One weird thing about the room layout is where the phone was placed (not on work desk!) Location is relatively good. It is just north of the convention center and the main downtown shopping area. (It is probably one of the hotel bordering the downtown area). It is a relatively short walking distance (15-20 minutes) to most of Seattle's top attractions such as Pike Street market. I highly recommend this property

“Excellent stay at the Madison” Booked the Madison through a "Luxury Link" auction so our package included breakfast and was very well priced. Check in was smooth and speedy, the woman who checked us in printed a letter with our package details, and we got two queen beds as requested (my mom and I went). The beds were firm and completely comfortable. Lots of pillows if you like that! Very quiet at night. The bathroom was spacious, plenty of counter space and fluffy towels. The water pressure was not enough for my taste, the shower was the "rainwater" type. Also the hot water seemed to only go up to a certain temp, perhaps to protect children, it was fine for a shower, but not a piping hot bath. Breakfast was absolutely delicious. My mom had granola with fruit and yogurt, and I had the pumpkin waffles. All of the staff were very friendly. We walked everywhere we wanted to go, but the Metro is not far. We really enjoyed our stay here.

“great hotel in the Gaslamp” We stayed at the Hard Rock San Diego with our two teenage girls. Hotel staff were awesome; very friendly and helpful. They were very accommodating with our request for a high floor away from the pool & lounge noise. Room was surprisingly quiet based on our expectations. We had a Hard Rock Suite, with plenty of room. The only problems: difficulty in regulating the temperature in the room, and the beds seemed smaller than the advertised queens. Excellent fitness room. Didn't use hotel parking, we used cabs when we needed to, and walked around the gaslamp quarter, which worked out fine. Trolley stop was right actross the street; but we didn't have any noise problems from it. Plenty of restaurants and shopping all around. Had a good (somewhat pricey) breakfast at Mary Jane's. Went to a Padres game, and hotel is basically one block away from Petco Park. Hotel resort fee includes fitness room, newspaper, internet, and business center. Overall, a great stay in San Diego.

“Amazing Hotel with Top-Notch Service” We loved our stay at the Park Hyatt. Our suite was impeccable. In advance of our arrival, the hotel had set up a nice wooden crib (MUCH nicer than hotels typically have) for our baby (complete with a "baby welcome pack" including Bumble&Bumble baby bath products). We couldn't have asked for better service - we were able to check in early, and the front desk was very helpful in general with our questions/requests. I would absolutely stay here again.

“A Great Place to Stay” I stayed here during the first four days of November, attending a conference next door at the Hyatt. The property is lovely. It is centrally located next to the Gaslight District, which has lots of interesting places to eat. My room in the South Tower overlooked both the city and the marina. The room was a bit larger than most hotel rooms. The bed was very comfy and fluffy. The bathroom was fine. I didn't like the fact that the bathroom door wouldn't stay open. There was no fan and if you took a hot shower, the room would fog over completely. Apparently, a California law regulates hotels to keep bathroom doors shut at all times to give immediate access to the entrance in case of an emgergency. Yes, you could hear the trains but it was never so loud that it disturbed me. The staff was very friendly and helpful. We had breakfast in LCs and really enjoyed the breakfast buffet. Be aware that, at least on the 17th floor, the maids don't start cleaning until after 3:00 PM. This happened every single day I was there. It makes taking a nap, refreshing ,etc., very hard. Also, be aware that they are pushing their timeshare resort. The night before I left, I got a recorded message inviting me to visit their office. Other than those minor issue, I enjoyed staying at this hotel. I would definitely come back with my husband and stay here.

“Great space in the one bedroom” We recently went to Chicago for a wedding and stayed at the hotel as it was down the street from the reception. The one bedroom was quite large, very clean and well fitted. We were a bit concerned that the bed backed up to the elevator, but we did not hear any noise at all through the wall. Breakfast was a bit chaotic with families, but there were enough grab and go items like yogurt, muffins, fruit, that you didn't need to wait in line for. If you don't mind a few furry friends, take the service elevator with the pets during the breakfast rush. The main elevators are really slow. There is cheaper overnight parking just down the street on Walton, or the Chester Street parking garage down the cross street. We would absolutely stay here again. Five stars for the type of long stay hotel it is.

“Upscale Common Areas, Average Rooms, Good Price” I have stayed at this hotel several times over the past year, and never been disappointed. First Impression is the lobby, ballroom hall, and the Bar are fantastic and reminiscent of old hollywood. It has a great gym also. The rooms are in need of an update of the bed linens to get them up to par with chains such as Hilton. The room itself was nice, the bathrooms are a bit small and cramped, and the tv's are very small. No wireless internet. 30.00 to park for guest which I think is outrageous. But if you book far enough in advance, the rates are very very good for such a beautiful hotel and its ammenities. I have never paid more than 150.00 a night, and for downtown LA that is a great rate. The Hilton across the street is close to 400.00 a night. The sports bar has pretty good food, or you can walk a block to McCormick & Schmidts as well. I would certainly recommend this hotel for busienss travelers, or even tourists should stay here at least once to check out the place.

“Decent hotel close to O'Hare” I had a late flight in to O'Hare, so I wanted a hotel close to the airport before heading in to town the next morning. Although this hotel had not been reviewed much yet on here, I decided to take a chance since this hotel is so close to the airport. It was not a disappointment at all. It is only two stops away from the airport on the Blue Line and there is a direct shuttle to and from the airport. The front desk staff was very friendly, even at the late hour that I arrived. The bed was awesome - very comfortable! There was free wireless and the bar in the hotel was open until 1am. Also, the price was reasonable for Chicago, about $110 for the night. If you have a overnight stay waiting for a connection or a late flight in, I highly recommend this place.

“Impressive fo the price” Stayed 3 nights here from 9th April to 12th April 2009 in Room 103 overlooking Vermont Avenue. The room is really very very nice, clean, comfortable and well maintained. I paid AUD $284 which is about US $205 for 3 nights which I thought was a good deal through Expedia the only thing about this hotel is that they have a few extra charges they charge upon check in which I think was something like US $5 per day for parking and US$2 each for the in room safe and unlimited local calls, adds up to just over US $9 per day which even with these added is still good for Los Angeles and the quality of the room. I guess if you don’t have a car you won’t pay the parking bit, I just would have preferred it to be added to the rate I paid through Expedia. The room was a little smaller than most other area motels I have stayed in, but was big enough, very comfortable kingsize bed but extremely high off the ground desk with reliable wifi available free of charge, 32” LCD TV, not the greatest selection of stations but ok, small fridge and microwave, really nice clean bathroom which I suspect has been recently renovated. The bathroom has a shower tub combination with a shower curtain which I am not a huge fan of, but the shower curtain had magnets sewn into the bottom which kept it in place against the metal tub and that worked really well. Really nice linens on the bed and enough good sized towels My room fronted onto very busy Vermont Avenue and this may be a problem if you are a light sleeper but didn’t seem to bother me during my stay. Most motels in this area and price range can be a bit hit or miss from what I have read on here but this one was the best of the few I have stayed at over the past few years. Maid service was efficient and everything was replaced daily, they serve a pretty standard continental type breakfast in a room of the lobby, coffee, toast, donuts, waffles, cereal which were all fine and a bit of a start to the day. The parking area under the hotel is a bit tight and one morning there were more cars than spaces, so that could be a problem. If you have never been to Los Angeles the area the hotel is in may be a little off putting but it is typical for a large urban US city from what I can tell, you probably won’t want to go walking around late at night but if you are using a car which you really do need in Los Angeles the location is good with easy access to the freeway a few blocks away and a metro station is on the same block. Overall great value for the money and I hope they have the same rate available next time I go to Los Angeles as I would definitely stay there again without hesitation.

“Great place to stay, they care” i've stayed in a lot of hotels and this one although part of a chain seemed really concerned that my stay and their services were up to par. Numerous times during my three day stay, I was asked (without being intrusive) whether they were doing a good job and whether I needed anything. Truly surprising. The location of this hotel is also very good, just blocks of Michigan, in the River north area so transportation and restaurants are just out the door.

“Another Bowden Review!: You get what you pay for” I HotWired this hotel for $50 under 2.5 stars and I was stunned when an Extended Stay came up. I stayed in Extended Stay before and I did not care for it, but that was at 2 stars. Then I looked more closely at the hotel name and it said Extended Stay Deluxe, so the "Deluxe" means a half of star apparently. The word "Deluxe" did make a big difference, as the hotel was much different than their standard version. First, they actually had a Continental Breakfast. In the non-deluxe version, you get nothing. At least this place had bagels, coffee and fruit, so that was decent. Second, the rooms were nicer than the normal Extended Stay and not nearly as dreary. Also, the temprature was controlled by a thermostat which was nice, so you could set the temprature. Place was quiet too. A full service kitchen is provided but I did not use it. Third, there is a work our facility and an outdoor pool. Might not sound like much, but the non-deluxe version does not even have that. Overall, I thought my stay was fine. Nice area just a few miles from downtown Columbus. Plenty of places to eat nearby, and a mall across the street. Not the "hotel experience" I enjoy or prefer, but for one night it was fine. A couple more nights and it might have gotten on my nerves as I like a little more "bells and whistles" in my hotels. For $50, it exceeded my standards. Just make sure when you book, you ask for the Extended Stay Deluxe, not the generic Extended Stay as there is one down the street. Like I said, for one night its fine. If you like the finer things in hotels, this place it not for you, or anyone high maintenance.

“ok” We spent three nights in Boston and during our search we found it very difficult to find a "cheap" hotel, meaning not having to pay 200€ a night. Chandler Inn is a good compromise. We paid 90€ a night for a standard room (their cheapest). The room was essential in furniture, and the bathroom was tiny, but at least it provides a/c, wi-fi connection, satelite tv and signature tiletries. Parking and breakfast are not included, but there is a cofee machine at reception that can be used for free. The reception staff was very helpful, they allowed us to check out one hour later without fee and stored our luggage all day, also without a fee. The hotel is near the Back Bay T station, not far from the Public Garden and John Hancock Tower, and in a quiet residential area. If I have to tell the truth, I think 90€ a night (ca. 120$) is a lot for a queen bed and a tiny bathroom, but that's one of the cheapest hoels you'll find in Boston, so go for it.

“Needs Some Updating” I have stayed here a couple of times and for one night it will do in the winter but not in the summer. My air conditioner was very loud and impacted my sleep. The location is convenient for visiting my clients but the rooms could use some sprucing up. The door on my closet would not close and I had trouble with the iron. The cord kept retracting while I tried to iron my clothes. I could tolerate one night but I was there for two and the shabbiness of the room started to bother me. The air conditioner kept waking me up.

“Best Hotel in Midtown” Myself and a couple of colleagues came to Midtown for some meetings and we stayed at the Moderne. It's a fantastic little hotel. I come to this area of New York a lot and this was my best hotel experience to date. Cute little lobby with excellent staff. They were always friendly and very helpful. They went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable and had great places to eat and shop. The hotel was very clean and stylish. There was a little lounge that we met in every morning and had a quick coffee The room was New York sized. It's not big but not the smallest I've stayed in in this town. I really liked the decor it's modern and funky without being nonfunctional or looking cookie cutter. The bed was comfy and clean. The bathroom was clean but you do have to get creative where to store toiletries. Wifi worked well. Flat screen tellie with decent amount of channels. There's no view but it's important to note its quiet. A word I've never used to describe a hotel in New York City. If you're staying in Midtown I recommend a stay at the Moderne.

“Prima Lage” wir waren im Februar in diesem Hotel, tolle Ausgangslage zum shoppen, Metro, Sehenswürdigkeiten. Auch Times Square mit Broadway Theatern durchaus gut zu Fuß erreichbar. Zimmer (Deluxe Queen) nicht groß, aber schön eingerichtet. Bad schön, aber recht klein. Alles da, was man braucht, von Schampoo über Duschgel, tolle Handtücher bis Fön; großer TV, aber dazu kommt man eh nicht. Wegen Renovierung des Restaurants gab es täglichen Weinempfang am Nachmittag, sehr großzügig, ausserdem freies kleines Frühstück und W-lan. Sehr netter Empfang, ausgesprochen freundlich. Wir hatten ein Zimmer hinten raus (ist schon recht nah zur Wand des Nachbargebäudes) aber total ruhig. Sehr bequemes Bett, und sehr sauber. Empfehlenswert. Auf Sonderpakete achten, die lohnen sich auch direkt auf der Hotelwebsite.

“Good price for a good-sized room in a place not TOO far from attractions” In New York City, location is everything. You can always "save" a ton of money by not staying on Manhattan, but then you will miss one of the main attractions of this city: its non-stop energy level. Spending an hour going to and from your lodging inevitably forces you to miss this facet of NYC. Skyline is not right at Manhattan's hot spots, but it's fairly close. Tenth Avenue (on the west side) at 49th Street (mid-town) is only "near" the Javits Convention Center, but not terribly far from Times Square and the Theater District. A subway is two "long" blocks away, a bus line goes right by the hotel, and one could even walk to Times Square. The general area is not bustling with people all day, but there are a number of delis, bars, and place to hang out. Thus, unless you need to be right AT a certain place, a substantial price savings may well make this place a bargain for its location. In addition, the room we stayed at (#422) was quite roomy for NYC lodging. At the price we paid ($427 for two nights) we got a lot more space than we expect for lodging in this city. As the photo below shows, there was clear water damage on the ceiling of our bathroom. The staff seems to be aware of it, as they tried to paint over it. I have no idea if they did anything more than that. There was no musty smell or mildew in the bath, but it doesn't appear there were any major repairs done to handle this water problem. The room featured air conditioning, TV with 40 channels, iron, mini-fridge (useful for cold drinks), phone (charges even for toll-free calls) and shower. It was clean, comfortable, and well-maintained. The hotel has a 24 hour exercise room, as well as pool -- but check the hours on the latter. Staff was professional and courteous. Note that all smoking is completely forbidden in all places inside the hotel. No breakfast is provided for guests, and I did not notice a restaurant in the hotel itself. However, several delis, bars, and fast-food restaurants are within a block of the hotel, so you will have several choices of where to eat. I recommend the Ramses Deli across the street for fresh sandwiches. The hotel charges for parking (no surprise in NYC), for wi-fi on a 24-hour basis, for use of the PC in the lobby, and for storing luggage after you check out. The latter is no more than what you would tip the bell hop at any other place, so consider it a mandatory tip.

“Perfect location for GW visit” We were very pleased to see how close this sedate historic hotel is to GW campus. This is a reasonably priced, old fashioned hotel, nicely updated but traditional. Compared to other DC hotels, the rates were extremely reasonable and the rooms are large, with mini kitchens. We were delighted with our oversized 9th floor suite, with views from the living room, the bedroom quietly set in the back, kitchen and hallway -- all for less money than a small double at other nearby hotels. A great spacious choice for families. I requested and was given a high floor, which is quieter (Pennsylvania avenue is directly below and noisy if you are in the front - -other quiet choices means no view) Founding Farmers restaurant is across the street -- well liked and fun farm to table, you must reserve for dinner.

“Great time, excellent amenities” Slight problem with the reservation. When we called in March the week before we were to arrive, they told us that our reservation change (Made in December) was not listed anywhere in their files. The reservations agent was pleasant, but said he couldnt change the reservation and we would have to check out a day earlier than planned. Since this was a reward trip, we were upset but just had him book a room for one night in Sedona (since we were going there anyway) My wife checked in on Monday afternoon with the kids. She asked for and got an upgrade to a casita. She asked when we were checking out, and they had the change in place (Magic?). She didn't say a word, just cancelled the Sedona reservation. I arrived in the evening and was very impressed with the Casita. The ground floor had a full kitchen and dinning room, half bath plus a living room with fold out bed and TV. You walk upstairs to a bedroom and full bath, with a private balcony off of the bedroom. While we did have a car, I dont understand why previous posters said there was nothing within walking distance other than Aunt Chilada's. There was a strip shopping center just across the street with a chinese carryout and some sort of sports bar. 1/2 mile away was a drug strore/liquor store and across the street from that was a supermarket. The kids enjoyed the lazy river, tubes and minature golf. We ended up buying the resort package, although the golf would have been free since we were diamond level, but I was sending and receiving large faxes and it made doing this more economical. Both restaurants were open. No complaints about the food. I read these posts and always wonder about the resorts - some people are very negative, some are very positive. I have found a balanced report is more telling. Just my $ 0.02

“Nettes Familienhotel” Ich war im Juli 2009 in diesem Hotel. Das Hotel oder besser Resort hat mir eigentlich sehr gut gefallen, doch wahrscheinlich würde ich nicht mehr dort nächtigen. Dies liegt daran, dass das Hotel eigentlich sehr abgelegen ist und man eigentlich nichts zu Fuß erreicht. Mit dem Auto ist man in 15 min natürlich wieder überall. Der Pool war ganz nett, doch es waren sehr viele Kinder in dem Hotel, was mir die Stimmung ein wenig trübte. Der Strand ist auch ganz ok, doch auch nicht zu empfehlen, da man nicht komplett aufs Meer Blickt sondern auf eine andere Bucht.

“Great hotel and location” I stayed three nights at really good price. Fantastic location with easy walking distance to all downtown sites. I had a very large room which was very comfortable. Fairly quiet - you could hear noise in the hallway, but even as a light sleeper it really did not bother me. Two minor complaints, none of which would prevent me from staying again. The TV didn't work right. They tried twice to fix it but instead gave me a food credit, so I used it for free breakfast. Secondly, the room had one very small window which faced another nearby building - I had no natural light. Normally I love my natural light, but because the rest of the accommodations were so comfortable, it was no longer important. Except for one staff member (reception on the night I checked in), staff was wonderfully friendly and helpful. I did choose to keep my car in a nearby parking garage for $11 per night rather than use the valet parking. Well worth it. As I said, I would absolutely stay again and I do recommend it.

“not bad....” Me and my wife planned a weekend getaway and ended up going to Graceland. We stayed at the Madison for two evenings, and was a pleasant stay. The hotel is on a crowded street Downtown Memphis, so the valet parking can get pretty jammed up, but they were fast and effecient. I went to the checkout desk and identified myself and the gentleman at the counter remembered me by name and where I was from. nice touch. The room itself was nice. Clean as a whistle with nice amenities. They sent up chocolate strawberries for our first evening there. nice touch. The hotel has a nice work out facility in the basement, as well as an indoor pool. The pool is small and is more of a lap pool than a hangout. Again clean as a whistle and the work out room was really cool. It had music that the volume was adjustable,and a mini fridge stocked with bottled water. good stuff. The room service menu was nice but pricey, but that is expected at a hotel of this caliber. Our room package came with a continental sit down breakfast that was nice, the only down side is that seating is limited , so send a scout down to check it out and stake your table. There is a nice bar attached to the hotel, but we didnt eat there. There is also a little pizza shop next door whose pizza wasnt too bad for the price, but they had weird hours. Beale street is only a five minute trolley ride down the street and the stops for it is right on the street that runs behind the hotel. We ate dinner at the Pig, hung out on Beale st, took the trolley all the way around the city and came back to the hotel. Very nice. The hotel's roof has one of the, if not the best views of the river. The only bummer was there was a large wedding on saturday on the roof, but wasnt too big a deal. A little tip about graceland isthat there are two or three free shuttles to graceland from Beale street, which we didnt find out until it was too late. All in all nice stay. A little pricey compared to some of the other boutique style hotels, but service was top notch, valet was excellent and most importantly it was as clean as you would expect from a boutique hotel. Overall a pleasant experience.

“ok...” The Hilton at the airport is just another typical airport hotel. There was a beautiful lobby, lots of restaurants, a 24/7 bistro. The room was nothing more than ok, it was very dark and had paperthin walls, so i couldn't really sleep at night. Our room was on the 3rd floor so we could walk outside to the patio, which was very nice! Overall the rooms are very aged and need make over! The restaurant however was a disaster, we went there for dinner, i ordered chiecked by a risotto al funghi with winter vegetables and what i git was chicken with some old rice( certainly not risotto) with carrots and bean as well as boiled carrots. It was the first time I actually sent a dish back to the kitchen, i mean i took this dish because of the rissotto al funghi...i don't know maybe the cook wasn't used to people who actually understood teh menu or something but it was uneatable! After sending it back, i got some rice with mushroom, but somehow i was having stomach ache for the rest of the evening after that dinner...we also had some problems at the reception because during checkin we were given a different room rate than the one which appeared on the bill later on, bu somehow we managed to sort that out! Also the charges were way too high (13 usd for internet, 20 for parking etc!) Next time I will try out a difefrent airport hotel at lax.

“3 uncomfortable nights” Room: Tiny--with one end table and one chair; no desk. Insufferably hot; thermostat was broken; A/C gave no relief. Clock radio non-functioning. Faucet dripping gallons of water; called about it--no response. Bedding out of date. Hotel: dreary hallways. Only positive was lobby had a very interesting design. Would not return to this hotel, regardless of deal.

“Great location, good room, good service” One night stay in April, great location particularly for arriving into Penn Station or for Madison Square Garden events. We had a room on the 38th floor with fantastic views out across the city and river. Rooms are small but clean and modern, nice set of toiletries provided together with a fridge containing a couple of (complimentary) cans of soda - nice touch. We were allowed to check in around midday which again was noce, friendly front desk staff are a credit to the hotel and not typical of New York. The Tick Tock diner next door is a great 24 hour diner with large varied menu and just the job for jetlagged tavellers who are awake and hungry at 5.00am. Location on 8th Avenue very close to Maceys, Empite State Building, and a short walk up to Times Square. Highly recommended.

“Ok stay” We stayed here based on location, price and trip ad visor reviews for a weekend [July 07/18/08- 07/19/08). Had a terrible view out rear of hotel of some heavy duty vent sort of things. There were clothes left in drawer from previous occupant, a dead fly on carpet after the room had just been done and the maid did not leave regular coffee. The worse part was there is no AC vent in bathroom and after taking a shower you had to open the door to finish dressing etc it was so hot in there, also no exhaust fan. The business office printer was out of order. Besides all that the location was great and the price was not bad. I would probably not return to this property.

“very nice” stayed for two nights on business, appreciated the helpful front desk, high quality linens, bathrobe, marble tiles, chocolates on the pillow, and efficient air conditioning. pleasantly surprised to find that although my room was quite small, it had windows in the bedroom, bathroom, and closet. and it could not be in a more central location, beyond all of the attractions, if you're looking for a drugstore or food most hours of the day/evening, not to worry.

“Not on par with with the price” This Conrad leaves much to be desired. The Conrad in Chicago is excellent and I expected the same here. The front desk staff needs a lot of work. It was like pulling teeth trying to get them to order a car for me for the morning of departure. The when I tried to check out, there was no one around. The Chicago location uses L'Occitane en Provence bath products, which is a really nice touch for $500/night. I suppose this location uses something else because the rooms are less expensive. On the surface it looks nice, but aving stayed in hotels that are better staffed, I was quite disappointed in this place.

“Third floor= more space and freedom to smoke” This hotel is conveniently located near LAX airport. If you are a smoker, then I recommend the third floor rooms that open to a large courtyard where you can enjoy a cigarette or even the open air. Their executive lounge has a breathtaking view of the LAX runways and its bustling takeoffs and landings. Also the availability of self check-in kiosks at the lobby is a plus if you want to bypass queues. The colours chosen for room interiors are very smooth and relaxing so is their beds. However, their courtesy bus frequency to LAX airport needs to be increased.

“Great hotel!” This hotel is in a great location, and very clean. The staff is super friendly! Only a few minutes walking to Little Italy - so many amazing restaurants - and a a short distance walking to Fells Point. We are looking forward to another stay soon in this great town, at this great hotel!

“Older Hilton - well kept with excellent customer service” stayed for a week. Am HIlton Diamond but this was my first visit to this Hilton. Overall excellent hotel but be mindful that the busy 16th street with the entrance renovation makes for a noisy experience. Rooms well appointed and property is in excellent shape. THe club level was dissapointing however, the breakfast was something you could get at a 2-star property. Nevertheless the staff makes up for it, very friendly, helpful and professional. Would stay here again.

“Average” I was there for a conference. The location is great - good running trails, the Metro and zoo are nearby and there are a good variety of restaurants across the street (although the same one that have been there for over 10 years!). But the rooms are average, they are either too hot or too cold and the housekeeping was subpar. I did like that there was always staff around to help direct you to your conference. Very helpful in such a large confusing hotel!

“Hmmmm.....” Where do I start? I have a hard time writing a negative review for the Chelsea Star mainly because it is such a bargain for the price. I booked directly through the hotel's website and got the $79/night deal! That being said, for some reason, the Chelsea Star was just, well, ...average. Bathroom and washroom facilities are shared. The other people staying on my floor were not particularly tidy and, at times, the bathrooms were not that clean. This is not the hotel's fault. I was, however, disappointed by the fact that my room only got 4 television stations. 2 of the 4 stations were the exact same one. One station was in Spanish and the last was HBO. Sometimes CBS would come in clear and other times it would not. This may not be a big deal to some people but I enjoy going to new places and watching local news and other city broadcasts after a long day of touring. As far as Wi Fi, I could not log on to the hotel's Wi Fi from my room. Free Wi Fi may only be available on the hotel's first floor. There are pay-by-the minute computers and printers available in the lobby that have access to the internet. The truly redeeming aspects of this hotel are the front desk staff and the location. The hotel is literally one block from Madison Square Garden and the Subway. I walked to 2 Knicks games during my stay. It is just a few blocks walk to Times Square. I felt very safe not only around the hotel but in Manhattan in general. Nice police presence. Overall, I recommend the Chelsea Star for its unbeatable price and location. However, it may be worth it for some people to spend a few more dollars per night for reliable television and private bathrooms.

“Convenient, standard Mariott” Stayed here to start a trip to Mt. Rainier as it was close to the airport. The property was pretty nice, they have a great indoor pool and a nice restaurant/lounge. The only drawback was the apartment behind the hotel, I could hear some noise from there. The rooms were clean, the staff was nice.

“Grand old hotel in the heart of Denver” I was delighted to find that my work in Denver was going to include a stay at the Brown Palace Hotel, which I remember from early visits to Colorado in my childhood! This is a truly special place with a wonderful history. The hotel is lovingly preserved and even though rooms are of variable sizes, they include good beds, nice linens and other amenities! Tea in the atrium is one of the grand old Denver experiences and not to be missed. The hotel staff was accomodating and cheerful! They even arranged a courtesy car to the Denver Botanic Garden for us! What a lovely place to stay in Denver!

“We Were Really Happy Here” We really liked the Marriott Marina San Diego. Yes, it's a big hotel, but we were there for a convention with lots and lots of attendees, so that's what we were expecting. We didn't think it was loud and the trains didn't bother us. In fact, I think I only heard one train one night, it woke me but I went right back to sleep. Actually, I thought the train sounds were nice! We were upgraded to a wonderful suite, complete with separate bedroom and a bath where the toilet area was almost floor-to-ceiling glass. That was an experience! I don't think you can beat the location. Right on the water, but within easy walking distance of all the great restaurants downtown. We would return!

“Great stay” I had a great stay, I was able to check in early and I had a king suite which was on the corner so I had no problems with noisy neighbors. The Room including the bathroom was huge! The staff was excellent and very efficient. Will stay here again without a second thought.

“Coffee delivered to your door.” As other reviewers have mentioned, be sure to sign up for the Omni Loyalty program prior to the stay. Then, you'll get hot Starbucks coffee delivered to your door each morning. That alone for me makes it worth staying at this hotel. The overall service is very good, the rooms and property are comfortable, stylish and spotless. The location is a bit remote.

“Conveniently Located, and nice too.” Great location for Riverwalk, La Villita, AlamoDome, etc. Historic hotel is a little misleading, near as I could figure, its an old building which is now a hotel. But nicely done. Good sized room, all the usual amenities. Because of street noise I'd go for the back side of the building, but again advertising must be taken with a grain of salt. The balcony rooms overlooking La Villita actually overlook a parking lot and yes you can see La Villita. Breakfast space very limited, also parking for which there is an extra fee. They don't have many spaces but since we got the last one I don't know what they do if the lot is full. Staff we connected with was very friendly and helpful.

“An extremely pleasant stay” Wasn't really sure what to expect with the fluorescent lights and the hotel in the middle of a residential block, but a good rule of thumb is if it's a Kimpton, you can't go wrong. Small, funky boutique hotel - the room was extremely large and well appointed, the happy hour featured some lovely sparkling white wine, breakfast was very pleasant, and the location is close enough to Dupont Circle and other downtown locations to walk or take a quick taxi ride. Would definitely stay again.

“The Hotel Seemed Tired And Run Down” I have stayed here 3 times before and had always been very satisfied however this time was different. The room we were given smelled like a horse or donkey was the last guest. I kid you not, it smelled like a stable. I called the front desk and advised the clerk and his response was this. Maybe you could buy some air freshener. I could not beleive this. We booked through Priceline and moving to another hotel was not an option. The shuttle drivers to MD Anderson did not seem nearly as friendly as in previous visits. Hopefully they will be better the next time I stay.

“In need of a major overhaul” My travel agent booked me in here again. I reviewed it last time and was not polite but here was a chance to be surpised, Sadly I wasn't. The good things are the location, which is excellent (and right next to my office which is why I get booked here) and the rooms are reasonably spacious for New York. But this place is so tired. To give you a flavour - the bathroom has a tin sink set in a white plastic worktop. There are rawlplugs sticking out of the tiles where previous fixtures have fallen out of the walls. The tap is barely hanging on to the wall. The bedroom was OK - clean and all the usual facilities but very tired. And this Doubletree idea of presenting you with a warm cookie as you arrive - it feels so out of date. Here I am after a long flight checking in late - what I really want from a receptionist is to give me a warm soggy cookie - I don't even open the bag before it goes into the trash. And all yours for $300 - its not as if its budget.

“Very nice but..” Stayed here one night for a business event. Very nice hotel downtown San Antonio. What you would expect for the price. Spacious rooms. Breakfast buffet was not that spectacular though. Nice terrace on the riverside. All fine but.. I got charged 5 USD for receiving a package in the hotel. Really disapointed about this. Kind of rude trying to make money this way. If you charge 250 USD + for a room, please dont try to make a buck this way. Another thing was that at 9 housekeeping started banging on my door. I mean, it is Saturday and went to bed at 3 AM. Kind of not what I would expect in this hotel.

“Quite Good Overall” My only criticism of this hotel is the soft, mushy, almost hammock-like mattress in our king bed suite. Other than this, the room was clean, spacious, and quiet. Staff was helpful after I badly injured my leg and ended up finishing my vacation on crutches. Indeed, they took the extra step of sending a complimentary fruit basket to our room while I was laid up. Definitely pay the premium for a courtyard room or you'll be hating life at 2am when the Tufts Medical Center ambulances and medivac helicopters come roaring through. As noted in other reviews, this hotel is near an orange line T stop. You can make your way here for $2.50 from the airport via the blue line to the orange line in about 30 minutes. A YMCA is right around the corner for your workout and there's a built-in Starbucks for your morning Joe.

“No complaints at all - excellent property” This is one of the few hotels that I have stayed in where I have never had a sinlge complaint. Even if I were pressed for a criticism of this hotel, I could not list even one. The location is perfect, the check-in was friendly and efficent, the room well-appointed and impeccably clean, the elevators always worked well and with little waiting, all staff members greeted you and even engaged in conversation, and the complimentary breakfast buffet and afternoon snack was a great treat. More importantly the noticeable security at all times was a tremndous reassurance that you were safe. Of the affordable hotels in NYC (under $300.00) this is the best I have ever stayed at, and will definitely stay there again.

“Very unexpected surprise” On a Friday afternoon, I made a last minute Saturday night reservation on Travelocity at a very reasonable rate - even the hotel would not honor the rate directly. I had never heard about the Sofitel but took a chance based on the reviews. The hotel was outstanding. Awesome location - right in center city. The rooms were fairly contemporary and very comfortable - great lighting and furniture. The bathrooms were marble and modern. Don't look for warm and cozy here - the place is sleek, but provides everything you would want at a 5 star hotel. The valet took the car and brought it quickly, check-in was really quick - the front desk was very accomodating. Valet parking is expensive (about NYC prices) but self-parking is not much of an option. By far, one of the best finds in Philadelphia. I'd say on par with the Ritz and Four Seasons at a much better price.

“Gehobenes Hotel im Zentrum New Yorks” Das Intercontiental New York Times Square ist ein neues Interconi in New York. Da das Interconti Barkley uns zu weit weg war, und das von uns favourisierte Crowne Plaza am Times Square zu unserer Reisezeit ausgebucht - entschlossen wir uns, daß Interconti Times Square zu testen. Der Eingang des Interconti ist sehr unspektakulär in einer Seitenstraße. Die Empfangshalle relativ klein und der Check-In unkompliziert. Die Zimmer sind von er Austattung auf Interconti-Niveau - leider aber relativ klein. Der Ausblick war i.O. und der Service entsprechend eines 4-5 Sterne-Hotels. Insgesamt haben wir uns sehr wohl gefühlt - allerdings ist das Hotel mit Preisen von 300-400 USD pro Nacht in meinen Augen zu teuer. Mein Tipp für Reisende, die auch noch mit dem Mietwagen unterwegs sein wollen: 1,5 Blocks weiter ist eine National-Vermietung - dort läßt sich schnell und einfach ein Mietwagen ordern und auch zurückgeben - so spart man sich die teuren Parkgebühren des Hotels.

“Beautiful hotel; great location for nightlife” Beautiful hotel with a hip and vibrant feel. My room was ready early and check in was a breeze. My room was oversized and was very tastefully furnished. Even the bathroom was large with lots of counter space. The bed was super comfortable and the linens and towels were top notch. Housekeeping was excellent. The location can't be beat: just off Dupont Circle within walking distance of the Metro and tons of great restaurants and bars. I've read other reviews that said it was noisy, but I was there on the weekend and never had a problem. Other pluses include the complimentary WiFi, the morning coffee and tea service and the manager's evening reception which is a really fun way to end the day and begin the evening. The Urbana Happy Hour in the bar is also a great deal. It was too early in the season for the pool, but I can tell that would be a fantastic amenity as well. Would definitely stay here again.

“Do not stay with a holiday......” Stayed here on memorial day weekend, mistake! They had workshops on Sunday night with the doors open and the people were screaming until 2am! We paid just like everyone else an if this place is going to host large groups then they new to house them correctly!!!! Most of the groups were African American men and women and they would yell and slam doors until 4am! We stayed on the first floor and it was nuts! But after these groups ended it was the way it should have been...QUIET:) I like that the first floor have slide window doors that open into patio pool area! This is top five pool areas ive experienced It's very serene and is boxed in by the buildings so no weirdos We always stay at this exit off of 71 I only recommend the larger hotels due to the lower class surroundings outside of the industrial parkway The hotel sits back into the park so it's secluded but around the other lower end motels lurk the weirdos like prostitutes and meth heads So stay here to get away from them! But the amenities here outshine the rooms because they are dated They have new headboards but then old 90s framed pictures and new big tvs but no little fridges or micros:(

“Seamless stay over holiday weekend” First of all, let me preface this by saying that I come to New York at least once a year for vacation. I have stayed at several Times Square hotels, as well as The Plaza and other boutique hotels throughout Manhattan. I found the Marriott Marquis to be above average in every single aspect of my stay. I arrived at the hotel at 10:00am, fully expecting my room not to be ready. It wasn't, but they offered me a standard king room if I wanted to check in immediately. Since I don't spend much time in my room, I agreed. They gave me a room on the 43rd floor that looked down on everything in Times Square. Talk about a room with THE view. The elevator system was easy enough to use, and I appreciated the simplicity of it. No worries about kids pushing all the buttons in the elevator. Just put in your floor and it tells you which elevator to go. I never waited more than a few minutes. The glass elevator can be dizzying, but I just closed my eyes and waited till I arrived on my floor! The beds were incredible, and the room was a good size for Manhattan. I had a king size room, flat screen tv, small loveseat, and desk area with plenty of room to navigate around the room. The bathroom was also standard size. There were Bath and Body Works products in the bathroom, as well as lotion and mouthwash. The in-room internet was $16.95/day, which I think is pricey, considering the lower properties at Marriott and Hilton offer it for free, but it's typical. There are multiple subway stops within a short walking distance of the hotel, which is always a plus for me. Times Square is always crowded, so if you are looking for a quieter stay, you want to stay out of that area anyway. I couldn't hear any of the street noise in my room though, and the shades did an excellent job of blocking out the light. I did not have any problems with this stay, and I could certainly recommend it to anyone looking for a consistent hotel in the middle of everything.

“Very Nice, but Not Quite Top Shelf” We used Starwood points to get a room here for two nights. We started out on the seventh floor, but as we were entering the room, it became apparent that our neighbors were a bit rowdy. We had no problem getting the hotel to move us to a different room on the fifth floor - one which was very quiet our entire stay. Staff at the entrance and in the lobby were friendly and helpful. The decor of the room we ended up in was unremarkable; I think maybe we expected a bit more for the money/points. We had a balcony large enough to sit on (with two chairs and a small table), but it overlooked the front parking lot and lots of traffic. Might be worth asking if they have the same type of room overlooking the golf course in the back. Our room had a king size bed, a comfortable armchair, a desk, and flat screen TV. I didn't like it that no in-room coffee maker was available, but that seems to be pretty typical of high-end hotels. Our bathroom was exceptional, with marble floors, a large tub, separate shower, monogrammed towels and bathrobes, and Remede amenities. My wife complained about the length of time it took to get hot water in the room - several minutes. We generally liked the hotel, but might have been a bit less happy if we had paid full price. I wouldn't be surprised if we came back here, but we also might try someplace different just to see what's out there.

“A great value for your meeting!” Just completed a meeting with my sales team. Very positive feedback from my sales reps regarding the meeting room, breakfast, internet and large, clean, comfortable rooms. A quiet bar with great staff and a pool table made for a lot of dialogue amongst the team. The hot breakfast was a great start to the morning and the managers reception in the evening was a good way to wind down. This staff hustles and aims to please! I have yet to be disappointed with the "can do" attitude that the sales staff brings.

“beautiful hotel” We stayed here for a weekend last year for a Flyers game. I am an Omni Select Guest - not really sure what that entails, but when the front desk saw that note, they instantly perked up. The concierge was very helpful with all of our questions. The room was excellent - big, comfortable, and clean. The bed was big and the sheets were soft. There was a sofa in our room. The bathroom was of a bigger size than I am usually used to. The location is close to bars and the subway. We just took the subway to the hockey game. We, of course, went to Pat's and Geno's for cheesesteaks and it was about a $5-8 cab ride. The location is also close to Independence Park (obviously) - so great for families with children that love American history. They were renovating last year and there was only one elevator working, but we weren't really bothered by that.

“Great hotel, great location” Loved this hotel. Excellent location, very comfortable rooms, lots of space, perfect for business travel. Restaurant was so-so, but with so many alternatives within walking distance, it wasn't a problem. Service was great - a bit slow at times, but still very good. Would highly recommend & would stay here again.

“Old, but Reliable” I stayed at this Hyatt several years ago and I'm back for another week and I swear it hasn't changed, with the exception of the carpeting that appears to have been updated. While it's not the nice new Sheraton across the street, the things that I like about this hotel is that it's clean, the rooms are large and the decor is adequate, but, most importantly, it's extremely quiet and the rooms are soundproof, which lends itself to an excellent night's sleep. This is one of the few hotels where I can hear myself think (instead of my next door neighbor). So, if you're looking for a clean basic hotel without alot of frills (and you can get a good rate), don't hesitate to book the Hyatt.

“Nice place..” Friendly employees upon arrival, was able to sit at roof top bar early in the evening but it was always reserved in the evenings. Room was clean and a decent size for a manhattan king room. Overall, I did not have any complaints- and I am really picky when it comes to here I lay my head down at night!

“Perfect Hotel” I was really impressed with the Park Hyatt Washington. From first entering the hotel, the staff was extremely welcoming and efficient, and remained that way throughout our stay. Our rooms were fabulous, with a roomy sitting area. Our stylish bathrooms also included a deep bath which was very welcome (and not necessarily standard in most US hotels). The breakfast was also fabulous. I look forward to returning to the hotel and Washington sometime soon!

“Nice & Convenient” We spent a Fri. & Sat. night at this hotel at the beginning of August. We redeemed our Hilton Honors points for the stay. We were able to check in upon arrival at 2 PM. The front desk staff was friendly both at check-in and check-out. The 7th floor City View room met our requests and the complimentary bottled water from Hilton Honors was delivered promptly. The shower was great and we did not have any plumbing problems experienced by an earlier reviewer. The air conditioning was fine and we set the fan to On to keep it running for a constant room temperature (the temperature seemed to go up at night when set to Auto). The maid knocked on the door about 9 AM the first morning, but we were about ready to leave, so it wasn't an inconvenience for us. Breakfast just after 8 AM on Sat. was very busy and chaotic with the many families present with children. We went at 7:30 AM on Sun. and it was much better. It costs $28/day to valet park in the hotel garage with in/out privileges. We did not use the car until we checked out and we walked easily to Seaport Village and the Embarcadero. We also walked to Petco Park on two nights and it was very safe with lots of people walking to & from the many hotels along the way. The Red Trolley also stops near the hotel and goes to Petco Park. If you are a light sleeper, bring earplugs. The trolley and Amtrak can be noisy at night with the frequent whistles and crossing signals, especially in City View rooms. I've stayed at this Embassy Suites numerous times, and it has always been an overall satisfying experience. I would stay here again in the future.

“Good - not great” As the title suggests, I had a good stay, but not a great stay. I expected much more in terms if 5 star service. Wednesday: I rolled up to the hotel in a taxi on a Wednesday night around 10:30 pm. A bellman/valet came right up to the taxi to get my luggage. He went straight for the trunk and didn't even bother to open my door or greet me in any way. There was another gentleman in a red coat (doorman?) who just stood there as well. The door was propped open, so he didn't actually have to do anything. No "good evening" - No "Welcome to The Mandarin" -- nothing. Check in was efficient, fast and friendly. Thursday: When I left the hotel for work, there were a pile of people (staff) near the front door, but again, no one said a word to me. Not a smile, not a hello, not a have a nice day, nothing. I stayed 4 nights and during those 4 nights, hardly anyone spoke to me. I'd pass obvious staff members around the property and it was like I was wearing an invisible suit. I'm no Donald Trump, but it's not like I am a hobo either. Besides, I was a guest and it really shouldn't matter. I went to the Empress Lounge, sat outside and ordered a Mojito and a salad. After I was served nobody ever came back. EVER. Friday: Was raining and I asked a man standing in the lobby (staff member whose name I wish I remembered) if he knew if there was an umbrella in my room. He said yes, but offered me an umbrella at the front door so that I would not have to go back to my room. First person to actually be nice to me since I arrived. Saturday: there was a wedding on the property on Saturday night and I watched them set up from the restaurant patio at lunch and then watched the wedding from my room as I had a nice view of the gardens/courtyard from my room. Sunday: woke up not too early and opened my drapes to see what the weather was like. Imagine my surprise when I saw a bunch of trash (programs) and plywood laying around the lawn from the wedding the night before. I was shocked that the mess wasn't cleaned up before the night was over and guests had to suffer with an unusable courtyard on a nice morning. It was a disgrace. HOWEVER: as much as I complained, there were some bright spots. Housekeeping was fantastic and turndown service was perfect with bottled water and fresh ice every evening. Vivian at the Empress Lounge was friendly and inviting. Room was comfortable and the bed fantastic. Bathroom was big with a deep soaking tub. I should have brought bath salts. Would I stay here again? Probably not. If someone can't even greet you when you walk in the door, then I would rather stay somewhere that will.

“Service Stands Out” I booked this hotel last minute via Hilton reservations when I missed my train out of New York. Around midnight, I rolled into the hotel with no luggage, or anything for a night's stay. The front desk staff was very helpful and right after I went up to my room, a bellman delivered a travel toothbrush and toothpaste. Positives: Convenient location, virtually brand-new furnishings, reasonable price. Excellent bed and bedding. The room was compact, but seemed just fine for the price. Negatives: Walls seem thin--- overheard way too much of an exuberant girlfriends' getaway next door. Design overkill: hard to decode the light switch in the bathroom. The service orientation of the front desk really set this hotel apart from my other recent stays at New York hotels. Great staff at the hotel. This is an excellent new hotel option in this area. Lots of the Chelsea/Midtown hotels are either way overpriced for the leisure traveler or economical but very rundown and even seedy.

“sehr schickes Hotel in bester Lage” Das Le Parker Meridien kann man getrost als ein sehr gutes Hotel bezeichnen. Die Lage ist perfekt für alle Touristen und Geschäftsreisende. Alle Höhepunkte von Mid-Down Manhattan sind in kurzer Distanz zu erreichen und der Central Park liegt auch (fast) vor der Tür. Das Hotel ist modern renoviert und die Zimmer sind sehr schick und zu gleich, sehr praktisch und sehr geräumig. Der einzige Nachteil vom Hotel es ist nicht ganz billig - das Preis-Leistungsverhältnis stimmt aber (was man von den meisten günstigeren Hotels nicht behaupten kann).

“Good” This used to be called the Miyako, now it is Hotel Kabuki. We booked a 4 night winter special for $101/night, which was less than most full-service hotels in central S.F. Our room was really big in my opinion, plenty of room to walk around and store our stuff for 2 people. There was 1 queen bed, 2 bathrobes, free wifi, a sitting area, chaise lounge, coffee table, a desk, a mini fridge/bar, snacks and a balcony on 2 sides. Even with all this furniture, there still was plenty of room for us to stretch out. The bathroom set up was a little odd. There was the main sink room, the toilet room to the left, and a shower and tub room to the right. There were 2 shower heads, one in the tub and then one that was just in the shower room. The toilets are low flow, and sometimes took a few flushes to make it work. The house keeping staff kept our room very clean. The room itself is starting to age. The sliding glass doors on the two balcony access points were a bit sticky and old. The Japanese window shades were a little worn. The room paint was a little worn. Over all, I feel like the room was a good value for S.F. and being centrally located in the city. We forgot some toiletries, and the hotel front desk was very attentive and had them sent to our room right away. We needed instruction on how to use the in-room alarm and iPod Docking station, and they sent staff right away to help us. I think the people next door had a baby or small child, as I briefly heard a crying child in the hallway before I heard the next room door close. Once the family was in their room, I could not hear the baby anymore. The hotel is in the heart of Japantown. There is a nice breakfast in the restaurant I think it is about $16 buffet. The breakfast buffet staff was attentive, and kept coming with coffee for us. The bacon, fruit, yogurt and oatmeal were very good quality. There are coffee and a breakfast kiosks in the Japantown mall next door to the hotel. The hotel restaurant later in the evening becomes a bar. The bar personnel was great! We got a couple bottles of wine from Sonoma, and they gave us glasses and wine opening for a tip. The lobby has some nice sitting areas, and the lobby has free wifi. Parking when I was there, I believe valet parking is $39 per day with in and out privileges at no extra cost. There is a public parking garage access around the corner with a elevator into the hotel. The public parking is by the hour up to $16/day, but there is no in-out privileges, so you get a new ticket every time you enter. There is limited street parking nearby, and the residential neighborhood has permit street parking, so the best bet is to valet or public garage a car if you have a car. For convenience, there is a Safeway grocery store about a 2 1/2 block walk from the hotel, and there are Japantown mall groceries as well.

“I would give a Fair review.” From the outside, this hotel doesn't look like much. When you walk in you can tell that the place have been newly furnished with modern decor and amenities. I would say this place is nice, clean and comfortable, but I do have a few minor complaints that ruined the stay for me. Two small things that I must have that you will not have in this hotel is a microwave or a refrigerator. I was told that the refrigerator would cost $20. Before I touch anything in a hotel room I do a small inspection of countertops, toilet, windows etc., just to see how well the room was cleaned. I noticed that the desk in my room had stains from someone's greasy arms and food stains. Same situation with the remote control that I had to sanitize about three times to get the grease off. Also, if you are someone who likes to use the gym, this one is pretty bad. The Gym has about 8 treadmills and only 2 are in working condition. Dumbbells are in an area where you cannot do anything overhead due to ceiling height. Bring your own water bottle because the only water available in the gym is from a drinking fountain. Overall, I would probably stay here again, but I have stayed in almost every hotel in the downtown area and there are better options for the same amount of money.

“good but not up to Kimpton standards” I've stayed in a number of Kimpton hotels and generally like them. The service at Kimpton hotels is generally very good, and 70 Park is consistent with this. The hotel has a small footprint and, for example, the elevators are small and somewhat slow, the lobby is smallish etc. Where 70 Park gets lower grades is on its overall appearance. As noted in several reviews, the place has a bit of a rundown feeling, the carpets and fixtures are worn, the rooms seem in need of sprucing up. Room rate was pretty good on promotion ($280/night), and the location is great, so not at all bad (I would give it sort of a 3.5 out of 5). I might be inclined to try a newer Kimpton property in NYC if I could get roughly the same rate.

“Smelly” I stayed her in August and hated it. We reserved one of the "suites", which turned out to be a standard cheap hotel room adjoined to another cheap room that had a couch instead of a bed. My nose went numb with the amount of airfreshener until, two days into the trip, we found something resembling an urinal cake lodged into the airconditioning units and removed them. I was traveling with some relatives, however, who liked the free breakfast (eggo-type waffles, cereal, Costco muffins) and the pool, which was clean, but looked onto the freeway. They also liked the proximity to the shopping mall and cheap chain resaurants.

“Very stylish and easy going” We stayed at W Washington in December 2011. While the rooms are quite small, they are very stylish and well laid out. The location is the best going around - right behind the Whitehouse. The concierge was fantastic and made great recommendations for places to eat. The hotel was a little slack with room cleaning (spilt hot chocolate wasnt cleaned up) and a tray was left outside our door for a day.

“Good Overall - Bad Internet Provider” I and several of my colleagues stay here routinely for business. I have stayed multiple times in the last 6 months. Good ---- 1) Very close to San Jose Airport 2) Full Service Hotel - coffee shop, fancy restaurant, night club, lobby-bar/sushi-bar. 3) Attractive lobby 4) New high-end beds in rooms Not so Good ----------- 1) Pay parking. Irritating and slows you down having to do the attendant rigamarole every time you go in and out. Also frustrating on your first visit because it is hard to tell where to park when you are checking in. 2) Terrible Internet Service Provider. Wireless and wired access provided in-room by a company called Datanamics. Promotion codes fail to work. It forgets your log on and forces you to register a new one. Forces you to power off and fully reboot your computer (multiple times!) to get a connection that won't bump you off. Strange firewall settings prevent your VPN from working unless you spend an hour doing trial-and-error work on obscure configuration settings. Note: we all work for one of the top 3 computer makers in the world; we are not technophobes. All of us routinely take our computers to any Starbucks in the country, power them on and connect instantly. There is simply no excuse for the hotel's service to not be as reliable and simple to use as the service at Starbucks.

“Good value in the South Loop” First off, the Essex Inn merits a 3.5, but that rating option is not available. It's a good value, comfortable place to stay, minus some of the extras of more expensive downtown Chicago hotels. The hotel has a small, functional lobby flanked by bright, airy seating areas with a somewhat dated look to them. The front desk staff was very pleasant and efficient. My room, a king single, was compact but not claustrophobic. The bathroom was small, but not oppressively so. Some reviews described the bathrooms as the smallest ever - clearly they've never stayed in a moderate-price London hotel. The bed was very comfortable, the room furnishings were very modern, and the mini-fridge was a big plus. The flat-screen TV was nice, but lacked pay movie options. Shower water pressure was very good. If you're a traveler who likes to wake to the silver coffee pots and trays of a room-service breakfast, don't stay here - you won't find it. But if you don't care about those amenities and want a good price ($57 per night on Priceline), comfy room and a location across from Grant Park, you'll love it. The hotel is on S. Michigan Ave & 8th, right across from Grant Park and close to museums and Soldier Field. For transit purposes, the CTA Harrison red line station is two short blocks away if you use the Polk St. entrance (unstaffed, you've got to have your CTA card already). Also, the bus routes that go down S. Michigan (King Drive, Cottage Grove) all stop next to the hotel.

“ニューヨークの代表的なホテル” ニューヨークを代表するホテルといえば、このウォルドルフアストリアホテルだと思います。正確にはウォルドルフアストリア本体とタワーがあるのですが、正面入り口は共通で、タワーに上がるには、セキュリティを通過しないと入れない仕組みになっています。 もちろん重厚感・高級感はありますが、かなり大きなホテルですので人の往来は非常に多かったですね。少しうるさいぐらいでした。 タワーに宿泊したのですが、部屋は少し古さが感じられるぐらいです。他のホテルと比較して同じ位の宿泊費でしたら若干広さは狭いと思います。アメニティ類は問題ありません。ホテル自体が「ウォルドルフ」を誇っているように、何にでもホテル名が書かれています。 1階のレストランは結構お薦めです。カジュアルレストランなのですが、アメリカ、ニューヨークに来た事を実感できます。お値段もソコソコです。朝食もここでいただけます。 ニューヨークに訪れた方は一度は外観をみたことがあるホテルですので、機会があれば一度は宿泊されてみるのもよいかもです。 英語がとても苦手な方には少しお薦めができないかもしれません。

“location, location, location” Emerging out of the BART station this wonderful hotel is right there! Great location for shoppers tourist to ride cable car and any public transport We had a plush room on the 21st floor with a great view. The only draw back were no robes as the ad stated. We also had no coffee in the lobby as I have read about. The homeless do not bother you anymore than other cities and we walked down Market ST from the Ballet at night and felt like time square before the clean up. But felt very safe at the hotel and the service was excellent.

“Good value, Good location, Good service” Stayed four nights with out any issues. This HI Express is a little better than most HIE's, within walking distance to Walk of Fame, Kodak Theatre, Hollywood Bowl. Hotel is located a few blocks south of the 101 which provides quick access to Warner Bros, Studios, Universal, Dodger Stadium, etc. Entire staff was polite, courteous and accomodating. Only problem that I found was that Highland Ave is busy and left turns in and out of the hotel can be an adventure and due to the street lay out, it is not practical to drive around the block.

“Give this place a chance!” With 200 rooms, the BW Hacienda is bound to please many yet offend some. Nestled on several terraces, the Hacienda has eight separate wings/buildings each housing several rooms. The first impression one receives is that of a colonial property with excellent gardens. In fact, these gardens are just one of several signs of constant attention at the hotel. Throughout our four-night stay, workers were painting, grouting, gardening to improve the grounds. We checked in on Sunday, June 2, and were greeted cordially and given our room assignment with a warning about the no-smoking policy, the $5 resort charge, and the early check-out fine (for those leaving before the agreed upon check-out date, there is a stiff $75 penalty). I concur that the $5 resort fee is nonsense and should either be a part of the room fees or be made optional. I noticed that upon check-out one guest did in fact contest her resort fee and was credited. But for the $5, you do get bottled water replenished each day, shuttle service, newspapers (we got two papers each day--you have to ask), free internet and printer service. Our room, in the 600's, has views over Heritage Park, and is, in fact, preferable to those which front directly the harbor, as the freeway noise is quite a distraction. (Too bad San Diego chose not to install sound barriers.) Yes, the rooms are dark as befitting the colonial atmosphere. And I do wish something would be done about the dreary armoires housing the TV's. But the carpet is Berber style and comfortable to walk on. The bathroom needs attention.
