The fan--defeaning--does little good and probably wakes up the occupants next door. Efforts to contact maintenance fell on deaf ears. We ordered room service breakfast one day and received it 30 minutes late, only because I had to call to remind the Acapulco about the order. The restaurant itself is ok for buffet breakfasts and also their spectacular rum-raisin French toast (the complete breakfast order included 2 eggs, and sausages--enough for two to share, I would hope). Some very good restaurants. El Agave has phenomenal old style Mexican cuisine with perhaps the most staggering inventory of tequilas I've ever seen. Fred's is fine for a quick meal. El Bandini is amusing and has romantic allure. Cafe Pacifico was disappointing for its lack of service. Go instead Uptown to Kimo Sabe, a highly ecelctic fusion restaurant with many side dishes on the plates. So why am I giving this four instead of three? Because the personnel are so kind and friendly and are working hard to do their best. Yes, there are other options in Old Town. All but one are quite a walk away. The B&B at Heritage Park looked inviting, but the management would not let us see any rooms even after agreeing to do so. The location of the Hacienda is excellent and you really can't do much better. We're going back next year and will write an up-date then. I hope the management does something about the plumbing and the TV armoires.

“Noisy Construction Ruined the Stay” The Club Quarters itself was fine, but during some of my stay the front of the hotel was a construction site. To enter the hotel, one had to walk a metal plank over a sunken part of the sidewalk. Then, on my first morning I was abruptly awakened by extremely loud construction, including the use of a jackhammer, performed directly in front of the hotel. Upon leaving and entering the building, I saw and felt particles blowing around, and some even entered one of my eyes. To minimize the noise while entering or exiting the hotel that morning, it was necessary to hold one's hands over one's ears. The hotel receptionist was even wearing a dust mask on her face, and conversation with her was difficult at best. Hotel guests were given no notice of this situation, either in advance or during the stay, and were offered no compensation. So, though the facility was quite nice, I can't recommend the hotel as of now.

“reasonable costs for location” Nice business hotel very convenient to Century City, excellent alternative to nearby Hyatt. Rooms are modern and clean, bathrooms excellent. Some rooms have windows that did not open, so if this is important you may want to make a specific request. Public areas were inviting and newly redone. Resaurant nicer than most, with very cute individually controlled TV's at some booths. No pool, but nice hot-tub on deck.

“You pay a lot, you get a lot.” At premium rates, you expect fresh, fluffy towels, high thread count sheets, and an attentive, well trained and unobtrusive staff...and you get them. While in the city, this is a quiet location, south of the Mall overlooking a bay off the Potomac. The lobby - and the entire hotel and conference area - is tasteful, opulent, yet not overpowering. The decor relies on deft touches of brilliance rather than overpowering excess. Lighting in all areas is utterly inspired. I want that designer for my house! This is a large hotel yet it feels more like a boutique property. Every spot holds a delight for the eye. One potential downside is the location. It is a convenient taxi ride to most places; the Mall, Dept of Agriculture and main Smithsonian building are 3 blocks away (as is the Smithsonian Metro station). However, the "busy" part of the city such as K street, the well known restaurants, tourist attractions mean cab or Metro ride. My impression of the guests during my stay was that most were there for political business at the Capitol. Unless you are a dedicated hoofer, this isn't the location to start a walking tour. Of course, this is what makes the location delightfully peaceful. It is across from the Washington Marina. The room was spacious and well appointed. The bathroom had a separate shower and tub, Small nit: no in room coffee. This seems to be custom in the higher end hotels, but I hate dealing with people, even room service, before my coffee. There is a minibar and refrigerator; and thankfully, bottled water. The tap water is not great. Turn down service was noteworthy. I never saw the hotel staff, but every evening, I returned to a room with bed turned down, foot mat on the floor next to the bed, bathrobe laid out and laundry and shoe service prepared. A fresh bottle of water and glass were on the nightstand next to the bed. Another thoughtful touch is an umbrella in the closet. The bed itself was very comfortable, although the pillows were all of the same type. If you like down, then you're good to go. The spa is on a floor of its own and features subdues lighting, locker rooms, pool, weights and cardio. I did not check all the services available, but the number of staff suggests they are extensive. However, the elliptical I used while there was mediocre in design, but nice looking, so form may take precedence over function. While I had no opportunity to sample the restaurants, the food associated with my meeting was excellent. There is no reason to expect anything less from the restaurants or room service. The meeting rooms themselves were designed to the same standard as the residence part of the hotel, and very nice.

“Hotel da film in NYC” Questo hotel,di ottima struttura e rinnovato pochi anni fà,sembra uscito da un film di Batman.Si tratta di un grandioso skyscrape di 46 piani nel cuore pulsante di Times Square,con vista spettacolare su NYC ai piani alti.Camere standard non grandissime,ma lettone king size ultracomodissimo,con bagni normali:si paga cara la location,la vista e naturalmente la Città.Tutti i confort e i servizi che volete al suo interno,e appena fuori dall'albergo,all'angolo con la 49th, vi troverete immersi nella follia e nella magica atmosfera di Times Square,comunque a due passi dalla 5 Avenue e da tutte le meraviglie che può offrire Manhattan.

“Al lado de Graceland” Está muy cerca de Graceland! Caminando está a menos de 5 minutos,pues solo 400 metros lo separa de la casa de Elvis. El centro de Memphis está a 11 kms, 10 minutos en coche. El hotel tiene piscina tiene forma de guitarra,el no va más, todo el hotel está decorado con fotos y cosas de Elvis, hasta en las habitaciones hay fotos del Rey. El desayuno es muy sencillo y es el típico hotel sencillo de carretera americano,pero con el toque temético de Elvis que es lo que lo hace especial. Nos quedamos también en el Peabody, y evidentemente es mejor hotel,pero este tiene otra gracia más auténtica.

“Affection for the Affinia - with Ear Plugs” The location is great for hockey fans - you could see Madison Square Gardens from the window. The room was HUGE! Not just for New York, but by any city standards. The bed was really comfortable and the staff were fantastic. Our only complaint was the noise. All night long we awoke to sirens and other loud street noises. A peaceful sleep is not easily won here. That said, we love the extra touches like Aveda products in the bathroom, the kitchen, the space and the staff. You can't go wrong here... just bring your best pair of ear plugs.

“Disappointed. Not up to Marriott standards.” Checked into the Marriott on Saturday, October 24th. No king bed available despite my Marriott rewards status and my reservation for a king bed. Finally found us a king bed in the "business wing" which required many steps and no elevator. Room was fine. Very average to below-average for a Marriott. No wireless in room, no ethernet cable and when I called for one, was told there would be a wait. Bartender at hotel bar (Sam) was less than friendly. Menu for room service and hotel restaurant was barely adequate. Was in town for the Marine Corps Marathon and was very disappointed when we tried to order spaghetti for room service the night before the marathon and was told, "Oh, we're out of spaghetti sauce." I said, "So you have a hotel full of marathoners and you don't have spaghetti sauce?" Woman on room service line said, "Yes, we've been out since yesterday." So I got a bowl of plain pasta and my husband got a small personal pizza. Personal pizza appeared to be a frozen microwave pizza and tasted that way. Overall, the only highlight of the hotel was the extremely friendly "Lobby Ambassador" Joe. He was kind, helpful and very friendly. Rest of the staff was eh, barely acceptable. Disappointed for a Marriott.

“Hotel with great service, nice decor, great location--a winner!” I was in Washington to visit friends and family over last weekend, and I needed to stay in a hotel in the city for one night. I usually stay in a Starwood or Hilton property for points or a Four Seasons/Ritz Carleton type property for a luxurious experience. Since I was only going to be there for a night, and I needed to be convenient to frieinds in Alexandria and in College Park, I ended up at the Hotel Palomar. I found it on expedia.com and had never heard of it or the chain before, but I had heard good things previously about the Kimpton chain. What good fortune that expedia search turned out to be. For just $139, I had a deluxe room with a king bed. The room was quite sizeable, and the decor reminded me of a more plush W type hotel. Very chic, modern decor, but not nearly as minimalist as a W can sometimes be. I found the room very comfortable and stylish. The hotel was extremely well-located, just a block or 2 above Dupont Circle, and about that distance from a the Dupont Metro station. Service was impeccable for such a short stay. Room service was delivered to me after my check-in within about 20 minutes. They had forgotten my dessert, but brought it to me in about 10 minutes free of charge and with sincere apologies. Directions and suggestions for restaurants were given with enthusiasm and a sincere desire to make my stay pleasant and easy. Not bad for a single night guest. All in all, I was extremely pleased. Fantastic value. Great decor. Nice service. Good location. I couldn't really complain about a thing. For the price, you can't go wrong. I will definitely try to stay here again. Points be darned!

“Pleasant Stay” My wife and I stayed at the Four Seasons this last weekend and found it worthy of its high ratings. The staff was wonderful. The property is well maintained. Our room was clean and comfortable. On the ninth floor you could still hear sirens etc but we slept soundly and enjoyed our stay. WiFi is not free. The Business Center is user friendly with no charge for the first 30 minutes on line.

“Clean - recently renovated hotel in Downtown LA” I travelled to LA for a meeting in late November and had to stay in downtown LA. I did my research on Trip Advisor. The reviews I read were very helpful and they turned out to be very accurate. The hotel recently was renovated, the room I stayed in was very clean and spacious. The hotel is home to "the most romantic downtown restaurant in LA - 2011" according to a local LA newspaper. The restaurant was nice, but I haven't spent enough time in other downtown LA restaurants to confirm or rebuff the claim it celebrates. The Omni offers a free black car ride to anywhere in the downtown LA area (i.e. within 3 miles radius from the Omni). I took advantage of this free service to have dinner at the L.A. LIVE complex (where the Staples Center and Nokia Theater are located). There are several restaurants in the L.A. Live complex - definitely worth checking out - rather than paying for a $30 one way cab ride to other LA neighborhoods. If you're in downtown for business - I definitely recommend the Omni for your stay.

“Beautiful, modern new hotel” Very contemporary, pretty new hotel near Beverly Hills. Nice rooms, good beds, and awesome views of the city. Pretty rooftop bar and pool. My only complaint is the cable tv. It was sorely deficient, with no ESPN, or PPV movies.

“Excellent Service” We got to the Westin Gaslamp after a long drive and I was disappointed to find out that the room was not ready at 7 PM. I did mention that to the agent, who, in turn, spoke to the supervisor and we quickly got a room on the 12th floor, with a nice view toward the Bay. The room proved to be noisy due to the AC, so I asked for it to be changed. The change was done seamlessly while we were out and about and was also upgraded to a larger corner room. The quick response from the staff was much appreciated - hiccups can happen, but it is the manner in which they are being resolved that matters. The rooms are newly renovated and have a fresh feel, in perfect agreement with one's expectation for a Westin. The area is very good, within walking distance from Gaslamp District, Seaport Village, USS Midway, Little Italy. The only negative aspect worth mentioning is the parking rate - only valet is available, at $32 / night. Coming from Vegas, where parking is free everywhere, I found it excessive to pay close to $100 for parking for a week-end, roughly the same amount I spent on gas for the drive from Vegas to San Diego and back.

“not as quirky as i thought it would be” We stayed here for 4 nights early last month, based solely on trip advisor reviews, i feel a little bit disgruntled. From the hotel website i thught our room was going to be really quirky but disappointingly it was just a bit old fashioned. Clean but old fashioned. We did have a seperate kitchen, bedroom and living room which was really handy when we put our son to sleep and then we could just chill out with a bottle of wine in the living room. The breakfast is nothing to write home about, and was a couple of pieces of fruit, some oj and some microwaved danish pastries ( never had hot danish before ) obviously brought straight out of the freezer and defrosted ?. Any way its a short walk to balboa park and the zoo about 5-10 mins. The staff were helpful but we didn't really see them much. The only main problem was that the tv didn't work throughout our stay, when we rang down they stated it was a problem with their cable service. i don't know if this was true or not. The pictures of the decking looks really nice but most of these flowers are plastic ?. All in all i can't really see why this is so high in trip advisors list.

“Great Location, Real Convenient” I was just down here for 2 nights on business and the hotel had it all. It was very conveniently located to everything in the area. Plenty of restaurants and bars within the vicinity. As figured, the hotel lounges were pretty pricey, about $7 for a domestic draft, but the vendors paid for it, so no problem. The rooms and mattresses were comfortable. The room was clean and had a nice view on the 33rd floor. I did notice that the wireless internet went in and out and was not consistent. Too bad they also charged $9.95/day for it. All in all, satisfied w/ the stay at the Hilton. I would definately return here for business, or even leisure.

“Great place to stay in Midtown” From the time I made the reservation to the time we checked out, our experience with this hotel was fantastic. My husband and I wouldn't stay anywhere else if we returned to New York. Lauren assisted me by phone with answering my many questions and making the reservation, and also left a personal, handwritten note in the room for us when we checked in. When she learned it was our first time in NY and we were staying for 10 days, she ensured we were booked into one of the square-shaped rooms (numbers end in 01 or 02) rather than the rectangular-shaped rooms (numbers end in 03-05), as they are configured to give more usable space - greatly appreciated. We found the size of the room to be larger than we had expected for the middle of Manhattan; we weren't tripping over each other the way we have in some other downtown big-city hotels we've stayed in. The king bed was very comfortable, if a little softer than I prefer. The shower was a good size, and there was lots of counter space in the bathroom. All the standard amenities, including coffee maker, hair dryer, in-room safe, flat-screen tv, iron and ironing board. But best of all, the room was immaculately clean, and this is coming from someone who is pretty fussy about these things. The linens looked as though they were brand new, and there wasn't a speck of dust anywhere. I had inquired when I made the reservation about the steps they take to prevent against bedbugs; suffice to say they take it very seriously, take significant prevention steps, and have never had an outbreak. There are so many little touches at this hotel - free wi-fi, free use of computers and printing in the lobby, brownies in the room at check-in, weather forecast card and chocolates placed in the room during turn-down each night. The staff are very welcoming and helpful - they greeted us each time we exited and entered the hotel, and answered countless questions about how to best get to points of interest in the city. The location of is great - a short walk to the Theatre District, Restaurant Row and subway stations, but not in the middle of the chaos of Times Square. The area is not unsafe or even unsavory. There are several hotels in a row on the street so lots of people coming and going at all hours. There is a significant NYPD presence in the Times Square and surrounding area; we never felt uneasy. From location to staff to cleanliness to amenities - everything was just excellent, and also an excellent value, and you really couldn't go wrong booking a stay here.

“Tired hotel, but good service” The hotel is in definate need of an updating. It is a good location, but just has seen better days. I am not a big fan of the walk able balcony on one side and the hall way entrance on the other. When I checked in I found out that the sliding door was unlatched. With some updates this will be a great hotel again.

“Great location!” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Omni 2/21 – 2/24 (Thursday – Sunday). I found a great rate of $219/night – probably due to it being off-season. I’m an Omni Select Guest member and we were upgraded to a deluxe King room. I requested to be away from construction as I had read of some complaints. We were right on 52nd street and didn’t hear a bit of construction. The room was quite large for NYC and had a sitting area with loveseat. The bathroom was clean and included a shower/bathtub combo. The TV is a bit small, but when in NYC, who watches a bunch of TV? As an Omni Select Guest, you get a free newspaper and 2 free beverages in the morning (you can pick what time they bring it). I thought this was a very nice touch and they were right on time with our coffee and juice each morning. There is an umbrella in the room, which came in handy on our trip. My only minor complaint about the room would be the towels and bathrobes seemed a bit dingy for a 4 star hotel, but really not that big of a deal. Turn-down service is offered nightly. The location is great, just a block off of 5th Ave. There is a subway station very close at 53rd and 5th Ave. that has the E line. There is also a close subway station at 51st and Lexington that has the 6 line. Since the weather was very cold on our trip (the biggest snow storm in 2 years!), we decided to cab it to Broadway shows at night. I think this could be walkable in better weather. However, there were often not cabs available and we often took the town cars that wait outside the hotel (for probably double the rate). This is probably not the hotel’s fault, but I wondered if there is some deal with the town cars and the hotel. Or maybe it was just the bad weather causing a lack of cabs. We were able to check in right away (even though we arrived at 11am) and also were granted late check out on our last day. We didn’t eat at the hotel, but the Fireside restaurant looked nice. I would definitely stay at this hotel again if I found a good rate. Any questions, feel free to PM me.

“Oldest Westin that seemed dirty and dark but in a supreme location” Hotel itself is historic looking, meeting rooms were dark without windows, rooms were good sized as was bathroom which were newer looking, everything was dark without enough lights and dirty along walls and corners, doors were old old old, room service was so so and the beds werent that comfy but the best part was the shower!!! Dbl headed and the best water pressure!!

“4 star decor - 3 star service” First thing to keep in mind about this hotel is that it appears to be a destination hotel built for baseball fans and it's situated directly across from the Astros stadium. With that perspective - it helps explain some otherwise odd rules that have been mentioned here (no coolers, $100/night "deposit", etc.). The hotel itself is very well decorated. The decor is built around a baseball theme - albeit sophisticated - so you'll see a lot of dark wood, granite, etc. The room was spacious and clean and contained all the amenities you'd expect from a luxury hotel. The service was spotty from the start. Upon arrival - three valets stood by their stand and left me standing in the street until I finally parked the car at the curb myself and walked over and handed them the keys. Every subsequent experience with the valet staff was top notch however and the $23/nightly valet fee is in line with what I'd expect from a downtown hotel. There was an event one morning that blocked off several streets in the area (including the one in front of the hotel) and made car exit from the hotel almost impossible. While I don't blame the hotel for this - the staff should have been aware and an advanced warning would have been helpful for me to time my departure. In light of the baseball crowd, I can understand a deposit, but not the logic of it being based per night of the stay. Housekeeping is in the room daily to spot anything and I doubt that people are inclined to do more damage on a longer stay (probably the opposite). With this in mind - I'd beware if you are booking a stay longer than a couple days as that fee could add up. All in all, it was a pleasant stay. I'd say if you are coming to Houston for a baseball game - this is a great pick and puts you in the middle of the action. For everything else - there are a couple boutique hotels downtown that do a better job of blending style and service.

“Sehr schön und preiswert” Wir konnten eine Übernachtung für USD 89 ergattern über die Seite des Hotels. Diesen Preis empfanden wir als sehr preiswert. Das Hotel ist sehr gut ausgestattet und bieten eigentlich sämtlichen Luxus. Das Personal war sehr freundlich. Die Zimmer waren Suiten und deshalb ziemlich geräumig. Einziger Nachteil: Das Hotel ist weit ausserhalb der Stadt.

“Absolutely Best Choice!” We stayed there for a 4 day Get-Away Trip on the Memorial Day Weekend. The staff was outstanding friendly, gave tips and information what to do without even asking, the reception hall is pleasent and bright. The room size is absolutely perfect and has modern interior. The bathroom was small comparing to the rest of the room but still okay. We've got every day new shower gel or body lotion if it was used the day before. They provide even special Facial Soap and a face cloth from Neutrogena, which is a good - not cheap brand. Everything was clean and the hotel was very quiet. (At least the time we stayed there) They have an inside and an outside pool, nice bar and restaurant. The breakfast buffet was comprehensive and fresh. The Location is very central and has a perfect connection to several highways. Easy short trip to Sea World, Downtown, Old Town, Balboa Park etc. It is sourrounded by several huge shopping malls and restaurants. Trolley Station across the street. Parking cost extra but there is alos plenty on street parking available. I would recommend this Hotel to everyone and Yes I would defenetly stay there again. Unfortunately we did not have nice weather at our stay but especially than I was glad to have a comfortable nice clean room.

“Nothing wrong with this place” I stayed at the W for one night recently, after not having stayed there for about six years. The rooms are admittedly small, but the hotel was clean and quiet, and well-located for my office building (Sears/Willis tower). The price was reasonable. If I were coming to Chicago for leisure and paying on my own, I would probably stay near the Magnificent Mile as the hotels are better located (more things to do in the evening). After 6pm, nothing is open near this hotel. The "business center" was incredibly expensive and not used (because of the high prices). Overall, no major complaints.

“Great hotel, but POOR meeting services” Excellent hotel in a great location. The rooms/facilities were great. I held a meeting here and was surprised to see a HUGE bogus charge on my CC a month later. The hotel sent me a bogus receipt that I have never seen before. My sign in sheet has a figure that does not come close to the hotel's figure. I would advise not to provide any CC details to this hotel as they just process numbers without warrant and or warning.

“Great Facility - Below Average Service” Pros: - New facility. - Next to a church (Seventh-day Adventist). - Flat-screen TVs with many channels. - Very clean rooms. - Micro-fridge in all rooms. - Completely non-smoking building. - Dependable wireless with computer/printer in lobby. - Very close to downtown (less than 5 miles from AT&T Center/ 7 miles from Alamo). - Fantastic rate (around $55 + coupon deals from hotels.com). - Ice machine on each floor. - Free parking. Cons: - Hotel staff help is sporadic with an attitude. It depends on who you ask/contact. - Breakfast area not kept full throughout breakfast times (6-9am). - Thermastat in room too sophisticated to run. - Walls are very thin (you will hear loud snorers next door). Summary: I recommend staying here with great facilities, but don't anticipate attentive service.

“Elegant and stately without being stuffy, and a great location.” This is an excellent, historic and stately hotel located in the heart of downtown Austin. Very nice rooms, with a good restaurant (Roaring Fork) and adjoining wine bar downstairs, and also a balcony bar upstairs as well. there are a number of good restaurants and bars located fairly close by within walking distance. Although my room was a bit small, and a view of the air conditioning units, it was quite well furnished and had a large bathroom with a comfortable bed.

“Luxushotel nahe Times Square” Das Sofitel liegt für eine New York Erkundung hervorragend, es sind nur wenige Schritte bis zum Times Square. Erfreulich ist das Innendesign mit Blumenarragements in der Lobby und gemütlichen Sitzecken. Der Service war hervorragend, die Bediensteten waren äußerst aufmerksam und zuvorkommend. Das Zimmer war von guter Größe, sehr sauber und mit allem ausgestattet, was man benötigt, um sich wohlzufühlen. Das Frühstück im Hotelrestaurant wäre bei Einzelbestellung ganz schön ins Geld gegangen, wir hatten es zum Glück inclusive. Gute Auswahl, ungewohnt, daß alles à la carte zu bestellen war und frisch aus der Küche kam.

“Improved over previous visits” This hotel has been renovated since my last visit. I honestly avoided this hotel in recent years, but due to other properties being sold out I had to stay here. The rooms have been renovated, and they are improved over my last visit. This hotel is frequently sold out, and you can tell as the hallway carpets (at least on the 2nd floor) have obvious wear and stains. The rooms are well used, but mine was clean. This hotel isn't in the nicest area. There is a Bob Evans in front, and a Texas Roadhouse to the South on Shadeland Ave. Other than that, dining choices are limited, and other than Bob Evans, you can't walk to eat. This hotel is right off of I70 and 465 East, so freeway access is easy. There is a decent indoor pool if you have kids.
“Closer to airport, very clean and updated!” Great hotel for value. Rooms are spotless and large. Modern and up to date.

“Mediocrrity thy name is Crown Plaza” On the plus side, the lobby is spacious and pleasant. Starbucks coffee is available...the lobby bar is cozy and drinks are well priced....rooms are adequate...nothing out of the ordinary but adequate....On the negative side...five elevators serve 400-plus rooms....for the better part of one day of our three day stay two elevators were out of service for guests because they were being used to cart materials for a conference from one floor to another...this resultred in 20 plus minute waits for a ride.....at cvheck in I requested a room with a river view in a nearly empty hotel...request politely but firmly denied, even with a Priority Club membership.....on the other end of our stay I requested a late checkout, a priviige usually granted Priority Club members space permitting...the hotel was not busy because it was a weekend,,,again, request denied.....minor annoyances....in room coffee maker did not work...requested a change....no coffee maker appeared.... None of these things made for a terrible experience, but staff inattentiveness and lack of responsiveness detracted from what could have been a better stay.

“Mixed feelings!” I stayed at this hotel first for a bachelorette party in the summer of 2006. Overall, the place is very clean and the accomodations are good. We had an ample size room for 8 girls that even had a little kitchenette. It worked out perfrectly for hosting our soire. After a pleasant stay, I recently booked this hotel when I needed to stay in the city for a wedding. I called ahead of time to request early check-in. The hotel standard check-in time is 3pm and I was hoping for a 2pm check-in so that I could shower and get ready for the wedding, which was to take place at 3:30pm. I was told that early check-in could not be gauranteed, but that my request has been noted. I was also told that the hotel has a full locker room for their gym facility. Not wanting to go through the hassle of showering and getting ready for the wedding in a locker room, I called again a few days before my arrival and was told I would most likely not be able to get the hotel room early since the hotel was booked in full the night before. This made no sense to me considering check-out time is at noon and they had 3 hours to prepare rooms for 3pm check-in. Surely they could have one room available by 2pm for me? I arrived at the hotel a few hours early since my train got into the city that morning. Again I was fed the same story that I could not check-in early. When I inquired why, I got the same response about the hotel being booked in full the night before. I explained that I didn't understand how this worked and that it seemed unreasonable that my request of an hour early check-in could not be granted. Fortunately after going back and forth, the receptionist phoned their nearby, sister hotel land transferred me there without any problems or additional payments. Overall, the hotel is not bad, but if you have to check-in early, I'm sure you can find a better place! At least they were accomodating in sending me to their nice sister hotel!
“okay motel in austin” i stayed here one night while visiting austin to see some friends - this is nothign special, but it's clean - i would consider this property again

“高いけどいい” 一人旅で利用しました。 便利なのはポートオーソリティがすぐ近くだと言うことです。 ウッドベリーに朝一に行くにもすぐいけて、帰りも大荷物でもあっさりホテルです。 吉野家がすぐ隣にあり、一人旅でレストランも面倒だったりする時に便利です。 部屋は広く、スターバックスのコーヒーも嬉しいです。 電話は通信がとても高いと聞いたので使ってません。 冷蔵庫の飲み物も抜くと課金されるため触ってません。 お風呂は実験室みたいですが、清潔でヨカッタです。 ベッドはうわさどおり快適でした。 価格が合えばまた利用したいです。

“Hip Hotel in Theater District” We stayed at this new InterContinental for a one-night vacation in NYC. We booked directly through the hotel's website. Although I thought the rate was high, it was the least expensive nice hotels in the city. Maybe because it was so new. The hotel is extremely close to most Broadway theaters, restaurants, and Metro stops. We saw "In the Heights," a very short walk away. The hotel itself is a modern tower with very hip decorations and furnishings. My one concern is that the staff's attitude seemed to reflect the self-understood hipness of the place. But everyone was friendly. The fitness center was a city-ish, fun room with lots of equipment. There wasn't a whirlpool or pool, which would've been nice. Our room was on the corner, so we had a decent view and could almost make out the Hudson River. The street noise was faint. The room was very clean and modern. I loved the bathroom, especially the shower.

“Low quality for Sheraton” This used to be the main hotel on College campus, until the Hilton opened up. This hotel has never been known to be that nice. Pros: staff was excellent, very helpful with needs, Location OK Cons: tight room, uncomfortable bed & linens If you need a place to stay on campus, it is serviceable. Nothing nice. The rate is high because of the location. Try to get into Hilton at Penn first!

“quiet” it has a perfect location in downtown Seattle. Within two blocks, we could get to Nordstrom, Macy's and Westlake center. Safe neighborhood and a comfort room(Artist King). Want to visit again. Area recommendations Downtown Seattle is a blast!

“Nice place close to everything” Priceline is always the luck of the draw. Your never sure where you might be put up. This time we lucked out. The place was definitely a great buy for NYC. Check in was quick and friendly. The room was clean, modern, small but for NYC, I would consider it average in size. The view from the room faced 5th ave and looked down upon St. Pat's. The bed cart was requested at check in and was brought up within 5 minutes. Checking out we requested they hold one bag so we could walk around the city. They did so graciously and charged us nothing. My only complaint, and this is really trying to find something wrong with the place but it would have to be the elevator and using your room card to access your floor. Once you got use to it and choose the floor quickly after inserting the card you were all right.. but it takes something to get use to. If your going to a play on Broadway or just looking to hang around Mid-Town, you can go wronger here. Highly recommend.

“Wonderfully Walkable.” Such a great location! I could walk to the Liberty Bell, Love Statue and the Market is spitting distance from the hotel. The room itself was insanely comfortable with a plush bed, big tv and fast WiFi. Valet was a huge cost at I think $26/night. My suggestion would be to shuttle from the airport and walk or taxi. Especially if you're not comfortable with driving on one way streets and cars parked in the middle of the lanes (they are spaces, but it takes getting used to). Very clean, quiet, comfortable, and kind. The bar was also a nice atmosphere with a friendly staff.

“Charming but tired” I have stayed here before and enjoyed it so was happy to be booked back in. However it did not quite live up to my memory. There is a fine line between traditionally charming and downright old fashioned! My room was on the 7th floor. The bed was comfortable and the room tidy and clean. The air conditioning was OK but was either off or on - no temperature control - at least that I could find. The bathroom was the disaster: a bath that would not drain away, a shower that was feeble and occasionally just decided to become scorching hot with no human intervention, a sink plug that would not plug, a toilet that flushed haphazardly, a washing line that was broken and interesting smells and gurgling from the overflow. The staff are pleasant and the location is great - its just the bathrooms that need a good overhaul.

“Little on the old side” Close to Hobby if that is your aim. Large rooms with great beds. Bathroom is so small that you have to close the door to use toilet. Strange since the rest of the room is spacious. Large desk and nice TV.
“What you expect from Hampton Inn....” I stayed there for a business trip.....the rooms were clean, the breakfast was fine....nothing really special, but decent accommodations.

“Très, très bel hôtel au coeur de Boston” Une décoration raffinée hors du temps, un personnel chaleureux et un emplacement proche de tous les centres d'intérêts font de cet hôtel un must à Boston. Les chambres sont cosy et décorées avec goût, les lits sont extrêmement confortables et le linge de bain particulièrement moelleux, le seul bémol des chambres reste leur surface, très variable dans la même catégorie. N'hésitez pas à en demander une spacieuse lors de votre check-in. Le petit déjeuner est simplement fabuleux, spécialement leurs oeufs Bénédicte, et leurs croissants parmi les meilleurs du monde!!!

“Wonderful Stay, we'll be back!” I just spent a wonderful night at the Hotel Sorella, Sat. March 24th. Service was wonderful and the rooms are very nice. I asked for a room on a high floor facing away from the citycentre activities and I'm glad I did! We didn't hear a thing and it made for a great night's sleep! The beds are very comfortable and decorated nicely. The room had plenty of pillows, towels and 2 bathrobes. We are from Katy so this was a mini staycation after having dinner at Eddy V's and sipping wine at the tasting room. We also visited the bar at the MonaLisa and they had a live band that was AWESOME!

“Excellent Hilton Property” I will combine my review of the Hotel and Lucas Oil Stadium. The Hotel was excellent. absolutely nothing negative to say. Breakfast,staff,room,internet.parking,everything outstanding. This hotel is close to Keystone Crossing shopping Center,and on Saturday night you had to hunt for a parking spot. We tried to eat at The Cheesecake Factory,A minimum one hour wait. Forget it. We attended a Indy Colts game on Sunday afternoon against the Falcons.Paid 16$ for tickets in section 626 Row 20. This is an excellent facility.Even in the Upper deck you could see the field great.This is a state of the art football stadium. I would certainly return to both the hotel and Lucas Oil Field. Parked at 327N Illinois street about a 15 min walk,advance pay only for 5$. Anthing around Lucas Oil Field was 20-30$.

“Disappointed.” Stayed at this "resort" for 2 days in August. Coincidentally before our stay, USA Today published an article about how great the pool area was. Perhaps this set expectations too high, as this resort was a huge disappointment. On the plus side, the grounds and overall property and design were very nice. Rooms has a garden, floral design and bathroom was huge with a nice shower. There is a nice computer system for rent in each room, and you could use it to efficiently make requests to the front desk or housekeeping (this part of the system was free). Property is also located next to Desert Ridge mall where you can find a bunch of shopping, restaurants, Target, etc. However, the resort experience left alot to be desired. The key item, as mentioned in other posts, is a faulty air conditioning system. The hallways smelled damp and musky. While the room A/C was better, it never cooled sufficiently or removed the humidity levels. Further, the pool area was awful. This could have been a result of this weekend being the most busy in the season (heard through another guest as claimed by their staff), but there were no seats, used food plates everywhere. It didn't quite live up to their Top 10 billing in USA Today. Hoping these guys will clean up their act and make this worth of the J.W. Marriott brand.

“Excellent value” We arrived early and although the staff was not able to immediately check us into a room, they were very helpful in storing our bags, offering us bottled water and showing us where the breakfast room was. As many other reviewers have stated, I found this staff to be very friendly and they seemed to welcome the guests coming back into the hotel with genuine enthusiasm. The rooms were extremely clean as well as all the public spaces. The location is terrific for walking to your destination, catching a cab or getting the subway. Small lobby and business center, but they are well equipped.

“We enjoyed it last year and came back!” We stayed two nights in semi transit to LA to return to Australia. This is a hotel we stayed at last year (see review of 7Nov10) and so we came back. The hotel provides a great location to get around SF and once you know the Muni system etc it's easy. The facilities are very good and rooms comfortable, although the smaller rooms can be little cosy. We would have liked tea or coffee in the room or a central point at which to go for it. Instead our enquiry was politely dealt with by a referral to the kitchen staff to see if they would co-operate. We had a fallback plan! WiFi was unreliable but we muddled through and maintained our holiday blog. Breakfast was a treat again. The server in the morning is so bright and cheerful that your day must start off well. Food is great and there is sufficient for a good start to your day. Listen carefully as the accent is a bit strong but then our accent is probably as difficult! There are some good restaurant options close by if you don't want the 4 course option in Jeanne D'Arc restaurant. The only killer is that walk up Powell St from Sutter to Bush! We'll stay here again if we get to visit SF again.

“Typical Quality Inn, Good Price” I stayed here one night driving cross-country; this was the least expensive of the Quality Inns in Indianapolis and one of the least expensive of comparable chains. I thought it was just fine. My room was clean, bed was very comfortable (quite firm), large room, normal Quality Inn amenities. Window opened about 5", a plus for me, though if you want quiet, best to keep window closed. The free breakfast was pretty typical - hard-boiled eggs, biscuits/gravy, make-your-own waffles plus assortment of cold items. Terrible coffee though - weak and only luke-warm. I would certainly stay here again if I were passing though but would go out for coffee or make in my room.

“Decent convention hotel” I have stayed at this property about 20 times during the past two years. The location (right above the Metro Center subway stop) is tough to beat and the rooms, while beginning to show a little wear and tear, are quite nice. If you have access to the Grand club that is an additional plus. The Cure Bar & Bistro is amazing. The gym is quite nice, but closes very early, especially on weekends. Over the years, I have had two major problems: 1) If you are in an atrium-facing room be prepared for noise issues. The outside-facing rooms are fine. 2) Service is hit or miss. The hotel has been great at recognizing me as a repeat customer and I honestly believe they had every intention of making my stays very comfortable, but for whatever reason the execution often failed. It felt like I had to complain about something every other stay and I finally determined last month that this hotel just doesn't offer the level of service I have come to expect from a Hyatt. Room service is not available until 6:30, so if you have an early flight or meeting there are no breakfast options even for coffee before then, which seems a little odd for a Grand Hyatt. Better Hyatt options in DC include the Hyatt Regency on Capitol Hill (excellent service) and, if your budget permits, the Park Hyatt. If you are looking for a dependable hotel for sightseeing or when you are attending a convention this is a worthwhile choice,

“Decent Budget Motel” We were greeted pleasantly and efficiently. The room and shower were clean. The room was small but well maintained. The bed was comfortable. The price is right. Next trip to or through El Paso we’ll go back

“This hotel was amazing...in the 30s. Stay Away!” As I am sure that this hotel was beautiful and amazing in the 1930s - they haven't redone the rooms since then. I was so disgusted when I saw my room I immediately checked out. The room had a rock hard bed, a 13" color box TV (???), and bolted shut windows overlooking a heavily crowded intersection of 5th street downtown. And I won't even start on the Motel 6 bathroom. PROS: - The lobby and ballroom are nostalgic CONS: - Location is horrible and you have to valet your car - Rooms haven't been updated since the 50s at LEAST - Bed is a rock - TV is ancient - Bathrooms look like they are from project housing

“Weird location but nice hotel” My company held its Christmas party in the hotel ballroom this year. The hotel offered $99 rates for guests who didn't want to drive home after the party. So my perspective is that of a local. The hotel is right in the middle of Georgetown Hospital, which is a bit strange, and it is connected to the University bookstore and other university functions. The room was nice, clean and quiet. Bath & Body Works toiletries (good stuff). The bed was the best--one of those new Revive beds. I slept like a baby. No view to speak of, but as a local, I really didn't care. I enjoyed walking around in Georgetown and acting like a tourist. I look forward to next year's Christmas party and staying here again.

“I Liked This Place!” I'm from L.A. and every year I teach here in S.F.and I'm put up in another place (can't remember the name) - This year I was put up at the Diva and I loved it. A very old building with a very new flair. Very Mercer-New York like. Modern. Everything was new, comfortable, worked. Granted there's no view, but why do you need a view when you're in San Francisco? Go walk! Convenient to everything. Especially the lively Union Square. Great restaurants, the nightlife. Are you kidding? For these prices??? You have to be nuts to stay anywhere else. I'm shocked that this is ranked (as of this writing) #47. The hotel front desk was very friendly and I even bought a DIVA T-Shirt (okay, okay, so it says SEXY on the back) Try it out. It's a hundred plus bucks in San Francisco! I saw these prices for Labor Day and am trying to talk my wife to going back. (She wants to go to Palm Springs. Ugh!)

“A Peaceful Oasis” My friend and I got a great rate on Priceline to stay here two nights Sept. 5-7. I had a terrible cold and had to spend a lot of time sleeping during our trip. The beds are SO comfortable--I have never slept so well in a hotel bed. In our two-bed room the beds were double-sized. We loved the look of the rooms--sort of Japanese modern with wood and olive trim. We called ahead and requested a room with a bathtub. Our room was located on the sixth floor, which I anticipated being dark. But it was actually just fine--about one-third of our window view was sky, so we had nice sunlight. The hallways are so cool--they are dimly lit with the room numbers glowing in cobalt blue. I want to stay here every time I visit--our room was such a pleasure to rest and relax.

“Better than I had expected!” I must say with some of the reviews I was prepared to be underwhelmed but the Hotel Chandler is a great little place in NYC. Note, emphasis on little. The rooms are TINY (I am guessing 200 square feet max). They have room service breakfast although for the life of me I don't know why - I can't imagine where you would sit to eat it. (tiny desk, one other chair in the room). There is no closet but a small wardrobe that holds about 5 hangers and space for a small suitcase. The bathroom is also tiny but the shower is AWESOME. Great overhead showerhead. Nice lobby and nice staff as well. I wouldn't plan on coming here for a week but for a night or two a lightly-packed single or couple would enjoy it.

“Ideal beach location” We stayed at the Catamaran for 5 nights in September 2010. The hotel is in a unique and desirable location. It is unique in that out the front door you are a 1 block walk from the Pacific Ocean, a fantastic beach and the PB / MB boardwalk while out the back door you are steps from the sands and calm waters of Mission Bay. You really are spoiled for choice and the phrase best of both worlds springs to mind. If you want for some reason to head downtown from here then there is a bus stop across the street and you are within walking distance to many eateries and bars. We have stayed in PB many times. This hotel itself is spot on. Lobby is a site to behold, performing parrots in the courtyard and the adjoining grounds would not seem out of place in a Hawaiian Island. The onsite gym is among the best I have experienced in relation to one provided by a hotel. The pool and hot tub and great as is the comfort of the surrounding loungers. In terms of the room, we stayed in the tower as opposed to the lower rise rooms which are dotted throughout the property. I have no issues with our room. Spacious, clean, nice balcony with a view to die for. Do not mistake me for equating this with a 5 star property because it is not. The thing is though that if luxury accomodation is what you seek then MB and PB aren't truely the places for you. The best you can get in terms of luxury would be the Tower 23 or the Pacific Terrace. However be prepared to pay 6 star prices for what is truely (in any other beach location) 4 star properties at best. If money is no object and/or you don't mind paying a premium then one of these 2 would be your preferred option. However, if you are happy with a solid 3 star in a great location for considerably less then you will not be disappointed with the Catamaran

“Wifi sucks, food expensive” I stay here 3-5 times a month due to work. Wifi sucks! Doesn't matter if you're on floor 5, or the executive floor on 13. Signal drops out every minute. Just gave up and used my 3G on my iphone. Food is expensive, as are most restaurants at hotels in this class. Pool is outdoors, but doesn't have that 'enticing' feel to it. Some nights it is loud in the hallways and I'm wondering am I at a motel? Beds are comfy and room is nice, but you can tell it's an old hotel. Old TV's in rooms, NO flatscreens. Thermostat is old fashioned dial where you're not really sure what the temp is. Just have to guess somewhere between 60-70, 70-80? Shower head is old and not great coverage/pressure. I don't mind staying here for the huge discount I get, but would NOT pay normal rates to stay here.

“Massive Room” Good all suite hotel offering very large rooms with free breakfast & dinner. Review based on a three night stay in October’10 (background of spending 80+ nights per year in different hotels around the globe) Location: Easily reachable with car, despite being “airport hotel” it is not actually located that near to the airport. Small mall located right next door including around 10 restaurants (Greek, Mexican, Subway etc) but no grocery store. Otherwise the neighborhood consists of purely office buildings. VTA train/tram Component station nearby allowing an easy & fast way to travel for example downtown San Jose for a beer. Or three. Room: I was upgraded to an absolutely huge two bedroom/two shower fireplace suite in the third floor. It was the first time for me being in a hotel room including one room that didn’t even step in (the second bedroom), so very much a true “home away from home” rather than the normal hotel room as such. Room was actually so big I almost lost things in there... Décor was very traditional, nothing too old or dark though. Room was rather well equipped with three LCD TVs, two bedrooms, two bathrooms (both including a shower), full kitchen and one fireplace. Room was clean, no stains etc anywhere. One issue is the there was no safe in the room. Or then I just didn’t find it! Etc: Breakfast was nothing to write home about. Happy hour during the evening served some “real” food and snacks with glorious full-bodied Bud Light on top and also some wine available. Didn’t think it was very good show... Small pool and a basketball court Would I return there? Absolutely, really spacious clean & quiet room with decent price

“Under construction, but still good hotel” Very reasonably priced and within walking distance to good restaurants. Area around the trolley line appears fairly safe - I walked at night with no issues. The entire lobby was under construction and I had to defeat a maze to find my room, but the room was quiet, clean, and spacious. I never heard construction noise from my room. Having stayed here before and during the construction, I prefer this hotel and will stay here again.

“Quiet and relaxing stay for my birthday” My bf and I checked in a day before my birthday. Having booked on Hotwire I was a bit worried that we would get stuck by the ice machine or the elevator but no. The front desk staff were very kind and got us situated in a comfy room. During the stay, the staff was very helpful recommending local resturants (non-touristy). The gentleman who took my order for room service was very patient and our food was made as ordered. Once again, the staff at the hotel make this our get away place in San Antonio.

“Great with kids” Great place to stay with kids. Was upgraded to a large corner suite. Room was very large and comfortable for the entire family. The corner room was quiet. Breakfast ok, not great, but free! Pool is very small and was crowded with kids. But it was a nice spot for them to let loose after touring all day. A bit of a walk to either of the 2 metro stations, but not bad. CVS and wine store about a block away for stocking up. Parking was a mess. Garage was full, so sent to the Ritz down the street.

“Exceptional Commitment to Customer Service” Had a 2 night stay while attending a business meeting. First of all, of all the Hiltons I have stayed in over the years, this ranks as #2 in terms of a friendly and professional staff (Hilton Green Park is still #1). Every staff member I encountered from the greeter, to front desk, to housekeeping, to wait staff all seemed genuinely interested in knowing that my stay was pleasant and without issues. As a business traveler, a commitment to customer service is important. I want to know that if there is an issue, it will be handled without complications. In terms of the room, I look for a comfortable bed, good work area, reliable high-speed wi-fi, overall quiet, and without any major maintenance/housekeeping issues. My room completely met my expectations with one exception as indicated below. There is a nightly manager’s reception for Hilton Honors members. It had to be the best manager’s reception I have ever attended. A variety of finger foods were served both buffet style and passed on a tray. Both quality and quantity were exceptional. Another nice little service touch: a manager was actually on-hand to greet attendees. Had dinner and breakfast in the restaurant and found service and food quality very acceptable. There are numerous indications that major renovations are occurring. My one complaint is with the doors to the guest rooms. They are designed to slam – maybe good for security but bad for noise. Not only does the slamming door cause a great deal of noise, it also causes the walls to shake. Hopefully with the renovations, this problem will be addressed. Overall, had a very pleasant stay and will definitely return.

“Excellent Hotel: Amazing Views” Stayed one night after booking on Priceline (2 adults, 2 kids). Boutique hotel is in a spectacular waterfront setting right on the pier. Staff were great. Views are breathtaking. Great lobby area takes in the water view and is very comfortable. The "hunting lodge" decor which some reviews take offense too seemed rather tasteful and appropriate to me (if you want bland, stay at a chain). Water side rooms get the views plus added amenities such as nicer bathrooms and flat panel tvs. City side rooms are almost as good but look backwards onto downtown. Major caveat on the city side rooms is the noise from the train tracks which are very close. Trains run all night. The hotel should invest in better soundproofing for the city side windows. Restaurant ("67") also has the amazing view and has excellent food. $26 valet parking charge is a little steep but not out of line for downtown Seattle. A regular lot across the street from the hotel is cheaper. It is about a 15 minute walk to the main part of downtown.

“Mixed feelings are unavoidable. Many ups but many downs” Booked at a decent price through priceline, the hotel is not bad in itself but - even though it HAS the POTENTIAL to be a decent 4* hotel, I don't think it reaches that level. First of all, the parking. It's amazingly bad that they wanna charge you 31 USD per night for the valet service. And that the self parking costs 20 USD per day but without in/out service. Ok, this seems to be a pretty standard fare at luxury hotels throughout the US, but still...! Then, the room: mine was very nice, newly redecorated. Bathroom was ample and quite nice. I liked the plasma tv (42"), but I find a bit strange that such a pricey place in a fancy city like LA doesn't provide you with complimentary slippers or bathrobes or coffee machine! Guys, come on! Internet is fast yet expensive in room (even though it's free in the lobby area). I liked the nice lanai. The swimming pool are looked ok. Again, I don't believe you have to pay 20 USD/day to access the Equinox fitness center! I didn't try the food, nor the room service; while the food and the main restaurant looked very nice, the prices were on the VERY STEEP side! Not even the Ritz-Carlton Dubai was so expensive! Location wise, it worked well for me: being in LA to visit UCLA it was a short drive from campus, and Beverly Hills is really minutes away (you can actually walk). Yet, all in all, I feel like a 4* hotel must offer more when it comes to complimentary items. If the Hyatt Regency Century Plaza will implement that policy, it will surely ranks as a 4* hotel. Otherwise, it will remain a big question mark in the LA luxury hotel panorama.

“tres bien placé” le principal atout de cet hotel est evidemment son emplacement à 5mn à pied sans souci de hollywood boulevard et du theatre chinois. facile de garer son auto avec le parking. sinon l'Hotel est assez classique pour les USA chambres agreables et renovées mais attention à celles qui donnent sur la rue elles sont tres buyantes (sunset blvd n'est pas une impasse ca bouge tout le temps) et les boulquies sont requis

“Close to everything! Washington Monument visible” This location couldn't be better if you have business in the District or if you plan to see the sights. Its close to the National Mall and the WHite House is about 2 blocks away. I had a great corner room with the Washington Monument visible from my window. The toiletries are much better than regular Marriott properties. The concierge lounge was always overcrowded with standing room only both at breakfast and for evening appetizers and drinks. This needs to be enlarged to account for the size of this hotel. The elevators are a notable standout. You need to enter the floor to which you want to go and the elevator will tell you which car to board to get to that floor. Nice for crowd control and very efficient when many people are trying to get in and out. Many good restaurants within walking distance as well

“Very nice!” I was very impressed with this hotel. The room was very large for NYC and it was clean and modern. I was able to get online quickly. I'm not a huge fan of all the stainless steel in the bathroom. It felt like a very upscale prison, but that is my only complaint. I was impressed with the amount of counter space. The neighborhood used to be very seedy, but not anymore. This hotel is conveniently located in Times Square near many Broadway Theaters. I was at the hotel for a meeting and the food was terrific. If you want to be in Times Square, this is a very good pick.
“cool - but not competent” If you want Hollywood Cool - this place has it. Very chic. If you want competency - not so much. Staff was very nice but one thing after another was off.

“great location” very stylish and exclusive feel to this hotel. the rooms are small like most nyc hotel rooms are the location across from Bryant Park is wonderful - ice skating and great holiday shopping in winter. service was excellent.

“Can't beat the location!” I stayed here for business in Feb. 2012. Company picked up the cost of the hotel room, but I felt that the rate could be slightly high. That said, this hotel is fantastic. It is so close to a huge mall, within walking distance of the Alamo and RIGHT on the riverwalk. Finding something to do in my down time was never a problem! I will be returning here in a few weeks w/ my spouse for a quick vacation!

“Great stay; not your typical Choice Hotels property.” I will preface this review by saying I typically would not stay at a Choice Hotel property, if I had another choice. Even for business travel, I like to stay at a nicer hotel,than Econo Lodge, Clarion, etc. I took a chance just from reading about the Ascend Collection brand and seeing pictures of this new hotel. It was indeed a pleasant surprise and certainly several steps above other Choice properties. I even had a celebrity sighting at the hotel, so they must be doing something right. The hotel had just opened and was nicely decorated with comfortable rooms. It was an easy walking distance to the subway. I am happy to say, I would stay here again!

“Very Nice Hotel” We stayed here in June and found it very nice. We had a corner room with double windows which was very great. The windows opened which I love in a hotel and as the weather was wonderful it was very refreshing. The room was very clean, the beds comfortable. Nice flatscreen TVs. The staff was very friendly always speaking to you as you came and left the buliding. There is a Starbucks close by as well as numerous other food shops. Valet parking is about the average for city hotels however the valet staff was very good and quick to bring your car when requested. The rooftop pool was very small but the view was nice.

“Not sure what I expected” For convenience it is great. Directly attached to Terminal B and with a shuttle service every 20 mins in the morning to all other terminals. It seems to be an older hotel despite the modern exterior. The staff were friendly, but every time I passed check-in there was a line - even at 4am! The room was very clean, but on the small side and the furniture and fittings looked a little past their best. The bed was comfortable and the room was quiet, in spite of facing onto a busy road. I ate at the restaurant. It is somewhat dark with a university boathouse theme. The hostess was absent from her podium a lot and I saw guests walk out after waiting too long, or going into the kitchen to find someone to seat them - not typical at a Marriott. The service was friendly, but also slow, and the food was fine, but nothing to write home about! The bathroom was small but plenty of hot water and a great shower. If you have an early or very late flight this is the most convenient choice and you will find a clean bed and friendly staff in a hotel that needs a somewhat improved infrastructure.

“One of the best Marriotts” My husband and I had stayed at this hotel 20 years ago for a wedding and we just recently stayed there for the DAR convention. We were pleasantly surprised to see that it had been updated but that it still had the same marble floors and beautiful chandeliers in the lobby. We stayed in a suite and it was very nice. There was at least one bathroom - can't remember if there was a powder room. The location is the best and everything of interest downtown is walkable. It's right next to the White House. The hotel restaurant is excellent as well and there is very good room service. The staff is friendly and helpful. Would definitely stay here again.

“OK not great” Considering how mediocre this place is I'm a bit embarassed at having stayed here several times over the years through several incarnations (it used to be a Lowes hotel). The room was rather tired, with a lousy view of a/c units on the roof of an adjacent bldg. Somewhat crumbling mortar in bath adds to the feel. Nice location, a few blocks removed from Rockefeller Center and walking distance to some great restaurants (eg Rosa Mexicano). Concierge was helpful. Adjacent parking is $30/night with hotel discount, ok for the city. Unless I got a great price (like $150 or so) I'd proably stay in Beekman Towers a few blocks east.

“The La Quinta Satisfies!” My stay at the LQ was on Aug 3-4th, 2007. The front desk attendant was efficient and polite. My room #213 was exceptionally clean and the AC unit was perfect. The swimming pool area was a delight. The gym is small with 2 pieces of equipment out-of-order. The early morning breakfast bar opens at 4 am! The LQ is walking distance from Bennigans and Ruby Tuesday and a short drive fron Chilis. The LQ is ideally located near the Airport; about 5 miles away. There is a transport bus that seems to come by every 30 mts for the airport.

“Funky but a tad disappointing on some things” I stayed at this hotel on business for a week in October 2003. This is a very funky looking hotel! The outside looks awesome, with glass shooting up into the sky. You have to go up an escalator to get into the lobby which is ok unless you want to take your own bags in which case it was a bit unwieldy. Check in was ok, but I got the impression we were one of many and so service was not as personal as it can be in other Westin hotels. I got a corner room which gave me a bit of extra space which was nice. The normal size room that my colleague had was not as big and kind of square which was a bit odd. Bed was divine! Shower was too! The decor was nice, but sort of metallic (I think that is the funky part!). My recollectiion of the food is that it was acceptable but not stand out. It was well located - right near Times Square which was very cool. That was a lot of fun, and probably great if you are NYC on holidays. I'd stay there again but not before trying some of the other Starwood hotels first.

“Nice hotel” This was a nice, well appointed JW. Rooms appeared recently redone and the bathroom was quite large. I will ding it a star for having an ice cold lobby, the most confusing maze of hallways known to mankind, and a less than impressive response to me mistakenly taking a bottle out of the mini-bar to look at it (they have one of those sensors that charges you automatically, which I realized once the bottle was in my hand since the sign wasn't too obvious. The woman at the desk acted like I committed a felony despite the fact that I called within 30 seconds of it happening. She seemed very put off that she had to send someone up to verify the stock in the minibar because I was an idiot. Granted, they were sold out, it was Lollapalooza after all, but I think we still deserved what is usually a high level of service from them. Or at least the benefit of the doubt. There was a pool listed in the amenities and on maps, but apparently it wasn't completed yet. That was a disappointment. This is a good location if you're travelling on business, but a bit of a hike from the shopping and restaurants, so take that in to consideration if you're going on the weekend - there isn't much near the place at all, and it gets a little sketchy after dark.

“Great hotel! Great value!Great staff!” You cannot beat the location of this Hyatt. It is right on the Riverwalk and central to everything. Costs us 22 bucks from the airport in a cab during the middle of the day. Apparently you can take a SANtran for 17 dollars per person. If you have more than 1 in a party, taxicab is IT!! We were upgraded to an Alamo view room and it was worth it! The check in/check out staff was excellent and courteous. The room is very spacious and clean. Housekeeping does an adequate job but very responsive. Loved the gym! There is fresh and cold water with lemon/orange slices round the clock. What a treat! We had a great rate booking with the hotel directly. Parking is a bit expensive but there are other parking garages. Overall, we had a great experience with this Hyatt and will definitely stay there again!!!

“Great location, beatiful rooms...don't use the phones!” We spent 3 nights at this hotel and loved every one of them! From check in to check out everything went just right. The only minor details that kept this from being a perfect hotel was the charges for the phone; $2 for a local call and charges for collect calls too!!!! I consider that price gouging especially when rates are not marked clearly anywhere. The other minor detail was when I called the front desk for shampoo and conditioner (which wasn't replenished after the room was cleaned) it took over 30 minutes and a follow up call for it to finally arrive. Regardless of these minor details, I would highly recomend this hotel and definately stay again.

“A magical conference at the Westin” This is my second stay at the Westin. This time I was there as the president of a professional group for our convention. When I checked in the front desk staff saw that I had my family in tow (wife, mom, three kids) and immediately upgraded us to a bigger suite. That was so thoughtful and we really needed the space! The suite was heaven and the entire conference was wonderful. Great rooms, great service, good food (room service was wonderful). The conference facilities were perfect for our 300 person conference and having the Riverwalk so close made having a fun time easy. The staff went out of their way to help us because on our last day the Rock and Roll Marathon took over the town. Thanks to the concierge and bellman we were able to secure a taxi with no problem, even in the midst of a marathon. I wish the gift shop was bigger (it is quaint) and one area was under construction but that was not an issue. My stay combined business and pleasure with my conference going well and my family also being entertained. It was a magical time. One issue - why is the internet so expensive? $13 a day? I know it's free in the lobby but the charge is excessive given internet is free at lesser hotels. I think it's time basic internet was free and maybe charge for high bandwith access.

“Great central location!” Recently stayed at the Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Avenue hotel. Was pleasantly surprised of the great location and fair price for two nights. Was able to book hotel online. Rooms are on the small side, but comfortable for a short trip. Easy access to Times Square and theater district. If need to stay overnight again would certainly consider this hotel again. Rooms were generally clean and furnsihings updated.

“Too dingy for three stars” I don't feel like complaining too much, because I got this hotel on Priceline for what I'd normally pay for a Motel 6, and it was definitely nicer than a no-frills motel. But it's just too run-down and dingy to qualify for 3 stars, in my opinion. The water pressure in the shower is awful, they only give you a little shampoo and soap for amenities, and you practically step into the toilet when you get out of the shower. But there were some very nice positive aspects as well. Free parking, free Internet which worked fine, and a 24-hour fitness room that had good working treadmills in it. The bed was fine for me, though some don't like the adjustable pressure thing. The TV got plenty of channels. The staff was very nice, gave me a quiet room when I requested it (so I didn't hear too much airport noise) and also gave me an extra hour to check out the next day, which I really appreciated. I would definitely come back here, but if I were paying a 3-star rate I'd be very disappointed in the accommodations. For $40, it was perfectly acceptable.

“Good option in pricey Boston” I stayed at the Bulfinch in May 2008 for four nights. I found the location of the hotel to be a bit removed from the main action of the town, but close enough to walk to Faniuel Hall and Quincy Market in about five minutes. That was actually a great thing since it seemed to be a bit quieter in the hotel, making it easier to sleep. I arrived at the hotel a bit too early for the 3:30 p.m. check-in but the hotel gladly held my bags while I searched for lunch in the area. It's only a short walk to the pubs that line the streets leading to the Boston Garden. The personnel at the hotel seemed friendly and helpful. When I returned to the hotel to check-in, the process was quick and efficient. The small lobby requires some manuevering if you have big bags. A nice touch - there's water dispensers next to the elevator, great refresh on a hot day. The rooms are small, but it is a city hotel in a really cool building. The style is a bit modern, with some retro touches. Because of the architecture of the building, my room had a funky, long hallway-shaped bathroom. The bathroom was nice, marble counters and good amenities. My bath only had a stand-up shower, which is fine for me, since I don't normally take baths in hotels. Good water pressure in the shower too! The bed was comfortable and the reading lights were adequate. The only complaints I had was there was no closet, just a wardrobe and more importantly to me, no luggage rack and that the air conditioner unit blew directly on you if you were working at the desk, which seems like I'm reaching to complain about something! I did not eat in the hotel restaurant so I can't comment on that. But I did really like this hotel. It was small enough to be friendly and it was only a long block from the Blue Line T stop (to go to and from the airport). I walked to my conference about a mile away and got to pass right by some of the historic sights in Boston. I would definitely stay in the Bulfinch again.

“fabulous hotel” Good location on 33rd. Check in/lounge very small, but i suppose thats new york. they did have ipods at the seating areas with preloaded music/movies, so thats a nice touch. Our jr king suite was excellent, however. very large, mega-nice bed and bedding. the corner-room view was spectacular (of the water and the city). superb executive-level desk. all furnishings nice and especially comfortable.. even pull-out sofabed.
“Great location” Great miracle mile location. Everything was within walking distance including Navy Pier. Worth staying if you can get a good rate on hotwire!

“Modern Luxury in a great location” Spent 4 nights at this hotel through New Years and had a wonderful stay. The staff was courteous & attentive. Our room was clean, modern and beautiful. The bathroom was absolutely fabulous. The location was terrific, just a couple of blocks to shopping at the Magnificent Mile and a couple of blocks to the red line metro stop. The bar downstairs was very hip and a fun place to hang out late night. Many restaurants and coffee shops in the area along with a terrific market 1/2 block away on N State street. We visited some of the other luxury hotels in the area and both agreed we were happy we picked the Sofitel.

“The right value for the price” like everyone else, i was a little apprehensive about the shared bathrooms, but they WERE VERY CLEAN!! probably the cleanest hotel bathrooms i've ever encountered. it seems like they somehow clean them after every use. the rooms were small, and yes, the elevator was too. but it's an old building and back then people didn't take up nearly as much space! seriously, it was clean, comfortable, and the staff was helpful and friendly. the right (and expected) value for the price. i have no complaints.

“Studio Minus! TEENY ROOMS!” Like another reviewer, I also got this hotel on Priceline for a bid of $32. For the price I'm pleased, BUT the room I got was by far the smallest I've ever had at a Studio Plus, which usually offers larger rooms than Extended StayAmerica, it's lower priced clone. The bed is crushed right up against the air con/heating unit! Along with all the furniture they've crammed in this clausterphobic space, it made for quite a squeeze for my husband and I. Pros.... Located right off of I-10 on the far west side of town Clean and new Full kitchens Plenty of shopping and fast food near by, plus a casino Cons... rooms are way too small, no counter space in bathroom the worst chairs I've ever experienced, low to the ground and tilted forward. These chair serve as both your dining and your workspace chairs, which makes both uncomfortable The little bitty TV is placed far away from the bed and couch, and at a weird angle, so it's hard to see from anywhere but the kitchen area This hotel would be okay for a single person, but not for two full sized adults!

“cool” I am staying here next time I find myself in DC. We had heard the place was really nice.You can't go wrong with a Kimpton , right? Anyway we went to meet friends at the bar for drinks. It was 30 minutes from opening. The wait staff was there setting up and they encouraged us to come in as they would go ahead and get us started. They were friendly and accomodating. The place is really cool. the bar had a bohemien feel to it. Comforatble chairs and sofas Jazz music playing. I could have stayed all night. It is in the Dupont circle area which is an awesome place to be however it is off the main drag so it is quieter. They grabbed us a cab as we left and all thanked us. They also showed us a room. They have a comfortable feel to them and offer yoga kits.

“Don't Stay at the Lancaster” We stopped staying at the Lancaster about 3 years ago because we thought it was getting run-down. This weekend we decided to try the Lancaster again for a weekend stay in the hopes that its owners (the Valencia Group) would have refurbished it. Bad news: they haven't. The upholstery on the couch in our room was stained and ripped, with the stuffing showing; the bed's mattress was lumpy and uncomfortable; the carpet was really grimy; the hallway smelled; the phone handset never worked and never was repaired (though we notified management); and the bathroom sink ran rusty water the first two times we turned it on. The tragedy is that in the mid-1990s, this was a lovely small hotel The hotel has a killer location (which is perfect for travelers who are in Houston for the opera, ballet, symphony or Alley Theater ), a nice staff (who despite failing to fix our phone problem are friendly, caring and attentive) and free wireless Internet access throughout the property. But for their rack room rate, one can do much better in downtown Houston and in locations that are still quite convenient to all the best cultural activities. We won't stay here again until there's evidence that it has been completely renovated and refurbished.

“Great Views!” We just got back from a week long stay at the San Diego Marriott. Overall, it was a good experiece. The main reason we were there was for a conference that my husband was attending, but we were also celebrating our 5 year weddng anniversary during the trip. We paid for a City View room and the hotel upgraded us to a Bay View Room w/a Balcony for free. They also sent some complimentary champagne to our room in honor of our anniversary. The room was nicely appointed and had Marriott's new bedding, which made for a very comfortable night's sleep. The bathroom was on the small side, but was clean and functional. The views of the city skyline and San Diego Bay from our balcony were fantastic! Having a balcony really added to our enjoyment of the room. The pool area was spacious and very pretty, but still tended to get extremely crowded on the weekends. Parking is not cheap here, but the valet attendants did an excellent job and made paying the extra $ for valet not quite as painful. The hotel's location is also excellent. You are within walking distance of the Gaslamp District, Petco Park and a very short walk to Seaport Village. We had some problems with housekeeping forgetting to clean our room during the first few days of our stay. This was annoying to have to deal with, especially at a 4 star hotel.
