I shouldn't have to call down to housekeeping everyday to request that my room be cleaned, especially when I wasn't in it all day. After the 4th day, the problem was pretty much ironed out and we had smooth sailing for the rest of our trip. Overall, we had a wonderful stay in San Diego and would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“3.5 star” Have to say there are many good things about the hotel (service, location, cleanliness, price) and I like the intimate boutique feel....really enjoyed that; however, the hotel could use an update...especially to the guestrooms, hallways and gym downstairs....all looked a little tired; however, the front desk did mention something about an upgrade soon. Overall a good choice and would return if the upgrades are made.

“Great deal but without the excellent service of most Starwood hotels” I decided to try out the new Aloft for business travels to Jacksonville. I love the Starwood family of hotels and it's my preference whenever I travel. I got my great corporate rate so it was a good deal...I liked that the hotel was pet friendly with no additional charge, there was in room free bottled water and free wifi. I will say that the service at the front desk was so relaxed that it was truly lacking and not very helpful really (unusual for Starwood no matter what level of hotel you are staying at). The hotel has a great location close to major highway and St John town center for shopping and food. The room was great for the price of the hotel. I really hope their front desk service improves, I don't want to find another hotel in Jax since I will be here 1 wk a month! (also I will acknowledge that other staff was friendly)

“Sì, ok!!” Confermo tutto quanto già letto sulla posizione dell'Hotel, eccezionale: sia per chi ama camminare a piedi (ma scarpinare fino a Lower Manhattan non è proprio una "passeggiata"!), sia per chi si sposta come noi agevolmente coi mezzi (dopo essere "entrati" nelle menti contorte che scrivono e posizionano i cartelli con le indicazioni, la metropolitana vi porta letteralmente ovunque, certo non è viaggiare in limousine, ma volete mettere il risparmio di tempo e denaro, of course?) quasi dimenticavo che l'albergo è a 30 secondi a piedi da Central Park!! Noi avevamo una stanza con vista su Times Square e Carnegie Hall (numero 1806) davvero unica per i neofiti di Manhattan! Io ho prenotato mese e mezzo prima direttamente sul loro sito, e ho risparmiato un bel 30% che su una stanza medio alta è una gran cosa. Vi consiglio di fare lo stesso, e se non ricevete da loro conferma, fargli una telefonatina per assicurarvi che la prenotazione sia a posto. La nota dolente de front-desk infatti è l'estrema scostanza e poca propensione all'ospite. Io parlo inglese perfettamente e hanno avuto da storcere il naso alle minime, necessarie, informazioni richieste. In giro per l'hotel ho notato tanti turisti italiani un pò in difficoltà su questo punto. Per la colazione "alla yankee" CONSIGLIO a due passi su 7th avenue un piccolo posto "la parisienne" gestito da un greco che fa dei breakfast menu eccezionali (quelli con uova bacon etc..) a prezzi davvero stracciati (15 $ in due) SCONSIGLIO assolutamente "Europa Cafè" poco più in su stesso marciapiede, praticamente ultimo block prima di central park, dove per lo stesso prezzo abbiamo avuto due caffè - se si possono chiamare così - e una crostatina che era una più che altro una maiolica, Ladri!) SCONSIGLIO assolutamente BENASH all'angolo pposto dove abbiamo pranzato per la vicinanza all'hotel il giorno della partenza: è un locale di infimo livello con prezzi inversamente proporzionali al suddetto (due burger e un bicchiere d'acqua 37$, evitatelo come la peste!) In definitiva, ci torneremmo senz'altro (anche se temo che il nostro bagno non sia mai stato pulito durante la nostra permanenza di 4 notti...unica nota veramente stonata della stanza)

“I stayed here because of a meeting at the...” I stayed here because of a meeting at the hotel. I am not a fan of historic hotels for several reasons and the Menger is no exception. 1. The room smelled 2. The bathtub and shower looked like the run down tubs I've had in "OMG we have to pull off the road motels" with paintings of Elvis and velveteen bedspreads. 3. The air conditioning in the room did not function properly . 4. The walls were thin. 5. It was spendy. 6. The fitness center had 2 ellipticals, 1 treadmill and a bike and is not open 24 hrs. There were positives: It is a beautiful hotel with a beautiful courtyard. It's right next to the Alamo and a shopping mall. Free Internet in your room.

“Comfortable accommodations, excellent service, great location, price & reliably good breakfast” Last minute booking at the Embassy Suites near the Biltmore Resort, Camelback & 26th St. Near shopping, restaurants, recreation. Less than 15 minutes from the airport. The hotel is one of the larger Embassy suites I have visited. Our room was exactly what we expected from an Embassy Suites. The service was excellent, though we really didn't have any demanding issues. There is plenty of convenient parking, though none in the shade. You can walk to all the shopping and restaurants in the Biltmore Fashion Park. You can also walk to the Biltmore Resort, which we did. The daily breakfast was delicious, especially the omelets, french toast, & pancakes. The hotel was quite busy on Saturday, so much so that they could not keep up with the coffee demand. The bed was a tiny bit saggy & lumpy, but I had no trouble sleeping like a baby. The kids loved the place. The atrium is huge and has a very peaceful pond system full of koi that were so tame an playful they let you pet them. From the fifth floor, they almost looked like dolphins. The pool was large, with lots of lounge chairs, towels, tables & chairs. One night, we were too pooped to go out for dinner and reluctantly ate at the hotel restaurant, which pleasantly surprised us as fantastic! Overall, I would easily stay here again.

“NEVER DISAPPOINTS” This was my third stay at the Affinia Shelburne, and it was every bit as wonderful as the first two. Comfortable rooms, friendly and helpful staff, reasonable prices, what more could you ask? Was it absolutely perfect? Not exactly. The shower drained slowly, and two of the lamps didn't work, but these are minor annoyances, which were promised to be addressed after I reported them at checkout. Do yourself a favor, stay here.

“It has everything” I stayed here in July for some meetings. It is a large resort that has everything from two golf courses, tennis courts, a full spa, and great grounds. My biggest complaint was the lounge area that was too noisy to hold a conversation. There was a combo playing, while good, created an overwhelming din. The room was nice -- nothing spectacular, but comfortable. My other complaint was the very long walk from the parking lot if you did not use the valet parking.

“Seaport Hotel, Boston” Dear Fellow travelers and road warriors, If you're looking for a BEAUTIFUL hotel to stay at in the Seaport district of Boston, this is definitely one of the best places to stay! Reasonably priced compared to other hotels in the areas, this hotel has so much more to offer, like an extravagant breakfast buffet, polite and professional staff - and a great set of quiet, clean rooms with plenty of space to stretch out, work and relax. There's a convenient Starbucks in the main lobby and the restaurant (AURA) is top notch! I'd stay here again in a heartbeat! Way to go, Seaport! A++ all the way!!!

“Great location, nice hotel” Everything I expected. It was a standard, cleaner than average hotel. I stayed on the 27th floor which ended up having great views including downtown, the ocean, and even the golden gate. We didn't really spend much time in our room, but did find the rooms well appointed and very clean. The turndown service at night was nice, especially the chocolates!! Cant comment on room service, in house dining, etc, because we didn't use any of that. You cant beat this location. Convient to loads of shops and restaurants, and only a short cab/cable car/trolley car ride to everything else you might want to see and do. We never had a problem with noise, other than the odd siren (big deal). Yes there are homeless people around the hotel...Any big city with decent weather and lots of tourists has a problem with homeless people. Would recommend this hotel to anyone, especially if you get a good rate!!!

“A clean 2/3 star hotel but a 5 star live on premise married management team” My wife and I decided one day last week to take a 5 day get away to SF. Low plane fare R/t from CVG to SFO $228. Even took my parents on a whim as they have never been to SF before. Got on this site not looking to stay at the Ritz but something that Trip advisor rates high. I have put my trust in this site in the past for various Europe trips and have yet to be disappointed. This hotel is by no means a 4-5 star, but it is a great value for the money. The rooms are very clean, the tub,bath were spotless. Beds have brass head boards and were very comfortable. The managers are a married couple Jay and Hemmy, (I don't think I spelled her name right, so pardon me). They live on premise, and took care of every request we had. You are 15 minutes to outer end of the wharf. Very safe surroundings. Famous Lombard crooked area three blocks from hotel. Parking was free, but we had other transportation most of the time. Isuggest a Limo thru Bauer limo ask for William Bennett driver, for 90.00 pick up from sfo in stretch., There are refrigs and micros in each room, blow dryer, iron coffee maker etc. Look.....you will not find a nicer front desk or clean hotel for this price. It is not a 4/5 star, but for a resonable place to stay ,clean and friendly, this is a great choice. As far as the previous reader being critical on the free breakfast....get over it...the attempt by this managing couple to make your stay pleasant is magnanimous, the light breakfast is another plus if you wish to partake. There are plenty of coffee shops within a 2 block radius . Would recommend this to anyone looking to have a safe clean room with home feel management. If looking for more, I suggest a hotel closer to wharf, but the price will triple.

“SIN LUJOS PERO RECOMENDABLE” he viajado varias veces a nueva york y honestamente recomendaría el hotel pensilvania por su inmejorable ubicación¡¡¡... no es un hotel de lujos pero debe recordar que en nueva york todos los alojamientos son costosos y este resulta realmente bueno en cuanto a su relación precio/ubicación, pues apenas caminando estás cerca de todo, en pleno manhattan... recomiendo reservar por página web las habitaciones del club penn, pues aparentemente son las que están más renovadas y esas son las que yo he reservado, por lo cual debo decir que el servicio de habitación en este particular es bastante bueno... las habitaciones son pequeñas (como es lo común en el estandar de nueva york) pero a mi me resultaron bastante óptimas y buenas en relación con la fantástica ubicación que es inmejorable, además que en nueva york es más el tiempo que se pasa fuera del hotel...

“Lovely hotel and staff BUT too close to hospital emergency room!” The hotel itself was beautiful and wonderful staff but the bottom line for me was that it was impossible to sleep through the night because the noise of the ambulance sirens continued throughout the night. For THREE consecutive nights. There was simply inadequate soundproofing - even 14 floors above the street (OK - 13 floors as there is no 13th floor). I hesitate to write this review but I rely on Trip Advisor reviews when traveling, and had I been warned about the ambulance sirens, I would have chosen to stay elsewhere. If you are a sound sleeper and noise is not an issue then it is a lovely hotel and excellent value. Conveniently located. Wonderful staff. But quiet is a key priority for me so I would not stay here again. :(

“Really wanted to love this place...” This is my third trip to HHC Resort. Loved it on the first trip several years back with kids. It was ok three years ago on a business trip. This time it was a disappointment with the family. Beds were sagging, food was mediocre yet still just as expensive (dinner for 2 with a mid priced bottle of wine and tip was over $150 and my wife and I walked away thinking we could take it or leave it). At 7:30AM it was very loud outside our room with screaming kids climbing a tree (We had kids with us, but they have manners). As beautiful as the property is, it overall has a "down market feel". Pains me to write this review, but this is an honest commentary from a previous fan. We will not be back.

“Nice But Not As Expected” This hotel has potential and it is nice, in a convenient location BUT......it is not as comfortable as one would hope for a boutique hotel. We found good rates on cheaptickets.com and booked through that. Upon 'check in' we were given a room that had windows with a view of the brick wall of the building next door. We called downstairs to ask for a change and were told that a room with a street view would be $20 more per night. That night, we were told a guitarist would be performing so we returned early from dinner. The set up was there but no musician so we thought he/she was on a break. We went up to our room and returned about a 1/2 hour later and still no one performing so I don't know what that was all about. Maybe the person didn't have an audience and ended up drinking at the bar? I recommend this hotel but with reservation. If you are looking for a convenient place to stay downtown- it's fine but skip it if you are planning a special weekend with a loved one. It's modern, small, has amenities but that's about it. Oh...and it costs $18 to park with the privilege of taking you car in and out.

“very modern, new hotel with great location” Stayed here for 5 nights. Had a room 1907 which was a corner room with 2 double beds. There was 2 adults and 1 child in the room. THe beds were very comfortable with luxurious bed linen and a choice of soft or hard pillows. It was a regular size for NYC, the two beds in the room, a desk, a small closet with iron and board. You had to clean up after you as it was easy for the room to seem like it was a tip due to the size. There was a flat screen tv, air conditioning which was lovely as the weather outside was in the 90's. Our room looked south and you could see other buildings. However, some of the rooms did overlook the Empire State building. The hotel is 26th st and 6th ave end. It was 5 mins walk to Penn Station and the nearest subway was 7th ave and 28th st. or broadway and 28th st. There were plenty of deli's nearby so dont worry about the lack of mini bar in the room. There were also ice machines and vending machines on 3 separate floors These had soda, water(2usd) and crisps and sweets. There was also an Olive Garden and McDonalds and Starbucks on 6th Ave. All within 5 mins walk. There was also a nice bar called Rogue where you could sit outside on 6th Ave. This had a nice seating area outside. There was also a bar next door to the hotel that looked nice. The bathroom had a small bath with adequate shower and small sink with hairdryer and basic toiletries. The towels were fluffy and replaced when required. The maids need to look at the rear of the bed though as we found a pair of mans underpants (yes a bit disgusting) and a mens deodrant. I wouldnt let this put you off though as obviously the staff are very new in the hotel. The staff were friendly and they stored our bags for us and sourced us a taxi with enthusiasm. The reception staff were very friendly and welcoming and tried very hard to keep you happy.The reception was small but hey alls its for is passing through. There was a bar next to reception with comfy sofas and bar stools. They were friendly and offered us lunch or evening menu on the night we ate there. The evening menu was a bit expensive but normal for a hotel in NYC. It was 8usd for a large glass of wine. The food was good and kids ate free and got a free soda. Next to this area was the restaurant which was part of the bar area. I gather this is where breakfast was served. I used my hubbys priority points for the trip and it was only 15000 a night this is very good for NYC as normally you would need 25000-40000 per night. There were no safes in the room. However, there were free safety deposit boxes at reception. If you lose the key they charge you 350usd. On the basement level there was a small gym area and a business centre. There were 2 computers with free internet. This closed at midnight. There was also free wifi in the hotel room if you had your laptop. Would I stay here again. It would have to be a yes. I would only pay 250 a night max though as i think there is other NYC hotels that have slightly larger rooms,.

“Old world charm and elegance.” The Sorrento Hotel is just a few short blocks east of Interstate 5 in Seattle's historic First Hill neighborhood. Calling itself the "city's first boutique hotel", the Sorrento opened its doors way back in 1909. Built in the Italian renaissance style, the 7 storey hotel contains 76 deluxe rooms and suites, no two of which are alike. Old world charm and elegance surround you as you enter the front doors and you realize you are in a special hotel. In the guest room, the bedding is superb - like sinking into a cloud. Stylish fixtures complement the extensively marbled bathroom. Amenities are a notch above normal and include a genuine coffee press, Mighty Leaf teas, gilded mirrors, his and hers bathrobes, fine art prints, and for the curious a bound book describing the history of the hotel. Downstairs, the Fireside Room, with its exquisite Honduran mahogany woodwork and irreplacable Rockwood pottery hearth warm the architectural soul while you have a drink and listen to talented jazz duets (with guest vocalists) on weekends if you are lucky enough to find an empty seat. The Hunt Club restaurant next door offers delicious meals with the added perk of a complementary bottle of wine as a guest of the hotel. The Sorrento is extremely good value for the money while providing a romantic getaway from the everyday hustle and bustle.

“Excellent Drury” We've stayed here numerous times and always enjoyed our stay. As mentioned by others, the staff is excellent which I've found typical in the Drury chain across the US. They seem to make a point of selection and training good folks. The hotel has been recently remodeled, so everything seems fresh and new. The grounds are especially nice with a well landscaped pool with separate sitting area with chairs, picnic tables, etc. Very nice on a cool spring day in San Antonio. Rooms are well equipped with micro, fridge, wide screens (suites have two TVs), good bedding and pillows. Breakfast is way above average and well presented, snacks in the evening are worth a look as well. Location is great for the airport, and there are main arteries nearby for quick access to downtown and other areas of the city. Ask for the eSaver rate or managers special to save a few dollars.

“Nice enough place in downtown Indy” I had some meetings in Indy and decided to go up the day before. I used Starpoints to get a free night here. I think the rate was close to $200/night, so I'm glad I got it for free. We drove up from Chicago. Self-parking at the hotel is $12 with validation. The room was pretty nice. Westin beds are always nice, so that was a plus. We got a room with a nice view - part of which was the rooftop swimming pool. Unfortunately, we did not have time to check that out, but it looked very nice. We had dinner in the bar, service was pleasant but a little inept. There was another couple sitting next to us, we were all trying to watch the Bears game on the big flat screen - and the bar had the easy listening music on the sound system cranked way up. I asked the server if he could do something, seeing as how the only customers there (10:30pm on a Sunday) were trying to watch the game. He said he didn't know how. Eventually, a manager came by and turned it down, but by then, we were ready to call it a night. The next morning, the sounds of a jackhammer greeted us. The property used to be a Radisson and I guess they are renovating. Anyway, this would have been a problem if we'd been staying more than one night. My Starwood status got me a late (4PM) checkout, but my meetings went super late and it was closer to 6pm before we got back to check out. I called the hotel around 4:30, once I realized that we wouildn't be back in time and they were quite gracious about the whole thing. I was worried I would get charged for this, but they just waved it off, which was really nice. It's a nice enough place - I'd check on the status of the renovation before staying again, though.

“Nice Hotel” I like the hotel. I typically don't like staying so far south in Chicago, but when you go to Chicago in the summer and you have a budget, you take what you can get. The staff was great. I hate to be picky but I did not care too much for the decor and style of the newly renovated rooms. Despite being far from the downtown action there is still plenty of great places to eat. Hotel is across the street from Grant Park which was nice for getting up in the morning and going for a run.

“My #1 choice for downtown Austin” I typically choose to stay at this hotel 2-3 times a year for business travel. Downtown Austin is a great place to be and the Hampton Inn & Suites put you right near all the action. You can walk to just about anywhere downtown within 5 minutes-6th Street, 4th St. Warehouse district, Town Lake, etc. There are even several restaurants directly across the street. Some of the aspects about this hotel that stand out are they have a complimentary manager's reception every evening (beer, wine & snacks-rare for a Hampton), the rooms are all spacious and in great shape, the front desk staff are always courteous and helpful, and I've never had any sound issues from other rooms. Now, there are a couple things to be aware of-overnight parking is something like $23. Steep! There used to be a self park lot next door that was either free or much cheaper, but there's a new hotel going up on that site, so valet appears to be the only option. Some rooms on the north side of the hotel may be able to hear all the construction noise that's going on, so keep that in mind. Overall though, I've never had a bad experience at this hotel and it will continue to be my choice based on my positive past experiences.

“Problems with the mostly good Marriott” We were very happy with the central location of this hotel and the staff was exceptional. The doorman actually had a copy of the Philly Zagat guide in his back pocket! The restaurants within walking distance are really excellent, as is the wonderful Reading Market. Our room on the 11th floor was comfortable and the bathroom was spacious . The health club had free earphones ( we always forget ours!) and was well run and not crowded - with good machines. The problem came with the group price of the room - $339.00/night. When I called last October I was apparently connected to Central Reservations, when I had intentionally called this property. I noted that we were with a large medical group meeting , named it, and they were somewhat rude about telling me, "All we have are rooms at this price." (The particular group had not noted a special rate in its information. )I was nonplused at the time, but we go to a lot of meetings and sometimes the room prices are just high for the hotel where the meeting is staged. When I finally followed this up on the day we left ( after a week's stay- and checking other hotel prices in town) the desk supervisor told me that the actual group rate was $208! ( Believe me, I felt stupid for not following this up earlier -)Anyway, the very pleasant staff guy told me to call Accounts Receivable last Monday. Those folks sounded reasonable, thought they could fix the problem, but said that they had to "look into it further", Two days later, having no answer, I called back and the staff person told me a bit hautily that I shouldn't expect an answer for "72 hours after a complaint is lodged", Well, as of today it has been five days, and still no response. I honestly can't believe that Marriott won't make good on this - but it certainly does seem that their reservation process is really a mess. (as another TA response stated earlier) So - warning, if you are with a group, make sure you get the particular local hotel reservations office - and pin down the group's rate.....

“Fantastic little hotel in the West Village” A lovely old brownstone with bargain rooms in a terrific location, the Larchmont is a find for the budget-conscious traveler. I stayed in one of the "cozy" rooms - which means it was TINY. About 5' x 10'. However, it had everything I needed for a one-night stay. Bed was comfortable, the little flat-screen TV on the wall was well-placed, I had my own bathrobe and slippers, a sink, a hairdryer and toiletries, a cute little reading lamp by the bed and there were hooks and a luggage rack. There was an extra blanket and pillow. There were two toilets/showers just down the hall, which were perfectly clean. Also, there was a full kitchen on the hall, with a refrigerator and stove and pots and pans, so if you stayed for more than a couple of days, you could cook breakfast or store juice or whatever. The lobby was bright and comfortable with free WiFi and an iBook and printer for use by the guests. Downstairs was kind of a cafe where they served a continental breakfast with coffee, tea, juice and pastries (fresh!) The staff was very friendly and welcoming - the bellhop took me up to my room and showed me how to work the keys. (Place felt very secure - key for the front door, key for the door to your wing, key for your room.) ONLY DOWNSIDE: My room got VERY hot, because it was so small and no way to adjust the heat. It was unseasonably warm for November...however, I managed this by turning on the air conditioner. I am staying here again next month with my daughter in one of the larger rooms and I am very pleased to find a place in NYC with a private room that is this nice for this price. PS: I have to say, I don't know WHAT the reviewed below me ("NoneNamedYet") is on about. Yes, there is a glass window in the lobby for check-in...so what? No different than many guest houses. The rooms are clean and bright (yes, and small) and the furniture is fine - certainly not "like something that was taken in from the street!" If there's "much better that you can get for the same price" I'd like to know about it!

“The Best Hotel for San Diego Comic Con & Convention Center” This is part of a continuing series of my impressions and experiences staying at various hotels and resorts while traveling to attend concerts worldwide. This review is for the San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina - for a stay in July 2012. Property: San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina Location: San Diego, California Address: 333 West Harbor Drive, San Diego, CA 92101 Phone: (888) 236-2427 Website: www.marriott.com/hotels/travel/sandt-san-diego-marriott-marquis-and-marina Room Type/Class: King Date: July 12-15, 2012 Booking Source: Travel Planners for Comic Con Intl' (San Diego Comic Con) Overall Rating: 4.5/5 [Note: Score is totally subjective based on price, location, and comparison to "like" properties within same area and price range] I have been going to Comic Con in San Diego going back to 1987 or so, and the San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina is far and away the best hotel I've stayed at for the event (and this is the second consecutive year with a 4-night stay). It is at an extremely convenient location for Comic Con, and I would imagine any event taking place at the Convention Center. Of all the hotels around the Convention Center, the Marriott is the only one that is adjacent, which makes it very easy to exit the front or back of the hotel to get to the nearby event. Additionally, Comic Con is a huge event (150,000+ attendees), and the Marriott seems to staff appropriately to account for all of the guests and attendees visiting the hotel for related events. With both of my stays in the past two years, I've had the same class of room in the same tower, with partial views of both the ocean and the city from the balcony. Views are spectacular both during the day and at night. The room was very clean and fresh, as has been my experience, and the room was spacious with a separate sitting area with couch and desk area. The hotel offers both wired and wireless Internet. There was no in-room refrigerator, but there was a coffee maker and safe. There are a few different restaurant options within the property, which were quite nice, as well as room service, which was also good. Proximity to the marina is a big plus, as there are other near-by attractions to walk to, as well as downtown shops and restaurants. This doesn't have anything to do with the hotel management, but if you call on or employ a taxi, be sure you have a discussion before using them for their fees. I was with a large group and returning from a local restaurant via taxi van, less than 1 mile away, they wanted to charge us $8 per person (and there were nine of us), which is obviously ridiculous for a five minute taxi ride. Again, nothing to do with the hotel, but just a tip. All in all, the San Diego Marriott Marquis & Marina remains my top choice for any event taking place at the Convention Center. Marriott quality in a great location.

“Cheap overnight hotel to catch your flight” Bottom line: For the money we paid since we only had to stay 8 hours this was acceptable. Any longer stays should look elsewhere. This was the cheapest hotel we could find since we missed our international flight from LAX (yes we gave ourselves 3.5 hours to get to the airport from the valley - it was insane traffic) and had to wait till the next day to catch the next available flight. Since we were spending all of 8 hours in the hotel we just wanted the cheapest thing we could find to crash for the night. If that is also your situation then this place can work. If you are going to spend more time here OR using this as your base hotel for an actual holiday in LA - this is the wrong place for you. There is a free shuttle pick up and drop off to/from LAX. The hotel is old and a bit musty but again for very short stays where you don't want to spend a lot of money is ok. Be sure to ask for a quiet room facing the back so you avoid all the street noise and airport noise. We did so and really didn't hear anything despite the fact that our window in our room really didn't close all the way. Bathroom is adequate as is the room with TV - again for a short stay. Hallways are on the "darkish" side with worn carpet and looking old and tired. In the lobby is a restauarant. If you are too scared or tired to run across busy Century Blvd. to go to the 24 hour Subway for Dinner or don't want McDonald's next door for dinner then the lobby restauarant would be your only other choice. The food & service are so-so - probably rate it a C (don't know if that's the actual food department rating). The folks next to us who ordered the fried chicken seemed happier than we were with our fried rice which was dry and blah. Underground parking is available for a fee.

“Cooles Hotel, aber gerade im Umbau” Ich mag die W Hotels gerne, speziell das Design. Das W in Seattle ist allerdings etwas "altmodischer" und nicht ganz so stylish. Die Lobby ist gerade im Umbau und somit danach wird es sicher wieder sehr attraktiv sein. Habe ein Eckzimmer bekommen im 9.Stock. Konnte die Strasse sehr gut überblicken, aber eben auch recht gut hören.

“Solid Business Traveler's Hotel” One rarely goes wrong with a Four Seasons property and this one is no exception. The rooms are what you would expect from an upscale hotel. They're roomy, clean, well-appointed, and have great beds. The bathrooms are likewise first rate. The last room I was in had a fabulous mirror on the wall. The pool is great although service can be spotty out there. Beware that parking is very expensive here and the same goes for the food and beverage service. But, like I said, this place is designed and built for upscale business travelers.

“Great service and location. Party-time location.” Booked a "premier" room at a reasonable rate and it was very large (albiet layout was a little awkward). Make sure you sign up for free membership rewards program as it gets you free wifi. Service was fantastic (free cookies for the kids sent up after we checked in, free juice/coffee delivered to your room in the morning, nice rollaway bed was already in the room, express check in even though I hadn't requested it, etc.) Outdoor pool area looked very cool with nice lounge chairs. Gym wasn't anything special. As mentioned frequently, parking spaces in garage is very tight for wide cars/trucks. At least rate of $10 was cheap. Location is either a pro or a con. Right across street from EpiCentre. You're right in the middle of all the action. We were there on St. Pat's night and it was party time there (didn't know it was such a big deal in Charlotte). You could hear the thumping music from the outdoor venues, but of course that wasn't the fault of the hotel. If you're a light sleeper, either get a very high floor or look for a hotel farther away from action.

“Pleasantly surprised by the Helix” I stayed at the Helix with 3 colleagues in April 2009. Though we were on business travel, I can imagine that this place would be a fun site for families or couples who are there to enjoy the DC area. I am a former resident of DC so staying in this hotel was a breath of fresh air and you really feel like you are in a neighborhood here. There is a strip of restaurants, a grocery store, a CVS, and a coffee shop all about 1-2 blocks away. Also you have a choice of 2 metro stations to walk to. You will have to taxi or metro to the tourist attractions from the hotel. I stayed in a Deluxe King room which was very spacious and modern. As with the previous poster, I travel frequently for business and was concerned at the beginning that it would be too flashy and hipster for me, but that wasn't the case. The layout was functional and cozy. I can tell that this hotel used to be an apartment building - I think the Deluxe King was probably a "studio" or "junior 1 bedroom". The tv was cool and the decor was nice, too. The bathroom was a little small but I loved the Aveda products. The only things they could improve in the room are: new alarm clocks (too confusing) and in-room coffee makers. Though there's a coffee joint nearby, many people like to get their first taste before setting foot out into the world! We were there for an offsite team building activity and my boss reserved the Helix Suite for herself and for our meeting area. It was awesome. It had so much space, it was like a 1-bedroom apartment! It had totally separate changing area, bedroom, and large closet. Then we used the sitting area with the L-shaped couch for our meeting area. We just ran to the Whole Foods around the corner for breakfast foods and snacks to eat throughout the day. We could fit 6 people in there comfortable on the couch and chairs for the meeting. This is a lower cost alternative for people who are traveling here for business. (They also have small meeting rooms for a fee, but we liked this better.) All in all, great hotel. Good customer service, good location, and nice ambience. I'd recommend this hotel for business or leisure travelers who want a fun change from the run of the mill chains... but don't forget you can get Kimpton points here! That's cool too.

“a bit disappointed” Stayed here one night for business. At $194 I thought I could get unstained sheets/linens, and a spotless bathroom. I didn't. Had a huge corner king room with sofa, and work table. Nice lobby/atrium area. Breakfast buffet seemed pricey, ($17-$19, can't remember) but had huge selection.

“Newly renovated rooms but thin walls!” I have mixed feelings about this Sheraton. On a good note the rooms look brand new, pretty spacious for NYC standards and the common areas of the hotel are well kept. On a not so great note, the hotel is noisy and it has nothing to do with being near Times Square. I was there on a 3 day business trip and the first room they gave me was 2717. I'm a light sleeper so when I got to the room I immediately noticed a " drumming" noise ( perhaps from pipes in the walls) that would happen every 30 seconds. I later found out that my coworker in room 2520 heard the same noise from the walls in her room too, and it never went away. So they put me in room 739 after I complained. No pipe noise but I could hear the neighbors next to me as if they were in my room. The first two nights I got woken up by their screaming baby! Needless to say I'll be looking for another option next time I'm in NYC on business!

“Good hotel with slow elevators” The hotel is clean and nice, with comfortable beds and kind staff. There is no bar, they do not serve any alcohol and the elevators are slow. The neighborhood toward convention center is OK, but in the opposite direction it is a little scary. Well, all said but that on busy hours you may expect some hot water problem. The window blind would not let you have a dark room in the day time. So many cons? well not really, still satisfied for a business trip.

“Dirty, smoky rooms” I booked this hotel because of a convention. The rate was good, but the rooms were very dirty: carpet stains, smoke smell covered up with heavy perfume. I originally had a large corner king room, but asked to move to another room because it smelled so bad I couldn't sleep. Then received a small room right next to the elevators. The smell was a little better in the smaller room, but the carpet was extremely dirty. There was also a party next to me one night, people up until all hours and lots of smoke. Do not stay here if you used to a full service Marriott, you will be disappointed. I had better service and cleaner rooms when I stayed at the Courtyard on 5th Ave. Pros: - Location - Cheap convention room rate Cons: - Sub standards service - Dirty - Extremely slow and cramped elevators

“Great Location” Beautiful hotel located right in the heart of Boston. 5 min walk any direction to sightseeing attractions. It is located opposite a huge busy hospital. we wer on the 3rd floor and were woken a couple of times by the sirens at night. If you stay here ask to be on a higher floor at the back of the hotel as the hospital is at the front end. Bathrooms were large with good pressure in the shower. there is a king size bed which was very comfy. There is a bar fridge in the room but be warned. Don't even think about even lifting an item out of it unless you are going to eat or drink it as it will be charged immediatley to your room. This goes for any item you think you can replace back in there. You will be billed twice for this item. There must be sensors in the fridge itself that registers when an item is removed . The warm choc chip cookie on arriavl is anice touch and tastes great too. If we were to visit Boston again we would probably stay here again but ask for a room at the back of the hotel.

“You will be pleasantly surprised from the moment you walk in the door!” This is a delightful boutique hotel in a great location and a great price. The staff was gracious and we were well taken care of. Upgrade to a suite and you will enjoy the space and the amenities. We will be back for sure!

“A Mixed Bag for Big Bucks” I stayed at the Mayflower for three nights during a business trip at a rate of $286 a night -- a price that the front desk said I was lucky to get because of the group negotiation. By the end of the stay, I wasn't so sure who came out ahead. The hotel was built in 1925 and occupies a terrific location and is often described as an architectural and social landmark. The public spaces are elegant and lovely -- including, for instance, a free-form cherry blossom sculpture during the time I was there -- and they suggest wealth and power. But take the elevators up to the rooms, and you get a different picture. The rooms seem terribly dated, and the bed was overly soft -- an impression confirmed by at least one other colleague attending the same gathering. It was not exactly shabby, but it seemed as if the dust covers had just been pulled off most of the furniture. Internet service was available at a cost of $12.95 a day -- which seemed the only concession to modernity. The in-room coffee was excellent, and the TV had a good range of cable channels. But when I opened the window curtains, the only view was of a neighboring building and the mechanical works of the HVAC system. To make things worse, the bang of the Dumpsters began about 5:30 a.m., which was most disturbing. There was yin and yang: Great Aveda toiletries and a wonderful mezzanine bar that afforded a great view of the lobby area. Yet the drinks seemed watery, and the service was uneven. The food at the hotel, which I experienced three times (a buffet breakfast, a lunch, and a formal dinner) was mediocre, with rubbery Danish at breakfast, an unremarkable chicken breast for lunch, and the exact same menu served that night for dinner. When my wife asked how I liked the dinner, I said, "It was OK, considering they served leftovers." All in all, I kept wondering about where the Mayflower ever got its great reputation and how the heck it could justify charging upwards of $500 a night. Next time, I will look elsewhere.

“Great Service On Such Short Notice” I was not suppose to have stayed in Houston on the night of February 19th. I was suppose to have been onboard the Carnival Ecstasy departing from Galveston, however, due to fog the Port of Galveston was closed. The ship was stuck out in the Gulf and we were stuck without a place to go. Carnival handed out a paper with 3 Hotel names on it, The Hilton was the 2nd one on the list and since all hotels in Galveston were booked we had no choice but to go to Houston. I am so glad I chose the Hilton. I don’t think anyone else could have been as nice as they were! Carnival had put the private cell phone number of the GM on the paper they gave us but she took it very well and just directed us to call the property directly where I was able to get a King size room. The room was very nice and was clean and my granddaughter loved playing in the big tub! I love Hilton properties anyway and will always stay at a Hilton property over any other brand but this was just a bonus for me. The Hotel is very lovely. There is a huge aquarium in the lobby that kept my 4 year old grandchild occupied while I was checking in along with about 50 others from my bus that had brought us to Houston. Our room overlooked the front parking lot and we could see the planes take off the next morning. There was a very nice restaurant onsite that was very gracious about allowing us to go ahead and be seated and order even though they were closing in 5 minutes. I felt so bad to do it but since we were without a car and it was late at night and I had a child to feed, I had to. But I do want to thank the hostess, waitress and cook for allowing this. The next morning the front desk clerk ( a young man) was so nice and sweet. He put up with all us panicky cruise passengers and was awesome about it. I think I owe him a great big thank you as well! There is a very nice business center on site that we could use (allot) to check the various websites to see when our Ship was coming in. I loved it there and if I ever have a cause to stay with the Hilton Hobby Airport location again I will! Thanks again to the poor manager who put up with about 500 cruise passengers calling her cell phone and for giving us a very good rate for such a wonderful property!

“Crowded with Conventions, but otherwise OK” I often stay in Seattle for business and the last time I stayed at this hotel, I found it very good for the price. This time the hotel was more expensive and I found it just average. Here are my thoughts: POSITIVES: - Location: This place has a great location within walking distance of most parts of downtown Seatlle and has many, many shops and restaurants within two blocks. Also very near Pikes Place Market. - Room: I stayed in the brand new Union Tower, on the 23rd floor. The room was very nicely appointed. My room had a king bed, a huge desk, a buffet table under the TV and a cosy chair. It had nice built in storage areas and a built-in closet all made out of rich,and warmly-stained hardwood. It had a 27 inch Plasma TV hung nicely on the wall. The bathroom was very nice, marble floors and countertops, a spacious shower with decent water pressure and a cool, built-in 3-way mirror. - Bed: This is almost always a given in Starwood hotels, but the bed was very luxurious in terms of the linens and the feel of the mattress. NEUTRALS: - Internet in room was $9.95, however, it was for 25 full hours rather than through noon the next day like in most hotels. - The service was simply average. The person at check-in was not particularly friendly, but wasn't rude . . .just doing her job un-enthausiastically. The bathroom in my room didn't have a blowdryer or the assortment of bath products you normal expect when I checked it. However, I called housekeeping and they sent someone immediately and offered to credit me some Starwood points for my inconvienence. But worst of all, they missed a wake-up call to me on the last day of my trip. Fortunately, I had set the alarm in the room as a back-up. - View: The view from my room was of the side of the building accross the street. The way the hotel is angeled the whole side of the hotel that I was staying on has nothing to see out the window. - Lobby: Very large and since I last stayed there they have attempted to make it more cozy. The lobby is oddly layed out and its quite a walk from the hotel elevators in order to exit the lobby. Its also funny that the first time I stayed here I didn't even know that the hotel had a bar in the far end of the lobby because its hidden around a corner. NEGATIVES: - Very Crowded: I stayed for three days and the hotel must have had three or for different conventions going at the same time. This made the hotel lobby, the check-in, check-out line, the elevators and the entry to the hotel SUPER CROWDED, extremely loud and hectic. - Construction: A lot of construction going on in the lobby and in one of the entryways (which was often closed because of the construction) added to the crowdedness and overall hectic feeling of the hotel in general. - Parking: I hate parking at downtown hotels as it is ALWAYS a RIP-OFF. You pull up at the hotel and the take your car at the valet and NEVER TELL YOU how much its going to be to park. I was in a hurry to check-in and forgot to askthe person at the front desk. When I received my bill, I was shocked to find out that parking was $35.00/night. That is absurd in light of the fact that you could park a block away for less than $10/night. I guess I learned a lesson the hard way. SUMMARY: In light of the foregoing, I feel the price ($236/night) was not worth this hotel and $35 was certqain high for parking. Nevertheless, I would stay there again if I could find it for under $150 and I would park in the lot accross the street.

“Last minute find on Hotel Tonight” I booked the Hotel Indigo on a last minute trip to San Antonio. The price was excellent ($57) per night. The hotel was easy to find, right off I10. Easy check-in with a super nice clerk at 1:00am. The room was very clean and full of nice bath amenities. The bed was comfortable and had nice linens. The bathroom had a large, walk-in shower and soft towels. The room itself was very large and comfortable. I only stayed one night, but I would definitely recommend this hotel for an extended stay. I didn't eat or drink anything, but the restaurant and bar area looked very nice.

“Absolutely fantastic” This place was great! We had a huge studio with an upstairs bedroom and 2 bathrooms! It was clean, quiet, and very comfortable. The pillows and linens were superior. They had a complimentary happy hour and dinner meal that was awesome. They had beer by the pitcherful, wine, a full hot bar for both dinner and breakfast. It was awesome. The only bad part was we could not check in early and had to wait until 4:00 which was a bit of a nuisance, but I'd rather wait then have a dirty room so it was worth the wait! I would definitely recommend this place to anyone and will stay again if I should be in that area in need of accommodations.

“Location, Location, Location!” We spent four nights at this lovely hotel, and had a fabulous visit! First off, we were coming into town from a red-eye flight, and they were able to accommodate us at 7:30 in the morning! Yipee! Our two bedroom, two bath suite was lovely, and very comfortable for our party of four. The beds were comfortable, and the extra space in the kitchen, dining and living rooms really came in handy -- as did the three TV's! The location -- right across the street from the beautiful City Hall, was superb. We were able to catch buses and subway within a few steps of the front door. Breakfast was great, and the hotel was located close to good restaurants and the Reading Market -- definitely worth a visit! We definitely recommend this hotel if you are looking for a place to stay in Philadelphia -- you will not be disappointed.

“Nice convention hotel” I stayed here for five days as part of a convention at the WCC. After reading some of the reviews, I was very concerned for my safety since I would be alone a majority of the time. Instead, I felt very safe, especially walking around to the varoius restaurants that are 2-3 blocks away. There were several convention service folks on the corners who were pleasant and very helpful. The Renaissance is a typical corporate hotel. The lobby is huge -- which is perfect being so close to the convention center -- and I had no problems with checking in, even thought it was only 12 noon. They delivered a new mini-refrigerator to my room, free of charge, when I requested it. The bell staff was helpful as well. The king room is a good size, especially being so close to the convention center. I had a view that looked out into the square and to the center itself. I was concerned it was going to be noisy, but the windows and the walls kept the noise to a minimum. The decor seemes to be recently renovated and the bed had the new luxury sheets and bedding. How nice! The desk area was nice as well, with plenty of space to set up my laptop and mini-printer. Plus, it had a 6-socket outlet in the wall which enabled me to plug in my cell phone, etc. The downside was, as usual, having to pay $12/day for internet service. For as much as I was paying per night, I was frustrated (as always) that Marriott insists on charging guests for the Internet. Although I didn't eat at the two restaurants, room service was prompt and good. They were accommodating when I requested to go off menu for a few items. Besides the Starbucks, there is the Liberty Street Market that featured fresh salads, drinks, sandwiches, etc. The only problem is that the hours weren't posted (that I could find) and it seemed to open up at different hours each day and not in the morning! The fitness center is located on the 3rd floor, so it takes a few twists and turns to get there off the elevator. Towels are offered complimentary, the shower facilities are nice, and you're able to get a locker. There is an area for aerobic and yoga classes, a nice weight machine area, and a few treadmills that are lined up along the windows. This felt pretty crowded, like they stuffed a lot of equipment in a small room. However, the machines had TVs like a modern health club, which was very nice. However, the pool is small and enclosed. It is more for laps than recreation. The mezzanine level connects to the K building next door, which has a full-service USPS, several small eateries, and a sundries shop that is cheaper than the hotel. The operating hours are 9 a.m. -5 p.m. Still, it was very nice having a USPS so close. Also close by are a full-service FedEx Kinko's and Capital Business Center for your last minute convention needs, and there are several shops that are in walking distance of the hotel. The business center was hit and miss. Like most hotel business centers, they charge for everything. You use your credit card to activate the services, so you can't bill them to your room. I was there four times, and three of those, a person wasn't behind the desk. I was asked by a hotel guest if I worked there. Finally, my company hosted two events at the hotel -- a business meeting and a symposium. The sales/catering staff were great to work with and very accommodating. Our business meeting was at the last minute and they were able to track down space for us. Instead of the traditional LCD project and tripod screen in the conference room, we had a large, flat screen plasma which worked much better. Our team was very happy even though it the meeting space on the 2nd floor was tricky to get to (similar to the health club) For our symposium, we had a lot of problems with cell phone service in the lower levels of the hotel. The room we were assigned felt like a hike from the main escalators. The service staff had a habit of clanking plates as they cleaned up during the lectures, which drove our audio engineer nuts. However, when our food began running out, the staff was quick to turn out new dishes and alerted me to how long each item would take. They even offered alternatives when they knew they couldn't make more of a particular item. Over all, it is a very nice hotel to stay at. I'm due back in late July for another conference.

“Clean, new hotel with great location” We arrived 2 hours early hoping to just stash our bags, and were pleasantly surprised when told our room was ready. The room itself was comfortable, with an LCD tv, comfy king bed, sofa, coffee maker, but no fridge. The room was moderately sized, bigger than many of the older hotels in SF. The heated indoor pool and jacuzzi were a nice plus. The room rate was very reasonable, but valet parking cost us over 1/3 of what we paid for the room itself. Even so, the combined cost was still a pretty good deal. I would stay here again.

“Service beyond” This hotel has service down pat. There is no detail left untended. Check-in was easy. We were upgraded to a partial ocean view. The room was nice, if a bit small, and the bathroom was luxurious. Housekeeping was great (please tip them). THe food in the restaurant was excellent. THe workout room was very nice with gatorade supplied. The spa area has a steam room and nice showers with all the amenities. I did notice, as did another reviewer, that the lower floor rooms facing the street are a bit noisey. When you leave they give you a bottle of water and directions.. I would definitely stay here again. It is pricey but worth every cent.

“Good location, Hotel is Massively Understaffed” Overall, the hotel has been very nicely re-done and is accross the street from the Ren Cen. The lobby and restaurant are nice looking, and better than one might expect at a Courtyard. While the people are generally nice, there are not enough staff. As such you can expect to wait as a one desk staff member tries to ring people up at the convienience store and people try to check in. Addtionally, the while the rooms look nice, there are a number of mechanical problems like slow drains, mildew on bath and weak air conditioning (despite the fact that it was freezing in the hall). Most surprisingly, my room had no shampoo in it. When I called they brought me handfuls of conditioner and one bottle of shampoo, which apparently was the last in the hotel. Adding more staff would make this a great little place.

“The Best Smelling Hotel in the World” I've wanted to stay at the Gramercy Park Hotel for some time -- in large part because I wanted to go into the private park. We had the opportunity to stay here this week, and when we walked through the front revolving door the first thing that we experienced was a wonderful smell -- apparently their signature candles mixed with the scent of a crackling fire. Our rooms were generous size, but our mahogany paneled bathroom was just too small, even by NYC standards. My sister's room -- adjacent to ours -- had a much larger bathroom. Staff were incredibly friendly, and we had a great (albeit short) stay. And, yes, the doorman walked us across the street and we had an enjoyable Sunday stroll in Gramercy Park. The only part of our stay that was flawed was room service. Why do most hotels seem to ignore the quality and responsiveness of room service -- while charging $25 for a glass of ice tea and a latte? The first ice tea I ordered was so weak it looked more like dirty tap water. The second latte we ordered took almost an hour to arrive (and one follow-up call by me) -- and the frothy milk on top was actually cold. I called this to the attention of hotel management, and the apologies were profuse and the charges removed. But I hope they will be able to improve the quality and responsiveness of room service in the future. We wanted to buy one of their "signature" candles, but they are $150 each. For a candle. It's a shame they don't price them at a more sensible level, and they would then sell more of them. I think these candles would be good ambassadors for the hotel -- friends would ask, "What smells so nice?" And the response -- "The Gramercy Park Hotel."

“Perfect for us!” We like Kimpton Hotels and this one was perfect. Location is fun and convenient to activites and public transportation -- we use buses and subways in NYC. Lovely rooms, polite staff, comfortable lobby.

“A+service! B+Accomodations C+ Room service” The service was outstanding, especially housekeeping. The public interior was vey nice, but rooms were only comparable to a full service Hilton or Marriott. I expected more from a Ritz. I could hear the elevator all night in my room. The room service menu was subpar and very over-priced for what was served (I've stayed in other 5 star hotels with less expensive but great food in room service.)

“My Favorite Hotel in Chicago!” I could literally go on and on about this hotel. The accomodating staff; superior location; comfortable and spacious rooms. A+++. I am from Chicago originally, and come back for business and family visits 2-3X a year. In the past 6 months, I have chosen to stay at the Palomar hotel 3 times because of the exceptional accomodations and GREAT customer service. First, if you want something, anything, JUST ASK. The staff will do everything they can to accomodate you. Your comfort and enjoyment is truly their #1 priority. If only every hotel treated their customers in this manner. I am a Hilton, Marriott and Sheraton Rewards Member. However, when I travel to Chicago, I choose the Palomar and am now a proud Kimpton member! In your room you will find a well stocked mini bar, with some of the best assortment of healthy foods and drinks I have yet to see in my travels. There is a bathrobe, slippers and large umbrella in the closet for guests to use. . . .and/or purchase if so desired. The Sable Restaurant is DELICIOUS! I am a fish eating vegetarian, and there are plenty of options available on the menu to choose from. And guess what? If you are not sure you will like the food/drink. . .the wait staff is so certain you will be satisfied, they offer you the opportunity to try it and if you don't like it, you can choose something else. WOW! What do you have to lose?!?! I did not have to return anything. . . .by the way. The hotel has a great work-out area, and is conveniently located within walking distance of the John Hancock Center and the Art Institute (IF you like a 20-30 minute walk!). We walked EVERYWHERE, including the Shedd Aquarium. And you are one block from the Red Line, which you can take North of the Loop. Many thanks to Mark, who is always SO helpful when we are looking for places to eat. Also, if you do have a car, I recommend parking in the parking Garage on Grand 1 block away. You will save $10! Seriously, look no further! Book this hotel. You won't be sorry!

“too noisy, too small” I stayed at this hotel last weekend. Rooms are tiny and bath rooms are so so. Dinner through room service was always too expensive and was not what I ordered. " whatever & whenever" service was wonderful. My room was on 14th floor but noise from the hallway and from out side the hotel woke me up several times during night and early in the morning. Next night I had to ask for ear plugs which helped.

“Good Value near I-410” Paid $70 E rate plus taxes. It's an older hotel and could do with upgrading. The carpets are getting soiled and the ceramic floors are sticky in the breakfast area because of the juice/pop machines. I had to report to reception that the bathroom smelled a little musty and the hot/cold knob was falling off the faucet. But for what we paid it was fine, with easy access, free parking, breakfast, evening drinks, internet/printer, free long distance calls and not too far from the airport..

“Great location, but service lacking” We stayed one night, Thanksgiving night. I didn't even choose the hotel; I used Priceline and requested a 4-star hotel in the Inner Harbor area. We paid $80 + tax for the one night. We self-parked for $27 a day, and then walked (outdoors, but mostly covered) from the pakring garage to the adjacent hotel. The heat lamps at the porte cochere were a nice touch. The building itself (the exterior) is visually striking, both from the street level as well as from across the harbor. You walk in and see a tall staircase flanked by escalators, also a pleasant sort of sight. The most convenient aspect of its location is that there is a pedestrian bridge from the second floor that goes above Light Street and brings you to the mall at the Inner Harbor. It is wonderfully convenient to not have to try to cross that very very busy street. Check-in was smooth and friendly enough. The room was good enough for someplace for us to sleep for the night. I'm not knocking it, there was nothing bad about it ... it was just an average hotel room. Two double beds, not queen beds ... again, not a complaint, as double beds were what was advertised. One nice touch was a lounging sofa in the corner. I may not be using the correct term ... it had a back on one short side and a partial back on part of one of the long sides. It was comfy to hang out in. An interesting touch is the elevators. All three are glass walled, meaning you have a nice view of the lobby and atrium for the first 3 floors, and then a nice view of the harbor after you rise past the third floor. To get to the 4th floor and beyond (which is where the guest rooms are), you must insert your key card before you can push the button for your floor number. And it works this way for each individual floor. In other words, I entered the elevator, inserted and removed my key card, and then pressed 7. Someone else got on and tried to press 10, but the button would not light; this other person needed to insert and remove his own key card to get the elevator to stop at the 10th floor. I understand the safety feature involved here, but it was also inconvenient at times. A fair trade-off, I suppose. I enjoyed the buffet breakfast at the restaurant. Pretty much standard fare. It wasn't done elegantly and didn't seem "special" in any way, but it was very good. All of the food offerings seemed perfectly prepared and tasty. The tables were not too close together, which made it a comfortable environment. My only actual complaint about the property was the service of the staff. They didn't seem eager to please or eager to help. I had a situation occur at Perks, the small kiosk area on the 2nd floor that sells coffee and pastries and the like. It is an unnecessarily cramped area, given the fact that there is a lot of "dead space" around it. Anyway, it is necessary to squeeze between a structural pole and a low refrigerated display. In doing so, I brushed my leg against the wooden casing and caught a corner, causing a large scratch on my leg that started bleeding; this was through my heavy sweatpants. The staff person expressed some concern when I showed her, and she suggested I inform the manager, but offered no assistance beyond that. I couldn't see any manager around, and I asked again, and she said there should be a manager around some time soon. I was bleeding and wasn't willing to wait. I went down one floor to the front desk and asked if they had any antibiotic ointment/cream and a band-aid or two. I wasn't making a big deal about it, I wasn't asking for any compensation, I was just looking for a way to clean up and prevent infection. I didn't bring those items with me. The woman at the front desk said they had nothing like that and told me I should try to find Security, as they might have a first aid kit. Again, she didn't say anything like, "I'll call someone who can help you with that." She told me I should look for people even though I didn't know what they looked like (i.e., uniforms) or where I might find them. Two employees came up to me a minute later. They went through a desk drawer at a desk across from the front desk; they found a single band-aid but no antibiotic ointment/cream. I asked if they had a first aid kit, and they said no. I then complained for the first time, telling them it was irresponsible to not have a first aid kit available anywhere. They explained they were not Security staff, but had overheard my question of the front desk clerk and were trying to help. One of them said he would find Security for me. That was nice. Unfortunately, he came back a few minutes later with an alcohol pad and a packet of hydrocortisone cream. I thanked him, but explained hydrocortisone cream was not useful in this situation. He said, "Well, that's all they gave me." I then went back to the front desk and before I was able to open my mouth, the same front desk clerk held up a packet of triple antibiotic and asked, "Is this what you were looking for?" I'd originally asked her 10 minutes earlier, and she, apparently, finally understood what I wanted and realized she had it. I thought that entire situation was very poorly handled. But all in all, I'd definitely stay there again, if I was looking simply for a clean place to sleep, which is really all I was looking for for that one night.

“Decent but dated” Attended a conference here recently and overall the property was OK. The rooms are a little dated, like taking a trip back to the late 1990s. Bath faucet dripped constantly, wasting precious water. Two old box-style TVs. Very outdated elevator broke down for a day. Conference rooms and exhibition hall were well-accommodating for the 1,000 attendees. I marked this "wheelchair accessible" but to avoid all the stairways you really have to go out of your way to get to where you want to go.

“Great Location, Great Staff” This is an average looking Courtyard but a terric location near the San Jose Airport and an exceptional staff. I love entering a hotel like this and having the front staff genuinely greet you and glad to see you stay with them. It wasn't scripted. They are a fun group, the lobby is updated with a Bistro (love the Bistro). The manager came to my table to ask about my meal. The market was out of peanut m&m's, but the staff went looking for more and found some for me. The room was really clean, faced the courtyard, and everything worked well. The bed was very comfortable and I got a great night sleep. My only complaint is that the steam iron didn't have the burst of steam feature. We road warriors really like the burst of steam. It's the best way to knock out a wrinkle in your suit. I will stay here again and again.

“Hits and misses” First the good. The location is great, walking distance to the Mall and White House. The room was huge, more like a small apartment. Also, there was a very good Italian restaurant next door, Piatti something. Highly recommended, especially on a warm night. Now the bad. Front desk staff was not especially helpful, bell captain became noticeably cool after receiving only a $5 tip. (?) Also, WiFi was supposed to be included, but it never worked in the room. We were told to try the Lobby, and then told to go in the bar, because it worked better there. This is not acceptable. WiFi is important to us, especially when staying for three days as we did. In any case, the physical surroundings were great, but the staff was not always helpful.

“Great Hotel for a Spring Break Trip with Family” We stayed at the hotel during part of our spring break trip to San Diego. The hotel was nice and had a good location. The rooms were comfortable and clean. The location of the hotel is good. Close to the area attractions as well as dining and shopping. While we were at the hotel, there were several school groups at the hotel as well. It made for a little bit of noise in the evening as the kids were going up and down the halls, but overall the hotel was fairly peaceful. We had two rooms, one with double beds and one with a king bed. The king be room was missing a lamp and an alarm clock when we checked in, but once we told the front desk, the issue was fixed. We did not eat at the hotel, but the restaurant looked nice. We would stay here again in the future.

“must have a car” Drove to this hotel from Chattanooga. Easy to find at I-40 and highway-64 intersection. Convenient to the Galleria shopping center and several restaurants. Nothing to do in the area. To see and tour downtown Memphis and/or Graceland you need a car. A full day can be spent downtown - park and walk or take a City tour. Don't miss a ride on the city trolley - it runs in a circle. Graceland is near the airport and is somewhat down-at-the-heels. If you're an Elvis fan it's worth the trip. The hotel was clean with breakfast included. Plenty of outdoor parking. Staff was helpful.

“Gorgeous setting” Lovely place, surrounded by hills and golf courses. Feels so remote and relaxing. The hotel is first rate. There is a walking trail around the hotel which is awesome. This would make a fantastic venue for a small intimate wedding. Short distance away from the beach and eclectic restaurants.

“So sterile and generic” I stayed one night at this hotel for a business trip. I selected this hotel because of its proximity to a very early meeting that I had the next day. The hotel lobby is dated and had an impersonal feel that is characteristic of other Grand Hyatts. I paid $419 for a king room with a shaft view. That's what I get for using the self-serve check in kiosk! I should have asked to switch but was already late for dinner. Every light in this hotel was a compact fluorescent, which made it appear dim and unattractive. The corridors were very plain and dingy looking as a result. The room itself was roomy for a New York hotel, with two windows, and a regular TV that seemed rather outdated. The decor was very plain, masculine and univiting. There was one giant unadorned wall at the end of the room that really needed some artwork. The worst problem was the compact fluorescent lighting everywhere, including the bathroom. The bed was comfortable enough, and the water pressure in the shower was good. The room service breakfast was good. I had cream of wheat which came with a nice size portion of fresh berries. This place was servicable for one night, but it not at all warm and inviting. There are far better hotels at this price range and I will not be back.

“A Classic Hotel” The Palace Hotel is a gorgeous old hotel in a perfect location of San Francisco. The entrance is off of Market. The Garden Court is breathtaking as you walk in. The Bart station is right outside the door which is very convenient. The rooms are spacious and the bathrooms have been recently updated. The Christmas decorations are just beautiful.

“Would not recommend” Elevators were not all working & you had to wait at least 10 minutes to get anywhere because of this. I took the stairwells as often as possible (to get to the Gold lounge), but we were on the 17th floor. There was only 1 person working front desk on a Sunday during checkout. REALLY. Be careful in the Gold Lounge- we had charges on there that we did not incur. The lobby bar was good & the Pyramid restaurant was good. Showers were good, but other than that room was small & average at best.

“Excellent location, fantastic staff” Location is superb for shopping, food, theatre, Art Institute, and other sights. Staff from the bell-hop to front desk to chambermaid are all excellent, friendly and courteous. All-suite rooms are tiny bit dated, but are clean and well-appointed, and bed comfortable. Noise was not a major issue, heard occassional talking in the corridor, like in every other hotel. Didn't eat at the 676 restaurant as there are many many places stones-throw away for breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack. I've been staying here every yr for the last 4yrs, each time for about one week, and look forwards to next stay.

“For baseball fans and night life seekers.” I stayed here for a week (7 days) on business. I like this hotel and thought is was nice. If you are coming to San Diego for vacation there are a few things you need to know first before choosing the Omni Hotel. I would only recommend this hotel to people visiting the Petco park for a baseball game or, for people looking to nightlife hot spots. Located in the Gas Lamp area of San Diego, the Omni is walking distance to the convention center and harbor. The hotel is actually attached to Petco Park on the 4th floor which is very convenient for fans attending a baseball game. Beware, there is no beach walking distance to this hotel. Pool and gym are very nice. I was impressed with the gym which will have everything you need. The pool area is fancy and has a plenty of space for sunbathing. The restaurant is also on the same floor as the pool so poolside service is great. Order anything from food to drinks poolside with out the long wait. Rooms are very nice and clean. The beds were comfortable and bathroom was very clean. Nice decor and beautiful view of the harbor. Rooms include large desk, reading couch, mini bar, small standing balcony, and 32" tv. Also, beware of the train noise. I didn't have a problem with it, but I heard others complaining of train, traffic, and stadium noise. The restaurant was pretty expensive but had good food. Located next to the pool on the 6th floor. All-in-all I had a nice time here at the Omni. The truth is, It's not for me. I'm not a baseball fan and I don't really go to bars. But if your into those things, it's perfect for you. There are plenty of other things to do in the area but I would prefer to stay in another hotel closer to the beach and shopping.

“Good Location” This hotel is in an ideal location for Seattle offering perfect views. The rooms and service are cookie-cutter Sherarton. The lobby has been redone and is gorgeous. I've stayed at this hotel many times and it's not bad. I guess it just kind of boderlines on borrrrrrrrring. There are certainly no surprises. Also, Sheraton will nickel and dime you for everything (internet, phone, mini-bar, parking, etc) . The rooms are in need of a re-do. The bedding and furnishings are starting to not look fresh. However Seattle has many unique boutique-like hotels that offer a lot more charm and charisma than this place. So check out your options before you settle on a "big box" like this.

“Gutes Hotel in bester Lage” Nach der Renovierung erstrahlt das Hyatt in neuem Glanz. Die Lobby erscheint sehr einladend, ist aber meistens extremst voll und daher etwas ungemütlich. Die Zimmer sind, wie in New York nicht unüblich, sehr klein aber ansprechend eingerichtet. Sauberkeit war in Ordnung, jedoch gibt es Zimmer in Nähe der Eismaschine und des Raumes für Reinigungspersonal was sehr laut ist. Das Personal ist angemessen freundlich. Frühstück á la carte (kein Buffet) ist übersichtlich aber sehr gut. Die Lage direkt an der Grand Central Station und damit mitten in New York / Manhattan ist sehr, sehr gut. In der Umgebung gibt es, wie eigentlich überall in Manhattan, zahlreiche Restaurants, Einkaufsmnöglichkeiten etc. (5th Avenue, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, Bryant Park, Carnegie Hall, Trump Tower zu Fuß schnell erreichbar).

“Great Bed, Too Bad That's About it” This hotel leaves me wondering what business they are in ??? It was apparent to me they are poorly managed. The front desk is actually amazing and clearly places operational convenience over old fashioned good hospitality. We requested consideration for an early arrival when making the reservation, but upon arrival, found no one had even read it. The nice folks behind the desk are friendly..."You guys" check your luggage (Robot Response). "We don't guarantee the room will be ready until 3:00pm". So, we checked our luggage and left to enjoy the city. Arriving back at 3PM, the desk clerk attempted to verify the availability of our assigned room by making calls over a fifties something walkie-talkie. Now we were thinking this looks like a "used car lot." In most hotels this is done out of the site of the guest and much more efficiently. Incidentally, the clerks are not in uniform, open collar shirts looking more like someone you would find in your neighborhood hardware store, not a New York hotel. The clock behind the desk was missing the dials. Then there is the game of who will be offered a glass of champagne or water, but that appeared to be sheer luck, we were not lucky. Now, onto the room a "Superior Plus King” Very spacious two room jr. suite Room 803. The bed is GREAT... LCD's in both the parlor and bedroom and a Bose radio a real plus.... Good recessed lighting. Room appeared to be recently decorated and had some nice features like the milky white glass doors throughout. Pathetic lack of attention to guest conveniences... drawer space, closet space and the worst the bathroom. Although very pleasing to the eye, the bathroom is hardly big enough to breath in. There is no room for even the most modest needs for a guest to shower and dress. My shaving kit had to either placed on the floor or in the nearby bedroom. The rain forest shower head was a welcome find. The carpet is old and worn. The mini bar fridge had no space to keep anything cool. The guest room floor hallway is about half as wide as normally found in hotels leading me to think this building must be an apartment building trying to be a hotel, but failing in most areas. There are nice touches... the complementary new paper in the Sunday New York Times and the coffee/tea station off the lobby. The location is great and an easy walk to Saint Patrick’s, Fifth Avenue Shopping, MoMa, and Rockefeller Center etc. The would be a really great hotel to come to for a one night sleepover after a night at a club or out partying. We are over that phase of life and desire more attention to creature comforts over flash and dash. Just go without expectations and you could possibly enjoy the experience. Good luck.... we may go back if the rate is really great and for one night only. Just one last note, the bellmen can be both good and bad. They can be standing at the hotel front entrance and ignore you, as if you are invisible at times.... and at others, greet and acknowledge you as anyone would display hospitality.
