“Fantastic!” I stayed here with my brother earlier this year. It is a new hotel on the Lower East Side of the city. Great location, close to shopping, multiple food places and Grand Central. Also within walking distance of Broadway and Times Square. Brand new rooms, complete with mini kitchens, full bathrooms, and fabulous views. The bed was very comfortable, and the service was outstanding. I have always been a fan of Hyatt, and they continue to make me a loyal customer.

“good stay - beware of pseudo taxi service” We had a great stay at this hotel in October 2011. LOVED the location. This trip we tried the service where you get an upgrade( you pay for) if one available on arrival. we will never use this again as all around the USA we found we were not offered the upgrade and had more success when we left it to chance and did not agree to pay. Back to the hotel itself it was clean and quiet and staff helpful. we did not use the hotel restaurant. Our order of drinks and cookies prior to arrival was not noted and had not arrived but did once we rang the front desk. On discharge from this hotel we asked for a taxi and the doorman and his 2 mates ( all at front door) called in a car and before we knew it we were put in the car and bags loaded. we then noticed it was not a taxi we asked him to stop and asked what the price would be he said a very inflated price and then dropped it considerably ( more than half) when we asked to get out. we also loudly complained that he was not a registered taxi and he said he worked for the hotel!!! He took us where we wanted to go and was helpful and we eventually got the trip for the same price we paid for taxi when we arrived but I feel this practice is deceptive . it is well and good to use a car service when the customer knows this is happening but we had asked for a taxi. we are 2 middle asked ladies travelling together and certainly for a few moments felt unsafe and taken advantage of. If this is a practice sanctioned by the hotel management it is not acceptable. We would definately stay at this hotel again but will be wiser next time.

“Omni a la Outsource” Hmmm...odd.... Pros: location, location, location (literally across the street from convention center)...main meeting point in lobby & bar for everyone at convention; clean & modern rooms; standard/expected omni expectations fulfilled, i.e., modern, clean rooms, delicious and prompt room service Cons: no spa - they need to "order in" a massage therapist for you (hint....go to lowes spa - it is off the beaten path on coronado so you can get a last minute appointment even during the height of conventions season). Odered room service at 9:15 pm - wanted some hot chocolate with my bagel. The outsourced hot chocolate vendor closed at 9 so no hot chocolate for me. What??!! Odd..strange... still...location and cleanliness outweigh my "cons". i would def stay here again for next convention. Candid traveler photos posted here are completely accurate and not from me. Enjoy!

“Fantastic staff, great hotel!” We stayed in this hotel as we wanted to be close to the centre of Boston, and everything really is just a short walk (Faneuil) or a quick T-ride (Harvard) or taxi away. The hotel is stylishly comfy in the manner of other Kimpton properties we have stayed at. Our double queen room was a little on the small side for a family of four with luggage in accordance for a 3 week trip all over the USA, but it was very comfortable nonetheless, particularly the beds, which were heavenly. If I had to find something negative about the room, it would maybe be that some corners were quite dusty, which is understandable in a room full of furniture ( housekeeping must have trouble moving around with the vaccuum cleaner, I know I would), but not something for 'clean freaks'. Please understand that I am saying 'dusty', and not dirty, as the room was perfectly clean otherwise. To get back to the positives, the staff in this hotel are absolutely fantastic ! Our check-in experience was a delight, were always greeted cheerily when entering or leaving the hotel, and when we got caught in a pre-Irene deluge just before we were due to leave for the airport, all of the staff at the front desk stepped in to literally save our sodden souls from what would have been a very cold, miserable & drenched trip to the airport. They gave us a place to change, plenty of towels, a hair drier and even a bag of sweets for our 7 year-old to cheer her up. We have found Kimpton staff to be very good in the past, but this was just wonderful. Thank you all once again for your friendly professionalism, it is much appreciated, and what makes your hotel stand out.

“Wonderful Stay and Location Great!” Let me start by saying the staff is very “customer friendly”. I was greeted by the door man whom I used many times to get me a cab and told me he had been there for 14 years. The front desk staff was also welcoming. I was at the Intercontinental for 3 days. My room was clean and very comfortable. The location of the hotel is right on the Magnificent Mile across from Nordstrom and a nice upscale Mall. On the corner is a Walgreens for misc item you may need to buy. There are many restaurants on Michigan avenue and right off the main street. Hotel has a Starbuck on one side of the Lobby. There is a business center down the hall in the lobby. The space is owned by FEDEX( I think). There is a cost to use the computers and you will need a credit card. As with most hotels there is a charge for internet service. But if you only need to print a boarding pass there is machine in the main lobby. I would definitely stay here again when I am in the Chicago area.

“Choose for location, not rooms or service” The location of this property is brilliant - not much else is. This hotel is priced like the better hotels in New York (St Regis, etc.) but really cannot compare in terms of the rooms, service or facilities. I recently stayed 2 nights at the Essex House -- I am a Marriott Platinum member -- and I was pretty disappointed on multiple dimensions. First, the internet is extremely slow if available at all. Wifi was not available either in my room or the room of my mother (who stayed at the Essex House at the same time). Second, service is very slow and/or disorganized. i was left on hold on the service line for so long I gave up and went to the front desk. Third, there is essentially no recognition for Marriott elite members --forget about late check out or things like that -- one of the managers told me that the Jumeriah Sirius Gold members (I was one of these) were "pampered" and had "too many privileges" (one of these privileges was 2 pm checkout). The hotel trades on its location and that is just about all that recommends it. If you are looking to pay a lot for a clean room on Central Park, this is your place. If you are looking for anything more, it probably won't happen.

“Great place for combining business with pleasure” I have stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Downtown on several occasions, mostly for business. I have always been impressed with the hotel desk staff, housekeeping, bellman, and valet's friendliness and professionalism- from the moment you pull up to the curb. My most recent stay I was upgraded to a suite because of my HHonors Member status, which was quite a treat. This Hilton Garden seems to be the only Hilton Garden Inn that takes its HHonors members serious with upgrades and free breakfasts, etc. Much appreciated for one who travels a lot for work. The perks are always appreciated. On this visit the GenX Gamers Convention (45,000 people) in Indianapolis had just concluded and the hotel seemed a bit worn and untidy in the halls and elevator. I also noted that at 5:30 AM the coffee was not ready in the lobby on Monday morning for those wanting an early morning cup of joe while reading their USA Today papers. Those would be my suggested improvement comments, but all in all it was-as always a pleasant stay. Hope you keep up with keeping your #1 rating on Tripadvisor.com because Hilton Garden Inn Downtown is a wondeful place for both business and pleasure.

“Perfect location for business downtown.” Stayed one night for business. Quiet rooms ( paperthin walls) and great comfy beds. Connects to the downtown tunnel system or to KBR building via skywalk. Only a couple blocks to the metro train to Reliant Center. Perfect for Texans football or the rodeo. Great value for the price.

“Disappointing given the reviews” I stayed for 3 nights while attending a meeting in DC. The pluses were proximity to the Metro station and free internet access. The minuses: I was given a room off the east promenade of the hotel... which is a bit of a hike from the lobby and confusing to get to...the room was dark and dingy...and it is clear the housekeeping left a lot to be desired. I have asthma and allergies and could see the layer of dust/cobwebs on the wall of the room. If you stay here, be sure to ask for a room in the newer part of the hotel.
“Ottimo” Solito ottimo servizio della catena Hyatt,personale estremamente gentile e capace.La posizione è fantastica.Lo consiglio.

“Reasonable, great location, but stay with caution” Excellent, central location. Walking distance to the Mall. Tons of excellent restaurants nearby. Decent value for the money. Easiest thermostat to use and keep the room comfortable. Now, for the negatives ... rooms show signs of wear, including bathtub and furniture. Towels smell so strongly of bleach, they're almost unusable. Tap water smells strongly of chlorine too. Staff is pleasant, but not sincere. Rooms are dark, because windows are tiny and dirty. Doors slam shut, the bottoms are shaved, so you can see and hear people in the hallway. Water temperature fluctuates while you're in the shower. Shower water pressure low. In room safes are there, but have been sealed shut, unusable. I recommend for short stays, or when the other (better) hotels are unaffordable.

“Excellent Stay-Wonderful Hotel” We stayed over the July 4th weekend for the fireworks, parade and concert on the Parkway. The hotel is located centrally to all Philadelphia's historical and cultural attractions as well as the train and bus lines. You can't ask for a better location. The staff was more than friendly. We arrived at 9am and our room was ready for us! The room was beautiful. Bed was comfortable and I had a great nights sleep. I didn't hear a sound from the hall, other rooms or the street. The room had a refrigerator, large flat screen, coffee maker and was extremely clean upon arrival. They had a very nice pool area with hot tub as well. Bathroom was a nice size and shower was great. I would highly recommend this hotel. I acquired this hotel on Priceline and hope I am lucky enough to get it again.

“Besonders empfehlenswert!” Kurz und bündig: Alles hat gepasst - die Lage zwischen Georgetown, Downtown und Adams Hill lässt alle Viertel und Sehenswürdigkeiten bequem zu Fuß erreichen, es gibt Gratis-WIFI im gesamten Hotel, das Personal ist sehr freundlich und hilfsbereit, die Zimmer sind ruhig, modern ausgestattet und gemütlich, in der Lobby gibt es gratis Café am Morgen, eine Bar, ein Café und ein Restaurant, in dem sich auch Locals bewegen, runden das Angebot ab und ganz in der Nähe fährt auch der Bus nach NYC ab. Das Dupont Circle ist eines der modernsten und angenehmsten Hotels, in denen ich jemals übernachtet habe.

“Great hotel, great location, great staff!” I stayed in a king-bedded suite for 3 nights mid May and have nothing but praise for this place. The room was extremely clean and had all the comforts of home. The staff were very welcoming and helpful. I was concerned at first about getting a shabby room as has been my experience with a couple of other Homewoods, but they have completed their remodel, so there's probably not a bad room in the place. The location is safe and perfect for anything you’d want to do in the downtown area. I’ll definitely stay here on my next trip to Chicago.

“Rooms are tiny, poor service” The hotel is a great location and I was hit on a $140 USD priceline bid so I don't feel so bad. But the rooms are tiny compared to The Palace, Intercon Barclay, or even the Downtown Marriott. They "upgraded" me to a handicap room which is supposed to be bigger but the room was still tiny and the bathroom was a huge disappointment. No tub and the shower looked like something out of my high school football locker room. When I arrived after a 16 hour flight from HK the doormen just staired as I struggled to bring in my 60 pound dive bag and my carry on. I think they were too busy trying to look cool in front of the Whiskey Bar, I'm not too sure?! For $140 usd this place is fine but you can stay at much, much better!

“Very Pleasant Stay, Would Only Change 3 Things” To start, I very much enjoyed staying in this hotel; I travel to NY frequently and have stayed at many properties from Chelsea to midtown, and this was one of my favorites. Our room was quiet, spotless, and the service was excellent. The beds were VERY comfortable, and the bathroom/shower were wonderful, very spa like. Also, there is a Keurig in the room for coffee, and a 37" wall mounted HD tv. Lastly, the rooftop bar was a beautiful space, enclosed with lots of seating and amagnificent view. Everyone we encountered was friendly and helpful; I would absolutely stay here again. However, there are 3 minor issues that some travelers may find fault with: (1) no fridge in the room; (2) no ice machienes (you call room service to have it delivered); and (3) very limited selection of tv channels. These are very minor inconvienences when compared to the positive aspects of the hotel; however, they may matter to some. Other items worth mentioning about the area; Chelsea is wonderful and only a 5 minute subway ride on the 1 train to all major attractions (subway one block away on 27th St). Also, if you stay, do not miss the following eateries: 1. Brooklyn Bagels on 8th Avenue between 26th and 25th (best NY bagels you'll find) 2. Two Bros Pizza on 6th Ave and 25th st (Excellent pizza for $1 per slice, open 24 hours) 3. The Doughnut Plant on 23rd between 7th and 8th, next to Hotel Chelsea. Quite possibly the best doughnut ever. Try the yeast donuts. Amazing. All in all, I would gladly return to this hotel: clean, quiet and comfortable, all in a great neighboorhood.

“Great location - room a little "worn"” This hotel has a wonderful locaion - overlooking Lake Michigan and Navy Pier! Our room hada city view, which was very nice as we were on the 30th floor. I imagine the lake view would have been amazing! The room was very clean and modern. The bed was comfortable, although the pillows were too soft for my taste. Although the room was nice, there were a lot of nicks and scratches on the furniture. Not a big deal, but I would have been disappointed if we had paid full price (we used Hotwire). I was also disappointed that there was not a coffee maker in the room. Overall, it was a good experience. Service was good and we would love to come back in the summer when we could enjoy the views from out doors

“Just a Bad Stay” We were attending a function during the week and our main objective was to find a hotel that was near Penn Station to catch a 6:00am train home the next morning. The location of the Doubletree was only a few blocks from Penn Station and seemed like a good fit. I can't even begin with the list of things that were not up to the Doubletree standard. First although the location is near Penn Station, it's on a dowdy side street that mostly has business that are out of business. It's a very depressing street. When we arrived the lobby was a nightmare. It was tiny and jammed with people. The front desk is just a podium for two people. There were no lines just clusters of people all fighting and arguing who was next. Each person seemed to have a problem that needed fixing now. It was chaos and bedlam. There was a woman sprawled out on the lobby couch sound asleep. When we got our turn we too had a problem. Originally I had booked one king room, however later it was determined that our daughter would join us and we required a room for three people. I called the hotel direct. I was told they did not have rollaways at this hotel, but we settled on a double (two beds). Somehow the day before we left I pulled the reservation and called a second time to check on the correct bedding (as I never received a second confirmation. They did not have me in a double room - still a king. So again I asked for a double room and they said it was taken care of. Well of course we get to the hotel and I still have a king bed for three people! The woman at the desk made it into a huge deal. She blamed me for calling reservations and not the hotel (I DID call the hotel direct), she said I called the wrong Doubletree (so how did they pull my reservation each time), she accused me of lying that I never called. Well finally it turned out they did still double rooms open - so why instead of all the hassle and words with us did she just not change it to a double room. I think she was mad at us as she made sure we didn't get the Doubletree cookies at check-in. She was short tempered and rude. When we got to the room it was tiny - postage stamp tiny. The room just fit two bed and no space to unpack or move around. When we took out the ironing board to iron our clothing the other people had to sit on the beds as there was no other room. Our view was of a building across the street and two massive water towers. The room stunk of old cigarette and cigar smoke. When we left for the function we could not get a cab as it was raining and no cabs come down this depressing side street. Nobody at the hotel was willing to get us a cab. We had to go back to our room and arrange a private car pick up. The staff was amazingly unhelpful. The hotel was just shabby, small, poorly run and the staff rude. There was a aura of things going wrong as most guests in the lobby were complaining about something. The worst part was that the room was $350.00 per night. I could have gotten a much nicer hotel a bit farther from Penn Station for around $199.00. We paid about $150.00 per night to stay in one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in!

“Location could be better, but it wasn't really that big of an issue” My girlfriend and I stayed here for the week in Boston because she was here for work. After reading some of the reviews I was pretty convinced that the location is the main issue of the hotel. However, after looking at the options to get into Boston, we didn't really find the location to be that big of an issue at all, and our overall stay at the hotel was quite good. We didn't get the city view side of the hotel in our room, but the only time we really looked outside was in the morning to see if we needed an umbrella or not. Commuting wise it cost about 20 dollars to get into Boston, and about 15 dollars to come back. Another option we had was the water taxi which was 17 dollars for a round trip or 10 dollars for a one way. However, the best option we found was taking the Airport shuttle to the Subway, and buying a weekly pass for $15 dollars. I found that going into Downtown Boston took a mere 20 minutes including the wait for the Airport Shuttle. Considering I only had to tip the shuttle driver, I spent very little to get to Downtown for the week. Once I got into Downtown Boston, everywhere was walkable, and the transit maps were very easy to navigate. I ended up spending the whole week commuting around Boston this way, and I didn't feel like I lost any precious time seeing the city because of it, while saving money in the process. As for the rooms, we got a King size bed with all the amenities. The towels were replaced daily, the beds were made daily, everything I expected a hotel to do for a customer it did. The bellmen gave prompt service and the front end counter staff was more than helpful in all my requests. I asked them what I could do to print some emails off my Blackberry, and they just told me to email them and they will gladly print it for me free of charge, rather than having to pay for the business center to do it. Although in regards to value I don't know how that fares. The rooms were about $200 a night at the Hyatt, but factoring in the location of the hotel, I would be interested to know how much it would cost to stay in for example Downtown Boston to know if the value was any good. But from speaking to the event planners who hosted the event at the Hyatt, they mentioned they saved much more money having it at the Harborside than at a hotel in Downtown Boston, and attendees were given additional discounts to the water taxi which was an added bonus. Either way, our stay at the Hyatt Harborside was very enjoyable and other than not being able to step out the front door to see Downtown Boston, there were absolutely no issues with this hotel whatsoever.

“Alte Dame ohne Falten” Vielfach sind die "grossen, alten" Hotels mit Geschichte in New York etwas runtergekommen. So auch Plaza, Waldorf Astoria und co - nicht so das Palace. Es strahlt nun seit Jahren den Glanz und Luxus aus, denn man als Besucher von Midtown doch vielerorts vermisst. Ob Frühstück in der Lobby oder Lunch im Restauarant, alles top - wenngleich nicht billig. Sehr zu empfehlen sind die Eckzimmer oder die Speziellen Rooms im "Tower" mit wunderbarem 24h service und Snacks. Auch das Personal ist sehr aufgeschlossen und Features wie der "Mailing Service" funktionieren wie es sich für eines der besten Stadthotels weltweit gehört. Weiter so!

“Great price, but aerage hotel” First the best part--the doormen and the rest of the staff was great. Helpful, bright and funny. We were on the 17th floor, but unfortunately looked out on a light well, so no view. The room was comfortable enough, especially the bed, but the furniture looked like my grandmother's, and there was nowhere to sit other than the desk chair and the bed. It's nice to have an extra chair. The kitchen seemed fine, though we didn't use it. The bathroom was OK, though the shower was kind of wimpy. The buffet breakfast was lousy. Cold sausages, and tasteless eggs and French toast. We went elsewhere the next morning for breakfast, and found a nearby diner that was great. Location fine for walking to Grand Central and other Murray Hill attractions, but it's not our favorite neighborhood. The hotel was chosen for us due to its proximity to a work event. We'd probably stay at a different Affinia hotel (Affinia 50?) next time.

“Gute Lage, die Zimmer sind nicht gut” Dieses Hotel liegt zentral an einem sehr schönen Boulevard unmittelbar an Austins Wasserader und einer sehr großen Brücke über selbige. Abends schwärmen hier bei guten Wetter tausende von Fledermäusen aus, und dieses Ereignis ist für viele Touristen und Einheimische etwas ausergewöhnliches. Ich selbst ziehe da die ebenfalls sehr nahe gelegene Restaurant- und Barszene Austins vor. Das Hotel verfügt über einen schönen Pool, leider ohne Duschen, Umkleidemöglichkeiten. Also muss man einen (kostenlosen) Bademantel an der Rezeption ausleihen, was lange dauert. Die Zimmer sind sehr altbacken eingereichtet und entsprechen unterem Standard, es gibt allerdings einen Kühlschrank und das Bett ist sehr bequem, schöner Blick von nahezu allen Zimmern, die Zimmer in den oberen Etagen sind zu bevorzugen. Der Starbucks-Coffee-Shop ist sehr teuer aber. Das Essen im zum Hotel gehörigen TGI-Fridays sieht nicht gerade lecker aus - lieber in ein Restaurant außerhalb gehen.

“Tolles Hotel mitten in Boston” Das Sheraton Boston ist wie wahrscheinlich fast jedes andere Hotel der grossen Gruppen nichts Überraschendes. Gross, viele Zimmer, viele Leute, ziemlich unpersönlich, etc. Nichtsdestotrotz hat es uns dort super gefallen! Die Lage mitten in Boston ist perfekt. Waterfront, Esplanade, Charles River, Fenway Park, Boston Common, Newbury Street, etc - alles in Fussdistanz zu erreichen! Vom Zimmer aus hatten wir einen super Überblick über die Stadt. Die Ausstattung war grosszügig, modern und sauber. In der Lobby hat es neben Gratis-Internet auch noch einen Starbucks. In unmittelbarer Nähe befindet sich grosse Shoppingzentren (Copley und Prudential Center). Zum Newbury-Street-Shopping sind es zwei Blocks. Man ist in Boston nicht auf einen Mietwagen angewiesen, alles gut und üerbsichtlich mit offentlichem Verkehr erschlossen. Sollte man trotzdem einen Mietwagen dabei haben, ist das Parking (wie überall in dieser Stadt) extrem teuer. Taxis von/zum Flughafen kosten ca $25, Dauer 15min. Würde bei meinem nächsten Besuch sofort wieder in dieses Hotel gehen!

“Good location and upmarket changin facilities” We booked this hotel through Virgin Holidays but as a member of the hotel’s loyalty scheme I contacted the hotel with our preferences before checking in. We had spent the previous night at the Hyatt across the road as due to flight cancellations by Virgin we arrived in Chicago a day early, but couldn’t get an extra night at the Sheraton. We strolled across the river to see if we could leave our bags at the hotel before checking in that afternoon and they checked us in there and then (08:15), with a king bedded room overlooking the river, though on the 8th floor (Room 855) but not a high floor as we had hoped. But we were pleased that we could get into our room and went straight back to get our cases and settle ourselves in for 4 nights. The room was reasonably sized as we were on the corner and so had a bit more room than in the hotel’s website pictures. There was a small safe but it was only big enough to store a small travel wallet, and couldn’t store valuables such as cameras. There was also a key that you had to carry around with you rather than a combination. The room should have been relatively quiet but there was some noise from the road across the river as well as a small amount of river traffic. It was also in an alcove at the end of the corridor but unfortunately for us we had some inconsiderate neighbours who despite them putting a sign out asking for quiet didn’t reciprocate this as they came and went at all hours slamming doors etc. We did use the pool and were quite impressed by the size for a city hotel. The changing facilities were probably some of the best that we have experienced. There is a business centre here but we struggled to find it open – I must admit we were there the labor day weekend but never got a chance to use it. There was no wifi access in the hotel and so we went to Dominicks (with a Starbucks) just over the road to pick up our emails. We were a little surprised that there was a charge for the use of the business centre on check-out but this was promptly removed from our bill when we explained that we had not used the business centre.

“Inexpensive comfortable airport hotel” Stayed at the Quality Inn because I needed to put my wife on a flight out the next morning. It has everything you can want in an airport hotel, courteous staff, large rooms, nice beds, and of course the airport shuttle. The location of the hotel is great for the airport but it is close to nothing else. For a budget hotel this Quality Inn was much better than average in terms of amenities and the all important bed and linens. The halls and carpets are a little shabby but I guess that is why it is not $200 a night. I will be back.

“Nice Hotel , Perfect location” location is perfect just near the white house and the tour bus stop. the rooms are nice , bathrooms are clean , the executive lounge is small but good. it also has starbuks coffee machine. I would stay here again if I visit washington in the future.

“Horrible location. Clean, nice rooms. Helpful staff.” The staff was super helpful and the room was very clean and spacious, especially for NYC. The room was very pretty and the bed was huge. With all the scare about bedbugs, we inspected and all was very clean. The hotel doesn't have much of a lobby and seemed short-staffed at times at the front desk, but everyone was nice and things didn't take too long. The problem? The neighborhood was not very nice. Times Square is in the hotel name but technically, it's closer to the Port Authority bus terminal. That's the subway stop closest to the hotel. Not a great location.

“Great Location - close to convention center and shopping” In the hustle and bustle of the city this is a nice Marriott. Location is great except for all the homeless people... but they are on alot of street corners in San Francisco. Only problem was the breakfast buffet was outrageously priced. $50+ for two people. Better to eat around the corner at the diner. Great gym. individual tvs and alot of machines. Very clean, except for the mats to do ab work.... they have definitely seen better days!

“Poor Service” We stayed at this hotel due to a business conference. After the driver dropped me off at the hotel, I found a multitude of steps to go up with a suitcase and a rolling lap top bag. I prepared some tip money as I could see about four or five gentlemen standing at the top of the steps. No one approached me so I started my trek up the stairs. Still no one even offered any help. Half way up I stopped with a huge sigh like WTF...then finally one of the men standing there doing nothing but watching me made a move figuring I was not going to take this unprofessional laziness very lightly. He helped me inside the doors but that was about it. What do these guys do, just wait to retrieve cars which throughout the week I saw very little of that as most people were there for business. The rooms are ok, standard Hilton and a few of the waitresses were very nice. My biggest complaint was in this economy why employee people who don't want to be a good reflection of the hotel in whatever position they are hired to do. Mr. Manager my arrive date was 6/20 around 8pm.

“Soothing business hotel” I last stayed at this hotel when it was a Park Hyatt. I remembered that the stress of even the most hectic business trip melted away once I entered the Asian-theme lobby. Even though this was a vacation trip, I decided to go back to see whether the magic had survived the change in management, and I can report that it has. The soothing lobby decor remains (though what's with the disorienting art installation that extends to the panels of the revolving doors?). The staff was extremely pleasant and helpful. The business center hidden behind the concierge desk was well-equipped and quiet. Our room -- with a partial view of the Bay -- was on the small side, but it was extremely comfortable and noise free. Only flaw -- particularly jarring in the otherwise well-tended setting -- was a light that didn't work. And the location can't be beat. Easy to take a quick stroll along the waterfront to calm jet-lagged nerves, and just a stone's throw from the food paradise that is the Ferry Building. It's a business hotel, but a very soothing one.

“Too Many Flaws” Hotel smelled of too much carpet fresh. We were given a renovated room; they should fire the designer and the decorator. Not enough lighting in the room, odd angles and wasted space in the foyer area. Small bathroom with shower only, no tub. Terrible position of TV in bathroom mirror; blocked grooming visibility. I have no plans to ever stay at this hotel again.

“Oh, well..” Expect slightly below average Marriott experience. Property looks new and clean, but maintenance seems a bit sloppy - to be honest, I have a hard time understanding why they would let the painting in the bathroom look so bad. Comfortable bed. No mini-bar service. Even though reception was able to accommodate me earlier, check-in at 4PM and check-out at 11AM is definitely a minus. The placard on the unavailability of public bathrooms that they've placed on the sidewalk is a bit too cheap.

“Historic Charm With Little Comfort” I recently stayed at the Menger for 4 nights. I was there on business and was definitely disappointed. While the lobby and surrounding areas have historic charm and were well kept the same could not be said for the guest rooms. I was on the renovated or "new" side of the hotel and was therefore able to control the tempature in my room. However, the beds were extremely hard (I actually enjoy a firm mattress but this bed was uncomfortable); the shower did not drain properly (I would have water up to my ankles by the time I was done with my shower); you could easily hear what was going on in the room next to you; and the rooms generally weren't set up for the business traveler. There was also a musty or "old" smell in many of the rooms. The fitness room was also extremely limited (the machines are old and a few were out of order). While in a great location, I can't say that I would recommend this hotel.

“Beautiful hotel” This is a beautiful hotel! Very clean and modern, certainly not the cookiecutter Sheraton I was expecting. Warm and prompt service, even in the midst of a big convention. Great location - near shops, restaurants, and the light rail system.

“Take Your Chances...” This hotel apparantly has a consistent problem w/ broken elevators and such was the case when we checked in on Dec. 26th. On the PLUS side it's got a trendy looking lobby. The room was fine. Don't ask me why but, in public spaces, there was debris left all over the place. It looks like they may be installing new T.V. wall-stands in some of the rooms and boxes of bolts and empty boxes are scattered about the elevators. I'm usually not too picky but that struck me as being really unprofessional. Especially since no-one ever cleaned it up. Breakfast is standard fare. Get there early, as it tends to crowd up. Note: Very friendly people working the breakfast area. Also, the valet parking people were both friendly and professional. I should point out that management allowed us to check out of our room and yet keep our car parked her until we left D.C. later in the evening @ no extra cost. That was very nice of them. Location is quite good for walking to the Washington Mall. Chinatown is only 1 block away.

“There Are Much Better Hotels to Choose in Downtown D.C.” As an SPG member, I stay at lots of Sheratons and Westins, but rarely Four Points. This hotel reminds me why. It is in a very good location in D.C., and only a few blocks from the Metro. The lobby is pleasant, check in was smooth, the corridors were newly carpeted and furnished since I have stayed here a few years ago. The room was of average size. The A/C did not work well, although the room was otherwise quiet. There is an unattractive pool in the building. This hotel deservs its lower end rating. For the price, I recommend staying at the Capitol Hilton or Courtyard Marriott. I am going back to D.C. next week and will stay, as a lower SPG member, at the Westin Downtown D.C. for only a few dollars more.

“LOVED the rooftop pool” I'll admit - the rooftop pool got us hooked! We've stayed here a previous time for a downtown race and stayed again b/c of the pool. it's awesome! A little pricey and a bit loud if you stay on the same floor as a group of high schoolers, but fun nonetheless!

“Good hotel!” We stayed at The Lancaster Hotel in July 2007 as it was very close to Jones Hall theatre. The rooms only had King beds and a sofa. We had to get a rollaway in as well as there were 4 of us in the room. Check in was interesting - I had requested for a Non-smoking room and they told me they upgraded me to the 9th floor and when we got there, it was a smoking room. Yikes! Down again I went to change the room back to what I had originally. All I want is a non-smoking room and enough room to sleep in. Very basic tolietries in the bathroom, the rooms were clean enough but could be cleaner. Had to valet the car and that was expensive! Didn't know Houston well enough to find the public parking. The restaurant was pretty good. We had breakfast there. Service was impeccable. All in all, it was an OK hotel to stay at.

“Nice hotel.” The Loews Philadelphia was a nice hotel, conveniently located, and the hotel staff was exceptionally friendly. We had a superiour room that was comfortable and clean. The bath towels were big and soft. We were traveling with our 3 year old son, so I chose this hotel based on the "family friendly" reviews I read. Although the hotel was nice, we didn't see any specific kid-friendly benefits. My son received a small pack of crayons and mini coloring book at check-in, which he liked, but I read on another website that a toy was issued at check-in. I even called the hotel to confirm and was told they give an age appropriate gift at check-in. My son didn't notice, and it wouldn't prevent us from staying at the Loews again, I was just a little disappointed. We didn't try the hotel restaurant, but we walked over to the Reading Terminal Market for a wonderful breakfast at the Down Home Diner. We also walked a few blocks to Franklin Square, which was a nice park with an outdoor carousel, miniature golf, playground and Square Burger with delicious burgers and fries.

“Not a CLEAN hotel” This was my first trip to Washington DC for a family conference. I had my husband and two children along. The hotel did not have the correct room based on my resveration available when we checked in so they agreed to upgrade us to a nice suite at no additional charge. Great, I thought. My biggest complaint about this hotel was the FILTHY dirty carpets. My daughter walked around in her socks the first evening for only a few hours and the bottom of her socks were black. Yuck! The walls are paper thin. We could hear the man next door using profanity, very clearly. Not good for the children and then that night we could hear him snoring. We also heard very loud animal noises right outside our window in the middle of the night. We were on the sixth floor. We think it was birds but I never saw anything. I would hate to think it was rodents. The first night it got cold and the heater would never come on in the room. The next morning I called for them to check the heater and no one ever came. That night when we returned to the room I found that still no one had checked on the heater. They finally sent maintenance up at 11:00pm after my children were asleep and the man said he could fix one unit for the bedroom but the other unit for the living area was broken. The next morning it took forever for room service and then the order was wrong. The common areas, elevators and halls are very worn and our room had a hole in the wall by the door. Overall, the hotel was awful and we would not return. I couldn't wait to check out!

“An Oasis” Fells Point can be kind of rowdy and very party like. Once you walk into the Admiral Fell Inn, you leave it all behind you. The staff is very efficient and are very willing to share their knowledge of the area and the Inn. The twisting hallways were a great fun surprise, and the king size bed was just wonderful. The room was kind of small, but you're in Fells Point, you're not going to spend copious amounts of time in your room. If you're on the street side, you'll get some street noise, but it's not really a big deal. You can walk to everything you need, so park the car for the weekend and do a little research. I can't say enough positive things about this place! We booked another stay as we checked out!

“Surly staff, dirty carpets, loud patrons, and not enough cribs....” We recently stayed here with our three young children. Before we arrived, we called up to get two cribs put in our room. We were told that wouldn't be a problem. So, we left South Florida without a Pack-and-Play. When we arrived, I asked if they had put the cribs in our room. The surly front-desk worker told me no and he went to the back to get me the cribs. He came back with only one and told me that was all they have. He said we could check back the next day for more. So, my poor infant had to sleep on the floor (she would have rolled off the bed) while my six-month old slept in the only crib. The next day, we again asked for an additional crib. An even more surly front-desk person told us that the hotel only had one other crib (only 2 cribs for a 200+ room hotel????!) and that it was taken for the rest of the weekend. When we told the front desk person that we were promised cribs and we would have brought our own had we only known, she became defensive and natsy. Oh well. Still, the worst part of the stay was the dirty carpets. After the first night, we were putting our kids to bed when we noticed their little feet were black from the dirty carpet. During the rest of the stay, we kept socks on them while in the room -- each night the socks were filthy. To make matters worse, the hotel had a large wedding on one night. Drunken patrons were singing and yelling in the halls most of the evening. This simply wasn't a good hotel.

“Great Chicago hotel” We stayed 2 nights in July 2012. There is a large area in front of the main lobby into which you can pull your car to unload luggage. The lobby is lovely, and the check in process was very smooth. The workers all seemed very excited about making our experience pleasant. Our room was on the 29th floor with a partial view of the river and the lake. The room was very big for downtown Chicago. The price we paid was excellent. The location is very good, right between the river and Millenium Park between Michigan and Columbus. There is a bus stop literally right in front of the hotel with a bus (#6) that takes you quickly to State street and any L train you need, or down to the Museum of Science and Industry, if that's what you want to do. I wasn't willing to pay $52 per night to park, although this is a typical price for a downtown hotel. We parked using Spothero (google it) for a grand total of $37 for the entire 2-night stay. It was worth the $67 dollar savings to walk half a mile at check in and check out. Our room was very comfortable, with nice beds, plenty of space, and even toothpaste provided. Plenty of elevators. We really enjoyed our stay here.

“Appreciated the modern amenities” I was actually pleasantly surprised by this hotel. One of my traveling companions is a real Kimpton 'afficionado" and insisted that during our stay in Chicago we stay at Kimpton Hotels. His favorite, the Hotel Monaco was prohibitively expensive for the first leg of our trip so we decided on the Allegro which was new to all of us. I arrived a day ahead of my traveling friends and checked into a room that was more spacious than I expected after reading these reviews. I mean it wasn't the Taj Mahal, but it was easy to move around for the most part, and the furniture was well placed. The check in clerk kindly let me know that there were two closets and the one with the hangers in it was behind a door that looked like a connecting room. With that advice, no closet problems. The bathroom is indeed pintsized, but that is mitigated by nice Aveda products, a good shower fixture with good pressure, and a cute little modern sink area. The bed was comfortable. My clock radio was an IPod dock which I really appreciate when traveling to recharge mine, and the desk provided a good and needed work space as I brought some office work to get done while waiting for my friends to arrive. The desk also had an outlet carousel which I appreciated for my laptop and phone charging. I joined the Kimpton "In Touch" loyalty program to gain free wireless internet access. Even the application process is kind of fun as you answer questions about your preferences and priorities when traveling. I didn't have much of a view-being surrounded on all sides by other tall office buildings, but it wasn't unpleasant. The decor was nice and modern. It was a comfortable place to sleep, work and relax between excursions. Even the minibar had a good wine to enjoy before bed. The hotel bar was very nice, the food and drinks good, reasonably priced and served by friendly professionals. Employees were courteous and helpful. Although it isn't in the center of the touristy part of the city, we found restaurants, bars, a breakfast cafe, shops and Starbucks within a few blocks' walk. They also have a wine hour in the late afternoon which is a nice touch. It is the opposite of the "old money" feel of the established, larger hotels such as the Intercontinental, Fairmont, etc, nor is it a cookie cutter business traveler's hotel. It seems designed for a younger clientele. I'm no spring chicken, but I felt very comfortable there. All my needs were met, and so for the price, it was a good choice for me. Although I didn't bring a pet along, I saw some pretty cute little doggie guests in the elevators. I'd recommend this hotel to my younger friends in particular.

“Hit and miss on this one.” This hotel is a curious mix of good/not so good. The location at first glance is horrible: situated right next to I-35 and a bevy of run-down and abandoned buildings, with homeless and down-and-outers roaming the area at all hours. However, the fabulous 6th Street entertainment district and warehouse entertainment district are an easy healthy walk westward. I had no intentions of venturing eastward into "no man's land". Once west of the hotel I felt very safe at all times. As for the hotel itself: what is with the miniscule pool with freezing water in 95 degree weather? There was a tiny walking area around the pool with no lounge chairs (only upright chairs), but there was a very attractive waterfall spilling that Arctic-like water into the pool. The driveway entrance was strewn with trash and at times empty of attendants (at other times there was attendant "overkill"). The interior of the hotel was clean and recently updated; I say updated because there seemed to be more "cosmetization" done than renovation. As far as the room goes, apparently there were not enough of the flat-panel HD TVs to go around, mine was a older clunker. The bed was not new; a thick mattress cover was thrown over the lumpy old bed in an attempt to fool. My back was not fooled. New attractive red pillows had been tossed upon a hideous gold crushed-velvet sofa. The effect was nauseating. The old toilet was cracked and leaked. There was no shower curtain liner. The coffee set-up was neglected (supplies not replenished). In its favor, there is a convenient mini-fridge and microwave in the room. The air conditioning sounded like a freight train each time it turned on, and the noise from other rooms, the hall, and other bathrooms can be heard loud and clear, in addition to the close-by fire hall and I-35. I ate breakfast at the rooftop restaurant which has a fantastic panoramic view of Austin. The room was woefully understaffed (Saturday 9/22/07) with one poor soul struggling to greet, answer the phone, deal with special requests off the buffet menu, clear tables, and settle checks. Hilton corporate should look into this incident. In my opinion it was abusive and I don't know how the young woman kept a cheerful attitude through it all. She should get a commendation. Post-partum from this mish-mosh I have to say that it was not worth the very cheap rate I received from HotWire, and under no circumstances should more than $100 a night be charged. This might be a better destination with some serious renovation not done on the cheap. The neighborhood around the hotel shows signs of a clean-up, with the construction of new condos. But for now, spend the extra buck and stay elsewhere.

“Friendly Staff and Good Value” Stayed here for a convention. Very friendly and helpful staff. Free shuttle to/from airport. Free breakfast that is decent by inexpensive hotel standards - always had some form of eggs along with fruit, cereal, pastries, warm mini-cinnamon rolls (tasty), sausage or biscuits and gravy, juice, coffee, etc. Room was clean and well-equipped. Bathroom small as others have noted, but clean and fine with a nice showerhead and good, fluffy towels. Additional perks here are warm cookies at night, and a free happy hour with wine, beer, or soft drinks and snacks on weekdays. Free internet worked fine. Conference rate of $89/nt. made this a great value. Wish it had a fitness center. There is a small pool. Only other down side for those needing to go to the convention center area daily is that it is a bit of a hike. But the upside is that you are in San Diego and it is almost always a very nice walk.

“Perfect Location, Great Restaurant” I stayed at the Hotel Solamar for two nights. The pool area has a great night scene and the restaurant is fantastic. The rooms are good with comfy beds and free wi-fi for Kimpton In Touch members. You have a great view of Petco Field and can even see into parts of the Park from your room. And you can't beat wine hour every night! The bathrooms were ok. They could stand a little refresh of the tubs and showers. But overall, a great place to stay.

“Beautiful, grand, classy hotel - with excellent service” Stayed here for 2 nights while attending a conference, and it was a wonderful stay. The staff is among the most welcoming I've encountered recently, and the hotel has that old world charm, but with modern amenities. The bed was very comfortable, the room well appointed, the views were fantastic. Occassionally I could hear people talking in the next room, and light does stream in under the door, so if you are a light sleeper like me - and need total darkness, I would recommend a sleep mask. The location is within walking distance of great shopping and restaurants, and there is an upscale food court in the bottom level where I had an excellent breakfast one morning. The restaurant XIX was breathtaking, and the food superb. I would highly recommend this hotel and hope I get to stay there again one day.

“Cool place, great location” Great location makes up for small rooms. Hey, this is an old hotel, built when we didn't demand huge rooms and massive bathrooms. It served my purpose well, and it's location near restaurants and bars was great.

“Kimpton Saga Part 5: great potential, but not quite there yet” This hotel is like a quirky, cool car from 1972 - but it'll take more than an extra-thick coat of white paint to make it right. That has already been tried. Being a big fan of Kimpton Hotels, I could not resist booking a room when I received the invitation with a great rate for Kimpton InTouch members. We arrove around 3.20 pm on a Saturday and were received by 3 (three!) men who looked like doormen or bellhops, but they were standing in the entrance watching us struggeling with our luggage, after we had given up the car to the valet next door and taken out our bags and suitcases. What was their purpose? Why were they there, if not for guests like us who came to check in? Why not bringing a cart to the car, so we could have loaded up our luggage onto that, like it is done at other properties? But we eventually made it to the front desk, and we were told that our room was not ready, as they had experienced some kind of water damage earlier that day. We were asked to wait in the lobby until the room was ready. As a compensation we were given wine vouchers for their Bar/Restaurant Zentan. We also received a generous gift for saying the "secret word" at checking in: free breakfast (for both of us!), also in the Zentan, that was REALLY cool. And since we are Kimpton InTouch members, we also got our minibar credit ($10) and free Internet. With all these freebies we were kept happy, so the wait didn't feel as a problem to us. We had fun sitting and swinging in the funny hanging chairs, also enjoying their free ice tea drinks as a refreshment. After a few minutes the Front Desk person (David?) came up and offered a room on the 5th floor. Acknowleding that we prefered a higher floor (data from our Kimpton profile), but our 7th floor room was still not ready, and this 5th floor would be ready sooner, and if we were interested. I declined and said I know I'd regret that, and I would rather wait longer to get the better room. We continued to wait, and after a while he came back again and offered another room now, this one was the same category but on the 10th floor, and we gladly accepted. The waiting time was about 45 minutes all together. The room was indeed great. OK, there were nicks and scruffs galore, and some of the furniture was even coming apart (see pictures), and some stains were impossible to ignore - but the outstanding view onto Thomas Circle, the spaceship-like bath room and the spacious layout of this room (King Premier) really made us forgive the flaws. It was clean enough, and since the bed and the bath were obviously cleaned, we were OK with the status of this room. There were enough towels for a night, plus we had Bigelow toiletteries (the black series which is made for Kimpton). The high floor was adding to the viewing experience, and we took many photos sitting in that space chair in front of the window, watching people walking by below us. We actually had 2 big windows in our room, looking to 2 various sides, so it was actually a corner room. Later we went down to the Lobby to get a share of their wine hour, and we tasted their own recipe of Sangria (made with water melon and fresh basil leaves - very interesting texture and aroma! Hubby found it weird, but I loved it!) They also offered IPA in bottles, and Hubby took one, and he said he liked that a lot better. The lobby was filling up with people, so they must have been booked pretty full. We sat in that alcove where currently the AIDS awareness quilt is in exhibition (see picture), and we found that moving and interesting. We also went up to their rooftop pool, and I swam for a while. It was extremely hot that day, and I couldn't stand it very long to be in the heat, as I had already a sunburn from a previous pool visit elsewhere some days before. The water in the pool wasn't exactly cool, so I left it with the few leaps that evening, and we went out for dinner. When we came back, we headed over to Zentan and were offered a free glass of wine each (for our vouchers from the Front Desk), and we went with the Pinot Grigio, which was a very good choice. That bar was obviously very popular, it was packed with people, it was very energetic. Many people also ate there. We were exhausted and went up to our room and had a good night's sleep. That weird cocon shaped shower stall acted as a night light (its round plastic wall is standing inside the bed room). Next morning we had the most excellent breakfast since a long time (see separate review on Zentan), and again we could watch Washingtonians walking by from where we were sitting. At the front desk I was asking Daisy if I could have a later check out, since I hadn't have a chance yet to try their spacy bath tub, and I was granted another hour with a smile. Thank you Daisy, that was so nice! We went up, started packing, and I had a wonderful spa bath in that big tub. It had no jets, but I didn't miss them. The shape was so interesting and comfortable also, holding me up by the shoulders and yet relaxing completely. It was very high, so I could soak in my ocean spa products up to the shoulders. That cocon shower has been described by many other reviewers already, so I don't think it is necessary to describe it again. It is really funny and interesting to stand inside it and have that shower coming out of the ceiling. But beware, it is a bit slippery! Watch your steps and go slowly! This is not your tiled stall where you can stand safely, here you'll have to pay attention! But definitely a great fun factor, and I urge you to stay in this hotel just for that shower alone! We thought the check out came way too soon, and we would have liked to stay longer, but we can never stay anywhere longer than one night at a time (animals alone at home). Good that we'll come back already in 3 weeks! On a critical note: there are quite a few hick-ups in our single night stay. Starting with the 3 guys watching us struggle with our luggage, the nicks and scuffs and stains in the room, and in the end the charges were put on the wrong credit card. At check in we were handing over our new Amtrak Visa card, requesting to put the charges onto that one instead of the older one which had been used at booking time months ago. The Amtrak card is giving points towards free train trips, and since our favourite Kimpton is in Virginia, we are going there by train, and free train trips are always welcome. At check out I foolishly did not request a print out of the invoice, so I saw the charges only a day later when I was back at home. The old card (not Amtrak) had been charged. I had to call bookkeeping to straighten that out (paying by the minute plus a connection fee, as it is not a free number). It will be fixed, I am sure, but it is a nuisance, especially after I had made it extra clear at check in that we wanted to charge the new card because of the Travel Points it gives us. Oh, and Hubby mentioned he saw some new scratches on the car door and some dents in the bumper. We didn't see that when we left, so we are out of luck, but he is convinced we didn't come with those. Oh well. All in all, a Kimpton Hotel with very high potential to become a true star - but they'll have a long way ahead of them.

“Average hotel which could improve in it's service” When you arrive at a hotel there are certain things that tell you whether this is going to be a decent hotel or not. Long waits for the elevator, no one to escort you to your table in the mediocre restaurant, no one answering the phone at reception (this happened several times), tells you this hotel has some issues. The standards and manning levels of the staff really need attention. Rooms are okay, but you can hear your neighbors in the room next door which is annoying. Location is good in downtown Seattle.

“Great place, great location.” I flew into Oakland and rented a car and drove to San Jose. This hotel was far superior than what I thought it would have been. It was very clean and the room was beautifully decorated, roomy and it even had a balcony. The grounds were immaculate, the pool was clean and the front desk employee was courteous, polite and very professional. The only complaint I would have, if any at all, was that there was only one person working at the breakfast buffet and it was extremely crowded. The poor employee was doing her best to keep up with keeping things stocked, but as it is at most buffet style breakfasts, the "feeders" depleted everything she put out. I would stay here again without a doubt. Even better is the location of this place. Only miles from downtown San Jose the hotel offers free shuttle to the airport also miles away. There is a light rail stop within about a block of the hotel that can even link you to BART from what I've heard.

“Convenience! Great Shuttle Service!” I had to catch a 6-am flight, so I stayed here for one night. The shuttle buses offer so much convenience. They come to the Denver airport to pick guests up every 15 minutes or so. Make sure you wait at the right place, and you don't need to call the hotel (unless you want to be picked up between midnight and 4am). They do the same to drop guests off the airport. Be sure to let the front desk know your flight departure time, and they will recommend a time for you to take the shuttle bus. The drive from the airport to the hotel is about 5-10 minutes. Sometimes, you might be able to ask the shuttle bus to drop you or pick you up at car rental places. You do need to call in these cases, but most of the drivers are happy to help. (I did, and the driver was very nice to be of help.) You can print your boarding passes at the hotel. They have dedicated terminals for this. There is a cafe/restaurant at the hotel which opens late (maybe until 1am, but I am not sure.) I ordered some pretty decent food there.

“Excellent location and good value!” I have also stayed at the Club Quarters Midtown and if I would need to chose which one is better I would say this one is better located, but the Midtown is a bit more spacious. In any case very good business hotels and surprisingly clean and in good shape for NY hotels. I would recommend staying there.

“Nice place to be, but get ready to be Nickle and Dimed” This hotel really is a great place if you are on a layover at Detroit Airport. The hotel is right in the concourse and even has its own security personnel, so you can clear security without having to face the long lines elsewhere. The rooms are great with the super "heavenly bed" that Westin offers. The food is excellent and the meeting rooms are very good. The downside is that the staff (especially the front desk) tend to be brisk, and borderline rude. The other negative is that the hotel nickle and dimes the customer to death. $16 for internet access - a bit high, plus $2.50 for a local phone call! Ridiculous. As well, after a certain period of time you start getting dinged .10/minute, even after paying $2.50 for a local phone call. I ended up going downstairs and using a payphone rather than pay what they wanted for a local call. The hotel unfortunately is using their convenience to squeeze more money out of its patrons in the form of local calls and internet access, etc. While the food is good, it certainly is overpriced (as is everything at the hotel).

“Perfect location” We spent a week Dec 25-Jan 1 at this hotel. It was , as others have written, perfectly situated. You could not be closer to the Contemporary Jewish Museum or SF MoMA. It is a healthy walk to the Ferry market, which I did several times. Many transit options run along nearby Market St. You can walk to the start of a cable car line. You can cross the street to the excellent Westfield Mall- and its unusual food court below street level. I agree the Starbucks could be open later hours. I agree the nonsensical snack tray on the desk should be removed. The business center is somewhat overprices at $.40 a minute for ocmptuer use. The breakfast on the second floor seems slightly overpriced. The health club is excellent.

“Loved the Peninsula” I saw the most celebrities at the Peninsula than I have ever seen in my life. Great rooms,amazing restaurant (where I ate next to John Travolta) the food was amazing! My dad went to the restroom next to Brad Pitt. Jokes apart, the hotel is gorgeous and it's definitely worth the spend!

“Very nice indoor pool” Located about 5 min from Sea-Tac via free shuttle, the hotel has a very nice tropical indoor pool in a large atrium. The room is nice and typical for standard Marriotr room. Room service was decent. It was delivered a bit later than the promised 30 min and I was automatically called by guest service to have the meal for free ( which I declined since I was not in a rush but it was a very nice gesture by the staff). The room is quiet and the bed is confortable. Overall, it is one of the nicest airport hotels that I have stayed in.

“Deserves it's number one rating!” As Diamond Members, we were upgraded to a suite. Not a demi-suite, but a real, honest to goodness suite, with a separate bedroom, kitchen and living area. The staff is pleasant and responsive, the lobby is clean and inviting. The exterior of the building is nothing special, but it is an airport property, just off the freeway. Once inside, you are treated to bright colors and pleasant decor. We only identified two minor issues during a two night stay. One, our toddler's feet turned black whenever he walked on the carpet in our room. I was a bit concerned about the dirty rug since toddlers are wont to eat off the floor. When I got home, I called the GM, and he assured me that they would address that issue. Two, one of the two computers in the "business center" was down over the holiday weekend, and the other was completely taken over by a group of teenagers(they were on for four hours straight). I would have been happier had the desk clerk enforced the 20 minute limit, but I also understand the reluctance to confront a group of teens. I was allowed to use the computer in the hotel office for my boarding pass needs. We would most definitely return if in the area.

“Great Value” Nice hotel, right downtown - easy to get on cable cars, trolley, or city buses. Close to shopping, museums etc. This is an old, retro-fitted building, but still nice. Room was very small, as was bathroom, but it still had a nice ambiance. TV was also small, with limited channels. Hotel restaurant was OK, but prices were not out of this world as they were at other locations. Knowing that most places in San Francisco start at $200+/night, I would choose this place again in a heartbeat.

“An ok stay, nothing extraordinary. But whatever you do DONT eat here!!!” Last weekend my boyfriend and i got the spa room and stayed 4 days there. Since we arrived we received an average treatment. Nothing special. They werent rude but they didnt make any difference like in some other 4 or 5 star hotels in which we have stayed at. No smiles, not even when they gave us our doubletree cookie. Our room were very spacious and had a nice view of the city. We could see the Chicago Theatre, the River and even the Bean! Our room had flat tv in the living room and main room, touch screen phones, kitchen (but you cant really cook in there, nice trick to consume their food**) microwave, mini fridge, 2 full bathroom (1st bathroom w/rain shower and tub, 2nd bathroom is fancier w/rain shower and jacuzzi with city view) In my opinion this is the best room spot :) Could sleep pretty well considering this hotel is located in the Loop Area and is not a very tall building. Hotel has also a top roof bar, but couldnt really enjoy it since it seems to be a club and we wanted something more romantic, but is up to you in whether to go up there or not. Is definitely nice though. The location is perfect! Chicago Theater is right around the corner. Walking distance to the Chicago River, Wrigley Building and Michigan Ave. **Cons Im wondering if theWit have food quality standards because believe me, it doesnt look like it. We had breakfast there every single day and i can tell their food is really greasy and when i mean really, is REEEALLY greasy. So greasy that you can even see the oil drops all over your plate. Every single day i expected my food to be better but i always got the same, a greasy meal. So there was no mistake on how they cook. People with high cholesterol be aware or they might kill you!. But the worst part is yet to come. I found a black hair in my food which of course made me lost my appetite. So why would you pay for this when they dont even have variety of meals. I'd strongly recomend you to go eat somewhere else. There are a bunch of restaurants around the corner for less. Also be aware to not grab anything thats in your mini bar or they will automatically charge it to your credit card, even if your intention was never to consume it. The same with the spa amenities. They charged everything we put out of their place. They have a tiny little message wich advises you but if you dont read it you might get caught by surprise like us. I think if you follow these advises i give you, your stay at theWit will be pleasant. Also note this is an adult and couples oriented hotel, not really a family oriented hotel.

“Good Deal” I booked this room based on Trip Advisor reviews having never heard of this place before. The staff was friendly, the room was clean and large, mine had a bedroom and a sitting / lounge area. Not super fancy but they don't bill it as a luxury place either. I think the representations were accurate. Internet access was included and worked well the entire stay. Overall I would stay here again and the hotel is in a good location. I got the room for $119 a night through Expedia and stayed for four nights during a business trip, it may not be as swanky as some other hotels, but being a seasoned traveler my experience left me feeling as though it was a fair deal.

“Prettiest pool for a Marriott - awesome location.” I took off one point because I am a plat member, but I though the stuffs they served at the concierge lounge in the evening sucks. They had a steak burger and a low quality cesaer salad. It paled in comparison to the stuffs served at JW Marriott LA where I was the night before. $38 valet parking $26 self parking $15 internet (free for gold/plat members) Having said that I think their architecture is beautiful two buildings, north and south tower. The swimming pools area feel like a paradise (tropical). Its right in the harbor so the view are amazing and wonderful to walk around during the evening. Its the perfect location to be in downtown San Diego if you want to see the convention center, Seaport Village, etc. Beats the Hilton (on the opposite side of the convention center) by an arm and leg based on its location and structure. My favorite Marriott so far in the San Diego Area. I got yet to try the rest of them in SD (have reservations for 8 hotels coming up).

“Not my first choice...” Pros: the hotel is in a good location within a mile walking distance to National Mall, White House, museums that sort of thing. Cons: located in a rather noisy area, must be near a hospital because there are constant sirens from ambulances using M Street, double rooms have a bit of a cramped sleeping area, in my case the microwave wasn't working and vending machines were empty for about three to four days straight, when mentioned to the front desk they suggested I try the gas station on the corner.

“Fantastic hotel with great staff” We loved the Fairmont, where we stayed just for one night in a gorgeous suite with an incredible view of Chicago. The room was spotless, and every detail in place. Everything that was supposed to work, did work; not a speck of dust or debris anywhere, and a fresh clean smell; nice furnishings and a very comfortable bed. The staff was also top-notch: professional, pleasant, helpful and friendly. The location is convenient to Michigan Avenue, but just far enough off the main drag to be a very quiet and peaceful location. My only complaint would be that our room was next to the elevator and while we did not get a lot of hallway noise overnight, we did get some sound effects from the elevator shaft itself; however, it was nowhere near as bad as I'd anticipated when we saw the location of the room, so I think their soundproofing is pretty good. We didn't even hear a peep from the fire station across the street.

“You'll be sorry” I stayed at about a dozen hotels in the DC area over the last two months due to business commitments. I limited my selections to 3 and 4 star hotels. Out of the dozen I would rate this hotel as 12 (with #1 being the best). For the life of me I can't figure out how it has a 3 star rating. A 1.5 star rating would be generous. As far as pros and cons, there are no pros. The cons are as follows: 1. When we checked in there was no valet service. 2. The front of the hotel faces the front of a cancer center across 50 feet of blacktop (unlike the website photo which gives the appearance that the hotel faces the street). 3. In order to get to the street from the hotel entrannce you have to walk through several parking lots and you can't see the hotel entrance from the street. 4. While being on the Georgetown campus sounds attractive, the reality is that the hotel is in the middle of a construction zone as major construction/renovation is being done on the campus next to the hotel. 5. If you chose to park on the street instead of paying the hotel a $25.00 a night parking fee, you need to carry your luggage close to half a mile through several parking lots and around a few buildings because if you leave your car in front of the hotel while you unload your luggage (see above-no valet) you will get a ticket for leaving your car in a no parking zone (we got one and the car was only there for 5 minutes). Complaints to the hotel and the University about their not disclosing this fact on their website remain unanswered. 6. The first room assigned to us had a faded rug, a desk light that didn't work and a window that faced a field with bright lights on all night. We asked for a switch. 7. The second room assigned to us also had problems with inoperative lights. We again asked for a switch. 8. We stayed in the third room assigned to us. We did this even though we then had to wait close to two hours for the overly loud air conditioner to cool off the room since the air was not on in this room prior to our arrival. At this point it appeared that faded rugs were a problem throughout the entire hotel. After eating wraped candy from the candy dish in this (third) rooom we noticed the next day that the dish also contained unwrapped candy that someone apparently had half eatten and then spit back into the bottom of the dish. It was never explained how housekeeping didn't notice this when they made up the room prior to our arrival. Next time I will inspect the entire contents of a dish of candy before I take one. Thinking I did not have to do this was one of the many things that I erroneously took for granted at this hotel. Expecting to not find half eatten candy in the candy dish, expecting the air conditioner to already be turned on in the room before it was assigned to me since it was 90 degrees outside, expecting valet service (or a legal place to park in front of the hotel while I carried my own bags into the hotel), expecting to not have to go up and down the elevator three times before I was assigned an acceptable room and expecting a reasonable reply to my complaints are other expectations that I had which were not met. 9. The staff appeared to be either poorly trained or too lazy to do their job correctly. They made no offer to help us with our luggage when they saw us struggling with it and when we made a comment about the quality of the rooms and the faded rugs in the hotel they simply said "all the rooms (are) the same". I would never stay here again. I paid $70.00 a night and I feel I way overpaid. Both Georgetown University and the Mariott Hotel chain should be embarrassed lending their name to this hotel. Again, a 1.5 star rating would be generous.

“Exquisite hotel - refined and generous accommodations” Spent two nights at Mandarin Oriental for a business conference and enjoyed every minute. The hotel is beautifully appointed, fresh flowers and gorgeous treatments throughout. The spa is well appointed and fitness center a good size. Got a corner room that boasted a beautiful view of the monument. The only drawback to the hotel is its location -- it is near the mall, but a good walk to any retail/restaurant area.

“Excellent - seemed like new Chicago hotel” Stayed 04/25/05 - 04/26/05. In Chicago taking photos for work and this hotel is very close to Michigan Avenue. The hotel had a very new look to it and the staff were first rate. Rooms had high speed internet and decent cable channel selection. Breakfast buffet was very crowded - a group I think - so I headed to Cambridge House 1 block south of the hotel - my favorite place for breakfast in Chicago. Valet parking was quick and they let me retrieve some items from the car after it had already been parked. Highly recommended.

“If the price is right- book without hesitation” I stayed at this location in early February 2007. At less than 250.00 (USD) a night, it was a great deal and it’s a very nice, friendly hotel. The Good. The staff is very friendly, they all go out of their way to greet you by name when ever possible. The hotel has a very classic look and the rooms are very generous in size. The bathrooms in particular are huge. The shoe shine service is complementary and a nice touch. Internet access worked well and was reasonable at 10.00 / 24 hours. The Not so Good: Being a Ritz, there is not much to say negative. The health club next door is an additional $15.00, well worth it if you have the time to relax and enjoy, but a bit pricey for a quick work out. The lower level business center is more trouble then its worth. Its not staffed, the hotel offers little support to it’s operation, plus you need a charge card to do anything there (the price is not the issue, it’s the inconvenience). The elevator do not go directly to the lower level meeting rooms, from the guest rooms. Although we had a negotiated meeting rate, the reservations people would only offer it to me for 2 of the 3 nights, the final night the rate doubled! Upon arrival I had no problem getting the negotiated rate for all nights of my stay. Overall, If you can get this hotel for a rate comparable to the Marriott or Area Hiltons, book it without hesitation. I would not recommend paying twice the rate of a Marriott, as you wont get twice the service or accommodations.

“A basic clean hotel at a reasonable price in Hollywood” The rooms at this hotel were basic but very clean and included a small fridge. We ate an early breakfast in the room that doubles as office and eating area but only 2 tables. The manager was exceptionally friendly and accomodating, booked tours for us, and offered information about the area. The parking was adequate (and free!) and we had a pleasant stay with no problems. If you're looking for a clean reasonable place to stay in Hollywood near all the attractions, you can book this hotel with confidence.

“Awesome for access to San Diego Conference Center” This looks like a new hotel and is in a great location. Close enough to the Gas Lamp area and conference center to walk but, far enough away to keep things quiet. The breakfast is good and free. There is a nice place to eat right across the street if you want something better. Parking is expensive at $32 a day valet only so maybe best if your only doing business in downtown to catch a taxi to the hotel. The biggest issue I had with my room was the lighting for the sink. It's only on one side. For my room that was the right side. That made it hard to shave in the morning because of the lack of lighting. I'll try to post photos of what I was talking about for the sink later. Other wise this hotel is great to stay at. Has a kitchen to heat the left overs nice little area to workout in and people watch or have people watch you.

“Excellent value for NYC” The rooms are excellent, health club is above average - and location is quiet - just south of World Trade Center Site. Rooms on highest floors have views of Statue of Liberty. We were in a weekend special rate so we weren't high enough (24th floor) and couldn't see it - but I heard if you're up at the top of the hotel (40th floor and higher) there are beautiful NY Bay views. We prefer to be closer to the Theatre District - but no rooms at moderate rates were available there when we made our reservations - after all - it was Memorial Day Weekend. Make sure if you stay here on weekend rate get a rate that includes breakfast/brunch. Their Sunday brunch is tremendous and is normally some $20 per person - a good deal in itself - but with the weekend special it's only $10-$20 extra for the entire room. Don't stay here if you depend on taxis as it's a $20 fare with tip to the theatre district and going back and forth th mid-town will get pricy - but the subway stop is a short walk so if you can handle the subway this hotel is fine. But if you're going to be in the financial district area - you just can't beat this hotel.

“Right where the action is” From the first interaction at the front desk we knew we had picked a winner. All of the staff are friendly and helpful. Location is perfect for visiting the clubs and eateries on Beale street. Rooms are spacious and comfortable with mini-frigs and microwaves. If you want extra room ask for the one over the rounded front entrance - we had 519. Great breakfast comes with the price.
