“Kimpton does it again ...” Check in was quick and easy and we were shown to our very well appointed room by the helpful bellstaff. The bed wes comfy as were the pillows and the temp control was very welcome during the very cold post Christmas period. The hotel is a 5 minute stroll from Union Station which has a great variety of shops and places to eat. A bit of a walk if you wanted the main area for restaurants, but taxis are cheap and plentiful. That evening we decided to try the restaurant Bistro Bis - do your wallet a favour - don't! The food was nice, but overpriced and not particularly well presented, I expected more from the write ups and the price! We did not eat breakfast at the hotel, we went to Union Station or to the Starbuck's just down the road. The wine reception each evening was a nice touch. We were able to meet withand talk to fellow guests, which gives the hotel a warm family atmosphere.

“Good rooms, convenient, GREAT price and just a couple, very minor problems” We stayed at the Houston Doubletree Hotel IAH for one night between flying into Houston Intercontinental (George Bush) Airport and driving down to Galveston for a one-week Caribbean cruise. For a review of that cruise (Carnival Conquest), see my posting (using the same "T. Advisor King" screen name) for March, 2009 at http://www.cruisecritic.com/memberreviews/memberreview.cfm?EntryID=54377 We gathered our baggage from IAH and walked outside to the shuttle bus pick-up area. The Doubletree shuttle was already there. Unfortunately it was full and we had to wait for the next one. However, we only had to wait maybe five (and certainly less than 10) minutes for the next empty shuttle to arrive. The hotel was nearby, but I don't have any recollection of aircraft noise. Usually, when you stay at an airport hotel, you have to accept that you will hear planes taking off and landing all night. Perhaps it was the direction of the wind, or maybe I just don’t remember it. But I certainly wasn’t kept up by aircraft noise. We (family of four, with children 11 and 14 years) had adjoining rooms. My only real complaint was that I had booked directly over the phone with Doubletree and been told that they could accommodate a reservation that specifically included a room with one queen adjoining a room with two twins. When we arrived, the check-in clerk informed me that all they had was adjoining twin rooms. I had pre-paid to get a favourable rate, so there shouldn’t have been an issue getting the room I had paid for. That said, everything else at the hotel was good. The total cost, including all taxes, was $98 per room. The hotel is a conference-style airport hotel, so it is larger than typical economy-style airport hotels, has an outdoor pool (which we didn’t use) and restaurant facilities. We had already had dinner before we arrived, so we didn’t need to find anywhere to eat. I understand that there is not much nearby, in terms of restaurants. There is fast food next door, as well as a gas station with a small grocery store. After we arrived, we walked down to the grocery store and bought some soda and liquor to take on the cruise. It was very convenient and the price was right. The rooms were fairly basic – nothing special. But they were more than adequate – very clean and comfortable. Each room had a flat-panel LCD television (something in the 35” range, I’d guess). However, I’ve yet to stay at a hotel with HD-capable TVs that actually provides HD programming. It’s sort of pointless to provide widescreen TVs without the widescreen, HD programming. Other than the problem with room types on check-in, the hotel staff were excellent. They provided excellent information when we asked about nearby grocery and liquor stores. In addition, we checked out around 10:30 and waited in the lobby for our hired car to pick us up at 11:00. Even though we were early (the car wasn’t late), the bellman insisted on calling the car service to make sure the driver would arrive on time. The car did arrive on time and got us quickly to Galveston for a price that was far better than the competition. I highly recommend “Z-Limousine” if you are looking for Town Car service at taxi price in the Houston area. Trip Advisor's rules preclude me from including their phone number of email address in this review. While I was thoroughly satisfied with the rooms and the price (except for the room-type issue), my review wouldn’t be accurate if I didn’t mention one thing I noticed literally as we were leaving the room to check out. As I was just about to drag my suitcases into the hallway, I stopped to toss some paper into the trash can in the bathroom and noticed a small line of ants working its way around the trash can. Because I hadn’t noticed them during my stay, it really didn’t affect my impression of the room. I mentioned it to the registration staff at check-out and they seemed genuinely concerned. I got the sense that they would have refunded the room charge if I’d been a “difficult customer” (or would have reduced my charges if I hadn't prepaid), but I told them that I had only noticed it as I was leaving and it really wasn’t a problem for me at that point. For the price I paid, I would definitely stay at the Doubletree Houston Intercontinental Airport Hotel again and I probably wouldn't bother looking around, hoping to find some place that might be better.

“Excellent choice for top end DC full service hotel” We just spent a few days at the Grand Hyatt Washington for business meetings. There were 5 of us and we all loved it. This is a full service large hotel with great restaurants, sports bar, spa, and is located perfectly downtown in the northwest section of the city. It's perfect because it's close to most attractions and businesses but also because the best metro stop, metro center, is located at the hotel. In fact if you take the 11th street exit, you don't even have to go outside! Metro center is where several lines intersect so you have lots of options for traveling around the city. Very nice clean room with nice amenities. The price was right for this quality of hotel. Absolutely no reason to pay more to stay elsewhere. This will be my new place to stay for most of my DC trips.

“Great Service” Positives: The staff at the Omni were very cordial and efficient. Housekeeping had told us about cookies for the kids at bedtime. From the front door to when we were leaving, everyone was very nice. The rooms were very well decorated and the beds were good. Very expansive bathroom. Negatives: The drop off point was right at the street and did not allow for more than 2 cars and a taxi at one time. Extremely low end for dropping off the family. Neutral: The cost was reasonable based on the fact that the hotel is located 1 block away from Independence Hall. Valet was reasonable.

“Great Hotel in Denver” Stayed last night at the Westin in Downtown Denver. I'm an SPG Platinum member, so was upgraded to a absolutely wonderful room -- a Mt. Evans Suite. Huge room, superior bath, big TV. Perfect stay. The location is great -- on the 16th St. mall, close to Lodo and Larimer Street. Definitely will stay there again.

“Outstanding Stay” I had never stayed at a Kimpton Hotel and now I am not sure I can stay anywhere else!! This place was fabulous--the staff was wonderful, the room was fabulous and the location was perfect. I had never been to SF before and was worried about the location based on some other reviews--but I do not know what they were talking about. I experienced more homeless closer to Union Square than I did at Taylor and O'Farrell. The car rental companies right across the street were super convenient and so much less expensive than an airport rental. The restaurant was fantistic and happy hour with $3 appetizers and drinks were an added bonus. Will return and stay again. Thanks to everyone there for the wonderful stay!!

“Great staff!” When we checked in late there was only a room with two beds available on the 2nd floor (facing a brick wall) so they said they'd move us the next day and they did! They even transferred all of our luggage for us to a great room on the 5th floor with a city view. Pros: -small, boutique hotel in a great location -very comfortable beds and pillows -clean room -staff was really friendly and gave great recommendations -free continental breakfast and happy hour daily Cons: -carpet in both rooms looked stained and in need of replacement -towels in bathroom are thin and scratchy -there is only 1 mirror in the bathroom- they need a full length one by the front entrance to the room

“Not The Best But Very Adequate” If you want the best Starwood Property in NYC, stay at the St. Regis or possible the W Times Square. I found the Westin to be just fine: larger than average rooms for NYC, nice bathrooms, good club lounge, very good fitness room, great location, friendly staff even in the hectic day leading up to New Year's Eve.

“Such a pretty hotel.” Great location, friendly staff and the hotel itself was really, really nice. Nothing but good things to say about my trip here and the city itself - I would go back in a heartbeat.

“Great location and service” Arrived early and the kind check in person was able to accommodate us. We opted to take an upgrade with a view of Pike Place and the Space Needle. The room was comfortable with a separate living space and bedroom. Always impressed by the Hyatt bathrooms and amenities. There is a Starbucks in the building which was convenient and there are malls all around. Greatly enjoyed the night at the hotel and found the whole experience good.

“Nice Weekend stay” We had a party to attend near downtown and stayed for one night. The staff was very friendly and professional. Our room was clean and the beds comfortable. The hotel was very quiet. We ate dinner at Noe that night and really enjoyed it.

“No frills, good location, friendly staff, quirky little room!” We went to NYC to see and experience NYC, not to stay in a 5 star hotel. We wanted a safe, clean, well located hotel. That's exactly what we got! It was quirky and had little frills (except the bathroom seemed recently remodeled and was great!-but they only gave us two bath towels). The staff was nice and helpful (we were able to leave our bags there before and after check out). Our view was into the neighbors apartment - which was amusing! Our room was very small - my husband was able to touch both walls when his arms were stretched out! It just added to our wonderful trip to NYC. We'd stay there again!

“It's not the Four Seasons, but it is Starwood comfortable” I don't stay in NY much, but when I have I find that the reasonably priced rooms are invariably small. Ditto here. The "Traditional" King room is tiny and as other reviewers have noted there is no space beside the sink to rest your toiletries.Being Platinum SPG and staying over the weekend we solved this by requesting and getting an upgrade to a suite. MUCH BETTER! The suites are two rooms put together with one as the sitting area and one as the bedroom. The bathroom is significantly better too. Get a suite if you can. Having said that, the Starwood beds are pure luxury. They also include a free bottle of water or two, and have showers instead of bathtubs with a shower head in them. Free coffee too. Room decor is modern; brown woods and leather. It's not harsh or depressing, just warm. Tried the restaurant in the lobby for dinner. It was comparable in price to the neighborhood eateries and was surprisingly good. We would probably have gone out to eat but it was 9 PM and about 10 degrees. In that case you can rely on the hotel restaurant. Dining room service was decent - although you pay for every soda or drink refill. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. Lobby, if you care, is really small. Internet is free and effective. This isn't Four Seasons luxury, but it's sort of like a cruise ship - comfortable if you aren't going to be in your room all day. Don't know about pricing as we were on a loyalty reward.

“Nice Quiet Hotel” This hotel seems new. It was quiet, clean and in a great location for getting on and off some of the major thoroughfares through San Antonio. My room was small, but it had a flat panel tv, fridge and microwave. The young lady at the front desk was efficient and friendly. The breakfast was just okay, but I would definitely stay here again.

“Nice Room, Good Location, Some Oddities” We stayed at the Royalton on a weekend visit and knew that it was going to be a fairly "hip" hotel. The lobby is dark and the check-in desk seems kind of hidden. The lobby is a bar/night club, with many beautiful people and a DJ. First ,the good: The room was huge, particularly by NYC standards. We believe the closet was the size of an actual room we had at the W New York. The bathroom was actually two rooms with tons of mirrors and a great shower. We had flat screen TV and and a couch. The Royalton is part of the Morgan group and is similar to the Hudson Hotel in the fact that it doesn't have a box spring and the beds are very close to the ground, which can be a hassle. We liked the location, about four blocks from Grand Central and near the Theater District. Second, the bad: The staff seemed put out to deal with you. Not rude, but not really into dealing with you. When I checked in I asked for the best possible room, because my wife wasn't sold on the hotel and I got no response from the front desk people. We were never greeted by anyone. Each morning I would walk by the front desk and the bell men and say "Good Morning", with no response. It really wasn't that big a deal, but it was a change from some of the places we have stayed recently. Third, the different: I already mentioned the beds being close to the floor. But what I found very odd was they had candles in the rooms and matches! I'm sure it would be romantic, but I thought that was kind of safety hazard. Overall, I would stay here again for the right price. We paid $239 a night and got a $20 Metro Card.

“Never again!” Just stayed here for a weekend while doing some hiking in the area with a friend. Did not need a fancy hotel, just something clean and comfortable. This one barely met those standards. The hotel is a little hard to find and in a strange location. I did not feel real safe going out to my car at night. The rooms were average/small, smelled musty and felt "wet". The bathroom needed significant updating and a good cleaning. The hallway was extremely hot. The knobs on the AC unit were broken off. The lobby seemed like the kind of place you would sit while waiting to get the oil changed in your car. Breakfast was poor, minimal at best ( cold boiled eggs, bannaas and toast). Would definitely not stay here again and would probably not stay at any Comfort Inn again....

“Nice hotel and location” We stayed here for the B1G championship game. Hotel is very nice but lacked a few things that were important to us. We traveled as a family and are used to having 2 adjoining rooms, King with 2 doubles. We had 2 Queen adjoining rooms. The front desk was extremely accommodating but I was surprised at the lack of King rooms. Apparently since its so close to convention center there are more requests for double rooms. Front desk said they have no King/double connecting rooms and we couldn't even get a room with a King and 2 queens on the same floor. Weird. The rooms also had no mini-bar. That's something I expect of a high end hotel. Room was updated and clean and nice but rather small.

“Fun place to stay in Chicago” If you are visiting Chicago and want to stay in a cute hotel in a lovely neighborhood, Hotel Lincoln is a great bet. The hotel is supposed to resemble your quirky aunt's house, and it does. You can even find tootsie rolls in some of the drawers of the front desk in the lobby. The hotel is right on Lincoln park and is super close to the zoo and Old Town. Cabs are easily caught right in front so you can be downtown in minutes. There's even a farmers market right across the street on the weekend. The lobby is fun and hip and the staff is warm and gracious. A colleague and I shared a suite and it was perfect for 2 since it had 2 full (albeit smallish) bathrooms and a really comfortable pull-out sofa. We had no issues at all during our stay and enjoyed free Wi-fi since we are JDV club members. I would definitely stay there again.

“Older downtown hotel building with lots of character, kept in great shape with modern comforts.” Granted, I stayed at the government discounted rate, but considering how nice the hotel was, it was a steal! From the nightly happy hour (really happy when its free!) to the friendly staff and good hot breakfasts along with a really comfortable room, this was an excellent stay. When I return to Dallas, I'm not looking anywhere besides the Magnolia. I definitely recommend trying the Iron Cactus restaurant next door also.

“Great location, customer service” As many people on here, I got a great rate from Priceline. The hotel has so many rooms that, if there is no conference in town, they go empty. For the money, it was an amazing hotel. We were helped immediately upon our arrival since the quick check-in kiosks were not working with our reservation. The lobby is somewhat elegant but not overdone and the rooms were clean and nice. The furniture is old, style-wise, but in good shape. I was really content with the hotel. Security is stellar, requiring all people entering the lobby to show their key in the evening. I wouldn't pay more than $175/night for the hotel and we paid considerably less than that. Overall, it was clean, friendly, well-located and worth the money we paid. I was content. Oh, and great water pressure in the shower! And the beds were extremely comfy. Flat screen tv in our room with a great picture. No bells and whistles but a solid, nice place to stay.

“Great for Meetings” This is the second time I have used this property for a business meeting, and it has been an excellent experience both times. First, the property is new and in great shape. The rooms are spacious suites with kitchens, and all the furnishings are stylish and first rate. Second, all the staff here is really helpful and attentive. They really help support you so you can focus on your meeting, and special requests are met with a positive attitude. The location, close to the airport, is a bit removed from development, but there are restaurants across the street. I traveled to downtown Denver in less than twenty minutes, so if you really want to mix it up with the crowds, it's no big deal. I am looking forward to my next meeting here, and I don't hesitate to recommend the Hyatt House Denver Airport.

“Great Position” The Phoenix Park Hotel is very well located for your exploring of Washingon. Very close to the Union Station and Capitol Hill it is very easy to be seeing the sights virtually from the time you leave the front door of the hotel. Reasonably priced, the rooms were on the small side but kept clean and tidy. Staff very helpful on arrival and nothing was too much trouble.

“The Place Just Works” Located on the West Side on at 45 W.81st St opposite the Hayden Planetarium, The Excelsior delivers a quality hotel experience at a moderate price point. The lobby with its marble floors and rich woodwork reassure travelers they've picked the right place. Rooms are tastefully decorated though I'd recommend requesting a room with a park view. These rooms overlook the softly glowing blue sphere of the Hayden Planetarium. Looking down on the blue sphere of the planetarium adds a slightly modern sci-fi quality that provides a tasteful cool factor. My preference is for the Park View Suites which provide a separate sitting room with French doors separating the master bedroom. I've been impressed by the spaciousness of these rooms and the extra drawer and closet space which seem to make extended visits in NYC especially comfortable. The bathroom is small and has one only one sink, but is plushly equipped and luxurious. As a nicely renovated pre-war structure the hotel is not modern, but it has been well maintained and has a certain 1940's feel to it which I find lends an air of stability, safety and attractiveness that I like. Complimentary shoe shine is efficiently arranged where you slide your shoes into the drop off bag and find them at your doorstep in the morning. The hotel has no restaurant, but has an elegant breakfast room in its richly carpeted Library where a friendly omelet chef and extensive breakfast buffet make for a relaxing and comfortable breakfast experience complete with the morning paper. This service runs to a decent hour so you always are able to start the day in a calm and relaxing manner before you hit the streets. Situated on an active cross street which extends across Central Park, the Excelsior is well located as a base for getting around town. There are ample restaurant choices on Columbus, multiple deli and pizza choices on Amsterdam, and, because of the cross street, abundant cab activity at every hour of the day rain or shine. There is also a subway stop at the corner of Central Park West. I have used this hotel for about ten trips and have always been satisfied, though I have occasionally been shown to an un-renovated interior room which I have rejected since I always specify a more expensive Park View Suite or renovated room with a Park View. Having shopped hotels in NYC fairly often and traveled there for business frequently, I have pretty much settled on The Excelsior as my best tradeoff in the moderate price point category. An east side alternative with better proximity to the museums is the Hotel Wales, but I find I'm completely happy with my West side nest at The Excelsior.

“Fantastic location, Ok hotel, Horrible staff” The Novotel Times Square is probably the best located hotel in NYC, and since NYC is the most important city in the world, does that not mean that this is the best located hotel in the world? Philosophical contemplation aside, it is basically as close as possible to TS without dumping you in the middle of the hordes. When we arrived at the hotel at just 5:00 AM, there was no one at the front desk. We tried shouting into the back room but they pretended not to hear us. Eventually a bar tender appeared and he went into that same room we were shouting in and dragged out a very sleepy employee who very clearly did not want to be there or help us. We booked two rooms with two double beds: We got two rooms with a king in each. We went back to the front desk to complain to a different guy who appeared and he was the rudest, coldest, most disnterested clerk I have ever encountered. Let's just say our request wasn't met and we put up with the kings for the rest of our stay. Another request that didn't get met was at least one room overlooking TS, but that had a happy side-effect of getting a near unobstructed view of the 4th of July fireworks. As for the room itself, while clean (and quite large for NYC), it was in desperate need of renovation. The bed covers are of the old colored variety, which I thought had been phased out in most hotels at least a few years ago. All furniture and walls were scuffed, dented, nicked, and in general really tired. Gaps were appearing in the cheap-looking ceiling panels, and some of them were filled in with some ugly paste that made the ceiling look worse! At least the TV was very new. Another annoyance was an internet connection that would cut out every 2 minutes. The bathroom was also large and well-appointed, but again looking pretty tired and mold was starting to grow in the shower. The nicest amenity of the hotel was the 7th floor terrace overlooking Times Square. Just bring some company and chill out for an evening watching Times Square go from light to darkness. All the seating was comfy and there seemed to be a good selection of drinks if you're into that. After our previous experiences with the staff, we were too scared to try the restaurant, but what I do know is that breakfast is outrageously expensive (think $20 per person) given all the options at your doorstep. If all you want is coffee and good pastries, try the Starbucks across the street - there it costs $20 for a family of 4! Given the price we paid, I don't think we got a bad deal, but I can't recommend staying here if renovations don't happen soon. However I think I'll try nearby Hampton Inn next time.

“Pretty Average Hotel” I have stayed in this hotel many times. I don't have anything negative to say about it, but it is really just average. I love the location because it is located in china town and there are hundreds of neat shops and restaurants to choose from. Really cool high tech japanese toilets.

“Not a bad place to stay in downtown Los Angeles” The Metro Plaza Hotel provides adequate accommodations. It is clean and fairly comfortable. The hallways need some deodorizer on the carpets but there is no odor problem in the room. The room itself is pretty roomy and it has a table and desk. I had to work at the table because there is no power supply at the desk to plug in a laptop. The Internet access is free and not too bad. One complaint is that there is no dresser to unpack to, just shelving. My standard complaint with most hotels that provide a refrigerator is that it never really gets or keeps anything very cold. Parking is cheap considering it's in downtown LA. The staff was a bit slow (they could use some technology updates) and courteous but not particularly friendly except for one gentleman working the desk in the morning. Another big upside is that you are right across the street from Phillipes which has the best dipped sandwiches. Also, being right at Olvera Street is nice. The Metro Plaza is far from the best hotel I've ever stayed at, but is also far from the worst. But given the rates, it is worth the price. I would stay there again when business takes me to downtown Los Angeles.

“A Classic” Booked a suite and it was absolutely beautiful. Tastefully renovated, beautiful white leather chairs, very nice bedroom and bathrooms, and as this was a corner suite, huge living room with and lots of windows. Great service. Ate at one of the restaurants downstairs. Food as ok, nothing special.

“2 Nights in a great location” So we just spent two nights at the Club Quartes in Boston. The negative up front. The rediculous atm check in/check out system which is status quo for Club Quarters. If you have an issue at check in, then you walk over to the person at the desk and the assist you. Which we did and they did. Why not just check in like every other hotel in the world? Secondly, we had a closet that was six inches wide. This is great if you are checking in with your assorted pool cues and starched jump rope collection. On the positive. Friendly staff, Excellent FREE bottle water dispenser on every floor. Location was superb. Less than a five minute walk to the State House T station and the Park Line T station. Elephant and Pub connected to hotel was quite convenient. Would definitely stay again even with the irritating atm check in check out.

“Serves the purpose most of the time, but can be chaotic and noisy” A very, very busy place at the edge of a hotel/restaurant complex a half-mile away from Midway Airport. I've stayed here many times and it's not too bad a place. The front desk staff work hard and are very courteous, but they seem understaffed at certain times. Some rooms can be noisy. If you aren't out of your room early in the morning and dare to hang a DND sign on your door, housekeepers will punish your audacity with interminable vacuuming and loud conversation just outside your home away from home. If you want to sleep late, avoid rooms on any floor ending in or nearby _36, which is located near a stairwell and housekeeper's closet, the doors of which undergo constant slamming. The last time I stayed there I was subject to a job fair held at the hotel, which involved an all-day traffic jam and a constant stream of job seekers in and out of the hotel. Very chaotic and unrestful. On the up-side, they do have a nice workout and pool area. On a nice-day, walkers/joggers might or might not enjoy a 4-mile jaunt around Midway Airport. Happy Exhaust Breathing.

“Wonderful Hotel” After reading all the negative reviews, I was not optimistic about what I'd find at this VERY expensive NYC hotel. I'll caveat this by saying that I was given a free upgrade to a junior suite on a high floor... but I found every aspect of the hotel to be wonderful. The room was large, elegant and clean. The bed was extremely comfortable. The desk area was efficient. The bathroom gorgious. The service was exceptionally friendly and proactive. The location was great, and I had a nice view of the Park. That being said, it is very expensive... and they keep trying to nickel-and-dime you for everything once you're there (e.g., $16 internet connection; insane mini-bar prices; room service). Even by NYC standards, this place is expensive. I would certainly stay there again on my next business trip to NYC.

“Everything was superb!” We booked a spa package and ended up being able to get a suite with the savings in the package. Read the rates carefully to get the best deal. I loved the location, the room, the public areas, the staff .... absolutely everything.

“Very cool zen-like Boutique hotel” Nice large rooms with 2 queen beds. Lovely lobby with lots of wood and open space. Free cucumber water and newspapers. Quiet location and the area is getting better everyday. The staff were very helpful; offering us a room when we got there very early but advising us wait until later because we would get a better room and we did. Joie de Vivre is a get company.

“Drury knows what Hospitality means!” Once again, the Drury brand has risen to the challenge and MORE than achieved the success it deserves and is recognized for - JD Power and Associates 7 years running! You can associate "luxury" with all sorts of names in the Hotel industry, and quite frankly, none will match the UNFETTERED, consistant results that Drury lives up to. From the moment you arrive, you have this instant "ahhhh...Home Sweet Home"! That "dated" look so many comment about in my opinion continues that "ahhhh...Home Sweet Home" charm. That unpretentious, warm, welcoming greeting you get from Mary, Christopher, and the rest of Jose's Team enforces that "ahhhh...Home Sweet Home" sense when you arrive. Check-in is always a breeze, one that says, "hey, hope your travel here was comfortable, and we're glad you're here." That anticipation of when the buttery hot, fresh, popcorn smell will begin to waffe through the lobby, to the "when's dinner - aka - 5:30 Kickback"; tell me, where are you going to get THAT feeling, and all at an incredible value? I actually appreciate the room, it's layout, and amenities. It tells me that I've paid a reasonable price, for a safe, clean, quiet roof over my head with all the "trimmings" of a FREE hot breakfast, FREE hot afternoon/evening Kickback, FREE good wireless internet, FREE long-distance phone calls, FREE daily popcorn/soda, FREE parking and amenities like an INDOOR/OUTDOOR pool, indoor hot-tub and exercise room... My roonm is meant for a few hours of shut-eye; not where to spend my day. And so, I don't want to pay a huge price just to say it's chi-chi and ooh-la-la! Proximatey to the Galleria, downtown Houston, 610, 10, 45, 290, River Oaks, and on and on. It's where to BE if you're going to be in Houston! Jose...you bet we'll be back. You have a tremendous Team, run a beautifully managed hotel, with Staff who show they enjoy working there. We can't wait to be back!

“Good location, but not as nice as many omnis” I stayed here for a recent conference and was very pleased by the location. The room was good, but it had not been upkept very well. By no means was it run down, but it was not worth the $248/night that I paid. Breakfast room service was quite good, but pricey...lunch and dinner room service was not particularly good. There was a nice pool and jacuzzi with fresh towels available at the facility. It is right on the trolley line and at the entrance to the gaslamp. I probably would not stay here again if given the choice, likely choosing the Hard Rock that is right across the street from the Omni.

“Have to Agree--Watertown is GREAT” After trying all different Seattle downtown and north/south metro hotels over the years, I gave Watertown a shot based on all the great reviews and--wow--was everybody right! I was there 4 nights and it poured pretty much everyday but was a restful and relaxing place to stay. I had a suite which reminded more of some of the modern boutique hotels I've stayed in large cities in Australia and Europe. I loved that the windows opened (European style) and the spaciousness of the suite, and all the funky yet very nice decorations. Breakfast bar each morning was better than most any I've ever had--who has guava juice besides here? The free parking was also a draw for me and saved me a good $80 over the downtown hotels that charge an arm & a leg. I had a trade show at the Seattle convention center and it was a snap getting there & back--less than 10 minutes even with Seattle's notoriously horrible traffice on I-5. When it wasn't raining I did get out to walk to the shops & restaurants in the University District, which were just a few minutes away. This hotel is very convenient off of I-5 and in the U District, but was very quiet and located in a nice non-busy neighborhood. I'll never stay anywhere else in Seattle from now on!

“Recommended!” The Palomar is very good hotel which I would recommend but I find it hard to believe that it is one of the best in Washington. The service provided by the staff is definitely exceptional and they are very helpful and welcoming. The rooms are large (apart from the bathroom) and are furnished OK. The Palomar is very close to Dupont circle and is in a great location for shopping and for restaurants. The walk to the Mall is a bit further but is definitely manageable and public transport is close by if not. All in all, this is a very good hotel which I would recommend but just don't go with too high expectations!

“Wonderful value for business travelers” Club Quarters is developing a reputation for good properties in major cities at below rack rate prices, especially if you're a corporate member. I'm not, but I paid $149 for this room, surely one of the best values in midtown Manhattan. Room was small but perfectly appointed. Only downside was noise from garbage trucks before dawn, but that can be true anywhere in the city, and I six floors up. Lovely executive lounge plus restaurant are available just steps from Times Square.

“Not quite a miracle” This hotel is in a great location - lots of shopping and easy access to downtown. The staff members were always friendly, and the property was always clean. My room was a good size: king bed and a sitting area with sofa. The view overlooked a courtyard. It wasn't exciting, but much better than any "light well" you may have previously encountered. My only 'beef' with the room was the slightly worn look of everything. It looks as if the rooms had been redecorated about 5 years ago so they weren't dated, just looking a bit tired. The bathroom was fine, but the tub surround looked as if they had caulked over mold. Not appealing. Another oddity for me - the rack holding clean towels was over the bathtub. This mean that every time you showered, they would get splashed & steamed. I didn't get to use the guest lounge, dining, and business center; however, I walked through one late evening and found the area to be well appointed and inviting. Another bonus - a washer & dryer available to the guests. It is coin operated. I spent 7 nights in Chicago and then had to immediately travel to another city for 5 more nights. Being able to do a load of laundry before I flew out the next day was a relief.

“Modern simplicity, only slightly insufferable.” When in Austin for leisure, it's pretty amazing to be able to stay right on S. Congress, which has shopping, dining and entertainment all within close walking distance. You pay a price for this luxury, particularly here due to its upscale, modern design. Make no mistake, this place is NOT for people who want to be pampered. It's not a luxury hotel. The room reminded me a bit of staying in a Los Angeles apartment for a couple of days. It's spare, it's a little cold, but it's really, really cool. The grounds are lovely. There are lots of places to gather, to eat a quick bite from Jo's Coffee (great coffee and pastries), to have a glass of wine. Above all, the most negative thing about this place is the noise level. We were in a room close to S. Congress, which is a very noisy street until after the bars shut down. We were kept up by cars growling down the street, drunk kids screaming on the sidewalk and live music from nearby venues. It seemed to die down by 1 a.m. Other hotel guests weren't very respectful either, screaming and playing music until late in the night, but we didn't complain to the hotel, so that's our fault. I guess you could say this place attracts a less-than-respectful clientele. In all, though, we enjoyed our stay because of the location and the novelty. I'm not sure we'll be back, but it's worth at least one stay if you have the right disposition.

“Great Location” I travel to Fort Worth on a regulad basis and have stayed at several hotels both downtown and out away from the city. I always seem to be draen back to the Worthington for the combination of location, great fitness center, nice rooms and staffing. The two negatives are the lack of free wireless internet and the parking fees. Overall it is a good value in a great location

“Posizione eccellente, hotel a 4 stelle ad un prezzo da vero affare” In quest' hotel ci sono stato nel 1991 e adesso nel 2010 e devo dire che a distanza di 20 anni è pure migliorato. La posizione e fantastica, di fronte a Westfield Shopping Center e accanto al capolinea dei cable car. L'hotel e bellissimo un vero 4 stelle rapportato ai canoni italiani. Modernissimo appena ristrutturato, tv Plasma 40", mancava solo il frigobar noi avevamo una stanza al 27 piano con visuale su tutta la città. Il prezzo per 4 notti, 316 euro per una matrimoniale. Un affare!!!Sempre con expedia.

“Not bad for a night. . .but bring your earplugs!” I got a tremendous rate on hotwire and so I stayed here the night before I left for a cruise in the South Pacific. I waited in what seemed like a VERY long, slow line to check in. . .it took over 20 minutes at 10:30pm. Once I got up to the counter, however, since I was prepaid, they gave me a key and sent me on my way. I had a very nice room on the 14th floor, although it was literally on one of the airport runways, and was exceptionally loud. The fan/ac in the room would turn itself off, so I couldn't use that as white noise, and I didn't use the earplugs since I didn't want to miss my alarm. . .so, every couple of hours I was woken up with some huge plane taking off right outside the window. I was hungry after traveling across the country, and went to eat dinner downstairs, except they don't really have a restaurant that's open that late. So, I ordered a pizza and a soda, and took it to my room. It was actually very tasty, albeit a bit expensive. I found the bed very comfortable, the room quite large, and the bathroom nicely appointed. The toiletries were basic--but it isn't the Four Seasons. I did, however, appreciate the relaxation cd, the eye mask, and the earplugs. It was a thoughtful touch! I would definitely stay here again given the opportunity.

“Superior location, great service, just a few quirks” The location was awesome for getting to/from airport and public transportation, it was always easy to catch a cab or walk. The service was pleasant and rooms were clean. Only quirks: gym wasn't impressive and the bathroom had a pocket door that never entirely closed. If you're sharing a room with someone else, you may also be sharing the full sensory experience of the bathroom.

“Incredible service” It is rare to have the opportunity to view up close a truly superior and well trained staff in the American hotel industry. I had this opportunity at the Omni San Diego this past week. I almost did not stay here due to parking and location issues but was glad I made the decision to be an Omni guest. Two very qualified concierges manned the information desk at most all waking hours and they were full of suggestions and could field an answer for almost any need. The housekeeping and front desk and valet parking people were equally helpful and always friendly. The lobbies, public spaces, pool and gym were all very attractive and well maintained. The rooms were very comfortable with perfect mattresses, better sheets than I have at home, robes, supplies, etc. I liked the "louvered doors" which slide open to make the bathroom sort of a part of the room, (but I can understand the reasons some reviewers might feel this compromises privacy). I did notice, that even though the hotel is pretty new, it must be getting used a lot by the baseball and convention crowds (Hotel sits between the baseball stadium and the convention center) and there was some minor carpet wear, tiny hole in comforter, and wear on the chair. Hopefully the management will catch these things before they begin to drag the place down. There are a couple of other glitches but none would stop me from staying here again. As most people mention, paying $26 for parking is a drag. However, I must say that the valets had my car to me in no time and in-and-outs are included in the bill. Some friends paid $15 for a parking deck a block away but could only take the car out once a day. The nearest free street parking looked to be about a 20 minute walk away, up by Balboa Park. The other problem mentioned by members of my group is the blowing of a whistle or horn by a nearby freight train in the wee hours of the morning. I heard it but quickly went back to sleep. You might discuss this when making reservations and ask for a room facing away from the train location...but then this might also knock you out of a view of the bay. If you have one, you might consider taking along a battery powered "white noise" machine which masks out sounds of the night. I forgot mine this trip. (You can get these at places like Sharper Image). Despite these glitches, I heartily recommend this hotel. It was a great experience. My rate was $131 (but it was a group rate for my conference/class so I can't comment on the relative value of normal rates). I found that the hospitality spilled over to the hotel restaurant, McCormick and Schmidt. Though a little pricier than I would have preferred, I had a good meal there and they honored a special diet request with good cheer.

“Perhaps the Most Overrated Hotel in NYC, Tourist Trap” Though perhaps the most famous hotel in the city, it is by far one of the most overrated and overpriced hotels in the world. Yes, the lobby will wow you with classic design and elegant appointments. It is everything that a grand hotel should be. Large and open, with an urban and classic feel and look. However, beware of fool's gold, because the rooms are actually worn and tired. Because of the sheer volume of rooms, the lobby is a whirlwind of commotion and chaos. Checking in feels like a cattle call to get all of the tourists in and out as quickly as possible. There is no personality, no charm and certainly no genuine feeling to the front desk staff. It is all business to get to the next person as quickly as possible. Migrating towards outer hallways, the hotel is simply beautiful. Marble everywhere, very expensive floral arrangements and a veneer of old world class. Again, don't be fooled. The rooms are extraordinarily small. The wall paper was peeling, the carpets were torn and the bathroom downright filthy. It was so bad, that I actually requested another room in the hopes of getting a better room. No luck. The room that I moved into was in similar condition. Dirty toilet, saggy matress and used towels in the closet. Zero attention to detail. None whatsoever. At the end of the day, the Waldorf is a "grand hotel" for tourists that never travel and want to stay in a name hotel. You will get ripped off and the only people that could be impressed with this average, at best, hotel are those folks that don't know any better.

“Bit of Miami in a New York setting” The Mondrian Soho is a very pretty small hotel in a great location. The rooms are tiny, but this is not exactly atypical for NYC hotel rooms. The design does make use of the small space, with a scaled down slipper chair, built-in drawers underneath the bed, a sliver of a desk, shower with no tub etc. If you are a light packer and a somewhat agile person this shouldn't be a problem. This design aesthetic is very "Miami" -- pure white and ocean blue everywhere, a bit of glitter here and there. We stayed when it first opened so everything looked pristine, but over time I would imagine it would be difficult to maintain this look. The restaurant looks like a solarium and is just gorgeous. We didn't eat here but the drinks were good. Service was good.

“A fine hotel in a great location.” Very professional and friendly front desk staff. Room was excellent and what a great bed! RARE eatery on premise was great and the b'fast a steal for NYC! Wonderful room and amenities and I WILL book and stay here again and with family too! You can't beat the location.
“Great Value” I really like this hotel - great location right downtown, near the sports stadiums. Good value with the breakfast and large rooms. Super nice staff!

“Amazing Location” a group of us had a wedding in boston. a few months back we started talking about where to stay. we decided that because we were going in june that we wanted a hotel with a pool. all fingers pointed to the colonnade. one of the group works for a company based in boston and she had a connection, so she got us 4 rooms(2 adults per room) for $179 per night. we all have young kids so we were thrilled. we were very excited until someone told us it was old and run down. we kept looking at the pics online and it looked nice. we pulled up and asked where to park bc we were staying there. instead of asking to help us with our bags, we were told where to self park. i had read that the service was not too great, and we hadnt even gotten out of the car yet...we parked and schlepped our stuff into the lobby, which we decided looked very nice...ok....we go to check in...again, prompt, but not overly friendly. we are still kinda skeptical about the decor, etc, but we have not yet disappointed. we were on the 7th floor, we opened the door and the room was great! it was kinda small but we were in a city after all(nothing could compare to my tiny studio i nyc!!), but new and modern and cool. the bathroom was small as well, but clean and new..and even had a little ledge for our stuff...we went up to the rooftop pool..this is worth everything. a FABULOUS rooftop pool deck with great pool and amazing chairs. they serve food and drinks up there. unfortunatly, the weather was awful so we really didnt get to use it. but its amazing!! if you want to be in the middle of the city, close to everything, this is the place. we ladies loved it bc the mall was directly across the street. our husbands were not so happy, but we were!!! always cabs, tons of everything.. beds soo comfy as are linens. bathrobe in room(2) which we love..products are sufficient but not outrageous. hd tv with flat screens in each room. if need be, i would def stay again. if you want to be in the heart of the city, i would say def stay here. the people that work here are a little rude but besides that its great!!! fyi-the parking is really expensive..$40 a day. see if you can work that into your room rate!

“Westin's are the best” We spent 4 nights at the Westin in Times Square the first week of Oct to celebrate my sister's 50th birthday. The room was perfect, best view of the city overlooking the Hudson River. The conceirge was the best I have ever dealt with (her name was Melanie) from flowers to champagne to suggestions for dinner and activities she gets my highest admiration. The heavinly beds are more than heavnily. The food at the Don Shula's Steak House, the best. The hotel bar was fun, drinks great and snacks some of the best without having to pay for them. We were within walking distance to almost everything. Did all the tourist things, carriage ride in Central Park, saw 2 fabulous shows and ended our stay with a supurb dinner cruise on the Hudson River circling the Statue of Liberty before returning to that heavinly bed. Its worth the trip, and Westin Hotel is worth the money.

“Hot and cold impressions” I stayed at the Warwick for a convention: the hotel is just beyond the city core on a low-density street of townhouses and small shops. It is a brisk 15 minute walk from the convention center, or an 8 dollar cab ride. A classic hotel in style, little changed since the 50's, it offers clean yet dated accommodation. The hotel is a combination of 'best of...', 'worst of...'. The lobby, staff consideration, water, breakfast, and internet is substandard. The lobby is tired, the staff indifferent. Water pressure is low and hot water is lukewarm. The buffet breakfast is expensive ($ 14) and sparse: bacon, scrambled eggs, a few breads and cereals. Wireless internet is slow and costs $10 per day, with a code that must be entered with every connection. The room size is generous and breathtaking: there is a huge bed, sitting area, a large TV (which doesn't turn far enough to be visible from the writing desk), and a big minibar. The bed is firm and comfortyable; street noise is acceptable. There are two large closets, one a walk in. The dinners are superb, with attentive and pleasant service and well-prepared meals (where are these chef's at breakfast?). We took a group of physicians to a large group meal and every arrangement was well-handled. It is easy to get a cab, and there is an exercise room on-premesis. Overall, a very mixed review, I know, but it's hard to overlook the areas that could be so much better despite the many things that are good about the hotel.
“Great location, but slightly vintage rooms.” Location is perfect for NYC sightseeing, but rooms are not as luxurious as other hotels. In particular, our bed was extremely soft/lumpy.

“Shabby,overpriced and will no way stay again” After reading reviews,I booked this hotel specifically requesting a renovated room. What I received was an extremely old shabby room with worn furniture, a TV relic of the 80's, a bathroom that badly needed redoing- all for the pleasure of $200 a night. I complained to both onsite staff and Marriott as I am a Marriott Rewards Member./ After the treatment I received, I cut my Marriott Rewards card into pieces. If you really want a class,comfy hotel upscale hotel to stay at - DON'T STAY HERE I should have booked the Westin - so should you

“Big, Convention-y but comfortable hotel” A good, basic hotel to stay in the downtown area, if you don't mind being overwhelmed by conventioners & large tourist groups. The Hilton is a massive hotel right off Powell St (up the street, round the corner from cable car terminus) with a large lobby and well-appointed rooms. Price was ok given convenience to downtown (corporate rate cheapest we could obtain). The area is a fun mixture of a 'billion' tourists, the homeless, and shoppers to the many stores...just turn right out of the main entrance. If you turn left on O'Farrell...more local 'color/sketchier.' We visit SF often, and have stayed at the Hilton once before, and knew what to expect. Our last stay was a very pleasant stay. Our experience this time: a pleasant stay, except for the huge crowds of conventioners. Upon arrival the lobby was overwhelmed with conventioners having drinks, food ,etc...making it noisy, busy, crowded.... and this was no small lobby! This occurred all 3 days we were here, as the convention lasted that long or longer. Once we got past the lobby, we were fine. We originally asked for a King-size bed, on hi-floor, but received the exact opposite ... given the hotel was booked mostly for the conventioners. The room was fine on the smallish side, but with 2 double beds. A clean, comfortable room with standard amenities of toiletries, mini-bar,etc. Hotel provided for 2 free bottles of water (probably b/c Hilton Honors member (or corporate?)) Would be nicer with in-room safe... Next day, requested a change of room .... and to our surprise got a change. We thought the conventioners booked the hotel solid. We simply asked ... did not demand or raise any fuss (in the noisy lobby). The new room was a suite on a high floor with the King-size bed we requested originally. Very good size room, with sofa and so much more space. A big plus !! Made the stay even better. We did not eat in the hotel, or use room service, as we were sure they were super-busy. Overall, we recommend this Hilton with the above warnings on conventions. It is very convenient and comfortable, though service was a little impersonal (probably due to the busy week we were there).

“NIce stay at the Hotel Allegro” My wife and I stayed at the Hotel Allegro over a long weekend a couple weeks back and thought overall that the hotel was very nice and worthy of its class and the reviews we had seen. We booked through PL and although the Allegro was not our first choice, we were very pleased. The hotel is right next to the Palace Theater and Chicago City Hall and has a number of services nearby and is just a short walk from State Street. It was very conveniently accessed from both the Kennedy Expressway and the L, which was two blocks away at Clark/Lake. Self-parking is about $35 a day in the ramps nearby ($49 valet), but you can save yourself a few bucks parking at Grant Park ($29) and walking the six blocks. The lobby and registration are upstairs one floor from the street, with plenty of valet and bell help at street level. Once checked in, we headed up to our room on the 8th floor, only to find out it was a double. After deciding against being Ozzie & Harriet for the weekend, we went back down and were quickly changed to a king without any fuss. As other posts have mentioned, the rooms are a bit on the small side and a little more like what you might find in Europe. We thought our room was clean and that good use was made of what space was available so that we didn't feel cramped. We had two small closets to hang clothes and a three-drawer dresser. The bed was also very comfortable. Our room was on the northwestern corner of the building, which sits at the corner of Wells and Randolph. The western leg of the Loop L runs on Wells, but we really didn't have too much trouble with noise from that or the street below. My only possible complaint with the room was with the mini-bar refrigerator, which cycled almost constantly, after which there was a audible "pop" of the condenser. We didn't avail ourselves of any of the hotel amenities during this stay. The hotel bar looked like what you'd expect from a hotel bar, while the restaurant looked like it might possibly attract a non-hotel guest clientele. Overall, we were please with our stay and would stay at the Hotel Allegro again.

“Great choice in San Antonio” I recently stayed for four nights at the Hilton Palacio Del Rio whilst at a convention in San Antonio. The hotel is very well located in central San Antonio and just a very short stroll to the convention center and is right on the Riverwalk, one of San Antonio's best features. Also, the Alamo is only a couple of blocks away. The hotel, although older than some in the city, is clean, safe and has excellent staff. I was upgraded when I checked in, to a suite with a good view of the city. The room was a little dated, but very comfortable and great value for money. The buffet breakfast was good and it is well worth booking a room with breakfast included, as it is a little expensive on its own. The hotel has a great Irish pub downstairs, right on the Riverwalk and the trolley ride stops right outside the hotel. For shopping, the Rivercenter Mall is a five minute walk. Overall, a very good stay and will definately stay again when in San Antonio.

“Rough Around the Edges” I have stayed at this hotel several times, the last time being a few years ago when it was quite nice. It’s not what it used to be and needs a renovation and some service improvements. Good points: Location is superb. Guest room was spacious and had in-room coffee. Television was enormous. Room was equipped with an ironing board and iron, and a safe. Climate control worked well. Bed was comfortable. I had breakfast in the restaurant, which was very good and somewhat reasonably priced. Bad Points: The common areas were dinged, worn, and a bit beat up. The room looked the same, with what looked like 10 sloppy coats of paint on the door frames and woodwork. The bathroom had debris, grunge, and hair in the corners (see photos). I could hear someone stomping around in the next room; noise has been a problem every single time I have stayed in this hotel. Internet connection is $12.95 per day, even in the meeting rooms. The room was not well appointed, and there were almost no amenities except for coffee and shampoo. Instead of an iPod dock, for example, there was a CD player which would have been great if I still lugged CDs around like in 1998. There was a robe that was rough and ratty-looking. The water pressure was so weak I had to turn off the second showerhead just to have decent water pressure. The linens were so stiff and rough it was like drying off with a big piece of sandpaper. The front desk staff seemed begrudging toward simple questions; for example, my invoice was to be emailed and the clerk acted like I was stupid for asking about my total upon checkout. There was nothing really egregious; no OMG! moments. But if I am paying $200 with few amenities and crappy equipment, the room better be really clean and the service impeccable. It wasn’t. This hotel is a good example of why I have been staying at Westins less and less these days. I have had so many average experiences at above-average prices that I am getting to where I don’t trust the Westin name anymore. I suggest looking around at the hundreds of hotels in the area before deciding on this one. Hope this helps. .

“This Hotel has Gone Downhill in Recent Years” I just spend the night at the El Tropicana Hotel in San Antonio. Several years ago this was an old Holiday Inn, but changed their name about five years ago. I have stayed at this hotel at least eight times over the past five years. It seems that the hotel has made a few renovations, but remains as a sub-par property. The hotel claims that it is on the River Walk, but the hotel is several books from any of the shops or restaurants on the River Walk. It is true that the river runs just at the back of the hotel, but this is not on the River Walk. Checking in was problematic and took about ten minutes. The one girl at the front desk was on the telephone, while two employees stood in the door way of the office area talking. Finally, I interrupted them and asked for assistance. The hotel rooms are small and the bathroom is even smaller. The carpet in my room was dirty and had several stains. The work desk was so small I could barely place my computer on it. The television is one of those old models and I could not locate a remote channel changer. The bathroom tub area had several large stains and while taking a shower the water would change from hot to cold in response to someone in another room flushing the commode. The mattress was lumpy and I woke with a sore back. The pillows were made of foam rubber and one pillow was too small, while two pillows were too large. I slept very poorly. Also, the hallway is very narrow. I do think the staff tries to be helpful, but they seem poorly organized and managed. This hotel continues to go downhill. As I trust most know, there are literally hundreds of hotel options. I think in the future I will choose to stay at some other property.

“Another Solid Courtyard Stay” This property wasn't one of the newer Courtyards, though it has been updated to have the same interior design feel: the red and gold decor, dark wood furniture, etc. Our room was clean and comfortable. We had a balcony, but opening the sliding doors was a mistake. The balcony was oppressively hot, and that made our AC struggle to re-cool the room. We chose the location to be closer to the gay areas of Dallas, and it wasn't a long drive at all. However, we weren't blown away by Dallas' gay scene. Maybe we missed the right places. The hotel was quite a solid experience.

“great addition to the marriott family” Stayed two nights in early Feb. Great lobby and dinning area. Staff was very attentive from the tme i stepped out of my car. Rooms are well appointed with seperate whirlpool tub and shower. Hotel is a bit isolated, but the have a great shuttle (suburban) that will run you to local dinning and entertainment. Overall a very good stay

“Great Value and Location” Stayed here December 17-20, 2006. The room was great - stayed in a room with two double beds, size of the room was good. Room also had coffee maker, fridge and microwave, as well as a tv. The staff were friendly, especially the porter who held our bags until we checked in and after when we checked out until we left by a cab to LaGuardia (which was arranged by the hotel too - $45 with tolls). Paid US$139 for the room. Breakfast was good - bagels, toast, oatmeal, juices, coffee, fresh fruit and donouts. Location was excellent, steps from Macy's, Penn Station and the Empire State Building. Street where the hotel is has lots of Korean restaurants and shops, a bit on the unsightly side compared to other places nearby. But always felt safe. Highly recommended, excellent hotel!

“New Hotel, Great Staff, Great Stay!” The Sleep Inn Inner Harbor is a great find - it's a little outside of downtown but located very close to Power Plant Live, the Aquarium and Harbor area/shopping plaza. It's about 1.5 Miles to Camden Yards/Ravens Stadium but it's all very walkable. The hotel itself is very nice and has a new feel - very boutiquey . The decor was very modern and not too busy. Beds were comfortable and the check in went very smoothly. Breakfast had a variety of items including eggs, sausage, waffle makers, cereal, fruit, muffins, breads etc. The hotel is also located within easy walking distance of Little Italy with a lot of great restaurants. Parking is $15 per night or you can park on the street at your own risk. They do have a computer in the lobby if you need to print your boarding pass or check your email. The front desk will also be glad to call cab for you if you need it! They do not have an airport shuttle but they do have a shuttle to bring you to John Hopkins if you need. One thing to note - our room only had a stand up shower, which may not work for some families with young children but for us it was fine.

“gutes Hostel, jedoch etwas abseits” Ich habe das Hostel nur fuer eine Nacht gebucht, da ich danach noch ein Hotel und ein zentraleres Hostel gebucht habe. Das Hostel ist sehr gut gelegen, wenn man am Flughafen La Guardia ankommt.(Busfahrt lohne umsteigen mit metroticket). Ansonsten ist das Hostel dann doch eher abseits gelegen. In der Naehe ist die Columbia University und der Central Park ist auch noch gut zu erreichen. Man kommt in NYC zwar gut und schnell mit der Metro rum, weswegen es eigentlich kein Problem ist. Es gibt jedoch auch hostels, die besser gelegen sind,... Gut gefallen hat mir, dass ich in einem Zimmer mit nur einem Hochbett war. Also nur 2er Belegung. Das Zimmer ist dafuer zwar auch relativ klein, aber vollkommen ausreichend. Insgesamt war alles ausreichend sauber. Die Baeder sahen relativ neu aus, jedoch musste ich unter kaltem Wasser duschen. Das war hoffentlich nur ein temporaeres Problem. Wenn es einem nichts ausmacht, dass man etwas weiter ins Zentrum mit der Metro fahren muss, ist es ein super hostel.

“TOP!” Ich habe war vom 25.-30.08.2011 wieder in diesem Hotel. Das Andaz Fifth Avenue besticht durch seine tolle Lage. Die Zimmer sind sehr schön, modern gemacht. Das Bad ist superfrisch, einladend und mit viel Glas gemacht. Das Hotel ist ja auch ganz neu. Der Parkettboden im Zimmer war gut - allerdings müsste m.E. der Teppicheinsatz rund um's Bett nicht sein. Ich frage mich, wieso denn nicht gerade Parkett durchgezogen wurde. Die Tagestarife des Hotels schwanken stark zwischen rd. 250 USD und 1'000 USD für einen Standard-Room. Empfehlen kann ich das Hotel alleweil - auch eine superprofessionelle Haltung während dem Hurricane "Irene" vom vergangenen Weekend!

“Great hotel” This is a nice new basic need motel. Rooms were a tad small but had everything one would need. The shower water pressure was a bit weak but service was top notch. The hotel isn't near anything on 1604 and about 4 miles from SeaWorld. But for the price the location is doable!

“TRY THE PANCAKES” I stayed here on business, and was pleasantly surprised with the interior and level of service. The rooms are average with nothing outside of Embassy Suites Standard room, but the cook to order breakfast was fantastic. You have to try the pancakes as they something special here.

“great location, really nice hotel” This location is great - very walkable for both business and going out to dinner, or to see local attractions. The lobby is nothing to write home about, so don't expect a hopping social scene or anything. The hotel itself is quite impeccable - from linens to cleanliness. A plush bed and lots of pillows make it comfy. Check-in was super fast and personable, and cabs are plentiful at the hotel's taxi stand to get anywhere quickly. Quiet hotel as well, which is always important. I had room service once - the menu was not huge, but for hotel food was above average. But you're in Seattle - may as well get out of the hotel and eat anyway! Would definitely stay here again.

“Awful” The hotel markets itself as an antique classic that has been restored to a "Hollywood" style glamor. NO WAY. I was thrilled to stay in an old-fashioned reconditioned hotel, but was uncomfortably surprised by just how "old" this place really is. Evidently, Hotel San Carlos has undergone some renovations in the recent past - but I can't for the life of me figure out what it involved (carpeting?). There are some charming features to be sure (the lobby looks like its glory days have long past, but if you squint hard enough you just might get a feel for the hotel's past). Otherwise, the hotel's rooms (bed, linen, bathroom, TV) all feel more like a MO-tel than a boutique hotel. And frankly, for this price I bet I can find a motel that has newer sheets and pillows. Oh, and I almost forgot - the shower's water pressure was equivalent to holding a small bottle of water and gently pouring it onto your head. No pressure at all. I do NOT recommend this hotel.

“Positive Experience, Some Reservations” The Algonquin has undergone an extensive renovation and what was a dark dank cramped hotel is now quite a bit better. The overall room size (even in a suite!) is still small and the elevators are small, too few, and painfully slow. The passenger elevators still double as staff elevators so expect to share with housekeeping. The restaurant food and wine selection is much better than before the remodel, although typical NY expensive. The affiliation with Marriott seems very sketchy, as noted in other reviews, just point earning and not much else -- no upgrades, staff seems completely clueless about the Marriott Rewards program levels. Room furnishings have been nicely upgraded, although the location brings with it nighttime noise and lights that are hard to block out. Staff was responsive in removing an unexpected charge on the bill, although it took a little effort.

“Only if you fly in/out Hobby Airport” I had business close to Houston's Hobby Airport, so the Hampton Inn, which is usually pretty good, was selected as being close and having a shuttle service. Unfortunately, my experience was not a good as it usually is with Hampton Inn. Having to wait 45 minutes for a shuttle bus is not really a 'service'. It came 30 minutes after I called the hotel to inquire as to the pick-up. It's a 5 minute drive from the airport - so not sure why the problem. There was no problem leaving early in the morning as the driver was ready to go. The staff were quite friendly and helpful. The room was good, bed comfortable and room quiet. Probably the hotel could do with a bit of refurbishment. The hot breakfast selection in the morning was not up to standard - everything was dried out and with not much flavor - I pitched it and went with the cereal/juice/coffee selection. There are no restaurants in the immediate area and it was suggested by my business hosts not to walk in the area in search of one. So if you're only flying in/out of Hobby Airport, it's an OK hotel. Flight crews seem to stay here.

“Very nice hotel - brand new - city center” I've stayed in all levels of hotels - from the Ritz to the Schlitz - everythIng in between. This hotel is branded along the lines of Aloft and/or a cheaper version of W. Anyway - it's brand new, very stylish, huge rooms, nice black/grey colors - all around amazing. Looking forward to the rest of my 3 nights here.

“Quite nice” Stayed for one night recently so not much to go on, but everything was fine. As a Hilton Diamond got an upgrade to a nice, huge room--really could be considered a suite. Decent breakfast included with my status (or is it included for everyone?), and the staff was very on top of making sure I had coffee, juice and anything else I needed as soon as I sat down. Bellboy similarly right on top of things in helping me get a taxi and with my bag. Only very minor glitch was that upon arriving close to midnight there was no one at the front desk to check me in. It took me a minute or two to notice the sign saying I should ring the bell for service.

“* Beware NO Guest Climate Control * and some survival hints” [Note to Priceline & other third-party guests] Like everyone else, 3rd-party customers read reviews and arrive with expectations; high attentiveness to guest needs is what distinguishes one 2-3 star from others. Third-party prices fill rooms, and provide the business with opportunities to sell services and win future customers. My advice to Priceline customers: pay attention to reviews, articulate your needs clearly (both in advance and on arrival) and speak directly and immediately to management if your expectations are not met. If basic room needs are unmet and you bought from Priceline, ask management for adjustment; if unresponsive, tell Priceline in writing; use snail mail to the company’s street address and direct to Customer Service VP. I’ve found them responsive. Talk to local management directly and pleasantly: they value meaningful guest feedback and often can use information you provide to correct persistent problems. Whatever rate you paid, be courteous and civil to a fault: it never helps to be confrontational. Commend with care what is commendable.] I discussed both commendations and problems thoughtfully with management, and was heard. I did not ask for adjustment. A resolution to issues discussed below (some of them out of the hotel’s control) was offered by way of a partial refund, which I did not request but which the hotel was generous to offer. This hotel has built-in issues, because it’s owned by Georgetown University, on the Medical Campus [great for walking but far, far from good public trans options] and managed once by Marriott but now under contract with Aramark Corporation. One must presume both entities wish to profit, but Aramark has inherited from Marriott some serious and long-term maintenance problems. Which leads us to . . . . . . Positives: Great, supportive, warm bedding. Nice Bath & Body Works toiletries. Unfailingly pleasant staff, housekeeping and especially a maintenance worker who came many, many times to adjust the room temperature, see below. A comp bottle of water in placed in the room most days with coffee. No tea. A no-cost guest washer and dryer on 5th floor. Not-so-greats, small-but frustrating things: nowhere near a Metro or other good, fast public transportation. It’s foot, or cab. Water and temp controls at bath are not intuitive; hot water supply on and off, and low temperature; tub drain leaks water: a bath you draw now will be drained out in 30 minutes. One seat in room, a desk chair with hydraulic controls that leak—set it up, in 30 minutes you will be 12 inches lower. Old TV, in a cabinet with one of two doors that auto-closes (it would have to be taped open). What-the-hotel will not tell you, on its website or anywhere else: FOOD--5 minutes away, across the parking lot, a huge buffet-style cafeteria and grill and sushi bar called “The Epicurean,” open early (6 am) and closing late (10p or after). I was referred there by students in the “Starbucks” hallway adjacent to the hotel lobby. It’s not owned by Aramark, so competes with Aramark food. Reasonable prices and great food. FREE WIRELESS: not available anywhere in the hotel, but available in the Starbucks hallway off the lobby, apparently provided as a university service. The Starbucks is not a corporate store, so a Gold Card is useless. The BIG bad ISSUE, also not disclosed: Guests (at least in some rooms) cannot control room temperature. This would not be an issue in summer, when the A/C is jacked to maximum. But at other seasons . . . . the valves that work the chiller and heater systems buried in the wall, are stuck in many or most rooms and must be manually manipulated. Result: room is overheated or overchilled, guest has recourse only by calling the staff to come or sometimes, by allowing in outside air. I speculate that this may violate health department regulations and that it could be a health hazard to elderly guests. After three calls to and visits from staff to “fix” matters temporarily, the front desk sent up a big plate of cookies and fruit, and I piled on the warm clothes. Nasty add-ons: I request a refrigerator so that, for health reasons, I can control my diet. The charge for a mini that can be bought new for $85 = $25 per day. This charge was removed when I complained to management. Internet, fair quality: $9.95 a day, a new access code must be bought daily. Parking, $25 for 24 hours, controlled by the university hospital.

“Noisy and a little worn out” I stayed at the Aloft right near the airport. The shuttle was great. My room was a little worn out. I liked the style and the room was highly functionable. The workout facilities were fine too, albeit a little limited. My major complaint was the noise level of my room. I had a room facing the road which was noisy for most of the night. I was on the 4th floor. I would ask for a room that faced the other side of the hotel which I imagine is much less noisy.

“Ein tolles Hotel” Wir waren im April 2007 im Hyatt at Fisherman ́s Wharf und begeistert. Besonders die Lage ist ausgezeichnet. Man ist in wenigen Gehminuten am Meer und in den Flanierstraßen. Die Ausstattung der Zimmer ist sehr schön, farblich in schwarz, braun und grau gehalten, fast japanisch anmutend. Die Betten waren mit einer besonders dicken Matratze ausgestattet, die sehr bequem war. Am Pool, der sich auf der 3. Etage befand, konnte man es trotz stetigem Wind sehr gut aushalten. DAs Personal war superfreundlich und darauf bedacht, alle Wünsche zu erfüllen.

“Great stay” We had reserved 2 rooms for 5 nights,the rooms were comfortable and clean But like other reviewers we did find the well appointed bathrooms a little dark. .The hotel is in a very good location easy to get around the city by subway but within walking distance of Battery park and restaurants,The staff were friendly and efficient especially Veronica who went out of her way to help.The complementary drinks and wine were most welcome after a busy day sightseeing and the baristas were knowledgeable and keen to please. We would stay again when visiting N,Y,

“Friendly staff, nice layout” The hotel is eight stories and my request to stay on a higher floor was honored with a seventh floor suite. There are two 32” flat screen TVs in the suite, with about 40 channels available including many in HD. Because of the approximately $10/night Internet fee, I did not test the Wi Fi service and can't comment on its performance as I typically do in my reviews. The area for the manager’s reception and the morning breakfast buffet was large and had ample tables and seating. I usually try to stay at hotels that are within walking distance of at least a few restaurants. There's not much in the area but in researching this hotel I decided that I would eat at the Omaha Steakhouse that is in the property, so I didn’t venture outside until I checked out. The hotel was quiet although in the morning I could hear some noise through the window from nearby I-77 (my room faced to the south). Staff were friendly throughout the stay and with the exception of the Wi Fi fee I was satisfied with the stay.

“ottima posizione per visitare Washington” Ideale per girare il centro della città a piedi (che privilegia la vita notturna dovrebbe scegliere il Westin Georgetown, intorno al Westin DC Center la vita serale è povera....). A 10/15 min a piedi della casa bianca e della parte commerciale della città. Bellissima struttura. Camere spaziose e confortevoli. Molto tranquillo. Piccolo consiglio : se non indispensabile NON chiedete informazione alla concierge : troppo insistente per farti pagare anche un sorriso e per consigliarti ristoranti carissimi che vuole prenotare lei per conto tuo (cosi sicuramente prende la commissione).

“The new benchmark for business hotels” The "Springhill Suites" brand of Marriott makes Courtyard, my other go-to brand look dated. Large rooms, modern decor, comfortable bed, and a good work area with a sofa make this room a pleasant stay for up to several nights. Lighting is very good and the room is bright enough in the daytime where you don't even need a light on till dark. Modern halogen lighting in the bathroom makes it look bright and clean and LED reading lights on the bed are kind of cool too. Overall this room is something so modern that I'd expect it in a big city in Europe or Asia, not Texas. Airplane noise is a bit annoying, but good on Marriott for raising the bar for a good hotel experience for not much money. All I want is a clean, bright room and this was what I got.
“Mile High Viste” Safe, clean place to attend a convention in Denver. Close to everything (but the Rockies) that you would / could want to visite in Downtown Denver.

“A little gem...and a little room” We had booked a room with a hotel that was not opened, so this was a last minute switch. An upgrade in quality. A super little hotel. The staff was a bit stuffly...but I loved the brit car that they picked us up in at the train station. Lots of very nice touches in the room. Jazz playing when we walked in. Lots of nice extras. The room was very small and very oddly shaped. The only down...the staff was a little stuffy.

“Wonderful experience” We had a wonderful experience at the Lenox Hotel. I can't say enough about how helpful and friendly the hotel staff was to us from the desk folks to the bellhops to the concierge.
