There was a slight mix-up in our reservations so they put us in a huge corner room that was magnificent! If any of you watch a Disney show called "the Suite Life of Zack and Cody", my kids felt like we were staying at the Tipton Hotel! The aging hotel was been re-done admirably and in a classy manner. We ordered room service one night for dessert and the cheesecake and apple cobbler were just great! Also ate breakfast several times at the hotel's Azure Restaurant and, again, a high quality experience. Rooms were kept very clean and twice daily service for our rooms including a turndown at night with luxurious robes on our beds. The location was great, near a T stop, and also near the very cool Newbury Street neighborhood. All in all, our experience was just great and well worth a return.

“Good Location for Downtown Chicago” I stayed here 3 nights for a work conference in July 2012. I think this hotel is in the process of being updated HOWEVER, they haven't made it to the 27th floor. I noticed while on the elevator that some of the floors had a more modern decor that was different than the 27th floor. I have stayed at a variety of locations in Chicago and I like this location. It is close to Magnificent Mile, Navy Pier, and many other fun sites. I was able to walk most places that I visited. I stayed in a corner room on the 27th floor (make this request). I had a city/navy pier view which was magnificent. The bed was cozy and comfy (good linens). The room was very quiet and I could rarely (if ever) hear neighbors. The decor as stated above was tired and in need of updating but was fine. The day I arrived my TV did not work nor did the outlet on the desk. I had to make two calls to get these items fixed. I have traveled enough not to get worked up about these small details but I know some of you really care about these things. The staff I encountered (which was limited) was pleasant. I guess that is about it. Good central location and adequate to sleep for a few nights. There was nothing that 'wowed' me about the place but I would stay there again. If I brought my family for a visit to Chicago, it would be a great choice.

“Best Holiday Inn Ever- Wish they were all like this” Stayed in August for 2 nights, selected this hotel b/c of the positive TA reviews and it was close to our business meetings. Friendly Faces upon entry, great dine in resturant/bar with great prices and very tasty food, had a chicken salad, and a burger there over 2 days. The food value and quality is so good that people not even staying at the hotel eat there. PCR Plat member, and was treated to a nice upgrade with a very clean room, which is all I hope for! Only criticism is that the bathroom lighting is a little dark, needs a few more lights or brighter bulbs. Would definately Stay Again, a nice surprise near DFW. Be back in Nov/Dec.

“home away from home” We have been staying here for the past five years on at least a once a month visit. I was concerned as to what would happend after The Dorchester Collection dropped this property, but the reality is that there in no difference at all.When you go, Request a high floor(35) and Cathedral view, and you will be treated to a fantastic view. All of the staff has been around for many years and cannot be nicer. The location in the hear of midtown makes this a perfect place to stay and acces the main attractions and restaurants.

“Safe Haven in a Storm” On Dec 19, we headed into NYC for the day. One of the largest blizzards in years was heading up the East Coast -- so, early that morning, I used priceline.com to secure two rooms (one single, one triple). The Renaissance Hotel 57 accepted my bid (less than half the rate at marriott.com). Upon arrival, we had two single rooms with a double bed each. While I'm not sure where the miscommunication was (priceline or marriott), the front desk did their very best to accomodate the triple room needs, by upgrading one room to a larger size - this in the face of a now packed hotel with the snow coming down outside. I commend the friendly and accomodating reception area. As for the hotel itself, it's a boutique hotel in a great area of midtown (57th @ Lexington). My room, the single, was small, but average for NYC/Europe sized rooms - and quite adequate for one person. The room is efficiently laid out, very technically friendly (HD flat screen TV, laptop and video connections, halogen spot reading lamps) and the bathroom has been upgraded, with a high-end, European flair. I would suggest this hotel for singles or couples, but not necessarily a family destination.

“Great Location; Not Business Traveler Friendly; Antiquated Check-In; Strikers” We were very disappointed. This once was a great hotel, but is so no longer, based upon our experience. We stayed here primarily because of location and the fact that most of the other near-by hotels had no rooms available that day . Location is great, but check-in was a problem. Entrance to hotel often was partially blocked by strikers (an 8 year old situation the strikers claimed). After a 10 minute wait in check-in line (only one clerk available, not many people in line), the front desk clerk was unable to find our reservation in her system...even though I showed her an e-mail with reservation number and date on it. After about another 30 minutes (and a trip to the manager’s office) she “found” our reservation. Apparently the reservation system and the front desk computers do not always communicate well. She admitted that this happens occasionally, but is not the norm- an old computer system was blamed. She was very nice though (as were most of the staff) and gave us a (presumably upgraded) room with a view of Grant Park ( which was a great view!). The room was large with a very high ceiling, tastefully decorated and looked clean and well-maintained. There was a wall mounted flat panel TV that seemed a bit too small (32”?) for this large of a room. There was no desk, but there was a small table that could make do....if one did not mind running internet cable from TV and unplugging coffee maker to plug in computer. The room looked to be recently remodeled, but had not quite been completed , leaving an ancient banged up air conditioning cabinet ( covering a window unit that had a fan control, but no obvious thermostat) and at least one part of trim painted a different color. There was a large walk-in closet with surprisingly little space to hang anything. There were no collapsible luggage racks – just a permanent one built into closet & reducing usable hanger space. The beds were OK, but nowhere near as comfortable those found in Starwood hotels as well as in most Hiltons and Marriotts. There was plenty of hot water and great water pressure. Amenities (soap, shampoo) were minimal and brand-less. There was very little flat space to put anything in the bathroom. It took 20 minutes to get car mid-day even though no one else seemed to be using valet service at the time. I would not recommend staying here unless you can tolerate strike lines, erratic check in and slow car-valet service.... and you could get room for less than about $100/night.

“Everything you are looking for” This hotel is in a good location, it has been recently renovated. The staff is very friendly. It has a good rate. I found it a step up from most Courtyards. The staff is the real difference. I felt welcomed the minute I arrived.

“A great value for money in the heart of Washington” I still can not believe that I got a room in this hotel for as little as 89 dollars without booking trough hotwire or priceline but directly with the property. First of all, the location is excellent since you can walk to many attractions and you can even access a red line metro station directly from the hotel. The lobby is a big interior patio with a kind of pool, next to the restaurant where you can enjoy a nice breakfast buffet. The room was perfectly clean, quiet and well equipped although it had no exceptional feature. We met only very friendly staff, at the front desk or in the breakfast restaurant. We needed two connecting rooms and they managed to meet our request. The only downside of your stay was a dinner at the other restaurant of the hotel which was expensive and... bad. But there are many dining options in the area so it is easy to skip that part. We also ordered sandwiches through the room service: quick and good.

“Decent choice but not great” Our extended family had four rooms here for three nights leading up to Thanksgiving Day. The rooms had older furnishings but pleasant decor. The lighting was somewhat dim, except for the excellent lighting in the sink area (which was separate from the bathroom). There were some noise issues. The interstate traffic sounds like a continual dull roar; it did not keep us awake but would be unsuitable for a light sleeper. The outer doors slammed shut loudly whenever someone went in or out. We occasionally heard an undefinable motor noise, which may have been air conditioning from a nearby room. The fan in the bathroom was also very loud but quite useless. Our room had a large mini-fridge with freezer, as well as a small microwave. The bed and pillows were very comfortable. The shower head was excellent and there was plenty of hot water, though we experienced some temperature variation while showering. The towels were scratchy. Our kids enjoyed the pool and spa. We had a decent continental breakfast each morning that included hard-boiled eggs, waffles, and oatmeal, along with the usual carbs. The hotel is in a good location but the area is heavily congested. Even though the hotel gave us printed directions to various restaurants and points of interest, we still went the wrong way a couple times. I saved $10 per room per night by rechecking the online price of the rooms on the day of our arrival and rebooking. The hotel will charge you extra for the use of the safe in the room unless you tell them at checkout that you didn't use the safe. Our parents had a suite that was roomy enough but had insufficient seating for a group. The hotel would not help us with this problem, so we had to carry in chairs from other rooms. Overall it was a decent place to stay, but I plan to look for something better the next time we're in San Diego.

“Super location, gorgeous hotel” Beautifully renovated hotel in a historic building. Very tasteful decor. Pros: extremely friendly and courteous staff; concierge was especially pleasant and helpful. We were given free internet for our one-night stay. I very much appreciated that we could keep our car parked there after checkout (until 5PM) - that way we could checkout, put our bags in the car (or could have left them with the bellman in the lobby) and grab lunch, shop, etc, without having to find another parking place. Room was spacious and very nicely decorated. Very clean - no complaints at all. Cons: very minor - but - the vending machine on the 16th floor must have been broken as the cold water I thought I was buying came out hot to the touch; more annoying was the fact that when I called the front desk to report it, they did not offer to replace the water with a cold bottle. Also, I didn't like being woken up by yipping dogs in the hall; if they want to accommodate guests with pets, they should keep them together on the same floor(s) and not near rooms without pets. And although we booked under the Philly parking special room deal (parking included in the room rate), there was a line item for parking (on top of the room rate that included parking) on my bill at checkout; the front desk easily took care of it with no hassle other than the short wait in line.

“Good Downtown Business Hotel” I usually stay at the Westin in downtown Denver but wanted to get Marriott points so I stayed here for this business trip and was not disappointed. The hotel is updated, pristine, very business like, has a great concierge level and updated rooms. It is in the heart of downtown Denver and an easy walk to tourist spots as well. I stayed here two nights in a corner, oversized room and would definitely stay here again when in Denver.

“Under Renovation” Like ccrosner, boston, we got a $269 a night suite over the side street and like that reviewer we experienced the early morning garbage pickup. Still, the suite was wonderful and made us feel that we in fact were in a small apartment. Unfortunately, the hotel is undergoing considerable renovation, so the lobby bar, the restaurant, and the fitness center are offline. The temporary fitness center consists of four machines in a stifling, small room. We got a temporary membership at the Washington Sports Club up Connecticut Avenue a block and that was a nightmare, but hardly the hotel’s fault. They offer access to the YMCA which we should have selected. The hotel seems to be missing small things that make a difference. For two days in a row I had to remind the front desk staff, for example, to get paper towels for the men’s restroom off the lobby. Also, the hot water in our room ran out and we had to be relocated. This wasted several hours of our time. I would have thought that the management would have done something in response to this, even a token gesture, but they did not. Clearly, the Mayflower is skipping a few beats while it renovates, but we will come back, but only after the renovations are complete.

“Great place to stay in Downtown Indy with a group” I stayed here for a wedding in Fishers with a group of friends that had never been to Indianapolis prior to this wedding. I suggested we stay downtown and not in Fishers (nothing against Fishers) since there is more to do within walking distance (i.e. no need to worry about designated drivers the night before the wedding). We didn't arrive until 12:40 a.m. and the man working the front desk was very efficient in getting me my keys, etc. for my room. I had already checked-in via the phone since I was originally schedule to arrive eight hours earlier but did not because of a canceled flight from Detroit. So everything was already to go for us to stay on the 16th floor. The room was very nice and the living room and bedroom each have ~32" LCD televisions that do in fact feature HD channels (not just the over-the-air variety (ABC, CBS, NBC, FOX), but your cable channels such as ESPN. This sure helped me from having to find a bar that carried HD channels to watch the FIFA World Cup. Not that its a huge problem to find ABC in HD, but it was nice to have to watch USA/England while getting ready for the wedding. I'm kind of an HD snob... The beds were comfortable and one of my friends insisted on passing out on the couch and claimed it was comfortable (I tried to explain that it does fold out into a bed, he said he was content with the traditional couch-passout method). There is a sink in the bedroom in addition to the sink in the bathroom. The living room features an empty mini-fridge with another sink. The rooms block the sound from the atrium well. You couldn't hear anything from the outside or our neighbors. And hopefully they couldn't hear us while watching the World Cup. The one problem I had with the room was the condition of the bathroom. The sink area was fine, but the tub looked like it was possibly under repair or soon to be under repair. I would disagree with previous reviews of the rooms (as a whole) looking tired because the rest of the room looked like it had recently been renovated... except for the tub/shower area. The exercise room looked nice, but it was small. The business center is free to use (and free printers) and there is a pool as well. You need your room key to access all three. The lobby area is nice and the doorman is more than happy to store your bags for you if need be. The person working the front desk on my last night at 3:30 a.m., was nice to extend check-out for me until 1 p.m.

“Way Exceeded Expectations” I figured this was just going to be a run of the mill conference center style hotel. It is, but it's so much more. My room looked like it was built the day before I got there. It was immaculate and the amenities were great. This is a very eco friendly hotel, but nothing is lost because of it. The staff was amazing. Friendly and helpful from the parking garage ticket taker to the room service delivery guy. Speaking of room service, I got back to my room late one night and got room service. It was one of the most amazing meals I've ever had. I can't say enough about this place. Friendly service, great location, great rooms and amazing food. Loved it.

“Down and up” Visited Seattle recently for a meeting held in the W. When I called to let them know I'd be arriving late (around 10:30 PM), they said no problem, and that parking shouldn't be an issue. However, arriving that late, I was stuck with one of the rooms facing the garage. While the interior of the room was nice, facing the fencing and parking lot made it feel like we were in prison. Also, the bathtub drain was slow/clogged. Very depressing and gloomy. Also, they had run out of parking for the night, so we needed to park in the big garage next door ourselves, which was a hassle that late at night when you just want to check in and go to sleep. It took my asking for a different room after 2 nights (they didn't voluntarily let me know rooms opened up), I got a room now facing the street. Much better. But the early experience with the garage-facing room had already soured me on the place. Really, it would have been better without a window, and just a big picture simulating an outdoor scene or something.

“Great stay, but no free WiFi?” We stayed for two nights. Reception staff was very friendly. We had a corner room on an upperfloor. The view was very nice, as it was a corner room. More windows than walls. The room was spacious, clean and quiet. The bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was big enough and clean as well. We had breakfast twice at the hotel. The breakfast area is bright and nice. Breakfast was good. There is plenty for everyone's need. The valet parking was great. They say it takes about 15 minutes to bring your car, but we never had to wait for more than 5 minutes. So they do a great job. Downtown Houston is very walkable. The hotel is only 6 block away from the theatre district, with lots of fun things to do and nice restaurants. Try Perbacco, a great Italian restaurant on Milam street. There's one thing I didn't like (I knew this before we arrived, so no surprise). No free WiFi. That's not sellable anymore nowadays. We stayed in quite a few hotels on our trip and this one (and the Hilton Skirvin) had no free WiFi. This has to change! It's 2012, everybody "needs" WiFi, it should be a service. Next time we will be staying at this Doubletree again and we will enjoy our free WiFi ;-)

“Not very Grand, not very clean and VERY noisy” I got a GREAT rate on Hyatt's own website of about $89 per night for a weekend. The hotel is located at the Metro Center metro station so that makes it a snap to get around DC. Most of the staff were nice, with the exception of those in the 2 restaurants I used (or attempted to use: no one waited on me after 15 minutes in the sports bar.) My room was an atrium view room but it was really not very clean. Dirt and mold on the vent, smushed bug juice (sorry) on the wall, dusty desk, floor not vacuumed-all in all housekeeping only gave the room a cursory cleaning. At least the sheets were fresh! The other guests were really noisy and doors were slamming all night. Security came to a room near mine and she was SO loud knocking and yelling at 4 AM that I thought she was outside my door. She was VERY rude when I opened the door (she was across the hall). She said "I am TRYING to get the noise to stop.." I said, "then perhaps you can use an inside voice and NOT wake up the whole floor..." She was not even at the right room-the noisy people had continued down the hall. Upon checkout, I complained and the manager said that I was not the first one to bring that up. The staff was pretty nice and assisted me with issues when needed. For instance, after scouring the hotel for a normal soup like chicken or french onion with no success, the manager sent it up to me from room service at no charge. (Of course the room service waiter was rather nasty.) The overall hotel wasn't bad, it just needs some TLC. The room I was in had a ceiling leak repaired and this was not well done, thus it looks bad and there is mold starting to show. I did not use or check out the pool. Internet was a decent speed-again there is a charge but as I have status with Hyatt I did not have to pay. There is a starbucks in the lobby and countless other places to eat within a few blocks walk. The convention center and the verizon center are within just a couple blocks so this property is very convenient for those attending events in either venue. I would go back in the future to give them another chance as many people were helpful, the location is great and the hotel is lovely. I was just very angry that the housekeepers do not pay attention to details like cleaning vents and dusting. It was worth the rate, but frankly it isn't worth much more than 90 bucks a night.
“Better than expected” We got a better than expected stay for a roadside hotel. The linens were good. Breakfast was better than expected.

“Unimpressed” We stayed here for a couple of nights at the end of our roadtrip through California and I have to say we left unimpressed. The lobby looks super-trendy but the rooms are just standard dated American hotel rooms with no frills or charms. In addition we initially got a room on the top floor next to the lift shaft which was so noisy that we almost didn't sleep at all during the night. To be fair, we were promptly given another room when we complained the next day, although it was looking out on a wall. All in all, we were unimpressed, we expected a trendy boutique hotel and all we got was a fancy lobby.

“Not a bad choice, but I was disappointed” I'm a big Kimpton fan, in general, but this was not a great experience. My room here (# 1112) was among the very smallest hotel rooms I've ever stayed in -- about 1/2 the size of a hotel room I just had in Manhattan in NYC two weeks ago. The one window in the room featured a view completely filled with the very close brick wall of the building next door. The hotel did not appear to be anywhere close to full occupancy so I can only guess that my discounted rate (booked directly through hotel - not through 3rd party service) led to my disappointing room assignment. (It was much smaller than the rooms in photos of this property I've seen on Trip Advisor -- scrolled back to fall 2010 in the photo archive. I should have also taken photos of my room for this site but I was there about 18 hours, total, and had a full work agenda) After check-in, I realized that the front desk employee hadn't acknowledged me being an InTouch member (the rewards program for Kimpton). I later stopped by the front desk to ask about the lack of the InTouch mention and perks (e.g., Raid the Minibar card), and for some reason my reservation didn't reflect my membership. This is the second time that's happened at a Kimpton property, but I always make all my reservations on the Kimpton website. I asked the front desk employee if she could please look up my InTouch # and tie it to my reservation, and she said she could not. She was friendly, though, and gave me a Raid the Minibar card. She then told me I could look up the # on my own and then share the info later with front desk. (The lack of the InTouch info in my reservation may be part of the reason why I ended up in such a tiny room, too. Not sure.) The positive parts of the room were that it was completely clean and had lots of lighting options. I like the fresh, hip, fun decor in Kimpton properties and enjoy that each property has its own design approach. The bathroom was also very small, but the shower had great water pressure. Besides the inconsistency with room size (as judged by checking out my room versus the other rooms pictured on this site), there were some other issues. The elevators were extremely slow in the morning. The staff in the attached Kimpton bar/restaurant were inattentive and distant on more than one occasion. Checkout, however, was a great experience, with the front desk employee telling me he actually could look up my InTouch # and tie it to my stay. He promised me he would take care of it, knowing I was off to catch a flight, and he had a great attitude and an efficient, can-do approach. (But I'm not sure why one employee could take care of the InTouch situation while another couldn't.) The next time I'm in Philly, I'll probably try another property instead. It wasn't a horrible experience, but it wasn't one that left me pining to return, either.

“Interesting...!” This is probably the strangest hotel I've ever stayed at....and although I thoroughly enjoyed the experience I probably wouldn't want to repeat the experience. Reception staff varied in friendliness. The room was a decent size for New York, with really nice pieces of furniture, and a lovely long sprig of fresh orchid in a vase on the writing table. Thankfully the bed which was massive and very comfortable was new! Bathroom was clean with nice toiletries and lots of fluffy white towels. The room was warm - but they do seem to have a major problem with their central heating plumbing as it made a huge knocking noise every half-hour or so (all day - all night). As I said - an interesting experience!

“Dark, tiny, but relatively inexpensive” This is a great neighborhood (townhouse a few feet away is on the market for $6mm), a block from Central Park and subways, friendly staff, free (abeit weak) Internet. And if you don't book well in advance, you may not get a better price on a decent hotel in NYC. My family had a room that was bigger than most, and it was tiny, spacious enough to accommodate two beds and a dresser and that's about it. The bathroom is similarly scaled -- kind of like an airplane bathroom but a bit more cramped. I couldn't really see if the room was dirty because it was so dark, the only light coming from an air shaft, but it was definitely on the dingy side. Not enough outlets for all our gadgets (chargers for phones and computers). You could hear your neighbors using the bathroom and talking, and occasionally there were banging noises coming from the air shaft, like a piece of wood hitting something, that kept us awake at night. We also experienced all kinds of problems with the plumbing. (You would not want to share a room with anyone you didn't know real well!) No service elevator, so in the morning you have to suck in your gut and squeeze in tight with the maintenance/service staff and their carts -- we took the stairs, but that's probably not an option if you're on the top floor. Breakfast: ok. My son liked the waffle maker, but it was so gunked up that he could only peel off the pieces. The orange juice was good, but for coffee, you're better off hitting one of the neighborhood java purveyors. I thought I'd be okay staying in a place like this (having read the TA reviews) because it's New York, and you're never in your room, etc etc. And maybe for one night it would have been okay. But longer than that: depressing.

“Excellent stay in a great hotel” We stayed here for 4 nights in August and were thoroughly impressed by the quality of the hotel, the excellence of its staff, and the brilliance of its location. Upon checking in we were allocated a very small but well maintained and presented room. The clerk on the check-in told us the room would be small, which we were expecting, but that he would check us into a bigger room for the last two nights of our stay when the hotel was not full to capacity. This was without any prompting from us and this excellence was pretty much representative of the whole of our stay. Both rooms that we stayed in were lovely, and everyone on the entire staff were super friendly and helpful. The roof terrace afforded great views of the city, and the complimentary coffee and internet PC in this area was also a really nice touch. I really cannot fault this hotel and would recommed anyone travelling to NYC to consider staying here. It's location is brilliant too, nicely situated between mid-town to the north and Greenwich Village/Downtown to the south. If you do stay here, the Lyric Diner (two blocks south from the hotel down 3rd Av) does amazingly tasty and good value breakfasts in a traditional diner style. The total bill including tip for two excellent breakfasts (each consisting of eggs w/ bacon and home fries, fruit cup, toast, coffee and water) was $15, and we really didn't need to eat again until the evening. This is a really exceptional hotel and we will certainly look to stay here again should we be lucky enough to return to NYC.

“GOOD overall but BAD noise problem” The good: large room, food at the restaurants (especially the clam chowder), bed, view from the elevators, service, shuttle every 20 minutes to and from the airport (5 minutes away) The bad: the insulation for the windows is awful, so the hotel is extremely noisy at night (at least if you are facing the airport): airplanes, busy airport boulevard, rooftop with furnaces/chillers etc. No wireless in the rooms. Cheap toiletries, few towels.

“An interesting Westin” Why Westin puts its name on the Essex House remains a mystery to me. It was just so different from your typical Westin. And given the capital Starwood spends on developing its brands, this inconsistency seems rather strange. Unlike the typical Westin, which features contemporary facility and down-to-earth service, Essex House is all about the old New York. In many ways, it reminded me of the Waldorf. The lobby was decorated in a conservative/traditional style, but it lacked the grandeur and scale of the Waldorf or even the run-down Plaza. The room I got was on the small side, and the "Heavenly" amenities were nothing special. Service was quite poor - snobbish staff without the class to back it up. What really bothered me was the fact that this hotel was neither grand nor intimate. The Carlyle and the Mark are small, but they leverage on their size to offer personalized service that creates a home-away-from-home for their guests. The Waldorf and the Plaza go the opposite by impressing you with their grand public spaces. They are all clear about their strengths and weaknesses, and they position themselves accordingly. In this case, the Essex House took the worst of both worlds - impersonal service and unimpressive public spaces. Is this a bad hotel? Absolutely not. But for the rate I paid, I expected much more.

“30+ years of stays.....more than 100 stays” We have been staying at the Olympic for more than 30 years. We've stayed when it was managed by Four Seasons and since it's been managed by Fairmont. We've stayed more than 100 times and love the place. Sure, we have favorite rooms but it's more than the rooms as they don't have that great Seattle view. It's the people......many of whom have been around the whole time. When in Seattle, the Olympic is that only place you should stay.

“Part hotel, part apartment -- a unique place!” Hats off to this developer (who also did XV Beacon) for coming up with this concept. It's midway between a hotel and a rental apartment -- and a LOT more stylish than most hotels or apartments in Boston. As most reviewers have pointed out, you quickly feel like a local. I had a top floor suite and loved the generous windows looking out over St. Botolph Street. In fact, since I was in Boston looking for a property to buy, I immediately added this neighborhood to my wish list -- it was that nice! The kitchenette was well stocked with dishes and cutlery. You probably couldn't cook a three-course meal in it, but it's more than adequate for making breakfast or eating a take-out meal. The bathroom was fairly tight, but since it was new, I didn't mind. There's free wi-fi, and it worked well. And all phone calls within the U.S. are free on your room phone, which I've never seen anywhere else. My flight out of Boston didn't leave until 9:30 pm. I was able to arrange for a 7 p.m. checkout for a very reasonable charge, although I had to move to a basement room since "my" room was no longer available. The office is open until 10 pm, and the staff is very helpful. The lounge is located in the basement, which to be honest, isn't all that inviting because it's dark. But you can use their Nespresso machine to make delicious coffee. I know Boston well, and this inn is unique in the city. If you've ever wondered what it feels like to live in a lovely neighborhood in Boston -- stay here!

“Bare-bones accomodations” I stayed here In early November 2008 for a downtown conference. Just plain old bare-bones accomodations. Clean comfortable room, clean comfy bed. Towels were clean and not too scratchy. Hot water was strong and plentiful. This location offers good value for a downtown location. You can expect to pay a lot less than the locations across the street. There is a hairdryer and iron/ironing board in the room. Continental breakfast served in the office area. Very convenient location . Two blocks from Riverceter Mall, the Alamo, and the Riverwalk. Walk to lots of good eating/shopping places.

“good transit hotel” My wife and I stayed at Radisson Sea-Tac on September 22-23, 2012. It's a perfect transit hotel: very close to the airport (3-min. walk, no need to wait for a shuttle), and 3-5 min. away on foot from the Link train station. It would take about 35-40 min. to get to downtown Seattle from the airport by train. There are also a couple of restaurants around the hotel. Our room was cosy and clean with a sleep number bed and a large LCD tv. Fast internet was free as well. I would highly recommend this hotel, especially if you have an early morning flight out of Seattle.

“Gute Lage, gutes Zimmer” Sehr freundliche Leute am Empfang. Gratis Parkplätze unmittelbar vor dem Haus. Um Convention Center herum etwas spezielle Leute. Daher, wenn man zu Fuss unterwegs ist, besser in Richtung First Avenue gehen, dann Kettner. Lage aber super. Zimmer nicht besonders sauber. An den Frottiertüchern häufig Haare. Auf den Gängen und im Lift sehr schmutzig. Unfreundliches Housekeeping. Preis-Leistung stimmt.

“STILL SO VERY CLASSY” It's an oldie but goodie -- and all dolled up with such San Francisco class. Yes, elevators are a little slow but it gives you more time to remind you, hopefully, you're on vacation. Beds are heavenly! And if you want bragging rights, walk up from the Powell Street BART station. Skip the cab. When you tell everyone what you did, they'll think you are amazing. Just like this hotel. P.S. There is coffee in the lobby and Starbucks is 3 blocks plus down the hill. Remember, what goes down must come up. There's a wonderful coffee and pastry shop just a block down!
“Loved it!” Quaint, affordable, nicely decorated, large, beautiful bathrooms and the windows open. Great restaurant-bar (pricey) and lobby. Overall, a comfortable stay.

“Excellent Service, Average Physical Plant” Great sevice at breakfast, but very plain food. Can't open windows in room. Free WiFi, but a little slow. Very small bathroom. Thin towels. Attentive service in bar in evening. No bell service; must carry bags yourself, and limited number of baggage carts. Nice people at front desk.

“Amazing Stay” This trip was a direct result of me winning a Glee-inspired contest at my job, where the grand prize was a weekend trip to stay in Manhattan at this luxury hotel. I had an amazing time. Most of the front desk and restaurant staff look like magazine models - which was a nice touch. Besides their gorgeous appearance, the service everyone provided was top notch. The staff used my name on almost every contact, and always delivered service with a smile when I was face-to-face with them. I was upgraded upon check-in to the top floor (36th), which not only padded my Platinum status-sized ego, it also gave me breathtaking views of the most beautiful concrete jungle in the world. Guest services also gave me a late check-out at 2pm at no cost- which saved me $75. The hotel is very close to a subway station and only a block or two from actual Times Square - so I could not have been in a more convenient location. I would heartily recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to be treated especially nice and made to feel like they are king of world.

“Stopover” This is the second time I have stayed at this hotel. This hotel is extremely comfortable and clean. Staff very friendly and complementary wifi a bonus. A fantastic addition since the last time we stayed is they now have a indoor walking route to the hotel from the airport, this is so much better no need to get a transfare and you can go at your own pace. We had a wheelchair room which we found to be very accessible. I would deffinately stay here again, is not too far from nice restaurants in Boston, we met friends and went to dinner in the Little Italy district which was only about 20 mins away. The hotel bar is very nice and breakfast for an added cost was also very pleasant.

“You will like this one!” I know this hotel has won a Trip Adviser award but it still amazed me! Outstanding in every respect, but the location was the best bit. Lovely spot directly on the water, with nice walks in all directions. Close to a good food supermarket, about five minutes drive away so you can buy and cook food if you want to. But good restaurants within a couple of hundred yards too. Check out the outdoor terrace on third floor of South building. We sat out there for sunset and to watch planes land ... It also has a lovely view of downtown and lights sparkling across the water! Would definitely recommend both for business travellers and families.

“Nice boutique hotel but missing the details” The Redbury is a nice boutique hotel right in Hollywood. I stayed in a Highland Flat, which was very spacious. The room had a full kitchen, a living room with a couch and two chairs, the bedroom, and a nice bathroom. The shower is huge with a rainfall shower head. The room itself was great but it was the small details that were irritating. The room had gnats in it, enough that it was bothersome. Not sure where they came from but definitely not something I want in my room. The other thing I noticed was the room could have been cleaned better. I realize this is me being very picky but you would think the room would be spotless since it's cleaned everyday. Even with the few negatives I would come back. The size of the room is great for what you pay.

“Comfortable and Convenient” My husband and I took my cousin's family for a weekend trip to DC and decided to stay at the River Inn for its proximity to a metro station and the fact that I got a good rate for a suite hotel. Check in was quick and efficient. Because we were staying for the weekend, the friendly check-in clerk told us that if we are able to find it, there are no restrictions for side street parking on the weekend, saving us the $30/day valet parking fee. We booked two rooms, one for each family, and the space was more than enough. The queen sized bed and sofa bed was comfortable for my cousin and his family. The room decor was pretty modern, in neutral tones. The bathroom had a low bathtub, so I didn't feel it'd be too comfortable for a soak. The little kitchen was sufficient to heat up food for simple meals. The single door fridge reminded me of the fridge in my first apartment, with a single cubicle for a freezer. Location-wise, it was two blocks away from the Foggy Bottom-GWU metro (right in front of the GWU hospital) and we took it to go to the Smithsonian. I meant to check out the Trader Joe's, but we didn't have time, but there was a 7-11 on the way to the metro station to grab a bottle of water. The only disappointment that I had was that their "24-hour fitness center" was a tiny room with a broken TV, a treadmill, an elliptical machine, and a stationary bike. There was also a door leading to a gutted room (that is probably the beginnings of a sauna?), which wasn't very attractive. I did use the filtered water machine in there though. Also, housekeeping seemed to be shortstaffed, as our room wasn't refreshed when we stopped by our room at 2pm, but that's not too big a deal for us. I didn't try the Dish Restaurant because it seemed a bit pricey (but the Ethiopian food in DC is great.!), though my husband did have a cup of coffee there the morning we left and had nothing bad to say about it. I would probably seek to see what type of rate I'd get here the next time I plan a trip to DC. If it is comparable to what I paid for this time, I wouldn't hesitate to book.

“Nice but Older” This hotel is located in the heart of Phoenix and is just a stones throw from the Phoenix Airport, even though you are that close you do not hear that planes at all. The property is a good value but is dated somewhat, and the room we stayed in had a musky smoke oder to it, as though the room had been a smoking room at some point in the past. The free breakfast was alright, but if there is a long line, I would skip it. The staff was very helpful, and even let me check in before 12 noon, and gave me a choice of rooms on the property. If you are not into kids stay away from the rooms that are near the pool as it gets loud. There are several restaurants located close by just north on 44th St. (Moes, IHop, Grill Next Door (burger joint), Slotsky's Deli, etc)

“Great high class, swanky hotel; could offer more free amenities” Spent two nights here with my wife. Very modern and high class hotel. We got our reservation via priceline. Check in was fast and easy. We had room 2101. Room was very modern. There was a desk area and a sofa chair. Desk area could use more electrical outlets. Had to move the desk to get to a free outlet to connect my laptop. Also found the desk chair to be very uncomfortable. King size bed was a little on the firm side for me, but still comfortable. The room did not offer any free wifi or wired internet. The room also didn't have a mini-fridge. You could have one sent up for an additional fee. Ice machines are not on each floor. The room had a safe where you could store your laptop and other valuables. There are many food options located within walking distance. There is a Ruth Chris steak house located in the lobby of the hotel. There is a also a sushi place located around the corner (accessible via hotel lobby), as well as a Cheesecake Factory. Valet parking costs $39. Lots of high class amenities such as a visual light do not disturb sign, motorized curtains, alarm clock with ipod dock. Bathroom was very big, with stand up shower and bathtub. Would definitely stay here again, for a good price. Wished hotel offered more free amenities such as free wifi.

“A Good Place to Stay” I was a guest at the Sea-Tac Embassy Suites for a work-related meeting in October 2004. This is an older property and for the most part, the place has been well-maintained. The carpet was stained in places and there were some off-odors prevalent in parts of the hotel, however, the staff was friendly and the customary amenities were of their usual high Embassy Suites quality. The breakfast and bar area was being remodeled during the time of my visit but the hotel had planned the project through and kept up with demand. The hotel shuttle took me and a co-worker to an off-site meeting location during one day of my stay. They will take you to, and/or pick you up from, any location within a 5-mile radius of the property. There are plenty of higher-end eating venues within a few miles of the hotel, but not much within walking distance. The Interurban Trail is accessible right out the back door, a plus for runners and bikers (paved bituminous asphalt surface). Wireless high speed internet access was available in the room for $10 a day. This was a clean, quiet place and I would stay here again.

“Satisfied, Great Price” I stayed at this hotel for only $28 a night through Priceline. I think I got a great deal. The hotel was easy to find for someone who had never been to Phoenix before. The room came with a fully equipped kitchen, sofa, tv with remote, two beds, and all the other usual ammenities. The carpet and sofa showed their age, but were acceptable nonetheless. You can get a pass to use a fitness center, but we didn't have the time. We went in the winter time, so we didn't use the pool. The staff was friendly. The free breakfast wasn't as good as it could have been. There was plenty of parking and if there aren't enough spots, there's more parking right next door at the restaurant. The seafood restaurant next door was great. Overall, I was satisifed and would stay there again if I were on a budget.

“Will be perfect once construction is complete!” First, this hotel sits right on top of a metro station--the red line. We had no trouble getting to the Mall daily. You will have to allow time to transfer to another line at either the Metro or Gallery Place stations. And bear in mind the trains run with varied frequency. It took us about 20-30 minutes to get to the Mall, depending on train wait times. This hotel is part of a shopping mall type complex and there is a Cheesecake Factory and a Maggiano's on premise. Right out the front door we found P,F. Chang's and other great eateries. This was great! Much of the downtown, National Mall area seems to be short on places to eat apart from the cafes inside the Smithsonian museums (which we found to vary greatly--Natural History cafe was the best we experienced.) Room at the Embassy are great--true suites with a closing bedroom door giving real privacy. Nice kitchen bar area with a sink and small refrigerator. All rooms open onto an atrium for a balcony feel which will be great once work is done. At the time of our visit, this was being worked on and had a huge tarp covering most of it---and was not air conditioned. The breakfast and manager's happy hour are served on floor 3 on this open air atrium balcony. It was quite hot in D.C. during our trip and we found the atrium to be uncomfortable--humid and about 80+ degrees. Again, it was still a good experience. Ben at the front desk was an amazing concierge. Just beware that for the next few months the renovations will be an issue. Note, too, the pool area is completely enclosed. Small, but nice. However, it's all tile in that area. We went when small kids were there and could hardly take the echo effect. That area is only pleasant when it's unpopulated.

“Love the Stockyards!” If you are looking for a great place to stay while visiting the Stockyards, this hotel is for you. You feel as if you have stepped into a different time. This hotel has a lot of history. It has been there since 1937. It has managed to keep all of the charm while being a nice place to stay for the modern traveler. It is smack in the middle of the Stockyards area which makes is very convenient to everything. Billy Bob's (a very large must see bar) is a very short stroll as are all of the popular restaurants and shops. I would recommend getting a suite. They are not that much more than the normal rooms. Ours was 189 a night over a holiday weekend and was very nice. We had the "cowboy corner" suite.I peeked in on the normal rooms and they seemed quite small. You will definately feel as if you have visited Texas after staying here. Everything is very Old West at this place. But, again, it is very nice. Highly recommend!

“great location great value” I find it really hard to understand any of the negative reviews for this hotel. The Inn of Chicago is a decent three star hotel. However, I have given it an extra star for its location (one block off the Magnificent Mile) and an additional star for the price which was far under $100 per night. You can't come anywhere close to that price for a hotel in downtown Chicago. The rooftop terrace is a gret place for a drink or a picnic - the view is great. The rooms are average, not too big, but clean and comfortable which is all we needed. If you want a room to lounge around in and lovely hotel facilities like pools etc then you are going to have to spend over $200 a night. For us the Inn of Chicago was the best choice

“Well worth it....if you get a good price!” An impressive lobby and good service from staff at the reception and front door when you arrive. Rooms are a good size and well equipped - no concerns over shabby rooms at all. The hotel has a good bar (although expensive) and business facilities. Rooms are comfortable, quiet and have good (and not noisy!) air conditioning. Would recommend this BUT look out for good offers as otherwise could be pricey.

“Hip boutique hotel” The website does this W hotel a disservice. We were afraid we were going to find a golf focused country club themed property. Instead we found a very modern boutique hotel that happens to be next to a golf course. Pet friendly, green (reserved spaces for hybrids and parking spots with chargers for electric vehicles), with the kind of modern style usually found only in new hotels in major cities. Very friendly service. Room was of average size and very nicely appointed. Only complaint is plastic cups--not what we expect at this level of style and at this price.

“Wonderful experience!” Booked with a nearby convention. Beautiful lobby and grounds, large beautiful room (3rd floor corner room), great restaurants and bars, quiet despite large crowds, plentiful staff who were helpful and friendly, cab service available, easy access to tollroad to Galleria, convenient parking. Not perfect - couldn't get king bed, a/c in room didn't cool very well (a friend on the 7th floor said she froze), expensive food, no maid service (did immediately bring up clean towels when requested). Overall a great experience - I've never stayed at a perfect hotel.

“Great East location” This was the second time I stayed at this Affinia. The location is wonderful for walking north or south and across to 5th Ave. The big beds are very comfortable and the new bathrooms very stylish. I think Affinia Hotels are a good bet when going to NYC.

“Great Hotel - Great Location” We stayed at the Crown Plaza Times Square on a Priceline bid. We got a great deal!! However, after my bid was accepted, I read the reviews and was a little worried, but I should not have been worried. Our room was on the 29th floor and it was very nice with a view of Times Square. I was traveling with my son, so we got a room with two double beds. The room was quite large by NYC standards. The room was updated (much better than either of the two Sheratons that are near by) and clean. Everyting was in working order (although the room was a little warm, but not too bad). Check-in was fast. We arrived early and our room was not ready. The front desk handled all the paperwork and when we returned all we had to do was show a photo ID. I used the health club one morning. It is a very impressive club. There is no fee if you are a member of the Priority Club (Crown Plaza's reward program. Would stay here again any time. We loved it.

“Bad night sleep” Let me just start by stating that I have stayed in over 15 hotels in Boston, therefore I am a pretty good judge of quality. The hotel is in a great location to see a Red Sox game, but not close to Faneil Hall or the waterfront. The staff was very nice and they have a couple great bar/restaurants connected to the hotel. The room was clean, and large with a separate sitting area and tv. But the bed was horrible!!!! It was so bad that my husband slept on the floor. We complained when we checked out and were told that the next time we stay there they will put a piece of plywood under the mattress... Are you kidding me! How about buying new mattresses, because the one is room 332 felt like it was 50 years old. It's a shame because everything else was good, but when I pay $300 per night I expect a good night sleep.

“Nice hotel for business travelers” The Amalfi is centrally located in Chicago, has an Italan motif to it, and is very well run. The guest rooms are appealing, clean and of adequate size. The bathrooms are spacious and clean. Every staff member was friendly and helpful. The hotel has a nice and convenient touch every morning by setting up a Continental breakfast buffet at a long table near the elevators on every floor for the guests to serve themselves and take their breakfast back to their rooms. My stay was not cheap by any standard on the week I travelled, but the Amalfi was a pleasant experience overall.

“So kann man eine Panne schön ausbaden” Ich melde mich mit einem Hotel aus Los Angelos. Das Hotel haben wir nur bekommen, weil wir den Weiterflug zum Pazifik versäumt haben. Eigentlich hat die Fluggesellschaft gesagt, wir sollen uns eines aussuchen und dann die Rechnung einschicken. Ich plädierte gleich für das Hilton LAX, weil wir das schon kannte. Wir holten unsere Koffer von der Gepäcksabholung und begaben uns nach draußen. Nach 15 Minuten kam der Hotelshuttle mit der gelben Einblendung Hilton LAX. Es war dann schon 23:30, als wir im Hilton ankamen. Das dauerte so 10 Minuten, da der Shuttle alle 8 Terminals abklappert. Das Hilton hatte eine dreifache Glastür und links und rechts lauerten zwei Marmorlöwen. Beim Check-in verlange ich eine Rechnung auf die Adresse der Fluggesellschaft. Nachher hatte ich dann Mühe, dass ich Hiltonpunkte für das Hotel bekomme, aber es klappte. Ich zahlte 99 Dollar für die Nacht für das Zimmer und fürs das Frühstück nochmals 30 Dollar. Die Lobby umspannte zwei Etagen. Ich fand den Lüster und den großen Teppich sehr schön. Als Blumenfan natürlich ebenso die Vase, mit den roten Strelizien. Die Sessel waren auf antik gemacht Eine interessante Lobby. Das Zimmer war nicht so wahnsinnig groß. Das Queensizebett ebenso wenig übermäßig breit. Dafür fanden doch noch 4 Pölster und eine Nackenrolle auf ihm Platz. Das braune Nachtkästchen hatte 2 Laden und eine Lampe. In der Ecke beim Fenster war noch ein Fauteuil. Das habe ich nicht mehr getestet, weil es schon spät war. Ich legte meine Unterlagen auf die Glasplatte des Schreibtisch, schaltete die Tischlampe ein und nahm kurz auf dem Bürosessel statt. Im Spiegel sah ich, dass ich von der Odysee schon geschafft war. Ich schaltete noch kurz den TV ein, während ich im kleinen Bad noch die Abendhygiene machte, Das hatte einen Marmor Waschtisch mit Spiegel und eine Wanne mit Duschvorhang. Das Bad war sauber. Am nächsten Morgen warf ich einen Blick auf die Zimmernummer: 7058. Das Frühstück entschädigte für alles. Es gab auf Eis eine Saftbar mit Obst und Obstsalaten. 8 verschiedene warme Gerichte. Wir aßen Egg Benedict. Ich wollte ein großes Baguette dafür aufschneiden, das war aber nur Dekoration. Die Tische waren so angeordnet, dass es Zweier und Vierertische gab. Dann noch 2 Sessel an einem Tisch und eine Sitzbank auf der anderen Seite. Dazwischen viele Blumen und Pflanzen, ich liebe es. Zur Nachspeise nahm ich Croissant und Kaffee. Ich kann endlos Gerichte aufzählen. Die ganze Hiltonpalette da. Anschließend fuhren wir mit dem Shuttle zum LAX

“Very disappointing” 4 star lobby, 3 star rooms. I took 2 lukewarm showers there, the TV was older than I am, and the room was so small my thigh is black & blue from where I kept hitting the chair because the room was so small. Staff were all very nice, but maintenance never showed up to deal with the lack of warm water. When they eventually did in the morning they explained that it's an old building & it is what it is. The woman at the front desk had the initiative to bring over the manager when I told her I was very disappointed with my stay. She had the courtesy to remove the bill for my internet usage. Still, two lukewarm showers in a 4 star hotel?

“Disorganized but not all bad.” We booked this last minute as a park and fly deal. The room was only $59 for the night which I thought with the shuttle and free parking was a steal. The rooms here are coming along. The place is under a remodel so I didn't expect much. It has potential to be a nice hotel but its going to need some pep talks here and there. The front desk was unorganized. They didnt even know if our room was clean or not. The front desk girl was on her cell phone. The biggest draw back staying here was the beds. The ad makes is sound like select comfort sleep number beds, Thats not in every room. Ours sure didnt have one. We slept on a sheet of plywood that night. At least thats what it felt like. Other than that its all you should expect from a $59.00 stay.

“A wonderful place for families” Just returned from a comfortable stay at the Crowne Plaza Silversmith. The location was exceptionally convenient, the staff was attentive and friendly, and the room was spotless. The blue line from O'Hare is 2 blocks away, all other lines are either out the front door or 1 black away, and there's a free green trolley(to the Aquarium) stop about 2 blocks away. Our executive floor room well-suited our family's needs with a large granite bathroom, a small breakfast buffet, and a refrigerator. In the lounge, available to all guests is a basket of apples and oranges, morning coffee, and on Monday-Thurs. there is evening dessert. The decor is tasteful and understated. Our only complaint was that our room faced a tall brick wall, so that we had no view, and the natural lighting was limited. But really, we weren't in the room much, so it wasn't a big deal. We would definitely stay there again.

“Fantastic Stay!” We had a wonderful stay at this hotel. The rooms are a nice size for New York and the staff was very helpful. The concierge really made our trip, they gave us directions on the subway and recommendations for places to eat. They really made our trip. We were very impressed with the level of service we were provided. I am a Silver VIP with Marriott and another hotel chain and I was treated with a high level of respect. We will stay here again. It is also in a great area, there were lots of places to eat around the hotel that were very affordable. The pizza around the hotel was what you would expect from New York. Also it is one block from Century 21. We have stayed at other places in the city and this is our favorite.

“Getting better.” I've stayed here several times over the last 3 years and I felt I had to hang in there as Marriott s usually shine and this one was just OK. I laways liked it's location as it's easy to walk downtown within 10 minutes, I could walk tio the U street shops/restaurants, Whole Foods is only a few blocks away and Dupont Circle is a 10 minute walk. Well.... they redid the lobby and it's beautiful. Light, feel very open, ultra clean, private booths in the lobby w/ TV 's or work and to meet friends and it's all good. Modest size rooms that have that nice Marriott touch and are always clean. i guess it was the new Lobby that impressed me but now a real charmer , good restaurant off lobby that was packed at Happy Hour and just a real pleasant stay.

“Nice Place - Would Stay Here Again” I saved ten dollars a night by booking through the hotel's site instead of Expedia. If you have a car -- or are willing to take the frequent buses that stop just a block away -- this is a nice place to stay while exploring Seattle (but not exploring it for the first time -- you will not be in the main, downtown area). The kitchenette with microwave is great for saving money (Safeway is a half block away and a fancy gourmet store is two blocks further). This lower Queen Anne neighborhood also has some nice coffee shops and restaurants. Best bet -- if you are attending a show at the Key Arena, this location can not be beat. You are just steps from the arena.

“Good for business travellers but mostly campus and hospitol visitors.” This Marriott is for a traveler who is visiting someone on the Georgetown campus or have business on campus or a long-term hospital visitor. The service was good, there was a bellhop that was VERY friendly and I didn’t get the impression he was bucking for a big tip, (and I can spot that a mile away because I hate it). Also the room service personnel were polite. Housekeeping was very polite but not very detailed. When I checked under my bed before checking out I noticed trash I knew was there since the first night we got there. There was obvious trash left on the floor. They did clean the bathroom well but dropped the ball in the living area. The rooms did not have enough seating. The room was small (like most rooms in DC and in other cities), but I expected to have a chair, beside the desk chair to sit in. Very comfortable beds and I have a particular back. The hotel is not near any of the Washington attractions or shopping but the shuttle buses are very convenient. They will take you to metro stops. The entire neighborhood of Georgetown is not part of the metro system so shuttles and buses are the way to get around, (I never recommend taxis in DC it’s one city where I recommend to avoid them). There is a little kind of food court on one side of the hotel where college students, hotel guest and staff from the hospital eat. But if you are a late night eater do not depend on these places to eat.

“Another excellent TA suggestion” I chose this hotel for our vacation based on the reviews I read here, and this ended up being perfect for us (DH, me, and our 2 year old son). The location was perfect--we could go just about anywhere we wanted to go in 20 minutes (La Jolla, Zoo, Coronado) and the neighborhood was nice and quiet. We took several walks along the water and felt safe the entire time. What blew me away, though, were all of the complimentary little touches--breakfast every day, dinner available almost every night, free parking (!), free wifi--things that many other hotels charge for. They served beer and wine with dinner, and I loved how they included a different local microbrew every week (the week we stayed they featured Stone Levitation). We were upgraded at no charge from a studio to a 2 bedroom suite, which was quite roomy. Since we were there in October (low season), my guess is that the hotel was only about a quarter full. We were put in one of the "dreaded" corner rooms (166), and didn't have any problems with it--we just had to keep the blinds closed as to not put on a show for passers-by. The extra space was great. The grounds are lovely and include multiple outdoor fireplaces and nice landscaping. There were only two things that I didn't love, but they were relatively minor: we could occasionally hear our upstairs neighbor stomping around, and on occasion the tv channels were scrambled, presumably from the satellite tv reception. Neither was a huge deal. I highly recommend this for families. We'll be back!

“It's average” I stayed here for only one night in January while attending a trade show at the convention center. Because I booked with the trade show group, they put me (and I assume everyone else associated with it) in their Tower building which is actually across the street from the main building. The rooms have been renovated within the last few years, but you can tell it's an old building. The room itself was a normal size for a standard king. The bathroom, though, was TINY! Unfortunately you couldn't open the windows in the room (really... not even a crack?) which is always a bummer at a hotel when you want some fresh air! The internet was, luckily, free (as a perk from the trade show) but as usual at a hotel... it was slow. I ate at the Irish pub downstairs for dinner and it was very mediocre with very slow service. I ate breakfast at the hotel's restaurant. The buffet was $15 and it's typical hotel breakfast food. The staff was nice... I'm only basing my entire review on one night, but I'd say it's an average place. If you get a good deal on this hotel, book it.

“Stay here for the view of the bay and proximity to airport - otherwise not special at all.” When the reservations were made (one night only for a business trip), I had this Hilton confused with the Bayfront Hilton. Bayfront is relatively new, 30 stories, luxurious, right on the Bay but walking distance to Gaslamp District and lots of restaurants/bars. About 15-20 minutes from the airport. I thought I was staying there...until I realized the directions to Harbor Island was the opposite direction from Bayfront (you can see Bayfront from the airport). Alas, the Harbor Island Hilton was fine. It is a typical average, basic Hilton. It's a bit shopworn, but not horrible. The room was clean and well functioning, and the staff was friendly. It is 5 minutes from the airport. I had a room on the top floor (8th floor?), with a small balcony and beautiful view of the bay. This hotel is NOT walking distance to anything (other than the beautiful shoreline) - but a drive into town is only 20 minutes or so. The price was MUCH cheaper than Bayfront Hilton - so that's a plus.

“Excellent value at the Michelangelo” We stayed at The Michelangelo for three nights, June 2-4, 2006, and had a lovely visit. Our room was large by NYC standards, clean and quiet. All of the amenities were up to snuff, the shower and tub were wonderful, and for $250/night in midtown Manhattan we felt we got a bargain. The only complaint was the housekeeping staff didn't stock our room with the advertised Bulgari toiletries...but they may do that at turn down and we kept the "do not disturb" sign on our door in the evenings. The location was ideal, we felt, due to its proximity to Times Square and the Theater District, two subway lines, MoMA, Fifth Avenue, and Central Park - not to mention the steady stream of taxicabs. We never had to wait for a cab and would pass other hotels where people were waiting. The complimentary breakfast was good, about what I expected. I had read on TripAdvisor that the staff was nasty about guests taking coffee and pastries up to their rooms, but I never saw that. One caveat - I don't feel they should advertise that they're offering capuccino when, in fact, they are merely ladling frothy steam milk onto a regular cup of coffee. The best thing, however, about the Michelangelo is James the concierge. He found us fourth-row-center tickets to Spamalot (Katherina McPhee of American Idol was sitting behind us), arranged for our transportation to the airport, gave us free passes to two nightclubs (Crobar and Pasha) and made sure the champagne on arrival in our room was the right bottle and nicely chilled. James alone is worth staying at this hotel. The staff is helpful and accommodating without being obtrusive. We would definitely stay here again, especially at this rate!

“Fabulous time - will definitely return!” We had a fabulous time at Westin in Philadelphia. This was a suggestion from a close friend who stayed there a few months ago. The location is amazing, a few blocks from Rittenhouse Square, shopping, restaurants, etc. It's even connected to a mall (Shops at Liberty Place). We parked underneath the mall for a whopping $33 A NIGHT. Damn. But it is a city. The entrance to the Westin from the mall is kind of weird and I thought it was a little hidden. Check in was seamless. We even got late checkout upon request. I am a SPG member, but I'm not sure if that made a difference? The employees were very nice, helpful, and welcoming. I wish we hung out downstairs a little bit more - it's very old school with couches and nice chairs in front of a fireplace. There's a restaurant too, but we didn't eat there or even look at the menu. The beds are LOVELY here - SO comfortable. All the other reviewers were absolutely right... heavenly bed! There was a double showerhead in the bathroom also - WOW. I want one in my bathroom now. The room was very clean and large. The TV was a flatscreen which I thought was a nice touch, like another reviewer said. We ran out of coffee and called down to see if we could come downstairs to get some, but they insisted on bringing it up. However, it took them over 30 minutes to do so. We called again and they came up almost instantly. Again, we had a great time and would definitely return!

“Sub-par Service; Sub-par Hotel” This hotel could do A LOT of things better. We encountered many problems over the course of our stay: 1) The shower did not drain properly, even after an engineer "fixed the problem." The drain simply could not handle the flow from the second shower head. So much for a heavenly shower. 2) The sound-proofing on the plumbing was abysmal. We could hear ALL the bathroom activities of the occupants above our room, which commenced very early in the morning. So much for a heavenly rest in their heavenly beds. 3) Service at one of the hotel restaurants, Bar 10, was terrible. No one even attempted to seat us and there were food remnants on the seats in the booths and all over the table. Moreover, the furniture looked worn. We ended up leaving, so we can't report on the food. 4) Our room was not made up until 330pm on Saturday. After a full morning and early afternoon sightseeing, we came back to a still dirty room with no clean towels. This is unacceptable. The pool area is quite small, with very limited seating. The gym, however, is spacious and well-equipped. The rooms are relatively large, though plainly outfitted, with no real sense of style and the bathroom was quite small, given the size of the room. All of this would be semi-acceptable at Holiday Inn prices, but this hotel charges a lot of money for their rooms. I got a special rate of $240 a night--the website and other sources had been quoting $329 per night. At those prices, you could stay at the Four Seasons (Weekend Rates), or many of the other hotels in the Back Bay, which I would highly recommend. This a convention hotel, through and through, not a luxury weekend hotel. The only saving grace of this hotel, if there is one, is its location. The hotel is located close to Newbury Street, Back Bay Station, the Public Garden, and so on. That said, there are many other hotels in the Back Bay, and many that are basically in the same location as the Westin. I would recommend searching around and avoiding this hotel, unless you can get a really good deal.

“Great location, good quality large hotel” We had a 5 night stay with 2 rooms on 16th floor of the North Tower with both a ( partial) harbour view and a city view. Check in late on a wednesday evening was a quiet pleasant experience, but seeing the long lines of a Thursday Friday and Saturday afternoon check in made me glad we arrived mid week. The rooms are spacious and Marriott standard which means perfectly clean and comfortable. Elevators took forever over the weekend but I suppose that's inevitable with a busy hotel. We used the DW restaurant for 2 meals and found it perfectly acceptable and reasonably priced, Starbucks in the lobby area was always busy and the free wifi in the surrounding area attracted lots of holidaymakers as well as conventioneers. The hotel wifi available in the rooms and elsewhere in the hotel is payable but I wouldn't bother as free wifi is everywhere outside of the room/hotel. The new pool area is nice although too busy over the weekend so we avoided it. Great location for the marina and city, and although trains do pass by frequently, they weren't disruptive to us on the 16 th floor. Overall a good hotel and a good sta.

“Lovely Hotel in SW Charlotte” Stayed at the Hilton Garden inn in Ayrsley for one night while visiting area. Located in a small but growing shopping/dining center within 10 minutes of the airport. Staff was friendly and quick at check-in. Room was standard HGI. Comfortable, clean. Overlooked a/c and roof but not there for view. Dining options within walking distance was very nice. Dined at Red Lion.

“Even I felt cool at Hard Rock San Diego” This is a review based on my one night business stay at the Hard Rock. As I always do I have broken my review down into the Great, Good, Bad, and Ugly. I will also offer some bottom line-type comments. Ready? Here goes . . . GREAT * DESIGN - okay, the design environment of the Hard Rock San Diego (henceforth referred to as HRSD) is very 'manufactured' and we know it but this hotel is an excellent mix of chic and sophistication where business people, partiers, and vacationers blend seemlessly - nobody feeling out of place. I loved the giant screen backdrop to the registration counters as well as the unique design of the rooms - backlit trim and unique furniture and bar designs help make an otherwise standard footprint room unique. This holds true to the rest of the building and common areas as well - dramatic lighting, 3D prominent song lyric quotes, and eclectic design all mean that you will remember the HRSD long after your stay. * LOCATION - Whether you are in town for a trade show or to have fun, go ahead . . . just TRY to top this location. The hotel is just across the street from the convention center on one side, and almost under the iconic arch that signals the beginning of the gaslamp main drag on the other. And to yet another side . . . you are a pop fly's distance from Petco Park. GOOD * TEMPERATURE / SOUND - I mentioned the unique design of the rooms. But, that's not all. I found the room temperature controls to be excellent while running more quietly than most. And . . . I had to unfortunately participate in an impromtu conference call from my room in the early a.m. and found the room to be highly sound proof. I didn't hear toilets or TVs from other rooms and nobody had to hear me talking about TPS reports and mission statements from their room. * SHOWER - The shower was fantastic with two dual-angle shower heads. Use either or both. * SERVICE - As noted, the hotel's chic design is all very manufactured. But, the HRSD is NOT just a mediocre hotel dressed up with a 'gimmick' . . . I still found this to be a highly effective business class hotel with excellent service, friendly staff, and a great business center. And, you won't feel 'price gouged' here either. They offer free internet access in-room and in the business center - this really saved me with that conference call I had to take part in. BAD (room for improvement) * ACCESS - The check in / out times of 4 pm / 11 am seem a tad restrictive to a HRSD guest who may be just trying to enjoy a few days of leisure. In most cases where I encounter late check-in times, I have been able to check in early but that was not the case at the HRSD - and it looked like they were far from booked in-full. The front desk person(s) did offer to call me via cell when they had a room ready so this may have been an isolated incident. * LIGHTING - While the room's illumination options are multiple - and very cool - even with all going to once you may find the room poorly lit at night. They do offer a cool bed backboard flexible snake light for late reading. UGLY * Based on the great location at the foot of the gaslamp district you may hear some drunken revelry and the occasional crackling police p.a. in the small hours. Of course, if you're one of those drunken revelers this shouldn't bother you. BOTTOM LINE * You will not regret your decision to stay at the HRSD - the overwhelmingly positive reviews here in a negative world speak volumes. * As a guitar player, I love to see all of those artist-signed and used axes. That and the hotel stylings make the HRSD a nice departure from the hotel norm. * The most important hotel review question is this - "in a similar circumstance, would I stay there again?" - that is an easy 'yes' for me. Feel free to contact me with any Q's

“Disappointing Stay in Seattle” Nothing fancy, in fact a bit cramped, not well laid out and located out of the way. Definitely not a walking destination to/from downtown or the seattle center. Was disappointing for a Marriott product.

“There Are Better in This Class of Hotel” I spent a week here due to business. The parking is all valet and it costs $19.00 a day. No self parking is available. We stayed on the 11th floor which is one lower than the top floor. When we walked in the room, it was freezing and the heater didn't appear to work. I kid you not, we had to get under the covers and huddle together to stay warm. I was with my girlfriend so that wasn't so bad. Eventually, the hotel had a space heater delivered and after a few hours, the room temperature became bearable. The hotel employee stated there wasn't any heat as the air conditioner is water chilled. After getting the room to a temperature that was bearable, it wasn't a problem from that point on. I asked others in the hotel if their room was like a meat locker when they checked in and they are stated it was so be prepared for a shock to your system when you walk in the door upon check-in. The bathroom looks very nice due to the granite tile in the shower, the black counter, the three way mirror but the tub isn't very wide and you are cramped. There isn't a fan in the bathroom either so the steam doesn't have anywhere to escape. It's one of the smallest bathrooms I have seen. The bed is a Temperpedic which is a foam bed. It doesn't have coils and springs so it really has a different feel to it. I would rather have a good pillow top bed myself but to each their own. The TV is probably a 27 or 30 inch. Some of the channels are very loud so beware when changing channels. The restaurant on the second level is pretty expensive. Expect to pay about about $20.00 per plate. Don't expect to walk out the door at night and get something to eat as there is nothing like that around. However, there are places just a few blocks away that are in easy driving distance. All in all, it's not a terrible place but there are so many other better choices in Houston in the same price range, it's hard to recommend it.

“Excellent, very clean” We stayed from Oct 15th - Oct 18th , we had a loft room for about $185 night, i think thats a great rate for mid October in Manhattan, i had cheked other hotels and they were very pricey. Location was good, whenever i make it back i'd like to stay midtown, there is a lot around tribeca, restaurants and small bars, but i like the excitement of midtown. Mudville saloon 9 across from Cosmo is fun bar and also a bar called Antartica on Hudson st was a lot of fun too. I liked Hudson st, we walked up and down it a lot. The hotel was extremely clean and the housekeeping was very nice, i was using sun silk shampoo and conditioner, and she must have noticed that because the next morning she left me samples of all the different sun silk products they have, and left a mini deodarant. Front desk was o.k, we had a room facing the street 2nd floor and yes it was noisy, but it is Manhattan and i kind of liked all the street noises, really didn't bother me. Room was fun, really liked the loft room, very cute. Greenwich village was one of my favorites and you can walk there very easily from the hotel. Overall had a great stay and if we wanted to be around downtown again, then this is a perfect hotel.No complaints.

“I love the hills” This was my first trip to San Francisco, after 1 afternoon spent a few years ago. I got a really good deal through IC hotels website. I was meeting some family for the weekend, who live in the South. I was really concerned how they would do in the "big city". Traveling from the Bart stop to the hotel was a little sketchy; my mom was stopped by the homeless people standing around trying to "guide you" for a fee, and some random guy tried to pick up my sister. So lesson there-try not to look like a tourist, which is exactly how my family looked. The Mark Hopkins really is quite a hike up the hill, but I loved it. It is a good workout!
