When you reach the top, however, you will see the most beautiful views of the city - fog in the morning, and a rainbow even one of the nights. Check-in was easy, we had a nice room on the 8th floor with the nicest hotel bathroom I've seen yet. Everyone at the hotel was pleasant, including the Concierge. They gave me maps and directions for my specific requests. Walking was easy, we never used any public transportation with the exception of the Bart on the way to the hotel. Walked from the hotel to the Farmers Market (highly recommend!) to Fisherman's Wharf and back up Hyde to California to get back to the hotel. Definitely hilly, but come on, you've been warned by someone if you come to San Francisco, and you have to appreciate it! One funny note - I went out to the hallway late Saturday night to take a phone call, and you can hear everything happening on the elevators. It spooked me a bit! I would recommend staying here if you find a good price and like to exercise. It is so worth it for the city views.

“Funky and very San Fran” San Francisco hotels can be very $$..this one is a decent price, but not for everyone. Narrow stairs & small old style elevator....Not much of a breakfast either.... Now, Good stuff: very cool artwork...different in each room and each floor has it's own theme. Convienent to Chinatown and the Art Academy is across the street. Overall...not bad for the price.

“Quiet, clean hotel and awesome location” My mom and I traveled to DC in March to do some sight-seeing and this was the perfect hotel for us. We only slept here, so we didn't need a lot of ammenities, but the hotel is very nice. The rooms were quiet, there are great restaurants within a 2 minute walk, and the mall is literally a 5-10 minute walk away. There is no conceirge, but they do have a computer in the lobby that lets you print a map and directions to anywhere you want to go. Staff was very friendly and the valets retrieved our car quickly every time. I'd stay here again if I go back to DC.

“5 Star all the way!” Starting with the curbside service from the second we pulled up to the hotel until they packed our car back up on our way out of the hotel the service at the Omni was GREAT! You won't find better service anywhere. I can't say enough about the hotel's staff. Location was perfect! One block from the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, Ben Franklin's home, etc. Perfect for the tourist. The rooms were quite large and very well appointed. Nice furnature, well decorated, good view, and a nice, well "stocked" bathroom. If I had to complain about something it would have to be the water saving devise in the shower head made for less than ideal water presure. Better pressure and massaging shower head would have made the place near perfect!

“Great Hotel” This hotel is the perfect place to stay while in Phoenix. Central to most everything with plenty of places nearby to eat. Great meeting spaces with the best catered food I have ever had at a meeting or convention.

“Tired, Dirty, & Poor” Generally speaking, Extended Stay America properties are usually pretty good for the money, unfortunately, their Castleton, IN property is quite a dissapointment. It's by no means terrible, but there were a few things that made me really annoyed during my brief, one-night, stay. For one, the AC unit in the room leaked all over the carpet. it leaked so much that the carpet surrounding one side of the bed actually "squished" when you walked on it. Not pleasent. The furniture was old, worn out, and pretty disgusting. My travelling partner wouldn't even sit on the desk chair. The bathroom was the same way. I stay in all types of motels/hotels when I travel, and it takes a lot for me to mention the cleanliness of a property. Read my other reviews if you don't believe me. But this place, really was quite tired, dirty, and poor.

“Great for conventions or other downtown activities” Comfort Inns are generally a great value for the price with Breakfast, Internet, and comfortable rooms. I had a King bed in one of the corners of the hotel (recommended) and it was pleasant, comfortable, and quiet. The bathroom was smallish, but the work desk was great. Hotel elevators broke once during my 3 night stay due probably to heavy use since the hotel was booked solid for a week-long convention. They probably need to be replaced since they appear to be about 50 years old. The location of the hotel is excellent- walking distance to 16th Street Mall, Convention center, and right across the street from the Brown Palace. If you want a cheaper alternative to the Brown Palace but need some good dining options, take the Comfort Inn and go get a steak at the restaurant of the Brown Palace. It was the best buffalo fillet I've ever had and the water comes from their own artesian well and is the freshest, purest water I have ever tasted, served at ground temperature of about 53°F.

“Hidden Jewel on the East Side” The Crowne Plaza UN is a beautiful hotel sandwiched between an old church and other tall buildings just off Third Avenue. I only stayed there one night and didn't spend much time in the hotel--but I was impressed. The rooms are of course small; this is New York, after all. If you've ever stayed in a full-sized Japanese hotel room, you know what to expect. However, it was really nice. Luxurious linens, very clean, and a great shower. They even provide a little gift bag containing (among other things) earplugs and a sleep mask, placed on each bed. Very thoughtful, considering that anywhere you stay in NYC, you're gonna hear some sirens. In the small stereo in the room, there's even a CD of new-agey fall-asleep music--which has hilarious commentary at the beginning. Check it out! The view out the window was of the building next door; but what else would it be? I walked past the lobby bar a few times, and it looked very nice, with lots of well-heeled-looking people having drinks there. It looked classy and cozy at the same time. The front-desk staff were also very nice, and checkin/checkout were a breeze. At just over $200 (corporate weekday rate), this wasn't a steal--but hey, it's New York. One other thing: I posted a comment on the hotel's website to suggest delivering some newspaper other than the USA Today in the mornings. I mean, it's New York, and the New York Times is one of the best papers in the world! (And no, I don't work for them.) I received a thoughtful e-mail from the manager saying that they'd consider this suggestion. The Crowne Plaza UN isn't terribly close to many of the main tourist attractions--but it's not far by subway, and walking to them is doable. And I would be this hotel is quieter than those near Times Square or in Lower Manhattan. If you have business at the UN or elsewhere in Murray Hill, staying at this hotel is a no-brainer.

“Room in poor repair, no water running in shower or tub” My stay at this hotel was not a pleasant experience. They did not have the room I requested and gave me a handicap room right next to the elevator (4112). No closet. Paint on walls touched up and did not match. Got up in the morning. Coffee maker did not work, no running water in tub or shower so I had to take a shower in the sink. No manager on duty at 8 am when I checked out. Desk person promised to call me with resolution, that didn't happen. Personally, there are far too many good hotels in NYC to put up with this kind of service. I would not stay here or recommend to anyone!

“A nice hotel with a great location” Stayed here for four nights in June. Selected this hotel based on previous reviews, and we don't regret it. The location is perfect, walking distance to a lot of Chicago's attractions (if you don't mind walking). Friendly staff who helped us with information and booking of various attractions. Room was bright and clean. We couldn't hear any noise from either the streets or the other rooms. Will probably use again if we ever find ourselves in Chicago again.

“Very Good and central” We arrived early at the hotel which was not a problem at all, they booked us into a very good room straight away. It was light and spacious. The bed was confortable and the bedding was lovely, it was changed every day as were the towels. Air conditioning was a bit noisy when we arrived and wouldn't shut off, and we couldn't work out how to open the safe, we phoned down and someone came and looked at both within 15 minutes. Staff were friendly and helpful, it was our first trip to New York and would certainly stay at this hotel again, it was so convenient, we were able to walk to most places within 15 minutes, Grand Central was just around the corner. There were lots of restaurants and bars on the next block!

“Très bien situé, très bon rapport qualité/prix” Comme son nom l'indique, l'hôtel est situé directement sur Times Square (ce qui n'est pas toujours le cas). Cela a ses avantages et ses inconvénients. Nous descendons habituellement au Morgans, mais pour un court séjour, nous voulions être au coeur de l'action. Avantage : nous y étions ! Inconvénient : nous n'étions pas seuls ! Il fallait se frayer un chemin dans la foule chaque fois que nous voulions entrer et sortir de l'hôtel. Nous sommes arrivés à 13h. Notre suite n'était pas prête, mais nous avons pu laisser nos bagages et partir nous promener. Lorsque nous sommes rentrés, notre suite nous attendait et nos bagages nous ont été amenés. La suite était correcte et bien équipée, mais sans charme particulier. En revanche, nous étions au 36e étage dans une suite d'angle et la vue sur Times Square était magique. L'isolation était très bonne : nous n'entendions rien du bruit extérieur, ni du bruit intérieur non plus (pourtant nous étions à côté de l'ascenseur). La literie était très confortable dans la chambre, mais, comme c'est souvent malheureusement le cas, le matelas du canapé-lit n'était pas bien épais. Nous sommes tout de même globalement très satisfaits de notre séjour car l'hôtel présente un très bon rapport qualité/prix pour New York.

“great room & location but the staff needs some training” The Good- The location on K street was excellent. 5-10 minute walk to 2 metro stops and the white house. the room was clean and comfy-especially the bed. Free wired internet in the room was nice. Free bottle of water is a nice touch considering most places charge about $4-5 for this! New, flat screen tv. Great happy hour in the bar with friendly bartender & staff. The bad- noisy AC, hall smelled like the swimming pool. room was small but that wasn't such a big deal. We accidentally went to the wrong room at first and the scary thing was our keycard worked! the ugly-internet kiosk/printers did not work and front desk staff refused to help- said its not their problem. The internet kiosk took my money and they would not assist me in getting a refund...totally unconcerned and offered no suggestions when I explained I was trying to print out an electronic ticket for a tour I had booked! Staff was unable to assist with directions and restaurant recommendations-said things like "I don't drive or live down here so I wouldn't know." Bellmen looked at us like we were speaking french when we asked them to stow our bags when we were checking out and had a late afternoon flight- there were 3 of them just standing around in front of the hotel but no one at the bell desk/podium. When we checked out the guy at the front desk told us we should have gotten a receipt under our door, and we told him we had not and he insisted we must have, we had to tell him 3 times we did not get a receipt under our door and he didn't believe us. He then could not print us a receipt because printers were down and offered no alternative for getting me a receipt-crazy! All in all if you can deal with lazy, unmotivated and incompetent staff and don't need to print anything out, it does not get much better that this for the price in this location.

“One of Our Favorite Small Hotels” We love small local hotels. This rates as a favorite in the U. S. Check in was easy. The Inn Keeper made it feel like it was home. We also received helpful information when needed for getting around the city. We enjoyed all of the cozy spots to sit and relax. Breakfast was simple, and fresh! Nice to smell it cooking. (Also nice that the Inn Keeper sat and visited with us during breakfast.) Wine in the afternoon was nice. The beds were super comfortable, and the pillows good. Important! We slept great. The shower was the best. A lot of planning went in to making this building become a hotel. The Riverwalk is right across the street so easy access to everything. Again....We loved it!

“My new favorite place in Columbus” We stayed here for 1 night after watching the footy. We didn't normally stay here when in Columbus but got a great price on Priceline, and I'm glad that we did. Easily accessible from the highway, the hotel is modern from top to bottom, the staff were generally very friendly, and the Max&Erma's restaurant is open late which is good because the food selection after hours near the nationwide area (5-7 min walk) is not very inspiring. The room itself was big enough and as a bonus, the flat screen TV actually featured HD cable! A nice bonus when it's raining in Columbus. We had no problem with this hotel and will hope to get it again on Priceline for our next visit to Columbus.

“Acceptable but nothing special” This hotel is in the vicinity of the convention center, but it's not one of the ones right across the street from it. You can walk in 5 minutes. The neighborhood within a few blocks of the hotel it totally dead, and it backs onto the Interstate. I did not feel unsafe - it's just dead. Three or four blocks brings you to a more lively district. I asked for a room not facing the highway, based on reviews here. I got a room on the south side at the end of the hotel away from the highway. But the highway, and its noise, still dominate the view. I had to leave the room fan running all the time to drown out the highway - it did this adequately. I stayed for 6 days. On two of those days my room was not made up. Both days I was out for 4 hours or so in the morning, then back in the room for a few hours around lunch, and then out until evening. I'm guessing that the housekeepers make one attempt to get into the room and then give up. Not so good. Elevators on the slow side. Internet started out great but then after the weekend got slow enough that I used my 3G cell phone for internet access. This was true whether wired or wireless. Bummer. Staff were certainly friendly. Coffee in the lobby in the morning, cookies in the evening. Fridge and microwave in the room are nice. I stayed here based on location and price. You get what you pay for so this is not a real complaint but I find the "perfect" reviews seen here to be more than a bit over the top.

“Excellent location, view and amenities” The Clift combines a sweeping view, a prime location and a unique charm that makes it a winner. Just two blocks off Union Square, this property manages to meld Old World high-end seclusion with modern chic sensibilities. Colored-mirrored elevators combine with stalely redwood-paneled lobby decor for a decadent, yet playful effect. The rooms are spacious and bright, with grand views of the city. Enormous mirrors and firm beds made the room a pleasure. Windows open to allow the city's breeze to cool you into a deep, relaxing sleep. The amenities are endless, from concierge services to an extremely well-stocked minibar. This is a hotel for the person who enjoys luxury, but enjoys it with a modern twist.

“Decent rooms, and a great location” The rooms at this property were pretty large, although the place is by no means fancy. It has some old school character, however, and the accomodations are fine if you're not looking for more than a decent room. And the view from our window was quite nice. The streetcar stops right outside the door, and the Castro is right around the corner.

“Wonderful Location” Our first time in Chicago and as Sofitel/Accor Favourite guest members we chose to stay at this property. We booked a Luxury room with a king bed on an upper floor and were upgraded to a Junior Suite which was wonderful. The hotel is very impressive from the outside and the staff the the front counter could not have been more helpful, Marie thank you and also Jackie the Concierge. Our room was not ready but they stored our luggage as we went to explore the city armed with maps and information provided by Jackie. Upon our return to the hotel we were delighted with our Junior Suite, the views from the room were unbelievable and there was so much space. The desk area was a two sided one so great for both of us to work at. Large comfortable bed and the standard Sofitel linens, doonas and bathroom products. Good size bathroom with separate shower and bath. Had room service one night and it was very good. Turndown service provided complimentary water each night and there was also free internet. Only issues we had was with the bar staff, after our wonderful experience with the restaurant staff and bar staff at the Sofitel in Washington DC we were disappointed with the service in the bar. Very slow and this was put down not to the waitress but the barman who was supposed to be making the drinks, he seemed to be more concerned with chatting to the single ladies at the bar than attending to his duties, also he was quiet noisy. The bar area was a little dark for drinks early in the evening, but after such poor service here we decided not to eat in the restaurant and instead went over the road to the seafood restaurant which was exceptionally good, McCormack and Something (I think it was called). Also tried the little diner/cafe down the road from the hotel, turn right as you go outside the hotel door, for breakfast as another trip adviser writer had suggested, lovely little place and great food but HUGE portions so you may only want to order a shared portion. Would I say here again - not sure, great location though

“Great Stay!” Upon arrival, we received an upgrade to a beautiful full suite and couldn’t have been happier with our four-night stay at the Ritz in SF. Service was excellent, linen was beautiful and the location was convenient for shopping, sight-seeing and dining. I highly recommend the hotel to anyone looking for a luxurious, comfortable, great stay in SF.

“Ok For One Night” The room was fine, clean and no real issues except for the poor AC unit in the room. The hallways and stairways were dirty and smelled. Breakfast was OK, but I usually just eat yogurt, bananas, and hard boiled eggs. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I wouldn't stay here again unless required by my employer.

“Nice midtown hotel” We have a rate here and I paid about $218 which is good value for this part of midtown. Room very well appointed and recently refurbished by the looks of it. Slept very well. The corridors and rest of the hotel could do with a bit of modernization, but on the whole no complaints.

“A nice, clean hotel at a reasonable price.” A very pleasant surprise. Good location. A $7-8 taxi ride from the Light Rail station Westlake Center. Reasonably priced. Pleasant reception by cherful, tall Jim. Clean, quiet room with a big comfortable bed and a big TV. Breakfast included way above the average fare. Belgian waffles with sausage, hardboiled eggs and a pleasant (!) smiling help. Whoa. Rare. USA Today in the morning by the room door. Will stay there again. Bring your own liquor if you arrive late in the evening. Seattle liquor stores close up at an ungodly early hour.

“Great Location and a Great Room” Stayed two nights in April. Fantastic location on Rittenhouse Square, a vibrant area of Philadelphia bordering a beautiful city park. Check in was a breeze. Our room was spacious and well appointed with a comfortable bed and everything one would expect of a hotel in this price range. The bathroom was first class as well. The lobby was sterile and uninviting, typical of many modern hotels. A glitch at afternoon tea was quickly remedied by the manager. The staff was, for the most part, warm and friendly. The gym was ok with the locker room less so due to space constraints. The breakfast was sub par. Overall, a very nice hotel. Spacious and comfortable room. At $350 per night it borders on overpriced when compared to a property such as the Park Hyatt Chicago, but I nevertheless enjoyed the stay.

“Small and noisy but also cute and clean” My husband and I stayed here at a discounted rate through Hotels.com over Thanksgiving. There is nothing to add to other reviewers' comments about the tiny size of the room- it's tiny. The closet only big enough to hang a few small things, you can't unpack much, and there's only one night stand on one side of the bed. However, we found the bed to be very comfortable (not hard like other reviewers have noted), and the room nice and clean. The shower was awesome, and I liked the European-style shower soap and shampoo, which are installed in pumps attached to the wall of the shower. It was a bit annoying that there is no conditioner available- the "conditioning shampoo" doesn't do the job at all, so I had to buy my own conditioner. We shared the same experience as other viewers, in that we only had a view of a brick wall and another guest room. We could still hear traffic from 8th Avenue, but we weren't too bothered by this. The noise that did bother me was from a very rude group of people staying on the same floor during my first night and morning (before my husband arrived). I was too tired to complain, but this group of people had no qualms about talking loudly with each other in the hallway at all hours. I don't understand why people feel they have the right to do this. And there doesn't seem to be much sound-proofing in the rooms, so there was no buffer between my room and their voices. I've noticed that the manager frequently refers reviewers to the hotel roof deck, urging people to check it out, especially when they gripe about the size of the rooms. My husband and I went up to take a look, and it was alright, but it was awfully cold when we were there, so I don't think anyone would have used it. I also don't feel like it's anything to write home about, and it's not that big. The manager was friendly in terms of helping my husband find a church to attend during our stay. We always found the staff at the front desk to be helpful and courteous- for instance, another staff member helped us find directions to the place wanted to go for lunch. Check-out took a little bit longer than we would have hoped for, but it was still within the acceptable range, I guess (there was only the manager working, and he was trying to deal with multiple customers checking out and phone calls coming in. It was a little surprising that there weren't any staff down there assisting him on a Sunday morning following a holiday, about an hour prior to check-out time). The cleaning staff that we encountered during our stay were very cheerful and friendly. I left little notes and tips for the staff member who cleaned our room, and I thought it was really nice that she left little notes in return. It is very annoying that the hotel charges $2 per night for the safe in each room, regardless of whether or not you use it. I have never used a safe in my life. I've also never been charged a separate safe fee in my life. The only reason I know that fee is for the safe is from reading previous reviews for this hotel, together with responses from the manager. Otherwise, I would have been worried and annoyed about the $8 charge (for 4 nights) that showed up at the end of our stay on my credit card. The hotel never told us about this charge, which I find a bit creepy. I have a feeling the manager might respond, as he has before, by saying that "the safe fee doesn't benefit the hotel in any way". What the heck does that mean? Either get rid of that fee, or at the very least be upfront with customers about it when they check in. It's dishonest. The location of the hotel is very nice, for guests who are not interested in staying in the middle of Times Square. We had never really explored Chelsea before, and the Chelsea Market is a must-see. It is only a short walk from the hotel. The subway is only a block away, next a great little deli that has tasty cannolis and other pastries, along with sandwiches, soups, cupcakes, etc. There are standard and gourmet grocery stores close by. The High Line is also very close, and also very much worth a visit. We also recommend the brunch at Colicchio and Sons, across from the back entrance of the Chelsea Market. The servers there were the most friendly we encountered during our whole trip, and the food was really good. There are quite a few restaurants in the neighborhood of the hotel, covering a wide range of tastes and price ranges. There's also a movie theatre around the corner from the subway, although we didn't have time to see a movie during our stay. I have mixed feelings about whether or not I'd stay here again. If we could get the same discounted price, or an even better price, we might stay here, and bring ear plugs or hope that the other people staying on our floor were quiet. It would be great if we had a room with more than a view of the wall and rooms across the way. I guess it would be better to stay here in the summer, when you have less stuff with you and don't need to hang up so many clothes in the tiny closet. I've seen the manager tell people to check out the larger rooms that are available, but of course that would mean you'd have to pay quite a bit more, and I'm not sure that'd be worth it.

“Great location, good hotel if you don't pay too much” We stayed at the Novotel Times Square four nights, in January 2009. First, hotel location is very convenient, being very close to Times Square, the 6th Avenue (Rockefeller Centre), Columbus Circle, Central Park etc. Despite being so close to Times Square, the hotel is slighly back from Broadway, so we had no traffic noise. The hotel lobby is actually on the 6th or 7th floor, and has an amazing view on Times Square. I am not sure any other hotels in the area have a similar view, since there is no need to look down, as Times Square is straight ahead, with no buildings blocking the view. The lobby was nicely decorated and modern, although quite a few chairs were stained and the lobby didn't look clean all the times. We had a room on the 25th floor, away from the lifts and the ice machine (very noisy), so we had a quiet stay. There was no noise from traffic nor from other rooms. The view was very nice, looking at the west side and New Jersey. The room was quite large for New York. There was also automatic air conditioning (set the temperature). The room had a king size firm bed, a desk, a sofa and a chair. There was a small safe, and a fridge (not possible to place items inside, since charged when lifting something). The TV was not a flat screen, so taking quite some space. Usual TV channels available, but no foreign european channels, which is surprising, given the clientele. The bathroom was fairly standard for the USA, and looked a bit old fashion (in beige plastic). There was a hairdryer, but no shower gel provided (only tiny round soaps). The room does not look at all like the pictures on the Novotel website. Their pictures are showing some modern-style Novotel rooms (white scheme), while the ones in Times Squares look more like Hilton or other american chains (yellow/beige colours). The room was advertised for $799 a night, which would be extremely expensive for what it is. However, we probably paid $150 a night through Expedia, making it good value for money. Buffet breakfasts were charged about $28 per person (including tip), with an amazing choice of items, even compared to the usual high Novotel standards. There was a choice of pancakes, waffles, bacon, smoked salmon, ham and custom-made omelettes and other types of eggs. Many types of cereals, fresh fruits etc However, there are many dinners around, offering breakfasts for much cheaper, but without the view and the buffet choice. We never had to wait for lifts (there are four going to the lobby, and then two going to the street). We were charged $1 per luggage to leave our luggage on the last day, which is very unusual. The doorman tried to direct us to some private cabs to go back to the airport, despite the fact that we had booked a van... Overall, a very good location and nice hotel, full of French tourists (given that Novotel is a French hotel chain). The room was OK, but the hotel is special because of its amazing view on Times Square.
“Great stay!!” Had a great stay at the Residence Inn. The breakfast was excellent and the front desk staff was super friendly and helpful. Will stay there again when we visit Houston.

“Central to the city and luxe accomodations” Everything you need is just steps away from your doorstep. Deep-dish pizzas are right around the corner and a grocery store right across the hotel are convenient food options nearby. The hotel itself is a relaxing sanctuary in the middle of the city.

“Great location, free wifi, cheap breakfast” I stayed here for business and was so pleasantly surprised. I usually stay at Starwood properties but thought I'd give the Omni a try due to its proximity to 6th St (1 block) and the $4/night difference. If you join their rewards program, the wifi is free, you get two free drinks for breakfast (and you can get a bagel delivered for $3 instead of the usual $10). The workout facility has plenty of cardio machines and weights. It is currently being remodeled so if you are sensitive to noise during working hours, ask before you book. It didn't bother me and I will certainly be staying here again next time I am in town.

“Very Pleased with the Courtyard” My family and I stayed at the Courtyard the other night when our power went out and the city was in the midst of a 110 degree heat wave. We literally walked in without reservations. The front desk staff (bravo Grace!!) was extremely helpful despite the fact that they were obviously busy. Grace was able to take care of our needs--crib for our infant, suite to accommodate all of us, etc.--without batting an eye. (Granted, it may help that I am a premium level Marriot member.) The price was fair, although given the heat, I would have given her a kidney if I could have had an air conditioned room for the night. I don't know if they allow pets, but no one squawked when we brought our dog in (somewhat hidden from view) as she couldn't stay at home without a/c!! The location is great for tourists and locals alike. While our 10th floor windows faced the freeway, it was quite and peaceful. My on concern, and it is a minimal one, is that the restaurant didn't open until 7 am for breakfast. Most of the world won't care, but when the kids are up and hungry at dawn, ya gotta feed them somehow! Lucky for us, the power was on the next day and we could move home, but this did make for a nice mini-vacation.

“Lovely room, well situated” Pleasantly surprised to find lovely, tasteful decor at the Elysee. The room was decorated in shades of pale yellow and light blue, with botanical prints on the walls. Tiny bathroom, but so what! The entryway with work desk and lamp was a nice touch, as were the included continental breakfast ( of good quality) and evening snacks. The staff at check-in and check-out was very courteous. The stay was quiet and lovely. I would be delighted to return to this conveniently located hotel (even though the bed was not the height of comfort)!

“Don't Let The Streetwalkers Scare You” I stayed at this excellent gem for three nights in mid-May. I was in town for the Subway Series and to visit friends, and as a former New Yorker I found this hotel to be an excellent jumping off point for my activities. Yes, there are prostitutes outside. Lest I thought I was mistaken the first night, they showed up again the next. But they would not serve as a deterrent to my recommendation, and indeed I have already booked another stay there next month. For the rate I got on a discount travel site, $244 per night for Thursday thru Saturday (a lot of places go up on the weekends, this one doesn't), I found the Park South to be a good value, compared with other NYC hotels I have stayed at during the last few years. First off, my plane didn't arrive at JFK until midnight, and I had no trouble with my room being held for late arrival. I checked in quickly around 1 a.m. and found the lights very dim in the lobby and candles flickering on the side tables. The desk clerk said that management likes it that way at night, but he did turn the lights up enough so that I could see what I was signing. I had a queen-sized bed, and true, while the room was typicaly NYC-small, with the obligatory view of the building next door, it wasn't as small as some I've encountered, where you could barely pass between the bed and the wall. The room was spotless, with two telephones, a TV-DVD combination, a Sony Dream Machine clock radio, a mini-fridge, safe, ironing board & iron, toiletries (shampoo, conditioner, lotion, shower gel & two sizes of soap), hair dryer and bathrobe. The latter is a great touch. The bathroom linens were thick and of a high quality. It was also very quiet, although the doors of the other rooms tend to slam, so that got to be annoying. There was a very small closet area with three or four drawers built-in below. If you're staying for more than a few days and want to hang up a lot of stuff it's not going to be sufficient. It was helpful, though, that there was also a coatrack by the front door. My room also had a desk with the second phone. In the morning I had both USA Today and the NY Times outside my door. I never ate at the continental breakfast, which is served in the Black Duck restaurant off the lobby, but I did stick my head in. It seemed to have a decent selection of fresh fruit, danish, breads, cereal, juice, coffee and tea. I stayed on the second floor, which held a darling alcove overlooking the lobby with two chairs and a lending library. There was also a selection of DVDs available to borrow at the front desk, along with an ever present huge bowl of Hershey's Minatures. I did use the business center, located on the lower lobby, which was convenient for printing out my boarding pass before my return flight. The only minor complaint I would have about that is that a staff member has to escort you and let you in, but I do believe it is open 24 hours. My first night back there was turndown service with two chocolates on the pillow, but for some reason that did not happen the next night. Housekeeping was a bit spotty in terms of resupplying towels and keeping them at the same amounts as there were upon check-in, but when I called down to say we'd been left no face cloths within five minutes there was a knock on my door with additional ones. The staff was friendly and helpful. Check-out was equally quick, although it took the bellhop a while to find the bags we had checked with him, and he actually had us come into the closet with him to find them. Overall, though, I was more than pleased and quite happy to find this place. It was very convenient to have the 6 train on the corner at Park Avenue, as well as a 24-hour Duane Reade (drugstore). There's also a 24-hour McDonald's, for those so inclined, and a nice bagel shop a couple of doors up, as well as a bodega on the corner of Lexington. I'm wishing I had discovered this place long ago when I was staying at other hotels in the city. I can't wait to go back.

“Great airport hotel and very efficient” We got a splendid rate on spg.com for a night in January including parking at this hotel. This is my third stay at this hotel and it still receives great compliments from me. The front desk is very efficient in attending to guest as every airport hotel should be considering the number of guests passing through. Being a SPG gold member, it helps. In my latest stay, I was given in one of the recently renovated rooms. The windows are extremely sound proof from any approaching aircraft into LAX. I have never tried the breakfast here but they do offer a buffet breakfast. I would definitely be back again. If you require a car rental, budget which is directly across the street couldn't be more convenient.

“Fine if staying in Downtown Area” I find the Bonaventure complex itself a bit complicated if are going to different areas of the hotel -- the food court, gym, the penthouse bar/lounge as you walk through the 3 interconnected buildings. As a Starwood Platinum member, was upgraded to a 1 bedroom suite with 1 1/2 baths; large space, fridge (no mini bar) and received a coupon for a free drink at the Penthouse. Old clock radio - wish they had an iPod station dock. Surprised how quiet the hotel from the traffic. Great location if you need to be in the downtown area.

“Really good upscale hotel.” There were high expectations before coming to this hotel and they were all met. From you entered the hotel via concierge and front desk you were very welcomed. From a standard room the bathroom was very nice. You felt really good staying here and the location in 44th between 5th. and 6th. Av is no drawback. Housekeeping did an excellent job and cleaned up in the evening as well.
“Amazing!!” Another wonderful stay at the Royal Palms. This is one of the most romantic resorts I've ever been to. The service is excellent. TCook's is a great romantic dinner experience.

“Happy once again!” We just spent the weekend here (2 nights) 6/11 & it was just as good as the other 2-3 times we have stayed there. It is a little away from the center of the riverwalk, so a little walk, but we love that. We prefer being away from the hustle & bustle, so perfect location for us. We have no complaints and will stay again on our next visit.

“Great location, beautiful hotel...but you pay for WiFi.” The Mark Hopkins is a stunning building, in a great location of San Fran. Close to the BART station and the trolley, with great restaurants around every corner. The Top of the Mark at the top of the hotel has great drinks, a stunning view. I only wish a hotel of this caliber offer free WiFi. Cmon! Stayed in romm 1621, checked out on 10/23/2011

“My favorite Chicago hotel; the Lobby still makes my heart skip a beat” OK, I admit it. I am more than a little biased when it comes to this hotel. This is my favorite hotel in Chicago. Everything about it is great. I have always had great service at this hotel. Great info and advice from staff on things to to, places to eat, etc. We requested a place to eat that had both free range meats and organic veggie options at a certain price point. Most hotel staff would give you a sigh or blank stair. Not the staff at the Palmer House. They immediately recommended a little place dow the street that was excellent and fit everything we were looking for! I could sit in the lobby for hours and look at the celing. The lobby bar is a great place to hang for this exact reason. One more thing ... when we stayed some of the rooms were newly decorated ... others had the old decor. Get the NEW rooms with the peacock theme. You will glad you did!

“Historic hotel in the hotest point of Gas Lamp district” This very beautiful hotel has a fantastique location as well as has a great location to Convention Center and nightlife at Gas Lamp. Excellent cost benefit. Very well kept.

“Convenient and professional Boston hotel” Of all the hotels in Boston, this is the one that the members of my family prefer the most. Why? The location is extremely convenient, across the street from a complete full service shopping mall, yet right in the middle of a bustling city center. The rooms are very comfortable, the room service is timely and attentive, and the parking is extremely convenient (a rarity in Boston). There are so many things to do and see within walking distance of the hotel.

“Relaxing Getaway” This resort is designed for kids to play while the parents are playing golf or using the spa. Our room layout was normal for most hotel rooms except we had Aveda products and a balcony. Most of the rooms of this three story building do not have terrific views since the trees have tall. The only negative remark about the room was the 'hard' bed and 'too soft' pillows. We did have a small fridge which is nice. This place is not too expensive where you had different food and drink options. Just like every time we stay at a nice place, the fire alarm went off in the middle of the night. We must be jinxed. The staff is friendly and nice. The grounds are stocked with different small animals which are fed and the plants are well taken care of. This place makes you feel you are not in the city, but in the Hill Country and a great place to stay if you are planning to go to Sea World.

“Nice hotel in downtown detroit” I had meetings about 4 blocks away and found this hotel to be excellent. My room was large, clean and quiet. I appreciated the in room coffee maker, extra pillows and towels. While not an inconvenience, other than check in I had no interaction with staff, i didn't need anything and they weren't clearly visible to me. The fitness room is nice, with cardio equipment, towels, water, weights and extra mats. Overall an excellent stay.

“Older hotel, but updated rooms and good experience” I had a big suite that was updated with lots of storage. The counters, desk and dresser tops are all granite. There is a flat screen TV and full length mirrors in the bedroom and in the living room. A small microwave oven, small refrigerator, and individual cup coffee maker are available. Terrible WiFi connection, but sufficient outlets and free Internet. The room was very quiet. The housekeeper did not take all of my trash the first day and I had a lot. I suspected the glasses were not exchanged daily, so I marked them, and sure enough, they were not. I hope they exchange them between guests. A hairpin and a toothpick in the carpet stayed there my entire 5 day stay. The hallway my room was on smelled musty, but the room smelled fine. The fitness center is open 24 hours. It is well equipped, including 2 TVs; however, there are no remote controls. The business center has 3 nice terminals. The hotel is located on Hwy 59 & Kirby and near I-610, shopping and restaurants. A hotel shuttle is available for a 3 mile radius. Garage parking is $8/night and valet is $14. The attendants are fast and friendly. A gift shop and laundryroom is available, and the USA Today is delivered to the rooms each morning. Check-in was very slow and there were only 2 clerks on duty for a lobby full of people.

“A very pleasant surprise” i had never stayed in Aloft before, so didn't know what to expect. Kind of weird walking into a hotel lobby with the noise blasting at you. Ceiling about 25" tall. Easy check in. Accommodated a change in type of room that I wanted. They put me on the second floor, right above the bar area. I was leery of being able to sleep, but didn't hear a thing. I couldn't believe it. The rooms are spacious. The room has indirect lighting. Strange configuration. Either all the lights are on, or all the lights are off, except for one over the shower. So if someone gets up in the middle of the night and wants to turn the bathroom light on, the switch turns them all on. There were no drinking glasses. And only one regular coffee set up and one decaf. So if two of you are there, someone gets decaf. And you can only make one cup at a time anyway. The beds are not Sheraton standard, not quite as comfortable. There is a half-ironing board, not full size. And the room has a fridge, but no microwave. Also, they don't have vending or ice machines anywhere other than in the lobby. Free wired and wifi, and portable electronics plug in and play on tv screen. Which is a 35" flatscreen. There is no inroom directory or phone book, so if you want a pizza, you have to figure that out some other way. There are two desks in the room, but only one chair. And it is shower only, no tub. There were two styrofoam cups for the coffee. There is a parking charge of $8. It is only one block from the convention center, so very easy to leave your car there and walk over. There is a place to order food. I had a breakfast sandwich, and it took a good ten minutes. There were only a few people in front of me, but the cook told me he is only allowed to make two sandwiches at a time. This was 10:00 on a Saturday. I don't know how you would ever get anything hot on a weekday at 7:30 am. Probably have to settle for bagels, cereal, or yogurt. The employees are friendly and will go out of their way to help you with anything. I didn't get a chance to see if there was a restaurant anywhere near by. But what they have there is just a simple kitchen with basic items, such as sandwiches, salads, etc.

“Slipping on the details.” I have stayed here a number of times and generally love the hotel. Maybe that is why it feels a little sad to write this review. My last few visits I have noticed housekeeping issues that are disappointing. Nothing I would call serious, but little things like only 2 bath towels left in a suite which would accomodate at least 2 people. Stains not cleaned off the bathroom counter and the kitchen counter, a sticky substance on the coffeetable/footstool. To be fair, I didn't complain and feel sure the management would have addressed these things, but I am noticing it is consistent enough to be a sign of a problem. There also seems to be a problem with the breakfast. I have noticed the food is not promptly refilled and empty trays stay empty. The staff starts clearing things up well before the end time of the food service and the excellent service attitude which the hotel staff usually has with its guests does not seem to extend to this part of the staff. The decor is simple and green (which I appreciate). The rooms are spacious and comfortable. The bed truly is heavenly. So, there are no BIG complaints, but on the last couple of stays I have noticed the lamps (cheap plastic pieces) are barely hanging together - every time I went to turn it on, the bulb tipped over at a 90 degree angle. This is a beautiful hotel. The front desk staff is always exceptional. Management appears professional and focused. There seem to be so many good things in place here, I cannot understand how these little lapses are allowed to continue unaddressed in areas which have a big impact on the overall impression a guest takes away from their stay - especially guests who have stayed here many times and know how good the place has been in the past.

“Needs Outdoor Pool, Otherwise Perfect” Came down with the girlfriend to the Ballantyne for a wedding at the hotel. Beautiful place. My third stay at a Luxury Collection property, after a great one in London and an above-average stay in south Florida. Stayed here for 2 nights and loved the hotel. Beautiful resort in the southern suburbs of Charlotte. Very nice facade, looks new, and nicely appointed lobby. Guestrooms are large and very attractive, however our room, like half the hotel, faces a shopping center across the street, which is not a great resort-style view. Very comfy bed however, and nice bathroom amenities. Provided mouth wash, which is rare, but welcome. Had a few rounds of drinks with wedding people at the Gallery bar. Beautiful bar and very adorable bartender made this a fun experience. Bar menu includes a ton of unique cocktails the girlfriend enjoyed ordering and they all came out delicious. Golf the next day was great, very playable course and friendly staff members. Lunch at the turn was a bbq pulled pork sandwich which was surprisingly good. A little pissed that the spa couldn't fit me in for a massage, which was frustrating and the major design flaw of the hotel is the fact there is no outdoor pool deck. On an otherwise beautiful 90 degree day, I was forced to take a nap lying down in the rough off the 18th fairway. Not the ideal situation. Other people were crowding off a small patch outside the indoor pool, but it was very makeshift. They need to improve this yesterday. There is a small, but effective sauna in the pool lockeroom which was a treat and the food that night at the wedding was outstanding. Did not taste like banquet food, far superior. All in all, a great place, my issues are with the overcrowded spa, no outdoor pool, and lastly it was somewhat awkward getting my golf bag back and forth from the lobby to the pro shop when arriving and leaving the hotel. They don't have a good system and I went nuts when the bellman didnt have my golf bag as I was checking out (they had to rush it from the golf clubhouse), which was a debacle. Overall, would still come back, and this time make the spa appointment months in advance.

“Have stayed here four times now. Best hotel in area I've stayed at” I have stayed at Loews Hollywood hotel four times now. I used to stay at the Roosevelt, and while I still like that hotel, I have to say that as long as I can afford it I will stay here whenever in Hollywood area from now. Very nice, big rooms. I usually stay in a junior suite. Even in the off season (is there really any off season for LA?) you are going to pay over $200 a room usually, but there are not to many places this nice in area that you won't. I love how the hotel is attached to Hollywood and Highland shopping area, it's just a 5 minutes elevator ride and walk from almost any room in the hotel. Good shopping, great dining only minutes away. Also only minutes away from Graumans and the walk of fame. A great hotel located in the center of the action in Hollywood area.

“Teeeny tiny rooms!” Until my recent stay, I've only had drinks at the Hudson. Little did I know how incredibly tiny the rooms were! I was warned by many friends but to have to walk through the bathroom door sideways. It would have been nice if there was a flat screen TV somewhere instead of that tiny 13inch tucked away in a closet. It was noisy but I am a deep sleeper so it didn't bother me.

“The best hotel in Boston” We're staying in the Colonnade Hotel right now. Purchased the family connection package, 2 rooms connected, 4 American breakfasts, tickets to Aquarium, internet free with privilege card. Love the location - 2 shopping malls, supermarket right beside of us. The T is literally at the front door and newbury street and copley square very near. People are sooooo nice here from the front desk, to the bellman, to the doorman, to the waiters at breakfast. Did our laundry around the corner at Executive Laundry with washers/dryers in the cute back bay houses. The rooms are very big for Boston. Very comfy hotel with tons of pillows to tempt you with an afternoon nap. Room clean, bathroom clean, prompt housekeeping offering a generous amount of towels. Wouldn't even dream of staying anywhere else. Thanks Colonnade!

“Happy with the Hilton.” Overall this is a very nice property and our experience was a good one. First the positives: - Good size rooms, nicely furnished, great beds. - Good location (just a few miles from all of the major attractions and is right across the street from lots of food and shopping). - Rock bottom price through Priceline bidding process (if I was basing the review on the price I got I would easily give it the top 5 of 5 rating, my 4 of 5 rating is purposely leaving price out as a factor in order to give a fair rating). - Great service... the front desk people were fantastic and they were very receptive to all of my requests and needs (some times when you get a room through Priceline or Hotwire you end up not getting quite the same level of service from the hotel that you would otherwise). Neutral: - Pool and spa were small, but serviceable and had long hours. - Styling in the rooms was a little dated, but nicely maintained with lots of quality touches (I imagine the renovated rooms must be extremely nice). Negatives: - Parking was tight and the parking elevators were out of service. In fairness they did offer valet parking at no additional charge though because of the elevator situation. The $12/night seemed unnecessary for the hotel circle area (I would expect it downtown, but not here). On the other hand after having recently paid: $22 in Arlington VA (outside of Washington DC), $29 in Toronto, $39 in Chicago, and $47 in New York City the $12 here didn't seem quite so bad. - Once an hour or so the A/C unit would make a noticeable "thumping" sound. Wasn't so bad that we lost any sleep though. Overall would recommend this hotel highly and I would be thrilled if I ever "won" this property again through either Priceline or Hotwire.

“Good business hotel” It is hard to go wrong with a Westin for business. Their properties are well located, predictable and fairly well appointed. This one in downtown Denver is within walking distance of the 16th street mall and LoDo. It has a Palm located in it, but it could use a refresher on its "bar". The lounge/bar area looks like an afterthought -- like they just dumped a drink cart in the middle of a conference break area. No T.V., no bar scene, no separation. Other than that, the rooms are good, and they offer the option to get points instead of maid service, which is good for us (but maybe not good for the maids who probably get lower tips as a result). Overall, I recommend it for business for one or two nights.

“Great price/location but smelly linens & bad bed” The Baldwin Hotel charges an incredibly low rate for SF near Union Square. But the linens and pillows smelled sweaty. The bed was very uncomfortable, squeaky, and caused my back to spasm. The internet speed was inconsistent and very slow (1 Mbyte) -- when it was working. The radiator could not be controlled. The pipes whistled while showering. The room was tiny and the bathroom had no counter space. No luggage rack.

“Gigantic Suite” Seriously surprised at how enormous our room is... I'm here now. It's a one bedroom suite with a full living room, dining area and kitchen. A balcony overlooks the city. The furnishings are nice enough, not fancy, but comfortable. The towels are plush and seem new. Internet connection is pretty bad. No complimentary breakfast like in the chain hotels. We have 3 huge walk in closets. Laundry machines are $2 /wash and $2 to dry across the hall on our floor. 2 of each machine, handy if you need to throw in a load. The pool on the 24th floor roof was very refreshing after a very hot day of sightseeing. We are here to visit University of Pennsylvania and couldn't be more pleased with our selection.

“Decent hotel near Rush/UIC, but noisy & bad curtains” I feel like I am cursed when it comes to loud hotels these days. I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. Why is it that hotel room doors have to slam shut? The room I stayed in had the typical drapes, except that in this room, only the shear/gauze like drapes closed all the way. The drapes that would have blocked out the bright morning sun (which appeared at 5:45am) only covered 1/2 the window. Between the noise and sunlight, I didn't sleep too well. Staff was very nice, especially in the hotel restaurant (where it seems that staff from Rush/UIC hang out after work for dinner and drinks). Minor restaurant complaint, it took way too long to get & pay for coffee in the morning.

“Would stay again!” Off the beaten path but close to all things San Diego. While the facility is older but it is well maintained. Dont expect the Hilton or Hyatt but expect a very enjoyable stay. I was afraid at first by booking a non brand name hotel and fears were quickly put to rest. The customer service is excellent, especially Tim. Complimentary breakfast buffet is offered and typical. Waffles, potatoes, eggs, fruit, bagels, etc.

“Good for business trip at local office” I've stayed here twice because it is local to the business I visit nearby. I did not have a car so I can give the perspective of a walker in the area. The hotel is around $60 taxi ride from the airport. I walked up to Vons (10 mins) for a few supplies and there are a couple places to get food in the complex if you want a low-key meal. Otherwise, I had room service which was fast with nice food, especially the sushi. The hotel itself has been refurbished since I last stayed and it's much nicer. I had a 5th floor corner room near the stairway and overlooking the highway. I noticed very little hallway noise, probably because it was a corner room. My refrigerator was not noisy as others have said and I was not disturbed by the aircon. There was a little traffic noise but mostly a dull hum that I quickly got used to. There's the usual plumbing noise from other rooms that you get in an older hotel. I had a business package so parking (if I had a car), breakfast and wifi were included in my rate. The breakfast was quality with nice options and the wifi was fast. Overall, a nice place to stay if you have local business. It's a long way from Del Mar and if I was travelling for a holiday, I would stay somewhere closer to the coast.

“It Just Gets Better! ver 2.0” Our second visit to the Hilton overlooking the 9/11 Memorial and Freedom Tower, Hilton still gets it right! We stayed on the 26th floor in a King Suite that offered a entryway/living room with a view towards midtown and the bedroom overlooking the Memorial. Sound/noise was minimal/almost zero at the 26th floor, no issue with sleeping through the night. The furniture is somewhat dated and scarred, but not a huge issue. The room is very clean and the bed was perfect. We check rooms very closley and were very happy with how Hilton continues to keep such standards at these large facilites. Our check in and check out was fast, no issues. The location is very busy, the lobby was full of people and the bar was overflowing!!! We had a very nice breakfast the next morning and were treated very kindly by a very professional staff. We were always greeted by all employees.

“not bad” stayed here for two nights while attending a conference at the coronado. went on priceline and got a decent deal. check in was quick and front desk staff was friendly (offered water or glass of wine upon arrival). Also had refreshments and pastries at the front desk. Rooms were small but had all the amenities and very modern in design. bed was comfortable. some of the snack bar items were complimentary (water, soda, juice, chips). free internet. the bad: their night club IVY (at the top floor) opens on Thursdays and through the weekends I believe--we were in room 402 and the noise was really distracting, and likely inappropriate if you had children with you as you can actually hear people screaming profanity at times. The party lasts till about 2am so you might be kept up until then--not a problem if you were out partying yourself I guess. Although close to the gaslamp district, the hotel is next to the salvation army, so the number of homeless folks that you see can ruin the atmosphere that the hotel tries to create. parking is $30 a night, but you can find parking at the meters. We parked at a nearby parking lot (on 7th and E) for $5 overnight (until 6am, but the attendant was nice enough to extend it to 7:30am for us. We were told we can park until 12noon for $10). If you park at the meters, make sure to look at the sign on the meter as to when street cleaning will take place (some will say tues/thurs/sat, others mon/wed/friday from 3-6am). If you park at the meters during street cleaning, you can get a ticket. Overall, not a bad short stay--it is comfortable enough but not very suitable for families or people who need to rest early--especially during nights when the night club is open. Shop around if you are going with kids or if you're taking a business trip.

“W delivers a great experience again” 4th or 5th stay at this property. Good location...just down the street from the JFK Memorial, cool shops and across the street from American Airlines arena. Rooms are contemporary and spacious and staff goes out of the way to accommodate. Never had a single issue at this property.

“Very nice airport business hotel with conference center” I just returned from a 3 week business trip which started with 2 nights at the Sheraton Charlotte Airport. I was meeting clients flying into the CLT airport, so it was easier to stay there. All in all, I was very pleased with the hotel. For an airport and business oriented traveler, this is a definite 4 star stay for me. There is nothing really in the vicinity, of course, being that it's a few miles from the airport and about 5 miles from the city center, so I couldn't bring myself to give it any higher. The exterior looks a little tired, but the interior of the hotel is quite nice. There is a massive interior atrium lobby with nice modern furnishings, a decent sized bar and restaurant area, and an indoor/outdoor swimming pool. The conference meeting rooms are spacious and well equipped, though they can get a bit stuffy if you don't watch the temperature controls. Service was actually quite outstanding throughout my stay. The front desk staff couldn't have been more helpful. I did have to wait a little longer than expected for the airport van to pick up a client, but otherwise I didn't have any problems at all. Food at the restaurant and from room service was solid and prompt. My club king junior suite was an upgrade due to my Starwood status, and it was spacious, clean, again with mice modern furnishings and everything in perfect working order. All in all, if I were to have to stay at the airport again by CLT, this is my choice.

“Beautiful lobby, rooms need overhaul (and a good wash)” My daughters and I spent three nights here in October. Usually I stay at the Surrey, but I thought I would give this hotel a try, because I heard they had renovated the rooms. The photos on the website looked amazing. I booked some sort of suite and they upgraded me to, I guess, a bigger one--and it was huge, no doubt about it. There was even a grand piano. Unfortunately, it wasn't that comfortable...or clean. The furniture was old and sparse, and it was too small for the rooms. The couch in the living room looked downright manky. Through the holes in the radiator covers (which were large and very visible from the couch) you could see big piles of lint and scuzz. The bed was lovely and the bed linens were absolutely first quality, but the lumpy brown carpet made the room feel old. And the bathrooms (two full and one half) seemed either old or improperly cleaned. There were lines of black (fungus?) around the caulking. Where are they hiding the beautiful suites pictured on the website?! Were only some of the rooms renovated? Did they run out of money and do a more thorough job on some rooms than others? And why have people employed full-time pushing elevator buttons when there is such a problem with cleaning and maintenance? That seems truly bizarre to me. On the upside, the hotel has a great Upper East Side location, walking distance from the Met and other wonderful museums. The bar/restaurant is fun and very old New York. And the staff is sweet. But this hotel can't hold a candle to the newer or more thoroughly renovated luxury hotels in the city.

“new york new york!” I stayed at this hotel after a tour as a way of seeing new york city.staff are freindly,rooms are huge and its close to everything new york has to offer including walking distance to central park!

“Consigliato” Ottimo hotel con una bellissima hall, wifi gratuito in tutta la struttura. Camera discreta. Distributore di acqua gratis ad ogni piano. Zona tranquilla, rispetto alla city hall piena di soggetti poco raccomandabili. Self check-in e check-out. Bagno piccolo ma funzionale. Personale gentile, pc a disposizione dei clienti anche per stampare le carte di imbarco.

“Our new property of choice in NYC!” My wife and I found this property by accident; I was the winner of a charity auction for a two-night stay in an Executive Park View Suite. We come to New York two or three weekends a year and treat ourselves to a good time. Previously, the Ritz-Carlton Central Park had always been our property of choice; not anymore! The following sums up our comparisons based on the same room category: Pros: Full kitchen (plates, cups, glasses, pots, pans, silverware) Fresh, modern, and exquisitely decorated (well done Ivanka!) View (Central Park, Broadway, 8th, and Columbus Circle) Price (although this stay was complimentary, the price is about half of the Ritz) Cons: Master bath is small (single sink) We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and felt very comfortable throughout our visit. We were saddened to leave, but we were also so happy with our new find. We were saddened to leave, but we were also delighted by our new discovery. The Trump International Hotel & Tower is our new property of choice in NYC!

“WOW, what a nice hotel!!” WOW is all I can say. We had such a great stay at this hotel. We booked an executive king and were upgraded to a large suite. The staff was very friendly. The hotel was small and quiet, what an escape from the big city. Our room was very clean and very large. This trip was so nice, I will ALWAYS book this hotel when I stay in the city. For the price, you can't beat the luxury and friendly service. We have stayed in very expensive hotels in the city and this one beats them all.
“Great stay” Spent two nights in Feb 2008 and have no complaints. Large comfortable room, pleasant staff, good resturant/lounge and great location. All furniture and fixtures were top notch.

“Quiet, convenient location. Very cool atmosphere.” Loved the St. Giles. We never stayed in the Murray Hill area before, and it is lovely. Streets are quiet and safe, but just a few blocks to Grand Central and all the other action. We were upgraded to a King suite with a balcony, with a great view of the Chrysler building. We were treated very well from all of the staff. We went to the almost-next door St. Giles Tuscany for a quick breakfast in the cafe, which was also very cool. Server there was friendly and the bagel was great. It wasn't cheap by any means, but...given the location, the cool atmosphere, the polite treatment...it was well worth every penny and I will definitely go back.

“Not Bad At All” We stayed here for one night only, over the weekend as my husband's parents were in town to catch a few shows so this would be convenient for all. 5 minute walk from Penn Station, and 30 second walk to Bryant Park. Although our stay was short, this would be a relatively comfortable home base for tourists wanting to explore the city in an excellent location. The R train was right around the corner, so you'll have easy access to Manhattan, and a lot of other trains are a few minutes walk away. Check-in was weird, only one person working the small counter. Took 10 minutes to get going. Guy was friendly though, but that doesn't make up for 1 person staffing the front. All it takes is one demanding, annoying person to hold everyone up! The room was average sized for NYC, not large but not tiny either. It looks like it was recently updated, with flat screen TV and comfortable bed and pillows. There were no odd smells or noticeable stains on the floor. Decent closet and easy to use safe. The bathroom was a tub/shower, one sink, clean and the water pressure was amazing! I was pleasantly surprised. The toiletries were a weird brand I've never heard of, but the soap bar had this great scent that I still remember...strange but I had to mention it. Free coffee in the room and down in the lobby in front of the elevators, not Starbucks quality but not bad, I had several cups during our 1 night stay. The gym was okay, nothing spectacular but there were 2 bikes, 2 ellipticals, 2 treadmills and some yoga mats and I don't remember but there might have been a small free weight station. Water and towels provided. We had breakfast at the hotel the next morning and it was fine. I can't remember the price but I do remember it was reasonable for a hotel in the city. Food wasn't knock your socks off but fine for what it was. There are plenty of options nearby, but if you are on the run I'd go here since it's so convenient and as it's a buffett, you won't wait long. Do not go to the concierge for dinner recommendations, for whatever reason my husband's parents asked him and the place was awful, some over-priced Italian that was subpar. Go to yelp.com and find restuarant recommendations that are from regular people who live and eat in New York and don't get kickbacks for sending you to these tourist trap restaurants that suck. Free Wireless in the room so bring your laptop and do all your research there instead. Overall, good stay. Not fancy, but worth it for the money. I think his parents paid $150 for the room on Marriott.com.

“A Little Tired” This Hotel was billed as a 4 star Hotel on Hotwire. I would guess that that was true about 10 years ago. First the good: It is in a great location particularly if you are doing business in the financial district. It is also close to China Town, the Ferry Building market, the waterfront and plenty of public transportation including the California street cable car. Like any Hyatt, it has a very impressive atrium housing a couple of restaurants and a cocktail lounge. Many of the rooms have balconies and many of those have water views. The problem is that the rooms are just beginning to look tired. The carpets are somewhat worn, the furniture has its share of scratches, no flat-screen HD TV's or DVD players, everything just needs to be updated. While the beds are generally quite comfortable, on my last trip one side of the bed had a distinct sag. Also be forewarned that the rooms on the Market St. side of this Hotel get a lot of street noise if you are on one of the lower floors. Like any business hotel, they are geared toward people on expense accounts so be prepared to pay through the nose for anything extra. Wireless Internet service is $10 per day, parking is about $50 per day and how about a couple of poached eggs for $19 bucks ... you get the picture. All in all it was worth the $110 I payed on Hotwire, but would require some updating to get me to pay anything like their rack rate of over $200.

“Absolutely great, classy hotel.” We got our reservations on priceline as always. Having never stayed at the Contessa before we were a little worried what we might get. Well, no worries - the hotel was small but cozy, right on the Riverwalk, and the room was very, very plush. We were just down the street from the Mercado and while that wasn't what I expected it was a great adventure since we had not been there before either. This hotel is close to a lot of things within walking distance and the trolly stops right at the front door so if you prefer riding to walking, it's there and cheap. Again, the room was extremely fashionable, updated, comfortable, and most important clean. We paid around 125+ for the room but the rack rate is almost $300 so I feel like it was a great value. The parking like every property downtown is high but that's because space is prime and you pay for easy access to the Riverwalk, so make your choices accordingly. The valet parking at downtown hotels is all around $28-$30 so why go there and then gripe about it, that's the situation. If you want free parking you need to book your room somewhere other than in the downtown area. I would never pay the rack rate even for this great hotel but priceline rocks!

“great location, average hotel” While the location of the hotel is convenient, if you are interested in theater, Times Square, etc., the property itself is average and does not necessarily represent the standards one would expect from Hilton, or for the price, at least during my stay. I have requested light bulbs for two consecutive days and I'm still waiting, the furniture in my room is significantly aged and in case of the desk chair, torn. The bedding is extremely soft and appears not to be similar of other Hilton bedding packages. The restaurant/bar area is weakly decorated as is the atypical small lobby. Unless you are bolstering your Honors account, I know there are other locations which are less money and better experiences in the Times Square area.

“A Solid Find!” This is a hidden gem! The rooms are the star here... newly renovated and nicely appointed. It feels very homey and serene. The bathrooms are top-notch, european modern, with Grohe faucets and fixtures. I would definitely stay here again for under $200/night. There is a decent parking garage right across the street for $35/night.

“An upgraded motel that needs some minding (and clean bedding)” Club Quarters Boston is about a ten minute taxi ride from Logan International Airport. The taxi ride cost us $34, including tips which I thought was way too expensive. All the taxi did was drive through a tunnel and then cross some streets. The hotel is located in the Financial District of Boston and not much is open late at night besides a Seven Eleven. Chinatown is within walking distance as is the harbor which was not very impressive at all. When we went back to the airport, we walked a few blocks to the subway station (which goes straight to the airport though you need to take a free shuttle bus to actually get to the airport). The subway ride was $2. There is a busy pub next door that is connected to the hotel. I'm going to tell you like it is. This is not a hotel. It is like a business motel with clean facilities, but does not provide the right services to serve properly as a business motel. For example, the phone in the room did not have any instructions on how to connect to the front desk or dial outside of the hotel. There is no room service either. I think that's why the word "hotel" is omitted from this establishment's name. From the outside, you can hardly tell it is a hotel as it looks like an apartment building. The room appear clean and looks okay at first sight. But you'll notice the furnishings are kind of a like an upgraded East Coast USA version of IKEA. In other words, it is not luxury or even close to it. The TV hangs above the desk and so you cannot get a straight view from the bed. It does swivel so you can see it better though. The bathroom looks like something that belongs in a low-cost Northern European hotel. There were barely no amenities and the toilet was the same as those found in a public restroom (steel bar for flushing). The shower was dorm room-like with a cheap curtain. I never stay at hotels with bathrooms like this! Maybe when I was a college student backpacking through Europe, but not now! Most upsetting of all was that I could not sleep for even one minute here. The bedding was cheap and rough. I felt itchy all over (bed bugs?) and scratched myself repeatedly on my arms, legs, and neck. I had stayed at hotels just before this and just after this (we were on a long business trip taking us to several different cities) and I did not experience the same situation at other places. I slept quite well in most other places. In addition, something (fire detector?) was making this faint screeching noise all night that I didn't notice during the day when I had the TV on. I wanted to call the front desk, but I couldn't figure out how and I was so tired that I just tried to sleep. I didn't think they'd be able to do anything about it anyhow. I tried and tried to sleep. Of course, I couldn't. Terrible experience. The staff at the desk are young women in their 20s. They are nice, but not professional or experienced hotel staff. In fact, one of them was a trainee. There is usually one staff member at the desk and there does not appear to be a real office. I thought they were nice and tried to be helpful. However, I am used to older, more experienced and professional hotel desk staff. There is no doorman and only an older man who helps with luggage when called. Club Quarters is also overpriced. I have stayed at better hotels for about the same price. SUMMARY: I am really shocked that Club Quarters Boston is rated four stars on certain sites. I want to give this hotel three stars because it looks like a three star, but I just can't because it does not act like one. If it weren't for the nice young lady at the desk was helpful when we were looking for somewhere to eat late at night, I would even consider giving this place one star. I don't think I need to tell you that I will not stay here again. I would rather camp outside in the park if I had no other choice.

“Pleasantly Surprised” For an airport hotel, this was very nice. Many airport hotels feel like a "guest" mill where people are just rolled in and rolled out with little concern for customer service. This Marriott, however, went the extra mile. Check in was easy and the front desk staff was friendly and informative. The room was small but nicely furnished. There was a refrigerator that was actually usable (not filled with honor bar stuff). There were three restaurant choices. Sports bar, steak house, and middle of the road. Also a Starbucks stand. Food was typical average Marriott with overpriced drinks. But again the service was great. Hotel shuttle very convenient. Need to be sure that you give yourself plenty of time as it takes a while for the bus to load up, and usually there are lots of stops at various terminals. Workout facility and pool looked nice with lots of people using. Location is great. Right across from the rental car agencies so I literally dropped off my rental car and walked to the hotel. I would definitely stay here again.

“Bad area of town” This was a budget hotel in all respects.No clock in the room,or coffeemaker.Was next to a junkyard.Its very industrial,near strip clubs and hookers.i wouldnt stay there again. The breakfast was bear bones. The shuttle was fine.

“Good for business or airport” Nice hotel. Suites were well sized and equipped. The pool, hot tub and workout room were average which is fine. Breakfast was pretty simple and average. Our bed was soft but very comfortable. All things considered, a good deal for the price. Nothing outstanding but also nothing to complain about. We didn't notice any noise from the airport.

“Freezing, but nice” I planned a two night stay with Indigo Saver. Great deal! Friday and Saturday. For some reason, I lost the Saturday night and could only get it back with an additional 149$ on my bill. So, I got a great deal for one night. They wouldn't correct the mistake. I checked in early with no problem. Rooms are clean, comfortable, small. The fire alarm ringer was shorting on the floor. Called down. I called again - this time because only cold air was blowing. They sent someone up and he said it was now repaired. The fire alarm still going. Two hours later, neither was fixed. I called again to request a new room if not repaired. Finally the fire alarm was repaired. Still no heat. 30 degrees outside. Another visit to repair the heat. Repaired? He said yes but it never got above 64 degrees. Gave up. Checkout was very good. They stored my luggage before I checked into my new hotel -- remember I lost the second night. I was supposed to get a 25% discount on food - not reflected in bill. Actually, I like the place without these glitches. Very reasonably priced with Indigo Saver and Priority Rewards. I'm staying at another hotel near Central Park. Review to come.

“Good choice if you have to stay near the airport” I got a good deal there. It's a bit faded, clean with the exception of the dirty vents on the HVAC. My room had a great view of the airport and there wasn't much airport noise. They've got a large outdoor heated pool, great for lap swimming. The lobby bar was OK. The staff were pleasant and helpful. I'd go back!
