“Do not look any further for that special hotel in NYC!” After reading Trip Advisor I wanted to book the Casablanca Hotel for a short weekend trip to NYC, but they would only take a minimum of three nights. So we booked with their sister hotel, the Library and it turned out to be excellent. From the moment we arrived by taxi from JFK to the moment we left, I could only fault the hotel on one element which was the small number of tables for the breakfast/evening cheese events. Everything else and I mean everything was perfect. From the excellent friendly reception, finding a room before check-in time, left luggage and drying our coats. The quirky atmosphere, dewy numbering of the rooms, huge bathroom, wealth of facilities and location was spot on. If you can afford this place, look no further, you will not be disappointed!

“Lovely friendly hotel - shame about the location” Stayed here a few weeks ago on recommendation of colleagues - it is really near to a business location we regularly work at. Also got a great deal through our travel agent. I paid absolutely no extras. I'd stay there again if working at the same location, but would not pick it for a holiday. Firstly downsides - which the hotel cannot do anything about - - it is right next to the San Diego Freeway - my room looked straight up the south ramp; and the soundproofing could be better. Some of the rooms on the quieter side of the building open into the interior patio, where breakfast is served from quite early in the morning - the location is a hub for the homeless - slightly uncomfortable during the day, and of concern at night; that said the hotel has a high level of visible security - it only serves breakfast - but it DOES have an excellent range of delivery and eat out menus to suit all tastes and budgets. The upsides - are lots especially if you are using it as a base for working: - friendly helpful staff at all times - free Wifi which works first time (although it also pops up a Boingo sign in which costs and needs to be avoided - I was aware of this, but it was irritating) - nice size room spotlessly clean, and that extends to the bathroom which positively glistened - and had good bathtowels and nice if unfancy toiletries (no dispenser bottles) - comfy bed with nice linen and lots of pillows and pleasant decor - efficient AC - the "continental breakfast" which included 2-3 different hot dishes everyday, plus cereals, a range of fresh bagels, toasts,hot cinnamon buns, juices and fruit, plus coffees, teas, hot chocolate. And a lovely lady who looked after us every morning - a real bargain at this price - in the reception a range of fresh coffees plus hot water for tea and chocolate all the time; plus fresh oranges and apples - and in the afternoon fresh baked cookies of various types - and there was also a coffee maker in the room too - the room also had a full sized fridge to load with your own food and drink, and a large CRT TV (did not try it out so no idea what the quality was like), plus a good radio alarm and lots of wardrobe and storage space; also lots of power outlets in useful places (too many hotels fail on this) - there was also plenty of secure parking which appeared to be free for residents (although a sign in the reception suggested it was $7 a day.. but then had small print that contradicted this - slightly odd ) - has an amazing looking cinema just a couple of doors away, and shops across the street (7-11 type but nothing special - just good enough to get bits and pieces for the fridge) So great for work for a few days - and if you are not fussy about location a bargain in my view. If I am working at the same location again I would stay there - and recommend it to colleagues.

“Better Options Nearby” I was disappointed in this hotel. There were some good aspects: nice hot breakfast and good location near downtown, 6th Street, and Capitol. There was a fridge in the room which I didn't use, but would be nice for some. Wireless internet was free. But, so many drawbacks. I had to strip the bed and remake it because housekeeping obviously didn't know how to make a bed and mine was "short-sheeted". The carpet was dirty. I had an accessible room and the shower spewed water all over the bathroom floor. The HVAC was noisy and I couldn't get it to stay at temperature. We ordered a cab for getting to our meeting in the morning and the driver called at the last minute to cancel so we scrambled for a cab. The cost was only slightly less than other hotels in the area, so you might want to choose the Hilton, Courtyard, or Radisson.

“Even though we only stayed for one night, it was great!” During a baseball road trip in August, we stayed here on August 29 while we were in town to see the Padres play. It was the perfect location and was walking distance from Petco Park!!!! And there was free breakfast!!! It was a great stay and I am definitely going back!!

“Short, but pleasant stay” We spent one night at the Renaissance OHare and found good value. Especially if you need a park, sleep and fly package for an early morning flight from OHare. Note, we left our vehicle for a week in the parking ramp and did not have any theft issues as noted in a different review. However we parked in the middle of the rows and did not leave anything of value in the vehicle. We checked in at 10 pm. The staff was energetic and courteous for that hour of the day. Our room was a suite and much more than we needed for our 7 hour stay with a fridge, sofa, TV and working area in the business side and our bed, bath and a TV in the bedroom area. The room was clean and fairly modern. The bed was only average, but very spacious. We ate in the hotel bar. At 1015 pm, t he menu was limited, but the food was okay. The service was very good. We also noticed a deli and snack area near the front desk with prepared sandwiches, salads, sodas and snacks which all looked pretty good. Check our was fast at 445 am and the shuttle took us right to the terminal. They also validated our parking at that time so it was not necessary to do that on the way back. We did wait a bit on the return for pick up, but on the whole the van service was adequate.

“Nice hotel in good location” This is a nice hotel that is centrally located in downtown San Fran. I stayed here while attending an event at the Hilton across the street. It was easy to get to the Hilton from Parc 55, and Parc 55 is centrally located for San Fran tourist activities. Hotel room was nice with spacious bathroom, great water pressure, and HDTV. Tub was slow to drain, and the carpets throughout the hotel did not seemed to be vacuumed regularly. I was on the 5th floor so street noise was an issue. Would recommend going for a room on a higher floor with a better view. Tried the Smooth Thai restaurant in the hotel, and they had great pad thai.

“Maybe in other time was a good hotel” I read some reviews at tripadvisor so I decide to reserve at this place, since it was close to Broadway, Hotel was pretty noisy, avoid to stay by 6th floor above they have their old aircondition machine, also you can hear next room conversations (and much more), carpet smells weird, we ask to change room but was full the place; Beds are really old, clean but old, their staff is kind of rude, the good thing is the parking, and is close to Times square, plays and piers. Elevator partially works, wifi is not free, Maybe 30 years ago was a nice hotel, not now, quiet old; for the price I paid I should move to another near by, I wont be here again. I change the hotel to The New Yorker Hotel some blocks ahead (34th st) and I paid the same (13 usd more) but much much better. is kind of one star hotel... Pool is ok do not expect that much, but it is ok

“Brilliant find” A big thank you to other Tripadvisors for helping me find this one! I have stayed in various hotels in New York in the past (some very nice ones) but for this trip I needed one that was good value and convenient. The Casablanca was a brilliant base for the sightseeing we did, the shows, and shopping. Setting off in the morning following a lovely continental breakfast, returning to have a welcome coffee and pastry mid-afternoon before setting off again, and then returning to have some wine and cheese before setting off for the evening really helped us to pace ourselves and enjoy NYC even more! Staff were lovely - friendly and helpful. Room was spotlessly clean and comfortable - and even though we were so close to Times Square - quiet!

“Nice hotel in midtown” The hotel is nice and the room size is good for NYC. The hotel lobby is quite small. There are more staffs in the lobby than customers constantly which I suppose it is good. My friend said he feltl being watched when he was waiting in the lobby for me. The room is good. I didn't know how to turn on the shower until I saw the instruction. There was good maid service that they came to my room in the morning and evening. However I felt bothered one morning that I got up late but I could hear the maid knocking other guests doors for maid service.

“Drab, drab, drab” Calling itself a 4 star hotel and spa is really pushing it! The carpets are brown, the walls are brown/tan, the curtains are brown. The hotel has a depressing feel about it. Since its a Sheraton the beds are very comfortable but if you value quietness I would avoid this hotel. I heard doors slamming, toilets flushing and boices in the hall. The gym is inadequate at best and the pool is covered and not well lit making it depressing. The value for the dollar is not good especially when you add in $18 to park thecar. Over all there are too many other better options. The staff however is very nice.

“Great Hotel, but may not be right for everyone.” We, (who all travel frequently) had three rooms at Hotel Chandler in November and all agreed it was a good little hotel and a good find, but that it may not (for now at least), be for everyone. Here's the scoop... -- The staff is fantastically helpful, without falling all over you. We can't say enough good things about them. -- Our standard rooms were very clean and all three of ours had been tastefully redone. -- The beds & pillows are comfortable and the 'rainshowers,' had great water pressure. -- We had NO bedbug issues. -- The hotel is being renovated and there was some significant noise that cranked up around 8am. However, we knew this was the case going in and it is manageable if you get up & get about your business. -- The rooms are very small and the bathrooms are tiny, even by NYC standards, but again if you just need a nice clean room to sleep in, it is a reasonable trade-off. -- The block it is in has a lot of wear & tear, but it is nonetheless very convenient. In summary, we would stay at the Chandler again in a heartbeat, but don't book it if you want a big room or a quiet morning.

“Gansevoort knows how to party” Reading over recent negative reviews, I have to think some fellow travelers weren't too conscious of the type of hotel they were booking. Gansevoort is located in the Meatpacking District, which is known for night life and a "see-and-be-seen" atmosphere. Were you coming here to sleep? If you're looking for a party and the chance to spot celebrities in their natural habitat, then Gansevoort is for you. Sure, there are a lot of people preening and vying for attention, but that's pretty standard at clubs everywhere. Travelers need to understand that on weekends in particular, Gansevoort is a club with a hotel attached. Expect noise. If you're there to party, you'll have a phenomenal time. If you're there to be in bed by 10, it may not be for you. The bathrooms are lovely with fabulous bath amenities. The robes are very plush and soft, the beds are comfortable, and the staff were never anything but pleasant when I was there.

“Modern, elegant rooms - great location!” Stayed here for a conference. Though my room felt like it is 10 minutes from the elevator (the hallways are lonnng), I had a corner room with windows on two sides with a view of the Washington Monument! The room looked days old. New furnishings, gorgeous bathroom with high-end finishes, nice flat screen and very comfy bed with extra pillows. Two tiny complaints: why do hotels that do not offer room wifi have the shortest internet cords known to man? I want to sit in bed people with my laptop! And the hotel lacks quick service food. It could use a Starbucks outlet that offers fresh bagels and sandwiches for those that are running between conference sessions. Others have said the rooms are small. Mine room with a King bed felt very spacious and featured a nice desk area and separate sitting area. Definitely would consider staying here in the future!

“loved being across from the park” for starters the service and friendliness of the staff was great. the location is also great, quiet enough (on 40th) and right across the street from the park. there are several places to get food/drink in the park itself, plus two bakeries (one on either side of the hotel) you can pick up coffee and a croissant and grab a table in the park. good location if you're going for theatre shows, too. rooms are smallish but nice enough, unusually spacious bathroom for botique nyc hotel, very comfy bed. storage space is limited (no real dresser), i will say that, but for a weekend trip you can make do. rates are too pricey some times of yr, but if you can get it for ~$200 it's good value. if i can find it at that price again i'll be there, but i personally wouldn't pay more than the low $200's.

“Awesome historic hotel” For anyone bored of the modern look of most hotels these days, this one retains the more traditional styling of the older, historic hotel that it is. The room was quite nice and clean and the bathroom was spacious. Check-in was painless and friendly. And of course the greatest asset the Intercontinental has is the location! Perfect for a shopping spree.

“A Nice Place to Stay in DC” It's very centrally located, close to the Withe House. The room was very clean, spacious and had a good bed. I really loved the ambiance and decor! we had some problems with our reservation. We bought a package that included Sunday brunch. A week before coming to the hotel, we got a call from one of reservations manager to sort out some confusion in our reservation. She assured us that we would have no problems. But when we got to the hotel a receptionist told us that the brunch was not included in the package, we protested and he was very rude. This receptionist was extremely disrespectful and dismissive, is name is Milan. In the next morning we spoke with the manager who was extremely helpful and apologetic. He solved the problem very quickly and saved our stay in the hotel! This hotel is a very good choice to stay in DC! I recommend!

“Great Location, Unique Room, Very Old” Great location, very close to the White House and Ford's Theatre. Our room had two double beds, and one twin bed, which worked great for 4 adults, and 1 child. The hotel is very old, thin walls, small bathroom(that did not latch). Parking is not remotely close, like 2 blocks up and 3 blocks over. Not exactly a safe walk at night either.

“awesome priceline value at $76” booked this 3.5 star hotel on priceline for $76 for a saturday night. rooms are big, clean and brand new. location was great. bar downstairs was awesome as well. over all we were very happy. would stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Nice location” Nicely located in the middle of all DC sites and convention center. Staff was very nice, rooms were clean with the usual amenities of this class of hotel. No free Internet in rooms. Gym opens late for early risers. Starbucks in the lobby. Nice restaurant onsite, with a happy hour.

“Lovely details, comfy room, great location” Stayed here for 2 nights recently and the staff could not have been more friendly or accommodating. The location is great - close to transit stops, but I simply walked everywhere. I had only one meal there --- some late-night room service, and I even Facebooked to my friends how innovative and tasty that one silly snack was! Highly recommended. I can't speak to any of the other amenities of the hotel (fitness room, restaurant, bar, etc). What I particularly enjoyed was the care with which they restored the hotel. I loved the architecture of the building itself, but the care of the re-design and the details -- really great. Lovely colors. Modern but appropriately retro features, including reproduction doors and inspired lighting features. I found the elevator number panel particularly amusing, though I'm not entirely sure it was intended to sound like a submarine. I had only 2 problems while I was there. One, I had requested a corner room (which allowed for great light, but also increased street noise - be prepared if you are sensitive to this). This gave me lovely partial views of Rainier and the Sound, but also let me overlook a construction site. I asked for a room change to a better view, but they were not able to provide one with similar features. Seeing the placement of the hotel in daylight, I could see why - because it is a historic hotel, it is moderately dwarfed by its neighbors, which means no one has a tremendous view; and the hotel is blocked by other properties. But that's really just fine - I was there for sleeping and working, and you can enjoy all the fantastic views of Seattle by getting out. My other problem was a clogged sink, and I only reported it upon checkout. I do believe someone had jammed the sink with tobacco, because there was an odor of tobacco whenever I ran water. Again, as soon as I reported the problem upon checkout, the concierge was calling maintenance in to unclog the sink. Highly recommended - would definitely stay here again!

“Nice, comfortable stay. Great location.” Was on a business trip to the city. As a HHonors member, I try to stay in Hilton hotels. I had meetings at the Waldorf, but was not impressed with the hotel rooms last time I stayed there. Was very pleased with the Doubletree. Many places in the city wow you with their lobby, but the Doubletree put it's effort in the rooms. While the room wasn't large, it was very nice by New York standards. Great location and the price was much better than the Waldorf across the street.

“Your basic faded motor inn” I got dumped here after being turned away from Hollywood City Inn (even though I had a pre-paid hotels.com reservation!). I was assured it was comparable in quality; it was not. The room was clean but very small and had a very sweet and smelly sanitizer odor that was irritating and probably covering up am even worse stench. I had to keep the a/c on at all times to keep "fresh" air coming in.. The inn's neighborhood is sketchy as evidence by the reception desk - it's behind bulletproof glass like a bank teller window! Still, for the price (under $70) it's probably one of the better faded motor inns in Hollywood. You get a basic room with free wifi and coffee and danish in the morning. The parking is free, but the lot gets crowded. Skip the skanky swimming pool behind the building. It looked like it was there for show, not for actual use. My advice: check out Hotwire or Priceline and go for a 3* hotel at a similar price (bid $65). Even if you have to pay for parking and the internet it's worth it.

“Nice Renovated room, but what about the bathrooms!!” Staye here for one night. Nicely renovated rooms, but somehow it looks like they did a light makeover because nothing is done with the bathrooms. The rest of the hotel has also only recieved a light finish upgrade, it is not completely renovated. Otherwise we had a nice stay.

“A good experience” Stayed two nights at the rate of $149 (exclusive of tax, etc) in late March booked off the Marriott website. The nearby 'discounted' conference hotel rate was $209 + tax so a not insignificant saving. Location is good. a couple of blocks back from the inner harbor. Lots of eating and drinking options in the vicinity. The room was comfortable and clean with a small kitchenette with fridge and microwave but no utensils, plates, etc - not that I'd have used them if hey were there. The free internet worked well. The gym was small with (from memory) a couple of cross trainers, a jogger and bike. Didn't use it. The free breakfast was the standard bagels, etc affair and perfectly adequate. Staff perfectly friendly and helpful in my limited interaction with them. The building itself is quite interesting. Downstairs there is a massive old safe which has been converted into a conference room - yes it's that big. Its worth a look. There is plenty of parking in the vicinity. I found one on Lombard Street (Arrow parking)with a $18 overnight/24 hour rate. others were circa $21.

“Wonder old school hotel” Classic great hotel. Rooms are larger than most old hotels and it is wonderfully maintained. For the business traveler, the rooms are not as well designed as a more modern hotel but it is a classy place.

“Good Location for the Boston Tourist” I stayed at the Harborside for two nights on a recent visit to Boston. I’ve been to Boston before on business trips, but this was my first visit as a tourist. The hotel’s location makes it a great choice for exploring the city as it’s centrally located to a number of Boston landmarks/neighborhoods. I felt the price we paid was very fair for a city center hotel during the week. It’s not a luxurious, or even full- service, property, but it met my needs. Rooms were okay. We had a Cityview room with a king bed. Really liked the hardwood floors and exposed brick walls in the room. Bedding was comfortable if a bit soft. Bathrooms needed some work. Limited counter space, cracked porcelain on the sink, fixtures were a bit worn and dated. Nothing outlandish, but everything just needs to be redone in the bathrooms. TV was okay, with a good channel selection. Small love seat and large table filled out the room. Front desk was very nice at check-in but other than that, pretty limited service/staff interaction. No room service or bar/restaurant. No bell desk or porter. Checking luggage was self-service. We went out late one night for some drinks and right outside the main door on State Street was a young man stumbling from the bar next door throwing up. The vomit stayed there, uncleaned, outside the front door for the next day and a half. Location is what really attracted us to this hotel. Minutes to Faneuil Hall, Waterfront and the North End. Short walks to the Financial District, Boston Garden, Boston Common, Beacon Hill, etc. There is a T stop right outside the front door as well. Plenty of bars /restaurants within minutes of the hotel. Really got to see a lot of Boston and this was a great home base. Overall, I would recommend the Harborside for anyone looking for a good, clean, well-priced, well-located property to explore Boston. However, if you’re looking for plush rooms or a little extra service, you might want to consider other options.

“Hotel Good - Parking Bad” Great Hotel, but parking is incredibly expensive ($25 per night!). It has a great location being right in the heart of downtown. Around the corner is a Church of Scientology, which a lady stopped to talk to us about/convert us.....so that was interesting. Places to eat would be Maggianos or TGIF. There is plenty of sightseeing with the "Rocky Steps" , Liberty Bell, etc... The hotel had very clean rooms, great breakfast, great customer service, but the parking was the only bummer.

“Loved the Joule” I thought the Joule was an awesome hotel. There are a lot of pluses - the feel, the location, the pool, Charlie Palmer, the service, the workout facilities. The minor negatives are half hearted negatives. 1 - the hotel smells great but it is a little strong for me. It was almost as if the hotel lobby and elevators were wearing cologne and it was a good scent but I am a little sensitive to scents so it was a little strong for me but was nice when walking in from the street. 2 - We stayed in the Demi-Joule room and it was very small. Didn't really bother us because it was laid out well but if we had been there a number of days and spent them in the room, it would have gotten cramped. Back to the good things. The Joule has a modern feel kind of like the W but it is warmer feeling and more comforatble than the W. The pool at the Joule is amazing and is actually where they film the outdoor bar scenes for ABC's The Deep End which is the show is set in LA but is actually filmed in Dallas. Charlie Palmer (the Joule's in house restaurant) is whole other raving review waiting to happen. The food was amazing! Until recently the center of Main Street in Dallas has not been the most amazing location in Dallas to stay, but the Joule is turning into an anchor location with the downtown Nieman Marcus a couple blocks in one direction and the JFK memorial a couple blocks in the other and about 6 or 7 popular restaurants surrounding the hotel. I would definitely recommend the Joule.

“Four Seasons San Francisco... too many problems” Honestly I had great expectation for the Four Season San Francisco and my stay has been not very satisfactory. Booked a typical FS Deluxe Room with a nice wiew. Small TV with no Plasma , no w-lan service in the rooms , bathroom nice but not more than this... Had several problems with the Management , very noisy room , service not similar to other FS hotels. So sorry to say but the RItz Carlton in San Francisco is a better hotel and next time I will stay at the Ritz..
“Good hotel and good location” This hotel is very well located. Rooms are a bit small but ok for 3days. Clean, quiet. Restaurant near the hotel is very good !

“great suites” beautiful, modern, european looking hotel. The suites are large enough for a family, seperate bedroom and living room, large TV in each room. Each room has privacy. Location is close to O'Hare airport and shuttles run every 15 minutes. I got the room on priceline for half of what it was listed on the website. Highly recommend this hotel.

“GREAT” This is a great hotel i would definetly recommend all to stay here if price is not an object. Service is top-notch good recommendation of restaurants, bars. Rooms large and comfortable, nice linens, chocolate, water, orchids, letterpaper with your name printed on it is a nice touch. Own kitchen, large wardrobe. Jacuzzi hot tub not so large but comfortable for one person. I would like to stay there again if somebody else pays the bill...One of my best hotel experiences sofar.

“Felt like a modern studio apartment - perfect!” Needed a place for one night & managed to land a reservation w/ the Staybridge (by the airport) at an excellent $80 Govt rate. Would have gladly paid more for what we received, but the rate was excellent. They gave us a one bedroom King suite on the first floor. It was perfect; modern, clean, spacious plus high cathedral ceilings (kudos to the architect of this place!). Felt like a studio apartment; was furnished with a small kitchen area as you walked in, and a work desk near the living area on the other side of the suite. The intimate living room space had a comfy sofa & flat screen TV. The bed & bath were tucked away in its little nook. They serve a FULL buffet style breakfast - excellent! We made our own waffles. :-) I'm glad we picked this hotel; its located in a newer & slightly less congested area than other parts of san antonio - so getting there & checking in was less stressful than picking a hotel in the heart of traffic. However, it only took me 10mins on the highway to drive to the section where I needed to be the next morning.

“Convenient and clean” We recently stayed here for Comic con convention. Check in was very swift and clerk was very polite. Rooms were on 14th floor with a view of the city. They were clean and spacious. Although we spent most of our time at the convention we loved our stay. Hotel is conveniently located to mall, lots of restaurants, convention center etc. The downfall is the outrageous amount they charge for valet parking. :/ .

“History only goes so far” Stayed at The Algonquin with my partner on a work trip, mostly because its location was convenient for the work purpose of the trip. Can't say a lot of wonderful things - it has ts charms, but it's mostly running on its historic interest. Alas, Dorothy Parker's time has passed, and The Algonquin has done little to keep up with the times, or to compete on its merits as a hotel. Rooms and amenities are just adequate, service is gracious, location excellent. When the work leg of the trip ended we relocated to a much nicer hotel on the same street.

“First class hotel” The Omni San Diego is a beautiful hotel that is classy from the lobby to my room. The front desk and lobby personel were fabulous! They provide personal wake up calls. This property hires qualified people to work their positions. The hotel is about 4 years old and sits rock throwing distance from the Padres home diamond. It is less than a five minute walk to the convention center. The hotel beds were fantastic, as were the views of the bay. I was able to walk to any restaurant with ease and felt safe along the way. There is only one restaurant in the hotel so plan on spending some money on food if eating in the hotel. I highly suggest staying at the Omni San Diego.

“Always a treat - even when crowded” My experience was the hotel staff accommodated our early arrival by storing our baggage and then calling us on the cell phone when the rooms were ready. We were in Michael Jordan's having a late lunch when called. The front desk was ready with our keys, the bell service (Clive) was friendly and we were in our room by 3:30 pm. The American Bar Association convention started the next day, so the hotel was flooded with early arrivals and a large check in. They moved quickly through the lines and made us feel welcome at the front desk and our room. And, there is no better location to walk Chicago.

“Friendly Staff - Great Room - Cool Hotel” Stayed at the Serrano one night for business. Had a great corner room with views of Nob Hill and Union Square. Loved the whimsical design of the room. Went down for the complimentary wine hour, where in addition to wine, was served goldfish crackers and a delicious tapanade. Asked the front desk for driving directions to a restaurant in North Beach, and the associate was happy to print them for me. Received a $10 "Raid the Minibar" voucher upon check-in by being a member of Kimpton In-Touch. It was appreciated and utilized. Would definitely return.
“Great property with excellent service” Beautiful place, great breakfast and managers reception. Ducks in the lobby pools are a nice touch.

“Can't Get Much Better” Our second visit to the Hotel Palomar Philadelphia since moving out of Philly to DC was another great stay. We love Kimpton Hotels because they are pet-friendly and the Palomar is one of the top Kimpton's we have visited. As always, love the mini-bar credit, free wifi, etc. that comes with Kimpton In-touch free membership. Had dog bowls and a pet bed in our room for our dogs and received an upgrade to a room with an amazing view and king bed for knowing the summer secret password! Will be staying here every time we decided to take a weekend trip to visit friends. The only thing I think that could improve is the valet parking: a bit high of a rate for Philly on the weekends. Since we know the city, I just parked for free over a few blocks south of Rittenhouse, but also know their are much cheaper parking garage options nearby. Perhaps Kimpton hotels could adjust their valet rate for weekend parking to bring it closer in line with other options.

“Ew, could of been better” The hotel is under renovations. Some rooms have been done and look nice but the quality of the work will show in a few months. Personally, I would of never put Pergo Flooring in the entry of every room. I think the originally design looks like they tried for "Modern"... but it is just sterile and blan. The lobby is all grey. The rooms were clean and well appointed but I wasn't overly impressed.

“Style and class! 4++ rating” What is most striking about this hotel is its chic, functional, modern style. The hotel is also among the cleanest I have ever seen. Lobby is gorgeous. Staff was helpful and efficient with check in and very helpful during the entire stay. We had a junior suite and got a great rate on expedia. There was no view to speak of but the room was just perfect. It had two large rooms separated by a swiveling tv. The tv was not hd but was more than adequate. The size of the rooms was very large by nyc standards. The furniture made the room seem like a new apt home, rather than hotel. Pull out sofa was terrific. Main bed was very comfortable. Ac kept the room cool. Closet space was large. Bathroom was delightful with good lighting and attractive glass enclosed shower with gray slate tiling. The towels were luxurious and large. Note, there is no coffee maker on the room ans we had to call for glasses. There are two shotglasses in the bathroom The elevators do take a while sometimes but staff was looking to help shuttle guests on the freight elevators. We really appreciated the late check out. The gym is modern and quite large, but there is a $10 fee for guests. Overall, this is a high 4 rating, nearly a 5 star.

“Nice hotel, great location” I stayed with my husband for one in the middle of the week. Maybe a little bit pricey but we used our Hilton points so it was fine with us! The room was spacious, the bed was super comfortable (AND we didn't hear a peep from the hallway while we were sleeping!), the bathroom was quite clean and large, there was a nice flat-screen TV, and the location was perfect - just across from North Market and in easy walking distance to tons of restaurants and bars.

“便利です。空港まで徒歩でアクセス可” ボストン観光最終日に泊まりましたが、本当に便利です。特に飛行機が朝のFlightの方にはお勧めです。ターミナルからは雨の日でも濡れることなくhotelに行けます。市内までも近いのでタクシーがいつもHOTEL前にいるため最終日おいしいものを市内のレストランで食べることも可能です。HOTELの中のレストランは料金も高くあまりお勧めできませんが、ちょっと足を延ばせばおいしいレストランがたくさんあります。また、レンタカーを返す際も便利で車両を返却した後、空港のターミナルAまでレンタカー会社にバスで送ってもらえば、徒歩でHOTELまですぐですので、レンタカーも前日に返却出来ます。次回も使うと思います。

“Good choice with kids” This Embassy Suites is in a nice quiet section of DC. It is a great hotel to stay at if you have kids. They give you a substantial hot breakfast, give an evening snack with cocktails and soft drinks, have computers in the lobby to access your email or check the internet, have a pool, and give you an actual bedroom. My only complaints are the following: 1. Rooms could use a upgrade. We saw a roach on the ceiling. AC/Heat was either too cold or too hot. Furniture is tired. Decor is very 80's. 2. Lobby is dark 3. Game room off the pool was like 100 degrees. Good choice for DC if you are travelling with kids. Safe location and easy to get to from almost everywhere.

“Hampton Inn Washington, DC: A superb property!” The Hampton Inn Washington, DC is simply a phenomenal hotel. Everything about it accounts for a memorable and pleasant stay. The hotel's location is decent. Union Station is a short walk away, and other locations can be conveniently reached. Chinatown is only a block away, providing varied and plentiful restaurants in arm's reach. The hotel's rooms are great! My room was the quietest in which I have stayed. The beds are superb, and the amenities and condiments are perfectly adequate. I particularly enjoyed my welcome card from Housekeeping, who kept my room spotless and homely. Although not the most luxurious, certainly the most notable room and stay I am yet to have. Every member of staff were simply incredible! Check in was quick, and very personable. The check in agent was very friendly, professional and above all, appeared human, having shared a laugh or two. Mayra, a staff member at breakfast, was extraordinarily polite, and ensured my table was kept clear. I was also farewelled and wished a pleasant day, which was a nice touch. Breakfast itself was perfectly adequate, and varied from cereals, toasts, pastries, coffee, juice, eggs, waffles, bacon, sausages, fruit and much more. It was varied each day also, which is very welcome if staying a few nights! The gym and pool are convenient and well maintained. I had no trouble finding an available treadmill, and the pool was never considerably busy during my stay. My one minor concern was the lift. You will find yourself waiting quite lengthy periods for a lift, particularly if the hotel is busy, and the hotel appears to be regularly filled with individuals staying for business, more so than the traveller or guest of leisure. Should you not wish to wait lengthy periods for a lift, I would suggest requesting a lower floor. I had no problem with the hotel. Overall, I have had one of my best stays here. I will certainly stay at Hampton Inn Washington, DC again, given the opportunity, particularly if I would like to ensure a remarkably pleasant stay.

“Needs improvement” Super small rooms, but that is not unusual for a city. But it was dark, poorly lit, and very worn. Hall carpet is dark grey dingy and worn. The whole place needs an uplift. And I will vouch for reviewer below complaining about smoke...they may claim it is smoke free but I too smelled smoke up and down the hallway. And the room had an ashtray or else it was a creepy soap dish. I can also vouch for the reviewer who complained only 3 out of 7 elevators work. Very annoying and very slow. I was here by myself for work but would I come back with my wife? No. For $350 per night I think you could do better. Wait till they actually do some of their claimed renovations then try again. This place could be really cute. It's in great location and has a lot of potential. But it needs improvement.

“Not like other La Quinta Inns in which we have stayed.” We have stayed at several La Quinta Inns in the past and they have all looked pretty nice from the outside but this one looked sort of crummy in comparison. The room was clean and comfortable, however the drain in the bathtub seem to be partially stopped up so that the water would not drain properly. When taking a shower, one stood in water up to his ankles due to the inadequate drain. I noted this on the room card before we left. The continental breakfast wasn't as good as in other La Quinta Inns. There were no bagles and cream cheese and the orange juice was watered down. We paid over $100 for the room and it sure wasn't worth it. I would never stay here again and will check out any of those in which we stay in the future.

“Return visit to the Monaco- Proposal Time!!!” We came to Chicago in March and stayed at the Monaco, and loved it so much that we went back in August. I was planning on proposing this trip, so I splurged a little and booked a Mediterranean Suite on travelzoo for $189/night. What a deal that was! This promotion booked you into a standard Med. Suite, so I emailed the hotel and told them my engagement plans, and they upgraded us to a river view Med. Suite gratis. This was above and beyond but greatly appreciated. I am a Kimpton InTouch member as well, so all my preferences were noted and accomodated. These suites are large with a separate living room with a rather uncomfortable sleeper sofa and bedroom, each with their own flatscreen TV. In the bedroom, we swiveled the TV around and watched the Olympics from the infamous window seats. The bathroom houses a humongous whirlpool tub, but the small standup shower tucked away in the corner seems like it was an afterthought. View the attached photos for a better idea of the room. Being from out of town, I dealt with the concierge quite a bit trying to work out the details of the special occasion, and Ryan truly exceeded expectations with trying to plan this special day. He went to Fox and Obel on his off day to pick up a picnic basket as well as Target to pick up a few items, set me up with a local florist, and even picked up our food the day of the event from Pastoral around the corner. Everything went off without a hitch. Let me sing the praises of a few other staff members. We met Oscar, one of the Bellmen, during our visit in March, and he recognized us this visit, which was fun. Also, a couple of new friendly faces this go 'round were Jared and Mark (red-haired guy -- hope I got the name right!). Jared was interested in our plans and provided friendly conversation as we came and went, and both offered suggestions on where to grab a late night Chicago dog, etc. Now with that being said, we did experience a few inconsistencies during our stay. For example, the first two nights our room was not turned down, and with the exception of the above, the overall mood and vibe from the staff was not as friendly this visit. The front desk staff often did not welcome us back when we returned from a day of adventures like they did in March, and no one ever greeted us by name our entire visit as they had previously done. I do know the hotel was booked solid this trip with a large convention in town, and in addition the hotel was hosting a wedding this weekend as well, so obviously they had a lot going on. The staff just seemed over the top before and seemed to exude cheerfulness, and now I'd say they were just above average with the exception of the above folks. They set the bar so high on our maiden voyage and couldn't sustain that perception with us this time. Lastly, while staying at such a property, one comes to expect a certain level of service. I just didn't feel the attention to detail was there. For example, since the hotel was heavily involved in the engagement, I halfway expected a congratulations note, or them to send up a piece of cake, etc. Overall, I'd give the service from Shannon (the director of rooms) and Ryan prior to arrival an A+++, and the service post arrival a solid B. We will be back... Oh, and she said yes!!!

“Good Hotel Great Location” I stayed at this La Quinta during the Christmas season. I was lucky and got it at a bargain rate. The hotel is pretty new and seems clean. The rooms are small but adequate, and the morning breafast is well above the norm. Its location is excellent. The one downer is that parking is expensive. I would select this hotel again.

“Decent for the price” Was attending a concert at Staples Center and my go-to hotel had gone 'upscale' and to pricey for my needs of simply needing a 'bed to sleep in'. This was an old hotel which has been remodeled into a boutique hotel. Very small street-front, you would miss it if not looking for it. A small hotel with an adjacent independant parking structure ($11.00/day or $20.00/day for in and out priviledges). Very easy check-in and check-out. I had their cheapest room ($98 + change) which was smaller than my apartment, but all I needed to simply spend the night. Very comfortable bed, in-room mini-fridge (which I was told was being switched out so I brought a cooler anyways), coffee maker which I had to move to the floor to make the cord reach an outlet. Bizarre shower fixture which sprayed water into the bathroom since there is only a half-panel glass for the shower. The water sprayes into the toilet area which is only closed off by a semi-luminescent (?sp?) sliding door. Hardly any shelf space near the sink for personal items. No 'guide book' for hotel features, ammenities, restaurant/bar menu, etc... Clock radio had no directions as to how to set the correct time (it was incorrect and I had to call the front desk) or how to 'program' the AC/Heat unit. The hotel does have a bar and restaurant but they included none of this information in the room. They did advise me of the complimentary breakfast buffet which was nothing but juice, coffee, bagels, and dry pastry. I had to leave the lights on 24/7, even during the day as the 'window' was nothing but a 'trough' looking at the walls and air-conditioning pipes. I heard the people above me constantly, not partying or being wild, but just what appeared to be walking around, as well as people on either sides of the room. All in all, even though I was only there to rest before a concert at Staples, and get a nights sleep before driving home, it was an irritating time. I never used their bar/restaurant, there is a Subway, iHOP, and Ralph's just a block away. When I was told there may mot be a mini-fridge I brought my cooler, with ice, as there are no ice machines available.

“Nice place but parking is a ripoff” This hotel was not as nice as the Hyatt down the way a bit but still a premium spot. Parking is overpriced as ever and unlike the Hyatt, there didn't seem to be a close alternative. But the beds are comfy, its usually available for well under $80 on priceline, and they do have a nice breakfast buffet that is about $15 i believe. Solid accomodations for Cambridge (but the Hyatt is vastly superior if you have the choice).

“great location downtown” This property is in a great location - easy to Coors Field, 16th Street Mall, tons of places for food and drink. The breakfast was great on both mornings - plenty of selection and didn't run out of food !! The rooms are decent/comfortable - but loud - thin walls and doors - can hear a lot. I was not impressed with the front desk staff - waited several minutes to be checked in while they answered the several phone calls - it's a busy location -> didn't seem to be efficient/friendly - kind of surprised at this.

“Perfect Location in New York City” We got an amazing rate on Hotwire for two days including Thanksgiving. The hotel is in a perfect location in New York City. It is located at 8th Avenue and 42nd Street, directly across from the Port Authority Bus Terminal. Hotel entrances on 42nd and 43rd Streets make it very convenient. The Westin is steps away from cute restaurants on 8th and 9th Avenues, as well as touristy dining options, attractions, and theaters on streets in the 40s, as well as Times Square. The hotel itself is attached to an entertainment complex called E-Walk that includes a Chevy's, Starbucks, and Regal Cinemas. The hotel lobby is on the second floor, so it is safe and separated from the activity and people at street level. For the Macy's parade, when other people where stopped from getting onto a side street, hotel guests could easily make their way down 43rd Street to watch the parade at 7th Avenue. The view was terrific! The hotel provided us with a list of attractions and Broadway shows open and closed on the holiday, as well as a parade map. The hotel is a super modern 45 story glass tower. Try to stay in a corner room, if possible, for great views of the city.
“okay” rooms were okay, nice size for an old building, but they need some t.l.c. staff was friendly. location good.

“Good place to stay” My stay at the Grand Hyatt was for 6 nights. The hotel is nicely situated right on the edge of Downtown - close enough to be within easy walking distance of all the main attractions, but just far enough out to be in a quiet location. The rooms are pretty standard considering the price, but nicely furnished and clean all the same, with comfortable beds. The marble bathroom however is very impressive with a separate bath and shower. The hotel restaurant had a good, reasonably priced breakfast choice, but I wouldn't recommend eating here in the evening - had a very average steak and the service wasn't very good either. Another complaint is that internet access isn't free (and is actually really expensive), and the "Business Center" consists of only one computer! These are just minor gripes though which didn't spoil a pleasant stay.

“Rooms are SMALL; Consider other options.” Man oh man, luckily I could reach the top of the closet...had to store everything up there. The room was very clean; the bathroom was adequate. the TV was nice. It was just too small. I know this sounds like an exaggeration, but if both of us were in the room, one of us needed to be in the bed (unless the other person was in the bathroom). I also picked this location because of it's proximity to Greenwich Village. It is true that Greenwich Village is about six or seven blocks away. However, the hotel is also on the "final glidepath" to the Holland tunnel. What this means is if the traffic is backed up in the Holland tunnel, it can take you 45 minutes to travel the last three blocks to your hotel. It also presents a problem when trying to check out. Overall, I would rate this as a fairly serious problem (I parked four blocks away. The morning we left it took me almost an hour to go around the block because of the Holland tunnel traffic). Also, getting ice is a total drag. You have to use your key to make the elevator move. You also have to switch elevators in the lobby and take a separate one to the basement. As if that were not bad enough, the ice bucket they give you is probably 20 ounce capacity. Honestly, it is so small, that you almost laugh when you pick it up. Really, I have never seen anything like it. It is just a joke. And the glasses were also very small. Now that I think about it, it is almost like they were afraid to pick normal size tools or implements for fear of making the room look as tiny as it was. The one thing that I really liked about this room is that you could open the window. You know how it is: you're in a small room high up in the sky with an obstructed view. It's nice to be able to open the window a few inches and get some fresh air and hear some city noises. Somehow it makes it seem less claustrophobic. also, to be fair, the bed was comfortable. Internet was free. However, these positives were probably not enough to make me want to stay here again. Let's put it this way: I would examine a lot of other options before I selected this hotel (oh and did I mention that parking is $65 per day?) Something that happened really wasn't the fault of the staff. However, they clearly did not fret very much about it. For some reason, probably alcohol induced, several women in a neighboring room chose to go out in the hallway at 2 AM and have a "cat fight." I am sure this woke everybody on the floor up. The problem is the hotel staff took 10 or 15 minutes to get up to the floor. By that time the fight had fizzled out and the girls had returned to the room. No apology was offered by the management. When we made an inquiry the next morning we got this response "what... Oh yeah, I heard something about that... sorry." While this was not a hotel horror story, I was semi-desperate when I booked this room. I probably would have to be semi-desperate to stay here again.

“Better, and $30 cheaper than the union square hilton” As title .. was exactly $30 cheaper than the hilton on union sq but arguably better, and its not long ago had a full refit (or so I was told) Bay view room on the 19th floor with a good view of alcatraz- room was immaculate as you would expect. Nice furnishings, quiet, and comfortable. Free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel which was fast enough. The beds are amazingly comfortable! Location is fine- ignore the financial district tag as its really not a big issue. If you want to go to union sq sort of area its a couple of bucks ride away- no more than a few minutes cab or a few mins drive. Its nice and central for most things in SF, but quiet enough at nite that you will get a decent nites sleep. Staff great, doorman helpful, and the hotel is as you would expect from a hilton. Dont park in the hotel lot (its $45!)- use the one across the st, or go 1 block up onto jackson st (turn right) and there is a good underground secured lot there which won't break the bank. Great irish bar (kels- see my seattle review for mention of their sister bar!) a block away on jackson, as well as a great burger place (whose name annoyingly escapes me..). Plenty of nightlife and restaurants not far away just a few blocks north of the hotel. Myself being a Hilton Hhonors gold card holder has its advantages... access to the exec lounge with complimentary continental breakfast saves a fair amount of cash over a stay- especially if you have more than one guest. Dont count on this unless you pay for an exec level room or have Hhonors status though! Will stay again without hesitation.

“Ask for a river view!” Being a Starwood Hotel member has its perks. While checking into The Westin Chicago River North, I was updated to a suite. The suite had a 'sweet' view of Chicago. I was overlooking the river and most of downtown Chicago, able to watch the sunset each night. The location of this location was perfectly located to many restaurants/bars. The House of Blues was right across the street from the hotel. The theater district was a short walk across the river (about 5 minutes by foot). The suite was very large, had a chaise lounge, large desk with plenty of counter space in the room. The hotel bar located near the check in was adequate, nothing amazing, but with so much to do outside of the hotel, this wasn't an issue. I have already recommended this place to other friends.

“Picturesque Paradise!” Well, first of all, I think it necessary at this hotel to go ahead and shell out the bucks and splurge on a waterfront room...The view IS the reason to stay at this hotel, and you will not be sorry..Beautiful! The room itself is wonderful with a fireplace that turns on and off with a push of a button! So cool! The bathroom is small but beautifully decorated, get one with a shower...Slate stone that is only closed halfway with glass...Very cool...Beds are very comfortable and overall, the room is decorated in what I would call "lodge-chic." If you stay before June 30th, book a "Breakfast on the Bay" package. Breakfast every morning, anything on the menu..Speaking of which, restaurant is absolutely wonderful..Excellent food, once again, beautiful view...Staff is friendly and accessable..Location is excellent...Hotel has complimentary transportation that will take and pick you up from locations you visit downtown...When you are through sightseeing, you just call them...What a savings, cab-wise! This is THE place to stay in Seattle...

“Simply the best hotel experience in Downtown LA - A+” I have just returned from a 3 night stay earlier this week at the Hilton Checkers with my teenage son (19), whom I was visiting to help nurse through an illness, and I have been raving to everyone about it since my return. My eldest son is a sophomore at USC and for the past two years I have been searching for a hotel to make my regular place to stay when in town for a visit. Thank goodness I have finally found the Hilton Checkers! It is heads and tails above the Millenium Biltmore, which is right across the street, in terms of both quality of cleanliness and service and far superior to the Hotel Miyako in nearby Little Toyko, which although charming and in a great location, was lacking in quality of room amenities. From the moment we checked in late Tuesday night, I knew that I had made the right decision to book at this property. The lobby was well appointed and the check-in process was completely hassle free. We were given a room with two queen beds on the 11th floor (room 1107), which was close to the elevator bank, but this fact did not result in any excess ambient noise in our room. The room was spacious, the beds extremely comfortable, the a/c in excellent working condition, and the bathroom was well appointed, with dual shower heads and all of the extras you could desire (cotton balls, q-tips, etc..). Even though we were arriving rather late, room service was open and the food we ordered was delicious - the hotel staff was even able to accomodate my son's specific dietary needs and prepare something off menu. But be forewarned - the room service prices were a bit steep! As we were there a total of three nights - and due to my son's illness, spent pretty much the entire time at either the hotel itself or in the immediate vicinity, I had plenty of time to formulate an opinion of both. I was extremely impressed with the attentiveness of the housekeeping staff, who arrived at approximately the same time each day and did a great job consistently. Also, when I needed to add on an extra night during our stay, the person whom assisted me at the front desk was very helpful and made sure that I was able to secure the same great AAA rate. Each time I called down for my car, the valet service was prompt and attentive (although once again, hotel parking is pricey). Honestly, every person with whom I came into contact during our stay was absolutely delightful. The Hilton Checkers will be the only place I stay in Downtown LA from here on out! Just a few comments on nearby restaurants: Directly across the street is a great little bakery called Mocha Java Bakery that has the best croissants (including chocolate!) that I have eaten outside of Paris. At the end of the block across the street is a Starbucks, Robecks Smoothies and Famima, which is an amazing general store that has everything you could possibly imagine, including delicious take away meals that provide a much more affordable alternative to room service. Just another block down on Grant and 7th is an amazing restaurant and take away cafe called Bottega Louis that has a wide array of freshly baked breads, fine French cheeses, and delicious salads, etc.. Just a short drive away (and possibly a walk, depending on how adventurous you are) is Little Tokyo, which is an oasis in the middle of Downtown LA. If you are craving high quality, delicious, Japanese cuisine, then Oomasa is the place for you! We ordered take out for one lunch and two dinners there, and I make sure to visit it at least once during each of my visits. You will not be disappointed. Bottom Line - It was a great pleasure to stay at this property and I am sincerely looking forward to my next visit, hopefully under better circumstances!

“nice hotel, front desk went out of their way to make the weekend special” this a nice hotel in the heart of downtown. upon arrival, the front desk asked why we were staying and we told them to celebrate our engagement (true). they upgraded our room and the next day had on the house champagne and chocolate strawberries in our room. very nice touch. we didn't eat at the hotel as their are lots of great places to eat. we spent a lot of the time driving around denver, hit golden, drove up that giant mountain which is the highest peak , also drove in boulder, saw a concert at red rocks, enjoyed it all. the hotel really was a place to rest for us and it did the trick perfectly. i'd stay here again.

“A Mixed Bag” I just returned from a week at the Doubletree, which is centrally located to the museums, White House, Dupont Circle, Connecticut Avenue, etc--if you don't mind a bit of walking. Check-in was confusing as the rate I was confirmed at via Doubletree's website was not the rate displayed or offered on arrival. I had to pay $13 per night higher, a not-very-appreciated surprise. The free breakfast that was part of my rate turned out to be a free pastry (which I don't eat)and coffee--not my definition of breakfast. Regardless, the staff was friendly and tried to be helpful. The room was clean, large, and quiet. I loved the much promoted Hilton radio that was in the room. The Internet connection didn't work using the hotel's ethernet cable but I always bring one along and was able to connect. The hotel's food was fine but I would suggest heading over to Dupont Circle where dozens of interesting restaurants can be enjoyed. As with an earlier reviewer the so-called hotel helpline went unanswered every time I called, as does the room service phone. The room hotel service directory has not been updated since the hotel changed over to a Doubletree and I had difficulty finding phone numbers for the front desk and housekeeping. I ended up calling the hotel operator to obtain numbers that should have been available in the room. Frustrating. The good features of the hotel outweigh the negative and I generally found my visit pleasant. I would probably stay there again.

“Great hotel, great deal” Loved the hotel. Got it on priceline for $40 at a total of $51 a night for 3 nights. The rooms were huge. Flat screen and an a.c. that kept things frigid the way I like it. Great location right off beltway 8. I can't think of anything bad to say about the hotel. Maybe a little harder to access if don't make the right turn. Once agin this hotel is a winner.

“I recommend it” I travel a lot and stay in many types of hotels. This is a very nice place, with modern fittings for the most part. It has the best location possible. It is somewhat pricey, but the suite is gorgeous and laid out well. I found the service to be quite good. I rated the "sleep quality" lower only because I had a room on the riverwalk and one night there was a very loud band playing so I couldn't get to sleep until late. Even thought this is the "quiet" side of the riverwalk, there is a bandstand about 50 yards away so beware. The pros of this hotel are: --location, location, location -- walk to everything --excellent suites, beautifully laid out --windows that open for the fresh air --very comfortable beds --good service The cons of this hotel are: --for the price, you might expect luxury items such as robes, turn-down service, and HD TV's which it did not have --prices for food and drink in the bar and restaurant were quite high. I paid $2.97 for one tiny glass of diet coke On balance, I recommend this hotel. But, I would suggest negotiating the price and don't pay more than you would pay at the nearby Marriott or Hyatt. And, eat and drink elsewhere because there are dozens of restaurants and pubs within 5 minute walk. I would stay here again.

“Everything one can expect from a Renaissance” I stayed in this hotel from 5th August till 10th August. Although I faced some problems regarding my reservation (It was made through 1800hotels.com), there’s nothing to complain about Renaissance Time Square. First of all, it is really in Time Square. The room is very comfortable with all the amenities that one could expect. The hotel is very clean and the staff very kind. I would stay there again.

“Financial district hotel convenient for business” I stayed for two nights at the Millenium Hilton hotel in New York City's financial district while on business in the area. The hotel is directly across Church Street from Ground Zero so the area is always crowded. The hotel was acceptable in all regards but is probably due for a refresh of its decor. The staff were more business-like than friendly, but that is characteristic of New York itself. It can be noisy on the lower floors due to all of the construction in the area so try for a higher floor as the work starts early in the morning.

“Wonderful Chicago; Just Okay Westin” We just got back from a quick weekend trip (Jan 6 and 7) to the city to take in the sights, see a show, and visit a new restaurant. We love this city and go there about once a month. We have stayed at many of the MIchigan Ave., Loop, and River North hotels. We do not feel that the Westin is a 4 Star hotel. However, it is very nice and would return again, but it would not be our first choice. As other reviews state, the rooms are a bit dated. Our room was on the 4th floor and overlooked the roof of the neighboring building. This roof and vents that roared constantly. If staying here, request a room on the south side of the building. I can compare this sound with the sound of traveling on a plane, I kept asking my husband when we were going to land. I think we may have assigned this room because we booked on Priceline. However, we have never had this happen to us before when staying at even nicer hotels in Chicago. The hotel has a great location! As someone else stated, who stays in the room while in such a wonderful and vibrant city? We did visit the bar. Nice and they made the best cosmo I have ever had!

“Nice and Convenient Hotel” I spent a day at the Marriott and found it to be very relaxing. A nice large room with a king sized bed that had 6 pillows! I had a view of the LAX runway and could see the planes taking off but not hear them. The hotel has a nice workout area and sauna and 3 different restaurants. The only down thing about the place is paying 9.95 for Internet. Other than that, I would not mind staying here again

“Enjoyed it more this time but $40 for a Belgium waffle. Really??” My first time at the setai (about 6 months ago) I was not super impressed. What a difference a few months makes. The service was perfect. Housekeeping came twice each day and there were fresh cookies in the room each evening. We had a larger suite so perhaps that helped. They also have a personal assistant to book stuff for you if you would like which is a nice touch. I was very happy with the room and would even say it may be the best suite yet in NYC beyond the plaza. So why only 4 stars? Their room service menu makes no sense in terms of price. $40 for a Belgium waffle with a choice of hot drink and a main entree (meat) is under $40. How does that make any sense?Also who would actually pay $40 for a Belgium waffle?? Bizarre quirk that for the level of hotel should not exist. Loved the room and service : just will have waffles elsewhere

“Great place to stay near Hobby Airport/Southeast Houston” Pros: - Close to Hobby Airport - Clean throughout - Newer construction - Free wi-fi - Flat-screen TV - Secure parking - Free parking - All rooms are suites with sofas, micro-fridge, etc. - Great breakfast with many cold & hot options - Helpful & courteous staff Cons: - Small TV channel selection (approx. 12-15) Summary: - Great place worthy of all its ratings.

“Absolutely OUTSTANDING” Having stayed at numerous NYC hotels, I chose this one based on my research and attempts to secure the very best for my week-long birthday celebration vacation in the Big Apple. This hotel is simply outstanding. From the moment I arrived (two days ago, five more to go), I have paid attention to almost every detail and have concluded that this is, by far, the best establishment I have visited in this city. The service is awesome. Everyone really cares and go out of their way to help - any request, any time. The penthouse "living room" where we are enjoying a quality continental breakfast in a laid-back environment is an impressive feature of this hotel. The rooms are better than anywhere I have stayed and guess what, no drab and predictable brown/beige decor! Two-toned grey and cream in a spacious room, a very comfortable bed and fully loaded with every comfort for our stay. It's bright, clean and very comfortable in design and furnishings. I cannot over-praise this establishment and I'm looking forward to the rest of my stay and - most probably - will not be looking for another NY hotel for future visits. This is perfect and...OUTSTANDING.

“Oasis in the City” We used to live in Chicago, but had no idea which hotel to stay at for a Labor Day Weekend trip. After reading the reviews on trip advisor, we chose the Conrad. We had an absolutely fantastic stay. The hotel is incredibly affordable and comes with all of the extras that you would normally pay for at other hotels. Free internet, water, fridge, robes, slippers, huge bathroom, Bose DVD player. When we wanted to heat up leftovers, they brought up a microwave and utensils. The beds are comfortable and the location is central to everything. Parking is pretty expensive, but good luck finding parking for less than $35 a day anywhere downtown. Would recommend to anyone wanting a peaceful oasis in the city.

“Thank you Omni” From the time we arrived, staff were professional, cheerful and knowledgeable. There presence quickly put us at ease, nothing was to trivial or unimportant. The door was grubby and i was anxious about it but they listened, understood and cleaned everything i needed to reassure me. Everything inside the room was immaculate, bedding, bathroom, all the bits you want to be sure are clean were. A special vote of thanks goes to the Bell and Valet Staff, and the wonderful woman who bought our Room Service with a smile and florish, and i'm sure added to the flavour of some much appreciated very late night meals we orded when we discovered there was nothing open when we returned on the last boat from Alcatraz Island. Our stay was very pleasant thanks to the staff, the decor and especially the cleanliness of the room. If you are going this month May 2011, just be aware that there is work on the cable line outside the front door. But don't let that put you off trying the comfort of the Omni for yourself.

“The staff makes this place....” My wife and I stayed at Morgans for two nights, in NYC to see Elton John at MSG. We are infrequent visitors to NY, and this place was easy to find, easy to get into with our car (valet parking, pricey, but that's NYC), and staffed with the friendliest, most helpful people I have ever found in a big city hotel. We had a basic room that was small, but well appointed, and very clean and in good repair. We enjoyed the complimentary continental breakfast both mornings, and explore the city on foot as the hotel is in a great location for seeing Manhattan. The only problem encountered was some confusion over the European style of bed linens, consisting of just a bottom sheet with a sort of comforter. Our first night there the maid had forgotten the sheet, but the problem was quickly solved with a phone call. We will undoubtedly stay there again.

“Desperately needs a revamp, limited amenities - but it's all about that view!” Pros: that view Cons: no bar, no restaurant, poor water pressure, no bath tub, dusty, desperate need of a makeover, expensive for what it offers On The Ave is a curious oddity of a hotel: located on the mid-upper west side, near to Central Park, its location well serves a number of sites. As a hotel for relaxation, however, there's limited appeal. Ignoring the facade of the downstairs reception and lobby, the rooms are 1980s all the way and in dire need of a makeover. There's only one reason you'd stay in this hotel and, admittedly, it does strike a chord: the view. Staying in a roomy Panoramic Deluxe I witnessed the sun setting on my private balcony over the west of the Hudson River while enjoying a glass of red. Excellent though this was, the $300/night fee was a tall asking price for such a reward (I stayed in Essex House and Trump Soho for nigh-on the same rate and these are much better hotels). Those not in the top-spec suites will have to settle for a north-facing public gallery on the 16th floor. The distinct lack of a hotel bar, no affiliated restaurant (and c'mon, 'Fatty Crab' around the corner really isn't going to cut it for me), desperately bare rooms falling to bits through years of use (although the bed was very comfy it had rusty wheels digging into the carpet). The bathroom was basic too. A shower with water pressure so limited that it sometimes stopped was worse than the piddly over-the-bath type shower that I get at home. Not what I expect from an apparent top hotel. There's little else to say for On The Ave really. The view is nice, but that's its only card. The rest of it is sub par and there's very little on offer.

“Great Changes at the Phoenix” We'd not stayed at the Phoenix since the courtyard remodel and Chambers opened. They did a great job updating the courtyard with nice seating areas and some cool new furniture. The funky but odd wooden "temples" are gone, replace by groupings of chairs. A water feature and fire pit has also been added. While we didn't eat at Chambers it appears to be quite popular. Bar scene was hopping on Friday and Saturday night. Staff was helpful as always. We had to "valet" park on Saturday afternoon since there was a band bus in the lot. The front desk took great care of the car and had it safely tucked away by early evening. The rooms are still very 60's and loads of fun. They've revised the breakfast to just be coffee and some pastries in the office which is really all you need given the other breakfast choices in the City. All in all this is a GREAT bargain for San Francisco. Its definitely always on the list when we want an inexpensive stay.

“Fantastic Boutique Hotel” I have just returned from another fantastic weekend in Boston staying at the Charlesmark Hotel. This is about the 4th time i've chosen to stay there and each time I'm more impressed. From the minute you walk in you're greeted by an inviting trendy bar area playing contemporary chill music. Checking in has never been easier and the fact that its a cozy boutique feeling hotel you dont feel the hustle and bustle of a huge overwhelming crowded lobby. The atmosphere is so relaxed it just sets the mood for your entire stay. You enter your room and there is music playing, chilled water, magazines, and a cozy bed waiting for you. The rooms are enjoyable (I suggest staying downstairs, you'll get the best night's sleep ever!) The water pressure in the shower is unlike any hotel i've ever been in. The operations manager Kyle is always there to help me out everytime I'm there. You are staying in the heart of Boston on Boylston St. yet you won't even want to leave the hotel because having a drink at the bar or lounge upstairs makes your night complete (the bartenders make the best cosmopolitans I've ever tasted!) I would never think of staying anywhere else when i make my monthly trips up to Boston from NY. Love the Charlesmark! ~Alex from NY

“Outstanding!” Even though we`re locals, we couldn`t resist the amazing travelzoo promotion that this hotel was offering at $109 for a junior suite. We spent President`s Day Eve here and spent a delightful Sunday overnight in Downtown Boston. This hotel is filled with old world charm and an extroverted, cheerful and helpful staff at every turn. Our suite (#564) was huge and stunning with a king sized bed with luxury bedding, a large sitting area with sofa, coffee table, and 2 chairs, a separate alcove with desk and chair,coffee maker, 2 good sized closets, a compact, but well thought out marble bath with abundant towels and thoughtful amenities and views of downtown from 2 large windows with luxury window treatments. Housekeeping here is superlative in every way and needs to be commended. After reading reviews on Tripadvisor we joined the select Omni guest program which is free and very advantageous. We had express check in, requested needs were in place upon arrival, beverages and newspaper delivered to the room in a timely manner in the morning, turndown service and late check out. We were so impressed with our stay that we`re considering doing it again next weekend while the promotional rate is still available. TA reviews indicate that many of the rooms here are very small. The junior suites are spacious and highly recommended. Not to be missed.

“Blech!” The only thing that made this hotel ok for me was that I only paid $68 on Hotwire. I was excited by this hotel due to it's location and size. I had hoped that such a large hotel would offer some excitement and glitz to my trip. That was not the case. This hotel (formerly the Adams Mark) is run down and depressing. The area surrounding the hotel in downtown Dallas is devoid of anything interesting to do. I had hoped to enjoy some interesting night life, but apparently Downtown Dallas has not enjoyed the urban renewal so many other US cities have experienced. Walking outside the hotel at night seemed dicey. Usually large hotels have some great entertainment oportunities and a nice lobbybar scene. Not this one. Nothing was particularly inspiring and the place was dead. Guess everyone else knew this hotel is a dud. Pros: -Very friendly and helpful staff Cons: -Dirty -Boring/sketchy part of town -$10 slow internet. I don't know for the life of me why hotels still do this. -Boring boring boring

“Efficient Service” Came in for a quick visit to Philadelphia. Received a pre-stay e mail from the GM of this property introducing herself and offering any assistance. I took her up on that and asked about shuttle service from Philly airport. She promptly responded. Got in around midnite and called the hotel as directed. Waited less than 5 minutes for the van pickup. Driver was helpful when I asked about the airport railline service into center city. There is a station less than 1/2 mile from the hotel. I chose to walk but you can have the shuttle fdrop you off. WHile it was after midnite, the front desk was attentive and quickly provided a room. The lobby has been updated like many of the Courtyards with the counter service restaurant, touch screen monitor for weather, news, etc. Good look. Didn't use the fitness room, but from a previous stay I ran in the adjacent business park which offered low traffic, flat roads that allowed a few laps to equal a couple miles. The room itself was well lit, had good blackout shades, at least a 42" LG flat screen, cheap radio/alarm. Convenience and value makes this a repeat location for me. PS, I don't beleive the photo shown in Trip Advisor is the actual hotel.

“Lovely” Very comfortable, clean and quiet. The room was bigger than many in the city and nicely appointed. Staff very responsive, but unobtrusive. I travel into NYC several times a year and will certainly stay at The Benjamin again.

“Consistantly acceptable” I stay here whenever the hotel runs a special price. We are in Chicago often because our children attend college here. It seems like we are always in a different hotel, with a couple places being our reliable fallbacks. This Hyatt falls in that category for us. I wasn't in Chicago for the New Year's celebration and glad this was not my motivation because the place was packed, as was the entire city! I checked in quickly, being a gold member. Checked in again when the first room did not meet my standards. I think it was an afterthought on their part to see if I would complain. I did. I was moved swiftly into a better room but no view. This is a huge hotel but we get over it and enjoy the location being central to just about everything in downtown Chicago. Staffing and security was top priority, it being New Year's Eve and all. At 3AM there were several people continuing their party in the hall outside our room. But they were quickly dispersed and no additional problems. This said a lot to me given the security issues that MIGHT have been. At 9AM you could not tell there had been a massive party. All clean, staff bright eyed and ready for a new day. Nicely done Hyatt, especially with the security and getting us into a room with two doubles and a chair!

“Nice property, decent location.” I stayed here for 4 nights this past week (2nd time at this property). Overall, the hotel is very nice. The rooms are clean, and the hotel restaurant, bar, etc., are excellent, though somewhat overpriced. Internet speeds are acceptable, and overall service was very good. The staff was courteous and helpful. The only negative is the gym. The gym is tiny, and is tucked in one corner, accessible via grungy stairs. There are 2 recumbent bikes and a couple of regular bikes, as well as a few treadmills, etc. There are 4 or 5 workout stations for upper and lower body work, as well as some weight equipment. However, the equipment is really jammed in together, and you have to sneak around other guests. Given the tightness of the surroundings, the gym isn't really fun to use at peak hours. For a high-end property, I would expect significantly better fitness facilities.

“Not great, but better than the rest” Had a decent stay at the Aloft prior to an early morning flight. On the plus side, the location was convenient, got 2 free drink coupons when checking in, and had secure gated parking.
